And here also that blinding of the Jewish people is predicted, verse 10, just as it is established from the undoubted interpretation of the New Testament, John 12:40: So far is it from being the case that the manifestation of the glory of God is restricted to Judea alone. Whence Cyril: The holy Seraphim declare the whole earth full of the majesty of the Lord, foretelling things to come and announcing the mystery of the dispensation administered through Christ. For before the Word was made flesh, that Demon, that destructive one, that Dragon, that deserter, occupied the world, and the creature was worshipped instead of the Creator. But when the only-begotten Word of God was made man, all the earth was filled with his majesty. Blessed David also proclaimed this in the spirit (Psalm 85): All nations whom you have made shall come and worship before you. This was perfected when the multitude of the nations was called, and all worshipped him who was made of us and for us, and who through himself remains above all things.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET DICEBANT, SANCT. SANCT. SANCT.] Id est, justa sunt Dei judicia in regem, proceres, & populum Trina autem vocis unius repetitio vehementer affirmat, vid. Ezech. 21, 27. Jer. 22, 29. Ex hoc loco sumtum est τρισά- γιος, Hymni nomen in Ecclesia Græca.

Iterum chorda oberrat Judaica, & Sociniana. Non ignorat, communi Ecclesiæ Catholicæ Græ- cæ, & Latinæ, vel Orientalis, & Occidentalis cal- culo, & suffragio hoc τρισάγιον de S. S. Trinitate explicari, quod in ejusdem honorem trinis vocibus clamarint Seraphim, SANCTUS, SANCTUS, SANCTUS, ac laudat ipse τὸ τρισάγιον Ecclesiæ Græcæ, & pugnat tamen contra Ecclesiam cum Ju- dæis & Photinianis, non continere trinam illam re- petitionem ullum mysterium, vehementius saltem affirmare, aut judicia trina in Regem, Proceres & populum insinuare. Quid ergo de Grotio ha- bendum sit, qui Judaizare & Arianizare iterum maluit, quam Ecclesiam sequi, ejusque fidem hic sciens prudens posthabuit, ultro constat. Quod enim non ad solum Filium dictum sit hoc Trisagium, verba sunt Damasceni lib. III. de Ortho. Fid. c. 10. sed ad Trinitatem, testis est divus & sacer Athana- sius, Basilius & Gregorius, & omnis cæterorum Patrum chorus, quod per trinam Sanctitatem tres supersubstan- tiales Deitatis hypostases sancti Seraphim insinuant; per unam autem dominationem unam divinæ princi- pantis Trinitatis substantiam & regnum notificant. Cyrillus in h. l. Cum vero Sanctus ter dicunt, clau- dunt hymnum in hoc, Dominus Sabaoth, in una na- tura Deitatis sanctam constituentes triadem, sub- sistere enim postea plane dicimus hic & Filium Spiri- tum S. Neque vero quos dicimus in naturalem ali- quam diversitatem ulla ratio dissecal, sed in Triplici hypostasi una Deitas intelligitur. Nec quidem nobis per hoc Sanctus Seraphim testatum faciunt, quod u- niversam terram majestate ejus plenam dictitant, fu- tura præcinentes & administratæ per Christum dis- pensationis mysterium prænunciantes. Taceo, quod Judæi ipsi agnoverint mysterium in hac repetitione: Siquidem in Thargum Jonathan Ben Uziel hæc inventa fuerit paraphrasis קדיש אבא Sanctus Pater, קדיש ברא קדיש רוחא קדישא Sanctus Filius, Sanctus Spir. Sanctus; & R. Simeon Ben Iobai ita explicavit τὸ τρισάγιον in Comment. ad h. San- קדש זה אב. קדש זה בן קדש זה רוח הקדש. l. ctus hic est Pater, Sanctus hic est Filius, Sanctus hic est Spiritus Sanctus: Vid. Galat. l. 11. de arc. Cath. ve- ritat. cap. 1. Weidnerus in locis Fidei Christian. præ- cip. tract. 1. D. Helvicus Tom. IV. Disp. Giessenf. X. Quæ explicatio in ipsa proprietate trinæ vocis SANCTUS, SANCTUS, SANCTUS, repeti- tionis fundatur. Non enim Sanctus Jehovah idem est, quod justa sunt Dei judicia, ut ineptit Grotius, quum Sanctus in se Dominus sit, etiamsi nulli es- sent, in quos exerceret judicia, sanctitasque attri- butum Dei absolutum, essentiale ac æternum sit, quod quis de judiciis Dei dicat? Sic ergo tres a- gnoscunt Seraphim, quibus in Deitate hoc attri- butum Dei essentiale & æternum convenit. Plures enim אלהים קדשים, hoc est, personas divinas san- ctas dari ejusdem divinæ essentiæ è Jos. 24, 19. invi- cta pluralit. personar. divinar. demonstr. c. 7. p. 38. seqq. ostendimus. Non poteritis servire Jehove, quia Elohim sancti ipsi. Has ergo personas divinas sacrosanctas ternario numero definiunt Seraphim, quum Elohim Kedoschim tres suo τρισαγίῳ desi- gnant. Tum vero neque plures, neque pauciores Scriptura agnoscit, quibus essentiale nomen Jeho- vah, & attributum Sanctus conveniat, quam hos tres, Patrem, Filium & Sp. Sanctum, quorum u- nam essentiam, unam gloriam, unum majestatis thro- num constituit, quos in universa terra celebrari vult Matth. 28, 19. quos à Seraphim ipsis coli, atque ado- rari docet, quos etiam misisse Prophetam, tanquam suum Legatum, certum est: qui uti sunt unus ille ve- rus Deus, ita pro Rege ac Domino Zebaoth, quem vi- dit Esaias, ab universa Ecclesia Catholica agnoscun- tur. Ideo ipsi etiam in plurali v. 9. ajunt: Quis ibit לנו Nobis, ad pluralitatem divinarum personarum in- nuendam. Et quum repetitur illud τρισάγιον in N. Test. Ap. 4, 8. ibi certe non innuitur judicium Dei adversus triplicem ordinem; Regem, proceres & populum; Aliam ergo subesse hujus trinæ pro- clamationis, SANCTUS, SANCTUS, SAN- CTUS, rationem oportet, quam quæ hic à Gro- tio fingitur. Sed quid multis nobis Christianis o- pus? quum Sp. Sanctus in Nov. Test. luculenter eam exposuerit; Non solum Dei Patris gloriam & sanctitatem celebratam esse (de quo nullum plane dubium est,) sed etiam Filii Dei aperte testatur Joh. c. 12, 40. 41. docens quod Propheta illic Filii Dei gloriam viderit, & de illo loquutus sit: Spiritus Sancti autem sanctitatem & gloriam ibi etiam cele- brari, Apostolus testis est Actor. 28, 26. cum dicit, quod Spiritus Sanctus ibi cum Propheta loquutus sit, & quod dixerit: Vade, & dices populo huic. Qua- propter aures præbuisse hic debebat Grotius Sp. Sancto, non vel infidelibus Judæis, sanctis Patri- bus, totique Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, non manipulo Ariano, aut etiam Calvino Judaizanti & Arianizan- ti, quem ipse alias pro impio & blasphemo ha- bet: quem pro merito compescuit B. Hunnius no- ster in Calvin. Judaiz. & Anti-Pareo. Oecolampa- dius certe, in eadem Schola, ne de aliis recentio- ribus Calvini ipsius Discipulis, qui plerique o- mnes ὁμοθυμαδὸν nobiscum agnoscunt S.S. Tri- nitat. mysterium hac trina repetitione insinuari, jam dicamus, dubio omni superiorem facit hanc nostram explicationem, imo totius Ecclesiæ Ca- tholicæ sententiam: eamque adversus omnes Ju- daicas glossas tuetur lib. II. Hypomnemat. in Es. 6. Hymnus ille angelicus, quem Græci τρισάγιον vo- cant, citra dubium personarum trinitatem, & unita- tem naturæ divinæ indicat, quam angeli spectant & laudant, spectandoq́; beati sunt, in qua & baptizati su- mus: Hebræi perpetui nostri adversarii, ne nihil di- cant, ajunt tertio dici sanctum propter creaturarum parietatem, quas creavit, & propter quas laudabi- lis fit: ponuntq́; tres mundos, super-cœlestem, cœle- stem, ac subcœlestem. Sanctus ergo in creatione an- gelorum, Sanctus in creatione cælorum, Sanctus & in- creatione eorum, quæ sub cœlo sunt. At Angeli pro sûa eminentia magis Spiritum laudant propter ipsummet quam propter creaturas, offerentes in hoc matutinum, ut vocant, sacrificium. Alii aliquanto tolerabilius ex- ponunt, tertio dici sanctum propter tria tempora, præ- teritum, præsens & futurum. Ad quod respexisse vide- tur Johannes in Apocalypsi cap. I. Gratia vobis, & pax ab eo qui est, & qui erat, & qui venturus est. Sane o- mnibus temporibus laudari Deum convenit. At nos cum Catholica Ecclesia cantamus: Sanctus Pater, San ctus Filius, Sanctus Spiritus. Unus Sanctus Domi- nus Zebaoth, id est, exercituum cœlestium. Calixto & Novatoribus cæteris, Christiano Drejero impri- mis, qui noviter sese hic Ecclesiæ opposuere ac fi- dem SS. Trinitatis ibi traditam esse, negarunt, in Harmonia Calixtino-Hæretica satisfecimus: qui- bus etiam abunde à Dn. D. Wellero nostro responsum est in Anti-Calixtinis scriptis eruditissimis. Hack- spanius certe, utut alias testimoniis S. Trinitatis in Vet. T. non satis æquus, agnoscit, dictum hoc con- tra Photinianos, qui N. T. accipiunt, revera esse convincens. Calviniani, inquit, equidem negant, quicquam inde erui posse vel contra Judæos, vel contra Photinianos: Sed perperam: Conferantur enim lo- ca Joh. 12, 41. ubi sermo de Christo, & Act. 28, 25. ubi agitur de Sp. S. vicissim Apoc. 4, 8. ubi itidem Christus innuitur, & facile apparebit Trinitatem involvi hac trina repetitione. Ipse Socinus in defens. animadv. Posnan. c. 12. p. 309. fatetur, si aliunde probata sit Trinitas, hunc locum roboris alicujus esse. Quod ve- ro idem Hackspan. adversus Judæos argumentum hoc insinuans tantum censet, non convincens, in eo Calixti hypothesi δουλεύειν voluit. At quum ipsimet Judæi hinc convicti fuerint de SS. Trinita- te, quod è B. Gerhardo T. II. Dispp. p. 1210. & Hel- vico agnoscit, & trina repetitio juxta ipsius V. T. ex- plicationem aliter, quam de tribus personis intel- ligi nequeat, (glossas enim alias, causasq; trinæ repe- titionis refellit hic ipse Hackspanius) atque ab ipso Esaìa Sanctum Jehovam exercituum esse Patrem, Fi- lium & Spiritum c. 48, 16. c. 63, 7. seqq. doceatur, hic vero palam etiam indicetur, plures personas es- se, à quibus missus Esaias est v. 8. quæ unus ille Je- hova sunt: annon luculentum satis hoc testimo- nium etiam ad Judæos ipsos convincendos censeri debet? Quod utique à Patribus etiam Judæis op- positum fuit. Conf. quæ T. III. Syst. Theol. de eo di- ximus. Mysterium Judæos in eo agnovisse P. Weid- ner. Conversus Judæos in locis fidei p. 38. docet: qui hunc locum, & Deut. 6, 4. mane & vesperi singulis diebus magna cum veneratione & cultu proferunt.

Vers. eod.

PLENA EST OMNIS TERRA GLORIA EJUS] In Ebræo: Omnis hæc terra. Judæa scilicet; Deus in his ipsis locis mirifice se patefaciet.

Temere restringitur ad terram Judæam, quod de omni terra dicitur. Habenda enim erit ratio voculæ universalis, quum præfixum ה non sem- per vim habere rem certam demonstrandi, notis- simum sit, vel ex ipso Bibliorum initio Gen. 1, 1. ubi etiam הארץ terram simpliciter notat, non aliquam regionem. Adhæc gloriam hic Messiæ visam Jo- hannes docuit, quæ sese diffudit per universam terram, non per Judæam solum; imo reliquas ter- ræ partes magis replevit, cum Judæis reprobatis gentes assumerentur, in quibus glorificatus ipse est per Sp. Sanctum. Et prædicitur hic quoque illa populi Judaici excœcatio vers. 10. quemadmodum ex indubitata N. T. interpretatione Joh. 12, 40. con- stat: Tantum abest, ut ad solam Judæam restrin- gatur gloriæ Dei manifestatio. Unde Cyrillus: San- cti Seraphim universam terram majestate Domini plenam dictitant, futura præcinentes & administra- tæ per Christum dispensationis mysterium prænuncian- tes. Priusquam enim verbum caro factum esset, ille Dæmon, ille exitialis, ille Draco, ille desertor orbem terrarum occupabat & creatura pro creatore adora- batur. At ubi factus est homo unigenitum Dei Ver- bum, omnis terra majestate ejus repleta est. Procla- mavit & hoc ante B. David in spiritu (Psalm. 85.) o- mnes gentes, quas fecisti, venient & adorabunt coram te. Hoc perfectum est, vocata gentium multitudine, & cunctis eum, qui de nobis & pro nobis factus est, adorantibus, quique per se ipsum manet supra o- mnia.

## 6:4
Verse 4. AND THE LINTELS OF THE HINGES WERE MOVED AT THE VOICE OF THE ONE CRYING] In the Greek ἐπήρθη τὸ ὑπέρθυρον. That τὸ shows that it is the upper threshold of the temple that is being dealt with here: If that trembled, how much more ought men to tremble.

AND THE HOUSE ITSELF WAS FILLED] Namely, of the Temple. WITH SMOKE] a sign of divine wrath.

Verse 4. WOE IS ME BECAUSE I HELD MY PEACE] That is, because I did not freely rebuke the sins of the King and others.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET COMMOTA SUNT SUPERLIMINA- RIA CARDINUM A VOCE CLAMANTIS] In Græ- co ἐπήρθη τὸ ὑπέρθυρον. Illud τὸ ostendit de limine supe- ro templi hic agi: Si id contremuit, quanto magis homi- nes debent tremere.

IMPLETĄQUE EST DOMUS IPSA] Nempe Templi. FUMO] signo iræ divinæ.

Vers. 4. VÆ MIHI QUIA TACUI] Id est, quia non libere reprehendi Regis aliorumque peccata.

## 6:5
BECAUSE I AM A MAN OF POLLUTED LIPS] I am not worthy to proclaim the praises of God.

Latin:

QUIA VIR POLLUTIS LABIIS EGO SVM] Non dignus sum, qui Dei laudes prædicem.

## 6:6
Verse 6. AND IN HIS HAND A COAL] A live coal. So both the Hebrew books and the Greek.

WHICH HE HAD TAKEN WITH THE TONGS FROM THE ALTAR] Namely, of burnt offerings. This fire taken from the altar itself signifies the gift of Prophecy, as the Chaldean rightly interprets, and at the same time purification: for fire is suited for that.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET MANU EJUS CALCULUS] Pruna. Sic & Hebræi libri & Græci.

QUEM FORCIPE TVLERAT DE ALTARI] Nempe holocaustorum. Hic ignis ab ipso altari sumtus si- gnificat donum Prophetiæ, ut recte interpretatur Chal- dæus, ac simul emundationem: ad eam enim aptus ignis.

## 6:7
Vers. 7. AND THINE INIQUITY SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY, AND THY SIN SHALL BE PURGED] Those things which you fear shall not hinder me from using your ministry to proclaim my praises and judgments.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET AUFERETUR INIQUITAS TUA, ET PECCATUM TUUM MUNDABITUR] Non impe- dient ista, quæ metuis, quo minus ad meas laudes ac ju- dicia prædicanda tuo utar ministerio.

## 6:8
Vers. 8. WHOM SHALL I SEND, AND WHO WILL GO FOR US?] He speaks as if concerning the opinion of a council of Angels.

Grotius owes this gloss to the Jews and Socinians: who, lest they should acknowledge here the mystery of the plurality of persons, strive equally to elide the passage. But in vain. For (1.) nowhere in the Scriptures does God speak as if concerning the opinion of a council of angels. Let a single similar example be brought forward. (2.) Scripture openly denies that God calls or admits anyone into His council, Is. 40, 13. (3.) He who sends Isaiah is that same One whose glory he saw. But he did not see the glory of the Angels, but of the Lord alone. The Angels were indeed seen, but covering their faces and their feet, and prepared for ministry; standing above the throne, which Grotius explains as 'beside the throne'; but not truly sitting here in the same council with GOD. (4.) Prophets are not Legates of the Angels, or of God and an Angelic council, but they are Legates of God alone: to whom alone this Prophet also presents himself: Behold me: I am prepared to execute commands. For the calling and mission of the Prophets happened immediately from GOD, not through Angels. But He alone is included by the word US, when the Lord says, who will go for US! who is the cause of the mission and calling of the Prophet. (5.) Socinus himself admits that those words; Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? explain each other, and are to be accepted by way of epexegesis. But the former are without doubt to be understood of God alone: therefore also the latter. (6.) The Doctors of the Church therefore acknowledge here the mystery of the plurality of persons, from whose opinion one must not rashly depart: especially because it is evident from the Seraphic Trisagion that the Holy Trinity is manifested here. Jerome in this place, for that which both we and all other Interpreters have translated US, which is said in Hebrew לנו, I know not what the LXX wanted when they placed πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τῦτον, that is, to this people, which is not found at all in the Hebrew. For when it is said from the person of God US, it must be accepted in that sense in which it is also read in Genesis: Let us make man in our image and likeness, so that it may indicate the Sacrament of the Trinity: For just as we read in the Gospel the Lord saying: I and the Father are one; and we refer 'one' to nature; 'are' to the diversity of persons: So with the Lord commanding, the Trinity commands. We have discussed other exceptions to this place in Invict. Assert. plural. personar. divin. è V. Testam. C. XIV.

BEHOLD ME] I am prepared to execute commands. Concerning this locution see 1 Sam. 3, 4. 6. 8. and Matt. 21, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QUEM MITTAM, ET QUIS IBIT NO- BIS? Loquitur tanquam de sententia consilii Angelorum.

Glossam hanc Judæis & Socinianis debet Gro- tius: qui ne agnoscant hic mysterium pluralitatis personarum, pariter locum elidere satagunt. At frustra. Nam (1.) nuspiam Deus in Scripturis ita loquitur tanquam de sententia consilii angelorum. Proferatur exemplum simile unicum. (2.) Scriptu- ra aperte negat, Deum quenquam in consilium suum advocare aut admittere Es. 40, 13. (3.) Ille qui mittit Esaiam, est idem ille, cujus gloriam vidit. At non Angelorum gloriam vidit, sed solius Domini. Angeli visi quidem sunt, sed faciem suam, pedesq; velantes, & ad ministerium parati; stantes supra so- lium, quod exponit Grotius juxta solium; non vero in eodem cum DEO concilio hic confiden- tes. (4.) Prophetæ non sunt Legati Angelorum, vel Dei & consilii Angelici, sed Legati solius Dei sunt: cui soli etiam sistit sese hic Propheta: Ecce ego: paratus sum jussa exequi. Vocatio enim & missio Prophetarum fiebat immediate à DEO, non per Angelos. Ille autem solum voce NO- BIS comprehenditur, cum ait Dominus, quis i- bit NOBIS! qui missionis & vocationis Prophetæ causa est. (5.) Verba illa; Quem mittam, & quis ibit nobis? mutuo se explicare, & κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν ac- cipienda esse, fatetur Socinus ipse. Priora autem fi- ne dubio de Deo solo intelligenda sunt: proinde & posteriora. (6.) Agnoscunt ergo hic Doctores Ec- clesiæ mysterium pluralitatis personarum, à quo- rum sententia temere recedendum non est: maxi- me, quia è Trisagio Seraphico constat, manifesta- tam hic esse S. Trinitatem. Hieronymus in h. l. pro eo, quod & nos & alii Interpp. omnes transtulerunt NOBIS, quod Ebraice dicitur לנו nescio quid volen- tes LXX. posuerint πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τῦτον, id est, ad populum istum, quod penitus in Ebræo non habetur. Quando enim ex Dei persona dicitur NOBIS, illo sensu accipiendum est, quo & in Genesi legitur: Fa- ciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram, ut Sacramentum indicet Trinitatis: Quo- modo enim in Evangelio legimus dicentem Dominum: Ego & Pater unum sumus; & unum ad naturam re- ferimus; sumus, ad personarum diversitatem: Sic Do- mino jubente, Trinitas imperat. Alias exceptio- nes ad h. l. discussimus Invict. Assert. plural. per- sonar. divin. è V. Testam. C. XIV.

ECCE EGO] Paratus sum jussa exsequi. De hac locutione vide 1. Sam. 3, 4. 6. 8. & Matth. 21, 30.

## 6:9
Vers. 9. HEAR YE INDEED AND UNDERSTAND NOT: AND SEE YE A VISION, AND KNOW NOT] Properly it sounds in the Hebrew: Hear (but it will come to pass) that you do not understand, and see (but it will come to pass) that you do not know, and thus the Greeks have accepted it. See what we have said concerning this passage at Matt. 13, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 9. AUDITE AUDIENTES ET NOLITE IN- TELLIGERE: ET VIDETE VISIONEM, ET NOLI- TE COGNOSCERE] Proprie in Hebræo sonat: Audite (sed fiet) ne intelligatis, & videte (sed fiet) ne cognoscatis, & sic accepêre Græci. Vide quæ diximus de hoc loco ad Matth. 13, 14.

## 6:10
Vers. 10. MAKE THE HEART OF THIS PEOPLE FAT, AND MAKE THEIR EARS HEAVY] We said in the same place on Matthew, that certain Hebrews take this in the infinitive mood, and understand 'al' or 'min'. See what was said there.

Latin:

Vers. 10. EXCOECA COR POPULI HUJUS, ET AURES EJUS AGGRAVA] Diximus eodem ad Mat- thæum loco, quosdam Hebræos hoc sumere in modo in- finito, & subintelligere על vel מן. Vide quæ ibi dicta.

## 6:11
Vers. 11. UNTIL THE CITIES BE WASTED WITHOUT INHABITANT, AND THE HOUSES WITHOUT MAN, AND THE LAND BE LEFT DESOLATE] They will be stubborn for so long, until Sennacherib lays waste the whole land.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DONEC DESOLENTUR CIVITATES ABSQUE HABITATORE, ET DOMUS SINE HO- MINE, ET TERRA DESERTA RELINQUETUR] Tamdiu contumaces erunt, donec Sennacheribus terram omnem vastet.

## 6:12
Vers. 12. AND IT SHALL BE MULTIPLIED, WHICH SHALL BE LEFT IN THE MIDST OF THE LAND] In the Hebrew: And the desolation shall be increased in this land: it shall grow more and more.

These things [are] with the Jews, and for the sake of recent Jews. For these, lest they be forced to admit that the threat strikes them, restrict it to the times of Isaiah or others long since passed. But Grotius helps them to no avail. The prophecy is too manifest. The question was concerning the blinding or hardening of the Jews by the Prophet: How long, O Lord, will that blinding last? But we know from John the interpreter, ch. 12, that that blinding is especially understood which occurred in the time of the N.T. Furthermore, the Lord's response is open. And the Lord said: Until the cities be desolated, and be left without inhabitant, and the houses, if any are still standing, be without man, inhabitant; and the land be left desolate, wasted and deserted. And the Lord shall make men far off (He shall scatter them far and wide into destruction) and there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land. Oecolampadius correctly expressed the emphasis in the former part, p. 63. The Lord threatens perpetual punishment to the incredulous. As if He were saying, I know that they will not be amended, as long as anything remains either in the city, or in the houses, or in the fields. And in this place also, 'Until' according to the propriety of the idiom, extends itself beyond the event of the thing. And see with what beautiful gradation he describes the forsaking of the land. Often cities are destroyed, and houses are left, and inhabitants; here the houses are not left. Often it happens that houses are destroyed, yet the field is not laid waste, here even the field is devastated. Often it happens that fields are devastated, and men, and farmers are transferred to a nearby place, but here the Lord shall remove them far away. Often it happens that they are transferred far away, but are brought back in a short time, here a great forsaking is predicted. A great forsaking, that is, for a long time, and in the midst of the land, which is most habitable. No one is ignorant that this happened to the Jews. He therefore renders the sense thus: their blinding will not cease before the whole world ceases. St. Jerome has also clearly expounded the whole passage: The Prophet answers, and asks anxiously about his people: How long, O Lord, will this sentence remain, that hearing they may not hear, and seeing they may not see? To whom the Lord answers: so long will they not hear and not see, and will have a blinded heart, until the cities of Judea are utterly subverted while Vespasian and Titus are fighting: to such an extent that not even their former names remain: and the houses, if any remain, are without an inhabitant, and the land is reduced to a wilderness, and the Jewish people are dispersed into the whole world either by flight or captivity: And by no means in Judea as before, but among all nations the people of the Jews shall be multiplied: so great will be the unhappiness of the remaining people, that in comparison with the former multitude, scarcely a tenth part remains. And when there shall be desolation in the land itself (for this passage can be understood in two ways, that a tenth part scarcely remains in the whole world, and in Judea itself scarcely a small part of the people is reserved), again these very remnants will be for plunder: when after almost fifty years Hadrian shall have come, and shall have utterly plundered the land of Judea, to such an extent that it is compared to a terebinth and an oak, which have lost their acorns. Finally, after the extreme devastation, even public laws were suspended. And the Jews were prohibited from entering the land from which they had been ejected. St. Cyril agrees, as does our Blessed Luther; who also observes that the Prophet here is wonderfully copious in repeatedly expounding the same thing in other and yet other words, and thus proposes here again, but in another way, those things which he had predicted in the preceding chapters; namely, the future destruction of the Synagogue, and the devastation of the Jewish kingdom by the Romans: However, Luther judges that the later words, 'it shall be multiplied,' which are left, exhibit a promise: The remnant shall be saved, and the believers shall inhabit the spiritual Jerusalem; which is also the opinion of Cyril. Most, however, still refer those words to the threatening; and thus Grotius also renders it: And the desolation shall be increased in this land, that is, it shall increase more and more. It follows in the text.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET MULTIPLICABITUR, QUÆ DE- RELICTA ERIT IN MEDIO TERRÆ] In Hebræo: Et augebitur vastitas in hac terra: magis magisque incre- scet.

Hæc cum Judæis, & in gratiam Judæorum recentium. Hi enim ne comminationem sese fe- rire fateri necessum habeant, ad tempora Esaiæ aut alia jam pridem elapsa illam restringunt. Nequic- quam autem juvat eos Grotius. Vaticinium nimis manifestum est. Quærebatur de excœcatione vel induratione Judæorum à Propheta: Usque quo, Domine, durabit illa excæcatio? Eam vero præci- pue intelligi excœcationem, quæ tempore N. T. obtigit, Johanne interprete novimus c. 12. Adhæc responsio Domini aperta est. Et dixit Dominus: Donec desolentur Civitates, & relinquantur absque habitatore, & domus, si quæ sunt adhuc erectæ, sint sine homine, inhabitante; & terra relinquatur de- serta, vastata & desolata. Et longe faciet Dominus homines (longe lateque eos in exitium disjiciet) & magna erit derelictio in medio terræ. In priori- bus emphasin recte expressit Oecolampadius p. 63. Perpetuam pœnam Dominus interminatur incredulis. Quasi diceret, scio quod non emendabuntur, quamdiu aliquid residuum fuerit vel in civitate, vel in domibus, vel in agris. Et hoc quoque loco, Donec juxta proprie- tatem idiomatis, ultra eventum rei se protendit. Et vide quam pulchro gradu derelictionem terræ descri- bat. Sæpe destruuntur civitates, & relinquuntur domus, & inhabitatores; hic non relinquuntur domus. Sæpe fit, ut destruantur domus, ager tamen non vasta- tur, hic & ager devastatur. Sæpe fit, ut devastentur agri, & homines, & agricolæ in propinquum locum transferantur, hic autem procul elongabit eos Domi- nus. Sæpe fit, ut procul transferantur, sed brevi re- ducantur, hic prædicitur multa derelictio. Multa derelictio, id est, multo tempore, & in medio terræ, quæ maxime habitabilis. Hoc Judæis evenisse nemo ignorat. Sensum ergo reddit hunc: excœcatio eorum non antea ceslabit, quam totus mundus ces- set. Totum etiam locum perspicue exposuit S. Hieronymus: Propheta respondet, & quærit solicitus de populo suo: Usque quo Domine hæc sententia per- manebit, ut audiens non audiat, vidensq́, non videat? Cui respondit Dominus: tamdiu non audiet & non videbit, & excæcatum habebit cor, donec civitates Judææ Vespasiano Titoque pugnantibus penitus sub- vertantur: in tantum ut ne nomen pristinum quidem permaneant: & domus, si quæ remanserint, sine habi- tatore sint, & terra redigatur in solitudinem, & vel fuga vel captivitate in totum orbem Judaicus populus dispergatur: Et nequaquam in Judæa ut prius, sed in cunctis gentibus Judæorum populus multiplicetur: tanta erit infelicitas residui populi, ut ad comparatio- nem prioris multitudinis, vix decima pars remaneat. Cumque & in ipsa terra fuerit solitudo (dupliciter enim locus iste intelligi potest, quod decima pars & in toto orbe vix remaneat, & in ipsa Judæa vix parva pars populi reservetur) rursum ipsæ reliquiæ erunt in deprædationem: quando post annos ferme quinqua- ginta Hadrianus venerit, & terram Judæam fuerit penitus deprædatus, in tantum ut terebintho & quer- cui, quæ glandes amiserint, comparetur. Denique post extremam vastitatem etiam leges publicæ pepende- runt. Et prohibiti sunt Judæi terram, de qua ejecti fuerant, ingredi. Consonat S. Cyrillus, ut & B. Lutherus noster; qui observat etiam Prophetam hic mire copiosum subinde eandem rem aliis atq; aliis verbis exponere, adeoque ea, quæ præce- dentibus Capp. prædixerat, hic iterum, sed alia ratione proponere; futurum nempe Synagogæ excidium, & vastationem regni Judaici per Roma- nos: Posteriora tamen verba, multiplicabitur, quæ derelicta, promissionem exhibere censet Luthe- rus: Reliquiæ salvabuntur, & credentes Hierosoly- mam spiritualem habitabunt; quæ etiam Cyrilli est sententia. Plerique autem illa adhuc ad commi- nationem referunt; atque ita etiam Grotius red- dit: Et augebitur vastitas in hac terra, id est, magis magisque increscet. Sequitur in textu.

## 6:13
Vers. 13. AND YET IN IT A TITHING] Rather a tenth, i.e., almost a tenth part of the people, the city of Jerusalem namely, will be immune from this evil.

AND IT SHALL BE FOR A SHOWING] In the Hebrew: And it shall be turned and shall be for a pasturing. That indeed means: It shall be pastured again. The same manner of speaking is in Psalm 78:41.

AS A TEREBINTH AND AS AN OAK] The Greeks: ὡς τερέβινθος καὶ ὡς βάλανος. The LXX often translate the word אלה as terebinth, the Chaldean sometimes as chestnut; others as elm or holm-oak.

WHICH EXPANDS ITS BRANCHES] In the Hebrew: in the casting out: this the LXX interpret as, ὅταν ἐκπέσῃ ἐκ τῆς θήκης ἀυτῆς. It is customary for certain coverings to be placed around trees, especially tender ones, which defended them from the biting of cattle: these being removed, the trees are exposed to every injury. Thus all the fields around Jerusalem were corrupted by Sennacherib. There follows in the Hebrew, a standing in them: that is, they shall nevertheless stand. The cause of which thing now follows.

A HOLY SEED SHALL BE THAT WHICH SHALL HAVE STOOD IN IT] In the Hebrew: A holy seed, its standing, that is, many pious men in the city will be the cause why God will not suffer the city to be taken.

If all the land is to be devastated, and all the cities are to be without an inhabitant, and all the houses without a man, how will Jerusalem be immune from every evil, which comprised not a tenth, but the greatest part of the Jewish people! A promise is therefore held here, but an Evangelical one, to be understood in a spiritual sense, according to the Blessed Luther; who explains it thus: The remnants shall be saved; and Osiander: And yet in that nation there shall be a tithing: so that from the huge multitude of this people I am to collect tenths, which (the others perishing) shall be saved. Thus also Brentius, who interprets it concerning the Apostles and the remaining disciples of Christ; as also Oecolampadius; He shows that a little flock shall be saved from the multitude of the Jews: And he calls here concerning the same thing either a tithing according to the LXX Ὑπόσταζον, which he said above concerning the seed and the remnants, namely the Apostles, and those who through the Apostles believed in Judea. Cyrillus and Jerome, however, still hold these for a threat, that hardly a tenth part of the people is to be left, which will again be subjected to plundering. Which sense seems to be confirmed by the following words, because it is added: And it shall be for a showing. Which Grotius renders from the Hebrew: And it shall be turned, and shall be for a pasturing, i.e., it shall be pastured again, as a similar manner of speaking is had in Isaiah 28:41. Osiander: And it shall be led away captive (the remaining nation) and shall be burned (the city of Jerusalem). Which sense the version of Luther also has: and the interpretation of Oecolampadius also goes to that: And it shall be turned, and shall be for an emptying (of grapes, as in chapter 3) in that, those who are to be freed are as grapes and clusters left behind after the vintage because of the excessive scarcity. But how these things in no way infringe upon the promise, the Blessed Luther taught in his own version, hinting that the force of the promise is to be sought in the attached simile: For it will be led away and devastated, like an oak and a linden, which have the trunk, although their leaves are cast off. A holy seed shall be such a trunk. And in the Commentary, that is, the greatest part of the people shall perish, and the remnants shall be for a new people and a new Church. He signifies, however, the power and efficacy of the Gospel, that from a dead mass and a sterile grain, a huge multitude is to come forth. Osiander followed Luther; It will be dealt with the Jewish nation, as when leaves and branches are cut from a tree, so that nevertheless the trunk is left, so that it is not utterly exterminated: Thus the Lord will leave some Jews, who will be converted to Christ and will be saved. And these will be the holy seed, or the remnants of this holy people. The Vinarians also agree, as does Oecolampadius from the Reformed, which are also clearer, and not so twisted as that which is hinted at here by Piscator concerning the gate of Shallecheth; even if these are not disapproved of by Amama in the Collat. Bibl. The gloss, however, which Grotius provides here, is merely precarious, and is easily refuted from the preceding as alien to the text. And it shall be pastured again, as a terebinth, and as an oak in the casting out, a standing in them, that is, they shall nevertheless stand. A holy seed its standing: which is that just as when the coverings are removed from trees, especially tender ones, they are exposed to every injury; so all the fields around Jerusalem were accustomed to be corrupted by Sennacherib, which itself, however, was to be preserved on account of many pious men in the city, for whose sake God would not suffer the city to be taken.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET ADHUC IN EA DECIMATIO] Imo decima i. e. decima fere pars populi, urbs nempe Hierosoly- mosum immunis erit ab hoc malo.

ET ERIT IN OSTENSIONEM] In Hebræo: Et convertetur & erit in depastionem. Id vero valet: Iterum de- pascetur. Idem loquendi genus Psalm LXXVIII. 41.

SICUT TEREBINTHUS ET SICUT QUERCUS] Græci: ὡς τερέβινθος καὶ ὡς βάλανος. Vocem אלה sæpe LXX. vertunt τερέβινθον, Chaldæus interdum castaneam; ulmum alii, aut ilicem.

QUÆ EXPANDIT RAMOS SUOS] In Hebræo: in ejectione: id LXX. interpretantur, ὅταν ἐκπέσῃ ἐκ τῆς θή- κης ἀυτῆς. Solent arboribus, teneris maxime, circum- poni velamenta quædam, quæ eas à pecudum admorsu defendebant: iis ablatis arbores ad omnem injuriam pa- tent. Sic omnes circa Hierosolyma agri à Sennacheribo corrupti fuêre. Sequitur in Hebræo, statio in eis: id est, stabunt tamen. Cujus rei causa jam sequitur.

SEMEN SANCTUM ERIT ID QUOD STETE- RIT IN EA] In Hebræo: Semen sanctum, statio ejus, id est, multi in urbe viri pii, causa erunt cur Deus non passurus sit urbem capi.

Si terra omnis devastanda, omnesque civitates absque habitatore, omnes domus sine homine e- runt, quomodo Hierosolyma immunis erit ab o- mni malo, quæ non decimam, sed maximam par- tem populi Judaici complectebatur! Promissio er- go hic habetur, sed Evangelica, spirituali sensu in- telligenda, secundum B. Lutherum; qui ita expo- nit: Reliquiæ salvabuntur; & Osiandrum; Et ad- huc in ea gente erit decimatio: ita ut de ingenti hujus populi multitudine ego decimas sim collecturus, quæ (cæteris pereuntibus) salvabuntur. Sic & Bren- tius, qui de Apostolis & reliquis discipulis Christi in- terpretatur; ut & Oecolampadius; Ostendit pusillum gregem ex Judæorum multitudine salvaturum: Et vocat hic de eadem vel decimatum juxta LXX. Ὑπό- σταζον, quod supra semen & reliquias dixit, nimirum Apostolos, & qui per Apostolos crediderunt in Judæa. Cyrillus tamen & Hieronymus hæc adhuc pro com- minatione habent, quod vix decima pars populi relinquenda sit, quæ rursus direptioni subjicietur. Qui sensus videtur è verbis seqq. firmari, quia ad- ditur: Et erit in ostensionem. Quod ex Ebræo reddit Grotius: Et convertetur, & erit in depastionem, h. e. iterum depascetur, uti simile genus loquendi ha- betur Es. XXVIII. 41. Osiander: Et captiva ab- ducetur (reliqua gens) & exuretur (urbs Hieroso- lyma.) Quem sensum etiam versio Lutheri ha- bet: atque eo etiam abit Oecolampadii interpreta- tio: Et convertetur, & erit in evacuationem (race- morum, uti cap. III.) eo, quod liberandi illi sint tan- quam racemi, & botri post vindemiam derelicti pro- pter raritatem nimiam. Sed quomodo hæc nihil in- fringant promissionem, B. Lutherus ipsa versione sua docuit, vim promissionis in similitudine adjun- cta quærendam innuens: Denn es wird weggefüh- ret und verheeret werden, wie eine Eiche und Linde, welche den Stamm haben, obwol ihre Blätter ab- gestossen werden. Ein heiliger Same wird solcher Stamm seyn. Et in Comment. id est, Maxima pars populi peribit, & reliquiæ erunt in novum populum & novam Ecclesiam. Significat autem vim & efficaciam Evangelii, quod ex medica massa & sterili grano, in- gens multitudo sit proventura. Sequutus Lutherum & Osiander; Agetur cum gente Judaica, quasi cum folia & rami de arbore resecantur, ut tamen relin- quatur truncus, ita ut non funditus exterminetur: Sic relinquet Dominus aliquos Judæos, qui convertentur ad Christum & salvabuntur. Et hi erunt sanctum semen, seu reliquiæ sancti hujus populi. Consonant etiam Vinarienses, ut & è Reformatis Oecolampa- dius, quæ & luculentiora sunt, neque adeo contor- ta, quam quæ hic innuitur à Piscatore de porta Si- challechtes; etsi hæc non improbentur ab Amama in Collat. Bibl. Glossa vero, quam Grotius hic tradit, mere precaria est, & e superioribus facile, ceu alie- na a textu refellitur. Et iterum depascetur, sicut tere- binthus, & sicut quercus in ejectione, statio in eis, id est, stabunt tamen. Semen sanctum statio ejus : quod sicut ablatis ab arboribus, teneris maxime, velamentis, illae ad omnem injuriam prostant; sic corrumpi sole- ant a Sennacheribo agri omnes circa Hierosolymam, quae ipsa tamen conservanda ob multos viros pios in urbe, quorum causa Deus non sit passurus urbem capi.

## 7:1 Argument
SERMON II. UNDER AHAZ. CHAPTER VII.

Jerusalem, besieged by the Syrians and Israelites, is predicted that the enemies will not prevail, with a sign given to the faithful of a virgin birth, on account of the impending Assyrian affliction in particular.

Vers. 1. AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE DAYS OF AHAZ] We shall not repeat here what we have gathered quite copiously for the understanding of this chapter and the following at Matthew 1:23. IN JERUSALEM TO FIGHT AGAINST IT] that is, to conquer Jerusalem.

Latin:

CONCIO II. SUB ACHAZ. CAPUT VII.

Obsessa a Syris & Israëlitis Hierosolyma prae- dicitur hostes non praevalituros, dato fide- libus signo partus virginei, ob imminentem imprimis Assyriacam afflictionem.

Vers. 1. ET FACTUM EST IN DIEBUS ACHAZ] Non repetemus hic, quae ad intellectum hujus capitis & se- quentis satis copiose congestimus ad Matth. 1, 23. IN JERUSALEM AD PRÆLIANDUM CON- TRA EAM] id est, ad expugnandam Ierusalem.

## 7:2
Vers. 2. SYRIA RESTED UPON EPHRAIM] that is, he settled with his forces in the land of the ten tribes, of which the tribe of Ephraim was the leader.

AND HIS HEART WAS MOVED, AND THE HEART OF HIS PEOPLE, AS THE TREES OF THE WOODS ARE MOVED BY THE FACE OF THE WIND] They were so terrified that he immediately joined himself as an ally to the Syrians against the Jews, 2 Kings 16:5.

Latin:

Vers. 2. REQUIEVIT STRIA SUPER EPHRAIM] id est, cum suis copiis consedit in terra decem tribuum, quarum princeps erat tribus Ephraim.

ET COMMOTUM EST COR EJUS, ET COR POPULI EJUS, SICUT MOVENTUR LIGNA STL- VARUM A FACIE VENTI] Ita perterriti sunt, ut sta- tim se Syris socios adjunxerit contra Judaeos II. Reg xvi. 5.

## 7:3
Vers. 3. AND WHO IS LEFT JASUB THY SON] In the Hebrew: & Shear Jasub thy son. But Shear-Jasub signifies, the remnant shall return. In that name was a prophecy of those few who, upon the approach of Sennacherib, had betaken themselves to Jerusalem, and soon, when Sennacherib and his army were overthrown, would return each to his own towns and fields, like the seed of a reborn people. Below, Isaiah says (8:18) that his sons were given as a sign, namely because they contained in their very names a signification of future things.

AT THE END OF THE AQUEDUCT OF THE UPPER POOL] That place was outside the city, as appears in 2 Kings 18:17. But God willed that the Jews be confirmed by Isaiah in the same place where Rabshakeh was about to utter the threats of the Assyrians to them.

IN THE WAY OF THE FULLER'S FIELD] That is, very near that part where the fullers dwell, who require much water for their craft.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET QUI DERELICTUS EST JASUB FI- LIUS TUUS] In Hebraeo: & Sear Jasub filius tuus. Sear- Jasub autem significat, reliquiae revertentur. In eo nomine e- rat vaticinium illorum paucorum, qui adventante Senna- cheribo Hierosolyma se receperant, & mox prostrato Sen- nacheribo & exercitu ejus, reversuri essent in sua quisque oppida & agros, velut semen populi renascentis. Infra dicit Esaias VIII. 18. filios suos in signum datos, nempe quia ipsis nominibus rerum futurarum significationem continebant.

AD EXTREMUM AQUÆDUCTUS PISCINÆ SUPE- RIORIS] Erat is locus extra urbem, ut apparet 2. Reg. 18, 17. Voluit autem Deus eodem in loco Judaeos ab Esaia confir- mari, ubi Assyriorum minas illis elocuturus esset Rabsaces.

IN VIA AGRI FULLONIS] Id est, proxime eam partem, qua fullones habitant, qui ad opificium suum aquis multis indigent.

## 7:4
Vers. 4. FROM THE TWO TAILS OF THESE SMOKING FIREBRANDS] He calls the ends of the firebrands tails, in which the fire is accustomed to be kept.

Latin:

Vers. 4. A DUABUS CAUDIS TITIONUM FUMI- GANTIUM ISTORUM] Caudas vocat extrema titio- num, in quibus solet ignis retineri.

## 7:5
V. 5. BECAUSE SYRIA HATH TAKEN COUNSEL AGAINST THEE FOR EVIL EPHRAIM AND THE SON OF REMALIAH] This is a transposition. The sense is: because Syria, and Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah had taken counsel to harm thee. He calls the son of Remaliah, Pekah, by way of contempt, as the son of a private man, made king through wickedness.

Latin:

V. 5. EO QUOD CONSILIUM INIERIT CONTRA TE STRIA IN MALUM EPHRAIM ET FILIUS RO- MELIÆ] Est transpositio. Sensus est: eo quod consilium ad nocendum tibi inierat Syria, & Ephraim, & filius Romeliae. Filium autem Romeliae appellat Phaceen per comtemtum, ut filium privati hominis, per scelus regem factum.

## 7:8
Vers. 8. THE HEAD OF SYRIA IS DAMASCUS AND THE HEAD OF DAMASCUS IS REZIN] The king of Syria shall not rule more widely than he now rules.

AND YET SIXTY AND FIVE YEARS, AND EPHRAIM SHALL CEASE TO BE A PEOPLE] There seems to be an error in the Hebrew Scripture, with the addition of ש to שש. For from this time to the deportation of the ten tribes, which Shalmaneser carried out (2 Kings 17), there are six and five years, that is, eleven: of which two pertain to the final times of King Pekah; but nine to the times of Hoshea, likewise king of the ten tribes. See 2 Kings 15:27, 16:1, 18:10; you will see these things to be most true. And the Hebrews, in order to protect the integrity of their codices, draw these 65 years back to that time when Amos had begun to prophesy against the Syrian and the Israelites.

Grotius is too bold in correcting the sources. For neither is an emendation necessary here: which, as we admit it must nowhere else be granted in the Hebrew truth, as being preserved from corruption by singular divine providence; so in this place also it is undertaken without sufficient cause: and it is clearly inept: since it is in no way likely that the Prophet wished to say six and five years instead of eleven. And who has ever spoken in such a way, 'there shall be yet six and five years,' so that eleven years are designated, especially where no cause for such a distribution has a place, why the number of eleven years should be divided into six and five years. Not to mention that from this regarding the prophecy concerning the abduction instituted by Shalmaneser, Chronologists count not eleven, but nineteen years. And the Hebrews here are much sounder, R. David Kimchi, R. Solomon, R. Aben-Ezra & Abrabaniel; since they see all their codices agreeing, and thus that no suspicion of corruption underlies it, deliberating on the computation of those 65 years, which they count from the prophecy of Amos instituted against the Syrians & Israelites; from whom Sanctius is not much different, explaining it thus: Samaria will fall, just as 65 years ago it had been predicted by Amos. Cornelius à Lapide observes that Jerome, Haymo, Procopius, Thomas, Hugo, & Dionysius also follow this computation of the Hebrews in Seder Olam ch. XIX, and he defends it, with this handed-down paraphrase: I, Isaiah, repeat and confirm the prophecy of Amos, which is commonly known and worn, namely, that from the beginning of his prophecy, after 65 years, Samaria will be devastated. Oecolampadius, Calvin, Pelican, the author of the notes to the French Bible, the Genevans, and Diodati also follow that explanation. On which see more extensively Buxtorf, Vindic. verit. Hebraic. part II, ch. 13, p. 943. The passage to which they refer in Amos is ch. VII. 11, 17. But since the words of the text do not admit that explanation, which fix the beginning of the 65 years at this prophecy, 'YET sixty-five years,' others more correctly interpret the prophecy concerning the total abduction of the tribes of Israel: i.e., not of that which was done by Shalmaneser (2 Kings XVII. 6, ch. XVIII. 9, 10, 11), which was only partial; but of the later one, which was done by Esarhaddon (Ezra IV. 2, 2 Kings XIX. 37), which brought an end to the Israelite people, with colonies from Babylon and other places of the kingdom of Samaria being brought into the same place (2 Kings XVII. 24). For from the first year of Ahaz, in which this prophecy seems to have been issued, to the 15th year of Hezekiah, there are 15 years (2 Kings XVI). 2. The years of Hezekiah are counted as 29 (2 Kings XVIII. 2). To these add the 21 years of Manasseh, and the sum of 65 years will emerge. Therefore, in that year of Manasseh, the final abduction of the Israelites seems to have taken place, through which, according to the present prophecy, with colonies brought into that kingdom mixed with the Israelites, Ephraim ceased entirely to be a people. Thus there is no need for the commentary of Cappel, by whom Grotius, seduced here, feigns a corruption, against the faith not only of the Hebrews, but also of the Chaldeans, Greeks, and others.

Grotius understands the oracle to be about the Son of Isaiah: whom he wishes to be called by this double name. He explained his own mind, lest anyone doubt it, at Matthew I. 23, to which annotations he referred us here at the beginning of the chapter. Thus he has it in that place: The scope of that time (during which the forces of the Syrians & Israelites were about to depart with vain effort) is described by this space, during which the girl, who was then still a virgin, would marry, conceive, give birth, and raise the infant, but within the years of the infant, or before the boyish age came to the knowledge of good and evil, or, which amounts to the same thing, before that infant had learned to greet his parents.--- The infant, however, to whom these things would apply, as far as can be gathered from what follows, does not seem to have been Hezekiah, as many of the Hebrews think, among whom is also Trypho disputing against Justin, as one who, if the times are correctly calculated, had already reached some age before the reign of Ahaz, just as has been correctly noted by Rabbi Solomon, although what is said in chapter 9 afterwards, seems to be able to be correctly referred to him, but rather he is that infant, the son of Isaiah himself, born of her who, still a virgin at the time the prophecy was issued, with Uriah and Zechariah called as witnesses, married Isaiah, who is also indicated to have been a prophetess herself. And just as when Isaiah approached the king, he had been ordered to take with him his son, to whom the name of good omen, Shear-jashub, had been given to excite the hope of the Jews, so to this infant two names were imposed: the first indeed Emmanuel, by which it would be shown that God was so present to Isaiah and his children that what had been foretold by them through words and signs would certainly come to pass: then indeed Maher-shalal-hash-baz, by which word it was signified that the arrival of the Assyrian to plunder Syria and Samaria was imminent. And this is what Isaiah says, that he and his sons given by God as a sign and evidence to the people, that the certainty of his prophecy could not be hindered by any human counsels, as if sealing it with the repeated exclamation 'Emmanuel.' And this indeed seems to us to be the simple and first-obvious sense of the words of Isaiah. These things are there by Grotius, by which everyone sees that he completely 'Judaizes' and utterly undermines and perverts the most illustrious oracle concerning Christ. For with the Jews, he understands the son not of an untouched virgin, but of a married woman. With the Jews, he interprets the prophecy according to the letter concerning the son of Isaiah. With the Jews, he interprets the name Immanuel concerning the divine presence. With the Jews, he feigns that two names were imposed on the son of Isaiah. With the Jews, he affirms that the sons of Isaiah were given as a sign to the people: so that an egg is not so similar to an egg as Grotius's gloss is to Jewish inventions. And he peddles this sense as simple and first-obvious: so that here again he yields the palm to the Jews, who contend that according to the literal sense the discourse is by no means about Christ, but about the son of Isaiah. For although some of the Jews twist this oracle to Hezekiah, others, as lies are never consistent with themselves, receive it concerning some other, I know not whom, son of Ahaz, whom he may have conceived from a young woman taken from his harem, yet some interpret it concerning the son of Isaiah, whom Grotius follows step by step, preferring the ridiculous and most vain inventions of the Jews to the infallible interpretation of the New Testament, nay, to the most evident Prophetic words, without profane impiety. Nor does he deserve an excuse for having added that there is a mystery concerning Christ in these, and that it clearly appears to those who acknowledge Christ. For since there is only one sense of a single statement; if the genuine sense of this oracle is that which he calls simple and first-obvious Grotius calls it obvious; how can it be accepted concerning Christ, or another sense entirely different, which he calls mystical, be affixed to the same? If that is conceded to the Jews, which according to the native and literal sense, or the sense first obvious, treats of a virgin not unmarried, but a man from... Vers. 9. AND THE HEAD OF EPHRAIM IS SAMARIA, AND THE HEAD OF SAMARIA IS THE SON OF REMALIAH] That is, in the meantime the kingdom of the ten tribes will remain within its own borders, and will not be propagated further.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CAPUT STRIÆ DAMASCUS ET CAPUT DA- MASCI RASIN] Non latius imperabit rex Syriae, quam nunc imperat.

ET ADHUC SEXAGINTA ET QUINQUE ANNI, ET DESINET EPHRAIM ESSE POPULUS] Omnino videtur error esse in Scriptura Hebraea, addito ש ad שש. Nam ab hoc tempore ad deportationem decem tribuum, quam fecit Salmanasar II. Reg. XVII. sunt anni sex & quin- que, id est, undecim: ex quibus duo pertinent ad ultima tempora Phaceae Regis: novem autem ad tempora Oseae, itidem Regis decem tribuum. Vid. II. Reg. XV. 27. XVI. 1. XVIII. 10. videbis haec esse verissima. Et Hebraei, ut codicum suorum fidem tueantur, hos LXV. annos retro trahunt ad id tempus, quo Amosus contra Syrum & Israe- litas vaticinari coeperat.

Audax nimis Grotius in corrigendis fontibus. Nam neque necessaria hic est emendatio: quam uti nuspiam alias in Ebraica veritate, utpote a corru- ptela divina singulari providentia conservata, con- cedendam esse admittimus; ita hoc quoque loco citra sufficientem causam ea fuscipitur: & inepta plane est: quum nullo modo verisimile sit, Prophe- tam sex & quinque annos dicere voluisse pro unde- cim. Et quis unquam ita locutus est, adhuc sex & quinque anni erunt, ut designentur anni undecim, maxime, ubi nulla causa istius distributionis locum habet, cur numerus undecim annorum in sex & quinque annos dirimatur. Ne dicam, quod ab hoc vaticinio ad abductionem à Salmanaffare institu- tam, non undecim, sed novendecim annos numerent Chronologi. Et saniores hic multo sunt Ebræi, R. David Kimchi, R. Salomo, R. Aben-Ezra & A- brabaniel; quum videant omnes codices suos consentire, adeòq; nullam suspicionem corrupte- læ subesse, dispicientes de Computo illorum LXV. annorum, quos à vaticinio Amosi contra Syros & Israëlitas instituto uumerant; à quibus non mul- tum alienus est Sanctius, sic explicans: Cadet Sa- maria, sicut 65. abhinc annis prædictum fuerat ab A- mos. Hanc Ebræorum in Seder Olam cap. XIX. computationem etiam Hieronymum, Haymonem, Procopium, Thomam, Hugonem, & Dionysium se- qui observat Cornelius à Lapide, eamq; tuetur, hac tradita paraphrasi: Ego Esaias repeto, & confirmo Prophetiam Amos, quæ vulgo nota, & trita est, scil. quod ab ejus vaticinio inchoando post 65. annos, va- stabitur Samaria. Sequitur eam explicationem etiam Oecolampadius, Calvinus, Pelicanus, autor no- tarum ad Biblia Gallica, Genevensia, Deodatus. De qua vid. prolixius Buxtorf. Vindic. verit. Hebraic. part. II. cap. 13. pag. 943. Locus, quem respiciunt, in Amofo est cap. VII. 11. 17. Sed quum eam expli- cationem verba textus non admittant, quæ initium 65. annorum figunt in hoc vaticinio, ADHUC se- xaginta quinque anni, rectius alii de totali tribuum Israëlis abductione vaticinium interpretantur: h. e. non de ea, quæ à Salmanassare facta est 2. Reg. XVII. 6. cap. XVIII. 9. 10. 11. quæ partialis tantum fuit; sed de posteriori, quæ facta ab Assur-Hadon Efr. IV. 2. 2. Reg. XIX. 37. finem attulit populo Israëliti colonits è Babel, aliisque locis regni Samariæ civi- tatibus ejusdem loco invectis, 2. Reg. XVII. 24. A primo enim Achazi anno, quo videtur hæc Prophe- tia edita, ad Hiskiam 15. anni sunt, 2. Reg. XVI. 2. Hiskiæ anni numerantur 29. 2. Reg. XVIII. 2. Qui- bus adde 21. annos Manassis, & prodibit summa 65. annorum. Isto ergo Manassis anno videtur ulti- ma abductio Israëlitarum facta, per quam juxta præsens vaticinium, commistis cum Israëlitis co- loniis in regnum illud traductis, Ephraim prorsus desiit esse populus. Sic opus non est commento Capelli, à quo hic seductus Grotius corruptelam fingit, contra Codd. non Ebræorum tantum, sed Chaldæorum etiam, Græcorum & aliorum fi- dem.

Intelligit oraculum Grotius de Filio Esaiæ: quem duplici hoc nomine nuncupatum vult. Mentem suam, ne quis de ea ambigat, exposuit ad Matth. I. 23. ad quæ annotata hic remisit nos sub initium capitis. Sic autem habet illo loco: Describitur tem- poris istius (quo discessuræ copiæ Syrorum & Israëlita- rum erant conatu irrito) ambitus hoc spatio, quo puella, quæ tum virgo adhuc erat, nuberet, conciperet, pareret & infantem educaret, sed intra infantis an- nos, sive priusquam puerilis ætas ad boni malique no- titiam veniret, aut, quod eo recidit, priusquam is in- fans parentes salutare didicisset.--- Infans autem,in quem ista convenirent, quantum ex sequentibus colli- gere est, non videtur fuisse Ezechias, ut existimant Ebræorum multi, inter quos & Tryphon adversus Iu- stinum disputans, ut qui, si tempora rectè supputentur, jam ante Achazi regnum ad ætatem aliquam pervene- rat, quemadmodum à Rabbino Salomone rectè est annotatum, quanquam quæ cap. 9. postea dicuntur, ad eum recte videantur referri posse, sed potius est is in- fans ipsius Esaiæ filius, natus ex ea, quæ virgo adhuc editi vaticinii tempore, testibus Uria ac Zacharia ad- hibitis, Esaia nupsit, quæ & ipsa προφῆτις fuisse indicatur. Sicut autem cum regem accederet Esaias, juffus erat secum ducere filium suum, cui Schearjasub boni ominis nomen, ad spem Judæorum excitandam, inditum fuerat, ita huic infanti duo nomina sunt im- posita, primum quidem Emmanuel, quo ostendere- tur, Deum ita adesse Esaiæ ejusque liberis, ut quæ verbis signisque per ipsos essent prænotata, eadem cer- to evenirent: Deinde vero Maher schalalchasbas,quæ voce significabatur brevi imminere Assyrii adventum ad spoliandam Syriam ac Samariam. Atque hoc est, quod ait Esaias, se filiosq; suos à Deo datos in signum & documentum populi, vaticinii sui certitudinem nullis humanis consiliis impediendam, repetita excla- matione Emanuel velut obsignans. Atque hic quidem nobis videtur simplex primoque obvius esse sensus ver- borum Esaiæ. Hæc ibi Grotius, quibus ipsum ex as- se ἰσδαΐζειν, & illustrissimum de Christo oracu- lum prorsus labefactare ac pervertere, nemo non videt. Cum Judæis enim virginis non illibatæ, sed nuptæ filium intelligit. Cum Judæis de filio Esaiæ secundum literam interpretatur vaticinium. Cum Judæis nomen Immanuel de παρᾳσίᾳ divina in- terpretatur. Cum Judæis Esaiæ filio duo nomina im- posita fingit. Cum Judæis filios Esaiæ in signum po- puli datos affirmat: ut ovum ovo non tam simile sit, quam Grotii glossa commentis Judaicis. Atque hunc sensum venditat pro simplici primoque obvio: ut hic iterum Judæis herbam porrigat, secundum sensum literalem neutiquam de Christo, sed de Esaiæ filio sermonem esse contendentibus. Quanquam e- nim Judæorum nonnulli ad Ezechiam hoc oracu- lum detorqueant, alii, uti mendacia nunquam fi- bi constant, de alio, nescio quo, Achazi filio id acci- piant, quem è juvencula è gynecæo suo ducta suf- ceperit, nonnulli tamen de Esaiæ filio interpretan- tur, quos κατὰ πόδα sequitur Grotius, ludicra ac vanis- sima Judæorum commenta interpretationi infalli- bili N.T. imo evidentissimis verbis Propheticis, nos absque profana impietate præferens. Neque vero excusationem meretur, quod addiderit, inesse in his μυσήριον de Christo, idque Christum agnosfen- tibus liquido apparere. Nam quum unius dicti non sit nisi unicus sensus; si hujus oraculi sensus genui- nus est, quem simplicem primoq; obvium dicit Gro- tius, quomodo id de Christo accipi, aut alius plane diversus sensus, quem mysticum vocat, affingi ei- dem potest? Si id Judæis concedatur, quod secun- dum sensum nativum & literalem, vel primo ob- vium agat de virgine non innupta, sed virum ex- Vers. 9. ET CAPVT EPHRAIM SAMARIA, ET CAPVT SAMARIÆ FILIVS ROMELIÆ] Id est, inter- ea temporis manebit regnum decem tribuum inter suos terminos, nec ultra propagabitur.

## 7:9
IF YOU WILL NOT BELIEVE, YOU SHALL NOT BE ESTABLISHED] It seems more congruent to the sense that the Hebrew can be translated thus: do you therefore not believe, because you are not confirmed? namely, by some conspicuous sign.

Latin:

SI NON CREDIDERITIS, NON PERMANEBI- TIS] Videtur congruentius sensui Hebræum sic posse ver- ti: an ideo non creditis, quia non confirmamini? signo sci- licet aliquo conspicuo.

## 7:11
ASK THEE A SIGN OF THE LORD THY GOD IN THE DEPTH OF THE GRAVE] Suppose, that the earth should immediately move, or gape open.

OR IN THE HEIGHT ABOVE] Suppose, that the sun should suddenly fail.

Latin:

PETE TIBI SIGNVM A DOMINO DEO TVO IN PROFVNDVM INFERNI] Puta, ut terra statim mo- veatur, aut dehifcat.

SIVE IN EXCELSVM SVPRA] Puta, ut fol subito deficiat.

## 7:12
Vers. 12. AND AHAZ SAID: I WILL NOT ASK, NEITHER WILL I TEMPT THE LORD] That is, I do not wish to be troublesome to God. What you say is clearly incredible. For, distrusting God, he was soliciting the help of the King of Assyria with gifts, II Kings XVI. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET DIXIT ACHAZ: NON PETAM, ET NON TENTABO DOMINVM] Id est, nolo Deo mo- lestus esse. Quæ dicis, plane incredibilia sunt. Nam Deo diffisus, ambibat muneribus opem regis Assyrii, II. Regum. XVI. 7.

## 7:13
Vers. 13. BECAUSE YOU ARE TROUBLESOME TO MY GOD] Injurious to him, to whom you think there is not enough strength to liberate you.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVIA MOLESTI ESTIS DEO MEO] In- juriosi in eum, cui putatis non satis esse virium ad vos li- berandos.

## 7:14
Vers. 14. THE LORD HIMSELF SHALL GIVE YOU A SIGN] To those not asking.

HIS NAME SHALL BE CALLED IMMANUEL] Besides the other name Maher-Shalal Hash-Baz VIII. 1. The name Immanuel signifies certain help from God against the Syrians and Israelites, and in preserving the city against Sennacherib. The other name signifies the desolation of the field and the destruction of the towns.

experienced in a common and ordinary birth, not a singular and miraculous one, of a simple and mere man, not a God-man (θεανθρώπῳ), by what right then will it be urged any further against the Jews, or by what right at least among Christians will that be explained concerning the undefiled virgin, the miraculous birth, and the divine supposition, concerning Christ the God-man (θεανθρώπῳ)? Grotius acknowledges that this cannot be urged against the Jews, and therefore says that it clearly appears to Christians that this mystery underlies it. But it does not appear clearly even to them! For who, under a woman who has experienced a man, would understand or allow himself to be persuaded that he must understand an undefiled virgin who has not experienced a man; who, under an ordinary birth proceeding from the marriage of a man and a woman, would understand a virginal birth; who, under a mere man (ψιλῷ), would understand or allow himself to be persuaded that he must understand a God-man (θεάνθρωπον)! Let us hear, however, how Grotius gathers his mystical sense. First, he concludes thus: If all the deliverances of the Jewish people were presages of that deliverance which God was to effect through Christ; surely that notable deliverance from hostile siege, which the Prophet was promising, also pertained to it. But what has this to do with a mystical sense! For the question is not about some typical fact, about a prefigurative deliverance, but about the sense of the Prophetic words intended by the Holy Spirit; nor, if it is established to us that the fact which is predicted was a figure of the deliverance of Christ, does it follow that a mystical sense underlies the Prophetic words beyond the literal sense. There are many histories of the Old Testament which provide some type, and can be applied by way of a type: concerning which, however, it is not appropriate to say, wherever they are read in the Old Testament, that in the historical account that sense underlies it, exhibiting a mystery. Therefore, a mystical sense of the expressions is not to be gathered immediately from prefiguring and typical facts. Furthermore, what has deliverance to do with those words: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and shall bear a son! If the deliverance promised under the sign of the son about to be born to the Prophet is acknowledged as a type of the deliverance of Christ, does the oracle, which predicts that a son is about to be born to the Prophet, as far as the literal sense is concerned, therefore also contain a mystical sense concerning the virgin's son about to be born to the same without the work of a man? What coherence is here; what evidence, so that this mystery may clearly appear? Finally, by that reasoning, must it not be concluded in all the deliverances which are read to have been predicted, that the deliverance to come through Christ was also predicted in a mystical sense, and that the birth of Christ from a virgin mother was also predicted?

Furthermore, secondly, Grotius applies the fact that Gabriel taught Mary (Luke 1:32) that the stability of the Davidic kingdom promised by the Prophet had its true fulfillment (πλήρωμα) in the eternal kingdom of Christ. But Gabriel does not refer to this oracle as far as the eternity of the kingdom of Christ is concerned, nor does he gather it from the stability of the Davidic kingdom (for this would be an unlearned (ἀπαίδευτος) and clearly weak collection, to demonstrate the eternity of the kingdom of Christ from the stability of the Davidic kingdom), but he points his finger to Isaiah chapter 9, in which the subject is not the kingdom of David, nor is the kingdom of the Messiah shadowed forth under the kingdom of David, but the kingdom of the Messiah itself is described according to the proper and native sense of the prophetic oracle. Then indeed, even if the stability of the Davidic kingdom had been promised here, in the present oracle, it could by no means be proved from that that the kingdom of Christ is eternal, or by what document will it be shown that the stability of the Davidic kingdom had its fulfillment (πλήρωμα) in the eternal kingdom of Christ? Finally, if this were also admitted, the mystical sense concerning the virgin's son would still not underlie the literal sense concerning the son of Isaiah begotten by the common law of marriage.

Wherefore, thirdly, Grotius betakes himself to the name of virgin. But that, 'a virgin shall conceive,' he says, how much more excellent a sense it has, if it is referred to her who conceived in such a way that she remained a virgin after conception, which befits Mary alone. But there will be no place for this sense if by 'virgin' here the wife of Isaiah or a young woman whom Isaiah was to marry is understood in the literal sense; because one and the same word placed in the same passage cannot obtain such contrary meanings at the same time. The word העלמה, if in this passage, 'a virgin shall conceive,' denotes a virgin taken into marriage, or one who has experienced a man, it cannot in the same passage signify an unmarried virgin who has conceived while preserving her virginity. Therefore, the sense is not only more eminent in this passage concerning Mary the undefiled virgin, but it is the only true and genuine one; provided that these words, A VIRGIN SHALL CONCEIVE, A VIRGIN SHALL BEAR, as they sound, in a simple and first-obvious sense, imply a virginal conception and birth with virginity unharmed, and cannot or ought not to be accepted otherwise in this oracle.

Grotius adds fourthly this reason for his mystical sense, also taken from the name Immanuel. For the name Immanuel, just like Jesus, may indeed have its own restricted and limited signification in other cases; but in Christ it has another, in infinite parts more perfect. For He is the one in whom all those excellent promises of God are 'Yes and Amen' (1 Cor. 1:20); He is the Word, who became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14); finally, in Him dwells the fullness of the Godhead bodily (τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος σωματικῶς, Col. 2:8). For those who do not believe in Him, there remains a fearful expectation of judgment (Φοβερὰ ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως, Heb. 10:27). But here again Grotius can be constrained by his own hypothesis (ὑποθέσει). For if the word עמנואל is to be understood in this passage in such a way that it denotes a God-man (θεάνθρωπον), the Word who became flesh, He in whom the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily, it certainly cannot be understood in this passage concerning a mere man (ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ), and vice versa: if this promised son is a mere man, the son of Isaiah or of anyone else, who is called Immanuel only to designate the gracious assistance of God, how can Jesus the God-man (θεάνθρωπος), the Son of God and the virgin Mary, be understood through the son promised here, and the union of the divine and human nature in the hypostatic person of Christ be designated by the name Immanuel! If you say that the son of Isaiah was a type of Christ, let us grant these things (even if it is established by no indication, nor is there any mention of the son of Isaiah by any word here), what then will be more certain than that this oracle, according to that hypothesis, dealing in the literal sense with the son of Isaiah, does nothing at all for the birth of the Son of God from the virgin Mary; much less does it simultaneously exhibit a more eminent sense, according to which it implies the birth of the God-man (θεανθρώπου) from a virgin! For if you wish to say: that a mystical sense underlies this literal one concerning the son of Isaiah, in that this ought to have been a type of the Messiah, you not only assume this type gratuitously, which you ought to have demonstrated from the Prophet, in whom there is nothing to be found concerning him, that the son of Isaiah existed as a type of the Messiah, (therefore no one of the Jews will grant that to you:) but it would also be absurd to constitute an infant born from marital intercourse as a type of a virginal birth, as such, or to make the conception and birth of a wife a type of the conception and birth of an undefiled virgin; and no less absurd, that the name Immanuel, which denotes only the presence and assistance to be provided to the son of Isaiah, and for that reason is to be imposed upon him, is by this notion a type of the hypostatic union of the divine and human nature in Christ: in which manner all, to whom God was ever present with his help, could have been marked by this name, and at the same time would have typically adumbrated the mystery of the hypostatic union; how inconvenient that is, everyone sees. But far more absurd, under the literal sense concerning the birth of a mere man to be procreated by his parents, to suppose a mystery, or another mystical sense, to lie hidden concerning the birth of the God-man from a virgin mother, that the words 'a virgin shall conceive' are to be understood of a virgin given in marriage conceiving from the intercourse of a man, that the name Immanuel brings in nothing else here according to the literal sense than the help of God, and yet that under these words a mystery lies hidden concerning the conception of an undefiled virgin, with her virginity to be preserved, and concerning the person of the God-man, who is to be called Immanuel, that is, God with us, for the reason that God is to become a sharer of our nature, or is to assume our nature into the unity of His divine hypostasis. No Christian has ever dreamed of such a mystery under such a literal sense, so far is it from being the case that he would demonstrate the truth of this mystery to any of the Jews from this oracle, while that literal sense stands: who will rather refute the Evangelists from it, because they would have tried in vain to carve out such a mystery from Prophetic words that bring in a clearly different and contrary sense (according to the Grotian hypothesis). How, therefore, can Grotius now conclude that it was most truly written by Matthew that in the birth of Christ the words of Isaiah were fulfilled, that is, brought to completion; if indeed in the words of Isaiah according to the proper and genuine sense, according to Grotius, nothing is held concerning the birth of Christ, nor could a contrary sense, which he calls mystical, lie hidden under those words, if they are to be accepted in that sense, from the intention of the Holy Spirit, as has now been demonstrated before our eyes. Rightly, therefore, Rivetus, Animadversions on the annotations of Grotius on Cassander, page 238. If that is the simple sense, and the one first obvious from the words of Isaiah, which Grotius desires, whatever is said afterwards about the mystical sense, about her who as a virgin gave birth, who was signified by that little woman who gave birth from the congress of a husband, all that will be uncertain, nay, even irrelevant. For what has a woman giving birth after intercourse with a man in common with a virgin who conceived and gave birth as a virgin? Justin Martyr certainly thought that Isaiah had predicted the birth of the virgin not obscurely, but in open words, word for word; nor is there any among the ancients who dreamed of a type here. Now indeed, says Justin, Apol. 2 for the Christians, p. 58, listen to how Isaiah predicted in express words that he would arise from a virgin. He predicted, however, in this manner: Behold, a virgin shall carry in the womb, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Immanuel, that is, God with us. For those things which were held to be incredible and impossible among men, God demonstrated through the prophetic Spirit would come to pass: so that when they had happened, they would not be called into doubt through incredulity, but would be held as certain through faith because of the prediction. But lest some, not understanding the prophecy which we have produced, object to us (through cavil) those things which we rightly objected to the Poets, who say that Jupiter frequented women for the sake of sexual pleasure, it seemed good to declare those words. Therefore, what was said: 'Behold, a virgin shall carry in the womb,' signifies that the virgin was to conceive without sexual custom. For if she had had intercourse with anyone, she would no longer have been a virgin. But Grotius is seduced here by the Jews, as we observed before: since R. Solomon Jarchi, R. Lipomanus, and R. Menasse Ben Israel in Conciliat. Hispan. on Isaiah explain it concerning the son of Isaiah: to whom R. Isaac Ben Abraham in his book against the New Testament, chapter 21, agrees: Then by Socinus in this part Judaizing, whose footsteps he closely adheres to here, as can be seen in Lectiones sacrae locorum, p. 37 seqq. For Socinus contends at length that the words of Isaiah are to be accepted in such a sense that whatever is predicted here pertains manifestly to those times of King Ahaz himself, and who this boy is, he says, to be born from a young woman, and who that young woman is, it is seen to be entirely clear from chapter 8 of Isaiah, that indeed that boy, whose name is to be called 'hasten the spoil, speed the prey,' is indeed he who is treated in chapter 7, namely the son of Isaiah. Furthermore, because of the explanation of the Evangelist Matthew, just as Grotius, Socinus observes that one and the same prediction has more than one sense. In this, however, Socinus was more sound than our author: that, although he asserted that that prediction could be accommodated and ought to be accommodated IN SOME WAY to someone else besides Jesus of Nazareth, namely to that boy born from the prophetess and Isaiah, he nevertheless recognized that, if the propriety of the words and of the whole place and sentence is looked at, the same is to be referred especially and primarily to Jesus himself. Which he also confirmed with some arguments: But with such as prove that it pertains not primarily, but solely to Jesus, according to the propriety of the words and of the whole place and sentence. Grotius, however, makes the simple and first obvious sense, i.e., the proper one, about the son of Isaiah: but he does not admit that according to the propriety of the words and of the whole place the discourse is about Jesus of Nazareth. The opinion of Grotius is therefore without doubt worse, and more adverse both to the Prophetic prediction and to the interpretation of the Evangelists. Simon Episcopius followed Grotius in his Institutiones Theologicae, book 3, chapter 14, striving at length to construct the same opinion, and by the same reasoning as he. Whence, lest it deceive anyone, and primarily for the sake of vindicating divine truth, the same must be weighed a little more fully.

But it must first be observed that the hypotheses and reasons on which Grotius relies here are merely precarious, destitute of any solid foundation; nay, some are even adverse to Holy Scripture. For whence will it be taught that the boy to whom the name Immanuel was to be imposed, and who was to be called Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz, is the same? Whence will it be shown that that prophetess was then a virgin, or that Isaiah married her, and for that purpose called witnesses? Whence will it be evinced that those things concerning the sons given for a sign are to be understood of the two sons of Isaiah, Shear-Jashub and Immanuel? All of which Grotius assumes rashly without proof.

Then indeed a sign is given here to the Jewish people, not a common one, but altogether singular and admirable. For since God had commanded through the Prophet that the King himself should ask for some sign, whether in heaven or on earth, and upon his refusal, He gave the sign Himself, it is manifest that a certain admirable sign is being dealt with here: a huge sign, which the word אות signifies, which is accustomed to be joined with the word מופת, an omen, Exod. 4, 9. 17. 25. Deut. 6, 21. Is. 20, 3. A sign which could contend with any other given either in heaven or on earth. For such a one the King had been commanded to ask. A sign which God Himself was about to give, which cannot be lighter than that which Ahaz hesitated to seek: a sign which God was about to give, not to an unfaithful King hypocritically mocking God, but to the house of David, not only for the present, but as a perpetual sealing of grace. Hear therefore, O house of David; is it a small thing for you to be troublesome to men, because you are troublesome also to my God? For this reason the Lord Himself will give you a sign. It is not therefore a common one, but altogether distinguished and excellent, which is promised here. Musculus acknowledged this: He does not say, ask a sign for yourself from me, but from the Lord. Ask such a sign, he says, that neither I, nor anyone else, but the Lord alone will be able to perform, so that you may know that I have been sent to you by Him. Grotius himself confesses that a plainly miraculous sign was to be asked for, explaining it thus: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God in the depth of the underworld, suppose that the earth may immediately be moved or split open. OR IN THE HEIGHTS ABOVE, for instance, that the Sun should suddenly fail. But what is there to be wondered at in the fact that a young maiden, while being given in marriage, should conceive and give birth from a marital union? But for an undefiled virgin to conceive and give birth, that is truly miraculous; that GOD should become man is such a great and unique sign, than which nothing more admirable has ever been heard, which sign happened both from heaven above and below on earth: because God in heaven was made man on earth, and through the admirable coming of the Spirit from the Heavens, was conceived in the womb of a virgin mother on earth, which is confessedly a great mystery 1 Tim. 3, 15. and that new thing, which alone is new under the sun, Jer. 31, 22. for which Cyprian, or whoever that very ancient author is, Serm. 3. de Nat. Domini rightly exclaims: O Lord, how admirable is thy name! Truly thou art God, who doest wonders. I do not only admire the stature of this world, not the stability of the earth, etc. I admire God in the womb of a virgin, I admire the omnipotent in a cradle, I admire how the Word of God adhered to flesh, how the incorporeal God put on the covering of our body! Cyril speaks excellently here, lib. 1. Orat. 4. in Es. p. 122. Let us therefore bid farewell to the deceits of errors, and let us embrace what is right and true, and believe that the holy virgin is denoted to us by God in this prophecy. For thus it will be a paradox truly, and incredible, and a greatest sign in the deep and in the height at the same time, according to the divine promise. For the only-begotten Son, born from on high and from God the Father according to nature, emptied himself, and was brought forth from a virginal womb according to the flesh, not by the human emission of seed, from which generation might follow, but by the power and efficiency of the Holy Spirit: and before him Justin Martyr Dial. cum Tryph. pag. 242. If he was not to be born of the virgin of whom Isaiah was speaking, into whom the Holy Spirit was exclaiming; Behold the Lord shall give a sign: Behold a virgin shall conceive in the womb, and shall bring forth a son? If, just like all other firstborns, he too was to be begotten from sexual intercourse, what sign did he say he was performing that was not common to all firstborns?
