Quis diceret enim miraculum, si quis ab aleatore primo jactu unionem in omnibus tesseris di- cat projici, quum hoc etiam alias possit contingere. Igitur aut virginem fateantur incorruptam aut mi- raculum indicari negent. Neque tunc miraculum in Alma fuerit, sed, pro miraculo, si Apellæ credas, habendust Propheta, quod masculum prædicere po- tuerit. Sed apage illas ineptias. Argumentum hoc de voce העלמה diligenter è veteribus pertracta- vit S. Hieronymus: cujus verba digna sunt, quæ hic legantur. Sic autem habet ad v.14. Quando au- tem dicitur; dabit Dominus ipse nobis signum; no- vum debet esse atque mirabile. Sin autem juvencula vel puella, ut Judæi volunt, & non virgo pariat, qua- le signum poterit appellari, cum hic nomen ætatis sit, non integritatis? --- Porro Alma apud nos verbum ambiguum est; dicitur enim & adolescentula, & ab- scondita, id est, ἀπόκρυφος. ---- Ergo Alma non so- lum puella vel virgo, sed cum ἐπιτάσει, virgo abscon- dita dicitur & secreta, quæ nunquam virorum patue- rit adspectibus, sed magna parentum diligentia custo- dita sit. Lingua quoque Punica, quæ de Hebræorum fontibus manare dicitur, proprie virgo alma appella- tur. ----- Et quantum cum mea pugno memoria, nun- quam me arbitror Alma in muliere nupta legisse, sed in ea, quæ virgo est, ut non solum virgo sit, sed virgo ju- nioris ætatis, & in annis adolescentiæ: Potest enim fie- ri, ut virgo sit vetula, ista autem virgo erat in annis puellaribus: vel certe virgo, non puella, & quæ ad- huc virum nosse non posset, sed jam nubilis. Quod è lo- cis Gen. XXIV. 43. Exod. II. 8. Ps. LXVIII. 26. Cant. I. 3. ipsi constare videtur.

Quid quod quarto diserte loquatur Propheta de VIRGINE, non quæ conceptura sit, postquam marito juncta fuerit, de quo nihil hic habetur, sed quæ & VIRGO, & jam prægnans sit. ECCE VIR- GO CONCIPIT, vel prægnans est. Verbum e- nim הרה præteriti temporis est, non futuri: vel cer- te est participium, uti sequens ילדת, ut ita designe- tur virgo prægnans & pariens: quia omnia Deo præ- sentia sunt. Non ergo id respicitur, quod acces- surus sit Propheta ad virginem, & ex illa filium su- scepturus; sed indigitat virginem prægnantem: quæ & virgo sit, & prægnans vel gravida. Quod ad- versus Judæos urget B. Lutherus l. de Schem-Ham- phorasch f. 130. Zum andern spricht Esaias, daß sol- che Alma schwanger sey, und das sol ein Wunder und Zeichen seyn. Spricht nicht, Sie wird schwan- ger werden, wie etliche Rabinen gerne gedeutet hät- ten. Sie müssen sich schämen für ihre eigen Gram- matica, denn הרה heist concepit, est prægnans. Sie ist schwanger, sie hat empfangen. Aber doch wollen sie sich da hinaus drehen, daß der Prophet habe in sei- nem Alter ein jung Mägdlein genommen, un sie ge- schwängert; Darauff sahe er an, und spricht: Si- he, die Alma ist schwanger, und wird einen Sohn gebähren. Daß also die Meynung sey, das ist nicht das Zeichen, daß die Alma schwanger ist, das hat der Prophet schon ausgericht, der ist ihr Mann, son- dern daß sie einen Sohn und nicht ein Mägdlein gebieret, Wem wollen wir nun gläuben? GOtt spricht, das sol ein Zeichen seyn, daß die Alma schwanger ist. Der Jüde spricht, o nein, Gott leugt, das ist kein Zeichen, weil der Prophet die Alma ge- schwängert hat. Also haben wir hie zween Text. Der Text Esaia stehet hell und klar da, Gott wird euch ein Zeichen geben, sihe, die Alma ist schwanger, 2c. Aber der Jüden Text ist dieser: Sihe, die Alma hat einen Mann, und ist schwanger vom Propheten da wird euch Gott ein Zeichen geben, daß sie einen

Sohn wird gebähren, und nicht eine Tochter. Hæc Megalanders adversus Judæos. Quæ Grotium etiam stringunt, utpote qui cum Judæis etiam mallet in textu legi, Concipiet, imo hic contra leges Gram- maticæ reddidit verbum præteritum in futuro, ut ad futuram imprægnationem Prophetissæ abripe- ret. Quod probe intellexêre Judæi, in præterito reddendum esse; ideo de muliere Prophetæ jam gravida explicant; neque potest in eo signum po- ni, quod Alma à Propheta imprægnata fuerit; quid enim in eo novum, vel tam magnifica Pro- phetæ oratione de admirando signo dignum? At cum verba, uti sonant, accipiuntur, de VIRGINE PRÆGNANTE, miraculum ingens, quemad- modum antea monitum, aperte exhibent. Quin- to He Hajediah etiam observandum, quod demon- strat voce העלמה virginem non certam aliquam, quia nulla designari poterat isto tempore; sed singularem quandam, qualis erat Maria, mater Immanuelis. Agnovit id itidem Socinus in lect. Sacr. p. 54. Ex quo consequitur, nihil absurdi esse, si hoc in loco litera illa non certam aliquam puellam si- gnificet, sed singularem quandam, ut certe singularis fuit Maria, mater Jesu. Imo videtur dicendum, signi- ficationem illam istius literæ, ut scil. rem aliquam no- tam ac certam indicet, vix habere locum in vatici- natione ista, & in verbo illa Alma, cui præposita est. Nam neq; ullius juvenculæ antea mentio ulla facta erat, nec, ad quamcunque tandem nomen illud referatur, pro tempore illo, quo Prophetia ista edita est; sive illa sit ea, cum qua congressus est Propheta, sive quæcunque alia, non apparet ulla ratione, quomodo illa nota & certa fuerit, ut ad eam sensus iste, ut ita dicam, relati- vus atque indicativus ejus literæ, accommodari possit.

Sexto is, de cujus conceptione & nativitate hic agitur, vocandus, h. e. reipsa futurus erat Imma- "nuel. Sic enim interpretatur ipse Grotius: Certe in- "quit, qui Prophetas non supine legit, nescire non "potest vocatum iri aliquo nomine dici ab illis eum "etiam, qui non eo vocis sono sit appellandus, sed "cujus rebus celebrandis vox ista conveniat. Loca "passim occurrunt Es.1,26. 9,6. 56,7.60,14.62,4. Jer. "3,17. & 23,6. Ezech. 48,35. Zach. 8,3. Ideo ubi Es. "14, 20. est יקרא, Chaldæus habet יתקים manebit: "& Lucas citans dictum locum, Es. 56, 7. יקרא vertit "ἕξιν 19,46. Tale est infra Ναζαραῖος κληθήσε "& υἱοὶ θεῦ κληθήσονται; Ubi & similem Philo- "nis locutionem citabimus. At nec Filius Esaiæ, nec quisquam alius ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος revera est עמנואל, hoc est, nobiscum Deus. Nomine enim hoc infertur divinæ & humanæ naturæ unio; quod Grotius agnoscit, si non restricta atque limitata, sed perfectior vocis significatio attendatur. At posterio- re eam esse accipiendam Angelus docuit Matth. 1. neque negat Grotius. Restricte autem & limita- te quoque intellig endam esse, unde probabitur? Repugnat id legibus τῆς ἑρμηνείας, quæ unam vo- cem non nisi unam significationem in eodem loco habere docent. Nec ullum in S. literis ea restri- cta significatio habet fundamentum. Adhæc si id notaret vox illa, quod Deus ipse adesse illosque be- nigne respicere & adjuvare velit, uti Grotius expli- cat, non filio illi, quem sibi fingit Grotius, Pro- phetæ nomen id erit proprium, sed omnibus con- veniet, quibus Deus adesse gratiose voluit, imo a- liis non paucis potiori ratione vendicandum erit, quibus nempe magis opem suam probavit Deus, uti sunt Moses, Josua, David, Ezechias, alii. Unde ne admissa quidem illa jejuna interpretatione, quam à Socino hausit, quod Immanuel notet præsen- tem Dei favorem, peculiariter vendicari potuit id nomen Esaiæ filio: quum ipsi, aut etiam populo

Judaico tam singularis, & tam insignis gratia non obtigerit, ut prae aliis quibusvis temporibus no- men Immanuel tum alicui ob favorem & auxilium Dei singulare imponendum & appropriandum fuerit. Quod fatetur etiam Socinus p. 44. Cum pax illa & quies, quae fuit in terra Juda, post vastationes illas Regum Syriae & Israëlis, de quibus ibi nominatim agitur, nec non postea etiam Regis Assyriae, fuerit ad- modum brevis ac dubia, vix videtur ullo modo pro- pter rem ejusmodi tantum, nisi aliud quidpiam subes- set, puero illi indi debere nomen istud Immanuel, quod significat aperte ac simpliciter praesentem Dei favorem atque auxilium. Notanda etiam hic συνέχεια, de qua praeclare Cyrillus: Pariet igitur, ait, filium & tu, ô domus David, quae nunc, inquit, renuis Deo credere si- gnumq; ab eo postulare ad confirmationem eorum, quae promissa sunt, propterea quod magis idolis addicta sis, vocabis nomen ejus Emmanuel, h. e. confiteberis, Deum in humana forma apparuisse. Quum enim apparuit secundum nos unigenitus Dei Sermo, tunc etiam nobiscum factus est. Qui enim supra omnem creaturam fuit, factus est nobis similis. Digna quo- que observatu sunt, quae Hieronymus hic habet, qui pariter verbum קראת ad domum David refert, & de invocatione nominis Immanuel explicat. Ergo iste puer, qui nascetur ex virgine ô Domus David, nunc à te appelletur Emmanuel, id est, nobiscum Deus, quia rebus ipsis probabis, à duobus inimicis regibus liberata, Deum te habere praesentem: & qui postea vocabitur Jesus, id est, Salvator, eo quod u- niversum hominum genus salvaturus sit, nunc à te Emmanuelis appelletur vocabulo. Et postea: Et est sensus, ô domus David, cui Dei sermone praecipitur, ut voces, id est, invoces in periculo constituta nomen Emmanuelis, id est, nobiscum Dei: non mireris ad rei novitatem, si virgo Deum pariat, qui tantam ha- beat potestatem, ut multo post tempore nasciturus te nunc liberet invocatus: ipse est enim, qui visus est A- braham, & locutus est Mosi.

Septimo Immanueli isti tribuitur terra Judaea, ceu propria Es. 8, 8. Et erit extensio alarum ejus ple- nitudo latitudinis TERRAE TUAE ô Immanuel. Hoc vero de filio Esaiae nullatenus dici potest. Num enim regnum & terra Juda filii Prophetae possessio fuit? Nimirum Immanuel constituitur à Propheta Dominus legitimus Judaeae, in quam nullum dominium obtinuit Filius Prophetae; nec alius quisquam isto tempore, cujus terra Judaea fuerit, extitit sub devastationem Judaeae à Sanalie- ribo factam praeter Ezechiam, quem vero per pue- rum hic promissum intelligi non posse, & Grotius, & quem ille sequutus est, Socinus ultro largiun- tur, imo invicto argumento probant: quia Eze- chias jam tum natus, & vel novem annorum erat, cum haec promissio fieret. Adscribam verba So- cini, quum liber non sit facile obvius: Quod qui- dam, quemadmodum Justinus in colloquio cum Trypho ne Judaeo de ipsis Judaeis sui temporis affirmat, ajunt puerum illum, qui Immanuel vocari debebat, esse Ezechiam, Achazi, qui tunc regnabat, filium, un- de consequeretur, merito ac proprie terram Juda il- lius esse, dictum fuisse, cum is ejus terrae Rex fuerit, id nullo modo admitti potest. Quandoquidem cum E- zechias regnare coepit, jam annorum 25. erat. Achaz vero cujus tempore praedictio ista facta est, regnum per sedecim tantum annos tenuerit, adeo ut etiamsi velimus in ipso regni Achazi initio, ut quidem verisi- mile est, ista praedicta fuisse, necesse futurum sit, ut Ezechias, qui statim Rex post Patris mortem extitit, tunc jam novem annos natus esset, cum ipsa prae- dictio est facta. Quomodo igitur Ezechias is puer es- se potuit, qui post praedictionem istam est natus. Quis ergo alius intelligi potest, cujus Judæa terra fit pro- pria præter Christum, de quo Ef. IX. dicitur, quod principatus ejus nullus sit finis? Fatetur fane ipse Hæ- reticorum antesignanus F.Socinus, non nisi impro- prie filio Esaiæ hoc ἀξίωμα competere. Chri- sto autem proprie convenire non negat. Jam qua ratione, inquit, dici poterit, nisi satis improprie, ter- ram Judæ fuisse illius puelli de Prophetissa nati? vel quid attinebat istam apostrophen facere ad eum, qui vocandus erat Immanuel, si is puellus ille Prophetæ fi- lius futurus esset? At ne improprie quidem terra Judæ filii Prophetæ erat, cui nullum plane in Ju- dæam sive proprium, sive improprium, sive di- rectum, sive indirectum Dominium convenit. Unde Judæorum nonnulli cum R. David Kimchi ex his verbis: Terra tua Immanuel; colligunt, puerum hunc esse filium Regis Achaz. Huc facit, inquit Kimchi, quod dicitur cap. 8, 8. implebit lati- tudinem terræ tuæ Immanuel, nempe eo, quod Regis filius esset. Sed Ezechias filius ejus, ad quem terræ dominium pertinebat, jam pridem natus ei erat, ideoque nativitas ejus hic promissa dici nequit, neque unquam Immanuel nuncupatus fuit. Re- stat ergo, ut de Messia intelligamus vaticinium, cu- jus terra, & universa ejus latitudo, & plenitudo e- rat. Cui Propheta tanquam supremo Domino & Judici quæritur, quod Exercitus Assyriorum alas suas extendat super terram ipsius.

Octavo Immanueli tribuitur dissipatio consi- liorum & confœderationum variorum populo- rum, ut adversus tam potentes hostes confidenter populus Dei citra pavorem ac timorem agere ac gloriari possit, ob hunc hyperaspisten suum Im- manuel. Congregamini populi & vincimini: & au- dite universæ procul terræ. Confortamini & vinci- mini, inite consilium, & dissipabitur; loquimini ver- bum, & non fiet: quia IMMANUEL, Ef. 8, 9. 10. Cui hoc mortalium tribui potest? & quis tum e- rat, cujus viribus cum ista παῤῥησίᾳ adversus quasvis molitiones & consilia quævis, etiam clan- destina & occulta, potentissimorum hostium niti potuerint? Unde concludimus: Is indigitatur hoc nomine Immanuel, in quo confidere poterant Ju- dæi adversus quasvis molitiones, qui consilia & fœdera hostium quorumvis dissipare facillime po- terat. At hoc non Esaiæ, non Regis filius, non ul- lus alius mortalium, sed solus Messias virginis fi- lius, utpote qui idem Dei filius est, Deus magnus & fortis, Jehovah Zebaoth, præstare potuit. Huic soli confidendum erat; hic solus pavor & timor & Sanctificatio ipsis esse debuit.

Unde nono oppositio probe notanda, quæ in- stituitur inter hostes, quos metuere poterat popu- lus, & inter hunc hyperaspisten ipsorum, qui so- lus ipsorum pavor esse debebat, qui Jehovah Ex- ercituum dicitur, ut manifestum adeo sit, quod Im- manuel ille non sit ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, sed sit ipse Jehovah exercituum. Non dicatis: Conjuratio; omnia enim, quæ loquitur populus iste, conjuratio est: & timorem ejus ne timeatis, neque paveatis. Dominum exercituum ipsum sanctificate, ipse pavor vester, & ipse terror vester. Et erit vobis in sanctifi- cationem: In lapidem autem offensionis & in petram scandali duabus Domibus Israël, in laqueum & invi- diam habitantibus Jerusalem. Quis hic non videt, ut ante Immanuel opponebatur hostibus, ceu dis- sipator consiliorum & machinationum ipsorum, & sospitator populi: Sic eundem nunc opponi iis- dem ceu Jehovam Exercituum, qui solus populi pa- vor & terror esse debeat, sub cujus præsidio ipse pavcre ac timere hostes opus minime habeat, sed ab iisdem securus esse possit: modo hunc Domi- num Immanuel metuat, atque sanctificet.

Quod decimo etiam confirmat Novi Test. explicatio. Quod enim Messias ille sit, qui hic ceu Dominus Exercituum metuendus ac sanctifican- dus proponitur, haut obscure liquet è Luc. 2. 34. Rom. 9, 32. 1. Pet. 2, 6. Argumentamur ita: Is, qui incredulis est in lapidem offenfionis, & petram scan- dali, in laqueum & ruinam, fidelibus autem in san- ctificationem, est Jehovah exercituum, qui Judæis solus debebat esse pavor & terror, quo niti pote- rant & debebant adversus hostes, ne timeant eo- rum consilia & machinationes. At Christus est is, qui incredulis est in lapidem offensionis & petram scandali, in laqueum & ruinam; fideli- bus autem in sanctificationem, teste Simeone Luc. 2. Ecce positus est hic in ruinam & in resurrectionem multorum; & Paulo Rom. 9. Israël, sectando legem justitia in legem justitia non pervenit: Quare? quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex operibus. Offenderunt enim in lapidem offensionis & petram scandali, & omnis, qui credit in eum, non confundetur; (Es. 28, 26. qui locus nostro parallelus est) & Petro 1. Epist. 2. ad quem accedentes (Christum indigitat) lapidem vi- vum, ab hominibus quidem reprobatum, à DEO au- tem electum & honorificatum.--- Propter quod con- tinet Scriptura: Ecce, pono in Sion lapidem sum- mum angularem, electum, pretiosum: & qui cre- diderit in eum, non confundetur. Vobis igitur ho- nor credentibus: non credentibus autem lapis, quem reprobarunt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput angu- li, & lapis offensionis, & petra scandali. Concludi- mus itaque: Ergo Christus est Jehovah Exerci- tuum, qui solus Judæis esse debebat pavor & ter- ror, quo adversus hostes eorumque consilia & machinationes niti poterant & debebant.

Undecimo neque id omnino negligendum, quod diçatur Virgo illa filium suum vocatura Imma- nuel. Quum enim alias ὀνομαθεσία liberorum competat Patri apud Ebræos, Gen. 16, 15. cap. 21, 3. quid causæ est, cur matri hic tribuatur filii sui de- nominatio, nisi quod ipse futurus sit ἀπάτωρ, & nasciturus è matre virgine. Si enim Haalmah marito copulata intelligeretur, maritus utique no- men imponeret filio, non ipsa Haalmah. Atque ita Angelus Mariæ Virgini ὀνομαθεσίαν filii tribuit Luc. 1, 31. Paries filium, & vocabis nomen ejus Jesum. Robur accedit argumento, si observetur, quod nulla plane hic viri mentio facta, quod notavit Oecolampadius in h. l. Animadverte, quod nulla hic viri sit mentio, & mos scripturæ est, ut viro genera- tio adscribatur. Nam si Jesaiæ fuisset uxor, dixisset: Ecce, uxor tibi pariet filium; - sicut de Abraham legimus: Sara uxor tibi pariet filium. Hic autem omnia tribuuntur virgini, quod prægnans sit, quod pariat, quod vocet nomen ejus.

Duodecimo ergo Angelica annunciatio, si cum præsenti vaticinio conferatur, digito velut ex- erto demonstrat Haalmah, hanc virginem, quam designarat Propheta: Ne timeas, Maria, invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum. Ecce concipies in utero, & paries filium, & vocabis nomen ejus Jesum. Quod Propheta dixit, ECCE, VIRGO CONCEPIT; id angelus interpretatus est: ECCE, TU VIRGO CONCIPIES. Quod Propheta: ECCE, VIRGO PARIET FILIUM; id Angelus, ECCE, TU VIRGO PARIES FILIUM. Quod Propheta: VIRGO VOCABIT NOMEN FILII ILLIUS SUI IMMANUEL; id Angelus, TU VIRGO MARIA VOCABIS FILII TUI NOMEN JE- SUM. Quid evidentius, quam quod docuerit ita Angelus, Prophetam locutum esse non de virgine nupta, sed de virgine pura de Alma, quæ non cognovit virum, uti Maria de se loquitur: quodq; testatus sit, nullam aliam virginem, quam Mariam, nullum aliu filium virginis, quam Jesum indicari à Propheta?

Decimo tertio, si quis in tanta luce adhuc am- bigat, Sp. S. omne dubium eximere voluit, cum de- scripsit revelationem Josepho factam de nativita- te Jesu, filii virginis. Remisit enim ad Propheticum hoc vaticinium, quo aperte testatur, quod illa eo- dem prædicta fuerit Matth. 1, 22. Hoc autem to- tum factum est, ut adimpleretur, quod dictum est à Do- mino per Prophetam dicentem: Ecce, virgo in utero habebit & pariet filium, & vocabunt nomen ejus Immanuel, quod est interpretatum, Nobiscum Deus. Quis jam glossæ Sociniano-Grotianæ locus, quod Propheta non de virgine pura, secundum sensum li- teralem & primo obvium, loquutus sit, non de Ma- ria Christipara, sed de Uxore Esaia: non de Jesu, filio virginis, sed filio nescio quo Esaiæ è conjugio procreato; siquidem Angelus ipse haud obscure Propheticum vaticinium designet, perinde uti fa- ctum in annunciatione Gabrielis, ad Mariam lega- ti, Luc. 1. adeoque è vaticinio Prophetico Jose- phum solicitum de Mariæ Sponsæ imprægnatione ita informet, ut nullus ipsi superesse scrupulus pos- sit, nulla dubia de virgine illæsa virginitate ute- rum gerente: vel certe ita nos informat Evangeli- sta, si quis hæc ab angelo adducta haud admittat. Si autem Propheta de virgine à se ducenda, & è συνουσία sua conceptura ullatenus (ne dicam sensu proprio & literali) egisset, nequicquam Josepho scrupulus ademptus, quin dubitatio & sollicitudo ejus multis modis aucta fuisset. Quid? quod ex eo liquere videatur, quod isto tempore in populo Dei neutiquam intellectum fuerit oraculum de Esaia- na conjuge: nec ita in angelica annunciatione vir- go ipsa, aut Josephus Sponsus ejus, per remissio- nem ad oraculum Propheticum certiores reddi aut confirmari potuissent in fide, neque Evangelista simpliciter ita testatus fuisset, impletum in eo fuis- se vaticinium Propheticum. Id certe manifestum est, quod juxta intentionem & mentem Sp. Sancti, qui & per Prophetam locutus, & per Evangelistam fui ipsius interpres infallibilis unice est, non de Conjuge, aut filio Esaiæ, sed de Maria virgine illi- bata, ejusque filio Jesu vaticinium intelligi debeat. Quod autem oraculum de virgine uterum gerente ejusque filio, Sp. Sancto teste, impletum est in vir- gine innupta, è Spiritu Sancto uterum gerente, sine congressu viri, in Maria θεοτόκῳ, ejusq; filio Jesu, populi sui Salvatore, id NULLO, NULLO MO- DO intelligi aut explicari potest, juxta senten- tiam quidem & mentem Sp. Sancti, de tali virgine, quæ non nisi nuptui data, per συνουσίαν maritalem imprægnata est, aut de filio Prophetæ, vel alterius cujusdam. Neque sicco pede hic prætereundum, quod Angelus Luc. 1. & Evangelista Matth. 1. no- mina illa ceu ἰσοδυναμοῦντα accipiant Immanuel & Jesus, non quod simpliciter æquipolleant, sed κα- τά. Quia nomen Immanuel Deum nobiscum fore infert, non per nudam παράστασιν, & gratiosam as- sistentiam, sed ita, ut Deus nostræ naturæ consors futurus, nosque salvaturus sit; adeoque nomen est & personæ & officii. Deum nobiscum fore naturæ nostræ assumtione vel communione, nostrique liberatio- ne ac Salvatione. Ut enim Deus, cum adesse ali- cui dicitur, eidem non tantum præsto est, sed etiam opitulatur, ut ne tunc quidem nuda παρουσία, sed etiam ἐνέργεια & operatio divina inferatur: ita quum innuatur hic personali unione naturæ no- stræ sese copulaturus, gratia, opitulatio ac salus, quam illa hypostatica præsentia & conjunctione allaturus est, simul designatur. Ut ergo nomen Jesu primo quidem designat officium, sed suppo- nit ac connotat tamen personam θεάνθρωπον, cui to- li hoc officium convenit: Sic nomen Immanuel primo designat personam θεάνθρωπον, subinsert au- tem simul finem unionis personalis divinæ & hu- manæ naturæ, reconciliationem Dei, & hominis, ac reductionem hominis ad Deum, adeoque salvatio- nem generis humani. Unde eo ipso, quo Christus Jesus, h. e. Salvator, est, Immanuel quoque est ra- tione personæ, quia nemo salvare à peccatis pote- rat, nisi Deus & homo Immanuel. Idem talis ra- tione officii, quia Deum nobis, & nos Deo conciliat. Est ergo Christus Jesus, h. e. Salvator & Immanuel simul, quia Salvator est per reunionem & reconcilia- tionem nostri cum Deo. Siquidem Propheta non præcise significare voluerit, quomodo Christus nominandus, sed quis revera & qualis futurus esset, quod supra agnovit Grotius. Quum ergo idem sit Immanuel, quod Jesus, quantum ad rei significatæ veritatem, quoad personam & officium, manifestum est, non posse hoc oraculum ullatenus de filio E- saiæ intelligi, qui neque vocatus unquam est Im- manuel, neque Immanuel quoad rei veritatem, aut Jesus fuit vel esse potuit: sed perinde nomen Im- manuel uni Christo convenire, uti nomen Jesus. Unde sententia illa, de filio Esaiæ Christi typo, jam pridem à sanctis Patribus atro carbone notata, & rejecta fuit. Judaizare illum, qui ita statuit, S. Hie- ronymus pronunciavit ad hunc locum p. 34. Qui- dam de nostris Judaizans Esaiam Prophetam duos fi- lios habuisse contendit, Jasub & Emmanuel: Et Em- manuel de Prophetissa uxore ejus esse generatum, in typum Domini Salvatoris: ut prior filius Jasub, quod interpretatur relictus sive convertens, Judai- cum populum significet, qui relictus est, & postea reversus. Secundus autem, id est, Emmanuel & nobis- cum Deus, gentium vocationem: postquam verbum caro factum est, & habitavit in nobis. Et ad c. 8, 18. unde miror, quendam nostrorum pueros istos duos E- saiæ filios intelligere, quos de Prophetissæ mulieris con- ceptione generarit: Jasub videlicet & Emmanuel, quorum prior in abjectione prioris populi, sequens in assumptione gentium præcesserit. Quod qui recipit, consequenter & Osee Prophetam vere meretricem u- xorem habuisse affirmabit. Hæc Hieronymus.

Accedant argumentis hisce nunc etiam postre- mo loco testimonia, quæ ab ipsis Judæis aliisque ἐξ ἐναντίας peti possunt. Nam è Judæis non tantum 72. Seniores per vocem Alma intellexêre puram virginem, cum reddidere, non uti Symmachus & Theodotio, in Judæorum favorem, νεανις adolescen- tula, sed ἡ παρθένος, quæ vox virginem puram no- tat. Unde versionem illam urget Irenæus lib. 3. cap. 24. Sed & Aquila reddidit ἀπόκρυφον abscon- ditam, & Chaldæus uterque, Onckelos, & Jonathan עלמתא virginem interpretantur: ne de eo dicam, quod R. Hakkadosh, è voce עלמת per Cabalam eruere conetur nomen מרים Mariæ. R. David Kimchi negat, de uxore Prophetæ intelligendam esse vocem; Etenim si fuisset uxor Prophetæ, dixisset Prophetissam, quemadmodum dicitur, & accessit ad Prophetissam. Huc facit, quod dicitur cap. 8. 8. im- plebit latitudinem terræ tuæ Immanuel. Sic ergo discrepant ipsi Judæi sententiis, nec inveniunt, in qua acquiescant. Nonnullis de Ezechia expli- cantibus, quos è Chronologia refellit R. Salomo: Aliis de filio Esaiæ cum R. Salomone & Aben-Ezra, quos, uti dixi, R. David Kimchi refutat: Kim- chi de quadam Achazi puella, vel uxore, ejus- que filio interpretante, de quo vero nuspiam in Scriptura verbum legitur. In abscondito quodam Judæorum libro hanc inveniri senten- tiam, quod puella quædam nondum matura viro conceperit & peperit, idq́; tanquam peculiare signum propositum fuerit, Helvicus disp. 14. t. 9. Giess. p. 32. testatur: quam etiam allegat R. Salomo. Porro alii signum in eo fuisse dicunt, quod de fœtu ado- lescentulæ statim post conceptionem Propheta certum prædicere potuerit, quod masculus esset. R. Aben-Ezra & R. David Kimchi in eo, quod in- fans vix editus statim butyrum & mel comederit, & noverit reprobare (cibum) malum, & eligere bonum, sive dulcem. Ita sententiis fluctuare, & ad in- eptias varias confugere oportet, qui certam Sp. S. sententiam relinquunt. Socinus fatetur, nullo pa- cto tempori Prophetæ convenire mirabile illud, quod hic prædicitur, aut uxori Prophetæ, quod ita probat: Satis est, inquit lect. sacr. f. 44. ad omnem rem mi- rabilem in conceptu & partu uxoris Prophetæ exclu- dendam id, quod ibi (cap. 8.) diserte narratur, Pro- phetam videlicet ad illam accessisse, quæ verba sine dubio honeste significant illum cum ea rem habuisse. Fatetur etiam non nisi improprie satis terram Juda fuisse illius puelli è Prophetissa nati: & geminum illum suum sensum de filio Prophetæ, & de Christo non potuit salvare, quin ad desperatæ causæ asy- lum profanum se reciperet, Deum in prædictioni- bus suis consuevisse obscure loqui, uti Diabolus in re- sponsis, quæ apud Ethnicos dare consuevit, obscure locutus est, qui proinde obscuritate illa hominibus non imperitis neque rerum divinarum penitus ignaris fa- cile persuaserit, responsa illa divina esse, ut inde, quod prædictiones ipsius obscuræ essent, & ad plures sensus accommodari possent, quemadmodum & ipsæ divinæ prædictiones, Loxias appellatus sit. Huc tandem redit illud amphiboliarum & æquivocationum de S. literis ἔγκλημα!

In Schola Calvini Musculum suum itidem & typum in hoc oraculo constituentem, quum pro- mittatur à Deo puer aliquis tum temporis nascitu- rus ex puella juvencula, sed ex congressu viri: & antitypum, quatenus simul eodem figuretur hic MESSIAS, refellit Fr. Spanhemius part. 1. Dubior. Evangel. Dub. 34. p. 296. Quid, inquit, miracu- losi in eo, vel extraordinarii proponi poterat populo, puellam è viro concepturam & parituram? Accedit & hoc, tantam Achazi impietatem fuisse, ut, si qui- dem puellam aliquam in individuo designasset Pro- pheta, omnibus modis operam daturus fuisset, ne cum ullo congrederetur, multo magis ne ex se conci- peret, vel saltim, ne fœtus ejus molliter educaretur, ne sua oraculo Prophetico constaret veritas. Imo hic nullum prorsus remedium incredulitati Judæo- rum, vel Achazi allatum fuisset. Nam incertum esse poterat æque hoc promissum, ac prius de eorum libera- tione, donec eventu ipso comprobaretur I. partus post aliquot menses. II. Educatio ejus post annorum ali- quot decursum; & antequam hoc fieret, animi eo- rum relinquebantur suspensi & anxii de sui conserva- tione. Certa vero erat promissio de Messia, de qua dubitare nefas erat, & quam ne ipse quidem Achaz palam in dubium vocare audebat, utpote in qua pro- ram & puppim sua gloriationis & spei constituebant Judæi. Adde sic obscurari non parum eximium illud privilegium Messiæ, illum nimirum solum nascitu- rum ex עַלְמָה virgine. Quin & applicatio Matthæi hoc modo in dubium vocari posset: Promptum enim erit excipere Judæis, in præcipuis faltem debere dari conformitatem inter tympum & antitypum. At hoc ex præcipuis esse ex עַלְמָה concipi. Si ergo typus non fue- rit natus ex עַלְמָה virgine, probationem nullam soli- dam dari posse, Messiam debere nasci ex virgine. Et sic & scopus & applicatio Matthæi, & singularis Mes- siæ prærogativa conciderent. Imo, cum innumeri in Judæa pueri in lucem tum temporis edi potuerint, pa- ra- cate educari, & superstites esse interitui Regum illorum, quid peculiare ad convictionem Achazi & Judæorum incredulorum peti poterat ex ejusmodi partu, ubi ni- hil singularis, nec eximii præ aliis. Hæc & alia plu- ra ibidem Spanhemius. Musculus ipse, etsi non temere se rejicere illam sententiam, quod hoc ora- culum de Messia non literali sensu, sed typice tan- tum agat, profiteatur, ad eam tamen interpreta- tionem cunctanter se accedere ait. Salmeronem, qui pariter geminum sensum hic fingit, alii è Pontifi- ciis refutant. Tirinus notat, Haalmah nuspiam in Scripturis pro alia puella, quam virgine & a viro in- tacta sumi: ac vaticinium hic Esaiæ de conceptione Christi in utero virginali Mariæ DE FIDE ESSE, ex Matth. 1, 22. ut fas non sit Christianis de hoc dubi- tare. Conf. etiam Esaias in h. l.

Neque vero est, quod dicas, non potuisse à Propheta Messiæ nativitatem Achazo signum libe- rationis constitui, utpote quæ aliquot seculis post i- psum sequuta demum est; Ideoque ut ratio signi dati sibi constet, & Judæorum scrupulis rectius satisfiat, typum ejusmodi constituendum esse. No- tandum enim non Achazo soli signum hic consti- tui; sed quum ille detrectaret per infidelitatem signum postulare, datum id esse, uti verba textus habent, domui Davidis toti: quæ non restringenda ad Esaiæ tempora: siquidem non ista solum ætate, sed per septem secula, usque ad nativitatem Christi domus Davidis, è qua Messias nasci debuit, Judæi cæteri, cumprimis vero inter ipsos, fideles & sancti erigendi ac confirmandi fuerint, de pro- missionum divinarum certitudine, ac complemen- to. Illud ergo gratiæ divinæ signum daturus erat in domo Davidis Dominus, quo omni ætate sem- per fideles sese erexerunt ac solati sunt: quodque hic domui Davidis promittitur; quod erat fructus benedictus ventris Mariæ virginis, per quem omnis obtingit gratia & benedictio, in quo & per quem omnes promissiones sunt etiam & amen, 2. Cor. 1. Ideo Cyrillus Alexandr. Comment. in Es. 1, 1. orat. 5. Re- nuente autem Achazo & perversissime dicente, non petam, neque tentabo Dominum, (attendit enim ma- gis vanorum vatum imposturis) sua sponte quodammo- do Deus ipse domui Davidis signum exhibuit. O- portebat enim, oportebat salutis per Christum præ- nunciationem fieri ad eos, qui ex familia erant Davi- dica, i. e. ex tribu Juda, de qua ortus est secundum carnem ipse Christus. Ex hoc ergo signo conclu- dere poterat domus Davidis, se neutiquam dele- tum iri ab hostibus, sed conservandam esse usque ad plenitudinem temporis; hoc signo etiam cer- tiores reddebantur, quia nova promissione ipsis id dabatur, novoque nomine Messias insigniebatur, de gratiosa Dei in præsenti necessitate assistentia & opitulatione: quod Filius Dei, qui è familia hac naturam humanam assumere vellet, illi etiam tum peculiariter succurrere eamque ab hostium peri- culis eripere dignaturus sit. Signum id erat potentiæ Dei, quum Achas minime crediderit, Deum ab ho- stium istorum Rezin & Pekaiah manu liberare Ju- dæos posse. Longe enim majus argumentum divi- næ potentiæ est, quod posteris & nepotibus ejus daturus erat Deus, excitaturus è virgine Messiam, & per eum à potentioribus hostibus, peccato, mor- te, inferno & Diabolo totum genus humanum li- beraturus; signum erat gratiæ divinæ opulatricis, quæ insigniori, magisque admirando argumento confirmari non poterat, quam exhibitione Mes- siæ, suo tempore præstanda, quem proinde ceu virginis filium è domo Davidis oriundum, & Im- manuel, Deum nobiscum, naturæ consortio & gra- tiæ auxilio, nova & illustri promissione pollicetur.

Non ergo obscurum est, quomodo promissio hæc Achazo fidem facere potuerit liberationis à duo- bus istis Regibus; quippe quæ non tantum majo- ris potentiæ experimentum sistebat, sed & funda- mentum erat conservationis Davidicæ, quæ tum vide- batur periclitari, si Hierosolyma in duorum illo- rumRegum infestissimorum manus traderetur,nec non omnium promissionum aliarum; q. d. Pro- pheta: Si Deus vobis aliquando daturus est quod majus est, quod difficilius est, quod stupendum prorsus & inauditum, ut virgo concipiat & pariat Immanuelem,quanto magis hoc, quod minus, vo- bis daturus est? Si Deus non saltem verax futurus est in exhibitione Messiæ, sed etiam potens satis in conservatione domusDavidicæ usque ad tempora Messiæ,verax utique & potens satis vobis etiam vi- deri debet in adimplenda promissione, à me pro- mulgata de conservatione & liberatione vestri è manu duorum illorum Regum; sic explicat Span- hemius. Quæ etiam Maldonati,Eman. Saa, Gabr. Vasquez, & aliorum est interpretatio. Si à majori illa vi atque exitio liberabit aliquandoDeus popu- lum oppressum, multo sane facilius id præstabit à duabus caudis titionum fumigantium. Et si ea fuit amoris vis in Deo, ut filium suum unigenitum da- ret, quomodo negaret alia, quæ infinitis spatiis leviora sunt. Quo facit Hornbeckii distinctio lib. 3. contra Judæos cap. 1. p. 227. Non figni exhibitio, at quidem ejus certa promissio potuit signum esse rei tum præstandæ. Quum quid Deus prædicit,propter e- jus infallibilitatem pro impleto non hic solum, sed & alibi passim habeatur atq; haberi merito debeat. Atque ideo etiam hicPropheta in præterito loqui- tur: Ecce, virgo CONCEPIT. Adde, quod gemi- num hic proponi signum nonnulli censeant cum Franc. Junio in Parall. lib. 1. part. 4. Alterum com- mune ad revincendam Achazi & Judæorum infide- litatem pertinens, promissionem nempe de Christo, quod Deus inde à principio Ecclesiæ dedit de se- mine mulieris, in quo omnes promissiones Etiam & Amen sunt; alterum specialius ad promissam li- berationem ab istis regibus peculiariter pertinens: quod Junius è vers.15. & 16. tradi vult; alii ad so- lum v.16. restringunt: nimirum pueruli pignoratio- nem: quod antequam ille reprobare malum, & eligere bonum noverit, Reges illi ex sua quisque terra & regno exterminandi sint. Prius signum desumeha- tur ex principiis primis religionis Judaicæ. Posterius in oculos incurrebat, ut ex omni parte inexcusabilis foret Achaz. Ut ait B. Sam. Bohl. Theologus Rosto- chiensis,amicus quondam meus perdilectusComment. moral. 3. Es. c. 10. p. 106. Quæ ideo conjuncta vi- deri possunt, ut nempe mutuo illa sese confirma- rent, ac de liberationis à Regibus & exterminiis eorundem veritate certiores redderentur Judæi per repetitam promissionem de semine mulieris: ac vice versa, ubi impletum viderint brevi libe- rationis illius promissum, in fide de adventu Mes- siæ simul hoc promisso stabilirentur. Neque ve- ro opus est, ut præcise signa confirmativa antece- dant tempore; quum sequantur nonnunquam,u- ti manifestum est Exod. 3, 12. in signo missionis Mosis ad eductionem populi, oblatione in mon- te post eductionem: qualia etiam leguntur 1. Sam. 2,34. c.10,2.1. Reg. 22,25.28.Es. 37,30. Jer.44,29.quæ signa ideo proponuntur, ut signorum futurorum promissione piorum fides & confirmetur simul, & simul exerceatur, ne verbo ipsius diffidant, ubi si- gno præsenti confirmatum non fuerit, Jos. 4, 48. in quam sententiam Grotius vers. 9. hujus 7. Capi- tis interpretatus est. An ideo non creditis, quia non confirmamini? Signo scilicet aliquo conspicuo. Quan- quam si recte rem expendamus, partus virgineus non sit spectandus, ut consequens signum, sed inde- finite, quod probe observavit Bohlius meus p. 52. Hoc est illud signum, quod non rogatus Deus regi A- chas seu domui David dedit, seu potius in memoriam revocavit. Hoc est illud signum, quod & ex cælo & inferis Deus conspicuum reddidit; & cum ne unam quidem ejusdem partem eligere vellet Achas, utramq; exhibuit Creator. Hoc est illud signum, quod facere debebat ad Hascheket, & veram fidem in eis, ubi ocu- lis conspicua omnia videntur esse erepta. Hoc est illud signum, quod testabatur non Deo illud, quod homini- bus, esse laborem. Hoc est illud signum, quod non ut futurum simpliciter & absolute, nec ut præteritum; sed ut indefinitum Christum Jesum heri, hodie, & cras, & in secula futurum Salvatorem designat. Quamvis enim futura prædicuntur, certo tamen re- spectu eâ fieri videmus: Hoc est illud signum, ad cu- jus memoriam contremiscis ô Sasan, vacillant portæ inferorum, & Jerusalem verum gaudet indefinen- ter. Nam signum est, quod ipse Dominus dabat, in- credulum Achas communibat, & fidelem Hiskiam confortabat. Quid? quod necessum etiam haut ap- pareat, ut verbum אות, cum Deus id se daturum promittit, de signo intelligatur; postquam signum Achaz ad mandatum Dei postulare per infidelita- tem detrectaret. Etsi enim idem nomen Deus ad- hibeat, nihil tamen obstare videtur, quo minus id generaliter nunc de re nova & stupenda accipiatur, q. d. Tu quidem in infidelitate tua persistis Rex, sed scias, tu cum tota domo Davidis, Deum ob veritatem suam & fideles, quos sibi servat in populo suo, & li- berationem illam, quam ex ore Dei annunciatam in dubium revocatis, impleturum & longe eminentius humanæque rationi multo incredibilius miraculum daturum, ut nempe virgo inter vos concipiat, & Deum ipsum pariat. Vid. Blasius Viegas in Ap. 12. & Barrad. T. 1. l. 8. c. 6. E quibus manifestum est, optime sibi constare oraculum, neq; opus esse, ut cum Judæis & Judaizantibus fingamus sensum lite- ralem de puero quodam tum nato in signum liberatio- nis. Ecquis vero persuaderi sibi patietur, Judæis satisfieri posse, cum in Judæorum itur sententiam? Annon ita gloriabuntur Apellæ, quod Christiani sibi herbam porrigant: inque sua reproba senten- tia confirmabuntur? Et quomodo convincentur de sensu ejusmodi typico, quod nempe hic puer fi- gura esse debuerit Messiæ, quum de eo penes Esai- am altum sit silentium: imo inconveniens sit, pue- rum in conjugio natum constitui typum filii nasci- turi ê pura virgine: ac Musculus ipse fateatur, ty- pis illis & umbris magis excæcari Judæos, quoniam veritatis lucem novo Testamento exhibitam non reci- piant. Merito itaq; Bohlius in Comment. ad h. l. p. 75. Iubemur ergo, adigimur, cogimur & impelli- mur, hæc omnia TANTUM simpliciter, pure & ab- solute referre ad Iesum Nazarenum virginis immacu- latæ filium, ut signo suum relinquatur pondus.

## 7:15
Vers. 15. BUTTER AND HONEY HE SHALL EAT] Sustenance will abound for him. He says this for this reason, because the Jews feared hunger for themselves from the siege.

THAT HE MAY KNOW TO REFUSE THE EVIL, AND CHOOSE THE GOOD] Translate from the Hebrew, until he knows, that is, until that boy has arrived at the use of reason. For those who are in early infancy are accustomed to be described by the ignorance of good and evil, Deut. 1, 39. Where we showed that Homer also speaks thus. Thus in the following chapter: Before the child shall know to call his father and his mother.

Concerning the son of Isaiah with the Jews, as I have said, Grotius explains these things again, because he had accepted the preceding oracle v. 14 concerning the same. Others, without prejudice to the preceding oracle, which is to be understood solely concerning the Messiah, maintain against the Jews, they grant that the present verse treats of the son of Isaiah, but one already born (not one about to be born) whom he had with him, and pointed out demonstratively. Thus Junius: Not even this boy (Shear-Jashub v. 3) will receive harm from those kings, but he will live, will be brought up in spite of them, and will grow up, and therefore by this sign let the kingdom of Judah be confirmed concerning its preservation. Then follows the amplification v. 16. Nay indeed, he says, those kings will have already perished before this boy begins to know. But that the eating of butter and honey pertains to the son of the virgin, the very coherence of the words teaches, and the pronoun suffix in the word לדעתו refers to him, to know him, or, that he (namely, the one of whom it was said before) may know to refuse the evil, nor does any other subject precede, and to drag back that הנער boy from the following verse is violent. Wherefore other interpreters almost all interpret the present verse also concerning the Son of the virgin. And Spanheim (P. I. Dubior. Evang. p. 293. §. Tametsi autem) refutes Junius here, although his name is suppressed. But what is that abundance of provisions, that so much milk and honey should still be available, from which an infant might otherwise be sustained? What of the fact that it cannot be proven that remarkable fertility followed even after many, let alone two, years? Whence the Grotian gloss enjoys almost no similarity. But the sign is truly stupendous, that IMMANUEL, GOD having put on our nature, should eat butter and honey, and that he himself should receive increase in the knowledge of good and evil. These things are certainly altogether to be wondered at concerning God, that he is fed and brought up, not in a phantastic body, or such as angels assumed, but in a true and proper one, like other infants, with milk and butter, with which infants weaned from mother's milk were commonly fed in the land of Canaan. But that an infant is fed with milk and honey is not new. But that the most high God should eat them is a miracle of miracles. Therefore Jerome connects these things with the preceding ones thus: Do not wonder, O house of David, at the novelty of the thing, if a virgin brings forth God, who has such power that, though about to be born at a much later time, he might now deliver you when invoked. For he is the one who was seen by Abraham, and spoke to Moses. I will say also another thing more wonderful: lest you think he is to be born in a phantasm, he will use the foods of infancy, he will eat butter and honey. Nor is it less to be wondered at that God grows as in age, so also in wisdom and piety: and thus progresses in the habitual gifts of soul and body, so that he may know to refuse the evil and choose the good. Which is read concerning Christ in Luke 2:40, 52. Although Jerome, and Cyril of Alexandria take this as an argument of divine wisdom, that while still wrapped in swaddling clothes and fed with butter and honey, he has judgment of good and evil, so that refusing evils, he may choose goods; so that through these words we may know that the infancy of the human body did not prejudice the divine wisdom. The former explanation, however, is simpler. Five things are thus designated in the Messiah: (1) True humanity: that he was not to have an imaginary body, which does not need food, as the Marcionites and Manichaeans dreamed, but a true and human one. (2) Customary education: that although that boy was conceived and born in a miraculous way, he was nevertheless to be brought up in the usual and common manner and with ordinary foods. (3) Native land. For since Judea is wont to be described in such a way that it flows with milk and honey, Exod. 3:8, 17, it is hinted by this agreement that the Messiah was to be born and brought up in Judea, as one who was to be brought up in the manner of other Jewish infants. (4) The mother's humble lot. Judea abounded with milk and honey, so that even men of the most humble lot among the Jews could nourish their children with such foods. And therefore it is tacitly hinted that he, although he was to be born from the Davidic house, would nevertheless come forth with his mother reduced to a humble state, and be fed by her in the common and humble manner. Let Isa. 7:22 be compared, where the humbleness of butter and honey also seems to be indicated. (5) Progress in habitual knowledge, that he had to grow like other men in age in acquired and experimental knowledge. Therefore, to the common mode of education, that he was to be fed with butter and honey, is joined the common increase of wisdom; so that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good. Not that such sustenance is the cause of knowledge, but that this will be the consequence, that one so sustained must grow not only in age and stature, but also in wisdom. There is therefore no reason why it should be translated with Grotius, until he knows to refuse the evil. Whose explanation hardly holds together: for if you explain it entirely concerning the abundance of provisions, did Judea abound with butter and honey only UNTIL Isaiah's son learned to refuse the evil? And what kind of such a remarkable promise is this, if divine blessing is not promised further than for two or three years? But our interpretation is well-founded: For butter and milk and honey are the food of infancy. But infants are cherished and brought up for this reason, not that they may learn gluttony, not that they may pursue impiety and iniquity, but that they may learn to flee evil, and to do good: that they may learn to know God, and to pursue the calling of God. This is the chief end of the education of infants; as Brentius rightly says.

Latin:

Vers. 15. BVTTVRM ET MEL COMEDET] Vi- ctus ei affluet. Hoc ideo dicit, quia ex obsidione famem sibi metuebant Judæi.

VT SCIAT REPROBARE MALVM, ET ELIGE- RE BONVM] Verte ex Hebræo, donec sciat, id est, donec is puer ad usum rationis pervenerit. Nam qui in prima sunt infantia, describi solent per ignorantiam boni & ma- li, Deut. 1, 39. Vbi ostendimus sic & Homerum loqui. Sic capite sequenti: Antequam sciat puer vocare patrem suum & matrem suam.

De filio Esaiæ cum Judæis, ut dixi, hæc iterum Grotius explicat, quia præcedens oraculum v. 14. de eodem acceperat. Alii, salvo præcedenti oracu- lo, quod unice de Messia intelligendum esse con- tra Judæos tuentur, versum præsentem de filio Esaiæ sed nato jam (non nascituro) quem secum habue- rit, & δεικτικῶς designarit, agere largiuntur. Ita Ju- nius: Ne puer quidem hic (Sear-Jasub v. 3.) damnum accipiet ab istis regibus, sed vivet, invitis illis educabi- tur, & grandescet, ac proinde hoc signo regnum Judæ de conservatione sua confirmatum esto. Deinde subjungitur amplificatio v. 16. Imo vero, inquit, jam Reges isti perierint, antequam hic puer incipiat sapere. Sed ad filium virginis pertinere illam comestione butyri & mellis, cohærentia ipsa verborum do- cet, & ad illum sese refert pronomen suffixum in voce לדעתו ad sciendum ipsum, vel, ut sciat ips (ille nempe, de quo antea dictum) reprobare ma- lum, neq; aliud præcedit subjectum, & retro trahe- re illud הנער puer è versu sequenti, violentum est. Quapropter alii Interpp. plerique omnes de Filio virginis versum etiam præsentem interpretantur. Et refellit Junium hic, licet suppresso nomine, Span- hemius P. I. Dubior. Evang. p. 293. §. Tametsi au- tem. Quæ vero illa est affluentia victus, quod tan- tum lactis ac mellis adhuc suppetat, ex quo infans alias sustentetur? quid? quod probari nequeat, insignem fertilitatem sequutam esse etiam post multos, nedum, duos annos. Unde nulla pene simi- litudine gaudet Grotiana glossa. Signum autem vere stupendum est, quod IMMANUEL, DEUS naturam nostram indutus butyrum & mel comedat, quodq; ipse in cognitione boni & mali incrementum capiat. Hæc certe de Deo prorsus admiranda sunt, quod non in corpore phantastico, aut qualia angeli assumsere, sed vero proprioque, instar aliorum infantum, cibetur, & educetur lacte & butyro, qui- bus infantes à lacte materno depulsi in terra Ca- naan communiter alebantur. Verum infantem la- cte & melle ali, novum non est. Sed Deum sum- mum illis vesci, miraculum miraculorum est. Ideo hæc ita connectit cum præcedentibus Hierony- mus: Non mireris, ô domus David, ad rei novita- tem, si virgo Deum pariat, qui tantam habeat pote- statem, ut multo post tempore nasciturus te nunc li- beret invocatus. Ipse est enim, qui visus est Abra- ham, & locutus est Mosi. Dicam & aliud mira- bilius: ne eum putes in phantasmate nasciturum, cibis utetur infantiæ, butyrum comedet & lac. Nec mi- nus mirandum est, quod Deus crescat ut ætate, ita etiam sapientia ac pietate: adeoque proficiat donis habitualibus animæ & corporis, ut sciat reprobare malum & eligere bonum. Quod de Christo legitur Luc. 2, 40. 52. Quamvis Hieronymus, & Cyrillus Alexandr. hoc accipiant ceu argumentum divinæ sapientiæ, quod pannis adhuc involutus & butyro pastus & melle, habeat boni malique judicium, ut reprobans mala, eligat bona; ut per hæc verba no- scamus, infantiam humani corporis divinæ non præ- judicasse sapientiæ. Prior tamen explicatio simpli- cior est. Designantur autem ita in Messia quinque: (1) Vera humanitas: quod non habiturus sit corpus imaginarium, quod cibis haud indiget, uti Mar- cionitæ & Manichæi somniarunt, sed verum & hu- manum. (2) Consueta educatio: quod etsi puer ille miraculoso modo conceptus & natus sit, more ta- men usitato & communi cibisq; ordinariis educan- dus sit. (3) Patria terra. Quum enim Judæa ita describi soleat, quod fluat lacte & melle, Exod. 3, 8. 17. innuitur hoc pacto, Messiam in Judæa nascitu- rum, & educandum esse, utpote qui more infan- tum Judæorum aliorum educandus. (4) Matris tenuis sors. Abundabat Judæa lacte & melle, ut vel tenuissimæ sortis homines inter Judæos ejusmodi cibis liberos suos nutrire potuerint. Ideoq; tacite innuitur, eum, etsi nasciturus sit è domo Davidica, matre tamen redacta in statum tenuem proditu- rum, ac communi, tenuique more ab ea alendum. Conferatur Ef. 7, 22. ubi etiam butyri & mellis te- nuitas indicari videtur. (5) Profectus in scientia habituali, quod cum ætate aliorum hominum in- star crescere debuerit acquisita & experimentali scientia. Ideo educationis modo communi, quod butyro & melle alendus sit, jungitur commune sa- pientiæ incrementum; ut sciat reprobare malum, & eligere bonum. Non quod sustentatio talis causa scientiæ, sed quod hoc consequens futurum sit, quod ita sustentatus non modo ætate & statura, sed etiam sapientia crescere debeat. Non ergo est, quod cum Grotio vertatur, donec sciat reprobare malum. Cu- jus explicatio vix sibi constat: nam si omnino de affluentia victus explices, num eo usque tantum Judæa butyro & melle affluebat, DONEC Esaiæ fi- lius disceret reprobare malum? Et quænam hæc tam insignis promissio, si ulterius non promittatur divina benedictio, quam ad biennium aut trien- nium? Bene autem se habet nostra interpretatio: Butyrum enim & lac & mel sunt cibus infantiæ. In- fantes autem idcirco foventur & educantur, non ut discant heluationes, non ut sectentur impietatem & iniquitatem, sed ut discant fugere malum, & facere bonum: ut discant cognoscere Deum, & sectari vo- cationem Dei. Hic est præcipuus finis educationis in- fantum; ut recte Brentius.

## 7:16
Vers. 16. THE LAND SHALL BE FORSAKEN, WHICH THOU ABHORREST, FROM THE FACE OF HER TWO KINGS] That is, those two kings of Syria and Israel will die. By the land, understand both; Pekah did not survive this time for three whole years:

We have said that here a second, more specific promise or document is proposed regarding the liberation of Judea from the power of two most hostile Kings, namely that both lands which the house of David now detested, that is, Ephraim and Syria, are soon to be abandoned by the face of their two Kings. Although most understand this as the death of the Kings, with Grotius, who both perished within three years, others explain it as the devastation of both lands, and others, with Leo Castalio, refer the same to the extreme desolation which befell the Jews from the Romans. Jerome leads the former, drawing an argument from the fact that Hezekiah cannot be understood by the 'little child,' but that Immanuel, the Son of the virgin, is indicated. This will likewise militate against Grotius's opinion regarding the son of Isaiah, if that explanation stands. In the sixth year of his reign, Hezekiah, says Jerome, Samaria was captured by the Assyrians, that is, in the thirty-first year of his own age. If, therefore, this one who is to be born, whether of a virgin, as we prove, or of a young woman, as the Jews wish, shall eat butter and honey, and shall be so small that he cannot discern evil from good, and before he passes the time of infancy, the land of Syria and Samaria is to be devastated by the Assyrians, let the Hebrews answer how Hezekiah is predicted to be an infant at thirty-one years of age, and of such a crude age that, eating honey and butter, like the children of Nineveh, he knew neither left nor right, that is, neither evil nor good. But related to Immanuel, which is interpreted as 'God with us,' it will have an easy understanding. Because by the mystery and the invocation of his name, the land of Syria and Samaria is devastated by the conquering Assyrian, and the house of David is liberated from the two Kings whom it feared, namely Rezin and Pekah. These are his words.

Furthermore, it is not necessary that we understand the word הַנַּעַר as referring to the son of Isaiah, much less that we concede to the Jews that the preceding passages also treat of the same. Most explain it as referring to Christ himself, which opinion our Lord Dr. Walther defends in Harm. p. 559. & the Vinarians in the Biblical Paraphrase, as also Mr. Dr. Müller in Judaism p. 657. and before them the blessed Brentius in his Commentary & Mr. Luc. Osiander in his Paraphrase: Before that boy of the virgin is born and grows up, those Kings (whom you nevertheless fear so much) will no longer rule in their kingdoms the Reformed, Oecolampadius also explained it thus: Before the boy knows to reject evil, that is, before he eats butter and honey, before he is born or conceived. One might say: If our salvation will not be until his arrival, who among us will live so long? He answers: I give you that sign indeed, if you believe in him, salvation will come to you, even while he is not yet born: whence he will be great and necessary, who, not yet born and only invoked, delivers from enemies. And thus also the ancient Fathers understand Christ by that boy, Jerome, as also Cyril: although the latter wishes it to be a spiritual discourse, so that the sense may be: With Immanuel born, the Church will be called to good hope, and all enemies are to be trampled, who, seeing it invincible, will depart, and, as preserved by God, will leave it. Calvin, however, prefers to take it generally concerning a boy: before the boys who will be born hereafter can discern good from evil, the land which you hate will be abandoned. Thus he thinks the Prophet returns from the general doctrine, to which he had digressed, to the present cause, and after he founded the hope of saving the city on the promised Messiah; he now teaches how it is to be saved. Piscator explains the word הנער individually indeed, but concerning Shear-Jashub, the son of Isaiah, whom the Prophet led with him by the hand. Which is also the opinion of Junius, which Frid. prefers to the rest. Spanheim, although he confesses that the common one concerning Immanuel has no inconvenience, Dub. Evangel. Part I. pag. 292. But because the Jewish people clung mostly to present things, and the violence and power of the enemies by whom they were vexed seemed to stand in the way of the promise concerning the Messiah, for that reason the Prophet repeats the special promise concerning the deliverance of Ahaz and the Jerusalemites from the hand of the enemies, the Syrians and Israelites, showing that not only would Jerusalem not succumb, nor be taken by those two kings, but also that they would be forced to the desertion of Judea, and departure, and that shortly, not only before the Messiah, that הנער antonomastically such, was to be exhibited, but also before the הנער, the boy, either individually, as Shear-Jashub the son of the Prophet present, or specifically, a boy, i.e., anyone then constituted in boyish age would arrive at the years of discretion. For there is no inconvenience, whether v. 16 is referred to the promised boy Immanuel, or to Shear-Jashub the son of the Prophet, or specifically to any who were then at that time constituted in boyish age, as if the Prophet says: Before he who is already a boy knows to reject evil and choose good, the land will be abandoned from the face of those two Kings. If it is referred to Immanuel, it is done through a frequent figure of Scripture, and the consequent is put for the antecedent, the discretion of good and evil. Although it must be confessed that the opinion of those is less forced and far more probable, who tear these verses apart and understand them concerning different subjects, taking היודעת here, not ἐξοχικῶς concerning the Messiah to be born from the העלמה, but either δει- κτικῶς and individually concerning Shear-Jashub the son of the Prophet, or specifically and distributively concerning any who were then of the age of a boy, since the Prophet does not say הנער הזה, which nevertheless he seems to have been about to say, if indeed he had wished the same boy to be designated again in the individual. And that it is not new for τὸ הנער to be taken thus by the Prophet is evident from the collation of chapter 3, verse 5, where the same locution occurs in the same sense, they behave themselves, הנער בזקן, the boy against the elder, the ignoble against the noble, LXX. προϲκόψει τὸ παιδίον πρὸς τὸν πρεσβύτην. And thus the sense will be plainer, for since those Kings were to be cut off within a few years, it seems harsher that they are said to be about to perish before the arrival of a boy who was to be born only after seven centuries. And the Holy Spirit would rather have said that it would happen before that boy is conceived and born, than before that boy knows to discern good and evil. But in this way all things flow and cohere among themselves most excellently, as if the Prophet says: There is no reason why you should distrust God concerning the preservation of your city and the Davidic house, eventually the Messiah will be born from it, and indeed miraculously from a virgin. Nor will those enemies, whom you have now deserved, be able to hinder his birth; for before our boys arrive at the years of judgment and discretion, they will perish, much more before the Messiah is exhibited. Among our own, the blessed Boblius in his Biblical Commentary on the Rabbis on the test. Orat. of Isaiah. Cap. 8. p. 77. not inconveniently teaches how הנער can be taken concerning the Messiah, or even some other boy, without prejudice to the truth of the Prophetic oracle, which the Jews impugn. If indeed ידע is explained by WOULD KNOW. Be that as it may, whether it is the same (namely the Messiah Immanuel) or some other boy, the time of the land being abandoned is proposed to us here periphrastically. For a boy in the second year of his age generally begins to know the discrimination of good and evil. This therefore is the sense: If, O Ahaz, your deceitful mind cannot yet acquiesce; Behold, I also add this, that if he were already born, and were the הנער, before he reached his second year, those Kings will be extirpated. Hence I wished to explain the word ידע by would know. A similar meaning of the future second is frequent in Scripture, provided the method of the institute permitted one to adhere only to Grammatical matters. These things will indeed seem to many obscure and distorted; but not so, if only the text is read and repeated properly and skillfully. For then it has been sufficiently proven, I think, that such a boy was not born. For if all these things could have calmed a wavering mind, namely the King's reasoning, God repeats more determinately the destruction of the enemy Kings, and thus removes a double doubt for the impious man, one concerning the true humanity of the virgin's son, the other concerning the certain destruction of the hostile Kings. And unless these things can be perceived quite properly, it may be said without any absurdity that this concerns a boy in general, as if I were to say: Ehe ein Knab möchte reden lernen, that is, within two years. Nor does the commonly but falsely called emphatic [article] stand in the way, for it is the articular ה, the knowledge of whose true nature is quite necessary, although these things are accustomed to be laughed at, to the public detriment of the Church, not without suspicion of shameful ignorance. Nor could a sufficient reason confuse me if I were to take הנער indefinitely, because it is also taken thus in the law of Moses, Num. 11:27: And the הנער ran and told Moses, etc. Here is your emphatic or demonstrative [article], show therefore the boy, who he was. I explain it, es lieff ein Junge und sagts Mose an, whether this was the boy of Moses, or of Simeon, or of Levi, it matters little, for it is taken indefinitely. The particle כי here is not simply explanatory. And lest I seem to doubt about the meaning of עד, which is appropriate for this one passage, I willingly pass over similar passages, for what is the use of lighting a candle in the sun? This seems to stand in the way, that the same rejection of evil and the same choice of good is attributed to this boy as to Immanuel. But a Rhetorical figure is known, called an allusion, where often the same phrase is allotted a different intention of meaning. Mr. Dr. Glassius also supports this interpretation: understanding the passage, to be sure, as concerning Isaiah's son Shear-Jashub, saving however the judgment of others: In this verse 16, I think that a sign of the liberation soon to come is proposed by the Prophet more particularly and as present before them. Namely, of the boy Shear-Jashub, the son of Isaiah, whom he had been commanded by God (certainly not in vain) to bring with him, v. 13. But the little word כי 'because' stands in the way (in the opinion of Musculus), which connects this verse to the preceding ones in such a way that it ought not to be torn from their meaning. Resp. That conjunction can be translated very well as 'nevertheless,' just as it is taken in Is. 66, v. 8, and thus the text flows most conveniently. v. 14, 15. Let the sign be to you Immanuel, promised by God, and certainly destined to be born of a virgin in his own time, on account of whom God will not desert his people, but will perform both other things and this promised benefit for you as well. v. 16. Nevertheless (so that you may also be confirmed more closely by some external and present sign), receive also this from me, that before this boy (הנער demonstratively), whom I carry in my hand, shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, not only will you be delivered from these enemies, but these very kings themselves, your enemies, will be exterminated each from his own land and kingdom, which also happened 2 Kings 15, v. 30, ch. 16, v. 9. Thus far B. Glassius in Exeges. Evang. & Epist. super Fest. Annunciat. part. II. p. 530. We judge it to be manifest that there is by no means any need for us to concede to the Jews that some other son of the Alma born in the time of Isaiah is indicated, while preserving the faith of the Christian Church, since the meaning of this prophecy is perfectly consistent with itself in that Immanuel is uniquely our Messiah: that before some infant—whether indefinitely whoever that may have been, or antonomastically the Messiah, if he were already born, or even demonstratively and individually the son of the Prophet, Sear-Jaschub, whom he had brought with him—shall have arrived at the years of discretion, those kings will perish. For it cannot be taught from history that that son of Isaiah was already of such an age at that time that he could be joined to him as a colleague, which is opposed here by some in vain. The little word כי is rightly rendered 'nay,' so that this special promise may be connected with the previous general one. Thus, I think, no scruple will remain concerning the oracle about the Messiah. But Episcopius, lib. 3. Inst. c. 13. p. 177, objects in vain that this is not to give a sign, but only to indicate the time when the liberation of the people was to be. For at the same time that this sign was to exist, the thing signified itself was also to exist. Resp. That that boy, and his progress to the years of discretion, is constituted by the divine voice as a sign of the destruction of the enemies, so that they may believe no less certainly in the same than they see boys arrive at the use of reason at a fixed time. If one does not wish to call it a sign, we shall say it is a figure or a symbol. Although it is established by examples that signs also exist with the thing signified, and the thing signified does not follow them, 1 Sam. 2, 34. Ch. 10, 2. 1 Kings 22, 26. But so that the occasion for every evasion might be cut off, we have said that not a special sign, but a more special promise was added to the general one. But enough about this oracle. Concerning which, whoever wishes may compare B. Luther, Tom. II. Jenens. in the book 'daß Christus ein gebohrner Jůde,' as also Tom. VIII. D. Helvic. T. IV. Disput. Giess. XIV. Dn. D. Johan. Müller in Judaism. Cap. XIX. p. 613. seqq. Dn. D. Mich. Walther, Harm. Bibl. ad h. l. Dn. D. Glassius loc. c. Dn. Jacob. Mart. libr. III. de Trib. Eloh. Frider. Spanhem. Joh. Hornbeck. l. c.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DERELINQVETUR TERRA, QUAM TV DETESTARIS, A FACIE DVORVM REGVM SVO- RVM] Id est, morientur Reges illi duo Syriæ & Israelis. Terram, intellige utramque Phacees huic tempori non to- tos tres annos fupervixit:

Promissum vel documentum hic alterum specia- lius proponi diximus liberationis Judææ à poten- tia duorum Regum infensissimorum, quod brevi derelinquenda sit terra utraque, quam nunc detestaba- tur domus Davidis, Ephraim nempe & Syriæ, à fa- cie duorum Regum suorum. Quod etsi plerique de morte Regum intelligant cum Grotio, qui intra triennium occubuere ambo, alii tamen de devasta- tione utriusq; terræ explicant, alii cum Leone Casta- lico ad extremam vastitatem, quæ Judæis accidit à Romanis, eadem referunt. Illis præit Hieronymus inde argumentum petens, quod Ezechias intelligi nequeat per parvulum: sed quod Immanuel virginis Filius indigitetur. Quod pariter etiam contra Gro- tii sententiam de filio Esaiæ militabit, stante illa ex- plicatione. Sexto imperii anno Ezechias, inquit Hie- ronymus, est ab Assyriis capta Samaria, id est, trice- simo primo anno ætatis ipsius. Si itaque iste, qui nasciturus, vel de virgine, ut nos probamus, vel de adolescentula, ut Judæi volunt, butyrum & mel comedet: & tam parvulus erit, ut malum à bono discernere nequeat, & antequam ille tempus egre- diatur infantiæ, terra Syriæ & Samariæ vastanda ab Assyriis sit, respondeant Hebræi, quomodo Eze- chias triginta & uno annis infantulus prædicetur, & tam rudis ætatis, ut mel & butyrum comedens; juxta Niniviticos pueros, nec sinistram, nec dex- tram, id est, nec malum nec bonum noverit. Rela- tum autem ad Emmanuel, quod interpretatur no- biscum Deus, facilem habebit intelligentiam. Quod ad mysterium & invocationem nominis e- jus terra Syriæ & Samariæ Assyrio superante vaste- tur, & domus David liberetur à duobus Regibus, quos metuit, Rasin videlicet & Phacee. Hæc ille.

Porro vocem הַנַּעַר non est necessum, ut de Esaiæ filio intelligamus, multo minus, ut Judæis con- cedamus, præcedentia etiam de eodem age- re. Plerique explicant eandem de ipso Christo, quam sententiam tuetur Dn. D. Waltherus noster in Harm. p. 559. & Vinarienses in Paraphraf. Bibl. ut & Dn. D. Müllerus in Judaismo p. 657. nec non an- te illos B. Brentius in Comment. & Dn. Luc. Osian- der in Paraphr. Priusquam nascetur & adolescet fi- lius ille virginis jamdudum illi Reges non ampliùs in suis regnis, (quos tamen adeo metuis) dominabun- tur, sed exterminati de terra in pulvere jacebunt. E Reformatis etiam ita exposuit Oecolampadius : Priusquam puer sciat reprobare malum, hoc est, prius- quam comedet butyrum & mel, priusquam nascatur vel concipiatur. Diceret quis : Si non erit salus no- stra, nisi usq́; ad adventum illius, quis ex nobis tam diu vivet? respondet : illud quidem signum do vobis, si cre- dideritis in eum, Salus vobis eveniet, etiam eo nondum nato : unde illum magnum fore, necessarium, qui non- dum natus & invocatus tantum, ab inimicis liberat. Atque ita etiam Patres antiqui per puerum illum Christum intelligunt, Hieronymus, ut & Cyrillus : quamvis hic spiritualem orationem esse velit, ut sensus sit : Nato Immanuele Ecclesiam bonam spem vocatum iri, omnesq́; hostes calcandos esse, qui invi- ctam illam videntes recessuri sint, & ut à Deo conserva- tam, relicturi. Calvinus tamen in genere de puero accipere mavult : antequam pueri, qui posthac na- scentur, bonum à malo discernere queant, terra, quam odisti, relinquetur. Sic à generali doctrina, ad quam digressus erat, Prophetam reverti ad præsentem causam, & postquam spem servandæ urbis funda- vit in Messia promisso ; jam quomodo servanda sit, docere existimat. Piscator vocem הנער individua- liter quidem, sed de Sear-Jaschub Esaiæ filio expli- cat, quem secum manu duxerit Propheta. Quæ Ju- nii etiam sententia est, quam præfert reliquis Frid. Spanhemius, licet communem illam de Immanuele ni- hil incommodi habere fateatur Dub. Evangel. Part. I. pag. 292. Quia vero populus Judaicus hærebat potissimum in præsentibus, & videbatur obstare promissioni de Messia violentia & potentia hostiũ, à quibus vexabantur, ob id repetit Propheta pro- missionem specialem de liberatione Achazi & Hie- rosolymitanorum è manu hostium, Syrorum & Israëlitarum, ostendendo, non saltem Hierosoly- mam non succubituram, nec expugnandam à duo- bus illis regibus, sed & eos cogendos ad desertionẽ Judææ, & discessum, idque brevi, non solum ante- quam Messias הנער ille antonomastice talis, esset exhibendus, sed etiam antequam הנער puer sive individualiter, ut Sear-Jaschub filius Prophetæ præ- sens, sive specifice, puer, h. e. quivis in ætate puerili tum constitutus ad annos discretionis perventurus esset. Nihil enim incommodi, sive v. 16. referatur ad puerum Immanuelem promissum, sive ad Sear- Jaschub filium Prophetæ, sive specifice ad quosvis tum temporis in ætate puerili constitutos, quasi di- cat Propheta : Antequam ille, qui jam puer est, sciat reprobare malum, & eligere bonum, terra de- relinquetur à facie duorum illorum Regum. Si ad Immanuelem referatur, fit id per figuram frequen- tem Scripturæ, & consequens ponitur pro antece- dente, discretio boni & mali. Etsi fatendum, mi- nus coactam & longe probabiliorem esse illorum sententiam, qui versus hos distrahunt & de diversis subjectis intelligunt, היודעת hic, sumpto non ἐξο- χικῶς de Messia nascituro ex העלמה, sed vel δει- κτικῶς & individualiter de Sear-Jaschub filio Pro- phetæ, vel specifice & distributive de quibusvis, qui tum ætate pueri erant, cum non dicat Propheta, הנער הזה quod tamen videtur dicturus fuisse, si quidem eundem in individuo puerum denuo desi- gnatum voluisset. Nec novum esse τὸ הנער ita su- mi à Propheta, patet ex collatione cap. 3. vers. 5. ubi eadem locutio eodem sensu occurrit, efferent se ju- הנער בזקן puer in senem, ignobilis in nobilem LXX. προϲκόψει τὸ παιδίον πρὸς τὸν πρεσβύτην. Et sic sensus planior erit, cum enim Reges illi inter paucos annos essent excindendi, durius videtur, il- los dici perituros ante adventum pueri, qui post se- ptem demum secula nasciturus erat. Et dixisset po- tius Sp. S. id futurum, antequam puer ille concipia- tur, & nascatur, quàm antequam puer ille sciat dis- cernere bonum & malum. Hoc vero modo omnia optimè & fluunt, & cohærent inter se, quasi dicat Propheta: non est, quod diffidatis Deo de conserva- tione urbis vestræ, & domus Davidicæ, tandem na- scetur & ex ea Messias, & quidem miraculose ex vir- gine. Nec isti hostes, quos jam meruitis, nativitatem illius impedire poterunt; antequam enim pueri nostri perveniant ad annos judicii & discretionis, peribunt illi, multo magis antequam exhibeatur Messias. E nostris B. Boblius in Comment. Bibl. Rabb. super Orat. test. Esai. Cap. 8. p. 77. non incommode docet, quomodo הנער de Messia, aut etiam alio quo- dam puero accipi possit, salva veritate oraculi Pro- phetici, quam impugnant Judæi. Si nempe ידע ex- plicetur per COGNOSCERET. Utut sit, sive idem (Immanuel nempe Messias) sive alius quidam puer sit, periphrastice hic nobis proponitur tempus dere- linquendæ terræ. Nam puer anno ætatis secundo gene- raliter incipit cognoscere discrimen boni & mali. Hic ergo est sensus: Si, ô Achas, animus tuus dolosus nondum acquiescere potest; Ecce & hoc addo, quod si jam natus esset, & esset הנער antequam secundum annum attingeret, Reges isti extirpa- buntur. Hinc vocem ידע per cognosceret explicare volui. Similis significatus futuri secundi in Scripturâ frequens est, modo instituti ratio permitteret, Gram- maticalibus tantum inhærere. Videbuntur hæc qui- dem multis obscura & detorta; sed non ita, si modo textus probè & dextre legatur & repetatur. Nam tum puerum talem non natum esse, satis, ut puto, evi- ctum est. Nam si hæc omnia animum fluctuantem, Regis sc. rationem, compescere potuissent, repetit Deus deter- minate magis exitium Regum hostium, & ita duplex dubium impio homini eximit, alterum de vera huma- nitate filii virginis, alterum de certo exitio Regum in- fensorum. Et nisi hæc sat probe percipi possunt, si- ne omni absurditate dicatur, hic agi de puero in gene- re, quasi dicerem: Ehe ein Knab möchte reden ler- nen, id est, innerhalb zweyen Jahren. Nec obstat, vulgo sed falso dictum emphaticum, est enim ה ar- ticulare, cujus certenaturæ cognitio sat est necessaria, quamvis cum publico malo Ecclesiæ hæc soleant non si- ne suspicione pudendæ ignorantiæ rideri. Nec sufficiens ratio me confundere posset, si הנער indefinite sumerem, quia etiam in lege Mosis Num. 2, 27. ita sumitur: Et currebat הנער & nunciabat Mosi &c. Hic vestrum emphaticum seu demonstrativum, monstrate ergo pue- rum, quinam fuerit. Ego explico, es lieff ein Junge und sagts Mose an, sive hic fuerit puer Mo- sis, seu Simeonis seu Levi parum refert, indefinite enim accipitur. Particula כי hic non est simpliciter redditi- va. Et ne de significatione עד uno huic loco compe- tente ambigere videar, loca similia lubens prætereo, quid enim juvat in sole accendere candelam? Hoc ob- stare videtur, quod eadem reprobatio mali, & eadem electio boni tribuatur huic puero qua Immanueli. Sed nota est figura Rhetorica, dicta allusio, ubi sæpe eadem phrasis diversam significandi sortitur intentionem. Accedit etiam huic interpretationi Dn. D. Glassius: de filio nempe Esaiæ Schear-Jaschub locum intelli- gens, salvo tamen aliorum judicio: In hoc versu 16. particularius & coram præsens signum liberationis mox futuræ proponi à Propheta, existimo. Pueri nimi- rum Sear-Jasubi filii Esaiæ, quem adducere se- cum Propheta à Deo (non certe frustra) jussus fue- rat, v. 13. sed obstat (censente Musculo) vocula כי quia, quæ hunc versum præcedentibus sic annectit, ut à sensu illorum avelli non debeat. Resp. Opti- me verti illa conjunctio potest, veruntamen, uti Es. 66. v. 8. accipitur, & sic commodissime fluit textus v. 14. 15. signum esto vobis Immanuel, à Deo promissus, & certo suo tempore ex virgine nasci- turus, propter quem non deseret Deus populum suum, sed & alia, & hoc etiam promissum vobis be- neficium præstabit v. 16. Veruntamen (ut & pro- pius, signo quodam externo & præsenti jam con- firmemini) accipitote etiam hoc à me, quod ante- quam hic puer (הנער δεικτικω̃ς) quem manu ge- ro, sciverit reprobare malum & eligere bonum, non solum liberati eritis ab his hostibus, sed & ipsi hi reges, hostes vestri, ex sua quisque terra & re- gno exterminabuntur, quod & factum est 2. Reg. 15. v. 30. cap. 16. v. 9. Hactenus B. Glassius in Exeges. Evang. & Epist. super Fest. Annunciat. part. II. p. 530. Nos id manifestum esse arbitramur, neuti- quam opus esse, ut Judæis concedamus alium quen- dam Almæ filium tempore Esaiæ natum indigitari, salva Christianæ Ecclesiæ fide, cum, quod unice Im- manuel sit Messias noster, optime sibi constet hujus vaticinii sententia: quod antequam infans aliquis, seu indefinite quicunque ille fuerit, seu antonomastice Messias, si jam natus esset, seu etiam δεικτικω̃ς & indi- vidualiter filius Prophetæ Sear-Jaschub, quem secum adduxerat, ad annos discretionis pervenerit, Reges illi interituri sint. Neque enim ex historia doceri pot- est, Filium illum Esaiæ tum ejus ætatis jam fuisse, ut adjungi ei ceu collega potuerit, quod à nonnullis frustra hic opponitur. Vocula כי recte redditur i- mo, ut connectatur hæc specialis promissio cum prio- ri generali. Sic nullus, arbitror, supererit scrupulus in oraculo de Messia. Nequicquam autem Epi- scopius lib. 3. Inst. c. 13. p. 177. obvertit, hoc non esse signum dare, sed tantum tempus indicare, quo libera- tio populi futura erat. Eodem enim tempore, quo signum istud extiturum erat, ipsa etiam res signata e- rat extitura. Resp. Quod puer ille, & progres- sus ejus ad annos discretionis, signum constituatur divina voce interitus hostium, ut non minus certo credant eundem, quam vident pueros stato tem- pore ad usum rationis pervenire. Si signum quis no- lit dicere, figuram, vel symbolum eum esse dicemus. Quamvis signa etiam cum signato extare, neque signatum sequi ab exemplis constet 1. Sam. 2, 34. C. 10, 2. 1. Reg. 22, 26. Ut autem omni elusioni oc- casio præscinderetur, non speciale signum, sed spe- cialius promissum generali additum diximus. Sed sa- tis de hoc oraculo. Quo de conferre, qui volet, poterit B. Lutherum Tom. II. Jenens. libro daß Christus ein gebohrner Jůde, ut & Tom. VIII. D. Helvic. T. IV. Disput. Giess. XIV. Dn. D. Johan. Müllerum in Judaism. Cap. XIX. p. 613. seqq. Dn. D. Mich. Waltherum Harm. Bibl. ad h. l. Dn. D. Glassium loc. c. Dn. Jacob. Mart. libr. III. de Trib. Eloh. Frider. Spanhem. Joh. Hornbeck. l. c.

## 7:17
Vers. 17. WITH THE KING OF THE ASSYRIANS] בּ here is 'by.' He will bring upon you evils never heard of, by him in whom you, having put God aside, trust.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CVM REGE ASSTRIORVM] בּ hic est per. Adducet tibi mala nunquam audita, per eum cui tu, Deo posthabito, confidis.

## 7:18
Vers. 18. THE LORD WILL HISS FOR THE FLY, WHICH IS IN THE EXTREMITY OF THE RIVERS OF EGYPT] He will beckon to Pharaoh Necho, that he may come against Judea, 2 Kings 23, 32. The fly is an impudent animal; such are the Egyptians.

AND FOR THE BEE THAT IS IN THE LAND OF ASSUR] Bees sting, which flies do not do. Such were the Assyrians to be under Sennacherib.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SIBILABIT DOMINVS MVSCÆ, QVÆ EST IN EXTREMO FLVMINVM ÆGTPTI] Innuet Pharaoni Nechao, ut contra Judæam veniat 2. Reg. 23, 32. Musca animal inverecundum, tales Ægyptii.

ET API QVÆ EST IN TERRA ASSVR] A- pes pungunt, quod muscæ non faciunt. Tales futuri e- rant Assyrii sub Sennacheribo.

## 7:19
Vers. 19. AND THEY SHALL REST ALL] They will pitch camp, as above 7, 2.

IN THE TORRENTS OF THE VALLEYS] In Hebrew: in the valleys of the field: as flies are wont to do.

AND IN THE CAVERNS OF THE ROCKS] as bees are wont to do. AND IN ALL THICKETS] Where ambushes are wont to be placed. The same word below 55, 13. Here it returns to the likeness of flies. AND IN ALL HOLES] thus the Greeks: ἐν πάσαις ῥαγάσι. Here it returns to the likeness of bees. The Chaldean: in all palaces. Vers. 20. IN THAT DAY THE LORD WILL SHAVE] He will shave Judea, which he compares to a human body. WITH A HIRED RAZOR] That is, by the Assyrians and the king of the Assyrians, as follows immediately, whom God enticed with a great reward of plunder. THE HEAD] The hair. AND THE HAIRS OF THE FEET] The pubic hair. For the Hebrews call the feet modestly τὰ αἰδοῖα, as has been noted several times. Vers. 21. AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY, A MAN SHALL NOURISH A COW OF THE HERD, AND TWO SHEEP] Few men will remain in the land devastated by Sennacherib, who will not have herds, as before, but one heifer, two sheep, from which they may live. But those heifers and sheep will give a great deal of milk, because every field will be pasture, and open to all because of the scarcity of men. Thus also the bees will wander most widely. Vers. 23.
