WHERE THERE WERE A THOUSAND VINES, FOR A THOUSAND SILVER PIECES] Vineyards which were rented for a reward of a thousand shekels each: that is, the best vineyards. See Cant. 8, 11. THEY SHALL BE FOR BRIARS AND THORNS] Because of the lack of cultivators, they will be turned into thickets and brambles. Vers. 24. WITH ARROWS AND BOW THEY SHALL ENTER THITHER] No one will dare to proceed there unless armed, for fear of wild beasts and serpents. See Levit. 26, 22. Vers. 25. AND ALL THE MOUNTAINS] The most fertile places in the mountains. WHICH SHALL BE CULTIVATED WITH THE HOE] Which places were wont to be cultivated most diligently, and purged with a hoe, so that nothing harmful might remain anywhere. THE TERROR OF BRIARS AND THORNS SHALL NOT COME THITHER] He calls the hedges of briars and thorns, which prevent access to the fields, terror. AND IT SHALL BE FOR THE PASTURE OF THE OX AND FOR THE TREADING OF THE FLOCK] Oxen and cattle will wander there everywhere, as they are wont to do in uncultivated and unguarded places.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET REQVIESCENT OMNES] Castra po- nent, ut supra 7, 2.

IN TORRENTIBVS VALLIVM] In Hebræo: in val libus agri: ut solent muscæ.

ET IN CAVERNIS PETRARUM] ut solent apes. ET IN OMNIBUS FRUTETIS] Ubi insidiæ poni solent. Eadem vox infra 55, 13. Hic ad similitudinem muscarum redit. ET IN UNIVERSIS FORAMINIBUS] sic Græci: ἐν πάσαις ῥαγάσι. Hic redit ad apum similitudinem. Chaldæus: in omnibus palatiis. Vers. 20. IN DIE ILLA RADET DOMINUS] Abradet Judæam, quam comparat humano corpori. IN NOVACULA CONDUCTA] Id est, per Assyrios & regem Assyriorum, ut mox sequitur, quem Deus magna mercede prædæ illexit. CAPUT] Comam. ET PILOS PEDUM] Pubem. Nam pedes σεμνῶς Hebræi vocant τὰ αἰδοῖα, ut notatum aliquoties. Vers. 21. ET ERIT IN DIE ILLA, NUTRIET HOMO VACCAM BOUM, ET DUAS OVES] Pauci restabunt in terra à Sennacheribo desolata homines, qui nón armenta habebunt, ut ante, sed buculam unam, oves duas, unde vivant. Illæ autem buculæ & oves plurimum daturæ sunt lactis, quia omnis ager erit pascuus, & omnibus patens ob hominum infrequentiam. Sic & apes latissime vagabuntur. Vers. 23. UBI FUERINT MILLE VITES, MILLE ARGENTEIS] Vineta quæ singula mille siclorum mercede locabantur: id est, optima vineta. Vide Cant. 8, 11. IN SPINAS ET VEPRES ERUNT] Ob colentium penuriam vertentur in vepreta & senticeta. Vers. 24. CUM SAGITTIS ET ARCU INGREDIENTUR ILLUC] Nemo nisi armatus eo audebit procedere, metu ferarum & serpentium. Vide Levit. 26, 22. Vers. 25. ET OMNES MONTES] Loca fertilissima in montibus. QUÆ IN SARCULO SARRIENTUR] Quæ loca diligentissime coli, ac sarculo purgari solebant, nequid usquam noxii resideret. NON VENIET ILLUC TERROR SPINARUM ET VEPRIVM] Terrorem vocat sepes è vepribus & sentibus, quæ aditum ad agros arcent. ET ERIT IN PASCVA BOVIS ET IN CONCVLCATIONEM PECORIS] Passim ibi vagabuntur boves & pecudes, ut solent in locis incultis & incustoditis.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII. The faithful being encouraged by Immanuel, it is predicted that among the extreme ingratitude and blindness of the Lord's people, some disciples will still be preserved, and they are recalled from the augurs to the Word of GOD.

Vers. 1. TAKE THEE A GREAT ROLL] That is, a large page, which can be both rolled up and unrolled. AND WRITE IN IT WITH A MAN'S PEN] That is, clear writing, as the Chaldean has it here, which anyone may easily read even from a distance, as Habakkuk 2:2. Same verse. MAKE HASTE TO THE SPOIL, HASTEN THE PREY] God wishes the name of the son, whom He was about to give to Isaiah, which was long, to be written out, lest it should slip from memory. That name is Mahar-Salal Hasbaz, that is, hasten to the spoil, hurry to the prey. This name signifies the decree of God concerning the summoning of Sennacherib. I TOOK UNTO ME FAITHFUL WITNESSES] Marriages were accustomed to be contracted before at least ten witnesses. But Isaiah, as in a matter of the greatest importance, wished there to be among those witnesses two of the greatest authority, Uriah the high priest, of whom 2 Kings 16:10, and Zechariah the Prophet 2 Chronicles 26:5, perhaps the same who is said to have been of the descendants of Asaph 2 Chronicles 29:13. Vers. 2. AND I WENT UNTO THE PROPHETESS] I took to wife a virgin famous for the gift of prophecy, so that the commands of God might be carried out as magnificently as possible. Vers. 3. AND THE LORD SAID UNTO ME, CALL HIS NAME] Impose upon him that name which I ordered you to write out. For this matter also, the same witnesses were employed as for the marriage. Vers. 4. THE RICHES OF DAMASCUS AND THE SPOIL OF SAMARIA SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY BEFORE THE KING OF ASSYRIA] Riches here signifies wealth. The wealth and spoils of both Syria and the ten tribes shall be carried off as trophies to the king of Assyria.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII. Erectis per Immanuelem fidelibus in extrema ingratitudine ac cœcitate populi Domini quosdam adhuc discipulos conservatum iri prædicitur, & revocantur ab auguribus ad Verbum DEI.

Vers. 1. SVME TIBI LIBRVM GRANDEM] Id est, paginam grandem, quæ & convolvi & evolvi possit. ET SCRIBE IN EO STYLO HOMINIS] Id est, scriptura clara, ut hic habet Chaldæus, quam facile quilibet vel eminus legat, ut Abacuc. 2, 2. Vers. eod. VELOCITER SPOLIA DETRAHE, CITO PRÆDARE] Deus nomen filii, quem daturus erat Esaiæ, quod longum erat, vult perscribi, ne memoriæ elaberetur. Id nomen est Mahar-Salal Hasbaz, id est, festina ad spolium, celera ad prædam. Significat hoc nomen decretum Dei de advocando Sennacheribo. ADHIBVI MIHI TESTES FIDELES] Matrimonia contrahi coram decem minimum testibus solebant. At Esaias ut in negotio maximi momenti, inter eos testes duos esse voluit maximæ autoritatis, Vriam summum sacerdotem, de quo 2. Reg. 16, 10. & Zachariam Prophetam 2. Par. 26, 5. eundem forte, qui ex Asaphi posteris fuisse dicitur 2. Par. 29, 13. Vers. 2. ET ACCESSI AD PROPHETISSAM] Virginem Prophetiæ dono claram mihi in uxorem sumsi, ut Dei mandata quam magnificentissime peragerentur. Vers. 3. ET DIXIT DOMINVS AD ME, VOCA NOMEN EJVS] Impone illi id nomen, quod te jussi perscribere. Huic quoque rei testes adhibiti iidem, qui ad matrimonium. Vers. 4. AVFERETVR FORTITVDO DAMASCI ET SPOLIA SAMARIÆ CORAM REGE ASSYRIORVM] Fortitudo hic opes significat. Opes & spolia tum Syriæ tum decem tribuum, tanquam trophæa perferentur ad regem Assyriæ.

## 8:6
Verse 6.

FORASMUCH AS THIS PEOPLE HATH REJECTED THE WATERS OF SILOAH, WHICH GO SOFTLY, AND HAVE TAKEN RIZIN AND THE SON OF REMALIAH] By the waters of Siloah going softly, he understands the house of David, weak in human strength, but supported by the protection of God, just as he presently explains the king of the Assyrians by the waters of the river, namely the Euphrates, called so κατ'ἐξοχὴν (by way of eminence): because waters are peoples, Rev. 17:15. And kings contain the force of peoples within themselves. This passage signifies that many Jews, having despised the house of David, wished for the kingdom to be transferred to the Syrians and to the kings of Israel who adhered to the Syrians, and rejoiced in their prosperity. For that is what the Hebrew words sound.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PRO EO QUOD ABJECIT POPULUS ISTE A- QUAS SILOE, QUÆ VADUNT CUM SILENTIO, ET ASSUMSIT MAGIS RASIN, ET FILIUM RO- MELIÆ] Per aquas Siloë lente euntes intelligit domum Davidis, viribus humanis tenuem, sed Dei præsidio suf- fultam, sicut jam in continenti aquas fluminis, nempe Euphratis, ita κατ'ἐξοχὴν dicti, explicat regem Assyrio- rum: quia aquæ sunt populi Apoc. 17, 15. Et reges vim populorum in se continent. Significat hic locus multos Judæos, spreta domo Davidis, optasse transferri regnum ad Syros & ad reges Israëlis Syris adhærentes, & horum prosperis gavisos. Id enim sonant Hebræa.

## 8:7
Verse 7.

THE KING OF THE ASSYRIANS, AND ALL HIS GLORY] Glory here signifies power in the Hebrew manner.

AND HE SHALL COME UP OVER ALL HIS CHANNELS, AND FLOW OVER ALL HIS BANKS, AND HE SHALL GO THROUGH JUDAH OVERFLOWING AND PASSING THROUGH, HE SHALL REACH EVEN TO THE NECK] He persists in the comparison of a great and overflowing river. Thus Lucan compares Pompey to a river in Book VI. Thus the Po, swelling with full mouth, runs over the banks safe by the dike, and shakes the whole fields, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

REGEM ASSYRIORUM, ET OMNEM GLO- RIAM EJUS] Gloria hic more Hebræo potentiam signi- ficat.

ET ASCENDET SUPER OMNES RIVOS E- JUS, ET FLUENT SUPER OMNES RIPAS EJUS, ET IBIT PER JUDAM INUNDANS ET TRANS- IENS USQUE AD COLLUM VENIET] Perstat in comparatione magni & exundantis fluminis. Sic Pom- pejum fluvio comparat Lucanus VI. Sic pleno Padus ore tumens super aggere tutas Excurrit ripas, & totos concutit agros. &c.

## 8:8
Verse 8.

AND THE STRETCHING OUT OF HIS WINGS SHALL BE] The Hebrews call all forces wings, not only cavalry, as the Latins do, but also infantry that are about to make an excursion, or even the fortifications of borders.

Here Grotius himself again assumes some things which stand in need of proof, and are by no means conceded by others; such as that Isaiah took another wife, the matter being, whether the former was deceased or still living, from whom Shear-Jashub was born; that the access to the Prophetess was made for the sake of marriage, or implies conjugal intercourse: that at that time the virgin was famous for the gift of prophecy, whom the Prophet took to himself as a wife: that he received a son from her: that he imposed that very long name upon the son begotten from that new wife: that those witnesses were employed in taking the wife; that the same were also employed as witnesses in imposing that name; concerning which he cannot produce even a jot from sacred history. But even if all those things were admitted, he nevertheless hallucinates most gravely when he believes this same son of Isaiah to be the son of the virgin, concerning whom the Prophet prophesied in the seventh chapter. But it has already been demonstrated that the Holy Spirit prophesied there concerning the chaste virgin conceiving and bearing, not concerning a married virgin, nor concerning a mere man (ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ), but concerning Him who is truly Immanuel, the God-man (θεανθρωπος). There are indeed not a few among Christian interpreters who wish for the discourse here to be about the same boy as was dealt with in the preceding chapter, but these everywhere understand uniquely Christ, the son of the Blessed Virgin, and wish for both the name of Immanuel and this present name, Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz, to be imposed upon Him. But the Grotian interpretation judaizes entirely, inasmuch as he wishes for the fulfillment of the previous prophecy to be had here, when the Prophet took a virgin and received a son from her. But let us suppose with Grotius that the same matter is proposed in this and the preceding chapter; will it not be better to explain the present passage also concerning the conception and birth of the Messiah with the ancient Fathers Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Origen, Epiphanius, Athanasius, Basil, Ambrose, Jerome, and Augustine, and other Christian interpreters of the highest name, than to interpret both passages with the Jews, the implacable (ἀσπόνδοις) enemies of the Christian name, concerning the conception and birth of the son of Isaiah, and everywhere in the literal sense exclude Christ, and openly contradict the interpretation of the Holy Spirit Himself delivered in the New Testament? to other Christians of the highest name, to explain the present passage concerning the conception and birth of the Messiah, than to interpret with the Jews, those ἀσπόνδοις enemies of the Christian name, both passages concerning the conception and birth of the son of Isaiah, and in both places to exclude Christ from the literal sense, and openly to contradict the very interpretation of the Holy Spirit delivered in the New Testament? Nor indeed does that interpretation of the ancients seem to be destitute of reasons. For since in the seventh chapter, according to the undoubted interpretation of the Holy Spirit, the subject is the birth of the Messiah, and in the ninth chapter his birth is again predicted in v. 6, the intermediate eighth chapter seems likewise to be understood of him. Then indeed there appears here a remarkable agreement with the oracle of Chapter VII. For there it is predicted: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and shall bear a son. Here the Prophetess, says Isaiah, conceived and bore a son: there, at the command of the Lord, a name is to be imposed upon him: here likewise God commands it, The Lord said to me, call his name. There it is added, because before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of the face of both her kings. Here not dissimilarly: Because before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the King of Assyria. Furthermore, both names fit Christ perfectly, who is Immanuel, because God is with us by the fellowship of nature and the help of grace, and Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz, because He hastens to take away the spoils and hurries to plunder the enemies of His people, because He is a swift plunderer and a hasty spoiler not only of spiritual enemies, but also of corporal ones. Previously, says Brentius in this place, Christ was called by his surname Immanuel, which signifies, God with us, so that you might confirm your faith and know that the divine power is present to assist, so that even at this time he may preserve you and your kingdom. But now he is called a swift predator and a hasty spoiler, so that you might again confirm your faith, and acknowledge that just as he mercifully preserves your kingdom, so he will powerfully and swiftly despoil, plunder, and oppress your enemies. These are the words of Brentius. Nor does the promise seem to contradict this: before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the land will be forsaken. Which, whether they are understood of any child indefinitely, or even of this child, of the Messiah, that before he has learned to speak, it will already be done concerning the strength and spoils of Damascus and Samaria. For although this was completed long before the birth of Christ, yet here the birth of Christ is set forth as if in the present, and before Christ, thus conceived and born, has learned to address Father and mother, the removal of the strength and spoils of both kingdoms, from which the Jews feared for themselves, is promised. For they understand these things concerning the conception and birth as if enacted in a vision, and therefore the years of childhood will also be designated here in the vision. Those interpreters also observe that in the Greek text of the LXX interpreters, that removal of strength and spoils is attributed to the child himself, before he knows how to address Father and mother: in which sense the Hebrew text itself can also be taken. Before the child knows how to call father and mother, he will take away the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria. Justin Martyr urges Trypho in the Dialogue, p. 236 of my edition, that the child, before he knows how to call Father or mother, will receive the power of Damascus. But you, he says, cannot prove that this ever happened to any of the Jews, whereas we are able to demonstrate that this was done to our Christ. He explains it thus, that it was signified that the power of the malignant demon inhabiting Damascus would be vanquished by Christ as soon as he was born. Which Irenaeus likewise urges in book III against heresies, chapter XVIII, as well as Cyril of Alexandria, whose words I append. Since God, existing by nature, became the Word with us, who appeared in our form, he could most wisely be denoted by the name Immanuel, then having become man, when he despoiled Satan, and those formerly carried off, and serving him through sin, he had snatched from his tyranny, he exercised and declared that: Swiftly spoiled, quickly the predator. Which also, so that God might be about to accomplish human redemption with inexplicable power, he foreshadowed saying: Before the boy knows Father or mother, he will take away the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria with the King of the Assyrians. These things Cyril. Jerome in this place renders the Hebrew indeed a little differently, yet he ascribes to the boy the Salvation of the people against the Syrians and Israelites. It is commanded to Isaiah, that the boy himself, who was previously called Emmanuel, he now call hasten, take away the spoils, make haste to plunder. For ascending on high he led captivity captive, he gave gifts to men, and before he assumed a human body and according to infancy called God Father and Mary mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be taken away by the King of the Assyrians, so that not yet born he might SAVE his people of the house of David by invocation alone. Finally, some also urge this, that the Chronology does not fit if the words are taken simply according to the letter, because Zechariah the son of Berechiah, who is brought forward here as a witness, was 170 years later than Isaiah: and also that Urijah, an infidel and worshiper of idols, should not seem to have been employed to bear witness to a matter so holy and excellent: indeed that it seems clearly absurd and little honorable that Isaiah should have had intercourse with his wife, with some witnesses present, which nevertheless seems to have to be said if those words are to be explained literally and concerning the son of Isaiah: and it is not certain that the wife of Isaiah was a Prophetess. Whence they judge that all these things happened to Isaiah in a vision and are to be referred immediately and literally to the Messiah, and that by the Prophetess the virgin Mary is understood, who truly prophesied concerning the power of the arm of the Lord Luke 1:52, concerning the taking up of Israel v. 54, and concerning the celebration of her blessedness among future generations v. 50. Therefore some interpreters render this sense: I approached the Prophetess, that is, I seemed to myself to approach (in revelation and prophetic vision to the virgin Mary, who is called a Prophetess; she was shown to me in a vision, so that I might approach her, and I approached), about to announce to her that it would come to pass that she would bear a son, and she conceived and bore a son, in a prophetic vision, to wit. (I saw in divine revelation her conceiving through the singular overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, and bearing a son.) To which contributes that of Cyril at the beginning of Chapter 8 of Isaiah; If anyone says that the holy Prophets not only received knowledge of future things, the Holy Spirit shining here for them and insinuating into their minds, but also that they sometimes existed as spectators of the things themselves, I judge that he cannot err in the least. D. Osiander followed that opinion in his Paraphrase, who indeed refers what is said, with witnesses being employed, to the public description of that prophetic name, and judges that it was done not only in a vision, but in reality, and thus wishes Urijah to have been taken into that testimony, before he fell away from the sincere Religion, and also Zechariah the son of Berechiah, not that one from the Prophets who are called minor, nor that one who is written to have been stoned 2 Chronicles 24, but another called by this name. Nor without reason do others observe that this Zechariah was not the son of Berechiah, but of Jeberechiah, and therefore seems to have been the father-in-law of Ahaz, the maternal grandfather of Hezekiah, of whom there is mention, 2 Chron. 29:2, or that one of the sons of Asaph, who are commemorated 2 Chron. 29:13, whom Grotius thinks is the same as Zechariah the Prophet, and seeing God in the time of Uzziah, 2 Chron. 26:5, but this one does not seem to have survived the times of Uzziah, let alone reached the reign of Hezekiah; if indeed it is said of Uzziah that he sought the Lord at least in the days of Zechariah, who understood and saw God, and thus it is implied that he did not seek the Lord after the death of Zechariah. There are those who refer these things to the Holy Spirit, not to the Prophet, as if the Holy Spirit were saying to the Prophet: I will employ faithful witnesses for myself. And I will approach the virgin Mary (through a special ἐπιέλευσιν [overshadowing]) and she will conceive and will bear a son, who is about to destroy his enemies; so that these things here may be held as Prophetic concerning that future miraculous ἐπιλεύσει [overshadowing] of the Holy Spirit over the Θεοτόκον [Mother of God], through which the Son of God was to be conceived. According to which explanation it will be able to be said, however known it may be what is signified by the Hebrew phrase, to approach a woman, especially when it is added, and she conceived and bore, here nevertheless it has a peculiar reason, just as the birth itself is clearly singular, which is predicted.

This explanation, supported by the authority of great Doctors both ancient and recent, does not seem easily to be rejected. Spanheim also acknowledges in Dub. Evangel. page 327, that it is a pious sense and a specious sense, even if he goes into all other things. If, however, to anyone those things concerning the approach in a vision, or even concerning the ἐπιλεύσει [overshadowing] of the Holy Spirit and concerning the Blessed virgin Prophetess seem a little too subtle, and he prefers to interpret these things according to the literal sense with most Reformed [theologians] concerning the Prophet and his wife, because a symbolic name had to be imposed upon the boy born from the Prophet, to signify the slaughter about to be brought upon Syria and Samaria, so that all things are historical, concerning the name being written on a public tablet and witnesses being employed for that purpose (so that it may be certain, both by the peculiar counsel of God and the zeal of the Prophet at the command of God, that this symbolic name was described and publicly proposed), concerning the approach of the Prophet to the Prophetess, and the conception of a son from the same, and those names imposed upon the same for the sake of signifying and confirming the same thing: yet the Judaizing Grotius will still obtain nothing for his opinion, namely that Immanuel is likewise the son of the Prophet. For the passages are diverse and very different; there the prophecy is held in ch. 7, 14, according to the undoubted interpretation of the N. T., nay, the clear meaning of the words: here the prophecy is held, not equally clearly: nor is it explained in the N. Test., and according to this explanation the history is only woven through. There the son of the Haalma, the virgin, is openly commemorated: here there is only mention of the son of the Prophetess, who is not expressly said to be the son of the virgin. There the son is introduced as ἀπάτωρ, because the mother is a virgin, from whom also his name is imposed: here is a son of such a kind, who has a father and mother; before the boy calls Father and Mother, etc. There the son about to be born, Immanuel, God with us, θεάνθρωπος, the Lord of Judea, whose is the fullness of all that land, is designated; but that this one, who is commemorated in ch. 8, should be the θεάνθρωπος or the Lord of Judea, is not so clear from the bowels of the text, nay, a different name is imposed upon him, Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz. There a sign is given of the preservation of the Davidic house: here, however, of the destruction of Damascus and Samaria. Add that Immanuel is opposed to the machinations of the enemies, as the perennial Lord of Judea, and the dissipator of the enemies' counsels, not Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz, even where he had already been introduced, and had obtained that name: and that the son of Isaiah could hardly be opposed to the enemies and the confederations of the foes, being most unequal to that task. Gather yourselves, O ye people, and be broken in pieces; take counsel together, and it shall come to nought: speak the word, and it shall not stand, because Immanuel. Who will believe that the son of Isaiah is pointed out here, or even in the preceding words. And the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. By what reason is the land of Judah called the land of the son of the Prophet, who obtained no dominion or empire in it? Whence he confesses by the force of truth, R. David Kimchi himself admits that Immanuel cannot be understood as the son of Isaiah. And who does not see that Grotius devised this opinion of his—that the Prophet approached a virgin distinguished by the gift of prophecy and took her in marriage—at least to the end that he might crush the prophecy concerning the birth of a virgin? For he has no author for this fiction, nor could he name one; which, therefore, must be credited to his own poetic genius. Forsooth, because painters and poets have always had an equal power of daring anything! Witnesses were not brought in to marry a prophetess, but to sign a symbolic name, and to approach a prophetess is not to join her to oneself in marriage. It is established that in the Hebrew phrase, especially when it is subjoined to it concerning a woman, 'and she conceived and bore,' something else is indicated, namely, sexual intercourse, not a nuptial betrothal. And can the wife of the Prophet, from whom Shear-Jashub was born, not be understood? Who can be called הנביאה, a prophetess, both because she was the wife of the Prophet, and because in bringing forth this prophetic and ominous birth, she did not sustain a private person, but a public one. Nor must it be conceded to Grotius that that long name signifies the decree of God concerning the summoning of Sennacherib. For another explanation of the symbolic name is subjoined in verse 4: 'The strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the King of the Assyrians,' which Grotius interprets thus: 'Strength' here signifies wealth. Wealth and spoils of the ten tribes, as trophies, will be carried off to the king of Assyria. These things are far different from the decree of God concerning the summoning of Sennacherib against the Jews, and they were fulfilled when from Samaria—that is, the Israelitic kingdom, which is so denominated from its metropolis—many cities and provinces subject to Samaria as the head of the kingdom were snatched away, as in 2 Kings 15:29. 1 Par. 5:26, almost five tribes are said to have been transported from the Israelitic kingdom. Similarly, concerning the taking away of the strength of Damascus, one may read in 2 Kings 15:9.

Verse 8. FILLING THE BREADTH OF THY LAND, O IMMANUEL] Nothing of either fields or towns will remain untouched. He addresses the boy as a witness of these future evils.

How would Isaiah address his little son, then not yet born? How would he call him a witness of these evils about to happen thereafter? How would he claim the land and region of Judah for his son, who did not even have a single small town in it? It is manifest that the true and proper Lord of the land is being addressed, that the Prophet is complaining before Him, and provoking His help and patronage, so that He, whose Immanuel the Messiah was the Lord and supreme Protector, might not look upon this occupation of His land—which He had chosen as His own possession—as an idle spectator, but might deign to have mercy on His land and assert and vindicate it from the power of the enemies. He is called Immanuel, therefore, as Judge and avenger, nay, as the supreme Lord and defender of His land, not as a mere witness of future evils. For this reason, He also promises His most present help immediately. Gather yourselves, O peoples (you Assyrians and their allies, as the Grotian interpretation has it), and be overcome (the imperative being placed for the future): be overcome, namely, by God, who will destroy the army of Sennacherib. Thus Grotius. He designates the same victor whom he had previously made the Lord, avenger, and protector of Judea; therefore he adds: 'Speak the word and it shall not stand: for here (on the side of the land and people of Judea) is IMMANUEL.' Here, therefore, will be the victor and the Defender of His land and His people.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET ERIT EXTENSIO ALARUM EJUS] Alas Hebræi vocant omnes copias, non equestres tantum, ut Latini, sed & pedestres excursurum, aut etiam finium munimenta.

ASsumit hic iterum Grotius ipse nonnulla, quæ probatione indigent, & ab aliis minime conceduntur; utpote quod Esaias aliam uxorem, rem, priori sive defuncta, seu superstite, ex qua Schear-Jaschub prognatus erat, duxerit; quod ac- cessus ad Prophetissam sit conjugii gratia factus, aut συνουσίαν inferat connubialem:quod tum tem- poris virgo prophetiæ dono clara extiterit, quam sibi in uxorem sumserit Propheta: quod ex ea filiū susceperit:quod filio ex illa uxore novella procre- ato nomen illud bene longum imposuerit;quod te- stes isti adhibiti fuerint in ducenda uxore; quod ii- dem etiam in imponendo isto nomine ceu testes adhibiti sint; de quibus ex historia sacra ne apicem proferre potest. Admissis vero illis omnibus gra- vissime tamen hallucinatur, cum hunc eundem E- saiæ filium credit esse filium virginis, de quo se- ptimo Capite vaticinatus est Propheta. Ubi vero de virgine intemerata concipiente & pariente, non de virgine nupta, neque de ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, sed de eo, qui vere est Immanuel θεανθρωπος, vaticina- tum esse Spiritum Sanct. jam demonstratum. Re- periuntur sane non pauci ex Interpp. Christianis, qui hic de eodem puero sermonem esse volunt, quo de præcedenti capite actum, sed hi utrobique U- nice Christum Beatæ virginis filium intelligunt, ei- que & Immanuelis & hoc præsens nomen Mahar- Schalal-Haschbaz impositum esse volunt. Grotiana autem interpretatio judaizat prorsus, siquidem cum Judæis velit hic complementum haberi vatici- nii superioris, cum Propheta virginem duxit, & ex ea filium suscepit. Ponamus autem cum Gro- tio, eandem rem proponi hoc & præcedenti capite, annon præstabit cum Patribus antiquis Justino Martyre, Irenæo, Origene, Epiphanio, Athanasio, Ba- silio, Ambrosio, Hieronymo & Augustino ac Interpp. aliis Christianis præcipui nominis, locum etiam præ- sentem de Messiæ conceptione & partu explicare, quam cum Judæis nominis Christiani hostibus ἀ- σπόνδοις utrumque locum de conceptione & partu filii Esaiæ interpretari, & utrobique Christum literali sensu excludere, ipsique Sp. Sancti interpre- tationi in N. T. traditae palam contradicere? Ne- que vero rationibus destitui videtur illa interpre- tatio veterum. Quum enim capite septimo juxta indubitatam Sp. Sancti interpretationem de Mes- siae nativitate agatur, ac nono iterum capite ejus nativitas praedicatur v. 6. intermedium octavum ca- put videtur pariter de ipso accipiendum esse. Tum vero insignis hic apparet convenientia cum oracu- lo Cap. VII. Nam ibi praedicitur: Ecce virgo concipiet, & pariet filium. Hic Prophetissa, inquit Esaias, concepit & peperit filium: ibi ad mandatum Domini nomen ei imponendum: Hic pariter id praecipit Deus, Dixit Dominus ad me, voca no- men ejus. Ibi additur, quia antequam sciat puer reprobare malum & eligere bonum, derelinquetur terra, quam tu detestaris, a facie duorum regum suo- rum. Hic non absimiliter: Quia antequam sciat puer vocare patrem suum & matrem suam, aufere- tur fortitudo Damasci & spolia Samariae coram Rege Assyriorum. Porro nomen utrumque Christo apprime convenit, qui Immanuel est, quod Deus nobiscum sit naturae consortio, & gratiae auxilio, & Mahar-Salal-Hasbaz, quod acceleret spolia detrahe- re & festinet praedari hostes populi sui, quod sit velox praedator, & festinus spoliator non tantum hostium spiritualium, sed etiam corporalium. Antea, in- quit Brentius in h. l. vocatus est Christus cognomine suo Immanuel, quod significat, Nobiscum Deus, ut confirmetis fidem vestram & cognoscatis, cum divina potentia praesto adesse, ut etiam hoc tempore vos & re- gnum vestrum conservet. Nunc autem vocatur ve- lox praedator & festinus spoliator, ut iterum confir- metis fidem vestram, & agnoscatis, quod sicut regnum vestrum clementer conservat, ita potenter ac velociter spoliaturus, praedaturus & oppressurus sit hostes ve- stros. Haec Brent. Neque etiam videtur repu- gnare promissio: antequam sciat puer vocare pa- trem suum & matrem suam, derelinquetur terra. Quae sive intelligantur de puero quocunque indefini- te, sive etiam de hoc puero, de Messia, quod prius- quam fari didicerit, jam de fortitudine & spoliis Damasci & Samariae actum sit. Nam licet longe ante nativitatem Christi hoc completum fuerit, hic tamen Christi nativitas velut in praesenti sisti- tur, & antequam Christus ita conceptus progeni- tusque Patrem & matrem compellare didicerit, promittitur ablatio virium & spoliorum utriusque regni, a quo Judaei sibi metuebant. Intelligunt enim haec de conceptione &partu quasi gesta in vi- sione, ideoque etiam in visione designati hic erunt anni pueritiae. Observant etiam Interpp. illi, quod in Graeco LXX. Interpp. textu ablatio illa for- titudinis & spoliorum puero ipsi tribuatur, ante- quam sciat Patrem & matrem compellare: in quam sententiam etiam ipse Ebraeus textus accipi potest. Antequam sciat puer vocare patrem & matrem, au- feret fortitudinem Damasci & spolia Samariae. Ju- stinus Martyr Tryphonem urget in Dial. p. mihi 236. quod puer, antequam norit appellare Patrem aut matrem, accepturus sit virtutem Damasci. At vos, inquit, alicui unquam Judaeorum hoc accidisse, pro- bare non potestis, nos autem demonstrare quimus fa- ctum hoc esse Christo nostro. Explicat autem ita, quod maligni Daemonis, Damascum incolentis, potestatem debellatum iri per Christum, quam primum genitus esset, significatum fuerit. Quod pariter urget Ire- naeus lib. III. adv. haeref. Cap. XVIII. nec non Cyrill. Alexandr. cujus verba adscribo. Quoniam Deus natura existens factus est nobiscum sermo, qui appa- ruit nostra specie, denotari Immanuelis nomine sa- pientissime potuit, deinde factus homo, cum dessoli- esset Satanam, & olim abreptos, eique per peccatam servientes ab illius tyrannide eripuisset, exercuit & declaravit illud: Velociter spoliato, cito prædator. Quod etiam ut Deus redemptionem humanam inex- plicabili virtute perfecturus sit, premonstravit di- cens: Priusquam noverit puerPatrem vel matrem, auferet potentiam Damasci & spolia Samariæ cum Rege Assyriorum. Hæc Cyrillus. Paulo aliter quidem Ebræa reddit, puero tamen Salutem po- puli adversus Syros & Israëlitas adscribit Hierony- mus in h. l. Præcipitur Esaiæ, ut ipsum puerum, qui prius vocabatur Emmanuel, nunc appellet accelera, spolia detrahe, festina prædari. Ascendens enim in altum captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona ho- minibus, & antequam humanum corpus assumeret & juxta infantiam Patrem vocaret Deum & ma- trem Mariam, auferetur Damasci fortitudo & spolia Samariæ per Regem Assyriorum, ut nec-dum natus populum suum domum David sola invocatione SAL- VARET. Denique id etiam urgent nonnulli, quod non congruat Chronologia, si verba simpli- citer quoad literam accipiantur, quia Zacharias fi- lius Barachiæ, qui hic testis adducitur, 170. annis po- sterior fuit Esaia: quoque Urias infidelis & idolo- rum cultor, non videatur adhibendus fuisse ad testimonium rei tam sanctæ & eximiæ perhiben- dum: imo quod absurdum plane ac parum hone- stum videatur, Esaiam cum uxore, testibus aliquot præsentibus, congressum fuisse, quod tamen dicen- dum videtur, si verba illa literaliter & de filio Esaiæ exponenda sint: neque constet, uxorem Esaiæ Pro- phetissam fuisse. Unde censent, hæc omnia Esaiæ in visione contigisse & immediate ac literaliter ad Messiam referenda esse, perque Prophetissam Ma- riam virginem intelligi, quæ vere vaticinata est de potentia brachii Domini Luc. 1, 52. de susceptione Israelis v. 54. deǵ; beatitudinis suæ celebratione penes generationes futuras v. 50. Sensum itaque hunc red- dunt Interpp. nonnulli: Accessi ad Prophetissam, id est, visus sum mihi accedere (in revelatione & vi- sione Prophetica ad virginem Mariam, quæ Pro- phetissa vocatur; ostensa ea mihi fuit in visione, ut ad eam accederem, & accessi), annunciaturus illi, fore, ut pareret filium, & concepit & peperit filium, in visione sc. Prophetica. (vidi in revelatione divi- na eam concipere per singularem inumbrationem Sp. Sancti, ac parere filium.) Quo facit illud Cyrilli sub initium Cap. I. Esaiæ; Siquis dicat, sanctos Pro- phetas non solum rerum futurarum cognitionem ac- cepisse, prælucente hic illis & in animos insinuante Sancto Spiritu, verum etiam rerum ipsarum quan- doq; spectatores extitisse, eum ego minime errare posse arbitror. Secutus eam sententiam est D. Osiander in Paraphr. qui vero, quod dicitur, testibus adhibi- tis, ad publicam nominis istius Prophetici descri- ptionem refert, idque non in visione tantum, sed revera gestum esse censet, adeoque Uriam in testi- monium illud adscitum vult, antequam descisceret à sincera Religione, nec non Zachariam filium Bara- chiæ, non illum è Prophetis, quos ita vocant, mino- ribus, neque istum, qui lapidatus fuisse scribitur 2. Paralip. 24. sed alium hoc nomine appellatum. Nec abs re observant alii, quod hic Zacharias non filius Berachiæ, sed Jeberechiæ, ideoque videri fuisse Socerum Achazi, avum maternum Ezechie, cujus mentio sit, 2. Par. 29, 2. aut illum de filiis Assaph, qui commemorantur 2. Par. 29, 13. quem Grotius eundem putat cum Zacharia Propheta, & vidente Deum tempore Oziæ, 2. Par. 26, 5. sed non videtur hic Oziæ tempora supervixisse, nedum Ezechiæ re- gnum attigisse; siquidem de Ozia dicatur, quod exquifiverit saltim Dominum in diebus Zachariæ, intelligentis & videntis Deum, adeoque innuatur Dominum non requisivisse post fata Zachariæ. Sunt, qui hæc ad Spiritum Sanctum referant, non ad Prophetam, quasi dicat Sp. Sanctus Prophetæ: Adhibebo mihi testes fideles. Et accedam ad virgi- nem Mariam (per specialem ἐπιέλευσιν) & conci- piet & pariet filium, qui destructurus est hostes suos; ut Prophetica hic habeantur de futura illa miracu- losa ἐπιλεύσει Sp. Sancti super Θεοτόκον, per quam concipiendus erat Filius Dei. Juxta quam ex- plicationem dici poterit, utut notum sit, quid Phrasi Ebræa, accedere ad mulierem, imprimis, cum subjicitur, & concepit & peperit, significetur, hic tamen peculiarem ejus esse rationem, uti partus i- pse singularis plane est, qui prædicitur.

Non videtur facile reprobanda hæc magno- rum Dd. antiquiorum pariter ac recentiorum au- toritate suffulta explicatio. Sensum pium & sen- sum speciosum esse, agnoscit etiam Spanhemius in Dub. Evangel. pag. 327. etsi in omnia alia eat. Si cui tamen illa de accessu in visione, vel etiam de ἐπι- λεύσει Sp. Sancti ac de B. virgine Prophetissa, paulo argutiora videantur, ac de Propheta, ejusque uxore hæc secundum literalem sensum interpretari cum plerisq; Reformatis malit, quod puero ex Prophe- ta nato nomen Symbolicum imponendum fuerit, ad significandam cladem Syriæ & Samariæ inferen- dam, ut historica omnia sint, de nomine in tabula publica scribendo & testibus eam in rem adhibendis (ut constet, & peculiari Dei consilio & Prophetæ studio ad mandatum Dei, Symbolicum hoc no- men descriptum publiceque propositum esse,) de Prophetæ accessu ad Prophetissam, & susceptione filii ex eadem, & nominibus illis eidem impositis ejusdem rei significandæ & confirmandæ gratia: nihil adhuc tamen pro sua opinione obtinebit Judaizans Gro- tius, scilicet quod Immanuel itidem sit Prophetæ filius. Nam diversa, multumque disparia sunt loca; Ibi vaticinium habetur c. 7, 14. juxta indubita- tam N. T. interpretationem, imo claram verbo- rum sententiam: Hic vaticinium haberi, non æque luculentum est: neque in N. Test. id exponitur & juxta hanc explicationem historia tantum pertexi- tur. Ibi filius Haalma virginis aperte commemo- ratur: hic filii Prophetissæ tantum mentio sit, quem vero filium virginis fore expresse non dicitur. Ibi filius ἀπάτωρ introducitur, quia mater virgo, à qua etiam nomen ei imponitur: hic filius ejusmo- di, qui Patrem & matrem habet; antequam puer ap- pellet Patrem & matrem &c. Ibi filius nasciturus Immanuel Deus nobiscum θεάνθρωπος, Dominus Judææ, cujus est plenitudo totius istius terræ, designa- tur; hunc autem, qui c. 8. commemoratur, fore θεάν- θρωπον aut Judææ Dominum, non ita è visceribus textus liquet, imo diversum nomen ei imponitur Maher-Schalal-Chas-baz. Illic signum datur con- servationis domus Davidicæ: hic vero destructio- nis Damasci, & Samariæ. Adde quod Immanuel op- ponatur hostium machinationibus, ut Iudææ Do- minus perennis, & dissipator consiliorum hostium, non Maher-Schalal-Chas-baz, etiam ubi hic jam introductus, idque nominis adeptus erat: quod- que Esaiæ filius hostibus, ac confœderationibus inimicorum opponi haud potuerit, maxime ad id impar. Congregamini populi & vincimini, inite consilium & dissipabitur: loquimini verbum & non fiet, quia Immanuel. Quis hic filium Esaiæ indi- gitari credet, aut etiam in verbis antecedentibus. Et erit extensio alarum ejus implens latitudinem ter- ræ tuæ ô Immanuel. Qua ratione terra Judæ vo- catur terra filii Prophetæ, qui nullum in ea domi- nium vel imperium obtinuit? Unde fatetur vi ve- ritatis coactus ipse R. David Kimchi, non posse per Immanuel intelligi Esaiæ filium. Et quis non vi- det, Grotium hanc sententiam suam, quod acces- serit Propheta ad virginem dono prophetiæ claram, eamque assumserit in matrimonium, saltem eum in finem excogitasse, ut elideret Prophetiam de par- tu virginis? Hujus enim commenti autorem nul- lum habet, aut nominare potuit; quod proinde ipsius Poëtico ingenio acceptum ferendum est. Scilicet quia Pictoribus atque Poëtis quodlibet au- dendi semper fuit æqua potestas! Non ad ducendum virginem Prophetissara, sed ad consignandum nomen Symbolicum testes adhibiti, neque accedere ad Prophetissam est eam matrimonio sibi copulare. Aliud phrasi Ebræa, imprimis cum subjungitur ei de mu- liere, & concepit & peperit, indigitari constat, συ- νεσίαν nempe, non desponsationem connubialem. Et annon intelligi potest uxor Prophetæ, è qua Sear- Jaschub prognatus est? Quæ הנביאה Prophe- tissa dici potest, tum quia uxor Prophetæ fuit, tum quia in partu hoc Prophetico & ominoso edendo non privatam sustinuit personam, sed publicam. Ne- que concedendum Grotio est, nomen illud bene longum decretum Dei de advocando Sennacheribo significare. Alia enim explicatio nominis Sym- bolici subjungitur versu 4. Auferetur fortitudo Damsci, & spolia Samariæ coram Rege Assyriorum, Quæ ita interpretatur Grotius: Fortitudo hic opes significat. Opes & spolia tum decem tribuum, tan- quam trophæa perferentur ad regem Assyriæ. Hæc longe diversa sunt à decreto Dei de advocando ad- versus Judæos Sennacheribo, & impleta sunt, cum Samariæ, hoc est regno Israëlítico, quod à Me- tropoli sic denominatur, urbes & provinciæ mul- tæ Samariæ ceu capiti regni subjectæ, ereptæ fue- runt, uti 2. Reg. 15, 29. 1. Par. 5, 26. quinque pene tribus è regno Israëlítico transportatæ dicuntur. Similiter de ablatione fortitudinis Damasci legere est 2. Reg. 15. v. 9.

Vers. 8. IMPLENS LATITUDINEM TERRÆ TUÆ, O IMMANUEL] Nihil aut agrorum aut oppidorum ma- nebit intactum. Puerum alloquitur testem futurorum horum malorum.

Quomodo filiolum suum alloqueretur Esaias tum nondum natum? quomodo illum testem ho- rum malorum appellaret deinceps eventurorum? quomodo filio suo terram & regionem Juda ven- dicaret, qui ne oppidulum quidem ullum in ea- dem habebat? Manifestum est, terræ verum & proprium Dominum compellari, coram eo queri Prophetam, ejus provocare opem & patrocinium, ut hanc occupationem terræ suæ, quam in pecu- lium elegerat, cujus Dominus Rex ac supremus Protector erat Immanuel Messias, non otiosus spe- ctator intueatur, sed terræ suæ misereri dignetur, eamque à potestate hostium adserat atque vindi- cet. Appellatur ergo Immanuel, ut Judex & vin- dex, imo ut supremus Dominus & defensor terræ suæ, non uti nudus testis malorum futurorum. Ideo etiam præsentissimum ejus auxilium actutum pol- licetur. Congregamini populi (vos Assyrii eorum- que socii, ut habet interpretatio Grotiana) & vin- cimini (imperativo posito pro futuro:) vincimini nem- pe à Deo, qui Sennacheribi exercitum destruet. Ita Grotius. Victorem designat eundem, quem an- tea Dominum vindicem ac protectorem Judææ fe- cerat, ideo addit: Loquimini verbum & non fiet: quia hic (à parte Judææ terræ populique) IMMA- NUEL. Hic ergo victor erit, & Hyperaspistes terræ suæ ac populi sui.

## 8:9
Verse 9. GATHER YOURSELVES, O PEOPLES] You Assyrians, and their allies. It is a concession.

AND BE OVERCOME] Here also the imperative is for the future, as above. Be overcome, namely, by God, who will destroy the army of Sennacherib.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CONGREGAMINI POPULI] Vos Assyrii, eorumque socii. Est συγχώρησις.

ET VINCIMINI] Hic quoque imperativus est pro futuro, ut supra. Vincemini nempe a Deo, qui Senna- cheribi exercitum destruet.

## 8:10
FOR GOD IS WITH US] Here he explains the force of the former name given to the boy. God is with us, that is, God is our helper. See what was said at the end of Matthew.

He does not so much explain the force of the name as repeat the name itself, and opposes Him who is designated by that name to the enemies of the Jews. For there is no reason why we should take that name here as an appellative, since it can be understood as a proper name, nor has it been accepted otherwise thus far: nay, not only is it manifest from chapter 7:14 that that name is a proper name, imposed upon the virgin's Son, the Messiah, but also that in this very chapter 8:8 it must undoubtedly be understood as a proper name, and all the confidence of the people was to be placed in the gracious protection and assistance of the Messiah, Ps. 2:13, 14; Ps. 24:8; Ps. 45:4; Ps. 72:12; Ps. 110:5, etc. Those things which Grotius noted at the end of Chapter 1 of Matthew (for he points to these), we have seen and discussed before.

Latin:

QUIA NOBISCUM DEUS] Hic explicat vim prioris nominis puero dati. Nobiscum Deus, id est, Deus adjutor noster. Vide quae dicta ad finem Matthaei.

Non tam vim nominis explicat, quam nomen ipsum repetit, & Eum, qui nomine illo designatur, hostibus Judaeorum opponit. Non enim causa est, cur nomen illud ut appellativum hic accipia- mus, quum intelligi possit, ut nomen proprium, ne- que aliter hactenus acceptum fuerit: imo non mo- do e cap. 7, 14. manifestum sit, nomen illud pro- prium esse, virginis Filio Messiae impositum, sed et- iam hoc ipso c. 8, 8. ut nomen proprium indubita- to intelligendum sit, omnisqua fiducia populi col- locanda fuerit in praesidio & assistentia Messiae gra- tiosa Ps. 2, 13. 14. Ps. 24, 8. Ps. 45, 4. Ps. 72, 12. Ps. 110, 5. &c. Ea, quae Grotius ad finem Cap. 1. Mat- thaei (haec enim indigitat) annotavit, ante vidimus & discussimus.

## 8:11
Verse 11.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

## 8:11
FOR THUS THE LORD SAITH TO ME: AS WITH A STRONG HAND HE INSTRUCTED ME] Better: When He had instructed me with a strong hand: that is, when He had added courage to me with His exhortations. For with those words, what follows is connected to me: 'Sanctify the Lord of hosts Himself.' The rest have the force of a parenthesis.

Latin:

HAEC ENIM AIT DOMINUS AD ME: SIC- UT IN MANU FORTI ERUDIVIT ME] Melius: Cum in manu forti erudisset me: id est, cum animum mihi addidisset suis hortamentis. Nam cum illis ad me cohaeret quod sequetur, Dominum exercituum ipsum sanctificate. Caetera vim habent παρενθέσεως.

## 8:12
Verse 12.

DO NOT SAY: A CONSPIRACY] Supply, let it be: do not say with the others: come, let us conspire with the enemies against our king.

FOR ALL THAT THIS PEOPLE SAYS, A CONSPIRACY] In the Hebrew: to all that this people shall say, a conspiracy. That is, as often as this people stirs up defection in their mind, such as many were already at this very time plotting with the Syrians and Israelites, above 6, and according to the Hebrews, the same was plotted against Sennacherib by the one named Sobna below 22, 15, with 130,000 men, as the same Hebrews say.

AND DO NOT FEAR HIS FEAR, NOR BE AFRAID] Do not add yourselves to their dread.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

NON DICATIS: CONJURATIO] Supple, fiat: ne dicite cum caeteris: age conjuremus cum hostibus con- tra regem nostrum.

OMNIA ENIM QUAE LOQUITUR POPULUS ISTE, CONJURATIO] In Hebraeo: ad omnia quum po- pulus iste dicet conjuratio. Id est, quoties populus iste de- fectionem animo agitat, qualem multi jam hoc ipso tem- pore ad Syros & Israelitas moliebantur, supra 6. & secun- dum Hebraeos molitus idem est ad Sennacheribum Sobna nominatus infra 22, 15. cum hominum CXXX. milli- bus, ut ajunt iidem Hebraei.

ET TIMOREM EJUS NE TIMEATIS, NEQUE PAVEATIS] Nolite illorum pavori vosmet addere.

## 8:14
Verse 14.

AND HE SHALL BE TO YOU FOR A SANCTIFICATION.] In the Hebrew: for a Sanctuary: that is, a place of asylum.

BUT FOR A STONE OF OFFENSE AND FOR A ROCK OF SCANDAL TO THE TWO HOUSES OF ISRAEL] That is, to the people of the ten tribes, and to the people of the two tribes. He who strikes against a hard stone falls heavily.

FOR A SNARE AND FOR A RUIN TO THOSE DWELLING IN JERUSALEM] Not to the whole city, which was preserved both at this time and under Sennacherib, but to many of them, as follows, namely those who will deem it better to follow the faith of the enemies than to await the fates of the city.

Who is he, who is said here to be about to be a stone of offense and of whom the rest is to be understood? Grotius does not admit that the Messiah is designated here: but there are many things which prove it. For first, the Lord speaks of the Lord: The Lord said to me: Sanctify the Lord of Hosts; therefore distinct divine persons are designated, as elsewhere throughout, where the Lord speaks of the Lord, the Father of the Son. Then God, whom they ought to have feared, and under whose protection they could live safely, and had no need to fear the conspiracies of enemies, was expressed a little before in verse 10, namely that He is IMMANUEL, the Lord of Judah, that is, the Messiah. Thirdly, they are commanded elsewhere to fear Him, Ps. 2, verse 11, serve, says David, the LORD, speaking of this LORD, in fear, and rejoice to Him with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest the Lord be angry and you perish from the righteous way. Fourthly, as he is made here peculiarly for us by the Lord for sanctification, 1 Cor. 1:30, so also the faithful are warned here concerning him: He shall be to you for sanctification. For in no other ought they to glory than in this Lord, Jer. 9:22, 1 Cor. 1:31, 2 Cor. 10:17. Fifthly, those who in such prophecies and in necessities of this kind were to be recalled to the Messiah, that they might learn to place their hope and trust in that one alone: outside of whom there is no salvation under heaven, Acts 4:12. Sixthly, a parallel passage in this very Prophet, ch. 28, confirms this, where (after Isaiah had threatened the unfaithful there, that they would fall backward, be broken, and be snared, and be taken:) he promises grace to the faithful, namely those who have believed in the Messiah, in contrast, and presents the Messiah by a similar metaphor as a stone in Zion, placed as a foundation of Zion or the Church: against whom those stumbling through unbelief fall backward and are broken, but those who believe are not confounded, v. 13, 16. The words in both places are the same when they are used of those offending through unbelief: they shall fall against this stone, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken, ch. 8, so that they may go and fall backward, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken, ch. 28:13. And that these passages are entirely parallel, and ought to be understood of Christ, St. Peter seventhly openly teaches, 1 Ep. 2:7, comparing and joining, as if predicted of Christ, analogous oracles concerning that stone rejected by the Architects, made the head of the corner, Ps. 118:21, placed in Zion as a chief cornerstone, elect, precious, in whom he who shall have believed shall not be confounded, Is. 28:16, who was to be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the unfaithful, Is. 8:14. According to this interpretation, therefore, it is not permitted to doubt that the present prophecy is to be understood of Christ. Eighthly, Paul explains this of Christ, Rom. 9:33, joining likewise those Isaiah passages, ch. 8:14 and 28:16, for they stumbled at the stone of stumbling; as it is written: Behold I place in Zion a stone (precious, which according to the intention of GOD was placed as a foundation of salvation and faith, Isaiah 28:16, but by the fault of men was to be a stone against which the Israelites themselves would stumble through unbelief, Isa. 8:14, and therefore ἐκβατικῶς and δικαστικῶς by a judicial will and consequently placed by GOD as a stone) of stumbling and a rock of offense. And everyone who believes in him shall not be confounded. Similarly, ninthly, St. Simeon points his finger to this prophecy, Luke 2:34. Behold this one is set FOR THE FALL and for the rising of many, just as Isaiah here: He shall be FOR A SNARE AND FOR A FALL to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Tenthly, although we do not deny that the unfaithful of those times are particularly looked upon; yet the object is the same, against which the unfaithful stumble at all times, concerning which they are repeatedly warned in the Prophets, so that he may be to them for sanctification, so that namely they may receive him through faith, and seek in him righteousness and sanctification, and that he may not be a stone of stumbling to them, against which by stumbling they are broken. Which exhortation (παρακλήσει) those afflicted in those times especially needed. Since therefore this general exhortation and rule, that the Messiah ought to be received through faith, and once received provides salvation, and that we must take the greatest pains lest we stumble against this stone through unbelief, lest we fall and be broken, is here in a special case and necessity, as is wont to happen, proposed by the Prophets to the people of GOD, the Apostles most rightly accepted these things concerning the faithful and the incredulous of the New Testament: and no less rightly are those things understood concerning the faithful and the unfaithful in the time of Isaiah:

because, as I said, they are general, and the same object is at all times proper to faith and unbelief. Cf. Acts 10:43. Eleventhly, similar passages are added, in which it is likewise predicted that the Messiah is to be an offense to his people. Here especially are to be compared Ps. 118:22, Isa. 52:13, ch. 53:1, Matt. 21:42, Mark 6:3, Luke 4:22, 1 Cor. 1:23. What? That finally the Jews themselves explain a similar passage, Ps. 118:22, concerning the Messiah; the Targum namely, as also Rashi on Micah 2. The passage in Zech. 3:6, where the Messiah is likewise designated by the name of a stone, the Targum similarly explains concerning the same. We add here the consensus of the Fathers, who interpret with us concerning Christ. It is pleasing to transcribe the words of Cyril: Do not fear their fear, neither be troubled, but rather let the Lord of glory be sanctified by you, that is, Christ, and let him be worshipped by faith and be terrible among you. For he shall be to you for sanctification, nor will you meet him as a stone of stumbling, nor as a rock of ruin. He establishes two great and excellent things in him. For first, he says, he will sanctify you who believe and will make you partakers of his divine nature through the Holy Spirit: and this also will bring gain, that you may not fall as if against a stone nor as against a rock of stumbling. And again: The Lord of all spoke to them concerning Emmanuel: Sanctify the Lord himself and he shall be your fear. And if he has trusted in him, he shall be to you for sanctification. Therefore, one must not rise up here to the Grotian Gloss: He shall be for sanctification, that is, in the place of an asylum. For it is not so much the protection which they were to have from the Lord, as the faith which they were to place in the Lord, that is hinted at, which the opposition teaches: To you he shall be for sanctification; to others for a stone of stumbling. As therefore to these he is a stone of stumbling through unbelief, so to those he is for sanctification through faith. A promise had already been made before concerning the CONQUERING of enemies and the dissipating of their counsels and confederacies by Emmanuel. Now therefore the people are reminded of their duty, that they should place their trust in Emmanuel, and that he himself should be their dread and terror, and be to them for sanctification, which two things imply repentance and faith and thus true conversion. Although the promise also seems to be included here according to the Weimar and Belgian Paraphrasts, because Christ both sanctifies us with his blood and spirit, and is glory, comfort, protection, and asylum to us (as the sanctuary was external) when we receive him himself by faith. Brentius renders it thus on page 130. Isaiah therefore says: There is no reason for you to fear the confederacy of the two kings your enemies. These will not bring destruction to your kingdom, but fear Christ, sanctify Christ, believe in Christ, celebrate the name of Christ, obey the calling of Christ (for by these acts of worship Christ is specified) so that you may obtain sanctification through him. For he is the one who brings true holiness, righteousness, and salvation to those who believe in him. But to the unbelieving, extreme destruction. For so that you may properly know what is to happen to your descendants on account of Christ, hear what the Holy Spirit says: He will be for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, that is, to the whole people of both the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel. Therefore, he understands these things particularly about the Israelites of the New Testament. Finally, we add the confession of Grotius in his annotations to Luke 2, verse 34, where he acknowledges that Isaiah said these things about the Messiah, as interpreted by Paul in Romans 9, verse 33, and Peter in 1 Peter 2, verse 8.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET ERIT VOBIS IN SANCTIFICATIONEM.] In Hebraeo: in Sanctuarium: id est asyli loco.

IN LAPIDEM AUTEM OFFENSIONIS ET IN PETRAM SCANDALI DUABUS DOMIBUS ISRAEL] Id est, populo decem tribuum, & populo duarum tri- buum. Qui in lapidem durum impingit graviter cadit.

IN LAQUEUM ET RUINAM HABITANTI- BUS IN JERUSALEM] Non toti civitati, quae & hoc tempore & sub Sennacheribo servata est, sed multis eo- rum, ut sequitur, nempe iis qui hostium fidem sequi quam civitatis fata opperiri potius ducent.

Quisnam est ille, qui lapis offensionis hic di- citur futurus & de quo caetera intelligenda? Mes- siam hic designari non admittit Grotius: multa autem sunt, quae id probant. Nam primo lo- quitur Dominus de Domino: Dixit Dominus ad me: Sanctificate Dominum Zebaoth; distinctae er- go personae divinae designantur, uti alias passim, ubi Dominus de Domino loquitur, Pater de fi- lio. Deinde Deus, quem ille timere debebant, & sub cujus patrocinio tuti agere poterant, nec timere opus habebant conjurationes hostium, expressus paulo ante erat vers. 10. quod nempe sit IMMANUEL Judae Dominus, hoc est, Mes- sias. Tertio hunc jubentur alias timere Ps. 2. vers. 20. servite, inquit David, DOMINO, de hoc DOMINO agens, in timore, & exul- tate ei cum tremore. Osculamini filium, ne quan- do irascatur Dominus & pereatis de via justa. Quarto uti hic peculiariter nobis factus est a Do- mino in sanctificationem 1. Cor. 1, 30. ita etiam hic monentur de eo fideles: Erit vobis in sanctifica- tionem. In nullo enim alio gloriari debebant, quam in hoc Domino, Jer. 9, 22. 1. Cor. 1, 31. 2. Cor. 10, 17. Quinto revocandi subinde erant, qui in talibus vaticiniis inque ejusmodi necessitatibus, ad Messiam, ut in illo uno spem & fiduciam suam collocare discerent: extra quem salus nulla est sub cœlo, Act. 4, 12. Sexto confirmat id locus paralle- lus in hoc ipso Propheta C. 28. ubi (postquam mi- natus ibidem erat Esaias infidelibus, quod casuri retrorsum, conterendi, & illaqueandi, & capiendi sint :) fidelibus, qui nempe crediderint in Mes- siam, gratiam ex adverso pollicetur, ac Messiam si- mili Metaphora sistit ceu lapidem in Sion, positum in fundamentum Sionis vel Ecclesiæ: in quem im- pingentes per infidelitatem retrorsum cadunt, & conteruntur, credentes autem non confunduntur v. 13. 16. Verba utrobique eadem cum usurpantur de offendentibus per infidelitatem: ad hunc lapidem ca- dent, & conterentur & irretientur, & capientur, C. 8. ut vadant & cadant retrorsum, & conterantur & il- laqueentur & capiantur, C. 28, 13. Atque hæc loca o- mnino parallela esse, ac de Christo intelligi debe- re, porro septimo palam docet S. Petrus 1. Ep. 2, 7. conferens & conjungens, ceu de Christo prædicta, analoga oracula de lapide illo ab Architectis reproba- to, in caput anguli facto Ps. 118, 21. posito in Sion in la- pidem summum angularem, electum, pretiosum, in quem qui crediderit, non confundetur Es. 28, 16. qui in- fidelibus lapis offensionis, & petra scandali futurus e- rat Es. 8, 14. Juxta hanc ergo interpretationem am- bigere non licet, quin præsens vaticinium de Chri- sto intelligendum sit. Octavo de Christo id ex- plicat Paulus Rom. 9. v. 33. conjungens pariter loca illa Esaiana cap. 8. vers. 14. & 28. vers. 16. offende- runt enim in lapidem offensionis; sicut scriptum est: Ecce pono in Sion lapidem (pretiosum, qui juxta intentionem DEI in salutis & fidei fun- damentum ponebatur Esai 28, vers. 16. sed vi- tio hominum lapis futurus erat, in quem Israëlitæ ipsi per infidelitatem impingent Esa. 8. vers. 14. ideoque ἐκβατικῶς & δικαστικῶς voluntate judi- ciaria & consequenti à DEO positum in lapi- dem) offensionis, & petram scandali. Et omnis, qui credit in eum, non confundetur. Similiter no- no digitum intendit ad hoc vaticinium S. Simeon Luc. 2, 34. Ecce positus est hic IN RUINAM & in resurrectionem multorum, quemadmodum hic Esaias: Erit IN LAQUEUM ET IN RUI- NAM habitantibus Jerusalem. Decimo etsi non diffiteamur peculiariter infideles istorum temporum respici; objectum tamen idem est, in quod impingunt omni tempore infideles, de quo subinde monentur in Prophetis, ut ipsis sit in sanctificationem, ut nempe per fidem id sus- cipiant, inque illo justitiam & sanctificationem quærant, acne lapis offensionis iisdem sit, in quem impingendo conterantur. Qua παρακλήσει ma- xime afflicti illis temporibus opus habebant. Quum ergo generalis hæc adhortatio & regula, quod Messias per fidem suscipi debeat, & susceptus sa- lutem præstet, quodque summo studio caven- dum sit, ne impingamus in hunc lapidem per infidelitatem, ne ruamus & conteramur, hic in speciali casu & necessitate, ut fieri amat, à Pro- phetis populo DEI proponatur, rectissime hæc Apostoli de fidelibus & incredulis Novi Testa- menti accepêre: nec minus recte illa de fideli- bus & infidelibus tempore Esaiæ intelliguntur:

quia, uti dixi, generalia sunt, idemque omni tempore objectum est proprium fidei & infideli- tatis. Conf. Actor. 10. vers. 43. Accedunt un- decimo loca similia, in quibus pariter prædici- tur, quod Messias populo suo futurus sit offen- diculo. Conferenda hic imprimis erunt Psalm. 118. vers. 22. Esa. 52. vers. 13. Cap. 53. v. 1. Matth. 21. vers. 42. Marc. 6. vers. 3. Luc. 4. vers. 22. 1. Corinth. 1. vers. 23. Quid? quod postremo Ju- dæi ipsi locum similem Psalm. 118. v. 22. de Mes- sia exponant; Thargum nempe ut & Raschi in Mich. vers. 2. Locum Zach. 3. vers. 6. ubi lapi- dis nomine itidem Messias designatur, de eodem pariter exponit Thargum. Addimus hic con- sensum Patrum, qui nobiscum de Christo in- terpretatur. Cyrilli verba adscribere placet: Timorem eorum ne timueritis, neque turbemini, sed potius sancte colatur à vobis gloriæ Dominus, id est, Christus, & colatur fide & apud vos sit terribilis. Erit enim ille vobis sanctificationi, nec ut lapidi of- fensionis occurretis ei, nec ut petræ ruinæ. Duo constituit in illo magna ac eximia. Primum etenim sanctificabit, inquit, vos qui creditis & participes reddet vos divinæ suæ naturæ per Sanctum Spiritum: atque hoc quoque lucri adferet, ut nec velut in la- pidem nec ut in petram offensionis incidatis. Et rursum: Allocutus est eos universorum Dominus de Emmanuele: Dominum ipsum sancte colite & ille erit tuus timor. Et si ei confisus sit, erit tibi in sanctificationem. Non assurgendum ergo hic Glossæ Grotianæ: Erit in sanctificationem, id est, asyli loco. Nam non tam protectio, quam à Do- mino habituri erant, quam fides, quam in Do- mino collocare debebant, innuitur, quod docet oppositio: Vobis erit in sanctificationem; aliis in lapidem offensionis. Ut ergo his in lapidem offen- sionis est per infidelitatem, ita illis in sanctifica- tionem est per fidem. Promissio jam erat facta antea de VINCENDIS hostibus & dissipandis eorum consiliis & confœderationibus ab Imma- nuele. Jam ergo de officio suo commonetur populus, ut fiduciam in Immanuele collocet, ut- que ipse illorum pavor & terror sit, & sit illis in sanctificationem, quæ duo pænitentiam & fidem adeoque veram conversionem important. Quan- quam etiam hic promissio comprehensa videatur secundum Vinarienses, & Belgicos Paraphrastas, quia Christus & sanctificat nos sanguine ac spiritu suo, & gloria nobis est, solatium, protectio & asylum, (uti externum erat sanctuarium) eum nos ipsum fide suscipimus. Brentius ita reddit pag. 130. Dicit ergo Esaias: Non est quod metuatis con- fœderationem duorum Regum hostium vestro- rum. Hi non afferent regno vestro perniciem, sed metuite Christum, sanctificate Christum, cre- dite in Christum, celebrate nomen Christi, o- bedite vocationi Christi (his enim cultibus spe- cificatur Christus) ut consequamini per ipsum sanctificationem. Hic enim is est, qui affert credentibus in ipsum veram sanctitatem, justi- tiam & salutem. Incredulis autem extrema pernicies. Nam ut probe cognoscatis, quid propter Christum posteris vestris futurum sit, au- dite quid Spiritus Sanctus dicat: Hic erit in la- pidem offensionis & petram scandali duabus do- mibus Israel, hoc est, toti populo tam regni Ju- dæ quam regni Israëlis. Hæc itaque peculia- riter intelligit de Israëlitis Novi Testamenti. Ad- dimus denique confessionem Grotii annot. ad Luc. 2. v. 34. ubi hæc de Messia dixisse Esaiam in- terprete Paulo Rom. 9. v. 33. & Petro 1. Epist. 2. v. 8. agnoscit.

## 8:16
Vers. 16. BIND UP THE TESTIMONY, SEAL THE LAW AMONG MY DISCIPLES] Bind up this testimony, and impose a seal upon it, and give it to be kept to the disciples after thee, so that it may be entirely certain among posterity that these things have been denounced by thee to the king and the people. תּוֹרָה does not everywhere signify law, but also διδαχὴν [teaching]. Thus, the same thing here will be what is meant by testimony.

Latin:

Vers. 16. LIGA TESTIMONIUM, SIGNA LE- GEM IN DISCIPULIS MEIS] Testificationem hanc obliga, & signa ei impone, & da custodiendam discipulis post te, ut omnino apud posteros certum sit hæc abs te re- gi ac populo esse denunciata. תּוֹרָה non ubique legem, sed & διδαχὴν significat. Ita idem hic erit quod testificatio.

## 8:17
Vers. 17. AND I WILL WAIT FOR THE LORD, WHO HIDES HIS FACE FROM THE HOUSE OF JACOB, AND I WILL LOOK FOR HIM] Here, the words of God having finished, Isaiah begins to speak again: wherefore also here is for 'however' in this way: Although God hides his benevolence toward the descendants of Jacob, that is, has not yet shown it by deeds, I, however, relying on his promises, will patiently await his aid.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET EXPECTABO DOMINUM, QUI ABSCONDIT FACIEM SUAM A JACOB, ET PRÆ- STOLABOR EUM] Hic finitis Dei verbis incipit ite- rum Esaias loqui: quare & hic est pro tamen hoc modo : Quanquam Deus benevolentiam suam adversus Jacobi po- steros abscondit, id est, factis nondum ostendit, ego tamen promissis ejus fretus opem ejus patienter opperiar.

## 8:18
Vers. 18. AND THE CHILDREN WHOM THE LORD HAS GIVEN ME ARE FOR A SIGN AND FOR A WONDER IN ISRAEL] Namely, through the names divinely imposed upon them, having a signification of future things.

These are not the words of Isaiah as if speaking of himself, as Grotius wishes, nor as bearing the type of Christ and all the saints, which pleased Oecolampadius and others: but they are the words of the Lord himself. For we have an undoubted interpreter, the Holy Spirit, Heb. 2. v. 11. seqq. For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one; for this cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying: I will announce thy name to my brothers: in the midst of the Church I will praise thee (Psal. 22, 23.) And again, behold I trusting in him; and again: Behold I and my children, whom God has given me. Which words are taken from that passage. If, therefore, the Prophet were speaking here of himself, and not the Lord, the Apostle could not thence prove that the Lord joins us to himself and makes us his brothers. Whence Cyril of Alexandria in this place introduces the person of Emmanuel himself, who grants a spiritual conjunction to those who place their hope in him. For the Son pours out his Spirit into us, and we have become as it were domestic and intimate, and in him we cry, Abba Father. Wherefore he calls us children of God and the Father, as having regeneration through the Spirit, so that we may also be called his brothers, who is by nature truly the Son. Which even the Belgian Interpreters, having deserted their Calvin, acknowledge, namely that these words are of Christ himself. After, therefore, the Lord warned through Isaiah that the people should sanctify the Lord of Hosts, Emmanuel himself now commands the Prophet to bind the testimony, to seal the law among his disciples. They are not the Prophet's disciples, but the Lord's. The Prophet is commanded by the Lord, who speaks here, to bind the law, as the Belgian interpreters here admit. Therefore, by the force of the connection, since the words cohere, the Lord continues the discourse. Whose disciples they are, therefore, his also are the children. But the disciples are the Lord's. Whence rightly B. Bohlius: One cannot soundly ascribe the verse to Isaiah. For hence Rabbi Solomon thinks that 'Thus says the Lord' is to be repeated or reassumed at the word 'and I will wait.' For they ascribe 'I will wait' to Isaiah, but the causal [particle] resists, for he who speaks is bound to give a reason why the law is to be sealed among 'my disciples,' namely because he himself, who speaks with Isaiah, is about to wait with the disciples, and not to provoke the Lord to the example of Isaiah's hearers; hence I say, whose the disciples are, his also are the children. The Osiandrine Paraphrase expresses the sense thus: Now Christ himself speaks of the blindness of the Jewish nation. Bind the testimony, seal the law among my disciples, that is, I see it will come to pass that the testimony or word of GOD will be to my hearers like a volume folded and bound, and as a letter sealed with a ring, so that no one may be able to read what is contained in the will or letter. And yet I will wait for the Lord, that he may have mercy on some at least of the Jews and convert them, who now hides his face from the house of Jacob, and behaves himself as if he had entirely cast off this whole people: and I will wait for him: for he will save some Jews, lest the whole nation perish forever. Moreover, CHRIST refers the salvation of the Jews to the heavenly Father because he speaks in the state of his humiliation (although, however, very few Jews are seriously converted to Christ: yet there is no doubt that that nation is divinely preserved by God among so many enemies, because there are still in it some elect who are about to believe in the Gospel of Christ and to be saved.) Meanwhile, however (says Christ), I have some who believe in me. Behold I (says the Son of God) and the children or sons (of mine) whom the Lord God the Father has given me, whom the heavenly Father has illuminated with my saving knowledge: whom I embrace not only with brotherly, but also with fatherly affection. (The Apostle to the Hebrews, chapter 2, interprets this saying concerning Christ and his faithful.) But we are for a sign and a wonder; more correctly: for signs and wonders, to the people of Israel, that is, men (especially the Jews) will be astonished at the miracles which I and my disciples are about to perform: and at the afflictions which we shall constantly sustain for the sake of the word of the Gospel (For we have been made a spectacle, says Paul, to the world, and to angels, and to men, 1. Corinth. 4.) This will be thus disposed by the Lord of hosts (that is, through the Holy Spirit, the eternal GOD,) who dwells in Mount Zion, who is present to his Church with admirable gifts: and will pour them out upon the Apostles in the city of Jerusalem (See with how much love Christ embraces us: inasmuch as he calls us his children.) Observe also the testimony of the Trinity. These things Osiander. Others [say] that this doctrine is indeed to be bound for the many, to whom it is closed by their own fault, such as were the Pharisees and Priests in the days of Christ's flesh with the greatest part of the people: but to be sealed for others, who through faith have received the same: and are sealed by the Holy Spirit, as those who are truly the disciples of the Messiah, to which the interpretation of the Belgians goes: or that the testimonies of the Old Testament are to be bound for the many, until they are delivered to the disciples of the Messiah under the New Testament, so that they may be openly promulgated, or to be bound so that they may be delivered to the disciples of the Lord as whole and properly bound. St. Jerome teaches that they are to be bound no less than sealed for the disciples: Bind the testimony, etc., the voice of the Lord speaking to the Prophet; because, he says, the Lord has become a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, and they were unwilling to receive the Emmanuel sent to them: Bind the testimonies of the Old Testament, and deliver them to my disciples, who may receive the Gospel, namely the Apostles or Apostolic men. Or certainly, let the law and the prophecy be bound up until John among them and be closed and sealed, so that what they read, they do not understand. But Franciscus Junius understands it as to be bound for some, but to be sealed for others: Bind the testimony, that is, this prophecy and your volume, of which v. 1, wrap it up, so that it may no longer be in the eyes of those people, since as infidels they mock it. Bind the law among my disciples: that is, announce it, commit it, and instruct those whom you know to have been touched by God.

Moreover, those words can entirely be taken in an exegetical and copulative sense: nor is it necessary that they be explained in a disjunctive and antithetical sense, if, namely, the Son of God is said to admonish that the testimony or Gospel be bound in the hearts of the disciples, by which they may be bound to Christ by faith and adhere to him, and the law be sealed or inscribed in the same, by which they may reflect the true obedience of the same as a figure in their lives and actions. To which Brentius's exposition almost tends: Although very many Israelites and citizens of Jerusalem may be offended in me and fall, nevertheless there will remain among them some pious ones, who will be my disciples, and in whom the testimony and the law shall be bound and sealed, that is, by whom my Gospel shall be received, and in whom it shall be so confirmed by the seal of the Holy Spirit, that they embrace it with great faith and adhere to it with their whole heart. Therefore, Grotius’s gloss does not deserve approval: Bind this testimony, and put signs upon it, and give it to the disciples to keep after you, so that it may be altogether certain among posterity that these things were denounced by you to the King and the people. These things are too jejune. For the antecedent and consequent parts prove that the Lord is not only looking to this prophecy, but that these sentences extend more widely and concern the entire heavenly doctrine, of which the believers are disciples. Therefore, in all these things, the Lord Messiah now presents himself as an example of true and constant trust: I will wait for the Lord, who hides his face from Jacob, and I will look for him. Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel. For if the Messiah himself waited for the Lord, why should Ahaz not be bound to wait for him? What connection does Bohlius provide: If the Messiah waited for the Lord, that he might have mercy on Jacob, when he had altogether hidden his face from him, and his expectation and trust were not in vain, then by his example the Jews were certainly bound to wait for the Lord and place their trust in him, from whom the Lord had not yet at that time so altogether hidden his face. For the Messiah is given to all as a merit and an example, whose disciples and imitators the Jews especially ought to have been, so that the law and the testimony of the Lord might be sealed in them. Since the Messiah, who was to arise from the posterity of Jacob, the lineage of Judah, and the house of David in the fullness of time, was to wait for the Lord when the Lord would appear to have altogether turned his face away from Jacob, the house of David, Ahaz with his own, and the entire Jewish people could be certain that the enemies would not now prevail, nor would the Davidic family or the Jewish people and their polity be reduced to extremities, just as the enemies were threatening. But if those things which precede concerning the offense at the stone of stumbling, the fall and contrition of the people, by which the Israelites were to be cast off on account of unbelief, and those who were to receive the Gospel were to be sealed, are explained with Brentius as referring to the time of the New Testament, the Messiah will be said to be waiting for the Lord, who hides his face from Jacob and threatens that he will cast off the descendants of Jacob, and waiting for those whom he will give to himself, whether from the Jews or from the Gentiles, so that he may receive them and protect and save them to eternal life. Now, therefore, Christ presents himself and testifies that he is not without children and disciples, whom the Lord has given him, even if they are for a sign and a wonder in Israel. Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me. Which passage the Epistle to the Hebrews examined with such keenness of the Holy Spirit, as our Brentius speaks, that it clearly teaches that Christ is proclaiming in these words that he will be a partaker of human flesh. For thus he writes in chapter 2: Behold, I and my children, whom God has given me. Since, therefore, the children have a share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise became a partaker of the same, that through death he might abolish him who had the power of death, that is, the Devil, and might set free those who through fear of death were subject to slavery throughout their whole life. This, however, is not to be thought of idly, but to be transferred into use, so that we may not only know that it was predicted by the Prophets that the Son of God would assume human flesh, but also that he would bestow his heavenly benefits upon all those who believe in him, so that just as he is a partaker of human flesh and blood, so those who have human flesh and blood, and believe in him, may become partakers of his victory, which he won over death and the Devil. Then he says that his disciples will be signs and wonders among men.
