Ezech. 22, 7. הכביד pro honorare, Jer. 30, 19. והכבדתים ולא יצערו honore eos affi- ciam, & non habebuntur exigui, est enim צער parvum esse, parvi pendi. Sensus est: Etsi graviter terram suam Deus sit afflicturus, non passurus tamen, ut in tenebris penitus delitescat. Sed sicut eam olim contemtui expo- fuerit, sic tandem honore eam affecturum, quum popu- lo in tenebris desidenti lux Evangelii est affulsura. Quam id cum mente Evangelistae ac scopo conve- niat, nemo non videt. Quam interpretationem etiam sequuti sunt Belgici translatores & Paraphra- stae. Nec alienus ab ea est D. Varenius sic Paraphra- sin Belgicam illustrans in Comment. ad h. l. p. 357. Terra illa, etsi tota angustiis pressa, non penitus obscu- rabitur, non ad plenam obscuritatem redigetur; quin idem Deus, sicut tempore superiori contemtibilem fe- cit, & despectam penitus terram Zabulon & Naph- thali, immissis hostilibus copiis Tiglat Pilezer Assyrii, per quas ignominiose tractata Israëlitarum terra: ita in novissimis temporibus gloriose illam illustrabit, & splendidissime exornabit, per primam scilicet Messiae Evangelicam praedicationem, per primam ejusdem Messiae Doctoralem in hac Tunica Israëlitarum manife- stationem, ita ut populus ille sedens in tenebris pri- mitus visurus sit lucem illam magnam.

Vulgatae tamen & Grotio favent B. Lutheri, Junii, Tremelliana & Piscatoris translatio: neque de his contendendum esse arbitramur, dummodo scopus & sensus Prophetae N. Test. explicatione il- lustratus, quod terrarum istarum commemoratio- nem Spiritus S. instituerit, ut locum, qui luce Evan- gelii sub Novi Testam. primordium collustrandus erat, designaret, non negligatur. Quem Grotius omnino posthabuit: ideoque separavit calamita- tes harum terrarum à tenebris, de quibus vers. 2. & luce populo promissa; haec ad quaevis alia trahens, neque obscurationem & tenebras, aut lucem de spirituali caligine ac illuminatione, sed de corpo- rali solum calamitate ac liberatione intellexit.

Ut res constet, ostendendum erit, definitum hic esse locum, in quo praeconii Evangelici lux pri- mum oriri debuerit. Quod penes Christianos qui- dem indubium esse debebat, siquidem apertissime id docuerit S. Matthaeus cap. 4, 12. seqq. Cum au- tem audisset Jesus, quod Johannes traditus esset, se- cessit in Galilaeam: & relicta civitate Nazareth, ve- nit & habitavit in Capernaum maritima in finibus Zabulon & Naphthali, UT ADIMPLERETUR, quod dictum est per Esaiam Prophetam: Terra Zabulon & terra Naphthalim, via maris trans Ior- danem Galilaea gentium populus, qui sedebat in te- nebris, vidit lucem magnam: & sedentibus in regio- ne umbrae mortis lux orta est eis. Quid luculentius dici poterat, ut doceretur, Esaiam terram Za- bulon & terram Naphthalim, viam maris trans Jordanem Galilaeam gentium designasse, ceu lo- cum, in quo populus in tenebris sederit, quem Christus luce Evangelii prae aliis collustrare de- buerit. Num hic par erat, Grotio, Judaeis aures po- tius praebere, quam S. Evangelistae, qui verbis lu- culentissimis docet, vaticinatum hic esse Prophe- tam, in quanam regione Christus praedicationem Evangelii inchoaturus sit? Neque est, quod dica- tur cum Grotio ad Matth. 4, 14. Matthaeum κᾀπ᾿ ἄν comma 2. cap. 9. Esa. citasse, sed quia non satis intelligi poterat, quo de populo ageret Propheta, ex antecedenti commate ea duntaxat addidisse, quæ ad populi illius designationem pertinebant: nam id præ- cipue Evangelistæ propositum erat populum illum designare. Ideo non tantum comma 2. citare vo- luit, sed verba etiam præcedentia, quæ palam do- cent, quisnam populus lucem viderit, nempe in terra Zabulon & Naphthali juxta viam maris trans vel ad Jordanem (uti mavult Grotius, quod vox πέραν ita sumatur Joh. 1, 28. Num. 32, 19.) habitans in Galilæa gentium. Causam enim exponit, cur Chri- stus in Galilæam secesserit, & in Capernaum mari- tima in finibus Zabulon & Naphthali habitarit, ver- bique ac miraculorum luce terras istas sub primor- dia muneris sui collustrarit! quia scilicet id ita præ- dictum olim erat. Unde etiam subjungit, refert- que Matthæus, Christum juxta mare Galilææ A- postolos docuisse & Evangelium regni prædicasse, omnemque languorem sanasse, ac turbas multas de Galilæa & Decapoli & de Hierosolymis eum trans Jordanem sequutas esse. Sed quum fateatur Gro- tius, populum illum, qui illuminandus dicitur v. 2. commatis præcedentis verbis designatum esse, quæ à Matthæo repetita sunt, quæ probationis causa ad- ducta esse ab Evangelista, contextus docet, utique speciatim ac διακριτικῶς de terris illis luce magna collustrandis Esajam vaticinari ἐπ' ἀγώνιον. Neque illa verba, via maris trans Jordanem Galileam gen- tium totum regnum Israelis designabunt, quod ad occidentem mare mediterraneum, orientem trans- itum Jordanis, septentrionem confinium gentium habet, ut explicat Oecolampadius & prolixius exe- quitur Abrah. Scultetus lib. 2. Exerc. Evangel. c. 10. neque abnuit Ludov. de Dieu l. c. Sic enim defi- nita iisdem non fuissent loca peculiaria, quæ Mat- thæus indigitare voluit.

Si dicas cum Grotio: Etsi verba Esaiæ directe agant de liberatione aliqua, quæ propius illa tempora contigerit, subesse tamen ὑπόνοιαν temporum Christi: quo etiam Calvini abit sententia: aut cum Zuvin- glio, Matthæum allegorikῶς hoc loco Prophetæ uti, ut quemadmodum olim Zabulon & Naphthali priores exterminium sentiebant, sic æquum esse, ut nunc prio- ribus lux oriatur: aut cum Sculteto, allusionem fieri à Matthæo & analogiam recentiorum cum veteribus institui: aut cum Spanhemio part. 3. Dub. Evangel. 21. p. 326. Verba Prophetæ sensu mystico vel accom- modativo etiam ac transumtivo ab Evangelista ad- duci: aut cum Cornelio à Lapide, nec non Tirino, figurari hic spiritualem deprædationem, qua per Im- manuelem terræ illæ Zabulon & Naphthali primo le- viter spoliandæ, Apostolis inde collectis, tum luculentior præda, factis ibi miraculis innumeris pluribusque conversis. Resp. (1) Falso supponi, quod ejusdem dicti sensus geminus detur, literalis & mysticus, proprius & transumtivus sit, vera διάνοια, & nescio quæ latens ὑπόνοια analogica. Nunquam enim ad- mittendi ejusdem dicti Scripturæ gemini sensus. (2) Adducta sunt verba Prophetæ ab Evangelista probationis ergo: At è nudo sensu mystico, accom- modativo, transumtivo, è nuda ὑπονοίᾳ & allusione analogica nulla institui potest probatio aut demon- stratio. (3) Evangelista cum cura & studio sele- git è Propheta ea, quæ ad designandum locum concionum & miraculorum Christi auspicatium faciebant, & verba ipsa urget premitque; terra Za- bulon & terra Naphthalim: tum etiam ista, via ma- ris trans Jordanem Galileæ gentium: ut constet, δια- κριτικῶς eam regionem designatam esse ac defi- nitam, illuminatione Christi lucis magnæ præ aliis nobilitandam. Cur alias ista peculiariter adduce- ret & quidem ista formula? nisi à Propheta id præ- dictum esset, in quo probando ibidem occupatur.

(4) Neque adducit tantum ex instituto illa Pro- phetica, sed narratione conjuncta ea ita etiam ex- plicat, ut nemini obscurum esse possit, Spiritum S. hic genuinum complementum vaticinii Propheti- ci demonstrasse, veramque ejus sententiam indi- casse. (5) Συνέχεια in Esaia recte se habet, si de temporibus N. Test. accipiatur. Nam si cum Cal- vino, Piscatore, Junio ac Tremellio, Sculteto, Span- hemio, de Dieu, Thoma, item Hugone, Vatablo, Ada- mo, Cornelio, ipsoque Grotio levioris afflictionis sub Tiglat - Palassare, & gravioris sub Salmanassare mentionem præcessisse dicas: Sensus oraculo ita constabit: non obscuratum iri perpetuo istas terras: sed illustrandas tandem per adventum Christi, uti Junius ac Piscator in notis, docent, & Lud. de Dieu l. c. Si cum Vinariensibus Paraphrast. majorem ad- huc calamitatem designari credas, quam utroque illo tempore fuerit, sed spiritualem, quæ tamen commutanda sit cum luce & gaudio spirituali, sco- po & allegationi Evangelistæ adhuc integra erit vis sua. Quæ in aprico maxime est, si versu 1. ca- pitis cum Brentio, Osiandro, Hieron. Prado, Ludov. de Dieu, Belgis Interpret. agnoscas præmissam qui- dem mentionem calamitatis terræ istius, quæ contem- ta fuerit olim & afflicta; sed simul indicatam glorifi- cationem ejusdem, quam per lucis magnæ illucesfen- tiam futuram, comma secundum hujus Capitis explicet. (6) Cohærent ita commode hæc cum præ- cedenti capite, uti notavit Brentius. Quum enim ante dictum sit, solam Christi doctrinam esse sectan- dam, exponit nunc Propheta, in qua regione Christus initio docturus sit Evangelium suum, & quem fru- ctum doctrina ejus sit allatura. (7) Optime hic ea, quæ sequuntur in hoc capite, de Christo congru- unt, si sensu literali hic de Christo etiam agi dica- tur: non item si proprie & quoad literam hæc sint intelligenda de temporibus Esaiæ vicinioribus. (8) Tenebræ & umbra mortis, in quibus populus sedere dicitur, non corporalem calamitatem, sed spiritualem designant. (9) Lux illa magna non li- berationem è calamitate temporali, sed illumina- tionem, quæ fit per verbum Evangelii, attulit, inter- prete Apostolo. Nuspiam certe illa de temporali liberatione exponitur. Quis vero admittet, sensum vaticinii tam insignis accommodatitium à Spiritu S. quidem traditum esse, genuinum vero & literalem nuspiam ab eodem expositum esse: Unde (10) ni- hil certi habent, qui alium sensum literalem fin- gunt, quam quem Evangelista tradidit. Grotius explicat cum Thoma, Hugone ac Janfenio, de luce liberationis ab exercitu Sennacheribi: Scultetus de liberatione è captivitate Babylonica: alii apud Span- hemium de utraq́; : nonnulli de calamitate & libera- tione tempore Maccabæorum. Calvinus de redemtio- ne Babylonica, sed tanquam præludio instaurandæ Ecclesiæ usque ad Messiæ adventum, ex quo omnis libertas, omnis beneficiorum largitio pendet. Quæ hic certitudo? (11) Conferri potest cum hoc oraculo vaticinium Davidis Ps. 68. Duces eorum principes Zabulon, principes Naphthalim, qui etiam primi Evangelii præcones à patria descripti sunt; de quo vide annotat. nostr. ad Psalm. 68. (12) De illuminatione, quam Christi adventus locis illis à Propheta designatis attulit, secundum literalem sensum intelligit Hieronymus: quia in regionibus duarum tribuum primum Salvator Evangelium prædicavit, quod per mare lacus Genezaret intel- ligatur; qui Jordane influente efficitur, in cujus littore Capernaum & Tyberias & Bethsaida & Chorazim sitæ sunt: in qua vel maxime regione Dominus im- moratus est: inque eam sententiam adducit Ebræos veteres conversos ipsosq́; Nazaræos. Primo tempore hæ duæ tribus Zabulon & Naphthalim ab Assyriis ca- pte sunt & ductæ in hostilem terram, & Galilæa de- serta est, quam nunc Propheta dicit alleviatam esse, eo quod peccata populi sustineret: Postea autem non solum duæ tribus, sed & reliquæ, quæ habitabant trans Jordanem & in Samaria, ductæ sunt in captivitatem. Et hoc, inquiunt, nunc Scriptura dicit: quod regio, cujus populus primus ductus est in captivitatem & Babyloniis servire cæpit, & quæ prius in tenebris ver- sabatur erroris, ipsa primum lucem prædicantis vide- rit Christi, & ex ea in universas gentes sit Evangelium seminatum: Nazaræi hunc locum ita explicare co- nantur: Adveniente Christo, & prædicatione illius coruscante, primo terra Zabulon & terra Naphtha- lim Scribarum & Pharisæorum est erroribus libera- ta, & gravissimum traditionum Judaicarum jugum excussit de cervicibus suis. Postea autem per Evange- lium Pauli, qui novissimus Apostolorum omnium fuit, ingravata est, h. e. multiplicata prædicatio & in terminos gentium & viam universi maris Christi Ev- angelium splenduit. Deniq; omnis orbis, qui ante ambulabat vel sedebat in tenebris & idololatriæ ac mortis vinculis tenebatur, clarum Evangelii lumen adspexit. Similiter exposuit Cyrillus Alexandr. Ordieur demonstrare (Propheta) qui sint primi, qui crediderunt & qui primitiæ fuerunt eorum, qui vocati sunt ad agnitionem Emmanuelis dicentis: Ecce ego & pueri, quos dedit Deus; narrant enim fines Zabulon & Naphthalim Tyberiadi stagno adja- cere & in extremis partibus Judaicæ regionis esse, ut Galilææ gentium sint conterminæ. Ex his maxime tribubus dicunt esse plerosq; S. Apostolorum. Quod ex Matth. 4. & Joh. 1. ibidem prolixe demonstrat Cyrillus. Hanc Patrum, imo Matthæi explicatio- nem sequitur Brentius; Non ignoro, quid Ebræi in- terpretes de sententia horum verborum scribant. Etsi autem licebit aliquoties ex Hebræis Interpr. signifi- cantiam vocabulorum petere, quanquam & in hac re plurimum hallucinari soleant: tamen Spiritus S. non proposuit nobis Hebræos Scriptores pro certis In- terpp. veræ sententiæ Sacræ Scripturæ, sed proposuit ea Apostolica Scripta: Hi sunt Commentarii, ex quibus vera Prophetarum sententia petenda est. Mat- thæus igitur Apostolus & Evangelista descripturus initium concionum & miraculorum Jesu Christi sic ait: Jesus secessit in Galilæam &c. Hic perspicue vi- des, quod Interprete Matthæo aut potius Sp. S. Esaias vaticinatus sit hoc loco, in qua regione Christus in- choaturus sit prædicationem Evangelii sui. Quod er- go hic dicitur sic legendum est: Primo tempore con- temta habita est terra Zabulon & terra Nephtha- lim. Novissimo autem tempore glorificata est via maris trans Jordanem, Galilæa seu confinium gen- tium, h. e. etsi regio maritima, quæ est trans Iordanem, in qua sita est civitas Capernaum, initio multis tem- poribus reputata est vilissima & contemtissima; atta- men in novissimis temporibus cum advenerit Messias, hæc Regio illustrabitur maxima gloria, & fiet lon- ge omnium clarissima. Quomodo ergo hoc fiet? Se- quitur: Populus, qui ambulabat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam, habitantibus in regione umbræ mortis lux orta est eis; h.e. incolæ hujus regionis fue- runt hactenus obruti magni tenebris. Non vide- runt, qua sit eundum ad justitiam & vitam. Post- quam autem venit Christus, primi omnium fuerunt, qui viderunt lucem Evangelii & miraculorum ejus. Christus enim inchoavit in ea regione prædicationem Evangelii sui, edidit in ea prima sua miracula, & se- legit ibi Apostolos suos. Circumibat (inquit Mat- thæus) totam Galilæam, docens in Synagogis illorum, ac prædicans Evangelium regni, & curans omnem morbum, & omnem languorem in populo. His ite- rum vides, quanto Spiritus Esaias illustratus fuerit, quod non solum cognoverit Christus venturum & prædicaturum Evangelion suum, sed etiam in qua regione, adeoqué etiam in qua parte regio- nis inchoaturus sit Evangelii sui prædicationem. Unde putas eum hoc hausisse, nisi ex ipso Sp. San- cto? Fortassis nonnihil adjutus fuit ex eo loco, qui est in Ps. 67. Principes Judæ, duces eorum, Principes Zabulon & Principes Naphthalim. Et Psal. 88. Thabor & Hermon in nomine tuo exultabunt. Sed indicare annis ante circiter septingentis tam certam regionem, in qua Christus concionem Ev- angelii sui & miracula inchoaturus sit, hoc de- mum venit ex singulari & insigni Sp. S. revelatione. Hoc autem revelatum est Prophetæ non tantum propter suos auditores coætaneos, ut confirma- rent fidem suam, ne in incursione duorum hosti- um, regis Israëlis & regis Syriæ desperarent de sa- lute sua, & de Adventu Christi: Minabantur enim hi Reges, se familiam Davidis, ex qua venturus erat Christus, deleturos: verum etiam revelatum est ei propter nos ac universam Ecclesiam Christi, ut cum videmus etiam hac in parte impletum esse in Jesu filio Mariæ virginis, quod Esaias prædixit, cer- to cognoscamus hunc solum esse verum Messiam. Unde existimo non sine divina dispensatione fa- ctum esse, quod Judæi ipsi testificati sint coram Pi- lato, Jesum exorsum esse prædicationem suam in Galilæa. Commovet, inquiunt, populum, docens per universam Judæam, exorsus à Galilæa usque ad hunc locum. Voluit enim DEUS hoc clamore Judæorum admonere pios hujus Prophetici dicti, ut sciant impiorum etiam testimonio hoc vatici- nium de Christo in Jesu impletum esse. Hactenus Brentius. Cujus vestigiis ut in plerisque aliis in- sistit Luc. Osiander. in paraphr. Neque abnuunt alii nostrates, hic designatas terras esse primi præ- conii Evangelici. Adstipulantur etiam ex ipsis Re- formatis non pauci: Oecolampadius in h. l. fatetur veritatem Matthæi cogere hunc locum referendum esse ad tempora Christi, ac sequitur fere explicatio- nem Nazaræorum supra adductam. E Calvini et- iam discipulis Junius & Tremellius agnoscunt, lite- rali sensu hæc tempora Christi respicere, præce- ptoris hic deserentes vestigia, ad v. 1. sequitur de- finitio certissima liberationis per Christum: qua Pro- pheta exponit exortum ac veluti primam lucem Ev- angelii ibi cepturam esse nominatim, ubi ceperit cala- mitas, & locum verbis apertissimis circumscribit. Eadem est sententia Johan. Piscatoris: ad quam fir- mandam etiam faciunt, quæ habet Spanhemius l. c. etsi Sculteto annuat: neque Calvini hic rejicere ve- lit explicationem. Summa, inquit, p. 327. consola- tionis est, non obscurandam esse (in perpetuum vide- licet) terram illam, qua geminam cladem esset vel ex- perta vel expertura; leviorem unam à Tiglath Pele- sare, graviorem alteram à Salmanassare, sed Deum tandem liberaturum populum suum ambulantem in tenebris & effecturum, ut videat lucem magnam & ut lux splendeat super illos etiam, qui habitaturi es- sent in terra umbræ mortis. E Pontificiis imprimis ad- ducendus Lyranus est, qui sententiam Grotio pro- batam aperte refellit: quod primo implicet contra- ria saltim in modo loquendi: quia primam captivi- tatem (per Tiglath Pillassarem, quæ Grotio prima est juxta hoc dictum) nominat alleviationem, & se- cundam (per Salmanassarem) aggravationem, cum tamen fuerit ejusdem rationis. Deinde quia Gali- lææ hic mentio non fieret, cum dicitur novissime ag- gravata, utpote quæ in prima captivitate captivata est saltim in magna parte: Sed magis Samaria, quæ erat regni Metropolis, & capta per Salmanasser.

Tertio, quia Matth. 4. dicitur hæc Prophetia com- pleta quoad literam de Christo: & cum omnes expo- sitiones dicant, quod c. 7. habetur de filio virgi- nis, de Christo intelligendum esse, eadem necessita- te compelli quemlibet Catholicum censet Lyranus, hanc etiam Prophetiam de Christo intelligere, quia æ- que hoc à Matthæo factum dicitur, ut impleretur, quod Propheta dixit Matth. 4. atq; illud de partu vir- ginis Matth. 1. Explicat idem Lyranus hæc Esaiæ verba de præconio Christi h. m. quod primo tempore alleviata sit terra Zabulon, & terra Naphthalim, quia ibi Christus circa principium suæ prædicatio- nis publice frequenter docuit, & miracula fecit: & sic fuit terra illa alleviata à jugo Diaboli per pote- statem Christi: veruntamen quia plures eorum rever- si fuerint ad vomitum, ideo subdit ait: Et novissimo, id est, circa finem prædicationis aggravata est via maris: de qua aggravatione Matth. 11, 20. seqq. Tunc cœpit exprobrare civitatibus, in quibus fa- ctæ sunt virtutes, væ tibi Chorazim, væ tibi Beth- saida, quæ erant supra mare Galilææ, in finibus Zabulon & Naphthalim: & postea subditur de Ca- phernaum, ubi Christus habitavit circa prædicatio- nis suæ principium, quia per prædicationem Christi fuit disposita ad consecutionem beatitudinis credendo: at postea depressa per demeritum damnationis ad vo- mitum redeundo. Menochius Jesuita, quem magni solet facere Grotius, secundum literam Evangeli- cam veritatem & Christum ipsum per lucem magnam intelligi fatetur. Cornelius à Lapide, etsi probare eam sententiam de Spirituali deprædatione operose conetur, quam suam fecere Tirinus & Menochius: non tamen improbare potuit supra adductam ex- plicationem Brentii & Hieronym. Prado: Aliter, inquit, NEC MALE hæc accipit Hieronym. Prado in Ezech. p. 275. Alleviari, iquit, est vilipendi: aggra- vari est honorari: nam hoc quoque significat Hebr. הִכְבִּיד & הֵקַל hecal & hicbid, q. d. olim nihili à Judæis ducebatur Galilæa, tum quia longius aberat à Jerusalem, tum quia defecerat à Juda & templo, tum quia habebat abjecta oppida, uti fuerunt viginti illa, quæ Salomon dedit Hiram Regi Tyri, quæ proinde terra Chabul, id est, vilis & ignobilis, sunt appella- ta: Unde & Christus à Judæis & à Juliano Apo- stata per probrum vocabatur Galilæus: verum in novissimis diebus hæc Galilæa, eam visitante, inco- lente & prædicante Messia, erit honoratissima. Si- mili enim modo dixit Aggæus c. 2. 10. templum à Zo- robabele constructum fore augustius Salomonico, ob Christi in eo præsentiam, & prædicationem. Et Mi- chæas c. 5, 2. Bethlehem extollit ex eo, quod in ea na- scetur Christus.

## 9:2
Verse 2, THE PEOPLE THAT WALKED IN DARKNESS]. The Jerusalemite people, established in most grievous dangers, which the Hebrews call by the name of darkness,

HATH SEEN A GREAT LIGHT] They will experience an extraordinary liberation when such a powerful army of Sennacherib has been slaughtered.

Grotius Judaizes here again. This is the gloss of the Jews: that the Prophet predicts nothing else than the danger and damage which was to be created for the Jews by the Assyrians, which is to be such that the slaughter brought by Tiglath-Pileser and by Shalmaneser is to be esteemed as nothing in comparison to it: he only adds a promise concerning a miraculous liberation through the destruction of the army of Sennacherib. An egg is not so like an egg as this Grotian interpretation is to the Jewish one. Which, although some Papists also—Thomas, Lyranus, Hugo, Spanheim, Adam Sasbouth—embrace, it can by no means be admitted. (1) Because this people cannot be understood as only the Jerusalemites. For there had been an explicit mention of the land of Zabulon and Naphthalim, the way of the sea beyond the Jordan and

Galilee of the Gentiles. How then are only the Jerusalemites indicated now by the people? From where can it be established that those are designated of whom no mention was made, even by a single word; but that those who are openly and prolixly described are excluded? (2) There is no trace of that comparison of the time of Hezekiah and the slaughter of Sennacherib at the time of the devastation of Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser: of the calamity of the Jerusalemite or Jewish people with the calamity of the Israelite people. This comparison is brought into the text, it is not brought out of the same. 3. What also would this sequence be: The land of Zabulon and Naphthali will be afflicted lightly at first; the way of the sea beyond the Jordan and Galilee of the Gentiles, or the ten tribes, will be afflicted more heavily afterwards: The Jerusalemite people, established in most grievous dangers in the time of Hezekiah, will experience an extraordinary liberation? There is no such connection in the Prophet, no coherence or comparison. The copulative or adversative particle is not prefixed, and the people, or But the people, who walked in darkness; but it is connected simply with the preceding, so that it may be designated by apposition that the inhabitants of the land of Zabulon and Naphthalim and at the way of the sea beyond the Jordan of Galilee of the Gentiles are primarily that people who are to see a great light: that to them before others that light is to arise, just as they sat before others in the squalor of darkness, because they were not only formerly grievously afflicted, but were also primarily filled with the densest spiritual darkness at the time of the advent of the Messiah. For just as those tribes of Zabulon and Naphthali had once been, more than others, subject to horrible desolation and horrible darkness; so also in the time of the Messiah that whole region, as being near to the nations and most remote from the city of Jerusalem, the seat of the worship of God, was entirely as it were immersed in the horrible darkness of idolatry and profanity, as Spanheim says, l. c. p. 308. Therefore Matthew used the word ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκότῳ; so that he might designate, indeed, not only the darkness of that people, but also their long delay in that darkness: inasmuch as they were truly in the time of the Messiah a λαὸς καθήμενος ἐν σκότῳ already for several centuries. 5. Some here observe the punctuation by the Royal Accent Athnach at the word הכביד, it is made heavy or it is glorified: whence they make this structure of the Prophet's words; that that region is not to be obscured forever, which was first more lightly afflicted by Tiglath-Pileser; afterwards more heavily by Shalmaneser (or thus: that land is not to be obscured always: but that which had been afflicted and despised in the first time, is to be glorified in the last.) The way of the sea, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Galilee of the nations, the people walking in darkness is to be illuminated with a great light. If it be said that Silluq stands in the way, such a structure could be assigned: that land is not to be obscured always, etc., namely the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations: The people (this one, I say, whom I mentioned) who walked in darkness, shall see a great light. 6. The citation of Matthew absolutely requires this sense: who expressly teaches that the inhabitants by the way of the sea of Galilee of the nations are that people who, placed in darkness, saw a great light, when Christ, that true light, arrived, enlightening every man, John 1:9, who illuminated those lands first and before all others with the light of the Gospel. 7. Although it may be admitted that neither the darkness nor the illumination is to be restricted to those tribes which are pointed out demonstratively, and therefore that Jerusalem and the Jewish people are also included under the name of the people: yet not without cause was mention made of those tribes distinctively: But so that the place might be indicated in which the Messiah ought to have begun his preaching. And did not the event itself teach that the Messiah with his light shone for the greatest part upon those regions, which seemed more than others to be plunged into the shadow of death. And therefore these things are also adapted to the illumination of the Gentiles, because that people was sticking in similar darkness. Concerning which Cyril: That the divine disciples were not to be called in their own times alone, but also a multitude of the Gentiles, he designates, saying: And the rest of the maritime regions beyond the Jordan of Galilee of the Gentiles, the people who walked in darkness, etc. For they were already proceeding just like the Gentiles and were dwelling in this world as if in death and in darkness, for the reason that they did not have the light of the true knowledge of God in their mind, but were rushing as if into every pit and into evil, just as if they were stumbling against any stone. 8. Nor indeed is it consistent, what is assumed in that Jewish gloss, that the calamity or disaster was more severe in the time of Hezekiah than in previous ones. Therefore Spanheim himself refutes the same in the cited place, whose words I shall not regret to transcribe: That Jewish exposition, that the misery of all Judea would be so great, such darkness, that all preceding things are light if they are compared with them, etc., is firstly groundlessly fabricated, and alien to the words and mind of the Prophet, and secondly absurd and ridiculous. For was there a greater calamity of the Jewish kingdom either in the time of Sennacherib, or in the time of the Babylonian captivity, than the calamity of the kingdom of the ten tribes not only destroyed by Shalmaneser, but never afterwards to be restored? Does the comparison of Sacred History teach that the destruction of the Israelite kingdom did not deserve the name of affliction when compared with the incursion of Sennacherib into Judea and with the siege of Jerusalem? Indeed, is there such a disproportion even between the total destruction of the Israelite kingdom and the temporary captivity of the Jews, to which an end was put when the period of LXX years was completed? So far, therefore, is it from the case that this θλῖψις can be understood as the Jewish disaster, that whether they are compared intensively or extensively, the disaster of the Jewish kingdom was far less than the disaster of the Israelite kingdom. Add that such a diluted speech is attributed to the Holy Spirit, as if to designate the θλῖψις of the Jewish disaster He wished to compare it with such a disaster as He Himself calls light, such as was the first disaster brought upon the Israelites by Tiglath-Pileser. 9. By the darkness in which the people walked, one must not understand only the darkness of calamities and bodily dangers, such as were pressing upon the people in the time of Hezekiah, but especially spiritual darkness; blindness, ignorance, idolatry, and sins, as is manifest both from the parallel passage Isaiah 60:1 and from Matthew's explanation. 10. Indeed, the Prophet himself explains it immediately when he says they dwell in the region of the SHADOW OF DEATH: which designate not a bodily calamity, but a spiritual one. Concerning which Cyril: He says they dwell in the region and shadow of death, because there is nothing else in their regions than only mist and darkness, namely of the mind and intelligence, and because they are like the dead while still living. For the shadow of bodies imitates their forms entirely, and as far as the similarity of figure is concerned, it does not differ in any way. But not to know God, who is by nature and truly God, is in a way an imitation and shadow of death. Jerome observes the distinction between death and the shadow of death: I think this is it, that the death is of those who have gone to the underworld with the works of death: For the soul that has sinned, it shall die. But the shadow of death is of those who, although they have not yet departed from this life; for they can, if they wish, do penance. 11. The great light likewise is not to be understood concerning liberation from a temporal disaster, but concerning spiritual illumination: indeed concerning Christ Himself, who testifies: I am the light of the world, John 12, of whom John Chapter 1:9: This was the true light, which illuminates every man coming into this world. Therefore the Evangelist explained it concerning Christ the light of the Gospel illuminating lands beset by the darkness of blindness. And indeed Naphtali had never even perfectly felt the שחר dawn after the Assyrian disaster: But then it saw the sun rising; as here the blessed Bohlius. 12. And the better part of the Interpreters agree in this opinion, Jerome, Cyril, Basil the Great, and of the more recent ones the blessed Luther, Brentius, Osiander, the Weimar Paraphrases; from the Reformed also Zwingli, Oecolampadius, Fr. Junius, Piscator, Lud. de Dieu; from the Papists Cornel. a Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, and others. Of Menochius, because Grotius attributes much to him, we transcribe the paraphrase: The people of Galilee of Zebulun and Naphtali in the DARKNESS of infidelity, that is, of Judaism mixed with Gentilism. A GREAT LIGHT, the Evangelical truth and Christ Himself, who is the true light, which illuminates every man IN THE REGION OF THE SHADOW OF DEATH, in the densest darkness of ignorance and sins. A LIGHT HAS RISEN FOR THEM, i.e., the faith, grace, and clarity of Christ have shone forth. These things Menochius from Cornel. a Lapide, whom he often follows: who here refutes the Grotian invention in Jansenius, that no mention is made here of Sennacherib and the Jews; and also that it is certain that these things are said of the Galileans, not of the Jews, both from the preceding verse and from St. Matthew Ch. 4:15, from which he says it is evident that these words of Isaiah were fulfilled LITERALLY by Christ preaching in Galilee. Spanheim, although he says that the opinion of his Calvin concerning the darkness of the Babylonian captivity, and indeed even that of Grotius concerning the danger from the army of Sennacherib, is not to be rejected here, nevertheless confesses that spiritual and internal darkness is designated by the word צלמות shadow of death, rather than bodily and external: nor does he ask without merit, whether that light could be called great comparatively, which shone upon the Jews either in the time of Sennacherib, or in the time of the Babylonian restoration, when the times of Hezekiah were followed by most grave calamities, and the Jews even returning from captivity were subject to most grave disasters under the Seleucids and Romans? Is not the light of spiritual illumination greater, which was brought to the true Israelites, preferred to others? Here indeed, he says, not without grave cause does the Holy Spirit mention this light. S. & of great light & of shining light & of light opposed not only to darkness, but also to the shadow of death, which is to be restricted only to the carnal benefit of carnal men & of those fixed only to the flesh and to the earthly clod. But that Spanheim invents a double sense, literal and mystical, that is often diluted, and suits neither Isaiah nor Matthew, who according to the letter treat of spiritual light: as Zwingli and Oecolampadius and other Reformed acknowledge. He certainly (I point to Zwingli), however much he may wish the preceding words to have been adduced by Matthew allegorically, nevertheless admits in these that it is treated in the proper sense concerning the illumination of the Gospel, and says that Isaiah adduced the land of Zebulun and Naphtali by way of example, and then proceeds to the prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles, and is entirely on that subject; and therefore that Matthew shows from that, that it then truly came to pass that light arose for the Gentiles, when Christ began His prophecy at Capernaum. Since after the Babylonian captivity the Jewish nation was never restored to itself; whence also they did not dwell in the land of promise alone or free, but mixed with Gentiles and subdued by foreign rule, by which it came about that Galilee was numbered among the Gentiles. And for that reason Oecolampadius and others interpret this prophecy with Zwingli concerning the calling of the Gentiles. (13.) To which finally can be added arguments taken from those things which follow in the text, which further refute the Jewish gloss of Grotius.

Latin:

Vers. 2, POPULUS QUI AMBULABAT IN TE- NEBRIS]. Populus Hierosolymitanus in gravissimis con- stitutus periculis, quæ tenebrarum nomine appellant He- bræi,

VIDIT LUCEM MAGNAM] Experietur egre- giam liberationem cæso Sennacheribi tam valido exercitu.

Judaizat hic iterum Grotius. Judæorum hæc est glossa: Prophetam nihil aliud prædicere, quam periculum & damnum, quod Judæis creari debebat per Assyrios, quod tantum sit futurum, ut clades à Tiglath-Pelesare & à Salmanassare illata præ illo ni- hili æstimanda sit: subjungere tantum promissionem de liberatione mirabili per internecionem exercitus Sennacheribi. Non ovum ovo tam simile est, quam hoc interpretamentum Grotianum Judaico. Quod etsi Pontificii etiam nonnulli Thomas, Lyra- nus, Hugo, Spanhemius, Adamus Sasbouth ample- ctantur, nullatenus tamen admitti potest. (1) Quia populus hic non potest de solis Hierosolymitanis intelligi. Facta enim diserta mentio erat terræ Za- bulon & Naphthalim, via maris trans Jordanem &

Galilaeae gentium. Quomodo ergo nunc per popu- lum soli Hierosolymitani indigitantur? Undenam constare potest illos designari, quorum nulla vel unico vocabulo facta est mentio; eos autem, qui aperte & prolixe describuntur, excludi? (2) Nul- lum est vestigium comparationis istius temporis Ezechiae & cladis Sennacheribicae tum tempore de- vastationis Tiglath-Pelasaris & Salmanassaris : cala- mitatis populi Hierosolymitani aut Judaici, cum calamitate populi Israelitici. Infertur haec compa- ratio textui, non effertur ex eodem. 3. Quae etiam συνέχεια haec foret, Terra Zabulon & Naphthali prius leviter affligetur; via maris trans Jordanem & Galilaea gentium, vel decem tribus affligentur post gravius: Populus Hierosolymitanus in gravissimis constitutus periculis tempore Ezechiae egregiam expe- rietur liberationem? nullus ita nexus in Propheta, nulla vel Cohaerentia vel σύγκρισις. 4. Non prae- mittitur particula copulativa vel adversativa, & po- pulus, vel Populus autem, qui ambulabat in tene- bris; sed connectitur simpliciter cum praeceden- tibus, ut designetur per appositionem incolas ter- rae Zabulon & Naphthalim & ad viam maris trans Jordanem Galilaeae gentium, esse cumprimis populum il- lum, qui lucem magnam visurus est: illis ante alios lucem illam exorituram, uti prae aliis in squalore te- nebrarum sederunt, quia non tantum olim graviter afflicti, sed & imprimis tenebris spiritualibus den- sissimis tempore adventus Messiae repleti fuere. Ut enim tribus ille Zabulon & Naphthali olim prae a- liis horrendae desolationi, horrendis tenebris ob- noxiae fuerant; Sic & tempore Messiae totus ille tractus, ut vicinus gentibus & maxime remotus ab urbe Hierosolyma sede cultus Dei, horrendis ido- lolatriae & profanitatis tenebris totus velut immer- sus erat, ut ait Spanhemius l. c. p. 308. Ideo Mat- thaeus adhibuit verbum ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκότῳ; ut nempe designaret, non tantum tenebras populi il- lius, sed & moram illius diuturnam in tenebris illis: quippe qui vere Messiae tempore erat λαὸς καθή- μενος ἐν σκότῳ jam per aliquot secula. 5. Observant hic nonnulli interpunctionem per Accentum Re- gium Athnach ad verbum הכביד aggravata est vel glorificata est: unde hanc faciunt structuram ver- borum Prophetae; non obscurandam regionem illam in perpetuum, quae primo levius à Tiglath-Pelesare; post gravius à Salmanassare afflicta (vel ita: non ob- scurandam semper terram illam: sed quae primo tempore afflicta & contemta fuerat, novissimo glori- ficatum iri.) Viam maris πέραν 8 Ἰορδάνε Gali- laeam gentium, populum ambulantem in tenebris col- lustratum iri luce magna. Si dicatur, ita obstare Sil- luc, structura talis assignari poterit: non obscuran- dam semper terram illam &c. utpote viam maris trans Jordanem Galilaeam gentium: Populus (hic inquam quem dixi) qui ambulavit in tenebris, vide- bit lucem magnam. 6. Sensum hunc omnino re- quirit citatio Matthei: qui expresse docet, incolas ad viam maris Galilae gentium esse populum illum, qui in tenebris positus vidit lucem magnam, cum ad- ventavit Christus vera illa lux, omnem hominem illuminans Joh. 1, 9. qui luce Evangelii terras illas primum & ante alias omnes collustravit. 7. Quam- vis admitti possit, neque tenebras, neque illumina- tionem ad tribus illas, quae δεικτικῶς designatae sunt, restringi, adeoque populi nomine comprehendi etiam Hierosolymam & populum Judaicum: non tamen absque causa tribuum illarũ διακριτικῶς men- tio facta est: Sed ut indicaretur locus, in quo au- spicari suam praedicationem debuerit Messias. Et annon eventus ipse docuit, Messiam cum sua luce maximam partem regionibus istis illuxisse, quae præ aliis videbantur in umbra mortis demersæ. Atque ideo etiam hæc ad gentium illuminatio- nem accommodantur, quia populus ille in similibus hærebat tenebris. Quo de Cyrillus: Quod autem di- vini discipuli suis temporibus non soli vocandi essent, sed etiam multitudo gentium, designat,inquiens: Et reli- qui maritimi ultra Jordanem Galilææ gentium, popu- lus, qui ambulabat in tenebris &c. Incedebant e- nim jam perinde ut gentes & commorabantur in hoc mundo tanquam in morte & in tenebris, propterea quod lumen veræ Dei cognitionis in animo non habe- rent, sed ruerent quasi in omnem foveam & in ma- lum,veluti ad quemvis lapidem impingerent. 8. Ne- que vero consentaneum est, quod in illa glossâ Ju- daica assumitur, graviorem fuisse calamitatem aut cladem tempore Ezechiæ, quam superioribus. Ideo refellit ipse Spanhemius eandem loco citato, cujus verba adscribere non pigebit: ἔκθεσις illa Judai- ca, tantam futuram totius Judææ miseriam, tan- tas tenebras,ut levia sint omnia præcedentia,si cum iis comparentur,&c. primo gratis conficta,& alie- na à verbis mente Prophetæ, deinde absurda & ri- dicula. An enim major calamitas fuit regni Ju- daici vel temporeSanheribi; vel tempore captivi- tatis Babylonicæ, calamitate regni decem tribuum à Salmanaffare non destructi tantum,sed nunquam postmodum instaurandi? An Historiæ Sacræ col- latio docet destructionem regni Israelitici non me- ruisse nomen afflictionis collatam cum irruptione Sanheribi in Judæam & cum obsidione Hierosoly- mæ? Immo num tanta disproportio etiam inter excidium totale regni Israelitici, & captivitatem temporariam Judæorum,cui LXX. annor.periodo exacta finis impositus? Tantum itaque abest, ut hic θλῖψις intelligi possit cladis Judaicæ, ut sive intensive,sive extensive comparentur,clades regni Judaici minor longe fuerit clade regni Israelitici. Adde, sic dilutam affingi orationem Spir. Sancto, quasi ad θλῖψιν cladis Judaicæ designandam illam voluerit conferre cum ejusmodi clade, quam ipse levem vocat,qualis fuit clades prima illata Israëlitis à Tiglath-Pelesare. 9. Per tenebras, in quibus am- bulabat populus, non sunt intelligendæ tantum te- nebræ calamitatum & periculorum corporalium, quales tempore Ezechiæ populo incumbebant,sed maxime tenebræ spirituales; cæcitas,ignorantia,ido- lolatria & peccatorum, ut tum è loco paralello Esai. 60,1. tum è Matthæi explicatione manifestum est. 10. Imo explicat id statim Propheta ipse, cum habita- re in regione UMBRÆ MORTIS eos dicit: quæ non corporalem calamitatem, sed spiritualem desi- gnant. Quo de Cyrillus: Habitare eos in regione & umbra mortis ait,quod sit in regionibus eorum nihil alind, quam sola nebula & caligo, mentis videlicet & intelligentiæ, quodg, sint instar mortuorum adhuc viventes. Corporum namque umbra omnino eorum formas imitatur, & quantum ad figuræ similitudi- nem, nulla ratione discrepat. Deum autem nesci- re, qui natura est & vere Deus, imitatio quodam- modo est & umbra mortis. Hieronymus discrimen observat inter mortem & umbram mortis: Hoc es- se puto, quod mors eorum est, qui cum operibus mor- tis ad inferos perrexerunt: Anima enim, quæ pec- cavit, ipsa morietur. Umbra autem mortis eorum est, qui cum nec dum de vita ista egressi sint; possunt e- nim, si voluerint, agere pœnitentiam. 11. Lux magna itidem non de liberatione à clade temporali, sed de illuminatione spirituali est intelligenda: imo de Christo ipso, qui testatur: Ego sum lux mundi Joh. 12. de quo Johannes Cap. 1,9: Hic erat lux ve- ra, quæ omnem hominem illuminat venientem in hunc mundum. Ideo de Christo luce Evangelii il- lustrante terras tenebris cœcitatis obsitas Evange- lista exposuit. Et sane Naphthali ne quidem שחר auroram perfecte unquam senserat post cladem Assy- riacam: Tunt autem videbat oriri solem; ut hic B. Bohlius. 12. Atque in hanc sententiam melior pars Interpp. consentit, Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Ba- silius M. & è recentioribus B. Lutherus, Brentius, Osiander, Paraph. Vinarienses; è Reformatis etiam Zvvinglius, Oecolampadius, Fr. Junius, Piscator, Lud. de Dieu; è Pontificiis Cornel. à Lapide, Tiri- nus, Menochius, aliique. Menochii, quia illi mul- tum tribuit Grotius, paraphrasin adscribimus: Po- pulus Galilææ Zabulon & Naphthali in TENEBRIS infidelitatis, id est, Judaismi mixti cum Gentilismo. LUCEM MAGNAM, Evangelicam veritatem & Christum ipsum, qui est lux vera, quæ illumi- nat omnem hominem IN REGIONE UMBRÆ MORTIS, in densissima caligine ignorantiæ & pec- catorum. LUX ORTA EST EIS, h. e. Christi fides, gratia & claritas affulsit. Hæc Meno- chius è Cornel. à Lapide, quem sæpe sequitur: qui hic Grotianum commentum in Jansenio refellit, quod de Sennacheribo & Iudæis nulla hic facta mentio; quoq́; hæc de Galilæis dici, non de Iudæis con- stet tum ex versu præcedenti, tum è S. Matthæo C. 4, 15. ex quo patere ait, hæc Esaiæ verba à Christo prædi- cante in Galilæa AD LITERAM fuisse impleta. Spanhemius etsi Calvini sui sententiam de tenebris captivitatis Babylonicæ, imo Grotii etiam de peri- culo ab exercitu Sennacheribi, & hic non rejicien- dam dicat, spirituales tamen potius, & internas tene- bras voce צלמות umbra mortis, quam corporales & externas designari fatetur: nec immerito quærit, an lux illa συγκριτικῶς magna dici potuerit, quæ il- luxit Iudæis vel tempore Sennacheribi, vel tempore re- stitutionis Babylonicæ, quum tempora Ezechiæ gra- vissimæ calamitates fuerint subsequutæ, Judæi et- iam reduces è captivitate gravissimis cladibus ob- noxii fuerint sub Seleucidis & Romanis? Annon major lux sit illuminationis spiritualis, quæ veris Israelitis fuit illata, aliis prælata? Hic sane, in- quit, non sine gravi causa & bis lucis meminit Sp. S. & lucis magnæ & lucis splendentis & lucis oppositæ non tantum tenebris, sed & umbræ mortis, quæ ad be- neficium carnale duntaxat arctare hominum carna- lium est & carni duntaxat ac glebæ terrestri affixo- rum. Quod vero Spanhemius duplicem fingit sen- sum, literalem & mysticum, id sæpius dilutum, nec vel Esaiæ vel Matthæo convenit, qui secundum lite- ram de luce spirituali agunt: uti Zvvinglius & Oeco- lampadius aliique Reformati agnoscunt. Ille certe (Zvvinglium indigito) utut præcedentia ver- ba ἀλληγορικῶς à Matthæo adducta velit, in his ta- men fatetur sensu proprio de illuminatione Evangelii agi, ac Esaiam dicit terram Zabulon & Naphthalim exempli causa adduxisse, ac deinde ad vaticinium gentium vocationis accedere, totumque in eo ar- gumento esse; ideoque Matthæum inde ostende- re, tum vere factum esse, ut gentibus lux oriretur, cum Christus Capernaum exordiretur Prophetiam suam. Siquidem post captivitatem Babylonicam gens Judaica nunquam sibi restituta fuerit; unde & in promissionis terra non soli aut liberi habita- runt, sed gentibus commixti & imperio peregri- no domiti, quo factum, ut Galilæa inter gentes numeretur. Atque eo nomine hoc vaticinium de gentium vocatione interpretantur cum Zvvinglio Oecolampadius & alii. (13.) Quibus denique addi possunt argumenta ex iis, quæ in textu consequun- tur, desumta, quæ ulterius refellunt Judaicam Grotii glossam.

## 9:3
Vers. 3. THOU HAST MULTIPLIED THE NATION, NOT-

MAGNIFICASTI LÆTITIAM] O you Assyrian, you have indeed gathered a great army to 185,000, but you will not rejoice the more for it.

LÆTABUNTUR CORAM TE] Namely, the Jerusalemites. Here Isaiah turns himself again to God, as such apostrophes are frequent in the Prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 3. MULTIPLICASTI GENTEM, NON-

MAGNIFICASTI LÆTITIAM] O tu Assyrie, magnum quidem exercitum contraxisti ad CLXXXV. millia, sed non eo magis gaudebis.

LÆTABUNTUR CORAM TE] Nempe Hiero- solymitani. Hic ad Deum iterum se vertit Esaias, ut fre- quentes sunt tales in Prophetis apostrophæ.

## 9:4
Vers. 4. JUGUM ENIM ONERIS] The most heavy siege.

ET VIRGAM HUMERIS EJUS] Imminent upon their shoulders.

ET SCEPTRUM EXACTORIS] The most harsh tributes, which the Assyrians had been about to impose upon the Jerusalemites.

SUPERASTI] You have driven away.

SICUT IN DIE MADIAN] When Gideon overcame them, Jud. 7. See also below 10, 26.

The prophetic words have indeed undergone various interpretation: but Grotius, according to his custom, chose the worst: which is that of some Papists. Namely, of Thomas, Lyranus, Hugo, Adam Sasbouth, and Tirinus: or rather of the blind Jews, R. Solomon and R. Kimchi, whom Lyranus and the other Papists, as is wont to happen, have imprudently followed. To maintain that commentary, Grotius feigns an apostrophe in the same clause, now to the Assyrian, of whom no mention is made by even the smallest word, now to God. He interprets 'nation' as the army of Sennacherib at will, without any indication in the text. He inserts the Jerusalemites, of whom not a jot is found here. And how wonderful is that gloss of the words: 'You have multiplied the nation, you have not magnified the joy,' that is, 'the great army of Sennacherib was slaughtered'? Thus, it will be permitted to make anything out of anything. Others, however, explain those words concerning the Jewish nation: others concerning the Gentiles converted in great numbers. Jerome leads the way in this: whose ἔκθεσις of this entire passage is: 'You have multiplied the nation, i.e., you have filled all nations with the knowledge of you, but you have not magnified the joy.' According to which the Apostle says that he has perpetual sorrow for his brothers, who are Israelites. And Jonah is saddened that the Ninevites were saved in such a way that the gourd or κίκαιον withered. ---- When therefore Christ has arrived and the nation of Christians has been gathered from all nations, then the Apostles will rejoice, just as reapers rejoice in the harvest, of whom the Lord was speaking. 'The harvest indeed is great, but the laborers are few.' And just as victors exult, who divide the captured booty. For when the strong man has been captured and bound, his whole house is plundered and the spoils are divided. But you, O Lord and Savior, the yoke of his burden, i.e. of the Devil, who previously exulted in the world, who commanded all nations, who pressed down the necks of all with the most heavy yoke of servitude; and the rod, with which he struck everyone and compelled them to render sins to him as a kind of tribute, you have taken away from their shoulders, and you have made them serve you freely without any army, and without the shedding of blood in a hidden hand: just as under Gideon you provided victory to the people of Israel over the Midianites. For just as a garment that has been stained with human blood cannot be washed, but, infected with blood, is consumed by fire, so that the stains perish with the foul gore of the garment: so the Devil's violent plundering and the tumults and crowds, by which he had subjected the human race to himself, have been consigned to the fires of Gehenna. Cyril speaks in almost the same manner: who understands then the joy of the disciples of Christ, because they gather the nations like grain into the Lord's barn and snatch them from the tyrannical power of Satan: then also [the joy] of those who have believed: and as regards the Gentiles, the inevitable yoke of sin and the scepter and kingdom of Satan, from which Christ has vindicated us into liberty: and also as regards the Jews, the truly intolerable yoke of the law and traditions and the rod of the rapacity of the Pharisees. Similarly, Basil the Great explains concerning spiritual joy and liberation from the Diabolical yoke. Clearly, he says, that exactor imposed an intolerable and very sharp yoke upon human life, namely, the common enemy of us all, a rod falling and

extorting from us, so that we might fulfill his will alone. Most of our own follow the interpretation of Jerome, B. Luther, the Vinarian Paraphrasts, and others: but Jerome refers those words: 'YOU HAVE NOT MAGNIFIED THE JOY,' to the zeal and condolence of the Apostles, because the nations were multiplied while the Jews were rejected. To which Haymo, Cornelius à Lapide, and Menochius agree: 'You have multiplied the nation,' that is, 'You, Immanuel Christ, through yourself and your Apostles will convert [them] from Jews and Gentiles, but you have not increased the joy, because you will see, and they themselves will see, a much greater part of them remaining incredulous, and consequently they will see then with the sorrow of their nation, such as both the Galileans and the Jews, for whom he himself with Paul will wish to be anathema, the destruction through Titus.' Whence Osiander, 'You have multiplied the nation,' you have made the nations powerful, around the time of the revealed Christ: (so that the Roman nation then subjugated the Jews, and them made them tributary, and commanded them) you have not magnified the joy, that matter certainly did not bring great joy to the Jewish people: for the Jews bore the Roman yoke with a most unjust spirit. Nevertheless, however, those who acknowledge Christ will perceive more joy from his recognition than sadness from the proud dominion of the Romans. For they will rejoice before you, O Christ Son of God, who have acknowledged you through faith, as those who rejoice in the harvest. Others refer it to the envy of the Jews: whence Blessed Luther thus paraphrases: The Gentiles receive the Gospel and thus the Church is increased by the accession of the Gentiles, but the Jews envy the Gentiles that happiness of the Gentiles: As he says, I will provoke them to jealousy with a foolish nation Deut. 32. Likewise with a people that is not a people I will provoke them. And this is what he says, you have not magnified the joy. Others interpret it concerning external calamities, which are accustomed to follow the reception of the Gospel, bringing sadness and sorrow: you have not magnified the joy regarding the external state: since many persecutions and miseries are to follow Matth. 10, 34. Joh. 15, 18. especially from the contumacious Jews 1. Thess. 2, 14. 15. as the Weimar theologians and Oecolampadius interpret: taking the rest that are added κατ᾿ ἀντίθεσιν (by way of antithesis) concerning internal joy: since it is said: They will rejoice BEFORE YOU, i.e., even if it does not appear before the world. For the Saints are not left in adversity without any joy. The cause is also added, why the faithful are to rejoice so, because we have been freed from the most grievous burdens of sins and punishments and the weight of the law and the rod and the goad of the ancient enemy or of the flesh Joh. 8. Some think the particle לא (not) is placed for לו (to him). You have multiplied the nation to him, you have magnified the joy: which opinion Oecolampadius notes is that of the Hebrews, and that Jonathan or the LXX do not differ from it. And the Masora itself observes this reading; whence the לא (not) according to the קרי (Qere) is to be taken for לו (to him). And thus some subordinate the כתיב (Kethiv) and קרי (Qere), so that the immediate sense is as it is read, or that the קרי (Qere) is 'you have multiplied the nation, and magnified the joy' (they prove this construction by the accent Tiphcha on the little word לא, by the force of which they also prefer the קרי, because the distinctive accent does not permit that little word to be explained as NOT) but the subordinate sense is in the כתיב, that in no way would joy be multiplied for the Jews, while for the Gentiles the same is going to be altogether great. Who allege a similar subordinate sense of reading and writing from Job 13, 15. Is. 49, 5. ch. 63, 9. Others take it interrogatively: among whom is Ludovicus de Dieu: I am unwilling to explain it negatively; but rather interrogatively in this way: You have multiplied the nation: would you not have amplified the joy? they rejoiced before you according to the joy in the harvest. The matter itself seems to demand an interrogation, because its answer is immediately subjoined. And now it is the same as if you were reading without an interrogation. The כתיב (Kethiv) interrogates but

The כתיב is more elegant and more effective. Zwingli had preceded; who wishes to inquire of the Prophet in the person of those wondering, whether God is about to pursue the people of the nations with equal grace, as he had hitherto done for the Jews? Thus rendering: But you will multiply the nation and will not magnify the joy: so that the Prophet may answer himself in the following words: They will rejoice before you, as they rejoice in the harvest. And these interpret it concerning the multiplication of the nations. Calvin wishes the discourse here to be about the state of the Jews after the Babylonian captivity compared with the former, bringing forward a singular explanation, as he does not deny. It is, he says, as if Isaiah were saying, there was not BEFORE greater joy, even though the multitude of the people was greater; although we are few in number and small, yet with that light which shines forth, you have so exhilarated us, that no joy of the former state can be compared with this. For that redemption (from the Babylonian captivity) was as it were a prelude to that which was finally exhibited in Christ, solidly perfected and of salvation. But neither is there anything here about the Babylonian captivity or about the liberation from the same, nor is a comparison instituted with the preceding state regarding the number or the light and joy of the faithful. That interpretation is therefore entirely foreign. What? That the multitude of the faithful was more copious thereafter, if the times of Christ are viewed at the same time: since before, the ordinary assembly of the Church stood within the borders of Judea. Fr. Junius wishes another σύγκρισιν (comparison) to be instituted here between the superior administration, which preceded the advent of Christ, and that which is in his kingdom: the whole, he says, of the superior administration was varied by favorable, adverse, joyful, sad, hard, easy, turbulent, quiet, and finally all unstable things, so much so that not even the most magnificent victory called for its own mourning? But of this kingdom, which Christ is about to undertake, and with which he is about to illuminate his Church, in it there will be eternal peace: the first member of this comparison is contained in three verses, the latter in v. 6 and 7. Amplifying this nation you have not magnified the joy, i.e., when you increased your people with some notable good, victory, or honor, you nevertheless did not provide stable joy. They rejoiced before you as the joy which is conducted in the harvest, as those who exult dividing the spoil, that is, they obtained no joy ἀκονιτὶ & ἀναιματὶ (without dust and without blood), but it cost them very dearly: for arduous labors preceded the brief joy, as sweats preceded the harvest and heavy battles the spoils in this verse, which is adorned by the two following. When you have broken the yoke of his burden and the rod of his shoulder, the scepter of him who oppresses him (that is, as often as you liberated your people from the tyranny of foreigners, which is figured by two metaphors) as in the day of the Midianites (Jud. 7. 8. by which a divine victory was brought back by the Israelites.) When the whole conflict of the one conflicting is in the shaking, and the garment is rolled in slaughters, finally the food of fire went into burning; that is, on the day when the whole camp of the Midianites was divinely set against itself as if by a fire kindled, and consumed with all its things: Even to this victory, he says, there were its difficulties, and the joy, which the people perceived from it, was changed after a short interval, etc. Thus Junius, departing clearly from others: whose interpretation, however, did not approve itself to others, nor could it seem undeservedly forced. Nor indeed did every victory, or even that which is alleged here against the Midianites, cost much sweat or blood, as is evident from history; not a few were obtained by the hand of God alone. Mr. Brentius interprets it more simply thus: Although the nation of the Jews was multiplied divinely according to the promise made to Abraham, yet when Christ is about to come and to preach the Gospel, very few will place faith in him.

The nation is many, but their joy will not be great: because few will believe the Gospel. Which all interpretations, if you except the Calvinian, hold themselves more correctly than the Grotian gloss. However, the explanation of the Holy Fathers Jerome, B. Luther, and the Weimar Paraphrasts is to be preferred to them.

To the comment of the Jews and of Grotius and of certain Judaizing Papists, so that we may now return to that, these things can be opposed. (1.) That that Gloss concerning the army of Sennacherib is too arbitrary: for it is established by no document that the times of Hezekiah are looked to here. (2) A false hypothesis is supposed, that by the child born and son given in verse 9, one should understand not the Messiah, but Hezekiah, which Jewish delirium will then be refuted. (3) The apostrophe to Sennacherib has no place, because there is no trace of Sennacherib here. If it is permitted to understand anyone at will, what certainty will be left? (4) He who multiplied the nation, before him there was joy, such as is in the harvest. This, however, does not agree with Sennacherib: but with God and the Messiah; before whom is that joy. (5) The same also broke the yoke of the burden and the scepter of the exactor, by the force of the context. For that variation of the apostrophe is merely precarious, and does not suit the text. But did Sennacherib break the yoke of the burden? (6) As by joy before God is signified true and solid joy, which is not except in Christ, not fallacious and evanescent: so the cause of the same consists not in the liberation from a temporal yoke, but from a spiritual one. (7) That heap of words, yoke of the burden, rod of the shoulder, scepter of the exactor, brings in not only fear and danger, but a very hard servitude. But at the time of Hezekiah, when the Lord liberated the city from the siege of Sennacherib, he snatched the people from fear and danger, not from servitude. For the scepter of the Assyrian did not dominate him. Who will admit that the yoke of the burden is the same as a most grave siege; which nowhere, as far as is known, comes by the name of a yoke? Or that the rod of the shoulder is that which WAS STILL THREATENING the shoulders, not yet lying upon them? And that the scepter of the exactor is the tributes, which the enemy was trying to impose? Those do not exhaust the emphasis of the words of the Spirit. Saints, which imply actual servitude and Tyrannical Dominion, not only affected, but exercised with the highest rigor. And who will believe that to OVERCOME the scepter is to drive away tributes? Do we say to overcome tributes? Or is to overcome the same as to drive away? But Grotius holds everything as the same, provided the Jewish gloss prevails. (8) The cause of liberation from the yoke of the burden and the rod of the shoulder and the scepter of the oppressor is established as the birth and office of the Messiah: verse 6. Because a child is born to us, a son is given to us. And therefore there should be no doubt that these things are to be understood concerning the spiritual liberation which Christ brings. (9) By the yoke of the burden, from which we are liberated so that we may rejoice before God, the yoke of the law is to be understood, which for us is truly an α'βαςακτον yoke, Acts 15:10, because it demands those things which we cannot perform, and casts men down into hell. It is called the same rod of the shoulder, because the shoulders are struck and afflicted with pain: and also the scepter of the oppressor or the staff which the oppressor uses on lazy servants, so that he may drive them to complete his works, demanding the works of perfect justice, and, if they are not performed, inflicting eternal pain. (10) Moreover, spiritual liberation from the law, sin, …death, and hell is compared with the liberation made in the time of Midian, Jud. 7, concerning which we add only the explanation of Blessed Luther: This (liberation) happens in the way that Gideon conquered the Midianites, namely, that the enemies themselves destroy themselves. The trumpet is blown, that is the voice of the Gospel. And the pitchers are broken, that is the passion of Christ. the Word therefore and the Spirit in the word, and then the passion of Christ, produce that remarkable victory for us, without any effort of our own. For because the law, sin, and death invaded Christ, in whom we believe, as enemies, as if he were a criminal. While they kill Christ, they kill themselves, and are shattered against the body of Christ, so that they can no longer harm those who believe in that passion of Christ, whose merit Christ through the word… passion of Christ, the merit of which passion Christ freely gives through the word to all believers, so that through that passion they may have the remission of sins without any merit of their own, etc. This is that glorious victory which the Prophet celebrates here; see death killed by itself without our work. Compare the Weimar Paraphrases. Cornelius à Lapide, at this passage, institutes a lengthy comparison of this battle with the battle of Christ, but one which should be read with judgment.

Latin:

Vers. 4. JUGUM ENIM ONERIS] Obsidionem gra- vissimam.

ET VIRGAM HUMERIS EJUS] Imminentem scapulis illorum.

ET SCEPTRUM EXACTORIS] Durissima tribu- ta, quæ imposituri fuerant Hierosolymitis Assyrii.

SUPERASTI] Depulisti.

SICUT IN DIE MADIAN] Cum eos devicit Gedeon Jud. 7. Vide & infra 10, 26.

VAriam quidem interpretationem passa sunt verba Prophetica: sed Grotius pro more suo pessimam elegit: quæ Pontificiorum nonnullorum est. Thomæ nempe, Lyrani, Hugonis, Adami Sas- bouth & Tirini: vel potius cæcorum Judæor. R. Salomonis & R. Kimchi, quos Lyranus & cæteri Pa- pistæ, ut fieri amat, imprudenter sequuti sunt. Pro eo commento obtinendo fingit Grotius in eodem Commate apostrophen, modo ad Assyrium, de quo nulla vel minimo verbo facta mentio, modo ad Deum. Gentem de exercitu Sennacheribi pro lubitu interpretatur sine ullo textus indicio. Hierosoly- mitanos ingerit, de quibus nullus apex hic reperi- tur. Et quam mirabilis illa glossa verborum: Mul- tiplicasti gentem, non magnificasti lætitiam, id est, cœ- sus est magnus exercitus Sennacheribi? Sic quidlib. ex quolibet licebit efficere. Explicant autem illa alii de Judæorum gente: alii de Ethnicis magno nu- mero conversis. His præit Hieronymus: Cujus hæc integri loci est ἔκθεσις: Multiplicasti gentem, h. e. replevisti omnes gentes notitia tui, sed non magnifica- sti lætitiam. Juxta quod Apostolus mœrorem sibi di- cit esse perpetuum pro fratribus suis, qui sint Israeli- tæ. Et Jonas contristatur, quod ita salvati sint Nini- vitæ, ut cucurbita sive κίκαιον aruerit. ---- Cum er- go Christus advenerit & Christianorum gens de uni- versis gentibus fuerit congregata, tunc lætabuntur A- postoli, sicut messores lætantur in messe, de quibus Dominus loquebatur. Messis quidem multa, opera- rii autem pauci. Et sicut exultant victores, qui ca- ptam dividunt prædam. Cum enim fortis capcus fue- rit & ligatus, omnis domus ejus diripitur & dividun- tur spolia. Tu autem Domine atque Salvator jugum oneris ejus, i. e. Diaboli, qui prius exultabat in mundo, qui cunctis gentibus imperabat, qui gravissimo servitu- tis jugo colla omnium deprimebat; & virgam, qua percutiebat universos & peccata sibi quasi quoddam tributum reddere compellebat, detraxisti de humeris eorum, & tibi liberos servire fecisti absq; ullo exer- citu, & absq; effusione sanguinis in abscondita manu: sicut sub Gedeone populo Israeli de Medianitis victo- riam præbuisti. Quomodo enim vestis, quæ humano sanguine cruentata est, lavari non potest, sed infecta sanguine igne comburitur, ut maculæ cum vestimento fœdi cruoris intereant: Sic Diaboli violenta præda- tio & tumultus ac turbæ, quibus humanum sibi subje- cerat genus, gehennæ ignibus deputata sunt. Ad eun- dem fere modum Cyrillus: qui tum discipulorum Christi lætitiam, quod veluti frumentum in horreum Dominicum gentes colligant & à Satanæ tyrannica vi seductos eripiant: tum etiam eorum, qui credide- runt, intelligit: & quoad gentiles, inevitabile pecca- ti jugum sceptrumque ac regnum Satanæ, à quo nos Christus in libertatem vindicavit: nec non quoad Judæos, legis & traditionum jugum vere intolerabile ac virgam rapacitatis Pharisæorum. Similiter Ba- silius M. de lætitia spirituali & de liberatione à jugo Diabolico explicat. Plane, inquit, intolerandum & peracre jugum ille exactor injecit humanæ vitæ, com- munis sc. omnium nostrûm inimicus, virga eadens &

extorquens à nobis, ut suam unius voluntatem exple- remus. Sequuntur interpretationem Hieronymi plerique è nostris, B. Lutherus, Paraphrasta Vina- rienses & alii: sed verba ista: NON MAGNIFI- CASTI LÆTITIAM, ad Zelum & condolentiam Apostolorum, quod Judæis reprobatis gentes mul- tiplicatæ sint, refert Hieronymus. Cui adstipulatur Haymo, Cornelius à Lapide ac Menochius: Multi- plicasti gentem, id est, Tuô Immanuel Christe per te & Apostolos tuos ex Judæis & gentibus convertes, sed non auxisti lætitiam, quia videbis tu & videbunt ipsi, multo majorem partem eorum manere incredulam, & consequenter videbunt tum dolore gentis suæ, puta tam Galilæorum quam Judæorum, pro quibus ipse cum Paulo optabunt esse anathema, excidium per Titum. unde Osiander, multiplicasti gentem, potentes red- didisti Gentes, circa tempus revelati Christi: (ita ut Romana gens Judæos tum subjugârit, eosq; vectigales fecerit, atq; illis imperaverit) non magnificasti læ- titiam, ea res populo Judaico non magnum sane attulit gaudium: Jugum enim Romanum Judæi iniquissimo animo tulerunt. Nihilominus tamen ii, qui Chri- stum agnoscent, plus gaudii ex ejus agnitione perci- pient, quam mœstitiæ ex Romanorum superbo Domi- nio. Lætabuntur enim coram te, ô Christe Fili Dei, qui te per fidem agnoverint, sicut qui lætantur in Messe. Alii ad invidiam Judæorum referunt: unde B. Lutherus ita παραφράζει: Recipiunt gentes Ev- angelium atq; sic augetur Ecclesia accessione gentium, sed eam felicitatem gentium Judæi gentibus invident: Sicut dicit, in gente stulta irritabo eos Deut. 32. Item in populo non populo provocabo eos. Atq; hoc est quod dicit, non magnificasti lætitiam. Alii de calamitatibus externis interpretantur, quæ con- sequi solent receptionem Evangelii, tristitiam & mœrorem afferunt: non magnificasti lætitiam quo- ad externam statum: siquidem multæ persecu- tiones & miseriæ sequuturæ sint Matth. 10, 34. Joh. 15, 18. maxime à contumacibus Judæis 1. Thess. 2, 14. 15. uti interpretantur Vinarienses & Oecolampa- dius: cætera quæ adduntur κατ᾿ ἀντίθεσιν de læti- tia interna accipientes: siquidem dicatur: Læta- buntur CORAM TE, h. e. etiamsi non appareat co- ram mundo. Neque enim Sancti in adversitate relin- quuntur absq; omni gaudio. Causa etiam additur, quare ita gavisuri sint fideles, quia à gravissimis pec- catorum sarcinis & pœnis atq; onere legis & virga & stimulo antiqui hostis vel carnis liberati sumus Joh. 8. Nonnulli particulam לא positam esse pro לו existi- mant. Multiplicasti gentem ipsi, magnificasti læti- tiam: quam sententiam Ebræorum esse, nec ablu- dere Jonathanem vel LXX. notat Oecolampadius. Et observat Masora ipsa hanc lectionem; unde τὸ לא secundum τὸ קרי sumendum pro לו Ei. Atque ita fubordinant quidam τὸ כתיב קרי, ut sensus proxim9 sit uti legitur, vel אד τὸ קרי gentem mul- tiplicasti, & magnificasti lætitiam (hanc constructio- nem ab accentu Tiphcha in vocula לא probant, vi cujus etiam τὸ קרי præferunt, quod accentus distin- ctivus non permittat explicari voculam eam per NON) sensus autem subordinatus sit in τῷ כתיב, i- ta nequaquam Judæis multiplicatum iri lætitiam, cum gentibus eadem omnino magna futura est. Qui simi- lem sensum lectionis & scriptionis subordinatum allegant ex Iob. 13, 15. Es. 49, 5. c. 63, 9. Alii inter- rogative accipiunt: è quibus est Ludovicus de Dieu: nolìm negative exponere; verum interrogative hoc modo: Multiplicasti gentem: annon amplificasses gaudium? gavisi sunt coram te secundum gaudium in messe. Res ipsa videtur interrogationem postula- re, quia ejus responsio statim subjicitur. Et jam idem est ac si legeres sine interrogatione. Interrogat כתיב sed

τὸ כתיב elegantius est & efficacius. Præiverat Zuvinglius; qui vult percontari Prophetam in per- sona admirantium, an Deus gentium populum sit pari gratia prosequturus, atque Judæis hactenus fecerat? Sic reddens; Sed multiplicabis gentem & non ma- gnificabis lætitiam: ut verbis sequentibus respondeat Propheta sibi ipsi: Lætabuntur apud te, quemad- modum gaudent in messe. Atque hi de gentium multiplicatione interpretantur. De Judæorum sta- tu post captivitatem Babylonicam cum priori com- parato hic sermonem esse vult Calvinus, singula- rem, uti non diffitetur, afferens explicationem. Perinde est, inquit, ac si diceret Esaias, non fuisse AN- TEA majorem lætitiam, tametsi major esset populi multitudo; quamvis pauci numero simus & pusilli, ta- men ea luce, quæ effulges, nos ita exhilarasti, ut nul- lum prioris statu gaudium cum isto comparari queat. Nam earedemtio (è captivitate Babylonica) veluti præludium ejus erat, quæ in Christo demum exhibita est solide perfecta& salutis. Sed neque de captivitate Babylonica hic quicquam aut de liberatione ex ea- dem, neque comparatio cum præcedenti statu in- stituitur quoad numerum aut lucem & lætitiam fi- delium. Aliena itaque prorsus est illa interpreta- tio. Quid? quod copiosior multitudo fidelium deinceps fuerit, si tempora Christi simul specten- tur: quum antea intra Judææ terminos steterit cœ- tus Ecclesiæ ordinarius. Fr. Junius aliam σύγκρι- σιν hic institui vult inter superiorem administratio- nem, quæ præcessit adventum Christi, & illam quæ est in regno ipsius: tota, inquit, superior administratio varia fuit secundis, adversis, lætis, tristibus, duris, fa- cilibus, turbulentis, quietis, omnibus deniq; rebus in- stabilibus, adeo ut ne magnificentissima quidem victo- ria suo luctu vocaverit? Sed regni hujus, quod susce- pturus est Christus, eoque Ecclesiam suam illustratu- rus, in eo pax futura est sempiterna: hujus compa- rationis prius membrum tribus versibus continetur, posterius v. 6. & 7. Amplificans hanc gentem non magnificasti lætitiam, q. d. quum populum tuum in- signi aliquo bono, victoria, aut honore auxisti, lætitiam tamen stabilem minime præstitisti. Lætati sunt co- ram te quasi lætitia, quæ agitur in messe, ut qui exultant partientes prædam, id est, nullam lætitiam consecuti sunt ἀκονιτὶ & ἀναιματὶ sine sudore & san- guine, sed permagno illis constitit: nam ardui labores lætitiam brevem anteiverunt, ut sudores messem & pugnæ graves spolia hoc versu, quod duobus sequ. ex- ornatur. Quum jugum oneris illius & virgam hu- meri illius, sceptrum opprimentis illum contrivisti (id est, quoties liberavisti populum tuum ab extero- rum tyrannide, quæ metaphoris duabus figuratur) ut die Medianitarum (Jud. 7. 8. quo divina victoria ab Israelitis reportata est.) Quando tota conflicta- tio confligentis in concussu, & vestimentum volu- tatum est in cædibus, denique abiit in excussionem pabulum ignis; id est, quo die tota Medianitarum castra divinitus inter se commissa tanquam igne ac- censo cum rebus suis omnibus consumta sunt: Etiam huic victoriæ, inquit, suæ fuerunt difficultates, & læti- tia, quam inde percepit populus, non longo intervallo mutata est &c. Ita Junius ab aliis plane discedens: cujus tamen interpretatio aliis sese non probavit, nec immerito coacta videri possit. Neque vero omnis victoria imo nec illa, quæ hic allegatur ad- versus Midianitas, multo sudore aut sanguine con- stitit, uti ex historia constat; non paucæ sola Dei manu obtentæ sunt. Dn. Brentius simplicius ita interpretatur; Etsi Judæorum gens multiplicata est divinitus juxta promissionem dictam ad Abraha- mum, tamen cum venturus est Christus & prædicatu- rus Evangelium, paucissimi adhibebunt ei fidem.

Gens est multa, sed non erit magna lætitia eorum : quia pauci credent Evangelio. Quæ omnes inter- pretationes, si Calvinianam excipias, rectius sese habent, quam Grotiana glossa. Præferenda autem iisdem S. Patrum Hieronymi, B. Lutheri & Para- phrastarum Vinariensium explicatio.

Judæorum & Grotii ac Papistarum quorundam Judaizantium commento, ut ad illud nunc redea- mus, hæc opponi possunt. (1.) quod Glossa illa de Sennacheribi exercitu nimis arbitraria sit : nul- lo enim documento constat, respici hic Ezechiæ tempora. (2) Falsa supponitur hypothesis, per pue- rum natum & filium datum versu 9. intelligendum esse non Messiam, sed Ezechiam, quod Judaicum delirium deinde profligabitur. (3) Apostrophe ad Sennacheribum nullum habet locum, quia de Sen- nacheribo nullum hic vestigium. Si pro lubitu quemlibet subaudire liceat, quænam relinquetur certitudo? (4) Qui multiplicavit gentem, coram illo lætitia fuit, qualis in messe est. Hoc vero non congruit Sennacheribo : sed Deo & Messiæ ; coram quo est illa lætitia. (5) Idem etiam contrivit jugum oneris & sceptrum exactoris, vi contextus. Illa enim varicatio apostrophæ mere precaria est, textuique haut convenit. At num Sennacherib contrivit jugum oneris ? (6) Ut per lætitiam coram Deo ve- rum & solidum gaudium, quod non est nisi in Chri- sto, non fallax & evanidum, significatur : ita ejus- dem causa non in liberatione à temporali jugo, sed à spirituali consistit. (7) Congeries illa verborum, jugum oneris, virga humeri, sceptrum exactoris non metum tantum & periculum, sed servitutem infert perquam duram. At Ezechiæ tempore, cum à Senna- cheribi obsidione urbem liberavit Dominus, po- pulum è metu ac periculo, non è servitute eripuit. Neque enim sceptrum Assyrii dominatum illi est. Quis admittet, jugum oneris idem esse, quod obsi- dionem gravissimam ; quæ nuspiam, quod constet, jugi nomine venit ? Aut virgam humeri esse, quæ IMMINEBAT ADHUC humeris, nondum in- cumbebat iisdem ? & sceptrum exactoris esse tri- buta, quæ hostis imponere conabatur ? Non ex- hauriunt illa emphasin verborum Sp. Sancti, quæ servitutem actualem & Dominium Tyrannicum, non affectatum tantum, sed exercitum summocum rigore important. Et quis credet, sceptrum SU- PERARE esse depellere tributa ? num tributa di- cimus superare ? aut superare idem est quod depelle- re ? Sed Grotius omnia perinde habet, modo Ju- daica glossa obtineat. (8) Causa liberationis à ju- go oneris & virga humeri & sceptro exactoris con- stituitur Messiæ nativitas & officium : vers. 6. Quia puer natus est nobis, filius datus est nobis. Ideoque dubium esse non debet de liberatione spirituali, quam affert Christus, hæc intelligenda esse. (9) Per jugum oneris, à quo liberamur, ut coram Deo læte- mur, jugum legis intelligendum, quod nobis vere est jugum α'βαςακτον Act. 15,10. quia exigit ea, quæ præstare non possumus, & deprimit homines in in- fernum. Dicitur eadem virga humeri, quia percu- tiuntur eadem ac dolore affliguntur humeri : nec non sceptrum exactoris vel baculus, quo exactor uti- tur in servos ignavos, ut ad perficienda opera sua impellat, exigens opera perfectæ justitiæ, ac, si non præstentur ea, æternum infligens dolorem. (10) Spi- ritualis autem liberatio à lege, peccato, morte, & infer- no confertur cum liberatione tempore Midian. facta Jud. 7. de quo solum B. Lutheri addimus ex- plicationem : Fit autem hæc (liberatio) eo modo, quo Gedeon vicit Madianitas, nempe ut ipsi hostes se- ipsos conficiant. Inflatur tuba, ea est Evangelii vox. Et lagenæ colliduntur, ea est passio Christi. Verbum igitur & Spiritus in verbo, dein Christi passio insignem illam victoriam nobis pariunt, sine ullo nostro studio. Quia enim lex, peccatum & mors, Christum, in quem nos credimus, hostiliter, tanquam reum invaserunt. Dum Christum occidunt, seipsos occidunt, & sunt in corpore Christi collisi, ut amplius nocere non possint cre- dentibus in illam passionem Christi, cujus passionis meritum Christus per verbum gratis donat omnibus credentibus, ut per eam passionem habeant remissio- nem peccatorum sine aliquo suo merito &c. Hæc est gloriosa illa victoria, quam Propheta hic celebrat, vi- dete mortem occisam per seipsam sine nostro opere. Confer. Paraphr. Vinarienses. Prolixam collatio- nem pugnæ istius cum pugna Christi, sed quæ cum judicio legenda, instituit Cornelius à Lapide ad h. l.

## 9:5
Verse 5. FOR EVERY VIOLENT PLUNDER WITH TUMULT, AND A GARMENT ROLLED IN BLOOD SHALL BE FOR BURNING, AND FOOD FOR FIRE] In the Hebrew it is thus: Every battle of those fighting (is wont to be) with noise and garments rolled in blood, (but this one shall be as) fuel for fire for burning. Other slaughters of enemies are wont to be prepared with much labor and much blood, but this one will be like a fire consuming suddenly. For it is clearly sudden, without tumult, without a wound, without the labor or danger of the Hebrews. The Assyrians were extinguished by an Angel. No flame could have killed them so quickly. See 10, 16.

Grotius owes this again to the Rabbis. But that parenthesis is not held in the text; Grotius inserts it on his own (But this one shall be as) or rather from Rabbinic commentaries. In the sources, however, a vau copulative occurs.
