But just as a spouse does not with difficulty bear external dissensions, if only he has domestic peace with his spouse; so he who has peace of conscience before God does not with difficulty bear the adversities which happen to him from without. The Hebrews are accustomed to designate every happiness by the name שׁלום. Thus, therefore, he is also called Prince of Peace for the reason that he is the author of all the happiness that falls to our lot, both temporal and eternal. For outside of him there is no salvation, Acts 4:12.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PARVULUS ENIM NATUS EST NOBIS] Id est, nascetur. Nam Hebræa præterita sumuntur pro futuris.

ET FILIUS DATUS EST NOBIS] Dabitur. Ezechias Patri Achazo multum dissimilis. De eodem infra XI. Sic tamen, ut multo excellentius hæc ad Messiam pertinere, non Christiani tantum agnoscant, sed & Chaldæus hoc loco.

Pessime iterum Judaizat Grotius, dum secundum literalem sensum vaticinium de Ezechia intelligit. Quanquam vero addat, excellentiori modo hæc ad Messiam pertinere, & Christianos & Chaldæum agnoscere, non tamen, an eam explicationem ipse calculo suo probet, significavit. Neque si sensu mystico de Christo intellectum velit, quod secundum literam de Ezechia dictum credidit, vel Christianorum ullorum vel Chaldæi interpretis suffragium habet: qui certe non de Ezechia simul, sed UNICE de Christo interpretantur. Judæis autem cæcis gratam præstat operam, à quorum Rabbinis hic etiam seductus sensus nativi objectum Ezechiam facit: Nam si hoc obtineant illi, facile concedere poterunt, suo modo mystice ea ad Messiam transferri posse. Non potest autem geminus ille sensus consistere. Nam si puer natus est Ezechias, secundum

Messias idem esse non potest: Si Epitheta illa sunt Ezechiæ hic tributa, non poterunt ea de Mes- sia explicari. Neque enim videndum, de quo- nam accipi POSSINT, aut cui ea convenire QUEANT, sed de quonam hic enuncientur ex intentione Spiritus Sancti, quæ non potest ge- mina esse, quum Spir. S. certum inesse sensum voluerit vaticiniis suis, non vero eadem diversa mente verbis ambiguis sensum pla- ne disparatum inferentibus protulerit, aut dis- parato sensu intellecta voluerit. Neque possunt illa de Ezechia intelligi. Nam de eodem nullum hactenus verbum prolatum, neque ullum ejus rei vestigium deprehenditur, quod hic de Hiskia va- ticinatus sit Propheta. Tum vero de liberatione ac jugo spirituali egit: quæ Hiskiæ adscribi nequit. Egit de gaudio coram Domino & in Domino, quod spirituale est fidelium gaudium. Et causam læ- titiæ & liberationis hujus nativitatem pueri consti- tuit. Num autem Hiskiæ nativitas lætitiam & liberationem illam spiritualem attulit? Hiero- nymus in hunc locum: Ideo Diabolus & omnis ejus violenta prædatio, qua humanum suppresse- rat genus, & sanguinem sanguine miscuerat, erit in combustionem & cibos ignis æterni, quia natus est nobis de virgine puer, de quo supra dictum est: antequam sciat puer &c. Adhæc de ejus nativi- tate agitur, qui lucem afferre debuit ambulanti- bus in tenebris Galilæis & Judæis. Quod de Christo unice intelligendum esse hactenus docui- mus; imo sonora voce docet Spiritus Sanctus Matth. 4. de Hiskia autem nemo dixerit. Ne- que ambigere licet, Prophetam hac tam magni- fica & illustri promissione denuo fideles confir- mare voluisse de signo augustissimo, quod ipsis antea promiserat, Cap. 7. ac plenius edocere, quidnam habere ac credere debeant de virginis filio Immanuele; siquidem hæc præcipua cura fuerit Prophetarum, fidem in Messiam excita- re ac confirmare, in quo munere præ aliis oc- cupatus fuit Prophetarum Coryphæus Esaias. Atque hæc argumenta à συνεχειᾳ anteceden- tium deprompta luce sua radiant. Jam si ver- ba ipsa vaticinii præsentis attendamus, Puer, in- quit Propheta, natus est nobis, Filius datus est nobis: vocans eum puerum simul & Filium, non certe per βαττολογιαν inanem: Sed quemad modum pii veteres observarunt, ut voce pueri naturam humanam, voce Filii divinam designet. Quia puer hic vere est Filius Dei, uti Angelus te- statur. Sanctum (vel puer ille sanctus) quod (vel qui) ex te nascetur, Filius altissimi vocabitur. Et apprime id illustrat locus parallelus de filio Dei unigenito nobis dato Johan. 3, 16. Calvinus hic ita habet: Filius sine adjectione non potest a- lius intelligi à DEI Filio. Et nunc κατ' ἐξοχὴν Christo tribuitur, ut sciamus hac insigni nota eum discerni à reliquo genere humano. Nec vero du- bium est, quin ad solenne illud oraculum respexerit Esaias; quod per ora omnium volitabat: Ero ei in Patrem & ipse erit mihi in Filium: sicut & Psalm. 2. repetitur: Filius meus es tu, ego ho- die genui te. Nisi enim res vulgo nota, & celebris fuisset, Messiam fore Dei Filium, inepte & absque sensu Filium simpliciter vocasset Esaias. Quare elogium hoc à superiore vaticinio dependet: ex quo Apostolus Heb. 1. Christi præstantiam colligit, supra omnes Angelos efferri. Cæterum quamvis in habitu pueri contemptibilis fuerit Christus: Filii tamen titulo ornatur ejus dignitas. Neque te- mere prætermittendum illud NOBIS. Nam Propheta se, ac fideles quosvis hac voce com- prehendit: quibus peculiariter natus, datusque est Messias (non vero Hiskias,) quemadmodum etiam supra eundem vocavit Immanuel Nobis- cum Deus. Nobis, inquit, natus est ille puer; nobis datus est ille filius, qui est עמנו־אל Nobis- cum DEUS. De qua voce Nobis Cyrillus in hunc locum: dicit nobis datum esse Filium. Fa- ctus est enim homo unigenitum DEI verbum, non propter seipsum, sed potius ut nostram conditionem, sicut fuit a principio, restauraret, & ut omnium vitæ pretium ac redemtionem suum corpus DEO & Patri in odorem suavitatis offerret. Sed imprimis pensi habenda sunt nomina & Epitheta, ut & mu- nia atque ἐνεργήματα, quæ huic puero tribuun- tur, quæ tanta sunt, ut neutiquam ulli Regum mortalium conveniant, neque ad Hiskiam, nisi per insignem ἐρεσχλίατητα transferri possint. Co- natur quidem Grotius de Ezechia omnia explica- re; sed uti in hoc plane judaizat, ita nimis ma- nifestum est, quantopere pervertantur verba il- lustrissima & enervetur totum vaticinium. Un- de ista collusione cum Judæis aliud nihil, quam omnium Cordatorum detestationem promeruit. Quis enim æquo ferret animo, cum puer hic vocandus dicitur פלא admirabilis, Hiskiæ id a- ptari ob summas, quæ in eo fuerunt, virtutes; quum nec David, neque Moses, neque Abra- ham ipse, aut ullus fidelium nomen id obtinue- rit: multo minus id Hiskiæ ceu proprium conve- niat: Messiæ autem convenire nemo dubitet. Qui etiam ita se appellat Jud. 13, 18. Quis admit- tet, titulos illos diversissimos, Consiliarius, Deus fortis, quos nemo non Interpp. Christia- norum, Judæorum pro diversis habuit, nova & inaudita ratione in statu constructionis expo- nendos esse CONSULTATOR DEI FORTIS! Quis non detestabitur depravationem illam emi- nentissimi tituli Pater futuri seculi vel Pater æ- ternus, id est, qui multos post se relicturus sit po- steros & in longum tempus: quo pacto Epithe- ton illud augustum אבי עד potius Abrahamo, & adhuc potiori jure Noacho, potissimo autem A- damo conveniret, neutiquam vero Ezechiæ ut proprium peculiariter vendicari deberet. Quis patietur titulum illum Ezechiæ appropriari, quod vocandus sit שר־שלום Princeps pacis! Id e- nim nominis potiori jure aliis, imprimis Salomo- ni conveniret, si de ψιλῶ ἀνθρώπῳ dicendum sit. Et quam jejuna est illa glossa, multiplicabi- tur ejus imperium, id est, durabit per annos 29. Ita multo magis id conveniret Asariæ imperio, qui per 52. annos regnavit; vel Joas, qui regnavit 40. annos; & Assæ, qui præfuit 41. annis, aliisque. Quam frivola, imo perversa est interpretatio ver- borum, PACIS EJUS NON ERIT FINIS, i. e. ad finem dierum suorum pace fruetur. Pacem æ- ternam fine carituram illa promittere, verborum ipsorum tenor convincit. Quam turpis est illa depravatio A MODO ET USQUE IN SEM- PITERNUM, id est, ab initio ad finem vitæ? Quid enim hic novi in Hiskia: quum de cæ- teris piis & fidelibus Regibus plerisque idem con- stet, quod in judicio & justitia stabilierint regna sua usque ad finem vitæ, eo, quo hæc explicat Grotius, sensu; quanquam de nullo Regum id ἁ- πλῶς dici possit, neque de Ezechia, quod confir- mavit regnum suum & stabiliverit in judicio & in justitia. Nemo enim repertus unquam est, qui non aliquando à judicio & justitia desciverit sive per ignorantiam & infirmitatem, sive per voluntariam declinationem. Et peculiari sensu hæc de Christo dici, eique appropriari, ex aliis parallelis locis con- stat; cui etiam omnes isti tituli indubie conve- niunt. Habemus hic Grotium confitentem. In Christo, inquit, & hæc, & quæ præcedunt, habent significationem multo ut augustiorem, ita & planio- rem. Cur ergo sensum illum multo non tantum augustiorem, sed etiam planiorem non sinit esse sen- sum nativum, proprium & literalem? Argumen- tor ita: Qui sensus multo augustior est multoque planior in Prophetiâ perquam insigni, is sine dubio pro literali & proprio magis habendus est, quam sensus minus augustus, minus planus, imo dubius prorsus, obscurus, insufficiens, alienus, inusitatus & cum insigni verborum τρεβλότητι conjunctus. At sensus de Messia multo augustior & planior est in hac tam insigni Prophetia: ideoque magis pro li- terali habendus, quam Grotianus.

Quid quod vaticinium hoc de Christo expli- carit Angelus Gabriel, & quidem in eam sententiam, ut planum sit, non posse id convenire Hiskiæ: nam Christum esse illum, qui super Davidis solium vi hujus vaticinii sedere ac Rex æternus esse debeat, cujus regni finis futurus non sit, testatur Luc. 1, 33. ideoque aperte docet, de illo Rege vaticinium esse intelligendum, cujus regni finis nullus est: nec ali- ter verba Prophetica, Pacis ejus non erit finis, & à modo & usq́ in sempiternum intelligenda esse, quam de æterna pace & de æterno imperio finem nullum habente. Quam interpretationem Angelicam di- cti Prophetici non diffitetur Grotius ad Matth. 22, 42. Quod si porro cum hoc oraculo conferas va- ticinium Es. 10, 1. de virga è radice Jesse, quia de eo- dem subjecto utrobique agi agnoscit Grotius, ul- terius refelli inde poterit Judaica glossa de Ezechia: siquidem ibi non de Ezechia, sed de Christo vati- cinatum esse Prophetam, luculentum sit, quemad- modum ad c. 11. probaturi sumus. Adde his jam totius Ecclesiæ Christianæ judicium. Hactenus e- nim nemo inter Christianos dubitavit, Prophe- tam quoad literam hic de Messia vaticinari. De quo unanimi consensu veteris Ecclesiæ Dd. hoc oracu- lum intellexêre. Justinus contra Tryphonem, Tertull. contr. Marcion. Novatianus de Trin. C. 26. Hieronymus, Cyrillus Alexandr. & Basilius M. in h. l. Athanasius, Ambrosius aliiqve Patres pas- sim hoc ceu indubitatum assumunt, quod hic de Filio Dei agatur: quod etiam Patres passim ad- versus Arianos, aliosque hæreticos adhibuisse in disputationibus leguntur. Neq; ab hæreticis ipsis ullum de eo dubium motum: nemini certe in mentem Ezechias venit. Imo Majores nostri hoc dictum tanti fecerunt, ut id commendarent Eccle- siæ publico carmine: eoque utatur Ecclesia in Fe- sto Nativitatis Domini, cum canit; Puer natus &c. Neque è recentioribus Judæis quisquam hoc con- cessit, secundum literam hic de Ezechia agi. Calvi- nus ipse, qui alias lubenter in talibus judaizat, im- pudentiam Judæorum hoc in loco perstrinxit: Ju- dæi detorquent impudentius locum hunc; Nam de Eze chia interpretantur. Sociniani, qui nihil non in o- raculis de Deitate Christi tentare solent, fatentur hic de Christo agi: Christus apud Esaiam vocan- dus Deus fortis, inquit Crellius lib. 1. de ver. Rel. c. 8. Similiter Volckelius l. 5. c. 10. Esaias olim præ- dixit Christum vocatum iri Patrem æternitatis seu sæculi futuri. Schlichting. disp. de Trinit. contr. Meisn. p. 244. 260. Patris nomine hic certa persona nempe Christus designatur. Nec aliter Episcopius Arminianus, quem sequi solet Grotius. Quid mul- tis? Grotius ipse fassus est, hoc vaticinium non ali- ter, quam de Christo intelligendum esse. Siquidem ad Matth. 22, 42. Christum fore filium Davidis à Ju- dæis agnitum esse dicat ex vaticinio Es. 9, 7. eoq́ tan- dem quam APERTISSIMO usum esse Gabrielem ad Mariam Luc. 1. Quomodo autem id apertissi- mum esset de Messia vaticinium, si sensu nativo a- geret de Hiskia?

ET FACTUS EST PRINCIPATUS EJUS, SU- PER HUMERUM EJUS] Id est, erit πορφυρογέννητος: ab ipsis cunis purpuram feret regiam: ut in regnum na- tus, Confer. Ezech. 28, 13.

Quid peculiare hoc de Hiskia? Annon omnes Reges Juda inde a Davide πορφυρογέννητοι fuere, quemadmodum Hiskias? siquidem perinde ita Reges hæreditarii fuerint. Nihil certe hac in re præ aliis proprium ac singulare habet Hiskias. Si vero phrasi illa id designetur, non quod tantum in Regnum natus sit hic puer: sed quod ab ipsa nati- vitate principatum gesserit, nulli certe nisi Messiæ hoc conveniret: qui Rex Judæorum natus purpu- ram ab ipsis cunis gessit, & ab Angelis in cunis cele- bratus ut Dominus, a Magis Orientis adoratus ut Rex Judæorum fuit. In quam sententiam explicant hoc veteres, quod parvulus hic ab initio conceptio- nis sua principatum gesserit, idque ex vi originis suæ propter unionem hypostaticam naturæ humanæ cum divina. Dicitur autem gestare principatum su- per humeros suos, quia signa regiminis feruntur hu- meris. Unde Princeps dicitur נשׂיא bajulus sui po- puli ac Reip. & currus atq; auriga, quia non tantum dirigit instar aurigæ, sed portat quoque onera in- star currus. Deinde etiam dicitur super humeros suos gestare principatum ad distinctionem alio- rum imperatorum & principum: qui magnam partem principatus & regiminis sui, consiliariorum suorum & officialium humeris imponunt. De nullo ergo mundano Monarcha hoc dici potest, quod principatum universum super humeros suos gerat; quia nec administrari regna, nec defendi possunt per unum solum hominem; imo principatus & ad- ministratio regni mundani magis est imposita in humeros alienos, quam in proprios humeros regis. Christus autem talis est Rex, cujus principatus est super ipsius solius humeros, ipse solus est, qui regit, gubernat & conservat populum suum per totum orbem. Ipse solus est, qui defendit ac tuetur eum adversus Satanam, mortem & infernum. Tertio notatur etiam obedientia Christi, cum factus dici- tur principatus super humeros ejus, h. e. impositum ei dominium; non certe leve, sed valde onerosum. Nam ut onera imponi solent humeris ab aliis, utpote subditis a principibus: ita huic principi onus im- positum super humeros ejus principatus & admi- nistrationis regiminis, ad quam pertinet cumpri- mis ereptio subditorum e potestate hostium spiri- tualium. Quod onus in humeros suos suscepit atq; exantlavit Christus, factus obediens Deo Patri usq; ad mortem, mortem autem crucis Phil. 2. Atque in eo iterum maximopere differt a mundano Monar- cha quocunque. Hi enim onera non portant ipsi, sed subditis imponunt; neque ipsorum est parere, sed imperare. At hujus Regis principatus paritio- nem & obedientiam importat. Ideoque imponi passus est humeris suis principatum, ut onera subi- ret ipse, quæ exantlanda erant: ut solet in Scriptu- ris obedientia, submissio & patientia notari, cum quid humeris imponi dicitur. Nonnullis videtur hic alludi ad virgam humeri, de qua v. 4. q. d. Dia- bolus & tyranni virgam & sceptrum, juxta onera imperii sui subditorum humeris imponunt: at Christus suis humeris sustinebit virgam & onus sui principatus. Hinc ergo Quarto applicatur etiam hoc ad crucem Christi, quæ humeris ejus imposita est. Quia principatus ejus in cruce est: per cru- cem & hostes destruxit, & subditos suos liberavit.

Idem per crucis suæ virtutem regit ac gubernat populum suum. Crux etiam illa, quam humeris suis bajulavit, quid aliud, quam insigne est & sce- ptrum imperii hujusce Regis nostri plane pro- prium & peculiare? Quo de Tertul. l. cont. Ju- dæos cap. 10. Quis omnino Regum insigne potestatis suæ humero præfert & non aut in capite diadema aut in manu sceptrum, aut aliquam propriæ vestis no- tam: sed solus Rex novus novorum seculorum, Christus Jesus novam gloriam & potestatem & subli- mitatem suam in humero extulit, crucem sc. ut secun- dum Davidis Prophetiam exinde Dominus regnavit in ligno. Quemadmodum Psalm. 95, 10. legebant in Græca versione LXX. Interpp. veteres: regnavit à ligno Deus. Quæ iisdem verbis repetit Tertul- lianus l. 3. advers. Marcion. C. 19. Eundem sensum ab aliis traditum notat & approbat Cyrillus: quo- niam crucem portans humeris Dominus noster J. Chri- stus ad passionem salutarem venit & exaltatus est & orbem terrarum per seipsum obtinuit: hinc fuisse di- citur principatus ejus super humero ejus. Sic Basi- lius: Cujus principatus est super humerum ejus, h.e. regnum & potestas in ipsius cruce. In crucem enim exaltatus ad seipsum pertraxit omnia. Atque ita etiam Hieronymus, Augustinus & ante illos omnes Justinus Apol. 2. pro Christ. ostendit hoc oraculum virtutem crucis, quam humeris applicuit in eandem actus.

Quinto designatur ita etiam fortitudo ejus. Quum enim per humerum notetur fortitudo, su- per humeris ipsius principatus factus dicitur, quod sua ipsius virtute & fortitudine humeris atque bra- chio suo eundem portet. Quem sensum reddit Cyrillus: ac cum priori conjungi videtur nimirum hic Propheticus sermo, humerum appellare fortitudi- nem. Omne siquidem robur nostrum in brachiis & humeris situm est. Et quidem brachium Dei ac Pa- tris dicitur Filius (Es. 53, 1.) Imperavit ergo orbiter- rarum sua ipsius potentia Christus, quippe fortitudo est Dei ac Patris. Similiter explicat quoque Hie- ronymus in h. l.

Sexto B. Lutherus aliud adhuc Regi huic pro- prium observat: quod nempe subditos suos gerat super humero suo. Videtur mihi simplicissime expo- ni posse; quod nos, qui sumus principatus ejus, ge- stamur in humero ejus, contra quam in mundi regnis fieri solet. In mundo enim subditi ferunt & tolerant Re- ges suos, à quibus tam res, quam corpora subditorum in servitutem rediguntur: Diversa autem ratio est Re- gni Christi, neq; enim portatur Christus à principa- tu & subditis suis, sed ipse portat principatum suum h. e. noster servus, ut nos simus liberi & Reges. Sic adhuc hodie nos fert. Quemadmodum autem ipse nos fert, ita vult vicissim, ut sui lapides alter alterum portet, ut tamen omnium nostrum portatio, qua alios portamus ad Exemplum Christi, portetur ab ipso la- pide angulari Christo. Hæc Sententia magis mihi placet, quod formam regni Christi continet & in se & in membris suis. Hæc B. Lutherus. Possunt au- tem conjungi illæ sententiæ, quia subordinatæ sunt, & ad Christi regnum omnes faciunt.

Vers. eod. ET VOCABITUR NOMEN EJUS] In Hebræo est, vocabit: supple quisque. Etiam Chaldæus vocabitur transtulit. Notum autem Hebræis dici sic vel sic vocari aliquem, cui tales tituli aut ἐπίθετα conveniunt.

Vers. eod. ADMIRABILIS] Ob summas, quæ in eo erunt Virtutes.

Nimis tenuiter. Si ob virtutes tantum mira- bilis vocatur hic puer, non est ipsi nomen hoc pro- prium: quod tamen indicat Propheta, quia virtu- tibus alii quoque claruere. Rectius proinde alii interpp. qui ὁμοθυμαδὸν de Christo hoc explicant vere admirabili, tum ratione personae, in qua nun- quam satis mirari possumus τὸ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα μυστήριον unionis duarum naturarum hypostaticae 1. Tim. 3. 16. tum ratione officii, in quo admiran- da potentia, sapientia & bonitas elucescit : in mu- nere Prophetico, qua doctrinam virtutemque istius doctrinae admirandam & miracula stupenda, qui- bus illam obsignavit: in Sacerdotali, qua sacrifi- cium mirabile atque effectum ejusdem vere admi- randum: In Regio denique, qua mirabilem ho- stium debellationem & Ecclesiae gubernationem, Tum denique ratione status ejusdem & exinanitio- nis, & exaltationis, in quo utroque & omnibus eo- rum actibus stupenda magnalia Dei meraque mi- racula occurrunt. Summa, nihil non mirabile est in hoc puero, quem describit Propheta: Qui etiam se mirabilem vocavit Jud. 13. 18. Quid quaeris nomen meum, quod est פלא mirabile ! Brentius observat, hoc cognomen Messiae tribui per anti- thesin mundanorum Principum. Hi enim non pos- sunt mirifice suos juvare & è periculis liberare. Ju- vant eos nonnunquam, sed pro more hujus seculi vel externis armis vel auxiliis sociorum. Messias autem juvat & liberat suos mirifice & nullo alio ad- jutore. Sunt autem duplicia miracula Messiae, quibus populum suum juvit: Alia sunt corporalia: Restituit enim caecis visum; leprosis mundiciem, claudis sanitatem, surdis auditum, mutis loque- lam, mortuis vitam. Sic nullus mundanus Mo- narcha suos adjuvare potuit. Alia sunt spiritua- lia. Messias enim mirabiliter conservat suos; In peccatis, ut reputentur justi: in morte, ut habeant vitam; in erroribus, ut firmi, ut accipiant feudum coeleste. Tam mirabilis enim est adjutor & li- berator, ut cum omnia humanitus videantur per- dita & desperata, ipse suo auxilio praesto adsit.

CONSILIARIUS, DEUS FORTIS] Imo consul- tator Dei fortis: id est, qui in omnibus negociis consi- lia à Deo poscet, per Prophetas scilicet, ut jam seque- tur.

Insignis & detestanda depravatio nominum Messiae, ut ad Ezechiam ea detorqueri possint. Qualis ne Judaeorum Magistris ipsis ad quaevis excogitanda ingeniosissimis in mentem venit. No- mina enim illa distincta esse agnoverunt, quia res clara est: ideoque ne Messiae tam augusta no- mina largiantur, DEUM Patrem illis describi commenti sunt, utpote qui Hiskiam nominatu- rus sit principem pacis, hoc pacto: Et vocabit eum admirabilis, consultor, Deus, fortis, Pater aeternus principem pacis. Quae aperta corrupte- la est. Siquidem non de Dei nominibus, sed de appellationibus pueri hic res sit. Hae vero sex numerantur ab Hieronymo aliisque In- terpp. MIRABILIS, CONSILIA- RIUS, DEUS, FORTIS, PATER AE- TERNUS, PRINCEPS PACIS. Cae- tera omnia simplicia sunt, & ut nomina separa- ta ponuntur; duo postrema composita esse nomina, virgula Makkaph docet: uti nomen פלא de puero simpliciter effertur; sic etiam nomen יעץ: ac similiter etiam nomen אל atque גבור cum Vulgata recte redduntur admirabilis, consiliarius, Deus, fortis. Porro quidnam hoc peculiare est, consilia à Deo poscere? Annon hoc caeteri etiam Reges fideles & sancti fecere? Neque de Hiskia id simpliciter verum est, quod in omnibus Deum per Prophetam consuluerit. Non consuluit certe, cum thesauros suos Lega- tis Babyloniis ostentaret, gravi ἐπανορθώσει ob id exceptus à Propheta, ac supplicio gravissimo in filiis suis affectus Esa. 39, 5. 6. 7. Quia vero de Messia hic agi probatum est: neque dissitetur Grotius, cui nomina illa vult sensu augustiori multoque planiori convenire, quomodo explica- tio illa sibi constabit? num & Messias in omni- bus à Deo per Prophetas consilia poscere de- buit? Quanto ergo rectius affirmant Interpp. ma- jestatem horum nominum divinam: qua perter- ritos credit LXX. Interpp. Hieronymus, cum non auderent de puero hoc dicere, quod aperte Deus appellandus sit, & pro his sex nominibus posuerint Magni consilii angelus &c. Agnoscunt utique ipsimet etiam hostes Deitatis Christi Aria- ni & Photiniani, qui nihil non in ejusmodi augu- stis oraculis ausi sunt inficiari, aut in dubium vo- care, nomen Dei אל hic tributum esse Messiæ: uti de Arianis veteribus ex Athanasio, & aliis an- tiquitatis Promachis, nec non de Socino, Crellio, Volckelio, Schlichtingio, aliisque recentioribus passim è scriptis eorum constat. Observavit quidem Hieronymus nonnullos bina nomina hic conjunxisse è veteribus Interpp. sed non probat illam explicationem. Qui autem ita, uti Gro- tius, exposuerit, neminem adhuc observare li- cuit. Unde εὑρημα illud Novum ipsi autori tri- buendum, cum aliis plurimis. Non enim, in- quit Hieronymus, uti plerique putant, bina jun- genda sunt nomina, ut legamus, admirabilis Con- siliarius & rursum Deus fortis, sed admirabilis le- gendum est separatim, quod Hebraice dicitur פֶּלֶא, & consiliarius seorsim, qui lingua eorum appella- tur יֹעֵץ, & DEUS separatim, qui Hebraice di- citur אֵל &c. Quid? quod explicatio Grotia- na Ebræo verbo יֹעֵץ haudquaquam conveniat: id enim eum, qui consilium dat, & consulit ali- cui; non vero qui consilium alicujus petit, no- tare, & usu verbi יָעַץ in kal. perpetuo & exem- plorum inductione constat; neque de eo penes Ebræos dubium est. Quomodo autem Consilia- rius Dei fuit Ezechias, quum neget Deus, se ullum habere à consiliis Esa. 40, 13. Rom. 11, 34. Unde manifestissimum est, consiliarium dici hic non respectu Dei, sed respectu hominum. Quod nomen quomodo Messiæ proprium sit, recte do- cet Brentius noster. Est & hoc Epitbeton anti- thesis erga mundanos principes. Hi enim non pos- sunt omnibus populis suis dare consilia in negotiis eo- rum, sed necessaria est eis opera Consiliariorum.. Habent multos Consultores, qui juvant ipsos in ad- ministratione regni: Et tamen nec principes, nec consiliarii eorum possunt ea dare consilia populis, quibus veram consequantur felicitatem. Messias autem ipse consiliarius est, non indiget aliorum con- silio, sed solus ipse sufficit dandis Consiliis, idque ad consequenda cœlestia bona.

Porro nomen אל evidentissime convincit, non posse Oraculum de Ezechia, vel ullo mero homine intelligi. Hoc enim nomen uni soli Deo proprium est, nec ulli creaturæ convenit, quemadmodum ex inductione locorum omnium demonstravimus, cum de nominibus divinis E- bræis egimus Tom. II. super August. Confess. Ad- scribo tantum Brentianam collationem: Tertius titulus est Deus. Mundani Principes sunt tantum homines. Messias autem non est tantum homo, sed etiam Deus omnipotens, quæ est summa omnium majestas.

Quartus titulus Fortis seu Heros aut Gigas. Mundani principes, etsi nonnunquam sunt ex- cellenti fortitudine præditi, tamen aut non sunt spirituales Heroes, qui audeant & possint Mo- nomachiam cum adversario suscipere, qualis

Heros fuit David adversus Goliathen, aut si sunt corporales Heroes, non tamen sunt spirituales Heroes, qui audeant & possint monomachiam cum morte suscipere, & victoriam reportare. Solus Messias est Heros ille, qui singulare certa- men iniit cum Morte & Inferno, ac etiam re- portavit victoriam, qua non solum ipse fruitur, verum etiam quotquot in ipsum credunt.

PATER FUTURI SECULI] In Ebræo non est fu- turi. Pater seculi est, qui multos post se relicturus sit po- steros, & in longum tempus.

Etfi in Ebræo non habeatur FUTURI, notatur tamen voce Ebræa עד æternitas. Ideo- que Pater æternus vel æternitatis dicitur, ac pro- inde etiam in futurum seculum se extendit hæc Pa- ternitas. Manifestum itaque est, non posse hoc Hiskiæ aptari. Quomodo enim illius paterni- tas porrigit sese in æternum? Et inaudita est Glossa, Patrem seculi esse, qui multos post se re- licturus sit posteros, & in longum tempus. No- men עד æternitatem, non longum tempus nota- re certum est. Tum vero longe aliud est Pa- trem esse seculi, quam posteros relinquere in longum tempus. Denique hoc Ezechiæ proprium non est, sibi cum multis commune, imo innumeris aliis magis, quam ipsi convenit. Ebræi ipsi a- gnoverunt, nomen Ebræum אבי עד soli DEO proprium esse: ideoque de Deo Patre intellexe- re. Sed quia nominatur eodem aperte Filius, manifestum est, paternitatem intelligendam es- se, non qualis est κατ' ἔσω intra complexum Deitatis, respectu filii unigeniti, quæ propria est primæ personæ divinæ; sed quæ est κατ' ἔξω re- spectu nostri. Brentius de hoc ita habet: Quin- tus (titulus) est PATER ÆTERNUS. Alii principes vocantur Patres Patriæ, quod vel de- fendant Patriam ab hostili incursione, vel impor- tent tempore famis magnam vim frumenti. Quæ beneficia, etsi grato animo agnoscenda sunt, ta- men non sunt perpetua: & Principes facile mutan- tur. Christus autem non vocatur Pater Pa- triæ: sed, quod longe majus est, Pater ÆTER- NUS. Primum igitur vocatur PATER, non persona sua in divina natura: sic enim Filius est, non Pater, sed vocatur Pater affectu. Semper enim habet paternum affectum erga suum populum, & in æternum non mutat hunc affectum, Esa. 49. Deinde dicitur etiam Pater æternus, quod servet populum suum non solum in hac vita, verum et- iam in futura & perpetua vita. Alii prin- cipes possunt populum suum in hac tantum vita, idque corporalibus duntaxat beneficiis, & pau- co admodum tempore servare, Christus autem est Pater æternus, servat in media morte, & resu- scitat ad vitam æternam. Similiter B. Lutherus in h. l. Æternus Pater. Hoc nomen non significat personam, sed opus personæ. Ut sit æternus Pater, qui semper generat, semper regnum & Ecclesiam suam auget; semper manet Pater, non est neque fiet aliquando judex, sed est in eo paternus affe- ctus sine fine. Sana autem non sunt, quæ hic ha- bet Zvvinglius. Patrem autem æternum vocari Filium non est durum piis auribus, qui didicerunt, personas quoque pro essentia per allæosin poni. Nam revera Filius non est Pater, sed id, quod Pater est. Sic ubique suam allæosin, larvam Diaboli B. Luthero dictam, ingerit Zvvinglius. At nuspiam essentiam & personas confundit Scriptura. Filius non dicitur Pater, quod sit id, quod Pater est; sed quod sit respectu nostri Pater: non ergo directe divina essentia eo nomine infertur: sed qua affectus ille Paternus adversus nos, & opus ex- ternum regenerationis non nisi divinæ naturæ con- venit. Ut plenius hoc nomen אבי־עד explicetur, operæ pretium erit repetere, quæ alibi de eo dixi- mus. Accipi autem id potest vel neutraliter, & ἁπλῶς, ut ὁ λόγος καθ’ ἑυτὸ per se consideratur, in quantum ipse æternus est: quomodo Chaldæus vi- detur intellexisse, qui reddidit גברא קים לעלמא vir permanens in æternum. Sic Ebr. עַד & עָלְמוֹא Targ. explicare licebit de absoluta æternitate, quæ est à parte ante & post, tametsi nec hoc, nec illud (quod adhuc ἐμφατικώτερον) omnimodam æterni- tatem inferat per se, & formaliter. Sed uti vi mate- riæ vere eandem importat Esa. 57. v. 15. Sic & h. l. quum hic אבי עד dicatur, qui est אל גבור, quem omnino æternum esse constat: utrumque etiam ita conjungitur 1. Joh. 5, 20. vel active & σχετικῶς ὁ λό- γος est Pater æternitatis, hoc est, autor & origo, quomodo constat, voce Patris interdum denotari primum autorem & originem; vid. Genes. 4, 20. Joh. 8. 44. Huc videntur respexisse LXX. interpretan- tes id πατὴρ ᾃ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος, Pater futuri se- culi, id est, vitæ æternæ. Hæc enim ejus est περίφρα- σις, Ebr. 6, 5. Et Vatablus, qui convertit, autor vitæ. Sed plura absque dubio involvuntur hoc nomine, quæ secundum Scripturas ita evolvimus. Quod sci- licet hoc titulo Christo tribuatur (1) Seculorum fun- datio. Nam per eum facta esse secula, docet Apo- stolus Ebr. 1, 2. Sicuti omnia per eum facta dicun- tur, quæ quidem facta sunt, Joh. 1, 2. (2) Æterni- tatis præparatio, quia in ipso præparata est ante ja- cta mundi fundamenta electis æterna gloria & glo- riosa æternitas, Eph. 1, 4. Col. 1, 5. (3) Vitæ æternæ ac- quisitio, quia ipse est autor vitæ, Act. 3, 15. deditque mundo vitam æternam meritorie & ratione acqui- sitionis, Joh. 6, 33. quando carnem suam, panem vitæ, dedit pro mundi vita, ibid. v. 51. (4) Æterna redem- tio, quam Christus invenisse dicitur Ebr. 9, 12. vere æterna: idque tum intensive immensitate vigoris, cui nihil ad summam efficaciæ perfectionem desit; tum extensive immensitate durationis, quod non sit temporaria saltim, ut erant δικαιώματα typica Vet. Testam. sed perpetua, quæ à principio mundi ad finem usque sese extendit: unde Jesus Christus di- citur χθὲς καὶ σήμερον ὁ αὐτὸς, καὶ εἰς τὸς αἰῶνας, Ebr. 13, 8. ut nemo mortalium à peccato & morte re- demtus sit vel redimatur adhuc, vel imposterum unquam redimi queat, nisi per hanc Jesu Christi re- demtionem. Conf. Act. 15, 11. & cap. 4, 12. Quodque non sit momentanea, ut sunt λυτρώσεις hujus vitæ fugaces & transitoriæ, sed æterna, infinitis seculorum myriadibus in altera vita perpetuanda & consum- manda. (5) Ecclesiæ Novi Test. gubernatio. Nam subjecit Deus Christo τὴν οἰκυμένην τὴν μέλλεσαν mundum illum futurum, Ebr. 2, 5. hoc est felix illud seculum, quod futurum prædixerant Prophetæ priore Christi adventu inchoatum, cujus comple- mentum futurum adhuc expectamus, cujus Pater est Christus, 1. Cor. 15, 15. Vocat autem Ecclesiam Novi Test. μέλλεσαν, non sui, sed Patrum respectu: quo pacto etiam μέλλοντα dicit ea bona, quæ sub Vet. Testamento quoad αἀντίτυπον & εἰκόνα non- dum fuerunt, sed tantum quoad τύπον & σκιὰν Ebr. 10. v. 1. quorum λειτυργὸς est Christus, Ebr. 9. v. 11. (6) Ad vitam æternam regeneratio; quia in Chri- sto Jesu regeneramur per Evangelium ad vitam æternam, 1. Cor. 4, 25. & per fidem in ipsum sumus filii Dei, Joh. 1, 12. Gal. 3, 26. & hæredes vitæ æternæ, Rom. 8, 16. (7) Æternæ vitæ donatio; quia dat credentibus vitam æternam, Joh. 3, 36. cap. 5. v. 24. cap. 6. v. 46. cap. 10. v. 28. carnem suam vivificam dat manducandam & sanguinem bibendum, Joh.

6, 54. concedit Evangelium, quod est verbum vitæ æternæ, cap. 6, 68. adde cap. 5, 39. Act. 5, 20. Phil. 2, 16. & largitur Spiritum Sanctum, qui est vita spiri- tus, ut in hac quoque vita habeamus æternam vi- tam, sed quoad πρόγευσιν, vel προποτισμόν per fidem & inchoative, Rom. 8, 24. 2. Cor. 5, 7. quam consequemur à Christo, quoad plenariam fruitio- nem, per speciem & consummative in regeneratio- ne, vel ut Syrus vertit חדתא בעלמא in seculo no- vo aut venturo, Matth. 19, 18. cap. 25, 46. Luc. 22, 29. Iob. 6, 40. 2. Tim. 4, 8. Apoc. 2, 10. Sic ergo Christus est אבי עד tum ratione divinæ naturæ (1) ὀυσιωδῶς κῃ κυρίως, essentialiter & principaliter, quippe qui est ipsa vita Joh. 11, 25. cap. 14, 6. ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς κῃ ζωὴ αἰώνιος, 1. Joh. 5, 20. (2) ἐνεργητικῶς καὶ δευτέρως, efficienter & minus principaliter, in quan- tum est autor æternitatis & seculorum, Ebr. 1, 2. Ioh. 1, 3. tum ratione humanæ naturæ ὑποστατικῶς καὶ ὀργανικῶς personaliter & instrumentaliter, quia caro humana evecta in ὑπόστασιν Filii Dei ἐνυπό- στατον & ἐνεργητικὸν ὄργανον τῆς θεότητος ἐχρημά- τησε subsistens & efficax instrumentum evasit, per quod vitam æternam reparavit λόγος, nobis- que impertit eandem Joh. 6, 33. 51. 54. tum ratione utriusque; partim ἱλασικῶς & quoad meritum, quia vitam æternam nobis promeruit ὁ ἀρχηγὸς τῆς ζωῆς καὶ σωτηρίας, Act. 3, 15. Ebr. 2, 10. 2. Tim. 1, 10. partim κοινωνικῶς, & quoad donum, quia dat vi- tam æternam his, qui credunt in ipsum Johan. 3, 16. partim δεσποτικῶς, & quoad dominium, quod ipse obtinet, ut Dominus futuri orbis & seculi, Ebr. 2, 5. cap. 6, 5. hoc est, perfectioris Ecclesiæ status, qui quidem in præsenti instaurari incipit, in futuro au- tem seculo consummabitur.

PRINCEPS PACIS] Princeps pacificus & in pace victurus.

Perquam jejuna interpretatio; Neque appa- ret, quomodo illa propria sit Hiskiæ. Non statim elogium illud augustum שׂר שׁלום princeps pacis ille meretur, qui in pace vivit pacisque studiosus est. Non autem dubium est, quin proprium id pe- culiari ratione Christo: qui uti princeps vitæ dici- tur, quia autor vitæ est Act. 3, 15. ita pacis princeps vocatur, quod pacis, quam cum Deo habemus & inter nos, mutuo autor ipse sit. Unde etiam pax nostra in abstracto vocatur Ephes. 2. Alii principes, inquit Brentius, solent plerumque esse autores bello- rum & multarum calamitatum. Et ut maxime inve- nias principem mundanum studiosum pacis, tamen non potest efficere, ut privati quique homines inter se pa- cem conservent, etiamsi nullum fuerit publicum bel- lum. Christus autem vere est princeps pacis, ac me- rito nominatur Friedenrichus, quod Latine significat divitem & plenum pace. Primum, quod pacificat Deum & homines. Maximum enim dissidium fuit inter Deum & homines: quia cum sit peccator, non potuit ei cum Deo convenire. Christus autem recon- ciliavit eos, ut homines justificati ex fide pacem ha- beant. Deinde Christus etiam autor est mutuæ pacis inter eos, qui credunt in ipsum. Nam qui credit in Christum, servat pacem, quantum in ipso est, cum o- mnibus hominibus. Fieri quidem non potest, ut pius semper externa tranquillitate in hoc seculo fruatur. Quemadmodum autem conjux non difficulter fert ex- tranea dissidia, si modo habeat cum suo conjuge dome- sticam pacem; ita qui habet pacem conscientiæ coram Deo, haud difficulter fert adversa, quæ ipsi extrinsecus accidunt. Ebræi nomine שׁלום felicitatem o- mnem designare solent. Sic ergo Princeps pacis eti am ideo dicitur, quod sit omnis felicitatis, quæ no- bis obtingit, autor, tum temporalis, tum sempiter- næ. Extra ipsum enim nulla est salus, Act. 4. 12.

## 9:7
Verse 7. HIS GOVERNMENT SHALL BE MULTIPLIED That is, it will last for 29 years. In this word, which signifies multiplication, there is a closed ם in the middle of the word; the Hebrews intend by this that stability is signified, just as by the open מ at the end, a rupture is signified, Nehemiah 2:13. It is not incredible that what one scribe in haste committed, others superstitiously imitated. These things are altogether wrongly restricted to the short time of Hezekiah's reign. Who will bear such a magnificent promise being understood so thinly! Others therefore more correctly acknowledge that the multiplication of the empire, both as to amplitude and as to duration, is attributed to this Augustus. For if there is no end to the peace of this empire, it is necessary that the duration of the empire be without end. How great an amplitude of empire is designated by this multiplication of the same, the Psalmist taught in Psalm 72: he shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and all the kings of the earth shall worship him. Whence some accept the square Mem in this way, because Christ's empire is to be dilated through the four corners of the world. Although others say that by the closed Mem the perpetual virginity of the mother of Christ is denoted, just as the same is signified by the closed gate, Ezekiel 44:2; others, the servitude of the people, who were to be oppressed until the coming of the Messiah; others, the exclusion of this nation from the society of that kingdom, which it deserved by its perfidy. For the error of the scribes, which B. Bohlius establishes here, is not to be rashly conceded, nor is any apex in the Scriptures in vain. But there is no reason why we should rely on these; since that multiplication of the Messianic empire is everywhere set forth in the most express words in the Scriptures: 2 Samuel 7, Psalm 2, Psalm 99, 110, Daniel 7, Zechariah 9.

Verse of the same.

AND OF HIS PEACE THERE SHALL BE NO END] He will enjoy peace to the end of his days, 2 Kings 20:19. This is an open depravation. For Isaiah teaches that there will be no end at all to that peace and empire. Grotius places the end with the term of Hezekiah's days. And how does this gloss respond to such a magnificent promise of God? What the genuine sense of the words of this prophecy is, beyond the literal meaning which radiates with its own light, the Angel Gabriel taught concerning eternal peace in the kingdom of Christ in Luke 1:32, who openly explained it concerning an everlasting empire, of which there will never be any end. For that this oracle is explained there, Grotius confessed in his annotations to Matthew 22:42. The Lord God, he says, will give unto him the throne of his father David (just as it was predicted in Isaiah 9:6: upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom he shall sit), and he shall reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. What? That here it is again most clearly said by the Prophet that his empire and happiness, and the peace of the empire, will be without end. Because the kingdom is to be established and corroborated UNTO ETERNITY. Indeed, the very confirmation in judgment and justice is so constituted that it brings eternity with it: for this justice is eternal, Daniel 9:24. Why many words? Since Grotius admits that these things are to be understood of Christ, whose dominion and the happiness of whose kingdom, and peace and confirmation in judgment and justice has no end, this certainly cannot be narrowed to 29 years. For in whatever passage it is a question of spiritual and eternal peace and happiness, of a kingdom not earthly and worldly, but heavenly and divine, of judgment and justice, not of this age, but pertaining to the administration of a spiritual kingdom, it is very poorly accepted according to the literal sense concerning temporal peace and happiness, concerning an earthly and worldly kingdom, concerning the judgment and justice of this age.

UPON THE THRONE OF DAVID, AND UPON HIS KINGDOM HE SHALL SIT] The interpreter has well supplied here that 'he shall sit,' which is understood in the Hebrew and Greek.

TO ESTABLISH IT AND TO CORROBORATE IT

IN JUDGMENT AND JUSTICE] Here judgment signifies the administration of law, justice signifies beneficence: through which empires flourish and thrive. Thus again these things are restricted to Hezekiah. But the kingdom of no earthly King, not even of Hezekiah himself, is so established and corroborated that it lasts forever: and that it brings eternal peace and happiness. Those words which are used here import an immovable stability and firmness, such as is given in no earthly kingdom. Nor is any kingdom so prepared, adapted, established, and corroborated that it runs at least from the beginning to the end in judgment and justice, and never deflects from it. It is known, however, that these voices are accustomed to be used concerning the kingdom of Christ in a far different sense: which therefore they demand here, where Grotius does not deny that the discourse is about Christ. For that judgment is designated which is exercised against the impious and Satan, the author of all impiety, and by which the pious are defended and guarded: but justice is proper to the kingdom of Christ, by which the faithful are adorned, so that they may stand eternally before the tribunal of God himself. The kingdom of Christ, says Brentius here, is far distant from worldly kingdoms, and therefore judgment is one thing, and justice is another in the kingdom of Christ than in worldly kingdoms. For judgment in worldly kingdoms is when innocent and honest men are defended from robbers, and when robbers are punished. And justice is when things taken away are restored to honest and innocent men, and they enjoy honors. But in the kingdom of Christ, judgment is when Satan and death are oppressed, and the pious are defended and saved, so that they are not absorbed by death and Satan. But justice is when believers are accounted just on account of Christ, and are adopted as sons of God, so that they may receive the heavenly inheritance. Whence John 16, Christ says: When the Paraclete has come, he will convict the world of sin, of justice, and of judgment. Of sin, because they do not believe in me. Of justice, because I go to the Father. Of judgment, because the prince of this world has already been judged. Wherefore Christ is said to perform judgment and justice in his kingdom, not because he administers an external polity and saves the pious with external aids, just as Monarchs defend their people. But because he saves the pious in death, and gives them eternal life, and he exercises this kingdom perpetually, because he always protects the pious who believe in him, whom he will also raise from the dead, so that with death abolished they may have life, justice, and everlasting happiness. Wherefore when the Prophet says that Christ will reign perpetually, he not only signifies that He will rise again from death, but also that He will preserve all the pious, so that they do not perish in death, but are awakened to eternal life. B. Luther places emphasis on the word לְהָכִין: Translate, he says at this place, 'to prepare,' but it signifies that Christ now reigns in this world through faith and is preparing us. We shall, however, be perfected on the last day. He prepares, moreover, in judgment, that is, by condemning and destroying the impious, and saving the pious. Likewise, in justice, because mercy awakens justice, by which we shall be freed from sin, death, and hell, etc.

FROM THIS TIME FORTH AND FOR EVERMORE] From the beginning to the end of life: for thus עולם is often taken, as in Ps. 89:2, 119:93. But in Christ both these and the preceding words have a meaning that is as much clearer as it is more august. He acknowledges that these and the preceding words have a much clearer meaning in Christ: he ought also to have acknowledged that this is the proper and genuine meaning. Certainly those words עַד עוֹלָם cannot be explained as referring to a short time up to the end of life. For although the word עולם when placed by itself sometimes designates not eternity, but the days of a life or of some thing; when joined together, those words עד עולם always imply eternity. Nor is it to be explained otherwise here, as we have already shown from the context and the angelic explanation in Luke 1.

THE ZEAL OF THE LORD OF HOSTS WILL DO THIS] That is, the burning love of God toward the pious, who are within the people, will give us and preserve for us so good a prince.

He returns again to his Hezekiah, who indeed had already been given at that time, and he does not interpret these things concerning the Messiah, concerning whom, however, they ought to have been explained according to a more august and plain sense. Nor indeed are these things to be referred only to this prediction, but they also exhibit the conclusion of that whole Isaianic discourse, as the interpreters have rightly observed. Because this was instituted chiefly concerning Christ, the Zeal of the Lord is best understood as love toward the human race, which God wished to be vindicated, out of immense love, from the seduction and tyranny of the Devil, so that He might again join to Himself the bride, snatched away by the craftiness of Satan, and assert His kingdom again. Whence Cyril on this passage: The apostate Dragon held the world as booty, and subjected man, made in the image of God, to his own scepters. It was therefore worthy of all zeal, and full of all tyranny, what was done to us. The zeal of the Lord of Sabaoth therefore liberated all the inhabitants of the earth. Rightly our Brentius: This is the conclusion of this discourse, which is described from the beginning of the seventh chapter. Wherefore, that we may rightly understand the conclusion, the state of this discourse must be repeated. The King and the remaining Princes of the family of David were fearing vehemently that their lineage might be cast out from the kingdom of Judah. For the enemies, the King of Israel and the King of Syria, were threatening that they would utterly destroy the family of David and install another King in Judah. And they were most powerful Kings. Wherefore the Princes of the kingdom of Judah were despairing of the safety of their family. But the Prophet rebukes their pusillanimity and consoles them with promises concerning Christ. For it cannot be that, when Christ is promised from the family of David, and is to sit on the throne of David, in the city of Jerusalem, and has not yet come, the enemies can destroy the family of David so that it does not rule in the kingdom of Judah. For it will absolutely come to pass that Christ will come and receive the throne and kingdom of David. The zeal of God will do that: it is not human merit, it is not human power, but it is the zeal of God. For first, God embraces the family of David with such love that He can in no way bear that those enemies should destroy it, but He will protect it in the kingdom of Judah because of the promise made to David. Then, God will fulfill the truth of His promise concerning Christ with such zeal that He would sooner bear the destruction of heaven and earth than of His word. Since, therefore, God burns with such zeal to perfect His promise concerning Christ, and Christ has not yet come in the flesh, you must not fear that those enemies, who threaten your family with slaughter, will become masters of their desire. This is the consolation concerning the preservation of the external kingdom in the posterity of David. For although afterwards Jerusalem was devastated by the king of Babylon, yet the royal family of David always remained, and was in certain expectation of the restoration of Jerusalem and the recovery of the principality, just as the Prophets Jeremiah and Ezekiel, stirred by the divine Spirit, were preaching. Wherefore, since the word of God promised that it would shortly come to pass that the princes of the family of David would be restored to the dominion of the throne of David, it must be understood that, although the family of David was for some years cast out from the principality before men, it always remained in the principality before God, until the promised seed should come, which was the expectation and justification of the nations, according to the prophecy

of the Patriarch Jacob. Then this discourse of Isaiah was also a consolation for the pious concerning the preservation of the spiritual kingdom in Christ. For just as the enemies were threatening that they would destroy the family of David, so that it might no longer reign in Judah: so Satan was threatening the pious in that kingdom that he would bring it about that Christ would not be sent, and he was also soliciting them to think that the promises concerning Christ were most vain trifles, and therefore that it was all over with their salvation. Wherefore Isaiah instituted a discourse concerning Christ and His kingdom, so that the pious might be certified of the advent of Christ, and might confirm their faith concerning their heavenly salvation, which we have in Christ. We add in the last place the confession of Grotius himself, that the throne of David promised in this place was the Messiah's, in his Annotations on Luke 24:47.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MULTIPLICABITUR EJUS IMPERIUM] Id est, durabit per annos 29. In verbo hoc, quod multi- plicationem significat, est ם claufum in media dictio- ne, eo stabilitatem significari volunt Hebræi, ut per מ apertum in fine rupturam, Nehem. 2, 13. Non incredibi- le est, quod unus scriba properans commiserat, id alios superstitiose imitatos. Perperam omnino hæc restringuntur ad exi- guum regiminis Hiskiani tempus. Quis feret, tam magnificam promissionem tam tenuiter intelligi! Rectius ergo alii multiplicationem imperii, & quo- ad amplitudinem & quoad durationem Augusto huic tribui agnoscunt. Nam si pacis imperii hu- jus nullus finis, duratio imperii fine careat neces- sum est. Quanta autem amplitudo imperii per hanc multiplicationem ejusdem designetur, Hie- ropsaltes docuit Psal. 72. dominabitur à mari usq; ad mare, & adorabunt eum omnes reges terræ. Un- de Mem quadratum ita accipiunt nonnulli, quod per quatuor plagas mundi dilatandum sit Christi imperium. Quamvis per Mem claufum alii vir- ginitatem perpetuam matris Christi denotatam di- cant, sicut eadem significata per portam claufam, Ezech. 44, 2. alii populi servitutem, qui premen- dus usque ad adventum Messiæ: alii exclusionem gentis hujus à regni istius societate, quam perfidia sua meruit. Non enim temere concedendus li- brariorum error, quem hic statuit B. Bohlius, ne- que frustra ullus est apex in Scripturis. Sed his non est; quod nitamur; siquidem multiplicatio illa imperii Messiani passim expressissimis verbis in scripturis exposita sit 2. Sam. 7. Psal. 2. Ps. 99. 110. Dan. 7. Zach. 9.

Vers. eod.

ET PACIS EJUS NON ERIT FINIS ] Ad fi- nem dierum suorum pace fruetur, 2. Reg. 20, 19. Aperta hæc est depravatio. Nam Esaias nul- lum plane finem fore pacis & imperii istius docet. Grotius finem ponit cum termino dierum Hiskiæ. Et quomodo hæc glossa tam magnificæ promissio- ni Dei respondet? Quis genuinus sensus verborum hujus vaticinii sit præter τὸ ῥητὸν, quod sua luce radiat, de æterna pace in regno Christi Angelus Gabriel docuit Luc. 1. v. 32. qui id de imperio sempiterno, cujus finis nullus unquam futurus est, aperte exposuit. Nam quod ibi hoc oraculum exponatur, confessus est Grotius annotatis ad Matth. 22, 42. Dabit, inquit, Angelus, illi Dominus Deus sedem Davidis Patris ejus, (quemadmodum Esa. 9. v. 6. prædictum: super solium David, & super regnum ejus sedebit,) & regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, & regni ejus non erit finis. Quid? quod hic à Propheta denuo luculentissime id di- catur, quod imperium ejus & felicitas, ac pax im- perii fine caritura sint. Quia regnum confirman- dum & corroborandum USQUE IN SEMPITER- NUM. Imo ipsa confirmatio in judicio & justitia ita comparata sit, ut æternitatem secum inferat: nam hæc justitia æterna est, Dan. 9. v. 24. Quid multis? de Christo hæc intelligenda esse, quum ad- mittat Grotius, cujus dominatio & regni felicitas, & pax & confirmatio in judicio & justitia nullum finem habet, non potest utique hoc ad 29. annos arctari. Quo enim loco agitur de pace ac felici- tate spirituali & æterna, de regno non terreno & mundano, sed cælesti ac divino, de judicio & justi- tia, non hujus seculi, sed ad regni spiritualis admi- nistrationem pertinente, is pessime secundum sen- sum literalem accipitur de pace ac felicitate tem- porali, de regno terreno ac mundano, de judicio & justitia hujus seculi.

SUPER SOLIUM DAVID, ET SUPER RE- GNVM EJVS SEDEBIT] Supplevit bene hic interpres illud sedebit, quod in Hebræo & Græco subintelligitur.

VT CONFIRMET ILLVD ET CORROBORET

IN JVDICIO ET JVSTITIAl Hic judicium juris ad- ministrationem, justitia beneficentiam significat: per quam florent vigentque imperia. Sic iterum restringuntur hæc ad Hiskiam. At nullius terreni Regis, nec ipsius Hiskiæ regnum ita confirmatur & corroboratur, ut in sempiter- num duret: utque pacem ac felicitatem æternam inferat. Verba illa, quæ hic adhibentur, immo- tam stabilitatem & firmitatem important, qualis in nullo terreno regno datur. Neq; regnum ullum sic præparatur, aptatur, firmatur & corroboratur, ut saltem ab initio ad finem usque decurrat in judi- cio & justitia, nec unquam ab ea deflectat. Notum autem est, quod de Christi regno adhiberi hæ vo- ces soleant longe alio sensu: quem proinde hic, ubi de Christo sermonem esse non diffitetur Gro- tius, postulant. Nam judicium illud designatur, quod adversus impios & autorem omnis impieta- tis Satanam exercetur, & quo pii defenduntur ac custodiuntur: Justitia vero regno Christi propria est, qua fideles ornantur, ut æternum coram ipsius Dei tribunali consistant. Regnum Christi, inquit hic Brentius, longe distat à regnis mundanis, ideoque aliud est judicium, alia est justitia in regno Christi, quam in regnis mundanis. Nam judicium in re- gnis mundanis est, cum innocentes & honesti ho- mines defenduntur à latronibus, & cum latrones puniuntur. Et justitia est, cum honestis & inno- centibus hominibus ablata restituuntur, & hono- ribus fruuntur. In regno autem Christi judicium est, cum Satan & mors opprimuntur, & pii defen- duntur ac servantur, ne à morte & Satana absor- beantur. Justitia autem est, cum credentes repu- tantur justi propter Christum, & adoptantur in fi- lios Dei, ut accipiant cælestem hæreditatem. Un- de Joh. 16. Christus ait: Cum venerit Paracletus, arguet mundum de peccato, de justitia & judicio. De peccato, quia non credunt in me. De justitia, quia ad Patrem vado. De judicio, quia princeps bu- jus mundi jam judicatus est. Quare Christus di- citur in suo regno facere judicium & justitiam, non quod administret externam politeian, & ser- vet pios externis auxiliis, quemadmodum Monar- chæ suum populum defendunt. Sed quod servet pios in morte, & det eis æternam vitam, & hoc regnum exercet perpetuo, quia semper tuetur pios credentes in ipsum, quos etiam excitabit à mortuis, ut abolita morte habeant vitam, justitiam & felicitatem sempiternam. Quare quum Pro- pheta dicit, Christum regnaturum perpetuo, non solum significat ipsum à morte resurrecturum, sed etiam ipsum conservaturum omnes pios, ne in morte pereant, sed ad æternam vitam excitentur. B. Lutherus in voce לְהָכִין emphasin ponit: Verte, inquit ad hunc locum, ut præparet, significat au- tem Christum nunc regnare in hoc mundo per fidem & præparare nos. Erimus autem absoluti in novissimo die. Præparat autem in judicio, hoc est, damnan- do & perdendo impios, ac servando pios. Item, in justitia, quod misericordia suscitat justitiam, qua li- berabimur à peccato, morte & inferno, &c.

A MODO ET VSQVE IN SEMPITERNVM] Ab initio ad finem vitæ : ita enim sæpe sumitur עולם ut Ps. 89, 2. 119, 93. Sed in Christo & hæc & quæ præ- cedunt, habent significationem, multo ut augustiorem, ita & planiorem. Agnoscit planiorem multo sensum hæc & præ- cedentia habere in Christo: agnoscere etiam de- bebat, hunc sensum proprium & genuinum esse. Verba certe illa עַד עוֹלָם non possunt de exiguo tempore usque ad finem vitæ explicari. Nam licet vox עולם seorsim posita quandoque non æternita- tem, sed dies vitæ aut rei alicujus designet; conjun- ctæ tamen illæ voces עד עולם æternitatem sem- per inferunt. Neque aliter hic explicandum esse, jam è contextu & explicatione Angelica Luc. 1. o- stendimus.

ZELUS DOMINI EXERCITUUM FACIET HOC] Id est, ardens amor Dei erga pios, qui insunt populo, dabit nobis ac servabit tam bonum principem.

Redit iterum ad Hiskiam suum, qui vero jam tum datus erat, neque de Messia hæc interpretatur, de quo tamen juxta sensum augustiorem & planio- rem explicanda erant. Nec vero tantum hæc refe- renda ad hanc prædictionem, sed & conclusionem exhibent totius concionis istius Esaianæ, uti recte observarunt Interpp. Quæ quia de Christo præ- cipue instituta est, Zelus Domini de amore adversus genus humanum, quod vindicatum voluerit Deus, ex immensa dilectione, à seductione ac tyrannide Diaboli, ut sibi iterum sponsam, Satanæ versutia abstractam, copularet, regnumque suum iterum adsereret, optime intelligitur. Unde Cyrillus adh. l. Draco Apostata orbem terrarum prædæ habuit, & suis sceptris hominem ad Dei imaginem factum sub- jecit. Erat igitur omni zelo dignum, & omni tyran- nide plenum, quod in nos factum est. Liberavit igi- tur zelus Domini Sabaoth omnes terræ incolas. Re- cte Brentius noster: Hæc est conclusio hujus con- cionis, quæ descripta est ab initio septimi capitis. Quare ut recte intelligamus conclusionem, repe- tendus erit status hujus concionis. Rex & reliqui Principes de familia Davidis vehementer metue- bant, ne genus eorum è regno Juda ejiceretur. Hostes enim, Rex Israël & Rex Syriæ, minabantur se familiam Davidis prorsum deleturos, & alium Regem in Juda instituturos. Et erant Reges po- tentissimi. Quare Principes regni Juda despera- bant de salute suæ familiæ. Sed Propheta repre- hendit pusillanimitatem ipsorum, & consolatur eos promissionibus de Christo. Fieri enim non potest, ut cum promissus sit Christus de familia David, & sessurus sit in throno Davidis, in urbe Hierusalem, ac nondum venerit, hostes queant fa- miliam Davidis delere, ut non dominetur in regno Juda. Omnino enim futurum est, ut Christus ve- niat, & accipiat thronum ac regnum Davidis. Ze- lus Dei faciet istud: non est humanum meritum, non est humana potentia, sed est zelus Dei. Pri- mum enim Deus tanto amore complectitur fami- liam Davidis, ut nullo modo ferre queat, quod hostes isti deleant eam, sed tuebitur ipsam in regno Juda propter promissionem Davidi dictam. Dein- de Deus tanto zelo adimplebit veritatem promis- sionis suæ de Christo, ut citius ferret interitum cœli & terræ, quam verbi sui. Cum igitur Deus tanto zelo ardeat ad perficiendam promissionem suam de Christo, & Christus nondum venerit in carnem, non est vobis metuendum, ne hostes isti, qui fami- liæ vestræ minantur internecionem, fiant voti sui compotes. Hæc est consolatio de conservatione externi regni in posteritate Davidis. Etsi enim postea Hierusalem devastata est per regem Baby- lonis, tamen semper mansit regia familia Davidis, & fuit in certa expectatione restaurandæ Hierusa- lem ac recuperandi principatus, quemadmodum Prophetæ Hieremias & Ezechiel excitati divino Spiritu concionabantur. Quare, cum verbum Dei polliceretur, brevi fore, ut principes de familia Davidis restituerentur dominationi throni Davi- dis, sentiendum est, quod etsi familia Davidis fuit aliquot annis è principatu coram hominibus abje- cta, semper tamen mansit in principatu coram Deo, donec veniret semen promissum, quod erat expectatio & justificatio gentium, juxta vaticinium

Patriarchae Jacob. Deinde haec concio Esaiae fuit etiam consolatio piorum de conservatione regni spiritualis in Christo. Sicut enim hostes mina- bantur se deleturos familiam Davidis, ne regnet amplius in Juda: Ita Satan minabatur piis in eo re- gno, se effecturum, ne mitteretur Christus, ac sol- licitabat etiam ipsos, ut existimarent promissiones de Christo esse vanissimas nugas, ideoque de salute ipsorum actum esse. Quare Esaias instituit con- cionem de Christo & regno ejus, ut pii certificen- tur de adventu Christi, & confirment fidem suam de coelesti salute sua, quam habemus in Christo. Addimus postremo loco ipsiusmet Grotii confes- sionem, quod solium Davidis Messiae hoc loco promissum fuerit, in Annotat. ad Luc. 24, 47.

## 9:8
Vers. 8. THE LORD SENT A WORD INTO JACOB] He often signified His threats through the law and the Prophets to all the descendants of Jacob. But the Greeks read דֶבֶר with other points, so that it signifies a plague. For they translate it θάνατον ἀπέστειλε κύριος. But θάνατος in their language is pestilence, as we showed on Matthew 24:7.

AND IT FELL UPON ISRAEL] But the ten tribes will feel the most full effect of those threats, not likewise Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VERBUM MISIT DOMINUS IN JACOB] Minas suas per legem & Prophetas saepe significavit omni- bus Jacobi posteris. At Graeci דֶבֶר legerunt punctis a- liis, ut pestem significet. Vertunt enim θάνατον ἀπέστει- λε κύριος. Est autem θάνατος illorum lingua pestilentia, ut ostendimus ad Matth. 24, 7.

ET CECIDIT IN ISRAEL] Sed decem tribus earum minarum plenissimum effectum sentient, non item Hierosolyma.

## 9:10
Vers. 10. THE BRICKS HAVE FALLEN, BUT WE WILL BUILD WITH HEWN STONE] That is, with marble. Those evils which the men of the ten tribes had suffered up to this point, they considered of little account, thinking that the losses could easily be repaired.

Latin:

Vers. 10. LATERES CECIDERUNT, SED QUA- DRIS AEDIFICABIMUS] Id est, ex marmore. Quae hactenus passi erant mala ista decem tribuum homines, ea parvi ducebant, rati facile damna posse resarciri.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. AND THE LORD WILL RAISE UP THE ENEMIES OF REZIN AGAINST HIM] The enemies of the king of Syria, by whose help they think themselves safe. Those enemies are Tiglath-Pileser with his allies, 2 Kings 16:7.

AND WILL TURN HIS ENEMIES INTO A TUMULT] He will gather them together. For that is what סכך is, which, besides this place, is found below in 19:2. He will summon enemies against the Israelites from every side. For 'his' here refers not to the neighbor, but to Ephraim.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET ELEVABIT DOMINUS HOSTES RA- SIN SUPER EUM] Hostes regis Syriae, cujus auxilio se tutos putant. Hostes illi sunt Theglathphalasar cum sociis suis, 2. Reg. 16, 7.

ET INIMICOS EJUS IN TUMULTUM VER- TET] Conglomerabit. Id enim est סכך, quod praeter hunc locum invenitur infra 19, 2. Ab omni parte inimi- cos Israelitis accerset. Nam ejus hic refertur non ad pro- ximum, sed ad Ephraim.

## 9:12
Vers. 12. SYRIA FROM THE EAST] For the Syrians, after the death of Rezin, had joined themselves to the Assyrians.

AND THE PHILISTINES FROM THE WEST] Who, being hostile to the Israelites from of old, seized every opportunity to harm them. And it is accustomed to happen thus: Δρυὸς πεσούσης πᾶς ἀνὴρ ξυλεύεται,

IN ALL THESE HIS ANGER IS NOT TURNED AWAY: BUT HIS HAND IS STRETCHED OUT STILL] God was not satisfied with so many evils of the Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SYRIAM AB ORIENTE] Nam Syri post mortem Rasinis adjunxerant se Assyriis.

ET PHILISTHIIM AB OCCIDENTE] Qui ab antiquo infesti Israelitis omnes occasiones eis nocendi ca- piebant. Et solet sic fieri: Δρυὸς πεσούσης πᾶς ἀνὴρ ξυλεύεται,

IN OMNIBUS HIS NON EST AVERSUS FU- ROR EJUS: SED ADHUC MANUS EJUS EXTEN- TA] Non est saturatus Deus tot Israelitarum malis.

## 9:13
AND THE PEOPLE HAVE NOT RETURNED TO HIM THAT SMITETH THEM, AND THEY HAVE NOT SOUGHT THE LORD OF HOSTS] And here 'et' is for 'nam' (for). For the cause is added, why God was not satisfied with their punishments, because they had neither acknowledged nor amended their fault.

Latin:

ET POPULUS NON EST REVERSUS AD PER- CUTIENTEM SE, ET DOMINUM EXERCITUUM NON INQUISIERUNT] Et hic est pro nam. Causa enim additur, cur Deus illorum poenis non fuerit satia- tus, quia culpam nec agnoverant, nec emendaverant.

## 9:14
Vers. 14. AND THE LORD WILL CUT OFF FROM ISRAEL HEAD AND TAIL] The highest and the lowest; the highest are the senators, the lowest are the soothsayers, as he will now explain.

THE BRANCH AND THE RUSH] In Hebrew it is: runcum & juncum, that is, the strong and the weak. But the interpreter looked to the verb כפף, which is to bend, and the other meaning of the noun אגמון, which the Greeks sometimes translate as κρίκον. See Job 40:21.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DISPERDET DOMINUS AB ISRAEL CAPUT ET CAUDAM] Summos & infimos, summi sunt senatores, infimi sunt arioli, ut jam explicabit.

INCURVANTEM ET REFRÆNANTEM] In Hebraeo est: runcum & juncum, id est, validos & invali- dos. Sed interpres respexit verbum כפף, quod est in- curvare, & significatum alterum nominis אגמון, quod κρίκον interdum vertunt Graeci. Vide Jobi 40, 21.

## 9:15
Vers. 15. THE ANCIENT] The senator.

Latin:

Vers. 15. LONGÆVUS] Senator.

## 9:16
Vers. 16. THEY THAT CALL BLESSED] They that praise.

AND THEY THAT ARE CALLED BLESSED] They that are praised.

Latin:

Vers. 16. QUI BEATIFICANT] Qui laudant.

ET QUI BEATIFICANTUR] Qui laudantur.

## 9:17
Vers. 17. SHALL HAVE NO JOY IN THEIR YOUNG MEN] Since youth is otherwise accustomed to be lovable.

SPEAKETH FOLLY] That is, a lie, as the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SUPER ADOLESCENTULIS EJUS NON LAETABITUR] Cum soleat alioqui juventus esse amabilis.

LOCUTUM EST STULTITIAM] Id est, men- dacium, ut hic Chaldaeus.

## 9:18
Vers. 18. FOR WICKEDNESS BURNETH AS THE FIRE] That is, wicked men.

AND IT SHALL BE KINDLED IN THE DENSITY OF THE FOREST] That is, of the wood.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SUCCENSA EST ENIM QUASI IGNIS IMPIETAS] Id est, impii homines.

ET SUCCENDETUR IN DENSITATE SAL- TUS] Id est, lignorum.

## 9:20
AND HE SHALL TURN TO THE RIGHT] He shall snatch. Kimchi. Driven by need, they shall live by snatching from every side, nor shall they be satisfied in the times of Sennacherib.

EVERY ONE SHALL EAT THE FLESH OF HIS OWN ARM] A figurative expression, meaning they shall consume the things of their kinsmen snatched by force.

MANASSEH EPHRAIM AND EPHRAIM MANASSEH]

NASSEM] Those discordant among themselves joined the enemies, others opposed them.

SIMUL IPSI CONTRA JUDAM] Namely, after Sennacherib had subdued the entire land of the ten tribes, 2 Kings 18:34, 35.

Latin:

ET DECLINABIT AD DEXTERAM] Rapiet. Kimchi. Prae victus egestate raptu undique vivent, nec saturabuntur temporibus Sennacheribi.

UNUSQUISQUE CARNEM BRACHII SUI VO- RABIT] Figurata locutio, pro res cognatorum vi raptas consument.

MANASSES EPHRAIM ET EPHRAIM MA- NASSEM]

NASSEM] Discordes inter se alii hostibus se aggrega- bunt, alii se opponent.

SIMUL IPSI CONTRA JUDAM] Nempe post- quam Sennacheribus omnem terram decem tribuum per- domuerit, 2. Reg. 18, 34. 35.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

The Prophet proclaims woe to those who pervert the law and to unjust judges, and prophesies that the Assyrian, the rod of the Lord, must also be humbled on account of the pride of his heart, and he consoles the Israelites so that they may not fear him, and predicts the conversion of the remnant of the people.

Vers. 1. WOE TO THOSE WHO ENACT UNJUST LAWS] Or rather, decrees or sentences.

ET SCRIBENTES INJUSTITIAM SCRIPSERUNT] More correctly thus: And to the Scribes who write unjust things. By Scribes he understands the legal experts, the assessors of the magistrates, whose duty it was to warn judges who were deviating from their duty.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Væ denunciato legem pervertentibus & inju- stis judicibus, Assyrium virgam Domini humiliandum etiam esse ob cordis sui su- perbiam vaticinatur Propheta, & Israëli- tas, ne ab eo timeant, consolatur, ac reli- quiarum populi conversionem prædicit.

Vers. 1. VÆ QUI CONDUNT LEGES INIQUAS] Imo decreta, sive sententias.

ET SCRIBENTES INJUSTITIAM SCRIPSE- RUNT] Rectius sic: Et Scribis qui injusta scribunt. Scri- bas intelligit jurisperitos, ædsessores magistratuum, quo- rum erat officium judices ob officio declinantes monere.

## 10:3
Vers. 3. IN THE DAY OF VISITATION AND CALAMITY COMING FROM AFAR] From as far as Assyria.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IN DIE VISITATIONIS ET CALAMI- TATIS DE LONGE VENIENTIS] Assyria ab usque.

## 10:4
NE INCURVEMINI SUB VINCULO, ET CUM INTERFECTIS CADATIS] You may translate it best: Unless one bows down among the bound, or casts himself among the slain, he will certainly not escape.

Latin:

NE INCURVEMINI SUB VINCULO, ET CUM INTERFECTIS CADATIS] Optime vertas: Nisi quis se incurvaverit inter vinctos, aut inter occisos se abjecerit, scili- cet non evadet.

## 10:5
Vers. 5. WOE TO ASSUR] That is, to the Assyrian, to Sennacherib and his army. They will not go unpunished who do not execute the decrees of God for God's sake, and who attribute the glory of their victories either to themselves or to idols.

IN MANU EORUM] That is, by them.

INDIGNATIO MEA] My severity, that is, the army.

Latin:

Vers. 5. VÆ ASSUR] Id est, Assyrio, Sennacheribo & exercitui ejus. Non impune ferent, qui decreta Dei non ob Deum exsequuntur, gloriamque victoriarum aut sibi aut Idolis attribuunt.

IN MANU EORUM] Id est, per eos.

INDIGNATIO MEA] Severitas mea, exercitus scilicet.

## 10:6
Vers. 6. CONTRA POPULUM FURORIS MEI] Against those who have deserved my wrath.

I WILL COMMAND HIM, THAT HE MAY TAKE AWAY THE SPOILS, AND PLUNDER THE PREY] Explanation of the name Mahershalalhashbaz.

AND MAY SET HIM] The people.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CONTRA POPULUM FURORIS MEI] Contra eos, qui iram meam sunt meriti.

MANDABO ILLI, UT AUFERAT SPOLIA, ET DIRIPIAT PRÆDAM ] Explicatio nominis Maharsa- lal hasbaz.

ET PONAT ILLUM] Populum.

## 10:9
Ver. 9. ARE NOT THE PRINCES TOGETHER KINGS] Do I not also have kings as instruments of servitude? Thus later the Romans.

IS IT NOT AS CHARCHEMISH] Carchemish on the Euphrates, 2 Chron. 35, 20.

SO CALNO] Better: as Calno: that is, Callinicum, of which we spoke in book 1 of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

AND AS ARPAD] As Aradus. See 2 Kings 18, 34.

SO HAMATH] More correctly: as Hamath: Amathus of Syria, 2 Kings 17, 24.

IS IT NOT AS DAMASCUS SO SAMARIA] Supply: is mine, by the same right as other cities.

Latin:

Vers. 9. NUMQUID NON PRINCIPES SIMUL RE- GES SUNT ] Nonne & reges habeo instrumenta ser- vitutis? Sic postea Romani.

NUMQUID NON UT CHARCOMIS] Cercu- sium ad Euphratem, 2. Paral. 35, 20

SIC CALANO] Melius: ut Calano: id est, Cal- linisum, de quo diximus ad librum 1. de Veritate Religio- nis Christianæ.

ET UT ARPHAD] Ut Aradus. Vide 2. Reg. 18, 34.

SIC EMATH] Rectius: ut Emath: Amathus Sy- riæ 2. Reg. 17, 24.

NUMQUID NON UT DAMASCUS SIC SA- MARIA] Supple, mea est, pari jure quo urbes aliæ.

## 10:10
Ver. 10. AS MY HAND HATH FOUND] That is, has acquired by war.

THE KINGDOMS OF THE IDOL] So many kingdoms of this or that petty god, not to be compared with the Sun, the god of the Assyrians.

SO ALSO THEIR IMAGES FROM JERUSALEM AND SAMARIA] You would translate more correctly: Whose images [are] above the possessions of Jerusalem and Samaria. For he holds the God of the Jerusalemites in the number of gods, as the deity of one people. See 2 Kings 18, 34, 35.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUOMODO INVENIT MANUS MEA] Id est, bello peperit.

REGNA IDOLI ] Tot regna hujus aut illius mi- nuti dei, non comparandi cum Sole deo Assyriorum.

SIC ET SIMULACRA EORUM DE JERUSA- LEM ET SAMARIA] Verteris rectius: Quorum simu- lachra præ(diis) Jerusalem & Samariæ. Nam Deum Hie- rosolymorum habet in numero deorum, ut populi unius numen. Vide 2. Reg. 18, 34. 35.

## 10:11
SO WILL I DO TO JERUSALEM AND HER IMAGES] In the Hebrew: To her terrors: that is, to her gods.

Latin:

SIC FACIAM JERUSALEM AC SIMULACRIS EJUS] In Hebræo: Terriculis ejus: id est, diis ejus.

## 10:12
Verse 12. WHEN THE LORD SHALL HAVE FINISHED ALL HIS WORKS ON MOUNT SION AND IN JERUSALEM] When he shall have punished that city with a tight siege, as much as he judges to be just.

I WILL VISIT UPON THE MAGNIFICENT FRUIT OF THE HEART OF THE KING OF ASSYRIA] I will take note of his insolent thoughts and words.

Latin:

Vers. 12. CUM IMPLEVERIT DOMINUS CUNCTA OPERA SUA IN MONTE SION ET IN JERUSA- LEM] Cum eam urbem arcta obsidione, quantum æ- quum judicat, castigaverit.

VISITABO SUPER FRUCTUM MAGNIFICUM CORDIS REGIS ASSUR] Animadvertam in cogitata ac verba ejus insolentia.

## 10:13
Verse 13. AS A MIGHTY ONE] Here the כ has a Patach, and the נ is without a point: which is a Syriac spelling, as appears in Jer. 25:36, Prov. 30:17, Eccles. 2:13, Zach. 12:5.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QUASI POTENS] Hic כ habet Patach, N vero sine puncto est: quæ scriptura Syriaca est, ut apparet Jer. 25, 36. Prov. 30,17. Eccles. 2, 13. Zach. 12, 5.

## 10:14
Verse 14. SO I HAVE GATHERED ALL THE EARTH] That is, I have added to my dominions.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SIC VNIVERSAM TERRAM EGO CON- GREGAVI] Id est, addidi ditionibus meis.

## 10:15
V. 15. AND THE ROD BE EXALTED, WHICH IS INDEED WOOD] And the rod (against him, who) is not a sign: that is, against a man, who can move himself by his own power: those things which we have added are repeated ἀπὸ κοινῆ from the preceding.

Latin:

V. 15. ET EXALTETUR BACULUS, QUI UTIQVE LIGNUM EST] Et baculus (contra eum, qui) non est signum: id est, contra hominem, qui se movere suapte vi potest: illa quæ addidimus, repetuntur ἀπὸ κοινῆ ex superiore.

## 10:16
Verse 16. THEREFORE SHALL THE LORD, THE LORD OF HOSTS, SEND IN HIS FAT ONES LEANNESS] Out of the greatest forces, very few will escape, 4 Kings 19:38, and below here 19.

AND UNDER HIS GLORY A BURNING SHALL BE KINDLED, AS THE BURNING OF A FIRE] A transposition for as a burning kindled, as a burning pyre. Glory, that is, the army. See the explanation above 9:5.

Latin:

Vers. 16. PROPTER HOC MITTET DOMINATOR DOMINUS EXERCITUUM IN PINGUIBUS EJUS TENUITATEM] Ex maximis copiis paucissimi evadent, 4. Reg. 19. 38. & infra hic 19.

ET SUBTUS GLORIAM EJUS SUCCENSA AR- DEBIT, QUASI COMBUSTIO IGNIS ] Transpositio pro quasi combustio succensa, quasi rogus ardens. Gloria, id est, exercitus. Explicationem vide supra 9,5.

## 10:17
Verse 17. AND THE LIGHT OF ISRAEL SHALL BE IN A FIRE] God shall be in the place of fire. AND HIS HOLY ONE IN A FLAME] He says the same thing twice. A BRIAR AND A THORN] Those who have pricked Israel. IN ONE DAY] That is, at one and the same time. For this happens at night. We have noted elsewhere that the word 'day' is taken in this way.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET ERIT LVMEN ISRAEL IN IGNE] Deus erit vice ignis. ET SANCTIS EJVS IN FLAMMA] Idem bis dicit. SPINA ET VEPRES] Qui Israelem pupugerunt. IN DIE UNA] Id est, uno eodemque tempore. Nam nocte hoc evenit. Sic vocem diei sumi, notavimus & alibi.

## 10:18
Verse 18. AND THE GLORY OF HIS FOREST AND OF HIS CARMEL] כרמל is not always a proper noun, but also signifies planted fields. He persists in the comparison of the fire: and he depicts the army under the name of a forest, whose soldiers are the trees of the forest, the tall planted trees.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET GLORIA SALTVs EJVS ET CAR- MELI EJVS] כרמל non semper nomen est proprium, sed significat & campos consitos. Perstat in comparatio- ne incendii: & exercitum sub silvæ nomine depingit, cu- jus milites sint arbores silvæ proceres arbores consitæ.

## 10:20
THE REMNANT OF ISRAEL SHALL NO MORE STAY UPON HIM THAT SMITETH THEM] Upon the Assyrians or Egyptians, who under the guise of treaties meditate the destruction of Israel.

Latin:

NON ADJICIET RESIDUUM ISRAEL, ET HI, QUI FUGERINT DE DOMO JACOB, INNI- TI SUPER EO, QUI PERCUTIT EOS] Super Assy- riis aut Ægyptiis, qui sub specie fœderum exitium Israeli meditantur.

## 10:21
Verse 21. THE REMNANT SHALL RETURN] An explanation of the name Shear-Jashub, which we had above 7:3. They shall return: that is, a few will return to the fields and smaller towns, who had immediately betaken themselves to Jerusalem upon the arrival of Sennacherib, 2 Kings 19:31, 2 Paral. 31:1.

Latin:

Vers. 21. RELIQUIÆ CONVERTENTUR] Expli- catio nominis Sear-Jasub, quod habuimus supra 7, 3. con- vertentur: id est, redibunt in agros & minora oppida pauci, qui statim adventante Sennacheribo Hierosolyma se receperant, 2. Reg. 19, 31. 2. Paral. 31, 1.

## 10:22
Verse 22. THE CONSUMMATION ABBREVIATED SHALL OVERFLOW WITH JUSTICE] The Greeks say λόγον συντελῶν, καὶ συντέμνων. Just as when accounts of receipts and expenses are calculated, the sum that remains is often small, so too at that time those who return will be few, but full of virtue.

Latin:

Vers. 22. CONSUMMATIO ABBREVIATA INUN- DABIT JUSTITIAM] λόγον συντελῶν, καὶ συντέμνων Græci. Sicut ubi rationes accepti & expensi exputantur, sæpe parva est, quæ remanet, summa, ita & tunc pauci e- runt illi reduces, sed pleni virtutis.

## 10:23
Vers. 23. IN THE MIDST OF ALL THE EARTH] Of Judea. The people will be small compared to what they were. See above 7, 21.

These things speak not of a return to the fields and towns, but of a conversion to God. This is taught both by the preceding context; the remnant of Israel will no longer lean upon him who strikes them, that is, upon the Assyrian, but will lean upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth, that is, truly in the one God, and will not place their hope and trust in men: and also by the name Sear-Jasub itself, which was imposed for the sake of signifying conversion, and the most evident explanation of the same, which is held here: The remnant shall be converted; to where? to the fields and towns? By no means. To God, I say, the mighty one, the remnant of Jacob shall be converted. What place is there here for the gloss of Grotius concerning a return to the fields? Then the following context v. 22. For if your people Israel were as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be converted from it, a consummation abbreviated shall overflow with righteousness. For the Lord GOD of hosts shall make a consummation and abbreviation in the midst of all the earth. These things speak again of the spiritual conversion of the remnant; I speak significantly of the remnant. For although the Israelite people is to be innumerable, like the sand of the sea, yet a few from that multitude, and indeed for the most part visible before the world, will embrace the Gospel. A consummation abbreviated shall overflow with righteousness, that is, indeed when the Israelites are cast off by God, the Lord will nevertheless abbreviate that consummation and that production, so that some also from the same may be saved and then themselves be filled with righteousness, because the righteousness of Christ is by far the most perfect, like a most abundant fountain of righteousness, and then they may also overflow others with righteousness, and lead them to true righteousness, and disperse true righteousness like a river among the nations. For God will make not only that consummation and destruction, but also an abbreviation, that is, He will ensure that from that destruction, through the removal, some remnant may still be saved. In the same sense, a consummation abbreviated is that small number of the faithful from the Jews, who will be reduced almost to a consummation: whom the Lord will cause to overflow with true righteousness: the nations everywhere in the midst of all the earth, because those surviving remnants of the Jews spread righteousness throughout the whole earth: which was done especially in the time of the New Testament. Whence Oecolampadius renders it not in a bad sense, consummated and those abbreviated remnants, the Apostles, namely, will inundate others with righteousness, as being Doctors of the whole world.
