Neque sermo hic de Ezechia est : sed vaticinium de Christo. Si laudes ejus hic continuantur, qui deprædicatus est cap. 9, 6. non Ezechiam, sed Christum hic celebrari sta- tuendum, quia elogia illa capite 9. Deus fortis, Pa- ter æternus, Princeps pacis, nullatenus Ezechiæ, sed Christo soli conveniunt. Præterea vaticinium hic habetur de eo, qui adhuc egressurus erat olim de radice Jesse : Ezechias autem jam tum natus erat, cum hoc prædiceret Esaias. Vaticinatur Pro- pheta de virga ex trunco egressura, cum nempe familia Davidis pene detruncata, & ad incitas red- acta fuerit : At id Esaiæ tempore factum non est. Cum autem prodiit Messias, actum pene videbatur de Davidis familia. Porro etsi in Regem pium ac virtutibus præclaris instructum aliquo modo cadant illa elogia, quod in ipso Spiritus sapientiæ & intellectus &c. requiescat, hoc tamen certum est, quod efferantur non vulgari, sed eminentiori ratione : nihil enim hic vulgare prædicitur, neque possunt encomia illa de judicio hujus Regis ulli Principi mundano vendicari, quæ hic occurrunt. Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit, neque secundum aurium auditum arguet. Hæc enim καρ- διογνωσίαν & omniscientiam divinam inferunt, quod ipsa cordis consilia etiam intueatur, non jux- ta speciem externam, vel relationem aliorum, quæ sæpe fallere possunt, judicium instituturus est. Ju- dicabit in justitia pauperes, & arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ. Justitiam semper administrare non est ullius Principis. Sæpe enim per ignoran- tiam, non raro per infirmitatem, frequentissime per ministrorum culpam justitiæ tenorem negli- gunt. Nec omnia ipsi judicant, sed per alios judicia exercent. Hic vero nunquam à justitia deflectet, nec aliorum opera indigebit. Erit justitia cingulum lumborum ejus, & fides cinctorium renum ejus. Quod de terrenis Regibus optandum quidem, affirma- ri autem minime potest : quia neque cingulum justitiæ, neque cinctorium fidei ipsis adhæret sem- per, aut proprium est ac perpetuum. Et quomo- do Ezechiæ aptari illa possunt ; percutiet terram virga oris sui, & interficiet impium spiritu labiorum suorum. Quæ de Christo dicta esse, & AntiChri- sto, quem per spiritum oris sui interfecturus ipse sit, ex Apostolica interpretatione 2. Theffal. 2. cer- ti sumus. Jam si ea, quæ de habitatione lupi cum agno, &c. sequuntur, expendas, non Ezechiæ tempori, cui infestus erat Sennacherib, nec ullius Regum ætati conveniunt, quia, etsi publica vigeat pax, privatæ tamen insidiæ, rapinæ, discordiæ nunquam cessant. Intelligenda ergo de pace spiri- tuali in regno Messiæ unice sunt. Insuper quæ de radice Jesse prædicuntur, quod in signum populo- rum elevanda sit, quodque ipsum gentes deprecatu- ræ sint, & requies ea futura sit gloriosa, nullatenus conveniunt Ezechiæ. Quem gentes non depreca- tæ sunt, neque in signum gentium erectum testatur historia. Messiæ solius ea propria sunt: cui debuit esse aggregatio gentium Gen. 49, 10. & ad quem gen- tes converti debuerunt: cujus scientia replenda est terra, sicut aquæ maris eam operiunt. Quomodo etiam illa explicantur ab ipso, Spiritu Sancto Rom. 15, 12. ita ut conversio gentium ad fidem Christi in- de demonstretur. Taceo, quod cætera, quæ hoc capite subjiciuntur, de Christo etiam intelligenda videantur, ac de temporibus N. Testamenti, quod Apostoli prædaturi sint Philistinos, Idumæos, Moa- bitas, Ægyptios &c. de quibus vid. imprimis Bren- tius in Comment. & Osiander in Paraphrasi. Ha- ctenus certe in Christiana Ecclesia id indubium fuit, sub initium hujusce Capitis vaticinium haberi non de Hiskia, sed de Christo unice: Sed Grotius aurem præbere maluit Judæis, R. Aben Ezræ, & R. Mose Hatcohen, quam Christianæ Ecclesiæ inter- pretationem sequi. Quanquam etiam alii Judæi saniores sint, ac de Messia vaticinium intelligant, quoad sensum literalem; Hieronymi utique tempo- re omnes de Messia accepisse, Hieronymus ipse au- tor est: Totum, inquit, hoc caput & sequens de Messia tam Christiani, quam tota circumcisio loqui fatentur, hoc tantum discrimine, quod Judæi de venturo & re- gno ejus temporali omnia simpliciter ad literam acci- piant; Christiani pleraque metaphorice de spirituali regno ejus, qui jam venit, Christi Dei intelligant.

Habetur itaque hic primo Nativitatis & pro- sapiæ Christi designatio. Egredietur virga de radice Jesse, & flos de radice ejus. Nasci Regem Judæis è prosapia Davidis nihil novi erat. Omnes enim à Davidis tempore è familia ejus prodierant. Ne- que nasci demum debuit Ezechias, sed jam natus e- rat, Quod argumentum urget ipse Abarbenel: Quia Hiskias prolata hac prophetia decem annos erat natus: Quomodo igitur dixerit וְיָצָא ET EGREDI- ETUR? Quæ verba docent, multis diebus post ipsum esse nasciturum. Et de Rege peculiari plane hic agi- tur. Quia prorsus singulare est vaticinium. Fa- tentur id Judæi, virgam & florem de radice Jesse Mes- siam interpretantes, quod sc. in virga regalis poten- tia, in flore pulchritudo demonstretur, uti observat Hieronymus, qui vero per florem quidem Messiam, per virgam autem matrem ejus intelligit. Nos au- tem virgam de radice Jesse sanctam Mariam virginem intelligamus, quæ nullum habuit sibi fruticem cohæ- rentem, de qua & supra legimus; Ecce virgo conci- piet & pariet filium. Et florem Dominum Salvato- rem, qui dicit in Cantico Canticorum (cap. 2.) Ego flos campi & lilium convallium. Alii tamen vete- res & virgam & florem de Christo intelligunt. Cy- rillus Alexandr. virgam nominavit Christum de radice Jesse juxta carnem, & præterea etiam florem. Per virgam, inquit, eum regiam dignitatem habere oblique subindicari videtur: Flos vero rursum, quo- niam hominis natura in illo ad incorruptionem & ad novitatem conversationis Evangelicæ refloruit, vel etiam propter suavem fragrantiam sub intelligentiam cadentem, appellatur. Sic etiam Basilius in h. l. Hilarius in Ps. 2. ut & Origenes hom. IX. Obser- vat etiam hic conditionem familiæ Davidicæ tempo- re nascituri Messiæ Hieronymus. Pro radice, quam soli LXX. transtulerunt, in Ebraico scriptum habetur גֶּזַע quod Aquila & Symmachus & Theodotion πυρ- μον interpretati sunt, id est truncum. Et pro flore, qui Ebraice dicitur נֵצֶר germen transtulerunt, ut o- stenderent, quod multo post, tempore Babylonicæ capti- vitatis nullo de stirpe antiqui regni gloriam possidente, quasi de trunco Messias & de Maria Christus exor- tus sit. De Davide olim per contemtum diceba- tur, 1. Reg. 12. Quæ nobis pars in David, vel quæ hæreditas in filio Isai? Mentionem ergo Isai hic fa- cit Propheta, ut significet, Christum tunc exoritu- rum, cum plane contemta, & abjecta est futura Davidis posteritas.

Deinde notanda etiam est peculiaris Christi appellatio. Qui Nazareus vocandus erat juxta Prophetas, teste Matthæo c. 2. Hanc enim appellationem è præsenti loco Veteres Ebraice docti deduxere. Quo de iterum Hieronymus: Illud quod in Evangelio Matthæi omnes quærunt Ecclesiastici, & non inveniunt, ubi scriptum sit: Quoniam Nazaræus vocabitur, Eruditi Ebræorum de hoc loco assumtum putant. Alibi notat Hieronymus Epistol. ad Pammach. de opt. interpr. gener. hæc verba ita reddi posse: Et Naziræus de radice ejus crescet.

Tertio observat hic ordinem Brentius. Quum enim dixerit Propheta c. 10, 20. reliquias Israel non in Assyriis, sed in Domino sancto Israel fiduciam collocaturas: explicat nunc, quis sit ille Dominus Sanctus Israel, in quo solo fidendum est, nimirum Messias, qui exoriturus est ex radice David: Subversum nempe iri arbores Assyriacas c. 10, 18. sed proditurum surculum è Davidis trunco pene emortuo.

Quarto descriptio Regis ea hic est, qua à Regibus mundanis Christus luculenter distinguitur. Super illo perpetuo requiescit Spiritus Domini, ut ab eo auferri non possit, quod de nullo Rege mundano dici potest. Super illo Spiritus sapientiæ & intellectus requiescit: hi natura stolidi sunt, & non raro in administratione regnorum suorum errant. Super illo requiescit Spiritus consilii & fortitudinis, ut sufficiat ad regendos subditos: Hi autem aliorum consiliis & aliena ope indigent: Soli regere ac defendere subditos suos non valent. Super illo requiescit Spiritus scientiæ & timoris Domini: hi autem deficiunt & in cognitione & in timore Domini, ut neque perfecte ipsum cognoscant, neque colant eum, uti par est. Verbo: illi datur Spiritus οὐκ ἐκ μέτρε Joh. 3, 34. ideo super ipso Spiritus Domini requiescere dicitur, & hoc proprium huic Regi esse indicatur. Hi autem etsi Spiritu Domini instruantur, κατὰ τὸ μέτρον, secundum certam mensuram donationis Christi eundem accipiunt Eph. 4, 7. Quum ergo super illo requiescere Spirit. dicatur, alii qui Spiritum accipiunt, nonnisi ab ipso, quia super ipso requiescit, eundem consequuntur. Absq; Christo igitur (quod recte infert Hieronymus) nec sapiens quis esse potest, nec intelligens, nec consiliarius, nec fortis, nec eruditus, nec pius, nec plenus timoris Dei. Nimis autem jejuna sunt, quæ hic habet Grotius de sapientia rerum divinarum, cognitione rerum naturalium, prudentia in rebus Politicis & constantia in adversis, Spirituque scientiæ circa interpretationem legis & sermonis Domini in Ezechia. Quem præterea istis donis præ aliis omnibus polluisse, ut hoc ei proprium sit, quod Spiritus Domini sic super ipso requieverit, perpetuumque ipsi id fuerit, non nisi temere adseritur. Nugæ sunt, quas insperfit Grotius de spiritu hic in sex partes, Apoc. 1, 4. vero in septem distributo: quia scil. creverit Spiritus in Christianismo. Nam ibi ut septiformis munere i.e. variis donis in Ecclesia sese explicans introducitur Spiritus Sanctus, quod ab ipso etiam sub V. T. factum. Quis vero vel ex hoc loco sex tantum Sp. S. dona in V. T. locum habuisse colliget, vel ex Apocalyptica Spiritus descriptione septimum donum Spiritus Sancti cœpisse in Nov. Testamento admittet?

Quinto administratio muneris Regis hujus observanda: quæ fit (1.) in timore Domini. Odoratus ejus (ut in Ebræo habetur) erit in timore Domini; i. e. judicabit argute, sed semper cum vero Dei timore; neminem temerario judicio gravabit, ut Osiander exponit: Qui sensus non inconveniens ipsifq; Rabbinis probatus, R. Dav. Kimchi, R. Aben Ezra: quod pios & impios homines facili negotio discreturus sit Messias, neque opus habiturus visio- ne oculorum, vel audita aurium : quia sensus odo- ratus certior videtur, quum sensus auditus & visus quandoque fallat. Vid. Sixt. Amama Anti-Barb. l. 4. p. 653. Alii per odorem ejus sacrificium ipsius, quod Deo odor gratus est, intelligunt, vid. Luther. glossa marg. cui annuit Glassius Phil. S. l. 5. tr. 1. c. 7. Grot. ita transfert : Et consolari ipsius (i. e. solatium) in timore Domini sive pietate. Pro pietate sua in maxi- mis periculis Deo confidet. Sed novus ille Commenta- rius est, & à phrasi & textu satis alienus. Versatur e- nim jam in officio explicando Prophetæ, quomodo id ab hoc Rege administretur. Neque quicquam his verbis habet de confidentia Dei. Ut taceam, quod in pietate sua nemo solidum locare queat in adversis solatium, quod in misericordia potius Do- mini collocandum.

(2) Regnum administrabit in justitia & æquitate. Nunquam à justitiæ tramite de- flectet. Non secundum visionem oculorum judica- bit, h. e. non juxta externum aspectum, quo alii ju- dices mundani falluntur sæpissime : neque secun- dum aurium auditum arguet, h. e. ex rumoribus, qui non raro mendaces sunt. Non ex actis & probatis solum, prout oculis auribusque exposita sunt, judicium feret, ut mundani judices, quia in- tuetur ipse coram omnia, etiam occulta quæque, ac corda insuper & renes hominum, & intima cor- dium consilia penitus perspecta habet. Sunt & hæc dicta, inquit Brentius, per Antithesin mundano- rum Regum. Hi enim natura sua non sunt tam ju- sti & tam timentes Dei, ut si proposita fuerit magna spes lucri, aut objectum aliquod magnum periculum, non declinent à rectitudine judicii, & non respiciant personas: nec sunt tam perspicaces in judicandis con- troversiis, ut possint hominum corda intueri: Sed ne- cesse habeant judicare secundum ea, quæ allegantur & probantur. Nam secundum visionem oculorum ju- dicare, est respicere personas, h. e. eum, qui habet justam causam damnare, quod vel sit pauper, vel i- nimicus : eum autem, qui habet injustam causam, absolvere, quod sit vel dives, vel amicus. Hæc solent frequenter fieri in humanis judiciis. Arguere autem secundum auditum aurium, est vel audita una tan- tum parte sententiam pronunciare, vel juxta pu- blicam tantum famam, re non diligenter perspecta, judicare, quod etsi est iniquissimum, tamen solet etiam ipsum sæpe ac multum in judiciis civilibus fieri. Præ- terea judicare secundum visionem oculorum, & au- ditum aurium, est etiam judicare secundum allega- ta & probata, ut ICti loquuntur. Hæc judices, cum sint homines, qui non possunt intueri litigantium corda, nec abscondita cognoscere,necesse habent in discernen- dis controversiis sequi: CHRISTUS autem longe alius est Judex. Alienæ autem maxime sunt Gro- tii glossæ. Non secundum visionem oculorum judica- bit, i. e. non desperabit, etiamsi maximum contra se exercitum hostilem videat. Neque secundum aurium auditum arguet, i. e. disputabit. Non ex rumoribus de futuro conjecturam faciet. Credit enim Prophe- tis. Quis vel ista, vel hæc è verbis Prophetæ hau- riet! Nemini, opinor, ante Grotium sensus talis in mentem venit : quod indicium illati est, non elati è verbis Scripturæ sensus. De judicio sermonem esse, verba ipsa clamitant. Atque id etiam, quæ se- quuntur, palam exprimunt. Sed JUDICABIT IN JUSTITIA PAUPERES, ET ARGUET IN ÆQUITATE PRO MANSUETIS TER- RÆ. Hæc docent, quod non futurus sit προσω- πολήπτης : non abjecturus pauperem, & miserum propter miseriam, sed defensurus summa justitia ; & non damnaturus affliccos, sed in æquitate pro ipsis sententiam dicturus contra affligentes & op- primentes. Quæ elogia Christo propria sunt, ac perpetua. B. Lutherus ita vertit: Er wird mit Ge- rechtigkeit richten die Armen und mit Gericht straf- fen die Elenden im Lande, Er wird sie durch Gna- de gerecht machen, und doch durchs Creutz lassen straffen den übrigen alten Adam im Fleisch, und das heisset mit Gericht straffen, das ist, Nicht im Grimm noch Zorn, sondern mit Vernunfft, und zu ihrem Nutz. Grotius ipse ad Joh. 5, 30. hæc de Christo exposuit: Ideo æquum est judicium meum quia à Patris regula non discedo. VideVaticiniumEs. 11, 4.

Sexto occurrit impiorum quorumvis, qui se huic Regi ac regno opponunt, deletio. Et percu- tiet terram virga oris sui: & spiritu labiorum suo- rum interficiet impium. Mundani Reges gladiis & lanceis pugnant, ac violenta manu hostes sibi subjiciunt. Hic autem Rex non subjiciet sibi ter- ram gladiis, sed virga oris sui: non interficiet im- pios lanceis, sed Spiritu labiorum suorum. Quod in specie, ac imprimis de Anti-Christo magno intelli- gendum esse, spiritu oris Domini interficiendo, ex Apostolica explicatione 2. Thessal. 2, 8. novimus. Virgam oris & spiritum labiorum perperam Grotius de precibus explicat, per quas Ezechias Assyrios con- fecit: quia preces nuspiam per spiritum labiorum, ac virgam oris designantur, neque per terram per- cussam Assyrii tantum intelligendi, sed, ut fatetur Grotius, impii quoq;, qui sc. de Deo nihil cogitant, sed humi affigunt divinæ particulam auræ. Et Anti- Christum hic comprehendi, aut peculiariter desi- gnari, è loco prædicto parallelo certum est. Unde etiam colligitur, quod per spiritum labiorum, aut o- ris Domini Spiritus Sanctus qui Ps. 33, 6. ita vocatur, & per virgam verbum Evangelii, per quod Spiritus Sanctus percutit impios, & regnum Anti-Christi destruit, intelligendum sit: quod sceptrum appel- latur Ps. 110, 2. & Ps. 45, 7. ac gladius est Spiritus S. Eph. 6, 17. gladius procedens de ore Domini Domino- rum & Regis Regum Christi Jesu ex utraq; parte acu- tus, quo percutiantur gentes Apoc. 19, 15. qui etiam easdem virga ferrea ibidem regere dicitur è Ps. 2, 9. De Christo ergo hæc unice intelligenda; neuti- quam vero de Hiskia.

Septimo celebrantur virtutes, justitia & fides hujus Regis. Et erit justitia cingulum lumborum e- jus, & fides cinctorium renum ejus. In regnis hu- jus mundi sæpe à justitia receditur, & abripiuntur non raro affectibus etiam optimi Principes, aut fascinantur ab aliis, ut per ignorantiam ac infir- mitatem quandoque à recti tramite deflectant; ne- que semper subditis suis fidem ac pacta conventa servant, etiamfi literis, sigillis, imo juramentis con- firmata fuerint. Hic autem Rex nunquam à justitia se abduci patietur, nunquam fidem violabit: quæ iterum uni Christo propria sunt. Glossa illa Judai- ca, quam è Chaldeo adducit Grotius, quod per Cin- gulum & cinctorium hoc pii & justi viri intelligantur, quos semper secum habiturus sit, non satis congruit verbis, quæ de justitia & fide ipsius Regis, non de piis Consiliariis loquuntur: neque de Eze- chia, aut ullo Rege id affirmari potest, quod sem- per pios & justos viros secum habeant, illique sem- per penes ipsos prævaleant: quum subinde aulis ese ingerant improbi & injusti, & quandoque et- iam apud pientissimos principes locum inveniant, imo sub specie recti non raro suis consiliis præva- leant.

Octavo felicitas & tranquillitas regni de- scribitur vers. 6. seqq. Tanta erit tranquilli- tas in hoc regno, ut efferæ & sylvestres be- stiæ cicurentur ac habitaturæ sint familiariter cum domesticis; unusque futurus sit grex ovium & leonum, vitulorum & ursorum. Tanta immitium bestiarum mansuetudo, ut parvulus puer queat eas in pascua agere, & ut serpentum quoque natura mansuescat, ac lusuri sint puelli cum aspidibus & serpentibus. Deniq; in universo sancto monte, qui quis alius est, quam Ecclesia? nulla erit bestia, quæ damnum aut nocumentum alicui inferat. Quæ non posse intelligi de regno mundano, sed unice de re- gno Christi accipienda esse, nemo non videt. Quæ vers. 7. de puero lupum cum agno ducente habentur, de ministris verbi contemtis explicant Interpp. Per infantes ab ubere matris vix depulsos recens con- versos intelligunt Vinarienses. Die Unmündigen und Säuglinge Pf. 8, 3. Matth. 11, 25. Das ist, die heili= gen Apostel sampt ihren treuen Nachfolgern wer= den sich nicht scheuen, den Namen deß HErrn Christi unter den ärgsten und gifftigsten Völckern zu predigen, und auch für den Königen und Ge= waltigen zu stehen. Apost. Geschicht 9, 15. 2. Tim. 4, 17. Nimis jejuna est Grotii interpretatio de alta & inconcussa pace sub Ezechia post Sennacheribi tempo- ra. Nam ut ut publica bella cessarint, privatas tamen cædes, rapinas, discordias & contentiones sub illius regno nullas fuisse, quis dicet? Non defuere piis lupi, non pardi, non leones, non ursi, non serpen- tes & aspides. Necessum ergo est, ut de regno Chri- sti & communione Sanctorum intelligamus. Ideo etiam additur explicatio: Non nocebunt & non oc- cident in universo monte sancto meo. Brentius hæc de mutatione maledictionis in benedictionem, quod ne bestiæ quidem, quæ in supplicium peccati ordi- natæ sunt, fidelibus nocumento esse possint Os. 2. Ezech. 34. Sed Osiander & alii Interpp. de mutatione animorum rectius interpretantur, quod, qui antea fuerint sæpe crudeles & violenti, leonibus, pardis, ursis, aspidibus & basilicis gemini, ita mutari & mansuescere debeant, ut non modo pacem daturi sint, sed etiam indefesso studio charitatis Christianæ officia exhibituri. Judæos autem carnaliter hæc in- telligentes eximie refellit hic Hieronymus, quem textus illustrandi causa adducemus: Hæc quoq;, Ju- dæi & nostri Judaizantes juxta literam futura conten- dunt, ut in charitate Christi, quem putant in fine mundi esse venturum, omnes bestiæ redigantur in man- suetudinem, & pristina feritate deposita, lupus & A- gnus pascantur simul, & cætera cum cæteris, quæ nunc videmus sibi esse contraria. Quos interrogare debe- mus, si omnia præsentis loci sic accipiuntur, ut scripta sunt, & nihil refertur ad intelligentiam spiritualem, juxta illud Apostoli, qui ait, Benedictus Deus Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui benedixit nos in o- mni benedictione spirituali in cœlestibus in Chri- sto: ergo & radix & virga & flos non referantur ad sensum: terra percussa verbo Dei, & interfectus im- pius spiritu labiorum ejus sic intelligantur ut scripta sunt, & docere cogantur, quomodo rebus incorporeis justitia & veritate renes Domini circumdentur. Sed & hoc eos interrogemus, quid dignum sit Domini Ma- jestate, ut lupus & Agnus pascantur simul, & pardus cum hædo accubet, & Leo paleas comedat & puer par- vulus mittat manum suam in foramine aspidum? nisi forte juxta fabulas Poëtarum, aureum nobis Saturni seculum restituent, in quo lupi & agni pascentur simul, & mulso vino plena current flumina, & de foliis ar- borum stillabunt mella dulcissima, lacteisq; fontibus omnia complebuntur. Quod si responderent pro bea- titudine temporum hæc futura, ut absq; cujusquam no- xa, homines bonis omnibus perfruantur, audiant à no- bis, nihil esse bonum, nisi virtutem, & nihil malum, ni- si vitium, dicente Psalmista: Quis est homo, qui vult vitam, & diligit dies videre bonos. Compesce lin- guam tuam à malo, & labia tua ne loquantur do- lum. Declina à malo & fac bonum. Divitiæ autem & sanitas corporis, & rerum omnium abundantia: & his contraria, paupertas, infirmitas, & inopia: et- iam apud Philosophos seculi, nec inter bona reputan- tur, nec inter mala: sed appellantur indifferentia. Unde & Stoici qui nostri dogmati in plerisque concor- dant, nihil appellant bonum, nisi solam honestatem at- que virtutem: nihil malum, nisi turpitudinem; Hæc breviter diximus, ut Judaizantes nostros gravissimo so- mno stertere convincamus. Ceterum juxta vivifican- tem spiritum facilis intelligentia est. Lupus enim Pau- lus, qui primam persequebatur & lacerabat Ecclesiam: de quo dictum est, Benjamin lupus rapax, habitavit cum Agno, vel Anania, à quo baptizatus est: vel Petro Apostolo, cui dictum est, Pasce agnos meos &c. Porrò subjungitur etiam tanta felicitatis & tranquillitatis causa, quæ soli Regno Christi convenit, quia reple- ta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aqua maris operien- tis. Nam ex agnitione DEI & Salvatoris hæc man- suetudo est, & doctrina Evangelii de gratia & mise- ricordia Dei implet animos hominum dilectione. Fides enim per charitatem efficax est Gal. 5. v. 6. Au- diamus iterum S. Hieronymum: Ne hoc (de monte sancto) putemus dici de monte Sion juxta Hebræo- rum errorem, sequenti versiculo Evangelicæ prædica- tionis Sacramenta monstrantur, quia repleta est terra scientia Domini, h. e. illud, quod supra dicebatur ob- scurius, habitabit lupus cum Agno, & Pardus cum hœdo accubabit. Et juxta consuetudinem suam Pro- phetalia in fine verba panduntur: Sicut aqua (inquit) maris operientis. Quomodo aquæ maris operiunt profunda maris: hoc est, terram quæ operta est flu- ctibus, sic scientia Domini omnis terra complebitur. Quam diversorum prius morum conjunctionem etiam beatus Apostolus Petrus in vase linteo, quod de cælo de- missum est, se vidisse testatur, habente quatuor princi- pia, quæ quatuor mundi plagas intelligamus, ut reple- tam terram Dei scientia cognoscamus: In quo vase e- rant quadrupedia & serpentes, & bestiæ cæli, ut quod arca in diluvio, hoc Ecclesia præstet in mundo.

Nono regni hujus dilatatio prædicitur: quod ad gentes perferendum sit. Quod non in Ezechia impletum est, sed in Christo. In die illa celebris erit radix Jesse, i. e. surculus natus è radice Jesse, qui stat in signum populorum instar vexilli erectus, ut varii ad ipsum confluant populi. Gentes deprecabuntur ipsum: nec id succeffibus carebit: Colent, venera- turæ eundem sunt gentes per totum orbem. Et erit sepulchrum ejus gloriosum. In Ebræo, requies ejus e- rit gloriosa; Ecclesia est requies Christi, qui habi- tare ac requiescere vult in cordibus fidelium, in Ec- clesia: quæ gloriosa est non quidem mundana & ex- terna, sed spirituali & interna gloria, fulgente in oculis Domini, ac per orbem etiam radios suos emittente. Matth. 5, 16. Phil. 2, 15. Ps. 45, 10. Quæ Reformatorum & B. Glassii in c. 17. Joh. est inter- pretatio, cui vero opponunt alii, quod nuspiam Ec- clesia requies Dei vocetur. Hieronymus de morte & sepulcro exposuit. Quo de ita habet: Pro requie ejus, in Hebraico positum est מְנֻחָתוֹ quod omnes similiter transtulerunt. Pro honore quoq́; in Hebræo legitur כָּבוֹד quod perspicue gloriam sonat. Et est sensus: erit mors ejus gloriosa: ut impleatur illud quod Salvator in Evangelio deprecatur: Pater glorifica me gloria, quam habui priusquam mundus esset, apud te. Di- ctum est de nativitate ejus, dictum est de cæteris in medio Sacramentis, venit ad mortem, quæ non consue- to mortalium nomine, sed quia in Christo erat vita per- petua requies appellatur. Nos enim ut manifestum le- genti sensum faceremus pro dormitione & requie, al- tero verbo, sed eodem sensu, sepulcrum vertimus. Unde de sepultura Christi gloriosa hic multa Docto- res. Cyrillus tradit utrumque sensum p. 202. Si quis mallet requietem hic Christi mortem in carne significare, quam propter nos sustinuit volens, non tan- quam mortem sustinens (vita enim erat natura) sed velut quiescere carnem faciens ad tempus: hoc illi a- liud nihil erat quam honor. Glorificatus est enim omnium Salvator, & Dominus noster Jesus Christus, cum necem pro mundo subiisset, & pro omnium vita voluntariam mortem esset perpessus. Et postea: Ho- spitium enim gratum illi est Sanctorum mens, & com- moratur cum dignis, & conquiescit cum animabus sa- cris ipsum colentium. Quod qui consequuti sunt, his honori est, & gloriæ. Quid enim cum hac nobili- tate & gloria conferendum est, Deum habere diver- santem, & in corde habitantem? Erit itaque, modo velimus, etiam hac ratione in nobis requies ejus ho- nor. B. Luther. in Comm. Psalm. 3. T. 2. Lat. p. 23. innuit conferendum esse Psal. 16. & caro mea requi- escet in spe: atq; ita explicat: Et erit requies ejus glo- ria, quasi dicat, cum aliorum Regum gloria finia- tur morte, & eorum gloria (ut ait Apostolus) fi- niatur in confusione, hujus contra gloria incipit in morte, in qua finitur ejus confusio: ita & omnium, qui sunt Christi, juxta illud Ps. 116. pretiosa in conspe- ctu Domini mors Sanctorum ejus. Gloriosa utique mors Christi ob gloriosam victoriam per mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem: atq; ita reddidere Judæi in Versione Germanica, Und es wird seyn seine Ruhung ehrlich, uti jam sepulcris inscribere talia solent: requies ejus sit in fasciculo viventium cum reliquis justis. Ita etiam Theod. Hackspan. ex- ponit: uti mors piorum pretiosa est, ita pretiosa, imo pretiosissima erit requies Christi: ut oppositio sit mor- tis Christi & regum terrenorum. Hi enim morte consumpti parum gloriæ habent: illius vero gloriosa erit resurrectio, ascensio. Sed quia de gentium voca- tione agitur, nimis prærupta illa mortis mentio vi- detur: nec una ista voce requies indicasset Prophe- ta tantum mysterium: imo uti se habet vexillum e- rectum, ita & requies ista gloriosa, vi contextus. Isto autem respicitur ad vocationem gentium, quæ confluunt ad radicem Jesse, unde requies & habi- tatio ipsius valde est gloriosa in Ecclesia & cordi- bus fidelium. Si quis de objecto præcipuo Evangelii, ad cujus agnitionem gentes vocantur, sermonem injici velit, id quidem MORTIS & CRUCIS Christi nomine exprimi consuevit, non tamen RE- QUIEI in sepulcro mentione uspiam designatur. Interim quia nec analogiæ fidei, nec dignitati rei in hac magnifica promissione illa sententia quicquam derogatur, & antiqui ad mortem, & sepulcrum Christi respici censuerunt, eam explicationem ceu piam nos reprobamus. Grotius non parum ma- gnificæ huic promissioni derogat, cum glossam ta- lem inducit: Ad Ezechiam concurrent multi ex gen- tibus ad verum Deum conversi: Et habitatio ejus e- rit gloriæ plena. Sed habemus hic interpretatio- nem infallibilem N. Testamenti, quod locus hic non nisi de Christo intelligendus sit, & de vocatione ac conversione gentium Rom. 15, 4. Et rursus Esaias ait: Erit radix Jesse & qui exurget regere gentes, in eum gentes sperabunt. Surculum è radice de eo exponit Apostolus, qui exurgere debuit, regere gentes. Et quod deprecatur a eum gentes dicuntur, de fiducia ac spe in Christum collocanda interpretatur. Quo pacto ergo hæc ad Ezechiam detorqueri possunt? Grotius mo- net, in Ebræo haberi QUÆRENT, quod Vulga- tus reddidit, deprecabuntur. Sed quale hoc quærere sit, è phraseos hujus usu, aliisque locis Propheticis constat. Adhibetur enim de inquisitione veri Dei, qui se patefecit in Ecclesia, de cultu Dei, cum quæ- ritur Deus, ut cultus ei præstetur, & ut ad eundem confugiamus. 2. Chron. 12, 14. Cap. 15, 2. 4. C. 19, 3. C

20, 3. Cap. 22, 9. Sap. 2, 3. & de conversione gentium Es. 65, 1. Os. 3, 15. Zach. 8, 22. tum a declaratione A- postolica manifestum est. Accedit decimo explicatio propagationis Regni hujus uberior, quomodo residuum populi sit ite- rum congregandum. Et erit in DIE ILLA, in- quit Propheta, innuens, de DIE ILLA se conti- nuare sermonem, de qua locutus erat v. 10. De quo Hieronymus: In die illa, hoc est, in illo tempore, de quo & supra dictum est, quum surrexerit radix Jesse in signum populorum, sive ut dominetur gentium, ap- ponet Dominus secundo manum suam, ut nequaquam juxta nostros Judaizantes, in fine mundi, quum intra- verit plenitudo gentium, tunc omnis Israel salvus fiat: Sed hæc omnia in primo intelligamus adventu: Neq; enim possumus, quum una dies dicatur & nunc & su- pra, illam referre ad primum adventum, & istam ad secundum: ne per hæc, quæ sequuntur & illa quæ præ- cesserunt, ad eum referenda sint Christum, quem Judæi nec dum venisse, sed venturum esse contendunt. Se- quitur in Propheta nostro: Adjiciet Dominus se- cundo ad possidendum residuum populi sui. Illud SECUNDO nonnulli respicere volunt liberatio- nem priorem e tyrannide Pharaonis, cum educti sunt ex Ægypto. Alii reductionem e captivitate Babylonica; Tum enim primum RESIDUUM populi sui reduxit Dominus. Ex Ægypto deduxit universum populum suum. Ita Osiander: Quem- admodum Filius Dei Dominus Jehovah collegit (sub imperio Cyri) Judæos dispersos in varias nationes, ut redirent ad patriam ex multis regionibus, qui super- fuerant prioribus cladibus; ita secundo extendet ma- num suam tanquam vexillifer, (Er wird das Fahn- lein fliegen lassen) & per Evangelii prædicationem colliget de orbe terrarum electos in Ecclesiam suam: & quidem non Judæos tantum, sed etiam gentes: ideo di- cit: Dominum levaturum signum ad gentes. Atq; ita hunc locum explicare videtur Joh. Cap. 11. Jesus moriturus erat pro gente, & non tantum pro gente (Judaica) sed ut filios Dei (electos) qui erant disper- si (inter gentes) congregaret in unum. Aliter vocem secundo intelligere videtur Hieronymus: quod nem- pe Israelitarum reliquiæ secundario tantum accessu- ræ sint in N. Testamento. Post vocationem igitur gen- tium, quæ quondam in caudam reputata sint, Israel in caudam reputabitur, ut apponat Dominus secundo manum suam, & possideat residuum populi sui: de quo & supra legimus, non omnem Israel, sed reliquias esse salvandas, quæ relictæ fuerint ab Assyriis & ab Ægy- pto, & a diversis per circuitum nationibus. Dicitur ergo Dominus collecturus residuum populi sui, quod relinquetur ab Assyriis, & ab Ægypto, & a Phatros (Petræa Arabia) & ab Æthiopia & ab Ælam (Me- dis vel Elameis, qui Medis contigui sunt) & a Sen- naar (a Babylone) & ab Emath (ab Antiochia) & ab insulis maris (a Græcia & tota occidentali parte mundi: Grotius: A Cypro, Creta, Macedonia & lo- cis Asiæ maritimis. Nam omnia mari adsita sunt איים Ebræis) & levaturus vexillum ad gentes & congre- gaturus profugos, seu exules de populo Israel, & disper- sos populi Judæ collecturus a quatuor plagis terræ. Ad hæc enim loca dispersi fuerunt Israëlitæ partim ca- ptivitate Assyriaca, partim captivitate Babylonica, partim persecutione Antiochi Epiphanis, partim aliis calamitatibus, ut h. l. Brentius. Non agi hic de li- beratione, quæ Cyri tempore facta est, agnoscit Grotius: quamvis ratio ejus solida non sit: quod nempe nondum ad res Nabochodonosoris devenerit Esaias, nec, cum hæc scriberet, revelationem earum rerum acceperit. Unde enim ipsi constat, quod tum nondum eam revelationem habuerit? annon jam eorum, quæ sub N. T. erant eventura, revela- tionem acceperat ac vaticinatus erat Propheta?

Certior & solidior aliorum Interpp. ratio est : quod sub Cyro pauci redierint in terram Canaan ; neg; talis ea liberatio fuerit, qualis hic prædicitur. Siquidem manserint in servitute regni Persici misere , qua finiti- mi postea oppressi fuerint. Grotius per residuum po- puli Israëliturum decem tribuum quosdam intelligit ex illis, qui ob Thiglath Pelesaris & Salmanassaris in- cursus in varias terras se receperunt, ad Ezechiam i- terum venturos : Per dispersos Judæ vero eos , qui sub Sennacheribo profugerant. Sed neque Israëlitae in tam varias regiones dispersi, & ex illis reversi Eze- chiæ tempore leguntur, neq; Iudæi e quatuor pla- gis mundi congregandi erant sub Sennacheribo. Ideoque sine dubio Propheta loquitur de libera- tione facta per Christum, de congregatione, quæ in N. T. futura erat, Evangelio in orbem terrarum di- vulgato , quum hoc signum seu vexillum erectum conspicuum reddi debuerit, inter nationes varias, in toto terrarum orbe, per hæc loca è diversis terræ partibus, designato : Ut de hoc loco eximie Hiero- nymus, quomodo ad reliquias populi manum apposue- rit Deus: Non omnem Israël, sed reliquias esse sal- vandas, quæ relictæ fuerint ab Assyriis, & ab Ægypto & à diversis per circuitum nationibus. Primum e- nim duodecim Apostoli, & septuaginta & centum viginti animæ in Dominum crediderunt. Jacobus quo- que ad Paulum Apostolum loquitur, qui & ipse de re- liquiis erat. Vides frater, quanta millia sint Judæo- rum credentium? hi omnes æmulatores legis sunt. Et in eodem volumine legimus : Erant autem in Hiezu- salem habitantes Judæi, viri timorati, de universis gentibus, quæ sub cælo sunt, qui omnes mirabantur atq; dicebant : Nonne isti Galilæi sunt, & quomodo nos audivimus unusquisq; linguam nostram, in qua nati sumus? Parthi & Medi & Elamitæ & habi- tantes in Mesopotamia & Syria, Cappadocia, Ponto & Asia, Phrygia & Pamphilia, Ægypto & Lybia & Cyrene, & advenæ Romani, Judæi & proselyti, Cretes & Arabes : audivimus loquentes eos nostris linguis magnalia DEI. De his igitur universis gentibus per Apostolos Israël reliquiæ salvabuntur. Tradunt Ecclesiasticæ historiæ, quod Apostoli in toto orbe disper- si Evangelium prædicarint : Ita ut quidam Persas In- dosq; penetrarent, & Æthiopia daret manus suas Deo, & trans flumina Æthiopiæ inde Christo munera de- ferrentur. Ac ne solum Orientales populos significare videatur, jungit & reliqua : Et ab Insulis maris. In- sulas autem maris occidentalem plagam significat, quæ Oceani ambitu clauditur. Levabit igitur signum cru- cis in universas nationes , & de Synagogis Judæo- rum primum Israël populum congregabit, ut Aposto- li præceptum Salvatoris implerent, qui dixerat , Ite ad domus perditas Israël. Deniq; & Paulus ad in- credulos loquitur ex Judæis : Vobis oportebat pri- mum loqui verbum Dei , sed quoniam repulistis illud & indignos vos judicastis æternæ vitæ , ecce convertimur ad gentes , sicut præcepit nobis Do- minus. Quatuor autem plagas, orientem & occi- dentem , meridiem & septentrionem significat, ut per hæc mundi vocatio demonstretur:

Undecimo unio & Concordia Israëlitarum & Judæorum non Ezechiæ tempore, sed in N. T. com- plementum habuit, quo de v. 13. Et auferetur Zelus Ephraim : Et hostes Iuda peribunt. Recte hæc Gro- tius de odio decem tribuum adversus Iudæos cessatu- ro accipit; sed in Ezechiæ tempore impletum esse non docet. Non redierunt ad Judæos decem tri- bus, sed divisæ manserunt: non volarunt conjun- ctis viribus in humeros Philistinorum. Neque gentes illæ, quæ deinceps recensentur , in auxiliis Philistinorum fuisse leguntur , uti putat Grotius. Ideoque intelligenda hæc de concordia sub Evange- lio. Involasse enim in humeros Philistiim dicuntur

& predati filios orientis, ut eos e faucibus Diaboli eriperent pro more spiritualium bellorum Domi- ni. Quo pacto in humeros eorum involavit Phi- lippus, cum in Azoto & aliis civitatibus Philistiim prædicavit Evangelium Actor. 8. Per filios orientis Arabas intelligit Grotius, qui cum Idumæis & Moa- bitis ut & filiis Ammon etiam se submiserunt Evan- gelio. Hieronymus in h. l. ita habet: Eo tempo- re, inquit Esaias, nequaquam Ephraim & Iudas, qui nunc me prophetante inter se hostili odio dissident, inimici erunt: Sed juxta Ezechielis Prophetiam, duæ virgæ in unam virgam copulabuntur, & jungentur in Christi Ecclesiam, qui prius fuerant separati, itaq; ut in gentibus communi labore desudent, & volent in humeros Philistim per mare, hoc est, primum mariti- mis prædicent Palæstinis, & per mare volucri cursu per- gant ad cæteras nationes; Sive juxta Septuaginta In- terpp. πετασθήσονται ἐν πλοίοις. θάλασσαν ἀλλο- φύλων ἅμα προνομεύσουσι, i. e. volabunt in na- vibus alienigenarum, mare simul prædabuntur. Quod de unius Pauli Apostoli exemplo intelligamus, qui per Pamphiliam & Asiam & Macedoniam & A- chajam, & diversas Insulas atq; provincias, ad Ita- liam quoq; & (ut ipse scribit) ad Hispanias alienigena- rum portatus est navibus. Igitur Ephraim & Iudas, i. e. qui de duodecim tribubus in Christum crediderunt ex Iudæis, simul prædabuntur Orientem: Et in Idu- mæa & Moab extendent manus suas: Iuxta illud, quod sub persona David Christus mystice loquitur: In Idumæam extendam calceamentum meum, mihi alienigenæ fervent. Hæ enim gentes eo tempore, quo Esaias prophetabat, adversariæ erant populo Iudæo- rum. Et idcirco nunc dicit, quod postquam surrexerit radix Iesse, ut regnet in gentibus, & vexillum crucis ob salutem totius orbis fuerit elevatum, tunc etiam I- dumæa & Moab, & filii Ammon, omnis sc. Arabiæ latitudo dent Apostolis manus, & in locis idololatriæ Christi Ecclesiæ suscitentur. Consulere hic potuisset Grotius Jesuitas suos Cornel. à Lapide, Menochium & Tirinum; è quibus hic ita sensum reddit ad v. 14. q. d. Subigent Christo tam Occidentales, quam O- rientales populos, & prædas ex iis colligent: Sic Petrus est Lyddam & Philistæa oppida: Sic Philippus est Azotum Philistinorum Satrapiam prædatus. A- lii Gazam & Ascalonem, ubi valde floruisse Ecclesiam Christi docent Athanasius & Chrysostomus, apud A- drichomium & Baronium. Sic Thomas Apostolus prædatus est Indiam, Bartholomeus Armeniam, Mat- thæus Æthiopiam, inquit Hieronymus, Basilius, Cyril- lus. Porro: Et desolabit Dominus, inquit Propheta, linguam, id est, sinum maris Ægypti (ostium Nili Brentius; Isthmum illum, qui est inter mare Ægypto adjacens & rubrum mare Grotius intelligit) eum- que ait consecratum h. e. intactum fore ab omnibus, quia res Deo Sacræ attingi nequeunt; alii reddunt, EXICCABIS. Eodem hactenus res recidit, quod tuto trajici aut pertransiri possit. Posteriorem tamen sensum ea, quæ sequuntur, firmant. Et levabit ma- num suam super flumen h. e. Nilum in fortitudine spi- ritus sui, vi sua vel etiam vehementi vento: & per- cutiet illud in septem rivis, h. e. in multis illius bra- chiis, ut transeant per illud calceati, i.e. exiccabit for- tissimo vento, ut qui velit, calceatus per illud trans- ire possit: adeoque via erit sine ullo obstaculo po- pulo residuo redeundi ad patriam, sicut fuit data copia Israëli in die illa, qua ascendit ex Ægypto, transeundi per mare rubrum. Impedimenta remo- tum iri, etiam Grotii explicatio infert, quamvis ali- ter reddat hoc modo: In septem rivos dividet Eu- phratem, h. e. imperium Assyriorum in plurimas par- tes. Medi enim ab Assyriis, Chaldæi à Medis defecerunt. Ita gentes illæ Hebræis infestissimæ domesticis diffidiis impeditæ faciles apud se exulantibus reditus dedere.

Intelligendus autem est non reditus in terram Ca- naan, sed ingressus in Ecclesiam Dei & regnum cæle- stê, à quo nos remorabantur peccatum & mors. Sed per Evangelium ostenditur, exemtum esse pecca- tum, & mortem victam. Hæc fuerunt profundissi- ma flumina, quæ nemo potuit trajicere. Sed postquam venit Christus & sparsit Evangelium suum in universum orbem, exsiccata sunt hæc flu- mina, ut nunc pateat liber accessus ad regnum cœ- leste, uti hæc exponunt Brent. Osiander, Vinarienses, & alii. Hieronymus tamen, Cyrillus, & Procopius de Sinu Pelusino accipiunt, quem, cum Augustus Cæs. Antonium & Cleopatram persequeretur, siccavit Deus in fortitudine Spiritus sui, i. e. austro vehemen- tissimo, præter morem immisso, qui aquas omnes etiam septem rivorum Nili, ut h. l. habet Tirinus, pro magna parte depulit in mare, adeo ut milites Augusti sicco pede transirent, & Pelusium, aliaq́; Ægypti clau- stra celerrime occuparent, & extincto Antonio ac Cleo- patra soli Augusto monarchiam orbis relinquerent, teste Strabone, Dione Cassio & Plutarcho. Idque divino consilio, ut hac ratione aditus Evangelio Chri- sti tum in Ægypto, tum in reliquo etiam orbe jam pa- cifico, & sub unius monarchiam redacto paulatim pa- tefieret. Simile quid contigit sub tempus reductionis Judæorum è Babylone in Judæam: Nam Euphrates (quem hic per flumen intelligit Chaldæus, & cum eo Sanchez) durante obsidione Babylonis à Cyro per se- ptem fossas & rivos ab urbe alio derivatus est, teste Herodoto, Xenophonte & Orosio, atq́; ita miles sicco pede in urbem immissus est, & Balthasar Chaldæus Rex è medio cum suis sublatus, & Cyro stabilita mo- narchia, & Judæis libertas obvenit. Quæ figuræ fuerunt eorum quæ sub tempora Christi obventura Ecclesiæ Isaias hic prædicit. Hactenus Tirinus, qui prior è Corn. à Lapide habet: posteriora v. è San- ctio desumsit. Quem vero hic merito Cornel. à La- pide refellit: Esaiæ oracula, inquit, sublimiora sunt, nec Judæos Babylone redeuntes, sed Christum, & Christianos spectant: & per flumen hic Nilum intel- ligi, patet ex septem rivis; hi enim in solo Nilo reperi- untur. Eadem Nili siccitas prædicitur inferius c. 19, 5. Quod vero indicat S. Hieronymus Nilum prius uno alveo fluentem, tunc primum in septem alveos fuisse de- rivatum, id cum veteribus historicis non consentit. Grotius noster attendere hic debuisset monitum S. Hieronymi, quod sub finem capitis hujus reli- quit: Prudens & Christianus lector hanc habeat re- promissionum Prophetarum regulam: ut quæ Judæi & nostri, imo non nostri Judaizantes, carnaliter futura contendunt: nos spiritualiter jam transacta doceamus, ne per occasionem istiusmodi fabularum & inextricabilium juxta Apostolum quæstionum, Judai- zare cogamur. Cæterum non dissimulamus, quod Cyrillus etiam in hisce explicandis historiam de re- ductione è captivitate Babylonica conferat, utut sensum genuinum vaticiniorum tempora N. Test. concernere agnoscat: non quod geminum sen- sum, literalem, ac mysticum, quem sublimiorem vocat Grotius, subesse putet, sed quod alludat Spir. Sanct. ad ea, quæ sub V. T. gesta sunt in describendis & explicandis illis, quæ futura erant sub N.T. eorum- que comparationem instituat. Unde ad vers. 12. ita habet Cyrillus: Propheta sermonem hunc hisce ver- bis mirabiliter pertexit. Sumit, quod historice factum est εἰς εἰκόνα πραγμάτων νοητῶν, ad imaginem de- scribendam rei sub intelligentiam cadentis. Prophe- tæ autem scopus fuit, ex rebus evidentioribus & ex il- lis, quæ olim evenerunt, Servatoris nostri adventus præclaras res gestas ostendere. Denique observan- dum, quod Chaldæus Interpres hoc vaticinium de Messia Rege intelligat, siquidem ita reddat: Et con- egredietur Rex de filiis Jesse, & Messias de filiis filio- rum ejus ungetur: quodque Judæi ipsi agnoscant, de Messia hic sermonem esse, non secundum sen- fum tantum sublimiorem, sed κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν, etsi plera- que carnaliter intelligant, adeoque non circa sub- jectum vaticinii errent, sed circa prædicata, quæ de Messia hic enunciantur: & circa explicationem, quia Messiam alium, quam Jesum Nazarenum in- telligunt: quomodo Abarbanel: Postquam sectio hæc non potest explicari secundum ullam earum sen- tentiarum (nec de Hiskia, nec de Zorobabele) pa- tet, quod non agat nisi de Messia justitia nostra cito re- velando. Cogor, inquit R. Lipomanus, exponere to- tam hanc sectionem de Rege Messia, etsi quibusdam è nostro populo bi versus alias clarissimi absconditi sint; ostendam autem ex iisdem, quod Messias hactenus nondum venerit. Vide Nizachon ejusdem adver- sus Christianos. Addimus, quæ de hoc loco Es. 11. v. 1. Raimundus Martinus in Pugione Fidei ad- versus Mauros & Judæos, Parisiis per Josephum de Voisin Anno 1651. edito, part. III. dist. I. Cap. 11. §. 6. p. 436. habet. Nota, quod in locis innumeris in Talmud boc de Messia exponatur, & nunquam de alio ab aliquo, qui alicujus apud Ebræos autoritatis sit. Quare patet, quod errent nimium Iudaizantes nostri, qui boc de Iosia ad literam non verentur exponere: de SOLO quippe Messia boc AD LITERAM in- telligendum fore ostenditur per R. Salomon, qui boc de ipso, non de Iosia exponit; quod juxta morem suum nullatenus egisset, si absque injuria sui Talmud, & Targum & sine Prædecessorum suorum præjudicio aliter exponere potuisset. R. Salomonis verba ad h. l. ita habent: Non ad visionem oculorum suorum ju- dicabit Rex Messias, sed cum sapientia Dei sancti & benedicti, qui in medio ejus erit, sciet & intelli- get, quis fuerit culpabilis & quis innocens, & arguet in æquitate, i. e. cum lingua quieta & tenera. In Bereschith Rabba super Gen. 1. v. 2. Spiritus Elohim: Hic est Spiritus Messiæ, de quo dictum est Esa. 11. & requiescet super eum Spiritus Dei. Talia plu- rima ex Rabbinis produci possent: Sed non est ul- lum de hoc loco etiam penes recentiores Judæos plerosque dubium, quod de Messia agat, quam- vis pleraque carnaliter intelligant, adeoque etiam ver- ba illa: habitabit lupus cum ariete, secundum lite- ram accipienda esse contendant. Quæ vero, R. Mo- ses Maimonides in Summa Talmud. tract. de Regibus cap. 2. allegorice intelligenda esse fatetur hoc sensu: fore, ut Israelitæ tuto & sine metu habitent cum impiis gentium mundi, qui comparantur lupo & pardo, Ierem. 5. v. 6.

## 11:11
Vers. 11.

THE LORD SHALL SET HIS HAND AGAIN THE SECOND TIME TO POSSESS THE REMNANT OF HIS PEOPLE] It is a transposition, for he shall set his hand to possess a second time. I do not think these things are to be referred to the times of Cyrus: for Isaiah had not yet come to the affairs of Nebuchadnezzar, nor when he wrote these things had he received a revelation of those matters, but he says that many of the Israelites of the ten tribes, who had betaken themselves to various lands at the incursions of Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser, would come to him in the times of Hezekiah. AND FROM PATHROS] From the Pharusii or Phaurusi in Ethiopia. See what we have said in book 1 on the Christian Religion. AND FROM ELAM] From the Elymaeans, who are contiguous to the Medes. See the same book. AND FROM SHINAR] From Babylonia. See again the said book. AND FROM HAMATH] See above X. 9. AND FROM THE ISLANDS OF THE SEA] From Cyprus, Crete, Macedonia, and the maritime places of Asia. For all places situated by the sea are אײי הים to the Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ADJICIET DOMINUS SECUNDO MANUM SUAM AD POSSIDENDUM RESIDUUM POPULI SUI] Trajectio est, pro adjiciet manum suam ad secundo possidendum. Non putem hæc ad Cyri tempora referen- da: nam nondum ad res Nabuchodonosoris devênit Esaias, nec cum hæc scriberet, earum rerum revelationem acce- perat, sed ex Israëlitis decem tribuum, qui ad Theglath- phalasaris & Salmanassaris incursus in varias terras se rece- perant, multos dicit Ezechiæ temporibus ad ipsum ven- turos. ET A PHETROS] Pharusis vel Phaurusiis in Æ- thiopia. Vide quæ nobis dicta ad librum 1. de Religione Christiana. ET AB ÆLAM] Ab Elymæis, qui Medis contigui. Vide eodem libro. ET A SENNAAR] A Babylonia. Vide iterum dicto libro. ET AB EMATH] Vide supra X. 9. ET AB INSULIS MARIS] A Cypro, Creta, Macedonia & locis Asiæ maritimis. Nam omnia mari ad- sita sunt אײי הים Hebræis.

## 11:12
Vers. 12.

AND HE SHALL ASSEMBLE THE OUTCASTS OF ISRAEL] Those of whom we spoke at verse 11.

AND THE DISPERSED OF JUDAH] Those who had fled under Sennacherib.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET CONGREGABIT PROFUGOS ISRAEL] Il- los de quibus diximus ad comma 11.

ET DISPERSOS JUDA] Qui sub Sennacheribo profugerant.

## 11:13
Ver. 13. AND THE JEALOUSY OF EPHRAIM SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY] That hatred with which the men of the ten tribes burned against the Jews will cease, because of the common danger, and because they will have a refuge among the Jews: the following words explain this.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET AUFERETUR ZELUS EPHRAIM] O- dium illud, quo decem tribuum homines adversus Ju- dæos ardebant, cessabit, ex communi periculo, & quia perfugium habebunt apud Judæos: explicant id sequen- tia.

## 11:14
THE CHILDREN OF THE EAST] The Arabs, who are to the east of the Jews. See what we said at the beginning of chapter 2 of Matthew. The Jews will take spoils from them.

IDUMEA AND MOAB THE COMMAND OF THEIR HAND] The putting forth of their hands. That is, the Jews will put forth their hand, they will make expeditions into their territories.

AND THE CHILDREN OF AMMON SHALL BE OBEDIENT] In the Hebrew: Their hearing: that is, they will serve as soldiers under the leadership of the Jews against the Philistines.

Latin:

FILIOS ORIENTIS] Arabas, qui ad Orientem Ju- dæis. Vide, quæ diximus ad initium capitis 2. Matthæi. Ab his prædas agent Judæi.

IDUMÆA ET MOAB PRÆCEPTUM MANUS EORUM] Immissio manuum eorum. Id est, Judæi ma- num immittent, expeditiones facient in eorum fines.

ET FILII AMMON OBEDIENTES ERUNT] In Hebræo: Auditus eorum: id est, sub Judæorum ductu militabunt contra Philistinos.

## 11:15
Ver. 15. AND THEY SHALL FLY UPON THE SHOULDERS OF THE PHILISTINES] You have the history in 2 Kings 18:8. The nations that follow seem to have been among the auxiliaries of the Philistines.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET VOLABUNT IN HUMEROS PHILI- STHIIM] Historiam habes 2. Reg. 18, 8. Quæ sequuntur gentes, videntur fuisse in auxiliis Philisthinorum.

## 11:15
Ver. 15. AND THE LORD SHALL DESTROY THE TONGUE OF THE EGYPTIAN SEA] In the Hebrew it is החרים, which in its primitive meaning is 'he will consecrate.' But because things consecrated to God could not be touched, therefore it must be understood here that that isthmus which is between the sea lying before Egypt and the Red Sea will be untouched by all, God so disposing matters that the Israelites who had fled into Egypt (see above 11) could safely return home.

AND HE SHALL LIFT UP HIS HAND OVER THE RIVER] When 'the river' is said simply, it signifies the Euphrates.

AND WITH THE MIGHT OF HIS SPIRIT] With his own strength.

AND HE SHALL SMITE IT IN SEVEN STREAMS] Or rather, he will divide the Euphrates into seven streams, that is, the empire of the Assyrians into many parts. For the Medes revolted from the Assyrians, and the Chaldeans from the Medes. Thus those nations most hostile to the Hebrews, hindered by domestic dissensions, provided easy returns for those living in exile among them, which will follow. It is frequent in the Holy Scriptures to signify empires by rivers: which the Greeks and Latins also do, as

The Euphrates will now flow with softer waves.

Likewise: And the Rhine, its horn now broken, three times by the wicked.

The later Apocryphal book called Esdras refers to this place, 13, 44. 47.

SO THAT THEY MAY PASS THROUGH IT SHOD] By a figurative expression he signifies an easy return.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET DESOLABIT DOMINUS LINGUAM MARIS ÆGYPTI] In Hebræo est החרים, quod primitivo significatu est consecrabit. Quia autem res Deo sacratæ attingi non poterant, ideo intelligi hic debet Isthmum illum, qui est inter mare Ægypto objacens, & ru- brum mare intactum ab omnibus fore, Deo ita res dispo- nente, ut qui in Ægyptum confugerunt Israëlitæ (vide supra 11.) tuto domum redire possent.

ET LEVABIT MANUM SUAM SUPER FLU- MEN] Flumen cum simpliciter dicitur, significat Euphra- tem.

ET FORTITUDINE SPIRITUS SUI] Vi sua.

ET PERCUTIET EUM IN SEPTEM RIVIS] Imo in septem rivos dividet Euphratem, id est, imperium Assyriorum in plurimas partes. Medi enim ab Assyriis, Chaldæi à Medis defecerunt. Ita gentes illæ Hebræis in- festissimæ domesticis dissidiis impeditæ faciles apud se exu- lantibus reditus dedêre, quod sequetur. Frequens est sa- cris literis per flumina significare imperia: quod & Græci Latinique faciunt, ut

Euphrates ibit jam mollior undis.

Item: Fractumque cornu jam ter improbo Rhenum.

Ad hunc locum respicit Apocryphus posterior Esdræ dictus nomine 13, 44. 47.

ITA UT TRANSEANT PER EAM CALCEA- TI] Figurata locutione facilem significat reditum.

## 11:16
Ver. 16. AND THERE SHALL BE A WAY FOR THE REMNANT OF MY PEOPLE, WHICH SHALL BE LEFT FROM THE ASSYRIANS] More correctly thus: And there shall be a way from Assyria for my remnant and surviving people. The following words show this: they shall come out from there as safely as they once did from Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET ERIT VIA RESIDUO POPULO MEO, QUI RELINQUETUR AB ASSTRIIS] Rectius sic: Et via erit ab Assyria populo meo reliquo ac superstiti. Osten- dunt id sequentia: ita tuto inde evenient, ut olim ex Æ- gypto.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

The sermon is concluded with a Eucharistic Hymn of the Church, by which it is to celebrate the thanks and salvation of the Lord.

Ver. 1. I WILL CONFESS TO THEE O LORD] I give thanks to thee.

BECAUSE THOU WAST ANGRY WITH ME, THY FURY IS TURNED] A Hebrew mode of speaking, for which in Latin we would say: Because when thou wast angry with me, thy wrath subsided.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Concio concluditur Hymno Eucharistico Ec- clesiæ, quo gratiam & salutem Domini ce- lebratura sit.

Vers. 1. CONFITEBOR TIBI DOMINE] Gratias ago tibi.

QUONIAM IRATUS ES MIHI, CONVER- SUS EST FUROR TUUS] Hebraicum genus loquen- di, pro quo Latine diceremus: Quia cum iratus fueris mihi, resedit ira tua.

## 12:3
Ver. 3. YE SHALL DRAW WATERS IN JOY FROM THE FOUNTAINS OF THE SAVIOUR] You shall enjoy the goods granted by God. In a mystical sense it can rightly be understood concerning the most perfect doctrine, as Jonathan took it here, which title fits the Gospel most excellently.

Latin:

Vers. 3. HAURIETIS AQUAS IN GAUDIO DE FONTIBUS SALVATORIS] Frueris bonis à Deo con- cessis. Sensu mystico recte accipi potest de perfectissima doctrina, ut hic sumsit Jonathan, qui titulus Evangelio o- ptime convenit.

## 12:4
Ver 4. MAKE KNOWN AMONG THE PEOPLES HIS INVENTIONS] That is, the counsels which God used for liberating you. He refers especially to those civil wars of the nations at the Euphrates.

Grotius persists in his preconceived opinion about a double sense: That, however, here by no means are bodily goods granted to the Jews, or the civil wars of the nations referred to, as far as the native and genuine sense which the Holy Spirit intends is concerned, but rather spiritual benefits and the liberation provided through the Messiah, is especially clear from the preceding prophecies, of which this is held to be the conclusion; since he sings an ἐπινίκιον (song of victory) in the person of the Church to God, who has leveled all paths and impassable ways for the Apostles and the faithful, just as he once did the Red Sea for the Hebrews, just as Moses and the Israelites sang a Eucharistic hymn after the crossing of the Red Sea, Exod. 15, inviting all Christians to thanksgiving, and admonishing them that they should rest in one Jesus with true peace of mind and confidence, and draw the waters of saving consolation from the Evangelical fountains, and refresh themselves with them. I will confess thee, because when thou wast angry with me, thy wrath recedes, as Grotius rightly explains. For this is the subject matter of this Hymn, this is the chief argument of every confession or celebration of God, that when he had been angry with the human race on account of sin, his wrath was turned into mercy by the intervention of the reconciliation of Christ; so much so that he refreshes us with consolation, who were subject to the curse, whence it is subjoined: Behold God, Jeschua or my Jesus, i.e., Behold, God himself (the second person of the Trinity) has been made my Saviour, my Jesus, he redeems me from sins, from the wrath of God, from death and eternal condemnation, and has brought true salvation. He himself MY STRENGTH strengthens me against the world, and its prince, (in this Lord is justice and strength, Is. 45, 24.) and my praise, (consequently he himself will be the object and subject matter of my praise, because he) has been made my salvation, (by his merit I have been made safe) from the fountains of this Jesus the Saviour all of you, whoever wishes, shall draw waters of life-giving refreshment; waters, namely, of Evangelical doctrine bringing true consolation, as Cyril and Jerome say: waters of the Sacraments, by which we are washed and refreshed, as Origen and Ambrose say: waters of consolation, devotion, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, as Bernard and others say. For all these waters can be drawn from the fountains of the Saviour. Cf. John 5, 14. He seems, however, to allude to the rock, which, struck by the rod of Moses, gave a perennial fountain of most sweet water. Compare 1 Cor. 10, 4. The fountains of the Savior, says Jerome, let us understand as the Evangelical doctrine, concerning which we read in the 67th Psalm: In the churches bless the Lord God from the fountains of Israel. Cyril: he names water, he says, the life-giving word of God, but the fountains the holy Apostles and Evangelists, add also the Prophets themselves; but the Savior, Christ. For the fountains of waters are the divine Disciples, who rain down words from on high and through the Spirit upon the whole world. Since the Chaldean himself understands it concerning the most perfect doctrine according to the literal sense, (for this he rendered in his interpretation) and the Jews do not deny it, one must marvel at Grotius, who here savors only of carnal and worldly things, concerning the literal meaning of the text, blinder than the Jews themselves, who are blinded by the judgment of God. The name of Jesus the Savior is repeated three times, so that Immanuel our God, whose advent and birth he had predicted, might be expressed by his proper name; which Jerome observed here. Whom above (these are the words of Jerome) he had called Emmanuel, then, 'take away the spoils, hasten to the prey': and by the remaining names: lest he should seem to be someone other than him whom Gabriel announced to the virgin saying, 'and you shall call his name Jesus, for he himself shall save his people': now he calls him Savior, and predicts that waters are to be drawn from his fountains: by no means from the waters of the river of Egypt, which were struck, nor from the waters of the river of Rahin, but from the fountains of Jesus, for this is how Savior is expressed in the language of the Hebrews. This is the proper object of trust, and the true cause of liberation from all fear. Therefore each of the faithful sings: Behold God my Savior, אֶבְטַח I will hope, I will place my trust in him, וְלֹא אֶפְחַד I will not fear: which elegant paronomasia expresses the joy of the faithful, resting in their Savior Jesus with the highest and joyful tranquility of soul. When therefore he wishes the inventions of the Lord (LXX: his glorious things) to be made known, he undoubtedly understands the counsels and ways in the redemption of the human race, which are to be divulged and preached among the peoples throughout the whole world, so that his name may be celebrated, since the name of Jesus the Savior is exalted. For this is that name above every name, in which it is fitting that the knees of all should bow, Phil. 2, 9. Sing to the Lord, for he has done magnificently: announce these things in all the earth. What is more magnificent, admirable, and sublime (as the LXX render it, he has done high things, i.e., admirable and sublime things) than what the Lord has done in our redemption? What was more necessary to be announced, or is now announced in all the earth, than this redemption of the Lord, in which alone is the joy of all the faithful, which is the primary matter of praise and celebration for them? And therefore the Prophet adds: Exult and praise, O habitation of Sion (the assembly of the faithful of the Church), because the Holy One of Israel is great, exalted, and glorious in the midst of you: Christ, who is the Holy One of Israel, is in our midst; by which allusion is also made to the name Immanuel, God with us. Beautiful is the explanation of our Brentius, which I shall subjoin here. You will draw, he says, in joy waters from the fountains of the Savior, etc., i.e., When Christ has arrived, and shall establish his kingdom, then men will no longer have need to drink sadness from pools and cisterns, but will drink with the greatest pleasure from the living fountains of the Savior. The pools and cisterns are the impious doctrines of the Scribes and Pharisees, which cannot render the conscience tranquil and cheerful, but cast it into eternal sadness and grief. But the fountains of the Savior are the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, or the preaching of Christ himself. This is the purest and most wholesome water. Everyone, says Christ himself, who drinks from this Samaritan water, will thirst again. But whoever drinks from the water that I shall give him, will not thirst forever, but it will become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life. See therefore, I pray, how great the benefits that have happened to the Apostles and the rest of the disciples of Christ, who heard Christ himself preach his Gospel, beyond other men who were before them. For others, even if they saw and heard the Patriarchs or Prophets, nevertheless heard only men, and their doctrine could not make the hearers saved, except insofar as it announced Christ; but the Apostles and the rest of the disciples of Jesus heard the Lord himself, the true God, speaking and preaching, by whose doctrine alone we can attain salvation. Whence it is said to them: Blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear. Amen, amen, I say to you, that many Prophets and just men desired to see what you see, etc. But what will happen then, after the Lord himself has opened the fountain of his preaching, so that the water of heavenly doctrine might be drawn from it. It is added: You will say in that day: Confess, or give thanks to the Lord, and call upon his name. Make known among the peoples, etc., i.e., After Christ the Lord our God has completed his course in these lands, his name and Gospel will be spread throughout the whole world, so that not only the Jews, but also the Gentiles may acknowledge Christ as the true God, and praise him, who has bestowed such magnificent and illustrious benefits upon them. For he has expiated sin, appeased God the Father, adopted believers as sons and heirs of God: He has conquered death, conquered hell, opened heaven, and leads with him all believers into heavenly and perpetual happiness. These are the things which Christ, the true God, has done magnificently. Wherefore, since the Holy One of Israel, who is Jesus Christ, our Lord, has done such and so great things, by which he himself is also declared great in the midst of his people, in the whole world, through the spreading of his Gospel, it remains that the habitation of Zion, i.e., all the inhabitants of the true Church of God, should exult, rejoice, and praise God, and give thanks to him for such great benefits, so that they may enjoy these perpetually on account of Christ, the Son of God.

SECTION II. EXOTIC SERMONS, denouncing punishment to the enemies of the Church.

Latin:

Vers 4. NOTAS FACITE IN POPULIS ADINVEN- TIONES EJUS] Id est, consilia, quibus ad vos liberan- dos usus est Deus. Respicit præcipue bella illa civilia gen- tium ad Euphratem.

PErsistit Grotius in præconcepta opinione de ge- mino sensu: Quod autem hic neutiquam bona corporalia Judæis concessa, aut bella civilia gentium respiciantur, quantum ad sensum nativum & ger- manum, quem Spiritus S. intendit, sed beneficia spiritualia & liberatio per Messiam præstita, ex an- tegressis vaticiniis imprimis luculentum est, quo- rum hæc habetur conclusio; siquidem Deo, qui A- postolis & fidelibus omnia avia & invia, sicut E- bræis quondam mare rubrum, complanavit, ἐπινί- κιον canat in persona Ecclesiæ, perinde uti Moses & Israëlitæ post transitum maris rubri hymnum Ev- charisticum decantarunt, Exod. 15, omnes Chri- stianos invitans ad gratiarum actionem, & admo- nens, ut in uno Jesu vera animi tranquillitate ac fi- ducia acquiescant, & aquas salutaris consolationis e fontibus Evangelicis cum gaudio hauriant, iisq; se reficiant. Confitebor te, quoniam cum iratus fue- ris mihi, recedit ira tua, ut recte exponit Grotius. Haec enim materia est Hymni hujus, hoc argumen- tum praecipuum omnis confessionis vel celebratio- nis Dei, quod quum ob peccatum humano generi iratus fuerit, conversa sit ira ejus in misericordiam interventu reconciliationis Christi; adeo ut con- solatione nos reficiat, qui maledictioni obnoxii e- ramus, unde subjungitur: Ecce Deus, Jeschua seu Jesus meus, q. d. Ecce, Deus ipse (secunda persona Trinitatis) factus est mihi Salvator, Iesus meus, re- demit me a peccatis, ab ira Dei, a morte & con- demnatione aeterna, veramq; salutem attulit. Ipse FORTITUDO MEA roborat me adversus mun- dum, ejusq; principem, (in hoc Domino justitia & fortitudo, Es. 45, 24.) & laus mea, (proinde ipse ob- jectum & materia erit laudis meae, quia ipse) fa- ctus est mihi in salutem, (merito ipsius salvus factus sum) ex hujus Iesu Salvatoris fontibus omnes, qui- cunque vultis, haurietis aquas salutiferae refectionis;. aquas nempe doctrinae Evangelicae veram consola- tionem afferentis, uti Cyrillus, & Hieronymus: aquas Sacramentorum, quibus abluimur & refici- mur, uti Origenes & Ambrosius: aquas consolatio- nis, devotionis, & donorum Spiritus S. uti Bernhar- dus & alii. Hae enim aquae omnes ex fontibus Sal- vatoris hauriri possunt. Conf. Ioh. 5, 14. Alludere autem videtur ad petram, quae virga Mosis percussa dedit fontem perennem aquae suavissimae. Confer 1. Cor. 10, 4. Fontes Salvatoris, ait Hieronymus, do- ctrinam intelligamus Evangelicam, de qua in 67. Psalmo legimus: In Ecclesiis benedicite Domino Deo de fontibus Israël. Cyrillus: aquam, inquit, nominat vivificum Dei verbum, fontes autem sanctos Apostolos & Evangelistas, adde etiam ipsos Prophe- tas; Salutare vero Christum. Fontes siquidem aqua- rum sunt divini Discipuli, qui sermones e supernis & per Spiritum in universum orbem terrarum depluunt. Quum Chaldaeus ipse de doctrina perfectissima in- telligat juxta sensum literalem, (hunc enim inter- pretatione sua reddidit) neque abnuant Judaei, mirari oportet Grotium, qui hic carnalia & mun- dana tantum sapit, circa literalem textus senten- tiam, ipsis Judaeis judicio Dei excaecatis caecior. Nomen Jesu Salvatoris ter repetitur, ut Immanuel Deus noster, cujus adventum & nativitatem prae- dixerat, nomine proprio exprimatur; quod hic ob- servavit Hieronymus. Quem supra (verba sunt Hie- ronymi) Emmanuel, deinde, spolia detrahe, festina praedari: & reliquis appellarat nominibus: ne vide- retur alter esse praeter eum, quem Gabriel virgini nunciavit dicens, & vocabis nomen ejus Jesum, ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum: nunc vo- cat Salvatorem, & de ejus fontibus aquas praedicit hauriendas: nequaquam de aquis fluminis Aegy- pti,, quae percussae sunt, neg; de aquis fluminis Rahin, sed de fontibus Iesu, hoc enim Hebraeorum lingua Sal- vator exprimitur. Hic est proprium fiduciae obje- ctum, & causa vera liberationis ab omni metu. Ideo canit fidelium quisque: Ecce Deus Salvator meus, אֶבְטַח sperabo, fiduciam collocabo in ipso, וְלֹא אֶפְחַד non timebo: quae elegans paronomasia laetitiam fidelium, summa laetaque animi tranquil- litate acquiescentium in Jesu Salvatore suo expri- mit. Cum ergo vult notas fieri adinventiones Do- mini (LXX. gloriosa ejus) consilia & vias in redemtio- ne generis humani sine dubio intelligit, quae in po- pulis per universum orbem divulgari ac depraedi- cari debent, ut celebretur nomen ejus, quoniam ex- celsum est nomen Jesu Salvatoris. Hoc enim est no- men illud supra omne nomen, in quo omnium genua flecti oportet, Phil. 2, 9. Cantate Domino, quoniam magnifice fecit: annunciate hæc in universa terra. Quid magis magnificum est, admirandum & subli- me, (ut LXX. reddunt, fecit excelsa, h. e. res admira- biles & sublimes) quam quod fecit Dominus in re- demtione nostra? Quid annunciandum potius e- rat aut annunciatur nunc in universa terra, quam hæc Domini redemtio, in qua sola omnium fide- lium gaudium, quæ laudis & celebrationis materia ipfis est primaria? Ideoque subdit Propheta: Exul- ta & lauda habitatio Sion (cœtus fidelium Ecclesiæ) quia magnus, exaltatus & gloriosus in medio tui est Sanctus Israël: Christus, qui est Sanctus Israël, in medio nostri est; quo alluditur etiam ad nomen Immanuel, Deus nobiscum. Pulcra est Brentii no- stri explicatio, quam hic subjungam. Haurietis, in- quit, in gaudio aquas de fontibus Salvatoris &c. h. e. Cum advenerit Christus, & instituet regnum suum, tunc non amplius necesse habebunt homines bibere tristitiam de lacunis & cisternis, sed bibent maxima voluptate de vivis fontibus Salvatoris. Lacunæ & ci- sterna sunt impiæ Doctrinæ Scribarum & Pharisæo- rum, quæ non possunt conscientiam reddere tranquil- lam & hilarem, sed conjiciunt eam in æternam tristi- tiam & dolorem. Fontes autem Salvatoris sunt Ev- angelion Domini nostri Jesu Christi, aut prædicatio ipsa Christi. Hæc est purissima & saluberrima aqua. Omnis, inquit Christus ipse, qui biberit ex aqua ista Samaritana, sitiet iterum. Quisquis autem bibe- rit ex aqua, quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æ- ternum, sed fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Vide ergo mihi, quanta beneficia Apostolis & reliquis discipulis Christi, qui audiverunt Christum i- psum prædicare Evangelium suum, præ aliis homini- bus, qui ante ipsos fuerunt, contigerint. Nam alii, etsi viderunt & audierunt Patriarchas aut Prophetas, audiverunt tamen homines tantum & doctrina eo- rum non potuit auditores salvos facere, nisi quate- nus Christum annunciaret, Apostoli autem & reliqui discipuli Jesu audiverunt loquentem & concionar- tem Dominum ipsum verum Deum, cujus solius do- ctrina salutem consequi possumus. Unde dicitur ad eos: Vesti beati sunt oculi, quia vident, & aures vestræ, quia audiunt. Amen amen dico vobis, quod multi Prophetæ & justi desideraverunt videre, quæ videtis, &c. Sed quid deinde fiet, postquam Dominus ipse aperuerit fontem prædicationis suæ, ut ex eo aqua cœlestis doctrinæ hauriretur. Additur: Dicetis in die illo: Confitemini, seu gratias agite Domino, & invocate nomen ejus. Notas facite in populis &c. h. e. Postquam Christus Dominus Deus noster com- pleverit cursum suum in his terris, vulgabitur nomen & Evangelion ejus in totum orbem terræ, ut non solum Judæi; sed & gentes agnoscant Christum verum Deum, & laudent eum, qui tam magnifica & præ- clara beneficia ipsis præstiterit. Expiavit enim pecca- tum, placavit Deum Patrem, adoptavit credentes in filios & hæredes Dei: Vicit mortem, vicit infernum, aperuit cœlum, & ducit secum omnes credentes in cœ- lestem & perpetuam felicitatem. Hæc sunt, quæ Chri- stus verus Deus magnifice fecit. Quare cum Sanctus Israël, qui est Jesus Christus, Dominus noster, tanta & tam magna fecerit, ex quibus etiam ipse declara- tus est magnus in medio populi sui, in toto orbe terra- rum, per divulgationem Evangelii sui, reliquum est, ut habitatio Zion, h. e. omnes incolæ veræ Ecclesiæ Dei exultent, jubilent ac laudent Deum, & gratias ei pro tantis beneficiis agant, quo his fruantur perpetuo pro- pter Christum, Filium Dei.

SECTIO II. CONCIONES EXOTICÆ, Hostibus Ecclesiæ pœnam denunciantes.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.

The Burden of Babylon, the huge and cruel devastation of the Babylonians by the Medes.

Vers. 1. THE BURDEN OF BABYLON] A sad prophecy against the Babylonians. We could interpret this Prophet, and others, more clearly and accurately if the Assyrian works of Abydenus and the Babylonian works of Berosus were extant. Now, both in the sacred scriptures few things of these matters are touched upon, and they almost entirely pertain to the Jews, and profane histories fail us. That, however, I hold for certain: the evil which is said here to be about to happen to Babylon happened between the times of Sennacherib the Assyrian and Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean. For between those times the Medes were preeminent under Deioces and other Kings, of whom Herodotus and Ctesias make mention. But it was easy for these to take Babylon, because before the times of Nebuchadnezzar it was neither very large nor well fortified, as can be known from those things which we have related in the words of Berosus and Abydenus in the Annotations to book 3 of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

What Grotius holds for certain has no foundation at all. These things, which the Prophet threatens to Babylon, to have happened after the times of Sennacherib before Nebuchadnezzar. He confesses that he is destitute of history, therefore he should not have invented history, or sold his own fabrications as a Prophetic complement. Which he did for this reason, namely, that being a slave to his hypothesis, he might force the order which he had preconceived in his mind upon the Prophet. For he has invented that the Prophet pursued only those things which happened up to Sennacherib. Since this hypothesis is most false, and it does not appear that an order of times is observed by the Prophet, he is in vain in inventing orders of kingdoms, about which he has nothing from either sacred or profane history. It is certain among most interpreters that this prophecy looks to Cyrus and the Persians: nor can there be any doubt that Babylon at that time, i.e., the one which is treated here, was already distinguished and very powerful, such as Grotius admits it was not before the times of Nebuchadnezzar. For Isaiah himself testifies concerning it v. 19: And that Babylon will be glorious in kingdoms, the famous pride of the Chaldeans, as the Lord overturned Sodom and Gomorrah. Whence it is also certain that this concerns a total extermination: because the Prophet says expressly: It will not be inhabited even to the end, and it will not be founded even to the generation. Therefore this evil, which is predicted here, did not happen before the times of Nebuchadnezzar. St. Jerome therefore more correctly designated the cause and argument of the prophecy: Babylon was the metropolis of the Chaldeans, whose King Nebuchadnezzar, having overcome all nations as far as Ethiopia, among others laid waste to Judea, and having besieged Jerusalem for a long time, captured it in the eleventh year of the reign of Zedekiah. Whom, having been captured, he led to Antioch, which was then called Riblah; and there, having killed his sons before the father, he ordered Zedekiah's eyes to be taken out; and having blinded him, he sent him into a cage, and dragged him in the manner of wild beasts to Babylon, the prophecy of Jeremiah being fulfilled, which sang: You shall enter into Babylon, and you shall not see it. Therefore, for the consolation of the people of the Jews, the ruin of Babylon is predicted: that just as Nineveh, the metropolis of the Assyrians, whose Kings, Pul and Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser and Sennacherib had captured the ten tribes, was subverted by the devastating Chaldean, so also this one, which has acted proudly against God, may be subverted by the onslaught of the Medes and Persians. Regarding the devastation of Babylon, Jerome has this: Up to the present day, therefore, the prophecy of Babylon is fulfilled, and just as God subverted Sodom and Gomorrah, so also this one shall not be inhabited for ever. For instead of it they made Seleucia and Ctesiphon, the famous cities of the Persians. And he shall not place there &c. Babylon shall be so devastated and deserted that it will not even be useful for the pastures of herds and flocks; for the Arab and the Saracen will not pitch their tents there, nor will shepherds rest there weary with labor after the tracks of their flocks, but they will dwell among the walls and narrow places of the ancient ruins ציים, which only the LXX translated as ϑηρία, that is, beasts. Others, by the very name which is written among the Hebrews, wishing types of demons or phantoms to be understood. And the houses, he says, as we have said, shall be filled with dragons: as Aquila translated, with typhons: but Symmachus אחים expressing the very Hebrew word. But the LXX and Theodotion translated ἤχες, i.e., clamors or sounds. And what follows, Hairy ones shall dance there: or incubi, or satyrs, certain wild men, whom some call fauns or assassins, or understand them as types of demons. For owls also, all translated the very Hebrew word איים, only the LXX translated them as onocentaurs. But sirens are called תַּנִּים, which we have interpreted either as certain monsters, or certainly as great dragons, which are crested and flying. By all these things, signs of desolation and solitude are shown, because the depopulation of the once most powerful city is so great that, because of the multitude of demons and beasts, no one of the shepherds, that is, no seeker of the desert, dares to enter it. We learned from a certain Elamite brother, who, coming out of those regions, now spends his life at Jerusalem among the monks, that there are royal hunts in Babylon, and that beasts of every kind are confined only by the circuit of its walls. Others have conveniently observed the connection of this prophecy with the preceding ones: which Osiander proposes thus: Although the promises concerning Christ and his kingdom stood out clearly: yet in such great power and majesty of the Babylonian kingdom (which was very hostile to the Jewish empire) the Jews were not altogether without reason afraid lest the Babylonian or Assyrian empire might one day absorb not only the remaining kingdoms, but even the whole Jewish one, and thus the promised kingdom of Christ would also vanish. For the power and majesty of the Babylonian Monarchy was immense. Its metropolis, Babylon (as Herodotus, Diodorus Siculus, and others testify), had a circumference of over three hundred stadia (more than twelve German miles), so that you would call it a region rather than a city. The walls were high, very wide, and a wide trench, filled with waters: and there are those who write that only on the third day after it had been captured by the Medes and Persians did certain citizens notice that it had been captured. Therefore the Prophet consoles the Jewish people while he prophesies that the city of Babylon will be captured: and that that Monarchy, which they feared so much, will fall. And this discourse seems to have been held in the time of King Hezekiah, when the Babylonian or Assyrian Monarchy was flourishing and was formidable to all nations (but especially to the Jews), just as today the Turkish Emperor is feared by the Christian world because of his remarkable power and cruelty. There is, therefore, no reason for us to desire here the monuments of lost historians: We have the fulfillment of the prophecy both in profane historians and in the Holy Scriptures themselves. Since Daniel, chapter 5, testifies that the Kingdom of the Chaldeans was divided and given to the Medes and Chaldeans, after the King of the Chaldeans, Belshazzar, was killed, to whom succeeded Darius the Mede, and Cyrus the Persian, who, after Darius died, soon reigned alone. For which reason Herodotus, who describes the storming of Babylon at length, attributes it to Cyrus alone. Strabo, book 16 of his Geography, says of Babylon: The Persians destroyed part of the city, time consumed part, and the negligence of the Macedonians, especially when Seleucus Nicanor founded Seleucia on the Tigris, three hundred stadia near to Babylon. For both he and all his successors were very eager about this city (Seleucia), and made it the head of the kingdom, and now it is greater than Babylon, although it is in great part deserted, so that it can easily be said of it what was said by someone about the great cities that were in Arcadia: A great city is a great solitude.
