Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Onus Babylonis, ingens ac truculenta Baby- loniorum à Medis vastatio.

Vers. 1. ONUS BABYLONIS] Triste vaticinium in Babylonios. Possemus clarius exactiusque interpretari hunc Prophetam, & alios, si Assyriaca Abydeni, & Berosi Ba- bylonica exstarent. Nunc & in sacris litteris pauca earum rerum & ferme ad Judæos pertinentia attinguntur, & pro- fanæ historiæ nos deficiunt. Illud tamen pro certo ha- beo, malum quod hic Babyloni eventurum dicitur, eve- nisse inter tempora Sennacheribi Assyrii, & Nabuchodo- nosori Chaldæi. Inter enim illa tempora Medi præpollue- re sub Dejoce, aliisque Regibus, quorum Herodatus & Cte- sias mentionem faciunt. His autem facile fuit Babylonem expugnare, quod ea ante Nabuchodonosori tempora, ne- que magna admodum, neque bene munita fuerit, ut co- gnosci potest ex iis, quæ Berosi & Abydeni verbis retulimus in Annotata ad librum 3. de Veritate Religionis Christia- næ.

QUod pro certo habet Grotius, nullum plane fundamentum habet. Hæc, quæ minatur Ba- byloni Propheta, post Sennacheribi tempora ante Nebuchodonosarem accidisse. Historia se destitui fatetur, non ergo fingere historiam debuit, vel commenta sua pro complemento Prophetico ven- ditare. Quod ex ea causa fecit, ut nempe τῇ ὑπο- θέσεϊ δουλεύων ordinem, quem animo præconcepe- rat, inveheret in Prophetam. Hucusq; enim solum persequutum esse ea Prophetam, quæ usq; ad Sen- nacheribum acciderunt, commentus est. Quæ hy- pothesis quum falsissima sit, neque servari ordinem temporum à Propheta appareat, frustra est in fin- gendis ordinibus regnorum, de quibus nec è sacra, nec è prophana historia quicquam habet. Penes interpretes plerosque certum est, hoc vaticinium Cyrum & Persas respicere: neque dubium esse po- test, Babylonem isto tempore, scil. de quo hic agi- tur, jam fuisse insignem ac potentem valde, qualem ante Nebuchodonosaris tempora eam non fuisse Grotius fatetur. Testatur enim de eo Esaias ipse v. 19. Et erit Babylon illa gloriosa in regnis, inclyta superbia Chaldæorum, sicut subvertit Dominus So- domam & Gomorrham. Unde id quoque certum, de πανωλεθρίᾳ & totali exterminio hic agi: quia di- serte Propheta: Non habitabitur usq́; in finem, & non fundabitur usque ad generationem. Non ergo ante tempora Nabuchodonosaris malum hoc evenit, quod hic prædicitur. Rectius itaque causam & ar- gumentum prophetiæ designavit S. Heronymus: Babylon fuit metropolis Chaldæorum: cujus Rex Ne- bochodonosar cunctis usq́; ad Æthiopiam gentibus su- peratis, inter cæteras vastavit & Judeam, diuque ob- sessam Hierusalem undecimo anno cepit regni Sede- chiæ. Quem & ipsum captum duxit in Antiochiam, quæ tunc vocabatur Reblata: ibique coram Patre fi- lius interfectis, oculos Zedechia jussit auferri: excæ- catumq́; misit in caveam: & in ritum ferarum tra- xit in Babylonem completo vaticinio Hieremiæ, quod canebat: Intrabis in Babylonem, & non videbis eam. Ad consolationem ergo populi Judæorum Baby- lonis ruina prædicitur: quod quomodo Ninive metro- polis Assyriorum, quorum Reges, Phul & Theglatpha- lasar & Salmanasar & Sennacherib decem tribus ce- perant, Chaldæo vastante subversa est: ita etiam hæc, quæ contra Deum superbierit, Medorum atq́; Persa- rum impetu subvertatur. De devastatione Baby- lonis hæc habet Hieronymus: Usq́; in præsentem ergo diem Prophetia Babylonis expletur, & sicut sub- vertit Deus Sodomam & Gomorram: sic & ista sub- versa non habitabitur in æternum. Pro illa enim Se- leuciam & Ctesiphontem urbes Persarum inclytas fe- cerunt. Nec ponet ibi &c. In tantum Babylon va- stata erit atq; deserta, ut ne ad pascua quidem armen- torum & pecorum utilis sit ; non enim tendet ibi A- rabs, Saracenusq; tentoria, nec pastores post vestigia gregum fessi labore quiescent, sed inter parietinas & angustias veterum ruinarum habitabunt ציים, quod soli LXX. ϑηρία, id est, bestias transtulerunt. Alii ipso nomine, quod apud Hebræos scriptum est, volen- tes genera Dæmonum intelligi vel phantasmata. Et replebuntur, inquit, domus, ut nos diximus, Dra- conibus : ut Aquila transtulit, typhonibus : at Sym- machus אחים ipsum verbum Hebraicum exprimens. LXX. vero & Theodotion ἤχες, i. e. clamores vel so- nitus, interpretati sunt. Quodq; sequitur, Pilosi sal- tabunt ibi : vel incubones, vel satyros, sylvestres quos- dam homines, quos nonnulli Faunos sicarios vocant, aut Dæmonum genera intelligunt. Pro ululis quoque omnes ipsum verbum Hebraicum איים, soli LXX. o- nocentauros transtulerunt. Syrenæ autem תַּנִּים vo- cantur, quas nos aut monstra quædam, vel certe Dra- cones magnos interpretati sumus, qui cristati sunt & volantes. Per quæ omnia vastitatis & solitudinis si- gna monstrantur, quod tanta sit depopulatio urbis quondam potentissimæ, ut præ multitudine Dæmo- num ac bestiarum nullus in eam audeat pastorum, id est, deserti appetitor intrare. Didicimus à quodam fratre Elamita, qui de illis finibus egrediens, nunc Hierosolymis vitam exigit Monarchorum, venatio- nes regias esse in Babylone, & omnis generis bestias mu- rorum ejus tantum ambitu coerceri. Vaticinii ergo hujus cum præcedentibus συνέχειαν commode observarunt alii : quam ita proponit Osiander : Et- si præclare extabant promissiones de Christo ejusq; re- gno : tamen in tanta potentia & majestate regni Ba- bylonici (quod Judaico imperio admodum infensum erat) non omnino abs re metuebant Judæi, ne Baby- lonicum seu Assyriacum imperium aliquando non mo- do reliqua regna, sed Judaicum etiam totum absorbe- ret, & sic Christi quoq; promissum regnum evanesce- ret. Fuit enim ingens potentia & majestas Babyloni- cæ Monarchiæ. Ejus Metropolis Babylon (ut testan- tur Herodotus, Diodorus Siculus, & alii,) habuit in circumferentia ultra trecenta stadia, (plusquam duo- decim milliaria Germanica) ita, ut regionem verius, quam urbem dixeris. Muri erant alti, latissimi, & fossa lata, aquis repletæ : & sunt, qui scribant, tertio demum die, postquam à Medis & Persis capta esset, cives quosdam animadvertisse, captam esse. Itaq; Propheta consolatur populum Judaicum, dum vati- cinatur, urbem Babylonem captam iri : & Monar- chiam illam, quam adeo metuebant, ruituram. Et videtur hæc concio habita tempore regis Ezechia, cum Monarchia Babylonica, seu Assyriaca floreret, atq; omnibus gentibus (præcipue vero Judæis) esset formi- dabilis, quemadmodum hodie Turcicus Imperator à Christiano orbe propter insignem potentiam & crude- litatem metuitur. Non ergo est, quod desideremus hic deperditorum historicorum monumenta : Habemus complementum vaticinii tum in propha- nis Historicis, tum in ipsis S. literis. Siquidem te- stetur Daniel cap. 5. divisum esse Regnum Chaldæo- rum, & datum Medis ac Chaldæis, interfecto Rege Chaldæorum Balthasare, cui successit Darius Me- dus, ac Cyrus Persa, qui Dario mortuo solus mox regnavit. Quo nomine Herodotus, qui prolixe Ba- bylonis expugnationem describit, eandem soli Cy- ro tribuit. Strabo lib. 16. Geogr. de Babylone, ur- bis, inquit, partem Persæ diruerunt, partem tempus consumpsit, & Macedonum negligentia, præsertim ubi Seleucus Nicanor Seleuciam ad Tigrim condidit ad stadia trecenta Babyloni proximam. Nam & ille & posteri omnes circa hanc urbem, (Seleuciam) maxi- mopere studuerunt, & regni caput effecerunt, & nunc Babylone major est, quanquam magna ex parte de- serta, ut id facile de ea dici possit, quod de magnis ur- bibus, quæ in Arcadia erant, à quodam dictum est: Magna civitas magna solitudo est.

## 13:2
Vers. 2. UPON THE CLOUDY MOUNTAIN] This is because old Babylon was situated in marshy places, from which the rising vapor obscured the city.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SUPER MONTEM CALIGINOSUM] Id ideo, quia vetus Babylon in palustribus locis sita erat, unde ascendens vapor urbem obscurabat.

## 13:3
Vers. 3. I HAVE COMMANDED MY SANCTIFIED ONES] That is, prepared by me, namely the Medes, is the translation, because those who are about to perform sacred rites first prepare themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 3. EGO MANDAVI SANCTIFICATIS MEIS] Id est, paratis à me, Medis scilicet, est translatio, quia sacra facturi prius se parant.

## 13:10
Vers. 10. THE STARS OF HEAVEN AND THEIR SPLENDOR SHALL NOT EXPAND THEIR LIGHT: THE SUN IS DARKENED IN ITS RISING AND THE MOON SHALL NOT SHINE IN ITS LIGHT] See what we have said on Matthew 24:29.

Latin:

Vers. 10. STELLÆ COELI ET SPLENDOR EA- RUM NON EXPANDENT LUMEN SUUM: OB- TENEBRATUS EST SOL IN ORTU SUO ET LU- NA NON SPLENDEBIT IN LUMINE SUO] Vide, quæ diximus ad Matth. 24, 29.

## 13:12
Vers. 12. A MAN SHALL BE MORE PRECIOUS THAN GOLD] That is, the Medes will not be able to be induced by any price to spare men. See below 17.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PRETIOSIOR ERIT VIR AURO] Id est, Medi nullo pretio induci poterunt, ut viris parcant. Vi- de infra 17.

## 13:20
Vers. 20. IT SHALL NOT BE INHABITED UNTO THE END] That is, unto the time determined by God. The Greeks translate εἰς τέλος.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NON HABITABITUR USQUE IN FI- NEM] Id est, usque ad tempus à Deo determinatum. Græci vertunt εἰς τέλος.

## 13:21
BUT BEASTS SHALL REST THERE] The Greeks ὄρνεα. Thus this name is taken also in Jeremiah 50:39.

AND THEIR HOUSES SHALL BE FILLED WITH DRAGONS] With weasels. Thus the Hebrews. In the Greek ἦχος: But I believe they retained the Hebrew word and wrote ἰχίνα.

AND OSTRICHES SHALL DWELL THERE] See Lam. 4, 3.

AND SATYRS SHALL DANCE THERE] The Greeks translate it as demons, namely goat-shaped ones, as Kimchi explains here. Others wish for owls or eagle-owls to be understood here.

Latin:

SED REQUIESCENT IBI BESTIÆ] Græci ὄρ- νεα. Sic hoc nomen sumitur & Jer. L. 39.

ET REPLEBUNTUR DOMUS EORUM DRA- CONIBUS] Viverris. Sic Hebræi. In Græco ἦχος: Sed credo eos retinuisse vocem Hebræam, & scripsisse ἰχίνα.

ET HABITABANT IBI STRUTHIONES] Vi- de Thren. 4, 3.

ET PILOSI SALTABUNT IBI] Δαιμόνια ver- tunt Græci, nempe τραγομόρφα, ut hic explicat Kimchi. Alii scopas aut otos hic volunt intelligi.

## 13:22
Verse 22. AND WILD CATS SHALL ANSWER THERE IN ITS HOUSES] Wild cats shall sing in turns in the palaces. Thus the Chaldean.

AND SIRENS IN THE TEMPLES OF PLEASURE] Serpents in the pleasure-palaces.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET RESPONDEBUNT IBI ULULÆ IN ÆDIBUS EJUS] Alternis canent feles feræ in palatiis. Sic Chaldæus.

ET SIRENES IN DELUBRIS VOLUPTATIS] Serpentes in prætoriis voluptariis.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV.

A prophecy is introduced concerning the liberation of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity and the casting down of the Babylonian for his pride and cruelty, as also the punishment of the Philistines and other gloaters.

Verse 1. IT IS NEAR, THAT ITS TIME MAY COME] This little verse in the Hebrew coheres with the previous chapter, and rightly so.

FOR THE GOD OF JACOB WILL HAVE MERCY] By punishing his enemies, but by comforting him himself.

AND HE WILL YET CHOOSE FROM ISRAEL] Above 10, 22.

THE STRANGER SHALL BE JOINED TO THEM] Above 11, 10.

He refers these, from a collation of the annotators who are cited here, as it appears, to the times of Sennacherib. Wrongly. For it has been shown that the preceding passages deal with those things which happened in the time of Cyrus. Under whom the Jews were restored, their captivity being dissolved: and as they were returning to their homeland, many from the Medes, Persians, and Babylonians, converted to the true religion, joined themselves to the Jews, and having abandoned their idols, betook themselves to Jerusalem. Some think that an Evangelical sermon is also held here: to whom Osiander in his paraphrase agrees.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV.

Inferitur vaticinium de Judæorum è captivi- tate Babylonica liberatione ac projectio- ne Babylonii ob superbiam & crudelita- tem, ut & punitione Philistinorum & alio- rum Ἐπιχαιρεκακῶν.

Vers. 1. PROPE EST, UT VENIAT TEMPUS E- JUS] Hic versiculus in Hebræo cum superiori capite co- hæret, & recte.

MISERABITUR ENIM DEUS JACOB] Pu- niendo hostes ejus, ipsum vero consolando.

ET ELIGET ADHUC DE ISRAEL] Supra 10, 22.

ADJUNGETVR ADVENA AD EOS] Supra 11, 10.

REfert hæc è collatione annotatorum, quæ hic citantur, ut apparet, ad tempora Sennache- ribi. Male. Ostensum enim, agi in præcedentibus de iis, quæ tempore Cyri accidere. Sub quo resti- tuti sunt Judæi, soluta eorum captivitate: iisque in patriam redeuntibus multi è Medis, Persis, Baby- loniis ad veram religionem conversi Judæis se ad- junxerunt, & relictis idolis Hierosolymam se con- tulere. Concionem Evangelicam hic etiam habe- ri putant nonnulli: quibus accedit Osiander in paraphrasi.

## 14:2
Verse 2. FOR MENSERVANTS AND MAIDSERVANTS] That is, as subjects, for those who from the nations abandoned idolatry, so that they might live safely, came into Judea.

AND THEY SHALL SUBDUE THEIR EXACTORS] They will draw many of the Assyrians themselves to their own religion.

Latin:

Vers. 2. IN SERVOS ET ANCILLAS] Id est, sub- ditos, nam qui ex gentibus Idololatriam deseruerunt, ut tuto viverent, in Judæam veniebant.

ET SVBJICIENT EXACTORES SVOS] Mul- tos ex ipsis Assyriis ad religionem suam pertrahent.

## 14:4
Ver. 4. THE TRIBUTE HATH CEASED] The word מדהבה is Chaldean, and signifies a payment of gold.

Latin:

Vers. 4. QVIEVIT TRIBVTVM] Vox מדהבה est Chaldaica, & pensionem auri significat.

## 14:8
Ver. 8. THE FIR TREES ALSO ARE GLAD AT THEE, AND THE CEDARS OF LEBANON: SINCE THOU ART LAID DOWN, NO FELLER IS COME UP AGAINST US] This appears to be an elegant personification, by which the trees of Lebanon are said to be glad because they would no longer be cut down for siege towers and other works of war, as they were while Sennacherib was alive. Jonathan, however, wishes for princes and wealthy men to be understood by the fir trees and cedars. See the end of the tenth chapter above.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ABIETES QVOQVE LÆTATÆ SVNT SVPER TE, ET CEDRI LIBANI: EX QVO DOR- MISTI NON ASCENDIT, QVI SVCCIDAT NOS] Videtur esse προσωποποιΐα elegans, qua dicuntur lætatæ ar- bores Libani, quod non amplius cæderentur ad turres obsidionales, aliaque belli opera, ut vivente Sennacheri- bo. Jonathan tamen per abietes & cedros viros principes ac divites vult intelligi. Vide finem capitis decimi supra.

## 14:9
Vers. 9. HELL BELOW IS TROUBLED] The depths of the earth, in which are the graves. THOU HAST RAISED UP GIANTS FOR THEE] More correctly, the dead, for thus the Hebrew word רפאים is usually taken, which word certain Greek interpreters retain here. ALL THE PRINCES OF THE EARTH HAVE RISEN FROM THEIR THRONES] It is a personification, in which the dead are introduced with the dignity they once held. Vers. 12. HOW ART THOU FALLEN FROM HEAVEN, O LUCIFER, WHO DIDST RISE IN THE MORNING] In the Hebrew: Son of the dawn: how art thou cast down, O Sennacherib, most bright of the Kings of the east? Thus Memnon is the son of the Dawn to the Greeks. The Hebrews are accustomed to use these words concerning all the impious. It is wrongly interpreted concerning Sennacherib, for they are dealing with the King of Babylon. The time is near, the Prophet was saying v. 1, namely of the Babylonian destruction. And v. 4. In that day thou shalt take up this parable against the King of Babylon. The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked. Thence v. 9. & following, he depicts the same Babylonian King in figurative speech descending to the underworld; whom the Kings and Princes dwelling there receive with sarcasm. Whence, since there is a continuous connection of speech, there can be no doubt that in v. 12 the fall of that King is also designated. Wherefore, interpreters commonly understand it of the King of the Chaldeans: Jerome, Cyril, Basil, Haymo, Brentius, Osiander, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, and others. Yet it is not to be understood as Nebuchadnezzar, who died a glorious death, and was buried in royal fashion, and had furthermore been converted to the true faith: But his impious son Balthasar, slaughtered by Cyrus and Darius, and cast out with the corpses of other slain men. That the ancients apply these words to the pride and fall of Lucifer the angel, Tertullian, Cyprian, Athanasius, can be admitted if it is done by way of accommodation and analogy, or even if it is said that this prophecy alludes to that fall of Satan, so that just as pride cast him into hell, so also the Babylonian King, whom the Prophet therefore called Lucifer because he is a twin to the morning star, is to be cast down. For the rest, the glosses of Grotius in the following verses are as novel as they are alien and less appropriate, that to ascend into heaven is to go into the land of Judea, which, being dedicated to God, is called heaven: to ascend above the stars is to go above men learned in the law, to go above the height of the mountains is to reach the sanctuary itself. For where in Scripture is the land of Judea called Heaven, and the sanctuary called the height of the mountains? Other interpreters are more correct. commonly understand heaven, the stars, and the height of the mountains literally, because the pride of the King was so great that he presumed to ascend even into heaven itself, and to become like God himself. But those words, I will sit on the mount of the Testament or of the assembly, are to be taken thus: I will place my throne on Mount Sion, I will subjugate the Church, which formerly boasted of Mount Sion. For in the time of Balthasar, King of Babylon, the temple had already been destroyed, and the city razed. Vers. 13. I WILL ASCEND INTO HEAVEN] Into the land of Judea, which is called heaven because it was dedicated to God. Thus the Hebrews, the host of heaven in Daniel 8, 10. ABOVE THE STARS OF GOD] Above men learned in the law. See at Matthew 24, 29. I WILL SIT ON THE MOUNT OF THE TESTAMENT] On the mount of the assembly: that is, on Mount Moriah, where the Temple was, to which the Jews used to assemble. IN THE SIDES OF THE NORTH] That is, in the palace of Sion, which is to the north of the city. Ps. 48, 3. Vers. 14. I WILL ASCEND ABOVE THE HEIGHT OF THE MOUNTAINS? That is, I will reach the sanctuary itself, where God is said to manifest himself in a cloud. Vers. 19. BUT THOU ART CAST OUT FROM THY GRAVE] Thou shalt lie long unburied, namely as long as the sons of his slayers could hold Nineveh. AS A ROTTEN CARCASS] With a mangled corpse. Vers. 21. PREPARE HIS CHILDREN FOR SLAUGHTER] By the Medes.

Latin:

Vers. 9. INFERNUS SUBTER CONTURBATUS EST] Ima terræ, in quibus sunt sepulchra. SUSCITAVIT TIBI GIGANTES] Rectius, mor- tuos, Nam sic sumi solet רפאים, quam vocem Hebræam hic retinere interpretes Græci quidam. OMNES PRINCIPES TERRÆ SURREXERUNT DE SOLIIS SUIS] Est προσωποποιΐα, in qua mortui in- troducuntur cum dignitate, quam olim habuere. Vers. 12. QUOMODO CECIDISTI DE CŒLO LUCIFER, QUI MANE ORIERARIS] In Hebræo: Fili auroræ: quomodo prostratus es Sennacheribe, luci- dissime Regum orientis? Sic Memnon Auroræ filius Græ- cis. Solent Hebræi hæc verba usurpare de omnibus im- piis. Perperam de Sennacheribo hæc interpretatur, agunt enim de Rege Babylonis. Prope est tempus, dicebat Propheta v. 1. excidii scil. Babylonici. Et v. 4. In die illa sumes parabolam istam contra Regem Babylonis. Contrivit Dominus baculum impiorum. Dehinc v. 9. & seqq. eundem Regem Babylonicum figurata oratione depingit ad inferos descendentem; quem sarcasinis excipiant Reges & Principes ibi degentes. Unde quum continua sit orationis συν- έχεια, dubium esse nequit, v. 12. etiam casum Re- gis illius designari. Quapropter de Rege Chaldæo- rum intelligunt communiter Interpp. Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Basilius Haymo, Brentius, Osiander, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, & alii. Non tamen intelligen- dus est Nebuchodonosor, qui gloriosa morte occu- buit, & regio more sepultus, adhæc ad veram fidem conversus fuerat: Sed impius ejusdem filius Bal- thasar à Cyro & Dario jugulatus, & cum aliorum cæsorum cadaveribus projectus. Quod veteres hæc verba de fastu & casu Luciferi angeli adhibent, Ter- tullianus, Cyprianus, Athanasius, admitti potest, si per accommodationem & analogiam fiat, aut et- iam hoc vaticinio ad casum illum Satanæ alludi di- catur, ut quemadmodum fastus ipsum præcipita- vit in infernum, sic etiam Rex Babylonius, quem idcirco Luciferum dixit Propheta, quod lucifero geminus sit, præcipitandus sit. De cætero, ut no- væ, ita alienæ minusq; congruæ sunt glossæ Grotia- næ in seqq. Commatibus, quod in cælum adscende- re sit in terram Judæam, quæ Deo dicata cælum vocetur: super astra afcendere sit super viros in lege peritos, supra altitudinem montium sit in adytum ipsum pervenire. Ubi enim terra Judæa in Scriptura Cælum, & adytum altitudo montium vocatur? Re- ctius alii Interpp. communiter cælum, astra altitu- dinem montium proprie intelligunt, quod tantus Regis fastus fuerit, ut præsumserit vel in cælum ipsum conscendere, Deoque ipsi similis evadere. Verba autem ista, sedebo in monte Testamenti vel conventus, fic accipienda: Collocabo thronum meum in monte Sion, subjugabo Ecclesiam, quæ monte Sion superbiebat olim. Nam tempore Balthasaris Regis Babyloniæ templum jam destructum, & urbs di- ruta erat. Vers. 13. IN CŒLUM CONSCENDAM] In terram Judæam, quæ cælum dicitur, quod Deo dicata esset. Sic Hebræi, exercitus cœli apud Danielem 8, 10. SUPER ASTRA DEI] Super viros in lege peri- tos. Vide ad Matth. 24, 29. SEDEBO IN MONTE TESTAMENTI] In mon- te conventus: idest, in Moria monte, ubi erat Templum, quo conveniebant Judæi. IN LATERIBUS AQUILONIS] Id est, in regia Sionis, quæ urbi ad Aquilonem. Pf. 48, 3. Vers. 14. ASCENDAM SUPRA ALTITUDINEM MONTIUM? Id est, in adytum ipsum perveniam, ubi Deus in nube manifestare se dicitur. Vers. 19. TU AUTEM PROJECTUS ES DE SE- PULCHRO TUO] Jacebis diu insepultus, nempe quam- diu filii interfectores ejus Niniven tenere potuerunt. QUASI CADAVER PUTRIDUM] Lacero ca- davere. Vers. 21. PRÆPARATE FILIOS EJUS OCCISIO- NI] Per Medos.

## 14:22
Vers. 22. I WILL DESTROY THE NAME OF BABYLON] Namely for a time, as above 13, 20. Indeed forever, so that there may no longer be an honorable mention of either the kingdom or the city, as Osiander rightly says: For it is added: and the remnants (if anything of the slaughter should survive) and the seed and the offspring (or as in the Hebrew, and sons and grandsons) of them I will destroy, i.e., or wipe out: And I will set it (the Babylonian city) in the possession of the hedgehog, i.e. (I will cause hedgehogs to dwell in the rubble and ruins of the city) and in pools of water, so that there may be there (instead of most pleasant gardens) foul and stinking marshes exhaling a pestilential vapor, and I will sweep it with a besom of destruction (in the Hebrew, of extermination, that is, I will utterly exterminate that city, just as if someone turns a broom over a floor and then throws the filth out the window.) There is subjoined a prophecy concerning the destruction of Sennacherib, King of the Assyrians, so that the prophecy against the Babylonian kingdom may be confirmed by the slaughter which threatened the Assyrian, and because it sets forth at the same time every counsel which he devised over all the earth (of the enemies of his people) and the hand stretched out over all nations, which have hitherto miserably afflicted the same: not to mention that both kingdoms, Babylonian and Assyrian, are considered as one Monarchy, v. 24, 25, 26, 27. The fulfillment of which prophecy is had in chapters 36 and 37.

Latin:

Vers. 22. PERDAM BABYLONIS NOMEN] Nem- pe ad tempus, ut supra 13, 20. Imo in perpetuum, ut non amplius vel regni, vel urbis honorifica fiat mentio, ut recte Osiander: Additur enim: & reliquias (si quid cladi superfue- rit) & germen & progeniem (vel ut in Ebr. & filios atque nepotes) ipsorum delebo sc. vel perdam: Et ponam eam (civitatem Babylonicam) in possessio- nem ericii, i.e. (faciam ut ericii in ruderibus & rui- nis urbis habitent) & in paludes aquarum, ut ibi sint (loco amoenissimorum hortorum) foedae & foe- tidae paludes pestilentem vaporem exhalantes, & scopabo eam in Scopa terens (in Ebr. exterminatio- nis, id est, funditus exterminabo eam urbem, ac si scopa vertit quis pavimentum, & sordes deinde per fenestram ejicit.) Subjungitur vaticinium de inte- ritu Sennacheribi Regis Assyriorum, ut ea, quae im- minebat Assyrio, clade confirmetur vaticinium ad- versus Babylonicum regnum, & quia consilium o- mne, quod cogitavit super omnem terram (hostium populi sui) & manum extentam super universas gentes, quae hactenus eundem misere afflixerunt, simul exponat: ut taceam, quod utrumque regnum Babylonicum & Assyriacum pro una Monarchia reputatum sit, v. 24. 25. 26. 27. Cujus vaticinii com- plementum habetur cap. 36. & 37.

## 14:25
Vers. 25. AND IT SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY FROM THEM] From my mountains.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET AUFERETUR AB EIS] Montibus meis.

## 14:28
Vers. 28. IN THE YEAR THAT KING AHAZ DIED WAS THIS BURDEN] It is another prophecy not coherent with the previous one. It was written at the beginning of the reign of Hezekiah.

Latin:

Vers. 28. IN ANNO, QUO MORTUUS EST REX ACHAZ, FACTUM EST ONUS ISTUD] Est alia Prophetia cum superiori non cohaerens. Scripta est initio Regni Ezechiae.

## 14:29
Vers. 29. REJOICE NOT, O THOU WHOLE PHILISTIA, BECAUSE THE ROD OF HIM THAT STRUCK THEE IS BROKEN] That is, do not be pleased with yourself on account of the death of Uzziah or Azariah the King, who had vehemently afflicted your affairs, with even no small cities captured, 2 Chronicles 27, 6.

FOR OUT OF THE ROOT OF THE SERPENT] From the blood of Uzziah through Jotham and Ahaz.

SHALL COME FORTH A BASILISK] Hezekiah, who will do you much more harm than Uzziah had done. Concerning the word צפע we have said something above 11, 8. Whatever it may be, it is some serpent more harmful than a common snake.

AND HIS SEED ABSORBING THE BIRD] You might better translate: a flying serpent with the Greeks, that is, a darting one. A snake proceeds slowly, and for that reason can be more easily avoided: a darting one comes upon one unexpectedly.

King Hezekiah, a pious man, is compared to a flying serpent, not because he is a violent tyrant, but because he will be the destruction of the enemies of the people of God. Cf. 2 Kings 19. For it treats of his clemency and kindness toward his subjects in v. 30, because the firstborn of the poor, that is, the most poor and the most destitute (as the firstborn is accustomed to be called, because it is the highest in its kind), will find rest under the government of this King.

Latin:

Vers. 29. NE LÆTERIS PHILISTHÆA OMNIS TU, QUONIAM COMMINUTA EST VIRGA PER- CUSSORIS TUI] Id est, noli tibi placere ob mortem O- ziae sive Azariae Regis, qui res tuas vehementer afflixerat, captis etiam urbium non minimis, 2. Paralip. 27, 6.

DE RADICE ENIM COLUBRI] Ex sanguine Oziae per Jothamum & Achazum.

EGREDIETUR REGULUS] Ezechias, multo vo- bis plus nociturus, quam Ozias fecerat. De voce צפע diximus supra aliquid 11, 8. quicquid sit, est serpens ali- quis colubro nocentior.

ET SEMEN EJUS ABSORBENS VOLUCREM] Melius vertas: serpens volans cum Graecis, id est, jaculus. Coluber lente procedit, & propterea facilius caveri po- test: jaculus improvisus supervenit.

Comparatur Ezechias Rex pius serpenti vo- lanti, non quod violentus tyrannus, sed quod ho- stibus populi Dei exitio futurus sit, Conf. 2. Reg. 19. De clementia enim & benignitate erga subditos v. 30. agitur, quod primogeniti pauperum, id est, maxime pauperes, & summe attenuati (ut primo- genitum dici solet, quod in suo genere summum est) in hujus Regis gubernatione acquieturi sint.

## 14:30
Ver. 30. AND THE FIRSTBORN OF THE POOR SHALL FEED, AND THE POOR SHALL REST CONFIDENTLY] Even the most destitute among the Jews will have the means to live. בכורים are those who excel in any kind.

AND I WILL CAUSE THY ROOT TO DIE WITH FAMINE, AND I WILL SLAY THY REMNANT] Both the highest and the lowest of your people will die of famine.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ET PASCENTUR PRIMOGENITI PAU- PERUM, ET PAUPERES FIDUCIALITER QUIE- SCENT] Etiam pauperrimi inter Judaeos habebunt de se unde vivant. בכורים sunt, qui in quoq; genere excellunt.

ET INTERIRE FACIAM IN FAME RADICEM TVAM, ET RELIQUIAS TVAS INTERFICIAM] Ex tuis & summates & infimates morientur fame.

## 14:31
Ver. 31. FOR FROM THE NORTH A SMOKE SHALL COME] For Judea is to the north of the Philistines.

THERE IS NONE THAT SHALL ESCAPE HIS TROOP] That is, there will be no one among the Jews who will not be most ready for this expedition. For בודד is he who gathers himself. The Greek here, as elsewhere, is very corrupt.

Latin:

Vers. 31. AB AQVILONE ENIM FUMUS VENIET] Judaea enim Philisthinis ad Aquilonem est.

NON EST, QUI EFFUGIET AGMEN EJUS] Id est, nemo Judaeorum non promptissimus erit ad hanc expeditionem. Nam בודד est is, qui se congregat. Grae- ca hic, ut & alibi, valde corrupta sunt.

## 14:32
Ver. 32. AND WHAT SHALL ONE ANSWER THE MESSENGERS OF THE NATION] To those inquiring about what is being done. He reads, as we do now in the Hebrew, מלאכי. But the Greeks [read] מלכי kings of the nations, i.e., what will those Kings of the neighboring nations say to these things (for thus the Hebrew ענה is often taken)? Namely, they will be compelled to confess that it is God who lifts up the Jews, however despised they may be.

It is very poorly preferred that the Greek version be placed before the modern Hebrew text, which it cannot be proven from the translation of the LXX Interpreters that it once had otherwise. For the errors of that version are well known. And the sense is well in agreement with the Hebrew text. And what will the messengers of the nations say? What kind of fame, do you think, will be spread everywhere among the nations, concerning this war of the Jews against the Philistines? This, undoubtedly, will be said; BECAUSE (the word is expletive) the Lord has founded Zion, and in him his poor will hope, that is, the people of the Lord will dwell safely and confidently in it, relying on the protection of the Lord, even if they are held to be cast off and vile. Capellus, from whom Grotius has it, and Buxtorf in Vindic. p. 698, have already replied to this importunate crisis, that they did not read it thus, but accepted it in this sense because of the affinity of the words ὁιό. Which appears from Jerome in this place: which also happens to them otherwise. Num. 21, 21. Prov. 13, 17. etc.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ET QUID RESPONDEBITUR NUNTIIS GENTIS] Sciscitantibus de iis, quae aguntur. Legit, ut nos nunc in Hebraeo מלאכי. At Graeci מלכי βασιλεῖς ἐθνῶν, h. e. quid ad haec dicent (sic enim sumitur saepe Hebraeum ענה) Reges illi Gentium vicinarum? nempe cogentur fate- ri Deum esse qui Judaeos, quamvis contemptos, sublevet.

Pessime praefertur versio Graeca textui Ebr. mo- derno, quem aliter olim habuisse, è LXX. Interpp. translatione probari nequit. Nota enim sunt ver- sionis istius παρεράματα. Et sensus probe sibi con- stat juxta Ebr. textum. Et quid dicent nuncii gentis? Qualis, putas, fama spargetur passim inter gentes, de isto bello Judæorum contra Philistinos. Hoc nimirum dicetur; QUIA (vox est expletiva) Do- minus fundavit Sion, & in ipso sperabunt pauperes ejus, id est populus Domini tuto & confidenter in ea habitabit, Domini nitens præsidio, etiam- si abjectus, & vilis habeatur, Respondit jam ad hanc importunam Crisin Capello, à quo eam habet Grotius, Buxtorf. in Vindic. p. 698. quod non sic legerint, sed hoc sensu ob affinitatem vo- cum acceperint ὁιό. Quod ex Hieronym. in h. l. apparet: quod etiam ipsis alias accidit. Num. 21, 21. Prov. 13, 17. &c.

## 15:1 Argument
III. AFTER THE DEATH OF AHAZ UNDER ZEDEKIAH. CHAPTER XV.

The burden of the Moabites, whose ruin is predicted.

Ver. 1. THE BURDEN OF MOAB] This prophecy lasts until chapter 17. It pertains, however, to the times of Shalmaneser. For the Moabites were neighbors to those parts of the ten tribes which are named here, and consequently participants in the same evils.

Jerome, Cyril, Thomas, Haymo, and Dionysius refer these things rather to Nebuchadnezzar, by whom it is evident from Jer. 48, which uses almost the same words as Isaiah does here, that Moab was devastated.

BECAUSE IN THE NIGHT AR-MOAB IS WASTED, IT IS SILENCED] I say, he says, that it will come to pass that Ar-Moab will be wasted in the night, nay, that it will even be cut off. For נדמה is often to be cut off. Ar-Moab is the most ancient city of that nation, situated on a mountain, Num. 21, 28.

Cyril teaches from historians that when the Chaldeans came, the walls of Ar fell by an earthquake, and therefore the city was easily occupied.

BECAUSE IN THE NIGHT THE WALL OF MOAB IS WASTED, IT IS SILENCED] The sense is that it will come to pass that Kir-Moab will likewise be wasted in the night, nay, cut off. קיר is the same as קריה. This city is called in this place the city of Moab, because it was the chief one of that region, but below 16, 7 and 11, the city of the Sun because of the worship of the Sun.

The Vulgate must therefore be corrected: for in the Hebrew it is not: the wall of Moab is wasted, but Kir (the city of the region) of Moab is wasted, and for it is silenced, it is cut down: As Vatablus took Kir as a proper name, and that is very likely to Cornelius from chapter 16, 7.

Latin:

III. POST MORTEM ACHAZI SUB ZEDEKIA. CAPUT XV.

Onus Moabitarum, quorum ruina prædici- tur.

Vers. 1. ONUS MOAB] Hoc vaticinium durat ad c. 17. Pertinet autem ad tempora Salmanasaris. Nam Moabitis vicina illis partibus decem tribuum, quæ hic nominantur, ac proinde particeps eorundem malorum.

AD Nebucadnezar hæc potius refert Hieronym. Cyrill. Thomas, Haymo, Dionysius, per quem vastatam esse Moab, è Jer. 48. constat, qui eisdem fere verbis, quibus hic Esaias, utitur.

QUIA NOCTE VASTATA EST AR-MOAB, CONTICUIT] Hoc dico, inquit, fore ut Ar-Moab nocte vastetur, imo ut & exscindatur. Nam נדמה sæpe est exscin- di. Ar-Moab est antiquissima urbs ejus gentis in monte sita, Num. 21, 28.

Cyrillus ex Historicis docet venientibus Chal- dæis muros Ar terræ motu corruisse, ideoque ur- bem facile occupatam fuisse.

QUIA NOCTE VASTATUS EST MURUS MOAB, CONTICUIT] Sensus est, fore ut itidem nocte vastetur, imo exscindatur Kir-Moab. קיר idem est, quod קריה. Dicitur hæc urbs hoc loco urbs Moab, quod præ- cipua esset ejus regionis, infra autem 16, 7. & 11. urbs Solis ob Solis cultum.

Corrigenda ergo Vulgata: in Ebr. enim non est: vastatus est murus Moab, sed vastata est Kir (urbs regionis) Moab, & pro conticuit est, succisa est: Uti Vatablus Kir pro nomine proprio acce- pit, idque valde verisimile est Cornelio è cap. 16, 7.

## 15:2
Ver. 2. THE HOUSE AND DIBON ASCEND TO THE HIGH PLACES TO WEEP OVER NEBO AND OVER MEDABA, MOAB HAS HOWLED] In the Hebrew: he will ascend into Baith, that is, the excellent Temple, which is fully called Beth-Baal-Meon, Jos. 13, 17, more contractedly Baal-Meon, Num. 32, 38 and 1 Chron. 5, 8. You have Dibon, a city of the Moabites, in Joshua at the said place: there were hills there consecrated to idolatry, as appears from this place. Those hills were called במות־בעל, Jos. 13, 17. Over Nebo, that is, because of the cut-down Nebo, the mention of which is in Num. 32, 38. Medaba, or as Ptolemy pronounces it, Μήδανα, (for the letter ב receives both sounds) is also named in Num. 21, 30 and Jos. 13, 16.

ON ALL ITS HEADS BALDNESS, AND EVERY BEARD SHALL BE SHAVED] Which is the custom of mourners in those places, Jer. 48, 37, Ezek. 7, 18. The law opposes itself to these customs, Lev. 19, 27, Deut. 14, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ASCENDIT DOMUS ET DIBON AD EXCELSA IN PLANCTUM SUPER NABO ET SU- PER MEDABA, MOAB ULULAVIT] In Hebræo: ascendet in Baith, id est, Templum eximium, quod plene vocatur Beth-Baal-Mehon, Jos. 13, 17. contractius Baal-Mehon, Num. 32, 38. & 1. Par. 5, 8. Dibon urbem Moabitarum habes apud Josuam dicto loco: ibi colles fuê- re idololatriæ sacrati, ut ex hoc loco apparet. Ii colles dice- bantur במות־בעל, Jos. 13, 17. Super Nabo, id est, ob excisam Nabuntem, cujus mentio Num. 32, 38. Medaba, aut ut Ptolemæus enuntiat, Μήδανα, (nam litera ב utrum- que sonum recipit) nominatur & Num. 21, 30 & Jos. 13, 16.

IN CUNCTIS CAPITIBUS EJUS CALVITIUM, ET OMNIS BARBA RADETUR] Qui mos lugentium illis in locis, Jer. 48, 37. Ezech. 7, 18. His moribus oppo- nit se lex Lev. 19, 27. Deut. 14, 1.

## 15:4
Ver. 4. HESHBON SHALL CRY OUT] See Num. 32, 37, Jos. 13, 21. For many places attributed to the Israelites were partly never possessed by them through their own sloth, and partly were received back by the Moabites and others, through the opportunities which the dissensions of the Hebrews among themselves gave.

UP TO JAHZAH THEIR VOICE HAS BEEN HEARD] That is, even to the furthest borders, for Jahzah is there, Num. 21, 23. Josh. 21, 36. It is called Ziza by Ptolemy. As regards the phrasing, we had a similar one above at 10, 30.

UPON THIS THE ARMED MEN OF MOAB SHALL HOWL] That is, even the soldiers, who ought to have been well-spirited above others.

HIS SOUL SHALL HOWL FOR HIMSELF] Others better: His soul shall be displeased with itself. That is, everyone shall be weary of his own life.

Latin:

Vers. 4. CLAMABIT HESEBON] Vide Num. 32, 37. Jos. 13, 21. Nam multa loca Israelitis attributa, partim pos- sessa ab ipsis nunquam fuêre per ipsorum ignaviam, partim recepta à Moabitis & aliis, per occasiones quas dederunt Hebræorum inter se dissidia.

USQUE JASA AUDITA EST VOX EORUM] Id est, ad extremos usque fines, nam ibi Jasa Num. 21, 23. Jos. 21, 36. Ptolemæo Ziza dicitur. Locutionem, quod attinet, similem habuimus supra 10, 30.

SUPER HOC EXPEDITI MOAB ULULA- BUNT] Id est, etiam milites, qui præ aliis bene animati esse debuerant.

ANIMA EJUS ULULABIT SIBI] Melius alii: A- nima ipsius displicebit ipsi. Id est, quemque vitæ suæ tædebit.

## 15:5
Ver. 5. MY HEART SHALL CRY OUT FOR MOAB] Understand, everyone shall say. This verb is often left unsaid. 'For Moab' instead of 'because of Moab'.

HER BARS] The Hebrew word can indeed signify this: but you would translate it more correctly as, 'and because of her princes': by the argument of the passage below at 21, 1. Cornelius thus comes to the aid of the Vulgate; 'Bars', i.e., her strong men, who protected Moab with their strength, just as bars protect the gates of a city. But is it fitting for interpreters to change words in this way, by making 'bars' out of 'strong men' or 'princes' because of some metaphor? UP TO ZOAR] That is, the cry shall be heard up to Zoar, which is a place on the border of Judea, Gen. 19, 22. A THREE-YEAR-OLD HEIFER] The interpreter wrote, as some books have it, 'conternantem' [consternating], that is, three years old: τριετὴς among the Greeks. But it must be translated as 'a three-year-old heifer', supply 'the cry', from the preceding. FOR BY THE ASCENT OF LUHITH WITH WEEPING HE SHALL ASCEND] A remarkable allusion: if they climb to the mountains, weeping shall ascend at the same time. The same phrasing is in the same matter in Jeremiah 48, 5. Luhith is Lytha in Ptolemy. AND IN THE WAY OF HORONAIM] Which was descended into the lowlands: the same passage in Jeremiah teaches this. This is Avara in Ptolemy. THEY SHALL RAISE A CRY OF DESTRUCTION] That is, they shall mourn with a low voice. A pair of allusions to that which is in the former member. FOR THE WATERS OF NIMRIM SHALL BE DESOLATE] By 'waters' he understands the pastures adjacent to the waters, which in time of peace were most fertile. See Num. 32, 3 and 36. Josh. 13, 27. FOR THE GRASS HAS WITHERED, ALL GREENNESS HAS PERISHED. More correctly, as Osiander notes, 'the hay shall therefore wither, the herbs shall fade, finally nothing at all shall be green', i.e., their Republic shall no longer flourish, but shall go to ruin, just as if plants and herbs, with moisture failing, should wither and perish. Ver. 7. ACCORDING TO THE MAGNITUDE OF THE WORK, AND THEIR VISITATION SHALL LEAD THEM TO THE TORRENT OF THE WILLOWS] You would translate more correctly: 'Furthermore, what the slaughter left remaining, and their [the Moabites'] wealth, they shall carry away to the torrent of the Arabians.' The Valley of the Arabians is the way by which one goes from the land of Moab into Assyria, as Jerome teaches us. Moreover, in valleys, torrents are not lacking. Ver. 8. UP TO GALLIM HER HOWLING] See above at 10, 30. Here N is added to the name, after the manner of the Moabites and Syrians. Compare what is above at 4. Therefore the Vulgate falsely put Gallim for Eglaim. AND UP TO THE WELL OF ELIM] See the cause of the name at Num. 21, 18. For those who are 'dorsh' to the Hebrews, they are 'elim' to the Moabites and Syrians. It is indicated that everything will be filled with the howlings, weeping, and cries of the Moabites, who are to be most miserably slaughtered everywhere. Ver. 9. FOR THE WATERS OF DIBON ARE FILLED WITH BLOOD] It must be read 'Dimon' from the Hebrew and Greek. Moreover, an allusion is made to the name Dimon, which has its origin from blood. There are those who think the name was given because the Moabites were once slaughtered there. 2 Kings 3, 24, 25. FOR I WILL PLACE ADDITIONS UPON DIBON] Again, 'Dimon' must be read. The sense is, I will give new causes why that river should be so deservedly called. Vatablus and Forerius explain the additions as concerning new streams, as if to say, 'then the blood of the slaughtered Moabites will flow into the river Dibon in many new streams.' Yet the exposition of Haymo is simpler, concerning the additions of plagues, as if to say, 'I will increase or aggravate their punishments: I will add plague to plague for them, so that they may be more Dimon, or their waters may flow with blood.' TO THOSE WHO SHALL HAVE FLED FROM MOAB AND TO THE REMNANTS OF THE LAND] A transposition. The sense is: 'Upon those of the Moabites who shall have fled from the enemy, or whom the enemy shall have left as survivors, (I will send) a Lion': that is, I will cause them to fall in with wild beasts. See a similar thing at 2 Kings 17, 25. Others rather understand by the lion the Babylonian soldiers, fierce like a lion, and powerful; or the King of Babylon, who, being sent against the Moabites as the most powerful and most ferocious, was to consume and destroy that which had remained from the first devastation. How 1. Chron. 12, 9, it is said of the soldiers of David: 'Their faces were as the faces of a lion', and the Babylonian kingdom is exhibited in the form of a lion at Dan. 7, 4. The first devastation was made by the Assyrians three years after this prophecy was issued, the second by the Babylonians.

CHAPTER

Latin:

Vers. 5. COR MEUM AD MOAB CLAMABIT] Subaudi, dicet quisq. Hoc verbum sæpe reticetur. Ad Moab pro ob Moab.

VECTES EJUS] Significare quidem hoc potest vox Hebraea: sed rectius vertas, & ob principes ejus: argu- mento loci infra 21, 1. Vulgatae ita succurrit Cornelius; Vectes, i. e. fortes ejus, qui suo robore Moab tutabantur, sicuti ve- ctes tutantur portas urbis. Sed itane verba immu- tare decet interpp. è fortibus vel principibus ve- ctes ob aliquam metaphoram efficiendo ? USQUE AD SEGOR] Id est, clamor exaudietur usque ad Segor, qui locus est in Judaeae limite, Gen. 19, 22. VITULAM CONSTERNANTEM] Scripsit inter- pres, ut quidam libri habent, conternantem, id est trimam: τριετὴς apud Graecos. Sed vertendum est, ut junicis trima, supple clamor, ex superiori. PER ASCENSUM ENIM LUITH FLENS A- SCENDET] Egregia allusio: si scandent ad montana, fle- tus simul ascendet. Eadem locutio in re eadem Jeremiae 48, 5. Luith Ptolemaeo est Λύθα. ET IN VIA ORANAIM] Quae descendebatur in humilia: docet id idem Jeremiae locus. Haec est Avara Ptolemaeo. CLAMOREM CONTRITIONIS LEVABUNT] Id est, voce humili lugebunt. Par allusio isti, quae in priore membro. AQUAE ENIM NEMRIM DESERTAE ERUNT] Per aquas pascua aquis adfita intelligit, quae tempore pa- cis erant uberrima. Vide Num. 32, 3. & 36. Jos. 13, 27. QUIA ARUIT HERBA, VIROR OMNIS INTERIIT. Rectius ut Osiander notat, exare- scet igitur foenum, olera flaccescent, denique nihil omnino virebit, i. e. non amplius florebit Respubl. eorum, sed pessum ibit, ac si plantae ac olera, deficiente humore, exareant, & pereant. Vers. 7. SECUNDUM MAGNITUDINEM OPERIS, ET VISITATIO EORUM AD TORRENTEM SALI- CUM DUCENT EOS] Verteris rectius: Praeterea quod reliquum fecit (supple occidio) & opes eorum (Moabitarum) ad torrentem Arabum perferent. Vallis Arabum est via, per quam itur ex Moabitide in Assyriam, ut nos docet Hieronymus. In vallibus autem non desunt torrentes. Vers. 8. USQUE AD GALLIM ULULATUS E- JUS] Vide supra 10, 30. Hic N nomini additum, more Moabitarum & Syrorum. Confer quod supra 4. Falso ergo Vulgatus pro Eglaim posuit Gallim. ET USQUE AD PUTEUM ELIM] Causam no- minis vid. Num. 21, 18. Nam qui דורש Hebraeis, ii Moabitis & Syris אלים. Indicatur omnia ululatibus, fletu & clamoribus Moabitarum repletum iri, qui miserrime passim trucidandi sint. Vers. 9. QUIA AQUAE DIBON REPLETÆ SUNT SANGUINE] Legendum est Dimon ex Hebraeo & Grae- co. Fit autem allusio ad nomen Dimon, quod originem habet à sanguine. Sunt, qui putent inde datum nomen, quod olim caesi ibi sint Moabitae. 2. Reg. 3, 24. 25. PONAM ENIM SUPER DIBON ADDITA- MENTA] Iterum Dimon legendum. Sensus est, novas da- bo causas, cur ita n. erito vocetur is fluvius. Vatablus & Forerius additamenta de novis rivis explicant, q. d. tunc plurimis novisq; rivis defluet sanguis caesorum Moabitarum in flumen Dibon. Simplicior tamen est expositio Haymonis, de addi- tamentis plagarum, q. d. augebo vel aggravabo ipsorum poenas: addam eis plagam ad plagam, ut magis Dimon sint, vel sanguine fluant aquae eorum. HIS QUI FUGERINT DE MOAB LEONEM ET RELIQUIIS TERRAE] Transpositio Sensus est: His Moabitarum, qui fugerint ab hoste, aut quos hostis reliquerit superstites, (immittam) Leonem: id est, efficiam, ut in fe- ras incidant. Simile vide 2. Reg. 17, 25. Alii potius per leonem intelligunt milites Ba- bylonicos feroces instar leonis, & potentes; aut Re- gem Babylonium, qui Moabitis immissus utpote po- tentissimus & ferocissimus, id quod primae devasta- tioni reliquum fuerit, absumere ac perdere de- buit. Quomodo 1. Par. 12, 9. de militibus Davidi- cis dicitur: Facies eorum quasi facies leonis, & re- gnum Babylonium Dan. 7, 4. leonis forma exhibe- tur. Prima vastatio per Assyrios triennio post edi- tum hoc vaticinium facta, Altera per Babylonios.

CAPUT

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI. After the consolation concerning the Davidic leaf, the causes of the punishments of Moab are brought forward: pride and idolatry.

Ver. 1. SEND THE LAMB, O LORD, THE RULER OF THE LAND, FROM THE ROCK OF THE DESERT TO THE MOUNT OF THE DAUGHTER OF SION] In the Hebrew it is only: Send the lamb, ruler of the land. He proceeds to speak to the Moabites, and warns them that the lamb, that is, the lambs which they had formerly paid to David for peace and protection (2 Kings 8:2), and then to the kings of Israel until the times of Ahab (2 Kings 3:4), now that the kingdom of Israel is overthrown, they should pay to the legitimate heir of David, that is, Hezekiah. But you would translate better, 'from the Rock to the desert,' than 'from the Rock of the desert': so that you may understand these things are commanded to all the Moabites, whose borders extended from Petra, possessed by the Edomites, to the desert of the Jordan.

He rightly corrects the Vulgate version from the Hebrew. But he ought to have done that in other places as well: not, however, vice versa, to correct the Hebrew text from the Vulgate. But because the LXX Interpreters agree with the Latin translation, and the Moabites were tributary not to the kings of Judah, but of Israel, and the kingdom of Israel had already been cut off, not a few Christian interpreters—Jerome, Hugo, Lyra, Vatablus, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, and others—accept these things concerning Christ; as if the Prophet were praying that Christ might be sent by God into the world, as the Lamb, the Ruler of the land, who might take away the sins of the world, and rule over the whole world, and thus deliver his own people, from whom he draws his origin, not only the Israelitic, but also the Moabitic, because he was to be born from Ruth the Moabitess, who, born from Petra, a desert city of Arabia, had long ago migrated TO THE MOUNT OF THE DAUGHTER OF SION, that is, into Judea. But the fountains of truth have it otherwise. Whence the explanation of the Hebrews, R. Solomon, and our own B. Brentius, Osiander, the Vinarieans, and others, as well as that of Calvin, Junius, and the rest of the Reformers, which Grotius has followed here, must be entirely subscribed to. Junius renders it thus: Send the lamb of the Ruler of the land, that is, of the King of Judah, who by the right and authority of God was their supreme Lord in Petra as far as the desert, i.e., send from all the borders, which are bounded on the south by the field of the Edomites, and on the north by the desert of the Jordan. For Petra, or Jokteel, was the metropolis of the Edomites (2 Kings 14:7). OTHERWISE IT WILL BE (Moab) like a wandering bird, that is, unless the Moabites obey the house of David, they will be put to flight, etc. B. Bohlius wanted it to be a mockery. Formerly the Moabites used to send to the King of Judah a certain number of rams as a recognition of superiority: now they are warned by this mockery, that they should even send the King himself, the ruler of the land, like a ram, and test whether they can acquire grace in the eyes of their superior!

Latin:

CAPUT XVI. Post folatium de folio Davidico causæ pœnarum Moab adducuntur superbia ac idololatria.

Vers. 1. EMITTE AGNUM DOMINE DOMINA- TOREM DE PETRA DESERTI AD MONTEM FI- LIÆ SION] In Hebræo est tantum: Mittite agnum do- minator terræ. Pergit ad Moabitas loqui, monetque eos, ut agnum, id est, agnos, quos pro tributo Davidi olim pependerant pro pace ac tutela 2. Reg. 8, 2. deinde regibus Israëlis ad Achabi usque tempora 2. Reg. 3 4. nunc ever- so Israëlis regno, pendant legitimo hæredi Davidis, id est, Ezechiæ. Melius autem vertas, de Petra ad deser- tum, quam de Petra deserti: ut intelligas hæc imperari Moabitis omnibus, quorum fines à Petra ab Idumæis pos- sessa ad desertum Jordanis pertingebant.

MErito corrigit Vulgatam versionem ex Ebræo. Sed id in aliis etiam locis facere debuit: non vero vice versa Ebræum textum è Vulgata corri- gere. Quia vero LXX. Interpp. Latinæ translationi consonant, ac Moabitæ non regibus Juda, sed Israël tributarii fuerunt, & Israëlis regnum jam excisum erat, de Christo hæc accipiunt non pauci Interpp. Christiani, Hieronymus, Hugo, Lyranus, Vatablus, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus & alii; quasi opret Pro- pheta, ut Christus à Deo in orbem emittatur, ceu Agnus Dominator terræ, qui tollat peccata mundi, totique orbi dominetur, adeoque liberet populum suum, ex quo originem trahit, non tantum Israëlïticum, sed etiam Moabiticum, quia ex Ruth Moabitide, quæ DE PETRA URBE DESERTA Arabiæ nata, jam olim migravit AD MONTEM FILIÆ SION, id est, in Judæam, nasciturus erat. Sed fon- tes veritatis aliter habent. Unde explicationi E- bræorum R. Salomonis & nostratium B. Brentii, O- siandri, Vinariensium & aliorum, ut & Calvini, Junii ac reliquorum Reformatorum, quam Grotius hic sequutus est, omnino subscribendum. Junius ita reddit: Mittite agnum Dominatoris terræ, id est, Regis Judæ, qui ex jure & autoritate. Dei supremus erat illorum Dominus in Petra ad desertum usque, i. e. universi mittite ex omnibus finibus, qui à meri- die agro Edomeorum, à septentrione deserto Jor- danis terminantur. Fuit enim Petra sive Jokteel Edomæorum metropolis 2. Reg. 14, 7. ALIO QUI ERIT (Moab) quemadmodum avis vaga, id est, ni- si pareant Moabitæ domui Davidis, fugabuntur &c. B. Bohlius volebat esse μυκτηρισμον. Olim mitte- bant Moabitæ ad Regem Juda certum numerum arie- tum pro recognitione superioritatis: jam monentur hoc μυκτηρισμῶ, ut vel ipsum Regem dominatorem terræ ceu arietem mittant & tentent, num gratiam in oculis superioris acquirere possint!

## 16:2
Ver. 2. AND IT SHALL BE LIKE A FUGITIVE BIRD, AND LIKE YOUNG BIRDS FLYING FROM THE NEST: SO SHALL THE DAUGHTERS OF MOAB BE AT THE DESCENTS OF ARNON] It is a metaphorical discourse. For the sense is: just as trees are a refuge for a fugitive bird and for young birds cast out of their nest, so the cities of the Moabites, which are at the fords of Arnon (that is, near to the Israelites, Judg. 11), are a refuge for the Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET ERIT SICUT AVIS FUGIENS, ET PUL- LI DE NIDO AVOLANTES: SIC ERUNT FILIÆ MOAB IN DESCENSU ARNON] Est sermo ἐκπεπτι- κός. Sensus enim est: sicut avi profugæ & pullis è nido suo ejectis arbores sunt pro perfugio. Sic urbes Moabi- tarum, quæ sunt ad vada Arnonis (id est, propinquæ Is- raëlitis, Jud. 11.) Israëlitis sunt pro perfugio.

## 16:3
Ver. 3. TAKE COUNSEL] In the Hebrew: Bring counsel. GATHER A COUNCIL] In the Hebrew: Do judgment. That is, perform for the Israelites what you owe them from the old covenant. MAKE THY SHADOW AS THE NIGHT IN THE MIDST OF THE DAY] In the most grievous heat (that is, in that incursion of Shalmaneser, who struck the Israelites with war before he reached the Moabites), cool them, as if it were night, through which the heat ceases. HIDE THE FUGITIVES, AND THE WANDERERS, DO NOT BETRAY THEM] Let there be a safe refuge for those wretches among you.

Latin:

Vers. 3. INI CONSILIUM] In Hebræo: Adfer con- silium. COGE CONCILIUM] In Hebræo: Fac judicium. id est, præsta Israelitis, quod debes ex fœdere veteri. PONE QUASI NOCTEM UMBRAM TUAM IN MERIDIE] In gravissimo æstu (id est, in illo incur- su Salmanasaris, qui prius Israelitas bello perculit, quam Moabitas attingeret) refrigera eos, tanquam nox esset, per quam cessat æstus. ABSCONDE FVGIENTES, ET VAGOS, NE PRODAS] Sit illis miseris tutus apud vos receptus.

## 16:4
Ver. 4. MY FUGITIVES SHALL DWELL WITH THEE] Dwellers, which the following words also explain. FOR THE DUST IS FINISHED, THE WRETCH IS CONSUMED, HE THAT TRAMPLED THE EARTH HAS FAILED] Translate from the Hebrew, with the past tenses taken in the sense of the future, as is wont to happen, especially in the Prophets: For the oppressor shall be finished, the spoiler shall cease, the trampler shall depart from the earth. That is, if you do what I have now said, God will cause Shalmaneser to depart while you remain untouched.

Latin:

Vers. 4. HABITABVNT APVD TE PROFVGI MEI] Habitantes, quod & sequentia explicant. FINITVS EST ENIM PVLVIS, CONSVMMA- TVS EST MISER, DEFECIT QVI CONCVLCA- BAT TERRAM] Verte ex Hebræo præteritis sumtis in sen- sum futuri, ut fieri solet, in Prophetis maxime: Finiet enim expressor, desinet populator, abibit de terra conculcator. Id ett, si faciatis, quæ jam dixi, Deus efficiet, ut abeat Salmanafar vobis intactis.

## 16:5
Ver. 5. AND A THRONE SHALL BE PREPARED IN MERCY] It shall be established, in the Hebrew. God, because of these works of mercy, will give you a happy state.

AND HE SHALL SIT UPON IT IN TRUTH IN THE TABERNACLE OF DAVID, JUDGING AND SEEKING JUDGMENT, AND SWIFTLY RENDERING WHAT IS JUST] You shall have good judges, and that under the protection of the Davidic house. Just as a tent protects men from the sun, so the later kings of David will defend you.

Some interpret these things concerning Christ. Osiander says: The Prophet now inserts, on account of the Israelitic people, a brief little discourse concerning the kingdom of Christ: As if he were saying: Truly the condition of all kingdoms is miserable and unstable: only the kingdom of the Messiah is truly stable and happy, and therefore it is to be aspired to by all, so that through faith in the Messiah they may be made heavenly citizens of that very kingdom. And a throne shall be prepared in mercy, that is, the Lord will erect a kingdom, the kingdom of Christ, which will be full of divine compassion toward all penitent sinners. What shall I say? It will be a kingdom of grace and immense clemency: not of severity and rigor. And the Messiah shall sit upon the royal throne in truth, i.e., administering the Republic in the tabernacle, or house, of David, out of equity and goodness. For Christ was to arise from the royal family of David. Judging and seeking judgment. i.e., he who is to administer the kingdom most justly: and swiftly rendering what is just, i.e., he will administer most justly to his subjects: he will not keep them in suspense for long: as happens sometimes in certain judgments, where the litigating parties die before they can extort a definitive sentence from the Magistrate. But then Christ most properly administered justice to us in his kingdom, when he delivered us, oppressed by the tyranny of Satan, through his death: and through the preaching of the Gospel absolved all who believe in him from sin and eternal damnation: and denounced eternal destruction to Satan and his members. Brentius had preceded him: You have often boasted, Moab, that you can provide a safe asylum for exiles and those cast out of their regions. Act therefore, receive now the fleeing Israelites, until the spoiler of the people ceases. But who? Will you then defend our exiles, you who cannot defend yourself? Away with that most vain boasting of yours concerning the strengthening of your kingdom. For neither the Moabite Kingdom, nor any other worldly kingdom, is of such power that it can truly defend and protect its subjects and inhabitants, and provide such a hiding place that those who flee to it may be saved from the waster, the predator, and the trampler of the earth. For a kingdom in which men may dwell safe from all afflictions is found in no nation of this earth, but only in the tabernacle of David. For a royal seat or throne shall be prepared or established in the tabernacle, in the family of David, on which throne shall reign a King by far the most just of all.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET PRÆPARABITUR IN MISERICORDIA SOLIUM] Firmabitur, in Hebræo. Deus propter ista misericordiæ opera dabit vobis statum felicem.

ET SEDEBIT SUPER ILLUD IN VERITATE IN TABERNACULO DAVID, JUDICANS ET QUÆ- RENS JUDICIUM, ET VELOCITER REDDENS, QUOD JVSIUM EST] Habebitis bonos Judices, id- que sub tutela domus Davidicæ. Sicut tentorium à Sole protegit homines, sic reges posteri Davidis vos defensa- bunt.

Hæc de Christo interpretantur nonnulli. Osi- ander: Inserit, inquit, Propheta nunc, propter popu- lum Israëliticum brevem conciunculam de regno Christi: Quasi diceret: Profecto misera est, & in- stabilis omnium regnorum conditio: solum Mef- siæ regnum vere stabile est & felix, ideoq; omni- bus eo aspirandum, ut per fidem in Messiam ipsius regni cives cœlestes efficiantur. Et præparabitur in misericordia solium, id est eriget Dominus re- gnum, regnum Christi, quod plenum erit misera- tionis divinæ, erga omnes pœnitentes peccatores. Quid dicam? Erit regnum gratiæ & clementiæ im- mensæ: non severitatis & rigoris. Et sedebit Mef- sias super thronum regium in veritate, i. e. ex æquo & bono administrans Rempublicam in taberna- culo, seu domo David. Oriturus enim erat Chri- stus è familia Regia Davidis. Iudicans & quærens judicium. i. e. justissime administraturus regnum: & velociter reddens, quod justum est, i. e. justissime administrabit, subditis: non diu tenebit eos su- spensos: ut sit interdum in quibusdam judiciis, ubi partes litigantes moriuntur, priusquam definiti- vam sententiam à Magistratu extorquere possint. Tunc autem Christus propriissime in regno suo nobis justitiam administravit, cum nos oppressos Satanæ Tyrannide per mortem suam liberavit: & per Evangelii prædicationem omnes in se creden- tes à peccato & damnatione æterna absolvit: & Satanæ ac membris ipsius æternum exitium de- nunciavit. Præiverat Brentius: Sæpe jactasti Moab, te posse exulibus & ejectis ex suis regionibus tutum a- sylum præbere. Age ergo, excipe nunc fugientes Is- raëlitas, donec cesset expilator populi. Sed qui? Tunc nostros exules defendes, qui teipsum defendere non potes? apage cum tua vanissima ista jactantia de firmatione regni tui. Neq; enim Moabiticum Regnum, neque ullum aliud mundanum regnum tantæ potentiæ est, ut queat subditos & incolas ejus vere defendere, & tueri, ac tale latibulum præbere, ut qui eo confu- giunt, serventur à vastatore, prædatore & conculca- tore terræ. Regnum enim, in quo homines tuti ab omnibus afflictionibus habitent, in nulla gente hujus terræ, sed in solo tabernaculo Davidis invenitur. Præ- parabitur enim seu instituetur solium aut thronus Re- gius, in tabernaculo, in familia Davidis, in quo thro- no regnabit Rex longe omnium justissimus.

## 16:6
Vers. 6. WE HAVE HEARD THE PRIDE OF MOAB] As if the Prophet were saying: we sing to the deaf: in vain do we give them good warnings, they will do nothing less than what is right.

HIS PRIDE, AND HIS ARROGANCE, AND HIS INDIGNATION, MORE THAN HIS STRENGTH] He translates בַּרָיו well. See Job 41, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 6. AUDIVIMUS SUPERBIAM MOAB] Quasi di- cat Propheta: sordis canimus: frustra bona illis monita damus, nihil minus illi facient, quam quod rectum est.

SUPERBIA EJUS, ET ARROGANTIA EJUS, ET INDIGNATIO EJUS, PLUSQUAM FORTITU- DO EJUS] Bene vertit בַּרָיו. Vide Job. 41, 3.

## 16:7
THEREFORE SHALL MOAB HOWL UNTO MOAB] The Moabite shall lament for the Moabite.

TO THOSE WHO REJOICE OVER THE WALLS OF BAKED BRICK SPEAK OF HIS STRIPES] חַרְשֶׂת elsewhere indeed signifies a potsherd: but here the Sun, as appears below 11. We said above 15, 1. You may translate this passage best thus from the Hebrew: Concerning the foundations of Kir-hareseth (the city of the Sun) you shall say: yet they are overturned: that is, we had indeed trusted in those great fortifications: but they could not stand against the Assyrians. See what we shall say on Jeremiah 48, 31.

Latin:

IDCIRCO ULULABIT MOAB AD MOAB] Planget Moabita ob Moabitam.

HIS QUI LÆTANTUR SUPER MUROS CO- CTI LATERIS LOQUIMINI PLAGAS SUAS] חַרְשֶׂת alibi quidem testam significat: at hic Solem, ut apparet infra 11. Diximus supra 15, 1. Vertas hunc locum opti- me sic ex Hebræo: De fundamentis Kircharesetb (oppidi Solis) dicetis: attamen eversa sunt: id est, confisi quidem eramus istis tantis munimentis: sed stare contra Assyrios non potuerunt. Vide, quæ dicemus ad Jeremiam 48, 31.

## 16:8
Vers. 8. SUBURBANA HESEBON] See above 15, 4. ET VINEAM SABAMA DOMINI GENTIUM EXCIDERUNT] Connect this with the preceding: and the vineyard of Sabama: concerning Sabama see Num. 22, 38. By vineyard or vine-plot, he understands the city. DOMINI GENTIUM EXCIDERUNT FLAGELLA EJUS] In the Hebrew: its best plants: that is, its most excellent citizens. AD JAZER PERVENERUNT] See Jos. 21, 37. ERRAVERUNT IN DESERTO] The Moabites will wander in the desert toward the Jordan. PROPAGINES EJUS RELICTÆ SUNT] In the Hebrew: its shoots have been extended: that is, they will have reached far. TRANSIERUNT MARE] Some, out of fear, will even cross the sea, for instance to Cyprus. Vers. 9. ELEALE] Above 15, 4. VOX CALCANTIUM] The roar of those destroying everything. Vers. 10. AUFERETUR LÆTITIA ET EXSULTATIO DE CARMELO] From the fertile field. For that is what כרמל means where it is commonly used. VOCEM CALCANTIUM ABSTULI] For they were accustomed to tread with songs. Vers. 11. QUASI CITHARA] Which does not sound unless struck. AD MURUM COCTI LATERIS] On account of Kir-hareseth, or Kir-heres. Verse 12. AND IT SHALL BE WHEN IT APPEARETH THAT MOAB HATH TAKEN PAINS UPON HIS HIGH PLACES] That is, when the Moabites shall see that they profit nothing by praying much upon the leafy hills. HE SHALL ENTER INTO HIS SANCTUARY] They will wish to go to the common idol of the nation, as if they were more likely to be heard there. AND SHALL NOT PREVAIL] They will not be able to reach that far. Verse 13. THIS IS THE WORD THAT THE LORD HATH SPOKEN CONCERNING MOAB SINCE THAT TIME] That is, what I have said thus far, God had revealed to me long ago without a predetermination of time. Verse 14. AND NOW THE LORD HATH SPOKEN, SAYING] But now He has also signified the time to me. IN THREE YEARS] After three years, from the time this last revelation happened to me. AS THE YEARS OF AN HIRELING] That is, precisely numbered, as is usually done by those who hire out their services, see 21, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SUBURBANA HESEBON] Vide supra 15, 4. ET VINEAM SABAMA DOMINI GENTIUM EXCIDERUNT] Connecte cum superioribus : & vinea Sabama: de Sabama vide Num. 22, 38. Per vineam aut vinetum, civitatem intelligit. DOMINI GENTIUM EXCIDERUNT FLAGELLA EJUS] In Hebræo: optimas plantas ejus: id est, cives præstantissimos. AD JAZER PERVENERUNT] Vide Jos. 21, 37. ERRAVERUNT IN DESERTO] Moabitæ errabunt in deserto ad Jordanem. PROPAGINES EJUS RELICTÆ SUNT] In Hebræo: emissiones ejus extensæ sunt: id est, longe extulabunt. TRANSIERUNT MARE] Quidam præ metu etiam mare trajicient, puta in Cyprum. Vers. 9. ELEALE] Supra 15, 4. VOX CALCANTIUM] Barritus omnia corrumpentium. Vers. 10. AUFERETUR LÆTITIA ET EXSULTATIO DE CARMELO] A campo ubere. Id enim est כרמל ubi communiter sumitur. VOCEM CALCANTIUM ABSTULI] Calcare enim solebant cum canticis. Vers. 11. QUASI CITHARA] Quæ non sonat, nisi percussa. AD MURUM COCTI LATERIS] Ob Kirchareseth, sive Kirchareseh. Vers. 12. ET ERIT CUM APPARUERIT QUOD LABORAVIT MOAB SUPER EXCELSIS SUIS] Id est, cum videbunt Moabitæ se in frondosis collibus multum orando nihil proficere. INGREDIETUR AD SANCTA SUA] Volent ire ad commune Gentis idolum, quasi ibi potius exaudiendi. ET NON VALEBIT] Non poterunt eousque pervenire. Vers. 13. HOC VERBUM, QUOD LOCUTUS EST DOMINUS AD MOAB EX TUNC] Id est, quæ hactenus dixi, sine præfinitione temporis jampridem mihi Deus revelaverat. Vers. 14. ET NUNC LOCUTUS EST DOMINUS, DICENS] Nunc vero etiam tempus mihi significavit. IN TRIBUS ANNIS] Post tres annos, ex quo postrema hæc revelatio mihi contigit. QUASI ANNI MERCENARII] Id est, præcise numerati, ut solet fieri ab his, qui operas locant, infra 21, 16.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

The burden of Damascus, which, together with the kingdom of Syria, must be laid waste, not without the affliction of the Israelites whom it was aiding, so that the Jews, beholding this, might turn themselves to God.

Vers. 1. THE BURDEN OF DAMASCUS] Damascus had been captured by Tiglath-Pileser, 2 Kings 16:9. But it was destroyed by Shalmaneser on account of the alliance which it had made against the Assyrians with the ten tribes. For this reason, the Prophet here joins the evils of Damascus with the evils of the ten tribes, as they have a common cause. If we possessed the histories of Nicolaus of Damascus, all these things would appear clearer than light. Damascus, a metropolis in Syria, Is. 7, Ezek. 27, the destruction of which is predicted here. The cause was cruelty toward the Jews, 2 Kings 8 and 13. The fulfillment, when the King of Assyria devastated Damascus, 2 Kings 16. Vers. 2. THE CITIES OF AROER ARE FORSAKEN] A region of Syria, which is more concisely A῎υειρα in Ptolemy. The cities of the region of Aroer, around Damascus, will also be devastated: they will be for flocks in pastures, and flocks will rest there. AND THE FORTRESS (defense) SHALL CEASE FROM EPHRAIM, from the Israelite kingdom. Vers. 5. AND IT SHALL BE AS ONE GATHERING IN THE HARVEST, THAT WHICH HAD REMAINED] He shall leave nothing of the Israelite people in the land; he shall take them away as diligently as those who glean ears of corn after the harvest. IN THE VALLEY OF REPHAIM] It is a valley fertile in grain near Jerusalem: Jos. 15, 8. Ver. 7. IN THAT DAY SHALL MAN BE INCLINED] Better: let him be inclined: and soon: let them look. So that this also may be a counsel, such as the one above 16, 3.

Others receive it as a promise, not as a counsel. In that day shall a man look to his Maker, and his eyes shall have respect to the Holy One of Israel, and shall not look to the altars (idolatrous), that is, then the Israelites, warned by horrendous divine punishments, will repent, and having abandoned their former idolatry, will worship the true God with legitimate rites: And because after the devastation of the Israelite kingdom very few Israelites from those remnants were converted to God, Brentius understands this prophecy of the preaching of the Gospel, as does Osiander, by which many Israelites were converted to the Holy One in Israel, that is, the Messiah: and thus they wish the Prophet here to console the Israelites, so that they may know that, although they are cast out of the land and are no longer a political people, they nevertheless remain the people of God: and although they do not reach with their bodily life until the advent of Christ in the flesh, nevertheless, if they apply faith to these promises concerning Christ, they obtain true salvation. With this promise, as if interrupted by a parenthesis, the Prophet returns to the description of the destruction of the Israelite kingdom.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII.

Onus Damasci, quod cum regno Syriæ non sine afflictione Israë̈litarum, quibus auxiliabatur, vastari debeat, ut Judæi hoc intuentes ad Deum se convertant.

Vers. 1. ONUS DAMASCI] Capta fuerat Damascus à Theglathphalasaro 2. Reg. 16, 9. Sed excisa fuit à Salmanassaro ob societatem, quam contra Assyrios fecerat cum decem tribubus. Ob id mala Damasci cum malis decem tribuum, ut communem causam habentia, Propheta hic conjungit. Si haberemus historias Nicolai Damasceni, hæc omnia luce clarius apparerent. Damascus Metropolis in Syria, Es. 7. Ezech. 27. cujus destructio hic prædicta. Causa fuit crudelitas in Judæos, 2. Reg. 8. & 13. Complementum, cum Rex Assyr. Damascum vastavit, 2. Reg. 16. Vers. 2. DERELICTÆ CIVITATES AROER] Tractus Syriæ, qui contractius Ptolemæo A῎υειρα. Civitates regionis Aroër, circa Damascum, etiam vastatæ erunt: Gregibus in pascua erunt, & requiescent ibi greges. ET CESSABIT ADJUTORIUM (munitio) AB EPHRAIM, à regno Israëlïtico. Vers. 5. ET ERIT SICUT CONGREGANS IN MESSE, QUOD RESTITERAT] Nihil de populo Israëlïtico in terra relinquet; tam diligenter eos auferet, quam qui post messem spicas legunt. IN VALLE RAPHAIM] Est vallis frumenti ferax apud Hierosolyma: Jos. 15, 8. Vers. 7. IN DIE ILLA INCLINABITUR HOMO] Melius: inclinetur: & mox: respiciant. Ut & hoc consilium sit, quale supra 16, 3.

Ut promissum, non ut consilium accipiunt alii. In die illa respiciet homo ad factorem suum, & oculi e- jus ad sanctum Israël respicient, & non ad altaria (idoloIatrica) id est, tunc Israëlitae admoniti hor- rendis pœnis divinis resipiscent, & omissa priore idololatria colent verum Deum legitimis sacris: Et quia post devastationem regni Israëlrtici paucissi- mi Israëlitae ex illis reliquiis ad Deum conversi sunt, de predicatione Evangelii hoc vaticinium in- telligit Brentius, ut & Osiander, qua multi Israëli- tæ conversi sunt ad Sanctum in Israël, h. e. Mes- siam: adeoque consolari hic volunt Prophetam Is- raëlitas, ut cognoscant, quamvis ejiciantur è terra, ne sint populus Politicus, tamen maneant populus Dei: & quanquam non pertingant corporali sua vita usque ad adventum Christi in carne, tamen, si adhibeant fidem his promissis de Christo, conse- quantur veram Salutem. Hac promissione qua- si per parenthesin intersecta redit Propheta ad de- scriptionem interitus regni Israëlrtici.

## 17:9
Ver. 9. CITIES OF HIS STRENGTH] Of the Syrian Decapolis.

DERELICT AS CAVES AND CORN-FIELDS, WHICH ARE DERELICT.

In Heb. As a forsaken branch, and as a top (of a tree, which still remains) which the enemies have forsaken.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CIVITATES FORTITUDINIS EJUS] Sy- riæ Decapolitanæ.

DERELICTÆ SICUT ANTRA ET SE- GETES, QUÆ DERELICTÆ SUNT.

In Ebr. Quasi derelictus ramus, & quasi cacumen (arboris, quod adhuc superest) quod dereliquerunt hostes.

## 17:10
Vers. 10. THEREFORE YOU SHALL PLANT A FAITHFUL PLANTATION, AND YOU SHALL SOW A STRANGE SHOOT: IN THE DAY OF YOUR PLANTATION YOU SHALL LABOR, AND IN THE MORNING YOUR SEED SHALL FLOURISH, THE HARVEST HAS BEEN TAKEN AWAY IN THE DAY OF INHERITANCE, AND HE SHALL GRIEVE GRIEVOUSLY] You shall arrange these obscure words thus: Therefore (although) you shall have planted an excellent plant, and you shall have grafted foreign shoots onto it: (according to that: Let the grafting come, let branch adopt branch) you shall have labored by day, so that the plant may grow, and in the early morning, so that what is grafted may turn out well, the harvest (for that is what נוד means) shall depart in the day of (hoped-for) possession, and (there shall follow) the pain of desperation. The Greeks, with different points, read כאב אנוש as father of man.

YOU SHALL SOW A STRANGE SHOOT. In the Hebrew: But you shall plant for another, namely, for foreign peoples.

Latin:

Vers. 10. PROPTEREA PLANTABIS PLANTA- TIONEM FIDELEM, ET GERMEN ALIENUm SE- MINABIS: IN DIE PLANTATIONIS TUÆ LABRU. SCA, ET MANE SEMEN TUUM FLOREBIT, AL- LATA EST MESSIS IN DIE HEREDITATIS, ET DOLEBIT GRAVITER] Obscura hæc sic collocabis: Propterea (quamvis) plantaveris plantam egregiam, etiam a- lienos surculos ei inseberis: (juxta illud: Venerit insitio, fac ramum ramus adoptet) de die laboraveris, ut crescat planta, & primo mane, ut quod insitum est bene proveniat, migrabit (id enim est נוד) messis in die (speratæ) possessionis, & (succe- det) dolor desperationis. Græci cum aliis punctis legerunt כאב אנוש ὡς πατὴρ ἀνθρώπε.

GERMEN ALIENUm SEMINABIS. In Ebræo: Sed vites alieno potes, populis sc. ex- traneis.

## 17:11
Vers. 11. WILD GRAPE. In the Hebrew it is: you shall make to grow, as Pagninus and Montanus (as much as is in you) and in the morning your seed shall flourish (more correctly, shall germinate, shall offer good hope of itself;) the harvest has been taken away in the day of inheritance, and he shall grieve grievously: In the Hebrew, a heap of harvest in the day of possession (according to your expectation) but (only from all his labor) a miserable (man shall perceive) pain, as Osiander, or, as Pagninus, desperate pain.

Latin:

Vers. 11. LABRUSCA. In Ebræo est: crescere facies, ut Pagninus & Montanus, (quantum in te est) & mane semen tuum florebit (rectius germinabit, spem bonam de se præbebit;) ablata est messis in die hæreditatis, & dolebit graviter: In Ebr. acervus messis in die posses- sionis (secundum expectationem tuam) sed dolo- rem (tantum ex omni labore suo) miser (percipies) ut Osiander, vel, ut Pagninus, dolor desperatus.

## 17:12
Vers. 12. WOE TO THE MULTITUDE OF MANY PEOPLES] He understands those who had adhered to the Syrians.

He does not pass to Sennacherib, as some wish, but continues to threaten Woe to the Damascenes and the Israelites who conspired against Judah, whose army he compares to the waves of the sea on account of its abundance, force, and roaring.

Latin:

Vers. 12. VÆ MULTITUDINI POPULORUM MUL- TORUM] Eos intelligit, qui Syris adhæserant.

Non transit ad Sennacherib, ut aliqui volunt,sed pergit intentare Væ Damascenis, & Israëlitis, qui contra Judam conspirarunt, quorum exercitum ob copiam, impetum & fremitum comparat flu- ctibus maris.

## 17:13
Vers. 13. AS A WHIRLWIND BEFORE A TEMPEST. In the Hebrew: as a globe before a whirlwind, as Vatablus, which, when it is seized by a whirlwind, is entirely rotated by its force and cast away.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SICUT TURBO CORAM TEM- PESTATE. In Ebræo: sicut globus ante turbinem, uti Va- tablus, qui ubi à turbine corripitur, totus impetu illius rotatur, ac projicitur.

## 17:14
Vers. 14. IN THE TIME OF EVENING, AND BEHOLD TROUBLE: IN THE MORNING, AND IT SHALL NOT SUBSIST] Suddenly fortune shall be changed.

THIS IS THE PORTION OF THOSE WHO HAVE DEVASTATED US, AND THE LOT OF THOSE WHO PLUNDER US] For those Damascene Syrians and their neighbors had always been very hostile to the Jews. See what we have brought forth from Nicolaus of Damascus in the Annotations to book 3 of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN TEMPORE VESPERÆ, ET ECCE TURBATIO: IN MATUTINO, ET NON SUBSI- STET] Subito fortuna mutabitur.

HÆC EST PARS EORUM, QUI VASTAVE- RUNT NOS, ET SORS DIRIPIENTIUM NOS] Syri enim illi Damasceni, eorumque vicini valde semper infesti fuerant Judæis. Vide quæ ex Nicolao Damasceno pro- tulimus in Annotatis ad librum 3. de Veritate Religionis Christianæ.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII.

The grievous affliction of the Ethiopians, with the consolation of the conversion of many to Christ.

Ver. 1.

WOE TO THE LAND WITH THE CYMBAL OF WINGS] In Hebrew: Woe to the land of the shadow of wings: i.e., whose extreme parts are overshadowed by mountains. See Strabo. This prophecy shows that God does not wish to use the work of the Ethiopians against Sennacherib, to whom the Ethiopian had declared war, lest it should be his prey, which God willed to be the Jews'. Hence we learn that the expedition which Tirhakah the king had undertaken into Assyria during the absence of Sennacherib turned out badly, 2 Kings 19:9.

WHICH IS BEYOND THE RIVERS], עבר does not always mean beyond, but often means at. Therefore you may translate correctly: which is at the rivers of Ethiopia: so that this last word may cohere with the word land.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII.

Æthiopum gravis afflictio, cum solatio conver- sionis multorum ad Christum.

Vers. 1.

VÆ TERRÆ CYMBALO ALARUM] In He- bræo : Væ terræ umbræ alarum: i. e. cujus extremæ partes montibus obumbrantur. Vide Strabon. Ostendit hæc Pro- phetia Deum Æthiopum opera uti nolle contra Sennacheri- bum, cui Æthiops bellum indixerat, ne præda illius esset, quam Judæorum esse Deus voluit. Hinc discimus Thara- cæ regi male successisse expeditionem, quam per absen- tiam Sennacheribi in Assyriam susceperat, 2. Reg. 19, 9.

QUÆ EST TRANS FLUMINA],עבר non sem- per trans, sed sæpe ad significat. Vertas ergo recte: quæ est ad flumina Æthiopiæ: ut hæc postrema vox cohæreat cum voce terræ.

## 18:2
Ver. 2.

WHICH SENDETH AMBASSADORS BY THE SEA] By the sea, namely the Arabian, ambassadors, that is, heralds to declare war against Assyria.

AND IN VESSELS OF BULRUSHES UPON THE WATERS] That is, papyrus ships, as Pliny speaks, 6.22. Diodorus Siculus also mentions them in book 1. Add the passage of Lucan produced by us at Exodus 2:2.

GO, YE SWIFT MESSENGERS] The words of the king of the Ethiopians. For angels put messengers.

TO A NATION SCATTERED AND PEELED] Whose great part is occupied in distant expeditions.

TO A TERRIBLE PEOPLE BEYOND WHICH THERE IS NO OTHER] In Hebrew: to a terrible people from itself (that is, from the most ancient time) and thenceforth. For the kingdom of the Assyrians was most ancient and renowned for many victories, but the Ethiopian thought his opportunity had arisen.

TO A NATION EXPECTING AND TRODDEN DOWN] In Hebrew: A nation of line, line, and treading down: that is, a nation which gradually extends the boundaries of its empire, and tramples the conquered with a proud foot. Justin from Trogus at the beginning of his history: Ninus, king of the Assyrians, was the first of all to change the ancient and, as it were, ancestral custom of nations with a new desire for empire. He was the first to bring wars upon his neighbors, and he subdued peoples still unaccustomed to resistance as far as the borders of Libya.

WHOSE RIVERS HAVE SPOILED HIS LAND] 'His' here abounds in the Hebrew manner. The Tigris, a violent river, abrades much from Assyria.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

QUI MITTIT IN MARE LEGATOS] Per ma- re, Arabicum scilicet, legatos, id est, feciales ad bellum indicendum Assyriæ.

ET IN VASIS PAPYRI SUPER AQUAS] Id est, navibus papyraceis, ut Plinius loquitur, 6, 22. Memi- nit earum & Diodorus Siculus 1. Adde Lucani locum pro- ductum nobis ad Exod. 2, 2.

ITE ANGELI VELOCES] Verba regis Æthio- pum. Pro angeli pone nuntii.

AD GENTEM CONVULSAM ET DILACERA- TAM] Cujus magna pars in longinquis expeditionibus occupata est.

AD POPULUM TERRIBILEM POST QUEM NON EST ALIUS] In Hebræo: ad populum terribilem ab ipso (id est, ab antiquissimo tempore) & deinceps. An- tiquissimum enim erat & multis victoriis inclytum regnum Assyriorum, sed Æthiops suam occasionem natam putabat.

AD GENTEM EXSPECTANTEM ET CON- CULCATAM] In Hebræo: Gentem lineæ lineæ & conculca- tionis: id est, Gentem, quæ paulatim protendit imperii sui terminos, & superbo pede victos proterit. Justinus ex Trogo initio historiæ: Primus omnium Ninus rex Assyrio- rum, veterem & quasi avitum gentibus morem nova imperii cupiditate mutavit.
