Hic primus intulit bella finitimis, & ru- des adhuc ad resistendum populos, terminos usque Libyæ per- domuit.

CUJUS DIRIPUERUNT FLUMINA TERRAM EJUS] Ejus hic Hebræo more abundat. Tigris violentum flumen multum abradit ab Assyria.

## 18:3
Verse 3.

ALL INHABITANTS OF THE WORLD, WHO DWELL ON THE EARTH, WHEN THE SIGN IS LIFTED UP ON THE MOUNTAINS YOU SHALL SEE, AND YOU SHALL HEAR THE BLAST OF THE TRUMPET] The words are still the Ethiopian's. Better: when the trumpet shall sound. Where my banners shall be raised on the mountains of Assyria, and my war-trumpet shall sound there, then you shall see and hear great things.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

OMNES HABITATORES ORBIS, QUI MO- RAMINI IN TERRA, CUM ELEVATUM FUERIT SIGNUM IN MONTIBUS VIDEBITIS, ET CLAN- GOREM TUBÆ AUDIETIS] Verba adhuc sunt Æthio- pis. Melius: cum tuba clanget. Ubi mea vexilla in mon- tibus Assyriæ attollentur, meumque ibi classicum sonabit, tunc videbitis & audietis res magnas.

## 18:4
Verse 4.

FOR THUS SAYS THE LORD TO ME] כי here is true: The Prophet opposes the counsels of God to the boasting of the Ethiopian.

I WILL REST AND I WILL CONSIDER IN MY PLACE] I will let him do what he wants: I meanwhile will provide for Judea.

AS THE MIDDAY LIGHT IS CLEAR, AND AS A CLOUD OF DEW IN THE DAY OF HARVEST] You might translate better: As serene heat after rain, and as a dewy cloud in the heat of harvest. For these are greatly desired, heat after a shower, and a shower after heat. Such, he says, will be the protection of God.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QUIA HÆC DICIT DOMINUS AD ME] כי hic est verum: Opponit Propheta Dei consilia jactationi Æthiopis.

QUIESCAM ET CONSIDERABO IN LOCO MEO] Sinam illum agere quæ vult: ego interim Judææ providebo.

SICUT MERIDIANA LUX CLARA EST, ET SICUT NUBES RORIS IN DIE MESSIS] Melius ver- tas: Sicut calor serenus post pluviam, & sicut nubes roscida in æstu messis. Hæc enim valde desiderantur, calor post im- brem, & imber post æstum. Tale futurum dicit Dei præ- sidium.

## 18:5
Verse 5.

FOR BEFORE THE HARVEST IT HAS ALL BLOSSOMED, AND THE IMMATURE GROWTH SHALL GERMINATE, AND ITS TWIGS SHALL BE CUT OFF WITH PRUNING HOOKS, AND WHAT HAS BEEN LEFT SHALL BE HIDDEN AND SHAKEN OFF] Better thus: For before the harvest (that is, the vintage) the bud was as if perfect, (the vine) but when it ripened (there appeared) a sour grape. It was a flower: but the branches are cut off with a sickle: the shoots also are taken away by pruning. These similitudes show that before the time of battle the hopes of the Ethiopians were excellent, but they fell before the event.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ANTE MESSEM ENIM TOTUS EFFLORUIT, ET IMMATURA PROFECTIO GERMINABIT, ET PRÆCIDENTUR RAMUSCULI EJUS FALCIBUS, ET QUÆ DERELICTA FUERINT, ABSCONDEN- TUR ET EXCUTIENTUR] Melius sic: Ante messem e- nim (id est, vindemiam) gemma erat quasi perfecta, (vitis) sed ubi maturuit (apparuit) omphax. Flos (fuit:) sed ab- scinduntur falce palmites: propagines quoque auferuntur am- putando. Hæ similitudines ostendunt ante tempus prælii egregias fuisse spes Æthiopum, sed eas ante eventum con- cidisse.

## 18:6
Verse 6.

AND THEY SHALL BE LEFT TOGETHER TO THE BIRDS OF THE MOUNTAINS] The corpses of the Ethiopians.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET RELINQUENTUR SIMUL AVIBUS MON- TIUM] Cadavera Æthiopum.

## 18:7
AT THAT TIME] While these things are being carried out in Assyria in the absence of Sennacherib.

A GIFT SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE LORD OF HOSTS] A portion of the spoil. Num. 31, 28. 2 Sam. 8, 11.

AND TO A PEOPLE DIVIDED AND TORN APART] The Prophet repeats all the insulting words of the Ethiopian against the Assyrians, approving them as truly spoken, but at the same time signifying that the Ethiopian was unworthy to rejoice in their spoils.

The Prophet had prophesied concerning the calamities of Ethiopia, which Grotius, along with Junius, draws to the expedition of Tirhakah undertaken in the absence of Sennacherib, 2 Kings 19, 9, which turned out badly for him. But here more serious evils, not merely the frustration of a plan, are predicted for Ethiopia. This other part of the prophecy concerning the Ethiopians to be converted to Christ is explained by Osiander, Tirinus, and others. Brentius brings forward a similar explanation concerning the Israelites on Mount Zion, who were to offer gifts, which he indeed calls analogous to faith, yet he seems to prefer that interpretation: namely, that Isaiah teaches that the Egyptian auxiliaries (which Hezekiah had expected from Tirhakah, and which he had promised him through messengers) are to be cast off, just as branches are accustomed to be pruned and thrown away: but that the Lord would so preserve the torn people of Judah without these auxiliaries, that they would again bring their sacrifices to the temple on Mount Zion, in Jerusalem: i.e. that the kingdom of Judah under Hezekiah is to be so restored that a numerous people may dwell in it and follow the true worship of God in Jerusalem. Which was fulfilled after Sennacherib returned, having lost his army from the slaughter of the angel, to his Nineveh. Brentius protests that he brings forward this twofold interpretation, not because he feels that one passage of Scripture has diverse senses and is like a wax nose, as the Allegorists feel about Scripture; but because partly the phraseology of Scripture is not as well understood by us as our own vernacular language, and partly the historical events of those times, during which Isaiah preached these things, are not all as diligently written down and propagated to us as the knowledge of them is necessary for us to understand his prophecies. This had to be noted here on account of those who even today attempt to introduce diverse senses of Scripture. The former sense B. Luther in his Commentary on this passage follows concerning the remnants of the Ethiopian people to be converted to Christ. If anyone desires a paraphrase and explanation of the whole chapter, let him consult here primarily Osiander, Cornelius à Lapide, and Tirinus. He predicts a slaughter for the Ethiopians, which was indeed begun by Sennacherib, but completed by Nebuchadnezzar. Therefore, in verse 5, what is said to be LEFT BY THE ASSYRIANS under tribute, the Prophet later denounces as TO BE CUT DOWN AND CAST OUT into a foreign land by Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldeans. But he promises conversion to the Ethiopian descendants, such promises as he subjoins to most threats.

Latin:

IN TEMPORE ILLO] Dum ista in Assyria absen- te Sennacheribo gerentur.

DEFERETUR MUNUS DOMINO EXERCI- TUUM] Pars de præda. Num. 31, 28. 2. Sam. 8, 11.

ET POPULO DIVULSO ET DILACERATO] Repetit Propheta omnia contumeliosa verba Æthiopis in Assyrios, approbans ea ut vere dicta, sed simul significans Æthiopem indignum fuisse, qui illorum spoliis gauderet.

De calamitatibus Æthiopiæ vaticinatus erat Propheta, quod Grotius cum Junio ad expeditio- nem Tharaci absente Sennacheribo susceptam tra- hit 2. Reg. 19, 9. quod male eidem cesserit. Sed hic graviora mala, non frustratio tantum consilii, præ- dicuntur Æthiopiæ. Hæc vero altera pars vatici- nii de convertendis ad Christum Æthiopibus ab O- siandro, Tirino & aliis explicatur. Brentius adfert similem explicationem de Israëlitis in monte Zion, munera oblaturis, quam quidem fidei analogam dicit, illam tamen interpretationem præferre vi- detur: quod nempe Esaias doceat, auxilia Ægyptia- ca, (quæ à Tharacon expectarit Ezechias, & illi per nuncios promiserit) disjicienda esse, sicut præcidi & abjici solent palmites: Dominum autem sine his au- xiliis ita conservaturum populum Judæ dilaniatum, ut iterum afferant sua sacrificia ad templum in mon- te Sion, in Jerusalem: h. e. regnum Judæ sub E- zechia ita restaurandum esse, ut populus frequens in eo habitet, & sequatur verum cultum Dei in Hierusalem. Quod impletum est, postquam San- herib reversus est amisso exercitu ex angeli clade ad suam Niniven. Geminam autem hanc interpre- tationem se afferre Brentius protestatur, non quod sentiat, unum locum Scripturæ habere diversos sen- sus, & esse velut cereum nasum, quemadmodum sentiunt de Scriptura Allegoristæ; Sed quia partim phrasis Scripturæ non tam perspecta nobis, quam est vernacula nostra lingua, partim res gestæ eorum tem- porum, quibus hæc Esaias concionatus est, non sunt o- mnes tam diligenter perscriptæ & ad nos propagatæ, quam necessaria nobis earum est cognitio ad intelligen- da ejusdem vaticinia. Quod ob eos, qui hodieque diversos sensus Scripturæ invehere conantur, hic monendum erat. Priorem sensum B. Lutherus in Comment. ad h. l. sequitur de populi Æthiopici re- liquiis ad Christum convertendis. Capitis totius para- phrasin & explicationem si quis desiderat, con- sulat hic cumprimis Osiandrum, Cornelium à Lapi- de, & Tirinum. Cladem prædicit Æthiopibus, quæ inchoata quidem à Sennacheribo, sed completa a Nebucadnezare. Ideo vers. 5. QUÆ AB ASSY- RIIS DERELICTA dicuntur sub tributo, postea à Nebuchodonosore & Chaldæis ABSCINDEN- DA ET EXCUTIENDA in alienam terram denunciat Propheta. Sed posteris Æthiopicis promittit conversionem, quales promissiones ple- risque comminationibus subjungit.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX.

The burden of Egypt with the consolation that many of them are to be converted, and an altar is to be erected to the Lord in the midst of Egypt, and that they themselves, together with the Assyrians and Israelites, are to receive the blessing of the Lord.

Vers. 1. THE BURDEN OF EGYPT] This prophecy pertains to almost the same times as the former ones. For, as we learn from Herodotus' Euterpe, Sethon, a priest of Vulcan, was king of Egypt, contemporary with Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, for Sennacherib also waged war against Sethon. After Sethon died, Egypt was divided into twelve kings, of whom Psammitichus was one: he, having been relegated to the marshes by the Egyptians, having gathered a faction and being aided by the help of the Ionians and Carians, who had infested the sea, conquered and killed the other eleven kings. To him, however, succeeded in the kingdom that Necho who made war on Josiah, as the Chronicles and Zechariah record.

HE SHALL ASCEND UPON A SWIFT CLOUD] The descent of the Lord signifies benefits elsewhere, but often, as here, the judgments of God.

THE IDOLS OF EGYPT SHALL BE MOVED] The deities worshipped by the Egyptians at that time were Vulcan, Latona, Osiris, Isis, Horus, Bubastis, and Apis, as we learn from Herodotus. Against all of them, says the Prophet, there will be no power to protect Egypt against the judgments of God.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX.

Onus Ægypticum solatio, quod ex iis multi convertendi, & altare in medio Ægypti Domino erigendum sit, eique ipsi cum Assy- riis & Israëlitis benedictionem Domini percepturi sint.

Vers. 1. ONUS ÆGYPTI] Vaticinium hoc ad ea- dem ferme tempora pertinet ad quæ priora. Nam, ut ex Herodoti Euterpe discimus, Sennacheribo Assyriorum regi coævus fuit Sethon Vulcani sacerdos rex Ægypti, nam & bel- lum Sethoni intulit Sennacheribus. Sethone mortuo di- visa est Ægyptus in reges duodecim, quorum fuit Psammi- tichus: is in paludes ab Ægyptiis relegatus, collecta factio- ne, & Jonum ac Carum, qui mare infestum habuerant, ope adjutus, undecim reges alios vicit atque interfecit. Huic autem in regnum successit is Nechos, qui Josiæ bellum fe- cit, memorantibus Paralipomenis & Zacharia.

ASCENDET SUPER NUBEM LEVEM] Domi- ni descensus alibi beneficia, sæpe, ut hic, judicia Dei signi- ficat.

COMMOVEBUNTUR SIMULACHRA ÆGT- PTI] Numina Ægyptiis culta eo tempore erant Vulcanus, Latona, Osiris, Isis, Orus, Bubastis, Apis, ut ex Herodo- to discimus. Illis omnibus, inquit Propheta, nulla vis erit ad tutandam Ægyptum contra Dei judicia.

## 19:2
Ver. 2. I WILL SET THE EGYPTIANS AGAINST THE EGYPTIANS] In that war of Psammetichus.

KINGDOM AGAINST KINGDOM] That is, as the Greeks rightly interpret it, νόμος ἐπὶ νόμον.

Latin:

Vers. 2. CONCURRERE FACIAM ÆGYPTIOS ADVERSUS ÆGYPTIOS] Bello illo Psammetichi.

REGNUM ADVERSUS REGNUM] Id est, ut Græci recte interpretantur, νόμ@ ἐπὶ νόμον.

## 19:3
AND THE SPIRIT OF EGYPT SHALL FAIL IN THE MIDST THEREOF] In the Hebrew it is, shall be exhausted: they will have no spirit, and therefore (as follows) they will be destitute of counsel.

Latin:

ET DIRUMPETUR SPIRITUS ÆGYPTI IN VISCERIBUS EJUS] In Hebræo est, deficiet: nihil illis erit animi, ac propterea (ut sequitur) consilii erunt inopes.

## 19:4
Ver. 4. AND A FIERCE KING SHALL RULE OVER THEM] Psammetichus.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET REX FORTIS DOMINABITUR EO- RUM] Psammitichus.

## 19:5
Ver. 5. AND THE WATERS SHALL FAIL FROM THE SEA] All these things are figurative. The situation will be such as if there were no water in the sea, because trade will fail on account of those pirates, the Carians and Ionians. Thus Herodotus. Strabo interprets the Ionians as Milesians, by whom he says the Milesian wall, Naucratis, and Schedia were founded in the times of Psammetichus.

AND THE RIVER SHALL BE WASTED AND DRIED UP] All parts of the Nile and other smaller rivers will cease to be navigable.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET ARESCAT AQUA DE MARI] Hæc o- mnia sunt figurata. Res ita se habebit, quasi nulla esset aqua in mari, quia commercia deficient per piratas illos Caras & Jonas. Ita Herodotus. Strabo Jonas interpre- tatur Milesios, à quibus conditum ait murum Milesio- sum, Naucratim & Schediam Psammitichi tempori- bus.

ET FLUVIUS DESOLABITUR ATQUE SIC- CABITUR] Omnes Nili partes aliaque flumina minora navigari desinent.

## 19:6
Ver. 6. AND THE RIVERS SHALL BE WASTED] Here in the Hebrew word והאזניחו the Aleph is redundant.

THE REEDS AND FLAGS SHALL WITHER] The reeds and papyri, from which ships used to be built, will be useless. See what is above at 18, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET DEFICIENT FLUMINA] Hic in verbo Hebræo והאזניחו abundat Aleph.

CALAMUS ET JUNCUS MARCESCENT] In- utiles erunt arundines & papyri, unde naves strui solebant. Vide quæ supra 18, 1.

## 19:11
Ver. 11. THE PRINCES OF ZOAN ARE FOOLS] This was a most ancient city of Egypt. Num. 13, 23. How from צען was made Τάνις, we have said at Matt. 1, 21.

HOW SAY YE UNTO PHARAOH] To that king who held the Tanitic Nome.

THE SON OF ANCIENT KINGS] For many Egyptian priests traced their lineage back to ancient kings.

Latin:

Vers. 11. STULTI PRINCIPES TANEOS] Urbs erat hæc Ægypti antiquissima. Num. 13, 23. quomodo ex צען factum sit Τάνις, diximus ad Matth. 1, 21.

QUOMODO DICETIS PHARAONI] Illi regi qui Taniticum Nomum tenebat.

FILIUS REGUM ANTIQUORUM] Multi enim sacerdotes Ægyptii ad reges antiquos genus suum refere- bant.

## 19:13
Vers. 13. THE PRINCES OF MEMPHIS HAVE BECOME WEAK] It is here in Hebrew נף, but it is written more correctly in Hosea 9:6 as מף. Thus the mountain attached to it is μώφι in Herodotus, Euterpe. It is common, however, for those nations to interpose the letter נ in the middle of a word, which, when followed by a consonant, the Greeks turn into μ. Thus from מף was made Μέμφις.

THEY HAVE DECEIVED EGYPT, THE CORNER OF ITS PEOPLES] For patach I would think there was here a Holem, פנת שבטיה, that is, the excellent ones of the tribes, as in Judges 20:2. Therefore פנת is the same as שרי.

Latin:

Vers. 13. EMARCUERUNT PRINCIPES MEM- PHEOS] Est hic in Hebræo נף, sed rectius scribitur O- sez 9, 6. מף. Sic mons ei adfitus μώφι Herodoto, Eu- terpe. Frequens autem illis gentibus in media voce נ interponere, quam sequente consona Græci in μ vertunt Ita ex מף facta Μέμφις.

DECEPERUNT ÆGYPTUM ANGULUM PO- PULORUM EJUS] Pro patach putem hic fuisse Holem, פנת שבטיה, id est, eximii tribuum, ut Jud. 20, 2. Ergo פנת idem quod שרי.

## 19:14
Vers. 14. THE LORD HAS MIXED IN THE MIDST OF IT A SPIRIT OF GIDDINESS] Namely, so that those eleven kings might consult nothing in common, but while they fight individually, they might all be conquered.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DOMINUS MISCUIT IN MEDIO EJUS SPIRITUM VERTIGINIS] Nempe ut undecim illi reges nihil in commune consulerent, sed dum pugnant singuli, vincerentur universi.

## 19:15
Vers. 15. AND THERE SHALL BE NO WORK FOR THE EGYPTIAN, WHICH THE HEAD AND TAIL, THE BRANCH AND THE RUSH, MAY DO] Translate: There shall be no office in Egypt which the head or tail, the branch or the rush, may perform. No one will perform an office, not the senator, not the priest, not the old man, not the youth. We have had and explained the same figure of speech in 9:14.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET NON ERIT ÆGYPTIO OPUS, QUOD FACIAT CAPUT ET CAUDAM INCURVANTEM ET REFRÆNANTEM] Verte: Non erit in Ægypto offi- cium, quod faciant caput aut cauda, ramus aut juncus. Ne- mo officium faciet, non senator, non sacerdos, non se- nex, non juvenis. Idem loquendi genus habuimus & ex- plicavimus 9, 14.

## 19:17
Vers. 17. AND THE LAND OF JUDAH SHALL BE A TERROR TO EGYPT] When they understand how Sennacherib invaded Judea, the Egyptians also will fear for themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET ERIT TERRA JUDA ÆGYPTO IN PAVOREM] Cum intelligent, quomodo Judæam inva- serit Sennacheribus, Ægyptii quoque sibi metuent.

## 19:18
Vers. 18. IN THAT DAY THERE SHALL BE FIVE CITIES IN THE LAND OF EGYPT SPEAKING THE LANGUAGE OF CANAAN] That is, Hebrew, which Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had learned while they lived in Canaan. The Phoenician or Canaanite and Hebrew language is the same, or certainly only slightly different. See what we have brought forward from Choerilus, Plautus, and Lucian to the first book on the Truth of the Christian Religion, where we deal with letters. When Sennacherib first invaded Judea, with Psammetichus, as it seems, reigning over Egypt, many Jews retreated into Egypt; this appears above in 11:11, 15. And there, worshipping the true GOD as is fitting, they gave an example to many Egyptians, having abandoned their idols, to worship the same God, which by the mercy of God was for the salvation of all Egypt. Josephus refers these things to times a thousand years later than this prophecy. But the whole context shows that this is to be referred to the same times of which he has treated thus far. However, there lies hidden in this prophecy, through a more sublime sense, the calling of the Gentiles through the Gospel.

AND SWEARING BY THE LORD OF HOSTS] Just as the law commands in Exodus 23:13, Deuteronomy 6:13, 10:20.

ONE SHALL BE CALLED THE CITY OF THE SUN] Heliopolis to the Greeks. An ancient city. See Josephus, Antiquities 2, 3.

He says this also, that in the very city which had long been the chief seat of idolatry, the Jews would live according to their own laws.

Latin:

Vers. 18. IN DIE ILLA ERUNT QUINQUE CI- VITATES IN TERRA ÆGYPTI LOQUENTES LIN- GUA CANAAN] Id est, Hebræa, quam Abrahamus, Isaacus, & Jacobus addidicerant, dum in Cananæa vive- bant. Eadem lingua Phœnissa, sive Cananæa & Hebræa, aut certa paululum diversa. Vide quæ ex Chœrilo, Plau- to, Luciano attulimus ad librum primum de Verit. Relig. Christian. ubi de literis agimus. Cum Sennacheribus Ju- dæam primum invasit, Psammeticho, ut videtur, per Æ- gyptum regnante, multi Judæi se recepere in Ægyptum; apparet id supra 11, 11. 15. atque ibi verum DEUM, ut oportet, colentes, multis Ægyptiis exemplum dedere de- relictis idolis, eundem Deum colendi, quod per Dei mise- ricordiam toti Ægypto saluti fuit. Josephus hæc refert ad tempora mille annis posteriora hoc vaticinio. Sed con- textus totus ostendit hoc ad eadem tempora, de quibus egit hactenus, referendum. Latet autem in hoc vaticinio per sensum sublimiorem vocatio gentium per Evange- lium.

ET JURANTES PER DOMINUM EXERCI- TUUM] Ita ut lex præcipit Exod. 23, 13. Deuter. 6, 13. 10, 20.

CIVITAS SOLIS VOCATUR UNA] Heliopo- lis Græcis. Urbs antiqua. Vide Josephum Originum 2, 3.

Hoc dicit etiam in ipsa urbe, quæ præcipua Idololatriæ se- des jampridem erat, Judæos victuros ex suis legibus.

## 19:19
Vers. 19. IN THAT DAY THERE SHALL BE AN ALTAR TO THE LORD IN THE MIDST OF THE LAND OF EGYPT] Namely, for a memorial, not for sacrifices. Compare Joshua 22:22, 23, 24, 25, 26.

AND A PILLAR TO THE LORD NEAR ITS BORDER] Columns on which the name of God will be inscribed.

This oracle does not intend, regarding the literal sense, to be understood concerning the time of the New Testament, although it concedes that in a more sublime sense the calling of the Gentiles also lies hidden here. But that διττότης (duplicity) of sense is by no means to be admitted. And it is too manifest that the conversion of the Egyptians is predicted here; nor is there reason for Grotius to urge the series and order of times. For the order of times is not always observed in these prophecies, which Grotius himself confessed above at chapter 14, 28, noting thus: There is another prophecy not coherent with the previous one: nor is it new for the Prophets to depart from threats looking to ancient times to promises concerning the times of the New Testament. It is too meager for so magnificent a promise, what Grotius brings forward concerning some Egyptians, who, having abandoned their idols, were converted to God in the time of Sennacherib: For the Prophet does not prophesy about a few, but about five entire cities, with a certain number put for an uncertain one, so that he may designate the multitude of those to be converted. Or by the five primary cities, or metropolises, enumerated in Ezekiel 29, Tanim, Memphis, Alexandria, Bubastis, and Heliopolis, the whole of Egypt may be designated. But then the Egyptians speak the language of Canaan, when they invoke and celebrate the true God with the same language with which the faithful Israelites in the land of promise confess Him, and they conform their language and confession to the language and confession of the Jewish Church: or when they speak Christianly, as in the Old Testament the Patriarchs and other faithful ones spoke, and in the New Testament the Apostles and those who believed through them. For the idiom of the language is not viewed materially, but formally, that is, regarding the sense, which regarding the mysteries of the faith is the same in both places, Acts 15:10, Hebrews 13:8. But specifically the Prophet prophesies about the city of Heliopolis, not that the Jews will live there by their own laws, as Grotius perverts it, but that it itself, even though it was a chief seat of idolatry (which, by the testimony of Strabo, was a city of priests), is to be converted to the true God: as if to say, Even that city, which was entirely idolatrous, will worship the true God with the others: and so it will be called one of those five cities; Furthermore, that there will be an altar of the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, does not pertain to a memorial, which is again a 5ρεβλότης (distortion) of Grotius, but to sacrifices, truly spiritual, not corporal, namely that in the midst of the kingdom true divine worship ought to flourish, just as it flourished in Judea, when sacrifices were offered to the altars of the Lord in Jerusalem according to the law of God. For the worship of the New Testament is accustomed to be described by the words of the Old Testament. Blessed Luther on this passage says of the altar, that it is in the midst of Egypt, and at the borders of Egypt. It cannot therefore be understood of a corporal altar, but it signifies that Christ will be worshipped everywhere, and that the word will be preached everywhere. This is our only altar, upon which praise and confession are sacrificed to God, for the grace exhibited through Him. In addition, the Prophet teaches that the title of the Lord will be near the border of Egypt: namely, that it would come to pass that not only in the midst of the kingdom, but even to the furthest borders, the name and memory of the Lord would be celebrated. For by columns erected here and there bearing the title of the Lord, or sacred monuments, the memory of the Lord being propagated through the kingdom is designated. Which were completed when the Christian religion was planted and disseminated in Egypt by Saint Mark and others. For frequent and illustrious were the Churches

Christians in Egypt, the Ecclesiastical History testifies. Which opinion the other things, which Isaiah sets forth at greater length, also clearly confirm. For they speak most openly concerning the conversion of the Egyptians, not of some, but that the whole kingdom is to be illuminated by the light of the Gospel, and to be led to the end of Christ. Let Cyril be compared, who observes here that the Prophet predicted particular things in detail concerning the language of the Canaanites, and he illustrates that which is held concerning the altar of the Lord and Zion thus; For all the land of the Egyptians abounds with shrines, and is full of altars: everywhere there were libations, and sacrifices offered, both to the elements of the world, and also, as I have said, to the images which were placed in the shrines, and they were pillars of demons. But why do I say this, when they even attributed to these the glory which is fitting for God, with the forms of animals lacking reason erected? See therefore, from what things Egyptian affairs have been converted and collapsed. For those who were once more superstitious than all others, and rushed forward with unbridled loose reins: In that day, he says, that is, from that time when the saving preaching shall shine upon them, they will embrace the worship of the natural and true God. For there shall be an altar to the Lord in the region of the Egyptians. This speech has great emphasis and force, being spoken not without admiration. For is it not alien to opinion and faith, and clearly a paradox, that an altar of the Lord should be seen even in the very region of the Egyptians, and furthermore even a pillar at its borders to the Lord? He says a pillar here, as it seems to me, either a holy temple, i.e., the Church, which perhaps was the first of others raised at its borders: or the sign of the holy cross, by which believers are accustomed to be surrounded and fortified. For we always use this thing, when we overturn every assault of the Devil, and break the attacks of demons. For the cross is an unbroken wall for us, and in it is the glorying that truly brings salvation. Therefore the wise Paul writes: But far be it that I should glory, except in the cross of Christ.

Latin:

Verf. 19. IN DIE ILLA ERIT ALTARE DOMINI IN MEDIO TERRÆ ÆGYPTI] Nempe ad memo- riam, non ad sacrificia. Confer Jos. 22, 22. 23. 24. 25. 26.

ET TITULUS DOMINI JUXTA TERMINUM EJUS] Columnæ in quibus inscriptum erit nomen Dei.

Non vult hoc oraculum quoad sensum literalem intellectum de Tempore N. Testamenti, quam- vis concedat sensu sublimiori etiam hic latere vo- cationem gentium. Sed διττότης illa sensus nul- latenus admittenda est. Et manifestum nimis est, hic prædici Ægyptiorum conversionem; neque est, ut seriem & ordinem temporum urgeat Grot. Nam neq; semper ordo temporum in his vaticiniis observatus est, quod supra fassus est ipse Grotius ad cap. 14, 28. ita annotans: Est alia Prophetia cum su- periori non cohærens: neque novum est à commina- tionibus ad antiqua tempora spectantibus discedere Prophetas ad promissiones Novi Testamenti tempora concernentes. Nimis exile est ad tam magnificam promissionem, quod affert Grotius de Ægyptiis nonnullis, derelictis idolis, tempore Sennacheribi ad Deum conversis: Nam non de paucis vaticinatur Propheta, sed de integris quinque Civitatibus, nu- mero certo pro incerto posito, ut multitudinem convertendorum designet. Vel per quinque civi- tates primarias, seu metropoles, Ezech. 29. enu- meratas, Tanim, Memphim, Alexandriam, Buba- stum & Heliopolin universa Ægyptus designetur. Tum autem loquuntur lingua Canaan Ægyptii, cum eadem lingua, qua fideles Israëlitæ in terra promis- sionis verum Deum confitentur, invocant, ac ce- lebrant, & linguam ac confessionem suam linguæ ac confessioni Ecclesiæ Judaicæ conformant: vel cum Christiane loquuntur, ut in Vet. Testamento Patriarchæ aliique fideles, in N. Testam. Apostoli, & qui per eos crediderunt, loquuti sunt. Non enim idioma linguæ materialiter spectatur, sed formali- ter, h. e. quoad sensum, qui quoad mysteria fidei idem est utrobique Actor. 15, 10. Ebr. 13, 8. Specia- tim vero vaticinatur Propheta de civitate Helio- poli, non quod in illa Judæi victuri sint legibus suis, ut pervertit Grotius, sed quod ipsa, etsi præ- cipua idololatriæ sedes fuerit, (quæ Strabone teste, Sacerdotum erat civitas,) ad verum Deum conver- tenda sit: q. d. Etiam illa civitas, quæ tota erat ido- lolatrica, cum cæteris verum Deum colet: adeoque vocabitur una ex istis quinque Civitatibus; Porro quod in medio terræ Ægypti altare Domini futurum sit, non ad memoriam, quæ iterum Grotii 5ρεβλότης est, sed ad sacrificia, verum spiritualia, non corpo- ralia pertinet, quod nempe in medio regno verus cultus divinus vigere debeat, quemadmodum vi- guit in Judæa, cum ad altaria Domini Hierosoly- mis oblata sunt juxta legem Dei sacrificia. Solet enim verbis V. Testamenti cultus N. Testamenti describi. B. Lutherus in h. l. Dicit de altari, quod sit in medio Ægypti, & in finibus Ægypti. Non potest ergo intelligi de corporali ara, sed significat, quod Chri- stus ubique coletur, & quod ubique verbum prædica- bitur. Hic est unica nostra ara, super quam sacrifi- cantur Deo laus & confessio, pro exhibita per ipsum gratia. Adhæc docet Propheta, quod titulus Do- mini juxta terminum Ægypti futurus: nimirum fo- re, ut non in medio tantum regni, sed ad extremos usque terminos nomen & memoria Domini cele- bretur. Per columnas enim passim erectas titulum Domini gerentes vel monumenta sacra memoria Domini per regnum propaganda designatur. Quæ completa sunt, cum à S. Marco aliisque in Ægy- pto Christiana religio plantata & disseminata est. Frequentes enim & illustres fuisse Ecclesias

Christianas in Ægypto, Historia Ecclesiastica testa- tur. Quam sententiam etiam cætera, quæ exequi- tur prolixius Esaias, luculenter confirmant. Aper- tissime enim de conversione Ægyptiorum loquun- tur, non quorundam, sed qua totum regnum Ev- angelii luce collustrandum, & ad finem Christi per- ducendum sit. Conferatur Cyrillus, qui hic Prophe- tam sigillatim particularia prædixisse observat de lingua Chananæorum, & quod id de altari Domi- ni & Sion habeatur, ita illustrat; Terra enim omnis Ægyptiorum, phanis abundat, & aris plena est: pas- sim liba erant, & sacrificationes, tum mundi elemen- tis, tum etiam ut dixi imaginibus, quæ in phanis col- locabantur, oblatæ, & dæmoniorum erant columnæ. At quid hoc dico, cum etiam animantium ratione ca- rentium erectis formis gloriam, quæ Deo congruit, his attribuerint? Vide itaq;, ex quibus Ægyptiacæ res conversæ & collapsæ sunt. Qui enim quondam aliis omnibus superstitiosiores fuerunt, & effrenate laxis habenis proruerunt: Illa, inquit, die, id est, ex eo tempore, quo salutaris prædicatio his illucescescet, cul- tum naturalis & veri Dei complectentur. Erit enim altare Domino in regione Aegyptiorum. Emphasin magnam & vim habet hæc Oratio, quippe non sine admiratione dicta. Annon enim est ab opinione ac fi- de alienum, & plane paradoxum etiam in ipsa regio- ne Aegyptiorum altare Domini videri, & adhæc et- iam columnam ad confinia ejus Domino? Columnam vero hic dicit, ut mihi videtur, vel templum sanctum, h. e. Ecclesiam, quæ forte prima aliarum ad confi- nia ejus excitata est: vel sanctæ crucis signum, quo obsepiri credentes solent & communiri. Uti enim semper sumus hac re, cum omnem Diabolum insul- tum evertimus, & dæmonum impetus infringimus. Mu- rus enim infractus est nobis crux, & in ea est gloriatio vere salutem afferens. Idcirco Paulus sapiens scri- bit: Absit vero, ut ego glorier, nisi in cruce Christi.

## 19:20
Vers. eod. FOR THEY SHALL CRY TO THE LORD IN THE FACE OF THE OPPRESSOR] The Jews shall cry to God, while Sennacherib shall occupy their land. AND HE SHALL SEND THEM A SAVIOR AND A DEFENDER, WHO SHALL DELIVER THEM] An angel, who destroyed the army of Sennacherib. AND THE LORD SHALL BE KNOWN BY EGYPT] By such a miracle many of the Egyptians shall convert themselves to the true God. AND THEY SHALL WORSHIP HIM WITH SACRIFICES AND OFFERINGS] Just as Naaman the Syrian 2 Kings 5, 17.

Latin:

Vers. eod. CLAMABUNT ENIM AD DOMINUM IN FA- CIE TRIBULANTIS] Judæi ad Deum clamabunt, dum terram eorum insidebit Sennacheribus. ET MITTET EIS SALVATOREM AC PRO- PUGNATOREM, QUI LIBERET EOS] Angelum, qui Sennacheribi exercitum confecit. ET COGNOSCETUR DOMINUS AB ÆGT- PTO] Tanto miraculo multi Ægyptiorum ad Deum ve- rum se convertent. ET COLENT EUM IN HOSTIIS ET MUNE- RIBUS] Ita ut Syrus Naaman 2. Reg. 5, 17.

## 19:22
Vers. 22. AND THE LORD SHALL STRIKE EGYPT WITH A PLAGUE, AND SHALL HEAL IT] A Hebrew idiom, for which it may be permitted to say: And the Lord shall heal Egypt from the plague with which he had struck it, that is, from civil wars.

A mere private interpretation. In the text there is nothing about the Israelites. That subject is intruded into the text by Grotius, of which there is no trace in it. There is also nothing about Sennacherib or the striking angel. The Egyptians are said to be about to cry to the Lord: because the discourse is about converted Egyptians: who will send them a Savior and a defender. By which name others with Cyril and Jerome understand Christ the Savior: others indeed any deliverer whatsoever. For Christ, constituted Savior by the Father, as often as he is present as a helper to his own, is rightly said to be sent by the Father, so that thus the name of the Lord may be more and more celebrated and glorified through Egypt. What is added: AND THE LORD SHALL STRIKE EGYPT WITH A PLAGUE, AND SHALL HEAL IT, is not to be understood of liberation from civil wars, as Grotius wishes, but of any calamities whatsoever, because the Lord is about to act with the Egyptians in a fatherly manner, to chastise them, and to heal them from the plague by the cross. B. Luther: They shall cry to the Lord. Not only will doctrine be there and abundance of the word, but there will be prayer also, the other part of divine worship, so that the Spirit of grace and of supplications may be joined. Because the word follows the cross, therefore there is need of prayer. And it shall be for a sign and a testimony. He says this by comparison against the Jews, that altar will not be for a rite or for pomp, as among the Jews, but for a sign and a testimony, that is, for teaching the Word. This is the unique worship of the New Testament which we perform to God, that we preach the benefit of God exhibited to us sinners in Christ. Thus with one word he abolishes all that pomp of sacrifices and offerings of the Old Testament. And he shall send them a Master a deliverer, that is, he will give them Teachers, who can save and teach them by the word. And they shall worship him with sacrifices. He said before an altar constituted for teaching, not for sacrificing; Therefore, the things which he says here about sacrifices are to be interpreted from the preceding. Therefore these things are to be accepted concerning spiritual sacrifices and offerings, just as Paul teaches Rom. 12. Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, etc. They shall make vows. The vows of Christians are to give thanks, to bless, to praise God. Nor do Christians only understand these things of the time of the New Testament; the Jews themselves acknowledge that they pertain to the Messiah. Concerning which Jerome lib. 5. Explan. in Ep. ad h. l. In that day there shall be an altar: From this place to the end of the Egyptian vision or burden, both the Jews and our own wish it to be understood of the coming of Christ: But they defer their vows to the future, we hold them as already accomplished. But take day for time: although Josephus contends that these things were done under Onias: who, a fugitive into Egypt, with a very great crowd of Jews built a temple and an altar, and attempted with rashness to fulfill the prophecy of Christ. And thus one altar is spoken of, in the way that there is one faith, and one baptism, and one Church. And the title near its border of the Lord: there is no doubt but that it signifies the Gospel and the writings of the Apostles. For just as above according to the tropological understanding the land of Judah is understood as the old Testament, formidable or solemn to Egypt: so also the title in the borders of Egypt is demonstrated as the history of the Gospels. Finally he joins: And it shall be for a sign and for a testimony, namely of the Lord's passion. Then those who have believed, with Egyptians rushing against Egyptians, and man fighting against his brother: and city fighting against city: when the time of persecution has rushed in, they will implore the mercy of the Lord, and immediately the Savior will arrive, that is, Jesus: for this is what it sounds like in our language, and the Lord will be known by the Egyptians: and they will know him, whether the persecutors, who have been overcome: or the believers, liberated by his present aid: And they will worship him with sacrifices and gifts: and they will vow vows to the Lord and pay them. Let the Jews answer: It is commanded by the Law that an altar should not be made, except in one place, which the Lord God has chosen: and sacrifices are only to be immolated by priests of the Levitical line: Behold, Isaiah openly teaches that the Egyptians will know the Lord, and worship him: and offer sacrifices and gifts, and vow and pay vows. If the Egyptians have a priesthood, the testimony of Paul is fulfilled in them also, saying: By the translation of the priesthood, it is necessary that a translation of the law should take place. Grotius also acknowledged, when he had not yet been demented by the more recent Jews, in book 5 of On the Truth of the Christian Religion, § 8, that this prophecy pertains to the time of the New Testament. Nor, he says, are prophecies lacking, which predicted that those sacrifices, about which there is controversy, would cease: which anyone will easily understand, who only considers that according to the law of Moses, sacrificing was granted only to the posterity of Aaron, and that only in the native land. Now indeed in Psalm 110, according to the Hebrew numbering, a king is promised who would rule most widely, with the beginning of his reign made from Zion, which king would also be a priest forever, and that after the manner of

of Melchizedek. But Isaiah, chapter 19, says that an altar will be seen in Egypt, where not only the Egyptians, but also the Assyrians and Israelites will worship God. This confession, proper to the man, is deservedly opposed to his Judaizing glosses.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET PERCUTIET DOMINUS ÆGYPTUM PLAGA, ET SANABIT EAM] Hebræa locutio, pro quo dicere liceat: Et sanabit Dominus Ægyptum a plaga, qua eam percusserat, id est, a bellis civilibus.

Mere ἰδία Ἐπίλυσις. In textu nihil de Israëllitis. Subjectum illud intruditur textui a Grotio, cujus nullum in eo vestigium. Nihil etiam de Sennache- ribo aut angelo percussore. Clamaturi dicuntur Aeg y- ptii ad Dominum: quia de conversis Aegyptiis ser- mo est: qui illis Salvatorem ac propugnatorem mittet. Quo nomine alii cum Cyrillo & Hieronymo Christum Salvatorem intelligunt: alii vero liberato- rem quemcunq;, alium. Christus enim a Patre consti- tutus Salvator, quoties suis opitulator adest, a Patre mitti recte dicitur, ut ita magis magisque nomen Domini celebretur & glorificetur per Ægyptum. Quod additur: ET PERCUTIET DOMINUS ÆGYPTUM PLAGA, ET SANABIT EAM, non de liberatione a bellis civilibus, uti vult Gro- tius, sed de quibuscunq;, calamitatibus intelligen- dum, quod Dominus paterno more cum Ægy- ptiis acturus, eosdem castigaturus, & a cruce ad plaga sanaturus sit. B. Lutherus: Clamabunt ad Dominum. Non solum doctrina ibi erit & abundan- tia verbi, sed erit oratio quoque, altera pars cultus di- vini, ut sint conjuncti Spiritus gratiæ & precum. Quia verbum crux sequitur, ideo oratione opus est. Et erit signum & testimonium. Dicit hoc per compa- rationem contra Judæos, non erit altare illud in ritum aut in pompam, sicut apud Judæos, sed in signum & testimonium, id est, ad docendum Verbum. Hic est unicus cultus Novi Testam. quem Deo præstamus, quod prædicamus beneficium Dei in Christo nobis pec- catoribus exhibitum. Sic uno verbo omnem illam pompam sacrificiorum & hostiarum V. T. abolet. Et mittet eis Magistrum liberatorem, id est, dabit eis Doctores, qui possint eos verbo salvare & docere. Et colent eum in hostiis. Dixit ante constitutam aram ad docendum, non ad sacrificandum; Sunt igitur, quæ hic de hostiis dicit, ex superioribus interpretanda. Accipienda ergò hæc sunt de hostiis & sacrificiis spiri- tualibus, sicut Paulus docet Rom. 12. Exhibite cor- pora vestra hostiam viventem sanctam, compla- centem Deo &c. Vota vovebunt. Vota Christiano- rum sunt, gratias agere, benedicere, laudare Deum. Neq; tantum Christiani hæc de tempore N. T. in- telligunt; Judæi ipsi agnoscunt, ea ad Messiam spe- ctare. Quo de Hieron. lib. 5. Explan. in Ep. ad h. l. In die illa erit altare : Ab hoc loco usq́, ad finem Ægy- ptiæ visionis sive ponderis, & Judæi & nostri de Chri- sti adventu intelligi volunt : Sed illi vota sua differunt in futurum, nos quasi jam transacta retinemus. Diem autem pro tempore accipe : quanquam sub Onia Jose- phus hæc facta contendat : qui profugus in Ægyptum, cum turba plurima Judæorum ædificavit templum & altare, & Prophetiam Christicassa implere temerita- te conatus est. Ita autem unum altare dicitur, quo- modo una fides, & unum baptisma, & una Ecclesia. Et titulus juxta terminum ejus Domini : haud du- bium quin Evangelium & Apostolorum scripta signifi- cet. Quomodo enim supra juxta Tropologicam in- telligentiam terra Juda Ægypto formidabilis sive so- lennis vetus intelligitur Testamentum : sic & titulus in terminis Ægypti, Evangeliorum historia demon- stratur. Denique jungit : Et erit in signum & in te- stimonium, dominicæ videlicet passionis. Tunc hi, qui crediderunt, concurrentibus Ægyptiis contra Æ- gyptios, & pugnante viro contra fratrem suum : & civitate contra civitatem dimicante: cum persecu- tionis tempus irruerit, implorabunt domini misericor- diam, statimque Salvator adveniet, id est, Jesus : hoc enim in lingua nostra sonat, & cognoscetur Do- minus ab Ægyptiis : & cognoscent eum, sive per- secutores, qui fuerint superati : sive credentes præsen- ti auxilio liberati : Et colent eum in hostiis & mune- ribus : votaque vovebunt Domino & solvent. Re- spondeant Judæi : Lege præceptum est, ut altare non fiat, nisi in loco uno, quem elegerit Dominus Deus : & hostiæ tantum à Sacerdotibus Levitici generis im- molentur : Ecce Esaias aperte docet, quod Ægyptii cognoscant Dominum, & colant eum: & hostias & munera offerant, & vota voveant atq́, persolvant. Si Ægyptii Sacerdotium habent, impletur & in illis Pauli testimonium dicentis : Translatione Sacerdotii necesse est, ut legis translatio fiat. Agnovit & Gro- tius, quum nondum à Judæis recentioribus de- mentatus esset, libr. 5. de Verit. Rel. Christ. §. 8. hoc vaticinium ad tempus N. T. pertinere. Neǵ; vaticinia, inquit, desunt, quæ sacrificia illa, de qui- bus controversia est, desitura prædixerint : quod faci- le quivis intelliget, qui modo considerarit secundum Mosis legem sacrificare soli Aaronis posteritati concessum, idque duntaxat in solo patrio. Jam vero Psalmo 110. secundum numerum Hebræum, promittitur rex latissime dominaturus initio re- gnandi facto ex Sione, qui rex idem & sa- cerdos in perpetuum futurus esset, idque instar

Melchisedeci. Esaias vero cap. 19. dicit, altare visum iri in Ægypto, ubi non tantum Ægyptii, sed Assyrii quoque & Israelitæ Deum sint culturi. Quæ confes- sio viri propria glossis ejus Judaizantibus merito opponitur.

## 19:23
Verse 23.

IN THAT DAY THERE SHALL BE A HIGHWAY OUT OF EGYPT TO ASSYRIA, AND THE ASSYRIAN SHALL COME INTO EGYPT, AND THE EGYPTIAN INTO ASSYRIA] That is, with Psammetichus now fully reigning, there will be deep peace and commerce between the Assyrians and the Egyptians, who had long been enemies to one another.

AND THE EGYPTIANS SHALL SERVE THE ASSYRIAN] That is, they will courteously observe the majesty of the King of Assyria.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

IN DIE ILLA ERIT VIA DE ÆGYPTO IN ASSYRIOS, ET INTRABIT ASSYRIUS ÆGYPTUM ET ÆGYPTIUS IN ASSYRIOS] Id est, Psammeticho jam plene regnante alta pax erit, & commercia inter Assy- rios & Ægyptios, qui diu hostes inter se fuerant.

ET SERVIENT ÆGYPTII ASSUR] Id est, co- miter majestatem Regis Assyrii observabunt.

## 19:24
Verse 24. IN THAT DAY SHALL ISRAEL BE THE THIRD WITH EGYPT AND WITH ASSYRIA] That is, he will be allied to both. This lasted through the times of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 20:19.

A BLESSING IN THE MIDST OF THE LAND] Peace and uncorrupted happiness.

Latin:

Vers. 24. IN DIE ILLA ERIT ISRAEL TERTIUS ÆGYPTO ET ASSYRIO] Id est, utrique erit fœdera- tus. Id duravit per tempora Ezechiæ, 2. Reg. 20, 19.

BENEDICTIO IN MEDIO TERRÆ] Pax & fe- licitas incorrupta.

## 19:25
BLESSED BE EGYPT MY PEOPLE] My people, he says, because of the many pious ones who were in Egypt at that time.

AND ASSYRIA THE WORK OF MY HANDS] Or rather, the Assyrian, whom, he says, I use as I wish, just as a potter uses his pottery work.

BUT ISRAEL MY INHERITANCE] A people peculiar to me.

This is not about political peace, but an evangelical prophecy is continued; and thus spiritual peace is promised between the Egyptians and the Assyrians; who, once enemies to each other, will be most closely joined in faith and will show mutual services to one another. The Egyptians serving the Assyrians is to be taken in a good sense, as Jerome suggests. For the Apostle also serves believers, that he may gain them. And Esau is subjected to his brother Jacob, so that he may become a participant in his blessing. Therefore, those who are the first of the nations to be saved, and have in themselves the altar of the Lord, will save those who persist in hardness by their own service, and by their mixing and association, they themselves will go to the Assyrians, so that they may lead the Assyrians to Egypt, and afterwards be able to reach the Israelite people. For this reason, I think, even a faithful woman serves an unbelieving husband, so that little by little she may draw him from Egypt and Assyria to Judea. IN THAT DAY SHALL ISRAEL BE THE THIRD WITH EGYPT AND WITH ASSYRIA. Grotius again understands this as a political alliance, that he will be allied to both; which he thinks was fulfilled in the time of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 20:19. But these things treat of a mystical union and concord, that out of these three one people is to be, who will be gathered into one Church. And therefore a blessing is promised in the midst of the land: with which the Lord is about to bless, and is about to give true happiness, which ought to have reached all the peoples of the earth in the seed of Abraham, the Messiah, saying: Blessed be Egypt my people: and (blessed be) Assyria the work of my hands and Israel my inheritance (blessed be). This naming and communion of spiritual blessing abundantly teaches that spiritual unity and concord are predicted here. For the discourse is about that which is proper to the people of God, the work of the hands of the Lord, and the inheritance of God, about that communion which the Israelites are to have among themselves, as the inheritance of the Lord, the Egyptians as the people of God, and the Assyrians as the work of the hands of the Lord or the new creatures of God, Psalm 95:7, Isaiah 51:16, Ephesians 2:10, which is joined with the communion of spiritual blessing in Christ, proper to the people of God, the work of the hands of the Lord, and the inheritance of God. That this is spiritual unity, concord, and peace is certain. Jerome on this passage, p. 64: In that day shall Israel be, etc. Israel will by no means be crushed in the middle between Egypt and Assyria, now with Antiochus and Demetrius drawing the kingdom to themselves, now with the Ptolemies claiming its possession for themselves: But even it, established under the Roman empire, and through this the empire of Christ, will be of that condition of which Egypt and

Assyrians: and he shall be blessed in all the earth: For out of Sion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem: Then it shall be said by the Lord: Blessed be my people of Egypt: when by no means Moses, but Christ the Lord going before, infinite thousands of men shall have filled the solitudes: and Pharaoh being drowned, they shall have said in the desert: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea. Then also the work of the hands of the Lord shall be in the Assyrians: for these nations especially flourish with swarms of monks, Egypt and Mesopotamia: and they contend with equal piety among themselves: But the inheritance of Christ is Israel: i.e. the places of his birth, and cross, and resurrection, and ascension, to which there is a running together from the whole world. Thus far Jerome. So also Justin Dial. with Trypho page 276. And through Isaiah he speaks thus concerning another Israel: In that day shall there be a third Israel in the Assyrians and Egyptians, blessed in the land, which the Lord of Hosts hath blessed, saying: blessed be my people, which is in Egypt, and which is in the Assyrians, and my inheritance in Israel. Since therefore God blesses, and calls this people Israel, and proclaims them to be his inheritance; why do you not repent, with which you deceive yourselves, as if you alone were Israel: then you curse the blessed with dire execrations. The sum therefore of this promise Brentius has rightly expressed: The Gospel of Christ shall not be preached only in Egypt, but also in Assyria, among all nations. There shall be a way from Egypt into the Assyrians, etc. and soon: Israel shall be the third to Egypt and the Assyrian, i.e. Although in these times the Ishmaelites, Egyptians and Assyrians differ among themselves in regions, customs, minds, and religion, yet after the Gospel concerning Christ shall have been revealed, there shall be one religion of the Israelites, Egyptians and Assyrians. And out of these nations there shall be one Church of Christ: The Lord shall say: Blessed be my people of Egypt. Blessed be Assur the work of my hands. Blessed be Israel my inheritance, i.e. the Egyptians, Assyrians, and Ishmaelites shall acknowledge Jesus Christ, the true seed of Abraham, in whom I promised the blessing. Why therefore in turn shall I not acknowledge all these nations for my people, and pour out upon them all my blessing because of Jesus Christ, my son. And B. Luther: It is a promise concerning the Gospel. And therefore there shall be Christians in Assyria, and in Egypt there shall be unity of faith, and there shall be a third Israel: And the text is most clear, that Israel shall be made equal to the nations and the Nations to Israel. All interpreters agree. Christians. Grotius alone with the Jews wishes to interpret the prophecy in a literal sense concerning bodily goods.

Latin:

BENEDICTUS POPULUS MEUS ÆGYPTI] Po- pulus meus, dicit propter multos pios, qui tunc in Ægy- pto fuere.

ET OPUS MANUUM MEARUM ASSYRIA] Imo Assyrius, quo, inquit, ego utor ut volo, sicut figulus ope- re figulino.

HÆREDITAS AUTEM MEA ISRAEL] Popu- lus mihi peculiaris.

Non hic de pace Politica agitur, sed continuatur vaticinium Evangelicum: adeoque pax Spiritualis inter Aegyptios & Assyriacos promittitur; qui o- lim inter se hostes, futuri sunt in fide conjunctis- simi mutuaque ministeria sibi invicem exhibitus ri. Servire Ægyptios Assyriis in bonam partem, inferente Hieronymo, accipiendum est. Servit enim & Apostolus credentibus, ut lucri eos faciat. Et Esau subjicitur fratri suo Jacob, ut particeps fiat be- nedictionem ejus. Igitur qui priores de gentibus sal- vati fuerint, & habuerint in se altare Domini, eos qui in duritia perseverant, sua servitute salvabunt, & commixtione ac societate eorum, ipsi pergent ad Assyrios, ut Assyrios ducant ad Ægyptum, & postea possint ad Israeliticum populum pervenire. Ob hanc causam reor, & fidelem mulierem servire viro infide- li, ut paulatim eum de Ægypto & Assyria pertra- bat ad Judæam. IN DIE ILLA ERIT ISRAEL TERTIUS ÆGYPTO ET ASSYRIO. Quod iterum de foedere Politico intelligit Grotius, utri- que erit fœderatus; quod tempore Ezechiæ imple- tum putat 2. Reg. 20, 19. Sed hæc de unione & con- cordia mystica agunt, quod ex his tribus unus po- pulus futurus sit, qui in unam colligentur Eccle- siam. Ideoque promittitur benedictio in medio terræ: qua benedicturus Dominus, ac veram fe- licitatem, quæ in semine Abrahæ, Messiæ, omnibus populis terræ obtingere debuit, daturus est, di- cens: Benedictus populus meus Ægypti: & (bene- dictum sit) opus manuum mearum Assyrii & hæredi- tas mea Israël (benedicta sit.) Quæ nuncupatio & benedictionis spiritualis communio abunde do- cet, spiritualem unitatem & concordiam hic præ- dici. De ea enim sermo est, quæ populo Dei, ope- ri manuum Domini, & hæreditati Dei propria est, de ea communione, quam inter se habituri sunt Israë- litæ, ut hæreditas Domini, Ægyptii ut populus Dei, & Assyrii ut opus manuum Domini vel novæ crea- turæ Dei, Psal. 95, 7. Esa. 51, 16. Ephes. 2, 10. quæ cum spiritualis benedictionis in Christo commu- nione, populo Dei, operi manuum Domini, & hæ- reditati Dei propria, conjuncta est. Quam esse spiritualem unitatem, Concordiam & pacem cer- tum est. Hieronymus ad h. l. p. 64. In die illa erit Israël, &c. Nequaquam Israël inter Ægyptum & Assyrium medius elidetur: nunc Antiochus & De- metriis ad se Judæ trahentibus regnum, nunc Pto- lemæis possessionem ejus sibi vendicantibus: Sed & ipsa sub Romano imperio, ac per hoc Christi imperio constituta, erit ejus conditionis, cujus & Ægyptus &

Affyriis: & benedicetur in omni terra: Quia ex Sion exibit lex, & verbum Domini de Hierusa- lem: Tunc dicetur à Domino: Benedictus popu- lus meus Ægypti: quando nequaquam Moyse, sed Christo Domino præeunte, infinita hominum millia solitudines repleverint: & Pharaone submerso, di- xerint in deserto: Cantemus Domino, gloriosè enim magnificatus est, equum & ascensorem de- jecit in mare. Tunc & opus manuum Domini e- rit in Assyriis: hæ enim vel maxime gentes monacho- rum florent examinibus, Ægyptus & Mesopotamia: & pari inter se pietate contendunt: Hæreditas au- tem Christi Israël est: h. e. nativitatis, & crucis, & resurrectionis, ascensionisq́, ejus loca, ad quæ de toto orbe concurritur. Hactenus Hieronymus. Sic etiam Justinus Dial. cum Tryphone pag. 276. Et per E- saiam de alio Israële ita loquitur: Die illo erit ter- tius Israël in Assyriis & Ægyptiis, benedictus in terra, quam benedixit Dominus Zebaoth, dicens: benedictus sit populus meus, qui est in Ægypto, & qui est in Assyriis, & hæreditas mea in Israël. Cum ergo Deus benedicat, & Israëlem vocet populum istum, & hæreditatem suam esse clamitet; cur pœ- nitentiam non agitis, quocum vos ipsos seducitis, ve- luti soli Israël sitis: tum benedictum diris execrami- ni. Summam ergo promissionis hujus rectè ex- pressit Brentius: Evangelium Christi non prædica- bitur tantum in Ægypto, sed etiam in Assyria, inter omnes gentes. Erit via de Ægypto in Assyrios, &c. & mox: Israël erit tertius Ægypto & Assyrio, h.e. Etsi his temporibus Ismaëlitæ, Ægyptii & Assyrii dis- sident inter se regionibus, moribus, animis, & reli- gione, tamen postquam revelatum fuerit Evangelion de Christo, una erit religio Israelitarum, Ægy- ptiorum & Assyriorum. Et ex his gentibus una erit Ecclesia Christi: Dicet Dominus: Benedictus po- pulus meus Ægypti. Benedictus Assur opus ma- nuum mearum. Benedictus Israël hæreditas mea, h. e. Ægyptii, Assyrii, & Ismaelitæ agnoscent Jesum Christum, verum semen Abrahæ, in quo promisi be- nedictionem. Quare ergo vicissim agnoscam omnes has gentes pro meo populo, & effundam in eas omnem meam benedictionem propter Jesum Christum, filium meum. Et B. Lutherus: Est promissio de Evange- lio. Ideoque erunt Christiani in Assyria, & in Ægy- pto erit unitas fidei, & erit Israel tertius: Et apertis- simus textus, quod Israel æquabitur gentibus & Gen- tes Israel. Consentiunt omnes interpp. Christiani. Solus Grotius cum Judæis literali sensu vaticinium vult agere de bonis corporalibus.

## 20:1 Argument
CHAPTER XX. Isaiah predicts that the Assyrians would lead the Egyptians and Ethiopians into captivity, both by the sign of being unshod, and by word.

Vers. 1.

IN THE YEAR, IN WHICH THARTHAN ENTERED] This is the same one who is named in 2 Kings 18:17. Sennacherib had sent him before him.

WHEN SARGON KING OF THE ASSYRIANS HAD SENT HIM] The same as Sennacherib. For those Kings were accustomed to have several names, which casts much darkness upon history.

AND HAD FOUGHT AGAINST AZOTUS, AND HAD TAKEN IT] As being of the dominion of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:8.

Others observe from Herodotus that Azotus, which was one of the chief cities of the Philistines, then held the Egyptians, who affirms that it was taken by Psammetichus the Egyptian King. Which the Assyrians afterwards in turn snatched away from the Egyptians. Which is predicted here.

The Prophet prophesies against the Egyptians and Ethiopians, so that the Jews, upon the arrival of Sennacherib, might not flee to their aid as was their custom, but rather place their hope in God. Although, therefore, Sennacherib came directly only against Judah in his own person, 2 Kings 18, he came concomitantly also against the neighbors, whence, remaining himself in Judea, he sent Tartan into Ashdod with a part of his forces. Verse 2. LOOSE THE SACKCLOTH FROM THY LOINS] A shaggy prophetic garment. See what is said at Matthew 3:4. Indeed, that the Prophet walked completely naked is more correctly observed by Ambrose in Psalm 39, Jerome, Cyril, Haymo, and others from verse 4; and because he is said to be made into a portent, some say that the nakedness of Christ on the cross was prefigured in him, which was full and complete to expiate the concupiscence of Adam, as Athanasius and Ambrose hand down. See Suarez, Part 3, Question 46, Article 8, Section 4. Although this manner of walking may seem foul to reason, nothing, however, is more honorable than the precepts of God, as Jerome warns. The laying aside of the prophetic garment would have neither argued against the Prophet nor been a portent. But the Nudipedal heretics, who imitate this according to Augustine in De Haeresibus 128, are foolish, because this was done not as an example, but as a portent and a sign. NAKED] Clad in an undergarment; see Mark 14:52, John 21:7. Now, those who were led away as captives were accustomed to behave in such a way, their better garment having been stripped off by the victors. Verse 3. THE SIGN OF THREE YEARS SHALL BE] That is, the event after three years. Therefore, the war of the Ethiopians against the Assyrians lasted for that much time. Cornelius says that the three-day nakedness of Isaiah refers to the three-year devastation of Egypt and Ethiopia, because it began in the 14th year of Hezekiah, in which the Assyrian went against Tirhakah, King of the Ethiopians, having left Rabshakeh in Judea, 2 Kings 19:9. after three years he returned to Jerusalem, whence he was occupied for three years with the war and devastation of Egypt and Ethiopia; whence Cornelius denies that these things are to be referred to the times of Esarhaddon, son of Sennacherib, as Grotius will now indicate. Pintus wishes that the Prophet walked naked three times, not for three days as Jerome says, much less for three years as Forerius says. Verse 4. SO SHALL THE KING OF ASSYRIA DRIVE] The captives of Egypt, that is, the Egyptians, who had joined themselves to the Ethiopians. The King of Assyria is Esarhaddon, son of Sennacherib. Captivity, that is, captives, he shall drive like cattle and slaves captured by hand in war, whom the victors drive before them like cattle. AND THE TRANSMIGRATION OF ETHIOPIA] The Ethiopians, who had come under Tirhakah as far as Assyria. See above 18. DISCOVERED IN THEIR BUTTOCKS] See 2 Kings 10:4 and above 3:17. Some say, with garments cut up to the buttocks, as 2 Samuel 10:4, it was done: But it is one thing to be cut up, another to be discovered: because the barbarian victors were accustomed to uncover the members which modesty covers, either for mockery or for the lust of the captive enemies. Gons. Jer. 47. Verse 6. AND THE INHABITANT OF THIS ISLE SHALL SAY] That is, of the maritime coast of the Philistines, in which is Ashdod. See Ptolemy. Now, that maritime coasts are called islands by the Hebrews has been noted already several times. TO WHOM WE FLED] Who are those in whom, when we were besieged, we had placed our hope? AND HOW SHALL WE BE ABLE TO ESCAPE?] Better: How could it happen that we might escape? Hezekiah was delivered because he had placed his hope in God. The Philistines were not delivered because they had trusted in human aid, which they experienced to be very vain. Others understand Judea by the Island, because it was situated like an island between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean, and was small in respect to Babylon, which is called the sea, as it was beaten on all sides by the waves and wars of its neighbors like an island, as Jerome explains, because the Jews, who had trusted in the Egyptians and Ethiopians, when they see them captured and devastated so ignominiously, are to be confounded. See Osiander and Cornelius a Lapide, as also Pintus, and likewise Sanctius on this passage.

Latin:

CAPUT XX. Assyrios Ægyptum & Æthiopes in capti- vitatem ducturos, & signo discalceationis, & verbo prædicit Esaias.

Vers. 1.

IN ANNO, QUO INGRESSUS EST THAR- THAN] Hic idem est, qui nominatur 2. Reg. 18, 17. Hunc ante se præmiserat Sennacherib.

CUM MISISSET EUM SARGON REX ASSY- RIORUM] Idem qui Sennacherib. Solebant enim Re- ges illi plura habere nomina, quod multas tenebras offun- dit historiæ.

ET PUGNASSET CONTRA AZOTUM, ET CEPISSET EAM] Ut quæ ditionis esset Ezechiæ, 2. Reg. 18, 8.

Alii Azotum, quæ una fuit ex præcipuis Philisti- norum civitatibus, tum tenuisse Ægyptios ex Hero- doto observant, qui eam à Psammeticho Rege Ægy- ptiaco expugnatam affirmat. Quam postea Assyrii Ægyptiis vicissim eripuêre. Quod hic prædicitur.

Vaticinatur autem Propheta contra Ægyptios & Æthiopes,ne adventante Sennacheribo,ad eorum opem de more confugiant Judæi, sed in Deo spem suam reponant. Etsi ergo directe Sennacherib tan- tum contra Judam venit in persona propria, 2. Reg. 18. concomitanter tamen venit etiam contra vicinos, unde manens ipse in Judæa misit Thartan in Azotum cum parte copiarum. Vers. 2. SOLVE SACCUM DE LUMBIS TUIS] Villofam vestem propheticam. Vide, quæ ad Matth. 3,4. Imo prorsus nudum incessisse Prophetam re- ctius Ambrosius in Psal. 39. Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Haymo, & alii observant e vers. 4. & quia factus di- citur in portentum, & in eo nuditatem Christi in cruce figuratam nonnulli ajunt, quæ plena & o- mnimoda fuit ad expiandum Adæ concupiscen- tiam, ut Athanaf. & Ambrosius tradunt. Vide Sua- retz 3. p. q. 46. art. 8. s. 4. Qui incessus etsi fœdus rationi videatur, nihil tamen honestius est Dei præ- ceptis monente Hieronymo. Depositio vestis Pro- pheticæ nec Prophetam arguiffet, nec portentum fuiffet. Inepti autem sunt Nudipedes hæretici, qui hoc imitantur apud Augustinum de hæref. 128. Quia factum hoc non in exemplum, sed in porten- tum & signum. NUDUS] Interula indutus, vide Marci 14,52. Joh. 21, 7. Solebant autem taliter se habere, qui captivi abdu- cebantur, detracta per victores veste meliore. Vers. 3. TRIUM ANNORUM SIGNUM ERIT] Id est, eventum post annos tres. Tantum igitur temporis duravit bellum Æthiopum in Assyrios. Triduanam nuditatem Esaiæ triennii vastita- tem Ægypti & Æthiopiæ Cornelius ait, quod cepe- rit anno 14. Ezechiæ, quo contra Taracam Regem Æthiopum perrexit Assyrius, relicto in Judæa Rabface, 2. Reg. 19,9. post tres annos Hierosoly- mam reversus, unde bello & vastatione Ægypti & Æthiopiæ distentus per triennium; unde negat Cornel. hæc referenda esse ad tempora Asarhad- don filiiSennacherib,uti jam Grotius indicabit. Ter nudum incessisse Prophetam Pintus vult, non ut Hieron. per triduum,nedum ut Forerius, per trien- nium. Vers. 4. SIC MINABIT REX ASSYRIORUM CA- PTIVITATEM ÆGYPTI] Ægyptiorum, qui Æthiopi se adjunxerint. Rex Assyriorum est Asarhaddon Sennache- ribi filius. Captivitatem, id est captivos, minabit quasi pecora,& mancipia in bello manu capta, quæ ante se minant vectores instar pecorum. ET TRANSMIGRATIONEM ÆTHIOPIÆ] Æ- thiopes, qui sub Tharaca in Assyriam usque venerant, Vi- de supra 18. DISCOOPERTUS NATIBUS] Vide 2. Reg. 10,4. & supra 3, 17. Nonnulli, præsectis vestibus usq; ad nates, ut 2. Sam. 10, 4. factum: Sed aliud est præsectis, aliud discoopertis: quia solebant victores barbari vel ad ludibrium vel ad libidinem hostium captivorum membra,quæ pudor tegit,detegere. Gons. Jer. 47. Vers. 6. ET DICET HABITATOR INSULÆ HU- JUS] Id est, oræ maritimæ Philisthinorum, in qua Azo- tus. Vide Ptolemæum. Oras autem maritimas ab He- bræis insulas vocari, annotatum jam aliquoties. AD QUOS CONFUGIMUS] Qui sunt illi, in qui- bus, cum obsideremur, spem nostram collocaveramus? ET QUOMODO EFFUGERE POTERIMUS NOS?] Melius: Quomodo fieri poterat, ut nos evaderemus? Ezechias liberatus est, quia in Deo spem suam collocaverat. Philisthini non sunt liberati, quia opi humanæ confisi fue- rant, quam perquam inanem experti sunt. Alii per Insulam Judæam intelligunt, quia sita erat insulæ instar inter mare mortuum & mediter- raneum, & parva respectu Babylonis, quæ mare di- citur, ut vicinorum fluctibus ac bellis velut insula undiquaq; tundebatur, ut explicat Hieron.quod Ju- dæi, qui confisi erant Ægyptiis & Æthiopibus,ubi videbunt eos tam ignominiose capi, & vastari, con- fundendi sint. Videat. Ofiand. & Cornel. a Lap. ut & Pintus, nec non Sanctius in h. l.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI. Concerning Babylon to be occupied by the Medes and Persians, the Idumeans to be devastated, the Arabians to be punished.

Verse 1. THE BURDEN OF THE DESERT OF THE SEA] The Prophet, just as he had rebuked those who had placed their hope in Ethiopia and Egypt, so now he turns himself to those who, having followed the side of the Assyrians, had placed their hopes in them, not in God. Now there are three peoples whom he addresses in this chapter: first, the Idumeans, who dwelt in the desert of Shur or Etham, at the very coast of the Arabian Gulf. See Ex. 13:20, 15:22, Num. 33:8, and add what Jerome has concerning this desert in the preface to Amos, and Strabo, book 17. Then the Dumathaeans from Ishmael (see Gen. 25:15). Then the Arabs of Petraea, sprung from Keturah. All these, although related to the Jews through Abraham, nevertheless had joined themselves to the Assyrians against the Jews. Verse 2. AS WHIRLWINDS FROM THE SOUTH COME, IT COMES FROM THE DESERT, FROM A TERRIBLE LAND, A HARD VISION IS ANNOUNCED TO ME] The sense is: Such as the south winds blow suddenly from the desert and horrible places of the Isthmus, such is the thing which has been revealed to me through a vision. HE THAT IS UNBELIEVING, DEALS UNFAITHFULLY, AND HE THAT IS A SPOILER, WASTES] You would rightly translate: The perfidious one [oppresses] the perfidious, the spoiler [oppresses] the spoiler, supply, he will oppress. Namely, the Mede the Assyrian, at which time also Babylon was captured by the Medes. See above 13:17 and what was said there. GO UP, O ELAM] The Elymaeans are contiguous to the Medes. Strabo, book 16. I HAVE MADE ALL THE GROANING THEREOF TO CEASE] Its groaning, namely of the perfidious Assyrian, understand the groaning of him whom he himself was exciting: as the wound slow to Ulysses, which Ulysses had made. Verse 3. THEREFORE ARE MY LOINS FILLED WITH PAIN] He says that those who dwelt in the desert by the sea will use these words. Verse 4. MY HEART HAS WITHERED] I like the distinction which the Latin interpreter has followed here. In the Hebrew: My heart palpitates from horror. DARKNESS HAS ASTONISHED ME] In the Hebrew: The twilight has terrified me: that is, that change of the good fortune of the Assyrians into adversity has struck me vehemently. BABYLON MY BELOVED IS SET FOR ME INTO A WONDER] The interpreter added that word Babylon not badly for the sense. For my beloved, in the Hebrew is שקת of my embrace. For into a wonder, the Hebrew word has into terror. Verse 5. SET THE TABLE, WATCH IN THE WATCHTOWER EATING AND DRINKING: ARISE YE PRINCES, SEIZE THE SHIELD] In the Hebrew: Anoint the shield. Thus in the Miles Gloriosus of Plautus: See that the brightness of my shield be clearer, Than the rays of the sun are wont to be when it is clear, So that, when the need comes to meet in close-packed hand, It may dazzle the sight of the eyes in the battle line of the enemy. The sense here is: While they set the table, (the Babylonians) while the watchman (appointed by them) watches, while they eat, (they) while they drink, arise ye princes, (you Medes) and have your shields anointed. He declares by the imperative what he sees will happen, that the Babylonians, secure in great danger while they are feasting, with the duty of keeping watch delegated to the most worthless men, may be suddenly overwhelmed. Verse 6. GO AND SET A WATCHMAN] Do what they themselves are about to do. Set one of your friends in the watchtower. I will cause him to see those things which will be done, and to announce them to you. Verse 7. AND HE SAW A CHARIOT OF TWO HORSEMEN, A RIDER OF AN ASS, AND A RIDER OF A CAMEL] He saw a chariot (that is, two chariots by a hypallage familiar to those nations) and two drivers, (in each chariot: for one was guiding the chariot, the other the beasts of burden) of which one chariot was carried by mules, (here also the singular is for the plural, and asses are said for mules) the other by camels. The Elymaeans, as also the Persians, used mules: the Medes, as being nearer to the Bactrians, used camels. Through those two chariots, therefore, the watchman placed by Isaiah understood which nations were about to conquer Babylon. Grotius reports these things in his Annotations to chapter 13, regarding the occupation of Babylon made by the Medes after the times of Sennacherib; concerning which there is deep silence in sacred and profane histories. But that they pertain to the occupation of Babylon made in the time of Belshazzar, son of Nebuchadnezzar, the circumstances show: which are here designated prophetically. Some wish it to be called the desert of the sea, because the Euphrates, which flowed through the middle of Babylon, had been so dried up then that the soldiers of Cyrus were able to cross: because the Hebrews are accustomed to call a great abundance of waters a sea. The treacherous man will oppress the treacherous man. For the Persians and Medes were confederated with the Babylonians: but the treacherous oath-breakers oppressed the treacherous man. And here the Lord addresses the Persian and the Mede explicitly: Ascend, O Elam, i.e., you Persian; because Elam is a part of the Persian region; besiege, you Mede, the city of Babylon. He introduces the Babylonian King, how much he was struck with terror and fear. Therefore my loins are filled with pain; and anguish has taken hold of me, like the anguish of a woman in labor. I collapsed when I heard (that the city had been captured) I was entirely troubled when I saw (the enemies already holding the city, whom I had never thought could penetrate into it.) My heart wandered, (I am entirely mindless and astonished from such a great and so unexpected a fall) terror made me tremble. My beloved Babylon is set for me as a wonder. Thus the Vulgate: which Grotius says the word Babylon was not badly added to by the assent, rendering the words from the Hebrew thus: The time of my embrace (or of my desire) has set me in fear. (That night, in which I indulged with my nobles in pleasures and our desires, is turned for me into the greatest terror and most grievous mourning.) Therefore come, says the Prophet, set the table (prepare sumptuous feasts) contemplate (you watchman) on the watchtower, eating, drinking, arise princes, anoint the shields. Grotius renders the sense thus: While they (the Babylonians) set the table, while the watchman (appointed by them) watches, while they eat, while they drink, arise princes (you Medes) and have your shields anointed. He declares by an imperative what he sees will happen, that the Babylonians, secure in great danger, while they themselves are feasting, with the duty of keeping watch delegated to the vilest men, are suddenly oppressed! Others wish the words: arise princes, to be said ironically to the Babylonian revelers: i.e., Arise from the banquet, seize your weapons, if by chance you might still be able to repel the enemy. It is acknowledged that by this vivid description the unforeseen ruin of Babylon is depicted, which happened while they were meanwhile gluttonizing and devoting effort to pleasures in the highest security. That all these things were fulfilled in this way, when the city was captured by Cyrus, is evident from Daniel Chapter V and profane historians. And Grotius himself explains the vision of the two chariots of horsemen, of whom one was carried by mules, the other by camels: the Persians, who used mules, and the Medes who used camels, as being closer to the Bactrians. Therefore, through those two chariots, he understood the watchman to mean which nations were going to storm Babylon. Others understand Cyrus himself the Persian, and Darius the Mede, to be designated by the horsemen in this vision. Most understand the chariot through synecdoche and enallage of number, as referring to a huge number of chariots, and an army fighting from chariots, as was accustomed to be done in ancient times. See Ex. 14, 6. 7. 1 Sam. 13, 5. Is. 36, 9. c. 43, 17. 1 Chron. 20, 6. 7. Ps. 20, 8. Finally, that cry, Babylon has fallen, has fallen, signifies total ruin; which (Babylon) Grotius confesses in the explanation of verse 10 will be to the Mede as that which is trodden by oxen on the threshing floor: which is not read to have been fulfilled at any time, except when the city was stormed by Darius and Cyrus. Moreover, this ruin is predicted here, partly so that the Jews might not perhaps rely on the Babylonians, since Hezekiah trusted much in the King of Babylon, and was showing all his treasures to his envoys: whence the Prophet predicted that they would be taken away by them: and partly so that the faithful might not lose heart in the very power of the Babylonians, because the people of the Lord were to be utterly destroyed, and the kingdom of Christ was never to emerge in it. Therefore he prophesies that Babylon is finally to be overturned; but the kingdom of Christ is to be erected, which will remain eternal. Which is also transferred to the ruin of the mystical Babylon, Rome, of which Babylon was a type, Rev. 14, 8. since that cry is also to be heard concerning that one: That great Babylon has fallen: Which Grotius confesses here in verse 9. The same words, he says, John uses concerning Rome. Since therefore this ruin of Rome is total and final, it appears that the discourse here is also about the total and final ruin of Babylon.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI. De Babylone per Medos & Persas occupanda, Idumæis vastandis, Arabibus puniendis.

Vers. 1. ONUS DESERTI MARIS] Propheta sicut re- prehenderat eos, qui in Æthiope & Ægypto spem suam col- locaverant, ita nunc ad eos se vertit, qui Assyriorum partes secuti, in illis, non in Deo habuerant spes repositas. Sunt autem, quos hoc capite alloquitur, tres populi, primi Idu- mæi, qui habitabant in deserto Sur sive Etham, ad ipsam oram Arabici sinus. Vide Ex. 13, 20. 15, 22. Num. 33, 8. & adde, quæ de hoc deserto habet Hieronymus in præloquio ad Amosum: & Strabonem lib. 17. Deinde Dumathæi ab Ismaële. (vide Gen. 25, 15.) Deinde Arabes Petrææ, orti à Cethura. Hi omnes quanquam per Abrahamum cogna- ti Judæis, tamen Assyriis contra Judæos se addiderant. Vers. 2. SICUT TURBINES AB AFRICO VE- NIUNT, DE DESERTO VENIT, DE TERRA HOR- RIBILI, VISIO DURA NUNTIATA EST MIHI] Sensus est: Quales Austri à desertis & horridis Isthmi lo- cis flant subito, talis res est, quæ mihi per visum revelata est. QUI INCREDULUS EST, INFIDELITER A- GIT, ET QUI DEPOPULATOR EST, VASTAT] Recte verteris: Perfidus perfidum, populator populatorem, sup- ple, opprimet. Nempe Medus Assyrium, quo tempore etiam Babylon à Medis capta est. Vid. supra 13, 17. & quæ ibi dicta. ASCENDE ELAM] Elymæi Medis contigui. Stra- bo lib. 16. OMNEM GEMITUM EJUS CESSARE FECI] Gemitum ejus, nempe perfidi Assyrii, intellige gemitum ejus, quem ipse excitabat: ut vulnere tardus Ulyssi, quod Ulysses fecerat. Vers. 3. PROPTEREA REPLETI SUNT LUMBI MEI DOLORE] His verbis usuros ait illos, qui in deser- to ad mare habitabant. Vers. 4. EMARCUIT COR MEUM] Placet mihi di- stinctio, quam hic secutus est Latinus interpres. In Hebræo: Palpitat cor meum præ horrore. TENEBRÆ STUPEFECERUNT ME] In Hebræo: Terruit me crepusculum: id est, illa mutatio bonæ fortu- næ Assyriorum in adversam vehementer me percelluit. BABYLON DILECTA MEA POSITA EST MIHI IN MIRACULUM] Illud Babylon interpres ad- didit ad sensum non male. Pro dilecta mea in Hebræo est שקת complexus mei. Pro in miraculum vox Hebræa ha- bet in pavorem. Vers. 5. PONE MENSAM, CONTEMPLARE IN SPECULA COMEDENTES ET BIBENTES: SURGI- TE PRINCIPES, ARRIPITE CLYPEUM] In Hebræo: Ungite clypeum. Sic in Plautino Milite: Curate ut splendor meo sit clypeo clarior, Quam Solis radii esse olim, cum sudum est solent, Ut, ubi usus veniat contra conferta manu Oculorum perstringat aciem in acie hostibus. Sensus hic est: Dum ponunt mensam, (Babylonii) dum spe- culator (ab illis constitutus) speculatur, dum comedunt, (illi) dum bibunt, surgite principes, (vos Medi) & clypeos unctos habete. Imperativo enuntiat, quod futurum videt, ut Baby- lonii in magno periculo securi, dum ipsi epulantur, vilissi- mis hominibus delegato excubandi munere, opprimantus subito. Vers. 6. VADE ET PONE SPECULATOREM] Fac, quod ipsi facturi sunt. Pone aliquem amicorum tuorum in specula. Ego faciam ut ea videat, quæ agentur, tibi- que enuntiet. Vers. 7. ET VIDIT CURRUM DUORUM EQUI- TUM, ASCENSOREM ASINI, ET ASCENSOREM CAMELI] Vidit currum (id est, currus duos per ὑπαλλαγὴν satisfamiliarem illis gentibus) & aurigas duos, (in quoque curru: nam alter currum regebat, alter jumenta) quorum currum alter mulis, (hic quoq; singulare est pro plurali, & asini dicuntur pro mulis) alter camelis vectabatur. Elymæi, ut & Persæ, mulis utebantur: Medi, ut Bactris propiores, ca- melis. Per duos ergo illos currus intellexit speculator ab Esaia positus, quæ gentes expugnaturæ essent Babylonem. Refert hæc Grotius Annot. ad cap. 13. ad occu- pationem Babylonis à Medis factam post tempora Sennacheribi; de qua in sacris & prophanis Histo- riis altum est silentium. Pertinere autem ea ad occu- pationem Babylonis factam tempore Balthasaris, filii Nebuchodonosaris, circumstantiæ docent : quæ hic designantur Prophetice. Nonnulli eam deser- tum maris dictum volunt, quod Euphrates, qui per mediam Babylonem fluebat, ita exiccatus tum fue- rit, ut milites Cyri transire potuerint: quia Ebræi magnam aquarum copiam solent mare appellare. Perfidus perfidum opprimet. Fuêre enim Persæ & Medi Babyloniis confœderati: sed fœdifragi perfidi perfidum oppresserunt. Et alloquitur hic Dominus diserte Persam & Medum: Ascende, ô Ælam, i. e. tu Persa; quia Ælam est pars regio- nis Persicæ; obside tu Mede urbem Babylonem. In- troducit Regem Babylonicum, quanto perculsus fuerit terrore ac metu. Propterea repleti sunt lumbi mei dolore; & angustia possedit me, sicut angustia par- turientis. Corrui, cum audirem (captam esse urbem) conturbatus sum totus, cum viderem (hostes jam ur- bem tenere, quos nunquam in eam penetrare pos- se putaram.) Erravit cor meum, (totus amens & attonitus sum è tanto, tamque insperato casu) terror tremere me fecit. Babylon dilecta mea posita est mihi in miraculum.
