O Chitim, (O you mighty hero Alexander the Macedonian King, arise and depart, prepare yourself, that you may take the city of Tyre, and lead its inhabitants away captive) for you must not remain there (at Tyre). But invade the land of the Chaldeans. Mr. Luther: You must also destroy Babylon after Tyre, (which was not a people) which formerly was not as powerful as it is now, but Assur has prepared it (the Assyrians have brought the Chaldean or Babylonian Empire into prominence, and have set it up) for ships (by means of the great river Euphrates) and have erected strong towers therein, and built palaces (it has mighty strong cities in the land of Chaldea or Babel) it is decreed (it is decided concerning them) that it shall be razed. Howl, you ships on the sea (you merchants who have hitherto carried on your trade through shipping, weep for the downfall of the city of Tyre) for your power is destroyed. This interpretation seems sufficiently convenient. For that the discourse here is about Alexander the Great, Osiander also concludes from v. 1 with B. Luther: Howl, ships of the sea; for it is laid waste (namely Tyre, whose burden is proposed here:) from the house, from coming. (so that no habitable houses are left there, nor do merchants gather any longer to carry on trade.) Luther, that there is no house, nor does anyone go there. Grotius renders: the house is laid waste, that is, the entrance of the city. But in the Hebrew it is מבוא from the house, and therefore the already cited version of Luther is to be preferred. From the land of Chitim it is revealed to them. B. Luther: From the land of Chitim (of the Macedonians) they will become aware of it. And in the marginal note: That has done the great Alexander from Macedonia.

For so very long before, Isaiah saw such things. For כִּתִּים is Macedonia, as Jer. 2. v. 9. Pass over to the isles of Macedonia, and 1. Macc. 1. * Μακέδονα ὃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς γῆς χεττιεὶμ, who came out of the land of Chitim: and Jerome observed that the opinion of most Doctors was that Chitim is indeed Macedonia. Others, however, prefer to understand the prophecy concerning the devastation wrought by Nebuchadnezzar, of which he also prophesied in Ezech. 26, 8: such as Jerome, Cyril, Procopius, Brentius, Oecolampadius, Calvin, Cornel. a Lapide, Tirinus, and others. For this explanation, Calvin especially urges on this passage that the restoration of Tyre is promised here again: but after Alexander conquered it, it was never restored. But how was it not restored, if indeed it flourished in its pristine bloom until the times of Christ, and was illuminated by the light of evangelical doctrine through Christ and the Apostles? However, the predictions of Ezekiel and this one of Isaiah seem to be different. For the former threatens Tyre with total and final extermination in the last verses of chapter 26, by which Tyre is to be reduced to nothing, so that it does not exist and is not found forever: which seems to be understood of Old Tyre, which was undermined by the waters and will never emerge. Concerning which the Lord says in Ezekiel: When I shall make thee a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited, and shall bring up the abyss upon thee and many waters shall cover thee, and I shall draw thee down with those who descend into the pit to the everlasting people, and I shall place thee in the depths of the earth, as Jerome translates it, concerning which see Paulus Crellius in Concord. at the word Tyre. Isaiah, however, prophesied indeed of a notable slaughter of Tyre, but one that would bring ruin for only seventy years: which happened to Tyre when it was renewed, or rather when a new one was built in the place of the old. The Prophet foresaw that this would be inflicted upon it by Alexander the Great, because the Holy Spirit wished to predict its slaughter in such a way as to simultaneously designate the conversion of the restored city to the true God, which did not happen to the ancient Tyre. Nor is it a wonder to pass over the former devastation or slaughter, and for the latter to be designated by the Prophet: which is observed throughout the predictions of the Old Testament, as can be seen from the final words of Jacob, and the Mosaic, and other prophecies. Not to mention that some, and among them Zwingli himself, as well as the Dutch Interpreters, wish for both slaughters to be designated, both that which was to be inflicted by Nebuchadnezzar and that which was to be inflicted by Alexander the Great. To whom, therefore, it must be said that from the later ruin this is in turn predicted to be restored after 70 years. Franz Junius interprets verse 1 thus: A burdensome prophecy of Tyre: Howl, ye ships of the Ocean, for it has been laid waste by those of the household (that is, the servants of the Tyrians, who, when they noticed the riches of their masters, made a conspiracy, killed all the free people along with their masters, invaded the Republic, and made Strato king, as Justin writes, book 18) by strangers (Heb. from the house, from the coming men, that is, from the Chaldeans or Babylonians, by the authority of Nebuchadnezzar, who besieged and conquered Tyre for 13 years. See Jer. 47. Ezech. 26. & seqq. and Josephus book I against Apion, Alexander) from the region of the Chittim it is revealed unto it (i.e. Cilicia, from whence Alexander the Macedonian set out and broke into the eastern tract. See Gen. 10, 4.) Junius, however, wishes verse 15 and following to be explained as the state of Tyre, which was first for 70 years from the devastation wrought by the Babylonians: then from the time of Cyrus until Alexander. It is to be wished that histories were available concerning the time of the restoration of this city: thus something more certain could be established about this prophecy: now one must be content with a merely probable conjecture as to what the terminus a quo and ad quem of these 70 years should be established, and whether they should be referred to the Babylonian or the Macedonian devastation. By whom and how Tyre was restored (Cornel. a Lapide here) neither sacred nor profane history narrates. For I shall show in Ezech. 29, 17 that Tyre was destroyed long after the destruction of Jerusalem, and therefore the Tyrians did not return from Babylon with the Jews, but long after. But concerning that, all Interpreters agree unanimously that that calamity of the Tyrians which is predicted here cannot be taken as the siege of Shalmaneser: since the Tyrians had obtained victory then, and, lifting their spirits from this most celebrated victory against the fleet of Shalmaneser and the Phoenicians, as if they were completely invincible, they acted ferociously against the neighboring Israelites and others: whence this prophecy was announced for the consolation of the people against the Tyrians, that there was no reason for them to exult so much: for new and far graver calamities were to arise for them daily.

Vers. 1. HOWL, YE SHIPS OF THE SEA) Tharsis in Hebrew, i.e., from Tartessus or Spain, which had frequent commerce with Tyre; the Greeks [use] ships of the Carthaginians, placing a city of Africa not far distant for a city of Spain. See what was said at 1. Kings 10, 22.

Jerome does not deny that Carthage is specifically understood with the LXX, because it was a colony of the Tyrians. Oecolampadius thinks that the Prophet addresses neighboring cities, as if Tyre were lamented; and that he first turns to the Cilicians, namely to Tarsus, then to the inhabitants of the Island, that is, of Cyprus; because these were neighboring regions which had the most commerce with Tyre. Tyre, however, has Tarsus, the Cilicians, and the island of Cyprus to the north, Egypt to the southwest, and Assyria to the east. Calvin also explains it concerning Cilicia: Jerome, however, and B. Luther interpret NAVES MARIS generally; Junius and Piscator [interpret it as] of the Ocean, that is, as many as exercise trade by ships on the sea, for whom the ruin of Tyre was to be lamented because of their frequent commerce with it.

Vers. eod. FOR IT IS LAID WASTE) That is, stripped of its wealth.

HOUSE) City, in the Hebrew manner. Thus Bethel, Bethain, Bethshemesh, and others.

FROM WHENCE THEY WERE ACCUSTOMED TO COME.) Nay, the entrance: i.e., where ships were accustomed to be brought in.

The Prophet says that Tyre has been laid waste, not stripped of its wealth: and the following verses reveal a more serious ruin and the extermination of the city, by the consensus of all Interpreters. Nor is it in the Hebrew: The house of entry is laid waste: but it is laid waste (Tyre) from the house, from the coming. Which implies a total devastation, so that neither did houses remain, nor did merchants migrate there, according to the explanation of most Interpreters. Junius, however, wishes the authors of the devastation, namely the domestic ones and the foreign Chaldeans, to be designated, as we indicated above.

Verse of the same. FROM THE LAND OF CHITTIM IT IS REVEALED TO THEM) The Chittim in Cyprus, brought back under the rule of the Assyrians, immediately announced to Spain that Tyre was being closed in on all sides by the arms of the Assyrians.

Others explain it thus: From the land of Chittim, that is, from the islands of the Mediterranean Sea, it was first revealed to them, namely, to the ships of the sea, that is, to the maritime merchants, that Tyre had been captured, laid waste, and burned. However, the land of Chittim is nowhere in the Scriptures taken to mean Cyprus or the islands of the Mediterranean Sea: but it has been observed before that it is taken to mean Macedonia. Therefore, this was revealed from the land of Macedonia, either to the ships of the sea, with the Macedonian expedition being spread by rumor; or to the Tyrians, who experienced it in reality: just as those things are manifest to us which we know by experience: these evils experienced from the Macedonians the Tyrians, as Osiander explains. Whence Luther significantly translated: From the land of Chittim they will perceive it. The verb נגלה denotes migrated in Piel & Hiphil, translated & caused to migrate. Whence such a sense is elicited by Zwingli, connecting these words with the previous מבוא מבית: That, however, (was done) by the inhabitants of the islands (by Chittim) having departed from their home and taking it for themselves. It could also be translated thus: From the Macedonian land one goes to them, because the verb is Niphal נגלה למו so that it is hinted that that expedition will not be in vain, such as was that of Shalmaneser, but will bring total ruin to Tyre.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII.

Tyri vastitas ob superbiam ad annos LXX. & negotiatio olim Domino consecranda.

ONUS TYRI] Nihil hic de Nabuchodonosoro, mul- toque minus de Alexandro Magno cogitandum. Omnia enim hæc vaticinia inter se cohærent, & ad tempora pro- xima pertinent. Quod præcessit vaticinium, pronuncia- tum est Salmanasaro urbem obsidente, continetque & res istas, & quæ secuta sunt sub Sennacheribo. Eodem tempore & revelatum est à Deo, & à Propheta prædicatum conscri- ptumque est, quod de Tyro nunc sequitur, impletumque non multo post. Nam ut ex Menandro Ephesio discimus, & ex Josepho libro nono Historiæ antiquæ, Rex Assyriorum Salmanasar, subacta Samaria, quam sub Phœnices no- mine comprehendit Menander, (ostendimus autem ad li- brum I. de Verit. Relig. Christian. apud Græcos satis late extendi Phœnicum nomen) Tyriis bellum intulit, certavit classe, fecit ut pretia rerum apud Tyrios multum intende- rentur. Tandem ipse decedens reliquit custodes ad flumi- na & aquæductus, qui Tyrios ab aqua omni (haud dubie, & à commercio) arcerent: idque toleratum Tyriis per annos quinque. His quinque annis si duos addas, per quos Rex in illis locis mansit ipse, habebis septem annos: quem nu- merum omnino tribus hujus capitis locis restituendum censeo, sicut pro שבעים legendum שבע diximus supra 7, 8. Nimirum par utrobique error, י per librarios ma- le adjecto, sive notis septenarii & septuagenarii numeri, quæ olim forte, ut nunc apud Arabas, uno punctulo adjecto, qui ex singulis faceret denos, distingwebantur, confusis.

Novam iterum Gloslam promit Grotius, ejusq; gratia Ebræam veritatem tribus in locis v. 15. seqq. corruptionis arguit. Sed si ob præconce- ptam opinionem corrigendi sint fontes, quænam relinquetur in Sacris literis certitudo? neque ul- lum pondus inest argumento, quod à συνεχείᾳ pe- tit ac ratione temporis. Nam non cohærere, quoad Chronologiam, omnia vaticinia in hoc aut aliis Pro- phetis res ipsa docet: & etiam hic συνεχείας ratio- nem observant Interpp. Ex his S. Hieronymus: Quomodo adversus Babylonem & Philistim, & Moab, Ægyptum, & Idumæos & Israelitas, supra Dei com- minationem legimus, quod insultaverint captivitati populi ejus. Ita etiam nunc adversum Tyrum & ini- micam & insultatricem subversionis Hierusalem Pro- phetia texitur, quod etiam ipsa ab eodem hoste sit de- struenda. Legamus Græcorum historias, & ma- xime eorum, qui Assyriæ gentis bella describunt: ibi- que reperiemus post captivitatem Hierusalem, Palæ- stinos & Arabas, & Damascenos, ac deinceps Ægy- ptios fuisse subversos &c. Porro non congruit histo- ria à Grotio adducta vaticinio. Quamvis enim bel- lum indixerit Tyriis & classe certarit cum iisdem Salmanasser, non tamen devicti Tyrii sunt; imo victoriam contra Salmanassarem & Phœnicum clas- fem insignem obtinuerunt, teste Alexandro Tyrio apud Josephum lib. IX. Antiq. Judaic. Hic vero prædicitur, Tyriis migrandum fore ad peregrinas sedes, easque ad ignominiam deducendas, Tyrum devastandam & in oblivione futuram. Porro non tantum per quinq́, aut septem, sed per septuaginta annos Tyrum abjectam futuram, Propheta tribus vicibus inculcat: neque ullum est indicium aut ve- stigium corruptelæ textus. Consonant enim Codd. Ebræi, Chaldæi, Græci, Latini ex asse. Ut prorsus te- merarium ac profanum sit, textum sacrum hic cor- rigere. Imo ne correctioni locus esset, cavit Spirit. Sanctus, dum post verba; Et erit in die illa, in obli- vione eris, ô Tyre, septuaginta annis; adjecit, SICUT DIES REGIS UNIUS. Quæ certe Grotiano commento de textus corruptione prorsus refra- gantur. Num enim septem anni dies unius Regis sunt? At septuaginta anni unius Regis dies recte dicuntur, sive dies vitæ spectes, quemadmodum Davidem tot annis vixisse constat; sive etiam regi- minis, uti explicat Oecolampadius: siquidem ad sum- mum ultra septuaginta annos ista ætate nemo re- gnavit. Unde etiam Zwingl. in h. l. Apparet, Re- gem apud Tyrios aliquando tam grandem natu factum esse, ut LXX. annis rebus præfuerit. Alii regni Baby- lonici annos, quibus id adhuc stare debuit, cum Piscatore intelligunt. Grotius hæc explicat, sicut dies Regis unius, i. e. quantum durabit vita Salmanassa- ris. Sed id fundamento caret, neque congruit. Num n. Salmanasser septem annis tantum vixit? Ut taceã quod non perinde Ebræi, uti Arabes suos numeros designare consueverunt, quod gratis assumit Gro- tius. Denique videmus, quantopere corrum- pendus sit sensus verborum Prophetæ, ut inserviat hypothesi Grotianæ. Nam cum in textu habetur, Tyrum VASTATAM esse v. 1. Grotius exponit, opibus exutam. Quæ maxime diversa sunt. Cum Pro- pheta v. 7. minatur, quod transituri sint in alias ter- ras Tyrii, quodque pedes ipsorum longe eos ducturi sint ad peregrinandum, ut exulare cogantur sede sua, quod fieri non potest, cum undiq; exitu claudun- tur, fingit Grotius, antequam clauderentur exitus multos in loca maritima, quamvis longinqua, migr a- visse. Sed manifestum est, prædici captivitatem & exilium. Ducent eam pedes sui longe ad peregri- nandum: i. e. qui in urbe capta cædibus superfuerint, migrabunt in longe dissitam terram in exilium.

Ubi per pedes Grotius intelligit pedes navium, vel etiam remos: fiquidem Latini funes, quibus tendun- tur vela, pedes vocent. Et Plautus nautas ipfos na- vales pedes. Neque nudam obfidionem illa tantum fonant, sed ruinam potius & everfionem; cum addi- tum fuerit, in Ægypto dolebunt, cum audierint de Tyro, fcil. everfa. Hoc vaticinium est, inquit Hie- ronymus, quod Ægyptii, postquam timerent poten- tissimam & vicinam gentem longa obfidione deletam, sciant etiam sibi interitum propinquare. Transite maria, &c. Rurfum pro mari & Tharfis LXX. Car- thaginem transtulerunt. Legimus in historiis Assy- riorum, obseffos Tyrios postquam nullam spem eva- dendi videbant, conscenfis navibus fugisse Carthagi- nem, & ad alias Jonii Ægeiq; maris insulas. Unde & in Ezechiel dicitur, Merces non est reddita ei, ne- que exercitui ejus de Tyro: eo quod omnes urbis opes translatæ sunt, & nobiles quoq; eam vacuam de- relinquerint. Hæc Hieronymus. Quis cogitavit hoc supra Tyrum coronatam, quæ majestate regia inter alias urbes fulgebat, cujus negotiatores erant principes & institores ejus erant inclutæ terræ viri? Quis confiliis fuis evertere tam potentem urbem potuit, cujus mercatores tam divites fuêre, ut vel unus integrum exercitura alere potuerit? Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret, (debilitaret) superbiam omnis gloriæ & ad ignominiam deduceret univerfos inclytos terræ. Transi terram tuam, quasi flumen, ô Tyre filia maris (in mari fita & quasi à mari prognata) quia non est cingulum ultra tibi. Quæ ita exponit Ofiander: Tu velociter per terram tuam (quam habes in continente) abibis in exilium: nec ullæ tibi vires erunt amplius, quibus rebus tuis poffis consulere. Accingere enim se dicuntur, qui expediti sunt ad res suas probe curandas. Grotius hæc ita interpretatur: TRANSI TERRAM TUAM; in terram tuam, id est, in aliquam colonia- rum tuarum. QUASI FLUMEN, quod à fonte fertur in mare. Sic tu ad Oceanum usq; abi, si potes. FILIA MARIS. In Ebræo: ad filiam (id est, ur- bem) Tharfisch, id est, Tarteschim, vel Hispaniam, cui frequens cum Tyrio commercium. NON EST CINGULUM ULTRA TIBI. Per Cingulum intellige munimenta urbi circumpofita, quæ tunc ho- stis tenebat. Ita Grotius; Rectius autem hæc B. Lutherus: Transi in terram quasi flumen: insignis figura, quæ difperfionem futuram fignificat: sicut flu- men primo curfu rapitur, omnia post se relinquens: fic vos vestras sedes, civitatem vestram abacti relin- quetis. NON EST CINGULUM ULTRA, Cin- gulum vocat Politiam, imperium, regnum, sicut Job. c. 12. Baltheum regis dissolvit. Et in glossa margina- li: Da ist kein Gurt (kein Regiment, und Ober- keit) mehr. MANUM SUAM EXTENDIT DOMINUS SUPER MARE, CONTURBA- VIT REGNA. In Hebræo: Perterrefecit regna: nempe exemplo tantæ urbis.

Ad v. 13. qui perobfcurus, hæc annotavit Gro- tius non incommode. ECCE TERRA CHAL- DAEORUM. In qua urbs Babylon, unde Berofi libri aliis Chaldaica, aliis Babylonica. TALIS POPU- LUS NON FUIT. Melius: Iste populus non est. Fuere Chaldæi populus: nunc provincia sunt Assyrio- rum. Quid ergo mirum, fi iidem Assyrii Tyrios ve- xant. ASSUR FUNDAVIT EAM: IN CA- PTIVITATEM TRADUXERUNT ROBU- STOS EJUS. Ex Hebræo vertas optime; Assyrius illam (terram) replevit hominibus deserti: erexerunt arces ejus. Assyrius homines σκηνίτας eo deduxit: arces quæ ibi apparent, condidere Assyrii. SUFFO- DERUNT DOMOS EJUS. Imo excitarunt. Nam hic fignificatus verbi עור melius cum præceden- tibus & sequentibus cohæret. POSVERVNT EVM IN RVINAM, id est, terram eam sive gen- tem fecêre sibi famulam, aut oppida eorum fecerunt mapalia. Nam Mapalia vox est Punica, ut notant Festus & Servius, quæ Hebraice scribitur, ut hic מפליו. Eodem fere redit versio & interpretatio Juniana: Ea terra Chaldæorum, iste populus non fuit, (jam nulla est ipsorum Respublica, sed devenit in potestatem alterius) ex quo Assyrius fundavit eam, pro Barbaris (statuit in ea colonos barbaros regioni incognitos.) Erexerant exploratorias speculas suas (id de Babyloniis intelligit Junius, quod sese omni- bus modis confirmarint) excitaverunt palatia il- lius: (Assyrius) disposuit illam in ruinam, (i. e. evertit totam regionem) ut πρότασιν illa exhibeant, ac confirmetur Prophetia exemplo Babylonici Regni, quod Sennacheribi majores occupaverant atq; e- verterant 2. Reg. 17, 24. C. 19, 2. & ἀπόδοσις reddatur vers. sequenti 14. EJULATE NAVES MARIS, QUIA DEVASTATA EST TYRUS VE- STRA. Ita & exemplum illud & applicatio rui- nam & devastationem, non vero obsidionem fru- straneam infert. Non potest certe v. 14. de sola ob- sidione accipi, quod opibus exuta sit: quum desola- tionem aperte minetur Propheta. B. Lutherus ad versum istum hæc annotat: Est obscura sententia, quæ si active accipiatur, de vastitate Chaldaica est intelligenda. Ego autem passive accipio, ut sit senten- tia: Non poteris resistere Alexandro, qui te expu- gnabit. Is enim & Babylonem quoque, ubi non- dum populus est, (i. e. ubi nondum Monarchia est) evertet. Sententia Ebræa sic fere reddi potest: Ecce terra Chaldæorum, in qua nondum populus quam Assur fundavit, ut navigari possit, & erexit turres, & extruxit palatia, & tamen posita est in ruinam. Unde in Bibliis Germanicis, prout ea Vinariensi Paraphrasi illustrantur, hæc ita habent v. 12. 13. 14. O Chitim, (O du mächtiger Held Alexander der Macedonier König, mache dich auf und zeuch fort, rüste dich, daß du die Stadt Tyrum einnehmest, und ihre Einwohner gefangen hinweg führest) denn du must da (zu Tyro) nicht bleiben. Sondern in der Chaldeer Land einfallen. Herr Lutherus: Du must nach Tyro auch Babylon verstören, (das nicht ein Volck war) das weiland nicht so mächtig war, als es jetzo ist, sondern Assur hat es angerichtet (die Assyrier haben das Chaldeische oder Babylonische Reich in Aufnehmen bracht, und es zugerichtet) zu schiffen (durch Behuff des grossen Flusses Euphra- tis) und haben veste Thürm drinn aufgerichtet, und Paläst aufgebauet (es hat gewaltige veste Städte im Lande Chaldea oder Babel) es ist gesetzet (es ist über sie beschlossen) daß sie geschleiffet werden soll. Heulet ihr Schiffe auff dem Meer (ihr Handelse leute die ihr durch Schiffahrt eure Kauffmanns schafft bißhero getrieben, beweinet den Untergang der Stadt Tyro) denn eure Macht ist zerstöret. Quæ interpretatio satis commoda videtur. Nam de Alexandro M. hic sermonem esse cum B. Luthero etiam è v. 1. concludit Osiander: Ululate naves ma- ris; quia vastata est(Tyrus scil. cuj9 onus hic propo- nitur:) à domo, a veniendo. (ut non relinquantur ibi domus habitabiles, neq; conveniant amplius mer- catores ad exercendam negotiationem.) Luthe- rus, daß kein Haus ist, noch jemand dahin zeucht. Grotius reddit: vastata est domus, id est, urbis in- troitus. Sed in Ebræo habetur מבוא à domo, id- eoq; præferenda jam adducta Lutheri versio. De terra Chitim revelatum est eis. B. Lutherus: Aus dem Lande Chitim (der Macedonier) werden sie es gewahr werden. Et in nota marginali: Das hat gethan der grosse Alexander aus Macedonia.

So gar lang zuvor hat Esaias solche Ding gesehen. | Nam כִּתִּים est Macedonia, ut Jer. 2. v. 9. Transite in- sulas Macedoniæ, & 1. Macc. 1. * Μακέδονα ὃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς γῆς χεττιεὶμ, qui exivit de terra Chitim: eamque sententiam, quod nempe Chitim Mace- donia sit, plerorumque Doctorum fuisse Hierony- mus observavit. Alii tamen malunt Prophetiam intelligere de vastatione per Nebucadnezarem fa- cta, de qua etiam Ezech. 26, 8. vaticinatus est: ut pote Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Procopius, Brentius, Oe- colampadius, Calvinus, Cornel. a Lapide, Tirinus, aliique. Pro qua explicatione urget Calvinus in hunc locum cumprimis, quod hic instauratio Tyri iterum promittatur: postquam autem eam Alexan- der expugnavit, nunquam ea instaurata fuerit. Sed qui non instaurata fuerit, siquidem ad Christi usq; tempora in pristino flore claruerit, & luce doctri- næ Evangelicæ per Christum & Apostolos collu- strata fuerit. Diversæ autem videntur esse prædi- ctiones Ezechielis & hæc Esaiana. Illa enim to- tale ac finale exterminium minatur Tyro cap. 26. v. ultimis, quo ad nihilum redigenda Tyrus, ut non sit, & requisita non inveniatur in sempiternum_: quod de Palætyro intelligendum videtur, quæ aquis subruta est nunquam emersura. Quo de Dominus apud Ezechielem: Cum dedero te urbem desolatam, sicut civitates, quæ non habitantur, & adduxero su- per te abyssum & operuerint te aquæ multæ, & detra- xero te cum his, qui descendunt in lacum ad popu- lum sempiternum, & collocavero te in profundo terra- rum, ut vertit Hieronymus, de quo vid. Paulus Crellius in Concord. ad vocem Tyrus. Esaias ve- ro de insigni quidem clade Tyri vaticinatus est, sed quæ ruinam septuaginta tantum annorum allatura: quæ accidit Tyro, cum renovata illa est, vel loco veteris potius nova extructa. Hanc prævidit Pro- pheta inferendam eidem ab Alexandro M. quia Spiritus S. ita cladem ejusdem prædicere voluit, ut simul designaret conversionem urbis restauratæ ad verum Deum, quæ non accidit antiquæ Tyro. Neque mirum est transilire priorem devastationem vel cladem, ac posteriorem per Prophetam desi- gnari: quod passim observatum in prædictionibus Veteris Testamenti, uti è verbis novissimis Jacobi, & Mosaïcis, aliisque vaticiniis videre est. Ne de eo dicam, quod nonnulli, & inter eos Zwinglius ipse, nec non Belgæ Interpp. utramque cladem, tum eam, quæ per Nebucadnezarem, tum quæ per Ale- xandrum M. inferenda erat, designatam velint. Quibus proinde dicendum erit, quod è posteriori ruina hæc vicissim post annos 70. restauranda præ- dicatur. Franz. Junius versum 1. ita interpretatur: Prophetia onerosa Tyri: Ejulate naves Oceani vasta- tam esse à domesticis, (id est, servis Tyrorum, qui quum divitias Dominorum animadverterent, con- spiratione facta, omnem liberum populum cum Dominis interfecerunt, Rempublicam invaserunt & Stratonem fecerunt regem, ut scribit Justin. l. 18.) ab advenis (Ebr. à domus, ab adventus viris, hoc est, à Chaldæis sive Babyloniis, auctore Nebucadnezare, qui Tyrum annis 13. obsessam expugnarunt. Vid. Jer. 47. Ezech. 26. & seqq. & Josephum lib. I. contra Appionem Alexandrum) à regione Cittheorum reve- latur in illam (i. e. Ciliciæ, unde profectus Alexan- der Macedo irrupit in orientalem tractum. Vid. Gen. 10, 4.) Vult autem Junius, v. 15. seqq. exponi statum Tyri, qui fuerit primum 70. annis à vasta- tione effecta per Babylonios: deinde à tempore Cyri ad Alexandrum usque. Optandum, prosta- rent historiæ de tempore restauratæ hujus urbis: ita certius quid de hoc vaticinio constitui posset: nunc probabili fere conjectura tantum acquie- scendum, quisnam terminus à quo & ad quem ho- rum 70. annorum constitui debeat, & num illi ad Babylonicam, an vero ad Macedoniam devasta- tionem referendi sint. Per quem & quomodo Tyrus restaurata sit (Cornel. à Lapide hic) nec sacra nec pro- fana narrat historia. Nam diu post excidium Hie- rosolymæ excisam esse Tyrum, ac proinde Tyrios cum Judæis non rediisse Babylone, sed diu post, ostendam Ezech. 29, 17. De eo vero ὁμοθυμαδὸν consentiunt omnes Interpretes, non posse illam calamitatem Tyriorum, quæ hic prædicitur, de Salmanaffaris obsidione accipi: siquidem Tyrii victoriam tum ob- tinuerint, atque ab hac celeberrima victoria contra Salmanassaris & Phœnicum classem animos eri- gentes, quasi prorsus invicti essent, in propinquos Israelitas, & alios ferocierint: unde hæc Prophetia ad consolationem populi contra Tyrios prænun- ciata, non esse, cur tantopere exultarent: novas enim indies calamitates longe graviores illis exo- rituras.

Vers. 1. VLVLATE NAVES MARIS) Tharsis in Hebreo, i. e. à Tartesso sive Hispania, cui frequens cum Ty- ro commercium, Græci πλοῖα Καρχηδόνων, posita urbe Africæ non longe distante, pro urbe Hispanæ. Vide quæ dicta ad 1. Reg 10, 22.

Non abnuit Hieronymus, quin specialiter Car- thago cum LXX. intelligatur, quia colonia Tyrio- rum erat. Oecolampadius putat, alloqui Prophetam vicinas civitates, quasi deplorata esset Tyrus; & pri- mum se ad Cilices convertere, nempe ad Tharsum, deinde ad inhabitatores Insulæ, hoc est, Cypri; quia hæ vicinæ erant regiones, quæ plurimum commer- cii habuerunt cum Tyro. Tyrus vero ad septen- trionem habet Tharsum, Cilices, & insulam Cy- prum, ad meridiem occidentalem Ægyptum, ad Orientem Assyriam. De Cilicia etiam explicat Calvinus: Hieronymus tamen & B. Lutherus gene- raliter interpretantur NAVES MARIS; Junius & Piscator Oceani, id est, quotquot exercent navi- bus mercaturam in mari, quibus deploranda erat ruina Tyri ob frequentia cum eadem commercia.

Vers. eod. QVIA VASTATA EST) Id est, opibus exuta.

DOMVS) Urbs, more Hebræo. Sic Bethel, Bethain, Bethsemesch, & alia.

VNDE VENIRE CONSVEVERANT.) Imo introitus: i. e. quo invehi naves solebant.

Vastatam esse Tyrum Propheta, ut antea mo- nuimus, dicit, non opibus exutam: & graviorem rui- nam & exterminium urbis sequentia aperiunt, con- sensu omnium Interpretum. Neque in Ebræo est: Vastata est domus introitus: sed vastata est (Tyrus) à domo, à veniendo. Quæ totalem vastationem, ut neque domus reliquæ fuerint, neque eo migrarint mercatores, juxta plerorumq; Interpretum expli- cationem, inferunt. Junius autem vastationis au- tores, domesticos nempe, & advenas Chaldæos designari vult, ut supra indicavimus.

Vers. eod. DE TERRA CETHIM REVELATVM EST EIS) Cittiæi in Cypro ad imperium Assyriorum re- ducti statim in Hispaniam nunciaverunt, Tyrum Assyrio- rum armis claudi undique.

Alii sic exponunt: De terra Cethim, id est, ex insulis maris mediterranei primo revelatum est eis, scil. navibus maris, id est, mercatoribus marinis, ca- ptam, vastatam, exustam esse Tyrum. Cæterum terræ Chetim nuspiam in Sacris de Cypro vel insulis maris mediterranei accipitur: sed de Macedonia eandem accipi, antea observatum. De terra ergo Macedoniæ hoc revelatum est, sive navibus maris, expeditione Macedonica per famam divulgata; si- ve Tyriis, qui id reapse experti sunt: quemadmo- dum illa nobis manifesta sunt, quæ experimento cognoscimus: mala hæc à Macedonibus experien- tur Tyrii, ut exponit Osiander. Unde significanter transtulit Lutherus: Aus dem Lande Chittim wer- den sie es gewahr werden. Verbum נגלה notat migravit in Piel & Hiphil, transtulit & fecit trans- migrare. Unde sensus talis elicitur à Zvvinglio, ver- ba hæc cum prioribus מבוא מבית connectente: Id autem (factum est) ab insularum cultoribus (à Chittim) domo sua profectis & eam sibi capientibus. Posset etiam ita transferri: De terra Macedonica itur ad illos, quia verbum Niphal est נגלה למו ut in- nuatur, expeditionem illam non frustraneam fore, qualis erat Salmanassaris, sed ruinam totalem Tyro allaturam.

## 23:2
Vers. 2. BE SILENT YOU WHO DWELL IN THE ISLAND) There was indeed a part of Tyre on the Island: but it is better to take the word more broadly for the seacoast, according to Hebrew custom.

MERCHANTS OF SIDON CROSSING THE SEA HAVE FILLED THEMSELVES) He describes the old fortune of the city, so that that which was about to come might appear sadder. The Sidonians used to bring both wood from Lebanon, and glass and garments made among them, on rafts to Tyre.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TACETE QVI HABITATIS IN INSV- LA) Erat quidem Tyri pars in Insula: sed latius sumere vo- cem satius est pro ora maritima, ex more Hebræo.

NEGOTIATORES SIDONIS TRANSFRE- TANTES MARE REPLEVERVNT SE) Veterem ur- bis fortunam describit, quo tristior appareat ea, quæ erat ventura. Sidonii & ligna à Libano, & vitrum & vestes apud se factas in ratibus Tyrum deferebant.

## 23:3
Vers. 3. IN MANY WATERS THE SEED OF THE NILE, THE HARVEST OF THE RIVER ITS FRUITS, AND IT BECAME THE MART OF NATIONS) From the Hebrew you may translate best: Whose produce are the sowings of the Nile in many waters, (irrigating the lands, of course) the harvests (brought up) by the river, which is the mart of nations. Thus Dyrrachium is the mart of the Adriatic. Tyre used to sell Nilotic grain to all peoples with its own profit.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IN AQVIS MVLTIS SEMEN NILI, MES- SIS FLVMINIS FRVGES EJVS, ET FACTA EST NEGOTIATIO GENTIVM) Ex Hebræo optime vertas: Cujus proventus sunt sata Nili aquis multis, (terras irrigantis, nimirum) messes flumine (educatæ) quæ es taberna gentium. Sic Dyrrachium Adriæ taberna. Frumentum Niloticum Tyrus omnibus populis cum lucro suo vendebat.

## 23:4
BE ASHAMED O SIDON) Parent of Tyre. Curtius and Justin teach this. Be ashamed, because you were not able to help Tyre, your offspring.

FOR THE SEA SAYS, THE STRENGTH OF THE SEA) Better: For it says of the sea, the sea, I say, the bulwark. He touched upon the very meaning of the name צור, which Greek interpreters are accustomed to translate as rock, whence the Greek word πύργος and the Etruscan tower. Moreover, the Tyrians were so powerful at sea that Tyrian seas passed into a proverb, as Festus teaches.

Vers. 4. I HAVE NOT TRAVAILED AND HAVE NOT BROUGHT FORTH AND HAVE NOT NURTURED YOUNG MEN, NOR BROUGHT VIRGINS TO MATURITY) The Hebrews do not have the optative and subjunctive: therefore they use the indicative for it. The meaning is: Would that I had never had any offspring. For in the scarcity of necessary things, a multitude either fails or is a burden.

Others explain more correctly: I have no surviving citizens, no sons, no daughters, they have all been captured; or killed by the enemy or fled to other places, I am left a widow and naked, just as if I had never begotten or nurtured any children. Or: I am no longer fruitful, I do not beget or educate offspring, the nursery of the Republic; it is all over with me, I have perished entirely and am desolate. Menochius wishes these words to be those of Sidon, testifying that she cannot bring help. Zwingli also attributes them to Sidon. But in the text it is clear that these words are spoken by the strength or bulwark of the sea, that is, Tyre: by which appellation Grotius rightly acknowledges that the meaning of the name צור, which denotes a rock, is touched upon. The Tyrians were so powerful at sea that Tyrian seas passed into a proverb, as Festus teaches. Whence Cyril; The very strength of the sea also, which is the mistress of the islands, namely Tyre, lamenting her own calamities, when she shall have seen herself naked of inhabitants and deserted by her sons, then she will plainly say: I have not travailed, nor brought forth, nor nurtured virgins, nor brought up young men. For they were, he says, in the same position as those who have not brought forth at all, nor educated young men, nor virgins, in that all have utterly perished, and no one at all has remained.

Latin:

ERVBESCE SIDON) Parens Tyri. Docent Cur- tius & Justinus. Erubesce, quod Tyro proli tuæ opitulari non valueris.

AIT ENIM MARE, FORTITUDO MA- RIS) Melius: Ait enim maris maris, inquam, munimentum. Ipsam attigit significationem nominis צור, quod πέτραν solent vertere Græci interpretes, unde Græca vox πύργος & Ethrusca turris. Fuêre autem mari ita potentes Tyrii, ut in- de in proverbium iverint Tyria maria, Festo docente.

Vers. 4. NON PARTVRIVI ET NON PEPERI ET NON ENVTRIVI JUVENES, NEC AD INCRE- MENTVM PERDVXI VIRGINES) Hebræi optativum & subjunctivum non habent: itaque pro eo utuntur indica- tivo. Sensus est: Vtinam nunquam mihi fuisset soboles ul- la. In rerum enim necessariarum penuria multitudo; aut deficit aut oneri est.

Rectius alii exponunt: Nullos habeo superstites cives, nullos filios, nullas filias, capti sunt omnes; vel cæsi ab hoste vel ad alia loca dilapfi, vidua me nu- daque derelicta, perinde ac si nullos unquam libe- ros procreassem vel aluissem. Vel: Non amplius sum fæcunda, non gigno aut educo sobolem, Semina- rium Reipublicæ; actum est omnino de me, tota perii & desolata sum. Menochius hæc vult verba Sidonis esse, opem se non posse afferre, testantis. Sidoni ea tribuit quoque Zwinglius. Sed in textu apertum est, hæc fortitudinem vel munimentum maris, hoc est, Tyrum dicere: qua appellatione attin- gi significationem nominis צור, quod petram notat, re- cte agnoscit Grotius. Fuêre mari ita potentes Ty- rii, ut inde in proverbium iverint Tyria maria, Fe- sto docente. Unde Cyrillus; Ipsa etiam navis forti- tudo, quæ insularum domina est, Tyrus scilicet suas deplorans calamitates, quando se incolis nudam, & filiis desertam conspexerit, tum plane dicet: Non par- turivi, neque peperi, neque enutrivi virgines, nec evexi juvenes. Erant enim, inquit, pari in loco cum his quæ prorsus non pepererunt, nec juvenes educa- runt, nec virgines, eo quod omnes funditus ad interi- tum pervenerint, nullusq́; omnino remanserit.

## 23:5
Vers. 5. WHEN IT SHALL BE HEARD IN EGYPT, THEY WILL GRIEVE WHEN THEY HEAR OF TYRE) Namely, because of the cessation of trade, which was no less useful to the Egyptians than to the Tyrians.

Indeed also because they fear that, since Tyre, most powerful and most fortified, has been overcome and destroyed, destruction also threatens them, as Jerome warned.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CVM AVDITVM FVERIT IN ÆGT- PTO, DOLEBVNT CVM AVDIERINT DE TTRO) Nempe ob cessationem commercii Ægyptiis non minus, quam Tyriis utilissimi.

Imo etiam quod vereantur, quum Tyrus po- tentissima & munitissima superata & destructa sit, sibi imminere quoque exitium, ut Hieronymus monuit.

## 23:6
Vers. 6. CROSS THE SEAS) In the Hebrew: to Tarshish: that is, go to Tartessus. The Greeks, ἀπέλθατε εἰς

Carthage. There is no doubt that, before the exits were closed, many migrated to maritime places, however distant, as the following also indicate. IN THE ISLAND) Interpret as above 2. Verse 7. IN HER ANTIQUITY) From the times of Agenor. HER FEET SHALL BRING HER AFAR TO SOJOURN) By feet understand the feet of ships, sails and oars. The Latins call the ropes by which sails are held, feet: Plautus calls the sailors themselves naval feet. Verse 8. WHO HATH TAKEN THIS COUNSEL AGAINST TYRE?) Who has ordained this? The answer to the question shows that it must be translated thus. WHOSE MERCHANTS ARE PRINCES) Wealthy no less than princes. HER TRADERS) In Hebrew: merchants. For כנעו is taken for a merchant, because the greatest and most ancient market was in the hands of the Phoenicians. Φοίνικες ἔμποροι Aelian 4. 20. Strabo 16. ἐμπορικῶς ὡς τοὺς φοίνικας. Sophocles: Ὠνὴν ἔθου κἀμ πρᾶσιν ὡς Φοῖνιξ ἀνήρ. Verse 10. PASS THROUGH THY LAND) Into thy land: that is, into one of thy colonies. AS A RIVER) Which is carried from a fountain into the sea. So go thou even to the Ocean, if thou canst. DAUGHTER OF THE SEA) In Hebrew: to the daughter, (that is, the city) Tharsisich, that is, Tartessus. THERE IS NO GIRDLE ANY MORE TO THEE) By girdle understand the fortifications placed around the city, which the enemy then held. Verse 11. HE HATH TROUBLED THE KINGDOMS) In Hebrew: He hath terrified the kingdoms, namely by the example of so great a city reduced to such straits. THE LORD HATH GIVEN A COMMANDMENT) That is, He has made a decree, as above 8. 9. AGAINST CHANAAN) It can either be a proper name, for Tyre is a part of Phoenicia, or a common one, as above 11. TO DESTROY THE STRONG ONES THEREOF) Her forces. There is here in the Hebrew, מעוניך, the letter נ placed in the Chaldean manner for a Dagesh, but the Dagesh itself had been in place of the repeated י. Verse 12. SUFFERING CALUMNY) In Hebrew: oppressed. VIRGIN) So called because of her beauty. DAUGHTER OF SIDON) See above 3. ARISING, CROSS OVER TO CETHIM) To Cyprus, where the city of Cittium is, itself also a colony of the Phoenicians. See the passage of Menander produced by us in the said book 3, on the Truth of the Christian Religion. Verse 13. BEHOLD THE LAND OF THE CHALDEANS) in which is the Babylonian city, whence Berosus's books are by some called Chaldean, by others Babylonian. SUCH A PEOPLE WAS NOT) Better: This people is not. The Chaldeans were a people: now they are a province of the Assyrians. What wonder then, if the same Assyrians vex the Tyrians? ASSUR HATH FOUNDED IT: THEY HAVE BROUGHT HER STRONG ONES INTO CAPTIVITY) From the Hebrew you may translate best: The Assyrian filled that (land) with the men of the desert: they raised her towers. The Assyrian led the σκηνίτας (tent-dwellers) there: the towers which appear there, the Assyrians founded. THEY HAVE DUG DOWN HER HOUSES) Rather, they raised them up. For this meaning of the verb עור coheres better with the preceding and following. THEY HAVE BROUGHT IT TO RUIN) That is, they made that land or nation a servant to themselves, or they made their towns into huts. For mapalia is a Punic word, as Festus and Servius note, which is written in Hebrew as here מפלה. Verse 15. SEVENTY YEARS) Seven years; as we said above. The same writing is to be replaced twice below. AS THE DAYS OF ONE KING) How long the life of Shalmaneser will last. A bold correction of the authentic text. Against which all translations and interpreters to a man protest, concerning which we have already treated before. No one, I think, has been found of such audacity, who would so confidently, or rather with such rashness, presume to correct the sources of Scripture, without the example or authority of any Codex or translation. For behold, the most audacious Capellus himself attempted this here. AS THE SONG OF A HARLOT) Why a song which is sung to a harlot, who has been away for a long time. The song, however, is that which follows. TAKE A HARP) Sallust: To play the harp, to dance more elegantly

than is necessary for a respectable woman. Such are the female harpists in the Comedies. THAT THERE MAY BE A MEMORY OF THEE) That all may know that thou both livest and art present. Vers. 17. TO HER MERCHANDISE) To her gains. AND SHE SHALL AGAIN COMMIT FORNICATION WITH ALL THE KINGDOMS OF THE WORLD UPON THE FACE OF THE EARTH) It is not signified here εἰδωλολατρεία, as elsewhere, but because she had taken the likeness of a harlot, thence he takes the metaphor, and wishes to say nothing else than that she will make gain from everywhere, as harlots are wont to do. The Tyrians sold purples to all kings. Vers. 18. AND HER MERCHANDISE AND HER HIRE SHALL BE HOLY TO THE LORD) Her gain shall become the property of God, that is, of the worshippers of the Hebrew God. THEY SHALL NOT BE STORED UP, NOR LAID UP) They shall not store much of it in chests. The Tyrians loved both to gain, and to squander what was gained. FOR TO THEM THAT SHALL DWELL BEFORE THE LORD, SHALL HER MERCHANDISE BE) The gain of that money shall reach the Hebrews who are neighbors to the Tyrians. THAT THEY MAY EAT TO SATIETY.) Namely, those Tyrians will celebrate great banquets: and therefore they will spend money on buying grain and wine and the meat of cattle, in which Judea abounds. AND FOR AN OLD COVERING) From the Hebrew you may best translate it as dense: that is, the best wool, such as Judea likewise supplied. A remarkable perversion of the Prophetic prophecy, which Interpreters by common consent accept concerning the conversion of the Tyrians to the Christian faith. For their merchandise is not then sanctified to the Lord or made the property of God, as they cunningly suggest, when the gain reaches the Jews: since very many of them would hardly spend the same on divine worship, as merchants and the very wealthiest are wont to be devoted to Mammon. Nor are the Tyrians' wages said to be sanctified to God by the Jews, but by the Tyrians. Nor is there anything here about the commerce of the Tyrians, but about their kindness and liberality, by which they will provide for the faithful. The sense therefore is plain: that the wealth acquired by trade will be sanctified by the Tyrians to the Lord: who will not store them up nor lay them up in the manner of the avaricious, but will liberally spend them on the Church and on those who dwell before the Lord, that is, who worship God rightly, have Him before their eyes, and are His care, so that they may eat to satiety and be clothed to thickness, that is, that they may be satisfied therefrom and be clothed with garments sufficiently dense and firm against the inclemency of the air. And therefore it is predicted: not only men of lower rank, but also the rich and opulent are to be converted to the faith, who will sanctify a good part of their wealth to the Lord, and from it will liberally sustain their poor brethren. Which was fulfilled in the time of the New Testament: when the Tyrians and Sidonians not only received Christ more readily than the Jews themselves, Mark 3, Luke 6. But subsequently, even as the Gospel flashed through the world by the preaching of the Apostles, the Tyrians embraced its light with ready spirits, and sealed their faith with frequent martyrdom in the persecutions of Diocletian and others. See Acts 21, Jerome Vol. 1, Epistle 27 to Eustochium, Eusebius book 8 of Ecclesiastical history, chapter 7. Concerning Tyre also ennobled by an Archiepiscopal chair, see Adrichomius in the Theater of the Holy Land, page 12, and let William of Tyre, Holy War, book 13, chapter 2, 23, book 14, chapter 12 be compared. Jerome and some others explain it concerning conversion to the true religion, even if they believe that what began to be fulfilled at the time of the restored temple attained its full completion under the New Testament. Yet most other Interpreters, both Reformed and Papist, interpret this prophecy solely concerning the conversion to the faith of Christ under the New Testament. Zwingli: It appears that he speaks of the beneficence by which those reborn in Christ spent their own on the Saints of God. Calvin: He describes the repentance of Tyre, by which, having previously been devoted to avarice, once converted to Christ, she no longer studies to accumulate wealth, but bestows it on liberality and beneficence. From the Jesuits, Menochius: sanctified to the Lord, that is, consecrated, namely, through Almsgiving, and because it is expended on other pious uses by the Tyrians converted to Christ. For in his own manner the Prophet flies from sad things to joyful ones and to Christ; By those who dwelt before the Lord, he understands the ministers of the Church. Cornelius à Lapide confesses that these things were fulfilled in the time of Christ, comparing that Psalm 45: The daughters of Tyre shall entreat thy face with gifts. So also from our own, B. Luther: I understand it concerning the future kingdom of Christ, that Tyre herself is also to be converted to the Lord. As also Brentius: He prophesies concerning the future Church of the Lord in Tyre, and signifies that Tyre is to be restored most of all because of the Church of the Lord that will be in it. Whence Psalm 86 says, Behold the foreigners and Tyre and the people of the Ethiopians were there, that is, in Zion or the Church not only Jews will be born, but also foreigners, Tyrians and Ethiopians. But that which was predicted by the Prophets concerning the Church of the Tyrians, the Apostolic Writings testify to have been fulfilled. For Christ himself, the Son of God, preached the Gospel and performed miracles in the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and when Paul had sailed to Tyre, he found a Church there, Acts 21, which was afterwards so increased that it was also illustrated by public monuments of writers. Here all our people agree. And from the ancients, Cyril: Formerly the gain, which arose from trade, was collected by those alone who exercise it: but no one at all brought the fruits to God. But when, the nations having been called into the grace of faith, she herself had recognized the preserver and redeemer of all, with a holy temple built by them, and a divine altar erected, the gain of trade is no longer stored up and laid away by them alone, but shall be sacred to the Lord, that is, it shall be anathema and a sacred gift to Him, and an offering of fruits, that they may eat and drink before the Lord. For formerly, occupied with the dwellings of idols and the shrines of demons, they offered sacrifices, and celebrated festivals and assemblies among themselves in honor and glory of their gods. For they were still wandering. But after, as I said, they had recognized the true God, the gain of trade was sacred to the Lord, they ate and drank thereafter in remembrance before the Lord, namely, they consecrated gifts of thanksgiving to God for prosperous things. To which also those things in Jerome in this place contribute: But just as I understand the time of the consummation in the vision of Babylon under the type of its overthrow, and refer the altar of the Lord placed in Egypt after the idols were destroyed to the time of Christ, and in the vision of Moab recognize the throne of the Savior placed in its land, and in all the other visions of Damascus do not doubt that they are mysteries of our times: so also in the vision of Tyre, which is the last, I interpret the time of Christian happiness: which, after it has been built, both their merchandise and their labor shall be dedicated to the Lord. Let us perceive the churches of Christ built in Tyre: let us consider the wealth of all, that it is not stored up, nor hoarded: but given to those who dwell before the Lord, who serving the altar, partake with the altar. The Tyrians minister, however, not for riches, nor for accumulating the wealth of priests, but for providing the necessities of life: so that (according to the Apostle) having food and clothing we may be content with these. And note, that he did not say the negotiations and merchandise of Tyre sanctified to the Lord are to be given to those who shall have dwelt in Jerusalem, as the Jews think: but to those who shall have been before the Lord, who serve him. Nor do Christian teachers alone interpret these things concerning the conversion of the Tyrians: the Jews also agree, although they vainly defer that conversion to other times, as as Jerome observed: the Jews defer their vows to the future, remembering that these are to be fulfilled after the Antichrist in a thousand years. Nor is it a wonder if they invent such things; they who, having spurned the truth of Christ, are about to receive the Antichrist, the instrument of the Devil: since even Judaizing Christians contend that these things were said concerning the blessedness of a thousand years.

Latin:

Vers. 6. TRANSITE MARIA) In Hebræo: in Tharsisch: id est, ite in Tartessum. Græci, ἀπέλθατε εἰς

Καρχηδόνα. Non dubium est, quin antequam clauderentur exitus, multi migraverint in loca maritima, quamvis lon- ginqua, ut & sequentia indicant. IN INSULA) Interpretare ut supra 2. Vers. 7. IN ANTIQVITATE SVA) Ab Agenoris temporibus. DUCENT EAM PEDES SUI LONGE AD PE- REGRINANDUM) Per pedes intellige pedes navium, vela & remos. Latini funes, quibus tenentur vela, pedes vo- cant: Plautus nautas ipsos navales pedes. Vers. 8. QVIS COGITAVIT HOC SUPER TY- RUM?) Quis hoc constituit? Ita vertendum ostendit respon- sio ad interrogatum. CUJUS NEGOTIATORES PRINCIPES) Opulen- ti non minus quam principes. INSTITORES EJUS) In Hebræo: mercatores. Nam כנעו pro mercatore sumitur, quia maximus & antiquissi- mus mercatus penes Phœnices. Φοίνικες ἔμποροι Ælianus 4. 20. Strabo 16. ἐμπορικῶς ὡς τοὺς φοίνικας. Sophocles: Ὠνὴν ἔθου κἀμ πρᾶσιν ὡς Φοῖνιξ ἀνήρ. Vers. 10. TRANSI TERRAM TUAM) In terram tuam: id est, in aliquam coloniarum tuarum. QVASI FLUMEN) Quod à fonte fertur in mare. Sic tu ad Oceanum usque abi, si potes. FILIA MARIS) In Hebræo: ad filiam, (id est, urbem) Tharsisich, id est, Tartessum. NON EST CINGVLVM VLTRA TIBI) Per cin- gulum intellige munimenta urbi circumposita, quæ tunc hostis tenebat. Vers. 11. CONTURBAVIT REGNA) In Hebræo: Perterrefecit regna, nempe exemplo tantæ urbis in tantas reductæ angustias. DOMINVS MANDAVIT) Id est, decretum fecit, ut supra 8. 9. ADVERSUS CHANAAN) Potest aut proprium es- se nomen, nam Tyrus pars Phœnices, aut commune, ut supra 11. UT CONTERERET FORTES EJUS) Vires ejus. Est hic in Hebræo, מעוניך, litera נ posita more Chal- daico pro Dagesch, Dagesch autem ipsum fuerat vice י re- petitæ. Vers. 12. CALUMNIAM SUSTINENS) In He- bræo: oppressa. VIRGO) Sic dicta ob pulchritudinem. FILIA SIDONIS) Vide supra 3. IN CETHIM CONSVRGENS TRANSFRETA) In Cyprum, ubi Cittium urbs, colonia & ipsa Phœnicum. Vi- de Menandri locum à nobis productum dicto libr. 3. de Ve- ritate Religionis Christianæ. Vers. 13. ECCE TERRA CHALDÆORVM) in qua urbs Babylonica, unde Berosi libri aliis Chaldaica, aliis Ba- bylonica. TALIS POPVLUS NON FVIT) Melius: Iste popu- lus non est. Fuêre Chaldæi populus: nunc provincia sunt Assyriorum. Quid ergo mirum, si iidem Assyrii Tyrios vexant? ASSUR FVNDAVIT EAM: IN CAPTIVITA- TEM TRADVXERVNT ROBVSTOS EJVS) Ex He- bræo vertas optime: Assyrius illam (terram) replevit homini- bus deserti: erexerunt arces ejus. Assyrius homines σκηνίτας eo deduxit: arces quæ ibi apparent, condidere Assyrii. SVFFODERVNT DOMOS EJVS) Imo excitarunt. Nam hic significatus verbi עור melius cum præcedentibus & sequentibus cohæret. POSVERVNT EVM IN RVINAM) Id est, ter- ram eam sive gentem fecere sibi famulam, aut oppida eo- rum fecerunt mapalia. Nam mapalia vox est Punica, ut notant Festus & Servius, quæ Hebraice scribitur, ut hic מפלה. Vers. 15. SEPTUAGINTA ANNIS) Septem annis; ut supra diximus. Eadem scriptura bis infra reponenda. SICVT DIES REGIS VNIVS) Quantum durabit vita Salmanasseris. Audax correctio textus avthentici. Cui o- mnes translationes & interpretes ad unum omnes reclamant, de qua vero jam egimus antea. Nemo, opinor, tantæ audaciæ repertus, qui tam confi- denter, vel potius tanta temeritate Scripturæ fon- tes corrigere præsumserit, sine ullius Codicis aut translationis exemplo vel authoritate. Nam ecc ipse audacissimus Capellus hic id tentavit. QVASI CANTICVM MERETRICIS) Quare canticum quod canitur meretrici, quæ diu abfuit. Canti- cum autem est id, quod sequitur. SVME CITHARAM) Sallustius: Psallere, saltare ele-

gantius, quam necesse est proba. Tales fidicinæ in Comœdiis. UT MEMORIA TUI SIT) Ut norint omnes te & vivere & adesse. Vers. 17. AD MERCEDES SUAS) Ad lucra sua. ET RURSUM FORNICABITUR CUM VNI- VERSIS REGNIS TERRÆ SUPER FACIEM TER- RÆ) Non significatur hic εἰδωλολατρεία, ut alibi, sed quia meretricis similitudinem sumserat, inde sumit trans- lationem, nihilque vult dicere aliud, quam quæstum un- dique faciet, ut solent meretrices. Tyrii purpuras vende- bant omnibus regibus. Vers. 18. ET ERUNT NEGOTIATIONES EJUS ET MERCEDES EJUS SANCTIFICATÆ DO- MINO) Quæstus ejus fiet peculium Dei, id est, culto- rum Dei Hebræorum. NON CONDENTUR, NEQUE REPONEN- TUR) Non multum inde in arcas reponent. Tyrii & quæ- sere amabant, & quæsita prodigere. QUIA HIS, QUI HABITAVERINT CO- RAM DOMINO, ERIT NEGOTIATIO EJUS) Quæstus illius pecuniæ ad Hebræos Tyriis vicinos per- veniet. UT MANDUCENT IN SATURITATEM.) Nempe illi Tyrii magna convivia celebrabunt: ideoque pe- cuniam impendent in frumentum & vinum & carnes pecu- dum emendas, quibus abundat Judæa. ET IN OPERIMENTUM VETUS) Ex Hebræo optime vertas densum: id est, lanam optimam, qualem itidem Judæa subministrabat. Insignis perversio vaticinii Prophetici, quod Interpretes communi consensu accipiunt de con- versione Tyriorum ad fidem Christianam. Non enim tum negotiationes Domino sanctificantur aut pe- culium Dei factæ sunt astutum, ubi quæstus ad Ju- dæos pervenit: quum plurimi eundem divino cul- tui haud impenderint, uti mercatores & ditissimi quique Mammonæ dediti esse solent. Neque à Ju- dæis sanctificandæ Deo mercedes Tyriorum di- cuntur, sed à Tyriis. Neque de Tyriorum com- merciis hic quicquam habetur, sed de benignitate ac liberalitate eorum, qua prospicient fidelibus. Sensus ergo planus est: negotiatione partas opes san- ctificatum iri à Tyriis Domino: qui eas non condent neq; reponent avarorum more, sed liberaliter im- pendent Ecclesiæ & his, qui habitant coram Do- mino, hoc est, Deum recte colunt, præ oculis habent, & curæ sunt, ut manducent illi in saturitatem & ve- stiantur ad crassitiem, hoc est, ut inde saturentur & vestibus satis densis & firmis adversus aëris incle- mentiam amiciantur. Ideoque prædicitur: non tantum tenuioris sortis homines, sed etiam divites & opulentos ad fidem convertendos, qui opes suas bonam partem Domino sanctificabunt, & de illis pauperes fratres suos liberaliter sustentaturi sint. Quod impletum tempore Novi Testamenti: quum non modo Christum Tyrii & Sidonii alacrius su- sceperint, quam ipsimet Judæi, Marc. 3. Luc. 6. Sed deinceps etiam coruscante per Apostolorum præconium Evangelio per orbem, Tyrii promtis animis lucem ejusdem amplexi fuerint, ac fidem frequenti martyrio in persecutionibus Diocletiani & aliorum obsignarunt. Vide Actor. 21. Hieronym. Tom. 1. Epist. 27. ad Eustach. Euseb. lib. 8. histor. Eccles. cap. 7. De Tyro Archi-Episcopali etiam cathedra nobilitata videatur Adrichomius in Thea- tro terræ sanctæ pag. 12. & conferatur Guilb. Tyrius bell. sacr. lib. 13. cap. 2. 23. lib. 14. cap. 12. De conver- sione ad veram religionem Hieronymus & alii non- nulli explicant, etsi tempore restaurati templi jam impleri cœpta credant, quæ plenum complementum sub Novo Testamento consequuta. Cæteri tamen plerique etiam Reformati & Pontificii Interpretes de conversione ad fidem Christi sub Novo Testa- mento vaticinium hoc unice interpretantur. Zvvin- glius: Apparet de beneficentia, qua in Sanctos Dei in Christo renati sua expendebant, eum loqui. Calvi- nus: Describit pœnitentiam Tyri, qua cum avaritiæ prius dedita esset, conversa ad Christum non amplius cumulandis opibus studeat, sed eas in liberalitatem & beneficentiam conferat. E Jesuitis Menochius: sanctificate Domino, id est, consecratæ scilicet per Eleemosynam, & quia erogatæ in alios pios usus à Tyriis ad Christum conversis. Suo enim more Pro- pheta à tristibus ad læta & Christum evolat; Per hos, qui habitaverunt coram Domino, Ecclesiæ ministros intelligit. Tempore Christi hæc imple- ta esse fatetur Cornelius à Lapide, conferens illud Psal. 45. Filiæ Tyri in muneribus vultum tuum de- precabuntur. Sic etiam è nostris B. Lutherus: Ego intelligo de futuro regno Christi, quod & ipsa Tyrus convertenda est ad Dominum. Ut & Brentius: Va- ticinatur de futura Ecclesia Domini in Tyro, & si- gnificat Tyrum instaurandam maxime omnium propter Ecclesiam Domini in ea futuram. Unde Psal. 86. dicitur, Ecce alienigenæ & Tyrus & popu- lus Æthiopum fuerunt illic, hoc est, in Zione seu Ecclesia non nascentur tantum Judæi, sed etiam alienigenæ Tyrii & Æthiopes. Quod autem de Ec- clesia Tyriorum à Prophetis prædictum est, hoc testantur Apostolica Scripta impletum esse. Nam & Christus ipse filius Dei prædicavit Evangelium, & edidit miracula in finibus Tyri & Sidonis, & cum Paulus ad Tyrum navigasset, reperit ibi Ecclesiam, Act. 21. quæ postea ita aucta est, ut etiam publicis Scriptorum monumentis sit illustrata. Hic con- sentiunt nostrates omnes. Et è veteribus Cyrillus: Olim merces, quæ ex negotiatione surgebat, collige- batur ab his solum, qui eam exercent: at nemo omni- no fructus Deo adduxit. At ubi vocatis in fidei gra- tiam gentibus, cognovisset & ipsa universorum con- servatorem & redemtorem, templo sancto ab eis ex- tructo, atq; divino altari erecto, non ipsis jam solis merces negotiationis reposita conditur, sed Domino sacra erit, id est, ei anathema & sacrum donarium erit, & oblatio fructuum, ut edant & bibant coram Domino. Olim enim idolorum domiciliis & dæmo- niorum phanis occupati, sacrificia obtulerunt, & panegyres cœtusq; inter se in honorem ac gloriam suo- rum numinum celebrarunt. Adhuc enim errabant. Postquam vero ut dixi, Deum verum agnovissent, quæstus negotiationis Domino sacer fuit, comedebant & bibebant deinceps in monumentum coram Do- mino, Deo videlicet ob res prosperas gratiarum dona consecrabant. Quo faciunt etiam illa apud Hiero- nymum in hoc loco: Ego autem quomodo in visione Babylonis sub typo eversionis ejus consummationis tempus intelligo, & in Ægypto destructis idolis altare Domini collocatum ad Christi tempus refero, & in visione Moab, thronum Salvatoris in terra ejus po- situm recognosco, & in Damasci cæteris visionibus omnibus, nostrorum esse temporum sacramenta non dubito: ita & in visione Tyri, quæ extrema est, Chri- stianæ felicitatis tempus interpretor: quod postquam ædificata est, & mercimonia & labor eorum Domino dedicentur. Cernamus in Tyro extructas Christi Ec- clesias: consideremus opes omnium, quod non reponan- tur, nec thesaurizentur: sed dentur his, qui habitant coram Domino, qui servientes altari, participant cum altari. Ministrant autem Tyrii non ad divitias, nec ad cumulandas sacerdotum opes, sed ad victus neces- saria suppetenda: ut (juxta Apostolum) habentes vi- ctum atq; vestitum his contenti simus. Et nota, quod non dixerit negotiationes & merces Tyri sanctificatas Domino his dandas, qui habitaverint Hierusalem, sicut Judæi arbitrantur: sed qui fuerint coram Domi- no, qui serviunt ei. Neq; solum Doctores Christiani hæc de conversione Tyriorum interpretantur: Consentiunt etiam Judæi, etsi eam conversionem in alia tempora nequicquam differunt, quod ibi- dem Hieronymus observavit: Judæi cassa in futu- rum vota differunt: post Antichristum in mille an- nis hæc explenda memorantes. Nec mirum, si ista con- fingant; qui spreta veritate Christi, organum Dia- boli Antichristum recepturi sunt: cum etiam Chri- stiani Judaizantes de mille annorum beatitudine hæc dicta contendant.

## 24:1 Argument
SECTION III. SERMONS CONCERNING THE ISRAELITES, both of the two and of the ten tribes, held especially concerning the imminent Babylonian captivity and the final devastation of Jerusalem. CHAPTER XXIV.

After the threatening of the final devastation of Judea, the conversion of the Gentiles and the glory of the elect are set forth for the consolation of the faithful.

Verse 1. BEHOLD THE LORD WILL DISSIPATE THE EARTH) The Prophets are accustomed to repeat the same things which they said before, under other words and figures, so that they may the more impress future events upon the mind. Now this prophecy pertains to the devastation of the land of the ten tribes effected by Shalmaneser, as most clearly appears in verse 10, and to the liberation of Jerusalem from Sennacherib, at the end of the chapter.

Grotius therefore preferred here also to follow the footsteps of the Jews rather than those of the Christians. For the Jews refer this prophecy to the Israelites and the devastation of their land. Whence they think these things were spoken hyperbolically, as Oecolampadius notes. The argument on which he relies is very futile, taken from the bare name Beth-aven, because the Bethel of the Israelites had been so called by the Jews. Which name, however, is not found here in verse 10. But a name far different, namely, an appellative name, not a proper one. The city of vanity is crushed; from that, Grotius forges the name Beth-aven, and because Beth-aven was of the Israelites, he concludes that the prophecy of this chapter pertains to the ten tribes. Which art of arguing he undoubtedly learned from the Jews, whom he chose as his masters. But because Grotius sees well that not everything which is contained in this chapter can be twisted to the slaughter of the ten tribes, he therefore feigns that the Prophet has slipped in verse 14 from the Israelites to the Jews, or the two tribes, and from the devastation of the land of the ten tribes effected by Shalmaneser to the liberation of Jerusalem from Sennacherib. But where is that continuity here, which Grotius so greatly boasts of in this Prophet? And the text contradicts this leap from the ten tribes to the Jews: for there is no trace that it is a matter of different people; rather, the pronoun in this verse, 'They shall lift up their voice,' openly teaches that the discourse is continued concerning those of whom he had begun. The discourse is concerning the same land in verse 19. 'With a breaking the earth shall be broken,' concerning which the Prophet had dealt before in verse 1, 'Behold the Lord will dissipate the earth,' and verse 4, 'the earth hath flowed down.' Nor is there anything which teaches that the former deals with Shalmaneser and the latter with Sennacherib. And therefore every one of the interpreters has gone in another direction in the explanation of this chapter. Cyril and Procopius think that it comprehends the sum of what had been said concerning the slaughter of the Jews and Jerusalem especially, and also concerning Babylon, Moab, Damascus, Egypt, Idumea, and Tyre. When the blessed Prophet, says Cyril, had commemorated the things which had been inflicted upon individual nations by divine wrath, he gathers together the sum of the whole discourse in these words, and calls it the destruction of the whole world, which happened to many nations. For not one city or two fell, but provinces and nations were destroyed. Which opinion is also that of Calvin and Francis Junius. Furthermore, others concerning the destruction

of the Jews effected by the Chaldeans interpret it, to which the Vinarie Paraphrase agrees. Thirdly, Theodoret, Eusebius, Vatablus, and Leo Castrius interpret it concerning the devastation of the Jews effected by the Romans. To which the explanation of Brentius and Osiander concerning the rejection of the Jews which happened after the resurrection of Christ almost tends. Fourthly, St. Jerome in this place, as also Ambrose in his book 'On Elijah and Fasting' chapter 21, with Cyril not dissenting, explain it concerning the consummation of the age, because the Prophet proceeds from the destruction of so many peoples to the universal destruction of the world. Which is the opinion of the blessed Luther, as well as Oecolampadius and Zwingli among the Reformed; and also of Sanctius, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, and others among the Papists. But one who, with Grotius, interprets it solely concerning the slaughter brought by Shalmaneser will not easily be found among Christians. It will be permissible, however, to accept those diverse explanations as subordinate in a certain way: if it be said that those things are repeated which had been predicted before concerning diverse peoples, but especially those concerning the Jews, both regarding the temporal devastation of the Chaldeans and also the final one of the Romans, and so, as this was a certain figure of the consummation of the world, with Christ himself hinting at it in Matthew 24, those things are also touched upon which are not only joined with the end of the Jewish Polity, namely the conversion of the Gentiles, but also those which are joined with the end of the whole world, namely the glorification of the elect: just as Cyril interprets it both concerning the particular destruction of peoples and the universal destruction of the world. But if to anyone that explanation seems preferable which wishes the slaughter of the Jews brought by the Chaldeans to be predicted, it must nevertheless be taken in such a way that regard is also had to the universal total destruction which the Romans were about to bring. For the things which are contained here agree more correctly with these than with the consummation of the age, although when there is discourse concerning the conversion of the Gentiles and the grace which comes to the faithful, that happiness is described which is only begun in these lands, but will be completed at the end of the age and in the future life; whence we do not deny that the things which are at the end agree in a more perfect way with the completion of the same in the blessed life.

Latin:

SECTIO III. CONCIONES DE ISRAELITIS tum duarum tum decem tribuum habitæ, cumpri- mis de imminente captivitate Babylonica, & ultima devaftatione Hieroso- lymæ. CAPUT XXIV.

Post comminationem devastationis Judææ fi- nalis, conversio gentium & gloria electo- rum in solatium fidelium sistitur.

Vers. 1. ECCE DOMINVS DISSIPABIT TER- RAM) Solent Prophetæ eadem, quæ ante dixerunt, repe- tere sub aliis verbis ac figuris, quo magis res futuras impri- mant animo. Pertinet autem hoc vaticinium ad devastation- nem terræ decem tribuum factam per Salmanassarem, ut maxime apparet v. 10. & ad liberationem Hierosolymorum à Sennacheribo, fine capitis.

MAluit ergo hic quoque Grotius Judæorum vestigia legere, quam Christianorum. Nam Judæi hoc vaticinium referunt ad Israëlitus & de- vastationem terræ ipsorum. Unde hæc putant hy- perbolice dicta, notante Oecolampadio. Argu- mentum, quo nititur, perquam futile est, è nudo nomine בית און desumtum, quod Israëlitarium Bethel à Judæis ita appellata fuerit. Quod nomen tamen hic non reperitur vers. 10. Sed longe diver- sum, nomen scil. appellativum, non vero proprium. Attrita est קרית־תהו civitas vanitatis; ex illo pro- cudit Grotius nomen Bethaven, & quia Bethaven Israëlitarum erat, concludit vaticinium hujus ca- pitis ad decem tribus pertinere. Quod argumen- tandi artificium sine dubio à Judæis, quos sibi Ma- gistros elegit, didicit. Quia vero videt probe Gro- tius, non posse omnia detorqueri ad cladem decem tribuum, quæ hoc capite habentur, idcirco fingit, dilapsum esse Prophetam vers. 14. ab Israëlitis ad Ju- dæos, vel duas tribus, & à devastatione terræ decem tribuum per Salmanassarem facta ad liberationem Hierosolymorum à Sennacheribo. Ubinam vero hic illa συνέχεια, quam in hoc Propheta tantopere cre- pat Grotius? Et repugnat textus huic saltui à de- cem tribubus ad Judæos: neque enim ullum vesti- gium est, quod de diversis agatur, imo palam pro- nomen in hoc versu, Hi levabunt vocem suam, docet, de illis continuari orationem, de quibus cœ- perat. De eadem terra sermo est vers. 19. Confra- ctione confringetur terra, qua de antea egerat Pro- pheta vers. 1. Ecce Dominus dissipabit terram, & v. 4. defluxit terra. Neque quicquam est, quod in prioribus de Salmanassare, in posterioribus de Sen- nacheribo agi doceat. Ideoque nemo non Inter- pretum in omnia alia ivit in explicatione hujus ca- pitis. Quod de Judæorum clade & Hierosolymæ cumprimis, nec non de Babylonis, Moab, Damasci, Ægypti, Idumææ & Tyri, quæ dicta erant, summam, comprehendere, Cyrillus & Procopius putant. Cum B. Propheta, inquit Cyrillus, quæ singulis gentibus dictis ex divina ira inflicta erant, commemoraverit, his verbis totius orationis summam recolligit, & to- tius orbis excidium vocat, quod multis gentibus acci- dit. Non enim una civitas aut duæ ceciderunt, sed provinciæ & gentes deletæ sunt. Quæ sententia etiam Calvini est & Franc. Junii. Porro alii de extidio

Judæorum per Chaldæos facto interpretantur, quibus Paraphrasis Vinariensis accedit. Tertio Theodore- tus, Eusebius, Vatablus, Leo Castrius interpretantur de vastatione Judæorum per Romanos facta. Quo fere abit Brentii & Osiandri explicatio de Judæo- rum abjectione facta post resurrectionem Christi. Quarto S. Hieronymus in h. l. ut & Ambrosius lib. de Elia & Jejunio cap. 21. non abnuente Cyrillo, de consummatione seculi explicant, quod Propheta à tot populorum excidio deveniat ad universale mundi excidium. Quæ B. Lutheri, tum Oecolam- padii & Zwinglii è Reformatis; nec non Sanctii, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirini, Menochii, & aliorum è Pa- pistis est sententia. Qui vero cum Grotio solum interpretetur de clade à Salmanassare illata, non fa- cile inter Christianos reperietur. Licebit autem diversas illas explicationes, ceu subordinatas, cer- ta ratione suscipere: si dicatur, quod repetantur ea, quæ antea prædicta erant, de diversis populis, sed im- primis, quæ de Judæis, tum quoad vastationem Chal- dæorum temporalem, tum Romanorum etiam fina- lem, adeog, uti hæc erat figura quædam consummatio- nis mundi, Christo ipso innuente Matth. 24. sic attin- gi etiam ea, quæ non modo conjuncta sunt cum fine Politiæ Judaicæ, conversione nempe Gentium, sed etiam quæ cum fine totius orbis, glorificationem nem- pe electorum: quemadmodum Cyrillus tum de ex- cidio populorum particulari, tum de excidio mundi universali interpretatur. Si cui autem præ- ferenda videtur ea explicatio, quæ cladem Judæo- rum à Chaldæis illatam prædici vult, sic tamen ea capienda, ut ad universalem etiam πανωλεθρίαν, quam Romani illaturi erant, respectus habeatur. His enim rectius congruunt, quæ hic habentur, quam consummationi seculi, etsi cum de conver- sione gentium & gratia, quæ fidelibus obtingit, sermo est, ea felicitas describatur, quæ in his terris inchoatur tantum, in fine seculi autem & vita futu- ra complebitur; unde perfectiori ratione comple- mento ejusdem in beata vita convenire, quæ sub finem habentur, haud diffitemur.

## 24:3
Verse 3. AND IT SHALL BE AS THE PEOPLE, SO THE PRIEST) Understand by priests those instituted by Jeroboam, 1 Kings 12:31.

AS THE USURER, SO HE WHO HAS RECEIVED A LOAN) That is, at usury. For even that law of Moses, which forbids usury, had begun to be spurned by the ten tribes, as many others, below 5.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET ERIT SICVT POPVLVS, SIC SACERDOS) Sacerdotes intellige illos ab Jeroboamo in- stitutos 1. Reg. 12, 31.

SICVT FENERATOR, SIC IS QVI MVTVVM ACCEPIT) Id est, fœnori. Nam & illa lex Mosis, quæ fœ- nus vetat, à decem tribubus sperni cœperat, ut multæ aliæ, infra 5.

## 24:4
THE EARTH HAS FLOWED AWAY) That is, it is desolate: as the Chaldean here.

THE WORLD HAS FLOWED AWAY) For that land had been as a certain world of its own, separated from the customs of other nations.

This is to be understood of Judea, as we have said: which was more separated from the customs of other nations than the land of the ten tribes, and was a world proper to God. Osiander rendered it, the earth withers: the world is weakened and dries up: that is, wherever you turn your eyes in the region of Judea, you will see everything squalid, flaccid, arid, desolate. And the height of the people of the earth is weakened, those who previously excelled in dignity among this people will be of no estimation. Which, with many other things, do not agree so well with the consummation of the age.

Latin:

Vers. 4. DEFLVXIT TERRA) Id est, desolata est: ut hic Chaldæus.

DEFLVXIT ORBIS) Fuerat enim terra illa velut or- bis quidam proprius, secretus ab institutis aliarum gentium.

De Judæa hæc, uti diximus, accipienda: quæ magis ab institutis aliarum gentium secreta, quam terra decem tribuum, & orbis proprius erat Dei. Osiander reddidit, marcescit terra: infirmatur & arescit orbis: id est, quaquaverfus oculos intenderis in regionem Judæam, omnia videbis squalida, flacci- da, arida, desolata. Et infirmata est altitudo populi terræ, qui prius in hoc populo dignitate præmine- bant, nullius erunt existimationis. Quæ cum aliis plerisque non conveniunt adeo consummationi seculi.

## 24:5
Ver. 5. IT IS INFECTED BY ITS INHABITANTS) Contaminated by sins, as this same Chaldean here.

THEY HAVE DISSIPATED THE EVERLASTING COVENANT) Which they ought to have kept always as long as God wished it to be kept. See what is in the 4th book on the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Latin:

Vers. 5. INFECTA EST AB HABITATORIBVS SVIS) Contaminata peccatis, ut hic idem Chaldæus.

DISSIPAVERVNT FEDVS SEMPITERNUM) Quod illi semper servare debuerant quamdiu Deus id ser- vari vellet. Vide quæ ad 4. lib. de Veritate Relig. Christ.

## 24:6
Ver. 6. AND THE INHABITANTS OF IT SHALL SIN) They shall pay for their sins.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET PECCABVNT HABITATORES E- JVS) Peccata luent.

## 24:9
Ver. 9. THE DRINK SHALL BE BITTER TO THOSE DRINKING IT) Wine will not taste good to them because of their sorrow.

Latin:

Vers. 9. AMARA ERIT POTIO BIBENTIBVS ILLAM) Vinum illis non sapiet præ mœrore.

## 24:10
Ver. 10. THE CITY OF VANITY IS CRUSHED) By other names signifying the same thing he expressed that city which was called by the Jews עיר תהו city of vanity, but by the Israelites בית־און Bethel.

Grotius concludes on very slight grounds that the discourse is about Beth-Aven. For had Jerusalem not deserved that name at all, so that it should be called קרית־תהו? Therefore, the Prophet speaks of it by the context: For the empty or desolate city is broken down: Every house is shut up, with no one entering: Great shall be the desolation of the city. There certainly appears no reason why the Prophet should treat specifically of Beth-Aven here.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ATTRITA EST CIVITAS VANITA- TIS) Aliis nominibus idem significantibus expressit eam urbem, quæ Judæis vocabatur עיר תהו urbs vanitatis, Israëlitis autem בית־און Bethel.

Levissimo argumento colligit Grotius, d Beth-Aven sermonem esse. Annon enim id nomi nis omnino meruerat Hierosolyma, ut קרית־תהו vocetur? De ea ergo Propheta vi contextus: At trita est civitas inanis vel desolata: Clausa est omni domus, nullo introëunte: Magna erit urbis vastitas Cur peculiariter hic de Beth Aven ageret Prophe ta, nulla certe apparet causa.

## 24:11
Vers. 11. THERE SHALL BE A CRY FOR WINE IN THE STREETS) For wine: that is, a greater cry than is usual for drunkards.

Incongruously: for the lack of wine is noted, which most interpreters have observed. They complain that there is no wine in the city, or even, as some explain, that no joy remains: because wine is accustomed to denote joy metonymically.

Latin:

Vers. 11. CLAMOR ERIT SUPER VINO IN PLATEIS) Super vinum: id est, major clamor, quam esse ebriorum solet.

Incongrue: nam defectus vini notatur, quod Interpretes plerique observarunt. Conqueruntur, nullum esse vinum in urbe, vel etiam, ut nonnulli ex- plicant, nullum superesse gaudium: quia vinum solet metonymice notare gaudium.

## 24:13
Vers. 13. AS IF A FEW OLIVES WHICH REMAINED ARE SHAKEN FROM AN OLIVE TREE, AND GRAPES WHEN THE VINTAGE IS FINISHED) This is because Tiglath-Pileser had already carried away many of the ten tribes before, 2 Kings 15:29.

These things have nothing to do with the matter: for the discourse is about a few olives and grapes being left from that slaughter which Isaiah predicts here: that the whole people will be so pressed that what remains of them will be just as if a few olives that remained were shaken from an olive tree, and a few grapes were left over when the vintage was finished.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QUOMODO SI PAUCÆ OLIVÆ QUÆ REMANSERUNT EXCUTIANTUR AB OLEA, ET RACEMI CUM FUERIT FINITA VINDEMIA) Hoc ideo, quia multos de decem tribubus jam ante transtulerat Theglathphalasar, 2. Reg. 15, 29.

Nihil hæc ad rem faciunt: nam de paucis olivis & racemis relinquendis ex clade illa, quam hic prę- dicit Esaias, sermo est: universum populum ita ex- pressum iri, ut quod reliquum fuerit ex iisdem, perinde futurum sit, ac si paucæ olivæ, quæ reman- serunt, excutiantur ex olea, & racemi pauci super- sint, cum finita fuerit vindemia.

## 24:14
Vers. 14. THESE SHALL LIFT UP THEIR VOICE) These, with whom I live, the people of Judah and Benjamin.

THEY SHALL CRY OUT FROM THE SEA) The Jews, even those who inhabit Joppa and other maritime places, shall sing of their triumph, because they themselves escaped that evil from Shalmaneser.

Grotius rashly inserts this of his own, which is not to bring out the sense, but to bring it into the Scripture. The pronoun המה, These, refers to the antecedents, namely those few survivors who will remain from the Babylonian or even the Roman devastation; these, converted to God, will lift up their voice and praise Him. When the Lord has been glorified (in Hebrew, in the excellence or magnificence of the Lord) they shall exult from the sea (i.e., the nations will acknowledge the true God, they will proclaim with exultation; that the Lord is magnified and exalted will be their greatest joy. It can also be referred to the exaltation of Christ, because the nations exulted after and because of the exaltation of Christ.) For this reason in the doctrines (in Hebrew, in the valleys) glorify the Lord, in the islands of the sea the name of the Lord God of Israel. From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, that glory is deferred to the JUST ONE and that He is sung of throughout the world. Which it is manifest pertains to the conversion of the nations and the universal preaching of the Gospel.
