And who is that JUST ONE, to whom it is sung and whose glory is celebrated among the nations from the end of the earth, by the force of this prophecy, if not Christ, to whom all knees were to bow, Isa. 45:23, Phil. 2, i.e., to whom all the ends of the earth were to be converted, Isa. 54:22, Ps. 72:8, who is Jehovah our righteousness, Jer. 23:6, and in whom the faithful are commanded to exult: Rejoice O Jerusalem and exult O daughter of Zion: (not only the Jews designated by Jerusalem, but also the nations ought to rejoice in Christ; who, having sprung from Zion, Isa. 2:3, Mic. 4:3, Luke 24:47, can be understood by the name daughter of Zion) because thy King comes, JUST, Zech. 9:9, whence the Grotian gloss is convicted of vanity: They shall cry out (or exult) from the sea. The Jews, even those who inhabit Joppa and other maritime places, shall sing of their triumph, because they themselves escaped that evil from Shalmaneser. But Blessed Luther rightly says: that what he says 'from the ends of the earth' signifies the efficacy and course of the Gospel. Hitherto psalms were accustomed to be sung only in the temple, now a song about the glory of the just is heard from the sea. Regarding what is had here, THE GLORY OF THE JUST, Blessed Luther says: The name signifies pleasantness, agreeableness. For he wishes to say that they shall sing of the most pleasant righteousness, which was never heard before in the world, namely that our sins have been forgiven us, that the world, death, hell, and Satan have been trampled underfoot without our strength, and that this victory has been given to us without our merit. For he takes the singular for the plural: The glory of the just, that is, of the just ones, because both Christ is just, and Christians are justified through Him. This will be the most pleasant song, that all these things are given to us freely.

Latin:

Vers. 14. HI LEVABUNT VOCEM SUAM) Hi, quibuscum ego vivo, Judæ & Benjaminis populus.

HINNIENT DE MARI) Canent triumphum Ju- dæi etiam qui Joppen, aliaque loca maritima habitant, quod malum illud à Salmanasare ipsi evaserint.

Temere hoc de suo ingerit Grotius, quod non est sensum efferre, sed inferre Scripturæ. Pronom.en המה Hi, refert se ad antecedentia, paucos nempe illos superstites, qui è devastatione Baby- lonica vel etiam Romana superabunt; Hi ad Deum conversi vocem suam levabunt, eundemq; laudabunt. Cum glorificatus fuerit Dominus, (in Ebræo, in ex- cellentia vel magnificentia Domini) exultabunt de mari (q. d. gentes agnoscent verum Deum, exulta- tione prædicabunt; quod magnificetur & exalte- tur Dominus, ipsis erit summa lætitia. Referri et- iam poterit ad exaltationem Christi, quia gentes post & propter exaltationem Christi exultarunt.) Pro- pter hoc in doctrinis (in Ebr. in vallibus) glorificate Dominum, in insulis maris nomen Domini Dei Israël. A finibus terræ laudes audivimus, gloriam JUSTO deferri eumq; per orbem decantari. Quæ ad conver- sionem gentium & universalem prædicationem Evangelii pertinere manifestum est. Et quis ille JUSTUS, cui cantatur & cujus gloria celebratur inter gentes ab extremo terræ, vi hujus vaticinii, nisi Christus, cui omnium genua curvari debebant, Es. 45, 23. Phil. 2. i. e. ad quem converti debebant omnes fines terræ, Esa. 54, 22. Psal. 72, 8. qui Jehovah est justitia nostra, Jer. 23, 6. & in quo exultare juben- tur fideles: Lætare Jerusalem & exulta filia Zion: (non tantum Judæi per Hierusalem designati, sed etiam gentes lætari debent in Christo; quæ à Zione prognatæ, Esa. 2, 3. Mich. 4, 3. Luc. 24, 47. filia Zio- nis nomine intelligi possunt) quia Rex tuus venit, JUSTUS, Zach. 9, 9. unde vanitatis convincitur glossa Grotiana: Hinnient (vel exultabunt) de mari. Canent triumphum Judæi, etiam qui Joppen aliaq; maritima loca habitant, quod malum illud à Salma- nasare ipsi evaserint. Recte autem B. Lutherus: quod dicit à finibus terræ significat efficaciam & cur- sum Evangelii. Hactenus in templo solum cantari Psalmi sunt soliti, nunc auditum carmen de gloria justorum à mari. Quod hic habetur GLORIAM JUSTI, de eo ita B. Lutherus: Nomen significat ju- cunditatem, amœnitatem. Vult enim dicere, quod ca- nen- nant de jucundissima justitia, quæ nunquam ante in mundo est audita, nempe quod nobis condonata sint pectata, quod mundus, mors, infernus & Satan sine nostris viribus sint conculcata, & ea victoria nobis sine nostro merito sit donata. Accipit enim singulare pro plurali: Gloriam justi, id est, justorum, quod & Christus sit justus, & Christiani per eum justifican- tur. Hæc erit jucundissima cantilena, quod omnia ista gratis nobis donantur.

## 24:15
Vers. 15. IN THE DOCTRINES GLORIFY THE LORD) In the Valleys. For the Hebrews note that this word is also accepted in this way, and that sense fits the place.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IN DOCTRINIS GLORIFICATE DOMI- NUM) In Ballibus. Nam & sic accipi hanc vocem notant Hebrei, & is sensus loco convenit.

## 24:16
AND I SAID, MY SECRET TO ME, MY SECRET TO ME.) Another version seems to fit the place better: Leanness to me, leanness to me: There will indeed be great cause for rejoicing, but not for long. For the sins of the Jews are so great that they themselves will also draw down great slaughters.

Latin:

ET DIXI, SECRETUM MEUM MIHI, SECRE- TUM MEUM MIHI.) Altera versio videtur loco melius convenire: Macies mihi, macies mihi: Erit quidem magna causa gaudendi, sed non diuturna. Nam peccata Judæorum tanta sunt, ut & ipsa attractura sint magnas clades.

## 24:18
HE WHO FLEES FROM THE VOICE OF TERROR WILL FALL INTO THE PIT) He falls into Scylla desiring to avoid Charybdis.

BECAUSE THE WINDOWS FROM ON HIGH ARE OPENED) As in the flood, Gen. 7, 11.

The other version is rightly preferred. But there is a different antithesis here, not the invasions of Salmanassar and Sennacherib at different times, but of different peoples: because while the nations exult at the glory of Christ, the Prophet has a most grave cause for grief at the foreseen incredulity, excision, and ruin of the Jews; as if to say, I waste away, I utterly waste away, while I see the hardening and rejection of my people. Therefore I grieve greatly. Woe is me, because the treacherous have dealt treacherously, and with the treachery of the transgressors they have dealt treacherously.

Latin:

QUI FUGERIT A VOCE FORMIDINIS CADET IN FOVEAM) Incidet in Scyllam cupiens vitare Charybdin.

QVIA CATARRACTÆ DE EXCELSIS APER- TÆ SVNT) Quasi in diluvio, Gen. 7, 11.

Recte præfertur altera versio. Sed alia hic est antithesis, non diversorum temporum invasiones Salmanassaris & Sennacheribi, sed populorum di- versorum: quod gentibus exultantibus ob gloriam Christi, Propheta Judæorum incredulitate, excisio- ne, ac ruina prævisa, dolendi causam habeat gra- vissimam; q. d. Ego contabesco, omnino contabesco, dum video populi mei indurationem & abjectionem. Itaque valde doleo. Væ mihi, quia prævaricantes prævaricati sunt, & prævaricatione transgressorum prævaricati sunt.

## 24:19
Ver. 19. WITH BREAKING THE EARTH SHALL BE BROKEN) The land of the two tribes, and it itself shall be miserably laid waste.

Latin:

Vers. 19. CONFRACTIONE CONFRINGETUR TERRA) Terra duarum tribuum, & ipsa misere vastabitur.

## 24:20
WITH SHAKING THE EARTH SHALL BE SHAKEN LIKE A DRUNKARD) Men do not know where it is going.

AND IT SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY LIKE A TABERNACLE OF ONE NIGHT) Thus towns shall be taken away, just as tabernacles are accustomed to be removed where a journey must be made in the morning.

AND IT SHALL NOT ADD TO RISE AGAIN) Many towns destroyed by Sennacherib shall remain in their ruins. See above 10, 28.

Most take this to refer to the whole earth, and wish the consummation of the age to be described here. We, however, admit that this must be explained concerning the land of the Jews, which was miserably laid waste both by the Chaldeans and most recently by the Romans. These things cannot be referred to the Sennacheribian slaughter. For that brought no devastation to the better and principal part of Judea, the metropolis Jerusalem itself. Nor are only towns said to be taken away, but that whole land, under which Jerusalem is especially included. Of it, it is said, IT SHALL NOT ADD TO RISE AGAIN. Whence not a few explain it of the final destruction by the Romans. Osiander translates and expounds it thus: With breaking it shall be broken, etc. In Hebrew: the earth shall be very ill and shall be dissipated (or laid waste): the earth shall be moved with commotion; the earth shall be shaken with agitation, like a drunkard, i.e., all things shall totter: it shall no longer be able to stand, the Republic. of the Jews, but shall stagger like a drunken man, reeling, until it falls into the mire: and it shall be taken away like a tabernacle of one night, i.e., their Republic shall collapse in no other way than if someone were to overturn, dissipate, and cast away a vile hut, made by some shepherd only for the use of one night. For its iniquity shall weigh upon it and it shall fall (it, the Republic) and it shall not add to rise again, i.e., it shall never be restored. For from that time, when Jerusalem was devastated under the reign of Titus Vespasian, the Jews have had no government of a Republic: neither in Judea, nor elsewhere. Those who interpret it of the devastation of the Chaldeans can take the latter words thus: AND IT SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO STAND, as B. Luther rendered it: His iniquity presses it, so that it must fall, and cannot remain standing. For the verb קום also denotes TO STAND or TO CONSIST, as from Ps. 1, 5, it stands: The ungodly shall not stand in the judgment. See also 1 Kings 14, 4. Verse 21. IN THAT DAY THE LORD SHALL VISIT UPON THE HOST OF THE HEAVEN ON HIGH.) He will take note of those images of the stars, which the Assyrians worship on the hills. For even in their camps they had such images, which all fell together with the Assyrians themselves. AND UPON THE KINGS OF THE EARTH WHO ARE UPON THE EARTH.) Understand kings, both the supreme King Sennacherib, and his princes. For we have often shown that the word מלך is taken in this way. See also above 10, 9. A new gloss again; That by the host of heaven on high, the images of the stars, worshipped on the hills, but to be visited in the camps (not on the heights) are to be understood. A new invention: that those images fell from the camps of the Assyrians. Sacred history declares that the army of Sennacherib was struck by the Angel of the Lord. It does not report that the images of the stars in the camps, which Grotius wishes to be called the army or host of the Heavens on high, were struck. Furthermore, that the Kings of the earth, who are upon the earth, Sennacherib, and his Princes, who were present with him in the camps, are to be understood, whence will it be taught? And was Sennacherib struck with his Princes in the camps? But if anyone should seek the genuine sense in an obscure passage, which various explanations have rendered more perplexing; with some understanding it of Devils, others of the Sun and stars, others of the Jews, whom God had adorned with a singular privilege and exalted even to heaven, Matt. 11, 23, others of the height of human reason exalting itself against the knowledge of God; others of the Army of the great King Nebuchadnezzar (which is Piscator's explanation): Calvin's explanation seems probable: The simple and true sense seems to me to be: That there will be no power so sublime that it is exempted from these scourges of God, even if they have exalted themselves above the clouds, yet the hand of God will come to that place, as it is said in the Psalm: Whither shall I go from thy Spirit? & whither shall I flee from thy face? If I ascend into heaven, thou art there: if I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea, even there shall thy hand lead me. For metaphorically he calls the heavenly Army the Kings and princes, who in the world are eminent and shine like stars, which metaphor he himself afterwards explains in open words, when he says: UPON the Kings of the earth: For I do not think they should be disjoined, as if he were speaking of different things, but that it is a repetition of the same sentiment, so that the latter member is exegetical: unless one prefers to explain it thus: He shall visit upon the kingdoms of the earth: nay, upon those very things which seem to surpass the human condition: For some things are so eminent above others, as if they were separated from the common condition of others. They could, however, in my judgment, not inappropriately also be explained thus: that by the armies of the height on high to be visited, the Diabolical powers, which are described as an army on high in Eph. 6, 12, and by the Kings of the earth upon the earth, the ungodly, and especially Tyrants upon the earth to be visited, are to be understood; because Devils cooperate with Kings and courts in the kingdoms and empires of the earth, and therefore when empires are visited and destroyed, it is rightly said that their assistants and machinations are also visited. In which manner the Prince of the kingdom of Persia was to be visited, and Michael himself had to fight against him, so that victory might be obtained for the Jews before the Kings of the Persians, Dan. 9, 13. It is also helpful to add the interpretation of the Blessed Luther: I, he says, saving the judgment of others, do not depart from the argument concerning the devastation of the Synagogue. For he calls the Jewish people the host of heaven and the kings of the earth, who alone had the worship of God, and served God. He threatens, therefore, that it will come to pass that at length that host of heaven and the kings of the earth, i.e., the Priesthood and the polity divinely instituted, shall perish. He uses these magnificent names, however, host of heaven and kings of the earth, to denote the presumption and pride of this people, who, inflated by the opinion of their righteousness and the worship of God, despised all the threats of the Prophets. For they wished simply by that name, because they were the host of heaven, to be irreprehensible and impassible, just as we see today in the Papists, boasting of the Church and the Fathers.

Latin:

AGITATIONE AGITABITUR TERRA SICUT EBRIUS) Nesciunt homines, quo eundem sit.

ET AUFERETUR QVASI TABERNACULUM UNIUS NOCTIS) Sic auferentur oppida, sicut tabernacu- la, ubi mane iter faciendum est, tolli solent.

ET NON ADJICIET UT RESURGAT) Multa oppida à Sennacheribo destructa in ruinis suis manebunt. Vid. supra 10, 28.

De terra universa plerique accipiunt, & con- summationem seculi hic describi volunt. Admitti- mus autem de Judæorum terra hæc explicanda esse, quæ vastata misere est tum à Chaldæis, tum novissi- me à Romanis. Ad Sennacheribeam cladem referri hæc nequeunt. Ea enim meliori ac præcipuæ parti Judææ, ipsi metropoli Hierosolymæ nullam vastita- tem attulit. Neque tantum oppida auferenda di- cuntur, sed tota illa terra, sub qua præcipue Hiero- solyma comprehenditur. De ea dicitur, NON ADJICIET, UT RESURGAT. Unde de finali Romanorum excidio non pauci explicant. Osiand. ita ea transfert & exponit: Confractione confringetur, &c. Hebraice: admodum male habebit terra & dissi- pabitur (seu vastabitur) terra: Commotione commo- vebitur terra; agitatione agitabitur terra, sicut ebrius i. e. omnia nutabunt: non amplius poterit consistere Resp. Judæorum, sed vacillabit tanquam homo e- brius, titubans, donec in lutum corruat: & aufere- tur quasi tabernaculum unius noctis, i. e. Resp. ipso- rum non aliter concidet, quam si quis tuguriolum vile, tantum ad unius noctis usum à pastore aliquo factum, everteret atq; dissiparet & abjiceret. Etenim gravabit eam iniquitas sua & corruet (ea Resp.) & non dejiciet, ut resurgat, i. e. nunquam restaurabitur. Ab eo enim tempore, quo Hierosolymæ impe- rante Tito Vespasiano sunt devastatæ, nullam un- quam Reip. gubernationem habuere Judæi: neq; in Judæa, neq; alibi. Qui de vastatione Chaldæorum in- terpretantur, posteriora verba ita accipere possunt: ET NON POTERIT CONSISTERE, uti B. Lutherus reddidit: Seine Missethat drücket es, daß es fallen muß, und kan nicht stehen bleiben. Verbum n. קום notat etiam STARE vel CONSISTERE, ut è Ps. 1, 5, con- stat: Impii non consistent in judicio. V. etiam 1. Reg. 14, 4. Vers. 21. IN DIE ILLA VISITABIT DOMI- NUS SUPER MILITIAM COELI IN EXCELSO.) Animadvertet in illas imagines astrorum, quas in collibus venerantur Assyrii. Nam & in castris tales habebant imagi- nes, quæ omnes cum ipsis Assyriis concidere. ET SUPER REGES TERRÆ QVI SVNT SUPER TERRAM.) Reges intellige, tum summum Re- gem Sennacheribum, tum principes ejus. Sic enim vocem מלך sumi sæpe ostendimus. Vid. & supra 10, 9. Nova iterum glossa; Per militiam cæli in ex- celso, imagines astrorum, in collibus cultas, sed in ca- stris (non in excelsis) visitandas intelligi. Novum commentum: quod imagines illæ à castris Assyrio- rum conciderint. Exercitum Sanheribi ab Angelo Domini percussum historia sacra perhibet. Ima- gines astrorum in castris, quas Grotius vocari vult exercitum, vel militiam Cælorum in excelso, percussas non refert. Porro Reges terræ, qui sunt super ter- ram, Sanherib, & Principes ejus, qui in castris ipsi adfuêre, intelligi, unde docebitur? & num Sanhe- rib percussus est cum Principibus suis in castris? Si autem quis in loco obscuro, quem variæ explica- tiones perplexiorem reddidêre; aliis de Diabolis, aliis de Sole & syderibus, aliis de Judais, quos Deus singulari privilegio ornarat & ad cælum usq; exal- tarat, Matth. 11, 23. aliis de altitudine humanæ ratio- nis extollente se adversus Dei cognitionem; aliis de Exercitu magni Regis Nebucadnezaris (quæ Pisca- toris est explicatio) intelligentibus, genuinus sen- sus sit quæras: probabilis videtur Calvini explica- tio: Simplex & verus mihi sensus esse videtur: Nul- tam fore tam sublimem potentiam, quæ ab istis Dei fla- gellis eximatur, etiamsi supra nubes sese extulerint, eo tamen venturam Dei manum, sicut in Psalmo dici- tur: Quo ibo à Spiritu tuo? & quo à facie tua fu- giam? Si ascendero in cœlum, tu illic es: si sum- sero pennas diluculi, & habitavero in extremis ma- ris, illuc etiam manus tua profequetur me. Nam metaphorice Exercitum supernum vocat Reges & principes, qui in mundo eminent ac refulgent instar syderum, quam metaphoram ipse postea apertis verbis exponit, dum ait: SUPER Reges terræ: Nec enim disjungenda puto, quasi de diversis loqueretur, sed ejusdem sententiæ esse repetitionem, ut posterius membrum sit exegeticum: nisi quis ita exponere malit: Visitabit super regna terræ: imo super ea ipsa, quæ humanam conditionem superare viden- tur: Quædam enim sic præ cæteris eminent, ac sies- sent à communi conditione aliorum segregata. Pos- sent tamen illa, meo judicio, non incommode etiam ita explicari: ut per exercitus altitudinis in excelso visitandos Diabolicæ potestates, quæ ut exer- citus in excelso describuntur Eph. 6, 12. per Reges terræ super terram impii, & maxime Tyranni su- per terram visitandi intelligantur; quia Diaboli in regnis & imperiis terræ Regibus & aulis coope- rantur, ideoque cum imperia visitantur, ac destru- untur, etiam visitari parastatæ, ac molimina eorum destrui recte dicuntur. Quo pacto visitandus erat Princeps regni Persarum, ac Michaëli ipsi pugnan- dum erat adversus ipsum, ut victoria obtineretur pro Judæis apud Reges Persarum Dan. 9, 13. Ad- scribere etiam juvat B. Lutheri interpretationem: Ego, inquit, salvo aliorum judicio, non discedo ab ar- gumento de vastatione Synagogæ. Militiam enim cæli & Reges terræ vocat populum Judaicum, qui so- lus habebat cultum Dei, & militabat Deo. Minatur igitur fore, ut tandem illa militia cæli & Reges terræ, h. e. Sacerdotium & politia divinitus instituta per- eant. Utitur autem magnificis his nominibus, mili- tia cæli & Reges terræ, ad notandam præsumtionem & superbiam hujus populi, qui inflatus opinione ju- stitiæ & cultus Dei, omnes minas Prophetarum con- temnebat. Volebant enim simpliciter eo nomine, quod essent militia cæli, irreprehensibiles & impassibiles esse, sicut hodie in Papistis videmus, jactantibus Ec- clesiam & Patres.

## 24:22
Verse 22. AND THEY SHALL BE GATHERED IN THE GATHERING OF ONE BUNDLE INTO THE PIT.) Just as useless things collected together are wont to be cast away, so those Assyrian Princes shall be cast away.

AND THEY SHALL BE SHUT UP THERE IN PRISON.) They will not be able to go out of their camps, no more than those who are bound in prison.

That these things are foreign, I think is evident from those things which have been said. And who will not see that gloss about the slain, they cannot go out of the camps, just like those who are bound in prison! Finally, what will become of those words AND AFTER MANY DAYS THEY SHALL BE VISITED! How were the slain Assyrians visited, whether by a visitation of wrath, or a visitation of thanks! Since Grotius had nothing to say, he passed over them with a dry foot. Those who explain it concerning Devils and the ungodly being gathered into one pit, bring forward various things, lest the Origenists, who, denying the perpetual fire of hell, took an opportunity for their heresy from this, should find support in it. Some explain, from many days, i.e., because of the many sins which they perpetrated for many years, they shall not be unpunished. Oecolampadius renders it thus: And they shall be visited after more than many days, so that these things do not take away the perpetuity, but rather show it. Haymo explains it thus: After many days, i.e., years, they shall be visited, so that, namely, the ungodly may rise again and be united in soul and body, or that Devils and the ungodly may be brought to judgment, and receive the completion of their torments. In which manner Thomas, it can be referred, he says, to the visitation, by which they shall be visited on the day of judgment, not that they may be freed, but that they may be further condemned. Cornel. à Lapide with Jerome, Adam Sasbouth, and Suarez (whom he cites), after many days, i.e., after many ages they shall be visited, i.e., they shall be punished, as if to say, although they are in hell for many days and years, yet their punishments shall never be ended: but after how many days and years soever there shall be a constant beginning of punishments: so that the word they shall be visited may denote a continued and perpetual act. Although, however, the preceding things do not speak of the consummation of the age, or the final Judgment, nothing nevertheless prevents that in the destruction of the Jews there was simultaneously exhibited the destruction of all enemies and despisers of the Gospel, and that in general it also predicted that all enemies, all the host of heaven, all the Kings of the earth, and whatever opposes itself to the kingdom of Christ, would be visited, and threatened them with eternal destruction: just as Osiander explains: And they shall be gathered in the gathering of (one) bundle into the lake, into the pit (or ditch) and shall be shut up there in prison, i. e. All the enemies of Christ shall die, and shall be buried in the earth (as if one were to gather twigs into one bundle, and cast them into a deep lake,) there their bodies in the earth and their souls in hell (as if in a prison) shall be detained until the day of the final judgment. And after many days they shall be visited, i. e. they shall be raised from the dead, that they may be set before the tribunal of Christ and hear the sentence of eternal condemnation. For the death of the wicked is a prison, in which they are detained, until they are delivered together with body and soul to perpetual torments. The Weimar Paraphrasts interpret this concerning the prison of the Babylonian captivity, and the liberation from it. Others interpret it concerning the gracious visitation through the word of the Gospel in the N. T., so that the things which are subjoined in the last verse concerning the glory of Christ, with which the Church ought to shine, may be understood. The Grotian Gloss, so far as I know, has occurred to no one among Christians.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET CONGREGABUNTUR IN CON- GREGATIONE UNIUS FASCIS IN LACUM.) Sicut solent res inutiles simul collectæ dejici, sic illi Assyrii Prin- cipes dejicientur.

ET CLAUDENTUR IBI IN CARCERE.) Non poterunt è castris suis exire, non magis quam qui in car- cere vincti sunt,

Hæc aliena esse, ex iis, quæ dicta sunt, constare arbitror. Et quis non videbit illam glossam de in- terfectis, non possunt exire è castris, perinde ut illi, qui vincti sunt in carcere! Deniq; quid fiet illis verbis ET POST MULTOS DIES VISITABUN- TUR! Quomodo occisi Assyrii visitati sunt, sive visitatione iræ, sive visitatione gratiæ! Quum non haberet, quid diceret Grotius, sicco illa pede præ- teriit. Qui de Diabolis & impiis in lacum unum congregandis explicant, varia adferunt, ne Origenia- nis, qui perpetuum ignem inferni negantes suæ hæ- reseos ansam hinc sumsere, illa patrocinentur. Nonnulli exponunt, à diebus multis, i. e. propter mul- ta peccata, quæ multis annis perpetrarunt, non erunt inulti. Oecolampadius ita reddit: Et plusquam mul- tis diebus visitabuntur, ut hæc non tollant perpetui- tatem, sed magis ostendant. Haymo sic exponit: Post multos dies, i. e. annos, visitabuntur, ut sc. resur- gant impii & anima & corpore uniantur, vel ut Dia- boli & impii judicio sistantur, & complementum cruciatuum sortiantur. Quo pacto Thomas, potest referri, inquit, advisitationem, qua visitabuntur in die judicii, non ut liberentur, sed ut amplius con- demnentur. Cornel. à Lapide cum Hieronymo, Adamo Sasbouth, & Suaretz (quos citat,) post multos dies, i. e. post multa secula visitabuntur, i. e. punientur, q. d. quamvis multis diebus & annis sint in gehenna, tamen nunquam pœnæ eorum finien- tur: sed post quantoslibet dies & annos erit jugis inchoatio pœnarum: ut τὸ visitabuntur notet actum continuatum & perpetuum. Quanquam ve- ro superiora non loquantur de consummatione se- culi, aut extremo Judicio, nihil tamen obstat, quin in exitio Judæorum simul exhibitum fuerit hostium & contemtorum Evangelii quorumvis exitium, quin in genere etiam omnes hostes, omnem militiam cæli, omnes Reges terræ, & quicquid se regno Christi op- ponit, visitatum iri prædixerit, iisque æternum exi- tium minatus sit: quemadmodum exponit Osian- der: Et congregabuntur in congregatione (unius) fascis in lacum, in puteum (vel foveam) & clauden- tur ibi in carcere, i. e. Omnes Christi hostes mori- entur, & in terram condentur (ut si quis in unum fasciculum colligat sarmenta, eaque in profundum lacum abjiciat,) ibi corpora eorum in terra & ani- mæ in inferno (tanquam in carcere) detinebuntur usque ad diem judicii extremi. Et post multos dies visitabuntur, i. e. excitabuntur à mortuis, ut sistan- tur coram tribunale Christi & audiant condemna- tionis æternæ sententiam. Est enim mors impio- rum carcer, in quo detinentur, donec una cum cor- pore & anima tradantur perpetuis cruciatibus. De carcere Babylonicæ captivitatis, & liberatione ex ea dem interpretantur Paraphrastæ Vinarienses. Alii de gratiosa visitatione per verbum Evangelii in N. T. ut quæ postremo versu subjiciuntur de gloria Chri- sti, qua Ecclesia coruscare debuit, intelligantur. Glossa Grotiana nemini, quod sciam, è Christianis in mentem venit.

## 24:23
Vers. 23. AND THE MOON SHALL BLUSH, AND THE SUN SHALL BE CONFOUNDED.) The LXX., when they thought that the sun and moon were natures among the Platonists, such as the Egyptian Kings were, read for חפרה, תפרסה, it shall be broken, and for לבנה, with the letters changed of לבנה, which is brick, and for חמה, having changed the patach into a holem, חומה, which is wall. And so they translated ταχησεται η πλινθος και πεσειται το τειχος, with a not bad sense. The received reading must nevertheless be retained: and by Sun and Moon are to be understood the images of the Sun and Moon, which by metaphor are said to be about to blush, because they could not save their worshippers.

WHEN THE LORD OF HOSTS SHALL REIGN IN MOUNT ZION.) When he shall have shown his power in the liberating of the city of Jerusalem.

AND IN THE PRESENCE OF HIS ELDERS HE SHALL BE GLORIFIED.) All the senators of the Sanhedrin will come into the temple with most magnificent garments to praise God.

The conjecture being dismissed; as to what they read, or why they translated differently than what is read in the sources (concerning which see Jerome in this place), we consider only the gloss of Grotius, which is not unlike the inept commentaries of the Rabbis, to be worthy of castigation. No one among Christians has hitherto understood the Sun and Moon as the idols of the Assyrians. The Chaldean explained it concerning the worshippers of the Sun and Moon who were to perish on the day of judgment, not concerning the idols themselves. Adam Sasbouth, however, [explained it] concerning the demons inhabiting the idols. Nor is it right to depart from the literal meaning of the words, and in place of the Sun and Moon to substitute their idols: rather, the glory of the Lord is compared here not with idols, but with the celestial bodies themselves: which are said to be about to blush at the majesty and glory of the Lord in a figurative sense, because their splendor will be nothing before the splendor of the Lord. But how the Lord is to reign on Mount Zion is explained in the following chapters. It is truly one thing for divine power to be exerted for the liberation of a city, of which there is no word here: another to reign gloriously in the Church, designated by Mount Zion. Finally, those things about the Elders appearing in the Sanhedrin in most magnificent garments are too meager for so illustrious and magnificent a promise. Which others interpret more correctly concerning the glorification of the Lord in the Church, throughout the world; others judge that not even thus is the emphasis and magnificence of this prophecy exhausted; therefore, they explain it concerning the glory of the Lord, which is to shine forth in the other life. Both expositions can, however, be joined: so that before the glory of the Lord, which was to spread itself through the Church in the time of the New Testament, the stars are said to be about to blush, which will indeed shine far more illustriously and will surround the elect in the kingdom of glory. So great will be the brightness of the kingdom of Christ, says Brentius in this place, that before it not only will the most famous Monarchies of this earth be obscured and extinguished, but even the luminaries of heaven, the Sun and the Moon. The Sun is the illustrator of the day, the Moon of the night. And truly there is nothing in this world clearer and more illustrious than these lights. And yet the light, which will shine in the kingdom of Christ, will be much clearer and much more illustrious. The Sun and the Moon indeed shine for man, so that he may walk on the earthly path, lest he strike his outer foot against a stone. And they shine so that you may finish your external works. But they do not shine so that you may walk without stumbling to true and eternal happiness. The Gospel, however, of the kingdom of Christ shines from sins into righteousness, from death into life, from the darkness of hell to celestial splendor. What is clearer than this light? Wherefore it is rightly said that the light of the Sun and the Moon is put to shame and obscured, before the great clarity of that light, which shines forth by the preaching of the Gospel in the Church or kingdom of Christ. For although the Gospel itself is also sometimes obscured either by human traditions or by tyrannical persecutions, yet it always shines piously in such a way that they can escape the darkness of death and hell to celestial life. Similarly Fr. Junius: There will be no light or glory of the Moon or of the Sun itself, if it is compared with the light of God reigning in the Church. That 'before the Elders,' the blessed Luther understands as the Apostles: When Christ shall reign through the preaching of the Apostles: for these are the Elders: these are the πρεσβύτεροι and the appointed Overseers of the Church. Cyril believes that all the faithful are indicated. I think he calls those Elders here who are sound in mind and perfect and endowed with a spirit as if gray-haired, so that with the eyes of the heart they may be able to behold the depth of his mysteries. Which will be perfectly fulfilled in the completion of the Kingdom of Christ, in the other life, in the heavenly Jerusalem; when he shall have been glorified in the presence of the Elders: i.e., the Apostles, who will sit with the Judge, Matt. 19:28. For these will behold the majesty of Christ, John 17:24. And then Christ will reign most perfectly, when all his enemies shall have been subjected to his feet, the demons and all the wicked thrust down to the underworld, Psalm 110:1. Which sense Osiander embraces. The Weimar Paraphrasts: The Prophet wants to say as much as this: The glory which God offers and promises to the believers in Christ is much more beautiful, clearer, and brighter than the radiance of the Sun and the Moon may be, 2 Cor. 3:18, which glory only begins in this life, but will be truly perfect in the eternal life, 1 Cor. 15:41, 42. Whence also the ancient Church teachers interpret this text as the Day of Last Judgment. So also Hector Pintus: We have explained this whole chapter concerning the destruction of the world, and the time of the last judgment; and this is the opinion of Dr. Jerome, whom many have followed afterwards, whose explanation we embrace. He adds the reasons why they cannot be accepted concerning the captivity of the X tribes: because in that [event] the host of heaven was not visited: then because at that time some other things in this chapter do not seem to agree with this interpretation. [He notes that] others explain it concerning the overthrow made by Titus, and that that opinion does not seem to have so many obstacles: others refer it to the overthrow and calamity of the Tyrians. But that exposition concerning the destruction of the world is more common, and more accommodating to the letter. These things, therefore, concerning the 24th Chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ERUBESCET LUNA, ET CON- FUNDETUR SOL.) Hæc LXX. cum putarent male so- natura apud Platonicos, quales erant Ægyptii Reges, pro חפרה legerunt תפרסה frangetur, pro לבנה mutatis earum punctis לבנה, quod est later, pro חמה mutato patach in holem חומה quod est murus. Itaque verterunt ταχησεται η πλινθος και πεσειται το τειχος, sensu non ma- lo. Retinenda tamen lectio recepta: & per Solem & Lu- nam intelligendæ imagines Solis & Lunæ, quæ per trans- lationem dicuntur erubituræ, quod suos cultores servare nequiverint.

CVM REGNAVERIT DOMINVS EXERCITV- VM IN MONTE SION.) Cum in liberanda urbe Hie- rosolymorum vim suam ostenderit.

ET IN CONSPECTV SENVM SVORVM FVERIT GLORIFICATVS.) Omnes senatores Syne- drii cum magnificentissimis vestibus in templum venient ac Deum laudandum.

Missa conjectura; quid legerint, aut cur se- cus verterint, quam in fontibus legitur (de quo vid. Hieronymus in h. l.) solummodo glossam Grotii, quæ ineptis Rabbinorum commentis non dispar est, castigandam ducimus. Per Solem & Lunam idola Assyriorum nemo hactenus è Christianis in- tellexit. Chaldæus de cultoribus Solis & Lunæ in die judicii corruituris exposuit, non de ipsis idolis. Adamus Sasbouth vero de Dæmonibus idola inha- bitantibus. Neq; vero à proprietate vocum par est discedere, ac loco Solis & Lunæ idola eorum substi- tuere: imo comparatur hic gloria Domini non cum idolis, sed cum ipsis corporibus cœlestibus: quæ erubitura dicuntur ad majestatem & gloriam Domini sensu figurato, quod splendor eorum nullus futurus sit præ splendore Domini. Quomodo vero Dominus regnaturus sit in monte Sion, sequentibus Capp. exponitur. Aliud profecto est vim divi- nam exeri ad urbis liberationem, de quo hic nullum verbum: aliud gloriose in Ecclesia, per montem Sion designata, regnare. Deniq; nimis exilia ista sunt de Senibus in vestibus magnificentissimis in Synedrio comparentibus ad tam illustrem & magnificam pro- missionem. Quam alii rectius interpretantur de glorificatione Domini in Ecclesia, per terrarum or- bem; alii ne sic quidem exhauriri censent empha- sin & magnificentiam hujus vaticinii; Proinde de gloria Domini, quæ in altera vita coruscatura est, explicant. Potest autem utraq; expositio conjungi: ut præ gloria Domini, quæ per Ecclesiam sese diffusu- ra erat tempore N. T. erubitura dicantur sydera, quæ vero longe illustrius coruscabit & circumfundet ele- ctos in regno gloriæ. Tanta erit claritas regni Christi, inquit Brentius in h. l. ut præ ea non solum obscuren- tur & extinguantur clarissimæ Monarchiæ hujus terræ, verum etiam luminaria cœli Sol & Luna. Sol illustrator est diei, Luna noctis. Ac profecto his lu- minibus nihil est in hoc orbe clarius & illustrius. Et tamen lux, quæ lucebit in regno Christi, multo clarior, & multo illustrior erit. Sol & Luna lucent quidem homini, ut incedat in terrena via, ne offendat exter- num pedem ad lapidem. Et lucent ut opera tua exter- na conficias. Sed non lucent, ut incedas sine offensione ad veram & æternam felicitatem. Evangelion au- tem regni Christi lucet è peccatis in justitiam, è morte in vitam, ex inferni tenebris ad cœlestem splendorem Quid hac luce clarius? Quare recte dicitur lux So- lis & Lunæ pudefieri & obscurari, præ magna clari- tate ejus lucis, quæ effulget prædicatione Evangelii in Ecclesia seu regno Christi. Etsi enim etiam Evange- lion ipsum aliquoties obscuratur vel humanis tradi- tionibus, vel tyrannicis persecutionibus, tamen piè semper ita lucet, ut queant tenebras mortis & inferni ad cœlestem vitam evadere. Similiter Fr. Junius: Nulla plane lux sive gloria Lunæ aut Solis ipsius futu- ra est, si cum Dei regnantis in Ecclesia luce compara- bitur. Illud coram Senibus, intelligit B. Lutherus d Apostolis: Cum Christus regnabit per prædicatio nem Apostolorum: Hi enim Senes sunt: Hi πρεσ βύτεροι & Præpositi Ecclesiæ constituti sunt. Cy- rillus quosvis fideles indigitari credit. Seniores puto vocare illum hic mente integros & perfectos & animo veluti cano præditos, ut cordis oculis mysteriorum ejus profunditatem possint intueri. Quod perfecte im- plebitur in Regni Christi complemento, in altera vita, in cœlesti Hierosolyma; cum in conspectu Senum glorificatus fuerit: i. e. Apostolorum, qui Judici assidebunt Matth. 19, 28. Hi enim majesta- tem Christi conspicient Joh. 17, 24. Et tum regna- bit Christus perfectissime, cum hostes ejus omnes pedibus ipsius fuerint subjecti, Dæmones & im- probi universi ad inferos detrusi Psal. 110, 1. Quem sensum amplectitur Osiander. Paraphrastæ Vina- rienses: Der Prophet wil so viel sagen: Die Herz= ligkeit/welche Gott den Gläubigen in Christo an= beut und verspricht/ist viel schöner/lichter und hel= ler/als der Sonnen und des Monden Glantz seyn mag 2. Cor. 3/18. welche Herrlichkeit in diesem Le= ben nur angehet/aber im ewigen Leben recht voll= kommen seyn wird 1. Cor. 15/41. 42. Dannenhero auch die alten Kirchenlehrer diesen Text auff den Jüngsten-Gerichts-Tag deuten. Ita etiam Hector Pintus: Totum hoc caput exposuimus de mundi inte- ritu, ultimig; judicii tempore; Et hæc est D. Hierony- mi sententia, quem postea secuti sunt multi, quorum explanationem amplectimur. Addit causas, quare accipi nequeant de captivitate X. tribuum: quia in illa non visitata militia cæli: tum quod tunc alia in hoc capite nonnulla huic interpretationi haud videan- tur congruere. Alios de eversione à Tito facta expli- care, eamq; opinionem non videri tot habere impedi- menta: alios ad Tyriorum eversionem & calamitatem referre. Sed illam expositionem de mundi interitu communiorem, literæq; accommodatiorem esse. Hæc ergo de 24. Capite.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV.

The Prophet celebrates God on account of the benefits toward the Church, which he protects against Tyrants, and the spiritual banquet on Mount Zion, and the future removal of all mourning through the Messiah.

Vers. 1. LORD GOD) Both this chapter and the following contain a laudation of GOD, as if to be sung when those things which he has just said have come to pass.

ANCIENT FAITHFUL THOUGHTS A- MEN) More correctly: Your counsels of old (supply: aforementioned) now appear true and firm.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV.

Celebrat Propheta Deum ob beneficia erga Ec- clesiam, quam adversus Tyrannos tuetur, & convivium spirituale in Monte Sion, omnis q; luctus ablationem per Messiam futuram.

Vers. 1. DOMINE DEVS) Et hoc caput & sequens laudationem DEI continent, velut canendam, ubi ea quæ modo dixit evenerint.

COGITATIONES ANTIQVAS FIDELES A- MEN) Rectius: Consilia tua pridem (supple prædicta) jam vera ac firma apparent.

## 25:2
Ver. 2. YOU HAVE MADE THE CITY A HEAP.) Samaria.

THE CITY OF STRANGERS) Supply: of gods. 1 Kings 16, 32.

Latin:

Vers. 2. POSVISTI CIVITATEM IN TVMV- LVM.) Samariam.

DOMINVM ALIENORUM) Supple, Deorum. 1. Reg. 16, 32.

## 25:3
Ver. 3. A STRONG PEOPLE :) Constant in religion; namely, the Jerusalemites.

THE CITY OF THE TERRIBLE NATIONS SHALL FEAR YOU) Enallage: that is, the neighboring cities will be terrified by this example.

Grotius wishes the present hymn to be about the victory against Sennacherib, because Samaria was indeed devastated by Shalmaneser by the just judgment of God; but Jerusalem was delivered from the siege of Sennacherib. But since he acknowledges that the praise of God is contained here, as if to be sung when those things which the Prophet just spoke of have come to pass, and it has already been shown that the preceding chapter can be understood neither of Shalmaneser nor of Sennacherib; it is now clear that the Eucharistic hymn must necessarily be referred to another. Nor do the words of the hymn itself permit it to be referred to that. Isaiah proclaims ANCIENT FAITHFUL THOUGHTS: O Lord, you are my God, I will exalt you, I will confess your name, for you have done wonderful things, ancient faithful thoughts, Amen. Which things concerning the eternal decree, concerning redemption & our salvation, Jerome interprets as execution. Similarly Cyril: He calls the counsel as ancient & wonderful things the mystery of the humanity of the only-begotten, & those things which were restored through it throughout the whole earth. Grotius translates: Thy counsels of old (supply predicted) now appear true and firm. But were those things (this being prophesied by Isaiah) already predicted long ago concerning the liberation of the city from the siege of Sennacherib? Furthermore, the Church celebrates God because He has placed the city into a heap. But were the Jews and the faithful to celebrate God because Samaria had been devastated? This matter was rather one for condoling and mourning. Nor can these things predicted be understood of Samaria. For Samaria was not placed into a heap and ruin by Shalmaneser, so that it is not a City and is not rebuilt forever, who, having only deported the Israelites, brought colonies there. Nor was the City κατ' ἐξοχὴν or called by the name of a strong city absolutely, nor is Samaria pointed out anywhere as a house of strangers, or understood above others. Furthermore, just as a strong people is to celebrate God, so also a city of robust nations is said to be about to venerate the same. Therefore, this is not to be understood of the terror and fear of neighboring nations, but rather of the filial fear of the faithful converted from the nations to the true God. Moreover, those general praises of God, 'He has been a strength to the poor,' etc., are wrongly restricted by Grotius to the Jerusalemites pressed by siege. The general description of the power of enemies is determined to the Assyrians beside the point. But above all, the feast of fat things is very badly transformed in a contrary sense into the destruction and slaughter of the Assyrians, so that to precipitate death is to avert the dangers of death, and eternity is time not so long-lasting, while, to wit, Hezekiah lived. Finally, when God is said to be about to wipe away the tear from EVERY face, it is perversely restricted to the besieged Jerusalemites. By which art of interpreting, anything could easily be elicited from anything. Hence also it never came into the mind of anyone, whether from Jewish or Christian Interpreters, as far as is known from their monuments. However, Doctors explain this Eucharistic hymn in various ways. Some wish that what had been predicted in the preceding Chapters concerning the ruin of various peoples, and concerning the people of God, is celebrated by this hymn: since the Prophet, after those horrible disasters had been proposed to him as if in a picture, betakes himself to God, persuaded entirely that God, amidst these tempests of His judgments, still wishes to provide for His Church, and to bring back into His power those who had previously been strangers. Thus Calvin and Junius. Our blessed Brentius also understands it generally concerning the enemies of the Church and concerning the liberation which befell the Church from Christ: for he believes Him to be addressed in the present hymn. He addresses Him as Lord God, whom at the end of the previous chapter he said reigns in Zion and Jerusalem. But this is Jesus Christ our Savior. Wherefore he also addresses Christ in this encomium, and acknowledges Him to be his true Lord God! But what does Christ GOD do worthy of praise and commendation? It follows. Therefore I praise thee, because thou doest wonderful things, and thy counsels from afar are true and firm. I do not doubt, however, that what Paul writes in 2 Cor. 1: 'How many soever are the promises of GOD, through him (Christ) they are also, and through him Amen,' is taken from this place of Isaiah. For the sense is: Christ admirably administers and preserves His Church, and completes in it all His counsels and promises. For although His promises seem to be deferred for a long time, so that they are argued of falsehood by the impious, yet they are also and Amen. Nothing is either truer or firmer than them. He seems to complete them slowly. But He completes them opportunely, gloriously, and admirably. What, therefore, are those promises? What are those counsels of Christ? These consist of two parts. One is that Christ is about to cast down and oppress all the kingdoms of the world which persecute His Church, and all impious tyrants, whether Kings or private individuals, who afflict the pious. The other is that Christ is about to liberate His Church, however afflicted and despised in this world, from all evils, and to preserve it perpetually. These were the counsels of Christ from the beginning. These are the promises of God from the very origin of the world. This God established when He said: 'The seed of the woman shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for his heel.' This God wills, when He says to Abraham: 'I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee. And in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed.' The first part of the counsel, therefore, according to Brentius, is celebrated here, that God casts down and devastates the most powerful Monarchies and kingdoms of this world, which persecute the Church, which are understood by the fortified cities, towns, and palaces of strangers, and this so that others, however strong and robust, may learn the fear of God, acknowledge the Majesty of God, and be converted to God and live. The other, that God has decreed that He will preserve His people and His Church in every affliction: 'Thou art a strength to the poor, a refuge in the tempest,' etc. From which explanation those depart little who think that the Prophet has dealt with the Babylonian captivity in the preceding [chapters], and that therefore the liberation is specifically celebrated from the same present hymn. Or those who wish the most recent destruction of Jerusalem and the conversion of the nations to be repeated here specifically: because general sentences in Psalms and hymns, especially when the benefits of God are proclaimed, are conceived in such a way that they look to certain times on the occasion of the Prophets: although they are applied to all times with a certain respect without injury to the text. Therefore, by the City which is said to be placed into a heap and ruin, Cyril understands every power of the wicked and of adversaries, and before others Satan himself: Others, as we have already observed, understand the kingdoms and cities which oppose themselves to the Church, which are the houses of strangers: others wish Babylon to be designated specifically; to whom Osiander and the Vinarie Paraphrasts have acceded. Blessed Luther, when he has explained the preceding things concerning the most recent devastation of Jerusalem, understands by the City and the strong city Jerusalem, which became a stranger to the Lord on account of infidelity. Likewise Jerome. The city once strong is understood to be Jerusalem, which has become the house of strangers: of whom the Savior says in the Psalm: The children of strangers have lied to me, the children of strangers have grown old and have halted from their paths. When this city has been destroyed, it shall not be built up forever, so that the thousand-year kingdom and the golden and jeweled Jerusalem dreams may rest. But Jerusalem having been destroyed for its impiety, a strong people shall praise the Lord: The following verse shows who the strong people is, The city of the strong nations shall fear thee: While those are blaspheming, the people of the nations shall fear thee. For the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. And a strong people shall praise thee, and the city of the strong nations shall fear thee, that is, the Church gathered from the nations, etc. Some Rabbis, as Jerome observes, understand Rome by the overturned City, which is to be utterly destroyed, since it has done all the things against God that the Prophet had mentioned above. Most Papists, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, interpret that City, which is to be placed in a tomb, concerning the orb of the lands, which in its greater part is the City of the impious. For they wish it to have been acted upon concerning the consummation of the age beforehand: Here, therefore, in the Eucharistic hymn, the Saints give thanks to God, because their impious and proud enemies having been depressed, and the world having been devastated, they themselves have arrived at the gate of salvation. It is better, however, to understand the city, which in any way opposes itself to the Church of God, as the house of strangers, or of infidels, in general, and specifically Babylon, which was about to afflict the people of God and devastate the land of the Jews, but in turn was to be placed by God into a mound and ruin. On account of this, the strong people, i.e., the faithful, who are strong and constant in faith, or even the most powerful nations, if the words added are taken by way of explanation (a city of robust nations), having recognized the majesty of God, will be converted to the true God, and will fear Him. Which was also fulfilled when Cyrus the Monarch propagated the true Religion in his Empire, Ezra V and VI. Rightly B. Luther on this passage: 'on this account the strong people will praise you.' Hitherto a small and stubborn people in a corner of Judea worshipped you; in its place you will have an ample and most powerful people, namely all nations. And you will note this passage, because it says openly what the worship of the New Testament is: not sacrifices, not the building of temples, not Masses, etc. But the praise and fear of GOD, because among the nations the sacrifice of praise will be sacrificed, and God is feared, so that hypocrisy may be excluded. For the fear of God is worship placed not in vestments or other external pomp, but in the heart. The following verses teach that the discourse is about spiritual fortitude, which is in the Lord: to whom Christ himself is said to have been made a fortitude to the poor.

Latin:

Vers. 3. POPVLVS FORTIS :) Constans in religio- ne; nempe Hierosolymitæ.

CIVITAS GENTIVM ROBVSTARVM TIME- BIT TE) Enallage: id est, civitates vicinæ exemplo hoc terrebuntur.

HYmnum præsentem de victoria adversus Sen- nacheribum, decantatum vult Grotius, quod Samaria quidem justo Dei judicio à Salmanassare vastata; Hierosolyma vero à Sennacheribi obsidio- ne liberata sit. Sed quum agnoscat laudationem Dei hic contineri, velut canendam, ubi ea, quæ mo- do dixit Propheta, evenerint, ostensum autem jam fuerit, caput præcedens neq; de Salmanassare, neq; de Sennacheribo intelligi posse; in aprico jam est, alio hymnum Eucharisticum necessario referen- dum esse. Neque vero permittunt verba ipsius hymni, ut eo referatur. Cogitationes ANTIQUAS FIDELES prædicat Esaias: Domine, Deus meus es tu, exaltabo te, confitebor nomini tuo, quo- niam fecisti mirabilia, cogitationes antiquas fideles, Amen. Quæ de æterni decreti, de redemtione & salute nostra, executione interpretatur Hierony- mus. Similiter Cyrillus: Consilium autem tan- quam antiquum & res miras appellat humanitatis unigeniti mysterium, & quæ per eam fuerunt per uni- versam terram instaurata. Grotius vertit: Confi- lia tua pridem (supple prædicta) jam vera ac fir- ma apparent. Num vero illa, (hæc vaticinante Esaia) erant jam pridem prædicta de liberatione urbis à Sennacheribi obsidione? Porro celebrat Ecclesia Deum, quod civitatem posuerit in tumu- lum. Num vero ideo Judæi ac fideles Deum cele- braturi erant, quod Samaria vastata fuerit? Ma- teria hæc condolendi & lugendi potius erat. Nec de Samaria prædicata hæc intelligi possunt. Nam Samaria neque in tumulum & ruinam posita fuit à Salmanassare, ut non sit Civitas & in sempiternum non ædificetur, qui translatis solum Israëlitis colonias illuc traduxit. Neq; Civitas κατ' ἐξοχὴν aut ur- bis fortis nomine absolute nuncupata fuit, neq; do- mus alienarum uspiam indigitatur, aut præ aliis in- telligitur Samaria. Ulterius ut populus fortis De- um celebraturus, ita & civitas gentium robustarum veneratura eundem dicitur. Non ergo hoc de ter- rore ac metu gentium vicinarum, sed de filiali potius timore fidelium è gentibus ad verum Deum conver- sarum intelligendum. Adhæc generalia illa elogia Dei, Factus est fortitudo pauperi &c. perperam re- stringuntur à Grotio ad Hierosolymitanos obsidione pressos. Generalis potestatis hostium descriptio præter rem ad Assyrios determinatur. Sed impri- mis pessime convivium pinguium transformatur sensu contrario in excidium & internecionem Assy- riorum, ut mortem præcipitare sit pericula mortis avertere, æternitas tempus sit non adeo diuturnum, dum sc. vixit Ezechias. Denique cum Deus lacru- mam ab OMNI facie ablaturus dicitur, per- verse id ad obsessos Hierosolymitanos restringitur. Quo interpretandi artificio quidlibet ex quolibet elici facile posset. Inde etiam nulli unquam in mentem venit hujusmodi interpretatio, seu è Ju- dæis seu è Christianis Interpretibus, quantum ex eorum monumentis notum est. Explicant autem hymnum istum Eucharisticum Doctores diversi- mode. Nonnulli quæ de variorum populorum ruina, deq; populo Dei superioribus prædicta fue- rant Capitibus, hoc hymno celebrari volunt: si- quidem Propheta, postquam ipsi horrendæ clades velut in pictura propositæ erant, sese recipiat ad Deum, persuasus omnino, Deum inter hasce tem- pestates judiciorum suorum velle adhuc consulere Ecclesiæ suæ, & redigere in potestatem suam, qui antea fuerant alieni. Sic Calvinus & Junius. B. Brentius noster generaliter etiam intelligit de hosti- bus Ecclesiæ & de liberatione, quæ Ecclesiæ obtigit à Christo: hunc enim compellari præsenti hymno credit. Alloquitur eum Dominum Deum, quem in fine prioris capitis dixit regnare in Zion & Hieru- salem. Hic vero est Jesus Christus Servator noster. Quare & Christum in hoc encomio alloquitur, & agnoscit eum esse verum Dominum Deum suum! Sed quid facit Christus DEUS laude & commen- datione dignum? Sequitur. Ideo laudo te, quia fa- cis admiranda, & consilia tua à longe sunt vera & firma. Non dubito autem, quin quod Paulus in 2. Cor. 1. scribit: Quotquot sunt promissiones DEI, per ipsum (Christum) sunt etiam, & per ipsum A- men, ex hoc Esaiæ loco acceptum sit. Sensus enim est: Christus admirabiliter administrat & servat suam Ecclesiam, & complet in ea omnia sua consilia, & promissiones. Etsi enim promissiones ejus viden- tur in longum differri, ut arguantur ab impiis men- dacii, tamen sunt etiam & Amen. Nihil iis nec ve- rius est, nec firmius. Videtur eas tarde complere. Sed complet eas opportune, gloriose, & admirabiliter. Quæ ergo sunt illæ promissiones? Quæ sunt illa con- silia Christi? Hæc constant duabus partibus. Una est, quod Christus omnia regna mundi, quæ perse- quuntur Ecclesiam suam, & omnes impios tyrannos sive Reges, sive privatos, qui affligunt pios sit dejectu- rus, & oppressurus. Altera est, quod Christus Eccle- siam suam, quamvis afflictissimam & contemptissi- mam in hoc mundo sit liberaturus ab omnibus malis, & servaturus perpetuo. Hæc fuerunt consilia Christi ab initio. Hæ sunt promissiones Dei jam inde ab exor- dio mundi. Hoc Deus constituit, cum dixit: Se- men mulieris conteret caput tuum, & tu insidiabe- ris calcaneo ejus. Hoc Deus vult, cum ad Abraha- mum ait: Benedicam benedicentibus tibi, male- dicam maledicentibus tibi. Atq; in te benedicen- tur universæ cognationes terræ. Prior ergo pars consilii, juxta Brentium, hic celebrata est, quod Deus dejiciat & vastet potentissimas Monarchias & regna hujus mundi, quæ persequuntur Eccle- siam, quæ per munitas urbes, civitates & palatia alienorum intelliguntur, idq; ut alii, quamvis fortes & robusti, discant timorem Dei, agnoscant Maje- statem Dei & convertantur ad Deum & vivant. Altera, quod decrevit Deus, se populum & Eccle- siam suam in omni afflictione servaturum: Tu es fortitudo pauperi, refugium in tempestate &c. A qua explicatione parum abeunt, qui de captivi- tate Babylonica in præcedentibus Prophetam egisse, adeoque liberationem ex eodem hymno præsenti speciatim celebrari, existimant. Aut qui destructio- nem Hierosolymæ novissimam, & conversionem gen- tium hic peculiariter repeti volunt: quia genera- les sententiæ in Psalmis & hymnis, maxime cum prædicantur Dei beneficia, ita concipiuntur, ut ex occasione Prophetarum certa tempora respi- ciant: tametsi omnibus temporibus certo respe- ctu citra textus injuriam, applicantur. Per Civita- tem ergo, quæ in tumulum & ruinam posita dicitur, Cyrillus unamquamq; potestatem improborum, & adversariorum, & ante alios ipsum Satanam: Alii, uti jam observavimus, regna & civitates, quæ se op- ponunt Ecclesiæ, quæ domus alienorum sunt, intelli- gunt: alii peculiariter Babylonem designari vo- lunt; quibus accessere Osiander, & Paraphrasta Vinarienses. B. Lutherus, quum superiora de va- statione Hierosolymæ novissima exposuerit, per Civitatem & urbem fortem intelligit Hierosoly- mam, quæ aliena à Domino facta propter infidelita- tem. Similiter Hieronymus. Civitas quondam fortis Hierusalem intelligitur, quæ facta est domus alienorum: de quibus Salvator dicit in Psalmo: Filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi, filii alieni invetera- verunt & claudicaverunt in semitis suis. Hæc civitas cum destructa fuerit, in æternum non ædificabitur, ut mille annorum regnum, & aurea Hierusalem atque gemmata somnia conquiescant. Destructa autem Hierusalem pro impietate sua laudabit Dominum populus fortis: Quis sit autem populus fortis sequens versus ostendit, Civitas gentium robustarum time- bit te: Illis blasphemantibus, gentium populus te timebit. Principium enim sapientiæ timor Do- mini. Laudabitque te populus fortis, & civitas gentium robustarum timebit te, h. e. Ecclesia de gentibus &c. congregata. Rabbini nonnulli per Civitatem subversam Romam, observante Hieronymo, intelligunt, quæ penitus delen- da sit, quum Deo adversa omnia, quæ supra di- xerat Propheta, fecerit. Pontificii plerique, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius Civitatem illam, quæ in tumulum ponenda, interpretantur de terrarum orbe, qui majori sui parte est Civitas impiorum. Volunt enim de consummatione se- culi antea actum esse: Hic ergo hymno Euchari- stico Sanctos gratias agere Deo, quod impiis & su- perbis hostibus suis depressis, mundoq; vastato ipsi ad salutis portam devenerint. Præstat autem vel in genere civitatem quamvis Ecclesiæ Dei sese oppo- nentem domum alienorum, seu infidelium intellige- re, ac speciatim Babylonem, quæ populum Dei af- flictura & terram Judæorum vastatura, sed vicissim à Deo in tumulum & ruinam ponenda erat. Ob hoc populus fortis, h. e. fideles, qui in fide fortes & constantes sunt, vel etiam potentissimæ gentes, si ver- ba addita κατ᾽ ἐπεξήγησιν accipiantur (civitas gen- tium robustarum) agnita Dei majestate ad Deum verum convertetur, eumq; timebit. Quod imple- tum etiam est, cum Cyrus Monarcha veram Reli- gionem in Imperio suo propagavit Esdr. V. & VI. Recte B. Lutherus in hunc locum: super hoc lauda- bit te populus fortis. Hactenus te parvus & pertinax populus in angulo Judææ coluit, illius loco habe- bis amplum & potentissimum populum, omnes gentes scilicet. Et notabis hunc locum, quia aperte dicit, qui sit Novi Testamenti cultus: non sacrificia, non ædificatio templorum, non Missæ &c. Sed laus & timor DEI, quod in gentibus sacrificium laudis sacrificabitur, & Deus timetur, ut exclusa sit hypo- crisis. Timor enim Dei est cultus non in vestibus aut alia externa pompa, sed in corde positus. De fortitu- dine spirituali, quæ est in Domino, sermonem esse, sequentia docent: quibus Christus ipse dicitur pauperi fortitudo factus.

## 25:4
Verse 4. YOU HAVE BEEN MADE A FORTITUDE TO THE POOR) Jerusalem being pressed by a grave siege.

These things do not concern Jerusalem alone: they celebrate the grace and salvation which the Lord provides to all the faithful: And which was to happen not so much to the Israelite people according to the flesh after the Babylonian captivity, as to be exhibited to the true and spiritual Israelites both at that time of liberation and under the New Testament: whence they understand these things concerning the elect in the other life, celebrating past benefits: We glorify you, O God, because, when there was no strength in us and we were utterly despairing of our own powers, then you were made a fortitude and strength to us, as Oecolampadius has in this place. It is a general eulogy of divine protection, by which it is pleasantly and sweetly set forth what kind of person Christ shows himself to be to his faithful. This is a sweet description of Christ, says B. Luther, what kind of person God is and what kind of people or kingdom he has, just as he himself describes it in Matthew XI. Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. Which is to say, his kingdom is a kingdom of the poor and afflicted who are to be comforted: and therefore it is added, A HOPE FOR THE CONTEMNED FROM THE WHIRLWIND, A SHADOW FROM THE HEAT, i.e., you are the trust of those who are tossed by the whirlwind and tempests, i.e., who suffer persecution on account of the word of God, who are pressed by sin and their own flesh and Satan. In all these dangers we have no other refuge against all the assaults of all evils.

FOR THE SPIRIT OF THE ROBUST.) The wrath of the Assyrians: thus also shortly in the section.

AS A CROWD IMPELLING A WALL.) It was shaking our walls in the manner of a whirlwind.

There is nothing here about the Assyrians specifically, nothing about the shaking of walls: concerning which there is not a jot in history, indeed the contrary is established from the promise of God in Isaiah 37. Thus says the Lord concerning the King of the Assyrians: He will not enter this City, and will not cast an arrow there, and a shield will not come before it, and no soldier will cast up a mound in its circuit. Who, therefore, would have shaken the walls of the city like a whirlwind? This, therefore, is what the faithful proclaim: that the Lord is a shadow of it from the heat of afflictions, when the spirit of the robust rages against them with great impetus, like a whirlwind impelling a wall, no otherwise than if a grave tempest were borne against a wall. As heat in thirst, more correctly in dry (land makes herbs wither, so that at length they dry up, thus) you will humble the tumult (or insolence) of strangers (infidel peoples) (so that they may be ashamed) AND AS HEAT UNDER A BURNING CLOUD (Hebr. so that the DRY may be preserved IN THE SHADOW OF A CLOUD, that is, the cloud meanwhile overshadowing other herbs, so that they do not perish with these) But the shoot (or seedling) OF THE STRONG (the raging tyrants) YOU WILL MAKE TO WITHER. (That is, You, O Lord, will at length send heat, that is, most grave calamities, upon the persecutors of the Church, so that they may wither and perish, like seedlings which dry up from the excessive heat of the Sun. Meanwhile, in these public disasters you will preserve your Church: just as if some herbs covered by the shadow of a cloud remain green and vivid. Thus the Osiandrian version and paraphrase. To which Brentius had preceded: Just as heat dries up herbs in a desert or dry place, so also you cause the strength of Tyrants, although they seem to be green and flourish, to be broken and their shoot to dry up and perish. Meanwhile, however, your people will rest in you and will be saved, just as men are refreshed by the shadow of a cloud. Which is also the sentiment of the most recent German version of B. Luther: 'You humble the insolence of strangers/like the heat in a dry place/so that the heat may destroy the vines of the tyrants/and the cloud nevertheless give shade:' although he rendered it a little differently in the Latin Commentary and the earlier German version: 'Turn,' he says there in the Enarrat. Annot. XXXII, 'you will humble the tumult of others, as heat in the desert, heat in the shadow of a cloud will humble the branch of the tyrants.' He says 'shadow of a cloud' for what we in German call 'Meeltau' [mildew], that harmful daily dew by which crops are scorched, and the leaves of trees and vines wither and perish. He understood the whole sentence, therefore, concerning the tyrants alone, and thus translated it: 'you humble the insolence of strangers/like a heat in the desert/so that the heat may destroy the vines of the tyrants with the shadow of the cloud/that is/with mildew,' as the marginal gloss had it at that time. And thus concerning the impious alone, according to the Vulgate version, AS HEAT UNDER A SCORCHING CLOUD, the Jesuits, Sanctius, Corn. a Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius interpret it, and they wish to allude to the sentence of Christ the judge sitting on a cloud, who will horribly torment and burn the impious, as if to say: With most vehement heat, such as is wont to be, which is born from solar rays united and constricted under a dense cloud, which eternal heat without refreshment will be far different from the momentary heat of the pious, to temper which God presents Himself as A SHADE v. 4. But the most recent version of B. Luther is simpler, plainer, and more convenient; so that these things may be referred both to the pious and to the impious; that the latter indeed are scorched by the heat of divine wrath, but the former are refreshed by the gracious shade of the cloud. Thus the words flow in the Hebrew source, and its force remains for the distinctive accent Athnach כְּחֹרֶב בְּצִיּוֹן שְׁאוֹן זָרִים תַּכְנִיעַ as heat in dryness (or in a dry place he unfolds the herbs) the tumult of strangers you will humble: Heat (I say of divine wrath) in the shade of a cloud (protecting the faithful) the shoot and branch of tyrants he will humble. Thus these things explain each other, but so that for the sake of the faithful consolation may be intermixed. Which explanation was also approved by Oecolampadius. Namely, the advent of the Lord to the just is the dew of the cloud, which nevertheless will make the shoot of the strong to wither, that is, will afflict the tyrants, taking them away, and cutting off whatever is green and very strong in them, just as the heat had made the gourd of Jonah to wither. The version of Zwingli is more alien: nor does the translation or interpretation of Calvin deserve consideration: who by the heat understands the wrath of the impious against the faithful, and by the shadow of the cloud, rain or a shower; nor that of Junius and Piscator, who wish the tumult of the impious to be compared to the driest heat, and divine protection to the densest shadow: but they introduce a twisted gloss to the latter words: You have dampened the tumult of the strangers with a shadow of a cloud, as it was suitable to the shoot of the tyrants. Which responded to the shoot of the tyrants: that it is forced, no one fails to see. Nor is the explanation of Ludovicus de Dieu worthy of approval; as the heat in a dry place is the tumult of strangers: you depress the heat with the shadow of a dense cloud: the excision of the truculent will testify. The latter does not fit the manner of speaking. For the Prophets are not accustomed to speak thus: Excision will testify to that. And the same thing would be declared or proven by that means by the same. For what else is that humiliation, than the excision of the truculent? Nor was the distinctive accent Athnach to be neglected. That the accent serves the modulation of voices rather than the distinctions of sentences is a precarious hypothesis: which we think should by no means be conceded.

Latin:

Vers. 4. FACTVS ES FORTITVDO PAVPERI) Hierosolymis gravi obsidione pressis.

Non hæc solum Hierosolymam concernunt: gratiam & salutem celebrant, quam Dominus omnibus fidelibus præstat: Et quæ non tam popu- lo Israëlitico secundum carnem post captivitatem Babylonicam, quam veris & spiritualibus Israëlitis eventùra erat tum isto liberationis tempore, tum sub Novo Testamento exhibenda: unde de electis in altera vita hæc intelligunt, præterita beneficia celebrantibus: Glorificamus te, Deus, quoniam, quum nihil nobis esset roboris & de viribus nostris prorsus desperaremus, tum factus es nobis fortitudo & robur, ut Oecolampadius habet in h. l. Generale est elogium divinæ protectionis, quo jucunde ac sua- viter sistitur, qualem se Christus fidelibus suis præ- beat. Est hæc suavis descriptio Christi, ait B. Luthe- rus, qualis sit Deus & qualem habeat populum seu regnum, sicut ipse id describit Matth. XI. Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis, ego refi- ciam vos. Quod sc. suum regnum sit regnum conso- landorum pauperum, afflictorum: & ideo additur, contemtorum SPES A TVRBINE, UMBRA- CULUM AB ÆSTU, q. d. tu es fiducia eorum, qui jactantur à turbine & tempestatibus, h. e. qui pariuntur persequutionem propter verbum Dei, qui premuntur peccato & sua ipsorum carne ac Sa- tana. In his omnibus periculis non habemus aliud refugium contra omnes omnium malorum insultus.

SPIRITVS ENIM ROBUSTORUM.) Ira Assyrio- rum: sic & mox §.

QVASI TVRBA IMPELLENS PARIETEM.) Tur- binis modo muros nostros quatiebat.

Nihil hic de Assyriis in specie, nihil de muro- rum concussione: qua de etiam in historia nullus apex habetur, imo contrarium ex promisso Dei constat Es. 37. Hæc dicit Dominus de Rege Assyrio- rum: Non intrabit Civitatem hanc, & non jaciet illuc sagittam, & non veniet ante eam clypeus, & non miles in circuitu ejus aggerem. Qui ergo concussif- set muros civitatis instar turbinis? Hocitaq; est, quod prædicant fideles: quod Dominus umbra- culum ipsius sit ab æstu afflictionum, quando spiri- tus robustorum in eos magno impetu grassantur, sicut turbo impellens parietem, non aliter quam si gravis tempestas in murum adversum feratur. Si- cut æstus in siti, rectius in arida (terra flaccescere facit herbas, ut tandem arescant, sic) tumultum (seu insolentiam) alienorum (populorum infide- lium) humiliabis (ut pudesiant) ET QUASI CALORE SUB NUBE TORRENTE (Hebr. ut conservetur ARIDA IN UMBRA NUBIS, id est, obumbrante interim nube alias herbas, ne cum his pereant) Propaginem autem (seu plan- tulam) FORTIUM (tyrannorum grassatorum) MARCESCERE FACIES. (Id est, Tu Domine tandem æstum, id est, gravissimas cala- mitates, immittes Ecclesiæ persecutoribus, ut marcescant ac pereant, sicut plantulæ, quæ nimio Solis ardore exarent. Interim in publicis istis cla- dibus conservabis Ecclesiam tuam: ac si aliquæ herbæ umbra nubis tectæ virides & vividæ manent. Ita Osiandrina versio & paraphrasis. Cui præive- rat Brentius: Quemadmodum æstus exsiccat herbas in loco deserto seu arido, ita etiam efficis, ut vires Ty- rannorum, quamvis videantur virere ac florere, frangantur & surculus eorum exarescat & pereat. Interim autem populus tuus in te conquiescet & ser- vabitur, sicut homines recreantur ab umbra nubis. Quæ etiam sententia est versionis Germanicæ B. Lutheri novissimæ: Du demuͤtigest der Frembden Ungestuͤm/wie die Hitze an einem duͤrren Ort/ daß die Hitze die Reben der Tyrannen verderbe/und die Wolcke dennoch Schatten gebe: etsi paulo aliter in Commentario Latino & priori Germanica ver- sione reddiderit: Verte, inquit illic in Enarrat. An- not. XXXII. tumultum aliorum humiliabis, sicut æstus in deserto, æstus in umbra nubis palmitem ty- rannorum humiliabit. Umbram nubis dicit, quod nos Germanice Meeltau, nocivum illum rorem diur- num, quo aduruntur sata, & folia arborum & vi- tium marcescunt & pereunt. De solis ergo tyran- nis totam sententiam intellexit, atq; ita transtulit: du demuͤthigest der Frembden Ungestuͤm/wie eine Hitze in der Wuͤsten/daß die Hitze den Reben der Tyrannen verderbe mit den Schatten der Wolcke/ das ist/mit Meelthau, uti tum habuit glossa margi- nalis. Atq; ita de solis impiis, juxta versionem Vul- gatam, QUASI CALORE SUB NUBE TOR- RENTE, interpretantur Jesuitæ, Sanctius, Corn. a Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, & alludi volunt ad sententiam Christi judicis in nube sedentis, qui im- pios horrende cruciabit, & uret, q. d. Æstu vehe- mentissimo, qualis solet esse, qui ex solaribus radiis sub densa nube unitis & constrictis nascitur, qui æternus æstus sine refrigerio longe alius erit, quam momenta- neus piorum æstus, cui temperando se exhibet UM- BRACULUM DEUS v. 4. Sed simplicior, pla- nior & convenientior est novissima B. Lutheri ver- sio; ut tum ad pios, tum ad impios hæc referantur; quod hi quidem adurantur æstu iræ divinæ, illi vero recreentur umbra nubis gratiosa. Sic fluunt verba in fonte Ebræo, & remanet vis sua accentui distin- ctivo Athnach כְּחֹרֶב בְּצִיּוֹן שְׁאוֹן זָרִים תַּכְנִיעַ sicut æstus in siccitate (vel loco sicco herbas explicat) tu- multu alienorũ humiliabis: חֹרֶב בְּצֵל עָב זְמִיר עָרִיצִים יַעֲנֶה Æstus (inquam iræ divinæ) in umbra nu- bis (protegente fideles) propaginem & palmi- tem tyrannorum humiliabit. Ita explicant se hæc mutuo, sed ut fidelium causa consolatio im- misceatur. Quæ explicatio etiam Oecolampa- dio probata. Nimirum adventus Domini justis est ros nubis, qui tamen propaginem fortium marce- scere faciet, h. e. affliget tyrannos, illos auferens, & amputans, quicquid in eis vel viride & prævalidum est, sicut æstus torrere fecerat cucurbitam Jonæ. Alienior est versio Zwinglii: neq; Calvini trans- latio, aut interpretatio calculum meretur: qui per æstum iram impiorum adversus fideles, & per umbram nubis pluviam vel imbrem intelligit; neq; Junii & Piscatoris, qui tumultum impiorum æstui siccissimo, protectionem divinam umbræ densissimæ comparari volunt: Posterioribus vero verbis contortam glossam inferunt: Du hast der Frembden Unges stüm gedämpffet mit einem Schatten der Wolcke, als dieselbe dem Schößling der Tyrannen füglich war. Qui propagini tyrannorum respondebat: quæ coacta esse, nemo non videt. Neq; Ludovici de Dieu suffragio digna est explicatio; sicut æstus in loco arido est tumultuatio extraneorum: deprimis æstum umbra densæ nubis: excisio truculentorum testificabitur. Postremum non congruit modo lo- quendi. Non solent enim ita loqui Prophetæ: Excisio id testificabitur. Et declararetur vel proba- retur eo pacto idem per idem. Nam quid aliud illa humiliatio, quam excisio truculentorum? neque negligendus erat accentus Athnach distinctivus. Modulationi vocum potius, quam distinctionibus sententiarum accentus inservire, hypothesis preca- ria est: quam minime concedendam putamus.

## 25:6
A FEAST OF FAT THINGS) The vengeance of God is often compared by the Prophets to a feast, because it both consumes enemies, as foods are consumed, and brings joy to God.

WINES ON THE LEES) From the best wine.

There are not wanting those who explain it concerning a bloody feast: since in the Scriptures vengeance is compared to a feast, and the wine of the wrath of God, and the cup of tribulations and vengeance not rarely occur in the Prophets. Luther himself in his Enarrations, when he believes that the most recent destruction of the Jews had been treated of before, explains it thus. Concerning the slaughter of the impious, the Lord says: He will prepare a feast on this mountain: that is, he will gather the whole people in Jerusalem, there he will allow them to be slaughtered by the Romans. The fat things are the rich. For marrow signifies whatever is most tender. Thus the marrow of wheat, that is, the best wheat: wines on the lees; rightly, of dregs expressed; that is, he will so destroy, that not even the dregs are left. Similarly Oecolampadius: A feast of fat things and of those on the lees and of marrow signifies the wrath and indignation of God, just as Scripture frequently indicates the same by the name of a cup. Zech. 12. Behold I will make a cup of reeling to all the peoples round about, that is, a cup of drunkenness. Lam. 4. the cup shall pass through unto thee also and thou shalt be drunken. And Jer. 21. A golden cup in the hand of the Lord. But no one will easily be found who has explained it with Grotius concerning the slaughter of Sennacherib. Nor is it obscure from the words and context of the Prophet that the discourse here is concerning the Evangelical Feast: which is prepared for the faithful in the kingdom of Christ. Because first, all things here are joyful, and express the hilarity of a feast: The Lord of hosts will make unto all peoples in this mountain a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things, of marrow, of wines on the lees. Nor indeed is the discourse about joy being prepared for God from the vengeance of enemies, but about the joy which will accrue to the peoples through such a sumptuous feast. Furthermore, that is not to be prepared by the Lord for one people only, not for the Jews or the Jerusalemites, but for ALL PEOPLES, as the Prophet says. Therefore these things cannot be understood concerning vengeance against enemies, much less concerning the slaughter of the Assyrians: but concerning the Feast, which is prepared for all nations and peoples, which is none other than the Evangelical Feast. Moreover, this feast was to be prepared on Mount Zion, which the Prophet points out demonstratively, ON THIS MOUNTAIN. But the spiritual feast is prepared on Mount Zion, because in the Jerusalem temple not only did Christ himself teach, and propose the apparatus of grace and the delicacies of the heavenly banquet, but from Mount Zion the Gospel was also to be published to the whole world Isa. 2, 3. And the scepter of the kingdom of Christ was to be sent forth Psalm 110, 4. And whom shall we have as a more certain interpreter of this most sumptuous Feast, than him who prepared it for us? who, comparing the kingdom of Heaven to a feast and a great Supper and a wedding, openly teaches which feast Isaiah predicted, Matt. 22. and Luke 14. Although also in the O.T. that spiritual and Evangelical Feast is everywhere set forth Ps. 22, 27. Ps. 23, 5. Psalm 36, 9. Jerem. 9, 2. seqq. Cant. 6. indeed by our Prophet himself c. 55, 1. seq. C. 65, 13.
