For in this alone we are taught how true trust in the mercy of God in Christ Jesus is to be awaited. YOUR NAME, the Prophet adds, AND YOUR MEMORIAL ARE IN THE DESIRE OF THE SOUL. MY SOUL HAS DESIRED YOU IN THE NIGHT: BUT ALSO WITH MY SPIRIT IN MY INMOST PARTS I WILL WATCH FOR YOU FROM THE MORNING. What is it that the faithful receive with such eagerness and desire, if not the doctrine of the Gospel and the benefits proposed in it? There is the name and memorial of God, by which he has graciously manifested himself, which the Prophet received with the highest desire of his soul. There Christ is exhibited with all his benefits, whom he desired so greatly. Whence Osiander refers this to the desire for the advent of the Messiah: My soul has desired you, etc., that is, I am all burning night and day, that I may know more and more about Christ from the Evangelical promises: and would that such happiness might befall me, that I might see you, Son of God, incarnate in this world. The judgments of the Lord, says Brentius in this place, are not here the law or afflictions, but are that path and way of which it was spoken before, namely the Gospel of our God Jesus Christ. Similarly also the name and memorial of God in this place are the preaching of the Gospel, by which God is known and celebrated. So also blessed Cyril: The way of the pious is UPRIGHT. For he who would not be upright and level would have nothing at all of the precipitous, when by speaking the word of faith we are justified and through holy Baptism we are abundantly and perfectly cleansed. Therefore those who enter this straight way say, we have hoped in your name and in the memory, which our soul desires. For all our hope is cast upon Christ, of whom we are also always mindful, having this desire, because we have also been saved from thence. This is Cyril. The pious therefore say, Lord, since the rectitude of your judgments, or of the Gospel, is so great that it leads us straight to righteousness and heavenly happiness, what else remains but that we should receive it and believe it, and that which promises to us, let us hope with certain and firm confidence! But this must be done by us not sluggishly; but with the whole affection of our heart, day and night: For then men can attain true justice, when your judgments shall be on the earth, that is, when the Gospel of Christ is preached sincerely and purely on the earth. WHEN YOU SHALL HAVE MADE (in Hebrew, when they shall be,) YOUR JUDGMENTS ON THE EARTH, THE INHABITANTS OF THE CITY SHALL LEARN JUSTICE. Thus also Blessed Luther and the Weimar Paraphrasts v. 8 & 9. For we wait for you, O Lord, in the way of your right (of your judgments,) the desire of the heart is toward your name and your memorial, (Luther's marginal gloss, to your Word, in which you have established the memorial of your name,) With my heart I desire you in the night, moreover with my spirit within me I watch early for you (that I may increase more and more from your Word in the saving knowledge). For where your law goes in the land, the inhabitants of the earth learn justice, (from the word of the Gospel men learn how they ought to be justified before God, and to apply themselves to justice in their life.) Memorial, says Blessed Luther in Enarr. h. l., of the name of the Lord was in the law, that he had led them out of Egypt. Today in the N. T. the memorial and name of the Lord is that he did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all. This memory, this benefit we celebrate not only in sermons, but from the desire of the soul, because we believe that Christ is our wisdom, justice, sanctification and resurrection, that we may thus trust not in our works, but in the merit of Christ. WHEN YOU SHALL HAVE MADE YOUR JUDGMENTS ON THE EARTH. It is a notable passage concerning the external preaching of the word, that it ought not to return without fruit. He calls them JUDGMENTS, because the Gospel condemns the works and pursuits of all men, and offers only the merits of Christ, upon which we may rely. In the absence of these judgments, men are seduced and impiety is learned under the guise of justice. Therefore, wherever the word is not, there neither is justice. This is Luther: whose observation is worthy of cedar, why the Gospel in the Scriptures is called a judgment. For in it the judgment of God is set forth. In it true justice is exhibited, outside of which God wills that no one be pronounced or judged just. Oecolampadius does not disapprove of this sense, that it can be understood as the profound judgments of God of predestination and justification in faith alone: although he also interprets it concerning the judgment of chastisement with Calvin. Jerome, interpreting the seventh verse, the path of the JUST, understands it through the just Christ: and therefore he continues to comment thus: The path of this just one therefore is straight, or, (that I may coin a new word) rectitudes, which the Greeks call εὐθύτητας, and we can more Latinly call equities: and they are called in Hebrew מֵישָׁרִים. In the one path of Christ, therefore, all justices are found, and for that reason he trod and wore it with his own foot, so that whoever wishes to walk through it, may walk with an unhindered course. In this path of the judgments of the Lord the saints sustained him, and hoped in him, because hope does not disappoint. And his name, and memorial they had in the desire of the soul, saying: my soul desired to desire your judgments at all times. And again: My soul desires, and faints for your salvation. But he who has the name of the Lord in desire, desires nothing else. And afterwards: but since Christ has been made for us by God wisdom, and justice, sanctification, and redemption: by which it is commanded that they know justice, this is ordered, that they learn and know Christ.

Latin:

Verf. 8. IN SEMITA JUDICIORVM TVO- RVM.) Tuæ legi semper obsequentes.

SVSTINVIMVS TE.) Expectavimus.

Non de doctrina legis, sed potius de Evangelio sermo est. Voces illæ judicia, semita judiciorum generaliter usurpantur, & doctrinam universam verbi Dei, adeoque etiam ipsum Evangelium deno- tant, uti vel è Psalm. 119. manifestum est. Dixerat antea: SEMITA RECTI JUSTA EST. Qui per fidem justificatus est. RECTUS CAL- LIS JUSTI AD AMBULANDUM. In Ebræo est apostrophe ad Deum, ut agnoscit Gro- tius, callem recti & justi tu dirigis. Nisi enim Deus spiritu suo efficeret, ut callem rectum incederemus viamque nostram dirigeret, à recta semita actutum deficeremus. Semitam rectam nonnulli è nostris de ipsa via, qua ad cœlum eundum est, quæ per so- lum Evangelium innotescit, explicant; utpote Brentius & Osiander. Expectare autem Dominum cum dicuntur fideles in semita judiciorum, quæ alia intelligi potest semita, quam Evangelii? In hac enim unice edocemur, quomodo expectanda sit vera fiducia Dei misericordia in Christo Jesu. NOMEN TUUM, addit Propheta, ET ME- MORIALE TUUM IN DESIDERIO ANIMÆ. ANIMA MEA DESIDERAVIT TE IN NOCTE: SED ET SPIRITU MEO IN PRÆCORDIIS MEIS DE MANE VIGILABO AD TE. Quid est, quod tanta aviditate ac desiderio fideles suscipiant, quam doctrinam Evangelii, & beneficia in eo pro- posita? Ibi nomen & memoriale Dei est, quo se gra- tiose manifestavit, quod summo animæ desiderio suscepit Propheta. Ibi Christus cum omnibus be- neficiis suis exhibetur, quem tantopere concupi- vit. Unde hoc ad desiderium adventus Messiæ re- fert Osiander: Anima mea desideravit te &c. id est, totus ardeo noctu dieque, ut de Christo magis magisque cognoscam ex Evangelicis promissionibus: atque uti- nam ea mihi contingere possit felicitas, ut te fili Dei, incarnatum in hoc mundo viderem. Judicia Domi- ni, inquit Brentius in h. l. non sunt hic lex vel affli- ctiones, sed sunt semita & via illa, de qua ante dictum est, videlicet Evangelium Dei nostri Jesu Christi. Similiter etiam nomen & memoriale Dei hoc loco sunt prædicatio Evangelii, qua Deus cognoscitur & celebratur. Ita etiam B. Cyrillus: Via piorum RECTA. Qui enim non esset recta ac plana nihilo omnino haberet prarupti, quando verbum fidei dicen- tes justificamur & per SS. Baptismum abunde ac perfecte repurgamur. Dicunt itaque qui rectam hanc viam ingrediuntur, speravimus in nomine tuo & in memoria, quam desiderat anima nostra. Omnis si- quidem spes nostra in Christum conjecta est, cujus su- mus etiam semper memores, hoc habentes desiderium, quia & inde servati sumus. Hæc Cyrillus. Dicunt ergo pii, Domine quum tanta sit rectitudo judicio- rum tuorum, seu Evangelii, ut nos recta ducat ad ju- stitiam, & cœlestem felicitatem, quid aliud reliquum est, quam ut suscipiamus illud & credamus, & quod nobis pollicetur, certa ac firma fiducia speremus! Id autem faciendum nobis est non oscitanter; sed toto cordis nostri affectu, diu noctuque: Tunc enim homines veram possunt justitiam consequi, cum judicia tua fuerint in terra, hoc est, cum Evangelium Christi prædicatur fincere & pure in terra. Cum FECE- RIS (in Ebræo, quando erunt,) JUDICIA TUA IN TERRA, JUSTITIAM DISCENT HABITATORES URBIS. Sic etiam B. Luthe- cus & Paraphraste Vinarienses v. 8. & 9. Denn wir warten auf dich, HErr, im Weg deiner Rechten (judiciorum tuorum,) des Herzens Lust stehet zu deinem Namen und deinem Gedächtniß, (Lutheri glossa marginalis, zu deinem Wort, in welchem du deines Namens Gedächtniß gestifftet hast,) Von Herzen begehre ich dein des Nachts, darzu mit meinem Geist in mir wache ich frühe zu dir (daß ich aus deinem Worte je mehr und mehr in dem selig- machenden Erkändtniß zunehme). Denn wo dein Recht im Lande gehet, so lernen die Einwohner des Erdbodens Gerechtigkeit, (aus dem Wort des Ev- angelii lernen die Menschen, wie sie für Gott sollen gerecht werden, und der Gerechtigkeit in ihrem Lebe sich befleißigen.) Memoriale, inquit B. Lutherus in Enarr. h. l. nominis Domini in lege erat, quod eduxis- fet eos ex Ægypto. Hodie in N. T. memoriale & no- men Domini est, quod non pepercit proprio Filio suo, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit illum. Hanc memo- riam, hoc beneficium celebramus non in concionibus solum, sed ex desiderio animæ, quia credimus, Chri- stum esse nostram sapientiam, justitiam, sanctificatio- nem & resurrectionem, ut sic confidamus non in no- stra opera, sed in Christi meritum. Cum FECE- RIS JUDICIA TUA IN TERRA. Est insi- gnis locus de prædicatione verbi externa, quod non debeat redire sine fructu. Vocat JUDICIA, quia Evangelium damnat omnium hominum opera & studia, & Christi tantum merita offert, quibus nita- mur. Absentibus his judiciis, seducuntur homines & impietas discitur sub specie justitiæ. Ergo ubicunque non est verbum, ibi nec justitia est. Hæc Lutherus: cujus observatio cedro digna est, cur Evangelium in Sacris judicium appelletur. In eo enim judicium Dei exponitur. In eo vera justitia, extra quam neminem Deus justum vult pronunciare aut judi- care, exhibetur. Non reprobat hunc sensum Oe- colampadius, posse intelligi profunda judicia Dei præ- destinationis & justificationis in sola fide: etsi etiam de judicio castigationis interpretetur cum Calvino. Hieronymus versum septimum, semitam JUSTI, interpretans, per justum Christum intelligit: ideo- que sic porro jam commentatur: Hujus ergo justi se- mita recta est, sive, (ut verbum novum fingam) re- ctitudines, quas Græci vocant εὐθύτητας, & nos æqui- tates Latinius possumus appellare: dicunturq; He- braice מֵישָׁרִים. In una igitur Christi semita omnes justitiæ reperiuntur, & propterea eam suo calcavit & trivit pede, ut, quicunq; per eam voluerit ambulare, cursu ambulet inoffenso. In hac semita judiciorum Domini sustinuerunt eum sancti, & speraverunt in eo, quia spes non confundit. Et nomen illius, & me- moriale habuerunt in desiderio animæ, dicentes: con- cupivit anima mea desiderare judicia tua in omni tempore. Et iterum: Desiderat anima mea, & defe- cit in salutare tuum. Qui autem nomen Domini ha- bet in desiderio, aliud non desiderat. Et postmodum: fin autem Christus factus est nobis à Deo sapientia, & justitia, sanctificatio, & redemtio: quibus præcipitur, ut cognoscant justitiam, hoc jubetur, ut Christum di- scant atq; cognoscant.

## 26:10
Vers. 10 LET US HAVE MERCY ON THE IMPIOUS AND HE WILL NOT LEARN JUSTICE: IN THE UNJUST LAND

HE WILL ACT, AND HE WILL NOT SEE THE GLORY OF THE LORD.) In the Hebrew: if grace is shown to the impious, he will not (however) learn justice, for in the very land of rectitudes (that is, Judea) he acts unjustly, nor does he consider the sublimity of GOD: that is, the power over all mortals.

Grotius's version is not disapproved: who deservedly corrects the Vulgate here from the Hebrew. But these things are wrongly restricted to Judea, when they look to the universal Church, which is truly the land of rectitudes: even if grace is offered to the impious through the proclamation of the Gospel, he will not however learn justice: he will not embrace the Gospel by faith, so as to attain true justice. Osiander and the Weimar Paraphrase explain it specifically concerning the obstinate Jews under the N. T.: who indeed had a direct way to life, but nevertheless continued in their incredulity and impiety, because even when the miracles of Christ and the Apostles were seen, they did not notice the divine power and majesty of Christ, so as to be converted to him. Not badly: because Prophetic sayings are not rarely, especially in the Psalms and Canticles, formed generally, so that they pertain to all times and to the pious or impious of all ages, even if they specifically point the finger to certain times: i.e. The matter is thus, when grace is offered to the impious: and so it will also be, when it is offered to the Jews at the coming of Christ. Whose glory they will not see with seeing eyes.

Latin:

Vers. 10 MISEREAMUR IMPIO ET NON DISCET JVSTITIAM: IN TERRA INIQVA

GES SIT, ET NON VIDEBIT GLORIAM DOMINI.) In Hebræo: si gratia fiat impio, non (tamen) discet justi- tiam, nam in ipsa terra rectitudinum (id est, Judæa) inique agit, nec, considerat DEI sublimitatem: id est, potentiam super omnes mortales.

Versio Grotii non improbatnr: qui merito corrigit hic Vulgatam ex Ebræo. Sed perperam hæc restringuntur ad Judæam, quum ad Ecclesiam universam spectent, quæ vere est terra rectitudi- num: etsi offeratur impio gratia per præconium Evangelii, non discet tamen justitiam: non am- plectetur Evangelium fide, ut veram consequatur justitiam. De Judæis tamen obstinatis sub N. T. in specie explicat Osiander & Paraphrasis Vinariensis: qui directam quidem viam habuerint ad vitam,sed perrexere tamen in sua incredulitate & impietate, quia visis etiam Christi & Apostolorum miraculis potentiam & majestatem Christi divinam non animadverterunt, ut ad eum converterentur. Non male: quia dicta Prophetica non raro, maxime in Psalmis & Canticis, formantur generaliter, ut ad omnia tempora & ad pios vel impios omnium æta- tum pertineant, etsi speciatim ad certa tempora pe- culiariter digitum intendant: q. d. Ita res habet, cum impio gratia offertur: atque ita etiam habebit, cum offeretur Judæis adventante Christo. Cujus glo- riam oculis videntibus non videbunt.

## 26:11
Vers. 11. O LORD, LET YOUR HAND BE EXALTED, AND LET THEM NOT SEE: LET THEM SEE AND BE CONFOUNDED, THE ZEALOUS OF YOUR PEOPLE, AND LET FIRE DEVOUR YOUR ENEMIES.) Translate best: O Lord, so exalt your hand, that they who envy your people may not see it: but when they shall see, they shall be ashamed, indeed fire shall devour your enemies. Fire, that is, sudden death, as if from a conflagration. above IX. 5.

Grotius understands it of the Assyrians, joined by sudden death. But there is no mention of these in a single word. It has been dealt with concerning the impious in general, to whom grace is offered, and yet he does not learn justice. What is this to the Assyrians? The Greek text is thus, let it be rendered word for word: O LORD, EXALTED IS YOUR HAND (and yet) THEY DO NOT SEE. THEY SHALL SEE AND BE AFFECTED WITH SHAME FOR THE ZEAL OF THE PEOPLE. ALSO FIRE SHALL DEVOUR YOUR ENEMIES. Which Brentius interprets concerning the impious, and especially under the New Testament, when the exalted hand of God shall be manifested by miracles, the resurrection of the Lord and the mission of the Holy Spirit and the spreading of the Gospel through the world; but the impious will not see, will not seek, will not care for this glory of Christ. But after they see him at the most recent coming of Christ, when he is about to reveal his glory to the whole world, then the impious adversaries and contemners of Christ will be so ashamed that they will waste away with zeal or emulation for those good things which will befall the people of God, and that they will be devoured or consumed by perpetual fire. Osiander understands this particularly concerning the Jews who will neglect the majesty of Christ, and then they will see the nations gathering themselves with great zeal to the Church of Christ, to be confounded and finally consumed by the eternal fires of hell. Which explanation is also that of the Weimar Paraphrasts: although these, according to the German version of Blessed Luther, not undeservedly refer the zeal not to the piety of the nations, but to the envy of the Jews against the nations gathering themselves to the Church. Because the Holy Spirit has also predicted this zeal of the Jews elsewhere. Conf. Deut. 32, 21. Rom. 10, 19. Jerome does not deny it: This can also be understood concerning the Jews, who did not know Christ, the arm of the Lord: And when they have seen and recognized him, whom they had affixed to the gallows, they will be confounded. Then the unlearned people and those not knowing the law of GOD will be incited by the goads of zeal, when they see that the nations have succeeded into their place, and they will have burned with the fire of repentance, or with the pain of punishment, when they shall hear that which is written: Go into the eternal fire, which was prepared for the Devil and his angels. But first of all, St. Cyril explained these things at length concerning the Jews who were about to reject Christ: Since God has threatened those who do not learn justice and do not do the truth, the Prophet falls into a mention of Israelite And afterwards: For when they have been cast away, and cast out of the hope in Christ, and declared to be aliens from the promises, and the nations have been assumed: hence they are consumed by emulation, and as if by a certain fire of envy, the miserable ones, forsooth, remain consumed. Vers. 12. LORD THOU WILT GIVE PEACE TO US,) Give us prosperous things. FOR THOU HAST WROUGHT ALL OUR WORKS FOR US.) That is, whatever good or evil happens to us, it happens by your care. He takes it as a prayer of the Jews for earthly prosperity. But an antithesis of the pious and the impious is instituted here: he had dealt with the latter, that they do not see the glory of the Lord, that they are confounded: that they are devoured by fire. Concerning the former, therefore, he testifies on the contrary: that the Lord grants them peace, i.e., every happiness, which is designated by the name of peace among the Hebrews: and that from mere grace: since all the good things which they perform, they accomplish by the help and aid of the Lord, who grants both to will and to perform. Whence, although they are subjected to other lords, and those harsh ones, in this world, they nevertheless remember the name of the Lord: they do not deny it nor do they fall away from the Lord, but they raise themselves up by the name, grace, and mercy of the Lord, and they constantly confess the name of the Lord. The paraphrase of Grotius on verse 13 is not to be disapproved here. LORD GOD, LORDS BESIDE THEE HAVE HAD DOMINION OVER US. (even though other lords oppress us as much as possible. ONLY IN THEE.) i.e., our hope shall be: although there is no need for that ellipsis, or for these things to be understood; if the words are explained thus, Only in thee (through thee and by thy help) will we make mention of thy name. For without God the name of God cannot be celebrated, 1 Cor. 12, 3. But what do these things have to do with the times of Hezekiah? What other lords then had dominion over the Jews beside God? For the Hebrew word is not to be taken as mere oppression, but it implies dominion at the same time. Vers. 13. LORD OUR GOD, LORDS BESIDE THEE HAVE HAD DOMINION OVER US.) Even though other lords oppress us as much as possible. ONLY IN THEE) Namely, our hope shall be. Vers. 14. THE DEAD SHALL NOT LIVE.) They shall not oppress us any further. THE GIANTS SHALL NOT RISE AGAIN.) That is, those tyrants shall not return to vex us. THEREFORE THOU HAST VISITED,) Because thou hast taken note of them. THOU HAST INCREASED THE NATION O LORD, THOU HAST INCREASED THE NATION,) Thou hast added to the nation O Lord, thou hast added to the nation. Namely, with many who had fled having been restored, thou hast increased the city of Jerusalem. The Greeks understood it concerning evils added to the Assyrian nation. Since these things are said generally, the dead shall not live, namely concerning the impious, who were here opposed by the Prophet to the faithful, who celebrate the name of the Lord even in affliction, why does Grotius restrict those things to the Jerusalemites besieged by the Assyrians? And is this not a manifest distortion, they shall not live, that is, they shall not oppress us any further! They shall not rise again, i.e., they shall not return to vex us. Furthermore, who could have doubted that, if the Assyrians were to be killed, because being killed they would not oppress the Jews any longer, nor return to vex them! That this interpretation is therefore inept is too manifest. Nor can what he added, Thou hast increased the nation O Lord, be taken concerning the return of fugitives to Jerusalem. For there was no new accession made to the Jewish nation then, much less such a significant one, which is signified here by the repetition of the word, thou hast increased the nation, thou hast increased the nation. Indeed, the discourse is not about the nation of the Jews, much less about the Jerusalemites: but about the Church, the nation of the Lord, to be enriched from various peoples. But our Brentius rightly explained these things, having observed here another antithesis of the pious and the impious. Concerning the latter it is said: They die, they shall not live, i.e., the impious, even if they seem happy for a long time, yet they must needs die at length, and fail. And when they die and fail, then they shall no longer live, nor rise again. And so all their happiness ends. For thou, O Lord, he says, visitest them in their time, thou crushest them, and destroyest all memory of them. But what he says, that the impious do not live after death, nor rise again, is not to be understood as if the impious die together with the soul, like brute animals, but that after death they do not attain any happy life, nor rise again to heavenly joys, but to eternal damnation. The impious will indeed live, but most unhappily, which life is to be called death rather than life. They will rise again, but to perpetual torments. This is a most miserable resurrection, Isa. 66. Matt. 25. John 5. But concerning the pious, THOU HAST INCREASED, he says, THE NATION, in the Hebrew, thou increasest the nation, O Lord, thou increasest the nation: thou art glorified and extended even to all the ends of the earth; that is, thou indeed destroyest the impious and blottest out their memory; but thou gatherest thy Church from the whole world and increasest it by continuous addition, so that the glory of thy name may be spread and dilated to all the ends of the world. Which the blessed Luther translated very well: but thou O Lord continuest always among the heathen, thou continuest always among the heathen, thou showest thy glory, and comest far even to the end of the world. Conf. Ps. 19, 5. Rom. 10, 17. Col. 1, 6. Grotius again twists the words of the Prophet, in order to extort a preconceived sense: Before we were compressed into every city, now little by little we are extended into the fields and deserted towns. But is this to have the glory of the Lord extended TO ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH, to have the Jews extended into fields and deserted towns? That is not to interpret Scripture, but to do violence to it. For the Lord is said to have acquired glory for himself in such a way that he extended the same not to the ends of Judea, but to all the ends of the earth. That pouring out of the people into the fields and towns of the land of Judah certainly never came into anyone's mind here. Oecolampadius understands all these things concerning the tribulations of the just; that they were so deplored that everyone says of them: they are rejected and shall not live: that they seem as if dead and placed in hell, and God still adds scourges to them: but those things are forced.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DOMINE EXALTETUR MANVS TUA, ET NON VIDEANT: VIDEANT ET CONFUNDAN- TVR ZELANTES POPULI TVI, ET IGNIS HO- STES TVOS DEVORET.) Vertas optime: Domine ita ex- celsa manus tua, ut eam non videant, qui invident populo tuo: sed ubi videbunt, pudescent, imo ignis devorabit hostes tuos. Ignis, id est, mors subita, quasi ex incendio. su- pra IX. 5.

De Assyriis intelligit Grotius, morte subita conjunctis. Sed de his nullo verbulo mentio facta. De impio generatim actum, cui gratia offertur, nec tamen discit justitiam. Quid hoc ad Assyrios? Græcus textus ita, κατὰ πόδα reddatur: DOMI- NE, EXCELSA EST MANUS TUA (& ta- men) NON VIDENT. VIDEBUNT ET PU- DORE AFFICIENTUR ZELO POPULI. ETIAM IGNIS HOSTES TUOS DEVO- RABIT. Quæ interpretatur Brentius de impiis, & cumprimis sub N. Testamento, cum excelsa Dei manus miraculis, resurrectione Domini & missio- ne Sp. Sancti divulgatione Evangelii per orbem manifestabitur;sed impii non videbunt, non requi- rent, non curabunt hanc gloriam Christi. Post- quam autem videbunt eum in adventu Christi no- vissimo, cum universo orbi revelaturus est gloriam suam, tunc impii adversarii & contemtores Christi ita pudesient, ut contabescant Zelo seu æmulatio- ne eorum bonorum, quæ contingent populo Dei, & ut devorentur seu consumantur igne perpetuo. Osiander peculiariter de Judæis Christi majestatem neglecturis, & tum videbunt gentes magno Zelo se ag- gregaturas ad Ecclesiam Christi, confundendis tan- demq; æternis inferni ignibus consumendis intelligit. Quæ etiam explicatio est Vinariensium Paraphra- starum: quamvis hi juxta B. Lutheri versionem Germanicam Zelum non ad gentium pietatem, sed ad Judæorum invidiam adversus gentes, Ecclesiæ sese aggregantes haud immerito referant. Quia hunc Judæorum Zelum etiam alias prædixit Spiri- tus Sanctus. Conf. Deut. 32, 21. Rom. 10, 19. Non abnuit Hieronymus: Potest & hoc super Judæis intelligi, qui Christum brachium Domini nescierunt: Cumq; viderint eum atq; cognoverint, quem patibulo affixerant, confundentur. Tunc ineruditus populus & nesciens legem DEI, Zeli stimulis incitabitur, quando viderit nationes in suum successisse locum, & igne pœnitudinis arserit, sive dolore supplicii, quando audierit illud quod scriptum est: Ite in ignem æter- num, qui præparatus est Diabolo & angelis ejus. Sed imprimis prolixe de Judæis Christum repro- baturis hæc exposuit S. Cyrillus: Cum Deus sit comminatus illis, qui justitiam non discunt & verita- tem non faciunt, Propheta in mentionem Israëliticæ ignorationis simul & inobedientiæ incidit &c. Et postea: Cum enim abjecti fuerint, & spe in Christum ejecti, & declarati à repromissionibus alieni, gentesque fuerunt assumptæ: hinc æmulatione conficiuntur, & tanquam igne quodam invidiæ videlicet miseri con- sumpti manent. Vers. 12. DOMINE DABIS PACEM NOBIS,) Da nobis res prosperas. OMNIA ENIM OPERA NOSTRA OPERATUS ES NOBIS.) Id est, quicquid nobis evenit boni malive, te curante evenit. Accipit ut votum Judæorum pro terrena pro- speritate. Sed instituitur hic antithesis piorum & impiorum: de his egerat, quod gloriam Domini non videant, quod confundantur: quod ab igne devorentur. De illis ergo contra testatur: quod Dominus ipsis pacem donet, h. e. omnem felicita- tem, quæ pacis nomine apud Ebræos designatur: idq; ex mera gratia: siquidem omnia bona, quæ præstant, auxilio & ope Domini perficiant, qui & velle & perficere largitur. Unde quamvis Dominis aliis iisq; duris subjiciantur in hoc mundo, recor- dantur tamen nominis Domini: non abnegant illud neq; deficiunt à Domino, sed erigunt sese no- mine, gratia & misericordia Domini, ac nomen Domini constanter confitentur. Non improban- da hic paraphrasis Grotii vers. 13. DOMINE DEUS, POSSEDERUNT NOS DOMINI ABSQUE TE. (ut maxime alii Domini nos op- primant. TANTUM IN TE.) sc. spes nostra erit: quamvis ellipsi illa opus non sit, vel ut ista sub- audiantur; si ita verba explicentur, Tantum in te (per te & ope tua) memorabimus nomen tuum. Nam sine Deo Dei nomen celebrari non potest, 1. Cor. 12, 3. Quid vero hæc ad tempora Ezechiæ? qui- nam Domini alii tunc absq; Deo possederunt Ju- dæos? Non enim de nuda oppressione verbum E- bræum accipiendum, sed simul Dominium infert. Vers. 13. DOMINE DEUS NOSTER, POSSEDE- RUNT NOS DOMINI ABSQUE TE.) Vt maxime alii Domini nos opprimant. TANTUM IN TE) Scilicet spes nostra erit. Vers. 14. MORTUI NON VIVENT.) Non oppri- ment nos ultra isti. GIGANTES NON RESURGENT.) Id est, Ty- ranni isti non redibunt ad nos vexandos. PROPTEREA VISITASTI,) Quia animadvertisti in eos. INDULSISTI GENTI DOMINE, INDULSISTI GENTI,) Addidisti genti Domine, addidisti genti. Nempe multis qui profugerant restitutis, auxisti civitatem Hieroso- lymitanam. Græci de malis additis genti Assyriæ intellexere. Quum hæc generaliter dicta sint, mortui non vivent, de impiis nempe, qui à Propheta hic oppo- nebantur fidelibus, Domini nomen etiam in affli- ctione celebrantibus, cur restringit illa Grotius ad Hierosolymitanos ab Assyriis obsessos? Et annon manifesta hæc στρεβλότης, non vivent, id est, non op- priment nos ultra! Non resurgent, i. e. non redibunt ad nos vexandos. Porro quis ambigere de eo pote- rat, si interficiendi Assyrii, quod interfecti non op- pressuri amplius Judæos, neq; redituri ad vexandos eosdem! Ineptam ergo hanc interpretationem esse, nimis manifestum est. Neq; quod addidit Do- minus genti plurimos, de reditu profugarum in Jeru- salem accipi potest. Non enim nova tum Judæo- rum genti accessio facta, nedum tam insignis, quæ hic repetitione verbi, addidisti genti, addidisti genti, significatur. Imo nec de gente Judæorum sermo est, nedum de Hierosolymitanis: sed de Ecclesia gente Domini è variis populis locupletanda. Re- ctë autem hæc exposuit Brentius noster, observata hic alia piorum & impiorum antithesi. De his dici- tur: Moriuntur, non vivent, h. e. impii, etiamsi diu videantur felices, tamen necesse habent vel tandem mori, ac deficere. Et cum moriuntur ac deficiunt, tunc non amplius vivent, nec resurgent. Itaque omnis eorum felicitas definit. Tu enim Domine, inquit, visitas eos suo tempore, conteris eos, & per- dis omnem memoriam eorum. Quod autem dicit, impios post mortem non vivere, nec resurgere, non est intelligendum, quod impii una cum anima morian- tur, sicut bruta animantia, sed quod post mortem non consequantur ullam felicem vitam, nec resurgant ad cælestia gaudia, sed ad æternam damnationem. Vi- vent quidem impii, sed infelicissime, quæ vita magis mors, quam vita dicenda est. Resurgent sed ad per- petuos cruciatus. Hæc est miserrima resurrectio, Esa. 66. Matth. 25. Joh. 5. De piis autem, INDUL- SISTI, inquit, GENTI, in Ebræo, auges gentem, Domine, auges gentem: glorificaris & elongaris usq; ad omnes fines terræ; id est, perdis quidem impios & deles memoriam eorum; Ecclesiam autem tu- am colligis ex toto orbe terrarum & auges eam continua additione, ut gloria nominis tui spargatur & dilatetur in omnes fines orbis. Quæ optime B. Lutherus transtulit: aber du HErr fahrest immer fort unter den Heyden, du fahrest immer fort unter den Heyden, beweisest deine Herrligkeit, und kom- mest ferne biß an der Welt Ende. Conf. Psal. 19, 5. Rom. 10, 17. Col. 1, 6. Grotius torquet iterum verba Prophetæ, ut sensum præconceptum extorqueat: Ante compressi eramus in omnem urbem, nunc paula- tim extendimur in agros & oppida deserta. Sed hoc- cine est elongari gloriam Domini IN OMNES TERMINOS TERRÆ, extendi Judæos in agros & oppida deserta? Id non interpretari est Scriptu- ram, sed vim eidem inferre. Gloriam enim ita sibi acquisivisse Dominus dicitur, ut eandem non in fi- nes Judææ, sed in omnes terminos terræ extenderit. Illa profecto effusio populi in agros & oppida ter- ræ Judaicæ nemini hic in mentem unquam venit. Oecolampadius hæc omnia de tribulationibus ju- storum intelligit; quod ita deplorati sint, ut omnes de illis dicant: rejecti sunt & non vivent: quod tanquam mortui & in infernum positi vi- deantur, Deusq; illis flagella adhuc addat: sed ea coacta sunt.

## 26:15
HAST THOU BEEN GLORIFIED?) In the Hebrew; thou hast acquired glory for thyself. But the Greeks read not נִכְבַּרְתָּ but נִכְבָּרִים glorious ones.

YOU HAVE EXTENDED ALL THE BOUNDARIES OF THE EARTH) Before, we were compressed into every city; now, little by little, we are extended into the fields and deserted towns.

Latin:

NUMQUID GLORIFICATUS ES?) In Hebræo; gloriam tibi acquisivisti. At Græci legerunt non נִכְבַּרְתָּ sed נִכְבָּרִים ἐνδόξοις.

ELONGASTI OMNES TERMINOS TERRÆ) An- te compressi eramus in omnem urbem, nunc paulatim ex- tendimur in agros & oppida deserta.

## 26:16
Verse 16. LORD, IN DISTRESS THEY HAVE SOUGHT YOU) The Jews.

IN THE TRIBULATION OF THE MURMUR OF YOUR DOCTRINE TO THEM.) From the Hebrew, They poured out whispered prayers, with you inciting them.

He does not speak of the Jews alone: but describes the faithful in general. He teaches that God is indeed glorified among them, but with the exception of the cross, through which the glory of the Lord may be more illustrious among the faithful. Blessed Luther expressed the sense of this clause more correctly: Lord, when there is tribulation, then one seeks you; when you chasten them, they call out anxiously. For the latter words are explanatory of the former: and the word מוּסָר denotes correction, discipline, and chastisement. Nor does the word לַחַשׁ signify prayers so whispered as it does anxious groans. Which Luther rightly notes in his Enarrations. When you chasten them, there is a clamor of murmuring, that is, an anxious calling out. They do not cry out, they do not complain, as the ungodly are wont to do in calamity, but they emit an ineffable groan, which comes forth through the mouth, like a murmur, as enchanters are wont to mutter, Rom. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DOMINE, IN ANGUSTIA REQUISI- VERUNT TE) Judæi.

IN TRIBULATIONE MURMURIS DOCTRINÆ TUÆ EIS.) Ex Hebræo, Effuderunt submissas preces, te eos instigante.

Non de Judæis solis loquitur: sed fideles in ge- nere describit. Penes quos Deum glorificari qui- dem docet, sed cum exceptione crucis, per quam gloria Domini apud fideles illustrior sit. Sensum vero commatis hujus rectius expressit B. Lutherus: HErr, wenn Truͤbsal da ist, so suchet man dich, weñ du sie zuͤchtigest, so ruffen sie aͤngstlich. Verba enim posteriora ἐξηγητικὰ sunt priorum: & verbū מוּסָר correctionem, disciplinam & castigationem notat. Neq; voce לַחַשׁ tam submissæ preces significantur quam gemitus anxii. Quod recte notat Lu- therus in Enarrat. Cum castigas eos, clamor mur- muris est, da ist ein aͤngstigliches Ruffen. Non vociferantur, non querulantur, sicut impii solent in calamitate, sed emittunt inenarrabilem gemitum, qui per os prodit, quasi murmur, sicut incantatores mussitare solent, Rom. 8.

## 26:17
Vers. 17. SO HAVE WE BEEN MADE BEFORE THY FACE O LORD) Thou disposing the causes.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SIC FACTI SVMVS A FACIE TVA DO- MINE) Te disponente causas.

## 26:18
AND WE HAVE BROUGHT FORTH SPIRIT) We have brought forth wind: like birds, which lay ὠὰ ὑπηνέμια (wind-eggs).

Πλήθουσι γάρ τοι καὶ ἀνέμων διέξοδοι Θήλειαν ὄρνιν πλὴν ὅταν τόκου παρῇ.

Plinius 10, 58. They lay vain eggs, from which nothing is born, which the Greeks call Hypenemia.

Vers. 18. WE HAVE NOT WROUGHT SALVATIONS IN THE EARTH: THEREFORE THE INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH HAVE NOT FALLEN) In the Hebrew it is not in the earth: but the earth: nor is it therefore not, but nor. The sense: We could not save our land (outside the city) nor have they fallen who inhabit the world. That is, the most widely powerful Assyrians have not been prostrated by thee, as once the Egyptians, Midianites & others. These are the complaints of the Jews, while they were still being besieged, to which God now responds.

Latin:

ET PEPERIMVS SPIRITVM) Ventum peperimus: ut aves, quæ edunt ὠὰ ὑπηνέμια.

Πλήθουσι γάρ τοι καὶ ἀνέμων διέξοδοι Θήλειαν ὄρνιν πλὴν ὅταν τόκου παρῇ.

Plinius 10, 58. Pariunt ova irrita, ex quibus nihil gignitur, quæ Hypenemia Græci vocant.

Vers. 18. SALVTES NON FECIMVS IN TERRA: IDEO NON CECIDERVNT HABITATORES TER- RÆ) In Hebræo non est in terra: sed terram: neque est ideo non, sed nec. Sensus: Non potuimus servare terram no- stram (extra urbem) nec ceciderunt qui habitant orbem. Id est, latissime potentes Assyrii non prostrati sunt abs te, ut olim Ægyptii, Madianitæ & alii. Hæ sunt querelæ Judæo- rum, cum adhuc obsiderentur, quibus Deus jam respondet.

## 26:19
THY DEAD SHALL LIVE) That is, those who were in the greatest perils of death, in the Hebrew manner of speaking. Mystically, however, the Hebrews refer this to the resurrection.

We see how he finds it necessary to twist the words of the Prophet, so that they may serve a preconceived opinion. Now he understands the whole Jewish land, now the remaining towns outside the city of Jerusalem, which indeed was the principal one in Judea. He restricts the inhabitants of the city most poorly to the Assyrians. He interprets the dead perversely concerning those who were in the greatest perils. The Hebrew text has it thus: We have not wrought salvations of the earth: nor have the inhabitants of the world fallen. What is understood by the earth, the latter part of the verse indicates; namely, the inhabitants of the world; the faithful complain that they can neither work salvation for them, nor prostrate them, and thus that the tyrants are neither converted to repentance by their prayers nor utterly cut off. Although it may also be rendered that salvations were not wrought for themselves by the earth, or by impious men, the inhabitants of the world, the powerful tyrants: because they were not delivered from them: nor could they prostrate them by their prayers, groans & cries, or that salvations of the faithful were not wrought for the earth, nor were the inhabitants of the world who were adverse to them prostrated. So that there may be an antithesis between the land of the faithful or the Church figured by the land of Canaan, and the world and its citizens, the reprobate persecutors of the Church. Brentius agrees with this sense of the Prophet, who interprets it thus: Nor has salvation happened to us in this land, nor do the inhabitants of the world fall, that is, the impious, who possess the world, always proceed happily in this world, while we are always oppressed and afflicted in it, nor does any happiness seem to shine upon us. Nor does Oecolampadius depart from this sense, that those lofty inhabitants of the earth have not yet been humbled (vers. 5.) nor have they fallen, because, as long as we live in this tabernacle, the tyranny is not yet entirely prostrated. Calvin understands the inhabitants of the world to be profane men and those alien to piety, and considers the rest of the world to be opposed to Judea, which is called the land κατ' ἐξοχήν (by way of eminence). Piscator, however, and others explain these things concerning the Babylonians: that salvation was not then wrought for the land of the Jews, nor were the Babylonians prostrated, who occupied and inhabited the Jewish world. But the Prophet persists in a general antithesis of the impious and the pious. And although the pious may be afflicted in this world, and the impious not rarely flourish, he teaches that that scene will nevertheless be changed. For the impious shall die and shall not live. The giants (centaur-tyrants) shall not rise again to a blessed life. But thy dead (O Lord) shall live, my slain shall rise again to an immortal, blessed and glorious life.

MY SLAIN SHALL RISE AGAIN) In the Hebrew: My corpse shall rise again: that is, My city, held as a corpse, shall flourish again.

YE THAT DWELL IN THE DUST) That is, ye who lie cast down, as Ps. 7, 6. Ps. 22, 16, & elsewhere.

FOR THE DEW OF LIGHT IS THY DEW) Thy seed shall be fruitful, as the dew of the dawn. See Ps. 110:3.

THE LAND OF THE GIANTS) Of tyrants, as above.

A merely arbitrary gloss. Nay, a mere corruption of the Prophetic words. For by the dead, the truly dead are to be understood, not merely those placed in danger of death; the antithesis of verse 14 proves this. There it was said: THE DEAD SHALL NOT LIVE, concerning the impious. Here concerning the pious: THY DEAD SHALL LIVE. However, God does not answer the Jews here, as it seemed to Grotius, but the faithful speak these things and in turn encourage themselves, as if to say: Although we complain thus, in anguish, calamities, and persecutions, as if it were all over for us, far be it, however, that we should despair: nay (of which we are certain by true faith), even if we must utterly perish, yet THY DEAD, O LORD, SHALL LIVE, those who die in thee, O Lord. He says to God, Jerome says: Thy dead shall live, who have been slain for thy sake. Similarly that [passage], MY CORPSE SHALL RISE, is not to be explained concerning the city, which is taken for a corpse, to be restored, but concerning those who had truly become a corpse, to be resurrected from the dust of the earth. Which the antithesis again teaches. For as it was said in verse 14 that the Giants (impious tyrants) shall not rise, to wit, to a blessed life: So, on the contrary, it is said of the faithful that their corpses shall rise to a glorious life. Which sense we have already shown to be consistent with the preceding [verses]. My corpse (says each one of the faithful) shall rise, or rather with the particle כ understood, so that the reason for the plural number may be kept in the verb, i.e., so that my corpse shall rise (those who die in the Lord) so that each faithful person may include himself, and join to himself other faithful ones dying in the Lord, who are to rise to eternal life: just as Job also spoke of himself individually in chapter 19:26. And for faith, an individual application of the glorious resurrection promised to all believers is required. The consequences also demand the same: AWAKE AND REJOICE, YE THAT DWELL IN THE DUST. For these things are not to be taken concerning the Jerusalemites, or those who lay cast out, as Grotius wrongly wishes; (for the Jerusalemites did not lie cast out in the time of Hezekiah) but concerning those who are hidden in the dust of the earth, concerning the dead in the Lord, and buried in the earth. Cf. Dan. 12, John 5, who shall awake and rejoice perpetually, [and] shall rise to eternal joys. Which Calvin himself acknowledged on page 206 of his Commentary. Therefore, he commands the dead TO AWAKE and TO EXULT: which seems to be vehemently alien to their condition: for among them there is nothing but sad silence. He notes, therefore, a manifest distinction between the elect of God, whom the corruption of the sepulcher and the dwelling of the dust shall not deprive of heavenly power, so as to prevent them from waking: and the reprobate, who, separated from God the fountain of life and from Christ, waste away while living, until they are entirely swallowed up by death. Furthermore, that gloss is new, and I add, inept: FOR THE DEW OF LIGHT IS THY DEW.) Thy seed shall be fruitful as the dew of the dawn. For the reason is not given here concerning the propagation of the seed of the Jews: but concerning the awakening of those sleeping in the dust. Here, therefore, the fruitfulness of the dew is not attended to, but the vivifying power, as Jerome and others have observed. Brentius [says] beautifully: When he makes mention of the dew awakening the herbs, he clearly signifies that God has painted before our eyes the resurrection of the pious to eternal joys, in all the meadows and gardens. For in these, during the winter, all things seem to have dried up and perished, but the root still remains in the earth, which in the spring, irrigated by the dew, pushes forth herbs and most pleasant little flowers. Thus also the dead seem utterly in the earth or dust to have to have nodded, but when the voice of the Son of God shall have sounded, then they shall leap forth from their monuments in the twinkling of an eye, and those who have believed in Christ shall receive eternal joys with Him. Finally, what is said concerning the land of the impious and tyrants, that it is to be dragged down into ruin, or destroyed utterly, how does that fit the slaughter of Sennacherib's army! Jerome understands by the land of the giants the bodies of the impious: by the world, the seat of tyrants to be destroyed by fire. Osiander interprets it thus: And you shall drag the land of the giants into ruin: that is: You shall then overturn all the kingdoms of the tyrants. For Christ, by His glorious advent, shall diminish all other kingdoms, Dan. 3. Which sense agrees with the preceding, v. 5. Certainly no one has been found thus far, as is evident, who has explained these things concerning the liberation from the Assyrian siege, even though diverse explanations are found. For some have understood it concerning liberation from hardships in general. Thus Calvin: He speaks simply of the dead, i.e., of the condition of the faithful, who lie in the shadow of death on account of various hardships which they must constantly endure. Whence it appears that this is not to be restricted to the final resurrection. Junius agrees with him, as Hackspan adds his vote to this opinion, although forced to admit that our exposition insists upon the letter, from which no one should rashly depart, and that the same cause has driven both Jews and Christians to accept the Prophet as speaking of the truly dead: assuming gratuitously in v. 14 that death and resurrection are taken improperly, which is not granted. See the things said in the same place. Piscator interprets it specifically concerning the liberation from the Babylonian captivity. Otherwise, almost all, both ancient and modern, have accepted it concerning the resuscitation from the dead. Irenaeus lib. 3. cap. 11. Tertullian de Resurr. cap. 21. Augustine lib. 20. de Civit. Dei cap. 21. & serm. 3. de Consolat. born. Cyril in this place. Jerome in this place, whose words it is pleasing to transcribe: Because those whom the Apostle calls dead in Christ, and who were killed for the name of the Lord, did not perform salvations on earth, they shall rise again in glory, and because their death is a sleep, they are by no means said, according to the LXX, to rise again, but to awake and be roused. Whence also Lazarus, who was about to be awakened, is called sleeping by the Lord. All therefore, the martyrs and holy men who shed their blood for Christ, and whose whole life was a martyrdom, shall rise again and awake, and shall praise God their creator, who now dwell in the dust, of whom it is written in Daniel: Many of those sleeping in the dust of the earth shall rise again, these to eternal life, and these to everlasting reproach and confusion. And in the Evangelist John we read: The hour shall come, and now is, when those who are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who have heard shall live, and they shall come forth, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment. For the dew of the Lord, according to the fables of the Poets, surpassing all Paeonian herbs, shall vivify the bodies of the dead. And just as the dew makes herbs gradually grow from seeds cast into the earth, and arrive at fruits of their own kind. So the dew which is placed for mercy by the Lord, shall be the dew of many men, which in Hebrew is called אורות. But the Lord shall drag the land, that is, the bodies of the Rephaim, namely of the giants and the impious, into everlasting punishments. These things Jerome. Not only the Papists and most of our own people agree with the Fathers, but also Oecolampadius from the Reformed: He builds up in this place the resurrection of the dead with their bodies. But they are called not only dead, but also the dead of God, as being dead in the Lord. For such shall rise again in glory and no others, as is Dan. 12. and Joh. 5. Similarly Zwingli: Your dead shall live: It is an opposition to the previously held opinion. For he recounted what happens to the impious and those who despise God when they depart from life: but now what happens to the pious returning to God. Add also the Belgian Interpreters, who in their Annotations on this place, having left Calvin's gloss, confess that the resurrection to eternal life is declared here. Of which thing they say there was a type in the reduction from the Babylonian captivity Isa. 37. More correctly indeed than Piscator, who wishes this reduction to be treated here, and the resurrection of the dead to be shadowed forth at the same time under it. By which pact a double sense of the same prophecy is established, one literal concerning the reduction from captivity, the other mystical concerning the resuscitation. Which is by no means to be admitted. Finally, the Jews are here sounder than Grotius, who accept the oracle concerning the resurrection of the dead according to the literal sense, and not merely mystically. For they assign no other sense to the letter. And they demonstrate from this place the resurrection of the dead against the Sadducees, as Theod. Hackspan observed on this place from the Talmud Sanhedrin cap. Chelek. Nor should Grotius have agreed here with the Vulgate translation: The dew of light. For the interpretation of others, who take the word אורת concerning green herbs and vegetables, undoubtedly fits more correctly. For so also Isaiah spoke in cap. 66, 14, your bones shall germinate like grass; and Sirach cap. 48, 12, let the bones sprout from their place; just as dew falling upon herbs makes them grow green and rise up: so the dew of grace falling upon dead bones shall resuscitate them. Thus Vatablus. Nor does Cornelius à Lapide deny it, as also Menochius in this place.

Latin:

VIVENT MORTVI TVI) Id est, qui in summis periculis mortis versabantur, more loquendi Hebræo. My- stice tamen Hebræi ad resurrectionem hoc referunt.

Videmus, quomodo necesseum habeat tor- quere verba Prophetæ, ut inserviant præconceptæ opinioni. Nunc terram totam Judaicam, nunc op- pida reliqua extra urbem Hierosolymitanam intelli- git, quæ vero præcipua erat in Judæa. Habitatores vero urbis pessime ad Assyrios restringit. Mortuos perverse de iis, qui in summis periculis versati sunt, interpretatur. Textus Ebræus ita habet: Salutes non fecimus terræ: nec ceciderunt habitatores orbis. Quidnam per terram intelligatur, posterior pars Commatis indicat; habitatores nempe orbis; illis neque salutem facere, neque prosternere eosdem se posse, queruntur fideles, adeoque tyrannos nec ad pœnitentiam converti precibus suis nec penitus excindi. Quamvis etiam reddi possit, salutes non esse sibi factas à terra, vel hominibus impiis, orbis habitatoribus, tyrannis potentibus: quod ab iis liberati non sint: nec ipsos prosternere potuerint precibus, gemitibus & clamoribus suis, aut quod salutes non sint terræ fidelium factæ, neque mundi habitatores ipsis adversi prostrati. Ut ἀντίθεσις sit inter terram fidelium vel Ecclesiam per terram Ca- naan figuratam, & inter mundum ejusque cives, re- probus persecutores Ecclesiæ. Convenit qua senten- tiam Prophetæ Brentius, qui sic interpretatur: Nec contigit nobis salus in hac terra, nec cadunt habita- tores orbis, hoc est, impii, qui orbem possident, semper feliciter pergunt in hoc mundo, cum nos semper in eo opprimamur & affligamur, nec ulla nobis felicitas affulgere videatur. Neque abit ab hoc sensu Oecolampadius, quod nondum sublimes illi habitatores terræ humiliati sint (vers. 5.) nec ceci- derint, quia, quandiu in hoc tabernaculo vivimus, nondum omnino prosternitur tyrannis. Calvinus incolas orbis prophanos & alienos à pietate homines intelligit, ac reliquum orbem Judææ, quæ κατ' ἐξο- χὴν terra nominatur, opponi censet. Piscator vero & alii hæc de Babyloniis explicant: quod salus tum non sit facta terræ Judæorum, neque prostrati Ba- bylonii, qui occuparunt & inhabitabant orbem Judaicum. Sed persistit Propheta in generali ἀντι- θέσει impiorum & piorum. Et quamvis pii in hoc mundo affligantur, impii non raro floreant, sce- nam tamen illam mutatum iri docet. Nam morien- tur impii & non vivent. Gigantes (tyranni centau- ri) non resurgent ad vitam beatam. At mortui tui (Domine) vivent, interfecti mei resurgent ad vi- tam immortalem, beatam & gloriosam.

INTERFECTI MEI RESVRGENT) In Hebræo: Cadaver meum resurget: id est, Civitas mea, pro cadavere habita, florebit iterum.

QVI HABITATIS IN PVLVERE) Id est, qui pro- jecti jacetis, ut Psal. 7, 6. Psal. 22, 16, & alibi.

QVIA ROS LVCIS ROS TVVS) Semen tuum fœ- cundum erit, ut ros auroræ. Vide Psal. 110, 3.

TERRAM GIGANTVM) Tyrannorum, ut supra.

Mere arbitraria glossa. Imo mera verborum Propheticorum corruptela. Per mortuos enim ve- re mortuos intelligendos, non tantum in periculo mortis constitutos, antithesis vers. 14. evincit. Ibi dicebatur: MORTUI NON VIVENT, de impiis. Hic de piis: VIVENT MORTUI TUI. Non respondet autem hic Deus Judæis, uti Grotio visum, sed loquuntur hæc fideles & semetipsos vi- cissim erigunt, q. d. Quamvis ita queramur, in an- gustia, calamitatibus & persequutionibus, quasi actum de nobis esset, absit tamen, ut desperemus: imo (quod certi sumus vera fide) etiamsi prorsus pereun- dum nobis sit, VIVENT tamen DOMINE MOR- TUI TUI, illi qui in te, Domine moriuntur. Dicit ad Deum, inquit Hieronymus: Vivent mortui tui, qui interfecti sunt propter te. Similiter illud, CA- DAVER MEUM RESURGENT, non de ci- vitate, quæ habita pro cadavere, restauranda, sed de iis, qui facti erant vere cadaver, è pulvere terræ re- suscitandis explicandum. Quod iterum ἀντίθεσις docet. Nam uti vers. 14. dicebatur, Gigantes (ty- ranni impii) non resurgent, ad vitam scil. beatam: Ita ex adverso de fidelibus dicitur, quod cadavera ipsorum resurrectura sint ad vitam gloriosam. Quem sensum antecedentibus etiam consonare jam ostendimus. Cadaver meum (inquit unusquis- que fidelium) resurget, vel potius subintellecta particula כ, ut pluralis numeri ratio habeatur in verbo, h. m. ut cadaver meum resurgent (qui in do- mino moriuntur) ut ita fidelis quisque se includat, sibique alios fideles in Domino morientes, ad vi- tam æternam resurrecturos, conjungat: quemad- modum etiam Job de se sigillatim loquutus est cap. 19, 26. & ad fidem requiritur individualis applica- tio gloriosæ resurrectionis, omnibus credentibus promissæ. Eandem poscunt quoque consequentia: EXPERGISCIMINI ET LÆTAMINI, QVI HABITATIS IN PULVERE. Hæc enim non de Hierosolymitanis, vel iis, qui projecti jacebant, uti Grotius perperam vult; (Hierosolymitani enim tempore Ezechiæ non jacuerunt projecti) sed de iis, qui reconditi sunt in terræ pulvere, de mor- tuis in Domino, & sepultis in terra accipienda. Conf. Dan. 12. Joh. 5. qui expergiscentur & læta- buntur perpetuo, resurgent ad æterna gaudia. Quod agnovit ipse Calvinus p. 206. Commentar. Itaque mortuos EXPERGISCI atque EXULTARE jubet: quod ab eorum conditione vehementer alie- num esse videtur: nam apud eos nihil præter triste silentium est. Manifestum igitur discrimen notat inter electos Dei, quos sepulchri corruptio & habita- tio pulveris non orbabit cælesti virtute, quo minus expergescant: & reprobos, qui à Deo vitæ fonte & Christo separati vivendo tabescunt, donec toti à mor- te exorbeantur. Nova porro, addo & inepta est illa glossa: QUIA ROS LUCIS ROS TUUS.) Se- men tuum fœcundum erit ut ros auroræ. Non enim hic de propagatione seminis Judæorum: sed de ex- citatione dormientium in pulvere ratio redditur. Hic ergo non fœcunditas roris attenditur, sed vis vivifica, ut Hieronymus aliique observarunt. Pul- chre Brentius: Cum facit mentionem roris excitan- tis berbas, manifeste significat Deum pinxisse nobis ob oculos resurrectionem piorum ad æterna gaudia, in omnibus pratis & hortis. In his enim per hyemem omnia videntur exaruisse ac periisse, sed reliqua ad- huc est radix in terra, quæ in vere irrigata rore pro- trudit herbas & flosculos amænissimos. Sic etiam mortui videntur prorsus in terra seu pulvere eva- nuisse, sed cum vox filii Dei sonuerit, tum exilient è monumentis suis in ictu oculi, & qui crediderunt in Christum, percipiunt cum ipso æterna gaudia. De- nique quod de terra impiorum & tyrannorum di- citur, quod detrahenda sit in ruinam, vel destruenda funditus, quomodo id convenit cladi exercitus Sen- nacheribi! Hieronymus per terram Gigantum cor- pora impiorum: per mundum sedem tyrannorum igne destruendam intelligit. Osiander ita interpre- tatur: Et terram gigantum attrahes in ruinam: id est: Regna tyrannorum tunc omnia evertes. Chri- stus enim adventu suo glorioso omnia alia regna im- minuet, Dan. 3. Qui sensus superioribus congruit, v. 5. Nemo certe repertus hactenus, quod constet, qui de liberatione ab obsidione Assyriaca hæc expo- suerit, etsi diversæ explicationes reperiantur. Non- nulli enim de liberatione ex ærumnis in genere intel- lexere. Sic Calvinus: Loquitur simpliciter de mor- tuis, i. e. de conditione fidelium, qui in mortis umbra jacent propter varias ærumnas, quæ ipsis assidue fe- rendæ sunt. Unde apparet ad ultimam resurrectio- nem hoc restringendum non esse. Cui adstipulatur Junius, uti hujus sententiæ calculum addit Hack- spanius, etsi fateri coactus, nostram expositionem literæ insistere, à qua temere nemo recesserit, atq; eandem causam eo usque adegisse cum Judæos tum Christianos, ut de vere mortuis Prophetam acciperent: assumens gratis v. 14. mortem & resur- rectionem improprie sumi, quod non conceditur. Vid. ibidem dicta. Piscator speciatim de liberatio- ne è captivitate Babylonica interpretatur. Cæterum plerique omnes tum veteres tum recentiores de resuscitatione à mortuis acceperunt. Irenæus lib. 3. cap. 11. Tertullianus de Resurr. cap. 21. Augustinus lib. 20. de Civit. Dei cap. 21. & serm. 3. de Consolat. nat. Cyrillus in h. l. Hieronymus in h. l. cujus verba adscribere placet: Quia salutes non fecerunt in ter- ra hi, quos in Christo mortuos Apostolus vocat, & pro- pter nomen Domini interfecti sunt, resurgent in glo- ria, & quia mors eorum somnus est, nequaquam jux- ta LXX. resurgere, sed expergisci & evigilare dicun- tur. Unde & Lazarus, qui evigilaturus erat, à Do- mino dormiens appellatur. Omnes igitur martyres & sancti viri, qui pro Christo fuderunt sanguinem, & quorum fuit tota vita martyrium, resurgent & evi- gilabunt, atq; laudabunt Deum creatorem suum, qui nunc habitant in pulvere, de quibus in Daniele scri- ptum est: Multi dormientium in terræ pulvere re- surgent, hi in vitam æternam, & hi in opprobrium & confusionem sempiternam. Et in Johanne Evangeli- sta legimus: Veniet hora, & nunc est, quando, qui in sepulchris sunt, audient vocem filii Dei, & qui audie- rint, vivent, & egredientur, qui bona fecerunt in re- surrectionem vitæ, & qui mala, in resurrectionem judicii. Ros enim Domini, juxta fabulas Poëtarum, vincens omnes herbas Pæonias, vivificabit corpora mortuorum. Et quomodo jactis in terram feminibus ros paulatim crescere facit herbas, & ad fruges sui generis pervenire. Sic Domino ros qui pro miseri- cordia ponitur, ros erit hominum plurimorum, quod Hebraice dicitur אורות. Terram autem, id est, cor- pora Raphaim, gigantium videlicet & impiorum Dominus in pœnas detrahet sempiternas. Hæc Hie- ronymus. Adstipulantur Patribus non tantum Pontificii & Nostrates plerique, sed etiam è Refor- matis Oecolampadius: Adstruit hoc loco resurrectio- nem mortuorum cum corporibus. Dicuntur autem non solum mortui, sed & mortui Dei, utpote in Do- mino mortui. Tales enim resurgent in gloria & non alii, ut est Dan. 12. & Joh. 5. Similiter Zwinglius Mortui tui vivent: Oppositio est superioris habitæ sententiæ. Recensuit enim, quod impiis ac Deum contemnentibus accidat, quum vita defunguntur: nunc vero quod piis ad Deum revertentibus Adde etiam Belgicos Interpp. qui Annotat. ad h. l. relicta Calvino glossa sua, fatentur hic declarari resurre- ctionem ad æternam vitam. Cujus rei typum fuisse ajunt in reductione è captivitate Babylonica Esa. 37. Rectius utiq; quam Piscator, qui de hac reductio- ne hic agi vult, & sub eadem adumbrari simul resur- rectionem mortuorum. Quo pacto geminus sensus ejusdem vaticinii constituitur, alius literalis de re- ductione è captivitate, alius mysticus, de resuscita- tione. Quod admittendum minime est. Denique saniores hic Grotio sunt etiam Judæi, qui de resur- rectione mortuorum oraculum juxta sensum litera- lem, non vero mystice tantum accipiunt. Nullum enim alium literæ sensum assignant. Et demon- strant ex hoc loco adversus Sadducæos mortuorum resurrectionem, ut è Talmud Sanhedrim cap. Che- lek observavit Theod. Hackspan. ad h. l. Neque ad- stipulari hic debuit Grotius Vulgatæ translationi: Ros lucis. Nam congruit sine dubio rectius alio- rum interpretatio, qui vocem אורת de herbis & ole- ribus virentibus accipiunt. Nam sic quoque Esaias locutus est cap. 66, 14. ossa vestra quasi herba germi- nabunt; & Syracides cap. 48, 12. ossa pullulent de loco suo; sicut ros super herbas cadens virescere eas facit & exurgere: ita ros gratiæ cadens super ossa mortua resuscitabit. Sic Vatablus. Neque abnuit Cornel. à Lapide, sicut etiam Menochius in h. l.

## 26:20
Vers. 20.

ENTER INTO YOUR CHAMBER) Keep yourselves all within the city.

SHUT THE DOORS UPON YOU) Keep the doors only shut.

HIDE YOURSELVES FOR A LITTLE MOMENT) Contain yourselves within these hiding places.

UNTIL THE INDIGNATION PASSES BY) Until the fury of the Assyrian shall have poured out all its impulses upon you.

These again smack of a private interpretation. Who, from the words 'enter into your chamber,' would ever have carved out this meaning, 'keep all things within the city,' if it had been without Grotius? Who would have dreamed that those words, 'shut your doors upon you,' were to be understood concerning the keeping of the city gates shut? Who would have understood the indignation concerning the fury of the Assyrian, of which there is here neither a trace nor a footprint? Most, however, have interpreted them as the chambers of sepulchers. Now he speaks to the saints, says Jerome, because the resurrection is promised to you, until the wrath of God rages against sinners and the impious: enter into your sepulchers, and hide yourselves: for it is a brief time, until the indignation of God passes by. So also Augustine, Ep. 36 to Casulanus; and Tertullian, book on the resurrection, chapter 27. Sepulchers, he says, will be store-chambers, in which those who have departed from life at the ends of the age under the final wrath of the Anti-Christ will have to rest for a little while. St. Cyril: Perhaps he calls the monuments on earth chambers by a most apt and auspicious name: and as if they had been discovered, he urges them to shut the doors and to endure to lie hidden for a little while, until the wrath of the Lord passes by. For it was said at the beginning of the race, that is, to Adam: You are earth, and into the earth you will return; and indeed nature was cursed on account of the transgression of man, whence it was subject to corruption. These things, however, brought on by divine wrath will be resolved, and that completely, at the time of the consummation: with death emptied out and the tyranny of the Devil removed, and sin buried and entombed. Hide yourself, therefore, he says, O my people, for a little while, until the death inflicted by the wrath of God passes by, and the time of the resurrection of all is declared. FOR EVEN IF, he says, you perhaps suffer death, with the insolence of enemies attacking even the ministers of the mysteries of the saints, nevertheless the Master of all will inflict punishment upon those who have taken away the saints. Similarly from more recent writers such as Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, and others among the Papists; until that INDIGNATION shall pass by, says Cornelius, that by which I punished Adam's sin, and each individual by the common death and decay of all, and rather that by which I shall punish the impious, especially towards the end of the world through so many plagues preceding the judgment and resurrection. For He commands the saints to sleep so that they may not feel these plagues. Oecolampadius, among the Reformed, also subscribes to this. He means to say: let it not be a burden to anyone that that body is afflicted here for a time and lies in the dust. From our own, we cite Osiander alone: Whence (meanwhile, until the coming of the Lord) my people, that is: let the pious meanwhile rest in their sepulchers, in their chambers (for so Isaiah ch. 56 calls the sepulchers of the pious) and this delay will seem to the elect to be of barely a moment. Meanwhile, the earth and the impious will be burned by fire, 2 Pet. 3. Parallel passages also confirm this meaning along with the preceding and following context: Is. 57:2, 'Let him rest in his bed, who walked in his uprightness,' and Apoc. 6:4, 'it was said to them that they should rest yet for a little time.'

Latin:

Vers. 20.

INTRA IN CUBICULUM TUUM) Tenete vos omnes intra urbem.

CLAUDE OSTIA SUPER TE) Portas tantum clausas tenete.

ABSCONDERE MODICVM AD MOMENTVM) Continete intra istas latebras.

DONEC PERTRANSEAT INDIGNATIO) Donec Assyrii furor omnes impetus suos in te effuderit.

Hæc iterum ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sapiunt. Quis ex verbis; intra in cubiculum tuum, exsculpsisset un- quam hunc sensum, tenete res omnes intra urbem, si absque Grotio fuisset? Quis illa: claude ostia tua super te, de portis urbis clausis tenendis intelligenda somniaffet? Quis indignationem de furore Assyrii, cujus hic nec vola nec vestigia, intellexisset? De cu- biculis autem sepulchrorum plerique exposuêre. Nunc ad sanctos loquitur, inquit Hieronymus, quia vobis resurrectio repromissa est, donec in peccatores & impios Dei ira desæviat: ingredimini in sepulchra vestra, & abscondite vos: Breve enim tempus est, donec Dei pertranseat indignatio. Sic etiam Augu- stin. Ep. 36. ad Casulam; & Tertull. lib. de resurrect. cap. 27. Sepulchra, inquit, erunt cellæ promæ, in qui- bus paulisper requiescere habebunt, qui in finibus se- culi sub ultima ira Anti-Christi vim excesserint. S. Cyrillus: Aptissimo & fausto nomine conclavia vo- cat fortassis in terra monumenta: ac perinde quasi detecti essent suadet, ut fores claudant, sustineantq; parumper latere, donec ira Domini pertranseat. Dictum enim est principio generis, id est, Adamo: Terra es, & in terram reverteris; ac quidem male- dicta fuit propter transgressionem hominis natura, unde corruptioni subjecta. Hæc autem ex ira divi- na illata solventur, idq; in solidum, consummationis tempore: exinanita morte & Diaboli tyrannide sub- lata, peccatoq; obruto ac sepulto. Abscondere igitur inquit, ô popule mi, subinde modicum quantulum- cunq;, donec mors ex ira Dei inflicta pertranseat, omniumque resurrectionis tempus declaretur. ETIAMSI enim, inquit, perpetiaris forte mortem, protervia ho- stium etiam in sanctos mysteriorum antistites assi- liente, attamen omnium herus supplicium his, qui sanctos sustulerunt, inferet. Similiter è recentiori- bus Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, & alii in- ter Pontificios; donec pertranfeat INDIGNATIO tum illa, inquit Cornelius, qua Adæ peccatum ve- strag; singula communi omnium morte & putrefa- Etione punivi, tum potius, qua impios puniam, præ- sertim sub finem mundi per tot plagas judicio & re- surrectioni prævias. Jubet enim dormire sanctos ut hasce plagas non sentiant. Cui è Reformatis quo- que Oecolampadius subscribit. Dicere vult: ne sit alicui grave, quod corpus illud ad tempus hic affliga- tur & jaceat in pulvere. E nostris Osiandrum so- lum adducimus: Unde (interea usq; ad Domini ad- ventum) populus meus, id est: pii interim quiescant in sepulcris, in cubiculis suis (sic enim Esaias cap. 56. vocat piorum sepulcra) & ista mora vix unius momenti videbitur electis. Interea terra & impii igne comburentur, 2. Pet. 3. Confirmant hunc sen- sum cum antecedentibus & consequentibus etiam loca parallela Es. 57, 2. Requiescat in cubili suo, qui am- bulavit in directione sua. & Apoc. 6, 4. dictum est illis, ut requiescerent adhuc tempus modicum.

## 26:21
Verse 21. THE LORD SHALL COME FORTH FROM HIS PLACE) From heaven. A manner of speaking in Scripture to express the judgments of God.

TO VISIT THE INIQUITY OF THE INHABITANT OF THE EARTH) Of the one dwelling widely, as above 18.

AND THE EARTH SHALL REVEAL ITS BLOOD) The earth will not be able to absorb the blood, so much will there be.

AND SHALL COVER NO MORE ITS SLAIN.) There will be no one to commit them to the earth.

This gloss is again both new and unheard of in the Church, and it also does not agree with the words. The Prophet does not speak definitely about one subject, nor has he spoken throughout this chapter, but indefinitely about any impious inhabitant of the earth whatsoever. Therefore, this is wrongly snatched away to Sennacherib: so that the inhabitant of the earth is the Assyrian Monarch dwelling widely: where he has been called by this name, Grotius has not yet indicated. Nor indeed is only his iniquity to be visited, but the inhabitants of the earth in general. The coming forth of the Lord is designated here not for a particular, but for a universal judgment. Also those words AND THE EARTH SHALL REVEAL ITS BLOOD speak of blood shed justly by the hand of the Lord, but unjustly by an iniquitous hand, and they allude to the cry of the just blood of Abel. Finally, those words, THE EARTH SHALL COVER NO MORE ITS SLAIN, are by no means to be understood as if there were no one to commit the slain to the earth. Since it rather indicates that those unjustly slain will no longer be covered by the earth, but that vengeance will be exacted from the slayers, and that they will hardly remain many. For many iniquities are covered in this age, many slaughters are hidden and concealed, many slain seem to be left as if unavenged, but the earth SHALL COVER NO MORE its slain, nay, it SHALL REVEAL ITS BLOOD which it was forced to swallow. The Grotian gloss completely perverts this force of the words. But if they are explained according to the continuity of the context regarding the final judgment, everything is clear: For then the LORD shall come forth, of whom the Prophet sang primarily in both these chapters, Christ our Savior from His place, that is, from heaven, as Grotius himself renders it, for a judgment not particular, but universal, so that He may visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth, not of this one or that one, but of all who have persevered in iniquity, with no repentance performed, AGAINST HIM: so that He may punish their iniquities and sins with worthy punishments. Then the earth shall reveal its blood, which it drank up unjustly since the foundation of the world: For the Lord will avenge the blood of the martyrs, and of the pious especially, from Abel the just, Matt. 23, Apocal. 6, and it shall cover no more its slain, slaughters will not remain hidden and unavenged. For the Lord on that day of His glorious coming will bring all the crimes of the impious and impenitent (especially indeed slaughters perpetrated among men) into judgment and will punish the impious and Tyrants with eternal torments. Thus Osiander with Brentius and others of our own: What could be said more clearly, what more conveniently for our text, by this paraphrase? Nor is Oecolampadius otherwise in the Church of the Reformers. Because BEHOLD THE LORD. Do not doubt, he says, that day will be present, in which there will be an end of the indignation of God upon you, and He is about to take vengeance on the impious. For the Lord will go forth from His place, and not only will He send Angels, but He Himself will judge, and will visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth afflicting you, and in such a way that the homicides, persecutions, and other evils by which they oppress the innocent here will be manifest on the day of judgment. And this is what he says, that the earth will reveal its blood, because impieties will then be manifest before the whole world. Similarly the pious ancients, and among them Jerome: Who, to illustrate the expression INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH, compares Hos. 4: 'Cursing and lying, and adultery and whoredom have been poured out upon the INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH.' And Apocal. 8: 'Woe upon the INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH.' He also warns that they are to be distinguished from the JUST, who are citizens not so much of the earth as of heaven: although the just may seem to be on earth, yet their conversation is in heaven, who can say: 'I am a sojourner on the earth and a pilgrim, as all my fathers,' and they enjoy the habitation of the Most High; of whom the Holy Spirit speaks: 'He who dwells in the help of the Most High, shall abide in the protection of the God of heaven.' And those words, 'then the earth shall reveal its blood,' he understands of the blood, concerning which God said to Cain, 'the voice of your brother's blood cries to me from the earth, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand': which, however, he acknowledges can also be understood of the Martyrs, who shed their blood for Christ, and cry out under the altar of God: 'How long, O Lord, do you not avenge our blood from those WHO DWELL UPON THE EARTH' (which passage clearly illustrates our own) of whom Moses also says in the Canticle (Deut. 32): 'The blood of his children will be avenged and he will take vengeance, and will render vengeance to his enemies.' This blood, says Jerome, the earth, which had received it, will reveal, and will by no means cover the slain of the Lord, but will bring them into public view, for the condemnation of those who killed the martyrs. Let this be said concerning the simple resurrection. Jerome says this, with whom Cyril agrees: But when the time is at hand in which those who have sinned against the sanctified will be so afflicted, the earth will reveal its blood, and will not hide the slain, that is, all the blood that has fallen upon the earth will be manifest, and no one will be hidden, or come into oblivion, of those who have been oppressed by injury. For the Maker of all will remember, nor will there be any at all of those who have been unjustly slain who will not be known, and of whom God will not be mindful. But these things are from Chapter 26.

Latin:

Vers. 21. DOMINUS EGREDIETVR DE LOCO SVO) De cœlo. Mos loquendi Scripturæ ad exprimen- da Dei judicia.

VT VISITET INIQVITATEM HABITATO- RIS TERRÆ) Late habitantis, ut supra 18.

ET REVELABIT TERRA SANGVINEM SUUM) Non poterit terra absorbere sanguinem, tam mul- tus erit.

ET NON OPERIET VLTRA INTERFECTOS SVOS.) Nemo erit, qui humo eos mandet.

Hæc glossa iterum tum nova & inaudita est in Ecclesia, tum etiam verbis non congruit. Non de uno subjecto definite loquitur Propheta, neque per hoc caput loquutus est, sed indefinite de habitatore terræ impio quocunq;. Perperam ergo hoc abripi- tur ad Sennacheribum: ut habitator terræ sit late ha- bitans Assyriorum Monarcha: qui ubi hoc nomine vocatus sit, nondum indicavit Grotius. Nec vero iniquitas tantum illius visitanda, sed habitatores terræ in universum. Egressus Domini non ad par- ticulare, sed ad universale judicium hic designatur. Verba etiam illa ET REVELABIT TERRA SANGVINEM SUUM, de sanguine juste manu Domini, sed injuste manu iniqua effuso loquuntur, & ad sanguinis justi Abelis clamorem alludunt. Deniq; illa, NON OPERIET ULTRA TER- RA INTERFECTOS suos, neutiquam ita acci- pienda, quod nemo sit, qui interfectos humo mandet. Siquidem potius indicet inique interfe- ctos non opertum ultra iri humo, quin vindicta exigatur ab interfectoribus, illosque haud multos mansuros. Multæ enim iniquitates operiuntur in hoc seculo, multæ cædes teguntur & occultantur, multi interfecti velut inulti relinqui videntur, sed NON OPERIET ULTRA terra interfectos suos, imo REVELABIT SANGVINEM SUUM quem sorbere necessum habuit. Hanc vim vocum penitus pervertit Grotiana glossa. Si autem juxta contextus συνέχειαν de novissimo judicio expo- nuntur, omnia luculenta sunt: Tum enim egressurg est DOMINUS, de quo hoc utroque capite im- primis cecinit Propheta, Christus Salvator noster de loco suo, hoc est, de cœlo, ut Grotius ipse red- dit, ad judicium non particulare, sed universale, ut nempe visitet iniquitatem habitatoris terræ, non hu- jus aut illius, sed omnium, qui in iniquitate, nulla acta pœnitentia, perseverarunt, CONTRA EUM: ut dignis suppliciis iniquitates & peccata ipsorum puniat. Tum revelabit terra sanguinem suum, quem injuste effusum imbibit inde ab orbe condito: Sanguinem enim martyrum, & piorum cumprimis, vindicabit Dominus inde ab Abele justo, Matth. 23. Apocal. 6. & non operiet ultra in- terfectos suos, non manebunt occulte, & inulte cedes injuste. Dominus enim illa die gloriosi adventus sui omnia impiorum & impoenitentium scelera (imprimis vero cædes in hominibus per- petratas) in judicium protrahet atque æternis cru- ciatibus impios & Tyrannos puniet. Ita Osiander cum Brentio & aliis Nostris: Qua paraphrasi quid clarius, quid textui nostro convenientius dici pote- rat? Nec aliter in Ecclesia Reformatorum Oeco- lampadius. Quia ECCE DOMINUS. Ne dubites, inquit, aderit dies illa, qua erit finis indi- gnationis Dei super te, & sumturus est pœnas de impiis. Exibit enim Dominus de loco suo, & non solum Angelos mittet, sed ipsemet judicabit, & vi- sitabit iniquitatem habitatoris terræ te affligentis, atque ita ut manifesta sint futura in die judicii ho- micidia, persecutiones, & alia mala, quibus hic innocentes opprimunt. Et hoc est, quod dicit ter- ram revelaturam sanguinem, quia manifestæ tunc erunt impietates coram toto mundo. Similiter pii veteres & inter hos Hieronymus: Qui ad vocem HABITATORUM TERRÆ illustrandam confert Os. 4. Maledictio & mendacium, & adul- terium & scortum effusa sunt super HABITATO- RES TERRÆ. Et Apocal. 8. Væ super HABI- TATORES TERRÆ. Monet etiam distin- guendos eos esse à JUSTIS, qui non tam terræ, quam cæli cives sunt: Justi licet videantur in ter- ra, tamen conversatio eorum in cælis est, qui pos- sunt dicere: Advena ego sum in terra & peregrinus, sicut omnes Patres mei, & fruuntur habitatione altissimi; De quibus Spiritus Sanctus loquitur: Qui habitat in adjutorio altissimi, in protectione Dei cæli commorabitur. Et verba illa, tunc revelabit terra sanguinem suum, intelligit de sanguine, quo de Deus ad Cain, vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra, quæ aperuit os suum, ut susciperet sanguinem fratris tui de manu tua: quæ tamen etiam de Martyribus intelligi posse agnoscit, qui pro Christo fuderunt sanguinem, & sub altari Dei clamitant: Usque quo Domine non ulcisceris sangui- nem nostrum de his, QUI HABITANT SUPER TERRAM (qui locus plane nostrum illustrat) de quibus & Moses dicit in Cantico (Deut. 32.) San- guis filiorum ejus vindicabitur & ulciscetur, & re- tribuet vindictam inimicis. Hunc sanguinem, inquit Hieronymus, terra, quæ susceperat, revelabit, & interfectos Domini nequaquam operiet, sed producet in publicum, ad condemnationem eorum, qui marty- res occiderunt. Hoc de simplici resurrectione dictum sit.
