Hæc Hieronymus, cui consonat Cyrillus: In- stante vero tempore, quo ita infligentur, qui contra sanctificatos deliquerunt, sanguinem suum revelabit terra, & non abscondet interfectos, id est, omnis san- guis, qui cecidit in terram, erit manifestus, ne- moque occultabitur, seu in oblivionem veniet, eorum, qui sunt oppressi injuria. Recordabitur enim omnium opifex, nec ullus omnino erit illorum, qui injuste in- terempti sunt, qui non erit notus, cujusque Deus non meminerit. Sed hæc de Cap. 26.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII.

Concerning the defeat of Satan, the fruitfulness of the Lord's vineyard, the chastisement of the faithful, the rejection of the unfaithful people, and the calling of the nations by the trumpet of the Gospel.

Ver. 1. IN THAT DAY) A continuation of the previous Canticle, UPON LEVIATHAN) For, as Varro says: He who is more powerful presses: as the great fish often eats the small ones, Therefore those kings who oppress smaller princes are called whales (Cete) in the Holy Scriptures. SERPENTEM VECTEM) The Hebrews use the word נחש & נחשן as much for fish as for serpents. Vectem, i.e., strong. SERPENTEM TORTUOSUM) The deceiver. QUI IN MARI EST.) In a great empire, for waters [are] peoples,

It is possible for the Canticle to be continued here; but just as it in no way sounded of the slaughter of Sennacherib, so Grotius in vain drags the present chapter into it, perverting individual things with his customary μεθοδέια & κυβεία. For Leviathan to him is Sennacherib: Leviathan, who is in the sea, is to him the emperor of many peoples: the world, verse 6, is to him the land of the Jews: and what other depravations there are, are to be noted in turn. Moreover, by Leviathan the bar-serpent and the tortuous serpent, most interpreters understand the Devil, who extends his dominion far and wide, like a sea whale and sea dragons, and now attacks with open force, now lies in wait for the Church with tortuous coils and incredible cunning, if indeed Satan is also shadowed forth under the species of Leviathan in Job 40, and is called a Dragon in Psalm 90 and Apocalypse 12. Whom the Lord is said to be about to visit and to take grave vengeance upon. Which was done when the seed of the woman crushed the head of the ancient and infernal serpent, Gen. 3:15, and through his death destroyed him who had the power of death, that is, the Devil, Heb. 2:14, and dissolved his works, 1 John 3:8, and will most fully come to pass on the last day, when the Lord is about to cast Satan into the lake of fire, Apoc. 28:10. Meanwhile, He protects the Church, His vineyard, against the same Leviathan, still raging through his instruments, tyrants and heretics, against the faithful, so that the gates of hell may not prevail against it. Thus, in just order, these things cohere with the preceding hymn, as St. Cyril noted. Having discoursed very beautifully on the necessity of bringing wrath upon those who acted impiously and killed the saints, he said that Satan himself, together with his sons, must also be removed, whose stratagems the opponents used to attack the saints, resisting their preachings. He calls Satan a dragon and serpent. For he is bitter, and a thrower of venom, and still timid, for it is always familiar to him to flee. He is also dire and delights in evil deeds. For he runs like a tortuous beast, but he will be removed, inasmuch as he will accomplish nothing in the future, nay rather he will pay for the impiety of his words, having suffered the ultimate punishment, and being detained at the gates of hell, the material and work of eternal flame, sustaining long and infinite punishment.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII.

De Satanæ devictione, vineæ Domini fructifi- catione, fidelium castigatione, populi infi- delis rejectione, & gentium per Evangelii buccinam vocatione.

Vers. 1. IN DIE ILLA) Continuatio prioris Cantici, SUPER LEVIATHAN) Nam, ut ait Varro: Qui potis plus, urget: pisces ut sæpe minutos Magnus comest, Ideo ii Reges, qui minutiores principes opprimunt, in sacris literis Cete vocantur. SERPENTEM VECTEM) Hebræi vocem נחש &amp; נחשן tam de piscibus, quam de serpentibus usurpant. Ve- ctem, i. e. validum. SERPENTEM TORTUOSUM) Deceptorem. QUI IN MARI EST.) In magno imperio, Nam aquæ, populi,

COntinuari hic prius Canticum, admitti po- test: sed uti illud nullatenus de Sennacheribi clade sonabat, ita nequicquam præsens caput eo abripit Grotius, consueta μεθοδέια &amp; κυβεία singula pervertens. Nam Leviathan ipsi est Sennacherib: Leviathan, qui in mari est, imperator est ipsi multo- rum populorum: Orbis verf. 6. est ipsi terra Judæo- rum: &amp; quæ aliæ sunt depravationes, deinceps no- tandæ. Cæterum per Leviathan serpentem vectem &amp; tortuosum Diabolum plerique Interpretes intel- ligunt, qui longe lateque, ut cetus marinus, &amp; dra- cones marini, dominium suum extendit, &amp; modo aperta vi grassatur, modo tortuosis nexibus, &amp; in- credibili astutia Ecclesiæ insidiatur, siquidem Sa- tanas sub Leviathan specie etiam Job. 40. adum- bratus sit, &amp; Draco vocetur Psal. 90. Apocalyps. 12. Quem Dominus visitaturus, &amp; gravem vindictam de eo sumturus dicitur. Quod factum, cum semen mulieris caput antiqui &amp; infernalis serpentis contri- vit, Gen. 3, 15. &amp; per mortem suam destruxit eum, qui habebat mortis imperium, hoc est, Diabolum, Ebr. 2, 14. atque dissolvit opera ejus 1. Joh. 3, 8. &amp; plenis- sime in novissimo die eventurum est, cum Satanam abjecturus est Dominus in stagnum ignis, Apoc. 28. v. 10. Interim tuetur Ecclesiam, vineam suam contra eundem Leviathan, adhuc furentem per or- gana sua, Tyrannos atq; hæreticos, adversus fide- les, ne portæ inferorum prævaleant adversus eandem. Sic justo ordine cohærent hæc cum præ- cedenti hymno, ut notavit S. Cyrillus. Inducen- dam iram his, qui impie egerunt, sanctosq; occide- runt, cum perpulcre disseruisset, ipsum quoq; Sata- nam dixit cum filiis suis una esse tollendum, cujus stratagematis cedentes oppugnarunt sanctos, illorum resistentes prædicationibus. Draconem vero &amp; ser- pentem nominat Satanam. Acerbus enim est, &amp; ve- neni jaculator, &amp; adhuc timidus, semper enim ei fa- miliare est fugere. Dirus est etiam &amp; maleficiis gau dens. Currit enim tortuosa instar bestia, at tolletur, quippe qui in posterum nihil efficiet, imo magis ver- borum impietatem luet, pœnam ultimam perpessus, &amp; in portis inferorum detentus, æternæ flammæ ma- teria ac opus, diuturnum ac infinitum sustinens sup- plicium.

## 27:2
Vers. 2. IN THAT DAY THE VINEYARD OF RED WINE SHALL SING TO IT) In that day, sing to the vineyard of red wine (that is, the best, Gen. 49:12, Prov. 23:31); these things which follow, from the person of God, call the city of Jerusalem a vineyard of the best wine, because it had brought forth the fruits of excellent faith in God and patience.

By the vineyard here, not the city of Jerusalem, but rather the Church of God is understood, inasmuch as it is compared to a vineyard everywhere in the Scriptures, Is. 5:1, Matt. 21:33, whose guardian is God, whom He preserves and waters, Matt. 1:8, ch. 16:13. Of which it is said, I WILL SUDDENLY WATER IT. Which Grotius correctly renders from the Hebrew: In time I will water it; that is, I will diligently care for this vineyard. LEST PERCHANCE IT BE VISITED AGAINST IT, lest it visit it, namely the enemy, that is, break through the broken hedge. Of which v. 4, INDIGNATION IS NOT IN ME. I cannot be angry with my vineyard. Which is true of the Church. God was not rarely angry with Jerusalem. WHO WILL GIVE ME THE THORN AND THE BRIAR IN BATTLE. The material of my wrath is not the vineyard, but thorns and briars. I WILL MARCH UPON IT, I WILL BURN IT ALIKE. I will not only trample these harmful burdens of the earth, but I will also burn them. For these things are fitting for the enemies of the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 2. IN DIE ILLA VINEA MERI CANTABIT EI) In die illa vinea rubentis vini (id est, optimi, Gen. 49, 12. Prov. 23. v. 31.) accinite; hæc quæ sequuntur ex Dei persona Civitatem Hierosolymitanam vocat vineam optimi vini, quod fructus egregiæ fidei in Deum &amp; patientiæ protulisset.

Per vineam hic non Hierosolymitana civitas, sed Ecclesia potius Dei intelligitur, utpote quæ vi- neæ passim in Scripturis comparatur, Ef. 5, 1. Matt. 21, 33. cujus custos Deus est, quam conservat atq; irrigat, Matth. 1, 8. cap. 16, 13. De qua dicitur, RE- PENTE PROPINABO EI. Quod ex Ebræo recte reddit Grotius: In tempore rigabo eam; id est, diligenter curabo vineam istam. NE FORTE VI- SITETUR CONTRA EAM, ne visitet eam, nempe hostis, id est, fracta sepe irrumpat. De qua v. 4. INDIGNATIO NON EST MIHI. Non possum irasci vineæ meæ. Quod de Ecclesia verum est. Hierosolymæ non raro iratus est Deus. QUIS DABIT ME SPINAM ET VEPREM IN PRÆLIO. Iræ meæ materia non sunt vinea, sed spi- næ &amp; vepres. GRADIAR SUPER EAM, SUC- CENDAM EAM PARITER. Non conculca tantum ista damnosa terræ onera, sed &amp; incendam Hæc enim conveniunt hostibus Ecclesiæ.

## 27:3
Vers. 3. I WILL SUDDENLY WATER IT) In the Hebrew: In time I will water it: i.e., I will diligently care for this vineyard.

LEST PERCHANCE IT BE VISITED AGAINST IT) Lest it visit it. Namely the enemy, that is, break through the broken hedge. For there is a litotes in the word of visiting; as in the word of seeing, 2 Kings 14:8.

Latin:

Vers. 3. REPENTE PROPINABO EI) In Hebræo: In tempore rigabo eam: i. e. diligenter curabo vineam istam.

NE FORTE VISITETUR CONTRA EAM) Ne visitet eam. Nempe hostis, id est, fracta sepe irrumpat. Est enim in voce visitandi λιτότης; ut in voce videndi, 2. Regum 14, 8.

## 27:4
Vers. 4. INDIGNATION IS NOT IN ME) I cannot be angry with my vineyard.

WHO WILL GIVE ME THE THORN AND THE BRIAR IN BATTLE) The material of my wrath is not the vineyard, but thorns and briars. See above 10:17.

I WILL MARCH UPON IT, I WILL BURN IT ALIKE) I will not only trample these harmful burdens of the earth, but I will also burn them. For in those places fire is accustomed to be made from the bramble, as noted elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 4. INDIGNATIO NON EST MIHI) Non pos- sum irasci vineæ meæ.

QUIS DABIT ME SPINAM ET VEPREM IN PRÆLIO) Iræ meæ materia sunt, non vineæ, sed spinæ & vepres. Vide supra 10, 17.

GRADIAR SUPER EAM, SUCCENDAM EAM PARITER) Non conculcabo tantum ista damnosa terræ onera, sed &amp; incendam. Nam in illis locis ex rhamno i- gnis fieri solet, ut notatum alibi.

## 27:5
Vers. 5. OR RATHER WILL IT HOLD MY STRENGTH) In the Hebrew: Or will it apprehend my strength: that is: or if I were to be angry with the vineyard, it would hold my force as if bound, namely by most humble prayers. He alluded to the history of Gen. 32:28.

HE SHALL MAKE PEACE WITH ME, HE SHALL MAKE PEACE WITH ME) That he might make peace with me as quickly as possible. A clearer explanation of that which had preceded.

Latin:

Vers. 5. AN POTIUS TENEBIT FORTITUDI- NEM MEAM) In Hebræo: Aut apprehendet fortitudinem meam: id est: aut si irascerer vineæ, illa vim meam quasi devinctam teneret, nempe precibus demississimis. Allusit ad historiam Gen. 32, 28.

FACIET PACEM MIHI, PACEM FACIET MI- HI) Quam celerrime mecum pacem faceret. Clarior ex- plicatio ejus quod præcesserat.

## 27:6
Vers. 6. THOSE WHO SHALL ENTER WITH FORCE FROM JACOB) In the Hebrew: in the coming (supply: times) Jacob shall take root. Under Hezekiah, after the slaughter of Sennacherib, the Jewish people will be in a firm state,

ISRAEL SHALL BLOSSOM AND BUD) Many from the ten tribes, who were exiles in distant places, will join themselves to his kingdom. Above 11, 11. 12.

AND THEY SHALL FILL THE FACE OF THE WORLD WITH SEED) Of the world, namely their own, as above 24, 4. Concerning the seed, see above 26, 19.

This is not precisely about the times of Hezekiah. It is promised simply to the Church of the Lord, that it is to be preserved, lest it perish, even if it be subject to adversities: that God will so plant it, that it may blossom in its own time, and bring forth copious fruit in the world. Which was fulfilled most of all in the time of the Apostles. Jacob did not finally take root under Hezekiah, nor did Israel then blossom and bud to such an extent. If some from the ten tribes joined themselves to his kingdom, what is this to such a notable promise? Just as it is not a physical vineyard, but the Church is designated by it, so neither is Jacob or Israel understood according to the flesh, but according to the spirit and the promise, Rom. 9, 8. He also exhorts the Church henceforth to bear hardships patiently: then because God does not afflict with a hostile spirit, but with a friendly and benevolent one: Has he struck him according to the striking of the enemy? as it is held in the Hebrew. Which Grotius wrongly draws to Sennacherib, explaining it thus: did he treat them as he did the army of Sennacherib? For nothing of that is held here. Rather, the enemies of the people striking them are designated. Does the Lord strike the people with that plague with which his enemies strike him, or does he kill him with that killing with which his killers kill him? Then because God sends such a harsh wind to his vineyard, and yet JUDGES IT IN MEASURE, BY LETTING IT GO, mit massen richtest du, und lässest sie loß: as B. Luther rightly: HE GROANED IN HIS EAST WIND IN THE DAY OF THE EAST WIND. Luther expressed the sense: When you have troubled them with your rough wind, namely with the East wind. Then finally because God sends so many calamities to this end, that sins may cease, and impiety and idolatry may be abolished. Which was fulfilled also in the Babylonian captivity. Grotius completely perverts the sense and the scope. Who v. 8. indeed understands it concerning the vineyard of the Lord, rendering it thus: You will chastise it by banishing it moderately: but soon he wishes to slip away to the Assyrian Prophet, translating the rest thus: It is taken away by a violent wind, in the time of the East wind: namely the Assyrian, as an opposition to the chastisements of the Jewish people, and the punishments which the Assyrian paid, as if suffocated by heat, he were held here: of whom, however, no trace appears in the text. Whence he transforms the active תֻּכַּר into a passive, and the illative, which follows in v. 9 לָכֵן IDCIRCO, he converts into an adversative, ON THE CONTRARY: he explains the dismissal, or expiation of iniquity, THE INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL BE FORGIVEN, as the breaking off of calamity, that is, his calamity shall not last: although it is in the open that not the end, or limit, but rather the final cause of the inflicted calamity is expressed, namely that iniquity may be expiated, not that human afflictions are expiations of sins, but because they lead to the acknowledgment of sin, and through true repentance and faith in Christ sins are expiated. Whence it is added, AND THIS IS ALL HIS FRUIT, namely that the people were chastised, THAT HIS SIN MAY BE TAKEN AWAY: Which Grotius again perverts: AND THIS IS ALL HIS FRUIT, so all his happiness is situated in this; THAT HIS SIN MAY BE TAKEN AWAY: that he (the people themselves) may take away his sin, that he may purge himself well. For it is manifest that the fruit of calamity and chastisement, and not indeed the happiness of the people, is being expounded.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QUI INGREDIENTUR IMPETU EX JACOB) In Hebræo: venturis (supple temporibus) radices agat Iacob. Sub Ezechia post cladem Sennacheribi populus Judæus in statu erit firmo,

FLOREBIT ET GERMINABIT ISRAEL) Multi ex decem tribubus, qui in locis longinquis exulabant, ipsius regno se addent. Supra 11, 11. 12.

ET IMPLEBUNT FACIEM ORBIS SEMINE) Or- bis, sui scilicet, ut supra 24, 4. De semine vide supr. 26, 19.

Non hic præcife agitur de Ezechiæ tempori- bus. Promittitur simpliciter Ecclesiæ Domini, eam servandam, ne intereat, etsi obnoxia sit adver- sitatibus: Deum eam ita plantaturum, ut floreat suo tempore, &amp; fructum copiosum adferat in orbe ter- rarum. Quod impletum maxime Apostolorum tempore. Non demum sub Ezechia radices egit Jacob, neque tum adeo floruit &amp; germinavit Israël. Si aliqui ex decem tribub9 sese regno ejus addide- re, quid hoc ad tam insignem promissionem? uti vinea corporalis non est, sed Ecclesia per eam desi- gnatur, ita neq; Jacob aut Israël secundum carnem intelligitur, sed secundum spiritum &amp; promissio- nem, Rom. 9, 8. Ecclesiam etiam deinceps horta- tur ad patienter ferendas ærumnas: tum quia Deus non affligit hostili animo, sed amico &amp; benevolo: Nunquid juxta percussionẽ hostis percussit eum? ut in Ebræo habetur. Quod perperam ad Senna- cheribum trahit Grotius ita explicans, an eos ita tractavit, ut Sennacheribi exercitum? Nihil enim de eo hic habetur. Hostes potius populi eundem percutientes designantur. Num percutit Dominus populũ ea plaga, qua percutiunt eum hostes ipsius, aut occidit eum ea occisione, qua occidunt eum oc- cifores ejus? tum quod Deus ita ventum durum immittat vineæ suæ, &amp; tamen eam IN MENSURA JUDICET, DIMITTENDO EAM, mit massen richtest du, und lässest sie loß: uti recte B. Luthe- rus: GEMUIT IN VENTO EJUS EURO IN DIE EURI. Lutherus sensum expressit: Wenn du sie betrübet hast mit deinem rauhen Wind, nem- lich mit dem Ostwind. Tum deniq; quod Deus hoc fine immittat tot calamitates, ut cessent peccata, &amp; aboleatur impietas &amp; idololatria. Quod imple- tum etiam in captivitate Babylonica. Grotius sen- sum &amp; scopum prorsus pervertit. Qui v. 8. quidem de vinea Domini intelligit, sic reddens: Moderate relegando castigabis eam: sed mox ad Assyrium Prophetam delabi vult, reliqua sic transferens: Aufertur vento violento, tempore Euri: nempe Assyrius, quasi oppositio castigationum populi Ju- daici, &amp; pœnarum, quas pependit Assyrius, velut æstu suffocatus, hic haberetur: de quo tamen nul- lum in textu comparet vestigium. Unde תֻּכַּר acti- vum transformat in passivum, & illativam, quæ v. 9. sequitur לָכֵן IDCIRCO, in adversativam con- vertit, CONTRA VERO: dimissionem vero, vel expiationem iniquitatis, DIMITTETUR INI- QVITAS DOMUI JACOB, de calamitate ab- rumpenda explicat, hoc est, non durabit ejus cala- mitas: quum tamen in aprico sit, non finem, seu ter- minum, sed causam finalem potius immissæ calami- tatis exprimi, ut nempe expietur iniquitas, non quod afflictiones humanæ expiationes peccato- rum sint, sed quia ducunt in agnitionem peccati, & per veram pœnitentiam & fidem in Christum pec- cata expiantur. Unde additur, ET ISTE O- MNIS FRUCTUS EJUS, quod nempe castigatus populus, UT AUFERATUR PECCATUM E- JUS: Quæ iterum pervertit Grotius: ET ISTE OMNIS FRUCTUS EJUS, ita omnis felicitas ejus in hoc sita est; UT AUFERATUR PECCA- TUM EJUS: ut auferat (ipse populus) peccatum suum, ut se bene repurget. Manifestum enim est, fructum calamitatis, & castigationis, non vero fe- licitatem populi exponi.

## 27:7
Vers. 7. HATH HE SMITTEN HIM ACCORDING TO THE STROKE OF HIM THAT SMOTE HIM) He shows God's goodness toward the Jews. He did indeed chastise them, he says, for their own good, but did he treat them as he did the army of Sennacherib?

OR IF ANY ONE HATH KILLED HIS SLAIN, HE IS SO KILLED) In the Hebrew: Is it after the manner of the slaughter of his slain (namely the Assyrian) that he is killed, namely the Jewish people.

Latin:

Vers. 7. NVMQVID JVXTA PLAGAM PER- CVTIENTIS SE PERCVSSIT EUM) Ostendit Dei bo- nitatem erga Judæos. Castigavit quidem eos, inquit, bono ipsorum, sed an eos ita tractavit, ut Sennacheribi exercitum?

AVT SI QVIS OCCIDIT INTERFECTOS E- JUS, SIC OCCISVS EST) In Hebræo: An ad instar oc- cidionem occisorum illius (nempe Assyrii) occisus est, nempe populus Judaicus.

## 27:8
Vers. 8. IN MEASURE AGAINST MEASURE WHEN IT SHALL BE CAST OFF, THOU WILT JUDGE IT) The people answer, approving God's words. The Hebrew words sound thus: By moderately banishing thou shalt chastise it: namely thy vineyard, just as fathers send away less obedient sons to the country.

HE HATH MEDITATED IN HIS SPIRIT IN THE DAY OF THE EAST WIND) In the Hebrew: he is taken away (for it is the active for the passive) by a violent blast, in the time of the East wind, namely the Assyrian. There is a perpetual opposition of the chastisements of the Jewish people and the punishments: which the Assyrian paid, as if suffocated by heat. See above 25, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 8. IN MENSVRA CONTRA MENSVRAM CUM ABJECTA FUERIT, JUDICABIS EAM) Re- spondet populus, Dei dicta approbans. Verba Hebræa sic sonant: Moderate relegando castigabis eam: nempe vineam tuam, sicut patres filios minus obsequentes rus amandant.

MEDITATVS EST IN SPIRITV SVO DIEM PER DIEM ÆSTVS) In Hebræo: aufertur (est enim acti- vum pro passivo) slanto violento, tempore Euri, nempe As- syrius. Est oppositio perpetua castigationum populi Judæi, & pœnarum: quas pependit Assyrius, velut æstu suffocatus. Vide supra 25, 11.

## 27:9
Vers. 9. THEREFORE UPON THIS) The sense is: on the contrary.

THE INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL BE FORGIVEN) His calamity shall not last.

AND THIS IS ALL HIS FRUIT) All his happiness is situated in this.

THAT HIS SIN MAY BE TAKEN AWAY) That he (the people themselves) may take away his sin: that he may purge himself well: which the following words explain.

WHEN HE SHALL HAVE MADE ALL THE STONES OF THE ALTAR AS STONES OF CHALK DASHED IN PIECES) That he may make the stones of the altar (namely of any altar placed outside the temple) like stones ground into lime. גִר in this place is lime, as גִיר in Daniel v. 5.

THE GROVES AND TEMPLES SHALL NOT STAND) That the groves and πυρεῖα may not exist. Concerning this latter word, see what was said at Levit. 26, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IC CIRCO SVPER HOC) Sensus est: contra vero.

DIMITTETVR INIQVITAS DO MVI JACOB) Non durabit ejus calamitas.

ET ISTE OMNIS FRVCTVS EJVS) Omnis feli- citas ejus in hoc sita est.

VT AUFERATVR PECCATVM EJVS) Ut aufe- rat (ipse populus) peccatum suum: ut se bene repurget: quod explicant sequentia.

CVM POSVERIT OMNES LAPIDES ALTA- RIS VT LAPIDES CINERIS ALLISOS) Ut faciat lapi- des altaris, (nempe cujusque altaris extra templum positi) tanquam lapides in calcem comminutos. גִר Hoc loco est calx, ut גִיר apud Danielem v. 5.

NON STABVNT LVCI ET DELVBRA) Vt non exstent luci & πυρεῖα. De hac voce posteriori vide, quæ dicta ad Levit. 26, 30.

## 27:10
Vers. 10. FOR THE FORTIFIED CITY SHALL BE DESOLATE) כִּי This is 'at' [but]. The sense: But truly Babylon shall be miserably laid waste: see above 13. & 21.

THERE THE CALF SHALL FEED) Everywhere, with no one hindering, it shall wander.

AND THERE IT SHALL LIE DOWN) Quite securely.

AND SHALL CONSUME ITS TOPS) Its branches, namely of the gardens, which were most beautiful in the city of Babylon.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CIVITAS ENIM MVNITA DESOLA- TA ERIT) כִּי Hic est at. Sensus: At vero Babylon mise- re vastabitur: vide supra 13. & 21.

IBI PASCETVR VITVLVS) Vbique nemine im- pediente vagabitur.

ET IBI ACCVBABIT) Secure admodum.

ET CONSUMET SVMMITATES EJVS) Ramos, nempe hortorum, qui pulcherrimi in urbe Babylone.

## 27:11
Vers. 11. IN THE DROUGHT ITS HARVESTS SHALL BE CRUSHED) In the very time of summer, when there was hope of enjoying them.

WOMEN COMING AND TEACHING IT) They shall set it on fire. Women: that is, the Medes, previously despised as too effeminate. Their garments are ἀναξυρίδες, κάνδυς, τίαρα. See Plutarch on Alexander.

FOR IT IS NOT A WISE PEOPLE) The Assyrian.

Concerning Babylon, that what is held in verse 10 is to be understood, whence shall it be proven? And why is the particle כִּי rendered with the opposite sense 'AT' [BUT]? Why is Jerusalem not understood by the name of the city, along with other interpreters?

For in this, most all the ancients and moderns agree. For the discourse was about the Church and the people of God, and the calamities to be sent upon the same, and their end and use, and therefore the native sense of the particle כי is rightly retained by others. FOR THE FORTIFIED CITY SHALL BE DESOLATE, as the Vulgate renders it, is, if I am not mistaken, authentic to Grotius. But that city was the metropolis of the Church of God. What is said in verse 11 about the women, that they are about to come and burn the branches so that they may be consumed by fire, is twisted without any probable reason to the Medes, previously despised as too effeminate: for the Medes are not understood metaphorically by the women, but the extreme devastation of the city is depicted in this way. That beautiful city shall be cast out and abandoned, as an uncultivated desert: There the calf shall feed, and there it shall lie down, and shall consume its shoots; which is wrongly drawn to the Babylonian gardens by Grotius. For the Prophet means this: grass shall grow in that place where the city stood, and shrubs shall grow there, so that calves may graze on the grass and shoots there, where previously magnificent palaces had stood. Its branches shall be dry, women coming shall break them, and shall kindle a flame from them. Here the discourse is about the branches of most fruitful and most pleasant trees, which, the gardens being laid waste and deprived of all cultivation, shall wither, because they are to be burned by any base women whatsoever. Grotius's gloss: IN THE DROUGHT ITS HARVESTS SHALL BE CRUSHED: in the very time of summer, when there was hope of enjoying them, WOMEN COMING shall set it on fire: that is, the Medes, neither agrees with the words, and is merely arbitrary. Since there is no mention made of the Medes by any word, who would believe that they are designated here by the word WOMEN? And it is manifest from what was said before that that explanation concerning the Assyrians is repugnant to the context. Moreover, the cause of such great devastation of the Jerusalemite city and the Jewish people is rendered. FOR IT IS NOT A WISE PEOPLE: THEREFORE HE WHO MADE IT SHALL NOT HAVE MERCY ON IT, AND HE WHO FORMED IT into a people: Which things square with the Jewish people, not likewise with the Assyrians. And Moses complains similarly about that in Deut. 32, 28. 29. It is a nation without counsel, and without prudence. Would that they were wise and understood, and would foresee their latter end! The cause is therefore rendered, why the Jews, who were the people of God, were cast off, and the metropolis laid waste; namely, not because they sinned gravely, but because when they had sinned, they did not want to understand the time of their visitation, they did not want to repent, and to accept Christ and his counsel. Whence, since it has been said, HE WHO MADE IT SHALL NOT HAVE MERCY ON IT, most understand the prophecy concerning the final devastation of Jerusalem, and the destruction of the Jewish people, Jerome, Cyril, and others from the ancients; and also from the moderns Brentius, Osiander, Oecolampadius, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, &c. To which is conveniently subjoined the promise concerning the universal proclamation of the Gospel, in the two final verses of the chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN SICCITATE MESSES EJVS CON- TERENTVR) In ipso æstatis tempore, cum spes erat fruendi.

MV LIERES VENIENTES ET DOCENTES EAM) Incendent eam. Mulieres: id est, Medi contemti an- tea ut molliores. Horum vestes ἀναξυρίδες, κάνδυς, τίαρα, Vide Plutarchum Alexandro.

NON EST ENIM POPVLVS SAPIENS) Assyrius.

De Babylone, quæ habentur versu 10. intelli- genda esse, unde probabitur? Et cur particula כִּי redditur sensu opposito AT? Cur civitatis nomine non intelligitur cum aliis Interpp. Hierosolyma?

In hoc enim plerique omnes veteres & recentiores confentiunt. Sermo enim de Ecclesia & populo Dei, & calamitatibus eidem immittendis, earumq; fine ac usu fuit, ideoq; recte sensus nativus particu- læ כי ab aliis retinetur. QUIA CIVITAS MU- NITA DESOLATA ERIT, ut Vulgata reddit, Grotio, ni fallor, authentica. Civitas vero illa erat metropolis Ecclesiæ Dei. Quod verf. 11. dicitur de mulieribus, quod venturæ sint, & incensuræ ramos, ut comburantur igne, id citra ullam probabilem ra- tionem detorquetur ad Medos antea contemtos, ut molliores: non enim metaphorice per mulieres Medi intelliguntur, sed extrema vastatio urbis ita depin- gitur. Speciosa illa urbs projecta erit & derelicta, quasi desertum incultum: Ibi pascetur vitulus, & ibi accubabit, & consumet surculos ejus; quod ad hortos Babylonicos perperam trahitur à Grotio. Id enim vult Propheta: nascetur gramen in eo loco, ubi stetit urbs, & nascentur ibi virgulta, ita ut ibi vituli depascantur gramen & surculos, ubi prius steterant magnifica palatia. Sicci erunt rami ejus, confringent eos mulieres venientes, & flammam iis ex- citabunt. Hic de ramis arborum fœcundissimarum & amœnissimarum sermo est, quæ vastatis hortis, destitutæ omni cultura, exarescent, quod à mulieri- bus quibusvis vilibus cremandi sint. Grotii glossa: IN SICCITATE MESSES EJUS CONTE- RENTUR: in ipso æstatis tempore, cum spes erat fruendi, MULIERES VENIENTES incendent eam: id est, Medi, neq; verbis congruit, & mere est arbitraria. Quum de Medis nullo verbo mentio facta, quis credat eos hic voce MULIERUM desi- gnatos? Et repugnare contextui illam explicatio- nem de Assyriis, ex antea dictis manifestum est. Redditur autem caussa tantæ vastationis urbis Hie- rosolymitanæ, & populi Judaici. NON EST ENIM POPULUS SAPIENS: PROPTEREA NON MISEREBITUR EJUS, QUI FECIT EUM, ET QUI FORMAVIT EUM in popu- lum: Quæ in Judaicum populum quadrant, non item in Assyrios. Et conqueritur similiter de illo Moses Deut. 32, 28. 29. Gens absq; consilio est, & si- ne prudentia. Utinam saperent & intelligerent, ac novissima præviderent! Causa ergo redditur, cur Judæi, qui populus erant Dei, abjecti, & metropo- lis vastata; scil. non quia graviter peccarunt, sed quia cum peccassent, non voluerunt intelligere tempus visitationis suæ, non voluerunt resipiscere, & Christum atque consilium ejus suscipere. Unde quum dictum sit, NON MISEREBITUR EJUS qui fecit eum, pleriq; intelligunt vaticinium de no- vissima devastatione Hierosolymæ, & populi Ju- daici excidio, Hieronymus, Cyrillus, & alii è vete- ribus; nec non è recentioribus Brentius, Osiander, Oecolampadius, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Meno- chius, &c. Cui commode subjungitur promissio de universali Evangelii præconio, duobus postremis capitis commatibus.

## 27:12
Vers. 12. FROM THE CHANNEL OF THE RIVER EVEN UNTO THE STREAM OF EGYPT.) The Medes will spread from Babylon to the furthest borders, which are towards Egypt. The river κατʼ ἐξοχὴν in these books is everywhere the Euphrates.

AND YE SHALL BE GATHERED ONE BY ONE, O YE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.) Those dissensions in the Assyrian empire will give an opportunity to many Hebrews to return safely to their own, with no one hindering. It is in other words the same as above 11, 15.

Thus the distinguished Evangelical promise concerning the conversion of the Israelites to God is perverted. In the Hebrew text there is nothing about the invasion of enemies. Nor is there anything here about the Babylonian kingdom; nor about the Medes, its enemies. The fountain of truth flows thus: In that day the Lord will thresh (not the Lord will strike, as is perpetually rendered by the Vulgate) from the riverbed of the river (Euphrates) as far as the torrent of Egypt, that is, the Nile; that threshing will extend itself through Assyria and Egypt; and you, children of Israel, will be gathered, one to another. Just as they are threshed, and afterwards cast out by a winnowing fan, and the grains are separated from the chaff, so through Assyria and Egypt the Lord will separate his elect from the children of Israel into his Church: as the proto-baptist says: the winnowing fan is in the hand of Christ, and he will purge his threshing floor, and will gather his wheat into the barn, Matt. 3, 12. For what kind of threshing it is, the following things explain, namely, that through which the dispersed children of Israel are gathered from those places to the Church: which was completed especially in the New Testament, as it is said in John 11, 5: that he might gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed. Concerning the dissensions in the Assyrian empire, not even a 'gry' or a 'my' is held in this whole prophecy; nor is there talk of the Jews returning to Jerusalem, but of the children of Israel being gathered into one. And since Grotius acknowledges that in the following verse the same sense is delivered, the matter is not obscure, that this prophecy is held here not concerning the return of the fugitive Jews, but concerning the conversion of the Israelites, and that it does not precisely designate those who are Israelites according to the flesh, although some of them also were to be converted, but those who are such according to the spirit. IN THAT DAY A GREAT TRUMPET SHALL BE SOUNDED. Which is the trumpet of evangelical preaching, truly great, because it is heard through the whole world, and among the very profane and most idolatrous nations, the Assyrians and the Egyptians. AND THEY SHALL COME WHO WERE LOST FROM THE LAND OF THE ASSYRIANS, AND WHO HAD BEEN IN THE LAND OF EGYPT. Not a few of them will be converted to God, AND THEY SHALL WORSHIP THE LORD IN THE HOLY MOUNT IN JERUSALEM. Which was fulfilled especially in the time of the New Testament, although a type of it was the return of the Israelites and Jews to the Jerusalem temple for the sake of restoring and celebrating true worship. Here, however, spiritual Israelites are designated, and the heavenly Jerusalem: to which not only those who were Israelites by lineage and dispersed among the nations were called and converted, but even the Gentiles themselves through the great trumpet of the Gospel, the sound of which went out into the whole world, Rom. 10, 18. The great trumpet, says Jerome, can be understood as the evangelical word: concerning which we also read in the same Prophet: Ascend upon a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion: exalt your voice, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem. The holy mount, therefore, and that Jerusalem is the one of which we have often spoken: You have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. A gathering is promised, at any rate, to worship the Lord in the holy mount in Jerusalem, which is not the external Mount Zion; for the children of Israel were never gathered to it from Assyria, nor after the most recent devastation of Jerusalem, concerning which most acknowledge the Prophet to have prophesied here, could they be gathered to it. And therefore, without doubt, in the Prophetic manner, the heavenly Jerusalem must be understood, the spiritual Mount Zion, the Church of God, to which, even if it were specifically designated here that the Jews and Israelites according to the flesh were to be gathered, it must nevertheless be confessed that this pertains primarily to the time of the New Testament, when the great trumpet of the Gospel will be heard through the whole world, and thus also in Assyria and in Egypt. Rightly, therefore, Brentius: How will they worship there, when a little before he said that that place was to be devastated and turned into pastures for calves! You will not understand the pious to be coming from all nations to the place of the city of Jerusalem corporally; but for that reason they are said to worship

the Lord in the holy mount in Jerusalem: because they believe in the Gospel of Christ, which was announced in the beginning in the city of Jerusalem, on the day of Pentecost, and from that place scattered into the whole world. That there is an allusion to the future return of the Israelites from Assyria and Egypt, to which they had been led away and had gone, as Jeremiah ch. 43 testifies, can be admitted, but one must be careful not to posit a double sense: one concerning those being recalled from captivity to the temple being restored in Jerusalem, another concerning the conversion to the Church of Christ under the New Testament. These things are far different: in an allusion to some history, that history is presupposed from elsewhere, as being either already described elsewhere, as happens, or predicted as about to happen; but when a twin sense is feigned in the same prophecy, literal and historical and mystical, then the history is not presupposed as known from elsewhere, but the same is believed to be inferred by the same words, by which a spiritual and also mystical sense is also considered to underlie them. Which the Dutch Interpreters think is happening here, accepting these things both concerning the return under Cyrus in the literal sense, and concerning the conversion under the New Testament in the mystical sense: but that is by no means to be admitted, lest Holy Scripture be rendered ambiguous and perplexed, which the Holy Spirit willed to be clear and certain. But the Grotian gloss, that these things are to be understood concerning the time of Hezekiah, after the city was freed from the siege of Sennacherib, bears no appearance of truth, and is hitherto unheard of: nor does it in any way satisfy so magnificent a promise. See here only how jejune this is: A GREAT TRUMPET SHALL BE SOUNDED: that is, the matter will be so, as if a retreat were being sounded in an army: AND THEY SHALL COME WHO WERE LOST FROM THE LAND OF THE ASSYRIANS, AND WHO HAD BEEN CAST OUT FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT: Many of the Hebrews will have an opportunity because of the dissensions in the Assyrian empire to return safely to their own. Many also will return from Egypt, to which they had withdrawn, first when Shalmaneser arrived, then Sennacherib: concerning whom nothing is read in sacred history. What Grotius had invented on Isaiah 11:11 has been discussed there. AND THEY SHALL WORSHIP THE LORD IN THE HOLY MOUNT IN JERUSALEM, that is, they will restore the omitted sacred rites. But that the sacred rites had been omitted at Jerusalem during the time of the siege of Sennacherib, or had need of restoration, is entirely false and contrary to sacred history; therefore there is οὐδὲν ὑγιὲς (nothing sound) in that gloss of Grotius: who ought here to have lent an ear to his Menochius on verse 12, noting thus: He teaches that the exiled and fugitive Jews will come to the Church of Christ. And to the words GATHERED ONE, AND ONE: You shall be gathered to one; as if he were to say: Whoever you are, true Israelites not by flesh, but by spirit, you shall individually be gathered to Christ in the Church. This is what is said in John 11. That he should gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed. To v. 13. GREAT TRUMPET. Of Evangelical preaching. THEY SHALL COME. They will flow together to Christ and the Church IN THE HOLY MOUNT IN JERUSALEM, in the Church, of which Mount Zion was a type. Which Tirinus explains more fully and sufficiently appropriately, having brought forward the authority of other interpreters, both ancient and modern. THE GREAT TRUMPET SHALL SOUND, namely of Evangelical preaching, by which the awakened true Israelites will run from all sides to Christ from the places in which they were living dispersed and as if LOST, even from Assyria and Egypt, and all unanimously will together worship the true God and their Messiah. IN THE HOLY MOUNT SION IN JERUSALEM, that is, in the holy Church of Christ. Thus St. Jerome, Cyril, and Theodoret, and following them Alvarez and a Lapide. It indeed alludes to the return of the Jews from the Babylonian and Egyptian captivity: but through these shadows he intends to designate the spiritual redemption of the human race through Christ. Oecolampadius acknowledges that this prophecy pertains to Christ and to the Church, which is to be observed against Junius and Piscator, who explain it solely regarding the return from the Babylonian captivity. Calvin himself understood these things more correctly than they did. This was indeed fulfilled under Darius, but there is no doubt that the Prophet wished to extend this prophecy further: because that restoration was like a certain obscure foreshadowing of the liberation which they obtained through Christ: at whose coming not only in Assyria or Egypt, but in the extreme parts of the world, the spiritual trumpet, namely that of the Gospel, was heard; then the people of God were gathered, so that they might flow together to Mount Sion, that is, into the Church. For we know that this form of speaking is customary for the Prophets, when they wish to signify the true worship of God and consensus in religion and piety. For they accommodated themselves to the custom of the people, so that they might be better understood. And we also know that the Gospel flowed from Sion. Jerome refutes the gloss of the Jews regarding this passage. In this place, the Jews promise themselves vain hopes, that at the consummation of the world, when their ἠλευθέρωσις (liberation) has come, the people dispersed from the Assyrians and from the land of Egypt will be gathered and come to Jerusalem, and having built the temple, will worship the Lord their God. Which, according to the letter, cannot stand at all. For they will be called not only from the Assyrians and from Egypt, but from the whole world, who are about to believe in Christ. And these things are regarding Chapter XXVII.

Latin:

Vers. 12. AB ALVEO FLUMINIS USQVE AD TORRENTEM ÆGYPTI.) Medi à Babylone ad ultimos fines, qui Ægyptum versus sunt, pervadent. Flumen κατʼ ἐξοχὴν in his libris ubique Euphrates.

ET VOS CONGREGABIMINI VNUS ET VNUS, FILII ISRAEL.) Dissidia ista in imperio Assyrio- rum occasionem dabunt multis Hebræis tuto, nemine im- pediente, ad suos revertendi. Est aliis verbis idem quod supra 11, 15.

Pervertitur ita insignis promissio Evangelica de conversione Israëlitarum ad Deum. In textu He- bræo nihil de hostium pervasione. Nec de regno Ba- bylonico hic quicquam; neque de Medis, ejusdem hostibus. Fons veritatis ita fluit: In die illa tritu- rabit Dominus (non percutiet Dominus, uti perpe- ram reddidit Vulgata) de alveo fluminis (Euphratis) usq́; ad torrentem Ægypti, hoc est, Nilum; trituratio ista per Assyriam & Ægyptum sese extendet; & vos filii Israël congregabimini, unus ad alterum. Quemadmodum triturantur, & postea ventilabro projiciuntur, separantur grana à quisquiliis, ita per Assyriam & Ægyptum Dominus separabit electos suos de filiis Israël in Ecclesiam suam: sicut πρωτο- βαπτιςὴς ait: ventilabrum est in manu Christi, ac re- purgabit aream suam, & congregabit triticum suum in horreum, Matth. 3, 12. Qualis enim trituratio sit, explicant sequentia, nimirum per quam ex illis locis colliguntur ad Ecclesiam filii Israël dispersi: quod cumprimis in Novo Test. completum est, uti dicitur Joh. 11, 5. ut filios Dei, qui erant dispersi, con- gregaret in unum. De dissidiis in imperio Assyrio- rum ne gry quidem vel my habetur in toto hoc va- ticinio; neque de Judæis Hierosolymam reversu- ris, sed de filiis Israël in unum congregandis sermo est. Et quum agnoscat Grotius, commate sequen- te eundem sensum tradi; res haud obscura est, non de reditu Judæorum profugorum, sed de Israëlita- rum conversione, vaticinium hic haberi, neq; præ- cise illos, qui secundum carnem sunt Israëlitæ, etsi eorum etiam nonnulli convertendi erant, sed qui secundum spiritum tales sunt, designari. IN DIE ILLA CLANGETUR IN TUBA MAGNA. Quæ est tuba Evangelicæ prædicationis vere ma- gna, quia exauditur per totum terrarum orbem, & inter ipsas prophanas & maxime idololatricas gen- tes, Assyrios & Ægyptios. ET VENIENT QUI PERDITI ERANT DE TERRA ASSYRIO- RUM, ET QUI EXTITERANT IN TERRA ÆGYPTI. Ex illis non pauci convertentur ad Deum, ET ADORABUNT DOMINUM IN MONTE SANCTO IN JERUSALEM. Quod impletum est cumprimis tempore Novi T. etsi typus ejus fuerit reversio Israëlitarum & Ju- dæorum ad templum Hierosolymitanum veri cul- tus restaurandi, & celebrandi gratia. Hic vero spirituales Israëlitæ designantur, & cœlestis Hie- rosolyma: ad quam vocati & conversi sunt non tan- tum qui prosapia Israëlitæ, & inter gentes dispersi fuêre, sed etiam ipsimet gentiles per magnam Ev- angelii tubam, cujus sonus exivit in totum terra- rum orbem, Rom. 10, 18. Tuba magna, inquit Hie- ronymus, potest intelligi sermo evangelicus: de quo & in eodem Propheta legimus: Super montem ex- celsum ascende, qui evangelizas Sion: exalta vo- cem tuam, qui evangelizas Hierusalem. Mons ergo sanctus & Hierusalem illa est, de qua sæpe diximus: Accessistis ad Sion montem & civitatem Dei viven- tis, Hierusalem cœlestem. Promittitur utiq; con- gregatio ad adorandum Dominum in monte san- cto in Jerusalem, qui non est mons Zion externus; ad eum enim filii Israël ex Assyria congregari nun- quam sunt, neque post vastationem novissimam Hierosolymæ, de qua hic vaticinatum esse Pro- phetam pleriq; agnoscunt, eo congregari potuêre. Ideoque sine dubio more Prophetico intelligenda erit cœlestis Hierosolyma, spiritualis mons Zion, Ec- clesia Dei, ad quam si maxime Judæos atque Israëli- tas secundum carnem congregandos esse, hic pe- culiariter designaretur, ad Novi tamen Test. tem- pus hoc imprimis pertinere, cum magna tuba Ev- angelii per totum orbem, adeoq; in Assyria etiam atque in Ægypto, exaudietur, fatendum erit. Re- cte ergo Brentius: Quomodo ibi adorabunt, cum paulo ante dixerit, eum locum vastandum & conver- tendum in pascua vitulorum! Non intelliges pios venturos ex omnibus nationibus ad locum urbis Hie- rusalem corporaliter; sed idcirco dicuntur adorare

Dominum in sancto monte in Hierusalem: quia cre- dunt Evangelio Christi, quod initio annunciatum est, in urbe Hierusalem, in die Pentecostes, & ab eo loco sparsum in totum orbem terræ. Alludi ad redi- tum futurum Israëlitarum ex Assyria & Ægypto, quo abducti, & profecti erant, teste Jeremia cap. 43. admitti potest, sed cavendum, ne duplex sta- tuatur sensus: alius de revocandis soluta captivitate ad templum restaurandum in Jerusalem, alius de conversione ad Ecclesiam Christi sub Novo Testam. Longe diversa hæc sunt: in allusione ad historiam aliquam præsupponitur ea historia aliunde, utpote vel descripta jam alibi, uti evenit, vel prædicta, uti eventura; cum vero geminus sensus in eodem vati- cinio fingitur, literalis, & historicus atque mysticus, tum non præsupponitur historia, uti aliunde nota, sed verbis iisdem inferri eadem creditur, quibus spiritualis etiam atque mysticus sensus subesse cen- setur. Quod Belgæ Interpp. hic fieri putant, tum de reditu sub Cyro sensu literali, tum de conversione sub Novo Test. sensu mystico hæc accipientes: sed id mi- nime admittendum est, ne Scriptura S. ambigua & perplexa reddatur, quam perspicuam, & certam es- se voluit S. S. Grotiana vero glossa, quod hæc in- telligenda sint de Ezechiæ tempore, post liberatam urbem ab obsidione Sennacheribi, nullam speciem veri præ se fert, & hactenus inaudita est: neq; tam magnifice promissioni ullatenus satisfacit. Vide hic modo, quam jejunum hoc sit, CLANGETUR TUBA MAGNA: id est, ita res se habebit, quasi in exercitu canatur receptui: ET VENIENT QUI PERDITI ERANT DE TERRA ASSYRIO- RUM, ET QUI EJECTI ERANT E TER- RA ÆGYPTI: Multi ex Ebræis occasionem habe- bunt propter dissidia in imperio Assyriorum tuto ad suos revertendi. Multi etiam ex Ægypto redibunt, quo concesserant, adventante primum Salmanassare, deinde Sennacheribo: de quo nihil in historia S. legi- tur. Quæ commentus erat Grotius ad Es. 11, 11. il- lic discussa sunt. ET ADORABUNT DOMI- NUM IN MONTE SANCTO IN JERUSA- LEM, id est, omissa sacra restaurabunt. Atqui tem- pore obsidionis Sennacheribi omissa sacra Hiero- solymis fuisse, aut restauratione opus habuisse, fal- sum omnino est, & historiæ sacræ contrarium; pro- inde οὐδὲν ὑγιὲς in illa glossa Grotii: qui hic aures præbere debuisset suo Menochio ad vers. 12. ita no- tanti: Docet Judæos exules & profugos venturos ad Ecclesiam Christi. Et ad verba CONGREGA- BIMINI UNUS, ET UNUS: Congregabimini ad unum; quasi dicat: Quicunq; estis veri Israëlitæ non carne, sed spiritu, singuli congregabimini ad Chri- stum in Ecclesiam. Hoc est quod dicitur Joan. 11. Ut filios Dei, qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Ad v. 13. TUBA MAGNA. Prædicationis Evan- gelicæ. VENIENT. Confluent ad Christum, & Ec- clesiam IN MONTE SANCTO IN JERUSA- LEM, in Ecclesia, cujus typus fuit mons Sion. Quod uberius & convenienter satis explicat Tirinus, alio- rum simul cum veterum, tum recentiorum Interpp. auctoritate adducta. CLANGETUR TUBA MAGNA, nempe prædicationis Evangelicæ, qua exciti veri Israëlitæ undiq; ad Christum accurrent ex locis, in quibus dispersi & quasi PERDITI dege- bant, etiam ex Assyria & Ægypto, & unanimiter omnes simul colent verum Deum & Messiam suum. IN MONTE SANCTO SION IN JERUSA- LEM, id est, in Ecclesia sancta Christi. Ita S. Hiero- nymus, Cyrillus & Theodorethus, & hos secutus Alva- rez & a Lapide. Alludit quidem ad reditum Judæo- rum è captivitate Babylonica & Ægyptiaca: sed per has umbras intendit designare spiritualem redemtio- nem humani generis per Christum. Pertinere hoc va- ticinium ad Christum & ad Ecclesiam, agnoscit Oe- colampadius, quod contra Junium & Piscatorem, qui solum de reditu è captivitate Babylonica expli- cant, observandum. Rectius his etiam Calvinus ipse hæc intellexit. Hoc quidem sub Dario impletum est, sed dubium non est, quin Propheta hoc vaticinium longius extendere voluerit: quia restitutio illa velut obscura quædam adumbratio fuit liberationis, quam per Christum consequuti sunt: cujus adventu non tantum in Assyria aut Ægypto, sed in extremis par- tibus orbis, tuba spiritualis, nempe Evangelii, clan- gor auditus est, tunc collectus est populus Dei, ut con- flueret ad montem Sion, id est, in Ecclesiam. Sci- mus enim hanc loquendi formam usitatam esse Pro- phetis, dum verum Dei cultum & consensum in reli- gione & pietate significare volunt. Accommodabant enim sese mori populi usitato, quo melius intelligeren- tur. Atq; etiam ex Sion Evangelium fluxisse scimus. Judæorum glossam circa h. l. refellit Hieronymus. In hoc loco Judæi cassa sibi vota promittunt, quod in consummatione mundi, quando ἠλευθέρωσις suus vene- rit, de Assyriis, & de terra Ægypti dispersus popu- lus congregetur & veniat in Hierusalem, & ædifica- to templo adoret Dominum Deum suum. Quod se- cundum literam omnino stare non potest. Neque enim de Assyriis tantum & de Ægypto, sed de toto orbe terrarum, qui in Christum credituri sunt, vo- cabuntur. Atque hæc de Cap. XXVII.

## 27:13
Ver. 13. IT SHALL BE BLOWN WITH A GREAT TRUMPET) The matter will be as if a retreat were sounded in an army. AND THEY SHALL COME WHO WERE LOST FROM THE LAND OF THE ASSYRIANS) The same sense as in the preceding verse. AND WHO WERE CAST OUT IN THE LAND OF EGYPT) For many had also gone there when first Shalmaneser, then Sennacherib, was approaching. See above 11, 11. AND THEY SHALL WORSHIP THE LORD IN THE HOLY MOUNT IN JERUSALEM) They will restore the omitted sacred rites.

Latin:

Vers. 13. CLANGETVR IN TVBA MAGNA) Ita res se habebit quasi in exercitu canatur receptui. ET VENIENT QVI PERDITI ERANT DE TER- RA ASSYRIORVM) Idem sensus qui commate præcedente. ET QVI EJECTI ERANT IN TERRA ÆGY- PTI) Nam & eo multi concesserant adventante primum Salmanassare, deinde Sennacheribo. Vide supra 11, 11. ET ADORABUNT DOMINUM IN MONTE SAN- CTO IN JERUSALEM) Omissa sacra instaurabunt.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII. A woe is denounced against the proud crown of Israel; it is predicted that the Lord will be a pleasant crown to the remnant of the people, and the punishment of the security of the unfaithful is designated, but to the faithful, security is promised in Christ the cornerstone.

V. 1. WOE TO THE CROWN OF PRIDE TO THE DRUNKARDS OF EPHRAIM AND TO THE FADING FLOWER.) Let it be permitted to translate the Hebrew thus: Woe to the proud crown of the Ephraimite drunkards, to the fading flower, i.e. Crown and flowers are the same. Drunkards were accustomed to place crowns upon themselves. Anacreon I. He shows, however, by an excellent simile, that those delights and pride will not last long. Such is that in the Greek Epigram: Ἄνθεὶς καὶ λήγεις καὶ σὺ καὶ ὁ ςέφανος (You bloom and you fade, both you and the crown). The LXX in this place read 'schin' with a left point: for they translate 'the hired ones'. OF THE GLORY OF HIS EXULTATION) In the Hebrew: Ornament of his glory: which is the ἐξάκουσος (famed) of the crown. All these things are repeated a little later. ON THE HEAD OF THE FAT VALLEY) The fat valley is the valley of Shechem. Samaria is on a mountain. V. 4. AS THE EARLY) As the early fig. BEFORE THE MATURITY OF AUTUMN) Before the summer. IMMEDIATELY AS HE SHALL HOLD IT IN HIS HAND, HE SHALL DEVOUR IT) Thus Shalmaneser immediately conquered the ten tribes and overturned their state from the foundations. TO THE REMNANT OF HIS PEOPLE) That is, the two tribes which were immune from that evil. Ver. 6. THE SPIRIT OF JUDGMENT TO HIM THAT SITTETH UPON JUDGMENT) God will give Hezekiah knowledge of the law. AND STRENGTH TO THEM THAT RETURN FROM THE WAR TO THE GATE) From the war against the Philistines. BUT THESE ALSO THROUGH WINE HAVE NOT KNOWN) They acted wantonly in prosperous things: Such is that: Fortunatâ dulci Ebria (In fortunate sweet drunkenness). Ver. 7. THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN HIM THAT SEETH) In the Hebrew: They have erred in vision: that is, they followed false prophets. FOR ALL TABLES) Under the figure he understands tribunals. V. 8. ARE FULL OF VOMIT AND FILTH) With corrupt judgments, which the Latins also call filth. WEANED FROM THE MILK, TAKEN AWAY FROM THE BREASTS)

Will God teach infants? for adults mock the precepts. BECAUSE COMMAND COMMAND, COMMAND COMMAND) In the Hebrew: Precept upon precept, precept upon precept, I gave to them, that is, I very often inculcated my laws to them. EXPECT RE-EXPECT; EXPECT RE-EXPECT) In the Hebrew: קו לקו קו לקו, whence the Nicolaitans and other heretics made 'caul-cau', as Epiphanius mentions regarding the Nicolaitans, and Jerome regarding this place. It signifies line upon line, line upon line: by a simile taken from masters, who guide the hands of their disciples through prescribed lines. V. 11. FOR IN THE SPEECH OF THE LIP) In a barbaric language. AND ANOTHER TONGUE) That is, exotic. HE SPEAKS TO THIS PEOPLE) That is, He will use the work of barbarians to chastise them. For Aquila also adapted these things to God, no less than Paul in I Cor. 14, 21. As we learn from the Philocalia of Origen. Ver. 12. THIS IS MY REST, REFRESH THE WEARY) This will be my joy if you relieve the miserable and afflicted. Ver. 13. AND THE WORD OF THE LORD SHALL BE TO THEM, COMMAND COMMAND) From the Hebrew: And the word of the Lord has become to them, precept upon precept, that is, through an illusory μίμησιν (imitation) they mock the words of the Prophets. Jerome interprets these things thus: The divine word speaks against the ten tribes, which were reigning in Samaria, and because of Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, they were called Ephraim. And he calls them the crown of pride, because compared to the two tribes, which were called Judah, they were more sublime both in number and in strength. And he calls them Ephraim the drunkards: who do not understand their creator, but instead of the Lord worship golden calves in Dan and Bethel. These were once in the flower of lords, and in glory, when they were ruled by David and Solomon, and in the twelve tribes they were worshipping God in the temple of Jerusalem: who were at the summit of the most fertile valley, which in Hebrew is called גיא שמנים. It signifies, moreover, the place where the Lord was betrayed: upon the summit of which valley the temple of the Lord is situated. These have been made drunk with the wine of error and madness, which Jeroboam mixed for them: wherefore the Lord threatens them with punishment, that just as a whirlwind of hail shatters everything, and the force of flooding waters carries off whatever it finds in its way: so they shall be destroyed by the army of the Assyrians, and what remains shall be transferred to the mountains or cities of the Medes. He compares, however, the glory of the ten tribes to a crown of various flowers, which had such beauty that, just as if someone, before summer and autumn come, seeing a πρόδρομον fig on a tree, immediately as he holds it in his hand, devours it: so also the ten tribes, when the Assyrian sees them, he shall lay waste and devour, and leave nothing at all of the former people in Samaria. Although indeed it may be admitted, as it has seemed to most others, to other interpreters, and it seems manifest from the subsequent rebukes of the drunkards, that these things refer to the drunkenness of the Israelites, not to idolatry, for the Jews are joined to them in this vice, but these also knew not because of wine, and erred because of drunkenness, etc., yet the flowers and crowns of drunkards are not to be fetched here from Anacreon, where the Prophet himself quite clearly explains the Crown as the glory of the kingdom, in which Ephraim boasted over Judah, and predicts that it will be a fading flower, when on the contrary the Lord of hosts himself shall be a crown of glory and a garland of exaltation for Judah. Most wish for the KINGDOM to be understood by the CROWN. Menochius: CROWN OF PRIDE, i.e., PROUD KINGDOM: FADING FLOWER, that is, whose crown of glory is like a fading flower, which as soon as it has …bloomed, withers and perishes. Oecolampadius thinks that by the crown and the flower, momentary happiness of life is indicated. No one besides Calvin, from whom Grotius has these things, is easily found who dreamed here of the custom of drunkards crowning their wines. Verse 13. THAT THEY MAY GO AND FALL BACKWARD, AND BE BROKEN, AND BE SNARED, AND BE TAKEN.) They will say these things for so long, until may they fall in their evil ways, and being oppressed and ensnared, may they be captured by the enemy, which happened to many when Sennacherib broke in.

That these things are to be understood concerning the irruption of Sennacherib is supported by no evidence, nor has any interpreter easily accepted them as such. Indeed, the text does not admit it. For here God threatens all the Jews, not just some cities, Jerusalem excepted; indeed, just as more serious sins were rampant in this metropolis than anywhere else in the kingdom of Judah, so it was by no means to be excepted from the judgment of God hanging over the people. Therefore, it does not square with the times of Hezekiah, during which, while other cities suffered violence from Sennacherib, the Metropolis remained safe. The Prophet complained in v. 5 et seqq. about the entire people, about the Priests and Prophets, about the judges and Princes equally as about the common people, about all the tables of judgment, so that except for those weaned from milk, those torn from the breasts, there remained no one whom the Lord might teach knowledge, and whom He might make to understand. Therefore, He threatens them all in general with a worthy judgment; they will go and fall backward, and be broken, and be snared and captured. Which emphatically define a judgment far more serious than what occurred under Hezekiah. Nor was such Epicureanism publicly rampant at that time under a pious King, to whom the Spirit of judgment was granted by God, v. 6; indeed, the Lord was then a crown of glory to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, v. 5, girding, adorning, and protecting them. And how do those words in v. 14, HEAR THE WORD OF THE LORD, YOU SCORNFUL MEN, WHO RULE OVER MY PEOPLE, WHO ARE IN JERUSALEM, fit the time and reign of so pious and just a King? Which Grotius so perverts; he wants it understood, of course, not as the city properly, but as the whole land, which was called the house of Jerusalem. But where is the whole land understood by the word Jerusalem, and the people who are in Jerusalem understood by such words as the remaining people in Judea outside of Jerusalem? Is this not a manifest inversion of the Prophet's words? He also twists the Epicurean voices of the scorners and mockers, who said WE HAVE MADE A COVENANT WITH DEATH, WE HAVE MADE LIES OUR REFUGE, into another sense: We will make a covenant with the deadly enemy Sennacherib, we will pretend that we are of the same religion as the Assyrians are. Where and how is Sennacherib called death, and hell (for the Prophet adds this to death)? He could have drawn a plainer and not at all twisted sense from his Menochius: We have made a covenant with death, i.e., we do not fear death. BECAUSE WE HAVE MADE LIES &c. They do not say it thus, but the Prophet interprets it thus, namely, that their hope is fallacious. Nor do others say it badly: That they said these things not in open words, but by the deed itself. The sense, therefore, will be that they behaved as if they had made a covenant with death, and had made an agreement with hell, and that they placed their hope and protection in nothing but lies. The Prophet looked at their affections and pursuits, not what they pretended. Some understand by lies the IDOLS, which the Samaritans served; indeed, they even make death and hell the names of idols. But these are twisted and foreign. Nor is this discourse about the Samaritans, but about the Jews. But that the Jews pretended the religion of the Assyrians in the time of Hezekiah is nowhere read in Sacred History: much less that they placed their protection and the confidence of their security in it.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVIII. Denunciato væ superbæ Israëliticæ coronæ, reli- quiis populi coronam jucundam Dominum futurum prædicitur, ac securitatis infide- lium pœna designatur, fidelibus vero in Christo lapide angulari securit. promittitur

V. 1. VÆ CORONÆ SUPERBIÆ EBRIIS EPHRAIM ET FLORI DECIDENTI.) Hebræa sic liceat vertere: Væ coronæ superbæ, ebriosorum Ephraimitarum, flori sc. caduco. Corona & flores idem. Ebrii solebant sibi coronas impo- nere. Anacreon I. Ostendit autem per egregiam similitu- dinem, non diu duraturas istas delitias ac fastum. Tale illud in Græco Epigrammate. Ἄνθεὶς καὶ λήγεις καὶ σὺ καὶ ὁ ςέφανος. LXX. hoc loco legerunt schin cum sinistro puncto: vertunt enim οἱ μισθωτοὶ. GLORIÆ EXSULTATIONIS EJUS) In Hebræo: Ornamento gloriæ ejus: quæ est ἐξάκουσος coronæ. Repetun- tur omnia hæc paulo post. IN VERTICE VALLIS PINGUISSIMÆ) Vallis pin- guissima est vallis Sichem. Samaria in monte. V. 4. QUASI TEMPORANEUM) Quasi ficus præcox. ANTE MATURITATEM AUTUMNI) Ante æstatem. STATIM UT MANU TENUERIT, DEVORA- BIT ILLUD) Sic statim Salmanassar decem tribus vicit, & statum earum funditus evertit. RESIDUO POPULI SUI) Id est, duabus tribubus quæ ab illo malo immunes fuere. Vers. 6. SPIRITUS JUDICII SEDENTI SUPER JUDICIUM) Dabit Deus Ezechiæ juris notitiam. ET FORTITUDO REVERTENTIBUS DE BEL- LO AD PORTAM) A bello contra Philisthinos. VERUM HI QUOQUE PRÆ VINO NESCIE- RUNT) Lascivierunt in rebus prosperis: Tale illud: For- tunatâ dulci Ebria. Vers. 7. NESCIERUNT VIDENTEM) In Hebræo: Erraverunt in visione: id est, secuti sunt falsos Prophetas. OMNES ENIM MENSÆ) Sub figura intelligit tribunalia V. 8. REPLE TÆ SUNT VOMITU SORDIUMQUE) Judiciis corruptis, quas & Latini sordes vocant. ABLACTATOS A LACTE, AVULSOS AB U- Tom. II. Y. T.

BERIBUS) An infantes Deus docebit? nam adulti præce- pta irrident. QUIA MANDA REMANDA, MANDA REMANDA) In Hebræo: Præceptum ad præceptum, præceptum ad præce- ptum, illis dedi, id est, sæpissime illis inculcavi meas leges. EXSPECTA REEXSPECTA; EXSPECTA REEXSPE- CTA) In Hebræo: קו לקו קו לקו, unde καυλαυκὰυ fece- re Nicolaitæ & Hæretici alii, memorantibus Epiphanio in Nicolaitis, & ad hunc locum Hieronymo. Significat id line- am ad lineam, lineam ad lineam: similitudine à magistris su- mta, qui discipulorum manus per præscriptas lineas ducunt. V. 11. IN LOQUELA ENIM LABII) Sermone barbaro. ET LINGUA ALTERA) Id est, exotica. LOQUITUR AD POPULUM ISTUM) Id est, Barbarorum opera utetur ad eos castigandos. Nam Deo hæc aptavit etiam Aquila, non minus quam Paulus I. Cor. 14, 21. Vt ex Philocalia Origenis discimus. Vers. 12. HÆC EST REQUIES MEA, REFICI- TE LASSUM) Hoc meum erit gaudium si miseros & af- flictos sublevetis. Vers. 13. ET ERIT EIS VERBUM DOMINI, MAN- DA REMANDA) Ex Hebræo: Et factum est eis verbum Do- mini, præceptum ad præceptum, id est, per illusoriam μίμησιν verba Prophetarum subsannant. Hieronymus hæc ita interpretatur: Loquitur sermo divinus adversus decem tribus, quæ re- gnabant in Samaria, & propter Hieroboam, qui de tribu Ephraim fuit, appellabantur Ephraim. Et vo- cat eos coronam superbiæ, quia comparati duabus tri- bubus, quæ appellabantur Juda, sublimiores erant & numero & robore. Ebriosq; eos dicit Ephraim: qui suum non intelligant creatorem, sed pro Domino ado- rent vitulos aureos in Dan & Bethel. Isti quondam in flore fuerunt domini, & in gloria, quando regeban- tur à David, & Salomone, & in duodecim tribubus e- rant adorantes Deum in templo Hierusalem: qui fue- runt in vertice vallis pinguissimæ, quod Hebraice dici- tur גיא שמנים. Significat autem locum, ubi traditus Dominus est: Super cujus vallis verticem templum Domini situm est. Isti inebriati sunt vino erroris & amentiæ, quod eis miscuit Hieroboam: Quapropter pœnam illis minatur Dominus, quod sicut grandinis turbo universa confringit, & impetus aquarum in- undantium, quicquid obvium invenerit, rapit: sic ab Assyriorum deleantur exercitu, & quod reliquum fuerit, in montes sive urbes Mediæ transferatur. Com- parat autem gloriam decem tribuum coronæ vario- rum florum, quæ tantam habuerit pulchritudinem, ut quomodo siquis, antequam æstas veniat, & autumnus, πρόδρομον ficum videns in arbore, statim ut manu te- nuerit, devorat: sic & decem tribus, cum Assyrius vi- derit, vastet & devoret, & nihil omnino pristini po- puli relinquat in Samaria. Quamvis vero admitti possit, quod plerisq; aliis visum est interpretibus, & è sequentibus ebriosorum reprehensionibus mani- festum videtur, hæc ebrietatem Israëlitarum respi- cere, non idololatriam, conjunguntur enim in hoc vitio iisdem Judæi, verum hi quoq; præ vino nescic- runt, & præ ebrietate erraverunt & c. non tamen flo- res & coronæ ebriorum huc arcessendæ ex Anacre- onte, ubi Propheta ipse Coronam de gloria regni, qua superbiebat Ephraim præ Juda, haud obscure ex- plicat, eumq; florem decidentem fore prædicat, quum ex adverso Judæ Dominus ipse exercituum fu- turus sit corona gloriæ, & sertum exaltationis. Pleriq; per CORONAM regnum intelligi volunt. Meno- chius CORONA SUPERBIÆ, i. e. REGNO SU- PERBO: FLORIDECIDENTI, id est, cujus corona gloria similis est flori decidenti, qui mox ut floruit, marcescit, & perit. Oecolampadius per coronam & florem momentaneam vitæ felicitatem indigi- tari putat. Qui ebriorum morem vina coronantium hic somniavit, nemo præter Calvinum, à quo hæc habet Grotius, facile invenitur. Vers. 13. VT VADANT ET CADANT RETROR- SUM, ET CONTERANTUR, ET ILLAQVEEN- TUR, ET CAPIANTVR.) Tamdiu ista dicent, donec in malis viis suis cadant, & oppressi, irretitiq; ab hoste capi- antur, quod multis evenit, irrumpente Sennacheribo.

De Sennacheribi irruptione hæc intelligenda esse, nullo indicio constat, nec facile quisquam In- terpp. ita ea accepit. Imo non admittit id textus. Minatur enim hic Deus Judæis universis, non ci- vitatibus tantum nonnullis, Hierosolyma excepta; imo ut in hac metropoli graviora peccata grassat funt, quam uspiam in regno Judæ, ita nequaquam illa excipienda erat à judicio Dei populo impen- dente. Non ergo quadrat id ad Ezechiæ tempo- ra, quibus, aliis civitatibus per Sennacheribum vim passis, Metropolis salva manebat, Questus est Pro- pheta v. 5. seqq. de integro populo, de Sacerdotibus & Prophetis, de judicibus & Principibus æque ac de vulgo, de mensis judiciorum omnibus, adeo ut præter ablactatos à lacte, avulsos ab uberibus non superarit, quem doceret Dominus scientiam, & quem intel- ligere faceret. His ergo in universum minatur di- gnum judicium, vadent & cadent retrorsum, & con- terentur, & illaqueabuntur & capientur. Quæ em- phatice judicium longe gravius definiunt, quam sub Ezechia evenerit. Neque tum publice grassa- batur ejusmodi Epicureismus sub Rege pio, cui Spiritus judicii à Deo concedebatur v. 6. imo erat tum Dominus corona gloriæ tribubus Juda & Ben- jamin v. 5. cingens, decorans & protegens easdem. Et quomodo illa v. 14. PROPTER HOC AU- DITE VERBUM DOMINI VIRI ILLU- SORES, QUI DOMINAMINI SUPER PO- PULUM MEUM, QUI EST IN JERU- SALEM, tempori, & Imperio tam pii, & justi Regis congruunt? Quæ ita pervertit Grotius, ni- mirum intelligi vult non urbem proprie, sed totam terram, quæ domus Jerusalem dicta fuerit. Sed ubi voce Jerusalem tota terra, & verbis ejusmodi popu- lus, qui est in Jerusalem, populus reliquus in Judæa extra Jerusalem intelligitur? Annon hæc manife- sta est inversio verborum Prophetæ? Voces etiam Epicureas illusorum & empæctarum, qui dicebant PERCUSSIMUS FOEDUS CUM MOR- TE, POSUIMUS MENDACIUM SPEM NOSTRAM, in alium sensum detorquet: Percu- tiemus fœdus cum hoste mortifero Sennacheribo, si- mulabimus, nos esse ejusdem religionis, cujus sunt Assyrii. Ubi & quomodo Sennacherib, & mors, & infernus, (hunc enim addit morti Propheta, nuncu- patur? Sensum planiorem ac minime contortum è Menochio suo haurire potuisset: Percussimus fœdus cum morte, q. d. non timemus mortem. QUIA POSUIMUS MENDACIUM &c. Non ita illi dicunt, sed ita interpretatur Propheta, sc. fallacem esse illorum spem. Neque male alii: Hæc ipsos non verbis quidem apertis, sed re ipsa dixisse. Sensus ergo erit, quod ita se gesserint, ac si cum morte fœdus percus- sissent, ac cum inferno pactum fecissent, quodq; non nisi in mendaciis spem & præsidium suum collocarint. Af- fectus & studia eorum, non quid obtenderint, spe- ctavit Propheta. Nonnulli per mendacium IDO- LA, quibus inserviêre Samaritani, intelligunt, imo etiam mortem & infernum nomina idolorum fa- ciunt. Sed hæc contorta & aliena sunt. Neque de Samaritanis, sed de Judæis hic sermo est. Simulasse vero Judæos tempore Ezechiæ religionem Assy- riorum nuspiam in Sacra Historia legitur: nedum quod in eo præsidium & fiduciam securitatis suæ collocarint.

## 28:14
SCORNFUL MEN WHO RULE OVER MY PEOPLE, WHO ARE IN JERUSALEM) He understands not the city properly, but the whole land, which was called the house of Jerusalem.

Latin:

VIRI ILLUSORES QUI DOMINAMINI SU- PER POPULUM MEUM, QUI EST IN JERUSA- LEM) Intelligit non urbem proprie, sed totam terram, quæ domus Jerusalem dicebatur.

## 28:15
Ver. 15. FOR YOU HAVE SAID WE HAVE MADE A COVENANT WITH DEATH) We will make, thus also the following are to be taken in the sense of the future; they hoped that by flattering they would find safety with Sennacherib. He calls the deadly enemy death.

WE HAVE MADE LIES OUR REFUGE) We pretended that we were of the same religion as the Assyrians are.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DIXISTI ENIM PERCUSSIMUS FEDUS CUM MORTE) Percutiemus, sic & sequentia sumenda in futuri significatu, sperabant se blandiendo salutē reperturos apud Sennacheribum. Mortem vocat hostem mortiferum.

POSUIMUS MENDACIUM SPEM NOSTRAM) Simulavimus nos esse ejusdem religionis, cujus sunt Assyrii.

## 28:16
Ver. 16. BEHOLD I WILL SEND IN THE FOUNDATIONS OF ZION) In the Hebrew: I will found in Zion.

A STONE, A TESTED STONE.) In the Hebrew: A corner of price: that is, a Stone, which makes a corner, of the greatest use, for walls lean most upon corner stones.

FOUNDED IN THE FOUNDATION:) In the Hebrew: a founded foundation: that is, most solid. By this translation, however, God signifies that if any wished to be saved, they must come to Jerusalem, so that there they might worship God purely with others: for there He had established Himself as the safest refuge for all.

HE WHO BELIEVES, SHALL NOT MAKE HASTE.) This is from the current Hebrew לא יחיש, but it appears that it was once לא יביש: For the LXX here have, οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ, as also Peter I. II. 6. But Paul to the Romans IX. 33, οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται. And this reading undoubtedly makes a better sense. He who believes, that is, he who, trusting in my promises, has not departed from the law. The Apostles very well refer these things to Christ in a more sublime sense.

Grotius wishes to force upon us again a double sense, preoccupied by the Papist hypothesis concerning the various senses of Scripture: the first literal: that a most safe refuge in Jerusalem, to which those who wish to be safe from the slaughter of Sennacherib might betake themselves, was established by God: the second mystical and more sublime: that Christ was placed by God as a cornerstone. But we have already refuted that Papist hypothesis above. And how can that double sense consist? For if by the name of a precious stone placed as a foundation a safe refuge in the city of Jerusalem is designated according to the letter, how can Christ Jesus be understood by the foundation and cornerstone in the same place? If anyone should say that a type of Christ was proposed there; we have warned more than once, that where any type is proposed, a double sense is by no means to be posited on that account. And by what evidence, I beseech you, is such a type exhibited or taught here, or elsewhere at least, that Jerusalem was a type of Christ in that it provided a refuge for the Jews betaking themselves there in the time of Sennacherib? Nor does the reasoning of the metaphor fit: for it is taken from a building, of which Christ is the foundation. What has that refuge to do with this? Finally, there is nothing in this whole chapter about Sennacherib. That the oracle, however, is to be accepted solely concerning Christ, we are led not only by the authority of the New Testament, in which it is explained, but it is also not obscure from the very words of the Prophet. Let us first look at the occasion of the same, the prediction concerning Christ fits perfectly: both so that the vain confidence of the people might be confounded, and the sole object of true trust might be exhibited, and so that for the sake of the faithful, a solid consolation might be set forth before the judgments which were to be promulgated against the Jews thereafter, by which they might be able to sustain themselves, and for the sake of the unfaithful, the cause might be indicated at the same time, on account of which they rendered themselves liable to those judgments, which is chiefly the neglect of the salvation which the Lord prepared in Zion. The wicked and secure, says our Brentius in explaining the continuity of the Prophetic text, hope that they will be safe from death and hell, and that we either become, or remain, the people of God. Hear therefore not my word, but the word of the Lord our God: Behold I, etc. The meaning of Isaiah, therefore, is this: The secure promise themselves the perpetuity of their external kingdom, and place their hope in vanity, thinking it impossible that, since they have a temple in Zion, they should be cast off, so as not to be the people of God, and be devoured by death and hell. But in truth, the matter is far otherwise. For God will found in Zion a cornerstone, which is Christ the only-begotten Son of God. He who shall stand firm in this stone by faith, he shall not tremble, he shall not flee, or as Peter and Paul interpret, he shall not be put to shame, he shall not be devoured by death and hell, but shall have with them eternal a covenant and agreement, so that they themselves can never do harm. But he who has not trusted in it, he must necessarily perish by death and hell. Now as to the individual words of the Prophet, Calvin, who not infrequently yields the palm to the Jews, rightly weighs their emphasis and has adapted each one to Christ alone: The demonstration BEHOLD makes for certainty; as if he had said: Although the impious despise my words and deny faith to them, yet I will perform that which I have promised: The pronoun I also is emphatic, so that the faith of the prophecy may stand certain. Nor does the Prophet without reason introduce God speaking, whose proper work it is to found the Church. For if all mortals were to devote their effort to this, they would not be able to erect even the smallest stone. Now from whom has Christ been given to us, if not from the Father? This, therefore, the heavenly Father has effected and performed, and has established Christ as our only foundation of salvation. But had not this stone been placed before? Has not the Church always been supported by this foundation? I certainly confess: But only by hope: because Christ had not yet been revealed, nor had he fulfilled the office of Redeemer. Therefore the Prophet speaks as if of a future thing: so that the faithful may be certainly persuaded that the Church, which they saw not only wavering and tottering, but gravely shaken and almost destroyed and dissolved into ruins, would nevertheless be stable with a new support, when it rests upon the Stone placed by the hand of God. He says, however, in Zion, because it was fitting that Christ should come forth from there; which contributes not a little to the confirmation of our Faith, since we see that he has come forth from that place which had been destined for that purpose so long before. Moreover, today Mount Zion is everywhere, since the Church has been propagated to the ends of the earth. This is Calvin, p. 222. Brentius observes not inappropriately that the Prophet used the name of a stone because the discourse was about the temple in Zion, which was constructed of stones: for in this the Jews trusted most. Cf. Jer. 7. They are therefore recalled here to a spiritual temple, to the Church, which is never to be overturned Matt. 16, 16. It is called a stone on account of its solidity: But a stone of probation, either because he himself was proved by God, because the foolish architects indeed rejected him Ps. 118. Acts 4. but God proved him: for he was tempted in all things as we are, but without sin Heb. 2. and 5. or because the stone is proved, to which others must be tested, thus B. Luther: I prefer to translate it as 'prover,' so that you may understand that Christ is such a stone, to whose form all others are tested, so that we also may be made conformable to his image through the cross; And Calvin: The usage of the Hebrew language demands that we interpret it rather actively: he calls him therefore a proving stone or a prover from the effect: since the whole building ought to be formed and adapted to this stone: and thus it will be necessary for it to slip and collapse. But Christ is truly a stone of probation, since the whole building must be erected toward him; nor can we be a structure of God unless we are fitted to him: Whence also Paul commands us to grow in him, who is the head, from whom the whole body must be joined and connected. He is called a corner stone, both because he is the fundamental and most firm stone of the whole building, containing and preserving all that in himself Eph. 3, 21. 1. Petr. 2, 4. chosen and honored by God 1. Petr. 2, 4. therefore he is called the head of the corner Ps. 118. and also from the office which he performs: because he connects two peoples, Jews and Gentiles, into one building of the Church Eph. 2, 14. Just as a certain corner stone, says Isidor. Pelusiota l. 1. c. 397. is found to be the bond of two walls, binding them to each other in a most tight and firm conjunction, in the same way the incarnation of our Lord, with the two peoples of the world coupled together and compacted into one body and one spirit, has been made the head of the corner, guarding a firm and not at all wavering conjunction by his interposition. Why would Jerusalem be called a corner stone, when it is established as a refuge for fugitive Jews, as Grotius wishes? The stone of which Isaiah speaks is called a stone of preciousness, or precious, because it is both most precious in itself, and brings great prices, great rewards to believers: therefore it is called chosen and honored by God, and by believers. 1. Petr. 2, 4. It is called a foundation of foundation, or as others prefer, a founded foundation מוסד, that is, most solid, (see similar places Ex. 12, 9. Ps. 64, 7.
