Prov. 30, 34.) or most firmly founded, which can be moved or overturned by no power, neither human nor angelic. As therefore such stones provide a firm foundation for a building Matt. 7, 24. So for the Church, none but Christ is a firm and immovable foundation, sustaining it against even the very gates of hell Matt. 16, 18. 1. Cor. 3, 11. And since otherwise in buildings the stone of the foundation and of the corner are distinct, if indeed stones of such magnitude are not had, which both complete the foundation and, placed in the corner, connect both walls: here, however, this stone is both in the place of the foundation and suffices to connect both peoples Eph. 2, 24. Bellarmine, Pref. Comment. in III. Tom. Controv., thinks that this eulogy can also be referred to the Roman Pontiff: because by him both Jews and Gentiles are contained as if by a corner stone: But not only the Pontiff, but also Angels and Archangels, and indeed all creatures are too weak to contain and sustain the whole body or building of the Church: and therefore this axiom must be left to Christ alone, outside of whom no other foundation can be laid 1. Cor. 3, 11. who alone is the immovable basis of our faith and justice, upon whom we may safely lean, upon whom alone the true citizens of the Church are built, as living stones 1. 1 Pet. 2:4. who are said to be built upon the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles, that is, upon Christ preached by the Prophets and Apostles, Eph. 2:20, Acts 10:43, John 15:27. Cf. Rev. 21:14. Whence Bellarmine himself valued this axiom so highly that he did not hesitate to draw from it an argument for the divinity of Christ, and an indissoluble one at that, namely that he is the cornerstone and foundation of the Church. To this is added that faith is required in this precious stone, placed in Zion. He who believes shall not make haste; therefore Peter says that he is precious, or τιμὴ, honor to those who believe, but to the unbelieving he is a stone of stumbling, 1 Ep. 2:7. He openly testifies that faith in this precious stone is required by Isaiah, ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ, he who believes in him, shall not be put to shame. For thus he explains the words of the Prophet. And why are those words added in the Prophet, where the stone placed by God is so prolixly described, he who believes shall not make haste, unless it be that by faith we may be built upon this precious and foundational stone, and that we may place our trust in him as the foundation of the spiritual building of the Church? For Christ is the base and foundation of faith and salvation, and therefore also of the faithful and those to be saved. The stone is most excellently and most firmly founded: it follows, therefore, that he who stands upon this stone, who has firm faith in Christ, does not tremble, nor is he put to shame, but has a covenant with death and hell, as Brentius rightly says here. To which must now also be added the parallel passages of the Old Testament, in which Christ is likewise called a stone, such as Dan. 2:34, cut out, which struck the statue and became a great mountain and filled the whole earth, which is explained concerning the kingdom of Christ in verses 44, 45, ch. 7:13, 14, and in Bereshith Rabba on Gen. 28. Then Zech. 3:9. A stone upon which are seven eyes, whose engraving the Lord has engraved, which words the Chaldean interpreter explained concerning the Messiah, Ps. 118:22, The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner: which passage is explained concerning Christ in Matt. 21:42, Acts 4:4, 1 Pet. 2:7, as also by R. Solomon on Micah 5:1. Finally, by this Prophet of ours he is called in ch. 8:14 a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense: which is likewise explained concerning Christ in Luke 2:34, Rom. 9:32. But especially luminous is the exegesis of our present prophecy, which the Holy Spirit delivered in the New Testament, Rom. Rom. Rom. 9:31 ff.: 'But Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not arrive at the law of righteousness. Why? Because it was not from faith, but as if from works: for they stumbled at the stone of stumbling and rock of offense: and everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.' And 1 Pet. 2:4: 'To whom, the Lord, coming as to a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen and honored by God; and you yourselves as living stones are built up, a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.' For which reason Scripture contains: 'Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, elect, precious, and he who believes in him will not be put to shame.' To you therefore is the honor who believe: but to those who do not believe, the stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner, and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense. It is most manifest from this declaration of both Apostles that this prophecy cannot be understood except of Christ alone, to whom the faithful are bound, so that they may place their trust in him: in that one alone is salvation to be sought, and therefore that one is the basis and foundation of faith and salvation. Nor is there need that we should judge the Hebrew text to be corrupted, since the LXX Interpreters often did not attend to the words, but to the sense, which, because it is excellently expressed here, the Apostle did not wish to depart from that version, which he for the most part retains: For those who are put to shame hasten elsewhere and take to flight, but those who are not put to shame have no need to hasten, or to flee to other remedies, or even to take to flight out of anxiety and trepidation of heart: just as those who follow another hasten (Ps. 16:4) and must necessarily fluctuate perpetually, being uncertain of their salvation, whence finally follows confusion. But those who believe in Christ have no need to flee or to be put to shame; indeed, since such a negation is sometimes taken among the Hebrews for the contrary affirmation, which figure they call meiosis or tapinosis, this sense is not inconveniently rendered: they shall not hasten, that is, they shall CONSIST, they shall STAND before God, for through faith in Christ we can stand before God. Whence Peter, when he rendered it with the LXX Interpreters HE SHALL NOT BE PUT TO SHAME, interprets by the contrary affirmation, HONOR, he says, shall be HIS: for to ignominy and confusion are opposed honor and glory; see similar examples in Isa. 42:3, Zech. 8:17. Elegantly, according to his custom, the Blessed Luther explains this. He describes, he says, in his enarrations on this passage, the virtue of faith by comparison with the ungodly; an evil conscience, such as is in the unbelieving, hastens, cannot stand, but at the least terrors and at the sound of a leaf it flees, and if it could break through a wall, it would do so. Just as the voice of the ungodly testifies, which Christ recites: 'Mountains cover us,' etc. But he who leans on this stone does not hasten, does not tremble, does not flee, but stands. For he knows that Christ is the Lord of death, and of life, and of sin, etc. This is the virtue of faith, which leans on Christ, not on us; therefore it does not fail us, but saves us in all dangers. And in the marginal notes to the German translation: 'He who believes, does not flee: An evil conscience would indeed fly through an iron mountain, if it were possible, so dreadfully does it tremble, and fears itself, as often as a need meets it, but a believing heart stands secure, and mocks even the gates of hell.' I add also Calvin's explanation: 'To this tends the Prophet, that the mind of those who will believe will be peaceful and tranquil, so that they desire nothing more, nor wander uncertain, nor hasten to seek other remedies, but are most fully content with that one alone.' But the translation is not harsh, since by the word HASTENING is denoted fervor or trepidation. Finally, the Prophet's purpose is to praise faith for this incomparable fruit, since in it we have a peaceful and quiet station. Whence it follows that we must necessarily be assiduously anxious and of an unquiet mind before we are endowed with it. For there is one harbor in which it is permitted to rest safely: namely, the truth of the Lord, which alone will render us peaceful and tranquil. And this fruit of faith the same Paul describes elsewhere, when he says that we, being justified by faith, obtain peace with God. The gloss of the Papists: 'He who believes, let him not hasten,' i.e., wishing this stone of Zion to be exhibited to him immediately, which, although it pleased Tirinus and Menochius after Pagninus and Cornelius, is too inept. Nor indeed did only the Apostles understand this of Christ, and with them all Christian Interpreters: But it is interpreted also from the Jews themselves by R. [Rabbi] the text. R. Solomon on this passage: 'I have founded,' is a past verb, and it is to be explained concerning the past thus: 'And I am he who have already founded in Zion a stone': that is, it is already defined, it is decreed before me, and I have constituted King Messiah, who is the stone BOHAN, which sounds strength or fortification. But what is said, the foundation of the foundation, that is, of foundations, ought to be understood as if it were said the most perfect foundation. Nor is the perversion of that word to be passed over at all, HE WHO SHALL BELIEVE, which Grotius wishes to be he who, trusting in the promises, has not departed from the law. For these are as far apart as heaven and earth: namely, faith and obedience rendered to the law, just as Law and Gospel are separated by a very great interval, especially in the state of Justification, by which a man ought to stand before God. Nor did either Apostle explain this by obedience, but by faith in Christ; indeed, from that passage Paul established the righteousness of faith against the righteousness of works, namely, that we are justified by faith in Christ alone, not from the works of the law, Rom. 10. Let there be added to these finally the confession of Grotius himself on Luke 24:47, that it was predicted here that Jerusalem would be the beginning of the Evangelical proclamation in the time of the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ECCE EGO MITTAM IN FUNDA- MENTIS SION In Hebræo: Fundabo in Sion.

LAPIDEM, LAPIDEM PROBATUM.) In He- bræo: Angulum pretii: id est Lapidem, qui angulum faciat, usus maximi, nam angularibus lapidibus maxime innitun- tur parietes.

IN FUNDAMENTO FUNDATUM:) In Hebræo: fundamentum fundatum: id est, solidissimum. Hac autem translatione significat Deus, si qui salvi esse vellent, illis ve- niendum Hierosolyma, ut ibi cum aliis pure Deum colant: ibi enim se perfugium tutissimum constituisse omnibus.

QUI CREDIDERIT, NON FESTINET.) Est hoc ex hodierno Hebræo לא יחיש, sed apparet olim fuisse לא יביש: Nam LXX. hic habent, ὀὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ, quomodo & Petrus I. II. 6. Paulus vero ad Romanos IX. 33. ὀὐ καταισχυνθήσεται. Et hæc lectio haud dubie melio- rem sensum facit. Qui crediderit, id est, qui meis promissis fisus à lege non discesserit. Optime vero hæc ad Christum in sensu sublimiore referunt Apostoli.

Iterum geminum sensum nobis obtrudere vult Grotius, Papistica hypothesi de variis Scripturæ sensibus præoccupatus: primum literalem: Hie- rosolymis refugium tutissimum, ad quod se recipi- ant, qui à clade Sennacheribi salvi esse velint, à Deo constitutum esse: Alterum mysticum & sublimio- rem: Christum positum esse a Deo in lapidem angula- rem. Sed Papisticam illam hypothesin profligavi- mus jam superius. Et quomodo sensus ille geminus consistere potest? Si enim lapidis pretiosi in fun- damentum positi nomine secundum literam perfu- gium tutum in civitate Jerusalem designatur, quo- modo per fundamentum & lapidem angulare eo- dem loco Christus Jesus intelligi potest? Si quis di- cat, typum illic Christi propositum fuisse; monui- mus non semel, Ubi typus aliquis proponitur, ne- quaquam geminum ideo sensum ponendum esse. Et quonam obsecro indicio vel hic, vel alibi saltim hujusmodi typus exhibetur, aut docetur, Hieroso- lymam in eo fuisse typum Christi, quod præbuerit perfugium Judæis eo se recipientibus Sennacheri- bi tempore? Neq; congruit ratio metaphoræ: Ea enim ab ædificio petita est: cujus fundamentum sit Christus. Quid huc facit illud perfugium? Deni- que nihil in toto hoc capite de Sennacheribo. Quod autem oraculum unice de Christo accipiendum sit, non solum autoritate N. Testamenti, in quo id ex- plicatur, inducimur, sed etiam è verbis ipsis Pro- phetæ haud obscurum est. Occasionem primum ejusdem sit respiciamus, congruit optime prædictio de Christo: tum ut vana confidentia populi confu- sa, veræ fiduciæ objectum unicum exhiberetur, tum ut judiciis, quæ adversus Judæos deinceps pro- mulganda erant, fidelium causa præmitteretur con- solatio solida, qua sese sustentare queant, infidelium vero gratia simul causa indicaretur, ob quam judi- ciis illis reddiderint se obnoxios, quæ præcipue ne- glectus est salutis, quam paravit in Zion Dominus. Impii & securi, inquit Brentius noster in explican- da συνεχείᾳ textus Prophetici, sperant se tutos fore à morte & inferno, & aut fiamus, aut maneamus po- pulus Dei. Audi igitur non meum, sed Domini Dei nostri verbum: Ecce Ego &c. Sententia igitur E- saiæ hęc est: Securi pollicentur sibi externi regni sui perpetuitatem, & collocant spem suam in vanitate, existimantes impossibile esse, ut cum habeant tem- plum in Sion, abjiciantur, ne sint populus Dei, & de- vorentur à morte atq; inferno. At vero res longe aliter se habet. Deus enim fundabit in Zion lapi- dem angularem, qui est Christus unigenitus DEI filius. Qui in hoc lapide fide constiterit, is non tre- pidabit, non fugiet, seu ut Petrus & Paulus inter- pretantur, non pudefiet, non devorabitur à mor- te & inferno, sed habebit cum eis sempiternum fœdus & pactum, ut nunquam possint ipsi nocere. Qui autem eo non fuerit confisus, is necesse habet morte & inferno perire. Jam quod ad verba sin- gula Prophetæ, recte Calvinus, qui non raro alias Judæis herbam porrigit, emphasin eorum expen- dit, ac singula uni Christo aptavit: Demonstratio ECCE ad certitudinem facit; ac si dixisset; Tamet- si verba mea despiciant impii, fidemq; illis derogent, tamen id quod pollicitus sum, præstabo: Pronomen etiam EGO emphaticum est, ut vaticinio certa constet fides. Nec abs re Propheta Deum loquen- tem inducit, cujus proprium opus est fundare Ec- clesiam. Nam si omnes mortales operam suam eo conferant, non poterunt vel minimum lapidem e- rigere. Nunc à quo nobis datus est Christus, nisi à Patre? Hæc igitur effecit ac præstitit cœlestis Pa- ter, atq; Christum nobis unicum salutis fundamen- tum statuit. Sed annon prius positus erat hic lapis? Nonne hoc fundamento semper subnixa fuit Ec- clesia? Fateor certe: Sed spe tantum: quia Chri- stus nondum patefactus erat, neq; expleverat offi- cium Redemptoris. Ideo Propheta quasi de re fu- tura loquitur: ut certo persuasi sint fideles, Eccle- siam,quam videbant non modo nutare & labascere, sed graviter concussam & fere dirutam dissolvi in ruinas, nova tamen fultura stabilem fore, ubi in Lapidem manu Dei positum recumbet. Dicit au- tem in Sion,quia illinc Christum prodire oportuit; quod non parum facit ad Fidei nostræ confirmationē, cum ex eo loco,qui tanto prius tempore ad id de- stinatus erat, videmus ipsum prodiisse. Cæterum hodie ubiq; est mons Sion,quum in fines orbis ter- rarum propagata sit Ecclesia. Hæc Calvinus p. 222. Lapidis nomine ideo usum esse Prophetam non in- commode observat Brentius, quia sermo erat de templo in Zion, quod ex lapidibus constructum erat: in hoc enim confidebant maxime Judæi.Conf. Jer. 7. Revocantur ergo hic ad spirituale templum, ad Ecclesiam, quæ nunquam evertenda Matth.16, 16. Lapis dicitur ob soliditatem: Lapis vero proba- tionis,vel quod probatus ipse sit à Deo,quia archi- tecti stolidi reprobarunt quidem ipsum Ps.118. Act. 4. sed Deus probavit eum: tentatus enim est per omnia sicut nos, sed absq; peccato Ebr. 2. & 5. vel quod lapis sit probatus, ad quem alii exigendi sint, sic B. Lutherus: Ego malo vertere, probatorem, ut intelligas, Christum talem lapidem esse, ad cujus for- mam omnes alii probentur, ut nos quoque per crucem conformes fiamus imagine ejus; Et Calvinus: Usus linguæ Hebraicæ id postulat, ut potius active inter- pretemur: lapidem igitur probantem vel probatorem vocat ab effectu: quoniam ad hunc lapidem totum æ- dificium formari & aptari debet: adeog; labi ipsum & corruere necessum erit. Est autem Christus ve- re lapis probationis, quoniam totum ædificium ad ipsum erigi necesse est; nec possumus structuraDei esse, nisi illi coaptemur: Unde & Paulus crescere nos jubet in eo,qui caput est,ex quo totum corpus conjungi ac connecti oportet. Vocatur lapis angu- laris, tum quod sit fundamentalis & firmissimus to- tius ædificii lapis, totum illud in se continens & conservans Eph.3, 21. 1. Petr. 2, 4. à Deo electus & honoratus 1. Petr. 2, 4. ideo dicitur caput anguli Ps. 118. tum ab officio, quo fungitur: quia duos populos connectit, Judæos & gentiles, in unum ædificium Ecclesiæ Eph. 2, 14. Quemadmodum angularis quidā lapis, inquit Isidor.Pelusiota l.1.c.397. duorum parie- tum vinculum esse invenitur,ad arctissimam & firmissi- mam conjunctionē eos inter se devinciens, eodem modo Domini nostri incarnatio duobus orbis populis inter se copulatis,atq; in unum corpus atq; unum spiritum com- pactis, in caput anguli effecta est, firmam ac minime nutantem conjunctionem interpositu suo custodiens. Cur diceretur Hierosolyma lapis angularis, cum pro- fugium constituatur profugis Judæis, uti vult Gro- tius? Lapis de quo Esaias, vocatur lapis pretiositatis, vel pretiosus, quia & in se pretiosissimus est, & ma- gna affert pretia, magna præmia credentibus: ideo electus & honoratus dicitur à Deo, & credentibus. 1. Petr. 2, 4. Dicitur fundamentum fundationis, vel ut alii malunt, fundamentum מוסד fundatum, id est, solidissimum, (vid. similia loca Ex. 12, 9. Ps. 64, 7. Prov. 30, 34.) vel fundatissimum, quod nulla nec hu- mana nec angelica potentia moveri aut everti pos- sit. Ut ergo lapides tales firmum ædificio præbent fundamentum Matth. 7, 24. Sic Ecclesiæ non nisi Christus firmum atq; immotum fundamentum est, sustentans eam adversus ipsas etiam inferorum por tas Matth. 16, 18. 1. Cor. 3, 11. Et quum alias in ædi- ficiis lapis fundamenti, & anguli distincti sint, siqui- dem tantæ magnitudinis lapides non habeantur, qui & fundamentum compleant, & in angulo positi utrumque murum connectant: hic tamen lapis & fundamenti loco est, & ad connectendum utrumq; populum sufficit Ephes. 2, 24. Bellarminus Præf. Comment. in III. Tom. Controv. hoc elogium ad Romanum Pontificem referri etiam posse putat: quod ab eodem & Judæi & gentes q. à lapide angula- ri contineantur: Sed non Pontifex tantum, verum etiam Angeli & Archangeli, omnesq; adeo creatu- ræ nimis infirmæ sunt ad continendum, & susten- tandum totum Ecclesiæ corpus, vel ædificium: ideo- que soli Christo hoc axioma relinquendum, extra quem aliud fundamentum poni nullum potest 1. Cor. 3, 11. qui solus est fidei ac justitiæ nostræ basis immota, cui tuto innitamur, cui soli fuperstruun- tur veri Ecclesiæ civis, ceu vivi lapides 1. Petr. 2, 4. qui super fundamentum Prophetarum & Apostolo- rum ideo extructi dicuntur, id est, super Christum à Prophetis & Apostolis prædicatum Ephes. 2, 20. Act. 10, 43. Johann. 15, 27. Conf. Apoc. 21, 14. Unde ipse Bellarminus hoc axioma tanti fecit, ut non du- bitarit inde pro divinitate Christi argumentum, id- que indissolubile depromere, quod nempe lapis angularis & fundamentum sit Ecclesiæ. His acce- dit, quod fides requiratur in hunc lapidem pretio- sum, in Zion positum. Qui credit, non festinat; ideo Petrus dicit, quod pretiosus, vel τιμὴ, honor sit cre- dentibus, incredulis autem lapis sit offensionis 1. Ep. 2, 7. idem fidem in hunc lapidem pretiosum ab Esaia requiri aperte testatur, ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ qui cre- dit in ipso, non confundetur. Sic enim explicat verba Prophetæ. Et cur adduntur illa apud Prophetam, ubi tam prolixe lapis à Deo positus descriptus est, qui credit, non festinat, nisi ut fide huic lapidi pre- tioso & fundamentali inædificemur, utq; fiduciam in ipsum tanquam fundamentum ædificii spiritua- lis Ecclesiæ collocemus? Christus enim est fidei & salutis, adeoq; etiam fidelium & salvandorum basis ac fundamentum. Lapis est optime, & firmissime fundatus: sequitur ergo, ut qui hoc lapide confi- stit, qui firmam fidem in Christum habet, non tre- pidet, nec pude fiat, sed habeat pactum cum morte & inferno, uti recte hic Brentius. Quibus addenda nunc etiam loca parallela Veteris Testamenti, qui- bus Christus itidem lapis dicitur, utpote Dan. 2, 34. abscissus, qui percussit statuam, & factus est mons magnus & implevit universam terram, quod de Christi regno explicatur vers. 44. 45. cap. 7, 13. 14. & in Bereschith Rabba ad Gen. 28. Tum Zach. 3, 9. Lapis super quo septem oculi, cujus sculpturam scul- psit Dominus, quæ verba de Messia exposuit inter- pres Chaldæus Ps. 118, 14. Lapis, quem reprobave- runt ædificantes, factus fuit in caput anguli: qui lo- cus de Christo exponitur Matth. 21, 42. Act. 4, 4. 1. Petr. 2, 7. ut & à R. Salomone ad Mich. 5, 1. Deniq; ab hoc Propheta nostro vocatur c. 8, 14. lapis offen- sionis & petra scandali: quod de Christo itidem ex- plicatur Luc. 2, 34. Rom. 9, 32. Sed imprimis lucu- lenta est præsentis nostri vaticinii ἐξήγησις, quam in Nov. Testamento tradidit S. S. Rom. 9, 31. seq. I- srael vero sectando legem justitiæ, in legem justitiæ non pervenit. Quare? quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex ope- ribus: offenderunt enim in lapidem offensionis & pe- tram scandali: & omnis qui credit in eum, non con- fundetur. Et 1. Petr. 2, 4. Ad quem, Dominum, acce- dentes lapidem vivum, ab hominibus quidem repro- batum, à Deo autem electum & honorificatum; & ipsi tanquam lapides vivi superædificamini, domus spiritualis, sacerdotium sanctum, offerre spiritua- les hostias acceptabiles Deo per Jesum Christum. Pro- pter quod continet Scriptura: ecce pono in Sion lapi- dem summum, angularem, electum, pretiosum, & qui crediderit in eum non confundetur. Vobis igitur ho- nor credentibus: non credentibus autem lapis, quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput an- guli, & lapis offensionis & petra scandali. Mani- festissimum est ex hac Apostoli utriusque declara- tione, non posse vaticinium hoc nisi de solo Chri- sto intelligi, cui alligantur fideles, ut in eum fidu- ciam collocent: in uno illo salus est quærenda, ide- oque unus ille basis & fundamentum est fidei, & sa- lutis. Neque opus est, ut textum Ebræum corru- ptum censeamus, quum LXX. Interpp. sæpe non verba attenderint, sed sensum, qui quia hic egregie expressus est, noluit Apostolus ab illa versione, quā plerumque retinet, discedere: Nam qui confundun- tur, festinant alio, & fugam capessunt, qui vero non confunduntur, festinare opus non habent, vel ad alia remedia confugere, vel etiam ex anxietate & trepidatione cordis fugam arripere: sicut qui alie- num sequuntur, festinant Ps. 16, 4. & perpetuo flu- ectuare necessum habent, utpote de salute SUA in- certi, unde tandem sequitur confusio. At qui in Christum credunt, non opus habent fugere, aut pudefieri, imo quum talis negatio pro contraria af- firmatione quandoque apud Ebræos accipiatur, quam figuram μείωσιν aut ταπείνωσιν vocant, non incommode sensus hic redditur, non festinant, id est, CONSISTENT, STABUNT coram Deo, per fidem enim in Christum coram Deo consistere pos- sumus. Unde Petrus, cum reddidit cum LXX. In- terpp. NON PUDEFIET, interpretatur per contrariam affirmationem, HONOR, ait, erit EI: nam ignominiæ & confusioni opponitur honor & gloria; vid. similia exempla Ef. 42, 3. Zach. 8, 17. E- leganter, pro more suo, explicat hoc B. Lutherus. Describit, inquit Enarrat in h. l. fidei virtutem, col- latione impiorum; mala conscientia, qualis in incre- dulis est, festinat, non potest consistere, sed ad minimos terrores, & ad sonitum folii fugit, & si murum per- rumpere posset, faceret. Sicut testatur vox impiorum, quam Christus recitat: Montes operite nos &c. Qui autem in hoc lapide nititur, non festinat, non trepidat, non fugit, sed consistit. Novit enim, Christum esse Dominum mortis, & vitæ, & peccati &c. Hæc fidei virtus est, quæ in Christo nititur, non in nobis, ideo non fallit nos, sed servat nos in omnibus periculis. Et in marginalib. ad Germ. translationem: Wer gläu= bet, der fleuget nicht: Ein böses Gewissen flöge wol durch einen eisern Berg, wo es müglich wäre, so greulich erschrickt es, und fürchtet sich, so offt ihm ei= ne noth begegnet, aber ein gläubig Hertz stehet si= cher, und spottet auch der Höllen Pforten. Addo & Calvini explicationem: Huc tendit Propheta, eorum qui credent, pacatum & tranquillum animum fore, ut nihil amplius desiderent, nec vagentur incerti, nec pro- hibe- perent ad alia remedia quærenda, sed eo unico plenissi- me sint contenti. Dura autem non est translatio, quum verbo FESTINANDI notatur fervor, aut trepidatio. Denig, Prophetæ consilium est laudare fidem ab hoc incomparabili fructu, quoniam in ea nobis placida sit & quieta statio. Unde sequitur, nos assidue angi & in- quieto animo esse oportere, priusquam ea præditi si- mus. Unus enim est portus, in quo tuto acquiescere liceat: nempe veritas Domini, quæ sola nos pacatos & tranquillos reddet. Atg, hunc fidei fructum descri- bit alibi idem Paulus, dum nos fide justificatos, pacem apud Deum obtinere dicit. Pontificiorum glossa: Qui crediderit, non festinet, sc. volens statim lapide hunc Zionis sibi exhiberi, quæ etsi post Pagninum & Cornelium, Tirino & Menochio placuerit, nimis ine- pta est. Nec vero Apostoli tantum de Christo intel- lexêre, & cum iis Christiani Interpp. universi: Sed è Iudæis ipsis quoq; interpretatur R' τὸ ῥητὸν. R. Sa- lomo in h. l. Fundavi, verbum præteritum est, atg, de præterito exponendum est sic: Et ego sum, qui fundavi jam in Zion lapidem: id est, jam definitum est, decretum est coram me, & constitui Regem Messiam, qui est lapis בחן, quod sonat fortitudinem, vel munitiem. Quod autem dicitur, fundamentum fundamenti, id est, fundamentorum, sic intelligi debet, ac si dicatur fundamentum perfectissimum. Neq; prætereunda est omnino perversio verbi illius, Qui CREDIDE- RIT, quod Grotius esse vult, qui promissis fisus, à le- ge non discesserit. Nam hæc toto cœlo distant: fides nempe & obedientia legi præstita, uti Lex & Evange- lium maximo intervallo à se invicem distant, cum- primis in statu Justificationis, qua homo coram Deo consistere debet. Neq; per obedientiam, sed per fidem in Christum hæc exposuit uterq; Apo- stolus, imo ex eo loco Paulus justitiam fidei, adver- sus operum justitiam adstruxit, sola nempe fide in Christum, non ex operibus legis nos justificari, Rom. 10. Accedat his deniq; ipsius Grotii confes- sio ad Luc. 24, 47. quod hic prædictum fuerit Hie- rosolymis initium futurum præconii Evangelici tempore N. Test.

## 28:17
V. 17. AND I WILL SET JUDGMENT BY THE PLUMMET, AND JUSTICE BY THE MEASURE.) In the Hebrew: Judgment a line, and justice to the weight. Similar 2 Kings 21:13. The sense is: in judging I will deflect nothing from my law, and the promises, and the threats added to it.

Some interpreters among our own, B. Brentius, also refer these things to the preceding promise concerning the Messiah: He explains, he says on p. 363, what will happen at that time when the cornerstone is placed in the foundations of Zion, that is, when Christ will come into this world and receive his kingdom. I will set, he says, judgment by the weight. When Christ has come and reigned, then judgment and justice will be most straight and most equitable on earth. No one will suffer injury any longer: But all things will be administered by the best law. The wicked will suffer punishment according to their deserts. The good will enjoy every happiness. In short, the weight will be equitable, the measure of all things in the kingdom of Christ will be equitable. This promise concerning the kingdom of Christ will be customary among the people of Israel. The seventy-first Psalm says: Give thy judgment, O God, to the king, and thy justice to the king's son. To judge thy people in justice, and thy poor in judgment. The Psalm speaks, however, of Christ and his kingdom. In Isaiah nine: upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom he shall sit, to confirm and corroborate it in judgment and justice from henceforth and even forever. Jeremiah twenty-three: A King shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. Which Brentius has carried out at greater length there. Nor is the mind of B. Luther any different. Having threatened here, he says, the impious who reject this stone: I will judge, but with measure, I will not destroy the impious with the holy, without distinction. The measure and rule of my judgment will be that stone, Christ in whom those who do not believe, them I will destroy, the rest I will save; here the righteousness of faith alone subsists and is preserved: Therefore also what is subjoined, AND IT SHALL SUBVERT THE HAIL OF THE LIE, Brentius explains concerning the Jews, who rejected Christ, and rejected that precious stone: that they are to be rejected, and very few of them are to be saved. You hope now that you will be the people of God forever, and will always dwell in this region, even if you commit the most impious crimes: but I say to you, when CHRIST shall have arrived, this most vain hope of yours will be subverted as if by hail, and the asylum in which you now trust will be overwhelmed as if by an inundation of water. Similarly also your covenant, which you say you have struck with death, will be abrogated, and the scourge, of which you were saying before, will trample you: the overflowing scourge, when it shall have passed through, shall not come upon us. This hope will put you to shame, because nothing is more certain than that the scourge, when it has come, will snatch you away and oppress you. For although it seems that much time still remains before Christ is to come, and you are to be cast out from the inheritance of heavenly goods, yet do not flatter yourselves; this calamity will come at the very dawn, or soon enough, and will last day and night, that is, for perpetual times. Other calamities, which have happened to you hitherto, and will still happen, have their end until the coming of CHRIST. But this calamity, by which after the coming of Christ you will be cast out from the people of God, will have no end ever. Which, although it is diligently predicted to you as much before by Moses as afterwards by other Prophets, and also by me, yet you mock us, you think we speak vain lies. Therefore only vexation will give understanding to the hearing, that is, you do not believe our prophecies concerning your rejection, until you feel it in reality, and the calamity itself teaches that our preaching is most true. For it will come to pass that, even if in these times you seem to be like the stars of the heaven and the sand of the sea, so that one region cannot contain you, yet at that time, when Christ shall arrive, so few of you will truly remain the people of God, that a very narrow bed will be able to contain you: The bed is narrowed, so that one falls out: and the cloak or short covering cannot cover both, that is, very few of the Jews were chosen. For this saying, about the bed and its covering, has a proverbial appearance, and signifies that when the Jews previously filled whole regions, now so few will truly be the people of God, that they will be able to rest in a narrow bed, which could scarcely contain one. But what follows concerning the valley, which is in Gibeon, interpreters think is said about that history which is written in Josh. 10, when the Sun stood still for the space of one day in the midst of the heaven. Which opinion is not to be despised. But because there is mention here of that history which is written about the victory which David reported over the Philistines on Mount Perazim, which they interpret as Divisions, 2 Sam. 5 and 1 Chron. 14, it seems to me that Isaiah, when he speaks of the valley of Gibeon, looks more to that second victory of David, which he reported over the Philistines, in the valley of Gibeon, and which immediately followed that former one, as Scripture clearly hands down in that place. For the Philistines, when they had heard that David had been elected and anointed King by the Israelites, undertook war against him, so that they might oppress him immediately at the beginning of his reign, before his forces were increased, and his kingdom was confirmed. For they feared that if David's kingdom should advance, they would have to perish: Wherefore they decided to withstand the beginnings and to abolish David's kingdom, while it still seemed weak. But David by divine power twice so conquered, put to flight, and dispersed them, that they even left their idols behind them. Whence also the place was called Perazim, that is, dispersions, because there the enemies of David had been dispersed. And in the later victory, Scripture says that David struck the enemies from Gibeon even to Gezer. This therefore is the meaning of Isaiah. Just as David so wonderfully routed and put to flight the Philistines, who were standing in the way so that he might not reign in Israel, twice, once on Mount Perazim, and again in the valley of Gibeon, that they flowed away and slipped away like waters: so Christ will put to flight, and cast out the impious Jews, who will try with all their strength to prevent him from advancing his kingdom. Thus Brentius.

AND THE HAIL SHALL SUBVERT THE HOPE OF THE LIE, AND THE WATERS SHALL OVERFLOW THE PROTECTION.) Those storms sent divinely will overturn that hope of protection, which you had placed in a lie.

Latin:

V. 17. ET PONAM IN PONDERE JUDICIUM, ET JVSTITIAM IN MENSVRA.) In Hebræo: Iudicium li- nea, & justitiam ad pondus. Simile 2. Reg. 21, 13. Sensus est: in judicando nihil deflectam à lege mea, & promissis, minisque ei additis.

Hæc etiam ad promissionem de Messia præ- cedentem referunt nonnulli Interpp. è nostris B. Brentius: Exponit, inquit p. 363. quid futurum sit eo tempore, quo lapis angularis ponetur in funda- mentis Zion, hoc est, quo veniet Christus in hunc mundum, & accipiet regnum suum. Ponam, inquit, judicium in pondere. Cum venerit Christus, & re- gnaverit, tunc judicium & justitia in terris erunt re- ctissima, & æquissima. Nulli fiet amplius injuria: Sed omnia administrabuntur optimo jure. Mali pro meritis pœnam sustinebunt. Boni fruentur omni felicitate. Breviter, æquum erit pondus, æqua mensura omnium rerum in regno Christi. Hæc promissio de regno Christi usitata erit in populo Israël. Psalmus septuagesimus primus dicit: Deus judicium tuum regi da, & justitiam tuam filio Regis. Ad judicandum populum tuum in justitia, & paupe- res tuos in judicio. Loquitur autem Psalmus de Chri- sto & regno ejus. Esaiæ nono: super solium David & super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet & corro- boret illud in Judicio & justitia à modo & usq; in sempiternum. Jerem. vigesimo tertio: Regnabit Rex, & sapiens erit, & faciet judicium, & justitiam in terra. Quæ ibi prolixius exequutus est Brentius. Neq; alia est mens B. Luthero. Hic comminatus, in- quit, impiis, qui hunc lapidem reprobant: Iudicabo, sed cum mensura, non perdam impium cum sancto, sine di- scrimine Mesura & regula erit judicii mei lapis ille Chri- stus, in quem qui non credunt, eos perdam, reliquos ser- vabo; hic sola fidei justitia subsistit & servatur: Ideo etiam quæ subjunguntur, ET SUBVERTIT GRANDEM MENDACII, de Judæis ex- plicat Brentius, qui Christum abjecerunt, & la- pidem illum pretiosum reprobarunt: quod abjicien- di, & paucissimi ex iis servandi sint. Speratis nunc vos perpetuo fore populum Dei, & semper in hac re- gione habitaturos, etiamsi impiissima quæq́; scelera designetis: at ego dico vobis, cum advenerit CHRI- STUS, hæc vestra spes vanissima, quasi grandine sub- vertetur, & asylum, quo nunc confiditis, quasi inun- datione aquæ obruetur. Similiter & fœdus vestrum, quod dicitis vos cum morte percussisse, abrogabitur, & conculcabit vos flagellum, de quo ante dicebatis: fla- gellum inundans, cum transierit, non veniet su- per nos. Hæc spes pudefaciet vos, quia nihil certius est, quam quod flagellum, cum venerit, abripiat & opprimat vos. Etsi enim videtur adhuc multum temporis superesse, quo venturus est Christus, & vos ex hæreditate cælestium bonorum ejiciemini, tamen nolite vobis blandiri, hæc calamitas summo diluculo, seu sat cito veniet, ac durabit die ac nocte, hoc est, perpetuis temporibus. Aliæ calamitates, quæ vobis hactenus acciderunt, & adhuc accident, usq́; ad ad- ventum CHRISTI suum habent finem. Hæc au- tem calamitas, quæ post adventum Christi ejiciemini extra populum Dei, nullum unquam finem habitu- ra est. Quod etsi vobis tam antea à Mose, quam postea ab aliis Prophetis, ac à me quoq́; diligenter præ- dicitur, tamen vos irridetis nos, existimatis nos vana mendacia loqui. Itaq́; tantummodo vexatio dabit intellectum auditui, hoc est, non creditis nostris vati- ciniis de abjectione vestri, donec eam reipsa sentiatis, & calamitas ipsa doceat concionem nostram esse ve- rissimam. Futurum enim est, ut etiamsi his tempo- ribus videamini esse sicut stellæ cæli & arena maris, ita ut una regio non possit vos capere, tamen eo tempo- re, quo Christus adveniet, tam pauci ex vobis remane- bunt vere populus Dei, ut lectus admodum angustus vos capere queat: Coangustatum est stratum, ita ut alter decidat: & pallium seu operimentum breve utrumque operire non potest, hoc est, paucissimi ex Judæis erant electi. Hoc enim dictum, de lecto & operimento ejus, habet faciem proverbialem, & significat, quod cum Judæi antea impleverint totas regiones, nunc tam pauci erunt vere populus Dei, ut in angusto lecto, qui vix unum capiat, requiesce- re possint. Quod autem sequitur de valle, quæ est in Gibeon, existimant interpretes dici de ea historia, quæ scripta est Jos. 10. cum stetit Sol spatio unius diei in medio cæli. Quæ sententia non est aspernanda. Sed quia sit hic mentio ejus historiæ, quæ scripta est de victoria, quam David reportavit à Philistinis in monte Parizim, quod interpretantur, Divisionum 2. Reg. 5. & 1. Paralip. 14. videtur mihi Esaias, cum de valle Gibeon loquitur, magis respicere in secun- dam illam victoriam Davidis, quam reportavit à Philistinis, in valle Gibeon, & quæ statim illam prio- rem secuta est, ut Scriptura eo loco perspicue tra- dit. Philistini enim, cum audissent, Davidem ab Israëlitis in Regem electum & unctū, suscipiebant bellum adversus eum, ut statim initio regni oppri- merent eum, priusquam vires ejus augerentur, & regnum ejus confirmaretur. Metuebant enim, ne si regnum Davidis promoveret, pereundū ipsis esset: Quare statuerunt principiis obstare & regnū Davidis, cum adhuc infirmum videretur, abolere. David autem divina potentia bis eos ita vicit, fu- gavit, & dispersit, ut etiam idola sua post se relin- querent. Unde & locus dictus est Parizim, hoc est, dispersiones, quod ibi dispersi essent hostes Da- vidis. Et in posteriori victoria, dicit Scriptura, Davidem percussisse hostes de Gibeon usque ad Gazera. Haec igitur est sententia Esaiae. Quem- admodum David Philistinos, qui obstabant, ne re- gnaret in Israel, bis, semel in monte Parizim, & ite- rum in valle Gibeon, ita mirabiliter fudit & fuga- vit, ut velut aquae diffluerent ac dilaberentur: ita Christus fugabit, & abjiciet impios Judaeos, qui to- tis viribus suis impedire conabuntur, ne regnum suum promoveat. Haec Brentius.

ET SUBVERTET GRANDO SPEM MENDA- CII, ET PROTECTIONEM AQUAE INVNDABVNT.) Spem illam protectionis, quam in mendacio positam habe- batis, evertent procellae divinitus immissae.

## 28:19
Vers. 19.

WHENEVER IT SHALL PASS THROUGH, IT SHALL TAKE YOU AWAY.) Because he had named this evil scourge as passing through, he shows that in the greatest haste there will be enough time for their destruction.

FOR IN THE MORNING AT DAWN IT SHALL PASS THROUGH.) Morning, morning, in the Hebrew: very early it will begin to pass through.

BY DAY AND BY NIGHT.) It will continue day and night in its passing. See above 10, 28.

AND ONLY VEXATION SHALL GIVE UNDERSTANDING TO THE HEARING.) In the Hebrew: And it shall be for the sufferer to understand the report: i.e., of those things which will happen to you.

There is no reason why the Vulgate should be corrected here, which agrees well with the Hebrew text: AND IT SHALL BE ONLY VEXATION (וְהָיָה רְוָחָה) TO UNDERSTAND THE HEARING, i.e., the word of the hearing: which is heard from God, from the Prophets, and ought to be heard, when it is announced to men from the mouth of God, Is. 53, 1. Rightly therefore the blessed Luther, 'for only vexation teaches one to pay attention to the Word.' Conf. his marginal gloss. Nor is Calvin alien to this sense: 'Only terror shall make one understand. It will happen that terror alone will make you capable of doctrine.'

Latin:

Vers. 19.

QVANDOCVNQVE TRANSIERIT, TOLLET VOS) Quia nominaverat hoc malum flagellum transi- ens, ostendit in summa festinatione satis fore temporis ad illorum perniciem.

QVONIAM MANE DILVCVLO TRANSIBIT) Mane, mane, in Hebraeo: valde mane incipiet transire.

IN DIE ET NOCTE) Diem & noctem continua- bit in transitu. Vide supra 10, 28.

ET TANTVMMODO SOLA VEXATIO IN- TELLECTVM DABIT AVDITVS.) In Hebraeo: Et pa- ssori erit vel famam intelligere: eorum sc. quae vobis obve- nient.

Non est, quod hic corrigatur Vulgata, cui be- ne convenit cum Ebraeo textu: ET ERIT TAN- TUM VEXATIO (וְהָיָה רְוָחָה) INTELLIGERE FACIET AUDITUM, h. e. verbum auditus: quod auditur a Deo, a Prophetis, & audiri debet, cum ab iis ex ore Dei annunciantur hominibus Es. 53, 1. Recte ergo B. Lutherus, denn allein die An- fechtung lehret aufs Wort mercken. Conf. glossa ejus marginalis. Neque alienus est ab hoc sensu " Calvinus: Tantummodo terror intelligere fa- "ciet. Accidet, ut solus terror vos doctrinae ca- "paces reddat.

## 28:20
Ver. 20.

FOR THE BED IS NARROWED, SO THAT ONE MAY FALL OFF; AND THE CLOAK IS SHORT, SO THAT IT CANNOT COVER BOTH.) The protection of God will not extend itself to the city and the region, but to the city alone.

An overly arbitrary gloss, that BOTH is to be understood of the city and the region, and the Hebrew has nothing about BOTH, or about the falling of the other: but they sound thus (as they are well rendered by Osiander) For the bed will be too short for one to be able to stretch himself, and the covering too narrow for one to be able to wrap himself in it. The bed will become too short for me, and the blanket much too narrow. That is, rest, tranquility, and the abundance of things will be taken away from you; and pressing disturbances of the Republic will follow, and a lack and indigence of all necessary things. Similarly Calvin: He signifies that the Jews will be so hemmed in that they will be oppressed by extreme straits, and the bed, which was given to men for rest, will be like a sack. Now if they seek a covering, he says the blanket will be too short to suffice. Thus, in addition to the previous evil, he says that this also will be added, that in those heavy miseries all necessary comforts will be lacking to them. For he wished to express this by the simile of a tighter blanket, so that they might understand that their condition would be most miserable of all, because the vengeance of God will pursue them on every side, both from below and from above: so that they have no relief or relaxation, nor find any remedy. To which also the interpretation of the Belgians is added: Nor is the explanation of Junius alien, although it is a little different: below, above, finally from no part will they be able to cover themselves from the scourges of God. Jerome did something else here, explaining the bed not holding two lovers as God and idols; whom, however, most Papists follow on account of the Vulgate version. The LXX Interpreters also did something else here, whose version has nothing in common with the Hebrew text.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

COANGVSTARVM EST ENIM STRATVM, ITA VT ALTER DECIDAT; ET PALLIVM BREVE V- TRVMQVE OPERIRE NON POTEST.) Dei tutela non extendet se ad urbem & regionem, sed ad urbem solam.

Nimis arbitraria glossa, UTRUMQUE de urbe & regione intelligendum esse, neque Hebraea quic- quam habent de UTROQUE, aut de alterius casu: sed ita sonant (ut bene redduntur ab Osiandro) Bre- vius enim erit stratum, quam ut quis sese extendere possit, & operimentum angustius, quam ut quis in illud se involvere queat. Es wird mir das Bette zu kurz, und die Decke viel zuschmal werden. Id est, quies, tranquillitas & rerum opulentia a vobis auferentur; Et succedent urgentes Reipubl. per- turbationes, & omnium rerum necessariarum ino- pia & indigentia. Similiter Calvinus: Judaeos sic con- clusum iri significat, ut extremis angustiis oppri- mantur, & lectum, qui ad quietem datus est homi- nibus, fore instar culei. Jam si integumentum quaerant, stragulam breviorem fore dicit, quam ut sufficiat. Ita ad superius malum hoc etiam acce- dere dicit, quod in illis gravibus aerumnis omnibus ipsis solatia necessaria deerunt. Hoc enim simi- litudine strictioris straguli exprimere voluit, ut omnium miserrimam conditionem suam fore in- telligant, quia eos undiquaque & subtus & supra ul- tio Dei persequetur: ut nihil habeant levamenti aut relaxationis, nec quicqua remedii inveniant. Quo etiam accedit Belgarum interpretatio: Nec aliena est Junii explicatio, quamvis paulo alia: inferne, su- perne, nulla deniq; ex parte poterit se a flagellis Dei te- gere. Hieronym. aliud hic egit, de lectulo duos ama- tores non capiente, Deum & idola explicans; quem tamen pleriq; Pontificii ob versionem Vulgatam se- quuntur. Aliud etiam hic egere LXX. Interpp. quo- rum versio cum Ebraeo textu nihil commune habet.

## 28:21
Ver. 21. FOR AS IN THE MOUNT OF DIVISIONS THE LORD SHALL STAND) In Mount Perazim. The history is 2 Sam. 5:20, 1 Chron. 14:11.

AS IN THE VALLEY WHICH IS IN GIBEON HE SHALL BE ANGRY) The history is Joshua 10:10 and following.

HIS STRANGE WORK) That which He is not accustomed to do. For God is accustomed to protect the Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 21. SICUT ENIM IN MONTE DIVISIO- NUM STABIT DOMINUS) In monte Pharasim. Historia est 2. Sam. 5, 20. 1. Par. 14, 11.

SICUT IN VALLE, QUÆ EST IN GA- BAON IRASCETUR) Historia est Josuæ 10, 10. & sequen- tibus.

ALIENUM OPUS EJUS) Quod non solet facere. Solet enim Deus protegere Israëlitas.

## 28:22
Ver. 22. DO NOT MOCK) To despise these threats.

LEST PERCHANCE YOUR BONDS BE TIGHTENED) Lest on account of this your captivity become harder.

But Grotius does not accept this prophecy as being about the captivity, but about the slaughter inflicted by Sennacherib: However, the sentiment of these words is general, that one must cease from contempt of the word of God, lest God subsequently punish stubbornness with more severe scourges.

FOR I HAVE HEARD A CONSUMMATION AND ABBREVIATION FROM THE LORD OF HOSTS UPON ALL THE EARTH.) A cut-off consummation: as above 10:22, that is, few shall escape the evil, namely those who either before the arrival of Shalmaneser had fled into distant lands, or already at his very arrival had fled to Jerusalem.

Nor does this gloss agree with the slaughter inflicted by Sennacherib. For in that, the metropolis itself was saved, and in it were saved not a few, but very many: Indeed, the greatest part of the people was then saved. Therefore, the evil did not then extend over the whole earth. How the words are to be rendered, we have said at chapter 10:22. The destruction of the whole kingdom is designated, which consummation, however, so that it may not be entirely universal, will be cut short for the sake of the elect, whom God is about to rescue.

Latin:

Vers. 22. NOLITE ILLUDERE) Contemnere has minas.

NE FORTE CONSTRINGANTUR VINCULA VESTRA) Ne ob id durior fiat captivitas vestra.

At non accipit Grotius vaticinium hoc de captivitate, sed de clade ab Sennacheribo illata: Cæterum generalis est sententia horum verborum, cessandum esse a contemptu verbi Dei, ne Deus subinde gravioribus flagellis contumaciam puniat.

CONSUMMATIONEM ENIM ET ABBREVIA- TIONEM AUDIVI A DOMINO EXERCITUUM SUPER UNIVERSAM TERRAM.) Consummationem præ- cisam: ut supra 10, 22. id est, pauci evadent malum, nem- pe qui aut ante adventum Salmanasaris in terras longin- quas, aut jam in ipso ejus adventu Hierosolyma confuge- rint.

Neq; hæc glossa congruit cladi à Sennacheri- bo illatæ. In ea enim metropolis ipsa servata fuit, & in eadem servati simul non pauci, sed oppido multi: Imo maxima pars populi tum servata fuit. Non er- go per universam terram malum tum sese exten- dit. Quomodo autem reddenda sint verba, ad c.10, 22. diximus. Totius regni excidium designatur, quæ tamen consummatio, ne prorfus universalis sit, præscindetur electorum gratia, quos erepturus est Deus.

## 28:23
Ver. 23. SHALL THE PLOWMAN PLOW ALL THE DAY TO SOW, SHALL HE OPEN AND HARROW HIS GROUND) It could be objected, why does God act so variously? He shows, therefore, by a similitude taken from agriculture, that GOD knows best the distinction of times and of men and of the ways by which each man ought to be treated. There is a time for plowing, a time for harrowing, a time for weeding. For farmers always harrow before they weed, says Plautus.

Latin:

Vers. 23. NUMQUID TOTA DIE ARABIT A- RANS, UT SERAT, PROSCINDET ET SARRIET HUMUM SUAM) Objici poterat, cur Deus tam varie? ostendit igitur similitudine sumta ab agri cultura, DEUM optime nosse discrimen temporum & hominum & modo- rum, quibus homines quique tractari debeant. Est tempus arandi, tempus occandi, tempus sarriendi. Nam semper oc- cant prius quam sarriunt rustici, ait Plautus.

## 28:25
Ver. 25. HATH HE NOT, WHEN HE HATH MADE PLAIN THE FACE THEREOF) When he has leveled the field by harrowing and weeding.

HE SHALL SOW GITH) Melanthium to the Greeks, as the LXX have it here, nigella to the Latins from the Greek.

AND HE SHALL PUT THE WHEAT IN ORDER) In the Hebrew: the best wheat.

AND BARLEY AND MILLET) In the Hebrew: marked barley: that is, set aside in a bag with a certain mark of excellence.

AND VETCH IN ITS BORDERS) The Greeks [use] ζέαν. Some of the Latins translate it as far, as Galen and Dionysius of Halicarnassus [translate] φάρος, others as spelt, which word even now remains in languages corrupted from Latin. Jerome has both in the fourth [chapter] of Ezekiel. In its borders: that is, in its own places.

Latin:

Vers. 25. NONNE CUM ADÆQUAVERIT FA- CIEM EJUS) Ubi complanarit agrum occando & sar- riendo.

SERET GITH) Melanthium Græcis, ut hic habent LXX. nigellam Latinis ex Græco.

ET PONET TRITICUM PER ORDINEM) In Hebræo: triticum optimum.

ET HORDEUM ET MILIUM) In Hebræo: hor- deum signatum: id est, sepositum in sacculum cum nota quadam excellentiæ.

ET VICIAM IN FINIBUS SUIS) Græci ζέαν. Latinorum alii far vertunt, ut Galenus & Halicarnassensis Dionysius φάρος, alii speltam, quod vocabulum etiam nunc manet in linguis ex Latina corruptis. Utrumque ha- bet Hieronymus in IV. Ezechielis. In finibus suis: id est, in locis suis.

## 28:26
Ver. 26. AND HE WILL INSTRUCT HIM IN JUDGMENT, HIS GOD WILL TEACH HIM) God instructs the farmer, and teaches him how he may do all these things in their own order. Aratus concerning Jove, that is, God: - - - he says when the clod is best for oxen and mattocks; he says when the seasons are favorable both to plant plants and to cast all seeds.

If God teaches the farmer these things, will He not Himself observe order and measure in His own affairs? A similar argument [is found in] Psalm 94, v. 9.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET ERUDIET ILLUM IN JUDICIO, DEUS SUUS DOCEBIT ILLUM) - Deus agricolam insti- tuit, ac docet, quomodo hæc omnia suo ordine faciat. A- ratus de Jove, id est, Deo: - - - λέγει δὲ ὅτε βῶλος ἀρίστη Βουσί τε καὶ μακέλησι· λέγει δ᾽ ὅτε δεξιαὶ ὥραι καὶ φυτὰ γυρῶσαι κ᾿ σπέρματα πάντα βαλέ- σθαι

Si Deus agricolam ista docet, an ipse in suis rebus non ser- vabit ordinem modumque? Similis argumentatio Psalm. 94. v. 9.

## 28:27
Ver. 27. FOR THE GITH SHALL NOT BE THRESHED WITH SAWS) You would translate it more correctly as threshing sledges, because here 'with saws' is less appropriate.

NOR SHALL THE CART WHEEL GO ROUND UPON THE CUMIN) The cart shall not be turned upon the cumin, for it would not be fit for bearing it.

BUT THE GITH SHALL BE BEATEN OUT WITH A ROD) It is beaten out with a pole.

AND THE CUMIN WITH A STAFF) [With one] lighter than a pole.

Latin:

Vers. 27. NON ENIM IN SERRIS TRITURA- BITUR GITH) Tribula rectius verteris, quod hic minus proprie in serris.

NEC ROTA PLAUSTRI SUPER CYMINUM CIRCUIBIT) Non versabitur plaustrum super cyminum, neque enim par esset ferendo.

SED IN VIRGA EXCUTIETUR GITH) Pertica excutitur.

ET CYMINUM IN BACULO) Leviore quam est pertica.

## 28:28
Ver. 28.

BUT BREAD) That is, wheat, from which bread is made, as in Ecclesiastes 11:1.

SHALL BE CRUSHED) It is accustomed to be crushed by the threshing sledge and the cart, as the following indicates. BUT HE WILL NOT BE THRESHING IT FOREVER) That is, the farmer takes good care of himself, lest he thresh for too long, otherwise he would not only be shaking out the ears and chaff, but also corrupting the grains, as the following indicates. NOR SHALL THE CART WHEEL VEX IT) Lest the cart wheel break it, namely that wheat. NOR SHALL HE DIMINISH IT WITH HIS HOOFS) And lest the teeth (namely of the threshing sledge) scatter it into small pieces. AND THIS HAS GONE FORTH FROM THE LORD GOD OF HOSTS) This judgment concerning the Hebrews was also made in a like manner by God, according to wisdom and equity, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

PANIS AUTEM) Id est, triticum, unde fit panis, ut Ecclesiastæ 11, 1.

COMMINUETUR) Comminui solet tribula & plau- stro, ut sequentia indicant. VERUM NON IN PERPETUUM TRITV- RANS TRITVRABIT ILLUM) Id est, bene cavet sibi agricola, ne nimis diu trituram faciat, alioqui non aristas tantum & paleas excussurus, sed & grana corrupturus, ut sequentia indicant. NEQUE VEXABIT EUM ROTA PLAUSTRI) Ne frangat rota plaustri illud, nempe triticum illud. NEC UNGULIS SUIS DIMINUET EVM) Et ne dentes (nempe tribulae) illud minutim dispergant. ET HOC A DOMINO DEO EXERCITVUM EXIVIT) Etiam hoc judicium de Hebraeis pari modo a Deo factum est, secundum sapientiam & aequitatem ut se- quitur.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX. The siege of Jerusalem by the Chaldeans is predicted, with the addition of comfort for the faithful, that the Jews would again struggle free, liberated from the power of the enemies, even though they were not going to turn out better, but rather would eventually harden their hearts, and so were to be plainly cast away, with the nations taken into their place.

Verse 1.

WOE TO ARIEL, ARIEL, THE CITY) Woe to the city of Ariel, Ariel. Ariel was the name of the altar of burnt offerings, as appears in Isaiah 29:1 [Efa. 43, 15], namely because that altar, like a lion, consumed the victims consecrated to God. The city of Ariel, therefore, is the city of Jerusalem, in which that altar was, the great glory of the city, and this whole prophecy alludes to the rites of that altar. ADD YEAR TO YEAR.) In the Hebrew: Add year to year: that is, wait for two years. This prophecy was pronounced and written two years before the siege made by Sennacherib. For God often wished the same things to be proclaimed, so that His providence might appear the more. THE SOLEMNITIES HAVE PASSED.) The lambs will be slaughtered. For חגים (feasts) are called not only festival days, but also victims, as in Psalm 118:27, by a likeness drawn from the altar, which he also pursues in the following verses, he signifies that it will come to pass that many men will perish through Sennacherib.

This prophecy is explained in various ways: Most take it concerning the siege of the Chaldeans, some concerning that of the Romans, and certain ones concerning both, such as Corn. a Lapide, Menochius, and Tirinus, along with Jerome. But it cannot be understood as concerning both: nor do all the things which are contained here agree with the latter siege, such as that the multitude of the nations of the enemies of the city is said to be like a dream in verse 7, and other things. Therefore, it is more correctly explained by the Vinarieans Osiander, Junius, and Piscator as concerning the siege of the Chaldeans made by Nebuchadnezzar, to which interpretation we add our support, yet in such a way that it is predicted thereafter in verse 9 and following that, through the liberation from the enemies, the Jews would turn out no better, nay rather that blindness and even hardening would follow, namely at the coming of Christ, such that by the just judgment of God they would finally be cast off, and the Gentiles would be assumed in their place. Which opinion our Osiander has rightly expressed. Nor does Brentius, or even Calvin, deny it. Grotius, however, persists in his preconceived opinion that all these things still look to the times of Hezekiah: and he twists this prophecy also to that, just as he did the preceding ones. Therefore, he wishes the siege made by the Assyrians to be understood here, which was also the opinion of Oecolampadius: But the things which are predicted here: And I will camp against Ariel, and it shall be heavy and sorrowful, and it shall be unto me as Ariel, and I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee, do not agree with Sennacherib: for the city was not surrounded by him in that way; nay, the Lord promised the contrary concerning him in chapter 37, 33: He shall not enter into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor shall the shield occupy it.

AND HE SHALL NOT CAST UP A MOUND AROUND IT: whence it appears that the army of Sennacherib, as soon as it returned to the siege of the city, before it could surround it with mounds and perform other things necessary for a siege, was struck down by the Angel of the Lord: And for that reason, 2 Kings 19:35, they are said to have been struck down in that night, namely, the one in which Sennacherib returned to besiege Jerusalem. Much less, therefore, do these things fit the machination of the Assyrians, which are read in verse 5 concerning the multitude of those who PREVAILED against the city. Now, since he renders the first verse thus: Woe to Ariel, to the city of Ariel, he acknowledges that these evils were predicted against the city itself. Since, therefore, the Prophet prophesies concerning it, AND I WILL BESIEGE ARIEL, that is, according to Grotius's interpretation, I will cause the city of Jerusalem to be besieged, AND IT SHALL BE TO ME AS ARIEL, i.e., as Grotius explains again, many will lie dead in the circuit of that city, just like victims before an altar: how, I ask, can he twist this to refer to the slaughtered Assyrians? For the Prophet does not threaten woe to the Assyrians, but to the city, and the slaughter of those whose siege he predicts, as the words themselves and the subsequent verses 3, 4, and 5 openly testify that all these evils hang over the city, which are predicted in this place: which is also called Ariel for this reason, that the people are to be slaughtered in it like victims. Therefore, those killed like victims cannot be understood as the soldiers of Sennacherib, or even as the Jews outside the city, because God threatens destruction primarily to the city. Nor is there anything here about waiting for two years: nor is it established by any document that this prophecy was made two years before Sennacherib's arrival at the city. Which Grotius assumes for himself without proof. The Hebrew words are not badly rendered: ADD YEAR TO YEAR, LET THE LAMBS BE SLAUGHTERED, but they are very poorly explained as: wait for two years: many will be slaughtered like victims by Sennacherib: which neither agrees with a similar way of speaking, and is refuted by the event and fulfillment itself. For the Jerusalemites were not slaughtered in that way then. But the Prophet addresses them, and threatens them with those evils, the siege, the storming, and the destruction. However, the meaning of these words, a year is added to a year, is rendered in various ways. Cyril understands it strangely concerning the two years of Christ's preaching in Judea: Jerome concerning the cessation of sacred rites, a year is added to a year, or subtracted, as Aquila interpreted, and the solemnities have revolved: for with the temple overturned and the Jewish religion removed, all their festivity perished, and he says that the Lord will besiege Ariel with a Babylonian army, and that it will be sad and mourning when it has been divided from them. So also Menochius, after two years, that is, after a few, the majesty of Jerusalem will be overturned, and hence its feasts will have revolved and will cease. And so also Adam and Forerius. Cornel. à Lapide [thinks] a little differently, a second year is added to a year, that is, a few more years will pass, and the solemnities have revolved, or will revolve, that is, a few Passovers will pass, and other annual feasts will be celebrated as the years recur, and I will besiege Ariel with the nets first of the Chaldeans, then of the Romans. Thomas, Haymo, Hugo, and Sanctius take it concerning the duration of the calamity: as if to say, for many years and feasts in exile, and in filth, the Jews will remain; but according to the Hebrew text, the meaning is clear, which our people have expressed: ADD (indeed, according to your custom, annual solemnities to annual ones) LET THE LAMBS BE SLAUGHTERED, AND (nevertheless the city) Ariel IS CAST INTO STRAITS. For God is not moved by the exercise of external ceremonies to spare His people, if the people continue to indulge in wickedness. Brentius explained it thus: Heap up annual feasts, add feasts to feasts, slaughter lambs for sacrifices, and yet not even so can you escape destruction. So that it is the same sentiment as that which he says in Jer. 7: Add your burnt offerings to your victims, and eat the flesh, etc. Your feast days and sacrifices will not profit you, because I, says the Lord, will besiege, I will straiten Ariel or the city of Jerusalem, so that it may become sad and mourning, and so that it may become entirely like Ariel, that is, like the Altar. For just as slaughterings of sacrifices take place around the Altar, and sacrifices are consumed by fire on the altar, so around the city of Jerusalem, and in Jerusalem, many men will be slaughtered and killed, so that Jerusalem may truly become Ariel, that is, a place of slaughter. And B. Luther, in his Enarrations on this place, [says] the greatest cause of the presumption of the Jews was this, that they had festivals and daily, monthly, and annual sacred rites, divinely instituted; under this pretext they were puffed up against the Gospel. The Prophet therefore mocks them: Go on, proceed, sacrificing bravely: It will come to pass that you will perish together with your sacrifices. Similarly Osiander and the Vinarienses. Nor do the Reformed, Oecolampadius, Calvin, Junius, Piscator, the Dutch interpreters, and others deny this.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX. Chaldaea Hierosolymae obsessio praedicta, addi- to ob fideles solatio, quod iterum eluctatu- ri sint Judaei e potestate hostium liberati, etsi non meliores evasuri, imo tandem animum induraturi, adeoque plane abjiciendi, as- sumptis in eorum locum gentibus.

Vers. 1.

VAE ARIEL ARIEL CIVITAS) Vae Arielis Arie- lis urbi. Ariel erat nomen altaris holocaustorum, ut appa- ret Efa. 43, 15. nempe quod id altare, ut leo, victimas Deo sacratas consumeret. Urbs Arielis ergo est urbs Hierosoly- ma, in qua erat illud altare, magnum urbis decus, & totum hoc vaticinium ad titus altaris istius alludit. ADDITUS EST ANNUS AD ANNUM.) In He- braeo: Adjicite annum ad annum: id est, exspectate bien- nium. Haec Prophetia pronunciata & scripta est biennio ante obsidionem, factam per Sennacheribum. Saepe enim Deus res easdem voluit praedicari, quo magis appareret e- jus providentia. SOLENNITATES EVOLUTAE SUNT.) Agni ju- gulabuntur. Nam חגים dicuntur non dies tantum festi, sed & victimae, ut Ps.118,27. similitudine ab altari ducta, quam & in sequentibus persequitur, significat fore, ut multi homines pereant per Sennacheribum.

DIversimode explicatur hoc vaticinium: Pleri- que de Chaldaeorum, nonnulli de Romanorum obsidione, quidam de utraque accipiunt, utpote Corn. a Lapide, Menochius, Tirinus, cum Hierony- mo. Sed intelligi de utraque non potest: neque congruunt posteriori obsidioni omnia, quae hic ha- bentur, utpote quod multitudo gentium civitatis hostium instar somnii futura dicitur vers. 7. & alia. Proinde de Chaldaeorum obsidione per Nebucadne- zarem facta rectius explicatur a Vinariensibus Osiandro, Junio, Piscatore, cui interpretationi cal- culum addimus, ita tamen, ut praedicatur deinceps vers. 9. seqq. per liberationem ab hostibus nihilo me- liores evasuros Judaeos, imo caecitatem etiam atq; in- durationem sequentibus, sub adventum sc. Christi, eam futuram, ut justo Dei judicio abjiciendi tandem sint, ac gentes eorum loco assumendae. Quam senten- tiam recte expressit Osiander noster. Neque ab- nuit Brentius, aut etiam Calvinus. Grotius vero persistit in sua praeconcepta opinione, haec omnia adhuc respicere Ezechiae tempora: atque eo tor- quet hoc etiam vaticinium, perinde uti praeceden- tia. Proinde obsidionem per Assyrios factam hic intelligi vult, quae etiam Oecolampadii fuit senten- tia: Sed quae hic praedicuntur: Et circumvallabo Ariel, & erit tristis & maerens, & erit mihi quasi Ariel, & circumdabo quasi Sphaeram in circuitu tuo, & faciam contra te aggerem, & munimenta po- nam in obsidionem tuam, non congruunt Sennache- ribo: ab eo enim ita circumdata urbs non fuit, imo contrarium promisit de eo Dominus cap. 37, 33. Non intrabit civitatem hanc, & non jaciet ibi sagittam, & non occupabit eam clypeus.

ET NON MITTET IN CIRCUITU EJUS AGGEREM: unde apparet, exercitum Senna- cheribi mox ut rediit ad obsidionem urbis, ante- quam aggeres cingeret, aliaque ad obsidionem ne- cessaria ageret, ab Angelo Domini cæsum fuisse: Atq; ea de causa 2. Reg. 19, 35. cæsi dicuntur in no- cte illa, scilicet qua Sennacherib rediit ad obsiden- dam Hierosolymam. Multo ergo minus conve- niunt ista machinationi Assyriorum, quæ vers. 5. de multitudine eorum, qui PRÆVALUERUNT contra urbem, leguntur. Jam cum versum primum ita reddit: Væ Arielis, Arielis urbi, agnoscit, hæc mala in urbem ipsam prædicta esse. Quum ergo de ea vaticinetur Propheta, ET CIRCUMVAL- LABO ARIEL, id est, interprete Grotio, efficiam, ut obsideatur urbs Hierosolyma, ET ERIT MIHI QUASI ARIEL, h. e. ut iterum Grotius exponit, in circuitu ejus urbis plurimi jacebunt mortui, sicut victimæ coram altari: quomodo obsecro hæc ad cæsos Assyrios detorquere potest? Non enim væ minatur Propheta Assyriis, sed urbi, & eorum cæ- dem, quorum obsessionem prædicit, ut verba ipsa, & subsequentes v. 3. 4. 5. palam testantur, mala hæc omnia urbi impendere, quæ hoc loco prædicun- tur: quæ etiam ideo Ariel vocatur, quod victimæ instar cædendus in ea populus sit. Proinde occisi victimarum instar non possunt de militibus Senna- cheribi, vel etiam de Judæis extra urbem intelligi, quia exitium urbi minatur potissimum Deus. Neq; hic de biennio expectando quicquam habetur: aut ullo documento constat, hanc Prophetiam biennio ante Sennacheribi adventum ad urbem factam. Quod gratis sibi sumit Groti9. Ebræa non male red- duntur: ADJICITE ANNUM AD ANNUM, AGNI JUGULABUNTUR, sed pessime ea expo- nuntur, biennium expectate: mactabuntur multi instar victimarum per Sennacheribum: quæ nec modo loquendi simili congruunt, & ab ipso eventu ac complemento refelluntur. Neq; enim ita Hie- rosolymitani tunc mactati sunt. At hos alloquitur, his mala illa, obsidionem, expugnationem, & exitium minitatur Propheta. Varia autem verborum istorũ, additus est annus ad annum, redditur sententia. Cy- rillus aliene de biennio prædicationis Christi in Ju- dæa intelligit: Hieronymus de cessatione sacrorum, additus est annus ad annum, sive subtractus, ut in- terpretatus est Aquila, & solemnitates evolutæ sunt: subverso enim templo, & Judaica religione subla- ta omnis eorum festivitas periit, dicitque se Domi- nus circumvallare Ariel Babylonico exercitu, & fore eam tristem atque mœrentem, quando ab eis divisa fuerit. Sic etiam Menochius, post duos annos, id est, post paucos Hierosolymæ majestas evertetur, hincq; ejus festa erunt evoluta, & cessabunt. Atq; ita etiam Adamus & Forerius. Cornel. à Lapide paulo aliter, binus additus est annus ad annum, id est, ex- current adhuc aliquot anni, & solemnitates evolutæ sunt, seu evolventur, id est, excurrent aliquot Pa- schalia, & alia anni festa, recurrentibus annis per- agentur, & retibus primo Chaldæorum, dein Ro- manorum circumvallabo Ariel. Thomas, Haymo, Hugo, & Sanctius de duratione calamitatis accipi- unt: q. d. multis annis & festis in exilio, & fordi- bus hærebunt Judæi; sed juxta textum Ebræum sensus luculentus est, quem nostrates expresserunt: ADDITE (sane, pro more vestro, annuas sole- mnitates ad annuas) AGNI JUGULENTUR, ET IN ANGUSTIAS CONJICITUR (nihil- ominus civitas) Ariel. Deus enim non movetur externarum ceremoniarum exercitio, ut parcat populo suo, si populu9 pergat sceleribus indulgere. Ita exposuit Brentius: Cumulate annua festa q;, addi- te festa festis, mactate agnos in sacrificia, & tamen ne sic quidem potestis effugere interitum. Ut sit eadem sententia, cum eo, quod Jer. 7. ait; Holocautomata vestra addite victimis vestris, & comedite carnes, &c. Non proderunt vobis vestri dies festi, & sacrificia, quia ego, inquit Dominus, circumvallabo, ego angu- stiabo Arielem seu urbem Hierusalem, ut fiat tristis & mœrens, adeoque prorsus fiat sicut Ariel, hoc est, sicut Altare. Nam quemadmodum circa Altare fiunt mactationes sacrificiorum, & in altari sacrifi- cia absumuntur igni, ita circa urbem Hierusalem, & in Hierusalem mactabuntur, & interficientur multi homines, ut Hierusalem vere fiat Ariel, hoc est, locus mactationis. Et B. Lutherus Enarr. in h. l. maxima causa præsumtionis Iudæorum erat hæc, quod habebant festivitates & sacra quotidiana, menstrua & annua, divinitus instituta; hoc prætextu contra Evangelium inflabantur. Propheta igitur ridet eos: Agite, pergite, fortiter sacrificantes: Fiet, ut una cum sacrificiis vestris pereatis. Similiter Osiander & Vinarienses. Neque abnuunt Reformati, Oeco- lampadius, Calvinus, Junius, Piscator, Belgæ in- terpp. & alii.

## 29:2
Verse 2. AND I WILL BESIEGE ARIEL) I will cause the city of Jerusalem to be besieged.

AND IT SHALL BE TO ME AS ARIEL.) In the circuit of that city many will lie dead, just like victims around the Altar.

Whether Grotius points to the soldiers of Sennacherib, or rather to the Jews outside the city, is ambiguous. But it can be explained as neither. The Prophet threatens the Jerusalemites themselves, WOE TO ARIEL, ARIEL: And it shall be to me as Ariel. He could have been taught about the truer meaning by the Jesuits, if he had refused to hear others: Cornel. à Lapide brings forward various explanations, but he approves more of the Chaldeans, Vatablus, Lyranus, and Adam. Ariel is called an altar here, just as in Ezek. 43, as if to say, just as an altar is surrounded by the blood of victims, and as if swims in it, so I, God, through the Chaldeans as my priests, will stain this city as an altar with the blood of the impious citizens, and will as if consecrate it to God, that is, to me and my vengeance, so that just as slaughtered cattle lie stretched out beside the altar, so in Jerusalem the corpses of the inhabitants may lie stretched out. Thus says Jer. 12:3, gather them like a flock for the slaughter, and sanctify them in the day of slaughter. And Isaiah 34:6. For the victim of the Lord is in Bozrah. Which is also the interpretation of Brentius, Osiander, Piscator, and the Belgians. And so also Calvin: He understands that all things will be bloody from the slaughter which will be brought forth at Jerusalem, and therefore he compares it to an altar, on which victims and sacrifices are slaughtered: just as also the wicked destined for slaughter are accustomed to be compared to a sacrifice. Finally, here alluding to the name of the altar, he says the whole city will be as Ariel, because it will overflow with the blood of the slain. Which Oecolampadius's observation confirms: Ariel is the same as Lion of God. For just as a lamb or calf is given to a lion in the morning and evening, so also a yearling lamb was offered on the Jerusalem altar in the morning and evening, as is commanded in Exodus 29. B. Luther in the marginal gloss to v. 1. and in the Enarrations of the passage somewhat differently: but the matter and the sum of what is said returns to the same thing; and in the same manner also Tirinus: I will conduct myself toward Jerusalem as hunters do toward strong lions and lionesses.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET CIRCVNVALLABO ARIEL) Efficiam, ut obsideatur urbs Hierosolyma.

ET ERIT MIHI QVASI ARIEL.) In circuitu ejus urbis plurimi jacebunt mortui, sicut victimæ circum Altare,

An milites Sennacheribi indigitet Grotius, an vero Judæos extra urbem, ambiguum est. Sed de neutris explicari potest. Hierosolymitanis ipsis mi- natur Propheta, VÆ ARIEL ARIEL: Et erit mihi quasi Ariel. De sensu ergo veriori à Jesuitis edoceri poterat, si alios audire recusarit: Cornel. à Lapide varias adducit explicationes, sed Chaldæi, Vatabli, Lyrani & Adami magis probat. Ariel hic vocari altare, uti & Ezech. 43. q. d. sicut altare cir- cundatur sanguine victimarum, & in eo quasi natat, ita ego Deus per Chaldæos quasi Sacerdotes meos, hanc urbem quasi altare sanguine impiorum civium cruen- tabo, & quasi consecrabo Deo, id est, mihi meæq; vin- dictæ, ut sicut juxta altare stratæ jacent jugulatæ pe- cudes, ita in Jerusalem strata jaceant incolarum ca- davera. Sic ait Jerem. 12, 3. congrega eos quasi gre- gem victimam, & sanctifica eos in die occisionis. Et Esaias 34, 6. Victima enim Domini in Bofra. Quæ etiam Brentii, Osiandri, Piscatoris, Belgarum est interpretatio. Atq; ita quoq; Calvinus: Intelligit omnia sanguinolenta fore ex strage, quæ Hierosolymis edetur, ideoq; comparat aræ, in qua victimæ & hostiæ mactantur: quemadmodum etiam impii mactationi destinati sacrificio comparari solent. Deniq; hic al- ludens ad nomen altaris, dicit, totam civitatem fore velut Ariel, quia interfectorum sanguine redundabit. Quod facit Oecolampadii observatio: Ariel idem est, quod Leo Dei. Nam sicut Leoni mane & vesperi da- tur agnus, vel vitulus, ita & in altari Hierosolymi- tano mane & vesperi offerebatur agnus anniculus, sicut præcipitur Exod. 29. B. Lutherus in glossa mar- ginali ad v. 1. & in Enarr. loci paulo aliter: sed eo- dem tamen res & summa dictorum redit; atque ad eundem modum etiam Tirinus: sic me erga Jeru- salem geram, sicut venatores erga fortes leones, & leænas.

## 29:3
Vers. 3. AND I WILL SURROUND AS A SPHERE IN THY CIRCUIT) I will cast a camp around thee like a ball (that is, rounded). For כַּדּוּר, as a ball, the LXX read כְּדָוִד, as David.

AND I WILL MAKE AGAINST THEE A MOUND) A military rampart, I will cast a trench about thee, the LXX here. And Luke uses the same words in the Lord's prophecy concerning the siege by Vespasian 19, 43. See what we have said there.

AND I WILL PLACE FORTIFICATIONS IN YOUR SIEGE) I will place against you מצדות, that is, πύργες, as the Greeks have it. But the word itself signifies all siege engines. Among which are also movable towers, of which Hirtius treats in the Alexandrian War: Vitruvius 10, 19. Vegetius 4, 17. Verse 4. YOU SHALL BE HUMBLED, YOU SHALL SPEAK FROM THE EARTH, AND YOUR SPEECH SHALL BE HEARD FROM THE GROUND.) Your citizens will hide themselves from the fear of enemy missiles in crypts and underground places. AND YOUR VOICE SHALL BE AS THAT OF A PYTHON FROM THE EARTH.) For those Pythonics often spoke from caves. The Prophet does not treat of hiding in crypts, but of a humble, thin, and mournful speech as if from caverns, because those who formerly sounded with great eloquence are about to speak with a thin and mournful voice, such as that of Pythons from the earth is wont to be, or of ἐγγαςριμύθων, ventriloquists; on account of, to wit, the utmost distress and most grievous anxiety, and they will hardly dare to open their mouth, just as if a divining spirit, called forth by some enchanter, were to hiss and mutter from the earth in a very low voice (so that it can hardly be heard and understood) rather than speak. You will become small-voiced: all your power will fall away, so that you will hardly dare to mutter: all things will be full of fear and sorrow.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET CIRCVMDABO QVASI SPHÆRAM IN CIRCVITV TVO) Castra sicut pilam (id est, rotun- data) tibi circumjiciam. Pro כַּדּוּר, quasi pila LXX. lege- runt כְּדָוִד, ὡς Δαυβὶδ.

ET FACIAM CONTRA TE AGGEREM) Val- lum castrense, βαλῶ περὶ σὲ χάρακα LXX. hic. Eademque verba Lucas usurpat in Domini Prophetia de obsidione per Vespasianum 19, 13. Vide, quæ ibi diximus.

ET MVNIMENTA PONAM IN OBSIDIONEM TUAM) Ponam contra te מצדות, id est, πύργες, ut habent Græci. Sed vox ipsa significat omnes machinas πολιορκη- τικάς. In quibus & turres ambulatoriæ, de quibus agit Hir- tius bello Alexandrino: Vitruvius 10, 19. Vegetius 4, 17. Vers. 4. HVMILIABERIS, DE TERRA LOQVE- RIS, ET DE HVMO AVDIETVR ELOQVIVM TV- VM.) Metu telorum hostilium occultabunt se cives tui in cryptis & locis subterraneis. ET ERIT QVASI PYTHONIS DE TERRA VOX TVA.) Nam Pythonici isti sæpe ex antris loque- bantur. Non de occultatione in cryptis, sed loquela hu- mili, exili, & lugubri velut è cavernis Propheta a- git, quod qui magno antea sonabant eloquio, exili & lugubri voce loquuturi sint, qualis Pythonum de terra esse solet, aut ἐγγαςριμύθων, ventriloquo- rum; ob summam sc. angustiam, & anxietatem gra- vissimam, nec audebunt fere os suum aperire, per- inde ac si spiritus vaticidus ab incantatore aliquo e- vocatus submissa admodum voce, (ut vix audiri ac intelligi possit) è terra verius sibilet ac mussitet, quam loquatur. Du wirst kleinlaut werden: tota potentia tua decidet, ut mutire vix audeas: omnia plena erunt timoris & mœroris.

## 29:4
HE SHALL MUTTER) See above 8, 19. Verse 5. AND THE MULTITUDE OF THOSE WHO FAN YOU SHALL BE AS THIN DUST) ὡσει κόνις. AND THE MULTITUDE OF THOSE WHO HAVE PREVAILED AGAINST YOU SHALL BE AS PASSING CHAFF, AND IT SHALL BE SUDDENLY, IN AN INSTANT) In the Hebrew: The multitude of those oppressing you, like chaff flying past quickly in a moment. This simile signifies both a huge number, as the former, and adds speed to the number. See above 28, 19. Verse 6. YOU SHALL BE VISITED BY THE LORD OF HOSTS IN THUNDER AND EARTHQUAKE) That is, suddenly. AND A FLAME OF DEVOURING FIRE.) Above 9, 5. 26, 11. From this remission it appears that the army of Sennacherib being devoured as if by a flame of fire is understood by Grotius. But the Prophet still persists in denouncing WOE to Jerusalem: and therefore, just as that תדברי in v. 4, so also תפקד is deservedly taken by Oecolampadius, Osiander, and others as the feminine of the second person: YOU SHALL BE VISITED by the Lord God of hosts in thunder, and earthquake, and a great voice (that is, by horrible thunders, a Hebrew phrase) of a whirlwind and tempest, and a flame of devouring fire, that is, according to the interpretation of Osiander: The destruction of the city of Jerusalem will be for you like a horrendous tempest: where a huge wind, or rather a whirlwind, knocks down roofs, uproots trees: and hail follows, prostrating everything in its way: and such thunders are heard that the earth is shaken and trembles, and lightnings fall into houses, which ignite them in a moment, and stir up a deadly conflagration which cannot be extinguished.
