Menochius, insisting on the Vulgate, which renders it 'shall be visited', indeed understands it of the crowd and multitude of enemies with Corn. à Lapide, but explains it of the Chaldeans: Tirinus, however, acknowledges that the discourse here is about Ariel or Jerusalem, as do also Vatablus and Leo Castrius. Which opinion agrees with ours, as far as the sense of the prophecy is concerned. Verse 7. AND THE MULTITUDE OF ALL NATIONS SHALL BE AS THE DREAM OF A NIGHT VISION.) Thus it shall suddenly vanish. Like light winds, and most similar to a fleeting dream. There are not wanting those who refer these things likewise to the threats made to the Jews: which is especially the explanation of Calvin: He rebukes, he says, the Jews, and argues their stubbornness, because they securely despised God and all his threats. And he inveighs against their false confidence and security with a most apt simile, while he denounces that enemies will arrive suddenly and unexpectedly, where the Jews will think they are enjoying tranquil peace and are far removed from all danger, and that the matter will be so sudden and unexpected that it will seem to be a dream. Although therefore you now conceive of perpetual quiet in your mind, he says, God will easily rouse you, and will shake off that security of yours. But the Prophet says the Jews dream because, immersed in their delights, they see or feel nothing: but with a mind overwhelmed and astonished they imagine happiness for themselves out of stupor. Whence he gathers that enemies will come suddenly, as if through a dream, who will strike terror into those sleeping, just as it often happens that sweet and pleasant slumber is disturbed by dire nightmares; whence it follows that the blandishments in which they sleep will be useless to them: because however much they think of nothing, yet a commotion will suddenly creep upon them. But Calvin's interpretation is twisted: For in the text the multitude of NATIONS fighting against Sion is said to be like those who dream. Others therefore explain these things more correctly concerning the enemies. Although indeed some with Junius think that only the insatiable tyranny of the enemies is hinted at, which is also the opinion of the Belgians, nevertheless the explanation of those who judge that consolation is brought here to the faithful is altogether to be preferred: that the enemies are to be rendered like those who dream, when the Lord will frustrate them, when they will seem to be almost in possession of their wish. From which explanation there is no reason why we should depart. For before more serious evils were predicted to happen to the Jews on account of their hardening, the pious had also to be raised up with some consolation, as the Prophets generally are in the habit of doing. Just as those who are hungry and thirsty seem to themselves in dreams to eat and drink: but when awakened they are hungry and thirsty nonetheless, and see that it was nothing but a dream. So the impious, the enemies of the Church of God, do this with great desire of heart, that they may devour the Church and absorb it entirely: and because the Lord grants them prosperous successes for a time, they exult beyond measure. But that temporary happiness of theirs is nothing but a certain dream. For a little later their dominion and tyranny is shaken off from them: the people of God are restored to their liberty and former happiness: but they themselves perish miserably, and fare worse than ever before. Which interpretation has pleased most. And thus we think the former prediction concerning the siege of the Chaldeans is concluded. Although indeed the same words are used by Christ in Luke 19, 13 concerning the siege made by Vespasian, which are read here in v. 3, it is not however to be thought that it was predicted in this place for that reason, since Christ only indicated that the latest siege would be similar to the former, and that the anxiety with which they will be afflicted by the Romans would be no less. For this consolation subjoined in verses 7 and 8, agrees more with the former devastation and slaughter, from which the Jews had again struggled out, than with the most recent. But since Isaiah also foresees that, that the Jews would turn out no better after their liberation, nay, that they would eventually harden their hearts and utterly reject the Evangelical doctrine concerning Christ, therefore, at the dictation of the Holy Spirit, he now prophesies in the other part of the chapter, v. 9 and following, concerning their rejection and the assumption of the Gentiles: BE ASTONISHED AND WONDER, FLUCTUATE AND WAVER. Or as it is held in the Hebrew: Be slow and stupid, blind yourselves, and be blind, that is, you will be such, and you will so blind yourselves. BE DRUNKEN, AND NOT WITH WINE, BE MOVED (stagger like the intoxicated) AND NOT WITH DRUNKENNESS. Which was fulfilled at the coming of the Messiah: inasmuch as the Jews neither admitted his sermons, nor attended to his miracles, however most illustrious, so stupid and blind were they: and they behaved themselves toward the sermons of Christ and the Apostles like the intoxicated, who, laden with wine, stagger hither and thither, and cannot stand on their feet, neither know what is said or done. For those drunk on Pharisaic doctrine, and the cares and pleasures of this age, did not notice, nor did they care, what Christ and his disciples say or do. To no time, I say, do these things apply more aptly than to the latest age of the Jews under the advent of Christ. And Paul himself, Rom. 11:8, explains these things which are added in verse 10, FOR THE LORD HAS MIXED FOR YOU A SPIRIT OF STUPOR, concerning the Jews of his own time. Then THE LORD HAS COVERED THE PROPHETS AND YOUR PRINCES, WHO SEE, WITH A VISION, namely with a veil of darkness, either because the sense of the Holy Prophets was veiled to them, 2 Cor. 3:14, or because they were especially blinded by the doctrine of the Pharisees and false prophets, and their eyes were covered, as those who prophesied falsely from a spirit of lies and error. HE HAS COVERED the prophets and your chief preachers with darkness, Brentius explains. For the High Priests, Priests, Scribes, Pharisees, and those who were set over teaching others, as well as the Elders and Magistrates of the people (Grotius thinks the leaders of the people are addressed here) were clearly blind to the Gospel of Christ. And whom shall we provide as a more certain interpreter than Christ himself, who expressly explained this prophecy concerning the Jews, Pharisees, and Doctors of the people of his own time: and testified in express words that the Prophet had prophesied about them here, Matt. 15:7, 'Hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy about you, saying: This people honors me with their lips; but their heart is far from me; but in vain they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.' Which are taken from v. 13 of this chapter. And when Christ speaks of the blinding of the Jews, and predicts the illumination of the Gentiles, John 9:39. I came into this world for judgment, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind, what else does it indicate than what is insinuated here through the Prophet, that there will be an overturning for the Jews, just as the words of a sealed book, but the Gentiles, though deaf, will hear the words of the book, and the blind eyes will see, v. 11 and 18. Nor without cause did the Apostle use this in the first place to confound the wisdom of the age, 1 Cor. 1, because it rejects the heavenly wisdom of the Gospel; because, namely, it was predicted in this place concerning the Jews of his own time, and of that kind, that heavenly wisdom would be a scandal to them, as being blinded and hardened by the just judgment of God. Finally, since v. 17 deals with the conversion of the Gentiles no less than with the blinding of the Jews: no doubt can remain that these things pertain to the times of the N.T.: concerning which there is also consensus among most Christian interpreters. But let us now see the Grotian glosses on the remaining part of the chapter.

Latin:

MVSSITABIT) Vide supra 8, 19. Vers. 5. ET ERIT SICVT PVLVIS TENVIS MVL- TITVDO VENTILANTIVM TE) ὡσει κόνις. ET SICVT FAVILLA PERTRANSIENS MVL- TITVDO EORVM, QVI CONTRA TE PRÆVA- LVERVNT, ERITQVE REPENTE CONFESTIM) In Hebræo: Multitudo opprimentium te, ut pluma celeriter in momento transvolans. Hæc similitudo & numerum in- gentem significat, ut prior, & numero adjicit celeritatem. Vide supra 28, 19. Vers. 6. A DOMINO EXERCITVVM VISITA- BITVR IN TONITRV ET COMMOTIONE TERRÆ) Id est, subito. ET FLAMMA IGNIS DEVORANTIS.) Supra 9, 5. 26, 11. Ex hac remissione apparet, devorandum velut flamma ignis exercitum Sennacheribi, à Grotio in- telligi. Sed perseverat adhuc Propheta in VÆ de- nunciando Hierosolymæ: ideoq; ut illud תדברי v. 4. ita etiam תפקד, pro fœminino secundæ per- sonæ merito habetur ab Oecolampadio, Osiandro, & aliis: à Domino Deo exercituum VISITABERIS in tonitru, & commotione (terræ) & voce magna (id est, horribilibus tonitruis, phrasi Ebræa) turbinis & tem- pestatis, & flamma ignis devorantis, id est, interprete Osiandro: Excidium urbis Jerosolymitanæ erit vo- bis instar horrendæ tempestatis: ubi ingens ventus, vel turbo potius tecta dejicit, arbores radicitus evel- lit: & insequitur grando, obvia quæq; prosternens: audiunturque tanta tonitrua, ut terra concutiatur, trematq;, & incidant in ædes fulgura, quæ momento eas accendant, & funestum incendium, quod restin- gui nequeat, excitent. Menochius Vulgatæ, quæ red- dit, visitabitur, insistens, intelligit quidem de turba & multitudine hostium cum Corn. à Lapide, sed de Chaldæis explicat: Tirinus tamen de Ariel vel Je- rusalem hic sermonem esse agnoscit, ut & Vatablus ac Leo Castrius. Quæ sententia cum nostra, quan- tum ad sensum vaticinii, convenit. Vers. 7. ET ERIT SICVT SOMNIVM VISIONIS NOCTVRNÆ MVLTITVDO OMNIVM GENTIVM.) Ita subito evanescet. Par levibus ventis, volucriq; simillima somno. Non desunt, qui hæc itidem ad comminatio- nes Judæis factas referant: quæ cumprimis Calvini est explicatio: Objurgat, inquit, Judæos, eorum- que pervicaciam arguit, quod Deum, minasque omnes secure contemnerent. Idemq; aptissima si- militudine in falsam eorum fiduciam & securita- tem invehitur, dum repente & inopinato adventu- ros hostes denunciat, ubi Judæi se tranquilla pace frui, & longe ab omni periculo abeffe existima- bunt, & rem adeo subitam & inopinatam fore, ut somnium esse videatur. Quamvis igitur nunc per- petuam quietem animo concipias, inquit, Deus te facile excitabit, & securitatem tibi istam excutiet. Salfe autem Propheta Judæos somniare dicit, quia suis delitiis immersi nihil vident, aut sentiunt: sed mente obruta & attonita beatitudinem sibi fingunt ex stupore. Unde colligit, subito, quasi per somni- um venturos hostes, qui dormientibus terrorem incutient, sicuti sæpe contingit, dulcem & jucun- dum soporem diris insomniis turbari; unde sequi- tur, blandicias, quibus indormiunt, fore illis inuti- les: quia utcunque nihil cogitent, subito tamen obrepet commotio. Sed contorta est Calvini in- terpretatio: Nam in textu multitudo GEN- TIUM dimicantium contra Sion dicitur esse instar somniantium. Rectius ergo alii de hostibus hæc explicant. Quanquam vero nonnulli cum Junio in- satiabilem hostium Tyrannidem solum innui pu- tent, quæ etiam Belgarum est sententia, præferen- da tamen omnino eorum explicatio, qui hic con- solationem adferri fidelibus censent: quod hostes si- miles reddendi sint somniantibus, ubi frustrabitur eos Dominus, cum pene voti compotes esse vide- buntur. A qua explicatione non est, cur disceda- mus. Nam priusquam graviora mala prædiceren- tur, Judæis, ob eorum indurationem, eventura, erigendi erant etiam aliqua consolatione pii, ut plerumque in more habent Prophetæ. Quemad- modum esurientes & sitientes videntur sibi in somnis edere & bibere: expergefacti vero nihilominus esu- riunt & sitiunt, & vident, nil nisi somnium fuisse. Ita impii, hostes Ecclesiæ Dei, magna cupiditate ani- mi hoc agunt, ut Ecclesiam devorent, eamque totam absorbeant: & quia Dominus illis ad tempus prospe- ros successus largitur, exultant illi supra modum. Sed ista ipsorum temporaria felicitas non est nisi quod- dam somnium. Paulo enim post excutitur illis Domi- nium & Tyrannis: restituitur populus Dei suæ liber- tati & pristinæ felicitati: ipsi vero misere pereunt, & pejus habent, quam unquam antea. Quæ inter- pretatio plerisque placuit. Atq; ita concludi existi- mamus priorem prædictionem de obsessione Chal- dæorum. Quanquam vero verba eadem Luc. 19, 13. à Christo de obsidione per Vespasianum facta adhi- beantur, quæ hic v. 3. leguntur, non tamen eam hoc in loco prædictam fuisse ideo putandum est, quum id tantum indicarir Christus, similem fore obsidio- nem novissimam priori, neque minorem anxietatem, qua à Romanis afficientur. Nam consolatio hæc 7. & 8. commate subjuncta, magis congruit priori vastationi & cladi, è qua iterum eluctati Judæi sunt, quam novissimæ. Sed quum id quoque prævideat Esaias, haud meliores evasuros Judæos post libe- rationem, imo tandem animum suum induraturos, ac doctrinam Evangelicam de Christo prorsus re- probaturos, idcirco S. S. dictitante vaticinatur nunc in altera capitis parte v. 9. & seqq. de eorum re- jectione, & gentium assumtione: OBSTUPESCITE ET ADMIRAMINI, FLUCTUATE ET VACILLATE. Vel ut in Ebr. habetur: Tardi & stupidi estote, ex- cæcate vos ipsos, & cæci estote, id est, eritis tales, & vos ita excæcabitis. INEBRIAMINI, ET NON A VINO, MOVEAMINI (titubate temulentorum in- star) ET NON AB EBRIETATE. Quod sub adven- tum Messiæ impletum est: siquidem Judæi neque conciones ejus admiserint, neque miracula atten- derint, utut illustrissima, adeo stupidi, cæcique e- rant: & ad conciones Christi & Apostolorum se- se habebant, ut temulenti, qui vino onusti hinc in- de titubant, neque pedibus insistere possunt, ne- sciuntq; quid dicatur, vel agatur. Ebrii enim in do- ctrina Pharisaica, & curis atque voluptatibus hujus seculi, non animadvertebant, neq; curabant, quid Christus, ejusq; discipuli dicant, aut faciant. Nulli, inquam, tempori aptius hæc congruunt, quam no- vissimæ Judæorum ætati sub adventum Christi. Et explicat hæc, quæ vers. 10. subjunguntur, QUO- NIAM MISCUIT VOBIS DOMINUS SPIRI- TUM SOPORIS, Paulus ipse Rom. 11, 8. de Ju- dæis sui temporis. Tum PROPHETAS ET PRINCIPES IPSORUM, QUI VIDENT, VI- SIONE OPERUIT DOMINUS, nempe vela- mine caliginis, sive quod sensu Prophetarum San- ctorum ipsis velato, 2. Cor.3, 14. sive quod Phari- sæorum & falsorum Prophetarum doctrina im- primis excœcati, atq; oculi ipsorum operti fuerint, utpote qui exSpiritu mendacii & erroris falsa pro- phetabant. CONTEXIT tenebris Prophetas & præcipuos vestros concionatores, exponit Brentius. Summi enim Pontifices, Sacerdotes, Scribæ, Pha- risæi, & qui aliis docendis præfecti erant,Seniores item & Magistratus populi (primores populi hic compellari censet Grotius) ad Evangelium Chri- sti plane cæci erant. Et quem dabimus certiorem interpretem, quam ipsummet Christum, qui hoc vaticinium expresse de Judæis,Pharisæis,ac Docto- ribus populi suo tempore exposuit: ac de iis hic va- ticinatum esse Prophetam disertis verbis testatus est, Matth.15, 7. Hypocritæ, bene prophetavit de vo- bis Esaias, dicens: Populus hic labiis me honorat; Cor autem eorum longe est à me; sine causa autem colunt me, docentes doctrinas & mandata hominum. Quæ è v. 13. hujus capitis desumta sunt. Et cùm de Judæorum excæcatione loquitur Christus,ac gen- tium illuminationem prædicit Joh. 11, 39. In judi- cium veni in hunc mundum, ut qui non vident, vi- deant, & qui vident, cæci fiant, quid aliud indicat, quam quod hic per Prophetam insinuatur, quod Judæis eversio futura sit, sicut verba libri obsigna- ti, gentes autem surdæ verba libri audituræ,& ocu- li cæci visuri sint v. 11. & 18. Neq; citra causam hoc cumprimis loco ad confundendam sapientiam se- culi usus est Apostolus 1. Cor. 1. quod sapientiam cœlestem Evangelii respuat; quia sc. de Judæis sui temporis, ejusque generis prædictum hoc in loco, quod cœlestis sapientia ipsis scandalo sit futura,ut- pote justo Dei judicio excæcatis atque induratis. Deniq; quum v. 17. de conversione gentilium non minus,quam de excæcatione Judæorum agat: nul- lum dubium superesse potest, quin hæc ad tempo- ra N. T. pertineant: de quo etiam inter plerosque Interpp. Christianos est consensus. Sed videamus jam glossas Grotianas in residuam capitis partem.

## 29:8
Verse 8.

— AND AS A HUNGRY MAN DREAMS AND EATS, BUT WHEN HE HAS AWAKENED, HIS SOUL IS EMPTY) That is, he himself. Hopes are the dreams of those who are awake.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

— ET SICUT SOMNIAT ESURIENS ET COME- DIT, CUM AUTEM FUERIT EXPERGEFACTUS, VACUA EST ANIMA EJUS) Id est ipse. Spes, sunt vigilantium somnia.

## 29:9
Verse 9. BE ASTONISHED AND WONDER) He addresses the leaders of the Jews, who, measuring all their things by human prudence, did not believe those things would come to pass which Isaiah was predicting.

BE DRUNK AND NOT WITH WINE) In the Hebrew there is a change of person: They are drunk, and not with wine. The Hebrews often do this, so that they speak of the same men now in the second, now in the third person. They wonder at what I say, and do not believe, therefore they do not understand.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OBSTUPESCITE ET ADMIRAMINI) Ju- dæorum primores alloquitur, qui cuncta sua humana pru- dentia metientes, non credebant ea futura, quæ prædice- bat Esaias.

INEBRIAMINI ET NON VINO) In Hebræo est mutatio personæ: Ebrii sunt, & non vino. Sæpe hoc faciunt Hebræi, ut de iisdem hominibus modo in secunda, modo in tertia persona loquantur. Mirantur, quæ dico, & non credunt, ideo nec intelligunt.

## 29:10
Verse 10. PROPHETS) Those who spoke not from God, but from themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 10. PROPHETAS) Illos, qui non à Deo, sed à se- metipsis loquebantur.

## 29:11
Verse 11. AND THE VISION OF ALL SHALL BE TO YOU) My prediction concerning so many and such great things will be to you as a closed book, or as an open book, but to one who does not know letters.

We judge that it is evident from the above that not only some small part of Isaiah's prediction is being referred to, whether concerning the expedition of Sennacherib against the city of Jerusalem, or concerning the miraculous liberation from the hand of the same, but whatever other Prophets had predicted at all, and especially the divine promises themselves concerning the Messiah, as being the A & Ω, the beginning and the end of the Prophetic predictions of the Old Testament. Therefore these things are said universally concerning the VISION OF ALL: Certainly those visions cannot be excluded, for which primarily the oracles were made to the Prophets, and for whose sake all other things were revealed, John 5:39, Acts 10:43, 2 Tim. 3:15. In the understanding of which the Jews especially wandered from the divine mind, nay, were clearly blind, especially during those times in which they were obtaining their fulfillment, concerning which Isaiah predicted that the wisdom of any of the wisest of this age would be confounded, which the Apostle interpreted concerning the mystery of the cross, 1 Cor. 1. For in these things ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν, in these things the veil remains upon the reading of the Old Testament, not being uncovered, which is done away in Christ, 2 Cor. 3:14. Rightly therefore here the Blessed Luther, f. 344: The vision of all, that is, all the prophecies, of which you boast, will be as a sealed book, that is, by your impiety you will bring it about that you close the whole Scripture to yourselves. As we see in the Jews today. Who, although they have the clearest Scriptures concerning the coming of Christ, by which they are said to be convinced and to confess that Christ has come. And although they see that a good part of the world follows this faith, yet they alone neither accept him, nor believe that he has come. Thus the book remains closed to them, which they do not understand, not because of a fault in the Scripture, that it is obscure, but because of a fault in the readers, who bring blind eyes.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET ERIT VOBIS VISIO OMNIUM)Mea de tot ac tantis rebus prædictio vobis erit, ut liber clausus, aut ut liber apertus, sed literas nescienti.

Non respici tantum prædictionis Esaiæ parti- culam aliquam, sive de expeditione Sennacheribi ad- versus urbem Hierosolymam, seu de liberatione mi- mi- raculosa à manu ejusdem, sed quicquid quid alii Prophetæ omnino prædixerant, ipsasque imprimis divinas promissiones de Messia, utpote quæ A & Ω, principium & finis sunt prædictionum Propheticarum Vet. Testamenti, è superioribus patere arbitramur. Ideo ita dicuntur hæc universa- liter de VISIONE OMNIUM: Excludi certe non possunt illæ visiones, ob quas πρώτως ad Pro- phetas oracula facta sunt, & quorum causa cætera omnia revelata sunt, Joh. 5, 39. Act. 10, 43. 2. Tim. 3, 15. In quarum intelligentia imprimis à mente di- vina aberrarunt, imo cæci plane fuêre Judæi, ma- xime sub ista tempora, quibus illæ complementum suum nanciscebantur, circa quas sapientiam quo- rumvis sapientissimorum hujus seculi confusum iri prædixit Esaias, quod de mysterio crucis Aposto- lus interpretatus est 1. Cor. 1. In his enim ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν, in his τὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀνα- γνώσει τῆς παλαᾷς διαθήκης μένει, μὴ ἀνακαλυπ- τόμενον, ὅ, τι ἐν χριστῷ καταργεῖται 2. Cor. 3, 14. Recte ergo hic B. Lutherus f. 344. Omnium visio, hoc est, omnium Prophetiæ, de quibus gloriamini, e- runt ceu liber obsignatus, id est, per vestram impieta- tem hoc efficietis, ut vobis claudatis totam Scripturam. Sicut videmus in Judæis hodie. Qui cum habeant cla- rissimas Scripturas de Christi adventu, quibus convicti fateri dicuntur Christum venisse. Cumq́; videant, bo- nam orbis partem hanc fidem sequi, tamen soli neque accipiunt eum, nec credunt eum venisse. Sic manet eis clausus liber, quem non intelligunt, non vitio Scripturæ, quod obscura sit, sed vitio lectorum, qui cæcos ocu- los afferunt.

## 29:13
AND THEY FEARED ME BY THE COMMANDMENT OF MEN AND DOCTRINES.) In the Hebrew: The worship with which they worship me is a commandment which men teach. Men, namely, not instituted by God, who place the worship of God in mere rites without the amendment of the soul. Such teachers were the false prophets of those times.

Christ, the best interpreter, applies this not to the false prophets in the time of Isaiah, but to the Pharisees and lawyers of his own time, and testifies that these things were predicted by the Prophet, Matt. 15, who, although they were instituted by God through Moses and the Prophets, yet being devoted above all to their own traditions, they neglected that which was chief in the law and the prophets, and were concerned primarily with external rites. Whence Cyril rightly says of them: Since they had despised Christ the pedagogue, and having deemed the law of God worthy of no place, had turned to the doctrines and commandments of men, hence most justly the book of the divinely inspired scriptures was sealed. For it was not consistent that those who held it in contempt should be enriched with the knowledge of Scripture.

Latin:

ET TIMVERVNT ME MANDATO HOMI- NUM ET DOCTRINIS.) In Hebræo: Cultus, quo me co- lunt, est præceptum, quod homines docent. Homines, nem- pe à Deo non instituti, qui in nudis ritibẹ sine animi emen- datione, cultum Dei collocant. Tales Doctores erant falsi illorum temporum Prophetæ.

Non ad falsos Prophetas tempore Esaiæ, sed ad Pharisæos & legisperitos sui temporis hæc ap- plicat Christus, interpres optimus, & de illis præ- dicta esse à Propheta testatur Matth. 15. qui etsi à Deo per Mosen & Prophetas instituti erant, suis tamen traditionibus dediti imprimis, id quod præ- cipuum erat in lege ac Prophetis, negligebant, & de externis ritibus potissimum soliciti erant. Un- de recte de illis Cyrillus: Cum pædagogum Christum contemsissent, & legem Dei nullo loco dignati ad do- ctrinas & mandata hominum conversi fuissent, hinc justissime divinitus inspiratæ scripturæ liber obsigna- tus est. Non enim consentaneum erat cognitione Scri- pturæ ditari eos, qui illam despectui haberent.

## 29:14
Vers. 14. THE WISDOM OF HIS WISE MEN SHALL PERISH.) Those crafty ones who agitate counsels, whether concerning summoning the Egyptians or making a surrender to the Assyrian, will profit nothing.

THE UNDERSTANDING OF HIS PRUDENT MEN SHALL BE HIDDEN) The Greeks in the active voice: I will hide the understanding of the prudent. Other interpretations have had I will set aside, in which way the Apostle cites it, 1 Cor. 1, 19, and Justin in his dialogue with Trypho.

Nothing of such counsels is found either in this text or in the history of the siege of Jerusalem. For it is not read that Hezekiah's counselors agitated or undertook such counsels. Therefore those comments are peculiar to Grotius, that these things are to be understood of the Pharisees and others who, by the persuasion of wisdom, rejected Christ, the true wisdom of God; we are certain of this from the interpretation of Christ and the Apostle, Matt. 15, 1 Cor. 1; whence the marginal gloss of the blessed Luther on this passage fits perfectly: for the word of the cross makes them all blind, mad, and foolish, when they hear that through the works of the law no one is made righteous before God, that one must kill the old man and condemn him, through the Word of the Spirit, which rebukes the world for the sake of sin, John 16:8. And thus Cyril explained it in the Greek Church. The LXX have διὰ τἳτο ἰδὲ πϱοσθήσω ἳ μεταθεῖναι τὸν λαὸν τἳτον, καὶ μεταθήσω αὐτὸς, καὶ ἀ- πολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν, καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν κϱύψω. Therefore behold I will again transfer this people, and I will transfer them: And I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and hide the intelligence of the intelligent. Regarding which words Cyril says: For the Jewish people were as if transported, in many ways, as it seems to me. For it was called the lot of God and his portion and his cord, but it was transferred in a certain way. For it was no longer called his lot, but it became the portion of foxes, and was given as food to Satan and unclean spirits. But it was transferred from a right sense to a reprobate mind, from glory to ignominy, from strength to weakness, from wisdom to extreme folly. For I will destroy, he says, the wisdom of the wise, and I will hide the intelligence of the intelligent. The scribes and Pharisees indeed seemed wise, and very prudent, having obtained the reputation of knowledge of the law: but it was hidden by God, and the intelligence of the wise, i.e., the law or the divinely inspired scripture, was all but constricted. Similarly, in the Latin Church, Jerome, explaining the Jews who accepted the traditions of the Pharisees and Scribes, and thus chose Barabbas and rejected the Lord, says: Therefore, he says, he threatens that he will add, according to the Septuagint, that he will by no means transfer them to the Assyrians and Babylonians, but will scatter them throughout the whole world. According to the Hebrew, he says that he will perform a great wonder and a stupendous miracle for the people of the Jews, so that he may destroy the wisdom of those who did not receive the power of God, and the wisdom of God, and hide and conceal the intellect of the prudent, so that, namely, they might not find him who is contained in the letter. Writing to the Corinthians about this passage, the Apostle Paul placed the testimony, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will reject the intellect of the prudent, explaining the same sense in other words, not that God is an enemy of wisdom, of which He is the Father, and through whom all wisdom is in men: But he placed it with the addition, as it is in the Hebrew, of the wise of the people, and of its prudent ones, that is, of the Jewish people. And in truth, God performed a great miracle among the people after the coming of the Lord Savior, so that at one and the same time Jerusalem burned, and the temple collapsed, and all the knowledge of the masters was taken away. Justin, here praised by Grotius, understood these things no differently than as concerning the Jews in the time of the New Testament, Dial. with Trypho, p. 193. All these things which I have brought forward, I relate through digressions among you, so that at last, having faith in those words uttered by God against you, that you are foolish children, and that I will therefore add to him, so that I may transfer this people, etc., you may cease to seduce both yourselves and those who were listening to you, and begin to learn from us, whom the grace of God has rendered wise. And p. 189, but you are of a hard heart, and a foolish people, and blind, and lame, and you are children in whom there is no faith, just as he himself says, honoring him only with their lips, while being far removed from him in their heart, and teaching your own doctrine, not his.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PERIBIT SAPIENTIA A SAPIENTIBUS EJUS.) Nihil proficient versuti illi, qui agitant consilia, sive de acciendis Ægyptiis, sive de deditione Assyrio facienda.

INTELLECTUS PRUDENTIUM EJUS AB- SCONDETUR) Græci in activo τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν κρύψω. Aliæ interpretationes habuêre ἀθετήσω, quomodo citat Apostolus 1. Cor. 1, 19. & Justinus colloquio cum Tryphone.

Nihil talium consiliorum vel in hoc textu, vel in historia de obsidione Hierosolymæ habetur. Non enim leguntur ejusmodi consilia agitasse, vel suscepisse Hiskiæ consiliarii. Commenta ergo il- la sunt Grotio propria, de Pharisæis, & aliis, qui sa- pientiæ persuasione Christum veram Dei sapientiam reprobarunt, hæc accipienda esse, è Christi & Apo- stolica interpretatione Matth. 15. 1. Cor. 1. certi su- mus; unde optime congruit B. Lutheri glossa mar- ginalis ad h. l. denn das Wort des Creußes machet sie alle blind, toll und thöricht, wenn sie hören, daß durch des Gesetzes Werck niemand für Gott gerecht werde, daß man den alten Menschen tödten und verdammen muͤsse, durch das Wort des Geistes, welcher die Welt straffet um der Suͤnde willen, Joh. 16, 8. Atque ita exposuit in Græca Ecclesia Cyrillus. LXX. habent διὰ τἳτο ἰδὲ πϱοσθήσω ἳ μεταθεῖναι τὸν λαὸν τἳτον, καὶ μεταθήσω αὐτὸς, καὶ ἀ- πολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν, καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν κϱύψω. Propter hoc ecce rursus transferam populum istum, & transferam illos: Et perdam sa- pientiam sapientum & intelligentiam intelligentium abscondam. Ad quæ verba hæc Cyrillus: Transpor- tatus enim veluti erat Judaicus populus, multis, ut mihi videtur, modis. Nam vocabatur sors Dei & portio ejus & funiculus, at translatus est quodammo- do. Non enim ultra appellatus est ejus sors, sed vul- pium portio factus est, & Satanæ immundisq́; spiriti- bus in cibum datus. Verum translatus est à recto sen- su in mentem reprobam, a gloria in ignominiam, a fortitudine in infirmitatem, à sapientia in extremam stultitiam. Perdam enim, inquit, sapientiam sapien- tum, & intelligentiam intelligentium abscondam. Videbantur nimirum scribæ & Pharisæi sapientes, & valde cordati scientiæ legis opinionem consequuti: at à Deo abscondita est, & tantum non coarctata sapien- tum intelligentia, i. e. lex seu scriptura divinitus inspi- rata. Similiter in Latina Ecclesia Hieron. de Ju- dæis, qui traditiones Pharisæorum Scribarumq́; su- sceperunt, adeoq́; elegerunt Barrabam, & Dominum respuerunt, explicans: Propterea, inquit, additu- rum se esse comminatur, juxta Septuaginta, ut nequa- quam in Assyrios & Babylonios eos transferat, sed in toto orbe dispergat. Juxta Hebraicum, admiratio- nem magnam populo Judæorum stupendumq́; mira- culum facturum se esse dicit, ut perdat eorum sapien- tiam, qui non receperunt Dei virtutem, Deiq́; sapien- tiam, & intellectum prudentium abscondat & celet, ne scil. eum reperiant, qui in litera continetur. De hoc loco Apostolus Paulus scribens ad Corinthios, po- suit testimonium, perdam sapientiam sapientum, & intellectum prudentium reprobabo, aliis verbis eun- dem edifferens sensum, non quod Deus sit inimicus sa- pientiæ, cujus Pater est, & per quem omnis est in hominibus sapientia: Sed cum additamento posuit, ut in Hebraico est, sapientium populi, & prudentium illius, id est, populi Judæorum. Et revera grande miraculum Deus fecit in populo post adventum Do- mini Salvatoris, ut uno eodemque tempore arderet Hierusalem, templumque corrueret, & omnis magi- strorum scientia tolleretur. Nec aliter, quam de Judæis tempore N. T. intellexit hæc Justinus, hic à Grotio laudatus Dial. cum Tryphon. p. 193. Ista o- mnia, quæ protuli, per digressiones apud vos refero, ut aliquando tandem verbis illis à Deo contra vos prola- tis fidem habentes, vos filios insipientes esse, & illi pro- pterea apponam, ut transferam populum hunc &c. definatis & vos ipsos, & eos, qui vos audebant seduce- re, & à nobis discere incipiatis, quos gratia Dei sa- pientes reddidit. Et p. 189. vos autem duro corde, & insipiens populus, & cæcus, & claudus, & filii e- stis, quibus non est fides cum ipsis, quemadmodum ipse ait, labiis tantum illum honorantes, corde longe ab eo remoti, ac propriam vestram, non illius docentes doctrinam.

## 29:15
Verse 15. THAT YOU MAY HIDE COUNSEL FROM THE LORD) Because you deceive men, you seem to hope that God also can be deceived by you.

Latin:

Vers. 15. VT A DOMINO ABSCONDATIS CONSILIVM) Quia homines fallitis, sperare videmini etiam Deum à vobis falli posse.

## 29:16
LET IT THINK AND SAY) Let it think so that it may say. It is a prosopopoeia, which attributes sense to clay.

TO ITS MAKER: YOU DID NOT MAKE ME) To its maker, he did not make me.

IT DOES NOT UNDERSTAND) It did not understand: namely, how the earthen vessel ought to be made.

Latin:

COGITET ET DICAT) Cogitet ut dicat. Est πϱοσωποποιΐα, quæ luto sensum affingit.

FACTORI SVO: NON FECISTI ME) De facto- re suo, non fecit me.

NON INTELLIGIT) Non intellexit: nempe quo- modo fictile fieri debeat.

## 29:17
Verse 17. LEBANON SHALL BE TURNED INTO CARMEL.) Into level fields, which is often said to be signified by the word כרמל taken commonly: The sense is: The lofty, such as the Assyrians were, shall be cast down,

AND CARMEL SHALL BE RECKONED AS A FOREST.) That is, level fields shall be raised into the appearance of mountains. The most afflicted Hebrews shall become victors.

Grotius persists in his gloss about the Assyrians. But just as the preceding parts taught that the discourse is about the time of the New Testament, about the blinding of the Jews, so it will not be obscure that the times of the New Testament are likewise looked to in those things which follow, if they are weighed a little more accurately. Therefore, the interpreters, with excellent consensus, have interpreted this conversion of Lebanon and Carmel as concerning the calling of the Gentiles and the rejection of the Jews, about which the consequences also treat; although they have not declared the meaning of Lebanon and Carmel in the same way. Most think that fertility and sterility are to be attended to: But they assign the latter to Mount Lebanon, and the former to Carmel: in which manner Osiander says: Carmel, he says, was a most fertile mountain; but Lebanon was a forest, consisting only of trees, and those unfruitful ones. The Prophet therefore wishes to say: In a short time there will be a great change of things. For those who seemed unfruitful among the people of God, namely sinners, publicans, harlots, will acknowledge Christ, will do penance, and will bear the best fruits of true faith: but the Pharisees and the rest of the hypocrites, who seemed full of holiness and good works, will be discovered to be unfruitful trees, haughty, and breathing only Pharisaic pride and persecution against the truly pious. Similarly, Piscator and the Belgian Paraphrasts understand that the wild spirits of the Gentiles will be fertile like Carmel, and the Jews, who seemed fertile to themselves, will be like the forest of Lebanon, and will be wild. Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, and Menochius also made this their own explanation: Lebanon, that is, the sterile and uncultivated Gentiles will be fertile in good works through the faith and grace of Christ: And conversely Carmel, that is, the field previously fertile, namely The Jews, formerly abounding in holy Patriarchs, Prophets, and other upright men, will be sterile, and will degenerate into an unfruitful and uncultivated thicket. This exposition is favored by the fact that Carmel is celebrated in the Holy Scriptures as a fertile and fruit-bearing place, and is known to be of Judea, because it is a mountain of Judea, and a fertile one at that (Jer. 2:7). A forest, however, designates heathendom (Is. 32:15), and Lebanon is a mountain in Phoenicia, which was inhabited by the Gentiles. Thus Cyril: Lebanon is a mountain of Phoenicia, and those who dwelt in it and around it were most superstitious men. Similarly also Chermel, or Chermelus, was the greatest mountain in the region of the Jews, in which Elias the Tishbite is said to have dwelt. Therefore, by mountains or regions in which there are mountains, he wishes to signify those who dwell in them, and says: Lebanon shall be transferred, that is to say, transformed, and shall be as Mount Chermel; but Mount Chermel as Lebanon, that is, those who formerly served idols will acknowledge the God who is worshipped in Judea, and will be reckoned in the number and class of the firstborn of Israel. Those who are of the seed of Israel will at some time be like those inhabiting Lebanon and wandering. For Israel has been cast out from the union which is with God, on account of their impiety toward Christ. The Gentiles have also been taken up and sanctified by the Spirit, and have been made partakers of the divine nature. Therefore, he says, Lebanon shall be transferred as Mount Chermel; but Mount Chermel shall be reckoned as a forest, that is, as a forest of wild trees, whose end is combustion. Thus Jerome also refers Lebanon to the people of the Gentiles, and the temple to the Jews, but with a different explanation of the names; namely, that the Gentiles, washed in the Lord, have been whitened, and that the Jews have the knowledge of circumcision. Others invert these things, namely, that Lebanon was a beautiful and fertile forest, and for that reason the Jews formerly flourished under the Old Testament, but on account of the rejection of the Gospel they will be like a field, or an unfruitful plain; but concerning the nations, let the contrary be brought forth: which is the exposition of the Weimar paraphrase, in favor of which it makes that Lebanon is used for the temple of Jerusalem, Zach. 11, 1: either because the temple was built from the trees of Lebanon, namely the most beautiful cedars, to which Blessed Luther nods in a marginal gloss, or because from the brightness and whiteness, whence this name has clung to Mount Lebanon on account of the snows whitening on its peaks throughout the whole year, being conspicuous from afar for its most white marble stones, it was so named. Which is the opinion of Arias Montanus. Others, however, think that the whole of Judea, not only the temple, is understood by Lebanon, the northern boundary of Judea, Zach. 11, 1. Conf. Tarnov. in Comment. on that place. And in that way Blessed Luther also interpreted it: Lebanon, i.e. Jerusalem, which has the Priesthood and the kingdom like trees, will be turned into a field, and the field, i.e., the nations, will be taken up into the people of God, in place of the Jews. Mr. Brentius wishes the fertility of both places to be designated, because all things in the Kingdom of Christ are alone joyful and fertile: Although others interpret this differently (the words of Brentius are), nevertheless because this discourse is about the kingdom of Christ on earth, it must be understood according to the conditions of this kingdom. Lebanon is a mountain noble for its tallest cedars: Carmel, however, is a mountain celebrated for the fertility of its wine. At what time, therefore, Christ will arrive, Lebanon will be turned into Carmel, and Carmel in turn into Lebanon, that is, all things will be cultivated, fertile, and blessed in the kingdom of Christ. Lebanon indeed has cedars fit for building, but it lacks vines and olives. Carmel has many vines and olives, but it lacks Cedars. When, therefore, Christ will receive his kingdom, there will be such a blessing of things that Lebanon will bring forth vines together with cedars, and Carmel will bring forth cedars together with vines. The same opinion is also stated later in chapter 32: The desert is in Carmel, and Carmel will be reckoned as a forest, i.e., Lebanon. And chapter 35: The deserts will rejoice, and the glory of Lebanon has been given to it, the beauty of Carmel and Sharon. Which sentences differ only in the manner of explaining, but as to the sense they all agree in this, that here the discourse is about the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the nations. Nevertheless, the explanation of Osiander seems to be preferred, which is also that of Theodoret and Procopius, provided that a forest or wood is gentility, and Judea is designated by the name Carmel on account of its fertility, Is. 32, 15: until the Spirit is poured out upon you, and the desert will be in Carmel, and Carmel will be reckoned as a forest. Where Blessed Luther rendered this explanation: The desert, that is, the remnant of the Jews, and the nations will be like a most cultivated field: They will bear most abundant fruits in the faith of Christ, And Carmel, that is, the Synagogue, which now flourishes, will be reduced to a forest, and will be desolated. Those who accept it concerning the devastation of Lebanon and Carmel, in this sense, that Lebanon will be cut down, and will be despoiled of its cedars, not unlike a field, and Carmel, now best cultivated and fertile, will here be uncultivated and neglected, so that with shrubs and thickets springing up here and there it acquires the appearance of a wood, is forced to explain the word Carmel in a diverse and contrary way, now for a despoiled field, now for a cultivated and fertile place, and they do not attain the force of the Prophetic phraseology, and they depart clearly from the Scope of the prophecy. But that these things are said to be about to happen in a short time and in a little while, even if they were to happen only at the advent of the Savior, most people after Jerome explain it thus: that from the times of Isaiah until the dispensation of the flesh assumed, a short and small space of time intervened for the comparison of eternity: not inconveniently, however, our Brentius observes that that short and small time is not to be estimated from the time when Isaiah preached these things, but when those things which he had said before were to be fulfilled, and when Christ was to be born. The gloss of Grotius, however, is clearly unheard of until now: For Grotius has not yet shown that by the word Carmel only the plain of fields, and by metaphor a depression, is designated: nor could any place be brought forward where by FOREST or WOOD height and elation in the appearance of a mountain, and metaphorically victory, had been indicated.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONVERTETVR LIBANVS IN CHAR- MEL.) In agros planos, quod significari voce כרמל com- pari muniter sumta sæpe dictum est: Sensus est: Sublimes, qua- les erant Assyrii, dejicientur,

ET CHARMEL IN SALTVM REPVTABITVR.) Id est, agri plani attollentur in montium speciem. Hebræi afflictissimi fient victores.

Persistit Grotius in glossa sua de Assyriis. Sed uti antecedentia docuêre, de tempore Nov. Testam. sermonem esse, de excæcatione Judæorum, ita in his, quæ sequuntur, itidem N. T. tempora respi- ci, haud obscurum erit, si ea paulo accuratius ex- pendantur. Proinde Interpp. consensu eximio hanc conversionem Libani, & Carmeli de vocatione gentium & Judæorum rejectione interpretati sunt, de qua etiam consequentia agunt; quanquam non eo- dem modo Libani & Carmeli significationem de- clararint. Pleriq; fertilitatem & sterilitatem atten- di censent: Sed hanc monti Libano, illam vero Car- melo assignant: quo pacto Osiander: Carmelus, in- quit, erat mons fertilissimus; Libanus vero erat sal- tus, tantum ex arboribus, iisq; infrugiferis constans. Vult igitur Propheta dicere: Brevi magna erit re- rum commutatio. Qui enim in populo Dei videban- tur infrugiferi, nimirum peccatores, publicani, me- retrices, & Christum agnoscent, pœnitentiam agent, & fructus optimos veræ fidei ferent: Pharisæi vero & reliqui hypocritæ, qui videbantur pleni sanctitatis & bonorum operum, deprehendentur arbores infru- giferæ, elatæ, & tantum spirantes superbiam Phari- saicam, & persecutionem adversus vere pios. Simi- liter Piscator & Paraphr. Belgici, feros animos gen- tium fertiles instar Carmeli, & Judæos, qui sibi fer- tiles videbantur, instar saltus Libani, efferos futu- ros intelligunt. Explicationem etiam hanc suam fecere Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus & Menochius: Li- banus, id est, steriles & incultæ gentes erunt fertiles bonorum operum per fidem & gratiam Christi: Et è converso Charmel, id est, ager ante fertilis, scil. Ju- dæi, olim S. Patriarchis, Prophetis & aliis viris pro- bis abundantes, erunt steriles, & in saltum infrugife- rum & incultum degenerabunt. Cui expositioni fa- vet, quod Carmel, ceu locus ferax & frugifer cele- bretur in S. literis, ac Judææ nota sit, quia mons est Judææ, isque fertilis Jer. 2, 7. Sylva vero genti- litatem designet Es. 32, 15. ac Libanus mons sit in Phœnicia, qui à gentibus habitabatur. Ita Cyril- lus: Libanus mons est Phœnicia, quiq; in ipso & cir- ca ipsum habitarunt, erant homines quam supersti- tiosissimi. Similiter etiam Chermel, vel Chermelus, mons erat in regionem Judæorum maximus, in quo ha- bitasse dicitur Elias Thesbita. Itaque per montes seu regiones, in quibus sunt montes, significare vult eos, qui in illis habitant, & inquit: Transferetur, nimi- rum transmutabitur Libanus, eritque velut mons Chermelinus: mons autem Chermelinus velut Liba- nus, id est, qui quondam idolis servierunt, Deum, qui adoratur in Judæa, agnoscent, & in numero clas- seque primogeniti Israëlis reputabuntur. Qui ex se- mine Israëlis sunt, erunt aliquando similes inhabitan- tibus Libanum & errantibus. Ejectus enim est Is- raël à conjunctione, quæ est cum Deo, propter impie- tatem in Christum. Assumtæ sunt etiam gentes, & sanctificatæ per spiritum, divinæ naturæ factæ sunt participes. Transferetur igitur Libanus, inquit, velut mons Chermel: mons vero Chermel, ut sylva reputabitur, id est, ut sylva lignorum agrestium, quorum finis est combustio. Ita Hieronymus refert etiam Libanum ad populum gentium, templum vero ad Judæos, sed alia nominum explicatione; quod nempe gentes lotæ in Domino dealbatæ sint, quodque Judæi circumcisionis scientiam habeant. Alii hæc in- vertunt, quod nempe Libanus fuerit sylva pulchra atq; fertilis, eaq; ratione olim floruerint Judæi sub V. T. sed propter Evangelii rejectionem futuri sint instar agri, vel campi infrugiferi; de gentibus vero contrarium efferatur: quæ expositio est Vinarien- sis paraphraseos, pro qua facit, quod Libanus pro templo Hierosolymitano Zach. 11, 1. usurpetur: sive quod ex arboribus Libani, cedris nempe pulcher- rimis exstructum fuerit templum, quibus annuit B. Lutherus in glossa marginali, sive quod à cando- re & albedine, unde monti Libano, propter nives in culminibus per totum annum albicantes, no- men hoc hæserit, longissime ob lapides marmo- reos candidissimos conspicuo, ita nuncupatum fue- rit. Quæ Ariæmontani est sententia. Totam ta- men Judæam, non solum templum per Libanum, terminum Judææ aquilonarem Zach. 11, 1. intelli- gi alii putant. Conf. Tarnov. in Comment. ad istum locum. Atque ea ratione interpretatus etiam est B. Lutherus: Libanus, h. e. Jerusalem, quæ habet Sa- cerdotium & regnum ceu arbores, convertetur in a- grum, & ager, h. e. gentes assumentur in populum Dei, loco Judæorum. Dn. Brentius utriusq; loci fertili- tatem designari vult, quod omnia in Regno Christi solum sint læta & fertilia: Etsi alii aliter hoc inter- pretantur (verba Brentii sunt) tamen quia hic sermo est de regno Christi in terris, intelligendum erit pro hujus regni conditionibus. Libanus mons est altissi- mis cedris nobilis: Carmelus autem mons est fertili- tate vini celebris. Quo igitur tempore Christus adve- niet, Libanus convertetur in Carmelum, & Carme- lus vicissim in Libanum, hoc est, omnia erunt in re- gno Christi culta, fertilia, & benedicta. Libanus ha- bet quidem cedros aptos ædificationi, sed caret vitibus & oleis. Carmelus habet multas vites & oleas, sed ca- ret Cedris. Cum igitur Christus accipiet regnum suum, tanta erit rerum benedictio, ut Libanus pro- ferat vites una cum cedris, & Carmelus proferat ce- dros una cum vitibus. Eadem sententia & postea cap. 32. dicitur: Desertum est in Carmel, & Car- melus reputabitur in saltum, h. e. Libanum. Et cap. 35. Lætabitur deserta & gloria Libani data est ei, de- cor Carmeli & Saron. Quæ sententiæ modo expli- candi solum differunt, quoad sensum autem omnes in eo conveniunt, quod hic de Judæorum reproba- tione, ac gentium vocatione sermo sit. Præferenda tamen videtur explicatio Osiandri, quæ etiam Theodoreti & Procopii est, siquidem saltus vel sylva sit gentilitas, & nomine Charmel ob fertilitatem Judæa designetur, Es. 32, 15. donec effundetur super vos Spiritus, & erit desertum in Carmel, & Carmel in saltum reputabitur. Ubi B. Lutherus hanc red- didit explicationem: Desertum, id est, reliquiæ Ju- dæorum, & gentes erunt ceu cultissimus ager: Ferent uberrimos fructus in fide Christi, Et Carmel, id est, Synagoga, quæ nunc floret, redigetur in saltum, & de- solabitur. Qui de vastatione Libani & Carmeli ac- cipiunt, hoc sensu, Libanus succidetur, eritq, Cedris suis spoliatus, haud dissimilis campo, & Carmelus nunc optime cultus ac fertilis, hic erit incultus ac ne- glectus, ut innascentibus illi passim fruticibus, & du- metis sylvæ faciem acquirat, vocem Carmel diverso ac contrario modo, nunc pro campo spoliato, nunc pro loco culto ac fertili explicare necessum habet, neque phraseologiæ Propheticæ vim assequuntur, & à Scopo vaticinii plane recedunt. Quod autem brevi & in modico hæc futura dicuntur, etsi in ad- ventu Salvatoris demum eventura, id post Hiero- nym. pleriq; ita explicant: quod à temporibus E- saiæ usque ad dispensationem carnis assumtæ, pro comparatione æternitatis breve & modicum tem- poris spatium intervenerit: non incommode ta- men Brentius noster observat, breve & modicum illud non ab eo tempore, quo Esaias hæc concio- natus est, sed quo ea, quæ ante dixerat, implenda erant, & quo Christus nasciturus erat, æstimandum esse. Glossa vero Grotii hactenus inaudita plane est: Nam voce Charmel solam agrorum planitiem, & per metaphoram depressionem designari, nondum ostendit Grotius: neq; locus ullus adduci potuit, ubi per SALTUM vel SYLVAM altitudo & elatio in speciem montis, ac metaphorice victoria indicata fuerit.

## 29:18
Vers. 18. AND IN THAT DAY THE DEAF WILL HEAR THE WORDS OF THE BOOK.) Even the most stupid will understand from the event what I have said, and how truly I have said it.

A new, and unheard-of gloss again. Isaiah does not predict what the deaf, let alone what the stupid, are about to understand from the event, but that those who had once been deaf in gentility are about to hear and perceive the words of the book of Holy Scripture, which was sealed, and could not be read by the Jewish people, as one whose eyes were closed, or blinded, and ears were stopped, v. 4. ch. 6, 10. John 9, 39. Thus Menochius understands the Gentiles by the deaf and blind: THE WORDS OF THE BOOK, that is; the oracles of the Scriptures concerning THE EYES OF THE BLIND WILL SEE OUT OF DARKNESS AND GLOOM: led out of darkness and gloom into the admirable light of God. THE MEEK IN THE LORD: The Gentiles made gentle through Christ, who allow themselves to be formed by the ministers of the Gospel with a meek and docile mind. So also Tirinus, as well as Cornel. à Lapide, whom Menochius and Tirinus mostly follow. Nor did Blessed Luther, the Weimar Paraphrase, Piscator, or the ancient Doctors think otherwise on this place. Jerome, Cyril, Procopius, Theodoret, Brentius, and Osiander understand it particularly concerning those who were judged deaf and blind by the Pharisees, the Apostles and the remaining Disciples of Christ; But the context teaches that it looks to the conversion of the Gentiles. Jerome observes that by the book is understood the Scripture, which proceeded from one Shepherd Eccl. 12. and comes under the name of a book Ps. 40, 8. Heb. 10, 9. What is said, THE MEEK IN THE LORD WILL ADD JOY, Grotius explains not badly, they will rejoice abundantly, who have submitted themselves to God. Others, however, understand it thus, HE WILL ADD joy to the Church, i.e., they will increase the same. But the words IN THE LORD express not an external joy, but a spiritual one, which are not to be referred to the subject with Grotius, i.e., the description of the meek, but to the predicate, the reason, foundation, and manner of the joy Phil. 4. as the words added by way of explanation teach: THE POOR MEN IN THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL WILL EXULT. Which most interpreters rightly understand concerning Christ: As one who is accustomed to be designated by the Prophets through the HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL: and in whom alone is true exultation and boasting, Isa. 45, Jer. 9, 1 Cor. 1. That Holy One, who acquired Israel for Himself as a peculiar possession, and is the Holy One to Israel, from whom it expects salvation by true faith, because He was made for Israel into redemption and salvation. And therefore blessed Luther rightly says here: It is a most noble sentence, which takes away joy from all our works and efforts, and delivers it to Christ, who alone is our righteousness, salvation, and consolation, who are poor, and do not boast of works, but acknowledge our infirmity, therefore peace and joy befall us in Christ. For that peace which is sought through us is weak. But that which is sought through Christ is firm, just as He Himself says: In Me you shall have peace, but in the world tribulation.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET AUDIENT IN ILLA DIE SURDI VERBA LIBRI.) Etiam stupidissimi ex eventu intelligent, quid dixerim, & quam vere dixerim.

Nova iterum, atq; inaudita glossa. Non quid surdi, nedum quid stupidi sint ex eventu intellectu- ri prædicit Esaias, sed quod qui surdi quondam fue- rant in gentilismo, verba libri Scripturæ S. auditu- ri ac percepturi sint, qui signatus erat, ac legi non poterat à populo Judaico, utpote cujus oculi clausi, vel excæcati, aures obturatæ erant v. 4. cap. 6, 10. Joh. 9, 39. Ita Menochius per surdos & cæcos gen- tiles intelligit: VERBA LIBRI, id est; oracula Scripturarum de TENEBRIS ET CALIGINE OCULI COECORUM VIDEBUNT: è tene- bris & caligine educti in admirabile lumen Dei. MI- TES IN DOMINO: Gentiles per Christum man- suefacti, qui miti & docili animo se formandos per- mittunt Evangelii ministris. Sic etiam Tirinus, ut & Cornel. à Lapide, quem Menochius & Tirinus ple- rumq; sequuntur. Neq; aliter B. Lutherus in hunc locum, Paraphrasis Vinariensis, Piscator, aut anti- qui Dd. Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Procopius, Theodore- tus, Brentius, & Osiander de iis, qui à Pharisæis sur- di & cæci judicabantur, Apostolis & reliquis Di- scipulis Christi, peculiariter intelligunt; Sed gen- tilium conversionem respici συνέχειa docet. Per librum Scripturam intelligi Hieronymus observat, quæ à Pastore uno profecta Eccles. 12. ac nomine li- bri venit Psal. 40, 8. Ebr. 10, 9. Quod dicitur, AD- DENT MITES IN DOMINO LÆTITIAM, non male Grotius explicat, cumulate gaudebunt, qui Deo se subdiderunt. Alii tamen ita intelligunt, ADDET Ecclesiæ lætitiam, h. e. augebunt eandem. Sed lætitiam non externam, verum spiritualem, verba IN DOMINO exprimunt, quæ non ad sub- jectum referenda cum Grotio, h. e. descriptionem mitium, sed ad prædicatum, rationem, fundamen- tum ac modum lætitiæ Phil. 4. uti verba κατ᾽ ἐπεξή- γησιν addita docent: PAUPERES HOMINES IN SANCTO ISRAEL EXULTABUNT. Quæ recte de Christo plerique Interpp. intelligunt: Utpote, qui per SANCTUM ISRAELIS desi- gnari à Prophetis solet: & in quo unice vera est ex- ultatio, ac gloriatio Ef. 45. Jerem. 9. 1. Cor. 1. San- ctus ille, qui Israëlèm sibi acquisivit in peculium, & Israëli Sanctus est, à quo vera fide salutem expectat, quia factus est Israëli in redemtionem & salvifica- tionem. Ideoq; præclare hic B. Lutherus: Est no- bilissima sententia, quæ aufert lætitiam ab omnibus nostris operibus & studiis, & tradit eam Christo, qui solus justitia, salus & consolatio nostra est, qui sumus pauperes, & non jactamus opera, sed agnoscimus in- firmitatem nostram, ideo contingit nobis pax & gau- dium in Christo. Ea enim pax, quæ per nos quæritur, est infirma. Ea autem, quæ per Christum quæritur, est firma, sicut ipse dicit: In me habebitis pacem, in mundo autem pressuram.

## 29:19
Vers. 19. AND THE MEEK SHALL ADD JOY IN THE LORD) They shall rejoice abundantly, who have submitted themselves to God.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET ADDENT MITES IN DOMINO LÆTITIAM) Cumulate gaudebunt, qui Deo se subdide- runt.

## 29:20
FOR THE TERRIBLE ONE IS BROUGHT TO NOUGHT) Where the oppressor Sennacherib shall have failed.

AND ALL ARE CONSUMED THAT WATCHED FOR INIQUITY.) Where all shall have been cut down. That is, where the authors of evil counsels shall have lost all authority.

Latin:

QUONIAM DEFECIT, QUI PRÆVALEBAT) Ubi defecerit oppressor Sennacheribus.

ET SUCCISI SUNT OMNES, QUI VIGILA- BANT SUPER INIQUITATEM.) Vbi succisi fuerint o- mnes. Id est, ubi auctoritatem omnem amiserint malorum consiliorum auctores.

## 29:21
WHO MADE MEN SIN BY A WORD.) Those who treated men as guilty of a crime because of the Word of God, that is, true Prophecy, for החטיא also signifies this, just as does הרשיע. It is wrongly applied here to the Sennacheribs, about whom there is nothing in the text. Nor had he prevailed over those of whom the discourse is. For through him who was prevailing, and through those who were watching over iniquity, some, with Jerome, understand demons, to whom Oecolampadius accedes: Others, the Jewish people, such as Cornel. à Lapide, Menochius, Tirinus, who WAS PREVAILING in religion, knowledge, and grace: but the mocker and contemner of the Prophets and divine mysteries FAILED, WAS CONSUMED, that is, fully taken away, AND WAS CUT OFF first by the Chaldeans, secondly by the Romans, BECAUSE THEY WERE WATCHING OVER INIQUITY, that is, they were keeping watch for this one thing, that they might fulfill their nefarious crimes no less by night than by day. AND MADE MEN SIN BY A WORD: Not a divine one, but their own human one, namely through their futile and perverse traditions, v. 13, and likewise through wicked counsels, flatteries, threats, and mockings, by which they drew men away from piety and the worship of God. Thus they. And Jerome observes that the Nazarenes also interpreted these things in this way: What we understood concerning the Devil and his Angels, the Nazarenes think were said against the Scribes and Pharisees, because the δευτερωται (teachers of traditions) had failed, who previously mocked the people with the worst traditions, and watched day and night to deceive the simple, who made men sin by the word of God, so that they would deny Christ the son of God. To this also returns the interpretation of B. Luther, Brentius, the Weimar and Belgian Paraphrasts, as well as that of Osiander, which renders this sense: The Church of God shall be delivered from the tyranny of those who labor much in teaching vain traditions: and by their doctrine seduce the credulous people: and are most impatient if they are argued against and convicted of error or impiety. Therefore they implore the power of the Magistrates, and through it attempt to destroy their adversaries: for they have abandoned the truth, and declined into errors and lies. For that, 'they were supplanting him who argues in the gate,' Osiander thinks should be explained thus: They lay snares in the gate for him who argues. Nevertheless, the Vulgate version is deservedly retained, as well as B. Luther's, to which Grotius agrees: They were laying snares for him who publicly rebukes sins. Which was the duty of the Prophets.

AND THEY WERE SUPPLANTING HIM WHO ARGUES IN THE GATE. They were laying snares for him who publicly rebukes sins. Which was the duty of the Prophets. AND THEY HAVE TURNED ASIDE IN VAIN FROM THE JUST) In the Hebrew: And they have corrupted the just (that is, justice) with a lie: namely, by slandering the words and deeds of the Prophets. Ver. 21. WHO REDEEMED ABRAHAM) Who delivered him from the Chaldeans, Egyptians, Philistines. JACOB SHALL NOT NOW BE CONFOUNDED.) That is, he shall no longer be put to shame. It is a personification, by which a dead man is placed before the eyes as if he were alive. Jacob is said to blush when his descendants withdraw themselves from the obedience of God: on the contrary, to lift himself up when the same perform their duty.

By Jacob is not understood the deceased Patriarch, but in the Prophetic manner the people of God: who is said to be no longer confounded, as happened in the old Church, when the people were often confounded because of the manifold idolatry with which they were infected: Therefore a happier state of the Church of the New Testament is predicted. But when the Church SHALL HAVE SEEN HER CHILDREN, the work of MY HANDS in the midst of her, SANCTIFYING MY NAME, when the Church shall rejoice, that is, as many as are truly Christians in her, AND THEY SHALL SANCTIFY THE HOLY ONE OF JACOB, AND SHALL DECLARE (Heb. shall fear) THE GOD OF ISRAEL, that is, the Church of Christ shall see with great joy her own increases: that indeed daily children are born to me, the Lord, through regeneration, whom I have created, and reformed by my spirit unto good works. And when these children of mine shall confess me before men, and shall lead a life worthy of Christians, that very thing shall redound to the glory both of me and of my Church: therefore she herself shall reverently and from the heart worship and celebrate me, her God: and shall fear me, and shall compose her actions and studies according to my will; as Osiander interprets. Similarly also Brentius takes it concerning the true Israelites: the interpretation of B. Luther agrees, that the people were confounded under impious Doctors, and profited nothing by their righteousness of works: but when not our righteousness, but that of Christ shall be preached, Jacob, or those who believe in the works of the hands of the Lord, shall not be confounded. By the holy one of Jacob, Cornel. à Lapide understands Christ, bringing forward Procopius, Adamus, and Pintus in support of his opinion. Tirinus and Menochius explain it concerning the Jews, that they shall not only be confounded, but in the time of the New Testament, when they shall see the Apostles, their children, the works of the hands of the Lord in the midst of them, sanctifying the name of the Lord, and preaching the holy one of Jacob, the Messiah. Which is also the interpretation of Jerome. But the former sense seems to be preferred, which Piscator and the Belgian Paraphrasts also follow. In the Hebrew the words are thus (as B. Luther also expressed the same): when they shall see their children, the work of my hands in the interior or midst of them, they shall sanctify (the Jacobites) my name, and they shall sanctify the holy one of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel. Where the designation of the Holy Trinity is had: He who speaks is God the Father, whose name is to be sanctified: the Holy One of Jacob is the Son of God, who is also to be sanctified; and therefore by the God of Israel, whom the believers fear, the Holy Spirit is understood. Therefore those words, AND THEY SHALL SANCTIFY THE HOLY ONE OF JACOB, are not to be explained as Grotius wishes, 'when they shall sanctify,' as if it were an exposition of what preceded. Nor is that perversion of Grotius to be admitted, 'THE WORKS OF MY HANDS: Whom I, says God, have miraculously preserved.' For that is like creating anew. For the discourse is not about the miraculous preservation of the Jews, but about the regeneration of the faithful, Eph. 2:10.

Latin:

QUI PECCARE FACIEBANT HOMINES IN VERBO.) Qui ob Verbum Dei, id est, veram Prophetiam homines, ut criminis reos tractabant, nam החטיא etiam hoc significat, sicut & הרשיע. Perperam ingeritur hic Sennacheribus, de quo nihil in textu. Neq; is prævaluerat illis, de quibus sermo est. Per eum enim, qui prævalebat, & per il- los, qui vigilabant super iniquitatem, alii cum Hie- ronymo Dæmones intelligunt, quibus Oecolampa- dius accedit: Alii populum Judaicum, utpote Cor- nel. à Lapide, Menochius, Tirinus, qui PRÆVALE- BAT religione, scientia, gratia: sed illusor & con- temtor Prophetarum & mysteriorum divinorum DEFECIT, CONSUMMATUS EST, id est, plene assum- tus, ET SUCCISUS EST primo per Chaldæos, secundo per Romanos, QUIA VIGILABANT SUPER INIQUI- TATEM, id est, ad hoc unum excubabant, ut nocte non minus, quam die explerent scelera sua nefanda. ET PECCARE FACIEBANT HOMINES IN VERBO: Non divino, sed suo humano, nempe per futiles & per- versas traditiones suas, v. 13. itemq; per prava consi- lia, adulationes, minas & subsannationes, quibus a- vellebant homines à pietate & cultu Dei. Sic illi. Atque ita etiam hæc interpretatos esse Nazaræos Hieronymus observat: Quæ nos super Diabolo & Angelis ejus intelleximus, Nazaræi contra Scribas & Pharisæos dicta arbitrantur, quod defecerint δευ- τερωται, qui prius illudebant populo traditionibus pes- simis, & ad decipiendos simplices die noctuq; vigila- bant, qui peccare faciebant homines in verbo Dei, ut Christum Dei filium negarent. Quo redit quoque B. Lutheri, Brentii, Paraphrastarum Vinariensium & Belgicarum interpretatio, ut & Osiandri, quæ hunc sensum reddit: Liberabitur Ecclesia Dei ab eorum Tyrannide, qui in docendis vanis traditionibus multum laborant: & sua doctrina seducunt popu- lum credulum: & sunt impatientissimi, si erroris aut impietatis arguantur & convincantur. Itaq; implo- rant Magistratus potentiam, atq; per eam suos adver- sarios delere conantur: reliquerunt enim veritatem, & declinarunt ad errores & mendacia. Nam illa, ar- guentem in porta supplantabant, Osiander ita expo- nenda censet: Insidias in porta struunt arguenti. Re- tinetur tamen merito versio Vulgata, & B. Lutheri, cui annuit Grotius: Insidias tendebant publice corri- pienti peccata. Quod erat officium Prophetarum.

ET ARGUMENTUM IN PORTA SUPPLAVTA- BANT Insidias tendebant publice corripienti peccata. Quod erat officium Prophetarum. ET DECLINAVERUNT FRUSTRA A JUSTO) In Hebræo: Et justum (id est, justitiam) corruperunt menda- cio: nempe calumniantes dicta & facta Prophetarum. Vers. 21. QUI REDEMIT ABRAHAM) Qui eum liberavit à Chaldæis, Ægyptiis, Philistinis. NON MODO CONFUNDETUR JACOB.) Id est, jam non pudefiet. Est προσωποποιϊα, qua mortuus ob o- culos ponitur, quasi viveret. Erubescere dicitur Jacobus, cum posteri ejus à Dei obsequio se subtrahunt: contra at- tollere se, cum iidem faciunt officium.

Per Jacobum non intelligitur Patriarcha defun- ctus, sed more Prophetico populus Dei: qui dicitur non confundendus amplius, ut in veteri Ecclesia factum, cum ob multiplicem idololatriam, qua in- fectus erat populus, confusus sæpe est: Felicior er- go status Ecclesiæ N. T. prædicitur. Sed cum VI- DERIT Ecclesia FILIOS SUOS, OPERA ni- mirum MANUUM MEARUM IN MEDIO SUI, SANCTIFICANTES NOMEN MEUM, cum gaudebit Ecclesia, quotquot scil. sunt in ea vere Christiani, ET SANCTIFICABUNT SAN- CTUM JACOB, ET DEUM ISRAEL PRÆ- DICABUNT, (Ebr. timebunt) id est, videbit Ec- clesia Christi magno cum gaudio sua incrementa: quod nimirum quotidie mihi Domino per regenera- tionem nascantur filii, quos ego creavi, & spiritu meo reformavi ad bona opera. Et cum hi filii mei confi- tebuntur me coram hominibus, & ducent vitam, Christianis dignam, cedet id ipsum in gloriam, & meam, & meæ Ecclesiæ: itaq; ipsa me, Deum suum, reverenter & ex animo colet atq; celebrabit: meque timebit, atque ad voluntatem meam suas actiones & studia componet; ut interpretatur Osiander. Simi- liter quoq; de veris Israëllitis accipit Brentius: con- gruit B. Lutheri interpretatio, sub impiis Doctoribus confusum esse populum, nihilq; profecisse sua justitia operum: cum autem non nostra, sed Christi justitia prædicabitur, non confusum iri Jacob, vel credentes opera manuum Domini. Per sanctum Jacob Chri- stum intelligit Cornel. à Lapide, adducens in senten- tiam suam Procopium, Adamum & Pintum. Tiri- nus & Menochius de Judæis explicant, eos confu- fum iri non modo, sed tempore N. T. cum vide- bunt Apostolos filios suos opera manuum Domini in medio sui, sanctificantes nomen Domini, & sanctum Jacob, Messiam prædicantes. Quæ etiam Hierony- mi est interpretatio. Sed præferendus videtur pri- or sensus, quem etiam sequuntur Piscator, & Pa- raphrastæ Belgæ. In Ebræo verba ita habent (uti expreffit quoq; eadem B. Lutherus) cum videbunt natos suos opus manuum mearum in interiori vel me- dio sui, sanctificabunt (Jacobitæ) nomen meum, & sanctificabunt sanctum Jacob, & Deum Israël time- bunt. Ubi S.S. Trinitatis designatio habetur: is, qui loquitur, Deus Pater est, cujus nomen sanctifi- candum: Sanctus Jacob est Filius Dei, qui & idem sanctificandus; ideoque per Deum Israël, quem ti- ment credentes, Spiritus Sanctus intelligitur. Non ergo verba illa, ET SANCTIFICABUNT SANCTUM JACOB, ita explicanda, ut vult Grotius, cum san- ctificabunt, quasi expositio habeatur ejus, quod præcessit. Neq; admittenda illa Grotii perversio, OPERA MANUUM MEARUM: Quos ego, inquit Deus, mirabiliter servavi. Id enim est vel- ut creare denuo. Non enim de Judæorum conser- vatione mirabili, sed de fidelium regeneratione sermo est, Eph. 2, 10.

## 29:23
THE WORKS OF MY HANDS) Whom I, says God, have miraculously preserved. For that is like creating anew.

AND THEY SHALL SANCTIFY THE HOLY ONE OF JACOB) That is, when they shall sanctify. For it is an exposition of what preceded.

Ver. 23. AND THEY THAT ERR IN SPIRIT SHALL KNOW UNDERSTANDING) Even those who had erred shall return to the true way.

Latin:

OPERA MANUUM MEARUM) Quos ego, in- quit Deus, mirabiliter servavi. Id enim est velut creare denuo.

ET SANCTIFICABUNT SANCTUM JACOB) Id est, cum sanctificabunt. Est enim expositio ejus, quod præcessit.

Vers. 23. ET SCIENT ERRANTES SPIRITU IN- TELLECTUM) Etiam, qui erraverant, in viam veram redibunt.

## 29:24
AND THE MURMURERS SHALL LEARN THE LAW.) The Pythonics themselves shall learn to observe the law, See above 8:19.

The Hebrew word לקח denotes not law, but doctrine: And that the Evangelical doctrine is being treated, the preceding things teach. Osiander therefore rendered the sense correctly: For they shall be converted to Christ, and shall receive the doctrine of the Gospel, who had stuck in horrible errors of religion, and who had previously blathered much about their fictitious and false religion, they will promptly surrender themselves to be instructed by those teaching the Gospel. Which B. Luther also applies not badly in a particular way to seducers in a marginal gloss, Und die Schwätzer/die unnüße Plauderer, als die Schwärmer, so eitel Geist rühmen, and in his Explanation on this passage, that is to say, not only the seduced people will be converted but also a part of those who were seducing and persecuting the word. Thus Paul was converted. And the mutterers shall learn doctrine, i.e., those who are prompt to teach, which is the characteristic of all impious teachers. Moreover, he calls them mutterers because they speak lowly, earthly, useless, uncertain things, from their own head, not from the word of God.

Others say they are called murmurers, who were murmuring against God and the Prophets, which was done quite often by the Jews. Cf. Matt. 29, 11. Luke 15, 28. Rom. 10, 19. Thus Cornel. à Lap., Piscator, the Belgians. However, Lyranus, Forerius, and Adam Sasbouth explain these as referring to converted Gentiles. But Sanctius, Cornel. à Lapide, and Menochius, along with Cyril and Thomas, refer them to converted Jews who had previously been mockers of the Prophets. In general, they can be understood as referring to true Jacobites, of whom the Prophet had spoken before. Tirinus, however, interprets these wrongly as referring to those who acknowledged the finger of God but remained erring in spirit and murmuring against God: because here it is not bare knowledge that is designated, but knowledge joined with doctrine, by which such murmurers will learn true doctrine.

And these things also concerning the twenty-ninth chapter.

Latin:

ET MUSSITATORES DISCENT LEGEM.) Ipsi Pythonici legem observare discent, Vid. supra 8, 19.

Vox Ebræa לקח non legem, sed doctrinam no- tat: Et de Evangelica doctrina agi, superiora do- cent. Sensum ergo recte reddidit Osiander: Con- vertentur enim ad Christum, & Evangelii doctri- nam recipient, qui in horribilibus erroribus religio- nis bæserant, & qui de fictitia & falsa religione sua antea multum blaterarant, ii se docentibus Evange- lion erudiendos prompte tradent. Quod peculiari- ter ad seductores quoque applicat non male B.Lu- therus in glossa marginali, Und die Schwätzer/die unnüße Plauderer, als die Schwärmer, so eitel Geist rühmen, & in Explanatione h. l. q. d. non so- lum populus seductus convertetur sed etiam pars eo- rum, qui seducebant & per sequebantur verbum. Sic Paulus conversus est. Et mussitatores discent doctri- nam, i. e. qui promti sunt ad docendum, id quod pro- prium est omnium impiorum doctorum. Ideo autem mussitatores vocat, quia loquuntur humilia, terre- stria, inutilia, incerta, ex suo capite, non ex verbo Dei.

Alii musfitatores vocari dicunt, qui contra Deum & Prophetas murmurabant, quod à Judæis sæpius fa- ctum. Conf. Matth.29,11. Luc.15,28. Rom.10,19. Sic Cornel. à Lap. Piscator, Belgæ. Cæterum de gentili- bus conversis hæc explicant Lyranus, Forerius, & Adamus Sasbouth. De Judæis autem conversis, qui antea fuerint Prophetarum illusores, cum Cyrillo & Thoma Sanctius, Cornel. à Lapide & Menochius. In genere de Jacobitis veris ea intelligi possunt, de quibus antea egerat Propheta. Male autem Tiri- nus hæc de iis, qui digitum Dei agnoscebant, sed manebant errantes Spiritu, & murmurantes con- tra Deum,interpretatur: quia hic scientia non nu- da, sed conjuncta cum doctrina, qua musfitatores tales veram doctrinam discent, designatur.

Atque hæc etiam de capite Vigesimonono.

## 30:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXX.

With the affliction of Sennacherib imminent, the Prophet, intending to recall the people from trust in the protection of Egypt, denounces punishment for this treachery by committing it to a book; he promises grace and blessing from the Lord to those who trust, and joy that will arise from the destruction of the enemies.

Ver. 1. WOE, REBELLIOUS CHILDREN.) Most refer these to the times of Jeremiah: wrongly. For nothing has been predicted, nor will be predicted up to chapter 36, which does not concern the times of Hezekiah: and thus all these things from chapter 29 to that 36 were predicted and written by the Prophet two years before the arrival of Sennacherib. Therefore, after these prophecies, he appends the history itself, from which it may appear that all things happened just as he had predicted, in chapters 36, 37, 38, 39. As soon as it was heard that Sennacherib had come from Assyria, the Jews, outside of Jerusalem, were distracted into different counsels: some thought that surrender should be made to the Assyrians: others that the Egyptians should be summoned: and indeed so foully, that the latter thought Egyptian rites should be adopted, the former Assyrian ones, for the sake of life. Hezekiah alone, and a few with him, had faith in the promises of God through Isaiah, and hoped against hope, with an admirable success, which excellently figures the liberation of the Christian Church from its enemies. Woe, children who desert the divine law!

It is so: most refer these to the times of Jeremiah: Jerome, Cyril, Theodoret, Procopius, and among the more recent ones Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, and others, and they wish them to have been spoken, as Cornelius explains, against the Jews who, 150 years later, after Gedaliah was killed by Ishmael, fearing the Chaldeans who had set him over Judea, fled into Egypt against the command of GOD: as can be read in Jerem. 42 and 43. Some, however, refer them to the Jews who, in the time of Zedekiah, when Nebuchadnezzar was besieging Jerusalem, were seeking help from Pharaoh, of which it is reported in Jerem. 30, who had defected from Nebuchadnezzar against their given word, and afterwards hoped for defense against the same from the auxiliary forces of the Egyptians. Which is the interpretation of Junius and Piscator, as well as the Belgian Paraphrasts. But we readily admit that these things are said against those who, while Sennacherib was devastating Judea, judged that help should be sought from the Egyptians, which is the opinion not only of certain Rabbis, but also of Lyranus and Sanctius among the Papists, as well as of our B. Luther, Brentius, Osiander, and the Vinarians. But the arguments which Grotius brings forward for this are not solid, but labor under a begging of the question. It is a μέγα λίαν ἄιτημα. That nothing was predicted, nor was to be predicted up to chapter 37, which does not concern the times of Hezekiah. For we have already shown that many other things were predicted in the earlier chapters which concern the Babylonian captivity and other things about to happen after the times of Hezekiah, and many things also which concern the times of the New Testament itself. This preconceived opinion, however, which for Grotius Tom. II. V. T.

peculiar and proper to him, and which perhaps never came into the mind of anyone before him, I will not say among Christian interpreters, but even among the Rabbis themselves, that nothing in all the prophecies of Isaiah up to chapter 36 was handed down which does not concern the times of Hezekiah, was the cause for Grotius to distort clear oracles, and not rarely to pervert them in wondrous ways, so that they might be forced to serve the hypothesis. Which we have already made plain by many proofs. Nor is it to be admitted that in those chapters which follow up to the history of Hezekiah, all things concern the times of Hezekiah. Our observations will teach the contrary. That is also built upon a ruinous foundation, that all things from chapter 29 to 36 were predicted and written two years before the arrival of Sennacherib. Which, having been constructed from a false interpretation of verse 1 of chapter 29, we have destroyed there. But where Grotius read that counsels were agitated about adopting Egyptian or even Assyrian rites, he does not show: nor does that REBELLIOUS CHILDREN imply it. For they were deserters because they disregarded both the general divine interdict against summoning the help of the Egyptians, by whom they had been oppressed with great tyranny and from whom they had been liberated by many miracles through the singular grace of God, Deut. 17, and the special warnings of the Prophet, and trusted more in a broken reed than in divine power and grace. And although history hands down nothing about these counsels of the Jews, it is nevertheless certain, not so much from this address of the Prophet as from the embassy of Sennacherib, that the Princes and citizens of Jerusalem trusted greatly in Egyptian help and had altogether decided that they would use it. For the legates of Sennacherib are ordered to say to Hezekiah: In what do you trust, that you dare to rebel! Do you hope in the broken reed of Egypt, etc. And afterwards: Will he have trust in Egypt because of chariots and horsemen!
