Which openly teach that the Jerusalemites had discussed plans about calling Pharaoh to their aid. But that this address pertains to the times of Hezekiah and the incursion of the Assyrians is to be sought not from the continuity with the preceding prophecies, but from the contents of this address. For prophecies and addresses do not always cohere by reason of time, but the Prophets not rarely make digressions from their own times to future times, and especially to the New Testament, and from time to time they introduce the Messiah, whom the Prophets carried in their heart and mouth. Rightly, therefore, B. Luther observes that the Prophet returns here to his own times. But mention is made expressly of the Assyrian in verse 29, where Cornel. à Lapide betakes himself in vain to a tropical sense, and understands the Devil or any tyrant and oppressor. In vain do others wish Assur to be placed for the Chaldean: since the slaughter of the Assyrians is manifestly described here: In vain also does Franc. Junius say that the judgment of God against the Assyrians is adduced only for the sake of an example, because the matter here was properly to be about the liberation from the same. Which we judge to be plain from the context.

THAT YOU MIGHT TAKE COUNSEL, AND NOT FROM ME) Contrary to me.

Latin:

CAPUT XXX.

Imminente Sennacheribi afflictione Propheta à fiducia in præsidium Ægyptipopulum re- vocaturus pœnam denunciat huic perfidiæ libro consignando, confidentibus à Domi- num gratiam, & benedictionem pollicetur, ac gaudium è deletione hostium oriturum.

Vers. 1. VÆ FILII DESERTORES.) Plerique hæc ad Ieremiæ referunt tempora: male. Nihil enim neque prædictum est, neque prædicetur usque ad caput 36. quod non spectet tempora Ezechiæ: atque adeo hæc o- mnia à capite 29. ad illud 36. à Propheta prædicata scripta- que sunt biennio ante adventum Sennacheribi. Ideo post hæc vaticinia subnectit ipsam historiam, ex qua appareat, omnia, ita ut prædixerat, evenisse, capitibus 36. 37. 38. 39. Cum primum ex Assyria venisse audiretur Sennacheribus, Judæi, extra Hierosolyma,in diversa distracti sunt consilia: alii deditionem Assyriis faciendam putarunt: alii Ægyptios advocandos: & quidem tam fœde, ut hi Ægyptia sacra,illi Assyriaca suscipienda vitæ causa censerent. Solus Ezechias, paucique cum eo, Dei per Esaiam promissis fidem habuit, & contra spem speravit, successu admirabili, qui Ecclesiæ Christianæ ab hostibus liberationem eximie figurat. Væ fi- lii desertores legis divinæ!

ITa est: referunt plerique hæc ad Jeremiæ tempo- ra: Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Theodoretes, Proco- pius, & è recentioribus Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, aliique, ac dicta esse volunt exponen- te Cornelio contra Judæos, qui post 150. annos occi- so ab Ismaële Gedalia, Chaldæos,qui eum Judææ præ- fecerant, timentes in Ægyptum contra DEI præce- ptum fugerunt: uti Jerem. 42. & 43. legere est. Nonnulli tamen ea ad Judæos referunt, qui Sedeciæ tempore, cum obsideret Nebucadnezar Hierosolyma, à Pharaone petebant auxilium, de quo refertur Jerem. 30. qui contra datam fidem defecerant à Nebucadnezare, & postmodum defensionem ad- versus eundem à copiis auxiliaribus Ægyptiorum sperabant. Quæ Junii & Piscatoris, nec non Pa- raphrastarum Belgicorum est interpretatio. Sed facile admittimus contra eos hæc dici, qui sub Sen- nacheribo Judæam vastanti opem ab Ægyptiis pe- tendam esse censuere, quæ non Rabbinorum so- lum quorundam, sed etiam Lyrani, & Sanctii è Pontificiis, nec non B. Lutheri nostri, Brentii, Osiandri & Vinariensium est sententia. Quæ vero Grotius pro ea adfert argumenta, solida non sunt, sed petitione principii laborant. Μέγα λίαν ἄιτημα est. Nihil neque prædictum esse, neque prædictum iri usque ad caput 37. quod non spectet tempora Ezechiæ. Nam multa alia in prioribus capp. prædicta esse, quæ captivitatem Babylonicam, & alia concernant post Ezechiæ tempora eventura,multa etiam, quæ ipsa Nov. Test. tempora spectent, jam ostendimus. Hæc autem præconcepta opinio, quæ Grotio pe- Tom. II. V. T.

culiaris est, & propria, ac nemini fortassis ante ipsum in mentem venit, non dicam inter Christia- nos Interpp. sed etiam inter ipsos Rabbinos, nihil in universis vaticiniis Esaianis usque ad cap. 36. traditum esse, quod non spectet Ezechiae tempora, Grotio causa fuit, luculenta oracula detorquendi, ac miris modis non raro pervertendi, ut cogeren- tur τῇ ὑποθέσει δουλεύειν. Quod pluribus docu- mentis planum jam fecimus. Neq; admittendum, in iis, quae adhuc usq; ad historiam Ezechiae sequun- tur capp. omnia Ezechiae tempora spectare. Con- trarium hae animadversiones nostrae docebunt. Ruinoso etiam fundamento illud superstruitur, omnia à cap. 29. ad 36. praedicata, ac scripta fuisse biennio ante Sennacheribi adventum. Quod è falsa interpretatione vers. 1. cap. 29. exstructum, illic destruximus. Ubi autem legerit Grotius, quod con- silia agitata fuerint de sacris Aegyptiis, vel etiam Assyriacis suscipiendis, non ostendit: neque illud FILII DESERTORES id infert. Nam deserto- res erant, quod tum generale Dei interdictum de non advocando Aegyptiorum, à quibus magna ty- rannide oppressi, ac singulari Dei gratia multis mi- raculis liberati erant, auxilio, Deut. 17. tum moni- ta specialia Prophetae posthaberent, ac baculo a- rundineo magis, quam divinae potentiae, ac gratiae confiderent. Etsi autem historia nihil tradat de hisce consiliis Judaeorum, certum tamen est, non tam ex hac concione Prophetae, quam ex legatione Sennacheribi, Principes & cives Hierosolymita- nos Aegyptiaco auxilio plurimum confisos, & o- mnino statuisse, se eo usuros. Jubent enim legati Sennacheribi dicere Ezechiae: In quo confidis, ut audeas rebellare! An speras in baculo arundineo & confracto Aegypto &c. Et postea: An fiduciam ha- bebit in Aegypto propter currus & Equites! Quae a- perte docent, quod Hierosolymitani consilia de vocando in auxilium Pharaone tractaverint. Quod autem haec concio ad Ezechiae & incursionis Assy- riorum tempora pertineat, non è συνεχεία cum praecedentibus vaticiniis, sed è contentis hujusce concionis petendum. Non enim cohaerent semper ratione temporis vaticinia, & conciones, sed digres- siones non raro faciunt Prophetae à temporibus suis ad futura tempora, & cumprimis ad Novum Testamentum, & subinde Messiam, quem in corde & ore gesserunt Prophetae, ingerunt. Recte ergo B. Lutherus observat, redire hic Prophetam ad sua tempora. De Assyrio autem expresse mentio fit v. 29. ubi frustra Cornel. à Lapide ad tropicum sen- sum se recipit, ac Diabolum seu quemvis tyrannum & oppressorem intelligit. Frustra alii Assur posi- tum volunt pro Chaldaeo: Siquidem manifeste cla- des Assyriorum hic describatur: Frustra etiam Franc. Junius exempli tantum causa judicium Dei adversus Assyrios adduci ait, quia de liberatione ab iisdem proprie hic agendum erat. Quod è contex- tu planum esse arbitramur.

UT FACERETIS CONSILIUM, ET NON EX ME) Mihi contrarium.

## 30:2
Ver. 2. YOU WHO WALK, THAT YOU MAY GO DOWN INTO EGYPT) Namely by sending ambassadors, as appears below in 4.

HOPING FOR HELP IN THE STRENGTH OF PHARAOH) Of Psammetichus.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUI AMBULATIS, UT DESCENDATIS IN AEGYPTUM) Nempe missis legatis, ut apparet in- fra 4.

SPERANTES AUXILIUM IN FORTITUDINE PHARAONIS) Psammitichi.

## 30:4
IN TANIS YOUR PRINCES) See above 19, 11.

THEY HAVE REACHED AS FAR AS HANES.) Daphnae Pelusiae, as Jonathan interprets here. Herodotus mentions that city in the affairs of Psammetichus. Moreover, that Hebrew name is also this Greek one, contracted from a fuller word, which is תחפנחס, Jer. 43, 7. 8. from which was made תחפניס, whence the name of the Queen 1 Kings 11, 19. and more briefly חנס, as in this place. That city looked toward Arabia, as we learn from Herodotus.

Hieronymus de Hanes observes that it was the last city of Egypt next to the Ethiopians and Blemmyes. Tanis was the royal city of Pharaoh, where Moses performed his mighty works before him, Ps. 77:43.

Latin:

IN TANI PRINCIPES TUI) Vide supra 19, 11.

USQUE AD HANES PERVENERUNT.) Daphnas Pelusias, ut hic interpretatur Jonathan. Meminit ejus urbis in Psammitichi rebus Herodotus. Est autem & illud Hebræ- um nomen, & hoc Græcum contractum ex pleniore voce, quæ est תחפנחס, Jer. 43, 7. 8. ex qua factum תחפניס, unde nomen Reginæ 1. Reg. 11, 19. & brevius חנס, ut hoc loco. Spectabat ea urbs Arabiam, ut ex Herodoto discimus.

Hieronymus de Hanes observat, quod fuerit ultima civitas Ægypti juxta Æthiopas & Blemmyos. Tanis regia fuit Pharaonis, ubi Moses coram eo sua fecit portenta, Psal. 77, 43.

## 30:5
Verse 5.

THEY WERE NOT FOR HELP, AND FOR ANY PROFIT, BUT FOR CONFUSION AND REPROACH.) Psammitichus, being allied with the King of the Assyrians (see above 19:23), did not wish to break the alliance with the most powerful King for the sake of the Jews. Thus, nothing resulted for the Jews from that plan except infamy for their vacillation in religion.

That Psammetichus was allied with the King of the Assyrians does not appear from chapter 19:13. For there it is not a matter of a political alliance of Psammetichus, but of a spiritual concord between the Egyptians and the Assyrians. Nor did the Assyrian consider the Egyptian to be a most powerful King: the speech of his envoys teaches otherwise. Thus says the great King, the King of the Assyrians: Behold, you trust in this broken reed staff, upon Egypt, Is. 36. If Sennacherib had been in an alliance with the Egyptian, his envoys would undoubtedly have opposed that to the Jews who were placing their trust in Egypt. But there is deep silence about that in that speech.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NON FVERVNT IN AVXILIVM, ET IN ALI- QVAM VTILITATEM, SED IN CONFVSIONEM ET OPPROBRIVM.) Psammitichus cum rege Assyriorum fœ- deratus (vid. supra 19, 23.) Judæorum causa fœdus cum Rege potentissimo rumpere noluit. Ita ad Judæos de isto consilio nihil nisi infamia ob vacillationem in religione redundavit.

Psammetichum confœderatum fuisse cum Re- ge Assyriorum, è. cap. 19, 13. non constat. Illic enim non de fœdere Psammetichi politico, sed de spiritua- li Ægyptiorum & Assyriorum concordia agitur. Ne- que pro Rege potentissimo Ægyptium habuit Assy- rius: Aliud docet legatorum ejus oratio. Hæc di- cit Rex magnus, Rex Assyriorum: Ecce confidis su- per baculum arundineum confractum istam, super Ægyptum Es. 36. Si in fœdere cum Ægyptio fuisset Sennacherib, sine dubio legati ejus id Judæis fidu- ciam in Ægyptum collocantibus opposuissent. At de eo altum in illa oratione est silentium.

## 30:6
Verse 6.

THE BURDEN OF THE BEASTS OF THE SOUTH.) This is not a new inscription, but the discourse is continued with the previous ones, as Jerome also noted regarding this passage. It must therefore be translated: the burden (supply: they carried) of the beasts toward the south, that is, toward Egypt, which is to the south of Judea. The burden soon explains the gifts which the envoys were carrying with them to purchase the alliance.

IN THE LAND OF TROUBLE AND ANGUISH, THE LIONESS AND THE LION FROM THEM, THE VIPER AND THE FLYING SERPENT.) You would translate it correctly: Through the narrow and strait land, from whence come the Lion, and the Tiger, and the viper, and the prester. The description of the Arabian Isthmus is clear enough.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ONVS JVMENTORVM AVSTRI.) Non est hic inscriptio nova, sed continuatur cum prioribus sermo, ut & Hieronymus ad hunc locum notavit. Vertendum ergo: onus (supple bajularunt) jumenta meridiem versus, id est, Ægyptum versus, quæ ad meridiem Judææ. O- nus mox explicat dona, quæ legati secum ferebant ad e- mendam societatem.

IN TERRA TRIBVLATIONIS ET ANGVSTIÆ, LEÆNA ET LEO EX EIS, VIPERA ET REGVLVS VOLANS.) Recte verteris: Per terram angustam & arctam, unde prodeunt Leo, & Tigris, & vipera, & prester. Descriptio est satis clara Isthmi Arabici.

## 30:7
Verse 7.

FOR EGYPT SHALL HELP IN VAIN AND TO NO PURPOSE.) Certain people had given the Jews vain hope of help from Egypt.

Others begin a new Prophecy here: the burden of the beasts of the South. The matter comes to the same thing. However, there is no need to fetch that supplement of the word THEY CARRIED from elsewhere. For in the same verse the verb is subsequently added. Blessed Luther rightly judged that it could be rendered thus: The burden of the beasts going to the South: Among which are in the land of anguish and necessity the Lion and the Lioness, the Basilisk and the flying Dragon. They carry the shoulders of these beasts, etc. Note, however, the allusion which Blessed Luther observes: The way from Judea to Egypt is a vast wilderness, and it abounds with every kind of beast, serpents, lions, etc. The Prophet therefore alludes to that way: Truly, he says, you envoys, together with the beasts which you lead laden with gifts, are making a journey through the wilderness of serpents and lions. For you yourselves are those dire Lions and venomous serpents, who infect my people with the hope of human help, so that they may depart from the faith, so that they may desert their God, and flee to human help. To this, what Brentius has fits well, that this money is carried through the desert, through a horrible region in which savage beasts dwell: because you will bring back nothing except horror and calamity and affliction. This periphrasis of the way is also added for that reason, so that it might be indicated that this so horrible journey was undertaken in vain. They will labor in vain. FOR EGYPT SHALL HELP IN VAIN AND TO NO PURPOSE: Every help of the Egyptians will be vain and empty. Grotius understands it thus: That certain people had given the Jews vain hope of help from Egypt. Some understand the Jews by the name of BEASTS, and interpret the burden of the vision here: that is to say, a burden, that is, a threatening and dire Prophecy against the Jews, who, against the will of God, go toward the South like beasts. But the things that are added prove that the name of beasts is to be taken properly.

THEREFORE I HAVE CRIED CONCERNING THIS: IT IS ONLY PRIDE, BE QUIET.) You may translate more correctly: therefore I have called it: (the Jewish nation) their strength is to be quiet. Only quiet and patience will protect them. The following v. 15 explains this.

Brentius also brought forward this interpretation: according to which Rahab is an appellative, which is approved by the Hebrews and Vatablus, as also by Junius, Piscator, the Genevan and English translators, and also by Amama and the Dutch. Others, however, take that name as a proper noun from Ps. 87:4, Ps. 89:21, Is. 51:4, in this sense: Since the matter is thus, therefore I publicly cry out and say that Rahab or Egypt, otherwise sufficiently haughty and proud, will cease and will bring no help to you. RAHAB IS QUIET. And so also B. Luther: Die Rahab wird still dazu stehen, and in the marginal note, Rahab ist Egypten, Psal. 86. 87. 89. und heiffet stoltz. Which sense, as being most agreeable to the Hebrew text רַהַב הֵם שָׁבֶת, the authors of the Dutch Bible Annotations have not disapproved.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ÆGYPTV S ENIM FRVSTRA, ET VANE AV- XILIABITVR) Vanam spem auxilii quidam ex Ægypto Judæis fecerant.

Alii hic novam Prophetiam ordiuntur: onus de jumentis Austri. Res eodem redit. Non opus autem aliunde supplementum illud verbi BAJU- LARUNT accersere. Nam in eodem commate verbum deinceps subjunctum est. Quod ita reddi posse, recte judicavit B. Lutherus: Onus jumento- rum ad Austrum euntium: Inter quæ sunt in terra angustiæ & necessitatis Leo & Leæna, Basiliscus & Draco volans. Portant hujus humeros jumento- rum &c. Notanda autem allusio, quam observat B. Lutherus: Via ex Judæa in Ægyptum est vasta solitudo, & abundat omni genere bestiarum, serpen- tibus, leonibus, &c. Propheta igitur alludit ad eam viam: Vere, inquit, vos legati una cum bestiis, quas muneribus onustas ducitis per serpentium & Leo- num solitudinem iter facitis. Ipse enim estis diri illi Leones & venenati serpentes, qui inficitis populum meum spe humanorum auxiliorum, ut à fide disce- dant, ut deserant Deum suum, & confugiant ad hu- mana auxilia. Adhæc probe convenit, (quæ ha- bet Brentius) ut hæc pecunia vehatur per deser- tum, per regionem horribilem, in qua sævæ bestiæ habitant: quia nihil præter horrorem & calamita- tem atq; afflictionem reportabitis. Adjecta etiam ideo est hæc viæ περίφρασις, ut indicaretur frustra hoc tam horridum iter susceptum esse. Sie wer- den sichs vergeblich sauer werden lassen. ÆGY- PTUS ENIM FRUSTRA ET VANE AUXI- LIABITUR: Vanum & inane erit omne auxilium Æ- gyptiorum. Grotius sic intelligit: Quod vanam spem auxilii quidam ex Aegypto Judæis fecerant. Nonnul- li Judæos JUMENTORUM nomine intelligunt, & onus de visione hic interpretantur: q. d. onus, id est, Prophetia minax & dira in Judæos, qui contra Dei voluntatem quasi jumenta versus Austrum proficiscuntur. Sed jumentorum nomen proprie sumi ea, quæ adduntur, convincunt.

IDEO CLAMAVI SVPER HOC: SVPERBIA TANTVM EST, QVIESCE.) Verteris rectius : ideo vo- cavi illam : (gentem Judæam) robur eorum est quiescere. So- la quies & patientia illos tuebitur. Explicant hoc se- quentia v. 15.

Hanc interpretationem adduxit etiam Bren- tius : secundum quam Rahab est appellativum, quæ Ebræis & Vatablo probatur, ut & Junio, Piscatore, Genevensi & Anglicano translatoribus, nec non A- mamæ & Belgis. Alii autem nomen id pro proprio habent è Psal. 87, 4. Psal. 89, 21. Es. 51, 4. hoc sen- su : Cum res sic se habeat, idcirco publice clamo, & dico, quod Rahab seu Ægyptus alioqui sic satis elata & superba cessatura sit, nec ullum in vos auxilium collatura. RAHAB QVIESCIT. Atq; ita etiam B. Lutherus : Die Rahab wird still dazu stehen, & in nota marginali, Rahab ist Egypten, Psal. 86. 87. 89. und heiffet stoltz. Quem sensum utpote Ebræo textui optime congruentem רַהַב הֵם שָׁבֶת non improbarunt Annotatorum Bibliorum Belgico- rum autores.

## 30:8
Vers. 8. WRITE IT FOR HIM UPON A BOX) On a tablet. AND IN A BOOK) On parchments, so that the memory may be preserved in two ways.

AND IT SHALL BE IN THE LAST DAY) יום אחרון to the Hebrews is all the time that follows.

A TESTIMONY EVEN UNTO ETERNITY) A perennial testimony.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SCRIBE EI SVPER BVXVM) In tabula. ET IN LIBRO) In membranis, ut duobus modis memoria conservetur.

ET ERIT IN DIE NOVISSIMO) יום אחרון Hebræis est omne tempus, quod sequitur.

TESTIMONIVM VSQVE IN ÆTERNVM) Te- stimonium perenne.

## 30:10
Vers. 10. WHO SAY TO THE SEERS, DO NOT SEE) They hinder the prophets as much as they can, so that they do not speak the truth. Above 29:20.

SPEAK UNTO US ERRORS) He says they said these things, not that they used those words, but that the things they wanted tended in reality to that. For to speak pleasant things to them, that was to mock them.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVI DICVNT VIDENTIBVS, NOLI- TE VIDERE) Prophetas quantum possunt impediunt, ne vera dicant. Supra 29, 20.

VIDETE NOBIS ERRORES) Illusiones dicit eos dixisse, non quod ea verba usurpurent, sed quod quæ vole- bant, reipsa eo tenderent. Placentia enim ipsis dicere, id erat ipsis illudere.

## 30:11
Vers. 11. TAKE AWAY FROM ME THE WAY) Depart from the way: that is, take another way. The speech of the Jews who care nothing for the law and the Prophets still continues.

LET THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL CEASE FROM OUR FACE) Do not repeat that name so often.

Latin:

Vers. 11. AVFERTE A ME VIAM) Recedite de via: id est, aliam viam inite. Durat adhuc Judæorum legem & Prophetas nihil curantium sermo.

CESSET A FACIE NOSTRA SANCTUS ISRA- EL) Nolite illud nomen toties repetere.

## 30:12
Vers. 12. IN CALUMNY) In oppression: that is, in riches obtained by force. See above 6.

AND IN TUMULT) In perversity.

Latin:

Vers. 12. IN CALUMNIA) In oppressione: id est, in opibus per vim partis. Vide supra 6.

ET IN TVMVLTU) In pravitate.

## 30:13
AS A BREACH FALLING AND REQUIRED IN A HIGH WALL.) As a part departing from a high wall, and being near to ruin, it juts out. So also their swelling will threaten ruin. See Ps. 62:4.

SINCE SUDDENLY WHILE IT IS NOT HOPED FOR, HIS DESTRUCTION SHALL COME.) That is, falling into pieces it will shatter.

Brentius has provided a clear paraphrase: Since therefore your impiety is so great that the word of the Lord is a source of the greatest disgust to you, come now, hear what that Holy GOD says, who chose Israel as His own people, and promised that He would give His Christ from it. For the reason that you reject this word, namely the promise by which I undertook that I would defend you from enemies and preserve you in all adversities, and you hope in calumny and perversity, that is, in the wealth and riches which you have acquired by impostures, calumnies, iniquities, and evil arts, and by which at this time you are undertaking to summon help from Egypt. Therefore, on account of this iniquity, extreme destruction will befall you. For just as a very high wall, if it begins to bulge and has received a crack, is accustomed to fall suddenly, beyond all expectation: So you have indeed been hitherto lofty and illustrious by the blessing of the Lord, but because you have begun to be split by the rupture of impiety, the time will come when you shall fall into extreme destruction unexpectedly. And just as when a notable stone falls, a clay vessel of a potter is crushed with such shattering that not even a shard is found with which you might take fire from a hearth, or with which you might draw water from a cistern: So also you, who have hitherto been vessels of the mercy of God, will be so oppressed that hardly any remnants will be saved. And although God strengthened the Kingdom of Judah during the incursion of the King of Assyria, on account of the most pious King Hezekiah: yet there is no doubt that those impious men (who had been the authors of seeking Egyptian protection, and placed their hope in them, not in God) paid heavy penalties for their impiety. And because the Jewish people labored under this vice perpetually, they finally collapsed, like a wall, when they were led away into captivity by the Babylonians: but they were utterly crushed, like a pitcher dashed against a rock, when the city was captured by the Romans, and the people were cast into eternal exile, and miserably scattered throughout the world. As Osiander rightly observes here. Ver. 15. IF YOU RETURN) That is, if you depart from those counsels. Ver. 16. WE WILL FLEE TO HORSES.) We will have our refuge in Egypt, strong in horses. See Deut. 17, 16. and what is said there. THEREFORE YOU WILL FLEE.) You will go into exile. Others, we will escape the danger on horses, which, namely, threatens from the Assyrians, therefore you will flee before the enemy. AND UPON THE SWIFT (horses, such as the Egyptians have) WE WILL ASCEND, so that together with the Egyptian Cavalry we may repel the force of the Assyrian King. THEREFORE THEY WILL BE SWIFTER WHO PURSUE YOU. Ver. 17. A THOUSAND MEN AT THE FACE OF THE TERROR OF ONE, AND AT THE FACE OF THE TERROR OF FIVE YOU WILL FLEE.) Namely all: that is, the dread will be so great that the sight of a few will put many to flight. The opposite, a promise to those keeping the law. See Levit. 26, 8. Deuteron. 32, 30. AS A SHIP'S MAST ON THE TOP OF A MOUNTAIN, AND AS A SIGN UPON A HILL) That is, few of the Jews will remain, with such rarity as monuments of a sea-course are wont to be. We approve here the Paraphrase and explanation of Osiander: The enemies will scatter you with slaughter and terror in such a way that very few of you are left: as when a forest is felled, and in it here and there one or another tall and straight tree is left, which is preserved so that it may provide, when necessity demands, a ship's mast to which a sail may be attached: or just as a wooden column, solitary, is placed in a high place (a wayside shrine) so that travelers may know in which direction they ought to steer their journey. B. Luther, however, understands the mast metaphorically as a spear, from which a banner hangs: that nothing will remain of the army except a military sign. But because this whole threat, as Osiander also observed, looks not only to that Assyrian devastation, but to a more serious destruction, indeed the reprobation of the people, and therefore it also had to be written on a box and in a book, so that by these two means the memory might be preserved, and in the last time they might be a TESTIMONY UNTO ETERNITY. Add here the explanation of Brentius. The Prophet prophesies that although the Israelites were chosen as the people of God, yet they were to be cast off by God from that time when, having despised the promises of God, they sought Egyptian aid. For after they began in the times of Isaiah to trust more in human and external aid than in the divine promise, they also began to fall, until they perished completely. And in the beginning indeed they fell by the Babylonian captivity, which was a ruin, just as if a wall had fallen, in which case the stones nevertheless remain, so that the building can be restored again. Thus also the Jews were restored again after the Babylonian captivity, somehow into some form of polity: But then they fell by the Roman devastation, which was a ruin, just as an earthen vessel is crushed by a huge stone. In which crushing not even a shard is left whole, so that you can draw water. Thus also the Jews in the Roman devastation were so constricted that not only did they never recover their land and polities, but they were also excluded from the inheritance of heavenly goods, and very few of them, who acknowledged Christ, were truly saved.

Latin:

SICUT INTERRVPTIO CADENS ET REQVI- SITA IN MURO EXCELSO.) Sicut pars discedens à mu- ro excelso, & ruinæ proxima præminet. Sic & illorum tu- mor ruinam minabitur. Vid. Ps. 62, 4.

QVONIAM SVBITO DVM NON SPERATUR, VENIET CONTRITIO EJUS.) Id est, cadens in parti- culas dissiliet.

Paraphrasin perspicuam tradidit Brentius : Cum ergo tanta sit impietas vestra, ut verbum Domini vobis summo sit fastidio, agite dum, audite, quid dicat Sanctus ille DEUS, qui Is- raëlem in populum suum elegit, & se ex eo Chri- stum suum daturum promisit. Pro eo, quod re- probatis verbum hoc, promissionem videlicet, qua recepi me vos ab hostibus defensurum & conservaturum in omnibus adversis, & speratis in calumniam & perversitatem, hoc est, in opes & divitias, quas imposturis, calumniis, iniquitati- bus, & malis artibus acquisivistis, & quibus hoc tempore suscipitis vocanda auxilia ex Ægypto. Id- circo propter hanc iniquitatem accidet vobis ex- trema internecio. Nam quemadmodum præaltus murus si incipiat turgescere, & acceperit fissuram, solet subito, præter omnem expectationem de- cidere : Ita vos fuistis quidem hactenus benedi- ctione Domini sublimes & illustres, sed quia in- cepistis diffindi ruptura impietatis, veniet tempus, quo in extremum interitum ex improviso decida- tis. Et sicut cadente insigni lapide testaceum va- sculum figuli tanta comminutione conteritur, ut ne testa quidem inveniatur, qua ignem de foco excipias, aut qua aquam è cisterna haurias : Ita & vos, qui hactenus fuistis vasa misericordiæ Dei, ita opprimemini, ut vix aliquæ reliquiæ salvæ fiant. Etfi autem Deus in incurfione Regis Affyriaci con- fortavit Regnum Juda, propter piiffimum Regem Ezechiam: tamen non dubium est, impios illos homines (qui autores fuerant, ut quærerentur Æ- gyptiaca præsidia, spemq; suam in illis, non in Deo habuerunt) graves dedisse suæ impietatis pœnas. Et quia populus Judaicus perpetuo hoc vitio labo- ravit, tandem corruit, ut murus, quum à Babylo- niis abductus est in captivitatem: plane autem con- tritus est, ut hydria petræ allisa, quando à Romanis urbs est capta, & populus in æternum exilium est ejestus, & in orbem terrarum misere dissipatus. Ut hic recte observat Ofiander. Vers. 15. SI REVERTAMINI) Id est, si ab illis consi- liis discedatis. Vers. 16. AD EQVOS FVGIEMVS.) Confugium nostrum habebimus ad Ægyptum, equis valentem. Vid. Deut. 17, 16. & ibi dicta. IDEO FVGIETIS.) Exsulabitis. Alii, super equos effugiemus periculum, quod sc. imminet ab Assyriis, ideo fugietis coram hoste. ET SUPER VELOCES (equos, quales Ægyptii habent) ASCENDEMUS, ut una cum Ægyptio- rum Equitatu propulsemus vim Assyriaci Regis. IDEO VELOCIORES ERUNT, QUI PER- SEQUENTUR VOS. Vers. 17. MILLE HOMINES A FACIE TERRORIS VNI- VS, ET A FACIE TERRORIS QVINQVE FVGIE- TIS.) Nempe omnes: id est, pavor erit tantus, ut pau- corum conspectus plurimos in fugam sit daturus. Oppoft- tum, promissum legem servantibus. Vid. Levit. 26, 8. Deu- teron. 32, 30. QUASI MALUS NAVIS IN VERTICE MONTIS, ET QUASI SIGNVM SVPER COLLEM) Id est, pauci Judæorum restabunt, tanta raritate, quanta esse solent mo numenta cursus marini. Probamus hic Paraphrasin & explicationem Osiandrinam: Hostes cædibus & terrore ita vos dis- sipabunt, ut paucissimi ex vobis relinquantur: quasi cum cæditur sylva, & in ea hinc inde relinquitur una & altera arbor alta & directa, quæ asservatur, ut præbeat aliquando, postulante necessitate, malum na- vis, cui velum appendatur: aut sicut columna lignea, solitaria, in sublimi loco collocatur (ein Bildstock) ut sciant peregrinantes, qua debeant iter suum in- tendere. B. Lutherus tamen malum metaphorice intelligit de hasta, è qua vexillum pendet: quod ni- hil reliquum futurum sit de exercitu, nisi militare signum. Quia vero tota hæc comminatio, quod Osiander etiam observavit, non illam solum vasta- tionem Assyriacam, sed gravius excidium, imo re- probationem populi spectat, atque ideo etiam su- per buxum, & in libro scribi debuit, ut duobus istis modis conservarentur memoria, & in tempore no- vissimo TESTIMONIUM essent USQUE IN ÆTERNUM. Addenda hic Brentii explicatio. Vaticinatur Propheta, quod etsi Israëlitæ electi sunt in populum Dei, tamen abjiciendi sint à Deo ab eo tempore, quo contemptis promissionibus Dei, quæsiverint auxilia Ægyptiaca. Postquam enim Esaiæ temporibus inceperunt magis huma- no & externo auxilio, quam divina promissione confidere, inceperunt etiam ruere, donec penitus interierint. Ac initio quidem corruerunt captivi- tate Babylonica, quæ ruina fuit, quemadmodum si murus ceciderit, in quo casu remanent tamen la- pides, ut iterum possit ædificium instaurari. Sic & Judæi iterum post Babylonicam captivitatem resti- tuti sunt utcunq; in aliquam formam politiæ: Dein- de autem corruerunt Romana vastatione, quæ rui- na fuit, sicut vas figulinum conteritur ab ingenti lapide. In qua contritione ne testa quidem relin- quitur integra, ut possis aquam haurire. Sic & Ju- dæi in Romana vastatione ita constricti sunt, ut non solum nusquam receperint suam terram, & politiæ, verum etiam exclusi sint ex hæreditate cœlestium bonorum, ac paucissimi ex ipsis, qui a- gnoverunt Christum, vere servati fuerint.

## 30:18
Ver. 18. THEREFORE THE LORD WAITS, THAT HE MAY HAVE MERCY ON YOU: AND THEREFORE HE WILL BE EXALTED SPAREING YOU.) That is, that he may be exalted. Therefore God delays his help, so that his power may appear greater.

To others, the little word לָכֵן is taken simply as a copulative, as is the varied use of conjunctions among the Hebrews, who understand the words THEREFORE HE WILL BE EXALTED thus: he will arise, he will gird himself, so that he may help you, THAT HE MAY HAVE MERCY from the most ardent affection and love, with which mothers are wont to embrace their children, Is. 49. Vatablus, he will be exalted, he will suspend the blow sparing you. Others in the opposite sense, he will lift his hand on high, as if threatening a powerful blow. But the exaltation or glorification of divine clemency is understood, as Jerome also rightly observed. But our Brentius has conveniently explained the sum of the promise, which begins here, and the whole discourse of this chapter, which, because the scope is already known, has no difficulty, there is no reason for us to labor much on it. For it is promised then the liberation and preservation of the city without external aid, indeed that the Lord wishes not only to preserve the external polity, but also to bestow various benefits necessary for the well-being of the Republic, governors, Teachers, fertility, bread, rain, etc. Then the slaughter of the King and the army of Assyria threatening, that the army is to be miraculously destroyed, and shortly the King himself is to perish.

GOD IS THE LORD OF JUDGMENT.) Tenacious of his law.

Brentius's observation on the Hebrew word is to be preferred: The Lord does not wish to permit the Assyrian enemy to oppress you, because God is the Lord of Judgment. For Judgment the Hebrew has מִשְׁפָּט, which signifies Judgment, Right, rule, ordinance, decree, constitution, and other things of that kind. The meaning therefore is, God does not wish to permit the Assyrians to plunder your city at this time, because God keeps his rule, keeps his right, keeps his decrees and ordinances. He has established and decreed, however, to free you from the hands of the enemies. He promises that he will defend you from the Assyrian. The rule and ordinance of God is that, although the kingdom of Israel has been abolished, yet the kingdom of Judah is not to be abolished at this time. Therefore be strong in spirit, only await the help of God, and the liberation will be certain. Nor is the marginal gloss of the blessed Luther to be rejected: The Lord is a God of judgment, not of raging or fury, but one who punishes with moderation, and does not do too much to him, as the vengeful are wont to do, Jer. 30, 11. He chastises in judgment and measure, that is, moderately and with fruit, he does not destroy entirely, as his Latin exposition has it.

BLESSED ARE ALL WHO WAIT FOR HIM) That is, who do not depart from the law for fear of any danger.

But these things are different, even if they cohere with one another: to wait for the Lord, which is done through trust in Him in adversity, and not to depart from the law of God. For this passage contains an exhortation and a provocation to believe, as the blessed Luther observes. Compare Hab. 2, 3, where the same verb חָכָה occurs regarding trustful waiting: and also Is. 8, 18. I will wait for the Lord, who will hide His face from the House of Jacob, c. 64, 4. which You have prepared for those who wait for You. Dan. 12, v. pen. Blessed is he who will wait. Ps. 33, 20. Our soul sustains (waits for) the Lord, because He is our helper and protector. The same verb in all places is used to signify the expectation which is made with the greatest effort, just as the hungry, with open mouth and adjusted palate, greedily gape for food, as Avenarius gathers in his Lexicon from the affinity with the word חָכָה. FOR THE PEOPLE OF SION SHALL DWELL IN JERUSALEM) It shall not be taken away, as others of the Jews. THOU SHALT WEEP NO MORE) That is, you shall not weep for long, O city of Jerusalem. Verse 20. AND THE LORD SHALL GIVE YOU BREAD OF TRIBULATION.) The Lord shall indeed give you the bread of distress: you shall be fed sparingly. AND SHORT WATER.) See above 22, 9. AND THY TEACHER SHALL NOT FLY AWAY FROM THEE ANY MORE.) Truly, good teachers shall not be absent from you: of whom Isaiah himself was the chief. Verse 21. THEY SHALL HEAR THE WORD BEHIND THE BACK OF THE ADMONISHER.) Just as pedagogues recall the boys following them to the true path, if by chance they should deflect. Grotius correctly expresses the sense. Yet the translation of B. Luther is not to be disapproved: The Lord will give you bread in tribulation, and water in distress. Which Amama criticized in his Biblisch. conferenz according to his custom. The sense remains the same. For both tribulation is thus predicted, and in tribulation bread and water, as far as necessity is concerned, and at the same time the refreshment of the word is promised, because man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. Deut. 8. Matt. 4. Nor does God take less care of the soul of the faithful in adversity than of the body. The version of Junius and the English version should rather have been criticized: None of those who teach you shall be enclosed in a CORNER any more. For the things that are subjoined teach that the word יִכָּנֵף here obtains the meaning of flying away rather, because they are said to be about to see with their eyes and hear with their ears their Teachers. Whence also with that meaning [it agrees] with the Vulgate of Jerome. D. Luther, Piscator, the Genevan and Italian, as well as the New Belgian translation, have rendered it. We do not see the wallet that is on the back! which often happens to the good Amama in that itch of amending the Belgian version adorned from the Lutheran German. Who also does not quite conveniently restrict these things to John the Baptist, Christ, and the Apostles. For not only are the teachers of the New Testament looked at, nor even, as Amama wishes, the Prophets alone, but there is a promise concerning the preserving of the ministers and teachers of the word among the people of God, even in anxiety and pressure, and it looks primarily at the calamity brought by Sennacherib. As for those words which Amama wishes to be rendered κατὰ πόδα, when you turn to the right, and when you turn to the left, and which he judges to be correctly rendered by Piscator, Junius, the English, Italian, and Genevan versions, when you shall have declined to the right or to the left, the sense again fits well, which B. Luther expressed with the Vulgate: Otherwise neither to the right, nor to the left. For while they are recalled to the path by the Teacher, those who deflect to the right and to the left are warned, indeed, to persist in that path and not to deflect to the right or to the left; they will deflect to the right by indulging their own good intention and chosen forms of worship, and to the left by depraved affections. Verse 22. AND YOU SHALL CONTAMINATE THE PLATES OF YOUR SILVER GRAVEN IMAGES.) That broken silver, from which the idols consisted and which was reduced into plates, you shall turn to profane uses, AND THE GARMENT OF YOUR MOLTEN GOLD.) Thus for Jupiter Olympius there was a golden cloak of great weight, as Valerius Maximus teaches us in book 1, chapter 3 of the externals: Clement of Alexandria, Arnobius, and others. AND YOU SHALL SCATTER THEM.) You shall keep such things far from you in the future. Verse 23. RAIN SHALL BE GIVEN TO YOUR SEED.) That is, to your sowing, which you shall have sown, as the following words show. There was a great abundance of things under the reign of Hezekiah. Our Brentius interprets these more correctly hypothetically, as if to say. The Prophet: God does not demand only from you that you sit quiet and tranquil in Jerusalem, nor that you summon Egyptian aid; but He also demands that you contaminate, or that you cast away as filthy and profane, your graven images covered with silver and your images molten from gold, and that you scatter them like the filth of a menstruous woman, and say to them, away with you hence to the devil. If you do this, the Lord will bless your land, according to the promises of Deut. 28 and Levit. 25. He shall give rain to your seed, wherever you shall have sown in the land, and the bread or fruit of the land shall be copious and most rich. Yet there is held here at the same time a promise, as Osiander observed: Then when you shall have experienced the help of God in repelling the Assyrians, you shall turn more perfectly to the Lord your God. And if by chance any silver or golden idols remained among some (secretly), which you had adorned with precious garments, then you shall cast all those things out (like the cloth of a menstruous woman) with great abomination and detestation, saying, Go out, you wicked and abominable thing, away with you, you loathsome filth. Then also (after the Lord shall have destroyed the Assyrians) the Lord will abundantly compensate with a copious harvest of crops for those things which the enemy had laid waste. And convenient and fruitful rain shall be given to your seed, wherever you shall have sown it in the land of the kingdom of Judah: you shall experience fruitful seasons everywhere. Amama here again corrects the Lutheran version, Your silvered idols, because in the Hebrew it is a covering, as the Italian, Spanish, English, and Genevan versions rendered it. But when the covering of idols is contaminated, it is certain that the idols themselves are contaminated. B. Luther, however, looked to the sense and did not always render word for word. Which is also observed in the word Unflat. For we do not deny that the Hebrew word דָּוָה designates specifically menstrual blood, which Junius, Piscator, the Spaniards, the English, the Italian, and the new Belgian version express, as does the Latin Vulgate: AS THE FILTH OF A MENSTRUOUS WOMAN. BREAD) See above 28, 28.

Latin:

Vers. 18. PROPTEREA EXPECTAT DOMINUS, UT MISEREATUR VESTRI : ET IDEO EXALTABI- TUR PARCENS VOBIS.) Id est, ut exaltetur. Ideo differt Deus auxilium suum, ut major appareat ejus po- tentia.

Aliis vocula לָכֵן simpliciter pro copulativa acci- pitur, uti varię solet esse usus conjunctionum apud Ebræos, qui verbum IDEO EXALTABITUR ita intelligunt, exurget, accinget se, ut vobis succur- rat, UT MISEREATUR ex ardentissimo affectu & amore, quo matres solent amplecti liberos suos Es. 49. Vatablus, exaltabitur, suspendet ictum parcens vobis. Alii contrario sensu, in altum tollet manum, quasi minitans validam plagam. Sed exaltatio vel glorificatio clementiæ divinæ intelligitur, uti recte etiam observavit Hieronymus. Summam autem promissionis, quæ hic inchoatur, totamque illam concionem hujus capitis commode imprimis ex- posuit Brentius noster, quæ quia, cognito jam sco- po, nullam difficultatem habet, non est, quod in ea multum laboremus. Promittitur nempe tum libe- ratio & conservatio urbis absque externo auxilio, imo quod non tantum externam politiam conser- vare, sed etiam varia beneficia donare velit Domi- nus ad εὐεξίαν Reipubl. necessaria, gubernatores, Doctores, fertilitatem, panem, pluviam, &c. Tum Regis & exercitus Assyriæ interitum comminan- tis internecio, quod mirabiliter exercitus delen- dus, brevi etiam Rex ipse periturus sit.

DEUS JUDICII DOMINUS.) Legis suæ tenax.

Præferenda Brentii observatio de Ebræa vo- ce: Non vult committere Dominus, ut hostis Assy- riacus vos opprimat, quia Deus est Judicii Dominus. Pro Judicio Ebræus habet מִשְׁפָּט, quod significat Ju- dicium, Jus, regulam, ordinationem, decretum, constitutionem, & id genus alia. Sententia igitur est, Deus non vult permittere, ut Assyrii hoc tem- pore vestram urbem diripiant, quia Deus servat re- gulam suam, servat jus suum, servat decreta & or- dinationes suas. Constituit autem & decrevit vos manibus hostium liberare. Promittit se vos ab As- syrio defensurum. Regula & ordinatio Dei est, ut etsi abolitum est regnum Israël, tamen regnum Ju- dæ hoc tempore non aboleatur. Quare estote for- tes animo, expectate tantum auxilium Dei, & certa erit liberatio. Neq; reprobanda B. Lutheri mar- ginalis glossa : Der HErr ist ein Gott des Gerichts, nicht des Wütens oder Grimmes, sondern der da straffet mit massen, und thut ihm nicht zu viel, wie die Rachgierigen pflegen, Jer. 30, 11. Castigat in ju- dicio & mensura, id est, modice & cum fructu, non perdit omnino, ut habet enarratio ejus Latina.

BEATI OMNES, QVI EXPECTANT EUM) Id est, qui nullius periculi metu a lege discedunt.

At hæc diversa sunt, etsi inter se cohæreant: expectare Dominum, quod fit per fiduciam in ipsum in adversis, & non discedere à lege Dei. Continet e- nim hic locus adhortationem & provocationem ad credendum, uti B. Lutherus observat. Confer Hab. 2, 3. ubi idem verbum חָכָה de fiduciali expe- ctatione occurrit : nec non Es. 8, 18. Expectabo Dominum, qui abscondet faciem suam à Domo Jacob, c. 64, 4. quæ præparasti expectantibus te. Dan. 12. v. pen. Beatus ille, qui expectabit. Ps. 33, 20. Anima no- stra sustinet (expectat) Dominum, quoniam adjutor & protector noster est. Verbū idem in omnibꝫ locis adhibitum est, significare expectationem, quæ summo nisu fit, quemadmodum famelici aperto o- re, aptato palato avide inhiant escam, ut è cognati- one cum verbo חָכָה colligit Avenarius in Lexic. POPULUS ENIM SION HABITABIT IN JERU- SALEM) Non auferetur, ut alii Judæorum. PLORANS NEQUAQUAM PLORABIS) Id est, non diu flebis, ô civitas Hierosolymorum. Vers. 20. ET DABIT VOBIS DOMINUS PANEM ARCTUM.) Dabit quidem vobis Dominus panem angustiæ: modice cibaberis. ET AQVAM BREVEM.) Vid. supra 22, 9. ET NON FACIET AVOLARE A TE ULTRA DOCTOREM TUUM.) Verum non aberunt à te boni ma- gistri: quorum præcipuus fuit ipse Esaias. Vers. 21. AUDIENT VERBUM POST TERGUM MO- NENTIS.) Sicut pædagogi pueros sequentes, eos ad ve- rum iter revocant, si qua forte deflectant. Sensum recte exprimit Grotius. Neque ta- men improbanda B. Lutheri translatio: Der HErr wird euch in Trübsal Brod, und in Aengsten Wasser geben. Quam pro more suo taxavit Ama- ma in Biblisch. conferenz. Sensus idem manet. Nam & tribulatio ita prædicitur, & in tribulatione panis & aqua, quantum ad necessitatem, simulque refectio verbi promittitur, quia non solo pane vivit homo, sed omni verbo, quod ex ore Dei egreditur. Deut. 8. Matth. 4. neque minorem Deus curam gerit animæ fidelium in adversis, quam corporis. Reprehendenda potius fuisset versio Junii & An- glicana: Non includetur ANGULO amplius ullus docentium te. Verbum enim יִכָּנֵף hic avolandi si- gnificationem potius obtinere, ea quæ subjungun- tur, docent, quia dicuntur oculis suis visuri, & au- ribus suis audire Doctores. Unde etiam ea signi- ficatione cum vulgata Hieronym. D. Lutheri, Pi- scatoris, Genevensis & Italicis, nec non Nova Bel- gica translatio reddidêre. Non videmus manticæ, quod in tergo est! quod sæpe bono Amamæ evenit in ista prurigine emendandi versionem Belgicam è Lutherana Germanica adornatam. Qui etiam hæc non satis commode restringit ad Johannem Bapti- stam, Christum, & Apostolos. Non enim solum No- vi Test. Doctores spectantur, neque etiam quod vult Amama, Prophetæ soli, sed promissio habetur de conservandis ministris & Doctoribus verbi, in po- pulo Dei, etiam in anxietate & pressura, ac respici- tur cumprimis calamitas à Sennacheribo illata. Quod ad verba illa, quæ κατὰ πόδα reddi vult A- mama, quando dextrabitis, & quando sinistrabitis, & à Piscat, Junio, Anglo, Italo, Genev. recte reddita censet, cum ad dextram vel sinistram declinaveri- tis, sensus iterum probe congruit, quem B. Luthe- rus cum Vulgata expressit: Sonst weder zur Rech- ten, noch zur Lincken. Dum enim à Doctore in viam revocantur, qui ad dextram & sinistram de- flectunt, monentur utique, ut via illa insistant, neque ad dextram vel ad sinistram deflectant, ad dextram declinabunt indulgendo propriæ bonæ intentioni, & cultibus electitiis, ad sinistram pra- vis affectibus. Vers. 22. ET CONTAMINABIS LAMINAS SCUL- PTILIUM ARGENTI TUI.) Confractum argentum illud, unde idola constabant, & in laminas redactum vertes in usus profanos, ET VESTIMENTUM CONFLATILIS AURI TUI.) Sic Jovi Olympio erat magni ponderis aureum amiculum, ut nos docent Valerius Maximus l. 1. externorum tertio: Clemens Alexandrinus, Arnobius, alii. ET DISPERGES EA.) A te longe habebis talia in posterum. Vers. 23. DABITUR PLUVIA SEMINI TUO.) Id est, sementi tuæ, quam conseveris, ut monstrant verba sequen- tia, Magna rerum abundantia fuit sub Regno Ezechiæ. Rectius Brentius noster hæc hypothetice in- terpretatur, q. d. Propheta: Deus non exigit so- lum à vobis, ut quieti & tranquilli sedeatis in Hie- rufalem, nec advocetis auxilia Ægyptiaca; Sed ex- igit etiam, ut contaminetis, seu ut sordida & pro- fana abjiciatis sculptilia vestra argento obducta, & simulacra ex auro conflata, ac dispergas ea sicut immunditiam mulieris menstruatæ, dicasque eis, apage te hinc in malam crucem. Hoc si feceris, benedicet Dominus terræ tuæ, juxta promissiones Deut. 28. & Levit. 25. Dabit pluviam semini tuo, ubicunque seminaveris in terra, & panis seu fructus terræ erit copiosus & uberrimus. Habetur tamen hic simul promissio, uti observavit Osiander: Tunc cum experti fueritis auxilium Dei in repellendis As- syriis, perfectius convertemini ad Dominum Deum vestrum. Ac siqua forte apud aliquos (clanculum) remanserint idola argentea vel aurea, quæ pretiosis vestibus exornastis, tunc ea omnia (tanquam pannum menstruatæ mulieris) foras projicietis cum ingenti abominatione & detestatione, dicentes, Exi res scele- sta & abominabilis, hinaus mit dir, du greulicher Unflat. Tunc etiam (postquam Dominus Assy- rios deleverit) copioso proventu frugum Dominus abunde compensabit ea, quæ hostis vastaverat. Et dabitur pluvia commoda & fæcunda semini tuo, ubi- cunque seminaveris illud in terra regni Juda: pas- sim fœcundas tempestates experieris. Corrigit hic iterum Lutheranam versionem Amama, Eure ü- bersilberte Götzen, quod in Ebræo sit operimentum, uti Ital. Hispan. Anglic. Genev. reddiderunt. Sed cum contaminatur operimentum idolorum, ipsa ido- la contaminari certum est. Sensum autem respexit B. Lutherus, nec semper verbum verbo reddidit. Quod etiam in voce Unflat observatur. Ebræum enim דָּוָה sanguinem menstruum peculiariter de- signare, non inficiamur, quem exprimit Junius, Piscator, Hispani, Angli, Italus, & nova Belgica versio, ut & Vulgata Latina: SICUT IMMUNDI- TIAM MENSTRUATÆ MULIERIS. PANIS) Vide supra 28, 28.

## 30:24
Verse 24.

THEY SHALL EAT MIXED PROVENDER) The LXX have here Ἄχυρα ἀναπεποιημένα ἐν κριθῇ. Thus Jud. 19, 21, in the Hebrew it is, he mixed for the asses. Ἀναποιέω for to mix is frequent among the Interpreters, as Levit. 6, 40. 7, 2. 23, 13. Num. 6, 15. 8, 9. 9, 12. 29, 3. AS IT IS WINNOWED IN THE FLOOR) In the Hebrew: Winnowed with a shovel and a fan. Most diligently cleaned, such will be the abundance. Amama rashly corrects Luther's version here, which uses the word gemenget Futter, which ought to have been rendered sluggish fodder. The Hebrew חָמִיץ is fermented: or seasoned with sourness, by which sourness it might provoke the appetite, concerning which see Cornelius à Lapide, mixed from various kinds of grain. Namely, as Jerome says, that by its variety it might be more pleasing. The new Dutch Interpreters themselves rendered it acid: but not pure. Nor is the Hebrew word ever taken in that way. And so the blessed Luther himself explained it in a marginal gloss, Gemenget, gebessert, oder getemperirt mit Süßigkeit: for the word בָּלִיל also implies a mixture.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

COMMISTUM MIGMA COMEDENT) Ἄχυρα ἀναπεποιημένα ἐν κριθῇ habent hic LXX. Sic. Jud. 19, 21. in Hebræo est, miscuit Asinis. Ἀναποιέω pro miscere fre- quens Interpretibus, ut Levit. 6, 40. 7, 2. 23, 13. Num. 6, 15. 8, 9. 9, 12. 29, 3. SICUT IN AREA VENTILATUM EST) In He- bræo: Ventilatum palo & ventilabro. Diligentissime purga- tum, tanta erit copia. Temere hic iterum corrigit Lutheri versio- nem Amama, qua qocem gemenget Futter, quod reddi debuerit pigrum pabulum. Ebræum חָמִיץ est fermentatum: seu acore conditum, quo acore suo appetitum provocet, quo de vid. Cornel. à Lapide, è variis generis frumentis mixtum. Scil. ut Hiero- nymus, ut varietate sua gratius sit. Belgici Interpp. novi ipsimet reddidere acidum: non vero purum. Neq; uspiam ita vox Ebræa accipitur. Atq; ita ex- posuit ipse B. Lutherus in glossa marginali, Ge- menget, gebessert, oder getemperirt mit Süßigkeit: nam vox בָּלִיל etiam infert mixtionem.

## 30:25
Verse 25.

RIVERS OF RUNNING WATERS) There will be such rain that even those things which by their own nature are most arid will be moistened. IN THE DAY OF THE SLAUGHTER OF MANY) After that slaughter of the Assyrians. Thus often בְּיוֹם signifies the subsequent time. WHEN THE TOWERS SHALL FALL) See above 11, 13. The towers here are the princes of the Assyrians.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

RIVI CURRENTIUM AQUARUM) Tanta erit pluvia, ut etiam ea madescant, quæ suapte natura erunt a- ridissima. IN DIE INTERFECTIONIS MULTORUM) Post illam stragem Assyriorum. Sic sæpe בְּיוֹם tempus sub- sequens significat. CUM CECIDERINT TURRES) Vide supra 11, 13. Turres hic sunt principes Assyriorum.

## 30:26
Verse 26.

AND THE LIGHT OF THE MOON SHALL BE AS THE LIGHT OF THE SUN.) A signification of joy. Thus the poets: The day itself seemed to me to go more beautiful. See what was said at Matt. 24, 29. AND THE LIGHT OF THE SUN SHALL BE SEVENFOLD AS THE LIGHT OF SEVEN DAYS.) The light will be sevenfold, as if besides the Sun there were six mock suns.

ON THE DAY, ON WHICH THE LORD SHALL BIND UP THE WOUND OF HIS PEOPLE.) After God shall have delivered the city of Jerusalem from all the evils which it was enduring and which it was fearing.

Most people understand these things as referring to the last day: that then the splendor of the Moon will be such that it will be seven times the splendor of the Sun, that is, far brighter than usual; which explanation Cornel. à Lapide observes is that of Jerome, Lyranus, Dionysius, Haymo, and Adam, and he prefers it to the other interpretations. Which also Tirinus and Menochius have followed. But others, both Hebrew and Christian interpreters—Hugo, Vatablus, Sanctius, Forerius, and among our own also B. Luther, Brentius, Osiander, and others—as well as most of the Reformed, understand that there will be the greatest light and joy when the Jews are liberated, as if the Moon were seen to shine there with the splendor of the Sun, and seven times more brightly than before, just as Light and the Sun are said to have risen for the Jews (Esth. 8:16; ch. 11:11). For to the sad and afflicted, the Sun and Moon seem clearly obscured. But after they have been liberated from affliction, and the mind is cheerful, all the stars seem brighter to them. There is, therefore, here an exaggeration of joy according to the affection of the pious, who have been suddenly liberated from most imminent death, as B. Luther rightly says; because the joy of the faithful is to be perfect only in the other life, therefore these interpretations can not inappropriately be joined: that for Hezekiah and other faithful ones, through that remarkable divine liberation, a huge joy shone forth, which was to arise when the Lord was about to heal the wound of the Jewish Republic inflicted by the Assyrians, especially because they were to perceive in it a foretaste (πρόγευσμα) of divine grace and everlasting joy: For as often as the elect are suffused with joy from the sense of divine grace, all things are the more cheerful and splendid to them, the more they know how to estimate from present grace and divine manifestation (φανερώσει) the glory of future happiness and divine manifestation (φανερώσεως). And therefore the opinion of B. Osiander is to be approved here entirely. Although the Prophet speaks here of the bodily liberation which occurred under King Hezekiah, yet this prophecy will then be most perfectly fulfilled when, liberated from every evil, we shall rejoice in the heavenly Kingdom with Christ for all eternity. The Papists, however, wrongly infer from this that the Sun and other material stars will attain greater splendor in the other life, either from the glory of glorified bodies or immediately from God himself. For as the earth, so also the heaven shall perish (Luke 16). The heavenly city does not need the Sun nor the Moon to shine in it. For the brightness of God shall illuminate it (Rev. 21:23; ch. 22). The Vinarienses (v. 25 and 26) explain it regarding the victory of Christ, by which through his death he overcame death, and brought forth true joy for us by his redemption. But the preceding and following context openly confirms the explanation of B. Luther already handed down. It does not please Amama that Luther rendered it (The sunlight will be seven times brighter than now), since the Hebrew text has כְּאֹור שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים as the light of seven days, as Piscator, Junius, the French, Italian, Spanish, English, and Genevan versions have. But since Luther said the splendor of the Sun would be seven times brighter than usual, does not the same sense result, namely that it will be just as if the light of the Sun of seven days had been collected into one day, as Amama thinks it should be explained?

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ET ERIT LUX LUNÆ SICUT LUX SOLIS.) Gau- dii significatio. Sic Poëtæ: Ipse mihi visus pulchrior ire dies. Vid. quæ dicta ad Matth. 24, 29. ET LUX SOLIS ERIT SEPTEMPLICITER SICVT LUX SEPTEM DIERUM.) Lux erit septupla, quasi præ- ter Solem sex essent Parelii,

IN DIE, QUA ALLIGAVERIT DOMINUS VUL- NUS POPULI SUI.) Postquam Deus civitatem Hiero- solymorum ab omnibus malis, quæ tolerabat, quæq; me- tuebat, exemerit.

Pleriq; hæc accipiunt de die novissimo: quod tunc Lunæ splendor is futurus sit, qui Solis splen- dorseptuplus, id est, longe clarior solito futurus sit; quam Hieronymi, Lyrani, Dionysii, Haymonis, & Adami esse explicationem, observat Cornel. à Lapide, ac cæteris interpretationibus præfert. Quam etiam sequutus est Tirinus & Menochius. Sed alii cum Hebræi, tum Christiani Interpp. Hugo, Vatablus, Sanctius, Forerius, è nostris etiam B. Lu- therus, Brentius, Osiander & alii; tum Reformati plerique Judæis liberatis summam fore lucem & læ- titiam intelligunt, quasi videatur Luna Solis splen- dore illic lucere, ac septuplo amplius, quam ante splendere, uti Lux & Sol ortus dicitur Judæis Esth. 8, 16. c. 11, 11. Tristibus enim & afflictis Sol & Lu- na videntur plane obscuræ. Postquam autem libe- rati fuerint ab afflictione, animusque hilaris est, videntur ipsis omnes stellæ lucidiores. Est ergo, hic exaggeratio lætitiæ secundum affectum piorum; qui subito ex præsentissima morte sunt liberati, ut recte B. Lutherus, quia lætitia fidelium in altera demum vita perfecta futura est, idcirco conjungi non incommode possunt hæ interpretationes: quod Ezechiæ, aliisque fidelibus per insignem il- lam liberationem divinam luxit gaudium ingens, exoriturum, quando Dominus vulnus Reip. Ju- daicæ ab Assyriis inflictum curaturus est, maxime quod ipsi in eo sensum gratię divinę ac lætitiæ sem- piternæ πρόγευσμα percepturi sint: Quoties enim electi gaudio è divinæ gratiæ sensu perfunduntur, tanto illis hilariora, & splendidiora sunt omnia, quanto magis è præsenti gratia & φανερώσει divi- na noverint æstimare futuræ felicitatis, ac φανερώ- σεως divinæ gloriam. Ideoq; hic probanda omni- no B. Osiandrisententia. Etsi Propheta hic de libera- tione corporali loquitur, quæ sub Rege Ezechia con- tigit, tamen hæc Prophetia tunc perfectissime imple- bitur, cum ab omni malo liberati in cælesti Regno cum Christo in omnem æternitatem gaudebimus. Perperam tamen Papistæ inde colligunt, Solem & alia sydera materialia majorem splendorem, sive è gloria corporum gloriosorum, sive immediate ex i- psomet Deo consequutura in altera vita. Nam ut terra, ita & cælum peribunt Luc. XVI. Civitas cæle- stis non eget Sole neque Luna, ut luceat in ea. Nam claritas Dei illuminabit eam Ap. XXI. 23. c. XXII. Vinarienses v. 25. & 26. de victoria Christi, qua per mortem suam mortem devicit, & gaudium verum redemptione sua nobis peperit, explicant. Sed antecedentia & consequentia B. Lutheri explica- tionem jam traditam palam confirmant. Amamæ non placet, quod Lutherus reddiderit (Der Son= nenschein wird siebenmal heller seyn denn ietzt,) si- quidem Ebræus textus habeat כְּאֹור שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים als der Schein von sieben Tagen, uti Piscator, Ju- nius, Gall. Ital. Hispan. Angl. Genev. habent. Sed quum septies clariorem solito splendorem Solis dixit Lutherus, annon idem redundat sensus, perinde nempe futurum, ac si lux Solis septem dierum col- lecta esset in unum diem, uti explicandum censet Amama.

## 30:27
Vers. 27.

BEHOLD THE NAME OF THE LORD.) That is, God, most worthy of all praise.

HE COMES FROM AFAR.) That is, unexpected, as those who arrive from abroad.

The Name of the Lord is the glory, power, and justice of the Lord. It is said, however, to come from afar, so that, namely, the affection of those expecting the hand of the Lord may be expressed. For God seems to defer help, and to look upon us late. Thus our B. Luther.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ECCE NOMEN DOMINI.) Id est, Deus omni lau- de dignissimus.

VENIT DE LONGINQUO.) Id est, inexpectatus, ut qui peregre adveniunt.

Nomen Domini est gloria, potentia & justi- tia Domini. Dicitur autem de longinquo venire, ut sc. exprimatur affectus expectantium manum Do- mini. Videtur enim Deus differre auxilium, & se- ro nos respicere. Ita B. Lutherus noster.

## 30:28
Vers. 28.

HIS SPIRIT His wrath. AND TO DESTROY THE NATIONS INTO NOTHING) Winnowing the nations with a winnowing to nothing: so that nothing remains. AND THE BRIDLE OF ERROR, WHICH WAS IN THE JAWS OF THE PEOPLES.) To destroy even the King himself, who was bridling so many peoples, and was leading them to the worship of false gods.

Osiander explains the latter part more correctly, whose paraphrase is: His Spirit, that is, his breath, clearly wrathful, breathing nothing but threats and destruction, is like an overflowing torrent, reaching up to the middle of the neck, so that it threatens death to him whom it catches with its speed and impels with its force: to destroy the nations into nothing: and the bridle of error, which was in the jaws of the peoples; Heb. that he may winnow the nations in the sieve of vanity, and (place) the bridle of error (on) the jaws of the peoples, i.e., the Lord is most vehemently angry with the Assyrians, and will sift them, but in such a way that almost nothing remains in the sieve: They will almost all fall through: but the rest, as if a bridle had been thrown on them, he will lead away against their will from the kingdom of Judah, and will make them wander and stray here and there, until they themselves are also dispersed. Which sense the version of B. Luther also exhibits.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

SPIRITUS EJUS Ira ejus. ET PERDENDAS GENTES IN NIHILUM) Ven- tilans gentes ventilatione ad nihilum: ut nihil supersit. ET FRÆNUM ERRORIS, QUOD ERAT IN MAXILLIS POPULORUM.) Ad perdendum ipsum etiam Regem, qui tot populos frænabat, eisque præibat ad falfo- rum Deorum cultus.

Posteriora rectius exponit Osiander, cujus pa- raphrasis, Spiritus, id est, anhelitus ejus plane ira- cundus, nihil aliud nisi minas & exitium spirans, est velut torrens inundans, usq; ad medium colli pertin- gens, ita ut mortem ei, quem sua celeritate compre- hendit, & sua vi impellit, minitetur: ad perdendas gentes in nihilum: & frenum erroris, quod erat in maxillis populorum; Hebr. ut ventilet gentes in cribro vanitatis, & frenum erroris (imponat) maxillis po- pulorum, i. e. iratus est Dominus vehementissime Assyriis, eosq; cribrabit, sed ita, ut nihil fere in cri- bro remaneat: Sie werden fast alle hindurch fallen: reliquos autem, quasi fræno injecto invitos è regno Juda abducet, eosque hinc inde errare & vagari faciet, donec & ipsi diffipentur. Quem sen- sum etiam exhibet B. Lutheri versio.

## 30:29
Ver. 29.

AS THE NIGHT OF A SANCTIFIED SOLEMNITY.) That is, at the supper which follows the feast day, during which the after-supper was held, the ποτήριον ἐυλογίας (cup of blessing) was carried around, and finally everything was full of joy. AS ONE WHO GOES WITH A PIPE, TO ENTER INTO THE MOUNTAIN OF THE LORD.) Into the temple. Tacitus concerning the Jews: Their priests played together with pipes and timbrels. See 2 Sam. 6:6.

We do not disapprove of these things. Others, however, understand it of the preceding evening, not the following one. Thus Osiander: The song shall be to you as the night of a sanctified solemnity. You shall then sing praises to the Lord, as you are accustomed to do on the evening of some great festival. For the Jews begin the day from noon, and finish the same at the noon of the next day; and so they count the preceding evening as belonging to the following feast day. And there shall be gladness of heart to you, as to him who goes with a pipe, to enter into the mountain of the Lord, to the mighty one, Hebr. to the rock of Israel, that is, you shall rejoice over the deliverance just as you are accustomed to ascend to the Temple of the Lord on festivals with very joyful musical instruments, in order to celebrate God. Thus also Pintus: When the victim was to be sacrificed in the morning, the Jews spent the whole preceding night with joy and songs. Others explain it as THE SONG OF THE NIGHT, i.e., such as the Hebrews sang when, having crossed the Red Sea by night and Pharaoh having been drowned, they sang: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously magnified. Thus Cornelius à Lapide, taking these things as the song of the elect in heaven with Jerome. Grotius, however, ought to have corrected the faulty reading here. For they read it as AS THE NIGHT, as the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Roman Latin codices have it, and not AS THE VOICE, as Plantin and others read it with Gregory the Great in Ezech. hom. 18, which he could have learned from the Jesuits themselves, Cornelius à Lapide, and others.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

SICUT NOX SANCTIFICATÆ SOLENNITA- TIS.) Id est, in cœna, quæ diem festum sequitur, in quæ fiebat postcœnium, circumferebatur ποτήριον ἐυλογίας, o- mnia deniq; erant plena lætitiæ. SICUT QUI PERGIT IN TIBIA, UT INTRET IN MONTEM DOMINI.) In templum. Tacitus de Ju- dæis: Sacerdotes eorum Tibia Tympanisq; concinebant. Vid. 2. Sam. 6, 6.

Non improbamus hæc. Alii tamen de vespera antecedente, non sequente intelligunt. Ita Osian- der: Canticum erit vobis sicut nox sanctificatæ solen- nitatis. Cantabitis tunc Domino laudes, ut sole- tis in vespera magnæ alicujus festivitatis. Judæi e- nim diem à meridie incipiunt, eundemque finiunt in meridie alterius diei; Itaque & antecedentem vesperam sequenti diei festo annumerant. Et læti- tia cordis erit vobis, sicut ei, qui pergit cum tibia, ut intret in montem Domini, ad fortem, Hebr. ad pe- tram Israël, id est, perinde gaudebitis de liberatio- ne, quasi cum valde læti adhibitis instrumentis Mu- sicis afcendere soletis in festivitatibus ad Tem- plum Domini, ut Deum celebretis. Sic etiam Pin- tus: Judæi cum mane esset immolanda victima totam noctem præcedentem cum lætitia & Canticis trans- igebant. Alii CANTICUM NOCTIS explicant, h. e. quale cecinerunt Ebræi, quando nocte transito mari rubro, & submerso Pharaone cecinerunt: Can- temus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est. Sic Cornel. à Lapide de cantico electorum in cœlis hæc accipiens cum Hieronymo. Corrigere autem hic vitiosam lectionem debuisset Grotius. Legendunt enim esse SICUT NOX, ut Hebræi, Chaldæi & Ro- manus Latinus Codd. habent, non vero SICUT VOX, uti legunt Plantinus & alii cum Gregor. M. in Ezech. hom. 18. è Jesuitis ipsis Cornel. à Lapide, & aliis didicisse poterat.

## 30:31
ASSUR STRUCK BY THE ROD.) In the Hebrew: The striking rod, that is, he who was accustomed to vex others most severely.

So also Piscator, Junius, the Genevan, Italian, and English versions. And Sixtinus Amama wishes our Luther's version to be amended in this way: But what prevents the latter Hebrew clause from being accepted as explanatory of the former, and the voice of the Lord being repeated from the former? The Lord himself shall strike (HIM) with a rod; indeed, the following verse demands this sense; for there it is explained what kind of rod it is, and what its striking is.

Latin:

ASSUR VIRGA PERCUSSUS.) In Hebræo: Virga percutiens, id est, qui solitus erat alios gravissime vexare.

Sic etiam Piscator, Junius, Genev. Ital. Angl. Atque ita emendari vult nostram Lutheri versio- nem Sixtinus Amama: Sed quid obstat, quo mi- nus Ebræum posterius Comma ut ἐξηγητικὸν prio- ris accipiatur, & vox Domini è priori repetatur? Ipse Dominus virga percutiet (EUM) imo hunc sensum versus sequens postulat; illic enim qualis virga, & quæ percussio ejus sit, explicatur.

## 30:32
V. 32. AND THE PASSAGE OF THE ROD SHALL BE FOUNDED, WHICH THE LORD SHALL MAKE TO REST UPON HIM WITH TIMBREL AND HARP, AND IN PRINCIPAL WARS HE SHALL FIGHT AGAINST THEM.) The passage of the rod, that is, the blows of the rod: founded, that is, fixed in his flesh: shall make to rest, that is, shall strike: with timbrel and harp, that is, these things shall be done in playing. For in principal wars, in the Hebrew it is, in wars of shaking, that is, as when one is beaten with rods. All these things signify nothing else than that God will destroy the Assyrians without the sweat and blood of the Jews, plainly as if in play and jest.

Osiander's paraphrase is to be preferred, which is also clearer: And the passage of the rod shall be founded, that is, the rod passing through the army shall penetrate even to the marrow: the punishment shall not be light or superficial, but one that penetrates to the depth. The rod will go in well: which the Lord shall make to rest, more correctly, which the Lord shall send upon it. And thus the Lord shall triumph over his enemies with timbrel and harp: for triumphant Emperors are accustomed to use musical instruments of every kind: and in principal wars, Heb. of elevation, he shall fight against them, that is, he shall fight against them gloriously and magnificently, yet not with a corporal sword. Timbrels and harps do not pertain to the manner of slaughter, because it is to be as if in play and jest, as Grotius wishes with Vatablus: But they ought rather to be referred to the joy following for the Hebrews, or even to the triumph of the Lord over his enemies, which pleased Brentius and Osiander. Forerius's explanation is foreign: that the Assyrians were to be conquered not by arms, but by sacrifices, which were offered with timbrels and harps. But the Prophet without doubt alludes in these things to the timbrels which were used when sons were sacrificed to Moloch in Tophet, as appears from the following verse. There joy was excited for Moloch: here God himself shall triumph and rejoice over his enemies.

Latin:

V. 32. ET ERIT TRANSITUS VIRGÆ FUNDATUS, QVAM REQUIESCERE FACIET DOMINUS SUPER EUM IN TYMPANIS ET CITHARIS, ET IN BEL- LIS PRÆCIPUIS EXPUGNABIT EOS.) Transitus virgæ, id est, verbera virgæ: fundatus, id est, infixus ejus carni: faciet requiescere, id est, incutiet: in tympanis & citharis, id est, ludendo hæc fient. Pro in bellis præcipuis, in He- bræo est, in bellis mutationis, id est, ut cum rudibus batui- tur. Hæc omnia nihil aliud significant, quam Deum sine su- dore & sanguine Judæorum deleturum Assyrios, plane quasi in ludo jocoque.

Præferenda paraphrasis Osiandri, quæ etiam luculentior est: Et erit transitus virgæ fundatus, id est, virga transiens per exercitum penetrabit usque ad medullas: non erit levis aut superficialis pœna, sed quæ ad profunditatem penetret. Die Rute wird wol hinein gehen: quam requiescere fa- ciet, rectius, quam immittet Dominus super eam. Et sic triumphabit Dominus de hostibus suis in tym- panis & citharis: solent enim triumphantes Impe- ratores omnis generis Musicæ instrumenta adhibe- re: & in bellis præcipuis, Hebr. elevationis, ex- pugnabit eos, id est, gloriose & magnifice expu- gnabit eos, non tamen gladio corporali. Tympa- na & Citharæ non ad modum internecionis perti- nent, quod quasi ludo, jocoque futura sit, uti cum Vatablo vult Grotius: Sed ad gaudium potius con- sequens Ebræorum, vel etiam ad triumphum Do- mini super hostibus referri debent, quod Brentio & Osiandro placuit. Aliena est Forerii explicatio: quod Assyrii vincendi non armis, sed sacrificiis, quæ cum tympanis & Citharis offerebantur. Alludit au- tem procul dubio Propheta hisce ad tympana, quæ adhibebantur, cum in Tophet filii Molocho immo- labantur, ut è sequenti versu apparet. Ibi lætitia Molocho excitabatur: hic Deus ipse super hosti- bus triumphabit ac lætabitur.

## 30:33
Vers. 33.

FOR TOPHETH IS PREPARED FROM YESTERDAY, PREPARED BY THE KING) It is a long time since King Hezekiah made the valley of Topheth outside Jerusalem empty of all worship of idols, and it was a place that would contain so many thousands of dead Assyrians. Hezekiah removed the idols 2 Chron. 29. Now among the places used in honor of idols was Topheth, 2 Kings 23, 10. But Hezekiah is said to have prepared Topheth for this use, not that he had proposed that to himself at that time, but that it happened so conveniently, as if he had proposed it. You have a similar way of speaking in Matt. 26, 12.

DEEP AND WIDE.) That is, with all impediments removed, it was made empty.

THE NOURISHMENT THEREOF IS FIRE AND MUCH WOOD: THE BREATH OF THE LORD AS A TORRENT OF BRIMSTONE KINDLING IT) An allusion to the custom of idolaters, who were accustomed to burn their children in the same valley of Topheth in honor of Moloch or Saturn. But you may translate it thus most excellently: Its pyre consists of fire and much wood: but God with his power, as if much brimstone were thrown in, kindles those woods. The sense is, that the Assyrians would perish so suddenly, as if they were consumed by a most violent fire. See above 9, 5.

In the Hebrew text the King is joined with others, and it is predicted that he, like his soldiers, will perish: FOR TOPHETH IS PREPARED FROM YESTERDAY, IT ALSO IS PREPARED FOR THE KING. It is said therefore to be prepared not by the King, as the Vulgate has it, and the Grotian gloss, but prepared for the King himself: and thus not Hezekiah, of whom no mention is made, but Assur, or the King of the Assyrians, Sennacherib, is understood. It is taught that hell is prepared not only for the army of the King, but for the King himself. How deep and wide God made it, whose breath kindles it. For this also contributes to that preparation. It is therefore a mere distortion that Hezekiah prepared the valley, which Grotius undertakes to defend with a far-fetched and twisted gloss. The case of the passage Matt. 26, 12 is far different: For there the woman's anointing is said to have been done by the secret direction of God, for the sake of Christ's burial. But who will admit that the evacuation of the valley of Topheth was directed divinely to that end, namely, that there might be a place there that would contain so many thousands of slaughtered Assyrians? It is therefore more correctly understood of the infernal hell, although we do not deny that an allusion is made to the valley of the sons of Hinnom, which is called by the Hebrews Ge-ben-Hinnom, or Ge-Hinnom, as it is written in Josh. 15, 8, and chap. 18, 16, Neh. 11, 30. For that valley was called by this name, in which the Jews near Jerusalem burned their children to Moloch, as those who were accustomed to beat timbrels, so that they would not be moved by their wailing, as R. Abraham, Lyranus, and others have observed, although others seek a different derivation of this word. Arias Montanus thinks that Moloch was Mercury, yet others more correctly make him Saturn, to whom the Phoenicians or Canaanites and others sacrificed their children. See Philo lib. 1 Hist. Phoenician. Diodorus lib. 10. Lyranus from the Rabbis observes in his Commentary on Lev. 18 that Moloch was a copper idol made in the form of a man, hollow inside, and in that cavity a fire was kindled until the idol was as if ignited, and then the child was placed between the hands of the idol. That valley was otherwise most pleasant and full of delights, and therefore the Jews, having left the temple, offered sacrifices in that valley, and even sacrificed their own children to Moloch in the same, 2 Kings 16, 3, 2 Chron. 33, 6, Jer. 7, 31. To abolish which terrible idolatry, Josiah, a most pious King, contaminated that place and ordered that the carcasses of horses, mules, and other animals should be thrown there, 2 Kings 22, 10. Therefore a perpetual fire was maintained in it, so that the filth and bones of the carcasses might be burned. Therefore it could not be unsuitably rendered from Luther as Topheth a pit, not that it was some subterranean pit or some dark cave, but that through that contamination the place turned into a pit for carcasses, a knacker's pit, so afterwards it also became a mound of the dead by the just judgment of God, of which Jer. 7, 32. Therefore, Behold the days shall come, saith the Lord, and it shall no more be called Topheth, and the valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter, and they shall bury in Topheth, because there is no place: And the carcass of this people shall be for food to the birds of the air, and to the beasts of the earth, and there shall be none to drive them away. From these, therefore, the causes can be gathered for which this name גי הנם, which coalesced into one, and among the Chaldeans גהנם, and among the Greeks γεέννα was pronounced, was applied to hell: Namely, that this was done (1) to indicate the supreme torments of hell, since those who were offered to Moloch were exposed to the most grievous torments. (2) And the wailing of the damned, Matt. chaps. 8 & 22, such as the pains in Topheth expressed for the infants exposed to the torments of fire. (3) On account of the joy and noise of the demons. For in Topheth everything resounded with trumpets and drums, as if those horrible rites were the highest festivity and joy, and so that the cries of the infants might not be heard: and thus the devils stirred up such tumults in hell with sarcasms and dancing, that the wailing and cries of the damned cannot be heard for eternity. (4) On account of the most vehement flame of fire, to which infants were exposed, and to which the damned will be exposed, and also on account of the unquenchable and perpetual fire, which was subsequently maintained in Topheth to burn the bones and filth of corpses, as witnessed by R. Kimchi on Psalm 27. (5) On account of the horror of hell. For that place, Topheth, was altogether horrible on account of the idolatry and the horrible cruelty which was practiced there; and so all things in hell will be horrible. The horrible aspect of the demons, the horrible torments of the damned, the horrible roarings and blasphemies of both. (6) On account of eternal ignominy. For as the valley of Hinnom was famous for perpetual ignominy through the decree of Josiah, so Gehenna is described by eternal ignominy and reproach. (7.) On account of the abyss and chasm, because the valley of Hinnom turned into a pit and a mound of corpses, and is therefore deservedly compared to the infernal pit in which the damned lie like sheep, and death feeds upon them, Psalm 49:15. Cf. Rev. 19:20. For these and other reasons of analogy, the name of Gehenna was applied to hell, both by the Jerusalem Targum on Genesis 3, and by Christ in Matthew 5:22, 29, 30, ch. 10:28, ch. 23:15, 33, Mark 9:43, 45, 47, Luke 12:5, and St. James ch. 3:6. In a similar way, Jerome explains the allusion of the word Gehenna in his Commentary on Matthew ch. 10. The name of Gehenna is not found in ancient books, but is first used by the Savior. Let us inquire, therefore, what is the occasion of this discourse. We read more than once that the idol Baal was near Jerusalem at the roots of Mount Moriah, in which there was a forest. This valley was a small plain of the field, it was well-watered and wooded, and full of delights, and a grove in it was consecrated to the idol. But the people of Israel had come to such madness that, having deserted the vicinity of the temple, they would offer sacrifices there, and delights would overcome the rigor of religion, and they would burn or initiate their sons to demons. And that place was called Ge-hinnom, that is, the valley of the sons of Hinnom. This volume of Kings and Chronicles, and Jeremiah, write most fully. And God threatens that He will fill the place itself with the corpses of the dead, so that it shall by no means be called Topheth and Baal, but shall be called a polyandrium, that is, a mound of the dead. Therefore, the future punishments and perpetual penalties, by which sinners are to be tormented, are denoted by the name of this place.
