Nor does Grotius deny this in his Annotations on Matthew 5:22, writing thus: But it was a well-known matter to all the Jews, how their ancestors outside the city of Jerusalem, shamefully imitating the cruel superstition of the Phoenicians, had instituted the practice of tormenting miserable infants with fires even unto death, while trumpets and drums sounded in the meantime, so that the cry wrung out by pain might not be heard. A place dedicated to such a savage rite was called Topheth: the wider place of that very location, the valley of the sons of Hinnom גּי הִנּוֹם which the pronunciation of later times brought out as γέεννα. But what is brought forward from the Hebrew Masters, that corpses were carried into the same place, agrees with the prophecy of Jeremiah 7:32, and that it began to be done in the times of Josiah, 2 Kings 23:10. For he is read to have polluted that place, by the bringing in of corpses, of course. For it was the custom of the Jews to make places used for forbidden ceremonies impure and abominable in that way, as can be seen in the said chapter 23, verse 16. Thus Josephus relates that the Samaritans, out of hatred for the Jewish temple, threw human bones into the porticoes, Antiquities XVIII. 3. But this does not pertain to the explanation of Christ's words. For it is apparent that Christ indicates torment, and indeed the most severe. But just as here the more severe punishments of the future age are compared to the fires of Gehenna, so elsewhere, by a comparison passing into custom, the punishments of the other age are signified by this very name. And in this sense this word is found in the Jerusalem Paraphrase on Genesis 3. Although Grotius wishes that name to be used only on account of the torments, nothing prevents us from believing that other reasons also were considered in the use of this word for hell. The words themselves teach that the fire kindled in Topheth is alluded to here by the Prophet; namely, that there are the fuel of the fire and much wood: and that they are kindled by the breath of the Lord. Therefore, the judgment of God against Sennacherib and his army is noted here, because not only for his soldiers, but for the King himself, a pit of destruction has already been prepared by GOD:

And that they themselves are shortly to perish in a horrible way, not only by temporal, but by eternal death. As if he were to say, the pit, or the Topheth of hell, is already awaiting them, which from OF OLD, that is, from the beginning of the world, and from eternity, was prepared for them and for all the reprobate, which the Lord has made sufficiently deep and wide, it has now also enlarged its soul, and opened its mouth, that it may devour them, Isaiah 5, Habakkuk 3. Its fuel, fire and much wood, are already prepared for their sake as well. The breath of the Lord's wrath, like a torrent of sulfur, kindles them, so that they too may be burned eternally, Revelation 19, 29. This is the reason why the Chaldean used the word גהנם, which Grotius admitted is used for hell, here. And most interpreters explain these things concerning infernal punishment. Jerome: for from of old, and from past time, Topheth has been prepared by the King the Lord, that is, a wide and spacious Gehenna, which may burn them with eternal heats. Its nourishment and fuel is fire, and much wood, that is, perpetual flame and the punishments of sinners. And since he had predicted concerning a furnace and a kiln of burning fire, the prophetic discourse preserves the metaphor: so that we may know that this is kindled by the breath and spirit and will of the Lord; with sulfur mixed in, which excites the flames, so that it may make the torments more acute. Others follow Jerome, and among them also Calvin; who, however, acknowledges that Topheth is not some place, unlike others, who derive the name from it. He proceeds, he says, Isaiah in denouncing the vengeance of God, and says that not only temporary destruction awaits the impious, but eternal ruin as well. For he says that Gehenna is prepared for them, and not only for the common people, but for the King himself and the magnates. By Topheth he undoubtedly understands Gehenna: not that one ought to dream of some place into which the impious after death are enclosed as if in a prison, to endure the torments they have deserved: but he signifies their miserable condition and extreme torments. Nor should Calvin's observation be passed over: That the Prophets wished to transfer the name of that place to the punishments and torments of the impious, so that its mere mention might strike horror into the pious, and that idolatry might be in greater detestation among all. To Oecolampadius the matter is so certain that he doubts whether Gehenna has been described so clearly elsewhere, and asserts that Christians and Jews agree on it.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

PRÆPARATA EST ENIM AB HERI TOPHETH, A REGE PRÆPARATA) Jamdudum est, quod Rex Eze- chias vallem Topheth extra Hierosolyma vacuam fecit ab omni cultu idolorum, & locus esset, qui tot millia As- syriorum mortuorum contineret. Ezechias idola abstu- lit 2. Paral. 29. inter loca autem usurpata in honorem ido- lorum fuit Topheth, 2. Reg. 23, 10. Dicitur autem Eze- chias præparasse Topheth in hunc usum, non quod tunc sibi id propositum habuerit, sed quod id tam commode evenit, quasi id propositum habuisset. Simile loquendi genus ha- bes Matth. 26, 12.

PROFUNDA ET DILATATA.) Remotis scil. impe- dimentis omnibus vacua facta est.

NUTRIMENTA EJUS IGNIS ET LIGNA MUL- TA: FLATUS DOMINI SICUT TORRENS SULPHU- RIS SUCCENDENS EUM) Allusio ad more idololatra- rum, qui in eadem valle Topheth liberos suos cremare in honorem Molochi sive Saturni solebant. Vertas autem sic optime: Pyra ejus ex igne constat, & lignis multis: Deus autem vi sua, quasi Sulphure multo injecto, ista ligna accen- dit. Sensus autem, perituros Assyrios ita subito, quasi i- gne violentissimo absumerentur. Vid. supra 9, 5.

In Ebræo textu Rex conjungitur cum aliis, eumque pariter, ut milites ipsius, periturum prædi- citur: QUIA PRÆPARATA EST AB HERI TOPHETH, ETIAM IPSA REGI PRÆPA- RATA EST. Dicitur ergo præparata non à Re- ge, ut Vulgata habet, ac Grotiana glossa, sed præpa- rata ipsimet Regi: adeoque non Ezechias, cujus nulla facta est mentio, sed Assur, vel Rex Assyrio- rum Sennacherib intelligitur. Non exercitui tan- tum Regis, sed ipsimet etiam Regi præparatam es- se gehennam docetur. Quam profunda in & dila- tatam satis fecerit Deus, cujus flatus eam succen- dit. Nam & hoc ad præparationem illam facit. Mera ergo στρεβλότης est Ezechiam vallem præpa- rasse, quam porro longe quæsita, & contorta glos- sa tuendam suscipit Grotius. Loci Matth. 26, 12. Longe alia est ratio: Nam ibi mulieris unctio arca- na Dei directione dicitur facta, sepulturæ Christi gratia. Eum autem in finem directam fuisse divi- nitus evacuationem vallis Thopheth, ut nempe illic locus esset, qui tot millia cæsorum Assyriorum conti- neret, ecquis admittet? Rectius ergo de gehenna infernali intelligitur, etsi ad vallem filiorum Hinnom, quæ Ebræis גיא בן הנם dicitur, vel גיא הנם vallis Hinnom, uti Jos. 15, 8. scribitur, & cap. 18, 16. Ne- hem. 11, 30. allusionem fieri non diffitemur. Fuit enim vallis illa hoc nomine appellata, in qua juxta Hierosolyma Judæi liberos cremarunt Molocho, utpote qui תוף tympana pulsare consueverant, ne ejulatu eorum moverentur, ut R. Abraham, Lyra- nus & alii observarunt, quanquam alii aliam vocis hujus derivationem quærant. Moloch illum Arias- Montanus putat Mercurium fuisse, alii tamen re- ctius Saturnum faciunt, cui Phœnices vel Cananæi, & alii liberos suos immolabant. Vid. Philo lib 1. Hist. Phœnic. Diodorus lib. 10. Lyranus ex Rabbi- nis observat in Comment. ad Lev. 18. Moloch fuisse idolum cupreum ad formam hominis factum, inte- rius concavum, & in illa cavitate accensum fuisse ignem, quousque idolum esset quasi ignitum, & tunc positum fuisse puerum inter manus idoli. Fuit alias vallis illa amœnissima, ac plena delitiis, atque ideo Judæi relicto templo sacrificia in valle ista offere- bant, atque liberos etiam suos Molocho in eadem immolabant 2. Reg. 16, 3. 2. Paral. 33, 6. Jerem. 7, 31. Quam terribilem idololatriam ut aboleret Jo- sias, Rex pientissimus, locum illum contaminavit, & jussit, ut equorum, mulorum, aliorumque ani- malium cadavera eo projicerentur, 2. Reg. 22, 10. Fovebatur ergo in eadem ignis perpetuus, ut sor- des & ossa cadaverum comburerentur. Ideo non incommode reddi potuit è Luthero Topheth fo- vea eine Grube, non quod fovea quædam subter- ranea, vel specu quoddam obscurum fuerit, sed quod per contaminationem istam locus evaserit in cadaverum foveam eine Schindergrube, sic post- modum & tumulus mortuorum inde factus est ju- sto Dei judicio, de quo Jerem. 7, 32. Ideo, Ecce dies veniet, dicit Dominus, & non dicetur amplius To- pheth, & vallis Filii Hinnom, sed vallis intersectio- nis, & sepelient in Thopheth, eo quod non sit locus: Et erit morticinium hujus populi in cibos volucribus cæli, & bestiis terræ, & non erit, qui abiget. Ex his itaque causæ colligi possunt, ob quas hoc nomen גי הנם quod in unum coaluit, & apud Chaldæos גהנם, & apud Græcos γεέννα pronunciatum, de in- ferno adhibitum sit: Quod nempe hoc factum (1) ad indicandos summos inferni cruciatus, siquidem gravissimis cruciatibus exponebantur, qui Molo- cho offerebantur. (2) Et damnatorum ejulatus Matth. 8. & 22. capp. quales in Thopheth exprime- bant dolores infantibus ignis cruciatibus expositis. (3) Ob dæmonum lætitiam & strepitus. In Topheth enim tubis & tympanis omnia perstrepebant, ac si summa festivitas, & lætitia, sacra illa horribilia es- sent, & ne exaudirentur clamores infantum: atque ita sarcasmis & tripudio tantos tumultus excitarunt in inferno Diaboli, ut damnatorum ejulatus & clamores in æternum exaudiri non possint. (4) Ob ignis flammam vehementissimam, cui exponeban- tur infantes, & exponendi erunt damnati, nec non ob ignem σβέσον & perpetuum, qui in Topheth de- inde asservabatur ad comburenda ossa, & sordes ca- daverum, teste R. Kimchi ad Psal. 27. (5.) Ob hor- rorem inferni. Nam horribilis omnino erat locus iste Topheth ob idololatriam & horribilem cru- delitatem, quæ exercebatur; itaque omnia in in- ferno erunt horribilia. Horribilis Dæmonum aspectus, horribiles damnatorum cruciatus, horri- biles utrorumque fremitus, & blasphemiæ. (6) Ob æternam ignominiam. Nam ut vallis Hinnom in- signis erat ignominia perpetua per Josiæ decretum, ita ab æterna ignominia & opprobrio describitur gehenna. (7.) Ob voraginem & hiatum, quod in foveam & tumulum cadaverum evaserit vallis Hin- nom, adeoque foveæ infernali, in qua damnati ja- cent ovium instar, & mors depascit eos Psal. 49, 15. merito comparatur. Conf. Apoc. 19, 20. Ob has & alias rationes analogiæ, nomen gehennæ inferno adhibitum est, tum à Targum Hierosolym. Genes. 3. tum à Christo Matth. 5, 22. 29. 30. c. 10, 28. c. 23, 15. 33. Marc. 9, 43. 45. 47. Luc. 12, 5. & S. Jacob. c. 3, 6. Simili modo allusionem vocis gehennæ explicat Hieronymus Comment. in c. 10. Matth. Nomen ge- hennæ in veteribus libris non invenitur, sed primum à Salvatore ponitur. Quæramus ergo, quæ sit ser- monis hujus occasio. Idolum Baal fuisse juxta Hie- rosalem ad radices montis Moria, in quibus Sylva fuit, non semel legimus. Hæc vallis erat parva cam- pi planicies, irrigua erat & nemorosa, plenaq; deli- tiis, lucusq; in ea idolo consecratus erat. In tantam autem dementiam populus Israel venerat, ut deserta templi vicinia, ibi hostias immolaret, & rigorem re- ligionis delitiæ vincerent, filiosq; suos dæmoniis incen- derent vel initiarent. Et appellabatur locus ille ge- hinnom, id est, vallis filiorum Hinnom. Hoc Regum volumen & Paralipomenon, & Hieremias scribunt plenissime. Et comminatur Deus, se locum ipsum impleturum cadaveribus mortuorum, ut nequaquam vocetur Topheth & Baal, sed vocetur polyandrium, id est, tumulus mortuorum. Futura ergo supplicia & pœnæ perpetuæ, quibus peccatores cruciandi sunt, hujus loci vocabulo denotantur. Nec abnuit Gro- tius Annot. ad Matth. 5, 22. ita scribens: Nota au- tem res erat Judæis omnibus, quomodo extra urbem Hierosolymamajores ipsorum turpiter imitati crude- lem Phœnicum superstitionem, instituissent miseros infantes ignibus ad mortem usq; cruciare, circum- strepentibus interim tubis tympanisq;, ne dolore ex- pressus clamor exaudiretur. Locus tam sævo sacro dicatus Topheth dicebatur: ipsius loci locus amplior, vallis filiorum Hinnomi גּי הִנּוֹם quod posteriorum temporum pronuntiatio extulit γέεννα. Quod autem ex Hebræis Magistris affertur, in eundem locum dela- ta fuisse cadavera, cum Jeremiæ vaticinio congruit 7, 32. cœptumq; id fieri temporibus Josiæ 2. Reg. 23, 10. Nam is legitur eum locum polluisse, illatis nimirum cadaveribus. Mos enim erat Judæis loca vetitis ce- remoniis usurpata eo modo impura atq; abominanda efficere, ut videre est dicto capite 23. commate 16. Sic Samaritas narrat Josephus odio Judaici templi διαῤ- ῥίψιν ἀνθρωπείων ὀςῶν ἐν ταῖς ςοαῖς ποιῆσαι, O- riginum XVIII. 3. Sed hoc ad verborum Christi expli- cationem non pertinet. Apparet enim à Christo crucia- tum & quidem gravissimum indicari. Sicut autem hic graviora futuri seculi supplicia gehennæ ignibus com- parantur, ita alibi comparatione in consuetudinem mi- grante hoc ipso nomine pœnæ ævi alterius significan- tur. Et hoc sensu vox hæc invenitur in Paraphrasi Hierosolymitana Gen. 3. Quamvis vero cruciatuum tantum causa nomen id adhiberi velit Grotius, ni- hil tamen obstat, quo minus alias etiam rationes in usu hujus vocis de inferno spectatas fuisse, creda- mus. Ad ignem in Topheth succensum hic à Pro- pheta alludi verba ipsa docent; quod nempe illic nutrimenta ignis & ligna multa: & quod ea à flatu Domini succendantur. Notatur ergo hic judici- um Dei adversus Sennacheribum, ejusque exerci- tum, quod non tantum militibus ejus, sed ipsimet quoque Regi fovea exitii à DEO jam parata sit:

Quodque ipsi brevi horribili modo perituri sint, non temporali tantum, sed æterna morte. Quasi dicat, expectat jam fovea, vel Topheth inferni ipsos, quæ Ab HERI, id est, ab initio mundi, & ab æterno ipsis præparata & omnibus reprobis, quam satis pro- fundam & dilatatam fecit Dominus, ea nunc etiam dilatavit animam suam, & aperuit os suum, ut eos devoret Esa. 5. Hab. 3. Nutrimenta ejus ignis & li- gna multa jam etiam ipsorum causa parata sunt. Fla- tus iræ Domini, sicut torrens sulphuris succendit eos- dem, ut ipsi quoque æternum ustulentur Apoc. 19. 29. Quod facit, quod Chaldæus voce גהנם quam de inferno usurpari fassus est Grotius, hic usus sit. Et de infernali supplicio plerique Interpp. hæc ex- plicant. Hieron. ab heri quippe, & à præterito tem- pore, præparata est à Rege Domino Topheth, id est, lata & spaciosa gehenna, quæ eos æternis urat ardoribus. Nutrimentum ejus & fomes ignis est, & ligna multa, id est, flamma perpetua & supplicia peccatorum. Et quoniam sicut de camino & fornaci ignis ardentis, propheticus sermo prædixerat, servat metaphoram: ut flatu & spiritu ac voluntate Domini hunc succen- di sciamus; mixto sulphure, quod flammas excitat, ut faciat acriora tormenta. Hieronymum sequun- tur alii, & inter eos quoque Calvinus; qui vero a- gnoscit Tophet non esse locum aliquem, secus at- que alii, qui ab ipso nomen trahunt. Progreditur, inquit, Isaias in denuncianda ultione Dei, atq; im- pios non temporariam solum cladem, sed æternum quoq; interitum manere dicit. Iis enim gehennam præparatam esse, nec tantum plebejis, sed Regi quoq; ipsi & magnatibus. Per Topheth gehennam haud dubie intelligit: non quod locum aliquem somniare oporteat, in quem impii post mortem tanquam in car- cerem inclusi, quæ meriti sunt tormenta perferant: sed conditionem ipsorum miseram extremosq; crucia- tus significat. Neque prætermittenda Calvini ob- servatio: Quod Prophetæ illius loci nomen ad impio- rum pœnas & cruciatus transferre voluerint, ut sola ejus commemoratio piis horrorem incuteret, atque idololatriæ majori in detestatione apud omnes foret. Oecolampadio res adeo certa est, ut dubitet, an ali- bi ita præclare descripta sit gehenna, ac in eo consen- tire Christianos, & Judæos asserat.

## 31:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXI.

Again woe is denounced on account of trust in Egypt, and the help of God is proclaimed, who like a roaring Lion will terrify enemies, and will protect his own under his wings, and the people are recalled to repentance and the renunciation of idolatry, with the destruction of the Assyrians foretold.

Vers. 1.

WOE TO THEM THAT GO DOWN TO EGYPT) These things cohere with the preceding, and the same matters are repeated in other words.

TRUSTING IN HORSES) See above 30, 16.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXI.

Iterum væ denunciatur ob fiduciam in Ægy- ptum, & Dei prædicatur auxilium, qui in- star rugientis Leonis hostes terrebit, suosq; sub alis suis tuebitur, & ad pœnitentiam & idololatriæ abdicationem revocatur popu- lus, prædicto Assyriorum exitio.

Vers. 1.

VÆ QUI DESCENDUNT IN ÆGYPTUM) Co- hærent hæc cum superioribus, & aliis verbis eædem res re- petuntur.

IN EQUIS SPERANTES) Supra 30, 16.

## 31:2
Vers. 2. HE HATH NOT REMOVED HIS WORDS) He will make valid those things which He spoke through the Prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VERBA SUA NON ABSTULIT) Rata fa- ciet, quæ per Prophetas dixit.

## 31:3
Vers. 3. THEIR HORSES ARE FLESH, AND NOT SPIRIT) They are not of immortal substance.

The Osiandrian Paraphrase is fuller and clearer; the Egyptian cavalry is carnal, and can easily be destroyed; it is not angelic cavalry (such as the Prophet Elisha saw in Dothan, who was defended by angelic cavalry against the Syrians, 2 Kings 6). And therefore the Egyptian cavalry will not be able to bring certain and true help to the Israelites.

AND THE LORD SHALL STRETCH OUT HIS HAND, AND THE HELPER SHALL FALL, AND HE THAT IS HOLPEN SHALL FALL DOWN) If the Lord extends his hand his own, the helper will fall, (i.e., Egypt, even if it wishes to help you as much as possible) and he to whom help is brought will fall, that is, the people of the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 3. EQUI EORUM CARO, ET NON SPI- RITUS) Non sunt substantiæ immortalis.

PLenius & luculentius Paraphrasis Osiandrina; Equitatus Ægyptiacus carnalis est, & facile deleri potest; non est equitatus Angelicus (qualem vidit Propheta Elisæus in Dothan, qui Angelico equi- tatu fuit defensus contra Syros, 2. Reg. 6.) Ideoque Ægyptiacus equitatus Israëlitis certam & veram opem ferre non poterit.

ET DOMINUS INCLINABIT MANUM SUAM, ET CORRUET AUXILIATOR, ET CADET CUI PRÆSTATUR AUXILIUM) Si Dominus extendat ma- num suam, corruet auxiliator, (i. e. Ægyptus, ut maxime auxiliari vobis velit) & cadet is cui fertur auxilium, id est, populus Judæorum.

## 31:4
Verse 4.

FOR THUS SAYS THE LORD TO ME) Moreover, thus he says.

AND WHEN A MULTITUDE OF SHEPHERDS SHALL MEET HIM, HE WILL NOT BE AFRAID OF THEIR VOICE.) Pliny on the lion: When wounded, it knows its attacker with remarkable observation, and in any multitude whatsoever, it seeks him out. Osiander translates and explains these things thus: Just as if a lion and a lion's cub should roar over their captured prey, when there has met him, Hebr. when a multitude of shepherds has shouted at him, he will nevertheless not be afraid of their voice, and will not be terrified by their multitude: so the Lord of hosts (for whom all creatures, but especially the angelic ones, fight) will descend to fight over Mount Zion, more correctly: for Mount Zion, and over the hill; more correctly, and for his hill, that is, for the temple, which is placed upon Mount Zion. This is: Just as a lion, when it has seized its prey, does not suffer it to be extorted from him, even if many shepherds pursue him with huge shouts: for he does not fear them: so the Lord has gripped his Church firmly (not to be torn apart, but to be preserved) and will not care for the power or the shouts of the King of the Assyrians, or of his captains. Amama observes that in the Hebrew it is a future, not active, but passive יִקָּרֵא even if a multitude of shepherds has been called together against him. But the sense is the same. For being called together is understood as shouting against the lion, inasmuch as he is said not to fear their voice.

TO FIGHT OVER MOUNT SION) More correctly: for Mount Zion.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QUIA HÆC DICIT DOMINUS AD ME) Insuper hæc dicit.

ET CUM OCCURRERIT EI MULTITUDO PASTORUM, A VOCE EORUM NON FORMIDABIT.) Plinius de leone: Vulneratus observatione mira percussorem novit, & in quantalibet multitudine appetit. Osiander hæc ita transfert, & exponit: Quomodo si rugiat Leo & catulus Leonis super captam prædam suam, cum occurrerit ei, Hebr. cum inclamaverit eum multitudo pastorum, nihilominus a voce eorum non formidabit, & a multitudine eorum non pavebit: sic descendet Dominus exercituum (cui omnes creaturæ, præsertim vero Angelicæ militant:) ut prælietur super montem, rectius: pro monte Sion, & super collem; rectius, & pro colle ejus, id est, pro templo, quod impositum est monti Sion. Hoc est; Quemadmodum Leo, ubi prædam rapuerit, non patitur sibi eam extorqueri, etiamsi multi pastores eum ingentibus clamoribus insequantur: non enim eos metuit: ita Dominus mordicus arripuit Ecclesiam suam (non dilaniandam, sed conservandam) nec curabit potentiam aut clamores Assyriorum Regis, aut Capitaneorum ejus. Amama observat in Ebræo esse Futurum non activum, sed passivum יִקָּרֵא etiamsi multitudo pastorum contra ipsum convocata sit. Sed sensus idem est. Nam convocata clamare adversus Leonem intelligitur, utpote qui vocem ejus non formidare dicitur.

UT PRÆLIETUR SUPER MONTEM SION) Rectius: pro monte Sion.

## 31:5
Verse 5. AS BIRDS FLYING) As birds [protecting] their brood. See Matt. 23, 37. PASSING OVER AND SAVING) Suddenly bringing salvation, and as if in passing.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SICUT AVES VOLANTES) Sicut aves pullitiem. Vid. Matth. 23, 37. TRANSIENS ET SALVANS) Subito salutem adferens, & quasi in transitu.

## 31:6
Verse 6. RETURN AS YOU HAD RECEDED INTO THE DEEP, O CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.) As deeply as you had descended, so high rise again.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CONVERTIMINI SICUT IN PROFUNDUM RECESSERATIS FILII ISRAEL.) Quam profunde descenderatis, tam in altum resurgite.

## 31:7
Verse 7. FOR IN THAT DAY A MAN SHALL CAST AWAY THE IDOLS OF HIS SILVER) After he has acknowledged the providence of God by such a great and singular benefit: See above 30, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 7. IN DIE ENIM ILLA ABJICIET VIR IDOLA ARGENTI SUI) Postquam Dei providentiam tam magno ac singulari beneficio agnoverit: Vide supra 30, 22.

## 31:8
Verse 8. ASSUR SHALL FALL BY THE SWORD NOT OF A MAN, AND THE SWORD NOT OF A HUMAN SHALL PUT HIM TO FLIGHT) The closer the times approach, the more clearly the future appears to the Prophets.

HE SHALL FLEE NOT FROM THE FACE OF THE SWORD.) King Sennacherib himself, with none of the enemy pursuing him.

AND HIS YOUNG MEN SHALL BE TRIBUTARY.) Better: they shall be dissolute: that is, his companions will dread the rustling of any leaf.

Calvin renders it thus: The young men shall be for melting. B. Luther understands that phrase THEY SHALL BE TRIBUTARY proverbially, as if to say: he wanted to rule over you, but they will succumb and be conquered. Thus I will deal with them, that they shall be glad that they remain peasants, who now promise themselves a kingdom over you.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CADET ASSUR IN GLADIO NON VIRI, ET GLADIUS NON HOMINIS FVGABIT EUM) Quo magis proximant tempora, eo futura clarius Prophetis apparent.

FVGIET NON A FACIE GLADII.) Ipse Rex Sennacherib, nemine hostium eum insequente.

ET JUVENES EJUS VECTIGALES ERUNT.) Melius: dissoluti erunt: id est, comites ejus quemvis horrebunt folii strepitum.

Calvinus ita reddit: Juvenes in liquefactionem erunt. B. Lutherus illud VECTIGALES ERUNT proverbialiter intelligit, q. d. voluit vobis dominari, sed succumbent & vincentur. Sic cum eis agam, dass sie froh sollen werden, dass sie Bauren bleiben, qui jam sibi promittunt regnum in vos.

## 31:9
Ver. 9. AND HIS STRENGTH SHALL PASS AWAY FOR FEAR) In the Hebrew: He shall pass by his fortress for fear. He shall flee even beyond the house, as the Latin proverb has it.

Thus also others, for the most part, according to Amama: For fear he shall pass to the rock, or into the fortified city NINEVEH. Which is also Calvin's interpretation. The explanation of others seems simpler: His rock (army) shall pass away for fear: or they shall betake themselves in very swift flight into Assyria. For this is said concerning the King. Cf. 2 Kings 19:39.

AND HIS PRINCES SHALL BE AFRAID OF THE ENSIGN.) In the Hebrew: His princes shall be afraid from the sign: that is, wherever they shall see any banner on some watchtower (mention of which is made above 30:17), they will think that the enemy's battle lines are threatening them.

Calvin otherwise: His leaders, whose duty it is to encourage other soldiers, will be so fearful that they will not dare to join battle or await a conflict, they will flee the banner. Osiander explains it concerning the military sign of God fighting for the Jews. His princes shall flee in dismay from the military sign: that is, the Lord God will carry off a glorious victory, and the Assyrians will not withstand his attack.

THE LORD SAID WHOSE FIRE IS IN ZION, AND HIS FURNACE IN JERUSALEM.) That is, whose Altar is always burning in Jerusalem.

We do not disapprove of the interpretation. It is pleasing, however, to add the opinion of B. Luther: I understand it economically, for the reason that the Lord dwells in Jerusalem, and is a householder to them, he dwells there just like some citizen. It is a sweet figure, which is of value for lifting up spirits. The same was said without a figure in Num. 35: Do not pollute the land in which you dwell, in which I dwell among you. I am the Lord, who dwell among the children of Israel. But since the Lord willed to dwell in Jerusalem in such a way that he had a peculiar Furnace and fire in his house for the sacrifice of an offering, there is no doubt that this is looked upon by the Prophet as an argument for the city not being destroyed and being consecrated. Calvin wished to be singular here: If it pleases one to read at the end of the verse, as others render it, whose fire is in Zion, the sense will be that God has at his disposal a fiery power to devour enemies, yet I think the relative אשר is redundant: or it must be translated in the nominative, because God is aptly called fire with respect to the Assyrian, whom he will consume. As to his naming fire, there are those who refer it to sacrifices, but such an interpretation seems to me little firm and too forced. I do not doubt that he is saying either that the Lord has fire to consume Assyria, or that God himself is like fire, so that he tacitly compares the Assyrian to stubble, and he says that this fire is kindled and cherished in Zion and Jerusalem, that is, in the midst of his people, to signify that the impious do not persecute the Church of God with impunity. But the common explanation is simpler, nor does it sufficiently agree that the Lordship of GOD in Jerusalem is taken concerning the vengeance of God for the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET FORTITVDO EJUS A TERRORE TRANSIBIT) In Hebræo: Arcem suam præ timore transibit. Fugiet etiam ultra casam, ut Latinum habet proverbium.

Sic etiam fere alii apud Amamam: Præ timore ad petram, vel in urbem munitam NINIVEM transiturus est. Quæ Calvini quoque interpretatio est. Simplicior aliorum videtur explicatio: Petra illius (exercitus) præ terrore transibit: seu celerrima fuga recipient se in Assyriam. De Rege enim hoc dicitur. Conf. 2. Reg. 19, 39.

ET PAVEBUNT FUGIENTES PRINCIPES EJUS.) In Hebræo: Pavebunt principes ejus à signo: id est, ubicunq; in specula aliqua vexillum aliquod videbunt(qualium mentio supra 30,17.) putabunt imminere sibi hostium agmina.

Aliter Calvinus: Duces ejus, quorum munus est, alios milites animare, adeo fore trepidos, ut manus conferere aut conflictum expectare non audeant, refu- giant vexillum. De figno militari Dei pugnantis pro Judæis Osiander explicat. Consternati fugient à figno militari principes ejus: id est Dominus Deus reportabit gloriosam victoriam, neque ejus impetum sustinebunt Assyrii.

DIXIT DOMINUS CUJUS IGNIS EST IN SI- ON, ET CAMINUS EJUS IN JERUSALEM.) Id est, cujus Altare semper ardens est Hierosolymis.

Non improbamus interpretationem. Adjice- re tamen placet B. Lutheri sententiam: Ego Oeco- nomice intelligo pro eo, quod habitet Dominus Hieru- salem, & sit istis Paterfamilias, habitet istic tanquam civis aliquis. Est suavis figura, quæ valet ad eri- gendos animos. Idem dixit sine figura Num. 35. Ne polluatis terram, in qua habitatis, in qua ego inter vos habito. Ego sum Dominus, qui habito inter fi- lios Israel. Sed quum ita in Jerusalem habitare vo- luerit Dominus, ut in ædibus suis peculiarem Ca- minum & ignem, ad sacrificium oblationem ha- buerit, hoc spectari à Propheta, tanquam argumen- tum non destruendæ, & consecrandæ civitatis ad- duci, dibitandum non est. Calvinus singularis hic esse voluit: In fine versus si legere placeat, ut alii red- dunt, cujus ignis est in Sion, sensus erit, Deo suppe- tere igneam virtutem ad hostes vorandos, puto ta- men relativum אשר redundare: vel in nominativo vertendum esse, quia scite vocatur Deus ignis respe- ctu Assyrii, quem consumet. Quod ignem nominat, sunt qui ad sacrificia referunt, sed parum firma & ni- mis coacta mihi videtur ejusmodi interpretatio. Ego non dubito, quin dicat, vel Domino ignem esse ad consumendum Assyriam, vel Deum ipsum esse in- star ignis, ut tacite Assyrium stipulæ comparet, atq; hunc ignem in Sion & Jerusalem accendi & foveri dicit, id est, in medio populi sui, ut significet, impios non impune persequi Ecclesiam Dei. Sed communis explicatio simplicior est, neq; satis convenit DEI Dominium in Jerusalem accipi de vindicta Dei pro Ecclesia.

## 32:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXII. The Messiah who is about to reign in justice is presented to the faithful, as also the outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the calling of the Gentiles, and the fruits of justice.

Ver. 1.

BEHOLD A KING SHALL REIGN IN JUSTICE: AND HIS PRINCES SHALL RULE IN JUDGMENT.) He predicts the future virtues of Hezekiah, as above 9:7. As the King is, such are the princes wont to be, Martial: No one has his own (this is the nature of the court of the powerful) But the Caesar-like man has the morals of the master. Theodoric the Goth: You make the purpose of the prince, either to neglect judges, or to love virtues.

IF this ought to be compared here with Is. ch. 9 v. 7, these things will have to be understood not of Hezekiah, but of Christ: whom we showed to have been predicted there, to the same place, even though Grotius, Judaizing, may wish Hezekiah to be understood there also. Although indeed the present prophecy is interpreted by not only the Rabbis, but also Lyra, Vatablus, our B. Luther, Wolfg. Musculus, Cramer in the summaries, and others concerning Hezekiah, and Corn. à Lapide, Menochius, and Tirinus explain it concerning Hezekiah as the Type, and Christ as the antitype, which mind they also say was that of Thomas, Hugo, and Sanctius: yet most others understand it of Christ reigning in justice in the Church; and Jerome, Procopius, Cyril, Haymo, Brentius, Osiander, and Hutterus establish that the princes of the Kingdom, who rule with Judgment over the Ecclesiastical Republic, are the Apostles.

Summaries. The Weimar Paraphrasts, Oecolampadius, Zwingli, Calvin, Piscator, Junius, the Belgian Paraphrasts, Amama, Adam Sasbouth, Emmanuel Sa, and others. This is supported by the fact that the King is being discussed here κατ' ἀντονομασίαν (by antonomasia): the King reigning in Justice, a title which is attributed absolutely to no one except Christ, Isa. 9:7, Jer. 23:6. For no king is found who does not at some time depart from the laws of justice. Nor were princes who presided in judgment ever called anything other than Apostles: who are so called in Ps. 45, 'You shall make them princes over all the earth,' and Ps. 68, 'Princes of Judah, their leaders'; and they administered judgment, not indeed by their own power in conquering and condemning Satan and the world, but by the power of the Word and the direction of the Holy Spirit, John 16. It is never so well with worldly empires that both the King and all his princes have the highest care for justice and judgment, and the subjects enjoy certain and firm tranquility. In wicked states, that which is found in Herodotus usually happens: τοῖσι μὲν χρηστοῖσι τῶν ἀνθρώπων κακοὶ δοῦλοι φιλέουσι γίνεσθαι, τοῖσι δὲ κακοῖσι χρηστοί: 'To good men, bad servants are wont to fall, and to bad men, good ones.' In worldly kingdoms, either the King is wont to be just and the officials unjust, or the officials just and the King unjust, or both the King and the officials unjust. You will never find it to be the case that both the King and his officials are just. In the kingdom of the Messiah, however, the King and his princes or officials perform justice and judgment. And it is known from other prophetic oracles that these things, namely justice and judgment, are claimed as proper to the kingdom of Christ. But he does not perform civil justice, nor civil judgment; rather, justice and judgment are spiritual, heavenly, and eternal. The distinction between these was excellently proposed by the blessed Brentius: To perform justice in a civil kingdom is to pronounce a man who is civilly honest as civilly just, and to honor him with civil rewards. And to perform judgment in a civil kingdom is to punish an external and civil enemy, or a thief, or a malefactor, so that he does not harm the good and honest. But to perform justice in the kingdom of Christ is to go to God the Father, to intercede before the Father, and to obtain that all who believe in the Gospel are reckoned just and are adopted as sons and heirs of God. So also to perform judgment is to conquer Satan, the capital and perpetual enemy of the human race. But Christ alone is the one who performs such justice and judgment, that is, who obtains that on his account we are reckoned just before God through faith, and that Satan is conquered and condemned. Furthermore, the discourse is about such a King who is a hiding place for all his subjects from the wind, a refuge against the flood, as a stream of waters in a dry place, as the shadow of a prominent rock in a desolate land, under whom each one can be as safe in adversity as he who, when the wind is blowing vehemently or a great rain is falling, has his fortified shelters; under whose kingdom anyone, if he happens to be afflicted, can be refreshed just as a dry place is by streams of water, and as one who is fatigued is refreshed in a land devoid of trees or scorched by the sun in the shadow of a great rock. These things apply perfectly to Christ the King and his kingdom, but they cannot be said of any worldly King. Moreover, of whom but Christ can these things be explained, which the Prophet promises here concerning the subjects! The eyes of those who see will not be dim, the ears of those who hear will listen diligently: The heart of the foolish will understand Scripture, and the tongue of the stammerers will speak readily and eloquently. In a worldly kingdom, the eyes of those who see often grow dim, and the ears of those who hear are fatigued: But in Christ's kingdom, the eyes of the mind are so opened through the Gospel that they do not go blind, but rightly know God, and the ears of the heart are opened so that they are not fatigued by hearing, but hear and believe promptly, and progress in the true knowledge of God. Although by 'those who see' the Prophets and Doctors of the Church can be understood in particular, and by 'those who hear' the other members of the Church, or their listeners. In the kingdom of the world, he who is foolish is not made wise, but is irritated so that he becomes foolish again and again: In the kingdom of Christ, however, the foolish become wise, the heart of the foolish understands knowledge: those who were previously impious, ignorant of heavenly things, and thus foolish and senseless, are endowed with heavenly wisdom, so that in spiritual matters they convince the wise of this world that they are foolish, Matt. 11, 1 Cor. 1. And how will the tongue of the stammerers speak quickly in the kingdom of the world? This is a peculiar feature of the kingdom of Christ, who suddenly endowed the Apostles with the knowledge of various languages and with heavenly eloquence: so that those who were stammering before the world and the orators of this age, being instructed with the highest eloquence—not indeed worldly, but one far more eminent, which contributes to the eternal salvation of men—confounded all the orators of the age; nay, he grants to the remaining believers also that they may be able to confess Christ before the world and give an account of their faith as much as is necessary, and he bestows upon them such eloquence that they may be able to obtain eternal salvation itself and all things from the heavenly Father by their prayers. Furthermore, as regards the leaders in this kingdom, they are taught to be such as are uniquely to be found in the kingdom of Christ: He who is foolish shall no longer be called a prince. Nor shall the fraudulent (or rather, the avaricious) be called a great man or a Lord (dynastes). In a worldly kingdom, the foolish, the avaricious, and the fraudulent very often preside, who exhaust their subjects with various extortions and frauds. In the kingdom of Christ, princes who are not foolish, not avaricious or fraudulent, but endowed with true wisdom and truly munificent, shall be set in charge. In a worldly kingdom, as Brentius explains, the names of things are inverted; the foolish and the sordid are often called a Prince, and the avaricious oppressor of the poor is called munificent: but in the kingdom of Christ it will not be so: the sordid will not be called liberal, and the avaricious will not be called munificent, but a spade will be called a spade. Finally, in the kingdom of Christ there is no place for hypocrisy and lying, but truth will occupy everything.

And this sense concerning Christ the King is confirmed furthermore by the subjoined prophecy concerning the judgment of God against the proud and refractory: which, even if it began a little after this prophecy in the time of Hezekiah, in subsequent times also, when the Jews had become no better, nay rather worse, He visited them with more grievous punishments, nay at length brought about the extreme πανωλεθρίαν [total destruction] of the Jewish polity. All of which things are designated by this commination. Finally, with what appearance of truth can it be denied that the promise of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the calling of the Gentiles pertain to the times of the New Testament? The whole συνέχεια [continuity] therefore of this chapter, and this entire prophecy, looks to the kingdom of Christ, and is subjoined to the preceding prophecy concerning the liberation from King Sennacherib, and the happiness under Hezekiah, lest, forsooth, anyone should expect that liberation and happiness under Christ the King. And thus the blessed Luther himself also explains the latter part of the chapter, from verse 9 onwards. For he does not wish only the Babylonian captivity to be predicted here, much less only the slaughter under Sennacherib, but all other calamities up to the advent of Christ, who was about to pour out His Spirit into the hearts of believers, and he acknowledges that verse 15 is to be understood concerning the calling of the Gentiles under the New Testament, which Wolfgang Musculus also admits in his commentary.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXII. Sistitur fidelibus Messias juste regnaturus, ut & effusio S. S. ac gentium vocatio, fru- ctusq; justitiæ.

Vers. 1.

ECCE IN JUSTITIA REGNABIT REX: ET PRINCIPES EJUS IN JUDICIO PRÆERUNT.) Eze- chiæ futuras virtutes prædicit, ut supra 9, 7. Qualis Rex est, tales esse solent principes, Martialis: Nemo suos (hæc est aula natura potentis) Sed domini mores Cæsarianus habet. Theuderichus Gotthus: Principis propositum facis, aut negli- gere judices, aut amare virtutes.

SI conferri hic debeat c. 9. Es. v. 7. non de Ezechia, sed Christo hæc intelligenda erunt: quem ibi prædictum esse, ad eundem locum ostendimus, etsi Ezechiam ibi quoq; intelligendum esse, Grotius Ju- daizans velit. Quanquam vero præsens vatici- nium non Rabbini tantum, sed etiam Lyranus, Vatablus, B. Lutherus noster, Wolfg. Musculus, Cramerus in summariis, & alii de Ezechia interpre- tentur, Corn. à Lapide, Menochius & Tirinus de E- zechia ut Typo, & Christo ut antitypo explicent, quam etiam mentem Thomæ, Hugonis & Sanctii es- se dicunt: alii tamen pleriq; intelligunt de Christo in justitia regnante in Ecclesia; ac principes Regni, qui cum Judicio præsunt Reipubl. Ecclesiasticæ, Apostolos esse statuunt Hieronymus, Procopius, Cyrillus, Haymo, Brentius, Osiander, Hutterus in

Summar. Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, Oecolampadius, Zwinglius, Calvinus, Piscator, Junius, Paraphrastæ Belgici, Amama, Adamus Sasbouth, Emmanuel Saa, & alii. Quibus favet, quod de Rege κατ' ἀντονομα- σίαν hic agatur: de Rege in Justitia regnante, quod elogium absolute nulli tribuitur nisi Christo Esa. 9. 7. Jer. 23, 6. Nullus enim reperitur Regum, qui ali- quando non migret justitiæ leges. Neque princi- pes, qui in Judicio præfuerunt semper, alii præter Apostolos nominabantur: qui sic vocantur Ps. 45. Constitues eos principes super omnem terram: Et Ps. 68. Principes Judæ Duces eorum; & administrarunt ju- dicium, non propria quidem virtute Satanam & mundum vincendo & condemnando, sed virtute verbi, ac directione SS. Joh. 16. Nunquam tam be- ne cum mundanis imperiis agitur, ut tam Rex, quam Principes ejus omnes summam curam habe- ant justitiæ & judicii, & subditi certa ac firma fru- antur tranquillitate. In improbis id fere fieri so- let, quod est apud Herodotum 7οῖς μὲν χρηστῖσι τ' ἀνθρώπων κακοὶ δῦλοι φιλέεσι γίνεσθαι, τοῖσι δὲ κακοῖσι χρηστοί: Bonis hominibus solent mali servi contingere & malis boni. In mundanis Regnis aut Rex solet esse justus, & officiales injusti, aut officia- les justi, & Rex injustus, aut tam Rex, quam officia- les injusti. Nunquam fore invenias, ut & Rex & of- ficiales ejus sint justi. In regno autem Messiæ Rex & principes ejus vel officiales faciunt justitiam & judicium. Et notum est ex aliis Propheticis vati- ciniis, Christi regno hæc ceu propria vindicari ju- stitiam, ac judicium. Justitiam autem facit non civilem, nec judicium civile, sed justitia & judicium spiritualia sunt, cælestia & æterna. Quorum di- fcrimen eximie proposuit B. Brentius: Facere ju- stitiam in regno civili, est hominem civiliter hone- stum pronunciare civiliter justum, & honorare eum civilibus præmiis. Et facere judicium in regno ci- vili, est externum & civilem hostem seu latronem seu malefactorem punire, ne bonis & honestis noceat. Fa- cere autem justitiam in regno Christi, est ad Deum Patrem ire, apud Patrem intercedere, ac impetrare, ut omnes credentes Evangelio reputentur justi, ado- ptentur in filios & hæredes Dei. Sic etiam facere Judicium est vincere Satanam, capitalem & per- petuum hostem humani generis. Solus autem Chri- stus is est, qui talem facit justitiam & judicium, hoc est, qui impetrat, ut propter ipsum reputemur coram Deo justi per fidem, & ut Satan vincatur & conde- mnetur. Adhæc de Rege ejusmodi sermo est, qui latibulum subditis omnibus à vento, confugium contra inundationem, in siti quasi rivus aquarum, in terra dissita umbra petræ prominentis sit, sub quo unusquisque ita tutus in adversis esse queat, sicut tutus est is, qui flante vehementer vento, aut deci- dente grandi imbre suas habet munitas latebras, sub cujus regno quisque, si afflicto accidat, ita re- focillari possit, sicut aridus locus à rivis aquarum, & sicut fatigatus in terra arboribus vacua, vel Sole exusta recreatur in umbra magnæ petræ. Quæ Christo Regi, ejusque regno apprime conveniunt, de nullo autem Rege mundano dici queunt. Por- ro de quonam nisi Christo hæc explicari possunt, quæ promittit hic de subditis Propheta! Non cali- gabunt oculi videntium, aures audientium diligenter auscultabunt : Cor stultorum intelliget Scripturam, & lingua balborum loquetur expedite & diserte. In regno mundano sæpe caligant oculi videntium, & fatigantur aures audientium: At in Christi regno ita aperiuntur per Evangelium oculi mentis, ut non cæcutiant, sed recte Deum cognoscant, & aures cordis, ut non fatigentur audiendo, sed prompte au- diant atque credant, ac in vera cognitione Dei pro- ficiant. Quanquam per VIDENTES Prophetæ peculiariter atque Ecclesiæ Doctores intelligi pos- sint, & per audientes cætera Ecclesiæ membra, vel auditores ipsorum. In regno mundi qui stultus est, non redditur sapiens, sed irritatur, ut fiat subin- de stultior: In regno autem Christi stulti fiunt sa- pientes, cor stultorum intelligit scientiam: qui an- tea impii, rerum cœlestium ignari, adeoque stulti & vecordes fuerint, cœlesti sapientia donantur, ut in rebus spiritualibus sapientes hujus mundi stultos esse convincant Matth. 11. 1. Cor. 1. Et quomodo in regno mundi velociter loquetur balborum lin- gua? Peculiare hoc est regni Christi, qui Aposto- los subito donavit variarum linguarum cognitio- ne, ac cœlesti eloquentia: ut qui balbutientes ço- ram mundo, & oratoribus hujus seculi fuerunt, summa eloquentia instructi, non mundana quidem, sed longe eminentiori, quæ ad æternam salutem hominum facit, omnes oratores seculi confude- rint; imo reliquis etiam credentibus concedit, ut Christum coram mundo confiteri, & rationem fi- dei suæ, quantum opus est, reddere queant, illisque tantam eloquentiam largitur, qua ipsam æternam salutem, & omnia precibus suis à Patre cœlesti im- petrare possint. Ulterius quod præfectos in hoc re- gno attinet, tales illi futuri docentur, quales unice in Christi regno reperire est: Non vocabitur ultra is, qui insipiens est, princeps. Neq; fraudulentus (vel potius avarus) appellabitur major, vel Dominus δυνάςης. In regno mundano sæpius præsunt insi- pientes, & avari, atq; fraudulenti, qui subditos ex- pilationibus & fraudibus variis exhauriunt. In regno Christi principes non insipientes, non avari aut fraudulenti, sed vera sapientia præditi, & vere munifici præficientur. In mundano regno, ut ex- plicat Brentius, vocabula rerum invertuntur, stul- tus & sordidus sæpe vocatur Princeps, & avarus oppressor pauperum vocatur munificus: in regno autem Christi non sic erit: sordidus non vocabi- tur liberalis, & avarus non vocabitur munificus, sed Scapha scapha, & ligo ligo vocabitur. In regno denique Christi nullus locus est hypocrisi, & menda- cio, sed omnia veritas occupabit.

Atque hunc sensum de Christo Rege confir- mat præterea subjunctum vaticinium de judicio Dei adversus superbos & refretarios: quod etiamsi ceperit paulo post hanc prophetiam Ezechiæ tem- pore, sequentibus etiam temporibus, quum nihil meliores imo deteriores evaserint Judæi, graviori- bus suppliciis eosdem affecit, imo tandem extre- mam πανωλεθρίαν Judaicæ politiæ attulit. Quæ omnia hac comminatione designata sunt. Denique promissionem effusionis Spiritus Sancti ac vocationem gentium ad Nov. Testam. tempora pertinere, qua veri specie negari potest? Tota ergo hujus capitis συνέχεια, & universa hæc Prophetia ad regnum Christi spectat, ac præcedenti vaticinio de libera- tione à Rege Sennacherib, & felicitate sub Ezechiâ subjungitur, ne sc. quis eam liberationem & felici- tatem sub Christo Rege expectet. Atque ita ex- plicat etiam ipse B. Lutherus posteriorem partem capitis, inde à v. 9. Neque enim solum captivita- tem Babylonicam hic prædici vult, nedum solum cladem sub Sennacheribo, sed omnes alias calami- tates usque ad Christi adventum, qui Spiritum suum effusurus erat in corda credentium, & vers 15. de vocatione gentium sub N. T. intelligendum esse agnoscit, quod fatetur etiam Wolfg. Musculus in Commentario suo.

## 32:2
Vers. 2. AND A MAN SHALL BE) That is, He. AS ONE WHO HIDES FROM THE WIND) In Hebrew: As a hiding place from the wind.

AND HIDES HIMSELF FROM THE TEMPEST.) In Hebrew: And a refuge against an inundation.

The Vulgate and B. Luther translated these somewhat differently: But here he expressed the same sense: That everyone (sc. under this King) shall be as one who is protected from the wind, like one who is hidden from the downpour. Therefore, Amama had no cause here to criticize the Lutheran version: Meanwhile, the Hebrew words were rendered κατὰ πόδας (word for word), as Grotius interprets, by Junius, Piscator, the English, Genevan, Italian, Spanish, and Pagninus. The sense is: Those who are ruled by Christ through the Apostles and sincere ministers of the word, they shall be safe from the horrible wrath of God, just as one who is hidden in a cave of a rock from the wind or a horrible whirlwind, and who hides himself in a cavern from the tempest. For even in bodily calamities the pious shall be so preserved that all things turn out for their good, Rom. 8. 1. Pet. 3.

AS RIVERS OF WATERS IN A DRY PLACE) Virgil: — — — — as in the heat to quench thirst with a leaping stream of sweet water.

AND THE SHADOW OF A PROMINENT ROCK IN A DESERT LAND.) In a land void of trees.

These things, and those said in the preceding verse, cannot be attributed to Hezekiah or to the rule of any human being. Therefore, they are rightly explained by Jerome as referring to Christ: The King shall reign justly, not accepting a person in judgment, and His Princes shall rule with truth, considering causes, not men. And whoever shall be under His shadow, he shall be safe in tribulations and distresses, and in the tempest of this unclean world, just as one who, fleeing the wind and the whirlwind, hides himself safely in a place, and who finds purest fountains in the desert, and who in vehement heat, with the sun's ardor scorching everything, has rested under a prominent rock. Brentius rendered the sense of these words well: The evangelical consolations, which the Holy Spirit will imprint upon their hearts through the ministry of the word, shall be as rivers of waters in a thirsty region, and as the shadow of a rock prominent far and wide in a desert, or arid, land. Just as rivers of waters refresh a thirsty region which is scorched by the ardor of the sun: and just as the shadow of a great rock defends nearby places from the ardor of the sun, so that they are not utterly burned up: So Christ, by His Spirit through the Gospel, shall console and refresh the pious, who are driven by various afflictions and temptations, so that they do not fail, but are preserved unto eternal life. Those who believe in Christ experience that these things are so.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET ERIT VIR) Id est, ille. SICUT QUI ABSCONDITUR A VENTO) In Hebreo: Sicut latibulum à vento.

ET CELAT SE A TEMPESTATE.) In Hebræo: Et confugium contra inundationem.

Paulo aliter hæc transtulit Vulgata, & B. Lu- therus: Sed hic sensum eundem expressit: Daß jederman (sc. sub hoc Rege) seyn wird als einer, der für dem Wind bewahret ist, wie einer der für dem Platzregen verborgen ist. Non ergo causam ha- buit hic taxandi Lutheranam versionem Amama: Interim κατὰ πόδας ita, ut interpretatur Grotius, red- dita sunt Ebræa verba à Junio, Piscatore, Angl. Ge- nev. Ital. Hispan. & Pagnino. Sensus est: Qui à Christo per Apostolos & sinceros verbi ministros reguntur, ii tuti erunt ab horribili ira Dei, sicut qui absconditur in caverna petræ à vento vel tur- bine horribili, & qui celat se in antro à tempestate. Nam etiam in corporalibus calamitatibus ita con- servabuntur pii, ut omnia illis in bonum cedant, Rom. 8. 1. Petr. 3.

SICUT RIVI AQUARUM IN SITI) Virgilius: - - - - quale per æstum Dulcis aquæ saliente sitim restinguere rivo.

ET UMBRA PETRÆ PROMINENTIS IN TER- RA DESERTA.) In terra arboribus vacua,

Non possunt hæc & quæ præcedenti commate dicta, Ezechiæ, aut ullius φιλανθρώπꙋ regimini tribui. Proinde recte ab Hieronymo de Christo explicantur: Rex regnabit juste, non accipiens per- sonam in judicio, & Principes illius cum veritate præerunt, causas, non homines considerantes. Et qui- cunq́; sub ejus umbraculo fuerit, sic tutus erit in tri- bulationibus & angustiis, & immundi istius tem- pestate, quomodo qui ventum & turbinem fugiens, se tuto abscondit loco, & qui purissimos fontes invenit in deserto, & qui in vehementi æstu, Solis ardore cuncta torrente, sub prominenti saxo requieverit. Horum verborum sensum probe reddidit Brentius: Evan- gelicæ consolationes, quas Spiritus Sanctus per mi- nisterium verbi ipsorum cordibus imprimet, erunt sicut rivi aquarum in sitibunda regione, & quasi umbra petræ longe lateq; prominentis in terra de- serta, seu arida. Quemadmodum rivi aquarum recreant regionem siticulosam, quæ ardore Solis torretur: & sicut umbra magnæ petræ defendit vi- cina loca ab ardore Solis, ne penitus exurantur: Sic Christus Spiritu suo per Evangelium consolabitur & recreabit pios, qui variis afflictionibus & tenta- tionibus aguntur, ne deficiant, sed conserventur ad vitam æternam. Hæc ita se habere, experiuntur, qui in Christum credunt.

## 32:3
Ver. 3. THE EYES OF THOSE WHO SEE SHALL NOT BE DIM) There shall not be those who call themselves Prophets bringing false visions.

AND THE EARS OF THOSE WHO HEAR SHALL HEARKEN DILIGENTLY.) Audience shall be given to true Prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NON CALIGABUNT OCULI VIDEN- TIUM) Non erunt qui se Prophetas dicant falsa visa adfe- rentes.

ET AURES AUDIENTIUM DILIGENTER AU- SCULTABUNT.) Veris Prophetis præbebitur audien- tia.

## 32:4
AND THE HEART OF THE FOOLISH SHALL UNDERSTAND KNOWLEDGE.) Even those who are of the slowest wit shall understand the greatness of God.

AND THE TONGUE OF THE STAMMERERS SHALL SPEAK SPEEDILY AND PLAINLY.) Even the most infantile shall praise God.

These do not attain the magnificence of the divine promise. It is not the cessation of false Prophets, who have never been lacking, that is predicted, but the illumination of true Teachers; nor is the understanding restricted to the knowledge of one benefit of God, such as the liberation in the time of Hezekiah, but the discourse is about any knowledge of spiritual things whatsoever. For it is said simply, the heart of the foolish shall understand Scripture. Therefore, this most distinguished promise is very poorly enervated by such a gloss: Those who are of the slowest wit shall understand the greatness of God from the slaughter of Sennacherib. And no less perversely are those things which Isaiah promises simply regarding the eloquence of the stammerers restricted to the proclamation of God by any infants whatsoever on account of the liberation from Sennacherib.

Latin:

ET COR STULTORUN INTELLIGET SCIEN- TIAM.) Etiam qui tardissimo sunt ingenio, Dei magnitu- dinem intelligent.

ET LINGUA BALBORUM VELOCITER LOQUE- TUR ET PLANE.) Etiam infantissimi Deum lauda- bunt.

Non assequuntur hæc magnificentiam pro- missionis divinæ. Non cessatio falsorum Propheta- rum, qui nullo tempore defuerunt, sed illuminatio verorum Doctorum prædicitur, neque ad unius Dei beneficii cognitionem intelligentia restringitur, qualis erat liberatio Ezechiæ tempore, sed de qua- vis rerum spiritualium cognitione sermo est. Sim- pliciter enim dicitur, cor stultorum intelliget Scri- pturam. Pessime ergo hæc tam insignis promif- sio tali glossa enervatur: Qui tardissimo ingenio sunt, è cæde Sennacheribi magnitudinem Dei intelligent. Nec minus perverse, quæ de eloquentia balborum præclara ἁπλῶς promittit Esaias, ad præconium Dei ab infantissimis quibusvis ob liberationem a Sen- nacheribo coarctantur.

## 32:5
Ver. 5.

HE SHALL NO LONGER BE CALLED, HE WHO IS A FOOL, A PRINCE) נדיב ευεργετης, an honorable title for a man of princely rank. See Luke 22:25. He calls fools those who do not believe in God or God's providence, as in Psalm 14 and 53. NEITHER SHALL THE FRAUDULENT BE CALLED GREAT) כילי, which is translated here as fraudulent, is properly a miser. But what is שוע here, is elsewhere משוע and is translated δυναστης.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NON VOCABITUR ULTRA IS QUI INSIPIENS EST, PRINCEPS) נדיב ευεργετης, honesta appellatio viri principis. Vide Luc. 22, 25. stultos f. insipientes vocat qui Deum aut Dei providentiam non credunt, ut Pf. 14. & 53. NEQUE FRAUDULENTUS APPELLABITUR MAJOR) כילי, qui hic fraudulentus vertitur, proprie est avarus. Quod autem hic est שוע, id alibi משוע & verti- tur δυναστης.

## 32:6
Verse 6. FOR THE FOOL WILL SPEAK FOLLY.) He gives the reasons why a good King ought not to entrust matters to the impious nor to the avaricious. An impious magistrate speaks impious things, and thus corrupts many. AND HIS HEART WILL WORK INIQUITY) No religion restrains him from unjust deeds. Concerning the connection between religion and justice, see what we have collected in Book II of 'De jure belli ac pacis', chapter 20, 45, and in the Annotations. TO ACCOMPLISH HYPOCRISY, AND TO SPEAK TO THE LORD FRAUDULENTLY,) That is, while he pretends to be good and pious. AND TO MAKE EMPTY THE SOUL OF THE HUNGRY.) To despoil the needy. AND TO TAKE AWAY DRINK FROM THE THIRSTY.) To spare no one.

Latin:

Vers. 6. STULTUS ENIM FATUE LOQUETUR.) Causas reddit, cur bonus Rex neq; impiis neque avaris man- dare debeat. Magistratus impius loquitur impia, & sic multos corrumpit. ET COR EJUS FACIET INIQUITATEM) Nul- la religio eum ab injustis factis prohibet. De nexu religio- nis & justitiæ vide quæ congessimus lib. II. de jure belli ac pacis c. 20, 45. & in Annotatis. UT PERFICIAT SIMULATIONEM, ET LO- QUATUR AD DOMINUM FRAUDULENTER,) Id est, dum se bonum piumque esse simulat. ET VACUUM FACIAT ANIMAM ESURIEN- TIS.) Spoliet egentem. ET POTUM SITIENTI AUFERAT.) Nemini parcat.

## 32:7
Verse 7. THE FRAUDULENT) The avaricious, as we have already said: now he describes another source of evils in the Republic. ARE THE WORST VESSELS.) His measures are the worst. But by measures, understand metaphorically, judgments. FOR HE HIMSELF HAS DEVISED THOUGHTS) He invents crafty schemes. TO DESTROY THE MEEK WITH WORDS OF FALSEHOOD.) That he may oppress the miserable (that is, ענוים, as the Masoretes read) through calumny. WHEN THE POOR SPOKE JUDGMENT) When he addresses the poor in judgment. That is, when as a Judge he interrogates the poor.

Some judge that these things are to be understood of the Magistrate in an earthly kingdom, so that by the comparison of foolish and fraudulent princes, the wisdom and justice of Hezekiah may be rendered more illustrious. Others more correctly wish the kindness and piety of Christ the King to be illustrated by this comparison: or that it be explained what it is to be a foolish נבל and a fraudulent person, and what it is to be truly a princely נדיב, so that we may not be deceived by the inversion of these words, as Brentius explains: namely, that the morals of men in earthly kingdoms are described, and the morals of the pious in the kingdom of Christ are opposed to them. Osiander judges that under the person of the impious, the chief Roman Anti-Christ is depicted, who seized dominion in the Church through tyranny: he is impious, and an Epicurean in his heart, and thus a fool by the phrase of Scripture: furthermore, he is most avaricious, as one whose avarice the world has not yet been able to satisfy. Most of his decrees are foolish and impious: and he is entirely occupied with establishing a hypocritical religion everywhere. For the Papistic religion is a sea of hypocrisy. The fool נבל is defined as one who works vanity in his heart, and most vain error, as if God did not care for human affairs, whence he does not place his hope in God, but in vain things, the riches and delights of the age. Then with his mouth he speaks folly and vanity; all his speech is foolish, and is about vain and earthly things. Finally, even if he simulates an honest life, and does not wish to appear an enemy or an impostor, yet he meditates and does this one thing night and day, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and to take away drink from the thirsty; that he may exhaust others, and let them hunger and thirst. The avaricious כילי or devourer and destroyer, from כלה to attenuate, to wear away, is described because he devises various plans, and the worst of arts, by which he may oppress the miserable through lies, and by catching at words, he inverts their just and right cause, and brings it about that it appears unjust. Words. בדבר אביון משפט, Junius, Piscator, the Genevan, Italian, and English versions do not translate badly, even when the poor man says what is right: But Luther's, with the sense not differing: 'wenn er den Armen Recht sprechen soll' (when he ought to speak justice to the poor), when the poor man is heard to have a just cause, they ought to pronounce in his favor also; and thus Luther in his Latin exposition: The poor man spoke rightly indeed, but he is oppressed by tyrants. And the preposition ERGA (towards) can be understood (when it says towards) the needy (in) judgment he ought to speak justice, as is explained in the margin of the English version, or also the prefix ל can be understood, when it says judgment to the needy.

Latin:

Vers. 7. FRAUDULENTI) Avari, ut jam diximus: jam alterum malorum in Republica fontem describit. VASA PESSIMA SUNT.) Mensuræ ejus pessimæ sunt. Per mensuras autem metaphoricῶs intellige judicia. IPSE ENIM COGITATIONES CONCINNAVIT) Invenit commenta vafra. AD PERDENDOS MITES IN SERMONE MEN- DACII.) Ut homines miseros (id est ענוים, quomodo le- gunt Masoretæ) per calumniam opprimat. CUM LOQUERETUR PAUPER JUDICIUM) Cum alloquitur pauperem in judicio. Id est, cum ut Judex paupe- rem interrogat.

Hæc de Magistratu in regno mundano efferri censet, ut è collatione stolidorum & fraudulento- rum principum sapientia & justitia Ezechiæ illu- strior reddatur. Alii rectius hac collatione Chri- sti Regis benignitatem, & pietatem illustrari volunt: vel explicari, quid sit stultum נבל & fraudulentum, quid sit vere principem נדיב esse, ne inversione horum vocabulorum decipiamur, uti Brentius ex- ponit: describi nempe mores hominum in regnis mundanis, iisque opponi mores piorum in regno Christi. Osiander sub persona impiorum præci- puum Anti-Christum Romanum depingi censet, qui arripuit Dominium in Ecclesia per tyranni- dem: Impius est, & Epicureus in corde suo, adeoq; phrasi Scripturæ stultus: Adhæc avarissimus, utpo- te cujus avaritiam hactenus mundus explere non potuit. Decreta ejus pleraque stolida & impia sunt: Et ipse totus in eo est, ut ubique religionem hypocriticam instituat. Papistica enim religio mare est hypocrisēos. Definitur נבל stultus, quod corde operetur vanitatem, & errorem vanis- simum, quasi non curet Deus res humanas, unde non in Deum collocat spem suam, sed in res vanas, opes & delitias seculi. Deinde ore suo loquitur stultitiam & vanitatem, omnis sermo ejus stultus, & de rebus vanis, ac terrenis est. Denique etsi ho- nestatem simulet vitæ, neque inimicus aut impo- stor videri velit, tamen hoc unum noctu diuque meditatur & agit, ut vacuam faciat animam esuri- enti, & sitienti potum auferat; ut alios exhauriat, eosque esurire ac sitire sinat. Avarus כילי vel devo- rator & contritor à כלה attenuare, atterere describi- tur, quod excogitet varia consilia, & pessimas quas- que artes, quibus opprimat miseros per mendacia, & captando verba in istis justam & rectam ejus cau- sam invertat, ac ut injusta videatur, efficit. Verba. בדבר אביון משפט non male Junius, Piscator, Ge- nev. Ital. Angl. reddunt, etiam cum pauper dicit quod rectum est: Sed Luthers sensu non discrepante: wen er den Armen Recht sprechen soll, cum pauperem audient, justam habere causam, pro ipso etiam pro- nunciare debent; atque ita Lutherus in Latina enar- ratione: Pauper recte quidem dixit, sed opprimitur a Tyrannis. Et subintelligi potest præpositio ERGA (cum erga) egenum (in) judicio jus dicere debet, uti ad marginem Anglicanæ versionis exponitur, vel etiam subaudiri præfixum ל, cum egeno dicit ju- dicium.

## 32:8
Vers. 8.

BUT THE PRINCE SHALL THINK OF THOSE THINGS WHICH ARE WORTHY OF A PRINCE, AND HE SHALL STAND ABOVE THE LEADERS.) You may translate it conveniently: The prince shall be he who will think generous thoughts, and will persist in generous actions. It is an argument ἐξ ἐτυμολογίας (from etymology). For נדיב, prince, has its name from generosity. Generosity is to be understood as a virtue of the mind for doing good to as many as possible.

Osiander accepts this concerning Christ in his antithesis to the Anti-Christ. But our Prince Jesus Christ, who is the Prince of peace, Isa. 9, will not govern his Church tyrannically, nor greedily, nor fraudulently, nor foolishly, but he will think of those things which are worthy of a prince, he will revolve and treat in his mind those things which are his own proper signs: and which make for the true and proper happiness of his Church: and he himself shall stand above the Leaders (the Apostles), that is, he shall be eminent before the Apostles, and all other chief Doctors of the Church. For all these shall subject themselves to Christ; and they shall be intent upon this, that they may do all things for his glory, and the salvation of the Church. Grotius seems to draw this peculiarly to Hezekiah: Cornel. a Lapide attributes these things to both Hezekiah and Christ, and wishes it to be said of both, whom Menochius and Tirinus follow as is their custom. The Weimar Paraphrase understands this concerning upright princes, and particularly concerning the Apostles instructed by the virtue of the principal Spirit, that they have the mind and divine thoughts of Christ, and constantly persist in them. But the saying is general נָדִיב נְדִיבוֹת יָעָץ, and it is not to be restricted to a prince alone. For the noun נדיב, although it is accustomed to designate a prince, whom generosity and munificence most befit, whence he is also called εὐεργέτης (benefactor) by the Greeks, Luke 21, 45, is more general, and is accustomed to be used of any munificent, liberal, and spontaneous person, as Ex. 35, 5. 22. let every munificent or spontaneous one in heart (the LXX have ὁ καταδεχόμενος, he who accepts) bring; and נדבה is munificence, liberality, as 2 Cor. 8, 29. Silver and gold is munificence to God himself, and also that which is spontaneously dedicated to God, as Deut. 16, 10. you shall give the voluntary contribution נדבת of your hand; Ps. 54, v. 8. in munificence I will sacrifice to you: Ps. 110, v. 4. your people נדבות of liberalities or spontaneous: Ps. 119. Accept now, O Lord, the spontaneous offerings of my mouth (τὰ ἑκούσια). Therefore others have rendered this sentence generally: the liberal man consults liberal things, and shall stand by liberal deeds, or as Vatablus, he shall rise clear. Musculus therefore wishes the sense to be this: the beneficent man thinks beneficent things: that is, he who is truly such that he is deservedly called a beneficent and magnificent man, namely a just, liberal, and principal-spirit-endowed man, he thinks not of iniquitous and crafty things to circumvent, but of those things which are of a beneficent man, namely, just, equitable, and liberal things to help the poor. He thinks of these things, in these he exercises himself, so that the distinction between him and those foolish and greedy men may be clear. AND HE SHALL STAND BECAUSE OF BENEFICENT THINGS, that is, he shall prosper and persist immovably, because he is beneficent, and conducts himself as such in all things. The Spirit of the Prophet does not only act to promise prosperity to the just, but at the same time threatens ruin and destruction to the foolish, greedy, and iniquitous. For what he says: and he shall stand because of beneficent things, includes a negative concerning unjust and iniquitous judges. That is to say, the foolish and greedy man, however, shall not stand because of his iniquitous pursuits. Which latter point, however, Calvin warned should be taken otherwise, so that, namely, a promise is not treated here, but rather perseverance in such counsels and liberal institutions is designated. I will transcribe his entire explanation: We said before that these sentences of the Prophet are more subtle than they are commonly thought to be. For he does not speak in the common manner, but discusses the reformation of the Church. This therefore pertains to the regenerated, in whom Christ holds the kingdom. Because although all are called by the voice of the Gospel, few however suffer themselves to be subjected to his yoke. The Lord makes these truly liberal and beneficent, so that they no longer seek their own advantages, but are prepared to bring help to the needy: not that they do this only once or a few times, but that they progress more and more daily in liberality and beneficence. This passage is commonly explained otherwise: namely, that the liberal promote themselves by right offices, and become great, because God rewards them, and heaps them with greater benefits. Which opinion pleases at first sight: But the Prophet rather teaches that the liberal will never make an end of giving, since they will make greater progress daily, and will pursue the same counsels, and will constantly confirm their mind in it: just as it is said in the Psalm, He has dispersed, he has given to the poor, his justice remains forever. But this is added because it is easy to simulate liberality for some time: many also think themselves liberal from the heart when they have given something, but they cease immediately, and change their plan. But true liberality is not momentary or temporary: those who are endowed with that virtue persist constantly, they do not spread themselves out by some sudden or light ardor, of which they might repent a little later. And the Prophet wished to express this by the word קום, which signifies to rise and to grow. Many things indeed happen which interrupt the course of our liberality; we experience a wonderful ingratitude in men, so that whatever we give seems to be ill-placed. Many snatch too greedily to themselves, and like swallows suck the blood of others. But let us remember this maxim, and let us hear Paul warning us not to grow weary in doing good. For the Lord does not exhort us to momentary liberality, but to that which may last throughout the whole course of our life. Our Brentius says almost the same: Here is also defined נדיב, that is, a liberal or munificent person, namely, one who in all his affairs has thoughts or counsels worthy of a free and pious man, and is not munificent only once or twice, but rises in munificence and liberality, and continually confers more and greater benefits on anyone according to his ability. Which he applies particularly to the Apostles, or illustrates by their example: Such, he says, were the נדיבים Peter, John, and the other Apostles, who, having left all their possessions, followed the calling of Christ. Such a נדיב was Zacchaeus, after he was converted to Christ. Such also was Paul, who, though he had nothing, yet enriched many. Such נדיבים Paul commands the rich to become, when he says: Charge those who are rich in this present age, that they be not high-minded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living GOD, who provides us all things abundantly for enjoyment, that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to communicate, laying up in store for themselves a good foundation, etc. Which he declares more fully in the same place, by the antithesis of worldly and pious men. They apply their study chiefly to this, that they may make empty the hungry soul, and take away drink from the thirsty, that is, that by whatever arts, deceits, trifles, impostures, lies, and perjuries they can, they may gather wealth and grow rich to the disadvantage of others. But in the kingdom of Christ, the customs are different. For the pious are truly liberal, because, content with their own little, or whatever it is that God has given, they trade justly, keep faith, help even the needy to the best of their ability, and depend entirely on God, to whose will they prefer to obey rather than possess all the riches of the world. And the explanation of the preaching also leads to this, he advises liberal things, which is that of our Dr. Luther in this place. He has liberal thoughts, how he may preside and accommodate everyone. For he feels that he was instituted for this reason, that he might benefit rather than preside, that he might serve rather than dominate. And he even perseveres in such thoughts. For what the Latin translates, HE SHALL STAND ABOVE LEADERS, the Hebrew has, he perseveres in liberality. Wherefore the version of the LXX, which is viral, has not departed entirely from the scope of the Holy Spirit: οἱ δὲ εὐσεβεῖς συνετὰ ἐβουλεύσαντο, κ͵ αὕτη ἡ βουλὴ μενεῖ: But the pious have thought prudently, and their counsel remains. On which passage Cyril says thus: Lovers of worldly wisdom and assertors of perverse dogmas also apply all zeal and diligence so that they may scatter and dissipate the discourses of the doctrine of the holy mystagogues, whom he also calls humble: however much they may have been made in judgment, that is, not sluggishly, but expensively and thoroughly, and in supernal and divine wisdom. For I think he teaches this by adding: But the pious have thought prudently, and this counsel remains. For the ornate loquacity of the wise in the world has vanished. But the counsel of the pious has prevailed, that is, the doctrine or preaching. And we say those are pious who administer the divine and Evangelical discourse to those who are throughout the whole earth. That we may contract everything into a sum, this seems to be the mind of the Prophet, that the faithful are munificent, liberal, endowed with a truly principal spirit, which David desires for himself in Ps. LI, prompt and voluntary in those things which are worthy of their person, which are to be beneficent, and endowed with a principal Spirit, that they may think, intend, undertake, and as much as is in them, do and expedite, that they may meditate on these things day and night, and be uniquely solicitous about such things, and desire to be, and so also show themselves in reality to be such toward others, both by helping the interests of the Republic to the best of their ability, and especially also by promptly succoring the needy with counsel and aid: And that such a one עַל־נְדִיבוֹת יָקוּם In or upon such counsels, institutions, and works worthy of a principal Spirit, he is to stand constant and unmoved, and will not allow himself to be moved from right and just counsels by prayer, nor price, nor threats, nor promises: Er wird darüber halten, as Blessed Luther rendered; in which he himself also, safe by divine protection, will persist unmoved, and will prosper. Which golden apophthegm of the Holy Scriptures, as I have wished it to be my Symbol from early adolescence, נדיב נדיבות יעץ, so I adore God uniquely, through Christ our ἱκέτην κ͵ μεσίτην, who is truly נדיב, and by his most holy example has shone the way for us, that רוח נדיבה that principal Spirit may support, strengthen, and confirm me, until I am raised by his immense thanks to the blessed society of true נדיבים at the goal of perfection, which is of the other age.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

PRINCEPS VERO EA QUÆ DIGNA SUNT PRIN- CIPE COGITABIT, ET IPSE SUPER DUCES STA- BIT.) Vertas commode: Princeps erit qui generosa cogitabit, & in generosis actionibus perstabit. Est argumentum ἐξ ἐτυ- μολογίας. Nam נדיב princeps a generositate nomen habet. Generositas intelligenda, animi virtus ad benefaciendum quamplurimis.

De Christo hoc accipit Osiander in ἀντιθέσει ad Anti-Christum. Princeps vero noster Jesus Christus, qui est Princeps pacis Esa. 9. non tyranni- ce, nec avare, nec fraudulenter, nec stolide suam Ecclesiam gubernabit, sed ea quæ digna sunt princi- pe, cogitabit, ea in animo suo volvet & tractabit, quæ ipsius propria sunt signa: & quæ ad Ecclesiæ suæ veram & propriam felicitatem faciant: & ipse super Duces (Apostolos) stabit, id est, eminebit pro Apo- stolis, & omnibus aliis præcipuis Ecclesiæ Doctoribus. Hi enim omnes subjicient sese Christo; & in id e- runt intenti, ut omnia ad ipsius gloriam, & Ecclesiæ salutem faciant. Ad Ezechiam id peculiariter tra- here videtur Grotius: Cornel. a Lapide cum Eze- chia, tum Christo hæc tribuit, ac de utroq; dictum vult, quem sequitur pro more Menochius, & Tiri- nus. Vinariensis Paraphrasis de Principibus probis, & peculiariter de Apostolis virtute Spiritus princi- palis instructis id intelligit, quod Christi mentem & divinas cogitationes habeant, ac constanter in ea persistant. Sed dictum generale est נָדִיב נְדִיבוֹת יָעָץ Neque ad principem solum restringendum. No- men enim נדיב etsi principem designare soleat, quem maxime generositas & munificentia decet, un- de & Græcis εὐεργέτης dicitur Luc. 21, 45. generali- us est, atq; usurpari consuevit de quovis munifico, liberali & spontaneo, uti Ex. 35, 5. 22. omnis munificus seu spontaneus corde (ὁ καταδεχόμενος habent LXX.) afferat; & נדבה est munificentia, liberalitas, ut 2. Cor. 8, 29. Argentum & aurum est munificentia ipsi Deo, nec non id, quod sponte Deo dicatur, ut Deut. 16, 10. contributionem נדבת voluntariam manus tuæ dabis Ps. 54. v. 8. in munificentia sacrificabo ti- bi: Ps. 110. v. 4. populus tuus נדבות liberalitatum vel spontaneus: Ps. 119. Oblationes spontaneas oris mei (τὰ ἑκούσια) accepta nunc Domine. Idcirco gene- raliter alii reddidere hanc sententiam: liberalis li- beralia consultat, & per liberalia facta stabit, vel ut Vatablus, clarus surget. Sensum itaque hunc esse vult Musculus: beneficus benefica cogitat: hoc est, qui vere talis est, ut merito vocetur beneficus, & ma- gnificus homo, videlicet justus, liberalis, ac spiritu principali præditus, is cogitat non iniqua & astuta ad circumveniendum, sed ea quæ sunt benefici, utpote, justa, æqua & liberalia ad juvandum pauperem. De his cogitat, in his sese exercet, ut luculentum sit in- ter ipsum & stultos illos avarosque discrimen. ET IPSE PROPTER BENEFICA STABIT, hoc est, prosperabitur & immote persistet, propterea quod beneficus est, & talem se gerit in omnibus. Spiritus Prophetæ non hoc tantum agit, ut promittat pro- speritatem justis, sed simul minatur ruinam & inte- ritum stultis, avaris, & iniquis. Quod enim dicit: & ipse propter benefica stabit, negativam de injustis & iniquis judicibus includit. Q. d. stultus vero & avarus propter iniqua sua studia non stabit. Quod posterius tamen Calvinus aliter accipiendum esse monuit, ut nempe non promissio hic tractatur, sed perseverantia potius in ejusmodi consiliis atque institutis liberalibus designetur. Adscribam in- tegrum ejusdem explicationem: Diximus antea has Prophetæ sententias subtiliores esse, quam vulgo putant. Nec enim loquitur vulgari more, sed de re- formatione Ecclesiæ disserit. Hoc igitur ad regene- ratos pertinet, in quos regnum obtinet Christus. Quia etsi voce Evangelii vocentur omnes, pauci tamen il- lius jugo se subjici patiuntur. Hos vere liberales & beneficos efficit Dominus, ne amplius quærant sua commoda, sed opem egeno ferre parati sint: non ut se- mel tantum aut aliquoties id faciant, sed indies ma- gis ac magis in liberalitate & beneficentia progredi- antur. Vulgo aliter exponitur hic locus: nempe quod liberales rectis officiis sese promovent, & magni evadunt, quia Deus ipsos remuneratur, ma- joribusque beneficiis cumulat. Quæ sententia pri- ma facie arridet: Sed potius docet Propheta liberales nunquam facturos finem largiendi, quoniam majo- res facient indies progressus, eademque agitabunt consilia, & constanter in eo animum suum obfir- mabunt: sicuti in Psalmo dicitur, Dispersit, dedit pauperibus, justitia ejus manet in seculum.
