Hoc au- tem ideo additum est, quod facile sit ad aliquod tempus liberalitatem simulare: multi etiam se ex animo libe- rales putant, cum aliquid largiti fuerint, sed desinunt protinus, atque institutum mutant. Vera autem li- beralitas momentanea aut temporaria non est: perse- verant constanter, qui ea sunt virtute præditi, non re- pentino quodam aut levi ardore sese diffundunt, cujus paulo post eos pœniteat. Idq; exprimere voluit Pro- pheta dictione קום, quæ surgere & crescere signifi- cat. Multa quidem accidunt, quæ liberalitatis no- stræ cursum abrumpant, miram in hominibus ingra- titudinem experimur, ut quicquid damus, male loca- tum esse videatur. Multi nimis cupide ad se ra- piunt, & instar hirundinum sugunt alienum sangui- nem. Sed meminerimus hujus sententiæ, & Pau- lum audiamus monentem, ne bene agendo defatige- mur. Nec enim hortatur nos Dominus ad momen- taneam liberalitatem, sed quæ toto vitæ nostræ cursu duret. Similiter fere Brentius noster: Definitur etiam hic נדיב hoc est, liberalis seu munificus, vide- licet, qui in omnibus suis negotiis habet cogitatio- nes, seu consilia libero & pio homine digna, nec semel tantum & iterum munificus est, sed assurgit in munificentia ac liberalitate, & subinde plura ac majora beneficia in quovis pro virili sua confert. Quod peculiariter applicat ad Apostolos, vel exem- plo eorum illustrat: Tales, inquit נדיבים fuerunt Petrus, Johannes, & alii Apostoli, qui relictis o- mnibus suis facultatibus secuti sunt vocationem Christi. Talis נדיב fuit Zachæus, postquam con- versus est ad Christum. Talis fuit & Paulus, qui cum nihil haberet, multos tamen ditavit. Tales נדיבים jubet Paulus divites fieri, cum ait: His qui divites sunt, in præsenti seculo præcipe, ne sint elato ani- mo, neq; spem ponant in divitiis incertis, sed in DEO vivente, qui præbet nobis omnia affatim ad fidendum, ut benefaciant, ut divites sint operibus bonis, ut faciles sint ad impertiendum libenter communicantes, recon- dentes sibi ipsis bonum fundamentum &c. Quæ u- berius ibidem declarat, ab antithesi hominum mundanorum & piorum. Illi in hoc præcipue stu- dium incumbunt, ut vacuam faciant animam esu- rientem, & potum auferant sitienti, h. e. ut quibus queant artibus, dolis, nugis, imposturis, mendaciis, perjuriis, opes congregent, & aliorum incommodo ditescant. In regno autem Christi alii sunt mo- res. Pii enim vere sunt liberales, quia contenti suo parvo, aut qualicunq; quod Deus dedit, negotian- tur juste, servant fidem, juvant etiam egentem pro virili, ac omnino ex Deo pendent, cujus voluntati malunt obedire, quam omnes divitias mundi possi- dere. Atque huc abit etiam prædicati explicatio, liberalia consulit, quæ est D. Lutheri nostri in h. l. Habet liberales cogitationes, quomodo præsit, & com- modet omnibus. Sentit enim se ideo institutum, ut prosit potius, quam præsit, ut serviat potius, quam do- minetur. Et in talibus cogitationibus perseverat etiam. Nam quod Latinus vertit, SUPER DU- CES STABIT, Ebræus habet, perseverat in libera- litate. Quapropter non abiit omnino à scopo Spi- ritus Sancti LXX. viralis versio: οἱ δὲ εὐσεβεῖς συνετὰ ἐβουλεύσαντο, κ͵ αὕτη ἡ βουλὴ μενεῖ: Pii autem pru- dentia cogitarunt, & consilium eorum manet. In quem locum ita Cyrillus: Amatores mundanæ sapientiæ & perversorum dogmatum assertores, etiam omne adhi- bent studium ac diligentiam, ut sermones doctrinæ sanctorum mystarum, quos etiam humiles nominat, dispergant atq; dissipent: quantumvis in judicio facti fuerint, id est, non oscitanter, sed expensè & excussè, ac in sapientia superna ac divina. Nam hoc opinor docet addens: Pii vero prudentia cogitarunt, & hoc consilium manet. Etenim sapientum in mundo compta loquacitas evanuit. Obtinuit autem pio- rum consilium, id est, doctrina sive prædicatio. Et pios esse dicimus, qui divinum & Evangelicum ser- monem his, qui per universam terram sunt, admini- strant. Ut in summam contrahamus omnia, hæc mens Prophetæ videtur, quod fideles munifici, libe- rales, spiritu vere principali præditi, quem sibi optat David Ps. LI. ad munia sua obeunda prompti atq; vo- luntarii ea, quæ personæ suæ digna sunt, quæ sunt bene- fici, & Spiritu principali præditi, cogitent, intendant, suscipiant, ac quantum in ipsis est, agant, atque expe- diant, quod ea meditentur diu noctuq;, ac de talibus unice soliciti sint, atq; esse cupiant, adeoque adversus alios etiam tales sese reapse demonstrent, tum Reipu- blicæ commoda pro virili juvando, tum imprimis etiam egenis, consilio atq; auxilio prompte succurren- do: Quodque talis עַל־נְדִיבוֹת יָקוּם In vel super ejusmodi consiliis, institutis, & operibus Spiritu principali dignis constans, & immotus perstiturus sit, nec prece, neq; pretio, nec minis, nec promissis, à rectis ju- stisq; consiliis sese dimoveri passurus: Er wird darü- ber halten, uti B. Lutherus reddidit; in quibus etiam ipse, divino tutus præsidio, immote persistet, & prospe- rabitur. Quod aureum S. S. apophthegma uti Sym- bolum meum esse à prima adolescentia volui, נדיב נדיבות יעץ, ita Deum adoro unice, per Chri- stum ἱκέτην κ͵ μεσίτην nostrum, qui vere נדיב est, suoq; exemplo sanctissimo viam nobis præluxit, ut רוח נדיבה Spiritus ille principalis me fulciat, robo- ret, & confirmet, donec ad beatam societatem ve- rorum נדיבים in perfectionis meta, quæ alterius seculi est, immensa ejus gratia evehar.

## 32:9
Vers. 9. WEALTHY WOMEN.) He says this to the women of the towns of Judea, which were besides Jerusalem.

Most understand the people of God concerning the cities themselves: Blessed Luther, Osiander, Brentius. Musculus says he calls the greater cities of the land of Judea women, the lesser with villages and hamlets daughters. Others, however, understand it of women properly, because in v. 11, stripping, and girding upon the loins, and lamentation upon the breasts is predicted. And so also Calvin: But that he addresses WOMEN especially, the Hebrews (as this meaning is customary for their language) understand cities: But I do not think the discourse here is figurative, and I rather retain the simplicity of the words. He addresses women rather than men, to show how great the slaughter will be: for otherwise women and girls are spared, because they are unwarlike, and have no power to defend themselves: But this destruction is said to be so monstrous that no one is spared. For not only are the women of the lesser cities besides Jerusalem to be understood: Because he dealt particularly with the CITY called κατ' ἐξοχὴν in v. 13 and 14, and predicted destruction to it. Furthermore, the Vulgate version does not please Musculus, therefore he says he does not see why Jerome, the LXX, and Oecolampadius rendered WEALTHY WOMEN, since the Hebrew word is derived from שאנן to be quiet, unless perhaps it was done because wealthy women are accustomed to be quiet and idle. He therefore renders it quiet women. Thus also the Genevan and Italian versions have it; Blessed Luther explained it as stoltze Frauen: because tranquility usually makes men more haughty, hence by metalepsis the Hebrew word denotes, he was insolent, and was proudly brought up, Is. 37, 29. Which sense agrees more: unless by quiet they are understood as secure; for tranquility itself cannot be disapproved.

CONFIDENT) You who live securely.

Latin:

Vers. 9. MULIERES OPULENTÆ.) Hæc dicit ad mulieres oppidorum Judææ, quæ erant præter Hieroso- lyma.

Plerique de civitatibus ipsis intelligunt po- puli Dei: B. Lutherus, Osiander, Brentius. Civitates terræ Judææ majores, inquit Musculus, vocat mu- lieres, minores cum pagis ac vicis filias. Alii tamen de mulieribus proprie intelligunt, quia v. 11. nuda- tio, & accinctio super lumbos, & planctus super ubera prædicitur. Atque ita etiam Calvinus: Quod au- tem MULIERES potissimum compellat, Hebræi (ut eorum linguæ hæc fignificatio usitata est) in- telligunt urbes: Sed figuratum hic sermonem esse non puto, ac potius retineo simplicitatem verbo- rum. Mulieres autem potius, quam viros com- pellat, ut ostendat, quanta futura sit clades: parci- tur enim alioqui mulieribus & puellis, quod imbel- les sint, neque sui defendendi potestatem habeant: Tam immane vero excidium hoc fore dicitur, ut ne- mini parcatur. Non enim intelligendæ tantum sunt mulieris civitatum minorum præter Hierso- lyma: Quia de CIVITATE κατ' ἐξοχὴν dicta v. 13. & 14. peculiariter egit, eique exitium prædixit. Cæ- terum non placet Musculo Vulgata versio, ideo ait se non videre, quare Hieronymus, LXX. & Oecolam- padius reddiderint MULIERES OPULENTÆ, quum Ebræa vox à שאנן quiescere derivetur, nisi forte id factum, quod mulieres opulentæ, quietæ & otiosæ esse soleant. Reddit ergo mulieris quietæ. Sic etiam Genev. & Italic. versio habet B. Lutherus stoltze Frauen exposuit: quia tranquillitas plerum- que reddit homines elatiores, inde per metalepsin Ebræum verbum notat, insolens fuit, & superbe e- ducatus est Es. 37, 29. Qui sensus magis congruit: ni- si per quietas intelligantur securæ; nam tranquillitas ipsa improbari non potest.

CONFIDENTES) Quæ secure vivitis.

## 32:10
Vers. 10.

FOR AFTER DAYS AND A YEAR.) That is, within three years, as above 19, 1.

Where the words after days and a year designate three years, Grotius could not show: therefore the gloss is merely arbitrary, concocted for the sake of a preconceived opinion, that the discourse here is about the incursion of Sennacherib. Which, however, also pleased Musculus: that that rest would not last for a full two years longer. But others more correctly refer those words, not to the time of peace and quiet, which still remained for them, but to the duration of the future calamity יָמִים עַל־שָׁנָה תִּרְגַּזְנָה בֹּטְחוֹת days above a year you will be troubled, secure women. Which sentence R. Kimchi explains as year with year, and thus Pagninus and the Italian version. Calvin interprets it thus: DAYS ABOVE A YEAR: he signifies by these words that the calamity will be long-lasting: that they will not suffer for one year, but that new troubles are to be seen thereafter. So also Brentius: You will be troubled FOR YEARS AND DAYS, i.e., for a long and indefinite time. For by the same phrase the Germans also circumscribe a long and indefinite time, Jahr und Tag. Nor is the mind of Blessed Luther in his Enarrations on this place any other; he signifies the future devastation by the Chaldeans, in which he includes all other evils up to Christ.

FOR THE VINTAGE IS FINISHED)

THE GATHERING SHALL COME NO MORE)

Brentius interprets this as the failure of the spiritual harvest. But it is better here to adhere to the literal meaning of the word: for the things that follow also bring about devastation. FOR THE VINTAGE IS FINISHED, that is, there will be no more vintage for you to expect. THE GATHERING SHALL COME NO MORE, it will be all over for the whole region and the Jewish nation. Osiander explains it as the gathering of grapes, and because wine is accustomed to signify joy in the Scriptures, he wishes it to be signified that God is about to take away all their joys: just as we see the Jews now, after the final devastation of Jerusalem, walking about stunned and as if half-dead, without any true cheerfulness of spirit, as if the divine wrath poured out upon them were inscribed upon their very foreheads. But with the blessed Luther, we prefer to understand these things literally. Nor does Calvin do badly here: Because the Jews were too addicted to earthly things and perishable food, he denounces to them a scarcity of wine and wheat according to their own understanding. If they had been better purged of their gross desires, he would rather have threatened the things which Jeremiah laments in his Lamentations, that the feast days had ceased, that the sacred assemblies had been abolished; but because, immersed in their own pleasures, they had not yet progressed so far in valuing spiritual goods, the Prophet, descending to their crudeness, addresses their bellies rather than their souls.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

POST DIES ENIM ET ANNUM.) Id est, intra triennium, ut supra 19, 1.

Ubi verba post dies & annum triennium desi- gnent, monstrare non potuit Grotius: Glossa ergo mere arbitraria est, conficta in gratiam præconce- ptæ opinionis, quod de Sennacheribi incursione ser- mo hic sit. Quæ tamen etiam Musculo placuit: haud amplius integrum biennium quietem illam du- raturam. Alii vero rectius verba illa referunt, non ad pacis & quietis tempus, quod adhuc illis reli- quum erat, sed ad durationem futuræ calamitatis יָמִים עַל־שָׁנָה תִּרְגַּזְנָה בֹּטְחוֹת dies supra an- num turbabimini securæ mulieres. Quam senten- tiam R. Kimchi exponit annum cum anno, atque ita Pagninus & Italic. versio. Eam sic interpretatur Cal- vinus: DIES SUPRA ANNUM: significat his verbis calamitatem diuturnam fore: non passuras ipsas uno anno, sed & novas deinceps ærumnas spectandas esse. Sic quoque Brentius: Perturba- bimini ANNIS ET DIEBUS, h. e. longo & in- definito tempore. Eadem enim phrasi etiam Germani circumscribunt longum & indefinitum tempus Jahr und Tag. Neque alia mens B. Lu- theris in Enarrat. h. l. significat vastitatem futuram per Chaldæos, in quam includit omnia alia mala usq; ad Christum.

CONSUMMATA EST ENIM VINDEMIA) De- fecit.

COLLECTIO ULTRA NON VENIET) Id est, Messis, quæ Græcis συγκομιδὴ dici solet.

De messis spiritualis defectu accipit Brentius. Sed præstat hic proprietati vocis inhærere: Nam devastationem inferunt etiam ea, quæ subjiciuntur. CONSUMMATA EST ENIM VINDEMIA, id est, nulla amplius erit vobis expectanda vindemia. COLLECTIO ULTRA NON VENIET, actum erit de tota regione & gente Judæa. Osiander de collectione uvarum explicat, & quia vinum læti- tiam in Sacris designare solet, id significari vult, quod Deus ipsis omnia gaudia ablaturus sit: quem- admodum post ultimam Hierosolymorum devasta- tionem Judæos videmus nunc attonitos, & quasi semimortuos obambulare, sine ulla vera animi hi- laritate, ut in frontibus quasi ipsorum inscripta sit ira divina in ipsos effusa. Sed cum B. Luthero hæc proprie intelligere malumus. Nec male hic Calvi- nus: Quia rebus terrenis & caducis alimentis ni- mium addicti erant Judæi: ex eorum sensu denun- ciat vini & tritici penuriam. Si melius à crassis cu- piditatibus purgati fuissent, potius minatus esset, quæ deplorat in suis Threnis Jeremias, sacrificia & festos dies cessasse, sacros conventus esse abolitos; fed quia in suis voluptatibus demersi nondum ita profecerant in æstimandis spiritualibus bonis, ad eorum ruditatem descendens Propheta, ventres eorum magis, quam animos compellat.

## 32:11
Ver. 11. STRIP YOURSELVES) Of precious garments.

He threatens that the most splendid garments will be stripped away. Although others understand this as the plundering of wealth and resources. And thus our Luther: Strip yourselves: it is imminent that I shall strip you of your kingdom, and political peace, and wealth, etc. AND BE CONFOUNDED, GIRD. In the Hebrew it is: nakedness and a girdle UPON YOUR LOINS, as Osiander renders it. Others explain it as: despoil, make naked, gird your loins. He commands them to be girded with sackcloth, describing the appearance of those mourning. Not only will precious garments be stripped from you, but you will stand naked and confounded, you will be clothed in sackcloth or the vilest attire. Because captive women were accustomed to be treated in this way. Whence Osiander again concludes that the destruction of the cities of Judea is being predicted, as well as the captivity and perpetual exile of their inhabitants.

GIRD YOUR LOINS) Prepare yourselves for menial tasks.

Latin:

Vers. 11. EXVITE VOS) Pretiosis vestibus.

Minatur detractum iri vestes splendidiss. Quam- vis alii de expilatione opum & facultatum intelli- gant. Atque ita Lutherus noster: Exuite: imminet, ut exuam regno, & pace politica, & opibus, &c. ET CONFUNDEMINI, ACCINGITE. In Ebræo est: nuditas & cinctorium SUPER LUMBOS VESTROS, ut reddit Osiander. Alii exponunt, spoliate, nudate, accingite lumbos. Sacco accingi ju- bet describens speciem lugentium. Non tantum vestes pretiosæ detrahentur vobis, sed stabitis nu- dæ & confusæ, sacco vel vilissimo vestitu induemi- ni. Quia ita tractari solebant captivæ mulieres. Unde iterum colligit Osiander, prædici urbium Ju- daicarum excidium, & inhabitatorum captivita- tem ac perpetuum exilium.

ACCINGITE LUMBOS VESTROS) Ad operas ancillares vosmet parate.

## 32:12
Ver. 12. UPON THE BREASTS LAMENT) Seneca in the Troades: Your breasts lie torn by maternal palms.

UPON THE DESIRABLE REGION) Judea.

UPON THE FRUITFUL VINE) Upon so many vineyards.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SUPER VBERA PLANGITE) Seneca Troa- dibus: Tibi maternis ubera palmis. Laniata jacent.

SUPER REGIONE DESIDERABILI) Judæa.

SUPER VINEA VERTILI) Super tot vinetis.

## 32:13
Ver. 13. UPON THE GROUND OF MY PEOPLE THORNS AND BRIARS SHALL COME UP) That is, upon the suburban lands near Jerusalem.

HOW MUCH MORE UPON ALL THE HOUSES OF JOY) That is, pleasant villas.

OF THE EXULTING CITY) In the Hebrew: the exulting town: by enallage and the omission of the copula. The sense is: And upon all the towns now full of joy.

Grotius falsely explains this as referring only to the suburban lands near Jerusalem: For by the ground of the Lord's people, the land of all Judea is understood, as if to say: The land of my people will not only be devastated by enemies, but will also be destitute of its cultivators in the future, and will lie uncultivated and waste. Nor are pleasant villas understood by the houses of joy, or towns full of joy by the exulting city: But the particle עַד here amplifies the calamity: indeed, upon all the houses of joy of the city (which is so named by way of eminence), of the Metropolis Jerusalem itself: which resounds with joys, secure. These things certainly cannot be restricted to the remaining towns, besides Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SUPER HUMUM POPULI MEI SPINÆ ET VEPRES ASCENDENT) Id est, super fundos subur- banos apud Hierosolyma.

QVANTO MAGIS SUPER OMNES DOMOS GAUDII) Id est, amœnas villas.

CIVITATIS EXSVLTANTIS) In Hebræo: oppi- dum exsultans: per enallagen & omissionem copulæ. Sen- sus est: Et super omnia oppida plena nunc lætitiæ.

Falso explicat Grotius de solis suburbanis fun- dis apud Hierosolyma: Nam per humum populi Do- mini terra Judææ universæ intelligitur q. d. Terra populi mei non modo vastabitur ab hostibus, sed & cultoribus suis in posterum destituta, inculta ac vasta jacebit. Neque per domos gaudii amœnæ villæ in- telliguntur, aut per civitatem exultantem, oppida lætitiæ plena: Sed amplificatur hic particula עַד ca- lamitas: imo super omnes domos gaudii civitatis (quæ ἐξοχικῶς ita nuncupata) ipsius Metropoleos Jeru- salem: quæ gaudiis secura perstrepit. Non possunt certe hæc restringi ad oppida reliqua, præter Hie- rosolyma.

## 32:14
Ver. 14. FOR THE HOUSE IS CAST DOWN) The villas will be empty.

THE MULTITUDE OF THE CITY IS LEFT)

These things confirm what we have said, that Jerusalem cannot be removed. For THE PALACE, that is, the temple itself is said to be abandoned. THE MULTITUDE OF THE CITY IS LEFT. The city of Jerusalem, which abounded with a huge multitude of people, shall lie deserted: as Osiander explains. Others understand it of magnificent palaces; but no one of villas: no one of towns outside Jerusalem. For in this Metropolis there were both principal palaces and a very great multitude of people.

DARKNESS AND TREMBLING HAVE BEEN MADE OVER THE CAVES FOREVER) He reads ערפל ובחל. We have עפל ובחן. In an excellent sense: The towers and castles shall become dens of wild beasts for a long time.

The error of the Vulgate is deservedly corrected. Which our German version also amended. But there is no reason why we should therefore immediately admit that a different reading once obtained: Since there is nothing more frequent among interpreters than a παρεόρασις (misreading). But having left this aside (concerning which Jerome may be consulted), we are more concerned with the sense of the Hebrew reading, which Grotius does not deny to be genuine. But it is not obscure what total and final destruction (πανωλεθρίαν) it brings upon the land of the Jews, namely that the palaces must be left desolate, the whole city lie deserted, the towers and most beautiful fortifications be laid waste, and become a perpetual cave or pasture for flocks. Nor is there any reason why the word עַד־עוֹלָם should be restricted to a long time: since its proper and primary signification should rather be heeded, and all things here import a monstrous and perennial desolation, and look to the final destruction. Jerome explained this sense, whose passage it is helpful to transcribe: He says the vintage is finished, and after the final desolation, which happened under Vespasian and Titus and Hadrian, that no other captivity is to come: nor will there remain clusters among the people that are to be gathered thereafter. Whence they are provoked to lamentation, and are commanded to bare their breasts and gird their loins, because the region once desirable and the fertile vineyard, of which it is written: I planted you a fruitful vineyard, but how have you turned into the bitterness of a strange vine, has been destroyed by the Roman laying waste. Upon the soil (he says) of my people, thorns and briars, or hay, shall ascend. And the sense is: If thorns and briars have filled the land of Judea, which is the land of promise, how much more other cities, which are full of joy, and which shall follow that Gospel: Woe to you who laugh now, for you shall weep. For the house, that is, my temple is dismissed; as I say to the Apostles: Arise, let us go hence; and to the incredulous: Your house shall be left to you desolate. Palpable darkness has possessed the inner sanctuaries of the temple and the secret mysteries, and they have been made not cellars for the vessels of the Lord, but caves even unto eternity. For they had heard from the Lord Savior: My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves. The joy (he says) of wild asses, the pasture of flocks. Which is to be understood either literally, because all things are deserted: or spiritually, that with Israel expelled, wild men and those not having the knowledge of God dwell in Judea. These are the words of Jerome. THE JOY OF WILD ASSES) Wild asses will graze there, as in desert places. THE PASTURE OF FLOCKS) Of those wandering with no one to hinder them. See above 7, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DOMVS ENIM DEMISSA EST) Vaca- bunt villæ.

MULTITUDO URBIS RELICTA EST) Oppida illa erunt vacua.

Hæc confirmant, quod diximus, eximi non posse Hierosolyma. Nam PALATIUM, hoc est, templum ipsum dicitur derelictum. MULTITU- DO URBIS RELICTA. Urbs Jerusalem, quæ ingenti multitudine populi abundabat, deserta jace- bit: ut Osiander explicat. Alii de palatiis magnifi- cis intelligunt; nemo autem de villis: nemo de op- pidis extra Hierosolyma. Nam in hac Metropoli & palatia præcipua erant, & maxima populi multi- tudo.

TENEBRÆ ET PALPITATIO FACTA SUNT SUPER SPELUNCAS IN ÆTERNUM) Legit ערפל ובחל. Ad nos habemus עפל ובחן. Sensu optimo: Tur- res & castella fient spelæa ferarum in longum tempus.

Merito corrigitur Vulgatæ error. Quam etiam emendavit versio nostra Germanica. Sed non est, quod ideo admittamus statim, olim diversam le- ctionem obtinuisse: Quum παρεόρασις interpp. ni- hil sit frequentius. Hoc autem relicto (de quo vi- deri poterit Hieronymus) de sensu lectionis Ebraicæ, quam germanam esse, non negat Grotius, magis soliciti sumus. Quem vero totalem & finalem παν- ωλεθρίαν terræ Judæorum inferre, haud obscurum est, quod nempe palatia desolata relinqui, urbs to- ta deserta jacere, arces & munitiones pulcherrima wastari, ac perpetua spelunca vel pascua gregum fieri debeant. Neque est, quod verbum עַד־עוֹלָם re- stringatur ad longum tempus: quum propria & præ- cipua ejus significatio potius attendenda sit, & omnia hic immanem ac perennem vastitatem im- portent, ac ultimum excidium spectent. Exposuit hunc sensum Hieronymus, cujus locum adscribere juvat: Dicit vindemiam consummatam, & post ul- timam vastitatem, quæ sub Vespasiano & Tito Ha- drianog; accidit, nequaquam aliam captivitatem esse venturam: nec remansuros botros in populis, qui deinceps colligendi sint. Unde provocantur ad plan- ctum, & jubentur nudare pectora & accingere lum- bos suos, eo quod regio quondam desiderabilis & vi- nea fertilis, de qua scriptum est: Ego plantavi te vineam fructiferam totam, verum quomodo con- versa es in amaritudinem vitis alienæ, Romano va- stante deleta sit. Super humum (inquit) populi mei spinæ & vepres, sive fænum ascendent. Et est sensus: Si terram Judæam, quæ repromissionis terra est, spinæ repleverunt & vepres, quanto magis alias civitates, quæ plenæ sunt gaudio, & quæ illud Ev- angelium consequentur: Væ qui gaudetis nunc, quoniam plorabitis. Domus enim, id est, templum meum dimissum est; dicente me ad Apostolos: Surgi- te, abeamus hinc; & ad incredulos: Relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta. Adyta templi & secre- ta mysteria palpabiles tenebræ possederunt, & facta sunt nequaquam cellaria vaforum domini, sed spe- luncæ usq; in sempiternum. Audierant enim à Do- mino Salvatore: Domus Patris mei domus oratio- nis vocabitur, vos autem fecistis speluncam latro- num. Gaudium (inquit) onagrorum, pascua gre- gum. Quod vel juxta literam intelligendum est, eo quod deserta sint omnia: vel spiritualiter, quod expulso Israële, feri homines & Dei notitiam non habentes habitent in Judæa. Hæc Hieronymus. GAUDIUM ONAGRORVM) Onagri ibi pascent, ut in locis desertis. PASCVA GREGVM) Nullo prohibente vagantium. Vide supra 7, 24.

## 32:15
Vers. 15. UNTIL THE SPIRIT BE POURED UPON US FROM ON HIGH) Until the love of God toward us appears: as above 30, 18. This is a manifest depravation of an illustrious prophecy: For the Prophet speaks of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, as the words themselves sound, which was to be in the New Testament. Not, however, in general of any proof of divine love whatsoever. Nor is God said anywhere to pour out the Spirit in this sense, that He wishes to declare His love, even though that outpouring is altogether a most eminent proof and testimony of divine love and grace. But while this promise is subjoined to divine judgments, regard is had for the faithful among the people of God: although most grievous punishments, and at length destruction itself, hang over the Jewish people, yet God will preserve a Church for Himself and will pour out the Holy Spirit from heaven, so that the horrible desert of the Gentiles may be converted into the most fertile Carmel mountain of the Church. Not that all the Jews will perish; but that the Holy Spirit will be poured out upon them, and through them the nations will be gathered to the Church. UNTIL IT BE POURED OUT. More correctly: IT SHALL YET BE POURED OUT. Which was fulfilled in the Apostles, who were Jews by race. It pleases Oecolampadius greatly if it be said: Those things which were predicted were not to be, UNTIL the Spirit is sent from heaven. Therefore, there is no reason why we should restrict that calamity to the Babylonian captivity, or with others to the times of the Maccabees. For it is connected openly with the final destruction of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the calling of the Gentiles. Which were also connected as regards the πλήρωμα itself.

AND THE DESERT SHALL BE IN CARMEL, AND CARMEL SHALL BE RECKONED AS A FOREST) He explains, as above 29, 17.

Above, he explained the casting down of the lofty Assyrians and the raising up of the cast-down Hebrews: but this sense neither agreed with that passage, nor can it be adapted to this one. Therefore, the discourse here is about the consequence and fruit of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, which is the conversion of the horrid desert of Gentilism into Carmel, a most fertile mountain, most joyful for the true Church: namely, that those who were hitherto seen as an uncultivated desert, never to bear any good fruit, are to be converted to the true faith and rendered fertile with good fruits. On the contrary, however, Carmel SHALL BE RECKONED AS A FOREST, the mountain once most fertile shall become an unfruitful wood: For although many even from the Jews were converted to faith in Christ after the coming of Christ, yet these, compared to the conversion of the Gentiles throughout the whole world and their numerous multitude, are to be considered very few, so that consequently Gentilism, the desert, is turned into Mount Carmel, famous for fertility, because of its spiritual frequency and fertility, and vice versa the people of the Jews, who once flourished in true religion and the fruits of good works like a most fertile mountain, seem to have passed into a horrid and unfruitful wood. If the Assyrians are to be understood here by the desert, and are said to be converted into Carmel, that is, into level fields, what will be the reason for the naming, and what will be the analogy here, the desert will be into level fields, that is, the lofty shall be cast down! For our author had handed down this exposition in chapter 29, 17. He calls them, he says, מדבר for the reason that they were, namely, lofty, like wooded mountains. But מדבר denotes a desert, not wooded mountains, and it is so called not because of loftiness, but because of emptiness, namely, that from there all things are overturned and inconvenient for cultivation. What has this to do with lofty mountains! Again, how will judgment dwell in the desert or solitude, that is, among the Assyrians? He had to devise a wonderful gloss here, AND JUDGMENT SHALL DWELL IN THE SOLITUDE: that is, God will severely punish those Assyrians. To whom could a sense of this kind ever have come to mind, except to Grotius, born apt for inventing anything! To dwell in judgment and for justice to sit are coupled together in the phrase of Scripture, they are not opposed to each other, and both are taken in a good sense, but by no means in a bad one. Since, therefore, the same ones who had been a desert are said to have become Carmel, it is said that judgment now dwells in that desert, and justice sits in Carmel, that is, among them: namely, that Gentilism is to be filled with judgment and justice: which is a periphrasis of the kingdom of Christ: for in it dwells judgment, and justice sits, Isa. 9, 7. Jerem. 23, 6. We consider this the simplest explanation: for the Prophet pursues the description of the kingdom of Christ: we do not deny, however, that the remnant of the Jews also pertains to Carmel, as that to which the multitude of the Gentiles was to be gathered, as to the one true Church: whence the Blessed Luther rightly: And the desert shall be in Carmel, the desert, that is, the remnant of the Jews: and the Gentiles shall be as a most cultivated field, they shall bear most abundant fruits in the faith of Christ. And Carmel, that is, the Synagogue, which now flourishes, shall be reduced to a forest, and shall be desolated. Others, however, distinguish those things which we join. Oecolampadius says that the justice which was previously among the Jews will come into the desert, and nevertheless will not be lacking in the cultivated field, that is, in the Apostles and others who believed from the Jews, so that from Jews and Gentiles there may be one Church. And Osiander: And judgment shall dwell in the solitude, that is, in the remnant of the Jews, that is, the converted Jews shall be rightly governed by the ministry of the Gospel: and justice shall sit in Carmel: that is, the converted Gentiles shall pursue justice in their whole life: but it is known that justice and judgment are joined in the kingdom of Christ, not separated: therefore, that separation is not to be admitted here either. Concerning which see Brentius on chapter 9 of Isaiah, verse 2. In the kingdom of Christ, there is justice when believers are reckoned righteous on account of Christ, and are adopted as sons of God, so that they may receive the heavenly inheritance; there is judgment when Satan and death are oppressed, and the pious are defended and saved, so that they are not absorbed by death and Satan (or even the world). Therefore, that gloss of Grotius is alien: AND JUSTICE SHALL SIT IN CARMEL, that is, the goodness of God will reveal itself toward the Jews, who had been like low ground. For Carmel is not indicated here because of humility, but because of fertility, and there is no discourse here about the goodness of God; but about the justice proper to the kingdom of Christ, the fruit of which is spiritual peace: much less about a temporal rescue from the power of the Assyrian, since spiritual goods are promised here, and the fruits that are to redound from the outpouring of the Holy Spirit are explained. And the word SHALL SIT is not to be taken concerning a transient act, such as that rescue was, but it implies some permanence: such as the preservation of justice is in the kingdom of Christ, as it is a good proper and perpetual to it.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DONEC EFFVNDATVR SVPER NOS SPIRITVS DE EXCELSO) Donec amor Dei erga nos appareat: ut supra 30, 18. Manifesta hæc est depravatio illustris vatici- nii: Loquitur enim Propheta de effusione Spiritus Sancti, ut verba ipsa sonant, quæ in novo Testam. futura erat. Non autem in genere de amoris divini quocunque documento. Neque uspiam effundere Spiritum Deus dicitur hoc sensu, quod amorem suum declarari velit, tametsi omnino effusio illa sit amoris & gratiæ divinæ documentum & testimo- nium eminentissimum. Dum autem hæc promis- sio judiciis divinis subjungitur, fidelium ratio ha- betur in populo Dei: tametsi gravissima supplicia, ac tandem ipsum excidiu populo Judaico incum- bant, Deum tamen Ecclesiam sibi servaturum ac Spiritum Sanctum effusurum de cælo, ut horri- dum desertum gentilium in Carmel montem fer- tilissimum Ecclesiæ convertatur. Non perituros Judæos universos; sed super ipsos effusum iri Spi- ritum Sanctum, & per eosdem gentes ad Ecclesiam congregandos. DONECEFFUNDETUR. Rectius: ADHUC EFFUNDETUR. Quod in Apostolis genere Judæis impletum est. Oecolam- padio admodum placet, si dicatur: Ista quæ prædicta erant, non futura, DONEC de cælo mittatur Spiri- tus. Non ergo est, quod ad captivitatem Babyloni- cam, vel cum aliis ad tempora Maccabæorum istam calamitatem restringamus. Connectitur enim aperte cum novissimo excidio Spiritus Sancti effusio, & gentium vocatio. Quæ etiam quoad πλήρωμα ipsum connexa fuêre.

ET ERIT DESERTUM IN CARMEL, ET CAR- MEL IN SALTUM REPUTABITUR) Explicat, ut su- pra 29, 17.

Supra de sublimibus Assyriis dejiciendis, & Ebræis projectis erigendis exposuit: sed hic sensus neque isti loco congruebat, neque huic aptari po- test. Igitur hic de consequenti sermo est, & fructu effusionis Spiritus Sancti, qui est conversio deserti horridi gentilitatis in Charmel montem fertiliffi- mum, lætissimum veræ Ecclesiæ: quod nempe illi, qui visi hactenus quasi incultum desertum, nullum unquàm bonum fructum laturi, ad veram fidem sint convertendi,bonisq; fructibus fertiles redden- di. Ex adverso vero Charmel IN SALTUM REPUTABITUR, mons olim fertilissimus fiet sylva infrugifera: Quamvis enim è Judæis quoque multi post adventum Christi ad fidem in Christum conversi, hi tamen præ gentium per totum terra- rum orbem conversione, numerosa multitudine, pauci admodum censendi, ut proinde gentilismus desertum in montem Charmelum fertilitate cele- brem, ob frequentiam & fertilitatem spiritualem conversus, ac vice versa populus Judæorum, qui quondam vera religione ac bonorum operum fru- ctibus instar fertilissimi montis floruit, in sylvam horridam & infrugiferam transiisse videatur. Si Assyrii per desertum hic intelligendi, & in Charmel convertendi dicantur, hoc est, in agros planos, quænam ratio appellationis, & quænam analogia hic erit, desertum erit in agros planos,id est,sublimes dejicientur! Hanc enim expositionem tradiderat Noster cap.29,17.Vocat illos,inquit, מדבר ob id quod fuerunt,nempe elati,ut montes sylvosi.At מדבר deser- tum notat,non sylvosos montes, neque ob sublimi- tatem, sed ob vacuitatem ita dicitur, quod nempe illinc omnia sint subversa & incommoda culturæ. Quid hoc ad elatos montes! Rursus quomodo ju- dicium in deserto vel solitudine habitabit, hoc est, penes Assyrios? Mirabilem hic glossam excogi- tare opus habuit, ET HABITABIT IN SO- LITUDINE JUDICIUM: id est, Deus Assyrios illos graviter puniet. Cui unquam in mentem ve- nire potuit sensus ejusmodi, præterquam Grotio, ad quævis fingenda apto nato! Habitare judicium & sedere justitiam, phrasi Scripturæ inter se copu- lantur, non sibi opponuntur, & utrumque in bo- nam partem accipitur, neutiquam vero in malam. Quum ergo iidem, qui desertum fuerant, Charmel dicantur evasisse, in deserto illo nunc judicium ha- bitare, & in Charmel,hoc est,penes eosdem justitia sedere dicitur: quod nempe gentilismus judicio, & justitia replendus sit: quæ περίφρασις est regni Christi: in eo enim habitat judicium, sedetq; justi- tia, Esa. 9, 7. Jerem. 23, 6. Quam explicationem simplicissimam arbitramur: persequitur enimPro- pheta descriptionem regni Christi: non negamus tamen ad Charmel etiam pertinere reliquias Judæo- rum, utpote ad quas aggreganda erat multitudo gentium, tanquam ad unicam veram Ecclesiam: unde recte B. Lutherus: Et erit desertum in Char- mel, desertum, id est, reliquiæ Judæorum: & gentes erunt ceu cultissimus ager, ferent uberrimos fructus in fide Christi. Et Charmel, id est, Synagoga, quæ nunc floret, redigetur in saltum, & desolabitur. Alii tamen ista, quæ conjungimus,distinguunt. Oeco- lampadius dicit justitiam, quæ antea apud Judæos. venturam in desertum, & nihilominus in agro culto non defuturam, hoc est, in Apostolis & aliis,qui ex Judæis crediderunt, ut ex Judæis & gentibus sint una Ecclesia. Et Osiander: Et habitabit in solitudi- ne judicium, id est, reliquiis Judæorum, hoc est, con- versi Judæi recte gubernabuntur Evangelii ministe- rio: & justitia in Charmel sedebit: id est, gentes con- versæ justitiam in tota sua vita sectabuntur: sed no- tum est, quod justitia & judicium in regno Christi conjungantur, non separentur: proinde neq; hic separatio illa admittenda. De quo Brentius ad cap. 9. Esa. v. 2. In regno Christi justitia est, cum cre- dentes reputantur justi propter Christum, & ado- ptantur in filios Dei, ut accipiant hæreditatem cœ- lestem; judicium est, cum Satan & mors opprimun- tur, & pii defenduntur, ac servantur, ne à morte & Satana (vel mundo etiam) absorbeantur. Aliena ergo illa glossa Grotii: ET JUSTITIA SEDE- BIT IN CHARMEL, id est, bonitas Dei se ape- riet erga Judæos, qui fuerant velut terra humilis. Nam neque Charmel hic ob humilitatem, sed ob fertilitatem indigitatur, neque de bonitate Dei hic sermo est; sed de justitia regni Christi propria, cu- jus fructus est pax spiritualis: multo minus de tem- porali ereptione è potestate Assyrii, quum bona hic promittantur spiritualia, & fructus ab effusione Spiritus Sancti redundanturi exponantur. Et ver- bum SEDEBIT non de actu transeunte, qualis erat illa ereptio, accipiendum, sed permansionem ali- quam infert: qualis conservatio justitiæ est in re- gno Christi, utpote quæ bonum ipsi proprium & perpetuum.

## 32:16
Vers. 16. AND JUDGMENT SHALL DWELL IN THE SOLITUDE) God will severely punish those Assyrians. He calls them מדבר for the reason that they were, namely, lofty, like wooded mountains. AND JUSTICE SHALL SIT IN CARMEL) The goodness of God will reveal itself toward the Jews, who had been like low ground.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET HABITABIT IN SOLITUDINE JV- DICIVM) Deus Assyrios illos graviter puniet. Vocat illos מדבר od id quod fuerunt, nempe elati, ut montes silvosi. ET JVSTITIA IN CHARMEL SEDEBIT) Bo- nitas Dei se aperiet erga Judæos, qui fuerant velut terra humilis.

## 32:17
Vers. 17. AND THE WORK OF JUSTICE SHALL BE PEACE, AND THE SERVICE OF JUSTICE SILENCE) More correctly: and the produce of justice tranquility. The goodness of God will bring forth for us peace and security. See above 9, 7. 11, 6. here above 1.

We admit the correction of the Vulgate: but not concerning the fruit of the grace of God in external liberation from enemies: But the discourse is properly concerning the fruit of the righteousness of the faithful, which is peace and tranquility of conscience. For being justified by faith in Christ we have peace Rom. 5, 1. Good things are promised here, not corporal, but spiritual. Which are to be expected from the outpouring of the Holy Spirit in the New Testament among the converted Gentiles, and the remnant of the Jews. And the Prophet openly signifies what kind of tranquility he understands, not temporary, but eternal: SECURITY FOREVER. And therefore he promises a perpetual dwelling in the tabernacles of peace, which the people of the Lord, that is, the faithful, shall have. Nor is the discourse about other goods in chap. 9, 7. 11, 6. or at the beginning of the present chapter. If therefore those things are to be compared here, it will be even more clearly evident that spiritual peace and tranquility are promised here. Musculus himself acknowledges the spiritual sense here (whom Grotius followed in this chapter) although he desires to draw these things also licentiously to Hezekiah: Until the Spirit be poured upon us from on high, those who are like a desert, namely destitute of every yield of piety and righteousness, may become like a fertile field, bringing forth the most abundant fruits of true piety and righteousness. And Carmel be reputed as a forest: that is, those who now flourish, and are thought to be like Carmel, when they are in reality devoid of true righteousness, then in respect of the true faithful they shall be found so uncultivated and sterile that they shall be reputed as a forest. And v. 17. The rest and security of the wicked is not forever, but the rest and security of the pious is forever; because the cultivation of righteousness is rest and security forever. These things are manifest, but it is difficult to rely upon them, unless we direct the eyes of our minds, as if with the keenness of an immovable faith, into the truth of the word of God. Musculus also warns that the word ישב he dwelt was not used here without reason by the Prophet: In both places, as much in the preceding verse as in this one, he uses the word ישב, which signifies to dwell, not idly. There he says that justice will dwell in the faithful, here that his faithful ones will dwell in the tabernacle of peace. We are admonished that we shall be as firm and unmoved in peace as justice, which is through the spirit of Christ, is firm in us. And he teaches that tabernacles here, in the genuine sense, are to be understood not as external, but as spiritual. He does not speak, he says, of that elementary and external tabernacle which was in Zion: but of the heavenly protection, which he metaphorically calls the tabernacle of peace, secure mansions, and the refreshment of rest. David expressed the same thing in other words, saying: He who dwells in the help of the Most High, abides in the protection of the God of heaven, etc. Meanwhile, we do not deny that the mansions of the pious and faithful can be called tabernacles of peace and secure mansions. But that sense which we provide is much more genuine. Blessed Luther here particularly observed that the Prophet designated a triple security against a triple disturbance. That the law demands from us justice which we cannot provide, then sin bites us, and finally death destroys and kills, and against these a triple security is promised. But because here peace is often still disturbed for the pious, this promise will attain its full complement in the other life: for then the elect will dwell in the habitation of peace, in the tabernacles of confidence, and in an abundant, or secure, rest, forever without any anxiety or disturbance.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET ERIT OPVS JVSTITIÆ PAX, ET CVLTVS JVSTITIÆ SILENTIVM) Rectius: & pro- ventus justitiæ tranquillitas. Dei bonitas nobis pariet pacem ac securitatem. Vid. sup. 9, 7. 11, 6. hic supra 1.

Admittimus correctionem Vulgati: sed non de fructu gratiæ Dei in externa liberatione ab hosti- bus: Verum de fructu justitiæ fidelium proprie ser- mo est, quæ est pax ac tranquillitas conscientiæ. Ju- stificati enim per fidem in Christum pacem habemus Rom. 5, 1. Bona hic promittuntur non corporalia, sed spiritualia. Quæ è Spiritus Sancti effusione in Novo Test. expectanda penes conversos gentiles, & reliquias Judæorum. Et aperte fignificat Pro- pheta, qualem tranquillitatem intelligat, non tem- porariam, sed æternam: SECURITAS IN SE- CULUM. Atque ideo perpetuam promittit man- sionem in tabernaculis pacis, quam populus Do- mini, hoc est, fideles habituri sint. Neque de aliis bonis sermo est cap. 9, 7. 11, 6. aut sub ingressum præsentis capitis. Si ergo ea hic conferenda, lucu- lenti9 adhuc patebit, hic pacem & tranquillitatem spiritualem promitti. Sensum spiritualem hic agnoscit ipse Musculus(quem in hoc capite sequu- tus est Grotius) etsi licenter hæc etiam ad Eze- chiam trahere cupiat: Donec effuso super nos Spiri- tu de excelso, ii qui instar deserti sunt, omni videli- cet pietatis & justitiæ proventu destituti, fiant instar agri fertilis, veræ pietatis & justitiæ fructus uberri- mos proferentes. Et Charmel pro sylva reputetur: id est, qui nunc florent, & quasi Charmel esse putan- tur, cum sint reipsa veræ justitiæ expertes, tum tem- poris respectu verorum fidelium sic deprehendentur inculti & steriles, ut pro sylva reputentur. Et adv. 17. Quies & securitas impiorum non est in secu- lum, in seculum vero est piorum; quia cultus ju- stitiæ quies est & securitas in seculum. Sunt hæc manifesta, verum difficile est illis inniti, nisi oculos mentis nostræ immota fidei velut acie, in veritatem verbi Dei intendamus. Monet etiam Musculus, quod hic verbo ישב habitavit non præter rem usus fit Propheta : Utrobiq́; tam præcedenti, quam hoc verfu verbo ישב, quod habitare fignificat, non otiofe utitur. Illic justitiam in fidelibus, hic fideles suos in tabernaculo pacis habituros, dicit. Admone- mur, tam fore nos in pace firmos & immotos, quam firma in nobis est justitia, quæ est per fpiritum Christi. Et tabernacula hic, germano fenfu, intelligenda esse non externa, sed fpiritualia docet. Non loquitur, in- quit, de elementario & externo illo tabernaculo, quod erat in Zion : sed de protectione cælesti, quam meta- phorice vocat tabernaculum pacis, mansiones secu- ras, & refrigerium quietis. Rem eandem David aliis verbis expressit, dicens : Qui habitat in adjuto- rio Altissimi, in protectione Dei cæli commora- tur, &c. interea non negamus mansiones piorum ac fidelium vocari posse tabernacula pacis, & mansio- nes securas. Verum sensus iste, quem tradimus, mul- to est germanior. B. Lutherus hic peculiariter ob- servavit, quod triplicem securitatem designarit Pro- pheta, contra triplicem turbationem. Quod lex exigat à nobis justitiam, quam non possumus præ- stare, peccatum nos deinde mordeat, tandem mors perdat, & occidat, & contra hæc promittatur tri- plex securitas. Sed quia hic pax fæpe turbatur ad- huc piis, promissio hæc plenum complementum consequutura est in altera vita : tum enim habita- bunt electi in habitatione pacis, in tabernaculis fiduciæ, & requie opulenta, vel secura, in perpe- tuum fine ulla solicitudine aut perturbatione.

## 32:19
Ver. 19. BUT HAIL IN THE DESCENT OF THE FOREST) But hail shall descend upon the forest. Upon the wooded mountains, that is, as we have already said, the Assyrians. Hail signifies the wrath of God above 28. 2. and often in the Psalms. AND THE CITY SHALL BE HUMBLED BY HUMILITY) Babylon. See above 13. That the wrath of God is signified by hail, there is no doubt. But Judea was called the FOREST, inasmuch as it was to be turned from Carmel into a forest. The Assyrians are nowhere called by this name. Nor is there any mention or trace of Babylon here. Therefore, the CITY said ἐξοχικῶς (by way of eminence) in Judea is understood as Jerusalem; and thus the judgment of God against the Jews and Jerusalem is designated: And since the former things are spiritual, the judgment here also is to be understood not so much of temporal as of spiritual punishments, concerning the hail of eternal unhappiness, by which the faithless and unfruitful Jews are to be destroyed: and concerning the final humiliation of the city of Jerusalem.

Latin:

Verf. 19. GRANDO AUTEM IN DESCENSIONE SALTVS) Grando autem defcendet fuper sylvam. Super montes sylvosos, id est, ut jam diximus, Assyrios. Grando Dei iram fignificat fupra 28. 2. & in Psalmis fæpe. ET HVMILITATE HVMILIABITVR CIVITAS) Babylon. Vid. fupr. 13. Per grandinem iram Dei significari, nullum est dubium. Sed SYLVA dicebatur Judæa, utpote quæ è Charmelo in sylvam vertenda. Assyrii nus- piam dicti hoc nomine. Neque de Babylone vola hic, vel vestigium. CIVITAS itaque ἐξοχικῶς di- cta in Judæa Jerusalem intelligitur; adeoque judi- cium Dei adversus Judæos & Hierosolyma desi- gnatur: Et quum priora spiritualia sint, judicium etiam hic non tam temporalium, quam spiritua- lium pœnarum intelligendum, de grandine æter- næ infelicitatis, quo infideles & infrugiferi Judæi perdendi: & de novissima humiliatione civitatis Hierosalem.

## 32:20
Ver. 20. BLESSED ARE YOU WHO SOW UPON ALL WATERS) In the Hebrew: Blessed are you, who sow by all waters. You Jews, who will make a sowing in irrigated places, and for that reason very fertile. SENDING FORTH THE FOOT OF THE OX AND THE ASS) Such an abundance of all fruits, that you will even permit beasts of burden to graze there. Fertility is designated, but spiritual. Nor are the Jews addressed here in the time of Isaiah. But the discourse is directed to the Apostles and any faithful ministers of the Church. For these sow spiritually, to these the fruit is promised, because they are to sow in places not horrid and sterile, but irrigated and fruitful, making a sowing everywhere, and thus their labor is not to be in vain in the Lord, nay, that the greatest abundance of spiritual things is to result. Although by the latter words the object of spiritual cultivation can also be understood, as Blessed Luther explained: Blessed are you Apostles, who sow, that is, preach the word everywhere by the waters, that is, among all nations, where you send forth both oxen and asses for pastures (for by the waters are fertile places suitable for pastures) that is, you teach, exercise, and instruct both perfect Doctors and weak and imperfect disciples. Others wish the laborious diligence of spiritual cultivation and the abundance of things to be cultivated to be designated:

Sending (seed after) the foot of the ox and the ass: after the earth has been broken up by the plow (the work not only of oxen, but also of asses). For the region will be so abundant for you to plow and sow, that you will be compelled to use oxen and asses (whatever beasts of burden are at hand) for the cultivation of the fields: nor will you be able to observe that Mosaic law which forbids sowing with an ox and an ass together. By these, Osiander judges it to be signified that the labor of the Apostles and other faithful ministers in disseminating the Gospel will not be void, but most fruitful, and that they will one day receive most abundant rewards for that labor, Dan. 12. For which reason they are called blessed. Grotius, however, savors only of earthly and temporal things here.

Latin:

Vers. 20. BEATI QVI SEMINATIS SUPER OMNES AQVAS) In Hebræo: Beati vos, qui feretis ad omnes aquas. Vos Judæi, qui sementem facietis in locis ir- riguis, & ob id valde feracibus. IMMITTENTES PEDEM BOVIS ET ASINI) Tanta omnium frugum copia, ut etiam jumentis permissuri sitis ibi pasci. Fertilitas designatur, sed spiritualis. Neque Judæi hic compellantur Esaiæ tempore. Sed ad Apostolos & quosvis fideles Ecclesiæ ministros sermo dirigitur. Hi enim ferunt spiritualiter, his fructus promittitur, quod in locis non horridis & sterilibus, sed irriguis & frugiferis seminaturi sint, ubique locorum sementem facturi, adeoque labor eorum non sit inanis futurus in Domino, imo quod summa spiritualium copia proventura sit. Quam- quam per verba posteriora etiam intelligi possit culturæ spiritualis objectum, ut B. Lutherus expo- suit: Beati vos Apostoli, qui seminatis, id est, prædi- catis verbum passim juxta aquas, id est, in omnibus gentibus, ubi immittitis tam boves, quam asinos pro pascuis (ad aquas enim fœcunda & pascuis commo- da loca sunt) id est, docetis, exercetis, instruitis tam perfectos Doctores, quam infirmos & imperfectos di- sipulos. Alii culturæ spiritualis sedulitatem labo- riosam, & colendorum copiam designari volunt:

Mittentes (semen post) pedem bovis & asini: post- quam aratro terra (opera non modo boum, sed etiam asinorum) est proscissa. Tam enim copiosa regio erit vobis aranda, & seminanda, ut cogamini boves & asinos (quæcunque ad manum modo ju- menta fuerint) ad culturam agrorum adhibere: ne- que possitis eam legem Mosaicam observare, quæ vetat, ne seminaretur in bove & asino. His Osian- der significari censet, Apostolorum & aliorum fide- lium ministrorum laborem in disseminando Evan- gelio non fore irritum, sed fructuosissimum, ejusque laboris eos olim percepturos præmia copiosissima Dan. 12. Quo nomine beati prædicantur. Grotius vero mere terrena & temporalia hic sapit.

## 33:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIII.

To the Assyrian devastator, devastation is denounced, with liberation promised to the faithful and to Jerusalem.

Ver. 1. WOE TO YOU WHO PLUNDER, SHALL YOU NOT ALSO BE PLUNDERED) The Interpreter has placed 'you shall be plundered' here in the passive. The sense is: O you plunderer Sennacherib, (of whom Jerome also rightly explains this passage) is it not just that you also should become plunder? See Rev. 13, 10.

Grotius is mistaken when he says that Jerome explains the passage concerning Sennacherib. For he explained the whole chapter up to the last two verses in a far different way: Nay, he refutes the Jews who explain it concerning Sennacherib. Therefore, Grotius did not examine Jerome; seduced, as it appears, by Tirinus the Jesuit, who says that Jerome understands these things according to the letter concerning Sennacherib, but allegorically concerning the Devil and his tyrant members, and he attributes that opinion also to Cyril, Procopius, and Theodoret, but that is the custom of the Jesuits: To introduce diverse opinions not only into the texts of Scripture, but also into the commentaries of the Fathers, and to excuse those senses which they affix to the Scriptures by allegorical, anagogical, or tropological means, or to expose those things which the Fathers understand according to the literal sense by this scheme, so that they may have them favoring themselves, even if they make a different literal sense than they do, namely, that the Fathers [spoke] only in an allegorical, or anagogical sense, etc. have explained it thus. Let us hear Jerome himself: The Hebrews, he says, think the previous chapter, in which it is read, Woe to you that plunder, shall not you yourself also be plundered: and the rest up to the end, was spoken against Sennacherib, King of the Assyrians, who, after he had overthrown the cities of the ten tribes which were called Israel, and, except for Jerusalem, had taken the cities of Judah also, was himself overcome: and by the striking of an Angel, his army was destroyed. Whence now, in the person of the people giving thanks to God, and saying: O Lord, have mercy on us, we have waited for thee: they contend that these things which are contained in the present chapter were spoken, because He himself was the arm, and the strength of the people, surrounded by a siege in the morning time, and salvation in time of need and distress. These things they said according to the history, striving with every reason to subvert the Sacraments of Christ and of his Apostles. But we, after the blessedness of the Apostles, of whom it was said above: Blessed are they that sow upon all waters, where the ox and the ass tread, and the lamentation and wailing of those who persecuted them, of whom it is said in the following, Woe to you that make yourselves miserable, but no one makes you miserable, and as a moth in a garment, so shall they be worn away: we prove these words to be from the person of the same Apostles, and of all believers: And the sense is: O Lord, we have hoped in thy help, and in thee we trust; the seed of the unbelievers has perished forever, and our salvation has appeared in the time of tribulation. Thus far Jerome. Furthermore, we easily admit that this prophecy concerning Sennacherib, according to the proper and literal sense must be accepted, nor should this other mystical sense be invented along with the Papists. There are clear indications in the text that these things were said against Sennacherib: which is also the opinion of the blessed Luther, Brentius, Osiander, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and most interpreters. Meanwhile, we think with Brentius that some things are interspersed concerning Christ and his kingdom, which the pious ancients rightly expounded, with whom it is better to side here than with the Jews and Grotius, who in every way subvert the sacraments of Christ and his apostles. But although these things are predicted specifically concerning Sennacherib, that the devastator of so many kingdoms will soon perish, the words are nevertheless formed in such a way that the judgment seems to be pronounced against all violent predators.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIII.

Assyrio vastatori vastatio denunciatur, pro- missa fidelibus & Hierosolyma liberatione.

Vers. 1. VÆ QVI PRÆDARIS, NONNE ET IPSE PRÆDABERIS) Prædaberis hic passive posuit Interpres. Sensus est: ô tu prædator Sennacheribe, (de quo hunc lo- cum etiam Hieronymus recte exponit) nonne æquum est, te quoque prædam fieri? Vid. Apoc. 13, 20.

FAllitur Grotius, cum ait, Hieronymum de Sennacheribo locum exponere. Totum enim caput usque ad postremos duos versus longe aliter exposuit: Imo Judæos de Sennacheribo explican- tes redarguit. Non ergo inspexit Hieronymum Grotius; seductus, ut apparet, à Tirino Jesuita, qui Hieronymum secundum literam de Sennache- ribo, allegorice de Diabolo ejusque membris ty- rannis hæc intelligere ait, eamq; sententiam etiam Cyrillo, Procopio, Theodoreto tribuit, sed ea Jesui- tarum est consuetudo: Sententias diversas non textibus solum Scripturæ, sed etiam Patrum com- mentariis inferre, ac sensibus illis, quos Scripturæ affricant, allegorico, anagogico, tropologico excusa- re, vel ea, quæ Patres secundum literalem sensum in- telligunt, ut faventes sibi eos habeant, etsi alium quam ipsi literalem sensum faciant, hoc schemate exponere, quod nempe Patres solum sensu allego- rico, vel anagogico, &c. ea ita exposuerint. Audia- mus ipsum Hieronymum: Hebræi, inquit, capitu- lum superius,in quo legitur, Væ qui prædaris, nonne & ipse prædaberis: & reliqua usq; ad finem, contra Sennacherib Regem Assyriorum dictum putant, quod postquam decem tribuum, quæ appellabantur Israël, subverterit civitates, & excepta Hierusalem, Judæ quoq; urbes ceperit, ipse superetur: & percu- tiente Angelo, ejus deleatur exercitus. Unde nunc ex persona populi gratias referentis Deo, atq; dicen- tis: Domine miserere nostri, te expectavimus: hæc dicta contendunt, quæ præsenti capitulo conti- nentur, quod ipse brachium fuerit, & robur populi, obsidione vallati in tempore matutino, & salus in ne- cessitate & angustia. Hæc illi juxta historiam dixe- runt omni ratione nitentes, Christi, & Apostolorum ejus subvertere Sacramenta. Nos autem post beati- tudinem Apostolorum, de quibus supra dictum est: Beati qui seminant super omnem aquam, ubi bos & asinus calcant, & lamentationem & planctum eorum, qui eos persequuti sunt, de quibus in conse- quentibus dicitur, Væ qui miseros vos faciunt, vos autem nemo facit miseros, & sicut tinea in vesti- mento, sic atterentur: ex persona eorundem Apo- stolorum, omniumq; credentium hæc dicta convinci- mus: Et est sensus: Domine in tuo speravimus au- xilio, & in te confidimus; semen incredulorum periit in æternum, & salus nostra in tempore tribu- lationis apparuit. Hactenus Hieronymus. Cæte- rum facile admittimus hoc vaticinium de Senna- cheribo secundum sensum proprium & literalem ac- cipiendum esse, neque fingendus hic alius mysti- cus sensus cum Pontificiis. Luculenta sunt indicia in textu, hæc adversus Sennacheribum dicta esse: quæ etiam B. Lutheri, Brentii, Osiandri, Vinarien- sium Paraphrast. & plerorumq; Interpretum est sen- tentia. Interea inspersa esse nonnulla de Christo, ejusq; regno omnino cum Brentio existimamus, quæ recte exposuêre pii Veteres, cum quibus hic facere præstat, quam cum Judæis & Grotio omni ratione Christi & Apostolorum ejus subvertere Sacramenta. Etsi autem hæc peculiariter de Sen- nacheribo prædicuntur, futurum ut brevi tot re- gnorum vastator pereat, verba tamen ita forman- tur, ut adversus omnes violentos prædatores sen- tentia lata videatur.

## 33:3
Verse 3. AT THE VOICE OF THE ANGEL THE PEOPLES FLED) In the Hebrew it is: at the terrible sound, the Greeks [say] διὰ φωνὴν τῶ φοβῦ. He understands the noise of the approaching Angel, so that the Latin here has expressed the matter more than the words, from 2 Kings 19:35.

If the Latin here has regarded the matter more than the words, why should it not be judged so in other places as well? Why, from a version alien to the words of the authentic text, is a different reading of the Hebrew text, which the interpreter may have had at hand, immediately presumed—which we have observed very often in Grotius.

Latin:

Vers. 3. A VOCE ANGELI FUGERUNT POPULI) In Hebræo est: à sono terribili, Græci διὰ φωνὴν τῶ φοβῦ. Strepitum Angeli adventantis intelligit, ita ut Latinus rem hic magis expresserit ex 2. Reg. 19, 35. quam verba.

Si hic Latinus rem magis quam verba respexit, cur non in aliis etiam ita censendum, cur è versione à verbis textus authentici aliena statim diversa le- ctio textus Ebræi, quem præ manibus habuerit In- terpres, præsumitur, quod sæpe sæpius in Grotio observavimus.

## 33:4
Verse 4. AND YOUR SPOILS SHALL BE GATHERED AS THE BRUCHUS IS GATHERED) Rather, as the bruchus is gathered: spoils will be gathered from you (the Assyrians) as with impunity as the bruchus devours herbs. The things that follow from the Hebrew demand this interpretation.

AS WHEN THE DITCHES WERE FULL OF IT) That גבים are locusts, or πρασοκυρίδας, appears in Amos 7:1. It must therefore be translated: as the running of locusts when they run.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET CONGREGABUNTUR SPOLIA VESTRA SI- CUT COLLIGITUR BRUCHUS) Imo sicut colligit bruchus : tam impune legentur de vobis (Assyriis) spolia, quam bru- chus herbas depascitur. Hanc interpretationem flagitant: quæ ex Hebræo sequuntur.

VELUT CUM FOSSÆ PLENÆ FUERUNT DE EO) גבים esse locustas, sive πρασοκυρίδας, apparet A- mosi 7, 1. vertendum ergo: ut discursus locustarum ubi discurrunt.

## 33:5
THE LORD IS MAGNIFIED) He shall be magnified.

FOR HE DWELT ON HIGH) He has brought forth sublime deeds, below 10.

Verse 5. AND THERE SHALL BE FAITH IN THY TIMES) There shall be firmness in thy times, O Hezekiah.

Indeed, some interpreters explain this promise concerning the times of Hezekiah, such as Menochius and most of the Reformed, as well as Osiander with the blessed Luther; others take it concerning Zion as a type, and at the same time concerning the Church of Christ as the antitype, such as Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, as well as the Weimar Paraphrasts, Oecolampadius, and Musculus. But our Brentius observes that the happiness of Hezekiah's times was less than what would correspond to such a magnificent prediction as exists in this place, and therefore he understands it concerning the kingdom of Christ, and concerning the salvation which came to the true Church, Zion, through Christ. By these words, 'In thy times,' the Prophet does not look to Hezekiah, of whom he had made no mention before, but looks to Christ, in whose times these things which are recited here were fulfilled, and are always being fulfilled in the Church, or in the kingdom of Christ. But concerning him whom the Prophet addresses here in the second person, he had spoken a little before in the third person: The Lord shall be exalted, because he dwells on high, he will fill Zion with judgment and justice. He therefore calls Christ the Lord Jehovah, i.e., the true God. This, therefore, is the opinion of the Prophet: Sennacherib is heaping blasphemy upon the God of Zion, that He is too weak to be able to help and defend His people! But you, citizens, trust well, do not be terrified by these blasphemies, and do not desert the Lord. For that Lord, who now seems to the enemies to be very weak, shall thus be exalted in His own times, when He has put on man, so that His majesty may be made known to the whole world, and He may bestow all kinds of benefits upon Zion. Brentius pursues these benefits thus: First, He fills Zion or the Church with judgment and justice: i.e., He conquers and condemns Satan, and obtains from the Father that as many as believe in Him, the Son of God, may be reckoned righteous. Then, in the kingdoms of the world there is no truth, or certainty and firmness. Covenants and promises are not kept. Nothing is firm and stable. In the kingdom of Christ, however, there is the highest truth, because He keeps all His promises and fulfills them. Even if men are weak, and in a way unbelieving, yet He remains faithful, He cannot deny Himself. The kingdom of Christ is also firm and perpetual. While all other kingdoms perish, this one alone stands forever, just as Daniel also preaches. Furthermore, in the kingdom of Christ there is the wealth of salvation, that is, the greatest and most powerful salvation. In the kingdoms of this world you will find hardly any bodily salvation. But in the kingdom of Christ there is perpetual salvation, preserving man even in death. Then, in the kingdom of Christ there is wisdom, and there is knowledge, because Christ is there and is known through His Gospel, who is the treasure of all wisdom and knowledge. So also Jerome: This is Zion, which was previously called a desert: and whoever shall dwell in it, the law of the Gospel shall be delivered to him, in whose treasure is our salvation, and the wisdom of believers, and discipline, and piety or faith, which is properly that of Christians, and the fear of the Lord, in which the treasures of wisdom are contained. Similarly Cyril; the earthly Jerusalem is deprived of this most illustrious glory. For it by no means admitted the justice of God and the Father, that is, of Christ, but the Church of the Gentiles is the intelligible and truer Zion, which has been made [full] with judgment and justice. If, however, anyone with the blessed Luther and Osiander prefers to refer these things to the times of Hezekiah, so that the continuity with the preceding and following things may be more evident, we shall not object. The sense therefore will be: The Lord will protect the city, which He has filled with justice and judgment: in which faith flourishes under a pious king; in which are stored the saving riches of wisdom and spiritual knowledge and the fear of the Lord, which is the most excellent treasure of the same. Therefore the Lord will show His majesty and power in defending the city and destroying its enemies, because He dwells on high; His majesty and power are most eminent and supreme, against which no forces can do anything.

Latin:

MAGNIFICATUS EST DOMINUS) Magnificabitur.

QUONIAM HABITAVIT IN EXCELSO) Edidit facta su- blimia, infra 10.

Vers. 5. ET ERIT FIDES IN TEMPORIBUS TUIS) E- rit firmitas temporibus tuis, ô Ezechia.

Explicant sane nonnulli Interpretes hanc pro- missionem de Ezechiæ temporibus, ut Menochius & Reformati pleriq;, nec non Osiander cum B. Lu- thero; alii de Sione ut typo accipiunt, ac simul de Ec- clesia Christi, ut antitypo, ut Corn. à Lapide, Tirinus, ut & Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, Oecolampadius item ac Musculus. Sed Brentius noster observat felici- tatem temporum Ezechiæ minorem fuisse, quam quæ tam magnificæ prædicationi, quæ hoc in loco extat, respondeat, ideoque intelligit ea de regno Christi, & de salute, quæ Ecclesiæ veræ Sioni per Christum contigit. His verbis, Temporibus tuis, Propheta non respicit in Ezechiam, cujus nullam an- tea mentionem fecerat, sed respicit in Christum, cujus temporibus hæc, quæ recitantur, hic impleta sunt, & implentur semper in Ecclesia, seu in regno Christi. Quem autem Propheta hic in secunda per- sona alloquitur, de eo paulo ante in tertia persona dixerat: Exaltabitur Dominus, quia habitat in excel- so, implebit Zion judicio & justitia. Vocat igitur Christum Dominum Jehovah, h. e. verum Deum. Hæc est ergo sententia Prophetæ : Sanherib blasphe- mia afficit Deum Zionis, quod imbecillior sit, quam qui possit populum suum juvare & defendere! Sed vos cives bene confidite, nolite his blasphemiis terre- ri, & Dominum deserere. Is enim Dominus, qui nunc videtur hostibus admodum imbecillis, sic temporibus suis, cum hominem induerit, exaltabi- tur, ut majestas ejus toti orbi nota fiat, & conferat omnia genera beneficiorum in Zionem. Quæ be- neficia ita persequitur Brentius: Primum implet Zionem seu Ecclesiam judicio & justitia: h. e. vincit & damnat Satanam, ac impetrat à Patre, ut quot- quot in ipsum filium Dei credant, reputentur justi. Deinde in regnis mundi nulla est veritas, seu certitu- do & firmitas. Non servantur pacta & promissio- nes. Nihil est firmum ac stabile. In regno autem Christi summa est veritas, quia servat omnes suas promissiones & implet eas. Etiamsi homines infir- mi sunt, & quodammodo increduli, tamen ipse ma- net fidelis, seipsum negare non potest. Est & re- gnum Christi firmum ac perpetuum. Cum omnia alia regna intereant, hoc solum stat in æternum, si- cut & Daniel concionatur. Præterea in regno Christi est opulentia salutis, hoc est, maxima & po- tentissima salus. In regnis huj9 mundi invenias vix aliquam corporalem salutem. At in regno Christi est perpetua salus, conservans hominem etiam in morte. Deinde in regno Christi est sapientia, est & scientia, quia ibi est & cognoscitur Christus per Evangelion suum, qui est thesaurus omnis sapien- tiæ & scientiæ. Sic etiam Hieronymus: Ipsa est Sion, quæ prius est appellata desertum: & quicunq; habitaverit in ea, tradetur ei lex Evangelii, in cujus thesauro salus nostra est, & sapientia credentium, & disciplina, & pietas sive fides, quæ proprie Christiano- rum est, & timor Domini, in quo thesauri sapientiæ continentur. Similiter Cyrillus; terrena Hierusa- lem hac tam illustri gloria destituitur. Nequaquam enim admisit justitiam Dei & Patris, id est, Christi, Ecclesia autem gentium intelligibilis & verior Sion est, quæ facta est judicio & justitia. Si quis tamen cum B. Luthero & Osiandro malit hæc ad Ezechiæ tempora referre, ut evidentior sit συνέχεια cum antecedentibus & consequentib9, non repugnabi- mus. Sensus ergo erit: Dominus proteget urbem, quam implevit justitia & judicio: in qua viget sub rege pio fides; in qua opes salutiferæ reconditæ sapien- tiæ & scientiæ spiritualis ac timoris Domini, qui ejus- dem thesaurus est præstantissimus. Ideo majestatem & potentiam suam ostendet Dominus in defendenda urbe, & perdendis hostibus ejus, quia in excelso habi- tat, eminentissima, & summa est ejus majestas & po- tentia, adversus quam nullæ vires quicquam possunt.

## 33:7
Vers. 7. BEHOLD THE SEERS SHALL CRY WITHOUT) In the Hebrew: Behold their altar shall cry without. אראל is the same as what is written in Ezekiel הראל, in Syriac איל with א substituted for אל: but above in this Prophet with an epenthetic 29 אריאל. v. 1. the Assyrians shall cry from the camps, behold their altar, in mockery, that is, those daily sacrifices will profit them nothing.

Aben Ezra and Forerius likewise think that word is put for אריאל. But they take it for the citizens of Jerusalem. Ariel is taken for the city itself in Is. 29. Other interpreters, however, Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion, took it for אראה להם I will appear to them. The Vulgate seems to follow them, as if to say: Behold, to whom I shall appear, that is, the seers. Some Hebrews and Arias Montanus take it for the name of an Angel. But others interpret it more correctly as their strong ones: and they understand it of messengers, powerful in authority, dignity, and strength, whom they call Ambassadors, as the Belgian Bibles have it; thus Luther, Osiander, and others rendered it, Messengers. Avenarius in his Lexicon: Behold אראלם their strong ones cried without. For אריאל is Lion of God, or strong Lion. And 2 Sam. 23:20, 2 Chron. 11:23. He himself struck two אריאל, that is, strong men of Moab. The authors of the Belgian notes understand the legates of Sennacherib, sent to Hezekiah and the people, 2 Kings 18:17, 18. others understand the legates of Hezekiah to Sennacherib: who are then called angels of peace, because they had to treat for peace. But since they brought back nothing but the gravest threats from the king of the Assyrians, seeing everything laid waste around them and imminent destruction for the city itself, they wept bitterly with torn garments, 2 Kings 18 [19]:2, Isaiah 36.

ANGELS OF PEACE WEPT BITTERLY) Understand the legates sent into the camp for peace, Eliakim, Shebna, Joah, who returning from there reported no hope of peace, but that everything was laid waste around them, 2 Kings 18 and following, where the same legates are said to have returned with torn garments, as in the bitterest mourning.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ECCE VIDENTES CLAMABUNT FORES) In Hebræo: Ecce altare ipsorum clamabunt foris. אראל idem quod apud Ezechielem scribitur הראל, Syriace איל po- sito pro אל: supra vero apud hunc Prophetam cum ἐπενθετικῷ 29 אריאל. v.1. clamabunt è castris Assyrii, ecce altare ipsorum, per irrisum, id est, nihil illis proderunt quo- tidianæ illæ victimæ.

Aben Ezra & Forerius pariter vocem illam po- sitam putant pro אריאל. Sed accipiunt pro civibus Hierosolymitanis. Ariel pro urbe ipsa sumitur Es.29. Alii tamen Intepp. Aquila, Symmach. & Theodot. acceperunt pro אראה להם apparebo eis. Quos vi- detur sequi Vulgatus, q.d. Ecce, quibus apparebo, h. e. videntes. Ebræi nonnulli, & Arias Montan. habent pro nomine Angeli. Sed rectius interpretantur alii, fortes eorum: ac de nunciis, potentibus autoritate, di- gnitate ac viribus intelligunt, quos Ambassadeur vocant, ut habent Biblia Belgica; Sic reddidere Lu- therus, Osiander, & alii, Nuncii. Avenarius in Lexic. Ecce אראלם fortes eorum clamarunt foris. Nam אריאל est Leo Dei, vel Leo fortis. Et 2. Sam. 23, 20. 2. Par. 11, 23. Ipse percussit duos אריאל, id est, fortes ex Moab. Legatos Sennacheribi autores notarum Bel- gicarum, ad Hiskiam & populum missos 2. Reg. 18, 17.18. alii legatos Hiskiæ ad Sennacheribum intelli- gunt: qui deinde Angeli pacis dicuntur, quod de pace tractare debuerint. Quin quum nihil nisi gra- vissimas comminationes à rege Assyriorum repor- tarint, omnia circumvastata, ipsiq; urbi imminens excidium videntes conscissis vestibus amare fleve- runt, 2. Reg. 12. Esa. 36.

ANGELI PACIS AMARE FLEBANT) Legatos intellige de pace in castra missos Eliacimum, Sobnam, Joahen, qui inde redeuntes nullam spem pacis, omnia autem circum- vastata retulerunt, 2. Reg. 18. & seqq. ubi dicuntur iidem legati rediisse scissis vestibus, ut in acerbissimo luctu.

## 33:8
Vers. 8. THE WAYS ARE WASTED) This is the report of the ambassadors. All exits are closed to us. For מסלול is translated ἄβατος, Jer. 49, 27. and שמם or שממה ἄβατος, in the same Jeremiah very often. See a similar passage Jud. 5, 6. THE COVENANT IS MADE VOID) The Assyrians do not wish to stand by the peace which they had last made with Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18, 14. THE CITIES ARE CAST OFF) He has scattered the towns of Judea. HE HAS NOT REGARDED MEN) That is, he has held all our men for nothing. See the words of Rabshakeh. Others take these things concerning the covenant of God with the Jewish people, as if to say: that God no longer has regard for that covenant: that he has cast off the cities, does not regard the miserable men, nor is he moved by the calamity of his people; the response of the Lord seems to agree more with these. Now I will arise, says the Lord, now I will be exalted, now I will be lifted up. Even if until now I may seem to have made the covenant void, and to have altogether cast off Judah, I will not, however, any longer desert my people: now I will arise, and gird myself to liberate the same. Vers. 9. THE EARTH MOURNED AND LANGUISHED) That is, Judea was in mourning and languor. LEBANON IS CONFOUNDED) That proud mountain Lebanon was suffused with shame. AND SHARON IS BECOME AS A DESERT) The fields near Bashan were desolate. See 1 Chron. 5, 16. BASHAN IS SHAKEN) Shaken off. AND CARMEL) This is a proper name. For the places through which Sennacherib had passed are mentioned. Tacitus Hist. 2. Carmel is between Judea and Syria. See also Pliny 5, 19. Some wish for the whole land of Judea to be designated here, which is bounded by these as its borders, because Lebanon looked to the North, Sharon to the West, Bashan to the East, and Carmel to the South. Vers. 10. NOW I WILL ARISE, SAYS THE LORD) As if he were saying: now at last, with all things despaired of, it is time that I move myself. Vers. 11. YOU SHALL CONCEIVE HEAT) More correctly: Trash. YOU SHALL BRING FORTH STUBBLE) That is, foolish counsels will have empty outcomes. God addresses the Assyrians here. YOUR SPIRIT AS FIRE SHALL DEVOUR YOU) Your anger will be your destruction. Vers. 12. AND THE PEOPLES SHALL BE AS THE ASHES OF A BURNING) In the Hebrew: and the peoples shall be the burnings of lime. That is, they shall be as if placed in a lime kiln. THORNS GATHERED SHALL BE BURNED WITH FIRE) In the Hebrew: Thorns cut down: as if to be understood. They shall be burned as thorns. We have often noted already that that sudden evil, which God sent upon the Assyrians, whatever it may have been, is compared to a fire. Vers. 14 FEAR HAS POSSESSED THE HYPOCRITES) He speaks of those who, having changed their religion, wished to seek safety from the Assyrian. WITH EVERLASTING BURNINGS) That is, with fire that is not extinguished. Such they thought the Assyrian power to be. The discourse is about the hypocrites among the people: not indeed about the apostates. The former simulate true religion and piety: the latter, however, fall away from true religion. The hypocrites are therefore joined with other sinners in Zion who have not yet repented: both are terrified, as hypocrites are wont to be, and other unrepentant sinners, being most timid in dangers, because they lack trust in God. This kind of man is most secure in prosperous circumstances, but again is most desperate in harsh circumstances, says Blessed Luther. WHO, they say, SHALL BE ABLE TO DWELL AMONG US WITH DEVOURING FIRE? WHO SHALL DWELL AMONG US WITH EVERLASTING BURNINGS (fires)? Most take these things concerning the Assyrian. They could, however, be explained concerning God himself, who is a consuming fire, Deut. 4, 24. Heb. 12, 25, whose anger the impious dread most in public calamities. A similar passage is Nah. 1, 6. Conf. 2 Chron. 34, 21. 26. Jerem. 44, 6. And thus the response fits best: as it explains who those are that shall dwell with God. The authors of the Belgian notes also favor this sense of ours, and indeed even Jerome: Who shall be able to dwell with God?

Latin:

Vers. 8. DISSIPATÆ SUNT VIÆ) Hæc est relatio legato- rum. Præclusi nobis sunt exitus omnes. Nam מסלול vertitur ἄβατος, Jer. 49, 27. & שמם vel שממה ἄβα- τος, apud eundem Jeremiam sæpissime. Simile vide Jud. 5, 6. IRRITUM FACTUM EST PACTUM) Assyrii stare nolunt pa- ci, quam postremam cum Ezechia fecerant, 2.Reg. 18, 14. PROJECTT CIVITATES) Disjecit oppida Judææ. NON REPUTAVIT HOMINES) Id est, omnes homines no- stros pro nihilo duxit. Vide verba Rabsacis. Alii hæc de pacto Dei cum populo Judaico accipiunt, q. d.
