Nor does the emphasis of this description, which is had here, fit any better than to heathendom, before it was converted to the Church, inasmuch as this was a waterless desert and a dry solitude, in which there were no waters of refreshment of the divine word, and in that horrid desert only dragons and serpents dwelt, both because it was a habitation of demons, and because the impious are also compared to dragons and serpents, as a brood of vipers. The Scripture delivered by the divine spirit, says Cyril, is wont to call the Church of the Gentiles desert and sterile, which was once in them, not having the intelligible Spouse from heaven, I mean Christ, but laboring under a lack of all goods and as it were a nurse of thorns, thirsty, and lacking waters. But when Christ was in it (for he was assumed through faith, and it was enriched by his divine rivulet, for he is the fountain of life and the torrent of delights, and he himself said among one of the holy Prophets: Behold I incline toward them, like a river of peace, and like a torrent inundating the glory of the Gentiles), it was no longer sterile, nor a desert, but rather fruitful, and under a spouse, and flourishing intelligibly. Let that which was once thirsty, therefore, rejoice, he says, and flourish like a lily, both flourishing and fragrant. For it was the odor of Christ.

Thirdly, the glory of Lebanon, the beauty of Carmel and Sharon, are to be understood not of worldly height and temporal fertility, but of the spiritual glory and beauty and fertility proper to Judea, in which was the Church of God, in the manner of Scripture, which is wont to designate heavenly and spiritual things with phrases taken from worldly and earthly things: And therefore it is implied that the spiritual glory and fertility, hitherto proper to Judea, was one day to be granted to heathendom: as Isaiah indicated in chapter 54, 1: Rejoice, O barren one, who dost not bear: for many are the children of the desolate. Thus Jerome: That which had once been a desert, of which it is said in the Psalm: The voice of the Lord shaking the solitude, and the Lord will move the desert of Kadesh: The voice of the Lord preparing the harts, and he will reveal the thickets of the woods, will be changed into an abundance of all things: and with the harts fighting, the beasts which had previously possessed them will be expelled from all the forests of the nations: that that may be fulfilled which is said in this same Prophet: Rejoice, O barren one, who dost not bear: break forth and cry, thou who dost not travail, for more are the children of the desolate than of her who has a husband: This was previously thirsty, or impassable, not having vital waters, and the Lord did not walk through it, which will now flourish like a lily: Or as Aquila expressed it more significantly: ὡς κάλυξ, which we can call a swelling rose, not yet dilated with leaves. But it will flourish, so that with the Apostle it may pronounce: We are the good odor of Christ in every place. And that of the Song of Songs: The flowers have appeared in the land, the mandrakes have given their odor. And that which is placed in the Septuagint καὶ ἀγαλλιάσεται τὰ ἔρημα τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, i.e., and the deserts of the Jordan will exult: it is not indeed had in the Hebrew, but we can say that the Baptism of Repentance of John in the river Jordan is demonstrated, which the Lord signed and confirmed with his own washing. And because of the solitude figuratively, which refers to the nations, in which John was, the Jordan can consequently be joined, so that through the desert of the nations we may come to the baptism of the Savior. Cyril of Alexandria agrees: Lebanon and Carmel are often called Jerusalem, and the very temple of God. But the glory worthy of the holy city and the divine temple was given to the Church of the Gentiles: And in it we have seen the glory of the Lord, and the height of God. For the Jews were brought to the Lord as to a naked man, and one having nothing extraordinary above others: But we have seen the height of his glory. For we know him to be God, made man for us by dispensation and providence, and thus God. And for that reason also our Blessed Luther interpreted these things concerning the conversion of the Gentiles. There follows, he says, now the prophecy concerning the Church itself, which was born from the remnants of the devastated Synagogue: THE GLORY OF LEBANON HAS BEEN GIVEN TO IT. All the gifts which the Synagogue had have been transferred into the Church gathered from the remnants of the Jews and the nations. For the glory is the kingdom and the Priesthood, and whatever was given to the Synagogue divinely, all these things have befallen us. Although indeed the Gentiles occupied Mount Lebanon, it is certain that it pertained to the Hebrews, and that by Lebanon the land of Judea is designated metonymically. See Josh. 13, 6. Ps. 29, 5. Ez. 17, 3. Hab. 2, 17. Nah. 1, 4. Some understand the temple by Lebanon, and the Jewish people by Carmel and Sharon. Thus Pintus says that by Lebanon is understood the temple of Solomon, just as in Zechariah chapter 11 and in Ezekiel chapter 17, as the Prophet expresses there immediately. By Carmel and Sharon is understood the people of the Jews, as we explained in chapter 33. Isaiah therefore wished to signify that all brightness, and the worship of God, and the knowledge and understanding of the Scriptures, and the fertility and abundance of spiritual fruits, and all glory and beauty, and finally all mighty works were to be taken away from the Synagogue and given to the Church. Christ signified this to the Jews, saying: The kingdom shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

Fourthly, such great loftiness, glory, and fertility do not suit the land of Judea, as is described here, in the time of Hezekiah: Nor is it probable that the Prophet described it here with such an apparatus of words, and, neglecting spiritual happiness, treated so laboriously only of temporal goods: The desert and the pathless place shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice, and shall flourish like the lily: It shall bud forth and blossom, and shall rejoice with joy and praise: the glory of Lebanon is given to it; the beauty

Carmel and Sharon: they shall see the glory of the Lord, and the beauty of our God. Nor indeed was such the solitude in Judea in the time of Hezekiah, that it should have been marked by these names: since that desert is described as utterly impassable, arid, and thirsty, in which dragons dwell, and lions and evil beasts, v. 7 and 9. But if you take these things regarding spiritual joy, flower, and beauty, it is no wonder that such profuse joy is celebrated by the Prophet; to whom nothing more joyful could happen than the glory and propagation of the spiritual kingdom of Christ, or that so horrible a solitude is designated, when it concerns the vast ignorance of the Gentiles in sacred matters, and the horrendous blindness and ἀταξία, which, deserted by salvation, by religion, by the worship of God, and by God himself, bristled with vices and sins, and could bring forth no fruits of justice; but having turned to God like a lily, by the singular virtue of a holy life and the fertility of good works, and every glory of Lebanon or of the Jewish Church it ought to flourish, and it ought to spread a pleasing odor of itself, (as in Lebanon the cedars and frankincense Isa. 10:34, c. 16:10,) it ought to flourish with all the beauty of Carmel and Sharon (whence the crops, grapes, olives, and other fruits which Judea enjoyed, Carmel especially abounded in copious grains, Sharon in joyful pastures). And in this the glory of God was seen above all, and the beauty of our God was manifested through the world, as Isaiah predicts here: The gloss of Grotius on these words: They shall see the glory of God: that is, they shall experience his powerful protection in reality, does not satisfy, because the following things teach what kind of manifestation of glory it is, namely that of which John 1:14, c. 17:5, Isa. 40:5, c. 60:1 speak, which appeared through the Messiah.

Fifth, nothing is more evident than the Evangelical sermon which is held here: which certainly does not look to temporal goods, but spiritual: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say to the faint-hearted: Be strong, and do not fear. Behold your God will bring the vengeance of retribution. God himself will come, and will save you. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped, etc. That these times look to the New Testament and the advent of the Lord our God, when he was manifested in the flesh and came into the world to save us, is manifest from the miracles which are predicted here, and the fulfillment which was performed through Christ: nor did Christ obscurely, informing the disciples of John, say: the blind see, the lame walk, the deaf hear, the poor have the Gospel preached to them, Matt. 11:5, he referred to this place of Isaiah, in which both the Gospel, by which the poor and faint-hearted are to be raised up, concerning the advent of God and the salvation which he provides, and the miracles which were to be performed under the advent of the Lord, are exhibited. The Grotian glosses are too diluted, by which the illustrious Evangelical sermon is plainly perverted: STRENGTHEN THE WEAK HANDS. You, all the prophets and other good men, add courage to the Jews, lest they tremble at the memory of the endured siege: GOD HIMSELF WILL COME, AND WILL SAVE YOU: He will bring it about that the Ethiopian does not reach you. Nor is there any indication that the discourse here is about the Ethiopian, nor do those miracles concerning the blind, the mute, the deaf, and the lame fit the time of Hezekiah. And therefore Grotius had to distort the words of the Prophet to alien and utterly incongruous senses, so that he might sail with his preconceived opinion. The Prophet speaks too openly about the advent of Christ the Lord, who is our God and our Savior, who made the vengeance of retribution, when he avenged the ruin of the human race in Satan, but saves us, because he acquires eternal salvation and wishes to give it to us: Cf. Ps. 72:4, or he comes for salvation to those who received him, but for vengeance to those who wished to remain in their infidelity, as

Hector Pintus explains. Nor should it be neglected that in the Hebrew the word יושעכם will save you, contains the name of Jesus, it will be your Jesus, which if it is read with other points ישעשע it signifies he will delight you: Because Jesus is joy and the delight of our heart. Sixth, what is predicted here about waters and fountains in the desert and solitude v. 6, 7, are not explained more correctly than in a spiritual sense, concerning the waters springing up into eternal life, John 4. and 7, as Cyril and Jerome explain, whose words I submit: The waters of saving baptism were cleft or burst forth in the desert of the former Church, and torrents and rivers in the solitude, namely diverse spiritual graces, and what was arid was turned into a pool and marshes, so that it not only lacked the heat of thirst, but was navigable and well-watered, and had many fountains, which the deer desires, which whoever drinks, can bless the Lord, according to that which is written, Bless the Lord from the fountains of Israel. We add the Commentary of Brentius. Another benefit is added: Waters shall be cut out in the desert and torrents in the arid land. And the parched land shall be reduced to a pool, and the thirsty land, or that burned by the heat of the Sun, into a spring of waters, so that where dragons or serpents, lovers of the most arid places, previously dwelt, there henceforth green grass of reeds and rushes shall grow. Christ did not indeed fulfill these things corporally in his advent: Nor did it happen that his disciples and listeners lacked water in the deserts, otherwise even the rocks would have poured out waters for them, lest they perish of thirst, just as the rock gave the Israelites water in the desert, and Christ fed many thousands of men in the desert with very few loaves and fishes. But by this metaphor of words Isaiah signifies that Christ in his advent would opulently pour out the Holy Spirit into his Church. Thus also Christ himself interprets, when he says John 7: If any man thirst, let him come to me, and drink. He that believeth in me, as the Scripture saith, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. And the Evangelist adds: This he said of the Spirit, which they that believe in him should receive. You see therefore that the admirable gifts of the Holy Spirit, which Christ conferred upon his disciples, are called torrents and springs of fountains in the desert. Not otherwise does B. Luther, explaining the propagation of the word: The deserts which before lay without any cultivation, those will stand most pleasantly, because rivers will be distributed into them. That is, the arid hearts of the Gentiles will be watered by the word of the Gospel, and will conceive life. Thus here at Wittenberg we have a stream, by which even neighboring places are watered. For the word is heavenly wisdom, from which arises a stream leaping into eternal life, John 4. Therefore the Prophet signifies by this allegory that the word will be preached copiously, and will presently be spread more widely, and from the Church of one place, many others will draw the word. Seventh, the path and way, which is to be called holy, through which no polluted person enters, and in which no fool wanders, v. 8, cannot be taken concerning a bodily way. Therefore, the interpreters explain it spiritually. Most understand it of Christ, who is the way, the truth, and the life, John 14:6, a holy and safe way, through which no profane or polluted person passes. Through this way: because as many as receive Christ through faith, receive also the remission of sins, are cleansed from their sins, are accounted righteous and holy before God. Furthermore, this way is so plain that not even fools can wander in it. For he who believes in Christ, even if someone should be simple, endowed with no carnal prudence, nevertheless walks straight to true righteousness and eternal salvation: for Christ is that way, by which alone one arrives at salvation. Thus our B. Luther, AND THERE SHALL BE A PATH, i.e., There shall also be other paths, which by the name of holiness will be celebrated. But this alone will be the holy path, in which the holy Patriarchs also walked. That way is faith in Jesus Christ, in the seed of Adam and Abraham promised. But all these things are said by the Prophet for this reason, that we may learn that faith follows the word, and that those who believe cannot err. For to the pure all things are pure, then faith naturally produces good works. But the impious can neither believe nor do good works; they produce only images of good works. Therefore he says, the polluted shall not pass through it. For in all other ways are the impious. Thus the cowl covers the impious Monk, etc. But faith in Christ alone is the way, which no impious person apprehends, because the members of Christ cannot be polluted, for they have a sanctifying head. It will be such a plain way, in which not even fools may err; he calls those fools, however, who with a simple heart adhere to the word. For the world calls these people fools, and judges them. To this explanation can be joined the ἔκθεσις of Cyril: because those senses are subordinate: He calls a pure life the virtue of Evangelical conversation, or otherwise, purification through the Spirit. For it wipes away the stain impressed upon the souls of men, and absolves them from offenses, and causes them not to be defiled by any filth. The way, therefore, is holy and pure, and indeed rightly called so, but inaccessible to those who have not yet been cleansed. For no one lives in an Evangelical manner who has not first been enriched by purification through holy Baptism: Nor therefore any of the infidels: for those who are impure, they will go, he says, in it. But they will walk dispersed, that is, those whom Satan has scattered. He truly hints at the Gentiles: nor will they err. Formerly, indeed, they were wandering, serving wood and stones, and insisting on crooked paths. But now they will learn the straight and pure way, leading to a holy life.

Eighthly, the things which are predicted concerning security, there will not be a Lion there, and a bad beast will not ascend through it, nor will it be found there, the glosses of Grotius do not agree, concerning temporal security: For was there no place for bad beasts in Judea? Therefore it is manifest that the discourse is about Spiritual things. By the Lion, Jerome understands the Demon, by the bad beasts his satellites, that God is about to remove the insults and machinations of the Demon and his instruments from the Church and from any of the faithful whatsoever. A bad beast in Hebrew is a violent wild animal, as Grotius notes. But he who devised an inept gloss concerning this way. Understanding the way, which leads to the temple by a straight path, which is called direct, because it is without tortuous windings, by which the ignorant could be deceived; that the polluted shall not pass through it, that is, no Syrian, Assyrian, Egyptian, Ethiopian shall be seen there. As far as I grasp it, he wants this: That the way will be secure, which leads to the temple by a straight path, which is the shortest. But that gloss is first merely precarious: furthermore, it is far-fetched, since no mention of a temple is made in the text: nor does it agree with that prediction: because the prophecy is instituted concerning a peculiar way, and path, which Isaiah predicts will be called a holy way, or will be so in reality, he does not only call it holy because it leads to the temple, nor is the polluted person pointed out as a Syrian, or Assyrian, but whoever has not been liberated, as the antithesis teaches, and they shall walk, who have been liberated, and redeemed by the Lord. Furthermore, joy is predicted not temporal, but spiritual, and eternal, verse 10, everlasting joy upon their head. Cold is the gloss of Grotius, concerning bodily liberation, AND THEY SHALL WALK WHEN THEY HAVE BEEN LIBERATED.) That is, those whom God has snatched from so many evils. AND REDEEMED BY THE LORD.) the Jews who, having been snatched from destruction, had been in exile in many places, see above 11, 11. THEY SHALL BE CONVERTED TO THE FATHERLAND.) they shall return to the Fatherland. AND THEY SHALL COME INTO SION.) On solemn days. Thus far Grotius. But he omitted the chief thing, namely, that it is held concerning joy, just as it is described both extensively, as to eternity: Everlasting joy upon their head: Then intensively, as to the perfection of joy; they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away. Which, as they are altogether clear, so they have moved most Interpreters to accept these things concerning eternal joys, which will befall the blessed and the elect in the other life, even if they already obtain the beginnings of them in this life. Concerning those liberated from the hand of Sennacherib, and their return to the fatherland, he who might accept it will not easily be found, even if Corvinus in his Defense of the opinion of Arminius explains it concerning the liberation from the Babylonian captivity. But it is too manifest that a far different redemption is treated here, concerning which it is pleasing to hear Cyril: Neither the Lion, nor any other bad beast will be there, that is, in the pure way. For formerly, like a savage beast, the inventor of sin insulted the inhabitants of the earth with impious spirits: but through Christ he has been broken, and driven away from the flock of believers, and cast out by Christ from this tyranny against them. In this pure way, therefore, those redeemed through Christ, and gathered through faith, will come together into one consensus of souls, and the old way being omitted, they will be converted, and will come into Sion, i.e., the Church, having constant joy both on earth and in heaven. Therefore they will carry God with praises, who has saved them. And exultation, and joy, and every kind of pleasure in Christ will seize them, nor will they taste any sorrow or sighing at all. For those who have been called to so ample a hope, who are to be heirs of eternal life, and are to be enriched with the adornments of heavenly glory, who expect to reign together with Christ himself, what sorrow will they perceive, or what sighing will they receive? when the God of all is about to destroy and lay waste the bad beasts: nay, they will rather rejoice, as those who are to be partakers of all good things altogether and in all ways. Cyril is supported by Jerome in this place, Eusebius in book 6 of the Evangelical Demonstration, chapter 21, Hilary in Psalm 61, Nazianzen in Oration 1 against Julian, and from the Papists Bellarmine, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius: From our own, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and most others, who acknowledge these things as predicted concerning Christ and the times of the New Testament, and explain them concerning the redemption made through Christ: not to mention that even the Jews themselves have observed that this is treated concerning the Messiah, even if they have dreamed that temporal joys are predicted under the latest times, and in the other life.

Latin:

DEVS IPSE VENIET, ET SALVABIT VOS) Efficiet ne Æthiops ad vos perveniat.

EXplicat hæc Grotius de temporali felicitate regni Judaici : sequutus iterum Judæos, qui pariter externam & temporalem felicitatem sibi promissam hic esse somniant. In eo tantum plus viderunt cæci Judæi, quam Grotius Christianus, quod de tempore adventus Messiæ hæc accipienda esse intellexerint, quæ Grotius ad tempora Ezechiæ detorquet. De Messia enim in textu luculenta prostant documenta; de Rege vero Ezechiâ nul- lus apex, nullum vestigiû apparet, quamvis Judæi hæc referant ad reductionem suam in Palæstinam è captivitate moderna, quam per Messiam suum ex- pectant, ac mira fingant, quæ eo tempore facturus sit: quod nempe nemo tam insipiens tum futurus sit, quin recta via perrecturus sit etiam ex ultimis ter- ræ partibus ad terram promissionis, quodq́; ne in locis desertis siti pereant, Deus fontes passim excitaturus, bestias sævas abacturus, arbores frondes producturus sit, quæ viatoribus umbram & refrigerium sistent, & quæ aliæ sunt ipsorum næniæ. Docet etiam S. Hie- ronymus, quod postremâ in hoc capite ad secun- dum adventum Messiæ retulerint nonnulli, adeoq; monet in Comment. suo, ne nos more Judaico au- ream quæramus Sion, & gemmatam Hierusalem, quæ juxta Prophetiam Danielis in æternos cineres redacta est. Judæi enim, inquit, & nostri Judaizan- tes ad secundum adventum referunt, occasione unius versiculi; CONVERTENTUR ET VE- NIENT IN SION CUM LAUDE, hostium sanguinem cunctarumq; gentium servitutem deside- rantes. Inter Christianos autem hactenus dubium nullum fuit, hoc vaticinium de Domino & Salva- tore nostro Christo Jesu accipiendum esse. Solus Grotius hic aliter sapit, & cum Judæis non de spiri- tuali regni Christi flore, sed de temporali & exter- na felicitate regni Judæorum interpretatur: quam tamen ad Ezechiæ tempora refert, non vero ad ad- ventum Messiæ. Operæ autem pretium erit insigne vaticinium ab hac detorsione vindicare, ejusq; sen- sum genuinum adserere, quod nempe felicitatem regni Christi sub adventum ejus in mundum descri- bat, qua cumprimis gavisuri erant gentiles ad Evan- gelium convertendi novi Testam. tempore, non exclu- sis tamen Judæis, nisi qui semetipsos per infidelitatem excluserunt, eaq; beatitudine privarunt. Nam de Ecclesia Novi Testam. agitur, quæ maxime è gen- tilibus collecta, quorum proinde lætitia & gloria hic præcipue descripta est: non pauci tamen è Ju- dæis ad eandem pertinent, qui cum exultatione etiam in Sion venêre, ceu redempti Domini: imo ad reliquias Judæorum collecta fuit gentium Ec- clesia, unde B. Lutherus hoc vaticinium intellexit de Ecclesia, è reliquiis Synagogæ nata, & omnia quæ Synagoga habuit translocanda in Ecclesiam è reli- quiis Judæorum & gentibus congregatam hic præ- dici monuit. Argumenta hæc notari possunt: Pri- mum è συνεχεία & collatione cum præcedenti capite. Quum enim ibi de hostibus Ecclesiæ, eorumq; exi- tio, ac novissimo impiorum, totiusq; orbis excidio actum fuerit, nunc de læta propagatione, ac felici- tate cum spirituali, tum cœlesti, quæ in hoc & ven- turo seculo eidem obtinget, agitur. Ibi Idumæis stragem, & terræ eorum perpetuam vastitatem prædixerat: Hic gentium, quæ deserti & solitudi- nis instar erant, vigorem, lætitiam & salutem prædi- cat, quam per Christum consecutura erant. Ideoq; malis, quæ ibi minatus erat, hic bona, quæ expe- ctanda sint, opponit, vastitati perquam horribili lætum ac floridum vigorem, quum deserta ipsa in- star Libani, Saron, & Carmeli futura sint, ferarum & avium infaustarum multitudini absentiam mala- rum bestiarum & dæmonum, mœrori & luctui perpetuo lætitiam, & exultationem sempiternam. Non male ergo hic Calvinus: Postquam tractavit hic Propheta de horrendis cladibus, totiusq; orbis mi- seram dissipationem significarit, pios consolatur hac promissione, qua instauranda omnia esse denunciat. Hoc autem fit per Christum, quo solo renovari atq; ex- hilarari licet; quando solus omnia instaurat, atq; in verum ordinem restituit, extra ipsum vero nihil præ- ter squalorem, & solitudinem, nihil præter dissipatio- nem & in cælo & in terra miserrimam esse potest.

Alterum petimus è consueta gentilismi descri- ptione. Per desertum enim & inviam terram de- scribi solet gentilismus in S. literis, unde Ecclesia gentilium dicitur è deserto afcendere. Cantic. 8. neq; rectius aliis, hujus descriptionis, quæ hic ha- betur, emphasis congruit, quam gentilitati, prius- quam ad Ecclesiam converteretur, siquidem hæc desertum inaquosum, & solitudo sicca fuerit, in qua nullæ aquæ refectionis verbi divini, & in deserto illo horrido Dracones solum & serpentes habitarint, tum quia dæmonum habitatio fuerit, tum quia Draconibus & serpentibus impii etiam, ceu geni- mina viperarum, comparantur. Desertam, inquit Cyrillus, & sterilem appellare solet divino spiritu tra- dita Scriptura gentium Ecclesiam, quæ olim in illis erat, non habens è cælo intelligibilem Sponsum, Chri- stum, inquam, sed inopia laborans bonorum omnium & quasi nutrix spinarum, siticulosa, & aquis carens. At ubi in ea esset Christus, (assumptus enim est per fi- dem, & divino ejus rivulo ditata est, fons enim est vi- tæ, & torrens deliciarum, dixitq; ipse apud quendam è sanctis Prophetis: Ecce ego inclino in eos, velut fluvium pacis, & velut torrentem inundantem glo- riam Gentium) ultra sterilis non erat, nec desertum, imò fœcunda, & sub sponso, & florida intelligibiliter. Quæ olim igitur sitiens erat, lætetur, inquit, & efflo- rescat quasi lilium, tum floridum, tum odoratum. Christi enim odor fuit.

Tertio gloria Libani, decor Carmeli, & Saron, non de mundana celsitudine, ac temporali fœcundi- tate, sed de spirituali gloria & decore, & fertilitate Judææ, in qua eratEcclesia Dei, propria, moreScri- pturæ intelligenda, quæ solet res cœlestes & spiri- tuales phrasibus à rebus mundanis & terrenis de- sumtis designare: Ideoq; innuitur, gentilitati glo- riam & fœcunditatem spiritualem, Judææ hacte- nus propriam, olim concedendam: uti cap. 54, 1 indicavit Esaias: Lauda sterilis, quæ non paris: quo- niam multi filii desertæ. Ita Hieronymus: Quæ quondam deserta fuerat, de qua in Psalmo dicitur: Vox domini concutientis solit dinem, & commovebit dominus desertum Cades: Vox domini præparantis cervos, & revelabit condensa sylvarum, mutabitur in rerum omnium abundantiam: & pugnantibus cervis, de universis saltibus nationum bestiæ, quæ eas prius possiderant, expellentur: ut impleatur illud, quod in hoc eodem Propheta dicitur: Lætare steri- lis, quæ non paris: erumpe, & clama, quæ non par- turis, quoniam plures sunt filii desertæ, magis quam ejus, quæ habet virum: Hæc erat prius sitiens, sive invia, non habens vitales aquas, & Dominus non gradiebatur per eam, quæ nunc florebit ut lilium: Si- ve ut significantius expressit Aquila: ὡς κάλυξ, quam nos tumentem rosam, & nec dum foliis dilatatam possumus dicere. Florebit autem, ut cum Apostolo pronunciet: Christi bonus odor sumus in omni loco. Et illud Cantici Canticorum: Flores visi sunt in terra, mandragoræ dederunt odorem su- um. Quodq; in Septuaginta ponitur καὶ ἀγαλλιά- σεται τὰ ἔρημα τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, i. e. & exultabunt de- serta Jordanis: in Hebraico quidem non habetur, sed possumus dicere, Johannis in Jordane fluvio Pæni- tentiæ Baptismum demonstrari, quod Dominus suo lavacro signavit atq; firmavit. Et quia de solitudine figuraliter, quæ refertur ad gentes, in qua fuit Johan- nes, consequenter jungi potest Jordanis, ut per deser- tum gentium veniamus ad baptismum Salvatoris. Consonat Cyrillus Alexandrinus: Libanus & Car- melus dicitur sæpe Hierusalem, & ipsum Dei tem- plum. Verum gloria digna sanctæ civitate, & divino templo, data est gentium Ecclesiæ: Et in ea vidimus gloriam Domini, & altitudinem Dei. Nam Judæi tanquam nudo homini, & præ aliis nihil egregium habenti, adducti sunt Domino: Nos autem altitudi- nem gloriæ ipsius vidimus. Deum enim scimus ipsum, propter nos ex dispensatione & providentia fa- ctum hominem, itaq; Deum. Atq; ea ratione etiam B. Lutherus noster de gentium conversione hæc interpretatus est. Sequitur, inquit, jam Prophetia de ipsa Ecclesia, quæ nata est ex reliquiis Synagogæ vastatæ: GLORIA LIBANI DATA EST EI. Omnia dona, quæ Synagoga habuit, sunt transla- ta in Ecclesiam è reliquiis Judæorum & gentibus con- gregatam. Gloria enim sunt regnum & Sacerdo- tium, & quicquid Synagogæ datum fuit divinitus, hæc omnia nobis contigerunt. Quanquam vero montem Libanum gentiles occuparint, ad Ebræos tamen eum pertinuisse, ac per Libanum terram Ju- dæ metonymice designari constat. Vid. Jos. 13, 6. Ps. 29, 5. Ez. 17, 3. Hab. 2, 17. Nah. 1, 4. Nonnulli per Libanum templum, per Carmelum & Saron po- pulum Judaicum intelligunt. Ita Pintus, per Liba- num, inquit, intelligitur templum Salomonis, quem- admodum apud Zachariam cap. 11. & apud Eze- chielem cap. 17. ut ibi statim Propheta exprimit. Per Carmelum & Saron intelligitur Judæorum populus, ut cap. 33. explanavimus. Voluit ergo Esaias signifi- care, omnem candorem, & Dei cultum, & Scriptura- rum scientiam & cognitionem, & fructuum spiri- tualium fertilitatem & abundantiam, & omnem gloriam & pulchritudinem, & omnes denique virtutes auferendas esse à Synagoga, & dandas Ecclesiæ. Id significavit Christus Judæis dicens: Auferetur à vobis regnum, & dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus.

Quarto non convenit tanta celsitudo, gloria, & fœcunditas terræ Judææ, quanta hic describitur tempore Ezechiæ: Neq; probabile est, tanto ver- borum apparatu hic eam descripsisse Prophetam, ac, neglecta spirituali felicitate, solum de tempora- libus bonis tam operose tractasse: Lætabitur de- serta & invia, & exultabit solitudo, & florebit quasi lilium: Germinans germinabit, & exultabit læta- bunda & laudans: gloria Libani data est ei; decor

Carmeli & Saron : ipsi videbunt gloriam Domini, & decorem Dei nostri. Néq; vero ea fuit solitudo Ezechiæ tempore in Judæa, ut ea hisce nominibus insignienda fuerit : Siquidem desertum illud ceu prorsus invium, aridum ac sitiens, in quo Dracones habitent, ac Leones & malæ bestiæ, describatur v. 7. & 9. De spirituali vero lætitia, flore, & decore si hæc accipias, non mirum tam profusa lætitia ea cele- brari à Propheta ; cui nihil lætius accidere pote- rat, quam spiritualis regni Christi gloria & propa- gatio, aut solitudinem adeo horribilem designari, cum de vasta gentilitatis in rebus sacris ignorantia, & horrenda cœcitate, ac ἀταξίᾳ agitur, quæ deser- ta à salute, à religione, à cultu Dei & à Deo ipso, vi- tiis & peccatis horrebat, nullosq; justitiæ fructus proferre poterat ; Conversa vero ad Deum instar lilii, singulari sanctitatis vitæ virtute, & operum bo- norum fertilitate, omniq; gloria Libani vel Judaicæ Ecclesiæ florere, gratumq; de se odorem spargere debuit, (uti in Libano Cedri & Thura Esa. 10, 34. c. 16, 10.) omni decore Carmeli & Saron (unde segetes, uvæ, olivæ, & alii fructus, quibus Judæa gaudebat, Carmelus præcipue frumentis copiosis, Saron pascuis lætis abundabat,) virere debuit. Atq; in eo conspecta est præprimis gloria Dei, & decor Dei nostri manifestatus est per orbem, ut hic prædicit Esaias: Glossa Grotii in hæc verba : Ipsi videbunt gloriam Dei: id est, potentem ejus tute- lam experientur reipsa, non fatisfacit, quia qualis gloriæ manifestatio sit, sequentia docent, ea sc. de qua Joh. 1, 14. c. 17, 5. Es. 40, 5. c. 60, 1. quæ per Messiam apparuit.

Quinto nihil evidentius est concione Evange- lica, quæ hic habetur : quæ certe non respicit bona temporalia, sed spiritualia : Confortate manus disso- lutas, & genua debilia roborate. Dicite ad pusillani- mes : Confortamini, & nolite timere. Ecce Deus vester ultionem adducet retributionis. Deus ipse ve- niet, & salvabit vos. Tunc aperientur oculi cœco- rum, & aures surdorum patebunt &c. Quæ tempo- ra respicere Novi Testamenti & adventum Do- mini Dei nostri, cum in carne manifestatus est, & in mundum venit nos salvaturus, è miraculis, quæ hic prædicuntur, & complemento quod per Chri- stum præstitum est, manifestum est : neque obscu- re Christus discipulos Johannis informans, cæci vi- dent, claudi ambulant, surdi audiunt, pauperes Evan- gelizantur Matth. 11, 5. ad hunc locum remisit E- saiæ, quo & Evangelium, quo pauperes, & pusil- lanimes erigendi sunt, de adventu Dei & salute, quam præstat, & miracula, quæ sub adventum Do- mini patrari debebant, exhibentur. Dilutæ nimis sunt Glossæ Grotianæ, quibus illustris Evangelica concio plane pervertitur : CONFORTATE MANUS DISSOLUTAS. Vos Prophetæ omnes aliig, viri boni addite animos Judæis, ne me- moria toleratæ obsidionis pavescant : DEUS IPSE VENIET, ET SALVABIT VOS: Efficiet ne Æthiops ad vos perveniat. Neq; ullum est indi- cium de Æthiope hic sermonem esse, nec miracula illa de cæcis, mutis, surdis & claudis tempori Eze- chiæ congruunt. Ideoq; verba Prophetæ Grotius ad sensus alienos & prorsus incongruos detorque- re necessum habuit, ut suæ præconceptæ opinioni velificaretur. Nimis aperte loquitur Propheta de adventu Christi Domini, qui est Deus noster & Sal- vator noster, qui ultionem fecit retributionis, cum cladem generis humani vindicarit, in Satana, nos autem salvat, quia salutem æternam acquirit, eam- que nobis donare vult: Conf. Ps. 72, 4. vel ad sa- lutem venit iis, qui eum receperunt, ultionem autem illis, qui in sua infidelitate permanere voluerunt, ut

Hector Pintus explicat. Neq; negligi debet, quod in Hebræo verbum יושעכם salvabit vos, nomen Je- su complectitur, erit Jesus vester, quod aliis si lega- tur punctis ישעשע significat oblectabit vos: Quia Jesus gaudium est, & lubitus cordis nostri. Sexto quæ de aquis & fontibus in deserto & so- litudine hic prædicuntur v. 6. 7. non rectius expli- cantur, quam sensu spirituali, de aquis salientibus in æternam vitam Joh. 4. & 7. ut exponit Cyrillus & Hieronymus, cujus verba subjicio: Scissæ sunt sive eruperunt in deserto quondam Ecclesiæ aquæ baptismi salutaris, & torrentes ac rivi in solitudine, diversæ sc. gratiæ spirituales, & quæ erat arida, in stagnum palu- desq; conversa est, ut non solum careret ardore sitis, sed navigabilis esset & irrigua, & haberet fontes plu- rimos, quos cervus desiderat, quos qui biberit, potest benedicere Domino, juxta illud, quod scriptum est, Benedicite Domino de fontibus Israel. Addimus Comment. Brentii. Accedit aliud beneficium: Aquæ exscindentur in deserto & torrentes in terra arida. Et torrida terra redigetur in stagnũ, & terra siticulosa, seu ardore Solis combusta in scaturiginẽ aquarum, ut ubi prius habitaverint Dracones seu serpentes aridissimorum locorum amatores, ibi crescat deinceps herba virens calami & junci. Hæc Christus in adventu suo non implevit quidem cor- poraliter: Neque enim contigit, ut discipuli & au- ditores ejus indigerent aqua in desertis, alioqui etiam petræ effudissent ipsis aquas, ne siti perirent, quemadmodum petra dedit Israelitis aquam in de- serto, & Christus paucissimis panibus ac piscibus multa hominum millia in deserto pavit. Hac vero metaphora verborum significat Esaias, Christum in adventu suo spiritum sanctum in Ecclesiam suam opulente effusurum. Sic & Christus ipse in- terpretatur, cum ait Joh. 7. Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, & bibat. Qui credit in me, dicit Scriptura, flu- mina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Et addit Ev- angelista. Hoc dixit de Spiritu, quem accepturi erant credentes in ipsum. Vides ergo, quod admi- randa dona Spiritus S. quæ Christus in suos disci- pulos contulit; dicantur torrentes, & scaturigines fontium in deserto. Non aliter B. Lutherus de propagatione verbi explicans: Deserta quæ ante sine omni cultu jacebant, illa jucundissime stabunt, quia distribuentur in ea fluvii. Hoc est, rigabuntur Evangelii verbo arida Gentium corda, & concipient vitam. Ita hic Wittenbergæ habemus rivulum, quo etiam vicina loca rigantur. Verbum enim est cœ- lestis sapientia, unde oritur rivulus saliens in æternam vitam Joh. 4. Significat igitur Propheta per hanc allegoriam, quod verbum copiose prædicabitur, & subinde latius spargetur, & ex Ecclesia unius loci, multæ aliæ haurient verbum. Septimo semita & via, quæ sancta vocanda est, per quam nemo pollutus ingreditur, & in qua ne- mo Stultus errat v. 8. non potest de corporali via accipi. Proinde spiritualiter eam explicant In- terpp. Pleriq; de Christo intelligunt, qui est via, veritas & vita Joh. 14, 6. via sancta & tuta, per quam nullus prophanus aut pollutus transit. Per hanc viam: quia quotquot accipiunt Christum per fidem, accipiunt etiam remissionem peccato- rum, emundantur à peccatis suis, reputantur coram Deo justi & sancti. Deinde hæc via tam plana est, ut nec stulti in ea errare queant. Qui enim in Chri- stum credit, etiamsi aliquis simplex fuerit, nulla carnali prudentia præditus, tamen recta incedit ad veram justitiam & æternam salutem: Christus enim ea via est, qua sola pervenitur ad salutem. Ita B. Lutherus noster, ET ERIT IBI SEMITA q. d. Erunt & aliæ semitæ, quæ sanctitatis nomine celebrabuntur. Verum hæc sola sancta erit semita, in qua sancti Patriarchæ etiam ambularunt. Ea via est fides in Jesum Christum, in semen Adæ & Abrahæ promissum. Hæc autem omnia ideo à Propheta di- cuntur, ut discamus, quod fides sequitur verbum, & quod credentes errare non possunt. Mundis enim omnia sunt munda, tum naturaliter parit fides bona opera. Impii autem neq; credere, nec bona opera fa- cere possunt, simulachra tantum bonorum operum edunt. Ideo dicit, non transibit per eam pollutus. In omnibus enim aliis viis sunt impii. Sic cucullus tegit impium Monachum &c. Sola autem fides in Chri- stum via est, quam nullus impius apprehendit, quia membra Christi non possunt esse polluta, habent enim sanctificans caput. Erit tam plana via, in qua ne stulti quidem errent, vocat autem stultos, qui simplici corde verbo adhærent. Hos enim mundus stultos vo- cat, & judicat. Cui explicationi conjungi potest Cyrilli ἔκθεσις: quia subordinati sunt illi sensus: Vitam puram vocat Evangelicæ conversationis vir- tutem, vel aliter, purificationem per Spiritum. De- tergit enim maculam animis hominum impressam, & à delictis absolvit, & efficit ne ullis commaculetur sordibus. Via ergo sancta & pura, & quidem recte dicta est, sed his qui nondum emundati sunt, inaccessa. Versatur enim nemo Evangelice, qui prius ditatus non est purgatione per sacrum Baptisma: Nec igitur quisquam infidelium: nam hi qui impuri sunt, va- dent, inquit, in ea. Sed ambulabunt dispersi, id est, quos sparsit Satanas. Innuit vero gentes: nec erra- bunt. Olim siquidem errabant, lignis & lapidibus servientes, & obliquis viis insistentes. Nunc autem discent rectam viam, & puram, ad sanctam vitam adducentem.

Octavo quæ prædicuntur de securitate, non erit ibi Leo, & mala bestia non ascendet per eam, nec invenietur ibi, non congruunt glossæ Grotianæ, de temporali securitate: Num enim nulli malæ be- stiæ locus in Judæa fuit? Ideoq; manifestum est de Spiritualibus sermonem esse. Per Leonem intelli- git Hieronymus Dæmonem, per bestias malas satelli- tes ejus, quod Deus amoliturus sit Dæmonis, & organorum ejus insultus & machinationes ab Ec- clesia & quibusvis fidelibus. Mala bestia in Ebræo ferarum violenta, uti notat Grotius. Qui vero de hac via ineptam excogitavit glossam.Viam intelli- gens, quæ ad templum ducit recto tramite, quæ dire- cta dicatur, quod sit sine tortuosis anfractibus, quibus ignari possint decipi; quod non transeat per eam pol- lutus, id est, nemo ibi spectetur Syrus, Assyrius, Ægy- ptius, Æthiops. Quantum assequor, hoc vult: Securam fore viam, quæ recto tramite, qui brevissi- mus,ducit ad templum. Sed ea glossa primum mere precaria est: adhæc longe petita, quum nulla in textu templi mentio fiat: neque prædictioni illi congruit: quia vaticinium instituitur de peculiari via, & semita, quam viam sanctam vocatum iri, vel reapse fore, prædicit Esaias, non solum sanctam vo- cat, quod ad templum ducat, neq; pollutus indigita- tur Syrus, aut Assyrius, sed quicunq; non est libera- tus, ut antithesis docet, & ambulabunt, qui liberati fuerint, & redempti à Domino. Porro gaudium prædicitur non temporale, sed spirituale, & æternum vers. 10. lætitia sempiterna super caput eorum. Frigida est Grotii glossa, de liberatione corporali, ET AMBULABUNT CUM LIBERATI FUERINT.) Id est, ii,quos Deus è tot malis eripuit. ET REDEMTI A DOMINO.) judæi qui exitio erepti multis in locis exu- laverant, sup. 11,11. CONVERTENTUR IN PA- TRIAM.) redibunt in Patriam. ET VENIENT IN SION.) Diebus solennibus. Huc usque Grotius. Qui vero præcipuum omisit, quod nempe de gau- dio habetur, prout id describitur cum extensive, qua æternitatem: Lætitia sempiterna super caput eorum: Tum intensive, quoad gaudii perfectionem; gaudium & lætitiam obtinebunt, & fugiet dolor & gemitus. Quæ uti luculenta omnino sunt, ita In- terpp. plerosq; moverunt, ut hæc de æternis gaudiis acceperint, quæ beatis & electis in altera vita ob- tingent, etsi eorum initia in hac vita jam confe- quantur. De liberatis è Sennacheribi manu, & redi- tu eorum in patriam qui acceperit, non invenietur facile, etsi de liberatione è captivitate Babylonica Corvinus in Defens. sentent. Arminii explicet. At nimis manifestum est, de longe alia redemptio- ne hic agi, de qua Cyrillum audire juvat: Nec Leo, nec alia quæpiam mala bestia illic erit, id est, in via pura. Olim enim tanquam sæva fera, cum impiis spi- ritibus, insultavit terræ incolis inventor peccati: sed per Christum fractus est, & à grege credentium ab- actus est, & à Christo ejectus est hac contra eos tyran- nide. In hac ergo via pura, per Christum redempti, & congregati per fidem, in unam animorum consen- sionem coibunt, & via veteri omissa, convertentur, & venient in Sion, i. e. Ecclesiam habentes & in terra & in cælo jugem lætitiam. Laudibus igitur vehent Deum, qui servavit. Et exultatio, & lætitia & omne genus voluptatis in Christo capiet eos, nec ullum pror- sus gustabunt dolorem aut gemitum. Nam qui vo- cati sunt ad spem adeo amplam, qui æternæ vitæ hære- des futuri sunt, & gloriæ supernæ decoribus locuple- tandi sunt, qui expectant, ut cum ipso Christo simul regnent, quem illi dolorem percipient, aut quem acci- pient gemitum? cum universorum Deus malas be- stias perditurus sit, & vastaturus: imo gaudebunt potius, ut qui futuri sunt omnium bonorum omnino omnibusq; modis consortes. Cyrillo adstipulantur Hieronymus in h. l. Eusebius l. 6. Demonstr. Evan- gel. c. 21. Hilarius in Ps. 61. Nazianz. Orat. 1. in Jul. & è Pontificiis Bellarminus, Cornel. à Lapide, Tiri- nus, Menochius: E nostris Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, & alii plerique, qui hæc de Christo & temporibus Nov. Testamenti prædicta agnoscunt, & de re- demptione per Christum facta explicant: ut tace- am, quod de Messia hic agi, etiam Judæi ipsi ob- servarunt, etsi hi gaudia temporalia sub novissima tempora, & in altera vita prædici somniarint.

## 35:5
Verse 5. THEN THE EYES OF THE BLIND SHALL BE OPENED.) Then even the most stupid will understand how much God favors his own.

Latin:

Vers. 5. TUNC APERIENTUR OCULI CŒ- CORUM.) Tunc etiam stupidissimi intelligent, quam fa- veat suis Deus.

## 35:6
Vers. 6. THEN SHALL THE LAME LEAP AS AN HART) Even those slow to move on account of old age and disease shall go forth, that they may behold the works of God.

AND THE TONGUE OF THE DUMB SHALL SING.) Even the most infant-like shall sing the praises of God. These things were fulfilled figuratively at that time, but most openly in the times of the Messiah.

If these things are to be understood concerning the times of the Messiah not figuratively, but most openly, that is, according to τὸ ῥητὸν, or the literal sense (for the literal and proper sense is opposed to figurative speech), what is more certain than that they ought to be accepted concerning the blind, the lame, and the dumb, as they are properly understood? For one must not depart from the propriety of words in the oracles of Scripture, unless necessity compels. Nor is there any reason to say that they ought to be accepted both properly concerning the blind, the lame, and the dumb, and figuratively concerning those who are stupid, slow from old age, and most infant-like: for thus a double sense of the same sentence and of the same words is invented, one figurative and improper, the other indeed proper, which is by no means to be admitted, unless we wish to make Scripture ambiguous and obscure. Furthermore, whom shall we provide as a better interpreter of this prophecy than the Lord Himself, who openly explains it concerning the miraculous healing of the blind, the lame, and the deaf, and assumes that sense as indubitable, and at that time well known and approved in the Jewish Church?

We do not deny, indeed, that Christ, by these miracles performed on the human body and by the liberation from bodily diseases, wished to foreshadow and figure his spiritual benefits, which he effects with no less a miracle in the soul of man, when he spiritually illuminates the blind to know the mystery of faith, spiritually opens the ears of the deaf to receive the Gospel through faith, spiritually makes the lame walk, and raises up loosened knees so that they may make straight paths, so that one who is lame may not go astray, but rather be healed, Heb. 12:13; and that for this reason especially he performed such miracles in the days of his flesh, which either immediately exhibited or in a certain way foreshadowed spiritual benefits: but it is one thing for a certain deed to be a figure of a thing that is to be done thereafter, and quite another for words which are to be taken properly, as they sound, to be at the same time taken figuratively, and for those in which rhetorical propriety—which is opposed to tropes and figures—prevails, to be understood in the very same statement not only in that proper sense, but at the same time in a tropical and figurative one, which is altogether absurd. And it is in this sense, finally, that the commentary of Jerome, which we append in full, has a place here: 'He himself will come and save them,' to whom it is said, 'Do not fear,' or to us: so that the Apostles may say that salvation is common to themselves with the believers. 'Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped: then the lame will leap as a deer, and the tongue of the dumb will be opened.' Although this was completed by the magnitude of the signs when the Lord was speaking to the disciples of John who had been sent to him: 'Go, report to John what you have heard and seen: the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have the Gospel preached to them'; yet it is fulfilled daily among the Gentiles, when those who were previously blind and were stumbling against wood and stones look upon the light of truth. And those who could not hear the words of the Scriptures with deaf ears now rejoice at the precepts of God, when those who were previously lame and did not keep the straight path leap like deer, imitating their teachers, and the tongue of the dumb will be opened, whose mouths Satan had closed so that they could not confess the one Lord. If, however, because of the preceding words, 'strengthen the loosened hands, and make firm the weak knees,' anyone should wish to take these ἐνεργήματα (mighty works) of the Messiah in a figurative sense (the necessity of which is none, since those could be figurative even if these were spoken not figuratively but properly) likewise concerning those who are blind in mind, and have loosened knees, and limp in their feet, and whose tongue is mute when it ought to resound with the praises of God, so that these might also look toward the conversion of the Gentiles, it must be said that this passage of Isaiah was either not pointed to by Christ, or that Christ looked to the same only insofar as his bodily healing was a certain foreshadowing, confirmation, and dispensation of spiritual healing and restoration. Foreshadowing, because the bodily healing was directed by Christ to this end, that spiritual things might be signified by bodily benefits: just as is observed very often in the Old Testament, e.g., that by the bodily leading out of Egypt, spiritual liberation from hell was foreshadowed, and many things similar to these occur. And therefore Hector Pintus rightly says on this passage: 'When Christ performed these miracles, they were then fulfilled bodily, but they are fulfilled daily spiritually, when those who previously had a blind intellect are illuminated by the splendor of truth and look upon the truth itself, of whom divine Paul says: "You were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord." And those who had deaf ears to the word of God hear willingly; and those who were lying in sins now run, that they may grasp the prize.'

And those who were mute now confess their sins. And when Christ performed these miracles bodily, he also wished to signify these spiritual things which were hinted at through them. He opened the eyes of the blind, to show by this deed that it would come to pass that he would illuminate the minds of the foolish and blind nations, which did not know God, with the light of wisdom, and would open their interior eyes to contemplate heavenly things. Confirmation, because the diseases of the body could not be healed unless medicine were prepared against the diseases of the soul, and sins, which are the containing cause of true (spiritual) diseases, as physicians speak, were removed. In which manner, when Christ wished to heal the body, he kept this method of healing, that he would first restore the health of the soul, so that by the cause being removed, the effect might be taken away, Matt. 9. And the Holy Spirit, when he was rendering the cause why Christ healed diseases of every kind, brought forward no other than that it had been predicted by Isaiah ch. 53, that he himself would take away the sicknesses of our soul and our sins by his passion and satisfaction, Matt. 8. In which manner the passage of Matt. 11 could be excellently compared here, referring us to the present prophecy of Isaiah ch. 35, with the allegation of Matthew made in ch. 8. Finally, the dispensation of spiritual medicine is also to be observed here: for Christ healed diseases, blindness, and other natural defects in such a way that he not only demonstrated himself as the Savior of the world who would heal the wounds of the soul, but by this external means and miracle he also stirred up faith, both in those whom he was healing and in others, and thus applied a healing hand to their souls as well, and at the same time illuminated the eyes of the mind and body, restored internal and external hearing, rendered the tongue speaking and speaking well and resounding with the praises of God, and healed those who were spiritually as well as bodily lame, so that those who once did not know how to stand on a straight foot, but were as if with a relaxed mind, might leap in the manner of deer, i.e., be agile in running and firm in their legs, namely νοητῶς (intellectually) or intelligibly, as Cyril has it on this passage. For by the light of the Gospel the eyes of men, who are by nature blind, are illuminated, so that they may see in what way they must enter into true righteousness and the heavenly kingdom. By the sound of the Gospel the ears of men, previously deaf, are so opened that from this hearing they may conceive the highest joy, and even eternal salvation. By the preaching of the Gospel the Holy Spirit is conferred through faith, which Spirit is so efficacious that it restores those who are limping and wandering to true safety and uprightness. From this preaching also the mute are made eloquent, because those who before did not dare to lift their face to heaven now approach with confidence to the throne of grace, and address God as Father and eternal Savior. These are the spiritual miracles which Christ works through His Gospel in the Church. To these, Saint John testifies that those bodily miracles were performed, chapter 20, 30, 31. The gloss of Grotius is entirely foreign to the text and clearly inept: as if the eyes of the stupid are said to be opened only so that they may understand, from the liberation of the people from the hand of Sennacherib, that God favors His own; and as if by the lame are designated none but those who, on account of old age and disease, are to be slow in leaving Jerusalem to behold the works of God; and as if the tongue of the mute is not said to be opened, as to the literal sense, except that even the most infantile are to sing the praises of God for that liberation. Which gloss agrees neither with the purpose of the Prophet nor the connection of the text, and it never came into the mind of anyone even in a dream, except that the Jews, as can be seen in Kimchi, took it concerning the Israelites, who in captivity, or rather exile, are similar to the blind, deaf, lame, and mute. And Grotius himself acknowledged that the times of the New Testament are regarded in Acts 3:7 in his Annotations on the New Testament.

Verse same. FOR WATERS ARE BROKEN OUT IN THE WILDERNESS, AND TORRENTS IN THE DESERT) All will say this, that a great change of things has been made, and indeed for the better for the Jews. See above v. 1. Not only is a future change of things for the better designated generally, but the abundant irrigation of the arid and dry desert is expressed specifically. Nor is Judea devastated by an enemy understood by the desert, but a spiritual desert, which is to be accepted primarily concerning the Gentile world. And therefore spiritual waters are designated: the doctrines of the Gospel, the salutary waters of holy baptism, and the streams of the graces of the Holy Spirit, which like torrents cleanse the Church in the time of the New Testament. Pintus does not speak ill: For waters are broken out in the desert: That is, because in the Church, which had once been a desert, the waters of salutary baptism will burst forth, and the torrents and rivers of grace and Evangelical doctrine. The Prophet alludes to those waters which flowed in the desert from the rock struck by the rod of Moses. All of which bore the figure of those things which were to be in the future, and which we assertively affirm and most firmly believe to have been completed. For the divine Paul says that all those things happened in a figure, and that that rock was Christ, from whose side, struck by a lance, flowed the waters by which we might be washed. Isaiah therefore says that it would come to pass that the Church, which had once been an arid desert, would abound with waters, of which he had spoken above in the twelfth chapter: You shall draw waters in joy from the fountains of the Savior.

Latin:

Vers. 6. TUNC SALIET, SICUT CERVUS, CLAUDUS) Etiam præ senio ac morbo tardi egredientur, ut conspiciant Dei opera.

ET APERTA ERIT LINGUA MUTORUM.) Etiam infantissimi Dei laudes canent. Hæc illo tempore figurate impleta, apertissime vero Messiæ temporibus.

Si de Messiæ temporibus non figurate, sed apertissime, h.e. quoad τὸ ῥητὸν, vel literalem sensum hæc intelligenda (nam figuratæ locutioni opponi- tur sensus literalis & proprius) quid certius est, quam quod de cæcis, claudis, mutis, prout proprie intelliguntur, ea accipi debeant? à proprietate enim vocum in Scripturæ oraculis discedendum non est, nisi cogat necessitas. Neq; est, quod dica- tur, & proprie de cæcis, claudis, & mutis illa accipi debere, & figurate de iis, qui stupidi, præ senio tardi, ac infantissimi sunt: Nam ita ejusdem sententiæ geminus fingitur sensus eorundemq; verborum, alius figuratus & improprius, alius vero proprius, quod minime admittendum, nisi Scripturam ambi- guam & obscuram facere velimus. Porro quem dabimus meliorem interpretem hujus vaticinii, quam Dominum ipsum, qui de miraculosa cæco- rum, claudorum & surdorum sanatione aperte expli- cat, illumque sensum ceu indubium, & in Ecclesia Judæa tum probe cognitum ac probatum assumit

Non diffitemur sanè, Chri- stum his miraculis in corpore humano patratis, & liberatione à corporalibus morbis adumbrare ac figurare voluisse spiritualia sua beneficia, quæ non minori miraculo in anima hominis efficit, cum spiritualiter cæcos illuminat ad cognoscendum fidei mysterium, spiritualiter surdis aures aperit ad suscipiendum per fidem Evangelium, spiritualiter claudicantes ambulare facit, ac genua soluta erigit, ut gressus rectos faciant, ut non claudicans quis erret, magis autem sanetur, Ebr. 12, 13. atq; ob eam imprimis causam talia miracula in diebꝫ carnis patrasse, quæ spiritualia beneficia vel immediate exhibebant, vel quadam ratione adumbrabant: sed aliud longè est factum quoddam esse figuram rei, quæ geri dein- ceps debeat, aliud vero verba quæ proprie, ut sonant, accipienda sunt, simul etiam figurate accipienda, & in quibus proprietas Rhetorica, quæ tropis & fi- guris opposita est, obtinet, ea in eodem prorsus di- cto, non proprio illo tantum sensu, sed simul tropico & figurato intelligenda esse, quod omnino absur- dum est. Atque hoc demum sensu locum hic ha- bet Commentarius Hieronymi, quem adscribimus integrum: Ipse veniet & salvabit eos, quibus dici- tur, nolite timere, sive nos: ut salutem cum credenti- bus Apostoli dicant sibi esse communem. Tunc ape- rientur oculi cæcorum, & aures surdorum patebunt: tunc saliet sicut cervus, claudus, & aperta erit lingua mutorum. Quod quanquam signorum magnitudi- ne completum sit, quando Dominus loquebatur discipulis Johannis, qui ad eum missi fuerant; Eun- tes renunciate Johanni, quæ audistis & vidistis, cæci vident, claudi ambulant, leprosi mundantur, surdi audiunt, mortui resurgunt, pauperes Evangelizan- tur; tamen quotidie expletur in gentibus, quando qui prius cæci erant, & in ligna & lapides impin- gebant, veritatis lumen aspiciunt. Et qui scriptu- rarum verba surdis auribus audire non poterant, nunc ad Dei præcepta lætantur, quando qui prius claudi erant, & rectam viam non tenebant, saliunt sicut cervi, imitantes Doctores suos, & aperta erit lingua mutorum, quorum Satanas ora concluserat, ne possent unum Dominum confiteri. Si tamen ob antecedentia verba, confortate manus dissolutas, & genua debilia roborate, hæc ἐvεργήματα Messiæ quis sensu figurato (cujus vero necessitas nulla est, quum illa figurata esse possint, etsi hæc non figura- te, sed proprie dicerentur) itidem accipere velit de iis, qui mente cæci sunt, & genua soluta habent, ac pede claudicant, & quorum lingua muta est, cum laudes Dei resonare debet, ut hæc ad genti- lium conversionem etiam spectent, dicendum erit à Christo vel non indigitatum esse hunc Esaiæ lo- cum, vel Christum eatenꝫ solum eundem respexis- se, quatenus nempe curatio ejus corporalis erat quædam adumbratio, confirmatio, & dispensatio spiritualis curationis & reparationis. Adumbratio, quia eo directa erat à Christo corporalis sanatio, ut significarentur per beneficia corporalia spiritu- alia: quemadmodum in V. Test. persæpius obser- vatur, v. g. quod per eductionem ex Ægypto cor- poralem spiritualis ex inferno liberatio adumbra- ta fuerit, & quæ his similia occurrūt plurima. Ideo- que recte Hector Pintus in h. l. Cum Christus hæc mi- racula fecit, impleta tunc sunt corporaliter, sed quotidie spiritualiter adimplentur, cum qui prius cæcum ha- bebant intellectum, splendore veritatis illuminentur, & ipsam veritatem aspiciant, de quibus ait divus Paulus: Eratis aliquando tenebræ, nunc autem lux in Domino. Et qui ad verbum Dei surdas au- res habebant, libenter audiant; Et qui in peccatis jacebant, jam currant, ut bravium comprehendant.

Et qui muti erant, nunc de peccatis suis confiteantur. Et cum Christus hæc miracula corporaliter fecit, vo- luit etiam significare hæc spiritualia, quæ per illa in- nuebantur. Aperuit cæcorum oculos, ut ostenderet hoc facto, fore, ut insipientium cæcarumq́; gentium, quæ Deum nesciebant, animos illuminaret luce sa- pientiæ, & ad cælestia contemplanda interiores ocu- los aperiret. Confirmatio, quia sanari morbi cor- poris non possent, nisi parata esset adversus mor- bos animæ medicina, & peccata, quæ causa conti- nens verâ (spiritualium) morborum sunt, uti Me- dici loquuntur, sublata essent. Quo pacto Christus cum sanare corpus vellet, hanc medendi metho- dum servavit, ut prius animæ sanitatem restitueret, quo ita sublata causa tolleretur effectus, Matth. 9. Et Spiritus Sanctus cum causam redderet, cur Christus omnis generis morbos curarit, nullam aliam adduxit, quam quod prædictum ab Esaia c. 53. fuerit, ipsum animæ nostræ ægritudines, & pec- cata nostra passione ac satisfactione sua sublatu- rum, Matth. 8. Quo pacto eximie conferri hic pos- set locus Matth. 11. remittens nos ad præsens Esaianum vaticinium cap 35. cum Matthæi allega- tione cap. 8. facta. Denique observanda etiam hic dispensatio spiritualis medicinæ: Nam curavit ita Christus morbos, cæcitatem, & alios defectus na- turales, ut non tantum sese ceu Salvatorem mundi curaturum animæ vulnera, demonstraret, sed hoc externo medio & miraculo fidem etiam, tum in iis quos sanabat, tum in aliis excitaret, adeoque ipsis quoque animabus medicam manum adhiberet, si- mulq; oculos animi & corporis illuminaret, inter- num & externum auditum restitueret, linguam lo- quentem & bene loquentem, laudesque Dei reso- nantem redderet, actum spiritualiter, tum corpo- raliter claudos sanaret, ut qui olim recto pede ne- sciverunt insistere, sed veluti remissa mente fue- runt, cervorum in morem exilirent, i. e. cursu agi- les & cruribus firmi sint, nimirum νοητῶς vel intelli- gibiliter, uti habet Cyrillus in h. l. Nam luce Evan- gelii illustrantur oculi hominum, qui sunt natura cæci, ut videant qua sit ingrediendum in veram ju- stitiam & regnum cœleste. Sono Evangelii aures hominum ante mutorum ita aperiuntur, ut ex hoc auditu summam jucunditatem, adeoque æternam salutem concipiant. Evangelii concione confertur Spiritus S. per fidem, qui Spiritus tam efficax est, ut claudicantes ac errantes in veram incolumitatem, & rectitudinem restituat. Ex hac quoque prædica- tione muti redduntur eloquentes, quia, qui antea non audebant tollere faciem suam ad cœlum, nunc accedunt cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, & allo- quuntur Deum, ut patrem ac æternum servatorem. Hæc sunt spiritualia miracula, quæ Christus per Evangelion suum in Ecclesia operatur. Ad quæ corporalia ista miracula facere S. Johannes testatur c. 20, 30. 31. Glossa Grotii à textu prorsus aliena est, ac plane inepta: quasi oculi stupidorum ideo tantum aperiendi dicantur, ut intelligant, ex liberatione po- puli à manu Sennacheribi, Deum suis favere, nec per claudos designentur, nisi qui præ senio, & morbo tar- di Hierosolyma egressuri sint, ad conspicienda Dei opera, nec mutorum lingua aperienda dicatur, quod ad sensum literalem, nisi quod etiam infantissimi lau- des Dei cantaturi sint pro illa liberatione. Quæ glos- sa neque instituto Prophetæ, aut συνέχειᾳ textus congruit, & nulli unquam in mentem vel per so- mnium venit, nisi quod Judæi ut apud Kimchium videre est, de Israëlitıs acceperint, qui in captivita- te, vel exilio potius similes sint cæcis, surdis, clau- dis, & mutis. Et tempora N. Test. respici agnovit Grotius ipse ad Act. 3, 7. in Annot. N. Test.

Verf. eod. QVIA SCISSÆ SVNT IN DESERTO AQVÆ, ET TORRENTES IN SOLITUDINE) Hoc dicent omnes, magnam factam esse rerum mutationem, & quidem judæis in melius. Vid. supra v. 1. Non solum γενικῶς futura rerum mutatio in melius designatur, sed εἰδικῶς exprimitur aridi & sicci deserti larga irrigatio. Neque per desertum Judæa ab hoste vastata, sed spirituale desertum in- telligitur, quod cumprimis de gentilisino accipien- dum. Ideoque aquæ spirituales designantur Evan- gelicæ doctrinæ, sacri baptismi aquæ salutares, & gratiarum Spiritus Sancti fluenta, quæ ceu torren- tes mundant Ecclesiam, tempore N. Testamenti. Non male Pintus: Quia scissæ sunt in deserto aquæ: Hoc est, quia in Ecclesia, quæ quondam desertum fu- erat, erumpent aquæ salutaris baptismi, & torrentes ac fluvii gratiæ & Evangelicæ doctrinæ. Alludit Propheta ad aquas illas, quæ in deserto de petra virga Mosi percussa fluxerunt. Quæ omnia gerebant figu- ram eorum, quæ postea futura erant, & quæ completa esse nos asseveranter affirmamus, & firmissime cre- dimus. Divus enim Paulus inquit, omnia illa in fi- gura contigisse, & petram illam esse Christum, ex cujus latere lancea percusso fluxerunt aquæ, quibus ablueremur. Ait igitur Esaias, fore, ut Ecclesia, quæ olim fuerat aridum desertum, abundaret aquis, de quibus supra dixerat capite duodecimo: Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris.

## 35:7
Verf. 7. IN THE HABITATIONS, IN WHICH PREVIOUSLY DRAGONS DWELT, SHALL SPRING UP THE GREENNESS OF REED AND RUSH) The fields of Judea, long desolate, shall flourish again. It is inept to understand the fields of Judea by the habitations, since the minds of men are designated, in which Dragons, Demons, or even errors, superstitions, and crimes, like virulent snakes and savage beasts, used to dwell: but joyfully flourishing mighty works ought to arise. The soul, says Hector, which previously had been an inn for untamed appetites and crimes, shall be a home and receptacle for holy thoughts and virtues: by Dragons understand vices, by the greenness of rush and reed, virtues. The divine Gregory in his 13th homily on Ezekiel understands by the beautiful and sounding reed the preachers of the Gospel, but by the rush the hearers of the Gospel: So that the sense may be: The Gentile world, which before the advent of Jesus Christ was like a certain marketplace of superstitions, having received the faith, will be a certain admirable and beautiful school of Evangelical truth.

Latin:

Verf. 7. IN CVBILIBUS, IN QVIBUS PRIVS DRA- CONES HABITABANT, ORIETUR VIROR CA- LAMI ET JUNCI) Agri Judææ, diu desolati, revirescent. Inepte per cubilia agri Judææ intelliguntur, quum animi hominum designentur, in quibꝫ Dra- cones, Dæmones, vel etiam errores, superstitio- nes, scelera, veluti virulenti angues, & sævæ feræ ha- bitabant: sed oriri debebant virtutes læte virentes. Anima, inquit Hector, quæ prius fuerat indomi- torum appetituum & scelerum diversorium, erit sanctarum cogitationum, & virtutum domicilium & receptaculum: per Dracones vitia, per virorem junci, & calami virtutes intellige. Divus Grego- rius in Ezechielem homilia 13. per calamum pul- chrum & sonorum intelligit Evangelicos concio- natores, per juncum vero auditores Evangelii: Ut sit sensus: Gentilitas, quæ ante Jesu Christi ad- ventum erat veluti quædam superstitionum merca- tura, recepta fide erit schola quædam admirabilis & pulchra Evangelicæ veritatis.

## 35:8
Verse 8. AND THERE SHALL BE A PATH AND A WAY, AND IT SHALL BE CALLED THE HOLY WAY) Namely, that way which leads to the temple.

IT SHALL NOT PASS THROUGH IT, THE POLLUTED ONE) No Syrian, Assyrian, Egyptian, or Ethiopian will be seen there.

AND THIS SHALL BE FOR YOU A DIRECT WAY) By a straight path, which is the shortest, without tortuous windings by which the ignorant could be deceived.

Latin:

Verf. 8. ET ERIT SEMITA ET VIA, ET VIA SAN- CTA VOCABITUR) Nempe illa via, quæ ad templum ducit.

NON TRANSIBIT PER EAM POLLUTUS) Nemo ibi spectabitur Syrus, Assyrius, Ægyptius, Æthiops.

ET HÆC ERIT VOBIS DIRECTA VIA) Recte tramite, qui brevissimus, sine tortuosis anfractibus, quibus ignari possent decipi.

## 35:9
EVIL BEAST) In the Hebrew: A violent one of the wild beasts.

Latin:

MALA BESTIA) In Hebræo: Ferarum violenta.

## 35:10
Verse 10. AND THEY SHALL WALK WHO HAVE BEEN LIBERATED) Those whom God has snatched from so many evils.

AND REDEEMED BY THE LORD) The Jews, who, having been snatched from destruction, had lived in exile in many places. Above 11, 11.

THEY SHALL BE CONVERTED) They shall return to their fatherland.

AND THEY SHALL COME INTO SION) On solemn days.

Latin:

Verf. 10. ET AMBULABVNT QVI LIBERATI FVERINT) Ii quos Deus tot malis eripuit.

ET REDEMIT A DOMINO) Judæi, qui exitio erepti multis in locis exsulaverant. Supra 11, 11.

CONVERTENTUR) Redibunt in patriam.

ET VENIENT IN SION) Diebus solemnibus.

## 36:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVI. Sennacherib, having captured the fortified cities of Judah, sends the Rabshakeh to occupy Jerusalem, who, having cast various insults at Hezekiah and blasphemies at God, exhorts the Jerusalemites to surrender.

From this chapter and the three following are taken those things which we have in 2 Kings 18:17 and thereafter up to 20:19.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVI. Sennacherib captis civitatibus Judæ munitis mittit Rabsacen ad occupandam Hieroso- lymam, qui jactatis variis in Ezechiam convitiis, in Deum blasphemiis, Hierosoly- mitanos ad deditionem exhortatur.

Ex hoc capite & tribus sequentibus desumta ea, quæ ha- bemus 2. Reg. 18, 17. & deinceps ad usque 20, 19.

## 36:5
Verse 5. OR BY WHAT COUNSEL OR STRENGTH DO YOU PREPARE TO REBEL?) In the Hebrew: I have said a word of the lips (that is, surely, in which Hezekiah trusts, as if he says, he believes flatterers: but) counsel and strength are required for war: Tacitus in Book 2 of the Annals said counsel and force, Caesar in Book 1 of the Civil War said counsel and sword. Evenus: Πρὸς σοφίᾳ μὲν ἔχειν τόλμαν μάλα σύμφορόν ἐστι.

Thus also Pintus explains the Hebrew text. But he hands down this sense: You, Hezekiah, trust in a word of the lips, or in your prayers: but you are deceived: For to wage war there is need of counsel and strength, but not of prayers. Which explanation fits more the impiety of this man, who is impious and insults God.

Latin:

Verf. 5. AUT QVO CONSILIO AUT FORTITU DINE REBELLARE DISPONIS) In Hebræo: Dixi cert verbum labiorum (est nempe, in quo Ezechias confidit, qual dicat, credit adulantibus: at) consilium & fortitudo ad bellu requiruntur: Consilium & vim dixit Tacitus 2. Annalium, consilium & gladium Cæsar. 1. de Bello Civili. Evenus, Πρὸς σοφίᾳ μὲν ἔχειν τόλμαν μάλα σύμφορόν ἐστι.

SIc etiam Pintus explicat Hebræum textum. Sed sensum hunc tradit: Tu Ezechia fidis verbo la- biorum, vel precationibus tuis: sed falleris: Nam ad bellum gerendum consilio & fortitudine opus est, non autem precibus. Quæ explicatio impietati hujus empactæ, Deo insultantis, magis congruit.

## 36:16
Verse 16. MAKE WITH ME A BLESSING) Give me gifts: thus ברכה is taken in 2 Kings 5:15.

The passage 2 Kings 18, parallel to this one, ought rather to be compared, in which it is held thus: Make with me that which is useful to you, or which may be of use to you, and may result in your blessing. And the LXX Interpreters: εἰ βύλεσθε εὐλογηθῆναι ἐκπορεύεσθε πρὸς ἐ- μέ. If you wish to be blessed, come out to me.

Latin:

Vers. 16. FACITE MECVM BENEDICTIONEM) Munera mihi date: sic ברכה sumitur 2. Reg. 5, 15.

Conferendus erat potius locus 2. Reg. 18. huic parallelus, in quo ita habetur: Facite mecum, quod vobis est utile, vel quod ex usu vobis esse queat, & in benedictionem vestram cedat. Atque LXX. In- terpp. εἰ βύλεσθε εὐλογηθῆναι ἐκπορεύεσθε πρὸς ἐ- μέ. Si velitis beati esse, egredimini ad me.

## 36:17
Verse 17. UNTIL I COME, AND TAKE YOU TO A LAND, WHICH IS, AS YOUR LAND) Maimonides thinks that Africa is understood, and that the Girgashites went there, this condition having been accepted. And I would believe that these are those Phoenicians, from whom the Tingitanians said they were descended. For as for the fact that Procopius in Vandalic War II refers them to the times of Joshua, it is credible that he was deceived either by ignorance of the language or by some impostor. The times of Dido, who led a colony from Tyre into Africa, from which many others flowed, are not a little later than these times.

The matter here is not about the Girgashites, but the Jerusalemites, nor did Sennacherib wish to lead them anywhere else than into their own land: concerning which Cyril speaks. He truly mitigates the horror of captivity, as it were, and covers the harshness of the thing with painted words, adding that: Until I come, and take you into a land, which is just like your land. For he assimilates the land of the Assyrians to the land of the Jews, to this effect: Judea having been lost, although you may be among us, you will nevertheless find nothing less than your own land. For it is a land of grain and wine, and bread, and vineyards, the region of the Persians and the Assyrians.

Latin:

Vers. 17. DONEC VENIAM, ET TOLLAM VOS AD TERRAM, QVÆ EST, UT TERRA VESTRA) Africam intelligi putat Maimonides, & eo ivisse, conditione hac accepta, Gergezæos. Et hos esse credam illos Phœni- cas, unde se ortos dicebant Tingitani. Nam quod Proco- pi9 Vandalicorum II. eos ad Josuæ refert tempora, in eo cre- dibile est illum aut linguæ ignorantia, aut ab impostore ali- quo fuisse deceptum. Didonis tempora, quæ de Tyro colo- niam in Africam deduxit, unde multæ fluxerunt aliæ, his temporibus non paulo posteriora sunt.

Non de Gergezæis, sed Hierosolymitanis hic res est, neq; aliorsum, quam in terram suam traducere eos volebat Sennacherib: de quo Cyrillus. Mitigat vero quasi captivitatis horrorem, & rei asperitatem fucatis verbis contegit, addens illud: Donec veniam, & accipiam vos in terram, quæ perinde est, ac terra vestra. Assimilat namq; Assyriorum terram terræ Ju- dæorum, in hanc fere sententiam: Amissa Judæa, etsi sitis apud nos, nihilo tamen minus vestram ipsorum terram invenietis. Terra enim est frumenti & vini, & panum, & vinearum, Persarum regio & Assyriorum.

## 37:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVII.

Hezekiah, dismayed on account of the blasphemies of the Rabshakeh, sends to Isaiah, that he might pray to the Lord, who, comforting him, promises divine aid: To repeated blasphemies Hezekiah prays ardently, soon the army of Sennacherib having been killed by an angel, he himself is also killed by his own sons.

Verse 1. HE RENT HIS GARMENTS) He tore.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVII.

Consternatus Ezechias propter blasphemias Rabsacis, mittit ad Esaiam, ut Dominum de- precetur, qui ipsum confortans divinum promittit auxilium: Ad iteratas blasphemi- as ardenter precatur Ezechias, mox cæso per angelum exercitu Sennacherib, etiam ipse à filiis suis interimiter.

Vers. 1. SCIDIT VESTIMENTA SVA) Rupit.

## 37:18
Verse 18. THE KINGS OF THE ASSYRIANS HAVE MADE DESERT THE LANDS AND THEIR REGIONS) In the Hebrew: All the nations and their regions. But it is a syllepsis. For the verb of laying waste is said differently of nations, and differently of lands.

Latin:

Vers. 18. DESERTAS FECERUNT REGES ASST- RIORUM TERRAS ET REGIONES EARUM) In He- bræo: Cunctas gentes & regiones earum. Est autem σύλληψις. Verbū enim vastandi aliter de gentib. dicitur, aliter de terris.

## 37:24
Vers. 24. THE HEIGHT OF ITS SUMMIT) That is, I reached the highest ridges: nothing was impassable to me.

The Vulgate renders it in the future: I will enter the height of its summit, i.e., as Pintus explains, into Jerusalem situated on a high mountain, which Sennacherib, having captured other cities, thought should be attacked. The LXX, however, explained it in the past: κ᾿ εἰσῆλθον εἰς ὕψος τὸ δρύως; & I entered into the height of the forest part. Which Cyril explains thus, that he also penetrated the cities of Judea: From a comparison of the passage 2 Kings 19:23, it appears that בית המקדש designates the house of the sanctuary, which in the Chronicles is called מעון קצן, a dwelling, with respect to GOD, and by Isaiah מרום קצן, a high place, with respect to the site of the sanctuary, because it was situated in a high place. But it is added, a dwelling, likewise the high place OF ITS EXTREMITY, because the house of the Lord was the extremity of that land. The words subjoined THE FOREST OF ITS CARMEL, according to Vatablus, express the temple, which as it were had been a forest in Carmel, i.e., in a fertile field, whose priests, according to the same, are as trees in a forest.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ALTITUDINEM SUMMITATIS EJUS) Id est, ad summa juga perveni: nihil mihi fuit invium.

VUlgata reddit in futuro: Introibo altitudinem summitatis ejus, i. e. ut Pintus explicat, in Hie- rusalem in monte alto sitam, quam Sennacherib aliis urbibus captis impugnandam censebat. LXX. ta- men in præterito exposuêre: κ᾿ εἰσῆλθον εἰς ὕψος τὸ δρύως; & intravi in altitudinem partis sylvæ. Quod ita explicat Cyrillus, quod etiam urbes Ju- dææ penetrarit: E collatione loci 2. Reg. 19, 23. ap- paret בית המקדש domū sanctuarii designari, quæ in Chronicis מעון קצן habitaculum, respectu DEI, ab Esaia מרום קצן excelsum, respectu situs sanctua- rii, quia in excelso loco situm, vocatur. Additur vero habitaculum, item excelsum EXTREMI EJUS, quia domus Domini erat extremum terræ illius. Verba subjuncta SALTUM CARMELI EJUS, secundum Vatablum, templum exprimunt, quod q. saltus fuerat in Carmelo, i. e. in agro feraci, cujus sacerdotes, juxta eundē, ut arbores sunt in saltu.

## 37:35
Vers. 35. AND FOR THE SAKE OF DAVID MY SERVANT.

By David, Coccejus here understands the Messiah at Hosea ch. 1: nor does Hackspan disagree at Dan. 9, 17. Nor does the opinion seem to be rejected: because FOR THE SAKE OF THE MESSIAH God protected his city, because he comes in the name of David, Hos. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 35. ET PROPTER DAVID SER- VUM MEUM.

Per Davidem Coccejus hic intelligit Messiam ad c. 1. Hoseæ: nec abnuit Hackspan. ad Dan. 9, 17. Neq; reprobanda videtur sententia: quia PRO- PTER MESSIAM Deus protexit civitatem suam quia Davidis nomine venit Hos. 3.

## 38:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVIII. Hezekiah, liberated from the death decreed for him through prayers, having received a sign on the sundial of Ahaz, and liberation from the Assyrian is promised to him. His Eucharistic Canticle.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVIII. Ezechias à morte sibi indicta per preces signo in horologio Achaz accepto liberatus, ac li- beratio ab Assyrio ei promittitur. Canti- cum ejus Eucharisticum.

## 38:9
Verse 9. THE WRITING OF HEZEKIAH KING OF JUDAH. Dictated to him, as is credible, by Isaiah himself. But whence is this credible? Why should we not believe that this prayer proceeded from Hezekiah himself, a pious king filled with the Holy Spirit? Not to mention that some maintain that the book of Judges was written by Hezekiah, as Sixtus Senensis testifies in lib. II. Bibl. under the word Hezekiah; some believe the books of Kings were collected and digested by the same, along with the proverbs of Solomon. Others more correctly say that it is Hezekiah's Canticle, even if it was expressed or comprised in these words by Isaiah.

Latin:
