Eccle- siam piorum in toto terrarum orbe ponat. Non sim- pliciter dicit, donec proferat judicium, quemadmo- dum secundo jam dixerat, sed donec ponat in terra judicium. Aliud est proferre Evangelium de Zion, & aliud ponere illud in terra. Hæc Musculus. Aliter illa accepit Calvinus, non deficiet, neque frangetur. Alludit, inquit, ad proximum versum, & confirmat id, quod prius dictum est, nempe Christum quidem placidum & lenem fore erga debiles, nihil tamen aut effœminatum aut molle habiturum, quia mandatum sibi à Patre munus suum viriliter exequetur. Ita & in translatione textus Ebræi, & in sensu ejusdem in diversas partes abripiuntur Interpp. Nemo ta- men facile inventus, qui de Esaia intellexerit, & ignorantiam ac metum eidem hic adimi credide- rit. Nos cur ab explicatione Brentiana, quæ O- siandri etiam est, & cui versio Germanica B. Luthe- ri consonat, discedamus, causam videmus nullam, quæ non Vulgatæ tantum versioni consonat, sed ad commendationem χρηστότητα Messiæ, in qua to- tus occupatur Propheta, interprete ipsomet S. S. in Novo Test. maxime facit. Id enim argumentum Prophetæ esse, allegatioEvangelistæ satis docet, qui ea de causa verba ista omisisse videtur, quod rem eandem exprimant, in qua sententia etiam verba Prophetæ accepit Hieronymus, & Aquila ac Theo- dotionis translationem pariter interpretatus est: Non erit tristis, neque turbulentus, sed æqualitatem vultus omni tempore observabit. Pro quo Aquila & Theodotio interpretati sunt: Non obscurabit, & non curret, donec ponat in terra judicium. Et est sensus: Nullum vultus tristitia deterrebit, nec festi- nabit ad pœnam, qui judicii veritatem ultimo tem- pori reservavit. LXX. etiam Interpp. translationem ad hunc sensum reducit Sanctius, ut significent Se- ptuaginta, Christum non futurum turbulentum, & tristem, id aut non contritione oris, aut ejus sere- nitate & splendore declarant, quia hæc modestia, ac pacis signa sunt. Aut certe dum dicunt non conteran- dum, indicant vincendum non esse à turbidis animi motibus, ac in aliis modestiam, & mansuetudinem exterminare solent.

Sed imprimis manifestant τρεβλότητα Grotii, quæ adduntur de gentibus vel Insulis: quæ apud LXX. ita habent: Et in nomine ejus gentes spera- bunt. Hieron. transtulit, & legem ejus insulæ expe- ctabunt. Quæ ita pervertit Grotius: Certo sciant illi, Assyrii, Mesopotamienses, atque alii eventura, quæ dicit Esaias. Nihil hic de Assyriis speciatim. Neque certitudinem solum prædictionum illarum firmat Propheta. Nec verba mandati hæc sunt, sed verba prædictionis: quid futurum sit, non quid fie- ri debeat, indicantia. Deniq; non paucos concer- nunt Assyrios, aut Mesopotamios, sed longe latius patent. Per insulas enim atque terras omnes com- prehendit Propheta. Ut recte Brentius observa- vit: Doctrinam Evangelii per judicium indicatam divulgandam tam in urbibus terræ, quam in Insu- lis maris, adeoque in toto orbe terrarum. Gemina fere est interpretatio Musculi. Verbum יחל & spe- rare & expectare significat. Per insulas autem in- telligit gentes, à reliqui orbis populis remotiores, & per maris ambitum separatas, ut sit sensus: usq; adeo in terra, i. e. terrarum orbe ponet verbum suum, ut insulani quoque à reliquis divisi & separati, doctri- nam ipsius amplexuri sint, ac spem suam in illam posituri, sic per insulas quidem gentes & nationes populorum, verum à reliquis separatas & seclusas intelligit, quarum hic propterea mentionem facit, ut amplitudinem regni Christi exprimat. A quo sensu non abit Grotius in Annot. ad Matth. imo probat eundem ex antecedentibus, verborum ἐμ- Φάσει & Evangelistæ allegatione. Adscribam lo- cum ejus integrum: quia ad explicationem verbo- rum facit, prout à Matthæo adducta sunt: & ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι ἀυτõ ἔθνη ἐλπιõσι, optime cum præcedenti- bus cohæret. Merito enim fiduciam gentes collocant in ejus bonitate, qui Judæos immorigeros tanta lenitate pertulit, איים, quod in Hebræo est, non semper Insu- las, sed sæpe regiones quasvis significat, ut Gen. 10, 5. Recte igitur & LXX. & noster Interpres sensum reddi- derunt voce ἐθνῶν. Itidem ייחלו ἐλπιõσι optime, nam ita & alibi exponunt tum LXX. tum Hebræi. Quod autem pro לתורתו apud LXX. viros habemus ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι, nullum est ex scriptorum vitium: nam & Iusting bis ita citat. Et noster hic, qui toto hoc loco LXX. non est sequutus, itidem reddit, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι, aut τῷ ὀνόματι, ut quidam habent codices. Nimirum תורה Hebræis frequenter significat id, quod ipsi alias דרך Græci elegantiores dicunt ἅιρεσιν. Hellenistæ autem idem vocant ὄνομα, quia moris est sectatores ab insti- tuti sui auctore nominari. Ita Paulus negat se quan- quam in suo nomine baptizasse, indicans nullius se no- vi instituti esse auctorem. Putarunt igitur LXX. qui locum hunc de populo Israëlítico interpretabantur, hoc velle Prophetam, exteras gentes fiduciam colloca- turas in professione Judaismi: cum sensus sit, ut Mat- thæus & res ipsa nos docet, id ipsum facturas gentes in professione Christianismi, qui in se Judaismi perfe- ctionem continet.

Quod ad verba, DONEC PONAT IN TERRA JUDICIUM, illis nonnulli definiri tem- pus putant, ac si dicat, erit usq; ad mortem mansue- tus & mitis, quia usq; ad mortem Evangelium nun- ciavit. Uti explicat Hector Pintus, durabit hæc mansuetudo usque ad mortem, tunc enim ponet judi- cium in terra, hominem Patri reconcilians, moriens pro peccatis nostris. Similiter fere Sanctius. Dici- tur futurus Christus mansuetus, & patiens donec ex- altatus in cruce, & victoria compos judicium ferat. Matthæus enim ita illa recitavit: Donec ejiciat ad victoriam judicium. Sed hæc ad personam, & ad tempus vitæ Christi restringi non debent. Nam qualis in diebus carnis fuit in ponendo in terra judi- cio, talis adhuc est Christus, etsi id nunc non agat immediate, sed per ministros suos. Quocirca re- cte Brentius: non exhibuit in terris tantum Ecclesiæ hanc virtutem, sed adhuc retinet eam, jam sedens ad dextram Patris sui. Quia descriptio virtutum Chri- sti eo pertinet, ut omnes gentes invitentur ad cre- dendum Evangelio Christi, & sciant, se non posse Deo cultum vere gratum præstare, nec veram salu- tem consequi, nisi hunc Christum fide sua comple- ctantur, & vocationem Evangelii ejus sectentur. De quo & Calvinus monuerat: Hoc ad Christi per- sonam restringi non debet, sed ad totum Evangelii cursum, quia non modo legatione sibi injuncta functus est per triennium, sed per suos ministros quotidie ean- dem continuat. Minus commode dicitur, legationem nunc continuare Christus, quia ad dextram Dei ex- altatus est; etsi judicium adhuc ponat in terra per legatos suos, & positurus sit usq; ad consummatio- nem seculi. S. Irenæus lib. 3. advers. Hæres. cap. 2. hæc ita legit, usq; quo emittet in contentionem judi- cium. Qua metaphora indicat doctrinam Evange- lii, quæ legis & judicii nomine venit, in contentio- nem venturam cum aliis legibus, quas libido, ava- ritia & ambitio in mundum evexere: quæ tandem cadent omnes, vincente atq; triumphante ubique terrarum Evangelio, vel judicio Christi.

## 42:6
Ver. 6. I THE LORD HAVE CALLED THEE IN RIGHTEOUSNESS.) God addresses Isaiah. You might translate it more correctly 'unto righteousness': I have called thee, he says, that thou mayest speak all things true and right.

He continues to ἰουδαΐζειν [Judaize], nay, to corrupt the text in a more than Jewish manner. He who treats not of Isaiah, but, as has been shown, of the Messiah, him therefore God addresses, which is testified by those things which are held in v. 7. For was Isaiah given for a covenant of the people, or for a light of the Gentiles? Were the eyes of the blind Gentiles opened by him, were the prisoners led out of the prison-house, sitting in darkness, in the house of the dungeon? All of which it is clearer than light concern the Messiah and the calling of the Gentiles. And lest any doubt should remain concerning him, although the matter ought deservedly to be free from all doubt, we have an interpretation superior to all exception in chap. 49. 'It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I have given thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.' Which can be understood of no one else but Christ. Finally, Simeon received the same things concerning Christ, when he composed his song from these passages in Luke 2, and called Christ a light for the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of his people Israel. And the Apostle

Acts 13:47. For so the Lord has commanded us: I have set you to be a light to the Gentiles, that you should be for salvation to the ends of the earth. Moreover, Christ is said to be called IN RIGHTEOUSNESS, that is, justly, note the Hebrew phrase בְּצֶדֶק, because his calling is by far the most just, and the source and fountainhead of all righteousness: therefore the end of the calling is not noted, nor is he said to be called so that he may speak just things, even if you translate it INTO RIGHTEOUSNESS, since he would rather be called called INTO RIGHTEOUSNESS who establishes righteousness, than he who speaks just things, although both are proper to Christ, who both restores and establishes righteousness, Dan. 9:24, and is the herald of righteousness, which no one would know unless his Spirit were teaching.

Verse of the same. I HAVE TAKEN HOLD OF YOUR HAND) In the Hebrew: I will take hold. I will strengthen you, as above 41:13.

AND I HAVE KEPT YOU) I will guard you: namely, until you have performed the task.

Latin:

Vers. 6. EGO DOMINUS VOCAVI TE IN JUSTITIA.) E- saiam Deus alloquitur. In justitiam rectius vertas: revoca- vi te, inquit, ut omnia vera & recta eloquaris.

Pergit ἰουδαΐζειν, imo plusquam Judaico more textum corrumpere. Qui non de Esaia, sed, ut o- stensum, de Messia agit, Hunc ergo Deus compel- lat, quod testantur ea, quæ v. 7. habentur. Num e- nim Esaias in fœdus populi datus, aut in lucem gen- tium? Num per ipsum aperti oculi cæcorum gen- tilium, num educti vincti de conclusione, sedentes in tenebris, in domo carceris? Quæ omnia Mes- siam & vocationem gentium concernere luce cla- rius est. Et ne illum supersit dubium, quamvis res omni dubitatione merito vacare debeat, habemus interpretationem omni exceptione superiorem c. 49. Parum est, ut sis mihi servus ad suscitandas tri- bus Jacob, & feces Israël convertendas. Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Quæ de nullo alio, quam Christo intelligi possunt. Denique de Christo eadem accepit Si- meon, cum ex his locis carmen suum concinna- vit Luc. 2. ac Christum dixit lumen ad revelationem gentium, & gloriam plebis Israël. Et Apostolus

Act. 13, 47. Sic enim nobis præcepit Dominus: Confti- tui te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus usque ad extre- mum terræ. Vocatus autem Christus dicitur IN JUSTITIA, h. e. juste, nota Ebræa phrasi בְּצֶדֶק , quia vocatio ejus longe est justissima, & omnis ju- stitiæ fons & scaturigo: non ergo finis vocationis notatur, nec vocatus dicitur, ut justa loquatur, e- tiamsi vertas IN JUSTITIAM, siquidem IN JUSTITIAM potius vocatus dicatur, qui justi- tiam erigit, quam qui justa loquitur, utrumq; vero Christo proprium est, qui & reparat atq; erigit ju- stitiam, Dan. 9, 24.. & præco est justitiæ, quam nisi ipsius Spiritu docente, nemo norit.

Vers. eod. APPREHENDI MANUM TUAM) In Hebræo: apprehendam. Confirmabo te, ut supra 41, 13.

ET SERVAVI TE) Custodiam te: nempe donec munus peregeris.

## 42:6
AND I HAVE GIVEN YOU AS A COVENANT OF THE PEOPLE.) That you may recall my Jewish people to the observance of the covenant.

He is said to be given as a covenant of the people, not he who recalls to the observance of the covenant by teaching, but he who establishes the covenant and is its author; and therefore Christ is designated here again, whose covenant of grace this is, which was promised to the Jewish people in him, to establish and sanction, who for that reason is called the mediator of the covenant, and he sanctioned it with his blood. This indeed looks to the whole human race, but it is called the covenant of the Jewish people, because God had chosen this people above others, to whom he might manifest, promise, and confirm that covenant by the Sacrament of circumcision, and other seals, with whom he not only entered into it, but also received from their blood the Mediator, in whom and through whom that covenant was to be established. Worthy of note are the things which the blessed Luther has here: I have given you as a covenant of the people, where then remains the covenant of Moses and the law? Thus with one word he drains and abrogates the whole law with all its righteousness, worship, and works. Moreover, this passage serves to establish the conscience. For because nothing is more pestilential than a scruple of conscience and doubt, therefore he says that Christ is our covenant, so that we may be certain of the first commandment, that God in Christ and through Christ wishes to be our Father and God, that Christ ought to be the covenant and pledge of grace, not any of our good works, etc. AND A LIGHT TO THE GENTILES. He is not the covenant of the Gentiles, for Christ was promised only to the Jews, and was only a minister of the circumcision. But from that covenant, from that ministry, that light is scattered among the Gentiles. At the same time, observe in this place the exclusive, that outside of Christ there is no covenant, no light, but blindness and enmity toward God, and the wrath of God.

Verse of the same.

INTO A LIGHT TO THE GENTILES.) That you may teach the Gentiles that there is one God, the creator of the world.

THAT YOU MIGHT OPEN THE EYES OF THE BLIND) Of the idolaters.

Latin:

ET DEDI TE IN FOEDUS POPULI.) Vt populum meum Judaicum ad observationem fœderis revoces.

In fœdus populi datus dicitur, non qui revo- cat ad observationem fœderis docendo, sed qui fœdus sancit, ejusdemq; autor est; Ideoq; Chri- stus hic iterum designatur, cujus hoc est fœdus gra- tiæ, quod populo Judaico promissum in ipso erat, erigere, ac sancire, qui ob id mediator fœderis di- citur, idq; sanguine suo sancivit. Quod ad totum quidem genus humanum spectat, sed populi judai- ci fœdus dicitur, quia præ aliis hunc populum Deus elegerat, cui fœdus illud manifestaret, promitte- ret, & confirmaret Sacramento circumcisionis, a- liisq; sigillis, cum quo id non tantum iniit, sed re- cepit quoq; ex sanguine ipsorum Mediatorem, in quo & per quem fœdus illud erigendum erat, dare. Observatu digna sunt, quæ hic habet B. Lutherus dedi te in fædus populi, ubi ergo manet fædus Mo- sis & legis? Sic uno verbo haurit, & abrogat totam legem cum omni justitia, cultu & operibus suis. Fa- cit autem hic locus ad stabiliendam conscientiam. Quia enim nihil pestilentius est, quam scrupulus conscientiæ, & dubitatio: ideo dicit, Christum esse fædus nostrum, ut simus certi de primo præcepto, quod Deus in Christo, & per Christum vult noster Pater & Deus esse, quod Christus debet fædus & pignus gra- tiæ esse, non aliqua nostra bona opera &c. ET LU- MEN GENTIUM. Non est fædus gentium, Chri- stus enim Judæis tantum promissus est, & fuit mini- ster tantum circumcisionis. Sed ex illo fædere, ex mi- nisterio illa lux in gentes spargitur. Simul observa hoc loco exclusivam, quod extra Christum nullum fædus, nulla lux est, sed cæcitas & inimicitia erga Deum, & ira Dei.

Vers. eod.

IN LUCEM GENTIUM.) Vt gentes doceas unum esse Deum mundi opificem.

UT APERIRES OCULOS COECORUM) Idololatrarum.

## 42:7
Verse 7.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

## 42:7
AND BRING OUT THE PRISONER FROM THE CONFINEMENT) That the Jews, warned by you about correcting their vices, might in this way find a way out from that custody in which they were detained.

FROM THE PRISON HOUSE THOSE SITTING IN DARKNESS) It is the same as what he has already said. Darkness here is the utmost sorrow.

The title 'light of the Gentiles' is far more illustrious than what might fall to a mere Teacher: for he is called the light of the Gentiles not only because he teaches the Gentiles, much less because he merely teaches them that there is one God, the creator of the world, which the Gentiles even acknowledged with nature as their guide and teacher, for τὸ γνωσὸν enim τῦ Θεῦ φανερὸν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, Rom. 1, 19, nor can that suffice for the illumination of the Gentiles; but because he illuminates their minds by the efficacy of his word and the Holy Spirit, and converts them from darkness to light. Because Christ alone accomplishes this by his Spirit, this name is appropriated to him, that he is the light of the Gentiles, Is. 49, Acts 13, Luke 2. Add that the Prophet explains this in the words that follow: 'that you may open the eyes of the blind': which is a divine effect. For God alone can open the eyes of the blind, whether they are blind corporally or spiritually. Which is appropriated to Christ, Is. 35, Eph. 5, Luke 1 and 2. No less divine is the operation that follows in the Prophet: 'AND YOU SHALL BRING THE PRISONER OUT OF THE PRISON, THOSE WHO SIT IN DARKNESS OUT OF THE PRISON HOUSE.' Grotius perverts these words in such a way that the Jews, warned by you about correcting their gods, might in this way find a way out of that custody in which they were detained: But these things are said not of the Jews, but of the Gentiles, to whom Christ has been given as a light. Of whom this is the description, that they sit in darkness, Is. 9, 2, ch. 60, 1, Luke 1, 79. Nor is the discourse about bodily captivity or custody; but just as the opening of the eyes is understood spiritually, so also is the leading of the prisoners out of the prison and of those sitting in darkness out of the prison house, Is. 49, 9, ch. 61. Jerome paraphrases these things thus: 'I have given you as a covenant of the people of Israel, to whom I had promised before that you would come. And as a light to the Gentiles, who were sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death, that you might open blind eyes, which had not seen the light before.' And you shall bring the prisoner out of the prison: for everyone is bound by the ropes of his own sins: And in the Gospel, the Lord loosed him whom Satan had bound. 'Out of the prison house those who sit in darkness,' who were occupied in the night and gloom of error. How the eyes of the blind are opened, Brentius explains excellently: 'Just as all men contract sin from Adam, so they also contract from him blindness of mind, so that by their own nature they cannot see the way by which they must escape from sin, from the darkness of death and hell, and enter into righteousness, and into the splendor of life and the heavenly kingdom.' What, therefore, is more calamitous for a man having nothing but natural things? It is an old saying: 'Blind man, miserable man.' Blind Mann, arm Mann. And the blindness of the soul is as much more miserable than that of the body as the soul surpasses the body in its dignity. Who, therefore, can deliver man from this most pernicious blindness? Certainly not human reason, not free will. For these are powers of the soul. But since the soul of man is by its own nature blind in heavenly things, it is necessary that its powers also be blind. But Jesus Christ, the Son of God, alone was given to us for this purpose, that he might open the eyes of the blind. But how? He undertakes to expiate our sins and to appease the wrath of God toward us. And he set forth this office of his from the beginning of the world through the Patriarchs and Prophets. Then he set it forth himself in person, when he had come in the flesh. Finally, he published it through his Apostles to the whole world, and preserves this Gospel of his office against the gates of hell, until the last day of this world. Whoever, therefore, receives Christ through faith, and truly believes his Gospel, to him the eyes of the mind are so opened and illuminated by the Holy Spirit that he walks straight from sin to righteousness, from death to life, from hell to heaven, because he is accounted righteous on account of Christ, is saved in death, and is carried into heaven; in token of which thing Christ willed, while he was still present on earth, to open the eyes of those also who were corporally blind, so that by this miracle he might testify that he was truly the one who would illuminate the eyes of the mind. Nor did he less excellently describe the liberation of the prisoners. The spiritual prison is death and hell. We are all cast into these prisons on account of sin. The darkness is the various afflictions in this world, the horrors of death and the smoke of hell, and we have been cast into this darkness on account of sin.

Christ, therefore, the Son of God, undertakes to expiate sin, and brings it about that as many as acknowledge him through faith obtain remission of sin and are accounted righteous on his account. But where sin is expiated and remitted, there afflictions, death, and hell can no longer bring harm. Nor can they oppress a man, even if for some time they seem to inflict trouble. For Christ, who expiated and remitted sin, also preserves the believer in death and the horrors of hell, so that he may be delivered. Wherefore, if anyone is bound by pains of either body or mind, let him hasten to Christ, who, even if he does not immediately free the one calling upon him from external bonds, yet frees him from the spiritual bond, which is sin. This bond being loosened and broken, there will be most certain deliverance, even bodily, but then, when it is useful to us and seems good to the Lord. What the Papists here say about the limbo of the Fathers, even the Jesuit Sanctius, are truly old wives' dreams. Rightly Corn. a Lapid. Infidelity and sin are darkness and the shadow of death: they are also a prison and chains, by which sinners are miserably bound and held by the Devil. This is what he says, that you might lead out from the conclusion, that is, from the prison, which is closed, a bond. It is clear, therefore, that everything convinces that the discourse is about the Messiah, not v. about Isaiah or any other. Which evidence of this prophecy concerning the servant of God R. Isaac Ben. Abravan. acknowledges, so that he does not hesitate to profess that those doctors are struck with blindness who feel that Isaiah speaks of himself or of Cyrus, even if among them there is R. Solomon, that great oracle of the Jews.

Latin:

ET EDUCERES DE CONCLUSIONE VINCTUM) Vt Ju- dæi per te moniti de corrigendis vitiis suis hoc modo ex- itum reperiant ex illa custodia, in qua detinebantur.

DE DOMO CARCERIS SEDENTES IN TENEBRIS) Idem est, quod jam dixit. Tenebræ sunt hic mœstitia summa.

Longe illustrior est appellatio lucis GENTIUM, quam quæ in merum Doctorem cadat: nam lux gen- tium dicitur non tantum, qui docet gentes, nedum qui solum easdem docet, quod unus sit Deus mundi opifex, quod gentes etiam natura duce ac doctrice agnovere, τὸ γνωσὸν enim τῦ Θεῦ φανε- ρὸν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, Rom. 1, 19. nec ad illuminatio- nem gentium sufficere potest; sed qui mentes ipso- rum verbi & Spiritus S. efficacia illustrat, & ex te- nebris ad lucem easdem convertit. Quod solus Christus Spiritu suo præstat, ideo ipsi nomen hoc appropriatur, quod sit lux gentium Es. 49. Act. 13. Luc. 2. Adde, quod Propheta id verbis subjunctis explicat, ut aperires oculos cæcorum: quod ἀποτέλε- σμα divinum est. Deus enim solus oculos cæco- rum aperire potest, sive corporaliter cæci sint, sive spiritualiter. Quod Christo appropriatur Es. 35. Eph. 5. Luc. 1. & 2. Nec minus divinum ἐνέργημα est, quod sequitur apud Prophetam, ET EDU- CERES DE CONCLUSIONE VINCIVM, DE DOMO CARCERIS SEDENTES IN TENEBRIS. Quæ ita pervertit Grotius, ut Ju- dæi per te moniti de corrigendis Diis sui hoc modo ex- itum reperiant ex illa custodia, in qua detinebantur: At non de Judæis hæc, sed de gentibus dicuntur, quibus lux datus est Christus. Quarum hæc descri- ptio est, quod in tenebris sedeant, Esa. 9, 2. cap. 60, 1. Luc. 1, 79. Nec de captivitate vel custodia corpora- li sermo est; sed ut apertio oculorum spiritualis in- telligitur, ita & eductio vinctorum è conclusione ac sedentium in tenebris de domo carceris, Esa. 49, 9. cap. 61. Hieronymus ita hæc παραφράζει: Dedi te in fœdus populi Israël, cui te venturum ante promi- seram. Et in lucem gentium, quæ sedebant in tenebris, & in umbra mortis, ut aperires oculos cæcos, qui lu- cem antea non videbant. Et educeres de conclusione vinctum: funibus enim peccatorum suorum unus- quisq́; constringitur: Et in Evangelio, quem Sata- nas vinxerat, solvit Dominus. De domo carceris se- dentes in tenebris, qui in erroris nocte & caligine ver- sabantur. Quomodo oculi cæcorum aperiantur, præclare exponit Brentius: Omnes homines sicut contrahunt ab Adamo peccatum, ita contrahunt etiam ab eo cæcitatem mentis, ut natura sua non queant videre viam, qua sit evadendum ex pecca- to, ex tenebris mortis & inferni, & ingredi in justi- tiam, & in splendorem vitæ ac regni cœlestis. Quid ergo homini nihil aliud præter naturalia habenti calamitosius? Vetus dictum est: Cæcus homo, miser homo. Blind Mann, arm Mann. Et tan- to miserior est cæcitas animæ, quam corporis, quanto anima dignitate sua superat corpus. Quis igitur liberare potest hominem ab hac tam perni- ciosa cæcitate? Non certe humana ratio, non li- berum arbitrium. Hæ enim sunt potentiæ animæ. Cum autem anima hominis sit in cœlestibus rebus natura sua cæca, etiam potentiæ ejus cæcæ sint ne- cesse est. Solus autem Jesus Christus Filius Dei in hunc usum datus est nobis, ut aperiat oculos cæ- corum. Sed quomodo? Suscipit in se expianda peccata nostra, & placandam iram Dei erga nos. Et hoc officium suum exposuit ab initio orbis per Patriarchas & Prophetas. Deinde exposuit ipse coram, cum venisset in carnem. Postremo vulga- vit per Apostolos suos in totum orbem terræ, & conservat contra portas inferorum hoc officii sui Evangelium, usque ad novissimum hujus mundi diem. Quicunque igitur recipit Christum per fi- dem, & vere credit Evangelio ejus, huic oculi men- tis per Spiritum S. ita aperiuntur, & illustrantur, ut recta incedat à peccato ad justitiam, à morte ad vitam ab inferno ad cœlum, quia reputatur propter Christum justus, servatur in morte, & deportatur in cœlum, in cujus rei fidem voluit Christus, cum adhuc in terra præsens esset, aperire eorum etiam oculos, qui corporaliter cæci erant, ut hoc mira- culo testaretur, se vere esse illum, qui oculos men- tis illustraret. Nec minus egregie liberationem vinctorum descripsit. Spiritualis carcer est mors & infernus. In hos carceres conjecti sumus omnes propter peccatum. Tenebræ sunt variæ afflictiones in hoc mundo, horrores mortis & inferni fumus, & in has tenebras propter peccatum conjecti sumus.

Christus igitur filius Dei suscipit peccatum expian- dum, & efficit, ut quotquot agnoscunt ipsum per fi- dem, consequantur remissionem peccati, & repu- tentur propter ipsum justi. Ubi autem peccatum est expiatum & remissum, ibi non possunt amplius incommodum afferre afflictiones, mors & infer- nus. Nec possunt hominem opprimere, etiamsi aliquanto tempore videantur molestiam inferre. Christus enim, qui peccatum expiavit, & remisit, idem etiam servat credentem in morte, & horrori- bus inferni, ut liberetur. Quare si quis vinctus fue- rit doloribus vel corporis vel animi, properet ad Christum, qui etsi non statim liberat invocantem externis vinculis, tamen liberat eum spirituali vin- culo, quod est peccatum. Hoc autem vinculo so- luto, & effracto, certissima erit liberatio, etiam cor- poralis, sed tum, cum nobis utile, & Domino visum fuerit. Quae hic Papistae de limbo Patrum, etiam Je- suita Sanctius, vere somnia sunt anilia. Recte Corn. a Lapid. Infidelitas & peccatum sunt tenebrae & umbra mortis: Sunt & carcer ac vincula, quibus misere vincti a Diabolo tenentur peccatores. Hoc est, quod ait, ut educeres de conclusione, hoc est, de car- cere, quod clauditur, vinclum. Patet ergo omnia convincere, quod de Messia sermo sit, non v. de E- saia; aliove ullo. Quam evidentiam hujus vati- cinii de servo Dei agnoscit R. Isaac. Ben. Abra- ban. adeo ut profiteri non dubitet caecitate percuf- sos esse doctores illos, qui Esaiam de seipso, vel de Cyro loqui sentiunt, etsi inter illos etiamsi sit R. Salomo, magnum illud Judaeorum oraculum.

## 42:8
Vers. 8. I THE LORD) יהוה. THIS IS MY NAME) By which I am distinguished from the gods of the nations.

MY GLORY I WILL NOT GIVE TO ANOTHER, AND MY PRAISE TO GRAVEN IMAGES.) Again a litotes: for he wishes to say that he will severely avenge himself on those who give the name, which is his own, to Bel, Nebo, Merodach, and others, τοῖς μὴ φύσει οὖσι θεοῖς (to those who are not by nature gods).

A merely new and precarious gloss. Who would look for this figure in these words, or has ever looked for it? The words of the Prophet do not speak of punishment against idolaters, much less specifically about the worshippers of Bel, Nebo, and Merodach, but about the nullity of idols. Concerning which we have treated at length and expressly in Theolog. Natur. & Revel. Let Hackspan also be compared here ad h. l. Since he has spoken at length against idolaters, he concludes the discourse here with a formula of protestation and seals the same, that he is by no means willing to give his glory to another, whoever he may be, much less to graven images, which were worshipped by the nations. He had already spoken about the glorifying of the Son, therefore these things cannot be opposed to him (that we may observe this incidentally against the Arians, whose mouths we stopped at the cited place, as was fitting, as also against Dan. Tossan. in Disp. Heidelb. th. 21. and other Calvinists, denying therefrom the communication of glory made to the human nature of Christ.) Nor is glory given with the Son, departing from the Father, but the Father is in the Son, and the Son is in the Father. Which he infers, (says Hieronym. h. l.) I the Lord, this is my name, my glory I will not give to another, does not exclude the Son, to whom, saying in the Gospel, Father glorify me with the glory which I had with you before the world was, he himself replied, and I have glorified, and will glorify. For he did not say, I will give my glory to no one, which if he had said, he would have excluded the Son also: but I will not give my glory to another besides you, to whom I have given, to whom I am about to give.

Latin:

Vers. 8. EGO DOMINUS) יהוה. HOC EST NOMEN MEUM) Quo a diis gentium discer- nor.

GLORIAM MEAM ALTERI NON DABO, ET LAUDEM MEAM SCULPTILIBUS.) Iterum λιτότης: vult enim dicere se vindicaturum severe in eos, qui nomen, quod ipsius est, dant Belo, Neboni, Meraducho & aliis, τοῖς μὴ φύ- σει οὖσι θεοῖς.

Glossa mere nova & precaria. Quis hanc fi- guram in istis verbis quaereret, aut quaesivit un- quam? Non de Poena adversus idololatras, mul- to minus speciatim de cultoribus Beli, Neboni, Me- raduchi, sed de nullitate idolorum verba Prophetae loquuntur. De quibus prolixe, & ex professo egi- mus in Theolog. Natur. & Revel. Conferatur e- tiam hic Hackspan. ad h. l. Quum adversus idolo- latras prolixe dixerit, concludit orationem hic protestationis formula, & obsignat eandem, quod gloriam suam nullatenus alteri dare velit, quisquis ille fuerit, nedum sculptilibus, quae a gentibus cole- bantur. De Filio glorificando jam dixerat, ideo ei haec opponi nequeunt (ut id obiter adversus Aria- nos observemus, quibus loco dicto, prout par erat, os obturavimus, ut & adversus Dan. Tossan. in Disp. Heidelb. th. 21. & alios Calvinianos, com- municationem gloriae humanae Christi naturae fa- ctam inde negantes.) Neq; cum Filio gloria datur, a Patre disceditur, sed Pater in Filio est, & Filius in Patre. Quod infert, (inquit Hieronym. h. l.) ego Do- minus, hoc est nomen meum, gloriam meam alteri non dabo, non excludit Filium, cui dicenti in Evan- gelio, Pater glorifica me gloria, quam apud te habui, priusquam mundus esset, ipse respondit, & glorifica- vi, & glorificabo. Neq; enim dixit, gloriam meam nulli dabo, quod si dixisset, exclusisset & filium: sed gloriam meam alteri non dabo praeter te, cui dedi, cui daturus sum.

## 42:9
Vers. 9.

THE THINGS WHICH WERE AT THE FIRST, BEHOLD THEY HAVE COME.) Isaiah speaks as if he were present at the Babylonian captivity. You see that those things have happened which I told Hezekiah about this calamity.

I ALSO ANNOUNCE NEW THINGS) The future liberation.

BEFORE THEY SPRING FORTH) Before any seeds of that matter exist.

The words are not Isaiah's, but God's, who from those things which he had previously foretold either through Isaiah or through others, which the Jews themselves could not deny had happened, commands them to conclude that the new things which he announces are likewise certainly about to happen before they spring forth, especially those which he had just foretold concerning the benefits of the Messiah, therefore they are commanded to sing a new song immediately, not the Jews only, but all throughout the circle of the earth, because those benefits reach the whole human race. Hence those words, I ALSO ANNOUNCE NEW THINGS, are rashly restricted to the future liberation from the Babylonian captivity, of which there was no word treated here. But Jerome rightly paraphrases these. The things which were first, behold they have come. The things which I have spoken, which I have promised through Moses and the Prophets, all are completed. But now I announce to you the Gospel, the calling of the Gentiles, the passion of Christ, the newness of faith, so that just as you see the former things fulfilled by events, so also you may believe that those things which I now promise are about to come. A little later he adds. What those new things are, he testifies in the following discourse: instructing the Apostles and Apostolic men to sing a new song, by no means in the oldness of the letter, but in the newness of the Spirit. And not only in the Old Testament, but in the New, and his praise reaches even to the ends of the earth. For his going forth is from the highest heaven, and his circuit even to the end of it. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. Or according to the LXX, his name is glorified in the ends of the earth, and in the whole world the name of Christ is announced among the Gentiles.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

QUAE PRIMO FUERUNT, ECCE VENERUNT.) Loquitur E- saias quasi captivitati Babylonicae intersit. Videtis evenis- se, quae Ezechiae dixi de hac calamitate.

NOVA QUOQUE EGO ANNUNTIO) Liberationem fu- turam.

ANTEQUAM ORIANTUR) Antequam ulla existant ejus rei semina.

Verba non sunt Esaiae, sed Dei, qui ex iis, quae antea sive per Esaiam, seu per alios praedixerat, quae evenisse ipsi Judaei diffiteri non poterant, colligere- eos jubet, quod pariter nova, quae annunciat, ante- quam oriantur, eventura certo sint, maxime quae de Messiae beneficiis modo praedixerat, ideo jubentur statim canticum novum cantare, non Judaei tantum, sed omnes per terrarum orbem, quod beneficia illa obtingant toti humano generi. Proinde illa, NOVA QUOQUE EGO ANNUNCIO, temere restringuntur ad liberationem futuram e captivitate Babylonica, de qua nullo verbo hic a- ctum fuit. Recte autem haec παραφράζει Hiero- nymus. Quae prima fuerunt, ecce venerunt. Quae lo- quutus sum, quae per Mosen, Prophetasq; pollicitus sum, universa completa sunt. Nunc autem annuncio vo- bis Evangelium, vocationem gentium, passionem Christi, novitatem fidei, ut quomodo priora cernitis rebus expleta, sic & ea quae nunc polliceor, credatis esse ventura. Paulo post addit. Quae sint illa nova, se- quenti sermone testatur: Apostolicis praecipiens & Apo- stolicis viris, ut canant canticum novum nequaquam in vetustate literae, sed in novitate Spiritus. Nec solum in veteri Instrumento, sed in Novo, & laus ejus pene- trat usq; ad extrema terrae. A summo enim caelo e- gressus ejus, & usq; ad summum illius occursus ejus. In omnem terram exiit Apostolorum sonus, & in ter- minos orbis verba eorum. Sive juxta LXX. glorifi- catur nomen ejus in terminis terrae, & in universo mundo Christi nomen annunciatur in gentibus.

## 42:10
Vers. 10. SING TO THE LORD A NEW SONG) Thus it is said in great joys, as Psalm 33:3, 40:4.

HIS PRAISE FROM THE ENDS OF THE EARTH.) Supply: let it sound.

YOU WHO GO DOWN TO THE SEA, AND ITS FULLNESS.) That is, both sailors and passengers. He indicates the Tyrians, much vexed by the Babylonians. See what we said regarding Tyre besieged by the Nebuchadnezzars for 13 years in Book III of On the Truth of the Christian Religion. We see πληρώματα used for passengers also in Thucydides, Book VII, as the Scholiast notes there: and in Suidas πληρώματα are explained as οι επιβάται.

THE ISLANDS AND THEIR INHABITANTS.) We spoke above about the meaning of islands. He notes especially those who are by the Euphrates and the Tigris.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CANTATE DOMINO CANTICUM NOVUM) So- let id dici in magnis gaudiis, ut Psalm XXXIII. v. 3. XL. 4.

LAUS EJUS AB EXTREMIS TERRAE.) Supple, sonet.

QUI DESCENDITIS IN MARE, ET PLENITUDO EJUS.) Id est, & nautae & vectores. Tyrios indicat multum ve- xatos a Babyloniis. Vide quae de Tyro per Nabuchodo- nosorum obsessa per annos 13. diximus ad librum III. de Veritate Religionis Christianae. πληρώματα pro vecto- ribus etiam apud Thucydidem videmus libro VII. ut ibi notat Scholiastes: & apud Suidam πληρώματα exponuntur οι επιβάται.

INSULAE ET HABITATORES EARUM.) De insulae signi- ficatu supra diximus. Praecipue eos notat, qui sunt ad Euphratem & Tigrim.

## 42:11
Vers. 11.

LET THE DESERT BE LIFTED UP AND ITS INHABITANTS.) Let the Idumeans rejoice, living by the Red Sea, who were enemies of the Medes and were treated badly by the Medes. See what we said at chapter 21.

CEDAR SHALL DWELL IN HOUSES) That is: And you, who dwell in tents, the Scenite Arabs: for these too had been of the same party: see the place just now indicated.

LET THE INHABITANTS OF THE ROCK PRAISE, FROM THE TOP OF THE MOUNTAINS THEY SHALL SHOUT.) That is, even those who are in Arabia Petraea will rejoice greatly about this matter. And deservedly, for these too had been enemies of the Medes.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

SUBLEVETUR DESERTUM ET HABITATORES EJUS.) Gaudeant Idumaei, ad sinum Rubrum habitantes, qui Me- dorum hostes, & a Medis male tractati fuerunt. Vide quae diximus ad cap. 21.

IN DOMIBUS HABITABIT CEDAR) Id est: Et vos, qui tentoria habitatis, Arabes Σκηνῖται: nam & hi earundem fuerant partium: vide locum jamjam indicatum.

LAUDATE HABITATORES PETRAE, DE VERTICE MON- TIUM CLAMABUNT.) Id est, etiam illi, qui in Arabia sunt Petraea, plurimum de hac re gaudebunt. Et merito, nam & hi Medorum hostes fuerant.

## 42:12
Vers. 12. THEY SHALL GIVE GLORY TO THE LORD) Let those Arabs, freed from such great evil, attribute glory to God.

AND THEY SHALL ANNOUNCE HIS PRAISE IN THE ISLANDS.) Let them announce these works of God in all distant shores.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PONENT DOMINO GLORIAM) Tribuant Deo gloriam Arabes isti a tanto malo liberati.

ET LAUDEM EJUS IN INSULIS NUNTIABUNT.) Nun- tient haec Dei opera in omnibus oris longinquis.

## 42:13
Vers. 13.

HE SHALL STIR UP ZEAL) That is, he will be driven against the enemies with great ardor.

HE SHALL SHOUT AND CRY OUT) He shall utter a war cry. For all these things are taken from military matters.

HE SHALL PREVAIL OVER HIS ENEMIES) Well said: He shall prevail over his enemies. The Prophet persists in the same comparison.

Grotius restricts this song to bodily liberation and the Tyrians besieged for 13 years by the Babylonians, and some others liberated from their enemies. But just as those benefits are not bodily, but spiritual, so in the preceding things which the Prophet wrote concerning the servant and chosen of GOD, he shall bring forth judgment to the nations, and kindly treat the wretched, whose doctrine the islands await, who has been set for a covenant of the people and for a light to the nations, and the Canticle, with which he now commands God to be celebrated for those benefits, so that his praises may reach to the ends of the earth, can by no means be restricted to a bodily liberation, but concern spiritual salvation. is accustomed to designate such odes by the name of a new Canticle, which are sung for the benefits of the Messiah, which is proper to such hymns, provided they concern the new grace which pertains to the new covenant, unless you prefer that the word 'new' be opposed to the common, and be called 'new' from the object, because it celebrates the incomparable grace of God which is exhibited in Christ. Thus in Ps. 88, 1.3. the Psalmist commands a new canticle to be sung, when he treats of the salvation of the Lord being made manifest to all the ends of the earth: nor does he less celebrate God with a new Canticle in Ps. 149, 1. when he describes the Messiah as King in Zion. Thus when he exhorts to a new Canticle in Ps. 33, 3. he sings especially of the gracious election of the people, whom God had taken as his own possession, ver. 2. nor does David present any other subject matter for the new canticle, with which the Messiah himself celebrates God in Ps. 40, 4. than that those who place their trust in his merit and love the salvation of the Lord may be filled with blessedness and joy, ver. 4, 5, and 17. Nor indeed does this new Canticle pertain only to particular peoples, or belong only to the Tyrians, and those who are by the Euphrates and the Tigris, and the Idumeans and Arabs, who were treated badly by the Babylonians or Medes: but it is to be sung by all throughout the whole world: therefore the Prophet commands to sing first indefinitely, while he demands that the praise of the Lord come from the ends of the earth: so that the nations, even those most far removed, may celebrate the name of the Lord. Furthermore, they are commanded to praise the Lord, who go down (in ships) into the sea, and the fullness thereof, that is, as the epexegesis subjoined declares, the islands, or the inhabitants thereof. Which are wrongly restricted to the Tyrians, and those dwelling by the Euphrates and the Tigris, since no one can fail to see that they extend more widely, and reach to any islands whatsoever: so that not only on the land even to its ends and boundaries is the praise of the Lord celebrated, but also in the islands. Therefore mention is made again of the desert lands, because they too are to celebrate the Lord, and of the islands, ver. 11, 12. Let the desert and its cities and the villages in which Kedar dwells (he understands the Arabs, who trace their origin from Kedar the son of Ishmael, dwelling not in cities but in villages and tents, so that it may be indicated that even barbarous and wild and rapacious men will acknowledge and celebrate God) lift up (their voice), let those dwelling in the rocks rejoice, let them shout from the tops of the mountains, and therefore they are called to the praise of the Lord, who dwell in the continent or the islands, in the desert or in cities, villages and tents, or in fortresses situated on rocks and mountains: so that all men everywhere may celebrate the name of the Lord, or celebrate the glory of the Lord, not only the Arabs, but all kinds of men, and announce his praise even in the islands of the sea. More correctly therefore than Grotius, Calvin on ver. 11: Since the Prophet comprehends all parts of the world, he names those especially which were better known to the Jews. For Judea had the sea on the west, and the desert and Arabia on the east. For when he speaks of the tents of Kedar, the desert and the rocks, he designates Arabia, but it is a synecdoche, by which he comprehends the whole east. It is therefore the same as if he said: From the rising of the sun even to its setting these praises are to be heard: since everywhere the Lord will be worshipped, whereas before he was worshipped only in Judea. Thus the state of affairs will be changed, and that praise will be heard in the ends of the earth. Cyril explained the matter very well.

Prophets, when they weave together discourses about the coming of our Savior, for the most part make mention of the calling of the Gentiles. For, as I said, CHRIST was the expectation of the Gentiles. However, they do not absolutely introduce discourses about such matters to everyone, that is, to the nations and peoples throughout the whole world. For it was not likely, when an innumerable multitude filled the world, that they would have wished to speak so subtly and minutely as to make mention of all by name and individually, but by taking the regions neighboring Judea, which were most addicted to idolatry, and saying that they would be called in their own time, they demonstrated the whole by a part. Therefore, since the wide wilderness bordering the Jewish land, situated to the South, which the nations of the Saracens and Arabs occupied, was there, he says that those who dwell in it will at some time obtain grace and salvation through Christ. The names also of the villages or small towns, which are, I say, in the wilderness, are villages, and Kedar: and Petra, which is in Arabia, and is situated to this day, and so named. These of whom there is speech are most superstitious, as I said, namely the inhabitants of these places, and they have fallen entirely into apostasy and defection from GOD, as those who worshipped impure spirits. That these things are to be understood of Christ the Lord, both the preceding things teach, because God the Father speaks and exhorts that a new canticle be sung to the Lord, that they may exclaim from every side with a joyful voice to their Savior Christ, and praise him throughout the whole world. For the Lord speaks of the Lord: God the Father of the Messiah Lord, whose glory was to be manifested to the world, and celebrated everywhere in the N. Testament. Then the following things, by which the subject matter of the new song and the cause of singing the same is exhibited, v. 13. The Lord as a strong man, or rather as a Hero, will go forth to enter into battle with his enemies, as a man of war he will stir up Zeal, i.e., he will excite himself to fervor of spirit, so that he may take vengeance upon them with great severity: he will sound with his voice, and will shout after the manner of those who enter into battle, he will be strengthened over his enemies, i.e., he will be superior, and will carry off the victory. Which is a spiritual battle, which he fought against Satan, death, and sin, Heb. 2, 14. Col. 2, 15. by the power of which through the preaching of the Gospel he overcomes the whole world, and breaks through with all tyrants unwilling, and dissipates the obstacles which delay the course of the Gospel. For God does not attack all on the continent and the islands of the sea with external and corporal weapons, nor does the material or argument for celebration arise from that, but rather for mourning and sorrow, since everything resounds with weapons: and who will be left to celebrate the Lord for liberation, if all are oppressed by external weapons!

Latin:

Vers. 13.

SUSCITABIT ZELUM) Id est, magno ardore agetur in hostes.

VOCIFERABITUR ET CLAMABIT) Barritum edet. O- mnia enim haec sumta sunt de re militari.

SUPER INIMICOS SUOS CONFORTABITUR) Bene ver- tas: Praevalebit hostibus. Persistit Propheta in eadem com- paratione.

Restringit Grotius hoc canticum ad libera- tionem corporalem & Tyrios per 13. annos a Baby- loniis obsessos, aliosq; nonnullos ab hostibus suis liberatos. At quemadmodum beneficia illa non corporalia, sed spiritualia sunt, ita in praecedenti- bus quae scripsit Propheta de servo & electo DEI judicium gentibus prolaturº, & benigne miseros tractaturo, cujus doctrinam insulæ expe- ctant, qui in fœdus populi & in lucem gentium posi- tus est, & Canticum,quo celebrare nunc Deum ju- bet, ob ista beneficia, ut laudes ejus ad extrema ter- ræ pertingant,neutiquam ad corporalem liberatio- nem restringi possunt, sed spiritualem concernunt salutem. Et solet Scriptura S. ejusmodi odas no- mine Cantici novi designare,quæ ob beneficia Mes- siæ decantantur,quod talib9 hymnis proprium est, siquidem novam gratiam, quæ ad fœdus novum pertinet, concernant, nisi malis τὸ novum vulgari opponi, & ab objecto novum dici,quod incompa- rabilem Dei gratiam celebret,quę in Christo exhi- betur. Ita Ps. 88, 1.3. cantare jubet canticum novum Hiero-psaltes, cum de salute Domini omnibus ter- ræ finibus manifestanda agit: nec minus celebrat Deum novo Cantico Psal. 149, 1. cum Regem in Zion Messiam describit. Ita cum hortatur ad no- vum Canticum Psal. 33, 3. gratiosam imprimis po- puli electionem, quem Deus in peculium assumse- rat,decantat,vers.2. neq; aliam materiam novi can- tici, quo Messias ipse Deum celebrat Ps. 40,4. sistit David, quam quod in ipsius meritum fiduciam col- locantes & salutem Domini amantes beatitudine ac gaudio perfundantur vers. 4. 5. & 17. Neque ve- ro ad particulares tantum populos pertinet hoc Canticum novum, aut Tyriorum solum est, & eorum, qui ad Euphratem ac Tygrim sunt, atque Idumæorum & Arabum, qui à Babyloniis vel Me- dis male tractati sunt: sed ab omnibus decantan- dum est per universum orbem: ideo indefinite pri- mum cantare jubet Propheta, dum postulat, ut laus Domini ab extremis terræ veniat: ut gentes, etiam longissime remotæ, nomen Domini cele- brent. Porro laudare jubentur Dominum, qui descendunt (navibus) in mare, & plenitudo ejus, hoc est, ut κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν subjunctam declarat, in- sulæ, vel habitatores earum. Quæ perperam restrin- guntur ad Tyrios, & habitantes ad Euphratem & Tygrim, cum nemo non videat latius ea patere, & ad insulas quasvis se extendere: ut non tantum in terra usq; ad fines & terminos ejusdem, laus Do- mini celebretur, sed & in insulis. Ideo denuo ter- rarum desertarum mentio fit, quod & illæ celebra- turæ sint Dominum, atque insularum vers. 11. 12. Attollunt (vocem suam) desertum & civitates ejus & pagi, in quibus habitat Cedar (Arabes intelligit, qui à Cedar filio Ismaelis originem ducunt, non in urbibus,sed in villis & tentoriis habitantes, ut indi- cetur barbaros etiam homines ac feros atque rapa- ces Deum agnituros ac celebraturos) habitantes in petris jubilent, de verticibus montium acclament, ideoque convocantur ad laudem Domini, qui in terra continente vel insulis, in deserto vel civitatibus, pagis & tentoriis, vel in arcibus sitis in petris ac mon- tibus habitant: ut omnes ubiq; homines celebrent nomen Domini, vel celebrent Domini gloriam non Arabes tantum, sed omnium hominum gene- ra, laudemque ejus in insulis etiam maris nuncient. Rectius ergo Grotio Calvinus ad vers. 11. Cum Pro- pheta omnis orbis partes comprehendat, eas præcipue nominat, quæ magis notæ Judæis erant. Nam ab occidente Judæa mare habuit, ab oriente de- sertum & Arabiam. Cum enim loquitur de tentoriis Cedar, deserto & rupibus, Arabiam designat, sed est Synecdoche, qua totum orientem comprehendit. Perinde igitur est, ac si diceret. A Solis ortu ad occasum usq́ audiendas esse has laudes: quoniam ubiq́ coletur Dominus, cum antea in Judæa tantum coleretur. Itaq́ immutabitur rerum status, atque in extremi terræ partibus laus ista audietur. Optime vero rem exposuit Cyrillus.

phetæ cum Sermones de adventu Servatoris nostri contexunt, plerumque mentionem faciunt vocationis gentium. Erat enim, uti dixi, expectatio gentium CHRISTUS. Cæterum de rebus ejusmodi non omnibus absolute sermones injiciunt, per universum sc. orbem gentibus & populis. Non enim verisimile erat, cum innumerabilis multitudo orbem terræ im- pleret, adeo subtiliter & minutim voluisse dicere, ut omnium nominatim & sigillatim facerent mentio- nem, sed regionibus accolis Judææ sumptis, idololatriæ deditissimis, quin illas vocandas suo tempore dicerent, ex parte totum demonstrabant. Itaque cum esset fini- tima Judaicæ terræ solitudo lata, ad Austrum sita, quam occuparunt Sarracenorum & Arabum gentes: dicit eos, qui in ea habitant, gratiam & salutem per Christum aliquando consequuturos. Nomina etiam vicis seu oppidulis, quæ sunt, inquam, in solitudine, sunt villæ, & Cedar: & Petra, quæ in Arabia, hodieque sita est, & sic nominata. Superstitiosissimi sunt, ut dixi, hi, de quibus sermo est, nimirum horum locorum incolæ, & in totum prolapsi sunt in apostasian & defe- ctionem à DEO, ut qui impuros spiritus coluerunt. Quæ de Christo Domino intelligenda esse, tum an- tecedentia docent, quia Deus Pater loquitur & hor- tatur, ut Domino novum cantetur canticum, ut ex- clament undiquaque læta voce Salvatori suo Chri- sto, eumque per totum orbem laudent. Loquitur enim Dominus de Domino: Deus Pater de Mes- sia Domino, cujus gloria orbi manifestanda, & ubi- que celebranda erat in N. Test. Tum consequentia, quibus materia carminis novi & causa decantandi ejusdem exhibetur v. 13. Dominus sicut fortis, vel potius ut Heros egredietur, ad ineundum prælium cum hostibus, sicut vir præliator suscitabit Zelum, i. e. excitabit se ad fervorem animi, ut magna seve- ritate ultionem ab iis capiat: voce sonabit, & cla- mabit eorum more, qui prælium ineunt, super ini- micos suos confortabitur, h. e. superior erit, & vi- ctoriam reportabit. Quæ pugna spiritualis est, quam adversus Satanam, mortem, & peccatum de- pugnavit Eb. 2, 14. Col. 2, 15. vi cujus per prædica- tionem Evangelii superat omnem orbem terra- rum, & perrumpit invitis omnibus tyrannis, atque dissipat obstacula, quæ cursum Evangelii remoran- tur. Nam armis externis & corporalibus non ag- greditur Deus omnes in terra continenti, & maris insulis, nec inde materia vel argumentum celebra- tionis, sed potius luctus & doloris oritur, cum omnia armis perstrepunt: & quis relinquetur, qui ob liberationem celebret Dominum: si omnes ar- mis externis opprimantur!

## 42:14
Vers. 14. I HAVE ALWAYS HELD MY PEACE, I HAVE BEEN STILL, I HAVE BEEN PATIENT LIKE A WOMAN IN LABOR) Saying, namely: (for this verb is often understood here and elsewhere) I have long restrained my anger, like the breath of women in labor.

I WILL SPEAK) I will cry out, as women in labor are sometimes compelled to do because of the pain.

I WILL LAY WASTE AND SWALLOW UP AT ONCE) I will desolate the lands, I will swallow up the men.

Latin:

Vers. 14. TACUI SEMPER, SILUI, PATIENS FUI SICUT PARTURIENS) Dicens scilicet: (nam hoc verbum hic & alibi sæpe subauditur) Diu continui iram meam, sicut ha- litum fœminæ parturientes.

LOQUAR) Clamabo, ut feminæ parturientes interdum præ dolore facere coguntur.

DISSIPABO ET ABSORBEBO SIMUL) Desolabo terras, absorbebo homines.

## 42:15
Vers. 15. I WILL MAKE WASTE THE MOUNTAINS AND HILLS) In which cities are for the most part situated.

AND ALL THEIR GRASS I WILL DRY UP.) That is, I will take away the citizens. The Hebrews love metaphors.

AND I WILL MAKE THE RIVERS ISLANDS AND WILL DRY UP THE POOLS.) Nothing is more true: for Cyrus made the Euphrates itself passable for himself. See what we said in Book III of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Indeed, nothing more diluted and alien to the mind of the Prophet could have been said here. Not only are certain cities situated on mountains and hills, but in the manner of Scripture, any kingdoms opposing themselves to Christ are designated, the more powerful by mountains, the less powerful by hills. The Lord is said to be about to take away all their grass, which is their adornment and all their majesty, because the sprouts of the mountains and hills are, he will strip away, so that at length they may perish as if they were dry grass, and he will bring it about that rivers become islands, that is, dry land, and that pools also be dried up, which, as they are by no means to be understood concerning an external war, so they are wrongly taken concerning external devastation and drying up. For since the discourse here is held concerning the spreading of the kingdom of Christ through the Gospel into the whole world, among all nations, therefore such a devastation of nations, mountains, and rivers is to be understood as corresponds to the Gospel of Christ, namely, that the Gospel will spread by the power of Christ through the whole world, through sea, through lands, through mountains and hills. The Kings and Princes of this world will indeed resist, but no King is so powerful, no mountain is so high, no sea is so deep, that it can impede the course of the Gospel.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DESERTOS FACIAM MONTES ET COLLES) In quibus plerumque sitæ sunt urbes.

ET OMNE GRAMEN EORUM EXSIC.) Id est, cives auferam. Amant Hebræi metaphoras.

ET PONAM FLUMINA IN INSULAS ET STAGNA ARE- FACIAM.) Nihil verius: Nam ipsum Euphratem pervium sibi fecit Cyrus. Vid. quæ diximus ad lib. III. de Verit. Relig. Christian.

Imo nihil magis dilutum atque alienum à men- te Prophetæ hic dici poterat. Non tantum urbes certæ in montibus & collibus sitæ, sed more Scri- pturæ regna quævis sese Christo opponentia defi- gnantur, potentiora per montes, minus potentiora per colles. Omne gramen eorum ablaturus dici- tur Dominus, quod ornatum atque majestatem omnem, quia germina montium & collium orna- tus sunt, detracturus sit, ut tandem quasi aridæ her- bæ pereant, atque effecturus, ut flumina fiant insulæ, h. e. terra arida, & ut Stagna quoq; exsiccentur, quæ uti neutiquam de bello externo intelligenda sunt, ita perperam de externa vastatione & exsiccatione accipiuntur. Quum enim concio hic habeatur de divulgando regno Christi per Evangelium in totum terrarum orbem, inter omnes gentes, idcir- co intelligenda talis gentium, montium & flumi- num vastatio, qualis Evangelio Christi congruit, videlicet, quod Evangelium pervagabitur potentia Christi totum orbem per mare per terras, per montes & colles. Obsistent quidem Reges & Prin- cipes hujus mundi, sed nullus Rex tam potens est, nullus mons tam altus est, nullum mare tam pro- fundum est, quod cursum Evangelii impedire queat.

## 42:16
Vers. 16.

AND I WILL LEAD THE BLIND INTO THE WAY, WHICH THEY DO NOT KNOW.) I will lead the Jews back home, who had hoped for nothing less.

I WILL TURN THEIR DARKNESS INTO LIGHT, AND CROOKED THINGS INTO STRAIGHT,) I will change adverse things into favorable, and I will render all things which seem most difficult to them, most easy.

THESE WORDS I HAVE DONE FOR THEM) Better: These things I will effect for them.

AND I HAVE NOT FORSAKEN THEM) For I will not forsake them.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET DVCAM COECOS IN VIAM, QVAM NE- SCIVNT.) Judæos domum reducam, qui nihil minus speraverant.

PONAM TENEBRAS EORVM EIS IN LVCEM, ET PRAVA IN RECTA,) Mutabo adversa secundis, & omnia eis quæ difficillima videntur, reddam facillima.

HÆC VERBA FECI EIS) Melius: Has res effi- ciam eis.

ET NON DERELIQVI EOS) Neque enim eos dere- linquam.

## 42:17
Vers. 17. THEY ARE TURNED BACK) Those Babylonians will flee. See the other fulfillment in John 15, verse 16.

LET THEM BE CONFOUNDED) They shall be confounded, that is, they shall be put to shame.

That the Prophet is here prophesying about the reduction of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity is supported by no evidence. All the things above have shown that the times of the New Testament are being regarded. Nor are these things said about the Jews, but about the nations. It is only later that the Jews are dealt with, when they are introduced as blind and deaf, who have not known how to walk in the ways of the Lord. And it has been demonstrated thus far that the discourse is not about bodily benefits, but spiritual ones. Such as were the blind, to whom the Messiah opened their eyes in verse 7, such also are the blind here to be led into the way. As he is called the light of the nations there because of spiritual illumination; so now spiritual illumination is promised, when darkness is to be turned into light. All men are by nature blind and do not know how one must escape from injustice to justice, from death to life, from hell to heaven. However, as many as receive the Gospel by faith become seeing from blind, so that they may walk the way which they previously did not know, and so that the darkness may be illuminated for them, and so that those things which were crooked may become straight. The illumination of the mind through the acknowledgment of the truth, and the conversion of the crooked will through sanctification, must necessarily be brought about by the Holy Spirit. Although if we attend to the emphasis of the word לפניהם before them, the phrase is to be explained not concerning darkness in the mind, but in the way: that he will bring it about that whatever is dark in the way may be illuminated before them, and that those things which are crooked may turn out straight, so that neither the internal blindness of the mind, nor external darkness, or the obliquity and crookedness of the way may be an impediment to them, so that they are not led to Christ, and to true justice and life. For God through the Gospel illuminates the blind, so that they may find the way which leads straight to heaven: and he shows them the path in which, walking, they rightly worship God. And he dispels the darkness of ignorance and errors, and directs all things to their salvation in such a way that even that dark and impeded and curved way, through various afflictions, indeed, and through death itself, may be luminous to those walking, and expedited and direct to eternal life. Therefore the Lord adds: These words I have done for them, or rather (so Grotius amends) these things I will effect for him. These benefits I will confer upon the nations, namely, those who will receive the Gospel. Nor will I forsake them. Concerning the others also, who persist in their old impiety and idolatry while despising the Gospel, he says, THEY ARE TURNED BACK, LET THEM BE CONFOUNDED. Grotius understands this concerning the Babylonians who are about to take to flight. But that they are specifically dealt with here is a matter of dispute, and is not proven by Grotius. It is a general threat made to idolaters, who trust in a graven image, who say to a molten image, you are our Gods. They are said to be turned back because they turn their back to the Lord, and prefer to persist in their impiety than to be converted to him, and although they hear the Gospel, they nevertheless retreat, and they shall be put to shame with perpetual confusion.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONVERSI SVNT RETRORSVM) Fu- gient illi Babylonii. Vide implementum alterum Johan. 15. vers. 16.

CONFVNDANTVR) Confundentur, id est, pude- fient.

De reductione Judæorum è captivitate Babylo- nica hic vaticinari Prophetam, nullo indicio con- stat. Tempora N. T. respici superiora omnia do- cuêre. Neque de Judæis, sed de gentibus ista di- cuntur. Tam de Judæis postea agitur, cum ut cœ- ci & surdi introducuntur, qui non noverint in viis Domini ambulare. Nec de beneficiis corporali- bus, sed Spiritualibus sermonem esse, hactenus de- monstratum. Quales erant cœci, quib9 oculos ape- ruit Messias v. 7. tales etiam cœci hic in viam de- ducendi. Ut lux gentium dictus illic ob spiritua- lem illuminationem; ita nunc illuminatio spiritua- lis promittitur, cum tenebræ in lucem ponendæ sint. Omnes homines sunt natura cœci & nesciunt, qua sit evadendum ab injustitia ad justitiam, ex morte ad vitam, ex inferno ad cœlum. Quotquot autem Evangelium fide accipiunt, fiunt ex cœcis videntes, ut viam, quam antea ignoraverunt, ambu- lent, & ut tenebrę eis illustrentur, ac ut ea quę erant prava, fiant recta. Illustratio mentis per veritatis agnitionem, conversio pravæ voluntatis per sancti- ficationem, per S. S. fiant necessum est. Quamvis si emphasin vocis לפניהם ante eos attendamus, non de tenebris in mente, sed in via, phrasis explicanda: quod effecturus sit, ut quicquid in via tenebrico- sum est, coram illis illuminetur, & quæ prava sunt recta evadant, ut nec cœcitas mentis interna, nec tenebræ exteriores, aut viæ obliquitas & pravitas ipfis impedimento sit, quo minus perducantur ad Christum, & ad veram justitiam & vitam. Deus enim per Evangelium illuminat cœcos, ut inveni- ant viam, quæ recta ducit ad cœlum: monstratque illis semitam, in qua ambulantes Deum recte co- lunt. Et ignorantiæ atque errorum tenebras dis- pellit, atque omnia ad ipsorum salutem ita dirigit, ut etiam tenebricosa illa & impedita ac curva via per afflictiones nimirum varias, & per mortem ipsam ambulantibus lucida sit, & expedita atque directa ad vitam æternam. Ideo subjicit Domi- nus: Hæc verba feci eis, vel potius (ita emendat Grotius) has res efficiam ejus. Hæc beneficia confe- ram in gentes, eos sc. qui Evangelium accipient. Nec derelinquam eos. De cæteris etiam, qui per- durant contempto Evangelio in veteri sua impie- tate, & idololatria, CONVERSI, inquit, SUNT RETRORSUM, CONFUNDANTUR. Gro- tius de Babyloniis fugam arrepturis intelligit. Sed de illis in specie hic agi, κρινόμενον est, nec proba- tur à Grotio. Generalis est comminatio idolola- tris facta, qui confidunt in sculptili, qui dicunt confla- tili, vos Dii nostri. Conversi retrorsum dicuntur, quod tergum obvertant Domino, & in impietate sua persistere malint, quam ad ipsum converti, & quamvis audiant Evangelium, tamen retrocedant, qui pudefient perpetua confusione.

## 42:18
Vers. 18. DEAF ONES HEAR, AND BLIND ONES LOOK UP TO SEE.) He addresses the nations, as above in chapter 7.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SVRDI AVDITE, ET COECI INTUEMINI AD VIDENDVM.) Gentes alloquitur, ut supra 7.

## 42:19
Vers. 19. WHO IS BLIND BUT MY SERVANT.) The sense is: although why do I rebuke the nations, when no one among them is blinder than many Hebrews after so many and such conspicuous benefits of God.

AND DEAF BUT HE TO WHOM I SENT MY MESSENGERS.) In the Hebrew: messenger: i.e., Isaiah, to whose many threats and promises a great part of the people became no better.

He refers the former words, 'deaf ones hear,' to the nations along with the Jews, whom Jerome declares it a foolish interpretation to contend that they pertain to the people of the nations. Cyril judges that the discourse had already been instituted concerning the Jews in the preceding verse. He very opportunely transfers the discourse to the Jewish nation, who, although they had the law of Moses, leading them by the hand to the recognition of the law, and so that they might wish to accomplish those things in which it was likely they would obtain praise: they lapsed into apostasy, and having slipped into the pit of the worship of many gods, they descended into the abyss of destruction: whence also not without cause did they offend God, who bestowed upon them every mercy and benevolence. Since therefore the discourse had previously proclaimed that the nations were to be called in their own time, and that they would tread paths they had not known, and that darkness would be turned into light and crooked things into straight: he uncovers the rudeness of those who arose from the Israelite blood, saying: 'They themselves, however, have turned backward.' That word, 'themselves,' must be taken emphatically, namely those who were instructed by the divine law, and were subject to my hand, and had Moses as a mediator. Others more correctly believe that the Jews are being addressed, not the nations, because the Lord subsequently rebukes the Jews as deaf and blind. But if we should even admit that the discourse is to the nations, so that they, namely, who were previously deaf, might hear with wonder: and the blind might see, being stripped, nevertheless neither the nations nor the Hebrews of that time are being looked at, nor is Isaiah precisely designated by the messenger; but just as the preceding things concerned the times of the New Testament, so also this discourse is about the stupendous blindness in the Jewish people of those who were considered servants and messengers of God, the Chief Priests, Pharisees, and Scribes in the time of Christ. For the Prophet had said that at the time when the Messiah is to come, it will be thus concerning the nations: Now therefore he explains what is to be concerning the Jews, who, since they are about to reject Christ, are in turn to be rejected themselves, so that they may no longer be the people of God. Some have indeed accepted these things as reproaches with which either Isaiah or Christ was afflicted by the impious Jews, as if they were blind or deaf. But it is not necessary that we understand these things from the mind of the blind and deaf calumniators, since the Holy Scripture itself seems to ask not without sorrow and detestation: Who is more blind than my servant, who is more deaf than the messenger whom I sent? Indeed, since the continuity of the text teaches that the times of the New Testament are being looked to, in which Christ was set as a light to the nations, and thus the words can be explained concerning the blindness and deafness of the Jews, the Chief Priests, Priests, and Pharisees, as if to say: the chief priests are my servants, whom I have appointed, that they may serve my Church in teaching the true religion: Priests are my messengers, whom I have ordained, that they may explain my law to the people; the Pharisees are the perfect, i.e., they profess perfection both in doctrine and in their manner of life. But no one is more blind than they, more deaf than they. They ought to have been the first who acknowledged Christ the covenant of the people, but behold there is no nation which less hears or admits Christ, less sees or acknowledges the truth of the Gospel, just as Christ objected to the Pharisees, if you were blind, i.e., if you acknowledged your blindness, you would not have sin. But now you say we see Joh. 9, 41. therefore the things which the Prophet had predicted concerning future blindness & deafness, Christ applies to none other than the Jews, and especially among these the Pharisees and Priests Joh. 12, 40. and the Apostle Act. 28, 26. Conf. Roman. 2, 19. seqq. Thus ours, B. Brentius, Osiander, Pappus, as also B. Luther: who in the words: You who see many things, will you not keep watch? observes the office of the Prophets and Doctors. To see signifies to teach, to preach. Hence those who see i.e. Prophets. Which Grotius thus renders and interprets from the Hebrew: By seeing many things you do not observe. You have seen many miracles and have not cared. These things also apply especially to the Pharisees and priests. More specifically, however, the Doctors, who were called those who see, and were set in the watchtower of the Lord, seem to be designated. And thus also the other phrase can be accepted; he who has open ears: For thus the Prophets were described as hearers of the words of GOD. Num. 24, 16. and such the Pharisees boasted themselves to be.

On the same Verse.

WHO IS BLIND BUT HE WHO HAS BEEN SOLD.) This Interpreter reads here not מְשֻׁלָּם, but מָשְׁכָר, the Greeks מְשַׁלְטָן οἱ κυριεύοντες ἀυτῶν. The reading received in the Hebrew is not bad, if you translate: as one in covenant: namely the Israelite people of God. The Mahometans in the same sense, although falsely, call themselves Mussulmans.

Latin:

Vers. 19. QVIS COECVS NISI SERVUS MEVS.) Sensus est: quanquam quid gentes objurgo, cùm nemo sit inter eas cæcior, quam multi Hebræi post tot & tam con- spicua Dei beneficia.

ET SVRDVS NISI AD QVEM NVNTIOS MEOS MISI.) In Hebræo: nuntium: i. e. Esaiam, ad cujus tot mi- nas & promissa magna pars populi nihilo fiebat melior.

Verba priora, surdi audite, ad gentes refert cum Judæis, quos ad gentium populum ea pertinere stulta interpretatione contendere Hieronymus pro- nunciat. Cyrillus versu præcedente jam de Judæis orationem institutam esse censet. Tempestive ad- modum transfert orationem ad gentem judaicam, qui cum legem haberent Mosis, manu ducentem ad le- gis agnitionem, & ut velint perficere ea, in quibus lau- dem eos consequuturos verisimile erat: lapsi sunt in apostasiam, & in multorum numinum cultus puteum illapsi, in barathrum exitii descenderunt: unde & non sine causa Deum, qui omnem ipsis & misericordiam & benevolentiam tribuit, offenderunt. Cum ergo ante oratio prædicasset, vocandas gentes suo tempore, & calcaturas, quas non noverunt vias, & tenebras in lucem, & obliqua in recta versum iri: ruditatem eo- rum, qui ex sanguine Israëlitico orti sunt, retegit, di- cens: Ipsi vero conversi sunt retrorsum. Illud, ipsi, sumendum est emphatice, nimirum qui divina lege instituti sunt, & manui meæ subditi sunt, & seque- strem Mosem habuerunt. Rectius alii Judæos com- pellari credunt, non gentes, quia Judæos ceu surdos & cæcos deinceps redarguit Dominus. Sed si maxi- me admittamus orationem ad gentes, ut illę sc. cum admiratione audiant, quæ surdæ prius fuêre: ac cæ- ci videant, diripi, non tamen vel gentes vel Ebræi istius temporis spectantur, aut per nuncium præci- se Esaias designatur; sed uti superiora concerne- bant tempora Novi Testam. sic etiam de stupenda cæcitate in populo Judaico eorum, qui servi, & nuntii Dei habebantur, Pontificum, Pharisæorum & Scribarum tempore Christi hic sermo est. Dixe- rat nempe Propheta, quod eo tempore, quo ven- turus est Messias, de gentibus futurum sit: Nunc ergo exponit, quod de Judæis, qui cum Christum abjecturi sint, abjiciendi vicissim & ipsi sint, ne am- plius sint populus Dei. Accepere quidem ista non- nulli ceu opprobria, quibus vel Esaias vel Christus ab impiis Judæis affectus est, ac si cæci, surdive es- sent. Sed non est necesse, ut hæc ex mente calu- mniatorum cæcorum & surdorum intelligamus, quum videatur ipse S.S. non absque dolore ac de- testatione quærere: Quis magis cæcus, quam servus meus, quis magis surdus quam nuncius, quem misi? si- quidem συνέχεια textus doceat, tempora Nov. T. respici, quibus Christus positus est in lucem gen- tium, adeoque verba explicari possint de cæcitate ac surditate Judæorum, Pontificum, Sacerdotum & Pharisæorum, q. d. pontifices sunt servi mei, quos constitui, ut serviant Ecclesiæ meæ in docenda vera religione: Sacerdotes sunt nuncii mei, quos ordi- navi, ut explicent populo legem meam; Pharisæi sunt perfecti, h. e. profitentur tam in doctrina quam in genere vitæ suæ perfectionem. Sed ne- mo est iis magis cæcus, iis magis surdus. Debuis- sent primi esse, qui agnovissent Christum fœdus populi, sed ecce non est gens, quæ minus audiat vel admittat Christum, minus videat vel agnoscat Ev- angelii veritatem, sicut Christus Pharisæis objecit, si cæci essetis, h. e. cæcitatem vestram agnoscere- tis, non haberetis peccatum. Nunc vero dicitis videmus Joh. 9, 41. ideo quæ de cæcitate & surdi- tate futura prædixerat Propheta, non aliis quam Judæis, & præcipue inter hos Pharisæis & Sacerdo- tibus applicat Christus Joh. 12, 40. & Apostolus Act. 28, 26. Conf. Roman. 2, 19. seqq. Sic nostri, B. Brentius, Osiander, Pappus, ut & B. Lutherus: qui in verbis: Qui vides multa, nonne custodies? observat Prophetarum & Doctorum officium. Videre si- gnificat docere, prædicare. Hinc videntes i. e. Pro- phetæ. Quæ ita ex Ebræo reddit & interpreta- tur Grotius: Videndo multa non observas. Vidistis multa miracula & non curastis. Hæc apprime etiam Pharisæis & sacerdotibus conveniunt. Spe- cialius tamen Doctores, qui videntes dicebantur, & in specula Domini constituti erant, designari vi- dentur. Atque ita etiam accipi potest altera æfi- φεασις; qui apertas habet aures: Nam ita Prophe- tæ describebantur ceu auditores sermonum DEI. Num. 24, 16. & tales se jactabant Pharisæi.

Eodem Vers.

QUIS CŒCUS NISI QUI VENUNDATUS EST.) Legit hic Interpres non מְשֻׁלָּם, sed מָשְׁכָר Græci מְשַׁלְטָן οἱ κυριεύοντες ἀυτῶν. Lectio in Hebræo recepta non mala est, si vertas: sicut fœderatus: nempe Dei populus Israëliticus. Mahumetistæ eodem sensu, quanquam falso, se appellant Mussulmannos.

## 42:20
YOU WHO SEE MANY THINGS, WILL YOU NOT KEEP WATCH?) From the Hebrew: By seeing many things you do not observe. You have seen many miracles and do not care.

YOU HAVE OPEN EARS, WILL YOU NOT HEAR?) In the Hebrew: He who has open ears, will he not hear? That is, ought he not to hear? To whom the voices of the Law and the Prophets have sounded for so long, was it not his duty to admit them into his mind? for to hear here is to be understood as concerning the attention of the mind, as Matth. 11, 15. and elsewhere.

Latin:

QUI VIDES MULTA, NONNE CUSTODIES) Ex Hebræo: Videndo multa non observas. Vidistis multa miracula & non curatis.

APERTAS HABES AURES, NONNE AVDIES?) In Hebræo: Qui apertas habet aures, nonne audiet? Id est, audire debet? Cui tamdiu insonuêre Legis & Prophe- tarum voces, nonne ejus fuit illas in animum admittere? nam audire hic de mentis attentione accipiendum, ut Matth. 11, 15. & alibi.

## 42:21
Verse 21. AND THE LORD WILLED, THAT HE MIGHT SANCTIFY HIM, AND MAGNIFY THE LAW, AND EXALT) You may rightly translate: God willed to render him (the people) just (or holy): he gave him a great law, (many precepts) that he might render him more illustrious.

Latin:

Vers 21. ET DOMINUS VOLUIT, UT SANCTI- FICARET EUM, ET MAGNIFICARET LEGEM, ET EXTOLLERET) Recte vertas: Deus voluit eum (popu- lum) justum (sive sanctum) reddere: magnam ei legem de- dit, (multa præcepta) ut illustriorem eum redderet.

## 42:22
Verse 22.

BUT THE PEOPLE THEMSELVES HAVE BEEN PLUNDERED, DEVASTATED) Nevertheless, he says, see what happens to him after so many honors. He will now render the cause.

A SNARE FOR THE YOUNG MEN ALL.) It seems better translated: A snare in all their holes. That is, nowhere will they be able to go out: thus everywhere will snares be laid for them. LXX. for the snare is in the storehouses everywhere.

AND IN THE HOUSES OF PRISONS THEY HAVE BEEN HIDDEN) כלא does not signify only a prison, but everything that is well closed. LXX. here: and in houses together where they hid them. Rightly therefore you may translate: & in recluded places where they were hiding, supply: & there will be snares. See the history 2. Kings 25, 5.

THEY HAVE BEEN MADE INTO PLUNDER, AND THERE IS NO ONE WHO RESCUES: INTO SPOIL, AND THERE IS NO ONE WHO SAYS RESTORE) No one either by deed or word vindicates them from injury. He describes the state of captured and remaining servitude.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

IPSE AUTEM POPULUS DIREPTUS EST, VA- STATUS) Attamen, inquit, vide quæ ei eveniant post tot decora. Causam jam reddet.

LAQUEUS JUVENUM OMNES) Melius verti vi- detur: Laqueus in omnibus foraminibus eorum. Id est, nus- quam exire poterunt: ita ubiq; eis tendentur insidiæ. LXX. ἡ γὰρ παγὶς ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις πανταχῦ.

ET IN DOMIBUS CARCERUM ABSCONDITI SUNT) כלא non carcerem tantum significat, sed o- mne id quod bene clauditur. LXX. hic: καὶ ἐν ὄικοις ἅμα ὅπυ ἔκρυψαν ἀυτὲς. Recte ergo vertas: & in reclusis locis ubi latitabant, supple: & ibi erunt insidiæ. Historiam vide 2. Reg. 25, 5.

FACTI SUNT IN RAPINAM, NEC EST QUI E- RUAT: IN DIREPTIONEM, NEC EST QUI DICAT REDDE) Nemo aut facto aut verbo eos ab injuria vin- dicat. Describit statum captæ & manentis servitutis.

## 42:23
Verse 23.

WHO IS AMONG YOU, WHO HEARS THIS, ATTENDS, AND LISTENS TO FUTURE THINGS? That is, how few there are who, when they hear these things predicted by God, correct themselves in time.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

QUIS EST IN VOBIS, QUI AUDIAT HOC, AT- TENDAT, ET AUSCULTET FUTURA) Id est, quam pauci sunt, qui cum hæc divinitus prædici audiant, in tempore se corrigant.

## 42:24
Verse 24. WAS IT NOT THE LORD HIMSELF AGAINST WHOM WE HAVE SINNED? This is again a koinosis: for Isaiah was not among those whose fault caused these things to happen: but he himself, although innocent, speaks as a part of the corrupt people.

AND THEY WOULD NOT WALK IN HIS WAYS) That is, because they would not. Thus 'aph is often used.

Latin:

Vers. 24. NONNE DOMINUS IPSE CUI PECCA- VIMUS) Est iterum κόινωσις: Neque enim Esaias inter illos erat, quorum culpa hæc eveniebant: Sed ipse, quan- quam integer, loquitur ut pars populi corrupti.

ET NOLUERUNT IN VIIS EJUS AMBULA- RE) Id est, quia noluerunt. Sic אף saepe sumitur.

## 42:25
AND PERHAPS WAR) From the Egyptian first, then from the Chaldean, 2 Kings 23:32, ch. 24, etc. 25.

Verse 25.

AND IT BURNED HIM ROUND ABOUT, AND HE DID NOT KNOW) That is, when all things situated around the city are destroyed by fire, the people will not yet repent.
