AND IT SET HIM ON FIRE, AND HE DID NOT UNDERSTAND) Not even then will they repent, when the city is burned by the Chaldeans, 2 Kings 25:9, Jeremiah 39:8.

The Hebrew reading in verse 19 is not only to be retained as not bad, but as uniquely good; for no other is authentic, whatever the Vulgate or the Seventy men may have read or seen, whose many and not insignificant errors the critics have observed. Whether you interpret the word as 'covenanted' or 'perfect', it fits the Pharisees best, who boasted that they were the chief among the covenanted and perfect above others. For that the Pharisees, Priests, and High Priests have been specifically designated by the Prophet thus far, appears also from the fact that in the following verses the office of the Teachers is insinuated: which should be rendered from the Hebrew thus: The Lord was held by desire because of his righteousness, that he might magnify the law and make it glorious, that is, God willed that the doctrine of the Gospel be preached clearly, widely propagated, and magnified among all, so that believers might be justified by faith. For thus the word Torah is frequently accepted among the Prophets for the Evangelical doctrine. That is, it should have been the chief duty of the Pharisees and Priests, who ought to have proposed true righteousness and defended the doctrine of the Gospel. Grotius says of that passage: You may rightly translate: God willed to make him (the people) upright (or holy): he gave him a great law (many precepts) to make it more illustrious. But in that version there are as many errors as there are words. The name of God is not there, but YHWH THE LORD. Nothing is there about the people: nothing about his sanctification. For thus the Prophet has YHWH chaphets lema'an tsidqo, The Lord willed, or desired, because of his righteousness; Nothing about many precepts given to the people, yagdil torah, He will magnify the doctrine, namely that which the Messiah, the covenant of the people and light of the nations, was about to deliver. For he intends to magnify this, Isa. 2:7. Nor is there anything about making the people more illustrious, because no mention of the people is made: but about making the doctrine of the Gospel more illustrious. Therefore, what is submitted in v. 21, BUT THE PEOPLE THEMSELVES ARE PLUNDERED, DEVASTATED, are not to be taken as Grotius wishes: Yet see what happens to him after so many honors: because that explanation proceeds from a false interpretation of the preceding, in which we deny that the honors of the people were delivered. Now, therefore, he turns from the Pharisees to the people themselves, who were suffering from equal blindness and deafness, whence he predicts a most grave punishment and designates their guilt. But the people themselves suffered plunder and were despoiled: And they were snared in caves, all of them, and in the houses of prisons, where they hid, they were for a prey, and there was none to deliver him; for a plundering, and there was none who said, Restore. We do not disapprove of the interpretation of Grotius, who takes it concerning the punishments of the people, even if others understand the plundering spiritually. Osiander with Breutius, as also Blessed Luther, explains it thus: The Pharisees and Scribes are ravenous wolves, plundering the flock of the Lord, and holding miserable men captive with their human traditions, so that they cannot extricate themselves from their snares by the torture and tyranny of their consciences. Nor does that explanation cohere badly with the preceding. But because the Prophet declares himself not obscurely what kind of plundering and what kind of prey he understands, while he asks in v. 23, Who gave Jacob for a plunder? and Israel to the spoilers? and uses the same words which he used before, so that it is by no means ambiguous that he speaks of the same plundering and devastation, and inquires into the cause of the same: Therefore, Jerome not objecting, we admit that it is understood of that bodily plundering and devastation, which all acknowledge these latter things treat of. But Grotius is mistaken in that he draws to the first plundering what treats of the most recent devastation. He rightly corrects the Vulgate, although he himself has not rendered it correctly. A SNARE FOR THE YOUNG MEN ALL. It seems better, he says, to be translated, A snare in all their holes, that is, they will be able to go out nowhere, so will snares be stretched for them. For the little word כֻּלָּם cannot be drawn to the holes: But it teaches that ALL OF THEM in the people are ensnared, so that the universal destruction of the people is designated, which no one can escape. Which things suit the most recent desolation, not likewise the former. Moreover, he not badly observes that the word כְּלֹא signifies not only a prison, but everything that is well closed. The LXX here [translate] ἐν οἴκοις ἅμα, ὅπε ἔκρυψαν αὐτὸς, so that it can be translated: & in enclosed places, where they were hiding, let it be supplied, & there will be snares. But when Grotius believed its fulfillment was to be found in the history of 2 Kings 25:5, he seems to have been asleep: For there the King is said to have been caught in flight, not in enclosed places, but in the open field. Furthermore, those words, THEY HAVE BECOME A PREY, AND THERE IS NONE TO DELIVER: A SPOILING, AND THERE IS NONE TO SAY, RESTORE, far more rightly agree with the most recent devastation and servitude than with the state of the Babylonian captivity and servitude; For then there was not lacking one who would deliver, nor one who would say, RESTORE. But now, such a one is expected in vain, for sixteen centuries, by the Jews.

Finally, that the rest in this chapter more aptly square with the total destruction and final blinding of the people, everyone sees: Because in the devastation of the Chaldeans there were not lacking those who recognized, grieved, and repented: The blinding and hardening was not as great as in the final destruction. Then the Lord poured out upon him (the whole Jewish people) the indignation of his fury (note the emphasis, as Luther warns, he poured out not drop by drop, but overwhelmed them with cataracts of wrath) then he truly sent a strong or heavy war, and burned, or kindled, (not the city only, but HIM, i.e., the people, of whom the Prophet treated) ROUND ABOUT (that is, he horribly devastated him on every side) AND HE DID NOT KNOW (the people, out of madness, what is the cause of such great calamities.) AND HE SET HIM ON FIRE (he dispersed the people on every side) YET HE DID NOT LAY IT TO HEART, he did not ponder why he was so horribly punished. For truly the stupor of the Jewish people is to be admired, who, although they have now been for so many centuries in dissipation and miserable servitude, yet neither understand their evils as is proper, nor recognize and ponder the cause of such great punishments, namely that they rejected the Messiah, and rejected his Gospel, whence they do not repent, but perish perpetually. Since he has been burned on every side, says Jerome, and has nothing of health in himself, yet he does not understand the cause of his punishment, that he was punished for this reason, because he did not receive the Son of God.

Latin:

ET FORTE BELLUM) Ab Aegyptio primum, deinde a Chaldaeo, 2. Reg. 23, 32. c. 24. &c. 25.

Vers. 25.

ET COMBUSSIT EUM IN CIRCUITU, ET NON COGNOVIT) Id est, cum omnia circum urbem sita incen- dio corrumpentur, nondum resipiscet populus.

ET SUCCENDIT EUM, ET NON INTELLEXIT) Ne tum quidem resipiscet, cum urbs a Chaldaeis incende- tur, 2. Reg. 25, 9. Jerem. 39, 8.

Lectio Ebraea versu 19. non modo ut non mala retinenda, sed ut unice bona; nulla enim alia au- thentica est, nisi Ebraea, quicquid legerint aut vide- rint vulgatus aut LXX. viri, quorum παροράματα bene multa, nec levia observarunt Critici. Sive interpreteris vocem foederatus, sive perfectus, opti- me convenit Pharisaeis, qui se praecipuos inter foe- deratos, & prae aliis perfectos venditabant. Nam quod Pharisaei, Sacerdotes, ac Pontifices speciatim hactenus designati fuerint a Propheta, ex eo etiam apparet, quod in seqq. officium Doctorum insinue- tur: quae ex Ebraeo ita reddenda: Dominus deside- rio tenebatur propter justitiam suam, ut magnificaret legem atq; insignem redderet, id est, Deus voluit, ut doctrina Evangelii clari praedicetur, late propage- tur, & magnifiat apud omnes, ut fide justificentur credentes. Nam ita vox תוֹרָה frequenter apud Prophetas accipitur pro doctrina Evangelica. Id est, praecipuum debebat Pharisaeorum & Sacer- dotum fuisse officium, qui veram justitiam propo- nere, ac doctrinam Evangelii propugnare debe- bant. Grotius ita de illo commate; Recte vertas: Deus voluit eum (populum) rectum (sive sanctum) red- dere: magnam ei legem dedit (multa praecepta) ut il- lustriorem redderet. Sed in ea versione tot errata, quot vocabula. Non habetur Dei nomen, sed יהוה DOMINUS. Nihil habetur de populo: ni- hil de ejus sanctificatione. Sic enim habet Propheta יְהוָה חָפֵץ לְמַעַן צִדְקוֹ Dominus voluit, vel desidera- vit propter justitiam suam; Nihil de multis praeceptis populo datis יַגְדִּיל תּוֹרָה Magnificabit doctrinam, illam sc. quam Messias foedus populi, & lux genti- um traditurus erat. Hanc enim magnificare inten- dit Esa. 2, 7. Neq; de illustriori reddendo populo quic- quam, quia populi nulla mentio facta: sed de illu- striori reddenda doctrina Evangelii. Quae ergo subjiciuntur. v. 21. IPSE AUTEM POPULUS DIREPTUS EST, VASTATUS, non sunt ita accipienda, ut Grotius vult: Attamen vide quae ei eveniant post tot decora: quia procedit ista explica- tio e ψευδερμηνείᾳ praecedentium, in quibq decora populi tradita esse negamus. Nunc ergo a Phari- saeis ad ipsum populum sese convertit, qui parili caecitate & surditate laborabant, unde & poenam gravissimam praedicit, & culpam eorum designat. Ipse autem populus praedam passus & direptus est: Il- laqueati sunt in speluncis, omnes ipsi, & in domibus carcerum, ubi latitarunt, fuerunt in rapinam, & non erat qui erueret eum; in direptionem, & non erat, qui diceret, Redde. Non improbamus interpreta- tionem Grotii, qui de poenis accipit populi, etsi alii direptionem spiritualiter intelligant. Osiander cum Breutio, ut & B. Luthero ita exponit: Pharisaei & Scribae sunt lupi rapaces, diripientes gregem Do- mini, & humanis suis traditionibus captivos te- nent miseros homines, ut sese ex ipsorum laqueis conscientiarum carnificina & tyrannide extricare nequeant. Nec male cohaeret illa explicatio supe- rioribus. Sed quia Propheta sese haud obscure declarat, qualem direptionem, & qualem praedam intelligat, dum quaerit v. 23. Quis dedit in direptione Jacob? ac Israel praedantibus? & verbis iisdem uti- tur, quibus antea usus est, ut minime ambiguum vi- deatur, de eadem direptione ac prædatione eun- dem loqui, ac causam ejusdem inquirere : Ideo non abnuente Hieronymo, admittimus de corporali deprædatione, & direptione ista accipi, de qua hæc posteriora agere omnes agnoscunt. Sed in eo fal- litur Grotius, quod ad primam direptionem trahat, quæ de novissima devastatione agunt. Merito Vul- gatum corrigit, quamvis nec ipse recte reddiderit. LAQUEUS JUVENUM OMNES. Melius, inquit, verti videtur, Laqueus in omnibus forami- nibus eorum, id est, nuspiam exire poterunt, ita eis tendentur insidiæ. Nam vocula כֻּלָּם trahi non po- test ad foramina: Sed OMNES IPSOS in populo illaqueatos docet, ita ut universalis populi clades designetur, quam nemo effugere queat. Quæ no- vissimæ desolationi conveniunt, non item priori. Vocem autem כְּלֹא non male observat significare, non carcerem tantum, sed omne id, quod bene claudi- tur. LXX. hic ἐν οἴκοις ἅμα, ὅπε ἔκρυψαν αὐτὸς, ut verti possit : & in reclusis locis, ubi latitabant, sup- pleatur, & ibi erunt insidiæ. Complementum vero ejus dum Grotius in historia 2. Reg. 25, 5. inveniri credidit, dormitasse videtur: Nam ibi Rex depre- hensus in fuga, non in reclusis locis, sed in aperto campo dicitur. Porro illa, FACTI SUNT IN RAPINAM, NEC EST QUI ERUAT: IN DIREPTIONEM, NEC EST QUI DICAT, REDDE, longe rectius congruunt convissimæ de- vastationi, ac servituti, quam statui captivitatis & servitutis Babylonicæ; Nam tum non deerat, qui erueret, non qui diceret, REDDE. Nunc autem frustra talis expectatur, per sedecim secula, à Ju- dæis.

Denique ad πανωλεθρίαν totalem, & excæca- tionem populi finalem cætera in hoc capite aptius quadrare, nemo non videt: Quia in Chaldæorum devastatione non deerant, qui cognoscerent, dolerent & resipiscerent : Tanta non erat excæcatio, & in- duratio, quanta in finali excidio. Tum effudit Do- minus super eum (populum Judaicum universum) indignationem furoris sui (nota emphasin monente Luthero, effudit non stillatim, sed cataractis iræ ob- ruit eos) tum bellum vere forte vel grave immisit, & combussit, seu accendit, (non civitatem tantum, sed ILLUM, sc. populum, de quo egit Propheta) IN CIRCUITU (id est, quaquaversum illum horribi- liter vastavit) ET NON COGNOVIT (po- pulus præ amentia, quæ sit causa tantarum calami- tatum.) ET SUCCENDIT EUM (undiquaque dispersit populum) NEQUE TAMEN PO- SUIT SUPER EUM, non perpendit, cur tam horribiliter sit punitus. Vere enim admirandus est stupor populi Judaici, qui cum jam per tot secu- la in dissipatione & misera servitute agat, tamen nec mala sua ut par est intelligat, nec causam tanta- rum pœnarum cognoscat, ac perpendat, quod nempe Messiam reprobarint, ejusq; Evangelium rejecerint, unde non resipiscunt, sed perpetuo pe- reunt. Cum ex omni parte combustus sit, inquit Hie- ronym. & nihil in se habeat sanitatis, tamen non in- telligit causam pœnæ suæ, quod idcirco punitus sit, quia DEI Filium non recepit.

## 43:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLIII.

The Lord comforts the faithful, demonstrating himself as Redeemer and foreknower of future things, predicting the punishment of the Babylonians, the enlargement of his Church through the conversion of the Gentiles, and the expiation of sins to be procured by his death, so that he may teach that grace comes to the faithful without any merits of their own.

Ver. 1.

CREATING YOU O JACOB AND FORMING YOU O ISRAEL, DO NOT FEAR, FOR I HAVE REDEEMED YOU) I have delivered Jacob from many evils, Parents are reckoned the same as their children.

AND I HAVE CALLED YOU BY YOUR NAME, YOU ARE MINE.) I gave him the name of Israel, just as servants are called Marcipores, Quintipores.

These things cannot be explained of the Patriarch Jacob. For he is understood by the name Jacob and Israel, whom the Lord addresses: Do not fear. But that the Patriarch is addressed here is absurd. And since it is said of the same subject in v. 2, when you pass through the waters, that is, the Red Sea, as Grotius explains, how can the Patriarch be understood? It remains, therefore, that not the redemption of the Patriarch from many evils, or the naming given to him, but the benefits shown to the people are indicated: who is designated by the name of Jacob and Israel, because he arose from Jacob; or as Israel is understood of God or according to the Spirit, Rom. 9:7, Gal. 6:16. For since he had threatened the people with total destruction, he now raises up the faithful with the sweetest consolations, lest they think it is all over with the Church. He addresses, therefore, the true and Spiritual Church, not only that which was at that time before the Babylonian captivity in the people of Israel, or which had been dispersed in the devastation of the city and the Babylonian destruction, to all nations, but also that which was to be in the New Testament. For all who believe in the Messiah are true Israelites. But God is said to create or form us, not by reason of the first article, but of the third, since the spiritual creation and regeneration proper to Israel is regarded, For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus Eph. 2:10, 2 Cor. 5. Redemption is understood as spiritual from the power of Satan, death, and hell, as the Belgian Paraphrasers rightly [say]. Nor does that calling denote the imposition of a name, but the gracious adoption, which is of the faithful. For these he calls by his name, you are mine: I have adopted you as an heir to eternal life. Cf. v. 7. I have called, says Cyril, you by your name. By what? Namely: you are mine. For we are said to be of Christ, and this is a glorious name, by which we are surnamed. But it must be known that in other Scripture it is said: I have called you by my name. But when he adds and says: You are mine, he dissolves the alienation, which those who are held by sins are accustomed to undergo. For they are not God's, even if they possess the Lord of all. And a proclivity to evil things disturbs [one] from the society and conjunction which is with him. Whence we say that those who are contaminated with defilements are not of God. Therefore, there is a certain emphasis of spiritual conjunction and kinship: You are mine. Jerome applies these things specifically to the primitive Church of Christ: Therefore, what we said above, that there are two Jacobs and two Israels, one carnal and the other spiritual, of those who were unwilling to believe in the Savior, and of those who received the Son of God: This is also to be understood now, that the chorus of the Apostles is provoked, and the first Church of Christ gathered from the people of the Jews, so that it may understand its creator and maker, who is the founder of both its soul and body. Nor should it fear persecutors, because it has been redeemed by the blood of Christ, who has called it by his name, and because of intimacy specifically calls it his people, but let it preach unhesitatingly, and fear no dangers. But although some things pertain to the Church of the New Testament, it is hardly ambiguous that certain things look to the faithful who lived before the Babylonian captivity. He also addresses them, that they should not fear, after he has prophesied both concerning the Babylonian servitude and the Roman πανολεθρία set; with a paracletic argument applied, derived both from redemption and from gracious calling and regeneration, and with the most sweet promise added, which now follows.

Latin:

CAPUT XLIII.

Dominus fideles solatur, Redemtorem & futu- rorum præscium demonstrans, Babylonio- rum pœnam, Ecclesiæ suæ per gentium con- versionem ampliationem, peccatorumq́; ex- piationem morte sua conciliandam prædi- cens, ut fidelibus gratiam sine ullis propriis meritis contingere doceat.

Vers. 1.

CREANS TE O JACOB ET FORMANS TE O IS-RAEL, NOLI TIMERE, QVIA REDEMI TE) Jaco-bum ex multis malis liberavi, Parentes cum liberis ii-dem censentur.

ET VOCAVI TE NOMINE TUO, MEVS ES TU.) Indidi illi nomen Israëlis, sicut servi vocantur Marcipores, Quintipores.

Non possunt hæc de Patriarcha Jacobo explica-ri. Is enim intelligitur nomine Jacob & Israël, quem compellat Dominus: Noli timere. At Pa-triarcham hîc compellari, absonum est. Et quum de eodem subjecto v. 2. dicatur, cum transires per aquas, id est, mare rubrum, ut explicat Groti9, quo-modo Patriarcha intelligi potest? Restat ergo, ut non redemtio Patriarchæ ex malis multis, aut ὀνο-μαθεσία ipsi facta, sed beneficia populo exhibita indigitentur: qui nomine Jacob & Israëlis desgina-tur, quia à Jacobo ortus est; aut ut Israel Dei vel secundum Spiritum intelligitur, Rom. 9, 7. Gal. 6, 16. Quum enim minatus fuerit populo πανολεθρίαν, erigit nunc fideles suavissimis consolationibus, ne actum fore de Ecclesia putent. Alloquitur itaq; veram & Spiritualem Ecclesiam, non eam tantum quæ illo tempore erat ante captivitatem Babyloni-cam in populo Israël, aut quæ dispersa fuerat in va-statione urbis & exitio Babylonico, ad omnes gen-tes, sed etiam quæ in N. T. futura erat. Omnes enim qui credunt in Messiam, veri sunt Israëlitæ, Creare vero aut formare dicitur nos Deus, non ra-tione articuli primi, sed tertii, quum spiritualis creatio & regeneratio Israëli propria respiciatur, Ipsius enim sumus factura, creati in Christo Jesu Eph. 2, 10. 2. Cor. 5. Redemtio intelligitur spiritualis è potestate Satanæ, mortis & inferni, ut recte Para-phr. Belgæ. Neque vocatio illa nominis imposi-tionem, sed gratiosam adoptionem notat, quæ fi-delium est. Hos enim vocat nomine suo, tu meus es: ego te in hæredem ad vitam æternam adoptavi. Conf. v. 7. Vocavi, inquit Cyrillus, te nomine tuo. Quonam? nimirum: meus es tu. Christi enim esse dicimur, & hoc præclarum nomen est, quo cognomi-namur. Sciendum vero, quod in alia Scriptura di-catur: Vocavi te nomine meo. Verum cum adjicit & dicit: Meus es tu, solvit alienationem, quam sub-ire solent, qui peccatis detinentur. Non enim illi sunt Dei, licet universorum Dominum teneant. Et de-turbat à societate & conjunctione, quæ cum illo est, ad res malas proclivitas. Unde dicimus eos, qui sunt contaminati inquinamentis, non esse Dei. Itaq; spi-ritualis conjunctionis & cognationis emphasis quæ-dam est: Meus es tu. Applicat hæc specialiter Hieronymus ad primitivam Christi Ecclesiam: Er-go quod supra diximus, duos esse Jacob & duos Israel, unum carnalem & alterum spiritualem, eorum qui in Salvatorem credere noluerunt, & eorum qui recepe-runt Filium Dei: Hoc etiam nunc intelligendum, quod provocetur Apostolorum chorus, & prima Chri-sti Ecclesia de Judæorum populo congregata, ut intelli-gat creatorem & factorem suum, qui & animæ & corporis ejus sit conditor. Nec timeat persecutores, quia redemptus sit Christi sanguine, qui vocaverit eum nomine suo, & ob familiaritatem specialiter ap-pellet populum suum, sed prædicet incunctanter, & nulla pericula reformidet. Sed quamvis nonnulla ad Ecclesiam Nov. Test. pertineant, quædam ta-men ad fideles, qui ante captivitatem Babylonicam vixerunt, spectare, vix ambiguum est. Illos etiam compellat, ne timeant, postquam & de Babylonica servitute, & de Romana πανολεθρία vaticinatus es- set; argumento paracletico adhibito tum à redem- tione, tum à gratiosa vocatione & regeneratione, ad- ditaq; promissione suavissima, quæ jam sequitur.

## 43:2
Verse 2.

WHEN YOU PASS THROUGH THE WATERS, I WILL BE WITH YOU.) Better: when you passed through the waters (that is, through the Red Sea), I was with you. AND THE RIVERS SHALL NOT OVERWHELM YOU.) The rivers (such as the Jordan, rising from two springs) did not inundate you; nay, they gave you a passage. WHEN YOU WALK THROUGH THE FIRE, YOU SHALL NOT BE BURNED, AND THE FLAME SHALL NOT KINDLE.) These words also must be changed into the past tense. For the sense is: when the army of Sennacherib was perishing in the circuit of your city by a sudden destruction (which we have often seen compared to flame), I kept you safe, as if from a conflagration. Horace also said 'to walk through fires' for being involved in dangers.

A distinguished promise, more precious than gold and gems, is most wickedly perverted. For the words do not speak of a past benefit shown to the Israelite people, but of a most gracious future παρασχέσει (provision), whether the faithful must pass through waters or through fires. Since the LORD exhorts: Do not fear, and by this promise shakes off all fear and dread, but stirs up confidence. Nor do the words sound in the past, but are uttered in the future. And so, by rendering both the words and the sense, the oracle is corrupted by Grotius. And such στρεβλότης (distortion) does not easily come to the mind of anyone except Grotius. For the interpreters commonly accept these as a promise. The Jews, with Jerome as witness, understand the Egyptians in the waters, but they think the Babylonians are noted in the rivers, the Macedonians in the fire, and the Romans in the flame. But no one has easily denied that a promise is held here. Cyril rightly says: He promises here to be an invincible help, that no temptation will invade him. For rivers and waters and flames designate the manifold assaults of temptations. If you pass through the water, I am with you. For if Christ be one with them, nothing will do injury to those who are His, but they will attain to such spiritual fortitude that they will make nothing of him who is able to harass and submerge them with tempests; nay, if persecution should sometimes invade in the manner of a river and a wave, and fire and flame should have power, they will nevertheless overcome, knowing that it is God who saves. For it is familiar to the divinely inspired Scripture to liken the assaults of temptations to both rivers and waters. Furthermore, who will not detest that audacity, that Grotius decides, by dictatorial power: 'These words also must be changed into the past tense.' Thus the jurist changes future tenses in the Holy Scriptures into past tenses for the sake of authority, and converts divine promises into histories and past events. Who will approve that merely arbitrary, nay, utterly violent gloss, which interprets the fire and the burning flame as the danger that was imminent from the army of Sennacherib? For here it is not the danger of the city, but of Jacob and Israel, that is pointed out; and although that city was of the Jews, the Prophet does not address the Jews specifically, but the Israelites and any of the faithful; nor, as I said, does he treat of a past but of a future liberation; and what kind of leap would that be from the passage through the waters, that is, through the Red Sea, to the liberation from the flames, that is, from the siege of Sennacherib?

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CUM TRANSIERIS PER AQUAS, TECUM E- RO.) Melius: cum transires per aquas, (id est, per mare ru- brum) tecum eram. ET FLUMINA NON OPERIENT TE) Flumina (ut Jordanes ex duobus fontibus oriens.) te non inunda- runt: quinimo transitum tibi dederuut. CUM AMBULAVERIS IN IGNE, NON AMBV- RERIS, ET FLAMMA NON ARDEBIT.) Hæc quoque verba in præteritum mutanda. Sensus enim est: cum in circuitu urbis tuæ Sennacheribi exercitus subito exitio (quod flammæ comparari jam sæpe vidimus) periret, te sal- vum, quasi ab incendio præstiti. Incedere per ignes etiam Horatius dixit, pro in periculis versari.

Pessime pervertitur insignis promissio, auro & gemmis pretiosior. Non enim de præterito be- neficio verba loquuntur, populo Israëlitico exhibi- to, sed de futura παρασχέσει gratiosissima, sive per aquas transeundum sit fidelibus, sive per ignes. Quum hortetur DOMINUS: Ne timeas, & hac promissione metum & timorem omnem ex- cutiat, fiduciam vero excitet. Nec in præterito sonant verba, sed efferuntur in futuro. Adeoque & verba & sensum reddendo, à Grotio corrum- pitur oraculum. Nec facile ulli præter Grotium ea στρεβλότης in mentem venit. Accipiunt enim communiter Interpp. hæc tanquam promissionem. Judæi, Hieronymo teste, in aquis Ægyptios quidem intelligunt, at in fluminibus Babylonios, in igne Ma- cedonas, in flamma Romanos notari putant. Sed ne- mo facile inficiatus est promissionem hic haberi. Recte Cyrillus: Promittit hic esse auxilium invi- ctum, quod nulla eum tentatio invadet. Nam fluvii & aquæ & flammæ, multiplices tentationum impetus designant. Si transieris aquam, tecum sum. Christus enim si una sit, nihil his qui sunt ejus, injuriam fece- rit, at eo spiritualis fortitudinis devenient, ut nihili sint facturi eum, qui valeat tempestatibus divexare & demergere: imo si persequutio in morem fluminis ac fluctus aliquando invadat, & ignis ac flamma vim habeat, sic tamen evincent, illud scientes, Deum esse, qui servat. Est enim familiare Scripturæ divini- tus inspiratæ, & fluminibus, & aquis tentationum in- sultus assimilare. Porro quis non detestabitur audaciam istam, quod pro dictatoria potestate de- cernat Grotius; Hæc quoq; verba in præteritum mu- tanda. Sic futura in S. Literis pro auctoritate mu- tat JCtus in præterita, & promissiones divinas conver- tit in historias, ac res gestas. Quis probabit il- lam mere arbitrariam, imo prorsus violentam glos- sam, quæ ignem & flammam ardentem de pericu- lo, quod à Sennacheribi exercitu imminebat, inter- pretatur; Nam hic non periculum urbis, sed Jacobi & Israëlis, indigitatur, & quamvis urbs illa Judæo- rum fuerit, non tamen in specie Judæos alloquitur Propheta, sed Israëlitas ac fideles quosvis, neque ut dixi, de præterita sed futura liberatione agit, & qua- lis ille saltus foret à transitu per aquas, id est, per mare rubrum, ad liberationem è flammis, id est, ab obsessione Sennacheribi?

## 43:3
Verse 3. I HAVE GIVEN EGYPT AS YOUR RANSOM, ETHIOPIA AND SABA FOR YOU.) The Greeks: ἄλλαγμα σου: That is, when Esarhaddon was thinking of bringing the ultimate evils upon you, I set against him another enemy, the Ethiopian Tirhakah, accompanied by a huge army from Egypt and Meroë, or as the Greeks have here, Syene. See above, chapters 18 and 37.

He follows Cornelius à Lapide in this. And that interpretation also pleased the Weimar Paraphrasts, as well as the Dutch. Our Brentius says the Egyptians were given for the Israelites when the former were submerged in the Red Sea so that the Israelites might escape, in whose army he thinks there were Ethiopians and Sabeans, because the Ethiopians, according to Josephus, were conquered by the Egyptians and subjected to them before the exodus of the Israelites; for Saba is the metropolis of Ethiopia. Osiander similarly understands the Egyptians to have been submerged. He wishes the Ethiopians to be designated by those who afflicted Asa from 2 Chronicles 14, and he includes the Sabeans under them. But whichever of those explanations is chosen (for what is brought forward here by Jerome, and that which Cyril handed down, are foreign), it will matter little to the intention of the Prophet, provided that the preceding promise is not converted into a historical commemoration with Grotius: for now at last the Prophet raises up and confirms the faithful with the example of an admirable liberation already performed, when He gave Egypt, Ethiopia, and Saba for the Israelites. We do not deny that this is rightly accepted concerning the liberation from the Assyrian, by the exchange of those peoples for the Jews. Compare Isaiah 20:5, Proverbs 11:8. And the Lord speaks likewise of this exchange in the following verse. Since you were precious in my eyes, after I chose you, and began to hold you in value, when I led you out of Egypt, you were glorious, and I loved you, and I gave a man for you, and peoples for your soul, which can be understood of the same ἀλλάγματι (exchange), so that the gracious election and anointing of God may be explained as the cause of the same. In which sense the Weimar and Dutch Paraphrasts accepted these. Grotius, however, refers the liberation to the future, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEDI PROPITLATIONEM TVAM ÆGY- PTVM, ÆTHIOPIAM AC SABA PRO TE.) Græci ἄλλαγμα σου: Id est, cum Asarhaddon cogitaret tibi inferre malorum ultima, objeci ei alium hostem Æthiopem Thara- cam, comitatum ingenti agmine ex Ægypto & Meroë, aut ut Græci hic habent, Syene. Vid. supr. cap. 18. & 37.

Sequitur in eo Cornelium à Lapide. Et pla- cuit ea interpretatio quoque Vinariensibus Para- phrastis, ut & Belgis. Brentius noster Ægyptios datos pro Israëlitus dicit, cum isti in mari rubro sub- mergerentur ut Israëlitæ evaderent, in quorum ex- ercitu Æthiopes & Sabæos fuisse putat, quia Æthio- pes ante exitum Israëlitatum ex Ægypto, teste Jo- sepho, ab Ægyptiis devicti, illisque subjecti sunt, Saba enim Metropolis Æthiopiæ est. Osiander simi- liter Ægyptios submersos intelligit. Æthyopes vero per Asam afflictoes è Paral.14. designari vult, & sub i- is complectitur quoque Sabæos. Utra autem earum explicationum eligatur (nam quæ hic ab Hierony- mo adfertur, tum illa, quæ Cyrillus tradidit, aliena sunt) parum intererit ad Prophetæ intentionem, modo ne cum Grotio promissio antecedens in com- memorationem historicam convertatur: nunc enim demum erigit Propheta & confirmat fideles exemplo præstitæ admirandæ liberationis, cum Æ- gyptum, Æthiopiam, & Saba pro Israëlitis dedit. Quam de liberatione ab Assyrio, data commutatio- ne istorum populorum pro Judæis recte accipi non abnuimus. Cons. Esa.20, 5. Prov.11, 8. Atque de hac commutatione loquitur pariter Dominus vers. sequent. Ex quo pretiosus fuisti in oculis meis, post- quam te elegi, & in pretio habere cœpi, cum educerem te ex Ægypto, gloriosus fuisti, & ego dilexi te ואתן & dedi hominem pro te, & populos pro anima tua, quod de eodem ἀλλάγματι intelligi potest, ut causa e- jusdem exponatur gratiosa Dei electio & unctio. Quo sensu hæc accepêre Paraphrastæ Vinarienses & Belgici. Grotius vero ad futurum liberationem refert, uti sequitur.

## 43:4
Verse 4.

SINCE YOU HAVE BECOME HONORABLE IN MY EYES, AND GLORIOUS, I HAVE LOVED YOU, AND I WILL GIVE MEN FOR YOU, AND PEOPLES FOR YOUR SOUL.) The sense is: What I have done heretofore, I will now also do: because you are of great value to me, and are held in much esteem by me and are loved, therefore I will spare no men or peoples to liberate you: This pertains to the Medes and Babylonians.

He embraces this sense for this reason, that he may interpret the things which follow concerning the reduction and captivity. But in the Hebrew text the prefixed Vau retains its conversive force, and therefore it should be rendered, AND I HAVE GIVEN A MAN FOR THEE, whence it is more correctly referred to a threatening or a substitution already made. That promise would have been too obscure and concise if the discourse were about liberation from the Babylonians. Nor are the things which are subjoined to be understood concerning the reduction, as we shall now advise.

Verse of the same. I WILL BRING THY SEED FROM THE EAST, AND I WILL GATHER THEE FROM THE WEST: I WILL SAY TO THE NORTH, GIVE, AND TO THE SOUTH, DO NOT FORBID.) That is, I will make you a returnee from all parts of the world. Thus Matt. 24, 31. ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων: Where see the remarks.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

EX QVO HONORABILIS FACTVS ES IN OCV- LIS MEIS, ET GLORIOSVS, EGO DILEXI TE, ET DABO HOMINES PRO TE, ET POPVLOS PRO ANI- MA TVA.) Sensus est: Quod antehac feci, nunc quoque faciam: quia apud me in magno es pretio, plurimique ha- beris à me & diligeris, propterea nullis hominibus, aut po- pulis parcam ad te liberandum: Ad Medos & Babylonios hoc pertinet.

Quem sensum ideo amplectitur, ut ea, quæ se- quuntur, de reductione & captivitate interprete- tur. Sed in Ebræo textu Vau præfixum retinet vim suam conversivam, adeoque reddendum, ET DEDI HOMINEM PRO TE, unde rectius ad comminationem aut surrogationem jam factam refertur. Nimis obscura & concisa fuisset illa pro- missio, si de liberatione à Babyloniis sermo esset. Neque de reductione intelligenda sunt, quæ sub- junguntur, ut jam monebimus.

Vers. eod. AB ORIENTE ADDVCAM SEMEN TV- VM, ET AB OCCIDENTE CONGREGABO TE: DI- CAM AQVILONI DA, ET AVSTRO, NOLI PROHI- BERE.) Id est, ex omnibus mundi partibus te reducem faci- am. Sic Matth. 24, 31. ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων: Vbi dicta vide.

## 43:7
Verse 7. AND EVERY ONE WHO CALLETH UPON MY NAME) The Greeks are closer to the Hebrew: πάντας ὅσοι ἐπικέκληνται τῷ ὀνοματί μυ: that is, those who profess themselves to be worshippers of the one GOD.

FOR MY GLORY) So that my power may appear, and my faithfulness and constancy in my promises.

I HAVE CREATED HIM, I HAVE FORMED HIM, AND I HAVE MADE HIM) These are to be translated by the future, and the sense is: I will as it were restore them all to life. For a miserable condition is called by the name of death.

Grotius understands these things concerning the reduction from Babylon. But at that time the Jews were not recalled from all parts of the world. Nor were they dispersed to all parts of the world. The discourse is about the gathering of the sons of God from the whole world, who are denominated from his name, whom God created for his glory, and prepared; Do not fear (he addresses his Church, that she may not fear, even if, of course, the greatest dangers show themselves) because I am with you in the very distress: Nay, even from the East I will bring thy seed: thy spiritual Sons, and from the West I will gather thee. I will say to the North, give me my sons, and to the South, do not forbid. Bring my sons from afar, and my daughters FROM THE ENDS OF THE EARTH. This is a description of the calling of the Gentiles to the Church, and clearly this is that which Christ says in Matt. 8, many shall come from the east and west, and shall recline with Abraham, Isaac & Jacob in the kingdom of heaven: & Acts 1. You shall be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and finally to the ends of the earth. Since this is the case, it is so far from being the case that the true Church of God perishes by the Babylonian captivity or other calamity, that it is rather preserved and increased by this occasion. They are therefore called the spiritual children of the Jewish Church, and to be gathered to the same, because the Church of the faithful collected from the Gentiles was procreated from the Jewish Church, and approached its communion. And the address was therefore made under the name of Jacob & Israel, because they were to come from all parts of the earth, that they might recline in the kingdom of heaven with Jacob or Israel. For that this promise is spiritual, and does not pertain only to the Jews to be brought back from captivity, is also confirmed by the appended catholic epiphonema: EVERYONE WHO ACKNOWLEDGES MY NAME, (In Hebrew, who is denominated from my name, these are the words of Christ, and therefore all true Christians are indicated, who are truly called by Christ, whether they be from the Jews or from the Gentiles) I have created him for my glory, I have formed him, and I have made him for the praise of my name, these I have created for eternal life, that I may show the riches of my mercy and goodness for all eternity. Which Grotius corrupts thus: I CREATED HIM, I FORMED HIM AND I MADE HIM. These, he says, must be translated by the future: I will restore all these as it were to life: for the miserable condition is called by the name of death. First, he decides by his own authority that the past must be converted into the future. Then he twists the words to the snatching away and misery, so that they are taken in a clearly unusual metaphorical sense, which neither the context demands, nor the ἀλληλουχία of similar passages. For the continuity of the prophecy teaches that the discourse is about the time of the New Testament and the promise of the Gentiles, and a comparison with v. 19 and 20 makes us more certain: indeed, the reprobation of the Jews, about which those things that follow in the text treat not obscurely, confirms that this concerns the calling of the Gentiles primarily. Grotius himself acknowledges that those things are to be understood of the Jews, even if he refers them to the Jews of that time. Osiander rendered them not badly: LEAD OUT FROM MY FACE & love THE JEWISH PEOPLE, hardened, blind, and yet HAVING EYES. THAT DEAF PEOPLE, & yet THEY HAVE EARS. Because the children of the kingdom were to be cast out, Matt. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET OMNEM QVI INVOCAT NOMEN MEVM) Græci propius ad Hebræum: πάντας ὅσοι ἐπικέ- κληνται τῷ ὀνοματί μυ: id est, illos qui se unius DEI cul- tores profitentur.

IN GLORIAM MEAM) Vt appareat mea potentia, & in promissis fides ac constantia.

CREAVI EVM, FORMAVI EVM, ET FECI EVM) Vertenda hæc per futurum, & sensus est: Eos o- mnes quasi vitæ reddam. Nam misera conditio mortis no- mine appellatur.

De reductione è Babylone intelligit hæc Gro- tius. At tum non ex omnibus mundi partibus revocati sunt Judæi. Nec ad omnes mundi partes dispersi fuêre. De filiis Dei congregandis ex universo orbe, qui denominantur à nomine suo, sermo est, quos creavit Deus ad gloriam, & præpa- ravit; Noli timere (alloquitur Ecclesiam suam, ne timeat, etiamsi maxima scilicet se ostendant pe- ricula) quia ego tecum sum in ipsa angustia: Quin etiam ab Oriente adducam semen tuum: spirituales Filios tuos, & ab Occidente congregabo te. Dicam Aquiloni, da mihi filios meos, & Austro, noli prohibere. Affer filios meos è longinquo, & filias meas AB EXTREMIS TERRÆ. Hæc est descriptio vocationis gentium ad Ecclesiam, ac pla- ne hoc illud est, quod Matth. 8. Christus dicit, mul- ti ab oriente & occidente venient, & recumbent cum Abraham, Isaac & Jacob in regno cælorum: & Act. I. Eritis mihi testes in Hierusalem, & in omni Judæa & Samaria, denique usque ad extrema terræ. Quod cum ita se habeat, tantum abest, ut vera Dei Eccle- sia captivitate Babylonica, aut alia calamitate per- eat, ut potius hac occasione conservetur & augea- tur. Dicuntur ergo spirituales filii Judaicæ Eccle- siæ, & ad eandem congregandi, quod procreata sit Ecclesia fidelium ex Ethnicis collectorum è Judai- ca Ecclesia, & ad ejusdem communionem accesse- rit. Et compellatio ideo facta est sub nomine Ja- cobi & Israëlis, quia venturi erant ex omnibus ter- ræ partibus, ut recumberent in regno cælorum cum Jacobo vel Israële. Quod enim hæc promis- sio spiritualis sit, nec ad Judæos solum è captivitate reducendos pertineat, confirmat etiam subjun- ctum Epiphonema catholicum: OMNEM QVI AGNOSCIT NOMEN MEUM, (In Ebræo, qui denominatur à nomine meo, verba Christi sunt, ideoque omnes indigitantur veri Christiani, qui vere à Christo appellantur, sive ex Judæis sint, sive è gentibus) in gloriam meam creavi eum, formavi eum, & feci eum in laudem nominis mei, hos ego creavi ad vitam æternam, ut ostendam divitias mi- sericordiæ & bonitatis meæ in omnem æternita- tem. Quæ ita corrumpit Grotius: CREAVI EUM, FORMAVI EUM ET FECI EUM. Vertenda, inquit, hæc per futurum: hos omnes quasi vitæ red- dam: nam misera conditio mortis nomine appellatur. Primum pro autoritate decernit præteritum in fu- turum convertendum esse. Tum verba detorquet ad ereptionem & miseriam, ut sensu plane inusitato metaphorico accipiantur, quem nec contextus postulat, nec ἀλληλουχία similium locorum. De tempore enim Novi Testamenti & promissione gentium sermonem esse, συνέχεια vaticinii docet, & collatio cum v.19. ac 20. certiores nos reddit: imo gentium imprimis vocationem hæc concernere, reprobatio Judæorum, de qua haud obscure ea, quæ in textu sequuntur, agunt, confirmat. Ea de Judæis intelligenda esse ipse Grotius agnoscit, etsi ea ad istius temporis Judæos referat. Quæ ita red- didit. Osiander non male: EDUC A FACIE MEA & amore POPULUM JUDAICUM, in- duratum, cæcum, & tamen OCULOS HABEN- TEM. SURDUM ILLUM POPULUM, & ta- men AURES EI SUNT. Quia filii regni ejici- endi erant, Matth. 8.

## 43:8
Vers. 8. LEAD OUT THE BLIND PEOPLE, AND HAVING EYES) Who is blind, although he has eyes. He understands the Jews, who had seen many works of God, and yet most did not sufficiently consider them. Lead out, that is, call to judgment.

DEAF, AND HE HAS EARS) Although he has ears: that is: who does not sufficiently retain in his mind many things heard from the fathers.

Latin:

Vers. 8. EDUC FORAS POPULUM CÆCUM, ET OCULOS HABENTEM) Qui cæcus est, quamvis oculos habeat. Judæos intelligit, qui multa Dei opera viderant, nec satis tamen pleriq; ea considerabant. Educ, id est, ad judi- cium voca.

SURDUM, ET AURES EI SUNT) Quamvis au- res ei sint: id est: qui multa à patribus audita non satis ani- mo retinet.

## 43:9
Vers. 9. ALL NATIONS ARE GATHERED, AND TRIBES ARE COLLECTED TOGETHER) You might translate more correctly: let them be gathered and collected, namely for judgment.

WHO AMONG YOU CAN ANNOUNCE THIS?) Who is there among the Gentiles who can tell you who and by what name he will be who is to liberate my people: which I will say through Isaiah.

AND WILL MAKE US HEAR WHAT THE FIRST THINGS ARE) Let him at least say those things which are about to happen next. See above XLI. 22.

LET THEM GIVE THEIR WITNESSES) Let them produce for us suitable witnesses concerning the divinity of those whom they worship.

LET THEM BE JUSTIFIED) That is, if they can perform that, their cause will be pronounced just. Cf. what is above 41, 26.

AND LET THEM HEAR) Then let them hear the witnesses of my side.

AND LET THEM SAY TRULY) That is, they will be compelled to say that the truth stands on my side.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OMNES GENTES CONGREGATÆ SUNT, SIMUL ET COLLECTÆ SUNT TRIBUS) Vertas rectius: congregentur & colligantur, nempe ad judi- cium.

QVIS IN VOBIS ANNUNCIET ISTUD?) Quis est ex gentibus, qui vobis possit dicere, quis & quo nomine futurus sit, qui populum meum sit liberaturus: quod ego dicam per Esaiam.

ET QVÆ PRIMA SUNT AUDIRE NOS FA- CIET) Dicat saltem illa, quæ proxime futura sunt. Vide supra XLI. 22.

DENT TESTES EORUM) Producant nobis te- stes idoneos de divinitate eorum quos colunt.

JUSTIFICENTUR) Id est, si id præstare possunt, justa illorum causa pronunciabitur Conf. quod sup. 41, 26.

ET AUDIANT) Deinde audiant testes meæ partis.

ET DICANT VERE) Id est, cogentur dicere à me stare veritatem.

## 43:10
V. 10. YOU ARE MY WITNESSES, SAYS THE LORD) You who have heard and will hear these things from Isaiah.

AND MY SERVANT WHOM I HAVE CHOSEN) Isaiah, as above 42, 1. A witness both by speaking openly, and by writing, and by sealing what was written.

THAT I MYSELF AM) Namely, God.

Latin:

V. 10. VOS TESTES MEI DICIT DOMINUS) Qui ista ex Esaia audistis & audietis.

ET SERVUS MEUS QUEM ELEGI) Esaias, ut supra 42, 1. Testis & dicendo palam, & scribendo, & scri- ptum consignando.

QVIA EGO IPSE SVM) Nempe Deus.

## 43:12
Vers. 12. I HAVE ANNOUNCED) I have foretold your salvation.

AND I HAVE SAVED) And I have performed, as I had foretold.

I HAVE MADE IT HEARD, AND THERE IS NO OTHER AMONG YOU) There is a transposition here as well. The sense is: I, and not any of the foreign gods, caused these prophecies to be heard among you so long before.

AND I AM GOD) That I am God.

Latin:

Vers. 12. EGO ANNVNTIAVI) Prædixi salutem vestram.

ET SALVAVI) Et præstiti, ut prædixeram.

AVDITVM FECI, ET NON IN VOBIS ALIVS) Est & hic transpositio. Sensus est: Ego, non autem aliquis deorum extraneorum, effeci ut hæc vaticinia apud vos tan- to ante audirentur.

ET EGO DEVS) Me esse Deum.

## 43:13
v. 13. HE WORKS, AND WHO SHALL TURN IT BACK?) Who will stand in the way if I wish to do anything? See above XIV. 27.

Latin:

v. 13. OPERATVR, ET QVIS AVERTET ILLVD?) Quis obstabit si quid facere velim? Vide supra XIV. 27.

## 43:14
Vers. 14. I HAVE SENT TO BABYLON) I will send against Babylon, namely, enemies.

AND I HAVE BROUGHT DOWN ALL THE BARS) You might better translate: And I will cause them all to descend by fleeing. I will cause the Babylonians to depart in flight to Borsippa. See the passage of Berosus, which we cited in the third book of Testimonies for the Truth of the Christian Religion.

AND THE CHALDEANS) this is, namely.

GLORYING IN THEIR SHIPS) Better: There will be a cry at the ships. They will urge one another to betake themselves to the ships for flight.

Latin:

Vers. 14. MISI IN BABYLONEM) Mittam adversus Babylonem, hostes scilicet.

ET DETRAXI VECTES VNIVERSOS) Melius vertas: Et faciam, ut illi omnes fugiendo descendant. Faciam ut Babylonii fuga abeant ad Borsippa. Vide locum Berosi, quem adduximus libro tertio Testimoniorum pro Veritate Religionis Christianæ.

ET CHALDÆOS) hic est nempe.

IN NAVIBVS SVIS GLORIANTES) Melius: Ad nares erit clamor eorum. Alii alios hortabuntur, ut in naves se conferant ad fugam.

## 43:15
Verse 15. CREATING ISRAEL) see above 7.

Vers. 15. CREANS ISRAEL) vide supra 7.

WHO GAVE IN THE SEA A WAY) In the Red Sea; as above 2.

AND IN THE RUSHING WATERS A PATH) Through the Jordan.

QVI DEDIT IN MARI VIAM) In mari rubro; ut supra 2.

ET IN AQVIS TORRENTIBVS SEMITAM) Per Jordanem.

## 43:17
WHO BROUGHT FORTH THE CHARIOT AND THE HORSE, THE ARMY AND THE STRONG) He led the Egyptians, strong with chariots and horses, from the land into the sea. See Exod. XV. 1. 4. 19.

THEY HAVE SLEPT TOGETHER, AND SHALL NOT RISE) As if he were saying to them: One perpetual night is to be slept.

THEY ARE CRUSHED AS FLAX, AND ARE EXTINGUISHED) Flax denotes Egypt.

QVI EDVXIT QVADRIGAM ET EQVVM, AGMEN ET ROBVSTVM) E terra in mare perduxis Ægyptios curribus & equis validos. Vide Exod. XV. 1. 4. 19.

SIMVL OBDORMIERVN­T, NEC RESVR- GENT) Quasi dicat illis: Nox est perpetua una dormienda.

CONTRITI SVNT QVASI LINVM, ET EX- STINCTI SVNT) Linum notat Ægyptum.

## 43:18
Verse 18. REMEMBER NOT THE FORMER THINGS, AND CONSIDER NOT THE ANCIENT THINGS) As if he were saying, there is no need for me to revolve old things. It will be enough to have new benefits from which I may be known.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NE MEMINERITIS PRIORVM, ET AN- TIQVA NE INTVEAMINI) Quasi dicat, nihil opus me vctera revolvere. Satis erit novorum beneficiorum unde cognoscar.

## 43:19
Verse 19. I WILL MAKE IN THE DESERT A WAY) Easy and level without obstacles, for usually in deserts the places are rugged, similar to above XLI. 16.

AND IN THE PATHLESS PLACE RIVERS) In thirsty places. Compare above XLI. 17.

Latin:

Vers. 19. PONAM IN DESERTO VIAM) Facilem ac planam sine offensis, plerumque enim in desertis loca sunt confragosa, simile supra XLI. 16.

ET IN INVIO FLVMINA) In locis siticulosis. Conf. supr. XLI. 17.

## 43:20
Verse 20. THE BEAST OF THE FIELD SHALL GLORIFY ME, THE DRAGONS AND THE OSTRICHES) By these figures he denotes wild nations.

THAT I MIGHT GIVE DRINK TO MY PEOPLE) That is, consolation.

Latin:

Vers. 20. GLORIFICABIT ME BESTIA AGRI, DRACONES ET STRVTHIONES) His figuris feras gentes denotat.

VT DAREM POTVM POPVLO MEO) Id est, solatium.

## 43:21
Verse 21. THIS PEOPLE HAVE I FORMED FOR MYSELF) I will form these who are returning.

Regarding the material way, Grotius understands verse 19: 'But since it cannot be denied that by these figurative expressions, WILD NATIONS, BEASTS OF THE FIELD, DRAGONS AND OSTRICHES are denoted, which are said to be about to glorify Christ, what is more certain than that the conversion of the nations is predicted here.' Therefore, a way is placed in the desert and the pathless, and waters and rivers are given in the desert, when Christ penetrates with the Gospel into those regions of the nations where no way seemed able to be found before, for the sake of propagating the Gospel there: and He brings it about that those who previously were as a certain desert, completely arid and unfruitful, are most abundantly irrigated by the Gospel, as if by a certain river, so that from faith in Christ, they may bear excellent and copious fruit. And therefore the most savage, most truculent, and most barbarous nations, through the preaching of the Gospel accepted by faith, will so soften, and will lay aside their malice and ferocity and barbarism, that they will sing praises to God because they have been called into the recognition of the Gospel. Therefore the ἐξήγησις (explanation) is added, THIS PEOPLE, gathered from the nations, who seemed completely reprobate, I HAVE FORMED FOR MYSELF, AND MY PRAISE SHALL REMAIN in this and the future age. Which Grotius perverts most badly in this way: 'I have formed this people for myself, that is, I will form those who are returning.' For it is manifest that the discourse was about the wild nations, not about the captive Jews. Therefore He wishes to form them into a people for Himself for His own glory. Nor is it about the erection, or re storation of the Jewish polity. But that the Lord wishes to form a new people for Himself. Where He had dealt with the bringing of the nations from the whole world. How in the preceding verse 7 He had claimed for Himself that anyone should call upon His name, so that he might truly be called by His name. I created him, He says, I formed him, and I made him. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, Eph. II. 10. St. Jerome thus paraphrases verse 19 and following: Therefore I command you this, that among my signs and miracles, by which the most powerful city of Babylon was destroyed, and by which a way was opened for my people in the Red Sea and the Jordan, you should by no means remember the old things, since in the Gospel I am about to do much greater things: in comparison with which the past ought to be passed over in silence. For I shall by no means find a way in the Red Sea anymore, but in the desert of the whole world. Nor shall one river or fountain burst forth from the rock, but many rivers, which may refresh not bodies as before, but thirsting souls: and let that be fulfilled which we read above: You shall drink waters from the fountains of the Savior. Then that which was never done shall come to pass: that all the beasts and dragons and ostriches, which shall dwell in the solitude of the nations, and will be like beasts in the blood of idolatry and the wildness of their morals, may glorify me and praise me. For dragons, which Theodotion alone, as it is written in the Hebrew, called תנים, the rest interpreted as sirens: portentous animals, which with sweet and deadly song used to cast those sailing into the Scyllaean dogs to be torn apart. And this signifies that those who were previously given to pleasure and luxury should be converted to the service of the Lord; although it is better that dragons be understood, because they are joined with ostriches, so that because He was speaking once about the beasts of the solitude, He might place these living creatures, which are familiar to the desert. But they will praise me, He says, and the beasts of the field, and the dragons and the ostriches will glorify me, because I have given waters in the desert of the nations, and rivers in the aridity of the nations, that my people might drink, whom I chose for myself, or my chosen race, and the people whom I acquired with my blood, that they might recount my praises and mighty works. Afterwards, therefore, it follows concerning the Israelite people κατ' ἀντίθεσιν (by way of antithesis), if we wish to hear Jerome here. You have not called upon me, Jacob, nor have you labored for me, Israel, etc. While the beasts of the field, the dragons, and the ostriches are praising me, you, Jacob, have by no means wished to call upon me, nor afterwards to labor, that you might amend your sin with repentance. But as for your thinking that you have offered victims to me and sacrificed rams, know that they were not accepted by me, because they were common to me and to idols. Similarly, Cyril explains concerning the calling of the nations. The desert is understood here, once arid and unfruitful, and as it were a parent of thorns, the multitude of the nations; because there is in it no one at all pious and approved, who certainly knows how to do good. In this desert, therefore, a way appeared, which leads those walking there to the true knowledge of God, to a holy and pure life, to every sense of all good things. We say that this way is either the divine and Evangelical and saving preaching: or perhaps Christ Himself. The beasts of the field seem to denote men who are in a way brutalized by extraordinary ignorance, and living in a rustic manner, etc. All these will celebrate me, as one who has given intelligible (spiritual) water and in a place that lacks water have shown rivers, that I might give drink to my chosen race. What kind of race is this, if not those whom the most wise Peter also addressed, saying, you are a chosen race, etc. 1 Ep. II. To Sebastian Münster, this passage, THIS PEOPLE, WHOM I FORMED, is so clear that he professes in his text at this place that he doubts whether any clearer passage from Scripture can be produced against the perfidious Jews, which so openly abrogates the ceremonies and sacrifices of the Jews. The Prophet says, the Lord will form a new people for Himself, who instead of Mosaic sacrifices would sing His praises.

Latin:

Vers. 21. POPVLVM ISTVM FORMAVI MIHI) Formabo istos reduces.

De via materiali Grotius vers. 19. intelligit: Cum vero diffiteri nequeat, FERAS GENTES figuratis istis loquutionibus, BESTIAS AGRI, DRACONES ET STRUTHIONES denota- ri, quæ glorificaturæ dicuntur Christum, quid certius, quam quod gentium conversio hic prædi- catur. Via ergo in deserto & invio ponitur, & aquæ ac flumina in deserto dantur, cum penetrat Chri- stus Evangelio in eas gentium regiones, ubi nulla antea via inveniri posse videbatur, ad propagan- dum ibi Evangelium: & efficit, ut qui prius tan- quam desertum quoddam plane aridi & infrugiferi erant, ad proferenda bona opera largissime irri- gentur Evangelio, tanquam flumine quodam, ut ex fide in Christum, optimum & copiosum fructum ferant. Ideoq; feræ immanissimæ, truculentissimæ & barbarissimæ gentes, per Evangelii prædicatio- nem fide acceptam, ita mitescent, malitiamque & ferociam, atque barbariem ponent, ut Deo laudes canant, quod in Evangelii agnitionem vocati sint. Ideo additur ἐξήγησις, POPULUM ISTUM, ex gentibus collectum, qui videbatur plane reproba- tus, FORMAVI MIHI, ET LAUS MEA MA- NEBIT in hoc & futuro seculo. Quæ pessime per- vertit Grotius hoc modo: Populum istum formavi mihi, id est, formabo istos reduces. Manifestum enim est de feris gentibus sermonem fuisse, non de Ju- dæis captivis. Illas ergo formare in populum sibi vult in suam gloriam. Neque de erectione, vel re- stauratione politiæ Judaicæ agitur. Sed quod no- vum sibi populum formare velit Dominus. Ubi de adducendis ex orbe universo gentibus egerat. Quomodo in præced. versu 7. sibi vindicarat, quod quis invocet nomen suum, ut vere à nomine suo voce- tur. Creavi eum, inquit, formavi eum, & feci eum. Nam ipsius factura sumus creati in Christo Jesu ad bo- na opera, Eph. II. 10. S. Hieronymus ita παραφράζει vers. 19. & seqq. Igitur hoc præcipio vobis, ut inter signa mea atque miracula, quibus Babylon urbs poten- tissima diruta est, & quibus in mari rubro atque Jor- dane populo meo aperta est via, nequaquam memine- ritis veterum, quum in Evangelio multo sum majora facturus: quorum comparatione præterita sileri de- beant. Nequaquam enim ultra in mari rubro, sed in deserto totius mundi reperiam viam. Nec unus flu- vius, sive fons erumpet de petra, sed multa flumina, quæ non corpora ut prius, sed animas sitientes refi- ciant: & impleatur illud, quod supra legimus: Bibe- tis aquas de fontibus Salvatoris. Tunc quod nunquam factum est, fiet: ut omnes bestiæ & Dracones & Stru- thiones, qui in solitudine gentium morabuntur, & idololatriæ sanguine, morumque feritate bestiarum si- miles erunt, glorificent me, atque collaudent. Pro Dra- conibus, quos solus Theodotio, ut in Hebraico scri- ptum est, appellavit תנים, reliqui Sirenas interpretati sunt: animalia portentosa, quæ dulci carmine atque mortifero navigantes Scyllæis canibus lacerandos præ- cipitabant. Hocque significat, quod voluptati prius & luxuriæ dediti, ad servitutem Domini convertan- tur; licet melius sit Dracones intelligi, quia jungun- tur & Struthiones, ut quia semel de bestiis solitudinis loquebatur, hæc animantia poneret, quæ deserto fami- liaria sunt. Laudabunt autem, inquit, me, & glori- ficabunt bestiæ agri, & Dracones & Struthiones, quia dedi in deserto gentium aquas, & in ariditate nationum flumina, ut biberet populus meus, quem ele- gi mihi, sive genus meum electum, & populus, quem acquisivi Sanguine meo, ut laudes meas virtutesque narraret. Postea ergo de populo Israëlitico sequi- tur κατ' ἀντίθεσιν, si Hieronymum audire hic veli- mus. Non me invocasti Jacob, nec laborasti in me I- sraël, &c. Bestiis agri, Draconibus & Struthionibus laudantibus me, tu Jacob nequaquam me invocare voluisti, nec postea laborare, ut peccatum emendares pœnitentia. Quod autem arbitraris obtulisse te mihi victimas, & arietes immolasse, scias eos à me non esse susceptos, quia mihi & idolis communes erant. Simi- liter de gentium vocatione explicat Cyrillus. Intel- ligitur hic desertum, arida quondam & infructuosa, & velut parens spinarum, multitudo gentium; eo quod sit in ea nullus omnino pius, & probatus, qui certo novit bene agere. In hoc igitur deserto apparuit via, quæ gradientes illac, ad Dei cognitionem veram ad sanctam & puram vitam, ad omnem omnium rerum bonarum sententiam deducit. Hanc viam esse dicimus, vel divinam & Evangelicam & salutarem prædica- tionem: vel forte ipsummet Christum. Bestiæ agri denotare videntur homines præ insigni inscitia effe- ratos quodammodo, & viventes more agresti, &c. Hi omnes celebrabunt me, ut qui dederim aquam intelli- gibilem (spiritualem) & in loco qui caret aquis, flu- mina ostenderim, ut potum dem generi meo electo. Qua- le (istud) genus est, nisi illi, quos etiam sapientissimus Petrus affatus est, inquiens, vos genus electum, &c. 1. Ep. II. Seb. Münstero locus hic, POPULUS ISTE, QVEM FORMAVI, tam clarus est, ut profiteatur in textu ad h. l. se dubitare, an clarior aliquis locus ex Scriptura contra perfidos Judæos produci possit, qui tam aperte abroget Judæorum ceremonias & sacrificia. Populum, inquit Propheta, novum sibi formabit Do- minus, qui pro sacrificiis Mosaïcis caneret laudes ejus

## 43:22
Vers. 22. YOU HAVE NOT CALLED UPON ME, JACOB) God gives the reasons for the deportation of the people: defection from the Law, the beginning of which was through Manasseh. See 2 Kings XXI. 17. NOR HAVE YOU LABORED FOR ME, ISRAEL) You would translate more correctly: Nay, you have been a weariness to me, Israel: as below 11. יגע is translated as κοπᾶν (to be weary) in Ecclesiastes X. 15. and παροξύνειν (to provoke) in Malachi II. 17. Vers. 23. YOU HAVE NOT OFFERED TO ME THE RAM OF YOUR BURNT OFFERING) Not to me, but to Baal and Moloch, and other stars. See the passage already mentioned. I HAVE NOT MADE YOU SERVE IN AN OBLATION, NOR HAVE I GIVEN YOU LABOR IN INCENSE) I have not been an expense to you, but your imaginary gods have. Vers. 24. YOU HAVE NOT BOUGHT ME CANE WITH SILVER) For incense. AND WITH THE FAT OF YOUR VICTIMS YOU HAVE NOT MADE ME DRUNK) You have not delighted me. NEVERTHELESS) On the contrary. YOU HAVE MADE ME SERVE IN YOUR SINS) Your sins are as heavy to me as the hardest servitude is to a man serving it. Vers. 25. I AM, I AM HE, WHO BLOTS OUT YOUR INIQUITIES FOR MY OWN SAKE) Content with your repentance out of my own goodness, I will not remember your former ones. We see, therefore, to what end Grotius labored so much to twist the whole text to the liberation from the Babylonian captivity: so that, indeed, he might pervert in the Jewish manner a notable oracle which deals with the passion of the Messiah. For it is possible to observe this constantly in these Annotations of his, that when prophecies concerning the passion and death of Christ, and the fruit and benefits of the New Testament, occur in the Prophets, the more illustrious they are, the more zealously he labors to cast soot upon them, and to twist them to those things which were done before the coming of Christ, or to the times of the Old Testament. As for the present oracle, Calvin certainly preferred to disparage the Interpreters who explain it concerning Christ, rather than to depart from the Jewish gloss, which Grotius has made his own here. Those who interpret this passage concerning Christ (so Calvin holds) twist the meaning of Scripture. Wherefore this interpretation seems simpler to me: for the Lord complains that men have compelled Him to bear a burdensome load with their sins, when they ought nevertheless to have reverently submitted themselves to Him. For when we rise up against God, we make Him, as it were, a servant by our insolence and petulance. But He explains this better when He says that He has labored, i.e., endured various tediums, and the wickedness of His people. But there is no reason for us to rise up here against the Jews, or against the Judaizing Calvin, and Grotius: For solid and invincible arguments teach that these things must be explained concerning the passion of Christ, on account of which sins are remitted to us. First, it is indisputably certain from the preceding context that the Prophet has been dealing with the benefits obtained by the passion and death of Christ, concerning the calling, regeneration, and protection of the Church, and concerning the conversion of the Gentiles and the propagation of the Gospel throughout the whole world: which, when Grotius wished to drag elsewhere, he had need of remarkable sleight of hand, by which he did violence to the words of the Prophet and the text, as has been shown thus far. Furthermore, in order that the Lord may institute a comparison in v. 18 between the old and new benefits, because the former cannot even be compared with the latter, and because the Church will easily forget the old on account of the greatness of the new benefits: He brings forward as an example the illustrious work of the calling of the Gentiles, that He will place a way in the wilderness and rivers in the pathless waste: and He now subjoins these things concerning His servitude, on account of the sins of men, and our redemption accomplished by His most laborious passion, and the expiation of our sins, of which benefits the old ones of the leading through the Red Sea and similar benefits were scarcely a shadow. Thirdly, lest we doubt that the second person of the Holy Trinity, the Son of God, is speaking here, He has described Himself with a character by no means obscure in verse 14: Thus says the Lord YOUR REDEEMER, THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL.

I am the Lord YOUR HOLY ONE, CREATING ISRAEL, YOUR KING. For the name גאל is proper to Christ the Redeemer, denoting the redemption which is made by right of kinship and by the intervention of a price: who is also called the HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL, because Israel awaited the HOLY OF HOLIES with true faith, and placed his trust in him, who was even made righteousness and sanctification for him, 1 Cor. 1:30. Whom Scripture frequently designates by the name of KING in Zion, or King of Israel, Ps. 2:6, Jer. 23:6, ch. 33:16, etc. Who also gave a way in the Red Sea, and led them in a pillar of cloud and fire, Exod. 14, ch. 23:20, 1 Cor. 10:4, 5. Fourthly, our Goël explains here the cause for which iniquities are blotted out and sins are remitted. That HE does this FOR HIS OWN SAKE, and not indeed for any merits or works of men, that the Israelites ought not to attribute this to their own sacrifices and burnt offerings, but that it is to be ascribed solely to this Goël, the REDEEMER, and to his passion and satisfaction. Therefore, the discourse here is about that servitude in sins, about that labor in iniquities, and about the Goël or REDEEMER, by whose merit of servitude and labor sins and iniquities are blotted out. Now this servitude of the Redeemer, this labor, is the passion of Christ, by which that righteous servant bore our iniquities, and his soul labored in our sins, Isa. 53:11. Fifthly, there is to be observed here specifically an antithesis of the Levitical sacrifices, by which the Lord denies that the Israelites acquired favor for themselves, and of the servitude and labor which the Lord himself sustained, so that they might obtain the remission of sins. Because Scripture is accustomed to oppose the Levitical sacrifices and the expiatory sacrifice of Christ, so that from this comparison and opposition the power of the sacrifice of Christ may shine forth, see Ps. 40:8 seqq. Sixthly, the blessed Hunnius argues thus against Calvin: He for whose sake our sins are blotted out is Christ; for they are blotted out for the sake of Christ alone. But here is introduced he for whose sake our sins are blotted out. And in order to teach that the phrase FOR MY OWN SAKE points to the merit of Christ, [he defends] the coherence of the text against Pareus, the defender of Calvin, who denied that that phrase FOR MY OWN SAKE should be accepted as FOR THE SAKE OF MY MERIT. You have not called upon me, O Jacob, nor have you labored for me, O Israel. You have not offered to me the ram of your burnt offering, and with your victims you have not glorified me: I have not made you serve with an oblation, nor have I provided labor for you in incense, you have not bought me cane with silver, and with the fat of your victims you have not inebriated me (here he removes all human merit: now he subjoins) nevertheless you have made ME serve in your sins, you have provided ME with labor in your iniquities and your sins (namely, having overturned all human merit, he raises up the merit of his own obedience, servitude, and passion alone, and for the sake of this he now subjoins) I, even I, am he who blots out your sins FOR MY OWN SAKE, that is, not for the sake of any labor or merit of yours, but by my own clemency alone through and for the sake of my merit and labor. Seventhly, since we have it clearly explained in Scripture what the SERVITUDE OF JEHOVAH GOEL, our Redeemer, was in our sins, on account of which our sins are blotted out, so that we may obtain the remission of sins, that anthropopathy is not to be admitted, nor are we to descend to an improper and figurative manner of speaking, where it is permitted to adhere to the propriety of the words of Scripture. Wherefore that gloss of Grotius is not to be admitted: YOU HAVE MADE ME SERVE IN YOUR SINS, your sins are as burdensome to me as the hardest servitude is to a man serving in it; since the words, if taken properly as they sound, imply this meaning, that our Redeemer had to be served in our sins: From which proper signification of the words it is a matter of conscience for us to depart, both because hermeneutical rules demand that we adhere to the letter where necessity does not persuade otherwise, and because the Holy Spirit in a clear voice has expounded this servitude in sins as the expiation of our sins, Isa. 53:11, in the knowledge of himself shall he, my righteous servant (who became obedient even unto the death of the cross, Phil. 2), justify many (but what is justification, if not the remission of sins?), and (because) he himself shall bear their iniquities. That servitude, therefore, is the cause of justification and remission, or the blotting out of sins, by which our Messiah, our Redeemer, bore their iniquities by his obedience even unto death and by his laborious servitude. The evidence of this matter compelled Zanchius, having set aside the gloss of his teacher here, to accede to the truth; whose words we repeat: Christ himself, the same, forgives our sins, having expiated them by his own blood, not for our merits, but for his own sake, that is, for the sake of HIS MERITS, HIS PASSION, AND HIS DEATH. Thus, primarily, these two things which the Prophet here proclaims concerning Jehovah: one, that he served in our sins; the other, that he remits them for his own sake, apply to Christ. Because, since he is God manifested in the flesh, he truly both served in our sins, that is, for the sake of our sins: and he blots out iniquities for his own sake, that is, for the sake of his own blood and his own merits, and not, however, those of another. Otherwise, if Christ is a mere man, and not also Jehovah, how is it true what Jehovah says: That he blots out our iniquities for his own sake, when it is manifest in the Scriptures that they are blotted out for the sake of Christ? It is therefore necessary that either it be false what Jehovah says, that he, with the merits of all excluded, blots out iniquities for his own sake, namely, alone: or that Christ himself be Jehovah, who for his own sake, that is, for the sake of his own obedience and servitude, BY WHICH HE WAS MADE MAN, served in our sins. This, however, is consistent with the sacred letters, where we read that Christ washed us in his blood: and exposed himself for the Church (behold the servitude of Christ in our sins) that he might sanctify it, after he had purged it, etc. FOR THE BLOTTING OUT of our iniquities for his own sake, that is, for the sake of his own blood. And that God redeemed the Church with His own blood: and other infinite things of that kind: which teach both, namely that Christ was made a servant, and served on account of our sins: And that the same One BLOTS THEM OUT for His own sake, that is, ON ACCOUNT OF HIS OWN DEATH. Eighthly, it is to be observed, that the Goël here treats not only of His servitude, which He sustained for our sins, but also adds the labor, which He endured in our iniquities. But what that labor is, which He sustained in our iniquities, Isaiah explains thus, c. LIII. 4. Surely He has borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows, He was wounded for OUR INIQUITIES, He was bruised for our transgressions. And verse 11. Because His soul HAS LABORED, He shall see and be satisfied, &c. And the Sacred Psalmist, Psalm LXIX. 4. I have labored crying, my throat is dried, &c. Therefore Israel offered this labor to the Lord in their iniquities: Inasmuch as He was delivered for our sins, Rom. IV. 24. nor did God spare His own Son, but delivered Him up for us, Rom. VIII. 32. Ninthly, the preposition ב denotes the meritorious cause, and ought to be translated ON ACCOUNT OF. Because it was necessary to serve on account of the MERIT of our sins, and to labor for the Lord on account of the merit of our iniquities: For thus the prefix ב is taken in similar cases, as Deut. 24, 16. everyone בחטאו in his sin, that is, on account of his sin, is put to death, Jer. 17, v. 3. בחטאת on account of sin in all thy borders. Compare.

Parallel passages confirm this sense: He was delivered dià PROPTER for our offenses; and similar ones. Tenth, our B. Hunnius very rightly warned in Anti-Par. page 171. The Lord is not introduced here as angry, as if it were his purpose to institute such a complaint against the wickedness of the people, namely, that he had endured various wearinesses on account of it, and is as it were wounded and pierced κατ᾿ ἀνθρωποπάθειαν (after the manner of men); but appeased and propitious: nor are the things which are related here sad, but joyful, so much so that he even makes mention of the sins and iniquities of the people, not in the manner of an angry judge, but of a most benign Savior, who himself bore them and freely forgives them, so that he is unwilling to remember them any further, as the tenor of the words clearly shows. Whatever, therefore, is read here concerning labor and servitude, it tends toward this through a clear antithesis: You did not labor or serve me, so that there is anything for which you may boast: For I labored and served in your sins, whence all the glory of the propitiation obtained and conferred upon you must be attributed entirely to me. Eleventh, therefore, that antithesis which is instituted here must be noted carefully. For in order that the Holy Scripture might show that the propitiation, deletion, and remission of sins is a gift purely gratuitous, at the beginning it removed all those things to which any merit might seem to anyone to inhere, so that it might soon exalt the sacrosanct merit of the one Messiah, serving and laboring in our sins and iniquities, out of respect for whom alone sins are freely and out of mere clemency remitted to them, so that the sense may be: not you, O Jacob (whose name denotes the Church), by your labor or course, or by the merits of offerings and victims, or by the dignity of works, have procured this my clemency for yourself; it must be attributed entirely to me, as one who, in your sins, did not shrink from serving and laboring to expiate them, so that in this way, without cause or merit of yours, out of mercy alone, and thus PROPTER ME IPSUM (for my own sake) with your sins forgiven, I might be propitious. Whence Brentius excellently paraphrases these things thus, q. d. The Lord: I do not acknowledge your zeal, your labor in doing the works of the law. I do not acknowledge your burnt offerings and your victims. For although I prescribed in the law the rites of sacrifices and victims, yet I did not want you to thrust upon me your burnt offerings, your incense, your aromatic reeds, and the fat of your victims with such opinions as you have conceived. For you undertake to do all these sacred things, not so that by them you may preserve the true doctrine concerning the gratuitous remission of sins to be obtained in me alone through faith, and so that by them you may confirm your faith in me, which is the only true use of these sacred things: but you undertake to do them so that by the merits of these works you may expiate your sins and be justified through them. This is a most impious opinion, which is so far from causing you to obtain the deletion of your sins that your sins are rather increased. For I did not impose this burden and this labor upon you, so that you might expiate sins by your works: but rather this burden was imposed upon me, because of the magnitude and gravity of your sins and iniquities, so that I might assume the form of a servant, and all human miseries, and finally even a shameful death, by which I might expiate your sins and reconcile you with God the heavenly Father. For neither can your justice delete sins, but I, I, I say myself, am he who by my passion and death delete your sins, and I delete them in such a way that before the tribunal of God there no longer exists any trace, nor is any mention of them ever made. I delete them, however, not persuaded or appeased by your merits, but PROPTER ME (for my own sake), that is, because of my clemency and gratuitous love, with which I am affected toward the human race, however impious and rebellious. Thus, therefore, Twelfth, the antecedents will cohere most excellently;

God does not render the causes of the Babylonian captivity, because he is not speaking to the people as one angry, but as one propitious and appeased, nor is an antithesis instituted between sacrifices offered not to him, but to Moloch and other idols of the Gentiles, but between the vain worship performed to him, from the false persuasion of the opus operatum, as the Scholastics speak barbarously, and between the true scope and complement of the sacrifices, in the servitude and labor of Christ in our iniquities. For the Lord opposes legal worship, the labor undertaken in worshiping God, to the servitude or his obedience rendered to God, when he was made under the law for our sake, Gal. 4. Then he opposes the offering of various sacrifices to his labor in our iniquities, when he suffered for them and offered himself to God as a propitiatory sacrifice. You have not offered to me the sheep of your burnt offering: For although you offered many sacrifices, yet because you offered them with a perverse opinion, they were all not offered to me: as Osiander rightly: Es ist mir nichts damit gedient gewesen (I have not been served by it at all). And with your victims you did not glorify, or celebrate me, your Messiah, but you celebrated and boasted of your own holiness. And when you ought to have shadowed forth my passion and merit with your sacrifices: you, which ought to have been done for my glory, converted into your own honor and the opinion of your own holiness and satisfaction. I did not make you serve in the offering, nor did I provide labor for you in burning incense: you could have well omitted these, if you had not wished to sacrifice and burn incense with another opinion: certainly I was not served: Du hättest dich wol nicht bemühen dürffen (You would not have needed to trouble yourself). You have not bought me sweet cane with silver, to prepare incense, and you have not sated me with the fat of your sacrifices; more correctly, you have not filled me: For all these things were not pleasing to me, for the reasons mentioned above (For I was never unworthy of these things: but the sacred rites which I instituted, I instituted to this end, that you might acknowledge me, and value MY Merits, not YOURS.) Since these things are so, I did not cause you (O Israel) trouble, or provide you with labors, but you made me serve in the expiating of your sins, you provided me with labor in the blotting out of your iniquities (For the sins of the human race could not otherwise be expiated and blotted out, unless the Son of God became man, and assumed the form of a servant (Phil. 2.) and undertook most troublesome labors, indeed horrible torments of soul and body to be endured: by the sustaining of which he might appease the most just wrath of the heavenly Father.
