I am (says the Son of God) I, I say, am he, who blots out your iniquities, not because of your merits, but because of me out of the immense love, with which I pity the human race, and for the sake of my praise and glory, that I may be heard as the SOLE, and UNIQUE REDEEMER of the human race. And I will no longer remember your sins: provided you truly believe in me. Some, by way of κατ' ἀνθυποφορὰν, wish these to be subjected to the preceding, in this way: Israel says, if you have called the nations, that they may praise you, what else do I do! Do I not sing Psalms and Hymns to you! Do I not offer you incense and sacrifices! The Lord answers, you do not call upon me, and your invocations, praises, sacrifices, are not my praises, but reproaches. Thirteenth, the sense which Grotius carves out does not agree with the truth. For had not Israel offered burnt offerings, had he not labored with incense? Indeed, the Lord complained not of neglected, but of offered [sacrifices] without faith, Isa. 1. nor did he reproach them for the paucity, but for the multitude of such offerings v. 11. To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices, etc.

Therefore, the Grotian στρεβλότητι being dismissed, it remains that we acknowledge that this treats of the satisfactory obedience and passion of the Messiah: which sense Corn. à Lap. observes that Leo Castrius, along with Lactantius, handed down in this place.

You have made me serve with your sins, that is, to put on the form of a servant, to take upon myself the punishments of a servant, namely the cross. And therefore the LXX thus translate it according to St. Jerome, ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις σὂ ὑπερησπησά σε, I defended you in your sins, and as a hyperaspistes, I opposed myself as a shield for you against the wrath of God. Thus also Cyril, Theodoret, and Eusebius in book X of the Demonstratio Evangelica read it from the LXX. Our B. Luther says thus on this passage: It is a notable passage, that all the righteousness of the law, all works, however great, holy, or specious they may be, are of no avail for obtaining righteousness before God, but are only sins for which it was necessary for Christ to make satisfaction and to labor. But this is our righteousness, that Christ labored. And this one article is of our faith and religion, which the whole world ignores. For all other doctrines judge thus, that he who has sinned ought to be punished. But this article teaches otherwise, namely that we sin, and another makes satisfaction for the sin, and takes the punishment of the sin upon himself, as John says: The Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. Therefore no punishment of ours makes satisfaction, not even for the smallest sin, but the suffering of Christ alone has made satisfaction for the sins of all. Our people unanimously defend this explanation of the Megalandros. To this, not only Leo Castrius from among the Papists, but many others add their approval, in that the discourse here is about the satisfaction of Christ. Vatablus rendered and explained it thus: Nay rather, you have made me serve in your sins, or because of your sins, etc., as if Christ were saying: I came that I might blot out your sins. In the margin of the old text in his Bibles edited by Rob. Stephanus, it is held thus at v. 22 seqq.: External worship destitute of faith is rejected: Christ made man, through whom our sins are remitted to us. No righteousness in us. Hector Pintus: The sense is, he says, that the sacrifices of the old law did not blot out sins, therefore I came, that I might blot them out. The sins of the world were the cause that I should take the form of a servant, undergo huge labors, and immolate myself. You have made me serve, and I, because I am merciful, blot out your sins for my own sake: Therefore also John said: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. Casparus Sanctius, although he leans toward another gloss, nevertheless favors our explanation not obscurely, when he has it thus: If you refer these to the time of the Gospel, and the economy of Christ, they have wonderful force: because when there was no such power that could make satisfaction for the sins of men, Christ, assuming the form of a servant, and undergoing the weight of a condition more than servile, a most bitter pain, and because those ancient sacrifices were of little efficacy to expiate sin, he willed to be the victim, which alone would have expiatory power for all from sins. Most of the authors take it in this sense, and another translation of the Septuagint greatly favors it, which has it thus: But in your sins I defended you. As Eusebius reads in book 10 of the Demonstratio, Cyril, Theodoret, and the Complutensian Codices, and indeed even Jerome, although he follows another translation in his Commentaries. The Complutensian edition has προΐσκησα, that is, I opposed myself as a shield in your iniquities, that is, against your iniquities. By which words it is best expressed what Christ has conferred upon us, and how it is said that he bore labor and pain for us. Finally, from the Reformed themselves, although not only Calvin, but also Zwingli and Wolffgangus Musculus, as well as the authors of the Belgian notes, favor the Jewish gloss; others nevertheless confirm with their approval the genuine opinion hitherto approved by us. Oecolampadius has it thus on this passage: Because man could not by himself make satisfaction to God, the Son of God was made man, the servile form having been assumed, and he served for the sake of abolishing our sins. For he himself bore our iniquities; below 53. 1. Pet. 2. For he refutes Calvin's gloss, concerning

the Jews, in this way: The Jews explain this passage concerning the patience of God, bearing those who sin long-sufferingly, and not prohibiting them from sins. But the following parts prove that this was the way of redemption, with Christ ministering: for he says, I blot out iniquities, I, to wit, who bear: and whom you have made to serve in sins, I blot out the sins, not for my own sake, i.e., for the sake of my own goodness: and I not only dismiss the guilt, but with the guilt also the punishment. Pareus himself, when he undertook the defense of his Calvin, had to admit in Calvin. Orthod. p. 160, that servitude and the labor of our sins are attributed to Christ the Mediator PROPERLY, but to Jehovah according to an anthropopathy: but one must not depart from the literal sense, unless necessity compels. Furthermore, he judged thus, that Calvin did NOT quite conveniently depart entirely from the interpretation of the rest: Finally, he acknowledged that a distinguished argument for the Deity of Christ is thus openly overturned for us Christians, which we oppose to the Jews and Arians in this way: This one serving and laboring in our sins, and blotting out our iniquities for his own sake, is Jehovah. But this same one is Christ, Is. 53. Therefore Christ is Jehovah. What is this other than for Calvin to Judaize and Arianize!

Latin:

Vers. 22. NON ME INVOCASTI JACOB) Causas reddit Deus deportationis populi: defectionem à Lege, cu- jus initium per Manassen. Vid. 2. Reg. XXI. 17. NEC LABORASTI IN ME ISRAEL) Rectius vertas: Imo tædio fuisti mihi Israël: ut infra 11. יגע κοπᾶν ver- titur Ecclesiastæ X. 15. & παροξύνειν Malach. II. 17. Vers. 23. NON OBTULISTI MIHI ARIETEM HOLOCAUSTI TUI) Non mihi, sed Baali & Molocho, astrisque aliis. Vide dictum jam locum. NON TE SERVIRE FECI IN OBLATIONE, NEC LABOREM TIBI PRÆBUI IN THURE) Ego tibi sumptui non fui, sed dii tui imaginarii. Vers. 24. NON EMISTI MIHI ARGENTO CA- LAMUM) Ad suffitum. ET ADIPE VICTIMARUM TUARUM NON INEBRIASTI) Non oblectasti me. VERUNTAMEN) Contra. SERVIRE ME FECISTI IN PECCATIS TUIS) Tam gravia mihi sunt peccata tua, quam servitus durissima homini eam servienti. Vers. 25. EGO SUM, EGO SUM IPSE, QUI DE- LEO INIQUITATES TUAS PROPTER ME) Ex mea bonitate pœnitentia vestra contentus, priorum non recor- dabor. Videmus ergo, quo fine sudarit tantopere Grotius, ut textum universum ad liberationem è captivitate Babylonica detorqueret: ut nempe Oraculum insigne, quod de passione Messiæ agit, Judaico more perverteret. Id enim perpetuo in hisce ejus Annotatis observare licet, cum vaticinia de Christi passione & morte, ejusque fructu ac be- neficiis Novi Testam. quæ in Prophetis occurrunt, quo illustriora illa sunt, eo impensius ipsum labo- rare, ut fuliginem offundat iisdem, & ad ea, quæ gesta sunt ante adventum Christi, vel ad tempora Vet. Test. illa detorqueat. Quod ad præsens ora- culum, maluit sane Calvinus etiam sugillare Inter- pretes, qui de Christo explicant, quam à Judaica glossa recedere, quam hic suam fecit Grotius. Qui hunc locum de Christo exponunt (ita habet Calvinus) sensum Scripturæ torquent. Quare simplicior mihi videtur interpretatio hæc: conqueritur enim Domi- nus, quod homines eum peccatis suis molestum onus subire coëgerint, qui tamen reverenter se ei subjicere debuissent. Nam cum insurgimus adversus Deum, eum quasi servum protervia & petulantia nostra fa- cimus. Hoc autem melius exponit, cum ait, se labo- rasse, i. e. varia tædia devorasse, & nequitiam popu- li sui. At non est, quod assurgamus hic Judæis, aut Calvino Judaizanti, Grotioque: Nam quod hæc de Christi passione, ob quam peccata nobis remit- tuntur, explicanda sint, argumenta solida & invicta docent. Primum ex antecedentibus ἀναντιῤῥήτως certum est, Prophetam egisse de beneficiis passio- ne ac morte Christi partis, de vocatione, regenera- tione, protectione Ecclesiæ, & de conversione gen- tium, ac propagatione Evangelii per universum terrarum orbem: Quæ cum Grotius aliorsum tra- here voluit, insigni opus κυβεία habuit, qua verbis Prophetæ, & textui vim fecit, ut hactenus osten- sum. Porro ut collationem instituat Dominus v. 18. inter vetera, & nova beneficia, quod ista ne compa- rari quidem cum hisce possint, præ novorum be- neficiorum magnitudine, veterum facile oblitura sit Ecclesia: illustre imprimis opus vocationis gen- tium in medium adducit, quod positurus sit in de- serto viam, & in invio flumina: ac subjungit nunc ista de servitute sua, ob peccata hominum, ac re- demptione nostra facta passione sua laboriosissima, & expiatione peccatorum nostrorum, quorum be- neficiorum vix umbra quædam fuere vetera dedu- ctionis per mare rubrum & similia beneficia. Ter- tio ne ambigamus, secundam personam SS. Trini- tatis Filium Dei hic loqui, charactere minime ob- scuro se descripsit vers. 14. Hæc dicit Dominus RE- DEMPTOR VESTER, SANCTUS ISRAEL.

Ego Dominus SANCTUS VESTER, CREANS ISRAEL, REX VESTER. Nam nomen גאל Chri- sti redemptoris proprium est, redemptionem, quæ jure cognationis, & pretii interventu fit, deno- tans: qui & SANCTUS ISRAEL dicitur, quod SANCTUM SANCTORUM vera fide expecta- rit Israël, & in eo fiduciam suam collocarit, qui ipsi etiam factus est justitia & sanctificatio, 1. Cor. I. v. 30. Quem nomine REGIS in Zion, vel Regis Israë Scriptura frequenter designat Ps. II. 6. Jer. XXIII. 6. c. XXXIII. 16. &c. Qui etiam dedit in mari rubro viam, & in columna nubis & ignis ipsos duxit, Exod. 14. c. XXIII. 20. 1. Cor. X. 4. 5. Quarto explicat hic Goël noster causam, ob quam iniquitates deleantur, & peccata remittantur. Quod id IPSE faciat PRO- PTER SE, non vero propter ulla merita aut opera hominum, quod non sacrificiis ac holocaustis suis id tribuere debeant Israëlitæ, sed unice huic Goëli REDEMPTORI accepto ferendum id, sit ejusque passioni ac satisfactioni. De illa ergo servitute in peccatis, de illo labore in iniquitatibus & Goël vel REDEMPTORIS sermo hic est, cujus servitutis & laboris merito delentur peccata & iniquitates. Hæc autem servitus Redemptoris, hic labor est passio Christi, qua servus ille justus iniquitates no- stras portavit, & anima ejus laboravit in peccatis nostris, Esa. LIII. 11. Quinto observanda hic specia- tim ἀντίθεσις est sacrificiorum Leviticorum, quibus negat Dominus, Israëlitas gratiam sibi comparasse, & servitutis ac laboris, quem sustinuit ipse Domi- nus, ut peccatorum remissionem consequerentur. Quia solet Scriptura opponere sacrificia Levitica, & sacrificium Christi expiatorium, ut ex hac colla- tione & oppositione vis sacrificii Christi elucescat, vid. Psal. XL. 8. seqq. Sexto B. Hunnius ita argu- mentatur contra Calvinum: Is propter quem de- lentur peccata nostra, est Christus; delentur enim propter solum Christum. At hic introducitur is, propter quem delentur peccata nostra. Atque ut doceat phrasin PROPTER ME digitum intende- re ad Christi meritum, συνέχειαν textus adversus Pareum, Calvini hyperaspisten, qui negabat phra- sin illam PROPTER ME sic accipiendam esse, PROPTER MERITUM MEUM. Non me in- vocasti Jacob, nec laborasti in me Israël. Non obtu- listi mihi arietem holocausti tui, & victimis tuis non glorificasti me: non te servire feci in oblatione, nec laborem tibi præbui in thure, non emisti mihi argento calamum, & adipe victimarum tuarum, non ine- briasti me (removet hic omne humanum meritum: jam subnectit) veruntamen ME servire fecisti in peccatis tuis, præbuisti MIHI laborem in iniquitati- bus peccatis tuis (nimirum everso omni humano merito, solius suæ obedientiæ, servitutis & passionis meritum attollit, atque hujus gratia nunc subdit) Ego ego sum, qui deleo peccata tua PROPTER ME, id est, non propter ullum laborem aut meri- tum tuum, sed sola mea clementia per & propter me- ritum & laborem meum. Septimo cum in Scriptura clare explicatum habeamus, quænam SERVI- TUS JEHOVÆ GOEL Redemptoris nostri fuerit in peccatis nostris, ob quam delentur pecca- ta nostra, ut consequamur remissionem peccato- rum, non est admittenda illa ἀνθρωποπαθεια, ne- que ad impropriam & figuratam loquendi ratio- nem descendendum, ubi proprietati verborum Scripturæ inhærere licet. Quapropter non admit- tenda glossa illa Grotii; SERVIRE ME FECISTI IN PECCATIS TUIS, tam gravia mihi sunt peccata tua, quam servitus durissima homini eam servienti; siquidem proprie verba, uti sonant, infe- rant hanc sententiam, quod Redemptori nostro ser- viendum fuerit in peccatis nostris: A qua propria ver- borum significatione discedere religio nobis est, tum quia regulæ Hermeneuticæ postulant, ut inhæ- reamus literæ, ubi aliud non suadet necessitas, tum quia λευκάδι φωνῇ S. S. hanc servitutem in pec- catis, ceu peccatorum nostrorum expiatricem ex- posuit, Esa. LIII. 11. in scientia sui justificabit ipse ju- stus servus meus (qui obediens factus est, usque ad mortem crucis, Phil. II.) multos, (justificatio au- tem quid est, nisi peccatorum remissio?) & (quia) iniquitates eorum ipse portabit. Illa ergo servitus causa est justificationis & remissionis, vel deletio- nis peccatorum, qua iniquitates eorum portavit obedientia sua, usque ad mortem, ac servitute labo- riosa, Messias redemptor noster. Evidentia hujus rei coëgit Zanchium, ut hic Præceptoris sui glossa posthabita, veritati accederet; cujus verba repeti- mus: Idem ipse Christus peccata nostra ita suo san- guine expiata condonat, non propter merita nostra, sed propter se, hoc est, propter MERITA SUA, PASSIONEM, ET MORTEM SUAM. Ita prime hæc duo, quæ hic prædicat Propheta, de Jeho- vah: unum, quod servierit in peccatis nostris; alte- rum, quod illa remittat propter se, competunt in Chri- stum. Quia, cum sit Deus manifestatus in carne, ve- re & servivit in peccatis, id est, propter peccata no- stra: & delet iniquitates propter se, hoc est, propter suum sanguinem, meritaque sua, non autem aliena. Alioqui Christus si purus est homo, & non etiam Je- hovah, quomodo verum est, quod ait Jehovah: Se delere iniquitates nostras propter se, cum manifestum sit in Scripturis, eas deleri propter Christum? Est igi- tur necessè, ut aut falsum sit, quod ait Jehovah, se ex- clusis omnium meritis, delere iniquitates propter se, nempe solum: aut Christus sit ipse Jehova, qui propter se, hoc est, propter suam obedientiam & servitutem, QUA FACTUS HOMO, servivit in peccatis nostris. Hoc vero consentaneum est cum sacris literis, ubi legimus, Christum lavisse nos in sanguine suo: & seipsum exposuisse pro Ecclesia (ecce Christi servitu- tem in peccatis nostris) ut eam sanctificaret, post- quam purgasse, &c. IN DELETIONEM iniqui- tatum nostrarum propter se, id est, propter suam san- guinem. Et Deum redemisse Ecclesiam suo sanguine: & alia id genus infinita: quæ utrumque docent, nempe Christum factum esse servum, serviisseque propter pec- cata nostra: Et eundem EA DELERE propter se- ipsum, hoc est, PROPTER SUAM MORTEM. Octavo observandum, quod non solum de servitu- te sua hîc agat Goël, quam ob peccata nostra susti- nuit, sed laborem etiam addat, quem exantlavit in iniquitatibus nostris. Quis autem labor ille sit, quem sustinuit in nostris iniquitatibus, ita expli- cat Esaias c. LIII. 4. Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, & dolores nostros ipse portavit, ipse vulneratus est pro- pter INIQVITATES NOSTRAS, attritus est propter scelera nostra. Et vers. 11. Pro eo, quod LA- BORAVIT anima ejus, videbit & saturabitur, &c. Et Hieropsaltes Psal. LXIX. 4. Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ, &c. Hunc ergo laborem præbuit Domino Israël in iniquitatibus suis: Siqui- dem traditus sit propter peccata nostra, Rom. IV. 24. nec pepercerit Deus Filio suo proprio, quin traderet ipsum pro nobis, Rom. VIII. 32. Nono præpositio ב causam meritoriam notat, & verti debet PRO- PTER. Quod propter MERITUM peccatorum nostrorum serviendum, propter meritum iniquita- tum nostrarum laborandum fuerit Domino: Sic enim præfixum ב accipitur in similibus, uti Deut. 24, 16. quisq; בחטאו in peccato suo, id est. propter peccatum suum, morte afficitur, Jer. 17, v. 3. בחטאת propter peccatum in omnibus terminis tuis. Confer.

Quem sensum loca parallela confirmant Traditus est dià PROPTER delicta no- stra; & similia. Decimo monuit rectissime B. Hunnius noster in Anti-Par. pag. 171. Introduci hic Dominum non iracundum, ut propositum ei sit, talem querelam contra nequitiam populi instituere, quod nempe ob eandem varia tædia devorarit, & κατ᾿ ἀν- θρωποπάθειαν quasi vulneratus & confixus sit; sed placatum & propitium: neque tristia sint, quæ hic re- feruntur, sed jucunda, adeo ut etiam peccatorum & iniquitatum populi mentionem faciat, non in modum irati judicis, sed benignissimi Servatoris, qui ipse ea portarit, ac gratis condonet, ut porrò illorum amplius recordari nolit, sicut verborum tenor clare ostendit. Quicquid ergo hic de labore & servitute legitur, id perclaram antithesin huc tendit: Tu non laborasti aut serviisti mihi, ut quicquam sit, quod glorieris: Ego enim laboravi & servivi in peccatis tuis, unde omnis gloria partæ & collatæ tibi propitiationis mihi in solidum attribuenda est. Undecimo ergo no- tanda sedulo est illa, quæ hic instituitur antithesis. Ut enim S. S. ostenderet, propitiationem, deletionem & remissionem peccatorum donum esse mere gratui- tum, initio removit universa ea, quibus ullam ali- quod meritum inesse videri cuipiam queat, ut mox sacrosanctum meritum attollat unius Messiæ, servi- entis, ac laborantis in peccatis & iniquitatibus no- stris, cujus solius respectu gratis, & ex mera cle- mentia remittuntur eis peccata, ut sensus sit; non tu ô Jacob (cujus nomen Ecclesiam notat) tuo labore vel cursu, vel oblationem & victimarum meritis, vel operum dignitate hanc meam clementiam tibi concilia- sti, in solidum ea mihi accepta ferenda est, ut qui in pec- catis tuis, ad expiandum illa non horruerim servire & laborare, ut hoc modo citra causam & meritum tuum, ex sola misericordia, adeoque PROPTER ME IPSUM tibi condonatis peccatis, essem propitius. Unde egregie Brentius hæc ita παραφράζει, q. d. Dominus: Non agnosco vestrum studium, vestrum laborem in faciendis operibus legis. Non agnosco ve- stra holocausta, & vestras victimas. Etsi enim præ- scripsi in lege ritus sacrificiorum, & victimarum, ta- men non volui, ut talibus opinionibus, quales vos con- cepistis, obtruderetis mihi vestra holocausta, vestra thura, vestros calamos aromaticos, & vestrarum vi- ctimarum adipem. Suscipitis enim omnia hæc sacra facienda, non ut his conservetis veram doctrinam de gratuita remissione peccatorum in me solo, per fidem consequenda, & ut his fidem vestram in me confir- metis, qui solus est verus horum sacrorum usus: sed suscipitis ea facienda, ut meritis horum operum ve- stra peccata expietis, & per ea justificemini. Hæc est impiissima opinio, quæ in tantum non sit, ut consequa- mini deletionem peccatorum vestrorum, ut potius peccata vestra augeantur. Non enim ego vobis impo- sui hoc onus, & hunc laborem, ut vos vestris operibus expiaretis peccata: sed potius mihi hoc onus, propter magnitudinem & gravitatem vestrorum peccato- rum, ac iniquitatum impositum est, ut ego assumam formam servi, & omnes humanas ærumnas, ac tan- dem etiam probrosam mortem, quo vestra peccata expiem, & reconciliem vos cum Deo Patre cœlesti. Neque enim vestra justitia potest peccata delere, sed ego, EGO, inquam ipse, is sum, qui mea passione & morte deleo peccata vestra, ac ita deleo, ut coram tri- bunali Dei non amplius extet aliquod vestigium, nec ulla unquam fiat mentio eorum. Deleo autem ea, non vestris meritis persuasus aut delinitus, sed PRO- PTER ME, hoc est, propter meam clementiam, & gratuitam dilectionem, qua erga humanum genus, quamvis impium, & rebelle afficior. Sic itaque Duodecimo antecedentia optime cohærebunt;

Non causas reddit Deus captivitatis babylonicae, quia non loquitur populo, ut iratus, sed ut propi- tius ac placatus, neque antithesis instituitur, inter sacrificia non sibi, sed Molocho & idolis aliis gen- tilium oblata, sed inter cultum vanum sibi præsti- tum, è persuasione falsa operis operati, ut Schola- stici barbare loquuntur, & inter verum scopum & complementum sacrificiorum, in servitute & labore Christi in iniquitatibus nostris. Nam opponit Do- minus cultum legalem, laborem in colendo Deo su- sceptum, servituti vel obedientiae suæ, Deo præstitæ, quando factus est sub lege nostri causâ, Gal. 4. tum oblationem variorum sacrificiorum, labori suo in iniquitatibus nostris, quando pro iisdem passus est, ac Deo se obtulit in sacrificium propitiatorium. Non obtulisti mihi ovem holocausti tui: Etsi enim multas hostias obtulisti, tamen quia perversa opinio- ne obtulisti, eæ omnes non sunt mihi oblatæ: ut recte Osiander: Es ist mir nichts damit gedient gewesen. Et victimis tuis non glorificasti, seu celebrasti me, Messiam tuum, sed celebrasti & jactasti tuam san- ctitatem. Cumque meam passionem & meritum de- buisses adumbrare tuis sacrificiis: tu, quæ ad gloriam meam fieri debuerant, in tuum honorem & opinio- nem propriæ sanctitatis & satisfactionis convertisti. Non te servire feci in oblatione, nec laborem tibi præbui in thure adolendo: potuisses hæc bene omit- tere, si non alia opinione sacrificare & adolere vo- luisses: mihi certe non est inservitum: Du hättest dich wol nicht bemühen dürffen. Non emisti mihi argento calamum aromaticum, ad parandum thy- miama, & adipe victimarum tuarum non inebria- sti me; rectius, non replevisti me: Hæc enim omnia non fuerunt mihi grata, propter supra commemora- tas causas (Neque enim unquam indigni istis rebus: sed quæ ego sacra institui, in eum finem institui, ut me agnosceres, & Merita MEA, non TVA magni faceres.) Quæ cum ita sint, non ego tibi (o Israël) molestias exhibui, aut labores præbui, verum tu servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis expiandis, tu præ- buisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis delendis (Non enim aliter potuerunt generis humani peccata expiari & deleri, nisi ut Filius Dei fieret homo, & assumeret formam servi (Phil. 2.) atque susciperet mo- lestissimos labores, imo horribiles cruciatus animi & corporis perferendos: quibus sustinendis placaret justissimam iram Patris cœlestis. Ego sum (inquit Filius Dei) ego, inquam, sum ipse, qui deleo iniqui- tates tuas, non propter tua merita, sed propter me ex immenso amore, quo misereor humani generis, & propter laudem & gloriam meam, ut audiam SO- LUS, & UNICUS humani generis REDEM- TOR. Et peccatorum tuorum non amplius recor- dabor: modo vere in me credideris. Nonnulli κατ' ἀνθυποφορὰν hæc superioribus subjici volunt, hoc modo: Dicit Israël, si gentes vocasti, ut te laudent, ego quid aliud ago! Nonne tibi Psalmos & Hymnos decanto! nonne tibi offero thura & victimas! Re- spondet Dominus, non me invocas, & tuæ invoca- tiones, laudes, sacrificia, non meæ laudes, sed vitupe- ria sunt. Decimo tertio veritati non consonat sensus, quem exsculpit Grotius. Annon enim obtulerat Israël holocausta, annon thure labora- rat? Imo non de neglectis, sed de oblatis sine fide, questus est Dominus, Esa. 1. nec paucitatem, sed multitudinem talium oblationum ipsis exprobra- vit v. 11. Quo mihi multitudinem victimarum ve- strarum, &c.

Missa ergo στρεβλότητι Grotiana superest, ut agnoscamus de obedientia & passione Messiæ satis- factoria hic agi: quam sensum cum Lactantio Leo- nem Castrium tradidisse Corn. à Lap. observat h. m.

Tuis peccatis servire, id est, servi carnem induere, servi pœnas, scilicet crucem suscipere me fecisti. At- quo ideo LXX. ita juxta S. Hieronymum vertere, ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις σὂ ὑπερησπησά σε, in peccatis tuis defendi te, & quasi hyperaspistes, scutum me pro te iræ Dei opposui. Ita & ex LXX. legere Cyrillus, Theo- doretus, & Eusebius lib. X. demonstr. Evangel. B. Lutherus noster ita ad h. l. Est insignis locus, quod universæ justitiæ legis, omnia, quantumvis magna, sancta, speciosa opera, nihil prosint ad justitiam co- ram Deo consequendam, sed sint tantum peccata pro quibus satisfacere & laborare Christum necesse fue- rit. Hæc autem nostra est justitia, quod Christus la- boravit. Atque hic unus articulus est nostræ fidei & religionis, quem totus mundus ignorat. Omnes enim aliæ doctrinæ ita judicant, eum debere puniri, qui pec- cavit. Hic autem articulus diversum docet, nempe quod nos peccemus, & alius pro peccato satisfaciat, & peccati pœnam in se recipiat, sicut Johannes dicit: Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Nulla igitur nostra pœna satisfacit, ne quidem pro minimo pecca- to, sed unius Christi supplicium pro omnium peccatis satisfecit. Quam Megalandri explicationem ὁμο- θυμαδὸν propugnant nostrates. Cui è Pontificiis non Leo Castrius tantum, sed multi alii calculum eatenus addunt, quod hic de satisfactione Christi sermo sit. Vatablus ita reddidit, & exposuit: Quin potius servire me fecisti in peccatis tuis, vel ob pecca- ta tua, &c. ac si dicat Christus: Ego veni, ut delerem peccata tua. Ad marginem textus veteris in ejus Bibliis à Rob. Stephano editis ita habetur ad v. 22. seqq. Cultus externus fide destitutus rejicitur: Chri- stus factus homo, per quem remittuntur nobis pecca- ta. Nulla in nobis justitia. Hector Pintus: Sensus est, inquit, sacrificia veteris legis non delebant pecca- ta, ideo ego veni, ut ea delerem. Peccata mundi in causa fuerunt, ut ego formam servi acciperem, ingen- tes labores subirem, & me ipsum immolarem. Tu me servire fecisti, & ego propter me, quia misericors sum, deleo peccata tua: Ideo & Johannes dicebat: Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Caspa- rus Sanctius, etsi in aliam glossam propendeat, no- stræ tamen explicationi non obscure favet, cum ita habet: Si hæc ad tempus Evangelii referas, Christique œconomiam, miram habent vim: quia cum nulla es- set tanta facultas, quæ pro hominum peccatis satisfa- cere posset, Christus servilem formam assumens, & plusquam servilis conditionis pondus dolorem subiit quam acerbissimum, & quia sacrificia illa antiqua parum erant ad expiandum peccatum efficacia, vi- ctima esse voluit, quæ una pro omnibus vim haberet à peccatis expiatoriam. In hanc sententiam capiunt plerique ex auctoribus, & favet valde alia translatio Septuaginta, quæ sic habet: Sed in peccatis tuis defen- di te. Ut legunt Eusebius lib. 10. demonstr. Cyrillus, Theodoretus, & Codices Complut. imo & Hieronym. licet in Commentariis aliam sequatur translationem. Complutensis editio προΐσκησα habet, hoc est, pro scuto me opposui in iniquitatibus tuis, id est, con- tra iniquitates. Quibus verbis optime exprimitur, quid nobis Christus contulerit, & quomodo dicatur, laborem & dolorem pro nobis pertulisse. E Reforma- tis denique ipsis, etsi non Calvinus modo, sed & Zvinglius, & Wolffgangus Musculus, ut & autores notarum Belgicarum Judaicæ glossæ faveant; alii tamen sententiam genuinam hactenus à nobis pro- batam, calculo suo comprobant. Oecolampadius ita ad hunc locum habet: Quia homo per se non po- tuit satisfacere Deo, Filius Dei homo factus est, ser- vili forma suscepta, servivitque propter peccata nostra abolenda. Ipse enim portavit iniquitates nostras; in- fra 53. 1. Petr. 2. Refellit enim Calvini glossam, de

, Judæis, hoc modo: Judæi hunc locum exponunt de patientia Dei, peccantes longanimiter ferentis, & à peccatis non prohibentis. Atqui sequentia compro- bant hanc redemptionis fuisse viam, ministrante Christo: dicit enim, ego deleo iniquitates, ego scil. qui porto: & quem fecisti servire in peccatis, deleo pec- cata, non propter me, h. e. propter meam ipsius bonita- tem: & non solum culpam dimitto, sed cum culpa etiam pœnam. Pareus ipse cum defensionem susce- pit Calvini sui, fateri debuit in Calvin. Orthod. p. 160. Christo Mediatori servitutem & laborem no- strorum peccatorum PROPRIE, Jehovæ autem κατ' ἀνθρωποπάθειαν tribui: à proprietate autem discedendum non est, nisi cogat necessitas. Adhæc ita censuit, Calvinum NON SATIS commode à reli- quorum interpretatione sua omnino recedere: De- nique agnovit præclarum Deitatis Christi argu- mentum ita aperte nobis Christianis everti, quod hinc Judæis & Arianis sic opponimus: Iste serviens & laborans in peccatis nostris, & delens iniquitates nostras propter se, est Jehova. Idem vero iste est Chri- stus Es. 53. Christus igitur est Jehova. Quid hoc aliud est, quam Calvinum Judaizare & Arianizare!

## 43:26
Vers. 26. BRING ME TO REMEMBRANCE) Tell me what you have done, and what you have suffered, that we may see whether you have suffered what you have suffered, justly or unjustly.

AND LET US JUDGE TOGETHER) Concerning that calamity of yours.

DECLARE IF YOU HAVE ANYTHING, THAT YOU MAY BE JUSTIFIED) If you have anything by which you hope you can show that these things happen to you undeservedly.

Latin:

Vers. 26. REDVC ME IN MEMORIAM) Narra mi- hi quæ feceris, & quæ passus sis, ut videamus, quæ pertu- listi, jure an injuria pertuleris.

ET JVDICEMVR SIMVL) Super ista calamitate vestra.

NARRA SI QVID HABES, VT JVSTIFICE- RIS) Si quid habes quo speres te posse ostendere immerito tibi hæc evenire.

## 43:27
Vers. 27. YOUR FIRST FATHER HAS SINNED) Manasseh. For kings are the fathers of peoples.

AND YOUR INTERPRETERS HAVE TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME) The priests and Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 27. PATER TVVS PRIMVS PECCAVIT) Manasses. Reges enim patres populorum.

ET INTERPRETES TVI PRÆVARICATI SVNT IN ME) Sacerdotes & Levitæ.

## 43:28
AND I HAVE PROFANED THE HOLY PRINCES) In the Hebrew: of holiness. I have caused the Pontiffs themselves not to be distinguished from the profane common people: because they have to live without a temple, without victims, without priestly attire. God speaks these things as if in the very time of the captivity.

I HAVE GIVEN JACOB TO SLAUGHTER) Nebuchadnezzar killed very many Jews. See 2 Kings 25, 6. 21.

AND ISRAEL TO BLASPHEMY) To reproaches, that is, I exposed the descendants of Israel to servitude, namely the Jerusalemites and others whom Nebuzaradan deported.

By the first father, Hebrew and Christian interpreters commonly understand either Adam, through whom sin was introduced, or Abraham, whom the Jews boasted was their father, who once served idols, Josh. 24, or sinned by diffidence, which Jerome and others wish to be referred to from Gen. 15. Other Fathers take it in a general sense, so that the singular number is placed for the plural, i.e., Your fathers sinned before against me, and you follow their footsteps. What then will you relate, by which you might justify yourself? Nor do they refer these things to the causes or times of the captivity, if you except Musculus, and perhaps a few others. Grotius seems to have followed him here; that by the Father the King is understood; although Musculus proposed that opinion only tentatively, nor could he rest in it. For it is added that this opinion is not sufficiently proven and that it is more improbable if the singular number is retained, so that we might explain it with R. David Kimchi concerning Adam (rather than concerning Abraham) in this sense: Why do you justify yourselves, as if you sinned nothing against me, nor is there need that I should blot out your sins! The very origin of the race is subject to sin. Adam, your first Father, sinned and involved all his posterity in sins, and you are pure and clean! But if it must be explained in the plural concerning the Fathers of this people, because in the Hebrew the word הראשון is to be taken adverbially as 'formerly' or 'first', and to be referred not to all in general, but to their reprobate ancestors, who by sinning in the desert, so often provoked the power of God by sinning. B. Luther understands it in general concerning the Fathers. He does not take it, he says, concerning Adam, and concerning original sin, but I take the singular for the plural generally, so that he may refute the common argument of all ages, which they object to us regarding the authority of the Fathers: Your fathers also erred. But the gloss of Grotius cannot stand: For the Prophet would not have called Manasseh FATHER OF YOU absolutely, nor did he sin first: and the Prophet speaks of that which was done, not of that which was to be. Nor was the people led into captivity only because of the sins of Manasseh and the Priests and Levites, nor was the people held bound to render an account for the sin of Manasseh and the Priests when called to judgment: And therefore most Interpreters have rightly observed that glory is taken away from one's own righteousness and merits, so that the remission of sins may remain purely gratuitous. Which Vatablus also noted, i.e., There is also no reason why you should object to me the works of your ancestors. For Adam sinned in me, Moses likewise and Aaron sinned. The princes of the holy people, or those whom I had consecrated to myself, and had chosen, that they might be the leaders of my people, Moses and Aaron, those I found contaminated, and unworthy to enter the holy land: I gave Jacob to slaughter, and Israel to reproaches, that is, I slaughtered the greater part of Jacob in the desert, and permitted that the Israelites be affected with reproaches. For when such a great slaughter was taking place in the desert, the enemies were saying to the Israelites by way of insult, Where is the God of the Israelites? Thus also Hector Pintus, Cornelius à Lapide, Sanctius, Menochius, Tirinus, as also Oecolampadius, and others. Some, however, understand by the Princes of holiness the Priests set over the sanctuary. Brentius explains it thus: Furthermore, I contaminated the Princes of the Sanctuary: For many High Priests followed Moses and Aaron, who performed the legitimate sacred rites in my Sanctuary, many Princes and leaders of my holy people followed, who because they were heads of religion could be held to be so just and so holy, that by their holiness they could defend both themselves and others before the judgment of God. But these also I contaminated and profaned, that is, I discovered that these also were contaminated and profaned by innumerable vices and sins. Calvin himself, even though he refers that POLLUTION to the captivity, and translates it in the future, I will therefore pollute the princes of the sanctuary, does not however acquiesce in that interpretation: If anyone, he says, should prefer to extend this to the various disasters by which God had affected his people with ignominy, and at the same time join the Babylonian exile, there will be no inconvenience. And perhaps it is better suited to be narrated what had happened to them long ago and often, so that they might be reminded for the future that they are not protected by any right so well, but that they might again pay the penalty for their ingratitude with the greatest disgrace. He shows, therefore, the cause of this exile: because the crimes of the fathers and the sons had to be punished, since, namely, there was no end to sinning, but they daily kindled the wrath of God against themselves, until at length He took notice of them. Nor indeed did God give Jacob the Israelites, by which name the whole people descending from Jacob, who were later distributed into the kingdom of Judah and Israel, is accustomed to be noted, to destruction, at the time of the captivity, even though very many Jews were killed. It is evident, however, if we look to the proper intention of the Prophet, that the justiciaries are confounded here, so that it may be left that the remission of sins is obtained only through the servitude, obedience, and righteousness of the Son of God our redeemer, and through the labor endured in the passion for our sins. Concerning which the Blessed Luther in this place: DECLARE, IF YOU HAVE ANYTHING, THAT YOU MAY BE JUSTIFIED. He challenges the justiciaries, who trusted that they were justified by the works of the law. Act, if you know another way by which you may be justified, bring it forth. For as for what you boast, that you received those institutions of living and laws from the Fathers, I do not care at all. For your Fathers were also sinners. Because therefore you establish another righteousness, for that reason I will reject you with all your righteousness and your works. He says the same thing that is in the Acts: There is no other name under heaven, in which we may be saved. Whatever therefore you may produce to establish your righteousness, besides Christ and without Christ, this is condemned, impious, and blasphemous.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ET CONTAMINAVI PRINCIPES SAN- CTOS) In Hebræo: sanctitatis. Feci ut à prophana plebe non distinguantur Pontifices ipsi: quia vivendum habent sine templo, sine victimis, sine habitu sacerdotali. Loqui- tur hæc Deus quasi in ipso tempore captivitatis.

DEDI AD INTERNECIONEM JACOB) Judæos plurimos occidit Nabuchodonosor. Vid. 2. Reg. 25, 6. 21.

ET ISRAEL IN BLASPHEMIAM) Opprobriis, id est, servituti exposui Israelis posteros, nempe Hieroso- lymitas, & alios quos deportavit Nabuzaradan.

Per patrem primum communiter Hebræi & Christiani Interpretes intelligunt vel Adamum, per quem peccatum invectum est, vel Abrahamum, quem patrem suum jactabant Judæi, qui idolis olim servierit, Jos. 24. vel diffidentia peccaverit, quod Hieronymus & alii respici volunt è Genes. 15. Alii Patres in genere accipiunt, ut sit numerus sin- gularis positus pro plurali h. m. Patres tui prius pec- caverunt contra me, & tu vestigia illorum sequeris. Quid ergo narrabis, quo te justifices? Neque ad capti- vitatis causas, vel tempora hæc referunt, Musculum si excipias, & paucos fortassis alios. Illum sequutus hic esse videtur Grotius; per Patrem Regem intel- ligi; quamvis δοκαστικῶς solum istam sententiam proposuerit Musculus, nec in ea acquiescere po- tuerit. Additur enim, non satis probari hanc senten- tiam & improbabilius esse, si singularis numerus re- tineatur, ut cum R. David Kimchi de Adamo expo- namus (quam de Abrahamo) hoc sensu: Quid vos ipsi justificatis, quasi nihil contra me peccetis, nec opus sit, ut peccata vestra deleam! Ipsa generis origo pec- cato est obnoxia. Adam primus vester Pater pecca- vit, omnemque suam posteritatem peccatis involvit, & vos estis puri ac puti! Si vero pluraliter exponendum sit de Patribus hujus populi, quod in Ebræo est הראשון adverbialiter per prius vel primo accipien- dum, & referendum esse non ad omnes in genere, sed ad reprobos ipsorum majores, qui in deserto peccan- do, toties potentiam Dei irritarunt peccando. B. Lu- therus intelligit in genere de Patribus. Non acci- pio, inquit, de Adam, & de peccato originis, sed gene- raliter singulare pro plurali accipio, ut confutet omnium seculorum commune argumentum, quod ob- jiciunt nobis autoritatem Patrum : Patres tui etiam erraverunt. Glossa vero Grotii subsistere nequit: Nam neque absolute ita vocasset Manassen. Pro- pheta PATER TUUS, neque primus ille pecca- vit : & loquitur Propheta de eo, quod factum, non quod futurum erat. Nec ob Manassis tantum pec- cata, & Sacerdotum ac Levitarum populus in ca- ptivitatem abductus, aut de Manassis & Sacerdo- tum peccato populus in judicium vocatus ratio- nem reddere tenebatur : Ideoque recte observa- runt Interpretes plerique justitiæ propriæ & meri- tis gloriam adimi, ut mere gratuita maneat pecca- torum remissio. Quod Vatablus etiam notavit, q.d. Non est etiam,quod majorum tuorum opera mihi ob- jicias. Nam Adam peccavit in me, Moses item & Aaron peccaverunt. Principes populi sancti, vel quos mihi consecraveram, & delegeram, ut essent Duces populi mei Moses & Aaron, illos contamina- tos offendi, & indignos, qui ingrederentur terram sanctam : dedi necem Jacob, & Israel opprobria, id est, majorem partem Jacob trucidavi in deserto, & permisi ut Israelitæ probris afficerentur. Nam cum tanta strages fieret in deserto, hostes Israelitis per contumeliam dicebant, ubi est Deus Israelitarum? Sic etiam Hector Pintus, Cornelius à Lapide, San- ctius, Menochius, Tirinus, ut & Oecolampadius, & alii. Per Principes tamen sanctitatis Sacerdotes san- ctuario præfectos nonnulli intelligunt. Brentius ita explicat : Præterea contaminavi Principes San- ctuarii : Nam Mosen, & Aaronem secuti sunt multi Pontifices, qui sacra legitima in Sanctuario meo per- egerunt, secuti sunt multi Principes & Duces populi sancti mei, qui quia erant capita religionis haberi possent tam justi & tam sancti, ut sua sanctitate tam se, quam alios caram judicio Dei defenderent. Sed hos quoque contaminavi & prophanavi, hoc est, de- prehendi hos etiam esse contaminatos & prophanatos innumeris vitiis & peccatis. Calvinus ipse, etiamsi ad captivitatem POLLUTIONEM illam referat, & in futuro vertat, ideo polluam Principes sanctua- rii, non tamen acquiescit illi interpretationi : Si quis, inquit, ad diversas clades, quibus populum suum ignominia affecerat Deus, extendere hoc ma- lit, & simul conjungere exilium Babylonicum, nihil erit incommodi. Et forte melius convenit narrari, quid pridem & sæpius illis acciderit, ut in posterum commonefiant, nullo jure tam bene se esse munitos, quin rursus cum summo dedecore pœnas suæ ingrati- tudinis luant. Hujus ergo exilii causam ostendit : quoniam scelera Patrum & filiorum puniri oporte- bat, cum scil. nullus esset peccandi finis, sed quotidie iram Dei contra se accenderent, donec tandem in ipsos animadvertit.Neque vero γενικῶς Jacob Israë- litas, quo nomine populus totus è Jacob descen- dens, qui postea in regnum Judæ & Israëlis distri- butus fuit, notari solet, ad internecionem dedit Deus, tempore captivitatis, etsi Judæi plurimi oc- cisi fuerint. Patet autem, si propriam intentionem Prophetæ respiciamus, confundi hic justitiarios, ut relinquatur remissionem peccatorum non nisi per servitutem, obedientiam, & justitiam Filii Dei redemptoris nostri, & per laborem in passione ob peccata nostra exantlatum, obtingere. Quo de B. Lutherus in h. l. NARKA, SI QVID HABES, UT JUSTIFICERIS. Provocat justitiarios, qui operibus legis se justificari confidebant. Agite, si aliam rationem, qua justificemini, novistis, afferte eam. Quod enim jactatis, illa vivendi instituta & leges vos à Patribus accepisse, nihil moror. Fuerunt enim & Patres vestri peccatores. Quia igitur aliam justitiam statuitis, ideo vos cum omni vestra justitia & operibus vestris abjiciam. Idem dicit, quod est in Actis: Non est aliud nomen sub cœlo, in quo sal- vemur. Quicquid igitur produxeris ad justitiam tuam stabiliendam, præter Christum & sine Christo, hoc damnatum, impium & blasphemum est.

## 44:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLIV.

With the promised outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the conversion of the Gentiles, the idolater is convicted with his idols of vanity, and Israel is invited to acknowledge its Redeemer, who confounds the soothsayers, and fulfills the words of his servants: about to promote the building of Jerusalem through Cyrus.

Vers. 1. AND NOW HEAR JACOB MY SERVANT) God addresses those who have been deported, now led by repentance for their sins.

THIS gloss proceeds from a false opinion, as if the preceding things dealt with the Babylonian captivity. But it is repugnant to this, that the outpouring of the Holy Spirit which took place in the New Testament is promised here, verse 3. And therefore the Blessed Luther, he speaks, he says, to the people of the Gospel elected from the Synagogue, you who are servants of that people, i.e., believers, or obedient to the faith, etc. This is the Blessed Luther. He addresses not those deported and led by repentance, but those about to be deported, and warns the pious against the scandal of the desolation and captivity, which was imminent according to the prophecies of the Prophets: and therefore, as our Brentius rightly noted, as in the previous sermons, so also in this one he treats two things especially: The one is, that he consoles the weak and the fearful, and commands them to trust, because by this affliction of captivity the Church of the Lord will be more dilated than abolished. The other is, that he opposes his Majesty to the Gods of the Gentiles, and teaches that the impiety of the idolatry of the Gentiles is more manifest than that which ought to be refuted by many words, if only someone applies a sound judgment of human reason. For idolatry is so gross, that its vanity can be detected even by human reason itself. Wherefore, he who is so offended by it, that he falls away from the true God of Israel to it, is he not to be said to have lost even human sense?

Latin:

CAPUT XLIV.

Promissa Spiritus S. effusione, & gentium con- versione idololatra cum idolis suis vanitatis convincuntur, & Israel ad agnoscendum Redemptorem suum invitatur, qui confun- dit ariolos, & verba servorum suorum im- plet: Hierosolymæ ædificationem per Cyrum promoturus.

Vers. 1. ET NVNC AVDI JACOB SERVE MEVS) Alloquitur Deus illos deportatos jam pœnitentia ductos peccatorum.

HÆC glossa è falsa opinione procedit, quasi præcedentia egerint de captivitate Babyloni- ca. Cui vero repugnat, quod promittantur hic ef- fusio Spiritus S. in Novo Testamento facta, vers. 3. Ideoque B. Lutherus, loquitur, inquit, ad populum Evangelii electum de Synagoga, vos qui estis de isto populo servi, h. e. credentes, seu fidei obedientes, &c. Hæc B. Lutherus. Non deportatos pœnitentia du- ctos, sed deportandos alloquitur, monetque pios adver- sus scandalum vastitatis & captivitatis, quod juxta vaticinia Prophetarum imminebat: ideoque quod re- cte notavit Brentius noster, ut in superioribus concio- nibus, ita & in hac duo præcipue tractat: Alterum est, quod consolatur imbecilles & meticulosos, & ju- bet eos confidere, quia hac captivitatis afflictione Ec- clesia Domini magis dilatabitur, quam abolebitur. Alterum est, quod opponit suam Majestatem Diis gentium, & docet, impietatem idololatriæ gentium manifestiorem esse, quam quæ pluribus refutari de- beat, si modo quispiam adhibeat sanum humanæ ra- tionis judicium. Tam crassa enim est idololatria, ut vanitas ejus etiam ab ipsa humana ratione depre- hendi queat. Quare, qui ea ita offenditur, ut ad eam à vero Deo Israel deficiat, ne ille humanum etiam sensum amisisse dicendus est.

## 44:2
AND MOST RIGHTLY WHOM I HAVE CHOSEN) יְשֻׁרוּן, that is, little Israel, as we are accustomed to address little children, See Deuteronomy 32, 15.

Ver. 2. FOR I WILL POUR WATERS UPON THE THIRSTY, AND FLOODS UPON THE DRY GROUND) What he signifies by this metaphor, he explains immediately: I will pour my Spirit upon your seed. I will give from you Prophets, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi.

Latin:

ET RECTISSIME QVEM ELEGI) יְשֻׁרוּן, id est, ἰσραηλίδιον, quomodo filiolos alloqui solemus, Vide Dev- teron. 32, 15.

Vers. 2. EFFVNDAM ENIM AQVAS SVPER SI- TIENTEM, ET FLVENTA SVPER ARIDAM) Quid hac metaphora significat, statim explicat: Effundam Spiri- tum meum super semen tuum. Dabo ex te Prophetas, Jere- miam, Ezechielem, Aggæum, Zachariam, Malachiam.

## 44:3
AND MY BLESSING UPON YOUR OFFSPRING) I will cause that you may have many descendants.

Latin:

ET BENEDICTIONEM MEAM SVPER STIR- PEM TVAM) Efficiam, ut multa tibi sit soboles.

## 44:4
Ver. 4. AND THEY SHALL SPRING UP AMONG THE GRASS AS WILLOWS BY THE WATER COURSES) Will they thus stand out among the peoples?

As cypresses are wont to do among the bending viburnums.

Thus Grotius explains the former parts concerning the raising up of Prophets, and the latter concerning bodily blessing, which is a mere twisting and perversion of an illustrious prophecy. For here is predicted the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and spiritual blessing, and consequently the spiritual multiplication of a spiritual seed. The water is to be poured upon the dry ground; by the name of the thirsty and the dry, the Prophets, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Zechariah, etc., are not noted, but generally miserable, afflicted, and sad souls, who are in need of the water of refreshment of the Holy Spirit, unfruitful and sterile of good works, such as we all are by nature, dry and thirsty, destitute of all juice of life-giving consolation, and utterly sterile and unfruitful, Jude v. 12. Therefore, this is not to be restricted to the Prophets, nor only concerning the Prophetic Spirit, but the extraordinary gifts, by which the Prophets in structed, but it must be understood concerning the gifts of the Spirit, which all those who are destitute of grace and consolation need, who thirst for the same, all who are barren for good works, and are compared to arid land, to an arid desert, not to a cultivated garden or fruitful earth. Nor indeed do those things look only to the times of the Old Testament, but since the conversion of the Gentiles is designated as the fruit of the poured-out Spirit, it must be believed that this promise extends itself altogether also to the times of the New Testament; just as the promise of Joel, twin to this one, ch. 2, 'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh,' is explained by Peter concerning the outpouring that took place in the N.T., Acts 2:17. And Christ himself seems to look to this passage when he says, John 7:37-38: 'If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink: he that believeth on me, as the Scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.' Especially since the Evangelist adds: 'This spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive.' For a similar exegesis of the outpouring of water and rivers is added by the Prophet: AND MY SPIRIT UPON THY SEED. For this seed are the believers, not precisely the Prophets, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, etc. Whence also this is referred to the Apostles by Cyril, to the rest from among the Jews who received the Gospel by Brentius, to the Gentiles, who before Christ were like arid land, by Cornel. à Lap., and it is explained generally concerning believers by Jerome, B. Luther, and most others. Because the Holy Spirit says indefinitely, THY SEED. And he points out any thirsty and arid ones whatsoever, even if he could have specifically encouraged the Church of that time with this consolation: inasmuch as the squalid and miserable state, by which Judea was to be an arid and thirsty land, had been predicted. Nor indeed does he address the Jews here according to the flesh, but according to the spirit: because that seed is spiritual, which is irrigated by the streams of the Spirit, and germinates, like willows, among the flowing waters. To which the observation of Jerome and Cyril contributes: where the people are accused, or something harsher is added, they are called by pure names without any dignity of title; but where the discourse is held to the Israel of God, certain privileges of name are added, as now, 'Hear, O Jacob my servant.' See, says Hector Pintus, here, with what gentleness of words God addresses his Church, as if he were saying, O Jacob according to the spirit, O my elect Israel, i.e., O my Church, hear me, who created thee, etc. Therefore he also employs the pleasant name ישרון which is a diminutive, and indicates most tender love, like an amatory endearment, as if you were to say 'my little beloved,' of which Grotius says: ישרון that is, Ισραηλίδιον, as we are accustomed to address little children, see. Deut. 32:15. B. Luther has it thus at this place: He confesses that the Church is thirsty and arid, because it is in perpetual heat, nor does it see anything but its own condemnation and ignominy. He says therefore, 'Fear not, I will overwhelm thee with fruitful rain, that abundant seed may come forth for thee. I will give the Holy Spirit, who may console thee, and irrigate thee, so that there may not be lacking descendants who may spread the Gospel more widely.' For it is a consolation, so that the Church may not despair in its present affliction, but may hope that God will give a numerous posterity, even if the wrath of the world and Satan threatens otherwise. For the Holy Spirit does not depart from the word, but is effective through the word.

Furthermore, the individual words teach that a large and copious outpouring of the Holy Spirit is promised here. For the word of OUTPOURING itself brings in abundance: and RIVERS are promised, i.e., not just a sprinkling or the irrigation of a few, but entire RIVERS of the gifts of the Spirit; therefore the VOICE OF BLESSING is added, which likewise imports a large collation of the charisms of the Holy Spirit. Nor is the outpouring of the H.S. and the blessing promised to certain ones only, but indefinitely to the THIRSTY AND ARID SEED OF ISRAEL, AND TO HIS OFFSPRING. Finally, since the offspring that is to germinate from there is said to be like willows among the rivulets of waters, so that one shall say, 'I am the Lord's,' and another shall call in the name of Jacob, which latter things the Interpreters unanimously understand concerning the calling of the Gentiles, that seed and offspring of Israel cannot in any way be restricted to Israel according to the flesh, much less to the times of the captivity. For those upon whom the H.S. will be poured out will germinate thus: of them one shall say, 'I am the Lord's,' and another shall call in the name of Jacob, etc. And therefore St. Cyril understands by Jacob and Israel the choir of the Holy Apostles. But he says that the SEED and children of the Holy Apostles are those who through them were called to spiritual regeneration. But if the Church is addressed generally by the name of Israel, those who have been spiritually propagated from her will be understood as her seed and offspring. But as to the BLESSING which is promised to his OFFSPRING, the connection of the text teaches that it is not corporal, but spiritual. For such as the water is, and such as the germination is, such also must the blessing necessarily be understood here. But the water which God promises here, by the admission of Grotius himself, is the H.S. For water is a life-giving thing, as Cyril says here, and makes plants and germs grow: and in a certain way it imitates the energy of the Holy Spirit: through whom all things have been established, and are well, and are strengthened, and the intelligible creature is enriched by the reception of all goods, and as it were breathes, and ascends to spiritual growth. Nor can any other germination be understood here than the spiritual, which is the fruit of the blessing. Therefore, there is no doubt that the spiritual blessing itself is designated here. Which also that exchange, as it were exegetical, teaches in the Prophet, when he exchanges the word of Spirit and blessing, just as the word of seed and offspring. 'I will pour my Spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thy offspring.' Finally, lest there be any doubt whether a spiritual or a corporal blessing and a multiplication of the race are promised, it is added: 'This one will say, I am the Lord's, and that one will be called by the name of Jacob.' And therefore Cyril explained these things thus: 'We call the BLESSINGS supplied to the Saints by God the variety of spiritual gifts.' Then he declared what the utility of the blessings is, when he added: 'They shall spring up as grass in the midst of water, and as a willow by the flowing water.' For herbs and plants that are in places lacking water grow very slowly, and when they have grown, they immediately wither: But those flourish best which the flow of streams and the course of waters washes, which preserves life, and the willow plant, always growing by streams and rivers, is always green. Therefore, he says, those who are irrigated by streams falling under the understanding, who have been enriched by these, will confess that they know me alone, and will call Him God who called them. Jerome notes that others understand a double calling through the HERBS and RE-SPRINGING WILLOWS, so that in the herbs there is the people of the nations, and in the willows those who believed from Israel. But these things can hardly be distinguished so subtly. Indeed, it will perhaps not be rashly observed, with Jerome leading the way, that the Holy Spirit and water are joined here, because in baptism we are reborn of water and the Spirit. For although it may be admitted that water is taken metaphorically, and that the word Spirit is here explanatory, nevertheless the Holy Spirit was not delighted in vain by this metaphor taken from WATER, since others were not lacking, but He seems to have chosen it for this reason especially, that He was going to unite Himself with the water of the Sacrament of baptism for the regeneration of countless souls. Therefore He says, 'I will pour waters upon the thirsty, I will pour' My Spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring, which shall be reborn of water and the Holy Spirit in baptism, and he compares those reborn in baptism to green herbs, and to the Willow, which grows beside flowing waters, and contrary to the nature of things brings forth fruits, which was previously barren, as Jerome [says] in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET GERMINABVNT INTER HERBAS SICVT SALICES INTER AQVARVM RIVULOS) Ita eminebunt inter populos?

Quantum lenta solent inter viburna cupressi.

Ita explicat priora Grotius de Prophetarum, excitatione, posteriora de benedictione corporali, quæ mera ςρεβλότης & perversio est illustris vati- cinii. Prædicitur enim hic effusio Spirit. Sancti, & spi- ritualis benedictio, adeoque spiritualis seminis spi- ritualis multiplicatio. Effundenda aqua supra ari- dam terram; sitientis & aridæ nomine non Prophe- tæ, Jeremias, Ezechiel, Zacharias, &c. notantur, sed generatim miseræ, afflicte & tristes animæ, quæ indigent aqua refectionis SpiritusSancti, infrugi- feræ & steriles bonorum operum, quales nos omnes sumus natura aridi, & siticulosi, succo omni vivificæ consolationis destituti, ac prorsus steriles & infrugiferi, Jud. v. 12. Non ergo restringenda hæc ad Prophetas, nec solum de Spiritu Prophetico, sed donis extraordinariis, quibus Prophetas in- struxit, sed de donis Spiritus intelligenda, quibus indigent omnes gratiæ & consolationis expertes, qui eandem sitiunt, omnes qui steriles sunt ad bona opera, & aridæ terræ, arido deserto comparantur, non horto culto aut terræ frugiferæ. Neque vero ad tempora solum Veteris Test. illa spectant, sed quum conversio gentium, ceu fructus effusi Spiri- tus designetur, ad Novi Test. tempora omnino etiam sese hanc promissionem porrigere, creden- dum est; quemadmodum Joëlis promissio huic gemina c. 2. effundam Spiritum meum super omnem carnem, à Petro de effusione in N. T. facta explica- tur Act. 2, 17. Et videtur Christus ipse ad hunc lo- cum respicere, cum ait Joh. 7, 37. 38. Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, & bibat: qui credit in me, sicut dixit Scriptura, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Præsertim cum Evangelista addat: Hoc dixit de Spiritu, quem accepturi erant, qui crederent in ipsum. Nam similis ἐξήγησις effusionis aquæ & flu- minum additur à Propheta: ET SPIRITUM MEUM SUPER SEMEN TUUM. Hoc enim semen credentes sunt, non præcise Prophetæ, Jeremias, Ezechiel &c. Unde etiam ad Apostolos hoc refertur à Cyrillo, ad reliquos ex Judæis, qui Evangelium receperunt, à Brentio, ad gentilitatem, quæ ante Christum instar terræ aridæ erat, à Cornel. à Lap, ac generatim de credentibus explicatur ab Hieronymo, B. Luthero & aliis plerisque. Quia in- definite dicit Spiritus Sanctus, SEMEN TUUM. Et quosvis siticulosos atque aridos indigitat, etsi il- lius temporis Ecclesiam hac consolatione specia- tim erigere potuerit: siquidem status squalidus & miser, quo Judæa futura erat terra arida & siticulo- sa, prædictus fuerit. Nec vero compellat hic Judæos secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum: quia semen illud spirituale est, quod irrigatur fluentis Spiritus, & germinat, quasi salices, inter præter- fluentes aquas. Quo facit observatio Hieronymi, & Cyrilli: ubi accusatur populus, aut durius quid additur, absque ulla nominis dignitate puris illum ap- pellari vocabulis; ubi autem ad Israel Dei sermo ha- betur, addi quædam nominis privilegia, ut nunc, au- di serve meus Jacob. Vide, inquit Hector Pintus, hic, quanta verborum lenitudine Deus Ecclesiam suam alloquatur, ac si dicat, ô Jacob secundum spi- ritum, ô Israel electe mi, h. e. ô Ecclesia mea audi me, qui te creavi &c. Ideo adhibet etiam jucundum no- men ישרון quod diminutivum est, ac amorem te- nerrimum indicat, ceu blandimentum amatorium, ac si dilectulum quem dicas, de quo Grotius: ישרון id est, Ισραηλίδιον, quomodo filiolos alloqui solemus, vid. Deut. 32, 15. B. Lutherus ita habet ad h. l. Con- fitetur Ecclesiam esse sitientem & aridam, quia est in perpetuo æstu, nec videt, nisi sui damnationem & ignominiam. Dicit igitur, noli timere, obruam te fœ- cunda pluvia, ut proveniat tibi copiosum semen. Da- bo Spiritum S. qui consoletur te, & riget, ne desint po- steri, qui Evangelium latius spargant. Est enim consolati, ne Ecclesia desperet in præsenti afflictione, sed speret Deum daturum numerosam posteritatem, etiamsi diversum minetur mundi & Satanæ ira. Nam Spiritus Sanctus non discedit à verbo, sed per verbum est efficax.

Porro promitti hic Spiritus Sancti largam & copiosam effusionem, verba singula docent. Nam verbum ipsum EFFUNDENDI copiam infert: & FLUMINA promittuntur, h. e. non aspersio so- lum aut paucorum irrigatio, sed FLUMINA inte- gra donorum Spiritus, ideo additur BENEDI- CTIONIS VOX, quæ itidem largam charisma- tum Spiritus Sancti collationem importat. Neque certis quibusdam tantum, de indefinite SITIEN- TI & ARIDO SEMINI ISRAELIS, & STIR- PI EJUS effusio S. S. & benedictio promittitur. Denique cum inde ita progerminatura soboles dica- tur, sicut Salices inter aquarum rivulos, ut iste dictu- rus sit, Domini ego sum, & ille vocaturus sit in nomi- ne Jacob, quæ posteriora ὁμοθυμαδὸν Interpp. de vocatione gentium intelligunt, non potest utique se- men illud, & stirps Israelis, ad Israelem secundum carnem, nedum ad tempora captivitatis restringi. Nam illi, super quos effundetur Spiritus S. germi- nabunt ita: ex illis iste dicet, Domini ego sum, & il- le vocabit in nomine Jacob &c. Ideoque S. Cyrillus per Jacobum & Israelem intelligit S. Apostolorum chorum. SEMEN autem & filios S. Apostolorum eos esse ait, qui per ipsos vocati sunt ad regeneratio- nem spiritualem. Sed si generaliter Ecclesia nomi- ne Israelis compellatur, semen & stirps ejus intelli- gentur, qui ab ea spiritualiter propagati sunt. Quod autem ad BENEDICTIONEM, quæ STIRPI ejus promittitur, eam non corporalem, sed spiri- tualem esse, συνάφεια textus docet. Qualis enim aqua, & qualis progerminatio, talis etiam bene- dictio necessario hic intelligenda. Aqua autem, quam Deus hic promittit, fatente ipso Grotio, est Spiritus S. Vivifica enim res est aqua, ut hic Cyrillus, & plantas & germina facit augescere: & quodam- modo imitatur sancti Spiritus energiam: per quem omnia constiterunt, & bene sunt, & firmantur, & in- telligibilis creatura omnium bonorum acceptione locu- pletatur, & velut affilit, & ascendit ad spirituale in crementum. Nec alia progerminatio hic intelligi potest, quam spiritualis, quæ fructus est benedi- ctionis. Ideo etiam ipsam benedictionem spiritua- lem hic designari, dubitandum non est. Quod etiam illa commutatio velut ἐξηγητικὴ docet apud Prophetam, cum vocem Spiritus & benedictionis, perinde ac vocem seminis & stirpis commutat. Po- nam Spiritum meum super semen tuum, & benedi ctionem meam super stirpem tuam. Denique ne du- bium sit, num spiritualis, an corporalis benedictio, ac generis multiplicatio promittantur additur: iste dicet, Dei sum, & ille vocabitur nomine Jacob. Ideo- que hæc ita exposuit Cyrillus: BENEDICTIO- NES autem Sanctis à Deo subministratas appellamus spiritualium donorum varietatem. Deinde quænam sit benedictionum utilitas, declaravit, cum adjecit: Exorientur, ut gramen in medio aquæ, & ut Salix juxta præterfluentem aquam. Herbæ enim & plan- tæ, quæ sunt in locis aqua carentibus, lente omnino crescunt, & cum creverint, statim emarcescunt: Sed optime florent, quæ rivulorum fluxus, & aquarum cur- sus alluit, quæ vitam conservat, semperque viret planta salicis fortibus ac fluminibus semper adnascens. Irri- gati ergo, inquit, rivulis sub intelligentiam cadentibus, qui his ditati sunt, confitebuntur, quod me solum sciant, & Deum nuncupabunt, qui eos vocavit. Hierony- mus notat, alios per HERBAS & RENASCEN- TES SALICES duplicem vocationem intelligere, ut in herbis populus nationum sit, in salicibus hi, qui ex Israel crediderunt. Sed hæc ita subtiliter vix di- stingui possunt. Id vero fortassis non temere obser- vabitur, præeunte Hieronymo, quod Spiritus San- ctus, & aqua hic conjungantur, quia in baptismo ex aqua & Spiritu renascimur. Nam quamvis admitti possit, aquam accipi Metaphorice, & vocem Spiri- tus ἐξηγητικὴν hic esse, non frustra tamen delecta- tus est hac metaphora ab AQUA defumpta, quum aliæ non defuerint, sed elegisse eam videtur Spiri- tus S. eo præcipue nomine, quod cum aqua baptis- matis Sacramento olim sese uniturus erat ad in- numerarum animarum regenerationem. Ideo dicit, effundam aquas super sitientem, effundam Spiritum meum super semen tuum, & benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam, quæ ex aqua & Spiritu S. renascetur in baptismate, comparatque in baptismate renascentes herbis virentibus, & Salici, quæ juxta fluentes aquas, & contra rerum naturam affert fru- ctus, quæ prius sterilis erat, ut Hieronymus h. l.

## 44:5
Ver. 5. THIS ONE SHALL SAY: I AM THE LORD'S.) Whoever has renounced idols shall serve God. AND THAT ONE SHALL CALL UPON THE NAME OF JACOB) He will wish to be considered not only as one of the descendants of Jacob, but also as his imitator. THIS ONE SHALL WRITE WITH HIS HAND TO THE LORD.) The LXX not badly [translate], 'he shall write upon his hand, I am God's.' Just as soldiers had the name of the emperor written on their hand. AND IN THE NAME OF ISRAEL HE SHALL BE SURNAMED) He shall be surnamed 'an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.' John the Evangelist 1, 47.

This notable promise cannot be restricted to the Israelite people alone: rather, it openly treats of the Gentiles being converted to the Church. For both the distribution and that phrase, 'he shall call upon the name of Jacob,' imply this. Our blessed Luther observed both well: 'THIS ONE SHALL SAY, I AM THE LORD'S,' are to be taken distributively. Christians will be dispersed throughout the whole world, i.e., here and there and everywhere there shall be Christians. 'THIS ONE SHALL BE CALLED BY THE NAME OF JACOB.' It is a most clear passage concerning the calling of the Gentiles, that they are to be made equal to the Jews and the children of Abraham, and to be called by their name. For the passage must be understood of those who were not previously called Jacob, nor are born of the flesh of Jacob, but are from the Gentiles. Moreover, such passages are to be diligently observed, in which is promised the transfer of the name, of the nationality, and of the inheritance, that not only those to whom the promise was made are Jacob, but the Gentiles also. So also Psalm 87 says of Zion, 'a man and a man was born in her.' For he speaks in that place of the Gentiles, Tyre, Sidon, Egypt, etc. That phrase, 'he shall call upon the name of Jacob, and in the name of Israel he shall be surnamed,' is indeed explained in various ways by interpreters. But all easily agree that it is to be understood concerning the conversion of the Gentiles to the Church. Jerome explains it thus: 'ANOTHER SHALL CALL,' (he implies, sinners) 'to repentance in the name of Jacob, so that they themselves may also supplant vices and sins: And in the name of Israel he shall be surnamed: For not all are from Israel, but a great part from the multitude of the Gentiles shall be surnamed in the name of Israel, so that they may receive the Law and the Prophets, and all the thanks of the Holy Scriptures which were promised to the people of Israel.' Cyril, when he says, 'this one shall say, I am God's.' And 'THAT ONE, I SHALL CRY OUT' (so it is held among the LXX, 'he shall cry out in the name of Jacob') 'and another shall write,' denotes the multitude of those running to him through faith in Christ. For not any one people shall be called, but rather all who are under the Sun: the multitude of the Gentiles, and all shall confess that they are God's, and shall name Him Savior and Redeemer, and shall henceforth be called by the name of Jacob (the LXX have, 'and another shall write upon his hand, I am God's, he shall cry out in the name of Israel'), that is, that they are the cord and the portion of God. For, he says, the people of the Lord became His portion, the cord of His inheritance, Israel. Furthermore, although some take the word יִקְרָא passively, 'he shall be called,' i.e., he shall be called a Jacobite (in which sense Grotius also seems to have taken it), yet in the Hebrew it does not have the passive יִקָּרֵא but the active יִקְרָא, 'he shall call.' Whence Cornel. à Lap. renders it, 'he shall invoke, or he shall preach the name of the God of Jacob': But because there is no mention of God, these things are more correctly expressed thus: 'he shall call' (sc. himself) himself) by the name of Jacob, so that this may respond to the following clause, 'and he shall be surnamed by the name of Israel,' and two heads of profession are designated: One, which pertains to God, the other which pertains to the people of God and the Church, that he is about to addict himself to God and His Church. Sanctius thinks it explains the zeal by which someone signifies in every way that he will be in the power of another, so that he may depart entirely from himself, and wish to be entirely and altogether another's: first, that he may profess this with his mouth, while he freely says, 'I am the Lord's'; then, that he may worship God with the religious cult of works, and join himself to the true worshippers of GOD. Thirdly, that Scripture may confirm this, as one who gives his name to the military. Of which, according to him, is contained in the word ASSIMILATED, that he may provide proofs of his religion by some likeness or character, or image; in which, however, he does not deny that Papists are assimilated to the Gentiles, who carried images of their gods on rings or bracelets, or gems hanging from their necks. But there is nothing here about that superstition of the Gentiles: For the Hebrew word implies SURNAMING, but not assimilation through the wearing of some image or character, nor are the Israelites read to have worn such images, as they were forbidden to them. Hector Pintus rendered the sense more correctly and simply, which we mentioned before, 'THIS ONE SHALL SAY': the sense is, he says, there will be believers everywhere who will glory in the Christian name, and will say that they are Israelites, even if they were born from the Gentiles. For Christ's Church is Israel according to the Spirit. One will say that he is a Christian, another will confess that he is of the Church. 'This one shall write with his hand to the Lord,' that is, he shall profess that he is a Christian, 'and in the name of Israel he shall be surnamed,' i.e., he shall be surnamed an Israelite according to the Spirit, that is, one believing in Christ. For it is known that Jacob and Israel are used in Scripture for those who believe in God and serve Him faithfully, Gal. 5, 16. He shall therefore call himself by the name of Jacob, that is, he shall openly confess that he pertains to the Church of Christ: for true Israelites are Christians, as Osiander rightly [says] here. This explanation is in excellent agreement with the scope and intention of the Prophet, even if it be admitted that this consolation was proposed with respect to the Babylonian captivity, as our Brentius explains: This is a great and notable promise concerning the preservation and expansion of the Church, not only among the Jews, but also among the Gentiles: You fear now, lest the Church of the Lord perish in the Babylonian captivity. But do not fear. For I shall so protect the Church, that it may not only be preserved in the Babylonian empire among the midst of the Gentiles, but also that it shall come to pass that the Gentiles themselves shall approach the Church, and become the people of the Lord.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ISTE DICET: DOMINI EGO SVM.) Quilibet abdicatis idolis Deo serviet. ET ILLE VOCABIT IN NOMINE JACOB) Volet se haberi non tantum de posteris Jacobi, sed & ejus imitatorem. HIC SCRIBET MANV SVA DOMINO.) LXX. non male ἐπιγράψει τῇ χειρὶ ἀυτῶ, τῶ θεῶ εἰμὶ. Sicut mi- lites imperatoris nomen in manu scriptum habebant. ET IN NOMINE ISRAEL ASSIMILABITVR) Cognominabitur ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος ἐκ ἔσι. Joh. Evangel. 1, 47.

Non potest insignis hæc promissio restringi ad solum Israëliticum populum: imo aperte de genti- bus convertendis ad Ecclesiam agit. Nam id infert tum distributio, tum phrasis illa, vocabit in nomine Jacob. Utrumque probe observavit B. Lutherus noster: ISTE DICIT, DOMINI EGO SUM, sunt distributive accipienda. Christiani erunt per totum orbem dispersi, q. d. hic & istic & ubique erunt Christiani. HIC VOCABITVR NOMINE JA- COB. Est clarissimus locus de vocatione gentium, quod sunt æquandæ Judæis & filiis Abrahæ, eorumque nomine appellandæ. Oportet enim locum intelligi de il- lis, qui ante non vocabantur Jacob, nec sunt ex carne Jacob nati, sed ex gentibus. Sunt autem hujusmodi loci diligenter observandi, in quibus promittitur transla- tio nominis, gentilitatis & hæreditatis, quod sunt Ja- cob non solum, quibus facta est promissio, sed etiam gentes. Sic etiam Psal. 87. de Zion dicit, homo, & homo natus est in ea. Dicit enim eo in loco de genti- bus, Tyro, Sidone, Ægypto, &c. Explicatur sane di- versimode phrasis illa, vocabit in nomine Jacob, & in nomine Israel assimilabitur, ab Interpp. Sed omnes facile conspirant, de gentium ad Ecclesiam conversione eandem accipiendam esse. Hierony- mus ita exponit: ALIUS VOCABIT, subau- ditur peccatores, ad pœnitentiam in nomine Jacob, ut & ipsi supplantent vitia atque peccata: Et in nomine Israel assimilabitur: Non enim omnes ex Israel, sed magna pars ex gentium multitudine, in nomine Israel assimilabitur, ut recipiat legem & Prophetas, omnesque gratias S. S. quæ Israel populo repromissæ sunt. Cyrillus, cum ait, hic dicet, Dei sum. Et ILLE, CLAMABO (sic apud LXX. habetur ἕτος βοήσεται ἐπὶ τῶ ὀνόματι ἰακὼβ) & alius scribet, multitudinem ad eum per fidem in Christo curren- tium denotat. Non enim vocabitur aliquis unus popu- lus, sed omnis potius, qui sub Sole est: multitudo genti- um, & omnes confitebuntur, quod sint Dei, & ipsum nuncupabunt Servatorem & Redemptorem, & appella- buntur deinceps nomine Jacob (LXX. habent, καὶ ἕτερος ἐπιγράψει τῇ χειρὶ ἀυτῶ, τῶ θεῶ εἰμὶ, ἐπὶ τῶ ὀνόματι τῶ ἱσραὴλ βοήσεται) id est, quod sint funi- culus & sors Dei. Factus est enim, inquit, populus Do- mini sors ejus, funiculus hæreditatis ejus Israel. Porro etsi verbum יִקְרָא passive accipiant nonnulli, vocabi- tur, q. d. ille vocabitur Jacobæus (quo sensu etiam vi- detur Grotius accepisse) In Hebræo tamen non ha- betur passivum יִקָּרֵא sed activum יִקְרָא vocabit. Unde Cornel. à Lap. reddit, invocabit, vel prædica- bit nomen Dei Jacob: Sed quia Dei mentio non fit, rectius hæc ita exprimuntur, vocabit (sc. sese) no- mine Jacob, ut sequenti commati hoc respondeat, & cognominabitur nomine Israel, ac designentur duo professionis capita: Unum, quod ad Deum, alterum quod ad populum Dei & Ecclesiam perti- net, quod Deo & Ecclesiæ ejus se addicturus sit. Sanctius explicari putat studium, quo modis omni- bus aliquis se futurum in alterius potestate signifi- cet, ita ut à se totus abeat, & alterius esse totus omnino velit: primum id ore profiteatur, dum li- bere dicit, Domini ego sum; Deinde operum cultu religioso Deum veneretur, & se adjungat veris DEI cultoribus. Tertio Scriptura id confirmet, quasi qui nomen suum militiæ dat. Quarum juxta ipsum est, in voce ASSIMILAVI comprehensum, quod similitudine aliqua aut charactere, seu effigie religionis suæ documenta præbeat; in quo tamen non diffitetur Papistas assimilari gentilibus, qui in annulis aut armillis, vel gemmis è collo pendentibus Deorum suorum imagines portarunt. De qua vero superstitione gentilium æmula hic nihil: Nam verbum Ebræum COGNOMINATIONEM in- fert, non vero assimilationem, per effigiei aut cha- racteris alicujus gestationem, nec Israëlitæ tales ima- gines gestasse leguntur, utpote quæ illis interdictæ fuere. Rectius & simplicius Hector Pintus sen- sum reddidit, quem antea diximus, ISTE DI- CET: sensus est, inquit, ubique erunt fideles, qui Christiano nomine glorientur, & Israelitas se esse di- cent, etsi ex gentibus nati sint. Est enim Christi Ec- clesia Israel secundum Spiritum. Quidam dicet, se esse Christianum, alter fatebitur, se esse de Ecclesia. Hic scribet manu sua Domino, id est, profitebitur se esse Christianum, & in nomine Israel assimilabitur, h. e. cognominabitur se Israelitam secundum Spiritum, id est, in Christum credentem. Notum enim est, Jacob & Israel in Scriptura pro his usurpari, qui in Deum cre- dunt, eique fideliter serviunt Gal. 5, 16. Vocabit ergo se in nomine Jacob, id est, fatebitur aperte, se pertinere ad Ecclesiam Christi: veri enim Israelitæ sunt Christiani, ut recte hic Osiander. Quæ explicatio scopo & intentioni Prophetæ apprime consonat, etiamsi admittatur Babylonicæ captivitatis respectu hanc consolationem propositam fuisse, quemad- modum explicat Brentius noster: Hæc est magna & insignis promissio de conservatione & dilatatione Ecclesiæ, non inter Judæos tantum, verum etiam inter gentes: Tu metuis nunc, ne captivitate Babylonica Ecclesia Domini pereat. At noli metuere. Ego enim Ecclesiam sic tuebor, ut non modo conservetur in Ba- bylonico imperio inter medias gentes, verum etiam futurum sit, ut ipsæ gentes accedant ad Ecclesiam, & fiant populus Domini.

## 44:6
Vers. 6. I AM THE FIRST AND I AM THE LAST) See above 41, 4. WITHOUT ME) In the Hebrew: besides me. THERE IS NO GOD) there are only λεγόμενοι θεοὶ [so-called gods], as Paul says 1 Corinthians 8, 5. LET HIM CALL, AND DECLARE, AND SET IN ORDER FOR ME, SINCE I APPOINTED THE ANCIENT PEOPLE) From the Hebrew you may translate thus: Who, like me, signifies and makes public, and that in order as I do, who have disposed all things for a people destined to endure forever? Which of those who are called Gods signifies beforehand to your peoples all things that are to come in their own order, as I do to that people whom I preserve in wondrous ways? TO COME) Imminent from near at hand. Compare what is above 41, 22. 23. AND WHAT THINGS ARE TO BE) Long after. Vers. 8. FEAR NOT, NEITHER BE TROUBLED) By this captivity. FROM THAT TIME I HAVE MADE THEE HEAR, AND HAVE DECLARED) Remember that this was predicted to you long ago through Isaiah. Weapons foreseen strike less.
