Cyri avo Astyagi inter quietem oblata est vitis quædam ex filiæ genitalibus prorumpens, quæ longâ palmitum propagine totam occuparet Asiam, futu- rumque è conjectoribus didicit, ut nepos ex filia nasci- turus totius Asiæ imperio potiretur. Accommodate ergo ad Astyagis somnium, in quo Cyrus Judaicæ liber- tatis assertor vitis appellatur, dicit imbrem desiderari, quo vitis illa ex materno utero, tanquam ex arvo nascatur & crescat. Justum vero seu Justitiam vo- cari ideo posse putat, quia divinæ justitiæ contra Baby- lonios administer fuit. Sed sane modus ipse loquendi, & rei magnitudo aliquid supra Cyri facultatem, & rerum ab illo gestarum gloriam ostendit. Quod ad lo- quendi .nodum attinet, docet noster Propheta sæpe, & alii non raro, quoties in typo versatur Prophetia, & ab eo per Apostrophen ad absentem convertitur, non jam de typo sermonem esse, sed plane de figurato, ac verita- te. Quod facile quædam de Christo oracula persua- dent Gen. 49. Postquam Jacob in filio Danumbram Christi Servatoris agnovit, fiat Dan coluber in via, cerastes in semita &c. Cum Apostrophe dicit, saluta- re tuum expectabo Domine. Et Zach. 9. cum præces- sisset typus, converso ad absentes sermone dicit Prophe- ta: Exulta satis filia Zion; ecce Rex tuus venit. Et cap. 13. cum obscura quædam umbra Christi Pasto- ris antecessisset, gradum inde faciens ad Christum per Apostrophen ait, Framea suscitare super Pastorem meum &c. & percute Pastorem. Quod ad rem ipsam spectat, Justi nomen, quod hic reperitur, illustrius est, & augustius, quam ut Cyro tribui ab Esaia debeat; quod nomen ab hoc Propheta, & in Evangelio & Apostolorum Actibus sæpe Christo tribuitur. Quare hæc de Christo omnino historice accipienda sunt, & claudenda parenthesi, quæ totam hanc clausulæm à continenti Prophetiæ filo secludat. Et quidem de Christo hæc accipit communis Patrum Interpretumque sententia. Hæc Sanctius. Hos primipilos, Cornel. à Lapide & Sanctium sequuntur alii. Hector Pin- tus, Tirinus, Menochius &c. Jam si glossam Grotii examinemus, quam sunt omnia frigida: Cyri imperium describi; Cum ter- ra dicitur prolatura salutem & justitiam, terram ple- nam sub ipso suæ justitiæ & felicitatis: Cyrum fuisse justum, magnanimum, clementem, liberalem. Sed hoc votum est Ecclesiæ, & fidelium in populo Do- mini: quos imperium Cyri designasse, quum opta- runt, ut terra salutem & justitiam proferat, cuinam persuadebit Grotius? Tum vero aliud est princi- pem utcunque justum esse, ac felicem: aliud, justitiam & salutem veram progerminare, quam omnes pii desiderant, atque exoptant. Porro si verba ita red- denda, hanc terram progerminare faciet is, quem ego creavi Dominus, quo pacto, sodes, hæc convenient Cyro, num is progerminare fecit justitiam simul & salutem? Hoc Dei est, non Principis aut Monar- chæ alicujus. Denique si similis hic locus noster est cum Psal. 72, 6. 7. quod fatetur Grotius, nihil cer- tius est, quam quod de Christo agat. Illum enim de Christo agere, cum de loco isto disseruimus, invicte probavimus. Oecolampadius etsi Cyrum ut typum intelligat, justitiæ tamen laudem & titulum illi quo- modo attribuat non invenit. Cyrus, inquit, non fuit vere justus, sed rapacissimus & crudelissimus, tametsi Judæis fuerit benignus. Et propterea, ut historiæ ha- bent, tandem à Tomyre Scytharum Regina extinctus est, cum 200000. capite ejus in utrem projecto sanguine oppletum, quæ & dixit ἐνεπλήσθητι αἱματοδιψάση κεφαλὴ, satiare sanguinem sitiens caput. At Christus noster vere justus, atque justitia ipsa, à Babyloniis atrocioribus nos eripuit.

## 45:9
Verse 9. WOE TO HIM WHO CONTRADICTS HIS MAKER.) He now brings forward the cause for the overturning of the Babylonian kingdom, because its Kings are to be impious toward the true God in words and deeds. See Daniel, V; but he illustrates by comparisons how wicked this is.

Others bring forward other reasons for the continuity, especially those who likewise refer the following to Christ. We willingly admit, however, that here the Prophet returns again to Cyrus. But he does not therefore bring forward the cause of the overturning of the Babylonian kingdom: for he is dealing with the Jews, nay, he is rebuking the Jews, who out of impatience, especially in the Babylonian captivity, were about to murmur against God. But Grotius inserts these things so that he may obtain that the Babylonians are also addressed thereafter, of which, however, no indication appears in the Prophet. For as to verse 11. ASK ME OF THINGS TO COME CONCERNING MY SONS, AND CONCERNING THE WORK OF MY HANDS COMMAND YE ME: Which Grotius takes thus: Ask of me what I wish to do concerning that people whom I embrace as a son: And command me: that is, hinder if you can; you will thus experience what you can do and what I can do; (As if they had been said to the Babylonians.) God addresses anyone from the opposite side who opposes himself to the counsels of God, whoever he may be, and he does not precisely understand the Jewish people by his sons, or their liberation from the Babylonian captivity by the work of his hands, but he speaks ironically: teach me how I ought to treat, punish, or rescue my sons. But Grotius perverts the words of Verse 9 even more.

SHALL THE CLAY SAY TO ITS POTTER: WHAT ARE YOU DOING? AND YOUR WORK IS WITHOUT HANDS.) Better; How do you make me? For your work there are no hands; that is, suitable ones. You do not have enough strength. That is, against those who denied the creator of things.

Latin:

Vers. 9. VÆ QVI CONTRADICIT FICTORI SVO.) Causam jam adfert evertendi regni Babylonici, quod ejus Reges in Deum verum impii futuri sint verbis factisque. Vid. Danielem, V, quam autem hoc sit iniquum, similitudinibus illustrat.

Alias rationes τῆς συνεχείας alii adducunt, ma- xime illi, qui sequentia itidem ad Christum refe- runt. Libenter tamen admittimus, hic jam denuo Prophetam redire ad Cyrum. Sed non ideo causam eversionis regni Babylonici adfert: Nam cum Ju- dæis agit, imo objurgat Judæos, qui ex impatientia, præsertim in captivitate Babylonica, murmuraturi erant adversus Deum. Sed ingerit hæc Grotius, ut deinceps quoque compellari Babylonios obtineat, cujus vero indicium non apparet in Propheta. Nam quod ad vers. 11. VENTURA INTERRO- GATE SUPER ME: SUPER FILIOS MEOS, ET SUPER OPUS MANUUM MEARUM MANDATE MIHI: Quæ Grotius ita accipit: Quærite à me, quid ego facere velim de illo populo, quem ut filium amplector: Et præcipite mihi: id est, impedite si potestis; quod ego de illis facere volo, ita experiemini, quid vos possitis & quid ego possim; (Ac si dicta essent ad Babylonios.) Compellat Deus quemvis ἐξ ἐναντίας, qui sese consiliis Dei oppo- nit, quisquis ille fuerit, neque præcise populum Iu- dæum per filios suos intelligit, aut per opus manuum suarum liberationem ejusdem è captivitate Baby- lonica, sed Ironice loquitur: docete me, quomodo filios meos tractare, punire, aut eripere debeam. Sed magis adhuc pervertit Grotius verba Vers. 9.

NUMQUID DICET LUTUM FIGULO SUO: QUID FACIS? ET OPUS TUUM ABSQUE MA- NIBUS EST.) Melius; Quomodo me facies? ad opus tuum non sunt manus; idoneæ scilicet. Non satis habes virium. H.e. adversus eos, qui rerum creatorem negabant.

## 45:10
WOE TO HIM WHO SAYS TO A FATHER, WHAT ARE YOU BEGETTING.) How could you beget?

AND TO A WOMAN, WHAT ARE YOU BRINGING FORTH.) How could you bring forth.

For these things were not said against the creation of God, but against divine providence and the governance of things: not as if it were denied that God can create or form something out of clay, because the clay is introduced insulting the potter, not because the potter lacks hands, force, and power, but because he is as if a potter weak toward the clay. The discourse is about the quality of the deed, not about the power of creating. Therefore, B. Luther rightly rendered those words 'your work is without hands' according to the sense: 'You do not show your hand in your work.' Let Grotius be compared here to Romans 9:20. The Apostle certainly in Romans 9:20 brought these things forward in a far different sense than Grotius interpreted, and understood them not of creation, but of the providence of God, to which the reprobate oppose themselves. Nor does the Prophet say woe to him who denies to a father or mother the power of begetting or bringing forth, for how would he be his father, or she his mother, without the power of begetting? or how can a son, if he is of sound mind, deny that his father begets, his mother brings forth, and that he who was born of a mother is not born? Grotius's gloss is therefore inept. And it can be obscure to no one that those who complain about the quality of the divine work, and the governance and disposition of God, are introduced, not those who deny him the power of creating, as Grotius prattles. A similar complaint is had in Jeremiah 15:10: Woe is me! my mother, why did you beget me a man of strife, a man of discord!

Latin:

VÆ QVI DICIT PATRI, QVID GENERAS.) Quomodo generare posses?

ET MULIERI, QVID PARTURIS.) Quomodo posses parere.

Non enim hæc dicta adversus Dei creationem, sed adversus divinam providentiam, rerumque gu- bernationem : non quasi negetur Deum creare aut ex luto aliquid formare posse, quia lutum figulo insultans introducitur, non quod figulo manus, vis, ac potentia desit, sed quod quasi figulus in lutum infirmus sit. De qualitate facti, non de potentia cre- andi sermo est. Ideo verba illa opus tuum absq; ma- nibus est, B. Lutherus recte ad sensum reddidit : Du beweisest deine Hand nicht an deinem Werck. Conferatur hic Grotius ad Rom. 9, 20. S. Aposto- lus certe Rom. 9, 20. hæc longe alio sensu addu- xit, quam Grotius interpretatus est, & intellexit non de creatione, sed providentia Dei, cui sese re- probi opponunt. Neque væ illi dicit Propheta, qui Patri aut matri vim generandi aut pariendi dene- gat, quomodo enim Pater ipsius esset, aut mater, si- ne vi generandi? aut quomodo negare potest fi- lius, si sanæ sit mentis, Patrem generare, matrem parere, ac matre natum esse non nasciat? Inepta er- go Grotii glossa est. Et nemini obscurum esse potest, de qualitate operis divini, ac gubernationis & dispositionis Dei conquerentes introduci, non qui de- negant ipsi creandi potentiam, ut nugatur Grotius. Similis querela habetur Jer. 15, 10. Væ mihi! ma- ter mea, quare genuisti me virum rixæ; virum discordiæ !

## 45:11
Verse 11. THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL HIS MAKER) Who as creator is acknowledged by him.

ASK ME OF THINGS TO COME CONCERNING MY SONS) Ask of me what I wish to do concerning that people whom I embrace as a son.

AND CONCERNING THE WORK OF MY HANDS COMMAND ME) And give me orders. That is, hinder me, if you can, from doing what I wish concerning them. Thus you will experience what you can do, and what I can do.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SANCTUS ISRAEL PLASTES EJUS) Qui ut creator ab ipso agnoscor.

VENTURA INTERROGATE ME SUPER FI- LIOS MEOS) Quærite a me, quid, ego facere velim de illo populo, quem ut filium amplector.

ET SUPER OPUS MANUUM MEARUM MAN- DATE MIHI) Et præcipite mihi. Id est, impedite, si potestis, ne, quod volo, de illis faciam. Ita experiemini quid vos possitis, & quid ego possim.

## 45:12
Vers. 12. AND TO ALL THEIR HOST I HAVE COMMANDED.) I command. See above 40, 26. How, therefore, would you hinder my decrees, to which even the stars obey.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET OMNI MILITIÆ EORUM MAN- DAVI.) Impero. Vide supra 40, 26. quomodo ergo vos mea decreta impediretis, quibus & astra parent.

## 45:13
Vers. 13. I HAVE RAISED HIM UP TO RIGHTEOUSNESS) I have raised Cyrus to the kingdom so that he might do those things which are just and equitable.

AND I WILL DIRECT ALL HIS WAYS) I will give him admirable success, as above in this chapter 1 and 2.

HE SHALL BUILD MY CITY.) That is, the temple, the most important part of the city, see 2 Chronicles 36, 23 and the beginning of Ezra.

He takes these things again concerning Cyrus. But the Fathers with great consensus wish the Prophet to be prophesying now about Christ; Jerome, Cyril, Procopius in this place, Origen likewise, Eusebius in book 5 of the Evangelical Demonstrations, Epiphanius, Hilary, Haymo, and others, whom Leo Castrius has followed. Cornelius à Lapide and Tirinus, although they interpret them concerning Cyrus, nevertheless acknowledge that certain things agree more with Christ, and thus they have recourse to a double sense, one literal concerning Cyrus, the other mystical concerning Christ. However, they are forced to admit that certain things in no way agree with Cyrus, but only with Christ: and yet they drag the whole text according to the literal sense to Cyrus: which is to import a sense into Scripture and to twist it. For if even a single sentence of a chapter or of some passage does not agree with Cyrus, how is the whole sequence to be understood literally concerning Cyrus? But that confession of theirs is sufficient for us, which is an argument that it is better to adhere to the explanation of the Ancients, inasmuch as not even the defenders of the double sense themselves deny that everything agrees aptly with Christ according to it. There are indeed not lacking even among our own people those who interpret the present verse 13 still concerning Cyrus, such as B. Brentius and Osiander, but these nevertheless determine that in v. 14 it is not a matter of Cyrus, but that the Prophet passes to a prophecy concerning the propagation of the Church of God, so that, namely, the Israelites might know that the Babylonian captivity would not oppress the Church of God, but after this evil was overcome in its own time there would be a far greater number of believers. However, there does not seem to be a sufficient reason why Cyrus should be introduced again in these words, and why we should depart from the explanation of the Fathers. Nor indeed can it be said of Cyrus that he built the city. For the fact that he permitted the temple to be built is a different matter. The Prophet is not prophesying here about the temple, but about the city. Therefore, others have long since referred these things to Zerubbabel, as Jerome reports. But Jerome refutes both here. Some, he says, refer these things to Zerubbabel, who led the captives out of Babylon, and built the city, and erected the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah were prophesying and saying: The hands of Zerubbabel have founded this house, and his hands shall complete it. But we say more correctly and more truly that neither did Cyrus build the city, which was later built under Nehemiah, nor were all his ways made straight. To whom it was said above: I have taken you, and girded you, and you have not known me: and Zerubbabel, who was under the nod and power of the Medes and Persians, exceeds all that is said. For Zerubbabel did not build the city: nor did he dismiss the captivity, nor can he be called King, who, living under other kings, lacked this title. We argue these things, however, in such a way that we will not peevishly object if the present verse alone is taken as referring to Cyrus, provided that the following ones are not dragged along to the same, because the preceding things look to him, and a new discourse seems to begin only at the following verse, 14.

Verse of the same. MY CAPTIVITY HE SHALL DISMISS) My captive people.

NOT FOR PRICE, NOR FOR REWARDS) He is neither going to accept nor to demand anything for such a great benefit from the Jews. He describes his truly royal spirit.

Latin:

Vers. 13. EGO SUSCITAVI EUM AD JUSTI- TIAM) Cyrum evexi in regnum ut ea quæ justa & æqua sunt faceret.

ET OMNES VIAS EJUS DIRIGAM) Successus ipsi admirandos dabo, ut supra hoc capite 1. & 2.

IPSE ÆDIFICABIT CIVITATEM MEAM.) Id est templum, partem urbis potissimam, vide. 2. Paralip. 36, 23. & initium Esdræ.

De Cyro hæc iterum accipit. Sed Patres ma- gno consensu de Christo jam vaticinari Prophe- tam volunt, Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Procopius in h. l. Origenes item, Eusebius lib. 5. Demonst. Evangeli- carum, Epiphanius, Hilarius, Haymo, & alii, quos Leo Castrius sequutus est. Cornel. à Lapide, & Tiri- nus etsi de Cyro accipiunt, quædam tamen magis Christo convenire agnoscunt, adeoque ad geminum sensum, alium literalem de Cyro, alium mysticum de Christo confugiunt. Fateri autem coguntur, quæ- dam nullatenus Cyro convenire, sed tantum Christo : & abripiunt tamen textum totum secundum sen- sum literalem ad Cyrum : quod est sensum inferre Scripturæ, eamque torquere. Si enim vel unica sen- tentia capitis, aut pericopes alicujus haud conve- niat Cyro, quomodo tota συνέχεια de Cyro intelli- getur literaliter? Sed sufficit nobis illa ipsorum confessio, quæ argumento est, quod adhærere præ- stet explicationi Veterum, utpote, juxta quam omnia apte Christo convenire, ne ipsi quidem ge- mini sensus propugnatores diffitentur. Non de- sunt sane etiam è nostris, qui versum præsentem 13. adhuc de Cyro interpretantur, utpote B. Brentius, & Osiander, sed hi tamen statuunt v. 14. non agi de Cyro sed transire Prophetam ad vaticinium de pro- pagatione Ecclesiæ Dei, ut sc. scirent Israelitæ Baby- lonicam captivitatem non oppressuram Ecclesiam Dei, sed post hoc superatum malum suo tempore majorem longe numerum futurum credentium. Non videtur autem causa sufficiens, cur Cyrus in his verbis ingerendus denuo sit, & cur à Patrum ex- plicatione discedere debeamus. Neq; vero de Cy- ro dici potest, quod ædificaverit civitatem. Quod enim templum ædificare permiserit, diversum est. Non de templo hic, sed de civitate vaticinatur Pro- pheta. Ideo alii hæc ad Zorobabelem, ut refert Hie- ronymus, jam pridem retulere. Sed utrumque re- fellit hic Hieronymus. Nonnulli, inquit, hæc ad Zo- robabelem referunt, qui eduxit captivos de Babylone, & ædificavit civitatem, & extruxit templum, pro- phetantibus Aggæo, & Zacharia atque dicentibus : Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam, & manus ejus complebunt eam. Sed nos rectius dici- mus & verius, nec Cyrnm ædificasse civitatem, quæ postea exstructa est sub Nehemia, nec omnes vias ejus fuisse directas. Cui supra dictum est : affumsi, & ac- cinxi te & non cognovisti me : & Zorobabel sta- tum, qui sub nutu ac potestate Medorum fuit atque Persarum,omnia quæ dicuntur excedere. Neque enim Zorobabel exstruxit civitatem : nec captivitatem dimifit, nec Rex appellari potest, qui sub aliis vivens regibus hoc nomine caruit. Hæc tamen ita disputa- mus, ut non morose refragaturi simus, si versus so- lum præsens de Cyro accipiatur, dum sequentes modo ad eundem non abripiantur, eo quod ante- cedentia ad ipsum spectent, & versu sequente 14. demum nova concio inchoari videatur.

Vers. eod. MEAM CAPTIVITATEM DIMITTET) Populum meum captivum.

NON IN PRETIO, NEQVE IN MUNERI- BUS) Nihil pro tanto beneficio ab Judæis aut accepturus aut postulaturus. Describit animum ejus vere regalem.

## 45:14
Verse 14. THUS SAYS THE LORD, THE LABOR OF EGYPT, AND THE MERCHANDISE OF ETHIOPIA, AND THE SABEANS, MEN OF STATURE SHALL PASS OVER TO YOU, AND SHALL BE YOURS) The sense is: Because you will do such an excellent thing, Cyrus, without being induced by any reward, I will give you a reward of my own accord. The Egyptians, Ethiopians, and Sabeans had been on the side of the Babylonians, and were likewise slaughtered, captured, and plundered in that battle in which Cyrus emerged victorious at Babylon. Those peoples, however, were very wealthy. Concerning Egypt, see 1 Kings 10:28; concerning the Ethiopians, Job 28:19, Psalm 68:32. Concerning the Sabeans, Pliny 6:28. The Sabeans are the most famous of the Arabs for their incense, with their nations extending to both seas. Thus in the auxiliaries of Antony in Virgil, Book 8: — All Egypt and the Indians, all the Arabs, all the Sabeans turned their backs in that terror.

THEY SHALL WORSHIP YOU) They shall prostrate themselves before you, in the manner of the Orient. Arrian says that this honor was first bestowed upon Cyrus among the Persians. Among other nations, it was quite ancient.

ONLY IN YOU IS GOD, AND THERE IS NO GOD BESIDE YOU) In the Hebrew: Only in you (that is, with you) is God, beside whom there is no God. These words will be those of the conquered nations to Cyrus.

Grotius drags all these things to Cyrus, but the Hebrew text resists, in which all the pronouns are of the feminine gender, whence Cyrus cannot be understood, to whom those nations were to pass, and whose they were to be. Nor indeed does that veneration, of which there is question here, befit Cyrus: and they shall worship you, and they shall beseech you, only in you is God. For how could these things be said to Cyrus, that God is only in him? For to render that 'in you' as 'with you' is not to explain, but to pervert the text. Let those of the Jesuits who understand this prophecy literally with Alvarez, Sanctius, and Cornelius see how they wish to explain it concerning Cyrus, an impious man, an idolater, and a tyrant, as they call him. Cornelius himself admits that these things do not befit Cyrus: for he says that what follows befits Christ, not Cyrus: only in you is God, and there is no God beside you, truly you are a hidden God. And although the Jesuit Sanctius recites Alvarez, Pintus, and Vatablus (whom he falsely adds here to the rest) as explaining them in such a way, certainly 'in you, Cyrus, is God, who fights and conquers,' he does not, however, approve of that gloss, but acknowledges that these things befit Christ properly: Truly these things befit Christ ALONE properly. Which he explains at greater length. But if they properly befit Christ alone, they will certainly not befit Cyrus, unless perhaps he wishes them to be taken improperly at the same time, which is absurd. Furthermore, the ancients have interpreted this prophecy concerning Christ with one accord. Ambrose, Book 1, On the Faith, ch. 2; Athanasius, On the Assumption of Man; Epiphanius, Book 1, against the Noetian heresies; Eusebius, Book 5, Demonstration, ch. 4; Hilary, Book 4, On the Trinity; Theodoret, Cyril, Procopius, Jerome here, and others everywhere, as the Jesuits admit, to whom our own people also accede, B. Brentius, Osiander, Pappus, and others. Jerome refutes at length those who understand it concerning Cyrus with the Jews, and demonstrates the Deity of Christ from this passage. And in this passage, those who follow the history say that Egypt, and the Ethiopians, and the nations of the Sabeans, which are beyond Ethiopia, served Cyrus, and that the furthest nations were subject to him: and that from the wonderful victory they understood that the Lord was in him, and that there was no other God beside him who dwelt in him. But this which follows: Truly you are a hidden God, the God of Israel the Savior, I do not understand how it can befit the person of Cyrus: Unless perhaps they use the edition of Theodotion: who translated: In you is a strong one, and there is no other God beside him: Therefore you are a strong hidden God, the God of Israel the Savior. Wherever they turn themselves, they will not be able to escape the snares of the truth. For suppose that God is in Cyrus, and that there is no other God beside him who is in Cyrus, how will it be fitting to say to the person of Cyrus: Truly you are a hidden God, the God of Israel the Savior? Therefore, the God in whom is God our Lord Jesus Christ is understood more correctly and more truly, who speaks in the Gospel: I and the Father are one. Who is called a hidden God, on account of the Sacrament of the assumed body, and the God of Israel the Savior, which is interpreted as Jesus. These are the words of Jerome. But since the pronouns of the feminine gender, of which six occur here, without any indication of enallage, sufficiently prove that Jerusalem or the Church is being addressed, and not Cyrus or Christ, we cannot therefore use that argument for the Deity of Christ, except according to man and by hypothesis. Wherefore it remains that these things be understood either as Jerusalem, whether implied or pointed out in chapter 44:24, or be referred to the city, mention of which is made here in the immediately preceding verse by the word עִירִי my city: Thus the spiritual city of the Lord to be built by the Messiah will be designated there, to which the Gentiles were bound to join themselves. Brentius observed this in this place. This discourse is directed to the assembly of Israel, or to the true Church of God, in which alone is the true God, and the true worship of God. But what is promised to the Church here? Oecolampadius wishes the Prophet to speak of tribute money spent on the expenses of the temple, because all those tributary peoples were bound to become subject to Cyrus, who reigned as far as the Ethiopians: But he does not acquiesce in that explanation, nay rather he understands it of the Church, whose temple Christ built, to which many came not only from Ethiopia, but also from the east and west, testifying that they had hitherto been ensnared by the chains of sins, and would henceforth serve Christ, and would protest and say to the Church, only in you is the true God, the true faith, etc. Which latter explanation is more apt: for the same text cannot admit both senses at once. Therefore our Brentius explains it concerning the access to the Church: By labor and trade are to be understood men laboring and trading, or industrious farmers and fishermen in Egypt, and merchants in Ethiopia. I will cause, he says, the labor of Egypt, i.e., the inhabitants of Egypt laboring hard, and

The Ethiopians, devoted to trade, and the Sabeans, whose inhabitants are famous for the length of their stature, shall come to you, my people or Church, and shall deliver themselves to you as captives: they shall follow you bound in chains, they shall venerate you as their King or Magistrate, and they shall be suppliants to you. These things cannot be referred to the time of the return from the Babylonian captivity. For the Jews, after their return, never came into such power or Majesty that Egypt and the Ethiopians acknowledged and worshipped them as their Kings and magistrates. But they must be referred to the time of the revealed and published Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ through the Apostles to the whole world. For then the Egyptians, Ethiopians, and neighboring Gentiles delivered themselves as captives to the Jews, and became suppliants to them, when they subjected themselves to the preaching of the Apostles, and believed the Gospel preached by the Apostles. Did not the Ethiopian Eunuch, Prefect of Candace, Queen of Ethiopia, become a captive and a suppliant to Philip, according to this prophecy of Isaiah, when he delivered himself to him not only to be instructed, but also to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, just as it is written in Acts 8? It stands in the monuments of ecclesiastical history that when Mark the Evangelist was preaching the Gospel of Jesus Christ in Egypt, such a multitude of men and women acknowledged Christ through faith, and testified to their faith by the honesty of their lives, that they were a miracle to all, even to the Heathens. This is certainly that which is said in Isaiah to the Church: The labor of Egypt, and the trade of Ethiopia, and the tall men of the Sabeans shall pass over to you. They shall be yours, they shall walk behind you in chains. For as many as receive the Gospel by faith, chains are cast upon them, so that they are captured as if they were prisoners. But they are most happy chains, by which men are led away from impious idolatry to the true worship of God, from sins to justice, from death to life, from hell to heaven, through Jesus Christ the Son of God. To this end serves what is also said below in chapter 49: Kings shall be your foster fathers and queens your nursing mothers. With face bowed to the ground they shall adore you, and shall lick the dust of your feet, etc. And chapter 60: The sons of those who humbled you shall come to you bowing down, and shall adore the footprints of your feet. These things are clear, so that there is no need for more. Sanctius admits that it is not very easy to demonstrate how those regions came to the sacred rites of the Jews, or to their society. Cornel. a Lapide acknowledges that the meaning is that the wealth of those Egyptians, Ethiopians, and Sabeans, that is, of any Gentiles whatsoever, shall serve Christ, or that they shall come to Christ having abandoned their own religion, bound in manacles, as if conquered in war, defeated, and led in triumph: and that this phrase signifies an all-encompassing or spontaneous subjection, which the following words of bowing down and supplication indicate. These manacles, therefore, are the grace of God and the impulse of the Holy Spirit, whose bonds are stronger than adamant, as Ambrose says in Psalm 37. Jerome rightly observes that other nations are included under these nations. No one doubts that Egypt and the Ethiopians and the Sabeans, tall and sublime men, served Him, when he sees that the world is subject to Him, and perceives that from the name of a few nations, which dwell in the extreme ends of the earth, all the corners of the heavens and all the shores of the earth are going to believe in Him. Whence it is beautifully called the labor of Egypt, as if for those laboring in the error of idolatry, to cease. For no nation was so devoted to idolatry, and worshipped such innumerable portents, as Egypt. Vatablus's opinion, that the Israelites were to possess the wealth of the Egyptians, Ethiopians, and Sabeans when God would strike the camps of Sennacherib at the walls of Jerusalem through an angel, is foreign, and frivolous, and cold, as well as doubtful and uncertain. Equally doubtful and uncertain, equally cold and foreign, is the Gloss of Grotius, that the Egyptians, Ethiopians, and Sabeans were in the parts of the Babylonians, and were likewise struck, captured, and despoiled by Cyrus, and made him richer, except that this also contradicts the letter, which it is certain cannot be understood of Cyrus because of the feminine pronouns. Nor do those words sound of Cyrus, but of the Church: only in you is God, because He is found only in the Church and in the doctrine of the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 14. HÆC DICIT DOMINUS, LABOR ÆGYPTI, ET NEGOTIATIO ÆTHIOPIÆ, ET SABAIM, VIRI SUBLIMES AD TE TRANSI- BUNT, ET TUI ERUNT) Sensus est: Quia mer- cede nulla adductus, Cyre, rem facies tam egregiam,ego ul- tro tibi mercedem dabo, Ægyptii, Æthiopes, Sabæi in Ba- byloniorum fuerant partibus, & pariter cum eis cæsi, capti, spoljati sunt eo prælio, quo ad Babylonem victor exstitit Cyrus. Erant autem populi illi ditissimi. De Ægypto vid. 1.Reg. 10, 28. de Æthiopibus Job. 28, 19. Ps. 68, 32. De Sa- bæis Plinius 6, 28. Sabæi Arabum propter thura clarissimi, ad utraque maria porrectis gentibus. Sic in Antonii auxiliis apud Virgilium 8. - - Omnis eo terrore Ægyptus & Indi, Omnis Arabs, omnes verterunt terga Sabæi.

TE ADORABUNT) Coram te se prosternent,mo- re Orientis. Hunc honorem inter Persas Cyro primum de- latum ait Arrianus. Apud alias gentes erat satis antiquus.

TANTUM IN TE EST DEUS, ET NON EST ABSQUE TE DEUS) In Hebræo: Tantum in te (id est, tecum) est Deus, præter quem Deus non est. Hæc verba erunt victarum gentium ad Cyrum.

Hæc ad Cyrum omnia pertrahit Grotius, sed repugnat textus Ebræus, in quo pronomina omnia sunt fœminini generis, unde Cyrus intelligi non potest, ad quem transituræ gentes illæ erant, & cu- jus futuræ erant. Neque profecto Cyro convenit illa veneratio, de qua hic agitur: & te adorabunt, teque deprecabuntur, tantum in te est Deus. Quomo- do enim hæc dicerentur ad Cyrum, quod in ipso tantum Deus sit? Nam illud in te reddere tecum, non est explicare, sed pervertere textum. Qui è Jesuitis hanc Prophetiam literaliter cum Alvarez, Sanctio & Cornelio intelligunt, viderint, quomodo de Cyro, homine impio,idololatra & tyranno, ut eum vocant, explicare velint. Fatetur Cornelius ipse, non convenire hæc Cyro : Christo enim,inquit, non Cyro competit proprie & plene, id quod sequitur: tan- tum in te est Deus, & non est absque te Deus, vere es tu Deus absconditus. Et quanquam recitet Jesuita Sanctius, Alvarecium, Pintum, Vatablum (quem postremum reliquis falso hic accenset) ea ita explicare, certe in te Cyre est Deus, qui pugnat & vincit, non probat tamen illam glossam, sed agno- scit Christo hæc convenire proprie: Verum pro- prie hæc SOLI Christo competunt. Quod prolixius explicat. At si proprie soli Christo, utique Cyro non convenient, nisi forte improprie simul ea ac- cipi velit, quod ἀσύςατον. Porro vaticinium hoc de Christo Veteres ὁμοθυμαδὸν interpretati sunt. Ambrosius lib. 1. de Fide c. 2. Athanas. de assumt. hominis. Epiphanius lib. 1. in hæres. Noëtian: Euseb. lib. 5. Demonst. c. 4. Hilarius lib. 4. de Trinit. Theodoretes, Cyrillus, Procopius, Hierony- mus hic, & alii passim fatentibus Jesuitis Interpp. quibus etiam nostrates accedunt, B. Brentius, Osi- ander, Pappus, & alii. Hieronymus prolixe refellit eos, qui de Cyro cum Judæis intelligunt, ac Deita- tem Christi ex hoc loco demonstrat. Et in hoc lo- co, qui sequuntur historiam, dicunt Ægyptum, & Æthiopes, gentesque Sabaim, quæ trans Æthiopiam sunt, servisse Cyro, & ei gentes ultimas fuisse subjectas: atque ex mirabili intellexisse victoria, quod in eo esset Dominus, & non esset alius præter eum, qui in illo ha- bitaret Deus. Sed hoc quod sequitur: Vere tu es Deus absconditus, Deus Israel Salvator, quomodo possit Cyri personæ convenire, non intelligo: Nisi for- te Theodotionis utantur editione: qui transtulit: In te est fortis, & non est alius præter eum Deus: Pro- pterea tu fortis absconditus Deus Israel Salvator. Quocunque se verterint, non valebunt laqueos verita- tis effugere. Fac enim, esse in Cyro Deum, & non esse alium præter eum, qui sit in Cyro, Deus, quomodo Cyri personæ dici conveniet: Vere tu es Deus abscondi- tus, Deus Israel Salvator? Ergo Deus in quo est Deus Dominus noster Jesus Christus rectius intelligi- tur & verius, qui in Evangelio loquitur: Ego & Pa- ter unum sumus. Qui Deus appellatur absconditus, propter assumpti corporis Sacramentum, & Deus Israel Salvator, quod interpretatur Jesus. Hæc Hieronymus. Sed quum pronomina fœminini ge- neris, quorum hic sex occurrunt, sine ullo enallages indicio, satis evincant Hierosolymam vel Ecclesiam compellari, non vero Cyrum, aut Christum, ideo ar- gumento illo pro Deitate Christi uti non possu- mus, nisi κατ' ἄνθρωπον & ex hypothesi. Quapro- pter restat, ut de Hierosolyma sive subintellecta, sive cap. 44. 24. indigitata hæc intelligantur, aut ad ci- vitatem, cujus mentio hic versu immediate præce- denti voce עִירִי civitas mea, facta est, referantur: Sic civitas Domini spiritualis ædificanda per Mes- siam ibi designabitur, ad quam se aggregare debe- bant gentiles. Observavit id Brentius in h. l. Dirigi- tur hic sermo ad cœtum Israelis, seu ad veram Eccle- siam Dei, in qua sola verus est Deus, & verus cultus Dei. Quid autem hic Ecclesiæ promittitur? Oe- colampadius Prophetam loqui vult de pecunia tri- butaria in sumptus templi expensa, quod populi illi omnes tributarii fieri debuerint Cyro, qui regnavit usque ad Æthiopes: Sed non acquiescit illi expli- cationi, imo de Ecclesia potius intelligit, cujus tem- plum Christus exstruxit, quod ad hanc multi vene- rint non solum ex Æthiopia, sed etiam ab oriente & occidente, testantes se hactenus vinculis pecca- torum irretitos, posthac servituros Christo, atque protestaturos & dicturos Ecclesiæ, tantum in te ve- rus Deus, vera fides &c. Quæ posterior explicatio aptior: utrumque enim sensum simul admittere idem textus nequit. Ideo Brentius noster de ac- cessu ad Ecclesiam exponit: Per laborem & nego- tiationem intelligendi homines laborantes & nego- tiantes, aut laboriosi agricolæ, & piscatores in Ægypto, & mercatores in Æthiopia. Efficiam ut labor, inquit, Ægypti, h. e. incolæ Ægypti duriter laborantes, &

Æthiopes negotiationibus dediti, & Sabaim, quo- rum incolæ celebres sunt longitudine staturæ, ve- niant ad te, populum seu Ecclesiam meam, & tra- dant se tibi captivos: sequentur te vincti compedi- bus, venerabuntur te, tanquam Regem seu Magi- stratum suum, & erunt tibi supplices. Hæc non pos- sunt referri ad tempus reditus ex captivitate Baby- lonica. Judæi enim, post reditum suum, nunquam venerunt in tantam vel potentiam, vel Majestatem, ut Ægyptus & Æthiopes agnoverint, & coluerint eos, tanquam Reges & magistratus suos. Sed refe- renda sunt ad tempus revelati, & vulgati Evangelii Domini nostri Jesu Christi per Apostolos in totum or- bem terræ. Tunc enim Ægyptii, Æthiopes, & finiti- mæ Gentes tradiderunt se captivos Judæis, & facti sunt eis supplices, cum subjecerunt se prædicationi Apostolorum, & crediderunt Evangelio per Apo- stolos prædicato. Annon Æthiops Evnuchus Præ- fectus Candaces Reginæ Æthiopiæ factus est capti- vus, & supplex Philippo, juxta hanc Esaiæ Prophe- tiam, cum tradidit sese ei non tantum erudiendum, sed etiam baptizandum in nomine Jesu Christi, quemadmodum scriptum est Act. 8. Extat in Ec- clesiasticæ historiæ monumentis, quod cum Mar- cus Evangelista Evangelion de Jesu Christo in Ægypto prædicaret, tanta virorum & mulierum multitudo Christum per fidem agnoverint, & ho- nestate vitæ suæ fidem testati sint, ut omnibus, etiam Ethnicis fuerint miraculo. Hoc certe illud est, quod in Esaia ad Ecclesiam dicitur: Labor Ægypti, & negotiatio Æthiopiæ, & viri longi Sebaim ad te transibunt. Tui erunt, post te ibunt in compe- dibus. Quotquot enim Evangelion fide accipiunt, iis injiciuntur compedes, ut velut captivi compre- hendantur. Sed sunt felicissimæ compedes, quibus abducuntur homines ab impia idololatria ad ve- rum cultum Dei, à peccatis ad justitiam, à morte ad vitam, ab inferno ad cœlum, per Jesum Christum Filium Dei. Huc facit quod & infra cap. 49. dici- tur: Reges erunt nutritii tui & reginæ nutrices tuæ. Vultu in terram demisso adorabunt te, & pulverem pedum tuorum lingent &c. Et cap. 60. Venient ad te curvi filii eorum, qui humiliaverunt te, & adora- bunt vestigia pedum tuorum. Luculenta hæc sunt, ut pluribus opus non sit. Fatetur Sanctius, quomo- do regiones illæ ad Judæorum sacra, sive ad societatem accesserint, non esse admodum promptum demon- strare. Cornel. à Lapide agnoscit, sensum esse, quod illorum Ægyptiorum, Æthiopum & Sabæo- rum, id est, quorumvis gentilium opes Christo servi- turæ sint, vel quod illi ad Christum deserta sua religio- ne accessuri sint, vincti manicis, quasi bello subacti, victique & in triumphum ducti: & hanc phrasin significare omnimodam, seu spontaneam subjectio- nem, quod indicant verba sequentia, incurvationis & supplicationis. Manicæ ergo hæ sunt gratia Dei, & impulsus S.S. cujus vincula adamante sunt fortio- ra, dicente Ambrosio in Ps. 37. Sub istis gentibus cæteras comprehendi recte observat Hieronymus. Serviisse autem ei Ægytum & Æthiopas & Sabaim, excelsos viros atque sublimes, nemo dubitat, cum ei mundum videat esse subjectum, & ex paucarum no- mine nationum, quæ habitant in extremis finibus ter- ræ, cunctos cælorum cardines, & omnia terræ litto- ra ei creditura perspiciat. Unde pulchre quasi labo- rantibus in errore idololatriæ, cessare labor Ægyti nominatur. Nulla enim gens ita idololatriæ dedita fuit, & tam innumerabilia portenta venerata est, quam Ægyptus. Vatabli opinio, quod Israelitæ po- tituri sint opibus Ægyptiorum, Æthiopum & Sa- bæorum, cum cædet Deus ad mœnia Hierusalem per angelum castra Sennacherib, aliena est, ac fri- vola gida, nec non dubia & incerta. Æque dubia & in- certa, æque frigida atque aliena est Glossa Grotii, quod Egyptii, Æthiopes & Sabæi in Babyloniorum partibus fuerint, & pariter cum his cæsi, capti & spo- liati sint a Cyro, eumque ditiorem reddiderint, nisi quod hæc etiam literæ repugnet, quam de Cyro non posse intelligi e pronominibus fœmininis cer- tum est. Nec de Cyro, sed Ecclesia sonant illa, tan- tummodo in te est Deus, quia is in sola Ecclesia, & Ecclesiæ doctrina invenitur.

## 45:15
Verse 15. TRULY YOU ARE A HIDDEN GOD.) Aquila: ἀποκρυπτόμενος. Theodotion: κρυφαῖος: that is, admirable. Here Isaiah begins to speak again.

Others take these as the words of the Church. But little depends on that. For most apply them not badly to Christ: Truly you are a hidden God and the Savior of Israel, because it is a notable confession concerning Christ, His Deity, and His office. Those Johannine words in 1 John 5:20 agree: This is the true God and eternal life. Thus the Son of God is hidden, as regards His hidden essence (Matt. 11:27), as regards the hidden counsels of His works, and as most of the Fathers declare, as regards the οἰκονομίαν, because He is hidden and covered by human nature, by human weaknesses, by the cross and death. But God the Savior of Israel is a proper epithet, indeed the office of the Son of GOD (Matt. 1:21, Acts 4:12), which He Himself will then explain more fully.

It is helpful, however, to add here what we proposed concerning this prophecy in an Academic program: the tenor of which was this:

Beyond controversy, great is the mystery of godliness: GOD was made conspicuous in the flesh! Stupendous was the dream of the Patriarch Jacob, when he saw a ladder that stood on the earth, but with its top reached the highest heaven, and was the seat of the most high God. Great was the vision of Moses, the Israelite leader, when the Lord appeared in the flame of fire in the midst of the bush, so that the bush indeed burned, but was not consumed. Nor is it to be doubted that an admirable ὅραμα was exhibited to King David, when, as if rapt out of himself, he exclaimed in astonishment: This is the form of the man who is the Lord God in the highest! Tremendous also was the spectacle of the Prophet Ezekiel, when he beheld the likeness of the glory of the Lord on a sapphire throne, and in it the Son of man shining with divine majesty. But with whatever admiration those things might strike the men of God; they were only visions, dreams, figures, and shadows. Here, however, the fulfillment, the truth itself, the body and substance is exhibited. Therefore, not even the leader of the Apostles could find words with which to express the admirable sublimity of the matter. He called it a mystery; because by reason of itself it is sacred, sublime, and divine, and by reason of us it is arcane and hidden, which can neither be investigated by sense or reason, nor comprehended by any created intellect, much less expressed in words by anyone. A mystery of godliness; because it is not profane, but sacred and religious, nay, the foundation of all religion and piety, and ought not to be considered except piously and religiously. A great mystery; which, if you look at the author, was decreed and ordained by the Great God; if you attend to the mystery itself, it concerns a truly great and admirable person, GOD-MAN, SON OF GOD AND MAN, A GIANT OF DUAL SUBSTANCE; if you consider the fruit, it exhibits the stupendous effects of the greatest works and benefits, since heaven is united to earth, God in turn to man, and what we shall admire eternally in ourselves, man divided from God is rendered a partaker of the divine nature. By the confession of all, and without any exception, a truly great mystery! For as soon as it is perceived, the human mind is turned into astonishment, every tongue is compelled to confess the ineffable magnitude. And what more admirable could be devised in heaven and earth, than that God should become man, and should be made visible in human flesh! God is an admirable deity; man is an admirable work of God, a miracle of the world that God is man, that the creator of the ages is created in an age, that the immutable is mutable flesh, that the invisible is made visible and conspicuous in flesh, that natures not only distant by the whole heaven, but infinitely distant, should unite into one person, should constitute one hypostasis, that indeed makes God, that makes man more admirable to us, and far surpasses the grasp not only of men, but of Angels and Archangels. O Lord, how admirable is thy name, truly thou art God, who doest wonders. I do not only admire the stature of this world, not the stability of the earth, since the revolving firmament encompasses it, not the individual days, not the defect and increase of the Moon, not the Sun always whole and his perpetual labor, not the vicissitudes of the seasons, in which some things wither, some things grow green, and those which seem dead for a moment, subsequently revive. I admire, with St. Cyprian, God in the womb of a virgin, I admire the omnipotent in the cradle: I admire how flesh adhered to the Word of God, how the incorporeal God put on the covering of our body. In other things, reasons of some kind satisfy in any way: here astonishment alone encompasses me; and with Habakkuk I sing: I have considered thy works, and I was afraid. But let us also rejoice, that for the sake of our salvation God has been manifested in the flesh. Behold I bring you good tidings of great joy, cries out first the celestial [messenger] of the New Test. Evangelist, which shall be to all people; for unto you is born this day a Savior, who is Christ the Lord in the city of David. For it is not right, in the judgment of Leo the Great, that there should be a place for sadness, where the birthday of life is, which, having consumed the fear of mortality, instills in us joy from the promised eternity. No one is separated from the participation of this cheerfulness, there is one common reason for joy for all, because our Lord, the destroyer of sin and death, just as he found no one free from guilt, so he came to liberate ALL. Let St. Athanasius, the Great Bishop of Alexandria, explain this to us more fully, who, dealing with the Incarnation of the Lord, says, There was need of death, and it was necessary that death be brought for ALL, so that what had been committed by ALL might be paid for. Wherefore the Word, since he could not die, being immortal, took to himself a body which could die, and offered it as his own for ALL, so that thus he himself, joined to the body for ALL, suffering death for ALL, might restrain him who has the power of death, that is, the Devil, and might liberate those, as many as were subject to servitude through all their life by the fear of death, the COMMON Savior of ALL. Who offered a sacrifice for ALL, delivered his temple to death for ALL, so that he might make ALL unliable and free from the ancient transgression. Thus, therefore, this joy is both truly great and altogether Catholic, which he prepared for all people. Which, so that it might be received by faith as undoubted, the Seraphic herald added a sign: You shall find the infant wrapped in swaddling clothes and laid in a manger. Concerning which sign most sweetly Augustus Augustine: The power is hidden in the limbs of the infant, God hangs at the breasts of his mother: He is covered by the squalor of vile rags, he suffers the straits of a most hard manger, and the merciful one suffers everything humbly, provided that the world, which had perished, is liberated. O blessed infancy, through which the life of our race is repaired! O most grave and delightful wailings, through which we have escaped the gnashing of teeth and eternal weepings! O happy rags, with which we have wiped away the filth of sins! O splendid manger, in which not only the hay of animals lay, but the food of Angels was found. Give suck, Mary, to your creator, give suck to the bread of heaven, the price of the world. Finally, you, as a mother, minister temporal substance to him, so that he himself may bestow upon us and you, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, life everlasting. Nor, however, is it fitting to meditate upon the mystery of God manifested in the flesh with only the religious veneration of admiration and the festive exultation of faith: But that we may also consecrate our whole selves with devotion of heart to God our Savior manifested in the flesh, the great sacrament of piety requires. For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all men, instructing us, that denying impiety and worldly desires we should live soberly and justly and piously in this age. God described the mode of devout subjection long ago, when he prophesied through Isaiah (c. 45) concerning the conversion of the Gentiles to Christ. * Thus says the Lord: The labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall pass over to thee, and they shall be thine: They shall walk after thee, they shall go bound with manacles, and they shall adore thee, and they shall make supplication to thee: Only in thee is God, and there is no God besides thee. Truly thou art a hidden God, the God of Israel the Savior. Jehovah himself, God the Father, speaks to another person equally divine, to whom they are to be converted: To THEE they shall pass over, they shall be Thine, they shall walk after THEE, they shall adore THEE, they shall make supplication to THEE. He adds the confession which they are to utter concerning him to whom they were to pass over. They shall adore Thee, they shall make supplication to Thee, by this, namely, formula of confession and religious veneration: Only in Thee (O Messiah) is God, and there is no God besides Thee. Truly thou art a hidden God, the God of Israel the Savior. What can be more clear, what more illustrious than this confession for celebrating the eternal Deity of Christ the Savior! Whom furthermore in verse 16 God opposes to idols, as the one God to fictitious deities, to whom the Gentiles were to be converted having abandoned them, as the only Jehovah the Savior, outside of whom there is no salvation. Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation, verse 17. Whom he also introduces himself speaking thus: I am the Lord and there is no other. I have not spoken in secret (these words Christ also made his own, and applied to himself in the days of his flesh, John 18:20.) I the Lord speaking righteousness, announcing things that are right (with which words Christ also described himself, Isa. 63:1.) Am I not the Lord, and there is no God besides me! A just God and a savior there is none besides me. Turn to me, and you shall be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other. To me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear: Therefore in the Lord, he shall say, is my righteousness and strength. Behold the characters of the Messiah, who is Jehovah our righteousness, Jer. 23:6, and our strength, by which we can do all things, Phil. 4:13, in whom alone we must glory, 1 Cor. 1:31. To whom the knees of all must be bowed, Rom. 14:11, Phil. 2:10. Which honor of genuflection the Church also exhibits to Christ at the holy name of Jesus the Savior: Whence Jerome says, Clearly, he says, in this is signified the Christian people: for it is an ecclesiastical custom to bow the knee to Christ. Which the Jews, showing the pride of their mind, do not do at all. For the Jews are accustomed to pray standing and upright. Therefore, God in whom is God, is Christ, as the ancients teach by common suffrage and it is most clearly evident from the text. Concerning which Jerome says: He is called a hidden God on account of the mystery of the assumed body; and God of Israel the Savior, which is interpreted Jesus. But that Egypt and the Ethiopians, and the Sabeans, men tall and sublime, have served him, no one doubts, when he sees the world to be subject to him, and from the name of a few nations, which dwell in the extreme ends of the earth, all the hinges of the heavens and all the shores of the earth are about to believe in him. Whence the labor of Egypt is beautifully called to cease, as if for those laboring in the error of idolatry. For no nation was so devoted to idolatry, and worshipped such innumerable portents, as Egypt. By this oracle, therefore, St. Athanasius convinced the Arians in Oration II in his book on the assumption of man; he convinced Macedonius in Dialogue III. Either you will become demented and deny that the Father is God, or, confessing that the Father is God, and likewise that the Son is God, and when you hear Him saying: 'I am God, and there is no other besides me,' you will confess a single Deity, and you will not be in danger. Therefore, having recited this oracle as being most evident, Ambrose exclaims in book 1 of De Fide, ch. 2: 'How does this agree according to the Arians?' Hilary exclaims in book 4 of De Trinitate. Is there still any room for rashness, or has any occasion for ignorance been left: unless it be that only this remains, that impiety openly betrays itself? Nor less excellently does Epiphanius refute Noetus from this, in heresy 57. But when he says, 'In Thee is God,' with what mystery, and how admirably does all Holy Scripture propose this. For in the flesh, as in a certain temple, the divinity was foreseen and shown to the hope of men through conversion to God: since the Son of God and God Himself, the Word, dwells as if in a certain holy city and religious temple in the assumed nature. Finally, Cyril of Alexandria most excellently confounded Nestorius (along with modern Nestorians) in book 1 on John, ch. 15: 'God is in the flesh, and with the flesh, according to nature. For He made that [flesh] His own, and yet He is understood as something else besides it, and is worshipped in it and with it (as Isaiah says): Men of stature shall pass over to you, etc.' Behold, he says, God is in him; we do not separate the flesh, that is, the man, from God. And again, he confirms there is no other God besides Him, joining to the Word the temple assumed from the Virgin, as His own; for Christ is one out of both. Similar things can be read in Eusebius, book 5 of Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. 4; Theodoret; the author of the commentary on Romans under the name of Ambrose, ch. 2; Procopius, and others. Therefore, let us trust in this our Savior as the one God with our whole mind, let us confess Him with an intrepid voice, and let us religiously worship Him in the flesh, and with the assumed flesh. Let us follow our patriarchs, the Magi from the East, since in them and their gifts, as Hilary teaches, the labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans—that is, the error of the world—are shown by the Magi worshipping, and the chosen gifts of the nations are offered by them to the Lord. Let us also offer the gold of faith, the incense of prayers, the myrrh of the mortification of the flesh. And that the labor of Egypt, that is, the wealth acquired by labor, may serve our Christ, let us deposit gifts at the altar of Christ with a cheerful hand for the ministers. Let us first of all present our bodies to Him as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God. Let us be entirely His, who spent His whole self for us. Let us walk after Him, bound with the shackles not of coercion, but of thanks and love, whose bonds, as Ambrose testifies in Psalm 35, are stronger than adamant. Let us bind and overcome our affections, the desires of the flesh, so that, bound by His laws, we may surrender ourselves in all-encompassing subjection.

Latin:

Vers. 15. VERE TV ES DEVS ABSCONDITVS.) Aquilæ ἀποκρυπτόμενος. Theodotioni κρυφαῖος : id est, ad- mirabilis. Hic Esaias iterum loqui incipit.

Alii hæc tanquam verba Ecclesiæ accipiunt. Sed in eo parum situm est. Ad Christum enim ple- rique non male applicant: Vere tu es absconditus & Deus Salvator Israelis, quod insignis sit confessio de Christo, ejus Deitate & officio. Consonant illa Johannæa 1. Epist. 5, 20. Hic est verus Deus, & vi- ta æterna. Sic absconditus est Filius Dei, quoad ab- sconditam essentiam Matth. 11, 27. quoad abscondi- ta operum consilia, & ut Patres plerique declarant, quoad οἰκονομίαν, quia absconditus & tectus est hu- mana natura, humanis imbecillitatibus, cruce & morte. Deus autem Salvator Israelis proprium est Epitheton, imo officium Filii DEI Matth. 1, 21. Act. 4, 12. quod deinde ipse plenius explicabit.

Juvat autem hic addere, quæ de hoc vaticinio in programmate Academico proposuimus : quod hujus erat tenor is :

Citra controversiam magnum est pietatis myste- rium, DEUS conspicuus factus est in carne! Stu- pendum fuit Jacobi Patriarchæ somnium, cum sca- lam vidit, quæ in terris consistebat, sed cacumine suo cœlum supremum attingebat, Deique altissimi sedes erat. Magna erat Mosis, Israelitici Ducis, vi- sio, cum in flamma ignis in medio rubi apparuit Dominus, ut arderet quidem rubus, sed non com- bureretur. Neque dubitandum est, admirandum Davidi Regi exhibitum fuisse ὅραμα, cum velut ex- tra se raptus præ stupore exclamabat, Ista est forma hominis, qui est Dominus Deus in excelsis! Tre- mendum quoque erat Ezechielis Prophetæ specta- culum, cum similitudinem gloriæ Domini in thro- no Sapphirino, & in ea Filium hominis majestate divina coruscantem cerneret. Sed quantacunque admiratione ista percellerent viros Dei; visiones tantum, somnia, figuræ & umbræ erant. Hic vero complementum, veritas ipsa, corpus & substantia exhibetur. Idcirco quibus verbis admirandam rei sublimitatem eloqueretur, ne Coryphæus quidem Apostolorum invenire potuit. Mysterium dixit; quia ratione sui sacra, sublimis & divina, ratione nostri arcana & abscondita est, quæ neque sensu aut ratione indagari, neque ab ullo creato intellectu comprehendi, nedum verbis a quoquam exprimi queat. Mysterium pietatis; quod non profanum id, sed sacrum ac religiosum, imo omnis religionis & pietatis fundamentum sit, nec nisi pie ac religiose considerari debeat. Mysterium magnum; quod, si au- thorem spectes, a Magno Deo decretum, & ordina- tum; Si mysterium ipsum attendas, magnam pror- sus ac admirandam personam, DEUM HOMI- NEM, FILIUM DEI ET HOMINIS, GI- GANTEM GEMINÆ SUBSTANTIÆ con- cernit; si fructum consideres, maximorum ope- rum ac beneficiorum stupendos effectus exhibet, quum cœlum terræ, Deus homini vicissim uniatur, & quod in nobis ipsis æternum admirabimur, ho- mo a Deo divisus consors divinæ naturæ reddatur. Omnium confessione, ac citra omnem exceptionem vere magnum mysterium! Quamprimum enim id percipitur, mens humana in stuporem convertitur, lingua omnis ineffabilem magnitudinem fateri co- gitur. Et quid admirandum magis in cœlo & terra excogitari potuit, quam quod Deus homo, & in carne humana conspicuus fieri debuit! Admiran- dum numen Deum est; admirandum Dei opus ho- mo, mundi miraculum, mundus ipse, ac totius uni- versi compendium. At quod Deus homo, quod se- culorum conditor in seculo conditus, quod immu- tabilis, caro mutabilis, quod invisibilis in carne visi- bilis, & conspicuus factus, quod naturæ non toto tantum cœlo, sed infinitum distantes in unam coë- ant personam, unam constituant hypostasin, id ve- ro Deum, id hominem nobis magis admirandum facit, & omnem non hominum tantum, sed Ange- lorum & Archangelorum captum longissime supe- rat. O Domine, quam admirabile est nomen tuum, vere tu es Deus, qui facis mirabilia. Non modo mun- di hujus staturam admiror, non stabilitatem terræ, cum eam complectatur volubile firmamentum, non singulos dies, non Lunæ defectum & incrementum, non Solem semper integrum & laborem ejus perpetu- um, non temporum vicissitudines, in quibus quædam arent, quædam virent, & quæ mortua modo videntur, deinceps reviviscunt. Miror, cum S. Cypriano, De- um in utero virginis, miror omnipotentem in cuna- bulis: miror, quomodo Verbo Dei caro adhæserit, quo- modo incorporeus Deus corporis nostri tegumentum induerit. In cæteris quocunque modo aliquæ satisfa- ciunt rationes: hic solus me complectitur stupor; & cum Habacuc cano: consideravi opera tua, & expa- vi. Sed & gaudeamus, quod nostræ salutis causa Deus in carne manifestatus sit. Ecce Evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, acclamat prius & cœle- stis Novi Test. Evangelista, quod erit omni populo; quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator, qui est Christus Dominus in civitate David. Neque enim fas est, Leo- ne M. judice, locum esse tristitiæ, ubi natalis est vitæ, quæ consumto mortalitatis timore nobis ingerit è pro- missa æternitate lætitiam. Nemo ab hujus alacritatis participatione secernitur, una cunctis communis læti- tiæ est ratio, quia Dominus noster peccati mortisque de- structor, sicut nullum à reatu liberum reperit, ita libe- randis OMNIBUS venit. Explicet id nobis ube- rius Magnus Alexandriæ Antistes S. Athanasius, qui de Incarnatione Domini agens, Morte, inquit, opus fuit, & mortem pro OMNIBUS inferri necessum erat, ut quod ab OMNIBUS delictum erat lueretur. Quamobrem Verbum, quoniam mori non potuit, ut- pote immortale, corpus sibi sumsit, quod mori poterat, illudque ut suum per OMNIBUS obtulit, ut ita pro OMNIBUS ipse corpore conjunctus OMNIBUS mortem patiens compesceret eum, qui habet mortis imperium, hoc est, Diabolum, & liberaret eos, quot- quot formidine mortis per omnem vitam servituti erant obnoxii, COMMUNIS OMNIUM Sal- vator. Qui pro OMNIBUS sacrificium obtulit, pro OMNIBUS templum suum morti tradidit, quo OMNES inobnoxios & liberos à veteri prævaricatio- ne efficeret. Ita ergo gaudium hoc & vere magnum, & prorsus Catholicum est, quod omni populo para- vit. Quod ut ceu indubitatum fide susciperetur plena, signum addidit præco Seraphicus: Invenie- tis infantem pannis involutum & positum in præsepi. De quo signo dulcissime Augustus Augustinus: Oc- cultatur in membris infantis potentia, Deus pendet ad ubera genetricis: Pannorum vilium squalore con- tegitur, durissimi suffert præsepis angustias, & totum misericors humiliter patitur, dummodo mundus, qui perierat, liberatur. O beata infantia, per quam nostri generis vita est reparata! O gravissimi delectabilesque vagitus, per quos stridores dentium æternosq; ploratus evasimus! O felices panni, quibus peccatorum sordes extersimus! O presepe splendidum, in quo non solum jacuit foenum animalium, sed cibus inventus est An- gelorum. Lacta Maria creatorem tuum, lacta panem coeli, pretium mundi. Postremo tu illi ut mater, tem- poralem ministra substantiam, ut ipse nobis & tibi una cum Patre, & Spritu S. vitam tribuat sempiternam. Nec religiosa tamen admirationis veneratione, ac festiva fidei exultatione meditari oportet Dei in car- ne manifestati mysterium: Sed ut Deo quoque Sal- vatori nostro in carne manifestato cum cordis devo- tione totos nos consecremus, magnum pietatis re- quirit sacramentum. Apparuit enim gratia Dei Sal- vatoris nostri omnibus hominibus, erudiens nos, ut abnegantes impietatem & secularia desideria sobrie & juste & pie vivamus in seculo. Modum devotae sub- jectionis jam olim descripsit Deus, dum de genti- lium conversione ad Christum per Esaiam (c. 45.) vaticinatus est. * Hoc dicit Dominus: Labor Aegypti & negotiatio Æthiopiæ, & Sabain, viri sublimes ad te transibunt, & tui erunt: Post te ambulabunt, vin- cti manicis pergent, & Te adorabunt, Teque depreca- buntur: Tantum in te est Deus, & non est absque te Deus. Vere tu es Deus absconditus, Deus Israël Sal- vator. Loquitur Jehovah ipse Deus Pater ad per- sonam aliam æque divinam, ad quam convertendi sint: Ad TE transibunt, Tui erunt, Post TE am- bulabunt, TE adorabunt, TE precabuntur. Addit confessionem, quam edituri de illo sint, ad quem transituri erant. Te adorabunt, Teprecabuntur, hac sc. confessionis & religiosæ venerationis formula: Tantum in Te (o Messia) est Deus, & non est absque Te Deus. Vere tu es Deus absconditus, Deus Israël Salvator. Quid hac confessione luculentius, quid illustrius esse potest ad celebrandam Christi Salva- toris æternam Deitatem! Quem porro vers. 16. opponit Deus idolis, ceu unum Deum fictitiis nu- minibus, ad quem desertis illis converti debebant gentes, ceu Jehovam Salvatorem solum, extra quem nulla est salus. Israël salvatus est in Domino salute æterna vers. 17. Quem etiam ipsum ita loquentem introducit: Ego Dominus & non est alius. Non in ab- scondito loquutus sum (hæc verba sua quoque fecit, sibique applicavit Christus in diebus carnis suæ Ioh. 18, 20.) Ego Dominus loquens justitiam, anuncians recta (quibus verbis se quoque Christus descripsit, Esa. 63, 1.) Numquid non Ego Dominus, & non est ultra Deus absque me! Deus justus ac salvans non est præter me. Convertimini ad me, & salvi eritis omnes fines terræ, quia ego Deus, & non alius. Mihi curva- bitur omne genu, & jurabit omnis lingua: Ergo in Domino, dicet, mea justitia, & virtus. En characte- res Messiæ, qui Jehovah est justitia nostra Jer. 23, 6. & virtus nostra, qua valemus omnia Phil. 4, 13. in quo solo nobis gloriandum 1. Cor. 1, 31. Cui omnium genua curvanda sunt. Rom. 14, 11. Phil. 2, 10. Quem genuflexionis honorem quoque ad sanctum Jesu Salvatoris nomen Christo exhibet Ecclesia: Unde Hieronymus, Perspicue, inquit, in hoc significatur populus Christianus: moris est enim Ecclesiastici Chri- sto genu flectere. Quod Judæi mentis superbiam osten- dentes omnino non faciunt. Solent enim Judæi stantes orare atque erecti. Deus ergo in quo est Deus, Chri- stus est, ut communi suffragio veteres docent & è textu luculentissime liquet. Quo de Hieronymus: Deus appellatur absconditus propter assumti corporis sacramentum; & Deus Israël Salvator, quod inter- pretatur Jesus. Serviisse autem ei Ægyptum & Æthiopes, & Sabaim excelsos viros, atque sublimes ne- mo dubitat, cum ei mundum videat esse subjectum, & ex paucarum nomine nationum, quæ habitant in ex- tremis finibus terræ cunctos cælorum cardines & omnia terra littora ei creditura perspiciat. Unde pul- chre quasi laborantibus in errore idololatrie cessare labor Ægypti nominatur. Nulla enim gens ita idelola- triæ dedita fuit, & tam innumerabilia portenta ve- nerata est, quam Ægyptus. Hoc ergo oraculo con- vicit S. Athanasius Arianos Oratione III. & Episto- la ad Serap. convicit Marcellinum l. de assumtione hominis, convicit & Macedonium Dialogo III. Aut demens factus negabis Patrem esse Deum, aut confi- tens, Patrem esse Deum, itidemque Filium esse Deum, & cum audias dicentem : Ego sum Deus, & præter me non est alius, unicam Deitatem fateberis, & non pe- riclitaberis. Ideo recitato hoc oraculo ceu longe evidentissimo exclamat Ambrosius l. 1. de Fid. c. 2. Quomodo hoc secundum Arianos convenit ? Excla- mat Hilarius l. 4. de Trinit. Estne adhuc aliquis te- meritati locus, aut ulla relicta est ignorationis occa- sio : nisi id tantum reliquum sit ut impietas professa se prodat ? Nec minus præclare Noëtum hinc refel- lit Epiphanius hæres. 57. At cum dicit, in Te Deus est, quanto cum mysterio, quamque admirabiliter omnia Scriptura S. proponit. Etenim in carne velut in templo quodam prævidebatur atque hominum spei per conversionem ad Deum ostendebatur divinitas : Siquidem Dei Filius ac Deus ipse verbum quasi in sancta quadam urbe religiosoque templo in assumta natura habitat. Optime denique Nestorium (cum hodiernis Nestorianis ) confudit Cyrillus Alexandr. libr. 1. in Joh. c. 15. Deus secundum naturam est in carne, & cum carne. Propriam enim illam sibi fecit, & tamen aliud præter ipsam intelligitur, & in ipsa & cum ipsa, (ut Esaias dicit) adoratur. Viri subli- mes ad te transibunt &c. Ecce Deum inquit esse in ipso; non disseparamus à Deo carnem, id est, homi- nem. Et rursus, non alium Deum, præter ipsum con- firmat, conjungens verbo templum de virgine assum- tum, ut ejus proprium; unus enim ex ambobus Chri- stus est. Similia penes Eusebium l. 5. demonstr. Evang. c. 4. Theodoreturn, autorem commentar. ad Roman. sub nomine Ambrosii c. 2. Procopium, & alios legi possunt. Huic ergo Salvatori nostro ceu uni Deo tota mente confidamus, hunc intrepi- da voce confiteamur, & in carne, ac cum carne as- sumta religiose veneremur. Sequamur Patriar- chas nostros, Magos ex oriente, siquidem in ipsis & muneribus eorum, Hilario docente, labor Ægyti, & mercatus Æthiopum, & Sabaim, error scilicet mundi, Magis adorantibus, ostendatur, & electa gentium munera ab ipsis Domino oblata. Offeramus & nos aurum fidei, thura precum, myrrham mortificatio- nis carnis. Et ut labor Ægypti, hoc est, opes labore partæ Christo nostro servant, munera ad altare Christi Ministris hilari manu deponamus. Sistamus imprimis ei corpora nostra in hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem. Simus toti ejus, qui totum se impendit nobis. Ambulemus post eum, vincti manicis non coactionis, sed gratiæ & dilectionis, cujus vincula, Ambrosio in Psalm. 35. teste, adaman- te sunt fortiora. Vinciamus, & vincamus affectus nostros, carnis desideria, ut legibus ejus devincti omnimoda subjectione nos mancipemus.

## 45:16
Verse 16. THEY SHALL GO INTO CONFUSION, THE MAKERS OF ERRORS) The Chaldean Astrologers.

But this restriction is entirely arbitrary, and furthermore too narrow. For are only the Chaldeans, and among them only the astrologers, the makers of errors, and why these above others? It concerns the errors of the Gentiles, and vain and superstitious cults, which are opposed to the true doctrine of the Church; indeed, the makers of idols are expressed, and the worshippers of strange gods: the word צירים denotes idolaters, and metonymically idols, because they bring sorrows. An opposition is instituted between the Gentiles, adhering to errors and idols, or any impious and infidel persons whatsoever—for they also are architects and worshippers of errors, חרשי צירים, who only beget sorrows, whom He says are to be confounded—and between the faithful, who are saved in Christ with eternal salvation. Therefore, the same thing is expressed as is taught in the Gospel; that those believing in Christ will obtain salvation, and that ignominy and confusion or condemnation await the unbelievers. Therefore, this Prophet testifies to what Peter asserts in Acts 10:43 that all the prophets testify concerning Christ: that all who believe in Him obtain remission of sins in His name: ISRAEL IS SAVED IN THE LORD WITH AN ETERNAL SALVATION. Which Grotius perverts most poorly: 'With the salvation of the ages,' that is, long-lasting: because the words sound of salvation not temporal, but eternal, and it is added for the sake of explanation that they should not be confounded, עד עולמי עד, 'unto the ages of the age,' which can in no way be restricted to a long time, but imply eternal perpetuity or simple eternity, nor is this phrase taken otherwise anywhere else. And therefore it is manifest that the Prophet promises Israel eternal salvation in the Lord, and liberation from the eternal confusion and ignominy which is that of the infidels (Is. 66:14, Dan. 12:2, John 5:29). Whence by the Lord, in whom that salvation is promised, and liberation from the eternal confusion of eternal condemnation, no one else is understood than Christ our Savior, outside of whom there is no salvation (Acts 4:12). Therefore, Brentius rightly says: 'You have, therefore, in this confession an epitome of the whole Gospel and of the Apostolic doctrine concerning Christ and His majesty.' For what is said: 'Truly Thou art a hidden God, and the God of Israel the Savior,' this is that which Peter says: 'Let all the house of Israel know most certainly that God has made (or declared) this Jesus, whom you have crucified, both Lord and Christ.' Or that: 'There is no other name under heaven given to men, in which we must be saved.' And what is said: 'They shall be confounded, they shall all blush, etc.,' this is that which is said to the Apostles: 'He who shall have believed (the Gospel) and shall have been baptized, shall be saved. But he who shall not have believed, shall be condemned.'

Latin:

Vers. 16. ABIERVNT IN CONFVSIONEM FA- BRICATORES ERRORVM) Chaldæi Astrologi.

Hæc vero restrictio prorsus arbitraria, adhæc nimis angusta est. Num enim soli Chaldæi, & in his soli Astrologi fabricatores errorum, & cur hi præ aliis? De gentilium erroribus, & cultibus vanis ac superstitiosis agitur, qui opponuntur veræ doctri- næ Ecclesiæ, imo idolorum fabricatores exprimun- tur, & cultores alienorum Deorum: vox צירים idololatras, & metonymice idola notat, quod af- ferant dolores. Oppositio instituitur inter gen- tiles, erroribus & idolis adhærentes, vel impios & in- fideles quoscunque, illi enim etiam sunt architecti & cultores errorum חרשי צירים, qui dolores solum pa- riunt, quos confundendos dicit; & inter fideles, qui salvantur in Christo, salute æterna. Idem ergo ex- primitur, quod in Evangelio docetur; credentes in Christum salutem consequuturos, incredulos ignomi- niam & confusionem vel condemnationem manere. Testatur itaque hic Propheta, quod omnes Pro- phetas de Christo testari Petrus asserit Actor. 10, 43. quod in nomine ipsius remissionem peccatorum con- sequantur omnes, qui credunt in ipsum: ISRAEL SALVATUS EST IN DOMINO SALUTE ÆTERNA. Quæ pessime pervertit Grotius: Salute sæculorum, id est, longe duratura: quia de salute non temporali, sed æterna sonant verba, & additur ἐξη- γήσεως causa, quod non confundi debeant עד עולמי עד usque in secula seculi, quæ nullatenus restrin- gi possunt ad tempus diuturnum, sed perpetuitatem æternam, vel simplicem æternitatem inferunt, nec us- piam alias phrasis hæc secus accipitur. Ideoq; ma- nifestum est Prophetam in Domino salutem polli- ceri Israeli æternam, & liberationem ab æterna con- fusione & ignominia, quæ est infidelium Es. 66, 14. Dan. 12, 2. Joh. 5, 29. Unde per Dominum, in quo salus illa promittitur, ac liberatio ab æterna confusio- ne æternæ condemnationis, nullus alius intelligi- tur, quam Christus Salvator noster, extra quem non est Salus Act. 4, 12. Recte itaque Brentius: Habes igitur in hac confessione epitomen totius Evangelii, & Apostolicæ doctrinæ de Christo & majestate ejus. Nam quod dicitur: Vere tu es Deus absconditus, & Deus Israelis Salvator, hoc illud est, quod Petrus ait: Certo sciat tota domus Israel, quod Domi- num & Christum fecerit (seu declaraverit) Deus hunc Jesum quem vos crucifixistis. Aut illud: Non est aliud nomen sub cælo datum hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri. Et quod dicitur: Confundentur, erubescent omnes &c. hoc illud est, quod ad Apostolos dicitur: Qui crediderit (Evan- gelio) & baptisatus fuerit, salvus erit. Qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur,

## 45:17
Verse 17. WITH ETERNAL SALVATION) In the Hebrew: with the salvation of the ages: that is, long-lasting.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SALUTE ÆTENRA) In Hebræo: salute sæculorum: id est, in longum duratura.

## 45:18
HE DID NOT CREATE IT IN VAIN) That land of Judea. He wills it to be inhabited and cultivated again. The Hebrews wish to infer from this that even after the resurrection the land will not be empty.

Latin:

NON IN VANUM CREAVIT EAM) Istam terram Judæam. Vult eam rursus habitari & coli. Hebræi hinc inferre volunt etiam post resurrectionem terram non fore inanem.

## 45:19
Ver. 19. I HAVE NOT SPOKEN IN SECRET, IN A DARK PLACE OF THE EARTH) He distinguishes Himself from the gods of the nations by three marks. The gods of the nations were heard from caves and places suitable for fraud. See the Scholiast on that passage of Papinius at the end of the first Thebaid: - - Or in the cave of Perseus beneath the rocks.

I HAVE NOT SAID TO THE SEED OF JACOB, IN VAIN) That salvation is promised, and deliverance from eternal confusion. The gods of the nations are unable to save their worshippers when they are standing, or to raise them up when they are prostrate.

Ver. 19. I THE LORD SPEAKING RIGHTEOUSNESS, DECLARING RIGHT THINGS.) According to the custom received among the Babylonians, all women prostituted their bodies, and that in honor of Venus, whom they called Mylitta. See Herodotus, Clio. The law of God is the guardian of chastity.

That the gods of the Gentiles are being compared, and that the idols of the Babylonians in particular are being set up in these words, rests on no foundation. And who ever carved out such an ἀντίθεσιν, or received it in a dream, between the Lord speaking righteousness, declaring right things, and the Babylonians exposing the bodies of women in honor of Venus? There is no doubt that everything alien to the rule of right, the divine law, is deservedly opposed to right things, but from where will it be taught that the Babylonians in particular, and this filthiness of theirs, are being referred to? Nor does it appear that an antithesis is being established in these words, which simply present Christ speaking righteousness.

Latin:

Vers. 19. NON IN ABSCONDITO LOCUTUS SUM, IN LOCO TERRÆ TENEBROSO) Tribus notis se à diis gentium discernit. Dii gentium audiebantur ex antris & locis ad fraudem idoneis. Vide Scholiasten ad illud Papinii fine primi Thebaidos: - - Seu Persei sub rupibus antri.

NON DIXI SEMINI JACOB, FRUSTRA QUÆ- falus illa promittitur, ac liberatio ab æterna confusio- RITE ME) Dii gentium cultores suos stantes servare, vel prostratos erigere non valent.

Vers. 19. EGO DOMINUS LOQUENS JUSTI- TIAM, ANNUNCIANS RECTA.) Apud Babylonios re- cepto ritu omnes fœminæ corpus vulgabant, idque in hono- rem Veneris, quam Mylittam vocabant. Vid. Herodotum Clio. Dei lex, custos castitatis.

Conferri Deos gentilium, & Babyloniorum qui- dem idola peculiariter componi his verbis, nul- lo nititur fundamento. Et quis exsculpsit unquam talem ἀντίθεσιν, aut per somnium accepit, inter Do- minum loquentem justitiam, annunciantem recta, & Babylonios fæminarum corpora in honorem Veneris exponentes. Rectis opponi merito omnia, à recti regula, lege divina, aliena, nullum est dubium, sed Babylonios in specie, & hanc illorum spurcitiem re- spici unde docebitur? Neque apparet, in his verbis institui antithesin, quæ Christum justitiam loquen- tem simpliciter exhibent.

## 45:20
Ver. 20. YOU WHO ARE SAVED FROM THE NATIONS) In Greek, οἱ σωζόμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν, that is, you who will be survivors from those disasters which Cyrus will inflict.

It is assumed without proof that the discourse is about the Babylonians effect. Nor do the survivors from the disasters bring in the Hebrew, which others have rendered more correctly: LIBERATORS OF THE GENTILES. B. Luther. The heroes of the heathens. Oecolampadius, Leaders of the gentiles. And thus R. David Kimchi rendered it with the active meaning פליטי Leaders, because they were considered as Leaders. He challenges all, as many as were authors and Leaders to the gentiles for idolatry, to be present and to pronounce concerning their gods which they carry, and yet stupidly worship. Cyril thinks they are summoned so that they may depart from error: Assemble yourselves, that is, be bound together by one faith and consensus of minds. Assemble yourselves to God, the ruler of all, through sanctification and justice. Come near, you who are still far off, removed from this cord and lot because of sin. Take counsel therefore, that is, be wise, you who are saved from the gentiles. Now, as if they were full of foolishness, he commands them to return to a wise mind, and to an admirable and blameless understanding, by which it may be permitted to perceive both the power and the majesty of God, the ruler of all.

THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN WHO LIFT UP THE WOOD OF THEIR CARVING) They know nothing of those things which I have mentioned, those who erect statues which they have caused to be carved.

AND THEY PRAY TO A GOD NOT SAVING) Of no strength.

Latin:

Vers. 20. QVI SALVATI ESTIS EX GENTIBVS) Græcis, οἱ σωζόμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν, id est, qui superstites eritis ex illis cladibus, quas Cyrus inferet.

Gratis assumitur, de Babyloniis sermonem- effe. Neque superstites ex cladibus inferuntEbræa, quæ rectius alii reddidere : LIBERATORES GENTIUM. B. Luther. Die Helden der Heyden. Oecolampadius, Duces gentium. Atque ita reddidit R. David Kimchi significatione activa פליטי Duces, quod illi haberentur pro Ducibus. Provocat omnes, quotquot gentilibus auctores ac Duces erant ad idololatriam, ut adsint & pronuncient de diis suis quos portant, & stupidi nihilominus ado- rant. Cyrillus advocari censet, ut ab errore recedant: Congregamini, id est, una fide. & animorum consensio- ne colligamini. Congregamini Deo omnium dominatori, per sanctificationem & justitiam. Venite prope, qui longe adhuc estis, ab hoc funiculo ac forte remoti pro- pter peccatum. Consulite igitur, id est, sapite, qui ex gentibus servamini.
