Nunc velut insipientiæ plenos ad mentem sapientem jubet eos redire, & admirabi- lem inculpatamque intelligentiam, qua perspicere omnium dominatoris Dei & potentiam, & majesta- tem liceat.

NESCIERUNT QVI LEVANT LIGNUM SCULPTURÆ SUÆ) Earum quas dixi rerum nihil no- runt illi, qui erigunt statuas, quas sculpi fecere.

ET ROGANT DEUM NON SALVANTEM) Nullarum virium.

## 45:21
WHO HATH MADE THIS HEARD FROM THE BEGINNING, FROM THEN HATH FORETOLD IT) He speaks again as if in those times, with Cyrus as victor and restoring the Jews. Who is there among all the fictitious gods who has foretold these things long ago with all their circumstances, as I have done?

Indeed, these things are too general to be restricted to the times of Cyrus. Nor is it necessary that we understand these things as said only about those times and that liberation: and therefore Osiander rendered it generally thus: Who ever, so long a time, indeed some centuries before they happened, foretold the greatest things and those most useful to be known: Have I not, the Lord, done this through my Patriarchs and Prophets?

Latin:

QVIS AUDITUM FECIT HOC AB INITIO, EX TUNC PRÆDIXIT ILLUD) Loquitur rursum quasi illis temporibus, Cyro victore & Judæos restituente. Quis est ex omnibus fictitiis diis, qui hæc olim prædixerit cum omnibus suis circumstantiis, ut ego feci?

Imo generaliora hæc sunt, quam ut restringi ea ad Cyrio tempora oporteat. Neque necessum est, ut de illis temporibus & liberatione ista tantum di- cta hæc intelligamus: Ideoque γενικῶς Osiander ita reddidit: Quis unquam tam longo tempore, imo aliquot seculis antequam fierent, prædixit res maxi- mas & scitu utilissimas: Nunquid non ego Dominus hoc feci per Patriarchas & Prophetas meos?

## 45:22
Ver. 22. TURN TO ME) Having renounced idols: which it is entirely credible that many did in those times: but that this was nothing compared to that change which Christ brought about.

AND YOU SHALL BE SAVED ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH) The Greeks explain this well: those from the ends of the earth.

Latin:

Vers. 22. CONVERTIMINI AD ME) Abdicatis ido- lis: quod multos illis temporibus fecisse omnino credibile est: sed ut id nihil esset ad eam mutationem, quam Christus effecit.

ET SALVI ERITIS OMNES FINES TERRÆ) Bene explicant Græci: οἱ ἀπ’ ἐσχάτε τῆς γῆς.

## 45:23
Ver. 23. A WORD OF JUSTICE SHALL GO FORTH FROM MY MOUTH) That is, a most true statement.

AND IT SHALL NOT RETURN) It shall not be void; like messengers who return with their business unaccomplished.

Latin:

Vers. 23. EGREDIETUR DE ORE MEO JUSTI- TIÆ VERBUM) Id est, dictum verissimum.

ET NON REVERTETUR) Non erit irritum; ut legati qui revertuntur re infecta.

## 45:24
Ver. 24. BECAUSE TO ME EVERY KNEE SHALL BEND, AND EVERY TONGUE SHALL SWEAR) That 'every' and 'all' here is not to be taken without exception is shown by what follows, that it will come to pass that those who oppose themselves to God will be put to shame. Therefore it is to be understood that out of many nations there will be some who come to call upon the true God in the circuit of the temple, as Solomon had predicted 1 Kings 8:41. Furthermore, many will also worship the true God at home, as Naaman had done. Worship, however, which is a generic name, is explained popularly by an oath, that is, its species.

These words are of the Son of God. Which Grotius perverts most badly. He saw that Christ was underlying these, and those things which he was about to effect: And he professed that his gloss in comparison to the explanation concerning Christ was nothing, indeed that what he brought forward concerning the time of the Babylonian redemption was nothing, in respect to that which is hinted to be about to be effected by Christ. And yet he did not abandon his gloss, but for its sake he even twisted clear words into a foreign sense. Wherefore, in order to refute the same, we observe that the statement is general, pertaining to all men of all times: Turn to me, and you shall be saved, all the ends of the earth. That, therefore, is indicated, that through conversion to the Lord, salvation is obtained by all, whoever are saved. Who, therefore, could doubt that the Savior is understood to be Christ, through whom alone salvation is obtained by all, Acts 4:12. So that those at last, who turn to him, and believe in him, may be saved, John 3:16, Mark 16:16. (2) In the Hebrew it is, look unto me. Whereby it is required that we look unto the Lord through faith, and behold him with the eyes of faith, who is established as the cause of salvation for the gaze of faith, John 3:15. And therefore the discourse is not only about conversion from idols, even if this also is included in the respect of idolaters, because those who serve idols do not look unto Christ by faith, unless they have left these and are converted to him, Gal. 4:8. Concerning which Brentius rightly says: He teaches how, by what means, and in what manner men obtain the salvation of Christ. For they do not obtain it by turning their face away from Christ, but by looking unto him. Look, he says, unto me. That you may enjoy my salvation, you must not look unto idols, unto the gods of the nations. Nor must you look unto ἐθελοθρησκείαν, unto worship invented by human reason. Nor must you look unto any merits of any human works, but you must look unto me, Jesus Christ the Son of God. How, therefore, is one to look unto Christ? One looks unto him by faith alone. For there is no other virtue, there is no other instrument by which Christ is apprehended and received, except faith. (3) He who institutes the discourse here has testified that he is the only Savior, outside of whom there is no salvation, v. 21. There is no just and saving God מושיע besides me. There is no God besides me who truly justifies and saves his worshippers, and therefore I exhort you all nations, all the ends of the earth, that you look unto me. For by this way alone can you obtain true righteousness and salvation. For I alone am the true God, nor is there another besides me. Which John thus sets forth concerning Christ in 1 Epist. 5, v. 20: This is the true God and eternal life. St. Peter so appropriates this to Christ that he pronounces that OUTSIDE of him there is no salvation in any other, Acts 4:12. Which is the same as this protestation, besides me there is no other Savior. Which is the reason that Christ is called by this name JESUS, because he is the only Savior of the human race, who, as the Angel interprets in Matt. 1, v. 21, saves us from our sins. (4) Concerning this Lord the Prophet had professed a little before, v. 17: Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation, which the words themselves αὐτολεξεὶ teach is to be understood not of temporal salvation, but of eternal. But who is that Lord in whom the faithful are saved with an eternal salvation, and to whom they ought to look with true faith so that they may obtain eternal salvation, if not Christ our only Savior? (5) That he is therefore called just is not to be understood only of the fact that he himself is just in himself, because the question here is about the manner by which men obtain righteousness and salvation, but that he reputes and justifies as just those who believe in him, and imparts true righteousness to us. For he himself is Jehovah our righteousness, Jer. 23, v. 6; ch. 33, v. 16. For he is of such goodness and clemency that the righteousness which he himself has before God his Father, he gives and imputes to all who believe in him. Therefore he is called blessed to whom God imputes righteousness without works, Rom. 4:5. And this is what the faithful then profess, that in the Lord they have righteousness. (6) By the same reason, therefore, the name of SAVIOR is to be understood. For such a Savior is not indicated who sits idle in the heavens, a spectator of human merits, such as are the judges of the games who distribute prizes for merits, but one who saves those who believe in him and look unto him by faith, not for any merits, but by gratuitous clemency, Eph. 2; Tit. 3. (7) What the Lord says here, I have not spoken in secret, Christ transfers to himself in John 18:20, and thus he testifies not obscurely that he is that Lord of whom the Prophet spoke. The title and periphrasis of this Lord also confirms it: I the Lord speaking righteousness and announcing things that are right, because Christ is thus described in Isa. 63:1, I who speak righteousness. Compare Rev. 19:13. (8) Not only those who are in the ends of the earth, but

ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH, and the hinges of the world, that is, all men throughout the whole world, are invited to this grace and salvation. The words are most clear, ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH, which are rashly corrupted by Grotius, as if only those who dwell at the extremity of the earth, and certain special nations, were understood. The salvation of CHRIST is offered to all, because it was procured for all through Christ, without distinction or any respect of persons, as the Apostle says in Rom. 10. There is no distinction either of Jew or Greek. For the same Lord of all is rich unto all that call upon him. Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Therefore the sound of the Gospel has gone out into all the earth, that all might be converted to Christ. It is manifest, therefore, that these things look to the calling of the Gentiles, and the universal proclamation of the Gospel. And that those who restrict these things may be utterly constrained, from verse 13, we conclude thus: All those from the ends of the earth are commanded to look to God, who ought to bow their knees to the Lord. But not only some from the ends of the earth, but all men whatsoever are bound to bow their knees to Christ, inasmuch as all are one day to be set before his tribunal: and therefore all men whatsoever are commanded to look to the Lord. Furthermore, whose salvation the Lord wills, them he wills to be converted to himself, or to look to him, that they may be saved. But the Lord wills the salvation of all, 1 Tim. 2, 2 Pet. 3. Nor do the Greeks say otherwise. Cyril, on these words, Be converted to me, and be saved from the end of the earth, has this: From which words it is very well permitted to perceive the greatness of the grace through Christ, pervading all who are on the earth. For salvation and grace had been contracted through Moses to the one nation of Israel: but grace through Christ has been extended as it were, and runs out even to the ends of the earth. For the whole earth has been captured and ensnared through faith in him, unto salvation and life. (9) The distortion is to be detested, when Grotius restricts what is said universally about the bowing of all knees, and the proclamation of all tongues, to a few individuals who are about to worship God in the circuit of the temple, or to worship the same at home from among the Gentiles; these words teach what the law is, namely that all knees ought to be bowed to the Lord, and the tongues of all confess, if they wish to obtain salvation, and do not explain what is to happen to the Jews returning from Babylon. And what more certain Interpreter shall we have than the Holy Spirit, who, teaching in Phil. 2 that all knees must be bowed to Christ the Lord, looks to this Prophetic oracle, and furthermore in Rom. 14 expressly explains it concerning Christ, that to him in the day of universal judgment all knees are to be bowed. For when the Prophet demands that the knees of all men be bowed to the Lord in true obedience of faith, and that all tongues profess him the Lord, which is done by the faithful and the elect, who obtain salvation in the Lord, even if it is not done by the unbelievers, who reject or deny the Lord, the Apostle teaches that all will one day acknowledge that Christ to be the Lord, to whom they ought to have bowed their knees, nay, that all even the unbelievers will bow their knees to him on the last day, as the judge of all flesh. We shall all, he says, Rom. 14:10, stand before the tribunal of Christ. For it is written, As I live, says the Lord, because to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall confess to God. He therefore, to whom every knee ought to be bowed, is Christ, by the interpretation of the Holy Spirit, and every knee is to be taken not restrictively, but absolutely universally, because the knee of those who are to be set before the tribunal of Christ must be bowed. But we are all to be set before the tribunal of Christ, all men in the universe, without exception. (10) What of the fact that the Prophet himself indicates that the discourse is about all, whether those who are justified, or those who are put to shame eternally, and are condemned. For of them he says that they shall profess, In the Lord are my righteousness and strength, or dominion. And, in the Lord, he says, shall all the seed of Israel be justified and shall glory, which is to be understood of the Israel of God, and according to the Spirit, that is, of the faithful. But of these, he says, all who oppose him shall be confounded. Which will be fully fulfilled on the last day, when the faithful will receive eternal salvation, and the unfaithful eternal confusion. (11) Therefore the word of righteousness, which goes out from the mouth of the Lord, and does not return, that is, is inviolable, and can never be retracted, which God confirms by an oath, not only because it is holy and just, or because it is firm and immovable: For this unretractable constancy is indicated by these words, AND SHALL NOT RETURN; but because it is the norm of the righteous judgment of God, which will be exercised over all men, in the day of universal judgment, and which is already being exercised, because he who does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God, John 3:7, or because this word concerns the righteousness which has been revealed in the Gospel, according to which judgment will be made, as the Apostle testifies in Rom. 2, because those who have received this righteousness by true faith will obtain salvation, those who have rejected the same will be eternally put to shame, and will be condemned, John 6:16. B. Luther says, The word of righteousness is the Gospel, which brings righteousness and the remission of sins. (12) That it is said that EVERY knee is to be bowed is to be understood of the genuflection of adoration, which is owed to Christ the Savior by all, therefore all are commanded to serve him, all to kiss him, Ps. 2. Those who refuse to exhibit this honor to him through faith, and persist in infidelity, they will nevertheless be compelled against their will to bow their knees to him as judge, when they are set before his tribunal, where THEY SHALL COME TO HIM even those who will be confounded, that is, all who now oppose him in this age. Therefore Sanctius thus paraphrases v. 23 and following: But if anyone should be unwilling to perform the due office of religion to me, willingly and gladly, I will cause that even against his will he shall perform it at some time. For I have sworn this by myself, and there shall not be wanting success and faith to the righteous word which I have spoken. I have sworn, I say, that all before me, in whatever place and order they may be, shall bend the knee, and by an oath conceived in the invocation of my name shall acknowledge me as God; therefore every tongue shall swear by the Lord, and shall say that in me is righteousness and power. Even those who shall turn away from that duty owed to God: who, from the sight of God which they shall unwillingly undergo, shall be put to shame and given over to eternal confusion. But indeed it will happen far otherwise to those who can truly and deservedly be called Israelites: for by God the judge, at the final moment of the ages, they shall be declared righteous, and praised by him, they shall receive the reward of things honestly done. (13) Since both that is required of us, both that we believe with the heart, and that we confess with the mouth, because with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession of faith is made unto salvation, and the object of saving faith and confession is Christ, and his righteousness or obedience, active and passive, because if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him (delivered for your sins) from death (for your righteousness) you shall be saved, Roman. 10. v. 9. Therefore Christ claims both for himself here, as not only genuflection, which includes the honor of adoration and trustful veneration, because by the external bending of the knees the internal is signified, (although here not so much the external is designated, as the spiritual and internal, by which the knees of the heart are bent, Ephes. 3, 14.) but also the confession, which is made by tongue and mouth; AND EVERY TONGUE SHALL SWEAR, to me namely, because from the former [verse] it must be repeated (every knee shall bow to me) as is clear from the very formula of confession, IN THE LORD, they shall say, are my righteousnesses. As the Lord had confirmed the word of truth and righteousness by an oath, so all are bound to bind themselves to the Lord by the sacrament of an oath, and as it were to confirm by oath the faith and certainty of that righteousness which they have in the Lord. Therefore the Apostle here used the word of confession, EVERY TONGUE SHALL CONFESS, Rom. 14, so that he might express the act of confession, but a holy one, and as it were an oath-taking one. Others wish that the Prophet used the word of swearing by a Hebraism for preaching, because they used to confirm the preaching of the word with oaths. (14) The symbol of confession, which all who are to be saved are bound to utter, is this: in the Lord (Christ the Savior. For the discourse is about Him) are my righteousnesses and strength, which symbol is also prescribed in Jer. 23:6, namely that the faithful are to call Christ, Jehovah our righteousness. In the Lord is this righteousness, because those who believe in Him are righteous, Rom. 10:4, nor is there any righteousness outside of Him. By His obedience are they constituted righteous, whoever are justified, Rom. 5:19. Therefore the plural is used, צְדָקוֹת, because the faithful acknowledge that whatever righteousness they have, they have it in the Lord, and that through faith they so appropriate to themselves the righteousness and obedience of Christ, both active and passive, that these righteousnesses of the Lord are the faithful's own, and each one can testify, through faith, that in God the Savior there are righteousnesses for him, i.e., He Himself fulfilled all the righteousness of the law for me, and by His passive obedience made satisfaction for all my sins, so that thus there is in Him for me a most perfect righteousness, which perfection is indicated by the plural noun of righteousness. Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth, Rom. 10:4. (15) It is added in this symbol of confession, that in the Lord we have עֹז strength, because He Himself is our might, and through Him, apprehended by faith, we alone overcome our enemies. Blessed is that man, whose strength is in Thee, says the sacred psalmist, Ps. 84:3. He has been made to us by God not only righteousness, but also sanctification, and redemption, so that he who glories, ought to glory in this Lord, 1 Cor. 1:10. For the Hebrew עֹז and מָעֹז the Greeks sometimes use the word ὑπερασπιστής, Ps. 27:1, Ps. 37:39. The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, who is also their strength, the ὑπερασπιστής. By which name Christ is excellently expressed in His redemptive office, viewed in His satisfaction and merit, whereby He, as our Goel, has vindicated us from the power of the Devil and asserted us for His kingdom. (16) Everyone is said to be coming to this LORD, because all shall be set before His tribunal, even those who did not acknowledge Him, not only those who received Him by true faith and professed, in the Lord are my righteousness and strength, which, that it might be done by all, He inculcated to all, look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth, but also those who now resist Him. The word הַנֶּחֱרִים signifies fury against the Lord, and those who are inflamed with anger, and hatred, and with every affection of the mind oppose Him: which cause of condemnation was also designated by Enoch, Jude v. 15, because the ungodly are said to be judged περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ᾽ αὐτοῦ against Him, namely our Lord Christ Jesus, who is said there to be coming to judgment. Others restrict the words TO HIM SHALL COME to the faithful, whose confession preceded, so that they may exhibit an antithesis to the rest concerning those who resist Him, i.e., those who are such, shall come to Him. Moreover, by this resistance, unbelief is described from the effect, just as faith is by the oath sworn to Him, because an oath-taking confession is the consequence and testimony of faith, and resistance is of unbelief. (17) The cause therefore of justification and salvation and of condemnation and eternal confusion is here expressed by way of antithesis, when all who resist Christ are said to be confounded, namely with eternal confusion, as is evident from verse 17, but all the seed of Israel, that is, all the faithful, because Jacob through faith became Israel, and obtained that name, Gen. 32, SHALL BE JUSTIFIED IN THE LORD, AND SHALL BE PRAISED or rather shall glory in Him, shall attain righteousness, and salvation, in Him shall he glory, He Himself shall be the everlasting glory of the faithful. (18) Which, since they are altogether clear, the ancients, and most all the recent Interpreters have acknowledged, are to be understood of Christ. Cyril refers them to the conversion of the Gentiles. To bow the knee, he says on page 623, to God, and His name will be used by all in an oath; what else does it signify, than the conversion of all and the acknowledgment, and the manifestation of conjunction with Him? For those who return to God through conversion, by no means bow the knee to unclean spirits, nor do they carry them about with their tongue as gods. For they will not swear by any one, as if by God: but knowing Him to be one by nature and truly, they submit their neck to His yoke, and bow the knee, and if they wish to swear lawfully, they make mention of Him alone. And he explains these things concerning the invocation of Christ on page 614. For every knee bows to Christ the Savior of all, and every tongue confesses, and all prayer ends in Him. For in Christ we ask for requests from God and the Father, and in Him we pray, confessing also that in Him is God, and besides Him there is no God. Jerome: He swears, he says, that idols being abandoned every knee is bowed to Him, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth, and every tongue of mortals swears by Him: In which the Christian people is clearly signified. It is also an Ecclesiastical custom to bow the knee to Christ. Which the Jews, demonstrating the pride of their mind, do not do at all. But also every language of all barbarian nations confesses God, not in synagogues, but in the Churches of Christ. And afterwards: These however, who have sprung from the stock of the children of Israel, and who have sprouted from the seed of the Apostles and have believed in Christ, shall have justice and everlasting glory. Nor does Calvin refuse this interpretation: The knee is bent to Christ, while his doctrine is obeyed, and the preaching of the Gospel is admitted, but many still resist, and securely despise him. Satan attempts many things, and assiduously wages war with him. We are therefore far from the fulfillment of this Prophecy. Then therefore every knee shall truly be bent to Christ, when, with his enemies conquered and utterly destroyed, he shall triumph, and shall render his majesty conspicuous to all, which is now attacked by Satan and the impious. Therefore Paul teaches that, while Christ shall ascend the tribunal to judge the world, that which began to happen from the beginning of the Gospel, and which we see happening daily even now, will be completed. Add that the sounder Rabbis themselves are [better] than Grotius, and in this chapter acknowledge the Messiah. For when in v. 17 it is said, Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation; the Targum explains it thus: Israel shall be saved in the Word of the Lord with an everlasting salvation; by which Word of the Lord he understands the Messiah. The Gloss of R. Solomon on Dan. 8, 14 explains it concerning the Messiah in these words: And the sin of Israel shall be remitted, and they shall be redeemed or saved with an everlasting salvation, or eternal, through King Messiah, as it is said in Isa. 45, 17. Thus also verse 22 is explained concerning the Messiah: Look unto me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; and verse 25: Because to me every knee shall bend. For it is too manifest that these things treat of the Messiah.

Latin:

Vers. 24. QVIA MIHI CURVABITUR OMNE GE- NU, ET JURABIT OMNIS LINGVA) Illud omne & omnis hic non sine exceptione sumendum ostendit, quod sequitur, futurum ut pudesiant, qui Deo se opponunt. Er- go intelligendum, de plurimis gentibus futuros aliquos, qui veniant invocatum Deum verum in ambitu templi, ut Sa- lomo prædixerat 1. Reg. 8, 41. Præterea multos etiam domi Deum verum culturos, ut Neheman fecerat. Cultus au- tem, quod est nomen generis, per juramentum, id est, spe- ciem suam explicatur populariter.

Hæc verba Filii Dei sunt. Quæ pessime per- vertit Grotius. Vidit Christum his subesse, & ea quæ effecturus erat: Et glossam suam in συγκρίσει ad ex- plicationem de Christo nihil esse, imo nihil esse id quod de tempore Babylonicæ redemptionis attulit, respectu ejus, quod à Christo effectum iri innuitur, professus est. Nec tamen glossam suam deseruit, sed ejus causa etiam verba luculenta in alienum sensum detorsit. Quapropter ad eandem refellen- dam observamus, generale esse dictum, ad omnes omnium temporum homines pertinens: Converti- mini ad me, & salvi eritis omnes fines terræ. Id ergo indicatur, per conversionem adDominum salutem obtingere omnibus, quicunque salvantur. Quis ergo ambigat Salvatorem intelligi Christum, per quem solum omnibus obtingit salus, Actor. 4, 12. Ita ut illi demum, qui ad ipsum convertuntur, & in eum credunt, salventur, Joh. 3, 16. Marc. 16. v. 16. (2) In Ebræo est, respicite ad me. Quo requiritur, ut per fidem respiciamus Dominum, oculisque fidei eum intueamur, qui fidei intuitus causa salutis con- stituitur Joh. 3, 15. Ideoque non tantum de conver- sione ab idolis sermo est, etsi hæc quoque respectu idololatrarum comprehendatur, quia fide non re- spiciunt Christum, qui idolis serviunt, nisi qui his relictis ad eum convertuntur Gal. 4, 8. de quo re- cte Brentius: Docet, quomodo, quo medio, qua ra- tione homines consequantur salutem Christi. Non enim consequuntur eam aversione vultus à Christo, sed respiciendo ad ipsum. Respicite, inquit, ad me. Ut fruaris mea salute, non est respiciendum ad idola, ad deos gentium. Nec est respiciendum ad ἐθελοθρη- σκείαν, ad cultus humana ratione confictos. Nec est respiciendum ad ulla ullorum humanorum operum merita, sed est respiciendum ad me, Jesum Christum Filium Dei. Quomodo ergo respicitur ad Christum? Respicitur ad eum sola fide. Non enim est alia vir- tus, non est aliud organon, quo Christus apprehendi- tur & accipitur, præterquam fides. (3) Qui sermo- nem hic instituit, testatus est, se esse Salvatorem unicum, extra quem non est salus, v. 21. Non est Deus justus & salvans מושיע præter me. Non est Deus præter me, qui cultores suos vere justificet & salvet, ideoque cohortor vos omnes gentes, omnes fines terræ, ut ad me respiciatis. Hac enim sola via justitiam & salutem veram consequi pote- stis. Ego enim solus sum verus Deus, nec præter me est alius. Quod Johannes ita effert de Christo 1. Epist. 5. v. 20. Hic est verus Deus & vita æterna. S. Petrus hoc Christo sic appropriat, ut pronun- ciet, EXTRA ipsum non esse in alio salutem, Act. 4, 12. Quod idem est cum hac protestatione, præ- ter me non est alius Salvator. Quæ causa est, quod Christus ab hoc nomine JESUS nuncupatus sit, quia unicus humani generis Salvator est, qui inter- prete Angelo Matth. 1. v. 21. nos salvat à peccatis nostris. (4) De hoc Domino professus erat paulo ante Propheta v. 17. Israël salvatur in Domino æter- na salute, quod non de salute temporali, sed æter- na intelligendum esse, verba ipsa αὐτολεξεὶ docent. Quis autem Dominus ille est, in quo æterna salute fideles salvantur, & ad quem respicere debent vera fide, ut salutem æternam consequantur, nisi Chri- stus Salvator noster unicus? (5) Quod ergo justus vocatur, non est intelligendum tantum de eo, quod ipse justus in se sit, quia agitur hic de ratione, qua homines justitiam & salutem consequantur, sed qua credentes in ipsum justos reputat & justifi- cat, nobisque justitiam veram impertit. Nam ipse est Jehovah justitia nostra, Jer. 23. v. 6. cap. 33. v. 16. Tantæ enim est bonitatis & clementiæ, ut quam ipse justitiam habet coram Deo Patre suo, eam do- net, atque imputet omnibus credentibus in ipsum. Ideo is beatus dicitur, cui Deus imputat justitiam sine operibus, Rom. 4, 5. Et hoc est, quod profiten- tur deinde fideles, in Domino justitiam sibi esse. (6.) Eadem itaque ratione SALVATORIS nomen in- telligendum. Non enim talis Salvator indigitatur, qui sedeat in cœlis otiosus, spectator humanorum meritorum, quales agonothetæ sunt, qui præmia pro meritis distribuunt, sed qui credentes in ipsum, eumque fide respicientes, ob nulla merita, sed gra- tuita clementia servet Eph. 2. Tit. 3. (7) Quod hic ait Dominus, non in abscondito locutus sum, ad se transfert Christus Joh. 18, 20. adeoque haud obscu- re testatur, se esse illum Dominum, de quo Prophe- ta. Confirmat id quoque titulus, & periphrasis hu- jus Domini: Ego Dominus loquens justitiam & an- nuncians recta, quia sic describitur Christus Esa, 63, 1. Ego qui loquor justitiam. Confer Apoc. 19, 13. (8) Non illi tantum, qui in finibus terræ sunt, sed

OMNES TERRÆ FINES, atque cardines mundi, hoc est, omnes homines per totum orbem, invitantur ad hanc gratiam & salutem. Verba cla- risima sunt, OMNES FINES TERRÆ, quæ temere à Grotio depravantur, ac si tantum illi, qui in extremo terræ habitant, ac speciales quædam nationes intelligantur. Offertur salus CHRISTI omnibus, quia omnibus parta est per Christum, si- ne distinctione aut ulla personarum acceptione, ut Apostolus ait Rom. 10. Non est distinctio vel Judæi vel Græci. Nam idem Dominus omnium, dives in omnes invocantes se. Quisquis invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit. Ideo in omnem terram sonus Evangelii exivit, ut omnes ad Christum converte- rentur. Manifestum itaque est, hæc respicere vo- cationem gentium, & universale præconium Ev- angelii. Et ut prorsus constringantur, qui hæc re- stringunt, è vers. 13. ita concludimus: Illi omnes è finibus terræ omnibus ad Deum respicere juben- tur, qui Domino genua curvare debent. At non tantum nonnulli απ' ἐσχάτων τῆς γῆς, sed omne omni- no homines Christo tenentur curvare genua, ut- pote qui omnes coram ipsius tribunali sistendi olim sunt: ideoque omnes omnino homines respicere jubentur Dominum. Adhæc, quorum salutem vult Dominus, illos ad se converti, seu respicere vult, ut salvifiant. At Dominus vult omnium salu- tem, 1. Tim. 2. 2. Pet. 3. Nec aliter Græci. Cyrillus ad hæc verba, Convertimini ad me, & servamini ab extremo terræ, ita habet: Quibus ex verbis optime perspicere licet gratiæ per Christum magnitudinem, omnes, qui sunt in terra, pervadentem. Contracta enim erat salus & gratia per Mosen, ad unam gentem Israelis means: at gratia per Christum porrecta est velut, & ad terminos usque terræ excurrit. Capta est enim & irretita per fidem in ipsum, ad salutem & vitam, terra universa. (9) Detestanda est ςρεβλό- της, cum quod universaliter dicitur de curvandis omnium genibus, & præconio linguarum omnium, ad paucos nonnullos restringit Grotius, qui in am- bitu templi Deum adoraturi, vel domi eundem culturi sunt è gentibus; Verba hæc docent, quid juris sit, quod curvâri nempe genua omnia Domi- no debeant, & confiteri linguæ omnium, si salu- tem consequi velint, non autem quid redeuntibus Babylone Judæis futurum sit, exponunt. Et quem habebimus certiorem Interpretem, quam S. S. qui Phil. 2. omnium genua Christo Domino flecten- da esse docens, hoc oraculum Propheticum respi- cit, ac præterea Rom. 14. diferte id de Christo ex- plicat, quod ipsi in die pantocritico omnium genua curvanda sint. Nam quum Propheta postulet, ut genua omnium hominum Domino curventur vera fidei obedientia, omnesque lingvæ ipsum Domi- num profiteantur, quod à fidelibus & electis fit, qui in Domino salutem consequuntur, etsi id non fiat ab incredulis, Dominum reprobantibus vel abne- gantibus, docet Apostolus, omnes olim agnituros esse Christum illum Dominum, cui genua flectere debuerint, imo omnes etiam incredulos ipsi in no- vissimo die genua sua curvaturos, ceu judici uni- versæ carnis. Omnes, inquit, Rom. 14, 10. stabimus ante tribunal Christi. Scriptum est enim, vivo ego, dicit Dominus, quoniam mihi flectetur omne genu, & omnis lingva confitebitur Deo. Is ergo, cui omne genu flecti debet, Interprete Spiritu Sancto est Christus, & omne genu non restricte, sed prorsus universaliter accipiendum est, quia illorum genu curvari debet, qui sistendi sunt coram tribunali Christi. At omnes coram tribunali Christi sistendi sumus, omnes in universum homines, sine exce- ptione. (10) Quid, quod Propheta ipse indicet, de omnibus sive qui justificantur, sive qui pudefiunt æternum, atque condemnantur, sermonem esse. Nam de illis dicit, quod professuri sint, in Domino meæ sunt justitiæ, & fortitudo, vel imperium. Et, in Domino, inquit, justificabitur, & laudabitur omne semen Israël, quod de Israële Dei, & secundum Spi- ritum, hoc est, de fidelibus intelligendum. De his autem, confundentur omnes, inquit, qui repugnant ei. Quod implebitur plene in die novissimo, cum fideles æternam salutem, infideles æternam confu- sionem accipient. (11) Ideo verbum justitiæ, quod egreditur ex ore Domini, & non revertitur, hoc est, inviolabile est, nec retractari unquam potest, quod Deus jurejurando confirmat, non tantum ideo, quod sanctum ac justum, vel quod firmum atque immotum sit: Hæc enim constantia irretractabilis verbis istis indicatur, ET NON REVERTE- TUR; sed quod norma sit δικαιοκρισίας, ac justi judicii Dei, quod super omnes homines exercebi- tur, in die pantocritico, quodque jam exercetur, quia qui non credit, jam judicatus est, eo quod non credit in nomen Filii Dei unigeniti, Joh. 3. v. 7. vel quod hoc verbum concernat justitiam, quæ in Ev- angelio patefacta est, secundum quod fiet judi- cium, teste Apostolo Rom. 2. quia qui justitiam hanc vera fide susceperint, salutem consequentur, qui eandem reprobarint, æternum pudefient, & condemnabuntur, Joh. 6, 16. B. Lutherus, Verbum justitiæ, inquit, est Evangelium, quod affert justi- tiam & remissionem peccatorum. (12) Quod OMNE genu curvandum dicitur, de genuflexione adora- tionis intelligendum, quæ Christo Salvatori ab omnibus debetur, ideo omnes ipsi servire, omnes eum osculari jubentur, Psal. 2. Quem honorem qui eidem detrectant exhibere per fidem, atque in in- fidelitate persistunt, illi tamen inviti cogentur ipsi genua flectere ceu judici, cum coram tribunali ejus sistentur, ubi VENIENT AD EUM etiam qui confundentur, hoc est, omnes qui nunc ei repu- gnant in hoc seculo. Ideo ita παραφράζει Sanctius v. 23. & seqq. Quod si quispiam debitum religionis officium præstare mihi nolit, volens & lubens, efficiam ego, ut vel invitus aliquando præstet. Juravi enim hoc per memetipsum, neque à verbo justo, quod loquu- tus sum, aberit successus, & fides. Juravi, inquam, quia omnes ante me, quocunque loco & ordine sint, ge- nua incurvabunt, meque juramento in mei nominis obtestatione concepto Deum agnoscent, per Dominum itaque jurabit omnis lingva, dicetque in me justitiam esse atque imperium. Etiam hi, qui officium illud debi- tum Deo aversabuntur: qui ex Dei conspectu quem inviti subibunt, pudefacti in æternam confusionem dabuntur. At vero multo aliter continget his, qui ve- re & merito vocari possunt Israëlitæ: A judice enim Deo in extremo seculorum articulo, declarabuntur justi, & ab eo laudati rerum honeste gestarum merce- dem accipient. (13) Quum utrumque illud requira- tur à nobis, tum ut corde credamus, tum ut ore con- fiteamur, quia corde creditur ad justitiam, & ore fit confessio fidei ad salutem, & objectum fidei salvifi- cæ & confessionis sit Christus, ac justitia ejus vel obedientia, activa & passiva, quia si confitearis in ore tuo Dominum Jesum, & in corde tuo credideris, quod Deus illum (pro peccatis tuis traditum) su- scitarit à morte (propter justitiam tuam) salvus eris, Roman. 10. v. 9. Ideo utrumque hic sibi vin- dicat Christus, utpote non tantum genuflexionem, quæ honorem adorationis & venerationis fiducia- lis complectitur, quia per externam genuum in- curvationem interna significatur, (quamvis hic non tam externa designetur, quam spiritualis & interna, qua cordis genua flectuntur, Ephes. 3, 14.) sed etiam confessionem, quæ lingua & ore fit; ET JURABIT OMNIS LINGVA, MIHI scilicet quod è priori repetendum (mihi curvabitur omn genu) ut ex ipsa formula confessionis liquet, in DO MINO, dicent, Justitiæ meæ sunt. Ut Dominu juramento firmarat verbum veritatis & justitiæ, it jurisjurandi sacramento Domino sese obstringer tenentur omnes, ac veluti juratorie confirmare fi- dem, ac certitudinem istius justitiæ, quam haben in Domino. Ideo Apostolus verbum confessionis hic adhibuit, CONFITEBITUR OMNIS LIN- GVA, Rom. 14. ut actum confesionis, sed sacrosan- ctum, ac velut juratorium exprimeret. Alii verbo jurandi per Ebraismum Prophetam usum esse, pro prædicare, volunt, quia juramentis prædicationem verbi firmabant. (14) Symbolum confesionis, quod edere tenentur omnes salvandi, hoc est: in Domino (Christo Salvatore. De hoc enim sermo est) meæ sunt justitiæ & fortitudo, quod Symbolum etiam præscribitur Jer. 23, 6. quod nempe vocaturi sint fideles Christum, Jehovab justitia nostra. In Domino hæc justitia est, quia qui credunt in ipsum, justi sunt, Rom. 10, 4. neque extra ipsum ulla est justi- tia. Ipsius obedientia justi constituuntur, quicunque justificantur, Rom. 5, 19. Ideo adhibetur plurale, צְדָקוֹת quod fideles agnoscant, quicquid sibi est justitiæ, in Domino sese habere, seque per fidem justi- tiam & obedientiam Christi, tum activam tum passi- vam sibi ita appropriare, ut hæ justitiæ Domini fide- lium propriæ sint, ac quisq; testari possit, per fidem, in Deo Salvatore sibi esse justitias, q. d. ipse omnem justitiam legis implevit pro me, & obedientia sua pas- siva satis fecit pro omnib. peccatis meis, ut ita mihi in ipso sit justitia perfectissima, quæ perfectio plurali nomine justitiæ indigitatur. Christus est finis legis ad justitiam omni credenti, Rom. 10, 4. (15) Additur in hoc confessionis Symbolo, in Domino nobis esse עֹז fortitudinem, quod ipse robur nostrum sit, & per ipsum fide apprehensum unice vincamus hostes nostros. Beatus ille bomo, cujus robur in te si- tum, ait Hieropsaltes Psal. 84, 3. Ipse factus est no- bis à Deo non tantum justitia, sed etiam sanctifica- tio, & redemptio, adeo ut qui gloriatur, in hoc Do- mino gloriari debeat, 1. Cor. 1, 10. Pro Ebræo עֹז & מָעֹז adhibent Græci quandoq; vocem ὑπερασπι- σὴς Ps. 27, 1. Ps. 37, 39. Salus justorum à Domino est, qui & fortitudo eorum est ὑπερασπισὴς. Quo no- mine Christus in officio redemptorio, satisfactione & merito spectatus, qua nos ceu Goël noster è po- testate Diaboli vindicavit & asseruit regno suo, egregie exprimitur. (16) Ad hunc DOMINUM venturus dicitur quique, quia omnes coram ejus tri- bunali sistentur, etiam illi, qui eum non agnovere, non tantum qui vera fide ipsum suscepere, ac pro- fessi sunt, in Domino mihi justitiæ & fortitudo, quod ut ab omnibus fieret, omnibus inculcavit, respicite ad me, & salvi eritis omnes fines terræ, sed & illi, qui nunc repugnant ei. Verbum הַנֶּחֱרִים significat furorem adversus Dominum, & eos, qui inflammati sunt ira, atque odio, omnique animi affectu ipsi adver- santur: quæ causa condemnationis etiam ab Eno- cho designata fuit, Jud. v. 15. quia judicandi dicun- tur impii περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ᾽ αὐτὂ contra ipsum, Dominum scil. nostrum Chri- stum Jesum, qui ibi venturus dicitur ad judicium. Alii verba AD EUM VENIET restringunt ad fideles, quorum confesio præcessit, ut ἀντίθεσιν exhibeant reliqua de iis, qui ipsi repugnent, q d. qui tales sunt, venient ad eum. Cæterum per hanc repugnantiam infidelitas à posteriori describitur, uti per juramen- tum ei præstitum fides, quia confessio juratoria consequens & testimonium est fidei, repugnantia infidelitatis. (17) Causa ergo justificationis & sa- lutis ac condemnationis & æternæ confusionis hic κατ’ ἀντίθεσιν exprimitur, cum omnes qui repugnant Christo confundendi dicuntur, æterna nempe confu- sione, ut è vers. 17. constat, omne autem semen Israël, hoc est, fideles omnes, quia Jacob per fidem evasit Israël, istudque nominis obtinuit Gen. 32. IN DO- MINO JUSTIFICABUNTUR, & LAUDA- BITUR vel potius gloriabitur in eo, justitiam con- sequetur, ac salutem, in eo gloriabitur, ipse erit gloria fidelium sempiterna. (18) Quæ quum lu- culenta omnino sint, veteres, & plerique omnes recentiores Interpretes agnovere, de Christo hæc intelligenda esse. Cyrillus ea refert ad conversio- nem gentium. Flectere se genu, inquit pag. 623. Deo, & nomen ejus ab omnibus in juramento adhibebi- tur; quid aliud significat, quam omnium conversio- nem & agnitionem, & conjunctionis cum ipso pate- factionem? Qui enim per conversionem ad Deum redeunt, prorsus nec genu immundis spiritibus fle- ctunt, neque lingva illos ut deos circumferunt. Non enim per ullum aliquem jurabunt, tanquam per Deum: sed unum natura & vere esse cognoscentes, ejus jugo cervicem supponunt, & genu flectunt, & si legitime jurare velint, ejus solius mentionem faciunt. Et de invocatione Christi hæc explicat pag. 614. Flectit enim omnium Servatori Christo omne genu, & omnis lingva confitetur, & in ipsum omnis preca- tio desinit. In Christo enim petimus à Deo & Patre postulata, & in ipso oramus, confitentes, etiam in ipso Deum esse, & præter ipsum non esse Deum. Hiero- nymus: Jurat, inquit, quod idolis derelictis omne ge- nu ei flectatur, cælestium, terrestrium, & inferno- rum, & omnis per illum juret lingva mortalium: In quo perspicue significatur populus Christianus. Moris est etiam Ecclesiastici, Christo genu flectere. Quod Judæi mentis superbiam demonstrantes, omnino non faciunt. Sed & omnis lingva cunctarum gentium barbararum, non in synagogis, sed in Christi Ecclesiis confitentur Deum. Et postea: Hi autem, qui de stir- pe filiorum Israël orti sunt, & qui de Apostolorum semine pullulaverunt & crediderunt in Christo, ha- beant justitiam & gloriam sempiternam. Nec ab- nuit huic interpretationi Calvinus: Flectitur genu Christo, dum paretur ejus doctrinæ, atque Evangelii prædicatio admittitur, sed multi adhuc repugnant, & secure ipsum contemnunt. Plurima molitur Sa- tan, & assidue bellum cum ipso gerit. Longe ergo ab- sumus ab hujus Prophetiæ complemento. Tunc ergo vere flectetur Christo omne genu, cum victis & fun- ditus deletis hostibus triumphabit, majestatemque suam omnibus conspicuam reddet, quæ nunc à Sata- na & impiis oppugnatur. Itaque docet Paulus, dum Christus tribunal ad judicandum orbem conscendet, completum iri, quod fieri cœpit ab Evangelii exor- dio, & quotidie adhuc fieri cernimus. Adde, quod Rabbini ipsi saniores Grotio sint, & hic in hoc ca- pite agnoscant Messiam. Nam cum v. 17. dicitur, Israël salvatus erit in Domino salvatione æterna; Targum id ita exponit: Israël salvatus erit in verbo Domini salvatione seculorum; per quod Verbum Domini Messiam intelligit. Glossa R. Salomonis ad Dan. 8, 14. de Messia id explicat his verbis: Et remittetur peccatum Israël, & redimentur vel sal- vabuntur salvatione seculorum, vel æterna per Re- gem Messiam, sicut dictum est Esa. 45, 17. Ita quo- que de Messia exponitur versus 22. Respicite ad me & salvamini omnes fines terræ; & vers. 25. Quia mihi flectetur omne genu. Nimis enim manifestum est, hæc de Messia agere.

## 45:24
Vers. eod. HE SHALL SAY, MINE ARE JUSTICES AND POWER: TO HIM THEY SHALL COME, AND ALL SHALL BE ASHAMED, WHO RESIST HIM) Here the reading which the LXX followed is better, namely לו for לי, so that that עדיי is as it were a repetition of that לו, a manner of speaking not infrequent among the Hebrews. The sense is: each one of them from the nations will say, when he sees those things which we have now said, that God is both most truthful and most powerful, and that they deservedly ought to be ashamed who oppose themselves to him.

Lest he omit nothing to deprave the oracle, he feigns a corruption of the authentic text, and prefers the Greek version to it: as if it had been written formerly לו THEY have justice & power: that is, God is most truthful and most powerful, because the Gentiles are to know this from the Babylonian liberation. But who will admit that bold and rash assertion about a corrupted source? It is not about the Lord's truth or power absolutely, but how the Lord is justice and strength to the faithful, who are thus to glory in the Lord, and to confess him. Which the last verse clearly confirms: IN THE LORD SHALL BE JUSTIFIED, AND SHALL GLORY ALL THE SEED OF ISRAEL. How therefore shall he be justified in the Lord, unless it be that in the Lord is justice itself? How does he glory in the Lord, unless it be that he thus confesses the Lord, in the Lord is justice and strength to me? But Grotius has even dared to deprave this verse, although it is most clear, and he understands the word of justifying not of justice before God, of which by the force of the antecedents, and verse 17, it must necessarily be understood, and by itself it sounds most clearly, but of justice before men.

V. 26. IN THE LORD SHALL BE JUSTIFIED AND PRAISED ALL THE SEED OF ISRAEL) That is, on account of the worship of the one God, the Israelitic people shall obtain praise and glory among all the good, who are among the nations. Δικαιοῦσθαι is often to be praised by the name of justice or probity, Matt. 11, 10. Luke 7, 29. ch. 10, 29. ch. 16, 15. 1. Timothy 3, 16. Ecclus. 1, 28. ch. 31, 5.

What it is to twist Scripture, if this is not it, I confess I am ignorant. Therefore I will deign no further word to this twisted gloss.

Latin:

Vers. eod. DICET, MEÆ SUNT JUSTITIÆ ET IMPERIUM : AD EUM VENIENT, ET CONFUN- DENTUR OMNES, QVI REPUGNANT EI) Hic le- ctio quam secuti sunt LXX. melior est, nempe לו pro לי, ut illud עדיי sit quasi repetitio illius לו, genere loquendi He- bræis non infrequente. Sensus est: dicet quisque illorum ex gentibus, cum ista quæ jam diximus videbit, Deum & veracissimum esse & potentissimum, meritoque eos erube- scere debere, qui se ei opponunt.

Ne nihil intermittat ad depravandum oracu- lum, corruptionem fingit textus avthentici, eique præfert versionem Græcam: ac si scriptum fuisset olim לו ILLI sunt justitia & imperium: id est, Deus est veracissimus & potentissimus, quod id cognituri sint gentiles ex liberatione Babylonica. At quis ad- mittet audacem illam & temerariam assertionem de fonte corrupto? Non de Domini veritate, aut potentia absolute agitur, sed quomodo Dominus fidelibus sit justitia & robur, qui ita in Domino glori- aturi sint, eumque confessuri. Quod versus postre- mus luculenter confirmat: IN DOMINO JU- STIFICABITUR, ET GLORIABITUR OMNE SEMEN ISRAEL. Quomodo ergo in Domino justificabitur, nisi quod in Domino ju- stitia ipsa sit? Quomodo gloriatur in Domino, ni- si quod ita confiteatur Dominum, in Domino mihi justitia & robur? Sed Grotius ausus etiam est hunc versum depravare, etsi luculentissimum, & ver- bum justificandi non de justitia coram Deo, de qua vi antecedentium, & vers. 17. necessario id intelli- gendum, ac per se luculentissime sonat, sed de ju- stitia coram hominibus intelligit.

V. 26. IN DOMINO JUSTIFICABITUR ET LAU- DABITUR OMNE SEMEN ISRAEL) Id est, propter unius Dei cultum, laudem ac gloriam consequetur populus Israeliticus apud omnes bonos, qui sunt in gentibus. Δικαι- οῦσθαι sæpe est justitiæ aut probitatis nomine laudari, Matth. 11, 10. Luc. 7, 29. cap. 10, 29. cap. 16, 15. 1. Timoth. 3, 16. Eccles. 1, 28. cap. 31, 5.

Quid sit torquere Scripturam, si hoc non sit, fateor me ignorare. Ideo glossam contortam nul- lo ampliùs dignabor verbo.

## 45:25
V. 25. THEREFORE IN THE LORD) Translate: namely by בּיהוה. By that name of the God of Israel, see what [is said] on Matt. 22, 44.

Grotius accepts these, as if the formula of the oath were indicated by the name ביהוה. But thus this would have to be drawn to the preceding verse, which is inconvenient. If it pertained to that, without doubt it would have been added here in that verse: And every tongue shall swear by יהוה, nor would Paul have omitted that in Rom. 14. Wherefore it is necessary that the word ביהוה be referred not to the antecedents, but to the consequents, in the Lord is justice to me, so that these things pertain to the material of the confession, which is designated by the voice of an oath, but not indeed to the formula of an oath. Add that the Apostle explained the word of swearing by confession; but confession is not by the name יהוה, but is of Jehovah as the object of confession.

Latin:

V. 25. ERGO IN DOMINO) Verte: nempe per בּיהוה. Per nomen illud Dei Israëlis, vid. quæ ad Matth. 22, 44.

Accipit hæc Grotius, quasi formula juramenti per nomen ביהוה indigitetur. At ita trahendum hoc erit ad præcedentem versum, quod inconve- niens. Si eo pertineret, sine dubio additum fuisset hic in illo versu: Et jurabit omnis lingua per יהוה neque Paulus id prætermisset Rom. 14. Quapro- pter necessum est, ut verbum ביהוה non ad an- tecedentia, sed ad consequentia referatur, in Domino mihi justitia, ut hæc ad materiale pertineant confes- sionis, quæ voce juramenti designatur, non vero ad juramenti formulam. Adde quod vocem jurandi per confessionem exposuerit Apostolus; Confessio autem non sit per nomen יהוה, sed sit de Jobovah ceu confessionis objecto.

## 46:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLVI.

The projection of the idols Bel & Nebo having been shown, and the vanity of both, the Israelites as if carried in the womb of God are recalled to the worship of the true God.

Vers. 1. BEL IS CONTRACTED) In Hebrew: Bel bowed himself, that is, he fell; ἔπεσε Βὴλ, as the LXX have here. בל is to the Babylonians, who is בעל to the Phoenicians, namely the Sun. Herodotus and others call this Jupiter, not because of the star of Jupiter, but because, just as to the Greeks Zeus was the highest of the gods, so the Sun was to the Babylonians. His temple was built most augustly in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, as Berosus testifies, whose words we have brought forward to book 3 of the truth of the Christian religion. There is mention of this temple also in Herodotus in Clio, and in the fragment of Hecataeus, which is in Josephus against Apion, the first. Bel is said to have fallen, because he could not be of help to Babylon. And it is customary when cities are captured for temples to be demolished, and images to be carried off or destroyed. C. Flaminius in his oration for M. Fulvius: The statues were carried off and other things done, which are customary when cities are captured. Tertullian in the Apologeticus: As many triumphs from gods as from nations, And in the book against the Nations: And the captive images remain. See what has been said by us on the law of War and Peace book 3, chapter 20.

NABO IS BROKEN) Nabo is cut down: as the Chaldean translates here. This is another god of the Babylonians, whence the name have Nabonassar, Nabopolassar, Nabuchodonosor, Nabonidus, and other kings of the Babylonians. He was, however, some Soothsayer consecrated as a god by the Babylonians for similar reasons, as Apollo ὁ Λοξίας among the Greeks.

THEIR IMAGES ARE MADE TO BEASTS AND CATTLE, YOUR BURDENS WITH HEAVY WEIGHT EVEN TO WEARINESS) You may translate best: They were for a grief to the beasts and cattle (which) were pressed by carrying the burden to weariness: It is a χλευασμὸς: for he says the beasts rejoiced, because it will not be in the future, that those idols should grow weary by carrying. Idols were accustomed to be carried in sacred carriages. Thus a certain Roman was saying, that bulls and calves were wishing that Caesar would not return.

This interpretation is not to be disapproved. For the thing itself speaks that it is a discourse about the gods of the Babylonians, since the idols worshipped by them are expressed. But that under special idols any kind in general is hinted at, since Scripture has been accustomed to designate a genus by a species, the Interpreters have observed not badly: Thus Oecolampadius, as also Calvin, who says, under the name of these idols, he comprehends other idols also, and signifies that all the superstitions of the nations and impious cults will be overturned, when God, having prostrated their worshippers, will celebrate a triumph, because now it will be manifest that he is the just avenger of his Church. For since the Chaldeans were proudly boasting in the protection of false gods, the Prophet blunts that fallacious confidence: because the God of Israel will not only defeat that impious nation, but will also ignominiously cast down its gods. Therefore he says they will be burdens of beasts of burden: since, placed upon wagons, they will be transferred elsewhere, and indeed cast down without honor, just as it pleased the drivers. For this is what 'to be depressed' signifies, because the plunderers will pack those gods, for whom the stature was previously sublime, into a dense heap. That this was indeed fulfilled, there is no doubt, when the Persians and Medes conquered Babylon. For the Monarchy having been transferred, these idols, as part of the booty, were carried away. But although Isaiah predicted this, he nevertheless looked further: namely to the coming of Christ, by which impious cults were to be removed and destroyed. For his kingdom being established, all idols immediately fall: nor is it possible that, with his knowledge, false religion and impious cults be retained. And from the Papists, Cornelius à Lapide: God had said in the preceding chapter, that in the time of Christ idols were to be crushed; and v. 23. To me every knee shall bow. Here he shows this in the primary idols of the Chaldeans and of the world, viz. Baal, or Bel, and Nabo, namely that these were to be laid waste and plundered by Cyrus the victor, and much more that these and all others were to be abolished by Christ in the golden age of the Gospel. Whom Menochius the Jesuit followed, an author approved by Grotius. B. Brentius, although he explains it specifically concerning the idols of the Babylonians, nevertheless does not entirely reject the general sense. But concerning these we leave the judgment free. Concerning Nabo, others warn that he is the same as Merodach, because, just as it is said here, Bel is broken, Nebo is crushed! Thus Jeremiah chapter 50, 1. Bel is confounded, he says, Merodach is overcome: And that Belshazzar the son of Nebuchadnezzar was called both Merodach and Nabiratus; because idolatrous kings were accustomed to borrow a name from their gods, just as Papists do from Ignatius Loyola, and their similar idols. Jerome writes thus concerning these. He testifies that after the calling of the nations and the election of believers from Israel, the idols fell; He fell, he fell or is broken is Bel, whom the Greeks call Belus, that is, Saturn. Whose religion was so great among the ancients, that they sacrificed to him not only human victims of captives and ignoble mortals, but also their own children. Nabo, however, is also an idol, which is interpreted as prophecy and divination, which signifies that after the truth of the Gospel [it] has fallen silent in the whole world, or according to the LXX, dagan, which however is not found in the Hebrew. And it is the idol of Ascalon, Gaza, and the remaining cities of the Philistines. And from the special it passes to the general: Their idols have been made for beasts and cattle

Latin:

CAPUT XLVI.

Ostensa idolorum Bel & Nebo projectione, u- trorumque vanitate, Israelitæ ceu in utero Dei gestati ad veri Dei cultum revocantur.

Vers. 1. CONTRACTUS EST BEL) In Hebræo: cur- vavit se Bel, id est, cecidit; ἔπεσε Βὴλ, ut habent hic LXX. בל Babyloniis est, qui בעל Phœnicibus, Sol scilicet. Jovem hunc vocant Herodotus aliique, non ob stellam Jovis, sed quod, sicut Græcis Ζεύς erat deorum summus, ita Sol Ba- byloniis. Templum ejus longe augustissimum erat Baby- lone structum à Nabuchodonosoro, ut testatur Berosus, cu- jus verba attulimus ad librum 3. de veritate religionis Chri- stianæ. Est ejus templi mentio & apud Herodotum in Clio, & in Hecatæi fragmento, quod est apud Josephum contra Appionem primo. Cecidisse dicitur Belus, quia Babyloni auxilio esse non potuit. Et solent captis urbibus dirui tem- pla, abripi aut destrui simulacra. C. Flaminius in oratione pro M. Fulvio: Signa ablata & cætera facta, quæ captis urbi- bus soleant. Tertullianus Apologetico: Tot de diis, quot de gentibus triumphi, Et in libro adversus Nationes : Manent & simulacra captiva. Vide quæ dicta à nobis de jure Belli ac Pacis lib. 3. cap. 20.

CONTRITUS EST NABO) Succisus est Nabo : ut hic vertit Chaldæus. Hic est Deus alter Babyloniorum, un- de nomen habent Nabonassar, Nabopolassar, Nabuchodo- nosor, Nabonidus, & alii reges Babyloniorum. Fuit autem Ariolus aliquis in Deum consecratus à Babyloniis paribus de causis, ut Apollo ὁ Λοξίας apud Græcos.

FACTA SUNT SIMULACRA EORUM BE- STIIS ET JUMENTIS, ONERA VESTRA GRAVI PONDERE USQVE AD LASSITUDINEM) Optime vertas : Fuerunt dolori bestiis & jumentis (quæ) gestando onere pressa sunt ad lassitudinem : Est χλευασμὸς: dicit enim gavi- sura jumenta, quod posthac non futurum sit, ut ista idola portando lassescant. Solebant in thensis idola portari. Sic Romanus quidam dicebat, tauros & vitulos optare ne Cæ- sar rediret.

Non improbanda hæc interpretatio. Nam de diis Babyloniorum sermone esse, res ipsa loqui- tur, quum exprimantur idola ab illis culta. Sed sub specialibus idolis in genere quævis innui, quum ita Scriptura per speciem genus designare consueve- rit, Interpretes haud male observarunt: Ita Oecolam- padius, ut & Calvinus, qui, sub horum, inquit, ido- lorum nomine, cætera etiam idola comprehendit, atque significat omnes gentium superstitiones, & cultus im- pios subversum iri, ubi Deus prostratis eorum culto- ribus triumphum aget, quia nunc patebit eum esse justum Ecclesiæ suæ vindicem. Nam quum falsorum deorum præsidio superbe gloriarentur Chaldæi, falla- cem illam confidentiam retundit Propheta : quia Deus Israëlis non modo impiam illam gentem profli- gabit, sed ejus quoque Deos ignominiose dejiciet. Pro- pterea jumentorum onera fore dicit: quoniam plau- stris imposita alio transferentur, & quidem sine ho- nore projecta, prout aurigis placuerit. Hoc enim valet Deprimi, quia Deos illos, quibus sublimis prius erat statura, raptores in densum acervum compin- gent. Hoc quidem impletum esse, dubium non est, quum Babylonem Persæ & Medi expugnarunt. Translata enim Monarchia, hæc idola, ut pars præ- dæ, ablata sunt. Sed quamvis hoc prædiceret, lon- gius tamen spectavit Isaias: nempe ad Christi adven- tum, quo impii cultus summovendi ac delendi erant. Nam stabilito ejus regno, idola omnia statim conci- dunt: nec fieri potest, ut cum ejus notione, falsa reli- gio & impii cultus retineantur. Et è Pontificiis Cornelius à Lapide : Dixerat Deus cap. præcedenti, tempore Christi conterenda esse idola; & v. 23. Mihi curvabitur omne genu. Hic id ostendit in primariis Chaldæorum & orbis idolis, scil. Baal, sive Bel, & Nabo, nimirum hæc à Cyro victore vastanda & diri- pienda esse, & multo magis hæc omniaque alia, à Chri- sto abolenda esse aureo Evangelii seculo. Quem se- quutus est Menochius Jesuita, autor Grotio pro- batus. B. Brentius etsi speciatim explicet de Baby- loniorum idolis, generalem tamen sensum non omnino rejicit. Sed de his liberum relinquimus judicium. De Nabone alii monent, quod idem sit cum Merodach, quia, sicut hic dicitur, confractus est Bel, contritus est Nebo! Ita Jeremias cap. 50, 1. Confusus est Bel, inquit, victus est Merodach: Quod- que Baltasar filius Nabuchodonosaris & Mero- dach & Nabiratus vocatus sit; quia solebant reges idololatræ à diis suis nomen mutuari, uti Papistæ ab Ignatio Lojola, & similibus idolis suis. Hiero- nymus de his ita. Post vocationem gentium & ele- ctionem credentium ex Israël idola corruisse testatur; Cecidit, cecidit sive confractus est Bel, quem Græci Belum, id est, Saturnum vocant. Cujus tanta fuit apud veteres religio, ut ei non solum humanas hostias captivorum, ignobiliumque mortalium, sed & suos liberos immolarent. Nabo autem & ipsum idolum est, quod interpretatur Prophetia & divinatio, quam post Evangelii veritatem in toto orbe conticuisse si- gnificat, sive juxta LXX. dagan, qui tamen in He- braico non habetur. Et est idolum Ascalonis, Ga- zæ, & reliquarum urbium Philistim. Et à speciali transit ad generale: Facta sunt simulacra eorum be- stiis & jumentis

## 46:2
THEY COULD NOT SAVE THE ONE CARRYING) Their bearers.

AND THEIR SOUL HAS GONE INTO CAPTIVITY) That is, the gods themselves, in a Hebrew idiom.

Latin:

Vers. 2. NON POTUERUNT SALVARE POR- TANTEM) Bajulos suos.

ET ANIMA EORUM IN CAPTIVITATEM IVIT) Id est, ipsi dii, locutione Hebræa.

## 46:3
WHO ARE CARRIED FROM MY WOMB, WHO ARE BORNE FROM MY MATRIX) In the Hebrew: Carried from the womb, borne from the matrix. That is, whom I have guarded from the very beginning with the most tender affection, such as that of mothers.

Latin:

QUI PORTAMINI A MEO UTERO, QUI GE- STAMINI A MEA VULVA) In Hebræo: Portati ab utero, gestati à matrice. Id est, quos ego à prima origine affectu tenerrimo, qualis est matrum, custodivi.

## 46:4
EVEN TO OLD AGE I MYSELF) Will carry you, as follows: in this I will surpass mothers.

Latin:

Vers 4. USQUE AD SENECTAM EGO IPSE) Portabo vos, ut sequitur: in hoc matres vincam.

## 46:5
TO WHOM HAVE YOU LIKENED ME?) To whom would you liken me? He says this so that, corrupted by the example of idolaters and weary from long servitude, they might not imitate the customs of the Babylonians: for the Persians did not have images.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CUI ASSIMILASTIS ME?) Cui assimilaretis me? Hoc ideo dicit, ne exemplo idololatrarum corrupti, & fessi longa servitute Babyloniorum mores imitarentur: nam Persæ imagines non habebant.

## 46:6
WHO POUR OUT GOLD FROM THE BAG, AND WEIGH SILVER ON THE SCALES, HIRING A GOLDSMITH, THAT HE MAY MAKE A GOD, AND THEY FALL DOWN AND WORSHIP) The best version is: After they have brought out gold from the purse, and weighed silver in the balance, they hire a goldsmith for a fee, who may make a God for them, before whom they may fall down or bow themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QVI CONFERTIS AVRVM DE SAC- CVLO, ET ARGENTVM STATERA PONDERA- TIS, CONDVCENTES AVRIFICEM, VT FACIAT DEVM, ET PROCIDVNT ET ADORANT) Versio optima est: Illi postquam promserunt aurum de marsupio, & in trutina expenderunt argentum, mercede conducunt aurifi- cem, qui ipsis Deum faciat, coram quo procidant, aut se in- flectant.

## 46:7
AND PLACING [IT] IN ITS PLACE) That is, upon a base.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET PONENTES IN LOCO SVO) Id est, super basim.

## 46:8
RETURN, TRANSGRESSORS, TO THE HEART) You may translate more correctly from the Hebrew: Bring back those who wander to wisdom.

Latin:

Vers. 8. REDITE PRÆVARICATORES AD COR) Ex Hebræo vertas rectius: Reducite eos, qui errant, ad sapien- tiam.

## 46:9
REMEMBER THE FORMER AGE) Compare all your past things with the events.

Latin:

Vers. 9. RECORDAMINI PRIORIS SÆCULI) Omnia vestra prædicta cum eventis comparate.

## 46:10
ANNOUNCING FROM THE BEGINNING THE LAST) Announcing from a long time ago things that would follow much later.

Latin:

ANNVNTIANS AB EXORDIO NOVISSIMVM) A longo tempore prænuntians multo post secu- tura.

## 46:11
CALLING A BIRD FROM THE EAST) Calling an Eagle from Persia, that is, Cyrus, who had an aquiline nose, as Plutarch notes. Aristotle in the Physiognomonics: those who have a hooked (nose) and one articulated with the forehead, are great-souled. It is referred to the eagles.

Others understand עיט Avern, or rather a crowd and collection of birds of prey, which fly swiftly and with force upon their prey, or they think Cyrus is so called because of his swiftness, whom Xenophon in book 7 of the Cyropaedia is the author of saying also carried a golden eagle with expanded wings on his standard. Whence this sign was used thereafter by the kings of the Persians, and later by the Romans. Nebuchadnezzar is also called a great eagle flying upon the Jews and other nations, Jerem. 48, 10. Ezech. 17, 3. For he also was endowed with an aquiline nature. Jerome thinks Christ is designated here. But most all interpreters interpret it concerning Cyrus, and more correctly.

Verse same. MAN OF MY WILL) In Hebrew: Man (that is, the executor) of my counsel.

I WILL BRING THAT) I will give effect to that counsel of mine.

I HAVE CREATED) I have preformed in my mind.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VOCANS AB ORIENTE AVEM) E Persi- de vocans Aquilam, id est, Cyrum, cui nasus erat Aquilinus, ut Plutarchus notat. Aristoteles in Physiognomonicis: οἱ γρυπὴν ἔχοντες (τὴν ῥῖνα) καὶ τῷ μετώπῳ διηρθρωμένην, μεγα- λόψυχοι. ἀναφέρεται ἐπὶ τὰς ἀετὸς.

Alii עיט Avern, vel turbam potius & colle- ctionem avium rapacium intelligunt, quæ celeriter & cum impetu in prædam involant, vel Cyrum ita ob celeritatem vocari putant, quem etiam in ve- xillo aquilam auream alis expansis gessisse, Xeno- phon lib. 7. Cyripædiæ autor est. Unde hoc signo deinceps reges Persarum, & postea Romani usi sunt. Vocatur & Nabuchodonosor aquila grandis & involans in Judæos, aliasque gentes, Jerem. 48, 10. Ezech. 17, 3. Nam ille etiam enafo aquilino prædi- tus erat. Hironymus Christum hic designari pu- tat. Sed plerique omnes Interpretes de Cyro, & re- ctius, interpretantur.

Vers. eod. VIRVM VOLVNTATIS MEÆ) In He- bræo: Virum (id est, effectorem) consilii mei.

ADDVCAM ILLVD) Consilium illud meum ef- fectum dabo.

CREAVI) Præformavi in animo.

## 46:12
Verse 12. HEAR ME, STOUT OF HEART) He addresses those from the captivity who were about to doubt the promises.

YOU WHO ARE FAR FROM RIGHTEOUSNESS) You who, because you are unfaithful, think me also to be such.

Latin:

Vers. 12. AVDITE ME DVRO CORDE) Illos de captivitate alloquitur, qui de promissis dubitaturi erant.

QVI LONGE ESTIS A JVSTITIA) Qui quod infidi estis, me quoque talem putatis.

## 46:13
I HAVE BROUGHT NEAR MY RIGHTEOUSNESS) The time is near at hand when I will fulfill my faithfulness.

AND IN ISRAEL MY GLORY) I will effect his liberation as most glorious for myself.

Vatablus, Brentius, Osiander, and Pappus understand these things concerning Christ; Cornelius à Lapide, along with Jerome, asserts that they pertain mystically to Christ, which Oecolampadius and the Belgian Paraphrasts also already intimate. Certainly those names MY RIGHTEOUSNESS, MY SALVATION, MY GLORY sound of Christ. Nor is it foreign to the custom of the Prophet that the restoration of the people, and their liberty, and the coming of the Messiah should be joined: since for the faithful, external liberation without the coming of the Messiah would have profited nothing, or would have offered meager comfort. Mr. Dr. Pappus says it is most manifest that these things ought to be understood concerning the Messiah. For outside of Christ, who has been made for us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification by the eternal Father, salvation can be obtained by no one. And this very salvation is given IN ZION only and to ISRAEL only: not, however, in the earthly Zion, nor to the carnal Israel, but in that which is above, the free Jerusalem, which is our mother the Church, and to Israel the son of promise, that is, to believers. And therefore, those who are prevaricators, and the strong, and the robust of heart are far from this righteousness, salvation, and glory; they are far off, who, since they do not acknowledge their own unworthiness and attempt to establish their own righteousness, fall away from the righteousness of faith by the just judgment of GOD. Zwingli himself acknowledged this: Behold, he says, how often, when the occasion permits, he brings forward the prophecy concerning Christ. Nor do the Weimar Paraphrasts deny it regarding the latter words: My salvation shall not tarry; even though they still refer the former: I have brought near my righteousness, to bodily liberation. But those things cannot be separated, and they speak of the same subject, and therefore more correctly [are they understood] by our other interpreters. all things are understood concerning Christ: for all things cohere. I have brought NEAR MY RIGHTEOUSNESS, it shall not be elongated, AND MY SALVATION shall not tarry. I WILL GIVE SALVATION IN ZION, and MY GLORY in Israel. These things are too august to be snatched away to a type and bodily liberation. Finally, Grotius himself acknowledges that these things were said concerning the Messiah. For thus he has it at Luke 2, 30. In Isaiah 46, 13, God speaking concerning the Messiah similarly says תשועתי My salvation, i.e., from me, and in the same [author] 49, 6. ישועתי in the same sense.

Latin:

PROPE FECI JVSTITIAM MEAM) Prope adest tempus, quo fidem meam implebo.

ET IN ISRAEL GLORIAM MEAM) Liberatio- nem ejus efficiam mihi gloriosissimam.

Hæc de Christo intelligunt Vatablus, Brentius, Osiander, Pappus; mystice ad Christum pertinere asserit cum Hieronymo Cornelius à Lapide, quod innuunt etiam jam Oecolampadius & Paraphrasta Belgici. Nomina certe illa JUSTITIA MEA, SALUS MEA, GLORIA MEA, Christum so- nant. Neque alienum est à more Prophetæ resti- tutionem populi, & libertatem & adventnm Mes- siæ conjungi: siquidem fidelibus externa liberatio sine Messiæ adventu nihil profuisset, aut exiguum solatium præbuisset. Dn. D. Pappus manifestissi- mum esse ait hæc de Messia intelligi oportere. Ex- tra Christum enim, qui nobis ab æterno Patre sapien- tia factus est, & justitia, & sanctificatio, nemini potest salus obtingere. Et datur hæc ipsa salus IN ZION tantum & ISRAELI tantum: non ta- men in terrena Sione, neque carnali Israëli sed in illa, quæ sursum est libera Jerusalem, quæ est mater no- stra Ecclesia, & Israëli filio promissionis, id est, cre- dentibus. Ideoque ab hac justitia, salute, & gloria procul absunt prævaricatores, & fortes, & robusti corde procul absunt, qui cum suam indignitatem non agnoscant, & justitiam propriam conentur consti- tuere, justo DEI judicio à justitia fidei excidunt. Zvvinglius ipse id agnovit: En, inquit, quoties per occasionem licet, vaticinium de Christo oggerit. Neque abnuunt Paraphrastæ Vinarienses de verbis posterioribus: Salus mea non morabitur; etsi prio- ra: Prope feci justitiam meam, adhuc ad liberatio- nem corporalem referant. Sed illa separari non pos- sunt, & de eodem subjecto loquuntur, ideoque rectius à cæteris nostris Interpp. omnia de Christo intelliguntur: cohærent enim omnia. PROPE feci JUSTITIAM MEAM, non elongabitur, ET SALUS MEA non morabitur. DABO IN SION SALUTEM, & in Israël GLORIAM MEAM. Augustiora hæc sunt, quam ut ad ty- pum & liberationem corporalem abripi possint. Denique agnoscit Grotius ipse hæc de Messia di- cta esse. Sic enim habet ad Luc. 2, 30. Apud Esa. 46, 13. Deus loquens de Messia similiter ait תשועתי Salus mea, i. e. à me, & apud eundem 49, 6. ישועתי sensu eodem.

## 47:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLVII.

The destruction of Babylon predicted on account of pride, mercilessness, magical arts, and the astrology of the Chaldeans.

Vers. 1. DESCEND) From the throne, as the following words show: for for some time the empire had almost been the Babylonians'.

SIT IN THE DUST) As was accustomed to be done in the most grievous mourning.

VIRGIN) Cities are accustomed to be described by the names and figure of women. He called her a virgin, indeed, because she was soft and tender in her way of life and dress, as will now follow.

Latin:

CAPUT XLVII.

Interitus Babyloni ob superbiam, immisericor- diam, artes Magicas, & Astrologiam Chal- dæorum prædictus.

Vers. 1. DESCENDE) De solio, ut sequentia osten- dunt: nam ab aliquo tempore pene Babylonios imperium fuerat.

SEDE IN PULVERE) Ut in luctu gravissimo fieri solebat.

VIRGO) Civitates feminarum nominibus & figura describi solent. Virginem vero dixit; quia mollis erat & te- nera in victu atque habitu, ut jam sequetur.

## 47:2
Vers. 2. TAKE THE MILLSTONE, AND GRIND FLOUR) Prepare yourself for servile tasks. See Job 31:10.

UNCOVER YOUR SHAME) In the Hebrew: Uncover, that is, shave your hair. That also was the custom for those mourning.

Sanctius, from a comparison with Isaiah 3:17, 'The Lord will make bald the crown of the daughters of Zion,' explains it: You will be made bald, and thus your shame, for instance baldness, will appear. Vatablus renders it: Loosen your curls. Forerius explains it: Your headband; so that, namely, with the headband removed, they may shamefully hang loose, as is the case with captive maidservants, or rustic women, or those mourning.

Vers. eod. UNCOVER THE SHOULDER) Prepare yourself for labor.

UNCOVER THE LEGS, CROSS THE RIVERS) That is, so that you may be able to cross the fords of the rivers while fleeing.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TOLLE MOLAM, ET MOLE FARINAM) Para te servilibus ministeriis. Vide Jobum 31, 10.

DENUDA TURPITUDINEM TUAM) In He- bræo: Detege, id est, rade capillos tuos. Etiam illud in more lugentibus.

SAnctius è collatione Esa. 3, 17. Decalvabit Do- minus verticem filiorum Sion explicat: Decal- vaberis, itaque apparebit tua turpitudo, puta calvi- tium. Vatablus reddit: Dissolve cincinnos tuos. Forerius explicat: Fasciam tuam; ut scil. fascia ab- lata turpiter diffluant, ut sit in ancillis captivis, vel rusticanis aut lugentibus.

Vers. eod. DISCOOPERI HUMERUM) Ad laborem te para.

REVELA CRURA, TRANSI FLUMINA) I. e. ut transire possis fluminum vada fugiens.

## 47:3
Vers. 3. YOUR SHAME SHALL BE UNCOVERED, AND YOUR DISGRACE SHALL BE SEEN) You will not have wherewith to cover even those things which modesty most desires to be covered.

AND NO MAN SHALL RESIST ME) And I will not take up any intercessor. For פגע means both to intercede and to admit those who intercede.

Avenarius renders it, I will not strike against you, as a man. Oecolampadius: And I will not meet you as a man. Thus also Vatablus, with an added explanation, not humanely, but cruelly as a lion. Amama observed that the Tigurine, Piscator, English, Spanish, Genevan, and Italian versions also express this sense. Zwingli had preceded Grotius in his translation and explanation. Calvin reported both of those explanations. He judged, however, that the more common one flows better, as far as the context of the words is concerned. But he believed the other has something forced in its construction. For thus פגעת would have to be taken passively, which could hardly be tolerated. Therefore, Grotius ought to have shown by some example that פגע admits of those praying. Both expositions come to the same thing, that the Lord will destroy the Chaldeans, and there will be no place for mercy at all.

Latin:

Vers. 3. REVELABITUR IGNOMINIA TUA, ET VIDEBITUR OPPROBRIUM TUUM) Non erit tibi unde vel ea tegas, quæ maxime tegi vult pudor.

ET NON RESISTET MIHI HOMO) Et non su- scipiam deprecatorem quemquam. Nam פגע est & deprecari & deprecantes admittere.

Avenarius reddit, non impingam in te, ut ho- mo. Oecolampadius: Et non occurram sicut homo. Sic etiam Vatablus addita ἐξηγήσει, non humaniter, sed crudeliter ut leo. Quem sensum etiam exprime- re Tigurinos, Piscator. Anglic. Hispan. Genev. Ital. versionem Amama observavit. Grotio præiverat Zvvinglius in sua translatione, & explanatione. Utramque illam explicationem retulit Calvinus, communiorem tamen illam melius fluere, quod ad verborum contextum attinet, judicavit. Alteram autem aliquid coacti habere in constructione cre- didit. Sic enim פגעת passive accipiendum esset, quod vix tolerari posset. Exemplo itaque quodam ostendere debuisset Grotius פגע esse deprecantes admittere. Utraque expositio eodem redit, Domi- num Chaldæos deleturum, nec ullum omnino miseri- cordiæ locum fore.

## 47:6
Vers. 6. I AM ANGRY WITH MY PEOPLE, I HAVE POLLUTED MY INHERITANCE, AND GIVEN THEM INTO THY HAND, THOU DIDST SHOW THEM NO MERCY) You may translate it correctly thus: When I, being angry with my people, allowed my own land to be polluted by you, and delivered the men into your hand, you had no pity on them.

UPON THE ANCIENT HAST THOU VERY HEAVILY LAID THY YOKE) Even upon the old. See Lam. Jer. 5, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 6. IRATVS SVM SVPER POPVLVM MEVM, CONTAMINAVI HÆREDITATEM MEAM, ET DEDI EOS IN MANV TVA, NON POSVISTI EIS MISERICORDIAS) Recte sic vertas: Cum ego iratus po- pulo meo terram mihi propriam abs te contaminari paterer, ho- minesque traderem in manum tuam, tu eorum nihil es miserta.

SVPER SENEM AGGRAVASTI JVGVM TVVM VALDE) Etiam super senes. Vide Lam. Jer. 5, 4.

## 47:7
THOU DIDST NOT LAY THESE THINGS TO THY HEART) You did not think about these things, which are now happening to you.

NEITHER DIDST REMEMBER THE LATTER END OF IT) This destruction did not come to your mind.

Latin:

NON POSVISTI HÆC SVPER COR TVVM) Non cogitasti de his, quæ nunc tibi eveniunt.

NEQVE RECORDATA ES NOVISSIMI TVI) Non venit tibi in mentem hoc excidium.

## 47:8
I SHALL NOT SIT AS A WIDOW, AND SHALL NOT KNOW THE LOSS OF CHILDREN) I shall not lack a king, nor yet posterity. The Apocalypse 18, 7 attributes similar words to Rome under the name of Babylon.

Latin:

NON REDIBO VIDVA, ET IGNORABO STE- RILITATEM) Non carebo rege, sed nec posteritate. Paria verba Romæ sub nomine Babylonis tribuit Apocal. 18, 7.

## 47:9
Vers. 9. AND FOR THE MULTITUDE OF THY SORCERIES) Of the priests. Thus חבר is taken by the Arabs, and soon here in verse 12. Baal Aruch explains this word in this way. It appears often in the Chaldean Paraphrasts.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET PROPTER DVRITIAM INCANTA- TORVM TVORVM) Sacerdotum. Ita حَبْد fumitur Arabibus, & mox hic 12. Ita vocem hanc explicat Baal Aruch. Apparet sæpe in Chaldæis Paraphrastis.

## 47:10
Vers. 10. THY WISDOM AND THY KNOWLEDGE, IT HATH PERVERTED THEE) Trust in the skill of astrological divination, which was so great in that nation that all of that profession were called Chaldeans. See the knowledge of the Chaldean art in Tacitus, Annals 6. See also Gellius 1.9, L. Nemo C. de Maleficis.

I AM, AND NONE ELSE BESIDE ME) The Chaldeans alone have obtained wisdom, in the oracle.

There is no apparent reason why these should be restricted to astrological writings, even though the same sense has approved itself to Corn. and Forerius: It is a general statement that human wisdom and manifold knowledge, and those who rely on them, and trust that they can beautifully foresee all things that are to happen and moderate and govern them by their own prudence, are confounded by God. Which is predicted here to the Chaldeans. Concerning the sorcerers, Magi, stargazers, and the like, it is treated again in verse 12 and following.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SAPIENTIA TVA ET SCIENTIA TVA HÆC DECEPIT TE) Fiducia in peritia Astrologicæ di- vinationis, quæ tanta in ea gente, ut omnes ejus professio- nis Chaldæi dicti fuerint. Scientia Chaldæorum artis apud Tacitum Annalium 6. Vid. & Gellium 1.9, L. Nemo C. de Maleficis.

EGO SVM, ET PRÆTER ME NON EST AL- TERA) μῶνοι Χαλδαῖοι σοφίαν λάχον in oraculo.
