For formerly they were devoid of spiritual consolation: they had no divine law, no prophet, no pedagogue, no master, no Doctor, no fountain of intelligible waters: But when they obtained mercy from God, spiritual goods were thereafter supplied abundantly, and they had food that helps the souls, they ate bread from heaven, they drank living water, of which Christ himself also spoke while making words to the Samaritan woman. But neither shall the heat strike them, nor the Sun. For Christ has been made a protector for them, who also formerly suspended a cloud for the children of Israel by day, and went before them in a pillar of fire by night. Therefore, he says, they shall be outside the sun and the heat, that is, they shall be covered by a divine shade, so that nothing may happen that is troublesome, or that leads to pusillanimity.

It is therefore frivolous and inept that Grotius accepts this great promise, which extends itself even into the other and most blessed life, as concerning only the ease of the journey, that nothing will be lacking to the Hebrews for the return to Judea. Finally, those things which are predicted concerning mountains being placed in the way and the paths of the Lord being exalted, those are likewise ineptly and frivolously snatched away by Grotius to a level road for the return, who here tastes nothing but carnal and temporal things. Other long ways and paths are understood, namely, the ways of the law and the depressed paths of the Lord: because our compassionate one makes it so that we walk in the ways of justice, and directs our feet into the ways of peace and the paths of the commandments of the Lord, so that we may walk according to the rule of the divine word, Gal. 6, 16, so that the mountains of pride and impiety may be depressed and humbled, and the depressed and humble paths, which are those crushed and depressed by true repentance, may be exalted. Or if these things are to be understood concerning the equality of the way and the ease of the journey, they designate not a way and path into Judea, but to the Church, because the whole promise treats not of corporal, but of spiritual benefits. I will make all even the rough places so stony, and the pathless paths so paved, that a great multitude of nations shall be about to approach, of which the following verses treat: Behold, these come from afar, etc. Which sense Jerome again well expressed. All stumbling blocks, which could have hindered the steps of believers, the Lord will turn for them into a plain, and will humble the high, and will exalt the low, that they may have a plain and level journey. But who these are, for whom the way is prepared; he sets forth more clearly: Behold, these shall come from afar. Calvin himself, even if he strives to draw some things in this promise to a corporal return, acknowledges that the spiritual benefits of Christ are described in verse 9: THAT HE MAY SAY TO THE PRISONERS. There is described, he says, in these words the change which happened at the coming of Christ. Nor is there any doubt, however, but that the Prophet wishes to bring comfort to the Jews in lost circumstances, lest the restoration to a better state be incredible to them: because they see themselves as almost devoted to destruction. Meanwhile, he shows in general what the office of Christ is: and defines that it is to restore desolate inheritances. For before Christ arrives, we are bound under a miserable yoke, and established in darkness. By these similitudes he signifies that we, as long as we lack Christ, to be overwhelmed by a heap of all evils. For through DARKNESS He excludes all things that pertain to the kingdom of Christ: faith, justice, truth, innocence, and the like. We are therefore in darkness until Christ says: SHOW YOURSELVES. We are bound until He says: COME FORTH. There is, however, very much weight in the word לאמר, that you may say. For it shows that the preaching of the Gospel is the way by which we are liberated. If, therefore, we desire the liberty and the light of the kingdom of God, let us hear Christ speaking: Otherwise, we shall be oppressed by the perpetual tyranny of Satan. Where now is the liberty of our will? For whoever arrogates to himself light or reason and intelligence will not be able to experience this liberation of Christ. For liberty is not promised to others, except to those who acknowledge themselves to be captives: Light and salvation to those who confess that they have been plunged into darkness. Oecolampadius, however, acknowledges that the other things which are held here also concern spiritual benefits. Regarding those words, THEY SHALL FEED UPON THE WAYS, he annotates thus: He describes the happiness of the faithful with wonderful and various hyperboles. For all things will be peaceful, fruitful, and sweet. Whence also the Lord invites us, saying: Take my yoke upon you, for my yoke is easy, and my burden is light. The Prophet first sets forth the abundance of pastures and waters. For they shall feed upon the ways; that is, they shall find pastures everywhere: And upon the hills shall be pastures, that is, in those places in which otherwise there are no pastures. Therefore, there shall be no hunger or thirst, but also no adversity, because the heat of persecution shall not strike. Nor is it a wonder, for the Lord will be our Leader and will help us, and will go before us, just as the Angel once went before the children of Israel departing from Egypt. And just as waters flowed from the rock in the desert, so also the merciful Lord will lead them to gushing and living waters, just as the Psalmist also says: The Lord ruleth me, and I shall want nothing; he hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment. There will likewise be a lack of labor and fatigue, for the mountains will be in the way, that is, level, so that all difficulty of the journey is absent. Here the Jew laughs and says: Where is that happiness of the Christians, whose Christ was crucified, and whose Apostles were subjected to various punishments, and for whom to embrace the cross is the first discipline? To whom we answer that we seek the happiness of the soul, not of the body, by which even the latter will follow when it shall be necessary. For there is no evil from the cross, for while the outward man is in a bad state, the inward man is renewed day by day. But there are also for us pastures, cups, and the heavenly bread, and we are fed much more delicately than the fathers in the desert: for they are dead, but whoever shall have eaten of our bread shall live forever. For we know how great things God has promised us, and lest we should waver in spirit, He sealed those promises with the death of our Lord Jesus Christ, His Son. It is impossible, however, that the souls of the faithful should not be refreshed by the memory of so great a benefit. There are also for us streams of the graces of the Holy Spirit, of which Christ says: If any man thirst, let him come to me, and rivers shall flow from his belly. These are truly the riches which the Spirit bestows. For in the mountains of afflictions, stripes, prisons, seditions, labors, watchings, fastings, and other difficulties, a way has been made for us, that we may bear all things in the gentleness of spirit, in the Holy Spirit, in kindness, in charity unfeigned, in the word of truth, in the power of God by the armor of justice, on the right hand and on the left, through glory and ignominy, etc., as the Apostle exhorts.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET PONAM OMNES MONTES MEOS IN VIAM) Id est, idem faciam quasi montes auferam. Vide supra 40, 4. ET SEMITÆ MEÆ EXALTABVNTVR) Id est, valles, ut via sit æqua, סלל ὁδοποιεῖν, מסלה vertitur ὁδὸς, διαβατὸν, τρίβον, πορεία.

Habemus novam promissionis itidem magni- ficentissimæ depravationem, quam præconcepta Judaica opinio, ac si de Esaia hic ageretur, huc sug- gessit, quæ vero non approbatorium, sed conde- mnatorium meretur calculum. Nam quodnam il- illud tempus placitum, quisnam dies salutis intelligi debeat, non ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει discere debemus, sed è Scripturis id depromendum: quæ ad Nov. Test. hoc tempus placitum, & hanc diem salutis διαρρή- δην referunt, 2. Cor. 6, 2. Hoc enim testimonio, verba sunt Hieronymi, Apostolus Paulus in secunda Epi- stola ad Corinthios usus, dicens: Tempore opportu- no exaudivi te, & in die salutis auxiliatus sum tui: Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile; ecce nunc dies sa- lutis. Si ergo vas electionis ad primi adventus refert intelligentiam, quæ dicuntur: & nos sequamur ex- positionis ejus vestigia: & instar parvulorum super adumbratas lineas præceptoris, literas imprimamus. Et quis ille sit, qui exauditus est, Propheta satis in- nuit, cum ait, DABO TE IN FOEDUS POPULI, quod frigida ista glossa, renovavi per te fœdus meum cum populo, nequicquam Grotius in rem suam per- vertere nititur. Non enim Propheta in fœdus po- puli datus, sed Messias, per quem Deus fœdus cum populo suo exerit: fœdus nempe novum, fœdus gratiæ, quo exhibentur nobis bona spiritualia, & cœlestia gratis, modo in Christum credamus. Quod sanguine suo in cruce sancivit, sed obsignat nobis in S. Cœna per eundem sanguinem novi fœderis, ad confirmationem gratiæ & salutis. Hoc enim fœ- dere passim eriguntur fideles. Per tempus placitum itaque intelligitur dies passionis, qui erat tempu Deo placitum, & dies salutis generis humani, ex quo fluere cepere omnes alii dies σωτήρως, quo ex- auditus ipse est ἀπὸ τῆς ἐυλαϐείας, v. 7. Et quod ib non sui, sed nostræ salutis causa exclamare, & exau- ditionem expetere opus habuerit, è Psal. 69. im- primis constat; hic ergo auditionem pollicetur Dominus, de qua etiam de cœlo ipsum confirma- vit, Joh. 12, 27. 28. cum precaretur: Pater salva me ex hac hora. Ideo recte Hieron. Tempus placitum & opportunum, & dies salutis passio Servatoris est, & resurrectio, quando orabat in cruce: Deus meus, Deus meus: quare me dereliquisti? Et servavit eum sive plasmavit morte superata, deditque in fœdus populi Judæorum, his videlicet, qui ex illis credere vo- luerunt, ut suscitaret terram.

Dubium est, quomodo 2. Cor. 6, 1. ad Eccle- siam totam accommodetur, quod de Christo agit, quæ ita explicat Calvinus: Paulus hanc sententiam ad totam Ecclesiam accommodat. Interea vero quod subjicit Propheta, DABO TE IN FOEDUS, ne- mini alteri quam Christo convenit, quomodo hæc in- ter se conciliabimus? nempe si consideremus Chri- stum non tam esse suum, quam nostrum, quia nec ve- nit, nec mortuus est, nec resurrexit sibi. Ipse enim in salutem Ecclesiæ missus est: nec quicquam sibi pro- prium quærit, cum nulla omnino re indigeat. Itaque promittit Deus universo Ecclesiæ corpori. Christus, qui velut sponsor intermedius est, recipit has promif- siones, nec sibi privatim stipulatur, sed toti Ecclesiæ, in cujus salutem missus est. Christum igitur non se- paratim compellat, sed quatenus corpori suo adhæret, eique perpetuo conjunctus est. Nec aliter Pontificii Interpp. Cor ael. à Lapide: q. d. Eo tempore, quo contemnebaris, vexabaris, imo crucifigebaris, ô Chri- ste ab impiis Judæis, orasti me, ut te ab hisce Judæo- rum & gentilium probris eriperem, glorificarem, à morte suscitarem, nomen tuum toto orbe celebrarem, & per illud justitiam & salutem darem omnibus gen- tibus. Dixisti enim in tempore contemptus tui, Psal. 68, 12. 14. Factus sum illis in parabolam. Ego vero orationem meam ad te Domine dirigebam, tem- pus beneplaciti, (adveniat) Deus. In multitudine misericordiæ tuæ exaudi me, in veritate salutis tuæ. Idem orasti in cruce cum clamore valido, & lachry- mis, & exauditus es pro tua reverentia, Hebr. 5,7. Nam tertio die à morte te suscitavi, quadragesimo die triumphantem in cœlos subvexi, quinquagesimo die in nomine tuo Spiritum S. in Apostolos tuos misi, qui mox tuum nomen toto orbe celebrarunt, tuamque fidem, gratiam & salutem omnibus Gentibus attu- lerunt & deprædicarunt. Tempus ergo placiti si- ve benevolentiæ (hanc enim significat Hebræum רצון) divinæ erga Christum & Ecclesiam, est tempus placabile, quo Deus placatus & reconci- liatus est per Christum generi humano, puta tempus gratiæ & Evangelii, præsertim id, quod mox Christi mortem consecutum est, in quo vivebant, docebant & convertebant orbem Pau- lus & Apostoli. Sic enim explicat S. Paulus 2. Cor. 6, 2. Tempore accepto exaudivi te & in die salutis adjuvi te. Ecce, nunc tempus accepta- bile, ecce nunc dies salutis. Idem enim est tem- pus acceptabile, quod dies, id est tempus salutis. Et ad illa, ET DEDI TE IN FOEDUS PO- PULI. Ut novum fœdus, pactum & testamentum conderes inter Deum, omnesque gentes, sicut vetus fœdus sanxit Moses inter Deum & Judæos, utque fœdus tua morte & sanguine sancires. Unde secun- do, dedi te in fœdus, id est, in victimam fœderalem, qua placatus Pater, hominibus reconciliatus est, cum iisque fœdus iniit de danda eis salute æterna. Ita Fore- rius. Huic explicationi Cornelii consonat etiam Brentiana in h. l. p. 619. dicens e 2. Cor. 6. ab eo tempore, quo Christus filius Dei homo factus est, & prædicavit Evangelion suum, ac divulgavit illud per Apostolos in totum orbem terræ, revelatum esse tempus acceptum, & diem salutis. Postquam enim venit Christus in hunc Mundum, hoc solum egit, & eo tantum spectavit, ut iram Dei placaret, & humanum genus cum Deo reconciliaret ac libe- raret: Cum igitur Christus filius Dei impetrave- rit precatione sua, non sibi tantum gloriam, verum etiam universæ Ecclesiæ suæ aditum ad Patrem, & patefecerit omnibus credentibus in ipsum januam ad thronum gratiæ: merito sentiendum est, ab eo tempore, quo Christus venit in Mundum, & divul- gavit Evangelion suum in totum orbem terræ, us- que ad finem hujus seculi, tempus esse acceptum, & diem salutis.

Neque vero suscitatio seu restauratio terræ cor- poralis, aut restitutio hæreditatis dissipatæ intelligi- tur, sed ea, quam vers. 6. de Messia prædixerat, quod suscitaturus scil. sit tribus Jacob, & quod deso- lationes Israël conversurus sit per reformationem Ecclesiæ ac immissionem credentium, virtute me- riti & passionis & resurrectionis, in hæreditatis beatæ possessionem, quod per peccatum deperdita erat. Non liberatio corporalis, sed spiritualis eo- rum, qui peccatorum vinculis ligati sunt, & in te- nebris mortis captivi tenentur, ut erepti e potestate tenebrarum in lucis consortium veniant, Col. 1, 20. ac pace conscientiæ & gaudio in S. S. fruantur Rom. 14. Hæc sic recitantur, inquit Brentius, per- inde ac si Filius Dei accepturus esset mundanum im- perium, & restituturus populum suum disjectum aut captivum in terram & libertatem suam. Sed hæc verba intelligenda sunt pro ratione regni Christi. Sic- ut enim regnum Christi non est de hoc mundo, ita ne- que instauratio terræ neque possessio desolatarum he- reditatum, neque liberatio captivorum, sunt mun- dana, sed spiritualia. Christus enim instaurat ter- ram, cum, juxta Paulum, reconciliat Deo Patri cuncta, pacificans per sanguinem crucis suæ, sive quæ in terra sunt, sive quæ in cælis. Possidet hæreditates dissipatas seu desolatas, cum, juxta Amos, suscitat ta- bernaculum Davidis collapsum & reædificat aper- turas murorum ejus: hoc est, cum, juxta Johannem, congregat filios Dei dispersos in unum, ut fiat unus pastor, & unum ovile. Dicit vinctis, Exite, & his, qui in tenebris sunt, Revelemini, cum prædicat Ev- angelion suum de Remissione peccatorum, & divul- gat illud per Apostolos in totum orbem terræ. Vere enim vincti sunt, non, qui catenis in carceribus vin- ciuntur, sed qui peccatorum vinculis sunt obnoxii. Vere in tenebris sunt, non, qui in obscuro & tetro car- cere hujus Mundi sunt conclusi, sed qui propter pec cata sunt in potestate Satanæ & mortis. Evangelion autem adnunciat nobis remissionem peccatorum, & liberationem à Satana & morte propter Christum. Quare solus Christus vere liberat vinctos à captivi- tate, & educit eos, qui in tenebris sunt, ad lucem, illos videlicet, qui Evangelion suum fide accipiunt. Sed quid profuerit multum, è carcere & tenebris li- berari, postea autem famelicum, sitibundum ac omnium rerum egentem errare? Huic autem solici- tudini medetur statim Dominus, cum addit: Super vias pascentur, & in omnibus planis, seu ripis pascua eorum. Hoc est: Ubique in campis obvia erunt irri- gua pascua. Sicut enim pastor ducit oves suas ad loca pascuosa, ita filius Dei pascet liberatos suos abun- dantur, ut non esuriant, nec sitiant, nec percu- tiat eos æstus & Sol: propterea quod is, qui mi- seretur eorum, filius Dei, regit eos, & ducit eos ad fontes aquarum. Non ergo tectura corporis aut pro- tectio adversus æstum Solis, sed refectio spiritualis designatur verbis seqq. ceu finis, cujus gratia ipsa corporalis liberatio promissa, nec tantum ea Ju- dæos attinet in Babyl. captivitate detentos, sed o- mnes eos, qui adducendi erant, & aggregandi ad Ecclesiam Judaicam: quam spiritualem refectio- nem Pastor bonus ille præstat. SUPER VIAS, id est, ubivis locorum PASCENTUR, ET IN O- MNIBUS PLANIS (Ebr. COLLIBUS) PA- SCUA EORUM (quia passim in orbe, N.T. tem- pore Ecclesiæ erunt, quæ verbo Evangelii & Sa- cramento Cœnæ Dominicæ pascentur (NON ESURIENT, NEQUE SITIENT ET NON PERCUTIET EOS ÆSTUS AUT SOL, QUIA MISERATOR EORUM (Filius Dei, qui summa erga ipsos misericordia tan- gitur) REGET SEU DUCET EOS CLE- MENTISSIME, eorumque curam diligentissi- me geret. ET AD FONTES AQUARUM limpidissimos POTABIT (in Ebr. DUCET) eos, ut affatim reficiantur. Quam spiritualem esse refectionem, quæ per S.S. & consolationis Evan- gelicas fit, cum afflictionis æstus sentimus, Matth. 11. Joh. 6. cap 7. ubi ex adverso impii in afflictione fame, siti & æstu deficiunt, desperant & pereunt. Ideo refectio illa plenarie ac perfecta ratione ab hoc miseratore nostro obtinget fidelibus in altera vita. Tum enim electi non esurient, neque sitient am- plius, nec cadet super illos Sol, neque ullus æstus, nulla tum afflictio, nulla tentatio) quoniam agnus, qui in medio throni est, reget illos, & deducet eos ad vitæ fontes aquarum, Apoc. 7, 16. Habemus ergo ex in- terpretatione S.S. omni exceptione majori, quis sit MISERATOR ILLE, qui fideles ducit vigore promissionis Esaiæ, quod nempe sit Agnus, qui in medio throni est, Christus Jesus, Pastor noster opti- mus, Psal. 23. Joh. 10. qui ovibus suis dat vitam æ- ternam. Etiamsi ergo illa resuscitatione terræ, & e- missione è vinculis alludant ad restaurationem Pa- læstinæ, & liberationem è captivitate Babylonica, non tamen hæc alio fine uspiam promissa sunt, quam ut inde salus Domini propagetur ad finem orbis, è Judæa scil. ad universas gentes per totum Orbem; quia pabula in omnibus collibus, & de- ductio ad fontes aquarum non nisi spiritualiter in- telligi possunt, & evidens hicProphetia habetur de vocatione gentium: unde priora etiam de spiritua- li resuscitatione ac liberatione rectissime interpreta- tus est S. Hieronymus: Servavit eum sive plasma- vit Deus morte superata,deditque in fœdus populi Ju- dæorum, his videlicet, qui ex illis credere voluerunt, ut suscitaret terram, quæ in idololatria jacebat erro- ribus, & possideret hæreditates dissipatas sive desertas, quæ habitatorem non habebunt Deum: Et diceret his, qui erant in vinculis: exite: qui peccatorum vinculis astringebantur. Quia funibus peccatorum suorum unusquisque constringitur: & qui erant in te- nebris, revelamini: Qui autem in istiusmodi viis atque semitis pastus fuerit & nutritus, nec esuriet, nec sitiet: neque calorem sentiet Solis; & implebi- tur de illo, quod scriptum est: Per diem Sol non u- ret te, neque luna per noctem: Ut nec adversa nec prospera hujus seculi sentiat. Siquidem misericors & miserator Dominus ipse consolabitur, & reget eos, & deducet ad fontes aquarum, sive potabit illos ad fontes, de quibus scriptum est: Benedicite Domi- no de fontibus Israël. Et in alio loco: Haurite a- quas de fontibus Salvatoris. Hi fontes in Veteri Testamento & Novo sunt. Et Cyrillus: Ubi Chri- sti gratia illuxit, vincula eorum solvit, illustravit cor, inde per omnem viam currere, bonumque men- tis ac intelligentia pabulum colligeres (hoc enim si- gnificat, Pascentur) omnemque semitam probitatis celeriter transire voluerunt, nihilque vetat dicere, quia semita & viæ nostros animos adducunt ad Deum, seu ad sanctam & excellentem vitæ institu- tionem, divinitus inspiratæ Scripturæ: quæ erran- tibus minime fuerunt cognitæ. Postquam autem ad lucem veritatis vocati sunt, suppetebant illis pastus & pascua, quæ spirituali robore nutriunt, omnium- que bonorum desiderio. Promittitque illis Deus gra- tiæ suæ & auxilii, & spiritualis consolationis copiam. Non enim esurient, neque sitient, inquit. Olim enim spiritualis consolationis expertes erant: nec divinam legem habebant, non prophetam, non pædagogum, non magistrum, non Doctorem, non intelligibilium aquarum fontem: At cum à Deo misericordiam con- sequuti sunt, spiritualia bona deinceps affatim suppe- ditabantur, & cibum, qui animos juvat, habuerunt, panem de cælo ederunt, aquam viventem biberunt, de qua etiam ipse Christus dixit ad Samaritanam mulierem verba faciens. Sed nec æstus illos feriet, neque Sol. Factus est enim illis Christus protector, qui etiam olim filiis Israël suspendit interdiu nubem, & noctu in columna ignis præcessit. Itaque, inquit, extra Solem erunt & æstum, id est, tegentur umbra- culo divino, ut nihil contingat, quod sit molestum, vel quod ad pusillanimitatem adducat.

Frivolum ergo & ineptum est, quod istam tan- tam promissionem, quæ se porrigit etiam in alte- ram & beatissimam vitam, Grotius de sola itineris facilitate accipit, quod ad reditum in Judæam nihil defuturum sit Hebræis. Denique quæ de montibus in viam ponendis, & semitis domini exaltandis prædicuntur, ea itidem inepte & frivole ad viam æquam in reditum abripiuntur à Grotio, qui hic nil nisi carnalia & temporali sapit. Viæ semitæque lon- gæ aliæ, viæ nempe legis depressæ semitæ Domini in- telliguntur: quia facit miserator noster, ut in viis justitiæ ambulemus, & pedes nostros dirigit in vias pacis, & semitas mandatorum Domini, ut secun- dum regulam verbi divini incedamus, Gal. 6, 16. ut montes superbiæ & impietatis deprimantur & hu- milientur, ac semitæ depressæ atque humiles, quæ vera pœnitentia contritæ & depressæ sunt, exalten- tur. Aut si de viæ æqualitate, ac itineris facilitate hæc intelligenda, non viæ & semitæ in Judæam, sed ad Ecclesiam designatæ, quia non de corporalibus, sed spiritualibus beneficiis tota promissio agit. Fa- ciam omnia etiam asperioda loca ita petrea, & semi- tas invias ita sternam, ut magna gentium multitudo sit accessura, de qua versus sequentes agunt: Ecce, isti de longe veniunt &c. Quem sensum iterum pro- be expressit Hieronymus. Omnia offendicula, quæ credentium poterant impedire gressus, Dominus eis vertet in planum, & excelsa humiliabit, atque hu- milia sublimabit, ut iter planum habeant, atque cam- pestre. Qui sint autem isti, quibus præparetur via; ponit manifestius: Ecce isti de longe venient. Cal- vinus ipse, etiamsi nonnulla in hac promissione ad corporalem reditum pertrahere nitatur, agno- scit Christi beneficia spiritualia vers. 9. descri- bi: UT DICAT VINCTIS. Describitur, in- quit, his verbis mutatio, quæ Christi adventu con- tigit. Neque tamen dubium est, quin Prophe- ta Judæis solatium afferre velit in rebus perdi- tis, ne restitutio in melius illis sit incredibilis: quia se excidio fere devotos esse videant. Inter- ea in genere ostendit, quale sit officium Christi: ac definit, quod sit restituere hæreditates desolatas. Nam priusquam adveniat Christus, sub misero ju- go vincti, atque in tenebris constituti sumus. His similitudinibus significat, nos, quamdiu caremus Christo, malorum omnium congerie esse obrutos. Nam per TENEBRAS excludit omnia, quae ad re- gnum Christi pertinent, fidem, justitiam, verita- tem, innocentiam & ejusmodi. Sumus ergo in tenebris, donec Christus dicat: OSTENDITE VOS. Sumus vincti, donec dicat, EXITE. Pluri- mum vero inest ponderis in verbo לאמר ut dicas. Ostendit enim praedicationem Evangelii modum esse, quo liberamur. Si ergo libertatem, si lucem regni Dei optamus, audiamus Christum loquen- tem: Alioqui perpetua Satanae tyrannide oppri- memur. Ubi nunc est arbitrii nostri libertas? Quisquis enim sibi lucem aut rationem & intelli- gentiam arrogat, hanc Christi liberationem expe- riri non poterit. Libertas enim non aliis pro- mittitur, nisi qui se captivos esse agnoscunt: Lux & salus, qui se in tenebris demersos esse confitentur. Oecolampadius vero etiam caetere, quae hic haben- tur, beneficia spiritualia concernere agnoscit. Ad verba illa, SVPER VIAS PASCENT, haec anno- tans: Miris & variis hyperbolis fidelium felicitatem describit. Pacifica enim erunt omnia, faecunda & suavia. Unde & Dominus invitat nos dicens: Tol- lite jugum meum, quia jugum meum leve, & onus suave est. Propheta primum ponit abundantiam pascuorum & aquarum. Super vias enim pascent; h. e. ubique invenient pascua: Et super colles erunt pascua, h. e. in locis illis, in quibus alioquin non sunt pascua. Proinde nulla erit fames vel sitis, sed & nul- la adversitas, quia non percutiet aestus persecutionis. Nec mirum, nam Dominus Dux noster erit & juva- bit nos, praeibitque, sicut olim filios Israel exeuntes ex Aegypto antecessit Angelus. Et sicut in deserto ex petra fluxerunt aquae, ita & misericors dominus ad scaturientes & vivas aquas deducet, sicut & Psaltes dicit: Dominus regit me, & nihil mihi deerit, in loco pascuae collocavit me. Super aquam refe- ctionis educavit me. Deerit item labor & fatigatio, montes enim erunt in viam, hoc est plani, ita ut ab- sit omnis difficultas itineris. Ridet hic Judaeus & di- cit: Ubi illa Christianorum felicitas, quorum Chri- stus crucifixus, & Aposti diversis suppliciis affecti, & quibus crucem amplexari prima disciplina est? Quibus respondemus, nos animi, non corporis felici- tatem quaerere, qua & ipsa sequutura est, ubi necesse fuerit. Nihil enim mali a cruce, nam dum externus homo male habet, internus de die in diem innovatur. Sunt autem & nobis pascua, pocula, & panis caelestis, multoque delicatius pascimur quam patres in deserto: nam illi mortui sunt, quisquis autem de nostro pane manducaverit, vivet in aeternum. Scimus enim, quanta nobis promiserit Deus, & ne vacillaremus animo, promissiones illas morte Domini nostri Jesu Christi filii sui obsignavit. Impossibile autem est, quin reficiantur fidelium animi tanti beneficii memo- ria. Sunt & nobis quoque fluenta gratiarum Spirit. Sanct. de quibus inquit Christus: Qui sitit, veniat ad me, & fluent flumina de ventre ejus. Haec vere divi- tiae sunt, quas Spiritus tribuit. In montibus enim afflictionum, plagarum, carcerum, seditionum, labo- rum, vigiliarum, jejuniorum, aliarumque difficulta- tum via nobis facta est, ut feramus omnia in animi lenitate, in Spiritu S. in benignitate, in charitate non simulata, in sermone veritatis, in potentia per arma justitiae, a dextris & sinistris per gloriam & ignomi- niam &c. ut hortatur Apostolus.

## 49:12
Vers. 12.

BEHOLD THESE SHALL COME FROM AFAR) That is, from the East, from Persia and other places situated to the East of Judea: for the following things require this. He speaks of the Hebrews.

AND BEHOLD THESE FROM THE NORTH) From Media, to which many had been deported.

AND FROM THE SEA.) That is, from the West. For the Syrian sea is to the West of Judea. By the sea, understand places across the sea, Cyprus, Crete, Macedonia. AND THESE FROM THE LAND OF THE SOUTH.) In the Hebrew, סינים. Do not think here with some about the Chinese beyond India, who are צינים, not סינים. After the East, the North, the West, the South remained. To the South of Judea are the Sinites, as this Interpreter translated the name סיני in Gen. 10:16, whence the desert region of Sin has its name, and in it Mount Sinai, Exod. 16:1. Grotius does not prove that the Prophet is speaking of the Hebrews. Just as the former benefits were spiritual, so here he designates not the corporal return of the dispersed Hebrews, but the spiritual conversion of both the Hebrews and other peoples throughout the whole world. Therefore, he expresses all four quarters of the world. For the Holy Scriptures are accustomed to describe the conversion of the Gentiles and the kingdom of Christ in this way. See Ps. 72, Is. 43, v. 10, Chap. 60, Zach. 9. Oecolampadius acknowledges this again, whose explanation we add here because of the glosses of Calvin, who dreams of a corporal return with Grotius. At the calling of the Apostles, the bound go forth in the whole world, and migrate to the heavenly Jerusalem, in such a multitude that no one can wonder enough. Behold, he says, those despised ones are present, so eager and so free through the preaching of the Gospel. This is the harvest of which the Lord makes mention in the Gospel, and the fullness of the Gentiles, which has entered in for the ungrateful Jews. He describes, however, the whole earth from the four parts, etc. Which sense the Belgian paraphrasts have also followed, having set aside the authority of their Calvin, as also Piscator in his Biblical Annotations. Nor were the Jews indeed dispersed through the whole world. à Lapide understands with Osorius and Arias Montanus the Chinese, and therefore he thinks and teaches at length that the prophecy is about the most vast and magnificent kingdom of the Chinese, in which Botterus writes are contained over 1150 cities, and are numbered 70 million men, which multitude is not in all of Europe; according to the calculation of Nicolaus Trigautius, they will be 250 million and more: And this is the reason why the Prophet commands the heaven and the earth to exult: PRAISE O HEAVENS AND EXULT O EARTH, SHOUT PRAISE O MOUNTAINS, BECAUSE THE LORD HAS CONSOLED HIS PEOPLE AND WILL HAVE MERCY ON HIS POOR. But if we admit that difference between סינים & צינים entirely, it is manifest that the Chinese are not excluded, nor any peoples, but all from all regions of the world are comprehended, and thus these things cannot be accepted concerning the Jews alone: Nor for the sake of the liberation of the Jews alone from the Babylonian captivity is such great joy, such great exultation of the heavens and the whole earth, of Angels and men proclaimed. For he wishes for the heavens and the elements all tongues, with which they may congratulate men returning from the captivity of sin, as Forerius says. St. Cyril says, He calls heaven and earth into one fellowship, and on account of those who have been saved by Him, he rightly commands a feast to be celebrated. The heavens can be understood, not the element itself, but those who dwell in the highest habitations, and have been enriched with a heavenly dwelling, and the holy powers, Principalities, Thrones, Dominions, and those which are beyond the Seraphim. The earth likewise, those who in it await that His apparition will be, and who know that He is to be present, to redeem the Israelites and all nations dwelling in the whole earth. God has had mercy on His people, and has comforted the humble of His people. For He has had mercy on all, when Christ had shone upon them. Since it is true, they were snatched from the hand of the devil, and the cruelty of demons, and from sin which exercised tyranny over them, to be liberated, and moreover from the bonds of death, and gifted with grace, and made partakers of the excellent gift of the Holy Spirit, and illuminated by the glory of adoption, and enriched with hope, which surpasses mind and thought. But observe the Prophet's admonition, for he says: He has comforted the humble of his people. We call those humble who submit a flexible and tractable neck to Christ, and do not despise the yoke of his kingdom, because they have admitted the faith, and are prepared to offer him adoration and worship in spirit and in truth: whereas those who have not admitted the faith are not humble, but raise their horn on high, and speak in righteousness against him, and lift up the proud neck of their mind, as it were, against his sacrosanct prophecies. These are not gifted with spiritual consolation, for they were not worthy. Jerome has it thus: It is commanded to the heavens and the earth, or to those powers which dwell in heaven and earth: or to Angels and men, that they sing the praises of God. And those who are placed in the height of virtues, testify to the joy of their mind with jubilation and exultation: Because the Lord has comforted his people. Those who were willing to believe from among the Jews. And he has had mercy on his poor and humble ones, or on all his people, who from the east and west, north and south, have been called to him. Having neither the law nor the Prophets, nor spiritual riches, but deserted, poor, and humble, they were subject to all demons. Grotius himself acknowledges at Luke 2:14 that this exhortation pertains to the redemption of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ECCE ISTI DE LONGE VENIENT) Id est, ab Oriente, a Perside & aliis locis ad Orientem Judaeae sitis: nam hoc sequentia requirunt. De Hebraeis loquitur.

ET ECCE ILLI AB AQUILONE) Ex Media, quo multi erant deportati.

ET MARI.) Id est, ab Occidente, Nam mare Sy- riacum ad Occidentem Judaeæ. Per mare intellige loca transmarina, Cyprum, Cretam, Macedoniam. ET ISTI DE TERRA AUSTRALI.) In Hebræo. סינים. Noli hic cum quibusdam cogitare de Sinenfibus ultra Indiam, qui sunt צינים, non סינים. Post or- tum, Septentrionem, Occidentem, restabat Auster. Ad Austrum Judaeæ sunt Sinæi, ut hic Interpres nomen סיני transtulit Gen. 10, 16. unde nomen habet deserta Regio Sin, & in ea mons Sinai Exod. 16, 1. De Hebræis loqui Prophetam dicit, non pro- bat Grotius. Ut priora beneficia spiritualia erant, ita hic non corporalem Hebræorum dispersorum reditum, sed spiritualem conversionem tum Ebræo- rum tum aliorum populorum per universum or- bem designat. Ideo omnes quatuor mundi plagas exprimit. Solet enim ita conversionem gentium, & regnum Christi describere S. S. Vid. Ps. 72. Es. 43. v. 10. Cap. 60. Zach. 9. Agnofcit id iterum Oeco- lampadius, cujus explicationem ob glossas Calvi- ni, hic corporalem reditum somniantis cum Gro- tio, adjicimus. Ad vocationem Apostolorum vin- cti in toto orbe exeunt, & migrat ad cœlestem Hiero- salem, tanta multitudine, ut nemo satis mirari queat. Ecce, inquit, illi contempti prædicatione Evangelii tam alacres, tamque liberi adsunt. Hæc est messis, cu- jus Dominus in Evangelio meminit, & plenitudo gentium, quæ pro ingratis Judæis subintravit. Descri- bit autem terram universam à quatuor partibus &c. Quem sensum posthabita Calvini sui autoritate e- tiam sequuti sunt paraphrastæ Belgici, ut & Piscator in Annot. Bibl. Neque vero Judæi dispersi fuere per totum terrarum orbem. Corn. à Lapide intelligit cum Osorio & Ariemontano per סינים Sinenses, adeoque censet ac prolixe docet; prophetiam esse de vastissimo & magnifico regno Sinarum, in quo Botterus scribit contineri supra 1150. urbes, & numerari 70. Milliones hominum, quæ multitudo non est in tota Eu- ropa, juxta Nicolai a. Trigautii computum 250. mil- liones erunt & amplius : Et hæc causa est, cur cœlum & terram exultare jubeat Propheta : LAUDATE COELI ET EXULTA TERRA, JUBILA- TE MONTES LAUDEM, QUIA CON- SOLATUS EST DOMINUS POPULUM SUUM ET PAUPERUM SUORUM MISERE- BITUR. Sed si differentiam illam inter סינים & צינים omnino admittamus, manifestum est, non excludi Sinenses, nec ullos populos, sed omnes ab omnibus plagis mundi comprehendi, adeoque de Judæis solis hæc accipi non posse: Neque ob solam liberationem Judæorum è captivitate Babylonica tanta lætitia, tanta exultatio cœlorum & universæ terræ, Angelorum & hominum indicitur. Optat enim cœlis & elementis omnes linguas, quibus congra- tulentur hominibus è captivitate peccati redeunti- bus, ut ait Forerius. S. Cyrillus, Cœlum, inquit, & terram in unum sodalitium convocat, & propter eos, qui ab illo servati sunt, festum celebrare optime præ- cipit. Cœli intelligi possunt, non ipsum elementum, sed qui in summis habitaculis commorantur, & cœle- sti locupletati sunt domicilio, & sanctæ potestates, Principatus, Throni, Dominationes, & quæ sunt ul- tra Seraphim. Terra similiter qui in ea expectant fore ejus apparitionem, & qui norunt illum affore, ad redimendum Israëlitas omnesque gentes in universa terra degentes. Misertus est Deus populi sui, & hu- miles populi sui consolatus est. Misertus est enim omnium, cum illis Christus illuxerat. Siquidem verum est, erepti sunt à manu diaboli, & sævitia dæ- moniorum, & à peccato quod in eos tyrannidem exer- cuit, liberari, & mortis insuper vinculis, donatique gratia, & excellenti dono sancti spiritus facti partici- pes, & adoptionis gloria illustrati, & spe, quæ mentem ac cogitationem superat, ditati. Verum observa ser- monem Prophetæ, ait enim: Humiles populi sui consolatus est. Humiles esse dicimus eos, qui flexi- le & tractabile collum submittunt Christo, & jugum regni ejus non contemnunt, eo quod fidem admiserunt, ac præparati sunt, in spiritu ac veritate adorationem & cultum ei præstare: cum hi qui fidem non admise- rant, non sint humiles, sed cornu in altum erigant, & in justitiam contra eum loquantur, & contra sacro- sancta ejus vaticinia superbam velut cervicem men- tis attollunt. Hi non sunt donati spirituali consola- tione, non enim erant digni. Hieronymus ita ha- bet: Præcipitur cælis & terræ, vel his virtutibus, quæ in cælo morantur & terræ : vel Angelis & homini- bus, ut Dei concinant laudes. Et qui in excelso virtu- tum positi sunt, mentis lætitiam jubilo & exultatione testantur : Quia consolatus est Dominus populum suum. Eos qui ex Judæis credere voluerunt. Et pauperum humiliumque suorum misertus est, sive omnis populi sui, qui de oriente & occidente, aquilone & austro, ad eum vocatus est. Non habens legem nec Prophetas, nec divitias spirituales, sed desertus, pau- per & humilis cunctis dæmonibus subjacebat. Agno- scit Grotius ipse ad Luc. 2, 14. hanc exhortationem pertinere ad redemtionem Christi.

## 49:14
Vers. 14. AND SION SAID.) He addresses the destroyed city of Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DIXIT SION. ) Urbi Hierosolymo- rum destructæ dat sermonem.

## 49:15
AND IF SHE SHALL HAVE FORGOTTEN) That is, Be it so: let this be possible.

Latin:

ET SI ILLA OBLITA FUERIT) Id est, Esto ta- men: possit hoc fieri.

## 49:16
Vers. 16. BEHOLD I HAVE DESCRIBED THEE IN MY HANDS) Those who wished to remember some business were accustomed to place some sign of it on one of their fingers. See Exod. 13:9.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ECCE IN MANIBUS MEIS DESCRI- PSI TE ) Solebant qui negotii alicujus meminisse vole- bant, signum ejus aliquod apponere digitorum alicui. Vide Exod. 13, 9.

## 49:17
V. 17. THY BUILDERS HAVE COME.) In Hebrew: They hasten. Cyrus will command this immediately.

THE DESTROYERS AND WASTERS SHALL GO FORTH FROM THEE) The Babylonians shall be far from thee, they shall be able to do thee no harm, nor shall Sanballat and Tobias the Ammonite any more.

Latin:

V. 17. VENERVNT STRVCTORES TVI.) In Hebr. Festinant. Jamjam Cyrus id præcipiet.

DESTRVENTES ET DISSIPANTES A TE EXIBVNT) Longe erunt à te Babylonii, nihil nocere tibi poterunt, nec magis Samballetes, & Tobias Ammanita.

## 49:18
ALL THESE ARE GATHERED TOGETHER) All these who are in exile through all the lands of the Assyrians, Medes, Babylonians, and Persians, that huge multitude.

THEY HAVE COME TO THEE) They shall come to thee immediately.

WITH ALL THESE THOU SHALT BE CLOTHED AS WITH AN ORNAMENT, AND SHALT BIND THEM ABOUT THEE, AS A BRIDE.) Just as brides are accustomed to be decorated with beautiful garments and necklaces, so their excellent virtues shall decorate thee.

That these things were said to a desolate city had to be proven, which the Chaldean Interpreter and Sanctius the Jesuit indeed believed, even though they also refer these things mystically to Christ thus far. But others have interpreted them of the Church, and have wished them to be understood of the times of the New Testament, even as regards the literal sense: that much more august things are said than can suit carnal Jews, Corn. à Lapide says, although he admits that they are alluded to: who, with Forerius and others, thinks that by Sion the Jews are designated, but those who are pious and believe in Christ. Leo Castrius determines this voice to be the complaint of the Church, and of the time of the persecution of the Apostles. Others commonly understand the Church sustaining affliction, which God here wished to raise up with consolation. Calvin, although he does not deny that the reduction of the Jews is looked to, nevertheless judges that the promise looks more broadly, and that it is only alluded to by way of similitude; he uses, he says, the similitude of a devastated city, whose walls and buildings are restored, to which the citizens return in such great numbers that its boundaries must be extended, because the former circuit cannot contain them all. He therefore understands not only the reduction of the people from Babylon, but the restitution which was made through Christ: when, namely, the Church was propagated far and wide not only through Judea, but also through the whole world. He also adds that protection will be ready if any enemies should infest it: indeed, that it will be quiet from their injuries and troubles, because God will drive them far away: not that the Church has ever been entirely peaceful and immune from all hostile violence: but yet God, sparing the infirmity of His own, has restrained the impious and repressed or scattered their attacks, so that the kingdom of Satan might not grow from the ruins of the Church. Similarly, the explanation of Oecolampadius also holds this, as does that of Zwingli, who, at v. 22, 'Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations,' observes that this is an irrefutable passage for the calling of the Gentiles; likewise Piscator, and also the Belgian Paraphrasts at v. 16, noting that this is the meaning: just as I am about to rebuild the wall destroyed by the Chaldeans, so too will I build up and guard the spiritual Jerusalem, my Church, which is now small and almost entirely collapsed. Our own people agree in this explanation; Brentius, who excellently, according to his custom, carries out this meaning, and Osiander, who likes to follow him in most things in his paraphrase: as well as D. Pappus, the Vinarian Paraphrast, and others. Which Megalander Luther also set forth brilliantly: 'Zion and those who are truly in the Church, and have the Gospel, and such an abundance of promises, cry out that they have been forsaken by God.' Nor did the pious Ancients understand it otherwise. Illustrious is the exposition of Jerome, who first unfolds the homonymy of the word Sion, noting (1.) Jerusalem, as in Matt. 23, Luke 21, in which sense he asserts the Jews take that word in this place. (2.) The congregation of the saints, who, established in the peace of the Lord and in the watchtower of mighty works, are rightly called Sion, of which it is said in Ps. 84: 'Its foundations are on the holy mountains; the Lord loves the gates of Sion more than all the tabernacles of Jacob.' For the foundations of the Jewish Sion, which we see is destroyed, were not loved by the LORD, or that which is loved by the LORD cannot be destroyed. (3.) The heavenly Jerusalem, of which in Heb. 12: 'You have come to Mount Sion, etc.' He adds (4.) that the Jews and Judaizing Christians, according to the Apocalypse of John, which they do not understand, imagine a golden and jeweled Jerusalem. Afterwards, he carefully weighs what Sion said: 'The Lord has forsaken me.' And he explains it concerning Sion according to the other meaning of the word, i.e., the spiritual: 'And there is no doubt,' he says, 'that the congregation of the Saints, which had been earlier among the Jews and was forsaken by the Lord, commemorates this and complains with a tearful voice that it is deserted and destitute of the Lord's help.' To which God responds, using a natural comparison: 'If it is possible for a mother to forget her infant and not be moved with mercy for the fruit of her womb, yet I will not forget you.' I will say something more: and if she should have forgotten, overcoming the hardness of her mind against the laws of nature, I nevertheless will not forget my creature, and I will always keep the souls of the saints in my heart. Know also, you who think yourself utterly forsaken, that you are described and depicted in my hands, and that your walls remain continually before my eyes: from which we learn that Jerusalem is by no means to be sought in the region of Palestine, which is the worst of the whole province, and is roughened by rocky mountains, and suffers from a shortage of water, so that it uses heavenly rains and is accustomed to compensate for the rarity of springs by the construction of cisterns, but in the hands of God, to which it is said: 'Your builders have hastened.' Or according to the LXX: 'You shall be quickly built up, by those by whom you had been destroyed.' For it was destroyed by the Jews, and built up by the Jews. Which, having been deserted due to the fault of the scribes and Pharisees, was gathered at the preaching of the Apostles of Christ, as much from the Jews as from the Gentiles. Cyril agrees, whose explanation is worthy of being added, because it also sheds light on Sion in other places. The Savior and Lord of all proposed, even before others, to the children of Sion, or those of the blood of Israel, grace through faith, and with infinite discourses he endeavored to convince them, so that they might seize the opportunity by which they could, if they had believed in him, be enriched. But these were stubborn, and disobedient, and having despised the laws which were described by the most wise Moses, and having neglected the prophetic preachings, they fell from the faith, and by the crime of the Lord others were taken as if in a snare. For this reason they fell, and were alienated far from the conjunction which is with Him. not perish utterly. However, few were saved, and in comparison to the multitude of the unfaithful, very few. Therefore, Zion, bearing the person of the mother of Judea, is now introduced almost, and mourns as if despised by God who casts her off. Hence, with very few children left to her, she says: The Lord has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me. And what does the Lord say to these things? He declares an incomparable love for men, and promises the goods of mercy to the intelligible Zion, and endeavors to persuade her that He could not at any time forget His own creation. For just as a woman who has given birth cannot forget her children, as one who has the law of nature as the dispenser and administrator of the highest piety and indulgence: so, He says, I cannot forget mine: since they surpass and supereminently exceed the affection and maternal indulgence, which are divine things. That one, however, it is not inconsistent that she could come into forgetfulness. But for Me, it is not right to suffer this. Therefore, the speech is as if from the earthly Zion, or the mother of the Jews, who has suffered either the sterility or the paucity of children, but the promise is as if to the intelligible Zion, to whom the most wise Paul says those who have believed have approached: so that you may understand the Church gathered from the Gentiles and Jews, having the type of the one above. And afterwards to the words: Lift up your eyes on every side. In the whole holy and divinely inspired Scripture it is clearly said that the portion and lot of Christ are those who are sprung from Israelitic blood or the children of the earthly Zion, in the extreme times of the age. For they shall return, He says, to the Lord their God, and to David their King. And they shall be amazed at the Lord, and at His goods, in the last days. For the Church of the Gentiles, which we also say is the intelligible Zion, has entered in while they were disbelieving. But they also shall be called, and there shall be one fold, one shepherd, so that two Zions may no longer be named, but both may be consummated into one Church, subjected to the hand of one supreme shepherd.

This exposition of the Christian Church certainly ought not to have been postponed to Rabbinical glosses. And Grotius could have seen even from these words, which were applied primarily for the consolation of Zion: Lift up your eyes in a circle, and see; all these are gathered, the sons have come, that the discourse is not about the earthly Jerusalem, and its rebuilding, but about the spiritual one, and its enlargement through the calling of the Gentiles, especially because God Himself added an interpretation clearer than the sun: Behold I lift up my hand to the Gentiles, and I will exalt my sign to the people, and they shall bring your sons in their arms and your daughters they shall carry upon their shoulders. And Kings shall be your nursing fathers, and Queens your nursing mothers. But to Grotius even the clearest things are opaque, because his mind is blinded, as is that of the Jews, so that he does not see the clarity of the Gospel. For how could the calling of the Gentiles to the kingdom of Christ have been expressed more clearly! And therefore it is certain and immovable that these things are not to be understood with the Jews concerning the corporal Zion and its destruction, but concerning the spiritual one, which, when it seems deserted—which happened not only in the Babylonian captivity, but also when Antiochus Epiphanes was raging against Israel, and especially in the time of Herod, when the polity was oppressed by his tyranny, and the ecclesiastical state of the Pharisees and Sadducees was most corrupted by abominations, and very few faithful remained, as if God had utterly forgotten His Zion, which moreover happened and will happen to the same in persecutions under Ethnic Emperors, under the Arian, under the Anti-Christ until the final liberation—is never not raised up by the Lord with this most sweet consolation, which, however, we judge with Cyril and Jerome, and other Doctors in the Greek and Latin Church, to look primarily to Zion at the time of the coming of Christ, when she was most deserted, since the sequence of the text and the harmony of events confirm this. We do not doubt, however, that the Prophet alluded to the aforementioned liberation from captivity in other prophecies, and the rebuilding of Zion, which most interpreters acknowledge and which was also observed by the ancients, especially Jerome and Cyril of Alexandria, because the words of the Prophet imply it: which we wish to be understood in such a way that the single literal sense concerning the spiritual Zion remains safe, which we have shown thus far to be the genuine one here, to which this verse 16, BEHOLD I HAVE DESCRIBED YOU UPON MY HANDS, corresponds, not equally to the earthly Zion. For not only is that memorial sign expressed by that phrase, of the kind that used to be placed on the fingers as Grotius wishes, but primarily the special love of God proper to the faithful. The reason for the place in Ex. 13:9 is different; there a sign is held in the hand; here no mention of a sign is made, but of a sculpture; and some think it alludes to rings, in which the image of the one who was dearly loved was accustomed to be worn. See Jerome on Dan. 3. Therefore, it is not a bare remembrance, but the care of the faithful, whom God carries inscribed in His hand, so that He may never forget them, that is to be understood. Whence some, with Procopius, understand the inscription in the book of life, which is in the hand of God, as proper to the elect. And the other phrase also implies this: YOUR WALLS ARE PERPETUALLY BEFORE ME. He uses, says Brentius, according to custom, those words by which the external Zion is accustomed to be described, when nevertheless He understands the spiritual Zion, and signifies that the care of the salvation and preservation of His Church is so meditated upon and fixed in Him, that it can never be deserted from His mind. The Holy Spirit shadowed forth this same thing in the two onyx stones, in which the names of the children of Israel were sculpted, and which Aaron carried before the Lord on both shoulders for a memorial. The same was also foreshadowed by the twelve gems, enclosed in the rational or breastplate of Judgment, which, marked with the twelve names of the sons of Israel, Aaron, when about to enter the Sanctuary, was accustomed to wear affixed to his breast: a memorial, as Scripture speaks in Ex. 28, before the Lord forever. For this ornament was instituted in the ministry of the Priesthood, not because God was delighted or appeased by it in Himself: But so that the Church might be admonished that it is not only always a care to God, but is esteemed more precious than all gems before Him. And as the names of the sons of Israel inscribed on the gems could not be erased, unless the gems were broken: so it cannot happen that the Church should be abolished from the mind of God. B. Luther notes the emphasis, that it is said before MY eyes, not yours. For we do not perceive that we are exposed to men, demons, sins, death, and hell; therefore they are invisible walls and only believable. Sectarians see their walls, Tyrants see their walls. This sense must be changed, that their walls are nothing, because they are before the eyes of men, but ours are before the eyes of God. Cyril says that we are described in the hand of the Lord through the passion of Christ, which is certainly most true by reason of the MERIT of this inscription. The passion of Christ, he says, and the precious cross and the affixing of His hands was a security, and an inaccessible and unbroken wall to those who have believed in Him: Therefore He could rightly say: Behold, I have painted your walls upon my hands. You will understand by my passion, or that passion is signified by this one thing, I have fashioned he said, and you are always before me. For if he suffered for us, how could he forget us? Or how could they not be in his eyes, for whose sake he was affixed to the wood? Whence Augustine in Soliloquies, ch. 2: Your hands, he says, O Lord, have made me and fashioned me: those hands, I say, which were affixed to the nails for me; do not despise the work of your hands, O Lord, I pray that you look upon the wounds of your hands. Because in your hands, O Lord, you have described me: Read the writing itself and save me. Compare also Ambrose, book VI, Hexaemeron, ch. 5.

Now as far as the Builders are concerned, v. 17, it does not appear how the architects and restorers of the physical Zion are to be understood. For it was not of such amplitude and capacity that it could receive the nations from all the regions of the world. Therefore, the Apostles and other spiritual architects under the New Testament are understood, 1 Cor. 3, although in the meantime we do not deny that there is an allusion to the Zion destroyed by the Chaldeans, which it had been predicted elsewhere would be restored, just as it may be admitted that under the name of the destroyers and dissipators, reference is made to Sanballat and men of a similar stamp, who were obstructing the structure, i.e. (which Cornel. à Lapide's explanation is consistent with most others) I see, as once so now, the ruins of your walls, O Zion; I know what needs to be done; I discern your enemies, Scribes, Pharisees, Emperors and tyrants, apostates and heretics, who go out from you and are deserters to the enemy; who want to destroy, dissipate, and overturn you. But I will avert them, or restrain them, or certainly ensure that they do not hinder your structure, but rather promote it. Whence the LXX translate, quickly you have been built, by whom you were destroyed. For the Jews, and especially the Emperors, persecuting the Church, later converted to it, propagated it all the more. So did Saul, when he became Paul. So did the Emperor Constantine and his successors. Thus explain St. Jerome, Cyril, Augustine, Tertullian, Justinian, and from them Leo Castrius. He says the same and amplifies it in the following. the Prophet, so clearly that St. Augustine, Tertullian, and Origen assert that it does not need interpretation. Cyril explains the adornment of the Bride thus: I will clothe you with all of them as with the adornment of a Bride. For the ornament of the Churches is the gathered multitude. For that reason, divinely inspired Scripture is accustomed to adorn the Church with golden and variegated clothing. For just as various and most precious species of stones, I say Indian ones, adhering to golden rules, add a certain admirable and visible ornament: So also the souls of the saints, decorated with the insignia of virtues, shine with most splendid beauty in the eyes of the divinity, so that everyone gives thanks to Christ and says: Let my soul exult in the Lord. For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and has surrounded me with the bridal ornament of the tunic of joy, and has placed a mitre upon me as if I were a bride. What Grotius says about the dispersed Israelites and their huge multitude, which went into exile through the various nations of the Assyrians, Medes, Babylonians, and Persians, does not conform to the truth of history: for those transported by the Assyrians did not return, and it cannot be taught that the Jews were then in exile in Persia or among the Medes when the Babylonian captivity was dissolved, so that such a great multitude flowed from there to restore the city, nor do they agree with the present prophecy, because here the Prophet prophesies not about the Jews, but about the nations being summoned to Zion, as the subjoined exegesis testifies. Concerning this prophecy, however, one may also compare Sermon XV in memory of the Just, Wittenberg, where from v. 14, 15, the more than fatherly mercy of God is set forth, the comfort of the weeping and deserted.

Latin:

OMNES ISTI CONGREGATI SVNT) Omnes isti, qui per omnes terras, Assyriorum, Medorum, Babylo- niorum, Persarum exsulant, ingens illa multitudo.

VENERVNT TIBI ) Jamjam venient ad te.

OMNIBVS HIS VELVT ORNAMENTO VE- STIERIS, ET CIRCVMDABIS EOS TIBI, QVASI SPONSA. ) Sicut vestibus speciosis & monilibus deco- rari sponsæ solent, sic illorum egregiæ virtutes te decora- bunt.

Desolatæ urbi hæc dici probandum erat, quod Chaldæus quidem Interpres & Sanctius Jesuita cen- fuerunt, etsi hi etiam mystice ad Christum hactenus referant. Sed alii de Ecclesia interpretati sunt, ac de temporibus Nov. Test. etiam intellectum vo- luerunt, quoad sensum literalem: multo augustiora dici,quam ut carnalibus Judæis conveniant, Corn. à Lapid. ait, etsi ad illos alludi fateatur : Qui cum Fo- rerio & aliis per Sion Judæos, sed in Christum cre- dentes & pios designari putat. Leo Castrius vo- cem hanc querulam Ecclesiæ, & Apostolorum tempore persequutionis esse statuit. Alii com- muniter Ecclesiam afflictionem sustinentem intelli- gunt, quam Deus hic solatio erigere voluerit. Cal- vinus, etsi ad reductionem Judæorum respici non abnuta, latius tamen promissionem spectare, & ad illum tantum per similitudinem alludi censet; uti- tur, inquit, similitudine urbis vastatæ, cujus muri & ædificia instaurantur, ad quam cives tam magno nu- mero redeunt, ut dilatanda sint ejus pomæria, quod prior ambitus omnes continere nequeat. Non solum ergo intelligit reductionem populi è Babylone, sed resti- tutionem, quæ per Christum facta est : cum sc. Ecclesia non tantum per Judæam, sed etiam per universum or- bem longe lateque propagata est. Addit etiam, præsi- dium fore paratum, si qui eam hostes infestent: imo quietam fore ab eorum injuriis & molestiis, quia Deus procul ipsos abiget: non quod Ecclesia unquam in totum pacata fuerit, & ab omni hostili violentia immunis: Sed tamen Deus suorum infirmitati par- cens impios prohibuit, eorumque impetus repressit, aut discussit, ne saltem ex Ecclesiæ ruinis regnum Satanæ cresceret. Similiter etiam habet Oecolampadii ex- plicatio, ut & Zvinglii, qui ad v. 22. Ecce levabo ma- num meam ad gentes, observat, irrefragabilem hunc esse locum vocationis gentium, Piscatoris item nec non Paraphrastarum Belgicorum ad v. 16. notan- tium hunc esse sensum : sicut murus à Chaldæis de- structos ædificaturus sum, ita & spiritualem Hieroso- lymam, Ecclesiam meam, quæ nunc exigua & fere to- ta collapsa est, exstruam & custodiam. In hac ex- plicatione conveniunt Nostrates ; Brentius, qui e- gregie pro more suo hunc sensum exequitur, & Osiander, qui illum in plerisque in paraphrasi sua sequi amat : Nec non D. Pappus, Paraphrasta Vina- riens. & alii. Quam etiam Megalander Lutherus præclare tradidit : Zion & ii qui vere sunt in Ec- clesia, & habent Evangelium, & tantam promissio- num opulentiam, clamant se derelictos à Deo esse. Neque aliter accepere pii Veteres. Illustris est Hie- ronymi expositio, qui evolvit primum ὁμωνυμίαν vocis Sion, quod notet (1.) Hierosolymam, ut Matth. 23. Luc. 21. quo sensu Judæos accipere illam vocem hoc in loco asserit. (2.) Sanctorum congregationem, qui in pace Domini, & in virtutum specula constituti recte vocantur Sion, de qua dicitur Pf. 84. Funda- menta ejus in montibus sanctis, diligit Dominus portas Sion super omnia tabernacula Jacob. Ne- que enim fundamenta Judaicæ Sion, quam vide- mus esse destructam, à DOMINO sunt dilecta, aut quod à DOMINO dilectum est, destrui po- test. (3.) Cælestem Hierosolymam, de qua Ebr. 12. Accessistis ad montem Sion &c. Addit (4.) Ju- dæos & Christianos Judaizantes juxta Apocalypsin Johannis, quam non intelligunt, auream & gemma- tam Hierosolymam fingere. Postea diligentius ex- pendit, quænam Sion dixerit : Dereliquit me Do- minus : Et de Sione juxta alteram vocis significa- tionem, h. e. spirituali explicat : Nec dubium est, in- quit, quin congregatio Sanctorum quæ prior fuerat in Judæis & à Domino derelicta est, ista commemoret & voce lacrymabili conqueratur se esse desertam & Do- mini auxilio destitutam. Cui respondit Deus natu- rali utens similitudine : Si potest fieri, ut mater sui obliviscatur infantis & ad partum viscerum suorum non flectatur misericordia, & ego obliviscar tui. Plus aliquid dicam : & si illa oblita fuerit vincens mentis duritia jura naturæ, ego tamen non oblivi- scar creaturam meam, & sanctorum animas sem- per in meo corde retinebo. Scito etiam tu, quæ te penitus arbitraris derelictam, in meis descriptam esse manibus atque depictam, & muros tuos coram oculis meis jugiter permanere : Ex quo discimus, nequaquam Hierusalem in Palestinæ regione quæren- dam, quæ totius provinciæ deterrima est, & saxosis montibus asperatur, & penuriam patitur sitis, ita ut cælestibus utatur pluviis, & raritatem fontium ci- sternarum exstructione soletur sed in Dei manibus, ad quam dicitur : Festinaverunt structores tui : Sive juxta LXX : Cito ædificaberis, à quibus destructa fueras. A Judæis enim destructa, à Judæis ædifica- ta est. Quæ ob culpam scribarum Pharisæorumque deserta, ad prædicationem Apostolorum Christi con- gregata est, tam de Judæis, quam de gentibus. Conci- nit Cyrillus, cujus explicatio digna est, quæ adjicia- tur, quod aliis locis deSione etiam lucem affundat. Proposuit universorum Servator & Dominus etiam ante alios, filiis Sion, seu ex sanguine Israel, gratiam per fidem, & infinitis sermonibus fidem illis conatus est facere, ut apprehenderent opportunitatem, qua pos- sent, si in illum credidissent, gloria patribus promissa locupletari. At hi refracti erant, & inobedientes, & legibus, quæ per sapientissimum Mosen descriptæ erant, despectis, & propheticis prædicationibus negle- ctis, à fide exciderunt, & crimine Domini alii, tan- quam laqueo capti sunt. Hac de causa lapsi sunt, & à conjunctione, quæ cum ipso est, procul sunt alienati. Reliquiæ tamen servatæ sunt, & funditus Israël non periit. Cæterum pauci sunt servati, & præ infide- lium multitudine omnino pauci. Perscite itaque Sion Judææ matris personam sustinens, nunc introdu- citur propemodum, & luget quasi despecta à Deo ex- plodente. Hinc paucissimis ipsi relictis liberis, dicit: Dereliquit me Dominus, & Dominus oblitus est mei. Et quid ad hæc Dominus? Incomparabilem in homines charitatem declarat, & Sioni intelligibili misericordiæ bona promittit, & quod non posset ali- quando sui figmenti oblivisci, conatur persuadere. Quemadmodū enim mulier, quæ peperit, suorum liberorum oblivisci non potest, ut quæ legem na- turæ habet summæ pietatis & indulgentiæ dispen- satricem & administratricem: sic, inquit, ego meo- rum oblivisci nequeo: siquidem affectum indulgen- tiamque maternam, quæ divina sunt, superant & su- pereminent. Illa autem, non dissentaneum, quin in ob- livionem venire possit. Me autem hoc pati fas non est. Itaque oratio est, velut à terrestri Sion, seu Ju- dæorum matre, quæ vel sterilitatem vel paucitatem liberorum passa est, promissio autem est velut ad in- telligibilem Sion, ad quam sapientissimus Paulus dicit accessisse eos, qui crediderunt: ut ex gentibus & Ju- dæis coactam Ecclesiam intelligas, typum habentem superioris. Et postea ad verba: Attolle undique oculos tuos. In tota sancta & divinitus inspirata Scriptura clare dictum est, portionem & sortem Christi esse sanguine Israëlitico oriundos seu terrenæ Sion liberos, in extremis seculi temporibus. Reverten- tur enim, inquit, ad Dominum Deum suum, & ad David Regem suum. Et stupebunt in Domino, & in bonis ejus, postremis diebus. Subingressa est enim illis diffitentibus Ecclesia gentium, quam e- tiam intelligibilem Sion esse dicimus. Vocabuntur autem & illi, eritque unum ovile, unus pastor, ut non amplius duæ Sion nominentur, sed ambæ in unam con- summentur Ecclesiam, unius summi pastoris manui subditam.

Hæc expositio Ecclesiæ Christianæ non de- bebat certe posthaberi glossis Rabbinicis. Et vi- dere poterat Grotius vel ex istis verbis, quæ conso- latione Sionis imprimis adhibita sunt: Leva in cir- cuitu oculos tuos, & vide; omnes isti congregati sunt, venerunt filii, quod non de terrena Hierosolyma, ejusque reædificatione, sed de spirituali, ejusdem- que ampliatione per vocationem gentium sermo fit, maxime quia Deus ipse interpretationem adje- cit Sole clariorem: Ecce levo ad gentes manum meam, & ad populum exaltabo signum meum, & af- ferent filios tuos ulnis & filias tuas super humeros portabunt. Et erunt Reges nutritii tui, & Reginæ nu- trices tuæ. Sed Grotio clarissima etiam sunt opaca, quia excæcata mens ipsi, ut Judæis, quo minus vi- deat claritatem Evangelii. Quomodo enim lu- culentius exprimi poterat gentium ad regnum Christi vocatio! Ideoque certum atque immotum est, non cum Judæis de Zione corporali, ejusque ex- structione hæc accipienda esse, sed de spirituali, quæ ubi deserta videtur, quod non tantum in Baby- lonica captivitate accidit, sed etiam cum Antiochus Epiphanes grassaretur in Israël, & cumprimis Hero- dis tempore, cum politia ab hujus tyrannide op- pressa, Ecclesiasticus status Pharisæorum & Sadu- cæorum βδελύγμασι maxime corruptus esset, ac paucissimi superessent fideles, quasi Sionis suæ obli- tus fuerit Deus penitus, quod insuper in persequu- tionibus sub Ethnicis Imperatoribus, sub Ariana, sub Anti-Christo eidem evenit & eveniet usque ad fi- nalem liberationem, à Domino nunquam non eri- gitur hac suavissima consolatione, quam tamen ad Sionem tempore adventus Christi maxime deser- tam imprimis spectare cum Cyrillo & Hieronymo, aliisque in Græca, & Latina Ecclesia Doctoribus censemus, siquidem id textus συνέχεια & eventus harmonia confirmet. Non dubitamus tamen al- lusisse Prophetam ad prædictam in aliis vaticiniis li- berationem è captivitate, & reædificationem Zionis, quod plerique agnoscunt Interpp. & à veteribus quoque observatum, Hieronymo imprimis ac Cyril- lo Alexandr. quia verba Prophetæ id inferunt:quod vero ita intellectum volumus, ut salvus maneat li- teralis sensus unicus de Sione spirituali, quem ge- nuinum hic esse hactenus ostendimus, cui istud v. 16. ECCE IN MANIBUS TUIS DESCRI- PSI TE, convenit, non æque Sioni terrenæ. Nam non solum exprimitur phrasi illa signum memoriale cujusmodi digitis apponi solebat ut Grotius vult, sed imprimis specialis Dei dilectio fidelium propria. Alia loci Ex. 13, 9. ratio est, ibi habetur signum in manu; hic nulla signi mentio fit, sed sculpturæ; & alludi censent nonnulli ad annulos, in quibus imago ejus, qui impense diligebatur, geri consuevit. Vid. Hie- ronymus in Dan. 3. Itaque non nuda recordatio, sed cura fidelium, quos in manu sua gerit insculptos Deus, ut nunquam eorum obliviscatur, intelligen- da. Unde nonnulli cum Procopio inscriptionem in librum vitæ, qui est in manu Dei, electorum pro- priam intelligunt. Atque id etiam altera phrasis in- fert: MURI TUI PERPETUO SUNT CO- RAM ME. Utitur, inquit Brentius, pro more iis verbis, quibus externa Sion describi solet, cum tamen intelligat spiritualem Sionem, & significat curam sa- lutis & conservationis Ecclesiæ suæ sic sibi meditatam & infixam esse, ut deseri ex animo suo nunquam pos- sit. Hoc idem adumbravit Spiritus Sanct. in duo- bus lapidibus onychinis, in quibus sculpta erant no- mina filiorum Israël, & quos portabat Aharon co- ram Domino in utroque humero ad monumentum. Idem adumbrabant etiam duodecim gemmæ, in ra- tionali seu pectorali Judicii inclusæ, quas duodecim nominibus filiorum Israël insignitas Aharon ingres- surus in Sanctuarium in pectore suo affixas gestare so- let: memoriale, ut Scriptura Ex. 28. loquitur, co- ram Domino in æternum. Institutus enim fuit hic ornatus in Sacerdotii ministerio, non quod eo Deus per se delectaretur, aut placaretur: Sed ut Ecclesia admoneretur, se non solum Deo semper curæ esse, sed coram eo omnibus gemmis preciosiorem reputari. Et ut nomina filiorum Israël in gemmas insculpta deleri, nisi confractis gemmis, non potuerunt: ita fieri non po- test, ut ex animo Dei Ecclesia ejus aboleatur. B. Lu- therus emphasin notat, quod dicatur coram oculis MEIS, non tuis. Neque enim sentimus, quod simus expositi hominibus, dæmonibus, peccatis, morti & in- ferno; sunt igitur muri invisibiles & tantum credibi- les. Sectarii vident suos muros, Tyranni vident suos muros. Hic est immutandus sensus, quod illorum muri nulli sint, quia sunt coram oculis hominum, no- stri autem coram oculis Dei. Cyrillus descriptos nos esse in manum Domini per passionem Christi dicit, quod certe verissimum est ratione MERITI huju- sce inscriptionis. Christi, inquit, passio & pretiosa crux & manuum ipsius affixio securitas fuit, & mu- rus inaccessus & infractus his, qui in ipsum credide- runt: Dicere ergo possit jure: Ecce manibus meis depinxi muros tuos. Intelliges per passionem meam, sive passionem hoc uno significari, depinxi pro effor- mavi, dixit, & coram me es semper. Si enim passus est pro nobis, quomodo nostri oblivisceretur? vel quo- modo non essent in oculis ejus, propter quos ligno affixus est. Unde August. in Soliloqu. c. 2. Manus tuæ, inquit, Domine fecerunt me, & plasmaverunt me: manus inquam illæ, quæ affixæ clavis sunt pro me; o- pus manuum tuarum Domine, ne despicias, vulnera manuum tuarum precor, ut aspicias. Quia in ma- nibus tuis Domine descripsisti me: Lege ipsam scri- pturam & salva me. Confer. etiam Ambros. l. VI. Hexaëm. c. 5.

Jam quod ad Structores attinet v. 17. non ap- paret, quomodo architecti & restauratores Sionis corporalis intelligendi sint. Hæc enim ejus ampli- tudinis & capacitatis non fuit, ut gentes ex omni- bus plagis mundi accipere potuerit. Ideo Apo- stoli & alii architecti spirituales sub N. Test. intel- liguntur 1. Cor. 3. etsi interim non negemus alludi ad destructam à Chaldæis Sionem, quam restaurandam esse alias prædictum erat, quemadmodum & sub destruentium & dissipantium nomine ad Sanebal- lat & similis furfuris homines, qui structuram suf- flaminabant, respici, admitti potest, q. d. (quæ Cor- nel. à Lapid. est explicatio plerisque cæteris conso- na) video uti olim ita & nunc ruinas murorum tuo- rum, ò Sion, scio, quid facto opus sit, cerno tuos hostes, Scribas, Pharisæos, Imperatores & tyrannos, aposta- tas & hæreticos, qui à te exeunt, suntque transfugæ ad hostes; te velle destruere, dissipare & evertere. Verum ego eos avertam, vel compescam, vel certe efficiam, ut tui structuram non impediant, sed potius promoveant. Unde LXX. vertunt, cito ædificata es, à quibus destru- cta fuisti. Nam Judæi, ac præsertim Imperatores, Ecclesiam persequentes, postea ad eam conversi, ma- gis eam propagarunt. Ita fecit Saulus, cum factus est Paulus. Ita fecit Constantinus Imper. ejusque posteri. Sic explicant S. Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Au- gustinus, Tertullianus, Justinianus & ex eis Leo Ca- strius. Idem dicit & amplificat in seqq. Propheta, adeo clare, ut S. Augustinus, Tertullianus & Orige- nes asserant, ea interpretatione non egere. Ornatum Sponsæ ita exponit Cyrillus: Omnibus eis in- duam te velut ornatu Sponsæ. Nam Ecclesiarum ornamentum est multitudo congregata. Nam ideo solet divinitus inspirata Scriptura Ecclesiam ve- stitu aureo & variegato exornare. Quemadmo- dum enim variæ & pretiosissimæ lapidum, Indico- rum inquam species aureis regulis inhærescentes ad- mirabile quoddam & spectabile ornamentum adjun- gunt: Ita quoque sanctorum animæ virtutum insignibus decoratæ splendidissima pulchritudine fulgent, divi- nitatis oculis, ita ut quisque gratias agat Christo, & dicat: Exultet anima mea in Domino. Induit enim me veste salutis, & tunicam lætitiæ sponsalem orna- tum mihi circumdedit, & quasi sponsæ circumpo- suit mihi mitram. Quæ Grotius de Israëlitis dis- persis & ingenti illorum multitudine, quæ exulavit per varias nationes Assyriorum, Medorum, Babylo- niorum, Persarum, neque veritati Historiæ conso- nant: nam ab Assyriis transportati non rediere, & in Persia, aut apud Medos tum exulasse Judæos, cum solveretur captivitas Babylonica, ut tanta multitudo inde confluxerit ad restaurandam civi- tatem, doceri nequit, neque præsenti vaticinio congruunt, quia hic non de Judæis, sed gentibus ac- cersendis ad Zionem vaticinatur Propheta, ut ἐξή- γησις subjuncta testatur. De hoc autem vaticinio conferri etiam potest Concio XV. in memoria Justor. Witeberg. ubi è v. 14. 15. sistitur Miseri- cordia Dei plusquam paterna, lachrymantium deser- torum solatium.

## 49:19
Verse 19. YOUR DESOLATIONS AND YOUR SOLITUDES) Places which were such for 70 years.

Latin:

Vers. 19. DESERTA TUA ET SOLITUDINES TUÆ) Loca quæ talia per LXX. annos fuere.

## 49:20
Verse 20. CHILDREN OF YOUR STERILITY.) Born to you, when you seemed sterile.

Latin:

Vers. 20. FILII STERILITATIS TUÆ.) Nati tibi, cùm sterilis videreris.

## 49:21
Verse 21. TRANSMIGRATED AND CAPTIVE.) Deserted, with the citizens abducted, the very soil itself reduced to miserable servitude.

Latin:

Vers. 21. TRANSMIGRATA ET CAPTIVA.) De- serta, abductis civibus, ipso etiam solo in miseram servi- tutem redacto.

## 49:22
Verse 22. BEHOLD I WILL LIFT UP MY HAND TO THE NATIONS) as those are accustomed to do who call someone to themselves.

AND TO THE PEOPLES I WILL EXALT MY SIGN) As leaders are accustomed to do, who want their soldiers to be ready.

AND THEY SHALL BRING YOUR SONS IN THEIR ARMS) In their bosom: as little ones are accustomed to be carried. Thus the Greeks here. Nor do the Arabs use the word حضن otherwise.

AND YOUR DAUGHTERS THEY SHALL CARRY UPON THEIR SHOULDERS) As if they were carrying them in litters: that is, they will provide all the comforts for the journey.

That these glosses do not square with the text of the prophecy is evident from what we have said. Nor do they accord with historical truth: for the land of Judea after the return from captivity was not too narrow for its inhabitants; indeed, before that it had far more numerous inhabitants, when a huge and countless multitude of Israelites dwelt there, and the land nevertheless sufficed for them. But that was fulfilled when the multitude of the Gentiles came to the remaining faithful of the Israelites. Therefore, the children of barrenness are not those whom Zion bore when she seemed barren at the time of the captivity, but spiritual children, whom she was to bear through the Word and Sacraments, at that very time when the Church seemed most miserable and deserted by all. For at the time of the captivity, so many were certainly not born to the Jewish people that there was need to say upon the return to their land: The place is too narrow for me, make room for me that I may dwell. Nor was there need to marvel on account of those who were born to them then: Who has begotten me these, who acknowledge and call me their mother? I was destitute and desolate, but these, where were they? The Church, however, truly receives such sudden and great increases that we are forced to be astonished at the consideration of that fact, as when with one sermon of Peter three thousand men were converted to Christ, Acts 2. Therefore Cyril refers it to νοητὴν τὴν Σιὼν, which we call spiritual. And he compares it with Isaiah chapter 54, enlarge the place of thy tent, spare not, extend still to the right and to the left, which passage he illustrates by the tabernacle of Moses extended to all quarters of the world, as a type of the amplitude of the sacred tents of the Church. Similarly, Blessed Luther: you are as a desolate and devastated land, few are they who follow you, but most happy champions. But note that the propagation begins from desolation and devastation. The children of thy barrenness shall say. He says the Church is barren, and yet has a numerous offspring. For fruitfulness is in secret, barrenness is in appearance: The Lord himself declares that the calling of the Gentiles is being regarded. BEHOLD I WILL LIFT UP MY HAND TO THE GENTILES AND TO THE PEOPLE I WILL EXALT MY SIGN or banner: For by these words he gives the reason why the Church is so increased, as if to say, I will take care that the Gospel is preached, and as if with extended hand and raised banner I will gather to myself a people and a multitude of spiritual soldiers, confessors and martyrs, and other faithful, who under my banner are to fight spiritually in true faith and piety against the temptation of the Devil, the allurements of the world, and the depraved desires of the flesh. AND THEY SHALL BRING THY SONS (that is, those to be committed to your care and to serve you) IN THEIR ARMS, AND THY DAUGHTERS THEY SHALL CARRY UPON THEIR SHOULDERS; which refers to infants newly born, who are brought into the Church through baptism, Osiander understands: But generally, the sons and daughters of the Church are called the faithful, who are gathered to the Church. Therefore, readiness is expressed in the gathering to the Church; as the blessed Luther observes. The Gospel is not a violent doctrine, as laws are; but it carries [them] gently in the word, so that the sons may flow in of their own accord, not coerced. Cyril refers [this] both to the manner of treating those tender in the faith, so that they are all but carried in the bosom, and placed upon shoulders and borne, and as infants are nourished with milk: and also to the ease of access to the Church. That for those who strive to go to Zion as to a mother, the access will be without any shame, because they will be taken into the bosom and carried on shoulders. This is, therefore, a manifest discourse concerning the calling of the Gentiles, and the increasing and preserving of the Church, even unto the last day of this age, as Brentius says on this passage. When he had promised to Zion, says Cyril, that she would have both many and good children, and that her sons would come in such a multitude that they would need a wider place than before, and would ask that the tabernacle be dilated: he immediately demonstrates that this multitude of children promised to her would arise not from Israel alone, but from the congregation of the Gentiles. But this is indeed true, and it is permitted to foresee it from the very facts.
