For the remnant from Israel has been saved, but that [is] indeed small and easily countable, but the whole world has been ensnared and captured through faith in Christ, and the power of Apostolic and Evangelical preaching has brought the inhabitants of the whole earth to Him. What, therefore, this will be, he shows: Behold, he says, I lift up my hand to the Gentiles. Moreover, that word 'I lift up' signifies I exalt, I extol; but 'hand' can denote strength or power. For when Christ became known to the Gentiles through Evangelical preaching and was made exalted and conspicuous on account of the miracles which He performed, and through the resurrection from the dead, when the sign of the precious cross was exhibited among those who by nature and truly had not known God at some time: then Zion was increased and enriched with a copious offspring: then they ran to her from all sides, and shouted to one another, exhorting and saying: Come, let us ascend the mountain of the Lord, and into the House of the God of Jacob, etc.

It is absurd that Grotius drags these things to the ease and convenience of the return into Judea. AND THEY SHALL CARRY THY DAUGHTERS UPON THEIR SHOULDERS. As if he will carry them in litters, that is, they will provide all conveniences for the journey. But the daughters of Zion are not called the daughters of the Jews, who, returning to Palestine, might have need to be carried upon shoulders, i.e., in the interpretation of Grotius, in litters: But the Gentiles are indicated, of whom [it is said] in v. 22, Behold I will lift up my hand to the Gentiles, by whom children are brought to the people of the Lord, who are called the sons and daughters of the spiritual Zion, because they are brought and committed to the same. If Grotius wishes the hand of the Lord to be lifted up and His sign to be exalted to the Gentiles and peoples only to that end, that through them a convenient journey might be provided for the returning Jews, I do not know if such a gloss has ever even entered the mind of any of the most trifling Jews. For the Gentiles and peoples are called, so that they themselves may be gathered to the Church: Whence also the root of Jesse is said to stand for a sign or banner of the peoples, Is. 11, 11. i.e., Christ, so that the Gentiles may pray to Him.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ECCE LEVABO AD GENTES MANUM MEAM) ut solent qui aliquem ad se vocant.

ET AD POPULOS EXALTABO SIGNUM MEUM) Ut solent duces, qui militem paratum esse vo- lunt.

ET AFFERENT FILIOS TUOS IN ULNIS) In sinu suo: sicut parvuli portari solent. Ita hic Græci. Nec aliter Arabes حضن usurpant.

ET FILIAS TUAS SUPER HUMEROS POR- TABUNT) Quasi in lecticis ferent: id est, omnia itineri commoda præstabunt.

Has glossas non quadrare textui vaticinii, ex iis, quæ diximus constat. Neque veritati histori- cæ congruunt: nam terra Judæa post reditum è ca- ptivitate non erat angusta nimis præ habitatoribus, imo antea longe copiosiores habuit incolas, cum Israëlitarum ingens & innumera multitudo illic ha- bitaret, & terra illis nihilofecius sufficeret. Impleta autem illa, cum accessit ad reliquos fideles Israëli- tarum multitudo gentium. Ideo filii sterilitatis non sunt, quos genuit cum steriles videretur Sion tempore captivitatis, sed spirituales filii, quos geni- tura erat per verbum & Sacramenta, eo ipso tempo- re, quo videbatur miserrima & ab omnibus deserta Ecclesia. Nam captivitatis tempore tot utique geniti non sunt Judaico populo, ut dicere opus ha- buerit sub reditum in terram suam: Angustus ni- mis est mihi locus, fac spatium mihi, ut habitem. Nec ob illos qui tum ipsis nati, admirari necessum ha- buit: Quis genuit mihi istos, qui me suam matrem agnoscunt & appellant. Ego destituta & desolata eram, mihi autem isti ubi erant? Ecclesia au- tem revera tam subita & magna incrementa su- mit, ut ad ejus rei considerationem obstupescere cogamur, ut cum una Petri concione tria milia ho- minum ad Christum conversa sunt Act. 2. Ideo Cy- rillus ad νοητὴν τὴν Σιὼν, quam nos spiritualem dici- mus, refert. Et Esa. 54. cap. confert, dilata locum tabernaculi tui, ne parcas, adhuc in dextris & sinistris extende, quem locum illustrat tabernaculo Mosis ad omnes plagas mundi extenso, ceu typo amplitudi- nis sacrorum tentoriorum Ecclesiæ. Similiter B. Lutherus: es tanquam desolata & vastata terra, pau- ci sunt, qui te sequuntur, sed propugnatores felicissimi. Sed nota propagationem incipere à desolatione & va- statione. Dicent filii sterilitatis tuæ. Dicit Ec- clesiam esse sterilem, & tamen habere numerosam So- bolem. Fœcunditas enim in abscondito est, sterili- tas est in specie: Vocationem gentium respici Domi- nus ipse declarat. ECCE LEVABO AD GENTES MANUM MEAM ET AD PO- PULUM EXALTABO SIGNUM seu vexil- lum MEUM: His enim causam reddit, quod Ec- clesia sic augeatur, q. d. curabo prædicari Evange- lium, & quasi extensa manu & sublato vexillo con- gregabo mihi populum & multitudinem spiritualium militum, confessorum & martyrum, aliorumque fide- lium, qui sub meo vexillo in vera fide & pietate spiri- tualiter militaturi sunt contra Diaboli tentationem, mundi illecebras, & carnis pravas concupiscentias. ET AFFERENT FILIOS TUOS (hoc est tuæ curæ committendos, tibique inserviendos) In UL- NIS, ET FILIAS TUAS SUPER HUME- ROS PORTABUNT; quod de infantibus re- cens natis, qui per baptismum Ecclesiæ inferuntur, Osiander intelligit : Sed generaliter filii & filiæ Ec- clesiæ dicuntur fideles, qui ad Ecclesiam colligun- tur. Ideo promptitudo exprimitur in aggregatione ad Ecclesiam ; ut observat B. Lutherus. Evange- lium non est violenta doctrina, sicut leges sunt; sed sua- viter portat in verbo, ut sponte affluant filii non coacti. Cyrillus refert tum ad modum teneros in fide tractan- di, quod tantum non in sinu gestentur, & in hume- ros repositi ferantur, ac velut infantes lacte nutri- antur : tum etiam ad facilitatem accessus ad Eccle- siam. Quod his, qui ad Sion tanquam ad matrem ire contendunt, accessus sit futurus citra omnem pudorem, quia in gremium assumentur, & in hume- ris tollentur. Manifesta ergo hæc est concio de vo- catione gentium, & augenda atque conservanda Eccle- sia, usque ad novissimum hujus seculi diem, ut ait Bren- tius in hunc locum. Cum promisisset Sioni, inquit Cyrillus, habituram ipsam & multos & probos libe- ros, filiosque suos eo multitudinis venturos, ut amplio- re loco, quam olim, indigerent, & dilatari tabernacu- lum rogarent: statim demonstrat, non ex Israël solum, sed ex gentium congregatione hanc promissorum ipsi filiorum multitudinem exorituram. Verum hoc quidem est, & ex ipsis rebus licet prospicere. Resi- duum enim ex Israel servatum est, sed exiguum qui- dem illud & facile numerabile, sed & irretitus ac ca- ptus est per fidem in Christo orbis terrarum, & Apo- stolice atque Evangelicæ prædicationis virtus univer- sæ terræ incolas ei adduxit. Quod igitur hoc futu- rum sit, ostendit : Ecce, inquiens, ego tollo ad gen- tes manum meam. Significat autem illud Tollo, exalto, extollo, Manus autem fortitudinem aut vir- tutem denotare potest. Quando enim gentibus in- notuit Christus per Evangelicam prædictionem & excelsus factus est & conspicuus propter ea, quæ edidit miracula, & per resurrectionem è mortuis, quando si- gnum pretiosæ crucis exhibitum est, apud eos, qui Deum natura & vere aliquando non noverant : tunc Sion copiosa Sobole aucta & ditata est : tunc undique ad eam accurrebant, & sibi mutuo acclamabant hor- tantes & dicentes : Adeste ascendamus montem Domini, & in Domum Dei Jacob &c.

Ineptum est, quod Grotius hæc pertrahit ad facilitatem & commoditatem reditus in Judæam. ET FILIAS TUAS SUPER HUMEROS PORTABUNT. Quasi in lecticis feret, id est, omnia itineri commoda præstabunt. At filiæ Sionis non dicuntur Judæorum filiæ, quæ redituræ in Pa- læstinam opus habeant, ut super humeros, h. e. in- terprete Grotio, in lecticis portentur : Sed gentes indigitantur, de quibus v. 22. Ecce levabo ad gen- tes manum meam, à quibus liberi afferuntur ad po- pulum Domini, qui filii & filiæ Sionis spiritualis di- cuntur, quia eidem inferuntur & committuntur. Si ad gentes & populos tantum ea fini manum Domi- ni levari & signum ejus exaltari vult Grotius, ut per illas iter commodum præstetur Judæis redituris, nescio an unquam etiam è nugacissimis Judæis ul- li talis glossa in mentem venerit. Nam gentes & populi vocantur, ut ad Ecclesiam ipsimet aggre- gentur : Unde etiam radix Jesse in signum vel vexil- lum populorum stare dicitur Es. 11, 11. h. e. Christus, ut gentes ipsum deprecentur.

## 49:23
Vers. 23. AND KINGS SHALL BE THY NURSING FATHERS) Such as Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes, mentioned by Ezra; Alexander the Great, his successors, especially Demetrius. For these conferred very many benefits, immunities, and gifts both upon the people and the Temple. Which can be seen in Josephus. Add what we have said on Matt. 24, 15. We have 'nutritium' for 'nutritore' (nursing father) also in the writer of the Alexandrian war.

AND THY QUEENS THY NURSING MOTHERS) Such as Esther: such as Cleopatra, the daughter of King Ptolemy, married to Alexander, King of the Jews, and others.

Grotius is concerned only with the external people and the material temple, along with the carnal Jews. Therefore, he takes it concerning the benefits and immunities which happened to them. But since the promises are spiritual, and the propagation of the spiritual Zion is designated, even if some of the monarchs of either sex contributed something to the Jewish temple and people, it is certain that far more august things are predicted here, which, to wit, make for the enlargement of the Church of God, for the multiplication of the assemblies of the faithful. Furthermore, that the times of the New Testament are referred to particularly, in which the hand of the Lord was lifted up to the Gentiles, and the sign was exalted to the peoples especially through the universal calling of the Gentiles to the kingdom of Christ, is most clear from the words of the Prophet, which therefore cannot be restricted to those things which were performed by Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes, and Ezra. And therefore Christian interpreters by common calculation understand these things primarily concerning the times of the New Testament. Cyril, when, he says, Christ became known to the Gentiles through Evangelical preaching, then Zion was increased and enriched with a copious offspring; and she will overflow with the highest honor and glory and happiness. Kings are nursing fathers and Queens are nursing mothers. For it is permitted to see those who believed in Christ affected with honor and deemed worthy of all mercy on account of the piety of the rulers, so much so that they seem to be nothing other than their foster children. For if they fall upon their faces and adore Zion, that is, the Church, and as if cast down with hands extended to the ground, they all but lick the dust of her feet, there is no doubt but that those who have been advanced to this knowledge, and enlightened by this grace of piety, add this to their deeds, that they affect the elect with honor, and hold those who have believed in Christ in the place of children. With this done, Sion will no longer be affected by shame as a barren and widowed woman, who as far as the Jews were concerned was bereft of children, but she will be crowned with glory. B. Brentius says, Here is promised to the Church hospitality and protection in empires and polities or cities of this age; Kings, he says, will be your foster-fathers, and Queens, that is, great cities, will be your foster-mothers. For although the Church is subject to the cross in this world, and the greatest empires are accustomed to inflict the greatest evils upon the Church: yet because it is necessary that the Church be instructed in pious doctrine and propagated to posterity: it is also necessary that it have its own lodgings on earth, and its own seats, in which the doctrine of the Gospel may be published and handed down to posterity. Indeed, there is no certain place and certain kingdom for the Church, as was once defined for the posterity of Abraham in this land. For after it was said to the Apostles: Go into the whole world, and preach the Gospel to every creature: and again: You shall be my witnesses even to the ends of the earth: The seat of the Church is not fixed to one or another place of the earth: but as its seat is there, where God reveals the Gospel of his son, and transfers his seat to where he also transfers the Gospel: So he also excites the Church's own foster-fathers and foster-mothers, namely Princes and Republics, who either assist the Church by their works, or at least tolerate it, and do not persecute it tyrannically or violently: Therefore the conversion of Kingdoms is also insinuated here, as B. Luther rightly warned. He says, it also signifies that Kings are to be converted. Thus Charlemagne, Theodosius, and other great Princes embraced the word, and sustained the Church with liberal alms, preserved peace, and defended Christians from force and injury. Thus today our Elector of Saxony contributes his empire to the use of the Church, while he fosters the teachers of the word. They have accepted this passage concerning goods donated to the Church. But I scarcely ever judge that the goods of the Church were donated on account of the Gospel, but rather they were snatched from Emperors by the fraud and thefts of the Popes. THEY SHALL LICK THE DUST OF YOUR FEET. Figuratively it expresses the reverence which great Princes are to exhibit to Christians.

The Osiandrian Paraphrase is therefore very appropriate here: And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers, i.e., Kings, Princes, and Republics will provide hospitality to you, O Church, in their kingdoms, will liberally assist you from their resources, and will confer upon you services of every kind. (This is fulfilled daily, when Princes and Republics promote the Ministry of the Gospel with their counsels and resources.) They shall worship with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet, i.e., They will pursue you with great honor, and will humbly submit themselves to you, congratulating themselves that they have been received into the Church of God. Almost all others agree. But Grotius preferred to side with the Jews here, and savors only of carnal things. Wolffg. Musculus, who is often corrupted even by the Rabbis, refers these things to the education of Daniel and his companions in the court of the King of Babel; indeed, he thinks the entire remnants of Israel were as it were educated and nourished by Kings and Queens, because they were not extinguished, as Pharaoh desired the Israelites to be extinguished. But more august things are predicted here, and Musculus's teacher, Calvin, had already demonstrated a far different meaning, who holds as follows on this passage: When he had spoken of the obedience of the nations, he shows that this pertains not only to the common people, but to Kings as well. He compares Kings to hired men who nourish the children of others: And Queens to nurses who hire out their services. Why so? Because Kings and Queens will provide all things necessary for nourishing the offspring of the Church. For although they had previously cast Christ out of their borders, they will henceforth acknowledge him as the supreme King, and will exhibit to him all honor, obedience, and worship. This happened when God revealed himself to the world through the Gospel. For great Kings and princes not only took upon themselves the yoke of Christ, but also contributed their resources to the erecting and fostering of Christ's Church: So that they proved themselves its patrons and guardians. Whence it is to be observed that something singular is required here of princes beyond a common profession of faith, since authority and power have been granted to them by the Lord, so that they may protect the Church and procure the glory of God. This indeed pertains to all: But Kings, the greater their power is, the more they ought to expend themselves and the more studiously they ought to care for this, and this is the reason why David calls upon them by name and exhorts them to be wise, and to serve the Lord, and to kiss the Son. To be compared with this passage is the similar one, Isa. 60:16, Thou shalt suck the breast of kings, to which it is certain the times of the New Testament refer. Theod. Hackspan. He is prolixly concerned here about the version of B. Luther, why he rendered the feminine in a masculine sense: Die Fürsten: but in the copy of Megalander published at Wittenberg in the year 1532 by Johann Lufft, which I have at hand, the feminine is held: Und ihre Fürstin deine Säugammen seyn.

Same verse.

WITH FACE BOWED TO THE EARTH THEY SHALL WORSHIP THEE, AND LICK THE DUST OF THY FEET.) It is clear here that אַפַּיִם אֶרֶץ is placed for אַפֵּי אֶרֶץ, such a construction is found in Exod. 28:17, Prov. 20:1, 21, and elsewhere. Understand, however, by אַפַּיִם אֶרֶץ those who are notable on earth, the honored: how that name is sometimes taken, the Hebrews note, passing to 1 Sam. 1:4. This pertains, however, to the princes of Idumea, Moab, and other lands, which the Jews, having returned, subdued. To lick the dust of the feet is not for Kings, but for subdued enemies. This appears in Ps. 72:9. Compare also what is below, 60:14. Statius calls this worshipping the footprints, that is, to prostrate oneself where another has walked. Regarding the Grotian explanation of the Hebrew phrase, we allow everyone free judgment. But the application to the princes of Idumea, Moab, and other lands is foreign. Nor are such documents produced from History. And the web of the promise begun here is continued, which, just as it dealt with the fostering of the Church by Kings: so now the discourse is about the veneration and honor to be exhibited to the same, by the common calculation of the Interpreters. Therefore, it is not about the subjection of enemies. To lick the dust of the feet is not only for subdued enemies, but also for those who exhibit honor to another according to the custom of the Persians, because among their Kings no one could speak unless prostrated on the ground he kissed the footprints of the Royal feet: Witness Xenophon, book VIII, and Plutarch in Alcibiades. Nor is it taken otherwise in Ps. 72:9 or Isa. 60:14. For there too the Holy Scriptures prophesy about the veneration and submission to be rendered to Christ the King. Therefore, B. Brentius is correct: Nor is this only promised, that Kings and Princes will be the nourishers of the Church, but also that they will be subject to the Church. With face, he says, bowed to the earth, they shall worship thee, and lick the dust of thy feet. This is not to be understood as meaning that Kings ought to kiss the feet of the Roman Pontiff, and defend with arms the tyranny, impiety, and idolatry of the Pontiffs: But that some Princes and Kings will be stirred up by the preaching of the Gospel, so that they themselves may believe in Christ, and join themselves most obediently with the Church of Christ, and serve it with whatever services they can.

Same verse.

UPON WHOM THEY WHO WAIT FOR HIM SHALL NOT BE ASHAMED) A Hebrew locution, for which you might say in Latin: He in whom they trust shall not be put to shame.

We do not disapprove of this meaning. How it ought to be elicited from the Hebrew phrase, Lud. de Dieu teaches on this passage.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ERUNT REGES NUTRITII TUI) Ut Cyrus, Darius, Artaxerxes, Esdræ memorati; Alexander Magnus, successores ejus, maxime Demetrius. Hi enim & in populum, & in Templum plurima beneficia, immunita- tes, dona contulerunt. Quæ videre est apud Josephum. Ad- de quæ diximus ad Matth. 24, 15. Nutritium pro Nutritore habemus & apud Scriptorem belli Alexandrini.

ET REGINÆ NUTRICES TUÆ) Ut Esthera : ut Cleopatra Regis Ptolemæi filia nupta Alexandro Judæo- rum Regi, & aliæ.

De populo externo & templo materiali tantum sollicitus est cum carnalibus Judæis Grotius. Ideo de beneficiis & immunitatibus, quæ illis obtigere, ea accipit. At cum promissiones sint spirituales, & propagatio Sionis spiritualis designetur, etsi Mo- narcharum aliqui utriusque Sexus, ad templum & populum Judaicum aliquid contulerint, longe ta- men augustiora hic prædici certum est, quæ sc. ad ampliationem Ecclesiæ Dei faciunt, ad cœtus fide- lium multiplicationem. Adhæc respici peculiari- ter tempora N. Test. quibus levata ad gentes manus Domini, & exaltatum signum ad populos impri- mis fuit per universalem gentium ad regnum Chri- sti vocationem, è verbis Prophetæ luculentissimum est, quæ proinde illis, quæ à Cyro, Dario, Artaxerxe & Esdra præstita sunt, restringi non possunt. Ideo- que Interpp. Christiani communi calculo hæc im- primis intelligunt de temporibus N. Test. Cyril- lus, quando, inquit, gentibus innotuit Christus per Evangelicam prædicationem, tunc Sion copiosa sobo- le aucta & ditata est; & honore summo & gloria & felicitate circumfluet. Reges nutricii & Reges nu- trices sunt. Licet enim videre, propter domina- torum pietatem honore affectos & omni misericor- dia dignatos eos, qui in Christum crediderunt, adeo ut nihil aliud quam eorum alumni esse videantur. Si enim in faciem procumbant & adorent Sion, id est, Ecclesiam, & velut in terram extensis manibus pro- jećti, tantum non pulverem pedum ejus lingant, du- bium non est, quin ii, qui ad hanc cognitionem prove- cti sint, & hac pietatis gratia illustrati, illud suis factis adjiciant, ut electos honore afficiant, & qui in Chri- stum crediderunt, eos in liberorum loco habeant. Quo facto non jam ut sterilis & vidua pudore afficietur Sion, quæ quoad Judæos orbata erat liberis, sed gloria erit coronata. B. Brentius, Promittitur hic, inquit, Ecclesiæ hospitium & tutela in imperiis & Politiis seu urbibus hujus seculi, Reges inquit, erunt Nutrito- res tui, & Reginæ, hoc est, magnæ urbes erunt Nutri- ces tuæ. Etsi enim Ecclesia subjecta est cruci in hoc mundo, & maxima quæque Imperia solent maxima mala Ecclesiæ inferre: tamen quia necesse est, ut Eccle- sia pia doctrina erudiatur, & ad posteros propagetur: necesse etiam est, ut habeat sua in terris hospitia, & suas sedes, in quibus doctrina Evangelii vulge- tur, & posteritati tradatur. Non est quidem Ec- clesiæ certus locus & certum regnum, sicut olim posteritati Abrahæ in hac terra definitum. Post- quam enim dictum est Apostolis: Ite in universum orbem, & prædicate Evangelion omni creaturæ: & iterum: Eritis mihi testes usque ad extrema ter- ræ: Sedes Ecclesiæ non est ad unum tantum & alte- rum locum terræ affixa: sed ut ibi est sedes ejus, ubi Deus revelat Evangelion filii sui, & eo transfert se- dem, quo & Evangelion transfert: Ita excitat etiam Ecclesiæ suos nutricios & nutrices, Principes videlicet & Respublicas, qui Ecclesiam aut sua opera adju- vant, aut saltem tolerant, & non tyrannice nec vio- lenter persequuntur: Ideo etiam conversio Regnum hic insinuatur, ut monuit recte B. Lutherus. Signifi- cat, inquit, etiam Reges convertendos esse. Sic Ca- rolus M. Theodosius, & alii magni Principes, verbum amplexi sunt, & Ecclesiam liberalibus eleemosynis sustentarunt, conservarunt pacem, defenderunt Chri- stianos à vi & injuria. Sic hodie noster Elector Sa- xoniæ Imperium suum confert ad usum Ecclesiæ, dum fovet Doctores verbi. Acceperunt hunc locum de bonis donatis Ecclesiæ. Sed ego vix unquam judico, bona Ecclesiæ propter Evangelium donata esse, sed fraude potius & furtis Pontificum Imperatoribus ere- pta sunt. PULVEREM PEDUM TUORUM LINGENT. Figurate exprimit reverentiam, quam Christianis exhibituri sunt magni Principes.

Optime ergo hic se habet Paraphrasis Osiandrina: Et erunt Reges nutritii tui, & reginæ eorum nutrices tuæ, i. e. Reges, Principes & Respublicæ tibi, ô Ecclesia, hospitium in suis regnis præbebunt, de suis facultati- bus te liberaliter juvabunt, & omnis generis officia in te conferent. (Hoc quotidie impletur, cum Prin- cipes & Respublicæ promovent Ministerium Ev- angelii suis consiliis & facultatibus) Vultu in ter- ram demisso adorabunt, & pulverem pedum tuorum lingent, i. e. Magno te honore prosequentur, & humi- liter sese subjicient tibi, gratulantes sibi, quod sint re- cepti in Ecclesiam Dei. Consonant cæteri pene omnes. At Grotius hic cum Judæis facere ma- luit, & carnalia tantum sapit. Wolffg. Musculus, qui sæpe etiam à Rabbinis corruptus est, ad educatio- nem Danielis & Sociorum in aula Regis Babel hæc refert, imo reliquias universas Israëlís, à Regibus & Reginis quasi educatas & nutritas putat, quia non ex- tinctæ sunt, ut Pharao extinctos cupiebat Israëlitas. Sed hic augustiora prædicuntur, & longe alium sen- sum jam demonstrarat Musculi Præceptor Calvi- nus, qui ita habet in hunc locum: Quum loquutus esset de obsequio gentium, ostendit hoc non ad plebeios tantum, sed ad Reges quoque pertinere. Reges autem comparat conductitiis hominibus, qui alienos liberos a- lunt: Et Reginas nutricibus, quæ operam suam lo- cant. Cur ita? Quoniam Reges ac Reginæ omnia ne- cessaria ad alendam Ecclesiæ sobolem subministra- bunt. Nam cum antea Christum è finibus suis ejecerent, eum deinceps agnoscent summum Regem, omnemque ipsi honorem, obsequium & cultum exhibebunt. Hoc accidit, quum Deus sese per Evangelium orbi terra- rum patefecit. Magni enim Reges ac principes non solum Christi jugum subierunt, sed etiam facultates suas contulerunt ad erigendam & fovendam Christi Ecclesiam: Ita ut se patronos ac tutores ejus præsta- rent. Unde observandum est, singulare quiddam hic à principibus requiri præter vulgarem fidei pro- fessionem, quoniam authoritas & potentia iis à Domi- no tributa est, ut Ecclesiam tueantur, & gloriam Dei procurent. Hoc quidem pertinet ad universos: Sed Re- ges, quo major est eorum potentia, eo magno sese impen- dere, & studiosius id curare debent, atque hæc ratio est, cur David eos nominatim compellet, atque adhortetur, ut sapiant, Dominoque serviant & Filium osculentur. Conferendus cum hoc loco similis Es.60,16. Mam- milla Regum lactaberis, quo etiam N. Test. tempo- ra respici certum est. Theod. Hackspan. prolixe hic solicitus est de versione B. Lutheri, cur Fœmi- ninum sensu Masculino reddiderit: Die Fürsten: sed in exemplariMegalandriAnno 1532. Witenber- gæ per Johann. Lufft edito, quod mihi ad manum est, habetur fœmininum: Und ihre Fürstin deine Säugammen seyn.

Vers. eod.

VULTU IN TERRAM DEMISSO ADORA- BVNT TE, ET PULVEREM PEDVM TVORVM LIN- GENT.) Patet hic אַפַּיִם אֶרֶץ positum pro אַפֵּי אֶרֶץ, qualis constructio reperitur Exod. 28, 17. Prov.20, l. 21. & alibi. Intellige autem per אַפַּיִם אֶרֶץ spectabiles in ter- ra, honoratos: quomodo id nomen interdum sumi notant HebTransient ad 1.Sam. 1,4. Pertinet autem hoc ad principesIdu- mææ Moabitidis & aliarum terrarum, quas Judæi reverfi subégere. Pulverem pedum lingere non est Regum, sed ho. stium subactorum. Apparet hoc Ps. 72, 9. Confer & quod infra est 60, 14. Vestigia adorare hoc dicit Statius, id est, ibi procumbere, ubi alter incessit. De Phraseos Ebrææ explicatione Grotiana permittimus cuivis liberum judicium. Aliena au- tem est de principibus Idumææ, Moabitidis, & alia- rum terrarum applicatio. Neque documenta ta- lia ex Historia producta. Et continuatur hic tela promissionis cœpta, quæ uti de fovenda Ecclesia à Regibus agebat: ita nunc de veneratione & hono- re eidem exhibendo sermo est, communi calculo Interpp. Non ergo de hostium subjectione. Pul- verem pedum lingere, non est tantum hostium sub- actorum, sed eorum etiam, qui honorem exhibent alteri ex more Persarum, quia apud Reges illorum nemo loqui poterat, nisi prostratus in terram vesti- gia pedum Regiorum exoscularetur: Teste Xeno- phonte lib. IIX. & Plutarcho in Alcib. Nec aliter accipitur Ps. 72, 9. aut Esa. 60, 14. Nam & ibi de ve- neratione & submissione Christo Regi præstanda vaticinatur SS. Ideo recte B. Brentius: Nec hoc tantum promittitur, Reges & Principes fore Ecclesiæ nutritores, verum etiam fore eos Ecclesiæ subjectos. Vultu, inquit, in terram demisso, adorabunt te, & pulverem pedum tuorum lingent. Hoc non est intelligendum, quod Reges debeant osculari pe- des Romani Pontificis, & armis tyrannidem, im- pietatem & idololatriam Pontificum tueri: Sed quod nonnulli Principes & Reges excitabuntur prædicatione Evangelii, ut & ipsi credant in Chri- stum, & conjungant sese obedientissime cum Eccle- sia Christi, & serviant ei, quibus possunt officiis.

Vers. eod.

SVPER QVO NON CONFVNDENTVR QVI EXPECTANT EVM) Locutio Hebraica, pro quo Lati- ne dicas: Cui qui confidunt non pudefient.

Sensum hunc non improbamus. Quem quo- modo è phrasi Ebræa erui debeat, docet Lud. de Dieu ad h. l.

## 49:24
Verse 24. SHALL THE PREY BE TAKEN FROM THE MIGHTY, OR SHALL THAT WHICH HAS BEEN CAPTURED BY THE STRONG BE ABLE TO BE SAFE.) In the Hebrew: Shall the prey be snatched from the mighty, and the captivity of the just escape? Zion is introduced speaking, and scarcely believing that it can be done. The captivity of the just, that is, those who have been captured by the law of war. What is done from a war declared between nations is said to be done according to a certain law, and to be a certain right, concerning which matter we have brought forward excellent passages in book III, ch. 10, of the Law of War and Peace. And therefore what is here called the captivity of the just will immediately be called the captivity of the violent, just as among the Romans in this argument the same thing is called both right and injury.

Latin:

Vers. 24. NVMQVID TOLLETVR A FORTI PRÆDA, AVT QVOD CAPTVM FVERIT A RO- BVSTO SALVVM ESSE POTERIT.) In Hebræo: An eriperetur forti præda, & captivitas justi evaderet? Sion loquens inducitur, & vix credens id fieri posse. Captivitas justi, id est, ii qui capti sunt belli jure. Quod à bello inter gentes indicto fit, id fieri dicitur κατά νόμον δε τινα, & esse δικαιόν τι, qua de re loca egregia adduximus lio. III. c. 10. de Jure Belli ac Pacis. Et propterea quæ hic dicitur captivitas justi, statim dicetur captivitas violenti, sicut apud Roma- nos in hoc argumento idem & jus & injuria dicitur.

## 49:25
AND THOSE WHO JUDGED YOU I WILL JUDGE.) More correctly: I will contend with those who contended with you. With the Babylonians, Idumeans, and others of those parts.

Latin:

EOS VERO QVI JVDICAVERUNT TE E- GO JVDICABO.) Rectius: Contendam cum iis, qui tecum contenderunt. Cum Babyloniis, Idumæis, aliisque illarum partium.

## 49:26
Vers. 26. AND I WILL FEED YOUR ENEMIES WITH THEIR OWN FLESH.) I will set them against one another, the Persians with the Medes, then the Persians and Medes with the Babylonians: all of whom had once served in the army of Nebuchadnezzar.

Since it has been shown thus far that the whole prophecy looks to the spiritual benefits of the Messiah and the calling of the Gentiles recently predicted, there is no place for that Grotius gloss borrowed from the Jews concerning the liberation from the Babylonian captivity, although Musculus also embraced it; but by the force of the context it is about the liberation from spiritual captivity, by whose merit and power the Gentiles are converted to the kingdom of Christ, and were to be effectively snatched from Satan, who held that prey, as if to say: Who could snatch the Gentiles from the devil, whom he holds as captured prey in his hand? For the captivity of the infidels under the power of Satan is just. The Lord therefore testifies that He will do this in v. 25, and that He is Christ appears from His words in Luke 11:21, where He seems entirely to have looked back to this passage: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils. And He who speaks these things in the Prophet describes Himself as being the Savior and the strong Redeemer of Jacob and Israel, upon whom he can safely rely with true faith. Jerome understands the Strong One of Israel to be He who wrestled with Israel and was the helper of the strength of Jacob, because He is then to be acknowledged as the Redeemer. Some understand these things as the redemption through the Blood of Christ, by which we have been freed from the power of Satan, Heb. 2:14. Of these words rum, says Cyril, this is the meaning: The world of lands was captured by the Devil and by the flock of demons, nor was it possible for anyone on earth to escape their perversities and tyranny. But I, says the Lord, will draw out and deliver those affected by injuries. Truly, although that redemption as a meritorious cause is rightly adduced for this prey to be snatched from Satan through the calling of the Gentiles, yet the actual rescue itself from the kingdom of Satan, which exists by virtue of the merit of Christ, is more rightly understood here. Brentius's ἐξήγησις also comes to the same thing, even if by the giant κτ' τὸ ῥητὸν he understands kings and tyrants, under whom are the nations to be converted to Christ, and from whom they are as it were to be snatched, so that they may submit themselves to Christ. Which is also the interpretation of Jerome. The rest concerning the judging of those who judged Zion, the enemies of the Church, are rightly accepted, yet they are not to be restricted to the Babylonians and Edomites alone, or to ancient times: Nay, by the force of the συνεχείας they concern the times of the New Testament in a peculiar way. That is to say: Furthermore, your enemies, who oppose you, I will feed with their own flesh and they shall be drunk with their own blood, as with new wine, i.e., they will be a destruction to themselves; I will cause enemies to rage against their own vitals and to destroy themselves by their own tyranny. Since tyrants, while they persecute the Church, not rarely bring the greatest damages upon themselves, and overturn their own kingdoms by their own strength. We add, moreover, for the illustration of this chapter, what we proposed in the Paschal program.

The Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered. The lamb was slain, but the Lion conquered; he conquered the blasphemies of the Jews on the gibbet, he bound the strong armed man in the atrium, and triumphed over the very empire of death. Where are your reproaches, Jew? Where are the vessels of captivity you speak of? Where, O death, is your victory? The slanderer is confounded: the ravisher is despoiled. A new kind of power, hitherto victorious death is stunned. Let it be permitted to us thus to make the words of St. Bernard our own. Truly a new kind of power, a new kind of victory! Death is plainly consumed in its own victory, says St. Augustine, Sermon 161 de Tempore, when, subjecting Christ to the laws of hell, it destroys itself when it conquers. For in that in which it possessed him, whom it believed it had overcome, it was conquered by him when he rose again. Where is your victory, O hell? Where is your sting, O death? He who once through Hosea (thus Jerome in the Epitaph of Nepotian to Heliodorus insults death) threatened you rigidly: I will be your death, O death; I will be your bite, O hell, by his death you are dead, by his death we live: you devoured and you were devoured; and while you were soliciting the bait of the assumed body of Christ, and thinking it prey with greedy jaws, your insides were pierced with a hooked tooth. We give thanks TO YOU, CHRIST Savior, your creature, that while you were being killed, you killed our powerful adversary. Great is the power of this adversary: who is that strong armed man, guarding his own atrium: But stronger than he is he who comes upon him, the giant of dual substance: The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. He therefore overcame him, and took away all his armor in which he trusted, and distributed his spoils: He had the empire of death and through death ruled the whole world: But our Redeemer, although he was made a participant of our flesh and blood in the same way as children, and had to taste death for us, through death he destroyed him who had the empire of death, i.e., the Devil, and delivered those who through fear of death were subject to slavery for their whole life. While we recall these things in the Church with grateful and due memory, it is a pleasure to hear our most august victor himself, how he predicted this glorious victory against that robust Giant through Isaiah. Shall prey be taken from the strong? Or shall that which was captured by the robust be able to be safe? Because thus says the Lord: Indeed, even the captivity shall be taken from the strong: and that which was taken from the robust shall be saved. But those who judged you, I will judge,

and your children I will save: And I will feed your enemies with their own flesh: and they shall be drunk with their own blood as with new wine: and all flesh shall know that I the Lord am your savior and your redeemer, the strong one of Jacob. That whole forty-ninth chapter, of which these are the final verses, treats of Christ, and introduces Christ speaking; who explains his calling, and the efficacy of his doctrine, and its most ample fruit throughout the whole world, when he was given not only to raise up the tribes of Jacob, but also for a light to the Gentiles, that the salvation of the Lord might be even to the end of the earth, and having shown the utility of his passion, and the great happiness of believers, he exhorts to thanksgiving: then indeed he kindly consoles Zion, which was complaining that it was deserted by God, promising that it would be glorious throughout the whole world, with all flowing to it, and its enemies crushed. We do not dwell on the glosses of the Jews: They are blind guides, nor do they agree among themselves: some snatch these things to Cyrus, others to something else. Nor do we here lend our ears to Hugo, who thinks that Isaiah is speaking in this chapter and explaining his own embassy and office: even if this pleased Zwingli, and Wolfgang Musculus contends far more audaciously that Isaiah is dealing with his own calling and the leading of Israel out of Babylon, so much so that he asserts that those who explain the cause of Christ are also defaming the cause of Christ with the suspicion of a twisted exposition of the Scriptures. But the other Hugo, we point to Grotius, seduced by the Jews, as it appears, twists this illustrious prophecy to Isaiah in such a way that it is more worthy of detestation than refutation: Let it be weighed, I beseech you, what kind of glosses these are: The Lord called me from the womb: The Hebrews interpret this concerning the excellent temperament of the brain: with which God is accustomed to endow prophets from their first birth. He remembered my name: he gave me a beautiful name, by which salvation to come from the Lord is signified. I have given you as a light to the Gentiles: that you may turn them also (Isaiah) from idols, and thus save very many. Princes shall arise and shall worship. Eliakim and good princes shall treat you with great honor. In an acceptable time I have heard you: interceding for Hezekiah. In the day of salvation I have helped you and preserved you: I have ensured that neither the Assyrians nor Sobna with his faction can harm you. And I have given you for a covenant of the people, that is, through you I have renewed my covenant with the people. These are his words: let us not ascribe others, which are of the same stamp. By which agreement it is too manifest that illustrious axioms, most proper to Christ, which were predicted by the Prophet concerning him, and explained by the Apostles concerning the same, are twisted toward others. With great consensus, indeed, the ancient Fathers teach that these things are to be understood of no one else than Christ, and they solidly demonstrate it, which was done especially by Cyril of Alexandria among the Greeks, and by Jerome among the Latin Doctors of the Church, with a distinguished explanation of the whole chapter. To whom not only our blessed Luther in his Commentary on Isaiah, Vol. III, Latin, Jena, with the entire choir of our Doctors, but also almost all of the Papist interpreters, Leo Castrius, Forerius, Sanctius, Cornelius a Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, and others, nay, even most of the Reformed, subscribe. Oecolampadius, certainly a not much less learned interpreter of Scripture than Zwingli, did not hesitate to give the name of Messiah to the last part of Isaiah, which he begins from this chapter XLIX, because in it all things that were fulfilled through him are so written down that even the companions of the cross are not passed over in silence. Calvin, however, who otherwise willingly perverts oracles concerning Christ, observes that even the Jews who have some sound mind confess that this passage can be understood of no one else than the Messiah. But soon he himself denies that the third verse and those following, in which certainly no other than he who began to speak from the beginning of the chapter continues the discourse, are to be restricted to the person of Christ, and he extends them to the members of Christ, not without a significant corruption of the text. But the dispute to enter into a discussion with these men is neither our duty now, nor our established practice. What could be clearer than that those words in v. 6, Behold I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, are explained as referring to CHRIST in Acts 13:47? And those in v. 8, In an acceptable time I have heard thee, as referring to the time of the Christian Church in 2 Cor. 6:2? Therefore, it is that Christ who cries out: Hear, O islands, and attend, ye people from afar, calling even the most remote nations; and who testifies, The Lord hath called me from the womb, and hath made my mouth like a sharp sword: from whose mouth a sword sharp on both sides went forth, Apoc. 1:16. And the same one continues: The Lord said to me, Thou art my servant Israel: Whether because he is an Israelite and of the seed of Israel, as most interpret with Cyril and Jerome; or because he is truly Israel, that is, prevailing with God, when he overcame the angry God with his obedience, and rescinded the sentence of condemnation passed upon us. Because I will be glorified in thee, which Jerome observes can be understood of no other of the servants than of CHRIST. The God of all, says St. Cyril, had been glorified even through the holy Prophets, but not in them. But in Christ, in an unusual and unheard-of manner, as one in whom he was glorified. And Christ being glorified, the Father is glorified in him. We see him shining forth in him through divine authority and power and energy in all things through sanctification and justice and every kind of clemency. The same one complains that he has labored in vain, because Israel will not be gathered, which Jerome calls a most powerful testimony against the Jews. It is helpful to explain this in the words of Cyril: The Savior of all appeared, that he might free the whole world from the malice of the Devil, from death and from sin, and might enlighten with holy gifts those who approach him through faith. But they were called to this before others, those sprung from the blood of Israel, and preferred to the Gentiles with this honor, so that Jesus says: I was not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. But they, having obtained so illustrious an honor, became infidels, and bold apostates, and dire and proud despisers. Therefore God raises up the Messiah: It is a small thing that thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to convert the dregs of Israel. Behold I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth, that thou mayest enlighten the whole world, and make my salvation, through which all are saved, reach even to the ends of the earth, as Jerome's paraphrase has it. Furthermore, it is added: Thus saith the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One, to the soul that is despised, to the nation that is abhorred, to the servant of rulers: Kings shall see and princes shall rise up and adore the Lord, who is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, who hath chosen thee. Which some among Jerome, Thomas, and others refer to the vile Jews liberated from Babylon; Hugo to Cyrus. But it is manifest that the discourse is directed to the same person, and that the same one is here said to be chosen by the Lord, who was previously called from the womb and glorified in the eyes of the Lord and called his servant and placed by the Lord like an arrow. And therefore Jerome praises the paraphrase of Theodotion and Aquila: to him who despises his soul, who is an abomination to the nation, who is a servant of rulers, which he says clearly fits the person of Christ, who laid down his soul for all, is an abomination to the nation of the Jews, whom they curse three times every day under the name of Nazarenes in their synagogues, who was a servant of rulers and so humble that he stood before Annas and Caiaphas and was handed over to Pilate and Herod to be crucified. Now the acceptable time, in which he was heard by the Lord, according to the Psalmist, is the time of the passion and resurrection, Ps. 69:12, 14, in which God was reconciled to the human race through CHRIST, which the Apostle also refers to the first advent, 2 Cor. 6:2. Whose footsteps Jerome therefore followed, like children, tracing letters over the outlined lines of a teacher. Nor can it be doubted that through the passion and resurrection Christ was given as a covenant of the people, that he might say to those who are bound, Go forth, and to those who are in darkness, Be enlightened, whence they found an abundance of pasture not only in Jerusalem, but everywhere among the Gentiles, John 10:9. They shall not hunger nor thirst, and the heat and the sun shall not burn them. Which happiness fully befalls the faithful in the other life, Apoc. 7:16. But that the fruit of the passion and resurrection may redound to all the Gentiles, it is predicted that Zion is not to be abandoned entirely, but that first of all a great number of Gentiles from all the regions of the earth are to be brought in; so that the purple of kings and the burning gems of diadems, which Jerome says to Laeta, may adorn the image of the saving cross. Thus saith the Lord: I will lift up my hand to the Gentiles and I will lift up my standard to the islands and they shall bring thy sons in their bosom; which Cyril, Jerome, and others rightly accept concerning the sign or banner of the cross. Hence therefore a doubt arises: Shall the prey be taken away from the strong? or can the captives be delivered by the JUST ONE? as the Hebrew has it. Some interpret this concerning the rescue of the Gentiles from the power of the Devil and the hands of tyrants, who, while they act most unjustly, wish to be considered just. But as that liberation rests upon the redemption made through Christ's death and resurrection, and comes about through its power: so the Lord here without ambiguity looked to the same: Indeed the captivity shall be taken away from the strong, and that which has been taken from the robust shall be snatched away. So that the sense may be: Why could not the Gentiles be snatched from this giant, so that they may be converted to the Lord, since all captivity is to be taken from that strong armed one, when the whole human race shall be freed from his power; under which it was held by the just judgment of God. According to Cyril, the meaning of these words is this: The world was captured by the Devil and by the flock of demons, nor was it possible for anyone on earth to escape the tyranny of their perversity. But I, says the Savior, will take the prey from the strong and, the yoke of servitude being cast off, I will render them illustrious by the grace of liberty. To which sentiment he brings the words of Christ in Luke 11: For how can anyone enter into the house of the strong one and plunder his vessels, unless he first binds the strong one and then plunders his vessels. For the house of the strong one, i.e. He understands this world to be Satan's, not because it truly was, but because it had been occupied by him. But after the incarnate Word himself entered it, having bound the strong man with ineffable power, he drew to himself his vessels, i.e., those who once felt the same as he did. Now therefore, as a certain one of the more recent theologians says, the Messiah dealt with the just God and the strong Satan, when he loosened our captivity; with God, as a just Judge, whose justice he was satisfying; with the Devil, as a Tyrant, whose strength he was breaking. He who was intoxicated with blood, as if with new wine, acted against himself as if drunk during the Lord's passion. He is fed with his own flesh, when we, who were his servants through the fall, crush his head in Christ. The authors of the notes to the Dutch translation combine both meanings regarding the victory of Christ's resurrection against spiritual enemies and the liberation from the Babylonian captivity. And we have already shown how those things can be combined. Nor indeed is that victory alone the foundation of all our liberation: but after Christ obtained the victory, he also transmitted the victory to us, as Cyril says again, and gave us the ability to trample upon serpents and scorpions and to snatch away Satan's other subjects also, as if they were booty. Let us therefore do this, let us resist the Devil through faith: let us fight against the princes and powers, against the world-rulers of these darknesses, clothed with the power of the Lord. Having been liberated from his hand, let us not again subject ourselves to him through sins. Let us constantly adhere to Christ the Redeemer with true faith and faithful obedience.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET CIBABO HOSTES TVOS CAR- NIBVS SVIS.) Committam illos inter se, Persas cum Me- dis, deinde Persas & Medos cum Babyloniis: qui omnes olim Nabuchodonosoro militaverant.

Quum totam Prophetiam spectare ad benefi- cia spiritualia Messiæ, & vocationem gentium pro- xime prædictam esse hactenus ostensum sit, glossæ illi Grotianæ à Judæis petitæ de liberatione ex capti- vitate Babylonica, quamvis eam etiam Musculus amplexus sit, locus non est; Sed vi contextus de li- beratione è spirituali captivitate, cujus merito & virtute gentes ad regnum Christi convertuntur, & efficaciter Satanæ, qui prædam istam detinuit, eri- piendæ erant, q. d. Qui à diabolo poterant eripi gen- tes, quas tanquam prædas captas tenet in sua manu? Justa enim captivitas est infidelium sub potestate Sa- tanæ. Id ergo se facturum testatur Dominus v. 25. quem Christum esse è verbis ejus Luc. 11, 21. ubi ad hunc locum respexisse omnino videtur, apparet: Cum fortis armatus custodit atrium suum, in pace sunt ea, quæ possidet, si autem fortior eo superveniens, vicerit eum, universa arma ejus auferet, in quibus confidebat, & spolia ejus distrihuet. Et qui hæc lo- quitur apud Prophetam, se describit, quod sit Salva- tor, & Redemptor fortis Jacob & Israelis, cui ille tu- to inniti vera fide potest. Fortem Israelis Hiero- nymus intelligit, qui cum Israele luctatus est, & au- xiliator fuit virtutis Jacob, quod is tum agnoscendus sit Redemptor. De redemptione per Sanguinem Christi hæc intelligunt nonnulli, qua è potestate Satanæ liberati sumus Ebr. 2, 14. Horum verbo- rum inquit Cyrillus,mens hæc est, Captus est orbis ter- rarum à Diabolo, & à grege Dæmoniorum, nec erat cuiquam in terra integrum eorum perversitates, ty- rannidem effugere. Sed ego, inquit Dominus, detra- ham & liberabo injuriis affectos. Verum quamvis redemptio illa ut causa meritoria recte adducatur prædæ hujus per vocationem gentium Satanæ eri- piendæ, Ipsa tamen ereptio actualis è regno Satanæ, quæ virtute meriti Christi sit, rectius hic intelligitur. Eodem recidit quoque Brentii ἐξήγησις, etsi per gigantem κτ' τὸ ῥητὸν intelligat Reges & tyrannos, sub quibus sunt gentes ad Christum convertendæ, illis- que quasi eripiendæ, ut Christo se submittant. Quæ Hieronymi etiam interpretatio est. Cætera de judi- candis illis, qui judicarunt Sionem, hostibus Eccle- siæ recte accipiuntur, non tamen ad Babylonios & Idumæos solum, aut ad antiqua tempora restringen- da sunt: Imo vi συνεχείας N. T. tempora peculiari- ter concernunt. q. d. Porro hostes tuos, qui obsistunt tibi, cibabo carnibus suis & inebriabuntur sanguine suo, quasi musto, i. e. sibi ipsis erunt exitio, efficiam ut hostes in sua viscera sæviant, & sese ipsi conficiant sua tyrannide. Siquidem tyranni, dum Ecclesiam perse- quuntur, non raro sibimetipsis maxima damna in- ferant, suaque regna suis ipsorum viribus evertant. Addimus autem ad illustrationem hujus capitis, quæ in programmate Paschali proposuimus.

Vicit Leo de tribu Juda. Occisus est agnus, sed vicit Leo; vicit Judæorum blasphemias in patibulo, fortem armatum alligavit in atrio, & de ipso mortis imperio triumphavit. Ubi sunt opprobria tua, Judæe? ubi sunt fabula vasa captivitatis? ubi est mors victo- ria tua? Confusus est calumniator: raptor spoliatus est. Novum genus potentiæ hactenus victoriosa mors obstupescit. Liceat ita nobis verba S. Bernh. nostra facere. Vere novum genus potentiæ, novum genus victoriæ! Consumta est plane mors in victoria sua, in- quit S. August. Serm. CLXI. de Tempore, cum Chri- stum inferni legibus subjiciens, ipsa se, cum vincit, ob- ruit. In eo enim, in quo illum, quem se superasse crede- bat, possedit, ab eo victa est, cum resurrexit. Ubi est, in- ferne, victoria tua? ubi est mors stimulus tuus? Qui per Oseam quondam (ita Hieron. in Epitaphio Ne- potiani ad Heliodorum morti insultat) tibi rigidus minabatur: Ero mors tua, ò mors; ero morsus tuus, in- ferne, illius morte tu mortua es, illius morte nos vivi- mus: devorasti & devorata es; dumque assumti corpo- ris Christi solicitans illecebra, & avidis faucibus præ- dam putas, interiora tua adunco dente confossa sunt. Gratias TIBI, CHRISTE Salvator, tua agimus crea- tura, quod tam potentem adversarium nostrum, dum occidereris, occidisti. Magna est adversarii hujus po- tentia: qui fortis ille armatus est, atrium suum custo- diens: Sed fortior eo est, qui supervenit, gigas gemi- næ substantiæ: Dominus fortis & potens, Dominus potens in prælio. Hic ergo devicit eum, & univer- sa arma ejus abstulit, in quibus confidebat, & spolia ejus distribuit: Ille mortis habebat imperium & per mortem imperabat toti mundo: Sed Redemptor noster etsi carnis & sanguinis nostri similiter, uti pueri, particeps factus sit, ac mortem pro nobis gu- stare debuerit, per mortem destruxit eum, qui habe- bat mortis imperium, i.e. Diabolum, & liberavit eos, qui timore mortis per totam vitam obnoxii erant servi- tuti. Hæc dum grata & debita memoria recolimus in Ecclesia, juvat ipsummet victorem nostrum au- gustissimum audire, quomodo gloriosam hanc vi- ctoriam adversus robustum illum Gigantem per E- saiam prædixerit. Num quid tolletur à forti præda? aut quod captum fuit à robusto, salvum esse poterit? Quia hæc dicit Dominus: Equidem & captivitas à forti tolletur: & quod ablatum fuerit à robusto, sal- vabitur. Eos vero, qui judicaverunt te, ego judicabo,

& filios tuos ego salvabo: Et cibabo hostes tuos carni- bus suis: & quasi musto sanguine suo inebriabuntur: & sciet omnis caro, quia ego Dominus salvans te & redemtor tuus fortis Iacob. Totum istud caput nonum & quadragesimum, cujus haec extrema sunt com- mata, de Christo agit, & Christum loquentem in- troducit; qui vocationem suam, & doctrinae effica- ciam, ejusque fructum longe amplissimum per to- tum orbem, quum non ad erigendas tantum tribus Jacob, sed in lucem etiam gentium datus sit, ut salus Domini usque ad extremum terrae, exponit, & ostensa passionis suae utilitate, ac magna credentium felici- tate, ad gratiarum actionem hortatur: tum vero benigne consolatur Sion, quae se è Deo desertam conquerebatur, promittens, eam toto orbe fore gloriosam, omnibus ad ipsam confluentibus, ejus- que inimicis contritis. Non moramur Judaeorum glossas: Caeci Ductores sunt, nec inter se conve- niunt: nonnullis ad Cyrum, aliis alio haec abripien- tibus. Neque Hugoni hic aures praebemus, qui Esaiam hoc capite loqui & legationem ac officium suum exponere, putat: etsi & Zvinglio hoc placue- rit, & longe audacius Wolffg. Musculus Esaiam de sua vocatione, & de eductione Israëlis è Babylone agere contendat, adeo ut eos quoque, qui de Chri- sto explicant causam Christi suspicione tortae Scriptu- rarum expositionis infamare, asserat. Hugo vero alter, Grotius indigitamus, à Judaeis, ut apparet, sedu- ctus, ad Esaiam vaticinium illustre ita detorquet, ut detestatione, quam refutatione dignior sit: Perpen- datur, obsecro, qualia ista sint gloffemata: Dominus ab utero vocavit me: Hebraei interpretantur de egregia temperatura cerebri: qua Deus à primo ortu donare solet Prophetas. Recordatus est nominis mei: indidit mihi nomen pulchrum, quo salus à Domino ventura significatur. Dedi te in lucem gen- tium: ut illos quoque (Esaia) ab idolis avertas, & sic plurimos serves. Consurgent Principes & adora- bunt. Magno honore te afficiet Eliakim, bonique Principes. In tempore placito exaudivi te: pro Eze- chia interpellantem. In die salutis auxiliatus sum tui & servavi te: effeci, ne quid Assyrii aut Sobna cum sua factione tibi nocere possint. Et dedi te in foedus populi, id est, per te renovavi meum cum po- pulo foedus. Haec ille: ne alia adscribamus, quae ejus- dem sunt commatis. Quo pacto illustria, Christoque maxime propria axiomata, quae à Propheta de ipso praedicta, ab Apostolis de eodem explicata sunt, ad alios detorqueri, nimis manifestum est. Magno uti- que consensu Patres antiqui de nullo alio haec acci- pienda esse, quam de Christo, docent, solideque de- monstrant, quod cumprimis à Cyrillo Alexand. inter Graecos, ab Hieron. inter Latinos Ecclesiae Doctores, insigni totius capitis explicatione, factum. Quibus non modo B. Luther noster Commentario in Esaiam Tom. III. Latin. Jenens. cum universo Doctorum nostrorum choro, sed è Pontificiis quoque Interpp. pene omnes, Leo Castrius, Forerius, Sanctius, Corne- lius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, alii, imo è Refor- matis etiam plerique subscribunt. Oecolampadius certe haut paulo eruditior Zwinglio Scripturae in- terpres ultimae parti Esaiae, quam ab hoc cap. XLIX. orditur, Messiae nomen dare non dubitavit, quod in ea ita universa, quae per ipsum impleta, perscripta sint, ut & crucis Socii non taceantur. Calvinus vero, qui a- lias libenter oracula de Christo pervertit, observat, Judaeos quoque quibus aliquid est sanae mentis, non de alio, quam de Messia hunc locum intelligi posse confiteri. Sed mox ipse versum tertium & subsequentes, qui- bus utique non alius, quam qui ab initio capitis lo- qui cepit, orationem continuat, ad Christi personam restringendos negat, & ad Christi membra, non absque insigni textus corruptela extendit. Sed disputa- tionem cum istis hominibus ingredi nostri neque muneris nunc est, neque instituti. Quid luculen- tius, quam quod verba illa v. 6. Ecce dedi te in lu- cem gentium, de CHRISTO Act. 13, 47. & illa v. 8. In tempore placito exaudivi te, de tempore Ecclesiæ Christianæ 2. Cor. 6, 2. explicentur? Christus ergo ille est, qui exclamat: Audite Insulæ, & attendite populi de longe, gentes compellans etiam remotissi- mas; quique testatur, Dominus ab utero me vocavit, & posuit os meum, quasi gladium: de cujus ore gla- dius utraque parte acutus exibat Apoc. 1, 16. Atque idem pergit: Dominus dixit mihi, Servus meus es tu Israël: Sive quod Israë̈lita & de semine Israël sit, ut interpretantur plerique cum Cyrillo & Hierony- mo; sive quod vere Israël, hoc est, Deo prævalens, cum Deum iratum obedientia sua vicit, ac senten- tiam damnationis in nos latam rescidit. Quia in te gloriabor, quod de nullo alio servorum intelligi posse observat Hieronymus, quam de CHRISTO. Glorificatus erat universorum Deus, inquit S. Cyril- lus, etiam per Prophetas sanctos, sed non in illis. In Christo autem inconsueto & inusitato modo, ut qui in illo glorificatus fuerit. Et Christo glorificato, Pater in ipso glorificatur. Videmus in illo relucentem eum per divinam autoritatem ac potentiam & energian in omnibus per sanctificationem & justitiam & o- mnimodam clementiam. Queritur idem, quod in vacuum laborarit, quia Israël nolit congregari, quod fortissimum Hieronymus testimonium dicit con- tra Judæos. Juvat id verbis Cyrilli explicare: Ap- paruit universorum Servator, ut totum orbem terra- rum à Diaboli malitia, à morte & à peccato libera- ret, & sanctis charismatis illustraret eos, qui per fidem ad ipsum accedunt, Vocati sunt autem ad hoc ante alios, orti ex sanguine Israëlis, & hoc honore præpositi gentibus, ut dicat Jesus: Non sum missus nisi ad oves perditas domus Israël. Sed hi adeo inclutum hono- rem sortiti infideles facti sunt, & apostatæ audaces, & contemptores diri & superbi. Erigit ergo Deus Messiam: Parum est, ut sis mihi Servus ad suscitan- das tribus Jacob & fæces Israël convertendas. Ecce dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad ex- tremum terræ, ut illumines universum mundum, & salutem meam, per quam omnes salvi fiunt, usque ad extrema terræ facias pervenire, ut habet para- phrasis Hieronymi. Additur porro: Hæc dicit Dominus, Redemtor Israël Sanctus ejus ad contem- tibilem animam, ad abominatam gentem, ad servum Dominorum: Reges videbunt & consurgent Prin- cipes & adorabunt Dominum, qui fidelis est, & San- ctus Israël, qui elegit te. Quæ nonnulli apud Hiero- nymum, Thomas & alii referunt ad viles Judæos Ba- bylone liberatos; Hugo ad Cyrum. Sed manifestum est, ad eundem directum esse sermonem, eundem- que hic electum dici à Domino, qui antea ab utero vocatus & glorificatus in oculis Domini & servus e- jus dictus est ac positus à Domino sicut sagitta. Ideo- que laudat Hieronymus Theodotionis & Aquilæ pa- raphrasin: ei qui despicit animam, qui abominatio- ni est genti, qui servus est Principum, quod manife- ste Christi personæ convenire ait, qui animam suam posuit pro omnibus, abominationi est genti Judæo- rum, cui ter per singulos dies sub nomine Nazareno- rum maledicunt in Synagogis suis, qui servus fuit Principem & tam humilis, ut staret ante Hannam & Caipham & crucifigendus Pilato & Herodi traderetur. Jam tempus placitum, quo exauditus est à Domino, teste Hieropsalte, tempus passionis est, & resurre- ctionis. Psal. 69, 12. 14. quo Deus placatus est per CHRISTVM humano generi, quod etiam Apo- stolus ad primum adventum refert, 2. Cor. 6, 2. Cu- jus proinde vestigia sequutus Hieronymus, instar parvulorum, super adumbratas lineas Præceptoris li- ne- teras impressit. Neque dubitari potest, per passio- nem & resurrectionem Christum in fœdus populi datum esse, ut diceret his, qui vincti sunt, Exite, & his, qui in tenebris sunt, illuminamini, unde super vias pascuorum non Hierosolymis tantum, sed ubi- que gentium copiam pabuli invenerunt Joh. 10,9. Non esuriunt neque sitiunt, & non urit eos æstus & Sol. Quæ felicitas plene obtingit fidelibus in al- tera vita Apoc. 7, 16. Ut autem fructus passionis & resurrectionis ad gentes omnes redundet, Zio- nem quidem non relinquendam penitus, sed impri- mis magno numero gentes ex omnibus terræ plagis adducendas esse, prædicitur; ut Regum purpuras & ardentes Diadematum gemmas, quod Hieronymus ad Lætam ait, patibuli salutaris pictura condecoret. Sic dicit Dominus: Tollo ad gentes manum meam & ad Insulas tollam signum meum & adducent filios in sinu suo; quod de signo vel vexillo crucis Cyrillus, Hieronymus, & alii recte accipiunt. Hinc ergo dubium nascitur: Numquid tolletur à forti præda? aut captivi à JUSTO liberari poterunt? ut Ebræa habent. De Gentium ereptione è potestate Dia- boli, & Tyrannorum manibus, qui cum injustissi- me agant, justi haberi volunt, nonnulli interpretan- tur. Sed uti liberatio illa nititur redemtione per Christi mortem & resurrectionem facta, ejusque virtu- te contingit: ita eandem hic citra ambiguum respe- xit Dominus: Equidem captivitas à forti tolletur, & quod ablatum fuerit à robusto, eripietur. Ut sen- sus sit: Quidni Gentiles eripi possent huic giganti, ut ad Dominum convertantur, quum captivitas omnis à forti illo armato tollenda sit, quando totum genus humanum è potestate illius liberabitur; Sub qua justo Dei judicio tenebatur. Secundum Cyrill. horum ver- borum mens hæc est: Captus est orbis terrarum à Diabolo & à grege Dæmoniorum, nec erat cuiquam in terra integrum eorum perversitatis tyrannidem effugere. Sed ego, inquit Servator, detraham forti prædam & jugo servitutis abjecto libertatis gratia il- lustres reddam. In quam sententiam confert ver- ba Christi Luc. 11. Quomodo enim potest quis in- gredi domum fortis & vasa ejus diripere, nisi prius ligaverit fortem & tum vasa ejus diripiat. Domum enim fortis i. e. Satanæ hunc orbem terrarum intelli- git, non quod vere esset, sed quod ab eo occupatus esset Sed postquam ingressum est ipsam incarnatum ver- bum, ineffabili potentia ligato forti vasa ejus, i. e. qui eadem cum ipso quondam sentiebant, ad se traduxit. Jam ergo, quod è recentioribus Theologis quidam ait, cum Deo justo & Satana forti egit Messias, cum nostram solvit captivitatem, cum Deo, ceu justo Ju- dice, cujus Justitiæ satisfaciebat; cum Diabolo, ut Tyranno, cujus robur infringebat. Qui sanguine inebriatus est, ceu musto, cum veluti ebrius in passio- ne Domini contra seipsum egit. Carne sua cibatur, cum nos, qui servi ejus eramus, per lapsum, caput ei conterimus in Christo. Vtrumque sensum de victo- ria resurrectionis Christi adversus spirituales hostes, & liberatione è captivitate Babylonia conjungunt Autores notarum ad translationem Belgicam. Et quomodo illa conjungi queant, jam ostendimus. Nec vero solum victoria illa omnis nostræ libera- tionis fundamentum est: sed postquam obtinuit Chri- stus victoriam, ad nos quoque victoriam transmisit, ut iterum Cyrillus, deditque nobis facultatem conculcan- di serpentes & scorpiones Satanæque alios etiam subdi- tos ejus, ceu prædam eripiendi. Hoc ergo agamus, Diabolo resistamus per fidem: pugnemus adversus Principes & potestates, adversus mundi rectores tene- brarum harum, induti virtute Domini. Liberati è manu ejus, ne denuo nos per peccata ipsi subda- mus. Christo Redemtori vera fide ac fideli obse- quio constanter adhæreamus.

## 50:1 Argument
CHAPTER L.

The Synagogue remains repudiated not because of God's impotence, but because of its own iniquities, refusing to receive Christ, who omitted nothing that ought to have been done so that he might be received; nay, for their sake he even willed to be struck and to suffer insults; therefore he declares that the Synagogue will perish with the pains of conscience.

Verse 1.

WHERE IS THIS BILL OF YOUR MOTHER'S DIVORCE, WITH WHICH I DISMISSED HER, OR WHO IS MY CREDITOR, TO WHOM I HAVE SOLD YOU? Morose husbands give a bill of divorce to their wives for trivial reasons, Deut. 24. Fathers, sometimes pressed by debt, sell their children, Exod. 21, 7. Neither applies to me. It remains, therefore, that the cause of this separation and of your misery lies within yourselves; it is yours to remove it.

Because the inquiry here is about the bill of divorce, there can be no doubt that the preceding passages do not pertain to the times of the Babylonian liberation, but look toward the times of the New Testament. For only to these does the complaint about the bill of divorce and the rejection of the Jews apply, the causes of which are now being set forth. I see, says the Synagogue of the Jews, as interpreted by our Brentius, a very great multitude of Gentiles acknowledging the Messiah and being gathered to the Church of the people of God. What, therefore, has happened, that we Jews are cast away and are not received with such a multitude into the communion of the benefits of the Messiah? Have we not been until now the chosen people of God? Was not the Messiah promised to us? Why, therefore, are we now expelled and excluded by the Messiah? But the Son of God, the true Messiah, answers with this discourse which follows, and teaches that the blame for the rejection of the Jews is not to be transferred to himself, but to the Jews themselves: for he had omitted absolutely nothing of those things by which they might be stirred to recognize the Messiah and obtain salvation; but their impiety was so great that they not only despised the offered Messiah, but even drove him to the cross. Where, he says, is this bill of divorce of your mother, with which I dismissed her? You Jews complain that I have cast you off and repudiated you, so that you are no longer the people of God: but you do me a manifest injury. For if I have repudiated you, come now, produce the bill of divorce by which you may prove that you have been repudiated by me. For the law is, Deut. 24, that a husband intending to repudiate his wife must give her a bill of divorce. I have, however, acknowledged your mother until now as my wife. Wherefore, if I have repudiated her, as I am accused by you, it must be testified by a bill of divorce. Next, who is my creditor, to whom I have sold you? You accuse me of having handed you over and sold you to another, so that you are no longer the true people of God. But I am accused by you most unjustly. For if I sold you, show the usurer or merchant who bought you from me. For the law, Exod. 21, allows a father to sell his daughter, but under certain conditions, so that a legitimate contract is made between the seller and the buyer. If, therefore, I sold you, come, show the buyer who may testify that he bought you from me. But it is mere calumny. For truly you were cast away not by my fault, but by your own; you yourselves, without any divorce, without any legitimate contract, deserted me, and you follow after strange husbands and Lords. Behold, for because of your iniquities you have been sold, and because of your crimes your mother has been dismissed or repudiated. That is, your iniquities and crimes are the cause why you have been cast away; what, therefore, are those iniquities and crimes on account of which the Jews have been repudiated, so that they are not the people of God? Although they are many and great, yet here only one crime is recounted, which, as it embraces all others in itself, is by far the most serious of all. Because I came, and there was no man: I called, and there was none, etc. Which Jerome explained thus: He speaks to the people of the Jews concerning Sion, who had previously said: The Lord has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me. Do you think that because of my hardness your mother, the earthly Jerusalem, has been cast out, and that I, of a rigid mind, gave her a bill of divorce: and do you not rather understand, which is the truth, that she departed from me by her own fault? Even when I said to her: Cease to do evil, learn to do good: she would not hear me, but turned her back upon me as she departed. Whence I spoke to her children: Woe to them, because they have departed from me. They are manifest who have acted impiously against me. And to her, Your departure will instruct you, and your malice will correct me, and you shall know that it is an evil thing for you that you have left me. But perhaps you cannot show a bill of divorce, and some creditor of mine, demanding money, and I not having what I might pay, took you in compensation for the debt! It is not so: But I will show you why I have forsaken the mother with her children. Your crimes and sins have sold you to the Demons, so that, ensnared by the pleasures of the present age, you might forsake your parent, and she her spouse: Whence I could no longer hold your adulterous mother, but, as she wished to go, I permitted it. But that everyone is sold by his own sins, while, being left to our own free will, we are led by our own will either to good or to evil, the Apostle Paul also teaches: But I am carnal, sold under sin. For he who commits sin is the slave of sin; and as the avaricious and robbers are slaves of mammon: so every sin dominates sinners, to whom it is said: Let not sin reign in your mortal body. But so that you may know that your mother was not repudiated by me, but departed by her own will, after many benefits, I assumed a human body: and I spoke not through the Prophets, but present: I came and there was no man, or human being, etc.

Verse of the same.

Latin:

CAPUT L.

Synagoga non ex Dei impotentia, sed propter suas iniquitates manet repudiata Chri- stum nolens recipere, qui nihil prætermi- sit, quod agendum fuerat, ut recipere- tur, imo ipsorum causa etiam percuti, & contumelias pati voluit, ideo Synagogam doloribus conscientiæ interituram denun- ciat.

Vers. 1.

QVIS EST HIC LIBER REPVDIi MATRIS VESTRÆ, QVO DIMISI EAM, AVT QVIS EST CREDITOR MEVS, CVI VENDIDI VOS) Morosi ma- riti levibus de causis instrumentum divortii uxoribus dant Deut. 24. Patres interdum ære alieno pressi, liberos ven- dunt. Exod. 21,7. Neutrum in me convenit. Restat ergo ut diffidii hujus miseriæque vestræ causa in vobis hæreat, eam amoliri vestrum est.

QUia hic de libro repudii quæritur, dubium nul- lum esse potest, antecedentia non pertinere ad tempora liberationis Babylonicæ, sed ad Novi Testamenti tempora spectare. His enim demum convenit querela de libello repudii, & de rejectio- ne Judæorum, cujus causæ nunc exponuntur. Vi- deo, inquit Judæorum Synagoga, interprete Bren- tio nostro, maximam gentium multitudinem agno- scere Messiam, & congregari ad Ecclesiam populi Dei. Quid igitur accidit, quod nos Judæi abjicimur, & non recipimur tanta multitudine ad communio- nem beneficiorum Messiæ? Annon fuimus nos hacte- nus electus populus Dei? Annon promissus est nobis Messias? Cur igitur nunc à Messia expellimur & ex- cludimur. Respondet autem Filius Dei verus Mes- sias hac concione, quæ sequitur, & docet culpam rejectionis Judæorum non in se, sed in Judæos ipsos transferendam: Se enim nihil prorsus earum rerum omisisse, quibus ad cognoscendum Messiam, & consequendam salutem excitarentur; sed tan- tam esse ipsorum impietatem, ut oblatum Messiam non solum contemserint, verum etiam in crucem adegerint. Quis est, inquit, hic liber repudii ma- tris vestræ, quo dimisi eam? Vos Judæi conqueri- mini, quod ego vos abjecerim & repudiaverim, ut non sitis amplius populus Dei: sed facitis mihi lu- culentam injuriam. Nam si ego vos repudiavi, agite dum, producite libellum repudii, quo probe- tis, vos à me repudiatos. Lex enim est Deut. 24. quod maritus repudiaturus uxorem debeat ei dare li- bellum repudii. Agnovi autem matrem vestram hactenus tanquam meam uxorem. Quare, si ego eam repudiavi, quemadmodum accusor à vobis, li- bello repudii testificandum erit. Deinde, quis est creditor meus, cui vendidi vos? Vos accusatis me, quod ego tradiderim & vendiderim vos alteri, ut jam non sitis verus populus Dei. Sed accusor à vobis injustissime. Nam si vendidi vos, ostendite fœneratorem, seu mercatorem, qui vos à me eme- rit. Lex enim Exod 21. concedit, ut pater vendat filiam suam, sed certis conditionibus, ut fiat legiti- mus contractus inter venditorem & emptorem. Si ergo vos vendidi, agite, ostendite emptorem, qui testificetur se vos à me emisse. Sed mera est ca- lumnia. Profecto enim non mea, sed vestra culpa abjecti estis; Vos ipsi sine ullo repudio, sine ullo legitimo contractu, deserivistis me, & sectamini alienos maritos & Dominos. Ecce enim propter iniquitates vestras venditi estis, & propter scelera ve- stra dimissa seu repudiata est mater vestra. Hoc est, Iniquitates & scelera vestra in causa sunt, cur ab- jecti sitis; quæ ergo sunt iniquitates & scelera illa, propter quæ Judæi repudiati sunt, ut non sint po- pulus Dei? Etsi ea multa sunt & magna, tamen hic recensetur unum tantum scelus, quod, ut omnia alia in se complectitur, ita est longe omnium gra- vissimum. Quia veni, & non erat vir: vocavi, & non erat &c. Quod ita exposuit Hieronymus: Loquitur ad populum Judæorum super Sion, qui prius dixerat: Dereliquit me Dominus, & Dominus ob- litus est mei. Putatis mea duritia matrem vestram, terrenam Hierusalem esse projectam, & quod ego mentis rigidæ dederim ei libellum repudii: & non po- tius quod verum est, intelligitis illam suo a me vitio re- cessisse? Dicente etiam me ad eam: Quiescite ini- que agere, discite bonum facere: audire me noluit, sed vertit contra me scapulam recedentem. Unde lo- quutus sum filiis ejus: Væ illis, quoniam recesse- runt à me. Manifesti sunt, qui impie egerunt in me. Et ad ipsam, Erudiet te abscessio tua, & mali- tia tua corripiet me & scies quoniam malum tibi sit, quod reliqueris me. Sed forsitan libellum repudii ostendere non potestis, & aliquis creditor meus exigens pecuniam, me non habente quod redderem, vos in de- biti compensationem suscepit! Non est ita: Sed ego ostendam vobis, quamobrem matrem cum filiis dereli- querim. Scelera vestra atque peccata vos Dæmo- nibus vendiderunt, ut præsentis seculi voluptatibus irretiti, & vos parentem, & ille conjugem derelin- queret: Unde adulteram matrem vestram ultra te- nere non potui, sed volentem abire, permisi. Quod autem peccatis suis unusquisque venundatur, dum proprio arbitrio derelicti, nostra voluntate vel ad bo- num vel ad malum ducimur, & Paulus Apostolus docet: Ego autem carnalis sum, venundatus sub peccato. Qui enim facit peccatum, servus est peccati; Et quomodo avari & raptores servi sunt mammonæ: Sic omne peccatum dominatur peccato- ribus, quibus dicitur: Non regnet peccatum in mortali vestro corpore. Ut autem sciatis non à me repudiatam matrem vestram, sed voluntate pro- pria recessisse, post multa beneficia, humanum corpus assumpsi: & nequaquam per Prophetas, sed præsens lo- quutus sum: Veni & non erat vir, sive homo, &c.

Vers. eod.

## 50:2
BECAUSE I CAME AND THERE WAS NO MAN) Why does no one present himself to me when I come? No one obeys me.

I CALLED AND THERE WAS NONE WHO WOULD HEAR) Does no one answer the caller? That is, why do you not accept that you will do the things to which the Prophets rouse you?

Grotius understands this concerning the disobedience of the Jews, to whom the Lord sent the Prophets: But it concerns the proper cause of the reprobate Jewish people, which was the rejection of the Messiah. And therefore these things are to be understood concerning the advent and proclamation of the Messiah. Which is further confirmed, both from what precedes: For it is established from the conclusion of the preceding chapter that Christ the Redeemer spoke there. Because he continues his discourse here: and from what follows. Because he testifies that he has come, to whom the Lord gave a learned tongue, whose ear he opened, and who gave his body to those who struck him. That this is Christ, is certain. I came therefore, he says, that is, according to the interpretation of Cyril, I put on humanity and appeared to the Israelites: and there was not among them a man, namely one of understanding, and who could know the time of redemption, I called, and there was no one hearing. For thus again the Prophet Isaiah says in the person of our Savior Christ, (I was found by those who do not seek me, I became conspicuous to those who do not ask for me. I said: Behold, I am here to a nation that did not believe in me. All day long I have spread out my hands to an unbelieving and contradicting people.) In the Evangelical Writings also we shall often find the Lord calling the Jews to faith: (Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. Take my yoke upon you again elsewhere: (He who follows me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.) He certainly declares that it is fruitful and useful for them to believe, saying: (Amen I say to you, that he who believes has eternal life.) And one could gather many other things to the same effect, if indeed one wished to pursue the matter at length. no one listening. This is the proper and genuine cause why the Jews were rejected.
