PRAYER II. Dealing particularly with the liberation of the human race, and the liberator Christ. CHAPTER LII.

Zion is aroused on account of her gratuitous redemption, and the preachers of evangelical peace are introduced, and all are provoked to recognize the salvation of God, Jesus, and to flee the company of the wicked, and CHRIST is set forth to be exalted after His passion, to be a stumbling block to others, but to sprinkle many nations with His blood, and to lead them to the recognition of Himself.

Verse 1. AND THERE SHALL PASS THROUGH THEE THE UNCIRCUMCISED AND THE UNCLEAN) Such as were the Assyrians, and the Egyptians, and the Chaldeans. See 2 Kings 18:23, 33, 34; chapter 24, 25.

Grotius, having followed the ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν or inventions of the Jews, explains these things concerning the earthly Jerusalem. But it has been said that the Prophet dealt with the spiritual Zion above, and that he continues to deal with the same, because his discourse is continuous, is certain. Nor could it be said of the earthly city that the uncircumcised and unclean would not pass through it after the Babylonian slaughter and the liberation from the same: since it suffered much from the uncircumcised, in the time of Antiochus, and in the most recent slaughter. Nor was it ever so well with the city of Jerusalem that all its citizens and inhabitants were truly just and clean. Therefore these magnificent promises pertain to the spiritual Zion. Which will be further evident from those things which follow in this chapter. Jerome proves this: To whom he had said above: Arise, arise, stand up O Jerusalem; now he speaks to the same: Awake, awake, put on thy strength O Zion. But what Zion is, the following verse shows: Put on the garments of thy glory O Jerusalem. We have said this to prove that Jerusalem and Zion are one city. He commands her even to put off her mourning garments, and to be clothed in those which she had before she drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of His fury. And she is called the city of the sanctuary, for this is what it sounds like on account of the temple which was built in it. Or holy on account of the knowledge of GOD, or holy; because she alone in the world had received the law. Whence also after the resurrection of the Savior the bodies of the dead appeared in the holy city. Which certainly could not be holy on account of the blasphemy and the hands laid upon the Lord. And what is promised: If she shall rise after her ruin, and shall be clothed in her strength and her glory, and the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no more pass through her: This signifies what the Apostle Paul also says, what participation of justice with iniquity? What fellowship of light with darkness? What agreement has Christ with Belial? What part has the believer with the infidel? What consensus has the temple of God with idols? Jerome therefore refutes the Jews, and in them Grotius: But all things which are promised to Sion and Jerusalem are not, as the Jews dream, said of its stones and ashes and embers, that it may be restored to its former state: But to the people of Jerusalem, who killed the Prophets and stoned those who had been sent to them, and at the last even laid hands upon the Son of God. Who, falling in the passion of Christ, was raised up in His resurrection, when many thousands of the Jews believed, and a remnant were saved. The same we can also [say] of the Church to say, what vision of peace and watchtower, if it has fallen into heresy, is ordered to depart, and to take up the ornaments of the former faith. And if it has been raised up, the rewards of holiness and continence are promised to it, so that the uncircumcised and the unclean may by no means pass through it. Which can be referred not to the cutting of the flesh and the foreskin, but to the uncleanness of works, so that we call those uncircumcised and unclean who serve the pleasure and lust of the body. Finally, Jeremiah speaks to those circumcised in flesh, not in spirit: All nations are uncircumcised in flesh, but the children of Israel are uncircumcised in their hearts. What of the fact that from the Jews Lippomanus, Disput. advers. Christian. on Isaiah and the XII minor Prophets, adds his calculation here §. CCXXVIII. It is written, put on the garments of thy beauty, for there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean. Which he says pertains to the times of the Messiah: and from there he tries to prove that the Messiah has not yet come. And §. CCXXXVI. This, he says, will be in the days of the Messiah. But the Jews are mistaken, while they expect that happiness in Jerusalem at the time of the Messiah, by which the uncircumcised are to have no place there. For it concerns the spiritual Jerusalem, and the foreskin of the heart: because the uncircumcised is explained by the unclean, and is opposed to the holy. Such, namely, is understood to be the Jerusalem in which there is no one unclean or uncircumcised in heart. But that cannot be the earthly Jerusalem. Compare Isa. 56, v. 3. chap. 60, v. 21.

Latin:

ORATIO II. Peculiariter de liberatione generis hu- mani, & liberatore Christo agens. CAPUT LII.

Excitatur Sion ob gratuitam sui redemtionem, & prædicatores pacis Evangelicæ introdu- cuntur, omnesque ad salutare Dei Jesum agnoscendum, & malorum consortium fu- giendum provocantur, ac sistitur CHRI- STVS post passionem suam exaltandus aliis scandalo futurus, gentes autem multas sanguine suo aspersurus, & ad sui agnitio- nem perducturus.

Vers. 1. ET PERTRANSEAT PER TE INCIRCVMCI- SVS ET IMMVNDVS) Quales erant Assyrii, & Ægyptii, & Chaldæi. Vide 2. Reg. 18, 23, 33. 34. cap. 24. 25.

DE terrena Hierosolyma hæc ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν vel commenta Judæorum sequutus, explicat Grotius. Dictum autem est de Zione spirituali su- perius egisse Prophetam, de qua porro eundem agere, quia oratio ejus continuatur, certum est. Neque de terrena urbe dici poterat, non pertrans- ituram per eandem incircumcisum & immundum post cladem Babylonicam & liberationem ex ea- dem: siquidem ab incircumcisis multa passa sit, tempore Antiochi, & in novissima clade. Nec un- quam tam bene actum fuit cum urbe Hierusalem, quod omnes cives & incolæ fuerint vere justi & mundi. Pertinent ergo hæ magnificæ promissiones ad spiritualem Sionem. Quod ex iis, quæ capite hoc sequuntur, porro constabit. Probat id Hieronymus: Cui supra dixerat: Elevare, elevare, consurge Hie- rusalem; nunc eidem loquitur: Consurge, consur- ge, induere fortitudine tua Sion. Quæ sit autem Sion, sequens versus ostendit: Induere vestimentis gloriæ tuæ Hierusalem. Hoc diximus, ut Hierusa- lem & Sion unam probemus urbem. Præcipit usque ei, ut lugubria vestimenta deponat, & induatur bis, quæ habuit antequam biberet de manu Domini calicem furoris ejus. Appellaturque civitas sanctua- rii, hoc enim sonat propter templum, quod in ea conditum fuit. Sive sancti propter notitiam DEI, vel sancta; quia sola in orbe terrarum acceperat le- gem. Unde & post resurrectionem Salvatoris appa- ruerunt corpora mortuorum in civitate sancta. Quæ utique propter blasphemiam & missas in Dominum manus sancta esse non poterat. Quodque promittitur: Si surrexerit post ruinam, & induta fuerit fortitu- dine & gloria sua, & nequaquam ultra transiturum per eam incircumcisum & immundum: Hoc signi- ficat, quod & Paulus Apostolus dicit, quæ partici- patio justitiæ cum iniquitate? Quæ societas luci ad tenebras? Quæ conventio Christi ad Belial? Quæ pars fideli cum infideli: Quis consensus templo Dei cum idolis? Refellit ergo Hieronymus Ju- dæos, & in eis Grotium: Omnia autem quæ pro- mittuntur Sion, & Hierusalem, non ut Judæi so- mniant, ad lapides illius & cineres favillasque dicun- tur, ut instauretur in pristinum statum: Sed ad po- pulum Hierusalem, qui occidit Prophetas, & lapi- davit eos, qui ad se missi erant, & ad extremum etiam in filium Dei misit manus. Qui corruens in passione Christi, in resurrectione illius suscitatus est, quando multa millia crediderunt è Judæis, & reli- quiæ salvæ factæ sunt. Eadem & de Ecclesia possumus dicere, quæ visio pacis & specula, si in hæresin cor- ruerit, jubetur exire, & pristinæ fidei ornamenta suscipere. Et si fuerit suscitata, sanctitatis ei & con- tinentiæ præmia promittuntur, ut nequaquam per eam transeat incircumcisus & immundus. Quod non ad carnis concisionem atque præputium, sed ad operum immunditiam referri potest, ut incircumcisos & immundos vocemus, qui corporis voluptati & libi- dini serviunt. Denique ad circumcisos carne, non spiritu loquitur Hieremias: Omnes gentes incir- cumcisæ carne sunt, filii autem Israël incircumcisi sunt cordibus suis. Quid, quod è Judæis Lippo- manus Disput. advers. Christian. ad Esaiam & XII. Prophetas minores, nobis hic calculum addit §. CCXXVIII. Scriptum est, indue vestes decoris tui, non enim ulterius veniet in te incircumcisus, atque immundus. Quod ad Messiæ tempora perti- nere ait: & inde probare conatur, quod nondum venerit Messias. Et §. CCXXXVI. Hoc, inquit, in diebus Messiæ erit. Falluntur autem Judæi, dum Hierosolymis expectant eam felicitatem Messiæ tempore, qua præputiati nullum habituri sint ibi- dem locum. Nam de Hierusalem spirituali, & de præputio cordis agitur: quia præputiatus per im- mundum explicatur, & sancto opponitur. Talis sc. Hierosolyma intelligitur, in qua non sit immun- dus, vel incircumcisus corde. At ea non potest es- se Hierosolyma terrena. Confer. Esa. 56. v. 3. cap. 60. v. 21.

## 52:3
Ver. 3. YE HAVE BEEN SOLD FOR NOUGHT, AND YE SHALL BE REDEEMED WITHOUT MONEY) To me, your Lord, your oppressors have paid no price, nor have they rendered any thanks at all.

Latin:

Vers. 3. GRATIS VENUMDATI ESTIS, ET SINE ARGENTO REDIMEMINI) Mihi, Domino vestro, nul- lum pretium persolverunt, ne gratiam quidem ullam retu- lerunt oppressores vestri.

## 52:4
Ver. 4. MY PEOPLE WENT DOWN INTO EGYPT IN THE BEGINNING) That is, long ago.

THAT HE MIGHT BE A SOJOURNER THERE) He came there of his own accord. This is so that it may be shown that the cause of the Assyrian is worse.

AND THE ASSYRIAN WITHOUT ANY CAUSE HATH OPPRESSED HIM) In the Hebrew: he oppressed him: namely Tiglath-Pileser, Shalmaneser, Sennacherib; the latter also by violating the treaty.

Latin:

Vers. 4. IN ÆGYPTUM DESCENDIT POPULUS MEUS IN PRINCIPIO) Id est, jam olim.

UT COLONUS ESSET IBI) Sponte eo venit. Hoc ideo, ut ostendatur pejor esse causa Assyrii.

ET ASSUR ABSQUE ULLA CAUSA CALU- MNIATUS EST EUM) In Hebræo: oppressit eum: nem- pe Teglatphalasar, Salmanasar, Sennacheribus; hic etiam violato fœdere.

## 52:5
Ver. 5. AND WHAT HAVE I HERE, SAITH THE LORD, THAT MY PEOPLE IS TAKEN AWAY FOR NOUGHT?) I have endured these things: but shall I also endure this, that those who curse me should rule over my people? The Chaldeans, namely, whose cause is worse than that of the Assyrians. See Jer. 50, 17.

They are said to be sold for nought, not with respect to God, as if they were sold for the merit of their sins, but with respect to the enemies, because the enemies to whom they were sold gave no price to claim them for themselves; they are redeemed for nought, and without money, because no price is paid to the enemies under whose power they are, so that they may be redeemed. Which are explained by instituting a comparison of the different sale and redemption of the people. For they were as if sold into Egyptian servitude, but for nought, because the Egyptians acquired the Israelites for themselves without any price given. But Israel went down into Egypt as the people of the Lord, the servant of no one, that he might be a sojourner there, and without cause, as far as the Egyptians are concerned, out of mere hatred, envy, and fear, he was reduced by them into servitude, as if they had sold themselves to them: but in turn they were redeemed from Egypt for nought and without money: The Assyrian without any cause oppressed him, and afflicted him, because עָשַׁק means he afflicted and oppressed by force and calumnies, which some understand of the Chaldean, when he was carrying them away into the Babylonian captivity, whom they wish to be called Assyrian, because he ruled over the Assyrians just as over other nations, and the Monarchy of the Assyrians was transferred to him, but this sense does not seem to fit: for Nebuchadnezzar did not carry away the people without cause, but because King Zedekiah was rebellious, and defected from him, 2 Kings 24, 20. And the discourse is about the affliction already done to the people, not about the future. Therefore others understand these things still of Pharaoh, whom they wish to be called ASSYRIAN by Ezek. 31, 3. Because otherwise the sentence about Egypt would be imperfect, gaping, and hanging. Which application of Cajetan and Forerius proved itself to Cornelius a Lapide. The LXX Interpreters, however, point to Shalmaneser, who carried away the ten tribes into Assyria: AND THE VIOLENT WERE CARRIED AWAY INTO THE ASSYRIANS. Others understand Sennacherib, who ravaged Judea in the time of Hezekiah. Grotius joins Tiglath-Pileser, Shalmaneser, and Sennacherib, who attacked the people not only without cause, but also by breaking the treaty. But the people were not sold to Sennacherib, even if he invaded Judea, much less to the others, who carried away the ten tribes, but not the Jewish people, of whom there is talk here: and therefore that interpretation concerning Pharaoh should be preferred, so that the sentence may be fulfilled, that the people of God went down into Egypt, that he might be a sojourner there, but by no means sold themselves. And the Assyrian (King Pharaoh) without any cause afflicted the same, and oppressed him by force and calumny: If only it could be proven that Pharaoh is designated anywhere by the name Assyrian, which from the passage of Ezek. 31, 1. can hardly be shown. Our Brentius understands it of the Assyrian captivity in 2 Kings 17. For in this not only was the kingdom of Samaria devastated, but also the captives were treated most cruelly. Whence he says: The Assyrian without any cause oppressed him. For although the Israelites had deserved this captivity and the devastation of the kingdom by their impiety, yet the Assyrians did not have a sufficiently legitimate cause why they should rage inhumanly against those who had already been punished by the removal of their kingdom and carried away into captivity. AND WHAT HAVE I HERE, SAITH THE LORD: THAT MY PEOPLE IS TAKEN AWAY FOR NOUGHT. Grotius draws that to the Babylonian captivity: But the Jews were not carried away into that without cause and their own fault. Besides, the Prophet did not treat in the preceding parts of the Babylonian captivity, which Grotius presupposes for nought. But those things which follow teach that the discourse is about the times of the New Testament. To which is added the interpretation of the Holy Spirit made in the New Testament, which openly teaches that it looks to the latest servitude and captivity, as being that with which the proclamation of the Apostles announcing peace was joined. Finally, this was by far the most grievous captivity. If you contend that this servitude and oppression in Egypt, or even the Assyrian one, is to be compared with the Babylonian captivity, this one certainly will not be judged more grievous, nor would it be a reason why the Lord should exclaim here as if in astonishment: AND WHAT HAVE I HERE! The comparison which Grotius institutes is null; I have endured these things; but shall I endure this, that those who curse me should lord it over my people? Namely, the Chaldeans, whose cause is worse than that of the Assyrians. That does not appear in Jer. 50, 17. That the cause of the Chaldeans was worse, nay, the Chaldeans had more cause against the Jews than the Assyrians. And yet the Chaldeans were kinder to the Jews in captivity. Inasmuch as King Evil-merodach even lifted up the head of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and exalted his throne above the thrones of all the kings who were in Babel, Jer. 52, 31. 32. And did not the Assyrians also curse the Lord, especially Sennacherib? Furthermore, as to who those are, by whose fault the name of the Lord is said here to be blasphemed, we have it more certainly from the Apostolic interpretation in Rom. 2, 23, where we are taught that this pertains to the Pharisees and Priests in the time of the N.T. and after the Messiah had been exhibited, whom the Apostle calls to account there, and teaches that this was written by Isaiah concerning them: Your cause, he says, the name of God is blasphemed AMONG THE GENTILES (which they add here

LXX. Interpreters & the Apostle following them) as it is written; therefore these things are most correctly explained by our B. Brentius: AND NOW WHAT HAVE I HERE! My people were indeed heavily afflicted before by the Egyptians & Assyrians, and they will be heavily afflicted again later by the Babylonians: but see what has happened to me now at this time among my people! My people have been taken away for nothing, their rulers act wickedly, & my name is blasphemed continually all the day. This is a description of that captivity into which the Scribes & Pharisees led the people of Israel by their impious traditions, which was also much heavier & more pernicious than those two former ones. For after the Israelites, from their return from Babylon and the restoration of the city of Jerusalem, degenerated into the customs of the nations, the Scribes & Pharisees, who are called rulers here, undertook to teach the people & to keep them in the ancestral religion. Which undertaking, as it seemed pious in itself, so they executed it impiously. For they did not teach truly pious things about the law of the Lord & about the promise of the Messiah: but they devised new traditions: under the pretext indeed of the divine law, but which in reality either abrogated or obscured the divine law. By these traditions they brought upon the Church of the people of God a far more horrible destruction, & led the people of God into a heavier captivity than when they were led away before into Egypt, or Assyria, or Babylon. For in those captivities they were despoiled only of bodily & earthly goods; but in this one they were despoiled of heavenly & eternal goods: in those they were stirred up to the acknowledgment of their sins, so that they might be converted to the Lord & obtain salvation: but in this one, seduced by the vain opinion of their own righteousness, they did not truly acknowledge their sins, nor did they obtain true forgiveness of sins. In those, the people & the Church of God still remained: but in this one, they were so cast away that they are no longer the people of God, and therefore were delivered into eternal damnation. What can be said or thought to be heavier than such a captivity? How much more tolerable it was to be captive in body under the Egyptians or Assyrians than in soul under the Scribes & Pharisees! MY PEOPLE HAVE BEEN TAKEN AWAY FOR NOTHING. It signifies that the people are led away, nay, carried off, by Pharisaic doctrines & traditions into a captivity by far the most calamitous of all. For that doctrine is called Pharisaic which, under the pretext of the divine law, institutes new forms of worship of God, & teaches that they are so pleasing to God that for their sake He favors the worshiper, remits his sins, & does him good in this life & the next. But such a doctrine leads its followers into eternal destruction. For it causes that neither are sins truly acknowledged, nor is the true office of Christ sought, nor are the true precepts & sacraments of God observed. Not to add also this, that the Chief Priests, Scribes, & Pharisees stirred up their people to reject & condemn our Lord Jesus Christ: so that they might defend this doctrine of theirs & keep the people in obedience to their traditions. From which it happened that the Jewish nation is not only oppressed by the Romans, but also cast away by God, so that it is no longer the people of God. But lest a scruple be injected because the Lord says that the people have been TAKEN AWAY FOR NOTHING, Brentius rightly meets this doubt: By this word he does not look to the merits of the common people before God, for in His judgment the Jews were not unjustly punished for false doctrine. But he looks to the office of the Scribes & Pharisees. For since the Jews were sinners & had the law and the promises concerning the Messiah, the Chief Priests, Scribes, & Pharisees, according to their calling, ought to have led their hearers, by explaining the law, into the acknowledgment of sins, & to have explained the promises concerning Christ, so that, having acknowledged their sins, they might obtain the remission of sins through faith in Christ, & declare themselves grateful by their obedience toward God their benefactor. For this purpose the Levitical Priesthood & the office of teaching were instituted: for this purpose the portions of sacrifices, tithes, firstfruits, & other stipends were conferred upon the Priests, Levites, & Doctors. But they, having cast away the true interpretation of the law & the promises concerning Christ, instituted new forms of worship of God & taught that God is honored by the observation of these & that sins are expiated by their merits. Since they did this against their office & calling, they are said to have seduced the people of God—who deserved no such thing from them—for nothing, without any legitimate cause, & to have led them into perpetual captivity. What then, is the people excused, & do they escape the same captivity? They do indeed escape the captivity if they are converted to Christ through the Gospel; but if they persevere in Pharisaic doctrine, they have neither excuse nor escape. Similarly, Cyril explains concerning the times of the New Testament: But now what are you here? That word, HERE, he says for, dispersed in the regions of the nations, & scattered to all the winds, according to the voice of the Prophet. For the sword of the Romans drove them out of all Judea, whoever were able to flee at all. Or, HERE, in that state of affairs in which you now are. For they were, as I said, in the greatest miseries: partly by the Roman army, by the law of war, invading their region: partly by the whole city being devastated, & the temple itself burned. Why therefore, he says, were they involved in these evils? Is it perhaps because they did not admit justifying faith, but treated with insults Him who called them to this in many ways, & impiously laid hands upon Him, and then also upon the righteous & the Prophets who were sent, of whom they killed some, others they stoned. These things are from Cyril.

V. same. THEIR RULERS ACT WICKEDLY) They raise their voice. For היליל is not said only of wailing, but also of every cry. They boast. The Chaldean.

AND CONTINUALLY ALL THE DAY MY NAME IS BLASPHEMED) By those Chaldeans, see Dan. 3. 5. 6. chapters.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET NUMQVID MIHI EST HIC, DICIT DOMINUS, QVONIAM ABLATUS EST POPULUS MEUS GRATIS?) Pertuli hæc: sed an & hoc feram, ut illi in populum meum dominentur, qui mihi maledicunt? Chaldæi scilicet, quorum causa pejor, quam Assyriorum. Vid. Jer. 50, 17.

Gratis venundati dicuntur, non respectu Dei, quod ob meritum peccatorum venundati sint, sed respectu hostium, quia nullum pretium dedere hostes, quibus venditi sunt, ut eos sibi vendica- rent; gratis, & sine argento redimuntur, quia ho- stibus sub quorum potestate sunt, nullum pretium persolvitur, ut redimantur. Quæ explicantur in- stituta comparatione diversæ venditionis & re- demtionis populi. Nam venditi quasi erant in ser- vitutem Ægyptiacam, sed gratis, quia Ægyptii nullo pretio dato acquisiverunt sibi Israëlitas. Sed descendit Israël in Ægyptum, ut populus Domini, nullius servus, ut colonus esset ibi, ac sine causa, quantum ad Ægyptios attinet, ex mero odio, invi- dia & metu in servitutem ab illis redactus est, ac si iisdem se vendidissent: at gratis vicissim & sine ar- gento ex Ægypto redempti sunt: Assur absque ulla causa calumniatus est, & afflixit eum, quia עָשַׁק est per vim & calumnias afflixit & oppressit, quod de Chaldæo intelligunt nonnulli, cum in captivita- tem Babylonicam eos abriperet, quem Assur dici volunt, quia Assyriis æque ac aliis gentibus domi- nabatur, & translata in eum fuit Assyriorum Mo- narchia, sed non videtur congruere hic sensus: non enim absque causa abduxit Nabuchodonosor po- pulum, sed quod rebellis esset rex Sedekias, & ab ipso deficeret, 2. Reg. 24, 20. Et de afflictione jam facta populo sermo est, non de futura. Proinde alii haec adhuc de Pharaone intelligunt, quem ab Ezech. 31, 3. ASSUR vocari volunt. Quod alioqui imperfecta, hiulca, & pendula foret sententia de Aegypto. Quae applicatio Cajetani & Forerii sese probavit Cornelio a Lapide. Salmanaffarem ta- men, qui decem tribus abduxit in Assyriam LXX. Interpretes indigitant: ET VIOLENTI AB- DUCTI SUNT IN ASSYRIOS. Alii Senna- cheribum, qui Ezechiae tempore Judaeam popula- tus est, intelligunt. Grotius conjungit Teglatphe- lassar, Salmenassar & Sennacherib, qui non modo sine causa, sed rupto etiam foedere populum ag- gressus est. Sed Sennacheribo populus venditus non est, etsi Judaeam invaserit, nedum caeteris, qui decem tribus abduxere, non vero populum Judai- cum, de quo hic sermo: ideoque praeferenda foret illa de Pharaone interpretatio, ut expleatur senten- tia, quod populus Dei in Aegyptum descenderit, ut colonus ibi esset, neutiquam vero se vendiderit. Assur autem (rex Pharao) absque ulla causa eundem afflixerit, ac per vim & calumniam oppresserit: Mo- do probari posset Pharaonem uspiam nomine As- sur designari, quod e loco Ezech. 31, 1. vix ostende- tur. Brentius noster de captivitate Assyriaca 2. Reg. 17. intelligit. In hac enim non solum vastatum est regnum Samariae, verum etiam captivi crudelissi- me sunt tractati. Unde ait: Assur absque ulla causa calumniatus est eum. Etsi enim Israëlitae meriti erant sua impietate hanc captivitatem, & regni va- stationem, tamen Assyrii non habebant satis legiti- mam causam, cur in eos, qui jam ablatione regni sui puniti & in captivitatem abducti erant, imma- niter grassarentur. ET NUMQVID MIHI EST HIC, DICIT DOMINUS: QVONIAM AB- LATUS EST POPULUS MEUS GRATIS. Illud Grotius ad captivitatem Babylonicam trahit: Sed in eam non absque causa & culpa sua abducti Judaei sunt. Adhaec non egit Propheta in antece- dentibus de captivitate Babylonica, quod gratis praesupponit Grotius. Ea vero quae sequuntur do- cent de temporibus Novi Testamenti sermonem esse. Quibus accedit interpretatio Spiritus Sancti in Novo Testamento facta, quae palam docet, ad servitutem & captivitatem novissimam respici, ut- pote cum qua praeconium Apostolorum pacem an- nunciantium conjunctum fuit. Denique haec lon- ge gravissima fuit captivitas. Hanc si servitutem & oppressionem in Aegypto, vel etiam Assyriacam contendas cum Babylonica captivitate, haec certe gravior censenda non erit, nec causa fuerit, cur hic quasi admirabundus exclamet Dominus: ET NUMQVID MIHI EST HIC! Comparatio, quam Grotius instituit, nulla est; Pertuli haec; sed an hoc feram, ut illi in populum meum dominentur, qui mihi maledicunt? Chaldaei sc. quorum causa pe- jor, quam Assyriorum. Id non apparet Jer. 50, 17. Chaldaeorum causam pejorem fuisse, imo Chaldaei plus causae habuere adversus Judaeos, quam Assy- rii. Et Chaldaei Judaeis tamen in captivitate beni- gniores fuere. Siquidem etiam caput Jojachim re- gis Judae evexerit rex Evilmerodach, & thronum ejus supra omnium regum thronos exaltarit, qui in Babel erant, Jer. 52, 31. 32. Et annon etiam maledi- xere Domino Assyrii, maxime Sennacheribus? Caeterum quinam illi sint, quorum culpa hic no- men Domini blasphemari dicatur, habemus cer- tius ex interpretatione Apostolica Rom. 2, 23. ubi docemur ad Pharisaeos ac Sacerdotes tempore N. T. & post exhibitum Messiam hac pertinere, quos ibi ad partes vocat Apostolus, ac de iis scriptum hoc ab Esaia esse docet: Vestri, inquit, causa nomen Dei blasphematur INTER GENTES (quod hic addunt

LXX. Interpp.& eos sequutus Apostolus) sicut scri- ptum est; ideo rectissime hæc explicantur à B.Bren- tio nostro: ET NVNC QVID MIHI EST HIC! Meus populus graviter quidem antea ab Ægyptiis & Assyriis afflictus est, graviter etiam post affligetur à Babyloniis: sed vide, quid mihi nunc hoc tempore in populo meo acciderit! Ablatus est populus meus gra- tis, dominatores ejus inique agunt, & nomen meum blasphematur jugiter tota die. Hæc est descriptio ejus captivitatis, in quam abduxerunt populum Israël Scribæ & Pharisæi, impiis suis traditionibus, quæ & multo gravior & perniciosior fuit, quam illæ duæ prio- res. Postquam enim Israëlitae à reditu è Babylone & instauratione urbis Hierusalem, degenerarent in mores gentium,susceperunt Scribæ & Pharisæi,qui hic dominatores vocantur, populum docendum,& in avita religione continendum. Quod institutum, ut per se pium viderur, ita illi impie sunt executi. Non enim docuerunt vere pia de lege Domini, & de promissione Messiæ: sed commenti sunt novas traditiones: prætextu quidem divinæ legis,sed quæ revera divinam legem aut abrogabant aut obscura- bant. His traditionibus intulerunt Ecclesiæ populi Dei longe horribilius exitium, & abduxerunt po- pulum Dei in graviorem captivitatem, quam cum abducti sunt antea in Ægyptum, aut Assyriam, aut Babylonem. Nam his captivitatibus spoliati tan- tum sunt bonis corporalibus & terrenis; in illa au- tem spoliati sunt bonis cœlestibus & æternis: in his excitati sunt ad agnitionem peccatorum suorum, ut converterentur ad Dominum, & consequeren- tur salutem: in illa autem seducti vana opinione propriæ justitiæ, non agnoverunt vere peccata sua, nec veram peccatorum veniam consequebantur. In his manebant adhuc populus & Ecclesia Dei: in illa autem sic abjecti sunt,ut non amplius sint popu- lus Dei, ideoque traditi in æternam damnationem. Quid tali captivitate potest gravius aut dici aut co- gitari? Quanto tolerabilius fuit, corpore sub Ægy- ptiis, aut Assyriis,quam animo sub Scribis & Phari- sæis captivum esse! POPULUS MEUS ABLATUS EST GRATIS. Significat populum Pharisai cis doctrinis & traditionibus abduci, imo auferri, in captivitatem longe omnium calamitosissimam. Nam ea dicitur Pharisaica doctrina, quæ prætextu divinæ legis instituit novos cultus Dei, & docet, eos Deo ita gratos esse, ut propter ipsos faveat cul- tori, remittat ei peccata, & benefaciat ei in hoc & futuro seculo. Talis autem doctrina abducit asseclas in perpetuum exitium. Efficit enim,ut nec peccata vere agnoscantur, nec verum officium Christi re- quiratur, nec vera præcepta & sacraDei observen- tur. Ut non & hoc addam,quod Pontifices, Scribæ, & Pharisæi excitarunt populum suum ad abjici- endum & damnandum Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum: quo hanc suam doctrinam tuerentur, & populum in obedientia suarum traditionum con- tinerent. Ex quo factum est, quod gens Judaica non tantum sit à Romanis oppressa, verum etiam à Deo abjecta, ne sit amplius populus Dei. Ne autem scrupulum injiciat, quod Dominus ait: GRATIS ABLATUM esse populum, recte du- bio huic occurrit Brentius: Hoc vocabulo non respi- cit ad vulgi merita coram Deo, in hujus enim judicio non injuste puniti sunt Judæi salsa doctrina. Sed re- spicit ad officium Scribarum & Pharisæorum. Nam cum Judæi essent peccatores & haberent le- gem ac promissiones de Messia,debuissent Pontifi- ces,Scribæ & Pharisæi, juxta vocationem ipsorum, auditores suos exposita lege in agnitionem pecca- torum ducere, & promissiones de Christo explica- re, ut agnitis peccatis consequerentur peccatorum remissionem per fidem in Christum, & declararent sefe obedientia sua erga Deum benefactorem gra- tos. In hunc enim usum institutum fuit Sacerdo- tium Leviticum, & officium docendi: in hunc usum conferebantur Sacerdotibus, Levitis, & Doctoribus partes Sacrificiorum, decimæ, primitiæ, & alia sti- pendia. Sed hi abjecta vera legis, & promissionum de Christo interpretatione, instituebant novos Dei cultus, & docebant Deum horum observatione honorari & peccata meritis eorum expiari. Quod cum fecerint contra suum officium & vocationem, dicuntur populum Dei nihil tale ab ipsis meritum gratis sine ulla legitima causa seduxisse, & in perpe- tuam captivitatem abduxisse. Quid ergo, num po- pulus est excusatus, & evadit eandem captivitatem? Evadit quidem captivitatem, si per Evangelion ad Christum convertatur; sed si perseveraverit in Pharisaica doctrina, nullam habet nec excusatio- nem, nec evasionem. Similiter explicat de tempo- ribus Novi Testamenti Cyrillus : Sed nunc quid hic estis? Illud, HIC, dicit, pro, in gentium regioni- bus dispersi, & ad omnes ventos dissipati, juxta Pro- phetæ vocem. Expulit enim eos ex omni Judæa Roma- norum gladius, quicunque valuerunt omnino fugere. Vel, HIC, in eo rerum statu, in quo nunc estis, Fue- runt enim, ut dixi, in summis miseriis : partim Ro- mano exercitu, lege belli, eorum regionem incursan- te : partim tota civitate vastata, & templo ipso cre- mato. Quare igitur, inquit, in his malis versati sunt? An videlicet quod fidem justificantem non ad- miserint, sed multifariam ad hoc vocantem contume- liis affecerint, eique impie manus intulerint, deinde etiam justis & Prophetis, qui missi sunt, quorum alios occiderunt, alios lapidaverunt. Hæc Cyrillus.

V. eod. DOMINATORES EJUS INIQVE AGUNT) Vocem attollunt. Nam היליל, non de ejulatu tantum dicitur, sed & de omni clamore. Iactant se. Chaldæus.

ET JUGITER TOTA DIE NOMEN MEUM BLAS- PHEMATUR) Ab illis Chaldæis, V. Dan. 3. 5. 6. capp.

## 52:6
Vers. 6. FOR THIS REASON MY PEOPLE SHALL KNOW MY NAME IN THAT DAY: THAT I MYSELF WHO WAS SPEAKING AM HERE) They shall acknowledge me to be יהוה: that is, in reality fulfilling what I promised.

That the Rulers are understood here as the Chaldeans is evident by no indication. That the Scribes, Pharisees, and High Priests of the Jews are designated in the time of Christ, the things which we have said confirm, through whom it also came to pass that the Jews were most miserably sold, inasmuch as they brought eternal destruction upon the people both by the traditions and corruptions of the saving doctrine, and were also the cause of their temporal ruin. Jerome also handed down this sense when he discusses the reasons why the Jews suffered these things: that they were seized either by the forces of the Romans or by the snares of the Devil, by which they are held even until now. But that they might suffer these things, their rulers and teachers acted unjustly: who according to Symmachus and Theodotion will howl: according to Aquila, they will weep, when they have been delivered to torments. For they themselves are the ones who incited the people against the Savior, so that with a harmonious voice they might shout, Crucify, crucify such a one; concerning whom he had already said before: The Lord himself will come with the elders of the people, and with his princes. But why have you set fire to my vineyard, and the plunder of the poor is in your houses? Wherefore according to the LXX he speaks to them: Because of you my name is always blasphemed among the nations. And it should be known that, among the nations, is not found in the Hebrew: but absolutely, my name is continually blasphemed, so that it may be understood, in your synagogues, who day and night blaspheme the Savior. And under the name (as I have often said) of the Nazarenes, three times a day they heap curses upon the Christians. Therefore, while they are blaspheming and cursing the Lord, his people, of whom frequently it has already been said, that is, the Christian people, shall know the name of him who is to come in the name of the Father. And therefore it shall know, because he himself, who previously spoke through the Prophets, will instruct the peoples while present. That promise of the Lord's presence therefore offers a new argument; because these things concern the time of the Messiah's advent MY PEOPLE SHALL KNOW MY NAME IN THAT DAY: BECAUSE I MYSELF WHO WAS SPEAKING: BEHOLD I AM PRESENT. For these things refer not only to the fulfillment of divine promises, but to the παρουσιαν & advent of the Lord. Indeed, the same Lord who speaks here, the Son of God, promises that he will be present, and that his people will then know his name more clearly; such clearer knowledge is proper to the N.T. Therefore the Apostle understands these things concerning the Jews of his own time in Rom. 2, 23, on account of whom the name of the Lord was blasphemed. Add that in the following verse 7, the proclamation of the Apostles is immediately subjected, who are to announce peace; so that the chosen people of the Lord may be freed from that iniquity of the rulers, and from most dangerous captivity. Cyril also agrees with us here in the Greek Church: THUS SAYS THE LORD, BECAUSE OF YOU MY NAME IS ALWAYS EVIL SPOKEN OF AMONG THE GENTILES. For you were, he says, the authors and cause that those who were subjugated suffered, allowing them to lack instruction, nay, not permitting them at all to return to God, and to see with the eyes of the mind him who comes from heaven, who appeared as God the Word in human form, that he might preach remission to the captives, and sight to the blind, and might heal those endowed with a contrite heart, and might call the acceptable year of the Lord. Therefore because of you my name is evil spoken of among the gentiles: For when Israel had been scattered through all regions & cities, he says; no one anywhere among the nations was ignorant that the holy city had been laid waste, and that the temple itself had been the work and material of fire: Then they assail my name with insults, and diminish my glory. If indeed they perhaps think my hand is weak, which was always auxiliary to Israel: but they are still ignorant of the true cause, nor did anyone among them know that they had paid the penalties for the Lord's slaughter, and for many other offenses. THEREFORE MY PEOPLE SHALL KNOW MY NAME. At that time, when I shall shine forth in the flesh to the inhabitants of the earth, whoever shall become my people, and shall admit the faith, whether they be from the Jews, or from the gentiles, these shall know my name. For he says name instead of glory. For it is familiar for the divinely inspired Scripture to speak thus. For he himself, who was speaking in the Prophets, am present. Thus Cyril. St. Jerome also urges v. 13. BEHOLD HE SHALL UNDERSTAND, &c. Lest any ambiguity be left for readers, as to who he is who said: I who was speaking, behold I am present. And as to what is the holy arm of the Lord, which has been revealed to all nations, God the omnipotent Father teaches clearly: Behold my servant, or my boy, shall understand. Concerning whom later.

Regarding the word יְיַלִילוּ it is particularly to be observed that there is no reason why, having abandoned the proper meaning of the word, which denotes TO HOWL, as it is expressed by the LXX Interpreters, it should be taken only of boasting, or of the raising of the voice. But the Pharisees and Chief Priests of the Jews were howling, like famished wolves panting for the prey of the people, or they were making the people, whom they were oppressing, to howl, as Cornelius à Lapide explains from Vatablus and Forerius. And therefore I paraphrase these things thus, Osiander, following Brentius: HIS (my people's) RULERS ACT UNJUSTLY (Hebr. MAKE TO HOWL) SAYS THE LORD: that is, the Doctors of the Church, who ought to teach the people sound and salutary doctrine, by which consciences might be pacified and gladdened, they themselves

(for the ministry) seize, and propose such doctrine, which produces nothing but wailing, that is, which afflicts and torments consciences. AND CONTINUALLY ALL THE DAY MY NAME IS BLASPHEMED, says the Lord, through the doctrine of the Pharisees and Scribes. BECAUSE OF THIS (says the Son of God) I will have mercy on my oppressed Church, and I will preach the Gospel to it, AND MY PEOPLE SHALL KNOW MY NAME IN THAT DAY, that is, then my Church shall acknowledge me as its Savior and Mediator: BECAUSE I MYSELF WHO WAS SPEAKING (more correctly who am speaking). BEHOLD I AM PRESENT, that is, I myself in my assumed flesh will preach the Gospel. Blessed Luther had also preceded in the German version and marginal gloss, His rulers make a howling, their teaching is a howling, and they make consciences heavy with laws, and howling. Add also those things which are held here in the Latin Enarrat. The Rabbis themselves understand these things, Therefore my people shall know my name in that day, because I behold I am present, concerning the Messiah who is to come, who will show his salvation, according to Isa. 45, 17. Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation, in Midrash Tillim, on Ps. 91, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 6. PROPTER HOC SCIET POPULUS MEUS NOMEN MEUM IN DIE ILLA : QVIA EGO IPSE QVI LOQVEBAR ECCE ADSUM) Agnoscent me esse יהוה : id, est reipsa implentem, quod promisi.

Quod Dominatores hic intelligantur Chaldæi, nullo indicio constat. Scribas, Pharisæos, Ponti- fices Judæorum tempore Christi designari, ea quæ diximus, confirmant, per hos etiam factum, ut mi- serrime venderentur Judæi, utpote qui tum tradi- tionibus & corruptelis doctrinæ salvificæ exitium populo afferebant æternum, tum etiam causa erant temporalis excidii. Quem sensum etiam tradidit Hieronymus, cum de causis, cur ista passi sint Ju- dæi, disserit: ut comprehensi vel viribus Romanorum vel Diaboli laqueis, quibus hucusque retinentur. Ut autem ista paterentur, dominatores eorum ac Magi- stri inique egerunt : qui juxta Symmachum & Theo- dotionem ululabunt : juxta Aquilam, flebunt, cum tormentis traditi fuerint. Ipsi enim sunt, qui adver- sum Salvatorem populum concitarunt, ut consona voce clamarent, Crucifige, crucifige talem; De quibus & ante jam dixerat : Ipse Dominus veniet cum senioribus populi, & cum principibus ejus. Vos autem quare succendistis vineam meam, & rapina pauperis in domibus vestris? Quamobrem juxta LXX. loquitur ad eos: Propter vos semper no- men meum blasphematur in gentibus. Et sciendum quod, in gentibus, non habeatur in Hebræo: sed ab- solute, nomen meum jugiter blasphematur, ut sub- audiatur, in synagogis vestris, qui diebus ac nocti- bus blasphemant Salvatorem. Et sub nomine (ut sæ- pe dixi) Nazarenorum, ter in die in Christianos con- gerunt maledicta. Illis itaque blasphemantibus & ma- ledicentibus Domino, populus ejus, de quo crebro jam dictum est, id est, populus Christianus, sciet no- men illius, qui venturus est in nomine Patris. Et pro- pterea sciet, quia ipse, qui prius loquutus est per Pro- phetas, presens erudiet populos. Argumentum ergo novum præbet illa præ- sentiæ Domini promissio; quod hæc adventus Mes- siæ tempus concernant : PROPTER QVOD SCIET POPULUS MEUS NOMEN MEUM IN DIE ILLA: QUIA EGO IPSE QVI LO- QVEBAR : ECCE ADSUM. Hæc enim non tantum impletionem promissionem divinarum, sed παρουσιαν & adventum Domini referunt. Idem nempe Dominus, qui hic loquitur, Filius Dei se ad- futurum pollicetur, & nomen suum populum tum clarius cogniturum; qualis cognitio evidentior N. T. propria est. Ideo de Judæis sui temporis hæc in- telligit Apostolus Rom. 2, 23. ob quos nomen Domi- ni blasphematum fuit. Adde quod subjugatur v. seq. 7. statim Apostolorum præconium, qui pacem ãnunciaturi sint; ut populus electus Domini libere- tur ab illa dominatorum iniquitate, ac captivitate periculosissima. Consonat hic nobis in Græca etiam Ecclesia Cyrillus : HÆC DICIT DOMINUS, PROPTER VOS SEMPER NOMEN MEUM MALE AUDIT INTER GENTES. Fuistis enim, inquit, vos autores, & causa, ut qui sub- jugati sunt, paterentur, sinentes eos carere institutio- ne, imo non permittentes omnino, ut ad Deum rever- terentur, viderentque animi oculis eum, qui de cœlo venit, qui in forma humana Deus verbum apparuit, ut prædicaret captivis remissionem, cæcisque visum, sanaretque contrito corde præditos, & annum Domini acceptum vocaret. Itaque propter vos nomen meum inter gentes male audit: Cum enim per omnes regio- nes & urbes dissipatus esset, inquit, Israël; vastatam esse sanctam civitatem, opusque & materiam ignis fuis- se ipsum templum, nemo uspiam gentium ignoravit : Tum meum nomen conviciis incessunt, & meam elevant gloriam. Siquidem fortassis putant meam manum debilem esse, quæ semper fuit auxiliaris Israë- li : veram autem causam adhuc ignorant, nec quis- quam apud eos scivit, eos cædis Dominicæ, & multo- rum aliorum delictorum pœnas solvisse. IDEO SCIET POPULUS MEUS NOMEN MEUM. Illo tempore, quo terræ habitatoribus in carne illuce- scam, quicunque mei fient populi, admittentque fidem, sive ex Judæis illi fuerint, sive ex gentibus, hi scient nomen meum. Nomen vero dicit pro gloria. Sic enim loqui familiare est Scripturæ divinitus inspiratæ. Ipse enim, qui in Prophetis loquebar, adsum. Hæc Cyrillus. Urget etiam S. Hieronymus v. 13. ECCE INTELLIGET, &c. Ne ulla legentibus ambigui- tas relinquatur, quis sit ille, qui dixerit : Ego qui lo- quebar, ecce adsum. Et quod sit brachium sanctum Domini, quod cunctis gentibus revelatum est, Deus omnipotens Pater perspicue docet : Ecce intelliget servus meus, sive puer meus. De quo postea.

De voce יְיַלִילוּ peculiariter observandum, non esse causam, cur relicta vocis propria significatio- ne, quæ ULULARE notat, uti à LXX. Interpp. expressa est, de sola jactantia, vel vocis elatione ac- cipiatur. Ululabant autem Pharisæi & Pontifices Judæorum, quasi lupi famelici prædæ populi in- hiantes, vel ululare faciebant populum, quem op- primebant, ut è Vatablo & Forerio explicat Cornel. à Lapide. Ideoque hæc ita παραφραζω̃ Osiander, Brentium sequutus : DOMINATORES EJUS (populi mei) INIQVE AGUNT (Hebr. ULU- LARE FACIUNT) DICIT DOMINUS : id est, Doctores Ecclesiæ, qui debebant docere ple- bem sanam salutarem doctrinam, qua conscientiæ pacificarentur & lætificarentur, ipsi Dominum

(pro ministerio) arripiunt, & talem doctrinam proponunt, quæ non nisi ejulatum efficit, hoc est, quæ conscientias affligit & excruciat. ET JUGI- TER TOTA DIE NOMEN MEUM BLAS- PHEMATUR, inquit Dominus, per Pharisæo- rum & Scribarum doctrinam. PROPTER HOC (inquit Filius Dei) miserebor Ecclesiæ meæ op- pressæ, & concionabor illi Evangelion, ET SCIET POPULUS MEUS NOMEN MEUM IN DIE ILLA, id est, tunc agnoscet me Ecclesia mea Salvatorem & Mediatorem suum: QVIA EGO IPSE QVI LOQVEBAR (rectius qui lo- quor. ECCE ADSUM, id est, Ego ipse in carne mea assumpta prædicabo Evangelium. Præiverat & B. Lutherus in versione Germanica & glossa marginali, Seine Herrscher machen ein Geheule, Ihre Lehre ist ein Geheule, und machen die Gewis- sen mit Gesetzen schwer, und heulend. Adde & ea, quæ hic habentur in Latina Enarrat. Rabbini ipsi hæc, Propter hoc sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ecce adsum, de Messiæ adventuro intelligunt, qui ostendet salvationem suam, juxta Esa. 45, 17. Israël salvatus est in Domino salvatione æterna, in Midrasch Tillim, super Ps. 91, 14.

## 52:7
Vers. 7. HOW BEAUTIFUL UPON THE MOUNTAINS ARE THE FEET OF HIM THAT BRINGETH GOOD TIDINGS AND PREACHETH PEACE)

How beautiful will be the ministry of Jeremiah, who will define the very Time, in which Sion, inhabited again, will flourish?

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVAM PULCHRI SUPER MONTES PEDES ANNUNTIANTIS ET PRÆDICANTIS PACEM)

Quam pulchrum erit ministerium Jeremiæ, qui definiet ipsum Tempus, quo Sion rursus habitata florebit?

## 52:8
Vers. 8. THE VOICE OF THY WATCHMEN: THEY HAVE LIFTED UP THE VOICE: THEY SHALL PRAISE TOGETHER)

You shall say, when the Levites are again to sing the praises of God in the temple.

WHEN THE LORD SHALL TURN SION) When he shall have made the people return into Sion.

A most wicked distortion of a famous passage. Grotius understands no Gospel in the Old Testament except a carnal one; he prattles of nothing here but bodily liberation. Therefore he thrusts in the Prophet Jeremiah, of whom neither palm nor footprint is detected in the text. He does this, indeed, with a most wicked purpose, namely, that he may distort the following chapter, which contains a famous prophecy concerning the passion and exaltation of Christ, such as hardly any other exists in the whole Old Testament, to Jeremiah, just as the Jews do. But that this passage cannot be understood of Jeremiah, but must be accepted as concerning the Apostles and other heralds under the New Testament, is clear, first, from the connection with the preceding verses, in which the most destructive dominion of the Pharisees and the most welcome advent of Christ, that they might be redeemed freely and without money from that destruction of the soul, is described. Concerning which Sebastian Münster has thus exhibited the sum of the coherence of the preceding and present matters, along with Rabbinical trifles: HE SHALL NOT ADD THAT THE UNCIRCUMCISED SHALL COME INTO THEE ANY MORE. The Hebrews, he says, understand all these things of the redemption which they expect in vain to be brought about by the Messiah: and by the uncircumcised they understand the kingdom of Edom, that is, of the Romans, and by the unclean, the kingdom of Ishmael, that is, the kingdom of the Turk and the Sultan. Our people, however, understand it of the redemption of Christ promised to the synagogue and now exhibited: as if God were saying: you have been so often captured and redeemed, and then again devastated, I will at some time establish a redemption which is eternal, and which no other captivity shall follow. And that redemption is spiritual, by which Christ on the cross freely delivered us from sins, eternal death, and hell, with no preceding merits of our own. What is this to me! My people, he says, is in another captivity, more grievous than that which was in Egypt or among the Assyrians: For those who rule over them dominate them according to their own will, and not according to my word; they lead them into errors, they make them howl and blaspheme my name all the day long. I will therefore take care I the Lord, that my people may acknowledge me, and hear me speaking. I will send Evangelists, who shall announce peace and salvation, and every good, not to private men, but they shall ascend the mountains with their most beautiful feet, and shall preach to the whole world the grace of God and the Gospel of Christ, and that henceforth God is to reign in us by his word, and not Moses by his ceremonies. Thus he. Let us hear our Brentius here: The Son of God, he says, rejected and condemned the Doctors of Pharisaic doctrine and human traditions. What then? Shall the Church of those pious ones, who in the times of the Pharisees and the coming of Christ still remain among the Jews, be utterly destitute of all Doctors, and of all ministry of preaching? Certainly nothing of the sort. For Christ the Son of God promises to his Church other Doctors in place of the Pharisees. First he promises that he himself will be their Doctor: Then he promises that he will send them his Apostles, who shall announce true peace, true salvation. Thus Brentius. Then what is a merely corporal liberation to the faithful under such pressure, with the spiritual one neglected, that it should be described so magnificently with such an apparatus of words? HOW BEAUTIFUL (or rather lovely) UPON THE MOUNTAINS ARE THE FEET OF HIM THAT ANNOUNCETH (more correctly Evangelizing) PREACHING PEACE, ANNOUNCING GOOD, PREACHING SALVATION, SAYING TO SION, THY GOD HATH REIGNED. The individual words are so arranged that they imply spiritual goods to be announced by the Apostles, but not a corporal liberation to be preached by Jeremiah. They are said to announce upon the mountains, i.e., not in Chaldea, but in Judea. Beautifully Brentius: what he says FEET UPON THE MOUNTAINS, regards the situation of the city of Jerusalem, which is surrounded by mountains. As he says in Psalm 124. Jerusalem, mountains are round about it. When therefore the Holy Spirit in the Prophet sees the Apostles hastening from Galilee, through the mountainous regions to the city of Jerusalem, so that having received the Holy Spirit there they may divulge the Gospel, not in Jerusalem only, but also into the whole world, he exclaims out of immense joy: How beautiful, he says, how grateful, how acceptable, how pleasant are the feet, or the pedestrian legates, whom I see setting out to our city through the mountains placed in a circuit, so that they may bring us the most expected news. Furthermore, the word EVANGELIZING without doubt fits the Apostles announcing the Gospel more correctly than Jeremiah preaching liberation from Babylon. And it is used for the joyful news of spiritual grace in this very Prophet c. 61, 1. But what does the preaching of peace exhibit if not the sum of the Gospel, since neither did Christ pray for anything other than peace for the Apostles, nor did the Apostles pray for anything else for the Churches in their letters? The people of the Lord were enjoying peace even in Chaldea, for they were not in war, but under servitude. Here, however, Evangelical peace is intimated, which is the reconciliation of God and man. GOOD is announced, than which there is no greater. True and eternal salvation is preached. It is said to spiritual Sion: THY GOD REIGNETH. No news is more joyful than that Christ Immanuel, God with us, our God sitting at the right hand of the Father, governs the Church, which he redeemed with his blood. Concerning which let the blessed Brentius be seen at greater length. Furthermore, lest we doubt that Evangelical messengers and Apostles are understood, God repeated the same promise in the same words through Nahum c. 1. BEHOLD UPON THE MOUNTAINS THE FEET OF HIM THAT EVANGELIZETH AND ANNOUNCETH PEACE; where a call is added to sacred solemnities, and spiritual festivities; Celebrate thy festivities O Judah, and render thy vows. But above all we have the interpretation

Clearer than the sun in the N.T. Since St. Paul interprets this prophecy in Rom. 10, 15. concerning the Apostles and the remaining Evangelical messengers of the N. Testament. For everyone, he says, whosoever shall call upon his name, (Christ's) shall be saved. How then shall they call on him, in whom they have not believed? Or how shall they believe in him, of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, if they be not sent? as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of them that evangelize good things? But not all believe the Gospel. Whence it is clear that the Prophetic saying is to be understood concerning the Gospel of Christ, by whose faith we obtain salvation, and not concerning the proclamation of Jeremiah announcing liberation from the Babylonian captivity, but of the Evangelical ministry announcing peace brought through Christ and eternal salvation. And by ANNOUNCING it is to be understood any one evangelizing, and not a certain individual, or a singular person. And lest we doubt that we are referred to Isaiah, and that his present place is regarded, there is subjoined in Rom. 10, 16. a complaint, concerning the voice of the Gospel not being received through faith from this very Isaianic prophecy: For Isaiah says: Lord, who hath believed our report? Lest I doubt that it is a matter of the report and word of the Gospel, and faith in Christ, the Apostle adds a conclusion of this kind: Therefore faith is from hearing, and hearing by the WORD OF CHRIST. Finally, lest we hesitate that the proclamation of the Apostles is designated, he points it out expressly, declaring what kind of heralds the Prophet regarded here. But I say: Have they not heard? And indeed their sound went out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. Whose, if not the Apostles'? Certainly not Jeremiah's. What kind of ecumenical and universal proclamation is here also predicted by Isaiah himself: THE LORD HATH PREPARED HIS HOLY ARM IN THE EYES OF ALL NATIONS. AND ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH SHALL SEE THE SALVATION OF OUR GOD, i.e., it shall not be revealed only to the Jews, but also to the nations through the whole world, so that the Gospel, or the word of Christ, may be announced even to the ends of the earth, that he himself is the SALVATION OF THE LORD, or the SAVIOR divinely sent to all believing in him, whether they derive their origin from the Jews, or from the nations. All of which GROTIUS saw without doubt, therefore in the Annotations ad Roman. 10, 15. He acknowledged that these things were taken by the Apostle from this oracle of Isaiah, nor could he deny that the same things were to be understood of Christ; indeed, he professed that the Jews themselves believe this, but he retreated to his customary κρησφύγετον, namely that they treat of the Messiah only according to the mystical sense, but as regards the literal sense, which he calls the primary one, they speak of Jeremiah; but of that literal sense, which he himself assigns, there is no indication in the Prophetic text; indeed, all things speak the contrary, as has been shown thus far. Nor do the Jews, who say that the discourse is about Christ, understand it as regards the literal sense to be about Jeremiah, but they say that that literal sense is about Christ. Nor did the Apostle ever prove the faith from a mystical sense, i.e., one that was intended by the Holy Spirit beyond the literal one. Indeed, nowhere in the Scriptures is another sense found to be intended by the Holy Spirit besides the literal one. It is therefore vain what he says, that in the FORMER SENSE these things are said of Jeremiah (because such a sense will never be proven), yet in such a way that the ANCIENT JEWS also understood these things to apply MORE EMINENTLY to the times of the Messiah. If they were spoken of the times of the Messiah by the intention of the Holy Spirit, concerning the proclamation of the Gospel and the peace obtained through Christ, which we have from the Apostolic interpretation, and which the ancient Jews do not deny, these things cannot have been said in a double sense, and by the intention of the Holy Spirit, both of the times of Jeremiah and of the announcement of liberation from the Babylonian captivity.

Furthermore, lest any doubt should remain that the discourse is about many evangelizers, and about the proclamation being propagated far and wide, it is added in our Prophet: THE VOICE OF YOUR WATCHMEN (that is, of those who keep watch for the salvation of Zion, Ezech. 3, Heb. 13, shall be heard) THEY HAVE LIFTED UP (more correctly, they shall lift up) THE VOICE (their own) THEY HAVE PRAISED TOGETHER (more correctly, they shall shout for joy) BECAUSE THEY SHALL SEE EYE TO EYE WHEN THE LORD SHALL CONVERT ZION. They shall not mutter, as Brentius rightly says, just as ventriloquists or the prophets of the heathens mutter from their caves: nor shall they whisper either in the corners of houses, or in the hiding places of woods and mountains with few witnesses: which is what seditious persons and others are accustomed to do, who flee the light either because of the foulness of their principles or the enormity of their crime: But they shall lift up their voice so high that it may be heard from the city of Jerusalem, even to the farthest ends of the earth. For their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. And not this alone, but they shall also praise together, they shall equally shout for joy. They shall not only teach the Gospel of Christ in the world, having made a beginning in Jerusalem, but all shall also teach the same Gospel with the greatest concord. There shall be one praise of all, one jubilation concerning the things accomplished through Christ the King of Zion. For it shall be seen eye to eye, it shall be manifested openly before all, both by doctrine and by miracles, that the Lord has converted or restored Zion, i.e., that Christ our Lord has redeemed His Church from the tyranny of Satan, from sins, from death and hell. The Prophet concludes with an exhortation to public and ecumenical joy: REJOICE AND PRAISE (shout for joy) TOGETHER, O YE DESERTS OF JERUSALEM: FOR THE LORD HATH COMFORTED HIS PEOPLE. What other consolation is this, than that which the Prophets so often inculcate, and our own in ch. 40, 1: Be comforted, be comforted, etc. Rejoice therefore and exult, not only those places which are contained within the walls of the city of Jerusalem, but also the deserts and solitudes around Jerusalem: because there shall now be such a multitude of citizens that the suburbs of the city shall be extended even to the deserts, and from the wilderness shall be made a most populous city. For the Lord Himself, not through His servants the Prophets, as of old, but in His own person openly comforts His people, announces His Gospel to the people, and redeems Jerusalem from all her iniquities, from the power of Satan and death. HE REDEEMS (גאל which is proper to the Son of God) JERUSALEM. That which the Lord had said before, YOU HAVE BEEN SOLD FOR NOTHING, YOU SHALL BE REDEEMED FOR NOTHING, this the faithful now boast and rejoice that it has been done, after the Salvation brought by the Lord has been announced to the world through the Apostles; HE REDEEMS JERUSALEM. For not only is such joy, which is so joined with jubilation, and which extends itself to the farthest ends of the earth, conceived from bodily liberation, but also from the spiritual redemption of the Messiah divulged through the Gospel. THE LORD (God the Father) HATH PREPARED (in Hebrew, laid bare, which some explain as an expedition to battle against spiritual enemies, the Devil, sin, and death; others more correctly explain it as the manifestation of Christ) HIS HOLY ARM IN THE EYES OF ALL THE GENTILES. What that holy arm of the Lord is, laid bare or manifested in the eyes of all the gentiles, the subjoined epexegesis, or the end of that manifestation, teaches. AND ALL THE ENDS OF THE EARTH SHALL SEE THE SALVATION OF OUR GOD. Wherefore the HOLY ARM OF THE LORD and THE SALVATION OF OUR GOD are the same: And so, since Christ is accustomed to be described by this latter name, the same is also understood by the arm of the Lord. Whom the Prophet also designated in this way in the following chapter, v. 2. And THE ARM OF THE LORD to whom has it been revealed? Jerome judges it to be clear from these things that, with the spiritual Jerusalem, that is, the Church, being built up by the Apostles, which had been abandoned by the Jews, the arm of the Lord is revealed to all the gentiles and all the ends of the earth see His salvation. Which is understood in two ways, as Jerome further warns: either the Father reveals His arm to all the gentiles, or the Son reveals His strength, of whom it is written: For virtue went out from Him, and healed all. And again, I felt virtue go out from me, which healed the woman with the issue of blood. That the Son of God is called the right hand and arm of the Father, there are many testimonies, of which we shall mention a few: His right hand and His holy arm shall save for Him. And elsewhere: In My arm the gentiles shall hope. Of whom also Jacob says: This shall be the expectation of the gentiles. And Psalm 88: Your arm with power. With this arm the Lord led the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt. But that He coupled all the ends of the earth to all the gentiles, who are to see the salvation of God, that shows what is also said in another place: Be converted to Me from the ends of the earth, and you shall be saved. And through Jeremiah: To You the gentiles shall come from the ends of the earth. And again: All the ends of the earth shall remember and be converted to the Lord. And all the families of the gentiles shall adore in His sight, because the kingdom is the Lord's, and He shall have dominion over the gentiles: so that not only the variety of individual nations, but also all the corners of the world are foretold to be about to believe in Christ. What of the fact that the Rabbis themselves refer this voice of the Evangelizer to the times of the Messiah; R. Chaja and others. See Midrash Shir Hashirim Cant. 2, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VOX SPECULATORUM TUORUM: LEVAVERUNT VOCEM: SIMUL LAUDABUNT)

Dicetis, quando Levitæ rursus in templo cantaturi sint lau- des Dei.

CUM CONVERTERIT DOMINUS SION) Cum populum in Sionem reverti fecerit.

Pessima detorsio loci illustris. Grotius nul- lum Evangelium in Veteri Testamento nisi carna- le sapit; nihil hic nisi liberationem corporalem crepat. Ideo Jeremiam Prophetam ingerit, de quo nec vola, nec vestigium in textu deprehenditur. Id vero facit fine pessimo, ut nempe cum Judæis se- quens caput, quod illustre vaticinium de Christi passione & exaltatione continet, quale vix ullum aliud in toto Veteri Testamento est, ad Jeremiam detorqueat. At non posse hunc locum de Jeremia intelligi, sed de Apostolis, aliisque præconibus sub Novo Testamento accipiendum esse, primum ἐ συνεχείᾳ cum præcedentibus, quibus dominatus Pharisæorum exitiosissimus, & adventus Christi gratatissimus, ut redimerentur gratis, & sine ar- gento ab isto animæ exitio, descriptus est, liquet. De quo Sebastianus Münsterus summam cohæren- tiæ præcedentium, & præsentium ita exhibuit, una cum nugis Rabbinicis: NON ADJICIET UT AMPLIUS IN TE VENIAT INCIRCUMCI- SUS. Hebræi, inquit, hæc omnia intelligunt de re- demptione, quam frustra expectant per Messiam fiendam: & per incircumcisum intelligunt regnum Ædom, hoc est, Romanorum, & per immundum, regnum Ismaël, id est, regnum Turcæ & Soldani. Nostri vero intelligunt de redemptione Christi sy- nagogæ promissa & jam exhibita: quasi dicat Deus: toties es capta & redempta, & deinde iterum vasta- ta, instituam aliquando redemptionem, quæ sit æterna, & quam nulla alia sequatur captivitas. Et ea redemptio est spiritualis, qua Christus in cruce nos gratis liberavit à peccatis, morte perpetua, & inferno, nullis nostris præcedentibus meritis. Quid mihi hic est! Est, inquit, populus meus in alia captivitate, graviori ea, quæ fuit in Ægypto, aut apud Assyrios: Nam qui illis præsunt, pro arbitrio suo, & non juxta verbum meum dominantur illis, ducunt eos in errores, faciunt eos ululare & blas- phemare nomen meum tota die. Curabo igitur ego Dominus, ut populus meus me agnoscat, & me loquentem audiat. Mittam Evangelistas, qui annuncient pacem & salutem, atque omne bonum non privatis hominibus, sed in montes pulcherri- mis suis pedibus ascendent, & toti mundo prædi- cabunt gratiam Dei & Evangelium Christi, & quod deinceps Deus in nobis regnaturus sit verbo suo, & non Moses ceremoniis suis. Hæc ille. Au- diamus hic Brentium nostrum: Rejecit, inquit, & damnavit Filius Dei Doctores Pharisæicæ doctrinæ & humanarum traditionum. Quid ergo? Num Eccle- sia eorum piorum, qui temporibus Pharisæorum & adventus Christi reliqui adhuc sunt inter Judæos, destituentur prorsus omnibus Doctoribus, & omni ministerio concionum? Nihil certe minus. Promit- tit enim Christus Filius Dei Ecclesiæ suæ alios pro Pharisæis Doctores. Primum promittit, seipsum fore eorum Doctorem: Deinde promittit, se missu- rum eis Apostolos suos, qui veram pacem, veram sa- lutem adnuntient. Hæc Brentius. Deinde quid ad fideles sub ista pressura liberatio mere corporalis, neglecta spirituali, ut tanto apparatu verborum tam magnifice describeretur? QVAM PUL- CHRI (vel potius amabiles) SUPER MON- TES PEDES ANNUNCIANTIS (rectius E- vangelizantis) PRÆDICANTIS PACEM, ANNUNCIANTIS BONUM, PRÆDICAN- TIS SALUTEM, DICENTIS SION, RE- GNAVIT DEUS. Singula verba ita comparata sunt, ut bona spiritualia ab Apostolis annuncianda, non autem liberationem corporalem à Jeremia prædicendam inferant. Super montes dicuntur an- nunciare, h. e. non in Chaldæa, sed in Judæa. Pulchre Brentius: quod dicit PEDES SUPER MONTES, respicit situm urbis Hierusalem, quæ cincta est mon- tibus. Sicut dicit Psalm. 124. Hierusalem, montes in circuitu ejus. Cum igitur Spiritus S. in Pro- pheta videt Apostolos è Galilæa, per montana ad ur- bem Hierusalem properare, ut accepto ibi Spiritu S. divulgent Evangelion, non in Hierusalem tantum, sed etiam in totum orbem terræ, exclamat præ ingenti gaudio: Quam speciosi, inquiens, quam grati, quam accepti, quam jucundi sunt pedes, seu legati pe- pestres, quos video ad nostram urbem per montes in circuitu positos proficisci, ut afferant nobis nun- cium expectatissimum. Porro verbum EVAN- GELIZANTIS rectius sine dubio convenit Aposto- lis Evangelium annunciantibus, quam Jeremiæ libe- rationem è Babylone prædicenti. Et de læto nun- cio gratiæ spiritualis adhibetur in hoc ipso Prophe- ta c. 61, 1. Pacis autem prædicatio quid nisi summam exhibet Evangelii, quum nec Christus aliud, quam pacem Apostolis, nec Apostoli aliud Eccle- siis in literis suis precati fuerint? Pace fruebatur etiam in Chaldæa populus Domini, non enim in bello, sed sub servitute erat. Hic vero Evangelica pax intimatur, quæ est reconciliatio Dei & homi- nis. Annunciatur BONUM, quo majus nullum est. Prædicatur salus vera & æterna. Dicitur Sioni spirituali: REGNAT DEUS TVVS. Nullum lætius nuncium, quam quod Christus Immanuel Deus nobiscum, Deus noster sedens ad dextram Patris gubernat Ecclesiam, quam sanguine suo re- demit. De quibus videatur prolixius B. Brentius. Porro, ne ambigamus, Evangelicos nuncios & Apostolos intelligi, eandem promissionem Deus iisdem verbis repetiit per Nahum c. 1. ECCE SV- PER MONTES PEDES EVANGELIZAN- TIS ET ANNVNCIANTIS PACEM; ubi ad- ditur celeusma ad solemnia sacra, & spirituales fe- stivitates; Celebra Juda festivitates tuas, & redde vota tua. Sed imprimis habemus interpretationem

Sole clariorem in N. T. Quum S. Paulus hoc vati- cinium Rom. 10, 15. de Apostolis & reliquis Evan- gelicis nunciis N. Test. interpretetur. Omnis enim, inquit, quicunque invocaverit nomen ejus, (Christi) salvus erit. Quomodo ergo invocabunt, in quem non crediderunt? Aut quomodo credent ei, quem non au- dierunt? Quomodo autem audient sine prædicante? Quomodo autem prædicabunt, si non mittantur? sicut scriptum est: Quam speciosi pedes Evangelizantium bona? Sed non omnes credunt Evangelio. Unde patet de Evangelio de Christo, cujus fide salutem conse- quimur, intelligendum esse dictum Propheticum, deq; præconio non Jeremiæ annunciantis liberati- onem è Babylonica captivitate, sed ministerii Evan- gelici annunciantis pacem per Christum partam & salutem æternam. Et per ANNUNCIANTEM in- telligendum esse quemcunque Evangelizantem, non autem individuum quoddam, aut personam singu- larem. Ac ne dubitemus nos ad Esaiam remitti, ac præsentem ejus locum respici, subjungitur Rom. 10, 16. querela, de non suscepta voce Evangelii per fidem ex hoc ipso vaticinio Esaiano: Esaias enim di- cit: Domine, quis credit auditui nostro? Ne ambigam9 de auditu & verbo Evangelii, atque fide in Christum agi, addit Apostolus συμπέρασμα ejusmodi: Ergo fides ex auditu, auditus autem per VERBUM CHRI- STI. Ne denique hæreamus, Apostolorum præco- nium designatum esse, en διαρρήδην id indigitat, de- clarans, quales hic præcones respexerit Propheta. Sed dico: Nunquid non audierunt? Et quidem in o- mnem terram exivit sonus eorum, & in fines orbis ter- ræ verba eorum. Quorum, nisi Apostolorum? Non certe Jeremiæ. Quale præconium œcumenicum, & universale hic etiam ab ipso Esaia prædictum est: PARAVIT DOMINUS BRACHIUM SAN- CTUM SVUM IN OCVLIS OMNIVM GENTIVM. ET VIDEBVNT OMNES FI- NES TERRÆ SALVTARE DEI NOSTRI, q. d. non revelabitur id tantum Judeis, sed etiam gen- tibus per totum orbem, ut ad fines usque terræ annun- cietur Evangelium, vel verbum Christi, quod ipse sit SALVTARE DOMINI, vel SALVATOR divi- nitus missus omnibus in se credentibus, sive à Judæ- is, sive à gentibus originem ducant. Quæ omnia vi- dit sine dubio GROTIUS, ideo in Annotat. ad Roman. 10, 15. agnovit hæc ex Esaiano hoc oraculo de prom- pta esse ab Apostolo, neque diffiteri potuit de Chri- sto eadem intelligenda esse, imo Judæos ipsos id crede- re professus est, sed ad consuetum suum κρησφύγε- τον se recepit, quod nempe tantum secundum sen- sum mysticum de Messia agant, at quoad literalem sen- sum, quem primum vocat, de Jeremia loquantur; sed sensus istius literalis, quem assignat ipse, nullum in- dicium est in textu Prophetico, imo omnia contra- rium loquuntur, uti hactenus ostensum. Nec Judæi, qui de Christo sermonem esse dicunt, quoad lite- ralem sensum de Jeremia intelligunt, sed literalem illum sensum esse ajunt de Christo. Neque Aposto- lus ex sensu mystico, h. e. qui præter literalem à S. S. intentus fuerit, uspiam probavit fidem. Imo nus- piam in Scripturis præter literalem sensum alius reperitur à S. S. intentus. Vanum ergo est, quod ait, SENSU PRIORE hæc dici de Jeremia (quia nun- quam talis sensus probabitur) ita tamen ut etiam VETERES JUDÆI intellexerint, hæc EMINEN- TIUS convenire in tempora Messiæ. Si de Messiæ tem- poribus ex intentione S. S. dicta sunt, de præconio Evangel. & pacis per Christum partæ, quod habe- mus ex interpretatione Apostolica, nec diffitentur Vet. Judæi, non possunt hæc dicta esse sensu gemi- no, & ex intentione S. S. de tempor. Jeremiæ, & annunciatione liberationis è captivitate Babyl.

Porro ne dubium ullum superesset, de pluribus E- vangelisantibus sermonem esse, deq; præconio lon- ge lateque propagando, additur in Propheta no- stro: VOX SPECULATORVM TUORUM (eo- rum se. qui pro salute Sionis excubias agunt Ezech. 3. Ebr. 13. audietur) LEVAVERUNT (rectius, levabunt.) VOCEM (suam) SIMUL LAUDA- RUNT (rectius jubilabunt) QVIA OCVLO AD OCVLVM VIDEBVNT CVM CON- VERTERIT DOMINVS SION. Non musfita- bunt, ut recte Brentius, sicut ἐγγαστρίμυθοι aut vates Ethnicorum è spelæis suis mussitant: nec susurra- bunt vel in angulis domorum, vel in latebris sylva- rum ac montium cum paucis arbitris: quod facere solent seditiosi & alii, qui vel instituti fœditate, vel sceleris immanitate lucem fugiunt: Sed attollent vocem suam tam alte, ut exaudiatur ab urbe Hie- rusalem, usque ad extremos fines terræ. In omnem enim terram exivit sonus eorum, & in fines orbis terræ verba eorum. Nec hoc solum, verum etiam simul laudabunt, pariter jubilabunt. Non tantum do- cebunt Evangelion Christi in orbe terrarum, initio facto in Hierusalem, sed etiam docebunt idem o- mnes Evangelion summa concordia. Una erit o- mnium laudatio, una jubilatio de rebus per Chri- stum Regem Zion gestis. Nam oculo ad oculum vide- bitur, palam coram omnibus manifestabitur, tum doctrina, tum miraculis, quod Dominus converterit seu reduxerit Sion, h. e. quod Christus Dominus noster redemerit Ecclesiam suam à tyrannide Satanæ, à pec- catis, à morte & inferno. Concludit exhortatione ad lætitiam publicam & œcumenicam Propheta: GAVDETE ET LAVDATE (jubilate) SI- MVL DESERTA JERVSALEM: QVIA CON- SOLATVS EST DOMINVS POPVLVM SVVM. Quæ consolatio quænam alia est, quam ea, quam toties inculcant Prophetæ, & noster c. 40, 1. Consolamini, consolamini, &c. Gaudete igitur & exultare, non tantum ea loca, quæ intra mœnia ur- bis Hierusalem continentur, sed etiam deserta & solitudines circa Hierusalem: quod tanta nunc erit civium multitudo, ut pomœria urbis usque ad deserta proferantur, & ex eremo fiat frequentissi- ma civitas. Dominus enim ipse, non per servos suos Prophetas, ut olim, sed sua ipsius persona coram consolatur populum suum, adnunciat populo E- vangelion suum, & redimit Hierusalem ab omnibus iniquitatibus suis, à potestate Satanæ & mortis. REDEMIT (גאל quod proprium est Filii Dei) JERVSALEM. Quod ante dixerat Dominus, GRATIS VENVNDATI ESTIS, GRATIS REDIMEMINI, hoc nunc factum esse, postquam Salus à Domino parta annunciata est per Aposto- los orbi, gloriantur & gaudent fideles; REDEMIT JERVSALEM. Neque enim tantum gaudium, quod tantum cum jubilatione conjunctum, & quod se porrigat ad extremos terræ fines, è libera- tione corporali, sed & spirituali Messiæ redempti- one per Evangelium divulgata concipitur. PARA- VIT (in Ebr. denudavit, quod alii de expeditione ad pugnam contra hostes spirituales Diabolum, peccatum, & mortem, alii rectius de manifestatione Christi explicant) DOMINVS (Deus Pater) BRACHIVM SANCTVM SVVM IN OCV- LIS OMNIVM GENTIVM. Quodnam illud brachium sanctum Domini sit, in oculis omnium gentium denudatum, seu manifestatum, ἐπεξήγησις subjuncta, vel finis istius manifestaionis docet. ET VIDEBVNT OMNES FINES TERRÆ SALVTARE DEI NOSTRI. Quapropter idem sunt BRACHIVM SANCTVM DOMI- NI, & SALVTARE DEI NOSTRI: Adeoque quum hoc posteriori nomine describi soleat Chri- stus, idem etiam per brachium Domini intelligitur. Quem etiam ita designavit Propheta cap. seq. v. 2. Et BRACHIUM DOMINI cui revelatum est? Perspicuum ergo ex his esse Hieronymus censet, extructa per Apostolos spirituali Jerusalem, id est, Ecclesia, quæ à Judæis fuerat derelicta, revelari bra- chium Domini cunctis gentibus & videre salutare ejus omnes fines terræ. Quod dupliciter, ut porro mo- net Hieronymus, intelligitur, aut enim revelat Pater brachium suum cunctis gentibus, aut Filius revelat fortitudinem suam, de quo scriptum est: Virtus enim ab eo egrediebatur, & sanabat omnes. Et iterum, sensi virtutem exiisse de me, quæ sanavit hæmorr- housam. Quod autem Filius Dei Patris dextera appel- letur & brachium, multa sunt testimonia, è quibus pau- ca dicemus: Salvabit sibi dextera ejus, & brachium sanctum illius. Et alibi: In brachio meo gentes sperabunt. De quo & Jacob dicit. Hic erit expe- ctatio gentium. Et 88. Psalmus: Tuum brachium cum potentia. Hoc brachio eduxit Dominus populum Israel de terra Ægypti. Quod autem cunctis gentibus omnes terræ terminos copulavit, qui visuri sunt salu- tare Dei, illud ostendit, quod & in alio loco dicitur: Convertimini ad me ab extremis terræ, & salvi eri- tis. Et per Hieremiam; Ad te gentes venient ab extremis terræ. Et iterum: Recordabuntur & con- vertentur ad Dominum omnes fines terræ. Et ad- orabunt in conspectu ejus omnes familiæ gentium, quia Domini est regnum, & ipse dominabitur gen- tibus: ut non solum varietas gentium singularium, sed & omnes mundi cardines credituri prænuncientur in Christo. Quid quod Rabbini ipsi vocem hanc Evan- gelizantis ad Messiæ tempora referant; R. Chaja & alii. Videatur Midras Schir Haschirim Cant. 2, 10.

## 52:11
Vers. 11. DEPART, DEPART, GO OUT FROM THENCE) The Chaldean: Separate yourselves, separate yourselves: that is, beware for yourselves of all legal uncleanness, and if you have contracted any, wash it away according to the law: do all things accurately when you go out. There shall be time enough; nor shall anyone hinder you.

YOU WHO CARRY THE VESSELS OF THE LORD.) You Sassabasat and his companions, Ezra 1. 8. 9. 10. 11.

It is easy to refute this merely Jewish gloss from what has been said: we shall see only how it was defeated in the Jews by Jerome. And this, he says, the Jews attempt to distinguish thus: go out from Babylon, and abandon their idols. Go out from the midst of it, and bring back to the temple the vessels which Nebuchadnezzar had taken when Jerusalem was captured, while Cyrus released the captives under Zerubbabel and Ezra, and do not depart from Babylon as you fled before from Egypt with tumult and fear, but with the peace and will of the King of the Persians and Medes, in whom appeared the will of the Lord, who protected and gathered you. Others interpret what we have said about Babylon as the Roman Empire, that at the coming of Christ, who is to liberate them, all these things may be fulfilled. But we, hearing above: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who announces and preaches peace? And: The Lord shall reveal his arm in the sight of all nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God: we understand this by no means of the Jews, but of the choir of the Apostles and all the Saints.
