But the Hebrew phrase does not allow that translation or paraphrase: for he is not said to be given into the hands of the powerful, or of the rich and the wicked, or to the rich and the wicked: since the case in Hebrew is the accusative, not the dative. The blessed D. Joh. Tarnovius explains it thus: Christ exposed his sepulchre with the wicked, i.e., he voluntarily offered himself to be scourged, crucified, to die and to be buried, no otherwise than if he himself had been wicked, and was rejected among them by men seeing him suffer these evils, nay, even with the rich (who is either unjust, or the heir of the unjust) he exposed himself, he was in death. A little more clearly in almost the same sense Osiander explains it thus: And his burial shall be given with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, i.e., he shall die and be buried no otherwise than any wicked man, or rich man, who snatch away their resources from others either by force or by impostures. For although Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus were pious men, who with a pious mind honorably buried CHRIST, yet the remaining Jews did not think more honorably of Christ's death and burial than if some most wicked impious person had died and been buried, and therefore they also took care to have him guarded by soldiers as if he were an impostor. Nor do the Weimar or Belgian Paraphrasts deny this, who guards were placed at the grave, Matt. 27. Others institute a transposition here, that he was buried with a rich man, but in death was with the impious, because he was crucified with thieves, but was laid in the monument of the rich man of Arimathea. Others, without such a μεταθέσει, place the prediction concerning Joseph here. But they vary again in their opinions: Vatablus refers these things to the place of crucifixion and burial, in this sense: he will die on Mount Calvary, where the graves of the impious were, and where punishment was taken of them, but when dead he will be carried by the rich Joseph into a grave, in which he will be hidden. But thus the impious are still joined with the burial, and the rich with the death, when the rich should have been joined with the burial, and the impious with the death. Therefore Münster interpreted it thus: He was cut off from the land of the living: that is, he was taken away by passion from this mortal life: and so that even in death he might be sated with reproaches, a grave was given to him not in the city of David, but in the place of Calvary, and where evildoers were put to death. And what is added: And with the rich man in his deaths: I think the Prophet looked to that which we read in Matt. 27: A rich man came from Arimathea, and placed the body in his new monument, etc. And he says in deaths, on account of the multiple punishments which they inflicted upon him, the innocent one. These are the words of Münster. The sum is: That he was led with the impious, near the criminals, to the place of punishment, and with the rich man, that is, in the monument of Joseph the rich man. The Genevan version takes that ויתן and he gave, impersonally, it was given, that is, his grave was disposed by the ordinance of men with the impious, but he was with the rich man in his death: that is, after he was dead, he was not buried with the impious, but in the grave of a rich man. To which the Italian version and the explanation of Amama also incline. Rivetus thinks that that Genevan interpretation can be helped thus: If that word AND HE GAVE is taken in the sense of esteeming, reckoning, comparing, i.e., everyone who saw him being subjected to punishment thought or reckoned that he would be buried with the wicked, and in the same grave with them, but the matter happened otherwise, because he was dead with the rich man, by whom he was buried and honorably laid to rest. Which explanation also pleased Constantine L'Empereur in Abraban. on this passage. AND THE PEOPLE DELIVERED HIS GRAVE WITH THE WICKED, i.e., intending in their mind that he should be buried with the wicked thieves, indeed he actually did this, while he was being taken from the midst by Pilate and the hands of the executioners along with the criminals, he was demanding it. BUT HE WAS WITH THE RICH MAN IN HIS DEATHS, i.e., divine providence so disposing it, that he should be in the hands of Joseph of Arimathea, a good and just man, a rich man, and a Senator of no common standing. Abr. Hulsius also made this his own interpretation in Theol. Judaic. l. 1. p. 2. p. 382, although in the former part of the verse he assigns the subject as the people, not with L'Empereur: whose opinion is nevertheless more convenient, because mention of the people was made in the preceding verse. Rivetus brings forward a similar explanation of others, which he also praises as EVEN MORE APT, namely that the ב is not held as a servile letter but a radical one, and it is not the noun מות signifying death, but the noun במה which signifies any building whatsoever exalted from the earth, or placed in a more excellent place. Whence among the Greeks βωμὸς an altar, as in this passage his monument, i.e., his tumulus, is noted: and the sense may be, his tumulus with the rich man, not the grave with the impious, as the enemies of the Messiah had determined. This observation, says Rivetus, is the more approved by me, because after it was noticed by Forster, a most learned German, Mercer reported the same with praise of the author, namely that the honorable and splendid burial of Christ is noted here, with which he was gifted by Joseph of Arimathea, a rich and noble man, although his grave had been destined beforehand among the impious and the condemned; and that learned man acknowledges that the conjectures which Forster uses are not light. The most learned author of the Pentaglot Lexicon, Valent Schindler, followed the same opinion as certain and explored; Bama, he says, signifies a building placed upon the grave of someone, a monument, an epitaph, etc. Is. 53, 9. bemotau his high places, i.e., his monuments, for bamotau with the Kametz changed into a Scheva contrary to custom. Therefore the Masoretes annotate in the margin that a similar one does not exist, which, that is, has a Scheva, and the quiescent vav is missing. Therefore קֶבֶר Kever, a grave, and בָּמָה, a monument, are the same. These are his words. This passage is therefore conveniently understood concerning the monument of the rich Joseph. For he is called by Matt. c. 27, 57, ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος, a rich man, as if the Evangelist had wished to point his finger to this passage of Isaiah. These are the words of Rivetus: referring that interpretation to Forster, who in R. בָּמָה rendered the text thus, that indeed his grave was with the impious as far as the destination of the Jews was concerned, but as far as divine direction was concerned, in death he was with Joseph the rich Senator. And he placed his grave with the evildoers, and his high places with the rich man. Which sense is also approved by Oecolampadius, as well as by Franciscus Gomarus, and is also praised in the Annotations on the Belgian Bible. Which Alexander Morus prefers to other interpretations. Although he wishes its first discoverer not to be Forster, but R. Aben Ezra, because he interpreted the word ET DEDIT as concerning thought, and בְּמֹתָיו as concerning high places: which he judges should be converted into a better sense in this way: And he gave (the Jew) i.e. he was thinking of giving him a grave with the wicked: But with the rich man his monument. The best sense, he says, arises from this, and is clearly Evangelical: the Jewish people indeed, whom he had given to him as companions in death, also destined for him companions after death, as far as the infamy of burial is concerned, but with the rich man was his monument, namely Joseph of Arimathea, who in Matt. 27, 57 is called ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος. Aben Ezra also brings forward other Rabbis who took the word בְּמֹתָיו as concerning High Places, as it is used in Deut. 32, 13. But some things seem to stand in the way of this interpretation; First, that no mention of the Jew has been made in the preceding. Then, that he who gave had been expressed before. For there is a copulative particle, which looks back to him: AND HE GAVE or HE PLACED, he of whom it was before: A blow to him. Thirdly, he refers the Hebrew verb וַיִּתֵּן to both, namely to the giving into the grave, and to בְּמֹתָיו, which Forster also acknowledged. And therefore it is rashly referred by Morus only to the former, and in the latter an ellipsis of the substantive verb is invented. Fourthly, it is precariously assumed that that verb implies only thought. It signifies he actually gave, not by thought alone. And since he was truly given בְּמֹתָיו not by thought alone, it is necessary that he was also truly given with the wicked into the grave. Fifthly, in the word בְּמֹתָיו a permutation of the points is established according to Forster, and thus a corruption of the text is argued here. There is one who translates it thus (Matthæus Wasmuth in Disp. inaugur. Anno 1666. held at Kiel) And he placed (set near) the wicked (soldiers) at his grave, and the rich man (that one from Arimathea) at his high places (i.e. the altar of the cross, so that the Savior might be honorably buried). But who placed, who the soldiers, the rich man? No mention of a subject here. Nor are the wicked and the soldiers synonyms, or can soldiers be understood from the name רשעים: nor is במות suitable for designating a cross, but rather high monuments or altars: however, the denomination of the cross as an altar is Ecclesiastical, not Biblical. Nor was Joseph of Arimathea placed at the altar of the cross, nor did he stand by it, but he granted his own monument for the burial of Christ, and brought the body of it. Add what Hackspan urges, that no passage can be brought forward where במות is taken for a sepulcher.

I omit the other interpretations, which refer to the manner of death and burial. The simplest sense seems to be if you render it κατὰ πόδα. AND HE PLACED (Christ, that is, of whom we previously warned that this should be understood) THE WICKED IN HIS SEPULCHER AND THE RICH IN HIS DEATHS: so that it may be understood concerning the fruit of his burial and death, in which this Prophet is entirely occupied here. For other examples show that the verb נתן is constructed with an accusative, and is similarly used when it concerns a place of reposition: it is established in countless places that this verb governs the accusative, and that את is the mark of the accusative when it is joined with that verb. That a similar construction is used with a similar meaning when the discourse is about a place, even with the ellipsis of the preposition ב, is established from 2 Sam. 20:3, and he placed them (in) the house of custody, Jer. 37:4, and they had not placed him (in) the house of the prison, c. 37:15. & they placed him (in) the house of the prison, which our Lord Dr. Weller proved with more [examples] in the cited place. And the preposition IN, omitted in the former member, can be repeated here from the latter, to which it is added. For the other member has it similarly: AND THE RICH במותיו IN HIS DEATHS, which the blessed Brentius most correctly observed: HE SHALL GIVE THE WICKED FOR A SEPULCHER &c. This ought to be translated thus: He gave the wicked into his sepulcher, and the rich into his death. For although the preposition IN is not added in the Hebrew text to the noun of the sepulcher, yet because in the latter part of this sentence it is added to the noun of death, it is to be understood in the former part as well. For in copulative sentences among the Hebrews, the latter part is accustomed to interpret the former, which is most frequent not so much in the Proverbs of Solomon as in the Prophets. And therefore, there is no room to doubt that the translation is correct.

But what will be the sense, how did he place THE WICKED in his sepulcher, or into his sepulcher, how did he place the rich in his deaths! A twofold explanation of this sentence is handed down, which serves to express the use of the passion of Christ, and thus is no less congruent with the text than it is consonant with the words, and therefore is to be preferred to other interpretations by a just judgment: We owe the former to the blessed Brentius, a most fortunate interpreter of the Holy Scriptures, which we shall ascribe to his words, as being equally the simplest and the sweetest. It is explained, he says, this sentence, what the Son of God effected by his cutting off from the land of the living, that is, by his death and burial. He indeed died and was buried, but he did not enter into his death and sepulcher alone, but took with him the wicked and the rich, that is, the unrighteous. For the rich are spoken of very badly not only in Holy Scripture, but also in the literature of the nations. Christ calls riches the Mammon of unrighteousness and thorns. And, The rich man, he says, will enter with difficulty into the kingdom of heaven. Elsewhere, however, the rich man is called either unrighteous, or the heir of the unrighteous. Wherefore the rich man in this place of Isaiah is understood as the unrighteous. When therefore the Son of God was dying and being buried, he led with him into his death and sepulcher the wicked and the unrighteous, so that, with their impiety and unrighteousness expiated and buried, they might enjoy together with him the benefits of his resurrection. The other is to be credited to our Lord Dr. Weller, which no less serves to commend the fruit of the death and burial of Christ, and commends itself by its sweetness: For he observes that the concrete is placed here for the abstract, a custom not unusual for the Hebrews, the wicked for impieties, the rich for riches; adding this elegant and sweetest paraphrase: Christ not only hid our sins in his sepulcher, lest they should make us restless and incite us to more evils (thus the use of the burial of Christ is described privatively), but also acquired and distributed to us the highest riches of soul and body through his most exquisite infernal sorrows (for thus the word of death is taken Gen. 2:17, Ex. 10:17, 2 Kings 4:40, Psalm 18:6) (thus the use of the passion is depicted positively). Such an interpretation was produced at the same time by the blessed Glassius in his Sacred Grammar, p. 823, which in the same year, that is, 1634. appeared at Jena, in which our Lord Dr. Weller's 'Armory of Christ-knowledge', or the explanation of the 53rd chapter of Isaiah, was published here at Wittenberg. But after he had warned that the concrete is sometimes placed for the abstract, he added these things in an appendix of certain past matters, as he calls them, concerning this place. To this could perhaps be referred Isaiah 53:9, עָשִׁיר rich for עֹשֶׁר riches. The words flow thus with a most pleasant sense and usage: וַיִּתֵּן and he gave or placed (Christ) אֶת־רְשָׁעִים impieties (from the singular רֶשַׁע impiety) קִבְרוֹ (in) his sepulcher (ellipsis of the prefix בְּקִבְרוֹ, which is expressly placed in the following word) וְאֶת־עָשִׁיר and riches (concrete for abstract) בְּמֹתָיו in his deaths (i.e., in his death: by enallage of the plural for the singular, for the sake of denoting excellence: see tract 1, can. 24) עַל because he did not commit iniquity, nor was there deceit in his mouth. These are the words of the blessed Glassius. Nor would we have spoken beside the point, that the concrete is used with emphasis by the Holy Spirit, because not only are our impieties hidden in the sepulcher of Christ, which he so carried in his body upon the wood of the cross that he brought them as it were into his sepulcher, so that they might be eternally hidden from the face of God, so that thus their ἀθέτησις (annulment) might be made, Heb. 9:16, and they might be buried with Christ, and as if they remained in the sepulcher, while he himself, without any burden of sin which he had taken upon himself, rose from the sepulcher and entered into his glory, as the blessed Glassius explains: But that also the UNRIGHTEOUS themselves seem to be buried with Christ, and placed in his sepulcher with him, just as the Holy Apostle, declaring the fruit of Christ, says that we are buried with Christ, Rom. 6:4, Col. 2:12, as if explaining this illustrious passage, and that thus HE PLACED THE UNRIGHTEOUS IN HIS SEPULCHER. For as by his death alone we all have died for the sins of the dead, as many as are subject to sin, and by reason of merit justified from sins Rom. 7, 7. because by his death justification from sins has been obtained for all 2. Cor. 5, 14. so by his burial we all have been buried with our iniquities: because by his burial a holy rest in the dormitories has been acquired for us, and when the Holy One of the Lord was enjoying rest, absolved from sin, and taken away from the judgment of God, he had no need to see corruption in the sepulcher. Thus for us all rest in the sepulcher has been procured, and incorruptibility, so that, to wit, we need not remain perpetually in corruption, but that our bodies may be able to come forth ἄφθαρτα: and so in this way the UNGODLY are as it were buried together with Christ, which sense, when it came into my mind, seemed to me the sweeter and more harmonious, the more abundantly it offers the most efficacious consolations of the Catholic merit of Christ, in whom alone our hope is reposed, even by reason of the article concerning the BURIAL OF CHRIST, and the more simply it overflows from the words; but it was rendered altogether more pleasing when, having inspected the most learned Brentian commentaries, I saw that the same had already pleased him, and had likewise been elucidated by him from the Apostolic phrase; whose words, therefore, for the sake of fuller illustration, I will add ἀυτολεξεὶ: when therefore the Son of God died and was buried, He took with Him into His death and sepulchre the ungodly and the iniquitous, so that, their impiety and iniquity being expiated and buried, they might enjoy together with Him the benefits of His resurrection. For this seems clearly to be that which Paul later said: Whoever of us have been baptized into death. WE HAVE THEREFORE BEEN BURIED together with Him through Baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life, etc. And shortly after: If we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him. And elsewhere: You have died with Christ from the elements of the world. And: For you have died, and our life is hidden with Christ in God: But how could Christ take the ungodly and iniquitous with Him into His death and sepulchre, so that their iniquity might be buried? The cause of this matter is added. He gave, he says, the ungodly for His burial, and the iniquitous for His death, because He Himself did no iniquity, and no deceit was found in His mouth. For if Christ Himself had committed iniquity and had designated sin, He would have had to enter into His death and sepulchre alone, and would not have been able to expiate the sins of others. But now, because He Himself never committed any sin, neither in heart nor in words nor in deeds, but is perfectly just and holy, therefore He expiated by His death, and buried and abolished by His burial the sins of others, so that it is rightly and aptly said that He took the ungodly and iniquitous with Him into His death and sepulchre.

Now if one prefers to understand RICH MAN properly, rather than interpret it as THE INIQUITOUS, although that exposition also commended itself to Blessed Luther (It is an obscure Hebraism that puts rich man for ungodly; but perhaps the trope was born from the fact that rich men are for the most part ungodly, just as in the Gospel Christ calls it the mammon of iniquity. Likewise, it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven) and it conforms quite well to the Prophetic custom of mutual ἐξήήσις (exegesis) of such hemistichs, by which the same thing is repeated in other words: for the sake of greater evidence and emphasis, and of exaggerating, let us say, THE RICH MAN PLACED IN THE DEATHS OF CHRIST, because all our spiritual and heavenly riches, in which we are rich in God, must be sought in the death of Christ, so that the most precious death of Christ may be proposed as a heavenly Treasury, in which is all the sufficiency of riches, of which Eph. 1:18, ch. 2:7, and that although all THE UNGODLY have been buried with Christ, so that no one should be considered ungodly any longer, provided he believes in Christ, by whose merit God justifies the ungodly: yet no rich man escapes otherwise than through the death of Christ: and thus BY HIS DEATH, in which He Himself was utterly forsaken, needy, and most afflicted, whoever is truly rich is rich, just as by HIS BURIAL the UNGODLY were buried to a man, because as far as it was in Him, He brought it about by His merit that no ungodly person should remain in the world any longer. If therefore you ask where the rich man is found in the Lord, you should seek him in the deaths of the Lord; for He was extremely miserable, since He was subjected not to one, but to several deaths, so that by that misery and poverty of His we might be made rich, 2 Cor. 8:9. Mention is made of DEATHS in the plural, because Christ truly sustained several deaths, not only of various afflictions, which were like death and deadly, but because He was subject to both temporal and also eternal or infernal death, forsaken by God, and made a curse for us. But mention is made of THE RICH MAN μοναδικῶς (singularly), or in the singular, so that an individual application, as they say, may be taught, that He not only died and was buried for all, so that He might acquire heavenly riches for all, and prepare liberation from impiety, but also for individuals, so that each one may be able to apply all those things to himself, as if they had been acquired for him alone, and each one may dare to profess with true confidence of heart, CHRIST HAS PLACED ME, A RICH MAN, IN HIS DEATHS, as Paul says, Christ loved me, and gave Himself into death for me, Gal. 2:20, i.e., He made me rich by His highest and most extreme, if I may say so, poverty, which in His death and desertion by God was as great as it could not be greater: for this was the highest degree of κενώσεως (emptying). If therefore you wish to be rich in God, you should believe that Christ has placed you in His deaths, that you are that very עשיר (rich man) whom He placed in His deaths, and thus that Christ underwent death for you, so that He might make you rich. Jerome also acknowledges that this pertains to the fruit, although he provides another explanation, which we subjoin: He gave the ungodly for His burial, and the rich man for His death. Or the worst, for His burial, and the rich for His death, signifying both peoples: so that in the bad and the worst, who before did not have the knowledge of God, the multitude of the Gentiles is shown: in the rich, whose was the testament and the legislation and the Prophets, the Jewish people is demonstrated. Therefore, for this reason the Lord suffered and was buried, so that He might gather to Himself a Church from both peoples. Analogous, which I note at the end, are in some way the interpretations of those who wish the powerful and fruitful passion of Christ to be indicated, so that He might subject the ungodly, who are powerful in morals and authority and wealth, and render them obedient to the Father's will, and thus they refer that 'He will give' to Christ, who by His burial and death was to bring it about that the ungodly would be converted to the Father: or, in almost the same sense, they refer it to God the Father, i.e., for the death which He bitterly endured, the Father will subject to Him ungodly men, and those of a profligate life. All these, therefore, acknowledge that these words look to the efficacy of the death and burial of Christ, since it is manifest that the Prophet in this chapter is not so much describing the passion of Christ historically, as explaining the fruit of the same. But enough of this rather difficult passage, yet one involved in greater difficulties through various interpretations. We return to Grotius.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET DABIT IMPIOS PRO SEPULTURA, ET DIVITEM PRO MORTE SUA.) Illi ipsum etiam in- terficere voluerant, ut legimus Jer. 26. At Deus ipsius vice viros potentes quidem, sed improbos, Sacerdotes nempe mortem Jeremiæ machinatos, morti dedit per Chaldæos 2. Reg. 25, 18. 19. 20. 21. Nihil illis divitiæ suæ profuerunt, quibus redimi se posse speraverant. Sensum hunc bene expresserunt Græci. EO QVOD INIQVITATEM NON FECERIT, NEQVE DOLUS FUERIT IN ORE EJUS.) Quan- quam nihil aliud dixerat, quam quod Deus ei manda- verat.

Non inhærebimus impiæ detorsioni textus. Nam utut quacunque ratione Sacerdotes per impios in- telligi possent, (quæ tamen glossa mere precaria est,) utut DIVITIS nomine illi etiam intellige- rentur, (quod vero probatum non est, nec pro- bari potest) falsissimum est de Chaldæis hic, & excidio per ipsos facto, agi: impium, verba illa, quæ de uno Christo sonant, ad Jeremiam detor- queri: nec minus impium, de munere recte ad- ministrato Prophetæ accipi, quæ omnimodam innocentiam & ἀναμαρτησίαν Christi exhibent. Nam nihil evidentius, quam quod verba ista, EO QUOD INIQUITATEM NON FECE- RIT, NEQUE DOLUS FUERIT IN ORE EJUS, omne peccatum, sive quod factis, sive quod verbis, sive quod animo committitur, ab hoc subjecto removeant. Qui enim nec iniquitatem fecit ullam, neque dolum ullum, is omnis pec- cati vere expers est. Neque aliter interpreta- tur hanc sententiam S. S. quam de absoluta inno- centia 1. Petr. 2. imo in hoc textu toties ea asseritur, quoties ipse propter peccata nostra vulneratus, pro- pter prævaricationem populi percussus dicitur, & quæ his similia sunt : illic enim negatur propter sua pec- cata percussus, & innocentia ejus asseritur. Ideo de nullo alio, quam de Messia, qui solus ἀναμάρτητος est, hæc accipi possunt. Hoc de nullo, inquit Hie- ronymus, penitus hominum intelligi potest, ut nec o- pere, nec sermone peccaverit, dicente Scriptura: Ne- mo mundus à sordibus, etiamsi unius quidem diei fuerit vita ejus, & omnes sicut oves erravimus, u- nusquisque in via sua declinavit, nisi de illo qui pec- cata nostra portavit, & pro nobis dolet, & vulneratus est pro iniquitatibus nostris, & afflictus est propter scelera nostra, cujus morte sanati sumus. Excusat jam Christum, inquit B. Lutherus & dicit fuisse in- nocentissimum, qui nec verbo nec vita quenquam læ- serit. Hæc enim summa innocentia est, neminem læ- sisse, neque dicto neque facto. Innocentissimus igitur pro nocentissimo judicatus. Sed quum habeamus inter- pretem omni exceptione superiorem S. Petrum, qui 1. Epist. 2. λευκᾷ δι Φωνῇ testatus est, hic nullum alium quam CHRISTUM intelligendum esse, qui pro nobis passus, reliquit nobis exemplum, ut se- quamur vestigia ejus: Qui peccatum non fecit, non in- ventus est dolus in ore ejus; quid opus est aliis argu- mentis ad jugulandum στρεβλότητα Grotii? qui de- nique in Annotatis ad locum Petrinum haud obscu- re videtur agnoscere hæc κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν de Christo accipienda esse, hanc exprimens verborum ex Esaia adductorum sententiam: Christus nullo suo cri- mine in mortem actus est Luc. 23, 41. Joh. 8, 46.

Quum ergo de subjecto dubium nullum esse de- beat, nec quisquam Christianorum ambigat; de ve- ro sensu horum verborum magis laborandum, de quo variant admodum sententiæ. LXX. Interpp. reddi- dere, & dabo pessimos pro sepultura ejus, & divites pro morte illius: ad quos frustra provocat Grotius, utpote qui de Jeremia nihil habent, nec forte de eo somniarunt. Cyrillus sic eos interpretatur: Vide- tur in his verbis illud velle significare, & id verum esse ostendere, quod jam diximus, eo quod impii admodum & iniquissimi fuerant, qui populo Dei accensi erant, propterea Christum esse ad mortem abreptum. Nam, inquit, quandoquidem impie in illum debacchati sunt, & principem vitæ interfecerunt, inconsiderate impie- tatem in eum etiam, qui servat, exercentes: hinc & quidem valde merito improbos & divites, inquit, pro sepultura ejus, & pro morte ejus, dabo in manus hostium. Duobus enim modis deliquerant Judæi, tum quod interfecerint Dominum: tum quod ejus se- pulturam calumniati fuerint. Similem fere sen- sum reddidit Hieronymus, quod Scribas & Phari- sæos ac Sadducæos, Sacerdotes & Pontifices, qui in po- pulo ante regnabant, & variis opibus affluebant, post Domini passionem Romanis tradiderit Deus, & æternæ subjecerit servituti, eoque sensu pro ejus sepultura & morte impii divitesque traditi sint. Analoga est Hack- spanii glossa de caterva impiorum deturbandorum in sepulcrum, quod (Messiæ) innocenti paraverant, & de divitibus (Synedrii assessoribus) pro morte ejus (Messiæ) judicium mortis, ac similes pœnas luituris. Sed etsi ob crucifixionem & interfectio- nem CHRISTI Judæi traditi sint, non tamen ob sepulturam ejus traditi dicendi. Neque commuta- tio in Ebræo textu designatur, ut Vulgatus reddi- dit cum LXX. Interpp. quod impii pro sepultura dandi sint, unde fundamentum istius & Grotianæ glossæ corruit. Porro non de exitio novissimo Judæo- rum hic res est, sed de passione, morte ac sepultura Christi, cujus exanitionem & exaltationem descri- bit Propheta. Denique non apparet, quomodo glossa ista Prophetæ verbis quadret: dedit impios sepulchrum ejus, id est, propter ejus mortem tradidit impios ultricibus hostium manibus, vel deturbavit im- pios in sepulcrum, quod innocenti paraverant, & di- vitem in mortibus ejus, id est divites illos ex Judæis, qui assessores erant Synedrii, in judicium mortis pro morte ejus, ut Hackspan. eam glossam incrustat. Quam inferri textui, non efferri ex eodem nimis clarum est. Et recongnoscere debuerat hic Theod. Hacksp. propria verba, qui ad v. 8. similem depra- vationem (Populo qui Christum pro plaga affecto habuit & abominabili, contigit ejusmodi plaga ut ipsi sint abominabiles prorsus:) Certum est, inquit, in hoc capite duo præcipue tractari, nempe quis pœnas dat, & qua de causa. Ille est Messias, hæc peccata omnium hominum etiam Judæorum. Non igitur pœna, quæ manet Judæos ob Christi con- temtum hic prædicitur. Nemo utique hunc sensum ex iis verbis elicet. Alii sepulturam & mortem impio- rum hic indigitari volunt, ipsis à Christo judice in- fligendam, eoque abripiunt Chaldaicam paraphra- sin: tradet impios in gehennam & divites divitia- rum, qui inique fecerint, in mortem perditionis. Non abnuit Raim. Martinus in Pug. Fid. pag. 430. Nota sicut descripsit eum Propheta per meritum passionis fidelium Redemptorem; Ita descripsit eum per potentiam Deitatis infidelium damnato- rem, ubi ait capitulo 53. ויתן את־רשעים קברו & dabit impios in sepulcrum, vel in fossam suam. Quod exponens Targum Jonathanis ait, וימסר ית רשיעיא לגיהנם & tradet impios ad gehennam. Sed quum ista contorta sint, ad sepulcrum & mortem Christi plerique hæc pertinere agnoscunt. Sed alii ad modum, alii ad fructum sepulturæ & mortis referunt. Priores iterum variant: Zwing. sic exponit: Sepulcrum ei dabitur cum impiis. Sepul- chrum ponitur pro nece per Synecdochen. Inter latro- nes n. interfectus est. ET EXALTATIO INTER PRÆDONES, i. e. cujus supplicium vel autoritas & dignitas ejus cum prædonum fortuna finem inveniet. Quæ vero quilibet videt intricata & contorta esse. Nam sepulcrum hic distinguitur à morte, non vero mortem notat. Nec è voce במותיו exaltatio ex- sculpi potest, nedum crucifixio, aut dignitas vel au- toritas. Deniq; עשיר prædones notare quomodo docebitur? Ideo perplexam istam glossam nemo se- quutus est è Zwinglianis. Oecolamp. ita transfert: & dedit cum impiis sepulcrum ejus, & cum divite excelsa ejus, i. e. Mausolea. Interpretationem autem hanc tradit: crucifigens occidet, sicut impium & oc- cidet sicut divites, qui non propter maleficia, sed divitias occiduntur: sed quis inde certum aliquem sensum hauriet! Credo quod seipsum haud intelle- xerit Oecolampad. Et cur sepulcrũ cum Mausoleo commemorat, si nihil aliud quam mortem indicare vult! Junii hæc est ἐξήγησις: Populus Judæorum de- dit impiis i. e. Ethnicis sepulturam Christi, i. e. tradidit eum gentibus occidendum, & diviti i. e. Pilato, ut eum morte afficeret, non quod aliquid in eo dignum mor- te viderent, sed contra, quia non poterant ferre ejus justitiam & integritatem. Sed recte reprobatur illa à Riveto: Quia per DARE SEPULTURAM intel- ligi tradere ad mortem, vix ex alia simili phrasi osten- di potest. Deinde divitis nomen ad Pilatum nulla ratio- ne astringitur: ideo coactam censet illam interpre- tationem. Addimus quod verbum DEDIT perpe- ram ad populum Judæorum referatur, quum potius ad Christum referri debeat. Quod Calvinus de Deo patre explicat, hoc modo, quod Deus Christum tra- diderit in manus impiorum, & divitis vel divitum vio- latorum, ut per impios & divites idem significetur, ac Pharisæi & Sacerdotes, Pilatus & Romani milites notentur. SEPULCRUM a. accipit Metaphorice, quod impij & violenti eum veluti obruerint, ut in- ter se & sanguinarias manus sepultus censeri possit, sed hoc coactum est. Non multum diversa est Gro- tii interpretatio, quam in libr. de verit. Christ. relig. V. n. XIX. tradidit: Ad mortem usque & sepultu- ram datus est in manus potentium atq; impiorum, cum tamen nemini fecisset injuriam. Sed phrasis E- bræa eam translationem aut paraphrasin non pati- tur: non enim in manus potentum, aut divitum atq; impiorum datus dicitur, aut divitibus & impiis: quum casus accusativus in Ebræo sit, non Dativus. B. D. Joh. Tarnovius sic exponit: Christus expo- suit cum improbis sepulcrum suum, h. e. voluntarie se- se obtulit ad flagellandum, crucifigendum, morien- dum & sepeliendum, non secus ac si ipse fuisset im- probus, & inter eos ab hominibus hæc mala eum perpeti videntibus reprobatus est, imo cum divite, (qui aut iniquus, aut iniqui hæres) se exposuit, in morte fuit. Paulo luculentius eodem pene sensu Osiand. ita exponit: Et dabitur cum impiis sepultura ejus, & cum divitibus in morte ejus, i. e. morietur & se- pelietur non aliter atque quisquam impius, vel dives, qui aliis suas facultates vel per vim, vel per imposturas eripiunt. Etsi enim Joseph de Arimathia & Nicode- mus fuerint pii viri, qui CHRISTUM animo pio honorifice sepelierint, tamen reliqui Judæi de Chri- sti morte & sepultura non honorificentius sense- runt, quam si sceleratissimus quispiam impius mor- tuus & sepultus fuisset, ideoq; etiam eum quasi im- postorem per milites custodiri curarunt. Neq; ab- nuunt Vinarienses, aut Belgici Paraphrastæ, qui reddunt, sepulchrum ejus cum impiis positum fuisse, id- que ita exponunt, quod impii custodes sepulchro ap- positi fuerint Matth. 27. Alii transpositionem hic in- stituunt, quod sepultus sit cum divite, in morte autem fuerit cum impiis, quia cum latronibus crucifixus, sed in monumento divitis Arimathiæ conditus fue- rit. Alii absq; ejusmodo μεταθέσει prædictionem de Josepho hic collocant. Sed variant iterum senten- tiis: Vatablus refert hæc ad locum crucifixionisex& sepulturæ, hoc sensu, morietur in monte Calvariæ, ubi erant sepulcra impiorum, & ubi de iis sumebatur supplicium, at mortuus deferetur à divite Joseph in sepulchrum, in quod recondetur. Sed ita adhuc con- junguntur impii cum sepultura, divites cum morte, cum divites cum sepultura, impii cum morte fuis- sent conjungendi. Proinde Münster. ita interpre- tatus est: Succisus est de terra viventium: hoc est, sub- latus est per passionem ab hac mortali vita: & ut et- iam in morte opprobriis saturaretur, datum est illi sepulcrum non in civitate David, sed in loco Calvariæ, & ubi malefactores interficiebantur. Et quod sub- ditur: Et apud divitem in mortibus ejus: ego pu- to Prophetam respexisse ad id quod Matth. 27. legi- mus: Venit homo dives ab Arimathia, & posuit corpus in monumento suo novo &c. Et dicit in mortibus, ob multiplices pœnas quas ei innocenti inflixerunt. Hæc Münsterus. Summa est: Ductum esse cum impiis prope facinorosis ad supplicii locum, se- pulchrum, & cum divite, id est, in monumento Jo- sephi divitis. Versio Genevensis impersonaliter ac- cipit illud ויתן & dedit, datum erat, id est, dispositum ordinatione hominum sepulchrum ejus cum impiis, sed fuit cum divite in morte sua: id est, postquam mor- tuus fuit, non fuit cum impiis sepultus, sed in sepulchro divitis hominis. Quo etiam Italica versio abit, & explicatio Amama. Genevensem illam interpre- tationem Rivetus ita juvari posse censet: Si verbum illud ET DEDIT sumatur significatione existi- mandi, reputandi, comparandi h. m. existimavit vel reputavit unusquisque qui eum vidit supplicio affici cum sceleratis, in eodem etiam cum illis sepulchro sepultum iri, sed aliter res accidit, quia mortuus fuit cum divite, à quo sepultus est, & conditus ho- norifice. Quæ explicatio placuit etiam Constan- tino L' Empereur in Abraban. ad h. l. ET POPU- LUS TRADIDIT CUM IMPROBIS SEPUL- CRUM EJUS sc. animo constituens, ut cum im- probis latronibus sepeliretur, imo reipsa hoc egit, dum à Pilato, & carnificum manibus, cum flagitiosis è me- dio tolleretur, exposcebat. AT CUM DIVITE FUIT IN MORTIBUS SUIS sc. divina provi- dentia sic disponente, ut in Josephi Arimat. viri boni & justi divitis, & Senatoris non vulgaris manibus esset. Quam interpretationem suam etiam fecit Abr. Hulsius in Theol. Judaic. l. 1. p. 2. p. 382. etsi in prio- ri parte versus subjectum tradens non assignet populum cum Lempereurio: cujus tamen senten- tia ideo convenientior, quod in versu præcedente populi mentio facta. Adfert Rivetus similem alio- rum explicationem, quam etiam, ceu ADHUC APTIOREM laudat, ut nempe ב non habeatur pro servili sed radicali, & non sit nomen מות mor- tem significans, sed nomen במה quod significat æ- dificium quodcunque à terra exaltatum, aut in loco excellentiori positum. Unde apud Græcos βωμὸς altare, ut h. l. monumentum, f. tumulus ejus note- tur: & sensus sit, tumulus ejus cum divite, non se- pulcrum cum impiis, ut hostes Messiae constitue- rant. Hæc autem observatio, inquit Rivetus, eo magis mihi probatur, quod postquam à Forstero doctissimo Germano fuit animadversa, eandem Mercerus, cum autoris laude retulit, nempe honestam & splendidam Christi sepulturam hic notari, qua à Josepho Arima- thæo, homine divite & nobili, donatus fuerit, quamvis inter impios prius, & damnatos, sepulchrum ejus de- stinatum foret; & agnoscit vir ille doctus, conje- cturas quibus utitur Forsterus, leves non esse. Ean- dem sententiam sequutus est tanquam certam & exploratam doctissimus Lexici Pentaglotti autor Valent Schindlerus; בָּמָה Bama, inquit, significat æ- dificium sepulchro alicujus impositum, monumen- tum, Epitaphium &c. Ef. 53, 9. bemotau excelsa sua, h. e. monumenta sua pro bamotau mutato Kametz in Scheva præter morem. Ideo in margine Masoretæ annotant, non extare simile, quod sc. Scheva habeat, & vav quiescens deficere. Idem igitur sunt קֶבֶר Kever sepulchrum, & בָּמָה monumentum. Hæc ille. Com- mode igitur hic locus intelligitur de monumento divitis Josephi. Hic enim dicitur à Matth. c. 27, 57. ἄνθρω- πος πλούσιος homo dives, quasi digitum voluisset in- tendere Evangelista ad hunc Esaiæ locum. Hæc Rive- tus: referens eam interpretationem ad Forsterum qui in R. בָּמָה sic reddidit textum, quod nempe se- pulcrum ejus fuerit cum impiis quoad destinationem Judæorum, at quoad directionem divinam in morte fuerit cum Josepho Senatore divite. Et posuit apud ma- lefactores sepulchrum ejus, & apud divitem excelsa e- jus. Qui sensus Oecolamp. etiam probatur, ut & Fran- cisco Gomaro, laudatur quoque in Annot. ad Bibl. Bel- gica. Quem Alexander Morus aliis interpretationi- bus præfert. Quamvis ejus primum repertorem non Forsterum esse velit, sed R. Aben Ezra quod vocem ET DEDIT interpretatus sit de cogitatione & בְּמֹתָיו de excelsis: quod ita in meliorem sensum convertendum censet: Et dedit (Judæus) i. e. cogi- tabat dare ipsi sepulcrum cum impiis: At cum divite monumentum ejus. Optimus autem, inquit, hinc ex- istit sensus, ac plane Evangelicus: Judæus quidem po- pulus, quos in morte ipsi socios dederat, etiam destina- bat ipsi post mortem socios, quoad infamiam sepulturæ, at cum divite fuit monumentum ejus, Josepho nimirum Arimathæo, qui Matth. 27, 57. ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος dicitur. Adducit Aben Ezra Rabbinos etiam alios, qui vocem בְּמֹתָיו de Excelsis acceperint, uti Deut. 27, 29. adhibetur. Sed huic interpretationi obsta- re videntur nonnulla; Primo quod nulla Judæi men- tio facta sit in antecedentibus. Deinde quod ille qui dedit, antea expressus fuerit. Nam habetur par- ticula copulativa, quæ illum respicit: ET DE- DIT vel POSUIT is, de quo antea: Plaga ipsi. Tertio refert se verbum Ebræum וַיִּתֵּן ad utrum- que, nimirum ad dationem in sepulcrum, & בְּמֹתָיו, quod agnovit etiam Forsterus. Ideoque temere à Moro tantum ad prius refertur, & in posteriori fin- gitur ellipsis verbi substantivi. Quarto precario id as- sumitur, quod verbum illud tantum cogitationem in- ferat. Significat actu dedit, non cogitatione sola. Et quum vere datus sit בְּמֹתָיו non sola cogitatione, ve- re etiam datus cum impiis sit in sepulchrum, necesseum est. Quinto in voce בְּמֹתָיו punctorum statuitur per- mutatio juxta Forsterum, adeoq; corruptionis tex- tus hic arguitur. Est, qui ita transferat (Matthæus Wasmuth in Disp. inaugur. Anno 1666. Kiloni ha- bita) Et adstituit (apposuit) improbos (milites) se- pulcro suo, & divitem (illum de Arimathia) excel- sis suis (i.e. aræ crucis, ut honeste funeraretur Salva- tor). Sed quis apposuit, quis milites, divitem? Nulla hic mentio subjecti. Nec improbi & milites Syno- nyma sunt, aut è nomine רשעים intelligi milites possunt: neque במות cruci, sed potius excelsis monumentis, aut aris convenit designandis: aræ autem crucis denominatio Ecclesiastica est, non Biblica. Nec Josephus de Arimathia appositus fuit aræ crucis, aut adstitit eidem, sed monumen- tum suum sepulturæ Christi concessit, & corpus Christi eidem intulit. Adde quod Hackspanius urget, quod locus nullus afferri possit, ubi במות de sepulcro capiatur.

Mitto cæteras interpretationes, quæ ad modum mortis & sepulturæ referunt. Smplicissimus sen- sus videtur, si κατὰ πόδα reddas. ET POSUIT (CHRISTUS sc. de quo id intelligendum esse, antea monuimus) IMPIOS IN SEPULCHRUM SUUM ET DIVITEM IN MORTES SUAS: ut de fru- ctu sepulturæ & mortis ejus intelligatur, in quo to- tus occupatus hic Propheta est. Nam verbum נתן cum accusativo construi, & similiter adhiberi, cum de loco repositionis agitur, exempla alia docent: verbum illud regere accusativum, & notam accusa- tivi את esse, cum isto verbo jungitur, innumeris lo- cis constat. Quod autem simili significatu cum de loco sermo est, similis constructio adhibeatur, et- iam cum ellipsi præpositionis ב, constat ex 2. Sam. 20, 3. & posuit illas (in) domum custodiæ, Jer. 37, 4. nec posuerant eum (in) domum carceris, c. 37, 15. & posuerunt eum (in) domum carceris, quæ pluribus probavit Dn. D. Wellerus noster l. c. Et repeti hic potest præpositio IN omissa in priori membro, è posteriori, cui addita est. Similiter enim habet membrum alterum: ET DIVITEM במותיו IN MORTIBUS EJUS, quod rectissime observavit B. Brentius: DABIT IMPIOS PRO SEPUL- TURA &c. Hoc sic verti debet: Dedit impios in sepulturam suam, & divitem in mnrtem suam. Etsi enim præpositio IN non adjicitur in Hebræo textu ad nomen sepulturæ, tamen quia in posteriori parte hujus sententiæ adjicitur ad nomen mortis, etiam in priori parte subintelligenda est. In sententiis enim copulativis apud Hebræos, posterior pars solet inter- pretari priorem, id quod non tam in Proverbiis Salo- monis, quam in Prophetis, frequentissimum est. Ideo- que de translatione, quin recte se habeat, dubitare adeo non licet.

Sed quis erit sensus, quomodo posuit IMPIOS in sepulchro suo, aut in sepulchrum suum, quomodo posuit divitem in mortibus suis! Gemina hujus sen- tentiæ traditur explicatio, quæ ad exprimendum usum passionis Christi facit, adeoque non minus textui congruit, quam verbis consonat, ac proinde aliis interpretationibus justo judicio præferenda: Priorem debemus. B. Brentio felicissimo S. litera- rum interpreti, quam verbis ejus adscribemus, ut- pote simplicissimam pariter & dulcissimam. Expo- nitur autem, inquit, hæc sententia, quid Filius Dei abscissione sua de terra viventium, hoc est, morte & sepultura sua effecerit. Mortuus quidem est, & se- pultus, non autem solus ingressus est in mortem & se- pulcrum suum, sed assumsit secum impios & divites, hoc est, iniquos. Divites enim non in sacra tantum Scriptura, verum etiam in literis gentium pessime au- diunt. Christus vocat divitias Mammonam ini- quitatis & spinas. Et, Dives, inquit, difficile in- trabit in regnum cœlorum. Alias autem dicitur dives aut iniquus, aut iniqui hæres. Quare dives in hoc Esaiæ loco pro iniquo intelligitur. Cum igitur Filius Dei moreretur & sepeliretur, duxit secum in mortem & sepulchrum suum impios & iniquos, ut expiata & sepulta impietate, ac iniquitate ipsorum, fruerentur una cum ipso beneficiis resurrectionis ejus. Altera accepto ferenda Dn. D. Wellero nostro, quæ non minus facit ad fructum mortis & sepulturæ re- Christi commendandum, ac suavitate sua se com- mendat: Observat enim concretum pro abstracto, more Ebræis non inusitato, impios pro impietatibus, divitem pro divitiis hic poni; addens hanc elegan- tem & dulcissimam paraphrasin: Christus non solum peccata nostra in sepulcrum suum abdidit, ne nos irre- quietos facerent, & ad mala plura instigarent (sic usus sepulturæ Christi ςερητικῶς describitur) sed & sum- mas animæ & corporis divitias exquisitissimis suis in- fernalibus doloribus (sic enim vox mortis sumitur Gen. 2, 17. Ex. 10, 17. 2. Reg. 4, 40. Psal. 18, 6.) nobis acquisivit & distribuit (sic usus passionis θετικῶς de- pingitur.) Qualem interpretationem ὁμοφώνως eo- dem tempore prodidit B. Glassius in Gr. Sacr. p. 823. quæ eodem anno, hoc est M DC XXXIV. Jenæ prodiit, quo Dn. D. Welleri nostri ὁπλοθήκης χριςο- πονήμων ἐξήγησις, seu Capitis 53. Esaiæ explicatio hic Witebergæ edita est. Postquam autem monuerat pro abstracto quandoque concretum poni, hæc in ἐπει- σάγματι præteritorum quorundam, ut vocat, de hoc loco adjecit. Huc posset forsan referri Esa. 53. v. 9. עָשִׁיר dives pro עֹשֶׁר divitiæ. Verba ita fluunt sensu usuque jucundissimo: וַיִּתֵּן & dedit seu posuit (Chri- stus) אֶת־רְשָׁעִים improbitates (à singulari רֶשַׁע improbitas) קִבְרוֹ (in) sepulcro suo (pro בְּקִבְרוֹ ellip- sis præfixi, quod expresse in voce sequenti ponitur) וְאֶת־עָשִׁיר & divitias (concretum pro abstracto) בְּמֹתָיו in mortibus suis (h.e. in morte sua: per enal- lagen pluralis pro singulari, excellentiæ denotandæ causa: vid. tract. 1. can. 24.) עַל propterea quod iniquitatem non fecerit, nec dolus (fuerit) in ore ejus. Hæc B. Glassius. Neque præter rem di- xerimus, concretum cum emphasi adhibitum à S. S. quod non tantum improbitates nostræ reconditæ sint in sepulchro Christi, quas ita portavit in corpore suo super lignum crucis, ut intulerit quasi in sepul- chrum suum, ut à facie Dei æternum sint abscondi- tæ, ut ita earum facta sit ἀθέτησις Ebr. 9, 16. & cum Christo sepultæ sint, atq; in sepulcro, quasi reman- serint, ipse vero sine omni peccati onere, quod in se susceperat, è sepulcro resurrexerit, & in gloriam suam ingressus sit, ut B. Glassius exponit: Sed quod etiam INIQUI ipsi cum Christo sepulti videantur, & in sepulcro ejus positi cum ipso, quemadmodum fru- ctum Christi declarans S. Apostolus nos cum Chri- sto sepultos dicit Rom. 6, 4. Colos. 2, 12. quasi locum hunc illustrem explicans, & quod sic IPSE PO- SUERIT INIQUOS IN SEPULCHRUM SU- UM. Nam uti mortuo ipso uno pro peccatis mortui sumus omnes, quotquot peccato sumus obnoxii, & ratione meriti justificati à peccatis Rom. 7, 7. quia morte ejus impetrata omnibus est justificatio à pec- catis 2. Cor. 5, 14. ita sepulto ipso nos omnes sepulti su- mus cum iniquitatibus nostris: quia sepultura ejus acquisita nobis est quies sancta indormitoriis, & cum Sanctus Domini quiete fruebatur absolutus à pecca- to, & ablatus è judicio Dei, in sepulcro non videre opus habebat corruptionem. Ita nobis omnibus parta est quies in sepulcro, & incorruptibilitas, ne sc. per- petuo in corruptione manere opus habeamus, sed ut prodire corpora nostra possint ἄφθαρτα: adeo- que ita quasi simul cum Christo IMPII consepulti sunt, qui sensus cum in mentem veniret, tanto suavior & conciunior mihi videbatur, quanto copiosius effi- cacissimas præbet meriti Christi Catholici, in quo uno spes nostra reposita est, etiam ratione articuli de SEPULTURA CHRISTI consolationes, quan- toque simplicius è verbis redundat; sed gratior omnino reddebatur, ubi inspectis eruditissimis commentariis Brentianis videbam eandem ipsi jam placuisse, & pariter ab eodem ex Apostolica phra- si dilucidatum esse; cujus proinde verba uberio- ris illustrationis gratia, ἀυτολεξεὶ adjiciam: Cum igitur Filius Dei moreretur & fepeliretur, duxit se- cum in mortem & sepulchrum suum impios & ini- quos, ut expiata & fepulta impietate ac iniquitate ipsorum, fruerentur una cum ipso beneficiis resurre- ctionis ejus. Nam hoc plane illud videtur, quod postea Paulus dixit: Quicunque baptizati sumus in Chri- stum Jesum, in mortem ejus baptizati sumus. SE- PULTI IGITUR SUMUS una cum illo per Ba- ptismum in mortem, ut quemadmodum excitatus est Christus ex mortuis per gloriam Patris, ita & nos in novitate vitæ ambulemus, &c. Et mox: Si mortui sumus cum Christo, credimus, quod & vi- vemus cum illo. Et alias: Mortui estis cum Chri- sto ab elementis mundi. Et: Siquidem emortui e- stis, & vita nostra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo: Sed quomodo potuit Christus impios & iniquos secum in mortem & sepulchrum suum assumere, ut iniquitas eorum sepeliretur? Additur hujus rei causa. Dedit, inquit, impios in sepulturam suam, & ini- quos in mortem suam, propterea quod ipse iniqui- tatem non fecerit, & non sit inventus dolus in ore ipsius. Si enim Christus fecisset ipse iniquitatem, & designasset peccatum, necesse habuisset folus in mor- tem & sepulchrum suum ingredi, nec potuisse alio- rum peccata expiare. Nunc autem quia ipse nullum unquam peccatum fecit, nec corde nec verbis, nec fa- ctis, sed est perfecte justus & sanctus, idcirco expia- vit morte, & sepelivit ac abolevit sepultura sua alio- rum peccata, ut recte & apte dicatur, quod duxerit impios & iniquos secum in mortem & sepulchrum suum.

Jam si DIVITEM malit quis proprie intelli- gere, quam per INIQUOS interpretari, quan- quam & B. Luthero illa expositio sese probavit (Est obscurus Hebraismus, quod divitem ponit pro impio; fortasse autem inde natus tropus est, quod di- vites plerumque sint impii, sicut in Evangelio Christus vocat Mammona iniquitatis. Item difficile est, divi- tem ingredi regnum cœlorum) & Propheticæ con- suetudini admodum conveniat ejusmodi hemistichio- rum mutua ἐξήγησις, qua idem aliis verbis repetitur: majoris evidentiæ & emphaseos, reiq; exaggeran- dæ gratia dicamus, DIVITEM IN MORTIBUS CHRISTI POSITUM, quod divitiæ nostræ uni- versæ spirituales & cœlestes, qua in Deo divites su- mus, in morte Christi quærendæ sint, ut mors Christi pretiosissima instar cœlestis Gazophylacii propo- natur, in quo omnis divitiarum fufficientia, de qui- bus Eph. 1, 18. cap. 2, 7. quodque IMPII quidem omnes sepulti cum Christo sint, ut nullus habendus fuerit impius amplius, modo in Christum credat, cujus merito justificat Deus impium: Dives vero quisquam non evadat aliter nisi per mortem Christi: adeoque EJUS MORTE, in qua ipse summe de- sertus, egenus & afflictissimus fuit, dives sit, qui- cunque vere dives est, quemadmodum EJUS SE- PULTURA sepulti sunt IMPII ad unum omnes, quia quantum in ipso fuit, merito suo effecit, ne ul- lus in mundo amplius superesset impius. Si ergo quæras, ubi dives in Domino inveniatur, in Domi- ni mortibus eum quæras; ille enim extreme miser erat, cum non uni, sed pluribus subjiceretur mor- tibus, ut illa ejus miseria & paupertate nos divites redderemur, 2. Cor. 8, 9. MORTIUM in plurali mentio fit, quia mortes plures revera sustinuit Christus non tantum variarum afflictionum, quæ instar mortis erant, & mortiferæ, sed quod cum morti temporali, tum etiam æternæ vel infernali ob- noxius fuerit, desertus à Deo, & maledictum fa- ctus pro nobis. DIVITIS autem μοναδικῶς men- tio fit, vel in singulari, ut individualis, ut loquun- tur, applicatio doceatur, quod non tantum prou- tei niversis mortuus & sepultus sit, ut omnibus acqui- reret divitias cœlestes, & pararet liberationem ab impietate, sed etiam pro singulis, ut unusquisq; illa sibi applicare possit universa, ac si uni sibi acquisita essent, ac quisque vera cordis παῤῥησίᾳ profiteri ausit, CHRISTUS POSUIT ME DIVITEM IN MORTIBUS suis, ut Paulus ait, Christus dilexit me, & tradidit sese in mortem pro me, Gal. 2, 20. h. e. divitem me fecit, summa & extremissima, ut ita di- cam, paupertate sua, quæ in morte & desertione Dei tanta erat in ipso, quanta major esse non pote- rat: hic enim summus erat κενώσεως gradus. Si ergo dives esse velis in Deo, credas, Christum te posuisse in mortibus suis, te esse illum ipsum עשיר, quem in mortibus suis posuit, adeoque Christum mortem pro te subiisse, ut te divitem faceret. Agnoscit & Hiero- nymus, ad fructum hæc pertinere, quamvis aliam tradat explicationem, quam subjungimus: Ipse de- dit impios pro sepultura sua, & divitem pro morte sua. Sive pessimos, pro sepultura ejus, & divites pro morte ejus, utrumque populum significans: ut in ma- lis & pessimis, qui ante Dei notitiam non habebant, ostendatur gentium multitudo: in divitibus quorum erat testamentum & legislatio & Prophetæ, Judaicus populus demonstretur. Ergo idcirco passus est Domi- nus & sepultus, ut ex utroque populo sibi Ecclesiam con- gregaret. Analogæ, quod sub finem annoto, sunt quodammodo eorum interpretationes, qui poten- tem & fœcundam indigitari volunt passionem Chri- sti, ut impios moribus, & authoritate atque opibus potentes subjecerit, Patrisque voluntati obsequen- tes reddiderit, adeoque illud dabit ad Christum re- ferunt, qui sepultura & morte sua effecturus erat, ut impii ad Patrem converterentur: vel, sensu ferme eodem, ad Deum Patrem referunt, h. m. pro morte, quam acerbam tulit, subjiciet illi Pater impios homi- nes, & vitæ profligatæ. Hi ergo omnes agnoscunt, verba hæc spectare ad efficaciam mortis & sepulturæ Christi, siquidem manifestum sit Prophetam in hoc capite non tam historice passionem Christi de- scribere, quam fructum ejusdem explicare. Sed hæc de loco satis difficili, at per interpretationes varias majoribus difficultatibus involuto. Regre- dimur ad Grotium.

## 53:10
Ver. 10. AND THE LORD WAS PLEASED TO CRUSH HIM IN INFIRMITY.) Yet it seemed good to God to crush and weaken him: i.e., to attenuate him with hunger, filth, and squalor. Active verbs among the Hebrews often have the meaning of permitting. The cause follows, why God permitted this. Ver. same. IF HE SHALL LAY HIS SOUL FOR SIN, HE SHALL SEE A LONG-LIVED SEED.) You translate correctly: That when he has subjected himself to punishments, he may see seed, and live long. Among the Hebrews, a punishment even unjustly inflicted is called אשם, because it is inflicted if not on the source, certainly as if on the source. Thus it appears that חטאת is taken in Gen. 31, 39. Zach. 14, 19. Jeremiah lived long in Egypt. AND THE WILL OF THE LORD SHALL BE DIRECTED IN HIS HAND.) Better: in his (namely) hand it shall prosper. Many will be converted to piety through him, which the following also explain. Ver. 11. HE SHALL SEE AND SHALL BE SATISFIED.) He shall see for a long time to satiety. A similar manner of speaking in Hebrew, Gen. 25, 8. 35, 29. 1. Paralip. 23, 1. 29, 28. 2. Paralip. 24, 14.

Grotius continues with his Jeremiah. But since these things are written with the very rays of the sun concerning Christ, there is no need for many words. First, it is referred to God, that he was crushed in infirmity. Which is snatched in vain to the permission concerning the persecution of Jeremiah. For it is not a bare permission, but a peculiar decree and counsel of God that is designated. That God so decreed, constituted, and willed that this servant of God, even though just, should be crushed, indeed that the Lord delighted in it, which the emphasis of the Hebrew word implies: which certainly is not a bare permission, nor does it suit the passion of Jeremiah. For חפץ is distinguished from אבת, this is simply 'he willed': that, 'he willed with the highest delight.' Furthermore, not only is a voluntary subjection to punishment noted, but a sacrifice for sin. 'If he shall have laid his soul as a sacrifice for sin,' which was not fulfilled in Jeremiah. For did Jeremiah lay himself down as a punishment or a sacrifice for sins? But it must be understood of Christ, who gave himself for us, and offered himself to God the Father as a sacrifice and a sweet-smelling savor, Eph. 5:2. That phrase is sacrificial, nor can it be taught by any example that 'to lay down one's soul for sin,' or similar expressions, is the same as 'to subject oneself to a punishment unjustly inflicted.' In the Hebrew it is, 'if he shall have laid אשם,' which denotes a sacrifice for sin, 'his soul,' as the blessed Luther most correctly [rendered]: 'When he has given his life as a guilt-offering.' For אשם signifies either a transgression in the Scriptures, or a sacrifice for a transgression, or a more grievous sin, from אשם 'to transgress, to sin,' Lev. 5:16, ch. 7:1, etc. Concerning which Tarnovius [writes] on this passage. The word אשם denotes first the guilt of a great sin, but then it signifies a victim or host for a sin committed out of set malice, which in Greek you would not ineptly call κάθαρμα, and in Latin a piaculum (expiatory sacrifice). See very many examples in Leviticus 4, 5, 7, 14. He wished by such an atrocious word, just as the Apostle did, to indicate the depravity of the sins of the Prophet, the severity of God the Father, and the charity of Christ, who was made ἁμαρτία and κατάρα for us. Also this, that he alone is the one truly expiatory victim, whereas the rest in the Old Testament were at least shadows and types, Heb. 9. And how in these [is] this one Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, Apoc. 13:8. Nor should the observation of Brentius be passed over here: For although in Moses there are diverse kinds of victims for sin, of which one is called Chatath, which they interpret as a host for sin; the other is called Ascham, which they interpret as a host for transgression, yet because in the description of the law of the host of ascham in Lev. 6 it is expressly added: 'The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and it shall be forgiven him for each one of all those things which he did, and in which he transgressed,' therefore I think the Holy Spirit wished in this place to call Christ Ascham rather than Chatath, so as to signify that Christ truly expiated each one of ALL things, whether sins or transgressions, in whatever way they had been designated by men. What of the fact that Grotius himself against Socinus, p. 16, had written thus: 'Scripture calls the expiatory host for sin, sin,' Lev. 4:3, ch. 5:6, Ps. 40:7. Following this formula of speaking, therefore, Isaiah 53 said of these: תשים אשם נפשו 'he laid his soul as sin,' i.e., he made his soul liable to the punishment of sins. Nor did Paul [speak] otherwise: 'Him who had not known sin, God made sin, that we might be the righteousness of God in him,' 2 Cor. 5:21. In which place, as also in Rom. 8:3 and Gal. 3:13, the Apostle alluded to this prophecy. Compare Rivetus on this passage. Grotius, in the places which he now brings forward to prove that אשם denotes only a punishment inflicted upon an innocent person, does not have that word, but חטאת, which in the other [passage], Zech. 14:19, is used not of a punishment unjustly, but justly inflicted by God upon the nations, and is not used of punishment alone, but brings in guilt at the same time: 'This shall be the sin of Egypt, and this the sin of all nations that shall not have ascended to celebrate the feast of tabernacles.' In the other [passage], Gen. 31:29, it is indeed used of an unjust exaction, but there it is a matter of the unjust Laban. But when God strikes someone, so that he has need to lay his soul as אשם, a sacrifice for sin, how will that punishment be considered unjust, unless God himself be argued of injustice! And what is this to the phrase 'to lay one's soul for a transgression,' by which it is most well known that not just any punishment, but death is brought in! For to lay one's soul is to lay down one's life, since Scripture is accustomed to denote life by the word 'soul.' It is therefore a mere perversion when it is explained otherwise concerning other punishments, not concerning death. Add that here the discourse is about a voluntary death: For the words in the source are to be rendered, HIS SOUL EXPOSED ITSELF AS A SACRIFICE FOR SIN, because תָּשִׂים is the 3rd person singular of the FEMININE gender, and therefore in construction it ought to be referred to נֶפֶשׁ. Therefore the discourse is not about a punishment unjustly inflicted, but voluntarily undertaken, when it was being inflicted by God the just judge. And thus B. Tarnovius explains it with Franc. Junius. But Ludovicus de Dieu suggests another paraphrase on this passage. I do not think תָּשִׂים here is the 3rd person perfect feminine gender to be construed with נַפְשׁוֹ, as Junius and others wished, by subaudition of 'himself,' much less is it put for יָשִׂים as it seemed to the Vulgate. But [I think] it is the 2nd person perfect masculine gender and is referred to God, and thus I translate: 'When you shall have laid his soul as a transgression,' and I think the Apostle alluded to this phrase, 2 Cor. 5:21, when he said, 'For him who did not know sin, he made sin for us.' Which in Hebrew you would correctly say: כִּי אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדַע אָשָׁם שָׂם אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ תַּחְתֵּנוּ. For him who did not know sin, he (namely God) laid his soul as sin for us. Furthermore, that phrase, HE SHALL SEE A LONG-LIVED SEED, 'Jeremiah shall see a seed, and shall live long,' how jejune and uncertain it is! For the seed and long-lived life is understood of him who shall have laid his soul or life for a transgression. But did Jeremiah, after he laid down his life, have a long-lived life? And what is that seed which he saw? For here is signified the seed of that very one who lays his soul as a sacrifice for transgression. Therefore it can be understood of no other than the Messiah, who had to see a spiritual seed, and have a long-lived life, after he shall have laid down his soul. For the faithful and pious are called the seed and children of Christ, Ps. 22:31 and ch. 11:3. And as seed arises from a grain cast into the earth, so also the pious [arise] from Christ having suffered, died, been buried, and resurrected. To which Christ himself looked, John 12:24. He seemed cut off from the land of the living, like some severed stock, but he shall bring forth innumerable plants. The death of other men takes away all hope of seeing seed, but the death of Christ was fruitful, and not only was it not an impediment to the propagation of the Church, but it was the cause of the begetting of offspring, because he who died vivifies his people, [and] acquires [those] to be propagated more and more. He seems, however, with Rivetus as judge, to allude to Isaac, whom his father placed upon the altar to be sacrificed, from whom, if not dead, yet destined for death, and as it were restored to his father after death, the seed was so propagated that it equaled the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea. And therefore interpreters rightly observe: that 'seed' is said emphatically, and connotes the resurrection of the Messiah, and life after death, and that blessing which the Lord bestows upon those whose posterity, while they themselves are living, is propagated through various generations. For there are those who indeed leave seed behind them, which however they do not see with their own eyes, or if they do see it, it happens only in part, and for a short time. But truly this one, living after death, so that he may never die, shall see his seed forever. That יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים 'he shall prolong his days,' refers to the seed, HE SHALL SEE LONG-LIVED SEED. But in the Hebrew text it pertains to the Messiah, i.e., he shall live perpetually. It will not be as those who, departing from life, leave children surviving them, in whom they live while dead themselves, but he shall live together with his seed, and shall remain forever. The Targum agrees, if you look at the phrase, explaining the 'seeing of seed' through the multiplication of sons and daughters. To which explanation the sequence of the context of this and the following chapter adds strength, inasmuch as in it, having explained the sufferings and the consequent glory of Christ, the Prophet turns himself to the Christian Church, as that which was to beget children of God in Christ, and it treats of the fruitfulness of the Church of the New Testament (whose bridegroom and husband is Christ) and of the multiplication and propagation of the seed of Christ throughout the whole world. Therefore, the things which are subjoined here are to be understood in the same sense concerning the Messiah: THE WILL OF THE LORD SHALL PROSPER IN HIS HAND, which are wrongly twisted again to Jeremiah. That will and εὐδοκία of the Lord, by which it pleased Him to crush Christ for us, and thus the work of redemption through his hand, i. e., through his own effort alone יצלח shall succeed most prosperously, and shall be perfected with all the barriers and obstacles of impediments broken through: concerning which will Christ [speaks in] Ps. 40:8, John 4:34, and Luther in the marginal gloss, deß HErrn Fürnehmen, that is, his will and works, which he has in mind, namely the redemption of men. Which prosperity of success is discerned not so much in the passion and resurrection of Christ as in the Church and the propagation of the spiritual seed, Job 6:43, ch. 13:24, Heb. 2:20. Wherefore that good pleasure of the Lord was that Christ should repair the lost justice by his life and death, should rise again from this, and should gather the Church throughout the whole world, which therefore ought to have been perfected through Christ, and to succeed most happily. FOR THAT WHICH HIS SOUL HAS LABORED, HE SHALL SEE AND SHALL BE SATISFIED. The word עמל, as our Dr. Weller rightly observed, denotes labor or troublesome pain of mind and body, and properly that anxious labor which was imposed upon man on account of transgression in the garden of Eden, and it has a kinship with מעל he has transgressed, Ps. 90:10. Soul is taken for man, and thus he himself is said to have labored as much in soul as in body; that the labor of the soul is indicated principally, however, is not obscurely gathered from the fact that the subject laboring has been denominated from the soul. The word HE SHALL SEE denotes not a simple vision, but by a common Hebraism, perception with a sense of pleasure. Compare Is. 60:5, ch. 66:14. R. Kimchi understands בטוב, which entire phrase is had in Jer. 29:32. Whence it is explained by the Blessed Luther: wird er seine Lust sehen [he shall see his desire]. HE SHALL SEE, HE SHALL BE SATISFIED. It is an asyndeton, not without emphasis, and that figure is used to judge more moved and rapid affections of the mind, as if you were to say, immediately and most abundantly he shall be surrounded with all good things. שבע is not to be explained concerning any satiety whatsoever, but in a peculiar manner and style of Scripture it expresses the joy with which the elect shall be satisfied in the other life, Ps. 16:3, 17:15, 22:27, 65:6, 91:16, as the Blessed Tarnovius rightly noted: Whence Dr. D. Weller elicits this paraphrase: His soul will indeed have to labor on account of the primal transgression of Adam, nevertheless, having been rescued, he will behold with singular delight and sweetness the good things, and will enjoy them abundantly even without weariness in eternal life. Which things, however, we judge are to be understood principally concerning the joy which the Messiah perceives from his spiritual seed. For he does not rejoice so much on account of his own happiness, but on account of the prosperous success in the work and good pleasure of the Lord, in the propagation of the Church, just as by his passion he willed to prepare joys not for himself, but for us, and our salvation is his highest delight. Which sense the consequences confirm: HE SHALL SEE AND SHALL BE SATISFIED IN HIS KNOWLEDGE, THE JUST SERVANT HIMSELF SHALL JUSTIFY MANY. Through the resurrection, Christ was not only himself enriched with immense goods and suffused with the satiety of heavenly joy, but he communicates them with his own, and from this he perceives the highest joys.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET DOMINUS VOLUIT CONTERERE EUM IN INFIRMITATE.) Tamen Deo visum est eum conterere & infirmare: i. e. attenuare fame, illuvie, squalore. Verba Activa apud Hebræos sæpe permittendi habent si- gnificatum. Causa sequitur, cur id Deus permiserit. Vers. eod. SI POSUERIT PRO DELICTO ANI- MAM SUAM, VIDEBIT SEMEN LONGÆVUM.) Ver- teris recte: Vt cum semetipsum subjecerit pœnis, videat semen, diuque vivat. Hebræis pœna etiam injuste irrogata אשם dicitur, quia infligitur si non fonti, certe quasi fonti. Sic חטאת sumi apparet Gen. 31, 39. Zach. 14, 19. vixit diu Jeremias in Ægypto. ET VOLUNTAS DOMINI IN MANU DIRI- GETUR.) Melius: in manu (ejus scilicet) prosperabitur. Multi per ipsum ad pietatem convertentur, quod & sequen- tia explicant. Vers. 11. VIDEBIT ET SATURABITUR.) Videbit diu ad satietatem. Simile loquendi genus in Hebræo, Gen. 25, 8. 35, 29. 1. Paralip. 23, 1. 29, 28. 2. Paralip. 24, 14.

Pergit Grotius suum Jeremiam. Sed quum hæc ipsissimis Solis radiis scripta sint de Christo, multis opus non est. Primum ad Deum refertur, quod contritus sit in infirmitate. Quod frustra ad permissionem circa Jeremiæ persequutionem abri- pitur. Non enim nuda permissio, sed peculiare Dei decretum & consilium designatur. Quod ita decre- verit, constituerit atque voluerit Deus, ut hic ser- vus Dei, etsi justus, contereretur, imo quod in eo de- lectatus fuerit Dominus, quod infert emphasis vocis Ebrææ: quæ certe non est nuda permissio, nec Jere- miæ passioni convenit. Nam חפץ distinguitur ad אבת, hoc simpliciter est voluit: illud, voluit cum summa delectatione. Deinde vero non solum spon- tanea pœnæ subjectio notatur, sed sacrificium pro deli- cto. Si posuerit pro delicto animam suam, quod non in Jeremia impletum est. Nunquid enim Jeremias seipsum posuit pœnam vel sacrificium pro deli- ctis? Sed de Christo intelligendum est, qui dedit semetipsum pro nobis, Deoque Patri obtulit in sacri- ficium & odorem suavitatis, Ephes. 5, 2. Phrasis il- la sacrificialis est, neque doceri ullo exemplo pot- est, ponere pro dilecto animam suam, aut similes lo- quutiones idem esse, quod pœnæ se subjicere inju- ste irrogatæ. In Hebræo est, si posuerit אשם, quod notat sacrificium pro delicto, animam suam, ut rectis- sime B. Lutherus: Wenn er sein Leben zum Schuld= Opffer gegeben hat. Nam אשם aut delictum significat in Scripturis, aut sacrificium pro delicto, vel peccato graviori, ab אשם delinquere, peccare, Lev. 5, 16. c. 7, 1. &c. De quo Tarnovius in h. l. Vox אשם notat primo reatum peccati grandis, deinde vero signi- ficat victimam seu hostiam pro peccato ex destinata malitia commisso, quod Græce non inscite κάθαρμα, Latine piaculum diceres. Vide exempla quam pluri- ma Levit. 4. 5. 7. 14. sapp. voluitque tam atroci vo- ce, sicut & Apostolus, indicare Prophetæ peccatorum pravitatem, Dei Patris severitatem, ac Christi, qui factus est ἁμαρτία & κατάρα pro nobis chari- tatem. Etiam hoc, quod hic solus unica vere expia- toria sit victima, cum reliquæ in V. T. fuerint saltem umbræ ac typi Hebr. 9. Et quomodo in his hic uni- cus Agnus ab origine mundi occisus, Apoc. 13, 8. Nec prætereunda hic observatio Brentii: Etsi enim in Mose diversa sunt genera victimarum pro peccato, quo- rum alterum vocatur Chatath, quod interpretan- tur hostiam pro peccato; Alterum vocatur A- scham, quod interpretantur hostiam pro delicto, tamen quia in descriptione legis hostiæ ascham Lev. 6. diserte additum est; Expiabit eum sacerdos co- ram Domino, & remittetur ei unumquodque o- mnium eorum, quæ fecit, & in quibus deliquit, idcirco puto Spiritum Sanctum voluisse hoc loco Chri- stum Ascham potius, quam Chatath vocare, ut signi- ficaret, Christum vere expiasse unum quodque OMNI- UM, sive peccatorum, sive delictorum, quoquo mo- do ea ab hominibus designata fuissent. Quid quod Grotius ipse contra Socin. p. 16. ita scripserat: Scriptura vocat hostiam piacularem pro peccato pec- catum Lev. 4, 3. c. 5, 6. Ps. 40, 7. Hanc ergo loquendi for- mulam sequens Esaias 53. de his dixit תשים אשם נפשו posuit peccatum animam suam, h. e. animam suam fecit peccatorum pœnæ obnoxiam. Nec aliter Paulus: Eum qui peccatum non noverat, Deus peccatum fecit, ut nos simus Dei justitia in ipso, 2. Cor. 5, 21. Quo loco, ut & Rom. 8, 3. Gal. 3, 13. al- lusit Apostolus ad hoc vaticinium. Conf. Rivetus in h. l. Grotius, in locis, quæ nunc adducit, ut pro- bet אשם pœnam solum infonti irrogatam notare, non habetur vox illa, sed חטאת quod in altero Zach. 14, 19, de pœna non injuste, sed juste à Deo gen- tibus irrogata nec de sola pœna usurpatur, sed cul- pam simul infert: Hoc erit peccatum Ægypti, & hoc peccatum omnium gentium, quæ non ascenderint ad ce- lebrandum festivitatem tabernaculorum. In altero Gen. 31, 29. de injusta quidem exactione adhibetur, sed ibi de Labane injusto agitur. At cum Deus aliquem percutit, ut animam ponere אשם sacrifi- cium pro peccato necessum habeat, quomodo inju- sta pœna illa censebitur, nisi Deus ipse injustitiæ arguatur! Et quid hoc ad phrasin animam pro de- licto ponere, qua non pœnam saltem quamcunque, sed mortem inferri notissimum est! Nam animam ponere est ponere vitam, quum animæ voce vitam notare soleat Scriptura. Perversio ergo mera est, cum secus explicatur de aliis panis, non de morte. Adde, quod hic de voluntaria morte sermo fit: Ver- ba enim in fonte reddenda, EXPOSUIT SE SA- CRIFICIUM PRO DELICTO ANIMA EJUS, quia תָּשִׂים est 3. singul. FOEMININI generis, a- deoque referri debet in constructione ad נֶפֶשׁ. Non ergo de poena injuste irrogata, sed voluntarie suspe- pta, cum a Deo justo judice infligeretur, sermo est. Atque ita explicat cum Franc. Junio B. Tarnovius. Sed aliam παράφρασιν suggerit Ludovicus de Dieu ad h. l. Non puto תָּשִׂים hic esse Tert. perf. foemin. gen. construendum cum נַפְשׁוֹ, ut Junius & alii volue- runt, subaudiendo seipsum, multo minus poni pro יָשִׂים ut Vulgato visum fuit. Sed esse Secund. perf. Masc. gen. & ad Deum referri, atque ita verto: Cum posue- ris delictum animam ejus, & ad hanc phrasin allusisse puto Apostolum, 2. Cor. 5, 21. cum dixit Τὸν γὰρ μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίη- σεν. Quod Hebraice recte dicas : כִּי אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדַע אָשָׁם שָׁם אָשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹ תַּחְתֵּנוּ. Nam qui pec- tum non novit, posuit (nempe Deus) peccatum ani- mam ejus pro nobis. Porro phrasis illa, VIDEBIT SEMEN LON- GAEVUM, Jeremias videbit semen, diuque vivet, quam jejuna atque incerta est! Nam semen & longe- vavita intelligitur ejus, qui animam vel vitam pro delicto posuerit. Num vero Jeremias, postquam vitam suam posuit, longaevam vitam habuit? Et quodnam semen illud est, quod vidit? Significatur enim hic semen illius proprium, qui animam ponit sacrificium pro delicto. Ideo de nullo alio, quam de Messia id intelligi potest, qui semen spirituale vide- re debuit, & vitam longaevam habere, postquam a- nimam suam posuerit. Fideles enim & pii vocan- tur semen & filii Christi, Ps. 22, 31. & cap. 11, 3. Et ut semen oritur ex grano in terram projecto, ita & pii ex Christo passo, mortuo, sepulto & resuscitato. Quo Christus ipse respexit Joh. 12, 24. Videbatur ab- scissus de terra viventium, tanquam abscissa quæ- dam stirps, sed plantas innumeras proferet. Alio- rum hominum mors spem omnem præripit eis se- men videndi, at mors Christi foecunda fuit, & non solum non fuit impedimentum ad Ecclesiae propa- gationem, sed causa fuit gignendæ sobolis, quia mortuus vivificat populum suum, acquirit magis ac magis propagandum. Alludere autem, Riveto Judice, videtur, ad Isaac, quem Pater immolandum aræ imposuit, ex quo si non mortuo, morti tamen destinato, & velut post mortem Patri reddito, sic propagatum est semen, ut stellas cœli & arenam maris æquaverit. Ideoque recte observant inter- pretes: videre semen ἐμφατικῶς dici, & connotare resurrectionem Messiæ, & vitam post mortem, eamque benedictionem, quam largitur Dominus iis, quo- rum posteritas, ipsis viventibus, propagatur per varias generationes. Sunt enim, qui semen qui- dem post se relinquant, quod tamen oculis suis non vident, aut si videant, id in parte tantum acci- dit, & ad tempus exiguum. At vero hic post mor- tem vivens, ut nunquam moriatur, videbit semen in perpetuum. Illud יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים prolongabit dies, ad semen re- fert, VIDEBIT SEMEN LONGÆVUM. Sed ad Messiam pertinet in textu Ebræo, i. e. perpetuo vivet. Non erit, ut qui discedentes è vita liberos re- linquunt sibi superstites, in quibus vivunt in se mor- tui, sed una cum semine suo vivet, & in æternum manebit. Consentit Targum, si phrasin respicias. explicans τὸ videre semen, per multiplicationem filio- rum & filiarum. Cui explicationi robur addit εἰρμὸς τῆς ἀκολουθειας, hujus & sequentis capitis, utpote in quo explicatis perpessionibus & gloria con- sequente Christi, convertit sese Propheta ad Ec- clesiam Christianam, ut quæ filios Dei in Christo esset genitura, agitque de fœcunditate Ecclesiæ N. T. (cujus sponsus & maritus est Christus) & de multiplicatione ac propagatione seminis Christi per totum terrarum orbem. In eandem ergo sen- tentiam de Messia intelligenda sunt, quæ hic subji- ciuntur, VOLUNTAS DOMINI IN MANU EJUS PROSPERABITUR, quæ perperam ad Jeremiam iterum detorquentur. Voluntas illa & εὐδοκία Domini, qua placuit Christum pro nobis atterere, adeoque opus redemptionis per manum e- jus, i. e. per unam illius operam יצלח prosperrime suc- cedet, & omnibus impedimentorum claustris & obstaculis perruptis perficietur: de qua voluntate Christus Psal. 40, 8. Ioh. 4, 34. & Lutherus in glos- sa marginali, deß HErrn Fürnehmen, das ist, sein Wille und Wercke, das er im Sinn hat, nemlich die Erlösung der Menschen. Quæ successus prospe- ritas non tam in passione & resurrectione Christi, quam in Ecclesia, & seminis spiritualis propagatione deprehenditur Iob. 6, 43. c. 13, 24. Ebr. 2, 20. Qua- propter beneplacitum illud Domini erat, ut Chri- stus justitiam amissam repararet vita & morte sua, ex hac resurgeret, & Ecclesiam per totum terrarum orbem colligeret, quod per Christum perfici pro- inde debuit, ac succedere felicissime. PRO EO, QUOD LABORAVIT ANIMA EJUS, VI- DEBIT ET SATURABITUR. Vox עמל quod recte observavit Dn. D. Wellerus noster, notat la- borem seu dolorem molestum animi & corporis, & proprie anxium illum laborem, qui homini ob transgressionem in horto Eden est impositus, & co- gnationem habet cum מעל prævaricatus est Psal. 90, 10. Anima pro homine accipitur, adeoque ipse tam anima, quam corpore laborasse dicitur, præci- pue tamen animæ laborem indicari, non obscure ex eo colligitur, quod ab anima subjectum laborans denominatum sit. Vox VIDEBIT non simpli- cem visionem, sed Ebraismo usitato perceptionem cum sensu voluptatis notat. Confer Es. 60, 5. cap. 66, 14. R. Kimchi subintelligit בטוב, quæ phrasis integra habetur Jer. 29, 32. Unde explicatur à B. Lu- thero: wird er seine Lust sehen. VIDEBIT, SATU- RABITUR.
