For since fruitfulness is the ornament and glory of a woman, it follows that barrenness is her ignominy and reproach, which is proven by the examples of Sarah, of Anna the mother of Samuel, and of Elisabeth the mother of John, who, when they were made fruitful from being barren, felt themselves liberated from extreme reproaches. You, therefore, O Church, seem to be a barren woman and exposed to ignominy, who brings forth no children, who is very few in number and closest to destruction. But be of good courage. I will cause you to forget all your barrenness and desertion. You are a virgin, or a widow. A husband will therefore be given to you so that you may become fruitful. For what the Vulgate reading has, he will rule over you, in the Hebrew is baalaich, which signifies, your husband. Wherefore, so that you, O Church, may become fruitful, so that you may bring forth many children, your husband will not be just any simple man, not a Prophet, not a Patriarch, but your MAKER, or CREATOR, whose name is the Lord Zebaoth and your Redeemer. The Holy One of Israel, who is called the God of the whole earth: With such a husband, how could you remain any longer barren and unfruitful?

Latin:

Vers. 4.

CONFUSIONIS ADOLESCENTIÆ TUÆ OB- LIVISCERIS] Adolescentiæ tempus, quod cum hæc e- venient diu exactum erit. Sic & mox 6.

At hic iterum confunditur ineptus Grotii Commentarius. In Adolescentia enim sua non confundebatur Hierosolyma, vel Judæa terrena, sed optimo gaudebat flore. Ideo ratio quinta hic figi potest, ad confutanda ejus commenta Judaica. Illa hic intelligenda est vidua, quæ confusionem in adolescentia sua passa est. At hanc passa non est terrena Hierusalem in adolescentia. Dubium au- tem hic movet ex mente Judæorum & Judaizan- tium Hieronymus, quomodo intelligi per sterilem possit Ecclesia gentium, quum illa vidua non fue- rit, ad quod non est quod responsiones ipsius ad- ducamus: siquidem dubio nullus sit locus, si per sterilem, quæ hic compellatur Ecclesia, γενικῶς intelligatur, non restricte Ecclesia gentium, uti e Brentio observavimus. Quo pacto expedita & pla- na sunt omnia. Qui hanc etiam promissionem feli- citer interpretatus est: NON CONFUNDERIS, NON PUDEFIES, non afficieris ignominia, NON ERUBESCES, SED CONFUSIONIS VIRGI- NITATIS TUÆ (Pro Adolescentiæ enim in He- bræo est alumaich, quod proprie significat, Virgi- nitatis tuæ) oblivisceris & opprobrii, viduitatis tuæ ul- tra non recordaberis. Perseverat incepta meta- phora mulieris, cujus tres sunt species. Una est virgo, alia vidua, tertia uxor, quæ habet maritum. Et hæc quidem in eo est vitæ genere, in quo conci- piat & pariat liberos. Virgo autem est sterilis, & vidua deserta, quod illa nec habuerit, nec habeat maritum: hæc etsi maritum habuit, tamen amisit eum. Dicit ergo: Tu Ecclesia visa es hactenus vir- go, & vidua, h. e. plane sterilis & deserta, ideoque, con- fusioni & opprobrio obnoxia. Cumenim fœcundi- tas sit mulieris ornamentum, & gloria, consequitur sterilitatem esse ignominiam & opprobrium ejus, id quod probant exempla Saræ, Annæ matris Samuelis, & Elisabethæ matris Joannis, quæ cum ex sterilibus fierent fœcundæ, sentiebant se extremis opprobriis li- beratas. Tu igitur Ecclesia videris esse mulier steri- lis & ignominiæ exposita, quæ nullos pariat liberos quæ numero sit paucissima & internecioni proxima. Sed bono sis animo. Efficiam ut omnis sterilitatis & de- sertionis tuæ obliviscaris. Virgo es, aut vidua. Da- bitur ergo tibi maritus ut fias fœcunda. Nam quod Vulgata lectio habet, dominabitur tui, In Hebræo est baalaich, quod significat, maritus tuus. Quare ut tu Ecclesia fias fœcunda, ut multos liberos parias, mari- tus tuus erit non simplex quispiam homo, non Prophe- ta, non Patriarcha, sed FACTOR, seu CREATOR tuus, cujus nomen est Dominus Zebaoth & Redemtor tuus. Sanctus Israelis, qui vocatur Deus universæ terræ: Quo marito, quomodo posses amplius mane- re sterilis, & infœcunda?

## 54:5
Vers. 5. FOR HE WHO MADE YOU WILL RULE OVER YOU] He who made you will be your husband: that is, he will make you fruitful.

Not only for the sake of fruitfulness, although we acknowledge that this is regarded primarily, but also on account of other duties of a husband, is God distinguished by this name: for indeed God is called our Spouse and husband in the Scriptures, not because He presides over cities and polities, and is their governor, and propagates them or renders them fruitful and ample; but on account of the spiritual marriage with the faithful: for of that former signification no testimonies exist, but of this latter mystical union they are obvious everywhere, Cant. 1, 1. c. 3, 11. Isa. 62, 5. Hos. 2, v. 19. Matt. 9, 15. 1 Cor. 11, 2. Eph. 5, 26. Rev. 19, 6. it is manifest again that spiritual children are understood, and not indeed citizens of the Jewish polity. For such as the marriage is that is pointed out for the sake of fruitfulness, such is the fruitfulness, such is the generation, such are the children promised. But that marriage is spiritual. And this is the sixth special argument against Grotius. It is to be observed, however, here ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ (as by the way) the mystery of the plurality of the divine persons, insinuated by a double word in this one verse: first by the word עשי WHO MADE THEE. For several persons are [implied] by that plu- is designated by such a name. If I ought to acknowledge and believe in more [than one] עשי who made me, then I am certainly bound to acknowledge and believe in more divine persons. For as to create is a personal action, and the creator is a person, so there must be more persons who create. But the former is true, as is evident both from this passage, 'thy husbands, thy makers, Jehovah Zebaoth is his name' (if it is to be rendered word for word), and from similar passages: Job 35:10, where 'GOD who made me?' [is found]; Psalm 149:2, 'let Israel rejoice in his makers' [or] 'in those who made him. The children of Zion in their King'; Isaiah 44:2, 'Thus said the Lord, thy makers who made thee.' Add also the passage Ecclesiastes 12:1. Nor indeed is an enallage to be conceded in these; rather, those passages confirm the plural signification. For as in Job 35:10, the Factor is named in the singular, so that it must be understood under distribution, that everyone who is אלה is hinted to be our factor, those passages of Scripture collected here teach, in which explicit mention is made of several אלהים who created us, Genesis 1:1, 26. And as it is said there of the אלה our Creator, that he instructs us, that it is his [role] to hear us, that he himself is omnipotent: so it is manifest from other passages of Scripture collected here that these things are assigned not only to the Father, one person of the Deity, but also to other persons and especially to the Son of God, that he instructs us, as the wisdom of God, Proverbs 8:12, Luke 11:49; that he hears our prayers, as he is also proposed everywhere to be invoked for that reason; that he is omnipotent, Revelation 1:8. The Holy Spirit is said to instruct us, Nehemiah 9:20, and to teach [us], 1 Corinthians 2:13, and indeed concerning all things, 1 John 2:27. The same is to be invoked, Matthew 28:19, Revelation 1:4. Finally, divine power is ascribed to him, Isaiah 11:1, 2 Timothy 1:7, etc. As for the second passage, Psalm 149:2, he is understood by the name עשי, whose name we ought to celebrate, in whom we ought to rejoice confidently, and whom we ought to acknowledge as our King. But it is certain from the Scriptures that these things belong not only to that one person, GOD the Father, but besides the Father, or rather with the Father, to the Son of God; indeed, it is clearly evident from the very Psalms of David (not to speak now of the Holy Spirit) since it is taught that he is also to be worshipped by all the Angels, Psalm 97:7, that one must trust in him, Psalm 2:12, and that he is to be acknowledged as King, v. 6, and elsewhere throughout. Thus in the third passage, Isaiah 44:2, he is understood by the name עשי, who is said to be about to pour out his Spirit, who is the King of Israel or the Church and the Redeemer, that Lord to whom all knees ought to bow, as is manifest from verse 3, 6, and chapter 44:23. But this is claimed not for the Father alone, but also for the Son, and thus for several persons, namely that he poured out his Spirit. Compare Joel 2:21, 22, Romans 10:13, that he is the King of the Church, Psalm 2:6, Jeremiah 23:5, the Redeemer, Job 19:25, Isaiah 59:20, that Lord to whom the knees of all ought to bow, Romans 14:11, Philippians 2:14. Concerning the fourth passage, we have spoken in the Annotations to the same, Ecclesiastes 12:1. To which, furthermore, strength is added from other passages of Scripture, by which we are taught whom we ought to acknowledge as our God the creator. For if several persons who created us are designated in the Scriptures and expressed by their names, then certainly by that plural name עשי (without enallage) several persons will also be comprehended who made us. But several persons are also designated in the history of creation, consulting among themselves about creating us, Genesis 1:26. 'Let us make man in our image and likeness,' from which this עשי is deduced, used in the plural number concerning God, see chapter 3:22, and they are expressed by their names, Genesis 1:1, 2, 3, Psalm 33:6, Psalm 102:26, Job 26:13, Job 1:3, 10, Colossians 1:16, Hebrews 1:2, 10, etc.

The other name is בעלים, which likewise provides testimony of the plurality of divine persons. For where there are several בעלים, there are several persons. But in the Deity there are several בעלים; therefore, in the Deity there are several persons. The major premise is proven because בעל and בעל is the name of a person denoting a husband, a Lord, a possessor: whence if several בעלים are spoken of properly and without enallage, they are several persons, whether denominated from dominion and possession, or from marital relation. The minor premise is evident from this passage, where it is said of the one true God, 'Thy husbands, thy makers' (if it is to be rendered word for word), 'Jehovah Zebaoth is his name, and thy redeemer the holy one of Israel, the God of all the earth shall he be called.' Which is further confirmed from the thing signified. For this name belongs without doubt to him to whom the thing signified by this name belongs. But the thing signified, to be the Husband or Lord of Israel or the Church, does not belong to the one person of the Father alone, but belongs also, besides the Father, to the Son, and thus to several persons: since not only the Father, but also the Son is the Lord of his Church, as the whole Scripture testifies, and the Socinians themselves admit; not only the Father, but also the Son is the spouse and husband of the Church. Compare Hosea 2:19, Isaiah 62:5, Canticles 1:1, chapter 3:11, Matthew 9:15, chapter 25:1, John 3:29, 2 Corinthians 11:2, 'I have betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ'; just as conversely the Church is called the wife of the Lamb, Revelation 19:6, see also Ephesians 5:26, 30, 32. Nor is there any reason for anyone to object from Socinus, Fragment of Scripture, p. 45 and 53, and Volkelius, book 5, On True Religion, c. 9, p. 406, that this name is of the number of those which, because they signify authority and dominion, the Hebrews are accustomed to express in the plural number, however much they are attributed to only one person, as may be seen in Exodus 21:29, c. 18:12, 15, c. 12:10, 11, Isaiah 1:3. For not to mention that in most places (Exodus 18:12, 15, this name does not even occur) it can be explained in the plural, v. 9, Isaiah 1:3, 'The ox knew his master's crib,' or 'of each of his masters': the reason for the name בעל which is used here is not entirely the same as the name בעל. This indeed is a name of dominion, but that one properly designates a husband: and although the latter may occur in the plural with a singular signification, it does not appear where the former is read in the plural with a singular signification. Where it also deserves observation that the name בעל does not occur used of God, whether in the singular or in the plural number; perhaps because God did not wish to be called by that name, which was attributed to an idol, in order to detest the most grave idolatry, which is gathered from Hos. 2:16, 17. In that day you will call me My Husband, and you will no longer call me בעלי, and I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth: Whence it is manifest that God indeed wished to be called by the name איש man or בעל husband, but not by the name בעל, which, even though it signifies Lord, had nevertheless become proper to an idol. Furthermore, when the plural name בעלים Lords is used singularly, it happens through an enallage, which also becomes manifest from the text itself. But that an enallage must be admitted in this place cannot be proven; nay rather, we have already proven with arguments that the plural signification must be retained. And therefore it is not permitted to conclude from other places to the present place: the kind of inference which is otherwise ἀσυλλόγισον (non-syllogistic), since it proceeds from a particular, is in the open: since the consequence does not hold: Elsewhere sometimes a plural noun is taken singularly. Therefore also here. Finally, as to how it happens that nouns signifying lordship are sometimes used in the plural regarding one individual, we have given the reason elsewhere, which does not destroy, but rather confirms our inference.

Verse of the same. AND YOUR REDEEMER THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL, THE GOD OF ALL THE EARTH SHALL HE BE CALLED.

Construe thus: The Holy One of Israel, the Lord of all the earth shall be called thy Redeemer.

He inverts this clause, keeping the position. For if you construe it as it sounds, 'Thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel, the God of all the earth shall be called,' this sense emerges, that He is to be called the God not only of Judea, but of the whole earth. And since the formula of the covenant of grace is thus: 'I will be thy God,' it is manifest that when He promises that He will be the God of the whole earth, the universal calling of the Gentiles, through the whole earth, is inferred. Which provides a new and therefore a sixth argument, that the discourse is not about the earthly Jerusalem, but about the Church extending itself through the whole world. These things openly look to the times of the New Testament, because in these Christ our Redeemer and the Holy One of Israel is celebrated as God through the whole earth, and is the GOD of the Gentiles, and of all peoples, because the covenant of grace, by which God promised He would be God, is propagated through the whole world.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUIA DOMINABITUR TUI QUI TE FECIT] Qui te fecit, erit tibi maritus: id est, fœcun- dam te faciet.

Non tantum fœcunditatis causa, etsi eam præ- primis respici agnoscamus, sed ob alias etiam ma- riti partes, hoc nomine Deus insignitur: quia vero Deus Sponsus & maritus noster dicitur in Scriptu- ris, non quod civitatibus & Politiis præsit, & guber- nator sit, easque propaget vel fœcundas & amplas red- dat; Sed ob spirituale connubium cum fidelibus: de illa enim priori significatione nulla extant testimo- nia, hujus autem posterioris mysticæ copulationis passim obvia sunt, Cant. 1, 1. c. 3, 11. Esa. 62, 5. Ose. 2. v. 19. Matth. 9, 15. 1. Cor. 11, 2. Eph. 5, 26. Apoc. 19, 6. manifestum iterum est, spirituales filios intelligi, non vero cives politiæ Judaicæ. Quale enim connubium indigitatur fœcunditatis causa, talis fœcunditas, ta- lis generatio, tales filii promittuntur. At conju- gium illud spirituale est. Atque hoc sextum est spe- ciale argumentum contra Grotium. Observandum autem hic ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ mysterium pluralitatis per- sonarum divinarum, gemina voce hoc uno versus commate insinuatum: primo voce עשי QUI TE FECERUNT. Plures enim personæ isto plu- tali nomine designatur. Si plures agnoscere & cre- dere debeo עשי qui fecerunt me, utiq; plures agno- scere, atq; credere teneor personas divinas. Quia ut creare est actio personalis, & creator persona, ita plures qui creant, plures personas esse oportet. At pri9 est verū, ut tū ex hoc loco constat בעליך עשיך mariti tui, factores tui Jehovah Zebaoth nomen ejus, si κτ᾿ πόδα reddendum sit, tum ex similibus locis Iob. 35, 10. ubi אל העשי DEUS qui fecerunt me? Psal. 149, 2. lætetur Israël בעשיו in his qui fecerunt ipsum. Filii Sion in Rege suo. Esa. 44, 2. Sic dixit Dominus עשיך qui fecerunt te. Adde & locum Eccl. 12. v. 1. Neque vero in hisce enallage concedenda est, imo confirmant loca illa pluralem significationem. Namq; ut Job. 35, 10. עלה nominatur Factor noster in singulari, ita sub distributione hoc intelligendum esse, ut unusquisque qui est אלה, factor noster esse in- nuatur, ea Scripturæ loca hic collata docent, in qui- bus plurium אלהים, qui nos crearunt, diserta fit mentio, Gen. 1, 1. 26. & ut illic de אלה Creatore no- stro dicitur, quod erudiat nos, quod ejus sit exaudire nos, quod ipse sit omnipotens: ita ex aliis Scripturæ locis hic collatis manifestum est, non soli Patri, uni personæ Deitatis, sed & aliis personis & maxime Filio Dei ista assignari, quod nos erudiat, ceu sapi- entia Dei Prov. 8, 12. Luc. 11, 49. quod exaudiat pre- ces nostras, uti passim etiam ideo invocandus proponitur, quod omnipotens sit Apoc. 1, 8. Spiritus Sanct. dicitur nos erudire Nehem. 9, 20. & docere 1. Cor. 2, 13. & quidem de omnibus, 1. Joh. 2, 27. Idem invocandus est Matth. 28, 19. Apoc. 1, 4. Ei denique adscribitur divina potentia Esa. 11, 1. 2. Tim. 1, 7. &c. Quod ad alterum locum Pf. 149, 2. is nomine עשי intelligitur, cujus nomen celebrare, in quo confi- denter lætari, quemque Regem nostrum agnoscere debemus. At non uni tantum illi personæ, DEO Patri, sed præter Patrem, vel potius cum Patre Filio Dei ea convenire, è Scripturis certum est, imo ex ipsiss Psalmis Davidis luculenter constat (ne nunc de Spiritu Sanct. dicamus) quum eundem etiam ab Angelis omnibus adorandum Psal. 97, 7. in eo confi- dendum esse Ps. 2, 12. eumq; pro Rege agnoscendum esse v. 6. & alibi passim doceatur. Sic in tertio loco Es. 44, 2. is nomine עשי intelligitur, qui effusurus dicitur Spiritum suum, qui Rex Israëlis vel Ecclesiæ & Redemptor est, Dominus ille, cui se curvare de- bent omnia genua, ut è vers. 3. 6. & c. 44, 23. manife- stum est. At hoc non uni Patri, sed etiam Filio vindicatur, adeoq; pluribus personis, quod nempe effuderit Spiritum suum. Conf. Joël. 2, 21. 22. Rom. 10. v. 13. quod sit Rex Ecclesiæ Psal. 2, 6. Jer. 23, 5. Re- demptor Job. 19, 25. Esa. 59, 20. Dominus ille, cui se omnium genua curvare debent Rom. 14, 11. Phil. 2, 14. De quarto loco diximus in Annot. ad eun- dem Eccl. 12, 1. Quibus porro robur accedit ex aliis Scripturæ locis, quibus docemur, quemnam agno- scere debeamus pro Deo creatore nostro. Si enim plures personæ, quæ crearunt nos, in Scripturis de- signantur, & nominibus suis exprimuntur, utique nomine illo plurali עשי (citra enallagen) plures personæ etiam comprehendentur, quæ nos fece- re. At plures personæ & designantur in creationis historia inter se de nobis creandis consultantis Gen. 1, 26. נעשה Faciamus hominem ad imaginem & similitudinem nostram, unde hoc עשי deductum est, in plurali numero de Deo adhibitum, vid. cap. 3, 22. & exprimuntur illæ nominibus suis Genes. 1, 1. 2. 3. Pf. 33, 6. Pf. 102, 26. Job. 26, 13. Iob. 1, 3. 10. Co- loss. 1. v. 16. Ebr. 1, 2. 10. &c.

Alterum nomen est בעלים, quod itidem testi- monium præbet pluralitatis personarum divina- rum. Ubi enim plures sunt בעלים, ibi plures sunt personæ. At in Deitate plures sunt בעלים E. in Deitate plures sunt personæ. Major proba- tur, quia בעל & בעל nomen est personæ notans maritum, Dominum, possessorem: Unde plures בעלים si proprie & citra enallagen dicantur, plu- res sunt personæ, sive à Dominio & possessione, sive à maritali relatione denominatæ. Minor ex hoc loco constat, ubi de uno vero Deo dicitur בעלים Mariti tui factores tui (si ad verbum reddendum) Iehovah Zebaoth nomen ejus, & redemptor tuus sanctus Israël Deus omnis terræ vocabitur. Quod firmatur ulterius è re significata. Ei enim competit hoc nomen abs- que dubio, cui res nomine isthoc significata con- venit. At res significata esse Maritum vel Domi- num Israëlis vel Ecclesiæ, non convenit uni tantum personæ Patris, sed convenit etiam præter Pa- trem Filio, adeoque pluribus personis: quum non solus Pater, sed & Filius sit Dominus Ecclesiæ suæ, teste universa Scriptura, & fatentibus ipsismet Socinianis, non solus Pater, sed & Filius sit sponsus & maritus Ecclesiæ. Conf. Os. 2, 19. Es. 62, 5. Cant. 1, 1. cap. 3, 11. Matth. 9, 15. cap. 25, 1. Ioh. 3, 29. 2. Cor. 11, 2. Despondi vos uni viro, ut virginem puram siste- rem Christo; quemadmodum vicissim Ecclesia nuncupatur uxor Agni Apoc. 19, 6. vid. & Eph. 5, 26. 30. 32. Nec est quod obvertat quis è Socino fragm. Script. p. 45. & 53. & Volkelio l. 5. de vera Relig. c. 9. p. 406. nomen hoc ex eorum esse nume- ro, quæ cum autoritatem ac dominatum significent, Ebræi consuevere numero multitudinis efferre, quantumvis unico tantum cuipiam attributa, uti videre Exod. 21, 29. c. 18, 12. 15. c. 12, 10. 11. Esa. 1. v. 3. Nam ne dicam, quod in plerisque locis (Exod. 18, 12, 15. ne occurrit quidem hoc nomen) pluraliter explicari possit v. 9. Esa. 1, 3. Cognovit Asinus præsepe Dominorum suorum, vel uniuscujusq; Domi- ni sui: non est eadem omnino ratio nominis בעל quod hic adhibetur, & nominis בעל. Hoc quidem est nomen Dominii, sed illud maritum designat pro- prie: Et licet posterius in plurali occurrat signifi- catione singulari, prius tamen in plurali, singula- ri significatione, ubi legatur, non apparet. Ubi ob- servationem quoque meretur, quod nomen בעל non occurrat de Deo usurpatum, sive in singulari, sive in plurali numero; Forte, quod Deus nomine isto, idolo attributo ad detestandam gravissimam idololatriam vocari noluerit, quod colligitur ex Hos. 2, 16. 17. In die illo vocabis me Maritus meus, & non vocabis me ultra בעלי & removebo nomina Baa- lim de ore ejus: Unde manifestum, quod Deus qui- dem nomine איש vir vel בעל maritus vocari vo- luerit, non autem nomine בעל, quod etsi Domi- num significet, idolo tamen erat factum pro- prium. Deinde cum nomen בעלים Domini plura- le singulariter adhibetur, fit id per enallagen, quæ etiam ex textu ipso manifesta evadit. At hoc in loco enallagen admittendam esse, probari non pot- est; quin imo argumentis probatum jam dedimus, pluralem significationem esse retinendam. Ideo- que ab aliis locis ad præsentem locum concludere non licet: cujusmodi illationem etiam alioquin esse ἀσυλλόγισον, quum à particulari procedat, in aprico est: Quandoquidem non valeat conse- quentia: Alibi quandoque plurale nomen singulari- ter accipitur. E. etiam hic. Denique qui fiat, quod nomina Dominium significantia de uno individuo quandoque pluraliter adhibeantur, rationem de- dimus alias, quæ non destruit, sed confirmat po- tius nostram illationem.

Vers. eod. ET REDEMPTOR TUUS SANCTUS ISRAEL, DEUS OMNIS TERRÆ VOCABITUR.]

Construe sic: Sanctus Israelis, Dominus omnis terræ voca- bitur Redemptor tuus.

Invertit hoc comma, θέσιν φυλάττων. Nam si construas, ut sonat, Redemptor tuus sanctus Israël, Deus omnis terræ vocabitur, sensus iste emergit, quod non solum Judææ, sed universæ terræ Deus vocandus sit. Et quum formula fœderis gratiæ ita habeat: Ero Deus tuus, manifestum est, cum Deum universæ terræ se fore promittit, vocationem gentium universalem, per terram universam, infer- ri. Quæ novum adeoque sextum argumentum præbet, quod non de terrena Hierusalem sermo sit, sed de Ecclesia porrigente sese per totum or- bem. Respiciunt hæc palam tempora Nov. Test. quia hisce Christus Redemptor noster & sanctus Israë- lis Deus per universam terram celebratur, & DEUS gentium est, & populorum omnium, quia fœ- dus gratiæ, quo Deus se promisit fore Deum, per orbem totum propagatur.

## 54:8
Vers. 8. IN EVERLASTING MERCY] Benefits that will endure for a long time.

Thus the clear text must be obscured, lest the false interpretation concerning earthly Judea shine through: and therefore everlasting mercy is transformed into benefits that will endure for a long time. But the Lord Himself explains that eternal mercy so explicitly that it cannot be taken otherwise than as concerning perpetuity without end. Whence the seventh reason against the insipid commentary of Grotius is born. For he compares this promise of grace, sanctioned by an oath, with the covenant concerning not bringing the waters of Noah or the universal flood upon the earth anymore: which is certainly a perpetual pact, and not one that will endure for a long time only, whence I conclude: Whatever covenant is so everlasting as the covenant with Noah, that must endure not for a long time only, but forever. Which is evident from Genesis 9, verses 15, 16. But this covenant of grace is so everlasting, as the Lord testifies expressly: 'In a moment of indignation I hid my face from thee for a little while, and with everlasting mercy I have had mercy on thee, said thy Redeemer the Lord: as in the days of Noah this is to me, to whom I swore that I would not bring the waters of Noah anymore upon the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with thee, and will not rebuke thee.' Where the beautiful observation of Brentius is not to be omitted: 'It is also to be noted in this place, that the celestial bow, which they call the iris, and which appears in the clouds in its own times, is not only a general sacrament, instituted as a monument of the promise of not destroying living creatures anymore by a flood of waters, but is also consecrated here by divine authority into a special sacrament, as if it were henceforth also a monument of the promise of preserving the Church in all adversities.' For the fact that God preserves living creatures, and especially the human race for so long a time safe and sound on earth, is done most of all for the sake of the Church, so that it may be gathered, increased, and preserved from among men. Wherefore if the Church is so pressed that it seems it will perish, let us lift our eyes to the celestial bow, and be reminded of the oath of God, that just as God once swore that He would no longer destroy living creatures with waters, and keeps that most constantly, so also He has sworn that, Christ His Son having been exhibited, He will no longer be angry with the Church, and will not even rebuke it. Furthermore, the words subjoined teach that this covenant of grace will endure not only as long as the earth stands, but into simple eternity: FOR THE MOUNTAINS SHALL BE MOVED AND THE HILLS SHALL TREMBLE, BUT MY MERCY SHALL NOT DEPART FROM THEE. For these speak of the destruction of the world, by which the mountains and hills will perish with commotion and trembling, as Christ says, 'Heaven and earth shall pass away' (Luke 16). Grotius perverts it thus: 'This can happen, as in a great earthquake': i.e., that they speak only of the possible commotion of the mountains and the trembling of the hills. But the text is clear: that the mountains and hills will indeed perish, but the mercy of the Lord will remain eternally. Those words, 'IT SHALL NOT DEPART FROM THEE,' infer not only a long duration of benefits, but the perpetuity of divine mercy, which is never to depart from the Church. And when it is added: 'AND THE COVENANT OF PEACE SHALL NOT BE MOVED'; the eternity of peace is confirmed. For such exegetical repetitions among the Hebrews make for the amplification and intensification of the matter. Wherefore eternal mercy and peace is promised to the Church, never to depart from it, never to be moved or taken away. Which do not fit the earthly Jerusalem. For its peace was not long-lasting: and the mercy of God so departed from it because of most grievous sins, that it was utterly cast off by God. Nor is earthly peace promised here, but spiritual. Therefore afterwards it is coupled with the divinely revealed Doctrine as the fruit of the Gospel; 'Thy children shall be taught of God, and the multitude of peace shall be to thy children.' Now God swears to His Church that He does not wish to be angry anymore, not that the Church will have no afflictions henceforth: for these are never lacking to the Church, and they are useful and salutary to it, but that God does not change His counsel, after He began to gather the Church from the Gentiles through the world, as He cast off the Israelites, but continues until the end of the age to gather the Church from the Gentiles. Then that, God being appeased through the death of His Son, there is no longer wrath, but only favor and grace for those who believe in the Son. For although the Church after the coming of Christ in the flesh and the Gospel being divulged in the world is afflicted no less grievously and horribly than it was afflicted before under the Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Antiochus, and Herod, yet because Christ has been manifested, and His Gospel concerning the remission of sin is publicly proclaimed, it has also been manifested and proclaimed that the wrath of God, previously exposed and inflamed by sin, is now appeased, and that these afflictions are no longer signs of an angry God, but of a benevolent God, who in this way renders the Church conformable to His Son, excites it to the fear of God and invocation, and prepares for it benefits as much greater as the afflictions are more grievous. For just as death itself, now that the Gospel has been revealed, is no longer death, that is, the wages of sin and an entry into hell, since sin has been expiated and hell conquered by Christ, but has been consecrated by the death of Christ so that it is an entry into heaven, to true and perpetual righteousness and salvation, so too afflictions are no longer proofs of an angry God, meditating destruction because of sin, but are proofs of a merciful God, desiring to do us good through afflictions, because of the remission of sin which we have in his Son through faith. Wherefore, since God has sworn that his Son is a perpetual Priest, that is, an intercessor, mediator, and appeaser of his wrath, and the Son at his coming undertook the office of Priest and published this Gospel in the world, the Prophetic assembly rightly says that God has sworn that he will no longer be angry with his Church, nor even rebuke it with words, because all his wrath has been appeased through the Son. Thus it is also said in Jeremiah: I will be merciful to their iniquity. And I will remember their sin no more. What is this other than if he had said: I will henceforth cast away all my wrath. Therefore these consolations which each of the faithful can apply to himself in particular. To the point, 'In a little moment I have forsaken thee': A remarkable consolation, says B. Luther, by which He promises that the affliction will be brief and momentary, so that it may work a great weight of glory for the future. But remember here that the Spirit is speaking. For reason cannot believe that the temptation is a moment and a point, but thinks it is eternal and infinite, because it clings only to present feeling, and feels, sees, hears, thinks, and understands nothing but present pain and present evil. Wherefore this is a spiritual practice: to leave behind all appearing specters and to accustom oneself to the non-appearing, that is, to cling by faith to the Word. For the Word alone, contrary to our sense, teaches and promises that the evil will not be eternal, but momentary and punctual, if I may say so. IN GREAT MERCIES I WILL GATHER THEE. The sense of divine wrath in temptation, the sense of affliction, is as it were the center. But my mercy is as it were the sphere. Wrath is a minute of time, against which mercy is like the whole time of eternity. But here too remember that this is not a material sphere, but a spiritual one. This is what it is to be words of faith, so that if you follow reason and the judgment of the senses, the opposite appears to be true, and mercy seems to be the center, whereas wrath and the sense of evil is the infinite sphere. Conf. sermon VI. under the title THE MARITAL HEART OF GOD in the Witeberg memorials of the Just.

Latin:

Vers. 8. IN MISERICORDIA SEMPITERNA] Benefi- ciis in longum duraturis.

Ita obfuscari oportet textum luculentum, ne transpareat ψευδεῤμηνεία de terrena Judæa: ideo- que misericordia sempiterna in beneficia in longum tempus duratura transformatur. At explicat Domi- nus ipse tam diserte æternam illam misericordiam, ut aliter quam de perennitate fine fine accipi non possit. Unde septima ratio adversus insul- sum commentarium Grotii nascitur. Nam con- fert promissionem hanc gratiæ juramento sanci- tam cum fœdere, de non inducendis amplius aquis Noæ vel diluvii universalis supra terram: quod cer- te pactum perpetuum est, non vero longum tem- pus tantum duraturum, unde colligo: Quodcun- que fœdus ita sempiternum est, uti fœdus cum Noacho, id non longum tempus tantum, sed in perpetuum durare debet. Quod è Genes. 9. vers. 15. 16. ἔυδηλον. At hoc pactum gratiæ ita sempiternum est, ut διαῤῥήδην testatur Domi- nus; In momento indignationis abscondi faciem meam parumper à te, & in misericordia sempiterna misertus sum tui, dixit Redemptor tuus Dominus: si- cut in diebus Noë istud mihi est, cui juravi, ne induce- rem aquas Noë ultra supra terram, sic juravi, ut non irascar tibi, & non objurgem te. Ubi non præter- mittenda pulcra observatio Brentii: Est & illud hoc loco animadvertendum, quod arcus cœlestis, quem iridem vocant, & suis temporibus in nubibus appa- ret, non sit tantum generale sacramentum, institutum ad monumentum promissionis de non delendis am- plius animantibus diluvio aquarum, sed etiam conse- cretur hic divina autoritate in speciale sacramentum, ut si deinceps etiam monumentum promissionis de conservanda Ecclesia in omnibus adversis. Nam quod Deus servat animantia, ac præsertim humanum genus tanto tempore in terris salvum & incolume, ma- xime omnium fit propter Ecclesiam, ut ea ex homi- nibus colligatur, augeatur & conservetur. Quare si Ecclesia ita premitur, ut videatur interitura, attol- lamus oculos nostros ad arcum cœlestem, & admonea- mur de juramento Dei, quod quemadmodum Deus quondam juravit, se non amplius deleturum animan- tia aquis, & servat illud constantissime, ita etiam ju- raverit, se exhibito Christo, Filio suo, non amplius Ec- clesiæ irasci, ac ne quidem increpare eam. Porro non tantum quo adusque terra consistit, sed in simpli- cem æternitatem hoc pactum gratiæ duraturum, subjuncta verba docent: MONTES ENIM COMMOVEBUNTUR ET COLLES CON- TREMISCENT, MISERICORDIA AUTEM MEA NON RECEDET A TE. Hæc enim de interitu mundi, quo montes & colles cum com- motione & tremore interibunt, loquuntur, ut Christus ait, Cælum & terra peribunt Luc. 16. Per- vertit id ita Grotius: Fieri hoc potest, ut in magno terremotu: q. sc. tantum de possibili montium com- motione ac collium tremore loquantur. Sed textus est clarus: Montes & colles quidem interituros, miseri- cordiam autem Domini æternum mansuram. Verba illa, NON RECEDET A TE, non longam tantum beneficiorum durationem, sed perenni- tatem misericordiæ divinæ inferunt, quæ nunquam recessura sit ab Ecclesia. Et quum addatur: ET FOEDUS PACIS NON MOVEBITUR; æ- ternitas pacis confirmatur. Repetitiones enim ejusmodi exegeticæ ad rei amplificationem & in- tensionem apud Ebræos faciunt. Quapropter misericordia & pax æterna promittitur Ecclesiæ, nunquam recessura ab ea, nunquam movenda aut auferenda. Quæ Hierosolymæ terrenæ non con- gruunt. Ejus enim pax diuturna non fuit: & mise- ricordia Dei sic ab ea ob gravissima peccata reces- sit, ut prorsus à Deo abjecta sit. Neque pax terrena hic promittitur, sed spiritualis. Ideo postea cum Doctrina divinitus patefacta copulatur ceu fructus Evangelii; Erunt filii tui docti à Deo, multitudo pa- cis erit filiis tuis. Jurat autem Deus Ecclesiæ suæ se amplius non velle irasci, non quod afflictiones nullas deinceps habitura Ecclesia sit: hæ enim nun- quam desunt Ecclesiæ, eiq; utiles sunt & salutares, sed quod Deus consilium suum non mutet, post- quam è gentibus Ecclesiam colligere per orbem cepit, quemadmodum Israëlitas abjecit, sed pergat usque ad consum nationem seculi Ecclesiam è gen. tibus colligere. Tum quod placato per mortem Filii Deo non amplius ira sit, sed tantum favor & gratia illis, qui in Filium credunt. Etsi enim Ec- clesia post adventum Christi in carne & divulgatum Evangelion in orbe, non minus graviter & horribi- liter affligitur, quam antea sub Assyriis, Babylo- niis, Persis, Antiocho & Herode afflicta est, tamen quia Christus manifestatus est, & Evangelion ejus de remissione peccati publice vulgatur, manifesta- tum etiam est & vulgatum, iram Dei peccato antea expositam & inflammatam, nunc placatam esse, & has afflictiones non esse amplius signa Dei irati, sed Dei benevolentis, qui hoc modo reddat Ecclesiam conformem filio suo, excitet eam ad timorem Dei & invocationem, ac præparet ei tanto majora be- neficia, quanto graviores sunt afflictiones. Nam quemadmodum mors ipsa nunc revelato Evange- lio, non amplius mors, hoc est, stipendium peccati, & ingressus in infernum est, quippe quod peccatum sit expiatum, & infernus expugnatus per Christum, sed est consecrata per mortem Christi, ut sit ingres- sus in cœlum, ad veram & perpetuam justitiam, & salutem, ita & afflictiones non sunt amplius argu- menta irati Dei, meditantis internecionem propter peccatum, sed sunt argumenta clementis Dei, cupi- entis nobis per afflictiones benefacere, propter peccati remissionem, quam habemus in filio ejus per fidem. Quare cum Deus juraverit Filium suum esse perpetuum Sacerdotem, hoc est, intercesso- rem, mediatorem & placatorem iræ suæ, ac filius ad- ventu suo susceperit Sacerdotis officium, & divulga- verit hoc Evangelion in orbe terrarum, recte dicit Prophetica concio, quod Deus juraverit se non am- plius irasci Ecclesiæ suæ, ac ne verbis quidem eam increpare, quia omnis ira ejus per filium placata est. Sic & in Hieremia dicitur: Propitiabor iniquita- ti eorum. Et peccati eorum non recordabor amplius. Quid hoc aliud est, quam si dixisset: Abjiciam dein- ceps omnem iram meam. Ideo consolationes has- ce quisque fidelium sibi speciatim applicare po- test. Ad punctum, in modico respui te: Insignis con- solatio, inquit B. Lutherus, qua promittit brevem & momentaneam afflictionem fore, quo magnum gloriæ pondus in futurum operetur. Sed memineris hic Spiritum loqui. Ratio enim non potest credere mo- mentum & punctum esse tentationem, sed putat æter- nam & infinitam esse, quia tantum in præsenti sensu hæret, nihil sentit, videt, audit, cogitat, intelligit, quam præsentem dolorem, & præsens malum. Quare spiritualis hæc est practica, omnia apparentia spectra relinquere, & assuefacere ad non apparentia, hoc est, fide in verbo hærere. Solum enim verbum contra sensum nostrum docet & promittit, non æternum fo- re malum, sed momentaneum & punctuale, ut sic di- cam. IN MISERATIONIBUS MAGNIS CONGREGABO TE. Sensus iræ divinæ in ten- tatione, sensus afflictionis, est quasi centrum. Mise- ratio autem mea est quasi sphæra. Ira est minutum temporis, contra quam misericordia est sicut totum tempus æternitatis. Sed hic quoque memineris, hanc non esse sphæram materialem, sed spiritualem. Hoc est esse verba fidei, ut si rationem & judicium sensuum se- quaris, contrarium appareat verum esse, & miseri- cordia videatur esse centrum, contra ira & sensus ma- li sit infinita sphæra. Conf. concio VI. sub Titu- lo COR DEI MARITALE in memor. Witeberg. Justor.

## 54:10
Vers. 10.

FOR THE MOUNTAINS SHALL BE MOVED, AND THE HILLS SHALL TREMBLE] This, he says, can happen, as in a great earthquake. See Seneca, Natural Questions VI, where in chapter XXIX you see whole regions torn from their foundations. Concerning the great part of Mount Taygetus that broke off, concerning two mountains that collided with each other with a great crash, attacking and receding, concerning estates that moved to opposite locations, concerning twelve cities destroyed in one night, see Pliny, Natural History II, chapters 81, 85, 86.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

MONTES ENIM COMMOVEBUNTUR, ET COLLES CONTREMISCENT] Fieri hoc, inquit, po- test, ut in magno terræ motu. Vide Senecam Naturalium quæstionum VI. ubi capite XXIX Vides totas regiones à suis sedibus revelli. De Taygeti montis magna parte abrupta, de duobus montibus, qui inter se concurrerunt crepitu maximo assultantes recedentesque, de prædiis in contrarias sedes transgressis, de duodecim urbibus una nocte pro- stratis, vide Plinium Historiæ naturalis II. capitibus 81. 85. 86.

## 54:11
Vers. 11.

I WILL LAY THY STONES IN ORDER] The Chaldean from the Hebrew: I will lay the stones of thy pavement in stibium. But by stibium understand blackish stones, as in 1 Chron. 29. Nothing is said here beyond the truth: For Josephus also, in his description of the Temple which he himself saw: 'The entire open space was paved and variegated with stones of every kind.' See also concerning the precious stones gathered by David for the use of the Temple, 1 Chron. 29, v. 2.

AND I WILL LAY THY FOUNDATIONS WITH SAPPHIRES] The Chaldean: With precious stones.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

EGO STERNAM PER ORDINEM LAPIDES TUOS] Chaldæus ex Hebræo: Sternam in stibio lapides pavimenti tui. Sed per stibium intellige lapides nigrican- tes ut 1. Par. 29. Nihil hic super verum dicitur: Nam & Josephus in Templi, quod ipse vidit, descriptione: τὸ δὲ ὕ- παιθρον ἅπαν πεποίκιλτο παντοδαπῶν λίθων κατεσρωμένον. Vi- de & de lapidibus pretiosis à Davide ad Templi usum con- gestis 1. Par. 29. v. 2.

ET FUNDABO TE IN SAPPHIRIS] Chaldæus: In lapidibus pretiosis.

## 54:12
Vers. 12.

AND I WILL MAKE THY BATTLEMENTS OF JASPER] Others better: I will make your windows of crystal. שׁמשׁות are windows, so called from the Sun, because as Martial says: '...the windows admit pure suns, and day without a torch.'

AND THY GATES OF CARVEN STONES] Both the Hebrew and the Chaldean and the Arabic language show that flaming stones are understood here.

AND ALL THY BORDERS OF PLEASANT STONES] The Greeks: 'thy surrounding wall with choice stones,' that is, in the peristyles there will be the purest marbles. Parian marble, says this Interpreter in the cited place 1 Chron. 29, 2. 'Monolithic columns of the whitest marble,' says Josephus, Jewish War 5, c. 14.

He dreams of a merely corporal, precious, and gem-studded Jerusalem. Therefore he translates the Hebrew in such a way as he judged it to fit a worldly city in any way possible. But that these things are to be understood spiritually is clear not only from the preceding, but that very majestic description of the foundation, the gates, and the borders of this city, which far exceeds the lot of an earthly city, convinces us: Behold I will lay thy stones in order; they render that from the Hebrew: I will place thy stones in carbuncle, that is, in the interpretation of Osiander, I will build you not with common stones, but with carbuncles. Thus the LXX translate the Hebrew פּוּך as carbuncle, because this is the color of stibium: I prepare for thee thy stone as a carbuncle. So also the Rabbis: I will make thy stones rest in carbuncle, that is, I will lay carbuncles under the stones of thy building. Kings and Princes are accustomed to pave the floors of their chambers with precious stone. If, therefore, you set out carbuncles, or as others do, render them with colored and shining marble, how will it befit Jerusalem? Are the pavements there laid out in such a way? And how are those founded on sapphires! Others prefer to refer both to the foundations, because מרביץ means 'I will cause to rest,' which is that they rest on the foundation in the earth. I WILL CAUSE THY STONES TO REST IN CARBUNCLE, I WILL FOUND THEE IN SAPPHIRES. Which fit more aptly, that the foundations of this city are carbuncles and sapphires, just as in the heavenly Jerusalem in Apoc. 21. v. 19, 20, they are precious stones, which in no way square with an earthly city. Furthermore, how did the Lord place jasper as the bulwarks in Jerusalem? For what Grotius renders, 'I will make your windows of crystal,' cannot be proven. The Hebrew שמשותיך from שמש signifies bulwarks that are orbicular, high, and shining with the rays of the sun, which are seen radiating from afar, so that they appear to be certain earthly suns, whence they are called Solaria, as here Cornel. à Lapide. And this explanation is confirmed by a comparison with Apoc. 21. v. 18, where the walls of Jerusalem are celebrated as being of jasper. There is, therefore, no reason for us to depart here from Jerome. Furthermore, when the gates are said to consist of sculpted stones, or as Grotius prefers, flaming ones, stones that are not cheap but precious are understood, as the analogy of the foundations and walls or bulwarks demands, and a comparison with the Apocalyptic passage teaches, where the gates are said to consist of pearls. Which again can in no way be adapted to an earthly one. Finally, God wishes to place ALL THY BORDERS in desirable stones or stones of desire, that is, beautiful and precious, where again there is a hypallage, so that the sense may be, 'I will place desirable stones in all your borders,' or 'I will enclose and form your boundaries with most precious and elegant stones.' Which could also be illustrated by the Johannine passage compared with the streets shining with pure gold. To which it contributes that Brentius translates, AND ALL THY CORNERS WITH PRECIOUS STONES. However, none of these things befits an earthly city. They are certainly too majestic to befit any palace throughout the world, let alone buildings in the restored city of Jerusalem. Therefore, the interpreters, with great consensus, if you except the Jews and Judaizers, understand it of the Church and its spiritual adornment and splendor, and thus the Holy Scripture itself explained it in Apoc. 21, where it exhibited the peak and highest degree of beauty which is expected in the heavens. For a comparison of both descriptions, namely the spiritual adornment of Jerusalem proposed by Isaiah and the adornment of the heavenly Jerusalem depicted by John, teaches that although even significant magnificence and majestic splendor are attributed by the Prophet to the spiritual Jerusalem, yet everything in the heavenly one is far more majestic and splendid, whether we look at the foundations, or the walls or bulwarks, or the gates, or finally the streets and borders of the city. Because the glory of the faithful and of the Church is only begun here, but it will be consummated in the other life. But the Blessed Brentius correctly expressed the proper sense concerning these spiritual ornaments generally: 'He described the spiritual Church by the metaphor of a bodily or worldly building. You are seen now as hardly a pastoral hut and a rustic cottage. But I will raise you up into a most magnificent palace. I will place your stones upon carbun cles, and I will found you with sapphires. Your foundation shall be of carbuncles and sapphires. I will make your windows of crystals, and your gates of sparkling stones, and all your corners of precious stones. It is, however, customary in Scripture that the Church is founded, built up, and adorned with precious stones and pearls, not indeed with those that are corporeal, but with those that are spiritual and heavenly, among which the foundational and corner stone is Christ the Son of God. The rest, however, are built upon as believers in the Son of God. Ps. 11. The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner. And Is. 28. Behold I will lay in the foundations of Zion a corner stone, a tried stone, a precious stone, etc. And Paul Eph. 2. Now you are no more guests and strangers, but fellow citizens of the saints and domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, the chief corner stone being Jesus Christ himself, etc. & 1. Pet. 2. You have tasted that the Lord is kind, to whom coming, who is a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen and precious before God, you also as living stones are built up, a spiritual house, etc. You have the structure of the Church. But when the Prophetic discourse says that the Church is founded and built up with precious stones, it signifies that two great benefits befall the Church; the one is its stability and firmness: the other, its ornament and beauty. For God builds His Church to be as firm as it is most ornate. He strengthens it with a most robust corner rock, which is Christ His Son, and the ministry of His Gospel. Upon this rock (he says) I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. He adorns it with the most brilliant gifts of the Holy Spirit. For after Christ had ascended into heaven, He sent the Holy Spirit to His Church, through whom to one is given, as Paul says, the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge, to another faith, to another the gifts of healing, to another the working of powers, to another prophecy, to another the discerning of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues, etc. These are the ornaments with which the Holy Spirit illuminated the Church in the beginning after Pentecost, and many of which He still confers upon the Church, so that its building may not only be preserved, but also expanded.

As for the special significance, because the foundation is carbuncle and sapphires, Christ, who is the foundation 1. Corinth. 3. v. 12, is compared to these stones, upon whom the faithful or true stones are built up 1. Petr. 2. By the carbuncle is denoted the fire of divinity, by the sapphire the throne of heavenly majesty, which was seen in the likeness of a sapphire Ezech. 1. Jerome interprets these a little differently, but only in terms of spiritual ornament and virtue: The carbuncle which is prepared or laid out in order, seems to me to be the fiery word of doctrine: which, having put to flight the error of darkness, illuminates the hearts of the believers. This is he whom one of the Seraphim took with tongs to purge the lips of Isaiah, who is born, according to the faith of Genesis, in the land of Havilah, where there is the best gold, and the carbuncle stone and the emerald: furthermore, the sapphire which is placed in the foundations has the likeness of the sky, and of the air above us, which is such that it can say with Socrates in Aristophanes: ἀεροβατῶ καὶ περιφρονῶ τὸν ἥλιον, which we can translate into the Latin language: I walk in the air, and I look down upon the sun. Or with the Apostle Paul: But our conversation is in heaven: The Scripture of Ezekiel also records that the place where the throne of GOD is, has the likeness of a sapphire: and the glory of the Lord consists in this color. Which [is] carried [as an] image above the heavenly. But Cyril understands Christ by the Carbuncle: For I will set your carbuncle stone. It seems, however, that by these words he wishes to signify Jesus, whom the Holy Scripture says is placed in the foundations of Zion: in whom if anyone believes, he shall not be ashamed. He names him here the Carbuncle. For he who is the inspector of all, Christ, can survey all things everywhere. The carbuncle is therefore placed as a stone; and as the immovable base of the holy city. He adds: Upon it, however, the sapphire stones perhaps denote the host of the holy Apostles. For they are closer to Christ, and have stood as certain foundations after Him for the whole world. The bulwarks or walls of Jasper are the Doctors of the Church; to whom can be applied the exposition of Gregory the Great, lib. XIIX. moral. c. XIX. And since Jasper is of a vivid color, he placed its bulwarks of Jasper, because they are set against adversaries for the defense of the holy Church, who, flourishing with internal desires, do not wither with any arid dryness of time. Concerning whom Jerome: But also the bulwarks of the Lord's city, that is, the walls of the ramparts, are strengthened with Jasper: which can destroy and convince every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and subject falsehood to truth. He therefore who is most strong in disputing, and strengthened by the testimonies of the holy Scriptures, he is the bulwark of the Church. Cyril, he says, calls the bulwarks, and the gates, and the fortification, the assembly of holy mystagogues, friendly to God and most wise: who are also the bulwarks, and the gates of the holy city, and the fortifications and walls. For they fight with those who bring war, that is, with those who are in it, namely the multitude of those who have been saved through faith: and they prudently resist the inventors of impious sects, and withstand the malice of the Devil, nor do they permit any savior to fall into his sinister tyranny, continuously and rightly leading those entangled by Ethnic fraud to the knowledge of God, and surrounding and fortifying them with warnings and mystagogues: so that they may not be exposed to evil powers, and to the scurrilous trifles of false Doctors, who pour the poison of falsely named knowledge into the souls of the simpler ones. The gates of this mystical city consist of carved precious stones. Aquila rendered it with the word ραιδαντους, which denotes pierced and engraved gems, as Jerome warns, in which images or emblems are carved, through which the Interpreters understand Priests, for these are the gates of the Church, and as a gate leads and introduces them into the Church, whose life ought to be polished and carved, so that in it the life of Christ and the Apostles may be seen as if expressed. Thus Gregory the Great explained concerning Priests: He set its gates in carved stones, for they are the gates of the Church, through whose life and doctrine the multitude of believers enters into it: Who, for the reason that they also excel in great works, and show by seeing that which they bring forth in speaking, are remembered as being not pure but carved stones. For in whose life right action is discerned, in those very ones is expressed what they have done. The LXX rendered it as crystal. Concerning which Jerome says: In the most intense colds of the Alps, and in caves inaccessible to the sun, waters are said to congeal into crystal: and to be a stone to the touch, but water to the sight. By which it is shown that those who are at the doors of the Church ought to be stained by no filth, but to be of the purest faith, and to say with the Prophet: I have understood from thy commandments, and to hear that: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they themselves shall see God. Whence Cyril: he compares the holy mystagogues, resplendent with a variety of virtues and intelligible beauty, to most precious stones: and says that some are placed in the foundations of the holy city, others in the bulwarks, others to serve the use and place of the gates and of the fortification. And these things indeed concerning the prefects of the city, which this discourse describes to us. But what, pray, does it say concerning those who inhabit it? And all thy children shall be taught of God. Others wish the faithful and just also to be designated by the stones of desire, which are in all the borders of this mystical city this: I will set thee round about with precious stones, there shall be no stone in thee which is not desirable, whithersoever thou turnest thyself, thou shalt tread upon all precious things, and thou shalt enjoy the abundance of all riches, as Jerome interprets, and also Gregory the Great, whose words are as follows: Where, concluding also the whole number of the Saints with a general collection, he added: All thy borders into desirable stones, namely, as he subjoins, all thy children taught of the Lord. Nor is it a wonder if the faithful are sometimes called stones, who are built upon the precious and elect cornerstone Christ, sometimes are comprehended under the name of all the borders of this mystical world, and sometimes are designated by the citizens of the same, since it is customary in such similitudes that the same persons are not rarely shadowed forth by different figures.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET PONAM JASPIDEM PROPUGNACULA TUA] Melius alii: Specularia tua ex Chrystallo faciam שׁמשׁות sunt specularia, à Sole sic dicta, quia ut ait Mar- tialis: - - - specularia puros Admittunt soles, & sine face diem.

ET PORTAS TUAS IN LAPIDES SCULPTOS] Et Hebraica & Chaldaica & Arabica lingua ostendunt intelligi hic lapides flammantes.

ET OMNES TERMINOS TUOS IN LAPIDES DESIDERABILES] Græci τὸν περιβολόν συ λίθυς ἐκλεκτώς, id est, In peristyliis erunt purissima marmora. Marmor Parium, ait hic Interpres dicto loco 1. Par. 29, 2. κίονες μο- νόλιθοι λευκοτάτης μαρμάρυ ait Josephus Belli Judaici 5. c. 14.

Somniat mere corporalem structuram & pretio- sam gemmatamque Hierosolymam. Ideo vertit ita Ebræa, uti quomodocunque urbi terrenæ conveni- re judicavit. Sed hæc spiritualiter intelligenda esse, cum ex antecedentibus jam clarum sit, tum vero i- psa illa augusta descriptio & fundamenti & porta- rum, & terminorum hujus urbis, quæ longe excedit sortem terrenæ civitatis, convincit: Ecce ego sternam per ordinem lapides tuos; id ex Ebræo reddunt; Po- nam in carbunculo lapides tuos, id est, interprete Osiandro, extruam te non vulgaribus lapidibus, sed ex carbunculis. Ita LXX. transferunt Ebr. פּוּך Carbunculum, quia hic coloris est stibii: Ego præparo tibi carbunculum lapidem tuum. Sic et- iam Rabbini: Quiescere faciam in carbunculo lapi- des tuos, id est, substernam lapides ædificii tui car- bunculos. Solent Reges & Principes pavimenta cubiculorum pretioso lapide insternere. Si er- go carbunculos exponas, aut ut alii, marmore colora- to & fulgido reddas, quomodo Hierosolymis conveniet? Num pavimenta ibi ita posita? Et quomodo illa fundata in sapphiris! Alii malunt utrumque ad fundamenta referre, quia מרביץ est quiescere faciam quod in fundamento quie- scant in terra. QUIESCERE FACIAM IN CARBUNCULO LAPIDES TUOS, FUN- DABO TE IN SAPPHIRIS. Quæ aptius conveniunt, quod fundamenta hujus urbis sint carbunculi, & Sapphiri, uti Hierosolymæ cœle- stis Apocal. 21. v. 19. 20. lapides pretiosi sunt, quæ nullo modo quadrant in urbem terrenam. Por- ro quomdo in Jerusalem Jaspidem posuit Domi- nus propugnacula? Quod enim Grotius reddit, specularia tua ex crystallo faciam, probari nequit. Ebræum שמשותיך à שמש propugnacula significat orbicularia, excelsa & radiis Solis fulgentia, quæ eminus radiantia conspiciuntur, ut videantur esse soles quidam terrestres, unde Solaria vocantur, ut hic Cornel. à Lapide. Et hæc explicatio confirma- tur è collatione Apoc. 21. v. 18. ubi muri celebran- tur Hierosolymæ ex Jaspide. Non ergo est quod hic ab Hieronymo discedamus. Ulterius cum portæ à lapidibus sculptis, aut ut mavult Grotius, flammantibus, constare dicuntur, lapides non viles, sed pretiosi intelliguntur, ut analogia fundamen- torum & murorum, vel propugnaculorum po- stulat, & collatio cum loco Apocalyptico docet, ubi portæ dicuntur margaritis constare. Quæ ite- rum nullatenus ubi terrenæ aptari queunt. De- nique OMNES TERMINOS Deus ponere vult in lapides desiderabiles vel desiderii, hoc est, spe- ciosos & pretiosos, ubi iterum hypallage est, ut sen- sus sit, ponam lapides desiderabiles in omnibus ter- minis tuis, vel pomæria tua includam & formabo lapidibus pretiosissimis & elegantissimis. Quæ etiam possent collato loco Johanneo è plateis auro puro micantibus illustrari. Quo facit, quod Brentius vertit, ET OMNES ANGULOS TUOS LA- PIDIBUS PRETIOSIS. Nihil autem horum terrenæ urbi convenit. Augustiora sane sunt, quam ut ulli regiæ per orbem, nedum ædificiis in restaurata urbe Jerusalem conveniant universa. Ideo Interpp. magno consensu, si Judæos & Judai- zantes excipias, de Ecclesia, & spirituali ejusdem ornatu, & splendore intelligunt, atque ita S. S. ipse exposuit Apoc. 21. ubi ἀκμὴν & supremum gradum decoris, qui expectatur in cœlis, exhibuit. Nam collatio utriusque descriptionis, ornatus nempe spiritualis Hierosolymæ ab Esaia propositi, & or- natus Hierosolymæ cœlestis à Johanne depicti do- cet, quod licet à Propheta etiam insignis magnifi- centia, & augustus splendor tribuatur spirituali Hierosolymæ, longe tamen augustiora & splendi- diora sint omnia in cœlesti, sive fundamenta specte- mus, sive muros aut propugnacula, sive portas, seu de- nique plateas & terminos civitatis. Quia inchoa- tur hic tantum gloria fidelium, & Ecclesiæ, sed in altera vita consummabitur. Sensum autem pro- prium de spiritualibus istis ornamentis γενικῶς re- cte expressit B. Brentius: Descripsit metaphora cor- poralis seu mundani ædificii, spiritualem Ecclesiam. Videris nunc vix casa pastoralis, & rusticum tugurio- lum. Ego vero excitabo te in regiam magnificentis- simam. Collocabo lapides tuos super carbun- culo, & fundabo te Sapphiris. Fundamentum tuum erit è carbunculis & Sapphiris. Faciam fe- neftras tuas è crystallis, & portas tuas è lapidibus rutilantibus, & omnes angulos tuos è lapidibus pretiosis. Usitatum autem est in Scriptura, quod Ecclesia fundatur, extruitur & ornatur pretiosis la- pidibus & margaritis, non quidem corporalibus illis sed spiritualibus & cælestibus, inter quos lapides fun- damentalis & angularis est Christus Filius Dei. Re- liqui autem superstructi sunt credentes in Filium Dei. Pf. 11. Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli. Et Es. 28. Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Zion lapidem angularem, lapidem probatum, preciosum &c. Et Paulus Eph. 2. Jam non estis hospites & peregrini, sed concives sanctorum ac domestici Dei, superstructi super fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum, summo angulari lapide ipso Jesu Christo &c. & 1. Pet. 2. Gustastis quod benignus sit Dominus, ad quem accedentes qui lapis est vivus, ab hominibus quidem reprobatus, apud Deum vero electus & preciosus, ipsi quoque veluti vivi lapides ædifice- mini, domus spiritualis &c. Habes structuram Ec- clesiæ. Sed cum Prophetica concio dicit, Ecclesiam fundari & extrui pretiosis lapidibus, significat duo magna beneficia contingere Ecclesiæ; Alterum est, stabilitas & firmitas ejus: Alterum, ornamen- tum & pulchritudo ejus. Deus enim architectatur Ecclesiam suam, ut firmissimam, ita etiam ornatissi- mam. Firmat eam angulari petra robustissima, quæ est Christus Filius ejus, & ministerium Evangelii ejus. Super hanc, (inquit) petram ædificabo Ec- clesiam meam, & portæ inferi non prævalebunt adversus eam. Ornat eam clarissimis donis Spiri- tus Sancti. Postquam enim Christus ascendisset in cælum, misit Ecclesiæ suæ Spiritum Sanctum per quem huic quidem datur, ut Paulus ait, sermo sapien- tiæ, alii sermo scientiæ, alii fides, alii dona sana- tionum, alii efficacia potentiarum, alii Prophetia, alii discretiones spirituum, alii genera linguarum, alii interpretatio linguarum &c. Hæc sunt orna- menta, quibus Spiritus Sanctus initio post Pentecostem Ecclesiam illustravit, & quorum multa adhuc in Ec- clesiam confert, ut ædificium ejus non conservetur tantum, verum etiam dilatetur.

Quod ad specialem significationem, quia fun- damentum carbunculus & Sapphiri sunt, Christus, qui fundamentum est 1. Corinth. 3. v. 12. his lapidi- bus confertur, super quem fideles seu lapides veri sunt superstructi 1. Petr. 2. Carbunculo notatur ignis divinitatis, Sapphiro thronus cælestis majestatis, qui Sapphiri similitudine visus Ezech. 1. Hierony- mus paulo aliter, sed non nisi de spirituali ornatu & virtute hæc interpretatur: Carbunculus qui para- tur sive per ordinem sternitur, videtur mihi ignitus sermo doctrinæ: qui fugato errore tenebrarum, illu- minat corda credentium. Hic est quem unus de Se- raphim tulit forcipe comprehensum, ad Esaiæ labia purganda, qui nascitur, juxta Geneseos fidem, in ter- ra Hevilat, ubi est aurum optimum, lapisque carbun- culus & prasinus: porro sapphirus qui ponitur in fundamentis, cæli habet similitudinem, & supra nos æris, qui talis est, ut possit Aristophanium dicere cum Socrate: ἀεροβατῶ & περιφρονῶ τὸν ἥλιον, quod nos in Latinum sermonem vertere possumus: Scando aë- rem, solemque despicio. Sive cum Paulo Apo- stolo: Nostra autem conversatio in cælis est: Eze- chielis quoque Scriptura commemorat, quod locus in quo thronus DEI sit, sapphiri habeat similitudinem: & gloria Domini in hoc colore consistat. Qui por- tati maginem super cælestis. Sed Cyrillus per Car- bunculum Christum intelligit: Ponam enim carbun- culum lapidem tuum. Videtur autem hisce verbis Jesum velle significare, quem Scriptura sacra dicit in fundamenta Sion esse positum: in quem si quis crediderit, non pudefiet. Hunc nominat hic Car- bunculum. Potest enim omnia passim perlustrare is, qui est omnium inspector Christus. Positus est igitur carbunculus in lapidem; & immotam sanctæ civitatis basim. Addit: Super ipsum autem lapides Sap- phiri fortassis sanctorum Apostolorum agmen deno- tant. Sunt enim illi Christo viciniores, & tan- quam fundamenta quædam secundum ipsum orbis terrarum extiterunt. Propugnacula vel muri e Jaspide, Doctores Ecclesiæ sunt; quibus applicari potest ἔκθεσις Gregor. Magn. lib. XIIX. moral. c. XIX. Et quoniam Jaspis vividi est coloris, Jaspidem propugnacula ejus posuit, quia illi contra adversa- rios pro sanctæ Ecclesiæ defensione objecti sunt, qui internis desideriis virentes, nulla temporis reproba ariditate marcescunt. De quibus Hieronymus: Sed & propugnacula urbis dominicæ, hoc est, muro- rum mænia, Jaspide roborantur: qui possunt omnem altitudinem elevantem se contra scientiam Dei de- struere atque convincere, & mendacium subjicere veritati. Qui ergo in disputando fortissimus est, & sanctarum Scripturarum testimoniis roboratus, iste propugnaculum Ecclesiæ est. Cyrillus, propugna- cula, inquit, & portas, & munimentum nominat sanctorum mystagogorum Deo amicum & sapientis- simum cœtum: qui etiam propugnacula sunt, & por- tæ sanctæ civitatis & munimenta ac muri. Pugnant enim cum his qui bellum inferunt illi, id est, his qui in ea sunt, multitudini nempe eorum, qui per fidem ser- vati sunt: & prudenter resistunt impiarum secta- rum inventoribus, ac Diaboli malitiæ obsistunt, nec quenquam servatorem permittunt in ejus incidere sinistram tyrannidem, continuo ac rite ad Dei cogni- tionem inducentes Ethnica fraude irretitos, monitis- que & mystagogis eos obvallantes & obmunientes: ut non sint expositi malis potestatibus, & falsorum Doctorum scurrilibus nugis, qui falso nominatæ sci- entiæ venenum animis simpliciorum offundunt. Por- tæ hujus civitatis mysticæ lapidibus sculptis pretio- sis constant. Aquila reddidit voce ραιδαντους, quæ foratas cælatasque gemmas notat monente Hie- ronymo, in quibus imagines aut emblemata incisa sunt, per quas intelligunt Interpp. Sacerdotes, hi e- nim portæ sunt Ecclesiæ, & quasi porta hos in Ec- clesiam inducit & intromittit, quorum vita polita & sculpta esse debet, ut in ea quasi expressa videa- tur vita Christi & Apostolorum. Ita de Sacerdotibus Gregor. M. exposuit: Portas vero ejus posuit in la- pides sculptos, quippe portæ sunt Ecclesiæ, per quo- rum vitam atque doctrinam intrat in eam multitu- do credentium: Qui pro eo etiam quod magnis operi- bus polleat, & id quod loquentes afferunt, videntes o- stendunt, non puri sed sculpti lapides esse memorantur. In quorum enim vita recta operatio cernitur, in eis- dem ipsis exprimitur, quod egerunt. LXX. reddi- dere per crystallum. De quo Hieronymus: Vehe- mentissimis Alpium frigoribus, & inaccessis soli spe- luncis, concrescere aquæ dicuntur in crystallum: & tactu quidem lapidem, visu aquam esse. Per quæ ostenditur eos, qui in foribus Ecclesiæ sunt, nulla debere sorde maculari, sed fidei esse purissimæ, & dicere cum Propheta: A mandatis tuis intellexi, & illud audi- re: Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum vi- debunt. Unde Cyrillus; sanctos mystagogas vir- tutum varietate & pulchritudine intelligibili resplen- descentes, lapidibus pretiosissimis comparat: & alios dicit in fundamenta positos esse sanctæ civitati, alios in propugnacula, alios portarum & munitionis usum ac locum supplere. Atque hæc quidem de civitatis præfectis, quam nobis hæc describit ora- tio. De his vero, qui eam inhabitant, quid tan- dem ait? Et omnes filios tuos doctos à Deo. Alii fideles & justos etiam designari volunt per lapides desiderii, qui in omnibus terminis hujus urbis my- sticæ positi dicuntur. Siquidem id indicet Do- minus: undique constituam te ex lapidibus pretiosis, nullus in te erit lapis, qui non sit desiderabilis, quo- cunque te vertes, pretiosa quæque calcabis, & omnium divitiarum abundantia perfrueris, ut Hie- ronymus interpretatur, nec non Gregor. M. cujus verba ita habent: Ubi omnem quoque Sanctorum numerum generali collectione concludens subdidit: Omnes terminos tuos in lapides desiderabiles, scili- cet ut subjungit, universos filios tuos doctos à Domi- no. Nec mirum est, si fideles modo lapides di- cantur, qui superstructi sunt lapidi pretioso & ele- cto angulari Christo, modo terminorum omnium hujus orbis mysticæ nomine comprehendantur, modo vero per cives ejusdem designentur, siqui- dem id in talibus similitudinibus solemne sit, ut eædem personæ non raro diversis figuris adum- brentur.

## 54:13
Ver. 13.

ALL THY CHILDREN TAUGHT OF THE LORD] Well instructed by Daniel, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, the Prophets.

This determination is too narrow and restricted. For it has been shown before that not only the faithful of that time are regarded, but that the discourse is generally about the Church, which is given to Christ as an inheritance, and about all the faithful, who are the seed of Christ having suffered, died, and risen again; nay, if any time is specially regarded, all things more rightly agree with the times of the New Testament, concerning which this oracle is also openly declared by Christ himself, John 6:45, concerning which passage we have treated above.

Ver. same.

AND THE MULTITUDE OF PEACE TO THY CHILDREN] All most prosperous things.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

UNIVERSOS FILIOS TUOS DOCTOS A DOMINO] Bene institutos à Daniele, Aggæo, Zacha- ria, Malachia, Prophetis.

Nimis angusta & restricta est hæc determina- tio. Non enim tantum fideles istius temporis re- spici, sed de Ecclesia generatim sermonem esse, quæ Christo donatur tanquam hæreditas, de fide- libus omnibus, qui Christi passi, mortui & resusci- tati semen sunt, antea ostensum, imo si quod tem- pus specialiter respicitur, rectius omnia tempori- bus Novi Testamenti conveniunt, de quibus et- iam hoc oraculum apertè declaratur ab ipso Chri- sto Joh. 6, 45. de quo loco supra egimus.

Vers. eod.

ET MULTITUDINEM PACIS FILIIS TUIS] Omnia prosperrima.

## 54:14
Ver. 14.

AND IN RIGHTEOUSNESS SHALT THOU BE ESTABLISHED] The men will be the best, who will restore the city, such as Ezra, Zerubbabel, Joshua the son of Josedech, Nehemiah.

DEPART FAR FROM OPPRESSION] עשׁק, which he translates here as calumny, signifies violence more. Do not act with violence toward those neighboring Samaritans and others, who will wish to hinder thee in building. For I will scatter their counsels. See Ezra 4, Nehemiah 6.

AND FROM TERROR] And from all strife,

These things are not to be understood concerning temporal prosperity, but spiritual; not concerning the righteousness of those who rebuilt the earthly Jerusalem, but concerning the righteousness of the citizens of the mystical Jerusalem, the true faithful. Nor do these things sound of a withdrawal from calumny, or violence against the Samaritans hindering the building of the city: this interpretation is merely precarious and idle. Nor are they to be rendered by way of an imperative, but they exhibit a promise of future grace, as the blessed Luther observed in his commentary, and in the German version he translated: He shall be free from violence and injustice. Which our Brentius explained most excellently. For indeed the benefits which divinely accrue to the citizens of this so fortified and adorned city are recounted here: The first of which is the gift of the Holy Spirit, that all shall be taught by the Lord, so that it may be established that true children of the Church are made not by human, but only by divine doctrine, and that no man is reckoned as a true citizen of the Church, unless God himself has taught him, and has stirred him to embrace Christ by faith. See Jer. 31. 1. Corinth. 12. v. 3. The second is spiritual peace: A multitude of peace shall be for your children; To the citizens of the Church there shall be given not only the Holy Spirit as Teacher, existing as true GOD together with the Father and the Son, but also a multitude of peace shall be given to them. They shall have very tranquil peace in their city. These things are not to be understood concerning political peace. For although the pious have peace, as much as in them lies, with all men, yet Satan and impious men do not have peace with them in this age, but disturb them in whatever way they can, and afflict them with as much cruelty as they are able: Wherefore the discourse here is not about worldly and unstable peace, but about true, heavenly, and eternal peace, which Christ himself, when he was preaching in person, promised to his Church: Peace, he says, I leave with you, my peace I give to you, not as the world gives, do I give to you, etc. This is that peace which the Son of GOD established between GOD his Father and us, so that as many of us as believe in the Son may have a propitious GOD, forgiving us our sins and adopting us as his children and heirs. Concerning which peace the Apostle also says: Justified by faith, we have peace toward GOD, through our Lord JESUS CHRIST, etc. elsewhere he says it surpasses all understanding. For the eye has not seen, nor the ear heard, nor has it ascended into the heart of man, how great are the advantages of this heavenly peace, of which we taste only the firstfruits in our conscience through faith in this age, being about to receive hereafter the tithes of them in reality in the future age. The third benefit, YOU SHALL BE ESTABLISHED IN RIGHTEOUSNESS, or you shall be prepared and strengthened. Citizens of other cities are accustomed to build and strengthen their cities and houses with iniquity, with wealth acquired unjustly and through imposture. Micah accuses the Princes and judges of Israel of having built Zion also with cruelty and iniquity: You who build, he says, Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity; For it is customary for Princes to build magnificent palaces with the sweat of the poor. But for common citizens it is customary to prepare and fill their houses with wealth obtained by deceit, imposture, perjury, and iniquity of that kind. But the Church, which is the heavenly Jerusalem, is built and strengthened by righteousness. All its citizens are righteous. In this city there is no injustice. The fourth benefit is, To depart far from calumny, etc. This is to be read thus: You shall be far from violence, and you shall not fear it, and from terror, because it shall not approach you. This is, after Christ has come, and shall spread his Gospel on earth, you shall no longer be violently oppressed, nor shall horrible things happen to you. So great shall be the security of the Church that no fear or terror shall invade it any longer. Just as it is also said in Jeremiah; In those days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently. They shall not fear anymore nor shall they be terrified. This is a great benefit, but it must be rightly understood. In the Church there is no longer any dread, no violent oppression, not that the Church in this age has no persecutions, or terrors of death: the sorrows of death surrounded me, and the torrents of iniquity disturb me. The sorrows of hell surrounded me, the snares of death anticipated me. But for this reason it is said that there is no longer any dread or violent oppression in the Church, because through CHRIST all terrible and horrible things, afflictions, Death, hell, and Satan himself have been conquered, and they can no longer oppress and destroy the Church. And we indeed perceive only the firstfruits of this benefit through faith in this bodily life, afterwards but we shall enjoy his tithes in the heavenly and everlasting life. Concerning which Blessed Luther says: RECEDE PROCUL A CALUMNIA. Translate: you will be far from calumny. Not that calumny and injuries are not present, for they cling to the back of Christians, but they will be far from your conscience. For evil approaches the flesh, and not the conscience, but the spirit can even make good use of evils, and through patience overcomes evil: Nor shall terror, he says, approach you. Not that Christians are outside of fear and dangers, but that no one will harm them. For they have God as Preceptor and Father, and the Church as mother; these do not allow peace to be snatched from us.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET IN JUSTITIA FUNDABERIS] Viri erunt optimi, qui urbem restituent, qualis Esdras, Zorobabel, Jasus Josedeci filius, Nehemias.

RECEDE PROCUL A CALUMNIA] עשׁק, quod hic calumniam vertit, vim magis significat. Noli vi agere cum vicinis illis Samaritis & aliis, qui te impedi- re in ædificando volent. Namque ego illorum consilia disslabo. Vid. Esdr. 4. Nehem. 6.

ET A PAVORE] Et à certamine omni,

Hæc non de prosperitate temporali, sed spiri- tuali, non de justitia eorum, qui reædificarunt ter- renam Hierusalem, sed de justitia civium mysticæ Hierosolymæ, verorum fidelium intelligenda sunt. Neque de recessu à calumnia, aut vi adversus Sama- ritanos, ædificationem urbis impedientes hæc so- nant: mere precaria & idia hæc est διάλυσις. Nec per modum imperativum reddenda sunt, sed pro- missionem exhibent futuræ gratiæ, uti observavit B. Lutherus in comment. & in Germanica versio- ne transtulit: Er wird frey seyn von Gewalt und Unrecht. Quam egregie exposuit Brentius noster. Quod nempe hic beneficia quæ civibus hujus tam munitæ & ornatæ urbis divinitus obtingunt, recen- seantur: Quorum primum est donum Spiritus San- cti, quod omnes futuri sint docti à Domino, ut constet veros filios Ecclesiæ non fieri humana, sed tantum divina doctrina, & nullum hominem repu- tari pro vero cive Ecclesiæ, nisi quem Deus ipse docuerit, & amplectendum Christum fide exci- raverit. Vid. Jer. 31. 1. Corinth. 12. v. 3. Alterum est pax spiritualis: Multitudo pacis erit filiis tuis; Civibus Ecclesiæ non solum dabitur Doctor Spi- ritus sanctus, verus existens una cum Patre & filio DEUS, sed etiam dabitur eis multitudo pacis. Habebunt valde tranquillam in urbe sua pacem. Hæc non sunt intelligenda de politica pace. Etsi enim pii habent pacem, quantum in ipsis est, cum omnibus hominibus, tamen Satan & im- pii homines non habent in hoc seculo pacem cum ipsis, sed perturbant eos, quoquo modo possunt, affligunt ipsos, quanta queunt immanitate: Qua- re non sit hic sermo de mundana & instabili, sed de vera, cœlesti & æterna pace, quam & Christus ipse cum coram concionaretur, Ecclesiæ suæ promisit: Pacem, inquiens, relinquo vobis, pacem MEAM do vobis, non quomodo mundus dat, ego do vo- bis &c. Hæc est pax illa, quam Filius DEI inter DEUM Patrem suum, & nos instituit, ut quot- quot in Filium credimus, habeamus DEUM propitium, condonantem nobis peccata & ado- ptantem nos in filios ac hæredes suos. De qua pa- ce etiam Apostolus ait: Justificati ex fide, pacem habemus erga DEUM, per Dominum nostrum JESUM CHRISTUM &c. alias exuperat, inquit, omnem sensum. Oculus enim non vi- dit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascen- dit, quanta sint hujus cœlestis pacis commoda, quorum tantum primitias gustamus in conscientia per fidem in hoc seculo, percepturi deinceps re- ipsa in futuro seculo etiam decimas eorum. Tertium beneficium, IN JUSTITIA FUN- DABERIS, seu præparaberis, & firmaberis. Cives aliarum urbium solent civitates & domos suas ex- truere & firmare iniquitate, opibus inique & per imposturam partis.
