Accusat Micheas Principes & judices Israëlis etiam Zionem ædificasse crudeli- tate & iniquitate: Qui ædificatis, inquit, Zion in sanguinibus & Hierusalem in iniquitate; Solenne enim est Principibus extruere magnifica palatia pauperum sudore. Vulgaribus autem civibus so- lenne est suas domos parare & implere opibus do- lo, impostura, perjurio, & id genus iniquitate par- tis. Ecclesiæ autem, quæ est cœlestis Hierusa- lem, ædificatur & firmatur justitia. Omnes cives ejus sunt justi. In hac urbe non est ulla injustitia. Quartum beneficium est, Recedere procul à calu- mnia &c. Hoc ita legendum est: Longe aberis à vio- lentia, nec timebis eam, & à terrore, quia non appro- pinquabit ad te. Hoc est, postquam venit Chri- stus, & divulgabit Evangelion suum in terra, non opprimeris amplius violenter, nec accident tibi horrenda. Tanta erit securitas Ecclesiæ, ut nul- lus metus aut terror eam amplius invadat. Sicut & in Hieremia dicitur; In diebus illis Juda salvabi- tur, & Israel habitabit confidenter. Non formi- dabunt ultra nec pavebunt. Magnum hoc est be- neficium, sed recte intelligendum. In Ecclesia nullus est amplius pavor, nulla violenta oppressio, non quod Ecclesia in hoc seculo nullas habeat per- secutiones, aut terrores mortis: circumdederunt me dolores mortis, & torrentes iniquitatis conturbant me. Dolores inferni circumdederunt me, præoccu- paverunt me laquei mortis. Sed idcirco nullus di- citur amplius pavor, nulla violenta oppressio in Ecclesia esse, quod per CHRISTUM victa sint omnia terribilia & horribilia, afflictiones, Mors, infernus & Satan ipse, nec possunt am- plius Ecclesiam opprimere & perdere. Ac percipimus quidem hujus beneficii primitias tantum per fidem in hac corporali vita, postea autem fruemur decimis ejus in cœlesti & perpe- tua vita. De quo B. Lutherus : RECEDE PROCUL A CALUMNIA. Verte, longe eris à calumnia. Non quod calumnia & injuriæ non assint, hærent e- nim in dorso Christianorum, sed procul erunt à con- scientia tua. Malum enim accedit in carnem, & non in conscientiam, sed spiritus etiam malis bene potest uti, & per patientiam vincit malum: Nec pavor, inquit, appropinquabit ad te. Non quod sint Chri- stiani extra metum & pericula, sed quod nemo eis no- cebit. Habent enim Præceptorem & Patrem Deum, & matrem Ecclesiam, hi non patiuntur nobis eripi pa- cem.

## 54:15
Verse 15. BEHOLD THE SOJOURNER SHALL COME, WHO SHALL NOT BE WITH ME] You may translate it best with the Chaldean: Gathering he shall gather you, (for thus גור is taken in Psalm 56:6 and 59:4) but not from me. The sense is: Sanballat will draw many neighboring nations to himself, in order to impede the work, but against my will, and I being about to easily disturb his counsels.

YOUR FORMER STRANGER SHALL BE JOINED TO YOU] The Chaldean translates best: Whoever shall join together against you, he shall fall before you. You have על for before in Zechariah 6:5 and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ECCE ACCOLA VENIET, QUI NON ERIT MECUM] Optime vertas cum Chaldæo: Congre- gando congregabit te, (nam sic גור sumitur Psal. 56, 6. & 59, 4.) sed non ex me. Sensus est: Samballetes multas vici- nas gentes ad se attrahet, ut opus impediat, sed me no- lente, ac facile ejus consilia disturbaturo.

ADVENA QUONDAM TUUS ADJUNGETUR TIBI] Optime vertit Chaldæus: Quisquis coibit contra te, is coram te cadet. על pro coram habes Zach. 6. v. 5. & alibi.

## 54:16
Verse 16. BEHOLD I HAVE CREATED THE SMITH BLOWING UPON THE COALS IN THE FIRE, AND BRINGING FORTH A VESSEL FOR HIS WORK, AND I HAVE CREATED THE SLAYER TO DESTROY] That is, just as I use the works of smiths for smithing works, so also for destroying those whom I wish, instruments are not lacking to me.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ECCE EGO CREAVI FABRUM SUF- FLANTEM IN IGNE PRUNAS, ET PROFEREN- TEM VAS IN OPUS SUUM, ET EGO CREAVI INTERFECTOREM AD DISPERDENDUM] Id est, sicut Fabri opera utor ad opera fabrilia, sic etiam ad per- dendos quos volo, non desunt mihi instrumenta.

## 54:17
Verse 17. EVERY VESSEL THAT IS FORMED AGAINST YOU] Translate: All weapons which are prepared against you. For thus כלי is very often taken, and is translated ὅπλον in Jeremiah 21:4, Ezekiel 32:26. Nor does the Chaldean here translate it otherwise.

AND EVERY TONGUE RESISTING YOU IN JUDGMENT I WILL JUDGE] In the Hebrew: Every tongue, which shall wish to contend with you in judgment, you shall refute. You will easily overcome all calumnies which shall be brought against you to the kings of the Persians.

That this Jewish gloss is false, those things which we have hitherto brought forward teach abundantly. For even if we admit that by virtue of this promise the efforts of those who were about to dare to obstruct the rebuilding of the city ought also to have been rendered void, yet it is general, promising divine assistance and defense to the Church against any enemies whatsoever: nor is this discourse about a material city or temple, but about the mystical unity of God, for whose sake God protects cities, provinces, and kingdoms, and willed Jerusalem and the temple to be rebuilt. Brentius therefore rightly places here the fifth benefit promised by God to the Church, namely its liberation from enemies, and teaches that these things are to be read thus from the Hebrew: Behold, in coming he shall come without me, whoever comes to you, to rush upon you or invade you. Behold I cause that the smith, who blows the coal for the fire, makes an instrument for his work, and I cause that there be a destroyer to destroy. Every instrument, which is formed against you, shall not prosper, and every tongue, which rises against you in judgment, you shall condemn or convince of impiety. But what is said: I cause that the smith blowing upon the coals for the fire, makes an instrument for his work, can be explained in two ways. Either that God causes that he who forges weapons, or undertakes war against the Church, does this to his own destruction, that he may kill himself with his own sword, as is the saying, and dig a pit into which he may fall. Or that God, even if He sometimes stirs up smiths, that is, enemies, who prepare weapons against the Church, nevertheless causes that they themselves eventually perish, but the Church is saved. Both opinions look to the same thing, that God so protects His Church that even if it has many adversaries who attack it, some indeed with weapons, that is, with external and corporal tyranny, others however with the tongue, that is, with insults, lies, heresies, and impious doctrine, it is nevertheless preserved wonderfully in the midst of enemies, and its enemies fall horribly together with their weapons and tongue. Thus also Blessed Luther: on the words, Behold the sojourner shall come who etc. The grammar here, he says, is obscure, yet the sentence can be rendered thus: Behold what sojourner shall come against you, to overwhelm you, when he shall come without me! He consoles the Church against the violence of tyrants. But what he adds, without me, removes that intolerable boasting of the adversaries, that they boast that they are rendering service to God when they persecute the pious, that they are fighting for the Church and for the faith against heretics. For thus they are accustomed, they adorn the violence which they bring upon the pious with the title of the divine name and of the Church. But Christ confirms us here, and says that they do it, but without me.

Verse of the same. THIS IS THE HERITAGE OF THE SERVANTS OF THE LORD] This is their privilege. AND THEIR JUSTICE IS WITH ME, SAYS THE LORD] That is, of those whose probity is perceived by me.

The conclusion corresponds to the sermon. Since therefore the Prophet has hitherto reviewed the catalog of the Lord's benefits, he now asserts that those benefits are to be handed over to the Church and the servants of the Lord as an inheritance. And it is added: THIS IS JUSTICE, that is, their just reward from me, which I, clearly, shall repay to them. He calls these benefits a just reward, not because the Church has earned them by its own works, but because God is just, who, since He promised that He would give them to the Church, for the sake of His Son, deems it just that He should keep this promise. Whence also he previously called it an inheritance, which even if it falls to children or grandchildren, by no merit of their own labors (for servants in a household, who are not participants in the master of the house's inheritance, have labored more than children or grandchildren) yet it is most justly received, because it is received by legitimate inheritance.

Latin:

Vers. 17. OMNE VAS QUOD FICTUM EST CONTRA TE] Verte: Omnia arma quæ contra te paran- tur. Nam sic כלי sæpissime sumitur, vertiturque ὅπλον Jer. 21, 4. Ezech. 32, 26. Nec aliter hic Chaldæus.

ET OMNEM LINGUAM RESISTENTEM TIBI IN JUDICIO JUDICABO] In Hebræo: Omnem lin- guam, quæ tecum judicio contendere voluerit, refelles. O- mnes calumnias, quæ adversus te ad reges Persarum defe- rentur, facile vinces.

Hanc glossam Judaicam falsam esse, ea quæ hactenus adduximus, assatim docent. Etsi enim ad- mittamus, vi hujusce promissionis etiam eorum molimina irrita esse debuisse, qui reædificationi ur- bis obstare ausuri erant, ea tamen generalis est, Ecclesiæ divinam assistentiam & defensionem pro- mittens, adversus quosvis hostes: neque de mate- riali urbe aut templo hic sermo est, sed de mystica Dei unitate, cujus gratia Deus urbes,provincias & regna tuetur, ac Hierofolyma & templum reædi- ficari voluit. Recte ergo hic quintum beneficium locat Brentius à Deo promissum Ecclesiæ, libera- tionem nempe ejusdem ab hostibus, & hæc ita legen- da ex Ebræo docet: Ecce veniendo veniet absq; me, quisquis venit ad te,ut super te irruat, vel te invadat. Ecce ego efficio, ut faber, qui exufflat igni carbonem, faciat instrumentum ad opus suum, & ego efficio, ut sit corruptor ad perdendum. Omne instrumentum, quod fictum est contra te,non prosperabitur,& omnem linguam, quæ insurgit adversum te in judicium, con- demnabis aut impietatis convinces. Quod autem di- citur: Efficio ut faber exufflans igni carbones, faciat instrumentum ad suum opus, dupliciter exponi po- test. Aut quod Deus efficiat, ut qui arma cudit, seu bellum suscipit adversus Ecclesiam, faciat hoc in suam ipsius perniciem, suo se gladio, ut dici so- let, jugulet, & foveam fodiat, in quam cadat. Aut quod Deus,etsi excitet aliquoties fabros, id est, ho- stes, qui parent arma adversus Ecclesiam, tamen efficiat,ut tandem ipsi pereant,Ecclesia autem ser- vetur. Utraque sententia eodem respicit, quod Deus Ecclesiam suam ita tueatur, ut etiamsi mul- tos habeat adversarios, qui oppugnent eam, alii quidem armis, hoc est, tyrannide externa & cor- porali, alii autem lingua, hoc est, convitiis,men- daciis, hæresibus, & impia doctrina, conservetur tamen in medio inimicorum admirabiliter, & ini- mici ejus corruant una cum armis & lingua sua horribiliter. Sic etiam B. Lutherus: ad verba, Ecce accola veniet qui &c. Grammatica hic, inquit, obscura est, sententia tamen sic potest reddi: Ecce quis accola contra te veniet, ut te obruat, cum absque me veniet! Consolatur Ecclesiam contra vim Tyrannorum. Quod autem addit, absq́, me, tollit illam intolerabilem jactantiam adversariorum, quod jactant se Deo obsequium præstare, cum persequuntur pios, se pugnare pro Ecclesia & pro fide contra hæreticos. Sic enim solent, ornant vim, quam piis afferunt, titulo nominis divini & Ecclesiæ. Veram Christus confirmat hic nos, & dicit, quod faciant id, sed absq́; me.

Vers. eod. HAEC EST HÆREDITAS SERVORUM DOMINI] Hoc est ipsorum privilegium. ET JUSTITIA EORUM APUD ME, DICIT DOMINUS] Id est, eorum quorum probitas mihi perspecta est.

Conclusio respondet concioni. Cum ergo hactenus Propheta recensuerit Catalogum beneficiorum Domini, asseverat nunc ea beneficia tradenda Ecclesiæ & servis Domini in hæreditatem. Et additur: HÆC EST JUSTITIA, hoc est, Justa merces eorum à me, quam ego videlicet retribuam eis. Vocat autem hæc beneficia justam mercedem, non quod Ecclesia meruerit ea suis ipsius operibus, sed quod justus sit Deus, qui cum se ea promiserit Ecclesiæ daturum, propter Filium suum, censeat justum esse, ut hanc promissionem servet. Unde & antea vocavit eam hæreditatem, quæ etsi contingit liberis aut nepotibus, nullo laborum suorum merito (plus enim laboraverunt in familia servi, qui hæreditatis patris familias non sunt participes, quam liberi aut nepotes) tamen justissime accipitur, quod legitima hæreditate accipitur.

## 55:1 Argument
CHAPTER LV. All are incited to the enjoyment of the Lord's banquet, since Christ is to be given for the sake of the promises made to David, and the nations are to be called to him. Therefore they are commanded to seek the Lord, and to abandon the wicked way: and the efficacy and fruit of the divine word is described.

Ver. 1.

ALL YOU THAT THIRST, COME TO THE WATERS] The same discourse is continued, and the peoples are warned to draw the doctrine concerning the one true God from Jeremiah. You who desire to speak the truth, come to this teacher. Thus the Chaldean here. AND YOU THAT HAVE NO SILVER, MAKE HASTE, BUY, AND EAT] Even the poor will be able to learn from him without any expense. True doctrine is compared to both drink and food, because it feeds and refreshes the soul, see Jerem. 15, 16. Ezech. 3, 3. Prov. 9, 5. Eccles. 15, 3. c. 24, 29. Philo, τὸ φαγεῖν σύμβολόν ἐσι τροφῆς ψυχικῆς. Add Maimonides, Guide for the Perplexed, l. 29. BUY WITHOUT SILVER] Take freely. WINE AND MILK] Both comfort for souls and nourishment.

Latin:

CAPUT LV. Incitantur omnes ad fruitionem convivii Domini, quum promissionum Davidi factarum causa Christus donandus sit, & gentes adeum vocandæ. Ideo quærere Dominum jubentur, & derelinquere viam pravam: & verbi divini efficacia ac fructus describitur.

Vers. 1.

OMNES SITIENTES VENITE AD AQUAS] Continuatur idem sermo, monenturque populi, ut doctrinam de uno vero Deo ab Jeremia hauriant. Qui verum dicere cupitis, ad hunc doctorem venite. Ita hic Chaldæus. ET QUI NON HABETIS ARGENTUM, EMITE ET COMEDITE] Etiam pauperes sine ulla impensa ab ipso discere poterunt. Vera doctrina & potui, & cibo comparatur, quia animum pascit & recreat, vid. Jerem. 15, 16. Ezech. 3, 3. Prov. 9, 5. Eccles. 15, 3. c. 24, 29. Philo τὸ φαγεῖν σύμβολόν ἐσι τροφῆς ψυχικῆς. Adde Maimoniden Doctoris dubitantium l. 29. EMITE ABSQUE ARGENTO] Sumite gratis. VINUM ET LAC] Et solatium animis & alimentum.

## 55:2
Ver. 2. WHY DO YOU SPEND SILVER FOR THAT WHICH IS NOT BREAD, AND YOUR LABOR FOR THAT WHICH DOTH NOT SATISFY] Why do you learn with great zeal and expense the Chaldean vanity, from which no fruit returns to the soul? HEARKENING HEARKEN TO ME] Speaking through Jeremiah. AND EAT GOOD] Learn salutary things. AND YOUR SOUL SHALL DELIGHT IN FATNESS] These nations will greatly delight in rich foods. Ps. 36. v. 9. Ps. 63, 6. Job 36, 11. You shall have peace of conscience.

That Isaiah calls all who thirst, so that they may gather to hear Jeremiah, is a purely Jewish gloss. For there is nothing here about Jeremiah, nor was any mention made of him in the preceding passages. But that it was treated of Christ in chapter 53, and of the fruitfulness and happiness of the Church in the time of the New Testament, we have abundantly shown that the Prophet had instituted his discourse in the preceding chapter. It is therefore to be understood concerning the proclamation of the Gospel, so that the discourse may cohere. For since he has taught concerning Christ and his benefits, which he confers upon the Church, he now adds an exhortation to hear and receive this Gospel by faith, and to perform repentance. Thus the blessed Luther explained the connection: He has taught hitherto in many chapters: what Christ is, likewise what the Church is, namely the congregation of those who cling to the word, and not to visible things. This he has comforted with various promises, against the scandal of the cross. Now he also exhorts that it be assiduous in the word, lest it fall into contempt or loathing of the word, than which temptation there is none more pestilential and common, from which all heresies have been born. Furthermore, he does not call any one nation, but all peoples: he does not invite the Jews to hear the sermon of Jeremiah, but all men to receive the Gospel through faith. Although the invitation pertains to all nations, he does not, however, call everyone indiscriminately, not the full, but the THIRSTY. The full, however, are the hypocrites, who, intoxicated by the justice of their own justice, loathe the waters of the Gospel, and the despisers, who, intoxicated by the pleasures of this age, do not seek heavenly happiness. The thirsty, however, are those who, having recognized their own sin, understand themselves to be so corrupt and depraved that they can find no true justice at all in their own powers and works, and therefore see that it is all over for their salvation, unless they draw another, and that a heavenly, justice. Now if we weigh to what they are called, namely to waters and to bread, to wine and to milk, it is not obscure that Christ himself made this invitation of his, when he invites the thirsty to himself, and calls them to water and to bread. John 5, v. 29: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink; He who will have drunk of the water that I shall give him, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly: Signifying the Holy Spirit, whom those who believe were about to receive. And John 4: If you knew the grace of God, and who it is who says to you, give me to drink, you would have asked of him, and he would have given you water: Everyone who drinks from the water will thirst again: but whoever will have drunk from the water that I SHALL GIVE, will not thirst forever; but the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life. And again concerning bread, John 6: I AM THE LIVING BREAD, which came down from heaven, if anyone will have eaten of this bread, he will live forever. Whence it is certain that the bread and water, which is here proposed to us to be bought, eaten, and drunk, is the word of the Gospel, by which Christ dispenses himself to be enjoyed, and drenches and refreshes us with this flowing Spirit. Jerome observes that these waters are offered to be eaten: In a wonderful manner, he says, they buy waters without money, and they do not drink them, but eat them. For he himself is both water and bread, who descended from heaven. But in the text, the thirsty are distinctly invited to water, namely to drink: and as many as do not have money, to buy and eat, namely the hungry. That therefore refers to the living water which Christ provides, but this latter refers to the bread of life, which Christ professes himself to be. Therefore, this water and this bread is not the doctrine concerning one God: which even the Gentiles had, who nevertheless were destitute of living water and the bread of life. That the doctrine of Christ is the water of life, we are also taught in the Apocalypse, ch. 22, v. 17. And the bridegroom and the bride say come, and he who thirsts, let him come, and he who wills, let him receive the water of life freely. And Grotius himself explained that mystical water as the doctrine of the Gospel of Christ, Annotations on John 4, 14. εἰ μὴ διψήση εἰς `τ αἰῶνα. Below 6, 34. ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐ- μέ, ῤ μὴ διψήση πώποτε. Therefore, the water here is that which is believed for salvation, which once drunk is not to be drunk again, but only to be retained. There is nothing that can be added to it, unlike the precepts of human wisdom, of which there is never an end: therefore the more it is drunk, the more the thirst grows; it is of this that Ecclesiasticus 24, v. 30 speaks. He also declared the mystical bread to be Christ and the word of the Gospel at John 6, v. 33. He (Christ) had just called his word bread, now he calls himself bread. For things that agree with the Gospel are accustomed to be attributed to Christ, its promulgator and sanctifier. To the object of the purchase also pertains wine and milk, which both Holy Scripture explains as the doctrine of Christ. For milk is called the food of believers, 1 Corinthians 3, 1 Peter 2, and wine is called the doctrine which hypostatic wisdom offers us, Proverbs 9, wine germinating virgins, Zechariah 9, v. 17. To which Jerome refers, that Moses, understanding wine and milk in the passion of Christ in mystical language, testifies: His eyes are gracious from wine, and his teeth white from milk. The blessed Luther says that wine and milk are offered to different subjects: Because there are weak and robust ones in the Church, to the robust, who are exercised by the temptations of sin and death, wine is given for consolation: But to the simple and weak, milk is given for nourishment, by which they are instructed. Thus also Musculus: He mentions milk, water, and wine quite conveniently. For heavenly grace, by which we are all nourished, has milk for infants, water for adolescents, wine for men and the elderly, dispensing its gifts with supreme providence according to the capacity and necessity of those whom it has undertaken to nourish. Clement of Alexandria, book 1, Paedagogus, chapter 1, understands everything concerning Christ: The Word (hypostatic) is said allegorically in many ways, food, and flesh, and nourishment, and bread and blood, and milk and wine. But because water must be distinguished from him by whom it is given, by water is understood the doctrine of Christ, or the word of the Gospel, which, because of its power of refreshing, and extinguishing thirst, and reviving in the heat of divine wrath, is compared to water, and since the Holy Spirit is joined to the word, indeed the word is spirit and life, John 6, therefore by the name of water the Holy Spirit with his gifts is also designated, Isaiah 44, Ezekiel 36, John 7, v. 37. Apoc. 22. which Christ provides, because through the word of the Gospel and the Holy Spirit and His gifts we are imbued and refreshed by Christ, and through and on account of Christ. Furthermore, the word is compared to bread, because it nourishes our soul, and because all power of nourishing in the word is from the object Christ, whom the word of the Gospel embraces, offers, and provides to us. Therefore, Scripture sometimes proposes Christ as heavenly bread and food of the soul, and sometimes the word itself, by which Christ is exhibited, and through which Christ is dispensed with His merit, so that we may enjoy the heavenly Manna itself, it makes the bread of life and food of the soul. The same word is also compared to wine, so that it may be indicated that the word is not only food, but also drink for our soul, not only serving for refreshment, which water also provides, but for the strengthening of our heart, which is proper to wine. Finally, it is compared to milk, both on account of sweetness and pleasantness, because we perceive the very pleasantness of the Lord in the word, Psalm 34:1. Pet. 2. both on account of the convenience of nutrition; because infants themselves are nourished by milk, therefore ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα we desire 1 Pet. 2:2. Further, as to the manner of purchase, BUY WITHOUT SILVER AND WITHOUT ANY EXCHANGE, it again fits spiritual goods perfectly, Matt. 16. Freely you have received, freely give. To which gratuitous purchase Christ invites in Apoc. 3:17 those who are poor and destitute of silver and gold: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich. From the comparison indeed of the invitations which Christ in the days of his flesh instituted, it appears clearer than the sun, that it is not Jeremiah to whom they are referred by our Prophet, but Christ, inasmuch as he, just as in this place, so in the days of his flesh, in order to testify that he was the one who instituted this invitation, invited likewise all who were in need of refreshment, Matt. 11. Come refresh you: all who hunger and thirst; Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied, Matt. 5. And John 6. v. 37. If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Which parallelism of places is so evident that Grotius, when he was commenting on John, acknowledged that Christ had taken those things from our passage: ἐάν τις διψᾷ, ἐρχέσθω πρός με, καὶ πινέτω. Christ was accustomed to take the occasion for his discourse from obvious things. On that day, however, the people were drawing water from the fountain of Siloam with great pomp, using that song from Isaiah: You shall draw waters in joy from the fountains of salvation; having observed this, Christ teaches them who is the truly saving fountain indicated by Zechariah 13. v. 1. He takes these words of his, however, from Isaiah 55. v. 1. The sense is: Whoever is consumed by a desire for happiness (for the Hebrews call that thirsting, as do other nations) let him come to me: I will quench his thirst. What madness, then, the devil, is it that he preferred to lend his ears to the Jews now rather than to Christ, snatching these things away to Jeremiah, of whom there is neither sign nor trace in the whole context.

As for the antithesis or opposition, therefore: WHY DO YOU WEIGH OUT SILVER NOT FOR BREAD, AND YOUR LABOR NOT FOR SATISFACTION, that is wrongly restricted to Chaldean vanity, and rather concerns those objects from which the satisfaction of the soul is expected in vain. For the opposite member teaches that the discourse is not about any fruit whatsoever returning to the soul, according to the very exegesis of Grotius: EAT THE GOOD, learn saving things. YOUR SOUL SHALL DELIGHT IN FATNESS. You shall have peace of conscience. It is not evident that the Israelite expected either saving doctrine or peace of conscience from that Chaldean vanity. Blessed Luther interpreted these more correctly in a moral sense: It is a refutation and abrogation of all other religions, doctrines, and works. That all religions, all doctrines, and all pursuits, outside of this doctrine of grace, are fruitless, and yet laborious, which do not make the soul tranquil, but afflict it. You will diligently note this predicate, which he attributes to all righteousnesses that are outside of grace, that they are, namely, laborious, and yet fruitless, as we experienced under the Pope. The words themselves exhibit the general sense: Why do you seek in vain with great labor, many troubles, and expenses for refreshment in those things which cannot render the conscience tranquil and cannot sedate spiritual hunger and thirst? HEAR, HEARING ME, preaching to you in my Gospel about the clemency of the heavenly Father toward the human race, and about my merit, and its power: AND EAT; more correctly you shall eat THE GOOD and saving FOOD for the soul, AND YOUR SOUL SHALL DELIGHT IN FATNESS, more correctly in richness. In the Gospel, such food and drink is proposed to us, which not only drives away hunger and thirst, but also wonderfully refreshes and delights, as sweet and rich foods do: for the refreshment of the soul in the Gospel of Christ is abundant. Only INCLINE YOUR EAR to hear the Gospel, AND COME TO ME, approach me by faith, the Throne of grace, HEAR what I say to you about the reconciliation of God with the human race; AND YOUR SOUL SHALL LIVE, you shall obtain eternal life: as the Osiandrian paraphrase most correctly states. Which sense may shine forth further from the following. For these cut to the quick the entire nerve of the Grotian depravation. Which is also refuted by this promise of life. For the LIFE OF THE SOUL is promised. Which Grotius, distorting to temporal life, perverts the words in this way.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUARE APPENDITIS ARGENTUM NON IN PANIBUS, ET LABOREM VESTRUM NON IN SATURITATE] Cur magno studio & impendio discitis ματαιοτεχνίαν Chaldaicam, unde nullus fructus ad animum redit? AUDITE AUDIENTES ME] Loquentem per Jeremiam. ET COMEDITE BONUM] Discite salutaria. DELECTABITUR IN CRASSITUDINE ANIMA VESTRA] Pinguibus cibis multum delectabuntur gentes istæ. Ps. 36. v. 9. Ps. 63, 6. Job. 36, 11. Habebitis pacem conscientiæ.

COnvocare Esaiam omnes sitientes, ut ad Jeremiam audiendum conveniant, glossa est mere Judaica. De Jeremia enim nihil hic, neque in antecedentibus ulla de eo facta est mentio. De Christo vero cap. 53. actum esse, deq; fœcunditate ac felicitate Ecclesiæ tempore N. Testam. præce- dente capite sermonem instituisse Prophetam, ab- unde ostendimus. De præconio ergo Evangelii in- telligenda, ut cohæreat oratio. Quum enim do- cuerit de Christo, ejusque beneficiis, quæ confert in Ecclesiam, jam exhortationem addit ad audien- dum & excipiendum fide hoc Evangelium, & ad agendam pœnitentiam. Ita συνέχειαν exposuit B. Lutherus: Docuit hactenus multis capitibus: quid sit Christus, item quid Ecclesia, nempe congregatio eorum, qui hærent in verbo, & non in rebus apparen- tibus. Hanc consolatus est variis promissionibus, con- tra scandalum crucis. Nunc cohortatur quoq;, ut sit assidua in verbo, ne in contemptum aut fastidium verbi incidat, qua tentatione haud alia pestilentior & communior est, unde natæ sunt omnes hæreses. Por- ro non vocat unam aliquam gentem, sed populos omnes: non Judæos ad audiendum sermonem Je- remiæ, sed universos homines invitat ad suscipien- dum per fidem Evangelium. Quamvis vero ad omnes gentes pertineat invitatio, non tamen in- discriminatim omnes vocat, non saturos, sed SI- TIENTES. Saturi autem sunt hypocritæ, qui in- ebriati justitia suæ ipsorum justitiæ fastidiunt aquas Evangelicas, & contemptores, qui inebriati volu- ptatibus hujus seculi, non requirunt cœlestem feli- citatem. Sitientes vero sunt, qui agnito peccato suo intelligunt se ita corruptos & depravatos, ut nullam plane veram justitiam in suis viribus & o- peribus invenire queant, ideoq; vident de salute sua actum esse, nisi aliam, eamq; cœlestem justitiam hauriant. Jam si expendamus, quo vocentur, ad aquas nempe & ad panem, ad vinum & lac, haud obscurum est, quod Christus ipse hanc invitatio- nem suam fecerit, cum sitientes ad se invitat, ad aquam & ad panem vocat. Joh. 5. v.29. Si quis sitit, veniat ad me & bibat; Qui biberit de aqua, quam ego dedero ei, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vi- tæ: Significans Spiritum Sanctum, quem credentes accepturi erant. Et Joh. 4. Si scires gratiam Dei, & quis est, qui dicit tibi, da mihi bibere, Tu petiisses ab eo, & dedisset tibi aquam: Omnis qui bibit ex a- qua, sitiet iterum: quisquis autem biberit ex aqua, quam EGO DABO, non sitiet in æternum; sed aqua, quam ego dedero ei, fiet fons in eo aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Et rursus de pane Joh. 6. EGO SUM PANIS vivus, qui de cœlo descendi, si quis e- derit ex hoc pane, vivet in æternum. Unde constat, panem & aquam, quæ hic nobis emenda, comeden- da & bibenda proponitur, esse verbum Evangelii, quo Christus se fruendum dispensat, ac fluentis Spiritus hujus nos perfundit, atque reficit. Hiero- nymus observat, aquas has præberi comedendas: Mi- rum in modum, inquit, emunt aquas absq; pecunia, & non bibunt eas, sed comedunt. Ipse enim & aqua & panis est, qui de cœlo descendit. Sed in textu in- vitantur distincte sitientes ad aquam scil. ut bibant: & quotquot non habent pecuniam, ut emant & comedant, esurientes scil. Illud ergo ad aquam vi- vam, quam præbet Christus, hoc vero ad panem vi- tæ, quem Christus se esse profitetur, refertur. Non ergo hæc aqua & hic panis est doctrina de uno Deo: quam habuêre etiam Ethnici, qui tamen aqua viva & pane vitæ destituti fuêre. Christi autem doctri- nam esse aquam vitæ, etiam in Apocalypsi docemur c.22. v.17. Et sponsus & sponsa dicunt veni, & qui sitit, veniat, & qui vult, accipiat aquam vitæ gratis. Et de doctrina Evangelii Christi viva aquam illam my- sticam exposuit Grotius ipse Annotat. ad Joh. 4, 14. εἰ μὴ διψήση εἰς `τ αἰῶνα. Infr. 6, 34. ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐ- μέ, ῤ μὴ διψήση πώποτε. Ergo hic aqua est id, quod creditur ad salutem, quod semel haustum am- plius hauriendum non est, sed retinendum tantum. Nihil est, quod ei adjici possit, aliter quam in huma- næ sapientiæ præceptis, quorum nunquam finis est: id- eo quo magis ea bibitur, eo magis crescit sitis, de ea sermo est Eccles. 24. v. 30. Panem etiam mysticum de Christo ac verbo Evangelii declaravit ad Joh. 6. v. 33. Modo verbum suum panem vocaverat (Christus) nunc se panem vocat. Solent enim, quæ Evangelio conveniunt, Christo tribui, ejus promul- gatori ac sanctori. Ad emptionis objectum perti- net etiam vinum & lac, quod utrumque de doctri- na Christi explicat Sacra Scriptura. Nam lac voca- tur cibus credentium 1. Corinth. 3. 1. Petr. 2. & vi- num dicitur doctrina, quam sapientia hypostatica nobis propinat, Prov. 9. vinum germinans virgines Zach. 9. v. 17. Quo refert Hieronymus, quod Mo- ses vinum & lac in passione Christi intelligens mystico sermone testetur: Gratiosi oculi ejus à vino, & can- didi dentes ejus à lacte. B. Lutherus vinum & lac diversis subjectis præberi dicit: Quia enim in Ec- clesia sunt infirmi & robusti, robustis, qui tentationi- bus peccati & mortis exercentur, datur vinum ad con- solationem: Rudibus autem & infirmis datur lac ad alimentum, quo instituuntur. Sic & Musculus: Admodum convenienter meminit lactis, aquæ & vi- ni. Habet enim cœlestis gratia, qua cuncti alimur, lac pro infantibus, aquam pro adolescentibus, vi- num pro viris ac senibus, dispensans summa providen- tia charismata sua pro captu & necessitate eorum, quos alendos suscepit. Clemens Alexandr. lib. 1. Pæ- dagog. cap. 1. omnia de Christo intelligit: Verbum (hypostaticum) multis modis allegorice dicitur, ci- bus, & caro, & nutrimentum, & panis & sanguis, & lac & vinum. Sed quia aqua ab eo, à quo datur distinguenda, per aquam Christi doctrina, vel ver- bum Evangelii intelligitur, quod ob vim reficien- di, & sitim extinguendi, & in æstu iræ divinæ refo- cillandi aquæ comparatur, & quum verbo con- junctus sit Spiritus Sanctus, imo verbum sit spiri- tus & vita, Joh. 6. ideo aquæ nomine etiam Spir. S. cum donis suis designatur, Esa. 44. Ezech. 36. Joh. 7. v. 37. Apoc. 22. quæ Christus præbet, quia per verbum Evangelii & Spiritu S. ac donis ejusdem à Christo, & per ac propter Christum perfundimur, ac reficimur. Porro verbum pani confertur, quia nutrit animam nostram, & quia vis omnis nutrien- di in verbo est ab objecto Christo, quem comple- ctitur, offert, & præbet nobis verbum Evangelii. Ideo Scriptura modo Christum ut panem cœle- stem & cibum animæ proponit, modo verbum ipsum, quo exhibetur, & per quod dispensatur Christus cum merito suo, ut ipso fruamur Manna cœlesti, panem vitæ ac cibum animæ facit. Com- paratur & vino idem verbum, ut indicetur verbum non modo cibum, sed & potum animæ nostræ esse, non tantum facere ad refocillationem, quod aqua etiam præstat, sed ad cordis nostri confortatio- nem, quæ vino propria est. Comparatur denique lacti, tum ob dulcedinem & suavitatem, quia ipsam Domini svavitatem in verbo percipimus, Psal. 34. 1. Pet. 2. tum ob nutritionis commoditatem; quia lacte nutriuntur infantes ipsi, ideo ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα concupiscimus 1. Pet. 2, 2. Ulterius quod ad emptionis modum, EMITE ABSQUE ARGENTO ET ABSQUE ULLA COMMUTATIONE, optime ille iterum bonis spiritualibus convenit, Matth. 16. Gratis accepistis, gratis date. Ad quam gratuitam emptionem invi- tat Christus Apoc. 3. v. 17. eos, qui pauperes sunt, & argento atque auro destituti: Svadeo tibi emere à me aurum ignitum probatum, ut locuples fias. Ex col- latione sane invitationum, quas Christus indiebus carnis suæ instituit, Sole clarius apparet, non Jere- miam esse, ad quem remittuntur à Propheta no- stro, sed Christum, utpote qui ad eam, ut hoc loco, ita in diebus carnis, ut testaretur se esse il- lum, qui hanc invitationem instituit, invitavit pariter omnes refectione indigos, Matth. 11. Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis, ego reficiam vos: omnes esurientes & sitientes; Beati qui esu- riunt & sitiunt justitiam, quia saturabuntur, Matth. 5. Et Joh. 6. v. 37. Si quis sitit, veniat ad me & bibat. Qui locorum parallelismus tam evidens est, ut a- gnoverit Grotius, cum in Johannem commenta- retur, Christum è nostro loco illa desumsisse: ἐάν τις διψᾷ, ἐρχέσθω πρός με, καὶ πινέτω. Ex rebus obviis ser- monis occasionem capere Christus solebat. Eo autem die populus magna pompa ex fonte Siloæ aquam hau- riebat canticum illud ex Esaia usurpans: Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus salutis, hoc conspecto do- cet eos Christus, quis sit fons vere salutaris indicatus à Zacharia 13. v. 1. Verba autem hæc sua sumit ex Esa. 55. v. 1. Sensus est: Qui desiderio felicitatis uri- tur (nam id sitire vocant Hebræi, ut & aliæ gentes) ad me veniat: ego sitim ejus restinguam. Quæ ergo, ma- lum, dementia est, quod nunc magis Judæis, quam Christo aures præbere maluit ad Jeremiam hæc abripiens, de quo nec vola, nec vestigium in to- to contextu.

Quod ergo ad antithesin vel oppositionem: QUARE APPENDITIS ARGENTUM NON IN PANIBUS, ET LABOREM VESTRUM NON IN SATURITATE, ea perperam re- stringitur ad ματαιοτεχνείαν Chaldaicam, & spe- ctat potius illa objecta, à quibus frustra expecta- tur saturitas animæ. Nam non de qualicunque fructu ad animum redeunte sermonem esse mem- brum oppositum docet, juxta ipsam Grotianam ἐξήγησιν COMEDITE BONUM, discite saluta- ria. DELECTABITUR IN CRASSITUDINE ANIMA VESTRA. Habebitis pacem conscien- tiæ. Ab illa ματαιοτεχνίᾳ Chaldaica Israëlitast vel doctrinam salutarem, vel pacem conscientiæ expectasse non constat. Rectius hæc ἠθικῶς in- terpretatus B. Lutherus: Est confutatio & abroga- tio omnium aliarum religionum, doctrinarum & ope- rum. Quod omnes religiones, omnes doctrinæ, & studia omnia, extra hanc gratiæ doctrinam sint fru- stranea, & tamen laboriosa, quæ non tranquillum fa- ciant animum, sed affligant. Diligenter autem notabis hoc prædicatum, quod tribuit omnibus justitiis, quæ sunt extra gratiam, quod scil. sint laboriosæ, & tamen fru- straneæ, sicut sub Papa experti sumus. Sensum ge- neralem ipsa verba exhibent: Cur magno labore, multis molestiis, & sumptibus frustra quæritis refe- ctionem in iis rebus, quæ conscientiam tranquillam reddere, & spiritualem famem ac sitim sedare ne- queunt? AUDITE AUDIENTES ME concio- nantem vobis in Evangelio meo de clementia Pa- tris cœlestis erga genus humanum, deque meo me- rito, & ejus virtute: ET COMEDITE; rectius comedetis BONUM & salutarem animæ CIBUM, ET DELECTABITUR IN CRASSITUDI- NE, rectius in pinguedine, ANIMA VESTRA. In Evangelio proponitur nobis talis cibus & po- tus, qui non modo famem sitimq; pellat, sed etiam mirifice recreet & delectet, ut suaves, & pingues ci- bi faciunt: Copiosa est enim animæ recreatio in Evangelio Christi. INCLINATE tantum AU- REM VESTRAM ad audiendum Evangelium, ET VENITE AD ME, accedite fide ad me, Thronum gratiæ, AUDITE quæ ego de reconci- liatione Dei cum genere humano vobis dico; ET VIVET ANIMA VESTRA, consequemini vi- tam æternam: ut rectissime paraphrasis Osiandri- na. Qui sensus è sequentibus ulterius elucescat. Hæc enim depravationi Grotianæ nervum omnem penitus incidunt. Quæ etiam ex hac vitæ promis- sione refellitur. Nam promittitur VITA ANI- MÆ. Quam Grotius ad temporalem vitam detor- quens verba ita pervertit.

## 55:3
Ver. 3. YOUR SOUL SHALL LIVE] You shall enjoy a long life.

But where, I ask you, is the life of the soul the same thing as a long life? When all saving things and the peace of conscience were promised, was it not better to understand the life of the soul as spiritual and eternal life than as temporal? Is that water not the water of eternal life, does that true bread not confer eternal life, with Christ as the interpreter? The covenant itself, which is the foundation of this grace and the establishment of this gracious promise, does not concern earthly and temporary things, but eternal goods, as those things which follow hereafter openly testify. But let us hear a new distortion.

AND I WILL STRIKE A PERPETUAL COVENANT WITH YOU] I will receive you into that covenant which I made with Noah and his posterity, Gen. 9. v. 9. which is also called perpetual ibid. v. 16.

THE FAITHFUL MERCIES OF DAVID] I show to them benefits as constantly as I showed them to David. This is what the Greeks mean when they say τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστὰ. For they are accustomed to translate with the neighboring word חסדים, ὅσια or ὁσιότητα.

Has anyone ever heard by report that the covenant of Noah is designated here? For it is a matter of a covenant yet to be completed: I WILL STRIKE a covenant WITH YOU. But the Lord had already struck the covenant of Noah long ago. It is a matter of the covenant promised to David: THE MERCIES OF DAVID, that is, those promised to David, the Lord himself points out as FAITHFUL: Not by analogy, because they are similar by reason of constancy, as Grotius perverts it, for no comparison is held in the text, but because he wishes to perform and exhibit those very mercies which he had promised to David, as the words expressly sound. Nor indeed was there any doubt about the covenant entered into with Noah, regarding not destroying the earth by a flood: But there was the greatest need for the covenant made to David, so that the faithful, exposed to so many calamities and disasters, might be confirmed from time to time, so that they could easily have hesitated about its fulfillment: and what did that covenant about the waters of the flood have to do with the present sermon or what at least did it do toward perceiving the doctrine from Jeremiah? For Jeremiah had to be sent, so that he might confirm that covenant. Those dreams are either more than Rabbinical ravings. We have an ἀνυπεύθυνον interpreter of this covenant, and one superior to every exception, the Holy Apostle, whose interpretation Grotius either did not observe, which is an inertia not to be borne in a commentator, or he cared nothing for it, which is a detestable insolence. For thus St. Paul, Acts 13:38. But that he raised him from the dead, no more to return to corruption, he said thus: Because I will give you the holy things of David, the faithful ones, ὅτι δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστὰ. Therefore, it is about that promise of God made to the faithful David that is treated here, by the force of which Christ was to be raised from the dead, which is indeed very badly twisted toward the Noachic pact, or toward temporal benefits, whatever those may be. The mercies, therefore, which God establishes here forever, are to be explained from the eternal kingdom of Christ, on account of which he could not remain in death, and they are those of which David sings: I will sing of the mercies of the Lord forever; I will make known thy truth with my mouth to generation and generation: I have sworn to David my servant, etc. Ps. 88:1, 2, 3. Those eternal mercies, however, are those which God established for David by an oath in the Messiah, who for that reason was delivered up to death for our sins, and was to be raised again for our justification, so that we might enjoy eternal mercy, that is, the forgiveness of sins, grace, and everlasting salvation. Which the blessed Luther explained most excellently concerning the covenant of grace and the New Testament. And I will make an everlasting covenant with you. He clearly abrogates the old covenant and promises a new one, namely, the faithful mercies of David. This is the covenant of grace and the remission of sins on the name of mercy, which he opposes to all merits and works, so that we may understand our righteousness to be a free gift. But what he adds, faithful, sharpens the exhortation. For fearful and weak minds always fear lest such great promises (because they are offered in the bare word) be void and deceive those who believe. Therefore, in order to consult our weakness, he calls the mercies faithful, that is, truthful, which he wills to truly perform and exhibit, just as they are believed. Bring here the antithesis and this predicate, faithful, take it away from all other doctrines and righteousnesses, because they are not faithful, but deceive. Furthermore, lest the bodily promises be understood concerning the land of Canaan, he therefore adds, the faithful mercies of David, so that he may distinguish the mercies of the new covenant from the mercies of the old covenant, by which he promised the land of Canaan to the Fathers. The blessed Brentius, worthy to be heard here, explains the whole matter clearly and solidly according to his custom. For he has it thus: Paul signifies first here by his allegation that this passage is to be understood clearly concerning Christ promised to David. Then it is not obscure that this passage is taken mutually from Psalm 88, which treats that promise which is written in 2 Samuel 7. But the Psalmist says thus: I will keep my mercy for him forever, and my covenant faithful to him, etc. You see that these are almost the same words of the Psalm and of this prophetic discourse. Therefore, what is said has this meaning: I once promised David that I would give from his posterity the Messiah or Christ, my son, whom I embrace with such love that on account of him I am propitious to all who believe in him, and I adopt them as sons and heirs of my heavenly goods. But I promised this not simply, but I confirmed it with an oath: The Lord has sworn, and he will not repent, You are a Priest, etc. And again: the Lord has sworn the truth and he will not frustrate him. Of the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne. This covenant, therefore, confirmed by an oath, I will keep perpetually, nor will I ever commit that the mercies, or benefits promised to David concerning Christ, should be vain and fallacious, but I will cause them to be faithful, that is, most firm and most certain. For I will give from his posterity Christ my son, so that whoever believes in him may not perish, but have eternal life. This is the Gospel, to the hearing of which the Holy Spirit calls through Isaiah, at the beginning indeed all the hearers of Isaiah, then all their posterity, nay, the universal Church, so that we may acknowledge that there is no other name given under heaven to men, in which it behooves us to be saved, except the Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ. The Jews themselves acknowledge that the discourse here is about the Messiah, and Rabbi David Kimchi understands by David here the Messiah himself: The faithful mercies of David, that is, the King Messiah, who is called David according to that (Ezekiel 37:25) And David my servant shall be prince forever. Which opinion, that Christ is understood by David, also pleased Jerome, Musculus, and others. But the former explanation is simpler.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VIVET ANIMA VESTRA] Longa vita frue- mini.

At ubi, sodes, vita animæ idem est, quod longa vita. Annon cum salutaria quæq; & pax conscientiæ promissa, animæ vitam præstabat intelligere de spi- rituali & æterna vita, quam de temporali? An- non aqua illa est aqua vitæ æternæ, annon panis il- le verus vitam æternam confert, interprete Chri- sto? Fœdus ipsum, quod fundamentum est hujus gratiæ & stabilimentum gratiosæ hujus promissio- nis, non terrena & temporaria concernere, sed æ- terna bona, ea quæ porro sequuntur, palam te- stantur. Audiamus autem novam στρεβλότητα.

ET FERIAM VOBISCUM PACTUM SEMPI- TERNUM] Recipiam vos in illud fœdus, quod cum Noa ejusque posteris feci, Gen. 9. v. 9. quod & sempiternum dicitur ibid. v. 16.

MISERICORDIAS DAVID FIDELES] Exhibeo illis beneficia tam constanter, quam Davidi exhibui. Hoc est, quod Græci volunt, cum dicunt τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστὰ. Nam חסדים voce vicina ὅσια aut ὁσιότητα solent trans- ferre.

Ecquis unquam fando audivit hic designari fœdus Noæh? Nam agitur de fœdere adhuc com- plendo: FERIAM VOBISCUM fœdus. At fœ- dus Noæh jam pridem ferierat Dominus. Agitur de fœdere Davidi promisso: MISERICORDIAS DAVID, id est, Davidi promissas, FIDELES Dominus ipse indigitat: Non per analogiam, quod similes ratione constantiæ, ut pervertit Grotius, nul- lum enim comparatio in textu habetur, sed quod illas ipsas misericordias, quas Davidi promiserat, præstare & exhibere velit, ut verba ῥητῶς sonant. Neque vero dubium erat de fœdere cum Noah i- nito, quoad non perdendam terram diluvio: Sed de fœdere Davidi facto maxime opus erat, ut sub- inde confirmarentur fideles, tot calamitatibus & cladibus obnoxii, ut facile de impletione ejus hæ- rere potuerint:& quid fœdus illud de aquis diluvii ad præsentem concionem aut quid saltem ad do- ctrinam ex Jeremia percipiendam faciebat? Nam mittendus erat Jeremias, ut fœdus illud confirma- ret. Somnia illa sunt aut deliria plusquam Rabbini- ca. Habemus fœderis hujus interpretem ἀνυπεύ- θυνον, & omni exceptione superiorem S. Aposto- lum, cujus vel non observavit interpretationem Grotius, quæ in commentatore non ferenda iner- tia, vel fusq; deq; habuit, quæ detestanda est pro- tervia. Sic enim S. Paulus Act. 13, 38. Quod autem su- scitarit eum à mortuis, amplius non reversurum in cor- ruptionem, ita dixit: Quia dabo vobis sancta David fidelia, ὅτι δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαβὶδ τὰ πιστὰ. De illa ergo promissione Dei fideli Davidi facta hic agitur, vi cujus Christus suscitandus erat à mor- tuis, quę vero pessime detorquetur ad pactum Noa- chi, aut ad beneficia temporalia, quæcunq; illa sint. Misericordiæ ergo, quas in æternum hic sancit Deus, explicandæ è regno Christi æterno sunt, ob quod in morte manere non potuit, suntque illæ, de quibus David canit: Misericordias Domini in æter- num cantabo, in generationem & generationem nun- ciabo veritatem tuam in ore meo: juravi David meo, &c. Ps. 88. v. 1. 2. 3. Misericordiæ autem illæ æternæ sunt, quas Davidi jurejurando sancivit Deus in Messia, qui propterea in mortem traditus ob peccata nostra, resuscitandus erat ob justitiam nostram, ut æterna misericordia frueremur, hoc est, condonatione peccatorum, gratia, & salu- te sempiterna. Quod B. Lutherus optime expo- suit de fœdere gratiæ & Novo Testamento. Et feriam vobiscum pactum sempiternum. Abrogat manifeste vetus pactum, & promittit novum, nempe, Mifericordias David fideles. Hoc est pactum gra- tiæ & remissionis peccatorum. Est enim emphasis in nomine misericordiæ, quam opponit omnibus meritis & operibus, ut intelligamus justitiam nostram esse gratuitum donum. Quod autem addit, fidelis, a- cuit exhortationem. Pavidæ enim & infirmæ men- tes semper metuunt, ne tantæ promissiones (quia in nudo verbo offeruntur) irritæ sint, & fallant cre- dentes. Ut igitur infirmitati nostræ consulat, vocat fideles misericordias, hoc est, veraces, quas velit vere prastare & exhibere, sicut creduntur. Huc affer antithesin & hoc prædicatum, fideles, adime omni- bus aliis doctrinis & justitiis, quod non sint fideles, sed fallant. Porro ne intelligantur promissiones corporales de terra Canaan, ideo addit, miseri- cordias fideles David, ut distinguat novi pacti mise- ricordias à misericordiis veteris pacti, quo promi- sit terram Canaan Patribus. Rem omnem perspi- cue & solide pro more suo explicat B. Brentius, di- gnus, qui hic audiatur. Ita enim habet; Significat primum Paulus hic allegatione sua perspicue hunc lo- cum intelligendum esse de Christo Davidi promisso. Deinde non est obscurum, quod hic locus mutuo acce- ptus sit è Psal. 88. qui tractat eam promissionem, quæ scripta est 2. Reg. 7. Sic autem dicit Psaltes: In æternum servabo illi misericordiam meam, & te- stamentum meum fidele ipsi, &c. Vides eadem pene verba esse Psalmi, & hujus Propheticæ concionis. Quod ergo dicitur, habet hanc sententiam: Promisi quondam Davidi, me daturum ex posteritate ejus Messiam seu Christum, filium meum, quem tanta charitate complector, ut propter ipsum propitius sim omnibus, qui credunt in eum, & adoptem eos in filios ac hæredes cœlestium meorum bonorum. Promisi autem hoc non simpliciter, sed confirmavi juramento: Juravit Dominus, & non pœnitebit eum, Tu es Sacerdos &c. Et iterum: juravit Domi- nus veritatem & non frustrabitur eum. De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam. Hoc igitur pactum juramento firmatum perpetuo servabo, nec unquam committam, ut misericordiæ, seu be- neficia Davidi de Christo promissa, sint vana, & fallacia, sed efficiam ut sint fidelia, hoc est, fir- missima & certissima. Dabo enim ex posteritate ejus Christum filium meum, ut quicunque in eum crediderit, non pereat, sed habeat æternam vitam. Hoc est Evangelion, ad quod audiendum vocat Spiritus S. per Esaiam, initio quidem omnes au- ditores Esaiæ, deinde omnem posteritatem eorum, imo universam Ecclesiam, ut agnoscamus, non esse aliud nomen sub cœlo datum hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri, præterquam Fi- lium Dei Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. A- gnoscunt ipsimet Judæi de Messia hic sermonem esse, & intelligit R. David Kimchi per Davidem hic Messiam ipsum: Misericordias Davidi fideles, id est, Rex Messias, qui vocatur David juxta illud (Ezech. 37. v. 25.) Et David servus meus princeps erit in seculum. Quæ sententia, quod per Davidem in- telligatur Christus, etiam Hieronymo, Musculo & a- liis placuit. Sed prior explicatio simplicior est.

## 55:4
Verse 4. BEHOLD I HAVE GIVEN HIM AS A WITNESS TO THE PEOPLES] Jeremiah, whose prophecies, being so definite, will give a certain testimony of my providence among all peoples.

A LEADER AND TEACHER TO THE GENTILES] It is the duty of a leader to go before the others.

What is to be thought of this gloss is evident from what has already been said. The depravation of this illustrious prophecy is to be detested. For not Jeremiah, but Christ is that witness of the peoples, and Leader and Teacher of the Gentiles. Those eulogies are too august to befit Jeremiah: they are truly proper to Christ. Whom God gave as a WITNESS to the peoples: he himself is the faithful witness, Revelation 1:5, chapter 3:14, and he professes concerning himself in John 18:37: For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, that I might bear witness to the truth; he himself was given as a covenant to the people, Isaiah 42:6, chapter 49:8, the same witness, not only by reason of providence, but by reason of the grace and mercy which he wills to exhibit to all peoples, because here it is a matter of the faithful mercy of the Lord, and of the everlasting covenant of grace, of which Christ is the witness, because he is not only numbered among the witnesses in heaven, 1 John 5:7. But he comes also by water and blood, that he might testify, not by the water of Baptism only, but also by his blood in the holy Supper, testifying concerning the grace of God, if indeed his Spirit also has always testified in the word in the Prophets and Apostles, and he himself willed to emit blood and water from his opened side on the cross, so that he might acquire that grace, and confirm it for us, and deign to testify through water in Baptism, through blood in the Holy Eucharist, so that he may render us partakers of that grace, and seal the same in us, 1 John 5:6, 8. Nor indeed is he a witness only by his doctrine, but also by his blood and his death. Concerning which Brentius beautifully says: He who gives testimony in a controversy between a plaintiff and a defendant, he is as it were the mediator of the controversy, according to whose words judgment is accustomed to be rendered. In what controversy, therefore, does Christ the Son of God give testimony? In that, namely, which God has against man on account of sin. For God, although he holds sin in hatred, and judges that sin must be punished with eternal torment, nevertheless promises to the peoples the forgiveness of sin, and swears even now that he does not will the death of the sinner, but rather that he be converted and live. And because the severity of the wrath of God against sin is so great, as the Law and punishments indicate, that it is not easily believed by God promising the remission of his wrath and the free forgiveness of sin, therefore he brings forward as a witness his only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, so that we may judge according to his words concerning the will of God. Wherefore the Son of God has testified to this clement and merciful will of God toward us, not only by his Gospel, but also by his blood and his death. I descended (he says) from heaven, not to do what I will, but what he wills, who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, the Father, that I should lose nothing of all that he has given me, but raise it up on the last day. And this is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, etc. And elsewhere: Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. Who now would not give credence to such a witness, confirming his words even with miracles? Who henceforth would doubt concerning God's benevolent will toward him? If sins, if afflictions, if the terrors of hell threaten destruction, you have Christ the Son of God, who testifies by his Gospel, by his miracles, by his blood, by his death and his resurrection that God the Father is appeased, forgives sins, saves in death, and gives eternal righteousness and salvation. Wherefore you have nothing more to fear and tremble at, but only this effort must be applied, that you give certain and firm faith to this witness, who can deceive no one, and obey his calling. B. Luther notes the emphasis in the word witness. Hitherto, he says, he has exhorted the Jews. Now he says this mercy is to be propagated to the ends of the earth: Not only you Jews shall be enriched, but nations also. Therefore this new covenant will extend more widely than the old. Moreover, there is emphasis in the word Witness. For a witness is one who speaks. Therefore, because Christ will reign among the peoples, being placed as a witness, he will reign through testimony, that is, through the preaching of the Gospel. Thus all things are gathered into the word and not into present things. This is Blessed Luther's view. Next, Christ is called נגיד, which they interpret as Leader or Prince. And because נגד in Hebrew signifies to demonstrate or to report, as Brentius again says, Christ seems here to be called Nagid from the leadership of the word and the principate of doctrine. For just as Christ was placed by God the Father as a witness of His will toward the human race, so also He was placed as a leader of the word and a prince of doctrine, so that among all Prophets and Apostles, Doctors and preachers, Christ may be the supreme head and standard-bearer, from whom all others may seek their doctrine, and to whose doctrine they may refer themselves. Therefore, what the Prophets before Christ and the Apostles after Christ preached, so that the Church might be built upon the foundation (as Paul says) of the Apostles and Prophets, with Jesus Christ himself as the chief cornerstone.

Thirdly, he is called מצוה, which signifies a preceptor or Commander, namely, not some simple teacher whose doctrine you may either acknowledge or reject, as you please, but such a one whose precepts or commands it is necessary to grasp, and whom not only Moses, but also the heavenly Father himself, commanded with a manifest voice to be heard, and consecrated as Commander. Moses says: The Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet from your nation and from your brothers, like me; YOU SHALL LISTEN TO HIM. The heavenly Father says: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: LISTEN TO HIM. But Christ himself also, when he was sending out his disciples, clearly signifies that he was divinely consecrated as such a Commander, whose commands all nations ought to keep. All power, he says, has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Going therefore, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to keep ALL things that I HAVE COMMANDED you. To this effect is the translation of Jonathan: Behold, I have appointed him as a Prince to the peoples, a King and Lord of all kingdoms. And what is found in R. Moses Hadarschan on Gen. 49 in Bereschith Rabba: And to him shall be the gathering of the people: For all peoples or nations shall gather themselves to him, that is, to the King Messiah, as it is said in Isa. 11:10. The root of Jesse, which stands as a sign for the peoples, and to him the nations shall seek. R. Chanina said, the King Messiah is not to come except to give precepts to the nations of the world. R. Rachmon said, and thus it says (Isa. 55:4): Behold, I have given him as a witness to the people, a leader and preceptor to the nations.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ECCE TESTEM POPULIS DEDI EUM] Jeremiam, cujus Prophetiæ adeo definitæ certum dabunt meæ providentiæ Testimonium apud omnes populos.

DUCEM AC PRÆCEPTOREM GENTIBUS] Ducis est anteire cæteris.

Quid de glossa hac habendum, è jam dictis constat. Detestanda est illustris Prophetiæ depra- vatio. Non enim Jeremias, sed Christus est ille testis populorum, & Dux ac Præceptor gentium. Elo- gia illa augustiora sunt, quam ut Jeremiæ conve- niant: Christo vere propria. Quem Deus dedit TESTEM populis: ipse est μάρτυς ὁ πιστὸς testis fidus, Apoc. 1. v. 5. cap. 3. v. 14. & profitetur de sese Joh. 18. v. 37. Ego ad hoc natus sum, & ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam verita- ti; ipse datus est in fœdus populo, Es. 42. v. 7. c. 49. idem testis, non tantum ratione providentiæ, sed ratione gratiæ & misericordiæ, quam omnibus po- pulis exhibere vult, quia hic agitur de miseri- cordia Domini fideli, & de gratiæ fœdere sempi- terno, cujus testis Christus est, quia non tantum testibus in cœlis accensetur 1. Joh. 5. v. 7. Sed ve- nit etiam per aquam & sanguinem, ut testaretur, non per aquam tantum Baptismi, sed etiam per san- guinem suum in sacra Cœna testificans de gratia Dei, siquidem & Spiritus ejus in verbo semper te- status sit in Prophetis & Apostolis, & sanguinem atque aquam ipse ex aperto latere suo in cruce e- mittere voluerit, ut gratiam illam acquireret, & firmaret nobis, & per aquam in Baptismo, per sanguinem in S. Eucharistia testari dignetur, ut gra- tiæ illius nos participes reddat, eandemq; in nobis obsignet, 1. Joh. 5. v. 6. 8. Nec vero testis tantum est doctrina sua, sed etiam sanguine, & morte sua. Quo de pulcre Brentius: Qui testimonium dicit in con- troversia inter actorem & reum, is controversiæ qua- si mediator, secundum cujus dicta judicium ferri so- let. In qua ergo controversia testimonium dicit Christus filius Dei? In ea videlicet, quam Deus habet adversus hominem propter peccatum. Deus enim etsi odio habet peccatum, & judicat peccatum puniendum esse æterno supplicio, tamen promittit po- pulis condonationem peccati, & jurat etiamnum, quod non velit mortem peccatoris, sed magis ut con- vertatur & vivat. Et quia tanta est severitas iræ Dei adversus peccatum, quemadmodum Lex & sup- plicia indicant, ut non facile credatur Deo promit- tenti remissionem iræ suæ, & gratuitam condonatio- nem peccati, idcirco producit in testem unigenitum Filium suum Jesum Christum, ut secundum hujus dicta de voluntate Dei judicemus. Quare Filius Dei testificatus est hanc clementem & misericordem Dei voluntatem erga nos, non solum Evangelio suo, ve- rum etiam sanguine & morte sua. Descendi (in- quit) de cœlo, ut faciam non quod ego volo, sed quod vultis, qui misit me. Hæc autem est vo- luntas ejus, qui misit me Patris, ne perdam ex omnibus, quæ dedit mihi, sed resuscitem illa in novissimo die. Et hæc est voluntas ejus, qui mi- sit me, ut omnis, qui videt filium & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam, &c. Et alias: Noli ti- mere pusille grex, quia complacitum est Patri ve- stro dare vobis regnum. Quis nunc tanto testi, dicta sua etiam miraculis confirmanti, non adhiberet fi- dem? Quis deinceps de benigna Dei erga se voluntate dubitaret? Si peccata, si afflictiones, si terrores infer- ni minantur exitium, habes Christum Filium Dei, qui testificatur Evangelio suo, miraculis suis, san- guine suo, morte sua & resurrectione sua Deum Patrem esse placatum, condonare peccata, servare in morte, & dare æternam justitiam ac salutem. Quare nihil amplius habes, quod metuas, ac tre- pides, sed tantum in hoc studium incumbendum est, ut huic testi, qui neminem fallere potest, cer- tam ac firmam fidem adhibeas, & vocationi ejus obedias. B. Lutherus emphasin notat in voce testis. Hactenus, inquit, Judæos exhortatus est. Jam dicit propagandam misericordiam hanc in fines terræ: Non solum vos Judæi impinguabimini, sed gentes etiam. Ergo latius patebit hoc pactum novum quam vetus. Est autem emphasis in vocabulo Te- stis. Testis enim est, qui loquitur. Ergo Christus quia regnabit in populis, positus in testem, regnabit per testimonium, id est, per prædicationem Evange- lii. Ita omnia colliguntur in verbum & non in res præsentes. Hoc B. Lutherus. Deinde vocatur Christus נגיד quod interpretantur Ducem, seu Prin- cipem. Et quia נגד Hebræis significat demonstrare aut referre, ut iterum Brentius, videtur Christus hîc dici Nagid à ducatu verbi & principatu doctrinæ. Sicut enim Christus positus est à Deo Patre in testem voluntatis suæ erga humanum genus, ita etiam posi- tus est in ducem verbi & principem doctrinæ, ut inter omnes Prophetas & Apostolos, Doctores & concionatores, Christus sit supremum caput, & ante- signanus, ex quo omnes alii doctrinam suam petant, & ad cujus doctrinam sese referant. Itaq́; quod Pro- phetæ ante Christum, Apostoli post Christum prædi- caverunt, ut Ecclesia superstructa sit super funda- mentum (quemadmodum Paulus ait) Apostolorum & Prophetarum, summo angulari lapide ipso Je- su Christo.

Tertio vocatur מצוה, quod significat præce- ptorem seu Imperatorem, videlicet, non simplicem quendam doctorem, cujus doctrinam sive agno- scas, seu rejicias, juxta referat, sed talem, cujus præcepta seu imperata capessas, necesse est, & quem non Moses tantum, sed etiam Pater ipse cœlestis, manifesta voce audiendum mandavit, & in Imperatorem consecravit. Moses dicit: Prophe- tam de gente tua & de fratribus tuis, sicut me, su- scitabit tibi Dominus Deus tuus, IPSUM AU- DIES. Pater cœlestis dicit; Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacitum est: HUNC AUDITE. Sed & Christus ipse, cum amandaret discipulos suos, clare significat, se esse divinitus in talem Imperatorem consecratum, cujus jussa omnes gentes servare debeant. Data, inquit, est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo & in terra. Euntes ergo docete omnes gentes, baptisantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filii & Spiritus Sancti, docentes eos servare O- MNIA, quæ PRÆCEPI vobis. Quo facit trans- latio Jonathan: Ecce Principem populis prefeci eum, Regem & Dominum omnium regnorum. Et quod habetur apud R. Mosen Hadarschan ad Ge- nes. 49. in Bereschith Rabba: Et ipsi congregatio populi: Omnes enim populi seu gentes congregabunt se ad eum, id est, ad Regem Messiam, sicut dici- tur Esa. 11. v. 10. Radix Isai, quæ stat in signum po- pulorum, & ad eum gentes studebunt. Dixit R. Chanina, Rex Messias non venturus est, nisi ad dandum præcepta gentibus sæculi. Dixit R. Rach- mon, & sic dicit (Esa. 55, 4.) Ecce testem populo dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus.

## 55:5
Verse 5.

BEHOLD THE NATION WHICH YOU DID NOT KNOW, YOU SHALL CALL] You, O Judea, shall call upon nations previously known to you in a friendly manner,

AND NATIONS WHICH HAVE NOT KNOWN YOU, SHALL RUN TO YOU] They shall come, so that they may invoke the true God in the precinct of the Temple destined for pious nations.

BECAUSE OF THE LORD YOUR GOD AND THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL, BECAUSE HE HAS GLORIFIED YOU] They shall come, stirred by the fame of the great benefits which God has bestowed upon you.

Grotius could have learned that Judea is not being addressed here from the pronouns, which are of the masculine, not the feminine gender, and from Musculus, whom he otherwise, as it appears, followed, who had warned of this: This verse is explained in two ways. Some more recent writers refer it to the Church of Zion, which the Hebrew Kimchi also does: Jerome, however, Lyranus, and some of the more recent ones refer it to Christ, who was mentioned in the preceding verse. This latter sense seems to me more probable for the reason that in the Hebrew all these words תדק, תרו, ידעוך, אליך, אלהיך are placed not in the feminine, but in the masculine gender. It is certain that the Prophet himself is speaking here, since he has hitherto introduced God as speaking. But if he were speaking to Zion, he would use the form which he used in the preceding chapter in the feminine gender: or at least that which he uses in this chapter in the plural number. But since he speaks in the singular, and in the masculine gender, I think that by apostrophe he is addressing Christ the Lord, and is congratulating Him, on the occasion of the preceding oracle of God, in which He is recorded as having been given as a witness, leader, and preceptor to the לאמים, that is, to the peoples, nations, and gentiles, upon the accession of the nations and the fulfillment of this oracle. God said, Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and preceptor to the peoples; the Prophet, for the sake of both declaring this and congratulating Christ himself, having turned in the Spirit to Him, adds, Behold the nation, that is, the nations (so that the singular is placed for the plural), which you did not know, you shall call; and nations which have not known you shall run to you. Those whom the Lord called לאמים, the Prophet calls גוי, that is, nations. Nor does he speak of some and others, whom Christ might have called at one time, and others who might have appeared without being called: but he speaks simply in this sense: Behold the nations, which you did not know, and which in turn did not know you, you shall call to yourself: and they, as soon as they have been called, shall run to you. This sense is plain. Christ called the nations to himself, not indeed in his own person, but through the Apostles: whom he sent out into the whole world for this reason, that through the preaching of the Gospel they might call all nations to the communion of his grace. This is Musculus. Blessed Brentius and Osiander wish the Apostolic assembly to be addressed: You, Apostolic assembly, shall gather by the preaching of the commands, or of the Gospel of this Commander, into the Church not only the Jews, but also external nations, which you have not known until now, and which have not known you. These shall hasten to you, because of the Lord your God, and because of the Holy One of Israel, that is, because of Christ, because he has adorned you, namely, not only with the office of preaching the Gospel, but also with the gift of performing miracles. Neither explanation is inconvenient: but Grotius's view is repugnant both to the letter of the text and to the whole Prophetic treatment, because this is not about Judea or a material temple: nor does that description admit this gloss: Nations which have not known you, and which you did not know: for neither were the nations ignorant of Jerusalem, nor were the nations unknown to the Jews, among whom they had stayed in captivity.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ECCE GENTEM QUAM NESCIEBAS, VO- CABIS] Tu, ô Judæa, gentes ante tibi cognitas amice compellabis,

ET GENTES QUÆ TE NON COGNOVE- RUNT, AD TE CURRENT] Venient, ut in Templi ambitu gentibus piis destinato Deum verum invocent.

PROPTER DOMINUM DEUM TUUM ET SANCTUM ISRAEL, QUIA GLORIFICAVIT TE] Venient illi exciti fama beneficiorum magnorum, quæ Deus tibi præstitit.

Judæam hic non compellari, discere poterat Grotius è pronominibus, quæ masculini, non fœ- minini generis sunt, & è Musculo, quem alias, ut apparet, sequutus est, qui de eo monuerat: Bifa- riam hic versus exponitur. Referunt eum recentiores aliqui ad Ecclesiam Sionis, quod & Kimchi E- bræus facit: Hieronymus vero, Lyranus, & quidam ex recentioribus referunt eum ad Christum, cujus in præ- cedenti versu facta est mentio. Posterior hic sensus mihi propterea videtur probabilior, quod in Hebræo hæc o- mnia תדק, תרו, ידעוך, אליך, אלהיך, non in fæminino, sed in masculino genere sunt posita. Cer- tum est loqui hic Prophetam ipsum, cum hactenus Deum loquentem introduxerit. Quod si ad Sionem loqueretur, uteretur ea forma, quæ usus est capite præcedente in genere fæminino: vel certe qua hoc ca- pite in numero plurali utitur. Cum autem loquatur in singulari, idque genere masculino, existimo eum per apostropham Christum Dominum alloqui, illique per occasionem præcedentis oraculi Dei, in quo te- stis, dux & præceptor לאמים, id est, populis, na- tionibus, & gentibus datus memoratur, accessionem gentium, & oraculi hujus adimpletionem gratula- ri. Dixit Deus, ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem populis; Propheta & de- clarandi hujus, & gratulandi gratia ad ipsum Chri- stumin Spiritu conversus subjungit, Ecce gentem, id est, gentes, (ut sit singulare positum pro plurali) quam nesciebas, vocabis; & gentes, quæ te non no- verunt, ad te current. Quas Dominus vocavit לאמים vocat Propheta גוי, id est, gentes. Nec de aliis at- que aliis loquitur, quarum alias Christus vocarit, aliæ non vocatæ occurrerint: sed simpliciter hoc sensu lo- quitur: Ecce gentes, quas nesciebas, & quæ te vi- cissim nesciebant, vocabis ad te: & illæ mox, at- que vocatæ fuerint, ad te current. Planus est hic sensus. Vocavit ad se gentes Christus, haud quidem in sua ipsius persona, verum per Apostolos: quos hanc ob causam in totum orbem emisit, ut per Evan- gelii prædicationem omnes gentes ad communicatio- nem gratiæ suæ vocarent. Hæc Musculus. B. Brentius, & Osiander volunt compellari Apostolicum cœ- tum: Tu Apostolicæ cœtus congregabis prædicatione mandatorum, seu Evangelii hujus Imperatoris in Ec- clesiam non Judæos tantum, verum etiam externas gen- tes, quas nec tu hactenus novisti, & quæ nec te nove- runt. Hæ properabunt ad te, propter Dominum Deum tuum, & propter Sanctum Israëlis, hoc est, propter Christum, quia decoravit te, videlicet non tantum officio prædicandi Evangelii, sed etiam dono edendorum miraculorum. Neutra explicatio incon- veniens est: Grotii vero & literæ textus, & toti tractationi Propheticæ repugnat, quia non agitur hic de Judæa aut templo materiali: neque illa de- scriptio hanc glossam admittit: Gentes quæ te non noverunt, & quas nesciebas: nam neque gentes ignorabant Hierosolymam, neque Judæis ignotæ erant gentes, inter quas in captivitate moratæ sunt.

## 55:6
Verse 6.

SEEK THE LORD WHILE HE MAY BE FOUND: CALL UPON HIM WHILE HE IS NEAR] Here God continues to exhort those from among the nations who are not yet converted to repentance, mixing promises with threats. Rabbi Aben Ezra says that God can be found everywhere and at any time, before the sealing of the decrees. The sealing of the decrees is called by the Hebrews that time when conditional decrees concerning the cutting off of some nation, on account of their long-standing stubbornness, pass into absolute ones: which they also call the full measure of judgment. See what we have said at Luke 19, verse 44.

This exhortation is not directed to the nations not yet converted, because nations not yet converted do not seek the Lord, nor do they call upon him, Isa. 65, verse 1. Nor is it said that he can be found and is near in such a way that temporal judgments have not yet been sealed, but that the covenant and mercy, of which he had treated, still endure; and therefore temporal punishments are not in view, with respect to which, if decrees are sometimes absolute, there is nevertheless no absolute rejection of anyone from eternal grace, but that a return to the Lord lies open to him. Therefore more correctly it is held to be a general exhortation, or if it is to be determined specifically, it pertains to the Jews. B. Luther accepted it in a general sense, who observes that threats are joined to the exhortation: as if to say, I have preached to you the benefits of the Gospel; if your own utility does not move you, let at least the danger and inconveniences which will rush upon you move you. For if you do not now receive the word, it will come to pass that it will be taken away from you, and afterwards all your efforts will be in vain. You will seek and will not find, you will call and no one will hear you. Thus also Brentius: He said that not only the Jews, but also the Gentiles are called to the Church by Apostolic preaching. He adds, therefore, now the Apostolic sermon, by which they are called to repentance and to the faith of the Gospel, not so much the contemporaries of Isaiah, who first heard this sermon, and the contemporaries of the Apostles, as men of all ages, whether they were before or after the coming of Christ in the flesh. For it is a general exhortation, which is customary for the Prophets and Apostles, and which ought always to resound in the Church. To this end, the Chaldean takes the time in which God is present and in which He can be found as the time of this life. Jerome understands it specifically concerning the Jews. Because, therefore, you were unwilling to receive the everlasting covenant and the faithful mercies of David, which the multitude of the Gentiles received when you were unwilling to accept them, I, the Prophet, warn you, my countrymen, and I testify: while there is time, repent. Turn to Him who now speaks to you through the Prophets, who is later to speak in person. Seek Him while He can be found, while you are in the body, while a place for repentance is given: and seek Him not by place, but by faith.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

QUÆRITE DOMINUM DUM INVENIRI PO- TEST: INVOCATE EUM DUM PROPE EST] Hic pergit Deus eos, qui ex gentibus nondum conversi sunt, ad resipiscentiam hortari, promissa minis miscendo. Aï Ab- benesdra Deum inveniri posse ubiq; & quovis tempore, an- te obsignationem decretorum. Obsignatio decretorum He- bræis dicitur tempus illud, cum conditionata decreta de gente aliqua exscindenda, propter longam eorum contu- maciam, transeunt in absoluta: quod & mensuram judicii completam vocant. Vide quæ diximus ad Lucam 19. v. 44.

Non dirigitur hæc exhortatio ad gentes non- dum conversas, quia gentes nondum conversæ non quærunt Dominum, nec invocant eum, Esa. 65. v. 1. Neque dicitur inveniri posse, ac prope esse ea modo ratione, quod nondum obsignata sint judicia temporalia, sed quod fœdus & miseri- cordia, de qua egerat, adhuc duret; ideoque non spectantur temporales pœnæ, quarum respectu si absoluta quandoque decreta sunt, non tamen ab- soluta ullius est ab æterna gratia rejectio, quin re- ditus ipsi pateat ad Dominum. Ideo rectius pro generali habetur exhortatione, aut si specialiter de- terminanda, ad Judæos pertinet. Generali sensu accepit B. Lutherus, qui exhortationi minas ad- junctas observat: q. d. prædicavi vobis commoda Evangelii, an si vos non movet vestra utilitas, mo- veat saltem periculum & incommoda, quæ in vos ingruent. Si enim verbum jam non susceperitis, fiet ut à vobis auferatur, post frustra erunt omnia vestra studia. Quæretis & non invenietis, invoca- bitis & nemo exaudiet vos. Sic & Brentius: Dixit non Judæos tantum, sed etiam gentes Apostolica præ- dicatione ad Ecclesiam vocari. Addit igitur nunc Apostolicam concionem, qua vocantur ad pœniten- tiam & ad fidem Evangelii, non tam coætanei Esaiæ, qui primi hanc concionem audiverunt, & coætanei Apostolorum, quam homines omnium seculorum, si- ve fuerint ante, sive post adventum Christi in car- nem. Est enim generalis cohortatio, quæ usitata est Prophetis & Apostolis, & quæ semper in Ecclesia so- nare debet. Quo facit quod Chaldæus tempus, quo Deus præsto est & quo inveniri potest, accepit pro tempore hujus vitæ. De Judæis speciatim intelligit Hieronymus. Quia igitur noluistis pactum recipe- re sempiternum & misericordias David fideles, quas vobis nolentibus suscipere, suscepit turba gentium, moneo vos populares ego Propheta, atque contestor: dum tempus est, agite pœnitentiam. Conver- timini ad eum, qui vobis nunc loquitur per Pro- phetas, qui postea loquuturus est præsens.
