Quæ- rite eum dum inveniri potest, dum estis in corpore, dum datur locus pœnitentiæ: & quærite non loco, sed fide.

## 55:8
Verse 8.

FOR MY THOUGHTS ARE NOT YOUR THOUGHTS] You are difficult in forgetting injuries: I am prompt to forgive. For this coheres with that which preceded.

Although these things are explained by some concerning the thoughts and ways of God as being as different as heaven from earth from the thoughts of the wicked and the ways of the impious, as for instance by Sanctius and others, they must nevertheless undoubtedly be accepted more generally; because a reason is rendered here for divine mercy and indulgence, namely that in all things the thoughts and ways of the Lord differ from the thoughts and ways of men, or even of the Israelites with whom this discourse is held, as much as heaven from earth; and specifically in the promptness of forgiveness; concerning which it had been said in verse 7: since He (the Lord) is abundant in forgiving, just as also in Psalm 103, verse 11, the mercy of the Lord is celebrated: For according to the height of the heaven from the earth, He has strengthened His mercy over those who fear Him. Thus Fulgentius, Epistle 3 to Venantius, chapter 3: If our God is merciful, He can dismiss all sins: It is not perfect goodness from which all malice is not overcome. For God, when offended, is not like a man who breathes threats and vengeance against the offender; but His mercy and indulgence contend with our offense (Romans 5, verse 20). You are men (the Paraphrase of Cyril of Alexandria, book 5 on Isaiah, has this at this place), I am God. Therefore the interval is immense, and the things that are of God are altogether incomparable. For He overcomes in strength, glory, and clemency; nor is there anything in the nature of things that seems to equal or even to approach His excellence. For men are devoid of anger: but this is inherent in the sum of all nature, that anger is not overcome. Man is sharp and prone to wickedness: but God is good by nature, or rather, He is goodness itself, αὐτόχρημα τὸ ἀγαθὸν. He forgives, therefore, as God, and will justify the impious, burying the lapses of ignorance in oblivion and wiping away the filth of error.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NON ENIM COGITATIONES MEÆ COGI- TATIONES VESTRÆ] Vos difficiles estis ad obliviscen- das injurias: ego promptus ad ignoscendum. Cohæret enim hoc ad id quod præcessit.

Hæc etsi à nonnullis de cogitationibus & viis Dei sanctis toto cœlo diversis à cogitationibus iniqui, & viis impii explicentur, utpote à Sanctio, & a- liis, generalius tamen sine dubio accipienda; quod ratio hic reddatur divinæ miserationis & indulgen- tiæ, quod nempe in omnibus cogitata & viæ Domi- ni tantum à cogitatis & à viis hominum, vel Israë- litarum etiam, cum quibus hic sermo est, distent, quantum cœlum à terra; & speciatim in promtitu- dine condonationis; qua de v. 7. dictum erat: quo- niam multus est (Dominus) ad ignoscendum, quem- admodum & Psal. 103. v. 11. misericordia Domini ce- lebratur: Quoniam secundum altitudinem cœli à ter- ra corroboravit misericordiam suam super timentes se. Ita Fulgent. Epist. 3. ad Venant. cap. 3. Si misericors est Deus noster, universa potest peccata di- mittere: Non est perfecta bonitas, à qua non omnis malitia vincitur. Deus enim offensus non est ut ho- mo, qui in offendentem spirat minas & vindictam; sed cum offensa nostra certat ejus misericordia & in- dulgentia (Roman. 5. v. 20.) Vos homines estis (ha- bet Cyrilli Alexand. Paraphrasis lib. 5. in Esa. ad h. l.) ego Deus. Ergo immensum est intervallum, & quæ Dei sunt, omnino sunt incomparabilia. Vincit enim fortitudine, gloria, clementia; nec est quic- quam in rerum natura, quod excellentiam adæquare, aut prope etiam accedere videatur. Homines enim ira vacant: at hoc omnium summæ naturæ inest, ut ira non vincatur. Acer homo, & pronus in nequi- tiam: at bonus natura Deus, imo potius ipsissima bo- nitas, αὐτόχρημα τὸ ἀγαθὸν. Remittit ergo ut Deus, & justificabit impium, ignorantiæ lapsus obli- vione obruens, & erroris sordes delens.

## 55:9
Verse 9.

AS THE HEAVENS ARE EXALTED ABOVE THE EARTH, SO ARE MY WAYS EXALTED ABOVE YOUR WAYS] The more sublime I am, the more merciful I am also.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SICUT EXALTANTUR COELI A TERRA, SIC EXALTATÆ SUNT VIÆ MEÆ A VIIS VE- STRIS] Quanto sum sublimior, tanto & clementior,

## 55:10
Verse 10.

AND AS THE RAIN AND THE SNOW DESCEND FROM HEAVEN, AND DO NOT RETURN THITHER ANY MORE] It does not lack effect.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET QUOMODO DESCENDIT IMBER ET NIX DE COELO, ET ILLUC ULTRA NON RE- VERTITUR] Non caret effectu.

## 55:11
Verse 11.

SO SHALL MY WORD BE THAT SHALL GO FORTH FROM MY MOUTH] Any promise of mine.

IT SHALL NOT RETURN TO ME VOID] That is, it shall not be made void, provided, of course, its conditions are met. A simile taken from an envoy who could not carry out the commands given to him.

BUT IT SHALL DO WHATEVER I HAVE WILLED] This is a metonymy. For the promise is attributed to that which is of the one promising.

AND IT SHALL PROSPER IN THE THINGS FOR WHICH I SENT IT] What I have said shall come to pass.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

SIC VERBUM MEUM QUOD EGREDIETUR DE ORE MEO] Promissum quodvis meum.

NON REVERTETUR AD ME VACUUM] Id est, non fiet irritum, sub suis scilicet conditionibus. Simi- litudo sumta à Legato, qui sibi mandata efficere non po- tuit.

SED FACIET QUÆCUNQUE VOLUI] Est me- tonymia. Nam promissio tribuitur id, quod est promittentis.

ET PROSPERABITUR IN HIS, AD QUÆ MISI ILLUD] Quæ dixi, evenient.

## 55:12
Vers. 12.

FOR YOU SHALL GO OUT IN JOY] You would translate that כִּי more correctly as 'therefore'. The sense is: since the constancy of my promises is so great, do not doubt, O Jews, that you shall go out from exile happily and with joy.

THE MOUNTAINS AND THE HILLS SHALL SING PRAISE BEFORE YOU] They shall echo your hymns.

AND ALL THE TREES OF THE FIELD SHALL CLAP THEIR HANDS] The trees, stirred by gentle winds, shall clap with their branches as if they were arms.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QUIA IN LÆTITIA EGREDIEMINI] Illud כִּי rectius vertas propterea. Sensus est: quandoquidem tanta est promissorum meorum constantia, nolite dubitare Judæi, quin de exsilio exituri sitis feliciter, & cum gaudio.

MONTES ET COLLES CANTABUNT CO- RAM VOBIS LAUDEM] Hymnos vestros resonabunt.

ET OMNIA LIGNA REGIONIS PLAUDENT MANU] Lenibus ventis agitatæ arbores ramis suis, quasi brachiis, plaudent.

## 55:13
Vers. 13.

INSTEAD OF THE BRIAR] The Greeks here have a̓ntì stoibh͂s, Στοιϐoì, which is also Φλεως, a marsh grass, which Theophrastus, Pliny, and Aristophanes in the Frogs mention. Aquila and Theodotion had κόνυζαν here, which the LXX have in the following verses. This interpreter translated the Hebrew word as 'thickets' here, as he did above at 7:19.

THE FIR TREE SHALL COME UP] There is here in the Hebrew בְּרוֹשׁ, which we also had above at 41:19, where this interpreter and the Chaldean likewise translated it as 'fir tree'. The Greeks there have 'myrtle', here 'cypress'.

AND INSTEAD OF THE NETTLE] The interpreter followed Symmachus in this place, as Jerome teaches us. For the LXX have κόνυζαν here. R. Abraham and R. David Kimchi hold it to be a type of thorn.

THE MYRTLE SHALL GROW] So also the LXX. And the Hebrews do not differ, when they explain the name Hadassah, which was given to Esther. The sense of this passage is: where harmful or useless weeds were growing due to a lack of cultivators, there trees excellent for use or pleasure shall be planted. The Chaldean takes it allegorically, that pious men shall succeed the wicked.

AND THE LORD SHALL BE NAMED FOR AN ETERNAL SIGN, WHICH SHALL NOT BE TAKEN AWAY] That is, these things being seen, the name of God shall be celebrated perpetually.

There is nothing here about the departure from Babylon, which neither the preceding nor the following context indicates. Nor about the growth of herbs in places previously deserted: But the spiritual fruit of the Gospel, about which the Prophet has preached throughout this whole chapter, is adumbrated. Since he had previously taught that the word of the Lord would not return empty. Our Brentius says, he has recounted here various kinds of fruits; which the rain of the Gospel, concerning the gratuitous mercy of God through Christ, is accustomed to bring forth. YOU SHALL GO OUT WITH JOY. Just as once Moses led out and liberated the Israelites from Egyptian tyranny, so now Christ leads out and liberates his Church by the Gospel from the tyranny of Satan, sin, death, and hell. Which liberation brings true and eternal joy. Which is also the explanation of the blessed Luther: According to the kind of fruit YOU SHALL BE LED FORTH IN PEACE: The Gospel not only leads the Church out from the chains of Satan, but also leads it forth in peace, renders it tranquil, and places it in safety, so that no hardship, no affliction, no death, no horror of hell may remain. A public applause is added concerning this leading forth: THE MOUNTAINS AND HILLS SHALL SING PRAISE BEFORE YOU, i.e., such will be the joy and congratulation, when the nations come from idols and the worship of demons to Christ, that the mountains and hills will seem to leap, exult, and applaud these things. The Dutch paraphrasts say this is the meaning, that all creatures will be promoting that work with congratulation. Brentius and Osiander refer it to the applause of creatures, when we are asserted into the liberty of the sons of God. But The former explanation seems simpler to us, which the Weimar Paraphrasts also followed. And the interpretation of the blessed Luther also tends toward this, because the mountains and hills seem to us to sing even in the very bodily temptation on account of joy in the spirit. Another fruit follows, INSTEAD OF THE BRIAR SHALL COME UP THE FIR TREE: AND INSTEAD OF THE NETTLE SHALL GROW THE MYRTLE. Jerome must be heard here, who, after he had brought forward some things concerning the names and their diverse exposition, says: however the propriety of the names may be, this must be said, that evils are turned into goods: and instead of vices, virtues are born, that is, instead of iniquity, justice: instead of rashness, fortitude: instead of luxury, temperance, instead of folly, prudence. Let us give examples of our elders. Matthew and Zacchaeus and the publicans were briars: and 5006n, and useless stocks, and novi?n of bitter taste, and most foul odor, saying: My scars have rotted and are corrupted from the face of my foolishness. These, suddenly changed into Apostles, were made a cypress and a fir tree, and a myrtle, of the best odor: and necessary for various works. Paul also, the persecutor of the Church, when he heard from the Lord: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? it is hard for you to kick against the goad: he was a nettle, having the stings of persecution. But when he preached the Gospel in the whole world, and could say: We are the good odor of Christ, he is rightly called a cypress and a myrtle. Harlots and publicans go before the Pharisees into the kingdom of God: and the thief from the cross passes into Paradise. Add Gregory the Great. Instead of the briar the fir tree comes up, while in the heart of the Saints, instead of the abjection of earthly thought, the height of heavenly contemplation arises. The nettle indeed is of an altogether fiery nature, but the myrtle is said to be of a tempering virtue. Therefore, instead of the nettle, the myrtle grows, when the minds of the just arrive from the itch and heat of vices to the temperance and tranquility of thoughts, while they no longer desire earthly things, while they extinguish the flames of the flesh with heavenly desires. The Chaldean himself has grasped the mind of the Prophet more correctly than Grotius; that pious men would succeed the impious.

The newest fruit of the Gospel is proposed thus in Hebrew: AND IT SHALL BE TO THE LORD FOR A NAME FOR AN ETERNAL SIGN, THAT SHALL NOT BE CUT OFF. Because the preaching of the Gospel, and the salvation of the Church, yields to the Lord for perpetual praise, and the celebration of his name, which will never have an end. The blessed Luther comments on these things thus: The name of Christ is that he is the Savior, who freely justifies and condemns our works, and gives us his works; where this name and this doctrine is, there is the sign of the presence of Christ; but this name of Christ ought to be eternal, which the gates of hell shall not eradicate. Sebastian Munster has embraced all those things succinctly: Through the word, justice and salvation are brought: and thence it happens that we go forth with joy from death, hell, and sin, into the kingdom of grace, and have joy in the spirit perpetual, and the mountains and hills seem to us to sing, etc. And so at last it will come to pass that in the Church there will not be left thorny and sterile trees, but fruitful and tall ones for the praise and glory of Christ, and as a sign that he will never be absent from his bride.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

PRO SALIUNCA] Græci hic habent a̓ntì stoibh͂s Στοιϐoì quæ & Φλεως palustris herba, cujus meminêre Theo- phrastus, Plinius, & in ranis Aristophanes. Aquila & Theo- dotio hic habebant κόνυζαν, quod in sequentibus habent LXX. vocem Hebræam idem hic interpres fruteta transtu- lit supra 7, 19.

ASCENDET ABIES] Est hic in Hebræo בְּרוֹשׁ, quam & supra habuimus 41. v. 19. ubi itidem abietem ver- tit hic interpres, & Chaldæus. Græci ibi myrtum, hic cu- pressum.

ET PRO URTICA] Secutus est hoc loco interpres Symmachum, ut nos docet Hieronymus. Nam LXX. hic κόνυζαν habent. Genus spinæ esse volunt R. Abraham, & R. David Kimchi.

CRESCET MYRTUS] Sic & LXX. Nec aliter He- bræi, ubi explicant nomen Hadassæ, quod Estheri datum. Sensus hujus loci est: ubi propter cultorum penuriam her- bæ nascebantur damnosæ aut inutiles, ibi satum iri arbores ad usum aut voluptatem egregias. Chaldæus allegorice sumit, impiis successuros viros pios.

ET ERIT DOMINUS NOMINATUS IN SI- GNUM ÆTERNUM, QUOD NON AUFERETUR] Id est, his visis Dei nomen celebrabitur perpetuo.

Nihil hic de egressu è Babylone, quem nec an- tecedentia, nec consequentia indicant. Neque de proventu herbarum in locis antea desertis: Sed fru- ctus spiritualis Evangelii, de quo concionatus est Propheta toto hocce capite adumbratur. Siqui- dem verbum Domini non reversurum vacuum, antea docuerit. Brentius noster, varia, inquit, hic recensuit fructuum genera; quos pluvia Evangelii de gratuita misericordia Dei per Christum afferre solet. EGREDIEMINI cum LÆTITIIS. Sicut olim Moses eduxit & liberavit Israëlitas Ægyptiaca tyran- nide, ita nunc Christus educit & liberat Evangelio suam Ecclesiam tyrannide Satanæ, peccati, mortis, & inferni. Quæ liberatio affert veram & æternam læti- tiam. Quæ etiam explicatio est B. Lutheri: Secun- dum genus fructus DEDUCEMINI IN PACE: Evangelium non solum educit Ecclesiam è vinculis Satanæ, verum etiam deducit eam in pace, reddit eam tranquillam, & collocat eam in tuto, ut nulla ærumna, nulla afflictio, nulla mors, nullus inferni horror super- sit. Additur applausus publicus circa hanc dedu- ctionem: MONTES ET COLLES CANTA- BUNT CORAM VOBIS LAUDEM, q. d. tanta erit lætitia & gratulatio, cum gentes ab idolis & dæmonum cultu venient ad Christum, ut montes & colles exilire, exultare, hisque applaudere videantur. Paraphrastæ Belgæ hunc sensum esse dicunt, quod omnes creaturæ sint cum gratulatione opus illud promoturæ. Brentius & Osiander referunt ad creaturarum applausum, cum adserimur in libertatem filiorum Dei. Sed nobis simplicior videtur explicatio prior, quam secuti quoque sunt Paraphrastæ Vinarienses. Et eo abit etiam B. Lutheri interpretatio, quod vi- deantur nobis cantare montes & colles etiam in ipsa corporali tentatione ob gaudium in spiritu. Sequitur alius fructus, PRO SALIUNCA ASCENDET ABIES: ET PRO URTICA CRESCET MYR- TUS. Audiendus hic Hieronymus, qui post- quam de nominibus & diversa expositione non- nulla adduxisset, utcumque, inquit, se habet nomi- num proprietas, hoc dicendum est, quod mala vertan- tur in bona: & pro vitiis nascantur virtutes, id est, pro iniquitate justitia: pro temeritate fortitudo: pro luxuria temperantia, pro stultitia prudentia. De- mus exempla majorum. Matthæus & Zacheus & publicani saliunca erant: & 5006n, & stirpes inutiles, & novi?n amari saporis, & odoris teterrimi, dicen- tes: Computruerunt & corruptæ sunt cicatrices meæ à facie insipientiæ meæ. Isti in Apostolos repen- te mutati, facti sunt cyparissus & abies, & myrtus, odoris optimi: & in varia opera necessarii. Paulus quoque persecutor Ecclesiæ, quando audiebat à Domi- no: Saule, Saule quid me persequeris: durum tibi est contra stimulum calcitrare: urtica erat, habens persecutionis aculeos. Quando autem in toto orbe Evangelium prædicavit, & dicere poterat: Christi bonus odor sumus, recte Cyparissus appellatur & myrtus. Meretrices & publicani præveniunt Phari- sæos in regno Dei: & latro de cruce transit in Pa- radisum. Adde Gregorium M. Pro saliunca ascen- dit abies, dum in Sanctorum corde pro abjectione ter- renæ cogitationis, altitudo supernæ contemplationis exoritur. Urtica vero igneæ omnino naturæ est, myr- tus autem temperativæ fertur esse virtutis. Pro urti- ca igitur crescit myrtus, cum justorum mentes à pru- rigine & ardore vitiorum, ad cogitationum tempe- riem tranquillitatemque perveniunt, dum jam terri- na non appetunt, dum flammas carnis desideriis cœ- lestibus extinguunt. Chaldæus ipse rectius assequu- tus est mentem Prophetæ, quam Grotius; impiis successuros viros pios.

Novissimus fructus Evangelii ita proponitur in Ebræo: ET ERIT HOC DOMINO IN NOMEN IN SIGNUM ÆTERNUM, QUOD NON DECIDETUR. Quia prædicatio Evange- lii, & salus Ecclesiæ cedit Domino in perpetuam laudem, & nominis ejus celebrationem, quod nullum unquam habebit finem. B. Lutherus hæc ita σχολιάζει: Nomen Christi est, quod sit Sal- vator, qui gratis justificet & damnet opera nostra, & donet nobis opera sua, ubi hoc nomen & hæc doctri- na est, ibi est signum præsentiæ Christi; debet autem hoc Christi nomen æternum esse, quod non eradicabunt portæ inferi. Complexus illa omnia succincte est Sebastianus Munsterus: Per verbum affertur justitia & salus: & inde sit, ut cum lætitia egrediamur de morte, inferno, & peccato, in regnum gratiæ, & ha- beamus gaudium in spiritu perpetuum, videanturque no- bis cantare montes & colles &c. Et ita demum fiet, ut in Ecclesia non relinquantur spinosæ, & steriles arbo- res, sed fructuosæ & proceræ in laudem, & gloriam Christi, atque in signum, quod ille nunquam deerit spon- sæ suæ.

## 56:1 Argument
ORATION IV. ON THE DUTIES OF THE REDEEMED. CHAPTER LVI.

An exhortation to judgment and justice, the observation of the Sabbath and the covenant, with a promise of grace made even to strangers: and a denunciation against blind and dumb shepherds, and Epicurean security.

Ver. 1. THUS SAYS THE LORD, KEEP JUDGMENT AND DO JUSTICE] That the nature of the promises, of which we have treated thus far, may be better understood: a warning is added to the Jews, that they themselves also should do their duty, and avoid those things on account of which such heavy punishments have come upon them. See above 1,16. 10, 1.

AND MY JUSTICE THAT IT MAY BE REVEALED] My faithfulness in fulfilling those things which can be expected from my side.

Latin:

ORATIO IV. DE OFFICIIS REDEMTORUM. CAPUT LVI.

Adhortatio ad judicium & justitiam, observa- tionem Sabbati & fœderis, cum promissio- ne gratiæ etiam advenis facta: & commi- natione adversus cæcos & mutos pastores, ac epicuream securitatem.

Vers. 1. HÆC DICIT DOMINUS, CUSTODITE JUDICIUM ET FACITE JUSTITIAM] Ut melius intel- ligatur natura promissorum, de quibus hactenus actum est: additur monitio ad Judæos, ut ipsi quoque officium fa- ciant, & ea evitent, propter quæ tam graves pœnas in se ac- cesserunt. Vide supra 1,16. 10, 1.

ET JUSTITIA MEA UT REVELETUR] Mea fides in implendis iis, quæ a mea parte expectari possunt.

## 56:2
Ver. 2.

KEEPING THE SABBATH, LEST HE POLLUTE IT] Taking care for himself not to violate the law of the Sabbath, and other laws which could be observed in exile. For it is a species for a genus.

That the duty of the captive Jews and those established in exile is looked at here, neither appears from the preceding, nor is it signified by any indication now. The Prophet had exhorted them to receive the Gospel through faith, with the addition of the promise of the fruits of the saving word. Now he excites them to the study of holiness and piety, and promises the coming of the Messiah, and at the same time prophesies concerning the communion of proselytes and the nations with the Church. Jerome explains the coherence of the chapters thus: The prophecy of the nations having been finished, which at the coming of the Word of God are to be changed from a briar and a nettle into a cypress and a myrtle: Isaiah speaks to the hearers of that time that they should do all things which are right and prepare themselves for the coming of the Savior: because he himself is the justice and mercy of God. The phrase 'to keep judgment and do justice,' when it occurs regarding the office of a Magistrate, denotes punishing and restraining the wicked, lest they harm the good, and defending the good and approving the justice of their cause. But where it is a general admonition, 'to keep judgment and do justice' embraces obedience to the whole law, that is, to beware of things forbidden, which have an annexed penalty or curse, and to observe things to be done, which have an annexed blessing. But because there is no one who can keep the whole law, the Son of God promises his coming, inasmuch as he was to fulfill the law for us and bring salvation to us. 'Lest any of us think,' says Cyril, 'that by these words the Israelites are incited to the observation of the law, which is situated in shadows and types, for no one is justified by the law before God; he says that his Salvation and mercy are near to be revealed.' FOR MY SALVATION IS NEAR, TO COME, AND MY JUSTICE, TO BE REVEALED. For by the name of SALVATION AND JUSTICE are comprehended the benefits which the Messiah brought by his coming, as has been observed several times in this Prophet. See Ch. 42 and 49. Therefore, the same thing which Christ warned here through the Prophet, he also preached at the time of his coming in these words: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' Because in the Gospel is promised the remission of sins, justice, salvation, and eternal life, which Christ had come into the world to acquire by his death and to announce through the Gospel; whence, when he himself was approaching, justice and salvation were near, and the kingdom of heaven itself. Although seven hundred years still remained until that πλήρωμα τō χρόνō, yet that sermon ought to have sounded at all times, because the word of the Gospel, by which those goods procured by Christ are dispensed, was near to the people and in their mouth Deut. 31, 12. Rom. 10, 8. And those who believed in Christ, at whatever time, perceived as much fruit of justice and salvation as they were to perceive if they had lived at the time when he was to come into the world. JESUS Christ yesterday, today, the same and forever. Heb. 13, 8. Therefore, it is not the faith of the promises that is indicated here by the justice of the Lord, but the eternal justice which the Lord was to bring back Dan. 9, 24, on account of which he himself is celebrated, that he is JEHOVAH our justice Jer. 23, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CUSTODIENS SABBATUM, NE POLLUAT ILLUD] Cavens sibi a violanda lege sabbati, & aliis legi- bus, quæ in exilio observari poterant. Est enim species pro genere.

Officium Judæorum captivorum & in exilio con- stitutorum hic spectari, neq; è superioribus constat, neq; ullo indicio jam significatur. Adhorta- tus erat Propheta ad suscipiendum per fidem Ev- angelium, addita promissione fructuum verbi salu- tarium. Nunc excitat ad sanctitatis & pietatis stu- dium, ac promittit Messiæ adventum, vaticinatur si- mul de proselytorum & gentium communione cum Ecclesia, Hieronymus ita capitum cohæren- tiam exponit: Gentium vaticinio terminato, quæ in adventu Sermonis Dei de saliuncula & urtica in cy- parissam, myrtumque mutandæ sunt: loquitur E- saias ad illius temporis auditores ut faciant cuncta, quæ recta sunt & parent se adventui Salvatoris: quia ipse est justitia & misericordia Dei. Phrasis custodire judicium & facere justitiam, cum de Magistratus occurrit officio, notat punire & coërcere malos, ne noceant bonis, & defendere bonos & justitiam causæ eorum approbare. Ubi autem est generalis admo- nitio, custodire judicium & facere justitiam comple- ctitur obedientiam universæ legis, h. e. cavere pro- hibita, quæ habent annexam pœnam aut maledi- ctionem, & servare facienda, quæ habent annexam benedictionem. Quia vero nemo est, qui uni- versam legem servare possit, Filius Dei promittit adventum suum, utpote qui legem pro nobis im- plere, nobisque salutem afferre debuit. Ne quis no- strûm putet, inquit Cyrillus, his verbis Israëlitas ad observationem legis, quæ in umbris nimirum & typis sita est, excitari; justificatur enim nemo in lege apud Deum, prope dicit esse Salutare suum & misericor- diam patefaciendam. QUIA JUXTA EST SALUS MEA, UT VENIAT, ET JUSTITIA MEA, UT REVELETUR. Nam SALUTIS ET JUSTITIÆ nomine comprehenduntur be- neficia, quæ Messias adventu suo attulit, ut in hoc Propheta aliquoties observatum. Videatur C. 42. & 49. Idem ergo, quod hic Christus per Prophe- tam monuit, prædicavit etiam sub adventum suum hisce verbis: pœnitentiam agite, Appropinquat enim regnum cœlorum. Quia in Evangelio promittitur remissio peccatorum, justitia, salus & vita æterna, quam ut morte sua Christus acquireret, & per Ev- angelium annunciaret, in mundum venerat; unde cum ipse appropinquaret, prope erat justitia & sa- lus, ipsumque regnum cœlorum. Etsi adhuc Septin- genti anni restabant ad illud πλήρωμα τō χρόνō, Concio tamen illa omni tempore sonare debuit, quod verbum Evangelii, quo illa bona à Christo parta dispensantur, prope erat populo & in ore ejus Deut. 31, 12. Rom. 10, 8. Et qui in Christum credidêre, quocunq; tempore, tantum fructus justitiæ & sa- lutis percepêre, quantum percepturi erant, si vixis- sent tempore, quo in mundum adventurus erat. JESUS Christus heri, hodie, idem & in secula. Ebr. 13, 8. Non ergo per justitiam Domini hic fides pro- missorum indigitatur, sed justitia æterna, quam redu- cere debuit Dominus Dan. 9, 24. ob quam ipse cele- bratur, quod sit JEHOVAH justitia nostra Jer. 23, 6.

## 56:3
Vers. 3. AND LET NOT THE SON OF THE STRANGER WHO ADHERES TO THE LORD SAY] A foreigner. But since pious foreigners were of two kinds, some who kept the precepts given to Adam and Noah, others who had subjected themselves to the whole law of Moses: the mention of the Sabbath shows that this latter kind is being dealt with here, which the Hebrews agree was not given to those of the former kind: whence also the covenant, of which mention will follow, is to be understood through Moses. Such was Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian in the times of Jeremiah.

THE LORD WILL SEPARATE ME FROM HIS PEOPLE] Such a proselyte could think that these magnificent promises pertained only to those who had their origin from Israel: and that he was excluded by them. God meets this opinion.

AND LET NOT THE EUNUCH SAY: BEHOLD I AM A DRY TREE] Thus also the Israelite eunuchs, when the law promised fertility and much offspring in prosperous circumstances to those following the law, could think that their effort would be in vain. Therefore, God says that He will compensate for what is lacking to them in this respect with other great benefits; thus no one's effort will be wasted.

Here occurs a fiction concerning a double kind of Proselytes, and concerning the precepts given to Adam and Noah, to whom Grotius dreamed, along with the Jews, that the whole law was not given, for the refuting of which there is no reason why we should linger, because he taught this by no testimony, so that it can be rejected with the same ease with which it is asserted. That the law was inscribed upon man in his primordial creation, and that all men are obligated to observe it, is so certain that this is the foundation of conscience and of thoughts, which accuse or excuse themselves, even in those who do not have the prescribed law, because the work of the law is inscribed τῇ Φύσει (by nature) in their hearts, as the Apostle testifies in 1 Cor. 2, v. 14. There were indeed two kinds of those who were converted to the faith from the Gentiles; some were joined to them only by faith, who remained in their own polity and had no need to undertake circumcision, such as, for example, Naaman the Syrian, the Ninevites, and others who learned the true religion from the exiles of Israel in the Babylonian and Persian kingdoms; others were joined not by faith alone, but by the assumption of the rights of Israelite citizens: for which right, because it was instituted by the Lord Himself, they were called those joined to the Lord: but only these latter are indicated here, and are accustomed to be called proselytes. Whence not a few interpreters refer these things to the proselytes in the time of Isaiah. However, the context of the text compels us to understand these things concerning the Gentiles, even if meanwhile we do not deny that there is an allusion to proselytes under the law, who were not admitted to public offices until the third generation, Deut. 23, who it is likely also existed among the people of God in the time of Isaiah, who, because they were somewhat abominable to the people of God, could also think that they were an abomination to God. Because just as the Prophet had dealt before with the calling of the Gentiles, so in this chapter he testifies with a resounding voice that it is also regarded, when in v. 7 he says: The Lord's house shall be called a house of prayer FOR ALL PEOPLES, which certainly cannot be restricted to proselytes. Therefore, he adds spirit and confidence to the Gentiles, that they will not have cause to say, THE LORD WILL SEPARATE ME FROM HIS PEOPLE, if indeed the house of the Lord is to be called a house of prayer for all peoples: by which saying Mr. Brentius confesses that the temple of God is opened to the Gentiles. For although, he says, this refers itself to that which is written in the prayers of Solomon in the third book of Kings, chapter eight: when the foreigner shall come, and pray in this place, you will hear in heaven in the firmament of your dwelling place, etc., nevertheless the Holy Spirit looks especially to the time of the spreading of the Gospel in the whole world, by which spreading the true temple of God was so opened to all Gentiles that as many as acknowledge Christ through faith from the Gospel, not only enter into the temple with their prayers, but even become themselves the true temple of God. You, says Paul, are the temple of the living God, just as God says, I will dwell in them, and walk among them. And other interpreters easily agree on this: therefore the Weimar paraphrasts rightly explain this promise concerning foreigners who adhere to the Lord as concerning the calling of the Gentiles: because in the New Testament the distinction between Jews and Gentiles has been abolished. But as for the eunuchs, because sterility under the Old Testament was also considered ignominious and was referred to among the curses of God, Luke 1:25, nor was it permitted for eunuchs to enter into the communion of the Lord, Deut. 23:1, the Lord promises that this will cease under the New Testament, and promises to eunuchs who keep the Sabbath, and choose those things which please the Lord, and keep the covenant of the Lord, in His house, i.e., in the Church, 1 Tim. 3:15, a certain place and an eternal name, namely that they shall be called the sons of God, John 1:12, 1 John 3:1. Just as it is promised to the Gentiles who have joined themselves to the Lord, an bringing to the holy mountain of the Lord, or communion with the Church, Gal. 4:25, Heb. 12, and participation in spiritual joy, as well as the gracious acceptance of their spiritual sacrifices.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET NON DICAT FILIUS ADVENÆ QUI ADHÆRET DOMINO] Alienigena. Cum autem pii alienigenæ duûm essent generum, alij qui præcepta Ada- mo & Noæ data servabant, alii qui toti Mosis legi se subje- cerant: de hoc posteriori genere hic agi ostendit sabbati mentio, quam illis prioris generis non esse datam consen- tiunt Hebræi: unde & fœdus cujus sequetur mentio, intel- ligendum de eo, quod per Mosen fuit publicatum. Talis fuit Jeremiæ temporibus AbdemeSignal Æthiops.

SEPARATIONE DIVIDET ME DOMINUS A POPULO SUO] Poterat cogitare talis proselytus hæc magnifica promissa ad solos eos, qui ex Israële ortum habe- rent, pertinere: ac se ab iis excludi, Huic opinioni oc- currit Deus.

ET NON DICAT EUNUCHUS: ECCE EGO LIGNUM ARIDUM] Sic & Israëlitæ Eunuchi, cum lex promitteret legem sequentibus fœcunditatem, & multam sobolem in rebus prosperis, cogitare poterant, inane fo- re suum studium. Ideo quod hac in parte ipsis deest, id aliis magnis beneficiis se compensaturum dicit Deus; ita nulli operam perituram.

Occurrit hic commentum de duplici genere Proselytorum, & de præceptis Adam & Noæ datis, quibus non universam legem datam esse cum Ju- dæis somniavit Grotius, cui refellendo non est quod immoremur, quia nullo testimonio id do- cuit, ut ea facilitate reprobari possit, qua adseritur. Legem inscriptam fuisse homini in primæva crea- tione, & ad eam observandam omnes homines ob- ligari, adeo certum est, ut hoc fundamentum sit conscientiæ & cogitationum, quæ se accusant, vel excusant, etiam in iis, qui præscriptam non habent le- gem, quia opus legis τῇ Φύσει inscriptum est in cordi- bus ipsorum, teste Apostolo 1. Cor. 2. v. 14. Dupli- cis generis quidem erant, qui ad fidem converte- bantur è gentilibus, alii adjungebantur illis tantum fide, qui in sua Politia manebant, nec opus habe- bant suscipere circumcisionem, quales verbi causa erant Naaman Syrus, Ninivitæ, & alii, qui ab exuli- bus Israëlis in regno Babylonico & Persico veram religionem didicerunt; alii non fide tantum ad- jungebantur, sed susceptione juris civium Israëliti- corum: ob quod jus, quia à Domino ipso institu- tum erat, vocabantur ipsi adjuncti Domino: sed hi solum posteriores hic indigitantur, & proselyti ap- pellari solent. Unde non pauci interpretes hæc ad proselytos tempore Esaiæ referunt. Cæterum suv- έχεια textus cogit, ut de gentilibus ea intelligamus, etsi interim non diffiteamur, alludi ad proselytos sub lege, qui non admittebantur ad publica officia, nisi in tertia generatione Deut. 23. quales in popu- lo Dei etiam fuisse tempore Esaiæ, verisimile est, qui, quod erant populo Dei nonnihil abominabi- les, etiam Deo abominationi se esse, opinari pote- rant. Quia uti de vocatione gentium antea egerat Propheta, ita in hoc capite eam etiam respici sono- ra voce testatur, cum v. 7. ait: Dominus mea domus orationis vocabitur CUNCTIS POPULIS, quæ certe restringi ad proselytos non possunt. Gen- tilibus ergo animum & fiduciam addit, quod o- pus non habituri sint dicere, SEPARATIONE DIVIDES ME A POPULO TUO, siquidem domus Domini domus orationis vocanda sit cun- stis populis: quo dicto fatetur Dn. Brentius ape- riri templum Dei gentibus. Etsi enim, inquit, hoc re- fert se ad illud, quod in precibus Salomonis tertio Re- gum octavo scribitur: cum venerit Alienigena, & oraverit in hoc loco, tu exaudies in cœlo in firma- mento habitaculi tui &c. tamen Spiritus Sanctus respicit maxime ominum in tempus divulgationis Evangelii in toto orbe terrarum, qua divulgatione verum Dei templum Gentibus omnibus ita patefa- ctum est, ut quotquot ex Evangelio Christum agno- scunt per fidem, non solum ingrediantur precibus suis in templum, verum etiam fiant ipsi verum Dei tem- plum. Vos, inquit Paulus, templum estis viventis Dei, quemadmodum dicit Deus, inhabitabo in il- lis, & inambulabo. Et consentiunt facile in eo cæteri interpretes: ideo recte paraphrastæ Vina- rienses hanc promissionem de alienigenis, qui ad- hærent Domino, de gentium vocatione explicant: quia in Novo Testamento discrimen Judæorum & gentilium sublatum est. Quod vero ad Eunuchos, quia sterilitas sub Vet. T. etiam pro ignominiosa habebatur & inter maledictiones Dei referebatur Luc. 1, 25. neque integrum erat Eunuchis ad com- municnem Domini accedere Deut. 23, 1. illud sub N.T. cessaturum promittit Dominus, ac pollicetur Eunuchis Sabbatum servantibus, & eligentibus ea, quæ placent Domino & fœdus Domini custodientibus, in domo sua, h. e. in Ecclesia, 1. Tim. 3, 15. locum certum & nomen æternum, quod scilicet filii Dei vocandi sint Joh. 1, 12. 1. Joh. 3, 1. Sicut gentibus promitti- tur, quæ se Domino adjunxerunt, adductio ad mon- tem sanctum Domini, vel communio cum Ecclesia, Gal. 4, 25. Ebr. 12. & gaudii Spiritualis participa- tio, nec non sacrificiorum ipsorum spiritualium gratiosa acceptatio.

## 56:4
Vers. 4.

AND CHOOSE THE THINGS THAT PLEASED ME] They have loved my precepts.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET ELEGERINT QUÆ EGO VOLUI] Ama- verint præcepta mea.

## 56:5
Vers. 5. A PLACE AND A NAME BETTER THAN SONS AND DAUGHTERS] In doxologies. In the temple their name will be remembered, and it will be more celebrated than if they had left offspring. We have many such doxologies in the son of Sirach. Christians imitated this by offering for the dead.

These things are not to be accepted concerning a doxology and public memory of a name in the temple of the Lord, of which nothing is found in Sacred history: for the fact that Sirach celebrates holy men has nothing to do with public doxologies and the commemoration of the names of saints in the temple, in public doxologies. Grotius invents that such a custom existed among the people of God, and asserts it without a witness, so that he may establish the Papistic oblation for the dead in the Mass, which he revealed not obscurely here. For what does such a commemoration, if it had been a precept, have in common with the oblation for the dead and the Mass-sacrifice of the Papacy for the sins of the dead and the living? Therefore, our people more rightly understand this promise here as concerning spiritual and heavenly dignity, because since eunuchs are members of Christ through faith, their names are written in heaven, in preference to those who are called sons in name only. For it is customary in the Holy Scriptures for spiritual things under the New Testament to be described by phrases taken from the things and names of the Old Testament. Since, therefore, eunuchs were excluded from dignity in the temple and the Church of Israel, the Holy Spirit promises them a place in the temple and a better name, and thus a more excellent dignity under the New Testament, above the sons and daughters of Israel, provided they have kept the Sabbath and held fast to the covenant of God, that is, have heard the Gospel and believed in Christ, whom God gave as a covenant to the nations.

Latin:

Vers. 5. LOCUM ET NOMEN MELIUS A FILIIS ET FILIABUS] In δοξολογίαις. In templo nomen ipso- rum memorabitur, eritque celebrius, quam si prolem reli- quissent. Tales δοξολογίας multas habemus apud Sirachi- den. Imitati sunt id Christiani offerentes pro mortuis.

Non de δοξολογίᾳ & memoria nominis publi- ca in templo Domini hæc accipienda, de qua nihil in historia Sacra reperitur: nam quod Syracides viros sanctos celebrat, nihil ad δοξολογίας publicas & commemorationem nominum sanctorum in templo, in δοξολογίαις publicis facit. Quam con- suetudinem in populo Dei fuisse ideo comminisci- tur, & sine teste asserit Grotius, ut Papisticam obla- tionem pro mortuis in Missa stabiliat, quod non ob- scure hic prodidit. Quid enim talis commemora- tio, si maxime præcepta fuisset, cum oblatione pro mortuis & sacrificio Missatico Papatus pro pecca- tis mortuorum & viventium affinitatis & commer- cii habet? Rectius itaq; nostri, hic promissionem intelligunt de Spirituali & cælesti dignitate, quod cum Eunuchi sint membra Christi per fidem, nomi- na eorum scripta sint in cælis, præ illis, qui nomine- tenus filii audiunt. Phrasibus enim à rebus & no- minibus V. T. desumptis res Spirituales sub N. T. describi S. Literis solemne est. Quum ergo Eunu- chi à dignitate in templo & Ecclesia Israëlis exclusi fuerint, locum in templo & nomen melius, adeoq; dignitatem præstantiorem illis sub N. T. promittit Spiritus Sanctus, præ filiis & filiabus Israëlis, mo- do servaverint Sabbatum & tenuerint fœdus Dei, hoc est, audierint Evangelium, & crediderint in Christum, quem Deus dedit in fœdus gentium.

## 56:7
Verse 7.

MY HOUSE SHALL BE CALLED A HOUSE OF PRAYER FOR ALL PEOPLES] Especially for proselytes, who were admitted with equal right with the Israelites within the τὸν θρίγχον (the barrier).

This determination concerning proselytes is added incorrectly. Because the words of the divine promise concerning ALL PEOPLES are general. And although regard is had, and an allusion is made, to the temple of the Lord, which ought to have been a house of prayer also for the Gentiles and other peoples, namely for any proselytes whatsoever, nevertheless a new prophecy is held here, which is accustomed to use the words of the Holy Scriptures adapted to the customs and reasoning of the Old Testament to describe the things of the New Testament. A house of prayer, says Jerome, is the Church, which is divided throughout the whole world, and not the temple of the Jews, which was confined by the very brief straits of the land of Judea. And they explain this sense sufficiently by the benefits which are promised here to foreigners: first, the bringing to the holy mountain of the Lord, by which Mr. Brentius acknowledged that the true and spiritual Church of God is designated: that they shall be true members of the Church. Second, the hearing of prayers. I WILL MAKE THEM JOYFUL IN MY HOUSE OF PRAYER. For he who is truly pious is made joyful and exhilarated in the house of prayer, because his prayers are heard, and he himself becomes master of his own vow. For the absurdities of the Jews, as if the house of prayer of God is so called because God prays, which he who wishes to see and laugh at may approach Hackspan on this passage. Third, the acceptance of Spiritual Sacrifices. THEIR BURNT OFFERINGS AND THEIR VICTIMS SHALL PLEASE ME UPON MY ALTAR. For good works, which the pious do out of faith, are sacrifices, burnt offerings, and victims, and they please God (Phil. 4, Heb. 13, Rom. 12). It is, however, a great benefit that the pious know that their works please God. Although they are not ignorant that their works are imperfect, yet because they are certain that they are in the grace of God, they believe that their obedience is not in vain, but pleasing to God, who approves of it and repays it with many benefits. Thus Cyril: This prayer is taken as if from the example and type of legal worship. For formerly the Israelites were accustomed to burn rams and goats and to offer sacrifices. But since, as I have said, the shadow has passed, those called from the Gentiles do not make an approach for themselves through blood: but they sacrifice themselves, as it were, to God: dying to the world, living to righteousness.

Verse same. I WILL YET GATHER TO HIM HIS GATHERED ONES] More correctly: those to be gathered. After the gathering of Ezra will follow the gathering of Nehemiah.

That the gathering to be instituted through Ezra and Nehemiah is treated here, was to be proven. The context does not teach this. Grotius was mistaken in this, that the preceding things should be understood concerning the liberation from the Babylonian captivity and the state in exile. But they must be compared with the words of the Lord: The Lord God says, gathering the dispersed of Israel: I will yet gather to him his gathered ones, with those things which are held in John 11. Jesus was about to die for the nation, and not only for the nation, but that he might gather into one the children of God who were dispersed. Which Jerome compares here: and thus he teaches that the discourse is about the remnants of Israel to be gathered by the Apostles, and about bringing into one flock those who had been dispersed before. Whence Vatablus rendered it thus: The Lord God says, who gathers the fugitives of Israel: I will yet gather to him beyond him, that is, beyond Israel I will gather those who shall have joined themselves to him from the uncircumcised, as if the Lord were saying, I am about to gather into my Church both Israelites and Gentiles. Indeed, these things look to the times of the New Testament and to the calling of the Gentiles, and do not concern only the Israelites according to the flesh. Because the matter is about opening the approach to all foreigners to the holy mountain of the Lord and the house of prayer of all peoples. Concerning which Cyril: That the divine temple, or house of prayer of God, who is above all, was not granted to the Israelites alone: but was made open to all throughout the world, called by conversion and faith to the knowledge of him, he makes clear, saying: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations. Which sentiment those things which follow also confirm.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

DOMUS MEA DOMUS ORATIONIS VOCA- BITUR CUNCTIS POPULIS] Maxime proselytis, qui pari jure cum Israëlitus intra τὸν θρίγχον admittebantur.

Perperam additur hæc determinatio de Prose- lytis. Quia generalia sunt verba promissionis divi- næ de CUNCTIS POPULIS. Et quamvis respe- ctus habeatur, atque allusio fiat ad templum Do- mini, quod domus orationis etiam pro gentibus & populis aliis esse debuit, nimirum pro quibusvis proselytis, tamen novum vaticinium hic habetur, quod uti soleat S. S. verbis mori & rationi Vet. T. accommodatis ad res Novi Testamenti describen- das. Domus orationis, inquit Hieronymus, Eccle- sia est, quæ in toto orbe dividitur, & non templum Judæorum, quod brevissimis terræ Judaicæ arctaba- tur angustiis. Et explicant hunc sensum satis beneficia, quæ alienigenis hic promittuntur: primo adductio ad montem sanctum Domini, quo veram & spiritualem Ecclesiam Dei designari, agnovit Dn. Brentius: quod futuri sint vera membra Ecclesiæ. Secundo exauditio precum. LÆTIFICABO EUM IN DOMO ORATIONIS MEÆ. Qui enim vere pius est, lætificatur & exhilaratur in domo orationis, quia preces ejus exaudiuntur, & fit ipse voti sui compos. Ineptias Judæorum, quasi domus orationis Dei dicatur, quia Deus orat, qui videre ac ridere vult, adeat Hackspan. ad h. l. Tertio acceptatio Spiritualium Sacrificiorum. HOLOCAUSTA EORUM ET VICTIMÆ EORUM PLACEBUNT MIHI SUPER ALTARI MEO. Nam bona opera, quæ faciunt pii ex fide, sacrificia sunt, holocausta & victimæ, ac placent Deo Phil. 4. Ebr. 13. Rom. 12. Magnum autem est beneficium, quod sciant pii, opera sua Deo placere. Etsi non ignorent, opera sua esse imperfecta, tamen quia certi sunt se esse in gratia Dei, obedientiam suam non esse vanam, sed gratam in Deo credunt, qui eam approbet, & multis beneficiis rependat. Sic Cyrillus: Oratio hæc tanquam ab exemplo & typo legalis cultus sumpta est. Nam olim arietes & hircos incendere, ac sacrificia offerre solebant Israëlitæ. Sed quoniam, ut dixi, umbra transiit, non per sanguinem aditum sibi faciunt, ex Gentibus vocati: sed veluti seipsos Deo sacrificant: mundo morientes, justitiæ viventes.

Vers. Eod. ADHUC CONGREGABO AD EUM CONGREGATOS EJUS] Rectius: congregandos. Post congregationem Esdræ sequetur congregatio Nehemiæ.

De congregatione per Esdram & Nehemiam instituenda hic agi, probandum erat. Non id docet contextus. Falsus in eo fuit Grotius, quod de liberatione è captivitate Babylonica, & statu in exilio superiora intelligenda sint. Conferenda autem cum verbis Domini: Ait Dominus Dominus, congregans dispersos Israel: Adhuc congregabo ad eum congregatos ejus, ea quæ habentur Joh. 11. Jesus moriturus erat pro gente, & non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei, qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Quæ hic confert Hieronymus: adeoque docet, de congregandis per Apostos reliquiis Israel sermonem esse, & de redigendis in unum gregem his, qui fuerant antea dispersi. Unde Vatablus ita reddidit: Dicit Dominus Deus, qui profugos Israelis colligit: Adhuc congregabo ad eum ultra eum, id est, ultra Israelem congregabo eos, qui illi se adjunxerint ex incircumcisis, ac si dicat Dominus, Ego in Ecclesiam meam sum congregaturus Israelitas & gentiles. Nimirum spectant hæc ad tempora Novi Testamenti & ad vocationem gentium, non tantum Israelitas concernunt secundum carnem. Quia de aditu cunctis alienigenis aperiendo ad montem sanctum Domini & domo orationis cunctorum populorum res est. Quo de Cyrillus: Quod autem non solis Israëlitic tributum sit divinum templum, seu domus orationis Dei, qui est supra omnes: sed omnibus per orbem terrarum, conversione & fide ad agnitionem ipsius vocatis patefactum, perspicuum facit, inquiens: Domus mea domus orationis vocabitur omnibus gentibus. Quam sententiam etiam ea, quæ sequuntur, confirmant.

## 56:9
Verse 9. ALL YOU BEASTS OF THE FIELD, COME TO DEVOUR, ALL YOU BEASTS OF THE FOREST] A new discourse begins here. For after the consolations liberally set forth for the pious, lest they should cast away their spirit, he returns to the rebuke of the impious, who were to exist in great numbers among the Jews after the times of Isaiah, with very grave threats added. By beasts of the field of every kind, understand the Egyptians, the marauders from the Chaldeans, from the Syrians, from the Moabites, from the Ammonites, who all afflicted Judah with disasters and great devastation, even before the deportation. See 2 Kings 23:33, 24:2.

This is not about the disaster inflicted by the Egyptians and the Chaldean marauders before the deportation: for that does not fit the order which Grotius fixed according to the series of times, but the discourse here is about the final destruction: therefore Christ, when he had brought forward the Prophet concerning the temple, which ought to have been a house of prayer, which they had converted into a den of thieves (Luke 19), predicted the final total destruction. For whose sake the Prophet calls together the wild beasts. Thus Jerome: But with the remnants of Israel gathered by the Apostles, and those who had been dispersed before reduced into one flock, all the beasts are provoked to come and devour Israel: namely, those who did not wish to believe, of whom the Apostle says: For the end has come upon them. And the Lord in the Gospel: but when you shall see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its consummation has arrived. Which explanation is also approved by Cyril: If the wild beasts are understood by us as those who devour Israel, that: Come, eat, is all but the act of one casting before them those who acted impiously, or to whom it deservedly happened that they should suffer this, inasmuch as they killed the prince of life, did not admit the faith, and were driven far away, who were near, and are no longer the people of God, but are held in hatred, as being murderers of the Lord.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OMNES BESTIÆ AGRI, VENITE AD DEVORANDUM, UNIVERSÆ BESTIÆ SALTUS] Novus hic sermo incipit. Nam post consolationes liberaliter piis expositas, ne animum abjicerent, redortitur objurgationem impiorum, qui post Esaiæ tempora exstituri erant inter Judæos plurimi, minis additis valde gravibus. Bestias agri omnis generis intellige Ægyptios, latrunculos ex Chaldæis, ex Syris, ex Moabitis, ex Ammonitis, qui omnes Judam cladibus & vastitate magna affecerunt, etiam ante deportationem. Vide 2. Reg. 23, 33. 24, 2.

Non de clade ab Ægyptiis, & latrunculis Chal- dæis ante deportationem illata: neq; enim id con- venit ordini, quem juxta seriem temporum fixit Grotius, sed de novissimo excidio hic sermo est: id- eo Christus cum de templo, quod domus orationis esse debuerit, Prophetam adduxisset, quod ipsi in speluncam latronum converterant Luc. 19. πανω- λεθρίαν novissimam prædixit. Cujus gratia con- vocat feras Propheta. Ita Hieronymus: Congre- gatis autem per Apostolos reliquiis Israel, & in unum redactis gregem his, qui fuerant ante dispersi, omnes bestiæ provocantur ut veniant & devorent Israel: eos videlicet, qui credere noluerunt, de quibus Aposto- lus: Etenim pervenit super eos finis. Et Domi- nus in Evangelio: cum autem videritis circumdari ab exercitu Hierusalem, tunc scitote, quod adve- nerit ejus consummatio. Quæ explicatio etiam Cyrillo probata: Sin feræ intelligantur à nobis, qui devorant Israëlem, illud: Venite, edite, est tantum non objicientis illis eos, qui impie egerunt, quibusve merito contigit, ut id patiantur, quippe qui princi- pem vitæ interfecerunt, fidem non admiserunt, ac longe abacti sunt, qui prope erant, nec amplius Dei populus, sed odio habiti sunt, utpote Dominicidæ.

## 56:10
Verse 10. HIS WATCHMEN ARE ALL BLIND] His, that is, of the Jewish people. By watchmen, understand both the Priests and those who sold themselves as Prophets. Compare Ezekiel 3:17, 33:2, 6, 7.

It is manifest that the cause of the perdition of the Jews is being rendered: Which resided chiefly in the watchmen, in the Priests, Pharisees, and Scribes, as the Evangelical History teaches. But lest God should seem to punish without cause, and to exact penalties for a thing of nothing, he immediately attaches to them the crimes by which, being entangled, they were given into destruction to the enemies, or for food to the beasts. For see, he says, because they are all blinded, they do not know how to be wise. For truly the Israelites were blind, and above others especially the Scribes, and Pharisees, and the rulers of the Synagogue. For they neither admitted the true light, nor wished to know Christ, although he was openly crying out, now: I am the light of the world: now again: I have come as a light into this world: he who follows me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life. Since therefore it was permitted, having received the faith, to be enriched with light, that indeed they did not do, as the Prophet also says: For them waiting for light, darkness was made: and waiting for brightness, they walked in gloom. And the Savior himself said of them, and of their people committed to their hand: They are blind, and leaders of the blind. All therefore, he says, are blinded, and they do not know how to be wise. Which sense Jerome also handed down: that all the beasts of the forest may come and devour those gathered, whether crowds of the Gentiles succeed into the place of the Jews; their watchmen are the cause, namely the scribes and Pharisees: because all being blind, they did not know the Lord the Savior, nor did they wish to see the light present. To whom the Lord was speaking: Fools and blind, what is greater, the gold, or the altar, that sanctifies the gold? And again: blind guides, straining out a gnat, and swallowing a camel? And: a blind man leading a blind man, both fall into the pit.

Verse of the same.

THEY ALL KNEW NOT] They did not see the evils to come.

MANY DOGS NOT ABLE TO BARK] They dissimulate the sins of others. Just as the duty of dogs is to bark at thieves, so it is the duty of Priests and Prophets to rebuke vices.

SEEING VAIN THINGS] They rave. This is for the Arabs with ז changed into ד, הדר.

SLEEPING] Lying down. He persists in the similitude.

LOVING DREAMS] Lovers of dreams.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SPECULATORES EJUS CÆCI OMNES] Ejus, id est, populi Judaici. Speculatores intellige, tum Sacerdotes, tum eos qui se pro Prophetis venditabant. Confer Ezech. 3, 17. 33, 2. 6. 7.

Manifestum est, causam reddi perditionis Ju- dæorum: Quæ præcipue residebat in speculatori- bus, in Sacerdotibus, Pharisæis & Legisperitis, ut Historia Evangelica docet. Ne autem sine causa punire videatur Deus, & de re nihili pœnas exige- re, statim illis crimina apponit, quibus implicati, dati sunt in exitium hostibus, vel in esum bestiis. Videte enim, inquit, quia omnes excæcati sunt, non no- runt sapere. Vere enim Israëlitæ cæci fuerunt & præ aliis maxime Scribæ, ac Pharisæi & præfecti Syna- gogæ. Nec enim veram lucem admiserunt, nec Christum scire voluerunt, licet aperte clamantem, nunc: Ego sum lux mundi: nunc iterum: Ego lux in mundum hunc veni: qui sequitur me, in tenebris non ambulabit, sed habebit lucem vitæ. Cum ergo lice- ret, fide suscepta luce ditari, id quidem non fece- runt, ut & Propheta inquit: Expectantibus illis lu- cem, factæ sunt tenebræ: & expectantes splendo- rem in caligine versati sunt. Et ipse Servator dixit de illis, & de populo illorum manui commisso: Cæci sunt, & cæcorum duces. Omnes igitur, inquit, excæcati sunt, neq; sapere norunt. Quem sensum & Hieronymus tradidit: ut omnes bestiæ saltus veniant & devorent congregatos, sive in locum Judæorum gen- tium turbæ succedant; speculatores eorum in causa sunt, scribæ scilicet & Pharisæi: quia omnes cæci, nescierunt dominum salvatorem, nec lucem voluerunt videre præsentem. Ad quos Dominus loquebatur: Stulti & cæci, quid est plus, aurum, an altare, quod sanctificat aurum? Et iterum: duces cæci, culi- cem liquantes, & camelum glutientes? Et: cæcus cæcum ducens, ambo in foveam cadunt.

Vers. eod.

NESCIERUNT UNIVERSI] Non viderunt mala ventura.

CANES MULTI NON VALENTES LATRARE] Peccata aliorum dissimulant. Sicut canum officium est allatrare fures, ita Sacerdotum & Prophetarum reprehen- dere vitia.

VIDENTES VANA] Delirant. Id Arabibus ז in ד mutato هذر.

DORMIENTES] Cubantes. Perstat in similitudi- ne.

AMANTES SOMNIA] Somni amantes.

## 56:11
Verse 11. AND MOST SHAMELESS DOGS] And for namely. For it is explanatory.

THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN SATIETY] they are insatiable. THE SHEPHERDS THEMSELVES HAVE NOT KNOWN UNDERSTANDING] They do not take pains with the law. He calls the same men shepherds whom he previously described as watchmen, and whom he depicted under the image of dogs. ALL HAVE TURNED ASIDE TO THEIR OWN WAY] They attend to their own affairs, not God’s. EVERY ONE TO HIS OWN AVARICE, FROM THE HIGHEST EVEN TO THE LOWEST] In the Hebrew: Every one to his own gain from his beginning: supply of the way, that is to say, to the end. Verse 12. COME, WE WILL TAKE WINE] Supply, they say. An ellipsis frequent among the Hebrews. LET US BE FILLED WITH DRUNKENNESS] Let us drink οἰνοποσ. See Luke 1:15 and what is said there. AND IT SHALL BE AS TODAY, SO TOMORROW, AND MUCH MORE] Tomorrow we shall dine even more sumptuously. Thus the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET CANES IMPUDENTISSIMI] Et pro nempe. Est enim ἐξηγητικόν.

NESCIERUNT SATURITATEM] sunt insatiabiles. IPSI PASTORES IGNORAVERUNT INTELLIGENTIAM] Non dant operam legi. Pastores vocat eosdem, quos ante speculatores, & quos sub canum imagine descripsit. OMNES IN VIAM SUAM DECLINAVERUNT] Res suas agunt, non Dei. UNUSQUISQUE AD AVARITIAM SUAM, A SUMMO USQUE AD NOVISSIMUM] In Hebræo: Unusquisque ad lucrum suum ab initio ejus: supple viæ, ad finem scilicet. Vers. 12. VENITE, SUMEMUS VINUM] Supple, dicunt illi. Frequens apud Hebræos ἔλλειψις. IMPLEAMUR EBRIETATE] Potemus οἰνοποσ. Vide Luc. 1, 15. & ibi dicta. ET ERIT HODIE SIC ET CRAS, ET MULTO AMPLIUS] Cras lautius etiam prandebimus. Sic Chaldæus hic.

## 57:1 Argument
CHAPTER LVII.

The death of the righteous is not regarded by the ungodly, with whom God expostulates on account of idolatry and other crimes, promising to the faithful the consolation of the Spirit and peace.

Vers. 1. THE RIGHTEOUS PERISHES] King Josiah dies, who was both righteous, that is, abstaining from evil, and very beneficent, 2 Kings 22:2, 2 Chronicles 34:2. AND THERE IS NO ONE WHO CONSIDERS IN HIS HEART] No one thinks about the reason why God does this. FOR THE RIGHTEOUS IS TAKEN AWAY FROM THE FACE OF EVIL] Translate: before the evil, that righteous man is gathered [to his ancestors]. Before the evil, that is, so that he may not see the captivity of the people. These are the very words of Huldah to Josiah in the name of God: I will gather you to your fathers and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace, that your eyes may not see all the evils which I am about to bring upon this place. In peace, that is, with the Jewish commonwealth intact.

Grotius, along with some Hebrews, understands this of Josiah. Others, however, among the Jews have explained it as referring to Manasseh, others to Isaiah. Concerning whom Jerome says: The Jews think that this and the rest which follows are to be understood either generally of all the righteous whose blood Manasseh shed, and he filled Jerusalem from gate to gate; or certainly that Isaiah is prophesying about his own death, that he was to be sawn asunder by Manasseh with a wooden saw, which is a most certain tradition among them. Whence also many of our own refer that which is set down in the Epistle to the Hebrews concerning the passion of the saints, "They were sawn asunder," to the passion of Isaiah. However, the commentary of Grotius is not consistent with itself. For while he himself urges the series and sequence of the times of history, he slips back now from the Babylonian captivity to the times of Josiah. But Cyril and Jerome understand Christ by "the righteous," insisting upon τῇ συνεχείᾳ of the preceding verses. On account of the blind watchmen and dumb dogs, says Jerome: who are themselves shepherds, knowing no understanding, nor are they satisfied with present pleasures, but always prepare themselves for future ones, the just man has perished. Concerning whom Pilate’s wife says: Have thou nothing to do with that just man. And what follows: And merciful men or just men are gathered and taken away, signifies the Apostles; who are killed by the impious, and are gathered by the Lord. And he renders the reasons why the just man was killed and taken away, saying: For the just man is taken away from the face of malice, that he might not see the evils of the world. Or on account of the malice of men, whose sins he himself was bearing, he ascended to the Father as a victor. Cyril has it thus: when he has shown that they were dumb dogs and possessed of insatiable avarice, he further demonstrates with these words that they were slothful and contemptuous, to such a degree that they hardened themselves in extreme wickedness and were not even prepared to bring themselves to repent. For the righteous man perishes, he says, and no one takes it to heart, and righteous men are taken away, and no one considers it. By these words he seems to intimate the nefarious undertakings of the Jewish flock against Christ, and whatever they did against the holy Apostles. For they killed Jesus, crying out and saying all but that prophetic word: Let us bind the just one, because he is inconvenient to us: and as far as their mind and counsel were concerned, that just one perished, that is, he who knew no sin: for they did not kill him for just causes, and they brought into danger, without mercy, just men who were bestowing upon them the divine and Evangelical word, and calling them to the recognition of their cruelty and to repentance. It is also expounded concerning the Messiah in Midrasch Koheleth upon Ecclesiast. 7, 14. R. Asaria said, in the hour in which God created the first Adam, He took him, and led him, and brought him back through all the trees of paradise, and said to him: See my works, how beautiful and how praiseworthy they are, for your sake I created whatever I created. Apply your mind, therefore, so that you do not corrupt, or destroy, disturb, shake, and pull down my age: For if you destroy it, there will be no one after you to repair it: And not only this; but you will also be the cause of death to that righteous man, as it is said in Isa. 57. v. 1. The righteous man himself dies, or perishes, and there is no one laying it to heart. So also says Ecclesiastes 7. v. 16. And the righteous man who perished in his righteousness.

The connection and συνάφεια of the prophecy will remain consistent, even if we understand "the just" as referring to those who are justified by faith, with the singular used for the plural for the sake of emphasis: now this just man, now that, or "the just man," whoever he may be, even if he greatly excels the others, has perished, and there is no one who considers in his heart, because the words that follow are ἐξηγητικὰ, for the sake of exaggerating the matter, expressing the same thing in a different way, according to the solemn custom of Scripture. For among the causes of destruction, not the least is that, since God snatches away from the impending ruin those just men who could have opposed themselves to His wrath like a wall and restrained it, there is no one who considers this. This is a deplorable blindness and a sign of the most serious impending destruction, which there is no doubt also happened before the final destruction of Jerusalem. And therefore this is rightly referred to the causes of the former destruction, nor does any necessity compel that it be considered as a peculiar passage of a sermon, which might have been inserted here out of order, since everything coheres perfectly in the way just stated. Calvin cites the death of Luther as an example of this matter, that the righteous man is snatched away before the evil. In our times, he says, a notable example was set forth in the death of Luther, who was withdrawn from the world a little before that grave disaster befell Germany, which he had predicted for many years, while he inveighed against the contempt of the Gospel, and against the crimes and lusts which were flourishing everywhere. He often asked the Lord that He would call him from this life before he beheld those grave punishments, at the apprehension of which he shuddered with his whole soul. And this he obtained from the Lord. Behold, a little after his death, a sudden and unforeseen disaster rushed in, by which Germany was miserably afflicted, when she feared nothing less. Daily examples of this kind exist, which, if they were heeded by men, they would not so securely indulge themselves and their vices. But I have thought this one especially should be cited: because it is recent, and also because it ought to be more conspicuous in such a notable herald of the Gospel, and Prophet of God. Therefore, we ought to diligently attend to the work of the Lord both in the life and in the death of the righteous. But especially in death, by which the Lord calls them to a better life, so that they may be exempted from the miseries in which it is necessary for the ungodly to be immersed. This is Calvin. If those who serve in the camp of Calvin held in high regard this eulogy attributed to the man of God, B. Luther, they would never so bitterly traduce and harass his doctrine.

Latin:

CAPUT LVII.

Iustorum interitus ab impiis non curatur, cum quibus expostulat Deus ob idololatriam, aliaque scelera, fidelibus promittens consolationem spiritus & pacem.

Vers. 1. JUSTUS PERIT] Moritur rex Josias, qui erat & justus, id est, mali abstinens, & beneficus admodum 2. Reg. 22, 2. 2. Paralip. 32, 2. ET NON EST QUI RECOGITET IN CORDE SUO] Nemo cogitat de causa, cur id Deus faciat. A FACIE ENIM MALITIÆ COLLECTUS EST JUSTUS] Verte: ante malum colligitur [ad majores suos] ille justus. Ante malum, id est, ne videat populi captivitatem. Sunt ipsa verba Holdæ ad Josiam Dei ex nomine: Colligam te ad patres tuos & colligeris ad sepulchrum tuum in pace, ut non videant oculi tui omnia mala, quæ inducturus sum super locum istum. In pace, id est, republica Judaica salva.

DE Josia intelligit Grotius cum nonnullis Ebræis. Alii tamen è Judæis de Manasse, alii de Esaia exposuêre. De quo Hieronymus: Judæi & hæc cætera quæ sequuntur, vel generaliter de omnibus justis arbitrantur intelligi, quorum Manasses fudit sanguinem, & implevit Hierusalem a porta usque ad portam. Vel certe Esaiam de sua prophetare morte, quod serrandus sit à Manasse serra lignea, quæ apud eos certissima traditio est. Unde & nostrorum plurimi illud, quod de passione sanctorum ad Hebræos ponitur: Serrati sunt, ad Esaia referunt passionem. Non constat autem sibi Grotianus commentarius. Nam quum ipse seriem & consequentiam temporum Historiæ urgeat, delabitur nunc à captivitate Babylonica retro ad Josiæ tempora. Cæterum Cyrillus & Hieronymus per justum intelligunt Christum, insistentes τῇ συνεχείᾳ superiorum. Propter speculatores, inquit Hieronymus, cæcos & canes mutos: qui ipsi pastores sunt, nescientes intelligentiam, nec præsentibus saturantur voluptatibus, sed semper se præparant ad futuras, justus periit. De quo dicit uxor Pilati: Nihil tibi sit & justo illi. Quodq́; sequitur: Et viri misericordiæ sive justi colliguntur atque tolluntur, Apostolos significat; qui interficiuntur ab impiis, & à Domino congregantur. Causasq́; reddit cur interfectus sit justus, atq́; sublatus, dicens: A facie enim malitiæ collectus est justus, ut mala seculi non videret. Sive propter malitiam hominum, quorum ipse peccata portabat, ad patrem victor ascendit. Cyrillus ita habet: cum ostenderit, eos canes mutos fuisse, & insatiabili avaritia præditos: his verbis porro demonstrat eos socordes esse & contemptores, adeo ut in extremis flagitiis obdurescerent, & resipiscere ne in animum quidem inducere parati essent. Periit enim justus, inquit, & nemo excipit corde, & homines justi tolluntur, & nemo animadvertit. Quibus verbis subindicare videtur nefarios ausus Judaicæ gregis contra Christum, & quæcunq́; fecerunt contra sanctos Apostolos. Occiderunt enim Jesum, tantum non propheticum illud clamantes & dicentes: Ligemus justum, quia incommodus nobis est: & quantum ad ipsorum animum consiliumque attinet, periit justus ille, id est, qui peccatum non novit: nec enim justis de causis eum interfecerunt, & viros justos, divinum illis & Evangelicum sermonem lar- gientes, & ad crudelitatis suae agnitionem ac resi- piscentiam vocantes, in periculum immisericordes ad- duxerunt. De Messia etiam exponitur in Mi- drasch Koheleth super Ecclesiast. 7, 14. R. Asaria dixit, in hora qua creavit Deus primum Adam, tulit ipsum, & duxit, atq; reduxit per omnes paradisi ar- bores, & dixit ei: Vide opera mea, quum pulchra, & quam laudabilia sunt, propter te creavi quicquid creavi. Praebe igitur mentem tuam, ut non corrum- pas, vel destruas, commoveas, concutias, & diruas se- culum meum: Si enim tu destruxeris, non erit post te qui reparet: Et non solum hoc; sed etiam illi justo eris causa mortis, sicut dictum est Esa. 57. v. 1. Ipse justus moritur, vel periit, & non est aliquis ponens super cor. Sic quoq; dicit Ecclesiastae 7. v. 16. Et justus qui periit in justitia sua.

Constabit autem sibi nexus, & συνάφεια vati- cinii, etiamsi justum intelligamus de iis, qui justifi- cantur per fidem, singulari pro plurali posito, em- phaseos causa: modo hic, modo ille justus, aut ju- stus, quicunque tandem sit, etsi caeteros valde prae- stet, periit, & non est qui recogitet in corde suo, quia verba subjuncta ἐξηγητικὰ sunt, rei exaggerandae causa, idem aliter efferentia, more Scripturae so- lemni. Inter causas enim excidii non postrema est, quod praeripiente Deo cladi imminenti viros justos, qui poterant irae ejus sese opponere, muri instar, eamq; cohibere, nemo sit, qui hoc recogitet. Quae est deploranda caecitas, & signum instantis gravissimi exitii. Quod etiam ante novissimum ex- cidium Hierosolymis accidisse, nullum est dubium. Ideoque recte hoc ad causas excidii superioris re- fertur, nec ulla necessitas cogit, ut pro pericopa concionis peculiaris, quae hic extra ordinem in- serta sit, habeatur, quum modo dicto omnia opti- me cohaereant. Exemplum hujus rei, quod justus ante malum eripiatur, allegat Calvinus Lutheri o- bitum. Nostris, inquit, temporibus insigne exemplum editum est in morte Lutheri, qui paulo ante subductus est è mundo, quam Germaniae accideret gravis illa cla- des, quam multis annis predixerat, dum in Evan- gelii contemptum, in flagitia & libidines, quae passim vigebant, inveheretur. Rogabat autem saepius Domi- num, ut prius ipsum ex hac vita evocaret, quam intue- retur graves illas poenas, ad quarum apprehensionem toto animo cohorrescebat. Atq; id à Domino impetra- vit. Ecce paulo post ejus mortem, repentina & improvi- sa irruit clades, qua Germania misere afflicta est, quum nihil minus vereretur. Extant quotidiana e- jusmodi exempla, quae si animadverterentur ab homi- nibus, non ita secure sibi & vitiis suis indulgerent. Sed hoc potissimum referendum duxi: quod cum recens sit, tum vero quod in tam insigni praecone Evangelii, & Propheta Dei, magis conspicuum esse debeat. Itaq; & in vita & in morte justorum opus Domini sedulo at- tendere debemus. Praecipue vero in morte, qua Do- minus ipsos ad vitam meliorem evocat, ut à miseriis, quibus immergi impios necesse est, eximantur. Haec Calvinus. Cujus elogium viro Dei B. Luthero tributum si pensi haberent, qui in castris Calvini militant, nunquam doctrinam ejus tam acerbe tra- ducerent, atque exagitarent.

## 57:2
Vers. 2.

LET PEACE COME, LET HIM REST IN HIS BED, WHO WALKED IN HIS UPRIGHTNESS] You translate correctly: Let peace come to him (King Josiah), Let them rest in their beds (that is, in

to the cemetery, and supply, his bones :) he walked (for) before him, that is, before God. The common people understood this of the body: the wise of the spirit, which rested in places known to God, unknown to us. But these things ought not to have been openly revealed before the time of the Messiah, to whom the disclosure of obscure things was reserved. These very words have been in use among the Jews for a long time, when they speak of the pious dead. This interpreter reads here not בִכְחוֹ, but בִכְנֹו as we do

A different reading cannot immediately be gathered from an interpretation alien to the modern text. But by what proof will that double sense of the wise and the common people be demonstrated?

Latin:

Vers. 2.

VENIAT PAX, REQUIESCAT IN CU- BILI SUO, QUI AMBULAVIT IN DIRE- CTIONE SUA] Verteris recte: Adveniat illi (Jo- siae Regi) pax, Requiescant in cubilibus suis (id est, in

τῷ κοιμητηρίῳ, & subaudi, ossa ejus :) ambulavit (enim) coram eo, Deo scilicet. Hæc vulgus intelligebat de corpore: sapientes de spiritu, qui in locis Deo cognitis, nobis inco- gnitis, quiescebat. Sed hæc aperte non debebant revelari ante Messiæ tempus, cui reservata erat rerum obscurarum patefactio. Hæc ipsa verba in usu sunt Judæorum jam o- lim, ubi de piis mortuis loquuntur. Legit hic interpres non בִכְחוֹ, sed בִכְנֹו ut nos

Non statim lectio diversa ex interpretatione colligi potest aliena à moderno textu. Cæterum geminus ille sensus sapientum, & vulgi quo do- cumento probabitur?

## 57:3
Verse 3. BUT YOU, DRAW NEAR HITHER, SONS OF THE SORCERESS] He followed what we have עֹנְנָה. But both the Chaldean and the Greeks read עוֹנָה, with a paragogic He, with a better sense. sons of lawlessness, or lawless ones, as the LXX have here.

SEED OF THE ADULTERER AND THE HARLOT] Seed of adulterers and of a harlot, that is, you who by your morals no more belong to Israel than by nature they belong to the said father whom an adulterous mother bore from an adulterer. A wicked and adulterous generation. Matt. 12, 39. 16, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VOS AUTEM ACCEDITE HUC FILII AUGURATRICIS] Sequutus est quod nos habemus עֹנְנָה. Sed & Chaldæus & Græci legerunt עוֹנָה, cum He paragogico, sensu meliore. υἱοὶ ἀνομίας, sive ἄνομοι, ut hic habent LXX.

SEMEN ADULTERI ET FORNICARIÆ] Σπέρ- μα μοιχῶν καὶ πόρνης, id est, qui moribus non magis ad Israëlem pertinetis, quam natura ad dictum patrem perti- nent quos mater adultera ex adultero genuit. Γενεὰ πο- νηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς. Matth. 12, 39. 16, 4.

## 57:4
Verse 4. AGAINST WHOM HAVE YOU SPORTED?] See what kind of King that was whom you despised. He speaks to those who had learned impiety from Manasseh, and had mocked Josiah for his piety, men like Shebna, who even to the detriment of piety wished to consult their own affairs.

AGAINST WHOM HAVE YOU WIDENED THE MOUTH, AND PUT OUT THE TONGUE?] To widen the mouth is to speak what one pleases, as Ps. 22, 14. 35, 21. To put out the tongue, among the three kinds of insults which the Scholiast of Persius has on Satire 1.

ARE YOU NOT WICKED CHILDREN?] Children of wickedness: that is, as if born for this, that you might commit crimes, sons of perdition in the Greek, just as we say in Latin a lost man.

LYING SEED] Of a lie, in a similar manner of speaking in Hebrew. Thus idolaters are called by the Prophets.

Again, without sufficient cause, a different reading is imagined in the Hebrew, nay, the Hebrew truth is even accused. For why would that sense be better concerning the children of injustice than concerning the children of the sorceress? The children of the sorceress are best described as those who were devoted to the superstitious arts of augurs, the seed of the adulterer and the harlot, who, begotten under idolatrous parents, and who were addicted to necromancy and the observations of augurs, insisted on the impious footsteps of their progenitors. As far as the sense itself is concerned, Isaiah preached punishments and crimes to the people, which he foresaw would one day happen, and now he inveighs with a grave correction against the Jews, whom he calls children of the sorceress, seed of the adulterer and the harlot, just as Christ proclaimed them a brood of vipers and an adulterous generation, Matt. 23 and 13. But those words AGAINST WHOM HAVE YOU SPORTED, AGAINST WHOM HAVE YOU WIDENED THE MOUTH, AND PUT OUT THE TONGUE, Jerome understands of the ignominy and reproaches brought upon Christ: Against whom, he says, have you sported, spitting in his face and plucking his beard: and against whom have you widened, and opened your mouth, and put out your tongue, saying to him: You are a Samaritan and have a demon: and again: This man does not cast out demons, except by Beelzebub the prince of demons. And afterwards in the passion: Crucify, crucify such a one. And again: His blood be upon us, and upon our children; and elsewhere: Vah, you who destroy the temple, and in three days build it up? He saved others, himself he cannot save: Let him descend now from the cross, and we will believe him. Nor does Cyril think otherwise; he calls those adulterers here who presided, the scribes and doctors of the law, who not only adulterated the Synagogue, and speaking to it the precepts of the law, but twisting them to what was not right and teaching doctrines as the commandments of men. But the Synagogue of the Jews was deservedly a harlot, as one that received the seeds of adulterers, and repudiated the law of the most wise Moses. Hence he most deservedly calls them children of iniquity. Say therefore, he says: against whom have you insulted, against whom have you opened your mouth? And against whom have you let loose your tongue? You have, he says, held the holy Prophets in derision: But who were they? The genuine children of the most high God, but also servants and subjects, and of human condition: and the crimes were committed against fellow-servants. But now against whom have you let loose your tongue? [for he was not like the Prophets, servants of our condition, subject to the yoke, but he himself the Lord of all, even if he did put on the form of a servant;] Therefore, he says, you are children destined for destruction; for you did not wish to receive the savior: and you are an iniquitous seed: for you did not wish for him, who instructed you in piety through the Evangelical oracles. Nor does that explanation conflict with the context. For although the correction subjoined concerns the worship of Idols, which flourished in the time of Isaiah, it was not inconvenient for even old crimes to be reproached to the Christ-killers, which was also done by Christ himself in Matt. 23, or for the idolaters of his own time, by whom that extreme impiety was at last to cease, to be set before their eyes, namely in the reprobation and agitation of the Messiah himself.
