The killers of the Lord, says Cyril, after he shows who they are, reveals another disease, that they are haters of God and headlong into committing slaughter, and that this is not new or recent in them, but has already long since and for many centuries past become ingrained among them. For you are, he says, those who in former times implored idols under leafy trees.

That the discourse is about Josiah, and directed to those who had learned impiety from Manasseh and had mocked Josiah for his piety, is a purely arbitrary interpretation. It has been shown that the preceding parts pertain to the times of the New Testament and to the calling of the Gentiles; and therefore nothing is more fitting than if the causes are said to be set forth here, which the Prophet also began to deliver when he dealt with the blind watchmen of the reprobate Jewish nation, which he summons from ancient times, especially their most execrable idolatry, their confidence in reprobate Gentiles and idolaters, their forgetfulness of the God of Israel, and other most grave sins, and their perseverance in the same, because through the sermons of the Prophets they were not made better, but worse, and were finally blinded by the just judgment of God and given over to a reprobate mind. Therefore the Prophet is commanded to cry out, to announce their crimes and sins, and to tax their hypocrisy in Chapter 58; then indeed he set forth their detestable impiety, injustice, lies, confidence in superstitious cults and human defenses, and similar offenses in Chapter 59, with the most just punishments added at the same time, because when they expected light, they were to be overwhelmed by darkness, and salvation was to be almost removed from them. However, for the consolation of the faithful, he graphically exhibited the victory of Christ against the tyranny of the Devil, by which He is about to claim into His power not only the islands and the nations, so that those who are from the west may fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the Sun His glory, but also that some among the Jewish people are to return from iniquity. Hence he turns in chapter 9 to the description and commendation of the spiritual kingdom of Christ, as we are about to say hereafter. Thus these prophecies cohere most excellently, nor is there any reason or necessity that we should draw them back to past times, by reason of the principal scope, and establish different prophecies or sections of prophetic sermons as looking to different times. In which analysis and method, namely that in that way everything is referred to the times of the New Testament, as far as the principal scope is concerned, even if arguments are also brought forward from ancient times, we have been not a little confirmed by the consensus of the ancient interpreters in both the Greek and the Latin Church, from whose footsteps we do not think we should rashly depart.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SUPER QUEM LUSISTIS?] Videte qualis fuerit ille Rex quem vos contemsistis. Ad eos loquitur, qui ex Manasse impietatem didicerant, & Josiam irrife- rant ob pietatem, homines qualis Sobna, qui etiam cum pietatis detrimento rebus suis consulere volebant.

SUPER QUEM DILATASTIS OS, ET EJE- CISTIS LINGUAM?] Dilatare os est loqui quæ lubitum est, ut Ps. 22, 14. 35, 21. Ejicere linguam, inter tria san- narum genera, quæ habet Scholiastes Persii ad Satyram 1.

NUMQUID NON VOS FILII SCELESTI?] Fi- lii sceleris: id est, quasi in hoc nati, ut scelera patretis, υἱοὶ ἀπωλείας in Græco, sicut Latine dicimus hominem per- ditum.

SEMEN MENDAX] Mendacii, in Hebræo si- mili loquendi genere. Sic vocantur à Prophetis idolola- træ.

Iterum citra causam sufficientem diversa in Ebræo fingitur lectio, imo accusatur etiam veritas Ebræa. Cur enim sensus ille melior esset de filiis injustitiæ, quam de filiis auguratricis? Optime de- scribuntur filii auguratricis, qui superstitiosis augu- rum artibus dediti fuêre, Semen adulteri & fornica- riæ, qui sub idololatris parentibus, & qui necro- mantiæ augurumque observationi addicti erant, procreati, progenitorum impiis vestigiis insistê- bant. Quod ad sensum ipsum attinet, supplicia & crimina populo prædicavit Esaias, quæ olim even- tura prævidit, jam invehitur gravi Epanorthosi in Judæos, quos filios auguratricis, semen adulteri & fornicariæ vocat, ut Christus eos progeniem vipe- rarum & genus adulterinum proclamavit Matth. 23. & 13. Verba autem illa SUPER QUEM LUSISTIS, SUPER QUEM DILATASTIS OS, ET EJECISTIS LINGUAM, de igno- minia & probris Christo illatis intelligit Hierony- mus: Super quem, inquit, lusistis, conspuentes faciem ejus barbamq́; vellentes: & super quem dilatastis, & aperuistis os vestrum, & linguam ejecistis, dicentes ei: Samaritanus es & dæmonium habes: & iterum: Iste non ejicit dæmonia, nisi in Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum. Et postea in passione: Crucifige, crucifige talem. Et rursum: sanguis ejus super nos, & super filios nostros; & alibi: Vah, qui de- struit templum, & in triduo instaurat illud? Alios salvos fecit, seipsum salvum facere non potest: De- scendat nunc de cruce, & credimus ei. Nec aliter Cyrillus; Adulteros hic appellat, qui præsidebant, scribas & legis doctores, qui non tantum adulterabant Synagogam, & ei legis præcepta loquentes, sed ad quæ fas non erat, detorquentes & docentes doctrinas man- data hominum. Meretrix autem merito erat Judæo- rum Synagoga, ut quæ adulterorum semina reciperet, & sapientissimi Mosis legem repudiaret. Hinc eos meritissimo appellat filios iniquitatis. Dicite ergo, in- quit: in quo insultastis contra quem aperuistis os ve- strum? & in quem laxastis linguam vestram? Se- se- pe, inquit, ludibrio habuistis sanctos Prophetas: At qui erant illi germani Dei summi filii, verum & fa- muli & subditi, & humanæ conditionis: ac in conser- vos ab ipsis patrata sunt facinora. Nunc autem in quem linguam laxastis? [non enim Prophetis similis fuit, nostræ conditionis famulis, jugo subditus, at ipse Dominus universorum, & siquidem formam ser- vilem induerit;] Filii itaq;, inquit, estis ad interitum destinati; nec enim voluistis recipere servatorem: & semen iniquum estis: nec enim voluistis eum, qui per Evangelica oracula vos ad pietatem instituit. Ne- que repugnat illa explicatio contextui. Nam etsi Epanorthosis subjuncta concernat cultum Ido- lorum, qui tempore Esaiæ viguit, non inconve- niens erat vel vetera etiam crimina κυριοκτόνοις exprobrari, quod à Christo ipso quoque factum Matth. 23. vel sui temporis idololatris, quo tan- dem defitura illa extrema impietas erat, ob ocu- los poni, nempe in Messiæ ipsius reprobationem, & exagitationem. Dominicidas, inquit Cyrillus, postquam eos esse ostendit, alium morbum patefacit, quod sint osores Dei & ad cædem faciendam præcipi- tes, nec id novum aut nuperum in illis sit, sed jam pri- dem & multis retro seculis apud eos inoleverit. Vos enim estis, inquit, qui superioribus temporibus im- plorastis idola sub arboribus frondosis.

De Josia sermonem esse, & ad eos, qui ex Ma- nasse impietatem didicerant, & Josiam irriserant ob pietatem, mere arbitraria est ἐπίλυσις. Ostensum est, antecedentia ad tempora N. T. & ad vocatio- nem gentium pertinere; ideoque nihil conve- nientius est, quam si causæ hic exponi dicantur, quas etiam exorsus est tradere Propheta, cum de cæcis speculatoribus egit, reprobatæ gentis Ju- daicæ, quas arcessit inde ab antiquis temporibus, idololatrism imprimis eorum maxime execrabi- lem, confidentiam in reprobis gentilibus & idolo- latris, oblivionem Dei Israëlis & alia gravissima, & perseverantiam in iisdem, quod per conciones Prophetarum non meliores, sed deteriores red- diti, tandem justo Dei judicio excæcati, & in men- tem reprobam dati sint. Ideo clamare, scelera, ac peccata eorum annunciare jubetur Propheta, & hypocrisin eorum taxare Cap. 58. tum vero dete- standam impietatem, injustitiam, mendacia, fidu- ciam in cultibus superstitiosis & præsidiis humanis, similia delicta proposuit C. 59. additis simul pœnis justissimis, quod cum lucem expectarint, tenebris obruendi sint, & salus ab ipsis pene elonganda sit. In solatium autem fidelium, Christi victoriam graphice exhibuit adversus tyrannidem Diaboli, qua in potestatem suam vindicaturus est non tan- tum insulas & gentes, ut timeant, qui ab occidente sunt, nomen Domini, & qui ab ortu Solis gloriam e- jus, sed redituri etiam sint ab iniquitate aliqui in populo Judaico. Hinc se convertit cap. 9. ad de- scriptionem & commendationem regni Christi spiritualis, uti deinceps dicturi sumus. Ita optime cohærent hæc vaticinia, neque ulla est ratio, nec necessitas, ut ad tempora antegressa, ratione scopi principalis, retrahamus, & diversas prophetias, aut pericopas concionum propheticarum ad tempora diversa spectantes constituamus. In qua ἀναλύ- σει ac methodo, ut nempe ea ratione omnia ad N. T. tempora, quantum ad scopum præcipuum, re- ferantur, etsi argumenta etiam ex antiquis tem- poribus adducta sint, nos non parum confirmavit ὁμοψηφία veterum interpretum cum in Græca tum in Latina Ecclesia, à quorum vestigiis temere discedendum nos non censemus.

## 57:5
Ver. 5. YOU WHO INFLAME YOURSELVES WITH GODS] You who grow hot among the gods, namely in lust. For in the temple of the groves women and men stood prostituted in the surroundings in honor of false gods. Therefore, groves near the temple were prohibited in the law.

UNDER EVERY LEAFY TREE] Under the dense shadows of trees. The same manner of speaking in 2 Kings 17:10, Hosea 4:13, Ezekiel 6:13.

SACRIFICING LITTLE ONES] According to the ancient custom of the Canaanites, or Phoenicians, about which we have treated elsewhere.

IN THE TORRENTS] נחל properly signifies a valley, which the LXX followed here: ἐν ταῖς φάραγξι. And because torrents are accustomed to be in valleys, therefore it also signifies a torrent. The valley of Hinnom is understood here especially, near the torrent Cedron.

UNDER EMINENT ROCKS] The Greeks: ἀνάμεσον τῶν πετρῶν. The Chaldean: Under the eminences of the rocks, under the precipices, which the Hebrews here and elsewhere call branches.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUI CONSOLAMINI IN DIIS] Qui in- calescitis apud Deos, nempe in venerein. Nam in lucis templo circumjectis prostabant feminæ & mares in honorem deo- rum falsorum. Ideo luci apud templum in lege prohibi- ti.

SUBTER OMNE LIGNUM FRONDOSUM] Sub densis arborum umbris. Idem loquendi genus 2. Reg. 17, 10. Oseæ 4, 13. Ezech. 6, 13.

IMMOLANTES PARVULOS] More vetere Ca- nanæorum, sive Phœnicum, de quo egimus alibi.

IN TORRENTIBUS] נחל proprie vallem signifi- cat, quod hic secuti LXX. ἐν ταῖς φάραγξι. Et quia in val- libus esse solent torrentes, ideo & torrentem significat. Intelligitur hic præcipue vallis Hinnomi, apud torrentem Cedron.

SUBTER EMINENTES PETRAS] Græci: ἀνά- μέσον τῶν πετρῶν. Chaldæus; Subter eminentias petrarum, sub præcipitiis, quæ Hebræi hic & alibi ramos vocant.

## 57:6
Verse 6. IN THE PARTS OF THE TORRENT IS THY PORTION, THIS IS THY LOT] It seems more correctly translated: among the stones which are placed at the banks of the torrents are my hope and trust. You rely on them as the rich do on their possessions.

AND TO THEM YOU HAVE POURED OUT A LIBATION] In honor of those stones you pour out wine. Ἐξέχεας σπονδὰς, the Greeks.

YOU HAVE OFFERED SACRIFICE] In the Greek θυσίαν. Thus the Greek interpreters of the Old Testament translate the Hebrew, which is here מנחה, which in the books of those speaking Greek is πόπανον. The idolaters themselves called them כונים, as in Jeremiah 7:18.

SHALL I NOT BE INDIGNANT OVER THESE THINGS?] Should I allow these things, which are contrary to my worship and prohibited by my law, to go unpunished?

Latin:

Vers. 6. IN PARTIBUS TORRENTIS PARS TUA, HÆC EST SORS TUA] Videtur rectius v verti: in lapi- gatis (lapidibus) qui sunt ad ripas torrentum positæ spes & fi- ducia mea. Illis siditis sicut divites possessionibus suis.

ET IPSIS EFFUDISTI LIBAMEN] In honorem illorum lapidum vinum libatis. Ἐξέχεας σπονδὰς Græct.

OBTULISTI SACRIFICIUM] In Græco θυσίαν. Sic Græci Veteris Testamenti interpretes vertunt He- bræum, quod hic est; מנחה quod in Græce loquen- tium libris est πόπανον. Ipsi autem idolatratæ vocabant כונים, ut Jer. 7, 18.

NUMQUID SUPER HIS NON INDIGNA- BOR?] An hæc ego meo cultui adversantia, mea lege pro- hibita, sinerem abire impune?

## 57:7
Verse 7. UPON A HIGH AND LOFTY MOUNTAIN] Which places were used as temples by the Canaanites and neighboring peoples.

YOU HAVE SET YOUR BED] For they used to spend the night in those places in the hope of obtaining dreams presaging the future. Thus it was once done at Delphi, before oracles were delivered there. Euripides, Iphigenia in Tauris: Ἀπὸ ζαθέων χρηστηρίων νύχια Χθὼν ἐτεκνώσατο φάσματα, etc.

AND YOU WENT UP THERE TO SACRIFICE VICTIMS] Victims of every kind.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SUPER MONTEM EXCELSUM ET SUBLI- MEM] Qui loci Cananæis vicinisque populis erant pro Templis.

POSUISTI CUBILE TUUM] Nam pernoctabant in illis locis spe consequendi somnia futurorum præsaga. Sic olim Delphis fiebat, antequam oracula ibi redderentur. Euripides Iphigenia in Tauris: Ἀπὸ ζαθέων χρηστηρίων νύχια Χθὼν ἐτεκνώσατο φάσματα. &c.

ET ILLUC ASCENDISTI UT IMMOLARES HOSTIAS] Victimas omnis generis.

## 57:8
Vers. 8. AND BEHIND THE DOOR AND BEHIND THE DOORPOST YOU HAVE PLACED YOUR MEMORIAL] Certain images of protection, as Jerome explains here, and that in that very part of the houses where the commandments of God ought to have been placed. Deut. 6, 9. 11, 20.

QUIA] Nay rather.

JUXTA ME] In my sight: that is, in my very Temple. See the history 2 Kings 21, 3. 4. 5. 6. 7.

DISCOOPERUISTI] You have done me as much injury as an adulterous wife could do to her husband. Thus the Chaldean here. Discooperuisti is what the Greeks would call ἀνέ- συρας.

ET SUSCEPISTI ADULTERUM] It translates well that which is in the Hebrew, you have made to ascend: that is, you have admitted an adulterer.

DILATASTI CUBILE TUUM] More correctly: You have been loosened by your cohabitation. For it appears that משכב is taken thus in Num. 31, 17.

ET PEPIGISTI CUM EIS FEDUS] More correctly: You have castrated some of them. Thus כרת is taken in Levit. 22, 24. Deuter. 23. Lustful women used to do this to slaves, so that they might avoid childbirth.

DILEXISTI STRATUM EORUM] That is, you have even delighted in the cohabitation of these. For here again is משכב.

MANU APERTA] In the Hebrew: You have seen the hand: that is, you have felt it. For every sense among the Hebrews is expressed by the word for seeing, as Ps. 34, 9. & elsewhere. It pleased you to be handled. The LXX omitted these on purpose.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET POST OSTIUM ET RETRO POSTEMPO- SUISTI MEMORIALE TUUM] Tutelæ quædam simu- lacra, ut hic explicat Hieronymus, idque in illa ipsa ædium parte, ubi præcepta Dei poni debuerant. Deuter. 6, 9. 11, 20.

QUIA] Quinimo.

JUXTA ME] In conspectu meo: id est, in ipso Templo meo. Vide historiam 2. Reg. 21, 3.4.5.6.7.

DISCOOPERUISTI] Tantarn mihi fecisti inju- riam, quantam uxor adultera marito facere posset. Ita hic Chaldæus. Discooperuisti est quod Græci dicerent ἀνέ- συρας.

ET SUSCEPISTI ADULTERUM] Bene vertit id quod in Hebræo est, ascendere fecisti: id est, admisisti adulterum.

DILATASTI CUBILE TUUM] Rectius: La- xata es concubitu tuo. Nam sic sumi משכב apparet Num. 31, 17.

ET PEPIGISTI CUM EIS FEDUS] Rectius: castrastis quosdam ex eis. Sic sumitur כרת Levit. 22, 24. Deuter. 23. faciebant hoc feminæ libidinosa servis, ut par- tum effugerent.

DILEXISTI STRATUM EORUM] Id est, etiam horum concubitu delectata es. Est enim hic iterum משכב.

MANU APERTA] In Hebræo: Manum vidisti: id est, sensisti. Nam omnis sensus apud Hebræos viden- di voce exprimitur, ut Ps. 34, 9. & alibi. Libuit tibi contrectari. LXX. hæc omisêre de industria.

## 57:9
Vers. 9. AND YOU HAVE ADORNED YOURSELF FOR THE KING WITH OINTMENT, AND HAVE MULTIPLIED YOUR PERFUMES] That is, you have even imitated Egyptian customs, so that you might please King Necho. 2 Kings 23, 35. 36. 37. You have a similar deed of Ahaz in 2 Kings 16, 10. & following.

MISISTI LEGATOS TUOS PROCUL] Like procurers of love.

ET HUMILIATA ES] You have cast yourself down.

USQUE AD INFEROS] Like a vile prostitute, ὡς χαμαιτύπη. Martial: They hide their filthy selves and the monuments of whores.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET ORNASTI TE REGI UNGUENTO, ET MULTIPLICASTI PIGMENTA TUA] Id est, et- iam Ægyptios mores imitata es, ut Nechoni regi placeres. 2. Reg. 23, 35. 36. 37. Simile factum Achazi habes 2. Reg. 16, 10. & sequentibus.

MISISTI LEGATOS TUOS PROCUL] Velut amorum pararios.

ET HUMILIATA ES] Projecisti te.

USQUE AD INFEROS] Tanquam vile scortum, ὡς χαμαιτύπη. Martialis: Abscondunt spurcas & monumenta lupas.

## 57:10
Vers. 10. IN MULTITUDINE VIÆ TUÆ LABORASTI] You have left nothing untried: you have been polluted in every way. Thus the Jews even now take ירך. See Prov. 30, 19.

NON DIXISTI: QUIESCAM] In Hebrew: You never said, my heart says nothing.

VITAM MANUS TUÆ INVENISTI] By such foul labor you provided a living for yourself.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN MULTITUDINE VIÆ TUÆ LABO- RASTI] Nil reliquisti intentatum: omnibus modis pollu- ta es. Sic Judæi etiam nunc sumunt ירך. Vide Prov. 30, 19.

NON DIXISTI: QUIESCAM] In Hebræo: Nunquam dixisti, cor mibilinquit.

VITAM MANUS TUÆ INVENISTI] Tam fœ- do labore victum tibi parasti.

## 57:11
Vers. 11. FOR WHOM YOU WERE ANXIOUS AND AFRAID, BECAUSE YOU LIED, AND DID NOT REMEMBER ME] In the Hebrew: Whom do you fear or dread, seeing that you have lied (to me, that is) and forgotten me?

NEQUE COGITASTI IN CORDE TUO] In Hebrew: Nor did you lay it upon your heart: I did not come to your mind.

BECAUSE I AM SILENT AND AS IF NOT SEEING AND FORGETFUL OF MYSELF] In the Hebrew: Is it because I have been silent for a long time, that you do not care for me? as if he were saying: I shall therefore begin to speak.

LET AURA, BUT HE WHO HAS TRUST &c. that those having been overcome by the power of God, the people may return to Judea, and possess Mount Sion, and all the obstacles of the journey may be removed: nor may they suffer the ambushes of any nation, because the Lord has made the way plain for his people. And they contend that these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel and Ezra. We, however, joining what is said to the preceding, assert this: that the wind and the storm shall take away all the idols that could not deliver them, and they shall be as dust, which the wind casts from the face of the earth. But those who have had trust in the Lord shall possess the land. Concerning which we are about to read in this same Prophet: He shall lift you up to the goods of the earth. From which it is clear: that this land is not below, but above. To which the Saint shall ascend with the Lord lifting him up, concerning which we have often said: Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land. And I believe, to see the goods of the Lord in the land of the living. But that holy mountain of God is to be understood, of which he speaks to the Hebrews, who writes the Epistle: You have approached Mount Sion, and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and many thousands of angels, and the Church of the firstborn, who are written in the heavens. Thus far Jerome, who has embraced the reasoning synecdochically: The prophetic discourse had begun against the people of the Jews, whose teachers he called blind watchmen and dumb dogs, and shepherds ignorant of understanding, and wicked children, and the seed of an adulterer and of a harlot: after which he comes to Jerusalem, whom he reproaches for her fornication, in that she had spread her bed for her lovers, and had received them with an open hand, and had adorned herself with all idols, and had sent messengers far away, so that they might also enjoy foreign lovers. With this rebuke he finishes, and comes to those who trust in the Lord, and to whom he had promised the land and the mountain to be possessed, and for whose return he had ordered the way to be prepared: There is no doubt but to the Apostles, at whose preaching they believed from both peoples. Mr. Brentius, although he thinks the former sermon of this chapter was delivered either under Ahaz or under Manasseh, in whose kings' times it was not only done with impunity, but was even considered pious and holy to devise and follow various worships of God without the word of God, (which times we have said how they are regarded) refers this other part with us to the times of the New Testament, and confirms this explanation both from the prophecy itself CONCERNING THE PEACE OF THOSE WHO ARE FAR OFF, and from the Petrine interpretation in Acts 2. The latter part of this sermon is that which consoles the pious with the promise of the Gospel concerning the vivification of the afflicted, and concerning the true and eternal peace to be provided through Christ the Son of God. This part of the sermon can, however, be understood generally, so that the sense is: The impious, who trust in their idols, even their idols shall vanish. But the pious, who trust in the Lord, shall be saved, and shall receive consolation. For God, although he dwells in the heights, nevertheless looks upon the humble and the afflicted, so that he may vivify them. And although he sometimes becomes angry with his people, and afflicts them, on account of sins, nevertheless he is not angry forever, nor does he afflict so that he may destroy, but so that he may save, so that he may lead back into the way, heal, and restore to him eternal consolation. This general sentiment, as it is pious, so it not ineptly agrees with the scope of this sermon: But because afterwards he manifestly preaches about the spreading of the Gospel among the Jews and the Gentiles: I create, he says, the fruit of the lips peace, peace, to him who is far off, and to him who is near: And Peter seems to preach from this passage, when in the second chapter of the Acts he says: To you is the promise made, and to your children, and to all WHO ARE FAR OFF, whomsoever the Lord our God shall call. Similarly Paul in the second chapter of Ephesians: coming, he says, he preached PEACE to you, who

were FAR OFF, and to those who were NEAR: Therefore we feel that the Prophet in this place specially looks to the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and to the spreading of his Gospel among the Jews, who were said to be near, and among the Gentiles, who were far away from salvation. But those words HE WHO HAS TRUST IN ME, Brentius claims for the Son of God, who promises to those believing in himself not an external land of Canaan, or Mount Sion: For not all the pious, who believed in the Son of God, received by inheritance that land of inheritance, which was given to the descendants of Abraham, or had their possession in Jerusalem and Zion, which was called the holy mountain of God; and since this is an Evangelical sermon of the Son of God, whose kingdom is not of this world, this promise is not to be understood concerning a worldly inheritance; but by these words, by which external goods were once signified in the law, spiritual and heavenly goods are signified in the Gospel of the Son of God. Therefore when he says, he who has trust in me, shall inherit the land, and shall possess my holy mountain, it is clearly the same thing that is said in the Evangelist: He who believes in him does not perish, but has life. This is indeed to inherit the land, and to possess the holy mountain of God, namely to obtain the blessing promised in the seed of Abraham, which is Christ, and to be a member of the true Church because of Christ and in Christ are the promises. What follows, AND I SHALL SAY: MAKE A WAY, foretell that the Son of God upon his coming will himself exhort that they prepare a way for him with all obstacles removed, so that God, having been received by faith, may be able to dwell in them. For since he, who speaks here, calls the faithful his people, and introduces God high and sublime, from whom the Holy Spirit proceeds, it is not obscure that the Son of God is speaking, MAKE A WAY, and again, PREPARE THE WAY, CLEAR THE PATH (Thus the Hebrew is to be rendered, and not turn aside from the path) TAKE AWAY THE STUMBLING BLOCKS FROM THE WAY OF MY PEOPLE: FOR THUS SAYS THE HIGH ONE &c. to which the sermon of the Son of God in the days of his flesh entirely tends, Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near: come to me and I will refresh you.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PRO QUO SOLLICITA TIMUISTI, QUIA MENTITA ES, ET MEI NON ES RECOR- DATA] In Hebræo: Quem tu vereris aut timeres, quan- doquidem mentita es, (mihi scilicet) meiq; oblita?

NEQUE COGITASTI IN CORDE TUO] In Hebræo: Nec posuisti super cor tuum: in mentem tibi non veni.

QUIA EGO TACENS ET QUASI NON VI- DENS ET MEI OBLITA ES] In Hebræo: An quia ego taceo jam pridem, ideo me non curas? quasi dicat: inci- pam ergo loqui.

LET AURA, QUI AUTEM FIDUCIAM HA- BET &c. quod illis Dei virtute superatis, popu- lus redeat in Judæam, & possideat montem Sion, & omnia itineris impedimenta tollantur: nec ullius gentis patiantur insidias, quia Dominus planam fece- rit viam populo suo. Et hæc sub Zorobabel & Esdra impleta contendunt. Nos autem jungentes superio- ribus quæ dicuntur, hoc asserimus: quod omnia idola quæ eos non poterant liberare, tollat ventus atq́; tempe- stas, & sint quasi pulvis, quem projicit ventus à facie terræ. Eos autem, qui habuerint in Domino fiduciam possessuros terram. De qua in hoc eodem Propheta lecturi sumus: Elevabit te ad bona terræ. Ex quo perspicuum est: hanc terram non deorsum esse, sed sursum. Ad quam Sanctus Domino elevante conscen- det, de qua crebro diximus: Beati mites: quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram. Et credo, videre bona Do- mini in terra viventium. Mons autem sanctus Dei ille intelligendus est, de quo ad Hebræos loquitur, qui scribit Epistolam: Accessistis ad Sion montem, & civitatem Dei viventis Hierusalem cælestem, & multa millia angelorum, & Ecclesiam primitivo- rum, qui scripti sunt in cælis. Hactenus Hierony- mus, qui rationem συνεκδοχικῶς complexus est: Cæ- perat sermo propheticus contra populum Judæorum, quorum magistros appellavit Speculatores cæcos & canes mutos, & pastores ignorantes intelligentiam, & filios iniquos, & semen adulterum atq́; meretricis: post quæ venit ad Hierusalem, cui exprobrat fornicationem ejus, eo quod dilataverit cubile amatoribus suis, & susceperit eos manu aperta, & ornaverit se cunctis i- dolis, & miserit legatos procul, ut peregrinis quoq́; a- matoribus fruerentur. Quâ increpatione finit, & ve- nit ad eos qui confidunt in Domino, & quibus terram montemq́; promiserat possidendum, & quorum rever- sioni iter jusserat præparari: Haud dubium quin A- postolis, ad quorum prædicationem de utroque populo crediderunt. Dn. Brentius etsi superiorem hujus ca- pitis concionem existimet vel sub Achaz, vel sub Manasse habitam, quorum regum temporibus non impune tantum fuit, verum etiam pium & sanctum habitum est, varios Dei cultus absq́; verbo Dei excogi- tare & sectari, (quæ tempora quomodo respician- tur diximus) hanc alteram partem nobiscum re- fert ad tempora Novi Testamenti, & hanc explica- tionem tum ex ipsa prophetia DE PACE EO- RUM QUI LONGE SUNT, tum ex interpre- tatione Petrina confirmat Act. 2. Posterior hujus concionis pars est, quæ consolatur pios promissio- ne Evangelii de vivificatione afflictorum, & de vera ac æterna pace per Christum filium Dei præstanda. Potest autem hæc concionis pars generaliter intel- ligi, ut sensus sit: Impii, qui confidunt idolis suis, & idola eorum evanescent. Pii autem, qui confidunt in Dominum, servabuntur, & accipient consolatio- nem. Deus enim etsi habitat in excelsis, tamen re- spicit humiles & afflictos, ut vivificet eos. Et quam- vis nonnunquam irascatur populo suo, & affligat eum, propter peccata, tamen non irascitur per- petuo, nec affligit, unde perdat, sed ut servet, ut re- ducat in viam, sanet, & reddat ei consolationem æ- ternam. Hæc generalis sententia ut pia est, ita non inepte cum scopo hujus concionis convenit: Sed quia postea manifeste concionatur de divulgatio- ne Evangelii inter Judæos & Gentes: Creo, in- quiens, fructum labiorum pacem, pacem, ei qui longe est, & ei qui prope: Et videtur Petrus ex hoc lo- co concionari, cum in Actis capite secundo ait: Vo- bis facta est repromissio, & filiis vestris, & omnibus QUI LONGE sunt, quoscunq́; advocaverit Dominus Deus noster. Similiter Paulus Ephes. capite secundo: veniens, inquit, Evangelizavit PACEM vobis, qui

PROCUL aberatis, & iis qui PROPE: Idcirco sentimus Prophetam hoc loco specialiter respicere in revelationem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, Filii Dei, & in divulgationem Evangelii ejus inter Ju- dæos, qui prope esse dicebantur, & inter Gentes, quæ longe à salute aberant. Verba autem illa QUI HABET FIDUCIAM MEI Filio Dei vendicat Brentius, qui promittit credentibus in sese non ex- ternam terram Canaan, aut montem Sion: Neque enim omnes pii, qui crediderunt in Filium Dei, hæ- reditate acceperunt illam terram hæreditatis, quæ posteris Abrahæ data, aut possessionem suam in Je- rusalem, & Zion habuêre, quæ dicta est mons san- ctus Dei; & quum hic sit Evangelica Filii Dei con- cio, cujus regnum non est de hoc mundo, promissio ista non est de mundana hæreditate intelligenda; sed his verbis, quibus quondam significabantur in lege externa bona, significantur in Evangelio Filii Dei spiritualia & cœlestia bona. Itaque cum ait, qui habet fiduciam mei, hæreditabit terram, & possidebit montem sanctum meum, plane idem illud est, quod in Evangelista dicitur: Qui credit in eum non perit, sed habet vitam. Hoc nimirum est hæreditare ter- ram, & possidere montem sanctum Dei, videlicet consequi benedictionem in semine Abrahæ, quod est Christus, promissam, & esse membrum veræ Ec- clesiæ propter Christum & in Christo sunt promissa. Quæ sequuntur, ET DICAM: VIAM FACITE, prænunciant Filium Dei sub adventum suum ipsum- met hortaturum, ut viam sibi præparent omnibus remotis obstaculis, ut fide susceptus habitare in ipfis possit Deus. Nam cum is, qui hic loquitur, fi- deles vocet populum suum, & introducat Deum ex- celsum & sublimem, à quo egreditur Spiritus San- ctus, haud obscurum est Filium Dei loqui, VIAM FACITE, & iterum, PARATE VIAM, EX- PURGATE SEMITAM (Sic Ebræa reddenda, non vero declinate de semita) TOLLITE OF- FENDICULA DE VIA POPULI MEI: QUIA HÆC DICIT EXCELSUS &c. quo prorsus tendit concio Filii Dei in diebus carnis, Agite pœnitentiam, appropinquavit enim regnum cœ- lorum: venite ad me & ego refocillabo vos.

## 57:15
Vers. 15. DWELLING IN THE HIGH AND HOLY PLACE, AND WITH A CONTRITE AND HUMBLE SPIRIT] Although he dwells in the high place, he nevertheless favors the humble. For that is what it is among the Hebrews to be with someone. Compare Ps. 51, 19.

He here brings forth again the Socinian and Judaic error, concerning God being enclosed in the heavens by reason of substance, and not present on earth with the pious except by favor and grace: Which Jerome here also noted in the Jews: Which we certainly ought not to accept in the Judaic manner, as if God were enclosed in any place, and dwelt only in heaven, who is diffused everywhere, and by whom all things are contained. We have, however, refuted this error, by which immensity is derogated from God, System. Theol. T. 2.

THAT HE MAY REVIVE THE SPIRIT OF THE HUMBLE] That is, may comfort those led by repentance.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IN EXCELSO ET SANCTO HABITANS, ET CUM CONTRITO ET HUMILI SPIRITU] Quanquam in excelso habitat, humilibus tamen favet. Id enim est apud Hebræos cum aliquo esse. Confer Ps. 51, 19.

Prodit hic iterum Socinianum & Judaicum errorem, de Deo substantiæ ratione in cœlis con- cluso, nec nisi favore, & gratia in terris præsente cum piis: Quem in Judæis hic etiam notavit Hie- ronymus: Quod utiq; non more Judaico debemus ac- cipere, ut Deus ullo claudatur loco, & in cœlo tantum habitet, qui ubiq; diffusus est, & à quo omnia continen- tur. Refutavimus autem hunc errorem, quo im- mensitas Deo derogatur, System. Theol. T. 2.

UT VIVIFICET SPIRITUM HUMILIUM] Id est, consoletur pœnitentia ductos.

## 57:16
Vers. 16. FOR I WILL NOT CONTEND FOR EVER] I will not be angry with them for long, namely after repentance.

THE SPIRIT SHALL GO FORTH FROM MY FACE, AND THE BREATH I WILL MAKE] You have translated correctly: Yea, a breeze (coming) from me shall cover (him, the humble and contrite:) and a gentle breeze I will make. Sorrow is compared to heat, but consolation to a cooling breeze.

There is no cause here for forging a new version, since Jerome has rendered it correctly: or if the meaning of GOING FORTH, approved by the LXX Interpreters and Jerome, does not please, it can be explained with other Greek Interpreters, as Jerome observed: The Lord who dwells in the high places and looks upon the lowly, whose name is holy, and who rests in the Holy ones, who upholds the afflicted, and grants life to the oppressed, he has spoken these things. I will not always be angry, nor will I be indignant forever. For I still strike so that I may amend: therefore I kill so that I may make alive. For I have compassion on my creature, and those whom I myself have created, I will not suffer to perish eternally. My spirit also, which shall go forth from me, or which according to the Hebrew, Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion, surrounds all things, for this is what περιελλίσσεται signifies, is the vivifier of all: And the breath or in the plural breaths, for this is indeed what נשמות sounds like, I have made. And the Grotian version is insipid and inconvenient. For it is not the function of a breeze to COVER. Ludovicus de Dieu rendered the word יעטוף as IT SHALL RETURN by the authority of the Syriac and Arabic languages, in which עטף signifies to return. But what sense is there in that, THE SPIRIT SHALL RETURN FROM BEFORE ME? for thus he translated it. If therefore the sense of going prevails, that construction, from my face, demands not the meaning of returning, but of going forth, as the LXX explained, for the Spirit shall go forth from me; and Jerome, because the spirit shall go forth from my face. Nor does the word for COVERING conflict with the Holy Spirit, who covers us not against the heat of divine wrath, and covers us with a gracious overshadowing. Raimundus Martini in Pug. Fidei explains it as, he shall clothe, wrap, or assist. Oecolampadius, the Holy Spirit shall proceed from me, he shall be wrapped in them, that is, he shall dwell in them. Therefore, regarding the meaning of the word רוח, Jerome brings forward a twofold opinion of the ancient interpreters. Some, he says, of our people say that this is the Spirit by which the whole world is inspired and governed, and all things have knowledge of God, whom a distinguished poet describing according to the Stoics, says: In the beginning, heaven and earth and the liquid plains, and the shining globe of the moon and the Titanian stars, the Spirit nourishes from within, and the Mind infused through the limbs moves the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body. And the rest. But others understand the Holy Spirit. Who in the beginning was borne over the waters, and was vivifying all things, who goes forth from the Father because of the fellowship of Nature, is sent by the Son, saying; It is expedient for you that I go: For if I do not go, the paraclete will not come to you: but if I go, I will send him to you. Of whom he says again: When the paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who goes forth from the Father. Let it not scandalize anyone if the spirit is said to go forth from the Father, since the Son also said of himself: I went forth from the Father and came, for I did not go forth from myself, but he sent me. He was speaking of this spirit: I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, that he may be with you always, the Spirit of truth. This is the Spirit, of whom Moses also writes: Who would grant that all the people of the Lord might be prophets, and that the Lord might give his spirit upon them? And Joel from the person of God: I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. And Zechariah: Nevertheless, receive my words and my statutes, which I command in my spirit to my servants the Prophets. And again: I will pour out upon Jerusalem a spirit of grace and mercy. And many other things from both Testaments, which it is now long to repeat. Although Jerome does not entirely accede to this other opinion, we say only this, that the same Prophet spoke equally of this spirit and breath. Thus says the Lord God, who made the heaven: And a little later: Who gives breath to his people, who is upon it, and spirit to those who tread upon it: yet that reasoning ought not to move us, because we see the Prophet himself distinguishing between רוח spirit and נשמות breath, with number, because he speaks of the former in the singular, and of the latter in the plural: then by phrase, because the former goes forth from the face of the Lord, but of the breaths it is said, I WILL MAKE. And therefore our people understand these things concerning the mission of the Holy Spirit and his effect, namely, by a pleasant breathing, by which we are refreshed. For when the Spirit goes forth from the face of the Lord, and is sent, we are recreated by his most sweet breath, which although it can be understood generally of the consolation and refreshing of the Church, yet because those things which precede preach of the revealed Gospel and the office which the Son of God undertook to administer in his flesh, and soon follows the propagation of the Gospel among the Jews and the Gentiles, Brentius judges that that appendix looks especially to that mission of the Holy Spirit which took place on the day of Pentecost. It is certain from the coherence of the whole text that it pertains to the N. Testament, and therefore it is wrongly restricted to the return from Babylon.

Otherwise, various interpretations of this opinion occur: The Jews accept it in this sense, that all souls were already created since the foundation of the world: I HAVE MADE THE SOULS: which opinion Origen also embraced. But Augustine, although in Epist. 157 to Optatus the Bishop he understands it concerning the creation of souls, yet says it is doubtful whether he still makes every breath from one breath (the inspiration of the Adamic soul), just as every body of man is made from one body, or whether he makes new souls from nothing. The Chaldean explains it thus: because I will bring back the spirits of the dead, (i.e., into the body) and I have made the breath: as if the discourse were about the vivification of the dead. Schindler and Tremellius rendered it thus with an obscure sense: For the spirit shall be overwhelmed from my sight, and the souls, which I have made. This is Vatablus's interpretation: The spirit from my sight shall clothe the body, and I have created the souls: that is, I create spirits and souls, which I afterwards send into the body, so that they are clothed as if by a certain garment, and the sense may be: I will not be angry with sinners eternally, because I am the author of the souls, which through the body performed actions contrary to my law. But from that interpretation it seems to follow that the damnation of the impious will not be eternal. Hackspan interprets it thus: The spirit from my face shall wrap itself, and I will make the souls: and he says that this is the sense: I will refresh your spirit, so that, freed from distress, you may at long last no longer fear my anger. He thinks that for the spirit to wrap itself, and for God to make the souls, is to vivify the heart and the spirit of the humble, or the afflicted, so that it can recover its former strength. But the words do not at all fit this explanation. That it is a simpler opinion than the one we have handed down (with which the translation of B. Luther also agrees) we have no doubt.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NON ENIM IN SEMPITERNUM LITI- GABO] Non succensebo illis diu, nempe post pœnitentiam.

SPIRITUS A FACIE MEA EGREDIETUR, ET FLATUS EGO FACIAM] Verteris recte: Imo aura à me (véniens) teget (illum humilem & contritum:) & ven- tulam ego faciam. Mæror æstui comparatur, solatium ve- ro auræ refrigeranti.

Non hic causa est novam versionem cudendi, cum recte reddiderit Hieronymus: aut si EGRE- DIENDI significatio, LXX. Interpp. & Hierony- mo probata non placeat, cum aliis Græcis Interpp. exponi poterit, ut observavit Hieronymus: Domi- nus qui in excelsis habitat & humilia respicit, cujus no- men est sanctum, & requiescit in Sanctis, qui su- stentat afflictos, & vitam tribuit oppressis, hæc locutus est. Non semper irascar, nec jugiter indignabor. Qui adhuc percutio ut emendem : ideo occido ut vivificem. Miseror enim creaturæ meæ, & quos ipse condidi, in æternum perire non patiar. Spiritus quoq́; meus, qui ex me egredietur, sive qui juxta Hebraicum, Aqui- lam, Symmachum & Theodotionem, cuncta circun- dat, hoc enim significat περιελλίσσεται, vegetator est omnium: Et flatum sive pluraliter flatus, hoc quippe נשמות sonat, ego feci. Atq; insipida ac in- conveniens est versio Grotiana. Auræ enim non est TEGERE. Ludovicus de Dieu vocem יעטוף reddidit REVERTETUR autoritate Linguarum Syriacæ & Arabicæ, in quibus עטף significat rever- ti. Sed quis inde sensus, SPIRITUS AB ANTE ME-REVERTETUR? sic enim transtulit. Si ergo eundi sensus obtineat, illa constructio, à facie mea, postulat non reversionis, sed egressionis signifi- catum, uti LXX. exposuêre, Spiritus enim à me e- gredietur; & Hieronymus, quia spiritus à facie mea e- gredietur. Neq; repugnat TEGENDI verbum Spiritui Sancto, qui tegit non adversus æstum iræ divinæ, & operit nos gratiosa obumbratione. Rai- mundus Martini in Pug. Fidei explicat, induet, ami- ciet vel auxiliabitur. Oecolampadius, Spiritus Sanctus à me procedet, involutus erit in eis, h.e. inha- bitabit in eis. Quod ergo ad significationem vocis רוח sententiam geminam adducit Hieronymus ve- terum Interpp. Quidam, inquit, nostrorum hunc esse ajunt Spiritum, quo omnis mundus inspiratur, & re- gitur, & cuncta habent notitiam Dei, quem juxta Stoicos insignis Poëta describens, ait: Principio cœ- lum ac terras camposq; liquentes, Lucentemque globum Lunæ Titaneaque astra Spiritus intus alit, totamq; infusa per artus Mens agitat molem & ma- gno se corpore miscet. Et reliqua. Alii vero San- ctum Spiritum intelligunt. Qui in principio fereba- tur super aquas, & vivificabat omnia, qui de Patre egreditur propter societatem Naturæ, à Filio mittitur, dicente; Expedit vobis, ut ego vadam: Nisi enim ego iero, paracletus non veniet ad vos: sin autem ego iero, mittam eum ad vos. De quo rursum ait : Cum venerit paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis à Patre, Spiritum veritatis, qui de Patre egreditur. Ne scandalizet quempiam, si spiritus egredi dicatur ex Patre, cum etiam Filius de se dixerit: Ego de Pa- tre exivi & veni, neq; enim à me ipso exivi, sed ille me misit. De hoc spiritu loquebatur: Rogabo Pa- trem, & alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut sit vo- biscum semper, Spiritum veritatis. Hic est Spiri- tus, de quo scribit & Moyses: Quis det, ut omnis populus Domini sit in Prophetas, & det Dominus spiritum super eos? Et Ioel ex persona Dei: Effun- dam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem, & pro- phetabunt filii vestri & filiæ vestræ. Et Zacharias: Veruntamen verba mea, & legitima mea suscipite, quæ ego præcipio in spiritu meo, servis meis Pro- phetis. Et iterum: Effundam super Hierusalem spiritum gratiæ, & misericordiæ. Multaq́; alia de utroque Testamento, quæ nunc longum est repetere. Quamvis vero non omnino huic alteri sententiæ accedat Hieronymus, hoc solum dicimus, quod idem Propheta de hoc spiritu & flatu pariter sit locutus. Hæc dicit Dominus Deus, qui fecit cœlum: Et post paululum: Qui dat flatum populo suo, qui est su- per eum, & spiritum his, qui calcant eum: ratio ta- men illa nos movere non debet, quia videmus Pro- phetam ipsum distinguere רוח spiritum & נשמות flatus, cum numero, quia de illis μοναδικῶς loquitur, de hoc πληθυντικῶς: tum phrasi, quia ille egreditur facie Domini, de flatibus autem dicitur, EGO FACIAM. Ideoq; de missione Spir. Sancti, ejusq; effectu nostri hæc intelligunt, afflatu nempe jucun- do, quo refocillamur. Cum enim egreditur de fa- cie Domini Spiritus, ac mittitur, flatu ejusdem sua- vissimo recreamur, quod etsi generaliter intelligi possit de consolatione & refocillatione Ecclesiæ, ta- men quia ea quæ præcedunt, concionantur de re- velato Evangelio & officio, quod Filius Dei in car- ne sua administrandum suscepit, & mox sequitur de propagatione Evangelii inter Judæos & gentes, censet Brentius, appendicem illam respicere præ- cipue in eam Spiritus Sancti missionem, quæ facta est in die Pentecostes. Certum est è totius textus cohærentia, quod ad N. Test. pertineat, ideoque perperam restringitur ad reditum è Babylonia.

Variæ cæteroquin occurrunt hujus sententiæ interpretationes: Judæi hoc sensu accipiunt, quod animæ omnes creatæ jam sint inde à condito mundo: ANIMAS EGO FECI: quam sententiam et- iam amplexus est Origenes. Augustinus vero etsi Epist. 157. ad Optat. Episcop. de animarum crea- tione intelligat, dubium tamen esse dicit, utrum omnem flatum ex uno flatu (inspirationis animæ Adamicæ) adhuc faciat, sicut ex uno corpore omne corpus hominis, an vero novas animas ex nihilo fa- ciat. Chaldæus ita exponit: quia spiritus mortuorum reducam, (sc. in corpus) & spiraculum ego feci: quasi de vivificatione mortuorum sermo sit. Schind- lerus & Tremellius ita reddidêre sensu obscuro: Nam spiritus à conspectu meo obruetur, & animæ, quas ego feci. Vatabli hæc est interpretatio: Spiri- tus à conspectu meo induet corpus, & animas ego crea- vi: id est, creo Spiritus & animas, quas postea in corpus immitto, ut illæ velut veste quadam induan- tur, ac sensus sit: peccatoribus non irascar æternum, quia ego sum auctor animarum, quæ per corpus edidê- re actiones legi meæ adversas. Sed ex ea interpreta- tione sequi videtur, damnationem impiorum non fore æternam. Hackspanius ita interpretantur: Spi- ritus à facie mea involvet se, & animas ego faciam: ac sensum hunc esse dicit: reficiam spiritum ve- strum, ut liberati ex angustiis tandem aliquando i- ram meam non amplius pertimescatis. Spiritum se involvere, & Deum animas facere esse putat, vivifi- care cor, & spiritum humilium, seu afflictorum, ut pristinas vires recuperare possit. Sed verba huic ex- plicationi haud congruunt. Simpliciorem eam es- se sententiam, quam tradidimus (cui etiam conso- nat B. Lutheri translatio) nulli dubitamus.

## 57:17
Verse 17. BECAUSE OF THE INIQUITY OF HIS COVETOUSNESS I WAS ANGRY] I had been. Covetousness is the root of almost all evils, 1 Tim. 6, 10. We learned above that the Jews suffered especially from this disease, 56, 12, and here 10.

AND I WAS INDIGNANT, AND HE WENT ON WANDERING IN THE WAY OF HIS HEART] That is, I was indignant while the people wandered, following the desires of their heart.

Latin:

Vers. 17. PROPTER INIQUITATEM AVARITIÆ EJUS IRATUS FUI] Fueram. Avaritia prope omnium malorum radix 1. Tim. 6, 10 Hoc autem morbo eximie laborasse Judæos supra didicimus 56,12. & hic 10.

ET INDIGNATUS SUM, ET ABIIT VAGUS IN VIA CORDIS SUI] Id est, indignatus sum, dum populus vagatur sequens cordis sui cupiditates.

## 57:18
Verse 18. I HAVE SEEN HIS WAYS] But now, when I see his ways corrected.

AND I HAVE HEALED HIM] I wish to bring medicine to his evils.

AND I HAVE BROUGHT HIM BACK] I will bring him back.

AND I HAVE RESTORED CONSOLATIONS TO HIM, AND TO HIS MOURNERS] I will console them as well, and those who grieve over their evils.

Latin:

Vers. 18. VIAS EJUS VIDI] Nunc vero cum videam vias ejus correctas.

ET SANAVI EUM] Volo medicinam adferre ma- lis ipsius.

ET REDUXI EUM] Reducam.

ET REDDIDI CONSOLATIONES IPSI, ET LUGENTIBUS EJUS] Solabor & ipsos, & eos qui ipso- rum malis indolent.

## 57:19
Verse 19. I HAVE CREATED THE FRUIT OF THE LIPS] I will give them material for which they may praise me and give me the greatest thanks.

PEACE, PEACE] The greatest salvation.

AND TO HIM THAT IS FAR OFF, AND TO HIM THAT IS NEAR] More correctly: to him who is far (from me) and near (has approached me), that is, to him who converts himself.

AND I HAVE HEALED HIM] I will take away his evils.

Latin:

Vers. 19. CREAVI FRUCTUM LABIORUM] Dabo il- lis materiam, cur me laudent, mihique gratias agant maximas.

PACEM, PACEM] Salutem maximam.

ET QUI LONGE EST, ET QUI PROPE] Re- ctius: ei qui longe (fuit à me) & prope (ad me accessit) id est, ei qui se convertit.

ET SANAVI EUM] Mala ejus auferam.

## 57:20
Verse 20. BUT THE WICKED ARE LIKE THE TROUBLED SEA, WHICH CANNOT REST] As a strait with a reciprocal tide, so they are agitated by their own thoughts.

AND ITS WATERS CAST UP MIRE AND DIRT] In the Hebrew: Its waters cast out mud and dirt. So also the heart of the wicked [casts out] foul actions.

Latin:

Vers. 20. IMPII AUTEM QUASI MARE FERVENS, QUOD QUIESCERE NON POTEST] Ut fretum æstu reciproco, sic illi cogitationibus suis agitantur.

ET REDUNDANT FLUCTUS EJUS IN CON- CULCATIONEM ET LUTUM] In Hebræo: Aquæ ejus expellunt cœnum & lutum. Sic & cor impii actiones fœ- das.

## 57:21
Verse 21.

THERE IS NO PEACE FOR THE WICKED, SAYS THE LORD GOD] I think the interpreter wrote 'my Lord,' as it is in the Hebrew and Chaldean: unless perhaps he preferred to follow the Greek: for some Greek books have ὁ θεὸς, others ὁ κύριὸς ὁ θεὸς. An epiphonema repeated from 48:22. The Greeks express the sense well here and there: ὐκ ἔsι χαίρειν τοῖς ἀσεβέσι. As bodies are torn by lashes, so the soul is torn by cruelty, lust, and evil counsels. Tacitus, Annals 6.

Grotius carries everything away according to the opinion which he has conceived in his mind, regarding the restoration from Babylon. But since the discourse is about the times of the New Testament, this passage deals with the return through repentance and the conversion and healing of the remnant of Israel; that although He was indeed angry with the people because of the iniquity of their greed, and struck them, and hid (or turned away) His face, and was indignant, yet when he walked mourning or converted in the way of his heart (which is to be understood of those from the people who returned to a sounder mind and performed repentance), He healed him, as Jerome and Cyril have explained. God therefore promises that He wishes to heal them, and to lead them back into the true way of salvation, and to render to them consolations after afflictions. The words of the Hebrew text in verse 18 are to be translated thus: I RENDER CONSOLATIONS TO HIM AND TO HIS MOURNINGS, or his sorrows and miseries. How God is going to do this, He explains Himself. I CREATE THE FRUIT, He says, OF THE LIPS, that is, I institute the public preaching of the Gospel (the beginning of which had to be made at Jerusalem, Luke 24), by which is announced PEACE, PEACE, that is, great peace, TO HIM WHO IS FAR OFF: namely, the Gentile, and to him WHO IS NEAR, that is, the Jew. This is the mode, this is the way by which I HEAL men, says the Lord. For whom should we rather believe, Grotius, or the holy Apostle clearly interpreting this passage in Ephesians 2? Coming, He preached PEACE to you WHO WERE FAR OFF, AND PEACE TO THOSE WHO WERE NEAR. For what is more certain than that the Apostle looked to this passage there? Those, therefore, who receive this word of the lips by faith, obtain not only the remission of sins and peace of conscience, but also true and eternal life and salvation. But those who do not believe the Gospel, but are wicked, for them there is no peace. Which interpretation is also that of Jerome; who wishes it to be understood here primarily of the wicked Jews in the time of Christ: But the wicked or unrighteous shall fluctuate like a boiling sea, and they shall never be able to rest. Which, although it can be understood of every wicked person, is nevertheless properly referred to the people of the Jews, who cried out with a consonant voice and persevered in their impiety, saying, 'Crucify, crucify such a one. We have no King but Caesar.' Just as, therefore, a boiling sea cannot rest, but its waves overflow and roll back to the shores, and are again sucked back, and broken in themselves create mud, which is trampled by feet: So the wicked shall be subject to eternal trampling, for whom there is no joy, and who rest in no peace, because they persevere in impiety. And afterwards He compares the wicked to the sea, which can never rest, but even in the greatest tranquility is rolled with broken waves to the shores: its end is mud and trampling. Which Grotius rendered from the Hebrew: Its waters cast out mire and mud, which similarly the heart of the wicked [casts out] foul actions. But even if that explanation is admitted, the rest, THERE IS NO PEACE FOR THE WICKED, denounces punishment to them, that they shall lack that peace which is promised in the Gospel. Nor could Grotius disapprove of that; indeed, he says the Greeks express the sense well, that the wicked shall have no joy; which is to be understood of the deprivation of eternal joy, and therefore of eternal happiness, as both the antithesis teaches and the evidence of the thing itself. For the wicked not infrequently enjoy worldly joy and the peace of the age: but peace and joy in the Holy Scriptures,

in which the kingdom of God is situated, they do not have, unless they are the faithful, Romans 14:17.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

NON EST PAX IMPIIS, DICIT DOMINUS DEUS] Scripsit puto interpres Dominus meus, ut est in Hebræo & Chaldaico: nisi forte Græcum sequi maluit: nam Græci libri alii habent ὁ θεὸς, alii ὁ κύριὸς ὁ θεὸς. Epi- phonema repetitum ex 48,22. Sensum hic & ibi bene ex- primunt Græci: ὐκ ἔsι χαίρειν τοῖς ἀσεβέσι. Ut corpora ver- beribus, ita sævitia, libidine, malis consultis animus dilace ratur. Tacitus Annal. 6.

Abripit omnia Grotius juxta opinionem, quam animo præcepit suo, ad reductionem è Babylone. Sed quum de temporibus Novi Testamenti sermo sit, de reditu per pœnitentiam & conversione ac sa- natione reliquiarum Israëlis hic agitur, quod iratus quidem populo fuerit propter iniquitatem avari- tiæ ejus, & percusserit eum, absconderit (vel aver- terit) faciem suam, & indignatus fuerit, sed cum am- bulavit mœrens sive conversus in via cordis sui (quod de illis è populo intelligendum, qui ad saniorem mentem rediêre, ac pœnitentiam egerunt) sanarit eum, uti Hieronymus & Cyrillus exposuêre. Pro- mittit ergo Deus, quod velit eos sanare, & in veram salutis viam reducere, & reddere ipsis consolatio- nes post afflictiones. Verba Ebræi textus v. 18. ita vertenda: REDDO CONSOLATIONES IPSI ET LUCTIBUS, seu doloribus & ærumnis ipsius. Quod quomodo facturus sit Deus, exponit ipse. CREO FRUCTUM, ait, sermonem LABIORUM, h. e. instituo publicam prædicationem Evangelii, (cu- jus initium fieri debuit Hierosolymis Luc. 24.) quo annunciatur PAX, PAX, hoc est, magna pax, EI QUI LONGE EST: videlicet Ethnico, & ei QUI PROPE EST, h. e, Judæo. Hic est modus, hæc est via, qua SANO homines, ait Dominus. Cui enim potius credamus, Grotione, an vero S. Apo- stolo hunc locum perspicue interpretanti Eph. 2. Veniens Evangelizavit vobis PACEM, QUI PROCUL ERATIS, ET PACEM IIS QUI PROPE. Quid enim certius, quam quod hunc lo- cum ibi respexerit Apostolus? Qui ergo hunc ser- monem labiorum accipiunt fide, consequuntur non solum remissionem peccatorum, & pacem conscientiæ, sed & veram & æternam vitam & salu- tem. Qui autem non credunt Evangelio, sed sunt impii, his nulla pax. Quæ interpretatio est etiam Hieronymi; qui de impiis Judæis imprimis hic agi vult tempore Christi: Impii autem sive iniqui flu- ectuabunt quasi mare fervens, & quiescere nunquam poterunt. Quod licet de omni impio possit intelligi, ta- men proprie refertur ad populum Judæorum, qui con- sona voce clamavit, & perseveravit in impietate sua, dicens crucifige, crucifige talem. Non habemus Re- gem, nisi Cæsarem. Sicut igitur mare fervens quiesce- re non potest, sed redundant fluctus ejus, & revolvunt ad littora, atque iterum resorbentur, & in se fracti lu- tum efficiunt, quod pedibus conculcatur: Sic impii æ- ternæ conculcationis subjacebunt, quorum nullum est gaudium, & qui nulla pace requiescunt, eo quod in im- pietate perseverant. Et postea impios comparat ma- ri, quod nunquam potest quiescere, sed etiam in summa tranquillitate fractis ad littora volvitur flu- ctibus: finis ejus lutum est, & conculcatio. Quod Grotius ex Ebræo reddidit: Aquæ ejus expellunt cœnum, & lutum, quod similiter cor impii actiones fœ- das. Sed admissa licet illa explicatione, cætera tamen, NON EST PAX IMPIIS, pœnam illis de- nunciant, quod pace ea carituri sint, quæ promitti- tur in Evangelio. Nec improbare id potuit Gro- tius, imo sensum bene exprimere Græcos, ait, quod im- pii nullum habituri sint gaudium; quod de privatio- ne æterni gaudii, adeoque æternæ felicitatis intelli- gendum esse, tum antithesis docet, tum ipsa rei evi- dentia. Nam mundano gaudio, & pace seculi fru- untur non raro impii: at pacem & gaudium in S.S.

in quibus regnum Dei situm est, non habent, nisi fideles, Rom. 14, 17.

## 58:1 Argument
CHAPTER LVIII. An admonition to show the people their hypocrisy and vain fasts, and the true manner of fasting and celebrating the Sabbath, with a promise of reward for those who celebrate it thus.

Verse 1. CRY OUT, DO NOT CEASE] God, because He had already promised a return to those led to repentance, seeing that there would be many among the Jews who would count themselves in that number, merely because they had fasted on the days of כפרים (Atonement), shows through the Prophet that He is not content with such repentance, but requires that if they hold anything belonging to another, they should return it, because, as it is usually said, sin is not forgiven unless what was taken away is restored, concerning which matter we said some things in book 3 of 'On the Law of War and Peace,' chapter 10, § 3, and in the Annotations to that place: furthermore, that they should abstain from all injustice and things forbidden by the law: in addition to this, that certain excellent works of mercy should be exercised: just as Daniel also advises Nebuchadnezzar in 4:24.

AS A TRUMPET EXALT YOUR VOICE] Use your throat for a trumpet, and lift up your voice as much as you can.

IN the text there is nothing about fasting on the days of כפרים. Therefore, Grotius inserted that rashly. The hypocrisy of fasts in general is taxed. But because the preceding things looked to the times of Christ, it will be appropriate to refer this rebuke also to that time, just as we see Christ in the days of His flesh greatly rebuked the hypocrisy of the Jews, not only generally (ἐθνικῶς) concerning the worship of God and the divine law, Matthew 15 and 23, but also specifically (ἰδικῶς), regarding fasts, Matthew 6 and 23. Nor is there any doubt that hypocrisy was the cause of the destruction, as Isaiah had predicted in chapter 28, and Christ Himself, repeating that prediction in Matthew 15, and in other places, had not infrequently indicated. But because even then, in the time of Isaiah, the highest hypocrisy was flourishing, the Prophet had to dissuade them from the same and prescribe to them wholesome precepts for instituting fasts and celebrating Sabbaths, with the promise of grace to be exhibited to the obedient faithful. Wherefore, on the occasion of a most grave threat of capital punishment, the Prophet seems to have instituted this sermon, that he might recall the people from hypocrisy, to whom, on account of hypocrisy and impenitence, πανωλεθρία and a most miserable destruction were finally impending. Jerome elegantly compares here the legal trumpet with the exaltation of the voice in announcing the Gospel: The former chapter being finished, in which peace is announced to the just and no rest to the impious, God commands Isaiah the Prophet to cry out in strength, and like a trumpet to exalt his voice, and not to fear to speak the sins and crimes of the people of Israel, by no means fearing death, nor the terrors and reproaches of the impious, but rather considering the commanding Lord. And because they have deaf ears, and can scarcely hear, according to Symmachus and Aquila, he should turn his throat into a trumpet, which in Hebrew is called שופר, which they have interpreted as κερατίνην, that is, horny. And above, indeed, where it was said to the Apostles: 'Go up into the high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem, exalt, do not fear,' neither a horn nor a trumpet is assumed, but they are commanded to ascend the mountain and to sound forth with their own voice. Here, however, because they were sinners to whom it must be announced, and they were dwelling below, the Prophet is not commanded to ascend a mountain, but only to exalt his voice like a trumpet, and to announce to them the wars to come. Otherwise, on the day of judgment, when in the resurrection of the dead, and the last trumpet is spoken of, it is written: 'For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall rise again incorruptible': so that just as they are to be judged at the sound of the trumpet, so Israel, dead in sin, may hear its crimes: and at the same time the people of God is called, that it may learn what kind of father it has lost, who even calls the sinner his people.

Latin:

CAPUT LVIII. Admonitio ad ostendendam populo hypocrisin & vana jejunia, veramq; jejunandi & Sabbati celebrandi rationem, cum pollicita- tione præmii ita celebrantium.

Vers. 1. CLAMA, NE CESSES] Deus, quia pœni- tentia ductis reditum jam promiserat, videns multos inter Judæos fore, qui se ei numero accenserent, tantum quod jejunassent in diebus כפרים, per Prophetam ostendit se tali pœnitentia non esse contentum, sed requirere ut si quid alieni teneant, id reddant, quia, ut dici solet, non dimit- titur peccatum, nisi restituatur ablatum, qua de re aliqua diximus libro 3. de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 10. §. 3. & in Annotatis ad eum locum: præterea, ut ab omni injustitia rebusque per legem veritis abstineatur: ad hæc, ut eximia quædam opera misericordiæ exerceantur: quomodo & Nabuchodonosorum Daniel monet 4, 24.

QUASI TUBA EXALTA VOCEM TUAM] Gutture pro tuba utere, & quantum potes attolle vocem.

IN textu nihil de jejunio in diebus כפרים habe- tur. Temere ergo id ingessit Grotius. Hypocri- sis jejuniorum in genere taxatur. Sed quia superio- ra ad tempora Christi spectabant, conveniens erit, hanc reprehensionem etiam eo referre, quemad- modum videmus maximopere Christum in diebus carnis suæ hypocrisin Judæorum reprehendisse, non modo ἐθνικῶς circa cultum Dei & legem divinam Matt. 15. & 23. Sed etiam ἰδικῶς, quoad jejunia Matt. 6. & 23. Neque dubium est hypocrisin causam fuisse excidii, ut Esaias prædixerat c. 28. ac Christus ipse Matth. 15. prædictionem illam repetens & alias non raro indicarat. Quia vero jam tum tempore Esaiæ hypocrisis summa vigebat, dehortari ab eadem & salubria instituendi jejunia, & celebrandi Sabbata præcepta his præscribere debuit Propheta, cum promissione gratiæ fidelibus morigeris exhiben- dæ. Quapropter occasione gravissimæ commina- tionis supremi supplicii hanc concionem instituis- se videtur Propheta, ut ab hypocrisi revocaret po- pulum, cui ob hypocrisin, & impœnitentiam πανω- λεθρία, & interitus miserrimus novissime impen- debat. Confert hic eleganter tubam legalem Hiero- nymus cum exaltatione vocis in annunciando Ev- angelio: Finito priori capitulo, in quo pax justis & nulla requies impiis nunciatur, præcipit Deus Esaiæ Prophetæ, ut clamet in fortitudine, & instar tubæ ex- altet vocem suam, & peccata ac scelera populi Israel di- cere non formidet, nequaquam mortem metuens, nec impriorum terricula & convitia, sed magis consideret imperantem dominum. Et quia surdas aures habeant, & audire vix possint, juxta Symmachum & Aquilam, guttur suum vertat in buccinam, quæ Hebraice dici- tur שופר, quam κερατίνην, id est, corneam interpre- tati sunt. Et supra quidem ubi Apostolis dicebatur: in montem excelsum ascende, qui evangelizas Hie- rusalem, exalta, noli timere, nec buccina assumitur nec tuba, sed montem jubentur ascendere, & voce pro- pria personare. Hic autem, quia peccatores erant, qui- bus nunciandum est, & morabantur deorsum, non ju- betur Propheta ut ascendat in montem, sed tantum ut exaltet sicut tuba vocem suam, & eis nunciet bella ventura. Alioquin in die judicii, quando in resurrectio- ne mortuorum, & novissima tuba dicitur scriptum est: canet enim tuba, & mortui resurgent incorrupti: ut quomodo illi ad vocem tubæ sunt judicandi, sic Is- rael peccato mortuus audiat scelera sua: simulq; ap- pellatur populus Dei, ut discat qualem patrem perdi- derit, qui etiam peccatorem vocet populum suum.

## 58:2
Vers. 2. FOR THEY SEEK ME FROM DAY TO DAY, AND WISH TO KNOW MY WAYS] That is, they say they wish to, as the Chaldean and Kimchi here. Thus they ask as if nothing were lacking to them except knowledge, and as if they were not doing many things which they knew to be wicked: as the following explains.

Jerome describes the hypocrisy of the Jews here with a better brush: This properly applies to the Jews, who run to the synagogues every day and meditate on the law of God, desiring to know what Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and what the rest of the saints did, and, revolving the books of the Prophets and of Moses by heart, they chant the divine commandments, to whom that will most rightly be applied: The wicked shall seek me and shall not find me. For if it is written, Everyone who seeks finds, whoever does not find is convicted of having sought wrongly. For the Lord is found by those who seek him in goodness, and is shown to those who are not incredulous to him. Since, therefore, they have abandoned the justice and judgment of God, by which names Christ is shown, as the Psalmist says: Give the king thy judgment, O God, and thy justice to the king's son: for Christ has been made for us redemption, holiness, and justice: they boast in vain of the knowledge of the law, since the saint glories not in the knowledge of the scriptures, but in works, saying: I have run the way of thy commandments, because thou hast enlarged my heart.

THEY WISH TO DRAW NEAR TO GOD] That is, they say they desire nothing more than to be reconciled to God: and they add what follows.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ME ETENIM DE DIE IN DIEM QUÆ- RUNT, ET SCIRE VIAS MEAS VOLUNT] Id est, dicunt se velle, ut hic Chaldæus & Kimchi. Ita interrogant quasi nihil praeter notitiam ipsis deesset, & quasi non multa facerent, quae sciebant iniqua esse: ut explicant sequentia.

Hieronymus Judaeorum hypocrisin hic peni- cillo meliori describit: Hoc proprie Judaeis conve- nit, qui per singulos dies ad Synagogas currunt & Dei legem meditantur, scire cupientes, quid Abraham, I- saac & Jacob, quid & caeteri sanctorum fecerint, & libros Prophetarum, ac Moysi memoriter revolventes, decantant divina mandata, quibus rectissime illud aptabitur: Quaerent me mali & non invenient. Si enim scriptum est, Omnis qui quaerit invenit, quicunque non inveniet, male quaesisse convincitur. Do- minus enim invenitur ab his, qui eum quaerunt in boni- tate, & ostenditur illis, qui non sunt ei increduli. Cum igitur justitiam judiciumque reliquerint Dei, quibus no- minibus Christus ostenditur, dicente Psalmographo: Deus judicium tuum regi da, & justitiam tuam fi- lio regis: Christus enim factus est nobis redem- ptio, sanctitas & justitia: frustra legis jactant scien- tiam, cum sanctus non in notitia scripturarum, sed in operibus glorietur, dicens: Viam mandatorum tuo- rum cucurri, quoniam dilatasti cor meum.

APPROPINQUARE DEO VOLUNT] Id est, dicunt se nihil malle, quam Deo conciliari: & addunt quod sequitur.

## 58:3
Ver. 3. WHY HAVE WE FASTED, AND THOU HAST NOT REGARDED, WE HAVE HUMBLED OUR SOULS AND THOU HAST NOT KNOWN] Since we fast so rigidly, why do you not set us free?

BEHOLD IN THE DAY OF YOUR FAST YOUR OWN WILL IS FOUND] This is now what the Prophet is commanded to say to them as if they were present: you fast indeed, but you continue to do the things that please you.

AND YOU EXACT ALL YOUR DEBTORS] That is, you drag them into prison without mercy. For this interpreter followed Symmachus and Theodotion, who have πάντας ὑποχρέως: and perhaps the LXX did not write otherwise, whose books now have the similar-sounding word ὑποχειρίως. To the Arabs, عص means to bind. Hence עצבים are the bound. You do not set others free, and how do you wish to be set free?

Latin:

Vers. 3. QUARE JEJUNAVIMUS, ET NON A- SPEXISTI, HUMILIAVIMUS ANIMAS NOSTRAS ET NESCISTI] Cum tam rigide jejunemus, cur nos non liberas?

ECCE IN DIE JEJUNII VESTRI INVENITUR VOLUNTAS VESTRA] Hoc jam est quod Propheta il- lis quasi praesentibus dicere jubetur: jejunatis quidem, sed pergitis ea facere quae vobis lubet.

ET OMNES DEBITORES VESTROS REPETI- TIS] Id est, sine misericordia in nervum abducitis. Nam secutus est hic Interpres Symmachum & Theodotionem, qui habent πάντας ὑποχρέως: & non aliter forte scripserunt LXX. quorum libri nunc habent vicina voce ὑποχειρίως. A- rabibus عص ligare. Inde עצבים sunt obligati. Non liberatis alios, & quomodo vultis liberari?

## 58:4
Ver. 4. BEHOLD YOU FAST FOR DEBATES AND STRIFE, AND STRIKE WITH THE FIST WICKEDLY] Not even on the days of fasting do you abstain from curses and evil deeds: so much have these things turned into a habit for you.

DO NOT FAST AS UNTO THIS DAY, THAT YOUR CRY MAY BE HEARD ON HIGH] In the Hebrew: as the day: that is, as you are accustomed to do on the days of כפר: so to quarrel, that your cry might be heard even in the mountains.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ECCE AD LITES ET CONTENTIONES JEJUNATIS, ET PERCUTITIS PUGNO IMPIE] Ne ipsis quidem diebus jejunii abstinetis a maledictis & malefactis: ita in consuetudinem vobis ista verterunt.

NOLITE JEJUNARE SICUT USQUE AD HUNC DIEM, UT AUDIATUR IN EXCELSO CLAMOR VESTER] In Hebraeo: sicut die: id est, pro ut in diebus כפר facere soletis: ita jurgari, ut vel in montibus clamor vester possit exaudiri.

## 58:5
Ver. 5. THAT WHICH I HAVE CHOSEN] That which I approve.

TO AFFLICT A MAN'S SOUL FOR A DAY] By 'a day' he signifies a short time. What it is to afflict oneself, the following explains.

IS IT TO BEND HIS HEAD AS A CIRCLE] From the Greek ὡς κρίκον. The Talmudists signify a rush by the word אגמון, which some interpreters here follow.

AND AN ACCEPTABLE DAY TO THE LORD]

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUOD ELEGI] Quod ego approbem.

PER DIEM AFFLIGERE HOMINEM ANI- MAM SUAM] Per diem significat exiguo tempore. Quid sit se affligere, explicant sequentia.

NUMQUID CONTORQUERE QUASI CIR- CULUM CAPUT SUUM] Ex Graeco ὡς κρίκον. Thal- mudici voce אגמון juncum significant, quod hic nonnulli interpretes sequuntur.

ET DIEM ACCEPTABILEM DOMINO] Ita exacto die Deum putatis contentum fore?

## 58:6
Ver. 6. LOOSE THE BANDS OF WICKEDNESS] Wicked bonds. The conspiracies of judges to the detriment of the innocent. Thus the Chaldean here, and soon in verse 9.

UNDO THE HEAVY BURDENS] In Hebrew: The bundles of the yoke: which the Greeks interpret as στραγγαλιὰς βιαίων συναλλαγμάτων. It signifies contracts extorted by force or fear, or usurious ones, by which the poor were oppressed. See Nehem. 5, 7.

LET THOSE WHO ARE BROKEN GO FREE] Let your kinsmen, worn down by your chains, go free. See Levit. 25, 39. For many powerful men used to despise that law. Compare Matth. 18, 30.

AND BREAK EVERY YOKE] In Hebrew: a yoke; which the LXX translate as πᾶσαν συγγραφὴν ἄδικον δίεσπα. Symmachus translates it, as Jerome testifies, in this manner: break every false bond: with the same sense as above. For whatever does not conform to what is fair and good, or to the law, is usually called false by the Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 6. DISSOLVE ALLIGATIONES IMPIETA- TIS] Nexus improbos. Coitiones judicum in fraudem in- nocentium. Ita hic Chaldaeus, & mox 9.

SOLVE FASCICULOS DEPRIMENTES] In He- braeo: Fasciculos jugi: quod Graeci interpretantur στραγγαλιὰς βιαίων συναλλαγμάτων. Significat contractus auc- extortos vi aut metu, aut foenebres, per quos opprimeban- tur pauperes. Vide Nehem. 5, 7.

DIMITTE EOS QUI CONFRACTI SUNT LI- BEROS] Consanguineos vestros vinculis vestris attritos dimittite. Vide Levit. 25, 39. Multi enim potentes eam legem spernebant. Confer Matth. 18, 30.

ET OMNE ONUS DISRUMPE] In Hebraeo: ju- gum; quod LXX. vertunt, πᾶσαν συγγραφὴν ἄδικον δίεσπα Symmachus vertit, Hieronymo teste, in hunc modum omnem cautionem falsam disrumpe: sensu eodem quo supra. Nam quicquid aut aequo & bono, aut legi non congruit, falsum Hebraeis dici solet.

## 58:7
Ver. 7. DEAL THY BREAD TO THE HUNGRY] If by chance anyone has no debtors toward whom he may show mercy, let him do good to any needy person. Loaves in those parts were such that they could be easily broken. Hence it came about that to break is said for to share. These things said here approach much to the Gospel. Compare those things in Matth. 25, 36 and following.

There lies hidden here a ὕπουλον [ulcer], concerning Christ the legislator, who brought more perfect precepts in the Gospel. Which stuck to Grotius from the School of Socinus and the Papacy. But in the Gospel there are no legal precepts: for it is a proclamation concerning the free remission of sins. And although Christ vindicated the law from corruptions, he did not increase it with new precepts, nor did any law have need of a προσθήκῃ [addition]; rather, because it was perfect, it admitted neither a πρόθεσιν [addition] nor an ἀφαίρεσιν [subtraction]. Concerning which, let those things be seen which are usually disputed elsewhere against the Socinians. We have exhibited the sum in Socinismo profligato.

AND BRING THE NEEDY AND THE WANDERING INTO THY HOUSE] Even hospitality is an excellent virtue. Matth. in the cited place, Rom. 12, 13, Hebr. 13, 2. מרודים here is rather [the wandering].

WHEN THOU SEEST THE NAKED, COVER HIM] See Matth. in the cited place; Jac. 2, 16.

AND HIDE NOT THYSELF FROM THINE OWN FLESH] Thy flesh, that is, thy kinsman from Abraham, Isaac, Jacob. LXX: ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων τῆ σπέρματός σε ἐχ᾽ ὑπερόψει. The same sense is clearly in the Chaldean. See what we have said on this matter in book 2 of De Jure Belli ac Pacis 7, 10, and in the Annotations.

Latin:

Vers. 7. FRANGE ESURIENTI PANEM TUUM] Si quis forte debitores non habeat, in quos misericordiam ostendat, cuivis egeno bene faciat. Panes in illis partibus erant tales qui facile frangerentur. Eo factum, ut fran- gere dicatur pro communicare. Multum ea quae hic di- cuntur ad Evangelium accedunt. Confer ea quae Matth. 25, 36. & sequentibus.

Latet hic ὕπουλον, de Christo legislatore, qui perfectiora præcepta in Evangelio tulerit. Quod è Schola Socini, & Papatu Grotio hæsit. At in Ev- angelio nulla sunt præcepta legalia : quod est con- cio de gratuita remissione peccatorum. Et quam- vis Christus legem vindicarit à corruptelis, non au- xit tamen eam novis præceptis, neque lex aliqua προσθήκῃ opus habuit, imo quia perfecta fuit, nul- lam vel πρόθεσιν vel ἀφαίρεσιν admisit. De quo videantur quæ advers Socinianos alias disputari so- lent. Summa exhibuimus in Socinismo profligato.

ET EGENOS VAGOSQUE INDUC IN DO- MUJM TUAM] Etiam φιλοξενία egregia est virtus. Matth. dicto loco, Rom, 12, 13. Hebr. 13, 2. מרודים hic est potius.

CUM VIDERIS NUDUM, OPERI EUM] Vide Matth. dicto loco; Jac. 2,16.

ET CARNEM TUAM NE DESPEXERIS] Car- nem tuam, id est, consanguineum tuum ex Abrahamo, Isaaco, Jacobo. LXX. ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων τῆ σπέρματός σε ἐχ᾽ ὑ- περόψει. Idem plane sensus apud Chaldæum. Vide quæ diximus hac de re libro 2. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 7,10. & in Annotatis,

## 58:8
Ver. 8. THEN SHALL THY LIGHT BREAK FORTH AS THE MORNING] Thy prosperity will succeed thy adversities, as the dawn succeeds the darkness of night.

AND THINE HEALTH SHALL SPRING FORTH SPEEDILY] τὰ ἰάματά σε ταχὺ ἀνατελεῖ. You will be quickly freed from captivity. For as every evil is a sickness, so every liberation from evils is called healing by the Hebrews. See how much negligent scribes err, who, for ἰάματα, by a slight change in letters but a great one in sense, wrote ἱμάτια. This reading, however, undoubtedly corrupt, was followed here by Tertullian, Cyprian, Ambrose, and Augustine. Jerome noted this error in this place.

AND THY RIGHTEOUSNESS SHALL GO BEFORE THY FACE] Thy probity shall be for a guide to thee into the fatherland.

AND THE GLORY OF THE LORD SHALL GATHER THEE] That is, the goodness of God, which is most glorious to God, shall follow thee. ἐραγήσει. For the Hebrew word אסף often signifies this, as appears in Num. 10:25, and the logic of the antithesis demands it, such as also above in 52:12. The Greeks translate this verb by συνάγειν and ἐπισυνάγειν: and the noun derived from it, מאסף, by ἐχατοι and by ἐραγᾶντες.

Because Grotius everywhere dreams of the Babylonian captivity, health here also in v. 8 sounds to him like liberation from captivity, but without example and without authority. But why should these things not be understood of the health of the soul or body itself? And why does he command that these be referred to the captives, as if these exhortations were given to them? Jerome compared this promise with that in Mal. 4:1 and explained it concerning the wounds of the soul. When you have not done those things which the preceding discourse narrated, and have done those things of which we have now spoken: Then thy fast shall be acceptable, and thy light shall break forth as the morning: The Sun of righteousness, and health in his wings. He who is called the sun there, is called light here. For just as the morning light dissolves the darkness, so the light of knowledge and truth puts all errors to flight. And thy healths (he says) shall spring forth speedily: For which Aquila, expressing word for word, put: And the scar of thy wound shall be quickly covered over, so that, namely, the wounds of our sins, at the rising of the sun of righteousness, may be quickly closed with a scar covered over. Brentius explains the word ארכה not as health, but as the prolongation and increase (which is noted by this word) of happiness: Thy health shall spring forth more quickly: This is to be read thus: The increase of thy happiness shall immediately germinate, that is, thy happiness shall not be deferred for long, but shall soon germinate in such a way, and shall subsequently become greater and more fortunate. This is that which is said in the twenty-eighth chapter of Deuteronomy: If thou shalt hear the voice of the Lord thy God, blessed shalt thou be in the city, in the field, blessed shall be the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle, etc. Blessed shall be thy barns, etc. That which follows AND THY RIGHTEOUSNESS SHALL GO BEFORE THY FACE, is twisted by Grotius, when he interprets it thus, Thy probity shall be for a guide to thee into the fatherland, as everyone sees. For the same thing is said as in Psalm 112: he hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor, his righteousness remaineth for ever and the end of the age: not that we are reckoned righteous before God by the merit of these works, but that he who does these works of charity from faith has before God a perpetual testimony of the righteousness which he possesses in Christ through faith. Cyril thus: Your righteousness shall go before you. It shall go before, smoothing, that is, the way of piety before you, and making rough things smooth and passable, and taking away what is steep, and as it were opening a course to all best things. THE GLORY OF THE LORD SHALL GATHER YOU: The sense is in the open: God shall preserve you gloriously and admirably in all your tribulations. Ps. 36. The Lord knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance shall be forever, etc. This is the Paraphrase of St. Cyril: The glory of God shall surround you, that is, shall gird you, and render you to be looked up to, and so that it may be a common protection for many.
