For the splendor of the saints helps not a little those who look upon them. We shall therefore be illustrious, with the divine glory surrounding and as it were clothing us, which He gives to the cultivators of righteousness.

Latin:

Vers. 8. TUNC ERUMPET QUASI MANE LU- MEN TUUM] Prosperitas tua succedet adversis, ut auro- ra tenebris nocturnis.

ET SANITAS TUA CITIUS ORIETUR] τὰ ἰάματά σε ταχὺ ἀνατελεῖ. Cito liberaberis à captivitate. Nam ut omne malum morbus, ita omnis à malis libera- tio Hebræis medicatio dicitur. Vid. quantum peccent ne- gligentes librarii, qui pro ἰάματα, levi ad litteras, sed ma- gna ad sensum mutatione scripserunt ἱμάτια. Hanc au- tem scripturam haud dubie corruptam secuti hic sunt Ter- tullianus, Cyprianus, Ambrosius, Augustinus. Notavit hunc errorem Hieronymus hoc in loco.

ET ANTEIBIT FACIEM TUAM JUSTITIA TUA] Tua probitas tibi pro duce erit in patriam.

ET GLORIA DOMINI COLLIGET TE] Id est, Dei bonitas, quæ Deo maxime gloriosa est, te subseque- tur. ἐραγήσει. Id enim sæpe significat vox Hebræa אסף, ut apparet Num. 10,25. idque exigit ratio ἀντιθέτε, quale & supra 52, 12. Græci vertunt hoc verbum per συνάγειν & ἐ- πισυνάγειν : & nomen inde deductum מאסף, per ἐχα- τοι & per ἐραγᾶντες.

Quia Grotius ubique somniat captivitatem Ba- bylonicam, sanitas etiam hic v. 8. ipsi sonat libera- tionem à captivitate, at sine exemplo, & sine auto- ritate. Cur vero hæc non de ipsa sanitate animi, vel corporis accipienda? Et quid jubet hæc ad capti- vos referre, quasi illis datæ sint hæ paræneses? Pro- missionem hanc contulit Hieronymus cum illa Mal. 4,1. & de vulneribus animæ exposuit. Quando illa non feceris, quæ præteritus sermo narravit, & ista feceris de quibus nunc diximus: Tunc acceptabile erit jejunium tuum, & erumpet mane lumen tuum: Sol justitiæ, & sanitas in pennis ejus. Qui ibi sol, hic lux dicitur. Sicut enim matutina lux solvit tenebras, ita lumen scientiæ & veritatis omnes errores fugat. Et sanitates (inquit) tuæ cito oriuntur: Pro quo Aqui- la, verbum de verbo exprimens, posuit: Et cicatrix vulneris tui cito obducetur, ut scilicet vulnera pec- catorum nostrorum ad ortum solis justitiæ, cito obdu- cta cicatrice claudantur. Brentius vocem ארכה non de sanitate, sed de prolongatione & incremento (quod notatur hac voce) felicitatis explicat: Sanitas tua citius orietur: Hoc ita legendum est: Incrementum felicitatis tuæ statim germinabit, hoc est, felicitas tua non differetur in longum, sed mox ita germinabit, & subinde major & fortunatior fiet. Hoc illud est, quod Deuteronomii capite vigesimo octavo dici- tur: Si audieris vocem Domini Dei tui, benedictus eris in civitate, in agro, benedictus fructus ventris tui, & fructus terræ tuæ, fructusq; jumentorum tuo- rum &c. Benedicta horrea tua &c. Quod sequitur ET ANTEIBIT FACIEM TUAM JUSTI- TIA TUA, torqueri à Grotio, cum ita interpre- tatur, Tua probitas tibi pro duce erit in Patriam, ne- mo non videt. Nam idem dicitur, quod Psal. 112. dispersit, dedit pauperibus, justitia ejus manet in se- culum seculi: non quod merito horum operum re- putemur coram Deo justi, sed quod qui hæc chari- tatis opera ex fide facit, habeat coram Deo perpe- tuum testimonium justitiæ, quam possidet in Chri- sto per fidem. Cyrillus ita: Præibit tibi justitia tua. Præibit autem lævigans scilicet ante pietatis viam, & aspera reddens lævia & pervia, & quod præruptum est tollens, & cursum ad omnia optima velut pate- faciens. GLORIA DOMINI COLLIGET TE: Sensus in aprico est: Deus conservabit te gloriose & admirabiliter in omnibus ærumnis tuis Psal. 36. Novit Dominus dies immaculatorum, & hæreditas eorum in æternum erit, &c. S. Cyrilli hæc est Pa- raphrasis: Gloria Dei circumdabit te, id est, cinget te, & te suspiciendum reddet, & ut commune sit mul- torum præsidium. Splendor enim sanctorum juvat haud mediocriter eos, qui intuentur. Erimus ergo illustres ambiente ac quasi amiciente nos divina gloria, quam dat justitiæ cultoribus.

## 58:9
Verse 9.

THEN YOU SHALL CALL, AND THE LORD SHALL HEAR] That is, if you shall have acted thus, God shall hear you calling.

YOU SHALL CRY, AND HE SHALL SAY: BEHOLD I AM HERE] To the one crying He shall say, I am at hand. He shall do what you shall pray for, as this Chaldean says. Compare Matt. 8, 2.

IF YOU SHALL TAKE AWAY FROM THE MIDST OF YOU THE CHAIN] That is, the yoke, of which above in 6. For there is in the Hebrew the same word מוטה, which Theodotion translates κλοιὸν. That indeed signifies a bond or a shackle.

AND SHALL CEASE TO EXTEND THE FINGER] The LXX, χειροτονίαν, but whose sense Symmachus, Aquila, and Theodotion interpret by δάκτυλον ἐκτεταμένον: if you shall cease to point out upright men with an infamous finger (as Persius speaks), and to mock their simplicity.

AND TO SPEAK WHAT DOES NOT PROFIT] In the Hebrew: words of iniquity: that is, words of violence, as the Chaldean interprets, words threatening the innocent: and the LXX perhaps intended the same, who translate ῥῆμα γογγυσμοῦ. For they use that word in the sense which I said, Exod. 15, 24. Num. 14, 2. and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

TUNC INVOCABIS, ET DOMINUS EXAU- DIET] Id est, si ita egeris, invocantem te Deus exaudiet.

CLAMABIS, ET DICET: ECCE ADSUM] Clamanti dicet, præsto sum. Faciet quod orabis, ut hic Chaldæus. Confer Matth. 8, 2.

SI ABSTULERIS DE MEDIO TUI CATE- NAM] Id est, jugum, de quo supra 6. Est enim in He- bræo vox eadem מוטה, quod Theodotio κλοιὸν vertit. Id vero nervum aut numellam significat.

ET DESIERIS EXTENDERE DIGITUM] LXX. χειροτονίαν, sed cujus sensum interpretantur Symmachus, Aquila, Theodotion per δάκτυλον ἐκτεταμένον: si desieris in- fami digito (ut Persius loquitur) denotare viros probos, & eorum simplicitati illudere.

ET LOQUI QUOD NON PRODEST] In He- bræo: verba iniquitatis: id est, verba violentiæ, ut Chal- dæus interpretatur, verba comminantia innocentibus: & idem forte voluerunt LXX. qui transferunt ῥῆμα γογγυσ- μõ. Utuntur enim ea voce in sensu, quem dixi Exod. 15, 24. Num. 14, 2. & alibi.

## 58:10
Verse 10. WHEN YOU SHALL POUR OUT YOUR SOUL TO THE HUNGRY] Soul signifies benevolence, and here by metonymy, the effect of benevolence. See Rom. 12, 8. 2 Cor. 9, 7.

YOUR LIGHT SHALL RISE IN DARKNESS] The same sense as above in 8. The Hebrews love to say the same things often, with words changed not a little.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CUM EFFUDERIS ESURIENTI ANI- MAM TUAM] Anima benevolentiam significat, & hic κατὰ μετωνυμίαν, effectum benevolentiæ. Vide Roman. 12, 8. 2. Cor. 9, 7.

ORIETUR IN TENEBRIS LUX TUA] Idem sensus qui supra 8. Amant Hebræi eadem sæpe dicere, mu- tatis nonnihil verbis.

## 58:11
Verse 11. AND THE LORD SHALL GIVE YOU REST ALWAYS] He shall give you a durable seat. The Chaldean derives this word not from נוח, but from נחה, which is to lead. The Greeks: ἔσται ὁ Θεός σου μετὰ σοῦ διαπαντός.

AND SHALL FILL YOUR SOUL WITH SPLENDORS] In the Hebrew: He shall fill you in drought (that is, in a time of lack of rain, and consequently also of famine). The Greeks: ἐμπλησθήσῃ καθάπερ ἐπιθυμεῖ ἡ ψυχή σου. As you have done, so shall it be done to you.

AND HE SHALL DELIVER THY BONES] חלץ signifies both to deliver and to make fat. The latter meaning fits this passage better, which the LXX also follow, and Jerome has in his notes, and the passage in Proverbs 15:30 confirms it. The Chaldean refers these things to the resurrection: in sense indeed, but not in the primitive meaning.

AND SHALL BE LIKE A WATERED GARDEN] You will flourish, you will bloom.

AND LIKE A FOUNTAIN OF WATERS, WHOSE WATERS SHALL NOT FAIL] Literally in Hebrew: As a spring of waters, whose waters do not deceive: that is, you will be abounding in all good things.

Both senses of verse 11 agree: He will give you rest, and GOD will lead you always. However, it does not precisely refer to a seat in the land of Canaan: as Grotius seems to wish. For not all the pious could have a seat there. In droughts, that is, in the scarcity and dearth of things, He will satisfy your soul, and will make fat your bones, and you will be like a watered garden, and like a springing fountain of waters, whose waters shall not fail; that is, when others, because of the barrenness of the land, shall waste away with hunger, you will be satisfied and will stand firm against such calamities, and when others shall perish and fail in the heat of afflictions, you will flourish, nor will refreshment and consolation ever be lacking to you; as in Prov. 11.

it is said, The soul that blesses shall be made fat; and he that waters, shall be watered also himself.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET REQUIEM TIBI DABIT DOMINUS SEMPER] Dabit tibi sedem durabilem. Chaldæus hoc verbum derivat non à נוח, sed à נחה, quod est deducere. Græci: ἔςαι ὁ Θεός σου μετὰ σοῦ διαπαντός.

ET IMPLEBIT SPLENDORIBUS ANIMAM TUAM] In Hebræo: Implebit in siccitate (id est, tempore ἀνομβρίας, ac proinde & famis) te. Græci: ἐμπλησθήση κα- θάπερ ἐπιθυμεῖ ἡ ψυχή σε. Ut tu fecisti, sic tibi fiet.

ET OSSA TUA LIBERABIT] חלץ & liberare & pinguefacere significat. Posterior significatio huic loco magis congruit, quam & LXX. sequuntur, & in notis suis habet Hieronymus, eamque firmat locus Proverb. 15, 30. Chaldæus ad resurrectionem hæc refert: sensu vero, sed non primitivo.

ET ERIT SICUT HORTUS IRRIGUUS] Vire- bis, florebis.

ET SICUT FONS AQUARUM, CUJUS NON DEFICIENT AQUÆ] Ad verbum in Hebræo: Ut sca- tebra aquarum, cujus aquæ non fallunt: id est, eris omnibus bonis affluens.

Uterque sensus v. 11. convenit: Requiem tibi dabit, & deducet te DEUS semper. Non autem re- spicitur præcise sedes in terra Canaan: uti velle vi- detur Grotius. Non enim omnes pii illic sedem habere potuêre. In siccitatibus, id est, in rerum pe- nuria & caritate saturabit animam tuam, & ossa tua impinguabit, & eris quasi hortus irriguus, & sicut fons aquarum scaturiens, cujus non deficient aquæ; id est, cum alii, propter terræ sterilitatem, fame contabescent, saturaberis & firmus adversus ejus- modi calamitates constabis, & cum alii æstu affli- ctionum peribunt, & deficient, tu virebis, neq; un- quam tibi refectio & consolatio deerit; ut Prov. 11.

dicitur, Anima, quæ benedicit, impinguabitur; & qui inebriat, ipse quoq́, inebriabitur.

## 58:12
Ver. 12.

AND THEY SHALL BUILD IN THEE THE DESOLATIONS OF AGES] That is, places long desolate not only from the devastation made by Nebuchadnezzar, but also that which was made by Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser and Sennacherib, shall by you be raised up again into cities and towns and villages.

THE FOUNDATIONS OF GENERATION AND GENERATION THOU SHALT RAISE UP] That is, which may last through many ages of men.

AND THOU SHALT BE CALLED THE BUILDER OF HEDGES] In Hebrew: Stopping up breaches, namely of walls. For גדר which is here in the Hebrew, is the very word from which Gadir was called a city by the Phoenicians, which Hesychius translates as περίφραγμα (enclosure), Pliny as a hedge, Avienus in Dionysius as a place hedged in on all sides, and in Ora maritima as a fenced place.

TURNING PATHS INTO REST] The LXX, as indeed Jerome cites, τὰς τρίβυς τὰς ἀναμέσον πάυσεις, that is, as he himself says the Jews interpret it, you will build such high walls that no enemy will be able to enter, and the entry of all enemies will be prohibited. Literally, turning paths to resting. You will leave no access for those lying in wait.

It is a general promise, which Grotius rashly restricts and determines without the text preceding, only τῇ ὑποθέσει δυλεύων (serving the hypothesis). These things are promised to the pious and faithful, but their duties are described at the same time; he addresses them, not Jerusalem, not the cities of Judea. The text according to the Hebrew truth stands thus: THEY SHALL BUILD FROM THEE THE DESOLATIONS OF THE AGE, THOU SHALT RAISE UP THE FOUNDATIONS FROM GENERATION TO GENERATION, THOU SHALT BE CALLED THE RESTORER OF THE BREACH, THE RESTORER OF PATHS, TO DWELL IN QUIET. By which nothing else is signified than that he who is beneficent and liberal to the poor will be so fortunate that he will even build up those things which were desolate, and will restore and illustrate his own family, which had been obscured and collapsed, and will bring back from it a distinguished name, as a restorer of his country or his family, of the Church or the Republic, as Brentius and Osiander have rightly expressed. There is nothing here about the return and rebuilding of Jerusalem; but those are general statements, and facts suitable to any beneficent persons, which cannot be restricted to the captive Jews. Therefore, when Grotius says that the desolate places, which had been devastated by Nebuchadnezzar, Tiglath-Pileser, Shalmaneser, and Sennacherib, were to be raised up again into cities and towns and villages, it is a purely arbitrary interpretation (ἐπίλυσις), which rests on no foundation. And who is that person whom the Prophet addresses, THEY SHALL BE BUILT IN THEE? Must it be believed that Judea is being addressed? It is not said in the Hebrew, they shall be built in thee, but from thee, nor does the name DESOLATIONS OF THE AGE fit Jerusalem, which was desolate for seventy years according to the LXX. Nor does it appear that Judea is addressed by any indication; indeed, the discourse does not suit it, in which anyone at all who pours out his soul to the hungry and fills or satisfies the afflicted soul—that is, who from the heart and as if pouring out his very heart refreshes the miserable out of true compassion (Grotius wrongly explains the phrase "to pour out" as "to pour out benevolence," because "soul" signifies benevolence, without any example from Scripture)—is introduced indefinitely and perpetually, and to him, whoever he may be, these promises are made: such as occur everywhere else, where there is no place for a commentary on the rebuilding of Jerusalem. E. g. Psalm XXXVII. 21 ff. The righteous shows mercy and gives; for those who bless him shall inherit the earth, but those who curse him shall be cut off. The steps of a man are directed by the Lord, and He shall delight in his way; and his seed shall be in blessing. The righteous shall inhabit the land, etc. Nor were the foundations thus raised after the return of the Jews, that they have lasted through MANY ages of men. Jerome has already noted this Jewish gloss, which Grotius observes here from Jerome; yet he prefers even in this passage to adhere to the Jews rather than to the Doctors of the Church, and therefore he did not hesitate to bend the Prophet's meaning to a part of the words. It is helpful, however, to hear Jerome himself, explaining the Jews' opinion and his own: These things the Jews and the friends of the letter that kills refer only to the restoration of the cities of the Palestinians. And they contend that they were either done under Zerubbabel and Ezra and Nehemiah, or will be in the last time: And to the restoration of Jerusalem, and that the deepest foundations are to be made in the circuit of the cities, and such high walls are to be built, that no enemy can enter, and the entry of all enemies into them is prohibited. But we, following the order of the explanation undertaken, say that those things which had been deserted among the Jews are being built in the Church, not for a short time, but forever: and its foundations from both peoples: that is, that is, to be raised up in two generations. Whence the Apostle said: As a wise Architect I have laid the foundation, another builds upon it, but let everyone see what he builds upon it. And in another place: We are God's husbandry, God's building. And again, built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, and to call it, or him who is born in it, the builder of hedges: Of whom we read in the Psalm: A man is born in it, and the Most High himself has founded it. Which hedges and walls, for this is what the Greek word φραγμούς signifies, Scripture commemorates as being surrounded by a field and vineyards: You brought a vine out of Egypt, you cast out the nations and planted it. And a little later: Why have you broken down its wall, and all who pass by the way gather its grapes? And in this same Prophet: The vineyard has become love, which describing in beautiful language, he added: I have built a tower, and surrounded it with a wall. He who destroys it, according to Ecclesiastes, the serpent will bite him. Which is therefore surrounded, so that the access of all beasts into the vineyard of God may be prohibited. But that is the crooked serpent, who deceived Eve in Paradise. Which sense is akin to our explanation, for we said that the restorer of the family, or even of the fatherland, is indicated, which must be understood not only with respect to the Republic, but primarily with respect to the Church, of which the most powerful account must always be held. Thus also our blessed Luther interpreted these promises: They are notable promises, that even in this life they will abound with every kind of good things: As it is said: give and it shall be given to you. LIGHT signifies happiness, peace, prosperity, etc. AND YOUR RIGHTEOUSNESS SHALL GO BEFORE YOUR FACE, Good works will confirm your conscience. THE GLORY OF THE LORD SHALL GATHER YOU. From that testimony of your conscience and from your works you will be made certain that GOD wishes you well, and approves your works. THEN YOU SHALL CALL: He promises certain help even in tribulation. For the prayer of a man walking in faith is always heard. THE DESERT PLACES SHALL BE BUILT IN YOU, You will be happy in all your deeds. You will help many, you will benefit many, and you will be the cause of many excellent things not only privately but also publicly, etc. Thus Naaman the Syrian saves his people. YOU SHALL LAY FOUNDATIONS, you will establish things that are salutary and lasting either in the Polity or in the Church: AND YOU SHALL BE CALLED THE BUILDER OF HEDGES. Hope signifies in the Hebrew manner, you will benefit all the remnants, as much to the Churches as to the Polities, which you will establish.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET ÆDIFICABUNTUR IN TE DESERTA SE- CULORUM] Id est, loca diu deserta non tantum à va- statione per Nabuchodonosarem facta, sed & illa quæ fa- cta est per Teglathphalassarum & Salmanasarum & Senna- cheribum, per te rursum in urbes & oppida & vicos eri- gentur.

FUNDAMENTA GENERATIONIS ET GENE- RATIONIS SUSCITABIS] Id est, quæ per multas ho- minum ætates durent.

ET VOCABERIS ÆDIFICATOR SEPIUM] In Hebræo: Obstruens hiatus, scilicet mœnium. Nam גדר quod hic in Hebræo est, id ipsum est verbum, unde Gadir urbs Phœnicibus dicta, quod περίφραγμα vertit Hesy- chius, Plinius sepem, Avienus in Dionysio locum undi- que septum, in Ora maritima conseptum locum.

AVERTENS SEMITAS IN QUIETEM] LXX. ut quidem citat Hieronymus, τὰς τρίβυς τὰς ἀναμέσον πάυσεις, id est, ut ipse interpretari dicit Judæos, tam excel- fos muros ædificabis, ut nullus hostium possit intrare, & omnium inimicorum prohibeatur ingressus. Ad verbum, convertens semitas ad quiescendum. Nullum insidiatoribus aditum relinques.

Generalis est promissio, quam temere restrin- git Grotius, atq; determinat non præeunte textu, solum τῇ ὑποθέσει δυλεύων. Piis & fidelibus hæc promittuntur, sed officia simul eorum describun- tur, illos compellat, non Hierosolyma, non civita- tes Judææ. Textus juxta Hebraicam veritatem ita habet: ÆDIFICABUNT DE TE DESERTA SECULI, EXCITABIS FUNDAMENTA A GENERATIONE IN GENERATIONEM, VOCABERIS INSTAURATOR RUPTU- RÆ, RESTITUTOR SEMITARUM, UT QUIETE HABITETUR. Quibus nihil aliud significatur, quam beneficum & liberalem in pauperes tam felicem fore, ut ea etiam quæ deserta erant, ædificet, & familiam suam obscu- ratam, & collapsam instauret, ac illustret, nomenq; insigne inde reportet, instauratoris patriæ aut fa- miliæ suæ, Ecclesiæ aut Reipublicæ, ut Brentius & Osiander recte expresserunt. Nihil hic de reditu & reædificatione Hierosolymæ; sed generalia sunt dicta illa, & facta beneficis quibusvis convenien- tia, quæ ad Judæos captivos restringi non possunt. Cum ergo loca deserta, quæ per Nabuchodonosa- rum, Teglathphalassarum, Salmanassarum, & Sen- nacheribum vastata erant, rursus in urbes & oppi- da & vicos erigenda dicit Grotius, mere arbitraria est ἐπίλυσις, quæ nullo nititur fundamento. Et quisnam ille est, quem compellat Propheta, Æ- DIFICABUNTUR IN TE? Num Judæam compellari credendum est? Non dicitur in Ebræo, ædificabuntur in te, sed de te, neque per LXX. an- nos desertæ Hierosolymæ nomen DESERTA SECULI congruit. Nec compellari Judæam ullo indicio apparet, imo non convenit oratio; in qua perpetuo indefinite quivis, qui esurienti ani- mam effundit, & animam afflictam explet vel sa- turat, hoc est, qui ex animo & quasi cor effundens miseros reficit ex commiseratione vera (perpe- ram Grotius phrasin effundere explicat, per ef- fundere benevolentiam, quod anima benevolen- tiam significet, citra scripturæ exemplum) intro- ducitur, illique promiscue, quicunque is fuerit, hæ promissiones fiunt: quales passim alibi occur- runt, ubi nullus locus est Commentario de re- ædificanda Jerusalem. E. g. Psal. XXXVI. 22. seqq. Justus miseretur & tribuet; quia benedicentes ejus hæreditabunt terram, maledicentes autem ei disse- ribunt. Apud Dominum gressus hominis dirigen- tur, & viam ejus volet; & semen illius in benedi- ctione erit. Justi inhabitabunt terram &c. Nec fundamenta post reditum Judæorum ita suscitata, ut per MULTAS hominum ætates durârint. Ju- daicam istam glossam notavit jam Hieronymus, quod hic ex Hieronymo observat Grotius, ma- vult tamen etiam hoc in loco potius Judæis, quam Ecclesiæ Doctoribus, adhærescere, ideoque sen- tentiam Prophetæ in verborum partem flecte- re non dubitavit. Juvat autem audire ipsummet Hieronymum, Judæorum suamque sententiam exponentem: Hæc Judæi & amici tantum occi- dentis literæ ad instaurationem referunt urbium Pa- læstinorum. Et vel facta sub Zorobabel & Esdra & Nehemia, vel in ultimo tempore futura contendunt: Et ad instaurationem Hierusalem, & in circuitu civitatum altissima fundamenta facienda, & tam excelsos muros ædificandos, ut nullus hostium possit intrare, & omnium in eas inimicorum prohibeatur ingressus. Nos autem sequentes captæ explanatio- nis ordinem, quæ deserta fuerant in Judæis, dicimus ædificari in Ecclesia, non ad breve tempus, sed in perpetuum: & fundamenta illius ex utroque po- pulo: id est, id est, in duabus generationibus susci- tanda. Unde dicebat Apostolus: Quasi sapiens Architectus fundamentum posui, alius superædi- ficet, unusquisque autem videat, quid superædifi- cet. Et in alio loco: Dei agricultura, Dei ædifi- catio sumus. Et iterum, ædificati super funda- mentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum, & vocan- dam eam, sive eum qui natus est in ea, ædificato- rem sepium: De quo in Psalmo legimus: Homo na- tus est in ea, & ipse fundavit eam altissimus. Quas sepes atque macerias, hoc enim Græcus sermo signi- ficat φραγμούς, agro & vineis circumdari Scriptu- ra commemorat: Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti, ejecisti gentes & plantasti eam. Et post paululum: Quare destruxisti maceriam ejus, & vindemiant eam omnes, qui transeunt viam? Et in hoc eodem Propheta: Vinea facta est dilectio, quam pulchro sermone describens, intulit: Ædificavi turrem, & maceria circumdedi. Quam qui destruxerit, jux- ta Ecclesiasten, mordebit eum coluber. Quæ ideo circumdata est, ut omnium bestiarum in vineam Dei prohibeatur accessus. Iste est autem coluber tortuosus, qui decepit Evam in Paradiso. Qui sen- sus nostræ explicationi affinis est, nam instaurato- rem diximus indigitari familiæ, aut patriæ etiam, quod non Reipublicæ solum, sed imprimis Ec- clesiæ respectu, cujus potissima semper habenda ratio, intelligendum. Sic etiam B. Lutherus no- ster has promissiones interpretatus est: Sunt insi- gnes promissiones, quod etiam in hac vita omni bono- rum genere misericordes affluent: Sicut dicitur: date & dabitur vobis. LUMEN significat felici- tatem, pacem, prosperitatem &c. ET ANTEI- BIT FACIEM TUAM JUSTITIA TUA, Bona opera conscientiam tuam confirmabunt. GLO- RIA DOMINI COLLIGET TE. Ex illo te- stimonio conscientiæ tuæ & ex operibus tuis certus redderis, DEUM tibi bene velle, & probare tua opera. TUNC INVOCABIS: Promittit etiam in tribulatione certum auxilium. Nam oratio viri in fide ambulantis semper est exaudita. ÆDIFI- CABUNTUR IN TE DESERTA, Felix eris in omnibus tuis factis. Multos juvabis, multis pro- deris, & eris causa multarum optimarum rerum non solum privatim sed etiam publice &c. Sic Naaman Syrus servat suum populum. FUNDA- MENTA JACIES, salutaria & duratura consti- tues sive in Politia, sive in Ecclesia: ET VOCA- BERIS ÆDIFICATOR SEPIUM. Spes signi- ficat more Ebraico, reliquiis omnibus proderis, tam Ecclesiis quam Politiis, quas constitues.

## 58:13
Vers. 13. IF YOU TURN AWAY YOUR FOOT FROM THE SABBATH

YOUR] He wishes all the other things, which indeed could be observed in exile, to be understood from one precept. To turn away the foot from the Sabbath: that is, to make no journeys on that day, except very short ones, for the sake of going to the Synagogue, or for moderate pleasure.

TO DO YOUR WILL ON MY HOLY DAY] It must be repeated from the common source [ἀπὸ κοινῦ] you shall turn away, that is, you shall abstain: Your will: that is, gain, as the Chaldean rightly explains here.

God is not concerned about the interrupting of journeys on the Sabbath day; He wishes the foot to be turned away from the Sabbath, so that they may restrain themselves, lest they indulge their own will and mind on the holy day of the Lord, and contaminate the Sabbath with wicked conversation. Therefore there is no need for the word YOU SHALL TURN AWAY to be repeated from the common source. Since the sense is plain, and the words cohere very well in this way: If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, so that you do not do your will on my holy day.

Vers. eod. AND YOU SHALL CALL THE SABBATH DELIGHTFUL, AND THE HOLY OF THE LORD GLORIOUS] In Hebrew: And you shall call the Sabbath delights, (supply, your own) and sacred to the Lord and glorious. On the Sabbath the Jews both rejoiced, and praised God, and were dressed more splendidly than on other days.

AND SHALL GLORIFY HIM] You shall have honor for that day. How that is to be done, follows.

WHILE YOU DO NOT DO YOUR WAYS] By undertaking no journey, except such as we have said.

AND YOUR WILL IS NOT FOUND] In Hebrew: And by not finding your will: that is, by making no gain, as the Chaldean again well [explains] here.

UT LOQUARIS SERMONEM] It will be better, but by speaking the word, so that ו stands for an adversative, which is not rare. Understand sermonem κατ' ἐξοχὴν as the word of God, that is, the law. The Chaldean and the LXX wish for a negative to be tacitly repeated here, and they understand the word as irascible.

Nimis jejuna est glossa] That gloss is too jejune, concerning clothes or the Sabbath journey. For God was not attending to those external things, but was requiring spiritual rest and the sanctification of the Sabbath. We see, however, that Grotius has chosen almost everywhere to strenuously ἰsdaizein. When God here reproves the eternal hypocrisy in the fasts and Sabbaths among the Jews, and prescribes the true reason for a spiritual fast and Sabbath, Grotius relapses to those external things, to more splendid clothes, as if those would procure splendor and glory for the Sabbath before God, and to the intermission of journeys. It is manifest that a far different glory than that of splendid clothes is indicated here, and that material ways are not being regarded, but the ways of sinners: and that not only the intermission of gain is prohibited, but the intermission of any vicious desires of the will whatsoever, i.e., a cessation from evil works, ways, and desires. Quod recte exposuit Cyrillus:] Which Cyril rightly explained: Therefore if anyone ceases from his own works, or hands over the command of his own will to the sacrosanct laws, this person sabbatizes spiritually, and truly celebrates the holy day. This is also shown to us by the prophecy which is at hand, the prayer. For if, he says, you turn away your foot from the Sabbaths, so that you do not do your own wills on the holy day. That: You shall turn away your foot from the Sabbaths, is nothing else, as I judge, than that one should not do what one might wish, nor pursue the paths of one's own desire. For that the scope of human wills looks toward pleasure, the most wise Paul will confirm, writing: For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I hate, this I do. For I delight in the law of God, as far as the inner man is concerned, but I see another law, which fights against the law of my mind, and makes me captive to the law of sin, which is in my members. Those therefore who wish to be approved by God must bravely and youthfully oppose their own will: and those who follow His divine laws in all things must briskly enter upon the admirable way of justice. And afterwards: submissively therefore and tractable and compliant characters offer to God a tender rest on the Sabbath, or a spiritual Sabbath-keeping; those who wish to observe this without the mark of reproach will not lift a foot to work, that is, they do not proceed to the act of things, but rather celebrate a holy and useful rest, from most shameful, I say, and detestable overcome anger and fury, and to place a door and a bolt upon the tongue. There is, therefore, no reason why we should here abandon the LXX Interpreters in explaining the words, THAT YOU MAY SPEAK A WORD, and understand the word of God. For those things cohere in the text as negative precepts. (1.) Not to make our ways impious and iniquitous, which is a most received exhortation among the Prophets, namely, that having deserted our own ways, we should walk in the ways of the Lord, that each one should turn from his evil way, that the impious should be converted from his ways, Jerem. 3. Ezech. 18. & 33. Jon. 3. So that the Sabbath of the Lord may be holy and glorious, it is necessary that you desert your way, which is impiety and iniquity, and walk in the way of the Lord. (2.) Not to do our own will, or that our will should be found, not to indulge our depraved will by doing those things which please our flesh. (3.) Not to speak our own word, to which we are too prone by nature. An improper, calumnious, scandalous word, or even, as Brentius explains, a word contrary to the rest of the Sabbath, or those economic mandates by which a family is distracted from the sanctification of the Sabbath. Which are manifest periphrases of repentance. For not to do one's own, but God's will, not to walk in one's own, but in God's way, not to speak one's own, but God's word, is to perform true repentance, and to offer true obedience to the word of God, and to study holiness, in heart, mouth, and deed, which three the Prophet has encompassed in that triple precept.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SI AVERTERIS A SABBATO PEDEM

TUUM] Ex uno præcepto cætera omnia, quæ quidem in exsilio observari poterant, vult intelligi. Avertere pedem à sabbato: id est, nulla itinera eo die facere, nisi pauxilla, Synagogæ adeundæ, aut modicæ oblectationis causa.

FACERE VOLUNTATEM IN DIE SANCTO MEO] Repetendum ἀπὸ κοινῦ averteris, id est, absti- nueris: Voluntatem tuam: id est, quæstum, ut hic recte explicat Chaldæus.

Non de itineribus intermittendis Sabbati die solicitus Deus est; averti vult pedem à Sabbato, ut contineant se, ne voluntati animoque suo in- dulgeant in die sancto Domini, & Sabbatum pra- va conversatione contaminent. Non ergo opus est, ut ἀπὸ κοινῦ repetatur verbum AVERTE- RIS. Cum sensus planus sit, & optime cohæ- reant verba h. m. Si averteris à Sabbato pedem tuum, ne facias voluntatem tuam in die sancto meo.

Vers. eod. ET VOCAVERIS SABBATUM DELI- CATUM, ET SANCTUM DOMINI GLORIOSUM] In Hebræo: Et vocaveris sabbatum delicias, (supple, tuas) & sacrum Domino ac gloriosum. In Sabbato & gaudebant Judæi, & Deum laudabant, & splendidius quam diebus cæteris vestiebantur.

AC GLORIFICAVERIS EUM] Honorem ei diei habueris. Quomodo id faciendum sit, sequitur.

DUM NON FACIS VIAS TUAS] Nullum iter, nisi quale diximus, suscipiendo.

ET NON INVENITUR VOLUNTAS TUA] In Hebræo: Et non inveniendo voluntatem tuam: id est, quæ- stum nullum faciendo, ut hic iterum bene Chaldæus.

UT LOQUARIS SERMONEM] Melius erit, sed loquendo sermonem, ut sit ו pro adversativa, quod non ra- rum. Sermonem κατ' ἐξοχὴν intellige Dei sermonem, id est, legem. Chaldæus & LXX. negativam hic tacite re- petitam volunt, & sermonem intelligunt iracundum.

Nimis jejuna est glossa illa, de vestibus aut itinere Sabbati. Deus enim non externa illa atten- debat, sed spiritualem quietem, Sabbatique san- ctificationem requirebat. Videmus autem, quod ubivis fere elegerit Grotius strenue ἰsdaizein. Quum Deus æternam hypocrisin in jejuniis & sab- batis penes Judæos hic redarguat, & veram ra- tionem spiritualis jejunii & Sabbati præscribat, re- labitur Grotius ad externa illa, ad vestes splendi- diores, quasi illæ splendorem & gloriam Sabba- to conciliarent coram Deo, & ad itinerum inter- missionem. Manifestum est, longe aliam gloriam, quam splendidarum vestium hic indicari, & vias non materiales respici, sed vias peccatorum: ne- que quæstus tantum intermissionem, sed quarum- vis vitiosarum libidinum voluntatis prohiberi, h. e. cessationem ab operibus, viis & libidinibus malis. Quod recte exposuit Cyrillus: Ergo si quis à suis operibus cessat, aut suæ voluntatis imperium sacro- sanctis tradit legibus, hic sabbatizat spiritualiter, & sanctum diem vere celebrat. Hoc etiam nobis o- stendit Prophetia, quæ præ manibus est, oratio. Si enim, inquit, averteris pedem tuum à Sabbatis, ut non facias voluntates tuas in die sancta. Illud: Averteris pedem tuum à Sabbatis, aliud nihil est, ut ego censeo, nisi ut non agat, quæ quis voluerit, nec propriæ cupiditatis semitas persequatur. Nam hu- manarum voluntatum scopum ad voluptatem specta- re, confirmabit sapientissimus Paulus, scribens: Non enim quod volo, hoc facio bonum, sed quod odi malum, hoc ago. Delector enim lege Dei, quod ad interiorem hominem attinet, video autem aliam legem, quæ repugnat legi mentis meæ, & captivum me reddit lege peccati, quæ est in membris meis. Qui ergo à Deo probari volunt, fortiter ac juveniliter suam voluntatem oppugnare debent: & qui divinas e- jus leges per omnia sequuntur, admirabilem justitiæ viam alacriter inire oportet. Et postea: Submisse igitur & tractabiles & fequaces mores tenerum Deo præstant in Sabbato otium, vel spiritualem Sabbati- smum; quem qui volunt fine reprehensionis nota cole- re, non levabunt ad opus pedem, id est, non ad rerum actum pergunt, sed potius sanctum & utile celebrant otium, à turpissimis, inquam, & detestandis ac Deo in- visis negotiis. Eos vult etiam iram ac furorem vince- re, & fores ac repagulum linguæ apponere. Non er- go est, quod hic LXX. Interpp. in explicandis verbis, UT LOQUARIS SERMONEM, relin- quamus, & verbum Dei intelligamus. Cohærent e- nim illa in textu,ceu præcepta negativa. (1.) Non facere vias nostras impias & iniquas, quæ exhortatio receptissima est penes Prophetas, ut scilicet deser- tis viis nostris ambulemus in viis Domini,ut rever- tatur quisque à via sua mala, ut convertatur impius à viis suis, Jerem. 3. Ezech. 18. & 33. Jon. 3. ut ergo Sabbatum Domini sacrum & gloriosum sit,necesse est viam tuam, quæ impietas est, & iniquitas,dese- ras,& viam Domini ambules. (2.) Non facere volun- tatem nostram, vel ut inveniatur voluntas nostra, non indulgere pravæ nostræ voluntati faciendo ea,quæ carni nostræ placuerint. (3.) Non loqui ser- monem nostrum,ad quem nimis propensi sumus na- tura.Sermonem improbum,calumniosum,scanda- losum, vel etiam,ut Brentius explicat, Sermonem quieti Sabbati contrarium, vel mandata œconomi- ca ea, quibus familia abstrahitur à sanctificatione Sabbati. Quæ sunt manifestæ periphrases pœni- tentiæ. Non enim facere suam, sed Dei volunta- tem, non ambulare in sua, sed in Dei via, non lo- qui suum,sed Dei sermonem,est veram agere pœ- nitentiam, & veram verbo Dei præstare obedien- tiam,& sanctitati studere,corde, ore, atque opere, quæ tria triplici illo præcepto complexus est Pro- pheta.

## 58:14
Vers. 14.

THEN YOU SHALL DELIGHT IN THE LORD] That is, if you do these things, God granting, you will have that with which you may be delighted. Compare Ps. 33, 21. & 37, 4. AND I WILL LIFT YOU UP ABOVE THE HEIGHTS OF THE EARTH] In the Hebrew: I will make you be carried (namely by chariots) upon the high land: that is, Judea, as in Deuteronomy 32, 13. For Judea is more mountainous than the neighboring lands. AND I WILL FEED YOU WITH THE HERITAGE OF JACOB YOUR FATHER] I will cause you to live from the fruits of your ancestral land. FOR THE MOUTH OF THE LORD HAS SPOKEN] That is, God has so decreed: as the Chaldean rightly translates here. He touched upon the sense of the former promise in some way: For the tranquility of conscience is a spiritual delight, which we have from peace with God: For this is delight in the Lord, joy in the Holy Spirit Rom. 14. The second is clearly turned and distorted to a bodily return. For neither did any of those return to that place whom the Prophet was addressing, nor do others, to whom these promises pertain, desire that. God does not wish to carry the observers of the Sabbath by chariot, but to lift them up by glory: not upon the high mountains of Judea, but upon the heights of the earth, because compared to those things which are sublime in the world, they are to be adorned with glory and Majesty, indeed to be lifted up above all the glory and height of the world. For what can be conferred upon such great majesty as that we are children of God? Is it not a more excellent Majesty to be a child of God than to be the child of the most powerful Monarch of this earth? The third promise is taken too meagerly concerning the fruits of the land of Canaan: I WILL FEED YOU WITH THE HERITAGE OF YOUR FATHER JACOB. For although these things are said as if a temporal inheritance and fertility were being promised, yet that custom of Scripture is most well-known, that it describes the spiritual things of the heavenly kingdom with the words of this age. Nor indeed would that promise, understood in that way concerning earthly things, do anything for the observers of the spiritual Sabbath and true believers:

when yet it is certain that those promises are general, and made not only to the captive Jews, but to all believers whatsoever. And the blessing promised to Jacob, and the inheritance, is far more eminent and august than what ought to be defined by these temporal things. And therefore Brentius rightly: To one who keeps the true Sabbath, a far more excellent inheritance is promised than that which is of this earth. For it was said in Genesis, chapter twenty-eight, to the Patriarch Jacob: In your seed shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed. By this saying, Christ the Son of God is promised from the posterity of Jacob, who brings with Him heavenly blessing to all who believe in Him. Therefore, the inheritance of the Patriarch Jacob is the blessing of all heavenly goods, which come to believers on account of the seed of Jacob, who is Christ. After, therefore, he who performs repentance is adopted as a child of God on account of Christ, he becomes also on account of Him the heir of every blessing, and thus of every heavenly majesty, than which benefit there is nothing more sublime nor more excellent.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

TUNC DELECTABERIS IN DOMINO] Id est, si ista facies, Deo dante habebis, quo te oblectes. Con- fer. Pf. 33, 21. & 37, 4. ET SUSTOLLAM TE SUPER ALTITUDINES TERRÆ] In Hebræo: Vectari te faciam (nempe curri- bus) super excelsam terram: id est, Judæam, ut Deutero- nomii 32, 13. Est enim Judæa vicinis terris montosior. ET CIBABO TE HÆREDITATE JACOB PA- TRIS TUI] Faciam ut vivas de fructibus terræ avitæ. OS ENIM DOMINI LOCUTUM EST] Id est, Deus ita decrevit: ut recte hic vertit Chaldæus. Prioris promissionis sensum utcunque attigit: Nam tranquillitas conscientiæ est delectatio spiri- tualis,quam ex pace cumDeo habemus: Nam hæc est delectatio in Domino,gaudium in Spiritu San- cto Rom. 14. Secunda plane vertitur & detor- quetur ad reditum corporalem. Nam nec illorum quisquam eo rediit, quos compellabat Propheta, nec alii, ad quos spectant istæ promissiones, id de- siderant. Non curru vehere Deus vult Sabbati ob- servatores, sed gloria evehere: non super altos mon- tes Judææ,sed super excelsa terræ,quod præ iis,quæ in seculo sublimia sunt,gloria & Majestate ornandi sint, imo supra omnem gloriam & altitudinem mundi evehendi. Nam quid tantæ majestati,quod filii Dei sumus, conferri potest? annon excellen- tior Majestas est, esse filium Dei, quam esse filium potentissimi Monarchæ hujus terræ? Tertia pro- missio nimis jejune de fructibus terræ Cananeæ ac- cipitur: CIBABO TE HÆREDITATE PA- TRIS TUI JACOB. Quamvis enim hæc ita di- cantur, ac si hæreditas & fertilitas temporalis pro- mittatur, notissima tamen est illa consuetudo Scri- pturæ, quod verbis hujus seculi describat res spiri- tuales regni cœlestis.Neque vero illa promissio ita intellecta de rebus terrenis quicquam ad observa- tores Sabbati spiritualis, verosq; fideles faceret:

quum tamen constet, promissiones illas generales esse, nec Judæis solum captivis, sed quibuscunq; fi- delibus factas. Et benedictio Jacobo promissa, ac hæreditas longe eminentior atque augustior est, quam quæ definiri temporalibus istis debeat. Ideo- que recte Brentius: Agenti verum Sabbatum longe excellentior promittitur hæreditas, quam quæ est hu- jus terræ. Nam dictum est Genes. capite vigesimo o- ctavo ad Patriarcham Jacob: Benedicentur in se- mine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ. Hoc dicto promit- titur de posteritate Jacob Christus Filius Dei, qui af- ferat secum omnibus credentibus in ipsum cælestem benedictionem. Itaq; hæreditas Jacob Patriarchæ est benedictio omnium cælestium bonorum, quæ credenti- bus propter semen Jacob, qui est Christus, contingunt. Postquam igitur is, qui agit pænitentiam, adoptatur in filium Dei propter Christum, fit etiam propter istum hæres omnis benedictionis, adeoq; omnis cælestis maje- statis, quo beneficio nihil est nec sublimius nec excellen- tius.

## 59:1 Argument
CHAPTER LIX.

Iniquities prevent sinners from being heard and saved, therefore the Jews confess that they are justly deserted by God, whose zeal against the wicked is depicted, but to those who repent, a Redeemer and the gracious covenant of God is promised.

Vers. 1. BEHOLD THE HAND OF THE LORD IS NOT SHORTENED THAT IT CANNOT SAVE] This discourse coheres with the previous one. The same sense as above L. 2. God has become neither weaker nor deafer.

Latin:

CAPUT LIX.

Iniquitates impediunt, ne exaudiantur, & salventur peccatores, ideo confitentur Ju- dæi se juste à Deo deseri, cujus zelus ad- versus malos depingitur, at pænitenti- bus Redemtor & fœdus Dei gratiosum pro- mittitur.

Vers. 1. ECCE NON EST ABBREVIATA MANUS DOMINI UT SALVARE NEQUEAT] Cohæret hic sermo superiori. Idem sensus qui supra L. 2. Deus nec imbecillior factus nec surdior.

## 59:2
Vers. 2. BUT YOUR INIQUITIES HAVE DIVIDED BETWEEN YOU AND YOUR GOD, AND YOUR SINS HAVE HIDDEN HIS FACE FROM YOU SO THAT HE WOULD NOT HEAR] Your crimes prevent your prayers for recovering liberty from being heard by God; for neither power nor goodness is lacking to Him for this.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SED INIQUITATES VESTRÆ DIVISE- RUNT INTER VOS ET DEUM VESTRUM, ET PECCATA VESTRA ABSCONDERUNT FACIEM EJUS A VOBIS NE EXAUDIRET] Crimina vestra impediunt ne preces vestræ pro libertate recuperanda à Deo exaudiantur; illi enim neque potentia ad hoc deest neque bonitas.

## 59:3
Vers. 3. FOR YOUR HANDS ARE POLLUTED WITH BLOOD] With the slaughter of the innocent.

AND YOUR FINGERS WITH INIQUITY] By rapine and theft.

YOUR LIPS HAVE SPOKEN FALSE- HOOD] False testimonies.

AND YOUR TONGUE UTTERS INIQUITIES] It slanders.

Latin:

Vers. 3. MANUS ENIM VESTRÆ POLLUTÆ SUNT SANGUINE] Cædibus innocentum.

ET DIGITI VESTRI INIQUITATE] Rapinis & furtis.

LABIA VESTRA LOCUTA SUNT MENDA- CIUM] Falsa testimonia.

ET LINGUA VESTRA INIQUITATUM FA- TUR] Calumniatur.

## 59:4
Ver. 4. THERE IS NONE THAT CALLS UPON JUSTICE] There is no one who utters a free voice for a just cause. When he says, there is no one, we must understand that there were few good men in the time of Manasseh and those following. Compare with this passage Psalm 14:3, from which passage, and this one which we now have in hand, with other parts of the Psalms added, the passage of Paul at Rom. 3:11 and following was composed, and adapted to Paul's times with a similar ἀυξήσει and ὑπερβολῇ.

Since he has hitherto drawn everything to the Babylonian captivity and the liberation from the same, even those things which most openly treat of the Messiah and the time of the N.T. and spiritual benefits, Grotius did not wish to fail in his duty here either, dragging the entire chapter, not only as regards the former part, which is legal, but also as regards the latter, the Evangelical, to the same. Not a few most learned interpreters deny that this discourse coheres with what follows. For although the coherence with the preceding chapter is less obscure or doubtful, yet with the rest of the chapter, namely 53, 54, 55, the συνέχεια is not so obvious, nor is it explained by all in the same way. If, however, it is said to cohere with those things which were predicted concerning the Babylonian captivity and the redemption from the same, those predictions must first be shown, and then it must be demonstrated that these things which we are now treating cohere with them. Although therefore it is said in this place, the iniquities of the Jews separate them from God, and their sins hide the face of God from the same, so that they might not be heard; yet there is no word had concerning the recovery of liberty, nor are the prayers which are made for it indicated, but it is treated in general against hypocrites, that their prayers are void, because their hands are polluted with blood, their fingers with iniquity, their tongues with slander. There is no doubt that these things can be applied to the Jews who lived in the Babylonian captivity, but it had to be shown that they were addressed as being established in that calamity. I would rather say, if those things were said concerning the special state and lot of the Jews, that they are viewed under the time of the latest destruction, not in the Babylonian exile. For at that time all those crimes which are recounted here had been brought to their peak; then also such great calamities, such great darkness followed, then they groped like the blind, and stumbled at midday, as they were shut in on all sides, as dead in their graves, etc. Thus, finally, the Evangelical sermon concerning liberation from the tyranny of the Devil in this chapter, and concerning the calling of the Gentiles in the following, will cohere more aptly. Add that those things which the Prophet used to describe the malice of the people, Paul brought forward when he treated of the redemption of Christ, as Grotius himself admits. If these things were to treat of the time of Manasseh and the scarcity of upright men in that age, they would be less correctly adapted to the times of Paul, nor would they serve to show the necessity of the redemption of Christ and justification by faith in Christ. But neither is there any document extant that these things pertain to the times of Manasseh, and since the text convinces that both Jews and Gentiles are concluded under sin, and there is no διαςολή here, those testimonies had to be brought forward which teach the universal corruption of men and the innate depravity, on account of which we all need Christ the Redeemer: of which innate depravity, when left to itself, the Jews of the latest age exhibited a living διατύπωσιν; then indeed those sayings from the O.T. were most convenient, in which, along with this depravity of men, the redemption of Christ is also exhibited, which is to be seen in Psalm 14, brought forward by Paul, and it will be established that the same is done in this our chapter in turn. Finally, the very entrance of the chapter testifies that the discourse is about such sins and iniquities on account of which the people had been divided and rejected by God, and which hid the face of the Lord from them, so that He might not hear the same. Which agree most with the latest times of the Jewish people, not likewise with the time of the Babylonian captivity. For then the people had not yet been plainly rejected, nor were its prayers rejected, and finally a certain term of liberation was fixed for them divinely. As to those words: THERE IS NONE WHO CALLS UPON JUSTICE, Grotius interprets them wrongly: There is no one who utters a free voice for a just cause, and he wishes them to be said καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν, because there were few good men at that time. There is no need for the figure of hyperbole. The Hebrew words sound thus: there is no one who calls, cries out, or preaches in justice, there is no one who judges in truth; which were said most truly concerning the priests, pontiffs, and lawyers in the time of Christ. The whole order of public ministry was corrupt, true justice was not preached, it was not judged in truth. Which from this chapter v. 7. & 8. the Apostle drew out Rom. 3. he did not adapt them to his own times, but from them he demonstrated the natural perversity of the human race, because this is the fountain and spring of that actual perversity which was exercising itself in the Jews and was placed as if before the eyes by this perversity of the Jews, as causes are wont to be known from effects, and to be seen in the effect. Indeed, the Jews provided a most clear example of the depravity which is inherent in our nature, such as it is when it is left to itself and is not restrained or mortified, but breaks forth most freely, with the reins loosened on all sides, even if the frequency of crimes and sins, which contracted not one habit of sin and a necessity of sinning, also increased it. There is, therefore, no reason why a hyperbole should be feigned here, much less in Paul, who treats openly and of set purpose concerning universal corruption and perversity. Which depravation Grotius owes to Socinus, or to Pelagius himself, who also denies original sin. For these, in order to crush these and similar testimonies, are wont to cry out 'hyperbole'.

Vers. same. BUT THEY TRUST IN NOTHING, AND SPEAK VANITIES] They seek a thing by evil deceits, about which they boast.

THEY HAVE CONCEIVED LABOR, AND BROUGHT FORTH INIQUITY] See Job XV. 35.

Latin:

Vers. 4. NON EST QUI INVOCET JUSTITIAM] Nemo est, qui vocem liberam pro causa justa emittat. Cum dicit, nemo est, debemus intelligere paucos Manassis tempore & sequentibus viros bonos fuisse. Confer cum hoc loco Psalm. 14, 3. ex quo loco, & hoc quem nunc ha- bemus in manibus, additis & aliis Psalmorum particulis, conflatus est locus Pauli ad Rom. 3, 11. & sequentibus, ada- pratusque Pauli temporibus simili cum ἀυξήσει & ὑπερβο- λῇ.

QUum omnia hactenus ad captivitatem Baby- lonicam & liberationem ex eadem pertra- xerit, etiam quæ apertissime de Messia & tempore N. T. ac beneficiis spiritualibus agunt, neq; hic suo deesse voluit officio Grotius, caput integrum non solum quoad priorem partem, quæ legalis est, sed etiam quoad posteriorem, Evangelicam, ad ean- dem abripiens. Cohærere cum sequentibus hunc sermonem non pauci Interpp. doctissimorum ne- gant. Etsi enim cohærentia cum capite præce- denti minus obscura, aut dubia fit, tamen cum cæ- teris c. nempe 53. 54. 55. συνέχεια non est ita obvia, nec ab omnibus eodem modo exponitur. Si autem cohærere cum iis dicatur, quæ de captivitate Baby- lonica, & redemtione ex eadem prædicta sunt, mon- stranda primum illæ prædictiones, & ostendendum deinde, hæc quæ nunc tractamus illis cohærere. Quanquam ergo dicatur hoc loco, iniquitates Ju- dæorum separare eos à Deo, & peccata ipsorum ab- scondere faciem Dei ab iisdem, ne exaudiantur, de libertate tamen recuperanda nullum verbum ha- betur, neq; preces, quæ pro illa fiunt, indigitantur, sed in genere adversus hypocritas agitur, preces ipso- rum irritas esse, quia manus pollutæ sint sanguine, di- giti iniquitate, linguæ calumnus. Hæc applicari pos- se ad Judæos, qui in captivitate Babylonica vixêre, dubium nullum est, sed compellari eosdem tan- quam constitutos in ista calamitate, ostendendum erat. Dixerim potius, si de speciali statu & sorte Ju- dæorum illa dicta sint, spectari eosdem sub novissi- mi excidii tempus, non in exilio Babylonico. Nam isto tempore omnia illa scelera, quæ hic recensen- tur, ad ἀκμὴν perducta erant; tum etiam tantæ ca- lamitates, tantæ tenebræ sequutæ sunt, tum cæco- rum instar palparunt, & impegerunt in meridie, ut conclusiundiq; fuêre, ut mortui in sepulcris suis &c. Ita deniq; aptius cohærebit concio Evangelica de liberatione è tyrannide Diaboli hoc capite, & de vocatione gentium sequenti. Adde quod ea, quæ ad describendam malitiam populi adhibuit Pro- pheta, Paulus, cum de redemptione Christi egit, ad- duxerit, fatente ipsomet Grotio. Quæ si de Manaf- sis tempore, ac paucitate virorum proborum ista ætate agerent, Pauli temporibus minus recte ad- aptarentur, neq; ad ostendendam necessitatem re- demtionis Christi ac justificationis per fidem in Christum facerent. Sed nec ullum documentum prostat, ista ad tempora Manassis pertinere, & quum convincat textus tam Judæos, quam gentes sub peccato conclusas esse, nullam hic esse διαςο- λὴν, ea afferenda erant testimonia, quæ corruptio- nem hominum universalem, & congenitam pravi- tatem, ob quam omnes indigemus Christo Re- demptore, doceant: cujus pravitatis congenitæ sibi relictæ vivam διατύπωσιν exhibebant Judæi novis- simæ ætatis; tum vero convenientissima erant illa è V. T. dicta, in quibus cum ista pravitate hominum redemtio etiam Christi exhibetur, quod in Psalmo 14. à Paulo adducto videre est, & in hoc nostro ca- pite itidem fieri deinceps constabit. Denique ipse ingressus capitis testatur, de talibus peccatis & ini- quitatibus sermonem esse, ob quæ populus à Deo divisus & reprobatus erat, quæq; abscondebant fa- ciem Domini ab iis, ne exaudiret eosdem. Quæ conveniunt maxime novissimis populi Judaici temporibus, non item tempori captivitatis Baby- lonicæ. Nam tum nondum reprobatus erat plane populus, nec preces ejusdem rejiciebantur, & deni- que certus terminus liberationis istis fixus erat di- vinitus. Quod ad illa: NON EST QUI IN- VOCET JUSTITIAM, perperam ea interpre- tatur Grotius: Nemo est qui vocem liberam pro causa justa emittat, & καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν dicta vult, quod pauci boni viri tempore illo fuerint. Non opus est hyperboles figura. Verba Ebræa ita sonant: non est qui vocet, clamet, aut concionetur in justitia, non est qui judicet in veritate; Quæ de sacerdotibus, pontificibus & legisperitis tempore Christi verissi- me dicta. Corruptus erat totus ordo ministerii publici, non prædicabatur vera justitia, non judica- batur in veritate. Quæ ex hoc capite v. 7. & 8. de- promsit Apostolus Rom. 3. non suis ille adaptavit temporibus, sed ex iis naturalem perversitatem hu- mani generis demonstravit, quia hæc fons & scaturi- go est istius perversitatis actualis, quæ in Judæis se- se exercebat & hac Judæorum perversitate velut ob oculos ponebatur, uti solent causæ ex effectis cognosci, & in effectu conspici. Nimirum exem- plum præbebant Judæi luculentissimum pravitatis, quæ naturæ nobis inest, qualis ea est, cum sibi reli- ctæ cta non refrenatur, aut mortificatur, sed liberrime prorumpit, laxatis undiq; habenis, etsi eam etiam auxerint frequentia scelerum & peccatorum, quæ peccati habitum non unum, & peccandi necessita- tem contraxerunt. Non ergo est, quod hic finga- tur hyperbole, nedum apud Paulum, qui aperte & ex instituto de universali corruptione & perversitate tractat. Quam depravationem Socino, aut Pelagio ipsi etiam peccatum originale inficianti debet Gro- tius. Hi enim ut elidant ista, & similia testimonia, hyperbolen crepare solent.

Vers. eod. SED CONFIDUNT IN NIHILO, ET LOQUUNTUR VANITATES] Dolis malis rem quærunt, de qua se jactant.

CONCEPERUNT LABOREM, ET PEPERE- RUNT INIQUITATEM] Vide Iob. XV. 35.

## 59:5
Vers. 5. THEY HAVE HATCHED ASP'S EGGS] That is, they hatch. They have produced worst thoughts into acts.

AND THEY HAVE WOVEN SPIDER'S WEBS] Useful for nothing, as follows in 6. See Job VIII. 14.

HE WHO SHALL EAT OF THEIR EGGS, SHALL DIE] That is, he who shall approve of their counsels, shall feel destruction.

AND THAT WHICH IS HATCHED, SHALL BREAK OUT INTO A BASILISK] In the Hebrew: But if anyone crushes it, a chick will come out: that is, it will do no harm itself. Thus the Chaldean seems to have taken it here. For אפרוח or מפרחי are chicks.

Latin:

Vers. 5. OVA ASPIDUM RUPERUNT] Id est, ex- cludunt. Pessima cogitata produxerunt in actus.

ET TELAS ARANEÆ TEXUERUNT] Nulli rei utiles ut sequitur 6. Vide Job. IIX. 14.

QUI COMEDERIT DE OVIS EORUM, MO- RIETUR] Id est, qui illorum consilia probabit, exitium sentiet.

ET QUOD CONFOTUM EST, ERUM- PET IN REGULUM] In Hebræo: At si quis comprimat, exibit pullus: id est, nihil ipse nocebit. Ita videtur hic sumpsisse Chaldæus. Nam אפרוח aut מפרחי sunt pulli.

## 59:6
Verse 6. THE WORK OF INIQUITY IS IN THEIR HANDS] The sense is: The punishing work, namely upon themselves. For חמס is also taken for punishment, as in Psalm 7:17 and elsewhere it is translated by the Greeks as ταλαιπωρία and πόνος. For there are here perpetual antitheses of evil counsel and unfortunate outcome.

Latin:

Vers. 6. OPUS INIQUITATIS IN MANIBUS EO- RUM] Sensus est: Opus puniens, ipsos scilicet. Nam חמס. etiam pro pœna sumitur, ut Psal. VII. 17. & alibi Græcis vertitur ταλαιπωρία & πόνος. Sunt enim hic per- petua ἀντίθετα mali consilii & infortunati eventus.

## 59:7
Verse 7. THEIR THOUGHTS ARE UNPROFITABLE THOUGHTS] Vain, which will profit them nothing.

WASTING AND DESTRUCTION ARE IN THEIR PATHS] And for because. The sense is: because they devise those things which are against the law.

Latin:

Vers. 7. COGITATIONES EORUM COGITATIO- NES INUTILES] Vanæ, nihil ipsis profuturæ.

VASTITAS ET CONTRITIO IN VIIS EO- RUM] Et pro quia. Sensus est: quia ea moliuntur, quæ contra jus sunt.

## 59:8
THEIR PATHS ARE CROOKED TO THEM] Their counsels are tortuous.

EVERYONE WHO TREADS IN THEM DOES NOT KNOW PEACE] Whoever follows them will be unhappy.

He brings these together with the preceding, their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood, and the Apostle interprets it far differently in Romans 3, from whose explanation it is a matter of religious duty for all the pious to depart. For he does not wish to indicate only that there is wasting when men devise those things which are against the law, or that those who follow their tortuous counsels are unhappy; but he teaches that we are so corrupted that there is nothing but destruction and unhappiness in our ways, because we do not know the way of peace: because there is nothing but perdition and corruption in our ways, and we are utterly alienated from the way of true peace and happiness. We all like sheep go astray, everyone turns to his own way, the way of sinners, a lost and most corrupt way, Isaiah 53. We are all inclined toward wickedness and sins, all our members are occupied by depraved concupiscence, no member of the body is immune from impurity and sin. Hands are polluted with blood, fingers with iniquity, lips with lying, the tongue with slander, the heart with confidence in vanity, thoughts with vanity, all ways with wasting and destruction, paths with depravity, the mind with ignorance, there is no one who knows the way of peace. Concerning which, those things which we have said in the Roman Apostolic Theology, Oracle XXVI, may be compared.

Latin:

SEMITÆ EORUM INCURVATÆ SUNT EIS] Tortuosa sunt eorum consulta.

OMNIS QUI CALCAT IN EIS IGNORAT PACEM] Qui ea sequitur, infelix erit.

Hæc cum antecedentibus, pedes eorum ad malum currunt & festinant, ut effundant sanguinem, adducit, longeque aliter interpretatur Apostolus Rom. 3. cujus vero explicatione discedere omni- bus piis religio est. Non enim tantum id indi- care vult, quod vastitas sit, cum homines moliuntur ea, quæ contra jus sunt, aut quod infelices sint, qui se- quuntur tortuosa ipsorum consilia; Sed docet, ita corruptos esse, ut non nisi contritio & infelicitas sit in viis nostris, quod viam pacis non cognoscamus: quia nil nisi perditio & corruptio est in viis nostris, nosque prorsus alieni sumus à via veræ pacis & fe- licitatis. Omnes nos quasi oves erramus, unusquis- que respicit viam suam, viam peccatorum, viam perditam & corruptissimam Esa. LIII. Ad scelera & peccata omnes propensi sumus, omnia mem- bra prava concupiscentia occupata sunt, nullum corporis membrum ab impuritate & peccato im- mune est. Manus pollutæ sunt sanguine, digiti iniquitate, labia mendacio, lingua calumnia, cor confidentia in vanitate, cogitationes vanitate, viæ omnes vastitate & contritione, semitæ pravitate, mens ignorantia, nemo est, qui novit viam pacis. De quo conferri poterunt, quæ in Theolog. Ro- mana Apostolica diximus Oraculo XXVI.

## 59:9
Verse 9. THEREFORE IS JUDGMENT FAR FROM US] Isaiah introduces the captive people speaking here. These are the causes, they say, why God does not vindicate us. For משפט is often translated as ἐκδίκησις. 7:4, 12:12, Num. 33:4, Ezek. 14:21, 16:37, 40, 20:4, 23:10, 45, 25:11, 30:14.

AND JUSTICE DOES NOT OVERTAKE US] That is, why the beneficence of God does not reach us.

WE HAVE WAITED FOR LIGHT] For liberty.

IMPE-

Latin:

Vers. 9. PROPTER HOC ELONGATUM EST JU- DICIUM A NOBIS] Populum captivum hic loquentem inducit Esaias. Hæ sunt causæ, ajunt illi, cur Deus nos non vindicet. Nam משפט sæpe vertitur ἐκδίκησις. 7, 4. 12, 12. Num. 33, 4. Ezech. 14, 21. 16, 37. 40. 20, 4. 23, 10. 45. 25. 11. 30, 14.

ET NON APPREHENDET NOS JUSTITIA] Id est, cur Dei beneficentia ad nos non perveniat.

EXSPECTAVIMUS LUCEM] Libertatem.

## 59:10
WE STUMBLE AT NOONDAY AS IN DARKNESS] Stumbling blocks are placed for us everywhere.

IN DARK PLACES AS IF DEAD] In Hebrew: In the graves as if dead; that is, as the Chaldean explains, we are so enclosed on all sides that we are like the dead in their graves.

Here again, it is not Isaiah—concerning whom there is deep silence on this matter—who introduces the captive people speaking, but Grotius. For he feigns that the discourse is about liberation from captivity, he does not demonstrate it. Be it so, let reasons be brought forward why God does not vindicate the Israelites: For the eleventh verse confirms this sense. He was certainly vindicating the people from the Babylonian captivity, nor could the people doubt it: because that vindication and liberation had been promised divinely. The complaint is more correctly understood as being about the most recent calamity; that for the stated reasons God does not vindicate them, nor does divine beneficence reach them, which we do not deny is indicated by the name of justice. Although others interpret those words differently, the matter finally returns to the same point, namely that they have no liberation to hope for from GOD; as if to say: We are unjustly afflicted by our enemies. We are pressed by such tyranny that neither judgment nor justice reaches us. God winks, so that we are afflicted by manifest injuries, and He does not seem to take any thought to avenge the injury brought upon us. WE HAVE WAITED FOR LIGHT, AND BEHOLD DARKNESS: FOR BRIGHTNESS, AND BEHOLD WE WALK IN DARKNESS. It is certain that these things are said not only about the expectation of liberty, but of liberation from the most grievous unhappiness; let Job 30 be compared. WE GROPE LIKE THE BLIND FOR THE WALL, AND AS WITHOUT EYES WE FEEL, WE STUMBLE AT NOONDAY AS IN DARKNESS, IN DARK PLACES AS IF DEAD, that is, just as the dead are buried in extreme darkness in the graves, so we are not moving in extreme evils, completely buried in the darkness of ignorance and calamity, so that we are ignorant of every true way of salvation. Which are especially true concerning the state of the most recent time, and fit it most of all, because hardened and blinded in the very noonday, when the Sun of justice was shining upon them, they were moving in darkness, and were buried in extreme darkness, dead in sins, as the Evangelical history testifies. See especially John 1, chapter 12. And that which Moses threatened in Deut. 28 was being fulfilled in them: The Lord shall strike you with madness and blindness and fury of mind, so that you grope in noonday, as the blind is accustomed to grope in darkness, and you shall not direct your way. Then they had to complain most of all: WE ROAR LIKE BEARS ALL OF US, AND LIKE DOVES WE MOURN. The roar of a hungry bear is horrible, but the mourning of a dove is miserable. Therefore, such great affliction is designated, before the gravity of which it was necessary to roar like hungry bears and to mourn like doves. WE WAIT FOR JUDGMENT, AND THERE IS NONE: FOR SALVATION, AND IT IS FAR FROM US. Which again fit not so much the Babylonian captivity as the most recent calamity of the Jews. For they were liberated from that, nor was salvation completely far from them. Add now also the crimes, which are here again graphically described. OUR INIQUITIES ARE VERY MANY BEFORE THEE. Some of which are recounted. TO TRANSGRESS AND TO LIE AGAINST THE LORD, AND TO TURN AWAY BACKWARD FROM OUR GOD. Which was the head of the iniquity, namely the abandonment of the covenant, both the Evangelical one initiated with Abraham concerning faith in the blessed seed, and the legal one sanctioned on Mount Sinai in Exod. 24 concerning the observation of the commandments of God. TO SPEAK CALUMNY AND REBELLION, TO CONCEIVE AND TO SPEAK FROM THE HEART WORDS OF FALSEHOOD, &c. We have here Jerome as one of the same mind: whose explanation we have woven in: They rightly ignored the way of peace, because they did not wish to accept its author. For He Himself is our peace, who says to the Apostles: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave with you. And to Jerusalem: If you had known the things that are for your peace, because the days will come upon you, and your enemies will surround you with a rampart, and will besiege you, and will dash your children to the ground. But those who have not accepted peace, consequently do not have judgment in their ways either. Him of whom it was said above: Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul has delighted, he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles. THEIR WAYS ARE PERVERSE. All the doctrine of the Pharisees is a subversion of the truth: through which he who has walked, not only does not find peace, but does not even know it, so that he might know what he ought to seek. THEREFORE IS JUDGMENT FAR FROM US &c. After the accusation of the Jewish people, the Prophet answers in their person what the penitent ought to say, if indeed they wish to receive health after their wounds. In the PRESENT time, therefore, all things are fulfilled. Judgment is far from the Jews, which has been announced to the Gentiles. And justice, which has been grasped by the nations, will not apprehend them. They waited for light, saying: Send forth thy light and thy truth, which had been promised to them through the Prophets, and they were occupied by the darkness of error. They were waiting for brightness, and they walked in darkness: thus, like the blind groping for a wall, they were in the holy scriptures: seeking only the words and leaves in them, not the sense and fruit, which is held in the letters. Finally, he joins and says, We stumble, or we shall fall at noonday, as in darkness: in dark places as if dead. For while the Sun of justice is shining with brightness in the whole world, they remain in darkness, namely as dead in sin. We shall roar (he says) like bears, and like doves meditating we shall groan: so that they are at once cruel and miserable: wild and savage toward the humble and subject: fearful and trembling toward those who are stronger: whom they dread like hawks. We read also in another place: As a bear whose cubs have been snatched away. And in Daniel a bloody kingdom, in which there are three rows of teeth, is compared to a most ferocious bear. And like doves meditating we shall groan, without sense and understanding of the scriptures, meditating only on words, which they chant from memory. But just as the doves of whom it is written: Ephraim is like a dove not having sense; and just as in the Gospel simplicity of doves is set against the malice of serpents: so in the present passage, simplicity without prudence, which is neighbor to folly, is shown in the mere meditation of words. They shall wait for judgment, and it shall not be, because it has migrated far to the nations. In which it is to be noted that they speak of all things in the future tense: so that what the Jews now endure may be indicated. MULTIPLIED ARE OUR INIQUITIES, etc. He renders the causes why they roared like bears, and meditated like doves: they waited for judgment, which was not: for salvation, which passed to the nations: because, they say, our iniquities are multiplied in your sight. From which for a long time you had turned away, so that you might not see them, so that you might not strike. And our sins have answered us, so that we might receive what we deserved. And our crimes are with us. And we have acknowledged our iniquities, which, committing for a long time, we thought to be justice. But what are the iniquities? To sin and to lie against God: or as Aquila translated according to the Hebrew, to deny God: which is referred to the Savior. And we abandon (they say) our God, saying we know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he is from: so that we might speak calumny. If this man were from God, he would not break the Sabbath. And: By Beelzebub the prince of demons he casts out demons. And transgression, which is more significantly called in Greek ἀπόστασις, when someone denies God, and is accused of prevarication. We have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood, contemning the law of God, and following the traditions of men, which they call δευτερώσεις: and which we have feigned in our heart. And judgment is turned away backward, and justice has stood far off. For what part has justice with iniquity? What consensus has Christ with Belial? Justice has stood among the nations, and has departed from us, because truth has fallen in the street. For wide and spacious is the way that leads to death: because they were unwilling to enter the narrow way, in which truth dwells. And truth has been made into oblivion: concerning which it is written: Truth has sprung out of the earth, and justice has looked down from heaven. In which it must be noted, that truth is frequently named, so that the person of Christ might be shown: whom abandoning, they followed a lie. AND HE WHO DEPARTED FROM EVIL, LAY OPEN TO PREY. Which although it may seem obscure, can be explained thus: as we fashion a lie from our heart and abandon the law of God, justice has stood far off, and truth has fallen in the streets, and equity could not enter to us: and the son of God, who is truth, has been made into oblivion: to such an extent, that whoever desired to depart from the traditions of the Jews, would immediately lie open to snares and persecutions: so that they expelled from the synagogues the man blind from birth, who had received his sight: and after the resurrection of the Lord Savior, they persecuted and stripped all who believed in him: to whom they directed the ministries of the Churches from the whole world of the nations, which they distributed through the hands of the Apostles. Thus far the gloss of Jerome.

Latin:

IMPEGIMUS MERIDIE QUASI IN TENE- BRIS] Ubique positae nobis sunt offensa.

IN CALIGINOSIS QUASI MORTUI] In He- braeo: In sepulcris sicut mortui; id est, ut Chaldaeus exponit, ita conclusi undique tenemur, ut mortui in sepulchris suis.

Iterum hic populum captivum loquentem in- ducit non Esaias, penes quem altum de eo est si- lentium, sed Grotius. De liberatione enim e ca- ptivitate sermonem esse fingit, non demonstrat. Esto, causae adducantur, cur Deus Israelitas non vindicet: Nam confirmat hunc sensum versus un- decimus. Vindicabat certe populum e captivitate Babylonica, nec de eo dubitare poterat populus: quia ea vindicatio & liberatio divinitus promissa erat. Rectius de novissima calamitate quaerela in- telligitur; quod ob dictas causas ipsos Deus non vindicet, nec ad ipsos perveniat beneficentia divina, quam justitiae nomine indigitari, non abnuimus. Quanquam vero verba illa aliter interpretentur alii, tamen eodem tandem res redit, quod nem- pe a DEO nullam liberationem sperare habeant; qs. d. Nos ab hostibus nostris injuste affligimur. Tanta premimur tyrannide, ut nec judicium, nec justitia nobis contingat. Deus connivet, ut mani- festis injuriis afficiamur, & non videtur ullam susci- pere cogitationem, ut injuriam nobis illatam ulcisca- tur. EXPECTAVIMUS LUCEM, ET EC- CE TENEBRAE: SPLENDOREM, ET EC- CE IN CALIGINE AMBULAMUS. Haec non de libertatis tantum expectatione, sed libe- rationis e gravissima infelicitate dici, certum est; Conferatur Job. 30. PALPAMUS SICUT COE- CI PARIETEM, ET QUASI ABSQUE O- CULIS CONTRECTAMUS, IMPINGIMUS IN MERIDIE QUASI IN TENEBRIS, IN CALIGINOSIS SICUT MORTUI, hoc est, Sicut mortui obruti sunt extremis tenebris in sepul- cris, ita non versamur in extremis malis, tenebris ignorantiae, & calamitatis prorsus obruti, ut igno- remus omnem veram viam salutis. Quae de novissimi temporis statu apprime vera sunt, illique maxime conveniunt, quia indurati & excaecati in ipsa me- ridie, cum ipsis luceret Sol justitiae, in tenebris ver- sabantur, & extremis tenebris obruti erant, in pec- catis mortui, teste historia Evangelica. Vide im- primis Joh. 1. cap. 12. Et implebatur in ipsis, quod minatus est Moses Deut. 28. Percutiet te Dominus amentia & caecitate, ac furore mentis, ut palpes in meridie, sicut palpare solet caecus in tenebris, & non dirigas viam tuam. Tum conqueri necessum ha- bebant maxime: RUGIMUS QUASI URSI OMNES, ET QUASI COLUMBAE GEMI- MUS. Horribilis est rugitus ursi esurientis, ge- mitus autem columbae miserabilis est. Tanta igitur designatur afflictio, prae cujus gravitate rugire sicut esurientes ursi, & ingemiscere sicut columbae opor- tebat. EXPECTAMUS JUDICIUM, ET NON EST: SALUTEM, ET ELONGATA EST A NOBIS. Quae iterum non tam captivitati Babylo- nicae, quam calamitati novissimae Judaeorum conve- niunt. Ex illa enim liberati sunt, neq; salus prorsus elongata ab ipsis fuit. Adde jam etiam scelera, quae hic denuo graphice describuntur. MULTAE NI- MIS SUNT INIQUITATES NOSTRAE CO- RAM TE. Quales recensentur nonnullae. PRAE- VARICARI ET MENTIRI CONTRA DO- MINUM, DEFICERE RETRO A DEO NO- STRO. Quod caput erat iniquitatis, dereli- ctio nempe foederis, tum Evangelici cum Abraha- mo initi, de fide in semen benedictum, tum legalis in monte Sinai sanciti Exod. 24. de observatione mandatorum Dei. LOQUI CALUMNIAM ET CONTUMACIAM, CONCIPERE ET LO- QUI SUA MEDITARI DE CORDE VER- BA MENDACII, &c. Habemus hic Hierony- mum ὁμόψυφον: cujus explicationem contexi- mus: Recte viam pacis ignoraverunt, quia autorem ejus suscipere noluerunt. Ipse est enim pax nostra, qui loquitur ad Apostolos: Pacem meam do vobis, pa- cem meam relinquo vobis. Et ad Hierusalem: Si scires quæ ad pacem sunt tibi, quoniam venient dies super te, & circundabunt te inimici tui vallo, & obsidebunt te, & filios tuos allident ad terram. Qui autem pacem non susceperint, consequenter nec judicium habent in viis suis. Illum de quo supra di- ctum est: Ecce puer meus quem elegi, dilectus meus, quem dilexit anima mea, judicium gentibus proferet. VIÆ EORUM PERVERSÆ. Omnis doctrina Pharisæorum subversio veritatis est: per quam qui ambulaverit, non solum non invenit pa- cem, sed nec cognoscit quidem eam, ut sciat quid quæ- rere debeat. PROPTER HOC ELONGA- TUM EST JUDICIUM A NOBIS &c. Post accusationem populi Judæorum, ex persona eorum Propheta respondet, quid loqui debeant pœnitentes, si tamen velint post vulnera recipere sanitatem. IN PRÆSENTI igitur TEMPORE universa com- plentur. Elongatum est judicium à Judais, quod gen- tibus nunciatum est. Et non apprehendet eos justitia, quæ a nationibus comprehensa est. Expectaverunt lucem, dicentes: Emitte lucem tuam, & verita- tem tuam, quæ eis per Prophetas fuerat repromissa, & erroris tenebris occupati sunt. Sustinebant splen- dorem, & ambulaverunt in tenebris: ita scripturas sanctas, quasi cæci palpantes parietem: verba tan- tum in eis & folia, non sensum fructumq; quærentes, qui tenetur in literis. Deniq; jungit & dicit, Impe- gimus, sive cademus meridie, quasi in tenebris: in caliginosis quasi mortui. In toto enim orbe Sole ju- stitiæ splendore rutilante, illi morantur in tenebris, videlicet ut peccato mortui. Rugiemus (ait) quasi ursi omnes, & quasi columbæ meditantes geme- mus: ut & crudeles sint pariter & miseri: feri & immanes, ad humiles atq; subjectos: pavidi atq; trepidantes, ad eos qui fortiores sunt: quos quasi ac- cipitres perhorrescunt. Legimus & in alio loco: Quasi ursa raptis catulis. Et in Daniele regnum cruentum, in quo sunt tres ordines dentium, ursæ fero- cissimæ comparatum. Et quasi columbæ meditan- tes gememus, absq; sensu & intelligentia scriptura- rum, tantum verba meditantes, quæ decantant me- moriter. Sed quomodo columbæ de quibus scriptum est: Ephraim quasi columba non habens sensum; Et quomodo in Evangelio contra serpentum mali- tiam, simplicitas ponitur columbarum: sic in præsenti loco, simplicitas absq; prudentia, quæ vicina stultitiæ est, in sola verborum meditatione monstratur. Ex- pectabunt judicium, & non erit, quia longe migra- vit ad gentes. In quo notandum, quod omnia futuro dicant tempore: ut quod nunc Judæi sustinent, indi- cetur. MULTIPLICATÆ SUNT INIQUI- TATES, &c. Reddit causas quare rugierint quasi ursi, & meditati sint ut columbæ: expectaverint judicium, quod non erat: salutem, quæ transivit ad gentes: quia multiplicatæ sunt, dicentes, iniqui- tates nostræ in conspectu tuo. A quibus multo tem- pore averteras, ne eas cerneres, ne ferires. Et pec- cata nostra responderunt nobis, ut reciperemus, quod meruimus. Et scelera nostra nobiscum sunt. Iniquitatesq; cognovimus, quas multo tempore per- petrantes, putabamus esse justitiam. Quæ sunt autem iniquitates? Peccare & mentiri contra Deum: sive ut juxta Hebraicum Aquila translu- lit, negare Deum: quod ad Salvatorem refertur. Et relinquimus (inquiunt) Deum nostrum, dicen- tes: Scimus quod Moysi locutus sit Deus, hunc au- tem nescimus unde sit: ut loqueremur calumniam. Hic si ex Deo esset, non solveret sabbatum. Et: In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dœ- monia. Et transgressionem, quæ significantius Græ- ce dicitur ἀπόστασις, quum aliquis negat Deum, & prævaricationis arguitur. Concepimus & locuti su- mus de corde verba mendacii, contemnentes legem Dei, & sequentes traditiones hominum, quas illi δευ- τερώσεις vocant: & quas in nostro corde simulavimus. Et conversum est retrorsum judicium, & justitia longe stetit. Quæ enim pars justitiæ & iniquitati? qui consensus Christi & Belial? Stetit justitia in gen- tibus, & recessit à nobis, quia corruit in platea veritas. Lata enim & spatiosa via, quæ du- cit ad mortem: quia angustam viam, in qua veritas commoratur,intrare nolebant. Et facta est veritas in oblivionem: de qua scriptum est: Veritas de ter- ra orta est, & justitia de cœlo prospexit. In quo a- nimadvertendum,quod crebro veritas nominata sit,ut Christi persona monstraretur: quam deserentes, se- cuti sunt mendacium. ET QUI RECESSIT A MALO, PRÆDÆ PATUIT.
