Quod quanquam videatur obscurum, sic edisseri potest: nobis menda- cium de nostro corde fingentibus & deserentibus legem Dei, justitia longe stetit, & veritas corruit in plateis, & æquitas ad nos intrare non potuit: & filius Dei, qui est veritas, factus est in oblivionem: in tantum, ut quicunq́; à traditionibus Judæorum cupierit recede- re, statim pateret insidiis & persequutionibus: ita ut cæcum à nativitate, qui oculos receperat, expule- rint de synagogis: & post resurrectionem domini Salvatoris, omnes qui in eo credebant, persequuti sint atq́; nudaverint: quibus de toto orbe gentium Ecclesiæ ministeria dirigebant, quæ per manus Apostolorum distribuerent. Hactenus glossa Hieronymi.

## 59:11
Ver. 11.

WE HAVE LOOKED FOR JUDGMENT] See above 9.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

EXPECTAVIMUS JUDICIUM] Vide supra 9.

## 59:12
Ver. 12. OUR SINS HAVE ANSWERED US] They speak testimony against us. For ענה also signifies this: namely because witnesses adjured and interrogated were answering. See above 3, 9. Just as the accused are accustomed to be condemned by the words of witnesses, so are we by the very evidence of our crimes.

FOR OUR WICKEDNESSES ARE WITH US] They show themselves to us on every side.

AND WE HAVE KNOWN OUR INIQUITIES] That is, we are compelled to acknowledge them. Their enumeration follows.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PECCATA NOSTRA RESPONDERUNT NOBIS] Testimonium contra nos dicunt. Nam ענה & hoc significat: nimirum quia testes adjurati & interroga- ti respondebant. Vide supra 3, 9. Sicut ad verba testium condemnari solent rei, sic nos ex ipsa criminum evidentia.

QUIA SCELERA NOSTRA NOBISCUM] Un- dique se nobis ostendunt.

ET INIQUITATES NOSTRAS COGNOVI- MUS] Id est, agnoscere cogimur. Earum enumeratio sequitur.

## 59:13
Ver. 13. TO SIN] In the Hebrew it is פשע, which is to stubbornly transgress the law.

AND TO LIE AGAINST THE LORD] To swear falsely.

AND WE HAVE TURNED AWAY] Here also in the Hebrew it is the infinitive to turn away.

AND TO SPEAK] And here it is to speak.

AND TRANSGRESSION] סרה, ἀποστασίαν.

AND WE HAVE SPOKEN OF THE HEART] In Hebrew, To meditate.

Latin:

Vers. 13. PECCARE] In Hebræo est פשע, quod est præfracte legem transgredi.

ET MENTIRI CONTRA DOMINUM] Falsum jurare.

ET AVERSI SUMUS] Hic quoque in Hebræo in- finitivum est averti.

AC LOQUEREMUR] Et hic est loqui.

ET TRANSGRESSIONEM] סרה, ἀποστασίαν.

ET LOCUTI SUMUS DE CORDE] In Hebræo Meditari.

## 59:14
Ver. 14. AND JUDGMENT IS TURNED BACKWARD] The judgments which the Jews exercised upon Jews by the concession of kings were corrupted.

TRUTH HAS FALLEN IN THE STREET] More correctly, in the forum.

AND EQUITY COULD NOT ENTER] It was excluded from the forum.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET CONVERSUM EST RETRORSUM JUDICIUM] Corrupta sunt judicia, quæ Judæi in judæos ex concessu regum exercebant.

CORRUIT IN PLATEA VERITAS] Rectius, in foro.

ET ÆQUITAS NON POTUIT INGREDI] A foro exclusa est.

## 59:15
Ver. 15. AND HE THAT DEPARTED FROM EVIL, BECAME A PREY] An innocent man is exposed to the injuries of all.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET QUI RECESSIT A MALO, PRÆDÆ PATUIT] Vir innocens ad omnium injurias patet.

## 59:16
Ver. 16. AND HE SAW THAT THERE WAS NO MAN] I saw that there was no one, namely, who would pour out serious prayers to God, as follows.

HE WAS ASTONIED] He was amazed.

BECAUSE THERE IS NONE TO INTERCEDE] To pray, as the Chaldean here.

AND HE SAVED HIS ARM FOR HIMSELF] These indicative [verbs] are to be explained by way of the subjunctive: that he might save him with his own arm.

AND HIS RIGHTEOUSNESS ITSELF CONFIRMED HIM] And by his goodness he might establish him.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET VIDIT QUIA NON EST VIR] Vidi esse neminem, nempe qui preces serias ad Deum funde- ret, ut sequitur.

APORIATUS EST] Obstupuit.

QUIA NON EST QUI OCCURRAT] Depre- cetur, ut hic Chaldæus.

ET SALVAVIT SIBI BRACHIUM SUUM] Hæc indicativa per modum subjunctivum exponenda sunt: ut suo brachio eum servet.

ET JUSTITIA EJUS IPSE CONFIRMAVIT EUM] Et bonitate sua ipsum stabiliat.

## 59:17
Ver. 17. HE PUT ON RIGHTEOUSNESS AS A BREASTPLATE

That he may be safe through justice, as if by the protection of a breastplate, namely if there were anyone praying to God, from the preceding.

AND THE HELMET OF SALVATION UPON HIS HEAD] That he may be safe in dangers, just as those who are helmeted in battle.

HE IS CLOTHED WITH THE GARMENTS OF VENGEANCE, AND IS COVERED AS WITH A CLOAK OF ZEAL] That God may protect him, by taking vengeance upon the oppressors, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 17. INDUTUS EST JUSTITIA UT LORICA

Ut per justitiam tutus sit, velut loricae praesidio, nempe si quis esset Deum orans, ex superioribus.

UT GALEA SALUTIS IN CAPITE EJUS] Ut salvus sit in periculis, quomodo galeati in praelio.

INDUTUS EST VESTIMENTIS ULTIONIS, ET OPERTUS EST QUASI PALLIO ZELI] Ut Deus ipsum protegat, vindictam sumendo de oppressoribus, ut sequitur.

## 59:18
Vers. 18. AS TO VENGEANCE AS TO THE RETRIBUTION OF INDIGNATION TO HIS ENEMIES, AND RECOMPENSE TO HIS ADVERSARIES: HE WILL RENDER RECOMPENSE TO THE ISLANDS] Translate from the Hebrew: As for deeds, as for (those very deeds, I say) he renders (someone) wrath to his enemies, and repayment to his adversaries, so (God) would render recompense to the islanders: that is, to the Mesopotamians, namely if there were those who would pray.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SICUT AD VINDICTAM QUASI AD RETRIBUTIONEM INDIGNATIONIS HOSTIBUS SUIS, ET VICISSITUDINEM INIMICIS SUIS: IN- SULIS VICEM REDDET] Vertas ex Hebraeo: Sicut pro factis, sicut pro (ipsis inquam factis) reddit (aliquis) iram ho- stibus suis, & repensationem inimicis suis, sic (Deus) redde- ret vicem insularibus: id est, Mesopotamiensibus, nempe si essent qui orarent.

## 59:19
Vers. 19. AND THEY SHALL FEAR] The nations would fear the power of God.

WHEN HE SHALL COME AS A VIOLENT RIVER, WHICH THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD DRIVES] The power of God would come upon them as suddenly as the Euphrates sometimes, driven by the winds, overflows the lands. Thus the Chaldean here is excellent. For Pliny, V. 26, is a witness that Babylonia is accustomed to be infested by the headlong course of the Euphrates.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET TIMEBUNT] Timerent gentes Dei po- tentiam.

CUM VENERIT QUASI FLUVIUS VIOLEN- TUS, QUEM SPIRITUS DOMINI COGIT] Superve- niret illis Dei potentia ita subito, sicut Euphrates inter- dum ventis impulsus terras obruit. Ita hic Chaldaeus opti- me. Solitam enim praecipiti Euphratis cursu Babyloniam infestari, testis est Plinius V. 26.

## 59:20
Vers. 20. AND A REDEEMER SHALL COME TO SION, AND TO THEM THAT RETURN FROM INIQUITY IN JACOB, SAITH THE LORD] The second ET is placed for 'namely,' so that the passage may have this meaning: A liberator shall come to Sion, namely to those who in Jacob (that is, among the Israelites) shall have turned themselves from iniquity: to God, that is. This liberator is Cyrus, a figure of Christ. גאל properly indeed means to redeem by right of kinship: but by κατάχρησιν [improper usage] to liberate in any way.

Here the better interpreters constitute the second part of this discourse, namely the Gospel concerning Christ, which the Lord saw, as is held in verse 15, that is, that all had turned aside, and there was no one who did good, nor was there found anyone who would avenge men from the power of Satan, and judge him himself: And when he looked around, whether there was a man who would meet the wrath of God, he was astonished that no one was found, and therefore the Lord himself, the Son of God, undertook the cause of men: of whom it is said: AND HE SAVED HIS ARM FOR HIMSELF, AND HIS JUSTICE ITSELF CONFIRMED HIM, i.e., he armed himself with his power, and usurped his justice with a firm and strong spirit, so that he might repress his enemies, but rescue men. HE IS CLOTHED WITH JUSTICE AS A BREASTPLATE, AND THE HELMET OF SALVATION UPON HIS HEAD; HE IS CLOTHED WITH VENGEANCE AS A GARMENT, AND IS COVERED WITH ZEAL AS A CLOAK. This, says Brentius, is the armor of Christ the Son of God, with which kind of armor Paul also clothes the soldier of Christ in Ephesians 6 and 1 Thessalonians 5. For the Son of God uses justice for a breastplate: he uses salvation for a helmet: for a garment, vengeance: for a cloak, zeal. For what purpose, then, is he so armed? For vengeance, he says, and for retribution to his enemies, as much to those who are in his own people among the Israelites, as to those who are in the islands, that is, the uncircumcised nations. He undertakes, however, to exercise this vengeance, so that he may save and protect his Church against enemies with his divine zeal, with which he embraces it. For the Son of God is said to be armed with the breastplate of justice, because since he is truly just, he also justifies, and causes that as many as believe in him are reputed just, and are defended in all adversities. For this is the work of justice in kings and princes, that they absolve their people from the wicked accusations of adversaries, and defend them from their enemies. Thus also the soldier of Christ is armed in Paul with the breastplate of faith, because since we are gifted through faith with the justice of Christ, it is to be set forth, like a breastplate, against all the accusations of Satan, so that through it we may stand safe against the fiery darts of Satan. The Son of God is also said to be armed with the helmet of salvation, because he brings true and eternal salvation to all who believe in him. Thus also the soldier of Christ is armed in Paul with the helmet of the hope of salvation, because the certain hope of salvation, which we have in

Christ, must be conceived, so that even if all the rest of our affairs perish, we may nevertheless keep our head fortified by the salvation of Christ, by which salvation we shall break through death itself to eternal life. The Son of God is also armed, or clothed, with the garment of vengeance, because he avenges both himself and his people upon his enemies and adversaries with immense strength of spirit and fortitude. Similarly Osiander: AS FOR VENGEANCE AS IF FOR THE RETRIBUTION OF INDIGNATION TO HIS ENEMIES, AND RECOMPENSE TO HIS FOES. Thus he armed: HE WILL RENDER RECOMPENSE TO THE ISLANDS, that is, he vanquished the nations, and will bring them under his own power. For the Prophet uses in a spiritual matter words borrowed from bodily victories: where warriors do this, that they take vengeance upon their enemies. Which sense concerning the subjugation of the nations, that he is about to subject to himself those same ones snatched from the power of Satan, is confirmed by those things which follow. AND THEY SHALL FEAR WHO ARE FROM THE WEST THE NAME OF THE LORD, AND THEY WHO ARE FROM THE RISING OF THE SUN, HIS GLORY. Everywhere among the nations in the world the divinity and majesty of Christ, both Savior and liberator of the human race, is acknowledged, WHEN HIS spiritual kingdom SHALL HAVE COME LIKE A VIOLENT RIVER, which, having been restrained for some time, afterwards rushes in with immense force, and snatches with itself everything it seizes. WHICH river also THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD DRIVES, or impels. For the course of the Gospel (where the Lord impels the minds of those teaching and learning by his Spirit) cannot be retarded, but breaks through suddenly through all obstacles, like a river sometimes restrained, but afterwards truly bursting forth, impelled also by the great force of the wind. AND HE SHALL COME, more correctly, and the Redeemer, Jesus Christ, shall come even to Zion itself, AND will bring aid TO THEM. WHO RETURN FROM INIQUITY IN the people of JACOB, SAYS THE LORD. This is, even if the nations are gathered in the greatest number into the Church of Christ and the Jews are cast away: nevertheless it will not be entirely over for the Jewish nation, but some will be converted from Judaism from their unbelief and impiety to Christ the Redeemer. To this opinion this saying of the Prophet is alleged by the Apostle in the 11th chapter to the Romans. And therefore the Jewish nation is still preserved divinely among Christians, Turks, and nations, not because the Lord approves of the unbelief of the Jews: but because there are in that people some elect, who are to be converted before the last day. Which Paraphrase, because it relies on Apostolic authority and the evidence of the Prophetic context, is without doubt to be preferred to the τῇ ἰδιλελύσει ἰδίᾳ and private [interpretation] of Grotius. Mr. Brentius explains excellently both the Apostle's bringing forward these things and the opinion of our Prophet, whom it is better to hear here, adhering to the authority of Holy Scripture, than to rise up to Grotian commentaries. What is said last in this pericope: The Redeemer shall come to Zion, etc. Paul, writing to the Romans in chapter 11, interprets clearly. For although the words of this place are read a little differently in Paul, since he, when he was writing to those who were skilled in the Greek language, uses the Greek translation, the meaning nevertheless is the same. For he warns the nations not to flatter themselves because of their election, nor to despise the Jews before them because of their rejection. For the Jews have not been so cast away by God that none of them can in any way obtain salvation. But their nation is indeed publicly cast away, so that it is no longer the people of God: Privately, however, whoever from among them acknowledges Christ through faith, becomes a member of the true people of God, and obtains eternal salvation. Whence also he said before: Behold the goodness and severity of God, toward those indeed who fell, severity, but toward you goodness, if you shall have remained in goodness. Since you also will have fallen, namely, if you shall not have remained in goodness, and they again, if they shall not have remained in unbelief, shall be grafted in, etc. And afterwards he adds: The gifts and the calling of God are of such a kind that he cannot repent of them. God once called the posterity of Abraham, that it might be the people or Church of God: And he endowed it with this prerogative, that whoever among them believed in the promised seed of Abraham, who is Christ, would be adopted as a son of God, and would obtain eternal salvation. Although, however, the descendants of Abraham are cast away at this time by God, because they themselves cast away the Son of God, nevertheless God does not retract his calling and gift, but keeps it firm and inviolate, so that whoever among the cast-away descendants of Abraham repents and acknowledges Christ through faith, may be received into the catalog of the people of God, and become a participant in every blessing which has been promised through the seed of Abraham or through Christ. The meaning of this prophetic saying, which Paul alleges, is clearly the same. For the Prophet commemorated the impiety and crimes of the Israelites. And he adds, that the Son of God would avenge himself upon his enemies and foes. He did not have, however, among men more virulent and cruel enemies than his own people, namely the descendants of the holy Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Wherefore the Prophet signifies that this people is to be cast away by God. Shall the Israelites then, someone will say, be so cast away that none of them can ever obtain salvation? Here the Prophet answers: Nothing less, they shall be so cast away: Because the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who from the descendants of Jacob repent from their impiety. For Christ the Son of God, the true Redeemer, did not so shut himself up among the nations, with the Israelites cast away, that he would never at all wish to be the redeemer of the Israelites anymore, but rather he published his redemption by the Gospel, so that not only the nations might enjoy it, but even the Israelites, although cast away, might be able to enjoy it, if they are converted from their unbelief, and acknowledge the Son of God through faith. For God does not repent of his calling and gifts, provided only that the Israelites do not grow weary of their reversion and repentance. He once called the Israelites his people: He still calls them his people, provided only that they wish to be his people through faith in Christ. You see therefore that Paul alleged this saying with the same meaning as the Prophet said it. Jerome favors this explanation: AND THEY SHALL FEAR WHO ARE FROM THE WEST THE NAME OF THE LORD. Then the foreigners, who are to come from the west and the east, that they may rest in the bosom of Abraham: (Matt. 8.) concerning whom it has also been said above (c. 49.) Behold these shall come from afar, others from the west, others from the North, &c. & (Mal. 1.) From the rising of the Sun even to the setting my name is glorified among the nations. The author of this blessedness is he, WHO SHALL COME AS A VIOLENT RIVER. THE REDEEMER SHALL COME TO SION. This is the meaning: Christ shall come, who shall redeem Sion with his blood. Or according to the Hebrew property, he who is near to Sion, and is generated from the stock of Israel: for this is what גוֹאֵל, that is, ἀγχιστεὺς signifies. And lest we think that all Sion is redeemed, and that she is freed from the crimes with which she was stained by the blood of the Lord, he significantly added: To those who return from iniquity, if they shall have wished to do penance: in whom the prayer of the Lord may be fulfilled: Father, forgive them: for they know not what they do. Therefore, there is redemption in Sion, and a kinsman, for those who shall have received him from Jacob: and to them he promises, saying: This is my covenant with them, or pact, as all others have translated: διαθήκην, that is, testament, as the Seventy have placed. Nor did B. Luther reject that interpretation, although he also explained it in another sense, indeed he professed that our sense agrees with the Apostle: But if anyone, he says, wishes to follow Paul's opinion here as well, he would refer the whole chapter to the redemption of Christ and to the blinding which happened to the Jews in the time of Christ. Nor could Calvin himself reject him; for although he refers this prophecy in some way to the Babylonian liberation, he nevertheless acknowledges that it was properly fulfilled in the coming of Christ. The Jews, he says, refer it solely to the Babylonian redemption, but Christians solely to Christ. I join both, so that we may comprehend that whole time, from which the people returned, with that which followed, up to the coming of Christ. Because this prophecy is not fulfilled except in Christ. AND TO NO OTHER, can what is said here APPLY. For neither was the glory of God revealed to the whole world before, nor were the enemies put to flight in such a way that they did not regain their strength, until Christ, the victor over Satan, sin, and death, celebrated a singular triumph. Therefore, it simultaneously embraces the kingdom of Christ and spiritual redemption. For this prophecy pertains to it. Whence Paul concludes that the Redeemer of the world could not have been, without it pertaining to other Jews, whose fathers he had chosen, and for whom this promise was specifically destined. The Belgian Paraphrasts, who are of one mind with us here, explained this prophecy SOLELY concerning Christ and the redemption of the human race, except that they interpret verse 19 a little differently: namely in this way: WHEN THE ENEMY SHALL COME LIKE A RIVER, THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD SHALL RAISE A BANNER or sign AGAINST him. Which sense the Geneva, Italian, Spanish, and English versions also provide, and Sixtinus Amama approves, namely that the word נוססה is derived from נס, a banner. What of the fact that the Rabbis themselves in the Talmud interpret these things concerning the Messiah: R. Jochanan said: If you see a generation belittling itself, and proceeding, expect the Messiah, as it is said in Psalm 18, v. 28. For you will save the humble people, and will bring down the haughty eyes. R. Jochanan said: If you see a generation upon which many tribulations come, expect the Messiah, as it is said in Isaiah 59, v. 19, When he shall come like a rushing river: and soon it is added, and the redeemer shall come to Zion before the tribulation. R. Jochanan also said, The Son of David will not come except in a generation that is entirely innocent, as it is said in Isaiah 60, verse 21. Your people are all righteous, they shall possess the land forever; or in a generation that will be entirely guilty, as it is said in Isaiah 59, v. 16. And he saw that there was no man, or anyone, and he was astonished, or was silent, because there was no one helping, and his own arm brought salvation to him, and his justice sustained him. These things are in the Talmud. Thus also in אבקת רוכל this passage is explained: but through repentance redemption will arrive, as it is written (Isaiah 59, v. 20.) and the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who have turned from transgression. And this Redeemer will be the Messiah, the Son of David, who will gather Israel. Finally, Grotius must be convicted by Grotius. He acknowledges, namely, that the liberator is promised here to those who among the Israelites have turned from iniquity, and that he is said to be coming to them. Which fits Christ, who although he is the Savior of all, is nevertheless especially the Savior of the faithful, and can be called their redeemer in a special way according to the analogy of faith. But this cannot be said of Cyrus. For he did not come only so that the faithful, and those who had turned to God, might be liberated, but in general to liberate the people. Grotius says at v. 21. This covenant concerning liberation was made with those who had been converted. But the covenant concerning liberation through Cyrus did not only concern the converted, but the whole people. Grotius acknowledges that גאל properly means to redeem by right of kinship. In which sense it fits Christ, but not Cyrus. Why then does he depart from the proper meaning of the word? He acknowledges that Paul, when he cites this saying in Rom. 11, v. 25, to prove what he had said, καὶ οὕτω πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται, is dealing with the true Israel, with the Israel of God, as he speaks in Gal. 6, v. 16, and is looking to the time when a certain great multitude of Jews was about to embrace Christ, when the military standards of the Romans were about to appear against the sight of the temple: and when after the temple was cut down, many Jews were clearly about to receive Christ. See Annotations on Romans 11, v. 15. Why many words, when Grotius himself has confessed that this word is to be understood here concerning Christ, convinced no doubt by the very evidence of the matter. For thus he annotated on Genesis 48, v. 16. Thus the Messiah is called גואל in Isaiah 59, 19. Who then now attempts to twist this passage to Cyrus?

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET VENERIT SION REDEMPTOR, ET EIS, QUI REDEUNT AB INIQUITATE IN JA- COB, DICIT DOMINUS] Secundum ET est positum pro nempe, ut sic habeat locus: Veniet Sioni liberator, nem- pe illis, qui in Iacobo (id est, inter Israëlitas) ab iniquitate se converterint: ad Deum scilicet. Is liberator est Cyrus fi- gura Christi. גאל proprie quidem redimere jure pro- pinquitatis: sed per κατάχρησιν quovis modo liberare.

Hic potiores Interpretes alteram partem con- stituunt hujus concionis, Evangelium nempe de Christo, quod viderit Dominus, ut vers. 15. habe- tur, quod scil. omnes declinârint, nec esset qui fa- ceret bonum, nec reperiretur, qui vindicaret ho- mines è potestate Satanae, ipsumque judicaret: Et quum circumspiceret, num esset vir, qui occurreret irae Dei, obstupuerit, quod nemo inventus fuerit, ideoque Dominus ipse Filius Dei hominum cau- sam suscepit: de quo dicitur: ET SALVAVIT SIBI BRACHIUM SUUM, ET JUSTITIA EJUS IPSA CONFIRMAVIT EUM, h. e. ar- mavit se sua potentia, & usurpavit firmo ac forti ani- mo suam justitiam, ut hostes suos reprimeret, homines vero eriperet. INDUTUS EST JUSTITIA UT LORICA, ET GALEA SALUTIS IN CAPI- TE EJUS; INDUTUS EST ULTIONE TAN- QUAM VESTIMENTO, ET OPERTUS EST ZELO TANQUAM PALLIO. Haec est, inquit Brentius, armatura Christi Filii Dei, quo genere armo- rum vestit etiam militem Christi Paulus ad Ephesios sex- to & 1. Thessal. quinto. Filius enim Dei pro lorica uti- tur justitia: pro galea utitur salute: pro veste, vindi- cta: pro pallio, zelo. In quem ergo usum sic ar- matur? Ad vindictam, inquit, & ad retributio- nem hostibus suis, tam iis, qui sunt in suo ipsius po- pulo inter Israëlitas, quam illis, qui sunt in insulis, hoc est, gentibus incircumcisis. Suscipit autem hanc vin- dictam exercendam, ut servet ac tueatur adversas ho- stes Ecclesiam suam divino suo zelo, quo eam com- plectitur. Filius enim Dei dicitur armari lorica ju- stitiae, quia cum sit vere justus, justificat etiam, & efficit, ut justi reputentur, quotquot in ipsum cre- dunt, & defendantur in omnibus adversis. Hoc enim est opus justitiae in regibus & principibus, ut populum suum absolvant ab iniquis adversariorum accusatio- nibus, & defendant eum ab hostibus suis. Sic & miles Christi armatur apud Paulum thorace fidei, quia cum donemur per fidem justitia Christi, objicienda est ea, tanquam thorax, omnibus accusationibus Satanae, ut per eam tuti adversus ignita tela Satanae consistamus. Dicitur & filius Dei armari galea salutis, quia affert omnibus credentibus in ipsum veram & aeternam sa- lutem. Sic & miles Christi armatur apud Paulum galea spei salutis, quia certa spes salutis, quam in Chri-

sto habemus, concipienda est, ut etsi omnia reliqua no- strarum rerum pereunt, servemus tamen caput muni- tum salute Christi, qua salute perrumpemus mortem ipsam ad æternam vitam. Armatur etiam, seu ve- stitur filius Dei vestimento ultionis, quia ulciscitur & se & populum suum de hostibus, & adversariis suis ingenti animi robore ac fortitudine. Similiter Osiander: SICUT AD VINDICTAM QUASI AD RETRIBUTIONEM INDIGNATIONIS HOSTIBUS SUIS, ET VICISSITUDINEM INIMICIS SUIS. Sic armavit : INSULIS VICEM REDDET, id est, debellavit gentes, easq́; in suam potestatem rediget. Utitur enim Propheta in re spirituali verbis à corporalibus victoriis mu- tuo sumptis: ubi hoc agunt bellatores, ut de ho- stibus suis vindictam sumant. Quem sensum de sub- jugatione gentium, quod easdem potestati Satanæ ereptas, sibi subjecturus sit, confirmant ea, quæ se- quuntur. ET TIMEBUNT QUI SUNT AB OCCIDENTE NOMEN DOMINI, ET QUI AB ORTU SOLIS sunt, GLORIAM EJUS. Passim inter gentes in orbe agnoscitur divinitas & majestas Christi, & Salvatoris, & liberatoris gene- ris humani, CUM VENERIT ejus spirituale re- gnum QUASI FLUVIUS VIOLENTUS, qui aliquandiu cohibitus postea ingenti impetu irruit, & omnia, quæ apprehendit, secum rapit. QUEM fluvium etiam SPIRITUS DOMINI COGIT, seu impellit. Cursus enim Evangelii (ubi Domi- nus Spiritu suo docentium & discentium animos impellit) non potest retardari, sed perrumpit subi- to per omnia obstacula, quasi fluvius aliquando co- hibitus, postea vero erumpens, magna etiam vi venti impulsus. ET VENERIT, rectius, & ve- niet etiam ipsi SION REDEMPTOR, Jesus Christus, ET EIS opem feret. QUI REDEUNT AB INIQUITATE IN populo JACOB, DI- CIT DOMINUS. Hoc est, etsi gentes maximo numero colligentur in Ecclesiam Christi & Judæi abjicientur: tamen non omnino actum erit de gen- te Judaica, sed convertentur aliqui è Judaismo à sua incredulitate, & impietate ad Christum Redem- ptorem. In hanc sententiam allegatur hoc dictum Prophetæ ab Apostolo Rom. 11. cap. Ideoq; Judaica gens adhuc conservatur divinitus inter Christia- nos, Turcas, & gentes, non quod Dominus Judæo- rum incredulitatem approbet: sed quod sint in eo populo aliqui electi, qui ante novissimum diem sunt convertendi. Quæ Paraphrasis, quia nititur autoritate Apostolica, & evidentia contextus Pro- phetici, sine dubio τῇ ἰδιλελύσει ἰδίᾳ & privatæ Gro- tii præferenda est. Explicat tum Apostoli hæc ad- ducentis, tum Prophetæ nostri sententiam eximie Dn. Brentius, quem hic audire præstat inhærentem autoritati Sacræ Scripturæ, quam Grotianis com- mentis assurgere. Quod in hac pericopa postremo di- citur: Veniet Zioni Redemptor, &c. Paulus ad Romanos scribens c. 11. perspicue interpretatur. Etsi enim verba hujus loci paulo aliter apud Paulum le- guntur, quippe qui cum scriberet ad eos, qui erant pe- riti Græcæ Linguæ, utitur Græca translatione, sen- tentia tamen eadem est. Monet enim gentes, ne sibi blandiantur propter suam electionem, nec præ se con- temnant Judæos, propter ipsorum abjectionem. Judæi enim non sic abjecti sunt à Deo, ut nullus eorum ullo modo salutem consequi possit. Sed publice quidem gens eorum abjecta est, ne sit amplius populus Dei: Pri- vatim autem quisquis ex ipsis agnoscit Christum per fi- dem, fit membrum veri populi Dei, & consequitur æ- ternam salutem. Unde & antea dixit: Ecce boni- tatem & severitatem Dei, in eos quidem, qui ceci- derunt, severitatem, in te vero bonitatem, si per- manferis in bonitate. Quoniam & tu excideris, vi- delicet, si non permanferis in bonitate, & illi rursus, si non permanferint in incredulitate, inferentur &c. Et postea addit: Dona & vocatio Dei ejusmodi sunt, ut eorum illum pœnitere non possit. Vocavit Deus quondam posteritatem Abrahæ, ut esset populus seu Ecclesia Dei: Et donavit eam hac prærogativa, quod quisquis inter illos crederet in semen Abrahæ pro- missum, qui est Christus, adoptaretur in filium Dei, & consequeretur æternam salutem. Etsi autem posteri Abrahæ abjecti sunt hoc tempore à Deo, propterea, quod ipsi abjecerunt Filium Dei, tamen Deus non re- tractat vocationem & donationem suam, sed servat eam firmam & inviolatam, ut quisquis inter abjectos posteros Abrahæ resipiscit & agnoscit Christum per fidem, recipiatur in Catalogum populi Dei, & fiat particeps omnis benedictionis, quæ per semen Abra- hæ seu per Christum promissa est. Eadem plane est sententia hujus propheticidi cti, quod Paulus allegat. Propheta enim commemoravit impietatem & scele- ra Israëlitarum. Et addit, Filium Dei vindicatu- rum se de hostibus & inimicis suis. Non habuit au- tem inter homines virulentiores & crudeliores hostes, quam suum ipsius populum, posteros videlicet sancto- rum Patriarcharum Abrahæ, Isaac & Jacob. Qua- re Propheta significat hunc populum à Deo abjicien- dum. Numquid ergo, dicet quispiam, sic abjicientur Israëlitæ, ut nullus eorum unquam possit salutem consequi? Hic respondet Propheta: Nihil certe mi- nus sic abjicientur: Quia veniet Zioni Redemptor, & iis qui ex posteris Jacob ab impietate sua resi- piscunt. Christus enim Filius Dei, verus Redem- ptor, non sic sese, abjectis Israëlitis, inter gentes con- clusit, ut prorsus nunquam velit amplius esse redemptor Israëlitarum, sed potius vulgavit Evangelio suam redemptionem, ut non solum gentes ea fruantur, verum etiam Israëlitæ, quanquam abjecti possint ea frui, si convertantur ab incredulitate sua, & agno- scant Filium Dei per fidem. Non enim pœnitet Deum vocationis & donorum suorum, si modo non tæ- deat Israëlitas reversionis & resipiscentiæ suæ. Vo- cavit quondam Israëlitas populum suum: Vocat ad- huc eos populum suum, si modo per fidem in Chri- stum voluerint esse populus ejus. Vides igitur Pau- lum eadem sententia allegasse hoc dictum, qua Pro- pheta dixit. Huic explicationi Hieronymus favet: ET TIMEBUNT QUI AB OCCIDENTE NOMEN DOMINI. Tunc alienigenæ, qui de oc- cidente & oriente venturi sunt, ut requiescant in sinu Abraham: (Matth. 8.) de quibus & supra dictum est (c. 49.) Ecce isti de longe venient, alii de occi- dente, alii ab Aquilone, &c. & (Mal. 1.) Ab ortu So- lis usq; ad occasum glorificatum est nomen meum in gentibus. Hujus beatitudinis ille autor est, QUI VENIET QUASI FLUVIUS VIOLENTUS. VENIET REDEMPTOR SION. Hic sensus est: Veniet Christus, qui redimet Sion sanguine suo. Sive juxta Hebraicam proprietatem, qui propin- quus est Sion, & de Israël stirpe generatus sit: hoc enim גוֹאֵל, id est, ἀγχιστεὺς sonat. Ac ne putemus omnem redimi Sion, & eam de sceleribus liberari, quæ sanguine Domini cruentata est, significanter ad- junxit: His qui redeunt ab iniquitate, si volue- rint agere pœnitentiam: in quibus oratio Domini compleatur: Pater, ignosce eis: quod enim faciunt, nesciunt. Eorum igitur in Sion redemptio est, & pro- pinquus, qui eum susceperint ex Jacob: & illis pollice- tur, dicens: Hoc fœdus meum cum eis, sive pa- ctum, ut omnes alii transtulerunt: διαθήκην, id est, te- stamentum, ut posuêre Septuaginta. Nec B. Luther. rejecit eam interpretationem, etsi alio sensu etiam exposuerit, imo sensum nostrum Apostolo con- venire professus est: Quod si quis, inquit, Pauli sen- tentiam sequi etiam hic volet, is totum caput referret ad redemptionem Christi & ad excæcationem, quæ tempore Christi Judæis contigit. Nec reprobare eum potuit Calvinus ipse; etsi enim hanc prophetiam aliqua ratione ad liberationem Babylonicam etiam referat, proprie tamen impletam esse in adventu Christi agnoscit. Judæi, inquit, ad redemptionem Babylonicam solummodo referunt, Christiani vero ad Christum solum. Ego utramq; conjungo, ut totum illud tempus, ex quo populus rediit, cum eo quod se- quutum est, usq; ad Christi adventum comprehenda- mus. Quia non est impleta hæc Prophetia, nisi in Christo. NEC ULLI ALTERI, quæ hic dicuntur, CONVENIRE POSSUNT. Nec enim prius univer- so orbi patefacta est gloria Dei, nec ita fugati hostes, quin vires redintegrarent, donec Christus Satanæ, pec- cati & mortis victor triumphum singularem egit. Simul ergo complectitur regnum Christi & redemptionem spiritualem. Ad eam enim hoc vaticinium perti- net. Unde Paulus colligit, Redemptorem mundi esse non potuisse, quin ad alios Judæos pertineret, quorum Patres elegerat, & quibus nominatim hæc promissio destinata est. De Christo & Redemptio- ne generis humani UNICE exposuêre hoc vati- cinium Paraphrastæ Belgici, nobis hic ὁμόψη- φοι, nisi quod versum 19. paulo aliter interpre- tentur: hoc nempe modo: CUM HOSTIS VE- NERIT QUASI FLUVIUS, SPIRITUS DO- MINI VEXILLUM vel signum ERIGET AD- VERSUS ipsum. Quem sensum & Genev. Ital. Hispan. & Anglic. versiones tradunt, & approbat Sixtinus Amama, ut nempe vox נוססה à נס vexil- lo derivetur. Quid quod ipsimet Rabbini in Tal- mud de Messia hæc interpretentur: Dixit R. Jo- chanan: Si videris generationem minorificantem se, & procedentem, expecta Messiam, sicut dictum est Psalmo 18. v. 28. Quia tu populum humilem salva- bis, & oculos sublimes demittes. Dixit R. Jocha- nan: Si videris generationem super quam veniunt multæ tribulationes, expecta Messiam, sicut dictum est Esa. 59. v. 19, Cum venerit sicut fluvius tribulans: & mox subjungitur, & venit jam ante tribulationem Sioni redemptor. Dixit etiam R. Jochanan, Fi- lius David non veniet nisi in generatione quæ tota est innocens, sicut dictum est Esaiæ 60. vers. 21. Popu- lus tuus omnes justi ad seculum possidebunt ter- ram; vel in generatione quæ tota erit rea, sicut di- ctum est Esa. 59. v. 16. Et vidit quod non esset vir, vel aliquis, & obstupuit, vel conticuit, quod non esset succurrens, & salvabit sibi brachium suum, & justitia ejus sustentabit eum. Hæc in Talmud. Sic etiam in אבקת רוכל exponitur hic locus: per pæ- nitentiam vero adveniet redemptio, sicut scribitur (Esa. 59. v. 20.) & veniet Sioni redemptor, & con- versis à defectione. Et hic Redemptor erit Messias Filius Davidis, qui congregabit Israëlem. Denique convincendus est Grotius ex Grotio. Agnoscit nempe liberatorem hic illum promitti his, qui inter Israëlitas ab iniquitate se converterint, illisq; ventu- rum dici. Quod Christo convenit, qui etsi Salvator omnium, maxime tamen fidelium est, & speciali ra- tione eorum redemptor dici potest juxta analo- giam fidei. De Cyro vero id dici non potest. Ille enim non tantum venit, ut liberarentur fideles, & qui conversi erant ad Deum, sed in genere ad libe- randum populum. Dicit Grotius ad v. 21. Hoc fædus de liberatione cum illis, qui conversi fuerunt, initum es- se. At fœdus de liberatione per Cyrum non tan- tum concernebat conversos, sed totum populum. Agnoscit Grotius גאל proprie esse jure propinquit a- tis redimere. Quo sensu Christo convenit, non vero Cyro. Cur ergo à propria vocis significatio- ne discedit? Agnoscit Paulum,ubi hoc dictum ad- ducit Rom. 11. v. 25. ut probet quod dixerat καὶ οὕτω πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται de vero Israële, de Israële Dei, ut loquitur Gal. 6. v. 16. agere, & tempus re- spicere,quo magna quædam multitudo Iudæorum Chri- stum erat amplexura, cum signa militaria Romano- rum apparitura contra conspectum templi: & cum post excisum templum multi plane Judæi Christum su- scepturi erant. Vid. Annotat. ad Roman. 11. v. 15. Quid multis, quum fassus sit ipse Grotius, de Chri- sto hanc vocem hic intelligendam esse, convictus sine dubio ab ipsa rei evidentia. Sic enim anno- tavit ad Genes. 48. v. 16. Sic Messias גואל dicitur Esa. 59, 19. Qui ergo nunc locum istum ad Cyrum detorquere conatur?

## 59:21
Vers. 21.

THIS COVENANT OF MINE WITH THEM] With those who shall have been converted. MY SPIRIT IS THAT WHICH IS IN THEE, AND THE WORDS, WHICH I HAVE PUT IN THY MOUTH] That is, Prophecies, as the Chaldean interprets here: A word proceeded from the Spirit of God. SHALL NOT DEPART FROM THY MOUTH, AND FROM THE MOUTH OF THY SEED, SAYS THE LORD, FROM NOW AND FOREVER] That is, it will be fulfilled in such a way that future posterity will always be mindful of it.

He therefore interprets those things concerning the covenant with the converted Israelites regarding the reduction from the Babylonian captivity; but strangely, perversely, and crookedly. For not to mention that God made a promise about liberating the people from that captivity, but nowhere is it read that he entered into a covenant about that matter, much less that he sanctioned such a pact or covenant anywhere for those who had been converted from the Israelites, and that in this whole chapter there is no mention made of the captivity or the solution of the same, it is manifest that a far different covenant is proposed here, namely concerning the Spirit and the word of the Lord not being taken away from the Israelites. And therefore Grotius openly does violence to the words of the illustrious promise, in many ways. First, while he makes the word proceeded from the Spirit of God out of the Spirit, when here the Spirit of God, which is in the people, and the words, which he has put in his mouth, are expressly distinguished from the Prophet. Then when the Lord says; My Spirit SHALL NOT DEPART FROM THY MOUTH, Grotius perverts it thus; The discourse proceeding from the Spirit shall be fulfilled. Thirdly the Prophet says, that the Spirit of the Lord and his word shall not be taken away from the mouth of the people, NOR FROM THE MOUTH OF HIS SEED. Grotius twists it thus: the prophecy shall be so fulfilled, that posterity shall always be mindful of it. Who ever could have carved such a sense out of the words themselves? Finally, the Lord does not speak only of the posterity of Israel according to the flesh, because He promises the παρά- sασιν OF THE SPIRIT FOR EVER. Which is to be understood of the faithful, and of Israel according to the spirit, to whom this grace is both promised, and is performed even unto the consummation of the age. It seemed to Jerome that these things were said of Isaiah: who observes that most people consider those things to have been said of Christ. Yet he cherishes the same sense as we do: This is the eternal covenant of the Gospel, that my spirit which is in thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, by which thou shalt predict things to come, shall not depart from thy mouth, nor from the mouth of thy sons and grandsons, and the offspring of thy seed: so that every generation through the series may be demonstrated: namely that the grace of the Prophets comes in the Apostles, and through those who from Israel are to believe through the Apostles. But what he infers from now even unto eternity: it agrees with that, Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. Nor should the observation of Jerome be omitted, which he delivered towards the end of this chapter, which brings light to not a few oracles. For having brought forward the explanation of this Apostolic prophecy from Rom. 11.

Blindness in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles should come in: and so all Israel should be saved: as it is written: There shall come out of Sion, who shall deliver and turn away ungodliness from Jacob, and this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. Jerome adds: We have pursued these things more broadly for this reason, that whatever promises we have read and are about to read concerning Sion and Jerusalem, we may understand them to be said not generally to all Jews, but specifically to those who were chosen from Israel in the Apostles and through the Apostles. This is Jerome. The Apostle, with other federal promises, joins this covenant of eternal assistance of the Spirit and preservation of the word, Grotius not dissenting in his Annotations on chapter 16. Rom. concerning the free remission and taking away of sins he joined Rom. 11:26, since this is the fruit and effect of the word and the Holy Spirit, and for that reason that covenant is directed, that the Word of the Lord and the Holy Spirit ought not to depart from the seed of Israel, so that, namely, sin may be taken away. But from this the perpetual preservation of the Church is rightly gathered: yet its visibility, or personal succession with the Papists, is not to be concluded from it, nor with the Calvinists the absolute perseverance of the faithful: because this promise was made to the whole Church, not to individual believers. But these things are concerning the 59th Chapter.

ORATION V. Concerning the kingdom of Christ and his ministers.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

HOC FOEDUS MEUM CUM EIS] Cum illis, qui conversi fuerint. SPIRITUS MEUS EST QUI EST IN TE, ET VERBA, QUÆ POSUI IN ORE TUO] Id est, Pro- phetiæ, ut hic interpretatur Chaldæus: Sermo à Spiritu Dei profectus. NON RECEDET DE ORE TUO, ET DE O- RE SEMINIS TUI, DICIT DOMINUS, A MODO USQUE IN SEMPITERNUM] Id est, ita implebitur, ut semper ejus memor sit futura posteritas.

Interpretatur ergo illa de fœdere cum conversis Israëlitis quoad reductionem è captivitate Babyloni- ca; sed aliene,perverse, & contorte. Nam ne di- cam, quod promissionem de liberando populo ex illa captivitate fecerit Deus,nuspiam autem fœdus legatur ea de re iniisse,nedum illis,qui ex Israëlitis conversi fuerint, sanciverit alicubi tale pactum, aut fœdus,quodque nulla in toto hoc capite de ca- ptivitate aut solutione ejusdem mentio facta sit, manifestum est, longe aliud fœdus hic proponi, nempe de Spiritu & verbo Domini non auferendo ab Israëlitis. Ideoque aperte vim infert Grotius verbis illustris promissionis,multis modis. Primo, dum è Spiritu facit sermonem à Spiritu Dei profe- ctum,cum diserte hic distinguatur à Propheta,Sp.- ritus Dei, qui est in populo, & verba,quæ posuit in ore ipsius. Deinde cum Dominus ait; Spiritus meus NON RECEDET DE ORE TUO, Gro- tius id ita pervertit; Sermo à Spiritu profectus im- plebitur. Tertio Propheta dicit, Spiritum Domini & verbum ejus non ablatum iri de ore populi, NEC DE ORE SEMINI EJUS. Id ita detorquet Grotius: ita implebitur vaticinium, ut semper ejus memor futura sit posteritas. Quis unquam talem sensum ex ipsis verbis exsculpierit? Deniq; non de posteritate tantum Israëlis secundum carnem lo- quitur Dominus, quia promittit Spiritus παρά- sασιν IN SEMPITERNUM. Quod de fidelibus,& Israële secundum spiritum intelligendum, quibus hæc gratia & promissa est, & præstatur usque ad consummationem seculi.Ad Esaiam hæc dici Hie- ronymo visum est: qui plerosq́; ad Christum illa di- cta æstimare,observat. Sensum tamen eundem nobiscum fovet: Hoc est pactum Evangelii sempi- ternum, ut spiritus meus qui est in te, & verba mea quæ posui in ore tuo, per quæ ventura prædices, non de tuo ore discedant, nec de filiorum tuorum ac nepo- tum, & feminis seminis tui: ut omnis per seriem ge- neratio demonstretur : quod scilicet gratia Prophe- tarum in Apostolis veniat, & per eos qui de Israël per Apostolos credituri sunt. Quod autem infert à modo usque in sempiternum: illi congruit, Cœlum & terra transibunt, verba autem mea non præteri- bunt. Neque prætermittenda observatio Hiero- nymi, quam sub finem hujus capitis tradidit, quæ lucem conciliat non paucis oraculis.Adducta enim explicatione hujus vaticinii Apostolici è Rom. 11.

Cœcitas ex parte Israël contigit, donec plenitudo gen- tium subintraret : & sic omnis Israël salvus fieret : si- cut scriptum est: Veniet ex Sion, qui liberet & aver- tat impietates à Jacob, & hoc illis a me testamentum, quum abstulero peccata eorum. Addit Hieron. Hæc idcirco latius prosequuti sumus, ut quicquid repro- missionum & legimus & lecturi sumus ad Sion, & ad Hierusalem, non generaliter ad omnes Judæos, sed specialiter ad eos dici intelligamus, qui in Apostolis & per Apostolos electi sunt ex Israël. Hæc Hierony- mus. Fœdus hoc sempiternæ assistentiæ Spiri- tus & conservationis verbi Apostolus cum aliis promissionibus fœderalibus, non dissentiente Gro- tio in Annot. ad c. 16. Rom. de gratuita peccatorum remissione & ablatione copulavit Rom. 11, 26. siqui- dem hic sit fructus verbi & effectus & Spiritus San- cti, eoque fœdus illud directum sit, quod non re- cedere debeat Verbum Domini & S. S. à semine Israëlis, ut nempe auferatur peccatum. Recte au- tem hinc colligitur Ecclesiæ perpetua conservatio: nec tamen visibilitas ejus, aut personalis successio cum Papicolis inde concludenda, neque cum Cal- vinianis absoluta fidelium perseverantia : quia toti Ecclesiæ hæc facta promissio, non singulis fideli- bus. Sed hæc de 59. Capite.

ORATIO V. De regno Christi & ministris ejus.

## 60:1 Argument
CHAPTER LX.

I congratulate the Church of the Prophet, because the glory of the Lord has risen upon it, and the Gentiles walk in its light, the multitude and gifts of which he describes, celebrating the holiness, riches, peace, justice, salvation, and eternal glory of the Church.

Verse 1. ARISE SHINE JERUSALEM] Shine: that is, awake. The cause follows, because the light is present, that is, prosperity. The name Jerusalem is not in the Hebrew, but it is not badly added to the sense, both by the Greeks and by the Chaldean.

Latin:

CAPUT LX.

Gratulor Prophetæ Ecclesiæ, quod in ea Domi- ni gloria orta sit, & gentes in lumine ejus ambulent, quarum multitudinem & mu- nera describit, celebrans Ecclesiæ sancti- tatem, divitias, pacem, justitiam & salu- tem, ac gloriam sempiternam.

Vers. 1. SURGE ILLUMINARE JERUSALEM ] Illumi- nare : id est, expergiscere. Causa sequitur, quia adest lux, id est, prosperitas. Nomen Jerusalem in Hebræo non est, sed non male ad sensum additum est, & à Græcis & à Chaldæo.

## 60:2
Verse 2. AND DARKNESS THE PEOPLES] The Medes first, then the Babylonians.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET CALIGO POPULOS] Medos primum, deinde Babylonios.

## 60:3
Verse 3. THE GENTILES SHALL WALK IN THY LIGHT, AND KINGS IN THE BRIGHTNESS OF THY RISING] They shall come to congratulate you.

Grotius snatches this whole very illustrious Prophecy to the restoration of Jerusalem, perverting the entire chapter so that all things signify only temporal happiness. Jerome noted similar explanations of the Jews and semi-Jews: The Jews and our semi-Jews, who expect a golden and gem-studded Jerusalem, contend that these things will happen in the thousand-year kingdom, when all nations are to serve Israel, and the camels of Midian and Ephah coming from Sheba shall bring gold and incense, and all the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together, and the rams of Nebaioth shall come, that they may be sacrificed upon the altar of the temple that shall have been built: Also that from the isles and especially the ships of Tarshish her daughters shall fly as doves, bringing the riches of gold and silver: And that the walls of Jerusalem shall be built by foreigners, over whom the kings of the nations shall preside: and that the gates of the city shall always be open, so that by days and nights the riches of Jerusalem and victims may be brought: And all things that are desolate are to be constructed with cypress and pine and cedar, cut in Lebanon: especially the temple of the Lord, in which there may be eternal joy: so that it may suck the milk of nations, and eat the riches of kings: and that there will be such an abundance of things that for brass they may have gold: for iron silver: for wood brass: for stones iron. Also that its princes shall enjoy eternal peace, and bishops shall preside over the peoples in justice, but also that the gates shall be engraved. And what is greater than these, that for the Sun and Moon, the Lord himself shall shine with eternal light: and that for one man it shall have a thousand most valiant men, and for little ones it shall possess most robust nations. These things are said by those who desire earthly pleasures, and seek the beauty of wives and a number of children, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame: he who follows the error of whom, UNDER THE CHRISTIAN NAME, confesses himself LIKE to the Jews. You might not undeservedly say that of Grotius. Who owes most of his commentaries in these Annotations to the Jews. But Christian interpreters easily agree that these things pertain to the times of the New Testament: Which opinion must be confirmed by certain arguments, before we approach the special discussion of the Grotian misinterpretation. But the first argument is provided by the coherence with the promise made at the end of the previous chapter. For since he had predicted the coming of the Redeemer and the conversion of some among the people of Jacob, and had promised to his spiritual seed, nay, had established a covenant with the same, that the Spirit and word of the Lord would never depart from the same, he now rouses Jerusalem, as the interpreters of the LXX have explained, (although that name is not held in the Hebrew text) because all things are expressed in the feminine gender, and in verse 14 the city of the Lord Sion is commemorated, that it may rise at the coming of Goel its Redeemer; and he prophesies concerning the light, which he is about to bring not only to them; but also to any Gentiles whatsoever throughout the world. Which sequence is an invincible proof that these things which are promised pertain to the times of the coming of Christ, and the calling of the Gentiles, and to the whole times of the New Testament, during which that divine covenant is performed, until the consummation of the age. We seek the second argument from the evident falsity of the literal sense. For since the letter is openly absurd, or false, the thing itself demands that we do not cling to the letter. But what is more evident than that Jerusalem or Zion was never such a worldly and external kingdom as is described here, and that such great happiness of this age never befell it as is promised in this place? Therefore, necessity requires that these things be understood of the spiritual kingdom of the Messiah, which He undertook to administer in Zion, and administers perpetually, Ps. 2,6. Ps. 110. 3. and which was established in the whole world by the preaching of the Gospel, having begun at Jerusalem. Truly, the Holy Spirit commends this kingdom by things far the most famous and excellent of all, such as never were or will be in any worldly kingdom. Namely, by the Majesty of the King, by the multitude of the inhabitants, by the veneration and obedience of all nations, by the magnificence of the buildings, by the plenty and abundance of all things, by the moderation and equity of the magistrates, by the justice of the subjects, and finally by true and perpetual happiness. Lyranus executes this argument against the Grotian gloss of the Jews: Those who returned, he says, were never in such prosperity as before: indeed, all things which are said here, 'your heart will wonder and be dilated, when the multitude of the sea shall be converted to you, the strength of the Gentiles shall come to you.' For although some, having abandoned paganism, adhered to them, yet they were few and of small reputation and virtue. Likewise, what is added afterwards: 'And the sons of strangers shall build your walls'; because they themselves built them in the time of Nehemiah, and with great labor and anxiety, so that with one hand they did the work and with the other they held the sword.

Nehemiah 4. And this fear of the adversaries, who were wishing to hinder them. And what is added here: thy gates shall be opened continually, &c. because they were kept closed more by fear of the adversaries. Also, what is added afterwards: For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish: because those kingdoms did not serve them, but rather the reverse: first by paying tribute to the Persians; afterwards to the Greeks, and afterwards to the Romans, as is evident from the books of Ezra and Nehemiah and the Maccabees, and the Gospels, and from the books of Josephus and other historiographers. A third argument is supplied by the interpretation of the Holy Spirit, who, neglecting the ῥητῷ, explains it spiritually. That, however, is without doubt the genuine meaning which was delivered by the Holy Spirit himself, 2 Pet. 1:21. The passage is Rev. 21, where the description of the heavenly Jerusalem is in good part taken from this prophecy: the city has no need of sun, nor moon, to shine in it. And then: its gates shall not be shut by day: And again: There shall be no night there, and they need no light of lamp, nor light of sun, because the Lord God illuminates them. Since, therefore, the Holy Spirit describes the glory and happiness of the heavenly Jerusalem with these words and meanings, these things must by no means be understood of the glory and happiness of the earthly Jerusalem, but of the heavenly, which is reserved for the spiritual Kingdom of Christ and the Church in the other life, of which it has a certain beginning spiritually in this age, but they await the heavenly completion in the other. We seek a fourth [argument] from the subject matter and argument of the following discourse, which is immediately connected here, inasmuch as it pertains, with Christ himself as interpreter, to the times of the New Testament and the prophetic office of Christ. For thus our Savior in Luke 4 in the Nazarene synagogue professed publicly: Today this scripture is fulfilled in your ears. Fifthly, the confession of the Jews themselves can confound Grotius. For thus it is read in Bereshith Rabba upon that Gen. 15:17: the sun was setting. In the hour in which the Messiah will come, of whom it is written in Ps. 89: His throne as the sun before me, in that hour there will be darkness, or obscurity, for the nations. For thus it is written in Is. 60: For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples, but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall appear upon thee. Similarly in the great exposition of Genesis on ch. 25:6: This is what is written in Job 6:19: Look to the paths of Tema, the ways of Sheba expect them: There is no Sheba except the sons of Abraham, as it is said in Gen. 25:3: And Jokshan begat Sheba and Dedan: and when Solomon was magnified in his kingdom, they said; Perhaps he is the Messiah, and immediately they came to him, as it is said in 1 Kings 10:1. And the Queen of Sheba having heard the fame of Solomon, came in the name of the Lord, to test him with riddles. Do not read Queen of Sheba; but kingdom of Sheba. And what is said in the Name of the Lord? There were prophets for those who prophesied in the name of the Lord their God the words which had been delivered to them, and which came successively to their hand from Abraham. And whence is it held that they were to come to the days of the Messiah, and to serve him? As it is said in Is. 60:6: The multitude of camels shall cover thee; the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, all they from Sheba shall come, they shall bring gold and incense: and they shall announce the praises of the Lord God; This is the King Messiah, as it is said in Jer. 23:6. And this is the name by which they shall call him, The Lord our righteousness. And thus says Isaiah ch. 60:2: God shall arise upon thee and his glory shall appear upon thee, and the nations shall go to thy light: and kings to the brightness of thy rising. Which meaning is also expressed in the Targum, that indeed this prophecy is to be understood of Christ: since it rendered it thus: Arise, be enlightened, Jerusalem, because the time of thy salvation approaches, and the honor of God shall reveal itself upon thee; because behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the kingdoms, and the Divinity of the Lord shall descend upon thee, and his honor shall be revealed upon thee, and the nations shall go to thy light, and kings to receive thy brightness. Behold, thus the Jews acknowledged the Messiah in this prophecy, whom Grotius the Christian did not acknowledge or see. But these things in general. A special ἐξήγησις suggests most clear special arguments, by which both κατασκευαστικῶς the common interpretation of Christians, that the discourse is about the spiritual kingdom of Christ, not about the happiness of the temporal Jerusalem, may be built up, and ἀνασκευαστικῶς the Jewish commentaries of Grotius may be destroyed. We draw the first special reason, therefore, from the Majesty of this King, for which Jerusalem is stirred up, that it may ARISE from squalor and mourning, that it may emerge from darkness, because it lay prostrate and cast down, established in calamity and sorrow: THAT IT MAY BE ILLUMINATED, i.e., become illustrious and blessed. FOR THY LIGHT HAS COME, AND THE GLORY OF THE LORD HAS RISEN UPON THEE. What, therefore, is that light of Jerusalem, what is the glory of the Lord, if not Christ promised to it, expected by the faithful, who is that great LIGHT, illuminating all men, John 1:9. The LIGHT of the world, John 8, ch. 12. and the glory of the people of Israel, the light of the Gentiles, Is. 22:6, ch. 49:6, and Luke 2. Thus the same is hinted by this metaphorical locution, which Zech. 9:9: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion, shout, O daughter of Jerusalem, because Behold thy King shall come to thee, just and a Savior. Montacutius in Origin. Eccles. on the life of Christ, book 1, p. 48, interprets this ῥῆσιν of the Angelic light, with which, to wit, the angel was surrounded on the night of Christ's birth, Luke 2. But he says it is a secondary sense. How, however, would the sense of the angelic light in the field of Bethlehem have a place here, where the matter is about the light of Jerusalem having risen to illuminate the nations. Grotius too jejunely understands prosperity by light. More correctly the Jews themselves, with the Targum leading the way, understand the MESSIAH. And the Prophet indeed exhorts, be enlightened, that with the darkness put to flight, there may be light for Jerusalem. Which Grotius wrongly explains as awake. The reason, however, why it ought to be illuminated is the arrival of the light and glory of Jerusalem, which must be different from that which the Prophet demands and requires of Jerusalem. But what is the cause of the rising and the illumination, if not the arrival of Him who is the light and glory of the people? For the hearers of Isaiah had been struck with fear of the future Babylonian captivity, both because they were anxious about the external safety of the city of Jerusalem, and indeed especially because they were more concerned about the true and eternal salvation of the Church and the arrival of the Messiah; and therefore the Prophet consoles them, and teaches that the city of Jerusalem, after its devastation, is not only to be restored, but also to be so illuminated by the presence, sermons, and miracles of the Son of God, that from it salvation may be spread abroad to all nations: Furthermore, since there is no remission of sins, righteousness, and salvation in any other than in Jesus Christ, Isaiah opportunely, nay necessarily, preaches to his hearers about the arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ and about his kingdom, so that, if any are terrified by the judgment of sin and thirst for righteousness and salvation, they may be stirred up to faith in Christ, and may receive through him the remission of sins, and be reckoned righteous before God and be saved, as our Brentius has it on p. 766. Therefore the faithful greatly desired the Messiah as their light and glory, as is evident from the example of Simeon and others: Luke 2:25, 32, 38. Concerning whom also the Rabbis in Bereschith Rabba on Gen. 41:44 have professed that he is the one whom Isaiah in the parallel passage, chapter 49:6, called the light of the nations: Can it be said that the Redeemer is a respecter of persons? Far be it: but all who confess him with their mouth, and with their works, and with their heart, he will save and deliver, as it is said in Jer. 23, 6. In those days Judah shall be saved, as if he were saying, All who confess him; and thus he says in Is. 45, 22. Turn to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth. bow, and every tongue shall swear. And of him the Scripture says, Is. 49, 6. And I have given you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the ends of the earth. And there is held concerning this very prophecy a most illustrious passage in the book Jalkut, from the ancient book Pesikta to these words, Arise my light, for your light has come, Is. 60, 1. where this light is said to be the light of the Messiah. The words are: The Synagogue of Israel said before God the blessed; Lord of the world, because of the Law, which you gave to me, which is called the Fountain or spring of life, I will delight in your light; What is, In your light we shall see light? This is the light of the Messiah, as it is said, And God saw the light, that it was good; for this teaches that God foresaw the age of the Messiah and his works, before the world was created, and therefore hid it for the Messiah and his generation, under the Throne of his glory. Satan said before God the Blessed; Lord of the world, that light, which is hidden under the throne of your glory, whose is it? God answered him, His, who is about to put you to shame, and to affect you with shame and ignominy. Satan replied; Lord of the world, show him to me. God said to him: Come and see him; after he saw him, he trembled, and fell on his face, saying, surely this is the MESSIAH, who is about to thrust me and all peoples into Gehenna, as it is said; he has swallowed up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away the tear from every face (Is. 25, 8.) At that hour the peoples were moved, and said; Lord of the world, Who is that, into whose hand we shall fall: what is his name? and what is his condition? God B. answered, His name is Ephraim Messiah of my righteousness, he will exalt his stature and the stature of his generation, and will illuminate the eyes of Israel, and will save his people, nor will any nation or tongue be able to rise up against him, as it is said; The enemy shall not exact from him, nor shall the enemy afflict him Ps. 89, 23. All his enemies and foes will be troubled and will flee from his sight, as it is said: And I will crush his enemies from his face. See v. 24. Nay, even the rivers will cease (to flow) into the sea as it is said; And I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers, ibid. v. 26. With these words God began to bargain with him (the Messiah, namely) after his enemies had fled, saying to him: The iniquities of those who are hidden with you, will thrust you into an iron yoke, and will make you like a calf, whose eyes grow dim, and they will constrain or strangle your Spirit in the yoke: because of their iniquities your tongue will cleave to your palate. Is such your will? (Do you wish to take this upon yourself voluntarily?) The Messiah said to God; Lord of the world; Perhaps these pains will last for many years? God answered, By your life and by the life of your head, I have decreed one week upon you, if this is troublesome to you, I will expel them immediately. He, (the Messiah;) Lord of the world, with the exultation of my heart, and with the joy of my heart I receive this upon me, provided that not even one from Israel perishes; and not only those who will live in my days, but also all who have been dead from the first Adam until now; nor even only those, but also all the aborted and embryos; finally all, whom you have determined to create, and have not been created. Under this condition I am willing, and I will receive these pains upon myself. They said; That week, in which the Son of David (the Messiah) will come, they will take iron beams, and will place them on his neck, so that his stature will be bent, he will exclaim, weep, and his voice will ascend into heaven, saying to

God; how great will be my strength! how great will be my spirit! how long will my soul last! how long will my limbs last! I am not flesh and blood. David wept over that hour, saying; My strength is dried up like a potsherd, Ps. 22, 16. Then God said to him; Ephraim Messiah my righteousness, you have already taken this upon yourself from the six days of creation etc. And afterwards: OUR RABBIS have handed down, at that hour, when the Messiah will come, and will stand upon the roof of the house of the sanctuary, he will proclaim, and will say to the Israelites; Humiliated and afflicted, the time of your redemption has approached, if you do not believe this, behold my light, which rises upon you, as it is said; Arise my light, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. From which it is evident, that this was a common TRADITION of the Rabbis, that the Prophet speaks here of the Messiah and of his advent, and that the mystery concerning the redemption of the Messiah was not unknown to the ancient Rabbis, even if they wrapped it up according to their custom in cabalistic inventions, and did not propose it in bare and open words.

The second reason is taken from the multitude of the subjects. Which the Prophet illustrates by the antithesis of the first state: BEHOLD DARKNESS SHALL COVER THE EARTH, AND THICK DARKNESS THE PEOPLES: BUT UPON YOU THE LORD SHALL ARISE, AND HIS GLORY SHALL BE SEEN UPON YOU. At the time of the advent of Christ, darkness of error and infidelity covered the earth, and thick darkness the peoples, in which all nations were still wandering. But a great light was rising upon Jerusalem, because the dawn from on high was visiting them Luke 1. The Lord himself arose as the true light John 1. And his glory was seen in the same: because they saw the glory of the only-begotten from the Father, John 1. The Chaldean translated, but in You shall dwell שכינתא the divinity of the Lord, whence John used concerning this matter the word ἐσκήνωσεν John 1, 14. The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, the glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, as if he had wished to express, and to point out this oracle with his finger. If anyone should say that the earthly Jerusalem is indicated here, inasmuch as it is compared with other peoples, overwhelmed by darkness, because the Lord is said to rise in it; and therefore all other things are to be understood of the earthly Jerusalem: I reply: I would not deny that this earthly metropolis of Judea is addressed by these words, but not as it is earthly: nor by reason of the external and political nature of its condition; but by reason of its internal and mystical dignity, by which it was the seat of the Church, and in respect of the faithful, who in it were awaiting the consolation of Israel. For the Messiah was their light, their glory, their joy. And therefore, not only those who were faithful within it belonged to this Jerusalem, but also those who, established outside of it, were joined to it through faith, not only Israelites, but also others embracing the Messiah by faith, the denomination nevertheless being made from that city, from whence the Gospel was to be spread to others. Wherefore it is no wonder if, here and in similar prophecies, certain things pertain properly to Jerusalem itself, while others concern the faithful commonly in and outside of Jerusalem, the mother of churches, with her daughters, as they speak today: because all the faithful belonged to Jerusalem in a certain way, as the seat of the Church, where God had his fire and hearth. But because the boundaries of Jerusalem were to be expanded through the calling of the Gentiles, …therefore, under the complex of this word, the Gentiles adhering to it by faith are also included. Nor is it necessary, however, to establish a double or triple sense of the same word in the same place, but the predicates of Jerusalem agree only by a different respect, for instance, either in respect of the external seat or the external temple, or in respect of the true and spiritual members in it, if even in a state of expansion, so to speak, with respect to any believers whatsoever, whether within it or outside of it. I am speaking of the same passage of Scripture. For we do not deny that this word obtains different meanings in different places, and is sometimes called the external city or metropolis of Judea, and sometimes the spiritual and mystical Jerusalem. Thus, in this place, the city of Judea itself is addressed, but as the metropolis of the kingdom of Christ, not as the metropolis of the Jewish kingdom. For that the city itself is designated is apparent from the fact that it is commanded to rise from the squalor of various afflictions, and that the Lord was to arise first IN it, and His glory was to be revealed, when darkness still surrounded other peoples, and that by the splendor and dignity of this city, which is promised to it around the time of the New Testament, all the most famous cities and metropolises are obscured. For in this city Christ preached His Gospel: in this city He performed many and great miracles, in this city He accomplished His sacrifice for the expiation of the sins of the whole world. In this city He rose from the dead. Not far from this city He ascended into heaven, in this city He sent the Holy Spirit to His disciples. Finally, from this city He spread the Gospel through the Apostles to all nations, so that as many as believe in the Gospel spread from this city may obtain eternal righteousness and salvation. However, that light is not confined within the walls of this city, so that its inhabitants alone may enjoy it and be enlightened. Indeed, only the mystical citizens of this city enjoy it, but not only Jews are citizens, but also the Gentiles become its citizens when they acknowledge the Messiah through faith and are enlightened by His light. For the Church of the Lord began indeed to be gathered from the Jews at the beginning, but soon, with the Gospel spread among the Gentiles, it was so increased and multiplied by the Gentiles that it could no longer be comprehended by any number. This is the explanation of Cyril: Observe above others, the divine light given to the Israelites by God, namely through Christ, that the Prophet says: Your light has come, showing that He who was once foretold in the Law and by the holy prophets, and who shone upon mortals in the flesh in the last times of the age, is all but present. And he calls Him who appeared the glory of the Lord. For Christ has arisen like a certain Sun, illuminating all things with divine light and intelligence and the splendor of the true knowledge of God: sending forth to those more ready to embrace the faith. And He is the glory of God and the Father. In Him and through Him and with Him He is glorified. And afterwards: For it is true that while Christ shone upon the Israelites above others, the multitude of the Gentiles was held in darkness, grace not yet having been transferred to them. Behold therefore, he says, the whole land of the Gentiles is covered with darkness and gloom, namely of ignorance and error. But the Lord will appear over you: For He has shone, as I said, upon them and indeed first, and His glory has been seen, by the extraordinary magnitude of works, signs, and wonders. For among them He performed miracles, as God, partly raising the dead from their tombs, partly sending light to the eyes of the blind, cleansing lepers with a nod, rebuking demons with authority, and omitting no means at all to convince them, and to persuade them that He is truly God and the natural Son of God. And the Kings, he says, shall walk in your light, and the Gentiles in your splendor. The Prophet again connects the calling of the Gentiles to the visitation of the Israelites: so that they may see, if they themselves despise their Redeemer by their disobedience, and recoil from His love, that with the destruction of their head, He will not be destitute of worshippers, but rather that He would bring in Gentiles and kings through faith. Afterwards, however, he says that the Prophet addresses the intelligible Jerusalem: He makes a prediction of all these things, and addresses the intelligible Jerusalem, that is, the Church constituted from the beginning from the Jews:

For those first ones believed: Lift up your eyes round about, and see your children gathered: For behold all your sons come from afar, and your daughters shall be carried on shoulders. For he addresses with these words those who, gathered from every nation and region, have believed, the Church, I say, with the divine and Evangelical preaching ensnaring the whole world, and inviting them as if to a certain most fortified city, to the grace of faith, to the food of the saints: just as indeed elsewhere: For it shall be, he says, in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be visible, set on the tops of the mountains, and it shall be elevated above the hills, and many nations shall come to it, and shall say: Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob. And He will announce to us His way: And we will walk in it. But the children of Jerusalem are not to be called only those who are sprung from the blood of Israel, but as many as have been called from every nation and region through faith to the light of truth: for as the most wise Paul writes: Not all who are of Israel, these are Israel: nor because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. For it was said by God to the divine Abraham: I have made you a father of many nations. Therefore, as if the multitude were already gathered from the Gentiles and worshipping Christ: Lift up, he says, your eyes round about, that is, survey the whole world, and from every part of it you will see your children running to you, and they shall come, even if they were once far away. Far is not said by reason of place, but pertains to the soul and the affection of the mind. These are the words of Cyril. Nor does Jerome inconveniently teach that these things are said of the spiritual Jerusalem: But let us believe, according to the former sense, that these things are said to the universal Church, which was first gathered from the Jewish people, and transmitted the light, which had arisen over it, through the Apostle to the Gentiles. To whom it is said: Arise, be enlightened: so that she who fell among the unbelievers may rise among the believers: she who fell in the Synagogues may rise in the Churches: and after she has risen, let her be enlightened: so that they may by no means have the darkness of error. For your light has come, he says: which all the Prophets were promising: which you were constantly expecting. And the glory of the Lord, which once was over His tabernacle and temple, has arisen over you. Of which it is said: Glorious things are said of you, O city of God. For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, those who savor earthly things: And mist the peoples: or as it is read in the Hebrew, tribes: which is properly referred to the Jews: of whom it is written in another Psalm: For thither the tribes ascended, the tribes of the Lord, the testimony of Israel. But the Lord shall arise upon thee, the Sun of righteousness, and his glory shall be seen upon thee. Of whom it is written: And we saw his glory, glory as of the only begotten of the father, full of grace and truth. And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light. We shall all walk in the light of the Apostles, which shines in the world, and the darkness did not comprehend it. And kings, he says, in the brightness of thy rising: when thou wast first born in Christ. Which is fulfilled both spiritually and carnally: That kings, whose heart is in the hand of the Lord, and in whom sin does not reign in their mortal body, may walk in the brightness of the nascent Church, or in him who has risen in the Church: and true kings submit their necks to the faith of Christ. Which we see fulfilled daily, when the error of idolatry being removed and the rage of persecution, Roman princes pass over to the faith and tranquility. He adds an observation, that the name of Jerusalem and of the nations, MIST UPON THE NATIONS, which is placed here by the LXX, is not found in the Hebrew: and it should be marked with an obelus, against those who assert that all things which are said, are said to Jerusalem. Grotius's gloss is inept, that by the peoples the Medes and Babylonians are understood.

Darkness shall cover the peoples, first the Medes, then the Babylonians. What, I ask, are the traces of this gloss in the text? And since darkness is said to cover the earth generally, and darkness the peoples, who gave Grotius the power of restricting those things which were spoken generally to certain peoples? Nor indeed is the discourse about bodily calamity, but about spiritual darkness, which both that light which is promised to Jerusalem, and the light in which the nations are to walk, and what are added further, teach. And the Jews themselves, the more sound ones, acknowledge this, whence in the aforementioned book Jalkut these things are brought forward from the tradition of the Rabbis, cohering immediately with those which have been brought forward just now: Upon them alone the glory of the Lord has arisen. For behold darkness shall cover the earth, and darkness the peoples, but upon thee the Lord shall arise, and his glory shall be seen upon thee v. 2. At that hour God will make the light of the Messiah and of Israel with splendor, and the nations shall walk to thy light, and Kings to the splendor of thy rising.

But that Grotius explains these things as having been done for the sake of congratulation upon the coming of the nations into Jerusalem, when it was being rebuilt, is a most unworthy digression. THE NATIONS, says the Prophet, SHALL WALK IN THY SEED, AND KINGS IN THE SPLENDOR OF THY RISING. Truly, if there is any illustrious prophecy concerning the calling of the nations to the Church, this very one is the most illustrious by the suffrage of all Christian interpreters. That it is corrupted by inept and twisted glosses, no pious person will admit without just detestation. As if the Holy Spirit were concerned about who might be coming to congratulate the city on its rebuilding, and this were THE NATIONS WALKING IN THE LIGHT OF JERUSALEM, AND KINGS IN THE SPLENDOR OF ITS RISING. That it implies participation and enjoyment of that light and splendor is manifest, and not indeed a bare congratulation, nor the participation of some external happiness only, but the enjoyment of spiritual light and splendor, for which the nations throughout the world, and even Kings and supreme heads, will congratulate not the Jerusalemites, but themselves.
