So great is the splendor of thy light, says the Prophet, that even external nations have acknowledged Christ, not only private individuals, but also Princes and Kings of the nations; examples are Cornelius the Centurion, the Ethiopian Eunuch, Sergius Paulus, Publius the Melite, Constantine, Theodosius, and others: Vatablus translates: THE NATIONS SHALL COME TO THY LIGHT. For to the Church arisen in Judea and Jerusalem (as if to a lighthouse flashing with an illustrious torch), the nations tossed and shipwrecked in the sea of errors, vices, and miseries hastened, so that following its light they might reach the harbor of salvation. Wolfgang Musculus acknowledged this here, although in the previous verses he is not averse to the Jewish gloss of Grotius: AND THE NATIONS SHALL GO TO THY LIGHT: he predicts altogether in this verse that it will come to pass that nations and Kings will embrace the religion of the people of God with great zeal, wherefore these things seem to be referred especially to the kingdom of Christ; afterwards, however, he relapses into Jewish trifles. The interpretation of Calvin holds itself more correctly: We have said that by the name of splendor the prosperous state of the Church is designated: but let us not estimate this state by external appearance: for the Prophet ascends higher: nor is there any doubt to me that he is discoursing about spiritual light and splendor. Otherwise that locution would not be appropriate, which he is about to use afterwards, The Nations shall walk to thy splendor: and the context of this chapter with the previous one easily shows it. For he says that this covenant is contained by word and Spirit. Finally, from the antithesis it is easily gathered that a different happiness of the Church is promised than in food and drink, or leisure and peace, and other comforts. Certainly there never followed a time thereafter in which a darkness of evils overwhelmed all nations, while the Jews were tranquil and joyful. Since therefore the condition of the Church is separated from the whole world, the benefit into whose possession Isaiah sends the Church is spiritual: and it is a spiritual splendor which he promises. Therefore, these things pertain to the spiritual kingdom of Christ: by which the light of the Gospel has shone through all parts of the world, and by which foreign nations have been enlightened. Thus also the Rabbis of the better sort understood. R. Saadia Gaon in the book Haemenuth ch. 19 interprets it concerning spiritual light: Then the light of the divine majesty will appear, rising over the temple, obscuring the luminaries etc. so that he who does not know the way of the temple may follow the way of that light: for it is extended from heaven to earth. What is said: And the nations shall walk in thy light; similarly these things are explained concerning spiritual light in Bereschith Rabba Paraschah 2, on Gen. 1. R. Chija said: From the beginning of the creation of the world, God the Holy and Blessed saw the house of the Sanctuary, built and destroyed, and built, as it is said Gen. 1. In the beginning God created heaven etc. Behold built as it is said Isa. 51, 16. To plant the heavens and to found the earth. And, Gen. 1, 2. the earth was tohu and bohu, that is, empty and void. Behold destroyed, just as it is said, Jer. 4, 23. I saw the earth, and behold Tohu. Gen. 1, 3. and God said, let there be light, and there was light. Behold built, and consummated for the future age, just as it is written Isa. 60, 1. Arise be enlightened, because thy light has come, and the glory of God has risen upon thee. And on Gen. 15, 17. In the hour in which the Messiah shall come, of whom it is written Ps. 89. His throne as the sun before me, in that hour there shall be darkness, or obscurity for the nations. So also it is written Isa. 60. Because behold darkness shall cover the earth, and darkness the peoples; but upon thee the Lord shall arise, and his glory shall appear upon thee. Whence it is clear that these things have been explained by the Rabbis concerning the times of the Messiah. What of the fact that Grotius himself at Luke 19, 42 acknowledged that these things pertain to the Messiah and his times. See our Annotations on Luke l. c. And at Luke 24, 47 he proved the calling of the nations under the New Testament from this place.

Latin:

Vers. 3. AMBULABUNT GENTES IN LUMINE TUO, ET REGES IN SPLENDORE ORTUS TUI] Venient tibi gratulatum.

AD restitutionem Hierosolymæ totam hanc per- quam illustrem Prophetiam abripit Grotius, integrum caput ita pervertens, ut temporalem so- lum felicitatem omnia significent. Similes explica- tiones Judæorum & semi-Judæorum notavit Hiero- nymus : Judæi & nostri semi-Judæi, qui auream atque gemmatam expectant Hierusalem, hæc in mille anno- rum regno futura contendunt, quando omnes gentes servituræ sunt Israël, & cameli Madian & Epha de Saba venientes, aurum deferent & thus, & omnes o- ves Cedar congregentur, arietesque Nabajoth ve- niant, ut immolentur super altare templi, quod fuerit extructum : De insulis quoque & maxime navibus Tharsis volare filias illius, ut columbas, auri & ar- genti divitias conferentes : Et ædificari muros Hieru- salem ab alienigenis, quibus præsint reges gentium: semperque apertas fore portas civitates, ut diebus ac noctibus divitiæ Hierusalem & victimæ deferantur : Et omnia, quæ deserta sunt, cyparisso & pino & ce- dro, sectis in Libano, construenda : præcipue templum Domini, in quo sit lætitia sempiterna : ita ut suget lac nationum, & regum divitias comedat : tantamque abundantiam rerum fore, ut pro ære aurum ha- beant: pro ferro argentum: pro lignis æs: pro lapidi- bus ferrum. Principes quoq́; illius æterna pace frui- turos, & Episcopos præfuturos populis in justitia, sed & portas futuras anaglyphas. Et quod his majus est, pro Sole & Luna, ipsum Dominum æterna luce ful- gurum: & pro uno homine habituram eam mille for- tissimos viros, & pro parvulis gentes robustissimas possessuram. Hæc illi dicunt, qui terrenas desiderant voluptates, & uxorum quærunt pulchritudinem ac numerum liberorum, quorum Deus venter, & glo- ria in confusione eorum: quorum qui sequitur erro- rem, SUB NOMINE CHRISTIANO Judæorum SE SIMILEM confitetur. Id non immerito de Grotio dixeris. Qui commenta sua in hisce An- notatis pleraque Judæis debet. Christiani vero In- terpp. facile consentiunt, hæc ad tempora Novi Testam. pertinere: Quæ sententia argumentis qui- busdam confirmanda erit, antequam ad specialem ψευδερμηνείας Grotianæ discussionem accedamus. Primum autem argumentum subministrat cohæ- rentia cum promissione sub finem capitis proximi fa- cta. Quum enim adventum Redemtoris & con- versionem nonnullorum in populo Jacob prædi- xerit, ac spirituali semini ejus promiserit, imo fœ- dus eidem sanciverit, nunquam recessurum Spiri- tum & verbum Domini ab eodem, excitat nunc Hierosolymam, ut Interpp. LXX. exposuêre, (quam- vis nomen istud in Ebræo textu non habeatur) quia omnia efferuntur in fœminino genere, & v. 14. civitas Domini Sion commemoratur, ut surgat sub adventum Goël Redemtoris sui; ac vaticinatur de luce, quam non ipsi tantum; sed gentibus etiam quibusvis per orbem terrarum allaturus est. Quæ συνέχεια invicto documento est, hæc quæ promit- tuntur ad tempora adventus Christi, & vocationis gentium pertinere, & ad tempora universa Novi Testamenti, quibus fœdus illud divinum præsta- tur, usque ad consummationem seculi. Alterum argumentum petimus à sensus literalis evidenti fal- sitate. Cum enim τὸ ῥητὸν aperte absurdum, aut fal- sum est, res ipsa postulat, ut literæ non inhæreamus. At quid evidentius, quam quod Hierosolyma, aut Zion tale regnum mundanum & externum nun- quam fuerit, quale hic describitur, quodque nun- quam ei tanta felicitas hujus seculi contigerit, quanta hoc loco promittitur. Ideo necessitas re- quirit, ut hæc intelligantur de Spirituali Messiæ re- gno, quod in Zione administrandum suscepit, ac perpetuo administrat, Ps. 2,6. Ps. 110. 3. quodque prædicatione Evangelii initio Hierosolymis facto constitutum est in toto orbe terrarum. Nimirum commendat Spiritus Sanctus hoc regnum à rebus longe omnium clarissimis, & excellentissimis, qua- les in nullo unquam mundano regno aut fuerunt, aut erunt. Videlicet à Majestate Regis, ab incol- larum multitudine, à veneratione & obedientia omnium gentium, à magnificentia ædificiorum, à copia & abundantia omnium rerum, à moderatione & æqui- tate Magistratuum, à justitia subditorum, denique à vera & perpetua felicitate. Quod argumentum ad- versus Judæorum glossam Grotianam Lyranus exe- quitur: Illi reduces, inquit, nunquam fuerunt in tanta prosperitate, ut prius: imo omnia, quæ dicun- tur hic, mirabitur & dilatabitur cor tuum, quando conversa fuerit ad te multitudo maris, fortitudo gentium venerit tibi. Licet enim aliqui, gentilita- te relicta, eis adhæserunt, tamen fuerunt pauci & parvæ reputationis & virtutis. Item, quod postea subditur: Et ædificabunt filii peregrinorum mu- ros tuos; quia ipsimet ædificaverunt eos tempore Ne- hemiæ, & cum magno labore & anxietate, ita quod una manu faciebant opus & altera tenebant gladium.

Nehem. 4. & hoc timore adversariorum, eos impe- dire volentium. Et quod hic subditur: aperientur portæ tuæ jugiter, &c. quia magis tenebantur clausæ adversariorum timore. It. quod postea subditur: Gens enim & regnum, quod non ser- vierit tibi, peribit: quia illa regna non servierunt eis, sed magis è converso: primo Persis tributum reddendo; postea Græcis, & postea Romanis, ut patet ex libris Esdræ & Nehemiæ & Maccabæorum, & Evangeliorum, & ex libris Josephi & aliorum historiographorum. Tertium argumentum suppeditat interpreta- tio Spiritus Sancti, qui neglecto ῥητῷ spiritualiter explicat. Illa autem sine dubio genuina est senten- tia, quæ ab ipso Spiritu Sancto tradita est, 2. Petr. 1, 21. Locus est Apoc. 21. ubi descriptio Hierosoly- mæ cœlestis bonam partem ex hoc vaticinio de- promta est, civitas non eget sole, neque Luna, ut lu- ceant in eâ. Et deinde: portæ ejus non claudentur per diem: Ac rursus: Nox ultra non erit, & non e- gent lumine lucernæ, neque Lumine Solis, quoniam Dominus Deus illuminat illos. Quum ergo his verbis ac sententiis Spiritus Sanctus gloriam & felicitatem cœlestium Hierosolymorum describat, de terrenæ Hierosolymæ gloria & felicitate hæc minime intelli- genda erunt, sed de cœlesti, quæ Regno Christi spi- rituali & Ecclesiæ reservatur in altera vita, cujus initium quoddam spiritualiter habet in hoc seculo, sed complementum expectant cœleste in altero. Quartum è materia & argumento sequentis concio- nis, quæ hic immediate connexa est, petimus, ut- pote quæ ipso Christo interprete ad tempora Novi Testamenti & officium Christi propheticum pertinet. Ita enim Salvator noster Luc. 4. in Synagoga Na- zarethana professus est publice; Hodie impleta est hæc scriptura in auribus vestris. Quinto confessio ipsorummet Judæorum confundere potest Gro- tium. Sic enim in Bereschith Rabba legitur super illud Gen. 15,17. fuit sol occidens. In hora, qua ve- niet Messias, de quo scriptum est Psal. 89. Thronus ejus sicut sol coram me, in illa hora erit caligo, vel obscuritas gentibus. Sic quippe scriptum est Es. 60. Quia ecce tenebræ operient terram, & caligo po- pulos, super te autem orietur Dominus, & gloria ejus super te apparebit. Similiter in expositione magna Gen. ad c. 25, 6. Hoc est, quod scriptum est Job. 6,19. Respicite semitas Tema, itinera Saba ex- pectate eos: Non est Saba nisi filii Abrahæ, sicut di- ctum est Gen. 25, 3. Et Jaksan genuit Saba & Dedan: cumque magnificatus est Salomob in regno suo, dixe- runt; Forsan ipse est Messias, statimq́; venerunt ad eum, sicut dictum est 1. Reg. 10, 1. Et Regina Saba audita fama Salomonis, ad nomen Domini venit, ad tentandum eum in ænigmatibus. Non legas Re- gina Saba; Sed regnum Saba. Et quid est dictum in Nomine Domini? Prophetæ fuerunt iis,qui propheta- bant in nomine Domini Dei sui verba, quæ fuerant eis tradita, & quæ venerunt successive ad manum eo- rum ex Abraham. Et unde habetur, quod venturi fo- rent ad dies Messiæ, & servituri ei? sicut dictum est Es. 60, 6. Multitudo Camelorum operient te; dromedarii Median & Epha, omnes ipsi de Saba venient, aurum & thus deferent: & laudes Do- mini Dei nunciabunt; Hic est Rex Messias, sicut dictum est Jer. 23, 6. Et hoc est nomen, quo vo- cabunt eum, Dominus justus noster. Et sic dicit E- saias c. 60, 2. Super te orietur Deus & gloria ejus super te apparebit, & ibunt gentes ad lumen tuum: & reges ad splendorem ortûs tui. Quæ sententia etiam in Targum expressa est, quod nempe hæc prophetia intelligenda sit de Christo: cum ita red- didit: Surge illuminare Jerusalem, quia appropin- quat tempus salvationis tuæ,& honor Dei super te re- velabit se; quia ecce tenebræ operient terram, & ca- ligo regna, & in te descendet Divinitas Domini, & honor ejus super te revelabitur, & ibunt gentes ad lu- men tuum, & reges ad suscipiendum splendorem tuum. Ecce ita agnoverunt Messiam in hac Pro- phetia Judæi, quem non agnovit aut vidit Grotius Christianus. Sed hæc in genere. Specialis ἐξήγησις argumenta suggerit specia- lia luculentissima, quibus & κατασκευαστικῶς Chri- stianorum communis interpretatio, quod de re- gno Christi spirituali sermo sit, non de felicitate temporalis Hierosolymæ, adstruatur, & ἀνασκευ- υαστικῶς Judaica Grotii commenta destruantur, Primam ergo specialem rationem è Regis hu- jus Majestate depromimus,ob quam excitatur Hie- rosolyma, ut SURGAT è squalore & luctu, ut e- mergat è tenebris, quia prostrata jacebat, & deje- cta, in calamitate, ac mœrore constituta: UT IL- LUMINETUR, h. e. illustris fiat, & beata. VE- NIT ENIM LUX TUA, ET GLORIA DO- MINI IN TE ORTA EST. Quæ ergo illa lux Hierosolymæ, quæ gloria Domini, nisi Christus ipsi promissus, à fidelibus expectatus,qui LUX illa magna est, omnes homines illuminans, Joh. 1, 9. LUX mundi, Joh. 8. c. 12. & gloria populi Israël, lux Gen- tium Es. 22, 6. cap. 49, 6. & Luc. 2. Sic idem me- taphorica hac locutione innuitur, quod Zach. 9,9. Exulta valde filia Sion, jubila filia Jerusalem, quia Ecce Rex tuus veniet tibi, justus & Salvator. Mo- untacutius in Origin. Eccles. de vita Christi lib. 1. p. 48. hanc ῥῆσιν de luce Angelica interpretatur,qua scil. angelus nocte Christi natali circumfusus fuit Luc. 2. Sed sensum illum secundarium dicit. Quo- modo autem hic de luce angelica in agro Bethle- hem sensus locum haberet, ubi de luce Hierosoly- mæ orta gentes illuminatura res est. Grotius jeju- ne nimis per lucem intelligit prosperitatem. Re- ctius ipsimet Judæi præeunte Targum, MESSIAM intelligunt. Et hortatur quidem Propheta, illu- minare, ut fugatis tenebris Hierosolymæ lux fiat. Quod perperam Grotius exponit per expergiscere. Causa autem cur illuminari debeat, est adventus lu- cis & gloriæ Hierosolymæ, quam oportet diversam esse ab eo,quod exigit & requiritPropheta abHie- rosolyma. Quæ autem causa surgendi & illumina- tionis, nisi adventus ejus, qui est lux & gloria po- puli? Percussi enim erant auditores Esaiæ metu fu- turæ captivitatis Babylonicæ,tum quod de externa incolumitate urbis Hierusalem angerentur, tum vero imprimis, quod magis de vera & æterna Ec- clesiæ salute ac Messiæ adventu solliciti fuerunt; ideoq; solatur eos Propheta, & docet urbem Hie- rusalem post devastationem ejus non solum instau- randam, sed etiam præsentia, concionibus, & mi- raculis Filii Dei ita illustrandam,ut ex ea salus ad o- mnes gentes divulgetur: Deinde cum non sit in alio quoquam remissio peccatorum, justitia & salus, præterquam in Jesu Christo, Esaias opportune, imo necessario concionatur auditoribus suis, de adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi, & de regno ejus, ut, si qui territi sunt judicio peccati,& sitiunt justitiam & salutem, excitentur ad fidem in Chri- stum, & accipiant per eum remissionem peccato- rum, & reputentur coram Deo justi & serventur, ut habet Brentius noster p. 766. Ideo desiderarunt maximopere fideles Messiam ceu lucem & gloriam suam, ut exemplo Simeonis & aliorum: Luc. 2,25. 32. 38. constat. De quo etiam Rabbini in Bere- schith Rabba ad Gen. 41, 44. professi sunt, quod sit ille, quem Esaias in loco parallelo cap. 49, 6. dixit lucem gentium: Poteritne dici, quod Redem- tor sit acceptor personarum? Absit: sed omnes con- fitentes ei ore suo, & operibus suis, & corde suo, sal- vabit & liberabit, sicut dictum est Jer. 23, 6. In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, quasi dicat, Omnes confitentes ei; & sic dicit Es. 45,22. Convertimini ad me, & sal- vabimini omnes fines terræ. Et iterum dicit Esaia 45, 23. Quia mihi flectetur omne genus, & jura- bit omnis lingua. Et de ipso dicit Scriptura, Es.49,6. Et dedi te in lucem gentium,ut sis salus mea usque ad fines terræ. Et habetur de hoc ipso vaticinio locus perquam illustris in libro Jalkut, è libro antiquo Pesikta ad hæc verba, surge lux mea,quia venit lu- mentuum, Es. 60, 1. ubi dicitur lux hæc, esse lux Messlæ. Verba sunt: dixit Synagoga Israëlis coram Deo benedicto; Domine mundi,propter Legem,quam dedistimihi, quæ vocatur Fons vel scaturigo vitæ, ob- lectatura me sum in luce tua; Quid est, In luce tua videbimus lucem? Hæc est lux Messiæ, sicut dicitur, Et vidit Deus lucem, quod bona esset; docet enim hoc,quod præviderit Deus seculum Messiæ & opera e- jus, antequam crearetur mundus, ac proinde abscon- derit eam pro Messia & ejus generatione, sub Solio gloriæ suæ. Dixit Satan coram Deo Benedicto; Do- mine mundi, lux illa, quæ abscondita est sub solio glo- riæ tuæ, cujus est? Respondit ei Deus, ejus, qui te pu- defacturus est, & pudore atq; ignominia affecturus. Regessit Satan; Domine mundi ostende illum mihi. Dixit ei Deus: Veni & vide eum; posteaquam vidit eum, contremuit, & cecidit in faciem suam, dicens, certe hic est MESSIAS, qui me & omnes populos detrusurus est in gehennam, sicut dicitur; absorpsit mortem in æternum, & absterget Dominus Deus lachrymam ab omni facie (Es. 25, 8.) Ea hora com- moti populi,dixerunt; Domine mundi, Quis est ille,in cujus manum nos incidemus: quod est nomen ejus? & quæ est conditio ejus? Respondit Deus B. Nomen ejus est Ephrajim Messias justitiæ meæ, hic exaltabit staturam suam & staturam generationis suæ, illumi- nabitq; oculos Israëlis, & servabit populum suum, neq; ulla gens aut lingua poterit insurgere in ipsum, sicut dicitur; Non faciet exactionem inimicus ab ipso, neque inimicus affliget eum Ps.89,23. Omnes ejus inimici & hostes conturbabuntur & fugient a conspectu ejus, sicut dicitur: Et conteram à facie e- jus hostes ipsius. Vid. v. 24. Quin & flumina ces- sabunt in mare (influere) sicut dicitur; Et ponam in mari manum ejus,& in fluminibus dexteram ejus, ibid. v. 26. His dictæ cepit Deus patisci cum eo (Mes- sia scil.) posteaquam fugissent inimici ejus, dicens ad eum: Istorum, qui absconditi sunt apud te, iniquita- tes, intrudent te in jugum ferreum, & facient te sicut vitulum, cujus oculi caligant, constringentque vel strangulabunt Spiritum tuum in jugo: propter ini- quitates ipsorum lingua tua adhærebit palato tuo. Num ita est voluntas tua? (Num voluntarie hoc vis in te suscipere?) Dixit Messias ad Deum; Domine mundi; Fortasse isti dolores per annos multos dura- bunt? Respondit Deus, Per vitam tuam & per vi- tam capitis tui,septimanam unam decrevi super te, si hoc tibi sit molestum,è vestigio expellam eos. Ille,(Mes- sias;) Domine mundi,cum exultatione cordis mei, & cum lætitia cordis mei recipio istud in me, modo ne vel unus pereat ex Israële; & non tantum illi serventur, qui vivent in diebus meis, sed etiam omnes, qui mor- tui sunt inde ab Adamo primo hucusque; neq; etiam tantum isti, sed & omnes abortivi & embryones; de- niq; omnes,quos constituisti creare, & non creati sunt. Sub hac conditione ego volo, & in me hos dolores re- cipiam. Dixerunt; Septimana illa, qua Filius Da- vidis (Messias) veniet, sument trabes ferreas, & im- ponent eos collo ipsius, adeo ut incurvetur statura ejus, exclamet,fleat,& vox ejus adscendat in cælum,dicens ad

Deum; quanta erit fortitudo mea! quantus erit spiri- tus meus! quandiu durabit anima mea! quandiu du- rabunt membra mea! Non sum caro & sanguis. Illam horam deflevit David, dicens; Exaruit tanquam te- sta virtus mea, Pf. 22, 16. Tunc dixit ei Deus; Ephra- jim Messia justitia mea, jam suscepisti in te hoc a sex diebus creationis &c. Et postea: RABBINI NO- STRI tradiderunt, ea hora, qua Messias veniet, & stabit super tecto domus sanctuarii, proclamabit, & dicet ad Israëlitas; Humiliati & afflicti, appropin- quavit tempus redemtionis vestræ, si id non credatis, en lucem meam, quæ oritur super vos, sicut dicitur; Surge lux mea, quia venit lumen tuum, & glo- ria Domini super te orta est. E quibus constat, fuis- se hanc TRADITIONEM communem Rabbino- rum, quod Propheta de Messia & de adventu ejus hic loquatur, neque innotum antiquis Rabbinis mysterium fuisse de redemtione Messiæ, etsi id pro more suo commentis cabalisticis involverint, non vero nudis & apertis verbis proposuerint.

Secunda ratio à subditorum multitudine peti- ta est. Quam illustrat Propheta ἀντιθέσει status pri- mi: ECCE TENEBRÆ OPERIENT TER- RAM, ET CALIGO POPULOS: IN TE AUTEM ORIETUR DOMINUS, ET GLO- RIA EJUS IN TE VIDEBITUR. Tempore adventus Christi terram operiebant tenebræ erro- ris & infidelitatis, & caligo populos, in qua omnes gentes adhuc versabantur. Sed super Jerusalem lux magna oriebatur, quia oriens ex alto visitabat eos Luc. 1. Dominus ipse ortus est tanquam lux vera Joh. 1. Et gloria ejus visa est in eadem: quia vide- runt gloriam unigeniti à Patre, Joh. 1. Chaldæus transtulit, sed in Te commorabitur שכינתא divinitas Domini, unde Johannes adhibuit de hoc negotio vocem ἐσκήνωσεν Joh. 1, 14. Verbum caro factum est, & habitavit in nobis, & vidimus gloriam ejus, glo- riam quasi unigeniti à Patre, ac si exprimere, & in- dice digito demonstrare hoc oraculum voluisset. Si dicat quis, Hierusalem terrenam hic indigitari, utpote quæ comparetur cum populis aliis, caligine obrutis, quia in ea oriri dicitur Dominus; ideoque cætera omnia de terrena Hierusalem accipienda esse: Resp. Non negarim his verbis terrenam istam metropolin Judææ compellari, sed non qua terrena est: nec ratione externa & politica suæ conditionis; verum ratione internæ & Mysticæ dignitatis, qua erat sedes Ecclesiæ, ac respectu fidelium, qui in ea expectabant solatium Israëlis. Horum enim lux, horum gloria, horum gaudium erat Messias. Id- eoque pertinebant ad hanc Hierosolymam non solum qui in ea erant fideles, sed etiam qui extra eam constituti per fidem ipsi conjuncti erant, non solum Israëlitæ, sed etiam alii fide Messiam com- plectentes, denominatione tamen facta ab ista ur- be, unde ad alios divulgari debebat Evangelium. Quapropter non mirum, si hic, & in similibus va- ticiniis quædam proprie ad ipsam Hierosolymam pertineant, alia vero concernent fideles commu- niter in & extra Hierosolymam Ecclesiarum ma- trem, cum filiabus, uti hodie loquuntur: quia o- mnes fideles ad Hierusalem certa ratione pertine- bant, ceu sedem Ecclesiæ, ubi Deus ignem & fo- cum habebat. Quia vero amplianda erant pomœria Hierosolymæ per gentium vocationem, ideo sub complexu hujus vocis etiam gentes fide ipsi cohæ- rentes comprehenduntur. Neque tamen necessum est, duplicem vel triplicem vocis ejusdem sensum in eodem loco statuere, sed respectu solum diverso conveniunt prædicata Hierosolymæ, puta vel re- spectu externæ sedis aut externi templi, vel respe- ctu verorum & spiritualium membrorum in ea, si- ve etiam in statu ampliationis, ut ita dicam, respectu fidelium quorumvis, sive in ea, sive extra eam. De eodem Scripturæ loco loquor. Nam alias in diversis locis diversas fignificationes hanc vocem obtine- re, ac modo urbem externam seu metropolin Ju- dææ, modo spiritualem & mysticam Hierosolymam compellari, non negamus. Ita hoc in loco compel- latur ipsa civitas Judææ, sed qua metropolis regni Christi, non qua metropolis regni Judaici. Nam civitatem ipsam designari ex eo apparet, quod illa e squalore variarum afflictionum surgere jubeatur, quodque IN ea oriri primum Dominus, & gloria ejus revelari debuerit, cum alios populos adhuc caligo circumvolveret, quodq; urbis hujus splen- dore & dignitate, quæ ipsi sub tempus N. Testam. promittitur, obscurentur clarissimæ quæque ur- bes & metropoles. In hac enim urbe conciona- tus est Christus Evangelium suum: in hac urbe edi- dit multa & magna miracula, in hac urbe peregit sacrificium suum in expiatione peccatorum totius mundi. In hac urbe resurrexit à mortuis. Non longe ab hac urbe ascendit in cœlum, in hac urbe misit Spiritum Sanctum Discipulis suis. Deniq; ex hac urbe divulgavit Evangelium per Apostolos in omnes gentes, ut quotquot Evangelio ex hac urbe divulgato credunt, consequantur æternam justi- tiam & salutem. Non autem intra urbis hujus po- mœria lux illa concluditur, ut eadem sola ejus in- colæ fruantur, & illustrentur. Soli quidem cives mystici hujus urbis fruuntur ea, non soli autem Ju- dæi sunt cives, sed etiam gentes fiunt cives ejusdem, cum Messiam per fidem agnoscunt, ejusq; luce illu- strantur. Ecclesia enim Domini initio quidem col- ligi cœpit ex Judæis, sed mox vulgato Evangelio in- ter gentes sic aucta & multiplicata est gentibus, ut nullo amplius numero comprehendi potuerit. Ex- plicatio hæc Cyrilli est: Observa præ aliis, data Is- raëlitis à Deo divina luce, per Christum videlicet, Pro- phetam dicere; Venit tua lux, tantum non præsentem esse ostendens eum, qui olim in lege & à sanctis prophe- tis prænunciatus est, quique in carne postremis seculi temporibus illuxit mortalibus, Vocatq; eum, qui ap- paruit, gloriam Domini. Ortus enim est Christus tanquam Sol quidam, luce divina ac intelligentia col- lustrans omnia & veræ Dei cognitionis splendorem: promptioribus ad fidem amplectendam immittens. Estque gloria Dei & Patris. In ipso & per ipsum & cum ipso glorificatur. Et postea: Verum est enim Christo præ aliis illucente Israëlitis, detentam fuisse tenebris gentium multitudinem, nondum translata in ipsas gratia. Ecce igitur, inquit, obtecta est tenebris & caligine, ignorationis scilicet & erroris, universa terra gentium. Super te autem apparebit Dominus: Illuxit enim, ut dixi, illis & quidem primum, & glo- ria ejus visa est, eximia magnitudine operum, signo- rum, & prodigii. Apud eos namq; miracula edidit, ut Deus, partim mortuos à monumentis suscitans, partim cæcorum oculis lumen immittens, leprosos emundans nutu, dæmones increpans cum autoritate, & nullum omnino modum prætermittens ad fidem fa- ciendam, persuadendumque se vere Deum esse & Dei naturalem filium. Et ambulabunt, inquit, Re- ges in luce tua, & gentes in splendore tuo. Adnectit iterum Propheta visitationi Israëlitarum, gentium vocationem: ut videant, si contemnant ipsi sua inobe- dientia Redemptorem, & resiliant ab ejus dilectione, cum capitis sui interitu, se non fore destitutum culto- ribus, sed Gentes potius & reges per fidem adductu- rum. Postmodum tamen τὴν νοητὴν ἱερυσαλὴμ. Pro- phetam alloqui dicit: Horum omnium prædictio- nem facit, & intelligibilem Hierusalem, id est, Ec- clesiam ab initio ex Judæis constitutam alloquitur:

Primi enim illi crediderunt: Leva in circuitu ocu- los tuos, & vide congregatos liberos tuos: Ecce enim veniunt omnes filii tui è longinquo, & filiæ tuæ in humeris tollentur. Affatur enim his verbis eos, qui ex omni gente & regione collecti credide- runt, Ecclesiam, inquam, divina & Evangelica præ- dicatione orbem terrarum irretiente, & tanquam ad civitatem quandam munitissimam, ad fidei gratiam, ad sanctorum cibum invitante: quemadmodum vide- licet & alibi: Erit enim, inquit, in postremis die- bus spectabilis mons Domini, propositus in ver- ticibus montium, & elevabitur supra colles, ve- nientq; ad illum gentes multæ, ac dicent: Adeste, ascendamus ad montem Domini, & ad domum Dei Jacob. Et annunciabit nobis viam ejus: Et ambulabimus in ea. Liberi autem Hierusalem, non hi soli dicendi sunt, qui ex sanguine Israël oriundi sunt, sed quotquot ex omni gente ac regione vocati sunt per fidem ad veritatis lucem: ut enim sapientis- simus Paulus scribit: Non omnes, qui ex Israël, hi Israël: nec quia semen Abraham sunt, omnes li- beri: sed liberi promissionis reputantur in semen. Dictum enim est à Deo ad divinum Abraham: Pa- trem multarum gentium constitui te. Itaque velut multitudine jam congregata ex Gentibus & adorante Christum: Tolle, inquit, circumcirca oculos tuos, id est, universum orbem perlustra, & ex omni par- te ejus videbis liberos tuos ad te accurrentes, ve- nientque, etsi procul abfuerint aliquando. Procul non ratione loci dicitur, sed ad animum mentisq; affe- ctionem pertinet. Hæc Cyrillus. Nec incommo- de Hieronymus docet, quod de spirituali Hieroso- lyma hæc dicantur: Nos autem juxta priorem sen- sum, ad Ecclesiam dici universa credamus, quæ pri- mum de Judaico populo congregata est, & lumen, quod super eam ortum fuerat, per Apostolum trans- misit ad gentes. Cui dicitur: Surge illuminare: ut quæ cecidit in incredulis, surgat in fidelibus: quæ cecidit in Synagogis, surgat in Ecclesiis: & postquam surrexe- rit, illuminetur: ut nequaquam habeant erroris te- nebras. Venit enim, inquit, lumen tuum: quod omnes Prophetæ pollicebantur: quod jugiter expecta- bas. Et gloria Domini, quæ quondam fuit super ta- bernaculum & templum ejus, orta est super te. De qua dictum est: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te civitas Dei. Ecce enim tenebræ operient terram, eos, qui terrena sapiunt: Et caligo populos: sive ut in He- braico legitur, tribus: quod proprie refertur ad Ju- dæos: de quibus in alio Psalmo scriptum est: Illuc e- nim ascenderunt tribus, tribus Domini testimoni- um Israël. Super te autem orietur DominusSol ju- stitiæ, & gloria ejus in te videbitur. De qua scriptum est: Et vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi unige- niti à patre, plenum gratiæ & veritatis. Et ambula- bunt gentes in lumine tuo. Nos omnes ambulabimus in Apostolorum luce, quæ lucet in mundo, & tenebræ eam non comprehenderunt. Et reges, inquit, in splen- dore ortus tui: quando primum in Christo nata es. Quod & spiritualiter impletur, & carnaliter: Ut reges, quorum cor in manu Domini est, & quibus non regnat peccatum in mortali corpore, ambulent in splendore nascentis Ecclesiæ, sive in eo, qui ortus est in Ecclesia: & veri reges Christi fidei collo submit- tant. Quod quotidie videmus expleri, quando Idolo- latriæ errore sublato & persequutionis rabie ad fidem & tranquillitatem Romani principes transeunt. Ad- dit observationem, quod Hierusalem & gentium no- men, CALIGO SUPER GENTES, quod hic à LXX. poni- tur, in Ebraico non habeantur: & obelo prænotan- dum sit, adversum eos, qui asserunt omnia, quæ di- cuntur, dici ad Hierusalem. Inepta est Grotii glossa, quod per populos Medi & Babylonii intelligantur.

Caligo operiet populos, primum Medos, deinde Baby- lonios. Quænam obsecro glossæ istius in textu vesti- gia? Et quum generaliter terram operire dicantur tenebræ, & caligo populos, qui potestatem Grotio dedit restringendi ea, quæ generaliter dicta sunt, ad certos populos? Neque vero de calamitate corpo- rali sermo est, sed de tenebris spiritualibus, quod & lux illa, quæ Hierosolymæ promittitur, & lumen, in quo gentes ambulaturæ sunt, & quæ adduntur por- ro docent. Ac Judæi ipsimet saniores agnoscunt, unde in prædicto libro Jalkut hæc ex traditione Rabbinorum adferuntur, illis quæ proxime addu- cta sunt immediate cohærentia: Super eos solos orta est gloria Domini. Quia ecce tenebræ ope- rient terram, & caligo populos, super te autem o- rietur Dominus, & gloria ejus super te videbitur v. 2. Ea hora splendore faciet Deus lucem Messiæ, & Israëlis, & ambulabunt gentes ad lumen tuum, & Reges ad splendorem ortus tui.

Quod vero Grotius hæc de adventu gentium in Jerusalem congratulationis ergo facto, cum reædi- ficaretur, explicat, παρεκβλότης est indignissima. AM- BULABUNT, inquit Propheta, GENTES IN SEMINE TUO, ET REGES IN SPLEN- DORE ORTUS TUI. Sane si quæ est illustris de gentium vocatione ad Ecclesiam prophetia, hæc ipsa omnium Christianorum interpretum suffra- gio illustrissima est. Quam ineptis & contortis glossis corrumpi nemo pius sine justa detestatio- ne admittet. Quasi Spir. Sanctus de eo solicitus sit, quinam adventuri sint, gratulatum urbi de reædifi- catione, & hoc sit AMBULATURAS GEN- TES IN LUMINE HIEROSOLYMÆ, ET REGES IN SPLENDORE ORTUS IPSIUS. Quæ participationem & fruitionem lucis & splen- doris istius inferre manifestum est, non vero nu- dam congratulationem, neque felicitatis tantum alicu- jus externæ participationem, sed spiritualis lucis & splendoris fruitionem, de qua non Hierosolymita- nis, sed sibi ipsis gratulabuntur gentes per Orbem, & Reges etiam, ac summa capita. Tantus est splen- dor lucis tuæ, inquit Propheta, ut etiam externæ gentes agnoverint Christum, non solum privati, sed etiam Principes & Reges gentium; Exemplo sunt Cornelius Centurio, Eunuchus Æthiops, Sergius Paulus, Publius Melitensis, Constantinus, Theodosius & alii: Vatablus vertit: VENIENT GENTES AD LUCEM TUAM. Ad Ecclesiam enim in Judæa & Jerusalem ortam (quasi ad Pharum illu- stri face coruscam) gentes in mari errorum, vitio- rum & ærumnarum jactatæ & naufragæ contende- runt, ut ejus lumen sequentes pertingerent ad portum salutis. Agnovit id hic Wolfgang. Muscu- lus, etsi in prioribus versibus à Grotii glossa Judai- ca alienus non sit: ET IBUNT GENTES AD LUCEM TUAM: omnino prædicit hoc versu futurum, ut gen- tes ac Reges religionem populi Dei magno studio am- plectantur, quare referenda videntur ista potissimum ad regnum Christi; postea tamen ad nænias judai- cas relabitur. Rectius sese habet interpretatio Cal- vini: Diximus splendoris nomine prosperum Ecclesiæ statum designari: sed ne hunc statum ab externa specie æstimemus: altius enim conscendit Propheta: nec mihi dubium, quin de spirituali luce & splendore con- cionetur. Alioqui non conveniret ea locutio, qua postea usurus est, Ambulabunt Gentes ad splendo- rem tuum: & contextus hujus capitis cum superiore id facile ostendit. Dicit enim fœdus hoc contineri verbo & Spiritu. Deniq; ex antitbeto facile colligi- tur, aliam Ecclesiæ felicitatem, quam in cibo & potu, vel otio & pace, & aliis commodis promitti. Certe nunquam deinde sequutum est tempus, quo malorum caligo Gentes omnes obrueret, tranquilli& lætisq́, Ju- dæis. Cum ergo separetur Ecclesiæ conditio à toto or- be, beneficium, in cujus possessionem Isaias Ecclesiam mittit, spirituale est: & spiritualis splendor, quem promittit. Itaq́, ad spirituale Christi regnum hæc per- tinent: quo lumen Evangelii per omnes orbis partes refulsit, eoque extraneæ gentes illustratæ sunt. Sic et- iam intellexêre Rabbini melioris commatis. R. Saa- dia Gaon in libro Haemenuth cap. 19. de spirituali lumine interpretatur: Tunc apparebit lux majesta- tis divinæ, oriens super templum, obscurans lumina- ria &c. ita ut qui viam nescit templi, viam illius lu- cis sequatur: quippe à cælo in terram porrigitur. Quod dicitur: Et ambulabunt gentes in lumine tuo; Similiter de luce spirituali exponuntur hæc in Bereschith Rabba Paraschah. 2. in Genes. 1. Di- xit R. Chija: A principio creationis mundi vidit Deus Sanctus, & benedictus domum Sanctuarii, ædificatam & destructam, & ædificatam, sicut di- ctum est Genes. 1. In principio creavit Deus cœ- lum &c. Ecce ædificata sicut dictum est Isa. 51, 16. Ad plantandum cœlos & fundandam terram. Et, Genes. 1, 2. terra erat tohu & bohu, id est, inanis & vacua. Ecce destructa, quemadmodum dictum est, Jer. 4, 23. Vidi terram, & ecce Tohu. Genes. 1, 3. & dixit Deus, fiat lux, & fuit lux. Ecce ædificata, & consummata in seculum futurum, prout scriptum est Es. 60, 1. Surge illuminare, quia venit lumen tuum, & gloria Dei super te orta est. Et super Ge- nes. 15, 17. In hora, qua veniet Messias, de quo scriptum est Psal. 89. Thronus ejus sicut sol co- ram me, in illa hora erit caligo, vel obscuritas gen- tibus. Sic quoq́, scriptum est Esa. 60. Quia ecce te- nebræ operient terram, & caligo populos; super te autem orietur Dominus, & glòria ejus super te apparebit. Unde patet de temporibus Messiæ à Rabbinis hæc exposita esse. Quid quod Grotius ipse ad Luc. 19, 42. agnoverit hæc ad Messiam, ejus- que tempora pertinere. Vid. Annot. nostra ad Lucam l. c. Et ad Luc. 24, 47. ex hoc loco vocatio- nem gentium sub Novo Testamento probârit.

## 60:4
Verse same. ALL THESE GATHERED] From long exile.

Verse 4. FROM THE SIDE THEY SHALL RISE] The interpreter wrote, they shall suck. Jerome has 'they shall suck milk' in his Commentaries. It seems therefore that for צד he read שד. But the Chaldean and the Greeks seem to have read העמסה for תאמנה.

Latin:

Vers. eod. OMNES ISTI CONGREGATI] Ex longo ex- silio.

Vers. 4. DE LATERE SURGENT] Scripsit interpres, sugent. Lac sugent, habet in Commentariis Hieronymus. Videtur ergo pro צד legisse שד. At Chaldæus & Græci pro תאמנה videntur legisse העמסה.

## 60:5
Verse 5. WHEN THE MULTITUDE OF THE SEA SHALL BE TURNED TO THEE] The riches of the sea shall come to thee. The Tyrians shall bring merchandise to thee. Neh. 13, 16. nay, and thou shalt take spoils from the Tyrians. See Josephus 12, 11. and 12.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUANDO CONVERSA FUERIT AD TE MULTITUDO MARIS] Venient ad te divitiæ maris. Ty- rii ad te res promercales adferent. Nehem. 13, 16. imo & de Tyriis spolia capies. Vide Josephum 12, 11. & 12.

## 60:6
VERS. 6. THE INUNDATION OF CAMELS SHALL COVER THEE] A plenty of camels shall cover the land. You will learn from the statement of Josephus in the place and 1 Macc. 5, 25, that both the Nabataeans, who will be named here very soon, and other Arabs, were allies and friends of the Jewish people.

AND EPHA] See Gen. 25, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 6. INUNDATIO CAMELORUM OPERIET TE] Copia Camelorum terram operiet. Disces ex dicto Josephi loco & 1. Macc. 5, 25. tum Nabatæos, qui jam mox hic nominabuntur, tum Arabas alios, socios & a- micos fuisse populi Judaici.

ET EPHA] Vide Gen. 25, 4.

## 60:7
VERS. 7. AND I WILL GLORIFY THE HOUSE OF MY MAJESTY] Namely, through those beasts which shall arrive to you from distant places.

These things are perversely applied to the Jews. For they were spoken concerning the nations and peoples gathered to Jerusalem. For since Isaiah had predicted that the nations would walk in the Light of Jerusalem, he now as it were points with his finger to the multitude of those arriving. Therefore, here is the third argument from the frequency and variety of the people being gathered. LIFT UP THINE EYES ROUND ABOUT, AND SEE ALL THESE ARE GATHERED TOGETHER, THEY COME TO THEE. Lift up and cast your eyes around in all directions, and the circuit of your region, to all the quarters of the world. Behold all this multitude of people, which you see to be numberless, they are assembling, that they may set out to you, and become your inhabitants and citizens. THY SONS FROM FAR, AND THY DAUGHTERS FROM

THEY SHALL RISE FROM THE SIDE. Therefore, whether you look to the length or the breadth of the earth, they shall flow to you from every side, and your sons and your daughters shall be present with you from afar and from the side, so that they may indeed turn out to be your citizens; they run together not only from nearby regions, but also from distant ones, which are both before you and at your side, from all the regions round about, even those situated far away. In the Hebrew it is: And your daughters SHALL BE NURSED AT THE SIDE, whence, what the Vulgate rendered, they shall rise from the side; Jerome, expressing the sense, translated it thus: and your daughters shall suck milk. For kings are said to be his nursing fathers, אמנים, Isa. 49:13, which word is had in this place. In the parallel passage, Isa. 49:22, these things are read thus: And your daughters shall be carried in arms, as nurses are wont to carry infants. Whence here also the LXX Interpreters: And your daughters shall be carried upon shoulders. There is therefore no need for divination or an Oedipus, or whether it is otherwise, or what the Greeks and the Chaldean read, who do not always express word for word, but often look only to the sense: which they have illustrated here from the parallel passage. THEN YOU SHALL SEE AND FLOW TOGETHER, AND YOUR HEART SHALL WONDER AND BE ENLARGED, WHEN THE MULTITUDE OF THE SEA SHALL BE CONVERTED TO YOU, THE STRENGTH OF THE GENTILES SHALL COME TO YOU. So great shall be the multitude of those coming to you, or of your citizens, that you yourself, when you see it, shall be seized with the greatest wonder, and shall even be astonished, and your heart shall exult for exceeding joy. For the multitude of the sea shall be converted to you, i.e., of those who dwell in the islands of the sea. And the strength shall come to you, i.e., a great abundance of the Gentiles. Jerome rightly explains these things: LIFT UP ROUND ABOUT: It is said to the Church, which was first gathered through the Apostles in Sion: of whom we also read in the Acts of the Apostles, that from the whole world there were religious men in Jerusalem, who received the word of God, and in the languages of their own and other nations, either heard others speaking, or they themselves spoke to the rest. And it is commanded that they lift up their eyes round about. Which the Lord also commanded the Apostles, saying: Lift up your eyes, and see: for the fields are white for harvesting. For from Sion and by no means from Mount Sinai shall the law go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And it is commanded that, with eyes lifted up, she may see her sons gathered, who come from afar. To whom it is also said in another place: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, preach, O daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, I come and will dwell in the midst of you, says the Lord; And many Gentiles shall come to the Lord, and shall be to me for a people, and I will be to them for a God. But we are the sons who have come from afar to the Lord, once strangers from the testament of God and his promises, having no hope, and without God in the world. But what does the Apostle say? You, who were once far off, are now made near. And what follows: And your daughters shall suck milk: that signifies that souls suckling in Christ, and in the baptism of infants; of whom the Apostle Peter also speaks: As newborn babes, desire the rational and guileless milk, let them suck the milk of the Apostles. To which infants and sucklings Paul also spoke: My little children, of whom I am again in labor, until Christ be formed in you. And in another place; As a nurse cherishing her children, so desiring you, we would gladly impart to you not only the Gospel of Christ, but also our own souls. But as to what is said for this in the LXX, αἱ θυγατέρες σε ἐκ ὤμων ἀρθήσονται, that is, your daughters shall be carried upon shoulders: it must be attended to more diligently. For sons, who are robust, come of themselves from afar, and are gathered to the faith of the Lord. But daughters, who are weaker, and by the fragility of their sex, have not yet come to a perfect man, are carried on the shoulders of the Apostles, that they may be brought into the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. THEN YOU SHALL SEE, etc. When you have lifted up your eyes and looked upon your sons and your daughters, either coming quickly of themselves or being carried on the shoulders of the saints: Then you shall rejoice, and you shall be inundated like rivers with sudden waters, and your heart shall wonder and be astonished, nay, it shall be enlarged, of one hearing the Apostle: My mouth is open to you, O Corinthians. And again: Be you also enlarged, lest by the narrowness of your breast you cannot have Christ as a guest: who says in the Gospel, I and the Father will come, and will make our abode with him. But what is added in the LXX, καὶ φοβηθήση, i.e., and you shall fear, is not had in the Hebrew. Unless perhaps after the magnitude of the joy, fear crept in, lest she should lack so great a good. Is it not joy to see the riches and the multitude of the sea transferred and converted to oneself, and the strength of the Gentiles coming to one, so that whatever is in the world and the whole earth may be one's own, and with the faith of the Gentiles strengthened, one may say, I can do all things in him who strengthens me, Jesus Christ? Cyril explains this place similarly. Calvin also agrees: LIFT UP ROUND ABOUT: That that promise concerning the restoring of the Church, which seemed altogether incredible, is confirmed by many things. For it was not easy in such a miserable and disturbed state of affairs to persuade the Jews of these things; then the kingdom of Judah alone remained, and that was still diminishing day by day; until it should utterly collapse. But when the people were dragged into exile in that horrible dissipation and sad ruins, all things were so desperate that it was thought that the Church was utterly finished. Therefore, this doctrine had to be confirmed by many things, lest their minds, naturally prone to diffidence, should doubt any further. Therefore, he brings the Jews as if into a present matter, even though it was far off: so that they might hesitate no more than if it were already placed before their eyes. He added ROUND ABOUT: so that they might hold for certain that the peoples would come not from one region only, but from everywhere, who would coalesce into one body: nor does he promise only the remedy and end of the dispersion that was to be, as it is said elsewhere: He will gather the dispersed of Israel: but this collection is extended more widely. For it signifies that there will be a wonderful conversion in the world, so that those who had previously been scattered and strangers may coalesce into one body. Finally, the propagation of the Church to the furthest ends of the earth is noted. There is also an underlying tacit antithesis, which denotes the miserable and calamitous state in which the world was before it was gathered under the auspices of Christ. Nor could Musculus deny this sense: THEN YOU SHALL SEE AND BE RADIANT AND YOUR HEART SHALL THRILL AND BE ENLARGED, WHEN THE ABUNDANCE OF THE SEA SHALL BE CONVERTED TO YOU. He predicts the accession of the Gentiles, and that it would be so numerous that it would strike amazement into those watching. Then, he says, you shall see. He does not speak precisely of the time of the return from Babylon, but of all that which was to follow up until Christ: so that it is the same as, From that time you shall see. WHEN THE ABUNDANCE OF THE SEA SHALL BE CONVERTED TO YOU. He expresses whence she would be astonished, and would be joyful with amazement: namely, from the fact that she would see the abundance of the sea and the wealth of the nations converted to her. By the abundance of the sea he understands the maritime and western peoples. For the Mediterranean Sea is to the west of Zion, and therefore in the Scriptures it is taken for the western region. However, what he says, When the abundance of the sea shall have been converted to you, is not to be understood of the entire multitude of western peoples: but it is the same as if he were to say, When many shall have been converted to you from the west. Thus Christ, Matt. 8, says: Many shall come from the east and from the west. Christian interpreters affirm with great consensus that the discourse is about the time of the New Testament, in which the Gospel was preached to the nations throughout the whole world, and a great multitude of Gentiles were converted to Christ. For these things do not refer to the return of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity, as that they do not agree is too manifest. By the multitude of the sea, they understand the islanders and transmarine nations—Greeks, Africans, Spaniards, Italians, French, English, Batavians, Norwegians, Danes, etc.; indeed, since Judea is as it were surrounded by the sea and divided from other nations, they think all transmarine nations are called by that name. FORTITUDO GENTIUM is explained by some as the valid and strong nations, with Vatablus; by others as the wealth of the nations, with Sanctus; by some as the multitude or army, as if it were a copious host of nations. To Lyranus, the strength of the nations is the Roman Empire, which dominates the whole world: he says this prophecy was fulfilled in the time of Constantine the Great. They agree, however, that the prophecy concerns the conversion of the nations. It is helpful to add the explanation of B. Luther, who exhibits the designated places geographically in his Enarration of this passage, f. 128. MULTITUDO MARIS. Here, one should not understand a multitude of waters, but maritime regions and towns, just as if we were to say: 'the whole Rhine is stirred up,' for 'all the Rhinelanders, as many as dwell by the Rhine, are stirred up.' But Scripture also has this custom, that although there are many seas, it calls only the Mediterranean Sea, absolutely, 'the sea.' For it calls the Red Sea and others by their own names. Furthermore, it is called 'Mediterranean' by writers because it inundates almost through the middle of the land, breaking in from the west, and having on the left Spain, Gaul, Italy, Greece, and Asia, as far as Cilicia; on the right, Africa and Egypt, as far as Palestine; and thus on both sides it has very broad and powerful regions; within, it has many islands, such as Crete, Rhodes, Cyprus, and countless others; today the Turk possesses almost all of them. This sea is called 'the sea' in Scripture, and it is to the west of Judea. For Palestine, the maritime region, is the boundary of Judea. Therefore, Scripture is accustomed to call the inhabitants of this sea, especially those on the left side, 'nations'; for the nations that inhabit the right part of this sea and those toward the east have their own names. Between these nations and us, and whoever dwells to the North from the left shore of the sea, we are counted. For this reason, Paul calls himself in 1 Tim. 1 and certain other places the Apostle of the Nations, because he preached in this part of the world, which is on the left shore of the sea, and wrote all his Epistles to them; nor do we read that he preached on the right shore and among the peoples living beyond it, except at the beginning in Damascus and in Arabia. These, therefore, are the nations living on the left of the sea, of whom Isaiah speaks here, saying, 'when the multitude of the sea shall be converted to you, and the power of the nations shall come to you,' understanding the same by the multitude of the sea and the power of the nations; indeed, by the latter he declares the former, that he is not speaking of waters, but of men. Thus, by the power of the nations, he does not understand the strength and fortitude of the nations—what would that do in the Church?—but the multitude of the nations; for many are usually able to do very much. Thus we say 'a great force of money' for 'much money,' etc. This prophecy was fulfilled most especially through Paul; he himself is the Apostle of the Nations, who first brought the multitude of the sea and the power of the nations to Christ, etc. This is B. Luther. The gloss of Grotius concerning the riches of the Tyrians is frivolous and inept. For it is manifest that the discourse is about the MULTITUDE OF THE SEA, not about riches, since all things designate the abundance and multitude of those flowing together. Nor is the Holy Spirit to be believed to have announced such remarkable admiration among the Jerusalemites for the reason that the Tyrians might perhaps bring merchandise to Jerusalem, or that the Jerusalemites might capture some spoils from the Tyrians. Nor is it certain that when the Holy Spirit said 'sea,' He indicated the Tyrians; indeed, He prophesies at length about various nations and peoples, describing with many words the beauty and multitude of those who are to be gathered to Jerusalem. R. David Kimchi, although he had begun to insert the particle כ for a comparative expression, 'AS THE MULTITUDE OF THE SEA,' nevertheless explains it as the multitude of peoples, which is like the abundance of the sea. Junius and Tremellius translate it thus: 'WHEN THE ROARING OF THE SEA SHALL BE CHANGED TOWARD YOU,' i.e., when the nations, which previously seemed to threaten you with destruction like a raging sea, with changed minds shall approach you. All agree that the multitude of nations and peoples is explained here. One will perhaps find no one besides Grotius who has explained it as referring only to the Tyrians. With this emphatic description of the multitude and variety of peoples who are said to be about to be converted to the Church, one can compare a similar delineation (διατύπωσις) of the same, which is had in chapter 49, where we demonstrated above that the discourse is about the calling of the nations. To the same multitude of nations look also those things which follow in v. 6: 'THE INUNDATION OF CAMELS SHALL COVER YOU, THE DROMEDARIES OF MIDIAN AND EPHA.' Which Grotius wrongly snatches away to a political society. For the influx of the nations to the Church is noted: that they shall walk in the light of the Church. As if he were to say, 'These nations, which use camels, shall hasten to you with such a multitude of camels that, just as a flood of waters covers the land, so they themselves shall occupy all places.' Midian was the son of Abraham by Keturah, and the son of Midian was Epha, Genesis 25. Whence those names adhered to some regions of Arabia, which used camels, and 'bikkurim' [firstborn] or younger camels, which the Latin rendered as dromedaries or running horses. Therefore, the descendants of Abraham are indicated in Midian and Epha, as if to say, they will not be able to be held back from hastening to you with camels. Such also was Saba, son of Jokshan, son of Abraham by Keturah, who also gave his name to his region: whose Queen once had visited Solomon. Kedar and Nebajoth were sons of Ishmael, from whom these eastern regions also obtained their names. Isaiah therefore predicted that all those would come to Jerusalem, not for the sake of a political society, but for sacrifices and offerings, so that the house of the majesty of the Lord might be glorified, i.e., for the glory and worship of the Lord, and not that those nations would depart from their own desert regions in a bodily manner to Jerusalem, and there possess the right of external citizenship, and offer external sacrifices. For how could one city contain so many nations? But that the Gospel will reach all these nations, whether dwelling on land or on the islands of the sea, and that the Church is to be gathered from all those nations, which may offer spiritual sacrifices to GOD. So that thus the Church of the living God 1. Tim. 3, 15. may be glorified and rendered illustrious. Calvin therefore aptly warned here: The Prophet figuratively describes the glory of the Church, and adapts his discourse to the time, and to the persons with whom he himself had to do. For it is to be kept in memory, what we have often said, that the Prophets had regard for the people whom they were teaching: and therefore mentioned customary things and known ceremonies, so that under their figures they might designate the spiritual worship of God. For they had first to be instructed: Then the nations to whom the truth of these things reached. Just as if he were saying, that peoples far distant would come with their wealth into the power of God. For as to the fact that he predicts that the Church is to be enriched, it ought not to be referred to the persons of men, but on account of the unity of the head and the members, which is proper to GOD and Christ, it is transferred to the Church. Foolishly, therefore, do the Jews, under the pretext of this prophecy, devour with their insatiable greed all the riches of the earth. Nor do the Papists any less wrongly distort these words to their own luxurious opulence and pomp. He makes mention, however, of camels, incense, gold, and sheep, because he is looking at what each region produces: so that he may show that all will consecrate to God whatever they have in their possession, and will offer themselves and all their belongings Finally, if you say that he is looking especially at the Jerusalem temple, that can be admitted by us for a certain reason: which was also observed by Calvin: Furthermore, under the glorification of the temple, he declares the true restoration of the people. For this was the chief part of happiness, that the temple should stand, in which GOD might be purely invoked: for the beginning must be made from this, that GOD may reign among us, so that we may be truly blessed. Therefore the Lord, when He signifies that the Church is to be restored, makes mention of the temple, because He restores its glory: As if He were saying, My house is now exposed to the mockery of the nations: but I will at last restore to it the glory of which it is now despoiled. It appears, however, from Zechariah, Haggai, and Malachi that this was not completed immediately upon the return of the people. Nor indeed must it be thought that the true dignity was in that sumptuous structure with which Herod shrewdly wished to acquire favor for himself: and therefore the dignity or honor of which mention is made here did not emerge until God opened the gates of heaven at Jerusalem; and from there openly called all nations to the hope of eternal salvation. But as to what is said, ALL from Sheba shall come. And: ALL the flock of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, is not to be understood in such a way that all the Sabeans and Kedarites are going to believe in Christ: For a great part of the nations remains in incredulity; but that the preaching of the Gospel is going to reach all, and that from all these places the Church is to be gathered, just as Paul also says in Colossians 1 concerning the Gospel, that it bears fruit in THE WHOLE WORLD.

Here, at the same time, the fourth reason for our explanation is presented from the offering of gifts and sacrifices. For since it is said here that the Sabeans will bring gold and incense and will announce the praise of the Lord, and that the flocks of Kedar and the rams of Nebaioth are to be offered upon the altar of the Lord, it is manifest that the discourse is not about temporal happiness, nor about a local approach, which neither happened nor could happen to that one city, but that these things must be understood spiritually, in the sense we have stated, ἐξ ἀνάγκης (of necessity), which the whole context demands. Rightly, therefore, does the interpretation of Blessed Luther hold: All these ARE GATHERED UNTO THEE. He signifies that the Gospel will be spread throughout the whole world. Wherefore these things cannot be understood literally and corporally. THE MULTITUDE OF THE SEA. Thus he calls the multitude of the Gentiles inhabiting maritime places, the islands, and the Mediterranean Sea. MIDIAN. Midian is toward the Red Sea. And Ephah is a part of Arabia Felix. He signifies, however, that it will come to pass that those nations will approach the Church through the preaching of the Gospel. ALL FROM SHEBA SHALL COME. Although not all have believed, yet the Gospel has reached all. GOLD AND INCENSE. I take these generally, that is, they will contribute their resources to help the Church. Included in this general sentiment, however, are also the Magi in Matthew 2. ANNOUNCING THE PRAISE OF THE LORD. This is the sacrifice of Christians: to praise God, to confess the Gospel, to teach others. For there is nothing else that we can render to God for His benefits. ALL THE FLOCK OF KEDAR. That is, Kedar also contributes his resources to help the Church. He names flocks, however, because the Arabs practiced animal husbandry. For Kedar and Nebaioth are parts of Arabia. THEY SHALL BE OFFERED UPON MY ACCEPTABLE ALTAR. THE ALTAR is Christ: The priests are those who teach the Gospel; they kill and slaughter whatever is magnificent in the world, the righteousness and wisdom of the flesh. For the Gospel convicts all of sin. Then, privately, we are each priests, while we daily mortify our old man, as in Romans 6. This passage contains, however, a manifest abrogation of the sacrifices of Moses and of the whole law. Which sense Cyril had also rendered: Sheba is a region beyond the land of the Arabs, and near the Red Sea: from which the Queen of Sheba of the Ethiopians came to Jerusalem in the times of Solomon. It is a region most fertile in incense, gold, and Indian stones. They shall come, therefore, he says, bearing fruit unto glory, and bringing incense and gold and stones, or the sweet fragrance of good works, and splendor falling under the understanding, and spiritual riches. And they shall evangelize the salvation of the Lord. For many have been called from the nations, and wise in heart, and holding sacred doctrines in their mind, endowed with the authority to teach: and preaching salvation and grace from Christ, the Savior of us all, to others, they have been crowned with the crown of nobility. They shall come also, he says, the sheep of Kedar, and the rams of Nebaioth, and they shall be offered acceptably upon my altar. Kedar and Nebaioth, again, are other regions, rich and pasturable, and they have very many inhabitants, but idolaters and wanderers. But even these, he says, shall bring rams and sheep, and all things shall be acceptable upon my altar: Even though it was not permitted by the Mosaic law for foreigners to offer sacrifices to God: and if they had offered them, He did not hold them acceptable. But behold, God commands them to be acceptable, on the holy altars. For in Christ Jesus there is neither slave nor free, barbarian, Scythian, Greek, and Jew, but Christ is all and in all. For the two peoples have been made one, when He broke down the middle wall of partition, and abolished the law of commandments in dogmas. Therefore the sacrifices of those who approach God through faith in Christ are acceptable. And the Lord has been made the glorious house of prayer. Again, consider for me the depth of the prayer: For He does not want the Church to be called a house of sacrifices and burnt offerings now, as indeed the Jerusalem temple was: but rather of prayer, that is, of spiritual worship. Moreover, the divine David sings somewhere and says: Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, the lifting up of my hands, the evening sacrifice. It should also be noted that the Savior Himself made mention of this verse: when He rebukes the business dealings of the Jews, and says: It is written: My house shall be called a house of prayer. But you make it a den of thieves. When, therefore, it has been made a house of prayer, then it has also been glorified. Cornelius à Lapide is mistaken here, while he wishes to denote not only שבא by the Arabian Schin; but also סבא by the Samech as the kingdom of the Abyssinians, because, forsooth, the letters Schin and Sin differ only by a point, confusing the letter Sin with Samech, and holding the genuine reading and the note in the same place: for there cannot be but one genuine reading, and therefore not but one genuine sense.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET DOMUM MAJESTATIS MEÆ GLO- RIFICABO] Nempe per illas pecudes, quæ tibi ex lon- ginquis locis advenient.

Perversè hæc ad Judæos trahuntur. Dicta e- nim sunt de gentibus & populis ad Hierosolymam congregatis. Nam quum prædixerit Esaias ambu- laturas gentes in Lumine Hierosolymæ, jam digito quasi demonstrat multitudinem advenientium. Tertium ergo hic argumentum à populi congregan- di frequentia & varietate. LEVA IN CIRCUITU OCULOS TUOS, ET VIDE OMNES ISTI CONGREGA- TI SUNT, VENERUNT TIBI. Attolle & circumfer oculos tuos in omnes partes, & circuitum regionis tuæ, in omnes mundi plagas. En omnis ista populi multitudo, quam vides innumeram esse, conve- niunt, ut ad te proficiscantur, & fiant tui incolæ ac cives. FILII TUI DE LONGE, ET FILIAE TUAE DE

LATERE SURGENT. Itaque sive longitudinem seu latitudinem terræ respicias, undiquaque ad te con- fluent, & de longe & de latere tibi aderunt filii tui & filiæ tuæ, ut nempe cives tui evadant; non tantum e propinquis regionibus, sed etiam e longinquis concurrunt, quæ sunt & ante te & ad latus tuum, ex omnibus circumcirca regionibus etiam procul dis- sitis. In Ebræo est: Et filiæ tuæ AD LATUS NU- TRIENTUR, unde, quod vulgata reddidit, de latere surgent; Hieronymus sensum exprimens ita transtu- lit: & filiæ tuæ lac sugent. Reges enim dicuntur futuri אמנים nutricii ejus Esa. 49, 13. quale verbum hoc loco habetur. In parallelo loco Esa. 49, 22. hæc ita leguntur: Et filiæ tuæ in ulnis apportabuntur, ut nutrices solent infantes. Unde hic etiam LXX. In- terpp. Et filiæ tuæ super humeros portabuntur. Non ergo divinatione aut Oedipo opus est, an aliter, aut quid Græci & Chaldæus legerint, qui non semper verbum verbo exprimunt, sed sensum sæpe tantum respiciunt: quem hic ex parallelo loco illustrarunt. TUNC VIDEBIS ET AFFLUES, ET MIRABITUR ET DILATABITUR COR TUUM, QUANDO CONVERSA FUERIT AD TE MULTITUDO MARIS, FORTITUDO GENTIUM VENERIT TIBI. Tanta erit multitudo advenientium ad te, vel civium tuarum, ut tu ipsa cum eam videris, maxima capiaris admiratione, ac etiam obstupescas, & cor tuum præ ingenti lætitia gestiat. Convertetur enim ad te multitudo maris, h. e. eorum, qui in insulis maris habitant. Et veniet ad te fortitudo, h. e. magna copia gentium. Recte hæc exponit Hieronymus: LEVA IN CIRCUITU: Dici- tur ad Ecclesiam, quæ primum per Apostolos congre- gata est in Sion: de quibus & in Actis Apostolorum le- gimus, quod de universo orbe terrarum viri religiosi fuerint in Hierusalem, qui susceperint sermonem Dei, & linguis suarum alienarumq́ gentium, vel au- dirent loquentes alios, vel ipsi loquerentur ad cæteros. Et præcipitur, ut levent oculos suos in circuitu. Quod & Dominus præcepit Apostolis, dicens: Levate o- culos vestros, & videte: quia albæ sunt segetes ad messendum. De Sion enim & nequaquam de monte Sina egredietur lex, & verbum Domini de Hierusa- lem. Præcipiturq́ ut elevatis oculis videat suos filios congregatos, qui de longe veniant. Cui & in alio loco dicitur: Gaude nimis filia Sion, prædica filia Hie- rusalem. Ecce, ego venio & habitabo in medio tui, dicit Dominus; Et venient gentes multæ ad Do- minum, & erunt mihi in populum, & ego ero eis in Deum. Nos autem sumus filii, qui de longe venimus ad dominum, peregrini quondam a testamento Dei & repromissionibus ejus, spem non habentes, & absq́ Deo in mundo. Sed quid dicit Apostolus? Vos, qui eratis aliquando longe, nunc facti estis prope. Quodq́ sequitur: Et filiæ tuæ lac sugent: illud si- gnificat, quod animæ in Christo lactentes, & in ba- ptismate parvulorum; de quibus & Petrus Apostolus loquitur: Quasi modo nati parvuli, rationabile & absque dolo lac desiderate, sugant lac Apostolorum. Quibus parvulis atq́ lactentibus loquebatur & Pau- lus: Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec Chri stus formetur in vobis. Et in alio loco; Quasi nutrix fovens filios suos, sic desiderantes vos cupimus im- pertire non solum Evangelium Christi, sed & ani- mas nostras. Quod autem pro hoc in LXX. dicitur, αἱ θυγατέρες σε ἐκ ὤμων ἀρθήσονται, id est, filiæ tuæ super humeros portabuntur: diligentius attenden- dum est. Filii enim, qui robusti sunt, ipsi per se de longe veniunt, & ad fidem Domini congregantur. Filiæ autem, quæ imbecilliores sunt, & pro fragilitate se- xus, nec dum in virum venêre perfectum, Apostolo- rum portantur humeris, ut deferantur in sinus Abra- ham, Isaac & Jacob. TUNC VIDEBIS &c. Quum d elevaveris oculos tuos & filios tuos filiasq́; prospexeris, vel per se venire velociter vel sanctorum humeris de- portari: Tunc gaudebis, & in modum fluviorum aquis subitis inundaberis, & mirabitur ac stupebit, imo dilatabitur cor tuum audientis Apostolum: Os meum patet ad vos ô Corinthii. Et iterum: Dila- tamini & vos, ne angustia pectoris non possitis habere hospitem Christum: qui dicit in Evangelio, Ego & pater veniemus, & mansionem faciemus apud eum. Quod autem additur in LXX. καὶ φοβηθήση, i. e. & ti- mebis, in Hebraico non habetur. Nisi forte post gau- dii magnitudinem subintravit timor, ne tanto bono careat. Annon est gaudium, cernere divitias & mul- titudinem maris ad se transferri atq́; converti, & for- titudinem gentium venire sibi, ut quicquid in seculo & orbe terrarum est, suum sit, & roborata fide gen- tium dicat, Omnia possum in eo, qui confortat me, Jesu Christo? Similiter explicat Cyrillus in hunc locum. Annuit quoque Calvinus: LEVA IN CIR- CVITV: Pluribus confirmari promissionem illam de restituenda Ecclesia, quæ incredibilis omnino videba- tur. Nec enim facile erat in tam misero & perturbato rerum statu, hæc Judæis persuadere, tunc regnum Juda solummodo restabat, idq́; adhuc indies minue- batur; donec prorsus concideret. Ubi vero in exilium tractus fuit populus in horrenda illa dissipatione, & tristibus ruinis, adeo desperata erant omnia, ut puta- retur de Ecclesia penitus actum esse. Pluribus ergo confirmanda fuit hæc doctrina, ne animi natura pro- pensi ad diffidentiam, amplius dubitarent. Propterea adducit Judæos velut in rem præsentem, tametsi pro- cul abesset: ut nihilo magis hæsitent, quam si jam ob oculos ipsorum poneretur. Adait IN CIRCUITU: ut certo teneant non ab una tantum plaga, sed undique venturos populos, qui in corpus unum coalescant: nec vero tantum dispersionis, quæ futura erat, remedium ac finem promittit, sicut alibi dicitur: Dispersos Is- raëlis congregabit: sed latius extenditur hæc colle- ctio. Significat enim mirabilem fore conversionem in mundo, ita, ut qui prius fuerant dissipati & extra- nei, in unum corpus coalescant. Deniq́; notatur Ecclesiæ propagatio, in ultimos terræ fines. Subest etiam taci- ta antithesis, quæ miserum & calamitosum statum de- notat, in quo prius erat mundus, quam auspiciis Chri- sti colligeretur. Neque dissiteri hunc sensum potuit Musculus: TVNC VIDEBIS ET SPLENDESCES ET STUPESCET AC DILATABITUR COR TUUM, QUAN- DO CONVERSA FUERIT AD TE MULTITUDO MA- RIS. Accessionem gentium prædicit, eamq́; tam nume- rosam, ut stuporem esset incussura spectantibus. Tunc, inquit, videbis. Non loquitur precise de tempore redi- tus à Babylone, sed omni eo, quod ad Christum usq́; erat sequuturum: ut idem sit, quod, Ab eo tempore vide- bis. QUANDO CONVERSA FUERIT AD TE MULTITUDO MARIS. Exprimit unde fuerit attonita, & cum stupore hilaris futura: ex eo videlicet, quod visura esset converti ad se multitudi- nem maris, & opes gentium. Per multitudinem ma- ris intelligit populos maritimos & occidentales. Nam mare mediterraneum est Sioni ab occidente, ideoq́; in Scripturis pro plaga occidentali accipitur. Non est autem de universa occidentalium populorum multitudine intelligendum, quod dicit: Quando multitudo maris ad te conversa fuerit: sed idem est, ac si diceret, Quando multi fuerint ad te ab occiden- te conversi. Sic Christus Matth. 8. Multi, inquit, ve- nient ab oriente & ab occidente. De tempore Novi Testamenti, quo gentibus per orbem universum Evangelium prædicatum, & magna multitudine gentes ad Christum conversæ sunt, sermonem esse magno consensu affirmant Christiani Interpp. Ju- dæorum enim reditui à captivitateBabylonica hæc non convenire nimis manifestum est. Per multitu dinem maris insulares, & transmarinas Gentes Græcos, Afros, Hispanos, Italos, Gallos, Anglos Batavos, Norwegos, Danos &c. intelligunt: imo quum Judæa mari quasi cingatur, & dividatur ab aliis gentibus, omnes gentes inde transmarinas dici putant. FORTITUDO GENTIUM à non- nullis de gentibus validis & fortibus cum Vatablo, ab aliis de opibus gentium cum Sancto, à quibusdam de multitudine, vel exercitu, quasi gentium co- pioso explicatur: Lyrano fortitudo gentium est Imperium Romanum, quod toti mundo domina- tur: qui impletum vaticinium dicit tempore Con- stantini Magni. Conveniunt autem in eo, quod de conversione gentium Prophetia agat. Juvat B.Lu- theri explicationem addere, qui Geographice loca designata exhibet, in Enarratione hujus loci f. 128. MULTITUDO MARIS. Hic non debet intelligi multitudo aquarum, sed regiones & oppida mariti- ma, sicut si diceremus: totus Rhenus commotus est, pro omnes Rhenani, quotquot accolunt Rhenum com- moti sunt. Sed Scriptura etiam hunc morem habet, ut licet multa maria sint, solum mare mediterraneum absolute mare appellet. Mare enim rubrum, ac alia suis cognominibus appellat. Porro mediterraneum ideo à scriptoribus vocatur, quod ferè per mediam terram inundet, irrumpens ab occidente, & habens à læva Hispaniam, Galliam, Italiam, Græciam & A- siam, usq́; Ciliciam; à dextra Africam, Ægyptum, usq́; Palæstinam: atq́; ita ab utraq́; parte habet latis- simas & potentissimas regiones: intra habet multas Insulas, ut Cretam, Rhodum, Cyprum ac alias innu- meras; hodie omnes fere Turca obtinet. Hoc mare in Scriptura vocatur, & est Judææ ab occidente. Pa- læstina enim maritima regio, Judææ terminus est. Hu- jus itaq́; maris accolas, præsertim sinistri lateris, scri- ptura solet gentes appellare: gentes enim, quæ dex- tram hujus maris partem, & versus orientem inco- lunt, propria habent nomina. Inter has Gentes & nos, ac quicunq́; ad Aquilonem, à sinistro littore ma- ris habitant, connumeramur. Hac causa vocat se Paulus 1. Tim. 1. ac aliis quibusdam locis, Apostolum Gentium, quod in hac mundi parte, quæ est à sinistro maris littore, prædicavit, ac omnes Epistolas suas ad hos scripsit, neq́; legimus in dextro littore, & apud po- pulos ultra illud habitantes, ipsum prædicasse, nisi ab initio Damasci & in Arabia. Hæc igitur gentes à sini- stro maris habitantes istæ sunt, de quibus hic Esaias loquitur, dicens, cum multitudo maris ad te fuerit conversa, & potentia gentium ad te venerit, eos- dem intelligens per multitudinem maris & gentium potentiam; imo per posterius hoc prius declarat, se non loqui de aquis, sed hominibus. Sic per potentiam gentium non intelligit robur ac fortitudinem gentium, quid ista faceret in Ecclesia? sed multitudinem gentium: multa namq́; solent plurima posse. Ita ma- gnam vim pecuniæ dicimus, pro multis pecuniis &c. Hoc vaticinium potissimum per Paulum impletum est; ipse Apostolus gentium est, qui maris multitu- dinem & gentium potentiam ad Christum primus perduxit &c. Hæc B. Lutherus. Glossa Grotii de divitiis Tyriorum frivola & inepta est. Nam de MULTITUDINE MARIS, non de divitiis ser- monem esse, quum omnia copiam & multitudinem confluentium designent, manifestum est. Neque tam insignem admirationem penes Hierosolymi- tanos prænunciasse credendus est Spiritus Sanctus ob id, quod Tyrii fortasse res promercales allaturi sint Hierosolymam, aut quod Hierosolymitani ali- quid spoliorum de Tyriis capturi sint. Neque cum mare dixit Spiritus Sanctus, Tyrios indicasse con- stat; imo de gentibus populisq; variis prolixe va- ticinatur, multis verbis venustatem & multitudi- nem eorum describens, qui ad Hierosolymam con- gregandi sint. R. David Kimchi etsi particulam כ ad inserendam comparativam locutionem inierat, SICUT MULTITUDO MARIS, de multitudine tamen populorum, quæ sit instar abundantiæ maris exponit. Junius & Tremellius ita vertunt: QUAN- DO MUTABITUR ERGA TE FREMITUS MARIS, h. e. quando gentes, quæ prius tanquam mare furens perniciem tibi minari videbantur, mu- tatis animis accedent tibi. Omnes consentiunt, gen- tium & populorum multitudinem hic exponi. De Tyriis solis, qui exposuerit forte præter Grotium invenietur nemo. Cum hac autem emphatica mul- titudinis & varietatis populorum, qui ad Eccle- siam convertendi dicuntur, descriptione, conferri potest similis eorundem διατύπωσις, quæ cap. 49. habetur, ubi de vocatione gentium sermonem esse, supra demonstravimus. Ad eandem gentium mul- titudinem spectant & ea, quæ sequuntur v. 6. IN- UNDATIO CAMELORUM OPERIET TE, DROMEDARII MADIAN ET EPHA. Quæ perperam Grotius abripit ad societatem politicam. Confluxus enim gentium ad Ecclesiam notatur: quod ambulaturæ sint in lumine Ecclesiæ. Qua- si dicat, Hæ gentes, quæ utuntur Camelis, pro- perabunt ad te tanta Camelorum multitudine, ut sicut eluvio aquarum terram operit; ita ipsæ omnia loca occupaturæ sint. Midian fuit filius Abrahæ ex Kethura, & filius Midian fuit Epha, Genes. 25. Unde nomina illa hæserunt regionibus Arabiæ nonnullis, quæ Camelis utebantur, & בברי primo- genitis, vel junioribus Camelis, quod Latinus red- didit, dromedarios vel equos cursores. Posteri er- go Abrahami indigitantur in Midian & Epha, q. d. teneri non poterunt, quin Camelis ad te festi- nent. Talis fuit & Saba filius Joxsan, filii Abra- ham ex Kethura, qui etiam suæ regioni nomen de- dit: Cujus Regina quondam Salomonem visitarat. Kedar & Nebajoth fuerunt filii Israëlis, à quibus & hæ orientales Regiones nomina sua consequutæ sunt. Illos ergo omnes Hierosolymam venturos prædixit Esaias non societatis politicæ causa, sed ad sacrificia & oblationes, ut domus majestatis Domi- ni glorificetur, h. e. ob gloriam & cultum Domini, nec quod gentes illæ profecturæ sint desertis suis regionibus corporali modo ad Hierusalem, & illic habituræ jus externæ civitatis, ac oblaturæ externa sacrificia. Quomodo enim una urbs tot gentes ca- pere posset? Sed quod ad omnes has gentes sive in terra sive in insulis maris habitantes, proventurum sit Evangelium, ex omnibus illis gentibus colli- genda sit Ecclesia, quæ sacrificia spiritualia DEO offerat. Ut ita domus Dei viventis Ecclesia 1. Tim. 3, 15. glorificetur & illustris reddatur. Commode ergo hic monuit Calvinus: Describit Propheta fi- gurate gloriam Ecclesiæ, atque sermonem suum tempori accommodat, & personis, quibuscum ipsi negotium erat. Est enim memoria tenendum, quod sæpius diximus, Prophetas habuisse rationem popu- li, quem docebant: ideoque res usitatas & notas cę- remonias commemorasse, ut sub earum figuris spiri- tualem Dei cultum designarent. Illi enim primum instituendi fuerunt: Deinde gentes ad quas istarum rerum veritas pervenit. Perinde ac si diceret, po- pulos longe dissitos cum suis opibus venturos in Dei potestatem. Nam quod Ecclesiam locupletandam prædicit, referri non debet ad hominum personas, sed propter unitatem capitis & membrorum, quod DEI & Christi proprium est, ad Ecclesiam trans- fertur. Stulte ergo Judæi hujus vaticinii præ- textu devorant inexplebili sua cupiditate omnes terræ divitias. Nec minus Papistæ perperam hæc verba ad luxuriosam suam opulentiam pompasq́; de- torquent. Camelorum autem, Thuris, Auri, Ovium adeo mentionem facit, quod spectet quid unaquæq́; re- gio proferat: ut ostendat, omnes consecraturas Deo quicquid penes sese habuerint, seq́; & sua omnia velut in sacrificium oblaturas. Denique si maxime tem- plum Hierosolymitanum respici dicas, certa id ra- tione admitti nobis poterit: quod etiam Calvino observatum: Porro sub templi glorificatione veram populi instaurationem declarat. Hæc enim præci- pua felicitatis pars erat, ut staret templum, in quo DEUS pure invocaretur: nam initium hinc faciendum est, ut DEUS inter nos regnet, quo ve- re beati simus. Propterea Dominus, cum Eccle- siam instauratum iri significat, templi mentionem facit, quod ejus gloriam restituit: Ac si diceret, Domus mea nunc ludibrio gentium exposita est: sed gloriam tandem, qua nunc spoliata est, ei restituam. Apparet autem ex Zacharia, Aggeo & Malachia non statim à populi reditu hoc fuisse completum. Nec vero in sumptuosa illa mole, quæ Herodes astute favo- rem sibi acquirere voluit, veram dignitatem fuisse putandum est: ideoq́; non ante emersit dignitas aut decus, cujus sit hic mentio, quam ubi januam cælo- rum Jerosolymæ aperuit Deus; & inde palam voca- vit omnes gentes ad spem æternæ salutis. Quod au- tem dicitur, OMNES de Saba venient. Et: OMNE pecus Kedar congregabitur tibi, non sic intelligendum est, quod omnes Sabæi & Cedere- ni sint in Christum credituri: Magna enim pars gentium manet in incredulitate; sed quod præ- dicatio Evangelii perventura sit ad omnes, & quod ex omnibus istis locis Ecclesia sit colligenda, sicut & Paulus Col. 1. de Evangelio dicit, quod fructifi- cet in TOTO MUNDO.

Exhibetur autem hic simul Quarta ratio no- stræ explicationis à donorum & sacrificiorum obla- tione.
