Quum enim hic Sabæi aurum & thus de- laturi & laudem Domini annunciaturi, & pecora Cedar, & arietes Nabajoth offerendi dicantur super altari Domini, manifestum est, non de temporali felicitate, neque de locali accessu, qui neque factus est, neque fieri potuit ad unam illam urbem, sermonem esse, sed spiritualiter hæc, eo quem diximus sensu, ἐξ ἀνάγκης intelligen- da esse, quem totus contextus postulat. Recte er- go se habet B. Lutheri interpretatio: Omnes isti CONGREGANTUR TIBI. Significat quod Evange- lium per totum orbem divulgabitur. Quare non possunt hæc ad literam corporaliter intelligi. MUL- TITUDO MARIS. Sic vocat multitudinem Gentium colentium loca maritima, Insulas & maris mediter- ranei. MADIAN. Madian est versus mare Ru- brum. Et Epha est pars Arabiæ felicis. Significat autem fore, ut illæ Gentes accedant ad Ecclesiam per prædicationem Evangelii. OMNES DE SABA VENIENT. Quanquam non omnes crediderunt, tamen ad omnes pervenit Evangelium. AURUM ET THUS. Generaliter ista accipio, id est, facul- tates suas conferent ad juvandam Ecclesiam. Inclu- duntur autem in hanc generalem sententiam etiam magi Matth. 2. LAUDEM DOMINI AN- NUNTIANTES. Hoc est sacrificium Christiano- rum, Laudare Deum, confiteri Evangelium, docere alios. Nihil enim aliud est, quod nos Deo pro suis beneficiis possumus reddere. OMNE PECUS KEDAR. Id est, confert & Kedar facultates suas ad juvandam Ecclesiam. Ideo autem Pecora nominat, quod Arabes pecuariam colebant. Sunt enim Ke- dar & Nabajoth Arabiæ partes. OFFERENTUR SUPER PLACABILI ALTARI MEO. ARA est Christus : Sacerdotes sunt, qui docent Evangelium, illi occidunt & mactant quicquid est magnificum in mundo, justitiam & sapientiam carnis. Arguit enim Evangelium omnes de peccato. Deinde privatim sin- guli sumus Sacerdotes, dum quotidie mortificamus veterem nostrum hominem, sicut Rom. 6. Continet autem hic locus manifestam abrogationem sacrificio- rum Mosi & totius legis. Quem sensum reddide- rat quoque Cyrillus : Saba regio est ultra terram Arabum, & prope mare rubrum : ex qua Sabba Æ- thiopum Regina, temporibus Salomonis, accessit Hierusalem. Fertilissima est regio thure, auro & lapidibus Indicis. Venient igitur, inquit, fructum parientes in gloriam, & adducentes thus & au- rum ac lapides, sive bonorum operum suavem fra- grantiam, & splendorem sub intelligentiam caden- tem, divitiasq; spirituales. Etevangelizabunt sa- lutem Domini. Complures enim vocati sunt ex gentibus, & corde sapientes, & sacra dogmata mente tenentes, docendi autoritate præditi : & salutem ac gratiam, ab omnium nostrum Servatore Christo, aliis prædicantes ingenuitatis corona redimiti sunt. Ve- nient etiam, inquit, oves Cedar, & arietes Nabeoth, & offerentur acceptabilia super aram meam. Ce- dar, & Nabeoth rursus regiones sunt aliæ, opimæ & pabulosæ, ac plurimas habent incolas, verum idolola- tras & errantes. Sed & hi, inquit, arietes & oves adducent, & omnia erunt accepta non super aram meam : Etsiambfi lege Mosaica licitum non fuerit alienigenis, Deo hostias offerre : & si obtulissent, acce- ptas illas non habebat. Sed ecce jubet Deus acceptas es- se, in sanctis aris. In Christo enim Jesu non est servus neque liber, barbarus, Scytha, Græcus & Ju- dæus, sed omnia & in omnibus Christus. Unum e- nim facti sunt duo populi, cum ille interstitium maceriæ dejecerit, & legem mandatorum in dogmatis abole- verit. Acceptæ igitur sunt hostiæ eorum, qui per fidem in Christum accedunt ad Deum. Et gloriosa effecta est Dominus orationis Dei. Rursus mihi considera orationis profunditatem : Non enim hostiarum & su- morum domum jam vocari vult Ecclesiam, sicut nimi- rum templum Hierosolymitanum : sed precationis potius, id est, cultus spiritualis. Psallit autem ali- cubi, & ait divinus David : Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo, elevatio manuum mearum, sacrificium vespertinum. Notandum etiam hujus versiculi mentionem fecisse ipsum Serva- torem : cum Judæorum negotiationes reprehendit, & dicit : Scriptum est : Domus mea, domus oratio- nis vocabitur. Vos autem ipsam facitis spelun- cam latronum. Cum igitur domus orationis fa- cta est, tunc quoque glorificata est. Fallitur hic Cornelius à Lapide, dum non solum שבא per Schin Arabiam ; sed etiam סבא per Samech A- byffinorum regnum notari vult, quia scilicet solo puncto differant literæ Schin & Sin, confundens literam Sin cum Samech, & eadem loco habens genuinam lectionem, ac notam : non enim nisi una lectio genuina esse potest, adeoque non nisi unus sensus genuinus.

## 60:8
Verse 8.

WHO ARE THESE, WHO FLY AS CLOUDS AND AS DOVES TO THEIR WINDOWS] In the Hebrew: to their dovecotes. The sense is well expressed by the Chaldean: how swiftly, like clouds, the Jews return from all sides into their fatherland, just as doves to their familiar towers.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

QUI SUNT ISTI, QUI UT NUBES VOLANT ET QUASI COLUMBÆ AD FENESTRAS SUAS] In Hebræo : ad columbaria sua. Sensus est bene à Chal- dæo expressus : quam velociter, ut nubes, Judæi undique in patriam redeunt, sicut columbæ ad notas turres.

## 60:9
Verse 9.

FOR THE ISLANDS WAIT FOR ME] Those nations situated by the rivers are attentive to my nod. AND THE SHIPS OF THE SEA IN THE BEGINNING, THAT I MAY BRING THY SONS FROM AFAR] that is, before all things, ships are prepared in the Persian sea, which may bring back the Jews.

THEIR SILVER AND THEIR GOLD WITH THEM] Many will help you with their generosity, out of reverence for God. Ezra 1:6.

Once again the Prophet's words are twisted into a foreign and hitherto unheard-of meaning: for this discourse is not about the Jews returning quickly to their Fatherland, but about the nations hastening with wondrous speed to the Church. He had most clearly defined the subject, or those who were to come, as the nations and peoples whom he had hitherto described by their abundance and variety: now, however, he depicts them by the speed and promptness of their gathering to the Church and their worship and submission, under the likeness of CLOUDS and DOVES flying swiftly to their dovecotes. Which will be the fifth reason for us, for they are said to fly to those about whom (1.) he has hitherto treated, by describing in various ways their arrival at the Church, (2.) to whom the ISLANDS look, awaiting the Lord, (3.) whom he said would bring their gold and other gifts, and would consecrate them to the Lord: if indeed he is prophesying here again about that: THEIR SILVER AND THEIR GOLD WITH THEM. That these things speak of one and the same subject is truly too manifest. Grotius, however, with more than Rabbinic audacity, tears these apart: and twists part of them to the Jews returning to their fatherland, and part to the nations waiting to be brought over to the same, and to help them with their generosity. But this is a detestable depravation, not heard of even among the Jews. WHO ARE THESE, WHO FLY LIKE CLOUDS? asks the Prophet, or even the Church with wonder, when it sees such a multitude carried with such force and hastening to know the doctrine of the Gospel, stirred by the divine spirit, just as clouds driven by the wind are snatched from the West to the East, and just as doves gathered together rush with great force into the windows, or the little doors of their dovecote: Christ answers, to whom some also attribute the previous questions: THE ISLANDS AWAIT ME AND THE SHIPS OF THE SEA FROM THE BEGINNING. To which Brentius: By islands are generally understood all the nations that are to the West of the Jews, whether they dwell in the sea or beyond the sea. For at the time when Isaiah preached in the city of Jerusalem, only certain islands of the sea were known to the Israelites, but not the nations beyond the sea, since these were still too obscure for their fame to have been spread so widely, when even Rome itself began to be founded first in the times of Ezekiel. But what he says: From the beginning, either looks to that of Psalm 71. The Kings of Tarshish or of the Sea and the islands shall offer gifts, the Kings of the Arabs and of Sheba shall bring presents. And all Kings shall worship him, all nations shall serve him. Therefore this will be the sense: It is not said now for the first time about the nations that they are to believe in my Gospel, but it was said long ago, from the beginning of the Israelite kingdom, through David, that the islands or nations and their kings are to approach my Church, and to help it in whatever way they can. Or it looks to that which is written in 2 Chronicles 9, that the envoys of various nations, and all the Kings of Arabia, and the satraps of the lands brought gold and silver to Solomon. And it is added afterwards: The King's ships went to Tarshish or the Sea with the servants of Hiram once in three years, and brought from there gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks. Therefore, this will be the sense: In the beginning indeed, when the kingdom of Israel was confirmed in the hand of Solomon, not only neighboring Kings brought gifts to Solomon, but also the islands of the nations. And just as then they brought apes and peacocks in ships, so now they will bring your sons or citizens, O Jerusalem, from afar, and together with them also their gold and silver to the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, who also adorns you with this glory and magnificence. Although all these things are recited as if the nations were to bring external gold in ships to the city of Jerusalem, just as was done in the times of Solomon, yet because it concerns the calling of the nations to faith in Christ, through his Gospel, therefore they are to be understood as the thing itself interprets, namely, that the nations, stirred by the Gospel, will believe in Christ, and will become spiritual citizens of the city of Jerusalem, which is the Church, and will contribute their wealth to help the Church, and to preserve the ministry of the Church, which is the preaching of the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. Sanctius explains that בראשנה in the Beginning from the place, 'Those who dwell in the Beginning,' i.e., in the East; others with the LXX Interpreters, 'chiefly and principally'; or with Jerome, 'in the beginning of time,' so that the beginnings of the New Testament are designated. By Tarshish they understand Cilicia, and by synecdoche, nations across the sea (and interpreters observe that ships are taken metonymically for nations). Cyril [understands it] of the Indians. Divine scripture often calls the Indians THARSIS. And they narrate that there is a famous city of Tarshish in Cyprus. Wherefore, because the islands, he says, and those who come from the region of the Indians, have sustained me, that is, have submitted to the yoke imposed by me; therefore the multitude of believers flows together from everywhere. For men not a few come even from the barbarian land itself, bearing the name of Christ, and bearing fruit to his glory, whatever region can produce them. And they say that the land itself is fertile in gold and silver. But they do not offer according to the old custom and institution, to certain inanimate Idols, and to flocks of demons: but because they held the name of the Lord as holy among them, and the Holy One of Israel as glorious. But there is not another Lord, and again another Holy One of Israel, but one and the same exists as Lord, and Holy, and glorified. It must be known, however, that cities which are in the circuit, vast and wandering for the most part and uninhabited, are also called islands. But if those also are said to sustain the Lord, that is, to serve him: you will understand those who inhabit regions and cities that are inaccessible and horrible in great solitude, as coming through faith and bearing fruit for Christ in gold and silver, and not simply that material for him, but as it were what is precious and illustrious in us and to be highly valued, namely faith, the splendor of all virtues. For these are gifts to God, these are the votive offerings of spiritual worship, and illustrious and admirable donations. It is also written in the book of Psalms concerning Christ, the Savior of us all: The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall bring presents: the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts: And all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him. As for the GOLD which is said to be brought with them, that, according to Calvin himself as interpreter, is a repetition of what he had said before, that the nations would come into obedience to God in such a way that they would offer themselves and all their possessions to Him. We observe this against Musculus, who, as in most other prophecies of Isaiah, sides here with the Jews and Grotius. Many other Reformed theologians have also followed Calvin, and especially the recent Dutch interpreters, who have explained these things not only with Calvin concerning the conversion of the nations, but the whole of that chapter with us concerning the magnificence and amplitude of the Church of Christ. That which is brought forward from Ezra 1:6 concerning the liberality bestowed upon the Jews is too meager. For the things promised here to the Church are far more ample.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ME ENIM INSULÆ EXSPECTANT] Ad meum nutum attentæ sunt gentes illæ fluminibus adsitæ. ET NAVES MARIS IN PRINCIPIO, UT AD- DUCAM FILIOS TUOS DE LONGE] id est, an- te omnia paratæ sunt naves in mari Persico, quæ Judæos deducant.

ARGENTUM EORUM ET AURUM EORUM CUM EIS] Multi liberalitate sua vos juvabunt, ob Dei reverentiam. Esdræ 1, 6.

Iterum in alienum & hactenus inauditum sen- sum detorquentur Prophetæ verba: non enim de Judæis velociter in Patriam redeuntibus; sed de gen- tibus mira festinatione ad Ecclesiam properantibus hic sermo est. Subjectum, vel illos qui adventuri sint, luculentissime definiverat, gentes & populos, quos hactenus à copia & varietate descripsit: jam vero à celeritate ac promptitudine aggregationis ad Ecclesiam & cultus atq; submissionis depingit, sub similitudine NUBIUM & COLUMBARUM ad columbaria sua velociter advolantium. Quæ quin- ta nobis ratio erit, nam illi advolare dicuntur, de quibus (1.) hactenus egit, eorum ad Ecclesiam ad- ventum variis modis describendo, (2.) ad quos spectant INSULÆ, Dominum expectantes (3.) quos dixit, aurum suum & alia dona collaturos, & consecraturos Domino: siquidem iterum hic de ea vaticinetur: ARGENTUM EORUM ET AURUM EORUM CUM EIS. Hæc de uno eodemque subjecto loqui, nimis profecto manife- stum est. Grotius vero, ausu plusquam Rabbini- co, hæc discerpit: & partem eorum ad Judæos de- torquet redeuntes in patriam, partem ad gentes ex- spectantes, ut eodem traducantur, & promptas, ut ipsos liberalitate sua juvent. Quæ vero detestanda est de- pravatio, ne inter Judæos quidem audita. QUI SUNT ISTI, QUI UT NUBES VOLANT? quærit Propheta, vel etiam Ecclesia cum admi- ratione, ubi videt tantam copiam tanto impetu ferri & properare ad cognoscendam Evangelii do- ctrinam divino excitatam spiritu, sicut nubes vento impulsæ ab Occidente in Orientem rapiuntur, & sicut columbæ una conglobatæ magno impetu ruunt in fene- stras, seu ostiola columbarii sui: Respondet Chri- stus, cui etiam priora verba ζητήματῶ tribuunt nonnulli: INSULÆ ME EXPECTANT ET NAVES MARIS A PRINCIPIO. Ad quæ Brentius: Per insulas generaliter intelliguntur O- mnes gentes, quæ Judæis sunt ad Occidentem, sive in mari sive ultra mare habitent. Nam quo tempore Esaias concionatus est in urbe Hierusalem, erant Israë- litis quædam tantum Insulæ maris notæ, non autem gentes ultra mare, quippe quod hæ adhuc obscuriores essent, quam ut fama earum tam late fuisset sparsa, cum & Roma ipsa cœperit primum condi Ezechie temporibus. Quod autem dicit: A principio, vel respicit in illud Psalmi 71. Reges Tharsis seu Maris & insulæ munera offerent, Reges Arabum & Saba dona adducent. At adorabunt eum omnes Re- ges, omnes gentes servient ei. Itaq́; hic sensus erit: Non jam primum de gentibus dicitur, quod sint Evangelio meo credituræ, sed jam olim, à principio regni Israëlitiçi, per Davidem dictum est, quod in- sulæ seu gentes & reges eorum sint accessuri ad me- am Ecclesiam, & eam quoquo modo possint adju- turi. Vel respicit in illud, quod 2. Par. 9. scriptum est, Legatos diversarum gentium, & omnes Reges Ara- biæ, & Satrapas terrarum comportasse aurum & ar- gentum Salomoni. Et additur postea: Naves Regis ibant in Tharsis seu Mare cum servis Hiram semel in annis tribus, & deferebant inde aurum, argen- tum, ebur, Simias & Pavones. Itaq́, hic erit sensus: A principio quidem, cum regnum Israëlis confirma- tum esset in manu Salomonis, detulerunt Salomo- ni munera non solum finitimi Reges, verum etiam Insulæ gentium. Et quemadmodum tunc addu- xerunt in navibus Simias & Pavones, ita nunc adducent filios seu cives tuos, ô Hierusalem, de longe, & una cum ipsis etiam aurum & argentum eorum nomini Domini Dei tui, & Sancto Israëlis, qui & te hac gloria & magnificentia ornat. Hæc o- mnia etsi ita recitantur, perinde ac si gentes allaturæ essent in navibus externum aurum ad urbem Hierusa- lem, quemadmodum factum est temporibus Salomo- nis, tamen quia agitur de vocatione gentium ad fi- dem in Christum, per Evangelion ejus, idcirco sic in- telligenda sunt, quemadmodum res ipsa interpreta- tur, videlicet, quod gentes excitatæ per Evangelion, credent in Christum, & fient cives spirituales urbis Hierusalem, quæ est Ecclesia, ac conferent opes suas ad juvandam Ecclesiam, & conservandum ministe- rium Ecclesiæ, quod est prædicatio Evangelii Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Illud בראשנה in Principio Sanctius de loco explicat, Qui habitant in Princi- pio, h. e. in oriente, alii cum LXX. Interpp. præci- pue & principaliter; vel cum Hieronymo in princi- pio temporis, ut primordia designentur Novi Te- stamenti. Per Tharsis Ciliciam & per Synecdochen transmarinas gentes intelligunt (navesq́; pro genti- bus accipi metonymice observant Interpp.) Cyril- lus de Indicis. THARSIS vero divina scriptura sæpe vocat Indicas. Narrantq́; in Cypro Tharsis ci- vitatem esse celebrem. Quapropter quia Insulæ, inquit, & qui ex Indorum regione veniunt, me su- stinuerunt, id est, impositum a me sibi jugum subie- runt; Idcirco undicunq́; confluit multitudo creden- tium. Veniunt enim & ex ipsa barbara terra viri non pauci, Christi nomen gerentes, & fructificantes in ejus gloriam, quæcunque regio ferre potest illorum. Auri autem & argenti fertilem ipsam esse dicunt. Of- ferunt vero non more institutoq́; veteri, inanimis qui- busdam Idolis, & dæmoniorum gregibus: sed quia sanctum habebant apud eos nomen Domini, & glorio- sus Sanctus Israël. Sed non est alius Dominus, alius rursum Sanctus Israël, sed unus & idem existit Do- minus, & Sanctus, & glorificatus. Sciendum est au- tem, insulas vocari etiam, civitates quæ per circui- tum sunt, vastæ & vagæ magna ex parte & non ha- bitatæ. Quod si dicantur illæ quoque sustinere Domi- num, id est, ei servire: intelliges eos, qui in accessas, & magna solitudine horridas regiones & urbes inhabi- tant, venturos per fidem & fructificaturos Christo au- rum & argentum, & non simpliciter ei illam mate- riam, sed veluti quæ in nobis sunt pretiosa & illustria & magni facienda, fidem scilicet, omnium virtutum splendorem. Hæc enim sunt Deo Xenia, hæc spiri- tualis cultus anathemata, & donaria illustria & ad- miranda. Scriptum est etiam in libro Psalmorum de omnium nostrum Servatore Christo: Reges Thar- sis & Insulæ dona adducent: Reges Arabum & Sabba dona afferent: Et adorabunt eum omnes reges terræ, omnes reges servient ei. Quod AURUM cum ipsis adferendum dicitur, id interprete Calvi- no ipso, repetitio est ejus, quod ante dixerat, sic venturas gentes in obsequium Deo, ut se ac sua o- mnia ipsi offerant. Quod contra Musculum, qui ut in plerisque aliis Esaiæ vaticiniis cum Judæis & Gro- tio hic facit, observamus. Calvinum etiam sequuti sunt alii plerique Reformati, ac imprimis Belgici Interpp. nuperi, qui hæc non tantum cum Calvino de conversione gentium, sed totum istud caput no- biscum de Ecclesiæ Christi magnificentia & amplitu- dine exposuêre. Nimis exile est quod de liberalita- te in Judæos collata ex Esdr. 1,6. affertur. Nam longe ampliora sunt, quæ Ecclesiæ hic promittuntur.

## 60:10
Verse 10.

AND THE SONS OF STRANGERS SHALL BUILD THY WALLS] Many proselytes will be helpers for the restoration of the temple and the city.

AND THEIR KINGS SHALL MINISTER UNTO THEE] παραστήσονταί σοι. They shall supply you with necessary things. See Ezra 1:8, 6:8, 9, 10. Therefore, he understands these things merely and only concerning the building of the temple and the city with the Jews. But we establish the sixth argument here, from the Majesty of Jerusalem. For the second temple, or the restored city, by no means attained the glory and magnificence which is promised here. The discourse here is not about a few proselytes who perhaps were present at the repair of the city, but about the sons of foreigners; not about the kings of proselytes, but about foreign kings: by which name all the sons of strangers and kings are designated, who were to contribute their ἐπιβάλλων μέρος [allotted share] to the building of the Church. And that not only those few are noted, but that some universality has a place here, what follows thereafter convinces. For the nation and kingdom that has not served you will perish. Which in no way fits the time of the rebuilt city. We argue, therefore, in this way: The prophecy here is about such a structure that, first, is sufficient for the multitude of nations, which the Prophet said would flow into it; second, which is to be carried out by the sons of foreigners, and to which various foreign kings will contribute much, indeed, nations and kingdoms will be bound to contribute, unless they are to perish. All these things are rightly said of the spiritual Jerusalem. Concerning that earthly city and material temple, all things can be said less correctly. Jerome deduces our sense concerning the spiritual Jerusalem, the Church of Christ, from the context: The Church marvels at the crowd of nations gathered first from the people of the circumcision, flying to her from the whole world: And having taken other gifts of the Holy Spirit, they hasten, according to Symmachus and Theodotion, to her windows, so that they may enter the Church: Or teachers with disciples, that is, doves with their young, flying to the Church from the Islands of the nations which, according to the prophecies of the Prophets, will wait for the Lord. Ships also of תרשיש [Tarshish], that is, of the sea: of which we spoke more fully in the vision of Tyre, will bring the sons of the Church in the beginning of the faith, carrying gold and silver. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Concerning which gold and silver it is written in the 67th Psalm, The wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold. And in the 71st Psalm. The kings of Tarshish and the isles will offer gifts: the kings of Arabia and Saba will bring presents. All of which are brought to the name of the Lord God and to the Holy One of Israel, who has glorified him. AND THEY SHALL BUILD &c. Among other things by which the Church is enriched, and the city of the Savior is built, foreigners also and the sons of strangers build its walls, so that the enemy may not be able to enter, nor perfidy find a place. But foreigners and strangers properly signify the people of the nations, who truly built the Church of Christ to such an extent that their kings and princes minister to, or assist, her. To whom Cyril is the ὁμόψηφος [of one mind] in the Greek Church: For the walls and fortifications, which keep the children of the Church, can be understood as right and irreprehensible faith, and the splendor of works, adorned with all the beauty of virtues. Moreover, the instructors of dogmatic and moral knowledge, and thus the teachers of divine proclamations, can be all the ministers, whoever are called to this by divine reckoning. And indeed the first fruits of this sacred preaching were the divine disciples for us, and many after them, who followed in their footsteps in preaching the word, not only from the Jews, but also from the ranks of the Greeks, who, instructed in secular wisdom and endowed with the faculty of speaking, turned out to be excellent instructors, elegantly building the firm word of faith in the souls of the initiated, and instilling in them an admirable conscience of living well. Therefore, they were foreigners, because they were not of the blood of Israel, as far as the flesh is concerned: yet they were wise architects, as the divine Paul speaks, and who rightly knew how to found Christ in us, namely through faith and the instruction of good things. These, I think, are: Foreigners shall build your walls, and their kings shall assist you. Whose kings? Undoubtedly those of the foreigners. And he says kings here, or princes and leaders of the peoples, who sit by the Church of Christ, fortifying her as if with a bodyguard, and protecting her children as if with a shield, and repelling every attack of enemies, as well those who are visible as those who are invisible: or certainly, those adorned with the highest honors, and holding the royal scepter, who also assist the Church. Assistance in this place signifies obedience. For they yield to the divine and sacrosanct prophecies, and hold the preaching of the Church in the highest esteem. By the sons of FOREIGNERS, who build, are rightly understood those who will arise from the nations as spiritual architects, Doctors of the Church: By the Kings of those nations, however, the Emperors, Kings, Princes, and highest heads, whose work, protection, guardianship, and munificence the work of the spiritual building of the Church succeeded, and who apply themselves to the end that the true Church may be propagated, and the doctrine of the Gospel be preserved in it. Concerning which spiritual building see Isa. 54, Matt. 16, 1 Cor. 3, etc.

Verse of the same.

FOR IN MY INDIGNATION I STRUCK YOU, AND IN MY RECONCILIATION I HAVE HAD MERCY ON YOU] Just as I afflicted you while gravely angry, so I will restore and adorn you, having had the greatest mercy on you.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET ÆDIFICABUNT FILII PEREGRINORUM MUROS TUOS] Proselyti multi adjutores erunt ad instau- randum templum & urbem.

ET REGES EORUM MINISTRABUNT TIBI] παραστήσονταί σοι. Suppeditabunt tibi necessaria. Vide Esdr. 1,8. 6, 8.9. 10. Hæc ergo nude tantum de ædificatione templi & urbis cum Judæis intelligit. Sed nos hic sextum argumentum figimus, à Majestate Hierosolymæ. Gloriam enim & magnificentiam, quæ hic promif- sa est, minime affequutum est templum secundum, aut urbs restaurata. Non hic de proselytis pauculis, qui forte reparationi urbis adfuerunt, sed de filiis peregrinorum; non de regibus proselytorum, sed Regi- bus alienigenis sermo est: quo nomine quicunque alienorum filii, & Reges designantur, qui suum ἐπι- βάλλων μέρος collaturi erant ad ædificandam Ec- clesiam. Nec tantum paucos illos notari, sed ali- quam hic universalitatem locum habere, quæ dein- de sequuntur convincunt. Gens enim & regnum quod non servivit tibi, peribit. Quod tempori reædifi- catæ urbis nullatenus convenit. Arguimus ergo hoc modo: De tali structura hic vaticinium est, quæ primo sufficiat multitudini gentium, quas eo confluxuras dixit Propheta; deinde, quæ à filiis a- lienorum peragenda, & ad quam multum conferent varii Reges exteri, imo conferre tenebuntur gen- tes, & regna, nisi pereundum ipsis sit. Hæc recte de spirituali Hierosolyma dicuntur omnia. De ter- rena illa urbe & templo materiali omnia minus re- cte dici possunt. Sensum nostrum de spirituali Hie- rosolyma, Ecclesia Christi è contextu deducit Hie- ronymus: Miratur Ecclesia de circumcisionis pri- mum populo congregata, volare ad se gentium turbam è toto orbe terrarum: Et assumptis aliis Spiritus San- cti festinare, juxta Symmachum & Theodotionem, ad fenestras suas, ut ingrediantur Ecclesiam: Sive doctores cum discipulis, id est, columbas cum pullis suis volare ad Ecclesiam de Insulis gentium quæ jux- ta vaticinia Prophetarum expectabunt Dominum. Naves quoq́; תרשיש id est, maris: de quibus in vi- sione Tyri plenius diximus, adducent filios Ecclesiæ in principio fidei, aurum argentumq́; portantes. Cor- de enim creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem. De quo auro & argento in 67. Psalmo scriptum est, Pennæ columbæ deargentatæ, & po- steriora ejus in fulgore auri. Et 71. Psalmo. Re- ges Tharsis & insulæ munera offerent: reges A- rabum & Saba dona adducent. Quæ omnia defe- runtur nomini Domini Dei & Sancto Israëlï, qui glorificavit eum. ET ÆDIFICABUNT &c. Inter cætera quibus ditatur Ecclesia, & urbs Salvatoris ex- truitur, alienigenæ quoq́; & filii peregrinorum ædifi- cant muros ejus, ne hostis possit intrare, nec locum in- venire perfidia. Alienigenæ autem & peregrini, proprie significant populum nationum, qui vere ex- truxerunt Ecclesiam Christi in tantum ut reges eorum & principes ministrent, sive assistant ei. Cui ὁμό- ψηφος in Græca Ecclesia est Cyrillus: Muri enim & munimenta, quæ Ecclesiæ liberos servant, intelligi possunt, fides recta & irreprehensibilis, & operum splendor, omni virtutum pulchritudine decoratus. Præceptores autem cognitionis dogmaticæ & moralis, adeoque doctores divinorum præconiorum, esse pos- sunt ministri omnes, quicunque calculo divino ad hoc vocantur. Et primitiæ quidem hujus sacræ prædi- cationis extiterunt nobis divini discipuli, & complures post illos, qui in sermone prædicando sequuti sunt eorum vestigia, non solum ex Judæis, sed & ex Græco- rum ordinibus, qui seculari instructi sapientia & di- cendi facultate præditi, optimi institutores evaserunt, firmum sermonem fidei ædificantes eleganter in ani- mis initiatorum, & inferentes in illis bene vivendi admirabilem conscientiam. Alienigenæ igitur fue- runt, quia non erant ex sanguine Israël, quod ad car- nem attinet: architecti tamen sapientes, ut divinus Paulus loquitur, quique recte norant in nobis Chri- stum fundare, per fidem videlicet, & rerum bonarum institutionem. Hos, opinor, est: Ædificabunt alie- nigenæ muros tuos, & reges eorum assistent tibi. Quorum reges? nimirum alienigenorum. Et re- ges hic dicit, vel principes & duces populorum, qui assidunt Ecclesiæ Christi, satellitio munientes velut eam, & liberos ejus tanquam scuto protegentes, ac omnem hostium impetum propellentes, tam qui aspe- ctabiles sunt, quam qui inaspectabiles: aut certe, summis ornatos honoribus, & regium sceptrum ha- bentes, qui etiam Ecclesiæ assistunt. Assistentia hoc in loco significat obedientiam. Cedunt enim divinis & sacrosanctis vaticiniis, atque prædicationem Ec- clesiæ summo in pretio habent. Per filios ALIENO- RUM, qui ædificant, recte intelliguntur, qui ex gentibus orientur architecti spirituales, Do- ctores Ecclesiæ: Per Reges autem earum gentium Imperatores, Reges, Principes & capita summa, quorum opera, præsidio, tutela & munificentia opus spiritualis ædificationis Ecclesiæ successit, & qui in id incumbunt, ut vera Ecclesia propagetur, & doctrina Evangelii in eadem conservetur. De quo spirituali ædificio Esa. 54. Matth. 16. 1. Cor. 3. &c.

Vers. eod.

IN INDIGNATIONE ENIM MEA PERCUSSI TE, ET IN RECONCILIATIONE MEA MISERTUS SUM TUI] Sicut graviter iratus te afflixi, ita summe tui misertus te restituam & ornabo.

## 60:11
Verse 11.

AND YOUR GATES SHALL BE OPENED CONTINUALLY: THEY SHALL NOT BE SHUT DAY OR NIGHT] As is accustomed to happen in deep peace. See Luke 21:37, John 18:1. THAT THE STRENGTH OF THE NATIONS MAY BE BROUGHT TO YOU] That is, wealth, namely that which was gained by the Jews in war. See 1 Macc. 4:23. AND THEIR KINGS MAY BE BROUGHT] Namely, captured in war; and by kings, understand any leaders whatsoever, according to the Hebrew manner of speaking.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET APERIENTUR PORTÆ TUÆ JUGITER: DIE ET NOCTE NON CLAUDENTUR] Ut in alta pace fieri solet. Vide Luc. 21, 37, Joh. 18, 1. UT AFFERATUR AD TE FORTITUDO GEN- TIUM] Id est, opes, bello scil. Judæis partæ. Vid. 1. Macc. 4, 23. ET REGES EARUM ADDUCANTUR] Nempe bello capti; & per reges, duces quosvis intellige, more loquendi Hebræo.

## 60:12
Verse 12.

FOR THE NATION AND KINGDOM THAT WILL NOT SERVE THEE SHALL PERISH] If any city, attacked by you in a just war, has not come to terms, it shall suffer destruction, as happened to very many cities, the mention of which is in the aforementioned chapters of Josephus, and 1 Maccabees 5. Thus also Pella was overturned, because it had refused to accept the laws of the Jews. Josephus 13, 23.

Who does not see how meager these things are in such a magnificent and august promise? The discourse is not about external restoration, about temporal peace and security, about earthly riches, about leaders captured in war, or cities overturned by the Jews; if prosperity were to be placed in these things, such as the Holy Scripture promises here, since misfortunes and calamities, which followed immediately after, far exceed that external happiness, how does the outcome correspond to such great promises? The Prophet surely promises here more august things to the Church than those which are to be defined by that external prosperity of a short time. Even more ample things, indeed extending themselves throughout the whole world, are promised; therefore, destruction is announced to all nations and kingdoms which have not served the city of the Lord. Wherefore the notable happiness of Jerusalem provides the seventh argument, which is described here in such a way that it is wrongly distorted toward earthly and temporary prosperity. Therefore, regarding those words, IN MY INDIGNATION I HAVE STRUCK THEE, the blessed Brentius rightly advised that in hearing this sermon of Isaiah, we must consider that Isaiah did not come forward among the citizens of the city of Jerusalem under Ahaz or Hezekiah, but under Herod, with Christ already born, and recited this sermon. Therefore, Cornelius à Lapide says these things thus: IN MY INDIGNATION I HAVE STRUCK THEE, O Jerusalem, namely, by leaving you impious before Christ, without Prophets, and by handing you over to the impious Scribes and Pharisees, and at length to Titus and the Romans for destruction; but through Christ I have been reconciled, and I have had pity on you, and I have restored your ruins, and I have supplied through the strength and abundance of the Gentiles, whom I have joined to you and gathered into the Church as follows. He alludes to the punishment of the Babylonian captivity, and from it the liberation and reconciliation. But even if some regard is had for the Babylonian captivity, the grace, however, which is promised, is by no means to be determined by the boundaries of the repaired city, but is to be explained according to the guidance of Jerome: or certainly this must be said, (so his words have it) that he reconciles to himself that which was once afflicted and delivered to captivity in the calling of the Gentiles, so that its gates may always be open, and be closed neither by day nor by night, and may be continually accessible to those desiring to be saved, etc. Nor indeed is only earthly peace promised, but if those words about the open gates are referred to peace, spiritual tranquility, peace, and security are primarily designated, which will be obtained perfect and consummated in the other life in the heavenly Jerusalem; whence this prophecy concerning the same is explained by reason of its plenary fulfillment in Apoc. 21, 25. Others refer it to easy reception, that the Church excludes no one, and grants access to all. Which Cyril joined in this place. It seems by these words to promise them peace and the tranquility which proceeds from it. For cities that suspect there will be some impression of enemies do not always have their gates open, unless when time and necessity so dictate, and that scarcely by day without fear. But those which have been freed from that fear, and do not expect that they will suffer anything of the kind, open them to those entering, and some even do this at night. If therefore God promises them peace and most ample happiness: certainly there will be a continuous concourse of those arriving and as it were a perpetual entry of those who are drawn in a certain way through faith to the acknowledgment of Christ, so that the gates seem to be thrown open, and there is no time when it is necessary for them to be closed, not only to those who are of low and humble fortune, and obey the yoke of the kingdom, but to those who have authority over all. And the added reason confirms this sense: THAT THE STRENGTH OF THE GENTILES MAY BE BROUGHT TO THEE. i.e., the gates will therefore always be open, so that when a great force, a great multitude of Gentiles, together with their Kings, are brought, they may find the gate open at any time, and be received with open doors. It is therefore manifest that the discourse here is not about the external city of Jerusalem, but about the spiritual one, which began to be built up in that external one on the day of Pentecost through the Gospel, whose gates are always open, both because the Gospel began to be spread from the city of Jerusalem to the whole world, and receives any men, whether circumcised or uncircumcised, whether rich or poor, whether honest or dishonest, to repentance and the communion of all heavenly goods Joh. 6, 37. Rom. 10. v. 12. 13. and also because the return is in turn open, if anyone after the first reception has become a deserter, and desires to be received in turn, so that he may be restored to the former right of the city. For to this use the gates of the Church are always open, so that the sinner, at whatever time he has performed repentance, may be admitted and received with open arms Luc. 15. Of bringing wealth obtained in war there is nothing here, nor is it necessary for that reason that the gates of Jerusalem be open night and day. Grotius dreams with the Jews everywhere of merely carnal things, temporal happiness, earthly wealth, and victories, which dreams have resulted for the Jews in their expecting at length none but an earthly Messiah. And how can the Jews boast that every nation, every kingdom, which was attacked by them in a just war, did not come to terms, but suffered destruction: although there is no word here about a nation attacked in a just war not accepting terms, but these are mere arbitrary glosses, and private interpretations and ones entirely alien. For what do war or terms have to do with these things which the Prophet hands down? This servitude and obedience, however, as Brentius rightly says, according to the consensus of Christian Interpreters, is not to be understood of bodily servitude, such as is in worldly kingdoms and cities, but of spiritual, such as befits the Kingdom of Christ. For nations and Kingdoms are then said to serve the city of Jerusalem or the Church, when they open their gates to the Gospel of Christ, and permit the Gospel a free course in their regions, and assist pious doctrine, so that it may not only be preserved in the present Church, but also propagated to posterity; for to this use especially have worldly kingdoms been established, so that with political peace and tranquility preserved, the kingdom of Christ may be advanced. And now, he says, understand, O Kings, be instructed, you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear, etc. If, however, kingdoms and nations not only do not permit the Gospel of Christ its course; but even impede it in whatever way they can, and persecute it, nothing else remains but that they are either changed, or cast down, or perish, even if for some time they seem to flourish happily. Furthermore, Kingdoms and nations are said to serve the city of Jerusalem, when they not only publicly give place to the Gospel of Christ, but also privately acknowledge through faith this Gospel, which was first of all revealed in the city of Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost and confirmed by great miracles. Go, he says, preach the Gospel to every creature. He who has believed the Gospel will be saved. But he who has not believed will be condemned. And again, God did not send his Son into the world, that he might condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him. He who believes in him is not condemned. But he who does not believe is already condemned, because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten son of God. This latter, He who does not believe is already condemned, is clearly what the Prophet says: The nation and Kingdom that will not serve thee will perish, and the nations, to wit, which will not have served thee, will be laid waste by solitude.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

GENS ENIM ET REGNUM QUOD NON SERVIERIT TIBI PERIBIT] Si qua civitas à vobis bel- lo justo impetita, ad conditiones non venerit, ea exci- dium feret, ut evenit plurimis civitatibus, quarum men- tio apud Josephum dictis capitibus, & 1. Macc. 5. Sic & Pella subversa, quod leges Judæorum suscipere noluisset. Josephus 13, 23.

Quis non videt, quam exilia hæc sint in tam ma- gnifica & augusta promissione? Non de externa restitutione, de temporali pace, & securitate, de opibus terrenis, de bello captis ducibus, aut eversis per Judæos civitatibus sermo est, in quibus rebus si prosperitas collocetur, qualem hic promittit S. S. quum his longe plura infortunia, & calamitates, quæ subinde sequutæ sunt, non parum illam exter- nam felicitatem superent, quomodo eventus tantis promissionibus respondit? Augustiora utique hic pollicetur Propheta Ecclesiæ, quam quæ ista tem- poris exigui externa prosperitate definienda sint. Ampliora etiam, imo per orbem universum sese extendentia promittuntur, ideo gentibus & regnis omnibus exitium indicitur, quæ non servierint civi- tati Domini. Quapropter septimum argumen- tum subministrat insignis Hierosolymæ felicitas, quæ hic ita describitur, ut ad terrenam & temporariam prosperitatem perperam detorqueatur. Quod ergo ad illa, IN INDIGNATIONE MEA PERCUSSI TE, recte monuit B. Brentius, quod in audienda hac concione Esaiæ cogitandum no- bis sit, Esaiam non sub Achazo, aut Ezechia, sed sub Herode, nato jam Christo in medium civium ur- bis Hierusalem processisse, & hanc concionem recitasse. Ideo hæc ita Cornelius à Lapide: IN INDI- GNATIONE MEA PERCUSSI TE, O Jeru- salem, scil. relinquendo te ante Christum impiam, sine Prophetis, tradendoq́; te impiis Scribis ac Pharisæis, at tandem Tito ac Romanis ad excidium; at per Chri- stum reconciliatus, & misertus sum tui, tuasq́; ruinas restauravi, & supplevi per fortitudinem ac copiam Gentium, quas tibi adjunxi & in Ecclesiam aggregavi ut sequitur. Alludit ad punitionem captivitatis Babylonicæ, ex eaǵ; liberationem & reconciliationem. Sed etiamsi respectus habeatur aliquis ad captivi- tatem Babylonicam, gratia tamen, quæ promitti- tur, neutiquam finibus reparatæ civitatis determi- nanda, sed secundum Hieronymi ductum explican- da erit: vel certe hoc dicendum, (ita habent verba ejus) quod afflictam quondam & captivitati traditam in vocatione gentium reconciliet sibi, ita ut portæ ejus semper apertæ sint, & nec die nec nocte claudantur, & salvari cupientibus jugiter pateant &c. Nec vero tantum pax terrena promittitur, sed si verba illa de portis apertis referantur ad pacem, spiritua- lis tranquillitas, pax & securitas imprimis designa- tur, quæ perfecta & consummata in altera vita ob- tinebitur in cælesti Hierosolyma; unde de eadem vaticinium hoc, ratione plenariæ impletionis expli- catur Apoc. 21, 25. Alii referunt ad facilem receptio- nem, quod neminem excludat, omnibus aditum concedat Ecclesia. Quæ conjunxit Cyrillus in h. l. Videtur his verbis pacem polliceri illis & tranquil- litatem, quæ inde provenit. Nam civitates, quæ ho- stium impressionem aliquam fore suspicantur, non semper apertas habent portas, nisi cum tempus ita fert & necessitas, idq́; vix interdiu sine metu. At quæ eo timore liberatæ sunt, nec passuras se quicquam tale ex- pectant, illas aperiunt ingredientibus, idque etiam quidam noctu faciunt. Si igitur pacem illis promit- tit Deus & amplissimam felicitatem: certe continuus erit adventantium concursus & veluti perpetuus in- gressus eorum, qui trahuntur quodammodo per fidem ad agnitionem Christi, ita ut patefactæ portæ esse videantur, & nullum tempus esse, quo eas claudi o- porteat, non his solum, qui demissæ & humilis fortunæ sunt, & jugo regni parent, sed illis, qui in omnes ha- bent imperium. Et addita ratio confirmat hunc sensum: UT AFFERATUR AD TE FOR- TITUDO GENTIUM. q. d. portæ idcirco semper patentes erunt, ut cum magna vis, magna multitudo gentium, una cum Regibus earum addu- centur, inveniant quovis tempore portam aper- tam, & excipiantur patentibus ostiis. Manifestum igitur est, quod non fiat hic sermo de externa urbe Hierosolyma, sed de spirituali, quæ in externa illa cepit in die Pentecostes per Evangelium extrui, cujus portæ patent semper, tum quia Evangelium cepit ab urbe Hierusalem vulgari in universum or- bem terræ, & recipit quosvis homines, sive circum- cisos sive incircumcisos, sive divites, sive pau- peres, sive honestos, sive inhonestos, ad pœ- nitentiam & communionem omnium cœlestium bonorum Joh. 6, 37. Rom. 10. v. 12. 13. tum quod reditus vicissim pateat, si quis post primam rece- ptionem transfuga factus fuerit, & recipi vicissim cupiat, ut priori civitatis juri restituatur. Nam in hunc usum patent semper portæ Ecclesiæ, ut pec- cator, quocunque tempore pœnitentiam egerit, admittatur & obviis ulnis excipiatur Luc. 15. De af- ferendis opibus bello partis hic nihil, nec ea de causa portæ Hierosolymæ ut noctu diuq; pateant, neces- sum est. Somniat Grotius cum Judæis ubivis mere carnalia, temporalem felicitatem, terrenas opes, & victorias, quæ somnia Judæis eo expedivêre, ut tandem non nisi terrenum Messiam expectarint. Et quomodo gloriari possunt Judæi gentem o- mnem, omne regnum, quod ab ipsis bello justo im- petitum, non venit ad conditiones, excidium tulisse: quanquam de gente bello justo impetita, conditio- nes non acceptante hic nullum verbum fiat, sed meræ arbitrariæ istæ glossæ sint, ac ἰπιλύσεις ἰδίαι exque prorsus alienæ. Quid enim ad hæc, quæ Pro- pheta tradit, bellum aut conditiones? Hæc autem servitus & obedientia, ut recte Brentius, ex consen- su Christianorum Interpretum, non est intelligen- da de corporali servitute, qualis est in mundanis regnis & civitatibus, sed de spirituali, qualis conve- nit Regno Christi. Gentes enim & Regna tunc di- cuntur servire urbi Hierusalem seu Ecclesiæ, cum aperiunt portas suas Evangelio Christi, & permit- tunt Evangelio liberum cursum in regionibus suis, & adjuvant piam doctrinam, ut non solum in præ- senti Ecclesia conservetur, sed etiam ad posteros propagetur; in hunc enim usum præcipue con- stituta sunt mundana regna, ut conservata politica pace ac tranquillitate regnum Christi proferatur. Et nunc, inquit, Reges intelligite, erudimini qui judi- catis terram. Servite Domino in timore &c. Si au- tem regna & gentes non solum non permittant Evangelio Christi suum cursum; verum etiam quo- quo modo possunt impediant, & persequantur, ni- hil aliud reliquum est, quam ut aut mutentur, aut dejiciantur, aut pereant, etiamsi aliquandiu felici- ter florere videantur. Deinde Regna & gentes di- cuntur servire urbi Hierusalem, cum non solum publice dant locum Evangelio Christi, verum etiam privatim agnoscunt per fidem hoc Evangelion, quod primum omnium in urbe Hierusalem in die Pentecostes revelatum & magnis miraculis confir- matum est. Ite, inquit, prædicate Evangelium u- niversæ creaturæ. Qui crediderit Evangelio, salvus erit. Qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur. Et iterum, non misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut condemnet mundum, sed ut servetur mundus per eum. Qui credit in eum, non condemnatur. Qui vero non credit jam condemnatus est, quia non credit in nomen unigeniti filii Dei. Hoc posterius, Qui non credit, jam condemnatus est, plane est, quod Propheta ait: Gens & Regnum, quod non servie- rit tibi peribit, & gentes, videlicèt, quæ non servie- rint tibi, solitudine vastabuntur.

## 60:13
Vers. 13.

THE GLORY OF LEBANON SHALL COME UNTO THEE] For Josephus also teaches us in the same place that many places of Syria were possessed by the Jews. Strabo, treating of the Jews: κέ τῆς Συρίας κατε- σρέφοντο κὰι τῆς Φοινίκης πολλήν. FIR AND BOX AND PINE] See above 41. v. 19. The Greeks here have cypress, pine, and cedar. TO BEAUTIFY THE PLACE OF MY SANCTIFICATION] To beautify the temple. AND I WILL GLORIFY THE PLACE OF MY FEET] Namely, from those trees of Lebanon. The place of the feet is the Ark, 1 Chron. 28, 2, and by synecdoche, the Temple itself.

By the glory of Lebanon are not denoted some obscure places of Syria, but these, as those things which are added concerning the trees for beautifying the place of the sanctification of the Lord teach, and as Grotius himself has admitted, that from those trees of Lebanon the place of the feet of the Lord would be glorified, pertain to the sacred structure. And therefore the Eighth Argument is suggested to us from the magnificence of the spiritual edifice. For the thing itself testifies that such glory as is here predicted did not happen to the second temple. For the glory of the other temple did not approach the glory of the former, if you consider the external appearance; nor was it placed for the PRIDE OF AGES, nor did gold fall to it for brass, silver for iron, or brass for wood, iron for stones, which it is manifest must be taken spiritually. Which Calvin also acknowledged, although he thought Cyrus was referred to in the tenth verse. Again, he says at v. 13, Isaiah uses the metaphor which he used before, while he compares the Church of God to a building or a city prepared. For he recites those things which are necessary for building: namely, the fir, the pine, and the box tree, which were born in Lebanon, which forest we know to have been clothed with excellent trees. Whatever, therefore, was excellent or exquisite in it, signifies that it will be brought into the Church. But from these figures, one must hold to the anagoge toward the spiritual worship of God. For the Lord adorns his Church with the title of sanctuary, because he resides in the midst of it. He always alludes, however, to the temple, so that he may accommodate himself to the time and the customary manner. He proposes to us, therefore, the model of the temple which existed at Jerusalem, so that under its image we may consider the spiritual temple, of which we are the living stones and living material. Now by THE PLACE OF MY FEET he signifies that he so resides in the temple that his majesty is not, however, enclosed within it; for he is not contained in so narrow a place. Therefore, only the feet and as it were the lowest part are there, so that we may ascend into heaven, and not remain in these external signs, by which we are instructed according to our capacity. This is what he says, whom the others follow, if you perhaps except one Musculus, who preferred to adhere to the Jews. We easily admit that an allusion is made to the material temple, but to the Solomonic temple, whose glory was obscure to no one. But what the Prophet intends by that allusion, B. Brentius has explained very well. The commendation of the city, he says, or of the temple of Jerusalem, that is, of the Church, is from the magnificence of the building. The glory, he says, of Lebanon, that is, the Cedars: for these are the glory of Lebanon, and they make Mount Lebanon glorious, will come to you. There will be brought to you from Lebanon the Cedars, likewise the Firs, the Pine, and the Box tree, so that from these the place of my sanctification, and of my feet (which place is the temple, in which I stand with my feet, or in which I walk and dwell) may be built, adorned, and glorified. He alludes, however, to that which is written concerning the construction of the Jerusalem temple in 3 Kings 5, and 2 Chronicles 2. For thus Solomon writes to Hiram, King of Tyre: I will build a house to the name of my God. Send me, therefore, cedar wood, and arcenthine (or fir), and pine, etc. But since in this passage of Isaiah the discourse is about the spiritual temple, it must be considered that just as that corporal temple of Solomon had its stones and wood, from which it was constructed, so also this spiritual temple of ours, which is the Church of Christ, has its stones, but living ones, and wood, but animated. You yourselves as living stones, says Peter, be built up, a spiritual house, etc. But as far as the wood or trees are concerned, behold the tallest Cedar is Peter, the tallest Cedar is Paul: the tallest Cedars are the remaining Apostles, who are the columns of the Church. Thus also other ministers and members of the Church are the fir, the pine, and the box tree, from which the building of the spiritual temple is completed. Some of these are illustrious for miracles and other spiritual gifts, others are distinguished by power, wisdom, and the other endowments of this age, such as Kings, Princes, and learned men, who after the spreading of the Gospel came through faith to the Church of Christ. With which Cyril's ἔκθεσις agrees. AND THE GLORY OF LEBANON SHALL COME TO THEE, IN THE CYPRESS AND THE PINE AND THE CEDAR, THAT MY HOLY PLACE MAY BE GLORIFIED. Lebanon is a mountain of Phoenicia, dense with cedars, cypresses, and pine, and with the very trees of incense. For this reason, this mountain which we have mentioned is held in admiration, as one which has the greatest abundance of wood, and abounds in the tallest and most fragrant trees. This glory, therefore, he says, will be given to you, intelligibly, that is, and spiritually. For the Church of Christ nourishes many and illustrious heads of saints, both sublime in virtue and most fragrant. For they breathe Christ sweetly. This also is present with them, that they are not subject to the corruption of carnal affections, just as the pine and the Cedar are not corrupted. Divinely inspired Scripture is accustomed to liken the multitude of the saints to such trees. For God said again by the voice of Isaiah: And I will produce water in the wilderness, and rivers in a place lacking water: I will place in the land lacking water the box tree, the cedar, the myrtle, the cypress, and the poplar. For he compares the nations to a land that is arid and lacking water. For there was no divine discourse among them, which can vivify, and lead to the growth of piety and an increase in the knowledge of God. But there were among them the Cedar and the box tree and the myrtle and the cypress and the poplar, that is, trees well-grown and wonderful. Of which the divine Psalmist also makes mention, saying: Bread strengthens the heart of man: the trees of the field shall be filled, and the Cedars of Lebanon, which you have planted. For as the most wise Paul writes: We are God's husbandry. This glory of Lebanon, therefore, he says, will be given to you, that is, you will flourish, filled with many and admirable heads of saints. But this will be, so that my holy place may be decorated. For the ornament of the Churches are those who have ascended to the height of virtues, and who have nothing earthly and humble in their mind, nor do they savor the things of the flesh: but who seek the high, and savor the things that are above, and as it were depart from the earth, and walk in the heavens, having their conversation in the heavens.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

GLORIA LIBANI AD TE VENIET] Nam & Syriæ loca multa possessa ab Judæis docet nos Josephus eo- dem loco. Strabo de Judæis agentes: κέ τῆς Συρίας κατε- σρέφοντο κὰι τῆς Φοινίκης πολλήν. ABIES ET BUXUS ET BINUS] Vide supra 41. v. 19. Græci hic habent cupressum, pinum & cedrum. AD ORNANDUM LOCUM SANCTIFICATIO- NIS MEÆ] Ad ornandum templum. ET LOCUM PEDUM MEORUM GLORIFI- CABO] Ex illis scilicet Libani arboribus. Locus pedum est Arca. 1. Paral. 28, 2. & per συνεκδοχὴν ipsum Templum.

Per gloriam Libani non notantur obscura aliqua Syriæ loca, sed hæc, uti quæ de arboribus ad ornandum locum sanctificationis Domini ad- duntur, docent, ac Grotius ipse fassus est, ex illis Li- bani arboribus locum pedum Domini glorifica- tum iri, ad structuram sacram pertinent. Ideoque Octavum Argumentum à magnificentia spiritualis æ- dificii nobis suggeritur. Nam eam gloriam se- cundo templo non contigisse, quanta hic prædi- citur, res ipsa testatur. Non enim accessit alterius templi gloria ad gloriam prioris, si externam spe- ciem consideres; neque in SUPERBIAM SECU- LORUM positum est, nec pro ære aurum, pro ferro argentum eidem obtigit, aut pro lignis æs, pro lapidi- bus ferrum, quæ spiritualiter accipienda esse, mani- festum est. Quod agnovit etiam Calvinus, etsi versu decimo Cyrum respici putarit. Iterum, in- quit ad v. 13. usurpat Esaias metaphoram, qua prius usus est, dum Ecclesiam Dei ædificio aut civitati com- paravit. Ea enim recitat, quæ ad ædificandum ne- cessaria sunt: abietem scilicet, pinum, buxum quæ in Libano nascebantur, quam silvam eximiis arboribus convestitam fuisse scimus. Quicquid ergo excellens aut exquisitum in eâ fuerit, in Ecclesiam invectum iri significat. Sed ab his figuris tenenda est anagoge ad spiritualem Dei cultum. Nam sanctuarii titulo or- nat Dominus Ecclesiam suam, quia in medio ejus re- sidet. Semper tamen alludit ad templum, ut se tem- pori & mori usitato accommodet. Exemplar ergo tem- pli, quod Jerosolymis extabat, nobis proponit, ut sub ejus imagine consideremus templum spirituale, cujus vivi lapides vivaq́; materia sumus Jam per LO- CUM PEDUM significat, se ita residere in templo, ut tamen majestas ejus in eo inclusa non sit; nec e- nim tam angusto in loco continetur. Pedes igitur tantum ac velut infimam partem illic esse, ut con- scendamus in cælum, nec in externis hisce signis hæ- reamus, quibus pro modulo nostro erudimur. Hæc ille, quem cæteri sequuntur, si unum forte Muscu- lum excipias, qui Judæis adhærere maluit. Allu- sionem fieri ad templum materiale, facile admitti- mus, sed ad templum Salomoneum, cujus gloria nemini obscura erat. Quid autem allusione ista in- tendat Propheta, optime exposuit B. Brentius. Commendatio urbis, inquit, seu templi Hierusalem, hoc est, Ecclesiæ, ab ædificii magnificentiâ. Gloria, in- quit, Libani, hoc est, Cedri: Hæ enim sunt gloria Li- bani, & reddunt montem Libanum gloriosum, ad te veniet. Advehentur ad te ex Libano Cedri, simili- ter Abietes, pinus & Buxus, ut ex his locus sanctifica- tionis meæ, & pedum meorum (qui locus est tem- plum, in quo pedibus meis consisto, seu in quo am- bulo & habito) extruatur, ornetur & glorificetur. Alludit autem ad id, quod de extructione templi Hie- rosolymitani scriptum est 3. Reg. quinto, & 2. Par. 2. Sic enim scribit Salomon Hiramo Regi Tyri: Ædifi- cabo domum nomini Dei mei. Mitte ergo mihi ligna cedrina, & arcenthina, (seu abiegna) & pinea &c. Cum autem hoc Esaiæ loco fiat sermo de spiritua- li templo, considerandum est, quod quemadmodum corporale illud Salomonis templum habuit suos lapi- des & ligna, ex quibus constructum est, ita & hoc no- strum spirituale templum quod est Ecclesia Christi ha- bet suos lapides, sed vivos, & ligna, sed animata. Ipsi veluti vivi lapides, inquit Petrus, ædificemini, do- mus spiritualis &c. Quod autem ad ligna seu arbo- res attinet, ecce altissima Cedrus, est Petrus, altissima Cedrus, Paulus: altissimæ Cedri, reliqui Apostoli, qui sunt columnæ Ecclesiæ. Sic & alii ministri, ac mem- bra Ecclesiæ sunt abies, pinus & buxus, ex quibus ab- solvitur ædificium spiritualis templi. Horum alii sunt illustres miraculis, & aliis donis spiritualibus, alii sunt insignes potentiâ, sapientiâ & reliquis dotibus hujus sæ- culi, quales sunt Reges, Principes, docti, qui post divul- gationem Evangelii accesserunt per fidem ad Ecclesiam Christi. Quibus consonat Cyrilli ἔκθεσις. ET GLORIA LIBANI AD TE VENIET, IN CYPARISSO ET PINU ET CEDRO, UT GLORIFICETUR LOCUS SANCTUS ME- US. Mons est Phœniciæ Libanus, cedris, cyparissis & pinu densus, & ipsis thuris arboribus. Admirationi autem habetur hac de causa hic mons quem comme- moravimus, ut qui maximam ligni vim habeat, abundetq́; arboribus procerissimis & fragrantissimis. Hæc igitur gloria, inquit, dabitur tibi, intelligibiliter scilicet & spiritualiter. Nutrit enim Ecclesia Christi plurima & illustria sanctorum capita, tum sublimia virtute, tum odoratissima. Spirant enim suaviter Christum. Adest illis quoq́; hoc, ut nulli sint carna- les affectus corruptioni obnoxii, ita ut pinus & Cedrus non corrumpuntur. Solet autem Scriptura divini- tus inspirata hujusmodi arboribus nonnunquam af- similare sanctorum multitudinem. Siquidem rur- sus dixit voce Esaiae Deus : Et producam aquam in solitudine , & in loco aquis carente flumina : Po- nam in terra aquis carente buxum, cedrum,myr- tum, cyparissum & populum. Cum terra enim a- rida & aquis carente gentes comparat. Non enim fuit apud eas sermo divinus,qui vivificare potest,& ad pietatis auctus, ac incrementum in cognitione Dei ad- ducere. Sed fuerunt apud illas Cedrus & buxus & myrtus & cyparissus ac populus, id est, arbores bene procerae & mirabiles. Quarum etiam meminit di- vinus Psaltes, dicens: Panis cor hominis roborat: saturabuntur ligna campi, & Cedri Libani, quas plantasti. Nam ut sapientissimus Paulus scribit : Dei agricultura sumus. Haec igitur,inquit,gloria Libani dabitur tibi,id est,florebis multis & admiran- dis sanctorum capitibus refertus. Erit autem hoc, ut decoretur locus sanctus meus. Decus enim Eccle- siarum sunt hi, qui ad virtutum celsitatem ascende- runt, & qui nihil habent in mente terrenum & humi- le, nec quae carnis sunt, sapiunt : sed qui altum pe- tunt, & quae supra sunt sapiunt, & velut è terra se- cedunt, ac in supernu ambulant, in caelis habentes conversationem.

## 60:17
FOR BRASS I WILL BRING GOLD] I will restore all things that have been taken from you with an increase.

The comparison of the passage in Ezra 4:2 is entirely irrelevant. For there the subject is not those who joined themselves to the Jews and worshipped the traces of their feet, but the enemies of the Jews, who approached with a hypocritical mind so that they might hinder the construction of the temple. Furthermore, if the worship of the traces of the feet is from the parallel passage in chapter 49:23, 'And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet,' it is manifest how ἀπροσδιονύσως (irrelevant) these things are applied to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and those who came to Zerubbabel under the pretext of helping the structure of the temple, but were hindering the same. Moreover, the CONVERSION OF THE ENEMIES of the Church to the faith is described in this way, which provides us with a new argument that the prophecy is to be understood not of the material structure of the temple, but of the spiritual Zion and city of the Lord, i.e. the Church. For we have already shown that the sense which Grotius brought forward concerning the cooperation in the structure of the material temple is evidently false; thus it is in the open that these and the following things graphically depict that even the enemies of the Church are to be gathered to the same, and are to show honor to it: Namely, that the descendants of those who previously humbled the Church, with bent or flexed knee, and with face lowered to the ground, are to venerate it with the greatest reverence, and are to worship the traces of its feet, i.e., are to show obedience to it, by submissively subjecting themselves to the doctrine of the Church, and are to call it the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel, i.e., are to acknowledge that it is the true Church, and are to confess the name of our Lord JESUS Christ. What he said above in chapter 14, 'The house of Israel shall possess them as servants and handmaids, and they shall be captors of those who had captured them': And Obadiah verse 21. 'upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess those who had possessed them.' Which in the calling of the nations has been fulfilled, and shall be fulfilled until the consummation of the age: FOR THAT THOU HAST BEEN FORSAKEN AND HATED, SO THAT NO ONE PASSED THROUGH THEE, I WILL PLACE THEE IN THE PRIDE OF THE AGE, A JOY UNTO GENERATION AND GENERATION. Which things certainly were not fulfilled in the earthly Jerusalem. For that city was neither placed in the pride of the ages, nor in a joy unto generation and generation, so that it might remain illustrious perpetually, and enjoy joy without end, seeing that it is left perpetually in squalor, deserted and trodden underfoot for sixteen hundred years. And although the earthly Jerusalem, which was the seat of the Church, was regarded by reason of its abandonment and rejection, because it was crushed and held in abomination, and by reason of the Babylonian devastation, yet not only the external repair of the same was designated here, but the restoration of the Church in it and the propagation through it: because it was restored for this reason, that the Church, which was in a pressed state under Babylonian servitude, might be propagated. But afterwards, the temple having been built, it was made more illustrious, and propagated far more widely, nay, and placed in the pride of the age and a joy unto generation and generation, not through a material temple, but when the doctrine of the Gospel went forth from Jerusalem through the whole world. For that these things pertain primarily to the times of the N.T. and the calling of the nations, those things which the Prophet added openly testify: And THOU SHALT SUCK the milk of the nations and shalt be suckled at the breast of Kings: For the daughters of the mystical Jerusalem or the Church are educated and fostered at the expense of the Nations and Kings: who are the nursing fathers of the Church, as is held in the parallel passage Isa. 49:23. B. Brentius refers these things particularly to the youth, who are fostered at the expense of Kings, until they have grown up, and he says it was fulfilled when Kings, Princes, and cities instituted Schools, in which the youth might be taught pious letters, and be instructed in catechisms, monasteries, and colleges of students, in which the doctrine of the Gospel was handed down to Adolescence, and propagated to posterity, and Academies, so that at their expense, as if by breasts and milk, the adolescents might be educated for ministries both Political and Ecclesiastical. There is no discourse here about attracting riches or earthly wealth only, but about the spontaneous beneficence of nations and Kings toward the Church, by which its nursing fathers will be nourished and fostered. The LXX Interpreters with the Chaldean have riches: but Jerome rightly: These riches according to the Hebrew truth are the breasts of Kings and Doctors, by which the infancy of those born in CHRIST is educated and nourished. Which when you have sucked and arrived at solid food, then you will know that I am your Savior, who redeemed you with my blood, or the strong GOD of Jacob. FOR BRASS I WILL BRING GOLD. These things are not to be taken concerning earthly works, or those things which, having been taken from the earthly city, are to be restored with increase. Such glosses are analogous to the dreams of the Jews, who everywhere imagine for themselves earthly riches and wealth and carnal prosperity: But if you wish to adhere precisely to the literal sense, let it be shown when this prophecy was fulfilled according to the literal sense: which certainly, if you look at the letter, does not speak of the restitution of things taken away, but promises immense riches, because for brass it promises gold, for iron silver, for wood brass, for stones iron. But how, I will not say the restored Polity of the exiled Jews, but the most powerful Monarchy under heaven ever had such great riches, such great treasures? It is manifest therefore again that these things must be understood spiritually concerning the kingdom of Christ, which is wont to be described by earthly kingdoms, with those even proposed in a most magnificent state, so that its majesty may be in some way shadowed forth to us, to whom these earthly things only revolve before our eyes, while the heavenly things are invisible and unspeakable. In a word, all things in the Kingdom of Christ are said to be about to be splendid, all things glorious, and truly majestic. But that splendor is internal, not external, it is a spiritual and heavenly splendor, even if it is shadowed forth by earthly and worldly splendor, such as indeed the splendor of the King's daughter will be, shining with gold, whose whole glory is from within Ps. 44:10, 13. These spiritual riches of the Church are Christ himself, who is the treasure of all goods, with whom have been given to her the remission of sins, justice and eternal salvation and all heavenly goods, than which nothing in any kingdom was ever more excellent, nothing more precious. Then besides these general riches, which are given to every believer, other wealth and gifts are also conferred upon the Church through Christ, by which the body of the Church is not only nourished, but also adorned, and rendered vigorous, such as are: Prophecy, tongues, etc. Finally, GOD also provides for the Church and for any believers whatsoever concerning necessary wealth, nay, he brings it about that the Church is also most rich according to eternal wealth. For he is rich, not who possesses much gold and silver, but who is content with few things. For godliness is great gain, with a mind content with its lot. But this is the work of faith in the pious, that it diminishes the desire for earthly riches and fills the mind with heavenly wealth, in comparison with the multitude and magnitude of which it does not reckon earthly riches, but is best content with those which the Lord has given, and from which, however few they may otherwise be, it receives as much of necessary things as any Croesus from all the revenues of his kingdom. Jerome explains these things spiritually in another way: Therefore in the restoration of the spiritual Jerusalem wood will be turned into brass: and stones will be changed into iron, that is, men who were once brutish and insensible will be changed into those materials which may provide some utility to the city. And the brass or iron itself through the increase of virtues will be changed into gold and silver; so that they may by no means have the appearance of utility, but also price and beauty.

Verse of the same.

I WILL PLACE THY VISITATION PEACE] פְּקֻדָּה signifies prefecture to the Hebrews, and metonymically it is taken for the prefects themselves, in which way both the Greeks and the Chaldean have taken it here. The sense is: you will be governed mercifully as by Ezra, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah and those like them.

Verse of the same.

AND THY PREFECTS JUSTICE] In the Hebrew: Thy exactors justice: that is, tributes will be exacted from you with the greatest equity and moderation. See Ezra 10, v. 32.

That these words describe and celebrate the prefects and overseers or exactors of Jerusalem is beyond doubt, but they are not described by political virtues, clemency, equity, and moderation in government or the exaction of tributes. For the whole treatment teaches that something far more sublime is being viewed here, in comparison to whose majesty those things are of little moment, even if one were clement in government or moderate in the exaction of tributes: and the ABSTRACTIVE words themselves signify more: For they do not promise CLEMENT AND PEACEFUL prefects, but he says, I will appoint PEACE as your PREFECTURE or PREFECTS: not moderate OVERSEERS, but I WILL APPOINT YOUR OVERSEERS RIGHTEOUSNESS. Brentius correctly expressed this emphasis, because an allusion is made to the Kingdom of Solomon: In the kingdom of Christ there are also his own overseers and exactors, whom we call presidents, Prefects, Schultheissen, and Publicans, but far more tolerable and better than were the prefects of the Israelites in Egypt, or even in the Kingdom of Solomon. For these men so disturbed the Israelites with their harshest exactions that they did not merely groan; but even, because of the gravity of the tyranny, they cried out: Why do you act thus against your servants? And, Your father imposed a most harsh yoke upon us. But if indeed one must speak of the ecclesiastical overseers and prefects of the Israelites, they were not more tolerable than those political ones, but more grievous. For some who urged human traditions did not bring peace to consciences but only perturbation and desperation. Others who urged the law itself did not bring justice, but rather injustice. For the law increases, it does not take away, sin. And although the law must necessarily be preached and rightly explained, so that once sin is acknowledged one may hasten to obtain the justice of Christ, yet if the law is preached without Christ, which is customary for the doctors of the law, it leads rather to the acknowledgment of injustice than of justice, and makes sin sinning in a greater manner. Christ, however, appoints his overseers Peace, and his prefects justice, that is, he establishes in the administration of his kingdom such prefects who bring peace and justice. He looks especially to this in the Apostles and the Apostolic preaching. For Christ chose his Apostles, and sent them into the whole world, that they might preach the Gospel to every creature. The Gospel, however, concerning JESUS CHRIST brings true peace of conscience, and true justice before God. For it announces that God the Father is reconciled and appeased toward us through his son Jesus Christ, and it teaches that the justice of the Son of God is given and imputed to all who believe in him, so that they are reckoned, on account of Christ, as just before God as if they had fulfilled the law by their own works. Justified therefore by faith, as Paul says, we have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ. The Apostles were followed by other overseers and prefects, who propagated the doctrine handed down by them, and bring peace and justice to the Church, through the doctrine handed down by the Apostles and confirmed by the Holy Spirit, so that even if the Apostles have departed from life, they remain nonetheless, through their doctrine, which the Church alone receives, the prefects and overseers of the Church. Concerning these, Ps. 55. Instead of your fathers, sons are born to you; you shall make them princes over all the earth. And again Ps. 68. The princes of Judah their leaders, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. And above c. 52. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who announces and preaches Peace, and in John c. 15. I have appointed you, that you should go and bring forth fruit, and your fruit should remain, etc. But the Apostolic fruit remains in the true Church perpetually. Rightly, therefore, do we say that they are the perpetual Princes, overseers, and prefects of the Church: especially since Christ also says to them elsewhere: You who have followed me in the regeneration, when the son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. These things, however, do not look to this, that we should invoke the Apostles as tutelary gods, or patrons and defenders in the judgment of God, but that we should know that no other doctrine of salvation is proposed to us except the Apostolic, and according to that doctrine the whole human race is to be judged before God, so that he who has believed the Apostolic doctrine may be saved, but he who has not believed it shall be condemned perpetually. Thus our Brentius: we do not deny, however, that this prophecy is also referred to other doctors of the Church: concerning which Jerome has this: I will place, he says, your Princes in peace, and your bishops in justice: For which the admirable majesty of the holy scriptures, because it named the future princes of the Church bishops: whose every visitation is in peace, and the name of their dignity is in justice: so that they may by no means accept a person in judgment: nor may anything iniquitous be heard in the land of the Church, nor contrition, and unhappiness in its borders. We judge, however, that justice and peace are to be understood as the justice and peace which the Gospel announces: because all things here are so arranged that they exhibit the spiritual goods which flourish in the kingdom of Christ. Whence the tenth argument of our opinion emerges from the description of the Presidents and Prefects in this city. For in what earthly city, in what kingdom of this age, does God place overseers as peace, and prefects as justice? You would not say, even of Ezra, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah, and the like, who are viewed in political government, that they were PEACE and JUSTICE, since there is no government so perfect in which only PEACE and JUSTICE flourish, and no hatreds or contentions, no injustice or iniquity are found. This is proper only to the kingdom of Christ. Compare Isa. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 17. PRO AERE AFFERAM AURUM ] Omnia quae tibi adempta sunt restituam cum augmento.

Aliena prorsus est collacio loci Esdr. 4,2. Nam ibi non de illis,qui se aggregarunt ad Judaeos & ado- rarunt vestigia pedum,termo est,sed de hostibus Ju- daorum,qui animo hypocritico accessêre,ut impe- dirent exstructionem templi. Porro si adoratio ve- stigiorum pedum è loco parallelo c. 49,23. Et erunt reges nutritii tui,& reginae nutrices tuae: vultu in ter- ram demisso adorabunt te, & pulverem pedum tuo- rum lingent, manifestum est,quam ἀπροσδιονύσως haec applicentur tribubus Judae & Benjamin,quique ad Serubabel venerunt sub praetextu juvandi structu- ram templi,sed praepediebant eandem.Describitur autem ita CONVERSIO HOSTIUM Ecclesiae ad fidem, quae argumentum nobis novum praebet, quod vaticinium intelligendum sit,non de materia- li structura templi,sed de spirituali Zione & civita- te Domini, h.e. Ecclesia.Nam illum sensum,quem de cooperatione ad structuram templi materialis attulit Grotius,evidenter falsum esse, jam ostendi- mus; ita in aprico est, haec & sequentia graphice depingere, quod ipsi etiam hostes Ecclesiae ad ean- dem aggregandi, eiq; honorem exhibituri sint : Quod nempe posteri eorum,qui humiliarunt antea Eccle- siam,incurvi seu flexo poplite,ac demisso in terram vultu, suma cum reverentia ipsam veneraturi sint, & adoraturi vestigia pedum ejus,h.e.obedientiam ipsi exhibituri,submissse sese doctrinaeEcclesiae sub- jiciendo, & vocaturi sint ipsam civitatem Domini Sionem sancti Dei Israëlisa,h. e. agnituri,ipsam esse veram Ecclesiam, & nomen Domini nostri JESU Christi confessuri. Quod supra c. 14. dixit, possi- debit eos domus Israël in servos & ancillas, & erunt capientes eos, qui se ceperant : Et Obad.v. 21. in mon- te Sion erit salvatio & erit sanctum,& possidebit do- mus Jacob eos,qui se possederant.Quod in vocatione gentium impletum, & implebitur usque ad con- fummationem feculi: PRO EO QUOD FUI- STI DERELICTA ET ODIO HABITA, UT NEMO PER TE TRANSIRET, PONAM TE IN SUPERBIAM SECU- LI, GAUDIUM IN GENERATIONEM ET GENERATIONEM. Quæ certe in Hierusalem terrena impleta non sunt Nam illa nec in superbiam feculorum posita, nec in gau- dium in generationem & generationem, ut illu- stris manserit perpetuo, & gaudio sine fine fruere- tur, utpote quæ per mille fexcentos annos deserta, & conculcata, in squalore relinquitur perpetuo.
