Wherefore, since even now ancient codices survive which do not have this particle, it is much more probable that it was added from Isaiah and the LXX interpreters than omitted by other scribes. For in the same way the Latin edition has it added from Isaiah in the following clause, & the day of retribution, which exists neither in the Greek nor in the Syriac. But our writers often use the passages of the Prophets with such liberty that they omit certain words in the middle, which could be done here with less damage to the sense, because the variation of the Prophet often expresses the same thing with a different manner of speaking. But these reasons are flimsy. For the fact that Origen in the recitation of the Greek words of this place, and Ambrose in the Latin, omit that particle, that by no means proves that they themselves did not find it in their own Greek and Latin Codices. For it is very well known that they do not always recite testimonies in full, but omit some things as the occasion requires. If, when some things are omitted from these cited passages, it could be concluded that they were omitted in their own Biblical Codices, we would have to be in doubt about the authority of the sacred words in infinite places. But who those ancient codices are, which Grotius says do not have this particle, whether Latin or Greek, he does not indicate, nor did those who most diligently compared the sacred Codices observe a different reading here; Erasmus, Stephanus, Beza, Valla, and others. The Greek Codices agree. The Latin agree, the Syriac and Arabic agree, and others. Which consensus confounds the Grotian invention. The Syrian distinguished in this way, ἔχρισέ με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, κ’ ἀπέσταλκέ με ἰάσασ- θαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν: Ludov. de Dieu observes at Luke 4 that this agrees with the Hebrew text, where the accent Reviab above ענוים separates them from the following, and connects them with the preceding.

Vers. eod. AND TO PREACH DELIVERANCE TO THE CAPTIVES] In the Hebrew: Liberty. And not otherwise in the Greek and Chaldaic. The Jews were not only exiles, but also captives as if in a loose chain, as once in Egypt: for it was not permitted for them to go out from the assigned places. AND RECOVERING OF SIGHT TO THE BLIND] What is in the Hebrew פקח־קוח most translate as the opening of a prison. That Hebrew word does not appear. But in the Chaldaic language, from which it is credible that Isaiah took this manner of speaking, because it treats of that captivity which was brought about by the Chaldeans, קיחה signifies a thong: And the opening or dissolution of a thong is not badly called by similitude that liberation which is treated of here. The LXX here placed τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, undoubtedly because the highest miseries are shadowed forth by blindness.

I find this single argument by which Grotius proves his Gloss, that the discourse is about the Babylonian captivity; because Isaiah uses a word derived from the Chaldeans: Therefore he speaks of the solution of the Chaldaic captivity. Which consequence is too frivolous to establish such a great matter, to which so many and such clear arguments, along with the interpretation of Christ himself, are opposed. Nor is the antecedent certain. For what does that word קוח have to do with this? Lexicographers more correctly translate the word פקחקוח as a noun from פקח with a duplication of the theme, increasing the meaning, so that an opening and liberation of every kind is designated, with which, whichever way you turn your eyes, all things are open. Which Grotius acknowledges in his annotations on Luke 4. That what follows קוח is a prison, as many wish, is proved by no testimony. Wherefore I do not see why we should disapprove of what the most learned of the Hebrews feel, that it is one word, פקחקוח but in which the later letters of the theme are repeated augmentatively; of which kind are ירקרק & אדמדם & מהרחר & הפכפך. The grammarians of the Hebrews dispute whether such a repetition of letters is intensive or augmentative. But even if the matter is doubtful concerning ירקרק & אדמדם, the two remaining words which I mentioned altogether demand an augmentative meaning, as can be seen in Psalm 38:11 and Proverbs 21:8. Therefore, those seem to think best who refer this word פקחקוח in this place of the Prophet to the fullest liberty of turning the eyes hither and thither, wherever one pleases. But that the discourse is about spiritual liberation, we have sufficiently proved before. And Christ understood it no differently when, with the LXX interpreters, he explained these things as τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν. For he was not speaking about the solution of captivity, when the Savior taught that it was fulfilled today, and therefore he did not signify that such a calamity had a place there metaphorically, such as is shadowed forth by blindness: But about the sight of the blind, or as Erasmus rendered it in his annotations, RECOVERY OF SIGHT. Which he undoubtedly understood concerning spiritual blindness and the restoration of sight. Why therefore should we admit any other meaning of the words than that which was handed down by Christ? Rightly therefore Brentius here again: TO PREACH DELIVERANCE TO THE CAPTIVES. The Son of God is anointed with the Holy Spirit, and is sent to this office, that he may expiate the sin of man, by which everyone who believes in the Son of God may be snatched from the captivity and servitude of Satan, and be restored to liberty, than which benefit nothing can happen more acceptable and more happy to a man who is a captive of Satan. For he who is thus liberated not only obtains the remission of sins, but is also accounted righteous before God, is adopted as a Son of God, is gifted with the Holy Spirit, by whom he may mortify the remnants of the flesh, is preserved in death, and is placed in the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom, so that together with the Son of God he may enjoy the joy of eternal life. Christ preaches about this liberty and manumission also in John. If you, he says, remain in my word, you are truly my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free. And shortly after: If the Son makes you free, you are truly free. And to the Hebrews: Since the children have communion with flesh and blood, he himself likewise became a participant of the same, that through death he might abolish him who had the power of death, that is the Devil, and might set free those who, through fear of death, were subject to slavery throughout their whole life. THAT I MAY PREACH OPENING TO THOSE WHO ARE SHUT UP, or liberation to the bound. Just as there was talk before of captives in slavery, so now there is talk of captives in prisons. For the Son of God was sent also for this purpose, that he might lead out those captured or shut up in prisons, and set them free. Although it is a heavy calamity to be shut up in an external prison, yet the most grievous calamity of all is to be shut up and bound in the spiritual prison of the divine Law. For he who is enclosed in the prison of the law and held bound, just as he is subject to sin, so he is subject to the curse, the power of Satan, and eternal condemnation. What heavier chains can befall a man? For the Law demands perfect righteousness from man. But since man does not fulfill it, he is led away by the law into the chains of the curse, so that it is necessary, as far as the law and he himself are concerned, for him to perish perpetually. For everyone who has not remained in all the words of the law is cursed. Christ therefore came to preach liberation to these bound ones, because he expiates sin and grants his own righteousness to the one who believes in him. Therefore, he releases the believer from the Right of the law, so that he may no longer be cursed, but may have every- the blessing of righteousness and salvation, so that he may no longer be held in chains by the Law, but be restored to heavenly liberty. The Law of the Spirit of life through Christ Jesus, says Paul, has set me free from the law of sin and death. And again, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, while he became a curse for us. Now if we approach the translation of Luke, Grotius thinks that in reality the same thing is said as in the preceding. The propriety of the words, he says, is in dispute. To me, the LXX, whom Luke follows, seem to have interpreted the Hebrew with sufficient consideration. פקח if anyone wishes to weigh the places in which that word appears, it does not signify any opening, like פתח but only that which pertains to the eyes, unless it is transferred to the ears, just as פצה is proper to the mouth. The LXX interpreters, however, in order to continue the translation, translated what precedes אסורים as blind, surely because, as we have said, פקח pertains to the eyes, it does not pertain to a prison. And therefore it is mostly said of the blind, as Ps. 146:8, Is. 42:7. But the Hebrews love to connect both proper things with figurative ones, and other figures with others. But those who live in darkness are accustomed to be called blind, which especially suits those whom a prison encloses. Therefore, in the same Isaiah 49:7, the blind and the bound. Therefore, blind captives, as to the Latins, blind, deprived of their eyes. Both similes signify the utmost misery, such as was that of the Jews in the Babylonian exile, and much more so of all men in that state of gross ignorance before the times of the Messiah. Compare the same Isaiah 43:8, where likewise the Jews in that exile are called blind, however much they may have eyes: because, namely, the utmost misery had taken away from their eyes the freedom of seeing. These are the words of Grotius. Granted, let the utmost misery be designated: it may also be conceded that there is an allusion to the Babylonian captivity. But in the direct and proper sense, which they call literal, the explanation of Christ does not permit it to be treated of that. Then, if the discourse is about the cause of the ignorance of men in the time of Christ, i.e., spiritual blindness, it will certainly not be treated here of captivity in the Babylonian exile. But the former is true from the interpretation of Christ, nor does Grotius deny it.

Latin:

CAPUT LXI.

Christus ipse testatur se S. S. unctum mitten- dum ad Evangelium de redemtione & Iobeleū gratiæ annunciandum, suosq́; ministros de- scribit: unde in eo exultant fideles vestibus justitiæ, & ornatu ejus Sacerdotali decorati.

Vers. 1. SPIRITUS DOMINI SUPER ME] Loqui- tur hic Esaias de se, ut notat Chaldæus. Sed in quo Chri- sti non obscuram conspicimus imaginem. Ideo me, in- quit, spiritu suo afflavit DEUS.

NE quicquam reliqui supersit, quod de Christo quoad literam textus loquatur, hoc etiam va- ticinium, illustrissimo alioquin, detorquet, & cum Judæis de Esaia intelligit. Quo errore occupatus jam fuit, cum Annotata ad Evangelista adornaret. Sic enim ad Luc. 4, 18. Πνεῦμα κυρίε ἐπ' ἐμέ. Sicut liberatio ex captivitate Babylonica & imago ac pignus fuit liberationis animorum, quam facturus erat Mes- sias, ita & Esaias, quæ de se dixerat, ita directa sunt à Deo, ut Domino Jesu excellentius convenirent. Etiam Kimchi ad Messiam hæc aptat. Sed hoc in loco, cum Esaiam tractat, ut id primum moneamus, συνεχείας immemor fuit, quam ipse in hoc Propheta perpe- tuam & concatenatam tradere voluit. Quum enim præcedens concio de reditu in Judæam secundum Grotium egerit, quomodo cohæret nunc oratio de officio Messiæ? Annon ita necessum est relabi Spi- ritum S. modo ad Jeremiam, quod de cap. LIII. so- mniavit Grotius, modo ad ipsummet Esaiam, quod hic fieri cum Judæis fingit. Quæ certe cum co- hærentia ista, quam tradere instituit Grotius, mini- me conveniunt. At si de Christo secundum literam intelligatur hoc vaticinium, optime cohærebit prę- cedenti. Quum n. de spirituali structura & incolis civitatis mysticæ, Ecclesiæ Christi, sub tempora im- primis N. Test. actum sit, introducitur Christus in diebus carnis suæ doctrinam Evangelii prædicatu- rus, per quam Ecclesia extruenda est. Quum præfe- ctorum ac præsidum mentio facta sit, qui in pacem & justitiam ponendi sunt, nunc supremus eorum præses, qui pacem & justitiam allaturus erat, & ob id Spiritu Sancto unctus est, sistitur salvator, qui muros occupaturus, Dominus, qui civitatem illu- straturus erat. Descripserat Esaias populum in ista civitate, cives & incolas, quod justi futuri sint; quod felicitate ac lætitia perenni gavisuri, quod germi- na plantationis Domini in celebrationem, quod fortes futuri sint, & sese copiose propagaturi: Nunc ergo hæc beneficia collaturum Christum uberius docet: utpote qui ponit lugentibus in Sion coronam, pro cinere oleum, gaudium pro luctu, ut vo- centur, qui in ea sunt fortes vel arbores justitiæ, sacer- dotes Domini, ac induantur vestimentis salutis, & ut geminet justitia & laus coram universis gentibus.

Porro secundo si personam loquentem è nexu orationis indagemus, is qui ad finem capitis præce- dentis loquutus erat, EGO DOMINUS in tempore suo subito faciam illud, continuat nunc orationem, spiritus Domini super me, idcirco unxit me. Quum ergo is, super quem Spiritus Domini est, Je- hovah sit, qui ista effecturus est, quæ prædixit E- saias, manifestissimum est, non posse hæc de Esaia intelligi, sed Christum loquentem introduci. Quo de Cyrillus: Qui in superioribus dixit de vocandis per fidem: Ego Dominus in tempore congregabo il- los, veluti jam instanti tempore, quo promisit eos se coacturum, & quasi factus jam homo, & similitu- dinem nostram suscipiens, & se ad inanitionem sub- mittens Spiritus Domini, inquit, super me: quoniam natura Deus existens unigenitus sanctus sit sancto- rum, & omnem ipse naturam sanctificet, utpote ex sancto patre natus, cumque ex se procedentem spiritum immittat superis potestatibus suis, & porro apparitio- nem ipsius agnoscentibus, quomodo igitur sanctifica- tus est? Deus nempe cum sit idemque homo, dat spi- ritum creaturæ Deitatis ratione, accipit autem illum à Deo & patre ratione humanitatis. Hanc dicimus esse unctionem. Quod observatum quoque Hiero- nymo: Ille qui supra dixerat: EGO DOMINUS in tempore congregabo eos; Sive juxta Hebrai- cam: Ego Dominus in tempore suo subito istud faciam, loquitur consequenter: Spiritus Domini Dei super me, non quod Dominus Deus habeat Do- minum Deum, sed quod juxta dispensationem car- nis assumptæ dicat ea, quæ humilia sunt. Quod con- firmatur ulterius Tertio ex aliis, quæ cap. præceden- ti Christum de se professum esse, ostendimus: Si- quidem, fatente Davide Pareo, haud dubie idem sit, qui loquitur cap. præcedenti, INSULÆ EX- PECTARUNT ME: & qui hic dicit: Spir. Do- mini super me; ipse autem Christus est, ut è con- textu liquet. Quarto è consequentibus. Nam idem ille, qui se unctum & missum testatur ad prædican- dum Evangelium, de se ita loquitur: QUIA EGO DOMINUS diligens judicium & odio habens rapi- nam in holocausto. Non ergo Propheta de seipso loquitur, sed Christus Dominus à Propheta lo- quens introductus est. Quod etiam Quinto testa- tur unctio, de qua agit. Spiritus Domini Dei super me, eo quod unxit me Dominus. Quia super Chri- stum Spiritus Domini est, ut c. 11, 1. Esaias docuit. Christum unxit Dominus Spiritu, ita non absolu- te, & κατ' αὐτονομασίαν משיח, χρισὸς & Unctus Do- mini dicatur: qui etiam solus inter Prophetas ab unctione nomen sortitus est, utpote quem unxit o- leo exultationis præ consortibus suis Ps. 45. Qui locus huic nostro παράλληλος est. Nam & à Da- vide Messias Deus unctus à DEO dicitur Ps. 45. & hic Jehovah à Jehovah dicitur unctus, & uti illic à Davide tali celebratur elogio, dilexisti justitiam & odisti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus oleo exultationis: ita hic unctus de se testatur: Ego Dominus diligens judicium & odio habens rapinam in holocausto. Adde quod Calvinus ipse fateatur, quod non de qualicunque unctione hic sermo sit, sed de plenitudine spiritus & de unctione supra omnes con- sortes ἄνευ μέτρου, quæ in solum Christum convenit. Sexto de illo sermo est hoc loco, qui missus est, non tantum ad Evangelizandum mansuetis; sed etiam ut sanaret contritos corde. At hoc de Propheta dici nequit: Sanatio enim contritorum est θεόεργημα opus divinum, quod ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ non conve- nit, Messiæ vero proprium est. Septimo quia hæc beneficia, quæ ab hoc uncto Domini annunciantur, ab eodem etiam reapse conferuntur, quæ omnia in- divulso nexu cohærent & uni eidemque Personæ tri- buuntur, qua quæso ratione abripi possunt ad Esai- am? Agnoscere hoc iterum debuit Calvinus, quod nempe solus Christus hæc præstet Ecclesiæ, quæ hic præ- co se præstiturum promittit. Accedit quod, fatente i- tidem Pareo, Deus iisdem prope verbis supra c. 42, 7. non Prophetam, sed Messiam compellavit. Dedi te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium, ut aperias oculos cæcorum & educas de carcere vinctum, & de domo carceris sedentes in tenebris &c. Nam hæc de se pro- fitetur hic unctus Domini, quod missus sit, ut mede- retur contritis corde, & prædicaret captivis indulgen- tiam, & clausis aperitionem &c. Octavo præconi- um redemtionis, sanationis & illuminationis, nec non gaudii, laudis & glorificationis tale hic designari, cu- jus præco illam redemtionem, sanationem, illumi- nationem, gaudium, laudem, glorificationem ipse effecturus sit, verba Prophetica luculenter infe- runt, quia ita missum se dicit ad ista annunciandum, ut medeatur simul contritis corde, ut efficaciter con- soletur lugentes omnes, ut ponat lugentibus in Sion, & det eis coronam pro cinere, oleum gaudii pro luctu, pallium laudis pro spiritu mæroris, ut vocentur in ea fortes justitiæ, plantatio Domini ad glorificandum. Nono is qui hic loquitur, & Dominum se vocat, & à Domino, hoc est Deo patre, nec non à Spiritu Domini aperte se distinguit: unde necessum est nul- lum alium hic loqui, secundum ipsammet textus li- teram, nisi Christum, qui solus Dominus est ὑποsα- τικῶς à Patre & Spiritu Sancto distinctus. Sic enim v. 1. loquitur: Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me Dominus. Et 8. Quia EGO DOMI- NUS diligens judicium & odio habens rapinam in holocausto: & dabo opus eorum in veritate, & fœdus perpetuum feriam eis. Qui promittit daturum se opus eorum in veritate & fœdus perpetuum eis positurum, distinguit postmodum v. 9. iterum se à Deo Patre. Omnes, inquit, qui viderint eos, cogno- scent eos, quia isti sint semen, cui benedixit DOMI- NUS. Loquitur ergo DOMINUS, super quo est Spiritus Domini, & qui fœdus perpetuum cum popu- lo suo ferire vult, de DOMINO, qui benedixit ei, hoc est Christus, verus DEUS, loquitur de Patre ve- ro DEO & DOMINO. Decimo cum respondet ad insignem hanc promissionem Domino Ecclesia gratulabunda v. 10. & gaudet atq; exultat se à DO- MINO indutam vestimentis salutis & indumentis justitiæ, quid aliud testatur, quam eum, qui dat Sion coronam pro cinere, oleum gaudii pro luctu, pallium laudis pro spiritu mæroris, induisse se vestimentis ju- stitiæ & salutis? Quia hæc gratulatio & exultatio in Domino respicit præcedentem promissionem, ex qua istud gaudium resultat penes fideles. De quo Hieronymus: juxta Hebræos, alterius capi- tis exordium est, in quo introducitur Ecclesia Christi respondere sermonibus: Gaudens gaudebo in Do- mino, & exultavit anima mea in Deo meo. Ne- quaquam in patribus, sicut Judæi gloriabantur di- centes: Semen Abraham sumus, & nemini un- quam servivimus, sed in Deo, scriptura dicente: multitudinis autem credentium erat cor unum, & anima una. Redditq; causas lætitiæ; quia induit me vestimentis salutis & indumento sive tunica justitiæ atque lætitiæ, quæ Hebraice dicitur מעיל ornavit atque circumdedit. Quotquot enim in Christo baptizati sumus, induimur Christo, & ha- bemus tunicam justitiæ, qui factus est nobis sancti- tas, justitia & redemtio. Undecimo quum hic conver- sio gentium connectatur cum ista annunciatione Evangelii, sicut terra profert germen suum & sicut hortus semen suum germinat, sic Dominus Deus germi- nabit justitiam & laudem coram UNIVERSIS GENTI- BUS, quomodo hoc præconium Esaiæ vindicari po- test? Annon manifestum est, eundem Dominum Deum, qui induit fideles vestimentis salutis & in- dumentis justitiæ, ut gaudentes gaudeant in hoc Do- mino, ut exultent in hoc Deo suo, designari, cum dici- tur DOMINUS DEUS germinabit JUSTITIAM ET LAU- DEM. Qui proinde nullus est, quam quem celebrant fideles hoc elogio ὁμολογητικῷ: Jehovah justitia nostra Jerem. 23. & Ef. 45, 14. In Jehovah justitia & fortitudo mea. Duodecimo habemus interpretem omni exceptione majorem Christum Jesum, qui hoc vaticinium de se explicat, non mystica ratione, sed quoad sensum literalem. Testatur enim λευκάδι φωνῇ in id se impletum esse, nec aliud agnoscit sub- jectum hujus vaticinii. Nam si in Esaia id imple- tum esset, si de liberatione è captivitate Babyloni- ca ab Esaia prædicta, id ageret, respondere potuis- sent Judæi, quid illa ad Te, quæ de Esaia Propheta loquuntur, & quæ de liberatione è captivitate præ- dicta, jam pridem impleta sunt? Sed ὁμολογουμένως certum tum erat penes Judæos, hæc non de Esaia agere, sed de Messia prædicta fuisse, nec de eo quis- piam dubium aut controversiam movebat. Ita enim legitur Luc. 4, 15. Et ipse docebat (regressus sc. à Jordane plenus Spirit. Sanct. & postquam è deser- to rediisset, & virtute Spiritus in Galilæam venisset) in synagogis eorum, & magnificabatur AB OMNI- BUS. Et venit Nazareth, ubi erat nutritus, & in- travit secundum consuetudinem suam die Sabbati in Synagogam & surrexit legere. Et traditus est illi li- ber Esaiæ Prophetæ, & ut revolvit librum, invenit locum, ubi scriptum erat: Spiritus DOMINI SU- PER ME, propter quod unxit me, Evangelizare pauperibus misit me, sanare contritos corde, prædi- care captivis remissionem, dimittere confractos in re- missionem, prædicare annum Domini acceptum, & diem retributionis. Et cum plicuisset librum, reddi- dit ministro & sedit: Et omnium oculi in Synagoga erant intendentes in eum. Cœpit autem dicere ad il- los: Quia HODIE impleta est hæc Scriptura in au- ribus vestris. Et OMNES testimonium illi dabant, & mirabantur in verbis gratiæ, quæ procedebat de ore ipsius. Adde quæ habentur v. 43. Quia & aliis civitatibus oportet me EVANGELIZARE regnum Dei, quia IDEO MISSUS sum. Quid luculentius est, quam Christum ex ipsiusmet propria interpre- tatione, & Evangelistæ narratione esse illum, qui juxta hoc Prophetæ vaticinium (1.) unctus Spiritu Sancto, quod in Jordane, cum venit super ipsum Spiritus Sanctus, declaratum publice est: (2.) Mis- sus à Domino ad Evangelizandum, quia venit ideo in virtute Spiritus in Galilæam, & testatus est se oportere Evangelizare regnum Dei, quod IDEO MISSUS SIT. (3) Idem ille sit, qui apud Pro- phetam loquitur: Spiritus Domini super me &c. (4.) & in ipso impletum id fuisse, in diebus carnis ejus, quod hic prædictum est, quia testatur ipse sonora voce, HODIE impleta est hæc Scriptura. (5.) Chri- stum esse istum PRÆCONEM & EVANGELI- STAM missum ad prædicandum pauperibus &c. non Esaiam. Quia cum prædicaret Christus Evan- gelium, testatus diferte: HODIE impleta est hæc scriptura IN AURIBUS VESTRIS, q. d. per hoc ipsum præconium Evangelii, quod nunc resonat in auribus vestris, impletur illa scriptura. (6.) Non tan- tum impletam docet hanc scripturam ratione præ- conii; sed etiam ratione cæterorum ἐνεργημάτων, quæ ibi Propheta prædixerat, utpote quæ omnia ex Propheta ipsis prælegerat, & de sefe explicarat, ni- mirum, quod missus sit sanare contritos corde, quod divinum opus reaple præstabat, quod missus sit præ- dicare captivis remissionem, quod utiq; non de ca- ptivitate Babylonica, aut alia corporali salvatione intelligi potest. Ejus enim causa Messias missus non est, neque mitti debuit; sed de spirituali capti- vitate & liberatione; ideoque violenta est detorsio, cum quod Christus ipse exposuit de spirituali libe- ratione, Grotius abripit ad liberationem corpora- lem. Similiter testatur Christus: HODIE impleta est haec scriptura, quod missus sit praedicare caecis vi- sum, quae cum de spirituali illuminatione exponat, contra Christi mentem & expositionem detor- quentur ad apertionem clausis in Babylonia annunci- andam. Testatur de se praedictum esse, quod missus sit DIMITTERE confractos in remissionem, quod e verbis Prophetae concludit; Hoc vero NULLO PACTO Esaiae applicari potest. Unde manife- stissimum est, perversissime hoc tam illustre vatici- nium ad Esaiam detorqueri. Quomodo enim di- misit Esaias confractos in remissionem? Testatur se missum esse ad praedicandum annum Domini acce- ptum, & diem retributionis. Ille ergo annus ac- ceptus, ille dies retributionis intelligi non potest de anno liberationis Babylonicae, quem praedicare non opus habebat Christus, cum jam pridem tran- sierit. (7.) Haec ἀναντιῤῥήτως certa & indubia fuis- se penes Judaeos tempore Christi, quod nempe ista praedicta non de Esaia, sed de Messia intelligenda sint, ex eo manifestum est, quod omnes isti testimo- nium dederint, nemo se illi interpretationi, & thesi, quod haec de Messia agant, opposuerit. Adde quod Christus etiam ex hoc loco concionetur Matth. 11. ad nuncios Johannis, eumque ceu indubie prophe- ticum de suo munere vaticinantem assumat, cum jussit Johanni nunciari, pauperes Evangelizantur. Quibus verbis significat haec Prophetae verba in se respicere: Cum igitur Filius ipse Dei hanc suam concionem, quam tot ante annis de suo ipsius offi- cio habuit, interpretetur, non est nobis ulla alia huic contraria, ne angeli quidem interpretatio au- dienda, sed haec sola est suspicienda & tenenda, ut graviter monet Brentius. Quae cum omnia lucu- lentissima sint, Calvinum suum hic tueri non po- tuit hyperaspistes Pareus, quin victas hic B. Hunnio nostro manus daret, qui Calvinum Judaizantem eo nomine redarguerat, quod Prophetam de se loqui, se a Domino missum esse & unctum, hoc est, neces- sariis instructum, dixerit. Malo tamen, ait, in sen- tentiam recepta concedere, ipsum Christum induci de vocatione officii & beneficiis suis concionantem. Pri- mo enim Christus diserte in se impletionem ostendit, si quis excipiat, non dicere CHRISTUM: Hodie primum, & in me solo impleta est, sed simplici- ter: Hodie impleta est haec scriptura: parum est firmum: cum Christus aperte ad PRAESENS tem- pus impletionem restringat, & quidem OMNEM. In NULLO enim ALIO impleri potuit, quod in NULLUM ALIUM, nisi in SOLUM Christum proprie competit, praesertim cum constet, non de typi- ca, sed de aeterna redemptione, deg; proprio officio, & beneficio Messiae hic agi: unde sane consequentia firma est: Impleta est in Christo: Ergo non in Propheta. Quanquam vero adhuc juvare Calvinum suum ve- lit, lusus tamen meros facit Pareus, quod ὀφθαλ- μοφανῶς docuit B. Hunnius. Ineptissimum enim est illud κρησφύγετον de gemina litera, una histori- ca, juxta quam hic praeco sit Propheta, beneficia Messiae annuncians, altera Prophetica, juxta quam sit Messias ipse, per os Prophetae de se ista procla- mans. Sic enim ubivis, cum Prophetia occurrit de Messia, geminam licebit fingere literam: Historicam Prophetae de Messia ista annunciantis, & Propheti- cam de Messia, cujus ista sunt beneficia. Non quae- ritur, utrum Propheta haec locutus sit, aut scripserit, per Spiritum CHRISTI, ita ut

CHRISTUS ea per os Prophetæ tum protulerit, sed de quonam subjecto illa agant, & quænam ista persona sit, quæ hic loquens introducitur à Pro- pheta: an de seipso loquatur, an vero de Messia. Hic utiq; veritatis vim effugere Pareus non potuit, quin nostram explicationem calculo suo firmaret, ac Judaicam glossam, quæ ipsius Calvini Grotiique est, explodendam esse pronunciaret: Hanc Pro- phetiam, inquit, Christum Nazarethi in Synagoga ad se accommodasse, & illius explicationem hoc Epi- phonemate clausisse: Hodie impleta est hæc scriptu- ra in auribus vestris, dubitari igitur non posse, quod ad Christum pertineat! Explodendam proinde esse JUDAICAM CORRUPTELAM, quæ est, ex- ponendum hoc esse AD LITERAM in Persona E- saiæ, quasi prædicantis de se, Spiritus Domini su- per me, eo quod unxit me. Neque enim de TEM- PORALIBUS beneficiis aut de LIBERATIONE CORPORALI ex Babylone hic agi, sed de spirituali- bus & æternis bonis, quæ nemo præstat NISI Christus, de quo PERSPICUIS Argumentis ex textu convin- cuntur Judæi. Misit me, inquit, hic præco ad Ev- angelizandum mansuetis, ad obligandum fractos corde, ad dandum illis ornatum loco cineris, ut vocentur quercus justitiæ: omnes vocentur sa- cerdotes Jehovæ, ministri Dei: ut eis sit lætitia perpetua: ut fœdus perpetuum pangat cum eis. Hæc & alia NON POSSUNT NISI de beneficiis Messiæ intelligi. Hæc verissime Pareus. Sed quibus palam refellit Calvinum, quem defendendum sus- ceperat. Notandus postremo loco hic consensus Interpp. Largitur nobis eum Pareus: Omnes Chri- stianos Interpretes in hoc CONSPIRARE video, Christum ipsum hic concionari de sua vocatione & un- ctione ad officium Messiæ, & ad danda Ecclesiæ æter- na beneficia, quæ tandem in carne exhibitus reipsa secum attulit, & Ecclesiæ in æternum præstat. Sed & Judæi ipsi confitentur, hoc oraculum secundum proprium & literalem sensum, de Messia intelligen- dum esse: Sic explicat illud R. Saadia Gaon in libro Haemunoth cap. 8. Occurret illis (Messias) filius David, ut confirmet cor eorum, & sanet fracturam eorum, & erigat animos eorum, quod dicitur Es. 61, 1. Spiritus Domini super me &c. R. David Kimchi in libro Radicum Rad. משח locutus est Propheta in Persona Messiæ, quasi Messias dixerit sic, ideoque DEUS unxit me &c. E quibus manifestum est, pervertere Grotium etiam Kimchii sententiam, cum ei tribuit, quasi saltem sensu aliquo mystico hæc Messiæ aptet, etsi sensu literali de Esaia dicta. Nam agnoscit Kimchius, hæc Esaiam IN PER- SONA MESSIÆ LOQUI, quasi Messias ista di- xerit. Sic etiam interpretes Biblici exposuêre in Midrasch Canticorum de exultatione in diebus Mes- siæ, quæ versu 10. in Midrasch Tillim de conversione gentium, quæ v. 11. habentur. Quæ postea addu- cemus. Viderunt ergo Judæorum cæci Ducto- res veram sententiam, quam Grotius Christianus videre non potuit, vel potius quum viderit olim, cum annotata ad Evangelistas & Acta Apost. ador- naret, ut ex annot. ad Luc. 24, 47. & ad Act. 10, 38. liquet, videre amplius noluit, postquam à cæcis Doctoribus excæcatus fuit. Ibi enim pœniten- tiæ κήρυγμα inter gentes Discipulis Christi deman- datum, hoc loco prædictum fuisse agnovit.

Vers. eod. EO, QUOD UNXERIT DOMINUS ME AD ANNUNCIANDUM MANSUETIS] Sensus est: ideo mihi spiritum suum dedit, quia munus magnificum mihi imposuit, quale est unctorum in regnum aut sacer- dotium. Illud annunciandum in Hebræo est, ad lætum nun- tium portandum: quibus? mansuetis, id est, bonis, ac pa- tienter sibi inflicta mala tolerantibus. LXX. πτωχοῖς literæ unius mutatione, de qua vide ad Luc. 4, 18.

Verbum משח non de unctione Spiritus S. sed officij, quale unctorum est in regnum & sacerdo- tium, impositione intelligit. Sed Esaiæ tale officium, quale unctorum ad regnum & sacerdotium est, im- positum fuisse, falsum est. Siquidem neque Rex, neque sacerdos fuerit. Et per unctionem Prophe- ticum officium Esaiam consecutum fuisse non con- stat. Neq; unquam Messiæ aut uncti nomine Pro- pheta aliquis insignitur. Quod Christo proprium est κατ' ἐξαίρετον λόγον, qui unctus hic dicitur à Domino non per impositionem muneris, quæ finis unctionis est, sed per donorum Spiritus S. commu- nicationem. Neque temere observatur vocem משח distingui à נסך, eo quod illa primo significet olei illinitionem, consequenter vero consecrationem: hæc vero, cum Personæ additur, constituendi & præ- ficiendi significatum obtineat. Quum ergo illa, non hæc, usurpetur, ut Prophetæ, non de constitutio- ne in officio, sed de unctione ipsa, qua oleo Spi- ritus propter officium unctus est Messias, sermo- nem esse, credendum est. Ob quam nomine Mes- siæ insignitur, de qua etiam in locis parallelis Pf. 45, 7. Rom. 9, 24. Act. 4, 24. r. 10, 38. agitur. Cyrillus libr. de recta fid. ad Theodos. in fin. Quando ver- bum caro factum est, tunc & nominatum dicimus es- se ipsum CHRISTUM Jesum. Nam quoniam un- ctus est oleo exsultationis, h. e. Spiritu Sancto, a Deo Patre, idcirco & Christus nominatus est. At- que eo sensu etiam unctionem istam declaratam esse, cum Spiritus Sanctus in Baptismo super Chri- stum venit, S. Athanasius docuit Orat. 2. contra Arian. Quando ista, spiritus Domini super me, & DEUS Jesum unxit Spiritu Sancto, de eo pronuncia- ta, dicta sunt, sive declarat publice, nisi tum, cum in carne constitutus baptizabatur in Jordane, ac Spiri- tus in eum descendebat? Et Hilarius l. 11. de Trin. Je- sus Spiritus & virtute Dei unctus est, tum cum ascen- dente eo de Jordane vox DEI patris audita est, Filius meus es tu, Ego hodie genui te, ut per hoc testimonium sanctificatæ in eo carnis unctio spiritualis virtutis co- gnosceretur. Quod etiam observavit Hierony- mus in Comment. ad h. l. Christi unctio eo expleta est tempore, quando baptisatus est in Jordane, & Spiritus Sanctus in specie columbæ descendit super eum. Quæ intelligenda de unctionis significatione & declaratione, ut Hilarius & Athanasius monuit. Nam unctio ipsa, vel communicatio donorum Spi- ritus S. in ipsa incarnatione facta est. Quo de Chry- sostomus homil. de Spiritu S. Christus ab eo tempore, quo Salvator dignatus est assumere creaturam no- stram, impletus est Spiritu S. & Augustin. l. 15. de Trin. cap. 46. Non tunc Christus unctus Spir. San- cto est, quando super eum baptisatum velut columba descendit, sed ista mystica & invisibili unctione tunc intelligendus est unctus, quando verbum DEI caro factum est. Quod etiam monuit Remigius in Ex- plic. Ebr. 1, 9. Albinus Alcuinus l. 11. contr. Felic. Urgell. Hugo Etherianus l. de Hæref. 3. c. 10. Theophyl. Comment. ad Marc. 1. Omnes in eo conveniunt, unctionem de donorum Spir. S. communicatione intelligenda esse. Nemo vero reperitur facile, qui unctionem per impositionem officii explicarit. Sensus ergo est in verbis Prophetæ, quem verba ipsa inferunt: Spiritus Domini est super me, eo quod unxerit Dominus me ad annunciandum Evangelium, hoc est, Spiritus Domini, Spiritus Sapientiæ, Spiritus virtutis &c. super me requiescit, ideo quod unxerit me Dominus Spiritu Sancto, ceu o- leo lætitiæ & donis ejus, ἐκ τοῦ μέτρου, eo fini, ut Evangelium annunciarem, & ut mederer contritis corde. Ubi manifestum est unctionem esse causam, cur requiescat & maneat super Christum Spir. S.

& finem hujus unctionis esse officium Propheticum, & redemtorium vel salvatorium, ad quod Sacerdota- lis & Regii muneris partes pertinere constat. Quem sensum confirmat explicatio Grotii ad Luc. 4, 18. ὅ ἕνεκεν ἔχρισέ με; videtur, inquit, ὅ ἕνεκεν aliquid consequens designare: cum contra ex usu Hellenista- rum antecedens significet: respondet enim Hebr. יַעַן, quæ vox non significat propterea, sed eo quod, ut Ge- nes. 22, 16. ὅ ἕνεκεν ἐποίησας τὸ ῥῆμα τῦτο καὶ ἐκ ἐ- φείσω τῦ ὑῖ σκ τῦ ἀγαπητῦ, ἦ μὴν εὐλογῶν εὐ- λογήσω σε. Ubi itidem ut hic in Hebræo est יַעַן, quam vocem alibi LXX. vertunt per ἀνθ' ὧν. Nec ullius hi- li ratio est, quam affert Grotius; ἔχρισϵ hic non do- nationem Spiritus significat (idem enim sui ipsius causa redderetur) sed injunctum munus. Non enim idem sui ipsius causa redditur; Sed ideo, quia unctus est Spiritu Sancto, requiescit & manet super ipsum Spiri- tus, cum immensa donorum suorum plenitudine. Alii sermonem hic esse ajunt de revelata & manifesta missione Spiritus Sancti in Christum Filium DEI, cum jam homo factus consecraretur publice in Baptismo, ad suscipiendam & perficiendam vo- cationem suam, quod indicet in hunc finem esse Spiritum S. in sese, ut ungeretur: vel etiam ideo, quod unctus esset Spiritu S. descendisse Spiritum S. su- per eum publice, ut unctio ista palam demonstraretur.

Quod ad Objectum præconii, quibus nempe Evangelium annunciet, non est, quod admittamus vocem עֲנָוִים secus legendam esse, aut aliter lectam a LXX. fuisse: siquidem non tantum cum scribitur עֲנָוִים, sed etiam cum ita occurrit, ut hoc loco scri- pta est, עֲנָוִים miseros & egenos significet, ideoque a LXX. Interpp. recte reddi potuerit πτωχοῖς, etsi aliter non legerint, quam nos. Non ergo cum Vul- gata MANSUETI, non cum Grotio BONI, ac pa- tienter mala inflicta tolerantes, sed cum LXX. In- terpp. cum S. Luca, imo cum ipso Christo PAUPE- RES & MISERI intelliguntur, quemadmodum & Matth. 11. hoc objectum definitur ᾖ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγε- λίζονται. Et agnoscit Grotius Annot. ad Luc. hanc significationem rectius congruere. Cujus locum integrum adjicimus: (πτωχοῖς) Inter diversitates le- ctionum, quæ in Hebræis codicibus occurrunt, nulla est frequentior ea, quæ nata est ex literarum ו & י in- ter se commutatione. Quare hæc ipsa vox, quæ hic apud Prophetam exstat, in Psal. 34, 3. 9, 13. & 19. & Prov. 16, 19. ab aliis עַנְיֵי ab aliis עֲנָוִים scribi- tur, agnoscentibus Masoretis, quorum auctoritatem Judæi sequuntur. Sed & alibi, ubi non nisi עֲנָוִים legitur, quomodo hoc Prophetæ loco scriptum habemus, LXX. vertunt πένητες. Ut in loco Psalmi apud He- bræos 10, 17. 22, 27. Sane origo vocis ostendit proprie miseriam hac voce significari: postea vero translatam ad modestia & submissi animi denotationem, quod & voce ταπεινῶν diximus. Et huic loco multo aptior est illa miseri status, quam animi modesti significatio.

Vers. eod. MISIT ME, UT MEDERER CONTRI- TIS CORDE] In Hebræo: Ut obligarem contritos corde: nempe quomodo boni chirurgi vulnera obligant, sic ego jussus sum illorum dolorem mitigare meis vaticiniis.

At non de dolore & contritione ob malum quod- dam corporale præcipue hic res est, nec de obliga- tione, quæ sit solum in vulnere, sed de malo spiri- tuali, quo conteruntur maxime corda & reddimur συντετριμμένοι τὴν καρδίαν ob vim peccati, consci- entia angorem, & legis maledictionem, quibus malis medetur Messias (de quo sermo est) non vaticiniis, nec sola prædicatione, sed efficaci sanatione, & vul- nerum conscientiæ curatione. Tali enim Medico opus est Matth. 9. & talis Christi est medicatio Es. 53. 1. Petr. 2. confer Es. 25, 4. Neque vero πτωχοὶ illi, quibus Evangelium prædicatur, sunt, qui externis mundi divitiis carent, aut qui miseri sunt ob cor- porales calamitates, & miserias, siquidem etiam Reges, ac principes vocarit antea Propheta, qui per Evangelium ad Christum convertendi sunt, neque acceptio personarum sit in regno Christi Actor. 10. sed intelligendi sunt spiritualiter miseri egeni, & pauperes, ut è Matth. 5. & 11. nec non Apoc. 3. con- stat. Origenes, Ambrosius, Theophyl. in Luc. 4. per pauperes imprimis gentiles intelligunt, qui ob pecca- ta depauperati, id est, gratia & salute destituti sunt, maxime qui se tales agnoscunt. Talibus enim præ- dicavit Christus Evangelium. Qui deinde dicun- tur contriti corde. Pauperes, inquit Brentius, hoc loco dicuntur, qui gravitate & magnitudine peccato- rum suorum in eam humilitatem, ac egestatem conje- cti sunt, ut sentiant sibi fame justitiæ perpetuo per- eundum esse. Quocunq́; enim se vertunt, nullam in- veniunt justitiam, qua saturentur & serventur: In lege multa quidem pia & honesta mandantur, sed deprehendunt carnem esse imbecilliorem, quam quod possit ea, quæ lex exigit, vere præstare. In humanis traditionibus proponuntur varia, speciem quidem pietatis habentia, sed quæ adversus portas inferi con- stare, & factorem servare non possunt. Quid ergo faciant? quo se vertant? Certe cum inveniant in se peccatum, & non queant nec ex divina lege, nec ex humanis traditionibus ullam justitiam assequi, nihil aliud reliquum est, quam ut fame justitiæ pereant. Hæc est ingens egestas, hæc est gravissima pauper- tas, quæ animum sic deprimit, ut sentiat se ad infer- num usq; detrudendum esse. Sed bene confidamus & expergiscamur. Filius enim Dei unctus est Spi- ritu sancto, & missus ut fungatur officio veri Sacer- dotis, videlicet, ut adnunciet pauperibus Evan- gelion. Quod ergo est illud Christi Filii Dei Evan- gelion? Non certe tale est Evangelion, quod pro- mittat corporalia bona. Neque enim talia bona re- quirunt pauperes spiritu. Neque talibus refocillan- tur, etiamsi plurima & maxima contingant. Inve- niunt haud difficulter, quo ventrem pascant, sed non inveniunt, quo famem & egestatem mentis su- stentent. Hic enim opus est non corporalibus, sed spiritualibus & cœlestibus bonis. Evangelion igi- tur Christi, filii Dei, hoc est, quod promittit & af- fert vera & cœlestia bona. Adnunciat enim Chri- stus, quod ipse sit verus peccatorum expiator, quod sit verus reconciliator inter Deum & hominem, quod donet omnibus in ipsum credentibus suam ipsius justitiam, ut quotquot in ipsum credunt, re- putentur coram Deo justi, & serventur. Proinde Symmachus, notante Hieronymo, & Theodotio, sensum expresserunt, dum exposuêre: AD ALLI- GANDA VULNERA PECCATORUM. Nec aliter Christus interpretatus est Luc. 4. Non certe respexit contritos ob captivitatem. De malis spi- ritualibus ac medicina, quam iisdem attulit, intelli- gendam esse docuit. De sanatione illa Brentius recte: Filius unctus est & missus ad hoc officium, ut medeatur, ut obliget vulnera confracti cordis, & cu- ret ea suo malagmate. Quod ergo est malagma illud, quo Filius Dei contritiones cordis curat? Non est è pharmacopolio quodam terreno, nec è Babylone aut Roma, sed ex ipso cœlo ad nos delatum, videli- cet Evangelion de expiatione peccati per Christum, de justitia Christi nobis donata, de placatione iræ Dei per Christum, de mitigatione divinæ sententiæ propter Christum. Pater omne judicium, inquit, dedit filio, ut omnes honorent filium, sicut honorant Patrem. Et mox: Amen, amen dico vobis: Qui sermonem meum audit, & credit ei, qui misit me, habet vitam æter- nam, & in condemnationem non veniet, sed transivit a morte ad vitam. Habes malagma, quod filius Dei attulit. Hoc si cordi sententia perpetuæ condemna- tionis vulnerato imposueris, continuo fequetur vera & æterna sanitas. Non prætereundum hoc loco, quod particulam hanc libenter expunctam cuperet Grotius è Codice S. Lucæ. Ita enim habet ad Luc. 4, 18. Κηρύξαι : Quod ante hanc vocem ha- bent codices quidam ἰάσασθαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν non fuisse in libris Græcis veteribus ex O- rigine apparet. Sed nec in antiquissimis Latinorum Codi- cibus apparuisse ex Ambrosii ad hunc locum explicatio- ne facile est collectu. Quare cum & nunc antiqui codices supersint, qui hanc particulam non habeant, probabilius multo est, additam ex Esaia & interpre- tibus LXX. quam ab aliis exscriptoribus omissam. Nam eodem modo Latina editio ex Esaia additum ha- bet commate fequenti, & diem retributionis, quod neq; in Græcis, neq; in Syriacis exstat. Sæpe autem nostri Scriptores Prophetarum locis utuntur ea liber- tate, ut verba quædam in medio omittant, quod hic eo minore sensus damno fieri potuit, quia Prophetæ variatio sæpe loquendi genere rem eandem exprimit. Sed hæ rationes ficulneæ sunt. Nam quod Orige- nes in verborum hujus loci Græcorum recitatio- ne, & Ambrosius in Latinorum particulam illam omittunt, id neutiquam probat, ipsos in Græcis & Latinis Codicibus suis eandem non invenisse. Notissimum enim est, quod non semper plena re- citent testimonia, sed pro re nata nonnulla omit- tant. Si ex istis allegatis cum omittuntur quædam, omissa ea fuisse in ipsorum Codicibus Biblicis con- cludi posset, in infinitis locis nobis hærendum es- set de αὐθεντίᾳ verborum sacrorum. Qui vero an- tiqui illi codices sint, quos hanc particulam non habere ait Grotius, Latinine an Græci, non indicat, neque diversam lectionem hic observarunt, qui di- ligentissime Codices sacros contulerunt; Erasmus, Stephani, Beza, Valla, alii. Consonant Græci Codi- ces. Consonant Latini, consonant Syri & Arabi- ci, aliique. Qui consensus Grotianum commen- tum confundit. Syrus hoc modo distinxit, ἔχρισέ με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, κ’ ἀπέσταλκέ με ἰάσασ- θαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν: Id cum tex- tu Hebræo, ubi accentus Reviab super ענוים divellit ea à fequentibus, connectit cum præcedentibus, con- sonare observat Ludov. de Dieu ad Luc. 4.

Vers. eod. ET PRÆDICAREM CAPTIVIS INDUL- GENTIAM] Ih Hebræo : Libertatem. Nec aliter in Græco & Chaldaico. Judæi non tantum exules erant, sed & quasi in laxa catena captivi, ut olim in Ægypto : exire e- nim illis de assignatis locis non licebat. ET CLAUSIS APERTIONEM] Quod in Hebræo est פקח־קוח vertunt plerique apertionem carceris. Vox illa Hebræa non apparet. Sed in Lingua Chaldaica, unde hoc loquendi genus credibile est sumfisse Esaiam, quod de ea captivitate ageretur, quæ per Chaldæos facta est, קיחה lorum fignificat: Apertio autem sive dissolutio lori non male per similitudinem dicitur illa, de qua hic agitur, libe- ratio. LXX. hic posuere τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, nimirum quia summæ miseriæ per cæcitatem adumbrantur.

Argumentum hoc unicum invenio, quo Gro- tius probat Glossam suam, quod de captivitate Ba- bylonica sermo sit; quia voce à Chaldæis derivata utitur Esaias : Ergo de Chaldaica captivitatis solu- tione loquitur. Quæ consequentia nimis frivola est ad rem tantam conficiendam, cui tot & tam lucu- lenta argumenta, cum ipsius Christi interpretatio- ne refragantur. Neq; antecedens certum est. Nam quid illa vox קוח huc facit? Rectius Lexicographi vertunt vocem פקחקוח esse nomen à פקח cum duplicatione thematis, significationem augente, ut apertio & liberatio omnimoda designetur, cum qua qua verteris oculos, omnia sunt aperta. Quod agno- scit vit Grotius annot. ad Luc. 4. Quod sequitur קוח esse carcerem, uti multi volunt, nullo testimonio pro- batur. Quare non video cur improbemus, quod doctis- simi Hebræorum sentiunt unam esse vocem, פקחקוח sed in qua literæ θέματος posteriores αὐξητικῶς re- petantur; Cujusmodi sunt ירקרק & אדמדם & מהרחר & הפכפך. Disputant Hebræorum Gramma- tici, talis literarum repetitio sitne ἐπιστατικὴ an αἰυ- ξητικὴ. Sed ut de ירקרק & אדמדם res sit dubia, duæ reliquæ, quas dixi voces, omnino auctivam significatio- nem postulant, ut videre est Psal. 38, 11. & Prov. 21, 8. Optime ergo videntur sentire, qui hoc Prophetæ loco פקחקוח referunt ad plenissimam libertatem oculos huc atœ illuc, qua lubet, circumferendi. De liberatione autem spirituali sermonem esse, satis antea proba- vimus. Nec aliter intellexit Christus cum LXX. In- terpp. hæc exponens τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν. De capti- vitatis enim solutione non loquebatur, cum hodie impletam illam Servator docebat, ideoque nec me- taphorice calamitatem talem ibi locum habuisse si- gnificabat, qualis per cæcitatem adumbratur: Sed de cæcorum visus, vel ut Erasmus reddidit in annot. REVIDENTIA. Quæ de spirituali cæcitate ac visus restitutione sine dubio intellexit. Cur ergo aliam admittamus vocum sententiam, quam quæ à Chri- sto tradita? Recte igitur hic iterum Brentius: UT PRÆDICEM CAPTIVIS INDULGEN- TIAM. Ungitur Filius Dei Spiritu Sancto, & mit- titur ad hoc officium, ut expiet peccatum hominis, quo omnis, qui in Filium Dei credit, eripiatur è captivita- te ac servitute Satanæ, & restituatur libertati, quo beneficio nihil potest homini Satanæ captivo acceptius, & felicius contingere. Nam qui sic liberatur, is non solum consequitur remissionem peccatorum, sed et- iam coram Deo reputatur justus, adoptatur in Filium Dei, donatur Spiritu Sancto, quo reliquias carnis mortificet, servatur in morte & collocatur in hæredi- tate cœlestis regni, ut una cum Filio Dei fruatur gau- dio æternæ vitæ. De hac libertate & manumissio- ne concionatur Christus etiam apud Johannem. Si vos, inquiens, manseritis in sermone meo, vere Di- scipuli mei estis, & cognoscetis veritatem, & veri- tas reddet vos liberos. Et mox: Si Filius reddiderit vos liberos, vere liberi estis. Et ad Ebræos: Postea- quam pueri commercium habent cum carne & san- guine, & ipse similiter particeps factus est eorundem, ut per mortem aboleret eum, qui mortis habebat im- perium, hoc est Diabolum, & liberos redderet eos, quicunque metu mortis per omnem vitam obnoxii e- rant servituti. UT PRÆDICEM CLAUSIS APERTIONEM, seu vinctis liberationem. Sicut ante est sermo de captivis servitute, ita nunc fit ser- mo de captivis in carceribus. Filius enim Dei mis- sus est etiam in hunc usum, ut captos seu clausos carceribus educat, & eos liberos dimittat. Etsi gra- vis calamitas est, clausum esse in externum carce- rem, tamen calamitas longe omnium gravissima est, clausum & vinctum esse spirituali carcere Legis divinæ. Nam qui carcere legis concluditur, & vin- ctus tenetur, is ut obnoxius est peccato, ita obno- xius est maledictioni, potestati Satanæ, & æternæ condemnationi. Quæ graviora vincula possunt ho- mini contingere? Lex enim exigit perfectam justi- tiam ab homine. Sed cum homo non implet eam, abducitur à lege in vincula maledictionis, ut neces- se habeat, quantum in lege & in ipso est, perpetuo perire. Omnis enim, qui non permanserit in omni- bus sermonibus legis, maledictus est. Venit igitur Christus, ut prædicet his vinctis liberationem, quia expiat peccatum, & donat credenti in ipsum justi- tiam suam. Itaque solvit credentem à Jure legis, ut non amplius sit maledictus, sed habeat omnem- justitiæ & salutis benedictionem, ne possit diutius à Lege in vinculis detineri, sed restituatur cœlesti libertati. Lex Spiritus vitæ per Christum Jesum, in- quit Paulus, liberum me reddidit à jure peccati & mortis. Et iterùm, Christus redemit nos à maledi- ctione Legis, dum pro nobis factus est maledictio. Jam si ad Lucæ translationem accedamus, censet Grotius reipsa idem dici quod superioribus. Ver- borum, inquit, proprietas in controversia est. Mihi videntur LXX. quos sequitur Lucas, Hebræa satis considerate interpretati. פקח si quis expendere velit loca, in quibus ea vox apparet, non significat quamvis aperturam, ut פתח sed eam duntaxat, quæ ad ocu- los pertinet, nisi quod ad aures transfertur, quomodo & פצה oris est proprium. Interpretes autem LXX. ut continuarent translationem, quod præcedit אסורים verterunt τυφλοὶ, nimirum quia ut diximus פקח ad oculos pertinet, ad carcerem non pertinet. Atq; ideo plerunq; de cæcis dicitur, ut Psal. 146, 8. Es. 42, 7. At Hebræi amant & propria figuratis, & alias figuras aliis connectere. Cæci autem dici solent, qui in tene- bris vivunt, quod præcipue convenit his, quos carcer claudit. Itaq; apud eundem Esaiam 49, 7. οἱ τυφλοὶ & οἱ δεδεμένοι. Captivi igitur cæci, ut Latinis cæci oculis capti. Utraque similitudo summam miseriam significat, qualis erat Judæorum in exsilio Babylonico, multoq; magis hominum omnium in illo crassæ ignoran- tiæ statu ante tempora Messiæ. Confer eundem E- saiam 43, 8. ubi itidem Judæi in exsilio illo cæci di- cuntur, quantumvis oculos habeant: quia scilicet summa miseria oculis videndi libertatem ademerat. Hæc Grotius. Esto, summa miseria designetur: concedi etiam potest, alludi ad captivitatem Ba- bylonicam. Sed sensu directo & proprio, quem li- teralem vocant, de eo agi non permittit explica- tio Christi. Tum si de causa ignorantiæ hominum tempore Christi, h. e. cæcitate spirituali sermo est, non utique de captivitate in exilio Babylonico hic agetur. At prius verum est ex interpretatione Christi, neque negat Grotius.

## 61:2
Ver. 2. TO PROCLAIM THE ACCEPTABLE YEAR OF THE LORD] To signify the time in which God would show himself propitious to the Jews, if they were led to repentance.

AND THE DAY OF VENGEANCE OF OUR GOD] Against the Babylonians.

Latin:

Vers. 2. UT PRÆDICAREM ANNUM PLACABI- LEM DOMINO] Ut significarem tempus, quo Deus se ostensurus esset propitium Judæis, si pœnitentia duceren- tur.

ET DIEM ULTIONIS DEO NOSTRO] In Ba- bylonios.

## 61:3
Ver. 3. TO APPOINT UNTO THEM THAT MOURN IN ZION, AND TO GIVE UNTO THEM A CROWN FOR ASHES] In the Hebrew, that which is פאר, generally indeed signifies every beauty or ornament, but it is taken for a crown also in Ezek. 24:17. More fully below 62:3, עטרת תפארת.

THE OIL OF JOY FOR MOURNING] Ointments, which were accustomed to be used in joyful circumstances.

THE GARMENT OF PRAISE] καταστολὴν δόξης, LXX. See Luke 15:22. Furthermore, by the mantle here is understood the Spirit of gladness, as the Chaldean interprets here, and the context shows.

AND THEY SHALL BE CALLED IN IT] Those who will be in it. TREES OF RIGHTEOUSNESS] More correctly others: trees of righteousness: because of what follows. They are called trees of righteousness who are firm in righteousness, as if with fixed roots. See what was said on Matt. 13:6. But this word is taken for a tree, and above 1:30.

That the acceptable year signifies the time of the liberation of the people from Babylon, and the day of vengeance is noted against the Babylonians, is not to be said; but it had to be demonstrated by Grotius. For his 'he himself said' does not hold here. Nor was the promise of liberation from Babylon made under the hypothesis of repentance: indeed, since Grotius wishes it to have been made in that way, he cannot understand the year of propitiation of the same. For this is certainly not promised here under a hypothesis. Nor is it about the time of the liberation of the Israelites from Babylon, or of vengeance against the Babylonians, but about the time of our spiritual liberation and vengeance against our spiritual enemies, that Christ understood and explained these things in Luke 4 is certain. But what more certain interpreter do we have than Christ? Furthermore, the Apostle also assumes the same sense, when in 2 Cor. 6:2 he exclaims: Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation. For Grotius himself compares this passage with our own in his Annotations on Luke 4. I pass over the fact that Isaiah himself, chapter 63:4, introducing the Messiah, confirms this exegesis: The day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my redeemed is come, which the thing itself teaches to be parallel passages with the harmony of the words, and it will be more fully established from the vindications of that chapter. Nor does a similar passage in Isaiah 49 suggest otherwise, which we have shown there to treat of Christ. Finally, Grotius himself acknowledges that the whole time in which the divine goodness poured itself out most abundantly under the New Testament is to be understood, the entire passage of which I shall transcribe, because it makes for a true explanation. Ενιαυτὸν κυρίυ δεκτὸν) Δεκτὸν is τὸ ἀρεστὸν, that which is pleasing and acceptable: as can be seen below in verse 24, Acts 10:35, Phil. 4:18. Thus also in Ecclesiasticus 2:5: In fire gold is tried, and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation. Elsewhere it is called by the Hellenists a time of good pleasure. But it is attributed to time figuratively, so that that time may be signified in which God shows himself benevolent. And thus in this place the LXX translate שנת־רצון as an acceptable year, as also in Isaiah 49:8, רצון בעת as in an acceptable time. But in Ps. 69:14, רצון עת is translated by them no less correctly as a time of good pleasure, by Symmachus as a time of reconciliation. The ancients are mistaken, both Clement and the Valentinians, who gathered from this that the preaching of Christ was completed in one year, and Epiphanius and others, who infer from the contrary, if there was one acceptable year, there was likewise one year of contradiction. For how many years Christ performed the office of teacher, the chronographers show. But here this year is certainly called from the likeness of the jubilee that whole time in which the divine goodness was pouring itself out most abundantly. Therefore Paul, 2 Cor. 6:2, calls that time, in which he himself was writing to the Corinthians, an acceptable time and a day of salvation. This time, just as it was among the Jewish people circumscribed by forty years, or thereabouts, after the death of Christ, so in individual men it has its own scope, unknown to us, known to divine providence, which for the most part is extended even unto death, unless on account of grave contumacy it is cut short even sooner. Therefore we are warned not to harden our heart, while it is called σήμερον, Heb. 3, 7, and following. If this sense is genuine and proper, which Grotius assigns here, that one cannot be held as genuine which he sells as literal concerning the liberation from Babylon. But what he adds concerning the cut-off time of grace for certain people must be understood dexterously, lest the error of the Novatians, which the Socinians have made their own, have a place. But this is for another place. As it is certain that there is an allusion to the year of liberation, in which slaves were set free, so it is not to be doubted that spiritual liberation and the time of reconciliation and divine propitiation made through Christ is understood, which is called the time of grace, the acceptable time, the time of Salvation, 2 Cor. 6, 2. Although this year began with the promulgation of the Proto-Evangelium, and will endure until the end of the world while the kingdom of grace endures, and indeed by reason of effect and perfection extends itself into all eternity, when the kingdom of grace shall be changed into the kingdom of glory, yet it can be referred particularly to the times of the New Testament, in which the day-spring from on high has visited us, and the Sun of righteousness has shone with a fuller beam, when Christ preached that the kingdom of heaven had drawn near. In the law of Moses, says Brentius, was the Year or time of the wrath of the Lord against His people. For the law shows sin, works wrath, and kills. Wherefore, those who are still under the law, these are also still under sin, and therefore also under the wrath of God, and in death and eternal damnation: Therefore the time of the Law, rightly called the Year of wrath and indignation of God. But Christ the Son of God was sent for this purpose, that He might announce the time of the appeased wrath of the Lord, and the time of Reconciliation. For since Christ has expiated sin, He has so appeased the wrath of God, and reconciled men with God, that God not only receives into grace all those who believe in Christ, and forgives their sins, but also adopts them as sons and heirs of His heavenly goods on account of Christ. This time, therefore, in which these things were both accomplished, and revealed through the Gospel, and spread abroad into the world, is truly called the Year of the appeasement or Reconciliation of the Lord. And this is so regarding the universal Church: but for individual believers, the year of grace lasts as long as life remains, and that TODAY, in which each one is called and invited to repentance. THE DAY OF VENGEANCE is to be understood as the great day of the passion of Christ, on which He exercised vengeance against our spiritual enemies. Is. 63:4, concerning which day see Zech. 3:9. Which vengeance, because it will be consummated on the last day, is therefore explained by some, along with Cyril and Brentius, as referring to the same; concerning which Christ certainly preached often and much, because then He will place all His enemies as a footstool for His feet, and will deliver them to perpetual destruction, which will be the final, plenary consummation and universal vengeance. Which also seems to be indicated when Luke omitted, while citing the passage of Isaiah, the day of vengeance; because, namely, Jesus Christ was then preaching not of the final vengeance, but of the time of grace, and wished to refresh everyone with the Gospel concerning the year of appeasement. This also seems to be the reason why, among the other benefits, all of which pertain to this time of appeasement, our most honeyed Evangelist, Jesus Christ, wished to add these for the sake of explanation and richer consolation: to send away the broken in forgiveness. Which words in Is. 58:6 are read in this way: send away the broken in forgiveness, that is, set free those who are broken; whence they are brought here by Christ, both because there is also a regard there for the Jubilee year, and because the preceding phrases and the office of Christ Himself illustrate it excellently; especially that phrase by which it was said, to heal the broken-hearted, which Grotius holds as equivalent, nor does he deny that by this locution to send away the broken in forgiveness is explained what had been said, recovery of sight to the blind, even if he is mistaken in that he takes those things concerning medication as interpolations: which error we have noted before. Nor can it be approved that he thinks the discourse is only about the announcement of liberation already prepared, and not about the benefit of liberation. For the words themselves, as they sound, when understood, bring in both: both the proclamation of recovery of sight to the blind, and of the acceptable year of the Lord, which pertain to the announcement of restoration and liberation, and the healing of the broken-hearted, and the sending away of the broken in forgiveness. Which concern the benefit itself of the healing and dismissal of those contrite in heart and broken. The reason is because Christ performs both, the one by reason of His Prophetic office, the other by reason of His Priestly and Kingly office: for both He was anointed and sent. He says that He completes both at this time, in which, namely, He had come to execute that office of His. Although, however, in a certain respect, these two benefits of Christ which we have mentioned are equivalent, they do not, however, simply say the same thing. For in the former, those broken in heart are said to be healed by Christ, as a Physician, and they are joined with the announcement of the restoration of spiritual sight. In the latter, those who are broken are said to be sent away free, so that the release from the bonds of captivity and the granting of liberty may be designated, which befits Christ as a liberator and Redeemer, and is joined with the announcement of the acceptable year or of appeasement and liberty. Concerning which liberation Christ says in John 8: If the Son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed. Let Heb. 2:14 also be compared. Whence it is manifest that the things which follow, that I might place for those who mourn in Zion, and give them a crown for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the mantle of praise for the spirit of heaviness, and they shall be called in it oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord that He might be glorified, are not to be understood as only the announcement of adornment and joy, but at the same time of the bestowal, which the words themselves bring in: PLACING AND GIVING. Nor is it signified only that they are to be called thus, but that this Messiah performs this, that they are truly called such, that is, they are so in reality. For this calling is not only of the name, but of the thing; not a human but a divine calling, which calls those things which are not, that they might be. And therefore when the Messiah calls those who are in Zion trees of righteousness and the planting of the Lord, He also causes them to be such as they are called, that is, trees which are themselves righteous, and bring forth righteous fruit: and the planting of the Lord, which is so planted that it cannot easily be uprooted, Matt. 15:13. But a CROWN is promised for ashes, because He makes us spiritual kings, although by nature we are most abject, and Royal glory crowns those who sit in ashes because of mourning and contempt: As easily as by the transposition of letters from אפר becomes פאר, so easily is it also for this Messiah of ours to convert ashes into a turban for His faithful ones. THE OIL OF JOY, which is the Holy Spirit, with which oil Christ was anointed, Ps. 45:7, is promised for mourning because of sin, by which word our Royal and Priestly dignity is again regarded: because Kings and Priests were anointed: and Christ was anointed with the oil of exultation above His fellows as King and Priest; or it alludes to weddings and feasts, in which both crowns were placed upon the head, and those rejoicing anointed themselves with oil composed of fragrant things. THE MANTLE OF PRAISE. It also denotes festive adornment, or even such as befits spiritual Kings and Priests, whence afterwards, because of such Priestly adornment, and such as is of the bridegroom and the bride, the faithful exult. By which is designated the righteousness of Christ, as that by which we are covered as with a mantle, singing the praise and glory of the Lord, and glorying in the Lord, or also in such a way that we receive praise and glory from the Lord, because by this righteousness we stand before the Lord. That the mantle is said to be conferred for the spirit of heaviness: because outside of this righteousness there is no joy, but mere mourning and sorrow. But where this righteousness is, there also is peace and joy in the Holy Spirit, and it is the kingdom of God itself, which we possess as spiritual Kings, Rom. 14, 17. Not badly does Cornelius à Lapide here, following Rupert: By these three antitheses he signifies the same thing, namely the exchange of mourning for joy and of abjection for glory: which everyone will easily detect and discern in himself, if he looks at what kind of person, and with how darkened, perturbed, and anxious a spirit he was, when he lived in sins, and what kind of person he is after conversion through the grace of Christ, when now, as if equal to the angels, walking before God, he exults with spiritual gladness, rejoices in hope, gives thanks in tribulations, and in penitence sheds sweet tears of consolation: because for mourning and tears he awaits everlasting joy, and the stole of immortality and heavenly glory, in which these things will be most perfectly fulfilled.

Latin:

Vers. 3. UT PONEREM LUGENTIBUS IN SION, ET DAREM EIS CORONAM PRO CINERE] In Hebræo, quod est פאר, generaliter quidem omne de- cus aut ornamentum significat, sed pro corona sumitur et- iam Ezech. 24, 17. Plenius infra 62, 3. עטרת תפארת.

OLEUM GAUDII PRO LUCTU] Unguenta, quæ in rebus lætis sumi solebant.

PALLIUM LAUDIS] καταστολὴν δόξης, LXX. Vi- de Luc. 15, 22. Cæterum per amictum hic intelligitur Spi- ritus lætitiæ, ut hic interpretatur Chaldæus, & ostendit contextus.

ET VOCABUNTUR IN EA] Qui in ea erunt. FORTES JUSTITIÆ] Rectius alii: arbores justi- tiæ: ob id quod sequitur. Arbores justitiæ dicuntur, qui firmi sunt in justitia, velut actis radicibus. Vide, quæ di- cta ad Matth. 13, 6. Pro arbore autem hæc vox sumitur, & supra 1. v. 30,

Annum placabilem, tempus liberationis po- puli è Babylone significari, & diem ultionis in Ba- bylonios notari, non dicendum; sed demonstran- dum erat Grotio. Non enim hic valet illius: ἀυτὸς ἔφα. Neque sub hypothesi pœnitentiæ promissio li- berationis è Babylone facta: imo quum eam ita fa- ctam velit Grotius, de eadem annum placationis in- telligere non potest. Hic enim certe non est pro- missus sub hypothesi. Nec de tempore liberationis Israëlitarum è Babylone, aut ultionis in Babylo- nios, sed de tempore spiritualis nostræ liberationis & ultionis in hostes nostros spirituales, hæc intellexis- se & explicasse Christum Luc. 4. certum est. Quem autem habemus certiorem interpretem, quam Christum? Porro eundem sensum assumit etiam Apostolus, cum 2. Cor. 6, 2. exclamat. Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. Hunc e- nim locum confert cum nostro ipso ipse Grotius in Annot. ad Luc. 4. Taceo, quod Esaias ipse cap. 63, 4. Messiam introducens, hanc ἐξήγησιν confirmat: Dies ultionis in corde meo, annis redemtionis meæ ve- nit, quæ loca parallela esse cum verborum harmo- nia, tum res ipsa docet, & e vindiciis istius capitis plenius constabit. Neq; aliud locus similis Esa. 49. suadet. Quem de Christo itidem agere ibi ostendi- mus. Deniq; agnoscit Grotius ipse tempus omne, quo se largissime divina bonitas effudit sub N. Test. intelli- gi, cujus integrum locum adscribam, quod ad veram explicationem faciat. Ενιαυτὸν κυρίυ δεκτὸν) Δεκ- τὸν est τὸ ἀρεστὸν, id quod gratum acceptumq; est: ut videre est infra commate 24. Act. 10, 35. Philip. 4, 18. Sic & Ecclesiastici 2, 5. Ἐν πυρὶ δοκιμάζεται χρυ- σὸς καὶ ἄνθρωποι δεκτοὶ ἐν καμίνῳ ταπεινώσεως. Alibi Hellenistis dicitur καιρὸς εὐδοκείας. Tempori autem tribuitur figurate, ut significetur id tempus, quo Deus se benevolentem ostendit. Atq; ita hoc loco LXX. vertunt שנת־רצון ἐνιαυτὸν δεκτον, ut & Esa. 49, 8. רצון בעת καιρῷ δεκτῷ. At Psal. 69, 14. רצון עת illis non minus recte vertitur καιρὸς εὐδοκίας, Sym- macho καιρὸς διαλλαγῆς. Falluntur veteres, tum Clemens & Valentiniani, qui hinc colligebant uno anno peractum Christi κήρυγμα, tum Epiphanius at- que alii, qui ex contrario inferunt, si unus fuit annus δεκτὸς, unum itidem fuisse ἀντιλεγόμενον. Per quot annos Christus doctoris functus sit munere, ostendunt οἱ χρονόγραφοι. At hic certe annus ex similitudine jubilæi dicitur tempus illud omne, quo se largissime divina bonitas effundebat. Itaq; Paulus 2. Corinth. 6, 2. tempus illud, quo ipse scribebat ad Corinthios, vocat καιρὸν δεκτὸν & ἡμέραν σωτηρίας. Tem- pus istud, sicut in Judaico populo, circumscriptum fuit annis post Christi mortem quadraginta, aut circiter, ita in hominibus singulis suum habet ambi- tum, nobis ignotum, notum divinæ providentiæ, qui plerumq; ad mortem usq; protenditur, nisi ob gravem contumaciam prius etiam præcidatur. Ideo mone- mur non obdurare cor nostrum, dum vocatur σήμε- ρον, Hebr. 3, 7. & sequentibus. Si hic sensus est genuinus & proprius, quem assignat hic Grotius, non poterit ille pro genuino haberi, quem ceu li- teralem venditat de liberatione e Babylone. Quod autem attexit, de præciso tempore gratiæ penes quos- dam, dextre intelligendum erit, ne Novatianorum error, quem Sociniani suum fecêre, locum habeat. Sed hoc alterius loci est. Ut certum est alludi ad annum liberationis, quo servi dimittebantur, ita spiritualem liberationem, tempusq; reconciliatio- nis & placationis divinæ per Christum factæ intel- ligi dubitandum non est, quod tempus gratiæ, tem- pus acceptabile, tempus Salutis dicitur, 2. Cor. 6, 2. Qui annus etsi ceperit cum promulgatione Prot- Evangelii, & duraturus sit usque ad finem mundi, dum regnum durat gratiæ, imo effectus & perfe- ctionis ratione porrigat se in omnem æternitatem, cum regnum gratiæ in regnum gloriæ commuta- bitur, peculiariter tamen ad Novi Testamenti tem- pora, quibus oriens nos visitavit ex alto, & Sol justi- tiæ pleniori jubare illuxit, referri potest, cum præ- dicavit Christus, appropinquasse regnum cælorum. In lege Mosis, inquit Brentius, fuit Annus seu tem- pus iræ Domini, adversus populum suum. Lex e- nim ostendit peccatum, operatur iram, & occidit. Quare, qui sunt adhuc sub lege, hi etiam sunt adhuc sub peccato, ideoque & sub ira Dei, & in morte ac æterna damnatione: Itaq; tempus Legis, recte vo- catur Annus iræ & indignationis Dei. Christus au- tem filius Dei in hoc missus est, ut annunciet tem- pus placatæ iræ Domini, & tempus Reconcilia- tionis. Cum enim Christus expiaverit peccatum, iram Dei sic placavit, & homines cum Deo recon- ciliavit, ut Deus omnes eos, qui in Christum cre- dunt, non solum in gratiam recipiat, & peccata eis remittat, verum etiam adoptet eos in filios & hæ- redes cœlestium suorum bonorum propter Chri- stum. Hoc igitur tempus, quo hæc & confecta, & per Evangelion revelata, ac in orbem divulgata sunt, vere dicitur Annus placationis seu Reconci- liationis Domini. Atque hæc quoad universam Ec- clesiam: qua singulos vero fideles durat annus gra- tiæ, quoadusque vita superat, atq; HODIE illud, quo unusquisque vocatur & invitatur ad pœniten- tiam. DIES ULTIONIS de die passionis Christi magna, quo ultionem adversus hostes nostros spi- rituales exercuit, intelligendus. Es. 63, 4. de quo die Zach. 3, 9. Quæ ultio, quia extremo die consum- mabitur, ideo de eodem nonnulli explicant cum Cyrillo & Brentio, de quo utique sæpe, ac multum concionatus est Christus, quia tum hostes univer- sos ponet scabellum pedum suorum, ac perpetuæ internecioni dabit, quæ novissima, plenaria con- summatio & universalis ultio erit. Quod etiam in- dicari videtur, cum prætermisit Lucas, adducens locum Esaiæ, diem ultionis; quia scil. tum concio- nabatur Jesus Christus non de novissimo ultione, sed de tempore gratiæ, omnesque Evangelio de anno placationis refocillare volebat. Hæc causa quoq; videtur, cur cæteris beneficiis, quæ omnia ad hoc tempus placationis pertineant, ἐξηγήσεως & uberio- ris consolationis gratia hæc adjicere voluerit Evan- gelista noster mellitissimus, Jesus Christus, ἀποστεῖ- λαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει. Quæ verba Es. 58, 6. hoc modo leguntur ἀπόστελλε τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀ- φέσει, dimitte eos, qui confracti sunt liberos, unde à Christo hic adducta, tum quia ibi ad annum Jubi- læum etiam respectus habetur, tum quia præceden- tes phrases ipsumque Christi officium eximie illu- strant; imprimis eam phrasin, qua dicebatur, ἰάσασ- θαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν, quæ ceu ἰσο- δυναμῶ habet Grotius, neq; diffitetur hac locutio- ne ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει explicari, quod dictum erat τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, etsi in eo fallatur, quod ista de medicatione pro ἐμβολιμαίοις habeat: Quem errorem antea notavimus. Nec pro- bari potest, quod de annunciatione tantum libera- tionis, jam paratæ, non de liberationis beneficio ser- monem esse putet. Nam verba ipsa, prout sonant, intellecta utrumque inferunt, & præconium ἀνα- βλέψεως τοῖς τυφλοῖς, & ἐνιαυτοῦ κυρίου δεκτοῦ, quæ ad reparationis & liberationis annunciationem pertinent, & τὸ ἰάσασθαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν, καὶ ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει. Quæ beneficium ipsum sanationis & dimissionis contri- torum corde & confractorum concernunt. Ratio est, quia Christus utrumque præstat, alterum ratione muneris Prophetici, alterum ratione Sacerdotalis & Regii: ad utrumque unctus & missus fuit. Utrum- que completum dicit isto tempore, quo scil. vene- rat ad munus illud suum exequendum. Quanquam vero certo respectu, hæ duo, quæ diximus, benefi- cia Christi concernere, ἰσοδυναμοῦντα sint, non ta- men idem simpliciter dicunt. Nam in priori confra- cti corde dicuntur sanari à Christo, tanquam Medico, & conjunguntur cum annunciatione restitutionis visus spiritualis. In posteriori dicuntur dimitti, qui confracti sunt, liberi, ut solutio à vinculis captivita- tis, & concessio libertatis designetur, quæ Christo ut liberatori & Redemptori convenit, & conjun- gitur cum annunciatione anni accepti vel placatio- nis & libertatis. De qua liberatione Christus Joh. 8. Si Filius vos liber averit, vere liberi eritis. Confera- tur etiam Ebr. 2, 14. Unde manifestum est, quæ se- quuntur, ut ponerem lugentibus in Sion, & darem eis coronam pro cinere, oleum gaudii pro luctu, pal- lium laudis pro spiritu mæroris, & vocabuntur in ea fortes justitiæ, plantatio Domini ad glorificandum, non esse intelligenda de sola ornatus & gaudii an- nunciatione, sed simul de collatione, quam verba ipsa inferunt, PONENDI ET DANDI. Neque significari solum, quod ita vocandi sunt, sed quod hoc præstet hic Messias, ut tales vere vocentur, id- est, reapse sint. Non enim vocatio hæc tantum no- minis, sed rei, non humana sed divina vocatio, quæ vocat ea, quæ non sunt, ut sint. Ideoque cum Messias vocat eos, qui sunt in Sion arbores justitiæ & plan- tationem Domini, efficit etiam ut sint tales, quales vocantur, h. e. arbores, quæ ipsæ sunt justæ, & pro- ferunt fructum justum: Et plantatio Domini, quæ sic plantata est, ut non facile eradicari queat, Matt. 15, 13. Promittitur autem CORONA pro cinere, quia reges spirituales nos efficit, cum natura abje- ctissimi simus, & gloria Regia eos, qui in cinere se- dent præ mœrore, & despectu, coronat: Quam fa- cili literarum transpositione ex אפר fit פאר, tam facile etiam est huic Messiæ nostro cinerem in cida- rim penes fideles suos convertere. OLEUM GAUDII, quod est Spiritus Sanctus, quo oleo un- ctus est Christus, Psal. 45, 7. promittitur pro lu- ctu ob peccatum, qua voce iterum Regia & Sacerdo- talis nostra dignitas respicitur: quia Reges & Sacerdotes ungebantur: & Christus præ confor- tibus oleo exultationis unctus est in Regem & Sa- cerdotem; vel alluditur ad nuptias & festa, in qui- bus & coronæ capiti imponebantur, & ungebant sese lætantes oleo, ex rebus odoriferis composito. PALLIUM LAUDIS. Ornatum quoque notat fe- stivum, vel etiam talem, qui Reges & Sacerdotes spi- rituales deceat, unde postea ob hujusmodi ornatum Sacerdotalem, & qualis sponsi ac sponsæ est, exultant fi- deles. Quo designatur justitia Christi, utpote, qua nos tanquam pallio tegimur, laudem & gloriam Do- mini decantantes, & in Domino gloriantes, vel etiam ita, ut laudem & gloriam reportemus à Domino, quia justitia hac consistimus coram Domino. Quod pallium pro spiritu mæroris conferri dicitur: quia extra hanc justitiam nullum est gaudium, merus lu- ctus & mœror. Ubi vero hæc justitia est, ibi & pax & gaudium in Spiritu Sancto, ipsumque regnum Dei est, quod nos ceu Reges spirituales possidemus, Rom. 14, 17. Non male hic Cornelius à Lapide præ- eunte Ruperto: Per has tres antitheses idem signifi- cat, nimirum commutationem mæroris in gaudium & abjectionis in gloriam: quam facile quisq́, in se depre- hendet & cernet, si aspiciat qualis quamq́, spiritu obtenebrato, perturbato ac anxio fuerit, cum in pec- catis viveret, & qualis sit post conversionem per gra- tiam Christi, cum jam quasi par angelis, coram Deo ambulans spirituali lætitia exultat, spe gaudet, in tri- bulationibus gratias agit, in pœnitentia suaves conso- lationis emittit lacrymas: quia pro luctu & lacrymis expectat lætitiam sempiternam, & stolam immorta- litatis ac gloriæ cælestis, in qua hæc perfectissime com- plebuntur.

## 61:4
Vers. 4. AND THEY SHALL BUILD THE DESOLATIONS OF OLD] That is, those which had been desolate for a long time: beyond fifty years: which is the time that the Hebrews call עולם.

This observation of Grotius, that a time of 50 years is called עולם, stood in need of witnesses; or rather of examples from the sacred Code. But nowhere will an example be found where עולם is used for a time of fifty years. FROM AN AGE of a day, that is, from ancient times it has been received. But those ancient times are not defined by the time of half a century, or fifty years; and that more ancient times are regarded, the other ages teach: AND THEY SHALL BUILD THE DESOLATIONS OF THE AGE, THEY SHALL RAISE UP ANCIENT SOLITUDES: AND THEY SHALL RENEW THE CITIES OF SOLITUDE, THE DESERTS OF GENERATIONS. Which seem especially to regard the Gentiles. For their regions and cities were desolate from the age, and cities of solitude. For there is no discourse here about earthly places, to be built in a material way. Because as the Messiah dealt with the proclamation of the Gospel of spiritual benefits, with spiritual healing, with the spiritual year of atonement, with spiritual joy, and with the spiritual trees of righteousness and the planting of the Lord, so also these things are to be understood concerning the spiritual building of the deserts. Most explain this concerning the Apostles, who were appointed by the Son of God as architects of the Church in the whole world, and having received the Holy Spirit at the feast of Pentecost, starting from the city of Jerusalem, they went out into the world, and restored the old ruins, namely those regions and cities which had been desolate from the age and dissipated from generation to generation. Jerusalem was laid waste by impious traditions, Samaria was laid waste by idolatry for long times, the regions of the Gentiles were desolate, because they lacked the worship of the true God from the age, but Peter and the other Apostles raised up Jerusalem, Philip Samaria, Paul and others the regions and cities of the Gentiles spiritually: concerning which spiritual structure Paul 1 Cor. 3, and thus also the building of those things which had been torn down, promised in Amos 9:11, St. James interpreted in Acts 15:16. Which opinion concerning the Apostles, as being not strangers, but Jews, can be confirmed from the following verse, where it is a matter of strangers: Since the Holy Spirit assigns these spiritual tasks to both, first to the Apostles from the seed of the Jews: then also to strangers and the sons of foreigners, who were to come forth from the Gentiles.
