Although placed indefinitely, AND THEY SHALL BUILD, can be taken indefinitely concerning any architects whatsoever. But it is certain that the Apostles are included under their name, who were the chief architects in this spiritual building.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET ÆDIFICABUNT DESERTA A SÆ- CULO] Id est, quæ diu deserta fuerant: ultra annos quinquaginta: quod tempus עולם Hebræis.

Observatio hæc Grotiana, quod tempus L. annorum עולם dicatur, testibus indigebat; vel ex- emplis potius è Codice sacro. Nuspiam autem in- venietur exemplum, ubi עולם de tempore quinqua- ginta annorum usurpetur. A SECULO diei, id est, ab antiquis temporibus receptum est. Sed illa antiqua tempora non definiuntur tempore dimidii seculi, vel L. annis; & antiquiora tempora respici, cæteræ ætates docent: ET ÆDIFICA- BUNT DESOLATIONES SECULI, SOLI- TUDINES ANTIQUAS ERIGENT: ET IN- NOVABUNT CIVITATES SOLITUDINIS, DESERTA GENERATIONES. Quæ impri- mis gentiles respicere videntur. Nam illorum re- giones & urbes erant à seculo desertæ, & civitates solitudinis. Neq; enim hic de locis terrenis, materia- li modo ædificandis, sermo est. Quia ut de præconio Evangelii beneficiorum spiritualium, de sanatione spirituali, de anno placationis spirituali, de gaudio spi- rituali, & de arboribus spiritualibus justitiæ & plan- tatione Domini egit Messias, ita etiam de ædificatione desertorum spirituali hæc intelligenda sunt. Expli- cant pleriq; de Apostolis, qui architecti à Filio Dei constituti sunt Ecclesiæ in toto terrarum orbe, & accepto in festo Pentecostes Spiritu Sancto exorsi ab urbe Hierusalem, egressi sunt in orbem, ac in- staurarunt veteres ruinas, videlicet eas regiones, ac urbes, quæ à seculo desertæ fuêre, ac dissipatæ de generatione in generationem. Vastata fuit Hiero- solyma per impias traditiones, vastata Samaria per idololatriam à longis temporibus, desertæ erant gentium regiones, quia cultu veri Dei caruêre à seculo, sed Petrus & alii Apostoli Hierosolymam, Philippus Samariam, Paulus & alii regiones & ur- bes gentium erexerunt spiritualiter: de qua stru- ctura spirituali Paulus 1. Cor. 3. atque ita etiam æ- dificationem eorum, quæ diruta erant Amos 9, 11. promissam, S. Jacobus Actor. 15, 16. interpretatus est. Quæ sententia de Apostolis, utpote non alie- nis, sed Judæis, è versu seq. ubi de alienis agitur, confirmari potest: Siquidem utrisque operas hasce spirituales assignet Spiritus Sanctus, primum Apostolis è Judæorum semine: tum alienis quoque & filiis peregrinorum, qui è gentibus prodituri e- rant. Quanquam indefinite posita, ET ÆDI- FICABUNT, indefinite de quibusvis Architectis accipi possunt. Comprehendi autem sub ipsorum nomine Apostolos certum est, qui præcipui fuêre architecti in hac spirituali ædificatione.

## 61:5
Ver. 5. AND STRANGERS SHALL STAND, AND SHALL FEED YOUR FLOCKS] You shall all be in such good fortune that you will easily find for any ministries whatsoever, either enemies captured in war, or others hired for pay. To stand here signifies to be ready at a nod, as above 48:13.

The Messiah, anointed by the Spirit of the Lord, was not solicitous about the goods of fortune, as they are called, or about good fortune, not about bodily ministries and services, but about feeding the flock of the Lord, that is, the Church, which He acquired for Himself with His own blood, Acts 20:28. But some understand the alien and foreign servants, shepherds, plowmen, and vinedressers as those who remain alien to the Church of God, and are not in the catalog of the true people of GOD, in which way Brentius rendered this sense: What he adds: Strangers shall feed your flocks, and foreigners shall be your plowmen and vinedressers, signifies only that the dignity befalls those who believe the Gospel, that other nations become their servants, so that they themselves may be free for their Priesthood. Which is to be understood not of bodily and worldly servitude, but of that which pertains to the spiritual kingdom of Christ. It seems that since the pious, who are members of Christ, participate in the dominion and Majesty of Christ, to whom all nations are subject, they have a necessity that all nations also serve them, that is, be of help for good. Which is not an inconsistent explanation. For although these things seem to be of the same opinion as that which was said in the preceding chapter: the sons of foreigners shall build your walls, and their kings shall serve you, yet since it is said not only of the Apostles, and those who from the Jews believed in Christ, but of the universal Church gathered from Jews and Gentiles, you shall be called the priests of the Lord, in the judgment of Brentius, it must be understood that in this antithesis, by strangers and sons of foreigners, those who have approached from the Gentiles are not to be understood, but those who are alien to the Church. Others understand that the shepherds, plowmen, and vinedressers will be foreigners to the Jews, but converted to Christ. Clearly, says Cyril, he says that there will be a translation of the law and the priesthood described in it. For the Levitical sacrifice, the name or the thing of the ministry would no longer fit: but these have been excluded, and this glory has been given to those who have been called from the Gentiles through faith. For they have been adorned by the calculation of God, and they themselves have been appointed ministers and priests. For they shall come, he says, strangers feeding your sheep. But this speech is held as if to the Church, whose sheep can be understood as the holy multitude of those saved through faith. This is fed by strangers. For once the Scribes and Pharisees, who obtained the duty of teaching among the Israelites, were slothful and faithless and most unskilled shepherds. Therefore they were cast down from the office of feeding the Lord's people henceforth, and that deservedly: for strangers were called to this, inasmuch as they were designated by Christ as Doctors of the Churches, wise and sensible, and filled and instructed with a sound understanding of dogmas, and men from the Greek Flock, not originating from the blood of Israel, these also turned out to be plowmen and vinedressers. For since believers are often called in the divinely inspired scriptures the chosen land, and vineyard, and garden, therefore it is said in this speech that they will be the plowmen and vinedressers, who are one day to be established as priests of the Lord, and ministers of God, rightly dividing the word of truth, and ministering the Gospel of Christ, just as it is written. Cornelius a Lapide, along with Forerius, Vatablus, and Adam, renders this sense from Procopius: Bishops and Pastors are chosen from the Gentiles and foreigners converted to Christ by the Apostles, who may feed and cultivate the Church that has arisen in Sion among the Jews, so that from its origin it may be called the property of the Jews. Therefore, he calls these Bishops from the Gentiles the pastors, farmers, and vine-dressers of Sion or of the Jews, that is, of the Church, whose first Pastors and faithful they were. Whence Jerome: How many a Prince of the Churches is from the Jews, and not from foreigners and men of external nations. Which Christ predicted to the Jews, Matt. 21, 41, when he says that he will transfer his vineyard from the Jews and hand it over to other farmers. Cornelius indeed calls this sense symbolic, but the Authors cited understand the prophecy in this way, as regards the literal meaning. And almost all Interpreters agree on this. in the proper, direct, and literal sense, the discourse here is about such servitude as pertains to the kingdom of Christ. Even Calvin himself, who although he may have gone in all other directions regarding the above, here nevertheless seems compelled to leave room for the truth. What he adds, he says, about feeding sheep, and cultivating fields and vines, are metaphorical expressions. For the Prophet treats of the kingdom of Christ, which is spiritual, but he declares its full happiness by these types, so that we may better perceive it from examples of those things which are known to us. He adds afterwards a general observation, which may serve to better understand these things: namely, that the Prophets, when they wish to express the glory and happiness of the kingdom of Christ, borrow similitudes from human affairs. If Musculus had observed this Rule of his Teacher, he would not have dreamed here with the Jews of merely carnal things, cattle, fields, vineyards, and other things of that kind: which perhaps provided Grotius with the cause for erring in these, and other similar matters.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET STABUNT ALIENI, ET PASCENT PECORA VESTRA] Ita in bona omnes fortuna eritis, ut facile ad quævis ministeria reperturi sitis, aut hostes bel- lo captos, aut alios mercede conductos. Stare hic signi- ficat, ad nutum præsto esse, ut supra 48, 13.

Non de bonis fortunæ, quæ vocant, aut de for- tuna bona, non de ministeriis & servitiis corpora- libus solicitus erat Messias Spiritu Domini unctus, sed de pascendo grege Domini, hoc est, de Ecclesia, quam sibi acquisivit sanguine suo Actor. 20, 28. A- lienos autem & extraneos servos, pastores, agricolas & vinitores nonnulli intelligunt eos, qui ab Eccle- sia Dei alieni manent, & non sunt in catalogo veri populi DEI, quo pacto hunc sensum reddidit Brentius: Quod addit: Alieni pascent pecora vestra, & peregrini erunt vestri agricolæ & vinitores, signifi- cat tantum dignitatem contingere credentibus Evan- gelio, ut aliæ gentes fiant servi ipsorum, quo ipsi va- care possint Sacerdotio suo. Quæ intelligenda non de corporali & mundana servitute, sed de ea, quæ spirituali regno Christi competit. Videtur, quod cum pii, qui sunt membra Christi, partici- pent dominationem & Majestatem Christi, cui subjectæ sunt omnes gentes, necesse habeant, & ipsis omnes gentes servire, hoc est, adjumento in bonum esse. Quæ non inconcinna est expli- catio. Etsi enim hæc videantur esse ejusdem sententiæ cum eo, quod in præcedenti capite di- ctum est: ædificabunt filii peregrinorum muros tuos, & reges eorum ministrabunt tibi, tamen cum non de Apostolis tantum, & iis, qui ex Judæis in Chri- stum crediderunt, sed de universa Ecclesia ex Ju- dæis & gentibus collecta dicatur, vos sacerdotes Domini vocabimini, Brentio judice, sentiendum est, quod in hac antithefi per alienos & filios pere- grinorum non intelligenda sint hi, qui ex gentibus accefferunt, sed qui sunt ab Ecclesia alieni. Alii pastores, agricolas & vinitores fore extraneos a Ju- dæis, sed conversos ad Christum intelligunt. Di- serte, inquit Cyrillus, legis & sacerdotii in ea descri- pti translationem fore dicit. Non enim jam Leviti- cis sacrificium, non ministerii nomen aut res quadra- verit: sed exclusi sunt isti, ac data est hæc gloria illis, qui ex gentibus per fidem vocati sunt. Dei enim cal- culo ornati sunt, & ipsi constituti sunt ministri ac sa- cerdotes. Venient enim, inquit, alienigenæ pa- scentes oves tuas. Habetur autem hæc oratio velut ad Ecclesiam, cujus oves intelligi possunt servatorum per fidem sancta multitudo. Hæc ab alienigenis pa- scitur. Olim enim Scribæ & Pharisæi, qui docendi munus apud Israëlicas sortiti sunt, socordes & de- fides ac imperitissimi pastores extiterunt. Dejecti itaque sunt ab officio pascendi deinceps Domini popu- lum, idq́; jure merito: Vocati sunt enim ad hoc a- lienigenæ, quippe qui Doctores Ecclesiarum a Christo designati sunt, sapientes & cordati, & sana dogma- tum intelligentia cumulati & instructi, & viri ex Græco Grege, non ex sanguine Israël oriundi, hi ex- titerunt etiam aratores & vinitores. Cum enim cre- dentes sæpe in scripturis divinitus inspiratis vocati sint electa terra, & vinea, & hortus, idcirco dicitur hac oratione, fore eos aratores & vinitores, qui olim constituendi sint sacerdotes Domini, & ministri Dei, verbum veritatis recte secantes, & Evangelium Chri- sti ministrantes, quemadmodum scriptum est. Quem sensum ex Procopio reddit Cornelius a Lapide cum Forerio, Vatablo & Adamo: Ex gentibus & alieni- genis ad Christum ab Apostolis conversis eligen- tur Episcopi & Pastores, qui pascant & excolant Ecclesiam ortam in Sion apud Judæos, ut ex sui o- rigine Judæorum propria dici possit. Hos ergo ex gentibus Episcopos vocat pastores, agricolas, vini- tores Sionis sive Judæorum, id est, Ecclesiæ, cu- jus primi Pastores & fideles fuerunt. Unde Hiero- nymus: Quotusquisq́; Ecclesiarum Princeps est ex Judæis, & non de alienigenis atq; externarum gen- tium hominibus. Quod prædixit Christus Judæis, Matth. 21, 41. dum vineam suam a Judæis se transla- turum ac traditurum aliis agricolis dicit. Quem sen- sum quidem Cornelius symbollicum dicit, sed Auto- res adducti sic, quoad literalem sententiam, vatici- nium intelligunt. Et conveniunt in eo plerique omnes Interpp. sensu proprio, directo & literali hic sermonem esse de tali servitute, quæ regno Christi competit. Etiam Calvinus ipse, qui etsi in alia omnia iverit circa superiora, hic tamen veritati locum re- linquere coactus videtur. Quod de pascendis, in- quit, ovibus addit, agrisq́, & vitibus colendis, me- taphoricæ sunt locutiones. Prophetæ enim tractat de regno Christi, quod spirituale est, sed plenam ejus fe- licitatem declarat his typis, ut melius ipsam ab exem- plis earum rerum, quæ nobis cognitæ sunt, percipia- mus. Addit postea generalem observationem, quæ ad hæc melius intelligenda faciat: quod nempe Prophetæ, dum regni Christi gloriam & felicitatem exprimere volunt, similitudines mutuentur a rebus humanis. Quam Præceptoris sui Regulam si ob- servasset Musculus, non hic cum Judæis mere carna- lia, pecora, agros, vineas, & id genus alia somniaf- set: Qui fortassis Grotio errandi causam in his, & similibus aliis præbuit.

## 61:6
Vers. 6. BUT YOU SHALL BE CALLED THE PRIESTS OF THE LORD] All Israelites were as priests at the Passover. We have spoken of this in Exod. 19:6. Moreover, even outside of this cause, all who live holily and pray to God holily can be called priests, that is, as it were priests. See Hierocles at the beginning of the Golden Verses. The Stoic dictum: μόνον ίερέυς ὁ σοφός (only the wise man is a priest).

The discourse is not only about the Israelites, but about all for whose sake the Messiah came, to whom He announced the Gospel and the year of favor, whom He wishes to heal and to give joy instead of mourning. As the trees of righteousness and the planting of the Lord are not only the faithful from among the Israelites, but all the righteous: so all the faithful and righteous are called priests of the Lord and ministers of our God. Because the Messiah has made us all priests, Apoc. 1 and 5, of which also in Is. 66: I will take from them for priests and Levites. We have here the vote of Calvin: Although the whole people was a priestly kingdom, we know nevertheless that only one tribe, the Levitical, performed this office. The Prophet announces that in the future it will be common to all. This, however, was not exhibited except under the kingdom of Christ. The restoration of the Church did indeed begin from the time the people returned from Babylon: but it was only at the coming of Christ that the faithful were adorned and distinguished with this dignity. For all the saints have been consecrated to Christ, and they perform that office of priesthood. To which pertains that saying of Peter: you are a holy nation, a royal priesthood.

Vers. same. THE STRENGTH OF THE GENTILES] Riches, as above 60:11.

If this comparison is admitted, and this place is held to be parallel to ours, 'you shall suck the milk of the Gentiles and shall be nursed at the breast of their Kings,' it is in the open how the Church now enjoys the wealth of the Gentiles, while Parishes and Schools are established at the expense of princes and cities; how it will exult in the glory of the Gentiles, while Kings and Princes, whose ancestors or predecessors were heathens and persecutors of the Church, now contribute power to help the Church and to preserve the doctrine of the Gospel: The Church is delighted also in this part of the glory of the Gentiles, while from the learned writings of the Gentiles it gathers in every kind of discipline those things which confer some utility upon it. Which sense most Interpreters follow. Brentius explains it thus: Since under the law the Gentiles ate the wealth of the people of GOD, and delighted themselves in His glory, now in turn the people of God will eat the wealth of the Gentiles, and will delight themselves in their glory, because they have in Christ the remission of sins and righteousness. But where there is righteousness, there is no longer a place for a curse, but only for a blessing, so that even if he who is righteous through faith in Christ is still oppressed by the Gentiles, and stripped of all his faculties by them, yet because he has Christ through faith, he has also such an abundance of heavenly blessing that he considers the oppression and the plundering of his faculties more a gain than a loss to himself, and is certain from the divine promise that a hundredfold will be restored to him for what was taken away, and that all the faculties and glory of this world are to be subjected to him in Christ his savior, of whom he is a member through faith. This truly is to eat the faculties of the Gentiles and to delight oneself in their glory. Thus Brentius: But the former exposition seems simpler, which Osiander also followed: Because those converted from the Gentiles will help the Church even with their wealth, and it itself will enjoy the majesty of kingdoms, while pious Princes use the power and splendor of their empires to preserve and enlarge the Church of God.

Latin:

Vers. 6. VOS AUTEM SACERDOTES DOMINI VOCABIMINI] Omnes Israëlitæ quasi sacerdotes in Pa- schate. Diximus de eo Exod. 19, 6. Cæterum etiam ex- tra hanc causam omnes sancte viventes sancteque Deum precantes, dici possunt sacerdotes, id est, quasi sacerdotes. Vide Hieroclem ad initium Aurei Carminis. Stoicorum dictum: μόνον ίερέυς ὁ σοφός.

Non tantum de Israëlitis sermo est, sed de omnibus, quorum causa venit Messias, quibus Ev- angelium & annum placationis annunciavit, quibus mederi & gaudium pro luctu dare vult. Ut arbores justitiæ & plantatio Domini, non tantum fideles ex Israëlitis, sed omnes justi sunt: ita omnes fideles, ac justi sacerdotes Domini vocantur, & ministri Dei nostri. Quia Messias fecit nos omnes sacerdotes Ap. 1. & 5. de quo etiam Es. 66. Assumam ex eis sa- cerdotes & Levitas. Habemus hic ὁμόψηφον Calvi- num: Etsi totus populus regnum erat sacerdotale, scimus tamen unicam solummodo tribum Leviticam hoc munere functam esse. Propheta in posterum com- mune fore omnibus denunciat. Hoc autem exhibitum non est, nisi sub regno Christi. Cæpit quidem in- stauratio Ecclesiæ, ex quo populus è Babylone reversus est: sed adventu demum Christi hac dignitate fideles ornati atœ insigniti sunt. Omnes enim sancti con- secrati sunt Christo, atœ isto sacerdotii munere fun- guntur. Quo pertinet illud Petri, vos estis gens sancta, regale sacerdotium.

Vers. eod. FORTITUDINEM GENTIUM] Divitias ut supra 60, 11.

Si collatio hæc admittatur, & locus iste paral- lelus nostri habeatur, suges lac gentium & mamilla Regum eorum lactaberis, in aprico est, quomodo Ecclesia nunc fruatur opibus gentium, dum insti- tutæ sunt impendio principum & civitatum Paro- chiæ & Scholæ, quomodo superbiet in gloria gen- tium, dum Reges & Principes, quorum majores, aut antecessores Ethnici & persecutores Ecclesiæ fuerunt, conferunt nunc potentiam ad juvandam Ecclesiam, & conservandam doctrinam Evangelii: Oblectatur Ecclesia & hac parte gloria gentium, dum ex eruditis scriptis gentium in omni genere Disciplinarum colligit ea, quæ aliquid utilitatis ipsi conferunt. Quem sensum plerique Interpretes se- quuntur. Brentius ita explicat: Quum sub lege gentes comederint opes populi DEI, & delectaverint sese gloria ejus, nunc vicissim populus Dei comedet opes gentium, & oblectabit sese in gloria eorum, quia habet in Christo remissionem peccatorum & justi- tiam. Ubi autem est justitia, ibi non est amplius maledictioni, sed tantum benedictioni locus, ut etsi is, qui est justus per fidem in Christum, op- primitur adhuc à gentibus, & exuitur omnibus fa- cultatibus ab ipsis, tamen quia habet Christum per fidem, habet & tantam cœlestis benedictionis copiam, ut oppressionem & facultatum direptio- nem ducat sibi magis lucro, quam detrimento, ac certus sit ex divina promissione, pro ablatis sibi restituenda centupla, adeoque omnes hujus mun- di facultates, & gloriam sibi in Christo servatore suo, cujus est membrum per fidem, subjicienda. Hoc vere est comedere facultates Gentium & in glo- ria earum sese oblectare. Hæc Brentius: Simpli- cior autem videtur prior expositio: quam etiam se- quutus est Osiander: Quia ex gentibus conversi opi- bus etiam suis juvabunt Ecclesiam, & ipsa fruetur re- gnorum majestate, dum pii Principes imperiorum suo- rum potentia & splendore utentur ad conservandam & amplificandam Ecclesiam Dei.

## 61:7
Vers. 7. FOR YOUR SHAME DOUBLE] The Chaldean: For your shame, double things. That is, I will give you double honors, as follows.

AND FOR BLUSHING THEY SHALL PRAISE THEIR PORTION]

The same Chaldean not badly: And blushing shall come to them who praise their portion. That is, idols: just as God is the portion of the pious, Psalm 73:26 and elsewhere.

FOR THIS IN THEIR LAND THEY SHALL POSSESS DOUBLE] He changes the person: for he passes from the second to the third; as often happens. For these things pertain to the Jews.

The Vulgate is rightly emended: for your shame not double, but double things (you shall receive); but what follows, 'for blushing they shall praise their portion,' is wrongly drawn to the idols of the Chaldeans. From the Hebrew it should be rendered thus: And for ignominy they shall exult in their portion. For although the person is changed by reason of the phrase, the sense nevertheless is the same. Because this is not unusual in the prophetic style. If one wishes it to be referred to others at all, it is not necessary that we understand the Chaldeans and believe that idols are designated. For it is a general description, which is contained in the Chaldean. And blushing shall come to them who praise their portion. Which can apply to those who trust in themselves and their own faculties. Moreover, those words: FOR THIS IN THEIR LAND THEY SHALL POSSESS DOUBLE, do not speak of Judea, but of the heavenly inheritance, because the faithful do not have their possession here but await it in the abiding city, Heb. 13, where double, that is, manifold things are repaid to them. And the things that are added, EVERLASTING JOY SHALL BE UNTO THEM, sufficiently teach that the discourse is about the other life. For here there is no solid and perpetual joy: much less everlasting. For in temporal things, as Cyril says here, we do not expect the remuneration to be, but in long hope and everlasting life and in goods exceeding thought and speech. Nor is there any other meaning to this promise, made to the faithful sustaining ignominy, than that which Christ promises them in Matt. 5: Blessed are you, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you, lying, for my sake. Rejoice and be exceeding glad, for your reward is great in heaven. It had to be proven that these things pertain to the Jews, and to them alone. Just as the paracletic office of the Messiah, so the benefits which are promised in this truly Evangelical sermon, pertain to all men, from whom the Gentiles cannot be excluded.

Latin:

Vers. 7. PRO CONFUSIONE VESTRA DUPLICI] Chaldæus: Pro pudore vestro duplicia. Id est, honores du- plos dabo vobis, ut sequitur.

ET RUBORE LAUDABUNT PARTEM SUAM]

Idem Chaldæus non male: Et rubor illis veniet, qui laudant partem suam. Id est, idola: sicut Deus est pars piorum Plal. 73, 26. & alibi.

PROPTER HOC IN TERRA SUA DUPLICIA POSSIDEBUNT] Mutat personam: transit enim de se- cunda ad tertiam; ut saepe. Nam ad Judaeos haec perti- nent.

Recte Vulgata emendatur: pro confusione ve- stra non duplici, sed duplicia (accipietis;) sed quae sequuntur, pro rubore laudabunt partem suam, per- peram ad Idola Chaldaeorum trahuntur. Ex Ebraeo ita reddenda. Et pro ignominia exultabunt in por- tione sua. Nam quamvis mutetur persona ratione phraseos, sensus tamen idem est. Quia hoc pro- phetico stylo insolens non est. Si omnino referri ad alios velit, non necesse est, ut Chaldaeos intel- ligamus & idola designari credamus. Nam gene- ralis est descriptio, quae in Chaldaeo habetur. Et rubor illis veniet, qui laudant partem suam. Quae convenire potest iis, qui in se & facultatibus suis confidunt. Verba autem illa: PROPTER HOC IN TERRA SUA DUPLICIA POSSIDE- BUNT, non de Judaea loquuntur, sed de haeredi- tate caelesti, quia fideles non habent hic posses- sionem suam sed expectant eam in civitate manen- te Ebr. 13. ubi duplicia, hoc est, multiplicia ipsis re- penduntur. Et quae adduntur, LAETITIA SEM- PITERNA ERIT EIS, satis docent de altera vita sermonem esse. Hic enim solida, & perpetua non est laetitia: nedum sempiterna. Nam in tem- porariis rebus, ut hic Cyrillus, non expectamus fore remunerationem, sed in spe longa & vita sempiterna & in bonis cogitationem & orationem excedentibus. Neq; alia mens huic promissioni, fidelibus igno- miniam sustinentibus factae, quam cum illis Chri- stus Matth. 5. promittit: Beati estis, cum maledixe- rint vobis homines, & persecuti vos fuerint, & dixe- rint omne malum adversus vos, mentientes propter me. Gaudete & exultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in caelis. Ad Judaeos haec pertinere, eos- que solos, probandum erat. Ut Messiae officium paracleticum, ita beneficia, quae in hac concione vere Evangelica promittuntur, ad omnes homines pertinent, à quibus gentes excludi non possunt.

## 61:8
Vers. 8.

HATING ROBBERY IN A BURNT OFFERING] Both the Greeks and the Chaldean read that בְּעוֹלָה with different points, so that it is from עָוֶל, not from עֹלָה. For they translate it ἁρπαγμα ἐξ ἀδικίας (robbery from iniquity). The Chaldean: Abominable before me is falsehood and violence. And this I approve more.

He therefore approves the Chaldean version more than the authentic text, which indeed cannot be proven to be false here. But our blessed Brentius eruditely elicits the sense here according to the Hebrew text, whose explanation is worthy to be brought forward. What judgment means in this place can be understood from the antithesis on the other side. For just as hating and loving are opposed to each other, so also are Robbery in a burnt offering and judgment opposed to each other. Since therefore Robbery in a burnt offering is the depravation and perversion of divine ordination, it is clear that judgment in this place is taken for the rectitude of divine ordination; for God indeed ordained a burnt offering in the law, but He forbade robbery. Wherefore when men offer Robbery in a burnt offering, they pervert and deprave the ordination of God, but God is by no means delighted with such worship, but rather hates and detests it. But He is delighted with and loves judgment, namely, if worship is performed rightly, according to the ordination of His word. The Son of God therefore says that He confers such great benefits upon His Church for this reason, that He is a God loving judgment, namely, that all things may be done rightly and according to His ordination and promises, and hating robbery in a burnt offering, namely, if His ordinations and promises are perverted and depraved. Or dained, however, that it should be well with the good and ill with the bad. For that this is judgment, that this is his rule and ordinance, he testifies, both in many places of Scripture, and especially in Leviticus twenty-six, and Deuteronomy twenty-eight. He ordained and promised that the Church of his people should be so happy and blessed that its friends should also be happy, but its enemies unhappy. To Abraham the Lord says in Genesis twelve: I will bless those who bless you and I will curse those who curse you. And in Numbers twenty-four, it is said of the whole people of God: Whoever blesses you shall himself be blessed: whoever curses you shall be reckoned in a curse. But because Satan was made, on account of man's sin, the prince of this world, he inverts these promises and ordinances of God in this age, and applies himself to this endeavor, that it should be ill with the good, but well with the bad, and that the Church of God's people should be treated in unworthy ways, while its enemies enjoy every kind of good. And to this inversion God is accustomed to connive in his own, and most prudent, counsel, so that some think that God has no regard at all for human affairs. Wherefore the Son of God affirms that he, since he is a lover of judgment and detests the inversion of what is right, restores the ancient ordinance of God and fulfills his promise, so that henceforth for the Church of his people there may follow joy for sadness, gladness for mourning, glory for confusion, the inheritance of the land for the plundering of goods, and eternal jubilation for sorrows. Osiander in his Paraphrase has briefly summarized the matter thus: But I, says Christ, will reform my Church, even while it dwells in these lands, so that it may be in a better state than before, as much indeed as the weaknesses of this life allow. Because I am the Lord Jehovah, the true God, loving judgment, that is, I will that all things be done and administered rightly. I like it when things go rightly: and hating robbery for a burnt offering: sacrifices offered from goods unjustly obtained are not pleasing to me: I detest every profanation of my worship. St. Cyril renders another συνέχειαν and meaning: For because I love justice, and hate robberies gathered from injustice, and because those leaders of the Jewish synagogue were such: I dismissed them and cast them out. For I will give the unjust robberies and labor of the robbers to others. Furthermore, in another way: The labor or care of the Scribes and Pharisees has been given to others, namely, to the teachers of the Gentiles. Christ therefore says: (Amen I say to you, the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits.) Therefore they, he says, have been cast out.

Verse same. I WILL GIVE THEIR WORK IN TRUTH] That is, I will give them a just reward: as the Chaldean here. For it is the custom of the Hebrews to signify reward by the name of work, μισθαποδοσίαν.

AND I WILL STRIKE AN EVERLASTING COVENANT WITH THEM] That is, I will restore my covenant with them, which on my part will never fail. On my part, Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi will be the sponsors. On the part of the people, those who are named in Nehemiah 10.

The discourse here is about an everlasting covenant, which simply never fails; not that it merely does not fail on one side. Nor is anything held or hinted here about sponsors on God's part, Haggai, Zechariah, or Malachi, let alone about sponsors on the part of the people. But the covenant of spiritual grace concerning the remission of sins is designated. Which is everlasting, and which the faithful enjoy forever, and which he initiates with the Church in such a way that he does not cast it away forever. The sense, therefore, and the coherence are in the open. I WILL GIVE THEIR WORK IN TRUTH, that is, I will cause that their acts of worship be not hypocritical, but sincere, proceeding from a truly pious heart, or also, that the work, that is, the reward of the work of the believer, be firm and immovable for everyone. AND AN EVERLASTING COVENANT

I WILL STRIKE WITH THEM, that is, I will not take away my grace and mercy from them. Cyril applies this to the Gentiles after the Jews were repelled: Therefore they, he says, have been cast out: But to you, who have been called from the Gentiles to the sacred ministry, I will arrange an eternal testament: Understanding thereby either the Evangelical preaching or the eternal life itself: Among the Gentiles, he says, their seed shall be known, and their offspring. Whoever sees them will recognize that these are the seed blessed by God. For those who have become sons of the holy mystagogues through instruction and doctrine on account of their remarkable probity and piety of life are most well-known to all.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ODIO HABENS RAPINAM IN HOLOCAU- STO] Et Graeci & Chaldaeus illud בְּעוֹלָה legerunt pun- ctis aliis, ut sit à עָוֶל, non à עֹלָה. Vertunt enim illi ἁρπαγμα ἐξ ἀδικίας. Chaldaeus: Abominabilis est coram me falsitas & violentia. Et hoc magis probo.

Magis ergo probat Chaldaicam versionem, quam textum authenticum, quem vero hic falso habere probari non potest. Sensum autem juxta textum Ebraeum erudite hic eruit B. Brentius no- ster, cujus explicatio digna, quae adducatur. Quid sic hoc loco judicium, ex altera parte antithesis intelli- gi potest. Sicut enim odio habens, & diligens inter se opponuntur, ita etiam opponuntur inter se Rapina in holocaustum, & judicium. Cum igitur Rapina in holocaustum sit depravatio & perversio divinae or- dinationis, perspicuum est, quod judicium hoc loco sumatur pro divinae ordinationis rectitudine, Deus enim ordinavit quidem in lege holocaustum, sed pro- hibuit rapinam. Quare cum homines offerunt Rapi- nam in holocaustum, pervertunt & depravant ordi- nationem Dei, Deus autem nequaquam delectatur tali cultu, sed potius odio habet, ac detestatur eum. Delectatur autem & amat judicium, videlicet, si cul- tus peragitur recte, juxta verbi sui ordinationem. Dicit ergo Filius Dei se idcirco conferre tanta benefi- cia in Ecclesiam suam, quod sit Deus amans judi- cium, videlicet, ut omnia recte & secundum suam or- dinationem, & promissiones fiant, & odio habens ra- pinam in holocaustum, videlicet, si ordinationes & promissiones suae pervertuntur & depravantur. Or- dinavit autem Deus, ut bonis fit bene & malis male. Nam hoc esse judicium, hanc esse regulam & ordina- tionem suam, testatur, cum in multis locis scripturæ, tum præcipue Levit. vigesimo sexto, & Deutero- nomii vigesimo octavo. Ordinavit & promisit, quod Ecclesiæ populi sui tam felix & beata sit, ut & amici ejus fælices fiant, inimici autem infælices. Ad Abraham dicit Dominus Genesis duodecimo: Bene- dicam benedicentibus tibi & maledicam maledicenti- bus tibi. Et Numeri vigesimo quarto, de universo populo Dei dicitur: Qui benedixerit tibi, erit & ipse benedictus: Qui maledixerit tibi, in maledictione re- putabitur. Sed quia Satan factus est, propter homi- nis peccatum, princeps hujus mundi, invertit in hoc seculo has Dei promissiones & ordinationes, & in- cumbit in hoc studium, ut bonis sit male, malis autem bene, & ut Ecclesia populi Dei indignis modis tracte- tur, hostes autem ejus omni genere bonorum fruantur. Et ad hanc inversionem solet Deus suo quodam, eog; prudentissimo consilio ita connivere, ut nonnulli exi- stiment, Deum nullam prorsus habere rerum huma- narum rationem. Quare Filius Dei affirmat se, cum sit amans judicii, & detestans inversionem recti, in- staurare veterem Dei ordinationem & implere pro- missionem ejus, ut deinceps Ecclesiæ populi sui conse- quatur pro mœstitia gaudium, pro luctu lætitiam, pro confusione gloriam, pro direptione faculta- tum hæreditatem terræ, & pro doloribus sempi- ternam jubilationem. Osiander in Paraphrasi bre- viter rem ita complexus est: Ego autem, inquit Christus, reformabo Ecclesiam meam, etiam dum in his terris degit, ut sit in meliori statu quam antea, quantum quidem hujus vitæ imbecillitates ferunt. Quia ego sum Dominus Jehova, verus Deus, dili- gens judicium, id est, volo, ut recte omnia fiant & ad- ministrentur. Ich hab gern/ daß es recht zugehe: & odio habens rapinam in holocaustum: non grata sunt mihi sacrificia de facultatibus inique partis obla- ta: detestor omnem cultus mei prophanationem. S. Cyrillus aliam συνέχειαν & sententiam reddit: Quia enim amo justitiam, rapinasq; ex injustitia con- flatas odi, & quia isti Judaicæ synagogæ præfecti ta- les fuerunt: dimisi eos & expuli. Rapientium enim injustas rapinas & laborem dabo aliis. Præterea alio modo: Labor seu cura Scribarum & Pharisæo- rum aliis data est, videlicet gentium doctoribus. Christus itaq; ait: (Amen dico vobis, tolletur re- gnum Dei à vobis & dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus.) Ergo illi, inquit, expulsi sunt.

Vers. Eod. DABO OPUS EORUM IN VERITA- TE] Id est, dabo illis æquam mercedem: ut hic Chaldæus. Nam Hebræis mos est operis nomine μισθαποδοσίαν significa- re mercedem.

ET FOEDUS PERPETUUM FERIAM EIS] Id est, fœdus meum cum ipsis instaurabo, quod ex parte mea nunquam deficiet. Ex mea parte sponsores erunt Ag- gæus, Zacharias, Malachias. Ex parte populi, illi qui no- minantur Nehem. X.

De fœdere perpetuo hic sermo est, quod sim- pliciter nunquam deficiat; non quod tantum haud deficiat ab altera parte. Nec de sponsoribus ex par- te Dei Aggæo, Zacharia, Malachia hic habetur aut in- nuitur quicquam, nedum de sponsoribus ex parte populi. Fœdus autem gratiæ spiritualis de remissio- ne peccatorum designatur. Quod perpetuum est, & quo fideles in sempiternum fruuntur, quodque cum Ecclesia ita init, ut in æternum eam non ab- jiciat. Sensus ergo & cohærentia in aprico est. ET DABO OPUS EORUM IN VERITATE, id est, efficiam, ut ipsorum cultus non sint hypocri- tici, sed sinceri, ex animo vere pio profecti, vel etiam, ut opus, id est, merces operis credentis, cuivis sit firma & immota. ET FOEDUS PERPETUUM

FERIAM CUM EIS, id est, gratiam & cle- mentiam meam ab illis non auferam. Ad gentes re- pulsis Judæis hæc applicat Cyrillus: Ergo illi, in- quit, expulsi sunt: At vobis, qui ex gentibus vocati estis ad sacrum ministerium, testamentum æternum disponam: Inde vel prædicationem Evangelicam, vel ipsem sempiternam intelligens: In gentibus, inquit, cognoscetur semen eorum, & progenies eorum. Quos qui viderit, agnoscet, quia hi sunt semen bene- dictum à Deo. Nam qui institutione & doctrina filii sanctorum mystagogorum extiterunt propter insignem probitatem & vitæ pietatem, omnibus sunt notissi- mi.

## 61:9
Verse 9.

AND THEIR SEED SHALL BE KNOWN AMONG THE GENTILES] In the Hebrew: shall be known: that is, their seed shall be noble among the Gentiles. This appeared in Daniel, and his friends, and in Zerubbabel.

THEY SHALL RECOGNIZE THEM, THAT THESE ARE THE SEED WHICH THE LORD HAS BLESSED] That is, they shall recognize them to be the posterity of Abraham, to whom God promised such great things. Gen. 26,4.

This is not to be restricted only to the Jews. They speak in general about the Church and the faithful, as has been shown. Nor are they to be explained as referring to temporal glory or blessing, but to spiritual. AND THEIR SEED SHALL BE KNOWN AMONG THE GENTILES, that is, the spiritual children, whom the Church begets through the word of the Gospel, shall become known and shall become clear even among the Gentiles. AND THEIR OFFSPRING IN THE MIDST OF THE PEOPLES, shall be recognized with admiration. ALL WHO SEE THEM, SHALL RECOGNIZE THEM, THAT THESE ARE THE SEED WHICH THE LORD HAS BLESSED, that is, all who rightly look into the conversation of Christians will recognize them to be men pleasing and acceptable to God. For God surrounds the Church with authority, as it is written about the Christians, the people magnified them, Acts 4. This passage can also, in the judgment of Brentius, be understood of the calling of the Gentiles to the Church. For when the Apostles, who are from the Jews, announced the Gospel among the nations, and performed miracles, many nations recognized that the Apostles and those believing their Gospel were the seed blessed by the Lord, and they themselves also approached the Church, so that they might obtain the blessing. Wherefore it came to pass that the Jews, who had always been abominable to the Gentiles before, became most acceptable and most desired by them. In the Acts of the Apostles, ch. 13, the Gentiles ask Paul and Barnabas to speak the words to them on the following Sabbath. And soon after: The Gentiles rejoiced, and glorified the word of the Lord, and believed as many as were ordained to eternal life. This is to recognize among the nations that the Church is the seed which the Lord has blessed, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET SCIENT IN GENTIBUS SEMEN EORUM] In Hebræo: cognoscetur: id est, nobile erit semen eo- rum in gentibus. Apparuit id in Daniele, amicisque e- jus, & in Zorobabele.

COGNOSCENT ILLOS, QUIA ISTI SUNT SEMEN, CUI BENEDIXIT DOMINUS] Id est, co- gnoscent illos esse posteritatem Abrahami, cui Deus tam magna promisit. Gen. 26,4.

Non tantum ad Judæos hæc restringenda. Lo- quuntur in genere de Ecclesia & fidelibus, ut osten- sum. Neque de temporali gloria aut benedictione, sed de spirituali explicanda sunt. ET SCIETUR IN GENTIBUS SEMEN EORUM, id est, fi- lii spirituales, quos per verbum Evangelii gignit Ecclesia, innotescent,& clari fient etiam inter gen- tes. ET GERMEN EORUM IN MEDIO POPULORUM, cum admiratione cognoscetur. OMNES QUI VIDERINT EOS, COGNO- SCENT ILLOS, QUIA ISTI SUNT SE- MEM CUI BENEDIXIT DOMINUS, id est, omnes, qui recte intuentur in Christianorum conver- sationem, agnoscent eos esse homines Deo gratos & acceptos. Deus enim Ecclesiæ autoritatem circun- dat, ut scriptum est de Christianis, magnificiebat eos populus Act. 4. Potest & hic locus, judicio Brentii intelligi de vocatione gentium ad Ecclesiam. Cum enim Apostoli, qui sunt ex Judæis, adnuncia- verunt Evangelion inter gentes, & ederent mira- cula, cognoverunt multæ gentes, quod Apostoli & credentes Evangelio eorum essent semen bene- dictum à Domino, & accefferunt etiam ipsæ ad Ec- clesiam, ut consequerentur benedictionem. Qua- re factum est ut Judæi, qui fuerunt ante semper gentilibus abominabiles, fierent eis acceptiffimi & exoptatissimi. In Actis Apostolicis c. 13. rogant gentes Paulum & Barnabam, ut loquerentur sibi sequenti Sabbato verba. Et mox: Gavisa sunt gentes, & glorificabant sermonem Domini, & cre- diderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam. Hoc est cognoscere inter gentes, quod Ecclesia sit semen, cui benedixit Dominus &c.

## 61:10
Vers. 10.

I WILL REJOICE GREATLY IN THE LORD] Here the city of Jerusalem answers the Prophet, as the Chaldean notes here.

HE HAS CLOTHED ME WITH THE GARMENTS OF SALVATION] He has surrounded me with prosperity as with a garment.

AS A BRIDEGROOM ADORNED WITH A CROWN] Namely, a nuptial one. It is the same word in Hebrew as above in chapter 3. The Greeks here have μίτραν, which word among other things also signifies a crown.

He dreams of merely carnal and temporal things with the Jews. Zion indeed answers, whom the Messiah consoles: But a spiritual Zion, exulting because of the …benefits communicated and exhibited to her by the Lord. Which some even of the Jews themselves acknowledged: explaining these things concerning the Messiah and his times. The passage is illustrious in Midrash upon that Cant. 1, 4: We will exult and rejoice in thee: which we shall add in its entirety. R. Abin explained that which is written in Psalm 118, v. 24: This is the day which the Lord has made, we will exult and rejoice in it. Rabbi Abin said, They did not know in whom they should rejoice, whether in the day or in the Lord, until Solomon came and said, We will exult and rejoice in thee: in thee: in God, and in thee in thy salvation. Now this is similar to a certain matron, whose husband the King went away, and his sons, and his sons-in-law to a maritime city. They came and said to her, thy sons have come: she said, What is that to me? Let my daughters-in-law rejoice. Again they said to her, Thy sons-in-law have come, she said, What is that to me? Let my daughters rejoice. But when they said to her, Thy husband the King has come: she said, Behold, this is perfect and sufficient joy for me! Thus it was to be, that the Prophets would be coming and saying to Jerusalem (Isaiah 60, v. 4) Thy sons shall come from afar, and she said to them, What is that to me? Let the daughters of Judah exult. Ps. 97, 8. And thy daughters shall be nourished upon the side. Isa. 60, 4. She said to them, What is that to me? Psalm 48, 12. Let Mount Zion rejoice. But when they said to Zechariah 9, 9, Behold thy King comes, just and saved: and it was written in Zechariah 2, v. 10, Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold I am coming, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, says the Lord, and many nations shall be gathered to the Lord in that day, and they shall be to me for a people, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know, or recognize, that the Lord of Sabaoth has sent me to thee: In that hour she was saying (Isa. 61, v. 10) I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall exult in my God; and this is, we will exult and rejoice in thee. Moreover, the Church confesses in this hymn δοξολογικῶς that she is exhilarated by the greatest joy of all and that she exults and triumphs because of the joy of her soul, but in the Lord and in her God, i.e., in the Messiah, whom with Thomas all believers acknowledge as their Lord and their God, John 20, 28. For the joy and gladness of the Church is not in the happiness of this world, in riches, in worldly power, but in Christ the Lord. This is the joy which is conceived from the Gospel announced by the Messiah, concerning the year of atonement, which the Messiah confers and excites, while he bestows and gives the oil of joy for mourning, a garment for ashes, and the mantle of praise for the spirit of heaviness. Concerning which the Church sings, because he has clothed me with the garments of salvation and has covered me with the robe of righteousness. For Christ clothes us with these garments, as is evident from Zech. 3; which are called garments of salvation, both because we put on Jesus himself, who is our salvation, as Paul says in Galat. 3, As many of you as have been baptized, have put on Christ, and because this garment is salvation to us and clothes us against the heat of wrath and the cold of death and afflictions; it is called a garment of righteousness, because we are clothed with the righteousness of Christ, so that our unrighteousness may be covered, and we may be reckoned righteous in the eyes of God. And not only a garment; but he also provides us with an ornament. Therefore the Church boasts that she is adorned, and every faithful person. magnificence, just as a bridegroom (is accustomed to be adorned and decorated,) just as a bride (is decorated) with her jewels. For he who puts on Christ, as Brentius says here, he is joined with Christ in a true and spiritual marriage, and is adorned with such magnificence as no bridegroom or bride, even of royal lineage, has ever tasted in these earthly nuptials. For Christ takes his bride, which is the Church, and every true member of the Church into the communion of all his heavenly goods, so that he may become a partaker of all his righteousness, majesty, dominion, and happiness in the heavenly kingdom. These are the jewels which surpass all the ornaments even of royal brides in these lands. Concerning which ornaments the 44th Psalm also sings: The Queen stood at thy right hand in golden clothing, surrounded with variety. Concerning which Cyril similarly: Not without merit is the person of the Church introduced, bursting forth into these voices because of exceeding joy: Let my soul exult in the Lord. For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and the tunic of joy. He calls our Lord Jesus Christ a tunic. Therefore Saint Paul writes to those who have believed in him: Put on our Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh in its lusts. But those who have had him as a garment, besides salvation, gain happiness and enjoy lasting joy. Christ, therefore, is that heavenly and supernal garment, that tunic of incorruption, which if anyone has taken, he will be crowned with every ornament, namely, that which falls under the understanding, and he will be adorned with the insignia of virtue. For he will be as a bridegroom girded with a mitre, and as a Bride excelling in every ornament. For Christians are powerful and very strong, and endowed with intelligible strength, and are enriched with every kind of beauty and virtue. Moreover, they are also like brides because of their fruitfulness, in that they are decorated with the varied splendor of virtues. We have also dealt with this verse 10 homiletically in a funeral sermon under the title, Priestly Joy and Ornament, which is sermon 25 in the Memorial of the Righteous of Wittenberg.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

GAUDENS GAUDEBO IN DOMINO] Hic Prophetæ respondet civitas Hierosolymorum, ut hic no- tat Chaldæus.

INDUIT ME VESTIMENTIS SALUTIS] Pro- speritate tan quam vesteme circumdedit.

QUASI SPONSUM DECORATUM CORONA] Nuptiali scilicet. Eadem vox est in Hebræo, quæ supra 3. Græci hic habent μίτραν, quæ vox inter alia etiam coro- nam significat.

Mere carnalia, & temporalia somniat cum Ju- dæis. Respondet quidem Zion, quam consolatur Messias: Sed Zion spiritualis, ob beneficia sibi communicata & exhibita à Domino exultans. Quod ex ipsis Judæis etiam agnovere nonnulli: de Messia & temporibus ejus hæc explicantes. Lo- cus illustris est in Midrasch super illud Cant. 1, 4. Exultabimus & lætabimur in te: quem integrum adjiciemus. R. Abin exposuit hoc quod scriptum est Psal. 118. v. 24. Hic est dies, quem fecit Dominus, exultabimus & gaudebimus in eo. Dixit R. Abin, Nesciebant, in quo esset lætandum, utrum in die vel in Domino, donec venit Salomo & dixit, Exultabi- mus & lætabimur in te: in te: in Deo, & in te in sa- lute tua. Simile est autem hoc matronæ cuidam, cu- jus Rex maritus ejus ivit & filii, & generi ejus ad ci- vitatem maritimam. Venerunt & dixerunt ei, ve- nerunt filii tui: ait, quid ad me? lætentur nurus meæ. Rursus dixerunt ei, venerunt generi tui, ait, quid ad me? lætentur filiæ meæ. Quando vero dixerunt ei; venit Rex maritus tuus: ait, Ecce hæc est mihi perfe- cta & sufficiens lætitia! Sic futurum fuit, ut Pro- phetæ essent venientes & dicentes ad Jerusalem (Esaiæ 60. v. 4.) Filii tui de longe venient, & ipsa dixit eis, quid ad me? Exultent filiæ Judæ. Pf. 97, 8.Et filiæ tuæ super latus nutrientur Esa. 60, 4. Dixit ipsis, quid ad me? Psalm. 48, 12. Lætetur Mons Sion. Cum vero dixerunt Zachariæ 9, 9. Ecce Rex tuus venit justus, & salvatus: & scriptum fuit Zachar. 2. v. 10. Canta, & lætare filia Sion, quia ecce ego veniens, habitabo in medio tui, ait Dominus, & congregabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illo, & erunt mihi ad populum, & habitabo in me- dio tui, & scies, vel cognosces, quod Dominus Sab- baot misit me ad te: In illa hora fuit ipsa dicens (Ef. 61. v. 10.) Gaudens gaudebo in Domino, exultabo in Deo meo; & hoc est, exultabimus & lætabimur in te. Confitetur autem Ecclesia in hoc hymno δοξολογικῶς se maximo omnium gaudio exhilara- tam & præ animi lætitia exultare atq; gestire,sed in Domino & in Deo suo, h. e. in Messia, quem cum Thoma omnes credentes agnoscunt Dominum suum & Deum suum Joh. 20, 28. Gaudium enim ac lætitia Ecclesiæ non est in felicitate hujus seculi, in divitiis, in mundana potentia, sed in Christo Do- mino. Hoc est gaudium,quod concipitur ex Evan- gelio à Messia annunciato, de anno placationis, quod confert & excitat Messias, dum oleum gaudii pro luctu, ornatum pro cinere, & pallium laudis pro spiritu mœroris largitur & donat, Quo de Ecclesia canit, quia induit me vestimentis salutis & circunde- dit me indumento justitiæ. Christus enim nos in- duit his vestimentis, ut è Zach.3. constat; quæ salu- tis vestimenta dicuntur, tum, quia Jesum ipsum, qui est salus nostra, induimus, ut Paulus dicit Galat. 3. Quicunq; baptisati estis, Christum induistis, tum quia salutare nobis est hoc vestimentum & induit nos adversus æstum iræ & frigus mortis & afflictio- num; vestimentum justitiæ vocatur, quia justitia Christi amicimur, ut tegatur nostra injustitia, nos- que justi reputemur in oculis Dei. Nec tantum vestimentum; sed & ornamentum nobis præbet. Ideoq; ornari se gloriatur Ecclesia, & fidelis quisq; magnificentia, sicut sponsus (ornari solet & conde- corari,) sicut sponsa, (condecoratur) monilibus suis. Nam qui induit Christum, ut hic Brentius,is con- jungitur cumChristo in verum & spirituale connu bium,& ornatur tanta magnificentia, quantam nul- lus unquam sponsus, aut sponsa etiam regii generis in his terrenis nuptiis gustavit. Christus enim ac- cipit sponsam suam, quæ est Ecclesia, & unum quodq; verum membrum Ecclesiæ in communio- nem omnium cælestium suorum bonorum, ut fiat particeps omnis justitiæ, majestatis, dominationis & felicitatis suæ in cœlesti regno. Hæc sunt mo- nilia, quæ superant omnia etiam regiarum spon- sarum in his terris ornamenta. De quibus orna- mentis canit quoque Psal. 44. Astitit Regina à dex- tris tuis in vestitu deaurato, circumdata varietate. De quo similiter Cyrillus: Non immerito Ecclesiæ persona introducta est, præ insigni gaudio in has voces erumpens: Exultet anima mea in Domino. In- duit enim me veste salutis & tunica lætitiæ. Tuni- cam vocat Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Scribit itaque sanctus Paulus his, qui in ipsum cre- diderunt: Induite Dominum nostrum Jesum Chri- stum, & curam ne gerite carnis in cupiditatibus. Qui autem illum tanquam vestem habuerunt, præter salutem lucrantur felicitatem, atque diuturno fruuntur gaudio. Christus igitur est illa cælestis & superna vestis, illa incorruptionis tunica, quam si quis sumserit, omni ornatu coronabitur, videlicet, qui sub intelligentiam cadit, & virtutis ornabitur insigni- bus. Erit enim tanquam sponsus mitra cinctus, & tanquam Sponsa omni ornatu excellens. Sunt e- nim Christiani potentes & fortissimi, & intelligibili robore præditi, omniq; genere decoris ac virtutis sunt locupletati. Similes sunt autem etiam sponsis propter fœcunditatem, eo quod vario splendore virtutum de- corati sunt. De hoc verf. 10. egimus etiam homi- letice in concione funebri sub titulo, Gaudium & ornamentum Sacerdotale, quæ est concio 25. in Me- moria justor. Witebergens.

## 61:11
Vers. 11.

THUS THE LORD GOD WILL CAUSE RIGHTEOUSNESS AND PRAISE TO SPROUT FORTH BEFORE ALL NATIONS] What is translated here as 'will sprout forth,' in the Hebrew is יַצְמִיחַ 'he will cause to sprout.' And by metaphor, he will cause to appear: just as the Chaldean translates it here. Righteousness and praise, namely of Jerusalem, which this same Chaldean rightly adds here.

Grotius takes the letter of the text concerning the righteousness and praise of Jerusalem only, as about to appear before the nations; but since Christ interpreted the preceding things concerning the time and benefits of the New Testament, and the thing itself teaches that this does not concern the earthly Jerusalem, these things are certainly explained concerning the dissemination and fruit of the Gospel among the nations. It is not a discourse merely about the showing of righteousness before the nations, but about the sprouting forth. Therefore Osiander rightly expressed the sense: Just as cultivated land brings forth its sprouts and fruits from divine blessing: so the Lord sprinkles the Church with the seed of the Gospel, so that those embracing it by faith may obtain righteousness before God, and from this life lead a pious and just life, and, imbued with spiritual joy, may perpetually celebrate the Lord. And this benefit is set forth and prepared for all nations, provided they receive the Gospel of Christ by faith. Similarly, the blessed Brentius: Finally, the Church also has this reason to rejoice, that the Gospel of Christ is not confined to only one corner of the earth, as the law of Moses was, but is spread throughout the whole world, so that it may bear fruit among all nations. The genuine explanation is that of Jerome: As the earth brings forth its sprout, and is irrigated by heavenly rains, and as a garden germinates its seed, which desires the waters of fountains and rivers: So, he says, the Lord will cause righteousness and joy to sprout before the nations: By no means before Israel, so that he may strike down the arrogance of the Jews, but before all nations, which are gathered in the Church. This sense concerning the calling of the Gentiles, the sounder Jews also saw and approved. For thus it is read in Midrasch Tillim upon Ps. 67, 3, where it is said: 'That thy way may be known upon earth, thy salvation among all nations.' Can the Jews say to the nations that the Redeemer is a respecter of persons? By no means, but trusting in themselves as it is said in Ps. 67, 4: 'Let the peoples praise thee, O God.' And here Isaiah 61, 11 says: 'For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.'

Latin:

Vers. 11.

SIC DOMINUS DEUS GERMINABIT JUSTI- TIAM ET LAUDEM CORAM UNIVERSIS GEN- TIBUS] Quod hic vertitur germinabit, in Hebræo est יַצְמִיחַ germinare faciet. Et per metaphoram, faciet ut appareat: quomodo hic vertit Chaldæus. Justitia & laus, nempe Hierosolymorum, quod hic idem Chaldæus recte addit.

De justitia & laude Hierosolymorum solum accipit Grotius literam textus, coram gentibus ap- paritura; sed cum Christus de tempore ac benefi- ciis N. T. interpretatus sit præcedentia, & res ipsa doceat, hoc non concernere terrenam Hierusa- lem, utiq; hæc de divulgatione ac fructu Evangelii inter gentes explicantur. Non de ostensione tan- tum justitiæ coram gentibus, sed de progerminatione sermo est. Ideoq; sensum recte expressit Osiander: Quemadmodum profert terra culta ex benedictione divina germina & fructus suos: ita Dominus Eccle- siam conspergit semine Evangelii, ut fide illud am- plectentes, consequantur coram Deo justitiam, & ex hac vita piam ac justam vitam ducant, atq; spirituali lætitia perfusi, Dominum perpetuo celebrent. Et hoc beneficium expositum, & paratum est omnibus gentibus, modo fide Evangelium Christi susci- piant. Similiter B. Brentius: Postremo habet Eccle- sia etiam hanc causam, cur gaudeat, quod Evange- lion Christi non concluditur in unum tantum angu- lum terræ, sicut lex Mosis, sed vulgatur in totum or- bem terræ, ut inter omnes Gentes fructificet. Genui- na est explicatio Hieronymi: Sicut terra profert germen suum, & cælestibus pluviis irrigatur, & sic- ut hortus semen suum germinat, qui fontium atq; fluviorum aquas desiderat: Sic, inquit, Dominus germinabit justitiam atq; lætitiam coram gentibus: Nequaquam coram Israël, ut supercilium decutiat Judæorum, sed cunctis gentibus, quæ in Ecclesia sunt, congregantur. Quem sensum de vocatione gentium Judæi saniores etiam viderunt & appro- barunt. Sic enim legitur in Midrasch Tillim su- per Pf. 67, 3. ubi dicitur ad agnoscendum in terra viam tuam in omnibus gentibus salutem tuam. Po- teruntne dicere Judæi gentibus, quod Redemptor sit acceptor personarum? Nequaquam, sed confiden- tes sibi sicut dictum est Psal. 67, 4. Confitebuntur tibi populi Deus. Et hic dicit Esa. 61, 11. Nam sicut terra producit germen suum & sicut hortus semina sua germinare facit; sic Dominus Deus noster germinabit justitiam & laudem coram cun- ctis gentibus.

## 62:1 Argument
CHAPTER LXII.

The prophet proclaims that the righteousness of Zion is to be acknowledged even by the nations, and their new name, happiness, and faithful ministers, and he promises defense against enemies, and exhorts to the preparation of life for the coming of the Messiah.

Ver. 1.

FOR ZION'S SAKE I WILL NOT HOLD MY PEACE, AND FOR JERUSALEM'S SAKE I WILL NOT REST] Here God begins to speak again, as the Chaldean observes. What is said here, I will hold my peace, is in Hebrew idiom the same as what follows, I will rest. The sense is: I will move all kingdoms, until Cyrus has gained control of affairs.

UNTIL HER RIGHTEOUSNESS GO FORTH AS BRIGHTNESS, AND HER SALVATION AS A LAMP THAT BURNETH] The righteous one here is Cyrus, that is, merciful toward the Jews: the same is their savior, bearing the figure of Christ, as has been said often already.

Latin:

CAPUT LXII.

Propheta Sionis justitiam à gentibus etiam agnoscendam, eorumq; novum nomen, feli- citatem & ministros prædicat fideles, ac de- fensionem adversus hostes pollicetur, & hortatur ad præparandam vitam ob ad- ventum Messiæ.

Vers. 1.

PROPTER SION NON TAGEBO, ET PRO- PTER JERUSALEM NON QUIESCAM] Hic Deus rursum loqui incipit, ut observat Chaldæus. Quod hic di- citur tacebo, id locutione Hebræa idem est ei, quod sequi- tur quiescam. Sensus est : regna omnia commovebo, donec Cyrus rerum potitus sit.

DONEC EGREDIATUR UT SPLENDOR JU- STUS EJUS, ET SALVATOR EJUS UT LAMPAS ACCENDATUR] Justus hic est Cyrus, id est, miseri- cors in Judæos : idem eorum sospitator, Christi figuram gerens, ut jam dictum est sæpe.

## 62:2
Ver. 2.

THOU SHALT BE CALLED BY A NEW NAME, WHICH THE MOUTH OF THE LORD SHALL NAME :] That is, she will obtain the glory predicted by God, namely that she may be a magnificent crown, as follows. For to be called among the Hebrews is to be able to be rightfully adorned with such an epithet.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

VOCABITUR TIBI NOMEN NOVUM, QUOD OS DOMINI NOMINABIT :] Id est, gloriam obti- nebit à Deo prædictam, nempe ut sit corona magnifica, sicut sequitur. Nam vocari apud Hebræos est jure tali e- logio ornari posse.

## 62:3
Ver. 3. THOU SHALT ALSO BE A CROWN OF GLORY IN THE HAND OF THE LORD] That is, through the Lord, by the benefit of the Lord.

AND A ROYAL DIADEM] A royal turban. You shall be the highest ornament of the Jewish people.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET ERIS CORONA GLORIÆ IN MANU DOMINI] Id est, per Dominum, Domini beneficio.

ET DIADEMA REGNI] Cidaris regia. Eris summum ornamentum populi Judaici.

## 62:4
Ver. 4. BUT THOU SHALT BE CALLED MY DELIGHT IS IN HER] That is, my beloved, as will be explained presently.

THY LAND MARRIED] בעולת properly possessed.

FOR THE LORD DELIGHTETH IN THEE, AND THY LAND SHALL BE MARRIED] The reason for both epithets is rendered.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SED VOCABERIS VOLUNTAS MEA IN EA] Id est, dilecta mea, ut jamjam explicabitur.

TERRÆ TUÆ INHABITATÆ] בעולת pro- prie possessæ.

QUIA COMPLACUIT DOMINO IN TE, ET TERRA TUA INHABITABITUR] Redditur ratio u- triusque ἐπιθέτε.

## 62:5
Vers. 5. FOR THE YOUNG MAN SHALL DWELL WITH THE VIRGIN, AND THY SONS SHALL DWELL IN THEE] The sense is, just as a young man lives amicably with the virgin whom he loves (suppose Jacob of old with Rachel), so shall thy citizens live among themselves. This was true in the first times after the return. The particle כ here is comparative. Moreover, this is a more distinct explanation of the second epithet.

AND THE BRIDEGROOM SHALL REJOICE OVER THE BRIDE, AND GOD SHALL REJOICE OVER THEE] That is, just as the Bridegroom rejoices over His Bride, so does God over thee. And this explanation is of that former epithet.

We admit that God is speaking here. Although Brentius, Osiander, Cornelius à Lapide, and others say that the Prophet is speaking these things, that he himself will not be silent: until the righteous one of Zion goes forth as brightness, and her Savior, i.e., until Christ arrives, which indeed he wishes to reiterate as long as he lives, and even after his death intends to celebrate the happiness of the Church through his writings; yet because he who speaks here says in verse 6: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which is a divine work proper to the Holy Spirit (Acts 20:28), we therefore affirm that the Holy Spirit is speaking these things through the Prophet. For He never is silent, He never has been silent about prophesying of Christ and His kingdom in the N.T. through the Prophets, and thus He graciously promises that for the sake of comforting Zion and Jerusalem He does not wish to be silent or hold His peace until Christ Himself arrives, and executes the office for which He was anointed and sent by the Holy Spirit, and preaches His Gospel publicly, and spreads it most clearly through the Apostles among all nations. He promises, therefore, the preservation of the Ministry in Zion until the advent of the Messiah, so that it may be preserved for the Church among the Israelites. Jerome draws this sense from the context of the chapters. The Lord and Savior had said: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He has anointed me, up to that place where it is written: All who see them shall acknowledge that these are the seed which the Lord has blessed. After which promise the Church responded: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, which in the third Psalm of the degrees she sang joyfully in the person of the penitent people: I was glad in those things which were said to me, we shall go into the house of the Lord. Now the person of the Prophet is introduced saying: For Zion's sake I will not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest. By days, he says, and by nights I will not close my mouth, nor shall my prayer ever be silent: but I will cry out for so long, and join prayers to prayers, until He who is promised comes, and illuminates the whole world with His splendor. Who is this, whom he seeks, whom he desires to come? He puts it more clearly: Until her righteous one goes forth as brightness, and her Savior is kindled as a lamp. Or according to the LXX: Until her righteousness goes forth as light, and her salvation burns as a lamp. Which He said in the Gospel: I am the light of the world; which, when it has been kindled in Zion and Jerusalem, will by no means shine in Judea alone, but it shall be said to her: The light which is kindled in thee, which has gone forth from the Father, has begun to burn in thy borders, it shall illuminate all nations. And all kings shall see thy glory, O Jerusalem, and Zion, who was generated from thy stock, who being exalted on the cross in thee, drew all to Himself, so that the nations may see His righteousness. But the gloss of Grotius, who takes these things as referring to the arrival of Cyrus, is taken from the archives of the Jews, whom Musculus follows especially among the Calvinists, not from the Prophetic context or the interpretation of the Holy Spirit. Whether all kingdoms were to be moved until Cyrus gained power, I do not know if anyone has ever extracted from these words: concerning speech and proclamation, as the Interpreters have commonly accepted. the discourse is not about the commotion of kingdoms: For just as the Prophet previously dealt with the announcement and proclamation of the Messiah, anointed by the Spirit of the Lord, and introduced the Church celebrating the name of the Lord, which is to rejoice like a bride because she is clothed by the Lord and adorned, so now the Spirit of the Lord promises that He Himself will always celebrate these benefits of the Messiah, and that glory and happiness, until the Messiah by His advent completes them, and propagates them throughout the whole world, and confirms Zion concerning these benefits, that she is no longer to be called desolate, but to be adorned with a glorious name, and that Christ Jesus, the Bridegroom of His Church, will Himself rejoice over her. He promises moreover to the Church in v. 6 that He has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem, who will not be silent all day and all night forever. Therefore the discourse in verse 1 is about that SILENCE, for which He wished to provide by the appointment of watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem, who will never be silent, night or day. Which comparison teaches how inconvenient and irrelevant the gloss of Grotius is concerning the commotion of all kingdoms. There is nothing here about kingdoms, nothing about Cyrus, nor about the earthly Jerusalem. He calls Zion, says Cyril, he calls the Church, whose firstfruits were the divine disciples and the firstborn sons, and those who through them were called to the knowledge of Christ, and before others, those who are sprung from the blood of Israel. For the remnant were saved, and many of those who believed. For although we do not doubt that the Prophet wished to encourage the Jews and his own citizens, who, terrified by the prophecy of those evils which were impending in the Babylonian captivity, could scarcely hope for any salvation, and on that occasion prophesied these things also to the end that the people might conceive good hope. Yet he does not speak of the arrival of Cyrus, nor of the restoration of the earthly Jerusalem, but of the arrival of Christ, and the preservation, propagation, and glorification of the Church, from which, however, the Jews could and ought to have gathered that Jerusalem was to be restored, if indeed the kingdom of Christ was to flow from it to the nations throughout the whole world. For that righteous one, and Savior of Zion, is certainly not Cyrus, not even under the type and figure of Christ: but

Christ himself. Because such great praises do not befit Cyrus, nor were the Jews so expecting the arrival of Cyrus, nor did they hold him for THEIR RIGHTEOUSNESS, or for THEIR SALVATION, which abstract nouns are found in the Hebrew. But they professed Christ alone as THEIR RIGHTEOUSNESS Jerem. 23. verse 6. & JESUS, or their SALVATION, Isa. 45. verse 23. seqq. as being he outside of whom there is neither righteousness under heaven, nor salvation. Acts 4, 12. chap. 10, 43. Concerning which righteousness it had also been treated in the preceding chapter.

Furthermore, that it is not a matter of the liberation of the people from Babylon through Cyrus, but of the arrival of Christ, who was about to illuminate Zion with the splendor of the Gospel, as if by the light of a lamp, and was about to diffuse light through the whole world, the words subjoined clearly teach: AND THE GENTILES SHALL SEE THY RIGHTEOUSNESS, AND ALL KINGS THY GLORY, that is, the Messiah, who is the righteousness and glory of his people, shall be spread abroad through the Gospel among the nations, in all the Kingdoms of the earth, so that his name may be made known, not only to a few certain private men, but also to all the Kings of the earth, of whom if any shall have believed in him, they shall obtain salvation, but those who shall not have believed shall be condemned. These things concerning the divulgation of the Gospel into all the kingdoms of this age, and concerning the accession of the Gentiles to the Church, are often and much repeated in this Prophet. Nor do they look only to this, that they may console the citizens of the city of Jerusalem terrified by the prophecy concerning the Babylonian captivity, or afterwards detained by that captivity, but also that they may testify to the Majesty of Christ, who, sitting at the right hand of God the Father, both propagates and protects his Church among all nations, as Brentius rightly [says] here. Some understand A NEW NAME as the name which we have from Christ, when we are called Christians, just as the people of God once obtained the name of Israelites from Israel; others, however, explain it as glory, but not of external political glory. For it is a matter of the Church, and therefore the proper dignity of the Church is insinuated, and it is signified that the state of the Church is to be changed, so that for the despised it becomes glorious, for the abject it becomes accepted, for the odious it becomes grateful, and thus for the unhappy it becomes most happy. Therefore it is said to be called a CROWN OF GLORY, i.e. Although now you are called by enemies foul, base, odious, abominable, yet God calls you a crown of glory, a diadem of a kingdom, i.e., most weighty, most pleasant, and in his sight most beautiful. Moreover, his calling is not an empty sound of letters or syllables, but is the creation and exhibition of the thing itself. Such as he now calls it, such he also makes you in reality. For he calls those things which are not, that they might be. He says, however, IN THE HAND OF THE LORD, which is not 'by the Lord', for thus he would have said BY THE HAND OF THE LORD. Nor is there need that we understand any Ornament whatsoever by the crown, or say that it is taken for rings and bracelets with Sanctius, and whatever other contorted explanations there are. It can be said, with Musculus, that the Holy Spirit accommodates himself in this locution more to the condition of the Church than to a Royal diadem. A diadem is indeed placed upon the head of a King, but the Church is not to be placed upon the head of God, but is to be commended to his hand, that is, to his care, providence, and moderation. Therefore, Musculus himself is forced to acknowledge that the discourse is not about Jerusalem, but about the Church. Thus also Cyril explains the phrase 'in the hand of the Lord': whose entire passage we shall add. He also teaches that it will be very beautiful and crowned with incomparable glory, saying: Thou shalt be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord and a diadem of a kingdom in the hand of thy God. For every holy soul and

the whole Church entirely, that is, the assembly of the saints, it is permitted to compare to a crown, composed of many little flowers, or to a royal diadem shining with Indian stones, and which has a manifold and varied elegance. There are also very many excellent virtues of the saints, and it is not one kind of ornament, but manifold and diverse. Since even the divine David introduces the Church of Christ surrounded and variegated in gilded clothing. In the hand of the Lord, he says, that is, I will protect you by the protection of my hand. And Christ himself also says concerning his sheep or the flock of those believing in him: No one shall snatch them from the hand of my father. Therefore, this sense, THOU O JERUSALEM SHALT BE THE HIGHEST ORNAMENT of the Jewish people, is merely arbitrary. For it is not called a crown with respect to the Jewish people: but because Zion, or the Church, will be so grateful, so gracious, and in the hand of God himself, as a crown and Diadem is wont to be, which is of such beauty in the eyes of God, that no King, no Monarch looks upon his royal crown, received into his hands, with as pleasant a countenance as the Lord looks upon it himself, as Brentius explains. The words which follow in the text, BUT THOU SHALT BE CALLED MY WILL IN HER, Grotius says are to be explained v. 5. AND THE BRIDEGROOM SHALL REJOICE OVER THE BRIDE, AND GOD SHALL REJOICE OVER THEE, that is, just as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so God over you: we admit it; but these things are to be understood concerning our spiritual Bridegroom Christ, to whom Holy Scripture peculiarly claims this name, Hos. 2, John 3, 2 Cor. 11. & in the Solomonic canticle, and also concerning the mystical Bride the Church, that indeed our Bridegroom is so about to rejoice over the Church, the bride, just as a bridegroom is wont to rejoice over his bride, which express the most ardent affection of love, such as is wont to be in a bridegroom towards a bride. This is what Christ calls the Church חפצי־בה my will, that is, my delights. How greatly, however, the bride Church is delighted, that is most especially set forth in the Song of Songs. As for the name of the land, that it is to be called בעולה, our Brentius explained that far more conveniently; who, since he has excellently illustrated this whole passage, I will not be loath to adduce his exegesis word for word: Thy land, which is now called deserted, he shall call בעולה, that is: Married, or joined to a Husband and beloved. But that he speaks not of an external change of the letters and syllables of the name, but of the change of the thing signified, he explains himself. For he adds: Because it has pleased the Lord in you, and your land shall be married, that is, now indeed you seem so abject and deserted, that those who look upon you think that you are a care neither to God nor to men, and they judge that you are deservedly to be surnamed forsaken and as it were a widow, either deserted or repudiated by a husband. But I, says the Lord, will so change this your misery and affliction, that it may become clear to all that you are most acceptable to me, that you are truly she to whom I may say, You alone please me. For with as much ardor as a young man desires to cohabit with a virgin betrothed to him, with so much ardor will your sons desire to be joined to you, and with as much flame of love as a new bridegroom burns toward his bride (and this ardor is most vehement), with so much love will the Lord your God pursue you. But as for what is promised here, if we turn our eyes to those times in which the Son of God, who is the Bridegroom of the Church, took on man, and the Sons of Zion, who are the Sons of the Church, received his Gospel, we shall see it manifestly fulfilled. For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, embraced his Church with such ardor of love that, in order to redeem her from sins, death, and hell, he not only emptied himself of his heavenly majesty, and took on man weaknesses, but also suffered himself to be dragged to death, and what was most shameful, to be crucified, and he did this, not when the Church was already pure, clean, beautiful and holy, but when it was defiled and disgraced by every kind of sin and wickedness. What can be said more ardent than this love? In this is charity, says John, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as a propitiation for our sins. And Paul: Scarcely for a righteous man will one die. For perhaps for a good man someone might even dare to die. But God commends his charity toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. And these things indeed concerning the love of the bridegroom Christ toward his Zion. But what shall we say about the sons? As (he says) a young man dwells with a virgin betrothed to him, so shall your sons dwell with you. Behold therefore for me, turn your eyes to the first sermon, which Peter, with the rest of his colleagues standing by him, delivered on the day of Pentecost, and you will immediately understand what this cohabitation means. For when Peter had finished his first sermon about Jesus Christ, the hearers were pricked in their hearts, whose hearts God had touched, and they said to Peter and the rest of the Apostles: What shall we do, men and brethren? These are the sons of Zion, and they signify openly that they now think of nothing else, breathe nothing else, than to be joined to Zion, that they may become true members of the true Church, etc. The explanation of St. Cyril is twofold; AND YOU SHALL NO LONGER BE CALLED FORSAKEN, NOR SHALL YOUR LAND BE CALLED DESOLATE. FOR YOU SHALL BE CALLED, MY WILL, AND YOUR LAND INHABITED. Again he teaches that he will lay aside the old hatred with which he often pursued the Jewish synagogue, that he will cease from anger, that he will make it willing and fruitful, and will adorn it with a multitude of believers. For Zion, having rejected our Lord JESUS CHRIST, was reduced to desolation, and the multitude of the infidels perished. But after the remnant received the faith, and furthermore the multitude of the Gentiles was called, and these two were founded into one people, and finally one Church was named from both: God grants to it that it may in no way be entangled in its former evils, nor be called forsaken or desolate, but rather that it may become obedient and willing to him: and it shall no longer be called desolate, but inhabited. We see this has come to pass in the very events, and the Churches everywhere placed in tranquility and serenity, and the faithful propagated to an immense multitude, and God celebrated on account of them.

Latin:

Vers. 5. HABITABIT ENIM JUVENIS CUM VIR- GINE, ET INHABITABUNT IN TE FILII TUI] Sensus est, sicut amice vivit juvenis cum virgine quam a- mat, (puta Jacob olim cum Rachele) ita vivent inter se cives tui. Hoc primis post reditum temporibus verum fuit. Particula כ hic est comparativa. Est autem hæc di- stinctior explicatio epitheti secundi.
