ET GAUDEBIT SPONSUS SUPER SPONSAM, ET GAUDEBIT SUPER TE DEUS] Id est, sicut Spon- sus de Sponsa sua lætatur, ita de te Deus. Et hæc explica- tio est ἐπιθέτε illius prioris.

DEum hic loqui admittimus. Quanquam Bren- tius, Osiander, Cornelius à Lapide & alii, Pro- phetam hæc loqui dicant, se non taciturum: donec e- grediatur ut splendor justus Sionis, & Salvator ejus, h. e. donec adveniat Christus, quod nempe quoad usq; vixerit, hæc ingeminare velit, imo etiam post fata per scripta sua Ecclesiæ felicitatem decantatu- rus sit, tamen quia is, qui hic loquitur, vers. 6. ait. super muros tuos Jerusalem constitui custodes, quod opus divinum est Spiritui Sancto proprium, Act. 20, 28. ideo Spiritum Sanctum hæc loqui per Pro- phetam, affirmamus. Nam is nunquam tacet, nun- quam siluit de Christo & regno ejus in N. T. vatici- nari per Prophetas, adeoque gratiose promittit, quod ad consolandum Sionem & Hierosolymam non velit tacere, aut silere, donec Christus ipse ad- veniat, & officium suum, ad quod à Spiritui Sancto ungebatur & mittebatur, exequatur, & concione- tur Evangelium suum publice, ac spargat illud per Apostolos clarissime inter omnes gentes. Polli- cetur ergo conservationem Ministerii in Sione, usq; ad adventum Messiæ, ut Ecclesiæ inter Israeli- tas conservetur. Hunc sensum è συνεχεία capitum eruit Hieronymus. Dixerat Dominus atq; Salva- tor: Spiritus Domini super me, propter quod unxit me, usq; ad eum locum, ubi scriptum est: Omnes qui viderint eos, cognoscent, quia isti sunt semen, cui benedixit Dominus. Post quam repromissionem respondit Ecclesia: Gaudens gau- debo in domino, quæ in tertio graduum Psalm- mo ex persona populi pœnitentis læta cantavit: Lætatus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi, in domum Domini ibimus. Nunc Prophetæ introducitur persona dicen- tis: Propter Sion non tacebo, & propter Hieru- salem non quiescam. Diebus, inquit, ac noctibus ora non claudam, nec mea unquam reticebit o- ratio: sed tamdiu clamabo, & precibus jungam preces, donec veniat qui promissus est, & splendo- re suo cunctum orbem illuminet. Quis est iste, quem quærit, quem venire desiderat? ponit manifestius: Donec egrediatur ut splendor justus ejus, & Salva- tor ejus ut lampas accendatur. Sive juxta LXX. Donec exeat sicut lux justitia ejus, & salutare illius sicut lampas ardeat. Quæ dicebat in Evangelio: Ego sum lux mundi; Quæ cum in Sion & Hierusa- lem fuerit accensa, nequaquam in sola splendebit Ju- dæa, sed dicetur ad eam: Lumen quod in te est ac- censum est, quod egressum est exPatre, in tuis cœpit ardere finibus, omnes gentes illuminabit. Et cun- cti reges videbunt inclytum tuum ô Hierusalem, & Sion, qui de tua stirpe generatus est, qui in te exalta- tus patibulo, omnes traxit ad se, ita ut gentes videant justitiam ejus. Glossa vero Grotii, qui hæc de Cyri adventu accipit, è scriniis Judæorum, quos Muscu- lus inter Calvinianos imprimis sequitur, deprom- pta est, non è contextu Prophetico, aut interpreta- tione Spiritus Sancti. Regna omnia commotum iri, donec Cyrus rerum potitus sit, nescio an aliquis un- quam ex hisce verbis exsculpserit: De loquela & præconio, ut communiter accepêre Interpp. non de commotione regnorum sermo est: Nam ut antea de annunciatione, ac præconio Messiæ, Spiritu Do- mini uncti, Propheta egit, & Ecclesiam celebran- tem nomen Domini introduxit, quæ instar sponsi gavisura sit, quod vestiatur à Domino, atq; exorne- tur, ita nunc promittit Spiritus Domini, sese sem- per hæc beneficia Messiæ, illamq; gloriam & felici- tatem celebraturum, donec Messias adventu suo ea compleat, & per orbem universum propaget, ac confirmat Sionem de hisce beneficiis, quod non amplius desolata vocanda, sed glorioso nomine or- nanda, quodq; Christus Jesus Sponsus Ecclesiæ su- per eandem ipse gavisurus sit. Promittit insuper Ecclesiæ v. 6. se constitutum custodes super muros Jerusalem, qui tota die & tota nocte in per- petuum non tacebunt. De eo ergo SILENTIO vers. 1. sermo est, cui cautum voluit constitutio- ne vigilum custodum super murosHierusalem, qui nunquam tacebunt, nocte aut die. Quæ collatio docet, quam inconveniens & ἀπροσδιόνυσο fit glossa Grotii de regnorum omnium commotione. Nihil hic de regnis, nihil de Cyro, nec de terrena Hierosolyma. Sion vocat, inquit Cyrillus, vocat Ecclesiam, cujus primitiæ extiterunt & filii primogeniti divini discipuli, & qui per ipsos ad agnitionem Christi vocati sunt, & ante alios, qui oriundi sunt ex sanguine Israel. Servatæ enim sunt reliquiæ & com- plures ex illis qui crediderunt. Etsi enim non ambi- gamus, erigere voluisse Prophetam Judæos, ac cives suos, qui vaticinio eorum malorum, quæ in Babylonica captivitate imminebant territi, vix ali- quam salutem sperare poterant, eaq; occasione hæc vaticinatum ea etiam fini, ut populus spem bonam conciperet. Non tamen de Cyri adventu, non de Hierosolymæ terrenæ restauratione, sed de adventu Christi, & conservatione, propagatione ac glorifica- tione Ecclesiæ loquitur, ex quo tamen colligere po- terant ac debebant Judæi, Hierosolymam restaura- tum iri, siquidem ex eadem dimanaturum sit re- gnum Christi ad gentes per universum orbem. Nam justus ille, ac Salvator Sionis non certe est Cy- rus, ne quidem sub typo, & figura Christi: sed

Christus ipse. Quia tanta elogia Cyro non conve- niunt, neque Judæi adventum Cyri adeo expecta- bant, aut ipsum pro JUSTITIA SUA, aut pro SALUTE SUA habebant, quæ abstracta nomi- na in Ebræo reperiuntur. Sed Christum unice profitebantur JUSTITIAM SUAM Jerem. 23. vers. 6. & JESUM, vel SALUTEM suam, E- sa. 45. vers. 23. seqq. utpote extra quem nec justi- tia sub cœlo est, neque salus. Act. 4, 12. cap. 10, 43. De qua justitia etiam in præcedenti capite a- ctum erat.

Porro, quod non de liberatione populi è Babylone per Cyrum, sed de adventu Christi, qui Zionem il- lustraturus erat splendore Evangelii, tanquam lu- ce lampadis, & lucem diffusurus per totum or- bem agatur, verba subjuncta clare docent: ET VIDEBUNT GENTES JUSTITIAM TUAM, ET OMNES REGES GLORIAM TUAM, hoc est, Messias, qui est justitia & gloria populi sui, vulgabitur per Evangelion inter gentes, in omnibus Regnis terræ, ut nomen ejus fiat notum, non tantum paucis quibusdam privatis homini- bus, sed etiam omnibus Regibus terræ, quorum si qui in eum crediderint, consequentur salu- tem, qui autem non crediderint condemnabun- tur. Hæc de divulgatione Evangelii in omnia regna hujus seculi, & de accessione Gentium ad Ecclesiam, sæpe ac multum repetuntur in hoc Pro- pheta. Nec eo tantum respiciunt, ut consolentur cives urbis Hierusalem territos vaticinio de capti- vitate Babylonica, aut postea ea captivitate jam de- tentos, sed etiam ut testentur Majestatem Christi, qui considens ad dextram Dei Patris, & Ecclesiam suam inter omnes gentes & propaget & tueatur, ut recte Brentius hic. NOMEN NOVUM non- nulli de nomine, quod à Christo habemus, cum Chri- stiani nuncupamur, qualiter populus Dei olim ab Israele Israelitarum nomen obtinuerant, intelli- gunt; alii tamen de gloria explicant, sed non de externa politica gloria. Agitur enim de Ecclesia, ideoq; Ecclesiæ propria dignitas insinuatur, & si- gnificatur mutatum iri statum Ecclesiæ, ut pro con- tempta fiat gloriosa, pro abjecta fiat accepta, pro odiosa fiat grata, adeoq; pro infelici fiat felicissima. CORONA ergo GLORIÆ vocanda dicitur, q. d. Etsi nunc vocaris ab hostibus fœda, turpis, odiosa, abominabilis, tamen Deus te vocat coronam gloriæ, diadema regni, h. e. gravissimam, jucundissimam, & in conspectu suo pulcherrimam. Vocatio autem ejus non est inanis sonus literarum aut syllabarum, sed est rei ipsius creatio & exhibitio. Qualem iste nunc vocat, talem etiam te reipsa facit. Vocat enim ea quæ non sunt, ut sint. Dicit autem in MANU DOMINI, quod non est per Dominum, sic enim dixisset PER MANUM DOMINI. Nec opus est, ut per coronam quodvis Ornamentum in- telligamus, aut pro annulis, ac armillis eam ac- cipi dicamus cum Sanctio, & quæ aliæ sunt contor- tæ explicationes. Dici potest, cum Musculo, quod loquutione hac magis se accommodet Sp. S. con- ditioni Ecclesiæ, quam Regii diadematis. Diade- ma quidem capiti Regis imponitur, verum Eccle- sia non capiti Dei imponenda est, sed manui, id est, curæ, providentiæ, ac moderationi illius commen- danda. Non ergo de Hierosolyma, sed de Ec- clesia sermonem esse agnoscere cogitur ipse Mu- sculus. Sic etiam explicat phrasin in manu Domini Cyrillus: cujus integrum locum adjiciemus. Fore quoq́; illam valde speciosam & incomparabili gloria coronatam docet, inquiens; Eris corona pulchritu- dinis in manu Domini & diadema regni in manu Dei tui. Unamquamq́; enim animam sanctam &

universam omnino Ecclesiam, id est, sanctorum cœ- tum, coronæ comparare licet, ex multis flosculis com- positæ, vel regio diademati lapidibus Indicis fulgenti, & quod multiplicem habet & variam elegantiam. Plurimæ sunt etiam sanctorum egregiæ virtutes, & non est unum ornamentorum genus, sed multiplex & diversum. Siquidem & divinus David Ecclesiam Christi in vestitu deaurato circumdatam ac variega- tam introducit. In manu Domini, inquit, id est, pro- tectione manus meæ protegam te. Et ipse quoq; Chri- stus de suis ovibus vel de grege credentium in ipsum dicit: Nemo eripiet eos de manu patris mei. Sen- sus itaque iste, TU HIERUSALEM ERIS SUMMUM ORNAMENTUM populi Judaici, mere arbitrarius est. Neque enim corona dicitur respectu populi Judaici: sed quod tam grata, tam gratiosa futura sit Sion, vel Ecclesia, & in ipsius Dei manu, ut corona & Diadema esse solet, quod in oculis Dei tantæ venustatis sit, ut nullus Rex, nullus Monarcha regiam suam coronam, in ma- nus acceptam, tam jucundo vultu aspiciat, quam ipsam Dominus aspicit, ut Brentius explicat. Ver- ba quæ sequuntur in textu, SED VOCABERIS VOLUNTAS MEA IN EA, explicari dicit Grotius v. 5. ET GAUDEBIT SPONSUS SU- PER SPONSAM, ET GAUDEBIT SUPER TE DEUS, id est, sicut sponsus de sponsa sua læ- tatur, ita de te Deus: admittimus; sed hæc de Sponso nostro spirituali Christo, cui hoc nomen peculiariter vendicant S. Literæ Os. 2. Joh. 3. 2. Cor. 11. & in cantico Salomoneo, nec non de Spon- sa mystica Ecclesia intelligenda, quod nempe ita Sponsus noster lætaturus sit de Ecclesia, sponsa, sicut sponsus lætari solet de sponsa sua, quæ affe- ctum amoris ardentissimum, qualis in sponso esse solet adversus sponsam, exprimunt. Hoc est, quod vocat Ecclesiam Christus חפצי־בה voluntas mea, id est delitiæ meæ. Quantopere autem delectetur Ec- clesia sponsa, id maxime in Cantico Canticorum expositum est. Quod ad terræ nomen attinet, quod vocanda sit בעולה, id longe convenientius expo- suit Brentius noster; Qui cum totum hunc locum eximie illustrarit, non gravabor ἐξήγησιν ejus αὐ- τολεξεὶ adducere: Terram tuam, quæ nunc vocatur deserta, vocabit בעולה, hoc est: Maritatam, seu Marito junctam & dilectam. Quod autem non de externa literarum & syllabarum nominis, sed de rei significatæ mutatione loquatur, exponit ipse se. Addit enim: Quia complacuit Domino in te, & terra tua erit maritata, hoc est, nunc quidem videris tam abjecta & deserta, ut qui te aspiciunt, putent te nec Deo nec hominibus curæ esse, & existiment te me- rito cognominandam derelictam & quasi viduam à marito vel desertam vel repudiatam. Ego vero hanc tuam miseriam & afflictionem, inquit Dominus ita mutabo, ut perspicuum omnibus fiat, te mihi esse acceptissimam, te vere eam esse, cui dicam, Tu mihi sola places. Quanto enim ardore adolescens cupit cohabitare cum virgine sibi desponsata, tanto ar- dore cupient se tibi conjungi filii tui, & quanta flamma amoris novus sponsus erga sponsam suam ardet, (hic autem ardor vehementissimus est) tan- to amore prosequetur te Dominus Deus tuus. Quod autem hic promittitur, hoc, si referamus oculos nostros ad ea tempora, quibus Filius Dei, qui est Sponsus Ecclesiæ, hominem suscepit, & Filii Zionis, qui sunt Filii Ecclesiæ, acceperunt Ev- angelion ejus, videbimus manifeste impletum. Fi- lius enim Dei, Jesus Christus, tanto amoris ardore complexus est Ecclesiam suam, ut ad redimendam eam à peccatis, morte & inferno, non solum exina- niverit sese sua cœlesti majestate, & susceperit hu- manas imbecillitates, verum etiam passus sit se ad mortem rapi, & quod probrosissimum erat, cruci- figi, idq; fecerit, non cum jam Ecclesia esset pura, munda, pulchra & sancta, sed cum esset omni gene- re peccatorum ac scelerum sordidata & turpifica- ta. Quid potest hoc amore ardentius dici: In hoc est charitas, inquit Johannes, non quod nos dilexeri- mus Deum, sed quod ipse dilexerit nos, & miserit Fi- lium suum propitiationem pro peccatis nostris. Et Paulus: Vix pro justo quisquam morietur. Siqui- dem pro bono forsitan aliquis etiam mori sustinet. Com- mendat autem suam charitatem erga nos Deus, quod cum adhuc essemus peccatores, Christus pro nobis mortuus est. Atque hæc quidem de amore sponsi Christi erga Zionem suam. Quid autem dicemus de filiis? Sicut (inquit) adolescens habitat cum vir- gine sibi desponsa, ita cupient tecum habitare tui filii. Ec- ce igitur mihi, verte oculos ad primam concionem, quam Petrus astantibus sibi reliquis collegis suis in die Pentecostes habuit, & confestim intelliges, quid sibi velit hæc cohabitatio. Nam cum Petrus absol- visset primam suam concionem de Jesu Christo, compuncti sunt auditores, quorum Deus tetigerat corda, & dixerunt ad Petrum & reliquos Aposto- los: Quid faciemus viri fratres? Hi sunt filii Zio- nis, & palam significant, se jam nihil aliud cogitare, nihil aliud spirare, quam ut Zioni conjungantur, ut fiant vera veræ Ecclesiæ membra, &c. Gemina est explicatio S. Cyrilli; ET NEQUAQUAM UL- TRA VOCABERIS DERELICTA, NEC TERRA TUA VOCABITUR DESERTA. TIBI ENIM VOCABITUR, VOLUNTAS MEA, ET TERRÆ TUÆ HABITATÆ. Rursus docet depositurum se vetus odium, quo sæpe prosequutus est Judaicam synagogam, ab ira desti- turum, facturum eam voluntariam, & fructuosam, ac multitudine credentium or naturum. Sion enim repudiato Domino nostro JESU CHRISTO, reda- cta est in vastitatem, & multitudo infidelium periit. Posteaquam vero reliquiæ fidem receperunt, & por- ro vocata est multitudo gentium, ac in unum popu- lum hi duo conditi sunt, & una demum ex ambobus dicta est Ecclesia: Largitur ei Deus, ut nullo modo pristinis malis implicetur, nec derelicta vocetur vel deserta, sed ut potius ei morigera & voluntaria fiat: & non amplius deserta, sed habitata vocabitur. Hoc autem ex rebus ipsis videmus usu venisse, & Ecclesias ubiq; in tranquillitate & serenitate collocatas, & fi- deles ad immensam multitudinem propagatos, & Deum propter illos celebrari.

## 62:6
Vers. 6.

UPON YOUR WALLS O JERUSALEM I HAVE SET WATCHMEN] That is, for your walls, for your safety I have set priests and Levites as intercessors.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

SUPER MUROS TUOS JERUSALEM CON- STITUI CUSTODES] Id est, pro muris tuis, pro salute tua precatores constitui Sacerdotes & Levitas.

## 62:6
KEEP SILENT] You priests and Levites, pray perpetually.

AND GIVE NO SILENCE

to God: do not let him rest: stir him up.

Latin:

TACEATIS] Vos Sacerdotes & Levitæ precamini per- petuo.

ET NE DETIS SILENTIUM DEI] Ne patia-

mini Deum quiescere: excitate eum.

## 62:7
Vers. 7. YOU WHO REMEMBER THE LORD, DO NOT

Latin:

Vers. 7. QUI REMINIS CIMINI DOMINI, NE

## 62:7
UNTIL HE ESTABLISHES AND UNTIL HE SETS

JERUSALEM AS A PRAISE IN THE EARTH] Until he restores the city of Jerusalem, and makes it widely famous.

Thus the sense of the Prophet is perverted. When watchmen are said to be set upon the walls of a city, everyone understands that it is not intercessors who are designated for the walls, but those who are placed on the walls, so that they may guard the city there and take care of it, watch for it, and perform the other duties that are of watchmen; sentinels, who indeed keep watch so vigilantly against enemies that they are silent neither by day nor by night.

THOSE WHO REMEMBER THE LORD. Because they are spiritual guardians, it is necessary for them to preach about the Messiah who is to come, so that they may keep this Lord alive in their memory, for they should never be silent until He establishes and renders Jerusalem, or the Church, glorious and adorned with every praise on earth. For it is their duty to remember God, as Paul admonishes Timothy: μνημόνευε ἰησῆν χριστὸν 2 Tim. 2:8, and never to be silent about Him. 1 Cor. 2:2. He addresses it, says Cyril, as an illustrious and inhabited city. For the most distinguished cities are always cared for by many vigilant guards, lest any enemy attack unexpectedly. Thus, the Church, the savior of all and the Lord, fortified by ineffable power and the protection of Angels, has chosen for itself wise and very vigilant guardians, having sleepless care for it, namely holy mystagogues, who in no way cease to commemorate His glory and His wonders, as it is written. For we are accustomed in the Church to preach to the subject peoples always the magnificence of the Savior and the proofs of divine excellence, so that from there they may conceive an immovable and unshaken faith in Him. This promise, therefore, is about the guardians of the Church being given, so that the spiritual Jerusalem may be established and praise may be placed on the earth, that is, it may be well confirmed in the knowledge of the Lord and may progress in true piety, so that it may be celebrated everywhere in terms of doctrine and morals. Grotius explains the phrase AND GIVE NO SILENCE TO GOD by ἰδίαν ἔκλυσιν: Do not allow God to rest, stir Him up; so that He may snatch this for the restoration of the city. But what kind of silence it is, is understood from the word for being silent. For these explain each other. Therefore, the guardians are commanded not to be silent or to keep silence. But it does not denote the silence of God's rest. They are said to cry out to Him, because for His sake, by His authority, and in His name, for His glory and honor, they do not keep silent, but cry out. They do not cry out for themselves, not for the world, but for God and their Lord, to whose glory and honor all things are directed, whose honor they sing, celebrate, divulge, and propagate, when they do not keep silent but cry out to the Lord. It is one thing, therefore, to cry out to the Lord, which is done in prayer and supplications; it is another to cry out and preach to the Lord, which is done in sermons, and when we confess His name. If, however, NOT TO BE SILENT is to be understood as referring to prayers, another duty of the guardians of the Church will be designated, since the duty and effort of teaching would not suffice unless prayers also were added, and therefore it is necessary to insist before God and to contend with constant prayers, so that He may grant some success to our labors, which would otherwise be useless, as Calvin says here. The words UNTIL HE ESTABLISHES, AND UNTIL HE PLACES JERUSALEM AS A PRAISE ON THE EARTH, are to be understood not of the restoration of the city so named, but of the spiritual Jerusalem, which is established and founded by God through the proclamation of the Gospel, and whose name is rendered famous throughout the whole earth. The promise here is about the preservation of the Apostolic voice in the Church, until it is all gathered from all nations, up to the very last day of this age. For on the day of Pentecost, the Ministry of the Gospel was instituted and confirmed by the greatest miracles, which the Apostles, who are the guardians and watchmen of whom the Prophet speaks here, began in the city of Jerusalem, and afterwards carried the Gospel throughout the whole world. As Christ says, you will be my witnesses, not only in Jerusalem, but also in all Judea, Samaria, and finally to the ends of the earth. And Paul testifies that it is still being fulfilled in his own time: the Gospel, he says, has been preached to EVERY creature which is under heaven. And although the Apostles have passed away in their own time, in their bodily life, yet their voice has always sounded in the Church until now, and will sound in this age until its final day, so that what pertains to the voice of the Gospel which is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth, are rightly said to be the perpetual guardians and sentinels of the Church, as the Brentian exegesis holds. Others understand the guardians not only as the Apostles, but as any Doctors and ministers of the Church, which sense even Musculus himself, however much he otherwise favors the Jewish glosses of Grotius in this chapter, did not disapprove, but took as literal: The Lord himself speaks here, and in a few words promises to his restored Church vigilant and faithful guardians. He understands, however, by guardians, Leaders, Pastors, Prophets, Priests, whose duty it was to keep watch for the salvation and security of the people; lest any harm be brought upon them from anywhere. That he may signify that he will give such as will faithfully and diligently execute their office, he adds: Who all the day and all the night shall not hold their peace, that is, who shall perpetually watch, and diligently give warning of what ought to be warned.

Latin:

DONEC STABILIAT ET DONEC PONAT

JERUSALEM LAUDEM IN TERRA] Donec reparet urbem Hierosolyma, eamque faciat late famosam.

Pervertitur ita sensus Prophetæ. Cum custo- des super muros civitatis constituti dicuntur, quili- bet intelligit non precatores designari pro muris, sed eos, qui in muris collocantur, ut ibi custodiant ci- vitatem ejusq; rationem habeant, pro eadem vigi- lent, & reliqua quæ sunt custodum munia pera- gendo; excubatores, qui nempe ob hostes tam vigi- lanter excubant, ut nec interdiu nec noctu taceant.

QUI REMINIS CUNTUR DOMINI. Quia spirituales custodes sunt, concionari eos opor- tet de Messia venturo, ut vivum in memoria habeant hunc Dominum, nunquam enim taceant, donec stabiliat & reddat Hierusalem seu Ecclesiam gloriosam, & omni laude ornatam in terra. Ho- rum enim officium est meminisse Dei, ut Paulus Timotheum monet μνημόνευε ἰησῆν χριστὸν 2. Tim. 2, 8. & nunquam de eo silere. 1. Cor. 2, 2. Alloqui- tur, inquit Cyrillus, velut civitatem illustrem & ha- bitatam. Semper enim civitates insigniores, plurimi & vigiles custodes curant, ne quis hostis de improviso adoriatur. Sic & universorum servator & Domi- nus ineffabili potentia & Angelorum præsidiis munita Ecclesia, delegit ei custodes sapientes, & pervigiles, & ejus curam insomnem habentes, sanctos videlicet mystagogos, qui nullo modo desinunt gloriam ejus & mirabilia ejus commemorare, sicut scriptum est. Consuevimus enim in Ecclesia, populis subditis sem- per magnificentiam Servatoris, & divinæ præstantiæ documenta prædicare, ut inde immotam & inconcus- sam de eo fidem concipiant. Promissio ergo hæc est de custodibus Ecclesiæ dandis, ut stabiliatur spiritua- lis Hierosolyma, & ponatur laus in terra, id est, bene confirmetur in agnitione Domini, & in vera pie- tate proficiat, ita ut doctrinæ & morum ratione passim celebretur. Illud ET NE DETIS SI- LENTIUM DEI, per ἰδίαν ἔκλυσιν Grotius exponit: Ne patiamini Deum quiescere, excitate eum; ut hæc ad reparationem urbis abripiat. At silentium quale sit, è verbo tacendi intelligitur. Hæc enim explicant sese mutuo. Quapropter non tace- re, vel silere jubentur custodes. Non vero silen- tium notat quietem Dei. Clamare autem לו ipsi di- cuntur, quia ipsius causa, autoritate, ac nomine, in ipsius gloriam & honorem non silent, sed clamant. Non clamant sibi, non mundo, sed Deo & Do- mino suo, ad cujus gloriam & honorem omnia di- recta sunt, cujus honorem cantant, celebrant, di- vulgant & propagant, cum non silent sed clamant Domino. Aliud ergo est clamare ad Dominum, quod in oratione ac precibus fit; aliud clamare ac prædicare Domino, quod fit in concionibus, & cum ejus nomini confitemur. Si tamen de precibus accipiendum sit NON SILERE ipsi, alterum mu- nus custodum Ecclesiæ designabitur, siquidem non sufficeret munus & studium docendi, nisi pre- ces quoq; accederent, ideoq; oportet instare apud Deum, & contendere assiduis precibus, ut suc- cessum aliquem præbeat laboribus nostris, qui in- utiles alioqui forent, ut hic Calvinus. Verba LO- NEC STABILIAT, ET DONEC PONAT JERUSALEM LAUDEM IN TERRA, non de reparatione urbis ita vocatæ, sed de spirituali Hie- rosolyma, quæ à Deo stabilitur & fundatur præco- nio Evangelii, & cujus nomen famosum redditur per universam terram, intelligenda. Promissio hic habetur de conservatione vocis Apostolicæ in Ecclesia, donec tota congregetur ex omnibus gen- tibus, usq; ad novissimum hujus seculi diem. Nam in die Pentecostes institutum, & maximis miraculis confirmatum est Ministerium Evangelii, quod ini- tio Apostoli, qui sunt custodes & excubitores illi, de quibus hic Propheta loquitur, inchoarunt in ur- be Hierusalem, & circumtulerunt postea Evange- lion in universo orbe terrarum. Sicut Christus in- quit, eritis mihi testes, non solum Hierosolymis, ve- rum etiam in universa Judæa, Samaria, deniq; usq; ad extrema terræ. Et Paulus testificatur etiam suæ ad- huc ætatis tempore impleri: Evangelion, inquiens, prædicatum est apud UNIVERSAM creaturam, quæ sub cælo est. Etsi autem Apostoli defuncti sunt, suo tempore, corporali sua vita, tamen vox eorum hactenus semper sonuit in Eccle- sia, & sonabit in hoc seculo usque ad extre- mum ejus diem, ut quod ad vocem Evangelii eo- rum,quod est potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti, attinet, recte dicantur, perpetui custodes & Excu- bitores Ecclesiæ,ut habet Brentiana ἐξήγησις. Alii custodes non de Apostolis modo; sed quibusvis Eccle- siæ Doctoribus & ministris intelligunt, quem sensum nec ipse Musculus, utut alias Judaicæ Grotii glossæ in hoc capite favet,improbavit,sed pro literali ha- buit: Loquitur hic ipse Dominus, & paucis pro- mittit restitutæ suæ Ecclesiæ vigiles ac fideles cu- stodes. Intelligit autem per custodes, Duces, Pa- stores, Prophetas, Sacerdotes,quorum omnium erat excubias agere pro salute, ac securitate populi; ne quid illi damni alicunde inferretur. Ut se ta- les daturum significet, qui officium suum fideliter ac sedulo exequantur, subjicit: Qui tota die ac tota nocte jugiter non tacent, hoc est, qui perpetuo vigi- lent, ac diligenter quæ monenda sunt moneant.

## 62:8
Vers. 8.

IF I SHALL GIVE THY CORN ANY MORE FOR MEAT TO THINE ENEMIES] As heretofore to the Assyrians, Egyptians, Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SI DEDERO TRITICUM TUUM ULTRA CI- BUM INIMICIS TUIS] Ut antehac Assyriis, Ægyptiis, Chaldæis.

## 62:9
WHO GATHER IT] Who shall have stored it in granaries.

AND SHALL DRINK IN MY HOLY COURTS] And for the same. They shall drink, namely, at those feasts to which they used to call the Levites in the places surrounding the Temple, Deut. 14, 23 and following.

Grotius makes these promises merely corporal, and restricted to the Jewish people, and indeed after the liberation from the Babylonian captivity; but from those things which have preceded, and also from those which follow in verses 10 and 11, it is sufficiently manifest that these do not precisely concern the returning Jews, but the Church of the Lord. And that this promise is more narrow, that solemn and tremendous oath of the most holy God testifies: THE LORD HATH SWORN BY HIS RIGHT HAND AND BY THE ARM OF HIS STRENGTH. Where Jerome wishes the Son of God to be designated: Now he swears by his right hand and the arm of his strength, of which we have often spoken, that it is our Lord and Savior, because according to the Apostle he is the power of God, and the sentence of God. Others say that God swears by his omnipotence, which is expressed by the right hand and the arm of the strength of the Lord. In such a great oath the Lord is not primarily solicitous about corporal benefits. Wherefore those promises do not mean that God will not permit strangers to devour the labors and faculties of the pious, for that happens in any age: but the Lord signifies that the curse of the law would be removed in the kingdom of Christ, such as this curse also, among others, had been made to the impious in Deut. 28: Thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof, the fruit of thy land, and all thy labors shall a people eat which thou knowest not. For since Christ has liberated us from the curse of the law, Galat. 3, 13, even though Christians sometimes suffer the plunder of their goods, yet it does not result in a curse and punishment for them, but in a trial, so that they themselves may know that they have been liberated from the wrath of God and the curse of the law, and therefore they reckon such loss not as a damage, but as a gain. For they know that they are to receive a hundredfold, and after this life are to attain eternal happiness, Matth. 19. Of which perhaps the Apostle of the Hebrews, Heb. 10, 34: Ye took joyfully, he says, the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring Substance. Thus Brentius, Osiander, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and others. Nor did the Blessed Luther think otherwise: He adds the Oath to confirm weak consciences, that it will come to pass that they shall feel the fruit of the word which they teach, that they shall feel the fruit of the faith which they have. It is not possible, however, that any impious person should feel the true gifts, the true fruits of the word and of faith, but only the pious are they who are edified and confirmed by the word, whose heart is purified by faith, and whose conscience is serenaded, and by whose doctrine others also are edified. But all this is done so that they may praise the Lord in the courts, in the assembly for preaching. Therefore, what is said, THEY SHALL DRINK IN MY HOLY COURTS, is not to be understood of the places surrounding the Temple, but because the discourse is about the universal Church, it alludes only to the feasts which were accustomed to be celebrated after the offered sacrifices, not far from the temple, by divine ordination. Conf. Deut. 12, 12. c. 14, 26. c. 16, 14. For the Holy Spirit loves to describe the benefits of the New Testament by the things of the Old Testament. S. benefits of the N. T. Therefore the Weimar Paraphrase explains it concerning the spiritual peace of the Church in the N. T. and concerning the celebration of the divine name, that the faithful are to celebrate God for spiritual and heavenly benefits with a joyful mouth.

Latin:

QUI COMPORTANT ILLUD] Qui in testas condiderint.

ET BIBENT IN ATRIIS SANCTIS MEIS] Et pro iidem. Bibent nempe in epulis illis ad quas Levitas vo- cabant in circumjectis Templo locis, Deut. 14, 23. & se- quentibus.

Ita mere corporales promissiones facit Grotius, easque restrictas ad populum Judaicum, & quidem post liberationem è captivitate Babylonica; sed ex iis, quæ antegressa sunt, nec non ex iis, quæ versu 10. & 11. sequuntur, satis manifestum est, non Ju- dæos reduces hæc præcise concernere, sed Eccle- siam Domini. Et angustiorem esse hanc promis- sionem solemne illud atque tremendum juramen- tum sanctissimi Dei testatur: JURAVIT DO- MINUS IN DEXTERA SUA ET IN BRA- CHIO FORTITUDINIS SUÆ. Ubi Hiero- nymus Filium Dei designari vult: Nunc jurat per dexteram suam & brachium fortitudinis suæ, de quo crebro diximus, quod sit Dominus noster atque Sal- vator, quia juxta Apostolum Dei virtus est, Deique sententia. Alii jurareDeum per omnipotentiam suam dicunt, quæ per dexteram & brachium fortitudinis Domini exprimatur. In tanto juramento de corpo- ralibus beneficiis non primario solicitus est Domi- nus. Quapropter non hoc volunt illæ promis- siones, quod non permissurus sit Deus, ut alieni devorent labores piorum & facultates, id enim quavis ætate contingit: sed significat Dominus,ab- latam fore in regno Christi maledictionem legis, qualis etiam hæc Deut. 28. inter alias maledictio- nis impiis facta erat: Plantabis vineam, & non vinde- miabis eam, fructus terræ tuæ, & omnes labores tuos comedet populus, quem ignoras. Cum enim Chri- stus liberarit nos à legis maledictione Galat. 3, 13. utut quandoque Christiani patiantur rapinam bo- norum suorum, non tamen id in maledictionem & pœnam ipsis cedit, sed in probationem, ut sciant ipsi, se ab ira Dei & maledictione legis liberatos esse, ideoque talem jacturam non pro damno,sed pro lucro reputant.Norunt enim quod centuplum accepturi sint, & post hanc vitam æternam felicita- tem consecuturi Matth.19. De qua Ebræorum for- te Apostolus Ebr. 10,34. Rapinam,inquit, bonorum vestrorum cum gaudio suscepistis, cognoscentes vos ha- bere meliorem, & manentem Substantiam. Sic Brentius, Osiander, Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, & alii. Nec aliter B. Lutherus: Addit Juramentum ad confirmandas conscientias infirmas, fore, ut sen- tiant fructum verbi,quod docent, ut sentiant fructum fidei,quam habent. Non est autem possibile, ut impius aliquis vera dona, veros fructus verbi & fidei sen- tiat, sed soli pii sunt, qui verbo eriguntur & con firmantur, quorum cor fide purificatur, & conscien- tia serenatur, & ædificantur eorum doctrina alii quoque. Fit autem hoc totum, ut laudent Dominum in atriis, in conventu ad prædicationem. Quod ergo dicitur BIBENT IN ATRIIS SANCTIS MEIS, non de circumjectis Templo locis intelli- gendum, sed quia de Ecclesia universa sermo est, alluditur solum ad convivia, quæ celebrari sole- bant post sacrificia oblata, non procul à templo, ex ordinatione divina. Conf. Deut. 12, 12. c. 14, 26. c. 16, 14. Nam per res Veteris Testamenti descri- bere amat Sp. S. beneficia N. T. Ideo de pace spi- rituali Ecclesiæ in N. T. & de celebratione nomi- nis divini explicat Paraphrasis Vinariensis, quod fideles Deum pro beneficiis spiritualibus & cœle- stibus læto ore celebraturi sint.

## 62:10
Vers. 10. GO THROUGH, GO THROUGH THE GATES] You Priests and Levites, of whom above, enter into the Temple.

PREPARE THE WAY FOR THE PEOPLE, MAKE THE PATH PLAIN] Teach them the right way. Ezra and his companions the Levites performed this office well, Ezra 7, 10. Nehem. 8, 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 18.

ELIGITE LAPIDES] That is, cast away all stumbling blocks which could impede an even gait. Such are marriages with foreigners: Ezra 9 & 10; avarice, usury: Nehemiah 5; violation of the Sabbath: Nehemiah 13; and other similar things.

ERIGITE SIGNUM AD POPULOS] Act so that other nations may be provoked to piety by the example of the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 10. TRANSITE, TRANSITE PER PORTAS] Vos Sacerdotes & Levitæ, de quibus supra, intrate in Tem- plum.

PRÆPARATE VIAM POPULO, PLENUM FA- CITE ITER] Docete eos recta. Hoc officio Esdras ejusque comites Levitæ bene functi sunt, Esdr. 7, 10. Ne- hem. 8, 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. 18.

ELIGITE LAPIDES] Id est, projicite omnia of- fendicula quæ æqualem gressum impedire possent. Talia sunt connubia cum alienigenis: Esdr. 9. & 10. avaritia, usuræ: Nehem. 5. sabbati violatio: Nehem. 13. aliaque si- milia.

ERIGITE SIGNUM AD POPULOS] Facite gen- tes aliæ exemplo Judæorum ad pietatem provocentur.

## 62:11
Vers. 11. ECCE DOMINUS AUDITUM FECIT IN EXTIMIS TERRÆ] That is, from the furthest parts of the earth He ordered this to be proclaimed, especially through Ezekiel.

DICITE FILIÆ SION: ECCE SALVATOR TUUS VENIT] Cyrus, as above at the beginning of this chapter.

ECCE MERCES EJUS CUM EO, ET OPUS EJUS CORAM ILLO] Here again the work is the reward of the work. The sense is: for this liberation of yours He has already received a reward in advance, the victory over the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ECCE DOMINUS AUDITUM FECIT IN EXTIMIS TERRÆ] Id est, ab extimis terræ partibus jussit hoc pronunciari, per Ezechielem maxime.

DICITE FILIÆ SION: ECCE SALVATOR TUUS VENIT] Cyrus, ut supra initio hujus capitis.

ECCE MERCES EJUS CUM EO, ET OPUS EJUS CORAM ILLO] Hic iterum opus est merces ope- ris. Sensus est: pro ista liberatione vestra jam mercedem in antegressum recepit, victoriam de Chaldæis.

## 62:12
Vers. 12. QUÆSITA CIVITAS] To which many will flow together.

These latter verses concern the calling of the Gentiles. For the preceding parts, which dealt with the benefits of Christ, teach this first. Then, indeed, those things which are said about raising a sign to the peoples are also clear. These cannot be taken only from the example of the Jews, but must be understood concerning the sign which, as he testified in the Prophet ch. 11, was raised up for the sake of the Gentiles. Which was to happen through the doctrine of the Gospel concerning the Messiah. Therefore, the way must be prepared and the path made level for those peoples to whom the sign ought to be raised; for them, obstacles must be removed which could hinder their arrival at the Church. Thirdly, the report which the Lord made in the EXTREMITIES OF THE EARTH cannot be drawn to Ezekiel and his proclamation concerning the return to Babylon. Because this report of the Lord extends through the whole world and the ends of the earth. Nor does any reason appear here why these things should be taken as a future prophecy of Ezekiel. Which gloss hitherto, unless I am mistaken, is unheard of in the Church and must be referred among the recent εὔρηματα of Grotius. Cyril has this concerning these things: And what is this, that this sign should be heard? which he says is to be lifted up to the nations and to the ends of the earth, that is, to be extolled, and this word of faith which we preach is to be spread everywhere, or perhaps the symbol of the saving passion, and that is the confession of faith. For it is necessary to say that the Lord is Jesus, and to believe that God raised Him from the dead. But this saves from death and sin. Therefore, not only of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles. For the sign is lifted up, not only to those believing from the blood of Israel, but to all nations everywhere. For the whole world under the embrace of heaven has been captured, as it were, by the Evangelical preaching. These things Cyril. Similarly Jerome: So that the Jews might not think it was said about them, it is joined: Lift up a sign to the nations and to the peoples of the nations, so that the straits of the land of Judah are by no means challenged for salvation, but a report may be made in the ends of the earth, so that the whole world may hear the passion of the creator of all. Fourth, that saying, TELL THE DAUGHTER OF ZION: BEHOLD THY SAVIOR COMETH, is wrongly snatched away to Cyrus. Since it treats of Christ the Savior. Which is evident then from the preceding, and then primarily it is also manifest from the very words BEHOLD THY SALVATION, where the name of JESUS itself is held (which name יִשְׁעֵךְ THY SALVATION is never used of a mere man, let alone of Cyrus) and also from the comparison of the passage Is. 35, 4. and especially ch. 40, 10. which is entirely parallel to this one. Where the very same phrase is held: Say to the CITIES OF JUDAH: BEHOLD YOUR GOD, BEHOLD THE LORD GOD SHALL COME IN STRENGTH. AND HIS ARM SHALL RULE; BEHOLD HIS REWARD IS WITH HIM, AND HIS WORK BEFORE HIM. A similar passage is added, Zech. 9, 9. which the Evangelist joined with this one of ours, when he said that the prophecy was fulfilled at the coming of Christ, which says, Tell the daughter of Zion, behold thy King cometh unto thee, Matt. 21, 5. For he teaches so openly that both this prophecy treats of the same, and is to be understood of Christ. Grotius therefore openly contradicts the Holy Spirit, when he explains this prophecy of Isaiah concerning Cyrus, which the Holy Spirit interprets concerning Christ: Just as also in the depravation of the other Zecharian passage he diametrically opposes the opinion of the Holy Spirit, if indeed he twists the same to Zerubbabel, who was never King, nor entered Jerusalem in that manner. But he who acknowledged that it pertains to the Messiah, along with the sounder Jews, the writer of Bereshith Rabba & Midrash Koheleth, at Matt. 21. Therefore this prophecy must entirely be explained of Christ. Therefore Cyril: He announces the coming of the Savior & whatever we have gained from thence, and the riches to be given to those believing in him. He names the daughter of Zion. But whether one wishes to understand that ancient one, as having already obtained mercy, and justified by faith, or the new one, that is, the Church: he would not absurdly say that this is the daughter of that Zion. For the first who originated from the blood of Israel believed: and the Church of the nations was called as a certain daughter of her, who was established by them from the beginning. But to whom does he command that they announce the Gospel to Zion? Is it not entirely to the holy mystagogues, who presided over the Churches, whom he also ordered to open the gates, and diligently to remove the stones from the midst? So also Jerome: He commands the Apostles and Apostolic men, that they enter and pass through the gates: against which hell does not prevail, and that they take all impediments out of the way, so that the people may enter the Church of the Savior without any scandal. Whence also John cried out: I am the voice of one crying in the desert, as Isaiah said: Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight his paths: Every valley shall be filled and every mountain and hill shall be brought low. And in other words the same sense is now said. Although indeed Christian interpreters vary, whom the Prophet here addressed, pass through, pass through the gates, yet they easily agree in this, that this does not concern the external Jerusalem temple, not the priests & Levites, but look to the Church of God, & to the kingdom of Christ. Some wish the Apostles to be addressed, whose task it was to prepare the way for the nations, and to raise a sign for the peoples. Thus Jerome, who having enumerated different opinions, both of the semi-Jews, as he calls them, who contend that this will be in the last time, when at some point after the fullness of the nations Israel is to be saved, & is to return to the Lord: and of others, who think it is to be fulfilled in the Kingdom of heaven, when there will be true joy, & each one will receive according to his merit, adds his own opinion, that these treat of the first coming of Christ, and that the Apostles and Apostolic men are to be understood, whom he also understands through the guards of the walls of Jerusalem, to whom it was commanded before, that they should not be silent. Others explain it of Doctors and Mystagogues generally. Thus Cyril: He addresses the guards themselves or doctors. For he orders the entrances of the holy city to be opened and to make the access plain and easy, void of delays and offenses, to those who wish to enter: for by stones he hints at scandals. To which also the Brentian Interpretation returns: He exclaims and exhorts either his fellow citizens, or his colleagues, that they prepare the public way and remove the stones and other impediments from the way, so that such a great multitude of nations may arrive expeditiously at Jerusalem or the Church. Pass through, he says, pass through the gates. Go out from the city through the individual gates, and level the public way for the people, namely for the uncircumcised nations, who flow together here in the greatest frequency, Prepare, prepare the way, clear it of stones, raise a sign, or banner to the peoples, so that they may know, whither they must come. What therefore has been done, that such a great multitude of nations hastens hither? It follows: Behold the Lord hath made it heard in the ends of the earth. This is, Jesus Christ, true God and our Lord, has divulged his Gospel even to the ends of the earth, by which preaching the Nations have been so excited, that they have undertaken the journey to the city of Jerusalem in the greatest frequency. But this journey is not made with bodily feet, but by faith. For as many as approach in their own places, whether in Scythia or in Judea, to hear the Gospel of Christ, & believe in Christ, these are said to set out to Jerusalem & to join themselves with the Israelites. Nay rather these alone are the true citizens of Jerusalem and true Israelites, & will also enjoy all those benefits, which God promised to his chosen people already from the beginning. Osiander explains it concerning the Jerusalem citizens; Pass through you citizens of Jerusalem, pass through I say through the gates to meet the arriving Nations: prepare the way for the people arriving from various regions, make the path plain, in Hebrew: pave, pave (I say) the path (Because one goes through a narrow way to life, Matt. 7. & choose, in Hebrew: remove the stones, lest those approaching the city stumble against them: Nay, also lift up (on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea, where it washes Palestine) a sign (a banner or something else of that kind) to the peoples: so that those who run to you by ships across the sea may be able to keep a straight course and land safely at the port. For that is the custom in regions adjacent to the sea, that by some sign (especially at night) the port is shown to those sailing. (But then the peoples come to Jerusalem, when they embrace the Gospel of Christ, even if they do not depart from their own regions. For they join themselves by faith to the Church of Christ, which is the heavenly Jerusalem. The Prophet commands, however, that the way be paved and the stones removed, so that he may admonish us that we should invite peoples alien to the true Religion by our piety to receive the Gospel of Christ, and that we should remove (as far as it can be done) the stumbling blocks by which they could be deterred from the Gospel of Christ.) He now shows the reason why the Gentiles hasten to the Church: For behold the Lord has made heard, or has caused to be preached (the Gospel) in the ends of the earth (everywhere in the world). For the Apostles will preach (the Prophet wishes to say) the Gospel, when Christ the King shall have come into the world to save repentant sinners, because it is certain (says the Prophet) that the Son of God will assume human nature and will enter Jerusalem as King, yet not as a worldly king. Say therefore to the Daughter of Zion (where Jerusalem is) Behold your Savior comes. Thus also the Weimar Paraphrasts explain it generally and indefinitely. Which expositions are subordinate. For while all ought to be engaged in preparing the way for the nations, then indeed this duty especially falls upon the mystagogues and Doctors, and the Apostles and Apostolic men performed this office most of all. therefore, Cyril: He announces the coming of the Savior, and whatever we have gained from it, and the riches to be given to those who believe in him. He names the daughter of Zion. Whether one wishes to understand that ancient one, as having already obtained mercy and been justified by faith, or the new one, that is, the Church: one would not absurdly say that this is the daughter of that Zion. For the first who were born of the blood of Israel believed: And the Church of the nations was called a kind of daughter of that which was established by them from the beginning. And Jerome: Say to the Daughter of Zion, who is called the daughter of Zion for this reason: because she first arose from the Jews. Of whom he says in the Song of Songs: The sons of my mother fought against me. Or certainly for this reason a daughter: because she received the name of adoption from God. For as many as received him, he gave them power to become the sons of God. But what is it that the masters and teachers are commanded to announce to the daughter of Zion? Behold your Savior comes, who in Hebrew is called Jesus. Whence also Gabriel to Joseph: And you shall call, he says, his name Jesus: for he himself shall save his people from their sins. Brentius explains this more lengthily and elegantly: Just as the Prophet in the spirit sees the Gentiles approaching in a great multitude to hear the Gospel and to believe in Christ: so also he sees Christ entering the city of Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, riding on an ass, and accompanied by a great crowd of people. For thus the Evangelist Matthew interprets this passage, when, about to recite the prophecy of Zechariah concerning Christ arriving on an ass, he prefixes this saying of Isaiah. Say to the daughter of Zion: signifying clearly that just as Zechariah sees in his discourse Christ arriving on a donkey on Palm Sunday, so Isaiah by these words commands it to be explained to the Church, who that is who arrives thus riding on a donkey, and what is to be thought of him. Say, he says, to the daughter of Zion, Behold your Savior comes. He seems indeed to be carried and to enter the city of Jerusalem as some abject man, and so needy that he does not have his own ass on which to be carried, but has need to use one borrowed: But you, daughter of Zion, do not judge him according to outward appearance. For behold, there comes ישוע, that is, JESUS or your Savior. For thus also Matthew writes elsewhere that the Angel said to Joseph: You shall call his name JESUS, that is, Savior, for he shall save his people from their sins. Jesus therefore comes into the city of Jerusalem, abject indeed and humble, if you look at his outward appearance, but if you unfold it and look at him more closely, he comes bringing with him his reward and recompense. Behold, he says, his reward is with him, and his work, that is, the reward of his work, is before him. What then is the reward, what is his recompense? Surely this, which is signified by his name. For he is called Jesus, that is, Savior. He brings therefore with him true, total, and eternal salvation. This is the reward, that is, the recompense of those who believe in him. Worldly kings, when they first come into their metropolises, are accustomed to confer their royal benefits, which are called Fiefs, upon those who have deserved well of them. But such as the Kings are, such are the Fiefs, namely worldly, earthly, and perishing: which can save the vassal neither in death nor in the horrors of hell. But Jesus Christ, the heavenly King, coming into his Metropolis, Jerusalem, places himself on the throne of his majesty, in order to confer upon his believers heavenly fiefs, which are his reward and recompense, of which fiefs one is the remission of sins, another the imputation of his righteousness, another adoption as sons and heirs of God, another liberation from death and hell: in short, all kinds of heavenly fiefs are comprehended under the one name of eternal salvation, which he brings with him to believers. What is said concerning his REWARD pertains both to the first coming and to the second: For that reward comes with him at the first coming by way of acquisition, because he prepared the same, and is ready to distribute the same, nay, he does distribute it: he also wishes a sign to be lifted up among the nations, and makes it heard even to the end of the earth: But the plenary distribution will take place at the final coming. Therefore this same sentence is applied to the same thing in Rev. 22. Thus Brentius. Which Osiander has briefly summarized: Say to the daughter of Zion (the city of Jerusalem) Behold the Savior comes. (For Christ first comes as Savior, finally he comes as Judge: In which judgment, however, he will nevertheless be a Savior to all who believe in him.) Behold his reward with him, and his work, that is, the recompense of his works before him, that is, Christ brings with him his entire merit, in order to impute and give it to all who truly believe in him. Now therefore it is not obscure how those new names of the people and the city are to be understood. Which are also an evident argument that these prophecies are not to be understood of an external city or the Jewish people: But of the Spiritual Jerusalem, the Church of God and the chosen people of the Lord. For it is proper to this that it is a Holy people redeemed by the Lord: And that is truly the city sought after, and not forsaken, whereas on the contrary it was later said to the earthly city of Jerusalem: Behold you are left desolate, Matt. 23. Which is to be observed against the Jewish gloss of Grotius. Whence Cyril: But you, O Zion, or Church, shall be called a sought-after city, and not forsaken. He calls it sought-after, and worthy of memory. For what is sought is held in memory. And not forsaken, like that first one, that is, the multitude of the unfaithful. It was therefore said by God, by the voice of Jeremiah: I have forsaken my house, I have left my heritage. And it was said by Him, the Savior of us all, Christ: Behold, your house is left to you. Jerome has it thus: And the Lord and Savior Himself shall call them. Or according to the Hebrew: They shall call them, the Apostolic men, a holy people and redeemed by the Lord, who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ. Rightly, therefore, does Brentius here compare the aforementioned names, so that the conclusion may agree with the beginning of this sermon. After Jesus, the Savior, has arrived and sat upon the throne of His majesty, in order to bestow heavenly fiefs upon His believers, then that which was said above will truly come to pass, that His people shall be called by new names. For now, because of many and great sins, because of the devastation of His metropolis, because of His servitude and captivity, the people are called profane, cast off by the Lord, and His metropolis is called deserted, which no one seeks, so as to dwell therein. But when JESUS, the Savior, has arrived, the people shall be called holy: because He will expiate their sins and appease the wrath of God, so that as many as believe in Him may be reckoned before God as just and holy on account of Jesus. They shall also be called a people redeemed by the Lord: because Jesus, who is our true Lord God, He will redeem them from the power of Satan, from death and hell, and will confer upon them eternal life and the heavenly kingdom. Similarly, Jerusalem, their metropolis, will no longer be called deserted or abominable, but will be called 'sought after,' because the nations, which they previously loathed with the utmost disgust, will in turn seek it with the utmost zeal and investigate it most diligently, so that they may become its citizens. Now this inquiry and investigation is accustomed to happen when the Gentiles apply themselves to this study, that they may know the Gospel of Christ and become participants in the justice and salvation of Christ. Cornelius the Centurion was seeking the city of Jerusalem when he called the Apostle Peter to himself, so that he might hear from him the Gospel of Christ. The Macedonians were seeking the city of Jerusalem when a Macedonian man appeared to Paul and begged him that, having set out into Macedonia, he might help them. And these things [refer] to chapter 62.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QUÆSITA CIVITAS] Ad quam multi con- fluent.

Hi postremi versus concernunt vocationem gentium. Nam id primo superiora, quæ de bene- ficiis Christi egerunt, docent. Tum vero & lucu- lenta sunt, quæ de erigendo signo ad populos dicun- tur. Hæc non de exemplo tantum Judæorum ac- cipi possunt, sed de signo quod ob gentes erectum in Propheta c. 11. testatus est, intelligenda sunt. Quod futurum per doctrinam Evangelii de Mes- sia. Illis ergo populis via præparanda & planum faciendum iter, ad quos erigi signum debet, illis obstacula removenda sunt, quæ adventum ad Ec- clesiam præpedire possunt. Tertio auditus, quem Dominus fecit in EXTIMIS TERRÆ non po- test ad Ezechielem & præconium ejus de reditu in Babyloniam trahi. Quia auditus hic Domini per totum Orbem & extremos terræ fines se porrigit. Nec ulla hic ratio apparet, quare hæc de futuro va- ticinio Ezechielis accipi debeant. Quæ glossa ha- ctenus, nisi fallor, inaudita est in Ecclesia & inter εὔρηματα nupera Grotii referenda venit. Cyrillus de his ita habet: Et quidnam hoc est, ut audiatur hoc signum? quod ad gentes & ad extrema terræ tollen- dum ait, id est, extollendum, & passim divulgandum hoc verbum fidei, quod prædicamus, seu forte passionis sa- lutaris symbolum, atque id est fidei confessio. Oportet enim dicere, Dominum esse Jesum, ac credere Deum excitasse ipsum è mortuis. Servat autem hoc à morte & peccato. Igitur non Judæorum modo, sed & gen- tium. Tollitur enim signum, non ad solum credentes ex sanguine Israel, sed ad omnes ubiq; gentium. Orbis namque totus sub cæli complexu Evangelica prædica- tione, tanquam rei captus est. Hæc Cyrillus. Simi- liter Hieronymus: Quod ne putarent Judæi de se di- ci, jungitur: Levate signum in gentes & ad populos nationum, ut nequaquam unius terræ Judæ ad sa- lutem provocentur angustiæ, sed auditum fiat in ex- tremis terræ, ut passionem omnium creatoris totus mundus exaudiat. Quarto istud DICITE FILIÆ SION: ECCE SALVATOR TUUS VENIT, perperam ad Cyrum abripitur. Quum de Christo salvatore agat. Quod tum è superioribus constat, tum imprimis manifestum etiam est è verbis ipsis ECCE SALUS TUA, ubi nomen ipsum JESU habetur (quod nomen יִשְׁעֵךְ SALUS TUA de ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ nunquam, nedum de Cyro adhi- betur) nec non è collatione loci Es. 35, 4. & maxime c. 40, 10. qui huic omnino parallelus est. Ubi ea- dem prorsus phrasis habetur: Dic CIVITATI- BUS JUDA: ECCE DEUS VESTER, ECCE DOMINUS DEUS TUUS IN FORTITU- DINE VENIET. ET BRACHIUM EJUS DOMINABITUR; ECCE MERCES EJUS CUM EO, ET OPUS ILLIUS CORAM IL- LO. Accedit similis locus Zach. 9, 9. quem cum hoc nostro conjunxit Evangelista, cum in adven- tu Christi completam Prophetiam dixit, quæ ait, Dicite filiæ Sion, ecce Rex tuus venit tibi Matth. 21, 5. Docet enim ita aperte utrumque hoc vaticinium de eodem agere, ac de Christo intelligendum esse. Contradicit itaque Spiritui S. palam Grotius, cum de Cyro hoc Esaiæ vaticinium explicat, quod de Chri- sto Sp. S. interpretatur: Quemadmodum etiam in alterius loci Zachariani depravatione καδδιάμε- τρον refragatur Sp. S. sententiæ, siquidem eundem ad Zorobabelem, qui nunquam Rex fuit, nec ea ra- tione Hierosolymam ingressus est, detorqueat. Quem vero ad Messiam pertinere cum Judæis sa- nioribus, scriptore Bereschith Rabba & Midrasch Koheleth agnovit ad Matth. 21. De Christo ergo hoc vaticinium omnino explicandum. Ideo Cy- rillus: Prænunciat adventum Servatoris & quæcun- que inde lucrati sumus, ac divitias dandas in ipsum credentibus. Filiam nominat Sion. Sive autem velit quis antiquam illam, utpote jam adeptam misericor- diam, & fide justificatam, sive novam, id est, Ec- clesiam, intelligere: non absurde dixerit, quod hæc sit illius Sionis filia. Primi enim ex sanguine Israelis oriundi crediderunt: & gentium Ecclesia velut filia quædam dicta est ejus, quæ ab initio ab illis constituta est. At quibus mandat, ut Evangelium annuncient Sioni? Annon omnino sanctis mystagogis, qui præfue- runt Ecclesiis, quos etiam jussit aperire portas, & la- pides diligenter è medio tollere? Sic etiam Hierony- mus: Præcipit Apostolis & Apostolicis viris, ut ingre- diantur & transeant per portas: quibus infernus non prævalet, & omnia tollant impedimenta de via, ut absque aliquo scandalo populus Ecclesiam Salvatoris introeat. Unde & Johannes clamabat: Ego sum vox clamantis in deserto, sicut Esaias dixit: Parate viam Domini, rectas facite semitas ejus: Omnis vallis implebitur & omnis mons & collis humilia- bitur. Aliisq; verbis nunc idem sensus dicitur. Quan- quam vero varient Interpp. Christiani, quos hic compellarit Propheta, transite, transite per portas, in eo tamen facile conveniunt, quod hæc non tem- plum externum Hierosolymitanum, non sacerdotes & Levitas concernat, sed ad Ecclesiam Dei, & ad re- gnum Christi spectent. Nonnulli compellari volunt Apostolos, quorum erat parare viam gentibus, & eri- gere signum populis. Ita Hieronymus, qui enumera- tis diversis sententiis, tum semi-Judæorum, quos vocat, qui hoc in ultimo tempore, quo aliquando post plenitudinem gentium salvandus est Israel, & ad Do- minum rediturus, futurum esse contendunt: tum alio- rum, qui in Regno cælorum explendum putant, quan- do erit vera lætitia, & unusquisq́; accipiet secundum meritum suum, addit suam sententiam, quod hæc de primo adventu Christi agant, & quod intelligendi sint Apostoli & Apostolici viri, quos etiam per custodes murorum Hierusalem intelligit, quibus antea præ- cipiebatur, nec tacerent. Alii de Doctoribus & My- stagogis generatim explicant. Sic Cyrillus : Ipsos jam custodes seu doctores compellat. Jubet enim patefieri sanctæ civitatis aditus & accessum planum & expedi- tum facere, remoris & offensionibus vacuum, his qui volunt ingredi: per lapides enim subinnuit scan- dala. Quo redit etiam Brentiana Interpretatio : Exclamat & hortatur seu cives, seu collegas suos, ut præparent publicam viam & tollant lapides ac alia impedimenta è via, quo tanta gentium multitudo expedite ad Hierusalem aut Eccle- siam perveniat. Transite, inquit, transite per portas. Egredimini ex urbe per singulas portas, & compla- nate publicam viam populo, gentibus videlicet in- circumcisis, quæ maxima frequentia huc conflu- unt, Parate, parate iter, repurgate à saxis, erigi- te signum, aut vexillum ad populos, ut sciant, quo ve- niendum sit. Quid ergo factum est, quod tanta gentium multitudo huc properet ? Sequitur : Ecce Dominus auditum fecit in extremis terræ. Hoc est, Jesus Christus, verus Deus ac Dominus noster, di- vulgavit Evangelion suum usq́; ad extrema terræ, qua prædicatione Gentes ita excitatæ sunt, ut susce- perint profectionem ad urbem Hierusalem ma- xima frequentia. Hæc autem profectio non fit cor- poralibus pedibus, sed fide. Quotquot enim accedunt in suis locis, sive in Scythia sive in Judæa, ad au- diendum Evangelion Christi, & credunt in Chri- stum, hi dicuntur ad Hierusalem proficisci & sese cum Israëlitis conjungere. Quin potius soli hi sunt veri cives Hierusalem & veri Israëlitæ, & fruentur etiam omnibus iis beneficiis, quæ Deus electo suo populo jam inde ab initio promisit. De civibus Hierosolymitanis Osiander explicat; Transite vos cives Jerosolymitani, transite inquam per portas ob- viam adventantibus Gentibus: præparate viam popu- lo advenienti ex variis regionibus, planum facite iter, Hebraice: sternite, sternite (inquam) semitam (Quia per angustam viam itur ad vitam, Matth. 7. & eligi- te, Hebraice: removete lapides, ne ad eos offendant accedentes ad urbem: Quin & elevate (in litore maris mediterranei, ubi alluit Palæstinam) signum (vexillum aut aliud quid tale) ad populos : ut qui trans mare navibus ad vos accurrunt, rectum cur- sum tenere & ad portam appellere tuto possint. Id enim moris est in Regionibus mari adjacenti- bus, ut signo aliquo (noctu imprimis) ostendatur navigantibus portus. (Tum autem veniunt popu- li ad Jerosolymam, cum amplectuntur Evangelion Christi, etiamsi è regionibus suis non egredian- tur. Adjungunt enim se fide Ecclesiæ Christi, quæ est cœlestis Jerusalem. Jubet autem Propheta viam sterni, & lapides removeri, ut admoneat nos, ut populus alienos à vera Religione invite- mus pietate nostra ad recipiendum Evangelion Christi, utq; offendicula (quoad ejus fieri potest) removeamus, quibus illi ab Evangelio Christi de- terreri possent.) Ostendit nunc causam cur Gen- tes ad Ecclesiam properent: Ecce enim Dominus auditum fecit, seu prædicari curavit (Evangelion) in extremis terræ (passim in orbe terrarum) Prædi- cabunt enim (vult Propheta dicere) Apostoli Ev- angelion, quando Christus Rex venerit in mun- dum, salvos facere peccatores resipiscentes, quia certum est (inquit Propheta) Filium Dei assumptu- rum humanam naturam, & ingressurum Jerosoly- mam, ut Regem, non tamen ut regem mundanum. Dicite igitur Filiæ Sion (ubi Jerusalem) Ecce Sal- vator tuus venit. Sic etiam Paraphrastæ Vinarien- ses exponunt generaliter, & indefinite. Quæ ἐκθέσεις subordinatæ sunt. Nam quum omnes debent in eo esse, ut via paretur gentibus, tum ve- ro imprimis id incumbit mystagogis, & Doctori- bus, eoque maxime functi sunt munere Apostoli, & Apostolici viri. Quod ad posteriora verba, di- cite filiæ Sion: Ecce Salvator tuus venit: quum habeamus eorum interpretationem omni exce- ptione majorem in Novo Testamento, religio nobis est, ab ea discedere. Recte itaque Cyril- lus; Prænunciat adventum servatoris, & quæcun- que inde lucrati sumus, ac divitias dandas in ipsum credentibus. Filiam nominat Sion. Sive autem velit quis antiquam illam, utpote jam adeptam mi- sericordiam, & fide justificatam, sive novam, id est, Ecclesiam intelligere: non absurde dixerit, quod hæc sit illius Sionis filia. Primi enim ex san- guine Israelis oriundi crediderunt: Et gentium Ec- clesia velut filia quædam dicta est ejus, quæ ab initio ab illis constituta est. Et Hieronymus: Dicite Fi- liæ Sion, quæ vel ideo appellatur filia Sion: quia pri- mum orta est ex Judæis. De qua dicit in Cantico Canticorum: Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt adver- sum me. Vel certe propterea filia: quia à Deo ad- optionis nomen accepit. Quotquot enim suscepe- runt eum, dedit eis potestatem, ut filii Dei fie- rent. Quid est autem, quod jubentur magistri at- que doctores Sion filiæ nunciare? Ecce Salvator tuus venit, qui in Hebraico dicitur Jesus. Unde & Ga- briel ad Joseph: Et vocabis, inquit, nomen ejus Je- sum: ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum à peccatis eorum. Quæ prolixius & eleganter exe- quitur Brentius: Sicut Propheta in spiritu videt Gentes magna multitudine accedere ad audien- dumEvangelion, & ad credendum inChristum: ita etiam videt Christum intrare in die Palmarum a- sino vectum, & multa populi turba comitatum, in urbem Hierusalem.Sic enim interpretatur hunc locum Evangelista Matthæus, cum recitaturus va- ticinium Zachariæ de Christo super asinam adven- tante, præponit hoc dictum Esaiæ. Dicite filiæ Sion: significans videlicet, quod sicut Zacharias videt in sua concione Christum asello in die Pal- marum advehi, ita Esaias his verbis jubeat expo- nere Ecclesiæ, quis sit ille, qui sic asello vectus ad- veniat, & quid de ipso sit sentiendum. Dicite, in- quit, filiæ Zion, Ecce Servator tuus venit. Videtur quidem avehi, & urbem Hierusalem ingredi ab- jectus quispiam homo, & tam egenus, qui non ha- beat proprium asinum, quo vehatur, sed ne- cesse habeat uti accommodatitio: Tu vero filia Zion, noli de ipso judicare secundum externam speciem. Ecce enim venit ישוע hoc est, JE- SUS seu salvator tuus. Sic enim & alias Mat- thæus scribit, Angelum ad Joseph dixisse; Vo- cabis nomen ejus JESUS, hoc est, Salvator, Is enim salvum faciet populum suum à peccatis suis. Venit igitur Jesus in urbem Hierusalem abjectus quidem & humilis, si externam ejus speciem intuearis, sed si explicueris eam, & propius eum inspicias, ve- nit afferens secum mercedem & præmium suum. Ecce, inquit, merces ejus cum illo, & opus, hoc est, præmium operis ejus, coram ipso. Quæ ergo est merces, quod est præmium ejus? Nimirum hoc, quod nomine ejus significatur. Vocatur enim Je- sus, hoc est, Salvator. Affert ergo secum veram summam & æternam salutem. Hæc est merces, hoc est præmium credentium in ipsum. Reges mundani cum initio veniunt in metropoles suas, solent Regalia sua beneficia, quæ vocant Feuda, in bene de se meritos conferre. Sed quales sunt Re- ges, talia sunt & Feuda, videlicet mundana, terrena, & peritura: quæ feudatarium nec in morte, nec in horroribus inferni servare possunt. Jesus Christus autem, Rex cœlestis, veniens in suam Metropolin Hierusalem, collocat sese in throno majestatis suæ, ut conferat in credentes suos cœlestia feuda, quæ sunt merces & præmium ejus, quorum feudorum aliud est remissio peccatorum, aliud imputatio ju- stitiæ suæ, aliud adoptio in filios & hæredes Dei, aliud liberatio à morte & inferno: breviter, uno æternæ salutis, quam secum credentibus affert, no- mine comprehenduntur omnia cœlestium feudo- rum genera. Quæ de MERCEDE ejus dicuntur, pertinent tum ad adventum primum, tum ad se- cundum: Nam merces illa cum eo venit sub primum adventum ratione acquisitionis, quia paravit ean- dem, & promtus est ad eandem distribuendam, imo distribuit eam: levari etiam inter gentes vult signum, & auditum facit usque ad extremum terræ: Sed ple- naria distributio fiet in adventu novissimo. Ideo de eodem hæc eadem sententia adhibetur Apoc. 22. Hæc Brentius. Quæ breviter complexus est Osian- der: Dicite filiæ Sion (urbi Jerusalem) Ecce Salva- tor venit. (Christus enim primo venit ut Salvator, postremo venit ut Judex: In quo tamen judicio omnibus in se credentibus nihilominus Salvator erit.) Ecce merces ejus cum eo, & opus ejus, id est, præmium operum ejus coram illo, id est, Christus adfert secum universum meritum suum, ut illud imputet atque donet omnibus in ipsum vere cre- dentibus. Nunc ergo obscurum non est quomo- do nova illa nomina populi & civitatis intelli- genda sint. Quæ argumento etiam evidenti sunt, non de externa civitate, aut populo Judaico ist- hæc vaticinia intelligenda esse: Sed de Spirituali Hierosolyma, Ecclesiâ Dei & populo Domini e- lecto. Huic enim proprium est, quod sit populus Sanctus à Domino redemtus: Et illa vere est civi- tas quæsita, & non derelicta, quum ex adverso ur- bi terrenæ Jerusalem postea dictum sit: Ecce de- serta relinqueris Matth. 23. Quod adversus glos- sam Judaicam Grotii observandum. Unde Cyril- lus: Tu autem ô Sion, sive Ecclesia vocaberis requisi- ta civitas, & non derelicta. Requisitam dicit, & memoria dignam. Tenetur enim memoria quod quæ- ritur. Et non derelicta, ut prima illa, id est, infide- lium multitudo. Dictum est igitur à Deo, voce Hieremiæ: Dereliqui domum meam, dimisi hæ- reditatem meam. Dictumq; est per ipsum omnium nostrum Servatorem Christum: Ecce relinquitur vobis domus vestra. Hieronymus ita habet: Et vocabit eos ipse Dominus atque salvator. Sive juxta Hebraicum: Vocabunt eos, Apostolici viri, populum sanctum & redemptum à Domino, qui redemti sunt Christi sanguine. Recte itaque confert hic Brentius nomina superiora, ut conclusio cum ini- tio hujus concionis conveniat. Postquam adve- nerit Jesus, Salvator, & sederit in throno ma- jestatis suæ, ut conferat in credentes suos cœle- stia feuda, tunc vere fiet id, quod suprà dictum est, ut populus ejus vocetur novis nominibus. Nunc enim propter multa & magna peccata, pro- pter vastationem metropoleos ejus, propter ser- vitutem & captivitatem ejus vocatur populus pro- phanus, à Domino abjectus, & metropolis ejus vocatur deserta, quam nemo requirat, ut in ipsa habitet. Sed cum advenerit JESUS, Salvator, vocabitur populus sanctus: quia expiabit peccata e- jus, & placabit iram Dei, ut quotquot in ipsum cre- dunt, reputentur coram Deo justi, & sancti propter Jesum. Vocabitur etiam populus redemptus à Domi- no: quia Jesus, qui est verus Dominus Deus noster, redimet eos a potestate Satanæ, a morte & inferno, & conferet in eos æternam vitam & cœleste re- gnum. Similiter Hierusalem metropolis eorum, non vocabitur amplius deserta, aut abominabilis, sed vocabitur quæsita, quia gentes, quam antea summo fastidio abominabantur, eam summo vicis- sim studio quærent & diligentissime investigabunt, ut fiant cives ejus. Hæc autem inquisitio & inve- stigatio tum fieri solet, cum Gentes in hoc studium incumbunt, ut Evangelion Christi cognoscant, & justitiæ ac salutis Christi participes fiant. Quære- bat Cornelius Centurio urbem Hierusalem, cum vocavit ad se Apostolum Petrum, ut audiret ex eo Evangelion Christi. Quærebant Macedones ur- bem Hierusalem, cum vir Macedo apparuit Pau- lo, & precatus est eum, ut profectus in Macedo- niam succurrat ipsis. Atque hæc ad c. 62.

## 63:1 Argument
CHAPTER LXIII. A dialogue of the Church and Christ concerning the bloody victory of the treader of the winepress, and a celebration of the mercies of the Lord, the Angel of the Redeemer, and the Holy Spirit the Guide, as well as a prayer for the liberation of the people and the trampling of the enemies.

Ver. 1. WHO IS THIS WHO COMES FROM EDOM, WITH STAINED GARMENTS FROM BOSRA] Here a vision was offered to the Prophet concerning Judas Maccabeus, who devastated Idumea, and captured and burned Bosra—which is Βόσρα in Ptolemy and Strabo, and Βοσόῤῥα in Josephus and the writer of the Maccabees—having killed all the males who were of military age. See Josephus 12, 11, 12. I Macc. 1, 5. Not unlike this is that Virgilian thought: 'Who is that from afar, distinguished by olive branches, bearing sacred things? I recognize the hair and graying chin of the Roman King.' The Idumeans had always rejoiced greatly at the misfortunes of the Jews. See Ps. 137, 7. Therefore, it was very relevant to the matter that this consolation from the evils which were about to befall the Idumeans through the Jews be represented to the Jews by the Prophet, like that [passage] in the same Virgil: 'He, the victor, will drive his chariot to the high Capitols, having triumphed over Corinth, distinguished by the slaughter of the Achaeans.' 'He will overthrow Argos and Agamemnonian Mycenae, and the descendant of the arms-powerful Achilles himself, having avenged his ancestors of Troy and the violated temples of Minerva.' Stained garments, that is, bloody from the blood of the enemies. THIS ONE BEAUTIFUL IN HIS ROBE] Beautifully dressed in a military cloak. MARCHING IN THE MULTITUDE OF HIS STRENGTH] That is, leading an army, and he himself like a great army. Ver. 2. I WHO SPEAK JUSTICE] That Maccabeus, who was one day to go forth, answers the Prophet: 'I am that one who defended the true religion against Antiochus and his power.' AND A CHAMPION TO SAVE] 'Who expose myself to all dangers so that I may save the people.' A true description of Judas Maccabeus. WHY THEREFORE IS THY GARMENT RED, AND THY CLOTHING LIKE THOSE TREADING IN THE WINEPRESS?] 'Tell me,' says the prophet, 'whence this gore has sprinkled your clothes, just as men are accustomed to be sprinkled who labor in the winepress.' This simile is frequent among the Hebrews. See Lam. 1, 15. But in that Hebrew word אדם, that is, 'red,' there is a manifest allusion to the name of Idumea.

Latin:

CAPUT LXIII. Colloquium Ecclesiæ & Christi de cruenta cal- catoris torcularis victoria, & celebratio miserationum Domini, Angeli Redempto- ris, & S. S. Ductoris, nec non oratio pro li- beratione populi & conculcatione hostium.

Vers. 1. QUIS EST ISTE QUI VENIT DE EDOM, TINCTIS VESTIBUS DE BOSRA] Hic Prophetæ ob- latum est visum de Juda Maccabæo, qui Idumæam va- stavit, Bosram quæ Βόσρα Ptolemæo & Straboni, Βοσόῤῥα Josepho & Maccabaicorum Scriptori, cepit atque incen- dit, cunctis maribus qui militaris essent ætatis interfectis. Vide Josephum 12, 11, 12. I. Macc. 1, 5. Non dissimilis est ἔννοια illa Virgiliana: Quis procul ille autem ramis insignis Olivæ Sacra ferens? nosco crines incanaque menta Regis Romani. Idumæi plurimum semper gavisi fuerant Judæorum malis. Vide Ps. 137, 7. Ideo multum ad rem pertinebat solatium hoc ex malis, quæ Idumæis per Judæos eventura erant, per Prophetam Judæis velut repræsentari: quale illud apud eundem Virgilium: Ille triumphata Capitolia ad alta Corintho Victor aget currum, cæsis insignis Achivis. Eruet ille Argos, Agamemnoniasque Mycenas, Ipsumque Æaciden genus armipotentis Achilli, Ultus avos Trojæ, templa & temerata Minervæ. Tinctis vestibus. id est, cruentis ab hostium sanguine. ISTE FORMOSUS IN STOLA SUA] Pulchre paludatus. GRADIENS IN MULTITUDINE FORTITU- DINIS SUÆ] Id est, Agmen agens, magnique ipse agminis instar. Vers. 2. EGO QUI LOQUOR JUSTITIAM ] Re- spondet Prophetæ ille exiturus olim Maccabæus: Ego ille sum qui religionem veram contra Antiochum, ejusque potentiam defendi. ET PROPUGNATOR AD SALVANDUM] Qui omnibus periculis me objicio, ut populum servem. Vera descriptio Judæ Maccabæi. QUARE ERGO RUBRUM EST INDUMEN- TUM TUUM, ET VESTIMENTA TUA SICUT CALCANTIUM IN TORCULARI?] Dic, ait prophe- ta, unde iste cruor vestes tuas aspersit, sicut viri aspergi solent, qui in torculari laborant. Similitudo hæc frequens Hebræis. Vide Thren. 1, 15. in ista autem voce Hebræa אדם id est, rubrum, manifesta est allusio ad nomen Idumææ.

## 63:3
Ver. 3. I HAVE TRODDEN THE WINEPRESS ALONE AND OF THE NATIONS THERE IS NO MAN WITH ME] Judas Maccabeus, offered in a vision to the Prophet, speaks again and says that it is no wonder if he is bloodied, since he himself alone with a few Jews, with no help from outsiders, fought first with the Philistines, then with the Idumeans. There is also an ingenious allusion here; for פורה, which signifies a winepress, is also the name of a city of the prince of the Philistines. I HAVE TRODDEN THEM IN MY WRATH] It is from the Hebrew בחמתי: the LXX read כעפרות, or something similar, for they translate it as 'as the earth.' THEIR BLOOD IS SPRINKLED UPON MY GARMENTS] In the Hebrew: 'Strength is sprinkled': metonymically, that is, blood, in which is the strength of man.

I HAVE STAINED] In the Hebrew word אגאלתי, the א is for ה.

Latin:

Vers. 3. TORCULAR CALCAVI SOLUS ET DE GENTIBUS NON EST VIR MECUM] Judas Macca- bæus in viso oblatus Prophetæ rursum loquitur, aitque non mirum esse, si cruentatus sit, quandoquidem ipse so- lus cum paucis Judæis, nullo externorum adjuvante, pri- mum cum Philisthinis, deinde cum Idumæis pugnaverit. Est & hic ingeniosa allusio; nam פורה quod torcular signi- ficat, est & nomen urbis principis Philisthinorum. CONCULCAVI EOS IN IRA MEA] Est ex Hebræo בחמתי: LXX. legerunt כעפרות, aut simile aliquid, vertunt enim ὡς γῆν. ASPERSUS EST SANGUIS EORUM SUPER VESTIMENTA MEA] In Hebræo: Aspersa est fortitu- do: μετωνυμικῶς, id est, sanguis, in quo est hominis for- titudo.

INQVINAVI] In voce Hebræa אגאלתי א est א pro ה.

## 63:4
Ver. 4. FOR THE DAY OF VENGEANCE IS IN MY HEART] I saw that the day long desired by me had come, in which I would take vengeance on the descendants of Esau.

THE YEAR OF MY REDEMPTION] In the Hebrew: 'Of my redeemed ones.' That is, so that, with the Idumeans subdued, I may henceforth free the Jews from vexations such as they have often suffered before now from the Idumeans.

Latin:

Vers. 4. DIES ENIM ULTIONIS IN CORDE MEO] Videbam venisse diem pridem mihi exoptatum, quo ul- tionem de Esavi posteris sumerem.

ANNUS REDEMTIONIS MEÆ] In Hebræo : Redimendorum meorum. Id est, ut perdomitis Idumæis, Ju- dæos imposterum liberem à vexationibus, quales sæpe antehac ab Idumæis pertulêre.

## 63:5
Ver. 5. I LOOKED AROUND, AND THERE WAS NO HELPER] At that time there were no treaties for the Jews with those nations: for those which were made with Demetrius, with the Romans, with the Spartans, were made afterwards.

MY ARM HAS SAVED FOR ME] My arm has procured salvation for me.

AND MY INDIGNATION ITSELF HAS HELPED ME] In the Hebrew: 'My heat (that is, my burning spirit) helped me.' For that Judas 'put on a breastplate as a giant, and girded on his weapons of war; he set up battles, protecting the camp with his sword, and he was likened to a lion in his works, and as a lion's whelp roaring for his prey. And he pursued the lawless, searching them out, and he burned those who troubled his people, and the lawless were shaken from fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled, and salvation was prospered in his hand; and he embittered many kings and gladdened Jacob in his works. And his memorial is for a blessing unto eternity.' Macc. 3. This heat is called ὁ ζῆλΘ; νόμε, such as was in Phinehas and Elijah. 1 Macc. 2, 54. 58.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CIRCUMSPEXI, ET NON ERAT AUXI- LIATOR] Eo tempore nulla erant Judæis cum gentibus il- lis foedera : nam ea quæ facta sunt cum Demetrio, cum Romanis, cum Spartiatis, facta sunt postea.

SALVAVIT MIHI BRACHIUM MEUM] Salu- tem mihi peperit brachium meum.

ET INDIGNATIO MEA IPSA AUXILIATA EST MIHI] In Hebræo: æstus meus (id est, animus æ- stuans) fulsit me. Nam Judas ille ἐνεδύσατο θώρακα ὡς γί- γας, κὶ συνεζώσατο τὰ σκέυη τὰ πολεμικὰ αὐτῦ· πολέμες συνεσήσατο σκεπάζων παρεμβολὴν ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ, κὶ ὡμοιώθη λέοντί, ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτῦ, κὶ ὡς σκύμνῶ; ἐξευγόμενΘ; εἰς θήραν. Καὶ ἐδίωξεν ανόμες ἐξερευνῶν κὶ τὲς ταράσσοντας τὸν λαὸν αὐτῦ ἐφλόγισε, κὶ συνεσάλησαν οἱ ἄνομοι ἀπὸ τῦ φόβε αὐτῦ, κὶ πάντες οἱ ἐργάται τῆς ανομίας συνεταράχ- θησαν, κὶ ἐυωδώθη σωτηρία ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῦ· κὶ ἐπίκρανε βασιλεῖς πολλὲς κὶ ἔυφρανε τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις αυτῦ. κὶ ἕως τῦ αἰῶνΘ; τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῦ εἰς ἐυλογίαν. Macc. 3. Æstus hic nominatur ὁ ζῆλΘ; νόμε, qualis in Phinea & E- lia. 1. Maccab. 2, 54. 58.

## 63:6
