Unde & Apostolus Paulus, qui secundum justitiam, quæ in lege est, universa com- pleverat, dicit se omnia duxisse pro damno, ut Christum lucrifaceret, & propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, propter quem cuncta arbitratur quasi stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciat: & invenia- tur in eo, non habens suam justitiam, quæ ex lege est, sed per fidem Christi, quæ est ex Deo justitia. Nimirum justitia, quæ in lege est, quatenus à nobis præstatur, immunda & stercorea habenda est respectu justitiæ Christi perfectissimæ & puris- simæ, quæ in Evangelio exhibetur per fidem ap- prehendenda.

Eadem explicatio est Bernhardi serm. 1. in Fe- sto omnium Sanctorum: Quid potest esse omnis no- stra justitia coram Deo? nonne juxta Prophetam vel- ut pannus menstruatæ reputabitur? Si distincte judi- cetur, injusta invenietur omnis nostra justitia, & minus habens. Et serm. 5. in dedic. Ecclcs. Si ipse quoque justitiæ nostræ omnes ad lumen veritatis inspi- cte, velut pannus menstruatæ inveniuntur, injustitiæ deinceps quales reputabuntur? Non ergo audiendi hic Remonstrantes, dum in Script. Synod. Dodrac. notant, inepte locum hunc afferri, ut probetur præ- stantissima quæque opera regeneritorum peccatis merito dici inquinata: nec probanda ipsorum censura, qua- si ista explicatione pernitiose corrumpatur textus, ut fovendis vitiis serviat. Quibus non solum Gro- tius, sed etiam Hackspanius aures præbuit ad Pon- tificiorum consensum insuper provocans. Bellarm. l. II. de Monach. c. 13. l. 4. de justific. c. 2. Feliciani Capitonis in Vindic. V. T. Becani in Manuali, Foreri in Manual. Luth. p. 442. & aliorum. Argumenta Hackspani nullius momenti sunt: Primum ita ha- bet: Tale quid h. l. debet intelligi, propter quod in captivitatem Babyl. abducti sunt Judæi: At illi ob pec- cata crassiora, quæ merebantur exclusionem è terra Canaan, abducti sunt. Resp. Crassiora peccata non negant, aut dissimulant, qui justitiam etiam suam velut pannum menstruatæ esse agnoscunt. Et lo- quuntur Israëlitæ de se universis: in quorum cœtu non solum erant justi ac renati, sed etiam reprobi. Quum ergo illi sua etiam confiteantur peccata, ac immunditiem, gravioribus obnoxios fuisse alios, qui maxime meruêre eam abductionem, in aprico est. Nec vero fidelium adultorum quisquam est, qui non aliquando gravibus peccatis sese contami- narit. Quod ergo (2) cum Remonstrantibus urget Hackspan. bona opera renatorum non esse pannum, aut vestem menstruatæ mulieris, sed insignibus orna- ri à S.S. elogiis, & nunc vestes mundas, nunc religio- si- nem immaculatam, nunc purpuram & byssum vo- cari, hinc etiam negari de pie viventibus, quod vestimenta inquinarint Apoc. 19, 8. Es. 61, 10. Ap 3, 4. Jac. 1, 27. 2. Pet. 3, 15. id cum prioribus non pugnat: sed dextre intelligendum est: Nimirum ea elogia sunt bonorum operum, qua considerantur primum Evangelice, uti e fide redundant, & ob fidem æsti- mantur, ac lucent in oculis Dei: deinde ratione principii, qua a S.S. proficiscuntur, & ab homine renato fiunt: tertio ratione formæ: qua cum lege divina consonant, & bona sunt: quarto ratione fi- nis, qua ad gloriam Dei directa sunt. Quæ vero ob adhærentem imperfectionem & immunditiem nihil- ominus, si Deus juxta legis suæ rigorem nobiscum agere velit, merito agnoscuntur esse veluti pannus menstruatæ, quo nomine B. Lutherus Tom. I. Lat. Jen. p. 286. ex hoc loco docet, in bono opere pecca- tum esse, & Tom. II. in Commentar. Latin. p. 585. omne opus bonum (non formaliter spectatum, sed materialiter, vel qua adjunctam imperfectionem) peccatum vocat: quam orthodoxiam omnes γνησίως Lutherani contra Remonstrantes pariter & Pontifi- cios hactenus sancte custodierunt; imo e Papistis ipsis non pauci agnoverunt. Joh. Gerson lib. 4. de consol. Theol. pr. 1. quod Esaias se cum cæteris in- volvens, sibique vilescens, humili confessione protule- rit, legimus: omnes justitiæ nostræ tanquam pan- nus menstruatæ. Quis ergo justitias suas velut glo- riabundus ostentaverit Deo plusquam pannum confu- sionis suæ mulier viro? Adrianus etiam de Traje- cto postea Pontifex Romanus in 4. sentent. refe- rente Cassandro in Consultat. p. 924. Quasi pan- nus, inquit, menstruatæ sunt omnes nostræ justitiæ. Jugiter enim super pannum vitæ, quem justitiæ o- peribus teximus, stillamus saniem diversorum crimi- num. Georgius Cassander ab universa Ecclesia do- ceri observat, justitiam, quæ in obedientia manda- torum divinorum posita est, per seipsam impuram & imperfectam esse. Joh.Hofmeisterus vero in Harmon. A. C. art. 6. p. 121. non arbitratur quemquam tam sto- lidum esse, qui dicere ausit, opera nostra non egere mi- sericordia, & propitiatore Christo. Conf. explicatio- nem Lutheri 1. Joh. 1. T. 6. Altenb. p. 1190.

Vers. 6.

## 64:7
THERE IS NONE, WHO CALLS UPON THY NAME, WHO RISES UP AND TAKES HOLD OF THEE] That is, they are few, as in Ps. 14, 3. Such ὑπερβολαὶ (hyperboles) are frequent among all peoples, especially the Orientals. To call upon the name of God is to direct prayers to Him, as the Chaldean interprets here. Who rises up, that is, who rouses himself, and takes hold of thee, that is, that he may cleave to thee.

THOU HAST HIDDEN THY FACE FROM US] Thou hast withdrawn thy benevolence from us, that is, thy benefits, by metonymy.

AND HAST DASHED US DOWN BY THE HAND OF OUR INIQUITY] Better: Thou hast delivered us into the hands of our sins, just as, for instance, a debtor is assigned to a creditor. מגן is to deliver. The Greeks: παρέδωκας ἡμᾶς διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν (thou hast delivered us because of our sins): Nor does the Chaldean Interpreter say otherwise. This one of ours derived it from מוג.

There is no need for us to admit a hyperbole. In Ps. 14, 3, it certainly has no place. The Prophet speaks here of a universal ἀποστασίᾳ (apostasy), such as certainly occurred during the final times of the Jewish polity, on account of which the Jews were cast off. Cyril rightly expressed the sense of the passage: THOU ART ANGRY therefore, because, namely, we have raged cruelly, and have become sinners and wicked, so much so that all our righteousness, he says, seems to be like the cloth of a menstruous woman, that is, it is to be abhorred and is impure. For you will not easily see righteousness among the Israelites, especially now after the impiety against Christ, which is not reproved and mocked. For those who have a breast entirely naked and empty of divine and intelligible light:

how could it be that they see the path leading straight to the holy laws? Or how can they truly be just, who lack the Evangelical preaching, from which it would be permitted to learn the way of a noble conversation? They are therefore impure, even if they seem to be good and upright. And they have fallen like leaves from a tree: nor is it a wonder if, when this happens to them, the miserable ones hope that they will be utterly cast away. For they have had a labile and slippery mind, which is blown about by every wind. Nor is there any one of them who knows how to invoke God genuinely and truly, or who remembers that the conjunction which is with Him must be apprehended and embraced promptly, and as it were youthfully. But we have fallen, they say, into such misery, because You have turned Your face from us, and have delivered us because of our sins. For they could not be blessed, being rejected by God: but it is clearly necessary that those who are so heavily burdened with many sins be pierced by every evil.

Latin:

NON EST, QUI INVOCET NOMEN TUUM, QUI CONSURGAT ET TENEAT TE] Id est, pau- ci sunt, ut Psal. 14, 3. Sunt ὑπερβολαὶ tales frequentes o- mnibus populis, Orientalibus maxime. Invocare no- men Dei est ad eum preces dirigere, ut hic interpretatur Chaldæus. Qui consurgat, id est, qui se excitet, & te- neat te, id est, ut tibi adhæreat.

ABSCONDISTI FACIEM TUAM A NOBIS] Benevolentiam tuam nobis subtraxisti, id est, beneficia, per μετωνυμίαν.

ET ALLISISTI NOS IN MANU INIQUITA- TIS NOSTRÆ] Melius: Tradidistinos in manus peccato- rum nostrorum, sicut scilicet debitor creditori addicitur. מגן est tradere. Græci: παρέδωκας ἡμᾶς διὰ τὰς ἁμαρ- τίας ἡμῶν: Nec aliter Chaldæus Interpres. Hic noster à מוג derivavit.

Non est opus, ut admittamus hyperbolen. In Ps. 14, 3. certe locum illa non habet. Loquitur hic Propheta de universali ἀποστασίᾳ, qualis utiq; sub novissima tempora politiæ Judaicæ accidit, ob quam abjecti Judæi sunt. Recte sensum loci ex- pressit Cyrillus: IRATUS ES ergo, eo quod videli- cet bacchati crudeliter sumus, & peccatores ac nefa- rii extitimus, adeo ut omnis justitia nostra, inquit, panno menstruatæ mulieris esse similis videatur, id est, abominanda sit & impura. Nec enim facile videbis justitiam apud Israëlitas, maxime nunc post impie- tatem in Christum, quæ non reprehendatur & ir- rideatur. Nam qui pectus habent divino & in- telligibili lumine omnino nudum & vacuum:

qui fieri posset, ut semitam recta ad sacras leges de- ducentem videant? aut quomodo justi vere sint, qui Evangelica prædicatione carent, unde liceret præcla- re conversationis viam discere? Impuri igitur sunt, etiamsi boni & probi esse videantur. Ac tanquam folia deciderunt de arbore: nec mirum est, si cum hoc illis accidat, etiam abjectum iri se plane sperent mise- ri. Labilem namque & lubricam mentem habuerunt, quæ omni vento circumfertur. Nec quisquam eorum est, qui germane ac genuine sciat Deum invocare, aut qui meminerit, conjunctionem, quæ cum ipso est, apprehendendam & complectendam prompte, & quasi juveniliter. Cecidimus autem, inquiunt, eo miseriæ, quia avertisti faciem tuam à nobis, & tradi- disti nos propter peccata nostra. Non enim beati esse poterant à Deo rejecti: at omni malo transfigi plane oportet eos, qui adeo multis peccatis onerati sunt.

## 64:8
Verse 16.

FOR YOU ARE OUR FATHER] You treat us as a father.

AND ABRAHAM HAS NOT KNOWN US, AND ISRAEL HAS NOT ACKNOWLEDGED US] You are more justly called our father than those from whom we were born in the order of nature, and who could not relieve us established in these evils. Thus to ignore is often taken, nor did the Chaldean take it otherwise here. And the Greeks translate יָדַע as to shepherd, to pity, to save.

GOD is not called Father here because he treats them as a Father: but because he had adopted them as sons, indeed they complain here rather that he no longer has and treats the Israelites as sons. To whom, however, the faithful betake themselves: whom they move as a father, that he might move the paternal bowels of mercy. Nor do they think they can be helped only by the aid of Abraham and Israel or Jacob. But Abraham, they say, has not known us, Israel ignores us: Therefore they acknowledge that the Saints living in heaven do not know and are ignorant of them and their state. For there is no reason why we should depart from the proper and famous meaning, with Grotius, who seems here to gratify the Papists, who ascribe to the saints a particular knowledge of those things which are done on earth, against whom this clear testimony fights. Nor indeed can the Papists be much helped in this way: since they themselves ascribe to the saints not only the knowledge of singular things and the hearing of prayers, but also aid and relief, or at least are persuaded that they help them by their intercession when they are invoked.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

TU ENIM ES PATER NOSTER] Tu nos ut pa- ter tractas.

ET ABRAHAM NESCIVIT NOS, ET ISRAEL IGNORAVIT NOS] Tu justius pater noster diceris, quam illi, ex quibus naturæ ordine geniti sumus, & qui nos in his malis constitutos sublevare non potuerunt. Sic ignorare sæpe sumitur, nec aliter hic sumsit Chaldæus. Et יָדַע Græci vertunt per ποιμαίνειν, οἰκτείρειν, σώζειν.

Non hic DEUS Pater dicitur, quod ut Pater tractet ipsos: sed quod eos in filios adoptararit, imo hic queruntur potius, quod Israelitas non amplius ut filios habeat ac tractet. Ad quem tamen se reci- piunt fideles: quem ut patrem moveant, ut pater- na viscera miserationum commoveant. Neque Abrahami & Israelis vel Jacobi ope solum juvari se posse putant. Sed Abraham, inquiunt, nescivit nos, Israel ignorat nos: Prorsus ergo Sanctos in cœlis agentes se ac statum suum nescire atque ignorare, agnoscunt. Neq; enim est, cur à propria & famosa significatione recedamus, cum Grotio, qui videtur hic Papistis gratificari, sanctis notitiam eorum quæ in terris geruntur, particularem adscriben- tibus, adversus quos luculentum hoc testimo- nium militat. Neque vero multum ita juvari possunt Papistae : Siquidem ipsi sanctis non solum notitiam rerum singularium & exauditionem pre- cum, sed etiam opem & sublevationem adscribunt, aut certe eosdem se juvare intercessione sua, cum invocantur, persuasi sunt.

## 64:8
Vers. 8. AND NOW O LORD] But now O Lord; namely, when You see us turned to better things. YOU ARE OUR FATHER, BUT WE ARE CLAY] Like pottery to the potter, which the following also show. Nor is only creation regarded here, but the whole dispensation of God concerning His people. Vers. 9. BE NOT ANGRY O LORD ENOUGH] In the Hebrew: vehemently. AND DO NOT REMEMBER OUR INIQUITY ANY MORE] As God could do by His right. Therefore, even those who have turned must use prayers. BEHOLD LOOK, WE ARE ALL YOUR PEOPLE] We profess that we are Your people, that is, that we owe all our things to You. So here the Chaldean. Vers. 10. THE CITY OF YOUR HOLY ONE HAS BECOME A DESERT] In the Hebrew: The cities of Your holiness have become a desert. That is, the cities of the land of Judea, which all acknowledge You as God. SION HAS BECOME A DESERT] Sion itself or Jerusalem, not only the lesser cities. Vers. 11. THE HOUSE OF OUR SANCTIFICATION] That is, the Temple, in which we were accustomed to be expiated and to worship You. AND OF OUR GLORY] Those things of which we boasted, palaces for instance. WHERE OUR FATHERS PRAISED YOU] From the times of Zerubbabel. HAS BECOME A BURNING OF FIRE] Synecdoche. For Antiochus did not burn the whole Temple, but he burned many things in the Temple and in the city. Josephus 12, 7, he burned its (the city's) most beautiful things. The writer of the Maccabean history I. 1, 23. And he entered into the sanctuary in pride and took the golden altar, and the lampstand of light, and all its vessels, and the table of the showbread, and the libation vessels and the bowls, and the golden censers, and the veil, and the crowns, and the golden ornament that was before the temple, and he stripped everything. And afterwards 33. and he took the spoils of the city and burned it with fire. And 57. they burned the books of the law with fire, having torn them. AND ALL OUR DESIRABLE THINGS HAVE BEEN TURNED INTO RUINS] This is easy to understand from those things which we have already said. Vers. 12. WILL YOU RESTRAIN YOURSELF OVER THESE THINGS O LORD, WILL YOU BE SILENT?] Could You, O Lord, overlook these things? AND WILL YOU AFFLICT US VEHEMENTELY?] And meanwhile leave us miserable. As if Judas Maccabeus were saying, this is not credible.

These things are wrongly twisted to the times of Judas Maccabeus. For such a great calamity did not exist then. It lasted barely three and a half years. Whence Grotius had to twist the text; and since the Prophet speaks openly of the temple having been made into a burning of fire, he perverts these things as if only many things in the temple and in the city were indicated as having been burned by Antiochus. Which openly contradict the letter of the words, and these most grave complaints of the people. Nor do they seem to have weighed their gravity sufficiently, or the series of the order, who have referred them to the Babylonian captivity. Zwingli is not wrong; for since the complaint of the Prophet is greater than the calamity of the Jews was in his time, it is certain that he speaks of other times. But if you wish to refer it now to that which was given to them by the Babylonian, the magnitude of the complaint itself again does not fit, since the Prophets saw not only the return from that captivity, but also the time of the return. But it is pleasing to hear Jerome, who explains this whole passage clearly. AND NOW O LORD YOU ARE OUR FATHER. If we consider our merits, we must despair. But if we consider Your clemency, You who scourge every son whom You receive, we dare to pour out prayers. For You are our Father, who deigned to say: Israel is my firstborn son. And although we are clay and the works of Your hands, and You are our potter, and the vessel cannot answer the potter, why it was made thus or so: nevertheless, knowing that we are sons, we dare to say: Be not angry O Lord enough. We do not avoid anger, nor do we seek beyond Your patience, through which we have treasured up for ourselves wrath in the day of wrath; but this we ask, that You be not angry with us enough: that in the time of vengeance and retribution You do not remember our iniquity, but rather look upon Your people, who were once called Your people. And have mercy on the city of Your sanctuary, in which Your name was invoked, which city is called Sion and Jerusalem: which the river's stream makes glad, and in which was once the watchtower of virtues, and the contemplation of peace. Your house also, that is, the temple of our sanctification and glory, in which our fathers praised You, has fallen into ruins and ashes, and has been destroyed by a devastating fire, so that by no means are victims offered in it: the passover is not celebrated, nothing is done of the ceremonies which You commanded to be done; but all our desirable things have been turned into ruins. Since these things therefore are so, will You, O Lord, restrain Your mercy over these things, and be silent while the adversaries blaspheme, and afflict us and humble us, not in the usual manner, but excessively? All of which the Jews think were completed in the times of the Assyrians and Babylonians. We, however, according to those things which follow from the person of the Savior: I appeared to those who did not ask: I was found by those who did not seek me; we refer everything to the time of the Roman victory. Which Josephus, the writer of Jewish history, explains in seven volumes, to which he gave the title of the Jewish captivity, that is, περὶ ἁλώσεως: and it is superfluous to discuss in speech those things which are open to the eyes, since all their desirable things have been turned into ruins, and the temple, celebrated throughout the whole world, has passed into a dunghill of the new city, which was called Helia by its founder, and into a dwelling place of owls: and in vain do they say daily in their synagogues: Over all these things, O Lord, will you endure and afflict us and humble us vehemently? Let us also hear Cyril from the Greek Church. When they have pre-signified the evils of the soul and have predicted that they are ensnared by sins, unstable, and like leaves tossed hither and thither by every state, they commemorate next the external calamities which were inflicted: and they seem to deplore the devastation of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple. For after the cross of the Savior all these things were affected. And, he says, Zion has been made a desert, which was once so beautiful, that famous and populous place. And our holy house has been made an execration. They say execration for contradiction and reproach by those who are ignorant of God. For the worshippers of demons, when the holy, or those who in some way adhere to God, suffer punishment, laugh profusely and are carried away, and hold the majesty of Him who saves them in mockery. For they think perhaps that His hand is weak, and that He cannot save them: nor do they consider that they are subjected to punishment for the reason that they have committed those things which are displeasing to Him. Therefore our holy house has been made an execration. For the Temple was holy among them. And it was burned with fire, he says, which was so celebrated by the voice of the holy Fathers, and proclaimed. They say that all glorious things have collapsed. For there was no veneration at all for the sacrosanct vessels which were placed in the divine Temple, no reverence for those who plunder and burn them. And you endured, he says, in all these things and kept silent? And you cast us down even to the ground. he nevertheless permitted them to grow strong and to rush even into the temple itself. They gather from this that they have been despised on account of anger and sins, and they conceive anger for these reasons. For it is manifest that he who can prohibit an injury, yet passes it over, and permits adverse and harsh things to progress and proceed to the very end, has without doubt distilled and poured out bitter anger upon them; so that he even held his own glory in neglect and endured the mockeries of enemies. These are the words of Cyril.

ORATION VI. and last. Concerning the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the Gentiles, the happiness of the faithful, and the unhappiness of the unfaithful.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET NUNC DOMINE] At nunc Domine; nempe quando nos vides in meliora versos. PATER NOSTER ES TU, NOS VERO LU- TUM] Sicut opus fictile ad figulum, quod & sequentia o- stendunt. Neque sola creatio hic respicitur, sed tota Dei circa populum suum dispensatio. Vers. 9. NE IRASCARIS DOMINE SATIS] In Hebræo: vehementer. ET NE ULTRA MEMINERIS INIQUITATIS NOSTRÆ] Ut Deus jure suo facere posset. Ideo etiam conversi deprecationibus uti debent. ECCE RESPICE, POPULUS TUUS OMNES NOS] Profitemur nos esse populum tuum, id est, o- mnia nostra nos tibi debere. Ita hic Chaldæus. Vers. 10. CIVITAS SANCTI TUI FACTA EST DESERTA] In Hebræo: Civitates sanctitatis tuæ factæ sunt in desertum. Id est, urbes terræ Judææ, quæ omnes te Deum agnoscunt. SION DESERTA FACTA EST] Ipsa etiam Sion sive Jerusalem, non tantum urbium minores. Vers. 11. DOMUS SANCTIFICATIONIS NOSTRÆ] Id est, Templum, in quo solebamus expiari & te co- lere. ET GLORIÆ NOSTRÆ] Ea, de quibus gloria- bamur, palatia puta. UBI LAUDAVERUNT TE PATRES NOSTRI] A Zorobabelis temporibus. FACTA EST IN EXUSTIONEM IGNIS] Συνεκδοχή. Non enim omne Templum, sed in Templo & in urbe multa exussit Antiochus. Josephus 12, 7 ἐνέπρησε δὲ ἀυτῆς (urbis) τὰ κάλλισα. Scriptor Maccabaicæ historiæ I. 1, 23. Καὶ ἐἰσῆλθεν ἐἰς τὸ ἁγίασμα ἐν ὑπερηφανίᾳ κὴ ἐλάβε τὸ θυσια- στήριον τὸ χρυσῶν, κὴ τὴν λυχνίαν τῶ φωτὸς, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκέ- υη ἀυτῆς, κὴ τὴν τράπεζαν τῆς προθέσεως, κὴ τὰ σπονδεῖα κὴ τὰς φιάλας, κὴ τὰς θυΐσκας τὰς χρυσᾶς, κὴ τὸ καταπέτασμα, κὴ τὲς σεφάνες, κὴ τὸν κόσμον τὸν χρυσῶν τὸν κατὰ πρόσωπον τῶ ναᾶ κὴ ἐλέπισε πάντα. Et postea 33. κὴ ἔλαβε τὰ σκύλα τῆς πόλεως κὴ ἐνεπύρισεν ἀυτὴν πυρὶ. Et 57. τὰ βιβλία τῶ νόμκ ἐνε- πύρισαν πυρὶ κατασχίσαντες. ET OMNIA DESIDERABILIA NOSTRA VER- SA SUNT IN RUINAS] Hoc facile intellectu ex iis, quæ jam diximus. Vers. 12. NUNQUID SUPER HIS CONTINEBIS TE DOMINE, TACEBIS?] Possesne hæc, ô Domine, dissimulare? ET AFFLIGES NOS VEHEMENTER] Et in- terim nos pati miseros. Quasi dicat Judas Maccabæus, non est hoc credibile.

Perperam hæc detorquentur ad tempora Ju- dæ Maccabæi. Tanta enim tum calamitas non fuit. Ea vix per tres & dimidium annum duravit. Unde torquere textum necessum habuit Grotius; & quum aperte Propheta loquatur de templo facto in exustionem ignis, hæc ita pervertit, quasi tan- tum in templo, & in urbe multa ab Antiocho exu- sta indigitarentur. Quæ palam refragantur literæ verborum, & querelis hisce gravissimis populi. Ne- que satis earum gravitatem expendisse videntur, aut ordinis seriem, qui ad Babylonicam captivita- tem retulêre. Non male Zvvinglius; Quum enim querimonia Prophetæ major sit, quam calamitas Judæorum esset suo tempore, constat omnino de aliis loqui temporibus. Si autem nunc ad eam voles referre, quæ à Babylonio eis data est, iterum non competit ipsa querimoniæ magnitudo, quum viderent Prophetæ non tantum ex ea captivitate reditum, sed etiam tempus reditus. Sed audire juvat Hieronymum, qui totum hunc locum dilucide exponit. ET NUNC DO- MINE PATER NOSTER ES TU. Si nostra consideremus merita desperandum est. Si tuam au- tem clementiam, qui flagellas omnem filium, quem re- cipis, audemus preces fundere. Tu enim pater noster es, qui dignatus es dicere: Filius primogenitus meus Israël. Et quanquam lutum sumus & opera manuum tuarum, & fictor noster sis, nec vas figulo valeat re- spondere, quare sic vel sic factum sit: tamen scientes nos esse filios, audemus dicere: Ne irascaris Do- mine satis. Non iram vitamus, nec ultra patientiam tuam quærimus, per quam thesaurizavimus nobis iram in die iræ; sed hoc quæsumus, ne irascaris nobis satis: ne tempore ultionis atq; vindictæ memineris iniquita- tis nostræ, sed magis respicias populum tuum, qui quon- dam tuus est appellatus populus. Et civitatis sanctuarii tui misereris, in qua invocatum est nomen tuum, Quæ civitas appellatur Sion & Hierusalem: quam fluminis impetus lætificat, & in qua fuit quondam specula virtutum, & pacis contemplatio. Domus quoque tua, id est, templum sanctificationis nostræ & gloriæ, in quo laudaverunt te Patres nostri, in rui- nas & cineres concidit, & incendio vastante deleta est, ita ut nequaquam in ea offerantur victimæ: non pascha celebretur, non quicquam fiat de ceremoniis, quas tu fieri præcepisti; sed omnia desiderabilia nostra versa sunt in ruinas. Cum hæc igitur ita se habeant, nunquid Domine super his continebis misericordiam tuam, & tacebis adversariis blasphemantibus, & af- fliges nos atque humiliabis, non more solito, sed ni- mis? Quæ omnia Judæi Assyriorum & Babylonio- rum temporibus putant esse completa. Nos autem juxta ea, quæ ex persona Salvatoris sequuntur: Ap- parui his, qui non interrogabant: Inventus sum ab his, qui me non quærebant; Ad tempus Roma- næ victoriæ universa referimus. Quæ Josephus Ju- daicæ Scriptor historiæ, septem explicat voluminibus, quibus imposuit titulum captivitatis Judaicæ, id est, περὶ ἁλώσεως: & superfluum est ea sermone disse- rere, quæ oculis pateant, cum omnia desiderabilia eo- rum versa sint in ruinas, & templum toto orbe cele- bratum, in sterquilinium urbis novæ, quæ à conditore appellabatur Helia, & in habitaculum transierit no- ctuarum: frustraq; quotidie dicunt in synagogis suis: Super his omnibus, Domine sustinebis & affliges nos atque humiliabis vehementer? Audiamus e- tiam è Græca Ecclesia Cyrillum. Cum præsignifica- runt animi mala prædixerintque se peccatis irretitos, instabiles, & foliorum instar omni statu huc illuc ja- ctatos esse, commemorant deinceps & externas cala- mitates, quæ illatæ sunt: ac videntur Hierosolymo- rum vastationem deplorare, templique incendium. Nam post Servatoris crucem hæc omnia affecta sunt. Et deserta, inquit, facta est Sion, quæ adeo speciosa fuit aliquando, celebris illa & populosa. Factaque est execratio domus sancta nostra. Execrationem dicunt, pro contradictione & convicio Deum ignoran- tibus. Cultores enim Dæmoniorum, cum sancti, aut qui aliquo modo adhærent Deo, patiuntur suppli- cium, profuse rident & efferuntur, & majestatem e- jus, qui servat illos, ludibrio habent. Putant enim fortassis manum ejus laborare, nec posse illos servare: nec cogitant eos pœnæ ideo subjectos esse, quod ea pa- traverint, quæ illi displicent. Execratio igitur facta est domus sancta nostra. Sanctum enim fuit apud illos Templum. Et igne combustum est, inquit, quod voce sanctorum Patrum adeo decantatum, celebratum ac prædicatum est. Concidisse ajunt o- mnia gloriosa. Nulla enim omnino erat veneratio sacrosanctorum vasorum, quæ in divino Templo po- sita fuerunt, nulla reverentia his, qui illa diripiunt & incendunt. Ac sustinuisti, inquit, in his omnibus & conticuisti? nosq; ad solum usque prostravisti. Quia enim repellere poterat hostilem incursum, per- misit tamen eos invalescere, & in ipsum etiam tem- plum irruere. Colligunt inde se propter iram & pec- cata despectos esse, iramq; his de causis concipiunt. Qui enim potest injuriam prohibere, prætermittit tamen, & res adversas & asperas ad finem usq; pro- gredi & procedere permittit, acerbam iram procul dubio in eos destillasse & effudisse eum, manifestum est: itaut etiam suam gloriam neglectui habuerit, & lu- dibria hostium sustinuerit. Hæc Cyrillus.

ORATIO VI. & ultima. De repudio Judæorum ac vocatione gentium, felicitate fidelium, infelicitate infidelium.

## 65:1 Argument
CHAPTER LXV.

The conversion of the Gentiles, and the rejection of the Jews on account of infidelity and idolatry, with a few of those remnants saved, is predicted: and a threat is denounced against those who abandon God, while on the contrary all prosperous things are to happen to the servants of God. A new heaven and a new earth are promised, and the happiness of the faithful, and of the whole Church.

Verse 1.

THEY SOUGHT ME, WHO BEFORE DID NOT ASK] Here God is introduced responding to Judas Maccabeus and kindly rendering to him the reasons for his dispensation. It can be translated very well: I became accessible to those who did not ask for me. So that the sense is, as above 64, 5. Most of the Jews were very corrupt when God liberated them from Antiochus and provided excellent opportunities for managing the matter well. Some codices seem to have had הדרשתי, which the Apostle translates as εὑρέθην in Romans 10, at the end. Nor do I believe the LXX read otherwise, who translated it ἐμφανὴς ἐγενήθην. I SAID: BEHOLD ME, BEHOLD ME, TO A NATION THAT DID NOT CALL UPON MY NAME] I showed that I was present when they did not worship me.

Latin:

CAPUT LXV.

Gentium conversio, ac Iudæis propter infide- litatem & idololatriam abjectio, paucis ex iis reliquiis servatis, prædicta: & commi- natio illis, qui Deum relinquunt, denunci- ata, quum ex adverso prospera omnia ser- vis Dei eventura sint. Promittitur novum cœlum, & nova terra, & felicitas fidelium, totiusq; Ecclesiæ.

Vers. 1.

QUÆSIERUNT ME, QUI ANTE NON INTER- ROGABANT] Inducitur hic Deus respondens Judæ Maccabæo & ei comiter causas reddens suæ dispensatio- nis, Optime verti potest: Obvius factus sum iis, qui me non in- terrogabant. Ut sensus sit, qui supra 64, 5. Judæi plerique corruptissimi erant, cum Deus eos ab Antiocho liberavit, & egregias rei bene gerendæ occasiones præbuit. Videntur quidam codices habuisse הדרשתי, quod εὑρέθην vertit Apostolus Rom. 10. in fine. Nec aliter credo legisse LXX. qui verterunt ἐμφανὴς ἐγενήθην. DIXI: ECCE EGO, ECCE EGO, AD GEN- TEM, QUÆ NON INVOCABAT NOMEN MEUM] Ostendi me præsto esse, cum illi me non colerent.

## 65:2
Verse 2.

I HAVE SPREAD OUT MY HANDS ALL THE DAY TO AN UNBELIEVING PEOPLE] That is, I incited them to conversion. פרש is translated by διάσκεψιν, Neh. 8, 10. UNBELIEVING] סרר rebellious. Thus the Chaldean here. Nor does it signify anything else, which is in the Greek ἀπειθοῦντα. WHO WALKS IN A WAY NOT GOOD AFTER HIS OWN THOUGHTS] Who obeys his own desires through illicit ways. Moreover, all these words must be explained by the imperfect: who was walking, was provoking, was sacrificing, etc.

By a forced interpretation, the former things are dragged to the Jews (since they treat of the calling of the Gentiles) and both to the times of Judas Maccabeus, when it is manifest that they pertain to the times of the New Testament. The words teach this: because the discourse is about those who previously did not ask for God, and about the Gentiles who did not call upon the name of the Lord. The context teaches this: because the reprobation of the Jewish people is added, about which there was also mention before concerning the description of the total destruction of their polity. Here a response is made to the preceding complaint about the reprobation of the Jews, and that the cause of it is not God, but the Jews themselves, because God spread out his hands to them all the day and they refused, but the Gentiles obeyed. The allegation of the Apostle teaches this, which provides an explanation clearer than the sun, Rom. 10, 20. 21., that this place treats of the calling of the Gentiles and the reprobation of the Jews, whence it is most manifest that Grotius openly contradicts the Apostle. But it is a frivolous thing that Grotius objects in his Annotations on Rom. 10, 20: that these things are adapted only to the peoples to whom the Gospel came, when they thought nothing about God and the worship of God, and that the Prophet in the latter words looks to the Jews who had followed the party of Antiochus: but that these things are applied best by the Apostle. If they could be such among the Jews then, what wonder if such are found even now. Which is a remarkable distortion of the Apostolic passage. For the Apostle does not only allude to the words of Isaiah, nor does he only apply them to his own times, but he teaches that what had been predicted about the taking in of the Gentiles and the reprobating of the Jews was fulfilled from Scripture, and for that reason he alleges the words of Isaiah, as is clear to anyone even glancing at the passage, and that is undoubted among all interpreters; Ambrose, Chrysostom, Origen on Rom. 10, 20, Cyril, Theodoret on this place, Cyprian lib. 1, cap. 10 and cap. 21, Hilary lib. 5, de Trinitat., etc. Jerome is correct; THEY SOUGHT ME WHO BEFORE DID NOT ASK. To the prayer of the people mixed with complaints, in which he had said: Why have you made us wander, O Lord, from your way: you have hardened our hearts so that we would not fear you, God the Father responded, as the Jews wish: as we prove, the Lord and Savior: I am not so rigid and cruel, who prefers the repentance of a sinner rather than his death: nor do I repel repenting children, who nevertheless have preserved the dignities of their name: so that I might even wish to save strangers. For those who did not seek me, nor could they say, whom Moses wrote of in the law and the Prophets, we have found Jesus: to them I appeared, of whom the Prophet also testified elsewhere: They to whom it was not announced concerning him, shall hear, and they who have not heard, shall understand. What Grotius trifles about a different reading of the Hebrew text is frivolous. For a different interpretation of words does not immediately suppose a different reading of the authentic text, because interpreters often looked not to the words, but to the sense. Concerning the hands spread out, Jerome also elegantly says: that Christ spread out his hands in the preaching of the word, in the exhibition of benefits and miracles, then also on the cross, when he was praying for the people: and that spread-out hands denote the generosity of the giver, that he denied nothing to them when they asked: but immediately returned health to the leper who was asking. And the man blind from birth received his eyes: And the hungry thousands of people in the desert, excluding children and women, were satisfied. That spread-out hands signify the clemency of a parent, who is eager to receive his own children into his bosom.

WHO WALKS IN A WAY NOT GOOD AFTER HIS OWN THOUGHTS.

Which there is no need to render in the past tense, since they are emphatically proposed in the present, so that that continuous perseverance of the people in defection might be expressed.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

EXPANDI MANUS MEAS TOTA DIE AD POPULUM INCREDULUM] Id est, incitavi eos ad conversionem. Vertitur פרש per διάσκεψιν, Neh. 8, 10. INCREDULUM] סרר rebellem. Ita hic Chal- dæus. Nec aliud significat, quòd est in Græco ἀπειθοῦντα. QUI GRADITUR IN VIA NON BONA POST COGITATIONES SUAS] Qui cupiditatibus suis obsequitur per vias illicitas. Hæc autem verba omnia per imperfectum exponenda sunt: qui gradiebatur, provo- cabat, immolabat, &c.

OBtorto collo priora pertrahuntur ad Judæos (quum agant de vocatione gentium) & utraq; ad tempora Judæ Maccabæi, quum manifestum sit, pertinere ad tempora N. T. Docent id verba: quia de iis sermo est, qui antea non interrogarunt Deum, & de gentibus, quæ non invocarunt nomen Domini. Docet contextus: quia subjicitur reprobatio populi Judaici, de qua etiam antea circa descriptionem πανωλεθρίας politiæ ipsorum. Respondetur hic querelæ præcedenti de reprobatione Judæorum, & quod causa ejus non Deus sit, sed ipsimet Judæi, quod ad illos tota die expanderit manus Deus, & illi abnuerint, gentes vero paruerint. Docet allegatio Apostoli, quæ explicationem Sole clariorem præ- bet, Rom. 10, 20. 21. agi hoc loco de gentium vocatio- ne & Judæorum reprobatione, unde Apostolo pa- lam repugnare Grotium manifestissimum est. Fri- volum autem est, quod Annot. ad Rom. 10, 20. ob- vertit Grotius: Aptari hæc solum populis, quibus ad- venit Evangelium, cum nihil de Deo, Deig, cultu co- gitarent, ac respicere Prophetam posterioribus verbis Judæos, qui Antiochi partes erant sequuti: Appli- cari autem hæc optime ab Apostolo. Si tunc tales esse potuêre in Judæis, quid mirum, si & nunc tales in- veniantur. Quæ insignis est στρεβλότης loci Apo- stolici. Nam non alludit tantum Apostolus ad ver- ba Esaiæ, nec applicat solum ea ad sua tempora, sed docet è scriptura impletum esse, quod de gentibus assumendis & Judæis reprobandis prædictum erat, & ea de causa allegat verba Esaiæ, uti cuivis locum vel obiter inspicienti patet, & penes Interpp. omnes indubitatum est illud; Ambrosius, Chrysostomus, O- rigenes ad Rom. 10, 20. Cyrillus, Theodoretes ad h. l. Cyprian. lib. 1. cap. 10. & cap. 21. Hilar. lib. 5. de Trinitat. &c. Recte Hieronymus; QUÆSIE- RUNT ME QUI ANTE NON INTER- ROGABUNT. Ad orationem populi mixtam querimoniis, in qua dixerat: Quare nos errare fecisti Domine de via tua: indurasti corda nostra, ut timeremus te, Respondit, ut Judæi volunt, Deus Pa- ter: ut nos probamus, Dominus atque Salvator: in tantum non sum rigidus & crudelis, qui malo pœ- nitentiam peccatoris quam mortem: nec repello filios pœnitentes, qui tamen sui nominis servave- rint dignitates: ut etiam alienos servare velim. Qui enim me non quærebant, nec dicere pote- rant, quem scripsit Moses in lege & Prophetæ, in- venimus Jesum: ipsis apparui, de quibus & alibi Propheta testatus est: Quibus non est annunciatum, de eo, audient, & qui non audierunt, intelligent. Quod nugatur Grotius de diversa lectione Ebrai- ci textus, frivolum est. Nam diversa verborum interpretatio non statim supponit diversam textus authentici lectionem, quia interpp. sæpe non ver- ba, sed sensum respexerunt. De manibus ex- pansis eleganter etiam Hieronymus: quod ex- panderit Christus manus in verbi prædicatione, bene- ficiorum & signorum exhibitione, tum in cruce etiam, cum deprecaretur pro populo: & quod expansæ manus largitatem donantis notent, quod nihil eis petentibus denegavit: sed statim roganti leproso red- diderit sanitatem. Et cæcus à nativitate acceperit oculos: Et esurientia in deserto, exceptis pueris & mulieribus, populorum saturata sint millia. Quod si- gnificent expansæ manus & parentis clementiam, suos filios in sinum recipere gestientis.

QUI GRADITUR IN VIA NON BONA POST COGITATIONES SUAS.

Quæ non opus est, ut in præterito reddantur, cum emphatice in præsenti sint proposita, ut ex- primeretur continua illa perseverantia populi in defectione.

## 65:3
Vers. 3. BEFORE MY FACE] That is, in the Temple itself & near the Temple.

WHO SACRIFICE IN GARDENS] In groves after the manner of the Gentiles, Exod. 34, 13. Deuter. 7, 5. 12, 3. Jud. 3, 7. 6, 28. 1. Reg. 14, 15. 23. 16, 32. 18, 19. 2. Reg. 13, 6. 17, 10. 16. 18, 4. and often elsewhere. AND SACRIFICE UPON BRICKS] Engraved with certain figures, Levit. 26, 1. Num. 33, 52. as it is in the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ANTE FACIEM MEAM] Id est, in ipso Tem- plo & apud Templum.

QUI IMMOLANT IN HORTIS] In lucis mo- re Gentium, Exod. 34, 13. Deuter. 7, 5. 12, 3. Jud. 3, 7. 6, 28. 1. Reg. 14, 15. 23. 16, 32. 18, 19. 2. Reg. 13, 6. 17, 10. 16. 18, 4. & alibi sæpe. ET SACRIFICANT SUPER LATERES] Figuris quibusdam incisos, Levit. 26, 1. Num. 33, 52. ut in He- bræo est.

## 65:4
Vers. 4. WHO DWELL IN THE SEPULCHRES] They stay in the sepulchres, that they may catch dreams there, as the Greeks have it here.

AND SLEEP IN THE SHRINES OF IDOLS] As was accustomed to be done in the Temples of Aesculapius. That is noted here by Jerome. You have an example in Aristides.

WHO EAT SWINE'S FLESH] They were eating it, compelled or enticed by the Gentiles, 2. Macc. 6, 18.

AND PROFANE BROTH IN THEIR VESSELS]

the Chaldean and the Greek translate it broth. If one follows the origin it seems rather that a fragment is signified. What is profane here, in Hebrew is פגול. By that word is signified whatever is forbidden by law, as appears in Ezekiel 4:14, where the Greeks [use] κρέας βέβηλον. But because that which we said פרק also signifies to reserve, Jerome thinks in his commentaries that the law given to the Priests in Leviticus 8:32 is looked to here, and that those are noted who were eating yesterday's broth, which, he says, the Greeks call ἑῶλον.

Blessed Jerome expressed the literal sense of these [words] thus: A PEOPLE, WHO PROVOKES ME TO ANGER BEFORE MY FACE ALWAYS. The Lord saying: you shall not make for yourself an Idol, nor the likeness of all things that are in heaven, and that are upon the earth. And through Moses rebuking: They provoked me by doing [so] with strange Gods, and provoked me to bitterness with their abominations. They sacrificed to Demons, and not to God. They, with a desire as if to offend, irritated and provoked God: they not only did what was not allowed, but they did it constantly and always, sinning in the sight of the Lord, to whose eyes all things are open; or sacrificing offerings to idols in his temple. And so that truly nothing might be lacking to the sacrilege, they sacrificed in gardens and burned incense upon bricks: joining luxury to idolatry, and pleasure to sacrifices: and for one altar, which had been constructed of unhewn stones by the law of God, they stained baked bricks and turfs of the fields with the blood of victims. WHO DWELT IN SEPULCHRES AND SLEEP IN THE SHRINES OF IDOLS &c. There was no sacrilege that the people of Israel omitted: not only sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense upon bricks: but also sitting or dwelling in sepulchres, and sleeping in the shrines of idols, where they were accustomed to lie down on the skins of victims, so that they might know future things through dreams. Which error the pagan [religion] and many others celebrate even to this day in the temple of Aesculapius, which are nothing else but the tombs of the dead. Nor were they content with this end of impiety, but they also fed on the flesh of swine, which was forbidden by law. And they devoured with greedy jaws the yesterday's broth which the Greeks call ἑῶλον. Whence both they themselves and their vessels were unclean: and they took on such increments of insolence and pride, that whoever was not led by a similar error, they thought him unclean, and fled from his touch. Just as the Samaritans and Jews do to us, and all heretics. And although the Jews, which is to be noted with Brentius, perhaps, who were in the times of Christ and his Apostles, did not sacrifice in gardens, nor burn incense on bricks, as their ancestors had done before the Babylonian captivity, yet by their Pharisaic and Sadducean traditions they did not only equal, but even surpassed the impiety of their ancestors: from which they were so far from repenting, and embracing the Son of God, the true Messiah, promised and expected so many years before, that they rather condemned him to death. Wherefore the Prophet, in describing the impiety of the Jews, uses indeed words customary in his own time: but by these he understands all the impious rites to which both the Jews of his own time and their descendants, up to the times of Christ and the Apostles, were subject. And so by sacrifices in gardens, incense on bricks, spending the night in caves, the eating of swine's flesh, and other impieties which the Prophet reproaches the Jews of his own time with, must be understood all those things of which Christ accuses the Jews of his own time, Matthew 15:19, 20, and in other places of the Evangelists. Cyril, however, whom some others follow, thinks that these look to the ancient customs of the people, who always strayed from God. For Christ himself also traces the punishment of the people from his ancient transgressions, Matthew

23:32. He argues, he says, against the impious Israelites, and not only at the time of his advent, but backwards and as if from the very root and from the Fathers, who, having rejected his divine law and having all but said goodbye to the Mosaic precepts, served idols, and sacrificed to falsely named Gods, and were worshippers of unclean spirits. This people, he says, is the one that always exacerbates me. For they sacrificed incessantly, i.e., for a long time, in my sight. Thus, before the Savior's advent, when Israel, whom we just mentioned, was wallowing in filth, a certain smoke and the beginnings of divine wrath appeared. But after they added to their former impieties also a raging against the Savior and Redeemer of all himself: for they killed the Prince of life, then the fury was kindled, and they were turned in a way into the flame of smoke. The most simple sentences favor this, which are added concerning the sins of the Fathers: I will repay and will recompense into their bosom your iniquities and the iniquities of your Fathers.

Latin:

Vers. 4. QUI HABITANT IN SEPULCHRIS] Manfitant in sepulchris, ut ibi captent somnia, ut hic habent Græci.

ET IN DELUBRIS IDOLORUM DORMIUNT] Ut in Æsculapii Templis fieri solebat. Notatum id hic Hieronymo. Exemplum habes apud Aristiden.

QUI COMEDUNT CARNEM SUILLAM] Comedebant à Gentibus coacti aut illecti, 2. Macc. 6, 18.

ET JUS PROFANUM IN VASIS EORUM]

jus vertunt Chaldæus & Græcus. Si originem sequa- mur, fragmentum potius significari videtur. Quod hic est profanum, in Hebræo est פגול. Ea voce significatur, quicquid lege vetitum est, ut apparet Ezech. 4, 14. ubi Græci κρέας βέβηλον. Sed quia illud, quod diximus פרק etiam reservare significat, putat in commentariis Hierony- mus, spectari hic legem Sacerdotibus datam Levit. 8, 32. & notari eos, qui edebant jus hesternum, quod, inquit, Græci vocant ἑῶλον.

Sensum literalem horum ita expressit B. Hie- ronymus, POPULUS, QUI AD IRACUNDI- AM PROVOCAT ME ANTE FACIEM MEAM SEMPER. Dicente Domino: non facies tibi Idolum, neque similitudinem omnium, quæ in cœlo sunt, & quæ super terram. Et per Mosen in- crepante: Facientes irritaverunt me in Diis alienis, & in abominationibus suis me ad amaritudinem provocarunt. Immolaverunt Dæmoniis, & non Deo. Illi studio quasi delinquendi irritarunt & pro- vocarunt Deum: non solum fecerunt, quod non li- cebat: sed jugiter semperq́; fecerunt, peccantes in con- spectu Domini, cujus oculis cuncta patent; vel in tem- plo ejus idolis hostias immolantes. Ac ne quid vero deeffet sacrilegio, immolabant in hortis & adole- bant thura super lateres: jungentes idololatriæ lu- xuriam, & sacrificiis voluptatem: & pro uno altari, quod impolitis lapidibus lege Dei erat constructum, coctos lateres & agrorum cespites hostiarum sanguine cruentabant. QUI HABITABANT IN SE- PULCHRIS ET IN DELUBRIS IDOLORUM DORMIUNT &c. Nihil fuit sacrilegii, quod Israël populus prætermitteret: non solum in hortis immolans, & super lateres thura succendens: sed se- dens quoque vel habitans in sepulchris, & in delubris idolorum dormiens, ubi stratis pellibus hostiarum in- cubare soliti erant, ut somniis futura cognoscerent. Quod in fano Æsculapii usq́; hodie error celebrat eth- nicorum multorumque aliorum, quæ non sunt aliud, nisi tumuli mortuorum. Ne hoc erant impietatis fi- ne contenti, sed porcorum quoque carnibus vesce- bantur, quod lege prohibitum erat. Et jus hesternum quod Græci vocant ἑῶλον, avidis faucibus devorabant. Unde tam ipsi, quam vasa eorum immundi erant: & in tantum procacitatis ac superbiæ augmenta ca- piebant, ut quicunq́; non simili duceretur errore, eum arbitrarentur immundum, contactumq́; ejus fugerent. Quemadmodum Samaritani & Judæi nobis faciunt, omnesq́; hæretici. Etsi vero Judæi, quod cum Brentio notandum, fortassis, qui fuerunt tem- poribus Christi & Apostolorum ejus, non sacrifi- caverunt in hortis, nec adoleverunt thymiamata in lateribus, quemadmodum majores eorum ante Babylonicam captivitatem fecerant, tamen Phari- sæicis & Sadducæicis suis traditionibus non æqua- bant tantum, verum etiam superabant majorum suorum impietatem: à qua tantum abfuit, ut resi- piscerent, & Filium Dei, verum Messiam, tot an- nis antea promissum & expectatum complecteren- tur, ut potius eum morte condemnarent. Quare Propheta, in describenda impietate Judæorum, u- titur quidem verbis suo tempore usitatis: sed his intelligit omnia impia sacra, quibus & Judæi sui temporis & posteri eorum, usq; ad Christi & Apo- stolorum tempora obnoxii fuerunt. Itaque per sa- crificia in hortis, suffitus in lateribus, pernoctatio- nem in speluncis, esum carnium suillarum, & alias impietates, quas Propheta exprobrat Judæis sui temporis, intelligenda sunt omnia illa, quorum Christus accusat Judæos sui temporis, Matth. 15, 19. 20. & in aliis locis Evangelistarum. Cyrillus ta- men, quem sequuntur alii nonnulli, hæc respicere antiquos mores populi, qui semper à Deo aberravit, existimat. Nam & Christus ipse pœnam populi ab antiquis ejus prævaricationibus repetit, Matth.

23, 32. Impios, inquit, Israëlitas arguit, nec solum ad- ventus tempore, sed retro & velut ab ipsa stirpe & ex Patribus, qui divina ejus lege rejecta & Mosaicis præ- ceptis tantum non vale dicto idolis servierunt, & fal- so nuncupatis Diis sacrificarunt, & immundorum spirituum cultores extiterunt. Hic populus, inquit, est qui semper me exacerbat. Sacrificarunt e- nim indefinenter, i. e. longo tempore, in conspectu meo. Itaœ, ante Servatoris adventum, cum in sor- dibus versaretur, quem modo diximus, Israël, velut fumi quidam & initia divinæ iræ apparuerunt. Post- quam verò prioribus suis impietatibus addiderunt et- iam debatchationem in ipsum universorum Servato- rem & Redemptorem : interfecerunt enim Princi- pem vitæ, furor deinde accensus est, & in flammam quodammodo fumi conversi sunt. Cui sententiæ sim- plicissimæ favent, quæ de Patrum peccatis addun- tur: Reddam & retribuam in sinu eorum iniquitates vestras & iniquitates Patrum vestrorum.

## 65:5
Verse 5.

WHO SAY, DEPART FROM ME, DO NOT APPROACH ME] Being impure themselves, they warded off others from themselves as impure, just as the Arab Geographer says the Samaritans cried out, Do not touch. Jerome also mentions this Samaritan custom in relation to this passage. THESE SHALL BE SMOKE IN MY FURY, A FIRE BURNING ALL THE DAY] עשׁן, if I am not mistaken, we will rightly understand here as the vapor from wood and other things, from which fire is kindled. In a more sublime sense, the Chaldean refers this to Gehenna.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QUI DICUNT, RECEDE A ME, NE APPRO- PINQUA MIHI] Ipsi impuri cum essent, alios à se ut imputos arcebant, sicut Samaritas Geographus Arabs cla- masse ait, Ne attingas. Ejus Samaritanum moris etiam ad hunc locum meminit Hieronymus. ISTI FUMUS ERUNT IN FURORE MEO, IGNIS ARDENS TOTA DIE] עשׁן, ni fallor, rectè hîc intelligemus vaporem ex lignis, rebusque aliis, unde ignis accenditur. Sublimiore sensu ad gehennam hoc re- fert Chaldæus.

## 65:6
Verse 6. BEHOLD IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE ME] I remember as well as Kings [remember] those things which they keep written in their commentaries. See Esther 6. I WILL NOT BE SILENT] I will not rest. I will not long defer their punishment, as the Chaldean [says] here.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ECCE SCRIPTUM EST CORAM ME] Tam benè memini, quam Reges ea, quæ in commentariis suis scripta asservant. Vide Esth. 6. NON TACEBO] Non quiescam. Non diu diffe- ram pœnam eorum, ut hîc Chaldæus.

## 65:7
Verse 7. BUT I WILL REPAY AND WILL RECOMPENSE INTO THEIR BOSOM YOUR INIQUITIES, AND THE INIQUITIES OF YOUR FATHERS TOGETHER] To repay into the bosom is to repay cumulatively, as things are accustomed to be poured into the bosom, Psalm 79:12. Here also the second and third persons are mixed. Those who are punished quite severely (though not above their deserts) are said to pay for both their own sins and those of them who preceded them in similar sins: and whose sins God left unpunished. See [the note] on Matthew 23:35.

Again Jerome is worthy to be heard here, paraphrasing thus: Because of your works, and the incredible arrogance of your mind, so that you, being unclean, thought the clean to be unclean, you shall be smoke, a burning fire, which is kindled from my fury. Moreover, we ought to understand fury, oblivion, anger, and repentance in God in the same way as feet, hands, eyes, ears, and other members, which the incorporeal and invisible God is said to have. Not that He is subject to these perturbations, He who extinguishes them in us by the gift of His grace, but that through our words we may understand God's affection toward us. For anger, which is a desire for vengeance, is not defined in God as it is in men: which has its matter in our vices, not in the will of the Lord: we who treasure up for ourselves wrath in the day of wrath, and revelation of the just judgment of God, so that the wise flame may consume our thistles and thorns, and tares, which we have brought forth instead of the seed of God, and also the wood, hay, and stubble, which we have built upon the foundation of Paul. Concerning this perpetual fire we also read in the song of Moses: A fire is kindled in my fury and shall burn even to the lowest hell. It shall devour the earth and its increase: it shall burn the foundations of the mountains and my arrows shall consume them. The sense of which testimony is that the fire and vengeance of God always burns for sinners, and pursues them even to the underworld. Such was that rich man clothed in purple in the Gospel, who, while Lazarus rested in Abraham's bosom, was tormented by eternal heats. Behold, he says, IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE ME. For all sins are open to the eyes of God, and are written in those books, of which we read in Daniel (chap. 7): Thrones were set, and the books were opened. I WILL NOT KEEP SILENCE. He who had said before; I have kept silent (ch. 42.) shall he not be silent forever, says the Lord, but he will repay everyone for what he has done in his bosom, that is, in the secret of the heart, so that their own conscience may torment them.

Same verse.

WHO HAVE SACRIFICED UPON THE MOUNTAINS, AND UPON THE HILLS HAVE REPROACHED ME] They have provoked me: as in the times of Abijah, Athaliah, Manasseh. For 'have sacrificed', in the Hebrew it is, 'have made incense'. Which both the Greeks follow, and the Chaldean. THE WORK OF THEM FIRST] That is, from the beginning I will repay the equivalent for all their deeds.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SED REDDAM ET RETRIBUAM IN SI- NU EORUM INIQUITATES VESTRAS, ET INI- QUITATES PATRUM VESTRORUM SIMUL] In sinum reddere est cumulatè reddere, ut quæ in sinum ef- fundi solent, Ps. 79, 12. Hic quoque permiscentur perso- næ secunda & tertia. Qui severe admodum puniuntur, (etsi non supra merita) dicuntur luere, & sua peccata, & eo- rum qui ipsos in similibus peccatis præcesserunt: quorum- que Deus peccata reliquit impunita. Vid. ad Matth. 23, 35.

Iterum dignus est, qui audiatur hîc Hierony- mus, ita παραφράζων: Propter opera vestra, & in- credibilem mentis arrogantiam, ut immundi mun- dos putaretis immundos, eritis fumus, ignis ardens, qui de meo furore succensus est. Furorem autem, oblivionem, iram, pœnitudinem, ita in Deo debemus accipere, quomodo pedes, manus, oculos, aures, & cæ- tera membra, quæ habere dicitur incorporalis & invi- sibilis Deus. Non quo his pateat perturbationibus, qui eos dono gratiæ suæ extinguit in nobis, sed quo per no- stra verba Dei erga nos intelligamus affectum. Neq́ enim ira, quæ est ultionis libido, ita definitur in Deo, ut in hominibus: quæ materiam habet in nostris vi- tiis, non in Domini voluntate: qui thesaurizamus nobis iram in die iræ, & revelationis justi judicii Dei, ut tribulos nostros & spinas, & zizania, quæ pro semine Dei attulimus, ligna quoque, fœnum, & sti- pulam, quæ super fundamentum Pauli ædificavimus, sapiens flamma consumat. De hoc igne perpetuo & in Moysis cantico legimus: Ignis accensus est de furore meo & ardebit usque ad infernum deor- sum. Devorabit terram & genimina ejus: com- buret fundamenta montium & sagittæ meæ consu- ment eos. Cujus testimonii sensus est, quod ignis Dei atq́; vindicta semper ardeat peccatoribus, & eos usq́; ad inferos persequatur. Qualis erat & dives ille in Evan- gelio purpuratus, qui requiescente Lazaro in sinu Ab- raham,æternis torquebatur ardoribus. Ecce, inquit, SCRIPTUM EST CORAM ME. Omnia enim peccata Dei patent oculis, & in his scripta sunt libris, de quibus in Daniele legimus (cap. 7.) Throni positi sunt, & libri aperti sunt. NON TACEBO. Qui prius dixerat; Tacui (c. 42.) numquid semper tace- bit, dicit Dominus, sed reddet unicuique, quod operatus est in sinu ejus, h. e. in cordis arcano, ut eos propria torqueat conscientia.

Vers. eod.

QUI SACRIFICAVERUNT SUPER MONTES, AC SUPER COLLES EXPROBRAVERUNT MIHI] Irritarunt me: ut temporibus Abiæ, Athaliæ, Manassis. Pro sacrificaverunt, in Hebræo est, suffitum fecerunt. Quod & Græci sequuntur, & Chaldæus. OPUS EORUM PRIMUM] Id est, à principio o- mnibus eorum factis vicem rependam.

## 65:8
Verse 8. AS IF A GRAIN BE FOUND IN A CLUSTER?] That is, a whole grape among many corrupt grapes. AND IT BE SAID, DO NOT DESTROY IT] A head of a household is accustomed to order it to be saved. BECAUSE IT IS A BLESSING] That is, in it is the hope of a new vine. The Hebrews call everything by which we are nourished by the name of blessing. SO WILL I DO FOR THE SAKE OF MY SERVANTS, THAT I MAY NOT DESTROY THE WHOLE] I will save a few good ones for the hope of the race, as once Noah with his own: which example the Chaldean uses here; and Lot in the destruction of the Sodomites. Paul adapts these things to the Gospel, Rom. 11:5.

If these things are adapted by the Apostle to the Gospel and N.T. times, Rom. 11:5, why are they dragged and snatched away to the times of Antiochus by Grotius? And therefore an argument is provided for us here again, that the present prophecy looks to the times of the New Testament, and to the remnant of Israel according to the election of grace, which were saved then, no differently than a grain in a cluster: in which there is a blessing, for the sake of the holy and faithful servants of the Lord. Brentius agrees: If the Jews are cast off and disinherited by the Lord, what then will happen? Shall all be cast off in such a way that not even one or another obtains salvation? The Prophet is now preaching about this matter, and teaches that even though the multitude of the Jews will be blinded and disinherited, yet a remnant shall be saved. For that he is preaching here about the salvation of the remnant, Paul explains not obscurely, who, writing to the Romans, imitates this place of the Prophet. For after he had recited what was said above: I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, and had explained concerning the rejection of the Jews, he immediately adds: I say then, Has God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, etc. And immediately; Even so at this time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace: This is clearly that which the Prophet is preaching in this place. The Israelites will indeed be cast off and disinherited: but just as, if in a vineyard devastated by enemies or wild beasts, or in the cutting down of a sterile vineyard, there is still remaining one or another cluster full of must, this cluster is not cast away or despised, but is diligently preserved, lest it be destroyed or trampled by feet, and the blessing and clemency of God is acknowledged, and thanks are given to him, because in such great poverty he has at least saved a few whole clusters, so it will also happen in the rejection of the Israelites. A great and horrible blindness will indeed rush upon the entire Israelite nation: and yet some will be saved by divine clemency, so that they do not perish together with the others. So will I do, says the Lord, for the sake of my servants, that I may not destroy the whole. Although the multitude of the Jews perishes, I still have among the Jews certain servants, whom I will preserve, so that they are not cast off together with the impious. These servants are Zechariah, Elizabeth, Simeon, Anna, the Shepherds, Joseph, Mary, the Apostles, the disciples, and those who were converted from the Jews on the day of Pentecost, and afterwards to Christ our Lord.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QUOMODO SI INVENIATUR GRANUM IN BOTRO?] Id est, acinus integer inter multas uvas corruptas. ET DICATUR, NE DISSIPES ILLUD] Solet paterfamilias illud jubere servari. QUONIAM BENEDICTIO EST] Id est, in eo spes novæ vitis. Omnia quibus alimur benedictionis no- mine appellant Hebræi. SIC FACIAM PROPTER SERVOS MEOS, UT NON DISPERDAM TOTUM] Paucos bonos servabo in spem generis, ut olim Noam cum suis: quo exemplo hic utitur Chaldæus; & Lothum in excidio Sodomorum. Hæc ad Evangelium aptat Paulus Rom. 11, 5.

Si hæc ad Evangelium & N. T. tempora aptan- tur ab Apostolo, Rom. 11, 5. cur trahuntur & abri- piuntur ad tempora Antiochi à Grotio? ideoque Argumentum hic iterum nobis subministratur, quod vaticinium præsens spectet ad tempora No- vi Testamenti, & ad reliquias Israëlisfecundum ele- ctionem gratiæ, quæ tum servabantur, non secus ac granum in botro: in quo est benedictio, propter servos Domini sanctos & fideles. Consonat Bren- tius: Si Judæi abjicientur & exhæredabuntur à Domino,quîd ergo fiet? Num sic omnes abjicien- tur, ut ne unus quidem aut alter salutem consequa- tur? De hac re concionatur nunc Propheta, & do- cet, quod etsi multitudo Judæorum excæcabitur & exhæredabitur, tamen reliquiæ salvæ fiant. Nam quod hic de salute reliquiarum concionetur, haud obscure exponit Paulus, qui ad Romanos scribens hunc locum Prophetæ imitatur. Postquam enim recitasset, quod supra dictum est: Expandi manus meas tota die ad populum rebellem, & exposuisset de abjectione Judæorum, mox subjicit: Dico igitur, Num repulit Deus populum suum? Absit. Nam & ego Israëlita sum ex semine Abraham &c. Et statim; Sic & hoc tempore reliquiæ secundum electionem gra- tiæ fuerunt: Hoc plane illud est, quod in hoc loco Propheta concionatur. Abjicientur quidem, & exhæredabuntur Israëlitæ: sed quemadmodum, si in vastata ab hostibus aut feris vinea, aut in excisione vineæ sterilis, reliquus adhuc sit botrus unus aut alter musto plenus, non abjicitur aut contemnitur hic bo- trus, sed diligenter conservatur, ne dissipetur, aut pe- dibus conculcetur, & agnoscitur benedictio & clemen- tia Dei, & aguntur ei gratiæ, quod in tanta pauperie vel saltem paucos botros integros servarit, ita fiet quo- que in abjectione Israëlitarum. Magna quidem & horribilis cæcitas irruet in universam gentem Is- raëliticam: & tamen servabuntur nonnulli divina clementia, ne una cum aliis pereant. Sic faciam, inquit Dominus, propter servos meos, ne totum disperdam. Etsi multitudo Judæorum perit, ha- beo tamen inter Judæos adhuc quosdam servos, quos conservabo, ne una cum impiis abjiciantur. Hi servi sunt Zacharias, Elisabeth, Simeon, Anna, Pastores, Joseph, Maria, Apostoli discipuli, & qui ex Judæis conversi sunt in die Pentecostes, & post- ea ad Christum Dominum nostrum.

## 65:9
Verse 9. AND I WILL BRING FORTH FROM JACOB A SEED] Just as in a seed, a small thing, there is a tree, so in those few there will be that from which the whole nation may be renewed.

It is too fragile an argument from the appellation of seed to conclude the renewal of the whole nation. Since the remnant are called seed not by reason of the generation of the carnal people, but because through them Israel was propagated according to the spirit. Whence, rightly Osiander (with other interpreters who easily agree here) thus paraphrased: who here easily agree) thus paraphrased: AND I WILL BRING FORTH FROM JACOB A SEED, that is, I will propagate from the Patriarchs some holy posterity, AND FROM the Kingdom of Judah I will give a people possessing my (holy) mountains: and my elect, whom I have created for eternal life, shall inherit that land: and my servants (who worship me with a sincere mind and faith) shall dwell there, that is, The holy Patriarchs shall have a copious spiritual posterity (Christians, indeed, arising from various nations:) that posterity shall not worship God on that one mountain of Zion, but on my many mountains, that is, in the Churches, which I am about to collect for myself here and there in the world by the preaching of the Gospel. And they shall be true members of the Church, and heirs of the heavenly kingdom. For those who believe in Christ (from whatever nation they derive their lineage) these are true Israelites, Gal. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET EDUCAM DE JACOB SEMEN] Sicut in semine, re parva, est arbor, ita in illis paucis erit unde gens tota renovetur.

Nimis fragile argumentum est ex appellatio- ne seminis ad concludendam gentis totius renova- tionem. Quum semen dicantur reliquiæ non ratio- ne generationis populi carnalis, sed quia per illos propagatus est Israël secundum spiritum. Unde, recte Osiander (cum cæteris Interpp. qui hic facile consentiunt) ita παρῳδησέ: ET EDUCAM DE JACOB SEMEN, id est, propagabo de Pa- triarchis sanctam aliquam posteritatem, ET DE Re- gno Juda dabo populum possidentem montes (san- ctos) meos: & hæreditabunt eam terram electi mei, quos ad æternam vitam creavi: & servi mei (qui me sincero animo & fide colunt) habitabunt ibi, id est, Habebunt sancti Patriarchæ copiosam posteri- tatem spiritualem (Christianos nimirum ex variis gen- tibus oriundos:) ea posteritas non colet Deum in unico illo monte Sion, sed in multis montibus meis, hoc est, in Ecclesiis, quas passim in mundo Evangelii præ- dicatione mihi sum collecturus. Et erunt illi vera membra Ecclesiæ, & hæredes regni cælestis. Qui enim in Christum credunt (ex quacunque gente genus suum ducant) hi sunt veri Israëlita, Gal. 6.

## 65:10
Verse 10.

AND THE PLAINS SHALL BE FOR FOLDS OF FLOCKS] in the Hebrew: And Sharon shall be a fold of the flock. That region shall be as full of cattle as folds are accustomed to be. Jerome says that region is near Lydda, Joppa, and Jamnia, most suitable for pasturing cattle, which we also learn from 1 Chron. 27:29.

AND THE VALLEY OF ACHOR FOR A FOLD OF HERDS] As full of herds as stables are wont to be. By the valley of Achor is understood that most beautiful tract near Jericho. See Jos. 7, 24. 26. Hos. 2, 15.

Since he follows Jerome in those secondary matters, why did he not follow him in that upon which the hinge of the matter turns? For the Saint had warned, from the Apostle, that God does not care for oxen, lest these things be drawn to carnal things alone. We shall add his passage. AND THE PLAINS or forests SHALL BE FOR THE FOLDS OF FLOCKS. For plains, in the Hebrew שרון is placed. Every region around Lydda, Joppa, and Jamnia is suitable for pasturing flocks. Concerning which it is also written in the Acts of the Apostles: the forests shall be turned into sheepfolds: according to that which is sung in the Psalm: The voice of the Lord perfecting the harts, and He shall reveal the forests, or the thickets of the woods: so that robbers may cease to hide there, and venomous beasts, animals, and places once of snares and blood, may pass into the Churches of the Lord: and flocks may be pastured there by Him who laid down His life for His sheep. Concerning whom it is written: He shall feed us forever. That voice of the Lord perfecting the harts, and revealing the thickets of the woods, was crying through John in the wilderness: Now the axe is laid to the root of the trees. Every tree which does not bring forth good fruit shall be cut down, and cast into the fire. AND THE VALLEY OF ACHOR shall be FOR A FOLD OF HERDS FOR MY PEOPLE, WHO HAVE SOUGHT ME. The valley of Achor, in which there was once a curse and punishment, shall be for the rest of herds. Which Paul, explaining, says: Does God care for oxen? Or does He say it altogether for our sakes? For he who plows ought to plow in hope: and he who threshes the floor, to thresh in hope of partaking. Concerning this valley it is also mystically written in Hosea: I will speak to her heart, without doubt, to Jerusalem: and I will give her possessors from thence, and the valley of Achor, to open her understanding. For therefore the valley of Achor is delivered into the possession of the herds of God's people, and the forests are turned into folds of flocks, that understanding may be opened and the truth of the Lord may be known. Similarly Cyril. This region, execrable in ancient times, shall be a rest for herds, i.e., stables of intelligible sheep, subject to the hand of Christ the Prince, the shepherd of all, who

He addressed the Jewish people, saying concerning the Gentiles: I have other sheep, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring. And there shall be one fold, one shepherd. For they sought him through faith, who once wandered: upon finding whom they were made his household, and fellow-citizens of the saints, and co-heirs of the goods promised to them. AND YOU WHO HAVE FORSAKEN THE LORD &c. In places, says Jerome, formerly wild and of crowds, in the places of the Gentiles shall be the sheepfolds: that is, the Churches of believers from the whole world. But you, O people of Israel, who have forsaken the Lord, and provoked to anger the Holy One of Israel: who have forgotten his holy mountain, of which we have often spoken, either the Lord Savior, who is the mountain of mountains, and the holy one of all saints: or Mount Sion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem: you who do these things and these things, I will deliver to the sword: that you may all fall slain together. There is no doubt, says Brentius, from the preceding, that here the discourse is about the Church, which was to be gathered through the Gospel from Jews and Gentiles. This Church is called the Elect and the servants, the children of God, believing, namely, in the Son of God, through the Gospel. It is promised, therefore, to this Church, that it shall dwell on Mount Sion, and that it shall possess two pastured places, Saron and the valley of Achor, for its flocks and herds. But it is manifest that it cannot be that the universal Church should dwell corporally in Jerusalem and on Mount Sion. And what heavenly salvation and happiness, to which alone we must aspire, will it bring to the Church, even if its sheep and oxen have very rich pastures? Does its salvation consist in the salvation of sheep and oxen? Wherefore these benefits are not to be understood according to the manner of the goods of an earthly kingdom, but according to the manner of the goods of the kingdom of Christ, which is spiritual and heavenly: namely, that when the Gospel is revealed, not carnal, but spiritual Israelites, gathered through the Gospel from Jews and Gentiles, are held for the true Sion or Church of the Son of God, and that in this Church there are most rich pastures: namely, the preaching of the Gospel, which is the power of God unto salvation. Concerning which pastures the Son of God preaches also in Ezekiel: I will gather, he says, my sheep from the lands, and I will bring them into their own land, and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the streams and in all the seats of the land, in most fertile pastures I will feed them. The Osiandrian Paraphrase is twofold: AND YOU WHO HAVE FORSAKEN THE LORD, who turn yourselves away from his word, neither believing nor obeying him. YOU WHO HAVE FORGOTTEN MY HOLY MOUNTAIN. The temple of the Lord on Mount Sion, that is, you who neglect true Religion: YOU WHO SET A TABLE FOR FORTUNE, Hebr. to Gad, AND OFFER LIBATIONS UPON IT, Hebr. and fill for Meni a libation: (that is, you who set up a table for Gad in honor, furnished with dishes or offerings, and pour out a libation abundantly to the idol Meni, these I will punish most severely. But it seems that Gad signified to them Mars: for Gad has its etymology from military expedition: but Meni perhaps was Mercury, the God of Merchants: for Meni is named from counting. And the following divine threat alludes excellently to these significations: I WILL NUMBER YOU TO THE SWORD, more correctly to the sword, AND YOU SHALL ALL FALL IN SLAUGHTER. That is, Because you are so greedy for war, and devoted to avarice, that counting money is among your primary delights: go on, I will number you for the slaughter and deliver you to be killed by the swords of the Roman soldiers. For although the Jews in the time of Christ perhaps worshipped neither Mars nor Mercury:

yet partly from the history of Josephus, partly from the Evangelical history, it is manifest that at that time the Jewish people were greedy for seditions and wars, and that even the Pharisees (who wished to be considered not a little better than the rest) were clearly devoted to avarice. Indeed, even trade in the temple was restored, John 2. Therefore, they are said to worship Mars and Mercury who were eager for wars and avarice, just as if one were to say of a man devoted to drunkenness and lust, that he worships Bacchus and Venus. For God generally punishes sins with those evils in which men have most delighted themselves. Let us also hear the explanation of B. Luther, which is of the same mind. THE PLAINS SHALL BE FOR FOLDS, translate it thus: SARON SHALL BE FOR A FOLD OF THE FLOCK. Furthermore, Saron and Carmel are the most praised mountains of Judea because of their pastures. Achor and Rephaim are the most praised valleys. He promises therefore Allegorically that the Church will be such, in which the word is preached daily, so that the faithful may be fed and multiplied, etc. The herds are the pious, the more robust in faith, who are apt for teaching; the flocks are the weaker ones.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET ERUNT CAMPESTRIA IN CAULAS GREGUM] in Hebræo: Et erit Saron caula pecoris. Tam plena erit ea regio pecore, quam caulæ esse solent. Eam Regionem Hieronymus esse ait apud Lyddam, Joppen & Jamnes pecori pascendo aptissimam, quod etiam disci- mus ex 1. Paral. 27, 29.

ET VALLIS ACHOR IN CUBILE ARMEN- TORUM] Tam plena armenti, quam esse solent stabula. Per vallem Achor intelligitur pulcherrimus ille tractus apud Hierichontem. Vide Jos. 7, 24. 26. Os. 2, 15.

Quum in istis secundariis sequatur Hierony- mum, cur non in illo, in quo cardo rei vertitur, se- quutus est? Monuerat enim Sanctus ex Apostolo, non de bobus curam esse Domino, ne ad sola carnalia hæc traherentur. Adjiciemus locum ejus. ET E- RUNT CAMPESTRIA sive saltus IN CAU- LAS GREGUM. Pro campestribus in Hebræo שרון ponitur. Omnis regio circa Lyddam, Joppen & Janiam apta est pascendis gregibus. De quo & in A- ctibus Apostolorum scriptum est: saltus autem ver- tentur in ovilia: juxta illud quod in Psalmo canitur: Vox Domini perficientis cervos, & revelabit sal- tus, sive condensa sylvarum: ut latrones ibi latitare desistant, & bestiæ venenatæ, animalia, & loca quon- dam insidiarum & sanguinis, in Ecclesias Domini transeant: & pascantur ibi greges ab eo, qui posuit a- nimam pro ovibus suis. De quo scriptum est: Ipse pascet nos in secula. Ista vox Domini perficiens cervos, & revelans condensa sylvarum, per Joan- nem clamabat in eremo: Jam securis ad radicem ar- borum posita est. Omnis arbor, quæ non facit fru- ctum bonum, excindetur, & in ignem conjicietur. ET VALLIS ACHOR erit IN CUBILE AR- MENTORUM POPULO MEO, QUI QUÆ- SIVERUNT ME. Vallis Achor, in qua quondam maledictio fuit atque supplicium, erit in requiem ar- mentorum. Quæ Paulus edisserens, ait: Numquid de bobus Deo est cura? an utique de nobis dicit? Quia debet in spe, qui arat, arare: & qui terit a- ream, terere eam in spe ut participetur. De hac val- le & in Osea mystice scriptum est: Loquar ad cor e- jus, haud dubium, quin Hierusalem: & dabo pos- sessores illius inde, & vallem Achor, ut aperiat in- telligentiam illius. Idcirco enim vallis Achor in pos- sessionem traditur armentorum populi Dei, & sal- tus vertuntur in caulas gregum, ut aperiatur intelli- gentia & Domini veritas cognoscatur. Similiter Cyrill. Hæc regio priscis temporibus execranda, requies erit armentorum, i. e. stabula ovium intelligibilium, manui Christi Principis omnium pastoris subjectarum, qui

Judaicum populum alloquutus est, dicens de genti- bus: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt de ovili hoc: quas etiam oportet me adducere. Eritq; unum ovi- le, unus pastor. Quæsierunt namq;, illum per fidem, qui aliquando erraverunt: quo invento facti sunt ejus do mestici, & concives sanctorum, & cohæredes promisso- rum ipsis bonorum. ET VOS QUI DERELIQUI- STIS DOMINUM &c. In locis, inquit Hierony- mus, quondam sylvestribus atq;, turbarum, in locis gentilium erunt caulæ ovium: id est, Ecclesiæ de toto orbe credentium. Vos autem ô popule Israël, qui dereliquistis Dominum, & ad iracundiam provo- castis sanctum Israël: qui obliti estis montem san- ctum ejus, de quo crebro diximus, vel dominum Salva- torem, qui montium mons est, & sanctorum omnium sanctus: vel montem Sion & civitatem Dei viventis Hierusalem cælestem: qui hæc & hæc facitis, tradam gladio: ut omnes interfecti pariter corruatis. Du- bium non est, inquit Brentius, è superioribus, quin hic fiat sermo de Ecclesia, quæ per Evangelion è Judæis & Gentibus colligenda erat. Hæc Ecclesia vocatur Electi & servi filii Dei, credentes videli- cet in Filium Dei, per Evangelion. Promittitur ergo huic Ecclesiæ, quòd habitatura sit in monte Sion, & quod possessura duo pascuosa loca, Saron, & vallem Achor, pro gregibus & armentis suis. Manifestum autem est quod fieri non possit, ut universa Eccle- sia habitet corporaliter in Hierusalem & in monte Zion. Et quam cælestem salutem ac felicitatem, ad quam solam nobis aspirandum est, afferet Ec- clesiæ, etiamsi oves & boves ejus habeant pascua valde pinguia? Num salus ejus constat salute ovium & boum? Quare hæc beneficia non sunt intelligen- da juxta rationem bonorum terreni regni, sed juxta rationem bonorum regni Christi, quod est spirituale & cælesfe: videlicet, quod revelato Evangelio, non carnales, sed spirituales Israëlitæ, collecti per Evangelion ex Judæis & Gentibus, ha- beantur pro vera Zione seu Ecclesia Filii Dei, & quod in hac Ecclesia pinguissima sint pascua: præ- dicatio videlicet Evangelii, quod est potentia Dei ad salutem. De quibus pascuis concionatur Fi- lius Dei etiam in Ezechiele: Congregabo, inquiens, oves meas de terris, & inducam eas in terram suam, & pascam eas in montibus Israël, in rivis & in cun- ctis sedibus terræ, in pascuis uberrimis pascam eos. Gemina est Osiandrina Paraphrasis: ET VOS QUI DERELIQUISTIS DOMINUM, qui ab ipsius verbo vos avertitis, neq; credentes neq; obedientes ipsi. QUI OBLITI ESTIS MON- TEM SANCTUM MEUM. Templum Do- mini in monte Sion, hoc est, qui negligitis veram Religionem: QUI PONITIS FORTUNÆ Hebr. ipsi Gad, MENSAM, ET LIBATIS SU- PER EAM, Hebr. & impletis ipsi Meni libamen: (id est, qui Gad in honorem collocatis men- sam ferculis aut oblationibus instructam, & fundi- tis large libamen Idolo Meni, hos ego severissime puniam. Videtur autem Gad fignificasse ipsis Martem: Gad enim ab expeditione bellica Ety- mologiam habet: Meni vero fortasse fuit Mer- curius, Deus Mercatorum: Meni enim à numeran- do denominatur. Et ad has fignificationes egre- gie alludit sequens comminatio divina: NUME- RABO VOS IN GLADIO, rectius ad gla- dium, ET OMNES IN CÆDE CORRUE- TIS. Id est, Quia adeo cupidi estis belli, & dedi- ti avaritiæ, ut pecuniam numerare sit inter primas vestras delitias: agite, ego numerabo vos ad lanie- nam & tradam vos occidendos militum Romano- rum gladiis. Etsi enim Judæi tempore Christi fortasse nec Martem nec Mercurium coluerunt:

tamen partim ex historia Josephi, partim ex histo- ria Evangelica manifestum est, quod tum temporis populus Judaicus fuerit cupidus seditionum & bel- lorum, quod etiam Pharisaei (qui caeteris non pau- lo plus meliores haberi volebant) plane dediti fue- rint avaritiae.
