Quin & mercatura in templo erat restituta, Joh. 2. Itaque Martem & Mercurium co- lore dicuntur, qui bellis & avaritiae studebant, per- inde ac si quis de homine dedito ebriati & lasciviae dicat, cum colore Bacchum & Venerem. Deus enim plerumque iis malis peccata punit, quibus homines maxime sese oblectarunt. Audiamus & B. Lutheri explicationem ὁμόψηφον. ERUNT CAMPESTRIA IN CAULAS verte sic: ERIT SARON IN CAULAM GREGIS. Porro Sa- ron & Carmelus sunt laudatissimi montes Judae propter pascua. Achor & Rephaim sunt valles laudatissimae. Promittit igitur Allegorice Ecclesiam fore talem, in qua praedicetur verbum quotidie, ut pascantur & multiplicentur fideles, &c. Armen- ta sunt pii, robustiores in fide, qui apti sunt ad docen- dum, Greges sunt infirmiores.

## 65:11
Vers. 11.

YOU WHO SET A TABLE FOR FORTUNE] Gad in the East, that is, to the Hebrews, Chaldeans, Arabs, signifies fortune, whether good or bad, but more often good. Thence was made the name for an idol, which the Idumeans especially, if we believe the Hebrews, worshipped. See, if you like, Beresith Rabba on Genesis 27, 31. and add what many interpreters have said on Gen. 30, 11. Jerome on this place: There is in all cities, and especially in Egypt, and in Alexandria, an old custom of idolatry, that on the last day of the year and of their month which is the last, they set a table filled with various kinds of food, and a cup mixed with honey-wine, hoping for the fertility of either the past or the future year. But the Israelites also did this, worshipping the portents of all idols.

AND OFFER LIBATIONS UPON IT] In the Hebrew: And you fill for Meni a libation. That is, to Meni, which God we learn from Strabo was worshipped in Armenia and Phrygia. Iamblichus also mentions him in the life of Pythagoras. But because that name comes very close to מנה, which is to count, therefore it follows here.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

QUI PONITIS FORTUNAE MENSAM] גד in Oriente, id est, Hebraeis, Chaldaeis, Arabibus, fortu- nam significat, sive bonam sive malam, sed saepius bonam. Inde factum est nomen idolo, quod Idumaei maxime, si He- braeis credimus, coluerunt. Vide, si libet, Beresith Rabba ad Genese 27, 31. & adde quae multi interpretes dixere ad Gen. 30, 11. Hieronymus ad hunc locum: Est autem in cunctis urbibus, & maxime in Aegypto, & in Alexandria idololatriae vetus consuetudo, ut ultimo die anni & mensis eorum qui extre- mus est, ponant mensam refertam varii generis epulis, & poculum mulso mistum, vel praeteriti anni vel futuri fertilitatem auspi- cantes. Hoc autem faciebant & Israelitae omnium simulachro- rum portenta venerantes.

ET LIBATIS SUPER EAM] In Hebraeo: Et im- pletis Meni libamen. Id est, διὰ Μηνὶ, quem Deum cultum in Armenia & Phrygia discimus ex Strabone. Meminit & ejus Jamblichus in vita Pythagorae. Quia autem id no- men proxime accedit ad מנה, quod est numerare, id- eo hic sequitur.

## 65:12
Vers. 12.

I WILL NUMBER YOU TO THE SWORD] That is, I will take care that you are killed by the sword of the Greeks, by famine, and by other evils, so that from the whole number no one is missing. It is a hyperbole.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

NUMERABO VOS IN GLADIO] Id est, gladio Graecorum, fame, malisque aliis vos interfici, curabo, ita ut de numero omni nemo desideretur. Est hyperbole.

## 65:14
Verse 14.

AND YOU SHALL BE CONFOUNDED] With things restored, you will be ashamed, you who have deserted the law. He says the same thing as Dan. 12, 2.

Let us compare Jerome's observations. YOU SET, he says, A TABLE FOR FORTUNE, AND YOU OFFER LIBATIONS UPON IT: or according to the LXX, you prepare for fortune, and you fill a cup for a demon, or κέρεσμα, which all have translated similarly: that is, a mixed drink. There is, however, in all cities, and especially in Egypt and in Alexandria, an ancient custom of idolatry, that on the last day of the year and of the month which is the last, they set a table filled with various kinds of food, and a cup mixed with honey-wine, hoping for the fertility of either the past year or the future. The Israelites also used to do this, venerating the portents of all idols: and they poured libations not to the altar, but to a table of this kind. And what the LXX translated τῷ δαιμονίῳ, that is, to a demon: in the Hebrew it has למני which Symmachus interpreted as 'without me,' so that the sense may be: You who prepare a table for fortune, and fill a drink without me, to show that it is not done for him, but for a demon. But he takes the sword by which they are killed as a punishment. For not all the people of Israel were delivered to the sword, of whom we see how many thousands are dispersed throughout the whole world, but to hunger and tortures, to captivity and ultimate servitude: according to that which is said elsewhere: All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword: and in the Song of Deuteronomy: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and the sword of mine shall eat the flesh of the wounded. It can hardly be credible that the arrows of the Lord are drunk with blood, and that His sword is sated with the flesh of the wounded. He speaks of these arrows, which were piercing Job at every single moment of the hours: The arrows of the Lord are in my body: the fury of which drinks up my spirit: for when I begin to speak, they stimulate me. Jerome is most correct in this. But Grotius wrongly drags these things to the sword and slaughter of the Greeks, and invents a hyperbole. The things which the Prophet adds confirm the sense no less: BECAUSE I CALLED AND YOU DID NOT ANSWER: I SPOKE AND YOU DID NOT HEAR: BUT YOU DID EVIL IN MY EYES AND CHOSE THINGS WHICH I DID NOT WANT. Because these things contain the cause of the reprobation of the Jews, as is manifest from those things which were said at the beginning of the chapter, and explained by the Apostle in Rom. 10: v. 30, 31, and indeed even from those things which follow further, they are rightly applied by the Blessed Jerome to the calling made by Christ himself (αὐτοπροσώπως), whom he had previously warned to speak these things. By the sword, he says, you are delivered: because not only did you abandon me, and forget me, and mix a cup of fortune, but when I was Emmanuel, that is, God with us, of whom John also writes; The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: I called you while present: Return to me, you returning children. And: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and you did not want to answer. I spoke in parables, and I did all things which I ought to have done and you did not hear me, nay, you even despised me. For I am he who also said above: I came and there was no man; I called and there was no one who would obey. Nor was this impiety sufficient for you, that you should despise me while present, and kill the heir sent to you, but you did evil in my sight, and chose things I did not want, and blasphemed the Son of God, and asked for yourselves Barabbas the thief, the author of homicide and sedition, and you still dare to say: Why have you made us err from your way? For if those who did not know me found me, and those who did not call upon me received me, what tortures are you worthy of, who did not want to receive me when I was sent to you and saying: I have not come except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, but instead fixed me to a cross? Brentius explains it in the same way: The Hebrew reads thus: You who adorn a table for Gad himself, and consecrate a libation for Meni himself. But what Gad and Meni signify in this place is a matter of varied opinion among interpreters. For some think Gad is Jupiter, others Fortune, others Mars. But others think Meni is the Planets, others Mercury, namely from counting: for מנה Manah signifies to count, from which they also think Mina descends. But whatever these two words signify: certainly those sacred rites are recited here, by whose names Impiety and Idolatry are signified, to which the Jews and Gentiles devoted such effort that, for their sake, they rejected and condemned Christ the Son of God. For what the Pharisee did by the works of his traditions, this the Gentile did by his sacrifice, which he offered to Jupiter or Mercury. And what the Gentile did by his sacrifice, the Pharisee did the same by the worship of his traditions. In both cases the impiety was the same, even if the species of the works was different. What then will happen to men so impious and of such deplorable blindness? I will count you, he says, to the sword. He said the impious offer libations to Meni, that is, to the God of numbers, or of merchants. He therefore takes up this word and says: Because you offer libations to Meni or the counter, therefore I will count you (manithi), that is, I will count you to the sword and you shall all fall by slaughter: for this reason, that when I called you with my Gospel, you did not answer, you did not obey, and when I spoke, when I announced my Gospel to you, you did not want to hear: but you proceeded to do evil before me impudently, and you undertook to do those things which I detested and abominated. FOR THIS REASON THUS SAYS THE LORD, BEHOLD MY SERVANTS SHALL EAT AND YOU SHALL BE HUNGRY. Not only (so the part of Jerome's paraphrase holds) shall you fall by the sword, you who abandoned the Lord and did evil in his sight and did not want to hear him when present, but you shall see a great difference between you and the multitude of the Gentiles. For those who have served me shall eat and drink, they shall rejoice and praise out of the exultation of their heart. But you, on the contrary, shall be hungry and thirsty, you shall be confounded, and you shall howl out of pain of heart and contrition of spirit. All of which the Chiliasts think must be fulfilled in a thousand years, believing that the kingdom of God is food and drink, and not understanding that which is written: Work not for the food which perishes, but for the bread of life and truth. And when those serving Christ and believing in him have rejoiced, and have praised God out of the exultation of their heart and joy, then they shall be confounded, seeing that others have succeeded into their place, and they shall cry out, out of pain of heart, fulfilling that which is written: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when the lambs of the Gentiles and the just have stood on the right, and the goats of the Jews and the impious on the left, with some receiving eternal rewards, others eternal punishments. But contrition of spirit out of pain of heart is to be understood in the conscience of sins, according to that which is written: Those erring in spirit shall know understanding. Grotius, to explain the confusion, brings in Dan. 12, verse 2. But he perverts this passage in a new way. For since it treats there of the eternal confusion of the damned, he himself understands it as a not unpraiseworthy shame for having deserted the law. Thus rendering this text of the Prophet: AND YOU SHALL BE CONFOUNDED: With things restored, you shall be ashamed of the deserted law. He says the same thing as Dan. 12, 2. In the annotations on Daniel, however, he has twisted this passage in yet another way. Concerning which we shall speak in the same place, section 9. We add the succinct but clear paraphrase of our Osiander: BEHOLD MY SERVANTS, (believing in Christ and living piously from that faith) SHALL EAT even to satiety, AND YOU SHALL BE HUNGRY. BEHOLD MY SERVANTS SHALL DRINK AND YOU SHALL BE THIRSTY. Those who fear the Lord shall be fed abundantly with the most wholesome food of the word of God, and they shall refresh their souls with the consolation of the Holy Spirit: but for you, despisers of God, there awaits a hunger and a spiritual thirst, not a hunger for bread, nor a thirst for water, but for hearing the word of God. And you shall wander from sea to sea, and from the North even to the East you shall go about, seeking the word of the Lord, and you shall not find it, Amos, chap. 8. BEHOLD MY SERVANTS SHALL REJOICE AND YOU in your wickednesses SHALL BE CONFOUNDED, and you shall be covered with ignominy (for the Jews are today in the highest reproach and contempt) MY SERVANTS SHALL PRAISE, or more correctly shall shout for joy, FOR EXULTATION, or gladness OF HEART, AND YOU SHALL CRY OUT FOR SORROW OF HEART AND FOR CONTRITION OF SPIRIT (or sadness and consternation of mind) YOU SHALL HOWL. For the Jews in their synagogues do not sing, but like dogs they howl horribly. But this also is signified, that Christians rejoice in the Lord from the peace of conscience: but the enemies of the Church and the impious rage from the hidden wound of conscience. The Apostles went away rejoicing from the sight of the Jewish Council, although they had been beaten with rods for the name of Jesus, Acts, chap. 5: but the Jews, with a desperate mind, raged against Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET VOS CONFUNDEMINI] Rebus instauratis pudebit, vos deserta legis. Idem dicit quod Dan. 12, 2.

Conferamus Hieronymi observationes. PONITIS inquit, FORTUNAE MENSAM, ET LIBATIS SUPER EAM: sive juxta LXX. paratis fortunae, & impletis Daemoni poculum, aut κέρεσμα, quod omnes similiter transtulerunt: id est, mixtam potionem. Est autem in cunctis urbibus, & maxime in Aegypto & in Alexandria idololatriae vetus consuetudo, ut ultimo die anni & mensis ejus qui extremus est, ponant mensam refertam varii ge- neris epulis, & poculum mulso mixtum, vel praeteriti anni vel futuri fertilitatem auspicantes. Hoc au- tem faciebant & Israelitae, omnium simulacrorum portenta venerantes: & nequaquam altari victimas, sed hujuscemodi mensae liba fundebant. Quodque LXX. transtulerunt τῷ δαιμονίῳ, id est, daemoni: In He- braico habet למני quod Symmachus interpretatus est, absque me, ut sit sensus: Qui paratis fortunae men- sam, & impletis absque me potionem, ut doceat non sibi fieri, sed daemoni. Gladium autem quo interfi- ciuntur, pro supplicio accipit. Neque enim omnis populus Israel gladio traditus est, quorum videmus quanta millia in toto orbe dispersa sint, sed panis atq; cruciatibus, captivitati & ultime servituti: juxta illud quod alibi dicitur: In gladio morientur omnes peccatores populi mei: & in Deuteronomii Cantico: Inebriabo sagittas meas in sanguine, & gladius meus comédet carnes vulneratorum. Haud cre- dibile esse potest, sagittas Domini inebriari sanguine, & gladium illius vulneratorum saturari carnibus. De his sagittis, quæ Job per singula horarum momenta pungebant, loquitur: Sagittæ Domini in corpore meo sunt: quarum furor ebibit spiritum meum: cum enim cœpero loqui, stimulant me. Hæc Hie- ronymus rectissime. Perperam autem ista ad Græ- corum gladium & cladem trahit, & hyperbolen fin- git Grot. Sensum non minus confirmant, quæ subji- cit Propheta: PRO EO QUOD VOCAVI ET NON RESPONDISTIS: LOQUUTUS SUM ET NON AUDISTIS: SED FECISTIS MA- LUM IN OCULIS MEIS ET QUÆ NOLUI ELEGISTIS. Quæ quia causam continent re- probationis Judæorum, ut ex iis quæ sub initium capitis dicta, & ab Apostolo explicata sunt Rom. 10: v. 30. 31. imo etiam ex iis, quæ sequuntur por- ro, manifestum est, recte à B. Hieronymo applican- tur ad vocationem αυτοπροσώπως à Christo fa- ctam, quem hæc eloqui antea monitum. Gladio, ait, estis traditi: quia non solum reliquistis me, & ob- liti estis mei & fortunæ poculum miscuistis, sed cum essem Emmanuel, id est nobiscum Deus, de quo & Jo- annes scribit; Verbum caro factum est, & habita- vit in nobis: præsens vos vocavi: Revertimini ad me filii revertentes. Et: Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis & respondere nolui- stis. Loquutus sum in parabolis, & omnia feci quæ facere debui & non audistis me, imo & con- tempsistis. Ego enim sum, qui & supra dixi: Ve- ni & non erat homo; vocavi & non erat, qui obedi- ret. Nec vobis hæc sufficiebat impietas, ut me præ- sentem contemneretis, & missum ad vos occideretis hæredem, sed fecistis malum in conspectu meo, & quæ nolebam elegistis & blasphemastis filium Dei, & pete- retis vobis Barrabam latronem, homicidii & seditio- nis autorem & adhuc audetis dicere: Quare nos er- rare fecisti à via tua? Si enim qui me nesciebant in- venerunt me, & qui me non invocabant, suscepe- runt me, quibus vos digni estis cruciatibus, qui missum ad vos atque dicentem: Non veni nisi ad oves per- ditas domus Israël, suscipere noluistis, sed insuper af- fixistis cruci? Brentius eadem ratione exponit: Hebræus ita legit: Qui adornatis mensam ipsi Gad, & consecratis libamen ipsi Meni. Quid vero si- gnificent hoc loco Gad & Meni, varia est interpretum sententia. Nam Gad existimant alii esse Jovem, alii Fortunam, alii Martem. Meni autem, sentiunt alii esse Planetas, alii Mercurium à numerando scilicet: מנה Manah enim significat numerare, unde & Mi- nam descendere putant. Quicquid autem hæc duo vocabula significent: certe recitantur hic ea sacra, quorum nominibus significantur Impietas & Idolola- tria, quibus Judæi & Gentes ita dederunt operam, ut præ ipsis Christum Filium Dei abjecerint & conde- mnarint. Nam quod Pharisæus fecit operibus sua- rum traditionum, hoc fecit Ethnicus suo sacrificio, quod obtulit Jovi aut Mercurio. Et quod Ethnicus sacri- ficio suo fecit, hoc idem fecit Pharisæus cultu suarum traditionum. Utrobiq; eadem erat impietas, etsi species operum erat diversa. Quid ergo fiet homini- bus tam impiis & tam deploratæ cæcitatis? Nume- rabo vos, inquit, ad gladium. Dixit impios liba- re Meni, hoc est, Deo numerorum, seu mercato- rum. Excipit igitur hoc vocabulum & dicit: Quia vos libatis Meni vel numeratori, idcirco manithi, hoc est, numerabo vos ad gladium & corruetis omnes cæde: propterea, quod cum vocarem vos Evan- gelio meo, non respondistis, non obedivistis, & cum loquerer, cum adnunciarem vobis Evangelium meum, non voluistis audire: sed perrexistis facere malum coram me impudenter, & suscepistis ea fa- cienda, quæ ego detestabar & abominabar. PRO- PTER HOC HÆC DICIT DOMINUS, EC- CE SERVI MEI COMEDENT ET VOS E- SURIETIS. Non solum (ita habet pars para- phrasis Hieronymi) gladio corruetis, vos qui de- reliquistis Dominum & fecistis malum in conspectu ejus & præsentem noluistis audire, sed multam inter vos & gentium multitudinem cernetis differen- tiam. Illi enim, qui servierunt mihi, comedent & bibent, lætabuntur & laudabunt præ exultatione cordis. Vos autem è contrario esurietis atq; sitietis, confundemini & præ dolore cordis & contritione spi- ritus ululabitis. Quæ omnia χιλιαϛαὶ in mille an- nis putant esse complenda, cibum & potum, regnum Dei esse credentes, nec intelligentes illud, quod scri- ptum est: Operamini non cibum qui perit, sed panem vitæ & veritatis. Cumq́; servientes Christo, & cre- dentes ei lætati fuerint, & laudaverint Deum præ ex- ultatione cordis & gaudio, tunc illi confundentur, vi- dentes in suum locum alios successisse, & clamabunt, præ dolore cordis, implentes illud quod scriptum est: Ibi erit fletus & stridor dentium, quum steterint agni gentium atq; justorum ad dexteram, & hædi Judæo- rum atque impiorum à sinistris, aliis recipientibus æ- terna præmia, aliis æterna supplicia. Contritio autem spiritus præ dolore cordis, intelligenda in conscientia peccatorum, juxta illud, quod scriptum est: Cognoscent errantes spiritu intelligentiam. Grotius ad explicandam confusionem adducit Dan. 12. vers. 2. Sed hunc locum nova ratione pervertit. Quum enim eo agatur de æterna confusione da- mnatorum, ipse de pudore ob desertam legem non illaudabili intelligit. Sic reddens textum hunc Pro- phetæ: ET VOS CONFUNDEMINI: Rebus instauratis pudebit vos desertæ legis. Idem dicit quod Dan. 12, 2. In annotatis tamen ad Danielem alio adhuc modo locum istum detorsit. De quo ibi- dem ξ. θ. dicturi sumus. Addimus istorum succin- ctam, sed perspicuam paraphrasin Osiandri nostri: ECCE SERVI MEI, (credentes in Christum & ex ea fide pie viventes) COMEDENT ad saturi- tatem usque, ET VOS ESURIETIS. ECCE SERVI MEI BIBENT ET VOS SITIETIS. (Timentes Dominum pascentur copiose pabulo saluberrimo verbi Dei & consolatione spiritus san- cti recreabunt animas suas: Vos autem contem- ptores Dei manet fames & sitis spiritualis, non fa- mes panis, nec sitis aquæ, sed audiendi verbum Dei. Et vagabimini à mari usque ad mare, & ab Aquilo- ne usque ad Orientem circuibitis, quærentes ver- bum Domini, & non invenietis, Amos. cap. 8.) EC- CE SERVI MEI LÆTABUNTUR ET VOS in sceleribus vestris CONFUNDEMINI, & igno- minia operiemini (sunt enim hodie Judæi in sum- mo opprobrio & contemtu) SERVI MEI LAU- DABUNT, rectius jubilabunt, PRÆ EXULTA- TIONE, seu lætitia CORDIS, ET VOS CLAMABITIS PRÆ DOLORE CORDIS ET PRÆ CONTRITIONE SPIRITUS (seu mœdestia & consternatione animi) ULULABI- TIS. Judæi enim in suis Synagogis non canunt, sed canum more horribiliter ululant. Sed & hoc significatur, Christianos ex pace conscientiæ læ- tari in Domino: hostes vero Ecclesiæ & impios fremere ex conscientiæ occulto vulnere. Ibant Apostoli gaudentes à conspectu Concilii Judaici, cum tamen virgis propter nomen Jesu essent cæsi Actor. V. cap: Judæi vero animo desperabundo fremebant adversus Christum.

## 65:15
V. 15. YOU SHALL LEAVE, YOUR NAME FOR AN OATH TO MY CHOSEN] The pious shall say when they swear: if I am mistaken, may that happen to me which happened to those ἐπιούσιοι under Antiochus.

AND HE SHALL CALL HIS SERVANTS BY ANOTHER NAME] חסידים Asidaeans, 1 Macc. 2.42. from which name the name of the Essenes was made, with the letter ן removed.

An overly arbitrary gloss, or rather one entirely alien to the formula of an oath and to the name חסידים. But Brentius conveniently expressed the sense of the Prophet: The name of the wicked shall be execrable to the pious: because the Lord God shall afflict them with a shameful death. But the pious shall be called by another name. Although indeed the Church of Christ now has another and new name. For we are no longer called either Jews or Gentiles, but Christians: and among Christians the names of Jews and Gentiles are held to be so execrable that if anyone wishes to signify the destruction of some thing, he is accustomed to say: This thing is as lost as the soul of a Jew is lost: nevertheless I think that here, according to the Hebrew custom, the things themselves are signified by the names rather than the words, so that the sense may be: the state of affairs will be far different with my Church than it has hitherto been with the Jews and Gentiles. For the Jews seemed to be a people chosen by God and holy, the Gentiles were held to be the most powerful and wisest of men. But now, after the Gospel is revealed and published, and the Church is gathered from Jews and Gentiles: The wicked Jews shall be cast off and execrable, with all their affairs. And the wicked Gentiles, who are not converted to Christ, shall be judged the most foolish of all by far. But the true Church shall possess in Christ her Lord holiness, power, and wisdom. We preach, says Paul, Christ crucified, to the Jews indeed a stumbling block, to the Greeks foolishness: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, the power of God, and the wisdom of God. And again: Jesus Christ is made unto us wisdom from God, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption. These are those other names which are now attributed to the Church, and by which new and heavenly things are explained. Osiander paraphrases these things thus: AND YOU SHALL LEAVE YOUR NAME FOR AN OATH TO MY CHOSEN, that is; you shall be execrable to Christians, so that concerning a condemned and lost thing they shall say that it has perished as certainly as the soul of a Jew: It is lost like a Jew's soul. AND THE LORD GOD SHALL SLAY THEE: by various misfortunes, and on a slight occasion you shall be slaughtered. (Histories testify to this, as often as all the Jews in some one city of the Christians were killed in a single day, and their houses plundered and torn down) AND HE SHALL CALL HIS SERVANTS the Lord no longer Israelites or Jews, but BY ANOTHER NAME, namely that they may be called Christians (denominated from Christ the Savior), which happened first at Antioch, Acts 11. Jerome assigned a different sense on account of the diversity of accents, i.e., vowels, because the LXX Interpreters rendered the Hebrew word otherwise, because they did not correctly attend to the genuine points, just as we have observed elsewhere. For πλησμονῆς, he says, that is, satiety (as the LXX have) which in Hebrew is called שבועה: the others interpreted it as an oath, because the word has many meanings, and is varied according to the diversity of accents. For it is understood as both an oath and satiety and fullness, and more, and seven. Concerning which we spoke in the book of Genesis, and in this volume, where seven women took hold of one man. Again, for that which the LXX translated: τ᾿ ἀληθινὸν, that is true, and in Hebrew is called אמן. Aquila translates πιστωμένως, that is, faithfully. But what he says is this: others succeeding to your place, your name shall be for an oath to my chosen, so that they may have you as an example of evils, and detest suffering such things, and swear thus: I will not suffer these things, which the people of the Jews have suffered. Or your name shall be for satiety: which is wont to be seen in those whose recollection and memory is odious, and who have come even to satiety and nausea. Or certainly this must be said, that they leave their name to the chosen of the Lord, so that for them a crowd of nations may succeed, and they themselves be called the children of Abraham and Israel. Of whom Paul speaks: Peace be upon them and upon the Israel of God. For neither are they who are of Israel, Israel, nor are all who are the seed of Abraham children, to whom it is said: If you were Abraham's children, you would do the works of Abraham.

Latin:

V. 15. DIMITTETIS, NOMEN VESTRUM IN JU- RAMENTUM ELECTIS MEIS] Dicent pii cum jurare volent: si fallo, eveniat mihi quod illis ἐπιούσιοι sub An- tiocho.

ET SERVOS SUOS VOCABIT NOMINE A- LIO] חסידים Ασιδαίους, 1. Macc. 2,42. ex quo nomi ne factum nomen Essenorum, extrita ן littera.

Nimis arbitraria Glossa, imo prorsus aliena de juramenti formula, & de nomine חסידים. Sen- sum autem Prophetæ commode expressit Brentius Nomen impiorum erit piis execrabile: propterea quod Dominus Deus afficiat eos probrosa morte Pii autem vocabuntur alio nomine. Etsi vero Ec- clesia Christi habet nunc aliud & novum nomen Non enim vocamur amplius vel Judæi, vel Ethni- ci, sed Christiani: & inter Christianos nomina Ju- dæorum & Ethnicorum tam execrabilia haben- tur, ut si quis velit significare alicujus rei interne- cionem, dicere soleat: Hæc res tam perdita est, quam perdita est anima Judæi: tamen existimo, hic more Hebræo, per nomina magis res ipsas, quam vocabula significari, ut sit sensus: longe ali- ter res sese cum Ecclesia mea habebit, quam hacte- nus cum Judæis & Ethnicis habuit. Nam Judæi visi fuerunt populus à Deo electus & sanctus, Eth- nici habiti sunt pro viris potentissimis & sapientis- simis. Nunc autem postquam revelabitur & divul- gabitur Evangelion, & congregabitur Ecclesia ex Judæis & Ethnicis: Impii Judæi erunt abjecti, & execrabiles, cum omnibus rebus suis. Et impii Ethnici, qui non convertuntur ad Christum, judi- cabuntur longe omnium stultissimi. Vera autem Ecclesia possidebit in Christo Domino suo sanctita- tem, potentiam, & sapientiam. Prædicamus, in- quit Paulus, Christum crucifixum, Judæis quidem offendiculum, Græcis stultitiam: sed iisdem vocatis, Judæis pariter & Græcis, Dei potentiam, & Dei sa- pientiam. Et iterum: Jesus Christus factus est nobis sapientia à Deo, justitia, sanctificatio, & redemptio. Hæc sunt ista alia nomina, quæ nunc Ecclesiæ tri- buuntur, & quibus res novæ ac cælestes explican- tur. Osiander hæc ita παραφράζει: ET DIMIT- TETIS NOMEN VESTRUM IN JURA- MENTUM ELECTIS MEIS, id est; eritis exe- crabiles Christianis, ut de re damnata & perdita di- cturi sint, eam tam certo periisse, quam animam Ju- dæi: Es ist verlohren wie eines Juden Seel. ET INTERFICIET TE DOMINUS DEUS: va- riis casibus, & levi occasione trucidaberis. (Te- stantur hoc historiæ, quoties uno die omnes Judæi in uno aliquo Christianorum oppido fuerint inter- fecti, & domus eorum spoliata & diruta) ET SER- VOS SUOS VOCABIT Dominus non amplius Israëlitas aut Judæos, sed NOMINE ALIO, ni- mirum ut Christiani (à Christo Servatore denomi- nati) appellentur, quod factum est primo Antio- chiæ, Actor. 11. Hieronymus pro accentuum, h. e. vocalium diversitate sensum diversum assignavit, quia LXX. Interpp. aliter reddiderunt vocem E- bræam, quod puncta genuina non recte attende- rint, quemadmodum id etiam alias observavimus. Pro πλησμονῆς, inquit, hoc est, saturitate (ut habent LXX.) quæ Hebraice dicitur שבועה: cæteri juramen- tum interpretati sunt, quod verbum multas habet in- telligentias, & pro diversitate accentuum variatur. Intelligitur enim & juramentum & saturitas & satie- tas, & plures, & septem. De quo in libro Geneseos diximus, & in hoc volumine, ubi septem mulieres apprehenderunt unum virum. Rursum pro eo, quod LXX. transtulerunt: τ᾿ ἀληθινὸν, id est verum, & in Hebraico dicitur אמן. Aquila vertit πιστωμένως, id est, fideliter. Quod autem dicit, hoc est: aliis in vestrum succedentibus locum, nomen vestrum erit in juramentum electis meis, ut pro malorum exem- plo vos habeant, & detestentur talia sustinere, & ju- rent sic: non hæc patiar, quæ passus est populus Judæorum. Sive nomen vestrum erit in satietatem: quod in his videri solet, quorum odiosa est recor- datio & memoria, & qui usque ad saturitatem nau- seamque venerunt. Vel certe hoc dicendum, quod nomen suum derelinquant electis Domini, ut pro illis gentium turba succedat, ipsi appellen- tur filii Abraham & Israël. De quibus Paulus lo- quitur: Pax super eos & super Israël Dei. Neque enim, qui ex Israëlitus sunt Israël, nec qui semen A- braham omnes filii, ad quos dicitur: Si filii essetis Abraham, opera Abraham faceretis.

## 65:16
Verse 16.

FROM WHICH, HE WHO IS BLESSED UPON THE EARTH SHALL BE BLESSED IN GOD AMEN] You may translate it conveniently: He who shall pray for good for himself on the earth, (Judea) he shall pray for good for himself from the true God. For אמן among other things also signifies true, as the LXX take it here. The Chaldean said the living God in the same sense. Both names are opposed to idols.

BECAUSE THE FORMER DISTRESSES HAVE BEEN DELIVERED TO OBLIVION, AND BECAUSE THEY HAVE BEEN HIDDEN FROM MY EYES] Namely, the causes of them. Neither shall I remember those calamities, nor the sins, and thus I shall show by the thing itself that I am their God.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

EX QUO, QUI BENEDICTUS EST SUPER TERRAM BENEDICETUR IN DEO AMEN] Vertas commode: Qui sibi bene precabitur in terra, (Judæa) is sibi bene precabitur à Deo vero. Nam אמן inter alia & verum significat, ut hic accipiunt LXX. Deum vibum, eodem sensu dixit Chaldæus. Utrumq; nomen opponitur idolis.

QUIA OBLIVIONI TRADITÆ SUNT AN- GUSTIÆ PRIORES, ET QUIA ABSCONDITÆ SUNT AB OCULIS MEIS] Nempe causæ earum. Ne- que illi calamitatura, neque ego peccatorum meminero, & ita ostendam reipsa, me esse ipsorum Deum.

## 65:17
Verse 17.

FOR BEHOLD I CREATE NEW HEAVENS, AND A NEW EARTH] A new heaven, that is, not cloudy as before, but serene: and a new earth, that is, not desert and sterile, but inhabited and fruitful. Just as those things are said to grow old which lose their strength, so those are said to be renewed which become vigorous.

AND THE FORMER THINGS SHALL NOT BE IN REMEMBRANCE] All those evils under Antiochus.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ECCE ENIM EGO CREO COELOS NOVOS, ET TERRAM NOVAM] Cœlum novum, id est, non ut ante nubilum, sed serenum: & terram novam, id est, non desertam & sterilem, sed habitatam & fœcundam. Si- cut vetustiscere dicuntur, quæ vim suam amittunt, sic in- novari, quæ vegeta fiunt.

ET NON ERUNT IN MEMORIA PRIORA] Omnia illa mala sub Antiocho.

## 65:18
Vers. 18. FOR EVER] For a very long time.

IN THESE THINGS WHICH I CREATE] The Hebrews use the word for creating regarding every magnificent work of God.

He rightly corrects the Vulgate here with Brentius and Osiander in this manner. So that he who shall bless himself in the earth, shall bless himself in the true God (that is, Christians shall bless themselves in the name of Jesus Christ, the true God, their Savior and Redeemer, and shall confirm some great matter, having called upon the name of Jesus Christ as a witness, such as are the sayings of the pious: May Christ save you, likewise rise in the name of the Father and of the SON and of the Holy Spirit. Likewise, swearing they say: so may Christ love me well, &c. For that Jesus Christ, whom the blinded Jews abhor, is the true God) in sum, it shall be well for Christians. BECAUSE THE FORMER DISTRESSES ARE DELIVERED TO OBLIVION, AND BECAUSE (says the Prophet) THE FORMER MISERIES ARE HIDDEN FROM OUR EYES (For although Christians are also afflicted in this life: yet because they are justified they are no longer under the wrath of God, but enjoy the peace of conscience: therefore the calamities of this age are only a certain shadow of calamities. Because the pious know that they have a merciful God, and they expect heavenly and eternal joys after this life. For the Prophets are accustomed often to connect the state of the Kingdom of Christ in this world with the Kingdom of Christ, such as it will be in the other age, because the Kingdom of Christ begun here will be truly perfect in the other life. And so the Lord speaks now of the renewal of the World, which is begun spiritually through the Ministry of the Gospel, but will be completed in the other life, where all things will be most absolute and most perfect.) FOR BEHOLD I CREATE NEW HEAVENS, AND A NEW EARTH, that is, I will renew the world, and I will take away all things which were perishable and full of miseries. AND THE FORMER THINGS SHALL NOT BE IN REMEMBRANCE ANY MORE, AND THEY SHALL NOT COME UPON THE HEART, that is: the pious shall no longer remember with groaning their labors and miseries (Peter cites this saying in 2 Pet. 3 and John in the Apocalypse chap. 21 concerning the renewal of the world, which will take place on the last day. Of what kind but whether the world will exist afterwards, Holy Scripture does not express, nor is it necessary for us to know in this life: but this is most certain: that all afflictions and miseries will be taken away;) BUT YOU SHALL REJOICE AND EXULT FOREVER, without any end, IN THESE THINGS WHICH I CREATE: because I am preparing for you such joys as have never been seen, nor heard, nor thought of by any man, 1 Cor. 2. FOR BEHOLD I CREATE or make JERUSALEM, AN EXULTATION, AND HER PEOPLE, A JOY, i.e., I will cause that in my Church and my people, all things may be full of gladness, exultation, and joy. AND I myself WILL EXULT IN JERUSALEM AND WILL REJOICE IN MY PEOPLE: my Church and my people will be a pleasure to me myself, so that I shall be rejoicing over them, just as a good Prince rejoices over his subjects, who revere and love him, and honor him with such services as they can. AND THERE SHALL NOT BE HEARD IN THAT people ANY MORE THE VOICE OF WEEPING AND THE VOICE OF CRYING, or wailing, but all things will resound with most joyful jubilations. The Lord Amen and God Amen is the true Lord and true God, just as Thomas, having been converted, professed Christ: My Lord and my God, John 20:28. And concerning Christ, John professed 1 John 5:20: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἀληθινὸς θεός. This is that true God, 1 Epist. 5, v. 20. For in Christ all the nations of the earth were to be blessed, Gen. 12:3, Ps. 72:17. Grotius, who here again tastes only of carnal things, drags these to the land of Judea and to the times of Antiochus. But the Prophet understands the Church, and treats of the times of the New Testament; indeed, he passes from the Kingdom of grace to the Kingdom of glory, as the Osiandrine Paraphrase rightly taught, following the interpretation of the Holy Spirit in 2 Pet. 3 and Apoc. 22, with the entire choir of interpreters concurring; for to have brought forward one is to have brought forward all. Grotius's gloss has not come into anyone's mind. The cause of joy, says Jerome, and of the confession of the true God, is that the eternal oblivion of former distresses will follow, so that they may in no way remember idols and their former error, but may pass from darkness to light, so that they may enjoy eternal beatitude. For they will forget former evils, not by an oblivion of memory, but by the succession of good things, according to that which is written: In a good day, there is a forgetting of evils: And elsewhere: The affliction of an hour makes one forget delights, in that those who are established in distresses do not at all enjoy former pleasures according to the error of Epicurus. Although it may also be said that in the new heaven and the new earth the memory of all former conversation is blotted out, lest this very thing be a part of the evils, to remember the former distress. Cyril, although he explains these things concerning the Church of Christ, nevertheless warns that some Interpreters refer them to the future life, and leaves it free for the wise to choose which interpretation they wish. Blessed Luther agrees with Cyril, who has certain αξιομνημόνευτα (things worthy of memory) here. Which, therefore, it is helpful to add, since they illustrate the happiness of the Kingdom of grace. This is a notable passage, which is valid for understanding other similar ones, where the Prophets speak of the Kingdom of Christ as if of the future eternal life. But the matter stands thus: the Kingdom of faith and the future life differ not in the thing itself, but only in the mode of the thing. For we are Children of God, as John says, but by hope. For it has not yet appeared. For he who has believed, he already has the remission of sins, he has life, and that eternal. We are therefore truly in the Kingdom of life, we already reign, we already sit in the heavens, we are already made safe, but by hope. For eternal life and beatitude began even then, when Christ transferred the kingdom of the Jews, when he was already being raised from the dead. Whoever, therefore, believes in Christ, he already has and possesses it. But, you will say, how does it happen that we are said to have such great goods, when nevertheless we not only do not feel them, but rather feel the opposite? I answer: While we live in this body subject to all evils, we are kept as if in a hidden enigma. For this skin, with which we are clothed, this flesh, with which we are burdened, does not properly belong to the kingdom of Christ, because it is still subject to sin and death: It is, however, to be cultivated until it is put off, and while we live, it is to be pressed and burdened. Therefore, by the fault of this skin and our flesh, it happens that we are sometimes troubled by the sense of a fearful conscience, of sin, of death, of the Devil, of hell, and of the world. Nor does this sense belong to the kingdom of Christ, but to that skin, which is like a sack, in which such a great treasure is enclosed. But it would be absurd to estimate the value of the treasure from the vileness of the sack in which it is placed. But Christ's kingdom, eternal life, and salvation are stored up outside of eyes and sense in Christ alone; in him truly is salvation, peace, life, even if we do not yet feel those goods because of this sack with which we are clothed. For thus the Prophet says here, that Christ's kingdom is a kingdom of blessing; therefore it is also a kingdom of justice, salvation, and life, against sin, death, and the law. It is therefore Emphatic, what he says, The former distresses are hidden from my eyes. Before the eyes of God the matter truly stands thus, but before our eyes and the eyes of the world it does not yet stand thus, but those distresses still endure, and they endure until we put off this flesh. We wait, however, in hope, and through faith we already have liberation. For those new heavens are already founded, but in promise; to us, however, they are not yet founded, because of the veil itself. In this manner the remaining passages of other Prophets are also to be treated, where they speak no less magnificently of the bodily life of the faithful than of the future life. This is Dr. Luther. Furthermore, Franciscus Junius laughs at those who here ask what will become of this heaven and this earth, and make literal things out of figurative propositions: in parallel. p. 584. Calixtus, de supr. jud. p. 147, thinks those hallucinate who have transferred these to the last day: because the prophetic grandiloquence and magnificent allegory speak words about the amplitude and glory of the Church. In which, as in many other things, Hackspan concurs. But we do not see a solid reason why we should depart from the explanation of most of our own, and with the Jesuit Sanctius, or the Calvinist Junius, take these μεταφορικως (metaphorically), especially because το ρητον (the literal sense) is to be retained, unless necessity compels, and the text convinces, that it must be abandoned. And from ch. 66, 22. It is clear that these things concern the glorious heaven of the other life; this is manifest primarily from 2 Pet. 3:13 and Rev. 21:1. Indeed, it is also gathered from this context in v. 18, 'you shall rejoice and exult FOREVER in those things which I create.' For the discourse is not about the serenity or fruitfulness of times after the liberation from Antiochus, as Grotius says, or after the return from the Babylonian captivity, as others wish, nor about the greatness and glory of the New Testament Church, which was the view of Calixtus and Hackspan, but about happiness in eternal life: for the emphasis of the words, from which one should not rashly depart, and the creation of a new earth and a new heaven, and the forgetting of the old, and eternal joy imply this, as does the explanation in ch. 66:22, 2 Pet. 3:13, Rev. 21:1. Nor do the antecedents and consequents suggest otherwise: for what prevents the Holy Scriptures, when those benefits are promised to the faithful by the enjoyment of which they may be able to forget former evils, v. 16, from proceeding to the promise of heavenly happiness itself, that they are not only to be gladdened by those benefits, but are to be endowed with eternal joy in the new heaven and new earth: even if then, for the sake of certainty, those promises which are to be exhibited to them in the Church militant are further interwoven. For the promises made to piety

in this life and the future; and they are best joined for the greater consolation of the faithful, which is otherwise also customary in the Holy Scriptures. However much, therefore, we may concede that the passage concerns the joy that will arise for the faithful in the Church later on, nothing prevents it from being a discourse about heavenly joy here, because spiritual joy coheres with the heavenly joy of the elect and is a certain foretaste of it, Rom. 14, 17. Heb. 6, 5. Cf. Jerome here and ch. 66, 22. Thus, it is not necessary to depart from the letter of the text, and the continuity and reason of the preceding and following parts remain intact and unimpaired, so that we have no need to concede that these are merely heavenly things, or to admit perpetual figurative expressions in their description. The Jews themselves acknowledge that these things concerning the new heaven pertain to the other life: but that they should also drag everything else to themselves, and hand down wonderful things about them here, belongs to their dreams.

Latin:

Vers. 18. USQUE IN SEMPITERNUM] Diutissime.

IN HIS, QUÆ EGO CREO] Creandi verbum Hebræi de omni magnifico Dei opere usurpant.

Recte hic emendat Vulgatam cum Brentio O- siander h. m. Ita, ut qui benedicet sese in terra, is be- nedicet se in Deo vero (id est, Christiani benedicent se in nomine Jesu Christi, veri Dei Salvatoris & Re- demptoris sui, & rem aliquam magnam confirma- bunt, in testimonium vocato nomine Jesu Christi, quales sunt piorum sermones: Servet te Christus, item surge in nomine Patris & FILII & Spiritus S. Item jurantes dicunt: ita me Christus bene amet, &c. Verus enim Deus est ille Jesus Christus, quem Judæi excæcati abominantur) in summa bene erit Christianis. QUIA OBLIVIONI TRADITÆ SUNT ANGUSTIÆ PRIORES, ET QUIA ABSCONDITÆ SUNT (inquit Propheta) AB OCULIS NOSTRIS priores miseriæ (Etsi enim Christiani etiam in hac vita affliguntur: tamen quia justificati non amplius sunt sub ira Dei, sed fruun- tur pace conscientiæ: ideo calamitates hujus seculi tantum umbra quædam sunt calamitatum. Quia norunt pii se habere Deum clementem, & expe- ctant post hanc vitam cœlestia & æterna gaudia. Solent enim Prophetæ sæpe statum Regni Christi in hoc mundo connectere cum Regno Christi, quale futurum est in altero seculo, quia Regnum Christi hic inchoatum, in altera vita erit vere per- fectum. Itaq; Dominus loquitur jam de renovatio- ne Mundi, quæ inchoata est spiritualiter per Mini- sterium Evangelii, completa autem erit in altera vita, ubi omnia erunt absolutissima & perfectissi- ma.) ECCE ENIM EGO CREO COELOS NOVOS, ET TERRAM NOVAM, id est, ego renovabo mundum, & omnia, quæ caduca & plena ærumnis erant, auferam. ET NON amplius E- RUNT IN MEMORIA PRIORA, ET NON ASCENDENT SUPER COR, id est: pii non amplius reminiscentur cum gemitu laborum & mi- seriarum suarum (hoc dictum Petrus 2. Petr. 3. & Johannes in Apocalypsi cap. 21. citant de renova- tione mundi, quæ fiet in novissimo die. Qualis autem postea mundus futurus sit, Sacra Scriptura non exprimit, neque nobis in hac vita scitu est ne- cessarium: hoc autem certissimum est: omnes af- flictiones & miserias fore ablatas;) SED GAU- DEBIS ET EXULTABIS USQUE IN SEM- PITERNUM, absque ullo fine, IN HIS QUÆ EGO CREO: quia talia vobis paro gaudia, qualia nunquam nec visa sunt, nec audita, neque ab ullo homine cogitata, 1. Corinth. 2. QUIA EC- CE EGO CREO seu facio JERUSALEM, EX- ULTATIONEM, ET POPULUM EJUS, GAUDIUM, i. e. efficiam, ut in Ecclesia & popu- lo meo, omnia plena sint lætitia, exultatione & gau- dio. ET ego ipse EXULTABO IN JERUSA- LEM ET GAUDEBO IN POPULO MEO: mihi ipsi voluptati erit Ecclesia mea & populus meus, ita ut sim super ipso gavisurus, sicut Princeps bo- nus gaudet super subditis suis, qui eum reveren- tur amant, & officiis quibus possunt, colunt. ET NON AUDIETUR IN EO populo ULTRA VOX FLETUS ET VOX CLAMORIS, seu ejulatus, sed omnia perstrepent lætissimis jubilationibus. Dominus Amen & Deus Amen est verus Dominus & verus Deus, quemadmodum Christum professus est Thomas conversus: Dominus meus & Deus meus, Joh. 20, 28. & de Christo professus Johannes 1 G- jst' o' a'lηd wo's deo's. Hic est verus ille Deus, 1. Epist. 5. v. 20. Nam in Christo benedicendæ erant omnes gen- tes terræ Gen. 12, 3. Ps. 72, 17. Grotius, qui hic iterum mere carnalia sapit, abripit hæc ad terram Judæam, & ad tempora Antiochi. Sed Propheta intelligit Ec- clesiam, & de temporibus Novi Testamenti agit, imo à Regno gratiæ transit ad Regnum gloriæ, ut ex interpretatione Spiritus Sancti 2. Pet. 3. & Apoc. 22. recte docuit Osiandrina Paraphrasis, suffragan- te universo Interpp. Choro; unum enim adduxisse est adduxisse omnes. Grotii glossa nemini in men- tem venit. Causa lætitiæ, inquit Hieronymus, & confessionis Dei veri est, quia æterna angustiarum priorum succedet oblivio, ut nequaquam idolorum meminerint, & erroris pristini, sed ad lucem de tene- bris transeant, ut æterna beatitudine perfruantur. Obliviscentur enim pristina mala non oblivione me- moriæ, sed bonorum successione, juxta illud quod scri- ptum est: In die bona, oblivio malorum: Et alibi: Afflictio horæ, oblivionem facit delitiarum, eo quod in angustiis constituti, nequaquam voluptatibus pristinis juxta errorem Epicuri animo perfruantur. Licet possit & hoc dici, quod in cælo novo & in terra nova omnis conversationis pristinæ memoria delea- tur, ne hoc ipsum pars malorum sit, prioris angustiæ recordari. Cyrillus etsi de Ecclesia Christi hæc explicet, monet tamen quosdam Interpretes ea re- ferre ad futuram vitam, liberumque relinquit cor- datis, quam velint interpretationem eligere. Cum Cyrillo facit B. Lutherus, qui αξιομνημόνευτα quæ- dam hic habet. Quæ proinde juvat adjicere, cum illustrent felicitatem Regni gratiæ. Est insignis hic locus, qui valet ad alios similes intelligendos, ubi Pro- phetæ de Regno Christi loquuntur, tanquam de futura æterna vita. Sic autem se res habet, Regnum fidei & futura vita differunt non ad rem, sed tantum ad modum rei. Sumus enim Filii Dei, sicut Johannes dicit, sed spe. Nondum enim apparuit. Nam qui cre- diderit, is jam habet remissionem peccatorum, habet vitam, eamq; æternam. Sumus igitur vere in Re- gno vitæ, jam regnamus jam sedemus in cælis, sumus jam salvi facti, sed spe. Vita enim æterna & beati- tudo jam tum cæpit, cum Christus transferret regnum Judæorum, cum jam ex morte resuscitaretur. Qui- cunq; ergo in Christum credit, is jam eam habet & possidet. Verum, inquies, qui fit, quod habere tanta bo- na dicamur, cum tamen non modo non sentiamus ea, sed diversum potius sentiamus? Respondeo: Dum in hoc corpore obnoxii omnibus malis vivimus, servamur ceu in abscondito ænigmate. Hæc enim cutis, qua sumus vestiti, hæc caro, qua sumus onerati, pro- prie non pertinet ad regnum Christi, quia est adhuc obnoxia peccato & mori: Est tamen excolenda, do- nec exuatur, & dum vivimus, premenda & oneran- da est. Hujus igitur cutis & carnis nostræ vitio ac- cidit, quod turbamur nonnunquam sensu pavidæ conscientiæ, peccati, mortis, Diaboli, inferni & mun- di. Neque pertinet hic sensus ad regnum Christi, sed ad cutem illam, quæ ceu saccus est, in quem tantus thesaurus est conclusus. Absurdum autem fuerit pretium thesauri, ex sacci vilitate, in quo situs est, æsti- mare. Sed Christi regnum, æterna vita & salus, reposita sunt extra oculos & sensum in solo Christo,in illo vere est salus, pax, vita, etiamsi nondum sentiamus illa bona propter hunc saccum, quo sumus induti. Sic enim Propheta hic dicit, quod Christi regnum bene- dictionis sit regnum; ergo est quoque regnum justitiæ, salutis & vitæ, contra peccatum, mortem & legem. Est igitur Emphaticum,quod dicit, Ab oculis meis absconditæ sunt priores angustiæ. Coram oculis Dei res se vere sic habet, sed coram nostris & mun- di oculis nondum sic se res habet, sed durant adhuc angustiæ illæ, & durant donec exuamus hanc car- nem. Expectamus tamen in spe, & per fidem jam habemus liberationem. Jam enim illi novi cæli sunt conditi, sed in promissione, nobis autem nondum sunt conditi, propter ipsum velamen. Ad hunc modum reliqui loci aliorum quoque Prophetarum sunt tra- ctandi, ubi non minus magnifice de fidelium corporali vita loquuntur, quam de futura vita. Hæc D. Lu- therus. Cæterum Franciscus Junius ridet eos qui hic quærunt, quid hoc cælo & hac terra fu- turum sit, & e figuratis propositionibus proprias fa- ciunt: in parallel. p. 584. Calixtus de supr. jud. p. 147. hallucinari censet eos, qui hæc ad extremum diem transtulerunt: quia grandiloquentia Propheti- ca, & allegoria magnifica verba fiant de amplitudine, & gloria Ecclesiæ. Cui, ut in aliis multis suffraga- tur Hackspan. Sed causam non videmus solidam cur a plerorumq; nostrorum explicatione disceda- mus, & cum Sanctio Jesuita, aut Junio Calviniano μεταφορικως hæc accipiamus, maxime quia το ρη- τον retinendum est,nisi cogat necessitas,textusq; con- vincat, id relinquendum esse. Et e c. 66,22. liquet, de cælo glorioso alterius vitæ hæc agere, inprimis manifestum id est ex 2.Pet.3,13, & Ap. 21,1. imo et- iam ex hoc contextu id colligitur v. 18. gaudebitis & exultabitis USQUE IN SEMPITERNUM in his, quæ ego creo. Non enim de serenitate, aut fœ- cunditate temporum post liberationem ab Antiocho, ut Grotius, aut post reductionem e captivitate Baby- lonica, quod alii volunt, nec de magnitudine & gloria Ecclesiæ Nov. Test. quod visum fuit Calixto& Hackspanio, sed de felicitate in vita æterna sermo est: Nam id verborum emphasis, a qua temere di- scedendum non est, & creatio novæ terræ,novi cæli, & oblivio veteris, & gaudium æternum important, nec non explicatio c. 66,22. 2. Petr. 3, 13. Apoc.21,1. neq; aliud suadent antecedentia, & consequentia: nam quid obstat, cum promittuntur ea beneficia fideli- bus, quorum fruitione oblivisci veterum malorum queant, v. 16. progredi S. S. ad felicitatis ipsius cæle- stis promissionem, quod non istis tantum beneficiis exhilarandi, sed in cælo novo & terra nova æterno gaudio mactandi sint: etiamsi deinde porro certi- tudinis gratia promissiones istæ quæ in Ecclesia mi- litante ipsis exhibendæ sint, pertexantur. Sunt e- nim arcte inter se devinctæ promissiones pietati fa-

œ in hac & futura vita; optimeque conjunguntur ad majorem fidelium consolationem, quod alias et- iam in Sacris solemne est. Utut ergo concedamus de gaudio fidelibus in Ecclesia orituro postmodum agi, nihil tamen obstat, quo minus hic de gaudio cœlesti sermo sit, quia spirituale gaudium cohæret cum cælesti electorum gaudio ejusq; est quoddam πρόγευσμα Rom. 14, 17. Ebr. 6, 5. Conf. Hieronym. hic & c. 66, 22. Ita nec à litera textus abire necessum est, & συνέχεια & ratio antecedentium & consequen- tium integra, & illibata est, ut sive in illis, sive in his concedere mere cœlestia, & perpetuas figuratas admittere loquutiones in eorum descriptione o- pus minime habeamus. Agnoscunt ipsimet Judæi hæc de cælo novo ad alteram vitam spectare: sed quod cætera omnia etiam ad se rapiant, & mira de illis hic tradant, ad somnia eorum pertinet.

## 65:20
Verse 20.

THERE SHALL NO LONGER BE THERE AN INFANT OF DAYS] Who lives for few days. For God, if the judges did not punish sins, had professed himself to be an avenger, as in Lev. 20, 3. 5. But the vengeance was the death of the one who had sinned, prematurely and without offspring. He now denies that this will happen any longer, because the judges were going to perform their duty excellently. An infant of days is called one who does not live beyond the years of infancy, which, as we have said, was a punishment for the parents.

AND AN OLD MAN WHO DOES NOT FILL HIS DAYS] Understand here an old man as opposed to an infant, who is of advanced age, though not the greatest.

FOR A BOY OF A HUNDRED YEARS SHALL DIE] In the Hebrew: An adolescent: that is, he who will be an adolescent at the time of the restored Temple will reach a most full age, such as one hundred years.

AND A SINNER OF A HUNDRED YEARS SHALL BE ACCURSED] If anyone has committed some crime against the law, not even extreme old age, which is usually spared by many, will prevent the judges from inflicting upon him the punishment of the law (which is wont to be called a curse). See what we have said on Deut. 21, 23. It is a wonder what some Jews will not invent, who refer these things to the times after the resurrection.

Grotius marvels at the Jews, what they will not invent, but one ought to marvel at Grotius himself, what he has not invented. For has the order of nature been so changed from the time of the restored temple, or even the times of Judas Maccabeus, that infants have not been found who lived for few days, that old men have not died except at the greatest age, and that those who were adolescents at the time of the restored Temple have not prolonged their life to a hundred years? These are foolish dreams, no better than the Jewish inventions, which Jerome recounts thus: The Hebrews contend that these things will happen before the resurrection in no Kingdom of years upon the earth, and that such long spans of future life are promised that a hundred years are considered infancy, but that a sinner will die in the hundredth year of his age, so that, clearly, he may not enjoy the wealth he has prepared, but may know that he is accursed because of sin. But if this is so, where will be the perfect beatitude, which is violated and corrupted by sin, and sin is punished by premature death? Furthermore, as regards the sense of the Prophet's words, because it seems to be a discourse about the new heaven and the new earth and the new Jerusalem, which was shown to John in Apoc. 21, Jerome explains these things thus: In such a city there will not be different ages, infant and old man, small and great, who does not fill his days: but as if children of the resurrection, all will arrive at a perfect man, into the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ, so that neither are the spans of years lacking to anyone, nor do they exceed. To which Brentius's exposition is genuine. Another, he says, prerogative of the new city of Jerusalem. There will no longer be mortality in it. For in mortality, infants and adults are snatched away by plague before they have reached a just age and old age. But in the new Jerusalem all will arrive in their age at their just and legitimate days and years. Wherefore there will be no mortality in it. Nor indeed will anyone die in it, unless by chance there should approach it a Naar, that is, a fool. (For thus also the Germans name a fool from this Hebrew word, einen Narren) And a Chote, that is, a sinner. For this one, clearly the fool, or the impious, and the sinner, have a necessity to be accursed, to die and to perish, even if they have lived happy and fortunate for a hundred years in this age. But the true citizens of this new city of Jerusalem will live perpetually and will be blessed. This is that which Christ later said in John: God so loved the world, that he gave his only-begotten son, that everyone who believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. And soon after: He who believes in him is not condemned. But he who does not believe (this is that fool and sinner, of whom mention is made here in Isaiah) is already condemned: clearly, even if he still lives happy for a hundred years in this World. And again: I am (says Christ) the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, even if he has died, will live. And everyone who lives and believes in me will not die forever. You have, therefore, that in the new city of Jerusalem, which is the Church, there is no mortality. But the FOOL or impious AND THE SINNER have a necessity to be accursed, to die and to perish, even if they have lived a hundred years in this age happy and fortunate. Osiander explains it otherwise: THERE SHALL NO LONGER BE THERE AN INFANT OF MANY DAYS AND AN OLD MAN, WHO nevertheless DOES NOT FILL HIS DAYS. That is: There will not be in the Kingdom of heaven stupid and depraved men, whom you could call infants (as regards true and heavenly wisdom), even if they have many years: nor will there be such old men, who, although they have lived very many years, have not yet attained true and spiritual wisdom, pertaining to the salvation of the soul: of whom you could say that many years are still lacking to them for being wise. FOR A BOY OF A HUNDRED YEARS SHALL DIE AND A SINNER OF A HUNDRED YEARS SHALL BE ACCURSED. That is, those children, that is, the impious sinners and wicked, who for many years of their life have not learned what makes for obtaining and retaining eternal life, shall be delivered to eternal death, and shall be subject to eternal curse or damnation, nor shall they any longer disgrace the Church of Christ with their wickedness (for on the last day the evil shall finally be perfectly separated from the good, Matt. 13). The interpretation of the blessed Luther in his Latin Commentary is somewhat more subtle, such as is found almost exactly in Cyril, imagining here an antithesis of Law and Gospel. But in his German scholium he hints at that sense which Osiander explained. The Weimar paraphrasts have also followed this: nor do we doubt that the same is conformable to the mind of the Holy Spirit. However, the blessed Luther and the Weimar authors understand these things concerning the spiritual Jerusalem, or the Church in the kingdom of grace. But Osiander explains it concerning the heavenly Jerusalem, or the Church in the kingdom of glory. The things which are subjoined in verse 21 and following seem to favor the blessed Luther. You may more correctly explain these concerning the spiritual Jerusalem than concerning the other life. For the things which follow in verses 24 and 25 manifestly pertain to the state of the present life. So also the Papist interpreters, especially Pintus and Tirinus, whose paraphrase we subjoin: THERE SHALL NOT BE THERE AN INFANT OF DAYS or AN OLD MAN, WHO DOES NOT FILL THE DAYS of his life granted to him by God, supply, by living well, and by rightly performing the duties and offices of his age. For just as days are empty and void which are spent viciously: so they are called full and complete which are filled honestly and with good works, for which they were given. Therefore, although among Christians someone may die A CHILD, that is, still of tender age, yet as regards morals and understanding he shall die just as die as if he were A HUNDRED YEARS OLD, that is, mature and aged in heavenly wisdom and virtues. For virtue and knowledge alone will be esteemed and praised, not indeed an age less or more adult. Whence whoever shall be a SINNER in it, even if he be A HUNDRED YEARS OLD, and has acquired the greatest arts and experience and wealth; because he lacks virtue, he will be esteemed as nothing, but will be shameful and CURSED among all. Thus St. Gregory, Arias, Alvarez, and others.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

NON ERIT IBI AMPLIUS INFANS DIERUM] Qui paucos dies vivat. Nam Deus, si Judices peccata non punirent, se vindicem erat professus, ut Lev. 20, 3. 5. Vindicta autem erat mors ipsius, qui deliquisset imma- tura & sine prole. Hoc amplius eventurum jam negat, quia judices optime erant facturi officium. Infans dierum dicitur, qui non vivit ultra infantiæ annos, quæ ut diximus, pœna erat parentum.

ET SENEX QUI NON IMPLEAT DIES SUOS] Senem hic intellige oppositum infanti, qui provectæ sit ætatis, non tamen maximæ.

QUONIAM PUER CENTUM ANNORUM MORIETUR] In Hebræo: Adolescens: id est, qui adole- scens erit tempore instaurati Templi, perveniet ad ple- nissimam ætatem, qualis est annorum centum.

ET PECCATOR CENTUM ANNORUM MA- LEDICTUS ERIT] Si quis contra legem facinus aliquod commiserit, ne summa quidem senectus, cui apud mul- tos parci solet, obstabit quo minus judices ei pœnam le- gis (quæ maledictio dici solet) infligant. Vide quæ diximus ad Deut. 21, 23. Mirum est quid non comminiscantur Ju- dæi quidam, qui hæc ad tempora post resurrectionem refe- runt.

Miratur Grotius Judæos, quid non commi- niscantur, sed mirari oportet ipsummet Grotium, quid non ipse commentus sit. Num enim à tem- pore instaurati templi, vel etiam temporibus Judæ Maccabæi ordo naturæ sic immutatus est, ut non inventi sint infantes, qui paucos dies vixerint, non mortui sint senes nisi maxima ætate, & ad centum annos vitam prorogarint, qui adolescentes fuerint restaurati Templi tempore? somnia hæc sunt ani- lia, non meliora commentis Judaicis, quæ ita recen- set Hieronymus: Hebræi hæc ante resurrectionem in nullo annorum Regno super terram futura conten- dunt, & tam longa futuræ vitæ spatia repromitti, ut centum anni reputentur infantiæ, peccatorem autem centesimo ætatis suæ anno esse moriturum, ne videlicet paratis opibus perfruatur, sed ob peccatum maledi- ctum esse noverit. Quod si ita est, ubi erit beatitudo perfecta, quæ peccato violatur atque corrumpitur, & peccatum immatura morte punitur? Cæterum quod ad verborum Prophetæ sensum attinet, quia de no- vo cœlo, & nova terra ac nova Hierusalem, quæ monstrata est Johanni Apoc. 21. sermo esse videtur, Hieronymus hæc ita explicat: In tali urbe diversæ ætates non erunt, infans & senex, parvus & ma- gnus, qui non impleat dies suos: sed quasi filii resur- rectionis, omnes pervenient in virum perfectum, in mensuram ætatis plenitudinis Christi, ut nec desint alicui annorum spatia, nec supersint. Cui genuina est Brentii ἔκθεσις. Alia, inquit, prærogativa novæ ur- bis Hierusalem. Non erit deinceps in ea morta- litas. In mortalitate enim abripiuntur peste infan- tes & adulti, priusquam ad justam ætatem ac senectu- tem pervenerint. In nova autem Hierusalem omnes pervenient ætate sua ad justos & legitimos suos dies & annos. Quare non erit in ea mortalitas. Neque ex enim quispiam in ea morietur, nisi si forte accefferit ad eam נער Naar hoc est stultus. (Sic enim & Germani ab hoc Hebræo vocabulo nominant stultum einen Narren) Et חוטה Chote, hoc est peccator. Hic enim, stultus videlicet, seu impius, & peccator, necesse habent maledici, mori & perire, etiam si centum annos in hoc seculo felices ac fortunati vixerint. Veri autem cives hujus novæ urbis Hierusalem perpetuo vivent & benedicentur. Hoc illud est, quod Christus postea in Jo- hanne dixit: Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut filium suum unigenitū daret, ut omnis qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat æternam vitam. Et mox: Qui credit in eum, non condemnatur. Qui vero non credit (hic est stultus ille & peccator, de quo hic in E- saia fit mentio) jam condemnatus est: videlicet, et- iamsi adhuc centum annos in hoc Mundo felix vivat. Et iterum: Ego sum (inquit Christus) resurrectio & vita. Qui credit in me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet. Et omnis, qui vivit & credit in me, non morietur in æternum. Habes ergo, quod in nova ur- be Hierusalem, quæ est Ecclesia, nulla sit mortalitas. STULTUS autem seu impius ET PECCATOR necesse habent maledici, mori & perire, etiamsi centum annos vixerint in hoc seculo felices, ac for- tunati. Aliter ea exponit Osiander: NON E- RIT IBI AMPLIUS INFANS multorum DIE- RUM ET SENEX, QUI tamen NON IM- PLEAT DIES SUOS. Id est: Non erunt in Regno cœlorum homines stolidi & pravi, quos di- cere possis infantes (quoad veram & cælestem sa- pientiam) etiamsi multos annos habeant: nec e- runt tales senes, qui licet plurimos annos vixerint, tamen nondum assecuti sint veram & spiritualem sapientiam, ad animæ salutem pertinentem: de qui- bus dicere queas, quod multi adhuc anni ipsis de- sint ad sapiendum. QUONIAM PUER CEN- TUM ANNORUM MORIETUR ET PEC- CATOR CENTUM ANNORUM MALEDI- CTUS ERIT. Id est, Pueri illi, hoc est, impii peccatores & scelerati, qui multis annis vitæ suæ non didicerunt, quæ ad vitam æternam consequen- dam & retinendam faciunt, tradentur æternæ mor- ti, & subjacebunt æternæ maledictioni seu damna- tioni, nec amplius improbitate sua dehonestabunt Ecclesiam Christi (in novissimo enim die perfecte demum separabuntur mali à bonis, Matt. 13.) Paulo subtilior est B. Lutheri interpretatio in Commen- tario Latino, qualis fere apud Cyrillum reperitur, antithesin hic fingens legis & Evangelii. Sed in scho- lio Germanico sensum illum innuit, quem Osian- der exposuit. Hunc etiam Paraphrastæ Vinarienses sequuti sunt: neque nos dubitamus, eundem sen- tentiæ Spirit. Sanct. conformem esse. De Hiero- solyma tamen spirituali, vel Ecclesia in Regno gratiæ B. Lutherus & Vinarienses ea intelligunt. At Osi- ander explicat de Hierosolyma cælesti, vel Ecclesia in regno gloriæ. B. Luthero favere videntur, quæ vers. 21. seqq. subjiciuntur. Quæ rectius de spiri- tuali Hierosolyma exponas, quam de altera vita. Nam quæ vers. 24. 25. sequuntur, manifeste ad sta- tum præsentis vitæ pertinent. Sic etiam Pontifi- cii interpretes, imprimis Pintus & Tirinus, cujus paraphrasin subjungimus: NON ERIT IBI INFANS DIERUM aut SENEX, QUI DIES vitæ suæ concessos sibi à Deo NON IMPLEAT, supple, bene vivendo, & suæ ætatis officia ac munia recte obeundo. Ut enim dies vacui & inanes sunt, qui vitiose traducuntur: sic pleni & completi di- cuntur, qui honeste & bonis operibus, ad quæ dati sunt, implentur. Quamvis ergo inter Christianos moriatur quis PUER, id est, ætate adhuc tenera, tamen quoad mores & sensum perinde MORIE- TUR ac si esset CENTUM ANNORUM, id est, sapientia cœlesti & virtutibus maturus ac in- veteratus. Æstimabitur enim & laudabitur sola virtus & scientia non vero ætas minus vel magis adulta. Unde quicunque fuerit in ea PECCA- TOR, etsi CENTUM sit ANNORUM, & artes & experientiam & opes nactus sit maximas; quia tamen virtute caret, nihil æstimabitur, sed probro- sus apud omnes & MALEDICTUS erit. Ita S. Gregorius, Arias, Alvarez & alii.

## 65:22
Vers. 22.

THEY SHALL NOT BUILD, AND ANOTHER SHALL INHABIT: THEY SHALL NOT PLANT AND ANOTHER SHALL EAT] It shall not happen according to that: Graft pears, O Daphne, your descendants shall harvest your apples. FOR ACCORDING TO THE DAYS OF THE TREE SHALL BE THE DAYS OF MY PEOPLE] They shall live as long as the tree itself. The tree of life according to the LXX, and the Chaldean and Rabbi Solomon in this place, does it look back to Paradise, or is it called the most long-lived tree in this way? AND THE WORKS OF THEIR HANDS SHALL GROW OLD] That is, the houses which they have built shall endure.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

NON ÆDIFICABUNT, ET ALIUS HABITA- BIT: NON PLANTABUNT ET ALIUS COMEDET] Non fiet secundum illud : Insere Daphne piros, carpent tua poma nepotes. SECUNDUM ENIM DIES LIGNI ERUNT DIES POPULI MEI] Tam diu vivent, quam ipsa arbor. Arbor vitæ apud LXX, & Chaldæum & Rabbinum Solo- monem hoc loco, an ad Paradisum respicit, an ita dici- tur arbor vivacissima? ET OPERA MANUUM EORUM INVETERA- BUNT] Id est, durabunt ædes quas struxerint.

## 65:23
Vers. 23.

MY ELECT SHALL NOT LABOR IN VAIN] Others shall not consume their sowing, which God threatens will happen to the impious in Leviticus 26, verse 16, and Deuteronomy 28, verse 30. NEITHER SHALL THEY GENERATE IN TROUBLE] From the Hebrew לבהלה. But the LXX read לאלה, into a curse, which the Chaldean interprets well, unto death, namely untimely, which is among curses. The received reading can be drawn into the same sense if by trouble we understand the grief of parents. Jerome thinks בהלה can be translated as non-existence. See what is said on Job 18, 13. THE SEED OF THE BLESSED OF THE LORD IS] In the Hebrew: The seed to them blessed by the Lord: supply they shall be. Therefore God will preserve infants in life, because He will love the parents.

This explanation of Grotius concerning material buildings does not sufficiently fit the history, to which he adapts it, and is entirely foreign to the prophetic text: which treats of the Church of the New Testament. And therefore the interpreters explain these things concerning the building and propagation of the Church. To build, says Blessed Luther, is not to heap up a pile of stones or wood, but to prepare, instruct, and increase households. It signifies, therefore, that from one Church ten others will arise, so that in this way a greater number of the faithful may be made. STRANGERS SHALL NOT INHABIT. No impious person shares in the fruits and gifts of the Church. Similarly, Brentius and the Vinarian paraphrasts explain that the curse of Deuteronomy 28, verse 30, is to be removed, that one should build and plant and another possess and enjoy, or that duration and preservation are promised to the faithful; finally, that the curse of men in labor and women in generation, Genesis 3, will cease, because after sin is expiated, a blessing follows. But those things which are to be understood spiritually teach concerning the all-encompassing blessing of this and the future life. To which interpretation Tirinus from the Papists agrees. THEY SHALL NOT BUILD HOUSES AND another SHALL INHABIT them. As happens in time of war, or when a creditor drives you out, or poverty compels you to sell. For the Church shall enjoy its goods in full peace and quiet, especially spiritual ones, which no thief, no force, no deceit, nor even the gates of hell themselves will snatch from you against your will. ACCORDING TO THE DAYS OF THE TREE, that is, according to the condition of a tree always flourishing by the waters, SHALL BE THE DAYS OF MY PEOPLE. Thus Arias and Sanchez. But St. Jerome, Cyril, Lyranus, Sasbout, a Lapide, and Alvarez explain it concerning the tree of life: because the LXX translate it so, and in the Hebrew it is of that tree, namely the famous and preeminent one above others. As if to say, My faithful shall be long-lived, joyful, cheerful, and very healthy, just as if they were in the primeval state of innocence, and were eating the fruit of the tree of life. Osiander and Gerhard on the consummation of the age, § 91, explain it mystically and symbolically concerning heavenly happiness: that an abundance and affluence of all things that can delight the pious will be at hand for them, that the curse of God is to be entirely removed, and that the possession of that happiness is never to be ended.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

ELECTI MEI NON LABORABUNT FRU- STRA] Non demerent alii illorum sementem, quod im- piis eventurum minatur Deus Levit. 26. vers. 16. & Deu- ter. 28. v. 30. NEQUE GENERABUNT IN CONTURBA- TIONE] Ex Hebræo לבהלה. At LXX. legerunt לאלה εἰς κατάραν, quod Chaldæus bene interpretatur, ad mor- tem, nempe ἄωρον, quæ inter κατάρας. Potest in eundem sensum trahi recepta lectio, si per conturbationem intel- ligamus luctum parentum. Hieronymus בהלה putat verti posse ἀνυπαρξίαν. Vid. quæ ad Jobum 18, 13. SEMEN BENEDICTORUM DOMINI EST] In Hebræo: Semen ipsi benedictorum Domino: supple erunt. Id- eo Deus infantes in vita conservabit, quia amabit parentes.

Explicatio hæc Grotiana de materialibus ædi- ficiis neque historiæ satis convenit, cui illam aptat, & aliena prorsus est à textu prophetico: qui de Ec- clesia N. T. agit. Ideoq; de ædificatione & pro- pagatione Ecclesiæ hæc exponunt Interpp. Ædifi- care, inquit B. Lutherus, non est struem lapidum aut lignorum congerere, sed œconomias parare, instrue- re, augere. Significat igitur ex una Ecclesia decem alias proventuras, ut ita major fidelium numerus fiat. ALIENI NON HABITABUNT. Nemo im- pius communicat Ecclesiæ fructibus & donis ejus. Si- militer explicant Brentius, & paraphrastæ Vina- rienses, sublatum iri maledictionem Deuter. 28. vers. 30. quod alius ædificet & plantet, alius pos- sideat & fruatur, vel promitti durationem & con- servationem fidelibus; denique maledictionem virorum in labore & fœminarum in generatione Gen. 3. cessaturam, quia expiato peccato sequi- tur benedictio. Quæ vero spiritualiter intelli- genda esse docent de benedictione omnigena hu- jus & futuræ vitæ. Cui interpretationi accedit è Pontificiis Tirinus. NON ÆDIFICABUNT DOMOS ET alius eas INHABITABIT. Ut fit tempore belli, vel creditore te expellente, vel inopia te ad vendendum compellente. Nam plena pace & quiete fruetur Ecclesia bonis suis, maxime spirituali- bus, quæ nullus invito tibi rapiet latro, nulla vis, nul- lus dolus, sed nec ipsæ portæ infernales. SECUNDUM DIES LIGNI id est, pro conditione arboris juxta aquas semper vernantis, ERUNT DIES PO- PULI MEI. Ita Arias & Sanchez. At S. Hie- ronymus, Cyrillus, Lyranus, Sasbout, à Lapide & Al- varez id exponunt de ligno vitæ : quia sic vertunt LXX. & in Hebræo est illius ligni, nempe famosi & præcellentis aliis. q. d. Fideles mei longævi, læti, ala- cres & bene sani erunt, perinde ac si essent in pri- mævo innocentiæ statu, & vescerentur fructu arbo- ris vitæ. De felicitate cœlesti μυστικῶς & συμβο- λικῶς explicat Osiander & Gerhardus de consum- mat. secul. §. 91. quod omnium rerum, quæ pios oblectare possunt, copia & affluentia illis præsto sit futura, quod maledictio Dei prorsus sit auferen- da, quod nunquam finienda sit felicitatis istius pos- sessio.

## 65:24
Vers. 24.

AND IT SHALL BE BEFORE THEY CALL, I WILL HEAR] I will avert evils before they complain of them.

WHILE THEY ARE YET SPEAKING I WILL HEAR] I will be ready to bestow good things as soon as I am asked.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ERITQUE ANTEQUAM CLAMENT, EGO EXAUDIAM] Mala avertam antequam de iis conqueran- tur.

ADHUC ILLIS LOQUENTIBUS EGO AU- DIAM] Ad bona largienda paratus ero, simulatq; rogabor.

## 65:25
Vers. 25. THE WOLF AND THE LAMB SHALL FEED TOGETHER, THE LION AND THE OX SHALL EAT STRAW] What preceded, together, must be repeated here. The sense is the same as above 11, 6, where see.

AND DUST SHALL BE THE SERPENT'S FOOD] His food shall be dust only, he shall not touch men, for serpents are accustomed to feed on dust. Gen. 3,14. With these are compared fierce men, who are compelled to lay aside their ferocity and obey the laws, as is most clearly to be seen in Mic. 7, 17. add. the place Ps 72, 9.

THEY SHALL NOT HURT, NOR SHALL THEY KILL IN ALL MY HOLY MOUNTAIN] There shall be no murders, no robberies. Thus the laws shall flourish. See above 20.

These things teach that the discourse is concerning the state of the faithful in this life: whom GOD wishes to anticipate in their prayers, and to preserve in tranquility. We have said, at Isa. ch. 11, ver. 6, that this tranquility is not political, but spiritual. Which passage Grotius himself here considers as a parallel. Osiander rightly expressed the sense here. There shall be true concord and love among those who are truly Christians. THE WOLF AND THE LAMB SHALL FEED TOGETHER, nor shall the wolf harm the lamb, AND THE LION AND THE OX shall eat STRAW together, nor shall the lion tear the ox; AND DUST shall be the SERPENT'S BREAD, or HIS food: he shall bite neither man nor any animal. THEY SHALL NOT HURT beasts, NOR SHALL THEY KILL anyone, IN ALL MY HOLY MOUNTAIN, in the heavenly Jerusalem: SAYS THE LORD. i.e., through the Gospel, men who had previously been virulent and cruel shall become so tame that they not only cease to rage and do harm, but also live together most unitedly and lovingly. I add what Cyril has handed down not inelegantly concerning this passage: THEN THE WOLVES AND THE LAMBS &C. You shall take these in two ways. For the Prophetic sentence can signify either the union of two peoples through faith: or that those who once, after the manner of wild beasts, insulted the saints and persecuted the Church, not unlike serpents, shall coalesce with them into one affection and agreement of mind, bound together also by the bond of peace through Christ, who justifies the ungodly, and gathers what is dispersed, and illuminates with divine light what is wrapped in darkness, and turns all things for the better. For He makes and transforms all things, as it is written. Therefore, the kids and the lambs from the law shall be consecrated and clean animals, so that they might be brought to the divine altar, and offered to God for an odor of sweet fragrance. But the wolf and the lion [represent] the profane and unclean, and those hostile to the ones we have named. The serpent, moreover, is most hostile to man and incited to this by the laws of nature. But with those who have been purified in Christ, and have instituted a holy and excellent life, through the Evangelical preaching, even these once detestable and unclean [beings], having a breast filled with beastly cruelty, shall coalesce into one agreement of minds, which is in faith: They shall do nothing harmful, he says, nor shall they destroy anyone in my holy mountain, that is, the Church. For the fierce shall eat with the tame. But their delights are Christ, the living bread descending from heaven, and giving life to the world. He nourishes, moreover, even with His own flesh, refashioning us unto immortality and life, and by His own preaching, that is, the Evangelical (for man, he says, does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.) Observe, however, that the lambs and the kids do not eat the food of lions and wolves: For he did not say: they shall eat flesh, but the wolves and lions shall use the tame food of the gentle animals, which are signified by the name of straw. He does not but they will follow the unclean of the world: nor will they emulate their institution and life, but rather the profane will imitate the probity of the mild and pure. Even the Rabbis themselves refute the Grotian gloss, who acknowledge that this chapter deals with the calling of the Gentiles: Thus R. Aben Ezra on v. 1. R. Moses Hacoban said the first verse is to be understood concerning the nations of the world: so that the sense may be: I have been called upon even by the Gentiles, who are not called by my name.
