And R. Saadia Gaon in Sepher Haëmenoth c. 8. acknowledges that these promises in v. 17 look toward the joy at the end of the world. There will be for them (at the end of the world) a world full of joy and exultation, so that their heavens and their earth are as if renewed, as Isa. (c. 65, 17) explains: Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth &c.

Latin:

Vers. 25. LUPUS ET AGNUS PASCENTUR SIMUL, LEO ET BOS COMEDENT PALEAS] Repetendum hic quod præcessit simul. Sensus idem qui supra 11,6. ubi vide.

ET SERPENTI PULVIS PANIS EJUS] Cibus e- jus erit pulvis tantum, homines non attinget, Serpentes so- lent pasci pulvere. Gen. 3,14. Cum his comparantur homi- nes feroces, qui coguntur ferociam deponere, & parêre le- gibus, ut videre est clarissime Mich. 7, 17. add. loco Ps 72, 9.

NON NOCEBEUNT, NEQUE OCCIDENT IN OMNI MONTE SANCTO MEO] Nulla homicidia, nullæ rapinæ erunt. Ita vigebunt leges. Vide supra 20.

Hæc docent de statu fidelium sermonem esse in hac vita: quos prævenire vult DEUS in ora- tionibus suis, & conservare in tranquillitate. Hanc autem tranquillitatem non esse politicam, sed spiritualem, ad Esa. cap. 11. vers. 6. diximus. Quem locum hic ipse Grotius pro parallelo habet. Recte sensum hic expressit Osiander. Erit vera con- cordia & dilectio inter eos, qui vere sunt Christiani. LUPUS ET AGNUS PASCENTUR SIMUL, nec lupus agnum lædat, ET LEO ET BOS simul COMEDENT PALEAS, neg; leo bovem laniabit; ET SERPENTI erit PULVIS PANIS, seu cibus EIUS: neque homi- nem neque ullum animal mordebit. NON NOCE- BUNT bestiæ, NEQUE OCCIDENT quenquam, IN OMNI MONTE SANCTO MEO, in cælesti Jerusalem: DICIT DOMINUS. i. e. per Evangelion homines, qui fuerant prius virulenti & crudeles, ita mansuescent, ut non modò sævire & nocere desinant, sed etiam in- ter se conjunctissime & amantissime vivant. Addo quæ Cyrillus de hoc loco non inelegantia tradidit: TUNC LUPI ET AGNI &C. Bifariam hæc acci- pies. Vel enim duorum populorum per fidem unionem significare potest Sententia Prophetica: vel qui quon- dam agrestium ferarum more sanctis insultaverunt, & Ecclesiam insectati sunt, serpentibus non dissimiles, cum illis in unum affectum animiq; consensionem co- alescent, vinculo pacis etiam colligati per Christum, qui justificat impium, & quod dispersum est, colligit, ac luce divina tenebris involutum collustrat, omniaq; convertit in melius. Facit enim omnia & transfor- mat, uti scriptum est. Hædi ergo & Agni ex lege erunt sacrata & munda animalia, adeout ad divi- num altare adducerentur, & in odorem suavis fra- grantiæ Deo offerrentur. Lupus autem & Leo pro- phana ac immunda, & his quæ nominavimus infesta. Serpens præterea homini inimicissimus & naturæ le- gibus ad hoc incitatus. Verum cum his, qui in Christo purgati sunt, & sanctam & eximiam vitam institue- runt, per Evangelicam prædicationem in unam ani- morum consensionem, quæ est in fide, coalescent etiam hi detestandi quondam & immundi & belluina cru- delitate pectus refertum habentes: Hi nihil nocebunt, inquit, neque perdent quenquam in monte san- cto meo, id est, Ecclesia. Comedent enim cum mansuetis efferata. Delitiæ vero illis Christus, pa- nis vivus de cælo descendens, & vitam dans mundo. Nutrit autem etiam carne propria, ad immortalita- tem ac vitam nos refingens, & sua prædicatione, id est, Evangelica (non enim in solo pane vivit, inquit, ho- mo, sed in omni verbo, quod prodit ex ore Dei.) Obser- va autem agnos & hædos leonum & luporum cibos non edere: Neque enim dixit: comedent carnes, sed lupi & leones mansuetis utentur cibis cicurum anima- lium, quæ palearum nomine significantur. Non se- quentur autem immundos mundi: neque illorum in- stitutum ac vitam æmulabuntur, sed prophani potius mitium & purorum probitatem imitabuntur. Glos- sam Grotianam refellunt etiam ipsi Rabbini, qui agnoscunt hoc capite de vocatione gentium agi: Sic R. Aben Ezra ad v. 1. Dixit R. Moses Hacoban primum versum de mundi gentibus intelligi: ut sit sensus: invocatus sum etiam à gentibus, quæ no- mine meo non vocantur. Et R. Saadia Gaon in Sepher Haëmenoth c. 8. agnoscit, has promissio- nes vers. 17. de lætitia ad finem mundi spectare. Erit illis (in fine mundi) mundus plenus gaudio & exultatione, ita, ut cæli eorum & terra eorum quasi innoventur, ut explicat Esa. (c. 65, 17.) Ecce, Ego creo cælos novos & terram novam &c.

## 66:1 Argument
CHAPTER LXVI. AND THE LAST.

The vain boasting of the Temple and Sacrifices is punished by the intimation of confusion on account of disobedience: But to those who fear the Lord, the fruitfulness of the Church and the abundance of the peace and joy of consolation, and the judgment of the Lord in the final destruction of the Jews, through whose remnants the Gentiles are summoned to spiritual sacrifices and to the holy mountain, is proposed: and the Prophet ends with the promise of an eternal Sabbath in the new heaven and new earth and the threat of eternal condemnation.

Vers. 1.

THUS SAYS THE LORD) The things which now follow serve to console those who were to see the profanation of the Temple under Antiochus, and the cessation of sacrifices for three years and a half. God therefore shows that there is no reason why they should be offended by this matter: that to Him the pious mind is the best Temple: that from it sacrifices are estimated. There is an oracle in Hierocles: Ἐυσεβέσιν δὲ βροτοῖς γάνυμαι τόσον, ὅσσον ὀλύμπῳ. Seneca: Do you wish to think of God as great and calm, and to be revered with gentle majesty, a friend and always near? Is He to be worshipped not with immolations and much blood, but with a pure mind and an honest purpose? Temples are not to be built for Him with stones piled to a height: He is to be consecrated in the breast of each one. See also other things of equal sense around the end of the Annotations to Book IV of the truth of the Christian Religion. But the things which are said here are all such that they pave the way for the Gospel.

HEAVEN IS MY THRONE) The seat of majesty.

BUT THE EARTH IS MY FOOTSTOOL) ὑποπόδιον, such as was for the thrones of kings. The earth, the viler part of things. See what is at Matt. 5, 35.

WHAT IS THIS HOUSE WHICH YOU WILL BUILD FOR ME, AND WHAT IS THIS PLACE OF MY REST?) This is small, if it is compared to heaven and earth. Euripides: Ποῖος δ᾽ ἂν οἶκος τεκτόνων πλασθεὶς ὕπο Δέμας τὸ θεῖον περιβάλοι τοίχων πτυχαῖς;

Latin:

CAPUT LXVI. ET ULTIMUM.

Templi & Sacrificiorum jactantia vana confusa pœna intimatur ob inobedien- tiam: Timentibus vero Dominum Ec- clesiæ fœcunditas & solatii pacis ac læ- titiæ abundantia, & judicium Domini in ultimo excidio Judæorum, per quo- rum reliquias gentes ad spiritualia sa- crificia & ad sanctum montem accer- sentur, proponitur: ac promissione æ- terni in novo cælo & nova terra Sabbati ac comminatione æternæ condemnatio- nis finitur Propheta.

Vers. 1.

HÆC DICIT DOMINVS) Quæ jam sequuntur consolandis illis serviunt, qui visuri erant profanationem Templi sub Antiocho, & sacrificiorum cessationem per an- nos tres & dimidium. Ostendit ergo Deus non esse, quod hac re offenderentur: sibi optimum Templum esse piam mentem: ex eo æstimari sacrificia. Est oraculum apud Hie- croclem: Ἐυσεβέσιν δὲ βροτοῖς γάνυμαι τόσον, ὅσσον ὀλύμπῳ. Seneca: Vultisne Deum cogitare magnum & placidum, & majestate leni verendum, amicum & semper in proximo? Non immolationibus & sanguine multo colendum, sed mente pura, honestoq; proposito? Non templa illi congestis in altitudinem sa- xis exstruenda sunt: in suo cuique consecrandus est pectore. Vide & alia paris sensus circa finem Annotationum ad Li- brum IV. de veritate Religionis Christianæ. Quæ autem hic dicuntur, omnia talia sunt, ut iter struant Evangelio.

COELVM SEDES MEA) Solium majestatis.

TERRA AVTEM SCABELLVM PEDVM MEO- RVM) ὑποπόδιον, quale erat regum soliis. Terra, pars rerum vilior. Vide quæ ad Matth. 5, 35.

QVÆ EST ISTA DOMVS QVAM ÆDIFI- CABITIS MIHI, ET QVIS EST ISTE LOCVS QVIETIS MEÆ?) Exiguum hoc est, si cælo & terræ com- paretur. Euripides: Ποῖος δ᾽ ἂν οἶκος τεκτόνων πλασθεὶς ὕπο Δέμας τὸ θεῖον περιβάλοι τοίχων πτυχαῖς;

## 66:2
Vers. 2.

ALL THESE THINGS MY HAND HAS MADE) All things which you see anywhere have been made by me, and therefore are of my right. You have a similar one in Ps. 50, 10.

That these things look to the times of Antiochus was not only to be said, but to be taught and proven. These brain-spun inventions of Grotius are rejected with the same ease with which they were proposed. But our people have rightly expressed the argument. Osiander: The Prophet preaches also in this chapter about the rejection of the Jews, because they had corrupted the worship of God with impious opinions, and were not doing penance. He also prophesies about the sudden increase of the Church of Christ, and finally speaks about the eternal rewards of the pious, and the perpetual punishments of the impious. That these things are so, the exegesis and vindications will teach. He had said that he would exult in Jerusalem, that nothing harmful would be in his holy mountain: Lest anyone should think of an earthly city or Mount Sion, and a material temple, GOD protested that He does not dwell in an earthly house, that He has no place of rest, but chooses a contrite heart as His seat and dwelling. By which very thing the difference between the Old and New Testament is clearly removed. For under the former, GOD had chosen to dwell in the tabernacle and in the temple, and there He wished to be worshipped in a peculiar way. But now, He says, what is this house which you will build for me, and what is this place of my rest? Because it was to be that under the New Testament, true worshippers would not worship in a temple or on a mountain, but would worship God everywhere in spirit and in truth, John 4, 23. everywhere throughout the whole world they were to lift up holy hands 1. Timoth. 2. v. 8. Therefore the Protomartyr, after the coming of Christ and the prediction of the final destruction of the Jerusalem temple, which not only Christ, but also Stephen testified was imminent, Acts 6, v. 14, used this oracle to demonstrate that it had been predicted by the Prophet that GOD did not wish henceforth for His worship to be restricted to a certain place, and thus that that economy of the ancient Levitical worship was to be abolished, Acts 7, v. 49. Whence it is not in the least obscure, since St. Stephen in his apology concerning the destruction of the Temple appealed to the present prophecy of Isaiah, that it concerns the final time of the Jewish polity, and is not to be snatched away by a perverse line of reasoning to the times of Antiochus, during which the temple was certainly not destroyed, but preserved, and remained under profane hands for no more than three years. And therefore the Jews had no need to think about the rebuilding of the Temple. But since Christ and the Protomartyr predicted a total and final destruction, which is never to be built again, and instead of an apology used a similar prediction made by the Prophet, which likewise states that the seat of the Lord's rest would be utterly taken away, and that GOD would inhabit no other dwelling except that of a contrite and obedient heart, it is manifest that these things were predicted for the times of the New Testament, and can in no way be drawn back to the times of Judas Maccabaeus, during which it had to be cleansed and consecrated again for divine worship, after which the temple of the Lord stood for more than two centuries longer and was the seat of divine worship. Cyril relates this συνέχειαν: When he has abundantly woven his discourse to the nations, he now turns his mystagogy to Israel itself. For he wishes them to depart also from the legal shadow, just as he clearly ordered those others to withdraw from their former error, seduction, and profane life. He therefore openly teaches that he values and cares for spiritual worship rather than that which is shadowy and typical, and that he values the latter as nothing. Rightly, therefore, Blessed Jerome says on these words: THUS SAITH THE LORD, HEAVEN IS MY THRONE, etc. Lest we should understand the holy mountain of Zion, and be covered by the Jewish error, which thinks that Jerusalem is to be built up, and all things which he promises are to be fulfilled there carnally, he removes this suspicion from us, and sets forth the Testimony which Stephen, a martyr in Christ, used against the Jewish contention: Solomon built him a house, no doubt for God, but he does not dwell in things made by hands, as the Prophet says: heaven is my throne, but the earth is the footstool of my feet. And Paul in the same volume: God who made the world and those who are in it, by no means dwells in temples made by hands. For if heaven is his throne and the earth the footstool of his feet, like one sitting on a seat and reigning: Who shall be enclosed in a small place, who fills all things? Whence also Moses: Do not say, he says, in your heart, it is far off: for God is in heaven above and on the earth below, and there is no other God besides him. And the Psalmist: Whither shall I go from your Spirit, and from your face whither shall I flee? If I ascend into heaven, you are there, if I descend into hell, you are present. To whom also Jeremiah agrees from the person of God, saying: Am I a God at hand, and not a God from afar? Shall anyone be able to hide in secret places, and I not see him? Do I not fill heaven and earth? For in him we all are and move, who think that the invisible and incorporeal and incomprehensible God can be enclosed by the temple of Jerusalem? Which indeed Solomon himself, the builder of the temple, confesses at greater length in his prayer to the Lord, etc.

And lest we think that the greatness of GOD is to be measured by heaven and earth as well, we read in another place about him: Who holds heaven with a span and the earth with a fist. By which it is shown that God is both outside and inside and infused and circumfused, while he is not enclosed by the surrounding seat, and he encloses with his fist and span. Who is the creator not only of heaven and earth, but of invisible things, of angels, and archangels, of dominions, of powers, and of all men, of whom the Apostle speaks: Which all the hand of God has wrought. Of which also Job and the Psalmist make mention: Your hand has made me and fashioned me. For all things were made through him, and without him nothing was made. Of whom John again: In the world, he says, he was, and the world was made through him. For he spoke and they were made, he commanded and they were created. And this which the Scripture of Genesis demonstrates in mystical language: God said and God made. For by the word of the Lord the heavens were established and by the spirit of his mouth all their power. And there is no place of the Lord's rest, except that which the Prophet subjoins: BUT TO WHOM SHALL I LOOK &c. Blessed Luther agrees, thus demonstrating the connection: Hitherto you have heard that the Prophet was engaged in reproving our pursuits and elective worships, which had been instituted without the word by superstitious Idolaters. For he accused Gad and Meni. Now a new accusation follows, and one much graver than the former, in which he does not reprove elective worship, but worship divinely instituted and commanded. Likewise the temple built not by human thought, but by divine promise. Just as that promise was first made to David. After the people and temple were devastated by the Babylonians, it was repeated. The Prophet therefore here strikes at the throat of the Synagogue, when he condemns even those things as flagitious and abominable before God, which had been established by the word of God and the divine promises themselves, such as that in Haggai 2: I will fill my house with glory, and similar ones. For the Jews, inflated by these promises, had the highest confidence that not only were these worships pleasing to God, but that they would be perpetual. On the contrary, the Prophet mocks and condemns them. Wherefore without doubt this prophecy was a principal Article, since the people ordered Isaiah to be sawn in half. Just as we also see in the Acts. After Stephen alleges the sentence, which he places here at the beginning of the chapter, there follows a horrible clamor of the Jews, accusing him as a blasphemer against the temple, the place, the law, and the people. And they intended these crimes against him with a clear conscience, wherefore with stopped ears they did not even want to hear Stephen, but having taken up stones they put him to death. Brentius is also worthy to be heard here: You see, he says, immediately at the beginning of this sermon of the Son of God, the temple is rejected and abrogated. Why so? was it not instituted by divine command? was it not sanctified by miracles from heaven? Rightly, but not for that use which the impious and unrepentant Jews dreamed of. For in instituting the Jerusalem temple, the counsel of GOD was that he might bind his Church, not indeed perpetually, but until the advent of Christ in the flesh, to a certain place and to certain sacred rites, by which the true doctrine concerning the Law, concerning the Messiah or Christ, and concerning the Kingdom of Christ might be preserved and propagated to posterity, so that the people, instructed by the law and the Gospel, might repent, believe in Christ the expiator of sin, invoke God from true faith in Christ, and walk in the calling of God: until they were called from this world to receive in reality the inheritance of the heavenly Kingdom. But the hypocrites and impious Jews were doing nothing less than taking pains to know the law and to acknowledge Christ through faith, but rather they persecuted those who urged this salutary and necessary doctrine: and although they did not repent at all, nor follow the good works commanded in the Decalogue, especially concerning true confidence in God, concerning true invocation of God, and concerning true love of neighbor, they nevertheless hoped and boasted that they would obtain righteousness and salvation by the worship and sacred rites of this temple. Whence also when Jeremiah threatened them with devastation, on account of impiety and impenitence, they shouted and repeated, The Temple of the Lord, The Temple of the Lord, etc., signifying that they were sufficiently safe from impending evils on account of the temple and its sacred rites, even if they were otherwise defiled by every kind of vice, and were doing no repentance at all. For they felt that God was so bound to this Temple and its sacred rites, that He could not abandon them and cast off the people of this temple and the worshipper of its sacred rites. Although Solomon had already before, in the dedication of this temple, condemned that opinion and impiety: 'Is it to be thought (he says) that God truly dwells upon the earth? For if heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee, how much less this house which I have built for Thee?' yet the impious and unrepentant passed over these words with deaf ears. Wherefore the Son of God takes up through Isaiah the sentiment of Solomon, or rather of the Holy Spirit, to be repeated, and the impious opinion of the hypocrites concerning the temple to be refuted: that He might explain the reason why the temple is deservedly cast down together with its people. These things shine forth from the whole συννεχείᾳ of the Prophet; nor do they have anything in common with the fiction of Grotius. Grotius himself, when he had not yet lent his ears to the inventions of the more recent Jews, professed that these things pertain to the times of the New Testament, lib. V. de verit. Relig. Christ. §. 8., proving it from this passage, because, to wit, Isaiah says it will come to pass that those most widely separated, and peoples of all languages, no less than the Israelites, shall offer gifts to God, and from them also shall be appointed those who are Priests and Levites, all of which things could not be done while the law of Moses stood.

Verse of the same. TO WHOM SHALL I LOOK?) He now comes to the sacrifices, which he says are as pleasing or displeasing to him, according to the life and mind of the one offering. EXCEPT TO THE POOR LITTLE ONE) עני the humble one, as the LXX translate here, that is, one who thinks modestly of himself. But the Chaldean [translates] ענו the meek one. Often these words of the same origin and similar meaning are intermingled among themselves. AND CONTRITE IN SPIRIT) One doing penance for sins, as in Ps. 51, 19. AND TREMBLING AT MY WORDS) One fearing to stumble against my laws. Jerome explains these things thus: With the altar and the earthly temple, which human hands had constructed, removed, the victims of the Jews are rightly taken away, lest perhaps they might say: We are not so foolish as to think that God can be enclosed in a place, but we offer to God in a separate place for sacrificing the victims which are commanded by the law. The inhabitant of heaven, therefore, nay rather the creator of all things, who denies that he has a temple on earth, willingly takes into his temple the man who is humble and quiet and trembling at his words. According to that of the Apostle: But you are the temple of GOD, and the Holy Spirit dwells in you. If anyone violates the temple of God, God will violate him. For the temple of God is holy, which you are. Whoever, therefore, is humble and quiet and trembling at the words of God, the Lord looks upon him. Blessed Luther speaks beautifully about this dwelling. He explains here where God wishes to dwell, what is his true workshop, in which God is accustomed to do his work, namely, a contrite spirit. Therefore, when the sadness of the Spirit and a contrite heart are felt, we ought to rejoice and be glad; but these things are too great to be believed by the human mind, at the time when it is in temptation. For what are all the palaces of the world, nay rather heaven and earth, to a contrite heart, if indeed it is the seat of the divine majesty? Thus in the Psalm: The Lord is near to the afflicted, and he will deliver those who are contrite in spirit. Likewise, Many are the afflictions of the just, but the Lord delivers him out of them all. For one cannot come to the knowledge of Christ, if through afflictions, and when someone is afflicted, then at last is the place, time, and space for being helped. For afflictions are the true matter, and that nothingness from which God is accustomed to make something, for God works in privative, not positive, matter. But because the Prophet speaks here of justification, he does not understand bodily afflictions, but the sense of sin, death, and conscience. He rejects, therefore, the greatest merits, namely the Temple, and commends to us a life without the Law; he offers his face to the undeserving and unworthy, who feel not justice, but sin, not peace, but the terrors of conscience. Let us not, therefore, despair when we have fallen into sins and grave errors, but, erected by such consolations, let us believe, even when we feel it least, that God looks upon us, is present, and favors us, etc. Nor should the paraphrase of Brentius be neglected: Nothing else is said than that God looks upon those who acknowledge their sins and believe in the Gospel of Christ. For these are they who, with an afflicted and contrite spirit, terrified by the recognition and judgment of sin, understand that they are liable not only to bodily death, but also to perpetual damnation in hell. But here it is added: I look upon him who trembles at my word. For it is not enough that you acknowledge your sin and be of an afflicted and contrite spirit: but it is also required that you tremble; that is, that you receive the word of God with great care, great zeal, great faith, and great reverence and obedience of faith. But this is the word of the Gospel, which God the Father placed in the mouth of his son, and which the Son preached: namely, that he alone is the expiator of sin and our justifier. This word must be received with fear and trembling, and with the highest reverence and obedience. Wherefore, he who thus acknowledges his sin, and is thus of a contrite spirit on account of sin, that he even believes in the Gospel of Christ, and embraces him with reverent faith: he is made such a temple and such a house that GOD looks upon him from on high, and as CHRIST says, The Father will love him and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

OMNIA HÆC MANVS MEA FECIT) Omnia quæ usquam videtis à me facta sunt, ac proinde mei juris. Simile habes Ps. 50, 10.

HÆc Tempora Antiochi spectare, non dicen- dum tantum, sed docendum & probandum erat. Commenta hæc cerebrina Grotii parili fa- cilitate rejiciuntur, qua facilitate proposita sunt. Recte autem argumentum expresserunt Nostri. Osiander: Concionatur Propheta etiam in hoc ca- pite de abjectione Judæorum, propterea quod cultum Dei impiis opinionibus corrupissent, neque pœniten- tiam agerent. Vaticinatur etiam de incremento subito Ecclesiæ Christi, & tandem loquitur de æternis præmiis piorum, & perpetuis impiorum suppliciis. Hæc ita se habere ἐξήγησις & vindiciæ docebunt. Dixerat se exultaturum in Hierusalem, nihil no- xii futurum in monte suo sancto: Ne quis terre- nam urbem aut montem Sion, ac templum mate- riale cogitaret, protestatus DEUS sese non ha- bitare in domo terrena, nullum habere locum re- quietionis, sed cor contritum in sedem suam & habitaculum eligere. Quo ipso tollitur plane differentia Veteris & Novi Testamenti. Nam sub illo in tabernaculo, & in templo elegerat DEUS habitare, ibique peculiariter coli volebat. Sed nunc, quæ, inquit, est ista domus, quam ædifica- bitis mihi, & quis est iste locus requietionis meæ? Quia futurum erat sub Novo Testamento, ut non in templo vel in monte adorarent veri adoratores, sed ubique Deum in spiritu & veritate adoraturi erant, Johan. 4,23.ubique per totum orbem sanctas manus elaturi erant 1. Timoth. 2. vers. 8. Ideo Pro- tomartyr post adventum Christi ac prædictionem eversionis finalis templi Hierosolymitani, quam non tantum Christus, sed etiam Stephanus immi- nere testatus Actor. 6. v. 14. hoc oraculo usus est, ut demonstraret prædictum fuisse à Propheta, DEUM nolle deinceps cultum suum adstrictum ad certum locum, adeoque οἰκονομίαν illam cultus Levitici antiqui sublatum iri Actor. 7. vers. 49. Un- de minime obscurum est,quum in apologia sua de eversione Templi, ad Esaiæ præsens vaticinium provocarit S. Stephanus, quin id concernat tem- pus novissimum politiæ Judaicæ, nec nisi perver- sa ratione abripiatur ad tempora Antiochi, quibus utique templum non eversum, sed conservatum fuit, nec nisi per triennium sub profana manu hæ- fit. Ideoque de reædificatione Templi cogitare opus non habebant Judæi. At cum Christus & Protomartyr totalem & finalem eversionem præ- dixerit, quod nunquam iterum ædificandum sit,& loco apologias prædictionem similem à Propheta factam adhibuerit, quæ pariter sedem requietionis Domini prorsus sublatum iri, nullamque aliam habitationem DEUM habitaturum, nisi pecto- ris contriti, & obsequentis, manifestum est, de tem- poribus hæc prædicta esse Novi Testamenti, nul- latenus autem retrahi posse ad tempora Judæ Mac- cabæi, quib9 repurgandum erat & cultui divino ite- rum consecrandum, post quæ ultra duo secula ad- huc stetit templum Domini & sedes fuit cultus di- vini. Cyrillus tradit hanc συνέχειαν: Cum abunde sermonem suum ad gentes pertexuerit, mystagogiam ad ipsum jam Israëlem convertit. Vult enim eos à le- gali etiam umbra desciscere, sicut videlicet illos quo- que jussit, à pristino errore, seductione & profana vita recedere. Aperte itaque docet, se spiritualem potius cultum æstimare & curare: umbratilem & ty- picum nihili æstimare. Recte itaque B. Hierony- mus ad hæc verba: HÆC DICIT DOMINUS COELUM SEDES MEA &c. Ne montem sanctum intelligeremus Sion, & Judaico operiremur errore, qui putant extruendam Hierusalem, & omnia quæ pollicetur ibi, explenda carnaliter, aufert nobis hanc suspicionem, & ponit Testimonium, quo usus est Stephanus martyr in Christo, adversum Judaicam contentionem: Salomon ædificavit ei domum, haud dubium quin Deo, sed non in manufactis excelsus ha- bitat, sicut Propheta ait: cœlum mihi thronus est, terra autem scabellum pedum meorum. Et Pau- lus in eodem volumine: Deus qui fecit mundum & qui in eo sunt, nequaquam in templis manufactis habitat. Si enim instar sedentis in solio atque re- gnantis cælum thronus ejus est, & terra scabellum pedum illius: Qui parvo claudetur loco, qui com- plet omnia? Unde & Moyses: Ne dicas, inquit, in corde tuo, longe est: Deus enim in cœlo sursum & super terram deorsum, & non est alius præter eum Deus. Et Psalmista: Quo ibo à Spiritu tuo, & à facie tua quo fugiam? Si adscendero in cœlum, illic es, si ad inferna descendero, ades. Cui & Hie- remias ex persona Dei congruit, dicens: Deus ap- propinquans ego & non de longe Deus. Num- quid latere quis poterit in absconditis, & ego non videbo eum? Nonne cœlum & terram ego impleo? In ipso enim omnes sumus & movemur, qui pu- tant invisibilem & incorporalem & incomprehensibi- lem Deum templo Hierusalem posse concludi? Quod quidem & ipse Salomon exstructor templi in oratione sua ad Dominum prolixius confitetur, &c.

Ac ne arbitremur cælo quoque & terra DEI magnitudinem metiendam, in alio loco de eo legimus: Qui tenet cœlum palmo & terram pugillo. Per quæ ostenditur Deus & forinsecus & intrinsecus & infusus & circumfusus, dum & solio ambiente non concluditur, & pugillo concludit ac palmo. Qui non solum cæli & terræ, sed invisibilium creator est, angelorum, & archangelorum, dominationum, pote- statum, & cunctorum hominum, de quibus Apostolus loquitur: Quæ omnia Dei manus operata est. De qua & Job & Psalmista commemorant: Manus tua fecit me & plasmavit me. Omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt, & sine ipso factum est nihil. De quo rursum Johannes: In mundo, ait, erat, & mun- dus per ipsum factus est. Ipse enim dixit & facta sunt, ipse mandavit & creata sunt. Et hoc quod Scriptura Geneseos mystico sermone demonstrat: Di- xit Deus & fecit Deus. Verbo enim Domini cœ- li firmati sunt & spiritu oris ejus omnis virtus eo- rum. Nullusq; locus est requietionis Domini, nisi iste quem Propheta subnectit: AD QUEM AU- TEM RESPICIAM &c. Consonat B. Luthe- rus ita demonstrans connexionem: Hactenus au- distis Prophetam versatum esse in reprehendendis stu- diis nostris & electitiis cultibus, qui sine verbo à su- perstitiosis Idololatris erant instituti. Accusavit enim Gad & Meni. Jam nova accusatio & multo gravior quam superior fuit, sequitur, in qua non re- prehendit electitium cultum, sed cultum divinitus in- stitutum & præceptum. Item templum ædificatum non humana cogitatione, sed promissione divina. Si- cut primo Davidi promissio illa est facta. Post vastato populo & templo per Babylonios repetita est. Propheta igitur hic jugulum Synagogæ petit, cum etiam ea tanquam flagitiosa & abominabilia coram Deo damnat, quæ verbo Dei erant constituta & ipsas promissiones divinas, qualis est illa Hag. 2. Implebo domum meam gloria, & similes. His enim promis- sionibus inflati Judæi summam fiduciam habebant, quod non solum placerent cultus isti Deo, sed quod es- sent perpetui futuri. Contra Propheta eos ridet & damnat. Quare sine dubio hæc Prophetia principa- lis Articulus fuit, cum medium dissecari Esaiam po- pulus jusserit. Sicut etiam in Actis videmus. Post- quam Stephanus allegat sententiam, quam initio ca- pitis hic ponit, sequitur horribilis clamor Judæorum, accusantium eum tanquam blasphemum contra tem- plum, locum, legem & populum. Et hæc crimina intendebant ei cum optima conscientia, quare obtu- ratis auribus ne audire quidem Stephanum volebant, sed acceptis lapidibus eum neci dederunt. Brentius etiam dignus est, qui hic audiatur: Vides, inquit, statim in principio hujus concionis Filii Dei rejici & abrogari templum. Quid ita? annon fuit divino mandato institutum? annon fuit miraculis de cælo sanctificatum? Recte, sed non in eum usum, quem im- pii & impœnitentes Judei somniabant. In institu- endo enim templo Hierosolymitano consilium DEI fuit, ut alligaret, non quidem perpetuo, sed usque ad adventum Christi in carne, Ecclesiam suam ad cer- tum locum, & ad certa sacra, quibus conservaretur vera doctrina de Lege, de Messia aut Christo, & de Regno Christi ac propagaretur ad posteros, ut populus lege & Evangelio eruditus, ageret pœnitentiam, cre- deret in Christum peccati expiatorem, invocaret Deum ex vera fide in Christum, & ambularet in vo- catione Dei: donec ex hoc mundo ad hæreditatem cælestis Regni reipsa percipiendam evocaretur. Hy- pocritæ autem & impii Judæi, nihil minus agebant, quam ut darent operam cognoscendæ legi & agno- scendo Christum per fidem, sed potius perseque- bantur eos, qui hanc salutarem & necessariam do- ctrinam urgebant: & cum nec ullam agerent pœ- nitentiam, ne bona opera in Decalogo, præsertim de vera fiducia in Deum, de vera invocatione Dei, & de vera dilectione proximi præcepta sectaren- tur, sperabant tamen & jactabant, se justitiam & sa- lutem cultu & sacris hujus templi consequi. Unde & cum Hieremias minaretur eis devastationem, propter impietatem & impœnitentiam, vocifera- bantur & iterabant, Templum Domini, Templum Domini &c. significantes se satis tutos esse ab im- minentibus malis, propter templum & sacra ejus, etiamsi alioqui omni genere vitiorum sordidati essent, & nullam prorsus pœnitentiam agerent. Sentiebant enim Deum huic Templo, & sacris e- jus ita intelligatum, ut non posset ea deserere & po- pulum hujus templi, & sacrorum ejus cultorem abjicere. Etsi autem Salomon jam ante in dedi- catione hujus templi damnaverat istam senten- tiam & impietatem: Ergone (inquiens) putan- dum est, quod vere Deus habitet super terram? Si enim cælum & cæli cælorum te capere non possunt, quanto minus domus hæc, quam ædifi- cavi tibi? tamen impii impœnitentes hæc di- cta surdis auribus transibant. Quare Filius DEI suscipit per Esaiam sententiam Salomo- nis, imo Spiritus Sancti repetendam, & impi- am opinionem hypocritarum de templo refutan- dam: ut exponat causam, cur templum merito una cum populo suo dejiciatur. Hæc è tota συν- νεχείᾳ Prophetæ elucent; nec minus è scopo apo- logiæ Protomartyris, nihil autem cum commento Grotii commune habent. Ad tempora No- vi Testamenti hæc pertinere Grotius ipse, quum nondum aures præbuisset commentis recentio- rum Judæorum, professus est lib. V. de verit. Re- lig. Christ. §. 8. ex hoc loco probans, quia scil. Esaias futurum ait, ut longissime dissiti, & o- mnium sermonum populi non minus, quam Israëlitæ munera Deo offerant, & ex ipsis quo- que constituantur, qui sint Sacerdotes, & Levi- tæ, quæ omnia, stante Mosis lege fieri non poterant.

Vers. eod. AD QVEM AVTEM RESPICIAM?) Jam venit ad sacrificia, quæ dicit ita sibi aut grata ut ingrata esse, prout est vita & animus offerentis. NISI AD PAVPERCVLVM) עני τὸν ταπεινὸν, ut vertunt hic LXX. id est, modeste de se sentientem. At Chal- dæus ענו mansuetum. Sæpe hæ voces ejusdem originis & vicini significatus inter se permiscentur. ET CONTRITVM SPIRITV) Pœnitentiam agen- tem peccatorum, ut in Ps. 51, 19. ET TREMENTEM SERMONES MEOS) Metuen- tem in leges meas impingere. Hæc ita edisserit Hieronymus: Sublato al- tari, temploque terreno, quod humana construxerat manus, recte auferuntur & victimæ Judæorum, ne forsitan dicerent: Non tam stulti sumus, ut putemus Deum loco posse concludi, sed in separato ad sacrifi- candum loco Deo victimas immolamus, quæ lege præ- cepta sunt. Habitator igitur cæli, imo creator omnium, qui in terris templum habere se denegat, humilem & quietum, & trementem sermones suos hominem li- benter assumit in templum. Juxta illud Apostoli: Vos autem estis templum DEI, & Spiritus San- ctus habitat in vobis. Si quis violat templum Dei, violabit illum Deus. Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos. Quicunque ergo humilis est & quietus, & tremens sermones Dei,ipsum respicit Do- minus. Pulchre autem de hoc habitaculo B. Lu- therus. Hic exponit, ubi velit Deus habitare, quæ ve- ra ejus sit officina, in qua Deus solet opus suum facere, nempe spiritus contritus. Ergo cum sentitur tristi- tia Spiritus & contritum cor, debeamus gaudere & lætari; sed majora sunt hæc, quam ut ab animo huma- no possint credi, tum, cum est in tentatione. Quid enim sunt ad contritum cor omnia palatia mundi, imo cælum & terra, siquidem sedes est divinæ maje- statis? Sic in Psalmo: Prope est Dominus affli- ctis, & contritos spiritu liberabit. Item, Multæ sunt afflictiones justi, sed ex iis omnibus eripit eum Dominus. Non enim potest venire ad cognitio- nem Christi, si per afflictiones, & quando aliquis est afflictus, tunc demum est locus, tempus & spatium ju- vandi. Sunt enim afflictiones vera materia, & nihil illud, ex quo Deus aliquid solet facere, Deus enim in materia privativa, non positiva operatur. Quia autem Propheta hic loquitur de justificatione, non in- telligit corporales afflictiones, sed sensum peccati, mor- tis & conscientiæ. Rejicit igitur maxima merita, scilicet Templum & commendat nobis vitam sine Le- ge, offert suam faciem immeritis & indignis, qui non justitiam, sed peccatum, non pacem, sed terrores con- scientiæ sentiunt. Ne ergo desperemus, ubi in pecca- ta & graves errores inciderimus, sed hujusmodi conso- lationibus erecti credamus tum, cum minime senti- timus, Deum ad nos respicere, adesse & favere nobis &c. Neque negligenda paraphrasis Brentiana: Nihil aliud dicitur, quam quod Deus respiciat eos, qui agnoscunt peccata sua & credunt Evangelio Christi. Nam afflicto & contrito spiritu hi sunt, qui territi agnitione & judicio peccati, intelligunt se obnoxios non morti tantum corporali, verum etiam perpetuæ in inferno damnationi. Sed hic additur: Respicio eum, qui contremiscit ad verbum meum. Non enim satis est, ut agnoscas peccatum tuum, & sis afflicto ac contrito spiritu: sed requi- ritur etiam, ut contremiscas; hoc est, magna cu- ra, magno studio, magna fide, magna fidei reve- rentia & obedientia suscipias verbum Dei. Hoc est autem verbum Evangelii, quod Deus Pater posuit in ore filii sui, & quod Filius conciona- tus est: videlicet, quod ipse solus sit peccati ex- piator & justificator noster. Hoc verbum susci- piendum est cum timore & tremore, ac summa reverentia & obedientia. Quare, qui sic agnoscit peccatum suum, & sic est contrito spiritu propter peccatum, ut etiam credat Evangelio Christi, & amplectatur ipsum reverenti fide: Is tale tem- plum & talis domus efficitur, ut DEUS eum ex alto respiciat, & quemadmodum CHRISTUS ait, Pater diliget eum & ad eum veniemus & man- sionem apud eum faciemus.

## 66:3
Verse 3.

HE WHO SACRIFICES AN OX AS IF HE WERE KILLING A MAN) One must understand 'otherwise': that is, if these virtues are absent, I abhor the victims, as if it were homicide: which God so execrates that he wishes even a murderer to be dragged away from his altar. Exod. 21, 14. Pythagoras: The sacrifices of the foolish are food for the fire.

HE WHO SLAUGHTERS A BEAST, AS ONE WHO BEHEADS A DOG) In the Hebrew: As if someone were to behead a dog, namely for sacrificing. A dog is so vile an animal to the Hebrews that not even its price could be received in the temple. See what was said at Deut. 23, 18.

HE WHO OFFERS AN OBLATION) מנחה, namely a cake of fine flour: σεμίδαλιν here [in the] LXX.

AS ONE WHO OFFERS SWINE'S BLOOD) Which is doubly illicit, both because a pig is unclean by law, and because all blood is to be poured out, not offered. Exod. 23, 18.

HE WHO REMEMBERS INCENSE, AS ONE WHO BLESSES AN IDOL) He who remembers me through incense as if he were speaking praises and thanks to an idol. Thus the LXX also took it: he who gives incense as a memorial. But the Chaldean reads אָוֶן for אוֹן; for he translates it as rapine.

ALL THESE THINGS THEY CHOSE IN THEIR WAYS) Namely, certain of the Hebrews, such as Jason, who bought the high priesthood for himself for a price from Antiochus, having cast out his brother Onias, an excellent High Priest: then Menelaus, who in like manner drove out Jason, but killed Onias, and substituted for himself as successor Lysimachus, a plunderer of the sacred treasury.

Verse of the same.

AND IN THEIR ABOMINATIONS THEIR SOUL HAS DELIGHTED) In violence, slaughters, rapines.

In the explanation there is no difficulty. But in the application to Jason, Menelaus, Lysimachus, as if the Prophet here had regard to those times and those persons, Grotius is mistaken: because there is no trace of that thing here, nay, all things convince that he looks to the most recent times of the Jewish people. We add again the exposition of Jerome. What follows in the Vulgate edition (the Greek of the LXX Interpreters) BUT THE WICKED (He who sacrifices a calf, etc.) is not had in the Hebrew, but it joins simply and says; He who sacrifices an ox, as one who kills a man. Which is also written in another place: I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. And through Malachi: You were doing all things that I hated, covering my altar with tears: is it worthy that I should look to your sacrifice and receive anything acceptable from your hands? Let the Jews hear that GOD does not seek sacrifices but the mind of those who offer. And he who slaughters, he says, cattle, as one who brains a dog. Whence also it is written through Moses: You shall not offer the hire of a harlot, nor the price of a dog in the house of your GOD. And beautifully are the dog and the harlot coupled: because each animal is prone to lust. And let us consider at the same time, that he did not say: He who sacrifices a ram, as one who sacrifices a dog, but he says, kills a dog. Which word is not placed in sacrifices, but in those things which are slaughtered illicitly.

He who offers an oblation and sacrifice is as one who offers swine’s blood. This also was forbidden by the law. Such are the ceremonies of the Jews. He who gives incense is as though he were a blasphemer, indeed as though blessing an idol. But the sense may also be this: after my Son, who came meek and poor, sitting upon the foal of an ass, I do not desire flesh, I detest the victims, I reject the sacrifices of the Jews, I disapprove the shadows of the Law, because the truth of the Gospel is pleasant to me. If this is being said, that after the lightning flash of the Gospel the old religion should be in a cloud, what will those answer who, believing out of the Jews, suppose that they can carnally offer sacrifices without harm to themselves?

THEY HAVE CHOSEN ALL THESE THINGS IN THEIR WAYS, AND THEIR SOUL HAS DELIGHTED IN THEIR ABOMINATIONS.

To slaughter a bull, to kill a ram, to offer sacrifice, to burn incense—things which God holds as if homicide and the offering of a dog and swine’s blood and blasphemy—they themselves have chosen, and it was of their own will that they cultivated such things. According to what he says through Ezekiel: “I gave them not good justifications, and not good precepts,” and, he says, “they walked in their ways, not in the way of the Lord.”

And their soul desired their abominations, that they might be lovers of themselves rather than lovers of God.

Brentius unfolds these things in a fuller and more lucid style: he had previously rejected the temple; now he also rejects the temple rites. And he compares the most holy rites of the Jews with the most impious abominations of the Gentiles. For the Gentiles were accustomed, in their greatest dangers, to sacrifice innocent men; they hoped that these sacrifices would be expiations of heavenly wrath. At other times they sacrificed dogs, swine, and other unclean beasts, and thus extolled their vain idols with praises, from whom also they expected every blessing. These things were in the eyes of the Church of the Jews execrable and horrid rites. In the Maccabees altars are set up in Jerusalem, idols are established, swine and other unclean animals are sacrificed: these things were in the eyes of the pious such an abomination that some, leaving everything, would set out into exile; others would rather die than do such execrable rites.

And yet the Holy Spirit here compares the best rites of the temple with those most profane rites of the Gentiles, and equates them in impiety. He who slaughters or sacrifices, he says, a bull does no better than he who among the heathen kills a man or sacrifices an innocent human being. He who kills cattle, namely a sheep or a goat, which according to the law of God it was permitted to offer, acts no more rightly than he who offers a dog in sacrifice, which is a sacrifice execrable before God. He who offers a Minha or grain sacrifice does no other worship to God than he who offers swine’s blood. He who burns incense to God does just as if he were burning it to a vain idol. But were not sacrifices of bulls and sheep and grain offerings and incense not only permitted by the divine law, but even prescribed and commended? I ask you therefore, what is it that these truly divine rites are here equated with the execrable and horrid rites of the Gentiles? What the cause of this matter is is immediately added: “All these things they have chosen in their ways, and their soul delighted in their abominations.” And soon after: “I called and there was no one who answered; I spoke, and they did not hear; and they did evil in my sight, and what I willed not they chose.” You have the cause why the Jewish rites, though instituted by God, are equated with the impieties of the Gentiles.

For in the first place the Gentiles performed their rites without the true fear of God and without true repentance. “They do” (says Paul) “the things which are not fitting, being filled with all iniquity, fornication, craftiness, greed,” etc. For, as they were before the performance of their rites defiled with every kind of crime, so also they remained after their performance, and there was in them no care for true piety before GOD, nor for sincere innocence before men. So also the Jews performed their rites without the true fear of God and without true repentance. “Thou that teachest another” (says Paul to the Jews) “dost not teach thyself. Thou that preachest that one should not steal, dost steal; thou that sayest one should not commit adultery ..., dost commit adultery,” etc. Therefore, although the rites of the Gentiles and of the Jews differed in outward appearance, yet because they agreed in the impenitence of the worshippers, they are rightly and aptly equated with one another.

Then, the Gentiles had indeed received the rite of sacrificing from the Patriarchs, but they had not retained the word and faith of the Patriarchs; but they had changed the rites, and sacrificed unclean animals, sometimes even men; and this without any faith in the remission of sins to be received on account of the seed of Abraham, that is, Jesus Christ; but rather with this opinion, that these works of sacrifices were merits by which they might expiate their sins, and appease the heavenly wrath, and obtain righteousness and salvation. So also the Jews, although their rites were divinely instituted, yet they did not perform those rites, nor with the use for which they were instituted, nor with the faith which they required and to which they looked.

This is that which the Prophet says: “They have chosen these things in their ways, and their soul has delighted in their abominations.” For the way of the Lord in these Levitical sacrifices was this, that it shadowed forth the sacrifice of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which alone the heavenly wrath is appeased, and that he wished by these to admonish the worshippers of faith in Christ, that believing in him they might be justified and saved. This was the legitimate and true use of the Levitical sacrifices. This was the way and counsel of the Lord in instituting and commending these sacrifices. But the Jews, despising this use and neglecting this way, fashioned a far different use and followed another way and other counsels. For they felt that sacrifices were, from the very action of the works, or as they say, ex opere operato, expiations of sins and appeasements of heavenly wrath. And so, when they were contaminated with every kind of impiety and crime, they heaped up sacrifices, that by their merit they might be justified before God and saved. But if they were called to the amendment of life and to faith in Christ by the Prophets and Apostles, they not only did not obey this doctrine, but even persecuted it. And as in this place the Son of God says: “I called and there was no one who answered. I spoke and they did not hear,” etc.

This was their way, which they followed while despising the way of God. These were the abominations in which their soul delighted.

From which it is most manifest in what sense the rites of the Jews are compared with the rites of the Gentiles, and that these are by no means to be referred to the times of Antiochus and the corporal profanation of the rites and to the times of Christ and the perverse opinion of the Jews concerning external sacrifices.

Nor does the Prophet indeed say that the Jews sacrifice men or disembowel dogs, or offer swine’s blood, or bless an idol. But that they are SIMILAR to them. Whence it cannot be distorted to those unclean external offerings in the time of the Maccabees, when idols were instituted, swine’s flesh offered, and other unclean animals offered. If you say that the sacrifices of the Jews in the most recent time are indicated as SIMILAR to such sacrifices made at that time, you will not wander from the truth. For the words of the Prophet demand this.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

QVI IMMOLAT BOVEM QVASI INTERFI- CIAT VIRVM) Subaudiendum alioqui: id est, si istæ virtutes absint, abominor victimas, quasi homicidium: quod Deus ita exsecratur, ut etiam ab altari suo homici- dam velit abstrahi. Exod. 21, 14. Pythagoras: θυηπολίαι ἀφρόνων, πυρὸς τροφή.

QVI MACTAT PECVS, QVASI QVI EXCE- REBRET CANEM) In Hebræo: Quasi si quis decollet canem nempe ad sacrificandum. Canis ita vile Hebræis animal, ut ne pretium quidem ejus in templo recipi posset. Vide quæ dicta ad Deut. 23, 18.

QVI OFFERT OBLATIONEM) מנחה, nempe libum ex simila: σεμίδαλιν hic LXX.

QVASI QVI SANGVINEM SVILLVM OFFE- RAT) Quod dupliciter illicitum, & quia sus immunda lege, & quia sanguis omnis effundendus, non offeren- dus. Exod. 23, 18.

QVI RECORDATVR THVRIS, QVASI QVI BENEDICAT IDOLO) Qui mei recordatur per thus qua- si idolo laudes ac gratias diceret. Sic sumsere & LXX. ὁ διδοὺς λίβανον εἰς μνημόσυνον. At Chaldæus pro אוֹן legit אָוֶן; ver- tit enim rapinam.

HÆC OMNIA ELEGERVNT IN VIIS SVIS) Nempe Hebræorum quidam, qualis Jason, qui pontifica- tum sibi pretio mercatus est ab Antiocho, dejecto fratre suo Onia Pontifice optimo: deinde Menelaus, qui pari mo- do Jasonem expulit, Oniam autem interfecit, successorem que sibi substituit Lysimachum sacri ærarii expilatorem.

Vers. eod.

ET IN ABOMINATIONIBVS SVIS ANIMA EORVM DELECTATA EST) In vi, cædibus, rapi- nis.

In Explicatione nulla difficultas. Sed in applicatione ad Jasonem, Menelaum, Lysima- chum, ac si ista tempora, & istas personas hic respexerit Propheta, fallitur Grotius: quia e- jus rei nullum hic vestigium, imo ad novissima populi Judaici eum respicere tempora omnia con- vincunt. Addimus iterum Hieronymi exposi- tionem. Quod sequitur in editione Vulgata (Græca LXX. Interpp.) INIQUUS AUTEM (Qui immolat vitulum &c.) in Hebraico non ha- betur, sed simpliciter jungit & dicit; Qui immolat bovem, quasi qui interficiat hominem. Quod & in alio scriptum est loco: Misericordiam volo & non sacrificium, scientiam magis Dei quam ho- locaustum. Et per Malachiam: Omnia quæ ode- ram faciebatis, operientes lacrymis altare meum: numquid dignum est, ut respiciam ad sacrificium vestrum & suscipiam placabile quid de manibus vestris? Audiant Judæi, quod DEUS non quærat sacrificia sed offerentium animum. Et qui ma- ctat, inquit, pecus, quasi qui excerebret canem. Unde & per Moysen scriptum est: Non offeres mercedem meretricis, neque pretium canis in domo DEI tui. Pulchreque canis & mere- trix copulantur: quia utrumque animal pronum est ad libidinem. Simulg; consideremus, quod non dixerit: Qui immolat arietem, quasi qui immolat canem, sed occidat, inquit, canem. Quod verbum non poni- tur in sacrificiis, sed in his quæ trucidantur illicite.

Qui offert oblationem & sacrificium, quasi qui sanguinem suillum offerat. Quod & ipsum lege prohibebatur. Tales sunt ceremonie Judaeorum. Qui thus tribuit, quasi blasphemus, imo quasi benedicens idolo. Potest autem & hic esse sensus: Post filium meum, qui venit mansuetus & pauper, sedens super pullum asinae, nolo carnes, detestor victimas, sacrificia Judaeorum, umbras Legis reprobo, quia delectabilis mihi est veritas Evangelii. Si autem hoc dicitur, quod post fulgur Evangelii vetus religio esset in nube: Quid respondebunt, qui credentes ex Judaeis arbitrantur absque noxa sui posse carnaliter offerre sacrificia?

HAEC OMNIA ELEGERUNT IN VIIS SUIS: ET IN ABOMINATIONIBUS SVIS ANIMA EORUM DELECTATA EST.

Immolare bovem, mactare arietem, offerre sacrificium, thus succendere, quae ita habet Deus, quasi homicidium & oblationem canis & suillum sanguinem atque blasphemiam, ipsi elegerunt, & ut talia colerent, eorum arbitrii fuit. Juxta quod dicit per Ezechiel: Dedi eorum justificationes non bonas, & praecepta non bona, & in viis, inquit, suis ambulaverunt, non in via Domini.

Et abominationes suas anima eorum voluit, ut amatores magis essent sui, quam amatores Dei.

Pleniori ac luculentiori stilo haec deducit Brentius: Rejicit antea templum: nunc rejicit etiam sacra templi. Et confert sanctissima Judaeorum sacra cum impiissimis Gentium abominationibus. Gentes enim in summis periculis suis solebant sacrificare homines innocentes: quae sacrificia sperabant esse coelestis irae piacula. Alias sacrificabant canes, sues, & alias immundas bestias, adeoque laudibus efferebant vana sua idola, à quibus etiam omnem benedictionem expectabant. Haec fuerunt in oculis Ecclesiae Judaeorum execranda & horribilia sacra. In Machabaeis aedificantur Hierosolymis arae, instituuntur idola, immolantur sues & alia immunda pecora: Haec fuerunt in oculis piorum tantae abominationi, ut alii relictis omnibus proficiscerentur in exilium, alii mallent mori, quam tam execranda sacera facere. Et tamen Spiritus Sanctus confert hic optima sacra templi cum profanissimis illis sacris Gentium & aequat ea in impietate. Qui immolat aut sacrificat (inquit) bovem, nihil melius facit, quam qui inter ethnicos occidit virum seu sacrificat hominem innocentem. Qui mactat pecus, videlicet ovem aut capram, quae juxta Legem Dei offerre licuit, nihilo rectius agit, quam qui offert in sacrificium canem: quod est sacrificium coram Deo execrabile. Qui offert Mincha seu sacrificium farinarium, non alium cultum praestat DEO, quam qui offert sanguinem suillum. Qui adolet thus Deo, perinde facit ac si adolet ea vano idolo.

Sed annon sacrificia boum & ovium & immolationes farinariae, ac thymiamata fuerunt divina lege non solum permissa, sed etiam praescripta & commendata? Quaeso igitur te, quid est, quod hi cultus vere divini aequantur hic execrandis & horrendis gentium? Quae sit hujus rei causa, statim additur: Haec omnia (inquit) elegerunt in viis suis, & in abominationibus suis delectata est anima eorum. Et mox: Vocavi & non erat qui responderet, locutus sum, & non audierunt, feceruntque malum in oculis meis, & quae nolui, elegerunt: Habes causam, cur Judaeorum sacra, quamvis divinitus instituta, aequentur impietatibus Gentium. Primum enim Gentes faciebant sacra sua sine vero timore Dei & sine vera poenitentia. Faciunt (inquit Paulus) quae non conveniunt, repleti omni iniquitate, scortatione, versutia, avaritia &c. Quales enim erant ante sacrorum suorum peractionem sordidati omni genere scelerum, tales etiam manebant post eorum peractionem, nec ulla erat eis cura vera coram DEO pietatis, & sincera coram hominibus innocentiae.

Sic & Judaei faciebant sua sacra sine vero Dei timore & sine vera poenitentia. Qui doces alium (inquit Paulus ad Judaeos) te ipsum non doces. Qui praedicas non furandum, furaris: qui dicis non adulterandum ..., adulterium committis &c. Quare, etsi Gentium & Judaeorum sacra differebant externa specie: tamen quia conveniebant cultorum impoenitentia, recte & apte inter se aequantur.

Deinde gentes acceperant quidem sacrificandi ritum à Patriarchis: non retinuerant autem verbum & fidem Patriarcharum: sed mutaverant ritus, & sacrificarant immunda animalia, aliquoties etiam homines: idque fine ulla fide accipiendae remissionis peccatorum propter semen Abrahae, hoc est, Jesum Christum: sed potius cum hac opinione, quod haec sacrificiorum opera essent merita, quibus expiarent peccata sua, & placarent coelestem iram, ac consequerentur justitiam & salutem. Sic & Judaei, etsi sacra eorum erant divinitus instituta: tamen non faciebant illa sacra, nec eo usu, quo erant instituta, nec ea fide, quam exigebant, & quo respiciebant.

Hoc illud est, quod Propheta dicit: Elegerunt haec in viis suis & in abominationibus suis delectata est anima eorum. Via enim Domini in his sacrificiis Leviticis haec erat, quod adumbraverit his sacrificium Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quo solo placatur coelestis ira: & quod voluerit his cultores admonere de fide in Christum, ut in hunc credentes justificarentur & servarentur. Hic fuit legitimus & verus usus Leviticorum sacrificiorum. Haec fuit via & consilium Domini, in instituendis & commendandis his sacrificiis. Judaei autem contempo hoc usu, & neglecta hac via, fingebant longe alium usum, & sequebantur aliam viam & alia consilia. Sentiebant enim, sacrificia esse ex ipsa operum actione, seu ut isti loquuntur, ex opere operato, expiationes peccatorum & placationes irae coelestis. Itaque cum essent omni impietatis & scelerum genere contaminati, cumulabant sacrificiis, ut horum merito justificarentur coram Deo & servarentur. Quod si ad emendationem vitae & ad fidem in Christum per Prophetas & Apostolos vocabantur: ibi tum non solum non obsequebantur huic doctrinae, verum etiam persequebantur eam. Et sicut hoc loco filius Dei dicit: Vocavi & non erat qui responderet. Locutus sum & non audierunt &c.

Haec fuit via ipsorum, quam contempta via Dei sectabantur. Hae fuerunt abominationes, quibus delectata est anima eorum.

E quibus manifestissimum est, quo sensu comparentur sacra Judaeorum cum sacris gentilium, quodque haec referenda minime sint ad tempora Antiochi & corporalem sacrorum prophanationem & ad tempora Christi & perversam sententiam Judaeorum de externis sacrificiis.

Neque vero Propheta dicit Judaeos homines immolare aut canes excerebrare, aut sanguinem suillum offerre, aut idolum benedicere. Sed illis SIMILIA esse. Unde non posse ad oblationes illas immundas externas hoc detorqueri tempore Maccabaeorum: cum idola instituta, carnes suillae oblatae, alia immunda pecora oblata. Talibus oblationibus isto tempore factis SIMILIA sacrificia Judaeorum tempore novissimo si dixeris indicari, à vero non aberrabis. Id enim verba Prophetae poscunt.

## 66:4
Verse 4.

AND I ALSO WILL CHOOSE THEIR DELUSIONS, AND WILL BRING UPON THEM THE THINGS THEY FEARED) Neither Jason nor Menelaus will retain the purchased high priesthood: Lysimachus will perish in the very crime: Jason and Menelaus will stir up arms against each other. 2 Macc. 4 & 5.

What, I pray, does this prophecy have to do with the high priesthood of Jason and Menelaus, or their mutual gladiatorial combats? What does it have to do with the death of Lysimachus? It is not the destruction of the people by deceivers that is predicted, but the deceivers are said to be chosen, by whom the people are to be punished. Namely, those who rejected Christ speaking to them, and chose the things He did not want. Therefore, God chooses their deceivers for their own destruction. For which reason, says Jerome, since they chose their own ways, and not Him who says: I am the way, and the Lord, He chose their delusions or deceivers, which are called in Hebrew תעלולי, that is, ἐμπαίκτας [mockers], so that He might appoint the worst princes, and bring upon them all their evils, or the things they feared, in like manner. And he gives the reasons why they were handed over to the scribes and Pharisees, their deceivers, of whom the first Psalm sings according to the Hebrews: And he has not sat in the chair of the scornful, whom the LXX call pestilent, such as were the sons of Eli, sons of pestilence, for which in the Hebrew it is written: בליער, that is, of the devil. Because, he says, I called, and there was no one to answer, I spoke, and they did not hear, and they did evil in my eyes, and chose the things I did not want. Which verses he places second in the present passage and above where it is said: I will number you in the sword, and you shall all fall in the slaughter. Because I called and you did not answer: and the rest similarly. In what sense that testimony ought to be accepted, has been said there. So also Cyril. Again he adorns an apology, and openly gives the reason why Israel was rejected, however much he was called the firstborn, and named the portion of God. For they chose, he says, their ways, and their abominations, which their soul desired, when he says: They chose, he declares them to be judges not upright in necessary matters, but rather to call good evil, and to turn darkness into light, and light into darkness, bitter into sweet, and sweet into bitter. AND I WILL CHOOSE THEIR MOCKERIES, that is, those who will mock, and rage against them. He designates, however, those who devastated Judea and burned the once holy and famous city, namely the Roman soldier. For I will repay, he says, their sins to them. For the things which I hate and did not want, they themselves chose.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

VNDE ET EGO ELIGAM ILLVSIONES EORVM, ET QVÆ TIMEBANT ADDVCAM EIS) Nec Jason, nec Menelaus retinebunt emptum pontificatum: Lysima- chus in ipso scelere interibit: Jason & Menelaus inter se movebunt arma. 2. Macc. 4. & 5.

Quid hæc Prophetia, obsecro, ad Jasonis & Menelai pontificatum, aut mutuas gladiationes? Quid ad Lysimachi interitum? Non illusoribus populi interitus prædicitur, sed illusores eligendi dicuntur, quibus puniatur populus. Qui sc. Chri- stum loquentem illis repudiarunt, & quæ ipse no- luit elegerunt. Ideo Deus eligit in ipsorum perni- ciem illusores ipsorum. Quam ob causam, in- quit Hieronymus, eligentibus illis vias suas, & non eum qui dicit: Ego sum via, & Dominus, elegit illu- siones sive illusores eorum, quæ Hebraice dicuntur תעלולי , id est, ἐμπαίκ[τ]ας, ut constituat principes pessimos, & omnia mala eorum, sive quæ timebant, pariter adducat. Causasque reddit, cur traditi sint scribis & Pharisæis illusoribus suis, de quibus pri- mus Psalmus juxta Hebræos canit: Et in cathedra illusorum non sedit, quos appellant LXX. pestilen- tes, quales fuerunt filii Heli, filii pestilentiæ, pro quo in Hebraico scriptum est: בליער, hoc est, diaboli. Quia, inquit, vocavi, & non erat qui responderet, locutus sum, & non audierunt, feceruntque malum in oculis meis, & quæ nolui, elegerunt, Quos ver- sus secundo ponit in præsenti loco & supra ubi dicitur: Numerabo vos in gladio, & omnes in cæde corrue- tis. Quia vocavi & non respondistis: & cætera similiter. Quod testimonium quo sensu accipi de- beat, ibi dictum est. Sic etiam Cyrillus. Rursus adornat apologiam, causamque aperte reddit, cur re- pudiatus fuerit Israël, quantumvis primogenitus di- ctus, & sors Dei nuncupatus. Elegerunt enim, in- quit, vias suas, & abominationes suas, quas anima ipsorum voluit, cum dicit: Elegerunt, declarat eos judices esse non rectos in rebus necessariis, sed potius dicere bonum malum, & vertere tenebras in lu- cem, & lucem in tenebras, amarum in dulce, & dul- ce in amarum. ET EGO ELIGAM LUDI- BRIA EORVM, id est, qui ludificent, ac in ipsos debacchentur. Designat autem eos, qui vastarunt Judæam & concremarunt sanctam quondam & cele- brem civitatem, nempe Romanum militem. Re- tribuam enim, inquit, illis peccata sua. Nam quæ ego odi & nolui, ipsi elegerunt.

## 66:5
Verse 5.

HEAR THE WORD OF THE LORD YOU WHO TREMBLE AT HIS WORD) You who were good men at that time; such as those who favored Onias.

YOUR BRETHREN SAID, HATING YOU) Those who were in the faction of Jason or Menelaus.

LET THE LORD BE GLORIFIED) That is, let Him do something great for your sake, if you are of such value to Him.

AND WE SHALL SEE IN YOUR JOY: BUT THEY SHALL BE CONFOUNDED) In the Hebrew: But He (namely God) shall be looked upon with your joy: but they shall be put to shame. What that may be now follows.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

AUDITE VERBUM DOMINI QUI TREMITIS AD VERBVM EJUS) Qui viri boni eritis illo tempore; ut qui Oniæ favebant.

DIXERUNT FRATRES VESTRI ODIEN- TES VOS) Isti qui in factione erant Jasonis aut Mene- lai.

GLORIFICETUR DOMINUS) Id est, faciat aliquid magni vestri causa, si tanti apud eum estis.

ET VIDEBIMUS IN LÆTITIA VESTRA: IPSI AUTEM CONFUNDENTUR) In Hebræo: At conspicie- tur (nempe Deus) cum gaudio vestro: illi autem pudefient. Id quid sit jam sequitur.

## 66:6
Verse 6.

A VOICE OF THE PEOPLE FROM THE CITY) I hear the ovation of Judas Maccabeus, and of his soldiers within the city abandoned by the soldiers of Antiochus and the impious Jews, who were of the party of Antiochus.

VOICE FROM THE TEMPLE) I hear those very same people in the Temple itself giving thanks to God for many victories.

VOICE OF THE LORD RENDERING RETRIBUTION TO HIS ENEMIES) God in those Psalms which they sing replies that He is now about to take vengeance upon those wicked Jews, some of whom fell by mutual slaughter, others by the hand of Judas Maccabeus. Such is Psalm 81, 89, v. 20 and following.

Mere distortions: Which agree neither with the context, nor the scope, nor finally the time of which the Prophet treats. It is manifest that he is addressing those whom he said look to God, trembling at the words of the Lord, such as were those from among the Jews who were about to believe in Christ, namely the Apostles and the rest of the primitive Christian Church: who, because by their conversion to Christ and confession of the Gospel they condemned the unbelief and impiety of their other brethren, endured most grievous afflictions from them. YOUR BRETHREN SAID, but falsely, HATING YOU AND CASTING YOU OUT FOR MY NAME'S SAKE, saying LET THE LORD BE GLORIFIED, may that God of yours, Christ, illustrate His majesty in saving you. AND WE SHALL SEE YOUR JOY, we shall look upon what He is about to do to refresh and gladden you, but be of good courage, says the Lord, you shall be delivered, but THEY (the mockers, or those who hate you) SHALL BE ASHAMED.

Their punishment is added, in the overthrow of the city, the temple, and the people, who had become an enemy and foe to the Lord Messiah. VOICE OF TUMULT FROM THE CITY, VOICE FROM THE TEMPLE, VOICE OF THE LORD RENDERING RETRIBUTION TO HIS ENEMIES. That is, as Osiander paraphrases with Brentius leading the way: All things at Jerusalem will be full of tumults and seditions, which will precede the final devastation of the city: A VOICE FROM THE TEMPLE will be heard, which will say: LET US DEPART HENCE: by which God will testify that He is about to depart from them, and will no longer defend either the city or the temple (Josephus testifies in Jewish War, book 7, ch. 12, that such a voice was heard before the final destruction of the city). THE VOICE OF THE LORD will be heard RENDERING RETRIBUTION TO HIS ENEMIES: the Lord will rebuke them, will threaten them, and will send destruction upon them. And it seems the Prophet in this place looked to that man (who without doubt was divinely impelled) who for several months went around Jerusalem, crying horribly: A voice from the east, a voice from the west, a voice from the four winds, etc. And: Woe to Jerusalem, etc., who could not be induced even by threats or blows to be silent, until he himself fell. See Josephus, Jewish War, book 7, ch. 12. Jerome had also rendered this sense. According to the Hebrew, the sense here seems to me to be: Hear, O Apostles, hear, O my disciples, who tremble at the word of the Lord: I will tell what your brethren have said, who hate and separate you and consider you strangers, not because of your evils, but because of my name: who consider all of their own race who believe in me to be unclean, and say, depart from me: for you are unclean. What then is it that he records them as having said? Let the Lord be glorified and we shall see your joy. The sense of this verse here is: Why do you introduce to us a humble God? Why a crucified one and a man of sorrows, and acquainted with infirmities? For we wish to see Him reigning in His (as you say) majesty: we shall look upon Him triumphing in His glory: we cannot see Him humble and cast down. And immediately he infers: but they themselves shall be ashamed: it is understood, those who speak such things, who do not understand the mysteries of the scriptures: and by their own evils they shall feel the power of Him whom they had despised for His humility. VOICE OF TUMULT FROM THE CITY. The Septuagint put CLAMOR for TUMULT, and the rest similarly (as in the Latin text) we wish to know what is the shame of the Jews, who said: Let the Lord be glorified, that we may see your joy, and contemplate the triumphs of your king, not by empty promises, but with our eyes. The voice (he says) of clamor from the city. There is no doubt that it signifies Jerusalem surrounded by the Roman army, and divided into three parts by internal sedition: when one obtained the temple, and possessed all things previously holy: fighting outwardly against enemies, and externally against citizens. At that time, both in the city and in the temple, the wailing of priests and Levites, as well as of the ignoble common people, women, and children, was heard: when the Lord rendered retribution to his enemies, fulfilling the threat with which he had said: Your house shall be left to you desolate. And that prophecy: I have forsaken my house: when the guardians of the temple said with a harmonious angelic voice: Let us depart from these seats. Concerning which not only Josephus, the writer of Jewish history, but the Psalmist many centuries before testifies, saying: I saw iniquity and contradiction, which surrounded its walls all day and all night: so that the city was overturned and another prophecy was fulfilled: Sion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be left as a hut in a cucumber patch. It is manifest that this is wrongly drawn by Grotius to the shouting voice.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

VOX POPULI DE CIVITATE) Audio ovatio- nem Judæ Maccabæi, & militum ejus intra urbem dereli- ctam ab Antiochi militibus & impiis Judæis, qui Antiochi erant partium.

VOX DE TEMPLO) Audio eosdem illos in ipso Templo Deo gratias agere de multis victoriis.

VOX DOMINI REDDENTIS RETRIBUTIO- NEM INIMICIS SUIS) Deus in illis Psalmis quos ca- nunt respondet jamjam ultionem se sumturum de illis ma- lis Judæis, quorum alii mutuis cædibus, alii manu Judæ Maccabæi conciderunt. Talis est Psalmus 81. 89. v. 20. & sequentes.

Meræ detorsiones: Quæ neque contextui, neque scopo, ne denique tempori, de quo agit Propheta, congruunt. Manifestum est, quod al- loquatur eos, quos respicere Deum dixit, tremen- tes sermones Domini, quales erant, qui ex Judæis credituri erant in Christum, utpote Apostoli & reliqui primitivæ Ecclesiæ Christianæ: qui quia conversio- ne sua ad Christum & confessione Evangelii aliorum suorum fratrum incredulitatem & impietatem da- mnarunt, gravissimas afflictiones ab ipsis sustinue- runt. DIXERUNT FRATRES VESTRI, sed falsi, ODIENTES VOS ET ABJICIENTES PROPTER NOMEN MEUM, dicentes GLORIFICETUR DOMINVS, ille Deus vester Christus illustret majestatem suam in vobis servan- dis. ET VIDEBIMUS IN LÆTITIA VE- STRA, aspicicmus, quod vos sit recreaturus & læti- ficaturus, sed bono animo estote, inquit Dominus, vos eripiemini, ISTI autem (illusores, vel odientes vos) CONFUNDENTUR.

Additur supplicium eorum, in eversione civi- tatis templi, & populi, qui factus erat Domino Mes- siæ hostis & inimicus. VOX FREMITUS DE CIVITATE, VOX DE TEMPLO, VOX DOMINI REDDENTIS RETRIBUTIO- NEM INIMICIS SUIS. Id est, ut recte præ- eunte Brentio παραφράζει Osiander: Omnia Hie- rosolymis plena erunt tumultibus & seditionibus, quæ præcedent ultimam urbis devastationem: VOX DE TEMPLO audietur, quæ dicet: MI- GREMUS HINC: qua Deus testabitur, se ab ipsis recessurum, nec amplius vel urbem vel tem- plum defensurum (talem vocem auditam esse ante novissimum urbis excidium, testatur Josephus de Bello Judaico, lib. 7. c. 12.) VOX DOMINI au- dietur REDDENTIS RETRIBUTIONEM INIMICIS SVIS: increpabit eos Dominus, mi- nitabitur illis & immittet illis interitum. Et vide- tur Propheta hoc loco respexisse ad illum virum (qui procul dubio divinitus impulsus) per aliquot menses Jerosolymis circuivit, horribiliter clamans: Vox ab oriente, vox ab occidente, vox à quatuor ven- tis &c. Et: Væ Jerusalem &c. qui etiam nec minis, nec plagis induci potuit, ut taceret, donec & ipse occubuit. Vide Joseph. de bello Jud. lib. 7. c. 12. Quem sensum etiam reddiderat Hieron. Iuxta He- braicum hic mihi sensus videtur: Audite Apostoli, audite discipuli mei, qui tremitis verbum Domini: narrabo quid dixerint fratres vestri, qui oderunt & separant vos & arbitrantur alienos, non propter mala vestra, sed propter nomen meum: qui immun- dos existimant cunctos de sua in me gente creden- tes, & dicunt, recede à me: quia immundus es. Quid ergo est, quod eos dixisse commemorat? glorificetur Dominus & videbimus in lætitia vestra. Cujus ver- siculi hic sensus est: Quid nobis humilem introducitis Deum? Quid crucifixum & virum dolorum, & sci- entem ferre infirmitates? Volumus enim in sua (ut di- citis) majestate conspicere regnantem: suspiciemus & in sua gloria triumphantem: humilem atque de- jectum videre non possumus. Statimque infert: ipsi autem confundentur: subauditur, qui loquuntur talia, qui non intelligunt mysteria scripturarum: ma- lisque suis sentient ejus potentiam, quem pro humili- tate contempserant. VOX FREMITUS DE CIVITATE. Septuaginta pro FREMITU CLA- MOREM posuerunt, & cætera similiter (ut in La- tino textu) volumus scire quæ sit confusio Judæo- rum, qui dixerunt: Glorificetur Dominus, ut vestram lætitiam videamus, & triumphos regis vestri nequa- quam cassis promissionibus, sed oculis contemple- mur. Vox(inquit) clamoris de civitate. Haud dubium, quin Hierusalem significet Romano exercitu circun- datam, & in tres partes integ seditione divisam: quando unus templum obtinuit, & omnia prius sancta possedit: forinsecus contra hostes, extrinsecus contra cives dimi- cans. Eo tempore & in urbe & in templo, tam sacer- dotum & Levitarum,quam vulgi ignobilis, mulierumq; ac puerorum ululatus auditus est: quando reddidit Do- minus retributionem inimicis suis, implens commina- tionem,qua dixerat: Relinquetur vobis domus ve- stra deserta. Et illam Prophetiam : Dereliqui do- mum meam: quando præsides templi consona angeli voce dixerunt : Transeamus ex his sedibus. De quibus non solum Josephus Judaicæ scriptor historiæ, sed multis prius seculis Psalmista testatur,dicens:Vi- di iniquitatem & contradictionem, quæ circumde- dit muros ejus tota die & tota nocte: ita ut subverte- retur civitas & impleretur aliud vaticinium : Sion quasi ager arabitur, & Hierusalem quasi casula in cucumerario relinquetur. Perperam ad vocem ovantem hoc trahi a Grotio manifestum est.

## 66:7
Verse 7.

BEFORE SHE WAS IN LABOR, SHE BROUGHT FORTH: BEFORE HER LABOR CAME, SHE BROUGHT FORTH A MALE CHILD) Before anyone could hope for it, the liberation of Judea came through Maccabeus.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ANTEQVAM PARTURIRET, PEPERIT: AN- TEQVAM VENIRET PARTVS EJVS, PEPERIT MASCVLVM) Priusquam quisquam id sperare posset,ve- nit Judææ liberatio per Maccabæum.

## 66:8
Verse 8.

SHALL THE EARTH BE BROUGHT FORTH IN ONE DAY, OR SHALL A NATION BE BROUGHT FORTH AT ONCE) Who ever saw that, that any whole state should be so suddenly restored, and where there was no people, a people should come into existence?

FOR SION HAS BEEN IN LABOR AND HAS BROUGHT FORTH HER CHILDREN) Just as Sion was in labor (that is, began to feel the labor pains for the first time), and (at the same moment) brought forth. In a single moment, as it were, she was filled with citizens, having been desolate.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NVMQVID PARIETUR TERRA IN DIE VNA, AVT PARIETVR GENS SIMVL)Quis unquam id vidit, ut ita subito restitueretur totus status aliquis, & ubi non e- rat populus, populus exsisteret?

QVIA PARTVRIVIT ET PEPERIT SION FILI- OS SVOS) Sicut parturivit (id est, partitudinem primùm sentire cœpit,)& (eodem momento) peperit Sion. Vno ve- luti momento impleta est civibus, quæ deserta fuerat.

## 66:9
Verse 9.

SHALL I WHO MAKE OTHERS BRING FORTH, NOT BRING FORTH MYSELF) In the Hebrew: Shall I who make to bring forth (namely women) not bring forth? That is, shall I not be able to suddenly cause a people to exist?

SHALL I BE STERILE) I shall be closed: that is, I shall be as a woman with a closed womb.

These things speak not of the corporal restoration of Jerusalem, but of the spiritual propagation of the Church: namely, that very many were regenerated and converted to faith in Christ. For conversion is described mystically through conception, parturition, and regeneration, as is known. As these are explained by Jerome, Cyril, and Theodoret concerning the primitive Church in the time of the Apostles, which brought forth very many to Christ without difficulty, Acts 2:40. But the interpretation of the Papists concerning the Blessed Mary bringing forth without pain is foreign: nor does Cornelius join both senses except ineptly, and he makes both literal. Compare verses 12, 13. Rightly here, after B. Brentius, Osiander expressed the mind of the Prophet; But, he says, just as the Jewish nation was almost entirely destroyed in that extreme destruction, so on the contrary the Church of Christ took on the greatest and most admirable increases, concerning which matter the Prophet speaks, full of wonder, in the following words: BEFORE SHE WAS IN LABOR, the Church of Christ (O stupendous thing!) has already BROUGHT FORTH: BEFORE HER LABOR PAIN CAME, she has already BROUGHT FORTH A MALE CHILD. WHO HAS EVER HEARD SUCH A THING? AND WHO HAS SEEN THE LIKE to this thing done anywhere before? SHALL THE EARTH BE IN LABOR IN ONE DAY? Has it happened that the earth, on the day it received the seed, brought forth fruit? OR SHALL A NATION BE BROUGHT FORTH AT ONCE? Who ever saw a whole new nation suddenly come into existence, which before had been none? Is this not worthy of the highest admiration? FOR SION (the Church) HAS BEEN IN LABOR AND HAS BROUGHT FORTH HER CHILDREN? so that on the day they were conceived, they were born? This came to pass when the Apostles, on the day of Pentecost, by the preaching of the Gospel, converted three thousand men to the Christian Religion, and afterwards by their sermons often suddenly gained a great multitude of men. For as soon as the seed of the word of God, the Gospel, was scattered, a new nation was immediately born spiritually, so that, indeed, Christians were suddenly born who on that very day had been Jews or idolatrous Gentiles. But to the Prophet wondering at so swift a generation of a new people, the Lord answers: SHALL I, WHO MAKE OTHERS BRING FORTH, NOT BRING FORTH MYSELF? In Hebrew: Shall I, who cause (women) to bring forth, not generate myself? SAYS THE LORD: YES, or more correctly: Shall I, WHO BESTOW GENERATION or the faculty of generating UPON OTHERS, be STERILE myself, SAYS THE LORD THY GOD? That is, Shall I, who bring it about that women can bring forth offspring (a wonderful thing, but a daily one, and therefore becoming cheap), not myself also generate spiritual children?
