And shall I, who give to men the power of begetting children, not myself also beget spiritual children? Then indeed the cause would be inferior to the effect. (For the Lord regenerates us. He uses, however, the work of the ministers of the Church, who preach the Gospel of Christ: Therefore Paul writes to the Corinthians: I HAVE BEGOTTEN YOU through the Gospel 1 Cor. 4. Which agree with similar passages in Isa. 49, 21. Psalm 87, verses 4, 5.) It is helpful to hear Jerome again: BEFORE SHE TRAVAILS, SHE HAS BROUGHT FORTH: With a clamor resounding from Jerusalem and its temple, when it was besieged and subverted: and with the enemies of Christ, who would not receive God as King, receiving eternal punishments for their impiety and blasphemies: the Church gathered in the name of the Lord, of which it is said in the Psalm: A man was born in her, and the Most High himself founded her: before she travailed, she brought forth: before her labor came, she brought forth a man-child. For not in a long time, as the people of the Jews grew greater through Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and the twelve Patriarchs, and again through their children and grandchildren, but at the Evangelical preaching, the whole world immediately conceived and travailed and brought forth a man-child, whom Pharaoh and Herod tried to kill: who also in Moses and in Christ was saved in Egypt. Sion, therefore, that is, the remnant from Israel and the faithful of the believing Apostles, brought forth a man-child, the Lord the Savior: who was generated in the whole world at once, which no one has heard, which no history narrates, nor any doctrine, that all nations should believe in a short time, and that from all peoples one nation of Christians should be made: of which Paul also speaks: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things have passed away, behold, all things have become new. According to that which is written elsewhere: And all the families of the nations shall worship in his sight, because the kingdom is the Lord's and he shall rule over the nations. For all (he says) nations which thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, and shall glorify thy name: of whom Jacob says: He is the expectation of the nations. And the Psalmist, the hope of all the ends of the earth. And the same Isaiah, whom we shall now explain: There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to be prince of the nations, in him shall the nations hope. The Apostles fulfilling what was commanded, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: that a new people may be born, of which the twenty-sixth Psalm also sings: The heavens shall declare his justice to the people that shall be born, whom the Lord hath made. And again: The people that shall be created shall praise the Lord. But this people was created in one day, whom the Sun of justice illuminates, the Scripture saying: The Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light. We can apply this, which is said: A nation shall arise at once, because Sion travailed and brought forth her children, and to that time thanks to return, when in one day three thousand and five thousand from the Jewish people believed. It is also said in the same book of the Acts of the Apostles, that from all nations which are under heaven, there were in Jerusalem those who heard them speaking in various languages the mighty works of God. And what follows according to the Seventy: But I have given this expectation, and you have not remembered me, says the Lord: Have I not made the bearing and the barren, said your God? It is put more clearly in the Hebrew, with which the other interpreters also agree. Shall I, who make others bear, not bear myself, says the Lord? If I, who grant generation to others, shall be barren, says the Lord your God: according to that which is said elsewhere: He who planted the ear, shall he not hear? He who fashioned the eye, does he not consider? Which is to say, that He who created all men from nothing, can from all nations make one part of those believing in Him the Church. Finally, in Psalm 28, where we read, The voice of the Lord shaking the desert: in the Hebrew it is written, the voice of the Lord making the desert bear. So that the desert Church may first bring forth, and the hinds may be perfected with open and broken leaps. Furthermore, according to the Seventy, the sense here is that at one time the preaching of the Gospels may arise from one nation of the whole world. Through many Prophets I have often promised, and you have not remembered my promise. O city, which art full of clamors. O temple, which has been abandoned by the Lord. O people, to whom I have rendered their vicissitude: Have I not (he says) made the parturient and the barren: she who had previously been barren, afterwards brought forth and gave birth. Of whom it is written in the Psalm: Who makes the barren to dwell in a house, a joyful mother of children. Or certainly the order of things is reversed: The bearing woman has become barren, and the once barren has brought forth many, because this is the sentence of the Lord.

The Jews themselves acknowledge that these things are to be understood concerning the time of the Messiah. Jonathan the Chaldean explains the text thus: Before she came out of distress, she was made safe, and before the pains of labor came to her, the Messiah was revealed. In Bereschit Rabba on Gen. 30, it is read thus: R. Samuel, son of Nachman, said, whence do you say that the Messiah was born on the same day that the house of the sanctuary was destroyed? Because it is said in Isa. 66, 7. Before she travailed, she brought forth, etc. In Bereschith Ketanna on Gen. 38, 1, similar things are held.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

NVMQVID EGO QVI ALIOS PARERE FACIO, IPSE NON PARIAM) In Hebræo: Qui parere facio (Nempe fœminas) non pariam? id est, non potero subito efficere, ut existat populus?

STERILIS ERO) Claudar: id est, ero velut mulier clauso utero.

Loquuntur hæc non de corporali Hierosoly- mæ restauratione, sed de spirituali Ecclesiæ propaga- tione : quod nempe regenerati fuerint plurimi, & ad fidem in Christum conversi. Nam conversio per conceptionem, parturitionem, regenerationē describitur mystice, uti notum est. Uti explicantur hæc ab Hieron. Cyrillo ac Theodor. de Ecclesia primitiva Apostolorum tempore, quæ plurimos Christo citra difficultatem peperit, Actor.2, 40. aliena autem interpretatio est Papistarum de B. Maria sine dolore pariente: nec nisi inepte sensum u- trumq; conjungit Cornelius ac utrumq; literalem facit. Conf. v. 12. 13. Recte a. hic post B. Brentium Osiander mentem Prophetæ expressit; Ut autem, inquit, gens Judaica in illo extremo excidio pene tota deleta fuit, ita contra Ecclesia Christi sumsit maxi- ma & admiranda incrementa, de qua re loquitur Propheta admirabundus sequentibus verbis: AN- TEQUAM PARTURIRET Ecclesia Christi (o rem stupendam!) jam PEPERIT: ANTEQUAM VENIRET dolor PARTUS EJUS, jam PE- PERIT MASCULUM. QUIS AUDIVIT UNQUAM TALE? ET QUIS VIDIT SI- MILE HUIC rei prius alicubi factum esse? NUNQUID PARTURIET TERRA IN DIE UNA? Num factum est, ut aliquando terra, eo die, quo semen excepit, protulerit fructum? AUT PARIETUR GENS SIMUL? quis un- quam vidit subito exstitisse novam totam gentem, quæ antea nulla fuerat? Annon hoc summa est ad- miratione dignum? QUIA PARTURIVIT ET PEPERIT SION (Ecclesia) FILIOS SUOS? ita ut eo die, quo concepti erant,nascerentur? hoc factum est, cum Apostoli in die Pentecostes præ- dicatione Evangelii converterent ad Religionem Christianam tria hominum millia, & postea suis concionibus sæpe subito magnam multitudinem hominum lucrifecerunt. Quamprimum enim sparsum est semen verbi Dei, Evangelii, mox nata est spiritualiter nova gens, ut nimirum Christiani nascerentur subito, qui eo ipso die fuerant Judæi aut Gentes idololatricæ. Admiranti autem Prophe- tæ tam celerem generationem novi populi, respon- det Dominus: NUMQUID EGO, QUI ALIOS PARERE FACIO, IPSE NON PARIAM? Hebraice: Nunquid ego, qui facio, ut enitantur (mulieres,) Ipse non generarem? DI- CIT DOMINUS: SI, rectius: Num EGO, QUI GENERATIONEM seu generandi faculta- tem CÆTERIS TRIBUO, ipse STERILIS E- RO, AIT DOMINUS DEUS TUUS? Id est, An ego, qui efficio, ut mulieres fœtum eniti pos- sint (rem mirandam, sed quotidianam, ideoque vi- lescentem) ipse non generarem etiam filios spiri- tuales? & ego, qui do viris potentiam gignendi li- beros, ipse non gignerem etiam filios spirituales? Tum vero causa deterior esset effectu. (Domi- nus enim nos regenerat. Utitur autem ministro- rum Ecclesiæ opera, qui prædicant Evangelion Christi: Itaq; Paulus ad Corinthios scribit: EGO VOS GENUI per Evangelion 1. Cor. 4. Quæ congruunt similibus locis Esa. 49, 21. Psalm. 87. vers. 4. 5.) Audire juvat iterum Hieronymum: ANTEQUAM PARTURIET, PEPERIT: Cla- more resonante de Hierusalem & templo ejus, quando obsessa atque subversa est: & inimicis Christi, qui Deum Regem suscipere noluerunt, recipientibus pro impietate sua atq; blasphemiis æterna supplicia: Eccle- sia in nomine Domini congregata, de qua in Psalm. di- citur: Homo natus in ea, & ipse fundavit eam altis- simus: antequam parturiret, peperit: antequam veniret partus ejus, genuit masculus. Non n. multo tempore, ut populus Judæorum per Abraham & Isaac & Jacob & duodecim Patriarchas, & rursum per li- beros eorum ac nepotes crevit in majus, sed ad Evan- gelicam prædicationem statim omnis mundus concepit & parturivit & peperit masculum, quem Pharao & Herodes conabantur occidere: qui & in Mose & in Christo salvatus est in Ægypto. Peperit igitur Sion, hoc est, reliquiæ ex Israel & Apostolorum credentium fideles masculum Dominum salvatorem: qui in to- to simul orbe generatus, quod nullus audivit, quod nulla narrat historia, aut alicujus doctrina, ut omnes crederent in brevi tempore nationes, & de universis gentibus una gens fieret Christianorum: de qua & Paulus loquitur: Si qua in Christo nova creatura, vetera transierunt, ecce facta sunt nova. Juxta illud quod alibi scriptum est: Et adorabunt in conspe- ctu ejus omnes familiæ gentium, quia Domini est regnum & ipse dominabitur gentium. Omnes enim (ait) gentes quas fecisti, venient & adorabunt co- ram te, & glorificabunt nomen tuum: de quo dicit Jacob: Ipse est expectatio gentium. Et Psalmi- sta, spes omnium finium terræ. Et idem Esaias, quem nunc edisseremus: Erit radix Jesse & qui sur- get, ut princeps sit gentium, in ipso gentes spera- bunt. Implentibus Apostolis quod præceptum est, doce- te omnes gentes, baptizantes eas in nomine Patris, filii & Spiritus Sancti: ut nascatur novus populus, de quo & vicesimus sextus Psalmus canit: Annuncia- bunt cœli justitiam ej9, populo qui nascetur, quem fecit Dominus. Et iterum: Populus qui creabitur, laudabit Dominum. Hic autem populus uno crea- tus est die, quem illustrat Sol justitiæ, dicente Scriptura: Erit tibi Dominus lux sempiterna. Pos- sumus hoc, quod dicitur: Orietur gens simul, quia parturivit & peperit Sion filios suos, & ad illud tem- pus referre, quando una die tria millia & quinq; mil- lia de Judaico populo crediderunt. Dicitur quoq; in eodem Actuum Apostolorum libro, quod de universis gentibus, quæ sub cælo sint, fuerint in Hierusalem, qui audiebant variis linguis loquentes magnalia Dei. Quodque sequitur juxta septuaginta: Ego au- tem dedi expectationem hanc, & non recordata es mei, dicit Dominus: Nonne ego parientem ac ste- rilem feci, dixit Deus tuus, Manifestius in Hebrai- co ponitur, cui & reliqui interpretes congruunt. Nunquid ego, qui alios parere facio, ipse non pa- riam, dicit Dominus? Si ego, qui generationem cæteris tribuo, sterilis ero, ait Dominus Deus tuus: secundum illud, quod alibi dicitur: Qui plantavit au- rem, non audiet: qui finxit oculum, non conside- rat: quod scilicet qui omnes homines creavit ex nihi- lo, possit de universis gentibus unam partem in se cre- dentium Ecclesiam facere. Deniq; in 28. Pf. ubi nos le- gimus, Vox Domini concutientis desertum: in Hebr. scriptum est, vox Domini parere faciens desertum. ut deserta prius Ecclesia generet, perficiantur cervi apertis saltibus atque contritis. Porro juxta septua- ginta hic sensus est, quod uno tempore prædicatio- nem Evangeliorum una gens totius orbis oriatur. Per multos Prophetas sæpe promisi, & non memi- nisti promissionis meæ. O urbs, quæ clamoribus es plena. O templum, quod à Domino derelictum est. O popule, cui reddidi vicissitudinem suam: Non- ne ego (inquit) feci parturientem & sterilem: quæ prius fuerat sterilis, postea parturivit & peperit. De qua in Psalmo scribitur: Qui habitare facit sterilem in domo, matrem filiorum lætantem. Vel certe re- rum ordo conversus est: Pariens facta est sterilis, & quondam sterilis peperit plurimos, quia Domini ista sententia est.

Agnoscunt ipsimet Judæi hæc de Messiæ tem- pore intelligenda esse. Jonathan Chaldæus textum ita exponit: Antequam veniret è angustia, salva fa- cta est, & antequam venirent ei dolores partus, Mes- sias revelatus est. In Bereschit Rabba super Gen. 30. ita legitur: Dixit R. Samuel, filius Nachman, unde dicis, quod ipsa die natus est Messias, qua destructa est domus sanctuarii? Quia dictum est Ef. 66, 7. Ante- quam parturiret, peperit, &c. In Bereschith Ketanna super Gen. 38, 1. habentur similia.

## 66:10
Verse 10. YOU WHO MOURN OVER HER) You who have mourned. For participles among the Hebrews are of any time. Many Hebrews refer these things mystically to the time of the resurrection.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVI LVGETIS SVPER EAM) Qui luxi- stis. Participia enim apud Hebræos sunt cujusvis tempo- ris. Hæc Hebræi multi μεσικῶς referunt ad tempus resur- rectionis.

## 66:11
Verse 11. THAT YOU MAY SUCK AND BE FILLED) That you may be partakers of the riches of the city and of its triumphs.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VT SVGATIS ET REPLEAMINI) Vt participes sitis divitiarum urbis ac triumphorum.

## 66:12
Verse 12. AS A RIVER OF PEACE) In the Hebrew: Peace as a river. As the Euphrates, says the Chaldean, that is, a huge abundance of prosperity.

THE GLORY OF THE GENTILES, WHICH YOU SHALL SUCK) The spoil from the Idumeans, Moabites, and other nations.

YOU SHALL BE CARRIED AT THE BREASTS) You shall be satisfied, as an infant hanging from the breasts.

AND UPON THE KNEES THEY SHALL COAX YOU) In the Hebrew: You shall be delighted, that is, you shall act joyfully in the fatherland city, no less than children who play in their mother's lap.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QVASI FLVVIVM PACIS) In Hebr. Pacem tanquam fluvium. Tanquam Euphratem, ait Chaldæus, id est, ingentem prosperitatis copiam.

GLORIAM GENTIVM, QVAM SVGETIS) Prædam de Idumæis, Moabitis gentibusque aliis.

AD VBERA PORTABIMINI) Satiabimini, ut infans de uberibus pendens.

ET SVPER GENVA BLANDIENTVR VOBIS) In Hebræo: Delectabimini, id est, læti agetis in urbe patria, non minus quam pueri, qui in gremio matris ludunt.

## 66:13
Verse 13. AS IF A MOTHER COAXES SOMEONE, SO I WILL COMFORT YOU) In the Hebrew it is: as if a mother should comfort someone: a weeping child, that is.

AND IN JERUSALEM YOU SHALL BE COMFORTED) That is, not only will good things happen to you privately, but you will also rejoice with the rejoicing fatherland, as above in 10.

Grotius accepts these things concerning carnal joy and the spoil from the Idumeans and Moabites: But the Prophet says nothing of this here, nor is sucking the glory of the nations to take spoil from them. The Prophet stirs the faithful to spiritual joy with the new Church of Jerusalem designated, and over her, those who are accustomed to mourn her in her miserable state. BECAUSE, he says, YOU SHALL SUCK AND BE SATIATED FROM THE BREASTS OF HER CONSOLATION. BECAUSE YOU SHALL MILK (the breasts of the Church) AND BE DELIGHTED BECAUSE OF THE SPLENDOR OF HER GLORY, as is held in the Hebrew. The pious shall suck the sweetest milk of the Gospel full of consolation, and shall rejoice, when they hear the sincere sermons of the Gospel, especially in public assemblies. And they shall congratulate themselves, and shall be greatly delighted over the illustrious gifts of the Holy Spirit, which He has bestowed upon the Church and her ministers. For thus says the Lord: Behold I will decline, or direct, upon her as a river of peace, and as an overflowing torrent the glory of the Gentiles, which you shall suck: and you shall be carried at the breasts, and upon the knees they shall caress you, as one whom the mother caresses, so will I comfort you, and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem, that is, according to Osiander's interpretation: I will give you through the Gospel the most abundant peace of conscience toward God: and the converted Gentiles shall bring their wealth and majesty to help the Church. And just as a mother now carries her little child in her arms, near her breasts, and presses him tightly to her breasts out of love: now she moves him gently while he is placed upon her knees, and cheers him with maternal play: so I, by my Holy Spirit through the Gospel, will most sweetly comfort and cherish you, so that from the Church of God, whose little children and members you are, you may perceive excellent consolation and joy. There is promised to the Church both Peace, which will be diverted into it like a river, than which there is nothing better in human affairs, and the GLORY OF THE GENTILES, which will inundate it like a torrent, than which there has been nothing more excellent and illustrious in these lands. For the Gentiles were distinguished in power, wisdom, and eloquence. For what among the kingdoms of this age was more powerful than the four Monarchies in Daniel? What wiser than the Philosophers and lawgivers? What more eloquent than the Orators, and especially Demosthenes and Cicero, who were from the Gentiles? This is the glory of the Gentiles, which God promises he will decline, that is, pour out into the Church, and that not bit by bit and drop by drop, but with full vessels. As a river, he says, and as an overflowing torrent, that is, most abundantly. But although these things seem to be said about external peace and glory: yet because the Kingdom of Christ is not of this world, they must be understood of that peace and glory which properly belong to the Kingdom of Christ. For although external and worldly peace is indeed a great benefit of God: it is not that peace by which we are truly saved before God. But that is the only true peace, by which the Son of God reconciled us with God his Father. For after sin alienated God from us, the Son of God undertook to expiate our sin by his cross and death, with which expiation God was so pleased that he not only entered into a covenant of peace with the human race, but also adopts from among men those who truly believe in Christ his Son as his children and heirs. But this pacification is poured out into the Church through the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: so that whoever has received and known the Gospel with true faith, that he has a propitious God on account of Christ, may have peace and tranquility even in the midst of the wars of this World and in the midst of death itself. Then, just as by peace is not understood here that worldly peace, but Christian, that is, spiritual and heavenly, so by the glory of the Gentiles, which are wisdom, power, and eloquence, are not to be understood those external gifts by which the Gentiles were illustrious in this world: but they are to be understood of those spiritual gifts, by which

Christ adorns the Church, according to the condition of His Kingdom: For He confers upon the assembly of His Church not that worldly power by which Babylon or Rome might be conquered by external forces, but that spiritual power by which Satan is overcome, death is vanquished, and hell is conquered. This is the power that surpasses the strength of all the monarchs of this age. In the world (He says) you have tribulation, but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world. And John, everything that is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that overcomes the world, our faith, etc. Nothing, therefore, is stronger, nothing more powerful than the Church through its Lord Jesus Christ. Then Christ confers wisdom upon His Church: wisdom, however, not that philosophical or political one: although He sometimes adorns His pious ones with this kind of wisdom as well: but heavenly wisdom, by which we are able to escape death, avoid the perpetual fires of hell, and attain heavenly life and happiness. For He said, I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, even if he has died, shall live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall not die forever. Therefore, he who hears Christ and believes in Christ is adorned with such great wisdom that he can retain life even in death, and thus never die and perish forever. Such and so great wisdom no philosopher, no lawgiver of the Gentiles, could ever attain from his own human reason. How, therefore, could it be that the Church, from such a salutary gift poured out upon it, would not be stirred to joy and exultation? Furthermore, Christ also confers eloquence upon His Church, namely that eloquence by which the eternal God and heavenly Father is persuaded not only to forgive us the sins for which we have deserved death and hell, but also to save us in death and the horrors of hell, for heavenly joys and perpetual life. A man is considered a notable orator who by his eloquence moves a judge to acquit a defendant accused of theft, or homicide, or sedition, or some other civil or criminal sin: how much more eloquent must he be considered who persuades not a man, but God Himself the judge, to let go free one who is liable to eternal death on account of his crimes, and furthermore to make him an heir of the heavenly kingdom? Such eloquence Christ pours out upon His Church. For He says: Amen, amen I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give to you; ask, and you shall receive, that your joy may be perfect. The Rabbis also attribute these promises to Christ, because it is so held in the Targum, ch. 1: as a man whom his mother consoles, so my word shall console them.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVOMODO SI CVI MATER BLAN- DIATVR, ITA EGO CONSOLABOR VOS) In He- bræo est: si quem mater consoletur: puerum flentem scilicet.

ET IN JERVSALEM CONSOLABIMINI) Id est, non privatim tantum vobis bona contingent, sed & gaudebitis patria gaudente, ut supra 10.

De carnali lætitia, & præda ab Idumæis & Moa- bitis Grotius hæc accipit: De qua autem nihil hic Propheta, neq; gloriam gentium sugere, est prædam ab ipsis accipere. Excitat Propheta ad gaudium spiri- tuale fideles cum Ecclesia nova Hierusalem desi- gnata, & super eam, qui in misero ejus statu eam lu- gere solent. QVIA, inquit, SVGETIS ET SA- TVRABIMINI AB VBERIBUS CONSOLA- TIONIS EJUS. QUIA MULGEBITIS (ubera Ecclesiæ) ET DELECTABIMINI PROPTER SPLENDOREM GLORIÆ EJUS, ut in E- bræo habetur. Pii sugent dulcissimum lac Evange- lii plenum consolationis, & lætabuntur, cum in pu- blicis imprimis congressibus audierint sinceras E- vangelii conciones. Et gratulabuntur sibi, atque valde delectabuntur super illustribus Spiritus S. donis, quæ in Ecclesiam ejusq; ministros contulit. QUIA HÆC DICIT DOMINUS: ECCE E- GO DECLINABO, seu dirigam SUPER EAM QUASI FLUVIUM PACIS, ET QUASI TORRENTEM INUNDANTEM GLORI- AM GENTIUM, QUAM SUGETIS: ET AD UBERA PORTABIMINI, ET SUPER GENUA BLANDIETUR VOBIS, QUO- MODO SI CUI MATER BLANDIETUR, ITA ET EGO CONSOLABOR VOS, ET IN JERUSALEM CONSOLABIMINI, h. e. Interprete Osiandro: Ego per Evangelium largis- simam vobis dabo pacem conscientiæ erga Deum: & gentes conversæ opes & Majestatem suam con- ferent ad juvandam Ecclesiam. Et quemadmodum mater filiolum nunc gestat in brachiis, juxtá ube- ra sua, eumq; præ amore arčte comprimit ad ubera: nunc eum super genua positum suaviter movet, eumque lusibus maternis exhilarat: ita ego Spiritu Sancto meo per Evangelium vos suavissime conso- labor atque fovebo, ut ab Ecclesia Dei, cujus filioli & membra estis, eximiam consolationem & lætiti- am percipiatis. Promittitur Ecclesiæ tum Pax, quæ quasi fluvius in eandem derivabitur, qua in huma- nis rebus nihil est melius, tum GLORIA GEN- TIUM, quæ instar torrentis eam inundabit, qua in his terris nihil fuit excellentius & illustrius. Gentes enim fuerunt insignes potentia, sapientia & elo- quentia. Quid enim inter regna hujus seculi po- tentius fuit quatuor Monarchiis apud Danielem? Quid sapientius Philosophis & legumlatoribus? Quid eloquentius Oratoribus, ac præcipue Demo- sthene & Cicerone, qui fuerunt ex gentibus? Hæc est gloria gentium, quam promittit Deus se decli- naturum, hoc est, effusurum in Ecclesiam, idq; non minutatim & guttatim, sed plenis vasis. Tanquam fluvium, inquit, & tanquam torrentem inundantem, hoc est, abundantissime. Etsi autem hæc videntur dici de externa pace & gloria: tamen quia Regnum Christi non est de hoc mundo, intelligenda sunt de ea pace & gloria, quæ proprie Regno Christi compe- tunt. Primum enim externa & mundana pax ma- gnum quidem beneficium Dei est: non est autem ea pax, qua vere coram Deo servamur. Sed illa de- mum vera pax est, qua Filius Dei reconciliavit nos cum Deo Patre suo. Postquam enim peccatum a- lienavit à nobis Deum, suscepit filius Dei peccatum nostrum cruce & morte sua expiandum, qua expia- tione Deus ita delectatus est, ut non solum inierit fœdus pacis cum humano genere, verum etiam ad- optet ex hominibus in filios & hæredes suos, quot- quot in Christum filium suum vere credunt. Hæc autem pacificatio effunditur in Ecclesiam per E- vangelion Domini nostri Jesu Christi: ut quicunq; Evangelion vera fide acceperit & cognoverit, se habere Deum propitium propter Christum, habe- at pacem & tranquillitatem in mediis etiam bellis hujus Mundi ac in media ipsa morte. Deinde sicut per pacẽ non intelligitur hic illa mundana pax, sed Christiana, hoc est, spiritualis & cœlestis, ita per gloriam gentium, quæ sunt sapientia, potentia & e- loquentia, non sunt intelligenda illa externa dona, quibus gentes fuerunt illustres in hoc mundo: sed sunt intelligenda de iis spiritualibus donis, quibus

Christus Ecclesiam, pro sui Regni conditione or- nat: Confer enim in cœtum Ecclesiæ suæ non po- tentiam illam mundanam, qua expugnetur exter- nis viribus Babylon, aut Roma: sed potentiam il- lam spiritualem,qua superaturSatan,vincitur mors, & expugnatur infernus. Hæc est potentia,quæ su- perat vires omniumMonarcharum hujus seculi. In Mundo (inquit) affli&tionem habetis, sed bono animo sitis, ego vici mundum. Et Johannes,omne, quod na- tum est ex Deo, vincit mundum Et hæc est victoria, quæ vincit mundum,fides nostra, &c. Nihil igitur est fortius, nihil potentius Ecclesia per Dominum suum Jesum Christum. Deinde confert Christus sapientiam in Ecclesiam suam: sapientiam autem non illam philosophicam, aut politicam: etsi & hoc sapientiæ genere pios suos nonnunquam ornat: sed sapientiam cælestem, qua possumus effugere mortem, vitare perpetuos ignes inferni, & conse- qui cælestem vitam ac felicitatem. Dixit enim,ego sum resurrectio & vita. Qui credit in me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet, & omnis, qui vivit & credit in me,non morietur in æternum. Quare qui audit Christum, & credit in Christum,tanta sapientia or- natur, ut queat etiam in morte vitam retinere, ad- eoq; nunquam in æternum mori ac perire. Talem ac tantam sapientiam nullus unquam Philosophus, nullus Gentium Legumlator, è sua humana ratio- ne consequi potuit. Quomodo igitur fieri posset, ut Ecclesia ex tam salutari dono in ipsam effu- so, ad gaudium & exultationem non excitaretur? Præterea Christus confert etiam eloquentiam in Ecclesiam suam, eam videlicet eloquentiam, qua æternus Deus & cælestis Pater persuadetur,ut non solum condonet nobis peccata, quibus mortem & infernum meriti sumus, verum etiam servet nos in morte & horroribus inferni, ad cælestia gaudia, & perpetuam vitam. Insignis habetur orator,qui elo- quentia sua permovet Judicem, ut reum vel furti, vel homicidii,vel seditionis vel alterius, seu civilis, seu criminalis peccati accusatum absolvat: quan- to eloquentiôr habendus est, qui non hominem, sed Deum ipsum judicem,persuadet, ut se propter crimina sua æternæ morti obnoxium liberum di- mittat, & insuper hæredem cælestis regni faciat? Talem autem eloquentiam effundit Christus in Ecclesiam suam. Dicit enim: Amen, amen dico vo- bis, quæcunque petieritis patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis, petite, & accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit perfectum. Tribuunt has promissiones Christo e- tiam Rabbini, quia ita in Targum habetur c. 1. sicut vir, quem consolatur mater sua: sic verbum meum consolabitur eos.

## 66:14
Vers. 14.

YOUR BONES SHALL GERMINATE LIKE GRASS) That is, they shall flourish, as Symmachus translates, according to Jerome. The Chaldean teaches us that by bones, metonymically, bodies are understood. Confer Ezech. 37.

AND THE HAND OF THE LORD SHALL BE KNOWN TO HIS SERVANTS.) It will now appear how powerful God is to save and adorn those whom He loves.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

OSSA VESTRA QVASI HERBA GERMINABVNT) Id est, florebunt, ut vertit Symmachus, teste Hieronymo. Per ossa autem μεταωνυμικῶς intelligi corpora docet nos Chal- dæus. Confer. Ezech. 37.

ET COGNOSCETVR MANVS DOMINI SERVIS EJVS.) Apparebit jam,quam potens sit Deus ad servandos & ornandos, quos amat.

## 66:15
Vers. 15. THE LORD SHALL COME IN FIRE, AND AS A WHIRLWIND HIS CHARIOTS.) By fire, efficacy is understood; by the whirlwind, swiftness.

TO RENDER HIS FURY IN INDIGNATION, AND HIS REBUKE IN A FLAME OF FIRE) Here that fury signifies ἐκδίκησιν (vengeance), as the Greeks rightly translated. What is here 'rebuke', the Greeks translated ἀποσκορακισμὸν (rejection/casting out). Suidas: ἀποσκορακίζω, ἐυτελίζω, ἐξορίζω, διώκω. Interpreters elsewhere translate the word גערה by ἐπιτιμῶν (to rebuke) or ἐμβριμασθαι (to snort/threaten). The noun derived from it, which we have here, is translated ἐπιτίμησις, ἀπειλὴ, ἐλεγμὸς. שבט is also translated by ἀποσκορακίζων in Psalm 27:9; for so Theodoret cites it from the LXX, where other codices have μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς με (do not forsake me). Σκορακίζει is said for εἰς κόρακας βάλλειν (to cast to the crows), as the Greeks mean. All these things threaten those Jews who indeed had not openly left the law, but in reality had become impious, and had not retained the law except, like Herod, to retain the favor of the people. All these paid the most severe penalties, as we learn from Josephus and the Maccabean History.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DOMINVS IN IGNE VENIET, ET QVA- SI TVRBO QVADRIGÆ EJVS.) Per ignem efficacia, per turbinem celeritas intelligitur.

REDDERE IN INDIGNATIONE FVROREM SV- VM, ET INCREPATIONEM SVAM IN FLAMMA IGNIS) Hic illud furorem significat ἐκδίκησιν, ut recte ver- torunt Græci. Quod hic est increpotionem, Græci verte- runt ἀποσκορακισμὸν. Suidas ἀποσκορακίζω, ἐυτελίζω, ἐξορί- ζω, διώκω. Verbum גערה alibi vertunt Interpretes per ἐπιτί- μῶν, vel ἐμβριμασθαι. Nomen inde derivatum, quod hic habemus, vertitur ἐπιτίμησις, ἀπειλὴ, ἐλεγμὸς, Vertitur & שבט per ἀποσκορακίζων inPsal. 27,9.ita enim ex LXX. citat Theodoretus, ubi alii codices habent μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς με. Σκορακίζει est dictum pro εἰς κόρακας βάλλειν, ut Græci len- tiunt. Hæc omnia minantur Judæis illis, qui legem quidem aperte non reliquerant, sed revera facti erant impii, neque legem retinuerant, nisi, ut Herodes, ad gratiam populi reti- nendam. Hi omnes gravissimas pœnas dedêre, ut ex Jose- pho & Maccabaïca Historia discimus.

## 66:16
Vers. 16. FOR IN FIRE THE LORD SHALL JUDGE, AND BY HIS SWORD AGAINST ALL FLESH.) He will avenge Himself with the burning of towns and camps, and with the great slaughter of men. See 1 Maccab. 4:20, 5:5, 44, 6:31, 10:84.

Most people accept these things regarding the resurrection of the dead just as in Ezech. ch. 37, to which Osiander adds in his paraphrase. But this joy of yours (says the Lord) begun in this life will be completed in the other age. For YOU SHALL SEE what great goods await you, AND YOUR HEART SHALL REJOICE for all eternity over the heavenly goods in which you will participate. For indeed YOUR BONES, which seemed corrupted and consumed in the monuments, shall again on the last day GERMINATE LIKE GRASS: they shall receive vigor, they shall be surrounded with flesh, they shall revive, and what was previously a mortal and corruptible body shall be immortal, incorruptible, and glorious (You have a testimony concerning the resurrection of the dead) AND THE HAND, the power OF THE LORD, SHALL BE KNOWN TO HIS SERVANTS; when He not only brings them back from death, but ALSO when HE SHALL BE INDIGNANT AT HIS ENEMIES, and shall afflict them with perpetual punishments. FOR BEHOLD THE LORD Jehovah Jesus Christ SHALL COME IN FIRE. For the world shall burn on the last day. AND AS A WHIRLWIND HIS CHARIOTS, that is, most swiftly, unexpectedly, and with great majesty, horribly like a storm He shall come (to the impious): TO RENDER to His enemies the rewards of impiety, IN INDIGNATION HIS FURY: more correctly, the fury of His indignation: AND HE SHALL DECLARE HIS REBUKE IN A FLAME OF FIRE. For He shall deliver the impious through His most severe sentence to the flames of Gehenna, Matt. 25. FOR IN FIRE THE LORD SHALL JUDGE; more correctly: He shall judge (that is: He shall punish) AND BY HIS SWORD AGAINST ALL FLESH, AND THE SLAIN BY THE LORD SHALL BE MULTIPLIED. That is, the number of those whom the Lord shall kill shall be huge. (This is, Jesus Christ, Jehovah, the eternal God shall come to judge the living and the dead, and by the sword of His word shall deliver to eternal death all who have not received the Gospel of Christ by faith.) The execution of the sentence, however, shall take place through eternal infernal fire. This explanation, approved also by the Vinarian Paraphrasts, and not disapproved by B. Luther and Brentius (although these also wish for the Jerusalem destruction to be included), is assumed by our B. Gerhard, de Extr. Secul. §. 13. and de Consummat. seculi §. 7., and others of ours. Which the Papistic interpreters also made their own. Cornel. à Lapide, although he notes that the words, 'your bones shall sprout like grass,' can be understood of bones squalid with grief and dead ones flourishing again with joy, nevertheless acknowledges that this will be properly fulfilled in the resurrection of the dead. Menochius assumes the former gloss of Cornelius, and confesses nevertheless that the fire of the conflagration of the world is designated here. Tirinus explains it concerning the fire of justice and temporal vengeance upon the obstinate Jews at the time of the Jerusalem destruction, then concerning the fire of conflagration on the day of the final judgment: he confesses, however, with Cornelius, that the words concerning the sprouting bones are explained by Tertullian, Irenaeus, Jerome, and Augustine concerning the resurrection of the bones of the saints. Hector Pintus explains it similarly, as does Vatablus concerning the day of the final Judgment. Caspar Sanctius, although he interprets it generally concerning the vengeance of God against enemies, does not, however, exclude the punishment of the final judgment; to which also the gloss of Calvin tends, as does the paraphrase of the others. Zwingli, however, Oecolampadius and Bullinger interpret the prophetic prediction solely of the day of the final judgment. The ancients handed down this sense: Irenaeus, book 5, chapter 15; Tertullian, book on the Resurrection of the Flesh, chapter 31; Cyprian, on the Good of Patience, near the end; Augustine, book 20, on the City of God, chapter 21, whose words we add: 'He signifies the punishment of judgment: since he says that the Lord himself is to come as fire, indeed to those for whom his arrival will be penal. But we not inappropriately accept his chariots, which are spoken of in the plural, as angelic ministries. But as to what he says: that all flesh and all earth are judged in his fire and in his sword, let us not understand here the spiritual and the holy, but the earthly and carnal: of whom it is said, "They who savor earthly things, and to savor according to the flesh is death": and such are altogether called flesh by the Lord, where he says: "My Spirit shall not remain in these men, because they are flesh." But what is placed here:' 'Many will be wounded by the Lord,' by this wound will come the second death. Similarly Cyril of Alexandria, whose words it is also pleasing to add: 'Having abundantly,' he says, 'comforted those who are in the new Sion, that is, the Church, and having promised the most abundant consolation and the support of spiritual goods, and furthermore the resurrection from the dead and the highest seats, and the glory that is there, he says that this bold undertaking against them will not go unpunished for the disobedient. For he will come,' he says, 'as fire. For he will descend from heaven in the glory of his Father with the holy Angels. For this is his chariot, just as it is celebrated in the Psalms: "The chariot of God is ten thousand-fold, thousands of those who rejoice." But he will come to render vengeance in fury and rebuke in the flame of fire.' Jerome has it thus in this place. 'The hand of the Lord, which will be made known to his servants and those who fear him, it itself threatens the incredulous or his enemies, so that if they have not done penance, they may endure what follows: "For behold," he says, "the Lord will come in fire, and his chariot as a whirlwind or tempest." Which we ought to understand as the angelic powers, when the Lord is about to come in the glory of the Father with his Angels to judge the living and the dead: not that the Lord is fire, but that to those enduring punishments he appears to be fire. But what follows, "AS A TEMPEST HIS CHARIOT" or his quadriga, we might explain by the examples of the Psalms, in which it is written, "God will come manifestly, our God and will not be silent. Fire will burn before him, and round about him a strong tempest." And elsewhere, "The chariot of God is ten thousand-fold, thousands of those who rejoice." With these chariots and horses Elisha was surrounded, which his servant could not see. Whence he says:' 'Lord, open the eyes of this boy, that he may see.' And with eyes opened, he says, 'he saw chariots, and quadrigae, and horses round about.' By this fiery chariot Elijah was also snatched to heaven, when Elisha was crying out: 'My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its driver.' But all these things are narrated, not that God either has chariots, or quadrigae, or is carried by the speed of horses: of whom it is written elsewhere: 'Who walks upon the wings of the winds.' But just as he is said to sit on a throne, just as he assumes the habit of one judging: so when he comes for vengeance, that he may defeat his adversaries, he is shown in the habit of a victor and one triumphing. Grotius, however, having disregarded such a consensus of interpreters, devised a peculiar gloss, which has come into no one's mind until now, about the punishments of the impious Jews and the burning of towns in the time of Antiochus: just as Musculus among the Calvinists thought their punishments were designated at the time of the Babylonian captivity. But just as the promises were too august to be explained concerning bodily goods, so the punishments are defined here as too grave to be restricted to bodily and temporal punishments. Then indeed it concerns the judgment against ALL

FLESH: and concerning works and thoughts, and all nations and tongues being gathered, so that the object in the universal judgment may be designated, both real, the works and thoughts of men, and personal, all nations and tongues. Furthermore, toward the end of the chapter, the judgment of the Lord and the punishment of the impious is explained, when mention is made of unquenchable fire and the worm that never dies: which Musculus himself understands concerning eternal punishment. Finally, since here the universal calling of the nations, which was to happen before the end of the world, is introduced, with Musculus himself admitting it, these things cannot be recalled either to the times of Antiochus or to those of the Babylonian captivity.

Latin:

Vers. 16. QVIA IN IGNE DOMINVS DIJVDI- CABIT, ET IN GLADIO SVO AD OMNEM CAR- NEM.) Incendiis oppidorum castrorumq;, & multa homi- num occidione se ulciscetur. Vide I. Maccab. 4, 20. 5, 5. 44. 6, 31. 10, 84.

De resurrectione mortuorum hæc perinde ut Ezech. c. 37. plerique accipiunt,quibus accedit O- siander in paraphrasi. Sed hoc vestrum gaudium (inquit Dominus) in hac vita inchoatum comple- bitur in altero seculo. VIDEBITIS enim, quanta bona vos maneant, ET GAUDEBIT COR VESTRUM in omnem æternitatem super bonis cœlestibus, quæ participabitis. Etenim OSSA VESTRA, quæ in monumentis corrupta & con- sumpta videbantur, rursus in novissimo die QUA- SI HERBA GERMINABUNT: vigorem reci- pient, carne circumdabuntur, reviviscent,& quod antea mortale & corruptibile corpus fuerat, im- mortale erit, incorruptibile & gloriosum (Habes testimonium de resurrectione mortuorum) ET COGNOSCETUR MANUS, potentia DO- MINI in SERVIS EJUS; cum non modo à mor- te eos reducet, sed ET cum INDIGNABITUR INIMICIS SUIS, eosque perpetuis suppliciis af- ficiet. QUIA ECCE DOMINUS Jehova Jesus Christus, IN IGNE VENIET. Conflagrabit enim mundus in die novissimo. ET QUASI TURBO QUADRIGÆ EJUS, id est, celerri- me,inexspectato & magna cum majestate, horribi- liter quasi tempestas (impiis) veniet: REDDE- RE hostibus suis præmia impietatis, IN INDI- GNATIONE FUROREM SUUM: rectius fu- roris sui: ET INCREPATIONEM SUAM de- clarabit in FLAMMA IGNIS. Impios enim per severissimam sententiam suam tradet flammis ge- hennæ, Matth. 25. QUIA IN IGNE DOMINUS DI- IUDICABIT; rectius: judicabit, (id est: puniet) ET IN GLADIO SUO AD OMNEM CARNEM, ET MUL- TIPLICABUNTUR INTERFECTI A DOMINO. Id est, ingens erit numerus eorum, quos interficiet Do- minus. (Hoc est, Jesus Christus, Jehova, æternus Deus veniet, judicare vivos & mortuos, & gladio verbi sui tradet æterni morti omnes, qui Evange- lion Christi fide non receperunt. Executio autem sententiæ fiet per ignem infernalem perpetuum.) Quæ explicatio probata etiam Paraphrastis Vina- riensibus, nec improbata B.Luthero, & Brentio(et- si hi etiam excidium Hierofolymitanum compre- hendi velint) assumitur à B. Gerhardo nostro, de Extr. Secul. §. 13. & de Consummat.seculi §. 7. aliis- que nostris. Quam Papistici etiam Interpretes su- am fecêre. Cornel. à Lapide,etsi verba, ossa vestra quasi herba germinabunt, de ossibus mœrore squalidis, & emortuis refiorescentibus lætitia intelligi posse no- tet, proprie tamen hoc in resurrectione mortuo- rum impletum iri agnoscit. Menochius assumit priorem Cornelii glossam, ac fatetur nihilominus ignem conflagrationis mundi hic designari. Tiri- nuctum de igne justitiæ & vindictæ temporalis in obstinatos Judæos tempore excidii Hierofolymi- tani explicat,tum de igne conflagrationis in die ex- tremi judicii: fatetur tamen cum Cornelio, verba de ossibus germinantibus à Tertull. Irenæo, Hierony- mo & Augustino exponi de resurrectione ossium san- ctorum. Similiter explicat Hector Pintus, ut & Va- tablus de die extremi Judicii. Caspar Sanctius etsi de vindicta Dei adversus hostes generaliter inter- pretetur, pœnam tamen novissimi judicii non ex- cludit; quo etiam abit Calvini glossa, ut & par- phrasis cæterorum. Zwinglius autem, Oecolampa- dius & Bullingerus de die solum extremi judicii va- ticinium Propheticum interpretantur. Quem sen- sum veteres tradidere: Irenæus l. 5. c. 15. Tertull. l. de Resurrect. carnis c. 31. Cyprianus de bon. pat. sub fin. August. l. 20. de civ. Dei c. 21. cujus verba adji- cimus: Pœnam judicii significat: quandoquidem ipsum Dominum quasi ignem dicit esse venturum eis profecto, quibus pœnalis ejus erit adventus. Currus vero ejus, qui pluraliter dicti sunt, angelica ministe- ria non inconvenienter accipimus: Quod autem ait: omnem terram & omnem carnem in ejus igne & in gladio judicari, non etiam hic spirituales intelliga- mus & sanctos, sed terrenos atq; carnales: de quibus dictum est, Qi terrena sapiunt, & sapere secundum carnem mors est: & quales omnino appellantur ca- ro a Domino, ubi dicit: Non permanebit Spiritus meus in hominibus istis, quoniam caro sunt. Quod vero hic positum est: Multi vulnerati erunt a Do- mino, isto vulnere fiet mors secunda. Similiter Cy- rillus Alexandrinus, cujus verba etiam adjicere placet: Abunde, inquit, consolatus eos, qui in nova Sion, id est, Ecclesia, & affluentissimam consolatio- nem ac spiritualium bonorum subsidium pollicitus, & præterea resuscitationem e mortuis & supremas sedes, ac quæ ibi est, gloriam, non impune fore dicit inobe- dientibus hoc audax contra illos institutum. Veniet enim, inquit, quasi ignis. Descendet namq; cælitus in gloria Patris sui cum sanctis Angelis. Hic enim est currus ejus, sicuti & in Psalmis celebratum est: Cur- rus Dei decem millibus multiplex, milia lætantium. Veniet autem redditurus ultionem in furore & incre- pationem in flamma ignis. Hieronymus ita habet h. l. Manus Domini, quæ nota fiet servis ejus & ti- mentibus eum, ipsa comminatur incredulis sive ini- micis ejus, ut si non egerint pœnitentiam, sustineant quæ sequuntur: Ecce enim (inquit) Dominus in igne veniet, & quasi turbo sive tempestas currus e- jus. Quas debemus intelligere angelicas potestates, quando venturus est Dominus in gloria Patris cum Angelis suis judicare vivos & mortuos: non quo Do- minus ignis sit, sed quo sustinentibus pœnas esse ignis videatur. Quod autem sequitur, QUASI TEMPE- STAS CURRUS sive quadrigæ ejus, Psalmorum edisse- remus exemplis, in quibus scriptum est, Deus mani- feste veniet, Deus noster & non tacebit. Ignis an- te eum ardebit, & in circuitu ejus tempestas valida. Et alibi, currus Dei decem millibus multiplex, mil- lia lætantium. His curribus & equis Elisæus erat circumdatum, quos puer ejus videri non poterat. Unde ait: Domine aperi oculos pueri hujus, ut videat. Et apertis (inquit) oculis vidit currus, & quadrigas, & equos per circuitum. Hoc curru igneo & Helias raptus ad cælum est, quando clamabat Elisæus: Pa- ter mi, pater mi, currus Israël & auriga ejus. Hæc autem universa narrantur, non quo Deus aut currus habeat, aut quadrigas, aut equorum velocitate porte- tur: de quo alibi scriptum est: Qui ambulat super pennas ventorum. Sed quomodo in solio sedere di- citur, quomodo assumit habitum judicantis: sic quando ad vindictam venit, ut debellet adversarios suos, in habitu victoris & triumphantis ostenditur. Grotius vero insuper habito tanto Interpp. con- sensu glossam peculiarem, quæ nemini hactenus in mentem venit, excogitavit de pœnis Judæorum im- piorum & incendiis Oppidorum tempore Antiochi: uti Musculus e Calvinianis eorum supplicia tempo- re captivitatis Babylonicæ designari putavit. Sed quemadmodum promissiones augustiores fuere, quam ut de bonis corporalibus explicari possint, ita pœnæ graviores hic definiuntur, quam ut re- stringi ad corporalia & temporalia supplicia debe- ant. Tum vero de judicio adversus OMNEM

CARNEM agitur: & de operibus ac cogitationibus, omnibusq; gentibus & linguis congregandis, ut obje- ctum in judicio universali designetur, tum reale, opera & cogitationes hominum, tum personale o- mnes gentes & linguæ. Porro sub finem capitis ex- plicatur judicium Domini & pœna impiorum,cum ignis inextinguibilis & vermis nunquam morientis mentio fit: Quæ de æterna pœna Musculus ipse in- telligit. Deniq; cum hic universalis gentium voca- tio,quæ ante mundi finem fieri debebat,introduca- tur, Musculo itidem fatente,non possunt ista vel ad Antiochi vel ad captivitatis Babylonicæ tempora revocari.

## 66:17
Verse 17. WHO WERE SANCTIFYING THEMSELVES, AND THOUGHT THEMSELVES PURE IN THE GARDENS BEHIND THE DOOR WITHIN) Since התקדשׁ is taken no less than the word itself קדשׁ both in a good and in a bad sense, you would not wrongly translate: Who polluted themselves, and then purified themselves (having taken water) in the groves. Compare what is above 1, 29. 65, 3. See also 1 Kings 4, 23. 15, 13. 2 Kings 23, 7.

BEHIND THE DOOR) Thus this interpreter translates here, because we read in the Hebrew אחר אחד, as also the Greeks, έν τοῖς προϑύροις, in a sense not bad, which can be understood from those things which are above 57, 8. But the Chaldean undoubtedly reads אחר אחד, that is, one after another, in a great crowd. I do not disapprove. If, however, the received reading is to be retained, I would take אחד for the Sun, the God of the Assyrians, who had a name, whence also the Latin is, because he is alone in his kind, and has nothing similar. The Hebrews say אחד, but the Syrians, with the guttural letter omitted and the last letter doubled, חדד. Philo of Byblos: Αδωδος βασιλεùς θεῶν. Macrobius, book 1, Saturnalia 23. Accept what the Assyrians think about the power of the Sun. For to the God, whom they venerate as the highest and greatest, they gave the name Adad. The interpretation of that name signifies 'one', therefore they adore this one as the most powerful God. Therefore it will be 'behind Adad', behind those shrines in which Adad was worshipped.

WHO WERE EATING SWINE'S FLESH) See what we said above 65, 4.

AND ABOMINATION) To be understood here as εἴδωλα λίϑινα (stone idols), you will be able to discern from the Chaldean above 28, 8.

AND THE MOUSE) Whose eating was forbidden by the law, Lev. 11, 29. There were those who would eat it, like the Italians with dormice, according to Varro.

Grotius's explanation of the words can be admitted. But he is mistaken in the application. For the Prophet describes in figurative language the crimes of the impious, both the superstitious and impious cults of those who purified themselves in gardens or groves, and the manifestly profane, who transgressed the law with their abominations, eating abominable and forbidden animals, under which species the Holy Spirit comprehends every impurity and filthiness of mind and morals, by which men are contaminated before God. Although Blessed Luther notes that these things were done literally in the time of Christ. And of these he says, those who did such things SHALL BE CONSUMED TOGETHER, that is, gathered they shall be delivered to eternal fire. Jerome has it thus in this place: The divine discourse reproves the peoples of the Jews, indeed the Scribes and Pharisees: whom the Lord also reproved, saying: You are they who justify yourselves before men: but God knows your hearts: for that which is exalted among men is an abomination before God, whence he rebuked them, and said: Woe to you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who clean the outside of the cup and the dish, and within you are full of uncleanness. And again: Who are whitened sepulchres: but within you are full of dead men's bones, and all uncleanness: who blessed with their mouth, and cursed with their heart, who spoke peaceable things to the Lord, and softened their words above oil, but they themselves were darts: of whom it was most rightly said: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. But God had commanded through Moses, that if anyone had been overtaken in sin, sprinkled with the ashes of a red heifer, and by other modes of expiation through sacrifices and victims, he should return to the temple, which they, being negligent, in places of delights and pleasures, that is, in most pleasant gardens, either built baptisteries, or pools for irrigating flower beds, adulteries and all the filthiness of lusts, thinking they cleanse themselves with simple waters: to whom that saying will most rightly be applied, and they purge the night with a river, etc. Augustine, book 20, On the City of God, chapter 21. Then, having briefly commemorated those who will be consumed by this judgment, under the figure of foods forbidden in the old law, from which they did not abstain, signifying sinners and the ungodly, he recapitulates from the beginning the grace of the New Testament, leading from the first coming of the Savior up to the last judgment and finishing the discourse.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QUI SANCTIFICABANTVR, ET MVN- DOS SE PVTABANT IN HORTIS POST JANVAM INTRINSECVS) Cum התקדשׁ non minus quam ipsa vox קדשׁ & in bono & in malo sensu sumatur, non male vertas: Qui se polluerunt, ac deinde lustrarunt (aqua sumta) in lucis. Confer, quæ supra 1, 29. 65,3. Vide & 1.Reg. 4, 23. 15, 13. 2. Reg. 23, 7.

POST JANVAM) Sic vertit hic Interpres, quod in Hebræo legimus אחר אחד, ut & Græci, έν τοῖς προϑύροις, sensu non malo, qui intelligi potest ex iis, quæ supra 57,8. At Chaldæus haud dubie legit אחר אחד, id est, alius post alium, magno agmine. Non improbo. Si tamen lectio re- cepta retinenda est, אחד sumam pro Sole Deo Assyriorum, qui nomen habebat, unde & Latinum est, quod solus sit in suo genere, nec quicquam simile habeat. Hebræi dicunt אחד, Syri autem omissa litera gutturali, & duplicata litera postrema חדד Philo Byblius; Αδωδος βασιλεùς θεῶν. Macro- bins 1. Saturn. 23. Accipe, quid Assyrii de Solis potentia opi- nentur. Deo enim, quem summum maximumq; venerantur, A- dad nomen dederunt. Ejus nominis interpretatio significat unus, hunc ergo ut potentissimum adorant Deum. Ergo post Adad e- rit, pone sacella illa, in quibus Adad colebatur.

QVI COMEDEBANT CARNEM SVILLAM) Vi- de, quæ diximus supra 65,4.

ET ABOMINATIONEM) Intelligenda hic εἴδωλα λίϑινα, dis ere poteris ex Chaldæo supra 28, 8.

ET MVREM) Cujus esus vetitus lege Lev. 11, 29. E- rant, qui eo vescerentur, ut gliribus Itali, teste Varrone.

Explicatio verborum Grotiana admitti potest. Sed in applicatione fallitur. Describit enim Pro- pheta figurato sermone scelera impiorum,tum su- perstitiosos & impios cultus eorum,qui se purifica- bant in hortis aut lucis,tum manifeste prophanos, qui legem abominationibus suis transgredieban- tur, abominabilia animalia & vetita in lege come- dentes, qua specie omnem animi, & morum impu- ritatem & spurcitiem comprehendit Spiritus S. qua homines coram Deo contaminantur. Quanquam B. Lutherus notet hæc Christi tempore ad lite- ram facta esse. Et de his ait, qui talia fecerunt SIMUL CONSUMENTUR, id est, collecti tradentur igni æterno. Hieronymus ita habet h.l. Arguit sermo divinus po- pulos Judæorum, imo Scribas & Pharifæos: quos & Dominus arguebat, dicens: Vos estis, qui justifica- tis vosmetipsos coram hominibus: Deus autem scit corda vestra: quoniam quod in hominibus ex- celsum est, abominatio est apud Deum, unde incre- pabat eos, atque dicebat: Væ vobis Scribæ & Phari- sæi, hypocritæ, qui mundatis quod foris est calicis & paropsidis, & intus pleni estis immunditia. Et iterum: Qui estis sepulchra dealbata: intus autem pleni estis ossibus mortuorum,& omni spurcitia:qui ore suo benedicebant, & corde suo maledicebant, qui Domino loquebantur pacifica, & molliebant verba sua super oleum, ipsi autem erant jacula: de quibus rectissime dicebatur: Populus hic labiis me hono- rat,cor vero ejus longe est à me. Præceperat autem per Mosen Deus, ut si quis præventus fuisset in pecca- to, vacca rufa aspersus cinere, & aliis expiationis mo- dis per sacrificia & victimas rediret ad templum, quod illi negligentes, in locis delitiarum & volupta- tum, hoc est, in hortis amœnissimis, vel baptisteria ex- truebant, vel piscinas ad areolas irrigandas, adulteria & omnem libidinum turpitudinem, simplicibus aquis se abluere putantes: quibus rectissime illud aptabitur, & noctem flumine purgant, &c. Augustinus lib. 20. de C. D. cap. 21. Deinde breviter commemoratis eis, qui per hoc judicium consumentur, sub figura cibo- rum in lege veteri vetitorum, a quibus se non absti- nuerunt, peccatores impiosq́; significans, recapitulat ab initio gratiam N. Testamenti, à primo Salvatoris adventu usque ad ultimum judicium perducens fi- niensq́; sermonem.

## 66:18
Verse 18. BUT I [KNOW] THEIR WORKS AND THEIR THOUGHTS) A colon should be placed here. And it is an aposiopesis. For 'I know' is understood, which the Greeks and the Chaldean supply.

I COME, THAT I MAY GATHER WITH ALL NATIONS AND TONGUES) In the Hebrew: I am coming to gather all nations and tongues. That is, the glory of the Jewish people will be so great that all nations will seek their alliances. The following words demand this meaning.

A new distortion. For the Prophet is not prophesying about the glory of the Jewish people, but about the glory of the Lord to be beheld. Nor does he treat of the forming of alliances of the Gentiles with the Jewish people, but discusses in the following verses the conversion of the Gentiles to the faith: indeed, since he threatens a most grave judgment against the Jews, the gloss about the glory of the Jewish people is inept. Nor is it necessary that the text be supplemented in that way. The sense is full without a supplement. For I come to gather their works and their thoughts with all nations and tongues. The Lord comes, therefore, says Jerome, to gather the works and thoughts of individuals. From which we learn that not only works, but also thoughts are to be judged on the day of judgment. And they shall come, and shall see my glory, when, surrounded by many myriads of Angels, I shall sit upon the throne of Majesty, Matt. 25. If, however, anyone wishes to supplement the sentence in that way, those things can be explained with Brentius in this manner: For when I, says the Lord, am not ignorant that all the pursuits and works, thoughts and deeds of these men are impious, I cannot be restrained from bringing it about that they are simultaneously taken away and destroyed. The rest, therefore, will pertain to the calling of the Gentiles. I COME, THAT I MAY GATHER ALL NATIONS, etc. Someone will say: If God rejects the Israelites, so that they are not his people, who will be his people? Or from what nation will he choose his Church? Thus, indeed, the hypocritical Jews thought: that if they themselves were not the true people of God and his true Church, God would have no Church, nor would he find any nation which he might choose as his people. But just as the Baptist says: I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones: so also in this place the Son of God says: I come, that I may gather all nations and tongues. Although I shall punish the Jews with fire and sword, and reject them so that they are not my people, yet I shall not be without a people or a Church: but I shall gather for myself a Church from all nations and tongues, which will come to me by its faith, and will see my glory: because it will recognize me to be the true Messiah and Son of God, which is the highest glory and Majesty. But I shall gather the Church from the Gentiles in this way. I will place, I will institute among them a sign or standard, which is the preaching of my Gospel (just as also above in chapter 11, the preaching of the Gospel is called a sign. He will lift up, he says, a sign to the nations, and will gather the fugitives of Israel). And I will send to the nations some of these Jews who have been saved. These are the Apostles and the remaining disciples, who, while the rest of the Jews were perishing, were saved by faith in Christ, so that they did not perish together with the others.

Latin:

Vers. 18. EGO AVTEM OPERA EORVM, ET CO- GITATIONES EORVM) Hic ponendum κῶλον. Et est ἀποσιώπησις. Subauditur enim scio, quod supplent Græci & Chaldæus.

VENIO, VT CONGREGEM CVM OMNIBVS GENTIBVS ET LINGVIS) In Hebræo: Eo congregatum gentes omnes & linguas. Id est, tanta erit gloria populi Ju- daici, ut omnes gentes eorum fœdera ambiant. Hunc sen- fum exigunt sequentia.

Nova detorsio. Nam non de gloria populi Ju- daici, sed de gloria Domini conspicienda vaticina- tur Propheta. Neq; de fœderibus Gentium cum po- pulo Judaico ineundis agit, sed de conversione gen- tium ad fidem in sequentibus disserit: imo cum comminetur judicium gravissimum adversus Ju- dæos, inepta est glossa de gloria populi Judaici. Nec neceslum est, ut ea ratione textus suppleatur. Sen- sus plenus est sine supplemento. Ego enim opera eo- rum, & cogitationes eorum venio ut congregem, cum omnibus gentibus & linguis. Venit ergo Do- minus, inquit Hieronymus, ut opera & cogi- tationes congreget singulorum. Ex quo disci- mus, non solum opera, sed etiam cogitatio- nes esse in die judicii judicandas. Et venient, & videbunt gloriam meam, quando stipatus multis Angelorum myriadibus sedebo super solium Ma- jestatis, Matth. 25. Si tamen ita quis supplere ora- tionem velit, cum Brentio explicari poterunt ista hoc modo: Cum enim ego, inquit Dominus, non ignorem omnia istorum studia & opera, cogitata & facta esse impia, teneri non possum, quin efficiam, ut simul tollantur & deleantur. Cætera ergo perti- nebunt ad vocationem gentium. VENIO, VT CON- GREGEM OMNES GENTES, &c. Dicet quispiam. Si Deus rejicit Israëlites, ut non sit populus ipsius, quis erit ejus populus? aut ex qua gente seliget Ec- clesiam suam? Sic quidem hypocritæ Judæi sentie- bant: quod si ipsi non essent verus Dei populus, & vera Ecclesia ejus, Deum nullam habiturum Ec- clesiam, nec inventurum ullam gentem, quam in populum suum eligat. Sed quemadmodum Bapti- sta ait: Dico vobis, quod Deus possit facere, ut ex la- pidibus surgant filii ipsi Abrahæ: ita & hoc loco di- cit Filius Dei: Venio, ut congregem omnes gentes & linguas. Etsi puniam Judæos igni & gladio, & reji- ciam eos, ne sint populus meus, tamen non ero sine populo aut Ecclesia: sed colligam mihi Ecclesiam ex omnibus gentibus & linguis, quæ veniet ad me fide sua, & videbit gloriam meam: quia cognoscet me verum esse Messiam & Filium Dei, quæ est sum- ma gloria & Majestas. Sic autem colligam Eccle- siam ex gentibus. Ponam, instituam inter eos signum seu vexillum, quod est prædicatio Evangelii mei (si- cut & supra cap. 11. prædicatio Evangelii vocatur si- gnum. Levabit, inquit, signum in nationes, & con- gregabit profugos Israël) Et mittam ad gentes ali- quos, ex his Judæis, qui salvati fuerint. Hi sunt Apo- stoli & reliqui discipuli, qui pereuntibus reliquis Judæis, servati sunt fide in Christum, ut non una cum aliis perirent.

## 66:19
Verse 19. AND I WILL SET A SIGN AMONG THEM) I will call them as if by an erected sign.

AND I WILL SEND OF THEM, WHO HAVE BEEN SAVED) From the Jews who will be survivors in those times.

of Antiochus. I will send, I will cause that envoys be sent to seek friendships. See 1 Macc. 12:2. TO THE NATIONS INTO THE SEA) In the Hebrew: to the nations of the Ocean: that is, to those who are situated by the Persian and Arabian sea. INTO AFRICA) From the Greeks, who read Phut, where we have Phul. That is a part of Africa near Fez. See what we have said in the Annotations to the first book on the truth of the Christian religion. The Chaldean, however, [reads] Phulai, that is, the Caucasian gates: concerning which see Pliny 6:11. AND THE LYDIANS DRAWING THE BOW) In the Hebrew: And the Lydians drawing the bow. Cyrus indeed subdued the Lydians twice, and wished a warlike nation to be corrupted by every kind of luxury, but it is easy to return to one's nature. Therefore, a proverb was born among the Greeks: You are calling a Lydian into the plain. INTO ITALY) As far as Rome, with whom they made a treaty. See 1 Macc. 8. But in the Hebrew it is Tubal, and neither the Greeks nor the Chaldeans read it otherwise. But that is Asiatic Iberia, as he who wishes will see in the said Annotations. It can be doubted whether certain Codices had Aithal. AND GREECE) See the said place 1 Macc. 12:2. TO THE ISLANDS AFAR OFF) To places far away situated by the sea or rivers. WHO HAVE NOT HEARD OF ME, AND HAVE NOT SEEN MY GLORY) To whom a thin report had arrived concerning Judea and the things done in Judea. See the reasons in Josephus against Apion, in the first book. AND THEY SHALL DECLARE MY GLORY TO THE GENTILES) A history full of the excellent deeds of God. Verse 20. AND THEY SHALL BRING ALL YOUR BRETHREN FROM ALL NATIONS AS A GIFT TO THE LORD) That is, in honor of God, the Romans and Greeks will restore to liberty and send home with honor the captives whom they had taken in the Macedonian and Syrian wars. See similar examples of kindness toward allied nations in book 3 of The Law of War and Peace 9:2, and in the Annotations to that place. AS IF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SHOULD BRING AN OFFERING IN A CLEAN VESSEL INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) With equal gladness and joy. In a clean vessel, i.e., in a dish well purged from all legal uncleanness. But the LXX understand musical instruments by the word 'keli'. For they translate it 'with psalms', not badly. For 'keli' is often accustomed to be taken in that sense, as 1 Chron. 15:16, 16:5, 42, 23:5, 2 Chron. 5:12, 7:6, 23:13, 29:26, 27, 30:21, 34:12. And the adjective 'tahor' which is added, is translated sometimes by 'holy', 'pious', 'approved'. Verse 21. AND I WILL TAKE OF THEM FOR PRIESTS AND LEVITES, SAITH THE LORD) From those Jews who, having been taken in war among foreign nations, had served in slavery: as if he were to say: that calamity, which was not their own fault but endured from the fortune of war, will not be an obstacle to them. Some objected to Hyrcanus that he could not perform the Pontificate because his mother had once been a captive: naturally because it is difficult to believe in the chastity of captive women. Otherwise, the right of postliminy restores all things to the state in which they were before the war.

These contain a most manifest prophecy concerning the calling of the Gentiles to the Church. But they are most perversely twisted with unheard-of ςεβλότητι. First, what sign is erected for the calling of the Gentiles is clear from the parallel passage, Isaiah 11. Which certainly does not treat of political alliances, but of the confluence of the Gentiles to the Church. Just as in harbors, says Osiander, some conspicuous sign is placed by the sea, to which sailors may direct their course: so I will raise the banner of the Gospel, that the Gentiles and Jews may direct their course to it, and may arrive at the harbor of salvation. Beautifully, Blessed Luther: the word is therefore a SIGN, because nothing of the Church is seen in the world except the word. For neither would the sacraments be anything, unless they had the word. Then, when those who are to be sent to the Gentiles are spoken of as being from those who have been saved, they are understood not as survivors from the time of Antiochus, but as those who are saved through faith from among the Jews, and the remnant according to election, just as the συνέχεια of the context teaches. Nor are they said to be sent as political legates to seek friendships, but as legates and messengers of the Son of God. For here he says, I will send from those who have been saved, to the Gentiles. Whence it is manifest that the Apostles are understood, who were sent out to the Gentiles into the whole world as legates of Christ and messengers of God. Thirdly, to That all those nations were sent envoys in the times of Antiochus, which are commemorated here, does not fit history. And therefore this prophecy is snatched away to that in vain. But concerning the calling of the Gentiles, these things are clear, that it was done from all parts of the earth, some of which are commemorated here, so that it may be established likewise concerning the rest: whence it is placed beyond doubt among all interpreters that this passage treats of the same thing. Musculus himself and Calvin, who referred the preceding things to the Babylonian captivity, were nevertheless forced to acknowledge that these things treat of the calling of the Gentiles to the Church. It signifies, says Calvin, that the knowledge of God is to be spread through the whole world. For the Greeks, Italians, Parthians, Cilicians, and other peoples had heard nothing of pure religion and the sincere worship of God, and the whole world was submerged in the deepest darkness of ignorance. Therefore, God promises that His glory will be known everywhere in the world. But there is an emphasis in the name of the GENTILES: because then the Lord was known to only one people, now He has revealed Himself to all. Musculus interprets this as the Apostles being sent into the four corners of the world: He specifies, he says, certain nations and languages, remote from the people of Israel, through which, however, he also understands the remnants. They understand, however, by this specification, that the four ends of the whole world are expressed, namely the east, the west, the south, and the north. Thus they assign Tarshish to the north: Phul, that is, Africa, to the south: Lud, that is, the Lydians, extending the bow to the east: Tubal and Javan, that is, Italy and the Ionians, namely the Greeks, to the west. By remote islands he understands peoples living more remotely from Israel: whence he also adds: Which have not heard my fame, in Hebrew אֶת שִׁמְעִי, my hearing, that is, they have heard nothing of me, nor have they seen: i.e., nor have they known my glory. To these nations, he says, and those which are still more remote from them, even so far that no mention of me has yet been made among them, I will send Apostles from the number of my elect, sealed and saved. As for the specification of the nations made by the Prophet, there is some difference among interpreters, but they all agree in this, that those nations are to be called to the Church in the time of the New Testament according to the mind of the Prophet. By GENTILES IN THE SEA or OCEAN, Grotius understands those who are situated by the Persian and Arabian sea. Concerning which Jerome says thus: Tarshish is called sea in the Hebrew language, and (as they say) a region of India: although Josephus, with a changed letter, thinks Tarshish is named for the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, to which Jonah, fleeing from Joppa, desired to go. Brentius says, these are the islands of the sea to the WEST of the city of Jerusalem, and the regions which are beyond this sea. But concerning PHUD, Jerome says thus: PHUD or PHUL are the Libyans, and all Africa as far as the sea of Mauretania, in which there is a river today which is called Phud, and its whole region is called Phutensis. So also the LXX interpreters. And we have Grotius agreeing in this. Furthermore, concerning LUD, Jerome has it thus: Lud, he says, they call the Lydians, whose colonists are the Etruscans, who are now called Tuscans, formerly most skilled in shooting arrows, and now they are said to be those stretching the bow. For which in the Hebrew is read מֹשְׁכֵי קֶשֶׁת, which all, except the seventy, translated similarly, stretching the bow. And the seventy placed Mosoch, interpreting the name for the verb. But if this is accepted, it signifies the Cappadocians: whose metropolis is Mazaca, which afterwards received the name Caesarea from Caesar Augustus. Who, wishing I know not what, even in Genesis, interpreted the last son of Aram, i.e. of the Syrians of Damascus, who are called Mes, as Mosoch, for which we do not translate more correctly Maeonians. Brentius notes that Lud in Genesis 10 is recounted among the sons of Shem and thence the name of Lydia has clung. But when it is added STRETCHING or extending THE BOW or Archers, he observes that this is referred either to the nations which were enumerated before, Phul and Lud, or to those nations which descend from Ishmael, and are described in Genesis 30. For it is written of Ishmael in Genesis 21 that he became an archer. Others think they are the Thracians. B. Luther thinks it is a singular nation, such as the Parthians are. TUBAL, however, or Thobet, Jerome continues, is interpreted either as Italy or Iberia, i.e., Spain, from the river Iberus, whence even today the region of the Spains is called Celtiberia. Of whom Lucan beautifully says: The Celts of the Gauls mixing the name of the Iberians: whom we can call Gallo-Spaniards. That which Grotius says can be doubted, whether certain codices had תורל, rests on no just cause. For although Jerome and others read תובל, they nevertheless rendered it Italy. Tubal is recounted in Genesis 10 among the sons of Japheth, and most interpret the region named thence as Italy. The GREEKS, however, as Jerome says again, who are called Javan in the Hebrew language, signify the Ionians: whence also the Greeks are Ionians, and the Ionian sea. And this is to be considered, as Jerome warns, that he placed the nations of Japheth, one of the sons of NOAH, mostly in the East, although in Tarshish and Phud, he also remembered the names of Shem and Ham, i.e., of India and Africa, so that he might show the WHOLE WORLD. It is added, TO THE REMOTE ISLANDS. Grotius understands places far away situated by the sea or rivers. But he does not teach how envoys of the Jews were sent to them for the sake of alliances. FOURTH, the description of these nations and peoples sufficiently teaches what kind are understood, and to what end messengers were sent to them. Who before HAVE NOT HEARD OF ME, says Christ, AND HAVE NOT SEEN before MY GLORY. And therefore the nations, which were without Christ, without God in the world, are noted in Ephesians 2. For which reason Christ sends His envoys to them, so that they may hear of His name, and know His glory and majesty. This is very badly perverted, as if it were only noted that a thin report had reached them concerning Judea and the things done in Judea. FIFTH, the end of the embassy is expressly expressed: AND THEY SHALL ANNOUNCE MY GLORY, that I am the eternal God, and that by my passion I have conquered the devil and death, TO THE GENTILES, so that they may believe in me as their Savior and be saved, John 20:31. Grotius's gloss concerning a history full of the excellent deeds of God is too diluted. If indeed it is not a question of such a history, but of the proclamation of the Gospel, which is the announcement of the glory of Christ, and his glorification, John 16:14. The glory of the Son of God is, says Brentius, that he is true God from eternity, that he is the true Messiah promised by the Prophets, that he is the expiator of our sins, that he is our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption, so that everyone who believes in him may be reckoned righteous before God, and have eternal salvation. This is the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, which the Apostles announced among the nations. SIXTH, the bringing of the brothers from all nations is not the restoration of the captive Jews to their former liberty effected by the Romans and Greeks; because they are to be brought by the Legates of the Son of God, and brought from ALL NATIONS, to whom those legates are to be sent, not from the Greeks and Romans alone. Finally, they shall be brought as a GIFT TO THE LORD. By which is expressed their conversion to the true God, to whom they consecrate themselves, to whom they are a pleasing gift and an acceptable offering. I do not doubt, says Brentius, that Paul had regard to this passage when he wrote thus to the Romans 15: Grace was given to me by God for this, that I should be a minister of Jesus Christ to the nations, administering (sacrificing) the Gospel of God, that the offering of the nations might become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit. Paul, therefore, and his remaining colleagues were true sacrificers: not Mass-priests, but Preachers, who brought the Israelites as an offering to the Lord from all nations, on horses, in chariots, in litters, on mules and in carriages, to the holy mountain of Zion: because by the preaching of the Gospel they gathered the Church from all nations, so that as many as received the Gospel by faith might become a most pleasing offering to God, and be taken up as citizens and heirs of the heavenly unharmed, the Israelites were accustomed to bring their offerings in vessels or instruments purified according to the Law to the temple of the Lord; so in the times of the Messiah, and of his revealed Gospel, the Apostles will bring on horses, chariots, and other kinds of transport, the nations, as an offering to the Lord far more acceptable than that external and Levitical one was. Moreover, it is manifest from the very deeds themselves that this bringing of the nations to the mountain of Zion was not done, nor is it done, in a bodily manner, but through the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: namely, that the nations are then conveyed in chariots and on horses, on mules and in litters, to Zion, when the nations hasten to the preaching of the Apostles and receive the Gospel of Jesus Christ through faith. Therefore, you should understand that you have set out or been conveyed to the holy mountain of Zion when you believe the Gospel of Christ and order your life according to his calling. Thus the nations in Antioch of Pisidia undertook the journey to the holy mountain of God, Jerusalem, when they asked Paul and Barnabas to speak words to them: and when almost the whole city gathered on the Sabbath to hear the word of God. And when Paul, writing to the Colossians, says that the Gospel is bearing fruit in the whole world, it is the same as if he had said that an offering is being brought from all nations to the Lord, to his temple, on horses and in chariots, in litters and in carriages. SEVENTH, since a comparison is instituted here of the sacred offerings of the Old Testament, AS IF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WERE BRINGING A GIFT IN A CLEAN VESSEL INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD, it is manifest that the discourse is not about political liberty, but about such an offering and gift by which the faithful are consecrated to the Lord. For the Holy Spirit is accustomed to describe the spiritual worship of the New Testament with the phrases and similitudes of the Levitical worship of the Old Testament. Those who were directed to the nations, says Jerome, and announced my glory to them, will thus bring your brothers from all nations as a gift to the Lord, with horses and chariots, and mules, and litters, and carriages, and diverse vehicles to the holy mountain of Jerusalem, just as the children of Israel were accustomed, while their religion stood and the ceremonies of the temple were observed, to offer victims with Psalms in the house of the Lord. Or as it is held in the Hebrew, and all have translated with a consonant voice: In a clean vessel: which even to this day the children of Israel, who behold God with their mind, offer in the house of God, which is the Church, as spiritual sacrifices with the fruits and virtues of their soul in clean vessels, that is, in holy bodies. Concerning which the Apostle writes: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Holy Spirit dwells in you? Whence Osiander thus paraphrases. Just as formerly the Israelites conveyed their gifts in clean vessels to the city of Jerusalem, so that they might offer them there in the Temple to the Lord: so from everywhere the Apostles, and their sincere and legitimate successors, will bring from various and far-distant regions, offerings and sacrifices to the Lord (not sheep, oxen, he-goats, or she-goats, nor incense, flour, grain, or other fruits: but they will bring their brothers, whom they have gained for Christ through the Gospel) as an offering to the Lord. They will not be slaughtered in the Church of God, like cattle, nor will they be offered in that manner: but they will slaughter and mortify by faith their old Adam and their wicked concupiscences, and will surrender and resign themselves entirely, with all that they have, into the power and will of the Lord. Of which kind of sacrifice Paul speaks when he says: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, your reasonable service, etc. Rom. 12. Moreover, the nations are brought to the Lord when they are converted to Christ, even if they never change the place of their habitation.
