EIGHTH, the Lord wishes to take as Priests and Levites those from the nations to be called to the Church, and not indeed, as Grotius perverts it, from the Jews who had served in slavery among foreign nations having been captured in war. Whence Jerome: When he says: I will take from them for Priests and Levites, he shows that the old Priesthood is passed over, which was owed to the Levitical tribe: where there is no election, but an order of nature, and a series of family descending through descendants. For the priesthood being translated, it is necessary that a translation of the law also be made, and that the election pertain to those to whom the priesthood is deferred not at all according to blood, but according to merits and virtues, who will come from the islands of the nations, and will announce the glory of the Lord: And they will be brought on horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules, and in carriages. Which was also observed by Blessed Luther: AS IF THY CHILDREN. It is a tacit abrogation of the old sacrifices, when he speaks of new sacrifices. He calls the word of the Gospel a clean vessel, because it is a most pleasant and most pure doctrine. For it makes men pure and pleasant. But the Law is polluted, because it makes men polluted, and it is also polluted and weakened by those who perform it. I WILL TAKE FROM THEM. Not only the sacrifice, but I will abrogate the whole priesthood. For if priests are to be established from the nations, it is necessary that the law of Moses perish entirely, which has priests born from only one tribe. Moreover, there are priests today, as many as teach. The Levites are the hearers. But because he speaks of all nations, he signifies that all nations have the right of priesthood. Finally, lest anyone hesitate regarding the fact that what was treated in the preceding [verses] was about the final judgment, Jerome explained the connection thus: 'But what follows, "I will send from them, who shall have been saved, to the nations," and he enumerates them individually, seems to be contrary to our exposition. For if it is spoken of the day of judgment, how does it return again to the first coming of the Savior, when the Apostles are directed to the nations, and hear from the Lord: "Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit"?' Which is solved thus: the day of judgment is preached, or rather threatened, so that through fear of future punishment they may receive the coming of the Savior and the Gospel of the Apostles, who are to be sent beforehand. But he said beautifully: 'And I will send from them, who shall have been saved.' For unless the Lord had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah. And the Apostle says: 'a remnant has been saved.' These are sent to the nations in Tarshish, and Phud, and Lud, and Meshech, and Tubal, and Greece, and the most distant islands, which have not heard the name of the Lord, nor seen his glory. And it is known that the universal preaching of the Gospel throughout the whole world is reckoned among the signs and antecedents of the final judgment. Finally, lest anyone be able to complain that the Gospel was not revealed to him, and therefore that he is condemned on the last day without his own fault, the Lord therefore adds that he will spread the Gospel into the whole world. What of the fact that Grotius himself acknowledged that these things are to be understood concerning the nations being assumed into the people of God, in his annotations on Mark 9:45, which passage we shall adduce later.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET PONAM IN EIS SIGNVM) Advocabo eos velut signo erecto.

ET MITTAM EX EIS, QVI SALVATI FVE- RINT) Ex Judæis, qui superstites erunt illis temporibus

Antiochi. Mittam, faciam, ut mittantur Legati ad amicitias quærendas. Vide I. Macc. 12, 2. AD GENTES IN MARE) In Hebræo: ad gentes Oceani: id est, ad eos, qui adsiti sunt mari Persico & Arabico. IN AFRICAM) Ex Græcis, qui legerunt פוט, ubi nos habemus פול. Ea est pars Africæ apud Fessam. Vide, quæ diximus in Annotatis ad librum I. de veritate religionis Christianæ. Chaldæus tamen פולאי, id est, πύλαι, portæ Caucasiæ: de quibus vide Plinium 6, 11. ET LYDIAM TENDENTES SAGITTAM) In Hebræo: Et Lydos tendentes arcum. Lydos quidem Cyrus bis subegit, & gentem bellacem omni luxus genere corrumpi voluit, sed facile reditur ad ingenium. Itaq; proverbium inter Græcos natum est: Λυδὸν εἰς πεδίον προσκαλεῖς. IN ITALIAM) Romam usq; cum qua fœdus fecere. Vide 1. Macc. 8. At in Hebræo est תובל, nec aliter legere aut Græci aut Chaldæi. Ea vero est Iberia Asiatica, ut in dictis Annotatis videbit, qui volet. Dubitari potest, an quidam Codices habuerint איתל. ET GRÆCIAM) Vide dictum locum I. Macc. 12, 2. AD INSVLAS LONGE) Ad loca longinqua mari aut amnibus adsita. QUI NON AUDIERUNT DE ME, ET NON VIDERUNT GLORIAM MEAM) Ad quos de Judæa & rebus actis in Judæa tenuis notitia pervenerat. Causas vide apud Josephum contra Appionem priore. ET ANNUNCIABUNT GLORIAM MEAM GENTIBUS) Historiam plenam eximiis Dei factis. Vers. 20. ET ADDUCENT OMNES FRATRES VESTROS DE CVNCTIS GENTIBVS DONVM DOMINO) Id est, in honorem Dei, Romani & Græci in libertatem restituent, ac domum remittent cum honore captivos, quos bellis Macedonico & Syriaco ceperant. Similia exempla benignitatis in socias gentes vide libro 3. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 9, 2. & in Annotatis ad eum locum. QVOMODO SI INFERANT FILII ISRAEL MUNUS IN VASE MVNDO IN DOMVM DOMINI) Pari lætitia ac gaudio. In vase mundo, i. e. in lance bene purgata ab omni immunditie legali. At LXX. per כלי intelligunt instrumenta musica. Vertunt enim μετὰ ψαλμῶν non male. Solet enim כלי sæpe eo sensu sumi, ut 1. Par. 15, 16. 16, 5. 42. 23, 5. 2. Par. 5, 12. 7, 6. 23, 13. 29, 26. 27. 30, 21. 34, 12. Et quod additur ἐπίθετον טהור, id vertitur interdum per ἅγιον, ὅσιον, δόκιμον. Vers. 21. ET ASSVMAM EX EIS IN SACERDOTES ET LEVITAS, AIT DOMINVS) Ex illis Judæis, qui apud gentes externas bello capti servitutem servierant: quasi dicat: non obstabit illis ista non ipsorum culpa, sed ex bellica fortuna tolerata calamitas. Hyrcano quidam objecerunt non posse eum Pontificatu fungi, quod mater ejus captiva aliquando fuisset: nimirum quia captivis feminis ægre creditur de pudicitia. Alioqui postliminii jus omnia restituit in eum statum, in quo ante bellum fuerant.

Continent hæc apertissimam Prophetiam de vocatione gentium ad Ecclesiam. Sed perversissime detorquentur ςεβλότητι prorsus inaudita. Primum quodnam signum ob gentes convocandas erectum sit è loco parallelo, Es. 11. constat. Qui certe non de fœderibus politicis agit, sed de confluxu gentium ad Ecclesiam. Sicut in portibus, inquit Osiander, ad mare collocatur aliquod conspicuum signum, ad quod nautæ cursum dirigere possint: ita erigam vexillum Evangelii, ut ad illud cursum dirigere Gentes & Judæi, & ad portum salutis appellere possint. Pulchre B. Lutherus, verbum ideo SIGNUM est, quod nihil de Ecclesia videtur in mundo nisi verbum. Nam neq; sacramenta quicquam essent, nisi haberent verbum. Deinde cum mittendi ad gentes dicuntur ex iis, qui salvati fuere, non tempore Antiochi superstites, sed illi, qui per fidem servantur è Judæis, & reliquiæ secundum electionem intelliguntur, quemadmodum contextus συνέχεια docet. Neque mittendi dicuntur ceu Legati Politici ad amicitias quærendas, sed ceu Legati & nuncii Filii Dei. Nam hic inquit, ego mittam ex eis, qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes. Unde manifestum est Apostolos intelligi, qui ad gentes in universum terrarum orbem ceu legati Christi & nuncii Dei emissi sunt. Tertio ad illas gentes omnes missos fuisse Legatos tempori- bus Antiochi, quæ hic commemorantur, historiæ non congruit. Ideoq; frustra hoc vaticinium eo ab- ripitur. De vocatione vero gentium hæc clara sunt, ex omnibus terræ partibus facta, quarum aliquæ hic commemoratæ sunt, ut pariter de cæteris sta- tuatur: unde penes Interpp. omnes id extra du- bium positum hic de eadem agi. Musculus ipse & Calvinus, qui superiora ad captivitatem Babyloni- cam retulêre, agnoscere tamen coacti sunt, hæc de gentium vocatione ad Ecclesiam agere. Significat, inquit Calvinus, spargendum esse notitiam Dei per universum orbem. Nam Græci, Itali, Parthi, Cilices, aliique populi nihil de pura Religione & sincero Dei cultu audierant, atq; universus orbis profundissimis ignorantia tenebris submersus erat. Notam ergo ubiq; terrarum fore gloriam DEUS promittit. Subest au- tem emphasis in nomine GENTIUM: quia tunc Dominus uni tantum populo notus erat, nunc omni- bus se patefecit. Musculus de emissis Apostolis in quatuor mundi plagas interpretatur: Speficicat, in- quit, quasdam gentes & linguas, remotas a populo Israëlis, per quas tamen & reliquias intelligit. Intel- ligunt autem per hanc specificationem, quatuor esse to- tius orbis fines expressos, orientem videlicet, occiden- tem, meridiem & septentrionem. Sic deputant Thar- sin Septentrioni: Phul, id est, Aphricam meridiei: Lud, id est, Lydios, arcum extendentes ad orientem: Thubal & Javan, id est, Italiam & Jonas, Græcos videlicet, occidenti. Per Insulas remotas intelligit populus remotius ab Israële habitantes: unde & ad- dit: Quæ non audierunt famam meam, Ebraice אֶת שִׁמְעִי, auditum meum, hoc est, nihil de me audie- runt, nec viderunt: i. e. nec cognoverunt gloriam meam. Ad hasce, inquit, gentes, & quæ adhuc il- lis sunt remotiores, usque adeo, ut nulla dum mei apud ipsas facta sit mentio, mittam Apostolos de numero electorum meorum, signatorum ac ser- vatorum. Quod ad gentium specificationem à Pro- pheta factam, aliqua inter Interpp. differentia est, sed in eo conveniunt omnes, quod gentes illæ vo- candæ sint ad Ecclesiam tempore Novi Testamenti juxta Prophetæ mentem. Per GENTES IN MARI vel OCEANO intelligit Grotius eos, qui adsiti sunt mari Persico & Arabico. De quo ita Hieron. Thar- sis lingua Ebræa mare appellatur, & (ut ajunt) In- diæ regio: licet Josephus littera commutata Tharsum putet nuncupari pro Tharsis urbem Ciliciæ, ad quam Jonas de Joppe fugiens, ire cupiebat. Brentius, hæ sunt, inquit, maris Insulæ ad OCCIDENTEM urbis Hierusalem, & regiones, quæ sunt ultra hoc mare. De PHUD autem ita Hieronymus: PHUD sive PHUL sunt Lybies, omnisque Aphrica usque ad mare Mauritaniæ, in qua fluvius hodie, qui Phud dicitur, & cuncta ejus regio Phutensis dicitur. Sic etiam LXX. Interpp. Et in eo consentientem habemus Grotium. Porro de LUD Hieronymus sic habet: Lud, inquit, Lydos vocant, quorum colo- ni Hetrusci, qui nunc Thusci appellantur, quondam mittendarum sagittarum peritissimi, & nunc dicun- tur tendentes sagittam. Pro quo in Hebraico legitur מֹשְׁכֵי קֶשֶׁת, Quod absq; septuaginta omnes similiter transtulerunt, tendentes arcum. Et septuaginta po- suerunt μοσόχ, nomen pro verbo interpretantes. Quod si accipiatur, Cappadocas significat: quorum Metro- polis Mazaca, quæ postea à Cæsare Augusto, Cæsarea nomen accepit. Qui nescio quid volentes, etiam in Ge- nesi ultimum filium Aram, i. e. Syrorum Damasci, qui appellant Mes, interpretati sunt μοσόχ, pro quo non rectius Mæonas transferimus. Brentius notat, quod Lud Gen. 10. recenseatur inter filios Semi at- que inde nomen Lydiæ hæserit. Quando autem ad- ditur TENENTES seu extendentes SAGITTAM vel Sa- gittarii, hoc vel ad gentes referri observat, quæ pri9 enumeratæ sunt, Phul & Lud, vel ad eas gentes, quæ descendunt ex Ismaël, & descriptæ sunt Gen.30. De Ismaële enim scribitur Genes. 21. quod factus sit vir sagittarius. Alii existimant esse Thraces. B. Luth. putat, singularem nationem esse, quales Parthi sint. THUBAL autem sive Thobet, pergit Hieron. aut Italia interpretatur aut Iberia, h. e. Hispania, ab Ibero flumine, unde & hodie Hispaniarum Regio ap- pellatur Celtiberia. De quibus pulchre Lucanus? Gallorum Celtæ miscentes nomen Iberi : quos nos possumus Gallohifpanos dicere. Quod Grotius dubi- tari posse ait, an quidam Codices תורל habuerint, nulla justa causa nititur. Nam etsi Hieronymus & alii legerent תובל, Italiam tamen reddidere. Re- censetur Gen.10. Thubal inter filios Japheti, ac ple- rique regionem inde vocatam Italiam interpretan- tur. GRÆCI autem, ut iterum Hieron. qui sermo- ne Hebraico appellantur Javan, Jonas significant: unde & Græci Jones, & mare Jonium. Et hoc con- siderandum, monente Hieronymo, quod maximè Orientales de Japheth posuerit nationes, uno filiorum NOE, licet in Tharsis & Phud, Sem quoq; & Cham, i. e. Indiæ & Africæ nominum fuerit recordatus, ut TOTUM ORBEM ostenderet. Additur, AD IN- SULAS LONGE. Grotius intelligit loca longinqua mari aut amnibus adsita. Sed quomodo ad ea missi sint legati Judæorum fæderorum causa, non docet. QUARTO descriptio harum gentium & populorum satis docet, quales intelligantur, & qua fini nuncii ad ipsos missi sint. Qui ante NON AUDIERUNT DE ME, inquit Christus, ET NON VIDERUNT ante GLORI- AM MEAM. Ideoq; gentes, quæ fuerunt sine Chri- sto, sine Deo in mundo notantur Eph. 2. Qua de cau- sa mittit Christus ad illos legatos suos, ut de nomi- ne suo audiant, & gloriam ac majestatem suam co- gnoscant. Pessime hoc pervertitur, quasi id tantum notetur, quod ad illos de Judæa & rebus actis in Ju- dæa tenuis notitia pervenerit. QUINTO exprimitur diserte legationis finis: ET ANNUNCIABUNT GLO- RIAM MEAM, quod sim æternus Deus, & quod pas- sione mea diabolum & mortem vicerim, GENTI- BUS, ut in me Salvatorem suum credant & serventur, Joh. 20, 31. Diluta nimis est Grotii glossa de histo- ria eximiis Dei factis plena. Siquidem non de tali historia, sed de præconio Evangelii agatur, quod est annunciatio gloriæ Christi, ejusq; glorificatio Joh. 16, 14. Gloria Filii Dei est, inquit Brentius, quod sit verus ab æterno Deus, quod sit verus Messias per Prophetas promiss9, quod sit expiator peccatorum nostrorum, quod sit sapientia, justitia, sanctificatio & redemptio nostra, ut omnis, qui credit in ipsum, re- putetur coram Deo justus, & habeat æternam salu- tem. Hoc est Evangelion Domini nostri Jesu Chri- sti, quod Apostoli inter gentes adnunciaverunt. SEXTO adductio fratrum de cunctis gentibus, non est restitutio captivorum Judæorum in libertatem pristinam à Romanis & Græcis facta; quia per Le- gatos Filii Dei adducendi sunt, & adducendi de CUNCTIS GENTIBUS, ad quos mittendi illi legati, non de Græcis solum & Romanis. De- nique adducendi erunt DONUM DOMI- NO. Quo exprimitur conversio eorum ad verum Deum, cui se consecrant, cui gratum sunt munus, & accepta oblatio. Non dubito, inquit Brentius, quin Paulus respexerit ad hunc locum, cum ad Ro- man. 15. sic scriberet: Data est mihi à Deo gratia in hoc, ut sim minister Jesu Christi, in gentes admini- strans (sacrificans) Evangelion Dei, ut fiat oblatio gentium acceptabilis, sanctificata per Spiritum San- ctum. Paulus igitur, & reliqui collegæ ejus fuerunt veri sacrificuli: Non Missarii, sed Concionatorii qui adduxerunt Israëlitas in oblationem Domini, ex omnibus gentibus, in equis, in quadrigis, in le- cticis, in mulis & carrucis, ad montem sanctum Zion: quia prædicatione Evangelii collegerunt Ec- clesiam ex omnibus gentibus, ut, quotquot Evan- gelium fide acceperunt, facta sint oblatio Dei gra- tissima, & assumpti sint in cives & hæredes cœlestis regni. Nam quemadmodum stante adhuc incolumi Republica Mosaica, Israëlitæ adducere solent obla- tiones suas in vasis seu instrumentis juxta Legem purificatis, ad templum Domini; ita temporibus Mesiæ, & revelati Evangelii ejus, adducent Aposto- li in equis, quadrigis & aliis vecturæ generib9, gen- tes, in oblationem Domini longe acceptiorem, qua illa externa & Levitica fuit. Manifestum autem est ex ipsis gestis reb9, quod hæc gentium adductio ad montem Zion nec facta sit, nec fiat corporali mo- do, sed per Evangelium Domini nostri Jesu Christi: videlicet quod tunc gentes advehuntur in curribus & equis, in mulis & lecticis, ad Zionem, cum gen- tes properant ad concionem Apostolorum, & acci- piunt Evangelion Jesu Christi per fidem. Itaque tunc sentias, te profectum aut advectum esse ad montem sanctum Zion, cum credis Evangelio Christi, & instituis vitam tuam ad vocationem ejus. Sic susceperunt gentes in Antiochia Pisidiæ profe- ctionem ad montem sanctum Dei Hierusalem, cum rogarent Paulum & Barnabam, ut sibi loque- rentur verba: & cum universa fere civitas convenit Sabbato ad audiendum verbum Dei. Et cum Pau- lus ad Colossenses scribens, dicit, Evangelion in to- to mundo fructificare, idem est ac si dixisset, ex uni- versis gentibus adduci oblationem Domino, ad templum ejus, in equis & quadrigis, in lecticis & carrucis. SEPTIMO, cum hic comparatio insti- tuatur oblationum sacrarum Veteris Testamenti, QUOMODO SI INFERANT FILII ISRAEL MUNUS IN VASE MUNDO IN DOMUM DOMINI, manifestum est, non de libertate politi- ca sermonem esse, sed de tali oblatione ac dono, quo fideles consecrantur Domino. Phrasibus e- nim & similitudinibus cultus Levitici Vet. Testam. solet describere Spiritus Sanctus cultum spiritua- lem Novi Testamenti. Qui ad gentes directi fue- rint, ait Hieronymus, & annunciaverint eis gloriam meam, sic adducent fratres vestros de universis natio- nibus munus Domino, cum equis & quadrigis, & mulis, & lecticis, & carrucis, & diversis vehiculis in montem sanctum Hierusalem, quomodo solebant filii Israël, dum eorum staret religio, & templi ceremo- niæ servarentur, offerre victimas cum Psalmis in do- mo Domini. Sive ut habetur in Hebræo, & omnes voce consona transtulerunt: In vase mundo: quod & usq; hodie offerunt in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia, filii Israël, qui mente conspiciunt Deum, hostias spiri- tuales cum fructibus atque virtutibus animæ suæ in vasis mundis, hoc est, in sanctis corporibus. De quibus Apostolus scribit: An ignoratis, quia templum Dei estis, & Spiritus S. habitat in vobis? Unde Osiander ita παραφράζει. Sicut olim Israëlitæ in vasis mun- dis advehebant dona sua ad urbem Jerusalem, ut ea ibi in Templo Domino offerrent: ita undiquaque Apostoli, eorumque successores sinceri & legitimi adducent ex variis & longe dissitis regionibus, ob- lationes & sacrificia Domino (non oves, boves, hircos, aut capras, ne thus, farinam, frumentum, aut alias fruges: sed adducent fratres suos, quos per Evangelion Christo lucrifecerunt) in oblationem Domino. Illi non mactabuntur in Ecclesia Dei, ut pecudes, nec ad eum modum offerentur: sed illi mactabunt & mortificabunt ex fide veterem suum Adamum & pravas suas concupiscentias, seq; totos cum omnibus, quæ habent, tradent & refignabunt in potestatem & voluntatem Domini. De quo fa- crificii genere loquitur Paulus, cum inquit: Obse- cro vos fratres, per misericordiam Dei, ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo pla- centem, rationabile obsequium vestrum, &c. Rom. 12. Adducuntur autem gentes Domino, cum ad Christum convertuntur, etsi locum habitationis suæ nunquam mutent. OCTAVO assumere vult Dominus in Sacerdotes & Levitas ex gentibus vo- candis ad Ecclesiam, non vero uti pervertit Gro- tius, ex Judæis, qui apud gentes externas bello capti servitutem servierant. Unde Hieronymus: Quan- do dicit: Assumam ex iis in Sacerdotes & Levitas, ostendit vetus Sacerdotium prætermissum, quod tribui Leviticæ debebatur: ubi non est electio, sed ordo natu- ræ, & series est familiæ per posteros descendens. Trans- lato enim sacerdotio, necesse est, ut & legis translatio fiat, & electio ad eos pertineat, quibus nequaquam juxta sanguinem, sed juxta merita atque virtutes sa- cerdotium defertur, qui venient de insulis gentium, & gloriam Domini nunciabunt: Et adducentur in equis, & in quadrigis, & in lecticis, & in mulis, & in carrucis. Quod etiam observatum B. Luthero: QUOMODO SI FILII TUI. Est tacita abroga- tio veterum sacrificiorum, cum de novis sacrificiis di- cit. Vas mundum appellat verbum Evangelii, quod sit jucundissima & purissima doctrina. Facit enim puros & jucundos homines. Lex autem polluta est, quia pollutos facit, & à facientibus quoq; polluitur & infirmatur. ASSVMAM EX EIS. Non solum sa- crificium, sed totum sacerdotium abrogabo. Si enim ex gentibus constituendi sunt sacerdotes, necesse est Mosi legem prorsus interire, quæ Sacerdotes ex una tantum tribu natos habet. Sunt autem hodie Sa- cerdotes, quotquot docent. Levitæ sunt auditores. Quia autem de omnibus gentibus dicit, significat o- mnes gentes jus Sacerdotii habere. Deniq; ne quis in eo hæreat, quod in superioribus actum fuerit de ex- tremo judicio, Hieronymus ita nexum expedivit: Quod autem sequitur, mittam ex eis, qui salvati fue- rint, ad gentes, & singulas enumerat, videtur exposi- tioni nostræ esse contrarium. Si enim de die judicii di- citur, quomodo rursum ad primum recurrit Salva- toris adventum, quando Apostoli diriguntur ad gen- tes, & audiunt à Domino: Ite, docete omnes gen- tes, baptizantes eas in nomine Patris & Filii & Spi- ritus Sancti? Quod ita solvitur: judicii prædicatur dies, imo comminatur: ut metu futuræ pœnæ reci- piant Salvatoris adventum & Apostolorum Evan- gelium, qui ante mittendi sunt. Pulchre autem dixit: Et mittam ex eis, qui salvati fuerint. Nisi enim Do- minus reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma essemus, & similes Gomorræ fuissemus. Et Apostolus: reli- quiæ, inquit, salvæ factæ sunt. Isti mittuntur ad gentes in Tharsis, & Phud, & Lud, & Mosoch, & Thobel, & Græciam & insulas plurimas, quæ longe sunt: & quæ non audierunt nomen Domini, neque viderunt gloriam ejus. Et notum est, quod signis & antecedentibus extremi judicii accenseatur univer- salis prædicatio Evangelii per totum orbem. Deniq; ne quis conqueri possit, sibi non revelatum Evange- lium, itaque se præter culpam suam in novissimo die damnari, ideo subjicit Dominus, se vulgaturum Ev- angelium in orbem terrarum. Quid quod Gro- tius ipse agnovit de gentibus assumendis in popu- lum Dei hæc intelligenda esse annot. ad Marc. 9, 45. quem locum postea adducturi sumus.

## 66:22
Vers. 22.

FOR AS THE NEW HEAVENS AND THE NEW EARTH) See above 65, 17, and what was said there.

That this treats of the heavenly state of the elect is apparent both from the opposition of the infernal state of the damned, v. 24, and from parallel passages, 2 Pet. 3:13, Apoc. 21. Nor does Cornel. à Lap. deny this, alleging for that matter the opinion of the ancients also: The sense is, he says, as if to say, for the faithful, especially in the heavenly and triumphant Church, there will be perpetual solemnity, perpetual rest and exultation, perpetual Sabbatism, perpetual New Moon, that is, a perpetual renewal of joy, grace, and glory, whereas on the contrary for the impious and damned there will be eternal fire, with the worm, as follows. Thus Theodor., St. August., and Tertul. These are the words of Cornelius.

SO SHALL YOUR SEED AND YOUR NAME STAND] It shall shine like the heaven, it shall flourish like the earth.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

QUIA SICUT COELI NOVI ET TERRA NOVA) Vide supra 65, 17. & ibi dicta.

De cœlesti statu electorum hæc agere, cum ex oppositione status infernalis damnatorum v. 24. tum è locis parallelis 2. Petr. 3, 13. Apoc. 21. apparet. Neque id diffitetur Cornel. à Lap. allegans eam in rem etiam veterum sententiam: Sensus est, inquit, q. d. fidelibus in Ecclesia præsertim cælesti, & trium- phante perpetua erit solemnitas, perpetua quies & exultatio, perpetuus Sabbatismus, perpetua Neome- nia, id est, perpetua gaudii, gratiæ & gloriæ innovatio, cum ex adverso impiis & damnatis æternus erit ignis, cum vermis, ut sequitur. Ita Theodor. S. August. & Tertul. Hæc Gornelius.

SIC STABIT SEMEN VESTRUM ET NO- MEN VESTRUM] Splendebit ut cœlum, florebit ut terra.

## 66:23
Ver. 23. AND IT SHALL BE MONTH FROM MONTH, AND SABBATH FROM SABBATH, ALL FLESH SHALL COME, TO WORSHIP BEFORE MY FACE, SAITH THE LORD] Men of every kind and nation shall come to worship in the outer court of the Gentiles. And that shall happen not only every month, but every week. You have a similar manner of speaking in Amos 8:5. See what was said on John 12:20.

That these things are not to be explained as referring to the external splendor and flower of the seed and name of Israel in the polity, nor to the gathering at the outer court of the Gentiles, is sufficiently convinced both by what precedes and by the very emphasis of the words. For mention is made of NEW HEAVENS and a NEW EARTH, of which we spoke at ch. 65:17: which denote the seat of eternal blessedness. Nor is this a discourse about the temporal duration of the Jewish seed and name, which was not preserved for a long time from the age of Judas Maccabeus, but about its eternal preservation, while the new heaven and new earth shall stand. Just as the new heaven shall stand immovable and the new earth incorruptible forever, so also shall your spiritual seed be stable, and your name; the salvation of the Lord's elect shall be stable, so that not one of them may be snatched from the hand of the Lord; John 10. Nor shall the Church of the Lord ever be destroyed, but on the contrary it is to prevail against all the gates of hell and be preserved forever. AND IT SHALL BE MONTH FROM MONTH (or rather new moon) AND SABBATH FROM SABBATH, that is, in the other life there shall be perpetual festivity, since the day of the new moon was a feast day of every month and the Sabbath day was holy to the Jews. Thus in the other life one festivity shall succeed another. We shall celebrate perpetual feast days without any labor and trouble. There shall be true, most holy, and most pleasant rest and recreation from all the miseries of life. Yet that rest shall not be spent in carnal and profane desires. But ALL FLESH SHALL COME, that is, those who shall be in the new heavens and new earth, for those are proposed as the seat and dwelling-place of the blessed: TO WORSHIP BEFORE MY FACE, it shall stand before my throne and serve me and celebrate me without end nights and days in my temple, into all eternity Apoc. 7:15. B. Gerhardus on the consummation. Sec. II. 45. paraphrases this passage thus: There shall be in eternal life perpetual festivity and most peaceful rest, because the new moons and Sabbaths were feast days for the Israelite people. Thus, therefore, the Prophet describes the things of the future age with the vocabulary of this age. Jerome has it thus: But when the new heaven and the new earth shall be, and the new Jerusalem, so that it may in no wise be said: Heaven and earth shall pass away. And again, the heaven shall be rolled up like a book, and the earth shall be dissipated by corruption: So in all things new, the people of God shall also become new, the Scripture saying: Old things have passed away, behold all things have become new. And in another place, if any is a new creature in Christ, there shall also be a new people. For Christ is the firstfruits. Then those who are Christ's at his coming. And the new heaven and earth: of which it is said among the eight beatitudes: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for they shall possess the earth: Since every creature is now subject to vanity in hope, because of him who subjected it. But they shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glory of the children of God, who from men shall become his children: and they shall stand in his sight always, and their name shall remain continually, so that no other nation may succeed them, which happened in the case of the Jews, but they shall remain forever. And it shall be (he says) month from month, and sabbath from sabbath, so that from carnal Sabbaths and months they may become spiritual, delicate sabbaths, which sabbatism is reserved for the people of God. Although Jerome and others interpret the coming of all flesh into the sight of the Lord as referring to the coming of the Gentiles and peoples to the Church, they do not, however, exclude worship in the heavenly Jerusalem: because it does not terminate in this age, but is consummated in the other. What follows (sc. in the LXX.) says Jerome, all flesh shall come to worship in my sight in Jerusalem, it should be known that in the Hebrew it is not written: Jerusalem, so that we may lower the eyebrow of the Jews: but only in my sight, so that the word of the Lord may be fulfilled, saying in the Gospel: Amen amen I say to you, when the hour shall come; when you shall worship the Father neither in this mountain, nor in Jerusalem. And again. God is a Spirit, And those who worship him, must worship in Spirit and in truth. And that of the Apostle; Lifting up holy hands in every place. But all flesh signifies not the people of the Jews, but the whole human race: according to that which was said above: All flesh shall see thy salvation. And in Joel: I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. And in Zechariah: Let all flesh fear before the face of the Lord. And in the Psalms: To thee all flesh shall come. Which is said in other words in another Psalm: All nations, which thou hast made, shall come and worship in thy sight; and shall glorify thy name O Lord. Afterwards he adds: All flesh, which is to worship in the sight of the Lord, either in the heavenly Jerusalem, or in every place in which pure hands are lifted up, etc. Finally, from the antithesis of death and eternal condemnation, it is manifest that that worship in the sight of the Lord in the new heavens and new earth is to be understood of the happiness and celebration of the blessed in eternal life. Which Jerome also acknowledged, when he says: THEY SHALL GO FORTH not in place but in understanding. For the corpses of the dead cannot be within with the Lord. But if all flesh is to worship the Lord, and on the contrary the corpses of men who have transgressed against the Lord shall be delivered to eternal burnings, there will be a resurrection of true flesh in both respects. Nor do the Hebrews deny this. For thus in Midrash Tillim on Psalm 90:15: Thus God in the future age will make for Himself one day, which is spoken of in Zech. 14:7. And it shall be one day and it is known to the Lord: not day, nor night: and at the time of evening there shall be light: this day is the future age and the vivification of the dead: and that is the light which God laid up for the righteous in the beginning of the world, namely that of which it is said in Gen. 1:4. And He saw the light that it was good: and again He says of it in Ps. 97:11. Light is sprung up for the righteous: and again Ps. 36:10. For with Thee is the fountain of life, in Thy light we shall see light. Furthermore he also says, Isa. last [chapter] verse 23. And it shall be from the sufficiency of month in its month and from the sufficiency of Sabbath in its Sabbath: that is the future age, which will be entirely a Sabbath, i.e., rest. Grotius in his gloss concerning the coming of other nations weekly, and others monthly, is not far from the fiction of the Chiliasts, which Jerome reports thus: They ridiculously interpret 'month from month, sabbath from sabbath, in which all flesh shall come to worship God,' the Chiliastai, whom we can call millenarians, as those who are in the vicinity should come to Jerusalem every Sabbath, those who are further away, by months, that is, when the cycle of the calends is complete, those who are very far away, by individual years, that is, on the days of Passover or of Tabernacles: according to that which is said in Zechariah: They shall go up from year to year, to adore the Lord the King of hosts the feast of tabernacles. And to provide greater laughter for their listeners, regarding what is written in the last volume of the same Prophet: And there shall be no merchant any more in the house of the Lord of hosts in that day, they interpret it so that merchants cease to exist in a thousand years. Because all things are born in all places, so that, clearly, we do not need leaf, amomum, and pepper, nor do the Indians desire pennyroyal from us. This is Jerome.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ERIT MENSIS EX MENSE, ET SABBATUM EX SABBATO, VENIET OMNIS CARO, UT ADORET CORAM FACIE MEA, AIT DOMINUS] Omnis generis gentisque homines venient oraturi in subdiali Gentium. Idque non tantum fiet singu- lis mensibus, sed quaque hebdomade. Simile loquendi ge- nus habes apud Amosum 8, 5. Vide quæ dicta ad Joh. 12, 20.

Non de splendore & flore seminis & nominis Israelis externo in politia, nec de confluxu ad sub- diale gentium hæc explicanda esse tum superiora sa- tis convincunt, tum ipsa verborum emphasis do- cet. COELI enim Novi & TERRÆ NOVÆ mentio fit, de quibus ad c. 65, 17. diximus: quæ se- dem æternæ beatitudinis notant. Neque de tempo- rali duratione seminis & nominis Judaici, quod non longum tempus inde ab ætate Judæ Maccabæi con- servatum fuit, sed de æterna ejusdem conservatio- ne, dum œlum novum & terra nova stabit, hic ser- mo est. Quemadmodum cœlum novum immobile, terra nova incorruptibilis stabit in æternum, sic etiam stabile erit semen vestrum spirituale, & no- men vestrum, electis Domini salus erit stabilis, ut nec quisquam eorum è manu Domini eripiatur; Joh. 10. neque Ecclesia Domini unquam deleatur, sed contra omnes inferorum portas prævalitura & in æternum conservanda sit. ET ERIT MEN- SIS EX MENSE (vel potius novilunium) ET SABBATUM EX SABBATO, in altera sc. vita perpetua erit festivitas, qui dies novilunii mensis cujusque festus dies & dies Sabbati sanctus erat Judæis. Ita altera vita una festivitas excipiet aliam. Perpetuos dies festos absq; omni labore & molestia agemus. Ibi erit vera sanctissima & jucun- dissima quies & recreatio ab omnibus vitæ miseriis. Nec tamen ea quies transigetur carnalibus & pro- phanis cupiditatibus. Sed VENIET OMNIS CARO, quæ sc. in novis cælis & nova terra erit, nam illa ut sedes & habitaculum beatorum propo- nuntur: UT ADORET CORAM FACIE MEA, stabit coram throno meo & serviet mihi ac ce- lebrabit me sine fine noctes & dies in templo meo, in omnem æternitatem Apoc. 7, 15. B. Gerhardus de consum. Sec. II. 45. hunc locum sic παραφράζει: E- rit in vita æterna perpetua festivitas & quies pacatissi- ma, quia neomenia & Sabbata erant populo Israëli- tico dies festivi. Sic ergo verbo hujus seculi descri- bit Propheta res futuri seculi. Hieronymus ita ha- bet: Quando autem cælum novum & terranova e- rit, & nova Hierusalem, ut nequaquam dicatur: Cœlum & terra pertransibunt. Et iterum, invol- vetur cœlum quasi liber, & corruptione dissipabi- tur terra: Sic in omnibus novis novus fiet & populus Dei, dicente Scriptura: Vetera transierunt, ecce fa- cta sunt omnia nova. Et in alio loco, siqua in Christo nova Creatura, erit q́, & populus novus. Primitiæ enim Christus. Deinde qui sunt Christi in adventu ejus. Cœlumque & terra nova: de quibus inter octo beatitudines dicitur: Beati pauperes Spiritu, quo- niam possidebunt terram: Siquidem omnis creatura nunc subjecta est vanitati in spe, propter eum, qui sub- jecit eam. Liberabuntur autem a servitute corru- ptionis in gloria filiorum Dei, qui fient de hominibus filii ejus: & stabunt in conspectu illius semper, & nomen eorum jugiter permanebit, ut nequaquam illis gens succedat alia, quod factum est in Judæis, sed maneant in æternum. Et erit (inquit) mensis ex mense, & sabbatum ex sabbato, ut de carnalibus Sabbatis mensibusq; fiant spiritualia sabbata delica- ta, qui sabbatismus Dei populo reservatur. Quan- quam verò Hieronymus & alii adventum omnis carnis in conspectum Domini de adventu gentium & populorum ad Ecclesiam etiam interpretentur, non tamen excludunt adorationem in cœlesti Hie- rosolymâ : quia non terminatur ea in hoc seculo, sed consuminatur in altero. Quod sequitur (sc. apud LXX.) inquit Hieron. veniet omnis caro, ut adoret in conspectu meo in Hierusalem, sciendum quod in Hebraico non sit scriptum: Hierusalem, ut decutiamus supercilium Judæorum: sed tantum in conspectu meo, ut sermo Domini compleatur, dicen- tis in Evangelio: Amen amen dico vobis, quum ve- niet hora; quum neq; in monte isto, neq; in Hiero- solymis adorabitis Patrem. Et iterum. Spiritus est Deus, Et eos qui adorant eum, in Spiritu & ve- ritate oportet adorare. Et illud Apostoli; Levantes sanctas manus in omni loco. Omnis autem caro non populum Judæorum, sed omne hominum significat genus: juxta illud quod supra dictum est: Videbit omnis caro salutare tuum. Et in Joële : Effundam de Spiritu meo super omnem carnem, & propheta- bunt filii vestri & filiæ vestræ. Et in Zacharia: Ti- meat omnis caro à facie Domini. Et in Psalmis: Ad te omnis caro veniet. Quod aliis verbis in alio Psalmo dicitur: Omnes gentes, quas fecisti, venient & adorabunt in conspectu tuo; & glorificabunt nomen tuum Domine. Postea addit: Omnis ca- ro, quæ adoratura est in conspectu Domini, vel in Hierusalem cœlesti, vel in omni loco, in quo levan- tur mundæ manus &c. Deniq; ex antithesi mortis & condemnationis æternæ manifestum est, adora- tionem illam in conspectu Domini in cœlis novis & terra nova de beatorum felicitate & celebratio- ne in æterna vita intelligenda esse. Quod etiam agnovit Hieronymus, cum ait : EGREDIEN- TUR non loco sed intelligentia. Neq; enim cadave- ra mortuorum possunt intus esse cum Domino. Quod si omnis caro est adoratura Dominum, & è contrario cadavera virorum, qui prævaricati sunt in Domino, æternis tradentur ardoribus, in utramq; partem veræ carnis erit resurrectio. Neque abnuunt Hebræi. Nam ita in Midrasch Tillim super Psalmum 90, 15. Sic Deus in futuro seculo faciet sibi unam diem, quod dicitur Zachar. 14, 7. Et erit dies unus & ipse no- tus est Domino: non dies, neque nox: & ad tempus vesperi erit lux: iste dies est seculum futu- rum & vivificatio mortuorum: & istud est lumen, quod Deus reposuit justis in principio mundi, videli- cet de quo dicitur Gen. 1, 4. Et vidit ipsum lumen quod esset bonum: & iterum dicit de ipso Ps. 97, 11. Lumen ortum est justis: & iterum Ps. 36, 10. Quo- niam tecum est fons vitæ, in lumine tuo videbimus lumen. Adhæc etiam dicit, Esa. ult. vers. 23. Et erit ex sufficientia mensis in mense suo & ex sufficientia Sabbati in Sabbato suo: istud est seculum futurum, quod totum erit Sabbatum, i. e. requies. Grotius glossa sua de adventu aliarum gentium hebdoma- dico, aliarum menstruo, parum abest à commento Chiliastarum, quod ita refert Hieronymus: Men- sem ex mense, sabbatum ex sabbato, in quibus ve- niet omnis caro, ut adoret Deum, ridicule interpre- tantur Χιλιάσαι, quos nos dicere possumus milliarios, ut qui in vicino sunt, omni Sabbato veniant in Hieru- salem, qui longius, per menses, id est, calendarum orbe completo, qui valde procul, per annos singulos, hoc est diebus Paschæ sive tabernaculorum: juxta illud quod in Zacharia dicitur: Ascendent ab anno in annum, ut adorent Dominum regem exercituum & celebrent festivitatem tabernaculorum. Et ut majorem risum præbeant audientibus, quod in ultimo ejusdem Prophetæ volumine scribitur: Et non erit mercator ultra in domo Domini exercituum in die illo, sic interpretantur, ut negotiatores in mille annis esse desistant. Quia omnia nascantur in omnibus lo- cis, quo scilicet nec nos indigeamus folio amomo & pi- pere, nec Indi à nobis puleium desiderent. Hæc Hie- ronymus.

## 66:24
Verse 24. AND THEY SHALL GO FORTH] Wandering through Judea.

AND THEY SHALL SEE THE CARCASSES OF THE MEN WHO HAVE TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME] That is, of those who were on the side of Antiochus.

THEIR WORM SHALL NOT DIE] That is, for a long time the worm shall feed on their carcasses, because they will be judged unworthy of burial.

AND THEIR FIRE SHALL NOT BE EXTINGUISHED.] Metonymy, that is, the fire of the signs in the burned towns. See what was said above in 16. Mystically, however, the Jews also draw these things to the day of Judgment. The Chaldean also does so in this place.

AND THEY SHALL BE UNTO SATIETY OF SIGHT TO ALL FLESH] To the point of nausea; that is, they shall stir up an odious stench from themselves.

As many words, so many perversions; first, he explains the going forth as a wandering through Judea. Will the elect therefore wander forth from the new heavens and the new earth? And how does this consist with a perpetual dwelling before the Lord and an eternal festival? They shall go forth, therefore, not in place, as Jerome says, but in understanding. The Holy Spirit uses the words of this age to describe the things of the future. The simile is taken from a bodily victory, where citizens go forth to see with pleasure the prostrate enemies. Furthermore, not the carcasses of those who were on the side of Antiochus, but in general those who have transgressed against Christ, which happens through unbelief, which is the cause of damnation, John 3:16, 17; Luke 5:14, shall be seen; how, namely, they themselves shall lie like sheep placed in hell and death shall feed upon them. Psalm 49:15. The blessed shall behold with pleasure the eternal punishments of the impious. For just as they will congratulate themselves perpetually on the mercy of God, which they have obtained, so they will also approve of God's justice, by which He will most severely punish the impious. Thirdly, THE WORM NOT DYING is taken as a natural worm, contrary to the force of the word and the explanation of Christ in Mark 9. Fourthly, their worm is said not to die, because it never dies, as the particle absolutely denying and its exposition teaches. On the contrary, Grotius understands it as a worm feeding for a long time on unburied carcasses. Christ hints that the worm of conscience consuming souls eternally is designated by the Prophet. Grotius interprets it as a natural worm that feeds on carcasses. FIFTHLY, the fire that shall not be extinguished, Grotius understands as the fire of the signs in burned towns, and thus places a Metonymy here. But that it is not to be understood metonymically, the predicate teaches: IT SHALL NOT BE EXTINGUISHED. For neither burning nor extinction belongs to signs. SIXTHLY, those things which treat of the inextinguishable fire of Gehenna, and are thus explained by Christ in Mark 9:45, Grotius explains as the fire in burned towns. He acknowledges that they are understood by the Jews as referring to the day of judgment, even by the Chaldean in this place, but he says that they understand these things only mystically; perverting their mind in the same way. Because they render the literal sense, those who explain it thus from the Jews, nor do either the Chaldean or others acknowledge another sense of the Prophet's words. The Chaldean translates it thus: And the impious shall be judged in Gehenna, until the just say over them, we have seen enough. This is, the Jews say, as it is reported in the Pugio Fidei, part 2, ch. 11, q. 20, that each just person, once he has seen them (the damned) full of immortal worms, is going to say, it is enough for me, I do not wish to see them anymore for eternity, and this is what is written in the last verse of the last chapter of Isaiah. And they shall go forth and see the carcasses of those who have been guilty against me: therefore their worm shall not die and their fire shall not be extinguished, and they shall be unto satiety to all flesh. R. Joseph in the Talmud in Pesach Schenu said: the fire, which the holy and blessed God created on the second Sabbath, that is, the second day of the week, shall not be extinguished for eternity. Just as it is said in Isaiah 66, last chapter. And they shall go forth, etc. There is also a tradition: R. Benach said, why was it not said on the second day of the week, Gen. 1, And God saw that it was good! Because the fire of Gehenna was created on it. Add that Grotius himself acknowledged in his annotations to Mark 9:45 that the very propriety of the words serves wonderfully for describing perpetual punishments. Whence, although he did not indeed refer them to those things which happened in the time of Antiochus, but to the (most recent) Jerusalem destruction in those Annotations, where he had not yet dreamed anything of that new gloss, as if these things pertained to the times of Antiochus, but said that the Prophet meant by this whole prophecy, what he often said elsewhere: that it would come to pass that the nations would be taken into the people of God, who would serve God not according to the rites of the flesh, but according to the law of the Spirit: but that those who had despised the salutary admonitions (the Jews, namely) would perish most miserably: yet he professed that these things more properly suit eternal punishments. For that, he says, does not end, and is not extinguished, has its sense in the Jerusalem destruction indeed, but restricted and limited by reason of the matter, yet in the punishments of the other life it has another, and that which is properly spoken. He adds that this opinion had been received among the Jews: which he confirms from the Apocryphal writings. Sirach 7:19. ἐκδίκησις ἀσεβῆς πῦρ ϰὴ σκώληξ. And Judith 16:21: 'to give fire and worms into their flesh.' Grotius says this there; why then does he now depart from the literal meaning? Why does he abandon the sense which the words of the Prophet convey, and which is the literal meaning? Why does he desert the opinion common in the ancient Church of the Jews, and adopt one that never entered anyone's mind, and which he himself, when comparing the passage of the Prophet with the words of Christ, would undoubtedly not have approved, since it is entirely alien to the mind of Christ, and indeed even to the sense of the Jewish Church? What is suggested regarding a double sense, one less literal and one literal, which is accustomed to have a place in prophecies containing a type, has been frequently refuted by us, nor could it hitherto be proven by any example of Scripture; here it certainly has no place. For how will it be taught that that miserable destruction of the Jews in the final overthrow was proposed as a type of eternal condemnation in those words 'THE WORM DOES NOT DIE, THE FIRE IS NOT EXTINGUISHED,' or that it was believed among the Jews, or that it ought to be believed by us? Saint Augustine, in book 20 of The City of God, chapter 22, indeed reports that the living worm and the unquenchable fire were explained differently by others. 'Some,' he says, 'referred both to the body, others both to the soul. Others referred the fire literally to the body, but the worm figuratively to the soul, which seems to be MORE PROBABLE.' But there was no doubt about the fact that these things pertain to the INFERNAL punishments of the wicked. Regarding those different opinions, let the same author also be consulted in book 21, chapter 9, in which he leaves judgment free to anyone: 'Let each one choose what pleases him, either to attribute the fire to the body and the worm to the soul, the former literally, the latter figuratively.' For I have already argued sufficiently above that animals can live even in fires, in burning without consumption, in pain without death, by the miracle of the most omnipotent Creator, he who denies that this is possible for Him, is ignorant of the source from which comes whatever is admired in all of nature. For He Himself is God, who made all the miracles in this world, both great and small, which we have mentioned, and even incomparably more which we have not mentioned, and included the same within the world itself the greatest miracle of all. Let each person choose one of the two which he may approve, whether he considers the word "worm" to pertain properly to the body, or metaphorically to the soul, transferred from corporeal to incorporeal things. This, however, he places beyond doubt, that these things treat not of the destruction of Jerusalem, or any other temporal punishment, but solely of the eternal and infernal penalty of the damned. Jerome, in this place, says: "The worm, which shall not die, and the fire, which shall not be quenched, is understood by MOST as the conscience of sins, which torments those established in punishment, etc." Isidore, Book 1, On the Chief Good, Chapter 3: There is a twofold punishment for the damned in hell, whose mind sadness burns and whose body flame burns in turn, so that those who devised in the mind what they carried out in the body may be punished in both soul and body at once. Ambrose, Book 7, On Luke, Chapter 14: Just as many fevers and worms arise from indigestion when someone consumes food intemperately, so if anyone heaps sins upon sins and does not digest them through repentance, but mixes sins with sins, he contracts an indigestion of old and recent offenses, and thence he is burned by a fire as if by a fever of his own, and he will be consumed by worms, that is, he will be tormented and tortured even unto consumption and death, yet in such a way that he is never consumed and dead. Innocent III, Book on the Contempt of the World: The worm, he says, will lacerate the conscience in a threefold way: memory will afflict it, late repentance will disturb it, and anguish will torment it. He is, however, mistaken in this, that he understands the worm and the fire as double; both worm and fire are double, interior and exterior, the interior which gnaws and burns the heart, the exterior which gnaws and burns the body. He is mistaken, I say, if it is understood as the Papists understand it; as if not only the worm of conscience were denoted tropically, but also literally horrible, most foul, most biting, and eternal bodily worms were designated in hell, just as Cornel. à Lapide philosophizes about them ad h. l., who strives at length to show that such are intended here by the Prophet, and will have a place in hell. One and the same word cannot be taken in the same place both literally and figuratively at the same time; nor will bodily worms exist in the other world, or be immortal; and therefore we leave those fables to the Papists. When you hear of the worm, Gregory of Nyssa has already warned the Catechumens, Orat. Catech. c. 40. do not let your thought be carried away to this earthly animal simply because the name is the same. For the addition of the words "that dieth not" suggests that a nature other than that which is known must be understood. SEVENTHLY, Grotius explains the final words concerning the stench of corpses. But what does such a stench, what does the nausea arising from it, have to do with the worm THAT DIETH NOT, with the FIRE UNQUENCHABLE, that is, with the eternal punishment of the damned! In the Hebrew these things are stated thus: AND THEY SHALL BE AN ABHORRING UNTO ALL FLESH, that is, all the blessed shall perpetually detest the impious and the damned, nor shall they be touched by any pity for them, but shall abhor their impiety and blasphemy, solely celebrating the divine justice and truth. The bodies of the damned, although animated, are called corpses, both because they are foul and stinking like corpses, and because they are in eternal death and at the same time in eternal punishment: for in order to signify death, He said corpses, but in order to express a life more bitter than any death, He said the worm that dieth not, and the fire that is not quenched. And therefore rightly does St. Bernard, lib. 5 de consider. c. 12, say: This is, that the worm which dieth not, the memory of things past, once injected or rather innate through sin, has clung firmly, never thereafter to be torn away. Nor does it cease to gnaw the conscience, and fed by that food, which is indeed inexhaustible, it perpetuates life. The holy man adds: I shudder at the biting worm and the living death. I shudder to fall into the hands of living death and dying life. This is the second death, which never perishes, but always kills. Who will grant them to die once, that they may not die for eternity; who say to the mountains, fall upon us, and to the hills cover us! From this death may the Lord deliver us, who prostrated death for us, and through death conquered him who had the empire of death: and may He make us stand before His throne in the new heavens and in the new earth, and to keep month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath as a festival, that with all the flesh of the elect we may come, and worship before His face for ever and ever, Amen. Blessing and brightness, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, honor and might and strength to our God for ever and ever, Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET EGREDIENTUR] Spatiatum per Ju- dæam.

ET VIDEBUNT CADAVERA VIRORUM QUI PRÆVARICATI SUNT IN ME] Id est, illorum qui in Antiochi fuerunt partibus.

VERMIS EORUM NON MORIETUR] Id est, diu vermis pascetur illorum cadaveribus, quia sepultura indigni judicabuntur.

ET IGNIS EORUM NON EXTINGVETUR.] μετωνυμία, id est, ignis signa in oppidis incensis. Vide quæ dicta supra 16. μυστικῶς tamen etiam Judæi hæc ad diem Ju- dicii trahunt. Etiam Chaldæus hoc loco.

ET ERUNT USQUE AD SATIETATEM VI- SIONIS OMNI CARNI] Ad nauseam; id est, fœtorem de se excitabunt odiosum.

Quot verba, tot perversiones, primum egres- sum per exspatiationem per Judæam explicat. Sic- cine ergo è cœlis novis & terra nova exspatiabun- tur electi? Et quomodo hoc cum perpetua com- moratione coram Domino & æterna festivitate consistit? Egredientur ergo non loco, ut Hierony- mus, sed intelligentia. Utitur Spiritus Sanctus ver- bis hujus seculi ad describendum res futuri. Simi- litudo desumpta est à corporali victoria, ubi cives egrediuntur, ut videant cum voluptate prostratos hostes. Porro non cadavera eorum, qui ab Antio- chi fuerunt partibus, sed in genere eorum, qui præ- varicati sunt in Christum, quod fit per incredulita- tem, quæ damnationis causa est, Joh. 3, 16. 17. Luc. 5, 14. videbuntur; quomodo nempe ipsi sicut oves in inferno positi jacebunt & mors depascet ipsos. Psal. 49, 15. Intuebuntur beati cum voluptate æterna imiporũ supplicia. Ut enim sibi gratulabuntur per- petuo de misericordia Dei, quam sunt consecuti, ita probabunt etiam Dei justitiam, qua severissime pu- niet impios. Tertio VERMIS NON MORIENS de naturali verme accipitur contra verbi δεινότη- τα, & explicationem Christi Marc. 9. Quarto, vermis eorum dicitur non mori, quod nunquam moriatur, ut particula absolute negans & ἔκθεσις ejus docet. Ex adverso Grotius de verme diu pa- scendo cadaveribus non sepultis intelligit. Vermem conscientiæ animas in æternum depascentem Chri- stus designari à Propheta innuit. Grotius de ver- me naturali, qui cadaveribus pascitur, interpreta- tur. QUINTO, ignem qui non extinguetur, Gro- tius de ignis signis in oppidis incensis intelligit, adeo- que Metonymiam hic ponit. At non intelligendum esse ignem metonymice, prædicatum docet, NON EXTINGUETUR. Signis enim nec incendium nec extinctio competit. SEXTO quæ de igne in- extinguibili Gehennæ agunt, atq; ita explicantur à Christo Marc. 9, 45. de igne in oppidis incensis ex- plicat Grotius. Agnoscit ea à Judæis de die judicii intelligi, etiam à Chaldæo hoc in loco, sed mystice so- lum eos hæc ita intelligere dicit; Mentem eorum ifidem pervertens. Quia sensum reddunt literalem, qui sic explicant è Judæis, neq; alium sensum verbo- rum Prophetæ vel Chaldæus, vel alii agnoscunt. Chaldæus ita vertit; Et erunt impii judicati in ge- henna, donec dicant super eos justi, vidimus satis. Hoc est, inquiunt Judæi, ut refertur in Pugione Fidei part. 2. c. 11. q. 20. quod quisq; justus cum semel vide- rit eos (damnatos) vermibus immortalibus plenos, dicturus est, sufficit mihi, nolo eos videre amplius in æternum, & hoc est quod scriptum est Es. ult. v. ult. Et exibunt & videbunt cadavera eorum, qui culpa- biles extiterunt in me: propterea vermis eorum non morietur & ignis eorum non extinguetur, & erunt usq; ad fatietatem omni carni. R. Joseph in Talmud in Pesach Schenu dixit: ignis, quem Deus sanctus & benedictus creavit in secunda Sabbahti, id est, feria secunda, non extinguetur in æternum. Sicut dictum est Es. 66. ult. Et egredientur &c. Traditio quoq; est: Dixit R. Benach, cur non fuit dictum in secunda Sabbathi, Gen. 1. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum! propterea quod creatus est in ea ignis gehen- næ. Adde quod Grotius ipse agnovit in annot. ad Marc. 9, 45. quod ipsa verborum proprietas mire in- serviat describendis perpetuis suppliciis. Unde etsi ea non quidem ad ea, quæ tempore Antiochi acci- derunt, sed ad Hierosolymitanum excidium (novis- simum) retulerit in istis Annotatis, ubi nondum quicquam somniavit de nova illa glossa, quasi ad tempora Antiochi ista pertineant, sed significare to- to hoc vaticinio Prophetam dixit, quod alibi sæpe. fore, ut gentes assumantur in populum Dei, qui non secun- dum ritus carnis, sed secundum legem Spiritus Deo serviant: eos autem qui salutares admonitiones con- tempserint (Judæos sc.) miserrime perituros: pro- fessus tamen est, magis proprie hæc convenire æternis suppliciis. Nam illud 8̀ τελευτᾷ, inquit, & σβέν- νυται in Hierosolymitano quidem excidio habet suum sensum, sed ratione materiæ restrictum ac limitatum, in pœnis tamen vitæ alterius alium κᾤ τὸ κυριολογέ- μενον. Addit, receptam fuisse inter Judæos eam sen- tentiam: quod è Scriptis Apocryphis confirmat. Syr. 7, 19. ἐκδίκησις ἀσεβῆς πῦρ ϰὴ σκώληξ. Et Judith. 16, 21. δῦναι πῦρ καὶ σκώληκας εἰς σάκρας ἀυτῶν. Hæc ibi Grotius, cur ergo jam à proprietate disce- dit? Cur sensum, quem verba Prophetæ inferuut κᾤ τὸ κυριολογόμενον, relinquit? cur tritam in Ecclesiâ Judæorum antiqua sententiam deserit, eamq; assu- mit, quæ nemini unquam in mentem venit, & quam ipse, cum locum Prophetæ cum verbis Christi con- ferret, sine dubio haud probasset, siquidem ea pror- sus à mente Christi, imo etiam à sensu Ecclesiæ Ju- daicæ aliena sit. Quod de gemino sensu ingeritur, altero minus proprio, altero proprio, qui in vatici- niis τύπος continentibus locum habere soleat, sæ- pius à nobis profligatum est, nec ullo exemplo Scri- pturæ comprobari hactenus potuit; Hic certe lo- cum non habet. Nam miserum illum interitum Judæorum in excidio novissimo ut typum æternæ condemnationis in verbis illis VERMIS NON MORETVR, IGNIS NON EXTINGUE- TUR propositum vel inter Judæos creditum fuis- se, vel à nobis credi debere, quomodo docebitur? Sanctus Augustinus l. 20. de Civ. Dei c. 22. refert quidē ab aliis aliter vermem vivacissimū & ignem inextinguibilem expositum esse. Alii, inquit, utrumq, ad corpus, alii utrumq, ad animam retule- runt. Alii proprie corpus ad ignem, vermem vero tropice ad animam, quod PROBABILIUS esse vi- detur. At de eo dubium non fuit hæc ad pœnas INFERNALES malorum pertinere. De diversis illis sententiis idem etiam conferatur l. 21. c. 9. in quo cuivis liberum judicium relinquit: Eligat quisq; quod placet, aut ignem tribuere corpori, animo vermem, hoc proprie, illud tropice. Jam enim satis su- perius disputavi, posse animalia etiam in ignibus vi- vere, in ustione sine consumptione, in dolore sine morte, per miraculum omnipotentissimi creatoris, cui hoc possibile esse, qui negat, à quo sit quicquid in naturis omnibus miratur, ignorat. Ipse enim est Deus, qui omnia in hoc mundo magna & parva miracula, quæ commemoravimus, etiam incomparabiliter plura, quæ non commemoravimus, fecit, eademq; ipso mundo uno atq; omnium maximo miraculo inclusit. Eligat unum de duobus, quisq; quod probet, utrum & ver- mem ad corpus proprie, an ad animum translatè à corporalibus ad incorporalia vocabulo existimet per- tinere. Id tamen extra dubitationem ponit, hæc agere non de excidio Hierosolymitano, aut alio aliquo supplicio temporali, sed de æterna & infer- nali damnatorum pœna unice. Hieronymus in h. l. vermis, inquit, qui non morietur, & ignis, qui non ex- tinguetur, à PLERISQUE conscientia accipitur peccatorum, quæ torqueat in supplicio constitutos &c. Isidor. lib. 1. de summo bono cap. 3. duplex damna- torum pœua est in gehenna, quorum & mentem urit tristitia & corpus flamma juxta vicissitudinem, ut qui mente tractaverunt, quod perfecerunt corpore, si- mul & anima puniantur & corpore. Ambros. l. 7. in Luc. cap. 14. ut multæ ex ruditate febres nascun- tur & vermes, quando quis cibum intemperanter su- mit. Ita si quis peccata peccatis accumulet, nec deco- quat ea pœnitentia, sed misceat peccata peccatis, cruditate contrahit veterum & recentiorum delicto- rum, indeq; igne quasi febre aduretur proprio, & ver- mibus consumetur, id est, torquebitur & cruciabitur usq; ad consumtionem & mortem, ita tamen ut nun- quam sit consumtus & mortuus. Innocent. 3. libr. de conf. mundi. Vermis, ait, tripliciter conscientiam lacerabit, affliget memoria, sera turbabit pœnitentia, torquebit angustia. Qui tamen in eo fallirur, quod vermem & ignetm duplicem intelligat; Vermis & ignis uterq; duplex, interior & exterior, interior, qui rodit & urit cor, exterior, qui rodit & urit corpus. Fallitur inquam, si id intelligatur, ut intelligunt Pa- pistæ; ac si non tantum vermis conscientiæ note- tur tropice, sed etiā proprie vermes corporales in inferno horribiles, fœdissimi, mordacissimi & æter- ni designentur, uti de iis philosophatur Cornel. à Lapide ad h. l. qui tales hic intelligi à Propheta, & in inferno locum habituros prolixe ostendere niti- tur. Non potest una eademque vox in eodem loco simul proprie & improprie accipi; neq; vermes corporales in altero seculo existent, aut immortales erunt; ideoque fabulas istas Papistis relinquimus. Cum vermem audieris, monuit jam Gregorius Nys- senus Catechumenos, Orat. Catech. c. 40. ne propterea, quod sit idem nomen, ad terrestre hoc ani- mal tua feratur cogitatio. Adjectio enim ejus, quod non moriatur, suggerit aliam intelligendam esse natu- ram, quam eam, quæ cognoscitur. SEPTIMO ver- ba ultima de fœtore cadaverum explicat Grotius. Quid vero fœtor talis, quid nausea inde oriunda, ad vermem NON MORIENTEM, ad IGNEM INEXTINGUIBILEM h. e. ad pœnam damnato- rum æternam! In Ebræo hæc ita habentur: ET ERUNT ABOMINATIONI OMNI CAR- NI, h. e. omnes beati detestabuntur perpetuo impios & damnatos, neq; ulla eorum tangentur commise- ratione, sed abominabuntur eorum impietatem & blasphemiam, unice celebrantes justitiam & verita- tem divinam. Dicuntur autem corpora damnato- rum, licet animata, cadavera, tum quia fœtida & olida sunt instar cadaverum, tum quia sunt in morte æterna, & simul in pœna æterna: Ut enim mor- tem significaret, cadavera dixit, ut vero vitam omni morte acerbiorem exprimeret, vermem dixit non morientem, & ignem inextinguibilem. Ideoq; recte S. Bernhardus l. 5. de consider. c. 12. Hoc est, ut vermis, qui non moritur, Memoria præteritorum, semel injectus vel potius innatus per peccatum, hæsit firmiter, nequaquam deinceps avellendus. Nec cessat rodere conscientiam, eaq; pastus esca utiq; inconsum- tibili perpetuat vitam. Addit vir sanctus: Horreo vermem mordacem & mortem vivacem. Horreo incidere in manus mortis viventis & vitæ morientis. Hæc est secunda mors, quæ nunquam peroccidit, sed semper occidit. Quis det illis semel mori, ut non mo- riantur in æternum; Qui dicunt montibus, cadite super nos, & collibus operite nos! Ab hac morte libe- ret nos Dominus, qui mortem pro nobis prostra- vit, & per mortem eum vicit, qui habebat mortis imperium: faciatq; nos stare coram suo throno in novis cœlis & in nova terra, & mensem ex mense & Sabbatum ex Sabbato festivum agere, ut cum omni carne electorum veniamus, & adoremus co- ram facie ipsius in secula seculorum, Amen. Bene- dictio & claritas, & sapientia, & gratiarum actio, honor & virtus & fortitudo Deo nostro in secula seculorum, Amen.

# Jeremiah

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
IN THE NAME OF JESUS ANNOTATIONS ON THE PROPHET JEREMIAH.

Latin:

I. N. J. ANNOTATA AD JEREMIAM PROPHETAM.

## 1:1 Introduction: Preface
PREFACE

JEREMIAS, ירמיהו, was named "the exalted of the Lord" from רום, high, whom the Lord exalted above Kings as an insurmountable pillar, ch. 1, 18; he was a native of Anathoth, the son of Hilkiah, sent by the mercy of God while captivity was imminent to the people, so that he might rouse them to repentance, and thus he himself might escape the Babylonian captivity now impending, as Jerome has it in ch. 1 of Jeremiah. In the 13th year of King Josiah, in the year of the world 3375, he began to preach while still quite young, being about 15 years of age, ch. 1, 7; ch. 25, 3; and he preached in Judea for 41 years: under Josiah for 19 years, under Jehoahaz for 3 months, under Jehoiakim for 11 years, under Jeconiah for three months, and under Zedekiah until Jerusalem was captured by the Chaldeans in the 5th month of that eleventh year; from which, when the Jews fled, he was taken away into Egypt, to Tahpanhes, a royal city, until the fourth year of the destruction of Jerusalem, 23. He likewise prophesied to the Hebrews and to all Egypt the destruction of Nebuchadnezzar, and to the King of Egypt, Vaphres, chains and slaughter by Nebuchadnezzar, which followed in the year immediately succeeding; he is believed to have been killed by his own fellow citizens and overwhelmed with stones, as Tertullian reports in Scorpiaco, and Jerome, Epiphanius, and Dorotheus. He was truly πολυπαθέστατος, as Isidore of Pelusium says, and in extreme and long-lasting calamity he showed an extraordinary loftiness of spirit. Besides this book of prophecies and the Lamentations, he is considered to have written the third and fourth books of Kings.

The present book is occupied primarily with the exhortation of the people to repentance, and when the Jews did not obey, with the foretelling of the captivity of the people and the destruction of the city by the Babylonians, with evangelical prophecies interspersed from time to time for the sake of the faithful concerning Christ and His Church, both after the liberation from captivity and in the time of the New Testament: yet he does not neglect the enemies of the Jews, the neighboring nations, but proclaims to them also the judgments of the Lord. Concerning his style, Jerome judges truly thus: Jeremiah, as much as he seems simple and easy in his words, is just as profound in the majesty of his meanings.

prophesying, that [fact] having been further confirmed by the death predicted for him by the Prophet, chap. 28. Finally, after the Epistle sent to the captives, chap. 29, had been presented, evangelical consolatory sermons follow, presenting consolation both common to the people, the first of which is about the return to the Fatherland, so that they may serve the Messiah there, chap. 30, and about the virgin birth and the New Covenant, chap. 31. The second, delivered in Jeremiah's prison about the return to the Fatherland, when the city was already being besieged, chap. 32. The third, likewise in prison, about the kingdom of Christ and the righteous branch of David, chap. 33; then presenting some special consolation, such as the fourth, when the city was being attacked, still leaving Zedekiah some consolation, namely that he would die in peace, chap. 34; and the fifth about the blessing promised to the family of the Rechabites for their obedience, when the punishment for the disobedience of the Jews was denounced, chap. 35. To these sermons there follow, furthermore, historical [accounts] concerning the events preceding the occupation of the city: such as 1. concerning the words of the Lord recorded in a book, chap. 36; 2. Concerning King Zedekiah, who asked that Jeremiah pray for him, and consulted Jeremiah, chap. 37, who persuaded the people to surrender, but was punished with a squalid prison, from which, however, he was rescued and kept in a narrower prison, and advised the King to surrender, chap. 38; then concerning the city captured and what happened then, chap. 39; then concerning the consequences, Jeremiah and the remnants of the people committing themselves to Gedaliah, chap. 40; and he being treacherously killed, the Jews contemplating [fleeing to] Egypt, chap. 41; and God prohibiting it in vain through Jeremiah, chap. 42; they betaking themselves there, and carrying off with them Jeremiah, who not only declares the slaughter of the Egyptians, chap. 43, but also the punishment of the Jews for their flight into Egypt, and disputes with the people speaking against it, chap. 44; and deals particularly with Baruch, chap. 45.

The economy of the book is this: first, the calling of Jeremiah and the summary of the prophecies is held, chap. 1; then his sermons and predictions, in the remaining chapters up to the last; finally, a description of the destruction of the city and the deportations into the Babylonian captivity with some consequences, chap. 52, at the end. But as for his sermons, we refer to them also the events and consequences, but especially their fulfillments: and some are domestic, others exotic. It will be permissible to distribute the domestic [ones] thus, that they partly present the Prophet's penitential sermons, in which Jeremiah excels, a preacher of repentance notable above the other prophets; partly historical relations. The penitential sermons are contained up to chapter 36 inclusive: and among them some are more legal and comminatory, others more evangelical and consolatory; and the legal [ones were] delivered partly by word of mouth up to chap. 28, and partly written out to the captives in Babylon, chap. 29. Some of the Prophet's sermons were made indefinitely concerning future calamity up to chap. 25; others define the Babylonian captivity by the space of LXX years expressed: There the following sermons are held. The first concerning spiritual fornication, chap. 2 and 3, with an exhortation to repentance, chap. 4, a rebuke of hardening, and a denunciation of punishment, chap. 5. The second, delivered at the gate of the house of the Lord, with a presentation of the arrival of the enemies premised, chap. 6, concerning vain confidence in the temple, chap. 7, and concerning impenitence and fatal punishment, chap. 8, with a lamentation of the people's calamity, chap. 9, and a dissuasion from the ways of the nations, lest they be seduced by them in Babylon, chap. 10. The third concerning the covenant with God violated, on account of which the Prophet fell into danger, chap. 11, expostulating with God, chap. 12, and by the command of the Lord, individually outlining the rejection of the people, chap. 13. The fourth predicts famine and drought, chap. 14. and that punishments are not to be forgiven, even if Moses and Samuel were standing before the Lord praying, chap. 15. The fifth is about the taking away of the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, chap. 16, and explains the causes of divine wrath and the captivity of the people, idolatry, confidence in men, and the profanation of the Sabbath, chap. 17. The sixth is about God having the people in His hand like a potter, chap. 18, and breaking an earthen vessel, chap. 19, with the outcome of this sermon, the imprisonment of Jeremiah, chap. 20. And these were delivered to the people. The seventh was delivered to the envoys of Zedekiah, that he should surrender to Babylon and administer justice, chap. 21, with a threat against the Royal House, chap. 22. The eighth is an invective against wicked shepherds, chap. 23. Finally, there follows the ninth, an explanation of the vision of the two baskets of figs, chap. 24.

Now follow the exotic prophecies, namely 1. against the Egyptians, chap. 46; 2. against the Philistines, chap. 47; 3. against the Moabites, chap. 48; 4. against the Ammonites, Syrians, Ishmaelites, and Persians, chap. 49; 5. against the Babylonians, chap. 50 and 51; subject, as we said, to chap. 52, at the end, the history of the Jerusalemite destruction and some consequences.

PART I. CONCERNING DOMESTIC SERMONS.

PRIOR SECTION PRESENTING THE PENITENTIAL SERMONS THEMSELVES CONCERNING THE DESTRUCTION OF JUDEA. AND THE FIRST SUBSECTION OF THE SAME CONTAINING THE MORE LEGAL AND COMMINATORY SERMONS

SECTIO PRIOR CONCIONES IPSAS POENITENTIALES DE EXITIO JUDÆÆ EXHIBENS. EIVSDEMQVE PRIMA SUBSECTIO CONCIONES MAGIS LEGALES ET COMMINATORIAS CON- TINENS.

## 1:1 Argument
CHAPTER I.

THE CALL of Jeremiah, with a summary of his penitential sermons, by a vision of a rod and a seething pot figuring the burning wrath of the Babylonians, kindled for the destruction of Judea, and a command to preach repentance, as well as a divine promise of assistance.

Ver. 1. THE WORDS OF JEREMIAH] A book. Moreover, this inscription of this book is at the end of chapter 39. Thence follows as it were another book, added to the former.

Furthermore, the Babylonian Captivity is defined from the fourth year of Jehoiakim as lasting LXX years, chapter 25, as is also the subsequent devastation of the temple, chapter 26, which the prediction concerning all peoples who would serve Nebuchadnezzar, and the exhortation concerning submitting the neck to his yoke, chapter 27, also confirms: to which sermon, when Hananiah contradicted it under Zedekiah, all other [false prophets]... Grotius explains the word דברי as 'book', without cause departing from the common sense and meaning of the word, and from the Vulgate interpretation. For it notes not the book, but the words, as the Vulgate rendered it, even if the words of Jeremiah are contained in the book. And therefore the words of the Prophecy, made from the more important denomination, as the Chaldean and Vatablus explain the word as Prophecies, or oracles, which Jeremiah heard from God, and reported to the people, are signified, or generally the words which Jeremiah, inspired by the divine Spirit, consigned to letters, both prophetic and historical. However, that two books of Jeremiah are presented here, the former up to the end of chapter 39, the latter in the remaining chapters, from which it might be taught, does not appear. The whole book of Jeremiah is more correctly divided by others into four parts. Because in the first part are held penitential sermons through 38 chapters threatening the destruction of Jerusalem: in the second, a historical description of the destruction is handed down with those things which were joined to it, up to chapter 43. The third, the Prophet prophesies against foreign peoples, up to to the last chapter. The fourth, the deportation of Zedekiah and the people, and the liberation and exaltation of King Jehoiachin is succinctly proposed. But we have already spoken about the fuller arrangement of the book.

For he is only said to be sanctified, because he was destined and consecrated to the office before he came out of the womb.

Vers. 1. VERBA JEREMIÆ] Liber. Est autem hæc inscriptio libri hujus ad finem capitis 39. Inde sequitur velut alter liber, additus priori.

Porro Captivitas Babylonica definitur à Jo- jakimi quarto LXX. annis cap. 25. ut & subse- quutura templi vastatio cap. 26. quam etiam præ- dictio de servituris Nebucadnezari omnibus po- pulis, & adhortatio de submittendo collo jugo ejus- dem cap. 27. confirmat: cui concioni cum con- tradiceret sub Zedekia Hanania, omnia alia va- VOcem דברי cum per Librum explicat Grotius, sine causa à communi sensu & significatione vocis, & interpretatione vulgata discedit. Notat enim non librum, sed verba, ut vulgatus reddidit, etsi verba Jeremiæ libro comprehensa sint.Ideoq; verba Prophetie, facta a potiori denominatione, uti Chaldæus & Vatablus per Prophetias vocem expo- nunt, vel oracula, quæ Jeremias audivit a Deo, & retulit ad populum, significantur, aut generatim verba, quæ Jeremias divino afflatus Spiritu literis consignavit, cum prophetica tum historica. Duos autem libros Jeremiæ hic exhiberi, priorem usq; ad finem cap. 39. posteriorem in reliquis capp. unde doceri possit, non apparet. Rectius in quatuor partes ab aliis dispescitur totus liber Jeremiæ. ## 1:1
Verse of the same. OF THE PRIESTS WHO WERE IN ANATHOTH] Who lived there, and served God in the Temple through their ἐφημερίας. Others, with the Hebrews, Clement of Alexandria l. 1 Strom., Jerome Questions on the 1st book of Chronicles, Paul of Burgos, and Maldonado, maintain that Hilkiah was not of the common order of priests, but of the high priests, who in the 18th year of Josiah, that is, the sixth of Jeremiah's prophetic office, is read to have found the book of the law, 2 Kings 22, 8. He was of the ancestors of Ezra, Ezra 7, 1. He could have had his field in Anathoth, even if he resided in Jerusalem because of the high priesthood, just as Abimelech resided in Nob, a bordering place, 1 Sam. 21, v. 1.

There is no need for us to say that this was done through an Angel. The case of Isaiah 6 is different. For there the text testifies that the ministry of an Angel was employed. Here there is no indication of this. The Lord himself is said to have put forth his hand to Jeremiah, and to have touched his mouth. He who speaks here αὐτοπροσώπως [in person]: Behold, I have put my words in your mouth. For no one else can use this speech, except the Lord. Therefore, it is credible that the Son of God, in the assumed form, κατ᾽ οἰκονομίαν [according to the dispensation] temporal, παρατατικῶς [in a continuous manner] in a certain human form, did this. He who, by the touch of his hand, also healed the infirmities of ears and tongue in the days of his flesh, Mark 7:23. Jerome observes this distinction in this place: It is to be noted that here the hand of God is sent, which touches the mouth of the Prophet and it is said to him: Behold, I have put my words in your mouth. But in Isaiah it is written: And one of the Seraphim was sent to me, and in his hand he had a coal, which he had taken with tongs from the altar; and he touched my mouth and said: Behold, this one has touched your lips, and will take away your iniquities and cleanse your sins. For there, because he was of solid and perfect age, and he himself simply confesses that he has unclean lips and dwells in the midst of a people having polluted lips, one of the Seraphim is sent, who touches his mouth not with a hand but with tongs and a coal, and takes away iniquities, and cleanses sins. But here the hand of God himself is sent, through which he has wrought all things, and which in another place is called the arm: not to take away sins, which he had not committed many of through childhood, but to bestow the grace of speaking.

Notandum quod hic ma- nus mittatur Dei, quæ tangat os Prophetæ & dicatur ei: Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo. In Esaia au- tem scriptum sit: Et missus est ad me unus de Sera- phim,& in manu habebat carbonem,quem forcipe tulerat de altari; & tetigit os meum & dixit: Ec- ce tetigit iste labia tua, & auferet iniquitates tuas & peccata tua mundabit. Ibi enim quia solida & per- fecta ætatis erat: & ipse simpliciter confitetur, quod immunda labia habeat, & habitet in medio populi polluta labia habentis, mittitur unus de Seraphim, qui non manu sed forcipe & carbone tangat os ejus, & iniquitates auferat, & mundet peccata. Hic autem ipsius Dei manus mittitur, per quam cun- cta operatus est: & quæ in alio loco brachium di- citur: non ut peccata auferat, quæ per pueri- tam multa non fecerat: Sed ut loquendi gratiam tribuat.

## 1:2
Verse 2. THE WORD OF THE LORD WHICH CAME TO HIM] This book was written for this reason, because God revealed to him many future things worthy to be committed to posterity as a sign of divine providence.

Verse same. IN THE DAYS OF JOSIAH) Three kings are named here, with two omitted, on account of their very brief reign. The order of the kings under whom Jeremiah lived is this: Josiah. Jehoahaz. Jehoiakim. Jehoiachin, who is also Jeconiah. Zedekiah.

The years during which Jeremiah acted as a Prophet in the land of Judah are gathered to be 41; after them, prophecies came to him in Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QVOD FACTVM EST VERVM DO- MINI AD EVM] Ideo hic liber scriptus est, quia Deus ei multa futura revelavit digna quæ posteris mandarentur in signum divinæ provide tiæ.

Vers Eod. IN DIEBVS JOSIÆ) Reges hic tres no- minantur, omissis duobus, ob breve admodum regnum. Ordo regum sub quibus vixit Jeremias hic est: Josias. Joachaz. Jojakim. Joachin qui & Jechonias. Sedecias.

Anni per quos in terra Judæa Prophetam egit Jeremias colliguntur 41, post eos in Ægypto Prophetiæ ei obvene- runt.

## 1:4
Verse 4.

AND THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME TO ME] Almost a boy still, as appears below in verse 7. See what we said regarding Isaiah 53:2.
