Verse same. BEHOLD I HAVE PUT MY WORDS IN YOUR MOUTH] I bestow upon you eloquence equal to the commands.

The phrase is not explained fully enough. For it is not only a gift of eloquence, but also a concession of θεοσδότων [God-given] words, by which divine matters are to be proposed, is proven; namely, that the very words would be placed by God in the mouth of the Prophet, as one who wishes not only to suggest the senses of those things which are to be proposed, but also to provide the words for promulgating them: just as he gave the Apostles to speak the great works of God, Acts 2. Which was rightly observed by our blessed father-in-law, Dn. D. Hülsemann, in this place. To put words into the mouth of someone signifies not only to bestow the faculty upon someone so that he can bring forth divine utterances, but also to prescribe the form and manner of the words, as in Isaiah 59:21, and therefore the Prophets were called the mouth of God, Jer. 15:19, and what they spoke was said to be the mouth of the Lord speaking, verse 10.

That he was almost a boy, the excuse of the Prophet in verse 6 says, and it is the common opinion that he was 13 years old then. However, the passage of Isaiah ch. 53 is clearly ἀκροσδιόνυσος [irrelevant]. For there the Prophet prophesies not about Jeremiah, but about the Messiah, as is evident from our vindications on that passage.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET FACTVM EST VERBVM DOMINI AD ME] Ferme puerum adhuc, ut apparet infra 7. Vide quæ diximus ad Esaiam 53, 2.

Vers. Eod. ECCE DEDI VERBA MEA IN ORE TUO] Eloquentiam tibi tribuo mandatis parem,

Non satis plene exponitur phrasis. Non enim tantum eloquentiæ donum, sed verborum etiam θεοσδότων, quibus res divinæ proponendæ concessio probatur, a Deo nempe verba ipsa po- situm iri in ore Prophetæ, utpote qui non tantum sensus eorum,quæ proponenda sunt,suggerere,sed verba quoq; iisdem promulgandis sufficere velit: quemadmodum Apostolis dedit eloqui magnalia Dei Act. 2. Quod recte observatum B. Socero no- stro Dn. D. Hülsemanno in h. l. Dare verba in os alicujus significat non solum facultatem alicui tri- buere, ut possit divina promere eloquia, sed etiam for- mam & modum verborum præscribere, ut Es. 59, 21. ideoque Prophetæ dicebantur os Dei Jer. 15, 19. & quod ipsi loquebantur, dicebatur os Domini lo- quutum esse v. 10.

Ferme puerum fuisse, excusatio Prophetæ v. 6. dicit & communis est sententia 13. annorum tum fuisse. Locus autem Esaiæ c. 53. plane est ἀκροσδιό- νυσος. Ibi enim non de Jeremia, sed Messia vaticina- tur Propheta, ut e vindiciis nostris ad istum locum constat.

## 1:5
Verse 5.

BEFORE I FORMED YOU IN THE WOMB I KNEW YOU, AND BEFORE YOU CAME FORTH FROM THE WOMB I SANCTIFIED YOU] You should rather translate it, 'had formed you'. See what was said regarding Isaiah 49:1.

This sanctification is to be understood as a destination to an office, not a donation of faith and holiness. Cf. Gal. 1:15. Whence the Papists rashly infer from this passage that Jeremiah was immune from original sin; although if it were even to be understood of the sanctification which brings about holiness, as in the case of John the Baptist sanctified in his mother's womb from Luke 1:44, Lombard, lib. 4 sentent. dist. 6, judges it better to say that they were prevented by grace in the womb after the common law and justified from sin, rather than immune. Tomus II. V. T.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PRIUSQVAM TE FORMAREM IN VTERO NOVI TE, ET ANTEQVAM EXIRES DE TERRA SANCTIFICAVI TE] Potius vertas, formassem. Vide quæ dicta ad Esaiam 49, 1.

Sanctificatio hæc de destinatione ad officium, non donatione fidei & sanctitatis accipienda. Conf. Gal. 1,15. unde Pontificii temere Jeremiam immu- nem fuisse a peccato originali ex h. l. colligunt; quanquam si etiam de sanctificatione, quæ sancti- moniam infert, accipiatur, uti de Johanne Baptista in utero matris sanctificato e Luc. 1, 44. Lombar- dus l. 4. sentent. dist. 6. censet, melius esse, ut dica- tur illos post communem legem in utero gratia præventos & a peccato justificatos, quam immunes Tomus II. V. T.

## 1:6
Verse 6.

I AM A BOY] Of weak age and not sufficiently suitable for speaking great things.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PVER EGO SVM] Ætatis infirmæ & ad res ma- gnas eloquendas non satis idoneæ.

## 1:7
Verse 7.

FOR TO ALL THINGS TO WHICH I SHALL SEND THEE THOU SHALT GO] You may translate not badly: Indeed, to all things (to be performed) to which I shall send you, go. Thus he speaks in those things which follow.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

QVONIAM AD OMNIA QVÆ MITTAM TE IBIS] Vertas non male: Imo ad omnia (pera- genda) ad quæ te mittam, ito. Sic in iis quæ sequuntur loquitur.

## 1:9
Verse 9.

AND HE TOUCHED MY MOUTH] Through an Angel. See Isaiah 6, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET TETIGIT OS MEVM] Per Angelum. Vide Esaiam 6, 7.

## 1:10
BEHOLD I HAVE SET THEE THIS DAY OVER THE NATIONS AND OVER THE KINGDOMS) To predict extraordinary things, which pertain not to individuals but to entire nations, such as the Jews, Tyrians, Idumeans, and great kingdoms, such as was that of Babylon, the Persians, and Egypt.

THAT YOU MAY ROOT OUT AND DESTROY AND DISPERSE AND BUILD AND PLANT] These are the works of God, to root out and restore kingdoms and peoples, see below 45, 4. But they are attributed to the Prophet, because what he had said (namely under their conditions) was to come to pass no less certainly than if He Himself were doing them. See Exod. 8, 5.

Latin:

ECCE CONSTITVI TE HODIE SVPER GEN- TES ET SVPER REGNA) Prophe am res eximias præ- dicturum, quæ non ad singulas sed ad integras gentes, ut Judæos, Tyrios, Idumæos, magnaq; regna, quale fuit Baby- lonis, Persarum Ægypti, pertineant.

VT EVELLAS ET DESTRUAS ET DISPER- DAS ET ÆDIFICES ET PLANTES] Dei hæc sunt opera, regna, populosq; evellere & restituere, infra 45, 4. Sed Prophetæ tribuuntur, quia non minus certo eventura erant, quæ dixerat (nempe sub suis conditionibus) quam si ipse ea faceret. Vide Exod. 8, 5.

## 1:11
Ver. 11. I SEE A WATCHFUL ROD) Theodotion translates it best as almond. See Eccles. 12, 5.

There is no reason why Theodotion's version should be preferred to the Vulgate, since Aquila and Symmachus agree. For the response and explanation of God confirm that the participle WATCHFUL rod is to be taken here as a noun, v. 12. Because I WILL WATCH, which Tremellius wrongly rendered, I am about to almond my word. See Ps. 102, 8. and 127, 1. Grotius himself rendered that word in v. 12 as to hasten, although he observes that the name for almonds was given from it. For I WILL WATCH, he says, you will more correctly put, I will hasten, for this שקד also signifies that.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VIRGAM VIGILANTEM EGO VIDEO) Theodotion optime vertit amygdalinam. Vide Eccles. 12, 5.

Non est causa, cur Theodotionis versio Vul- gatæ, cum Aquila & Symmachus consonent, præfera- tur. Participium enim virgam VIGILANTEM non nomen hic haberi, responsio & explicatio Dei confirmat, v. 12. Quia VIGILABO, quod per- peram Tremellius, ego amygdalaturus sum super verbum meum. Vid. Ps. 102, 8. & 127, 1. Grotius red- didit ipse verbum istud v. 12. per maturare, etsi in- de nomen amygdalis datum esse observat. Pro VIGILABO, inquit, rectius pones, maturabo, nam & hoc שקד significat.

## 1:12
Ver. 12. FOR I WILL WATCH OVER MY WORDS, TO PERFORM IT] For I will watch, you will more correctly put, I will hasten: for this שקד also signifies that: and from it the name שקד almond, because the almond tree blooms first of all in the month of January, but in March the fruits are ripe, says Pliny 16, 26. Just as in dreams according to Artemidorus and others, many things signify ἐξ ὁμωνυμίας (by homonymy), so from the sight of the almond rod, the hastening of those things which God had determined ought to have been understood.

The sense in our judgment comes to the same thing. For God is said to watch to execute matters, because He hastens them, and executes them maturely and watchfully: nor does a watchful rod denote anything other than the swift vengeance of God. The rod watches, says Jerome, considering all the sins of the people, so that it may strike and correct the delinquents. Whence also the Apostle writes to those who sin. What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness? Some render the Hebrew, the rod of a WATCHFUL God. The Chaldean expresses the sense in this way: I see the King of the Chaldeans hastening to strike the Jews and other nations,

Latin:

Vers. 12. QUIA VIGILABO EGO SUPER VER- BA MEA, UT FACIAM ILLUD] Pro vigilabo, rectius pones, maturabo: nam & hoc שקד significat: & inde no- men שקד amygdala, quia floret omnium prima amygdala mense Januario, Martio vero poma matura, ait Plinius 16, 26. Sicut in somniis apud Artemidorum & alios, multa si- gnificant ἐξ ὁμωνυμίας, ita ex conspectu amygdalinæ virgæ, intelligi debuit maturatio eorum quæ Deus constituerat.

Sensus eodem nostro judicio recedit. Vigila- re enim Deus dicitur ad res exequendas, quia ma- turat ea, & mature ac vigilanter exequitur: nec aliud virga vigilans, quam celerem Dei ultionem notat. Vigilat virga, inquit Hieronymus, cuncta populi peccata considerans, ut percutiat & corripiat delinquentes. Unde & Apostolus scribit peccantibus. Quid vultis? in virga veniam ad vos, an in charita- te & spiritu mansuetudinis? Nonnulli Ebræum reddunt, virgam VIGILANTIS Dei. Sensum exprimit Chaldæus, hoc modo: Ego video Regem Chaldæorum festinantem ad percutiendum Judæos & alias gentes,

## 1:13
Ver. 13. A SEETHING POT] In Hebrew: blown upon, that is, boiling. A representation of Judea about to feel the most grievous calamities as if from fire, so that even the citizens are cast out of it. See Ezech. 11, 7. and what is at Ps. 58, 10.

ITS FACE FROM THE FACE OF THE NORTH] That is, that fire, which kindles it, is placed from the North.

Latin:

Vers. 13. OLLAM SUCCENSAM] In Hebræo: suf- flatam, id est, bullientem. Speciem Judææ gravissimas cala- mitates sensuræ quasi ab igne, sic ut etiam cives extra eam projiciantur. Vide Ezech. 11, 7. & quæ ad Psal. 58. 10.

FACIEM EJUS A FACIE AQUILONIS] Id est, ignis ille, qui eam accendit, est positus ab Aquilone.

## 1:15
Ver. 15. ALL THE FAMILIES OF THE KINGDOMS OF THE NORTH] For the Babylonian Kingdom extended itself much into the north: and the Medes were allied to Nebuchadnezzar, who had taken the daughter of the King of Media as his wife. See what is at Book 3 of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

The Chaldean, Pagninus, and Vatablus take the word נפוח not as a participle but as a noun, and by a boiling pot they understand Nebuchadnezzar breathing out the fire of fury, to whom Cornel. à Lapide adds his support. But we acknowledge with Jerome, Theodoret, and others that it is more correctly rendered as blown upon and that Jerusalem is understood as being blown upon by the wrath of God, through Nebuchadnezzar from the north, like a pot, just as the symbol of a pot is used in Ez. 11, 7. c. 24, 3. For Babylon, even if it is eastern, with respect to Jerusalem is northern, and more equinoctial than Jerusalem. OUT OF THE NORTH EVIL SHALL BE OPENED. The Hebrew is ἐμφατικώ τερον (more emphatic), it shall be opened, as if hidden until now in the treasuries of God, so that there is an allusion to the word צפון North from צפן he hid. For northern things were hidden. See Solinus cap. 20.

THEY SHALL SET EVERY ONE HIS THRONE] That is, his military headquarters.

AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE GATES] In the way by which one goes to the Gates.

AND UPON ALL THE WALLS THEREOF] Around the walls.

Latin:

Vers. 15. OMNES COGNATIONES REGNO- RUM AQUILONIS] Nam Regnum Babylonicum mul- tum in septentrionem se porrigebat: & Medi erant fede- rati Nabuchodonosoro, qui Mediæ Regis filiam uxorem duxerat. Vide quæ ad Librum 3. de Veritate Religionis Christianæ.

Chaldæus, Pagninus & Vatablus vocem נפוח non pro participio sed nomine habent, & per ollam ferventem Nabuchodonosarem ignem furoris ef- flantem intelligunt, quibus accedit Cornel. à Lapi- de. Sed agnoscimus cum Hier. & Theodor. aliisq; re- ctius sufflatam reddi & Hierosolymam intelligi ab ira Dei, per Nabuchodonosarem ab aquilone in- star ollæ sufflatam, uti ollæ symbolum adhibetur Ez. 11, 7. c. 24, 3. Nam Babylon, etsi orientalis sit, respe- ctu Hierosolymæ septentrionalis est, & magis æqui- noctialis quam Hierosolyma. AB AQUILONE PANDETUR MALUM. Ebræum ἐμφατικώ τερον est, aperietur, quasi clausum hactenus in the- sauris Dei, ut alludatur ad vocem צפון Aquilo a צפן abscondidit. Aquilonares enim erant abscon- ditæ. Vid. Solinus cap. 20.

PONENT UNUSQUISQUE SOLIUM SUUM] Id est, prætorium suum castrense.

IN INTROITŲ PORTARUM] In via qua ad Portas itur.

ET SUPER OMNES MUROS EJUS] Circum muros.

## 1:16
Vers. 16. I WILL SPEAK JUDGMENTS WITH THEM] I will proclaim my decrees to them, through you, Jeremiah, through Huldah, Zephaniah, Ezekiel. Consider what follows.

Latin:

Vers. 16. LOQUAR JUDICIA CUM EIS] Prædi- cam illis mea decreta, per te, Jeremia, per Holdam, Sopho- niam, Ezechielem. Considera quæ sequuntur.

## 1:17
Vers. 17. GIRD UP YOUR LOINS] Prepare yourself for the work. See what is at Luke 12:35.

DO NOT BE AFRAID OF THEIR FACE] Do not fear them. NOR WILL I MAKE YOU FEAR THEIR COUNTENANCE] In the Hebrew: Lest I terrify you before them: that is, destroy you. Compare 1 Cor. 1:16. Vers. 18. OVER ALL THE LAND, THE KINGS OF JUDAH, ITS PRINCES, AND PRIESTS] Both the particle על and the particle ל here signify 'against': so that the sense may be: I will make you invincible against all the people of the land, and all the leading men. Vers. 19. THEY WILL FIGHT AGAINST YOU] They will do many evils to you. Thus πολεμεῖν is used in Rev. 17:14. AND THEY WILL NOT PREVAIL] They will not bring death upon you. I AM WITH YOU SAYS THE LORD, TO DELIVER YOU] By moving the hearts of kings and princes. These things are more correctly explained concerning punishments as decreed judgments of God to be executed by enemies from the North. B. Hülsemann is of this opinion in this place. Because God had said that He would place the thrones of the Kings at the entrance of the gates, where judgment was accustomed to be contended and defined, Ruth 4:1, Ps. 127:6. He continues in this allegory, and threatens that He will execute His judgment upon them from those thrones of the Kings and through those Kings, and will afflict them with just punishments. For to speak judgment here signifies to pronounce sentence upon the guilty and to impose punishment, as in ch. 4:12, 1 Kings 20:4, Ez. 16:38. Jerome renders this sense: and when (he says) the city has been captured, then I will speak to them that my judgments were righteous, and that each one received what they deserved: not for other vices, to which the human condition is subject, but especially for idolatry, through which, abandoning me, they worshipped the works of their own hands.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ACCINGE LUMBOS TUOS] Para te operi Vide quæ ad Lucam 12, 35.

NE FORMIDEs A FACIE ILLORUM] Ne eos extimescas. NEC ENIM TIMERE TE FACIAM VULTUM EORUM] In Hebræo: Ne ego te coram illis perterrefaciam: id est, perdam. Confer. 1. Cor. 1, 16. Vers. 18. SUPER OMNEM TERRAM, REGIBUS JUDÆ, PRINCIPIBUS EJUS, ET SACERDOTIBUS] Tam על quam particula ל hic valent contra: ut sit sen- sus: Faciam te invictum adversus omnem populum terræ, & omnes viros summates. Vers. 19. BELLABUNT ADVERSUM TE] Multa mala tibi facient. Sic πολεμεῖν sumitur Apoc. 17, 14. ET NON PRÆVALEBUNT] Mortem tibi non inferent. EGO TECUM SUM AIT DOMINUS, UT LIBEREM TE] Movendo corda regum ac principum. Rectius hæc de pœnis explicantur ceu decretis judiciis Dei exequendis per hostes ab Aquilone. B. Hülsemannus ita in h. l. Quia dixerat Deus se loca- turum solia Regum ad introitum portarum, ubi sole- bat contendi & definiri judicium Ruth. 4, 1. Ps. 127, 6. Pergit in hac allegoria, & minatur se de soliis illis Re- gum & per Reges illos exequuturum judicium suum super eos, eosœ, justis pœnis affecturum. Judicium enim loqui significat hic sententiam reo dicere & pœnam irrogare, ut c. 4, 12. 1. Reg. 20, 4. Ez. 16, 38. Hieronymus hunc reddit sensum: cumque, (ait) capta fuerit civitas, tunc loquar ad eos recta fuisse judicia mea, & recepisse singulos quæ merebantur: non pro cæteris vitiis, quibus subjacet humana conditio: sed maxime pro idolatria, per quam deserentes me, ado- raverunt opera manuum suarum.

## 2:1 Argument
SERMON I. A comminatory sermon concerning spiritual fornication. CHAPTER II.

Expostulation on account of ingratitude and idolatry under the image of fornication: and a threat of confusion and calamities on account of various sins, having sought in vain the help of the Egyptians and Assyrians.

Latin:

CONCIO I. Comminatoria de fornicatione spirituali. CAPUT II.

Expostulatio ob ingratitudinem, & idolola- triam sub fornicationis pictura: & com- minatio confusionis, & calamitatum ob varia peccata, conducto frustra Ægyptio- rum, & Assyriorum auxilio.

## 2:2
Vers. 2. I HAVE REMEMBERED YOU, PITYING YOUR YOUTH] That is, how I was merciful to your youth, how I protected you. Consider the following. For God wishes to show that after so many and such great benefits, He was undeservedly abandoned. AND THE CHARITY OF YOUR ESPOUSALS] How I loved you when you were first betrothed to me. WHEN YOU FOLLOWED ME IN THE DESERT, IN A LAND WHICH IS NOT SOWN] Where, namely, I provided food for you. Vers. 3. ISRAEL IS HOLY TO THE LORD] Namely, he was then. He was my peculiar possession. THE FIRST FRUITS OF HIS INCREASE] Just as the first fruits of the harvest are God's, and by the law of God fall to the priests, so that people, the first chosen from all peoples for God, belonged to God. ALL WHO DEVOUR HIM OFFEND] Read: were devouring and were offending. Those who eat from the harvest or other produce before they have given the first fruits to the priests are condemned by the law. Exod. 22:19, 34:26, Num. 15:19, Deut. 26:2 and following. Thus they were condemned then, not only those seven nations, not the parents of the Israelites by denunciations, but also others who harmed the Israelites in any part, such as the Amalekites, Midianites, and others. EVILS WILL COME UPON THEM] Translate: were coming. Vers. 5. WHAT INIQUITY DID YOUR FATHERS FIND IN ME?] When did I first abandon them? To which part of the covenant did I not stand? Compare Micah 6:3. AND THEY WALKED AFTER VANITY] That is, idols. For that is what הבל is to the Hebrews, which is translated as εἴδωλον in Deut. 32:21, below 14:21, 16:18. AND THEY BECAME VAIN] Brutish and senseless. See Psalm 115:8. Vers. 6. AND THE SHADOW OF DEATH] צלמות, which the LXX mostly translate as σκιὰν θανάτου, are properly those shadows which arise for those about to die: improperly, all places full of dangers, such as those were through which the Israelites once walked, full of serpents and scorpions and wild beasts. See Deut. 8:15.

Latin:

Vers. 2. RECORDATUS SUM TUI MISERANS ADOLESCENTIAM TUAM] Id est, quomodo mise- rus fuerim adolescentiæ tuæ, quomodo te protexerim. Con- sidera sequentia. Vult enim ostendere Deus post tot ac tan- ta beneficia immerito se derelictum. ET CARITATEM DESPONSATIONIS TUÆ] Quomodo te primum mihi desponsatam amaverim. QUANDO SECUTA ES ME IN DESERTO, IN TERRA QUÆ NON SEMINATUR] Ubi scilicet cibum tibi præbui. Vers. 3. SANCTUS ISRAEL DOMINO] Nempe tunc erat. Erat peculium meum. PRIMITIÆ FRUGUM EJUS] Sicut frugum pri- mitiæ Dei sunt, & jure Dei sacerdotibus cedunt, ita populus ille primus ex omnibus populis Deo selectus ad Deum per- tinebat. OMNES QUI DEVORANT EUM DELIN- QUUNT] Pone devorabant & delinquebant. Qui de mes- se aut fruge alia comedunt, antequam primitias dederint sa- cerdotibus, ex lege damnantur. Exod. 22, 19. 34, 26. Num. 15, 19. Deut. 26, 2. & sequentibus. Sic tunc damnati fuere, non tantum septem illi populi, non parentes Israelita- rum denunciationibus, verum etiam alii, qui Israëlitis ulla ex parte nocuerunt, ut Amalecitæ, Madianitæ, & alii. MALA VENIENT SUPER EOS] Verte venie- bant. Vers. 5. QUID INVENERUNT IN ME PATRES VESTRI INIQUITATIS?] Quando ego prior eos defe- rui? cui parti fœderis non steti? Confer. Mich. 6, 3. ET AMBULAVERUNT POST VANITATEM] Id est idola. Id enim הבל Hebræis, quod εἴδωλον verti- tur Deuter. 32, 21. infra 14, 21. 16, 18. ET VANI FACTI SUNT] Bruti & amentes Vi- de Psal. 115, 8. Vers. 6. ET IMAGINEM MORTIS] צלמות, quod plerumque σκιὰν θανάτου vertunt LXX. proprie sunt tenebræ illæ, quæ morituris oboriuntur: improprie omnia loca plena. periculis, qualia illa erant, per quæ incessere olim Israëlitæ, plena serpentum & scorpionum ferarumque. Vide Deut. 8, 15.

## 2:7
INTO THE LAND OF CARMEL) כרמל is not a proper noun here, but a common one, signifying a fertile field. Among the Talmudists, an ear of corn is called by that name.

YOU HAVE DEFILED MY LAND) Already from the times of the Judges, and thereafter. Compare Nehemiah 9. The land is said to be defiled most of all by the most eminent crime, that is, idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 7. IN TERRAM CARMELI) כרמל non est hic proprium, sed commune, agrum feracem significans. Apud Thalmudicos spica eo nomine vocatur.

CONTAMINASTIS TERRAM MEAM) Jam a Judicum temporibus, ac deinceps. Confer Nehem. 9. Maxime contaminari terra dicitur per eminentissimum cri- men, id est, idololatriam.

## 2:8
THEY THAT HOLD THE LAW) Those who professed themselves to be masters of the law, סופרים.

AND THE PASTORS TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME) Kings, as the Chaldean here: add also princes. See I Kings 22:17, Ecclesiastes 12:11, Isaiah 63:11.

THE PROPHETS PROPHESIED IN BAAL) In the name of Baal.

Latin:

Vers. 8. TENENTES LEGEM) Qui profitebantur se legis magistros, סופרים.

ET PASTORES PRÆVARICATI SVNT IN ME) Reges, ut hic Chaldæus : adde & principes. Vide I. Reg. 22, 17. Eccl. 12, 11. Es. 63, 11.

PROPHETÆ PROPHETAVERUNT IN BAAL) In nomine Baalis.

## 2:10
THE ISLES OF CHITTIM) Cyprus, where Κίττιον is, and the neighboring islands and coasts.

SEND UNTO KEDAR) To the Kedarite Arabs.

Latin:

Vers. 10. INSVLAS CETHIM) Cyprum ubi Κίττιον, & insulas orasque vicinas.

IN CEDAR MITTITE) Ad Arabas Cedarenos.

## 2:11
HATH A NATION CHANGED THEIR GODS) See whether any of them have renounced their gods, such as Adonis, Venus, or Dushara.

AND CERTAINLY THEY ARE NOT GODS) But in truth those are not gods.

HATH CHANGED HIS GLORY INTO AN IDOL) כבודו. But formerly it was כבודי, my majesty: but because that word in later times had begun to signify a certain wonderful presence of God, therefore the scribes changed this, as also in Psalm 106:20.

Even if it were granted that it was written otherwise in former times, this modern reading is not to be held as less genuine and authentic. For if the scribes, who corrected the copies at that time, are said to have restored the true reading by that correction of theirs, by what right will that be denied? This is the opinion of Buxtorf concerning the Tikkun Sopherim, written to the blessed Mr. Glassius, and presented in book 2 of Philologia Sacra, p. 494. That these Sopherim were the sacred authors themselves, Moses and the Prophets, who never wrote otherwise than as it is read written today. But the wiser Hebrews, he says, being more perceptive, noticing a certain inconvenience in those passages, wrote that those authors ought to have spoken otherwise, and according to the coherence of the proposed text to have written thus or so, but that they preferred to write thus instead of that, and to express it in such a way as it is in the text today.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SI MVTAVIT GENS DEOS SVOS) Vi- dete an ulli eorum abdicaverint deos suos, ut Adonin, Ve- nerem, Dusarem.

ET CERTE IPSI NON SVNT DII) At vero illi dii non sunt.

Vers. eod. MVTAVIT GLORIAM SVAM IN IDOLVM) כבודו. Sed olim fuit כבודי meam majesta- tem: sed quia illa vox posterioribus temporibus mirabilem quandam Dei præsentiam significare cœperat, ideo muta- runt hoc scribæ, ut & in Psal. 106, 20.

OLim secus scriptum fuisse etiamsi concedere- tur, non tamen hæc moderna lectio pro mi- nus genuina & authentica habenda. Nam si scri- bæ, qui correxerunt tum temporis exemplaria, illa sua correctione veram lectionem restituisse dicantur, quo jure id negabitur? Buxtorfii de Tik- kum Sopherim hæc est sententia ad B. Dn. Glas- sium perscripta, & ad libr. 2. Phil. Sacr. p. m. 494. exhibita. Sopherim hosce fuisse ipsos autores sacros, Mosen & Prophetas, qui nunquam aliter scripserunt, quam hodie scriptum legitur. At sapientes, inquit, Hæbræorum nasutiores, animadvertentes inconve- nientiam quandam in istis locis, scripserunt, aliter istos autores loqui debuisse, & secundum cohærentiam propositi textus sic vel sic scribere, sed pro eo maluis- se sic scribere, & id sic efferre, ut illud hodie in tex- tu est.

## 2:12
BE ASTONISHED, O YE HEAVENS, AT THIS) That is, the Angels, synecdochically.

AND BE YE ASTONISHED, O YE GATES) Mourn, ye porters. There is a double figure here: for both gates are spoken of for porters, and to be astonished for to mourn, κατὰ μετωνυμίαν (by metonymy).

Grotius adhered here to the Vulgate, but a πα- ρόραμα (oversight) of the interpreter occurs in it. Because in the Hebrew it is שַׁעֲרוּ which is 'be ye horrified,' not שַׁעֲרֵי 'its gates.' The LXX agree with the Hebrew text. Nor is there any place for suspicion of a corruption having been made. Therefore, one must not think here of the gates, or of the porters of heaven, nor even of the angels, for they are not commanded to be stunned or to be horrified, but the heavens are. Nor is there any reason why we should understand angels by the heavens synecdochically or metonymically. Since it is known that Scripture introduces inanimate things through personification, even heaven and earth, as for example Deut. 4, 26; c. 32, 1; Is. 1, 2. Which figure contributes not a little to moving the spirits, namely that sins are so foul and shameful that even the heavens themselves are stunned, horrified, and astonished. Just as the Apostle says that the creation συσενάζειν καὶ συνωδίνειν (groans and travails in pain together) with the children of God because of the vanity to which it is subjected. Rom. 8, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 12. OBSTVPESCITE COELI SVPER HOC) Id est, Angeli, συνεκδοχικῶς.

ET PORTÆ EJVS DESOLAMINI) Janitores ejus lugete. Duplex hic est figura : nam & portæ dicuntur pro janitoribus & desolari pro lugere, κατὰ μετωνυμίαν.

Adhæsit hic Vulgatæ Grotius, sed in eo πα- ρόραμα Interpretis occurrit. Quia in Ebræo est שַׁעֲרוּ quod est inhorrescite, non שַׁעֲרֵי portæ ejus. Ebræo textui consonant LXX. Neque ullus est locus suspicioni factæ corruptionis. Non ergo vel de portis, vel de janitoribus cœli hic cogitandum, sed nec de angelis, illi enim non jubentur obstupe- scere aut inhorrescere, sed cœli. Neque est, quod per cœlos synecdochice vel metonymice angelos in- telligamus. Cum notum sit Scripturam per Proso- popœiam introducere res inanimatas, cœlum e- tiam & terram, uti sit e. g. Deut. 4, 26. c. 32, 1. Es. 1, 2. Quæ figura ad movendum animos non parum fa cit, peccata nempe tam fœda esse, atque turpia, ut ipsi etiam cœli obstupescant, inhorrescant & desolentur. Quemadmodum Apostolus creatu- ram dicit συσενάζειν καὶ συνωδίνειν filiis Dei ob vanitatem, cui subjecta est. Rom. 8, 22.

## 2:13
Verse same. THEY HAVE FORSAKEN ME THE FOUNTAIN OF LIVING WATER) That is, perennial, who can perpetually make them abound in all good things.

Verse 13. BROKEN CISTERNS) Leaking.

Latin:

Vers. eod. ME DERELIQVERVNT FONTEM AQVÆ VIVÆ) Id est, perennis, qui perpetuo eos omnibus bonis abundantes facere possum.

Vers. 13. CISTERNAS DISSIPATAS) Perfluentes.

## 2:14
V. 14. IS ISRAEL A SERVANT?) Did he sell himself because of poverty? See Deut. 15, 12. No poverty had pressed the people.

OR A HOMEBORN SLAVE?) A verna, that is, born from a handmaid, who was in the dominion of him whose mother she herself was. He removes false causes, so that he may more vehemently establish the true one. The Israelites had come from Sarah, a mistress of the house lawfully wed.

WHY THEN IS HE BECOME A PREY?) That is, he has become a prey to outsiders.

Latin:

V. 14. NVMQVID SERVVS EST ISRAEL?) An pau- pertatis causa se vendidit ? Vide Deut. 15, 12. Nulla po- pulum presserat paupertas.

AVT VERNACVLVS) Verna, id est, natus ex ancilla, qui in dominio erat ejus, cujus ipsa mater. Cau- sas falsas removet, ut veram vehementius adstruat. Israëli- tæ ex Sara venerant matrefamilias legitime ducta.

QUARE ERGO FACTUS EST IN PRÆDAM) Id est, præda factus est externis.

## 2:15
Verse 15. THE LIONS ROARED UPON HIM) Kings, as the Chaldean explains here: But properly understand here the Assyrians, Tiglath-Pileser, Shalmaneser, Sennacherib.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SUPER EUM RUGIERUNT LEONES) Reges, ut hic explicat Chaldæus: Sed proprie hic Assyrios intellige, Teglathphalasarem, Salmanasarem, Sennache- ribum.

## 2:16
Verse 16. ALSO THE CHILDREN OF MEMPHIS AND TAPHNES HAVE DEFILED THEE EVEN TO THE CROWN OF THE HEAD) Taphnes is Daphne at Pelusium, as we have said elsewhere. רעע is to corrupt: wherefore the interpreter here does not badly translate 'defiled' with a general word adapted to a special place. Nor did the LXX mean anything else when they say ἔγνωσάν σε (they have known thee). But 'they have defiled even to the crown of the head,' this is what the Greeks would say ἐφοινίκιζον, the Latins irrumarunt: which itself signifies the greatest contempt and mockery both in Latin and here in the Hebrew. And it agrees well with history. For the Egyptians had taken much money from the Jews, and when they were in the greatest dangers, they helped them in no way against the Assyrians. 2 Kings 23, 35; 24, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 16. FILII QUOQUE MEMPHEOS ET TAPHNES CONSTUPRAVERUNT TE USQUE AD VERTICEM) Taphnes est Daphne ad Pelusium, ut alibi diximus. רעע est corrumpere: quare non male gene- rali voce aptata ad locum specialem vertit constuprare hic Interpres. Nec aliud voluere LXX. cum dicunt ἔγνωσάν σε. At constuprarunt usque ad verticem, hoc est quod dicerent Græci ἐφοινίκιζον, Latini irrumarunt: quod ipsum tum in Latino, tum hic in Hebræo maximum contemtum & illu- sionem significat. Et bene convenit cum historia. Nam Ægyptii multas ab Judæis pecunias abstulerant, & cum in summis essent periculis, nihil eis adversus Assyrios opitula- bantur. 2. Reg. 23, 35. 24, 7.

## 2:17
WHO LED THEE THROUGH THE WAY) Straight and easy.

Verse 17. AND NOW WHAT HAST THOU TO DO IN THE WAY OF EGYPT, TO DRINK THE WATER OF THE TROUBLED RIVER?) In the Hebrew מי שיחור, that is, the waters of the Nile, which is called Σῆρις (Siris) by the inhabitants, as we have said.

Latin:

QUO DUCEBAT TE PER VIAM) Rectam ac facilem.

Vers. 17. ET NUNC QUID TIBI VIS IN VIA Æ- GYPTI, UT BIBAS AQUAM TURBIDAM) In He- bræo מי שיחור, id est, aquas Nili, qui Σῆρις dictus acco- lis, ut diximus.

## 2:18
Verse 18. AND WHAT HAST THOU TO DO WITH THE WAY OF ASSYRIA, TO DRINK THE WATER OF THE RIVER?) Namely of the Euphrates: which is everywhere the river κατ' ἐξοχήν (by way of eminence). To drink the water is not here simply to seek their help, but also to adopt their gods, so that they might be more acceptable to them: which we have already learned was often done from Isaiah.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET QUID TIBI CUM VIA ASSYRIO- RUM VT BIBAS AQUAM FLUMINIS?) Nempe Euphratis: quod ubique κατ' ἐξοχήν flumen. Aquam bibe- re non est hic simpliciter eorum auxilia quærere, sed etiam Deos illorum afciscere, ut eo apud illos essent commen- dabiliores: quod sæpe factum didicimus jam ex Esaia.

## 2:19
Vers. 19. YOUR WICKEDNESS WILL REPROVE YOU] It will be an argument that you are justly punished.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ARGUET TE MALITIA TUA] Argu- mento erit juste te puniri.

## 2:20
Vers. 20. OF OLD YOU HAVE BROKEN MY YOKE, YOU HAVE BURST MY BONDS] Thus also the Greeks translate συνέτριψας καὶ διέρρηξας. They therefore read שברת and נתקת in the second person, and עלי: whereas the current Hebrew reading and the Chaldean have the first person, and עלי. Jerome also in his commentary follows the Greek reading. Neither sense is inconvenient. For he either says that for their liberation from the Egyptians and other enemies, an evil return of thanks was made to him: or that the Israelites had long since been law-breakers, and had often relapsed into the same disease.

AND YOU SAID: I WILL NOT SERVE (לא־אעבוד. And the Chaldean reads לא תעבור, as it is also written in the Hebrew margin in this sense: you promised that you would no longer do such things against the law and the covenant. Although both senses may be convenient, one should not depart from the reading of the authentic text, with which the Chaldean primarily agrees, nor should one, for the sake of the LXX Interpreters, whose codex is by no means uncorrupted, and whose παροράματα have been observed in countless places by sacred critics, call the source into suspicion of corruption. But this has often been warned about. Certainly no pregnant cause for such suspicion is detected here.

Vers. eod. YOU PROSTRATED YOURSELF AS A HARLOT] As a harlot. Prostrating oneself is appropriate for both, both the idolater and the harlot.

Latin:

Vers. 20. A SECULO CONFREGISTI JUGUM MEUM, RVPISTI VINCULA MEA) Sic & Græci ver- tunt συνέτριψας καὶ διέρρηξας. Legerunt ergo שברת & נתקת in secunda Persona, & עלי : ubi Hebræa nunc le- ctio & Chaldæus habent primam, & עלי. Hieronymus etiam in commentario Græcam lectionem sequitur. Neu- ter sensus est incommodus. Nam aut dicit pro liberatione ab Ægyptiis & hostibus aliis malam sibi relatam gratiam: aut jampridem Israelitas fuisse legirupas, & sæpe in eundem morbum eos recidisse.

ET DIXISTI: NON SERVIAM( לא־אעבוד. Ac Chaldæus legit לא תעבור, ut & in Hebræo margine scri- bitur hoc sensu: promisisti te non ultra facturum talia con- tra legem & fœdus. Etsi sensus uterque commodus sit, non tamen à lectione textus authentici, cui Chaldæus imprimis consonat, discedendum, nec in gratiam LXX. In- terpp. quorum Codex minime incorruptus est, & παροράματα in locis innumeris observata sunt à Criticis sacris, in suspicionem corruptelæ fontis vocandi sunt. Sed de his monitum sæpe est. Nulla certe hic causa prægnans ejusmodi suspicionis de- prehenditur.

Vers. eod. TV PROSTERNEBARIS MERETRIX) Ut meretrix. Sternere se utrique convenit, & idololatræ, & meretrici.

## 2:21
Vers. 21. YET I PLANTED YOU A CHOICE VINE] I planted, that is, I established you in the best places. Ex. 15, 17. Ps. 44, 3. A choice vine, that is, so that you might be a most noble vine, which is sorec to the Hebrews.

EVERY TRUE SEED) That is, a plant in no part adulterated or grafted, but from Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Sarah, Rebecca, Leah, Rachel, the best men and women.

A STRANGE VINE) You have degenerated, you have become useless, as the Chaldean here: you produce grapes, neither fit for making wine, nor edible.

Latin:

Vers. 21. EGO AVTEM PLANTAVI TE VINEAM ELECTAM) Plantavi, id est, in locis optimis constitui. Ex. 15, 17. Ps. 44, 3. Vineam electam, id est, ut esses vitis nobilissima, quæ sorec Hebræis.

OMNE SEMEN VERVM) Id est, plantam nulla ex parte adulterinam, aut insititiam, sed ex Abrahamo, Isaaco, Jacobo, Sara, Rebecca, Lea, Rachele, viris & fe- minis optimis.

VINEA ALIENA) Degenerasti, facta es inutilis, ut hic Chaldæus: producis uvas, neque aptas unde vinum fiat, neque τρωξίμους.

## 2:22
Vers. 22. IF YOU WASH YOURSELF WITH NITRE] Nitre eats away filth. Pliny 31, 10.

AND MULTIPLY FOR YOURSELF THE HERB BORITH) בורית is explained as soap. But Jerome, who lived in those places, says it is the herb of fullers, which grows in the green and moist places of Palestine. See Malachi 3, 2. and the Chaldean in this place. The sense is: the guilt is too heavy to be expiated by victims.

That sense is contrary to Scripture. For no guilt, as Scripture testifies, is too heavy to be able to be expiated by victims. Because by victims even the heaviest sins, and all impieties, transgressions, and prevarications were expiated on the solemn feast of expiations, and through the propitiatory victim of our only high priest Christ JESUS, the sins of all (because all were cast upon him) have been expiated, is the explored truth of the Scriptures. Nothing else is therefore indicated, than that hypocrisy and impurity shine through, however much they may cleanse themselves, and that they strive in vain to purify themselves with external purifications This sense Maldonatus, along with Theodoret, Hugo, and Lyranus, acknowledges, so that it is in vain that Cornel. a Lapide wishes to carve out from this that the act of sin, passing away, leaves behind it a habitual stain in the soul.

Verse of the same.

THOU ART STAINED IN THINE INIQUITY BEFORE ME) In the Hebrew: Thy iniquity is marked before me. That is, the stain is too deeply impressed to be washed away so easily.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SI LAVERIS TE NITRO) Nitrum sordes erodit. Plinius 31, 10.

ET MVLTIPLICAVERIS TIBI HERBAM BO- RITH) בורית explicatur sapo. At Hieronymus qui in istis locis vixit, herbam esse fullonum ait, quæ in virenti- bus & humectis Palestinæ nascitur locis. Vide Malachiam 3, 2. & Chaldæum hoc loco. Sensus est: gravior est culpa, quam ut victimis expietur.

Sensus ille Scripturæ contrarius est. Nulla e- nim culpa, Scriptura teste, gravior est, quam ut victimis expiari potuerit. Quia victimis pec- cata etiam gravissima, omnesque impietates, trans- gressiones & prævaricationes in festo expiationum solenni sunt expiatæ, & per victimam ἱλαστικὴν unici nostri pontificis Christi JESU peccata o- mnia (quia omnia in ipsum conjecta sunt) expia- ta esse, Scripturae explorata veritas est. Nihil ergo aliud indicatur, quam quod transpareat hy- pocrisis & impuritas, quomodocunque se pur- gent, quod frustra externis purificationibus se mundare nitantur, cum corda purificata non sint fide. Quem sensum Maldonatus cum Theodore- to, Hugone, & Lyrano, agnoscit, ut frustra Cor- nel. a Lapide hinc exsculpere velit, actum pec- cati transientem post se maculam in anima habi- tualem relinquere.

Vers. eod.

MACVLATA ES IN INIQVITATE TUA CORAM ME) In Hebraeo: Signata est iniquitas tua coram me. id est, altius impressa est macula, quam ut tam facile e- luatur.

## 2:23
Verse 23. HOW SAYEST THOU, I AM NOT POLLUTED, I HAVE NOT GONE AFTER BAALIM) Just as among Christians some eating ειδωλοθυτα denied that they were ειδωλολατρας, so also among the Jews, those who had partaken of the table of demons wished to be believed to have done nothing wrong. See canon 4 of the Synod of Ancyra.

SEE THY WAYS IN THE VALLEY) Of Hinnom. LXX: εν τω πολυανδριω. For there were many bones of those burned in that valley.

A SWIFT DROMEDARY TRAVERSING HER WAYS) From Symmachus and Theodotion, who had translated δρομας κυφη, for which the scribes erroneously wrote δρομευς: for בכרה is a dromas, a kind of camel. It is translated καμηλος in Isaiah 60:6. Camels mate all day long: Aristotle, third book of the History of Animals, chapter 2. To the harlot, to whom he had compared the Jewish nation, he further compares the most lustful animals, so that the foulness of the matter may appear the more.

TRAVERSING HER WAYS) The Chaldean here has 'depraving her ways'; that is, running about from male to another male.

Latin:

Vers. 23. QVOMODO DICIS, NON SVM POL- LVTA, POST BAHALIM NON AMBULAVI) Si- cut inter Christianos quidam ειδωλοθυτα manducantes ne- gabant se esse ειδωλολατρας, sic & inter Judaeos, qui de mensa daemoniorum participaverant, credi volebant ni- hil mali fecisse. Vide Ancyranae Synodi canonem 4.

VIDE VIAS TVAS IN CONVALLE) Hinno- mi. LXX. εν τω πολυανδριω. nam multa erant ossa combu- storum in ea valle.

CVRSOR LEVIS EXPLICANS VIAS SUAS) Ex Symmacho & Theodotione, qui verterant δρομας κυφη, pra quo librarii fecere δρομευς, mendose: nam בכרה est dromas cameli genus. Vertitur καμηλος Esaiae 60, 6. Ca- meli toto die coeunt: Aristoteles tertio de Historia Ani- mantium libro 5. cap. 2. Meretrici, cui Judaicam gentem comparaverat, ulterius comparat animantes maxime libi- dinosas, quo magis foeditas rei appareat.

EXPLICANS VIAS SVAS) Depravans vias suas habet hic Chaldaeus; id est, a mare ad marem alium discur- sitans.

## 2:24
Verse 24.

A WILD ASS ACCUSTOMED IN THE WILDERNESS) Understand a female wild ass: for this word, like many others in this and other languages, is επικoινος (common).

SHE HATH DRAWN IN THE WIND OF HER DESIRE) She smelled the male from afar. This interpreter and others read תאבתה, where we have תאותה, that is, of her meeting, namely, the breeze coming to meet her.

NONE SHALL TURN HER AWAY) There is no one who can restrain her, so that she does not run to the male.

ALL THEY THAT SEEK HER WILL NOT WEARY THEMSELVES) He returns to the first comparison. Thus he also says, whoever wished to use this harlot, no one was refused.

IN HER MENSTRUAL PERIODS THEY SHALL FIND HER) That is, even in her menstrual periods those who wish will find her ready. He could not have described a most shameless harlot better.

The translation of de Dieu seems more suitable, whose passage I shall transcribe: As a wild ass accustomed to the desert, in the desire of her soul she pants for the wind. Who shall turn away her occasion? None who seek her were wearied, in her new moon they shall find her. He expresses the most shameless lust of spiritual whoredom. First, that like a wild ass panting for the wind, she desires nothing else in her mind than to be breathed upon by the spirit of idols. Second, that she burns with this desire in such a way that no one can turn her away from an occasion of whoring once found. Third, that there is by no means any need for lovers to be much wearied in pursuing her, since she is most easy to find. And because they were accustomed to meet at every new moon, and on account of the solemnity of the feast, and the new Φασιν of the moon, which is even now received with great honor by all Orientals, they burned with a certain peculiar fervor and idolatrous worship, he adds that in her new moon she can be found. That some, following the Vulgate, translate בחדשה as in her menstrual periods, does not seem to be approved. A menstrual period is called נדה, not חדש, and it is strange that Junius wishes the same meaning to be attributed to it, Hos. 5, 7. Furthermore, למוד מדבר, taught of the desert, is rightly translated as accustomed to the desert. The word למד has this meaning, especially in the Ethiopic language, where it is most commonly used for to be accustomed and to be used to. As in Matt. 27, 15. Luke 2, 42. and John 18, 15. That disciple, who is said to have been γνωστὸς, known to the high priest, is called by the Ethiopic interpreter למוד, as if accustomed to the priest and used to associating with him. These things are from de Dieu.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ONAGER ASSVETVS IN SOLITVDINE) O- nagrum feminam intellige: est enim haec vox ut aliae mul- tae & in hac & in aliis linguis επικoινος.

ATTRAXIT VENTVM AMORIS SVI) Emi- nus olfecit marem. Legit hic interpres & alii תאבתה, ubi nos habemus תאותה, id est, occursus sui, nempe auram obviam.

NVLLUS AVERTET EAM) Nemo est qui inhi- bere eam possit, ne ad marem currat.

OMNES QVI QVAERVN T EAM NON DE- FICIENT) Redit ad primam comparationem. Sic etiam ait, qui hac meretrice uti voluit, nemo recusatus est.

IN MENSTRVIS EJVS INVENIENT EAM) Id est, etiam in menstruis eam paratam invenient, qui vo- lent. Non potuit impudentissimum scortum melius descri- bere.

Convenientior videtur translatio de Dievii, cujus locum ascribam: Sicut onager assuetus de- serto in desiderio animae suae anhelat ventum. Occa- sionem ejus quis avertet? nulli quaerentes eam lassa- bantur, in novilunio ejus invenient eam. Impu- dentissimam spiritualis scortationis libidinem expri- mit. Primo, quod instar sylvestris onagri anhelan- tis ventum, nihil aliud animo desideret, quam af- flari spiritu idolorum. Secundo quod ita ferveat hoc desiderio, ut ab inventa scortandi occasione nemo eam avertere queat. Tertio quod nequa- quam opus sit, amatios in persequenda ea multum lassari, quandoquidem facillima sit inventu. Et quia singulo novilunio convenire solebant, atque ob fecisti solemnitatem, novamque lunae Φασιν, quae etiamnum magno honore ab omnibus Orien- talibus excipitur, peculiari quodam fervore ac cultum idololatricu flagrabant, addit in novilunio ejus inveniri eam posse. Quod quidam secuti Vul- gatam בחדשה vertunt in menstruis ejus, non vide- tur probandum. Menstruum נדה dicitur, non חדש & peregrinum est, quod eandem ei fignificatio- nem tribui velit Junius, Hos. 5, 7. Porro למוד מדבר edoctus deserti recte vertitur affuetus deserto. Significatione eam verbu למד habet, prae fertim in lingua Æthiopica, ubi pro folere & af- fuevisse usurpatur usitatissime. Ut Matth. 27, 15. Luc. 2, 42. & Joan. 18, 15. Discipulus ille, qui dicitur fuiffe γνωστὸς notus Pontifici maximo, ab Æthiop. Interprete dicitur למוד quasi assuetus Pontifici & solitus cum eo versari. Hæc de Dieu.

## 2:25
Vers. 25.

WITHHOLD THY FOOT FROM NAKEDNESS) That is, if anyone has said to you: (for this must be supplied here) do not uncover the female parts. For the Hebrews, like others, honestly call them by the name of feet. See Gen. 49, 10.

AND THY THROAT FROM THIRST) A new translation in the comparison itself; for by thirst he understands lust. You will understand what the throat is from Prov. 30, 16. 20.

AND THOU HAST SAID: I HAVE DESPAIRED) In the Hebrew: It is despaired: that is, I cannot abstain.

STRANGERS) In the comparison, men: in the application, gods.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

PROHIBE PEDEM TUUM A NUDITATE) Id est, si quis tibi dixit: (id enim hic supplendum) noli de- nudare partes muliebres. Eas enim Hebræi, ut & alii, ho- neste pedum vocant nomine. Vide Gen. 49, 10.

ET GUTTUR TUUM A SITI) Nova transla- tio in ipsa comparatione; nam sitim intelligit libidinem. Guttur quid sit intelliges ex Prov. 30, 16. 20.

ET DIXISTI: DESPERAVI) In Hebræo: Despe- ratum est: id est, abstinere nequeo.

ALIENOS) In comparatione viros: in ἀνταποδόσει Deos.

## 2:26
Vers. 26.

AS THE THIEF IS ASHAMED WHEN HE IS FOUND) Namely, he who was acting the part of an honest man.

SO ARE THEY ASHAMED) Better in the future, they shall be put to shame, by the very event, abandoned by their idols. Isaiah 46, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

QUOMODO CONFUNDITUR FUR QUANDO DEPREHENDITUR) Nempe qui honestum hominem agebat.

SIC CONFUSI SUNT) Melius in futuro, pudefient, ipfo eventu, derelicti à suis idolis. Esaias 46, 7.

## 2:27
Vers. 27. SAYING TO A STOCK: THOU ART MY FATHER) That is, God. Thus Jupiter, Marspiter, Diespiter among the Latins. Moreover, the images of the gods bore names, and indeed the gods themselves were believed to dwell within them.

AND TO A STONE, YOU HAVE BEGOTTEN ME) Which was accustomed to be said especially to the sun.

AND IN THE TIME OF THEIR AFFLICTION THEY WILL SAY: ARISE AND DELIVER US) Then, having abandoned their ineffective idols, they will have recourse to me.

Latin:

Vers. 27. DICENTES LIGNO: PATER MEUS ES TU) Id est, Deus, Sic Juppiter, Marspiter, Diespiter apud Latinos. Simulacra autem Deorum ferebant nomina, imo & Dii in ipsis habitare credebantur.

ET LAPIDI, TU ME GENUISTI) Quod Soli præsertim dici solebat.

ET IN TEMPORE AFFLICTIONIS SUÆ DICENT: SURGE ET LIBERA NOS) Tunc omissis inefficaci- bus idolis ad me recurrent.

## 2:28
Verse 28. WHERE ARE YOUR GODS?) Supply: but I will answer.

ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF YOUR CITIES, INDEED, WERE YOUR GODS, JUDAH) You have the same below 11, 13. Add 4 Kings 21.

Latin:

Vers. 28. UBI SUNT DII TUI?) Supple: ego au- tem respondebo.

SECUNDUM NUMERUM QUIPPE CIVITA- TUM TUARUM, ERANT DII TUI JUDA) Idem habes infra 11, 13. Adde 4. Reg. 21.

## 2:30
Verse 30. IN VAIN HAVE I STRUCK YOUR CHILDREN) During the course of the Assyrians.

YOUR SWORD HAS DEVOURD YOUR PROPHETS) Given to you by God, in the times of Asa, Joash, and Manasseh. You have the same in Neh. 9, 26 and Matt. 23, 34. Add Luke 13, 34; 11, 49; Acts 7, 52; James 5, 10.

O GENERATION, AS A WASTING LION: SEE THE WORD OF THE LORD) In the Hebrew, that 'as a wasting lion' closes the previous sense: then follows, O generation! (O men of this age!) you, I say, consider the word of the Lord; as if he were saying: I have spoken about your ancestors: now I come to you: attend to what I am about to say.

Latin:

Vers. 30. FRUSTRA PERCUSSI FILIOS VESTROS) In cursu Assyriorum.

DEVORAVIT GLADIUS VESTER PROPHE- TAS VESTROS) Vobis à Deo datos, Asæ, Joasi, Ma- nassis temporibus. Habes idem Neh. 9, 26. & Matt. 23, 34. Adde Luc. 13, 34. 11, 49. Act. 7, 52. Jac. 5, 10.

QUASI LEO VASTATOR GENERATIO VE- STRA: VIDETE VERBUM DOMINI) In Hebræo il- lud quasi leo vastator priorē sensum claudit: sequitur deinde, ô generatio! (o homines hujus seculi!) vos, inquam, confide- rate verbum Domini; quasi dicat: locutus sum de majori- bus vestris: jam ad vos venio: attendite quid dicturus sim.

## 2:31
HAVE I BECOME A WILDERNESS TO ISRAEL?) That is, have I been unfruitful to them, like the deserts of the Arabs?

OR A LATE LAND) He translates well what is here מאפליה. Thus אפילות is taken in Exod. 9, 30. In the Talmudic writings, rains, clouds, and crops are often called אפילי. The sense is: have I been slow in bringing benefit to them? Nay, most swift, while they obeyed me.

Latin:

NUMQUID SOLITUDO FACTUS SUM I- SRAELI?) Id est, an infructuosus ipsis fui, ut Arabū deserta?

AVT TERRA SEROTINA) Bene vertit quod hic est מאפליה. Sic אפילות sumitur Exod. 9, 30. In Thalmudicis sæpe imbres, nubes, fruges אפילי. Sensus est an tardus fui in utilitate ipsis adferenda? imo celerri- mus, dum mihi paruerunt.

## 2:32
Verse 32. DOES A VIRGIN FORGET HER ORNAMENT) These are feminine ornaments, with which a woman is adorned: such as earrings, bracelets, armlets, rings, besides signet rings, and everything that is prepared for no other purpose than for the sake of adorning the body, of which number these also are: gold, gems, small stones: says Ulpian in Law 'Argumento', D. de auro, argento mundo.

OR A BRIDE HER BREAST-BAND) That breast-covering in the Apophioreta: Cinna's breast-band: 'Girding her nursing breasts with a breast-band.' And Turpilius, in whom a virgin speaks: 'Woe is me, for the letter fell from me between the ways, unhappy me, from between the little tunic and the breast-band where I had placed it.' See, if you like, what we have said regarding the image of the virgin in the Aratea.

Latin:

Vers. 32. NUMQUID OBLIVISCITUR VIRGO ORNAMENTI SUI) Ornamenta muliebria sunt, quibus mulier ornatur: Veluti inaures, armillæ, viriolæ, annuli, præter fignatorios, & omnia quæ ad aliam rem nullam pa- rantur, nisi corporis ornandi causa, quo ex numero etiam hæc sunt aurum, gemmæ, lapilli: ait Ulpianus L. Argu- mento, D. de auro, argento mundo.

AVT SPONSA FASCIÆ PECTORALIS SUÆ) Id mamillare in Apophioretis: Strophium Cinnæ: Strophio lactentes cincta papillas. Et Turpilio apud quem virgo loquitur: Me miseram quoniam inter vias epistola excidit mihi Infelix, inter tuniculam, ac strophium quam collocave- ram. Vide si libet quæ diximus ad imaginem virginis in Arateis.

## 2:33
Verse 33. WHY DO YOU STRIVE TO SHOW YOUR WAY TO BE GOOD, TO SEEK LOVE) In the Hebrew: by seeking love: as if he were saying: You clear yourself in vain, since you do nothing except what is pleasing to you.

WHICH FURTHERMORE YOU HAVE ALSO TAUGHT YOUR WAYS OF MALICE) That 'malices' is explained by 'your ways': That is, by your example you make even wicked nations more wicked.

Latin:

Vers. 33. QUID NITERIS BONAM OSTENDERE VIAM TUAM, AD QUÆRENDAM DILECTIO- NEM) In Hebræo: quærendo dilectionem: quasi dicat: Fru- stra te purgas, cum nihil agas nisi quod tibi sit libitum.

QUÆ INSUPER ET MALITIAS TUAS DO- CVISTI VIAS TUAS) Illud malitias exponitur per vias tuas: Id est, tuo exemplo etiam gentes improbas improbio- res facis.

## 2:34
Verse 34.

AND IN YOUR WINGS) Namely, of your garments, just as כנף is used in 1 Sam. 24:6, Lam. 4:14.

NOT IN THE DITCHES HAVE I FOUND THEM) In the Hebrew: Not with a digging (instrument) did you find them: so that those, namely, you could kill them as if they were directarios according to the law. See Exodus 21, 22, and what we have said about the Law of War and Peace, book 2, chapter 12. BUT IN ALL THINGS WHICH I MENTIONED ABOVE) That is: You killed them for this reason, because they would not follow your idolatries. The Greeks took אלון not for the pronoun 'these', but for an oak, less conveniently. Verse 35. I WILL CONTEND WITH THEE IN JUDGMENT, BECAUSE THOU HAST SAID: I HAVE NOT SINNED) The denial of guilt increases the guilt. Verse 36. HOW VILE ART THOU BECOME, REPEATING THY WAYS] In the Hebrew: Why do you run about so much by changing your way? That is, now you flatter the Assyrians, now the Egyptians, by imitating their cults. AND THOU SHALT BE ASHAMED OF EGYPT, AS THOU WAST ASHAMED OF ASSUR) The Assyrian, having violated the pacts, laid waste the land: the Egyptian besieged the city, exacted tribute for a great matter, and it will profit you nothing. 1 Kings 23, 24 chapters. Verse 37. FOR THOU SHALT GO OUT ALSO FROM THIS) That is, your envoys will return in vain with the greatest sorrow, as follows. AND THY HANDS SHALL BE UPON THY HEAD) Which is a custom for women in deep grief. 2 Samuel 13, 19. THE LORD HATH DESTROYED THY CONFIDENCE.) In the Hebrew: thy confidences: He has corrupted all your hopes. None of them will succeed.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

ET IN ALIS TUIS) Nempe vestium tuarum, quomodo כנף sumitur 1. Sam. 24, 6. Thren. 4, 14.

NON IN FOSSIS INVENI EOS) In Hebræo: Non cum perfossorio (instrumento) invenisti eos: ut illos scili- tet tanquam directarios occidere ex lege poffes. Vide Exod. 21, 22. & quæ à nobis dicta de Jure Belli & Pacis libro 2, č. 12. SED IN OMNIBVS QVÆ SVPRA MEMO- RAVI) Id est: Ideo eos occidisti, quod tuas idololatrias sequi nollent. Græci אלון, non pro pronomine istis, sed pro quercu sumsere, minus commode. Vers. 35. EGO JVDICIO CONTENDAM TECVM, EO QVOD DIXERIS: NON PECCAVI) Auget cul- pam culpæ negatio. Vers. 36. QVAM VILIS FACTA ES NIMIS, ITE- RANS VIAS TUAS] In Hebræo: Quid discursas adeo mutando viam tuam? Id est, nunc Assyriis blandiris, nunc Ægyptiis, ipsorum cultus imitando. ET AB ÆGYPTO CONFUNDERIS, SICUT CONFUSA ES AB ASSUR) Assyrius pactis violatis ter- ram vastavit: urbem obsedit Ægyptius magna de re tribu- ta exegit, nec quicquam tibi proderit. 1. Reg. 23. 24. capp. Vers. 37. NAM ET AB ISTA EGREDIERIS) Id est, Legati tui irriti redibunt cum mœrore summo, ut se- quitur. ET MANUS TUÆ ERUNT SUPER CAPUT TUUM) Qui mos feminis in gravi dolore 2. Sam. 13, 19. OBTRIVIT DOMINUS CONFIDENTIAM TUAM.) In Hebræo: confidentias tuas: Omnes spes tuas corrupit. Nulla earum succedet.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. An invitation of the fornicating Judea to repentance. The punishment of the divorce of the fornication of Israel is proposed to Judah; she is ordered to repent, with a promise of grace, and of betrothal, and of the multiplication of the faithful under the New Testament. A formula of repentance.

Verse 1. SHALL HE RETURN TO HER ANY MORE) Is there any husband so remiss that, even if the law permitted it, he would want to take her back? The Arabs, for the highest execration, say: Would you take back a woman thrice dismissed and possessed by others? SHALL NOT THAT WOMAN BE DEFILED AND POLLUTED?) In the Hebrew: But is not that land defiled and polluted? That is Judea, so that here an anapodoton begins. But the Greeks, whom this interpreter follows, read אשה instead of ארץ. Who will believe that the LXX Interpreters read אשה instead of ארץ? They looked to the sense, as often elsewhere, and did not render the word word-for-word. And therefore there is no need to invent a new reading. YET RETURN TO ME) Yet I am of such patience that I would want to take you back. LIFT UP THY EYES ON HIGH) In the Hebrew: on the height. Verse 2. IN THE WAYS THOU SAT.) In all the crossroads and alleys. See Genesis 38, 14. WAITING FOR THEM AS A ROBBER IN THE WILDERNESS) In the Hebrew, as the Chaldean has interpreted it, Like an Arab in the desert. You laid snares for everyone, like those Arabs who, even up to the times of Jerome (and indeed up to our own), used to raid the borders of Palestine, and would besiege the roads for those descending from Jerusalem to Jericho. THOU HAST POLLUTED THE LAND) As above in verse 1. Verse 3. WHEREFORE THE SHOWERS WERE WITHHELD, AND THERE WAS NO LATE RAIN: THOU HADST A HARLOT'S FOREHEAD, THOU WOULDST NOT BLUSH) It is better to translate with others: And although the drops of rain were withheld, and there was no late rain (which is the late rain for the Hebrews, among whom the popular year began from autumn), yet you kept the forehead of a harlot, so that you would not blush. Verse 4. THEREFORE AT THE LEAST FROM HENCEFORTH CALL TO ME) Or even now at least, taught by so many evils. MY FATHER) Who loved me as a father. THOU ART THE GUIDE OF MY VIRGINITY) In the Hebrew, O guide of my youth; who cherished me from my earliest age. Compare Proverbs 2, 16. Verse 5. WILL THOU BE ANGRY FOR EVER?) These are the words that you ought to have spoken. BEHOLD THOU HAST SPOKEN, AND HAST DONE EVIL, AND HAST BEEN ABLE) The sense is: If you were to speak thus, although you have done (many) evils, you would prevail: that is, you would take away my anger.

Latin:

CAPUT III. Invitatio Judææ fornicatricis ad pœnitenti- am. Pœna repudii fornicationis Israelis proposita Juda deterior resipiscere jube- tur, cum promissione gratiæ, & desponsa tionis, & multiplicationis fidelium sub N. T. Formula pœnitentiæ.

Vers. 1. NUMQUID REVERTETUR AD EAM UL- TRA) Estne maritus aliquis adeo remissus, ut, etiamsi lex id permitteret, vellet eam recipere? Arabes pro summo ex- secratione dicunt: Ter dimissam, & ab aliis subactam recipias. NVMQVID NON CONTAMINATA ET POL- LUTA ERIT MULIER ILLA?) In Hebræo: An vero non contaminata & polluta est terra illa? Id est Judæa, ut hic incipiat ἀναπόδοτον. At Græci, quos hic interpres sequi- tur, legerunt אשה pro ארץ. QUis credet LXX. Interpp. legisse אשה pro ארץ? Sensum respexere, ut sæpe alias, non verbum κατὰ πόδα reddiderunt. Ideoque opus non est novam lectionem fingere. TAMEN REVERTERE AD ME) Tamen tanta sum patientia, ut recipere te velim. LEVA OCULOS TUOS IN DIRECTUM) In Hebræo: in excelso. Vers. 2. IN VIIS SEDEBAS.) Cunctis in triviis & angiportis. Vid. Genes. 38, 14. EXPECTANS EOS QVASI LATRO IN SO- LITUDINE) In Hebræo, ut Chaldæus interpretatus est, Velut Arabs in deserto. Insidias fecisti omnibus, sicut Ara- bes illi, qui ad Hieronymi usque tempora (imo & ad no- stra) incursabant terminos Palæstinæ, & descendentibus de Jerusalem in Jericho, obsidebant vias. POLLUISTI TERRAM) Ut supra 1. Vers. 3. QUAMOBREM PROHIBITÆ SUNT STILLÆ PLUVIARUM, ET SEROTINUS IMBER NON FUIT: FRONS MULIERIS MERETRICIS FACTA EST TIBI, NOLUISTI ERUBESCERE) Melius cum aliis vertas: Et quamquam retentæ sunt guttæ pluviæ, neque ullus fuit imber serotinus, (qui serotinus Hebræis, apud quos annus popularis ab autumno inchoabat) tibi ta- men mansit frons meretricis, ne erubesceres. Vers. 4. ERGO SALTEM A MODO VOCA ME) Vel nunc saltem tot malis edocta. PATER MI) Qui me amasti, ut pater. DUX VIRGINITATIS MEÆ TU ES) In He- bræo, ô dux adolescentiæ meæ; qui me à prima ætate fovisti. Conf. Prov. 2, 16. Vers. 5. NUMQUID IRASCERIS IN PERPE- TUUM?) Hæc sunt verba, quæ te loqui oportuit. ECCE LOCUTA ES, ET FECISTI MALA, ET POTUISTI) Sensus est: Si ita loquereris, quamquam mala (plurima) fecisti, prævaleres: id est, iram mihi adime- res.

## 3:6
Verse 6. AND THE LORD SAID TO ME IN THE DAYS OF KING JOSIAH] Here a new chapter ought to have begun. We have said elsewhere that the rites were somewhat corrected by Josiah, but that the mind of most of the people remained from the times of Manasseh.

BACKSLIDER] Turned away from God: The LXX read מושבה, the dwelling.

ISRAEL] Thus the 10 tribes are called here. For the name opposite to Judah follows, that is, the tribe of Judah and Benjamin, together with the priests and Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD ME IN DIE- BVS JOSIÆ REGIS] Hic novum caput inchoari de- buit. Diximus alibi à Josiæ ritus aliquantum correctos fuisse, sed plerisque è populo mansisse mentem ex Manassis tem- poribus.

AVERSATRIX] Aversa à Deo: LXX. Legerunt מושבה, ἡ κατοικία.

ISRAEL] Ita hic vocantur X. tribus. Sequitur enim nomen oppositum Juda, id est, tribus Judæ & Benjaminis, una cum sacerdotibus & Levitis.

## 3:8
Verse 8. I HAD GIVEN HER A BILL OF DIVORCE) I had cast her off from my protection.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DEDISSEM EI LIBELLUM REPVDII] Abdicâssem illam à tutela mea.

## 3:9
Verse 9. AND BY THE EASE OF HER FORNICATION) By ease understand frequency: others interpret it as fame.

SHE HATH DEFILED THE LAND.) See Deuteronomy 24, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET FACILITATE FORNICATIONIS SVÆ) Per facilitatem intellige frequentiam: alii famam in- terpretantur.

CONTAMINAVIT TERRAM.) Vide Deut. 24, 4.

## 3:10
Vers. 10. WITH ALL HER HEART) That is, with a sincere mind.

BUT IN FALSEHOOD) Deceitfully.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN TOTO CORDE SVO) Id est, sincero animo.

SED IN MENDACIO) Simulatè.

## 3:11
Vers. 11. BACKSLIDING ISRAEL HATH JUSTIFIED HER SOUL, IN COMPARISON OF TREACHEROUS JUDAH) That is; she appeared less guilty. See Ezek. 16, 51. & Luke 18, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 11. JUSTIFICAVIT ANIMAM SVAM AVER- SATRIX ISRAEL, COMPARATIONE PRÆVARI- CATRICIS JUDÆ) Id est; minus nocens apparuit. Vide Ezech. 16, 51. & Luc. 18, 14.

## 3:12
Vers. 12. GO AND PROCLAIM THESE WORDS TOWARD THE NORTH) Toward Media and the neighboring regions, into which the men of the ten tribes had been deported by Tiglath-pileser and Shalmaneser.

RETURN, THOU BACKSLIDING ISRAEL) Return to the law and the worship of the one true God. Since most of them never obeyed that condition, it is no wonder if the promises made here were not fulfilled in them.

FOR I AM HOLY) In the Hebrew: Benign.

Latin:

Vers. 12. VADE ET CLAMA SERMONES ISTOS CONTRA AQVILONEM) Mediam versus & vicinas re- giones, in quas decem tribuum homines à Teglathphalas- saro & Salmanassare erant deportati.

REVERTERE AVERSATRIX ISRAEL) Redite ad legem & unius veri Dei cultum. Ei conditioni cum ple- rique illorum nunquam paruerint, non mirum est, si pro- missa hic facta in ipsis impleta non sunt.

QVIA SANCTVS EGO) In Hebræo: Benignus.

## 3:13
NEVERTHELESS KNOW THINE INIQUITY) Better: Only acknowledge thy guilt.

Vers. 13. THOU HAST SCATTERED THY WAYS TO THE STRANGERS) To the gods, that is. Lucan 2. Nor did all the temples of the highest Thunderer lie prostrate: They divided the gods.

Latin:

VERUMTAMEN SCITO INIQVITATEM TVAM) Melius: Tantum agnosce culpam.

Vers. 13. DISPERSISTI VIAS TVAS ALIENIS) Diis scilicet. Lucan. 2. Nec cunctæ summi Templi jacuere Tonantis: Divisere deos.

## 3:14
TURN, O BACKSLIDING CHILDREN) In the Hebrew: Refractory.

V. 14. AND I WILL TAKE YOU ONE OF A CITY, AND TWO OF A FAMILY) Even if in some city and village there were only one or two Israelites, I will not forget even them. The Rabbis also refer these things mystically to the times of the Messiah: But what follows below in verse 20 shows that the primary sense is different.

Latin:

CONVERTIMINI FILII REVERTENTES) In Hebræo: Refractarii.

V. 14. ET ASSVMAM VOS UNVM DE CIVITA- TE, ET DVOS DE COGNATIONE) Etsiamsi in aliqua urbe & vico unus tantum aut duo essent Israelitæ, etiam illorum non obliviscar. Ad Messiæ tempora μυσικῶς hæc etiam Rabbini referunt: Sed alium esse sensum primum ostendunt quæ sequuntur infra 20.

## 3:15
Vers. 15. AND I WILL GIVE YOU PASTORS ACCORDING TO MY HEART) That is, Princes, as above 1, 7.

AND THEY SHALL FEED YOU WITH KNOWLEDGE AND DOCTRINE.) That is, skillfully and wisely, as the Chaldean and the LXX here.

But why should these not be understood as referring to the Doctors of the Word and Priests, who feed the people with knowledge and doctrine? Indeed, the following verses teach that these things speak of the preaching of the Apostles and their successors in the New Testament. Cf. also Ez. 34, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET DABO VOBIS PASTORES JVXTA COR MEUM) Id est, Principes, ut supra 1, 7.

ET PASCENT VOS SCIENTIA ET DOCTRI- NA.) Id est, perite ac sapienter, ut hic Chaldæus & LXX.

Cur vero non de Doctoribus verbi & Sacerdo- tibus, qui scientia, & doctrina pascunt populum, hæc accipiantur? imo de prædicatione Apostolo- rum & successorum in N. T. hæc loqui sequentia docent. Conf. & Ez. 34, 12.

## 3:16
Vers. 16.

THEY SHALL NO MORE SAY: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT OF THE LORD.) Supply, let it go before us into battle. The following verses teach that this must be understood entirely in this way: for it was accustomed to be brought into the camps in the hope of more immediate protection, as appears in 1 Sam. 4, 4. Add Joshua 3, 3. 6, 11. ch. 4, 7. 6, 8. 13. 2 Sam. 4, 3. 7, 2. 11, 11. 15, 24.

NEITHER SHALL IT COME TO MIND, NEITHER SHALL THEY REMEMBER IT.) Namely, for that use.

NEITHER SHALL IT BE VISITED, NEITHER SHALL IT BE MADE ANY MORE.) That is, there shall be no fighting, nor shall those things be done which are now accustomed to be done in war. To use 'visit' for 'to fight' is a χαριεντισμὸς, such as in 2 Kings 14, 8. פקד is often translated by ἐκδικεῖν. See also Isaiah 27, 3. The Chaldean here: Neither shall battle be joined in it any more.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

NON DICENT VLTRA : ARCA TESTA- MENTI DOMINI.) Supple, præcedat nos ad prælium. Omnino sic intelligenda hæc esse docent sequentia: Solebat enim ea in castra adferri spe præsentioris præsidii, ut appa- ret 1. Sam. 4, 4. Adde Josuæ 3, 3. 6, 11. c. 4, 7. 6, 8. 13. 2. Sam. 4, 3. 7, 2. 11, II. 15, 24.

NEQVE ASCENDET SVPER COR, NEQVE RECORDABUNTUR ILLIUS.) Nempe ad eum usum.

NEC VISITABITVR, NEC FUIT VLTRA.) Id est, non pugnabitur, nec ea fient, quæ nunc in bello fieri solent. Visitare pro pugnare est χαριεντισμὸς, qualis 2. Reg. 14, 8. פקד vertitur sæpe per ἐκδικεῖν. Vide & Esaiæ 27, 3. Chaldæus hic: Nec in ea amplius inibitur prælium.

## 3:17
Vers. 17.

AT THAT TIME THEY SHALL CALL JERUSALEM THE THRONE OF THE LORD.) That is, the divine power will appear in it. Certain Rabbis refer this passage to the time after the resurrection, namely in a certain more sublime sense.

AND ALL THE NATIONS SHALL BE GATHERED UNTO IT.) Many from the nations shall come, to offer true worship to God in the court of the Gentiles.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

IN TEMPORE ILLO VOCABVNT JERVSA- LEM SOLIVM DOMINI.) Id est, potentia divina in eo apparebit. Hunc locum Rabbini quidam ad tempus post resurrectionem referunt, nempe sensu quodam sublimiore.

ET CONGREGABVNTVR AD EAM OMNES GENTES) Multi ex gentibus venient, Deo vero cultum exhibituri in subdiali Gentium.

## 3:18
Vers. 18. THE HOUSE OF JUDAH SHALL GO TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL.) The two kingdoms, long divided and having clashed with each other in grievous wars, shall unite.

AND THEY SHALL COME TOGETHER OUT OF THE LAND OF THE NORTH.) Namely those whom Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser took captive from the ten tribes, and no less those whom Sennacherib took captive from Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 18. IBIT DOMVS JVD A AD DOMVM ISRAEL.) Regna duo diu divulsa, & gravibus bellis inter se collisa coalescent.

ET VENIENT SIMVL DE TERRA AQVILO- NIS.) Nempe illi, quos Teglathphalasar & Salmanasar ex decem tribubus, nec minus illi, quos Sennacheribus ex Judæa captivos fecit.

## 3:19
Verse 19.

I WILL PLACE YOU AMONG THE CHILDREN, ] I will cause you to flourish with much offspring. I WILL GIVE YOU A DESIRABLE LAND ] Worthy to be sought after with prayers. A PREEMINENT HERITAGE ] That is, most pleasant. You have צבי concerning the land of Judea. And 2 Sam. 1:19, and Ezek. 25:9, Dan. 11:6. OF THE ARMIES OF THE NATIONS ] Better with the conjunction added, and the armies of the nations, I will give to you, namely, for slaughter, captivity, and plunder. AND I SAID: YOU SHALL CALL ME FATHER, AND YOU SHALL NOT CEASE TO FOLLOW ME. ] Better: But at the same time I said: Call me Father, and do not cease to follow me. Under this law I promise these things.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

PONAM TE IN FILIOS, ] Efficiam, ut multa So- bole floreas. TRIBUAM TIBI TERRAM DESIDERABILEM] Dignam quæ votis expetatur. HÆREDITATEM PRÆCLARAM ] Id est, arb4 letiffima. צבי de terra Judæa habes. Et 2. Sam. 1, 19. & Ezech. 25, 9. Dan. 11, 6. EXERCITUUM GENTIUM ] Melius addita copu- la, & exercitus gentium, tibi dabo scilicet in occidionem, captivitatem, prædam. ET DIXI: PATREM VOCABIS ME, ET POST ME INGREDI NON CESSABIS. ] Melius : Sed simul dixi: Patrem me voca, & ne ceffa me sequi. Sub hac lege ista promitto.

## 3:20
Verse 20. BUT AS A WOMAN DESPISES HER LOVER, SO HAS THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL DESPISED ME. ] He now shows why those promises had not had their effect, because, forsooth, Israel on its part did not do what it ought.

Grotius, in this passage, in his customary manner, most wretchedly perverts a notable testimony of the Christian faith which the Church uses against the Jews. For since this passage concerns the abrogation of the Levitical worship and the calling of the Gentiles and the preaching of the Gospel under the New Testament, Grotius twists it into a completely contrary sense, in a thoroughly Jewish manner, as if the discourse were not about the abrogation of the Levitical worship, nor about the time of the New Testament, but about the tranquil state of the Jewish polity. Therefore, having deserted the opinion of the Christian Church, he interprets it with the blind Jews, or rather corrupts the illustrious passage: inasmuch as R. Isaac Ben Abraham in Chizuk Haënum, who recounts this Rabbinic gloss, says there will be no war, nor any necessity for the ark of the covenant to be brought into battle, as was done formerly. And with R. Menasse Ben Israel, q. 7 in Levit. What is said about not remembering the ark is to be understood as meaning that they will not demand the ark to prepare for war, or to lead it with them into battle. R. David Kimchi had preceded them in this, explaining it in this way: Even if you multiply and become fruitful in the land, yet the nations will not envy you so as to come and wage war against you, and thus you have need to go out to war and lead the ark of God with you, as was their custom, for when going out to war they led the ark with them; for in those days there will be no need for that thing. For there will be no war anymore. Hence he says: They will not visit it, nor will it happen again, i.e., that thing, that they should lead the ark into war. And R. Solomon: It will not happen again, i.e., that which was formerly done in Shiloh, when in the time of Eli they led it into war against the Philistines. From which it is manifest that Grotius judaizes here completely. But that Jewish gloss is easily refuted, and the sense of the Christian Church shines forth, if these things are observed. First, that it is customary for the Prophets, when they exhort the people to conversion and call them back from idolatry, to deal with and prophesy about the times of the Messiah, in which idolatry is to cease, and about his benefits, which only the faithful and penitent enjoy. Furthermore, when a spiritual betrothal is promised here, 'Return, O backsliding children' (or rather, refractory; as B. Luther rendered it from the Hebrew, in which opinion Grotius also amends the Vulgate), the Lord says, 'for I am your husband,' which betrothal does not look to the Polity or the political state, but to the Church; not to bodily benefits, but to spiritual ones, Hos. 2:14, 1 Cor. 11:2. Therefore, the Prophet deals with such benefits as pertain to the spiritual betrothal of the Lord, and are proper to the faithful and the converted. Thirdly, when it is promised, 'And I will take you, one from a city and two from a family,' it is not a matter of a small multitude in the polity, city, or village being taken or cared for; but of the faithful, who, although they will make a small number from the Jews in the Church, will not, however, be none, because the Lord will preserve some seed for himself. Nor is there any discourse about a reduction into Jerusalem, because those recalled from Babylon were not such a small number, but many thousands: which argument Cornelius a Lapide uses. The Prophet, or rather God, does not speak here of the return of the Jews from Babylon under Cyrus and Ezra, as the Hebrews, Theodoret, Hugo, and S. Thomas wish; for then not one or two, but 42,000 returned. If anyone says that it is only indicated that those indeed were to be led back into their Fatherland, but that that reduction would not be universal, but restricted and few in respect to those who were to remain in Babylon of their own accord and willingly, when it is said: 'I will take one from a city, and two from a family': that could indeed be admitted, without detriment to the cause of the Christians, as Joh. Buxtorf explained in Hist. arc. foeder. c. 13, so that, namely, this may be indulged to the Jews: but without danger and prejudice to the following prophecy, and so two parts of this prophecy are established: the first concerning that which God was to perform at that time, v. 14, 15; the second concerning that which is to be afterwards, after they had been restored and again rooted and confirmed in their land, in the time of the Messiah, v. 16, 17, 18, 19; both because the Jews themselves acknowledge these two parts, and because it is most customary for the Prophets, while dealing with the temporal things of deliverance, especially concerning the Babylonian captivity, to fly off as it were abruptly, and make a transition from them to the spiritual deliverance of the Messiah. But because Christian Interpreters for the most part, as Buxtorf admits, do not wish the Prophet to be dealing here with that bodily reduction, but to be making a promise and prophecy about the taking of some of the Jews and their leading into the Kingdom of Christ and to his Church, which they understand by Zion, and to be saying of them, 'one from a city, two from a family,' and that very few in total in respect to the rest were to be converted from the beginning of the Gospel, and that v. 15 is said about the shepherds, whom the Lord was to give according to his heart, feeding them with knowledge and understanding, they interpret it as the Apostles instructing men with the true knowledge and cognition of Christ, so that in the following words it is further described what the state of the Church will be, after it has been increased and multiplied by the calling and accession of the Gentiles also to it: we see no reason why we should depart from this passive interpretation of the Christians and Rabbis. For although no mark of distinction or transition to a new prophecy connects these with the preceding, it is nevertheless not new, when a people is stirred to conversion and repentance, for arguments to be brought forward from the benefits of the Messiah: and these cohere excellently: that the refractory among the people ought to be converted, since God is about to show this people such grace, that He is about to betroth it to Himself, to have care of it as a husband, and from the remnant of this people to build for Himself a catholic Church through the Apostles. Thus Jerome: Be converted to me, etc. The Jews think this was fulfilled after the return from Babylon under Cyrus, King of the Persians, and Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, even though not all returned: that this is signified by, I will take one from a city and two from a family. But it is better [referred] to the advent of Christ, when the remnant were saved, as the Apostle says and explains: Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom and would have been like Gomorrah. Then they were introduced into Zion, of which it is written: Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God. What of the fact that some of the Jews themselves refer these to the times of the Messiah, not only μυστικῶς, as Grotius perverts their meaning, but in such a way that they assert this to be the literal sense? For thus in the Codex Sanhedrin, distinct. Chelek, it is explained concerning the time of the Messiah.

Rabbi said: All the terms and the whole (of the coming of Christ) are fulfilled. There is a tradition that R. Eliezer said: If they repent, they will be redeemed, as it is said in Jer. 3:14: Return, O backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. R. Joshua said: And is it not said (Jer. 3:14): And I will take you one of a city and two of a family? Fourthly, the shepherds who are promised here are not Princes, as Grotius wishes with the Jews, but those whose office it is to feed the people with knowledge and doctrine, which is the duty of heralds of the word and Doctors, not of Princes. For they are not said to be about to feed only skillfully and wisely, so that the manner might be indicated, but to feed with knowledge and doctrine, so that the object about which these shepherds are to be occupied might be designated, and their proper duty defined, which is situated in the communication of knowledge and doctrine, especially because the fruit of this pasturing and information is expressed: the recognition of the divine name, and walking not according to the desires of the heart, but according to the will of the Lord; and it corresponds to that pasturing that, being thus informed by doctrine and knowledge, they are not to serve the Lord God according to the manner of the Levitical cult, but are to recognize and venerate Him in Spirit and truth as Father, v. 16, 19. Jerome in this place. And shepherds were given according to His heart, Apostles and apostolic men, and they fed the multitude of believers: not in Jewish ceremonies, but with the knowledge and doctrine of Christ: And in the whole world, with the preaching of the Gospel sown, they will by no means have confidence in the ark of the Lord, which was the guardian of the Mosaic law, but they themselves will be the temple of God: Nor, according to the erring Nazarenes, will they serve by abolishing sacrifices, but they will pursue spiritual worship. Fifthly, there is no mention made here of war by any word, nor is there anything in the text that indicates that sense, that there will be no more fighting, nor that there will be a place for those things which are wont to happen in war. That gloss is introduced into the text, it is not drawn from the words of the text. Therefore, those words, NEITHER SHALL IT BE VISITED, NEITHER SHALL IT BE MADE ANY MORE, are rashly rendered thus, that is, there shall be no fighting. To visit is indeed sometimes used in the sense of judging, but when it concerns the active visitation of God, which is either of judgment or of benefit, of wrath or of thanks, not when it concerns the visitation of men; and the interpretation is inept and twisted: THE ARK SHALL NOT BE VISITED any more, that is, there shall be no more fighting. For the ark was accustomed to be visited by the Israelites for the sake of worship. And therefore the verb of visiting must be taken properly. If you take visit improperly for ἐκδικεῖν or to fight here, what sense will it be, the Israelites shall not visit the ark any more, that is, they shall not judge or fight the ark any more? There is another reason for τὸ χαριεντισμᾶ in 2 Kings 14, namely, when conflict and battle are expressed through mutual inspection or vision. For armies are said to see one another when they engage for the sake of mutual conflict. But what is this to the visitation of the ark? Sixthly, the discourse is about the proper and ordinary use of the ark of the covenant, that it is about to cease: Because the words imply that: They shall say no more: the ark of the covenant of the Lord: For it is simply denied that the ark of the Lord will be carried, and that the memory of it will have remained any longer. To which that accumulation of phrases, used for the sake of emphasis, contributes: They shall say no more the ark of the covenant of the Lord, neither shall it come upon them, neither shall they remember it, neither shall it be visited, neither shall it be made any more.
