Rightly Buxtorf in the place cited: Not in vain and idly did the Prophet use this variety and reduplication of phrases concerning one and the same thing, but he undoubtedly wished to note something singular and most memorable. Which Abarbenel also observes: What, he says, was the need for this repetition, I wish I knew and understood it! He does not say 'any more' without an expressed Nominative, who are those who will not say it so any more? But because the Israelites cried out repeatedly, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord (Jer. 7:4), without doubt they are understood, that they will no longer boast of the ark or the material temple. Add that it is thus noted that the ark of the Lord will never again be carried. They shall not say, or IT SHALL NOT BE SAID any more. See similar passages in Jer. 16:15, 16; ch. 23:7, 8; ch. 31:29. There will therefore be another reason for divine worship under the New Testament, where there will no longer be an appeal to the ark of the Lord, worship will no longer be celebrated at the ark of the Lord, it will no longer be carried. Which sense the rest also demand. NEITHER SHALL IT COME UPON THE HEART, that is, no one will think of it. For this is to come upon the heart (2 Kings 12:12, 5; Jer. 7:31; ch. 32:33; Ez. 38:10). NEITHER SHALL THEY REMEMBER IT, they will not think of it, nor will they make mention of it. NEITHER SHALL THEY VISIT IT, or as others render: They shall not require, they shall not desire it. Because previously it was visited and required for the sake of worship. That, therefore, is predicted to cease. IT SHALL NOT BE MADE ANY MORE, that. Others explain it thus: The ark shall not be made any more: Others in this way: it shall not be made any more, that is, so that they might pray to it, sacrifice, perform sacred worship, none of these things will be done to it any further. B. Luther rendered it: Noch daselbst mehr opffern: because the word עשה is used concerning sacrifices (Ex. 10:25; Jud. 13:5; 1 Kings 18:28). And sacrifices were to cease at the time of the New Testament (Dan. 9:27). He thinks, therefore, that it is indicated by this oracle that neither worship at the ark of the covenant nor sacrifices will have a place any longer. There is not a jot of evidence concerning the bringing of the ark to battle. Nor was there any use for the ark here, except an extraordinary and singular one, which is never read to have been used in battle by divine command, except that it was carried around Jericho before the camp of Israel (Josh. 6). For what was used in the war against the Philistines 1. 1 Sam. 4, it was done against the command of God, whence the ark of the covenant itself was captured. Therefore, the ark was not ordained for the purpose of being led out into battle, as Grotius, along with the Jews, imagines: but its proper and perpetual use was restricted to the worship of God, Ex. 25, 10, whence they prayed before the ark of the Lord, Jos. 7, 6, and God manifested Himself from it, Ex. 25. And although in the earliest times, before it obtained a fixed and quiet place, it was carried about, yet that was never done in the time of the temple, nor could it be done. Concerning which, Abarbenel is to be heard on Jer. 3 (in Buxtorf, c. l. p. 208): In the time of the first temple, when Israel followed the lust of its own heart, all their holiness consisted in the House of the Sanctuary and in the Ark of GOD, which was there: And that partly because, through the presence of the Ark, they were guarded and were certain of the gracious providence of God, provided that they were righteous, etc. partly because through the ark, which contained the Tables of the covenant, they were drawn back from sin, and invited to seek the remission of sins from God; partly because oaths were accustomed to be made before it; and finally, because they prayed before it if the heaven were shut up, and rain did not descend, or if plague, war, or other public calamities threatened. Therefore, blessed Brentius rightly says on this passage: In the Church there is not that external ark of the Testament, which was fashioned by Moses in Exod. 25, in which was the Manna, the rod of Aaron, and the Tables of the Testament. Heb. 9. But with Christ coming, these shadowy things ceased, and the truth succeeded into their place. For Christ is the ark of the covenant. In whom is the Manna, for He Himself is the living bread. And the rod of Aaron, by which death and sin are repelled. And the tables of the Testament, that is, the Decalogue. For He did not come to abolish the law, but to fulfill it. The Church is the throne of the Lord, Ps. 131. This is my rest, He says, here I will dwell, for I have chosen it. Seventh, the opposition teaches that the discourse is not about war, but about the abrogation of the Levitical worship: Because the Israe- lites' gathering to the ark, or the visitation of the ark, is opposed by the congregation of the nations to the Church; the distinction between Jews and Gentiles, which existed in the Old Testament, is removed. Because Jerusalem shall be called the throne of the Lord, that is, it shall be recognized by all as the glorious seat in which God resides, and manifests His presence, glory, and majesty, to which all nations shall be gathered, to the name of the Lord at Jerusalem; by which name the earthly Jerusalem cannot be understood; for that was not of such capacity that it could contain all nations; for which not even all of Judea was sufficient. And therefore the mystical Jerusalem is designated, which is the mother of all us believers Gal. 4, 26. Wherefore, since the ark of the covenant was the seat and throne of the glory of the Lord, and the whole of Jerusalem is said to be His future throne in its place: it is intimated that the glory of the Lord will no longer be restricted to one place, as formerly, where He sat within the ark between the Cherubim, but that it will be extended more widely, nay, is to be enlarged through all nations, so that the Father may be worshipped everywhere in Spirit and in truth Joh. 4, 21. and that in every place holy hands may be lifted up 1. Tim. 2, 8. and in every place incense may be offered to the name of the Lord Mal. 1, 11. Some understand this of the city of Jerusalem, and render this meaning: In those days Jerusalem shall no longer be celebrated because God resides there in the temple, and in it within the ark between the Cherubim, and has His throne; but because the Lord Himself, not in cloud and fire, but manifested in the flesh, is about to appear to them, and not through a voice issuing from the propitiatory ark and speaking to Moses alone, but is about to teach and preach His Gospel publicly in the city, in the temple, at the crossroads, in the fields, etc., and thence through His Apostles is about to propagate it in the whole world. For then the Law shall go forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem Es. 2, 3. just as formerly the word of the Lord went forth to Moses from the ark. Then that Lord shall come to His temple, whom they sought in the Old Testament Mal. 3, 3. Then was fulfilled what He promised in Zechariah c. 3, 3. I return to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and Jerusalem shall be called the city of truth, (not of shadows and types) and the mountain of the Lord of hosts that mountain of holiness, as Buxtorf has it in the cited place.

Seventhly, these things cannot be understood of the external honor or splendor of Jerusalem, since it was not in such glory and reverence after the Babylonian captivity was ended, but was almost always subject to servitude, first of the Persians, then of the Greeks, and finally of the Romans. Nor can these be drawn to the congregation of the nations in the open air of the Gentiles. For here the discourse is not of a small or particular influx, but ALL NATIONS, says the Prophet, SHALL BE GATHERED TO IT. That this speaks of the calling and conversion of the Gentiles to the Church is too manifest: And the Prophet adds that they shall be gathered TO THE NAME OF THE LORD, because they shall turn themselves from their idols to worship and invoke Him. The Messiah can also be understood by the name of the Lord, as in Bereschith Rabba, the parallel passage Zeph. 3, 9. Because then I will turn to the peoples a pure lip to invoke all the name of the Lord, and to worship Him with one shoulder, is explained: It is not the name of the Lord that is mentioned here, except King Messiah, as it is said (Es. 30, 22.) Behold the Name of the Lord comes from afar. Furthermore, since the nations are said to be no longer going after the desire of their heart, the cessation and abdication of idolatry is indicated, from which the Israelites shall be converted to the true God, just as it was predicted in other parallel places Es. 11, 18. In that day the Lord alone shall be exalted, and the idols shall be utterly destroyed, Zach. 13, 2. And it shall be in that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will destroy the deities of the idols from the earth and they shall be remembered no more. Compare Es. 18, 7. 19, 19. 60, 1. seqq. Zach. 2, 11. Soph. 3. 9. Jerome explains these things thus: By no means shall the Lord sit upon the ark of the covenant and the Cherubim, to whom it was previously said by that people: Thou who sittest upon the Cherubim, manifest Thyself: but all perfectly believing shall be the throne of God. Or certainly it is better to understand the whole of the Church: when all nations are gathered in the name of the Lord in Jerusalem, in which is the vision of peace, and they by no means walk after the wickedness of their own evil heart: that they may do what they desire, nor do they follow their own errors, but say with the Prophet: My soul has followed after Thee: Thy right hand has upheld me. Eighthly, he predicts that in those days the house of Judah shall go to the house of Israel and both shall come together from the land of the North, to the land given to the Fathers. Which cannot be understood of a bodily return, because the ten tribes led away by Shalmaneser, as the Jews themselves admit, were never brought back to their fatherland: And therefore these things are to be understood spiritually, as in similar Prophetic places everywhere, concerning the conversion of many from the Israelites alike and the Jews, in the time of the New Testament, that they are to be gathered in the Spirit to the mystical Jerusalem together with any Gentiles whatsoever, to worship with one heart, and to serve Him with one shoulder. Concerning which the blessed Brentius: It seems indeed to speak of the return from the Babylonian captivity: but the following things testify that the Spirit looks further, to the liberation of Christ. Moreover, the land promised to the Fathers is not only that Canaan, but the heavenly fatherland, which all the Patriarchs sought, Hebr. 11. Our blessed Hulsemann agrees. What is said here and elsewhere concerning the singular frequency of the city of Jerusalem is not to be understood of the preeminence of the second Temple, as far as the worship of the Jews is concerned, for in this respect the second temple was much baser than the former, as is evident from Neh. 1, 9. But it is to be understood of the glory of the Church of the New Testament, which was to derive its origin from the earthly Jerusalem and itself to constitute a certain heavenly Jerusalem, which becomes the mother of all the faithful. Gal. 4, 26. Is. 2, 3. Joel 3, 7. Zech. 12, 6. Acts 2, 8. Jerome, on those words 'in those days the house of Judah shall go to the house of Israel,' has it thus: This is properly fulfilled in the coming of Christ, when from the twelve tribes together they believed in the Gospel, leaving the land of the North of the harshest cold, and departing from the empire of the devil: then they received the land of promise, which He had promised to their fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And to this point pertains the ninth [point], which is contained in verse 19. But I said, how shall I put thee among the children, and give thee a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the hosts of the nations? What other is that goodly heritage than the Church of the nations, called by the Apostles, which God gave to Christ for an inheritance, Ps. 2? Therefore it is called the goodly heritage of the hosts of the nations. What is that pleasant land, if not that in which God fixed the memory of His name, which is the seat of the Church? Who are put among the children, if not the faithful, who obtain εξουσίαν (authority), that they may become the sons of God, John 1, 12. Some understand the land of desire and the goodly heritage of the heavenly felicity of the other life, which the sons of God obtain. Which sense is not incongruous. But the exposition concerning the land of Canaan ought to be considered altogether foreign. For this was not made the heritage of the hosts of the nations, nor is it the land of desire of the sons of God. Tenthly, lest anyone should doubt that the discourse here is about spiritual grace, the confession of the faithful is added, who in the Spirit are to call upon God as Abba Father, and are to cleave to Him alone: 'And I said, Thou shalt call me, My father; and shalt not turn away from following me.' Which are τεκμήρια (proofs) of true believers. Which, when Grotius had well understood, he dared to corrupt the illustrious passage with a new στρεβλότητι (perversion) by placing 'I will place you among the children' as concerning the corporal multiplication of offspring, and 'that illustrious inheritance' as receiving it from the widest fields, as if the promises were merely earthly and corporal: and stuffing in the conjunction AND from his own, so that the text is perverted: 'I will give you an illustrious inheritance, that is, the widest fields, AND the armies of the nations' (instead of the armies of the nations) i.e., I will give you into siege, captivity, plunder: finally those things which exhibit a notable promise, And I said, You shall call me Father, he turns into a command, and makes legal things out of prophetic words, hypothetical out of absolute promises, and a condition of the superior promises: under this law I promise those things. Which forgery is not to be endured at all. Eleventh, we can oppose to Grotius the Jews themselves, who (1) acknowledge that these things look to the times of the Messiah, and (2) Part reject that gloss, concerning the ark being led into battle. Which Abarbenel, having recited it from R. Solomon, rejects thus: You, reader, see that all these things are ἀπροσδιόνυσα [irrelevant]. For the text has nothing at all about war, or about the rest, whence I cannot give assent to this exposition, although Jonathan also inclines toward it. But Abarbenel brings forward this interpretation. To say that the Prophet, at the time of the redemption and future gathering through the Messiah, there will be such holiness among the Israelites, that not only, while they are still few, one from a city, and two from a family, shall have been gathered, will they be just, pious, and upright, but also after they have been multiplied and have grown in the land: which otherwise is not wont to happen commonly, since with a growing people holiness for the most part decreases; so that at that time men will not be saying; The ark of the covenant of the Lord; namely, by placing holiness in the Ark, and the covenant of God contained in it, nay, they will not even be thinking or speaking about it, or making mention of it, namely in oaths to be taken before it; since they will have holiness in themselves, and will carry it about with them, and will offer pleasing incense to God everywhere, Malach. 1, 11. nor will they be visiting it any longer, to worship for public needs, and calamities of the Church; finally, they will not be making, i.e., mention of the covenant, which God once struck with them; nor will God be about to strike a new covenant with them; for the reason that all Jerusalem will be in that degree of holiness and glory in which the ark once was, so that not only the Israelites are to attribute that holiness to it, but all the nations. But Apella is mistaken, because he understands these things concerning the earthly glory of Jerusalem, and attributes to the people of Israel according to the flesh that holiness, which is to be taken concerning the Israelites according to the Spirit and the mystical Jerusalem. For external Jerusalem was never in a degree of holiness and glory in which the ark once was, nor did the nations attribute it to it. Nowhere is it predicted that this will happen in the Prophets, who rather threaten it with total destruction, and prophesy the conversion of the nations to the Church, the spiritual Zion. He is mistaken, while he wishes to refer these things concerning the ark only to the nations, because they will not be saying, the ark of the covenant of the Lord, because their degree will not ascend, so that it approaches the ark of God, or so that it looks into the place of the habitation of judgment; because no mention of the nations is made in that verse 16, but the Prophet deals with the Jews, whom he recalls to repentance by this promise made. Nor does that particle עוד [no longer] suit the nations; they will not say ANY LONGER; but did they boast of the ark of the Lord before? Whence it appears that these things are violently twisted toward the nations, concerning whom it is dealt with only later in verse 17. (3.) Nor do the Jews deny here and in parallel passages that the conversion of the nations is predicted. Even if they reject the coming of the Messiah, and the conversion of the nations, to the end of the world, and connect it with the resurrection of the dead, and dream of an earthly kingdom of the Messiah, who, with all their enemies cast down, is to effect universal peace in the world, is to restore the Jews to their former and greater glory, and thus is to reign for a thousand or however many years, and together with himself is to make the Jews the masters of the whole world and of all nations, and finally is to restore the Mosaic worship again. But all these things are diametrically opposed to this passage. Because here the coming of the Messiah is promised, not at the end of the world, but at the end of the days of the law and the temple or the ark of the covenant, and at that time the ark with all the worship pertaining to it is to cease, so that no one will even be about to make mention of it. Since therefore it will clearly not exist at the time of the Messiah, what is more manifest than that the ceremonial worship must have been clearly abrogated at that time, as that of which the ark was as it were the soul and center. Just as the Jews themselves also confess that with the Messiah all feasts are to be abrogated except Purim and the day of atonement, for this reason, because there will be no need for the multiplication of benefits, or the recounting of happiness at the time of the Messiah. Finally, as to the argument of Grotius from v. 20, it rests on a false interpretation, as if it were shown there why those promises did not have their force, namely because Israel on its part did not do what it ought. For those promises were not hypothetical concerning the calling of the nations, concerning the preservation of the remnants of Israel and the Jews, concerning the abrogation of the Levitical worship, but absolute. Nor was it the time there to show the outcome of those promises, as they were made concerning times not of Jeremiah or prior to the same, but concerning a future time, as the prophecy has it expressly. But that is what the Lord indicates here, that not even this promise concerning the restoration of the kingdom of Israel effects anything among the impenitent, as the blessed Hülsemann correctly observed the connection. See more concerning this passage in Buxtorf, loc. cit., and Dr. D. Müller, Refutation of Judaism, ch. 15, p. 463, and following. But because our B. Bugenhagius has treated this passage with special diligence, and better commentaries of this kind by our predecessors are now either not easily found or are rashly rejected, we shall repeat from there those things which serve here to overthrow the Jewish gloss and the depravation of GROTIUS. CONVERTIMINI. Here is promised, says B. Bugenh. p. 69, Christ, and the Gospel of the glory of the great God, a thing which the Jews will be forced to concede to us in this passage, whether they like it or not. For they cannot show us when one of them carried a city, and two an entire region and Kingdom to Mount Zion. Likewise, they see here that the Jewish worship, commanded in the law, is abolished, when it says that the ark of the Lord is to be abandoned and the place of the Ark, outside of which it was not permitted to sacrifice, Deut. 12, after Jerusalem shall have been revealed as the throne of the Lord, when there will not be there the ark and the mercy seat, the seat of God according to the promise Exod. 26, 1 Kings 8, and 9? Add, When have all nations been converted and gathered to the Lord in Jerusalem? Finally, let them see what the Prophet says about bringing back not only Judah, but also Israel, and that one kingdom is to be made of them again, just as there was one under David and Solomon. To the kingdom of Judah, a return was promised after seventy years, not to the kingdom of Israel, and the tribe of Judah with the tribe of Benjamin was brought back and restored to its seats and fields, as you read in Ezra. Although I shall speak elsewhere in this Prophet also about the return of Israel. Likewise, to those brought back, the inheritance of the nations is also promised here. I am silent now about the grace of God, which is described here, which neither the Jews nor any self-righteous persons can understand. Let the Jews show us all these things fulfilled in their earthly Kingdom after the captivity. And since they will not be able to show it, we show that these things were so fulfilled in Christ, that not even a jot of them has perished, as attested for us by other Prophets and places of Scripture. First he says, 'Return, O backsliding children,' in which pure grace is preached, so that we may not arrogate anything to our own merits. For he does not call the righteous, but sinners, Isaiah 43. 'I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.' Second: 'Because I will betroth you to me.' The wonderful grace of Christ our bridegroom is signified to us here in the image of marriage. Since we are one with him and through him we are accepted by the Father, he makes all our evils his own and takes them away from us, the Lamb of God who bears the sins of the world, and he communicates all his goods to us and makes them ours, when meanwhile he himself, as great as he is, is ours, and through him the Father himself is ours; read Eph. 5. 'Husbands, love,' etc. Hosea 2, these things are said thus: 'And I will betroth you to me forever; and I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in judgment and in loving-kindness and in mercies, and I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you shall know that I am the Lord.' He does not say, 'I will make a covenant with you, as with the fathers,' but 'I will betroth you to me.' There is no greater love on earth than between a bridegroom and a bride. These nuptials, as you hear, are the kingdom of faith, which the King makes for his son, as it is in the Gospel. Third he says: 'I will bring you,' so that one may lead with himself a whole city, and two a whole region or land. Or thus: 'And I will take you, one with a city, and two with a nation.' Interpreters in this place were afraid to translate it thus, judging it would be absurd. And they understood from many on all sides that a few were to be received, and a remnant to be saved, as Scripture promises elsewhere, when on the contrary it is said here that they are to be received and multiplied in the greatest number, so that one received by God may snatch with himself to God some one city and two some whole region or nation. This happened when the Gospel began to be spread. One brought many, that is, converts to Christ, and a few preachers many nations. Read the Acts of the Apostles and other histories. So also in Isaiah 49 it is said: 'Lift up round about,' etc. 'Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations and set up my standard to the peoples, and they shall bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders,' etc. Rev. last. 'The Spirit and the bride say, Come, and let him who hears say, Come.' Fourth he says, 'And I will bring you into Zion.' Below he says 'into Jerusalem,' the Church of Christ is called Zion and Jerusalem in the Scriptures. Because thither formerly the people of the Messiah were gathered to the word of God and sacrifices. And afterwards the Gospel, the Holy Spirit having been sent from heaven, began to be preached there, and the Church of Christ to be gathered, as you read in Acts 2, but it did not remain in that place alone. Since it grew, multiplied, and thence was dilated through the whole world, according to that of Isaiah 2 and Micah 4: 'Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.' Because 'out of Zion shall go forth the law and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem,' etc. And in the Psalm: 'The rod of your strength, or the scepter of your Kingdom, that is, the Gospel, the Lord will send forth out of Zion.' Therefore Zion and Jerusalem is the Church of Christians gathered from Jews and Gentiles in the unity not of place but of faith, to the Lordship and to his Christ, Psalm 2: 'But I have set my King upon Zion my holy mountain.' Because Christ came to sanctify the people, not the place, and it is added there concerning the dilation of the kingdom: 'Ask of me and I will give you the nations as my inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession.' This is what Paul says concerning the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of heaven or the Kingdom of Christ, whose citizenship is not on earth (Philip. 3), Gal. 4: 'The Jerusalem which is above, not that earthly one, is our mother,' read to the Hebrews 12: 'You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of Angels and to the assembly of the firstborn, who are written in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, and to Jesus the mediator of the new Testament and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than the blood of Abel.' Concerning this holy city and Kingdom of Christ the Prophets often speak, read Isa. 49, 52, 54, 55, 60, 61, 62, 65, 66. And in the Psalm which begins 'Its foundations,' the Philistines, Tyrians and Ethiopians, Egyptians and Babylonians, that is, the nations, are said to be born in Zion, just as Jeremiah says here, that all nations are to be gathered there. These certainly do not admit of Judaic expositions, but are fulfilled in the Church of Christ. Meanwhile, however, what he says must not be neglected: 'I will bring. I will introduce,' etc. So that we may not attribute anything to ourselves in this grace of Christ, etc. Fifth he says: 'And I will give you pastors according to my heart, who will feed you with doctrine and wisdom.' Whom he promises as preachers against Pseudo-Prophets and Pharisaical traditions, Ezech. 34: 'Behold, I myself will seek my sheep,' etc. It is an excellent and supreme gift of God when he gives good Doctors, preachers and Rectors. Whence Christ admonishes: 'Pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send laborers into his harvest,' who also 'ascending on high gave gifts to men, for he made some Apostles, some Evangelists, others Prophets, others pastors and Doctors for the edification of his body, which is the Church,' etc. Eph. 4. On the contrary, it is the supreme curse of God when the word is taken away, read Amos 8: 'And I will send you a famine, not of bread but of hearing the word,' etc. Sixth he says: 'When you have been multiplied and have grown in the land, in those days, says the Lord, they shall no longer speak of the Ark of the covenant of the Lord: It shall not come to mind, it shall not be preached of anymore. They shall not seek it, nor shall anything be made, that is, it shall not be sacrificed there. But in those days they shall call Jerusalem the Throne of the Lord. And all nations shall be gathered to it, because of the name of the Lord, which shall be in Jerusalem.' This is the manifest abolition and abrogation of the law and of the old observance commanded by God to the Jews. The Ark of the covenant of the Lord is nothing here, for which a place chosen by God was sought before and afterwards a Temple was built for it by Solomon. The sacrifices of the law, which were commanded to be performed in the place of the Ark of the Lord, are nothing here. In short; God is neither worshipped nor found any longer upon that mercy seat of the Ark. God is no longer here in all that worship of the old law. Since in that heavenly Jerusalem, that is, in the Church of Christ, there is another mercy seat and throne, which is Christ Jesus through his blood; there he is worshipped, there God is found. Rom. 3. Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation [mercy seat] &c. Heb. 4. Let us come to the throne of grace &c. 1 John 2. Who is the propitiation for sins &c. For now the righteousness of God is manifested through the Gospel without the law. Rom. 3. Righteousness is imputed to us, that is, sin is remitted to us and eternal life is freely given on account of Christ alone, whom we have present everywhere, so that there is no need to run to Jerusalem, Rome, etc., nor is there need for the Antichristian preaching of the Papists: Lo here, Lo there is Christ. Just as Simeon sang concerning the child Christ in Luke 2: I see thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples. A light &c. But what he adds, for the name of the Lord, which shall be in Jerusalem, alludes to this, that after the Temple was built it was said: The name of the Lord dwells in Jerusalem, and truly he was there, because his word was preached concerning God, sacrifice was offered to God according to the word of God, God was invoked, and God heard those invoking him there, according to his own promise in Exod. 29: I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel &c. But now there is another Jerusalem for us, in which we dwell, namely not earthly, but heavenly.

There alone is the name of the Lord, because there the Gospel is taught, God is invoked, the Sacraments of Christ are administered, and all things are done to the glory of God in Christ Jesus our Lord. Seventh, he says: When all nations shall have been gathered into Zion (when would this earthly Jerusalem contain them?) then they shall no longer walk after the thoughts of their wicked heart. The Jews had the written law and through it they could not be justified. The Gentiles do not have it and are justified, you see here. Therefore, righteousness is not from the law before God, but from the grace (as is said here) of betrothal, when we believe in the promise of grace in Christ. You see therefore that just as before the abolition of the law, so also now the abolition of sin even among the Gentiles without the law, who were the people of Satan, entirely without God and without Christ in this world, Eph. 2. According to another prophecy of Daniel 9. That transgression may be finished, and sin may receive an end, and iniquity may be blotted out, and everlasting righteousness may be brought in, etc. Nowhere in the scriptures is grace more expressed than when the Gentiles, who cannot even feign merit for themselves, are called and received into grace and incorporated into Christ. Eighth, he says: In those days the house of Judah shall go to the house of Israel, and they shall come together from the land of the North into the land which I gave as an inheritance to your fathers. This cannot be understood of the return from the Babylonian captivity, as was said above, when from Judah and Benjamin only the Jews were brought back into the land of Judah, not into the land of Israel, where the Samaritans and others held Samaria, having been substituted in the place of Israel by the Assyrian King; therefore these things are said of the spiritual return, by which men, cast off by God on account of sin and impiety, are brought back by faith to Christ, the Gospel having been published. Then also many from Israel, from every nation that is under heaven, were dwelling in Jerusalem on account of religion, Acts 2. But concerning the bodily return also of Israel or the ten tribes (which nevertheless have not been returned to their own fields) I shall speak more clearly elsewhere in this Prophet. But others from Israel remaining in their own places, dispersed among the nations of all the nations that are under heaven, afterwards received the Gospel. Which is the true return, of which it is spoken here, not a change of place but of infidelity. This is the true entry into the holy land promised and given to the fathers. Since indeed by faith they entered into the dwellings of God, of which it is often sung in the Psalms: And Abraham did not receive even a foot's length in the land of Canaan. Acts 7. That which Heb. 11 says thus: They look for a city having foundations: Let us go forth with Jesus outside the camp, bearing the reproach of the cross. For we do not have here a permanent city, but we seek the future one, as those fathers did of old. And again: According to faith all these died not having received the promise here, etc. Furthermore, many saints and Prophets once suffered all evils in their own land under the impious, of whom it is said in the same place: All these, having been approved by the testimony of faith, did not receive the promise, God providing something better for us, that they should not be made perfect without us. You easily see, therefore, that by land here is understood Jerusalem and Zion, in that way which we said above, which we seek not by a change of place. Since indeed it has been dilated through the whole world, nay, it is called a new world, as in Ps. 8. For I will see thy heavens, the works of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast founded, as it is in the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 2. For God did not subject to the Angels the world to come of which we speak. This kingdom of heaven on earth is wonderful. For it is not seen by the world. For it does not change place, face, clothing, food, age, owed works, holiness, languor, times, laws, customs, polities, magistrates, marriages, children, possessions, heaven, air, sun, day, night, etc., unless something be base and unworthy of an honest man, yet it makes new men, a new light, new affections, a contempt for earthly things, so that they possess what they have been given and entrusted by God, not otherwise than as God's gifts, not leaning on these transitory things, but only on the grace of the Father, in whose house or Kingdom they acknowledge themselves to dwell through faith. Concerning this conjunction of Judah and Israel, who once after the death of Solomon were perpetually destroying one another, and concerning the inheritance of the Gentiles coming to the Jews, inserted into Christ through faith (which was done through the Gospel, which came from the Jews to us Gentiles) it is thus also said in Is. 11. In that day the root of Jesse, that is, Christ, etc. And he will gather the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth (not only from the North) and the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away, that is, of the Kingdom of Israel, etc. And Hosea 3. For many days the children of Israel shall sit without a King, without a Prince, without a sacrifice, without an altar, without an Ephod, without the worship of God. After these things the children of Israel shall be converted and shall seek the Lord their God and David their King (that is, Christ who is to be born from the flesh of David) and they shall worship the Lord and his grace in the last of the days. And ch. 1. And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which is without measure, and shall not be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it was said to them: You are not my people, it shall be said to them: You are the children of the living God. And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together and shall appoint for themselves one head (that is, Christ) and shall go up from the land, because great is the day of Jezreel (that is, of the seed of God, or the people who are the seed of God). So also Ezekiel says ch. 34. I will raise up over them, and he himself shall be a shepherd to them, but I the Lord will be their God, and my servant David a prince in the midst of them, I the Lord have spoken, and I will make with them a covenant of peace and I will cause the most evil beasts to cease etc. Concerning this Kingdom of David, that is, of Christ, and concerning this reduction of the People, you will see below Jer. 23 and 31. Behold the days shall come, says the Lord, and I will strike a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, not according to the covenant which I struck with their fathers etc. Ninthly is added the promise of God (which, he says, I will multiply you etc.) concerning the multiplication of the people in the Church of the nations, and concerning the expansion of the Church through the whole world, Psalm 21. Christ says to the Father: I will declare your name to my brothers, in the midst of the Church I will praise you. From you is my praise in the great Church. The kingdom is the Lord's and he himself shall rule over the nations etc. Isa. 49. Lift up your eyes round about etc. Tenthly. And I promise, that then you shall call me Father and you shall not turn away from me. This cannot be done through the law and our studies or merits. John 1. Who not of bloods etc. These things the Blessed Predecessor, a faithful supporter of Luther, which illustrate this whole Prophecy excellently. Lastly we observe that Grotius himself from this passage Jer. 3, 16. proves that in the time of the Messiah sacrifices were to cease, annot. to book 5. de Verit. Relig. Christ. §. 8. p. 168.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SED QUOMODO SI CONTEMNAT MULIER AMATOREM SUUM, SIC CONTEMSIT ME DOMUS ISRAEL. ] Ostendit jam cur illa promissa vim suam non habuerant, quia nimirum Israel sua ex parte non fecit quod debuit.

Grotius hoc loco, morte consueto, testimo- nium insigne fidei Christianæ, quo Ecclesia adver- sus Judæos utitur, pessime pervertit. Quum enim hic agatur de abrogatione cultus Levitici & vocatio- ne gentium & prædicatione Evangelii sub N. Test. Grotius in plane contrarium sensum detorquet, more prorfus Judaico, quasi non de abrogatione cultus Levitici, nec de tempore Novi Test. sermo sit; sed de tranquillo statu politiæ Judaicæ. Ideo de- serta Christianæ Ecclesiæ sententia, cum cæcis Ju- dæis interpretatur, vel corrumpit potius illustrem locum: utpote cum R. Isaac Ben Abraham in Chi- suk Haënum, qui hanc recenset Rabbinicam glos- fam, nullum bellum, neq; ullam necessitatem fore, ut arca fœderis in prælium adducatur, quemadmodum olim factum. Et cum R. Menasse Ben Israel q. 7. in Levit. Quod dicitur arcæ non recordaturos, intelli- gendum, quod arcam non flagitabunt ad apparandum bellum, vel ad eam secum ducendam in prælium. Qui- bus præiverat R. David Kimchi, h. m. exponens : Etiamsi multiplicemini & fœcundi fiatis in terra, ta- men non invidebunt vobis gentes, ut veniant, & bel- lum vobis inferant, atq; sic necesse habeatis in bellum exire, & arcam Dei vobiscum ducere, prout moris il- lorum fuit, ut in bellum egredientes arcam secum de- ducerunt, in diebus enim illis ista re nihil erit opus. Nullum quippe amplius erit bellum. Hinc dicit : Non visitabunt eam, neq; fiet ultra, sc. res ista, ut educant arcam in bellum. Et R. Salomo: Non fiet amplius, id sc. quod olim factum est in Silio, quando eam tempore Eli eduxerunt in bellum cum Philistæis. E quibus manifestum est, ex asse hic judaizare Grotium. Fa- cile autem glossa illa Judaica profligatur, sensus- que Ecclesiæ Christianæ effulget, si hæc observen- tur. Primo, quod solemne sit Prophetis, cum ad conversionem exhortantur populum, & ab idolo- latria revocant, de temporibus Messiæ, quibus ces- satura est idololatria, & de beneficiis ejus, quibus soli fideles ac pœnitentes fruuntur, agere ac vatici- nari. Porro quum promittatur hic spiritualis de- sponsatio, convertimini filii revertentes (vel potius refractarii; ut B. Lutherus ex Ebræo reddidit, in quam sententiam etiam Grotius Vulgatam emen dat) dicit Dominus quia ego vir vester, quæ despon satio non respicit Politiam, vel statum politicum sed Ecclesiam, non beneficia corporalia, sed spiri tualia Hos. 2, 14. 1. Cor. 11, 2. De talibus ergo bene ficiis agit Propheta, quæ ad spiritualē desponsatio nem Domini pertinent, & fidelium ac converso rum propria sunt. Tertio cũ promittitur, & assum vos, unum de civitate & duos de cognatione, non d exigua multitudine in politia, urbe, aut vico assu menda, aut curanda agitur;sed de fidelibus, qui et parvum numerum è Judæis facturi in Ecclesia, no tamen nulli futuri sint,quod semen aliquod sibi ser- vaturus sit Dominus. Neque de reductione in Je- rusalem sermo est, quia revocati e Babylone non tam exiguo numero, sed multa millia: quo argu- mento utitur Cornelius a Lapide Prophetua aut po- tius Deus hic non loquitur de reditu Judæorum ex Ba- bylone sub Cyro, & Esdra,ut volunt Hebræi, Theo- doretus, Hugo & S. Thomas; tunc enim non unus aut duo,sed 42. millia redierunt.Si dicat quis, id tan- tum indicari, illos quidem in Patriam reducendos, sed non universalem fore illam reductionem, sed respectu eorum, qui sponte & ultro in Babylone mansuri erant,restrictam & paucam, cum dicitur: assumam unum ex urbe, & duos de familia: admitti sane id possit, citra detrimentum causæ Christiano- rum, quemadmodum exposuit Joh. Buxtorf. Hist. arc. fœder. c. 13. ut nempe Judæis hoc indulgeatur: at sine periculo & præjudicio sequentis vaticinii, adeoq; duæ constituantur partes hujus Prophetiæ: prima de eo, quod Deus isto tempore præstiturus erat v.14. 15. altera de eo,quod postmodum futurum sit, po- steaquam restituti, & in terra sua iterum radicati, & confirmati erant, tempore Messiæ v. 16. 17. 18. 19. tum quia Judæi has duas partes ipsimet agnoscunt,tum quia usitatissimum Prophetis est, ut subinde de li- berationis temporalibus agentes, maxime de ca- ptivitate Babylonica, ex abrupto quasi evolent, & ab illis transitum faciant ad spiritualem Messiæ libe- rationem. Sed quia Christiani Interpretes majori ex parte, ut fatetur Buxtorsius, hic volunt non a- gere Prophetam de illa reductione corporali, sed promissionem & vaticinium facere de quorundam ex Judæis assumptione, & inRegnum Christi atque ad ejus Ecclesiam, quam per Zionem intelligunt, adductione, & de illis dicere, unum ex urbe, duos e familia, & quod pauci omnino respectu reliquo- rum ab initio Evangelii convertendi essent, & quod v.15. dicitur de pastoribus, quos Dominus secundum cor suum daturus erat, scientia & intelligentia pa- scentibus, interpretantur de Apostolis vera Christi scientia, & cognitione homines instruentibus, ut sequentibus verbis porro describatur, qualis futu- rus sit Ecclesiæ status, posteaquam illa per vocatio- nem & accessionem etiam gentium ad eam fuerit aucta, & multiplicata: causam nullam videmus,cur ab hac passiva Christianorum Rabbinorum inter- pretatione discedendum sit. Etsi enim nulla discre- tionis, vel transitionis ad novam Prophetiam nota hæc cum præcedentibus cohæreant, non novum tamen est, cum ad conversionem & pœnitentiam excitatur populus, argumenta a beneficiis Messiæ adferri: & cohærent hæc apprime: Converti debere refractarios e populo, siquidem Deus huic populo ea exhibiturus sit gratiam, ut ipsum sibi desponsa- turus,ejus curam tanquam maritus habiturus, & e reliquiis hujus populi per Apostolos sibi Ecclesiam catholicam extructurus sit. Ita Hieronymus: Con- vertimini ad me &c. Judæi impletum hoc putant post reversionem ex Babylone sub Cyro rege Persarum, & Zorobabel filio Salathiel, etiamsi non omnes reversi sunt: hoc significari, assumam unum de civitate & duos de cognatione. Sed melius in adventu Christi, quum reliquiæ salvæ factæ sunt, dicente & exponente Apostolo: Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma essemus & similes Gomorrhæ fuissemus. Tunc introducti in Sion, de qua scri- ptum est: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei. Quid quod e Judæis ipsis nonnulli hæc ad Messiæ tempora referant, non μυστικῶς solum, ut Grotius mentem eorum pervertit,sed ita,ut hunc literalem sensum esse adferant. Nam ita in Cod. Sanhedrin distinct. Chelek exponitur de Messiæ tempore.

Dixit Rab. impleti sunt omnes termini atque universi (adventus Christi). Traditio est, quod R. Eliezer di- terunt regenti pœnitentiam, erunt redemti, fi- cut dictum est Jer. 3, 14. Revertimini filii rebelles, & curabo perversiones vestras. Dixit R. Josua. Et nonne dictum est (Jer. 3, 14.) Et assumam vos unum de civitate & duos de cognitione. Quarto Pastores, qui hic promittuntur, non sunt Principes, uti cum Judæis vult Grotius, sed quorum officium est pascere populum scientia & doctrina, quod præconum verbi & Doctorum est, non Principum. Non enim tantum perite & sapienter pasturi dicun- tur, ut modus indicetur, sed pasturi scientia & do- ctrina, ut designetur objectum, circa quod occu- pandi sint isti pastores, & proprium eorum munus definiatur, quot situm est in communicatione scientiæ & doctrinæ, imprimis quia fructus hu- jus pasturæ & informationis exprimitur, nominis divini agnitio, & ambulatio non secundum deside- ria cordis, sed secundum voluntatem Domini, & pasturæ illi respondet, quod ita informati doctrina & cognitione Domino Deo non servituri sint, jux- ta morem cultus Levitici, sed ipsum in Spiritu & veritate ceu patrem agnituri, & veneraturi v. 16. 19. Hieronymus in h. l. Et dati sunt Pastores juxta cor ejus, Apostoli & apostolici viri, & paverunt creden- tium multitudinem: non in Judaicis ceremoniis, sed scientia Christi atq; doctrina: Et in toto orbe prædica- tione Evangelii seminata, nequaquam in arca Domi- ni, quæ custos fuit legis Mosaïcæ, habebunt fiduciam, sed ipsi erunt templum Dei: Nec juxta errantes Na- zaræos, abolitis sacrificiis inservient, sed spiritualem cultum sectabuntur. Quinto de bello hic nullo verbo mentio facta, nec quicquam in textu est, quod illum sensum indicet, non pugnatum amplius iri, nec locu fore iis, quæ in bello fieri solent. Glossa illa in tex- tum introducitur, non è verbis textus depromitur. Temere itaque illa, NEC VISITABITUR, NEC ERIT ULTRA, ita redduntur, id est, non pugna- bitur. Visitare usurpatur quidem nonnunquam sen- su judicandi, sed cum de visitatione Dei activa, quæ vel judicii, vel beneficii est, iræ vel gratiæ agitur, non cum de visitatione hominum; & inepta & contorta est interpretatio, NON VISITABITUR amplius arca, id est, non pugnabitur amplius. Nam visitari ab Israëlitis consuevit arca cultus gratia. Ideoque pro- prie verbum visitandi accipiendum est. Si impro- prie visitare pro ἐκδικεῖν vel pugnare hic accipias, quis sensus erit, non visitabunt amplius Israëlitae ar- cam, id est, non judicabunt vel pugnabunt amplius arcam. Alia ratio est τὸ χαριεντισμᾶ 2. Reg. 14. sc. cum conflictus & pugna exprimitur per mutuam lustrationem vel visionem. Exercitus enim dicun- tur se videre mutuo, cum congrediuntur mutui con- flictus causa. At quid hoc ad visitationem arcæ? Sexto de usu arcæ fœderis proprio, & ordinario ser- mo est, quod is cessaturus sit: Quia id verba im- portant: Non dicent ultra: arca testamenti Domi- ni: Nam simpliciter negatur arcam Domini por- tatum iri, ac memoriam illius amplius remansu- ram. Quo facit ille phrasium cumulus, empha- seos causa adhibitus: Non dicent ultra arca testa- menti Domini, neq; ascendent super eos, neq; recorda- buntur illius, nec visitabitur, nec erit ultra. Recte Buxtorfius l. c. Non frustra & otiose Propheta hanc de una & eadem re, phrasium varietatem & condu- plicationem adhibuit, sed singulare aliquid & maxi- me memorabile procul dubio notare voluit. Quod & Abarbenel animadvertit: Quid, inquit, opus fuit ista ingeminatione, utinam id sciam & intelligam! Non dicit ultra sine expresso Nominativo, quinam sint illi, qui non ultra ita sint dicturi? Sed quia Israe- lit& clamarunt subinde, templum Domini, templum Domini, templum Domini Jer. 7, 4. sine dubio illi intelliguntur, quod non amplius gloriaturi sint de ar- ca, vel templo materiali. Adde, quod ita notetur, nunquam deinceps arcam Domini portatum iri. Non dicent, vel NON DICETUR amplius. Vi- de similia Jer. 16, 15. 16. c. 23, 7. 8. c. 31, 29. Alia er- go ratio erit cultus divini sub Nov. Test. ubi non amplius ad arcam Domini provocabitur, non am- plius cultus ad arcam Domini celebrabitur, non amplius illa portabitur. Quem sensum cætera etiam postulant. NEQUE ASCENDET SUPER COR, hoc est, nemo de ea cogitabit. Hoc enim est ascendere super cor 2. Reg. 12. 12, 5. Jer. 7, 31. c. 32, 33. Ez. 38, 10. NEQUE RECORDABUNTUR EJUS, Non cogitabunt de ea, neq́, mentionem ejus- dem facient. NEQUE VISITABUNT EAM, vel ut alii reddunt: Non requirent, non desiderabunt eam. Quia antea visitabatur & requirebatur cultus gratia. Id ergo cessaturum prædicitur. NON FIET AMPLIUS id. Alii ita explicant: Non fiet amplius arca: Alii hoc modo: non fiet amplius, ut sc. ad eam orent, sacrificent, cultum sacrum peragant, horum nihil ulterius ei fiet. B. Lutherus reddidit: Noch daselbst mehr opffern: quia vox עשה de sacrificiis usurpatur Ex. 10, 25. Jud. 13, 5. 1. Reg. 18, 28. Et sacrificia cessatura erant tempore Nov. Test. Dan. 9, 27. Putat ergo indicati hoc oraculo, quod neq; cultus ad arcam fœderis neque sacrificia am- plius locum habitura sint. De arcæ deductione ad prælium nullus apex habetur. Neque arcæ hic usus erat, nisi extraordinarius & singularis, quæ nunquã legitur adhibita in prælio, jussu divino, nisi quod in circuitu Hiericho portata fueritante castra Israe- lis Jos. 6. Quod enim in bello adversus Philistinos adhibita 1. Sam. 4. factum est contra mandatum Dei, unde arca ipsa fœderis capta fuit. Non ergo ordinata fuit arca ad id, ut in prælio educeretur, quemadmodum Grotius cum Judæis fingit: sed usus ejus proprius & perpetuus erat ad cultum Dei adstrictus Ex. 25, 10. unde orabant ad arcam Do- mini Jos. 7, 6. & Deus ex illa manifestabat se Ex. 25. Et quamvis primis temporibus, antequam cer- tum locum quietum nancisceretur, circumducta fuerit, nunquam tamen id tempore templi factum, nec fieri potuit. De quo audiendus Abarbenel ad Jer. 3. (apud Buxtorf. c. l. p. 208.) Tempore templi primi, quo Israel sequebatur libidinem cordis sui, omnis ipsorum sanctitas consistebat in Domo San- ctuarii & in Arca DEI, quæ ibi erat: Idque partim propterea, quod per Arcæ præsentiam custodiebantur, & certi erant de gratiosa Dei providentia, siquidem justi essent &c. partim quod per arcam, quæ Tabu- las fœderis continebat, retraherentur à peccato, & invitarentur ad remissionem peccatorum à Deo pe- tendam; partim quod ad eam juramenta fieri sole- rent; & deniq;, quod coram ea orarent, si cœlum oc- clusum esset, & pluvia non descenderet, vel pestis, bel- lum, vel aliæ calamitates publicæ ingruerent. Ideo recte B. Brentius in h. l. In Ecclesia non est externa illa arca Testamenti, quæ Exod. 25. à Mose fabricata est, in qua erat Manna, virga Aaronis & Tabulæ Testamenti. Heb. 9. Veniente autem Christo, hæc um- bratilia cessarunt, & veritas in locum eorum succes- sit. Est enim Christus arca fœderis. In qua est Man- na, ipse namq; panis vivus est. Et virga Aaronis, qua mors & peccatum propellitur. Et tabulæ Testamenti, id est, Decalogus. Non enim venit solvere legem, sed implere. Ecclesia solium Domini est, Ps. 131. Hæc re- quies mea inquit, hic habitabo, quoniam elegi eã. Septimo oppositio docet, non de bello, sed de abro- gatione cultus Levitici sermonem esse: Quia Israe- litarum conventui ad arcam, vel visitationi arcæ opponitur gentium congregatio ad Ecclesiam, tol- litur discrimen Judæorum & gentium, quod in Vet. Test. erat. Quia Hierusalem vocabitur solium Do- mini, id est, agnoscetur ab omnibus sedes gloriosa, in qua Deus residet, ac præsentiam, gloriam & ma- jestatem suam manifestat, ad quam congregabuntur omnes gentes, ad nomen Domini Hierosolymam; quo nomine intelligi nequit Hierosolyma terrena; ea enim tantæ capacitatis non erat, ut omnes gentes capere potuerit; ad quas ne Judæa quidem univer- sa sufficiebat. Ideoque Hierosolyma mystica de- signatur, quæ est omnium nostrorum credentium mater Gal. 4, 26. Quapropter cum arca fœderis fuerit sedes & solium gloriæ Domini, ac loco ejus tota Hierosolyma ipsius solium futura dicatur: in- nuitur, non adstrictam amplius fore gloriam Do- mini ad unum locum, ut olim, ubi intra arcam inter Cherubinos sedebat, sed latius extensum iri, imo ampliandam per omnes gentes, ut ubique adoretur Pater in Spiritu & veritate Joh. 4, 21. & in omni lo- co sanctæ attollantur manus 1. Tim. 2, 8. atque in omni loco suffimentum offeratur nomini Domini Mal. 1, 11. Nonnulli de urbe Hierosolyma accipiunt, & hunc sensum reddunt: In diebus illis non erit am- plius Hierosolyma celebrata ab eo, quod Deus illic in templo, & in eo in arcâ inter Cherubinos resideat, & thronum suum habeat; sed quod Dominus ipse non in nube & igne, sed in carne manifestatus illis sit appari- turus, neq; per vocem ex arca propitiatoria egressam & soli Mosi loquentem, sed publice in urbe, in templo, in compitis viarum, in campis &c. docturus & Evan- gelium suum prædicaturus, & inde per Apostolos suos illud in orbe universum propagaturus. Tunc enim e Zion exibit Lex & verbum Domini de Jerusalem Es. 2, 3. sicut olim verbum Domini ad Mosen ex ar- ca est egressum. Tunc veniet ad templum suum Do- minus ille, quem in Vet. Test. quæsiverunt Mal. 3, 3. Tunc impletum fuit, quod apud Zachariam promi- sit c. 3, 3. Revertor ad Zionem & habitabo in medio Hierosolymæ, & vocabitur Hierosolyma urbs verita- tis, (non umbrarum & typorum) & mons Domini exercituum mons ille sanctitatis, ut loco laudato ha- bet Buxtorfius.

Septimo de externo honore, vel splendore Hie- rosolymæ hæc intelligi nequeunt, siquidem ea post solutam captivitatem Babylonicam in tanta gloria & reverentia non fuerit, sed fere semper sub- jecta servituti, primum Persarũ, tum Græcorum, de- niq; Romanorum. Neq; ad congregationem genti- um in subdiale gentium hæc trahi possunt. Nam hic de confluxu non exiguo, aut particulari sermo est, sed CONGREGABUNTUR, inquit Pro- pheta, AD EAM OMNES GENTES. Quæ de vocatione & conversione gentium adEcclesiam loqui, nimis manifestum est: Et addit Propheta il- los congregatum iri AD NOMEN DOMINI, quod ad illud colendum & invocandum se ab idolis suis conversuri sint. Potest etiam per nomen Do- mini Messias intelligi, uti in Bereschith Rabba lo- cus parallelus Zeph. 3, 9. Quia tunc vertam ad po- pulos labium electum ad invocandum omnes nomen Domini, & ad colendũ eum humero uno, explicatur: Non est nomen Domini, cujus hic sit mentio, nisi Rex Messias, sicut dicitur (Es. 30, 22.) Ecce Nomen Do- mini venit à longinquo. Porrò cum dicantur gentes non ituræ amplius post lubitum cordis sui, cessatio & abdicatio idololatrias indicatur, à qua converten- tur ad verum Deum Israëlitz, quemadmodum in aliis locis parallelis prædictum Es. 11,18. In die illa e- levabitur solus Dominus, & idola conterentur peni- tus, Zach. 13, 2. Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus exer- cituum, disperdam numina idolorum a terra & non memorabuntur ultra. Confer. Es. 18, 7. 19, 19. 60, 1. seqq. Zach. 2, 11. Soph. 3. 9. Hieronymus haec ita ex- plicat: Nequaquam Dominus sedebit super arcam te- stamenti & Cherubim, cui prius ab illo populo dice- batur: Qui sedes super Cherubin manifestare: sed o- mnes perfectamente credentes erunt thronus Dei. Vel certe melius totum de Ecclesia intelligendum: quando congregantur omnes gentes in nomine Domini in Hie- rusafem, in qua est visio pacis, & nequaquam ambu- lant post pravitatem cordis sui pessimi: ut faciant quae desiderant, nec suos sequuntur errores, sed dicunt cum Propheta: Adhaesit anima mea post te: me suscepit dextera tua. Octavo praedicit in diebus illis domum Juda ituram ad domum Israel & utrasque simul ven- turas de terra Aquilonis, ad terram Patribus datam. Quae non possunt intelligi de corporali reditu, quia tribus decem a Salmanassare abductae, fatentibus ipfismet Judaeis, nunquam in patriam reductae sunt: Ideoque spiritualiter, ut in similibus locis Prophe- ticis passim haec intelligenda, de conversione multo- rum ex Israelitis pariter & Judaeis, tempore N. T. quod in Spiritu congregandi sint ad mysticam Hie- rosolymam una cum gentibus quibusvis uno corde adoraturi, eique uno humero servituri. Quo de B. Brentius: Videtur quidem loqui de reditu e capti- vitate Babylonica: sed Spiritum longius respicere, in liberationem Christi, sequentia testantur. Ter- ra autem Patribus promissa non solum illa Chana- an est, sed patria coelestis, quam omnes Patriarchae inquifiverunt, Hebr. 11. Consonat B. Hulsemannus noster. Quae hic & alibi de singulari frequentia urbis Hierosolymorum dicuntur, non sunt intelli- genda de praeeminentia Templi secundi, quod ad cultum Judaeorum attinet, nam hoc respectu tem- plum secundum multo vilius fuit priori, ut patet ex Neh. 1, 9. Sed de gloria Ecclesiae N. T. quae origi- nem ductura erat ex terrena Hierosolyma & ipsa constitutura coelestem quandam Hierosolymam, quae omnium fidelium mater fit. Gal. 4, 26. Es. 2, 3. Joel. 3, 7. Zach. 12, 6. Act. 2, 8. Hieronymus ad verba illa in diebus illis ibit domus Juda ad domum Israelis, ita habet: Hoc proprie in Christi completur adventu, quando de duodecim simul tribubus Evangelio credi- derunt, relinquentes terram Aquilonis durissimi fri- goris, & a diaboli imperio recedentes: tunc receperunt terram repromissionis, quam pollicitus fuerat Patri- bus eorum Abraham, Isaac & Jacob. Atque huc fa- ciunt Nono, quae habentur v. 19. Ego autem dixi, quomodo ponam te in filios & tribuam tibi terram desiderabilem haereditatem praeclaram exercituu gentium. Haereditas illa praeclara quaenam alia, quam gentium Ecclesia, vocata per Apostolos, quam dedit Deus Christo in haereditatem Ps. 2. Ideo dicitur hereditas praeclara exercituum gen- tium. Quae illa terra desiderabilis, nisi ea, in qua Deus nominis sui memoriam fixit, quae sedes est Eccle- siae? Quinam ponuntur in filios, nisi fideles, qui con- sequuntur εξουσίαν, ut fiant filii Dei Joh. 1, 12. Non- nulli terram desiderii & haereditatem praeclaram in- telligunt de felicitate coelesti alterius vitae, quam consequuntur filii Dei. Qui sensus non incongruus est. At expositio de terra Canaan aliena prorsus censeri debet. Haec enim non facta est haereditas exercituum gentium, nec est terra desiderii filio- rum Dei. Decimo ne quis ambigat, de gratia spiri- tuali sermonem hic esse, additur confessio fidelium, qui in Spiritu Deum invocaturi sint Abba Pater, & ei soli adhaesuri: Et dixi, Patrem vocabis me, & post me ingredi non cessabis. Quae sunt τεκμήρια vere cre- dentium. Quod cum probe intellexerit Grotius, nova στρεβλότητι locu illustrem corrumpere ausus est: illa ponam te in filios, de corporali sobolis mul- tiplicatione: illa hæreditatem præclaram, de arvis latissimis accipiens, quasi mere terrena & corpo- ralia promissa sint: Et de suo infarciens copulam ET, ut ita pervertatur textus: Tribuam tibi hære- ditatem præclaram, id est, arva latissima, ET exer- citus gentium (pro exercituum gentium) sc. tibi da- bo in obsidionem, captivitatem, prædam: deni- que illa, quæ promissionem insignem exhibent, Et dixi, Patrem vocabis me, in mandatum conver- tit, & è verbis propheticis legalia facit, è promissis absolutis hypothetica, ac conditionem superiorum promissorum: sub hac lege ista promitto. Quæ νοθεία est minime ferenda. Undecimo opponere possumus Grotio ipsos Judæos, qui (1) agnoscunt hæc ad tem- pora Messiæ spectare, ac (2) Pars reprobant glossam istam, de arca in prælium deducenda. Quam è R. Sa- lomone recitatam Abarbenel ita rejicit: Tu lector, vides, hæc omnia esse ἀπροσδιόνυσα. Nihil quic- quam enim habet textus vel de bello, vel de cæte- ris, unde non possum assensum præbere huic expositioni, quamvis Jonathan etiam ad eam inclinet. Affert au- tem Abarbenel hanc ἔκθεσιν. Dicere Prophetam tem- pore redemtionis & collectionis futuræ per Messiam, tantam fore inter Israelitas Sanctitatem, ut non tan- tum, dum pauci adhuc, unus è civitate, & duo ex fa- milia, congregati erunt, justi, pii & probi sint futu- ri, sed etiam posteaquam multiplicati fuerint & cre- verint in terra: quod alias communiter fieri non so- leat, cum crescente populo Sanctitas plerumque decre- scat;, adeo ut eo tempore homines non dicturi sint; Ar- ca fœderis Domini; Sanctitatem scilicet in Arca, & fœdere Dei in ea comprehenso, collocando, imo ne quidem de ea cogitaturi aut locuturi, vel ejus mentio- nem facturi sint, scilicet in juramentis præstandis coram ea; cum sanctitatem in se ipsis sint habituri, & secum circumlaturi, atque ubique Deo incensum gra- tum oblaturi, Malach. 1, 11. non etiam eam amplius visitaturi, ad adorandum pro publicis necessitati- bus, & calamitatibus Ecclesiæ; non denique facturi, sc. mentionem fœderis, quod olim Deus cum illis pepigit; neque Deus novum fœdus cum illis pa- cturus sit; eo quod universa Hierosolyma in eo gradu sanctitatis & gloriæ sit futura, quo olim fuit arca, ita ut non tantum Israelitæ eam sanctitatem illi sunt dela- turi, sed universæ gentes. Sed fallitur Apella, quod de terrena Hierosolymæ gloria intelligat hæc, & po- pulo Israelis secundum carnem istam sanctitatem tribuat, quæ de Israelitis secundum Spiritum & my- stica Hierosolyma accipienda sunt. Nunquam e- nim Hierosolyma externa in gradu sanctitatis & gloriæ fuit, quo olim arca, nec gentes ei illam detu- lerunt. Nusquam id futurum in Prophetis prædici- tur, qui πανωλεθρίαν ipsi potius minantur, & gen- tium ad Ecclesiam, Sionem spiritualem, conversio- nem vaticinantur. Fallitur, dum ad gentes tantum hæc de arca referre vult, quod illæ dicturæ non sint, arca fœderis Domini, quia gradus eorum non ascendet, ut accedat ad arcam Dei, aut ut inspiciat in locum habitaculi ali judicii; quia nulla in illo qui- dem vers. 16. gentium mentio facta, sed agit Pro- pheta de Judæis, quos ad pœnitentiam hac facta promissione revocat. Neque gentibus convenit il- la particula עוד non dicent AMPLIUS; Num au- tem illæ antea de arca Domini gloriatæ sunt? Un- de apparet violenter hæc ad gentes torqueri, de quibus postea demum agitur vers. 17. (3.) Neque negant Judæi hic & in parallelis locis conversionem gentium prædici. Etsi adventum Messiæ, & conver- sionem gentium in finem mundi rejiciant, & cum resurrectione mortuorum connectant, ac regnum Messiæ terrenum somnient, qui dejectis omnibus hostibus ipsorum pacem universalem in orbe effe- cturus, Judæos in pristinam, & majorem gloriam restituturus, & sic per mille vel quotquot annos re- gnaturus, & una secum Judæos universi orbis & o- mnium gentium dominos facturus, denique denuo cultum Mosaicum instauraturus sit. Quæ vero o- mnia huic loco καθδιάμετρον repugnant. Quia hic adventus Messiæ promittitur, non in fine mundi, sed in fine dierum legis & templi vel arcæ fœderis, eo- que tempore arca cum universo cultu ad eam spe- ctante cessatura sit, ut ne mentionem quidem de ea quisquam facturus sit. Quum ergo ea plane extitu- ra non sit tempore Messiæ, quid manifestius, quam quod cultus ceremonialis plane abrogari debuerit illo tempore, utpote cujus anima quasi, & centrum arca erat. Quemadmodum etiam ipsimet Judæi fatentur cum Messia abroganda festa omnia exce- pto Purim & expiationis, hac de causa, quia opus non erit multiplicatione beneficiorum, aut recen- sione felicitatis tempore Messiæ. Postremo quod ad Argumentum Gortii e v. 20. nititur id ψευδερ- μηνείᾳ, quasi ibi ostendatur, cur illa promissa vim suam non habuerint, quia sc. Israel ex parte sua non fecit, quod debuit. Nam promissa illa non fuere hypothetica de vocatione gentium, de conservatione reliquiarum Israelis & Judæorum, de abrogatione cultus Levitici, sed absolutæ. Neque ibi erat tem- pus ostendere promissorum istorum ἔκβασιν, ut- pote quæ facta sunt de temporibus non Jeremiæ aut eodem prioribus, sed de tempore futuro, ut διαῤῥήδην habet vaticinium. Id autem est, quod hic indicat Dominus, quod ne quidem hæc promissio de instauratione regni Israelis apud impœnitentes quicquam efficiat, uti συνέχειαν recte observavit B. Hülsemannus. Plura de hoc loco vide apud Bux- torff. l. c. & Dn. D. Müllerum Judaismo refut. c. 15. p. 463. & seqq. Quia vero hunc locum diligenter imprimis tractavit B. Bugenhagius noster, & com- mentarii ejusmodi meliores antecessorum nostro- rum nunc aut non reperiuntur facile, aut temere rejiciuntur, repetemus inde ea, quæ huc faciunt ad profligandam Judaicam glossam & depravationem GROTII. CONVERTIMINI. Hic promittitur, in- quit B. Bugenh. p. 69. Christus, & Evangelium glo- riæ magni Dei, id quod cogentur nobis permittere hoc loco Judæi, velint, nolint. Nam non possunt ostendere nobis, quando unus ex ipsis portarit civi- tatem, & duo totam aliquam regionem & Regnum ad montem Zion. Item vident hic Judaicum cultum, in lege mandatum aboleri, quando dicit arcam Domi- ni relinquendam & locum Arcæ, extra quem no lice- bat sacrificare, Deut. 12. postquam revelatum erit Jerusalem solium Domini, quando non erit ibi ar- ca & propitiatorium sedes Dei secundum promis- sionem Exod. 26. 1. Reg. 8, & 9? Adde, Quando omnes gentes ad Dominum conversæ, congregatæ sunt in Jerusalem? Denique videant, quid Propheta di- cat de reducendo, non solum Juda, sed etiam Israe- le, & quod unum regnum ex eis rursum futurum sit, sicut unum fuit sub Davide & Salomone. Regno Ju- da promissa erat reductio post septuaginta annos, non regno Israelis, & tribus Juda cum tribu Benja- min reducta est, & reddita suis sedibus & agris, ut legis in Esdra. Quanquam & de reductione Israelis alias dicam in hoc Propheta. Item reductis etiam hic promittitur hæreditas gentium. Taceo nunc de gratia Dei, quæ hic describitur, quam neque Judæi, neque ulli justitiarii intelligere possunt. Ostendant nobis Judæi hæc omnia in suo terreno Regno post captivitatem completa. Et cum non potuerint o- stendere, nos ostendimus in Christo hæc ita com- pleta, ut ne jota quidem ex his perierit, attestanti- bus nobis & aliis Prophetis & Scripturæ locis. Pri- mum dicit, convertimini filii desertores, in quo me- ra gratia prædicatur, ne quid meritis nostris arro- gemus. Non enim vocat justos, sed peccatores, E- saiæ 43. Ego sum, Ego sum ipse, qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter Me, & peccatorum tuorum non recorda- bor. Secundo: Quia ego desponsabo vos mihi. Mira- bilis gratia Christi sponsi nostri nobis hic signifi- catur in imagine conjugii. Siquidem unum sumus cum eo & per eum accepti sumus Patri, omnia ma- la nostra facit sua aufertque ea à nobis Agnus Dei qui portat peccata mundi, & omnia sua bona com- municat nobis & nostra esse facit, quando interim ipse quantus quantus est noster est, & per eum ipse pater est noster; lege Eph. 5. Viri diligite &c. Os. 2. hæc ita dicuntur: Et sponsabo te mihi in æternum & sponsabo te in justitia & in judicio & in misericordia & miserationibus, & sponsabo te mihi in fide, & scies, quod ego sum Dominus. Non dicit, Paciscar tecum, ut cum patribus, sed sponsabo te mihi. Non est major amor in terris quam inter sponsum & sponsam. Hæ nuptiæ, ut audis, sunt regnum fidei, quas Rex facit filio, prout est in Evangelio. Tertio dicit: Addu- cam vos, ut unus secum ducat totam civitatem, & duo totam regionem vel terram. Vel sic: Et assumam vos, unum cum civitate, & duos cum natione. Interpretes hoc loco metuebant ita transferre, absurdum fore judicantes. Et intellexerunt ex multis undiq; pau- cos suscipiendos, & reliquias salvandas, ut alibi scri- ptura promittit, cum contra hic dicatur, eos maxi- mo numero suscipiendos & multiplicandos, ita ut unus susceptus à Deo rapiat secum ad Deum unam aliquam civitatem & duo totam aliquam regionem vel nationem. Hoc factum est, ubi cœpit invulgari Evangelium. Unus multos adduxit, id est, conver- tit ad Christum, & pauci prædicatores multas na- tiones. Lege Acta Apostolorum & alias historias. Ita & Esaiæ 49. dicitur: Leva in circuitu &c. Ecce levabo ad gentes manum meam & ad populos exalta- bo signum meum, & adferent filios tuos in ulnis, & filias tuas super humeros portabunt &c. Apoc. ult. Spiritus & sponsa dicunt, veni & qui audierit, dicit, veni. Quarto dicit & introducam vos in Zion. In- fra dicit in Jerusalem, Ecclesia Christi in scripturis Zion & Jerusalem appellatur. Quia illuc olim po- pulus Messiæ congregabatur ad verbum Dei & sa- crificia. Et postea Evangelium, misso è cœlis Spi- ritu Sancto, ibi cœpit prædicari, & Ecclesia Chri- sti congregari, ut legis Act. 2. sed non in eo loco solo permansit. Siquidem crevit multiplicata & in- de dilatata est per totum mundum, secundum illud Esaiæ 2. & Micheæ 4. Venite ascendamus ad mon- tem Domini & ad domum Dei Jacob, & docebit nos vias suas, & ambulabimus in semitis ejus. Quia de Zion exibit lex & verbum Domini de Jerusalem &c. Et in Psalm. Virgam virtutis tuæ, sive sceptrum Re- gni tui, id est, Evangelium, emittet Dominus ex Zion. Ideo Zion & Jerusalem Ecclesia Christiano- rum est ex Judæis & gentibus congregata in unita- te non loci sed fidei, ad Dominium & ad Christum ejus Psalm. 2. Ego autem constitui Regem meum su- per Zionem montem sanctum meum. Quia Christus venit sanctificaturus populum non locum, & addi- tur ibi de dilatatione regni; Postula à me & dabo ti- bi gentes hæreditatem meam & possessionem terminos terræ. Hoc est quod de superna Jerusalem, id est, Re- gno cœlorum sive Regno Christi, cujus conversa- tio non est in terris (Philip. 3.) dicit Paulus, Gal. 4. Jerusalem quæ sursum est, non illa terrena, est mater nostra, lege ad Hebr. 12. Accessistis ad montem Zion & ad civitatem Dei viventis Jerusalem cælestem & ad innumerabilium Angelorum cœtum & ad concio- nem primogenitorum, qui conscripti sunt in cælo, & ad judicem universorum Deum, & ad Spiritus justo- rum perfectorum, & ad novi Testamenti meditatorem Jesum & ad sanguinem aspersionis meliora loquen- tem, quam loquebatur sanguis Abel. De hac sancta civitate & Regno Christi sæpe dicunt Prophetæ, le- ge Esa. 49. 52. 54. 55. 60. 61. 62. 65. 66. Et in Psalm. qui incipit Fundamenta ejus, dicuntur Philistæi, Tyrii & Æthiopes, Ægyptii & Babylonii, id est, gen- tes nasci in Zion, quemadmodum hic Jeremias di- cit, eo congregandas omnes gentes. Hæc certe Judai- cas expositiones non admittunt, sed in Christi Ec- clesia complentur. Interim vero non negligendum est quod dicit: Ego adducam. Ego introducam &c. Nequid in hac Christi gratia nobis tribuamus &c. Quinto dicit: Et dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, qui pascant vos doctrina & sapientia. Quos prædicatores promittit contra Pseudo-Prophetas & Pharisaicas traditiones, Ezech. 34. Ecce Ego ipse requiram oves meas &c. Egregium & summum do- num Dei est, quando dat bonos Doctores, prædi- catores & Rectores. Unde Christus admonet: Rogate Dominum messis;ut mittat operarios in mes- sem suam, qui & ascendens in altum dedit dona ho- minibus,fecit enim quosdam Apostolos, quosdam Ev- angelistas,alios Prophetas,alios pastores & Doctores in ædificationem corporis sui,quod est Ecclesia &c. Eph. 4. Contra summa Dei maledictio est, quando au- fertur verbum, lege Amos. 8. Et mittam vobis fa- mem,non panis sed audiendi verbi &c. Sexto dicit: Cum multiplicati fueritis & creveritis in terra, in diebus illis, dicit Dominus, non dicent ultra de Arca fœderis Domini: Non erit memoria ejus, non prædi- cabitur ultra de ea.Non quærent eam, neŕ, quicquam fiet, id est, non sacrificabitur ibi. Sed in diebus illis vocabunt Jerusalem Thronum Domini. Et congre- gabuntur ad eam omnes gentes,propter nomen Domi- ni, quod erit in Jerusalem. Hæc est manifesta aboli- tio & abrogatio legis & veteris observantiæ à Deo Judæis præceptæ. Arca fœderis Domini hic nihil est,cui locus electus à Deo ante quærebatur & post- ea Templum ei à Salomone ædificabatur. Nihil hic sunt omnia legis sacrificia, quæ in loco Arcæ Domini fieri jubebantur. Breviter; Non adoratur neque invenitur nunc ultra Deus super illud Arcæ propitiatorium.Non est Deus hic ultra in omni il- lo cultu veteris legis. Siquidem in Jerusalem illa cœlesti,id est,in Ecclesia Christi est aliud propitia- torium & solium est Christus Jesus per sanguinem suum, ibi adoratur, ibi invenitur Deus. Roman. 3. Quem Deus proposuit propitiatorium &c. Hebr. 4. Accedamus ad Thronum gratiæ &c. 1. Joh. 2. Qui est propitiatio pro peccatis &c. Est enim nunc justitia Dei manifestata per Evangelium sine lege. Rom. 3. Imputatur nobis justitia, id est, remittitur nobis peccatum & gratis donatur vita æterna propter so- lum Christum,quem habemus ubique præsentem, ut non opus sit currere Jerosolymam, Romam &c. neque opus sit Antichristiana Papistarum prædica- tione: Ecce hic, Ecce illic Christus. Quemadmodum Simeon cecinit de Christo puero Lucæ 2. Video sa- lutare tuum, quod parasti ante faciem omnium popu- lorum. Lumen &c. Quod autem addit, propter no- men Domini, quod erit in Jerusalem,alludit ad hoc, quod post ædificatum Templum dicebatur: Nomen Domini habitare in Jerusalem,& vere ibi erat, quia de Deo prædicabatur ejus verbum, sacrificabatur secundum verbum Dei Deo, invocabatur Deus & Deus ibi exaudiebat invocantes, secundum ipsius promissionem Exod. 29. Habitabo in medio filiorum Israel &c. Nunc vero est alia nobis Jerusalem, in qua habitamus, nempe non terrena, sed cœlestis.

Ibi solum est nomen Domini, quia ibi docetur Ev- angelium, invocatut Deus, administrantur Christi Sacramenta, omnia fiunt ad gloriam Dei in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Septimo dicit: Ubi congregatæ fuerint omnes gentes in Zion (has terrena Jerusalem quando caperet?) tunc non ambulabunt ultra post cogitationes cordis sui pravi. Judæi habuerunt legem scriptam & per illam non potuerunt justificari. Gen- tes eam non habent & justificantur, hic vibes. Er- go ex lege non est justitia coram Deo, sed ex gratia (ut hic dicitur) desponsationis, quando credimus promissioni gratiæ in Christo. Vides itaque ut an- tea abolitionem legis, ita & nunc abolitionem pec- cati etiam apud gentes sine lege, quæ erant populus Satanæ, omnino sine Deo & sine Christo in hoc mundo Eph. 2. Secundum aliam Prophetiam Da- nielis 9. Ut consummetur prævaricatio, & finem ac- cipiat peccatum & deleatur iniquitas, & adducatur justitia sempiterna &c. Nusquam in scripturis ma- gis exprimitur gratia, quã quando gentes, quæ ne fingere quidem sibi meritum possunt, vocantur & suscipiuntur ad gratiam & Christo incorporantur. Octavo dicit: In diebus illis ibit domus Iuda ad do- mum Israel, & venient simul de terra Aquilonis in terram, quam dedi Patribus vestris hæreditatem. Non potest hoc intelligi de reductione ex captivi- tate Babylonica, ut supra dictum est, quando ex Ju- da & Benjamin reducti sunt Judæi tantum in ter- ram Juda, non in terram Israelis, ubi Samariam Sa- maritani, & alii tenebant, in locum Israelis ab Assy- rio Rege subrogati; itaque hæc dicuntur de spiri- tuali reductione, qua homines propter peccatum & impietatem à Deo abjecti reducuntur fide ad Chri- stum, invulgato Evangelio. Tunc & multi ex Israel, ex omni natione, quæ sub cœlo est, habitabant Ieroso- lymis propter religionem, Act. 2. Verum de corporali etiam Israelis sive decem tribuum reductione (quæ tamen non sunt redditæ suis agris) clarius alibi in hoc Propheta dicam. Alii vero ex Israel manentes in suis locis, dispersi inter gentes omnium natio- num, quæ sub cœlo sunt, postea susceperunt Evan- gelium. Quæ est vera reductio, de qua hic dicitur, non mutatio loci sed infidelitatis. Hic est verus in- gressus in terram sanctam patribus promissam & datam. Siquidem fide ingressi sunt in habitacula Dei, de quibus in Psalmis sæpe canitur: Et Abraham ne passum quidem pedis accepit in terra Canaan. Act. 7. Id quod Hebr. 11. sic dicitur: Expectant civitatem habentem fundamenta : Exeamus cum Iesu extra castra, opprobrium crucis portantes. Non enim hic habemus permanentem civitatem, sed futuram in- quirimus, ut patres illi olim. Et rursum: Iuxta fi- dem hi omnes defuncti sunt non accipientes hic pro- missionem &c. Præterea multi sancti & Prophetæ o- mnia mala in terra sua olim sub impiis passi sunt, de quibus ibidem dicitur : Hi omnes testimonio fidei probati, non acceperunt repromissionem, Deo pro no- bis melius aliquid providente, ut non sine nobis con- summarentur. Facile igitur vides, hic terram intel- ligi Jerusalem & Zion, ea ratione, qua ut supra di- ximus, quam non mutatione loci quærimus. Siqui- dem dilatata est per totum orbem terrarum, imo novus orbis dicitur, ut Psal. 8. Quoniam videbo cœ- los tuos, opera digitorum tuorum, lunam & stellas, quæ tu fundasti, ut est in Epistola ad Hebr. cap. 2. Non enim subjecit Deus Angelis Orbem terræ futu- rum de quo loquimur. Mirabile est hoc regnum cœ- lorum in terris. Nam à mundo non videtur. Non enim mutat locum, faciem, vestem, victum, ætatem, opera debita, sanctitatem, languorem, tempora, le- ges, consuetudines, politias, magistratus, conjugia, liberos, possessiones, cœlum, aërem, solem, diem, noctem &c. nisi quid turpe sit & homine probo in- dignum, attamen facit novos homines, novum lu- men, novos affectus, terrenorum contemptum, ita ut quæ donata & commisfa habent à Deo, non aliter possideant, quam ut Dei dona, nō hisce trans- itoriis innitentes, sed tantum gratiæ Patris, in cu- jus domo sive Regno se habitare per fidem agno- scunt. De hac conjunctione Juda & Israel, qui olim post mortem Salomonis perpetuo sese mutuo conficiebant, & de hæreditate gentium ad Judæos, Christo per fidem insertos, perventura (quod fa- ctum est per Evangelium, quod ex Judæis venit ad nos gentes) sic etiam dicitur Ef. 11. In die illa radix Jesse, id est, Christus &c. Et dispersos Juda colliget à quatuor plagis terræ (non solum ex Aquilone) & auferetur in vidia Ephraim, id est, Regni Israel &c. Et Oseæ 3. Dies multos sedebunt filii Israel sine Rege, sine Principe, sine sacrificio sine altari sine Ephod, sine cultu Dei. Post hæc convertentur filii Israel & quæ- rent Dominum Deum suum & David Regem suum (id est, Christum ex carne David nasciturum) & venerabuntur Dominum & gratiam ejus in novissimo dierum. Et cap. 1. Et erit numerus filiorum Israel, quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est, & non nu- merabitur. Et erit in loco, ubi dictum est eis: Non po- pulus meus vos, dicetur eis: Filii Dei viventis. Et congregabuntur filii Juda & filii Israel pariter & po- nent sibimet caput unum (id est Christum) & ascen- dent de terra, quia magnus dies Jesreel (id est semi- nis Dei, sive populi qui est semen Dei.) Sic & E- zechiel ait c. 34. Suscitabo super ea, & ipse erit eis in pastorem, ego autem Dominus ero eis in Deum, & servus meus David princeps in medio eorum, Ego Dominus locutus sum, & faciam cum eis pactum pa- cis & cessare faciam bestias pessimas &c. De hoc Re- gno Davidis, id est, Christi, & de hac reductione Populi, infra videbis Jer. 23. & 31. Ecce dies venient, dicit Dominus, & feriam domui Israel & domui Ju- da fœdus novum, non secundum fœdus quod pepigi cum patribus eorum &c. Nono additur promissio Dei (quam, inquit, multiplicabo te &c.) de multi- plicatione populi in Ecclesia gentium, & de dilata- tione Ecclesiæ per totum orbem terrarum, Psal. 21. dicit Christus ad patrem: Narrabo nomen tuum fra- tribus meis, in medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te.
