De te laus mea in Ecclesia magna. Domini est regnum & ipso dominabitur gentium &c. Ef. 49. Leva oculos tuos circumquaque &c. Decimo. Et promitto, quod tunc vocabis me Patrem & non deficies à me. Hoc per le- gem & studia nostra vel merita fieri non potest. Joh. 1. Qui non ex sanguinibus &c. Hæc B. Ante- cessor, fidelis Lutheri parastates, quæ totam hanc Prophetiam eximie illustrant. Postremo observa- mus Grotium ipsum ex hoc loco Jer. 3, 16. probare, quod tempore Messiæ desitura siut sacrificia annot. ad l. 5. de Verit. Relig. Christ. §. 8. p. 168.

AND OUR SHAME SHALL COVER US) As if a blanket.

ET OPERIET NOS IGNOMINIA NOSTRA) Quasi stragula.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV.

To true conversion forgiveness is promised with a threat of the Babylonian storm, of a sad messenger, of a war trumpet, of horror, of devastation, of stripping, and of pain, just as in childbirth.

Verse 1. IF YOU WILL RETURN O ISRAEL, SAYS THE LORD RETURN TO ME) Distinguish it thus: If you return to me, Israel: return, supply, to the fatherland. The following member demands this sense. The Chaldean adds: Before the sentence is signed.

YOU SHALL NOT BE MOVED) In the Hebrew: You shall not be an exile: that is, any longer.

Others more correctly understand it concerning a return to God, along with Lyranus, Pagninus, Vatablus, and Tremellius, i.e., if there is still hope that you will at some time be converted, return to me: so that this return is opposed both to the stubbornness in not returning (ch. 3, 10) and to hypocrisy or feigned repentance (ch. 3, 5). Which sense is also approved by B. Hülsemann. Thus also Jerome: According to the Hebrew, the sense here is: If you return to me, Israel, and once desiring salvation, you say that you have sinned and have not heard the voice of the Lord your God: return fully, and believe in Him whom you denied, and then there will be a full conversion.

Latin:

CAPUT IV.

Veræ conversioni venia promittitur cum com- minatione procellæ Babylonicæ, tristis nun- cii, tubæ bellicæ, horroris, vastitatis, denu- dationis, & doloris, veluti in puerperio.

Vers. 1. SI REVERTERIS ISRAEL, AIT DOMI- NUS, AD ME CONVERTERE) Ita distingue, Si ad me reverteris Israel: reverteris, supple, in patriam. Hunc sensum exigit membrum sequens. Chaldaeus addit: An- tequam signetur sententia.

NON COMMOVEBERIS) In Hebraeo: Non exsu- labis: ultra scilicet.

REctius alii de reversione ad Deum intelligunt cum Lyrano, Pagnino, Vatablo, & Tremellio, q. d. si adhuc spes est, te aliquando conversum iri, ad me revertere: ut haec reversio opponatur tum pertinaciae in non revertendo c. 3, 10. tum hypo- crisi vel fictae poenitentiae c. 3, 5. Qui sensus & pro- batur B. Hülsemanno. Sic etiam Hieronymus: Jux- ta Hebraicum hic sensus est: Si reverteris ad me Israel & semel salutem desiderans, peccasse te dicis & vocem domini Dei tui non audisse: plene convertere, & cre- de quem negasti, & tunc erit plena conversio.

## 4:2
Ver. 2. AND YOU SHALL SWEAR, THE LORD LIVES) This form of oath shall be: not, Baal lives.

IN TRUTH, IN JUDGMENT, AND IN JUSTICE) Nothing false, nothing iniquitous.

It can be admitted that this concerns an oath to be taken lawfully in the name of GOD in truth, in judgment, and in justice, which three conditions interpreters commonly, and not wrongly, make for an oath; but because the worship of God is wont to be expressed by an oath in general, as can be seen in Ps. 63, 12, Is. 65, 12, and in our Prophet ch. 16, 14, 15. Just as, conversely, an oath taken by false gods was a proof of a false religion (Exod. 23, 13, Acts 9, 16, Zeph. 1, 5), B. Socer not inappropriately observed that by an oath in truth, and in judgment, and in justice, is designated in this place the true worship of God, which was wont to be renewed among the Israelites by an oath taken after the repudiation of idolatry (2 Chron. 15, 14, Ezra 10, 5, Neh. 6, 12). Which sense is confirmed by those things which are added concerning the nations, that in Him they shall be blessed and shall glory in Him. For this glorying in the Lord, which is the cause of the blessing, embraces true faith in the Lord and true religion. Whence here a promise is held pertaining to the New Testament, concerning the spiritual worship of God, of Jews and Gentiles, with the middle wall of partition broken down. Similarly Jerome: You shall swear, is said here for confession. And further: And when Israel shall have done this, and shall have been a teacher of the nations through the Apostles, then all nations shall bless, or shall be blessed in Him, and shall praise Him because salvation has proceeded from Israel. Let it be compared especially with Is. 45, 23.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET JURABIS, VIVIT DOMINUS) Forma jurisjurandi haec erit: non, vivit Baal.

IN VERITATE, IN JUDICIO, ET IN JU- STITIA) Nihil falsi, nihil iniqui.

Admitti potest, agi de juramento in nomine DEI praestando legitime in veritate, in judicio & ju- stitia, quas tres conditiones juramenti faciunt communiter, nec male Interpp. sed quia per jura- mentum in genere cultus Dei exprimi solet, uti vi- dere est Psal. 63, 12. Es. 65, 12. & apud nostrum Pro- phetam cap. 16, 14. 15. Quemadmodum ex adverso juramentum per falsos Deos praestitum τεκμήριον erat falsae religionis Exod. 23, 13. Act. 9, 16. Soph. 1, 5. non praeter rem observavit B. Socer, per juramen- tum in veritate, & in judicio & in justitia designari hoc loco verum cultum Dei, qui solebat apud Israe- litas ob repudiatam idololatriam praestito jura- mento renovari. 2. Chron. 15, 14. Esdr. 10, 5. Neh. 6, 12. Quem sensum firmant ea, quae adduntur de gen- tibus, quod in ipso benedicendae sint & gloriaturae in ipso. Haec enim gloriatio in Domino, quae causa est benedictionis, complectitur veram fidem in Dominum, veramque religionem. Unde hic pro- missio habetur ad Nov. Test. pertinens, de spiri- tuali Dei cultu, Judaeorum & Gentilium, rupto pariete intergerino. Similiter Hieronymus: Jura- bis, pro confessione hic dicitur. Et porro: Cumque hoc fecerit Israel, & per Apostolos magister fuerit gentium, tunc benedicent, sive benedicentur in eo omnes gentes, & ipsum laudabunt quod salus proces- serit ex Israel. Conferatur cumprimis Es. 45, 23.

BREAK UP THE FALLOW GROUND) Clear out the field of the heart.

AND DO NOT SOW AMONG THORNS) To add sins to sins.

NOVATE NOVALE) Repurgate agrum cordis.

ET NOLITE SERERE SUPER SPINAS) Pec- cata peccatis addere.

Latin:

Vers. 4. AUFERTE PRAEPUTIA CORDIUM) Prae- putia per translationem apud Hebraeos dicuntur ea quae sunt inutilia. Impietatem vertit Chaldaeus: Graeci σκληροκαρδιαν.

Ver. 5. BLOW THE TRUMPET) Namely, so that all may withdraw themselves from the fields.

Vers. 5. CANITE TUBA) Nempe ut omnes se ex a- gris recipiant.

BE STRONG) In the Hebrew: Flee: Chaldean: Migrate. Greeks: σπεύσατε.

FROM THE NORTH) As above 50, 14.

Latin:

V. 6. LEVATE SIGNUM IN SION) Virgilius: Ut belli signum Laurenti Turnus ab arce Extulit.

CONFORTAMINI) In Hebraeo: Fugite: Chaldaeus: Migrate. Graeci: σπεύσατε.

AB AQUILONE) Ut supra 50, 14.

Vers. 7. THE LION IS COME UP FROM HIS LAIR) The King from his citadel: Chaldean here: Declaring the beast to be a king: Zeno in the Lion-fighter, where the beast is a Lion. It appears the Nebuchadnezzars are being described.

THE DESTROYER OF NATIONS) Preferred by his own to Hercules: the devastator of Africa itself and Spain. See what we have brought to book 3 of the truth of the Christian religion.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ASCENDIT LEO DE CUBILI SUO) Rex ex arce sua: Chaldaeus hic: Τὸ θηρίον βασιλέα δηλῶν: Zeno in Leone Iconomacho, ubi θηρίον est Leo. Nabuchodo- nosorum describi apparet.

PRAEDO GENTIUM) Herculi praelatus à suis: Afri- cae ipsius & Hispaniae vastator. Vide quae attulimus ad li- brum 3. de veritate religionis Christianae.

## 4:10
Vers. 10. HAST THOU THEN DECEIVED THIS PEOPLE) In the Hebrew: surely thou hast deceived: that is, thou hast allowed them to be deceived. For often among the Hebrews, verbs active in sound are permissive in meaning.

SAYING: PEACE SHALL BE UNTO YOU) That is, through those who were saying, salvation shall be unto you, through those false prophets, of whom there is mention below 6, 14. 7, 4. 10. 23, 5. THE SWORD REACHETH UNTO THE SOUL) Let there be a great slaughter. Vers. 11. A BURNING WIND) Pestilential. IN THE WAYS THAT ARE IN THE DESERT THE WAY OF THE DAUGHTER OF MY PEOPLE) In the Hebrew: From the heights through the desert, by which one goes to my people. In Chaldea there are many mountains: Between Chaldea and Judea there are many desert places. NOT TO FAN, NOR TO CLEANSE) But to burn everything, for that is understood. Vers. 12. A WIND FULL FROM THESE SHALL COME TO ME) The sense is: A wind more vehement than those things: that is, more vehement than to serve for fanning or cleansing. AND NOW I WILL SPEAK MY JUDGMENTS WITH THEM) That is, through this wind I will avenge myself on the Jews. Vers. 15. THE VOICE OF ONE ANNOUNCING FROM DAN, AND MAKING KNOWN THE IDOL FROM MOUNT EPHRAIM) That is, the slaughter and exile of the ten tribes ought to be a warning to you, what reward idolatry receives. He names specifically Dan and Ephraim, because the calves had been placed there 1 Kings 12, 29. For Bethel was in the part of Ephraim. Vers. 16. KEEPERS TO COME) It is a mockery, from an ambiguity. Keepers apply care to fields, lest one enter the field: and besiegers, lest one enter the city. But the former ward off harmful things, the latter, beneficial things. The following words make this sense clearer. Theodotion for נֹצְרִים, reads בֹּצְרִים, vintagers. Vers. 18. THIS MALICE BECAUSE IT IS BITTER, BECAUSE IT HATH TOUCHED THY HEART: MY BOWELS, MY BOWELS I AM IN PAIN) These seem to cohere, and to be an ellipsis of a word, you will say: in this sense: Because the punishment of thy sin brings bitterness to thy mind, you will say: I am in pain in my bowels: That is, the trumpets will loosen your bowels for you, wretch. THE SENSES OF MY HEART ARE TROUBLED WITHIN ME) In the Hebrew: the walls of my heart (and) my heart is in a tumult. The walls of the heart are the viscera surrounding the heart. הֹומִית is in a tumult, which Aquila had translated as ἐκκλάζει, Theodotion as καμμύσσει. Jerome denies that he understands what that is. But it is to be insane, and it is found thus in Lycophron, Sophocles, Herodotus, and others. I WILL NOT HOLD MY PEACE) I cannot abstain from testifying to my fear with a cry. MY SOUL HATH HEARD) In the Hebrew: Thou hast heard: so that my soul is myself, and it is a construction according to the meaning. Vers. 20. DESTRUCTION UPON DESTRUCTION IS CALLED) Disaster follows disaster. Compare Psalm 42, 8. SUDDENLY ARE MY TENTS WASTED, SUDDENLY MY CURTAINS) That is, dwellings, a metaphor taken from tent-dwellers. Vers. 21. SHALL I SEE THE FUGITIVE) In the Hebrew: the standard, namely, the hostile one. Vers. 22. FOR MY PEOPLE IS FOOLISH THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN ME) Thus far it was a mimicry of those things which the people were about to cry out for fear. Now God gives the reasons why that is to happen. THEY ARE WISE TO DO EVIL) They are ingenious for that one thing. Thus φρονιμώτερος is taken in Luke 16, 8. Vers. 23. I BEHELD THE EARTH, AND LO IT WAS VOID, AND OF NOUGHT) In the Hebrew exactly as at the beginning of Genesis תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ: Chaldean: desert and void. Aquila: empty. Symmachus: confused. The sense is: the earth will be without inhabitants, without houses, without fruits, such as it was at the beginning of things. AND THE HEAVENS, AND THERE WAS NO LIGHT IN THEM) Smoke rising from everywhere will cover the stars with a cloud. Vers. 24. I BEHELD THE MOUNTAINS AND LO THEY WERE MOVED, AND ALL THE HILLS WERE TROUBLED) Everything will tremble at the passage of such great armies. Vers. 25. AND THERE WAS NO MAN) All are either killed, or captured, or have fled. AND ALL THE FOWL OF THE HEAVEN WAS GONE) Not surprising, since we read that birds even fell from the sky, the air being shaken by the military clamor. Vers. 26. AND LO CARMEL IS A DESERT) You may better explain it here as a fertile field, as above 2, 7. Vers. 27. ALL THE EARTH SHALL BE DESERT, BUT YET I WILL NOT MAKE A FULL END) That punishment will not yet suffice for me. I want the earth to remain so for a long time, as was said in Leviticus 26, 34. Vers. 29. AT THE VOICE OF THE HORSEMAN) Horace: Nor let the Medes ride unpunished with you as leader, Caesar. AND OF THE ARCHER) Propertius: Susa is not armed with so many Achaemenian arrows. THEY HAVE ENTERED INTO THE THICKETS) In the Hebrew: dense places, that is, woody: as the Chaldean interprets. The Jews fled into the woods and rocks.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ERGONE DECEPISTI POPULUM I- STUM) In Hebraeo: certe decepisti: id est, sivisti decipi. Saepe enim apud Hebraeos verba sono activa fignificatu per- missiva sunt.

DICENS: PAX ERIT VOBIS) Id est, per eos qui dicebant, salus erit vobis, per pseudoprophetas illos, quorum & infra mentio 6, 14. 7, 4. 10. 23, 5. PERVENIT GLADIVS USQUE AD ANIMAM) Magna sit occidio. Vers. 11. VENTUS URENS) Pestilens. IN VIIS QUÆ SUNT IN DESERTO VIÆ POPULI MEI) In Hebræo: Ab eminentiis per desertum, qua itur ad populum meum. In Chaldæa multi sunt montes: Inter Chaldæam & Judæam multa loca deserta. NON AD VENTILANDUM, NEQVE AD PURGANDUM) Sed ad urenda omnia, id enim subintel- ligitur. Vers. 12. SPIRITVS PLENVS EX HIS VENIET MIHI) Sensus est: Ventus istis rebus vehementior: id est, ve- hementior, quam ut ventilationi aut purgationi inserviat. ET NUNC EGO LOQVAR JUDICIA MEA CUM EIS) Id est, per hunc ventu vindicabo me de Judæis. Vers. 15. VOX ANNVNTIANTIS A DAN, ET NOTUM FACIENTIS IDOLVM DE MONTE E- PHRAIM) Id est occidio & exsilium decem tribuum tibi pro monitore esse debet, quam mercedem accipiat idolo- latria. Nominat autem specialiter Dan & Ephraim, quia ibi positi fuerant vituli 1. Reg. 12, 29. Nam Bethel fuit in parte Ephraimi. Vers. 16. CUSTODES VENIRE) Est χλευασμὸς, ex ambiguo. Custodes agrorum curam adhibent, ne in agrum intretur: & obsessores ne in urbem. Sed illi noxia arcent, hi profutura. Hunc sensum apertiorem faciunt verba sequen- tia. Theodotio pro נֹצְרִים, legit בֹּצְרִים, vindemiatores. Vers. 18. ISTA MALITIA QVIA AMARA, QVIA TETIGIT COR TVVM: VENTREM MEUM, VENTREM MEUM DOLEO) Videntur hæc cohærere, & ἔκθλιψις esse verbi, dices: hoc sensu: Quia pœna peccati tui amaritiem affert animo tuo, dices: Ventrem doleo: Id est, misero solvent tibi classica ventrem. SENSUS CORDIS MEI TURBATI SUNT IN ME) In Hebræo: parietes cordis mei (&) cor meum tumul- tuatur. Parietes cordis sunt viscera cordi circumjecta הֹומִית tumultuatur, quod Aquilæ ἐκκλάζει, Theodotio verterat καμμύσσει. Id quid sit negat se intelligere Hieronymus. Est autem insanire, & sic reperitur apud Lycophronem, So- phoclem, Herodotum, alios. NON TACEBO) Abstinere non possum, quin cla- more metum tester. AUDIVIT ANIMA MEA) In Hebræo: Audisti: ut anima mea sit ego, & constructio κατὰ τὸ σημαινόμενον. Vers. 20. CONTRITIO SVPER CONTRITIO- NEM VOCATA EST) Clades cladem sequitur. Confer. Psal. 42, 8. REPENTE VASTATA SUNT TABERNACU- LA MEA, SUBITO PELLES MEÆ) Id est habitacula, Metaphora à scenitis desumpta. Vers. 21. VIDEBO FUGIENTEM) In Hebræo: ve- xillum, nempe hostile. Vers. 22. QUIA STULTUS POPULUS MEUS ME NON COGNOVIT) Hactenus μίμησις fuit eorum quæ populus præ pavore erat clamaturus. Nunc Deus reddit causas, cur id futurum sit. SAPIENTES SVNT UT FACIANT MALA) In id unum ingeniosi sunt. Sic φρονιμώτερος sumitur Lucæ 16, 8. Vers. 23. ASPEXI TERRAM, ET ECCE VACUA ERAT, ET NIHILI) In Hebræo plane ut initio Geneseos תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ: Chaldæus: deserta & vacua. Aquila: κενή. Sym- machus: συνκεχυμένη. Sensus est: erit terra sine habitatori- bus, sine domibus, sine frugibus, qualis initio rerum fuit. ET COELOS, ET NON ERAT LUX IN EIS) Fumus undique surgens nubem sideribus obducet. Vers. 24. VIDI MONTES ET ECCE MOVEBAN- TUR, ET OMNES COLLES CONTURBATI SUNT) Tantorum agminum transitu trement omnia. Vers. 25. ET NON ERAT HOMO) Omnes aut occisi, aut capti sunt aut aufugerunt. ET OMNE VOLATILE COELI RECESSIT) Non mirum, cum etiam cecidisse de cœlo aves legamus, militarem per clamorem concusso aëre. Vers. 26. ET ECCE CARMELUS DESERTVS) Melius & hic explices agrum fertilem, in supra 2, 7. Vers. 27. DESERTA ERIT OMNIS TERRA, SED TAMEN CONSUMMATIONEM NON FACIAM) Nondum ea pœna mihi sufficiet. Volo terra diu sic maneat, ut dictum Levit. 26, 34. Vers. 29. A VOCE EQVITIS) Horatius: Nec finas Medos equitare inultos Te duce Cæsar. ET MITTENTIS SAGITTAM) Propertius: Non tot Achæmeniis armantur Susa sagittis. INGRESSI SVNT ARDUA) In Hebræo: densa, id est, Sylvestria: ut interpretatur Chaldæus. Fugerunt Judæi in silvas & rupes.

## 4:30
Verse 30. AND THOU SHALT PAINT THINE EYES WITH ANTIMONY) In the Hebrew, thou shalt open. Antimony dilates the eyes: therefore it is called πλατυόφθαλμον. See what is said in 2 Kings 9:30. Correct here the Greek edition, where it is ἐγχρίσῃς τιμῇ τῆς ὀφθαλμύς σε, and read σίμμι. That is, for it is antimony. The error arose from a very similar pronunciation.

THY LOVERS HAVE DESPISED THEE) They seek no further intercourse.

THEY SEEK THY LIFE) They threaten thy life once their lusts are satisfied, although it is shameful that a man and a woman, just joined, are immediately enemies.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ET PINXERIS STIBIO OCVLOS TVOS) In Hebræo, aperueris. Stibium dilatat oculos: ideo πλατυό- φθαλμον dicitur. Vide quæ dicta 2. Reg. 9, 30. Corrige hic Græcam editionem, ubi est ἐγχρίσῃς τιμῇ τῆς ὀφθαλμύς σε, & lege σίμμι. Id est enim stibium. Error ex pronun- ciatione persimili.

CONTEMSERUNT TE AMATORES TUI) Non ultra concubitum quærunt.

ANIMAM TUAM QUÆRUNT) Vitæ imminent expletis libidinibus, quamvis Turpe vir & mulier, juncti modo, protinus hostes.

## 4:31
Verse 31. ANGUISH AS OF A WOMAN IN TRAVAIL) In the Hebrew it is, of one bringing forth for the first time. The Greeks say πρωτοτοκέσης. This is not without emphasis. Thus in the Andria: 'Nor is she worthy enough to be entrusted with a woman in her first labor.'

THE VOICE OF THE DAUGHTER OF SION AS OF ONE DYING) Fainting from grief. The Greeks say ἐκλυθήσεται.

AND SPREADING HER HANDS) As women are accustomed to do in great grief. See above 2:37.

MY SOUL FAINTED BECAUSE OF THE SLAIN) In the Hebrew: because of the slayers. My soul fainted for love of those who appear as slayers instead of lovers.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ANGUSTIAS UT PUERPERÆ) In Hebræo est, primum parientis. Græci πρωτοτοκέσης. Non caret hoc emphasi. Sic in Andria. Nec satis digna cui committas primo partu mulierem.

VOX FILIÆ SION INTERMORIENTIS) De- ficientis præ dolore. Græci ἐκλυθήσεται.

EXPANDENTISQUE MANUS SUAS) Ut solent feminæ in dolore magno. Vide supra 2, 37.

DEFECIT ANIMA MEA PROPTER INTER- FECTOS) In Hebræo: propter interfectores. Amore defecit eorum qui pro amatoribus appareut interfectores.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

A reproach of the sins of the whole people, of the princes and nobles, of the prophets and priests, and of the promiscuous crowd, against the first and second table: and a threatening of spiritual and corporal punishments on account of their continued defection from GOD and contempt of the word of GOD, yet with the addition of consolation, that God in his wrath will have regard for his own.

Verse 1.

AND I WILL BE MERCIFUL TO HIM) I will exempt him from the common destruction, as Lot from Sodom.

In the Hebrew, the feminine לָהּ is held, which therefore must be referred to the city, not indeed to that faithful individual. Jerome observed this sense: Great is the love of justice, so that God did not deliver the city according to the interrogation of Abraham and the answer of God for ten just men, but if He found one, Jerusalem was even then about to perish. And because it could happen that some might be found among the people who would feign the worship of God and swear by God, He prevents this, because God is not at all delighted by vain words, but by the truth of faith, and says: I do not love those who swear by me and swear in falsehood, but those whose lips and hearts agree.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Exprobratio peccatorum universi populi, Prin- cipum, & optimatum, Prophetarum, & sa- cerdotum, turbæq́; promiscua, adversus pri- mam, & secundam tabula: & comminatio ob continuatam defectionem à DEO, & con- temtum verbi DEI pœnarum spiritualium & corporalium, addita tamen consolatione, quod Deus in ira suorum habiturus sit rationē.

Vers. 1.

ET PROPITIUS ERO EI) Eum communi exitio eximam, ut Lothum è Sodomis.

IN Ebræo habetur fœmininum לָהּ quod proinde ad civitatem referendum, non vero ad indivi- duum illud fidele. Quem sensum observavit Hie- ronymus: Grandis amor justitiæ, ut nequaquam juxta interrogationem Abrahæ & responsionem Dei pro decem viris justis Deus liberavit civitatem, sed si unum invenerit, jam jamque peritura Hieru- salem. Et quia poterat fieri, ut aliqui invenirentur in populo, qui simularent cultum Dei & jurarent per Deum, hoc prævenit, quod nequaquam Deus vanis sermonibus, sed veritate fidei delectetur, & dicit: Non eos diligo, qui jurant per me & ju- rant in mendacio, sed quorum labia cordaque consentiunt.

## 5:2
Vers. 2. NAY, IF THEY EVEN SAY, THE LORD LIVES, THEY WILL ALSO SWEAR THIS FALSELY) Even they who swear not by gods, but by the true God, despise Him so much that they apply His name to false things.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUIN SI ETIAM, VIVIT DOMINUS, DIXERINT, ET HOC FALSO JURABUNT) Etiam ipsi qui non per Deos, sed per Deum verum jurant, adeo cum contemnunt, ut ad res falsas ejus nomen adhibeant.

## 5:3
Vers. 3. LORD, THINE EYES LOOK UPON FAITH) In the Hebrew: Do not Thine eyes look to truth? That is: But Thou, O Lord, art not deceived by those simulators: Thou seest even the innermost thoughts.

The Vulgate translation is incorrectly corrected. For by אֱמוּנָה the Hebrews express faith, 1 Sam. 26:23, Hab. 2:4. And the sense is that the eyes of the Lord look upon faith, and that it pleases God. Because without it, it is impossible to please God, Heb. 11:6. To which that classic passage Hab. 2:4 especially pertains: The just shall live by his faith. Where the thing itself teaches that faith is understood as falsified, the Apostolic interpretation especially confirms it. Rom. 1:17, Gal. 3:11, Heb. 10:28. For in the Hebrew the same word occurs. Jerome on this passage: After the words of the Lord by which He had commanded, saying: Go around the ways of Jerusalem, and the rest, the Prophet speaks to the Lord: Lord, Thine eyes look upon faith, which in Hebrew is called אֱמוּנָה, not the works of the Jews, in which they boasted according to the ceremonies of the law: but the faith of Christians, through which by grace we have been saved.

Vers. e d. THEY HAVE HARDENED THEIR FACES) They have become shameless.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DOMINE, OCULI TUI RESPICIUNT FIDEM) In Hebræo: Oculi tui nonne ad veritatem? Id est: At tu Domine à simulatoribus illis non falleris: etiam inti- ma cogitata pervides.

Perperam corrigitur vulgata translatio. Nam per אֱמוּנָה fidem exprimunt Ebræi 1. Sam. 26, 23. Hab. 2, 4. Et sensus est oculos Domini fidem respi- cere, eamque Deo placere. Quia sine illa placere Deo impossibile est Ebr. 11, 6. Quo facit cumpri- mis locus ille classicus Hab. 2, 4. Justus fide sua vivet. Ubi falsificam fidem intelligi cum res ipsa docet, tum interpretatio Apostolica imprimis confirmat. Rom. 1, 17. Gal. 3, 11. Ebr. 10, 28. In Ebræo enim eadem vox occurrit. Hieronymus ad hunc locum: Post verba Domini quibus imperaverat dicens: Cir- cuite vias Hierusalem, & cætera, Propheta loquitur ad Dominū: Domine oculi tui respiciunt fidem, quæ Hebraice dicitur אֱמוּנָה, non opera Judæorum, in quibus juxta legis ceremonias exultabant: sed fi- dem Christianorum, per quā gratia salvi facti sumus.

Vers. e d. INDURAVERUNT FACIES SUAS) De- puduerunt.

## 5:4
Vers. 4. PERHAPS THEY ARE POOR AND FOOLISH, IGNORING THE WAY OF THE LORD) In the Hebrew: Perhaps the poor are foolish, because they have not learned the way of the Lord, that is, the law. He says this as if by concession, so that he may press them more heavily.

Latin:

Vers. 4. FORSITAN PAUPERES SUNT ET STUL- TI IGNORANTES VIAM DOMINI) In Hebræo: Forte pauperes defipiunt, quia viam Domini, id est, legem, non didice- runt, Hoc dicit quasi per concessionē, ut eos gravius premat.

## 5:5
Vers. 5. FOR THEY HAVE KNOWN THE WAY OF THE LORD) That is, they have nothing by which to excuse themselves, since both leisure and wealth are available to them for learning the law.

THEY HAVE BROKEN THE YOKE) They have despised the law. See what is said on Psalm 2.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IPSI ENIM COGNOVERUNT VIAM DO- MINI) Id est, illi nihil habent quo se excusent, cum & o- tium & opes illis suppetant ad discendam legem.

CONFREGERVNT JUGUM) Legem spreverunt. Vide quæ dicta ad Psalm. 2.

## 5:6
Vers. 6. THEREFORE A LION FROM THE FOREST HAS STRUCK THEM, A WOLF AT EVENING HAS DEVASTATED THEM, A LEOPARD WATCHING OVER THEIR CITIES) Nebuchadnezzar is compared to a lion because of his strength, as also above 4:7, to a wolf because of his rapacity, to a leopard because of his speed. You may rightly translate these past tenses as future. For such things are accustomed to be mixed in the Hebrew. The present for the future in prophecies, says Servius.

EVERYONE WHO SHALL HAVE GONE OUT FROM THEM SHALL BE CAPTURED) There will be danger as much outside the cities as in the cities. See 2 Kings 25:4 and 5.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ICCIRCO PERCUSSIT EOS LEO DE SILVA, LVPVS AD VESPERAM VASTAVIT EOS, PARDVS VIGILANS SUPER CIVITATES EORVM) Nabuchodonosor leoni comparatur ob vires, ut & supra 4, 7. lupo ob rapacitatem, pardo ob velocitatem. Hæc præ- tertia per futurum recte vertas. Solent enim ista misceri in Hebræo. Præsens pro futuro in vaticiniis, ait Servius.

OMNIS QVI EGRESSVS FVERIT EX EIS CAPIETVR) Tam extra urbes quam in urbibus periculum erit. Vide 2. Reg. 25, 4. & 5.

## 5:7
Vers. 7. THY CHILDREN HAVE FORSAKEN ME) The individual citizens.

I HAVE FED THEM TO THE FULL AND THEY HAVE COMMITTED ADULTERY) For in fullness there is Venus. See also Ezekiel 16:49.

AND IN THE HOUSE OF THE HARLOT THEY LIVED LUXURIOUSLY) In the Hebrew: They ran together into the brothel.

Latin:

Vers. 7. FILII TVI DERELIQVERUNT ME) Ci- ves singuli.

SATURAVI EOS ET MOECHATI SVNT) ἐν πλησμονῇ γὰρ κύπρις. Vide & Ezech. 16, 49.

ET IN DOMO MERETRICIS LVXVRIABAN- TVR) In Hebræo: In lupanar concurrebant.

## 5:8
Ver. 8. THEY BECAME AMOROUS HORSES AND STALLIONS. EVERY ONE NEIGHED AFTER HIS NEIGHBOR'S WIFE) He meant to say stallions, by which name Cicero also defames a lustful man in his speech against Piso. But in the Hebrew it is: As a horse fed in the morning: So each one neighed after another's wife. Horses are more lively in the morning, especially when well fed.

Latin:

Vers. 8. EQVI AMATORES ET EMISSARII FACTI SVNT. VNVSQVISQVE AD VXOREM PROXIMI SVI HINNIEBAT) Voluit dicere admissarii, quo nomi- ne etiam Cicero hominem libidinosum infamat oratione in Pisonem. Sed in Hebræo est: Ut equus pastus mane: Sic quisque alienæ uxori adhinnivit. Mane alacriores sunt e- qui præsertim bene pasti.

## 5:10
Ver. 10. ASCEND HER WALLS AND DESTROY) The words of God to the Chaldeans.

BUT DO NOT MAKE A FULL END) Do not think this is enough, but take the whole nation from the earth, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ASCENDITE MUROS EJVS ET DIS- SIPATE) Verba Dei ad Chaldæos.

CONSMMATIONEM AVTEM NOLITE FA- CERE) Ne satis hoc putate, sed omnem gentem de ter- ra tollite, ut sequitur.

## 5:12
Ver. 12. AND THEY SAID: IT IS NOT HE) The God who is worshipped in Judea is not that Lord of the universe.

WE SHALL NOT SEE THE SWORD AND FAMINE) There will be no siege against us. For sieges kill some by the sword, others by famine. To see, for to experience.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET DIXERUNT: NON EST IPSE) Deus qui in Judæa colitur, non est ille Dominus universi.

GLADIVM ET FAMEM NON VIDEBIMVS) Nulla erit obsidio adversus nos. Nam obsidiones alios fer- ro, alios fame interimunt. Videre, pro experiri.

## 5:13
Ver. 13. THE PROPHETS HAVE SPOKEN TO THE WIND) ἀνεμώλια βάζον, as Homer speaks.

AND THERE WAS NO ANSWER IN THEM) In the Hebrew: The word (supply: of God) was not in them. They had no divine revelation.

THEREFORE THESE THINGS SHALL HAPPEN TO THEM) May they happen. May these sad omens fall back upon their own heads. Up to this point are the words of the impious.

Latin:

Vers. 13. PROPHETÆ FVERUNT IN VENTVM LOCVTI) ἀνεμώλια βάζον, ut Homerus loquitur.

ET RESPONSUM NON FVIT IN EIS) In He- bræo: Verbum (supple Dei) non fuit in eis. Nullam habue- runt divinam revelationem.

HÆC ERGO EVENIENT ILLIS) Eveniant. In ipsorum capita recidant tristes istæ ominationes. Huc usque verba impiorum.

## 5:14
Ver. 14. I GIVE MY WORDS IN THY MOUTH FOR FIRE) By your words their stubbornness will be convinced, and they will pay the penalties for it. Similar to above 1, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DO VERBA MEA IN ORE TVO IN I- GNEM) Per tua verba convincentur contumaciæ, & ejus pœnas dabunt. Simile supra 1, 10.

## 5:15
Ver. 15. A NATION FROM AFAR) Words of the law, Deut. 28, 49. See also Isaiah 5, 26.

AN ANCIENT NATION) Gen. 10, 10. 11, 2. See also what was brought forward by us in the first book on the truth of the Christian Religion.

Verse of the same. A NATION WHOSE LANGUAGE YOU WILL NOT KNOW.

It is the nation of the Chaldeans: whose language was unknown to the Jewish people before the captivity, even though it was in use among the Jews after the captivity. The Jews indeed still retained the Hebrew language among the learned until the destruction of the second temple, from which time it then migrated from the land of Canaan, yet in such a way that they spoke Chaldean, but corruptly, until the composition of the Talmud; afterwards, however, the Chaldean and Hebrew languages being clearly buried, wherever they came in the world, they assumed the language of the inhabitants, as Kimchi admits in the preface to the book Michlol. Moreover, before the captivity, the Hebrew language was their vernacular, but they could not understand the Chaldean language, 2 Kings 18:26.

Latin:

Vers. 15. GENTEM DE LONGINQVO) Verba legis Deut. 28, 49. Vide & Esaiæ 5, 26.

GENTEM ANTIQVAM) Genes. 10, 10. 11, 2. Vi- de & quæ allata à nobis ad librum primum de veritate Re- ligionis Christianæ.

Vers. eod. GENTEM CUJUS IGNORA- BIS LINGUAM.

Chaldæorum gens est: quorum lingua ante ca- ptivitatem ignota fuit populo Judaico: etiamsi post captivitatem Judæis in usu fuerit. Retinuerunt qui- dem adhuc Judæi linguam Ebræam inter eruditos usque ad destructionem templi secundi, ex quo dein- de è terra Canaan migravit, ita tamen, ut usque ad compositionem Talmudis Chaldaice, sed corrupte locuti sint; postmodum autem Chaldæa & Ebræa lingua plane sepultis, quocunque locorum venere, incolarum linguam assumserunt, fatente Kimchio in præfat. libr. Michlol. Cæterum ante captivitatem Ebræa lingua ipsis erat vernacula, Chaldaïsmum autem intelligere non poterant 2. Reg. 18, 26.

## 5:16
Verse 16. THEIR QUIVER IS LIKE AN OPEN SEPULCHRE) Just as there are many dead in one sepulchre, so also one Chaldean quiver will yield many dead.

ALL THE MIGHTY ONES) They are all most warlike.

Latin:

Vers. 16. PHARETRA EJVS QUASI SEPVL- CHRUM PATENS) Sicut in uno sepulchro multi sunt mortui sic & una Chaldæia pharetra multos dabit mortuos.

VNIVERSI FORTES) Omnes sunt bellacissimi.

## 5:17
V. 17. HE SHALL DEVOUR YOUR SONS AND YOUR DAUGHTERS) Namely, with the sword. For every consumption is accustomed to be called אכל by the Hebrews.

Latin:

V. 17. DEVORABIT FILIOs TVOS ET FILIAS TVAS) Nempe gladio. Nam omnis consumptio Hebræis solet dici אכל.

## 5:18
Verse 18. I WILL NOT MAKE YOU A CONSUMPTION) In the Hebrew: With you: that is, I will not yet refrain from punishing you, as above in 10; what remains is a long servitude, of which he will now treat.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NON FACIAM VOS IN CONSVMMA- TIONEM) In Hebræo: Vobiscum: id est, nondum absti- nebo punire vos, ut supra 10. quod restat, est longa servi- tus, de qua jam aget.

## 5:22
FROM MY FACE YOU SHALL NOT GRIEVE) You shall tremble: as this Chaldean [version has it].

Vers. 22. WHO HAVE PLACED THE SAND as a boundary for the sea) The shores. AND THEY SHALL BE MOVED) Supply, the waves: which is to be understood here from what follows. AND THEY SHALL NOT BE ABLE) They shall not prevail. Vers. 23. THEY HAVE GONE BACK AND DEPARTED) From my law, which the sea also observes. Vers. 24. THE FULLNESS OF THE ANNUAL HARVEST KEEPING FOR US) The Greeks and this interpreter read שבעות with the Schin marked on the left corner. But the Chaldean and Hebrew codices with the Schin marked on the right: that is, He keeps for us the weeks of the appointed harvest. The sense is: He causes all the crops to ripen in those weeks which are between Passover and Pentecost. A different spelling is not immediately to be argued from a different interpretation; and one must acquiesce to the Hebrew text, with which the Chaldean agrees, as also the first edition of Aquila and Symmachus, as Jerome testifies. Although indeed these [people] translate these things with no dissimilar reasoning along with Grotius—Aquila, Symmachus, Pagninus, Tremellius, Piscator, Castro, Maldonatus, Cornelius a Lapide (who nevertheless do not agree in sense and explanation, some accepting it with Piscator and Tremellius regarding the seventh and Sabbatic year, others rather regarding those seven weeks between Passover and Pentecost destined for the harvest, Lev. 23, 13; Deut. 16, 9)—the interpretation of B. Luther is nevertheless not to be rejected, to which the version of Vatablus and the Tigurine is akin: who kept the harvest for us by an appointed oath. Which Ludov. de Dieu also approves and confirms with his own calculation at this place; thus I translate, he says: He keeps the oaths of the harvest, that is, the sworn statutes of the harvest, just as He swore, Gen. 9, 1. Vers. 23. YOUR INIQUITIES HAVE TURNED AWAY THESE) These things have turned away: namely, good things from you. Vers. 26. LYING IN WAIT AS FOWLERS) In the Hebrew: Who watch, (singular for plural) as when snares are set. AND TRAPS( משחת, which is here in the Hebrew, seems to be a pit: and nouns of the same origin are translated elsewhere by βόθρος. Vers. 27. AS A CAGE FULL OF BIRDS) Rather 607s, or ὀρνίθων, as the Chaldean understood it. V. 28 AND MY WORDS HAVE PASSED BY MOST WICKEDLY) You could translate, they exceed evil things: so that it is the same as the following, they have prospered. THEY HAVE NOT JUDGED THE JUDGMENT OF THE POOR) Either they do not render justice to them, or they judge perversely. Moreover, He names those persons most especially who, being powerless of themselves, are most in need of public aid. Vers. 30. STUPOR AND WONDERS HAVE BEEN DONE IN THE LAND) Stupendous and horrible things. THE PRIESTS CLAPPED WITH THEIR HANDS) Better: the priests were ruling, (namely, over the people through them: that is, the false prophets, whose works they used). AND MY PEOPLE LOVED SUCH THINGS) It wanted to be treated thus. WHAT THEREFORE SHALL BE DONE IN ITS END) In the Hebrew: What will you do hereafter? that is, where will this wickedness not escape to, unless I repress it with punishments?

Latin:

A FACIE MEA NON DOLEBITIS) Pavebitis: ut hic Chaldæus.

Vers. 22. QVI POSVI ARENAM TERMINVM MARI) Littora. ET COMMOVEBVNTVR) Supple, fluctus: quod ex sequentibus hic intelligendum. ET NON POTERvNT) Non prævalebunt. Vers. 23. RECESSERVNT ET ABIERVNT) A le- ge mea, quam & mare observat. Vers. 24. PLENITVDINEM ANNUÆ MESSIS CV- STODIENTEM NOBIS) Græci & hic interpres legerunt שבעות cum Schin notato in sinistro cornu. At Chaldæus & Hebræi codices cum Schin notato in dextro: id est, Se- ptimanas statutorum messis servat nobis. Sensus est: efficit, ut omnia sata maturefcant f pestis illis septimanis, quæ sunt inter Pascha & Pentecosten. Non diversa scriptio statim arguenda est è di- versa interpretatione; & acquiescendu Ebræo tex- tui, cui Chaldæus consonat, ut & Aquilæ prima edi- tio & Symmachi teste Hieronymo. Quanquam ve- ro hæc no absimili ratione transferant cum Grotio Aquila, Symmachus, Pagninus, Tremellius, Pisca- tor, Castro, Maldonatus, Cornelius a Lapide (qui ta- men in sensu & explicatione non conveniunt, non- nullis cum Piscat. & Tremell. de septimo & Sabba- thico anno, aliis potius de septem illis hebdomadis inter Pascha & Pentecosten messi destinatis Lev. 23, 13. Deut. 16, 9. accipientibus) non reprobanda ta- men interpretatio B. Lutheri, cui gemina est Vata- bli & Tigurina versio: qui juramento statuto mes- sem nobis custodivit. Quam calculo suo probat & confirmat Ludov. de Dieu ad h. l. ita verto, inquit: Juramenta statutorum messis servat nobis, id est, jurata statuta messis, sicut juravit Gen. 9, 1. Vers 23. INIQVITATES VESTRÆ DECLINAVE- RVNT HÆC) Averterunt ista: bona scilicet a vobis. Vers. 26. INSIDIANTES QVASI AVCUPES) In Hebræo: Qui observant, (singularis pro plurali) sicut quando ponuntur laquei. ET PEDICAS( משחת, quod hic est in Hebræo, videtur esse fovea: & nomina ejusdem originis per βόθρος vertuntur alibi. Vers 27. SICVT DECIPVLA PLENA AVIBVS) I- mo 607s, sive ὀρνίθων quomodo accepit Chaldæus. V. 28 ET PRÆTERIERVNT SERMONES MEOS PESSIME) Vertere possis, superant res malas: ut idem sit cum sequente prosperaverunt. JVDICIVM PAVPERVM NON JUDICAVE- RVNT) Aut jus illis non reddunt, aut prave judicant. Eas autem personas maxime nominat Deus, quæ per se impote tes publici auxilii maxime egent. Vers. 30. STUPOR ET MIRABILIA FACTASVNT IN TERRA) Stupenda & horrenda. SACERDOTES APPLAUDEBANT MANIBVS SUIS Melius: sacerdotes dominabantur, (in populum sci- licet per illos: scilicet falsos prophetas, quorum opera ute- bantur. ET POPVLVS MEVS DILEXIT TALIA) Ita tra- ctari voluit. QVID IGITVR FIET IN NOVISSIMO EJVS) In Hebræo: Quid facietis posthac? id est, quo non evadet ista improbitas, nisi ego eam pœnis reprefsfero?

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

The arrival of enemies, whom one meets in vain, because of the impenitence of the people to be led away and severely punished: And their cruelty, because the Prophet tried in vain to purify the Jews like a goldsmith.

Vers. 1. BE STRENGTHENED O SONS OF BENJAMIN IN THE MIDST OF JERUSALEM) Better: Depart from the Jerusalemites, O Benjaminite. It is, however, a mockery toward the Benjaminites who lived in Jerusalem, that they should go to defend their fields and villages against the approaching enemy: for he wishes to signify that all these things will be vain and useless. AND IN THECOA BLOW THE TRUMPET) Which village was twelve miles distant from Jerusalem, as Jerome teaches us. AND OVER BETH-HACCHEREM LIFT UP A BANNER) In the Hebrew: a torch; namely, from which the arrival of the enemy was understood, a beacon. Beth-haccherem is another village situated on a mountain, looking toward that region through which the Chaldeans were to come: which is described here as if in a representation. Vers. 2. I HAVE LIKENED THE DAUGHTER OF SION TO A BEAUTIFUL AND DELICATE ONE) She will be like the best pasture land, where shepherds are accustomed to gather with great flocks. There is, however, a mockery here in the word 'shepherds,' such as in the word 'watchmen' above 4, 16.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Hostium adventus, quibus frustra occurritur, ob impœnitentia populi abducendi & gra- viter puniendi: Eorumque crudelitas, quia nequicquam purgare aurifabri instar, Ju- dæos Propheta conatus est.

Vers. 1. CONFORTAMINI FILII BENJAMIN IN MEDIO JERVSALEM) Melius: Excedite ex Hierosoly- mitis Benjaminita. Est autem χλευασμὸς ad Benjaminitas, qui Hierosolymis habitabant, ut agros suos & villas irent defensum contra hostem adventantem: significare enim vult omnia ista fore vana atque inutilia. ET IN THECVA CLANGITE BVCCINA) Qui vicus XII. millibus distabat ab Hierosolymis, ut nos docet Hieronymus. ET SVPER BETACHEREM LEVATE VEXILLVM) In Hebræo: facem; nempe ex qua intelligebatur adventus hostis, Φρυκτωρίαν. Est Betacherem vicus alter in monte po- situs, eam regionem spectans, per quam venturi erant Chal- dæi: quod hic velut in repræsente describitur. Vers 2. SPECIOSÆ ET DELICATÆ ASSIMVLA VI FILIAM SION) Similis erit optimæ terræ pascuæ, quo pastores cum magnis gregibus convenire solent. Est autem hic in voce pastorum χλευασμὸς, qualis in voce custodum supra 4, 16.

## 6:3
Vers. 3. EVERYONE SHALL FEED THOSE WHO ARE UNDER HIS HAND) In the Hebrew: His hand: that is, the flocks entrusted to him: namely, his own legions, wings, troops, cohorts.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PASCET VNVSQVISQVE EOS QVI SVB MANV SVA SVNT) In Hebræo: Manum suam: id est greges sibi creditos: suas nimirum legiones, alas, turmas, cohortes.

## 6:4
Vers. 4. SANCTIFY WAR AGAINST HER) What is called 'Sanctify' here, you may rightly translate 'prepare': for that verb often has that sense, although the translation is derived from the rites of the Temple. Moreover, understand 'war' here as a siege. The words are those of the Chaldeans exhorting one another.

LET US ASCEND AT NOON) He shows by these words how great was the eagerness of the Chaldeans to destroy the city.

WOE TO US BECAUSE THE DAY HAS DECLINED) They are indignant at the first arrival that they could not seize the city.

BECAUSE THE SHADOWS OF THE EVENING HAVE BECOME LONGER) Virgil likewise describing the evening: And longer shadows fall from the high mountains.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SANCTIFICATE SVPER EAM BELLUM) Quod hic Sanctificate dicitur, recte vertas præparate: nam eu sensum habet sœpe id verbū, quanquam à Templi ritibus deductã translatione. Bellum autem hic intellige oppugnationem. Verba sunt Chaldæorum se mutuo adhortantium.

ASCENDAMVS IN MERIDIE) Ostendit his verbis quanta fuerit Chaldæis aviditas exscindendæ urbis.

VÆ NOBIS QVIA DECLINAVIT DIES) Indignantur primo adventus de non potuisse rapi urbem.

QUIA LONGIORES FACTÆ SVNT VMBRÆ VESPERI) Virgilius itidem vesperam describens: Majoresque cadunt altis de montibus umbræ.

## 6:5
Vers. 5. LET US TEAR DOWN HIS HOUSES) Towers.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DISSIPEMVS DOMOS EJVS) Turres.

## 6:6
Vers. 6. FOR THUS SAITH THE LORD OF HOSTS) These things shall come to pass, because God willed these things to come to pass.

CUT DOWN HIS WOOD) For battering rams, ballistae, and other siege instruments.

CAST UP A MOUND AROUND JERUSALEM) That is, move a mound toward the city. Vegetius 4, 1. A mound, moreover, is raised from earth and wood against a wall, from which missiles are thrown.

THIS IS THE CITY OF VISITATION) In the Hebrew: visited: that is, from which vengeance is taken.

ALL OPPRESSION IN THE MIDST OF IT) Better: how great soever the violence is in it: supply, is seen.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QVIA HÆC DICET DOMINVS EXERCITVVM) Fient hæc, quia Deus fieri hæc voluit.

CÆDITE LIGNVM EJVS) Ad arietes, ballistas, aliaque oppugnandi instrumenta.

FVNDITE CIRCA JERVSALEM AGGEREM) Id est admovete urbi aggerem. Vegetius 4, 1. Agger autem ex terra lignis que attollitur contra murum, de quo tela jactantur.

HÆC EST CIVITAS VISITATIONIS) In Hebræo: visitata: id est, de qua ultio sumitur.

OMNIS CALVMNIA IN MEDIO EJVS) Melius: quanta quanta est violentia in ea: supple conspicitur.

## 6:7
V. 7. AS A CISTERN HATH MADE COLD ITS WATER: SO HATH SHE MADE COLD HER MALICE) He followed the Greeks, who derive הקרה from קרר. But the truer version: As the water of a well springs forth, so their malice always grows anew.

BEFORE ME ALWAYS INFIRMITY AND THE PLAGUE) That is, these things shall be rendered by me to them for iniquity and plunder.

Latin:

V. 7. SICVT FRIGIDAM FECIT CISTERNA AQVAM SVAM: SIC FRIGIDAM FECIT MALITIAM SVAM) Secutus est Græcos, qui הקרה à קרר derivant. At verior versio: Sicut putei aqua scaturit illorum malitia, nova semper succrescit.

CORAM ME SEMPER INFIRMITAS ET PLAGA) Id est, hæc à me ipsis reddentur pro iniquitate ac direptione.

## 6:8
Vers. 8. LEST PERCHANCE MY SOUL DEPART FROM THEE) Lest I cast thee off entirely, as the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NE FORTE RECEDAT ANIMA MEA A TE) Ne te plane abjiciam, ut hic Chaldæus.

## 6:9
Vers. 9. EVEN UNTO THE GRAPE) They shall make a gleaning, that is, they shall leave nothing on the earth.

TURN THY HAND AS A GRAPE-GATHERER TO THE BASKET) Here one must understand them saying: bring back thy hand again, as a grape-gatherer carrying a basket. That is, the Chaldeans will come twice or thrice, to see if even a little remains that could be carried away. See below 52, 58.

Latin:

Vers. 9. VSQVE AD RACEMVM COLLIGENT) Racemationem facient, id est nil in terra relinquent.

CONVERTE MANUM TVAM SICVT VINDEMIATOR AD CARTALLVM) Hic subintelligendum dicentes: iterum manum tuam refer, ut vindemiator gerens cartallum. Id est, bis terve venient Chaldæi, ut videant, si quid vel exiguū restet, quod auferri posset. Vide infra 52, 58

## 6:10
Vers. 10. THEIR EARS ARE UNCIRCUMCISED) Stopped up with filth.

Latin:

Vers. 10. INCIRCVMCISÆ AVRES EORVM) Sordibus obturatæ.

## 6:11
V. 11. THEREFORE I AM FULL OF THE FURY OF THE LORD) I feel within myself how grievously God is angry at these.

I HAVE LABORED HOLDING IN) I can no longer contain that feeling within myself.

POUR OUT UPON THE CHILD OUTSIDE) In the Hebrew: to pour out: that is, that I might not refrain from pouring out this feeling of mine, by denouncing most grievous evils upon his age, sex, and rank. That word 'outside' in the Hebrew signifies in the street. For children are accustomed to run out into the streets.

UPON THE COUNSEL OF THE YOUNG TOGETHER) Upon the companies of the young.

THE OLD MAN WITH THE FULL OF DAYS) He calls the aging man old here.

Latin:

V. 11. ICCIRCO FVMO DOMINI PLENVS SVM) Sentio intra meipsum, quam graviter his Deus succenseat.

LABORAVI SUSTINENS) Sensum illum non diutius intra me continere possum.

EFFVNDE SVPER PARVULUM FORIS) In Hebræo: effundere: id est, quo minus hunc sensum meum effundam, gravissima mala ætati, sexui, atque ordini denunciando. Illud foris in Hebræo significat in platea. Solent enim pueri in plateas excurrere.

SVPER CONSILIVM JUVENUM SIMVL) Super juvenum choros.

SENEX CVM PLENO DIERVM) Senem hic vocat senescentem.

## 6:14
Vers. 14. AND THEY SHALL HEAL THE CONTRITION OF MY PEOPLE WITH IGNOMINY.) In the Hebrew: upon the light: that is, as if it were a very light matter. Contrition: that is, a wound.

SAYING, PEACE) That is, it will heal immediately.

AND THERE WAS NO PEACE) It was not healing.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET CVRABVNT CONTRITIONEM POPVLI MEI CVM IGNOMINIA.) In Hebræo: super levi: id est, quasi res esset levissima. Contritionem: id est, vulnus.

DICENDO, PAX) Id est, jamjam sanescet.

ET NON ERAT PAX) Non sanescebat.

## 6:15
Vers. 15. NAY RATHER THEY ARE NOT CONFOUNDED WITH CONFUSION) This is an ἐπανόρθωσις; why do I say they are put to shame? Nay, no sense of shame remains in them.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QVIN POTIVS CONFVSIONE NON SVNT CONFVSI) Est ἐπανόρθωσις, quid dico eos pudefactos? imo pudoris nihil illis restat.

## 6:16
Vers. 16. THUS SAITH THE LORD) The Lord was accustomed to say these things.

STAND UPON THE WAYS, AND SEE, AND ASK) Do as travelers are accustomed to do when they are in doubt as to which way they should go.

OF THE ANCIENT PATHS) Through which Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob went.

YOU SHALL FIND REST FOR YOUR SOULS) Rest. The Chaldean: The Greeks ἁγιασμὸν, that is, forgiveness of sins.

Latin:

Vers. 16. HÆC DICIT DOMINVS) Hæc dicere Dominus solebat.

STATE SVPER VIAS, ET VIDETE, ET IN-TERROGATE) Facite ut viatores solent, ubi dubitant, qua eundum sit.

DE SEMITIS ANTIQVIS) Per quas iverunt Abraham, Isaac, Jacob.

INVENIETIS REFRIGERIUM ANIMABVS VESTRIS) Requiem. Chaldæus: Græci ἁγιασμὸν, id est, criminam veniam.

## 6:17
Ver. 17. WATCHMEN) Prophets. Isaiah 57, 2. Ezek. 3, 17. 33, 2. 6. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SPECVLATORES) Prophetas. Esaias 57, 2. Ezech. 3, 17. 33, 2. 6. 7.

## 6:19
Ver. 19. HEAR O EARTH) The whole human race.

THE FRUIT OF HIS THOUGHTS) They shall suffer things equal to those which they did to others. Prov. 1, 31. Ps. 28, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 19. AVDI TERRA) Omne genus humanum.

FRVCTVM COGITATIONVM EJVS) Sentient paria iis, quæ in alios fecere. Prov. 1, 31. Ps. 28, 4.

## 6:20
Ver. 20. TO WHAT PURPOSE DO YOU BRING ME INCENSE FROM SABA) Virgil: The soft Sabaeans their incense. Compare what is in Isaiah 1, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 20. VT QVID MIHI THVS DE SABA AD-FERTIS) Virgilius: Molles sua thura Sabæi. Confer quæ apud Esaiam 1, 11.

## 6:21
RUINS) Spikes or mules. Verse 23. HE WILL SEIZE THE ARROW AND THE SHIELD τόξον & σιβύνην, the Greeks. In the Glosses σιβύνη, a hunting spear. Polybius & Diodorus take it for a spear-shaft; כידון which is here in the Hebrew, is elsewhere translated γαῖσον, elsewhere ἐγχειρίδιον HE IS CRUEL AND WILL NOT HAVE PITY) Similar to Isaiah 13, 17. 18. PREPARED AS A MAN OF WAR) The whole army will be moved as easily as one man. Verse 24. WE HAVE HEARD THE FAME OF IT, YOUR HANDS ARE LOOSENED) He says 'ours' for the Jews', because the Prophet himself is also from that nation. At the first rumor, the spirit of all the Jews will collapse. Verse 25. DO NOT GO OUT TO THE FIELDS) It will be of no use to go out of the city, death is everywhere. MOURNING FOR AN ONLY SON) Such as a mother weeps for an only child who has been killed. Thus also Amos 8, 10. & Zach. 12, 10. Verse 27. I HAVE GIVEN YOU AS A PROVER TO MY PEOPLE, A ROBUST ONE: AND YOU SHALL KNOW AND PROVE THEIR WAY) More correctly with Symmachus & Theodotion: I have placed you as a fortress or a most fortified place among my people: that is, proceed constantly. I will protect you like a most fortified fortress, nor will it be difficult for you, established as if on high, to explore what each one is doing. The noun בחון ἅπαξ λεγόμενον signifies a prover, or a lookout and explorer: בחן he proved, he explored Ps. 17, 3. Ps. 139. 36. Jer. 9, 7. Zach. 13. v. last. But מבחן is a fortification. Therefore these words are not to be confused. And so Grotius wrongly prefers the version of Symmachus & Theodotion here, which however Pagninus, Arias Montanus, and Isidorus have also followed, with Tremellius not dissenting, who rendered it an exploratory watchtower, or Piscator, who explained it as a tower, by comparing the place c. 1, 18. as a parallel. Jerome's translation is to be preferred: to which Vatablus's is akin: I have given you as a refiner, & the Syriac as a searcher I have made you, and the Arabic, I have made you, that you may search. Which most understand concerning the scrutiny and office of the Prophet: who ought to have searched and explored the people: others concerning the penal exploration of the King of Babylon, whom they judge to have been appointed as an explorer by the force of similar places Jer. 9, 2. Ez. 20, 38. c. 21, 18. Zach. 13, 9. But since God is addressing the Prophet, not the King of Babylon, of whom there is no trace in this address, it is better to understand it concerning prophetic exploration and probation. Therefore Jerome: A robust prover is given to the Prophet for the incredulous people, which in Hebrew is called מבצר which sounds either fortified according to Aquila, or closed and surrounded according to Symmachus and the Septuagint, like a most firm city: so that he may fear no snares of the people: and when you have proved, he says, and known the way of the delinquent people, then you may understand that silver mixed with copper cannot be purified by any reason. For how is lead mixed with metals that have been adulterated and violated, so that the foreign material may be separated; and if by chance it has not been purified, all the lead is consumed and reduced to nothing: so every utterance of doctrines and prophetic speech perishes in those who disdain to listen. Verse 28. PRINCES DECLINING) Better, most contumacious defectors. COPPER AND IRON) They have nothing of silver, let alone gold. It is known what Hesiod and Ovid said about the ages and what Plato said about the various temperaments of souls related to metals. Verse 29. THE BELLOWS HAVE FAILED IN THE FIRE) The bellows are torn by blowing. THE LEAD IS CONSUMED) With which they were then burned for the purification of metals, the power of quicksilver not yet being known. IN VAIN THE MELTER HAS MELTED) So that he might extract some silver from it. FOR THEIR MALICIES ARE NOT CONSUMED) In the Hebrew: And their malicies are not consumed. By so many evils, which the Assyrians and Egyptians had brought upon them, they were made no better. The words of comparison and the thing compared are mixed, as often. Verse 30. REPROBATE SILVER CALL THEM) They sell themselves for silver; but the exploration through fire shows that the appearance was of silver, not the reality.

Latin:

RUINAS) Murices vel mulos. Vers 23. SAGITTAM ET SCUTUM ARRIPIET τόξον & σιβύνην, Græci. In Glossis σιβύνη, venabulum. Pro hastili sumunt Polybius & Diodorus; כידון quod hic in Hebræo est, alibi vertitur γαῖσον, alibi ἐγχειρίδιον CRUDELIS EST ET NON MISEREBITUR) Si mile Esaïæ 13, 17. 18. PRÆPARATI QUASI VIR PRÆLIANS) Tam facile totus exercitus movebitur quam vir unus. Vers. 24. AUDIVIMUS FAMAM EJUS, DISSO- LUTÆ SUNT MANUS VESTRÆ) Nostræ dicit pro Ju- dæorum, quia & ipse Propheta ex ea gente. Ad primum rumorem Judæis omnibus concidet animus. Vers. 25. NOLITE EXIRE AD AGROS) Nihil pro- derit exire de urbe, mors ubique. LUCTUM UNIGENITI) Qualis peremtum quæ flet unicum mater. Sic & Amos 8, 10. & Zach. 12, 10. Vers. 27. PROBATOREM DEDI TE IN POPU- LO MEO ROBUSTUM: ET SCIES ET PROBABIS VIAM EORUM) Rectius cum Symmacho & Theodo- tione: ut arcem aut munitissimum locum posui te in populo meo: id est, perge constanter. Ego te protegam ut arcem muni- tissimam, nec difficile tibi erit, velut in sublimi constituto, explorare quid agant singuli. NOmen בחון ἅπαξ λεγόμενον probatorem si- gnificat, vel speculatorem & exploratorem: בחן probavit, exploravit Ps. 17,3. Ps. 139. 36. Jer. 9, 7. Zach. 13. v. ult. מבחן vero munitio est. Non ergo confundendæ hæ voces. Ideoq; perperam Symma- chi & Theodotionis versionem hic præfert Grotius, quam tamen sequuti etiam sunt Pagninus, Aria- montanus, Isidorus, non abnuente Tremellio, qui reddidit exploratoriam speculam, vel Piscatore, qui exposuit turrim, conferendo locum c. 1, 18. ceu pa- rallelum. Præferenda Hieronymi translatio: cui ge- mina est Vatabli: Excoctorem te dedi, & Syriaca scru- tatorem te feci, atque Arabica, feci te, ut scruteris. Quod pleriq; de scrutinio & munere Prophetæ in- telligunt: qui scrutari populum & explorare de- buerit: alii de exploratione pœnali Regis Babylonici quem exploratorem constitutum censent vi loco rum similium Ier. 9, 2. Ez. 20, 38. c. 21, 18. Zach. 13, 9. Sed quum alloquatur Deus Prophetam, non Re gem Babylonicum, cujus nullum in hac compella- tione vestigium, de prophetica exploratione & pro batione intelligere præstat. Ideo Hieronymus: Datur Prophetæ populo incredulo robustus probator quod Hebraice dicitur מבצר quod vel munitum juxta Aquilam, vel clausum atq; circumdatum juxta Symmachum & Septuaginta sonat, instar urbis fir- missimæ: ut nullas populi pertimescat insidias: & cum probaveris, ait, & scieris viam populi delinquen- tis, tunc intelligas argentum commixtum ære nulla ratione posse purgari. Quomodo enim plumbum mi- scetur metallis, quæ adulterata sunt atq; violata, ut materia separetur aliena; & si forsitan purgata non fuerit, plumbum omne consumitur & in nihilum re- digitur: ita omne eloquium doctrinarum & sermo propheticus perit, in his qui audire contemnunt. Vers. 28. PRINCIPES DECLINANTES) Melius defectores contumacissimi. ÆS ET FERRUM) Nihil de argento habent, ne- dum de auro. Notum quid Hesiodus & Ovidius de ætati- bus dixerint & de variis animorum temperaturis ad metalla relatis, Plato. Vers. 29. DEFECIT SUFFLATORIUM IN IGNE) Folles disrupti sunt flando. CONSUMPTUM EST PLUMBUM) Quo tunc urebantur ad metallorum purgationes, nondum cognita vi argenti vivi. FRUSTRA CONFLAVIT CONFLATOR) Ut aliquid argenti inde eliceret. MALITIÆ ENIM EORUM NON SUNT CON- SUMTÆ) In Hebræo: Et malitiæ eorum non sunt consum- tæ. Tot malis, quæ Assyrii Ægyptiiq; intulerant, nihilo me- liores facti sunt. Miscentur voces comparationis, & rei comparatæ ut sæpe. Vers. 30. ARGENTUM REPROBATUM VOCA- TE EOS) Pro Argento se venditant; sed exploratio per ignem ostendit speciem fuisse argenti non rem.

## 7:1 Argument
SERMON II. DELIVERED AT THE GATE OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD. CHAPTER VII.

The vain confidence of the impenitent in the temple, which is to be cast away, and the land to be reduced to a wilderness: nor will the intercession of Jeremiah be of any use, nor sacrifices because of the high places of Topheth and their contumacy.

Latin:

CONCIO II. IN PORTA DOMUS DOMI- NI HABITA. CAPUT VII.

Vana impœnitentium confidentia in templo, quod abjiciendum, ac terra redigenda in solitudinem: nec profutura intercessio Je- remiæ, neq; sacrificia propter excelsa To- pheth & contumaciam.

## 7:2
V. 2. STAND IN THE GATE OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) Namely, that through which the people entered to the great open-air court.

YOU WHO ENTER THROUGH THESE GATES, TO WORSHIP THE LORD) That you may bow yourselves to the Lord.

Latin:

V. 2. STA IN PORTA DOMVS DOMINI) Illa nempe per quam populus ingrediebatur ad sobdiale maximum.

QUI INGREDIMINI PER PORTAS HAS, VT ADORETIS DOMINUM) Vt vos incurvetis Domino.

## 7:3
Verse 3. AND I WILL DWELL WITH YOU IN THIS PLACE) In the Hebrew: And I will make you dwell in this place. I will make it so that you do not migrate, as is understood in the following.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET HABITABO VOBISCUM IN LOCO ISTO) In Hebræo: Et faciam habitare vos in loco isto. FAcian ne migretis, ut intelligitur in sequentibus.

## 7:4
Verse 4. DO NOT TRUST IN LYING WORDS) The lie of the prophets, such as are all those who hold rituals as the most important things.

SAYING) Of those saying.

THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD, THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD, THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) In the Hebrew, 'are' is added. Thus, a singular noun is often constructed with a plural noun because of the parts of the thing, such as there were three in the Temple: אולם, היכל, which is also דביר & קדש. The sense here is the same as that which Stephen attacks in Acts 7, and which the Chaldean well explains here. This Temple was built by the command of God through Solomon, appearing there three times a year, you bow down, you offer victims. How could it be that God would not regard this place and worship, even if other things were going badly? A grave error, and one which most distinguishes Pseudo-Prophets from prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 4. NOLITE CONFIDERE IN VERBIS MEN- DACH) Prophetarum mendacium, quales sunt omnes, qui ritualia pro præcipuis habent.

DICENTES) Dicentium.

TEMPLUM DOMINI, TEMPLUM DOMINI, TEMPLUM DOMINI) In Hebræo additur sunt. Ita sæpe nomen singulare construitur cum nomine plurali ob rei partes, quales in Templo erant tres אולם, היכל, quod & דביר & קדש. Sensus hic idem est, quem oppugnat Stephanus Act. 7. & quem bene hic explicat Chaldæus. Templum hoc Dei imperio structum fuit per Solomonem, ibi ter anno apparens, procumbitis, offertis victimas. Quomodo fieri posset ut Deus locum hunc cultumq; non respiciat, etiamsi cætera male habeant? Gravis error, & qui vel maxime Pseudo-Prophetas à prophetis distinguit.

## 7:5
Vers. 5. FOR IF YOU HAVE AMENDED YOUR WAYS) Which he soon explains through three excellent parts: justice, goodness, and piety.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUONIAM SI BENEDIXERITIS VIAS VESTRAS) Quod mox per tres partes eximias explicat, justitiæ, bonitatis ac pietatis.

## 7:7
Vers. 7. I WILL DWELL WITH YOU) I will make you dwell. As above in 3.

WHICH I GAVE TO YOUR FATHERS FROM ETERNITY EVEN TO ETERNITY) That is, from the times of Joshua to those times in which the Prophet was speaking these things.

Latin:

Vers. 7. HABITABO VOBISCUM) Habitare vos faciam. Ut supra 3.

QVAM DEDI PATRIBVS VESTRIS A SECV- LO VSQVE IN SECULUM) Id est, ab Josuæ temporibus, ad ea tempora, quibus hæc loquebatur Propheta.

## 7:8
Vers. 8. YOU TRUST IN WORDS OF FALSEHOOD) In those sayings of the Pseudo-prophets flattering you.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CONFIDITIS VOBIS IN SERMONIBVS MENDACII) In illis dictis Pseudo prophetarum vobis blandientium.

## 7:9
Vers. 9. TO STEAL) Or by stealing. Thus also the following infinitives are for gerunds, which the Hebrews do not have. See how the excellent Prophet, rebuking sins, does not name the eating of forbidden food through ignorance, nor parsimony in victims, nor omitted minor washings, but thefts, murders, adulteries, perjuries, false Gods. Certainly all the Prophets are excellent guides to the Gospel.

Latin:

Vers. 9. FURARI) An furando. Sic & sequentia infinitiva sunt pro gerundiis, quæ Hebræi non habent. Vide ut egregius Propheta peccata reprehendens, nominet non manducationem per ignorantiam cibi vetiti, non parsinioniam in victimis, omissas lotiunculas, sed furta, homicidia, adulteria, perjuria, Deos falsos. Certe Prophetæ omnes egregii ad Evangelium duces.

## 7:10
Vers. 10. AND YOU CAME) Meanwhile you came. For the discourse coheres with the preceding.

WE ARE DELIVERED BECAUSE WE HAVE DONE ALL THESE ABOMINATIONS) You would translate it more correctly as, 'although we have done.' We are delivered through victims and washings. Thus, little by little, paganism had insinuated itself into Judaism: by which it was the more necessary that all those things by which such errors could be nourished be abolished through the Gospel.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET VENISTIS) Interim venistis. Cohæret enim oratio cum superioribus.

LIBERATI SVMVS EO QVOD FECERIMVS OMNES ABOMINATIONES ISTAS) Rectius verteris, quamvis fecerimus. Liberati sumus per victimas & lotiones. Sic paulatim in Judaismum insinuaverat se paganismus: quo magis necessarium fuit omnia ea per Evangelium aboleri, quibus errores tales nutriri poterant.

## 7:11
Vers. 11. IS THIS HOUSE THEREFORE BECOME A DEN OF ROBBERS.) That is, shall I allow that, just as dens are for robbers as a refuge, so my temple should defend you against all crimes? Certainly I will not.

I AM, I HAVE SEEN) There is nothing that is hidden from me.

Latin:

Vers. 11. NUMQUID ERGO SPELUNCA LATRO- NVM FACTA EST DOMVS ISTA.) Id est, patiarne ego, ut sicut speluncæ latronibus sunt pro perfugio, ita templum meum vos contra omnia scelera defendat. Certe non faciam.

EGO SUM, EGO VIDI) Nihil est, quod mihi lateat.

## 7:12
Vers. 12. GO GO TO THE PLACE OF SHILOH, WHERE MY NAME DWELT FROM THE BEGINNING) Immediately after the entry into the promised land. An excellent argument, which Stephen also uses in Acts 7:45, to prove that God's benevolence is not bound to a place. For formerly the Tabernacle and the Ark were in place of the Temple.

SEE WHAT I HAVE DONE TO IT BECAUSE OF THE MALICE OF MY PEOPLE ISRAEL) Namely, I have despised those things which they think are the greatest to such an extent that I allowed the very ark to be captured by enemies because of their sins. Psalm 78:60, 61. 1 Samuel 4.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ITE ITE AD LOCUM SILO, UBI HABI- TAVIT NOMEN MEUM A PRINCIPIO) Statim post ingressum terræ promissæ. Egregium argumentum, quo & Stephanus utitur Act. 7, 45. ut probet Dei benevolentiam loco non adstringi. Nam olim Tabernaculum & Arca erant vice Templi.

VIDETE QUÆ FECERIM EI PROPTER MA- LITIAM POPULI MEI ISRAEL) Nempe eo usq; ista, quæ illi putant maxima, contempsi, ut ipsa arca propter peccata ipsorum siverim capi ab hostibus. Psal. 78, 60. 61. 1. Sam. 4.

## 7:14
Verse 14. I WILL DO TO THIS HOUSE) To the Temple, which is nothing but a house.

AS I DID TO SHILOH) Which place having been neglected, I fixed a Temple for myself elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers 14. FACIAM DOMUI HUIC) Templo, quæ nihil est nisi domus.

SICUT FECI SILO) Quo loco posthabito, fixi mihi Templum alibi.

## 7:15
Verse 15. AS I CAST OFF ALL YOUR BRETHREN, THE WHOLE SEED OF EPHRAIM) Thus by synecdoche the people of the ten tribes is called, because it had kings from the stock of Ephraim.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SICUT PROJECI OMNES FRATRES VE- STROS, UNIVERSUM SEMEN EPHRAIM) Sic per συνεκδοχὴν vocatur decem tribuum populus, quod Reges habuerit ex Ephraim stirpe.

## 7:16
Verse 16. THEREFORE DO NOT PRAY FOR THE PEOPLE

HOC) For the people, that is, who remain stubbornly in their sins.

AND DO NOT OPPOSE ME] A manner of speaking by which the efficacy of prayer is signified. Ex. 32, 10. Ps. 106, 30. Num. 16, 47.

Latin:

Vers. 16. TU ERGO NOLI ORARE PRO POPULO

HOC) Pro populo scilicet in suis peccatis contumaciter permanente.

ET NON OBSISTAS MIHI] Loquendi genus, quo pre- cis efficacia significatur. Ex. 32, 10. Pf. 106, 30. Num. 16, 47.

## 7:18
Verse 18. THE CHILDREN GATHER WOOD] No age, no sex is free from the worship of idols.

AND THE WOMEN KNEAD THE DOUGH] They knead the mass, the Chaldean: τρέχουσι σάις, that is, they soak the flour with water and knead it.

TO MAKE CAKES] πόπανα, as Chrysostom interprets: πέμματα as Olympiodorus and the LXX. They retained the Hebrew word χαυῶνας. That word is in the Etymologicum and Suidas; Solomon Jarchi adds, which I think is true, that in those cakes there were little images of the gods.

QUEEN OF HEAVEN] The moon, which was called כוכת by those nations, Βᾶλτις according to Abydenus in the place which we produced in the Annotations to Book 3 on the truth of the Christian Religion. The same name is written Βαάλτις according to Philo of Byblos.

AND POUR OUT DRINK OFFERINGS TO STRANGE GODS] Wine, that is, which is יין הגוים, libations to the Greeks.

Latin:

Verf. 18. FILII COLLIGUNT LIGNA] Nulla ætas, nullus sexus ab idolorum cultu vacat.

ET MULIERES CONSPERGUNT ADIPEM] Conspergunt massam, Chaldæus: τρέχουσι σάις, id est farinam aqua macerant ac depsunt.

UT FACIANT PLACENTAS] πόπανα, ut Chry- sostomus interpretatur: πέμματα ut Olympiodorus LXX. Hæbræam vocem retinuere χαυῶνας. Est vox ea apud Ety- mologicum & Suidam; Salomon Jarchi addit, quod verum puto, in illis libis fuisse deorum icunculas.

REGINÆ CŒLI] Lunæ, quæ כוכת dicebatur illis gentibus, Βᾶλτις apud Abydenû loco quem produximus An- notatis ad Librum 3. de veritate Religionis Christianæ. Ef- idem nomen scriptû Βαάλτις apud Philonem Byblium.

ET LIBENT DIIS ALIENIS] Vinum scilicet quod יין הגוים σπονδὰς Græcis.

## 7:19
Verse 19. DO THEY PROVOKE ME TO ANGER?] That is, do they hope that they will harm me? All that will fall back upon themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 19. NUMQUID ME AD IRACUNDIAM PRO- VOCANT?] Id est, an sperant se mihi nocituros? omnis ista in ipsos recident.

## 7:20
Verse 20. UPON THE MEN, AND UPON THE BEASTS AND UPON THE WOOD OF THE REGION] It is a metonymy, the cause for the effect. The sense is, I wish all those things to be consumed.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SUPER VIROS, ET SUPER JUMENTA ET SUPER LIGNUM REGIONIS] Est μετωνυμία, cau- sa pro effectu. Sensus est, omnia ista consumi volo.

## 7:21
Verse 21. YOUR BURNT OFFERINGS] Which were burned whole, Levit. 1.

ADD TO YOUR VICTIMS] Whether they are offered for obtaining benefits, or for giving thanks or praises, or for expiating a crime or fault. See what we have said regarding Leviticus.

Latin:

Vers. 21. HOLOCAUTOMATA VESTRA] Quæ solida urebantur, Levit. 1.

ADDITE VICTIMIS VESTRIS] Sive illæ pro bene- ficiis impetrandis, sive pro gratiis laudibusve agendis, sive pro crimine culpave expianda offeruntur. Vide quæ ad Leviticum diximus.

## 7:22
V. 22. I DID NOT SPEAK WITH YOUR FATHERS AND I DID NOT COMMAND THEM IN THE DAY THAT I BROUGHT THEM OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT, CONCERNING THE MATTER OF BURNT OFFERINGS AND VICTIMS] Note, in the day, that is, at the time, when first the voice said I brought them out of Egypt. If I did such great goods for you before I had brought any law concerning those burnt offerings or victims, even from this I know you could understand that those things are not cared for by me. It was indeed an ancient custom that such things were done, but it proceeded from human ingenuity, as we have shown the ancients thought in the Annotations to Book 4 for the Christian Religion. Long after, the law was brought in, when the worship of the calf showed that they needed such restraints. The reason for the Passover is different: for that was a feast more than a sacrifice.

Latin:

V. 22. NON LOCUTUS SUM CUM PATRIBUS VE- STRIS ET NON PRÆCEPI EIS IN DIE QVA EDUXI EOS DE TERRA ÆGYPTI, DE VERBO HOLOCAU- TOMATUM ET VICTIMARUM] Nota, in die, id est in tempore, cum primum vox ex Ægypto eduxi. Si tanta vobis bona feci, priusquam legem ullam tulissem de holo- caustis illis vel victimis, vel ex hoc scio intelligere poteratis non ista a me curari. Mos quidem erat vetustus, ut talia fie- rent, sed ab humano ingenio profectus, ut ostendimus sen- sisse veteres in Annotatis ad Librum 4. pro Religione Chri- stiana. Multo post lex lata est, cum cultus vituli ostendit illos talibus frænis egere. Paschatis alia est ratio : id enim convivium magis erat quam sacrificium.

## 7:23
Vers. 23. BUT THIS WORD I COMMANDED THEM SAYING: HEAR MY VOICE, AND I WILL BE YOUR GOD, AND YOU SHALL BE MY PEOPLE: AND WALK IN EVERY WAY, WHICH I HAVE COMMANDED YOU, THAT IT MAY BE WELL WITH YOU] I commanded those departing only those things which are honest in themselves. The same matter is in other words in Exod. 15, 26, where see what we have noted.

Sacrifices were not devised by human ingenuity, but instituted divinely, nor were they first in use among the gentiles, or those destitute of God, but among the faithful taught by God, since the faithful offered sacrifices under the very infancy of the Church after the fall, as witnessed by the example of Abel, whom the Holy Spirit teaches in Heb. 11 to have offered sacrifice through faith. It is therefore false, what is suggested for the sake of Papists and Socinians, as if God had indulged sacrifices to the people by accident, inclined as they were to such rites devised by the gentiles, when it is certain that God instituted the same by Himself, and that the Patriarchs offered sacrifices relying on nothing but the word of God; because faith and the word of God are related, nor could they have been offered by faith if they had been destitute of the word of God. And what is more evident than that God commanded sacrifices, and defined them by certain laws, as can be seen in Ex. 37 et seqq. and especially in Leviticus. Therefore, as to the present passage, it is in vain that Isidore and Cajetan distinguish between counsel and precept, that God indeed instituted sacrifices, but only under the aspect of counsel. Because sacrifices were sanctioned in a similar form as other precepts, and are called precepts in Matt. 8. 5. Nor should this be conceded to the Pontifical interpreters Gislerius, Cornelius, and Castro, along with Grotius, as if they were erected only on the occasion of the calf, and God admitted them through connivance, and not indeed from a just purpose, nor immediately on that day on which He led the people out of Egypt. For that is opposed both to the first calling of Moses, where mention of sacrifices was made immediately by the Angel in the bush, Ex. 3. 12, and the dismissal of the people for the sake of sacrifices was commanded v. 18, and to the order of the precepts, since before the μοσχολατρεία [calf-worship] described in Ex. 32, they were already commanded in c. 20, 24 and c. 27. sacrifices had already been demanded (even if the promulgation of those laws followed only afterwards), whence the μοσχολατρεία [calf-worship] cannot be held as the occasion for the sanctioning of sacrifices; and then finally to the proper and principal end of sacrifices, which was symbolic and typical of foreshadowing the expiatory sacrifice of Christ. And this is what God testifies here, namely that He did not command such sacrifices, or to that end, as those which the Israelites offered, and to what end they offered them; He did not sanction them as expiatory and meritorious in themselves, but as typical and representative of the unique expiatory sacrifice, and therefore salutary not by the work performed [opere operato], as they love to speak barbarously, but when they are offered with true faith, which is not idle, but active through love. Let Col. 2, 17 and Heb. 10, 1 et seqq. be compared. Whence God did not require naked sacrifices, as the Jews would think, but those which are offered through faith. Not that external worship without the interior, but primarily the interior worship, in which faith holds the primacy, to be excited, fostered, declared, and publicly manifested by this external worship. For which reason God here requires obedience and observance of His word and commandments v. 27. He does not want, says Augustine lib. 10 de civ. Dei c. 5, the sacrifice of a slaughtered beast, but He wants the sacrifice of a contrite heart. Thus, therefore, He said that He did not want those things, in the way that they are believed by the foolish to be wanted by Him, as if for the pleasure of His own grace. To which also pertain those things of Jerome in this place: Whose temple He rejected, consequently He also rejects the sacrifices: and He obliquely argues against them, that they offer victims not out of veneration for Him, but out of a desire for feasts. Cf. Iren. l. 4 c. 32.

What Grotius brought forward in l. 5 de verit. Relig. Christ. c. 8, to prove that sacrifices were devised by human ingenuity before they were commanded by God, does not prove it. For in Is. 2 this sentiment is not rejected, that sacrifices offered by true faith are pleasing to God and a true part of piety: and those from among the Hebrews, as Grotius admits, are correct who say that it is directed against those who offered sacrifices with an impure mind and life. For even if God addresses His own people, and the pious ones there, yet the words themselves teach that God desired something even in them. From these, however, Grotius rashly tries to conclude that sacrifices had nothing in themselves pleasing to God. If he understands that IN THEMSELVES without relation to the sacrifice of the Messiah, we concede it: but because he thinks that sacrifices devised by human ingenuity were permitted or enjoined by God only for the reason that they might not return to the worship of false gods out of a love for gentile sacrifices, being destitute of sacrifices, or out of the memory of their sojourn in Egypt, as he speaks, this is by no means to be admitted, nor could such a thing be extracted from this Psalm, or from other places Ps. 40, Ps. 51, Is. 1, Hos. 6, Mic. 6, where sacrifices are treated, or from the present text. Nor do they deserve to be heard in this, even with the Jew Maimonides as a guide, l. 3 c. 32, or Tertullian advers. Marcion. 2, when they bring forward such a cause for sacrifices, which is alien to the sacred scriptures, nay, contrary to them. For where is it read in the Scriptures that God wished to bind His people, prone to idolatry and transgression, to such religious duties by which the superstition of the age was conducted, in order to call them away from it, commanding them to be done to Himself as if He were desiring them, so that they would not sin by making idols; which Tertullian asserted in the cited place? Does not Scripture rather teach that God instituted sacrifices for the mystery of the satisfaction of Christ, to be foreshadowed to the ancient people, of which the gentiles knew nothing, whence the rite of sacrifices passed not from the gentiles to the people of God, but from the people of God to the gentiles, through their zeal without knowledge [κακοζηλίαν], and the all-wickedness [πανσεγίαν] of the Devil, who thus wished to mock the sacrifice of CHRIST.

What the author of the Questions ascribed to Justin, Quest. 83, and Chrysostom, 12, on the statues, say about sacrifices offered before the law by Abel and other saints without God's command, does not agree with the testimony of the Apostles in Heb. 11, which teaches that they were offered through faith, even before the law. For faith has no place without the word of God, which is the basis, foundation, principle, rule, and norm of faith. If Abel offered through faith, as the Holy Scripture testifies, then it was not through an instinct of nature, nor without the word of God. And since sacrifices had the shadow of Christ, how could they have been offered by an instinct of nature? For in nature there is not even an obscure shadow of Christ. Finally, nothing at all can be brought from nature for the cult of sacrifices, but rather it seems absurd to reason to worship the invisible God with victims and sacrifices.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SED HOC VERBUM PRÆCEPI EIS DI- CENS: AUDITE VOCEM MEAM, ET ERO VOBIS DEUS, ET VOS ERITIS MIHI POPULUS: ET AM- BULATE IN OMNI VIA, QUAM MANDAVI VO- BIS, UT BENE SIT VOBIS] Ea tantum præcepi exeun- tibus, quæ per se honesta sunt. Res eadem verb s aliis est Exod. 15, 26. ubi quæ notavimus vide.

SAcrificia non sunt humano ingenio excogitata, sed divinitus instituta, nec primum apud genti- les, seu Dei expertes, sed penes fideles à Deo edo- ctos in usu fuere, fiquidem sub ipsa Ecclesiæ post lapsum incunabula sacrificia obtulerint fideles, te- ste exemplo Abel s, quem per fidem obtulisse sacri- ficium Spiritus S. docet Ebr. 11. Falsum ergo est, quod in gratiam Papistarum & Socinianorum inge- ritur, ac si sacrificia Deus per accidens indulsérit po- pulo, ad ejusmodi ritus à gentilibus excogitatos propenso, quum eadem Deum per sefe instituisse, nec nisi verbo Dei nixos sacrificia obtulisse Patriar- chas, certum sit; quia fides & verbum Dei relata sunt, nec fide offerri potuissent, si verbo Dei desti- tuta fuissent. Et quid evidentius, quam quod Deus præceperit sacrificia, eaq; certis legibus definive- rit, uti Ex. 37. seqq. & imprimis in Levitico videre est. Quod ergo ad præsentem locum, frustra est Isi- dorus & Cajetanus inter consilium & præceptum di- stinguens, q. Deus instituerit quidem sacrificia, sed solum sub ratione consilii. Quia parili forma, ut alia præcepta sacrificia sancita sunt, ac præcepta dicun- tur Matth. 8. 5. Neq; id gratificandum est Pontifi- ciis Interpp. Gislerio, Cornelio, Castro, cum Grotio, quasi occasione demum erecti vituli, & per conniven- tiam Deus ea admiserit, non vero ex justo proposito, neque illo statim die, quo eduxit populum ex Ægypto. Nam id adversatur tum primæ Mosis vocationi, ubi ab Angelo in rubo statim sacrificiorum mentio fa- cta, Ex. 3. 12. & præcepta populi dimissio ob sacrifi- cia v. 18. tum ordini præceptorum, quum ante μοσχο- λατρείαν Ex. 32. descriptam c. 20, 24. c. 27. sacrificia jam demandata fuerint, (etsi promulgatio legum istarum deinceps demum sequuta sit) unde μοσχο- λατρεία non potest haberi occasio sanctionis fa- crificiorum; tum deniq; fini proprio & præcipuo sa- crificiorum, qui erat fymbolicus & typicus adum- brandi sacrificii Christi expiatorii. Atq; hoc est, quod hic Deus testatur, quod nempe non præcepe- rit sacrificia talia, vel eo fine, qualia, & quo fine of- ferebant ea Israëlitæ, non sanciverit ea, ut per se ex- piatoria, & meritoria, sed ut typica, & repræsentati- ve sacrificii unici expiatorii, ideoq; salutaria non opere operato, ut barbare loqui amant, sed cum vera fide offeruntur, quæ otiosa non est, sed per charita- tem operosa. Conferatur Col. 2, 17. Ebr. 10, 1. seqq. Unde non nuda sacrificia, ut putabunt Ju- dæi, requirebat Deus, sed quæ offeruntur per fi- dem. Non externum illum cultum absq; interiori, sed imprimis interiorem cultum, in quo το πρωτειον fides obtinet, externo isto cultu & excitandum ac fovendum, & declarandum, ac publice manife- standum. Quo nomine requirit Deus hic obe- dientiam & observantiam verbi & mandatorum suorum v. 27. Non vult, inquit Aug. lib. 10. de civ. Dei c. 5. sacrificium trucidati pecoris, sed vult sacri- ficium contriti cordis. Sic itaq; illa Deum nolle dixit, quomodo à stultis ea velle creditur, velut suæ gratiæ voluptatis. Quo etiam pertinent illa Hieronym. in h. l. Quorum reprobavit templum, consequenter reprobat & sacrificia: & oblique arguit eos, quod non veneratione sui, sed epularum desiderio immolent victimas. Conf. Iren. l. 4. c. 32.
