Quæ Grotius l. 5. deverit. Relig. Christ. c. 8. adduxit, ut probaret, sacrificia prius ab hominum ingenio excogitata, quam à Deo jussa, id non pro- bant. Nam Ef. 2. non rejicitur hæc sententia, quod sacrificia vera fide oblata Deo grata & vera pietatis pars sint: & recte illi, qui ex Ebræis, fatente Grotio, ajunt, agi advertus eos, qui sacrificia offerebant ani- mo, vitaq; impuri. Etsi enim populum suum, & pios etiam alloquatur ibi Deus, tamen in illis etiam quid desiderasse DEUM, verba ipsa docent. Ex iis vero temere id efficere conatur Grotius, quod fa- crificia nihil per se Deo gratum habuerint. Si illud PER SE intelligat citra σχέσιν ad sacrificium Mes- siæ, concedimus: quia vero sacrificia ab hominum ingenio excogitata à Deo ideo solum permissa, vel in- juncta putat, ne ad falsorum deorum cultum sacrifici- orum gentilium amore, destituti sacrificiis, vel me- moria Ægyptii incolatus, uti loquitur, redirent, mi- nime id admittendum est, nec vel è Psalmo isto, vel ex aliis locis Pf. 40. Pf. 51. Ef. 1. Of. 6. Mich. 6. ubi de sacrificiis agitur, vel è præsenti textu tale quid ex- sculpi poterit. Nec in eo vel Judæus Maimonides ductore dubitant. l. 3 c. 32. vel Tertullianus advers. Marcion. 2. audiri merentur, cum talem sacrificio- rum causam adferunt, quæ à sacris literis aliena, imo contraria iisdem est. Ubi enim hoc in Scriptu- ris legitur, industriam Dei populum pronum in idolo- latriam & transgressionem ejusmodi officiis religioni suæ voluisse adstringere, quibus superstitio seculi age- batur, ut ab ea avocaret illos, sibi jubens fieri quasi desideranti, ne simulacris faciendis delinqueret; quod Tertulian. loco citato adferuit? Annon potius Scriptura docet, Deum ob mysterium satisfa- ctionis Christi, veteri populo adumbrandum, de quo gentiles nihil noverant, sacrificia instituisse, unde non à gentilibus ad populum Dei, sed à po- pulo Dei ad gentiles transit sacrificiorum ritus, per horum κακοζηλίαν, & Diaboli, qui sic illudere vo- luit sacrificio CHRISTI, πανσεγίαν.

Quod autor Quæstionum Justino adscriptarum Quæst. 83. & Chrysostomus 12. de statuis ante legem sine DEI jussu ab Abele, aliisq; sanctis oblata sacri- ficia dicunt, non congruit Apostolos testimonio Eb. 11. qui per fidem ea, etiam ante legem, oblata esse docet. Fides n. sine Dei verbo locum non habet quod basis, fundamentum, principium, regula, ac norma fidei est. Si per fidem obtulit Abel, quod testatur S. S. non ergo per instinctum naturæ, non absq; verbo Dei. Et quum sacrificia umbram ha- buerint Christi, quomodo instinctu naturæ offerri potuere! In natura enim nulla ne obscura quidem Christi umbra est. Deniq; nihil omnino è natura afferri potest pro cultu sacrificiorum, quin abso- num potius videtur rationi, Deum invisibilem ho- stiis & sacrificiis colere.

## 7:24
Vers. 24. AND THEY HAVE GONE BACKWARD, AND NOT FORWARD) That is, from the first time they have always receded further from me: namely, if not individual moments of time, but whole ages are considered. See Neh. 9.

Latin:

Vers. 24. FACTIQVE SVNT RETRORSVM, ET NON IN ANTE) Id est, à primo tempore longius sem- per à me recesserunt: nempe si non singula momenta tem- porum, sed tota sæcula spectentur. Vide Neh. 9.

## 7:25
Vers. 25. RISING UP EARLY IN THE MORNING) That is, with the greatest diligence, as those who rise very early for work. Thus also above 13.

Latin:

Vers. 25. PER DIEM CONSVRGENS DILUCU- LO) Id est, summa cum diligentia, ut qui bene mane ad opus surgunt. Sic & supra 13.

## 7:26
Vers. 26. THEY HAVE DONE WORSE THAN THEIR FATHERS) As below 16, 12. The age of our parents, worse than our grandparents, has brought forth us, who are more wicked, says Horace.

Latin:

Vers. 26. PEJVS OPERATI SVNT QVAM PA- TRES EORVM) Ut infra 16, 12. Ætas parentum pejor avis tulit Nos nequiores, Ait Horatius.

## 7:29
Vers. 29. CUT OFF THINE HAIR AND CAST IT AWAY) Jerome on this passage: Among the ancients, this was the custom of all who were mourning, to cut their hair. But now, on the contrary, to let the hair grow is a sign of mourning. See Job 1, 20. The Chaldean preferred, to pluck out the hairs. Thus in Seneca's Hippolytus: Hair pulled and torn locks.

AND TAKE UP A LAMENTATION ON HIGH PLACES) In the Hebrew: Lift up lamentations in eminent places: that is, from where you may be heard from afar, as above 3, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 29. TONDE CAPILLUM TVVM ET PRO- JICE) Hieronymus ad hunc locum: Apud veteres hæc erat omnium consuetudo lugentium tondere cæsariem. At nunc è con- trario comam dimittere luctus indicium est. Vide Job. 1, 20. Chaldæus maluit, evellere capillos. Sic in Hippolyto Senecæ: Crinis tractus & laceræ comæ.

ET SVME IN DIRECTUM PLANCTVM) In Hebræo: Attolle lamenta in locis eminentibus: id est, unde longe audiaris, ut supra 3, 16.

## 7:30
Vers. 30. THEY HAVE SET THEIR ABOMINATIONS IN THE HOUSE) LXX. βδελύγματα, and the Chaldean abominations: that is, idols. Others from the Greeks translated it προσόχθισμα, as Deut. 7, 26. 2 Kings 23, 13. 24. Ezek. 5, 11. 7, 20. 37, 23. and from there this Latin.

Latin:

Vers. 30. POSVERVNT OFFENDICULA IN DO- MO SUA) LXX. βδελύγματα, & Chaldæus abominationes: id est, idola. Alii ex Græcis verterunt προσόχθισμα, ut Deut, 7, 26. 2. Reg. 23, 13. 24. Ezech. 5, 11. 7, 20. 37, 23. & inde hoc Latinum.

## 7:31
Vers. 31. THAT THEY MIGHT BURN THEIR SONS AND THEIR DAUGHTERS IN THE FIRE) See what we have brought to the sense of this and other passages at Deut. 18, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 31. UT INCENDERENT FILIOS SUOS ET FILIAS SVAS IGNE) Vide quæ ad sensum hujus & alio- rum locorum attulimus ad Deuter, 18, 10.

## 7:32
Vers. 32. BUT THE VALLEY OF SLAUGHTER) That is, as the Greeks rightly interpret, ἀνῃρημένων, from the huge multitude of Jews, whom the Chaldeans, having killed them, will cast into that place.

AND THEY SHALL BURY IN TOPHETH, FOR THERE IS NO PLACE) You might better translate: So that there is no place: namely, empty of the dead.

Latin:

Vers. 32. SED VALLIS INTERFECTIONIS) Id est, ut Græci recte interpretantur, ἀνῃρημένων, ab ingenti mul- titudine Judæorum, quos à se occisos Chaldæi in eum lo- cum projicient.

ET SEPELIENT IN TOPHETH, EO QVOD NON SIT LOCVS) Melius vertas: Ita ut non sit locus: nempe vacuus à mortuis.

## 7:33
Vers. 33. AND IT SHALL BE THE CARCASS) That is, and they shall be corpses.

FOR THE FOWLS OF THE HEAVEN AND FOR THE BEASTS OF THE EARTH) Lactantius said: To lie as prey for wild beasts and birds. See what we have said in book 2 of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 20, 2, and in the Annotations to that passage.

AND THERE SHALL BE NONE TO DRIVE AWAY) For fear of the enemy. See the Antigone of Sophocles.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ET ERIT MORTICINUM) Id est, & erunt cadavera.

VOLUCRIBUS COELI ET BESTIIS TERRÆ) Lactantius dixit: Feris ac volucribus in prædam jacere. Vide quæ diximus libro 2. de Jure belli ac pacis cap. 20, 2. & in Annotatis ad eum locum.

ET NON ERIT QUI ABIGAT) Præ hostium metu. Vide Antigonem Sophoclis.

## 7:34
Ver. 34. AND I WILL CAUSE TO CEASE FROM THE CITIES OF JUDAH, AND FROM THE STREETS OF JERUSALEM THE VOICE OF MIRTH, AND THE VOICE OF GLADNESS.) Similar to Ez. 26, 13.

THE VOICE OF THE BRIDEGROOM AND THE VOICE OF THE BRIDE) Songs which the bridegroom used to sing before the young men, and the bride before the virgins. So also below 16, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ET QUIESCERE FACIAM DE URBIBUS JUDA, ET DE PLATEIS JERUSALEM VOCEM GAUDII ET VOCEM LÆTITIÆ.) Simile Ez. 26, 13.

VOCEM SPONSI ET VOCEM SPONSÆ) Car- mina quæ sponsus juvenibus, sponsa virginibus præcine- bant. Sic & infra 16, 9.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

A rebuke of the security, idolatry, and avarice of the people, and a denunciation of fatal punishments, with a lamentation over their destruction.

Ver. 1. AT THAT TIME, SAITH THE LORD, THEY SHALL BRING OUT THE BONES OF THE KINGS OF JUDAH) as is accustomed to be done when cities are captured. Horace: Alas, the barbarian victor shall trample upon the ashes, and the horseman shall make the city resound with his clattering hoof, and the bones of Quirinus, which are hidden from winds and suns—it is a sin to see—he shall insolently scatter.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Reprehensio securitatis, idololatriæ, & ava- ritiæ populi, & pœnarum fatalium denun- ciatio, cum deploratione interitus.

Vers. 1. In ILLO TEMPORE, AIT DOMINVS, EJICIENT OSSA REGUM JUDA) ut captis urbibus solet fieri. Horatius: Barbarus heu cineres insistet victor, & urbem Eques sonante personabit ungula, Quæq; carent ventis & solibus ossa Quirini, Nefas videre, dissipabit insolens.

## 8:2
Ver. 2. AND ALL THE HOST OF HEAVEN) Such as the star of Saturn, of Venus, of Jupiter, of Mars, and the rest.

THEY SHALL NOT BE GATHERED) That is, the bodies of those who shall die then shall not be carried to the monuments of their ancestors: for that is what אסף means.

AND THEY SHALL NOT BE BURIED) Indeed, they shall not even attain to a common grave, such as was accustomed to be given to the poor. Such is that of Lucan: We do not seek individual tombs and separate pyres: give one fire to the nations. Horace, Sat. 1. 8: This stood as a common grave for the wretched plebs, for Pantolabus the buffoon, and Nomentanus the spendthrift. A cippus gave a thousand feet in front and three hundred into the field here: that the monument should not pass to the heirs. See also what is at Matt. 27, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET OMNEM MILITIAM COELI) Ut astrum Saturni, Veneris, Jovis, Martis, & cætera.

NON COLLIGENTUR) Id est, eorum qui tum morientur corpora non deferentur ad monumenta majo- rum: id enim est אסף.

ET NON SEPELIENTUR) Imo ne commune quidem omnibus, quale pauperibus dari solebat, sepulchrum continget. Tale illud Lucani: -- Petimus non singula busta Discretosq; rogos: unum da gentibus ignem. Horatius I. Sat. 8. Hoc miseræ plebi stabat commune sepulchrum, Pantolabo scurræ, Nomentanoq; nepoti. Mille pedes in fronte, trecentos cippus in agrum Heic dabat: hæredes monumentum ne sequeretur. Vide & quæ ad Matth. 27, 7.

## 8:5
Ver. 5. BY A CONTENTIOUS AVERSION) Obstinate.

Latin:

Vers. 5. AVERSIONE CONTENTIOSA) Pertinaci.

## 8:6
Ver. 6. NO MAN SPEAKETH THAT WHICH IS GOOD) A hyperbole, such as in Ps. 14, 3, and elsewhere.

In Psalm 14, we have warned in our vindications that there is no hyperbole.

EVERYONE HAS TURNED TO HIS OWN COURSE) They are carried along with a poured-out rush.

Latin:

Vers. 6. NEMO QUOD BONUM EST LOQUITUR) ὑπερβολὴ, qualis in Psal. 14, 3. & alibi.

In Psalmo 14. nullam esse hyperbolen, in vindiciis ejus monuimus.

OMNES CONVERSI SUNT AD CURSUM SUUM) Effuso impetu feruntur.

## 8:7
Ver. 7. KITE) Others, like the Chaldean, place diconia here. See what we have said at Job 39:13.

Most interpreters, including the Papists, have Stork.

AND THE STORK) Swallow, according to the Chaldean, as also according to our own at Isaiah 38:14.

The Hebrew word never signifies a Stork: Is. 38:14 denotes a groaning or croaking crane; which meaning is not unsuitable here. For this bird observes the time of its migration and return. Compare Is. 1:6, Deut. 31:15, ch. 32:28.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MILVUS) Alii, ut Chaldæus, hic ponunt diconia. Vide quæ diximus ad Jobum 39, 13.

Ciconia habent pleriq; Interpp. etiã Pontificii.

ET CICONIA) Hirundo, apud Chaldæum, ut & apud nostrum Esaiaæ 38, 14.

Vox Ebræa nunquam Ciconiam significat: Ef. 38, 14. gruem gementem aut crocitantem notat; quæ significatio hic non inconveniens. Hæc enim avis migrationis suæ & reditus tempus observat. Conf. Esa. 1, 6. Deut. 31, 15. c. 32, 28.

## 8:8
Ver. 8. TRULY THE LYING PEN OF THE SCRIBES HAS WROUGHT A LIE) Truth, if I am not mistaken, is best: in fact, the pen writes lies, falsehood is with the scribes. Falsity to the Hebrews is often that which is iniquitous. How do your teachers say they keep the law, when they daily write decrees against the law? as in Isaiah 10.

Christ also rebukes such scribes everywhere, Matt. 7:20, ch. 15:1, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VERE MENDACIUM OPERATUS EST STILUS MENDAX SCRIBABUM) Veritas, ni fallor, optime: profecto stilus mendacia scribit, falsimonia penes scribas. Falsitas Hebræis sæpe id quod iniquum est. Quomodo doctores vestri dicunt legem se tenere, cum quotidie decreta scribant contra legem? ut Esaiæ 10.

Tales etiam scribas reprehendit Christus passim Matth. 7, 20. C. 15, 1. &c.

## 8:9
Ver. 9. THE WISE MEN ARE CONFOUNDED) That is, therefore they shall be punished.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CONFUSI SUNT SAPIENTES) Id est, ideo punientur.

## 8:11
V. 11. TO IGNOMINY) Or as a light matter. See above 6:14.

Latin:

V. 11. AD IGNOMINIAM) Vel ut rem levem. Vid. sup. 6, 14.

## 8:12
V. 12. YEA RATHER THEY WERE NOT CONFOUNDED WITH CONFUSION) An emendation, the same as above 6:1.

Latin:

V. 12. QUIN IMO CONFUSIONE NON SUNT CONFUSI) ἐπανόρθωσις eadem quæ supra 6, 1.

## 8:13
Ver. 13. GATHERING I WILL GATHER THEM) You would translate more correctly: I will utterly destroy them: just as the Chaldean here, the LXX translate סוף by ἀπόλλυμι in Ezekiel 24:4, and elsewhere by ἄγω or ἀφαιρέω.

THERE IS NO GRAPE ON THE VINES) The sign of comparison is missing. For the full sense is: as when there is no grape on the vines: where all the grapes have been cast down by some storm.

AND THERE ARE NO FIGS ON THE FIG TREE) That is, on the fig tree.

THE LEAF HAS FALLEN) Or as leaves are cast down from trees while living.

AND I HAVE GIVEN THEM WHAT HAS PASSED BY) Because I gave them (the law, to be sure, which the Chaldean supplies here) and they transgress (it).

More correctly almost all other interpreters: what I had given them, shall pass away from them. For it is a matter of punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 13. CONGREGANS CONGREGABO EOS) Rectius vertas: Omnino perdam eos: quomodo hic Chaldæus, LXX. סוף per ἀπόλλυμι vertunt Ezech. 24, 4. alibi per ἄγω aut ἀφαιρέω.

NON EST UVA IN VITIBUS) Deest comparationis nota. Plenus enim sensus est: sicut cum non est uva in vitibus: ubi omnes uvæ dejectæ sunt aliqua tempestate.

ET NON SUNT FICUS IN FICULNEA) Id est, in ficu arbore.

FOLIUM DEFLUXIT) Aut sicut folia ab arboribus dejiciuntur viventi.

ET DEDI EIS QUÆ PRÆTERGRESSA SUNT) Quia dedi eis, (legem scilicet, quod hic supplet Chaldæus) & (eam) transgrediuntur.

Rectius alii Interpp. fere omnes: quæ dederam eis, transibunt ab iis. Agitur enim de pœna.

## 8:14
Ver. 14. WHY DO WE SIT) He now describes the counsels of those who will be in the weaker towns when the enemy arrives. They will think that they will have safety in Jerusalem, and that this storm will pass away, as once in the time of Sennacherib.

LET US ENTER THE FORTIFIED CITY) Jerusalem.

AND LET US BE SILENT THERE.) Let us keep ourselves quiet.

BECAUSE THE LORD OUR GOD HAS MADE US SILENT) He did not wish to give us victory over the enemies.

AND HAS GIVEN US WATER OF GALL TO DRINK) He wished us to undergo this ignominy, that we should keep the enemy away with walls. They speak thus, because they believed that nothing worse was impending.

FOR WE HAVE SINNED AGAINST THE LORD) This is often said even by those who do not cleanse their soul. See 1 Kings 21:29.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QUARE SEDEMUS) Describit jam consilia eorum qui in oppidis infirmioribus futuri erunt adventante hoste. Ii putabunt se salutem habituros Hierosolymis, abiaturamque hanc procellam, ut olim Senacheribi tempore.

INGREDIAMUR CIVITATEM MUNITAM) Hierosolyma.

ET SILEAMUS IBI.) Quietos nos contineamus.

QUIA DOMINUS DEUS NOSTER SILERE NOS FECIT) Noluit nobis victoriam dare de hostibus.

ET POTUM NOBIS DEDIT AQUAM FELLIS) Voluit nos hanc ignominiam subire, ut mœnib9 hostem arceamus. Ita loquuntur, quod nihil pejus instare crederent.

PECCAVIMUS ENIM DOMINO) Hoc sæpe dicunt etiam, qui animum non repurgant. Vide 1. Reg. 21, 29.

## 8:15
Ver. 15. WE HAVE WAITED FOR PEACE) In the Hebrew: Wait for peace. For the Prophet answers those whom he had just introduced as speaking. Wait indeed as much as you like for better times.

AND THERE WAS NO GOOD) In the Hebrew: and no good. That is: but in truth there shall be nothing of good.

TIME OF HEALING) Wait until the Chaldeans depart.

AND BEHOLD TERROR) Then evils will come most especially, when you are within the city.

Latin:

Vers. 15. EXSPECTAVIMUS PACEM) In Hebræo: Exspecta pace. Respondet n. Propheta illis, quos modo loquentes induxerat. Exspecta sane quantũ liber meliora tempora.

ET NON ERAT BONUM) In Hebræo: & non bonum. Id est: at vero nihil erit boni.

TEMPUS MEDELÆ) Expecta donec abeant Chaldæi.

ET ECCE FORMIDO) Tunc maxime venient mala, cum intra urbem eritis.

## 8:16
Ver. 16. FROM DAN THE SNORTING OF HIS HORSES IS HEARD) Because, with Phoenicia subdued, Nebuchadnezzar was approaching from there through the borders of the Danites. Thus Jerome here. Compare what we have brought forward in book 3 on the truth of the Christian Religion.

ALL THE EARTH IS MOVED) It trembled.

THEY HAVE DEVOURED THE LAND AND THE FULL ness thereof) They will snatch away all the fruits of the trees and crops, all their wealth. Vers. 17. QVIBVS NON EST INCANTATIO) By a metaphor are understood hard men, mitigable by no prayers. ET MORDEBUNT VOS) They will afflict you with most grievous evils. Vers. 18. DOLOR MEUS SUPER DOLOREM, IN ME COR MEVM MOERENS) In the Hebrew: In my consolation over my pain, my heart languishes within me. That is, while I console myself with empty hope, and nothing succeeds, I faint in spirit. These are the words of those who had endured a siege, as the following indicates. Vers. 19. ECCE VOX CLAMORIS FILIÆ POPU- LI MEI.) Namely, that which I said will be their cry. DE TERRA LONGINQVA) Synecdoche; because of those coming from afar, the Chaldeans. NUMQUID DOMINVS NON EST IN SION, AVT REX EJUS IN EA?) They will also add this: does God, our king, no longer look upon this city? QVARE ERGO ME AD IRACUNDIAM CON- CITAVERVNT?) God answers them: If I am God and your king, why have you preferred idols to me? Vers. 20. TRANSIIT MESSIS, FINITA EST Æ- STAS, ET NOS SALVATI NON SUMUS) The people speak again: Behold, for such a long time we have endured the siege, and no hope appears. Vers. 21. SVPER CONTRITIONE FILIÆ POPU- LI MEI CONTRITVS SVM) The Prophet speaks, grieving for the evils of his countrymen. Vers. 22. NUMQUID RESINA NON EST IN GA- LAAD) Thus the LXX translated צרי both in this place and Gen. 37, 25, where there is likewise mention of the land of Gilead. Nor otherwise in Gen. 43, 10. To the Arabs, رت is the terebinth. Pliny, book 14, ch. 20, on resin: In the East, they produce the best and finest resin of the terebinth. Again, dealing with resin, book 24, 6: Liquid from the terebinth: then: In the difference of trees, terebinth is pleasing. Usus autē quis sit resinæ, de quo hic agitur, eodem Plinii loco satis discimus: We learn sufficiently from the same passage of Pliny what the use of resin is, which is treated here: Resin is dissolved for the use of wounds and for poultices with oil, and in potions with bitter almonds. Its nature in healing is to contract wounds, to purge, and to disperse swellings. In the land of Gilead, where there was much resin, there were also many physicians, that is, surgeons. Therefore, if any were wounded and were not cured, it was their own fault for refusing to offer themselves to the physicians. Thus, the Israelites had never lacked warnings and Prophets, such as Elijah the Gileadite, 1 Kings 17, 1, and his School. But that they were not healed was due to themselves. Castro thinks it is an ironic question: Is there no resin in Gilead? Are the idols which you worship in Gilead not a remedy for you? But B. Hülsemann rightly judges that interpretation to be too harsh. Regarding the abundance of resin in Gilead, see Jer. 17, 8; ch. 46, 11; Ezek. 27, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 16. A DAN AUDITUS EST FREMITUS EQUORUM EJUS) Quia Phœnice subacta, inde per Danitarum terminos adventabat Nabuchodonosor. Ita hic Hieronymus. Confer quæ adduximus ad librum 3. de veritate Religionis Christianæ.

COMMOTA EST OMNIS TERRA) Intremuit.

DEVORAVERUNT TERRAM ET PLENITU- DINEM EJUS) Omnes arborum fegetumq; fruges, Opes omnes abripient. Vers. 17. QVIBVS NON EST INCANTATIO) Per metaphoram intelliguntur homines duri, nullis preci- bus mitigabiles. ET MORDEBUNT VOS) Gravissimis malis vos afficient. Vers. 18. DOLOR MEUS SUPER DOLOREM, IN ME COR MEVM MOERENS) In Hebræo: In consolatione mea super dolorem, cor meum in me languet. Id est, dum memet spe inani consolor, nec quicquam succe- dit, linquor animo. Hæc sunt verba eorum, qui obsidio- nem erant perpessi, ut indicant sequentia. Vers. 19. ECCE VOX CLAMORIS FILIÆ POPU- LI MEI.) Nempe is quem dixi erit eorum clamor. DE TERRA LONGINQVA) Synecdoche; pro- pter illos è longinquo venientes, Chaldæos. NUMQUID DOMINVS NON EST IN SION, AVT REX EJUS IN EA?) Hoc etiam addent: an Deus, rex noster, hanc urbem non ultra respicit? QVARE ERGO ME AD IRACUNDIAM CON- CITAVERVNT?) Respondet illis Deus: Si Deus sum & rex vester, cur idola mihi prætulistis? Vers. 20. TRANSIIT MESSIS, FINITA EST Æ- STAS, ET NOS SALVATI NON SUMUS) Populus iterum loquitur: Ecce jam tanto tempore toleramus obsi- dium, neque spes ulla apparet. Vers. 21. SVPER CONTRITIONE FILIÆ POPU- LI MEI CONTRITVS SVM) Loquitur Propheta in- dolens popularium malis. Vers. 22. NUMQUID RESINA NON EST IN GA- LAAD) Ita צרי & hoc loco & Gen. 37, 25. ubi itidem Ga- laaditidos terræ mentio, verterunt LXX. Nec aliter Gen. 43, 10. Arabibus رت est terebinthus. Plinius l. 14. c. 20. de resina: In oriente optimam tenuissimamq; terebinthi fun- dunt. Iterum de resina agens l 24, 6. Liquida è terebinthi: de- inde: In arborum differentia placet terebinthina. Usus autē quis sit resinæ, de quo hic agitur, eodem Plinii loco satis discimus: Resolvitur resina, ad vulnerum usus & malagmata oleo, in potio- nes amygdalis amaris. Natura in medendo contrahere vulnera, purgare, discutere collectiones. In Galaaditide, ubi multa erat resina, multi etiam erant medici, id est, chirurgi, Itaq; si qui vulnerati erant, nec curabantur, ipsorum erat culpa, medicis præbere se nolentium. Sic Israëlitic nunquā defuerant mo- nita & Prophetæ, qualis & Elias Galaadites 1. Reg. 17, 1. & Schola ipsius. Sed quo minus sanarentur, per ipsos stetit. Castro putat esse interrogationem Ironicam: Nunquid resina non est in Gilead? Num idola, quæ in Gilead colitis, vobis non sunt remedio? Sed ni- mis durum esse illum sensum recte judicat B.Hül- semannus. De resinæ copia in Gilead Jer. 17, 8. c. 46, 11. Ezech. 27, 17.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX.

Luget interficiendos in Judæa, ob cujus vasta- tionem vult omnes assumere luctum. In so- lo Domino (Christo) ejusq; cognitione glo- riandum, nisi cum infidelibus pereundum. Vers. 1. QVIS DABIT CAPITI MEO AQVAM) Hebraism for 'would that my head were water': a torrent, that is, as the Chaldean has it here. ET OCULIS MEIS FONTEM LACHRYMA- RVM) And that my eyes were a fountain flowing perpetually. ET PLORABO DIE AC NOCTE) That I might always be able to weep for the slaughters which I foresee. Vers. 2. QUIS DABIT ME) Let him give me. IN SOLITVDINE DIVERSORIUM VIATO- RVM) Some hut, such as that into which those traveling through desert places take shelter. He desires this, so that he may not be forced to look upon the crimes of the city with his utmost grief. Vers. 3. QVASI ARCVM MENDACII) For calumny is more harmful than any weapon. Vers. 4. ET IN OMNI FRATRE SUO NON HA BEAT FIDVCIAM) A description of a most wretched age, such as Hesiod places before our eyes: Οὐδὲ κασίγνητος φίλος ἔσσεται, ὡς τὸ πάρος περ. And Ovid: -- Fratrum quoq; gratia rara est. Verse 5. AND A MAN SHALL MOCK HIS BROTHER. Better: he circumvents. Verse 6. THY HABITATION IS IN THE MIDST OF DECEIT; THROUGH DECEIT THEY REFUSE TO KNOW ME. The words of God to Jeremiah. He says they offend not by a light, nor even by a broad fault, but by evil deceit. Compare Eph. 6, 5. For those words מרמה במרמה the LXX read מרבה במרבה, which is τόκος ἐπὶ τόκῳ.

Hieron., Raban., Hugo, and Maldon. indeed make this an apostrophe to GOD in their commentaries on Jeremiah, because he dwells among the deceitful, but it is more correctly understood as a reproach of Jeremiah to the people, so that it may cohere with what precedes: To sit or dwell in the midst of deceit signifies a perpetual and continuous devotion to frauds, Ps. 1, 1. 36, 5. 50, 20. Zach. 5, 7.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Luget interficiendos in Judæa, ob cujus vasta- tionem vult omnes assumere luctum. In so- lo Domino (Christo) ejusq; cognitione glo- riandum, nisi cum infidelibus pereundum. Vers. 1. QVIS DABIT CAPITI MEO AQVAM) Hebraismus pro utinam caput meum sit aqua: torrens scili- cet, ut hic Chaldæus. ET OCULIS MEIS FONTEM LACHRYMA- RVM) Et oculi mei sint fons perpetuo fluens. ET PLORABO DIE AC NOCTE) Ut semper deflere possem clades quas prævideo. Vers. 2. QUIS DABIT ME) Det mihi. IN SOLITVDINE DIVERSORIUM VIATO- RVM) Tugurium aliquod, quale est in quod per deserta lo- ca viam facientes se recipiunt. Optat hoc, ne urbis scelera summo suo cum dolore aspicere cogatur. Vers. 3. QVASI ARCVM MENDACII) Nam calu mnia omni telo nocentior. Vers. 4. ET IN OMNI FRATRE SUO NON HA BEAT FIDVCIAM) Descriptio pessimæ ætatis, qualem ob oculos nobis ponit Hesiodus: Οὐδὲ κασίγνητος φίλος ἔσσεται, ὡς τὸ πάρος περ. Et Ovidius: -- Fratrum quoq; gratia rara est. Vers. 5. ET VIR FRATREM SVVM DERIDEBIT. Melius: circumvenit. Vers 6. HABITATIO TVA IN MEDIO DOLI; DO LO RENVERVNT SCIRE ME) Verba Dei ad Jeremiam Dicit eos non levi, ac ne lata quidē culpa, sed dolo malo de linquere. Confer Ef. 6, 5. Pro illis vocibus מרמה במרמה LXX. legerunt מרבה במרבה, quod est τόκος ἐπὶ τόκῳ

Apostrophen hic quidem DEI faciunt Hieron. Raban. Hugo. Maldon. ad Jeremiam, quod inter dolosos versetur, sed rectius accipitur, ut exprobra- tio Jeremiæ ad populum, ut cohæreat antecedenti- bus : Sedere vel habitare in medio doli significat perpetuum & continuum fraudum studium Pf. 1, 1. 36, 5. 50, 20. Zach. 5, 7.

## 9:7
Vers. 7. ECCE EGO CONFLABO ET PROBABO EGO ) Melius : Ego excoquens eos probabi, misi minora ma- la Josiæ & Joakimi temporibus, experiens an per ea purga- ri possent. Similitudo qualis supra 6, 29. Vers. 7. ECCE EGO CONFLABO ET PROBABO EGO ) Better: I, smelting them, will test them; I sent lesser evils in the times of Josiah and Jehoiakim, testing whether they could be purged by them. A similitude such as above, 6, 29.

QUID ENIM ALIUD FACIAM A FACIE FILIÆ POPULI MEI ? ) Quid aliud facere poteram ejus causa ? QUID ENIM ALIUD FACIAM A FACIE FILIÆ POPULI MEI ? ) What else could I do for her sake?

Latin:

Vers. 7. ECCE EGO CONFLABO ET PROBABO EGO ) Melius : Ego excoquens eos probabi, misi minora ma- la Josiæ & Joakimi temporibus, experiens an per ea purga- ri possent. Similitudo qualis supra 6, 29.

QUID ENIM ALIUD FACIAM A FACIE FILIÆ POPULI MEI ? ) Quid aliud facere poteram ejus causa ?

## 9:10
Vers. 10. SUPER MONTES ASSUMAM FLETUM) Propheta loquitur, Super montes : id est, propter montes illos quondam plenos pascuis. Vers. 10. SUPER MONTES ASSUMAM FLETUM) The Prophet speaks, Upon the mountains: that is, because of those mountains once full of pastures.

Montibus abundabat Judæa. Ex. 15, 17. Deut. 11, 10. Pf. 34, 2. Ita אל adhibetur v. 12. 13. Judea abounded in mountains. Ex. 15, 17. Deut. 11, 10. Ps. 34, 2. Thus אל is used in v. 12, 13.

ET SUPER SPECIOSA DESERTI) Melius : amœnas planities. Ita n. sæpe דבר נו sumi aliquoties observavimus. ET SUPER SPECIOSA DESERTI) Better: pleasant plains. Thus we have observed several times that דבר נו is often taken.

BECAUSE THERE IS NO MAN PASSING THROUGH ) Not only does no one dwell there, but not even one passes through. All things have been made the lairs of wild beasts.

AND THEY HAVE NOT HEARD THE VOICE OF THE POSSESSOR ) Translate: The voice of the cattle is not heard. No lowing is heard, no bleating.

FROM THE BIRD OF THE HEAVENS EVEN TO THE CATTLE THEY HAVE MIGRATED AND DEPARTED ) Both birds and the living creatures of the earth. For that is בהמת. Jerome on Hosea 4: He who does not believe this happened to the people of Israel, let him look at Illyricum, let him look at the Thracias, Macedonia and the Pannonias, and all the land which stretches from the Propontis and the Bosphorus as far as the Julian Alps, and he will prove that along with men, all living creatures also fail, which were previously nourished by the Creator for the uses of men.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SUPER MONTES ASSUMAM FLETUM) Propheta loquitur, Super montes : id est, propter montes illos quondam plenos pascuis.

Montibus abundabat Judæa. Ex. 15, 17. Deut. 11, 10. Pf. 34, 2. Ita אל adhibetur v. 12. 13.

ET SUPER SPECIOSA DESERTI) Melius : amœnas planities. Ita n. sæpe דבר נו sumi aliquoties observavimus.

EO QUOD NON SIT VIR PERTRANSIENS ) Non modo nemo ibi habitat, sed ne transit quidem. Omnia facta sunt ferarum lustra.

ET NON AUDIERUNT VOCEM POSSIDEN- TIS ) Verte : Non auditur vox pecoris. Nullus auditur mu- gitus, nullus balatus.

A VOLUCRE COELI USQUE AD PECORA TRANSMIGRAVERUNT ET RECESSERUNT ) Tam aves quã terræ animantia. Id enim בהמת. Hieronymus ad 4. Oseæ : Hoc qui non credit accidisse populo Israel, cernat Illyricum, cernat Thracias, Macedoniam atque Pannonias, omnemq; terram, quæ à Propontide & Bosphoro usq; ad Alpes Julias tenditur, & probabit cum hominibus & animantia cuncta deficere, quæ in usus hominum à creatore prius alebantur.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. I WILL MAKE JERUSALEM INTO HEAPS OF SAND ) Into ruins.

AND THE DENS OF DRAGONS ) Lairs.

AND THE CITIES OF JUDAH ) The other towns.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DABO JERUSALEM IN ACERVOS ARE- NÆ ) In ruta cæsa.

ET CUBILIA DRACONUM ) Lustra.

ET CIVITATES JUDA ) Oppida cætera.

## 9:12
WHO IS THE WISE MAN WHO MAY UNDERSTAND THIS, AND TO WHOM THE WORD OF THE MOUTH OF THE LORD MAY COME, THAT HE MAY ANNOUNCE THIS, WHY THE LAND HAS PERISHED ) That is, if there is anyone among you who is wise either by himself or is instructed by a prophetic gift, let him tell us the causes of such great devastation: or if there is no one who can or will say, I will say it.

AS A DESERT, BECAUSE THERE IS NO ONE PASSING THROUGH ) So that there is no one who passes through.

Latin:

QUIS EST VIR SAPIENS QUI INTELLIGAT HOC, ET AD QUEM VERBUM ORIS DOMINI FI- AT, UT ANNUNTIET ISTUD, QUARE PERIERIT TERRA ) Id est, si quis inter vos aut per se sapit, aut pro- phetico dono instructus est, dicat nobis causas tantæ vastita- tis : aut si nemo est qui dicere possit aut velit, ego dicam.

QUASI DESERTUM, EO QUOD NON SIT QUI PERTRANSEAT ) Ita ut non sit qui pertranseat.

## 9:13
Vers. 13. AND THE LORD SAID ) To me, says Jeremiah, God revealed the causes of that matter.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET DIXIT DOMINUS ) Mihi, inquit Jere- mias, Deus causas ejus rei aperuit.

## 9:15
Vers. 15. WITH WORMWOOD ) With extreme bitterness. Ψωμίζω ἀυτὺς ἀνάγκας, the Greeks. See what ἀνάγκη is, Luke 21, 23.

AND I WILL GIVE THEM WATER OF GALL TO DRINK ) As above 8, 14. The same below 23, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ABSINTHIO ) Summa amaritie. Ψωμίζω ἀυτὺς ἀνάγκας, Græci. Quid sit ἀνάγκη vid. Luc. 21, 23.

CO ET POTUM DABO EIS AQUAM FELLIS ) Ut supra 8, 14. Eadem infra 23, 15.

## 9:16
Vers. 16. AND I WILL SEND THE SWORD AFTER THEM ) Not even flight will be safe. Below 42 and following.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET MITTAM POST EOS GLADIUM ) Ne fuga quidem tuta erit. Infra 42. & sequentibus.

## 9:17
Vers. 17. CALL FOR THE MOURNING WOMEN. ) Female mourners. See Festus & Nonius.

TO THOSE WHO ARE SKILLED, SEND) Those taught in mournful songs.

Latin:

Vers. 17. VOCATE LAMENTATRICES. ) Præficas. Vide Festum & Nonium.

AD EAS QUÆ SAPIENTES SUNT, MITTITE) Edoctas cantus lugubres.

## 9:19
Vers. 19. HOW ARE WE DEVASTATED? ) Here begins the imitation of the song of the mourning women.

WE HAVE ABANDONED THE LAND ) That is, we are forced to migrate. The Chaldean: The land is deserted.

OUR TABERNACLES ARE CAST DOWN ) Dwellings overturned.

Latin:

Vers. 19. QUOMODO VASTATI SUMUS ? ) Hic incipit μίμησις carminis præficarum.

DERELIQUIMUS TERRAM ) Id est, cogimur mi- grare. Chaldæus : Deserta est terra.

DEJECTA SUNT TABERNACULA NOSTRA ) Habitationes eversæ.

## 9:20
Vers. 20. HEAR THEREFORE, O WOMEN ) You, the mourning women.

YOUR DAUGHTERS ) Your disciples in that art.

Latin:

Vers. 20. AUDITE ERGO MULIERES ) Vos præficæ.

FILIAS VESTRAS ) Discipulas vestras in ista arte.

## 9:21
Vers. 21. DEATH HAS CLIMBED THROUGH OUR WINDOWS ) Those stones from ballistae. A very vivid description.

IT HAS ENTERED YOUR HOUSES ) That is, it passed through the houses themselves, nor did it stop there.

TO DESTROY THE LITTLE ONES FROM OUTSIDE, THE YOUNG MEN FROM THE STREETS ) So that those same stones passing through the houses also killed very many in the streets.

Jerome, Thomas, and Lyranus more correctly understand this as the violence of invading enemies; others explain it as an unexpected and swift irruption: that the enemies were about to break in suddenly and as if through windows, where thieves and robbers are accustomed to creep in. Joel 2:9. John 10:1. Grotius's gloss is new, and not sufficiently consistent with the phraseology of Scripture or the manner of waging war of that age.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ASCENDIT MORS PER FENESTRAS NOSTRAS ) Saxa illa balistaria. διατύπωσις valde vivida.

INGRESSA EST DOMOS VESTRAS ) Id est, per ipsas domos transivit, nec ibi substitit.

DISPERDERE PARVULOS DE FORIS, JUVE- NES DE PLATEIS ) Ita ut eadem illa saxa der domos transeuntia etiam in plateis plurimos occiderent.

Rectius Hieronymus, Thomas, & Lyranus, in- telligunt de violentia hostium irrumpentium, alii de insperata celeriq; irruptione explicant : quod ex im- proviso & velut per fenestras, ubi fures & latrones irrepere solent,hostes irrupturi sint. Joël 2,9. Joh. 10, 1. Grotii glossa nova est, neq; scripturæ phrasi aut mori belligerandi istius ætatis satis congrua.

## 9:22
Vers. 22. SPEAK: THUS SAYS THE LORD ) Continue to speak these my commands.

AND LET THE DEAD BODY OF A MAN FALL AS DUNG UPON THE FACE OF THE FIELD, AND AS

HAY BEHIND THE BACK OF THE REAPER, AND THERE IS NO ONE TO GATHER IT) What it means to gather has already been said above 8, 2. No one gathers dung. And if any sheaves fall out (for that is what the word עמיר also signifies to the Chaldeans and Arabs), the reaper hired for wages cares little for them. Human bodies will be worth no more than that then.

Latin:

Vers. 22. LOQVERE : HÆC DICIT DOMINVS ) Perge hæc mea mandata loqui.

ET CADAT MORTICINUM HOMINIS QVASI STERCUS SVPER FACIEM REGIONIS, ET QUASI

FOENVM POST TERGVM METENTIS, ET NON EST QVI COLLIGAT) Quid fit colligere, jam dictum supra 8, 2. Stercus nemo colligit. Et manipulos si qui exci- dant id enim vox עמיר etiam Chaldaeis & Arabibus so- nat) eos parum curat messor mercede conductus. Non pluris tunc fient humana corpora.

## 9:23
Vers. 23. LET NOT THE WISE MAN GLORY IN HIS WISDOM) Let him not trust in it too much. For Solomon fell from the grace of God.

AND LET NOT THE STRONG MAN GLORY IN HIS STRENGTH) For Samson, the strongest, was deceived by a woman and met his destruction.

AND LET NOT THE RICH MAN GLORY IN HIS RICHES) For Ahab, son of Omri, king of the ten tribes, was very rich: but because of his impiety he fell into the greatest evils. The Chaldean not without reason brings forward these three examples here.

Latin:

Vers. 23. NON GLORIETVR SAPIENS IN SAPIEN- TIA) Ne ei nimium fidat. Nam Solomon Dei gratia excidit.

ET NON GLORIETVR FORTIS IN FORTI- TVDINE SVA) Nam Samson fortissimus a foemina de- ceptus exitium reperit.

ET NON GLORIETVR DIVES IN DIVITIIS SVIS) Nam Achab filius Amri decem tribuum rex, ditissi- mus fuit: sed propter impietatem in maxima incidit mala. Haec tria exempla non abs re hic affert Chaldaeus.

## 9:24
Vers. 24. BUT LET HIM WHO GLORIES GLORY IN THIS, TO KNOW AND TO KNOW ME) Let him trust in this, that he has known me, provided that he also shows this by his deeds.

WHO EXECUTE MERCY, AND JUDGMENT AND JUSTICE IN THE EARTH) He does not say, that they may know me according to my nature: for that surpasses the grasp of men. But according to those properties which concern men, which the Hebrews call מדות, the chief of which are kindness to the pious, severity to the impious, and in all things the most perfect ὀρθότης, which is signified here by the name of justice taken more generally, since otherwise that word has various meanings. And note that phrase in the earth: against the philosophers who, before Aristotle, thought that God's providence did not reach to sublunary things.

It is certainly not a matter of simple knowledge, nor is legal knowledge, which brings about the practice of moral works, being considered: But a practical apprehension of divine mercy and justice exhibited in Christ and revealed in the Gospel is designated, just as faith is wont to be described by knowledge, Is. 53, 11. Job 19, 25. John 17, 3. which explanation the Apostle provides in 1 Cor 1, 30. 31. teaching that the Lord, by whose knowledge alone it is lawful to glory, is Christ Jesus, who has been made for us justice and redemption, so that he who glories, may glory in this Lord alone: by the knowledge and faithful apprehension of whose justice we ought to be justified, Is. 45. c. 53, 11. What is meant by the name of mercy, justice, and judgment, when they are joined together, has been explained elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 24. SED IN HOC GLORIETVR QVI GLO- RIATVR, SCIRE ET NOSSE ME) In eo fidat, quod me noverit, nimirum si & hoc factis ostendat.

QVI FACIO MISERICORDIAM, ET JVDI- CIUM ET JVSTITIAM IN TERRA) Non dicit, ut me noverint secundum naturam meam: ea enim homi- num captum superat. Sed secundum eas proprietates, quae homines spectant, quas מדות appellant Hebraei, quarum praecipuae sunt benignitas in pios, severitas in impios, & in omnibus rebus perfectissima ὀρθότης, quae hic significatur nomine justitiae generalius sumtae, cum alioqui ea vox va- rias habeat significationes. Et nota illud in terra: contra Philosophos qui ante Aristotelem censuere Dei providen- tiam ad sublunaria non pervenire.

Non sane de notitia simplici agitur, neque notitia legalis, quae praxin operum morale infert, respici- tur: Sed practica apprehensio misericordiae & justi- tiae divinae in Christo exhibitae & in Evangelio pa- tefactae designatur, uti solet fides per notitiam de- scribi Es. 53,11. Jobi 19,25. Joh. 17, 3. quam explica- tionem Apostolus tradit 1. Cor 1, 30. 31. docens Do- minum, cujus unius cognitione gloriari fas est, esse Christum Jesum, qui nobis factus est justitia & re- demptio, ut qui gloriatur,in hoc Domino glorietur unice: cujus justitiae cognitione & fiduciali appre- hensione nos justificari oportet Es. 45. c. 53,11. Quid misericordiae, justitiae & judicii nomine indigite- tur, cum illa conjunguntur, alias expositum est.

## 9:25
Vers. 25. I WILL VISIT UPON EVERYONE WHO HAS A CIRCUMCISED FORESKIN) From the Hebrew you may translate most correctly, by supplying ὥστε: I will punish every circumcised person (namely, the wicked: and no less him who is) in uncircumcision. In like manner I will treat them according to their deserts, and that tiny bit of skin retained or rejected will not move me.

Latin:

Vers. 25. VISITABO SVPER OMNEM QVI CIR- CVMCISVM HABET PRAEPVTIUM) Ex Hebraeo re- ctissime vertas, supplendo ὥστε: puniam omnem circum- cisum (nempe flagitiosum: nec minus eum qui est)in prae- putio. Pari modo eos pro meritis tractabo, neque me move- bit tantilla pellicula retenta, vel rejecta.

## 9:26
Vers. 26. UPON EGYPT, AND UPON JUDAH, AND UPON EDOM, AND UPON THE CHILDREN OF AMMON, AND UPON MOAB) See below 46. 48. 49.

AND UPON ALL WHO ARE SHORN IN THE HAIR, DWELLING IN THE DESERT) That is, the Scenite Arabs. See what we have brought forward concerning their custom at Lev. 19, 27. Add what is below 25, 23. and 49, 32. where the Arabs are noted by the same περιφράσει.

Vers. 27. FOR ALL THE NATIONS) Those, namely, which I have just named.

HAVE A FORESKIN) Namely in the glans, or if not in the glans, certainly in the heart. But what does it matter where that which offends God is? The heart is worth more than the symbol of the heart. The Idumeans and Arabs were bound to circumcision, no less than the Jews, but they had previously omitted it. The Egyptians, Ammonites, and Moabites were not held by that law. But all alike had a heart full of things to be cut away.

Latin:

Vers. 26. SVPER AEGYPTVM, ET SVPER JUDA, ET SVPER EDOM, ET SVPER FILIOS AMMON, ET SVPER MOAB) Vide infra 46. 48. 49.

ET SVPER OMNES QVI ATTONSI SVNT IN COMAM, HABITANTES IN DESERTO) Id est, Arabas Scenitas. Vide quae de eorum more protulimus ad Levit. 19, 27. Adde quae infra 25, 23. & 49,32. ubi Ara- bes eadem περιψράνοι notantur.

Vers. 27. QVIA OMNES GENTES) Istaee scilicet quas jam nominavi.

HABENT PRAEPVTIUM) Nempe in glande, aut si non in glande, certe in corde. Quid autem refert,ubi sit quod Deum offendit? cor pluris quam σύμβολον cordis. Idumaei & Arabes obligati erant ad circumcisionem, non minus quam Judaei, sed prius em eam omiserant. Aegyptii, Ammonitae, Moabitae ea lege non tenebantur. Sed omnes pariter cor habebant plenum rebus resecandis.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

The constellation of the heavens is not to be feared, nor most vain idols: But the Lord, who alone is God, the creator and governor of all, who will lay waste to Judea, whence the Prophet laments and prays for the mitigation of evils.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Non timenda caeli constellatio nec idola va- nissima: Sed Dominus, qui solus est Deus creator ac gubernator omnium, qui va- stabit Judaeam, unde plorat Propheta & orat pro malorum mitigatione.

## 10:2
Verse 2. ACCORDING TO THE WAYS OF THE GENTILES DO NOT LEARN) He understands especially the Chaldeans, whence the name of the Chaldean art.

AND BE NOT AFRAID OF THE SIGNS OF HEAVEN, WHICH THE GENTILES FEAR) Namely, as if all events of human affairs depended upon them. Most nations did not acknowledge the first cause, and the same acting freely, as Maimonides teaches.

THE LAWS OF THE PEOPLES ARE VAIN) Understand rites.

Latin:

Vers. 2. JVXTA VIAS GENTIVM NOLITE DI- SCERE) Chaldaeos maxime intelligit, unde nomen arti Chaldaicae.

ET A SIGNIS COELI NOLITE METVERE, QVAE TIMENT GENTES) Nempe quasi ab illis omnes eventus rerum humanarum pendeant. Pleraeque gentes primam causam, eandemque libere agentem non agno- scebant, ut docet Maimonides.

LEGES POPULORUM VARIAE SUNT) Ritus intellige.

## 10:3
Verse 3. THE WOOD OUT OF THE FOREST HE CUTS THE WORK OF THE HANDS OF THE WORKMAN WITH THE AXE) The sense is: wood is cut out of the forest which then becomes the work of the hands of a workman using an axe. The work surpassed the material. He joins the discourse about idols here with the discourse about the stars, because most of the idols of those nations in the East represented the Sun, Moon, Saturn, Venus, or another star, and indeed with the opinion of men such that they believed that a spirit drawn down by certain magical rites from the stars dwelt in the idols, and there exerted its power for the good of those venerating the idols. Moreover, this passage about idols is expressed from two [passages] of Isaiah 40:20, 44:19, and following. He omits nothing by which he might take away authority from the idols. The material, lifeless wood: the maker, a mortal man, needing food. The instruments, axe, nails, hammers.

Latin:

Vers. 3. LIGNVM DE SALTV PRAECIDIT OPVS MANVVM ARTIFICIS IN ASCIA) Sensus est: ex- scinditur e saltu lignum quod deinde sit opus manuum arti- ficis utentis ascia. Materiam superabat opus. Ideo autem sermonem de simulacris eo jungit cum sermone de astris, quod gentium illarum in Oriente simulacra plera- que, Solem, Lunam, Saturnum, Venerem, aut astrum a- liud referrent, & quidem cum ea hominum opinione, ut crederent deductum magicis quibusdam ritibus spiritum ab astris in simulacris morari, atque ibi vim suam exserere bono illa simulacra venerantium. Est autem hic locus de simu- lacris expressus, ex duobus Esaiae 40, 20. 44, 19. & se- quentibus. Nihil omittit, quo auctoritatem demat simu- lacris. Materia, lignum exanime: opifex, homo mor- talis, victus indigens. Instrumenta ascia, clavi, mallei.

## 10:4
Verse 4. HE FASTENED) Which the Greeks more elegantly call γομφῶν.

THAT IT BE NOT MOVED) In the Hebrew: That it may not go out: that it may be able to stand. See what their infirmity is, which cannot sustain themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 4. COMPEGIT) Quod Graeci elegantius dicunt γομφῶν.

VT NON DISSOLVATVR) In Hebraeo: Vt non exeat: ut stare possit. Vide quae illorum infirmitas, quae semet sustinere nequeunt.

## 10:5
Verse 5. THEY ARE MADE LIKE THE PALM TREE) In the Hebrew: By their likeness as a palm tree.

THEY ARE CARRIED AND TAKEN UP) In the Hebrew: By carrying they are carried: namely, on shoulders.

BECAUSE THEY CANNOT WALK) And this is a great infirmity, not to be able to go: and well he infers from this: If those cannot [walk], how much less can they profit or harm.

Latin:

Vers 5. IN SIMILITUDINEM PALMAE FABRICATA SUNT)In Hebraeo: Adaequatione eorum ut palmae arboris.

PORTATA TOLLENTVR) In Hebraeo Portando portantur: in thensis scilicet.

QVIA INCEDERE NON VALENT) Et haec ma- gna infirmitas, ire non posse: & bene hinc infert: Si ista non possunt, quanto minus prodesse aut nocere.

## 10:7
Verse 7. AMONG ALL THE WISE MEN OF THE GENTILES) Many of whom were also related to the gods, such as Taautes.

Latin:

Vers. 7. INTER CUNCTOS SAPIENTES GEN- TIVM) Quorum multi & in Deos relati, ut Taautes.

## 10:8
Vers. 8. THE DOCTRINE OF THEIR VANITY IS WOOD) The things which they believe concerning those images are most vain.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DOCTRINA VANITATIS EORVM LI- GNVM EST) Ea quae de istis simulacris credunt do.enti; sunt vanissima.

## 10:9
Vers. 9. SILVER BEATEN OUT) In the Hebrew: extended, namely into plates.

OF THARSHISH) From the Ocean, that is, from Spain, where there is the greatest fertility of gold. Pliny 33, 4. The Chaldean placed Africa here, doubtless because the Carthaginians sought Spanish gold from Carthage.

AND GOLD FROM UPHAZ) It is the same name as in Dan. 10, 5. There is an island πάζος in India mentioned by Stephanus from Alexander Polyhistor; it is believed to be the same which Pliny names Topazos in the Red Sea, from whence the gem Topaz gets its name, which is זהב פז. All things from India were carried to that island, and from there were distributed: Therefore the Chaldean explains this as the gold of Ophir. Concerning Ophir, see what has been said elsewhere.

AND THE HANDS OF THE GOLDSMITH) I believe the interpreter wrote Aurarii. אומן signifies a craftsman of every kind, but the material proves that a goldsmith is being discussed here.

THE WORK OF THE CRAFTSMEN) Of mortals.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ARGENTVM INVOLVTVM) In He- braeo: extensum, nempe in laminas.

DE THARSIS) Ab Oceano, id est, ab Hispania, ubi maxima auri fertilitas. Plinius 33, 4. Africam hic po- suit Chaldaeus, nimirum quia Poeni Carthagine aurum Hi- spanicum petebant.

ET AURUM DE OPHAZ) Est idem nomen Dan. 10, 5. Est insula πάζος in India memorata Stephano ex A- lexandro Polyhistore; creditur eadem esse, quam in mari rubro Topazon Plinius nominat, unde gemmae Topazio nomen, quae זהב פז. In eam insulam cuncta ex India perferebantur, atque inde distribuebantur: Ideo aurum Ophir hic explicatChaldaeus. DeOphir vide quae dicta alibi.

ET MANVS AEARII) Interpres credo scripserit Aurarii. אומן omnis generis fabrum significat, sed hic de aurario agi evincit materia.

OPVS ARTIFICVM) Mortalium.

## 10:11
Vers. 11. THUS THEREFORE SHALL YE SAY UNTO THEM: THE GODS THAT HAVE NOT MADE THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH, SHALL PERISH FROM THE EARTH, AND FROM UNDER THESE HEAVENS) It is an old saying even among certain Greeks: he who calls himself a god besides the one God, let him make another world. The Chaldean thinks these are an Epistle sent by Jeremiah to the leaders of the exiles in Babylon. But the very series of the Prophecies shows these were spoken in advance, but so that they might be used especially then, when they had to live among idolaters. And for that reason the Prophet wished to use the language in this place, not Hebrew, but Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers.11. SIC ERGO DICETIS EIS: DII QVI COELOS ET TERRAM NON FECERVNT, IER- EANT DE TERRA, ET DE HIS QVAE SVB COE- LO SVNT) Vetus est dictum etiam inter Graecos quos- dam: qui praeter unum Deum se Deum dicit,mundum al- terum faciat. Chaldaeus putat haec esse Epistolam ab Jere- mia missam ad primores exfulum in Babylonia. Sed series ipsa Prophetiarum ostendit haec in antecessum dicta, sed ut tunc praecipue usurparetur, cum inter idololatras viven- dum esset. Et ideo sermone voluit uti Propheta hoc loco, non Hebraeo, sed Chaldaeo.

## 10:12
Vers. 12. HE THAT MAKETH THE EARTH BY HIS POWER) Translate, who made: and soon, prepared: he is our God and Lord. The Jews will answer this to the Chaldeans, and thus many of them will be turned away from Idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QVI FACIT TERRAM IN FORTITU- DINE SVA) Verte, qui fecit: & mox, praeparavit: is est Deus ac Dominus noster. Hoc Judaei respondebunt Chal- daeis, & sic multi eorum ab Idololatria avertentur.

## 10:13
Vers. 13. AT HIS VOICE HE GIVETH A MULTITUDE OF WATERS IN THE HEAVENS) That is, where he himself commands. For voice or word of God, especially among the Chaldeans, signifies will.

HE MAKETH LIGHTNINGS FOR THE RAIN) Supply, by God's permission. Thus also in Psalm 133, 7. From where these words and those immediately following are taken.

Latin:

Vers. 13. AD VOCEM SVAM DAT MULTITU- DINEM AQVARVM IN COELO) Id est, ubi ipsi lu- bet. Nam vox aut verbum Dei, apud Chaldaeos maxime, voluntatem significant.

FVLGVRA IN PLUVIAM FACIT) Supple, deo sinere. Sic & in Psal. 133, 7. Unde haec verba & proxime sequentia sumpta sunt.

## 10:14
Vers. 14. EVERY MAN IS BRUTISH IN HIS KNOWLEDGE) It seems to be an ἰδιωτισμός, so that the sense may be: Every man becomes brutish (departing) from knowledge: that is, from the knowledge of the one God: that it is so taken, the following words will show.

FALSE IS THAT WHICH HE HATH MOLTEN) It is not that which is said.

AND THERE IS NO SPIRIT IN THEM) Sent down from heaven, as they themselves think.

Latin:

Vers. 14. STVLTVS FACTVS EST OMNIS HO- MO A SCIENTIA) Videtur esse ἰδιωτισμός, ut sensus sit: Brutescit omnis homo (recedens) a scientia: id est, a cogni- tione unius Dei: id ita sumi sua ent sequentia.

FALSVM EST QVOD CONFLAVIT) Non est id quod dicitur.

ET NON EST SPIRITUS IN EIS) A caelo de- missus, ut ipsi arbitrantur.

## 10:15
Ver. 15. IN THE TIME OF THEIR VISITATION THEY SHALL PERISH) As if when it has pleased God to turn His mind to their deeds.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IN TEMPORE VISITATIONIS SVAE PERIBVNT) Quasi ubi Deo vacaverit ad illorum facta animum adjicere.

## 10:16
Ver. 16. NOT LIKE THESE IS THE PORTION OF JACOB) There is no God like these, whom the Israelites worship.

ISRAEL IS THE ROD OF HIS INHERITANCE) His portion: just as a rod or measuring pole was accustomed to be used to designate the portion of a prince in a kingdom. See Ezek. 48, 21.

THE LORD OF HOSTS IS HIS NAME) He is the Lord both of the angels and of the stars.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NON EST HIS SIMILIS PARS JACOB) Non est his similis Deus, quem Israelitae colunt.

ISRAEL VIRGA HEREDITATIS EJUS) Portio ipsius: sicut virga vel pertica in regno designari solebat pars principis. Vide Ezech. 48, 21.

DOMINVS EXERCITVVM NOMEN ILLI) Dominus & Angelorum & fiderum ipse est.

## 10:17
Vers. 17. GATHER UP THY WARES OUT OF THE LAND, O THOU THAT DWELLEST IN THE FORTRESS) כנעתך we shall translate better as your things, namely those which can be carried away. It will be necessary to migrate with one's baggage. And for in the fortress we shall more correctly put, O thou that dwellest in a fortified place, ἐν τειχισμάτι, as the LXX here, that is, the Jerusalemite people.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONGREGA DE TERRA CONFVSIO- NEM TVAM, QVAE HABITAS IN OBSIDIONE) כנעתך melius vertemus res tuas, nempe quæ absportari possunt. Convafa migrandum erit. Et pro in obsidione rectius ponemus, quæ habitas in loco munito, ἐν τειχισμάλι, ut hic LXX. id est, plebs Hierosolymitana.

## 10:18
Vers. 18. I WILL CAST THEM OUT FAR) It translates the sense well. Aquila and Symmachus are closer to the word σφενδονήσω, I will cast out as if with a sling.

AND I WILL DISTRESS THEM, SO THAT THEY MAY BE FOUND.) You will translate more correctly with a sense approaching the meaning which the Chaldean intended in this place: I will afflict them, so that they may find, namely that I am not a liar in those things which I said through the Prophets. And they themselves will acknowledge that with the words which now follow at the end of the chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 18. LONGE PROJICIAM) Sensum bene vertit. Aquila & Symmachus propius ad verbum σφενδονήσω, eji- ciam velut funda.

ET TRIBULABO EOS, ITA VT INVENI- ANTVR.) Rectius verras sensu accedente ad sensum, quem voluit Chaldæus hoc loco : Affligam eos, ut inveniant, nempe me non esse mendacem in iis quæ per Prophetas di- xi. Id autem ipsi agnoscent verbis, quæ jam sequuntur ad finem capitis.

## 10:19
WOE IS ME FOR MY HURT) Ah, how great a wound I have received.

BUT I SAID) Furthermore I said, namely the city of Jerusalem.

Vers. 19. TRULY THIS IS MY GRIEF, AND I WILL BEAR IT) Understand, it is great: and shall I bear it? Read with an interrogation: Shall I be able to bear it?

Latin:

VÆ MIHI SVPER CONTRITIONE MEA) Ah quantum vulnus accepi.

EGO AVTEM DIXI) Præterea dixi, nempe civitas Hierosolymorum.

Vers. 19. PLANE HÆC INFIRMITAS MEA EST, ET PORTABO ILLAM) Subintellige, magna est: & portabo illam? lege cum interrogatione: Erone ferendo?

## 10:20
Vers. 20. MY TABERNACLE) The same metaphor as above 4, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 20. TABERNACVLVM MEVM) Metaphora eadem quæ supra 4, 20.

## 10:21

## 10:23
Verse 23. I KNOW O LORD THAT THE WAY OF MAN IS NOT HIS OWN, NEITHER IS IT IN MAN THAT WALKETH TO DIRECT HIS STEPS) The men of those unhappy times also say this: (for as it is said ὑπὲρ Μαλέαν πλεύσας ἐπιλαθέσθων) we know that the successes of war do not depend upon human prudence or fortitude alone, but especially upon your will, who easily undo the efforts of even the most powerful Kings. To direct steps is to grant success, as in Psalm 37, 23.

However, this sentiment is not badly applied to spiritual objects. For if the events of civil affairs are by no means simply in our hand, much less does man have spiritual matters in his own hand. Just as this saying is urged by Augustine throughout against the Pelagians. Let the new preachers blush, says Jerome in this place, who say that everyone is ruled by his own will: since even this prophet says: It is not of man his way. And David sings in a lyric poem: The steps of a man are directed by the Lord, and he shall greatly desire his way.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SCIO DOMINE QVIA NON EST HO- MINIS VIA EJVS, NEC VIRI EST, VT AMBV- LET ET DIRIGAT GRESSVS SVOS) Hoc etiam di- cent illorum infelicium temporum homines: (nam ut di- citur ὑπὲρ Μαλέαν πλεύσας ἐπιλαθέσθων) scimus successus bel- licos non pendere à sola prudentia, aut fortitudine huma- na, sed à tuo maxime arbitratu, qui etiam potentissimorum Regum conatus facile dissas. Dirigere gressus est successus dare, ut Psal. 37, 23.

Non male autem hæc Sententia applicatur ad objecta spiritualia. Si enim eventus rerum civilium in nostra manu simpliciter nequaquam sunt: mul- to minus res spirituales in manu sua habet homo. Quemadmodum dictum hoc Augustinus passim adversus Pelagianos urget. Erubescant, inquit Hie- ronymus in h. l. novi predicatores, qui ajunt unum- quemque suo arbitrio regi: quum & hic propheta di- cat: Non est hominis via ejus. Et David in lyrico canat carmine: A Domino gressus hominis diri- gentur, & viam ejus volet nimis.

Vers. 15. WHAT IS IT THAT MY BELOVED HATH WROUGHT MANY CRIMES IN MY HOUSE?) My beloved: that is, the people once beloved to me, as the Chaldean rightly says. Hath wrought many crimes: that is, he mixed idolatrous rites with my worship. See 2 Kings 16, 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. And what follows here.

SHALL HOLY FLESH TAKE AWAY FROM THEE THY MALICIES?) In Hebrew: Shall holy flesh cause to pass over thee (that is, to overlook) that in which thou hast formerly exulted in thy malice? That is, shall legitimate victims be able to purge thee from victims offered against the law? A little leaven infects the whole lump. The Chaldean well expresses this sense here.

## 11:19
Vers. 19. AND I WAS LIKE A GENTLE LAMB, THAT IS BROUGHT TO THE SLAUGHTER; AND I KNEW NOT THAT THEY HAD DEVISED DEVICES AGAINST ME) I was no more thinking that these things were being plotted against me than a lamb that is led to the temple.

These things are drawn to Christ by certain ancients and especially by Papist interpreters. But the συνέχεια of the text teaches that the discourse is about Jeremiah: Yet if anyone should say that Jeremiah was a type of Christ in those sufferings of his, he will be able to defend that more easily. Since the way of the Prophets was also prophetic. Whence Jerome concludes this chapter thus: That we may be freed from all trouble of interpretation, let us follow that rule: That all the Prophets performed many things in the type of the Lord Savior, and whatever was fulfilled according to the present time in

Jeremiah, that this is prophesied in the future concerning the Lord. For he saw well that the text does not cohere if it is understood according to the letter as referring to anyone other than Jeremiah. Therefore, he asserts that the Prophet was a type of Christ in it.

Verse of the same.

SAYING: LET US CAST WOOD INTO HIS BREAD) LXX. ἐμβάλωμεν ξύλον εἰς τὸν ἄρτον ἀυτῦ : just as Chrysostom also cites it, De Trinitate, Tom. 6, Savilian edition. In the Hebrew: Let us corrupt the wood in his bread: by hypallage, for his bread with wood, namely poisoned, as the Chaldean rightly took it here. Thus, Pliny says that yew trees contain poison, and from there it is believed that the name 'toxica' comes, 16, 11. Lucan: 'The impious Sabaeans pluck the ripe poisons.' He treats, however, under this similitude of the counsels of the priests for his destruction. See below 29.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET EGO QVASI AGNUS MANSVE- TVS, QVI PORTATVR AD VICTIMAM, ET NON COGNOVI, QVIA COGITAVERVNT SVPER ME CONSILIA) Non magis cogitabam ista in me agitari, quam agnus, qui ad templum ducitur.

AD Christum ea pertrahuntur à veteribus qui- busdam & maxime à Pontificiis Interpp. Sed συνέχεια textus docet de Jeremia sermonem esse: Quod si tamen Jeremiam typum in illis pastoribus suis fuisse Christi quis dicat, facilius id tueri poterit. Siquidem via Prophetarum etiam prophetica fuerit. Unde ita concludit Hieronymus hoc caput: Ut omni interpretationis molestia liberemur, illam sequamur regulam: Quod omnes Prophetæ in ty- pum Domini Salvatoris pleraque gesserint & quic- quid juxta præsens tempus completum sit in

Hieremia, hoc in futurum de Domino prophetari. Vidit enim probe non cohærere textum, si secun- dum literam de alio, quam Jeremia intelligatur. Ideo Christi typum in eo fuisse Prophetam asserit.

Vers. eod.

DICENTES: MITTAMUS LIGNUM IN PA- NEM EJUS) LXX. ἐμβάλωμεν ξύλον εἰς τὸν ἄρτον ἀυτῦ : quomodo citat & Chrystost. περὶ τριάδ Tom. 6. Savilia- no. In Hebræo: Corrumpamus lignum in pane ejus: per hy- pallagen, pro panem ejus ligno, nempe venenato, ut re- cte hic sumfit Chaldæus. Sic taxis inesse venenum, ait Pli- nius, & inde credi toxica nomen habere 16, 11. Lucanus: Toxica fatilegi carpuns matura Sabæi. Agit autem sub hac similitudine de consiliis sacerdotum in perniciem ipsius. Vide infra 29.

TO THE MEN OF ANATHOTH) Just as no prophet is held in high regard in his own country, so also Jeremiah had no enemies more hostile to him than the priests living with him at Anathoth, who also incited the other priests against him.

THOU SHALT NOT PROPHESY IN THE NAME OF THE LORD) Do not prophesy.

AND THOU SHALT NOT DIE IN OUR HANDS) Lest you perish by us.

Vers. 21.

AD VIROS ANATHOTH) Sicut Propheta nemo magni factus in patria sua, ita & Jeremias nullos sibi ha- buit inimiciores, quam sacerdotes secum Anathothis habi- tantes, qui & cæteros sacerdotes adversus eum incitarunt.

NON PROPHETABIS IN NOMINE DOMINI) Ne vaticinare.

ET NON MORIERIS IN MANIBUS NO- STRIS) Ne per nos pereas.

Verse 23.

FOR I WILL BRING EVIL UPON THE MEN OF ANATHOTH, THE YEAR OF THEIR VISITATION) Better 'in the year', as the Greeks have it here, that is, in its own time.

Vers. 23.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

An expostulation on account of the successes of the wicked and the calamities of the righteous. Concerning the destruction of the people and neighboring nations, and their restoration and conversion to the profession of the Gospel.

Verse of the same.

AND HIS NAME BE REMEMBERED NO MORE) Let us condemn even the memory, as of a False Prophet.

Ver. 1.

RIGHTEOUS INDEED ART THOU O LORD, IF I DISPUTE WITH THEE) In Hebrew: Righteous art thou O Lord, namely thou shalt appear. Thou shalt prevail, if I contend with thee in judgment. Ps. 51, 6. I know there are causes for thee, not manifest to us.

YET I WILL SPEAK RIGHTEOUS THINGS UNTO THEE) In Hebrew: Yet I will speak judgments with thee: that is, I will deal with thee moderately, in which way משפט is taken above 10, 24. Ps. 112, 5. Let it be permitted to me not to dispute, but to wonder.

WHEREFORE DOTH THE WAY OF THE WICKED PROSPER) This thought of those times often arose to the pious because of the promises and threats pertaining to this life, which nevertheless did not take away from God the right of testing his children for a time, and thus of paving the way for the Gospel. See Job passim and Ps. 73. Concerning the wonderful prosperity of Nebuchadnezzar, the Jews bring forward many things here, and the Chaldean also draws this passage hither. I would rather judge that it concerns the priests opposing Jeremiah. Consider the following.

There is no need that we should posit here a hypallage of such a kind. Which is sufficiently perplexing. And without it, the Rabbis with the Targum explain it in the same sense: taking the word עץ in a general sense for poisonous wood. But the explanation of Forster seems to be preferred, let us cast down the tree with its fruit: because the second clause confirms it: and let us cut him off from the land of the living. For that phrase concerning the casting down and uprooting of trees is used in Deut. 20, 19. Nor does it seem inconvenient to take לחם for any food or fruit. Whence B. Luther rendered it in a similar way. The sense therefore is: the tree with its fruit, Jeremiah with his doctrine, ought to be cut off. Similarly Junius in his later translation (which Amama here confuses with the former in Anti-Barbar. pag. 714. but that they are to be distinguished and that Junius corrected his own mind is taught by B. Glaffius in Grammat. S. pag. 688.) let us destroy the stalk with its grain. Amama also agrees in the cited place. Ludovicus de Dieu suggested another sense, whose words it is pleasing to transcribe: It came into our mind that לחם signifies not only bread, but, as in the Arabic language, so also in Hebrew it often signifies flesh, and is said not only of the flesh of beasts, as Lev. 3, 10. 11. and 21, 8. Num. 28, 2. and elsewhere, but of the flesh of man, Job 6, 7. as also in another form לחום, Job 20, 23. Zeph. 1, 17: Hence therefore we translate, let us break wood into his flesh. עץ wood for wooden staves. As 2 Sam. 21, 17. וַעַץ חֲנִיתוֹ and the wood, that is, the shaft of his spear. The sense is, let us so bruise his flesh with staves, that the very woods may be corrupted and destroyed, let us kill him with the blows of spears, so that by their force even the spears themselves may be broken: whence it follows, And let us cut him off from the land of the living. Those who seek the cross of Christ in this wood, follow a private interpretation. The cross of Christ is altogether foreign to the present text. Nor can it be carved out from these words: so that one may wonder that Cornelius calls this sense most apt. But how does he fashion the cross for himself? Let us send wood into his bread, that is, instead of bread let us feed him with wood, i.e., let us crucify him. Likewise let us corrupt his bread into wood: i.e., let us pervert his bread, and send it into wood, so that instead of bread he may eat wood, that is, cudgels or a cross. Thus indeed anything can be carved out of anything, Cornelius out of wood, and wood out of Cornelius, if it be permitted to twist and bend the words of Scripture in that manner. Those among the Fathers who applied these to the cross of Christ, being ignorant of the language and Prophetic phraseology, are to be excused here, Scripture is not to be twisted for their sake.

Note here again the error of Grotius drawn from Socinus, that in the O.T. there were only promises and threats which pertain to this life. Which we have previously refuted. Nor indeed was the way paved for the pious only for the Gospel. But the Evangelical promises inculcated by the Prophets are everywhere. And that testing of the pious through the cross under the N. Testament has no less place than under the Old, just as it is manifest that promises and threats pertaining to this life are also delivered in the New Testament, and minds are also fortified against the scandal concerning the happiness of the wicked.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Expostulatio ob successus impiorum & cala- mitates proborum. De populi & gentium vicinarum excidio & restitutione ac con- versione ad professionem Evangelii.

Vers. eod.

ET NOMEN EJUS NON MEMORETUR AM- PLIUS) Etiam memoriam damnemus, ut Pseudo - Pro- phetæ.

Vers. 1.

JUSTUS QUIDEM TU ES DOMINE, SI DIS- PUTEM TECUM) In Hebræo: Justus tu Domine, nempe apparebis. Vinces, si tecum judicio contendam. Psal. 51, 6. Scio tibi causas esse, nobis non patentes.

VERUNTAMEN JUSTA LOQVAR AD TE) In Hebræo: Veruntamen judicia tecum loquar: id est, agam tecum moderate, quo modo משפט sumitur supra 10, 24. Psal. 112, 5. Liceat mihi non disputare, sed mirari.

QUARE VIA IMPIORUM PROSPERATUR) Hæc cogitatio illorum temporum piis sæpe oborta propter promissa & comminationes ad hanc vitam pertinentes, quæ tamen Deo jus non adimebant filios ad tempus explo- randi, ac sic viam sternendi Evangelio. Vide Jobum pas- sim & Pf. 73. de Nabuchodonosori mira prosperitate multa hic adferunt Judæi, & huc etiam hunc locum trahit Chal- dæus. Ego potius de sacerdotibus Jeremiæ adversantibus censeam agi. Considera sequentia.

Non opus est, ut hic hypallagen ejusmodi po- namus. Quæ satis perplexa est. Et sine illa expo- nunt sensu eodem Rabbini cum Targuim: vocem עץ generalem pro ligno venenato accipientes. Sed præferenda videtur Forsteri explicatio, dejiciamus arborem cum fructu suo: quia eam, colon alteram confirmat: & succidamus eum è terra vivorum. Nam phrasis illa de dejectione & extirpatione ar- borum adhibetur Deut. 20, 19. Neque incommo- dem videtur לחם de cibo quovis aut fructu accipe- re. Unde parili modo reddidit B. Lutherus. Sen- sus ergo est: arborem cum fructu suo, Jeremiam cum doctrina sua exscindi debere. Similiter Junius in po- steriori translatione (quam cum priori confundit hic Amama in Anti-Barbar. pag. 714. distinguenda autem esse & correxisse Junium mentem suam do- cet B. Glaffius in Grammat. S. pag. 688.) perdamus culmum cum grano ejus. Annuit etiam Amama lo- co citato. Alium sensum suggexit Ludovic. de Dieu, cujus verba adscribere placet: Nobis in men- tem venit, לחם non tantum panem, sed, ut in Lin- gua Arabica, ita & in Hebræa sæpe carnem significa- re, nec de bestiarum tantum, ut Lev. 3, 10. 11. & 21, 8. Num. 28, 2. & alibi, sed de hominis carne dici, Job. 6,7. ut & alia forma לחום, Job. 20, 23. Sophan. 1, 17: Hinc ergo vertimus, rumpamus lignum in carnem ejus. עץ lignum pro baculis ligneis. Sicut 2. Sam. 21, 17. וַעַץ חֲנִיתוֹ & lignum, id est, scapus hastæ ejus. Sensus est, baculis carnem ejus ita contundamus, ut ipsa ligna corrumpantur & perdantur, hastarum ictibus interficiamus eum, ut eorum vi vel ipsæ ha- stæ frangantur: unde sequitur, Et exscindamus eum è terra viventium. Qui in hoc ligno crucem Christi quærunt, ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sectantur. Aliena prorsus à textu præsenti est crux Christi. Nec ex- sculpi ex verbis hisce potest: ut miret Cornelium hunc sensum aptissimum dicere. Quomodo vero crucem sibi fabricat? Mittamus lignum in pane e- jus, id est, loco panis pascamus eum ligno, h. e. cruci- figamus. Item corrumpamus panem ejus in lignum: i. e. pervertamus ejus panem, & mittamus in lignum, ut pro pane comedat lignum, hoc est, fustes aut cru- cem. Ita sane quodvis ex quovis exsculpi, ex ligno Cornelius, & è Cornelio lignum poterit, si verba Scripturæ ea ratione torquere, atque inflectere li- citum sit. Qui è Patribus hæc ad crucem Christi ap- plicarunt linguæ & Phraseos Propheticæ ignari, excusandi hic sunt, non torquenda in eorum gra- tiam Scriptura.

NOta hic iterum errorem Grotii è Socino hau- ftum, quod in V. T. tantum promissa & comminationes fuerint, quæ ad hanc vitam per- tinent. Quem antea profligavimus. Neque vero tantum ad Evangelium piis via sternebatur. Sed Evangelicæ promissiones à Prophetis inculcatæ passim sunt. Et illa piorum exploratio per crucem sub N. Testam. non minus habet, quam sub Veteri, madmodum etiam promissiones & commina- tiones ad hanc vitam pertinentes in Novo Te- stamento traditas esse manifestum est, & animi muniti quoque sunt adversus scandalum de felici- tate improborum.

## 12:2
Ver. 2.

THOU HAST PLANTED THEM, AND THEY HAVE TAKEN ROOT) They are in a firm state.

THEY PROFIT AND BRING FORTH FRUIT) They grow wealthy.

YOU ARE NEAR IN THEIR MOUTH, AND FAR FROM THEIR REINS) They speak much of the law, yet they do not wish to follow it.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

PLANTASTI EOS, ET RADICEM EGERUNT) Firmo sunt in statu.

PROFICIUNT ET FACIUNT FRUCTUM) Opulescunt.

PROPE ES TU ORI EORUM, ET LONGE A RENIBUS EORUM) De lege multa loquuntur, neque tamen eam sequi volunt.

## 12:3
Vers. 3.

YOU HAVE TESTED MY HEART WITH YOU) What kind it is toward you.

GATHER THEM LIKE A FLOCK FOR THE SLAUGHTER) See what was said at Ps. 109.

SANCTIFY THEM FOR THE DAY OF SLAUGHTER) That is, prepare everything for their punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

PROBASTI COR MEUM TECUM) Quale sit erga te.

CONGREGA EOS QUASI GREGEM AD VI- CTIMAM) Vide, quæ dicta ad Pf. 109.

SANCTIFICA EOS AD DIEM OCCISIONIS) Id est, præpara omnia ad eorum pœnam.

## 12:4
Vers. 4.

HOW LONG SHALL THE LAND MOURN, AND EVERY HERB OF THE REGION WITHER, BECAUSE OF THE MALICE OF THOSE DWELLING IN IT) He gives the reasons why he prays to God that He might remove them, namely, lest the lands remain sterile on account of their sins, producing no good fruit. See below 14.

THE ANIMAL AND THE BIRD ARE CONSUMED) The animals have died of hunger, the birds have departed from despair of pasture.

BECAUSE THEY SAID: HE WILL NOT SEE OUR LATTER END) That is, God does not care about the outcomes of human affairs. Thus אַחֲרִית is taken for reward, Proverbs 23, 18.

Vers. 20.

AND YOU TEST THE REINS) That is, the desires of men. AND HEARTS) Counsels.

FOR TO YOU I HAVE REVEALED MY CAUSE) That is, I have commended it, by a metaphor. For those who commend their cause to someone, first make it known.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

USQUEQUO LUGEBIT TERRA, ET HER- BA OMNIS REGIONIS SICCABITVR, PROPTER MALITIAM HABITANTIUM IN EO) Causas reddit, cur Deum oret, ut illos tollat, nempe ne propter ipsorum peccata terræ maneant steriles, nihil bonæ frugis proferen- tes. Vide infra 14.

CONSUMTUM EST ANIMAL ET VOLU- CRE) Animalia emortua sunt fame, volucres desperatio- ne pastus abierunt.

QUONIAM DIXERUNT: NON VIDEBIT NOVISSIMA NOSTRA) Id est, non curat Deus even- tus rerum humanarum. Sic אַחֲרִית pro mercede sumitur, Proverb. 23, 18.

Vers. 20.

ET PROBAS RENES) Id est, desideria hominum. ET CORDA) Consilia.

TIBI ENIM REVELAVI CAUSAM MEAM) Id est, commendavi, per μεταφορὰν. Nam qui causam suam alicui commendant, prius eam notam faciunt.

## 12:5
IF YOU HAVE RUN WITH THE FOOTMEN AND THEY HAVE WEARIED YOU, HOW WILL YOU BE ABLE TO CONTEND WITH HORSES?) God, addressing Jeremiah, signifies that the things of which he was complaining were small, namely the insults and threats of the Anathothites, compared to those evils which the Jerusalemites were about to bring upon him.

WHEN YOU HAVE BEEN SECURE IN THE LAND OF PEACE) Supply: and yet, contrary to expectation, snares have been laid for you. The land of peace: that is, among friends and relatives, as below in verse 6.

WHAT WILL YOU DO IN THE PRIDE OF THE JORDAN?) In the Hebrew: In the height of the Jordan: That is, where the Jordan will swell with waves: with which he compares the Jerusalemite populace.

Latin:

SI CUM PEDITIBUS CURRENS LABORA- STI, QUOMODO CONTENDERE POTERIS CUM EQUIS?) Deus Jeremiam alloquens significat exigua esse de quibus querebatur, nempe contumelias & minas Ana- thothanorum, præ iis malis, quæ ipsi illaturi essent Hie- rosolymitani.

CUM IN TERRA PACIS SECURUS FUERIS) Supple, & tamen præter expectationem insidiæ tibi factæ sint. Terra pacis: id est, inter amicos & cognatos, ut infra 6.

QUID FACIES IN SUPERBIA JORDANIS?) In Hebræo: In altitudine Jordanis: Id est, ubi Jordanis fluctibus intumescet: Cum quibus comparat vulgus Hie- rosolymitanum.

## 12:6
Vers. 6. FOR EVEN YOUR BROTHERS, AND THE HOUSE OF YOUR FATHER, EVEN THEY HAVE FOUGHT AGAINST YOU, AND THEY HAVE CRIED OUT AFTER YOU WITH A FULL VOICE) The Anathothites.

DO NOT BELIEVE THEM, WHEN THEY HAVE SPOKEN GOOD THINGS TO YOU) That is, there is much less reason for you to hope for good from the Jerusalemites, even if they sometimes flatter you.

Latin:

Vers. 6. NAM ET FRATRES TUI, ET DOMUS PATRIS TUI, ETIAM IPSI PUGNAVERUNT AD- VERSUM TE, ET CLAMAVERUNT PER TE PLE- NA VOCE) Anathothani.

NE CREDAS EIS, CUM LOCUTI TIBI FUE- RINT BONA) Id est, multo minus est, quod bene spe- res de Hierosolymitanis, etiamsi interdum blandiantur tibi.

## 12:7
Vers. 7. I HAVE FORSAKEN MY HOUSE) Because all things are so corrupted, I will cease to protect the Temple itself.

I HAVE ABANDONED MY HERITAGE) I will allow the Jewish people to be led away.

I HAVE GIVEN MY BELOVED SOUL INTO THE HAND OF HER ENEMIES) Better: The beloved of my soul: i.e., the people whom I had loved. Thus the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 7. RELIQUI DOMUM MEAM) Quia adeo corrupta sunt omnia, ipsum Templum tueri desinam.

DIMISI HEREDITATEM MEAM) Populum Ju- daicum abduci sinam.

DEDI DILECTAM ANIMAM MEAM IN MA- NU INIMICORUM EJUS) Melius: Dilectionem ani- mæ meæ: i.e. populum, quem dilexeram, Ita hic Chaldæus.

## 12:8
Vers. 8. MY HERITAGE HAS BECOME TO ME AS A LION IN THE FOREST: IT HAS GIVEN ITS VOICE AGAINST ME, THEREFORE I HAVE HATED IT) Just as the roaring of a lion is a horror to men, so is this people to me, speaking impious things.

Latin:

Vers. 8. FACTA EST MIHI HEREDITAS MEA QUASI LEO IN SILVA: DEDIT CONTRA ME VOCEM, IDEO ODIVI EAM) Sicut rugitus Leonis ho- minibus horrori est, ita mihi hic populus, loquens impia.

## 12:9
Vers. 9. IS MY HERITAGE A DISCOLORED BIRD TO ME, IS IT A BIRD DYED ALL OVER?) This passage is translated and explained in various ways: most conveniently thus, if I am not mistaken: Is not my heritage (said to be) a certain discolored bird to me, and do not (therefore) (other) birds round about attack it? If any bird of a strange color comes to other birds, it is accustomed to be attacked by the others.

COME, GATHER TOGETHER ALL THE BEASTS OF THE EARTH) The Chaldeans, Syrians, Ammonites, Moabites. See the cited passage in 2 Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 9. NUMQUID AVIS DISCOLOR HEREDI- TAS MEA MIHI, NUMQUID AVIS TINCTA PER TOTUM) Varie hic locus vertitur & exponitur: com- modissime sic ni fallor: An non hereditas mea mihi (dicta) est avis quædam discolor, & an non (propterea) aves (aliæ) circumquaque ei adversabantur? Solet si qua avis peregrini coloris ad alias aves advenerit, ab aliis impeti.

VENITE, CONGREGAMINI OMNES BE- STIÆ TERRÆ) Chaldæi, Syri, Ammonitæ, Moabitæ. Vide dictum locum 2. Regum.

## 12:10
Vers. 10. MANY SHEPHERDS) Kings and Princes.

Latin:

Vers. 10. PASTORES MULTI) Reges ac Principes.

## 12:11
Vers. 11. AND IT MOURNED OVER ME) They lament, and cry out to me, and are not heard.

BECAUSE THERE IS NONE THAT CONSIDERETH IN THE HEART) Who may repent, and return to me.

Latin:

Vers. 11. LUXITQUE SUPER ME) Lamentantur, & ad me clamant, nec exaudiuntur.

QUIA NULLUS EST, QUI RECOGITET CORDE) Qui resipiscat, ad me redeat.

## 12:12
Vers. 12. UPON ALL THE WAYS OF THE WILDERNESS) Of the field, that is, from every side.

FROM THE END OF THE EARTH EVEN TO THE END OF IT) From one end to the other.

THERE IS NO PEACE) There shall be no salvation.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SUPER OMNES VIAS DESERTI) Agri, id est, ab omni parte.

AB EXTREMO TERRÆ AD EXTREMUM EJUS) Ab uno fine ad alterum.

NON EST PAX) Non erit salus.

## 12:13
Vers. 13. THEY HAVE SOWN WHEAT, AND HAVE REAPED THORNS) All their labors are vain and void.

THEY HAVE RECEIVED AN INHERITANCE, AND IT SHALL NOT PROFIT THEM) As if someone were an heir by right, but should fail in the possession.

YE SHALL BE ASHAMED OF YOUR FRUITS) Your works shall bring ignominy upon you.

BECAUSE OF THE ANGER OF THE FURY OF THE LORD) God being angry.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SEMINAVERUNT TRITICUM, ET SPINAS MESSUERUNT) Omnes eorum labores cassi atq; irriti.

HEREDITATEM ACCEPERUNT, ET NON EIS PRODERIT) Ut si quis jure heres sit, sed possessio- ne excidat.

CONFUNDEMINI A FRUCTIBUS VESTRIS) Opera vestra vobis ignominiam parient.

PROPTER IRAM FURORIS DOMINI) Deo irasceste.

## 12:14
Vers. 14. AGAINST ALL MY NEIGHBORS) The Ammonites and Moabites.

BEHOLD, I WILL PLUCK THEM OUT OF THEIR LAND, AND PLUCK OUT THE HOUSE OF JUDA FROM AMONG THEM) That is, there is no reason for them to be pleased with themselves regarding the evils which they now inflict upon the Jews: I will take care that the Jews are taken far away from them. But neither are they themselves to remain in their own places. See below 48. 49. Ezech. 25.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ADVERSUM OMNES VICINOS MEOS) Am- monitas & Moabitas.

ECCE, EGO EVELLAM EOS DE TERRA SVA, ET DOMUM JUDA EVELLAM DE MEDIO EORUM) Id est, non est, quod sibi placeant de malis, quæ nunc inferunt Judæis: Judæos longe ab ipsis auferri cura- bo. Sed nec ipsi in suis locis mansuri sunt. Vide infra 48. 49. Ezech. 25.

## 12:15
Vers. 15. AND WHEN I HAVE PLUCKED THEM OUT, I WILL RETURN AND HAVE COMPASSION) I will bring back the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET CUM EVULSERO EOS, CONVERTAR ET MISEREBOR) Judæos reducam.

## 12:16
Vers. 16. AND IT SHALL BE, IF THE LEARNED SHALL HAVE LEARNED THE WAYS OF MY PEOPLE, TO SWEAR BY MY NAME, THE LORD LIVETH, AS THEY HAVE TAUGHT MY PEOPLE TO SWEAR BY BAAL: THEY SHALL BE BUILT UP IN THE MIDST OF MY PEOPLE) That is, if the Ammonites and Moabites, who were the authors of idolatry to the Jews, now being better instructed by the Jews, betake themselves to me, that is, to the worship of the one God, they shall live peacefully in the vicinity of the Jews, with no one harming them.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET ERIT, SI ERUDITI DIDICERINT VIAS POPVLI MEI, UT JVRENT IN NOMINE MEO, VIVIT DOMINVS, SICVT DOCUERUNT POPV- LVM MEVM JVRARE IN BAAL: ÆDIFICABVN- TVR IN MEDIO POPVLI MEI) Id est, si Ammonitæ & Moabitæ, qui Judæis auctores fuerunt ad idololatriam, nunc melius à Judæis instituti ad me, id est, Dei unius cul- tum, se referant, vivent placide in vicinia Judæorum, ne- mine ipsis nocente.

## 12:17
Vers. 17. BUT IF THEY WILL NOT HEAR, I WILL PLUCK UP THAT NATION BY PLUCKING UP AND DESTRUCTION, SAITH THE LORD) Thus a part of the Ammonites was slain by Judas Maccabeus: Pella in the land of Moab was cut off in the time of Alexander, king of the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QUOD SI NON AUDIERINT, EVELLAM GENTEM ILLAM EVULSIONE ET PERDITIO- NE, AIT DOMINUS) Sic Ammonitarum pars cæsa ab Juda Maccabæo: Pellæin Moabitide excisa tempore Ale- xandri Judæorum regis.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.
