By the sign of a new girdle, and afterwards a rotten one, the rejection of Judea, which first clung to GOD, is intimated on account of pride and idolatry, with an exhortation to repentance. Humiliation is denounced to the King: and the devastation of Jerusalem on account of idolatry.

Vers. 1. GO AND GET THEE) Acquire.

GIRDLE) Περίζωμα to the Greeks, which adheres most closely to the body. Thus God had brought the Jewish people closer to Himself than other peoples. Below 11.

The people are compared to a girdle on account of purity, as the High Priest was therefore to be girded with it Ex. 28, 42. Levit. 6, 10. and dignity, because it was in use among Kings: 2. Sam. 6, 14. Ezech. 16, 10. as also for firm adhesion, which God had desired from the people.

AND THOU SHALT NOT PUT IT INTO WATER) Let that linen be rough, such as the Jewish people is,

Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Signo cinguli recentis, & postea putrefacti Judææ primum DEO adhærescentis ob su- perbiam & idololatriam abjectio intima- tur cum exhortatione ad pœnitentiam. Regi humiliatio denunciatur: & vasta- tio Hierosolymæ ob idololatriam.

Vers. 1. VADE ET POSSIDE TIBI) Acquire.

LUMBARE) Περίζωμα Græcis, quod corpori pro- xime adhæret. Sic populum Judaicum Deus præ cæteris populis proxime sibi admoverat. Infra 11.

Comparatur cingulo populus ob puritatem, uti Pontifex ideo illo cingendus erat Ex. 28, 42. Levit. 6, 10. & dignitatem, quia Regibus in usu erat: 2. Sam. 6, 14. Ezech. 16, 10. ut & firmam adhæ- sionem, quam Deus à populo desiderarat.

ET IN AQVAM NON INFERES ILLUD) Si- nes linum illud esse asperum, qualis est populus Judaicus,

## 13:4
Vers. 4. GO TO THE EUPHRATES) Whither, to be sure, the Jewish people were to be led, Psal. 137, 1.

AND HIDE IT THERE IN A HOLE OF THE ROCK) In remote and barren places, such as those were into which the Jews were led.

Latin:

Vers. 4. VADE AD EUPHRATEM) Quo scilicet ducen- dus erat populus Judaicus, Psal. 137, 1.

ET ABSCONDE IBI ILLUD IN FORAMINE PETRÆ) In locis remotis ac sterilibus, qualia fuere illa, in quæ deducti Judæi.

## 13:7
Vers. 7. AND BEHOLD, THE GIRDLE WAS ROTTEN) Thus the people wasted away in that miserable servitude, according to the predictions in Leviticus 26, 39. which what follows here explains further,

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET ECCE, COMPUTRUERAT LUMBA- RE) Sic populus in misera illa servitute contabuit, secun- dum prædicta in Levitico 26, 39. quod amplius expli- cant, quæ hic sequuntur,

## 13:12
Vers. 12. EVERY BOTTLE SHALL BE FILLED WITH WINE) An earthen flagon, as Is. 13, 12.

AND THEY SHALL SAY TO THEE: DO WE NOT KNOW THAT EVERY BOTTLE SHALL BE FILLED WITH WINE? What is new in this matter? They say this because they did not yet understand whither these circumlocutions were tending.

Latin:

Vers. 12. LAGUNCULA IMPLEBITUR VINO) Lagena fictilis, ut Es. 13, 12.

ET DICENT AD TE: NUMQUID IGNORA- MUS, QUIA OMNIS LAGUNCULA IMPLEBITUR VINO) Quid in hac re novi est? Hoc ideo dicunt, quia nondum intelligebant, quo irent istæ ambages,

## 13:13
Ver. 13. WITH DRUNKENNESS) That they may become as if senseless from the miseries. See Is. 51, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 13. EBRIETATE) Ut præmiseriis fiant velut amentes. Vide Es. 51, 17.

## 13:14
Ver. 14. AND I WILL SCATTER THEM, MAN FROM HIS BROTHER) Into various regions, with no regard for kinship. Thus, in Tacitus, Civilis, speaking of the Roman levy: The levy is pressing, by which children are separated from parents, brothers from brothers, as if for the last time. The same in Annal. XIV: Unknown to one another in different companies, without a leader, without mutual affections, as if suddenly collected into one from another race of mortals, a number rather than a colony.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DISPERGAM EOS, VIRUM A FRA- TRE SUO) In varias regiones, nulla cognationis ratione habita, Sic apud Tacitum Civilis de dilectu Romanorum a- gens: Instare dilectum, quo liberi à parentibus, fratres à fra- tribus velut supremum dividantur. Idem Annal. XIV. Ignoti in- ter se diversis manipulis, sine rectore, sine affectibus mutuis, quasi ex alio genere mortalium repente in unum collecti, nu- merus magis quam colonia.

## 13:16
Ver. 16. GIVE GLORY TO THE LORD YOUR GOD) Acknowledge your guilt, as in Jos. 7, 19. 20.

AND BEFORE YOUR FEET STUMBLE UPON THE DARK MOUNTAINS) Upon the misty mountains of Media.

YOU SHALL LOOK FOR LIGHT, AND HE WILL TURN IT INTO THE SHADOW OF DEATH, AND INTO DARKNESS) That is, at the time when God, while you look in vain for better things, will involve you more and more in adversities.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DATE DOMINO DEO VESTRO GLO- RIAM) Agnoscite culpam, ut Jos. 7, 19. 20.

ET ANTEQVAM OFFENDANT PEDES VE- STRI AD MONTES CALIGINOSOS) Ad montes Mediæ nebulosos,

EXSPECTABITIS LUCEM, ET PONET EAM IN UMBRAM MORTIS, ET IN CALIGINEM) Id est, quo tempore Deus vos frustra meliora exspectantes adversis magis magisque involvet.

## 13:17
Ver. 17. MY SOUL SHALL WEEP FOR THE FACE OF PRIDE) That is, because of your pride and contumacy.

Latin:

Vers. 17. PLORABIT ANIMA MEA A FACIE SU- PERBIÆ) Id est, propter superbiam & contumaciam vestram.

## 13:18
Ver. 18. SAY TO THE KING AND TO THE QUEEN) To Jehoiachin and his mother Nehushta, who were deported to Babylon at the first coming of Nebuchadnezzar, 2 Kings 24, 8. 15. Thus Jerome here.

Latin:

Vers. 18. DIC REGI ET DOMINATRICI) Joachi- mo & matri ejus Neheste, qui deportati sunt in Babylonem priore adventu Nabuchodonosoris, 2. Reg. 24, 8. 15. Ita hic Hieronymus.

## 13:19
ALL JUDAH IS CARRIED AWAY WITH A PERFECT CAPTIVITY) That is, this deportation will be followed by another much more severe.

Latin:

TRANSLATA EST OMNIS JUDA TRANS- MIGRATIONE PERFECTA) Id est, hanc deportatio- nem sequetur altera multo gravior.

## 13:20
Ver. 20. SEE, YOU WHO COME FROM THE NORTH) Better: See, (the Chaldeans and Medes) who come from the North: as the Chaldean has it. These are they who will bring that to effect. WHERE IS THE FLOCK, WHICH WAS GIVEN TO THEE?) He addresses the King. Behold, your people are being scattered. THY GLORIOUS CATTLE) In the Hebrew: The cattle of thy glory: because the multitude of the people is the glory of the king, Proverbs 14:28.

Latin:

Vers. 20. VIDETE, QVI VENITIS AB AQVILONE) Melius : Videte, (Chaldæos & Medos) qui veniunt ab A- quilone: quo modo habet Chaldæus. Hi sunt, qui illud effectum dabunt. UBI EST GREX, QUI DATUS EST TIBI?) Regem alloquitur. Ecce, populus tuus dispellitur. PECUS INCLYTVM TVVM) In Hebræo: Pecus gloriæ tuæ: quia multitudo populi gloria regis, Proverbio- rum 14, 28.

## 13:21
Ver. 21. FOR THOU HAST TAUGHT THEM AGAINST THEE, AND HAST LEARNED INTO THY OWN HEAD) Thou hast been a leader to them in idolatry, 2 Kings 24:9. SHALL NOT SORROWS TAKE THEE AS A WOMAN IN TRAVAIL?) Most bitter sorrows, ὠδῖνες, Matt. 24:8.

Latin:

Vers. 21. TU ENIM DOCUISTI EOS ADVERSUM TE, ET ERUDISTI IN CAPVT TVVM) Dux illis fuisti ad idololatriam, 2. Reg. 24, 9. NUMQVID NON DOLORES APPREHENDENT TE QUASI MULIEREM PARTVRIENTEM) Dolo- res acerrimi, ὠδῖνες, Matth. 24, 8.

## 13:23
Ver. 22. THY SHAMEFUL PARTS HAVE BEEN REVEALED, THY POLLUTIONS HAVE BEEN MADE PLAIN) That is, you will be led away naked and barefoot, as captives are wont to be, Is. 20:4.

Ver. 23. IF THE ETHIOPIAN CAN CHANGE HIS SKIN, OR THE LEOPARD HIS SPOTS: THEN YOU WILL BE ABLE TO DO GOOD, WHEN YOU HAVE LEARNED EVIL) You, that is, you King and your mother. This passage shows the greatest difficulty in changing habits that have been long ingrained. Evenus the old Poet: Φημὶ πολυχρόνιον μελέτην ἔμεναι, φίλε, καὶ δὴ Ταύτην ἀνθρώποισι τελευτῶσαν φύσιν εἶναι. Jerome on this passage: Whatever is learned is not nature, but of study and one's own will: which by excessive custom and love of sinning is in a way converted into nature. But this, which is impossible for men, is possible for God. Grotius does not touch the source of this evil, namely original sin. For thence and therefore it is so difficult to change evil habits, when the custom of sinning is ingrained, because the sin of nature is intimately fixed, by which we are solicited to evil, that ἁμαρτία ἐυπερίςατος, as it is called Heb. 12:1. the evil which lies close to us, and makes us captives under the law of sin, Rom. 7. for which even the saints must sigh, wretched man, who shall deliver me from the body of this death! Whence Cornelius à Lapide rashly imagines a hyperbole here. Since the whole man, as Scripture testifies, if you look at the natural state after the fall, becomes flesh of flesh, and is wholly unclean, stony, iron, dead in sins. What wonder then, if he is as unable to change his nature as the Ethiopian his skin, and the Leopard his spots? A bad tree cannot bear good fruit, Matt. 7. Therefore Estius in this place acknowledges with Jerome that this is impossible among men, possible only with God. Whose alone it is to regenerate and convert us, to take away the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh, to create and implant a new spirit, to call back from the dead into life. As therefore man cannot contribute anything to his own generation or vivification, so he cannot change his own corrupt nature. There is therefore no hyperbole here.

Latin:

Vers. 22. REVELATA SVNT VERECUNDIORA TUA, POLLUTÆ SVNT PLANE TUÆ) Id est, feminudus & excalceatus abduceris, ut captivi solent, Ef. 20, 4.

Vers. 23. SI MUTARE POTEST ÆTHIOPS PELLEM SVAM, AUT PARDUS VARIETATES SVAS: ET VOS POTERITIS BENEFACERE, CVM DIDICE- RITIS MALVM) Vos, id est, tu Rex & mater tua, Often- dit hic locus difficultatem maximam in mutandis moribus diu inplitis. Evenus vetus Poëta : Φημὶ πολυχρόνιον μελέτην ἔμεναι, φίλε, καὶ δὴ Ταύτην ἀνθρώποισι τελευτῶσαν φύσιν εἶναι. Hieronymus hoc loco : Quicquid didicitur, non natura est, sed studii & propria voluntatis: quæ nimia consuetudine & amore peccandi quodammodo in naturam convertitur. Sed hoc, quod hominibus impossibile est, Deo possibile est. Non tangit Grotius fontem hujus mali, pec- catum nempe originale. Nam inde & ideo tam diffi- cile est mutare mores malos, cum consuetudo pec- candi inolita est, quia naturæ peccatum intime infi- xum est, quo ad malum solicitamur, ἁμαρτία illa ἐυπερίςατος, ut vocatur Ebr. 12, 1. malum, quod adjacet nobis, & captivos nos facit sub legem peccati, Rom. 7. ob quod etiam sanctis suspirandum est, miser homo, quis me liberabit à corpore mortis hu- jus! Unde temere Cornel. à Lapide hic hyperbo- len fingit. Siquidem totus, Scriptura teste, homo, si naturalem statum post lapsum spectes, caro fit de carne, & immundus totus, lapideus, ferreus, in pec- catis mortuus. Quid ergo mirum, si æque uti Æ- thiops pellem, & Pardus varietatem suam mutare nequeat? Mala arbor non potest ferre fructus bo- nos, Matth. 7. Ideo Estius in h. l. agnoscit cum Hieronymo, hoc apud homines impossibile esse, apud solum Deum possibile. Cujus unius est nos regenerare, & convertere, cor lapideum auferre & carneum dare, novum spiritum creare atque in- dere, à mortuis in vitam revocare. Quam ergo non potest homo quicquam ad sui aut generatio- nem aut vivificationem conferre, tam non potest suam corruptam naturam immutare. Nulla ita- que hic hyperbole.

## 14:1 Argument
SERMON IV. THREATENING FAMINE. CHAPTER XIV. A prophecy concerning a great drought and famine in Judea: and the Prophet's prayer. A complaint about idolatry and false Prophets, upon whom he denounces punishment, as also upon the people: for whom he intercedes.

Latin:

CONCIO IV. COMMINATORIA FAMIS. CAPUT XIV. Prophetia de magna siccitate, & fame in Ju- dæa: & oratio Prophetæ. Querela de idolo- latria, & falsis Prophetis, quibus pœnam denunciat, ut & populo: pro quo intercedit.

## 14:1
Ver. 1. THE WORD OF THE LORD WHICH CAME TO JEREMIAH) This is the title of the two following chapters; formerly they were undivided. Compare above 1:2. CONCERNING THE WORDS OF THE DROUGHT) על־דברי to the Hebrews is nothing other than because of. Therefore God said these things to Jeremiah concerning the future great drought, which the Jews say occurred at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah. LXX. περὶ τῆς ἀβροχίας. Josephus calls this very thing ἀπομβρίαν in the affairs of Elijah: to the Hebrews it is called retention, namely of rain.

Latin:

Vers. 1. QUOD FACTVM EST VERBUM DOMINI AD JEREMIAM) Titulus hic est duorum capitum se- quentium; olim ea erant indivisa. Confer supra 1, 2. DE SERMONIBUS SICCITATIS) על־דברי Hebræis nihil aliud quam propter. Itaque hæc Deus dixit Jeremiæ de futura siccitate magna, quam Judæi ajunt inci- disse in initium regni Sedeciæ. LXX. περὶ τῆς ἀβροχίας. Hoc ipsum ἀπομβρίαν vocat Josephus in rebus Eliæ: Hebræis di- citur retentio, nempe pluviæ.

## 14:2
Ver. 2. JUDEA MOURNED) It will mourn, and so the rest. The mourning of the land signifies its lividness and blackness, which is wont to be born from drought, Jer. 12:4, 11. Hos. 4:3. The interpretation of Tremellius and Junius concerning the mourning of men in the land is not to be approved: because the mourning of the land itself is noted, on account of the drought. AND HER GATES HAVE FALLEN) They have been weakened. That is, the cities are exhausted, as the Greeks here also interpret and the Chaldean. THE CRY OF JERUSALEM HAS ASCENDED) Of a city in itself by no means well-watered, See Isaiah 22:9. Tacitus Hist. 5. Ver. 3. THE GREATER) That is, the chief men. SENT THE LESSER,) Their servants or domestics. TO THE WATER) Supply, to be sought. THEY CAME TO DRAW) In the Hebrew: to the cisterns: very well. See Tacitus in the cited place concerning Jerusalem. Nor does the Chaldean here say otherwise. THEY WERE CONFOUNDED) That is, they were grieved. AND COVERED THEIR HEADS) That was wont to be done in mourning. 2 Sam. 15:30.

Latin:

Vers. 2. LUXIT JUDÆA) Lugebit, & sic cætera. Luctus terræ significat livorem, & atrorem ejusdem, qui ex ficcitate nasci solet, Jerem. 12, 4. 11. Of. 4, 3. Non probanda Tremell. & Junii interpre- tatio de luctus hominum in terra: quia ipsius terræ luctus notatur, ob siccitatem. ET PORTÆ EJUS CORRUERUNT) Infirmata sunt. Id est, urbes exhaustæ, quomodo & Græci hic in- terpretantur & Chaldæus. CLAMOR JERUSALEM ASCENDIT) Urbis per se minime aquosæ, Vid. Esaiam 22,9. Tacitum Histor.5. Vers. 3. MAJORES) Id est, Viri fummates. MISERUNT MINORES, ) Servos aut Domesti- cos suos. AD AQUAM) Supple, quærendam. VENERUNT AD HAURIENDUM) In Hebræo: ad cisternas: optime. Vide Tacit. dicto loco de Hieroso- lymis. Nec aliter hic Chaldæus. CONFUSI SVNT) Id est, indoluerunt. ET OPERUERUNT CAPITA SVA) Id in luctu fieri folebat. 2. Sam. 15, 30.

## 14:4
Ver. 4. BECAUSE OF THE DEVASTATION OF THE LAND) In the Hebrew: Because of the ground crushed or broken: which the LXX interpret not badly, τὰ ἔργα τῆς γῆς ἐξέλιπεν. Ver. 5. THE HIND IN THE FIELD CALVED AND LEFT) That is, what she brought forth, she left in the field, because being destitute of pasture she had no milk with which to nourish the offspring. The hind has great care for its offspring, Plin. 8:32. Ver. 6. AND THE WILD ASSES STOOD ON THE ROCKS, THEY DREW IN THE WIND) Namely in place of water. In high places the wind is freer. AS DRAGONS) Which because of their very hot blood seek cold places: and therefore they also crave the blood of elephants, which is very cold. Plin. 8:12. THEIR EYES FAILED) That is, they were driven inward by emaciation.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PROPTER TERRÆ VASTITATEM) In Hebræo: Propter humum contritam aut fractam: quod non male in- terpretantur LXX. τὰ ἔργα τῆς γῆς ἐξέλιπεν. Vers. 5. CERVA IN AGRO PEPERIT ET RE- LIQUIT) Id est, quod peperit, reliquit in agro, quod pastu destituta lac non haberet, unde fœtum aleret. Cervæ ma- gna cura fœtus, Plin. 8, 32. Vers. 6. ET ONAGRI STETERUNT IN RUPI- BVS, TRAXERVNT VENTVM) Nempe vice aquæ. In altis locis liberior est ventus. QUASI DRACONES) Qui ob calidissimum san- guinem quærunt frigora: ideoq; & elephantis sanguinem, qui frigidissimus est, appetunt. Plin. 8, 12. DEFECERUNT OCULI EORUM) Id est, præ macie acti sunt introrfum.

## 14:7
Ver. 7. IF OUR INIQUITIES HAVE ANSWERED AGAINST US) Better: have testified against us: as the Chaldean rightly does here. O LORD DO IT FOR THY NAME'S SAKE) So deal with us, that thou mayest remember that we are thine. BECAUSE OUR AVERSIONS ARE MANY, WE HAVE SINNED AGAINST THEE) Better: if our aversions are many, we have sinned against thee. We have not offended our neighbors; it is a matter of thy right.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SI INIQUITATES NOSTRÆ RESPON- DERINT NOBIS) Melius: testificatæ sunt contra nos: ut hic recte Chaldæus. DOMINE FAC PROPTER NOMEN TUUM) Ita nobiscum age, ut memineris nos tuos esse. QUONIAM MULTÆ SVNT AVERSIONES NOSTRÆ, TIBI PECCAVIMVS) Melius: si multæ sunt aversiones nostræ, tibi peccavimus. Vicinos nostros non of- fendimus; de tuo jure agitur.

## 14:8
Ver. 8. WHY ART THOU AS A SOJOURNER IN THE LAND) Tenants are wont to exhaust the land, because it is not theirs, but this is thine. The interpretation from the Hebrew is simpler: As a stranger, or a traveler: as that word is used Gen. 23:4, Ps. 39:13. AND AS A WAYFARER TURNING ASIDE TO TARRY?) A wayfarer is not anxious about the safety of that land through which he passes. But thou dost not turn aside here, but dwellest.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QUARE QUASI COLONUS FUTURUS ES IN TERRA) Solent conductores terram exhaurire, quia ipforum non est, at hæc tua est. Simplicior est interpretatio ex Ebræo: Sicut peregrinus, aut peregrinator: uti vox ista adhibe- tur Gen. 23, 4. Pfal. 39, 13. ET QUASI VIATOR DECLINANS AD MA- NENDUM?) Viator de Salute ejus terræ, per quam trans- it follicitus non est. Tu autem hic non diverteris, sed habitas.

## 14:9
Vers. 9. WHY WILL YOU BE LIKE A WANDERING MAN, AS A STRONG MAN, WHO CANNOT SAVE?) נרדם is not found elsewhere in the Holy Scriptures. To the Arabs, دهم means to come upon, wherefore you would be like a princely man, who, coming upon someone in danger, is not strong enough to deliver him.

Vers. 25. THIS IS YOUR LOT) He speaks here to a woman, namely to the king's mother. TRUSTING IN A LIE) In idols.

Vers. 26. I HAVE UNCOVERED YOUR THIGHS AGAINST YOUR FACE, AND YOUR SHAME HAS APPEARED) That is, I will lift your garments over your head, which is accustomed to be done to women for the sake of ignominy, especially those captured by the right of war.

YOUR ADULTERIES AND YOUR NEIGHING THE WICKEDNESS OF YOUR FORNICATION) It will appear how loose you have become, by satisfying your lusts.

Vers. 27. I HAVE SEEN YOUR ABOMINATIONS) Both the idolatry and the lusts which accompanied the idolatry. WOE TO YOU, JERUSALEM, WILL YOU NOT BE CLEANSED AFTER ME? HOW LONG YET?) Better from the Hebrew: Will you not be cleansed at last? When indeed? That is, will not this so foul treatment of the King and the Queen turn you to a better mind?

BUT YOU ARE IN US O LORD) You do not pass by, and as you come upon us. You are in us both by your majestic and your gracious presence, you make your dwelling in us, Lev. 26, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QUARE FUTURUS ES VELUT VIR VA- GUS, UT FORTIS, QVI NON POTEST SALVA- RE?) נרדם alibi in sacris litteris non est. Arabibus دهم est supervenire, quare similis effes viro principi, qui super- veniens alicui periclitanti, non satis validus est ad eum liberandum.

Vers. 25. HÆC SORS TVA) Ad feminam hic loquitur, nempe ad regis matrem. CONFISA IN MENDACIO) Idolis.

Vers. 26. NUDAVI FEMORA TVA CONTRA FACIEM TVAM, ET APPARVIT IGNOMINIA TVA) Id est, attollam vestes tuas super caput tuum, quod ignominiæ causa feminis fieri solet, præsertim belli jure captis.

ADULTERIA TVA ET HINNITUS TVVS SCELVS FORNICATIONIS TVÆ) Apparebit quam laxa facta fis, libjdines tuas explendo.

Vers. 27. VIDI ABOMINATIONES TVAS) Et idolola- triam & libidines, quæ idololatriam comitabantur. VÆ TIBI, JERVSALEM, NON MVNDABE- RIS POST ME? USQVE QUO ADHVC?) Melius ex Hebræo: Non mundaberis tandem? quando vero? Id est, annon hæc tam fœda Regis & Augustæ tractatio te ad men- tem meliorem vertet?

TU AUTEM IN NOBIS ES DOMINE) Non transis, & ut fupervenis. In nobis es & majestatica, & gratiofa præsen- tia, in nobis mansionem facis, Lev. 26, 11.

## 14:10
Ver. 10.

THUS SAYS THE LORD TO THIS PEOPLE) Concerning this people. WHO HAVE LOVED TO MOVE THEIR FEET) With me neglected, they have run now here, now there, above 11, 18. I will cause them to run about exceedingly. Concerning the movement toward crimes, see Theodor. Raban. Hugo Prov. 1, 5. c. 7, 10. and especially toward spiritual fornication Jer. 2, 10. Ezech. 26, 25.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

HÆC DICIT DOMINUS POPULO HUIC) De populo hoc. QUI DILEXIT MOVERE PEDES SUOS) Me neglecto nunc huc, nunc illuc discursarunt, supra 11, 18. Faciam ut egregie discursent. De motu ad scelera Theodor. Raban. Hugo Prov. 1, 5. c. 7, 10. & imprimis ad scortationem spi- ritualem Jer. 2, 10. Ezech. 26, 25.

## 14:11
Ver. 11.

DO NOT PRAY FOR THIS PEOPLE FOR GOOD) Above 7, 16. Ver. 12. BY SWORD, FAMINE AND PESTILENCE) Which even individually would suffice. These are the three most grave instruments of divine wrath, See 1 Sam. 24.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

NOLI ORARE PRO POPULO ISTO IN BO- NUM) Supra 7, 16. Vers. 12. GLADIO, FAME ET PESTE) Quæ vel singula sufficerent, Sunt hæc tria gravissima iræ divinæ in- strumenta, Vide 1. Sam. 24.

## 14:13
Ver. 13.

AH AH AH LORD GOD: THE PROPHETS SAY TO THEM: YOU SHALL NOT SEE THE SWORD, AND FAMINE SHALL NOT BE TO YOU, BUT HE WILL GIVE YOU TRUE PEACE IN THIS PLACE) See also below 23, 17. Jeremiah brings this forward, so that he may make the guilt of the people seem lighter.

Latin:

Vers 13.

AH AH AH DOMINE DEUS : PROPHE- TÆ DICUNT EIS : NON VIDEBITIS GLADIUM, ET FAMES NON ERIT VOBIS, SED PACEM VE- RAM DABIT VOBIS IN LOCO ISTO) Vide & in- fra 23, 17. Adfert hoc Jeremias, ut leviorem faciat po- puli culpam.

## 14:14
Ver. 14.

THE PROPHETS PROPHESY FALSELY IN MY NAME) God does not accept this excuse: for the people ought not to have believed those who, by flattering, fostered vices, nor had they, by any prediction well defined and circumscribed by circumstances as is fitting, and by the event having followed, made it credible that they had a mandate from God. See Deut. 18, 22. and what is said there.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

FALSO PROPHETÆ VATICINANTUR IN NOMINE MEO) Deus hanc excusationem non re- cipit : neque enim credere debuit populus iis, qui blandien- do fovebant vitia, neque ex ulla prædictione circumstan- tiis, ita ut oportet, bene definita ac circumscripta, & secuto eventu, fidem fecerant se à Deo mandatum habere. Vide Deut. 18, 22. & ibi dicta.

## 14:15
Ver. 15.

THOSE PROPHETS SHALL BE CONSUMED, AND THE PEOPLES TO WHOM THEY PROPHESY, SHALL BE CAST OUT IN THE STREETS) Both the seducers and the seduced shall perish, Ezech. 33, 6. I WILL POUR OUT UPON THEM THEIR EVIL) In the Hebrew: Their malice, that is, the punishment corresponding to their malice.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

CONSUMENTUR PROPHETÆ ILLI, ET POPULI QUIBUS PROPHETANT, ERUNT PRO- JECTI IN VIIS) Peribunt & seductores & seducti, E- zech. 33, 6. EFFUNDAM SUPER EOS MALUM SUUM) In Hebræo: Malitiam ipsorum, id est, pœnam malitiæ re- spondentem.

## 14:17
Ver. 17. LET MY EYES SHED A TEAR BY NIGHT AND DAY) He wishes Jeremiah to speak these very words, so that the people may be terrified.

Latin:

Vers. 17. DEDUCANT OCULI MEI LACHRI- MAM PER NOCTEM ET DIEM) Hæc ipsa verba vult Jeremiam loqui, ut perterrefiat populus.

## 14:18
Verse 18.

THE PROPHET ALSO AND THE PRIEST HAVE GONE INTO A LAND, WHICH THEY KNEW NOT) את ארץ סחר אל ארץ, is to go around for the sake of trading, which the Greeks translate as ἐμπορεύεσθε: Whence also here it seems that ἐμπορεύθησαν should be read, not ἐπορεύθησαν. See Gen. 34, 10. 22. 42, 34. 2. Paral. 9, 14. Prov. 3, 14. 31, 14. Ezech. 27, 21. Therefore the sense here also is that both those false Prophets, or Scribes, as the Chaldean has it here, and the Priests equally did this, so that they might have the folly of the people as a source of gain for themselves, which we learned was true also above at 5, 21.

WHICH THEY KNEW NOT) In the Hebrew: And they did not know: That is, the Jews did not understand that they were being deceived by the tricks of charlatans.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

PROPHETA QVOQVE ET SACERDOS ABIERUNT IN TERRAM, QVAM IGNORABANT) את ארץ סחר אל ארץ, est circuire terram negoti- andi causa, quod ἐμπορεύεσθεy vertunt Græci : Unde & hic ἐμπορεύθησαν legendum videtur, non ἐπορεύθησαν. Vide Gen. 34, 10. 22. 42, 34. 2. Paral. 9, 14. Prov. 3, 14. 31, 14. Ezech. 27, 21. Ergo & hic sensus est, tam Prophetas il- los falsos, sive Scribas, ut hic habet Chaldæus, quam Sacer- dotes pariter id egisse, ut stultitiam populi sibi haberent quæstui, quod verum esse etiam supra 5, 21. didicimus.

QVAM IGNORABANT) In Hebræo : Et non co- gnoverunt : Id est, Judæi non intellexerunt se decipi agyr- tarum dolis.

## 14:19
Verse 19.

WHY THEN HAST THOU SMITTEN US, SO THAT THERE IS NO HEALING) Why then wouldst thou smite. For since the Hebrews do not have a subjunctive, they put the indicative for it. The sense is: strike more moderately.

WE LOOKED FOR PEACE, AND THERE IS NO GOOD) Repeated from that which is above at 8, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

QVARE ERGO PERCUSSISTI NOS ITA, UT NULLA SIT SANITAS) Quare ergo percuteres. Nam Hebraicum subjunctivum non habeant, pro eo ponunt in- dicativum. Sensus est : moderatius feri.

EXPECTAVIMUS PACEM, ET NON EST BONUM) Repetitum ex eo, quod supra 8, 15.

## 14:21
Verse 21.

NEITHER DO THOU DISHONOR THE THRONE OF THY GLORY) In the Hebrew: Do not cast down the throne of thy glory. Do not so despise Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

NEQVE FACIAS NOBIS CONTUMELIAM SOLII GLORIÆ TVÆ) In Hebræo : Ne dejicias solium gloriæ tuæ. Noli Judæam ita vilipendere.

## 14:22
Verse 22.

ARE THERE ANY AMONG THE VANITIES OF THE GENTILES THAT CAN CAUSE RAIN?) We seek rain, not from idols, but from thee, who art able to give it.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

NUMQUID SVNT IN SCULPTILIBUS GEN- TIVM, QVI PLVANT?) Pluviam petimus, non ab ido- lis, sed abs te, qui dare potes.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

God protests that he will not be swayed by the prayers of any saint, because he delivers the people to pestilence, the sword, famine, and captivity, because having been chastised they have not been amended. He consoles the Prophet, that he will defend him among the impious, from whom he complains that he has suffered reproach, and will bless his labors.

Vers. 1.

IF MOSES AND SAMUEL SHOULD STAND BEFORE ME) Better: If they were standing: If either Moses or Samuel, those two most loving men of this people, were alive now, they would not move me. Similar to Ezek. 14, 14. To stand, the posture of those praying among those peoples. See what has been said at Matt. 6, 5. and Luke 18, 11.

CAST THEM OUT FROM MY FACE) That is, allow them to be cast out.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Deus protestatur nullius sancti precibus se fle- ctendum, quia populum pesti, gladio, fami & captivitati tradat, quia castigatus non est emendatus. Consolatur Prophetam, quod ipsum inter impios, à quibus oppro- brium se passum queritur, defensurus, & laboribus ejus benedicturus sit.

Vers. 1.

SI STETERINT MOSES ET SAMUEL CO- RAM ME) Melius : Si starent : Si viveret nunc aut Moses, aut Samuel, duo populi hujus amantissimi, non me move- rent. Simile Ezech. 14, 14. Stare, gestus orantium in il- lis populis. Vide, quæ dicta ad Matth. 6, 5. & Luc. 18, 11.

EJICE ILLOS A FACIE MEA) Id est, patere ejici.

## 15:2
Vers. 2.

THOSE WHO ARE FOR DEATH, TO DEATH) Understand death here as plague. See what has been said at Matt. 24, 7. The sense is, it makes no difference to me how they are taken from this earth, provided they are taken. To the three kinds of death, plague, hostile sword, and famine, he adds a fourth by wild beasts in Ezek. 14, 25. But here the wild beasts will follow, not as slayers of the living, however, but as lacerators of the dead.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

QUI AD MORTEM, AD MORTEM) Mortem hic pestem intellige. Vide dicta ad Matth. 24, 7. Sensus est, nihil mea refert, quomodo ab hac terra tollantur, dum- modo tollantur. Tribus mortis generibus, pesti, gladio ho- stiti, & fami, quartum per feras addit Ezech. 14, 25. At hic feræ sequentur, non tamen ut interemtrices vivorum, sed ut laceratrices mortuorum.

## 15:3
Vers. 3.

I WILL VISIT UPON THEM FOUR SPECIES) In Hebrew: I will set over them four kinds, namely of carnivorous things, as the enumeration shows.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

VISITABO SUPER EOS QUATUOR SPECIES) In Hebræo : Præficiam illis quatuor genera, rerum scilicet carnivorarum, ut denumeratio ostendit.

## 15:4
AND I WILL GIVE THEM INTO A COMMOTION TO ALL THE KINGDOMS OF THE EARTH) Into a commotion: that is, that they may wander as vagabonds. This word is taken from Deut. 28, 25.

BECAUSE OF MANASSEH THE SON OF HEZEKIAH KING OF JUDAH, FOR ALL THAT HE DID IN JERUSALEM) That is, on account of all those sins of which Manasseh was the author, and the people the imitators. In a similar way, the sins of Jeroboam are brought forward as the cause of punishment, 1 Kings 14, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET DABO EOS IN FERVOREM UNI- VERSIS REGNIS TERRÆ) In commotionem : id est, ut vagi errent. Sumtum est hoc verbum ex Deut. 28, 25.

PROPTER MANASSEM FILIUM EZECHIÆ REGIS JUDA, SUPER OMNIBUS, QUÆ FECIT IN JERUSALEM) Id est, ob peccata illa omnia, quorum auctor fuit Manasses, imitator populus. Simili modo cau- sa pœnæ adferuntur peccata Jeroboami 1. Reg. 14, 16.

## 15:5
Vers. 5.

FOR WHO WILL HAVE PITY ON THEE, O JERUSALEM) That is, Who would have pity? Who would be so gentle that he could have pity on thee?

OR WHO WILL BE SORRY FOR THEE?) Who would grieve for thy evils? The speech grows gradually.

OR WHO WILL GO TO ASK FOR THY PEACE?) Who would wish to move a foot, to inquire how thou farest? Thus this Chaldean: שאל לשלם is so taken 2 Sam. 8, 11. 1 Chron. 8, 10. Ps. 122, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QUIS ENIM MISEREBITUR TUI JERUSA- LEM) Id est, Quis miseraretur? Quis ita effet lenis, ut tui posset misereri?

AUT QUIS CONTRISTABITUR PRO TE?) Quis indoleret tuis malis ? paulatim crescit oratio.

AUT QUIS IBIT AD ROGANDUM PRO PACE TUA?) Quis pedem movere velit, ut inquirat, quo- modo valeas? Ita hic Chaldæus : שאל לשלם sic sumi- tur 2. Sam, 8, 11. 1. Paral. 8, 10. Psal. 122, 6.

## 15:6
Ver. 6. I HAVE LABORED ASKING) In the Hebrew: I am weary of repenting: that is, of withholding my indulgence for so long against the threats of the law.

Latin:

Vers. 6. LABORAVI ROGANS) In Hebræo : Lassus sum pœnitendo : id est, indulgentiam meam tamdiu præ- stando contra legis minas.

## 15:7
Ver. 7.

AND I WILL SCATTER THEM WITH A FAN IN THE GATES OF THE LAND) I will cast them into all the borders of the land, so that indeed they may be carried away through them. I will scatter as chaff is scattered by a fan.

I HAVE SLAIN AND DESTROYED MY PEOPLE) That is, I have heretofore delivered many to the enemies to be slain, such as those who fell at Megiddo.

AND YET FROM THEIR WAYS THEY HAVE NOT RETURNED) Namely, those who were survivors of those disasters.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET DISPERDAM EOS VENTILABRO IN PORTIS TERRÆ) Disjiciam illos in omnes terminos terræ, ut nempe per eos evehantur. Disjiciam ut palea dis- jicitur ventilabro.

INTERFECI ET DISPERDIDI POPULUM MEUM) Id est, multos antehac tradidi hostibus interfi- ciendos, ut eos, qui in Mageddo ceciderunt.

ET TAMEN A VIIS SUIS NON SUNT RE- VERSI) Nempe, qui istis cladibus fuerunt superstites.

## 15:8
Ver. 8.

THEIR WIDOWS ARE MULTIPLIED UNTO ME) They shall be multiplied. And so the rest.

I HAVE BROUGHT UPON THEM AGAINST THE MOTHER OF THE YOUNG MAN A WASTER AT NOONDAY) This is, I will bring upon them him who, not by ambushes, but in broad daylight, bereaves mothers of their children. Who slaughters the son before the father's face, the father at the altars.

To speak with Virgil. He well joins the bereaved with the widows.

I HAVE BROUGHT SUDDEN TERROR UPON THE CITIES) There will be so much terror on every side that none of the smaller towns will dare to resist.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

MULTIPLICATÆ MIHI SUNT VIDUÆ EJUS) Multiplicabuntur. Et ita cætera.

INDUXI EIS SUPER MATREM ADOLESCEN- TIS VASTATOREM MERIDIE) Hoc est eum illis ad- ducam, qui non per insidias, sed clara die matres orbet liberis. Natum ante ora patris, patrem qui obtruncet ad aras.

Ut cum Virgilio loquar. Viduis bene subjicit orbos.

MISI SUPER CIVITATES REPENTE TERRO- REM) Tantum undique terroris erit, ut minorum oppi- dorum nullum resistere audeat.

## 15:9
Ver. 9.

SHE THAT HATH BORNE SEVEN IS WEAKENED, HER SOUL HATH GROWN FAINT) That is, Jerusalem, the parent of a numerous offspring, shall succumb to the enemy.

HER SUN IS GONE DOWN, WHILE IT WAS YET DAY) In the midst of the course of prosperous affairs, she was overturned.

AND THE RESIDUE I WILL DELIVER TO THE SWORD) Those who fell with Gedaliah by the hands of their own countrymen, 2 Kings 25:25.

BEFORE THEIR ENEMIES) That is, they fell for the delight and before the eyes of their enemies, as Tacitus speaks in a similar matter.

Latin:

Vers 9.

INFIRMATA EST, QUÆ PEPERIT SEPTEM, DEFECIT ANIMA EJUS) Id est Hierosolyma, nume- rosæ prolis parens succumbet hosti.

OCCIDIT EI SOL, CUM AD HUC ESSET DIES) In medio rerum secundarum cursu eversa est.

ET RESIDUOS IN GLADIUM DABO) Illos, qui cum Godolia, qui popularium suorum manibus ceci- dere, 2. Reg. 25, 25.

IN CONSPECTU INIMICORUM EORUM) Id est, oblectationi, oculisque hostium occiderunt, ut Taci- tus in re simili loquitur.

## 15:10
Vers. 10. WOE IS ME, MY MOTHER) Jeremiah speaks, complaining of the greatest hatreds which the prophecy of such things brought upon him. For obsequiousness begets friends, truth begets hatred.

WHY HAST THOU BORN ME?) Into what miseries have I been born?

A MAN OF STRIFE, A MAN OF CONTENTION TO THE WHOLE EARTH) Whom all hate, whom all attack with curses. σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον, Luke 2:34.

I HAVE NOT LENT ON USURY, NOR HATH ANY MAN LENT TO ME) Usury was forbidden among the Hebrews. Therefore it must be translated: I have neither given borrowed money to anyone, nor has anyone to me. No business of money has intervened for me with anyone, from which quarrels are accustomed to arise.

Latin:

Vers. 10. VÆ MIHI MATER MEA) Loquitur Je- remias conquerens de maximis odiis, quæ ipsi pareret ta- lium rerum vaticinatio. Nam Obfequium amicos, veritas odium parit.

QUARE GENUISTI ME?) In quas miserias sum genitus?

VIRUM RIXÆ, VIRUM DISCORDIÆ IN UNIVERSA TERRA) Quem odere, quem maledictis in- cessunt omnes. σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον, Luc. 2, 34.

NON FENERAVI, NEC FENARAVIT MIMI QUISQUAM) Fenus inter Hebræos vetitum. Itaque ver- tendum : mutuam pecuniam nec dedi ego cuiquam, nec quis- quam mihi. Nullum mihi pecuniarum negotium cum quoquam intercessit, unde lites oriri folent.

## 15:11
Vers. 11

ON JEREMIAH CHAP. XV.

Ver. 11. IF NOT THY REMNANT FOR GOOD) May I not be held truthful, unless thy final affairs shall be prosperous.

IF I HAVE NOT MET THEE IN THE TIME OF AFFLICTION, AND IN THE TIME OF TRIBULATION AGAINST THE ENEMY) Unless in the wretched and calamitous time I be a conciliator of grace for thee before the enemy. See below 40.

Latin:

Vers. 11

AD JEREM. CAP. XV.

Verf. 11. SI NON RELIQVIÆ TVÆ IN BONVM) Ne verax habear, nisi ultimæ res tuæ futuræ sint prosperæ.

SI NON OCCVRRI TIBI IN TEMPORE AF- FLICTIONIS, ET IN TEMPORE TRIBULATIO- NIS ADVERSVS INIMICVM) Nisi in tempore mise- ro ac calamitoso tibi conciliator sim gratiæ apud hostem. Vide infra 40.

## 15:12
Ver. 12. SHALL IRON BE ALLIED WITH IRON FROM THE NORTH AND BRASS) Jerome notes that there was much variety of versions here. That arose from the fact that some read ירע, as we also have, but Theodotion read ידע, he knows. Again, others derive that ירע from רעע, so that it may be 'it will harm'. Others from רעח, so that it may be 'it will be allied': in which way the Chaldean also seems to have understood it. The version most suitable to the passage seems to be this: Shall iron be able to harm both Northern iron and brass? Understand by Northern iron steel, so called from the Chalybes, a people to the north, concerning whom see Strabo 12 of the Geographica. The sense, however, is this: Be it that the Jews are hard as iron, I will be for thee as a double wall, one of steel, the other of brass.

Latin:

Verf. 12. NVMQVID FEDERABITVR FERRVM FER- RO AB AQVILONE ET ÆS) Multam hic fuisse ver- sionum varietatem notat Hieronymus. Ea inde nata, quod alii legere ירע, ut & nos habemus, Theodotio vero ידע, cognoscit. Rursum illud ירע alii derivant a רעע, ut sit noce- bit. Alii a רעח, ut sit federabitur: quomodo & Chaldæus accepisse videtur. Versio maxime loco conveniens hæc ef- se videtur: An ferrum nocere poterit & ferro Aquilonari & æri? Ferrum Aquilonare intellige chalybem, ita dictum a Chalybibus populis ad septentrionem, de quibus vide Stra- bonem 12. Geographicôn. Sensus autem hic: Esto, Judæi sint duri ut ferrum, ego tibi ero pro duplici muro, altero chalybeo, altero aheneo.

## 15:13
Ver. 13. THY RICHES FROM THE TREASURE FOR A SPOIL I WILL GIVE) Here the speech of God turns to Judea.

GRATIS) I will receive nothing for that service, content with vengeance.

IN ALL THY SINS, AND IN ALL THY BORDERS) On account of all the sins which thou hast committed in all thy borders. That which we have below 17, 3 shows us this sense. Among the sins, however, idolatry is most especially to be understood.

Latin:

Verf. 13. DIVITIAS TVAS EX THESAVRO IN DIREPTIONEM DABO) Hic sermo Dei ad Judæam se convertit.

GRATIS) Nihil pro eo munere accipiam, contentus ultione.

IN OMNIBVS PECCATIS TVIS, ET IN O- MNIBVS TERMINIS TVIS) Propter omnia peccata, quæ in finibus tuis omnibus commisisti. Hunc sensum nobis monstrat id, quod infra habemus 17, 3. Inter peccata au- tem vel maxime intelligenda idololatria.

## 15:15
Ver. 15. THOU KNOWEST O LORD, REMEMBER ME) Jeremiah speaks again, and commends himself to divine protection.

DO NOT IN THY PATIENCE TAKE ME UP) That is, do not be patient and slow in avenging my injuries. Thus, he who is under the protection of another is also said in Latin to be 'taken up' (susceptus).

Latin:

Vers. 15. TV SCIS DOMINE, RECORDARE MEI) Ite- rum Jeremias loquitur, & se tutelæ divinæ commendat.

NOLI IN PATIENTIA TVA SVSCIPERE ME) Id est, noli patiens esse, & tardus in injuriis meis vindican- dis. Sic susceptus etiam Latinis dicitur, qui in alterius est tutela.

## 15:16
Ver. 16. THY WORDS WERE FOUND, AND I DID EAT THEM) As soon as I understood thy commands, I immediately admitted them into my mind. See Ezek. 3, 1.

FOR THY NAME IS CALLED UPON ME) I rejoiced that I was called a Prophet of God.

Latin:

Verf. 16. INVENTI SUNT SERMONES TVI, ET CO- MEDI EOS) Simulatque intellexi mandata tua, statim ea in animum admisi. Vide Ezech. 3, 1.

QVONIAM INVOCATVM EST NOMEN TUUM SVPER ME) Lætabar Prophetam Dei me vocari.

## 15:17
Ver. 17. I HAVE NOT SAT IN THE COUNCIL OF THE MERRY) In the choir of those singing and dancing.

AND I HAVE GLORIED) Nor have I exulted. That is, nothing has been sweet to me since that time.

FROM THE FACE OF THY HAND I SAT ALONE) Because of the commands imposed upon me, I am deserted by all.

BECAUSE THOU HAST FILLED ME WITH THREATENING) Because all the prophecies which thou hast imposed upon me are mine.

Latin:

Verf. 17. NON SEDI IN CONCILIO LVDENTIVM) In choro cantantium & saltantium.

ET GLORIATVS SVM) Neque exsultavi. Id est, nihil mihi ab eo tempore fuit dulce.

A FACIE MANVS TVÆ SOLVS SEDEBAM) Propter mandata mihi imposita desertus sum ab omnibus.

QVONIAM COMMINATIONE IMPLESTI ME) Quia omnia vaticinia, quæ mihi imposuisti, sunt mi- ac ia.

## 15:18
Verf. 18. WHY IS MY PAIN PERPETUAL) Better: would it become. And soon: would refuse to be healed. Why do you allow me to be perpetually oppressed?

IT HAS BECOME TO ME AS A LIE OF UNFAITHFUL WATERS) More correctly: And you would become to me deceitful, like unfaithful waters: which roar much in winter, but do not appear in summer. Compare Job 6, 15.

Latin:

Verf. 18. QVARE FACTVS EST DOLOR MEVS PER- PETVVS) Melius: fieret. Et mox: renueret curari. Cur pa- tereris me perpetuo opprimi?

FACTA EST MIHI QVASI MENDACIVM AQVARVM INFIDELIVM) Rectius: Et fieres mihi fallax, ut aquæ infideles: quæ hyeme multum strepunt, æ- state non comparent. Confer Jobum 6, 15.

## 15:19
Vers. 19. IF THOU WILT CONVERT, I WILL CONVERT THEE) Better: Because you turn, to where I turn you. That is, you are ready for all my commands.

AND THOU SHALT STAND BEFORE MY FACE) You stand: i.e., and because you minister to me. For that is what it means to stand before someone. See Deut. 10, 8, and what we said at Matt. 18, 10.

THOU SHALT BE AS MY MOUTH) You are as my mouth. You faithfully report what I have commanded you. The same manner of speaking in Exod. 4, 16.

THEY SHALL CONVERT TO THEE, AND THOU SHALT NOT CONVERT TO THEM) They will ask you, not you them. See this fulfilled in 42, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 19. SI CONVERTERIS, CONVERTAM TE) Me- lius: Quia berteris, quo te verto. Id est, ad cuncta imperia mihi præsto es.

ET ANTE FACIEM MEAM STABIS) Stas: i. e. & quia ministras mihi. Id enim est stare coram aliquo. Vi- de Deut. 10, 8. & quæ diximus ad Matth. 18, 10.

QVASI OS MEUM ERIS) Quasi os meum es. Fi- deliter refers, quæ tibi imperavi. Idem loquendi genus Exod. 4, 16.

CONVERTENTVR IPSI AD TE, ET TV NON CONVERTERIS AD EOS) Illi te rogabunt, non tu illos. Vide impletum hoc 42, 2.

## 15:20
Vers. 20. AND I WILL GIVE THEE TO THIS PEOPLE AS A STRONG BRAZEN WALL) You will overcome all their blows.

AND THEY SHALL FIGHT AGAINST THEE, AND SHALL NOT PREVAIL) They will indeed vex you in many ways, but they will not take your life from you.

SERMON V. Concerning the taking away of the voice of the Bridegroom and the Bride, and the cause of such great divine wrath.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET DABO TE POPULO HUIC IN MVRVM ÆNEVM FORTEM) Superabis omnes illorum ictus.

ET BELLABUNT ADVERSVM TE, ET NON PRÆVALEBVNT) Multis quidem modis te vexabunt, sed vitam tibi non auferent.

CONCIO V. De auferenda voce Sponsi & Sponsæ, & causa tantæ iræ divinæ.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI.

The Lord forbids the Prophet to take a wife, announcing that the Jews will perish by various kinds of death on account of idolatry and the abandoned law of the Lord: yet promising restoration and the calling of the Gentiles.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI.

Prohibet Dominus, ne uxorem ducat Prophe- ta, denuncians varie mortis genere Judæos interituros, propter Idololatriam & dere- lictam legem Domini: promittens tamen restitutionem & gentium vocationem.

## 16:2
Vers. 2. THOU SHALT NOT TAKE A WIFE, AND THERE SHALL BE NO SONS AND DAUGHTERS TO THEE IN THIS PLACE) He forbids Jeremiah to take a wife and beget children, on account of the imminent evils, by which it is better for one to be exposed than many. See Paul, 1 Cor. 7, 29.

Latin:

Vers. 2. NON ACCIPIES UXOREM, ET NON ERUNT TIBI FILII ET FILIÆ IN LOCO ISTO) Vetat Je- remiam uxorem ducere, & liberos gignere, propter mala imminentia, quibus satius unum exponi, quam plures, Vi- de Paulum 1. Cor. 7, 29.

## 16:4
Vers. 4. BY DEATHS OF SICKNESSES) By pestilence, as above 15, 2. for it follows concerning famine and the sword.

Latin:

Vers. 4. MORTIBUS ÆGROTATIONUM) Peste, ut supra 15, 2. nam de fame & gladio sequitur.

## 16:5
Vers. 5. ENTER NOT INTO THE HOUSE OF FEASTING) That is, be an example to them even now, so that they may learn to lack all signs of joy, as all things will shortly be taken away from them. The things which follow below in verse 9 suggest this meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 5. NE INGREDIARIS DOMINUM CONVI- VII) Id est, jam nunc exemplum illis esto, ut discant carere omnibus gaudii signis, ut quæ brevi omnia ab ipsis erunt au- ferenda. Hunc sensum suggerunt, quæ sequuntur infra 9.

## 16:6
Vers. 6. AND THEY SHALL NOT CUT THEMSELVES, NOR SHALL BALDNESS BE MADE FOR THEM) Which customs many had indeed taken from their neighbors, having spurned the law which exists in Leviticus 19, 27. 28. Deut. 14, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET NON SE INCIDENT, NEQVE CAL- VITIUM FIET PRO EIS) Quos scilicet mores multi à vicinis sumserant, spreta lege, quæ extat Levitici 19, 27. 28. Deut. 14, 1.

## 16:7
Vers. 7. THEY SHALL NOT BREAK BREAD AMONG THEM FOR THE MOURNER, AND THEY SHALL NOT GIVE THEM THE CUP OF CONSOLATION TO DRINK FOR THEIR FATHER AND FOR THEIR MOTHER) For it was the custom, as the Hebrews note, for feasts and wine, the very best, to be sent by friends to those mourning. See Ezek. 24, 17. It appears that both this interpreter and the LXX read לחם and not לוח, undoubtedly better. Jerome here notes a not dissimilar custom of the Greeks in ἐν περιδείπνοις, and of the Latins in the Parentalia.

Grotius prefers the Vulgate interpretation and the LXX interpreters to the authentic text: and he wishes it to be read no differently in our codices than in their time. But an argument from a different interpretation to a different reading of the original text is too weak. The LXX rendered the sense, they did not express word for word. However, with the reading of the Hebrew text (which we acknowledge as uniquely true) retained, the same sense results: And they shall not extend or distribute להם to them over the mourning for consolation: because to distribute, even when placed absolutely, is used regarding the distribution of bread, Psalm 112, 9. Lam. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 7. NON FRANGENT INTER EOS LUGEN- TI PANEM, ET NON DABUNT EIS POTUM CA- LICIS AD CONSOLANDUM SUPER PATRE SUO ET MATRE SVA) Mos enim erat, ut notant Hebræi, lugentibus mitti ab amicis & epulas, & vinum, longe opti- ma. Vide Ezech. 24, 17. Apparet & hunc interpretem, & LXX. legisse לחם non לוח, melius haud dubie. Non dissimilem morem Græcorum ἐν περιδείπνοις, & Latinorum in Parentalibus notat hic Hieronymus.

PRæfert Grotius interpretationem vulgatam, & LXX. Interpp. textui authentico: ac secus non legi vult in Codicibus nostris, quam istorum tem- pore. At argumentum ab interpretatione diversa, ad diversam lectionem textus originalis nimis im- becille est. Sensum reddidere LXX. non verbum verbo expressere. Retenta autem lectione textus Ebræi (quem unice verum agnoscimus) idem sen- sus redundat: Et non extendent seu distribuent להם eis super luctum ad consolandum: quia distribuere etiam absolute positum de panis distributione usur- patur, Psal. 112, 9. Thren. 4.

## 16:8
Vers. 8. THE VOICE OF JOY AND THE VOICE OF GLADNESS, THE VOICE OF THE BRIDEGROOM AND THE VOICE OF THE BRIDE) He repeats from those things which are above in 7, at the end.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VOCEM GAUDII ET VOCEM LÆTITIÆ, VOCEM SPONSI ET VOCEM SPONSÆ) Repetit ex iis, quæ supra 7. in fine.

## 16:10
Vers. 10. WHEREFORE HATH THE LORD SPOKEN AGAINST US) Compare what is above 13, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUARE LOCUTUS EST DOMINUS SUPER NOS) Confer quæ supra 13, 22.

## 16:12
Vers. 12. EVERY ONE WALKETH AFTER THE STUBBORNNESS OF HIS EVIL HEART) No desire so wicked occurs to you that you do not fulfill it in deed.

Latin:

Vers. 12. AMBULAT UNUSQUISQUE POST PRAVITA- TEM CORDIS SVI MALI) Nulla tam prava vobis in- cidit cupido, quam non opere impleatis.

## 16:13
Vers. 13 AND THERE YE SHALL SERVE STRANGE GODS DAY AND NIGHT) That is, you shall serve the peoples who serve those gods, as the Chaldean here interprets excellently. For he who commands the Lord seems also to command the servant.

There is no reason to move from the proper meaning of the word to an improper one. For why should it not be understood by these words that they are to serve strange gods themselves, just as they have it ῥητῶς?

Verse same. WHO SHALL NOT GIVE YOU REST) You may translate it very well to connect with the sense that follows: until I have had mercy on you.

Latin:

Vers. 13 ET SERVIETIS IBI DIIS ALIENIS DIE AC NOCTE) Id est, servietis populis, qui illis diis serviunt, ut hic optime interpretatur Chaldæus. Videtur enim, qui Domino imperat, & servo imperare.

Non est cur à propria vocis significatione ad impropriam accedatur. Cur enim per hæc verba non ipsis diis alienis servituri intelligantur, uti ῥη- τῶς habent?

Vers. eod. QUI NON DABUNT VOBIS REQUIEM) Optime ad sensum, qui sequitur, connectendum vertas: donec vestri misertus fuero.

## 16:14
Verse 14. THEREFORE BEHOLD THE DAYS SHALL COME) For indeed, behold the days shall come. The reason for the last statement is given.

IT SHALL NO MORE BE SAID) That is, new benefits will obscure the memory of the old; just as new songs are more pleasing.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PROPTEREA ECCE DIES VENIENT) Etenim, ecce venient dies. Causa redditur postremi dicti.

NON DICETUR ULTRA) Id est, nova beneficia obscurabunt veterum memoriam; sicut magis placent no- va cantica.

## 16:15
Ver. 15. OF THE LAND OF THE NORTH) Concerning Media and the places neighboring it. Ver. 16. BEHOLD, I WILL SEND MANY FISHERS, SAITH THE LORD, AND THEY SHALL FISH THEM) Those fishers are the Chaldeans, who caught the Jews from everywhere, as if with a casting-net or a drag-net. AND AFTER THESE THINGS I WILL SEND THEM MANY HUNTERS, AND THEY SHALL HUNT THEM FROM EVERY MOUNTAIN, AND FROM EVERY HILL, AND FROM THE CAVERNS OF THE ROCKS) Those hunters are the Persians, who will gather the Jews from all places. Ver. 17. MINE EYES ARE UPON ALL THEIR WAYS) Both evil and good. Ver. 18. AND I WILL RECOMPENSE FIRST DOUBLE THEIR INIQUITIES AND THEIR SINS) I will not bring them back before I have punished them most severely. The mention of double punishment is in the same sense as Isaiah 42:3, to which these words seem to look back. The Chaldean interprets ראשונה משנה as first and second: the first who were carried away under Jeconiah, the second who were under Zedekiah. IN THE CARCASSES OF THEIR IDOLS) In the corpses of their gods. That is, in human victims. See below 19:5. & Ezek. 16:20. AND WITH THEIR ABOMINATIONS) With their idols. Ver. 19. O LORD MY STRENGTH) Jeremiah seizes upon God's promise concerning the bringing back of the people, and approves it with joy. TO THEE THE GENTILES SHALL COME) Great flocks of Jews. TRULY OUR FATHERS POSSESSED A LIE, VANITY, WHICH DID NOT PROFIT THEM) They had their hopes badly placed: they will say this, taught by experience. Ver. 20. SHALL A MAN MAKE GODS FOR HIMSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT GODS?) That is, who are not God. Can it be that human audacity has taken that right to itself, of making gods out of non-gods? Tertullian in his Apology: Among you, divinity is weighed by human judgment: unless God pleases man, He will not be God: man will now have to be propitious to God. Ver. 21. THEREFORE BEHOLD I WILL SHOW THEM FOR THIS TIME, I WILL SHOW THEM MY HAND, AND MY MIGHT) God answers the Prophet, because the Jews had admitted a thing so foul, as Jeremiah confesses, that He would give manifest indications of His Divinity. Understand the hand in punishing them, the might or power in bringing them back. AND THEY SHALL KNOW, THAT MY NAME IS THE LORD) יהוה, that is, He who is constant to me in promises. See Exod. 6:2. As for ver. 16, not a few understand this prophecy concerning the penal fishing and hunting of enemies, because enemies from everywhere would pursue the Jews, in the manner of hunters killing wild beasts, and fishermen pulling out fish with hooks. Which sense is confirmed both from the use of this similitude, which is accustomed to be applied to tyrants: see Gen. 10:9, Amos 4:2, Hab. 1:14, as also Ezek. 12:13, and from the context: because the following verse 17 teaches that the discourse is about the vengeance of God, before whose eyes iniquity is not hidden. Thus Theodoret, Thomas, Lyranus, Vatablus, Capella, and de Castro, and most Calvinist interpreters, as well as the Hebrews. Grotius prefers to understand it of the friendly fishing and hunting of the Chaldeans and Persians done for the sake of the restoration of the Jews. But most of the ancients interpret the prophecy concerning spiritual fishing and hunting: which was to be in the New time through the Apostles and other Evangelical Teachers. Which sense Amama in Anti-Barb. Bibl. rashly imputes to the Postillators, since it has been handed down by the Fathers: Origen Hom. 12 in Jer., Tertull. l. 1 c. Marc. c. 3, Ambrose serm. 6 in Ps. 118, and Jerome, who highly approved of it, and who teaches that it was the same for Christian doctors. Different, he says, is the interpretation of this chapter. For the Jews think that the Chaldeans are signified, who are described by the name of fishers, and afterwards the Romans who are compared to hunters, and hunted the unhappy people from the mountains and hills and caverns of the rocks. But the Lord says that He did this: because He looked upon their ways, and recompensed the iniquities with which they had contaminated the land, venerating idols, and

polluted His inheritance with the abominations of their idols. But our people think more rightly and better that the Prophet prophesied this concerning the future. For because he had said above: I will bring them back into their land, which I gave to their fathers: now he shows how they are to be brought back, that first He sends the Apostles, to whom the Savior said: Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men: And afterwards hunters, whom we can take to be either ecclesiastical men or angels. Nor does the context seem to disagree. For that the promise is made concerning benefits, not a threatening of punishment, the preceding verses teach, ver. 15, in which the restoration of the Israelites is promised: whence the Prophet could easily, according to the prophetic custom, turn from that to the spiritual liberation and restoration of the Messiah: if you take those with some others concerning the bodily restoration of the Israelites: which, however, are also more rightly explained concerning the spiritual, as will be evident in the parallel passage chapter 23:7. Although indeed it is a question of the eyes of God looking upon iniquities in v. 17, and a threatening is added of recompensing iniquities in v. 18, yet the Prophet not obscurely hints that the benefit of spiritual fishing will follow this punishment, when he says: And I will recompense FIRST double their iniquities, and their sins: which Grotius paraphrases thus: I will not bring them back before I have punished them most severely. Which emphatic word Jerome here rightly observed. It should be known that FIRST is placed in the Hebrew, and omitted in the LXX edition. But when He says: I will recompense first double their iniquities and their sins, He shows: that after they have received evils, they are also to receive goods. But these who are afterwards to be transferred, contaminated the land of the Lord with the carcasses of their idols, and filled His inheritance with their abominations, so that the whole world might be made subject to God, and by no means be preserved by its own merit, but by His mercy. The prayer of the Prophet, or address, by which he turns himself to God, also favors this explanation: inasmuch as in v. 19 he prophesies that the gentiles will be called to God. For thus spiritual fishing and the conversion of the gentiles to God cohere. Finally, it makes for this, that in Ez. 47:10 this benefit is promised under the same similitude of fishers. I do not see why I should entirely reject this opinion, approved by the ancients and our Brentius, which the Belgian paraphrasts also praise: especially because the Prophet next adds: O Lord, my strength, to thee the gentiles shall come from the ends of the earth, i.e. he will not only fish and hunt for Israelites from every side, but will also bring in Gentiles from the ends of the earth. Cf. John 11:32; Rom. 10:18 ff. Pappus also approves of it, although interpolated a little differently: Nor does the Prophet stop here, but teaches further what is to become of the people who are brought back. For at this beginning, fishers are promised who will gather them into the net of the Church: namely, the Apostles and other ministers of the New Testament, appointed fishers of men by the Lord Himself. But then, because most were going to show themselves disobedient to these fishers, the Lord also threatens them with hunters, i.e., most bitter enemies, the Romans, who would eventually destroy the whole people. Although there are some among the interpreters who take both fishers and hunters as enemies; and again, others who take both as Apostles and heralds of grace. But the former exposition seems more suited both to the words of the Prophet and to the event itself. For those whom the fishers, the Apostles, could not draw into the obedience of faith, those the Roman hunters, by the just judgment of God, destroyed. This is Pappus. Jerome also accepted what follows in this sense: Shall a man make gods for himself, and they are not gods? And the Gentiles speak this, who have come to the Savior from the ends of the earth, mocking both their own ignorance and that of their ancestors, by which they thought that gods could be made by man, when it is God's prerogative to make men. Therefore, behold, I will show them my hand, etc. The hand of God, through which He has wrought all things, and the power, of which the Apostle spoke, 'Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God,' is shown to the nations, the passion of the Son being completed. And he said beautifully: 'I will show them by this turn: I will show them manifestly, and not as before, in shadow and in image, and in the prophecy of future things, so that after they have known, they may know my name, and hear from the Son: Father, I have manifested your name to men.' And thus he also adapts the prophecy immediately joined to the following chapter: THE SIN OF JUDAH IS WRITTEN WITH A PEN OF IRON, etc. Concerning the nations that had been converted to the Lord, it was said above: 'Behold, I will show them by this turn, I will show them my hand and my power.' Now he speaks of Israel, who has been cast off: The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, with the point of a diamond, and the rest. Brentius also noted this connection (συνέχειαν) of the chapters.

in Christ, a mere man, as he believes, to be worshipped. He says not simply, in Antivvujeco page 147, that this man is pronounced cursed here, who trusts in man, but he who trusts in such a way that he makes flesh his arm, that is, places his hope in human powers themselves, or in man himself by himself, apart from the work of the spirit and divine power: for this is entirely signified by the word 'flesh.' Afterwards he denies that he trusts in Christ the man in such a way that he attributes to his human powers, apart from the spirit and power proceeding from that one God, the ability to bring us aid. Resp. (1.) That the words of the Prophet joined below are not restrictive, but rather explanatory (ἐξηγητικὰ), is too manifest: Namely, as many as trust in man, they make flesh their arm: because man is nothing but flesh; and confidence is so constituted that one expects help, support, protection, and other things of that kind from him in whom he trusts, which is the same as making him one's arm. Because it is most customary for the arm to be taken for power and strong help. See 1 Sam. 2:31, Job 22:8, ch. 35:9, Jer. 48:25, Isa. 30:22, ch. 31:17, ch. 22:6, Zech. 11:17. (2.) If only he is cursed who trusts in man by himself, apart from the help of the spirit and divine power, trust or confidence could be placed in man, provided the help of divine power is not excluded; and thus this will not strike those who place their trust in any man whatsoever with the hope of divine help. Which is absurd. (3.) No less is he pronounced cursed here who trusts in man than he who makes flesh his arm. (4.) Moreover, any man is called flesh, as a fragile and weak thing, which is denoted by that word in Psalm 56 and 78:39, Isa. 31:3. that man is indiscriminately designated by the word 'flesh,' without regard for that opposition of divine power, is evident from various places where 'flesh' is used for man: Gen. 6:2, Ps. 65:3 & 145:21, Isa. 40:6, Luke 3:6, Rom. 3:20, 1 Cor. 1:29. But where 'flesh' is placed simply, or used to explain the word 'man' without an explicit antithesis (ἀντίθεσιν) of the spirit in the Old Testament, it is used in the Socinian sense to denote a man devoid of divine power; this has not yet been shown. (5.) Moreover, it is clear by no evidence that confidence in man is pronounced cursed here in that way at least, by which divine help is postponed, but rather it is implied that divine help is postponed by that very fact, while one trusts in man: for he is said to depart in heart from the Lord. Therefore (6.) the Lord alone is proposed here as the object of trust: as He who alone tests the hearts and reins to give to each according to his way, verse 10. and from whom alone is the blessing, verse 7. And therefore Jehovah alone is called the expectation of Israel, and those who forsake Him are put to shame, v. 13. (7.) The Israelites could have equally retorted to this accusation (κατηγορίαν) of the Prophet, that while they trusted in strange gods, or even placed their trust in men, they did not, however, postpone divine help. But would they have escaped the lightning of the divine curse by that reasoning? (8.) Add that Schlichting, in his Disputation on the Trinity against Meisner, page 335, admits that the same sentiment is repeated here, in the manner of the Hebrews, and 'flesh' is put for 'man.' But the fact that he retorts that Christ is by no means a common man and similar to others, that has nothing to do with the matter: since, as has been shown, we are forbidden to trust simply in him who is a mere man, whether he be considered a common man or a divine one. Socinus also seizes upon this, that it is added here, 'and his heart departs from the Lord,' so that, namely, it may be understood that God will have some regard for those who, although they trust in some man more than is right, attributing to human powers what is proper to God Himself, nevertheless do not meanwhile fail from God Himself, nor hold a mind averted or alienated from Him. Thus also Soci-

Latin:

Vers. 15. DE TERRA AQVILONIS) De Media & vicinis ei locis. Vers. 16. ECCE, EGO MITTAM PISCATORES MVLTOS, DICIT DOMINVS, ET PISCABVNTVR EOS) Piscatores isti sunt Chaldæi, qui Judæos undique vel- ut ἀμφιβλήσρῳ, sive everriculo cepere. ET POST HÆC MITTAM EIS MVLTOS VE- NATORES, ET VENABVNTVR EOS DE OMNI MONTE, ET DE OMNI COLLE, ET DE CAVER- NIS PETRARVM) Venatores isti sunt Persæ, qui ex omnibus locis Judæos recolligent. Vers. 17. OCVLI MEI SVPER OMNES VIAS EO- RVM) Malas ac bonas. Vers. 18. ET REDDAM PRIMVM DVPLICES INIQVI- TATES ET PECCATA EORVM) Non ante eos re- ducam, quam gravissime eos punierim. Duplicis pœnæ mentio eodem sensu Esaæ 42, 3. quo videntur hæc verba respicere Chaldæus: ראשונה משנה interpretatur primis & secundis: primis qui avecti sub Jechonia, secundis qui sub Sedecia. IN MORTICINIS IDOLORVM SVORVM) Cadaveribus deorum suorum. Id est, victimis humanis. Vide infra 19, 5. & Ezech. 16, 20. ET ABOMINATIONIBVS SVIS) Idolis. Vers. 19. DOMINE FORTITVDO MEA) Arripit Je- remias pollicitationem Dei de reducendo populo, & cum gaudio approbat. AD TE GENTES VENIENT) Magni greges Ju- dæorum. VERE MENDACIVM POSSEDERUNT PA- TRES NOSTRI, VANITATEM, QUÆ EIS NON PROFVIT) Spes habuerunt male collocatas: hoc dicent experimento edocti. Vers. 20. NVNQUID FACIET SIBI HOMO DEOS, ET IPSI NON SVNT DII?) Id est, qui Dei non sunt. Fieri- ne potest, ut humana audacia id jus sibi sumserit, ex non diis faciendi deos? Tertullianus Apologetico: Apud vos de hu- mano arbitratu divinitas pensitatur: nisi homini Deus placue- rit, Deus non erit: homo jam Deo propitius esse debebit. Vers. 21. ICCIRCO ECCE EGO OSTENDAM EIS PER VICEM HANC, OSTENDAM EIS MANUM MEAM, ET VIRTUTEM MEAM) Respondet Deus Prophetæ, quia rem tam fœdam, Jeremia fatente, admiserant Judæi se manifesta daturum Divinitatis suæ indicia. Manum intel- lige in illis puniendis, virtute sive potentiam in reducendis. ET SCIENT, QVIA NOMEN MIHI DEUS) יהוה, id est, qui in promissis mihi constem. Vide Exod. 6, 2. Quod ad vers. 16. non pauci intelligunt hanc Prophetiam de piscatura & venatura hostium pœ- nali, quod undiquaque hostes persequuturi sint Ju- dæos, more venatorum feras interficientium, & pi- scatorum hamis pisces extrahentium. Qui sensus firmatur tum è similitudinis hujus usu, quæ solet de tyrannis adhiberi: vide Gen. 10, 9. Amos 4, 2. Ha- bac. 1, 14. ut & Ezech. 12, 13. tum è contextu: quia de vindicta Dei, coram cujus oculis occultata non est iniquitas, sermonem esse versus sequens 17. docet. Ita Theodoretus, Thomas, Lyranus, Vatablus, Capella, & de Castro, Calviniani pleriq́, Interpp. ut & Ebræi. Grotius mavult intelligere de amica piscatura & venatura Chaldæorum & Persarum reductionis Ju- dæorum causa facta. Veteres autem pleriq; inter- pretantur vaticinium de piscatura & venatura spiri- tuali: quæ sub Novo tempore per Apostolos, a- liosque Evangelicos Doctores futura erat. Quem sensum temere imputat Amama in Anti-Barb. Bibl. Postillatoribus, quum à Patribus traditus sit: Orige ne Hom. 12. in Jer. Tertull. l. 1. c. Marc. c. 3. Ambro- sio serm. 6. in Psal. 118. & Hieronymo valde se proba- rit, qui eundem doctorum Christianorum fuisse do- cet. Diversa, inquit, hujus capituli interpretatio est Judæi enim autumant significari Chaldæos, qui fue Piscatorum nomine describuntur, & postea Romanos qui venatoribus comparantur, & de montibus colli busq́, & cavernis petrarum infelicem populum sun venati. Hoc autem Dominus fecisse se dicit: quia re spexerit vias eorum, & reddiderit iniquitates, quibu contaminaverant terram, simulacra venerantes, &

abominationibus idolorum polluerunt hæreditatem ejus. Nostri autem rectius & melius hac de futuro va- ticinatum Prophetam putant. Quia enim supra di- xerat: Reducam eos in terram suam, quam dedi pa- tribus eorum:nunc ostendit, quomodo reducendi sint, quod primum mittat Apostolos, quibus Salvator di- xit: Venite post me, & faciam vos piscatores ho- minum: Et postea venatores, quos vel ecclesiasticos viros, vel angelos possumus accipere. Neq; videtur re- fragari contextus. Nam quod de beneficiis promis- sio fiat, non pœnæ comminatio, antecedentia do- cent vers. 15. quibus promissa est reductio Israëlitæ- rum:unde facile pro more prophetico ab eadem se convertere ad spiritualem liberationem & redu- ctionem Messiæ poterat Propheta: si illa cum non- nullis de corporali reductione Israëllitarum accipias: quæ tamen etiam de spirituali rectius exponuntur, ut loco parallelo cap. 23, 7. constabit. Quamvis ve- ro de oculis Dei respicientibus iniquitates v. 17. agatur, & comminatio subjungatur reddendarum iniquitatum v. 18. hanc pœnam tamen consequu- turum beneficium piscaturæ spiritualis, non obscu- re innuit Propheta, cum ait: Et reddam PRIMUM duplices iniquitates, & peccata eorum: quod ita πα- ραφράζει Grotius: Non ante eos reducam, quam gra- vissime eos punierim. Quam vocem emphaticam observavit hic probe Hieron. Sciendum, quod in Hebraico positum sit PRIMUM, & in LXX. editione prætermissum. Quando autem dicit: Reddam pri- mum duplices iniquitates & peccata eorum, sub- ostendit: quod postquam receperint mala, recepturi sint & bona. Hi autem qui postea transferendi sunt, contaminaverunt terram Domini in morticiniis ido- lorum suorum, & abominationibus suis impleverunt hæreditatem ejus, ut omnis mundus subditus fiat Deo, & nequaquam suo merito, sed illius misericordia con- servetur. Favet etiam huic explicationi oratio Pro- phetæ, vel προσφώνησις, qua se ad Deũ convertit: siquidem v. 19. vaticinetur, gentes ad Deum voca- tum iri. Nam ita cohærent spiritualis piscatura, & gentium ad Deum conversio. Deniq; facit huc. quod Ez. 47, 10. sub eadem similitudine piscatorum hoc beneficium promissum sit. Sententiam hanc vete- ribus & Brentio nostro probatam, quam etiam pa- raphrastæ Belgici laudant, non video, cur reprobare omnino debeam: imprimis quia proxime subjun- git Propheta: Domine, fortitudo mea, ad te gentes ve- nient ab extremis terræ, q.d. non tantum piscabitur & venabitur Israëlitas undequaq; sed adducet etiam gentiles inde ab extremis terræ finibus. Conf. Joh. 11, 32. Rom. 10, 18. seqq. Probat eam etiam Pappus, etsi paulo aliter interpolatam: Neq; hic consistit Pro- pheta, sed ulterius etiam docet, quid de populo reduce futurum sit. Huic enim initio piscatores promittun- tur, qui ipsos in sagenam Ecclesiæ colligant: Apostoli videlicet, & cæteri ministri N. T. piscatores hominum constituti ab ipso Domino. Deinde vero, quia plerique his piscatoribus immorigeros sese præstituri erant, comminatur iis quoque Dominus venatores, i. e. hostes acerrimos, Romanos, qui totum tandem populum de- leturi sint. Quanquam sunt ex interpretibus, qui & piscatores & venatores pro hostibus: rursus etiam, qui utrosque pro Apostolis, & præconibus gratiæ acci- piant. Sed prior expositio & verbis Prophetæ, & ipsi eventui videtur accommodatior. Quos enim Pisca- tores Apostoli in obsequium fidei pertrahere non po- tuerunt, eos venatores Romani justo Dei judicio pes- fundederunt. Hæc Pappus. In quem sensum etiam ea, quæ sequuntur, accepit Hieronymus: Numquid faciet sibi homo Deos, & ipsi non sunt dii. Et hoc gen- tes loquuntur, quæ venerunt ad salvatorem ab extre- mis terræ, sugillantes ignorantiam tam suam, quam majorum suorum, qua putaverunt ab homine fieri Deos, cum Dei sit homines facere. Idcirco ecce ego ostendam eis manum meam &c. Manus Dei per quam cuncta operatus est & virtus, de qua dixit A- postolus, Christus Dei virtus & Dei sapientia often- ditur gentibus, filii passione completa. Pulchreque dixit: Ostendam eis per vicem hanc: Ostendam autem manifeste,& non ut prius,in umbra & in imagi- ne,& vaticinio futurorum,ut postquam cognoverint, sciant nomen meum, audiantque a Filio: Pater ma- nifestavi nomen tuum hominibus. Atque sic e- tiam aptat Prophetiam sequentis capis immediate subjunctam: PECCATUM JUDA SCRI- PTUM EST IN STYLO FERREO &c. De gen- tibus quæ ad Dominum conversa fuerant, supra di- ctum est: Ecce ego ostendam eis per vicem hanc, ostendam eis manum meam & virtutem meam: Nunc de Israel, qui abjectus est, loquitur: Peccatum Judæ scriptum est stylo ferreo in ungue adamanti- no, & cætera. Quam capitum συνέχειαν notavit etiam Brentius.

in Christo, mero,ut credit,homine colendo. Non simpliciter, inquit, in Antivvujeco pag. 147. pronun- ciatur hic maledictus homo ille, qui in homine confidit, sed qui ita confidit,ut ponat carnem brachium suum, id est, in ipsis humanis viribus spem suam collocet, seu in homine ipso per se, citra spiritus ac virtutis divinæ opus: hoc enim omnino per vocabulum carnis signifi- catur. Postmodum negat,se in Christo homine ita confidere, ut humanis illius viribus citra spiritum ac virtutem ab illo uno Deo proficiscentem nobis opem fe- rendi potestatem tribuant. Resp. (1.) Verba Pro- phetæ subjuncta non esse restrictiva, sed potius ἐξη- γητικὰ,nimis manifestum est: Nimirum quotquot confidunt in homine,illi ponunt carnem brachiũ suum:quia homo nihil est,nisi caro; & confidentia ita comparata est, ut auxilium, subsidium, prote- ctionem & id genus alia expectet quis ab eo,in quo confidit,quod est eundem ponere brachium suum. Quia brachium pro potentia & auxilio forti accipi usitatissimum. V. 1. Sam. 2, 31. Job. 22, 8. c. 35, 9. Jer. 48, 25. Efa. 30, 22. c. 31, 17. c. 22, 6. Zachar. 11,17. (2.) Si is tantum maledictus, qui in homine per se confi- dit,citra spiritus ac virtutis divinæ opẽ, fiducia vel confidentia locari poterit in homine, modo non excludatur divinæ virtutis auxilium; atque ita non feriet hoc eos, qui in quemcunque etiam hominẽ fiduciam collocant cum spe auxilii divini. Quod absurdum. (3.) Non minus hic maledictus hic pro- nunciatur,qui in homine confidit,quam qui ponit carnem brachium suum. (4.) Caro insuper dicitur quivis homo,utpote res fragilis debilisque,quæ de- notatur ea voce Psalm. 56, & 78, 39. Efa. 31, 3. quin voce carnis hominem promiscue designari, non pensi habita illa oppositione virtutis divinæ, e variis locis constat,ubi caro pro homine adhibetur Gen. 6, 2. Psal. 65, 3. & 145, 21. Efa. 40, 6. Luc. 3, 6. Rom. 3, 20. 1. Cor. 1, 29. Ubi autem caro simpliciter posita, aut voci hominis explicandæ adhibita citra ἀντίθε- σιν disertam spiritus in Veteri Testam.sensu Socini- ano adhibetur,ut notet hominem virtutis divinæ ex- pertem, nondum ostensum est. (5.) Nullo insuper documento liquet, illo saltem modo confidentiam in homine maledictam hic pronunciari, qua divi- num auxilium posthabetur,quin eo ipso potius di- vinum auxilium posthaberi innuitur, dum in ho- mine quis confidit: Is enim corde à Domino rece- dere dicitur. Proinde (6.) solus Dominus hic proponitur,ut fiduciæ objectum: utpote qui so- lus corda probat & renes ad dandum unicuique juxta viam suam verf. 10. & à quo solo benedictio verf. 7. Ideoq;expectatio Israel solus Jehova dicitur, quem qui derelinquunt, pudore afficiuntur, v. 13. (7.) Israëlitæ pariter regerere potuissent ad hanc κατη- γορίανProphetæ,quod dũ alienis diis confidebant, aut etiam fiduciam in hominibus collocabant, non posthabuerint tamen auxilium divinum. Num au- tem ea ratione fulmen maledictionis divinæ effu- gissent? (8.) Adde quod Schlichting. Disput. de Trinit. adversus Meisnerum pag. 335. fatetur, quod hic eadem sententia repetatur, Ebræorum more, & pro homine caro ponatur. Quod autem regerit Chri- stum minime vulgarem & cæterorum similem ho- minem esse,id nihil ad rem facit: quum,ut often- sum,simpliciter in eum, qui merus homo est, sive censeatur vulgaris homo,sive divinus, confidere prohibeamur. Arripit & hoc Socinus, quod hic addatur, & à Domino recedit cor ejus, ut, sc. intellr- gatur, Deum habiturum aliquam rationem illorum, qui licet homini cuipiam plus æquo confidant, huma- nis viribus id tribuentes,quod ipsius Dei est proprium, tamen interea ab ipso Deo non deficiunt, nec mentem ab ipso aversam aut alienam gerunt. ## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

He teaches that the obstinate Jews are to be laid waste, and that all who trust in human powers are cursed, while on the contrary those who hope in the Lord are blessed, and he exhorts them to sanctify the Sabbath.

Vers. 1.

THE SIN OF JUDAH IS WRITTEN WITH A PEN OF IRON, WITH THE POINT OF A DIAMOND) The Chaldean is better: 'and with the point of a diamond.' For in both places it is a mark of the instrument. The point of the diamond is its sharpness with which it is accustomed to be written. See the Jerusalem Paraphrast on Deut. 32:13. The sense is: by treating them harshly, I will make them remember what and how great things they have sinned. For 'is written,' you will rightly translate, 'shall be written.'

GRAVEN UPON THE TABLE OF THEIR HEART) Sculptured (supply, it shall be) on the table of their heart. It was customary for certain amulets (περίαπτα) to be hung upon the heart for idolaters, in which were the names of gods, or characters (χαράγματα), or numbers. Alluding to these, he says that that idolatry will not easily depart from their heart, on account of the punishments, namely, which they are about to feel.

AND ON THE HORNS OF THEIR ALTARS) The names of the gods were accustomed to be written on the horns of altars. See Acts 17:23. Alluding to that custom, he signifies this: that they will be pierced by those horns, that is, they will be treated most wretchedly because of those deeds. Compare Psalm 22:21.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII.

Judæos obstinatos vastandos, & maledictos omnes, qui in humanis viribus confidunt, beatos contra qui in Domino sperant, do- cet, ac ad Sabbatum ferio sanctificandum hortatur.

Vers. 1.

PECCATUM JUDA SCRIPTUM STYLO FER- REO IN VNGVE ADAMANTINO) Melius Chaldæus: & ungue adamantino. Est enim utrobique nota instru- menti. Unguis adamantis est acumen ejus quo scribi solet. Vide Paraphrasten Hierosolymitanum Deut, 32,13. Sensus est:ego dure eos tractando faciam, ut meminerint quæ & quanta peccaverint. Pro scriptum est, recte verteris, scribetur.

EXARATVM SVPER LATITVDINEM COR- DIS EORVM) Sculptum (supple, erit) in tabula cordis eo- rum. Solebant ad Idololatris περίαπτα quædam suspendi cor, in quibus erant Deorum nomina, aut χαράγματα, aut numeri. Ad ea alludens dicit illam idololatriam non faci- le abituram ab ipsorum corde, ob pœnas scilicet quas sint sensuri.

ET IN CORNIBVS ARARVM EORVM) In cornibus ararum fcribi solebant deorum nomina. Vide Act. 17,23. Ad eum morem alludens hoc significat,fore ut illis cornibus transfodiantur, id est,pessime tractentur ob ista facta. Confer, Psal. 22, 22.

## 17:2
Verse 2.

WHEN THEIR CHILDREN SHALL HAVE REMEMBERED THEIR ALTARS) In the Hebrew: According to the remembering of the children of their altars. The sense is: that they may remember for a long time what they have done,

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CVM RECORDATI FUERINT FILII EORVM ARARVM SVARVM) In Hebræo; Secundum recordari filios ararum suarum. Sensus est: ut recordentur diu, quid fecerint,

Verse 3.

O MOUNTAIN IN THE FIELD) That is, O you Jerusalemite, who inhabit Mount Zion in the best field.

YOUR STRENGTH) That is, your wealth, vessels, gems, garments.

ALL YOUR TREASURES) Heaped-up weights of silver and gold.

YOUR HIGH PLACES BECAUSE OF SINS IN ALL YOUR BORDERS) Better: and your high places which were for a sin to you in all your borders: All these things, says God, shall be plundered.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

MONTANE IN AGRO) Id est ô tu Hierosolymi- ta, qui in agro optimo montem Sionis inhabitas.

FORTITUDINEM TUAM) Id est,opes tuas, vasa, gemmas, vestes.

OMMES THESAVROS TUOS) Congesta argen- ti pondera & auri.

EXCELSA TVA PROPTER PECCATA IN U- NIVERSIS FINIBVS TVIS) Melius: & excelsa tua quæ tibi in peccatum fuere in universis finibus tuis: Omnia hæc, ait Deus, diripientur.

## 17:4
Verse 4.

AND YOU SHALL BE LEFT ALONE FROM YOUR HERITAGE) An excellent version and consistent with the Chaldean. And you shall make an intermission, you and those with you, from your heritage. That is, you shall be forced not for one year, as the law commands in Exodus 23:11, Deuteronomy 16, but for many years you, with your household, shall cease from cultivating the land, namely, as I once threatened in Leviticus 26:34.

IT SHALL BURN EVEN UNTO ETERNITY) In the Hebrew: for an age: that is, for a long time.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET RELINQVERIS SOLA AB HÆREDITATE TVA) Versio optima & Chaldaicæ congruens. Et inter- missionem facies tu,& qui tecum ab hæreditate tua. Id est,coge- ris non unum annum, ut lex præcipit Exod, 23, 11. Deut. 16. sed multos annos tu cum domesticis tuis cessare à colenda terra, nimirum ut olim comminatus fui Levit. 26, 34.

VSQVE IN ÆTERNUM ARDEBIT) In Hebræo; in seculum: id est, diu.

## 17:5
Verse 5. CURSED IS THE MAN WHO TRUSTS IN MAN, AND MAKES FLESH HIS ARM, AND HIS HEART DEPARTS FROM THE LORD.) That is, while in the meantime his heart departs from the Lord. A similar addition in Isaiah 30:1. Flesh, that is, a mortal man subject to all accidents. Arm, that is, power.

He gratifies Socinus with this explanation, whose evasion this is for the sake of sustaining his ἀνθρωπολατρεία unless the interpreters in the disputation with Christ. Franck, p. 38, judge that he who so places his trust in man, that meanwhile his heart in no way departs from God, is not cursed. Schlichting, l.c., says that Jeremiah is speaking not of any faith whatsoever, but of that by which one does not lean upon faith in God, nor is it referred to that, which is what is subjoined, and that they are a certain limitation of the former; and he declares this by the example of the Israelites, who are said to have believed not only in God, but also in Moses his servant, Exod. 14:31. Nothing prevents us from trusting in a mortal man, insofar as he is an instrument of God, after having first leaned upon God. Ostorodus adds in Instit. Relig. Christian. c. 15, p. 88, that God himself commanded that the Israelites should believe in Moses forever, according to the Hebrew truth in Exod. 19:9, just as Jehoshaphat also commanded to believe in God and in his prophets, 2 Chron. 20:20, and there although not in the versions, yet in the Hebrew text the words sound in the same way concerning Moses and the prophets as they do concerning Jehovah himself.
