Whence they further infer that confidence can be placed in Christ: especially since by that very act the heart is not in the least departing from Jehovah himself. We answer, however, (1) that the adversaries commit a petitio principii, while they assume, and do not prove, that the words subjoined contain a certain limitation of the former, as if we were prohibited from trusting in man only in that way by which the heart departs from the Lord; and furthermore, that one could trust in man in such a way that the heart does not depart from the Lord. (2) The Prophet strikes with a curse from the mouth of the Lord all who trust in man, no less than those who make flesh their arm, as also those who depart from the Lord with their heart (if indeed those are taken as three distinct things); nay, he implies that those who trust in man depart from the heart from the Lord, since those words are added aetiologically. For hence they are subject to the divine curse who trust in man, because by that very act they depart from the Lord in their heart. Those words, therefore, are not restrictive or limitative, but rather exegetical and aetiological, explanatory and causal. (3) We urge again that not only are we simply prohibited from placing trust in man, but also that God alone is proposed as the sole object of trust. For although the exclusive particle is not explicitly added, it is nevertheless evidently gathered partly from the opposition, because one must trust in God in such a way as not to trust in man or flesh, or anything else that is not God, by the force of this whole discourse, just as the genus is wont to be understood by a certain named species, in which way all creatures are removed from the object of trust, with man, the noblest of creatures, being removed; since the reason for the interdict is equal regarding all creatures: partly from the description of trust: for saving trust is noted here, since it is the fountain and source of every blessing, which pertains to the first table of the Decalogue, and therefore has God alone and one as its object; since the entire worship of the first table is proper to God: nor does it acknowledge any other object than the one God; partly from the subjoined reason and property of God. That he searches the hearts and reins. For this is proper to God alone; partly from the remaining attributes of God. For just as the rest, which are claimed here for God, are implied to be proper to God alone, even if an exclusive is not explicitly added, so also this, that God is the object of trust, is to be understood as being proper to God. Which shines forth sufficiently from the whole context. He alone rewards everyone according to his way: He alone was (certainly he ought to have been) the hope and expectation of Israel; the help of the Lord alone is implored here, and must be implored: heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed, save me, and I shall be saved, etc. partly from the notation of idolaters, since they are said to depart from the Lord, and to forsake the fountain of living waters, where surely it must be judged that not only those who denied the supreme God are designated, but also those who, while wishing to appear to worship God, also worshipped idols besides God, just as the Samaritans are rebuked in 2 Kings 17:33, because they served their own gods together with the God of Israel. If, therefore, those also are said to depart from the Lord who worship others together with the Lord, no less are those to be judged to depart from the Lord who trust both in the Lord and in man; and thus true worshippers of God must trust in God alone. (4) It is added that Scripture also teaches elsewhere that those depart entirely from the Lord who trust not in God alone, but also in other things or persons. Thus, those who set their heart on riches, even if they wish to serve God at the same time, are judged as idolaters before God. See Ps. 62:11, Eph. 5:5. Col. 3:5. Because we cannot serve two masters at the same time, Matt. 6:24, Luke 16:13. Those who trust in man are judged not to have trust in God, by the example of King Asa, 2 Chron. 16:4. For which reason woe is denounced against them, Isa. 31:2. And it is forbidden to trust in the sons of men, Ps. 118:7, 8, 9, and 146:3, and others of this kind. For just as one must serve God alone, so also one must trust in God alone. Matt. 4:10, 6:24, and as God must be loved with the whole heart, not half, by the force of the first table of the law, Deut. 6:5, Matt. 22:37, so one must trust in God with the whole heart, not half, and thus our heart must trustfully rest in one and the only God, since the worship of the first table is indivisible and impartible. And indeed, even from the very terms it is manifest that he who turns himself to man, by trusting in him, turns himself away from God, since man is not God; nay, man and God are infinitely distant. (5) Therefore, as regards the Christ of the Socinians, it is certain that while they trust in him, and indeed with that trust which is proper to God, they depart from Jehovah, since they deny that he is Jehovah. For whoever adheres with a trustful heart to him who is not Jehovah, he turns his heart away from Jehovah, nor does he trustfully adhere to Jehovah with his whole heart. (5) Socinus gratuitously assumes that those who trust in any man more than is right, attributing to human strength what is proper to God himself, will be immune from the curse. On the contrary, however, it is manifest that they are injurious to God, nay, idolaters by the judgment of God, who attribute to men what is proper to God himself, even if they seem to themselves not to fail from God himself: since they ascribe the honor and glory proper to God to others, with whom God has not shared it, which Crellius also judges to be having strange gods, in his book De Deo et Attributis Divinis, c. 17. (7.) The examples which are brought forward to the contrary are ἀλλότρια, and foreign. For they do not speak of divine, salvific trust, or that which is proper to the first table, but only of human and historical faith, very far removed from the trust of the first table, or certainly of assent only, not of trust; nor does the word בטח of trusting occur in them, which is in this place, but האמין of believing, the rationale of which is entirely the same. We do not believe not only in God, but also in others; but one must trust only in GOD, not in man. But that the same construction occurs in the Hebrew text, when it is taught that one must believe in God and in Moses and the Prophets, it cannot be inferred from that, that one must believe in Moses and the Prophets as in God, or that the instruments or ministers of God are also the object of salvific trust, unless we wish to say that God commanded or approved of idolatry, which is impious. Nay, it is manifest that the prefix ב, as sometimes elsewhere, so also in those places serves to designate the Dative case, and that is to be ascribed to the peculiar construction of some verbs, as Hebrew Grammarians observe. Which is clear that it obtains in the verb הֶאֱמִין from Psalm 106:12, 24, where to believe בִּדְבָרָיו in his words, and לדברו with his word, and in that manner that word with the prefix ב occurs in Deut. 28, 66. 1 Sam. 27, 12. Psalm 78, 22. Nor is the sense any different in Exod. 14, 31, crediderunt ביהוה ובמשה in the Lord and in Moses, than that they believed the Lord and Moses. Likewise, that passage in Exod. 19, 9 must be taken, that the people may believe בך in thee, that is, in you, as also 2 Chron. 20, 20, believe בנביאיו in his Prophets, that is, the Prophets. Since Ostorodus did not understand this nature of Hebrew construction, he castigated the translations which rendered it thus in the Dative, and rendered it correctly, he himself being most worthy of castigation. Since it is evident from very many places of Scripture that it is most false that by that construction of the verb according to Hebrew truth it is designated to place trust in something or someone, see Job 24, 22. Psalm 119, 66. Prov. 26, 25. Jerem. 12, 5. Mich. 7, 5. Whence it is not from the force of the Hebrew phrase, but from the diversity of the objects toward which faith tends, that one must judge concerning faith itself. Therefore, it is not lawful to infer from the fact that one must believe not only God, but also his servants the prophets, that trust is to be placed in man; since we can believe someone, and join faith to his words, while yet not placing our trust in him; nay, one must believe the ministers of the Lord in such a way that our trust rests solely in the Lord, and is not placed in men. That some trust can be placed in man, provided it at least leans upon faith in God and is referred to it, is a mere begging of the question, nor can it be shown from Scripture, which, just as it restricts religious service and adoration, so also it restricts religious trust to God alone, and if it is placed in others, it threatens a curse. (8.) Holy Scripture, as often as it treats of religious trust, always and everywhere constitutes that one God as its object, teaches that one must trust in him with all one's heart, Prov. 3, 5, and declares those who trust in him to be blessed, and testifies that the faithful and holy have placed their trust in none but the Lord. See 2 Kings 18, 5. 1 Chron. 5, 20. Ps. 4, 6. & 9, 11. & 21, 8. & 22, 3. 5. & 24, 1. & 26, 1. & 28, 7. & 33, 21. & 37, 3. 5. & 52, 8. & 55, 27. & 56, 3. 4. 11. & 62, 8. & 78, 26. & 84, 13. & 86, 2. & 91, 2. & 112, 7. & 114, 17. 18. 19. & 118, 8. 9. & 125, 1. & 143, 9. Prov. 16, 20. ch. 28, 25. ch. 29, 25. Isa. 12, 5. ch. 50, 10. Jerem. 39, 18. Zeph. 3, 2. But it denies that one should trust in others, whether idols, or men, or things whatsoever, and it reprobates those who trust in the same, and decrees them subject to the wrath of God and various punishments; as can be seen in Ps. 44, 8. & 49, 7. & 52, 7. & 115, 16. & 118, 9. & 146, 2. Prov. 1, 28. Isa. 42, 17. Jer. 5, 17. ch. 7, 3. 7. ch. 46, 25. ch. 48, 7. 13. ch. 49, 4. Ezech. 16, 15. ch. 33, 13. Hos. 10, 14. Amos 6, 1. Hab. 2, 18. in all of which places the verb בטח is used, which is employed here. It remains, therefore, unmoved that religious trust must be placed in God alone, according to the perpetual tenor of Holy Scripture. We conclude now with Jerome in his commentary on this passage: If every man is cursed who trusts in men, but Paul of Samosata and Photinus (and also Socinus and his cohort), although they proclaim the savior holy and excelling in all virtues, yet confess him to be a man; therefore they will be cursed who have hope in man. And with Epiphanius in the Ancoratus n. 94, 95, p. 96: It is obscure to no one that we confess without any doubt that the Lord and God λόγον is man, not according to appearance, but truth. But such a man is not to be believed to be one who has arrived at divinity by a certain progression. For hope of our salvation is not established in man. Since from all men who have been propagated from Adam, no one could bring us salvation, but God alone, and the Word made Flesh, so that our hope might not be in man, but placed in the living God, who is made true man; ἐπικατάρατος γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ ἐλπίζων ἐπ’ ἄνθρωπον. For cursed is he who trusts in man. Verse 6. FOR HE SHALL BE LIKE THE TAMARISK IN THE DESERT] ערער some translate as tamarisk, others as juniper: in which sense the Arabs also use the same word. AND SHALL NOT SEE WHEN GOOD COMES] That is, which, when the time comes for trees to bring forth edible fruit, itself brings forth nothing of the kind. The opposite member indicates this sense to us. IN A LAND OF SALT AND UNINHABITABLE] Such as the land of the Sodomites, says the Chaldean here. Verse 8. A TREE THAT IS TRANSPLANTED OVER THE WATERS] As a tree planted by a stream of water. AND IN THE TIME OF DROUGHT] ἀβροχίας, ἀνομβρίας. There is the same word here in the Hebrew as above 14, 1. Verse 9. THE HEART IS DECEITFUL ABOVE ALL] Crafty. He speaks of most of the Jews of that time. AND INSCRUTABLE] The Hebrew word אנוש is translated by the Chaldean as strong, that is, hard. The Prophet does not complain of an acquired depravity of heart, peculiar to the Jews, but of a natural one, common to all men: Because he speaks indefinitely: The heart is deceitful. And as the Lord knows the heart of all men; so he teaches that the heart of all is deceitful and perverse, I the Lord searching the heart and testing the reins. Which certainly cannot be restricted to the Jews. Similarly David, Ps. 14, 2, complains of God looking down from heaven upon the sons of men, not to find one who does good. Whence it is a general axiom that God gives to each according to his way, according to the fruit of his works: so no less general are the axioms concerning divine καρδιογνωσίᾳ, that he searches the hearts of all, and concerning the depravity of the human heart, inscrutable to us. Furthermore, the Prophet had commanded to trust in God alone, not in men. He adds: The heart of man is deceitful and anxious: Which words either contain the reason why one should not trust in man: and thus they are to be understood generally, that one should trust in no man, because the heart of men is a deceitful and supplanting heart: or they render the cause of the dissuasion: why one must especially beware of trust in men and diffidence in God, because by nature the heart of man is tumid and timid, and therefore too prone to those vices. Whence also Jeremiah himself desires to be healed from this depravity, v. 14. Heal me O Lord and I shall be healed. Furthermore, original sin is graphically described in these words: For by reason of this, the human heart is truly עקב, crooked above all things, or supplanted, from עקב, to supplant; which, just as a way trodden by feet loses its smoothness and afterwards becomes callous and rough, so the heart of man, deprived of its original rectitude, has had depravity and hardness succeed into its place, as the blessed Chemnitius noted in his Loci Communes, page 253. Compare Isaiah 40:5. Moreover, it is called crooked and perverse מכל, because there is nothing at all above the perversity of the human heart, which has overflowed from the fall. Thence comes every other ἀνομία and perversity. And truly so great is the perversity of the human heart that it is deservedly called מכל, perverse above all things and over all things: because at all times, in all acts, in all ways, and above all things, it so inclines toward all evil things that no one can sufficiently comprehend it or explain it in words. It knows a thousand ways and modes of its depravity, nay, innumerable ones. Truly the human heart, by reason of this evil, is אָנוּשׁ, anxious, miserable, and vehemently diseased, and incurable. In which sense that word is taken in Jeremiah 15:18, chapter 30:16, Micah 1:9. Because that depravity of the human heart is most miserable and incurable, which is not put off except with life itself. Finally, concerning this depravity, the Prophet truly exclaims: Who shall know it? For that abyss is unsearchable, an inexhaustible spring of all malice, the depth (τὸ βάθος) of which no one besides God can know. We [know] the extreme [nature] of this evil

And we can never penetrate and investigate the deep abyss. Our heart, says Brentius in this place, is a lerna of evils, and known to none except the Lord alone, and thus a place of hell, but not burning, unless inflamed by the judgment of the Lord. From this depravity it overflows that the human heart is swollen in prosperity and timid in adversity: that it trusts easily in carnal things and distrusts too much the divine promises, from which evils it cannot be healed except by the omnipotent hand of the Lord. Therefore, my father-in-law renders this connection: It is indeed good to adhere to the Lord, it is evil and harmful to trust in men, nevertheless the human heart is so fraudulent that if hope in God does not immediately succeed, it trusts in human means, nor yet does it dare to rely safely on these, but perpetually fears a bad outcome. Which sense Jerome, Theodoret, Rabanus, Vatablus, Castro, and Cornelius follow. But that some of the Ancients interpret these things in a good sense concerning the inscrutable majesty of Christ, Jerome rightly observed that this is done out of a certain pious vow against the Jews rather than according to knowledge.

Latin:

Vers. 5. MALEDICTVS HOMO, QVI CONFIDIT IN HOMINE, ET PONIT CARNEM BRACHIVM SVVM ET A DOMINO RECEDIT COR EJVS.) Id est,cum interim à Domino recedat cor ejus, Similis additio Esaiæ 30,1. Carnem, id est,hominem mortalem omnibus casibus obnoxium, Brachium, id est, potentiam.

Gratificatur hac explicatione Socino,cujus hoc est effugiu pro sustinenda sua ἀνθρωπολατρείᾳ ni interpretes in disp. cum Christ. Franck. p. 38. eum qui ita in homine fiduciam habet, ut interim nul- lo pacto à Deo ejus cor recedat, maledictum non esse censet.Schlichting.l.c.Jeremiam,ait,loqui non de fi- de quavis,sed de ea,qua fidei in Deum non innititur, nec ad eam refertur,quod ex iis quæ subjunguntur, &priorum limitatio quædam sunt,perspici vult;& Israëlitarum exemplo declarat, qui non tantum in Deum,sed etiam in Mosen servum ejus credidisse di- cuntur Exod. 14,31. nihil impedire, quo minus Deo primum nixi, etiam homini mortali, quatenus Dei instrumentum est,confidamus. Addit Ostorodus in Instit. Relig. Christian. c. 15.p.88.Deum ipsum præ- cepisse, ut Israëlita in æternum in Mosen credant, se- cundum Ebraïcum veritatem Exod.19, 9. ut & Josa- phat jussisse in Deum credere & in Prophetas ejus 2. Par. 20, 20. ibiq́; etsi non in versionibus, in Ebreo tamen textu eodem modo verba sonare de Mose & Prophetis, uti de ipso Jehovab. Unde porro infe- runt, in Christo confidentiam locari posse : præ- sertim cū eo ipso minime recedatur corde ab ipso Jehovah. Respondemus autem (1.) τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ petere adversarios,dum assumunt,nō probant,ver- ba subjuncta continere priorum quandam limita- tionem,quasi ea tantum ratione prohibeamur in homine confidere,qua receditur corde à Domino; &porro confidere quis possit in homine,ita ut cor- de nõ recedat àDomino.(2.)Propheta maledictio- ne ferit ex oreDomini,omnes,qui confidunt in homi- ne, non minus,quam qui brachium suum carnem po- nunt,ut & qui recedunt corde suo à Domino(siquidem accipiantur illa,ut tria distincta) imo innuit eos re- cedere corde à Domino, qui confidunt in homi- ne,cum verbe illa αἰτιολογικῶς addita sint. Hinc enim maledictioni divinæ obnoxii sunt, qui confi- dunt in homine,quod eo ipso corde recedantàDo- mino.Verba ergo illa non sunt restrictiva,vel limi- tativa,sed potius ἐξηγητικὰ & αἰτιολογικὰ,expli- cartiva,& causalia (3.) Urgemus iterum, quod non solum simpliciter prohibeamur fiduciam ponere in homine,sed quod etiam solus Deus propona- tur ceu unicum fiduciæ objectum. Nam licet difer- te non addatur particula exclusiva,colligitur tamen eadem evidenter partim ex oppositione, quia sic in Deum confidendum est,ut non in hominem vel carnem,vel aliud quicquam, quod non est Deus, vi totius hujus concionis,ut solet certa nominata specie genus intelligi, quomodo removentur o- mnes creaturæ ab objecto fiduciæ, remoto homine creaturarum nobilissimo; quum par sit ratio inter- dicti,quoad omnes creaturas: partim ex descriptio- ne fiduciæ:Notatur enim hic salvifica fiducia,quum benedictionis omnisons & scaturigo sit, quæ per- tinet ad primamDecalogi tabulam,adeoqueDeum solum & unum pro objecto habet; cum totus cul- tus primæ tabulæ Deo proprius sit:nec aliud ea ob- jectum agnoscat,quam unumDeum;partim ex sub- juncta ratione, & proprietate Dei. Quod is corda & renes scrutetur. Hæc enim uni Deo propria est; partim è reliquis Dei attributis. Ut enim cætera, quæ hic Deo vindicantur,soliDeo propria esse in- nuuntur,etsi diferte exclusiva non addatur, sic etiã hoc quodDeus objectum sit fiduciæ, Deo propriū esse,intelligendū.Quod è toto contextu satiseluce- scit.Solus ipse retribuit unicuique secundum viam suam:Solus erat (esse certe debebat) spes & exspe- Etatio Israëlis; solius Domini auxilium hic implo- ratur,& implorandum: sane me Domine, & sana- bor,salvum me fac,& salvabor &c. partim ex idolo- latrarum notatione, quum recedere à Domino di- cantur,& fontem aquarum viventium relinquere, ubi sane non tantum illos, qui Deum summum ab- negabant, designari censendum est,sed & eos, qui cum Deum colere videri vellent, idola quoq; præ- ter Deum colebant, uti Samaritæ reprehenduntur 2. Reg. 17,33. quod una cum Deo Israelis suis servie- rint Diis. Si ergo illi quoque à Domino recedere dicuntur, qui una cum Domino alios colunt, non minus etiam illi àDomino recedere judicandi sunt, qui & in Domino & in homine merq̄ confidunt: adeoque in solo Deo confidendum erit veris Dei cultoribus. (4.) Accedit, quod alibi quoque scri- ptura doceat, eos omnino à Domino recedere, qui non in solo DEO, sed in aliis sive rebus, sive personis quoque confidunt. Ita qui cor suum apponunt divitiis, etiamsi simul Deo servire velint, idololatræ censentur coram Deo. Vid. Psal. 62. v. 11. Eph. 5,5. Gol. 3, 5.Quia non possumus simul servi- re duobus Dominis Matth. 6,24. Luc. 16, 13. Qui confidunt in homine, judicantur non habere fidu- ciam in Deo exemplo Regis Asæ 2. Par. 16. v. 4. Quo nomine væ illis denunciatur Esa. 31,2. Et pro- hibetur confidere in filiis hominum Psal. 118,7.8.9. & 146, 3. & quæ hujus generis alia. Ut enim soli Deo serviendum, ita etiam soli Deo confidendum. Matth. 4,10. c. 6, 24. & ut toto corde non dimi- dio Deus diligendus, vi primæ tabulæ legis Deut. 6,5. Matth. 22, 37. sic toto corde, non dimidio Deo confidendum, adeoque cor nostrum in uno & solo Deo fiducialiter recumbere debet, quum cultus primæ tabulæ sit ἀμέριςος, & impartibilis. Et sane vel ex ipsis terminis manifestum est, eum qui con- vertit se ad hominem, ei confidendo,avertere sese à Deo, quum homo non sit Deus, imo homo & Deus in infinitum distent. (5.) Quod ergo adChri- stum Socinianorum, certum est, dum in eo confi- dunt,& quidem ea fiducia, quæ Deo propria est, eosdem recedere à Jehovah, quum illum negent esse Jehovam, Quicunque enim corde fiduciali ad- hæret ei, qui non est Jehovah, is cor suum avertit à Jehovah,nec toto corde fiducialiter adhæret Jeho- væ. (5.) Qui homini cuipiam plus æquo confidunt, humanis viribus id tribuentes,quod ipsius DEI est proprium,eos immunes fore à maledictione, gratis assumit Socinus. E contra autem manifestum est, eos in Deum injurios imo idololatras esse judicio Dei, qui quod ipsius Dei est proprium hominibus tribuunt, etsi videantur sibi ab ipso Deo non defi- cere: quum honorem & gloriam Dei propriam a- liis adscribant,quibus cum Deus eam non commu- nicarit,quod etiamCrellius judicat esse habere Deos alienos l. de Deo & attrib. Div. c. 17. (7.) Exem- pla quæ in contrarium adducuntur, ἀλλότρια sunt, & aliena.Non enim de fiducia divina, salvifica, vel primæ tabulæ propria loquuntur,sed tantum de fide humana & historica, longissime à fiducia primæ ta- bulæ diversa, vel certe de assensu tantum, non de fiducia;nec in illis occurrit verbum בטח confiden- di,quod hoc in loco,sed האמין credendi, quorum est omnino eadem ratio. Non credimus non Deo solum, sed & aliis; at confidendum solum in DEO non in homine. Quod autem eadem constructio occurrit in Ebræo textu,cum Deo & Mosi ac Pro- phetis credendum esse docetur, ex eo inferri non potest,in Mosen & Prophetas credendum esse, ut in Deum, aut fiduciæ salvificæ objectum quoque esse instrumenta vel ministros Dei, nisi velimus dicere Deum jussisse vel approbasse idololatriam, quod impium. Imo manifestum est,præfixum בut alias nonnunquam, ita & in locis illis tnservire casuiDa- tivo designando,idque peculiari adscribendum est verborum nonnullorum constructioni, ut Gram- matici Ebræi observant.Quod in verbo הֶאֱמִיןob- tinere è Psal. 106,12.24. liquet,ubi credere בִּדְבָרָיו in verba ejus, & לדברו verbo ejus permutantur, eoq; pacto verbum illud cum præfixo ב occurrit Deut. 28, 66. 1. Sam. 27, 12. Psalm. 78, 22. Nec alius sen- sus est Exod. 14, 31. crediderunt ביהוה ובמשה in Do- minũ & in Mosen, quam quod crediderint Domino & Mosi. Paritet accipiendum est illud Exod. 19, 9. ut credat populus בך in te, id est, tibi, ut & 2. Par. 20, 20. credite בנביאיו in Prophetas ejus, id est, Prophe- tis. Quam constructionis Ebraicæ indolem quum non intellexerit Ostorodus, translationes, quæ ita reddiderunt, in Dativo, & recte reddiderunt, casti- gavit, ipse castigatione dignissimus. Quandoqui- dem è plurimis scripturæ locis constat: falsissimum esse quod secundum Ebraicam veritatem ea verbi constructione designetur fiduciam in aliquid vel a- liquem collocare, vide Job. 24, 22. Psalm. 119, 66. Prov. 26, 25. Jerem. 12, 5. Mich. 7, 5. Unde non ex vi phraseos Ebraicæ, sed ex diversitate objectorum, in quæ fides tendit, de ipsa fide est judicandum. Non ergo ex eo, quod non Deo tantum, sed etiam servis ejus prophetis credendum, inferre fas est, quod fiducia in hominem collocanda sit; quum credere alicui possimus, fidemq; adjungere verbis ejus, ut tamen in illo fiduciam non locemus, imo ita credendum sit ministris Domini, ut unice fiducia nostra cumbat in Domino, non autem locetur in hominibus. Quod autem quædam fiducia in homi- ne locari possit, dum saltim fidei in Deum innita- tur & ad eam referatur, mera est principii petitio, nec è scriptura ostendi potest, quæ ut religiosã ser- vitutem & adorationem, ita quoque fiduciam reli- giosam ad solum Deum adstringit, & si ea in aliis collocetur, maledictionem minatur. (8.) Scriptura S. quoties de religiosa fiducia agit, semper & ubiq; Deum illum unum ejus objectum constituit, huic toto corde confidendum docet Prov. 3, 5. & confi- dentes in ipso beatos prædicat, fidelesq; & sanctos non nisi in Domino fiduciam suam collocasse te- statur. Vid. 2. Reg. 18, 5. 1. Par. 5, 20. Psal. 4, 6. & 9, 11. & 21, 8. & 22, 3. 5. & 24, 1. & 26, 1. & 28, 7. & 33, 21. & 37, 3. 5. & 52, 8. & 55, 27. & 56, 3. 4. 11. & 62, 8. & 78, 26. & 84, 13. & 86, 2. & 91, 2. & 112, 7. & 114, 17. 18. 19. & 118, 8. 9. & 125, 1. & 143, 9. Prov. 16, 20. cap. 28, 25. c. 29, 25. Esa. 12, 5. c. 50, 10. Jerem. 39, 18. Zeph. 3, 2. In aliis autem confidendum esse ne- gat, sive idolis, sive hominibus, sive rebus quibus- cunque, & qui confidunt in iisdem, reprobat, iræq; Dei & pœnis variis obnoxios decernit; ut videre est Psal. 44, 8. & 49, 7. & 52, 7. & 115, 16. & 118, 9. & 146, 2. Prov. 1, 28. Esa. 42, 17. Jer. 5, 17. c. 7, 3. 7. c. 46, 25. c. 48, 7. 13. c. 49, 4. Ezech. 16, 15. c. 33, 13. Ose. 10, 14. Amos 6, 1. Hab. 2, 18. in quibus omni- bus locis adhibetur verbum בטח, quod hic usur- patur. Manet itaq; immotum, religiosa fiducia non nisi in solo Deo confidendum, secundum perpe- tuum Scripturæ S. tenorem. Concludimus jam cum Hieronymo hoc Oraculum incomment. ad h. l. Si maledictus est omnis homo, qui confidit in homi- nes, Paulus autem Samosatenus & Photinus (nec non Socinus ejusdemque cohors) quamvis sanctum & cunctis excelsum virtutibus prædicent salvatorem, tamen hominem confitentur; Ergo maledicti erunt spem habentes in homine. Et cum Epiphanio in Anco- rato n. 94. 95. p. 96. Nemini obscurum est, quin sine ulla dubitatione fateamur, Dominum ac Deum λό- γον hominem esse non secundum apparentiam, sed ve- ritatem. Verum non ejusmodi homo esse credendus est, qui ad divinitatem quadam progressione pervenerit. Non enim in homine spes est salutis nostræ constituta. Siquidem ex universis hominibus, qui ab Adamo pro- pagati sunt, salutẽ afferre nobis nemo potuit, sed Deus duntaxat, & verbum Homo factum, ut ne spes in ho- c mine nostra sit, sed in Deo vivo posita, qui verus homo fit factus; ἐπικατάρατος γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ ἐλπίζων ἐπ’ ἄνθρωπον. Maledictus enim est, qui confidit in homine. Vers. 6. ERIT ENIM QUASI MYRICÆ IN DE- SERTO] ערער alii myricam, alii juniperum vertunt: quo sensu & Arabes vocem eandem usurpant. ET NON VIDEBIT CUM VENERIT BONUM] Id est, quæ, cum tempus venerit arboribus fructum esculen- tum proferendi, ipsa nihil profert tale. Hunc sensum no- bis indicat membrum oppositum. IN TERRA SALSUGINIS ET INHABITABILI] Qualis terra Sodomorum, ait hic Chaldæus. Vers. 8. LIGNUM QUOD TRANSPLANTATUR SUPER AQVAS] Quasi arbor plantata propter rivum aquæ. ET IN TEMPORE SICCITATIS] ἀβροχίας, ἀνομβρίας. Est hic eadem vox in Hebræo quæ supra 14, 1. Vers. 9. PRAVUM EST COR OMNIUM] Dolosum. De Judæis plerisque illius temporis loquitur. ET INSCRUTABILE] Vox Hebræa אנוש à Chal- dæo vertitur validum, id est, durum. Non de acquisita cordis pravitate, Judæorum propria, sed de naturali, omnibus hominibus com- muni queritur Propheta: Quia indefinite loqui- tur: Pravum cor. Et ut Dominus cor omnium ho- minum cognoscit; ita omnium cor pravum & per- versum esse docet, Ego Dominus scrutans cor & pro- bans renes. Quæ restringi certe non possunt ad Ju- dæos. Similiter David Ps. 14, 2. Deum è cælis prospici- entem super filios hominum, ne unum invenire, qui bonum faciat, conqueritur. Unde generale axioma est, quod unicuique dat Deus juxta viam suam, jux- ta fructum operum suorum: ita non minus genera- lia sunt axiomata de καρδιογνωσίᾳ divina, quod o- mnium corda scrutatur, & de pravitate cordis hu- mani, nobis inscrutabili. Adhæc jusserat Propheta, soli Deo confidere, non in hominibus. Addit: Pra- vum est cor hominis & anxium: Quæ verba vel ra- tionem continent, cur in homine confidendum non sit: atque ita generaliter intelligenda sunt, nulli hominum confidendum esse, quia cor hominum cor pravum & supplantativum est: vel causam dehor- tationis reddunt: cur à confidentia in hominibus & diffidentia in Deo maxime cavendum sit, quia natura cor hominis tumidum, & timidum est, adeo- que ad vitia illa nimis proclive. Unde etiam optat Jeremias ipse ab hac pravitate sanari, v. 14. Sana me Domine & sanabor. Porro graphice describitur istis verbis malum originale: Hujus enim ratione vere cor humanum עקב pravum est præ omnibus, vel supplantatum, ab עקב supplantare, quod uti via pe- dibus calcata planitiem amittit, & post callosa fit, at- que aspera, ita cor hominis prima rectitudine pri- vatum sit, inq; ejus locum pravitas & durities suc- cesserit, ut B. Chemnitius in LL. CC. pag. 253. anno- tavit. Conf. Es. 40, 5. Dicitur autem pravum & perversum מכל quia nihil omnino est supra per- versitatem humani cordis, quæ è lapsu redundavit. Inde omnis alia ἀνομία & perversitas. Et tanta est profecto cordis humani perversitas, ut merito מכל præ omnibus & supra omnia perversu dicatur: quod omni tempore, in omnibus actibus, modis omnibus & super omnia, ita propendet in prava omnia, ut nemo satis id comprehendere aut verbis explicare possit. Mille vias & modos pravitatis suæ novit, imo innu- meros. Vere cor humanum ratione hujus mali est אָנוּשׁ anxium, miserum, ac vehementer morbidum, atq; insanabile. Quo sensu vox illa accipitur Jerem. 15. 18. c. 30, 16. Mich. 1, 9. Quia miserrima & incura- bilis est illa humani cordis depravatio, quæ nõ nisi cum ipsa vita exuitur. Deniq; de hac pravitate ve- re exclamat Propheta: Quis cognoscet? Nam abys- sus illa imperscrutabilis est, scaturigo inexhausta omnis malitiæ, cujus τὸ βάθος cognoscere præter Deum nemo potest. Nos mali hujus extremam

& profundum voraginem penetrare & indagare fatis nunquam possumus. Cor nostrum, inquit Bren- tius in h. l. est lerna malorum, & nulli cognitum, præterquam soli Domino, adeóq; locus inferni, sed non ardens, nisi judicio Domini inflatum. Ex qua pravi- tate redundat, quod cor humanum tumidum sit in prosperis, & timidum in adversis: quod confidat facile in carnalibus, & diffidat nimium divinis pro- missis, à quibus malis sanari non potest, nisi omni- potenti manu Domini. Nexum itaque hunc reddit B. Socer: Bonum quidem est adhærere Domino, malum & noxium confidere hominibus, veruntamen cor humanum tam est fraudulentum, ut si fpes in De- um non statim succedat, humanis mediis confidat, nec tamen his tuto audet insistere, sed perpetuo timet ma- lum exitum. Quem sensum Hieronymus, Theodo- retus, Rabanus, Vatablus, Castro & Cornelius se- quuntur. Quod vero in bonam partem hæc non- nulli interpretantur è Veteribus de inscrutabili Christi majestate, ex pio quodam voto contra Judæos potius, quam secundum scientiam id fieri, Hierony- mus recte observavit.

## 17:11
Verse 11. THE PARTRIDGE HATH HATCHED WHAT IT DID NOT LAY) In the Hebrew: The partridge hatches eggs, but does not lay. That is, it often happens that the chick does not follow, because the eggs are addled. See Aristotle on the History of Animals VI, 2. Pliny 10. 33. The sense of the Vulgate is not inconvenient. For the partridge, as Theophrastus, Pliny, and Aristotle testify, is accustomed to steal the eggs of another partridge and hatch the chicks, which when they have grown and heard the voice of the one who hatched them, fly away from her as if she were a stranger to their mother, just as wealth flies away from unjust possessors as if to other masters.

HE HATH MADE RICHES AND NOT IN JUDGMENT) By unjust means he sought for himself wealth that will not last.

IN THE MIDST OF HIS DAYS HE SHALL LEAVE THEM) See Psalm 55, 24.

AND IN HIS END HE SHALL BE A FOOL) That is, and finally it will appear that he himself was not wise, just as he had thought himself to be. See Luke 12, 20. Job 20, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PERDIX FOVIT QVÆ NON PEPERIT) In Hebræo: Perdix ova fovet, sed non parit. Id est, sæpe sit ut pullus non sequatur, quia ova sunt subventanea. Vide Aristotelem de Historia Animantium VI, 2. Plin. 10. 33. Sensus Vulgatæ non incommodus. Perdix enim Theophrasto, Plinio, & Aristot. testibus alte- rius perdicis ova furari & pullos excludere solet, qui cum adoleverint & vocem excludentis audi- verint, ab ea quasi aliena ad matrem avolant, si- quidem similiter opes ab injustis possessoribus ceu alienis heris avolent.

FECIT DIVITIAS ET NON IN JUDICIO) Ini- quis modis opes sibi quæsivit non mansuras.

IN DIMIDIO DIERUM SUORUM DERELIN- QVET EAS) Vide Psal. 55, 24.

ET IN NOVISSIMO SVO ERIT INSIPIENS) Id est, tandemque apparebit ipsum non fuisse sapientem, sicut se esse putaverat. Vid. Luc. 12, 20. Job. 20, 18.

## 17:12
Verse 12. A GLORIOUS HIGH THRONE FROM THE BEGINNING, THE PLACE OF OUR SANCTIFICATION) Here the Prophet opposes himself and some of his own to those of whom God had spoken. The place, he says, of our worship, is not the high places and groves, but that magnificent temple destined for that purpose by you yourself, O God, already from the times of Solomon.

Others with Theodoret, Jerome, Rabanus, and Isidore understand not the temple of Solomon, as Vatablus, Tremellius, and Castro do, but the majestic seat in the heavens, so that the solid and glorious object of the faith of the faithful may be designated. Psalm 20, 3. Psalm 69, 36. Isaiah 57, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SOLIVM GLORIÆ ALTITUDINIS A PRINCIPIO, LOCVS SANCTIFICATIONIS NO- STRÆ) Hic Propheta se suosque nonnullos opponit illis, de quib. Deus locut9 fuerat. Locus, inquit, cult9 nostri, no sunt excelsa & luci, sed illud templum magnificum abs te ipso, Deus, jam à Salomonis temporibus ei rei destinatum.

Alii cum Theodor. Hieron. Rabano, Isidoro non de templo Salom. ut Vatabl. Tremellius & Castro, sed de sede majestatica in cælis intelligunt, ut obje- ctum fidei fidelium designetur solidum, & glorio- sum. Psal. 20, 3. Pf. 69, 36. Esa. 57, 15.

## 17:13
Verse 13. THEY SHALL BE WRITTEN IN THE EARTH) Those things which are written in the dust are erased by a light wind.

This inscription does not note [being written] in the earth, as the Arminians wrongly [claim in the] Collatio Hagiensis p. 102, but temporal and eternal perdition. Psalm 69, 29.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE FORSAKEN THE FOUNTAIN OF LIVING WATERS, THE LORD) That is, the spring of every good.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN TERRA SCRIBENTVR) Quæ in pul- vere scribuntur, ea levi vento delentur.

Non notat hæc inscriptio in terra, uti perpe- ram Arminiani collat. Hagienf. p. 102. sed perdi- tionem temporalem & æternam. Psal. 69, 29.

QVONIAM DERELIQVERVNT VENAM AQVARVM VIVENTIVM, DOMINVM) Id est, sca- turiginem omnis boni.

## 17:14
Verse 14. HEAL ME O LORD, AND I SHALL BE HEALED) Bring comfort to those most grievous pains of mine, of which I complained in 15, 10, so that I may be better. Save me, and I shall be saved: that is, protect me against the machinations of my enemies, so that they may not harm me.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SANA ME DOMINE, ET SANABOR) Adfer solatium gravissimis illis doloribus meis, de quibus quæstus sum 15, 10. ut melius me habeam. Salvum me fac, & salvus ero: id est, protege me contra inimicorum machinationes, ne mihi noceant.

## 17:15
Ver. 15. THEY SAY TO ME: WHERE IS THE WORD OF THE LORD? LET IT COME) where does the outcome of your prophecies delay so long? Let it be present. Thus they mocked the Prophet.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IPSI DICUNT AD ME: UBI EST VER- BVM DOMINI? VENIAT) ubi tam diu moratur tuo- rum vaticiniorum eventus? Adsit. Ita illudebant Prophetæ.

## 17:16
AND I HAVE NOT BEEN TROUBLED FOLLOWING THEE AS SHEPHERD) Better: I have not run after thee to be a shepherd: that is, I did not seek this Prophetic office.

AND I HAVE NOT DESIRED THE DAY OF MAN) The Hebrew punctuation requires: I have not wished for the day of sorrow: namely, for my countrymen. Thus also the Chaldean.

And among the more recent [commentators] Vatabl., Tigurin., Arias, Pagn., Maldonat., B. Hulsemann. Which is opposed to the calumnies of the Jews. Others with Nazianz. Orat. XL., Hieron., Thomas, Lyranus understand it as praise or applause from men, from 1 Cor. 4, 3. But the Hebrew word denotes infirmity or a blow, v. 9, ch. 15, 28, ch. 30, 16, and is not correctly rendered by the Vulgate as 'day of Man'.

Ver. 16. THOU KNOWEST: THAT WHICH WENT FORTH FROM MY LIPS, WAS RIGHT IN THY SIGHT) In the Hebrew: That which went forth from my lips was before thee: that is, it proceeded from thee.

Latin:

ET EGO NON SVM TURBATVS TE PASTO- REM SEQVENS) Melius: Ego non cucurri post te, ut pastor essem: id est, non ambii munus hoc Propheticum.

ET DIEM HOMINIS NON DESIDERAVI) Hebræa punctatio requirit: Diem doloris non optavi: nem- pe popularibus meis. Sic & Chaldæus.

Et è recentioribus Vatabl. Tigurin. Arias, Pagn. Maldonat. B. Hulsemann. Quod calumniis Judæo- rum opponitur. Alii cum Nazianz. Orat. XL. Hie- ron. Thoma, Lyrano laudem seu applausum ab ho- minibus intelligunt è 1. Cor. 4, 3. Sed vox Ebræa infirmitatem seu plagam notat v. 9. c. 15, 28. c. 30, 16. nec recte à Vulg. redditur dies Hominis.

Vers. 16. TU SCIS: QUOD EGRESSVM EST DE LABIIS MEIS, RECTVM IN CONSPECTU TVO FVIT) In Hebræo: Quod egressum est de labiis meis coram te fuit: id est, à te processit.

## 17:17
Ver. 17. BE NOT THOU A TERROR UNTO ME) That is, destruction: as here the Chaldean: μετανοια.

Latin:

Vers. 17. NON SIS TU MIHI FORMIDINI) Id est, exitio: ut hic Chaldæus: μετανοια.

## 17:18
Ver. 18. DESTROY THEM WITH A DOUBLE DESTRUCTION) Subdue them with manifold evil.

Latin:

Vers. 18. DUPLICI CONTRITIONE CONTERE EOS) Multiplici malo eos edoma.

## 17:19
Ver. 19. THUS SAITH y Thus he had said.

STAND IN THE GATE OF THE CHILDREN OF THE PEOPLE BY WHICH THE KINGS OF JUDA ENTER, AND GO OUT) He understands the gate of the city, which was nearest to the king's palace.

AND IN ALL THE GATES OF JERUSALEM) Namely, through which the people were accustomed to enter and go out.

Latin:

Vers. 19. HÆC DICIT y Hæc dixerat.

STA IN PORTA FILIORUM POPVLI PER QVAM INGREDIUNTUR REGES JVDA, ET EGRE- DIUNTUR) Portam intelligit urbis, quæ regis palatio erat proxima.

ET IN CUNCTIS PORTIS JERVSALEM) Nem- pe per quas populus intrare & egredi solebat.

## 17:21
Ver. 21. TAKE HEED TO YOUR SOULS) That is, attend to yourselves.

DO NOT CARRY BURDENS ON THE SABBATH DAY, NOR BRING THEM IN THROUGH THE GATES OF JERUSALEM) Neither bring in goods yourselves, nor allow them to be brought in by others into the city on the sabbath day. See Neh. 13, 16, 17, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CUSTODITE ANIMAS VESTRAS) Id est, attendite vobis ipsis.

NOLITE PORTARE PONDERA IN DIE SAB- BATI, NEC INFERATIS PER PORTAS JERVSA- LEM) Neque ipsi merces inferte, neque ab aliis inferri in urbem finite die sabbati. Vide Neh. 13, 16. 17. 18.

## 17:22
Vers. 22. AND DO NOT CARRY BURDENS OUT OF YOUR HOUSES ON THE SABBATH DAY) Consider these as filth.

AND YOU SHALL DO NO WORK) Namely, the servant. See the Decalogue.

HALLOW THE SABBATH DAY) Namely, by observing rest.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET NOLITE EJICERE ONERA DE DOMIBVS VESTRIS IN DIE SABBATI) Sordes puta.

ET OMNE OPVS NON FACIETIS) Nempe famulum. Vide Decalogum.

SANCTIFICATE DIEM SABBATI) Nempe quietem servando.

## 17:24
Vers. 24. IF YOU HEAR, SAYS THE LORD, THAT YOU DO NOT BRING IN BURDENS) Συνεκδοχικῶς, that is, if you observe both the law concerning the Sabbath and my other laws.

Latin:

Vers. 24. SI AVDIERITIS, INQVIT DOMI- NUS, VT NON INFERATIS ONERA) Συνεκδοχικῶς, id est, si & legem de Sabbato, & alias leges meas obser- vaveritis.

## 17:25
Vers. 25. IN CHARIOTS AND HORSES) Magnificently.

Latin:

Vers. 25. IN CURRIBVS ET EQVIS) Magnifice.

## 17:26
Vers. 26. FROM THE PLAINS AND FROM THE MOUNTAINS AND FROM THE SOUTH) A distribution of the whole into its parts: For the strong part of Judah was to the South, part in the plains, part in the mountainous regions. Joshua 15.

BRINGING BURNT OFFERINGS AND SACRIFICES) Safely, that is, with no one hindering.

Latin:

Vers. 26. DE CAMPESTRIBVS ET DE MONTO- SIS ET AB AVSTRO) Distributio totius in suas partes: Nam fortis Judæ pars erat ad Austrum, pars in planis, pars in montanis locis. Josue 15.

PORTANTES HOLOCAUSTUM ET VICTI- MAS) Tuto scilicet, nemine impediente.

## 17:27
Vers. 27. I WILL KINDLE A FIRE IN ITS GATES) In these very gates, through which Jeremiah spoke to you by my command.

AND IT SHALL DEVOUR THE HOUSES OF JERUSALEM AND IT SHALL NOT BE EXTINGUISHED) That is, it shall not be extinguished until it has consumed all the houses of the city. That word 'houses' in Hebrew is ארמנות which signifies towered houses.

Latin:

Vers. 27. SUCCENDAM IGNEM IN PORTIS E- JUS) In his ipsis portis, per quas Jeremias meo mandato vos alloquutus.

ET DEVORABIT DOMOS JERUSALEM ET NON EXTINGUETUR) Id est, non extinguetur donec omnes domos urbis absumserit. Illud domos in Hebræo est ארמנות quod domos turritas significat.

## 18:1 Argument
SIXTH SERMON ON GOD COMPARED TO A POTTER. CHAPTER XVIII.

By the example of the potter, God asserts his freedom in punishing deserved crimes, and in granting the remission of temporal punishments, if repentance is performed: denouncing destruction on account of the obstinate malice of the people. The prophet, treated unworthily by those to whom he wished well, commends his cause to God, and indicates what is to be expected by the enemies of the servants of God.

Vers. 1. GO DOWN TO THE POTTER'S HOUSE) Go down, from the Temple, that is. For under the Temple were potteries. See what is at Matthew 27, 10.

The lower place is not always denoted by the word descent, but any movement whatsoever. Luc. 10, 31. Joh. 4, 49.

Latin:

CONCIO SEXTA DE DEO FIGULO COMPARATO. CAPUT XVIII.

Figuli exemplo Deus libertatem suam adserit in puniendis promeritis sceleribus, & ve- niatemporalium pœnarum concedenda, si pœnitentia agatur: interitum denuncians ob obstinatam populi malitiam. Propheta ab iis, quibus bene volebat, indigne tractatus, causam suam Deo commendat, & quid ho- stibus fervorum Dei expectandu sit, indicat.

Vers. 1. DESCENDE IN DOMVM FIGULI) Descen- de, ex Templo scilicet. Nam sub Templum erant figulinæ. Vide quæ ad Matth. 27, 10.

Non notatur semper loc9inferior voce descen- sus, sed motus quicunq; Luc. 10, 31. Joh. 4, 49.

## 18:2
Vers. 2. UPON THE WHEEL) Thus also the Chaldean. Others prefer to interpret it as stools, in which way the word אבנים is taken in Ex. 1, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SUPER ROTAM) Sic & Chaldæus. Alii sellas malunt interpretari, quomodo vox אבנים sumitur Ex.1,16

## 18:4
Vers. 4. AND THE VESSEL WHICH HE WAS MAKING OF CLAY WAS MARRED IN HIS HANDS) Which he had made. But broken by him, because it displeased him.

Although the power of overturning a people is known by this similitude, yet it is not absolute, as Calvinists imagine at Rom. 9, 10, nor is the discourse only about the punishment, but the condition of man also regarding spiritual matters is noted by this simile, and the power of God in refashioning our souls and the conversion of man, which the Jesuits wrongly deny: certainly the failure of the clay under the hand of the potter intending to form a perfect vessel v. 4 cannot be understood of the evil of punishment, but of the evil of fault. In that respect, however, man differs from clay, in that he can hinder his own reformation, Acts 7:51.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET DISSIPATUM EST VAS QUOD IPSE FACIEBAT E LUTO MANIBUS SUIS) Quod fecerat. Fractum autem ab ipso, quia ei displicebat.

Etsi potestas evertendi populum noscetur hac similitudine, no tamen absoluta, uti Calvin. fingunt ad Rom. 9, 10. neque de sola pœna sermo est, quin conditio etiam hominis quoad spiritualia hoc si- mili notetur & potestas Dei in refingendis animis nostris & conversione hominis, quod Jesuitæ per- peram negant: defectio certe luti sub manu figuli intendentis vas perfectum formare v. 4. non po- test de malo pænæ, sed de malo culpæ intelligi. In eo tamen differt homo à luto, quod impedire possit sui reformationem Act. 7, 51.

## 18:6
V. 6. AS THE CLAY IN THE HAND OF THE POTTER, SO ARE YOU IN MY HAND) I.e., thus I can break and break again.

Latin:

V. 6. SICVT LVTVM IN MANU FIGVLI, SIC VOS IN MANV MEA) I. e. ita vos possum frangere & refringere.

## 18:7
Vers. 7. I WILL SPEAK SUDDENLY) At some time I will speak, as the Chaldean here.

THAT I MAY ERADICATE AND DESTROY) Such threats, as also promises, have their tacit condition, things remaining as they are. See the history of Jonah. Therefore, God does not properly repent of his decrees, nor does he change them, but he acts as if he were changing them, since the change is in the thing, not in himself. Thus we say to those sailing that the lands recede.

Latin:

Vers. 7. REPENTE LOQVAR) Tempore aliquo lo- quar, ut hic Chaldæus.

UT ERADICEM ET DESTRUAM) Tales minæ, ut & promissa, suam habent tacitam conditionem, rebus sic manentibus. Vide Jonæ historiam. Non ergo proprie Deus aut pœnitentiam agit suorum decretorum, aut ea mu- tat, sed ita agit quasi mutet, cum mutatio sit in re, non in ipso. Sic dicimus navigantibus terras recedere.

## 18:11
Vers. 11. I AM FASHIONING AGAINST YOU EVIL) I will fashion. For it remains in the comparison of the potter.

AND I AM DEVISING AGAINST YOU A THOUGHT) That is, with a plan taken up against you.

Latin:

Vers. 11. EGO FINGO CONTRA VOS MALUM) Fingam. Manet enim in comparatione figuli.

ET COGITO CONTRA VOS COGITATIO- NEM) Id est, consilio contra vos sumpto.

## 18:12
Vers. 12. WHO SAID: WE HAVE DESPAIRED) It is desperate, as above 2:25.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QUI DIXERUNT: DESPERAVIMUS) Desperatum est, ut supra 2, 25.

## 18:14
Vers. 14. WILL THE SNOW OF LEBANON FAIL FROM THE ROCK OF THE FIELD?) From those things which now follow in the ἀπόδοσις, this version seems to be the best: Will (some traveler) forsake the field for the sake of the rock and the snow of Lebanon? Will there be anyone so foolish who would prefer to enter upon a rugged path covered with snow, rather than flat roads?

Thus indeed Vatablus, Lyra, Pagninus, Tremellius, Piscator; but because there is no indication of a traveler here, and the mention of Mount Lebanon would thus be useless, the parabolic sense is more correctly rendered: the snow of Lebanon does not fail as quickly as the people fail from me.

OR CAN THE COLD FLOWING AND RUNNING WATERS BE PLUCKED UP?) Or will (some thirsty person) forsake the flowing waters for those corrupted by frost? So that there is a certain transposition of words and a lack of the letter מ before נוזלים.

Latin:

Vers. 14. NUMQVID DEFICIET DE PETRA A- GRI NIX LIBANI?) Ex iis quæ jam sequentur in ἀποδό- σει, videtur hæc versio esse optima: An deseret (viator ali- quis) agrum præ rupe ac nive Libani? Eritne aliquis tam stul- tus, qui iter confragosum ac nivibus obsitum malit inire, quam vias planas?

Ita quidem Vatabl. Lyr. Pagn. Tremell. Piscat. sed quia nullum indicium hic viatoris, & montis Li- bani mentio sic frustranea foret, rectius sensus pa- rabolicus redditur: non deficit tam cito nix Libani quam cito populus à me deficit.

AUT EVELLI POSSUNT AQUÆ ERUMPEN- TES FRIGIDÆ ET DEFLUENTES) Aut deseret (siti- ens aliquis) aquas fluentes præ corruptis gelu. Ut sit transpo- sitio quædam verborum & defectus literæ מ ante נוזלים.

## 18:15
BECAUSE MY PEOPLE HAVE FORGOTTEN ME) Yet they have forgotten me. For there is an opposition.

Vers. 15. OFFERING IN VAIN) In the Hebrew: Burning to a vain thing. That is, to an idol.

AND STUMBLING IN THEIR WAYS) In the Hebrew: they made (idols) so that (the Jews) might wander in their journey.

IN THE PATHS OF THE AGE) In the Hebrew here, the מ is again missing, and the sense is: from the ancient paths, which Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, and the Prophets had trodden.

THAT THEY MIGHT WALK THROUGH THEM IN A WAY NOT SAFE) That they might go through the paths of a way not leveled; through rugged places. For he insists upon the comparison begun.

Latin:

QVIA OBLITUS EST MEI POPVLVS MEVS) Attamen oblitus est. Est enim oppositio.

Vers. 15. FRUSTRA LIBANTES) In Hebræo: Ado- lentes rei vanæ. Id est, idolo.

ET IMPINGENTES IN VIIS SUIS) In Hebræo: fecerunt (idola) ut (Judæi) errarent in itinere suo.

IN SEMITIS SECVLI) In Hebræo hic iterum de- est מ, & sensus est, à semitis antiquis, quas Abrahamus, Isaacus, Jacobus, Moses & Prophetæ institerant.

UT AMBULARENT PER EAS IN ITINERE NON TUTO) Ut irent per semitas viæ non explanatæ; per eo confragosa. Instat enim cœptæ comparationi.

## 18:16
Ver. THAT THEIR LAND MIGHT BECOME A DESOLATION) that it may become: that is, this will be the outcome of those wicked actions.

AND INTO AN EVERLASTING HISSING) A hissing of long time. A sign of contempt similar among all nations: 1 Kings 9:8. Thus the people hiss at me. A shepherd's pipe in Cicero.

AND HE SHALL SHAKE HIS HEAD) This also is a sign of contempt, as 2 Kings 19:21, Matt. 27:39.

Latin:

Vers. UT FIERET TERRA EORVM IN DE- SOLATIONEM) ut fiat: id est, hic erit exitus illarum pravarum actionum.

ET IN SIBILUM SEMPITERNVM) Sibilum lon- gi temporis. Similis apud omnes gentes signum contem- ptus: 1. Reg. 9, 8. Sic populus me sibilat. Pastoritia fistula apud Ciceronem.

ET MOVEBIT CAPVT SVVM) Signum & hoc contemptus, ut 2. Reg. 19, 21. Matt. 27, 39.

## 18:17
Ver. 17. AS A BURNING WIND I WILL SCATTER THEM BEFORE THE ENEMY) In the Hebrew: A wind from the East. It is violent in those places, and snatches away everything in its path. Job 27, v. 21.

BACK AND NOT FACE I WILL SHOW THEM) In the Hebrew: neck. To turn one's back to someone is the act of one who is averse.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SICVT VENTUS URENS DISPERGAM EOS CORAM INIMICO) In Hebræo: Ventus ab Orien- te. Is violentus est illis in locis, & obvia quæque abripit. Job. 27. v. 21.

DORSVM ET NON FACIEM OSTENDAM EIS) In Hebræo: cervicem. Tergum alicui obvertere, est aversantis.

## 18:18
Ver. 18. LET US DEVISE THOUGHTS AGAINST JEREMIAH) Accusations: as follows immediately: let us strike him with the tongue.

FOR THE LAW SHALL NOT PERISH FROM THE PRIEST, NOR COUNSEL FROM THE WISE, NOR THE WORD FROM THE PROPHET) This accusation will be that he prophesies falsely. For it cannot be that God would allow this land, beloved to Him, to be without priests who teach the law, and without scribes who unravel obscure things, and without prophets who reveal the will of God. Compare what is above 5:12.

Latin:

Vers. 18. COGITEMVS CONTRA JEREMIAM COGITATIONES) Accusationes: ut mox sequitur: per- cutiamus lingua.

NON ENIM PERIBIT LEX A SACERDOTE, NEQVE CONSILIVM A SAPIENTE, NEQUE SER- MO A PROPHETA) Accusatio hæc erit, eum falsa va- ticinari. Neque enim fieri potest, ut Deus hanc terram si- bi dilectam sinat esse sine sacerdotibus, qui legem doceant, & sine scribis, qui obscura enodent, & sine prophetis, qui Dei voluntatem revelent. Confer quæ supra 5, 12.

## 18:19
Ver. 19. ATTEND O LORD TO ME) They do not attend: do Thou, O Lord, attend.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ATTENDE DOMINE AD ME) Illi non attendunt: tu Domine attende.

## 18:20
Ver. 20. THEY HAD DUG A PIT) Thus he calls that accusation. See also shortly 22.

I SHALL HAVE STOOD IN THY SIGHT) I shall have ministered to thee.

Latin:

Vers. 20. FODERANT FOVEM) Sic vocat illam ac- cusationem. Vide & mox 22.

STETERIM IN CONSPECTU TUO) Ministra verim tibi.

## 18:21
Ver. 21. DELIVER UP THEIR CHILDREN TO FAMINE) I no longer stand in the way of your bringing about all the things you have threatened, since I see that their malice is so hardened.

Latin:

Vers. 21. DA FILIOS EORVM IN FAMEM) Nihil obsto amplius, quin omnia efficias, quæ minatus es, cum tam obduratam esse ipsorum malitiam video.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX.

By a broken earthen flask, the destruction of Jerusalem is predicted, and the ruin of the people in the siege by sword and famine on account of manifold idolatry and hardening.

Ver. 1. THUS SAITH THE LORD) He said. For he narrates what was commanded to him by God.

A POTTER'S FLASK) An earthen flask, which, just as easily as it is broken, so easily was God about to break the Jewish people. The flask בַקְבֻּק has a name among the Hebrews by onomatopoeia, because the sound which it emits is not poorly expressed in this way.

FROM THE ELDERS OF THE PEOPLE, AND FROM THE ELDERS OF THE PRIESTS) Who would believe that an earthen vessel could be bought by so many leading men? It is entirely an ellipsis or rather a syllepsis: for קָנִית can also be referred here, although less properly, which has been well seen by both the Chaldeans and the Greeks, if we follow the later editions. καὶ ἄξεις ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων τῶ λαῶ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερέων, supply some. Take them to yourself as witnesses: namely from the great Sanhedrin, which consisted partly of priests, partly of men of other tribes, so that no one might later have an excuse of ignorance: for those LXXII represented the whole people.

The verb to be repeated must be taken from the elders in common. See v. 10. Thus Jerome, Theodoret, Vatablus, and others.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX.

Per lagenam testaceam confractam excidium Jerusalem prædicitur, populiq. interitus in obsidione per gladium & famem ob idolo- latriam multiplicem, & indurationem.

Vers. 1. HAEC DICIT DOMINVS) Dixit. Narrat e- nim sibi a Deo imperata.

LAGVN CVLAM FIGVLI) Lagenam fictilem, quae quam facile frangitur, tam facile Deus fracturus erat populum Judaicum. Lagena בַקְבֻּק nomen apud He- braeos habet ἐξ ὀνοματοποιΐας, quia sonus quem edit, sic non male exprimitur.

A SENIORIBVS POPVLI, ET A SENIORIBVS SACERDOTVM) Quis credat fictile emi potuisse a tot viris summatibus? Est omnino ἔκλειψις aut σύλληψις potius: nam קָנִית etiam huc, quanquam minus proprie, potest referri, quod bene visum & a Chaldaeis & a Graecis, si edi- tionum posteriores sequimur. καὶ ἄξεις ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέ- ρων τῶ λαῶ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἱερέων, supple τινας. Eos tibi assume testes: nempe ex magno synedrio, quod partim ex sacer- dotibus, partim ex aliarum tribuum hominibus constabat, ne quis postea excusationem haberet de ignorantia: nam illi LXXII. totum populum repraesentabant.

REpetendum verbum ἀπὸ κοινῶ accipe a senio- ribus. Vid. v. 10. Ita Hieronym. Theodoret. Vatabl. & alii.

## 19:2
Ver. 2. WHICH IS BY THE ENTRY OF THE POTSHERD GATE) In Hebrew החרסות or החרסית. For the reading is double: some wish it to be understood from חרס, which sometimes signifies the sun, as the gate opposite the rising sun, of which there is mention at Neh. 3, 29. But the Chaldean explained it as תרע קלקלתא, that is, the dung gate. The word חרסית which is found here in the Hebrew signifies clay to the Chaldeans. But חרש with a dot on the left horn of the Shin, which is almost the same as Samech, and is very often interchanged, is earthen. And I would prefer this interpretation to the others, so that it was the gate outside of which the potters, who made vessels for the uses of the Temple very near the Temple, threw away the fragments of earthen vessels, where it is not incredible that other refuse was also thrown. This interpretation is confirmed by what we said above 18, 2, and what we shall have presently 10, and 14, and Zach. 11, 13. The Valley of Hinnom, or Topheth, and the torrent of Cedron were very near the temple. In the same place the potters inside the gate: and outside the gate those places of refuse.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QVAE EST JUXTA INTROITUM POR- TAE FICTILIS) Hebraice החרסות aut החרסית. Nam duplex est lectio: quidem a חרס, quod solem interdum significat, intelligi volunt portam soli orienti oppositam, de qua mentio apud Neh. 3, 29. At Chaldaeus exposuit תרע קלקלתא id est, portam sterquilinli. Vox חרסית quae hic in Hebraeo reperitur, Chaldaeis lutum significat. At חרש cui puncto in cornu Schin sinistro, quod ferme idem est cum Samech, & saepissime permutatur, est fictile. Et hanc interpre- tationem caeteris praeferam, ut illa fuerit porta, extra quam figuli, qui proxime templum vasa in usus Templi fabrica- bant, fragmenta fictilium abjiciebant, quo deinde & alias sordes abjectas fuisse non est incredibile. Hanc interpreta- tione firmant quae diximus supra 18, 2. & quae modo habe- bimus 10, & 14. & Zach. 11, 13. Vallis Ennomi, sive Topheth, & Cedron torrens proxime templum fuere. Ibidem figuli intra portam: & extra portam ista loca ejectamentorum.

## 19:3
Ver. 3. KINGS OF JUDAH) That is, the king and the Queen. See above, 13, 18.

SO THAT EVERY ONE WHO HEARETH IT, HIS EARS SHALL TINGLE) A Hebrew idiom 1 Sam. 3, v. 11. 2 Kings 21, 12. The sense is: the ears of all will be struck by this news as if by thunder.

Latin:

Vers. 3. REGES JUDA) Id est, rex & Augusta. Vide supra, 13, 18.

ITA UT OMNIS QVI AVDIERIT ILLAM, TINNIANT AVRES EJVS) Locutio Hebraea 1. Sam. 3. v. 11. 2. Reg. 21, 12. Sensus est: aures omnium hoc nun- cio quasi tonitru percellentur.

## 19:4
Ver. 4. AND HAVE MADE THIS PLACE ALIEN) They have profaned the Temple. See what is above 7, 30.

AND HAVE OFFERED LIBATIONS IN IT) They have burned incense. As we have already noted several times above.

AND HAVE FILLED THIS PLACE WITH INNOCENT BLOOD) Of children. When he says this place, he points with his finger to the valley of Hinnom, which was not far from the Temple, where this discourse was held. See Psalm 105, v. 37, above 7, 31.

THEY SHALL ALSO BUILD THE HIGH PLACES OF BAAL.

Baal is called Moloch, as Selden notes, and Milchom 1 Kings 11, whence the Punic names Hannibal, Asdrubal, Adserbal. By the Assyrians he is called Bel, whence Bel Adan, Belchazar. The first mention of Βῆλος among the Greeks is in Hesiod. Belus ὀρανιὸς, according to Hesychius. Suidas. Berosus, a priest of Bel, according to Eusebius, says: βῆλος, ὃν καὶ Δία μεθερμηνεύεσιν, Belus, whom they also interpret as Jupiter. This is the same as Olympian Jupiter, which is Beelsamen, who among the Phoenicians is the Lord of heaven, that is, the Sun, but among the Greeks is Jupiter; these are the words of Philo from Tacitus and Sanchuniathon. The LXX have ὁ βῆλος, and οἱ βάαλ, see 1 Kings 19, 18. By Symmachus and Theodotion he is called βασιλεὺς and ἄρχων 2 Sam. 12, 31. Jer. 49, 15. Βασιλεὺς θεῶν in the most ancient Theology of the Phoenicians. Adodus by Sanchuniathon is worshipped by the Syrians as Hadad, or Adad, which signifies one thing according to Macrobius 2. Saturnalia 18. For the images of both & of Adad and of Moloch, writers record them as the same, made to represent the sun. R. David Kimchi and Iarchi say that Nibchaz, the deity of the Avites, bore the image of a dog. Bartak the figure of an Ass, Adramelech of a Mule, Anamelech of a Horse; we think it is one deity, says Selden, and we refer it to Moloch! Ἀμιλάκαν

The Carthaginians worshipped [him], as Athenagoras testifies. Amilcas is to be derived from the same source as Molech: both are purely Hebrew or Punic and denote King. Hence the name Militi and Imilces, which is queen, and Melicus. Hence Μέλκαρτος or Μέλκαρθον, Hercules worshipped by the Tyrians, according to Strabo; hence Bomilcar, Hamilcar. Furthermore, the face of this idol (to wit, Moloch) was like the face of a calf, as P. Fagius testifies from the Ialkat, where its seven chambers are mentioned. Thus there were seven gates of Mithra (Celsus in Origen, book 5). Mithra, however, by the consensus of all antiquity, is to be considered the same as the Sun. Mithir also, or Minther, signifies a ruler in Persian. Scaliger, book 6, on the emendation of times.

Men, women, and children were sacrificed to Moloch, as Photius testifies in the life of Athanasius. Others, however, think otherwise. R. Solomon Iarchi, David Kimchi, and Moses Mikozi (negative precept 40) and Maimonides write that the children were not burned or sacrificed, but only led between two constructed pyres by the priests who were in charge of the Molochir. But it is evident from this and other passages that they were burned. Compare Jer. 7:31, Ezek. 16:20, 21, and 23:37, 39, Wis. 14:23, ch. 12:5, 6, and Apollinarius on Ps. 105. By another ancient rite, they were accustomed to pass through the fire (πῦρ διέρπειν) when they swore oaths and confirmed the truth of their words with an inviolable pledge. The priests of Moloch, like those of other deities

are called כְּמָרִים, because they were accustomed to be dressed in black garments, according to Kimchi. Compare Zeph. 1:4.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET ALIENVM FECERINT LOCUM ISTVM) Templum profanarint. Vide quae supra 7, 30.

ET LIBAVERINT IN EO) Adoleverint. Ut supra jam aliquoties notavimus.

ET REPLEVERUNT LOCVM ISTVM SAN- GVINE INNOCENTVM) Puerorum. Locum istum cum dicit, digito vallem Ennomi demonstrat, quae non longe erat a Templo, ubi hic sermo habitus. Vide Psal. 105. v. 37. supra 7, 31.

AEDIFICABUNT QUOQUE EXCEL SA BAAL.

Baal dictus est Moloch notante Seldeno & Milchom 1. Reg. 11. unde nomina Punica Anni- bal, Asdrubal, Adserbal. Assyriis Bel dictus, unde Bel Adan, Belchazar. Βῆλος mentio prima apud Grae- cos, in Hesiod. Belus ὀρανιὸς, apud Hesich. Suid. Be- rosus Beli sacerdos, apud Eusebium βῆλος, inquit, ὃν καὶ Δία μεθερμηνεύεσιν, Belus, quem & Jovem in- terpretantur. Id ipsum est Olympius Iupiter, quod Beelsamen, qui apud Phoenices est Dominus caeli, id est, Sol, apud Graecos autem est Iupiter, sunt verba Philonis ex Tacito & Sanchuniathene. LXX. ha- bent ὁ βῆλος, & οἱ βάαλ vid. 1. Reg. 19, 18. A Sym- macho & Theodotione dicitur βασιλεὺς & ἄρχων 2. Sam. 12, 31. Ier. 49, 15. Βασιλεὺς θεῶν in Phoenicum vetustissima Theologia. Adodus a Sanchuniathene Syris culto ab Hadad, seu Adad, quod unum signifi- cat juxta Macrob. 2. Satunar. 18. Effigies enim utri- usq; & Adadi & Molochi easdem memorant scri- ptores, ad exprimendum solem factas. Nibchaz Avi- tarum numen canis imaginem retulisse ajunt R. David Kimchi & Iarchi. Bartak figuram Asini, Adramelech Muli, Anamelech Equi, nos unum numen putamus inquit Seldenus & ad Molochum referimus! Ἀμιλάκαν

Carthaginenses venerati sunt, teste Athenagora. Amilcas ab eodem, quo Molech, fonte deducendus: utraque pura puta Ebraica seu Punica sunt & Re- gem denotant. Hinc Militi nomen & Imilces, quod est regina & Melicus. Hinc Μέλκαρτος sive Μέλκαρθον Hercules Tyriis cultus, apud Strabo- nem, hinc Bomilcar, Hamilcar. Porro facies hujus idoli (scil. Molochi) erat ut facies vituli, teste P. Fa- gio ex Ialkat, ubi septem ejus conclavia memoran- tur. Sic septem portæ erant Mithræ (Cels. apud Orig. l. 5.) Mithra vero totius antiquitatis consen- su idem qui Sol æstimandus. Mithir item aut Min- ther Persice Dynastam significat. Scaliger libr. VI. de emendat. tempor.

Viri, fæminæ & pueri Molocho mactabantur, te- ste Phot. in vit. Athanas. Alii tamen aliter sentiunt. Non combustos vel mactatos pueros, sed duabus pyris exstructis traductos solum Sacerdotibus Molo- chirem procurantibus, scribunt R. Salomo Iarchi, David Kimchi, Moses Mikozi præcept. negat. 40. Maimon. Sed crematos illos fuisse ex hoc aliisque locis constat. Conf. Ier. 7, 31. Ezech. 16, 20. 21. & 23, 37. 39. Sap. 14, 23. c. 12, 5. 6. & Apollin. ad Ps. CV. Alio ritu vetusto ignem pertransire πῦρ διέρπειν so- litifunt, qui jurabant, & illæsam fidem dictis ad- struebant. Sacerdotes Molochi, uti aliorum Numinū

כְּמָרִים sunt nuncupati, quod nigris indui solerent vestibus juxta Kimchium. Conf. Sophon. 1. 4.

## 19:5
Verse 5.

WHICH I DID NOT COMMAND, NOR DID I SPEAK, NOR DID THEY COME INTO MY HEART) Repeated from those above at 7:31. Whence it is rightly gathered that worship which God has not commanded is idolatrous: Deut. 17:3, Num. 5:29. And that by the force of the prohibition in Deut. 12:28. Verse 6. AND THE VALLEY OF SLAUGHTER) Namely, not of children, but of men; not of the innocent, but of those who deserved it. This is also repeated from the same chapter, 7:32. Verse 7. AND I WILL DISSIPATE THE COUNSEL OF JUDAH AND JERUSALEM IN THIS PLACE) He still points to the valley of Ennom or Hinnom, where a part of the Chaldean camp was to be. Verse 8. INTO ASTONISHMENT AND HISSING) See above 18:16. The same manner of speaking is below at 50:13. Verse 9. AND I WILL FEED THEM WITH THE FLESH OF THEIR SONS) Horrendous, but true. We had a similar one in 2 Kings 6:28, and another in Josephus, 7:8, of the Jewish War. Verse 10. AND YOU SHALL BREAK THE FLASK IN THE EYES OF THE MEN) An old custom in the East, and among other nations, to speak not only with words but also with things: hence symbols. Verse 11. WHICH CANNOT BE RESTORED ANY MORE) A broken flask is not restored, but another flask is made from the same material, above 18:4. Thus God made a new Jewish people, not the same from the same, but through substitution. AND THEY SHALL BE BURIED IN TOPHETH, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OTHER PLACE TO BURY) More correctly: so that there is not (enough) place to bury. As we said above at 7:32. Verse 12. TO THIS PLACE) Now he points out the city from the Temple, as the following indicates. Verse 13. AND THE HOUSES OF JERUSALEM AND THE HOUSES OF THE KINGS OF JUDAH SHALL BE, LIKE THE PLACE OF TOPHETH, UNCLEAN) That is, full of corpses. Jerome denies that that [phrase] 'houses of the kings of Judah' was in the Hebrew copies of his time. But it is in ours and in the Chaldean, no less than in the Greek. You see the variety of copies. ON WHOSE ROOFS THEY SACRIFICED TO ALL THE HOST OF HEAVEN) That is, on the flat roofs, or terraces, which the Greeks call δώματα and the Hebrews גַּגּוֹת. See what [is said] on Matt. 10:27. For such roofs were used for high places, because there was a clear view of the stars there. Verse 14. AND HE STOOD IN THE COURT OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) For the Temple was not far from Tophet. He understands the court, the great open-air one. AND HE SAID TO ALL THE PEOPLE) Since there was a very great crowd.

SERMON VII. TO THE ENVOYS OF ZEDEKIAH AND TO ZEDEKIAH.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QUÆ NON PRÆCEPI, NEC LOCVTVS SVM, NEC ASCENDERVNT IN COR MEVM) Re- petita ex illis supra 7, 31. Unde recte colligitur cultum, quem Deus non præcepit esse idololatricum: Deut. 17, 3. Num. 5. v. 29. Idque vi interdicti Deut. 12, 28. Vers. 6. SED VALLIS OCCISIONIS) Nempe non puerorum, sed virorum, non innocentium, sed eorum, qui id sunt meriti. Repetita & hæc ex eodem capite 7, 32. Vers. 7. ET DISSIPABO CONSILIVM JVDA ET JERVSALEM IN LOCO ISTO) Adhuc vallem En- nomi sive Hinnomi demonstrat, ubi pars futura erat ca- strorum Chaldaicorum. Vers. 8. IN STVPOREM ET SIBILVM) Vide supra 18, 16. Idem loquendi genus infra 50, 13. Vers. 9. ET CIBABO EOS CARNIBVS FILIO- RUM SUORVM) Horrenda, sed vera. Simile habuimus 2. Reg. 6, 28. & aliud in Josepho 7, 8. belli Judaici. Vers. 10. ET CONTERES LAGVNCVLAM IN OCVLIS VIRORVM) Mos vetus in oriente, & apud alias gentes, non vocibus tanrum, sed & rebus loquendi: inde σύμβολα. Vers. 11. QVOD NON POTEST ULTRA IN- STAVRARI) Lagena fracta non instauratur, sed ex eadem materia fit alia lagena, supra 18, 4. Sic Deus novum fe- cit populum Judaicum, non eundem ex iisdem, sed per suffectionem. ET IN TOPHETH SEPELIENTVR, EO QVOD NON SIT ALIVS LOCVS AD SEPELIENDVM) Re- ctius ita ut non (sufficiat) locus ad sepeliendum. Ut diximus supra 7, 32. Vers. 12. LOCO HUIC) Jam ex Templo urbem mon- strat, ut sequentia indicant. Vers. 13. ET ERVNT DOMVS JERVSALEM ET DOMVS REGVM JUDA, SICVT LOCVS TO- PHETH, IMMUNDÆ) Id est, plenæ cadaveribus. Illud domus regum Juda negat Hieronymus in Hebraicis sui temporis exemplaribus fuisse. At est in nostro & in Chal- daico, non minus quam in Græco. Vides varietatem ex- emplarium. IN QVARVM DOMATIBVS SACRIFICAVE- RVNT OMNI MILITIÆ COELI) Id est, in tectis pla- nis, sive solariis, quæ Græci δώματα, Hebræi גַּגּוֹת vo- cant. Vide quæ ad Matth. 10, 27. Nam talia tecta pro excel- sis usurpabantur, eo quod liber ibi esset siderū conspectus. Vers. 14. ET STETIT IN ATRIO DOMVS DO- MINI) Neque enim longe à Tophet erat Templum. A- trium intelligit, subdiale maximum. ET DIXIT AD OMNEM POPULUM) Cum maxima esset frequentia.

CONCIO VII. AD LEGATOS SEDECIAE ET SEDECIAM.

## 20:1 Argument
CHAPTER 20.

On account of this preaching, Jeremiah is cast into prison by Pashhur, and being brought out, he prophesies captivity for him and for all of Judea, complaining that he is a laughingstock to everyone, yet raising himself up by the help of God, but again broken by impatience, cursing the day of his birth.

Vers. 1.

AND PASHHUR THE SON OF IMMER THE PRIEST, WHO HAD BEEN APPOINTED PRINCE IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) That is, from the priestly family of the sixteenth ἐφημερίας, 2 Chron. 24:12. A prince נגיד in the Temple: that is, στρατηγὸς τῦ ἱερῦ, who had the right of arrest over those who committed offenses in the temple, as we said at Matt. 26:46 and Luke 22:4. However, the judgment did not rest with him, or with the priests alone, but with the Sanhedrin, in which there were generally many from the priests. See below, 26.

Latin:

CAPUT XX.

Ob hanc prædicationem Jeremias à Phassur in carcerem conjicitur & eductus eidem & Judææ toti captivitatem vaticinatur, con- querens se omnibus esse ludibrio, erigens ta- men se Dei auxilio, sed rursus impatientia fractus maledicens diei nativitatis suæ.

Vers. 1.

ET AUDIVIT PHASSVR FILIUS EMMER SA- CERDOS, QUI CONSTITUTUS ERAT PRIN- CEPS IN DOMO DOMINI) Id est, ex sacerdotali fa- milia ἐφημερίας decimæ sextæ 2. Paral. 24, 12. Princeps נגיד in Templo: id est στρατηγὸς τῦ ἱερῦ cui jus erat prehensionis in eos, qui in templo delinquabant, ut diximus ad Matth. 26, 46. ad Lucam 22, 4. Judicium autem non erat penes illum, aut penes sacerdotes solos, sed penes Synedrium, in quo plerunque multi erant è sacerdotibus. Vide infra. 26.

## 20:2
Vers. 2. AND PASHHUR STRUCK JEREMIAH THE PROPHET) That is, he laid hands on him: in which way also the Greek word πατάσσειν is taken in Matt. 26:31 and Mark 14:27. Where in the Syriac it is מחא, signifying the same as that which we have here, נכה. Moreover, this נכו is translated by ἁλώκειν in Ezek. 33:21, 40:1.

AND PUT HIM IN THE STOCKS) That is, into prison, as the Chaldean has it here; the LXX call it καταῤῥάκτην, below 29:26, ἀπόκλεισμα. But Symmachus calls it sometimes βασανιστήριον, sometimes στρεβλωτήριον. He who translated the Paralipomena calls it φυλακήν. Some say it was a pillory made of wood, in which there were holes: one through which the neck was passed, and two others through which the hands were passed.

WHICH WAS IN THE UPPER GATE OF BENJAMIN) That is, in that upper gate which was called after Benjamin.

IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) In the outbuildings of the Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET PERCUSSIT PHASSUR JEREMIAM PROPHETAM) Id est manum ei injecit: quomodo & Græca vox πατάσσειν sumitur Matth. 26, 31. & Marci 14, 27. Ubi in Syriaco est מחא, idem significans, quod id quod hic habemus נכה. Hoc autem נכו per ἁλώκειν vertitur Ezech. 33, 21. 40, 1.

ET MISIT EUM IN NERVUM) Id est, in car- cerem, ut hic habet Chaldæus; LXX. καταῤῥάκτην vocant, infra 29, 26. ἀπόκλεισμα. At Symmachus modo βασανι- στήριον modo στρεβλωτήριον. Is qui Paralipomena interpreta- tus est φυλακήν. Ajunt quidam fuisse cippum factum est li- gnis, in quibus erant foramina: unum per quod collum, duo altera per quæ manus trajiciebantur.

QUOD ERAT IN PARTE BENJAMIN SUPE- RIORI) Id est, in summa porta illa, quæ à Benjamine di- cebatur.

IN DOMO DOMINI) In Templi appendicibus.

## 20:3
Vers. 3. THE LORD HATH NOT CALLED THY NAME PASHHUR) That is, an increasing prince, from פוש and חור.

BUT TERROR ON EVERY SIDE) Magor-Missabib, that is, destruction on every side: for the Hebrews call this by metonymy by the name of fear; the Greeks, from גור, which is to migrate, translate it μέτοικον, or by similar words. See Jerome here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NON PHASSUR VOCAVIT DOMINUS NOMEN TUUM) Id est, augescentem principem à פוש & חור.

SED PAVOREM UNDIQVE) Magor-Misabib, id est exitium undique: nam id per μετωνυμίαν formidinis nomi- ne appellant Hebræi Græci à גור, quod est migrare, ver- tunt μέτοικον, aut verbis similibus. Vide hic Hieronymum.

## 20:6
Vers. 6. TO WHOM THOU HAST PROPHESIED LIES) Namely, saying that it could not be that God would leave this land without priests, Prophets, and Doctors. See above 5:31 and 18:38.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QUIBUS PROPHETASTI MENDACIUM) Nempe dicens fieri non posse ut Deus hanc terram relin- queret sine sacerdotibus, Prophetis & Doctoribus. Vide supra 5, 31. & 18, 38.

## 20:7
Vers. 7. THOU HAST SEDUCED ME, O LORD, AND I AM SEDUCED) Here now begin the complaints of Jeremiah, when he was in that prison, not much unlike the complaints of Job. But you would translate it best: If you have seduced me, O Lord, I am seduced. These men say that I prophesy falsely, but I cannot be deceived unless you have deceived me, in whom I have placed my faith.

These things hold better than when the Jesuits interpret it as a deception, as if God had not stood by his promises, that he would make the Prophet into a fortified city, etc. Others, however, take it in such a way that the Prophet was led to preach by God from ch. 1:5, ch. 15:20.

YOU HAVE BEEN STRONGER THAN ME, AND HAVE PREVAILED) You who are much stronger than I, have imposed this burden of prophesying upon me. How could I refuse?

I HAVE BECOME A LAUGHINGSTOCK ALL THE DAY) And yet, when I do what is my duty, I am mocked, vexed, and tormented.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SEDUXISTI ME DOMINE, ET SEDU- CTUS SVM) Hic jam incipiunt questus Jeremiæ, cum ef- set in illo carcere, Jobi questibus non multum dissimiles. Optime autem vertas; Si tu me seduxisti, Domine, seductus sum. Isti homines ajunt me falsa vaticinari, at ego decipi non possum, nisi tu me deceperis, cui fidem habui.

Hæc melius habent, quam cum Jesuitæ de- ceptionem interpretantur, quasi Deus non ste- terit promissis, quod Prophetam in civitatem mu- nitam facere velit &c. Alii tamen ita accipiunt, quod inductus Propheta sit ad prædicandum à Deo è c. 1, 5. c. 15, 20.

FORTIOR ME FUISTI, ET INVALVISTI) Tu qui multo meis validior, hoc onus vaticinandi mihi impo- suisti. Quomodo detrectare potui?

FACTUS SVM IN DERISVM TOTA DIE) At- tamen cum faciam quod mei est muneris, irrideor, vexor, excrucior.

## 20:8
Vers. 8. THE WORD OF THE LORD HAS BECOME FOR ME A REPROACH) Namely, because the things he had spoken did not come to pass immediately. And yet justice, as Euripides says, σῖγα κὶ βραδεῖ ποδὶ στείχουσα μάρπτει [advancing with silent and slow foot, overtakes].

Latin:

Vers. 8. FACTUS EST MIHI SERMO DOMINI IN OPPROBRIUM) nempe quia non illico eveniebant quæ dixerat. Atqui δίκη ut ait Euripides, σῖγα κὶ βραδεῖ πο- δὶ στείχουσα μάρπτει.

## 20:9
Vers. 9. AND I SAID: I WILL NOT REMEMBER HIM, NOR WILL I SPEAK ANY MORE IN HIS NAME) This thought sometimes occurs to me, that I would act more rightly and safely if I suppressed the commands given to me in silence.

AND IT BECAME IN MY HEART AS A BURNING FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES, AND I WAS WEARY, NOT ABLE TO BEAR IT) The fear of punishment to be inflicted by God repressed that thought, just as the Apostle says 1 Cor. 9, 17. ἀνάγκη γὰρ μοὶ ἐπίκειται. ὀυαὶ δέ μοι ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ ἐυαγγελίζω [for necessity is laid upon me; and woe is unto me if I preach not the gospel]. That passage from Lucan does not differ: - - Magnoque exæstuat igne Iratum te Phœbe ferens, nec verbere solo Uteris & stimulis flammasq; in viscera mergis [And she seethes with a great fire, bearing you, angry Phoebus, and you use not only the lash and goads, but plunge flames into her vitals].

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET DIXI: NON RECORDABOR EJUS, NEQVE ULTRA LOQVAR IN NOMINE EJUS) Co- gitatio hæc interdum mihi incidit, rectius tutiusque me fa- cturum, si mihi mandata silentio premerem.

ET FACTUS EST IN CORDE MEO QVASI IGNIS EXÆSTVANS CLAVSUSQVE IN OSSI- BUS MEIS, ET DEFECI, FERRE NON SVSTI- NENS) Repressit illam cogitationem metus pœnæ à Deo inferendæ, sicut Apostolus ait 1. Cor. 9, 17. ἀνάγκη γὰρ μοὶ ἐπίκειται. ὀυαὶ δέ μοι ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ ἐυαγγελίζω. Non abludit illud Lucani: - - Magnoque exæstuat igne Iratum te Phœbe ferens, nec verbere solo Uteris & stimulis flammasq; in viscera mergis.

## 20:10
Vers. 10. FOR I HAVE HEARD THE SLANDERS OF MANY) Better: I have indeed heard: so that it may be a preparation for that which follows immediately: But the Lord.

AND TERROR ON EVERY SIDE) Better. Magormissabib: which name Jeremiah had imposed upon Pashhur above in chapter 3. I have heard, he says, for a long time past, what snares he and his companions were laying for me.

PERSECUTE, AND LET US PERSECUTE HIM) Better: report, and we will report. This they were saying to the friends of Jeremiah, as follows: Tell us something evil about him, so that we may bring an accusation before the Sanhedrin, and thus oppress him.

OF ALL THE MEN WHO WERE MY PEACEABLE FRIENDS, AND WATCHING MY SIDE) Better in the dative, To all the men: Supply, such things were said by the men of Pashhur.

IF BY ANY MEANS HE MAY BE DECEIVED) If by chance he should say anything contradictory in any matter, or otherwise ἐνδιάβλητα (slanderous).

AND WE MAY PREVAIL AGAINST HIM) In the judgment of the Sanhedrin.

Latin:

Vers. 10. AUDIVI ENIM CONTVMELIAS MUL- TORUM) Melius: audivi quidem: ut sit præparatio ad id, quod mox sequitur: Dominus autem.

ET TERROREM IN CIRCVITV) Melius. Ma- gormissabib: quod nomen Jeremias Phassuri indiderat supra 3. Audivi inquit jam pridem, quas insidias ille & sodales ejus mihi tenderent.

PERSEQVIMINI, ET PERSEQVAMVR EUM) Melius: annuntiate & annuntiabimus. Hoc illi dicebant amicis Jeremiæ, ut sequitur: Indicate nobis aliquid mali de ipso, ut nos indicium faciamus Synedrio, & sic eum op- primamus.

AB OMNIBVS VIRIS QVI ERANT PACIFI- CI MEI, ET CVSTODIENTES LATVS MEVM) Melius in dativo, Omnibus viris: Supple talia dicebant ho- mines Phassuris.

SI QVO MODO DECIPIATVR) Si qua forte in re dixerit repugnantia, aut aliter ἐνδιάβλητα.

ET PRÆVALEAMUS ADVERSVS EVM) In judicio Synedrii.

## 20:11
Vers. 11. FOR THEY HAVE NOT UNDERSTOOD THE EVERLASTING REPROACH, WHICH SHALL NEVER BE BLOTTED OUT) Better: the matter will not succeed for them: nay, eternal infamy will follow them, which shall never be blotted out. The event itself proves that the Prophet truly predicted this. For to this day the name of those who plotted the destruction of the Prophet is infamous.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QVIA NON INTELLEXERVNT OP- PROBRIVM SEMPITERNUM, QVOD NVNQVAM DELEBITVR) Melius: non succedet res eis: imo sequetur eos infamia æterna, quæ nunquam delebitur. Quod vere prædixisse Prophetam, res ipsa comprobat. Est enim in hunc diem infame nomen eorum, qui Prophetæ exitium machinati sunt.

## 20:12
Vers. 12. PROVER OF THE JUST) You who test the constancy of good men in many ways.

FOR TO THEE HAVE I REVEALED MY CAUSE) That is, I have commended it. A metonymy, such as above 11, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PROBATOR JVSTI) Qui virorum bono- rum constantiam multis modis exploras.
