TIBI ENIM REVELAVI CAVSAM MEAM) Id est, commendavi. μετωνυμία, qualis supra 11, 20.

## 20:13
Vers. 13. HE HATH DELIVERED THE SOUL OF THE POOR FROM THE HAND OF THE EVIL) This deliverance seems to have occurred when Zedekiah succeeded Jehoiachin, or Jeconiah, in the kingdom. This seems to be gathered from the two following chapters.

Latin:

Vers. 13. LIBERAVIT ANIMAM PAUPERIS DE MANU MALORVM) Liberatio hæc contigisse videtur cum Joachino, sive Jechoniæ, in regnum successit Sede- cias. Id colligi videtur ex capitibus duobus sequentibus.

## 20:14
Vers. 14. CURSED BE THE DAY WHEREIN I WAS BORN) It is understood here that I had said this, namely, while detained in that prison. Compare Job 3.

Blessed Hulsein rightly observed from a comparison of verse 13 and the last verse with chapter 39, 14, that this curse is spoken not from the feeling of the Prophet, but from the person of the lost Jews through ethopoeia; because, namely, he himself knew that he was not to be destroyed in the captivity, but rather to be honored. So also Jerome, Calvin, Tremellius, Piscator, Maldonatus, Castro, Gisler.

Latin:

Vers. 14. MALEDICTA DIES, IN QVA NATVS SVM) Subauditur hic dixeram, nempe in carcere isto de- tentus. Confer Jobum 3.

Maledictionem hanc non ex sensu Prophetæ, sed ex persona perditorum Judæorum per Ethopoeiam dici è collatione v. 13. & ult, cum c. 39,14. recte ob- servavit B. Hulsein. quia sc. ipse norat se non per- dendum in captivitate, sed potius honorandum. Ita & Hieronym. Calvin. Tremell. Piscat. Maldonat. Castro. Gisler.

## 20:16
Ver. 16. LET THAT MAN BE AS THE CITIES, WHICH THE LORD OVERTHREW, AND HE REPENTED NOT) That is, which are so overturned that they are not even now inhabited, as the Chaldean has explained here. The Prophet refers to Sodom and the neighboring cities.

Latin:

Vers. 16. SIT HOMO ILLE VT SVNT CIVITA- TES, QVAS SUBVERTIT DOMINVS, ET NON POENITUIT EUM) Id est, quæ ita eversæ sunt, ut ne nunc quidem habitentur, ut hic exposuit Chaldæus. Respi- cit Propheta Sodoma & vicinas urbes.

## 20:17
Ver. 17. WHO DID NOT KILL ME FROM THE WOMB) Rather, in the womb, that is, together with my mother, which sense the following words require.

AND HER WOMB A PERPETUAL CONCEPTION) And her womb pregnant perpetually: That is, without birth.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QVI NON ME INTERFECIT A VUL- VA) Imo, in utero, id est, una cum matre, quem sensum requirunt sequentia.

ET VULVA EJVS CONCEPTVS ÆTERNVS) Et uterus ejus prægnans perpetuo: Id est, sine partu.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI.

He advises Zedekiah, inquiring about the outcome of the war, to surrender to the Chaldeans so that they may be preserved in life: and he exhorts him to the administration of justice, and not to trust in their fortifications.

Ver. 1. KING ZEDEKIAH) These things were done somewhat later than those predictions which we have had were published. When he wrote these things, Jeremiah was free, and that which we had above 15,19 began to be fulfilled.

PASHUR THE SON OF MALCHIAH) This Pashur is different from him who was dealt with in the preceding chapter. For that one was of the sixteenth course: but this one indeed of the fifth, as is to be seen in 1 Chron. 24,9. To the priests in these books a surname is added, not from the father, but from the family.

AND ZEPHANIAH THE SON OF MAASEIAH) That is, of the twenty-fourth course; see 1 Chron. 24,17.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI.

Zedekiam de eventu belli quærentem monet, ut se dedant Chaldæis, ut in vita serven- tur: & hortatur ad administrationem ju- stitiæ, & ne confidant munitionibus suis.

Vers. 1. REX SEDECIAS) Hæc aliquanto sunt poste- rius gesta, quam editæ istæ, quas habuimus prædictiones. Cum hæc scriberet liber fuit Jeremias, & incepit impleri quod habuimus supra 15,19.

PHASSVR FILIVM MELCHIÆ) Alius est hic Phassur ab eo, de quo actum capite præcedente. Nam ille erat ἐφημερίας decimæ sextæ: hic vero quintæ, ut videre est 1. Par. 24,9. sacerdotibus in his libris cognomen additur, non ex patre, sed ex familia.

ET SOPHONIAM FILIVM MAASIÆ) Id est, ἐφημερίας vicesimæ quartæ; vide 1. Par. 24,17.

## 21:2
Ver. 2. HE FIGHTETH AGAINST US) The LXX, ἐφίστηκεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς, he brings war upon us.

IF PERADVENTURE THE LORD WILL DEAL WITH US, ACCORDING TO ALL HIS WONDROUS WORKS) That is, let us know whether God is willing to be present with us by His admirable power, as when He besieged us with the Sennacheribs.

AND HE DEPART FROM US) Namely Nebuchadnezzar, compelled by divine power.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PRÆLIATVR ADVERSVM NOS) LXX, ἐφίστηκεν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς, bellum nobis infert.

SI FORTE FACIAT DOMINVS NOBISCUM, SECVNDVM OMNIA MIRABILIA SVA) Id est, scia- mus an Deus nobis adesse velit potentia sua admirabili, ut cum Sennacheribus nos obsedit.

ET RECEDAT A NOBIS) Nempe Nabuchodo- nosor, divina virtute coactus.

## 21:4
Ver. 4. BEHOLD I WILL TURN THE WEAPONS OF WAR, THAT ARE IN YOUR HANDS) I will turn them to other uses by far than those for which they were destined.

AND I WILL GATHER THEM IN THE MIDST OF THE CITY) That is, I will cause that, the city having been broken into, all your weapons taken from you be brought into some place of your city, which the victorious Chaldeans shall have chosen for that purpose.

This is too jejune: others more correctly, I will cause them to return into the midst of the city, that is, that the citizens may destroy themselves with their own weapons.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ECCE EGO CONVERTAM VASA BEL- LI, QVÆ IN MANIBVS VESTRIS SVNT) Vertam in alios longe usus, quam quibus destinata sunt.

ET CONGREGABO EA IN MEDIO CIVITA- TIS) Id est, efficiam, ut urbe irrupta arma vestra omnia vobis erepta adferantur in locum aliquem urbis vestræ, quem ad id elegerint victores Chaldæi.

Nimis jejunum hoc: rectius alii, faciam redi- re ea in medium civitatis, h. e. ut cives suismet ar- mis se conficiant.

## 21:5
Ver. 5. AND I WILL FIGHT AGAINST YOU WITH AN OUTSTRETCHED HAND) Through the Chaldeans. All the words are magnificent, I, by famine and pestilence, as the following explain.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET DEBELLABO EGO VOS IN MANU EXTENTA) Per Chaldæos. Verba omnia magnifica, Ego, fame & peste, ut sequentia explicant.

## 21:7
Ver. 7. INTO THE HAND OF ENEMIES) Under the power of the enemies.

AND HE SHALL SMITE THEM WITH THE EDGE OF THE SWORD) See how distinctly these things were predicted, not as λοξία θεσπίσματα (ambiguous oracles). Compare 2 Kings 25:6, 7. Them, namely the sons of Zedekiah, many of the nobles and the people. Zedekiah himself, just as Jeremiah below 34:4 and Ezekiel 9:13 predicted, died in Babylon, indeed not a violent death, but undoubtedly one contracted from grief.

Latin:

Vers. 7. IN MANU INIMICORUM) Sub potestatem hostium.

ET PERCUTIET EOS IN ORE GLADII) Vi- de quam distincte hæc prædicta, non ut λοξία θεσπίσματα. Confer 2. Reg. 25, 6, 7. Eos, nempe filios Sedeciæ, mul- tos ex proceribus & populo. Sedecias ipse, ita ut Jeremias infra 34, 4. & Ezechiel 9, 13. prædixerunt, mortuus est Ba- bylone, morte quidem non violenta, sed haud dubie ex mœrore contracta.

## 21:8
Ver. 8. BEHOLD I SET BEFORE YOU THE WAY OF LIFE, AND THE WAY OF DEATH) I will announce to you the conditions through which you will be saved or will perish. If you surrender to the Chaldean King, you will live: if not, you will perish. These things were true, but no one fails to understand with how much danger they were spoken. Nevertheless, they had to be spoken. And the Prophet did what was his duty. The freedom of προαίρεσις (choice) is shown here, as in many other places.

In such external and civil matters, no one would deny the freedom of προαίρεσις (choice). But if from there the freedom of the will in spiritual matters is asserted with the Papists, there will be no strength in the consequence. For the reason for civil and external acts, such as surrendering oneself to the Chaldean king, is far different from that of moral and spiritual acts, such as turning oneself to God and fulfilling the law of God. Which distinction the Augsburg Confession therefore rightly inculcates against the Pelagians.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ECCE DO CORAM VOBIS VIAM VITÆ, ET VIAM MORTIS) Enuntiabo vobis conditiones, per quas salvi eritis, aut peribitis. Si vos deditis Regi Chaldæo, vivetis: sin minus peribitis. Hæc vera erant, sed quanto cum periculo dicerentur, nemo non intelligit. Tamen dicenda erant. Et fecit Propheta quod erat officii sui. Libertas προ- αιρέσεως hic ostenditur, ut multis aliis in locis.

In externis ejusmodi & civilibus libertatem προαιρέσεως nemo negaverit. Sed si inde in spiri- tualibus arbitrii libertas adstruatur cum Papistis, nullus erit in consequentia nervus. Nam longe alia ratio est civilium & externorum actuum, qualis erat se dedere regi Chaldæo, alius moralium ac spi- ritualium, sese ad Deum convertere ac legemDei implere. Quod discrimen proinde recte inculcat adversus Pelagianos Augustana Confessio.

## 21:10
Ver. 10. FOR I HAVE SET MY FACE AGAINST THIS CITY FOR EVIL, AND NOT FOR GOOD) I will look upon it with an angry countenance. See Lev. 17:10 and 20:5.

IT SHALL BE GIVEN INTO THE HAND OF THE KING OF BABYLON) It shall come into his power, as above in 7.

Latin:

Vers. 10. POSUI ENIM FACIEM MEAM SUPER CIVITATEM HANC IN MALUM, ET NON IN BONUM) Maligno vultu illam aspiciam. Vide Lev. 17, 10. & 20, 5.

IN MANU REGIS BABYLONIS DABITUR) Veniet in ejus potestatem, ut supra 7.

## 21:11
Ver. 11. TO THE HOUSE OF THE KING OF JUDAH) To Zedekiah, his mother, his wives, his sons.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DOMUI REGIS JUDA) Sedeciæ, matri, u- xoribus, filiis ejus.

## 21:12
Ver. 12. EXECUTE JUDGMENT IN THE MORNING) We have said elsewhere that judgments in those places were exercised only in the morning. See what is at Job 24:17. The King of the two tribes was also able to judge himself: and to take care in the Sanhedrin that judgment was not perverted by bribes,

AND DELIVER THE OPPRESSED BY FORCE OUT OF THE HAND OF THOSE WHO SLANDER) This interpreter always translates עשק, which is to shake or extort, as the Roman jurists speak, as to slander, less accurately.

LEST PERCHANCE MY INDIGNATION GO FORTH LIKE FIRE, AND BE KINDLED, AND THERE BE NONE TO QUENCH IT, BECAUSE OF THE EVIL OF YOUR DOINGS) Even with the decrees of God sealed against the city, the king could have been saved, and his house, and other pious ones, no less than Jeremiah was saved, and Ebed-melech, and so many others.

Latin:

Vers. 12. JUDICATE MANE JUDICIUM) Diximus alibi judicia in illis locis tantum mane exercita. Vide quæ ad Job. 24, 17. Rex duarum tribuum etiam ipse judicare, pote- rat: & curam adhibere inSynedrio, ne per sordes judicaretur,

ET ERUITE VI OPPRESSUM DE MANU CA- LUMNIANTIUM) Semper hic interpres עשק, quod est concutere, ut Jurisconsulti Romani loquuntur, vertit ca- lumniari, minus accurate.

NE FORTE EGREDIATUR UT IGNIS INDI- GNATIO MEA, ET SVCCENDATVR, ET NON SIT QVI EXSTINGUAT, PROPTER MALITIAM STV- DIORVM VESTRORVM) Etiam decretis Dei contra urbem obsignatis, poterat servari rex, & ejus domus, & pii alii, non minus quam Jeremias servatus est, & Abdeme- lech, totque alii.

## 21:13
Ver. 13. BEHOLD I AM AGAINST THEE, O INHABITANT OF THE VALLEY OF THE ROCK, AND OF THE PLAIN) Better: Now I turn myself to thee (O city) who inhabitest the valley, who (as it were) lookest down upon the rock of the plain. The city of Jerusalem, situated for the most part on mountains, looked down upon wide valleys, such as those of the Rephaim and of Hinnom. See Josh. 15, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ECCE EGO AD TE HABITATRICEM VALLIS SOLIDÆ, ATQVE CAMPESTRIS) Melius: Nunc ad te me verto (ô civitas) quæ habitas vallem, quæ (velut) rupes planitiei (immines.) Urbs Hierosolyma magna sui parte in montibus sita late valles, Raphaimorum puta & Hinnomi, despiciebat. Vide Jos. 15, 8.

## 21:14
Ver. 14. AND I WILL KINDLE A FIRE IN THE FOREST THEREOF) A change of person is frequent among the Hebrews: then a metonymy. For he calls the houses built of cedar a forest. See shortly 22, 7. Add 2 Kings 25, 12. 2 Chron. 36, 19. below 52, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET SUCCENDAM IGNEM IN SALTU EJUS) Mutatio personæ frequens Hebræis: deinde μετω- νυμία. Nam silvam vocat domos à cedro exstructas. Vide mox 22, 7. Adde 2. Reg. 25, 12. 2. Par. 36, 19. infra 52, 13.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII.

A court sermon that they should execute judgment and justice: The Law and threat made to the Royal House, by which he denounces the burial of an ass to Jehoiakim, and deportation to Babylon to Jeconiah and his mother.

Ver. 1. THUS SAITH THE LORD) Thus he said. For Jeremiah, speaking to Zedekiah, at the same time repeats what he had predicted to the preceding kings, namely to his own brother, and to his brother's son, so that they might have nothing to complain of regarding such a grave vengeance of God.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII.

Concio aulica ut judicium & justitiam faciant: Lex & comminatio Domui Regiæ facta, qua Iojakimo asini sepulturam, Iechoniæ & ma- tri deportationem in Babylonem denuntiat.

Vers. 1. HÆC DICIT DOMINUS) Hæc dixit. Jere- mias enim Sedeciæ loquens simul repetit quæ regibus an- tecedentibus fratri scilicet ipsius Sedeciæ, fratrisque filio prædixerat, ne quid haberent quod de tam gravi Dei ultio- ne conquerentur.

## 22:2
Ver. 2. KING OF JUDAH) Who in 2 Kings 23, 30 is called Jehoahaz, but here below in 11 and 1 Chron. 3, 15, Shallum: which signifies retribution, an omen not good for him.

Latin:

Vers. 2. REX JUDA) Qui 2. Reg. 23, 30. Joachaz vocatur, hic vero infra 11. & 1. Par. 3, 15. Sellum: quod retributionem significat, omine ipsi non bono.

## 22:3
Ver. 3. EXECUTE JUDGMENT) Render justice holily,

AND JUSTICE) Exercise beneficence.

DELIVER THE OPPRESSED BY VIOLENCE FROM THE HAND OF THE OPPRESSOR) Supra 21, 12. AND THE STRANGER, AND THE FATHERLESS, AND THE WIDOW DO NOT OPPRESS) Supra 7, 6. AND DO NOT SHED INNOCENT BLOOD IN THIS PLACE) In the said place 7, 6. Vers. 4. THEY SHALL ENTER THROUGH THE GATES OF THIS HOUSE) Of the palace. See above v. 1. KINGS SITTING OF THE LINEAGE OF DAVID UPON HIS THRONE) As above 17, 25. Vers. 6. GILEAD YOU ARE TO ME THE HEAD OF LEBANON) Do not trust too much in either riches or the situation of the place; it is a most opulent region of the Gileadites. See Gen. 37, 25. & it is situated in Lebanon itself. Nevertheless, it was devastated by Tiglath-Pileser 2 Kings 15, 29; the same will happen to this palace. IF I SHALL NOT HAVE MADE YOU A SOLITUDE) May I not be held truthful, unless I do this.

Latin:

Vers. 3. FACITE JUDICIUM) Jus sancte reddite,

ET JUSTITIAM) Beneficentiam exercete.

LIBERATE VI OPPRESSUM DE MANU CA- LUMNIATORES) Supra 21, 12. ET ADVENAM, ET PUPILLUM, ET VI- DUAM NOLITE CONTRISTARE) Supra 7, 6. ET SANGUINEM INNOCENTEM NE EF- FUNDATIS IN LOCO ISTO) Dicto loco 7, 6. Vers. 4. INGREDIENTUR PER PORTAS DOMUS HUJUS) Palatii. Vide supra v. 1. REGES SEDENTES DE GENERE DAVID SUPER THRONUM EJUS) Ut supra 17, 25. Vers. 6. GALAAD TU MIHI CAPUT LIBANI) Noli aut opibus, aut situ loci nimium confidere, Galaadi- tis regio est opulentissima. Vide Gen. 37, 25. & sita est in ipso Libano. Attamen vastata est per Teglathphalasarem 2. Reg. 15, 29. idem huic regiæ eveniet. SI NON POSVERO TE SOLITUDINEM) Ne habear verax, nisi id facio.

## 22:7
Vers. 7. I WILL SANCTIFY AGAINST YOU) I will prepare and instruct against you. As above 6, 4. below 51, 27. YOUR CHOSEN CEDARS) From which the palace was built. Cant. 1, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SANCTIFICABO SUPER TE) Præparabo & instruam contra te. Ut supra 6, 4. infra 51, 27. ELECTAS CEDROS TUAS) Unde fabricata erat regia. Cant. 1, 16.

## 22:10
Vers. 10. DO NOT WEEP FOR THE DEAD, NOR LAMENT OVER HIM WITH WEEPING) King Josiah, who had fallen gloriously in battle against the Egyptian, snatched away from the coming evils, 2 Kings 23, 30. 22, 20. Isaiah 57, 1.

Others prefer to understand it indefinitely; that is to say, that not so much the dead who die in their own country are to be lamented, as those who are led away captive. Jerome, however, and Theodoret, as also Vatablus and Tremellius, think that it refers to Josiah.

LAMENT FOR HIM WHO GOES FORTH) Who will be carried hence into Egypt by Necho. He is Shallum himself, as follows, who is Jehoahaz, as we said 2 Kings 23, where see verse 32.

Latin:

Vers. 10. NOLITE FLERE MORTUUM, NE- QUE LUGEATIS SUPER EVM FLETU) Regem Josiam, qui in prælio contra Ægyptium gloriose occubuerat, ereptus adventantibus malis, 2. Reg. 23, 30. 22, 20. Esaias 57, 1.

Alii malunt indefinite intelligere; q. d. non tam mortuos, qui in patria sua obeunt deflendos esse, quam qui captivi abducuntur. Hieron. tamen, & Theodor. ut & Vatablus & Tremell. Josiam re- spici putant.

PLANGITE EUM QUI EGREDITUR) Qui e- vehetur hinc in Ægyptum per Necaonem. Is est ipse Sel lum, ut sequitur, qui Joachaz, ut diximus 2. Reg. 23. ubi vide comma 32.

## 22:11
Vers. 11. WHO HAS GONE FORTH FROM THIS PLACE) That he will go forth from this place: namely, by the compulsion of the king of Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QUI EGRESSUS EST DE LOCO ISTO) Egressurum illum de loco isto: nempe rege Ægypti cogente.

## 22:13
Vers. 13. WOE TO HIM WHO BUILDS HIS HOUSE IN INJUSTICE) For Jehoahaz did evil before the Lord: as we read 2 Kings 23, 32.

AND UPPER CHAMBERS NOT IN JUDGMENT) Not given, as follows, to the workers for wages, against the law Levit. 19, 23. Deut. 24, 14.

HE SHALL OPPRESS HIS FRIEND IN VAIN.) He who oppresses his fellow citizen with evils for no just cause.

Latin:

Vers. 13. VÆ QUI ÆDIFICAT DOMUM SUAM IN INJUSTITIA) Fecit enim Joachaz malum coram domino: ut legimus 2. Reg. 23, 32.

ET COENACULA NON IN JUDICIO) Non data, ut sequitur operantibus mercede, contra legem Levit. 19, 23. Deut. 24, 14.

AMICUM SUUM OPPRIMET FRUSTRA.) Qui popularem suum nulla justa de causa malis premit.

## 22:14
Vers. 14. WHO SAYS: I WILL BUILD FOR MYSELF A WIDE HOUSE) Widely extending, as is the custom of kings who have abundant money,

AND SPACIOUS UPPER CHAMBERS) In the Hebrew: exposed to the wind, such as the house of Emperor Anastasius at Constantinople called Magnaura, LXX here ῥιπιστά.

WHO OPENS WINDOWS FOR HIMSELF) On every side.

AND PAINTS WITH SINOPIS) In Hebrew ששר. The Greeks translate this as μίλτον here, elsewhere as χρώματα. There are those who think that indigo is meant.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QVI DICIT: ÆDIFICABO MIHI DO- MVN LATAM) Late patentem, ut solent reges quibus pecunia abundat,

ET COENACULA SPATIOSA) In Hebræo: ven- to exposita, qualis Anastasii Imperatoris ædes Constanti- nopoli dicta Magnaura, LXX. hic ῥιπιστά.

QVI APERIT SIBI FENESTRAS) In omne latus.

PINGITQUE SINOPIDE) In Hebræo ששר. Græci hic μίλτον vertunt, alibi χρώματα. Sunt qui Indi- cum significari putant.

## 22:15
Verse 15. SHALT THOU REIGN, BECAUSE THOU COMPAREST THYSELF TO THE CEDAR) For תתחר, which signifies cedar, the LXX clearly read תתחרה, so that the sense could be very excellent: Do you think that you will reign long and happily because you sin by the example of Ahaz? Concerning whom see 2 Kings 16 and 2 Chronicles 28. תתחר, which word we have here in the Hebrew, is elsewhere translated as ἁμαρτάνειν, elsewhere as πονηρὸν εἶναι.

Although the LXX may have rendered it thus, it is not to be concluded that the Hebrew codices had the name תתחר in their time. For the frequent oversights (παροράματα) of the LXX interpreters are well known. Nor should the Hebrew reading be abandoned, the sense of which is entirely excellent: Because thou comparest thyself to the cedar? or contendest with the cedar, or emulatest the cedar in pride, because by reason of sublimity kings are wont to be compared to cedars. And the Hebrew word denotes to contend, to emulate out of arrogance, Jer. 12:5, Psalm 37:1. Arias Montanus rendered it, because thou mixest thyself with the cedar, that is, thou dwellest in cedar chambers, as Grotius explained above v. 7, thy chosen cedars, from which the palace was built, and v. 23, Thou that nestlest in the cedars.

Verse same. DID NOT THY FATHER EAT AND DRINK?) That is, he was in prosperous circumstances for a long time, Josiah.

Latin:

Vers. 15. NUM QUID REGNABIS, QUONIAM CONFERS TE CEDRO) Pro תתחר, quod cedrum signi- ficat, LXX. manifeste legerunt תתחרה, ut sensus esse possit longe optimus: Ideone te diu ac feliciter regnaturum pu- tas, quod Achazi exemplo peccas? de quo vide 2. Reg. 16. & 2. Par. 28. תתחר quod verbum hic habemus in He- bræo, alibi vertitur ἁμαρτάνειν, alibi πονηρὸν εἶναι.

Etsi LXX. ita reddiderint, non colligendum tamen, ipsorum tempore Codices Ebræos nomen תתחר habuisse. Nota enim sunt παροράματα LXX. Interpp. frequentia. Neque deferenda est Ebræa le- ctio cujus sensus omnino optimus est: Quoniam con- fers te cedro? vel contendis cum cedro, aut æmu- laris cedrum superbia, quia ratione sublimitatis so- lent Reges cedris comparari. Et verbum Ebræum notat contendere, æmulari ex arrogantia Jer. 12, 5. Psalm. 37, 1. Ariasmontanus reddidit, quia misces te cedro, id est, habitas in conclavibus cederinis, uti supra exposuit Grotius v. 7. electas cedros tuas, unde fabricata erat Regia, Et v. 23. Nidificas in Cedris.

Vers. eod. PATER TUUS NUMQUID NON CO- MEDIT ET BIBIT?) Id est, fuit in rebus prosperis diu, Josias.

## 22:16
Verse 16. DID NOT THEREFORE BECAUSE HE KNEW ME, SAITH THE LORD) They are said to know God who show by their deeds that they know what is pleasing to God, which Josiah had done.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NUMQUID NON IDEO QUIA CO- GNOVIT ME, DICIT DOMINUS) Cognoscere Deum dicuntur, qui factis ostendunt scire se quid Deo placeat, quod fecerat Josias.

## 22:18
V. 18. THEREFORE THUS SAITH THE LORD TO JOAKIM THE SON OF JOSIAH) You will best translate לכן as furthermore, and said, instead of saith. For Jeremiah, just as he had reported to Zedekiah those things which he had previously said by God's command to his brother Joachaz, or Sellum, so he proceeds to report what he had said to Joakim, who was once reigning, likewise a brother of Zedekiah: coming then to Jechonias, who had preceded Zedekiah in the kingdom next, so that, as we just said, the justice of his vengeance which God was preparing to take, from so many preceding warnings and threats, might become more manifest.

THEY SHALL NOT LAMENT HIM, WOE BROTHER, AND WOE SISTER) Ah brother, and ah sister: Thus in mourning did kinsmen speak.

THEY SHALL NOT LAMENT HIM, WOE LORD, AND WOE NOBLE, They shall not say in weeping, Ah lord, and ah his glory. That is, the kingdom, as the Chaldean well explains here. Thus were subjects wont to speak in mourning.

Latin:

V. 18. PROPTEREA HÆC DICIT DOMINUS AD JOAKIM FILIUM JOSIÆ) לכן optime vertes præter- ea, & dixit, pro dicit. Nam Jeremias, sicut retulerat Sede- ciæ ea quæ fratri ejus Joachazo, sive Sellumo ex Dei man- dato antehac dixerat, ita pergit referre quæ Joakimo quon- dam regnanti, itidem fratri Sedeciæ, dixerat: venturus de- inde ad Jechoniam, qui proxime in regno Sedeciam præces- serat, ut, sicut modo diximus, ultionis ejus quam Deus su- mere parabat justitia, ex tot monitis ac minis antecedentibus, apertior fiat.

NON PLANGENT EUM, VÆ FRATER, ET VÆ SOROR) Ah frater, & ah Soror: Ita in luctu dice- bant consanguinei.

NON CONCREPABUNT EI, VÆ DOMINE, ET VÆ INCLITE, Non flendo dicent, Ah domine, & ah decus ejus. Id est, regnum, ut bene hic exponit Chaldæus. Ita solebant in luctu dicere subditi.

## 22:19
Verse 19.

HE SHALL BE BURIED WITH THE BURIAL OF AN ASS) Without honor.

OUTSIDE THE GATES OF JERUSALEM) Better: Far from the gates. For that is the Hebrew מהלאה, and the Greek ἐπέκεινα. See Gen. 19:9 and Amos 5:27. Joakim was led away into Babylon by the Chaldean robbers, of whom mention is made in 2 Kings 24:2, as we read in 2 Chronicles 36:6; there he perished far from his country, far from his own.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

SEPULTURA ASINI SEPELIETUR) Sine ho- nore.

EXTRA PORTAS JERUSALEM) Melius: Lon- ge à portis. Id enim est Hebræum מהלאה, & Græcum ἐπέκεινα. Vide Gen. 19, 9. & Amos 5, 27. Joakim à Chaldæis latronibus, quorum mentio 2. Reg. 24, 2. abdu- ctus est in Babylonem, ut legimus 2. Par. 36, 6. ibi interiit longe à patria, longe à suis.

## 22:20
Verse 20.

ASCEND LIBANUS, AND CRY, AND IN BASHAN GIVE THY VOICE) Jeremiah had said these things also to the city of Jerusalem, before King Jehoiakim was carried away. Cry to the Syrians thy friends: they will profit thee nothing.

AND CRY TO THE PASSERS-BY) In the Hebrew: Across the fords. Of the Nile, that is. Cry also as much as thou pleasest to the Egyptians, they will not help thee.

BECAUSE ALL THY LOVERS ARE BROKEN) Thy friends. See 2 Kings 24:7.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ASCENDE LIBANUM, ET CLAMA, ET IN BASAN DA VOCEM TUAM) Hæc etiam dixerat Je- remias civitati Hierosolymorum, antequam aveheretur rex Joakim. Clama ad Syros amicos tuos: nihil tibi proderunt.

ET CLAMA AD TRANSEUNTES) In Hebræo: Trans vada. Nili scilicet. Clama etiam quantum lubet ad Ægyptios, non juvabunt te.

QUIA CONTRITI SUNT OMNES AMATO- RES TUI) Amici tui. Vide 2. Reg. 24, 7.

## 22:21
Verse 21.

I SPOKE TO THEE IN THY ABUNDANCE) To thee, O Jerusalem. In thy tranquil times: when thou wert still living safe and secure.

THIS IS THY WAY FROM THY YOUTH) It is long since thou hast spurned my warnings. See above 2:2; Isaiah 47:12.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

LOCUTUS SVM AD TE IN ABUNDANTIA TVA) Ad te, ô Hierosolyma. In tranquillitatibus tuis: cum adhuc tuta ac secura viveres.

HÆC EST VIA TUA AB ADOLESCENTIA TUA) Jam pridem est, quod mea monita spernis. Vide supra 2, 2. Esaias 47, 12.

## 22:22
Verse 22.

ALL THY PASTORS THE WIND SHALL FEED) Vain hope suckles all thy kings and princes.

AND THY LOVERS SHALL GO INTO CAPTIVITY) The Egyptians. See below 46.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

OMNES PASTORES TUOS PASCET VENTUS) Reges tuos omnes ac principes vana spes lactat.

ET AMATORES TUI IN CAPTIVITATEM IBUNT) Ægyptii. Vide infra 46.

## 22:23
Verse 23.

THOU THAT SITTETH IN LIBANUS, AND NESTLEST IN THE CEDARS) He said the same thing twice. For by Libanus, the trees of Libanus, of which the cedars are the chief, are understood, from which the Temple, the palace, and the principal houses of Jerusalem were built. Compare Zechariah 11:1.

HOW HAST THOU GROANED) Thou shalt groan.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

QUÆ SEDES IN LIBANO, ET NIDIFICAS IN CEDRIS) Idem bis dixit. Nam per Libanum, Libani ar- bores, quarum præcipuæ cedri, intelliguntur, ex quibus Templum, palatium, ac præcipuæ domus Hierosolymorum ædificatæ erant. Confer Zach. 11, 1.

QVOMODO CONGEMUISTI) Ingemisces.

## 22:24
Verse 24.

AS I LIVE, SAYS THE LORD) The Lord said. He now comes to those things which He had formerly predicted to Jeconiah, the son of the brother of Zedekiah.

THOUGH JECONIAH THE SON OF JEHOIAKIM KING OF JUDAH WERE THE SIGNET UPON MY RIGHT HAND, YET WOULD I PLUCK THEE THENCE) In the Hebrew here it is Coniah, with the Yod removed, which makes the beginning of the name, and with a Vav added to the end. The former signifies the diminution of his head that was to happen to him. The latter is a mark of contempt, as if He were to say, that Coniah. Even if, says God, I had hitherto held him as dear and guarded him as solicitously as a signet ring is wont to be held and guarded (which is properly chotham, as both the Greeks and the Chaldean have taken it here), yet now, when I see his crimes, I would cast him away. For 'I will pluck him,' in the Hebrew it is, 'I will pluck thee.' For the Hebrews often mix persons.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

VIVO EGO, DICIT DOMINUS) Dixit Dominus. Venit jam ad ea, quæ olim Jechoniæ prædixerat, filio fra- tris Sedeciæ.

SI FUERIT JECHONIAS FILIVS JOACHIM REGIS JUDA, ANNULUS IN MANU DEX- TERA MEA, INDE EVELLAM EUM) In Hebræo hic est כניהו, ablato Jod, quod initium facit nominis, & addito ad finem ו. Prius illud eventuram ipsi capitis deminutionem significat. Alterum est contemtus nota, quasi dicat, conia ille. Etiamsi, inquit Deus, antehac eum tam carum habuissem, & sollicite custodissem, quam habe- ri ac custodiri solet gemma signatoria, quæ est in annulo (id proprie חותם, ut & Græci & Chaldæus hic accepere) ta- men nunc, cum facinora ejus video, eum abjicerem. Pro evellam eum, in Hebræo est, evellam te. Miscent enim He- bræi sæpe personas.

## 22:26
Verse 26.

AND I WILL CAST THEE OUT, AND THY MOTHER THAT BARE THEE) Nehushta, concerning whose shameful acts see above 13:18 and following. See the fulfillment in 2 Kings 24:12 and 15.

INTO A STRANGE LAND) Babylon, as can be seen in the aforementioned place of the history of the Kings, and 2 Chronicles 36:10.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ET MITTAM TE, ET MATREM TUAM, QUÆ GENUIT TE) Nohestam, de cujus flagitiis vide supra 13, 18. & sequentibus. Vide implementum 2. Reg. 24, 12. & 15.

IN TERRAM ALIENAM) Babylonem, ut videre est dicto loco historiæ Regum, & 2. Par. 36, 10.

## 22:27
Verse 27.

BUT TO THE LAND WHEREUNTO THEY DESIRE TO RETURN, THITHER SHALL THEY NOT RETURN) Into Judea, to which they most ardently desire to return.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ET IN TERRAM AD QUAM LEVANT IPSI ANIMAM SUAM, UT REVERTANTUR, NON REVERTENTUR) In Judæam, quo redire ardentissime desiderant.

## 22:28
Vers. 28. IS THIS MAN JECHONIAH A VILE AND BROKEN POT? IS HE A VESSEL WITHOUT ANY PLEASURE? This is an objection of the Jews who did not have faith in the words of Jeremiah. The Hebrew words are as follows: Is this man Jechoniah as a vile and broken sculpture (namely, before God), or as a vessel that displeases: that is, refuse, as Jerome says Symmachus translated it here. Would God, they said, hold our king in such contempt?

There is no reason why the speech of Jeremiah should be interrupted here, and these words and the following ones attributed to the Jews. There is no trace in the text of a change in the person speaking. Nor is there a 'potter's vessel' in the Hebrew; but as Luther rightly translates: is not this man Jechoniah sorrowful, despised, and dissipated? Is he not a vessel in which there is no pleasure? Cf. ch. 48, 38; Hos. 8, 8; Psalm 31, v. 13.

WHY ARE HE AND HIS SEED CAST OUT, AND CAST INTO A LAND WHICH THEY KNEW NOT?) Translate: Why were he and his seed rejected, and cast into an unknown land?

Latin:

Vers. 28. NUMQUID VAS FICTILE ATQUE CONTRITUM VIR ISTE JECHONIAS ? NVM- QUID VAS ABSQUE OMNI VOLUPTATE) Est objectio Judæorum fidem Jeremiæ verbis non habentium Verba Hebræa sic habent: An ut sculptile vile atque confra- ctum esset, (scilicet apud Deum) vir iste Jechonias, aut ut vas quod displicet: id est, quisquiliæ, ut hic vertisse Symmachum ait Hieronymus. An ita Deus, ajebant, regem nostrum haberet despicatui?

Non est causa, cur hic oratio Jeremiæ inter- rumpatur, & verba hæc ac sequentia Judæis tribu- antur. Nullum mutatæ personæ loquentis in textu est vestigium. Neque vas fictile in Ebræo est; sed uti recte Luther. vertit: annon dolorosus, con- temtus & dissipatus vir iste Iechonias. Annon vas, in quo non est voluptas. Conf. c. 48, 38. Os. 8, 8. Psalm. 31. v. 13.

QUARE ABJECTI SUNT IPSE ET SEMEN EJUS, ET PROJECTI IN TERRAM QUAM I- GNORAVERUNT?) Verte: Quare repudiarentur ipse & semen ejus, ac projicerentur in terram ignotam?

## 22:29
Vers. 29.

EARTH, EARTH, EARTH, HEAR THE WORD OF THE LORD) Jeremiah responds, and by calling out to Judea three times, so that the adjuration may be more notable, he clearly asserts that this is the decree of God.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

TERRA, TERRA, TERRA, AUDI SERMO- NEM DOMINI) Respondet Jeremias, & ter inclamans Judæam, quo notabilior sit obtestatio, plane asseverat hoc esse Dei constitutum.

## 22:30
V. 30. WRITE) So that the memory of my words may remain, which the outcome will prove. Record in the acts that I have said this.

THIS MAN BARREN) That he will depart having left no son: for that is what ערירי means to the Hebrews.

That does not agree with the words of the text, where mention is made of his seed, nor with the passage 1 Chron. 3, 17, where his sons are enumerated, nor with the genealogy of Matt. 1, 12, in which it is said that he begat Shealtiel: The Hebrew word does not precisely denote one childless, much less barren, but one destroyed and unhappy in his lineage, as observed by Jerome; it is rendered by Aquila as ἀνάυξητος, and by the LXX and Theodotion as ἐκκήρυκτος. By Luther, 'ein Verdorbenen'.

A MAN WHO IN HIS DAYS SHALL NOT PROSPER) That he will be unhappy throughout the whole time of his life.

FOR THERE SHALL NOT BE OF HIS SEED A MAN WHO SHALL SIT UPON THE THRONE OF DAVID, AND HAVE POWER ANY MORE IN JUDA) In the Hebrew: There shall not prosper of his seed. Which the Greeks say ἐμὴ ἀυξηθῇ ἐκ τῶ σπέρματος ἀυτῶ. There will be no survivors for him, so that he can hope that the kingdom will ever return to his posterity, or even any dignity lesser than the kingdom. See what we have said about this matter at Luke 3, 23.

It must be said entirely that Shealtiel and Zerubbabel, whom Luke 3 brought forward in the genealogy of Christ, were not from the lineage of Solomon, which according to this prophecy did not reign after the captivity: But from the posterity of Nathan; concerning which we are about to speak more fully at Luke 3, 23.

Latin:

V. 30. SCRIBE) Ut memoria dictorum meorum perma- neat, quæ probabit eventus. Refer in acta me hoc dixisse.

VIRUM ISTUM STERILEM) Decessurum nullo filio relicto: id enim Hebræis est ערירי.

Id non convenit verbis textus, ubi seminis e- jus mentio fit, nec loco 1. Par. 3, 17. ubi filii ejus enumerantur, neque genealogiæ Matth. 1, 12. in qua dicitur genuisse Selathielem: Vox Ebræa non præcise orbum liberis nedum sterilem notat, sed de- structum & infelicem in genere, uti Hieronymo ob- servatum, ab Aquila redditur, ἀνάυξητος, à LXX. & Theodotione ἐκκήρυκτος. Luthero ein Verdorbenen.

VIRUM QUI IN DIEBUS SVIS NON PROSPE- RABITVR) Infelicem eum fore toto vitæ tempore.

NEC ENIM ERIT DE SEMINE EJUS VIR QUI SEDEAT SVPER SOLIUM DAVID, ET PO- TESTATEM HABEAT ULTRA IN JVDA) In He- bræo: Non prosperaturum de semine ejus. Quod Græci dicunt ἐμὴ ἀυξηθῇ ἐκ τῶ σπέρματος ἀυτῶ. Non erunt ei super- stites, ut sperare possit unquam regnum ad suam posterita- tem rediturum, aut etiam dignitatem aliquam regno mino- rem. Vide quæ de hac re diximus ad Luc. 3, 23.

Dicendum omnino est, Salathiel, & Serubabel, quos in Genealogia Christi Lucas 3. adduxit, no fuis- se ex Salomonis prosapia, quæ juxta hanc prophetiā non regnavit post captivitatem: Sed è posteritate Nathanis; quo de ad Luc. 3, 23. dicturi sumus fusius.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII.

The punishment of the shepherds scattering the flock of the Lord: in whose place faithful ministers, but especially the Messiah our righteousness, are promised to be sent, and the fault and punishment of the false prophets are declared, and their boasting confounded, and the power and efficacy of the divine word is commended.

Vers. 1.

WOE TO THE SHEPHERDS) All these things up to chapter 28 contain a commemoration made by Jeremiah before Zedekiah, concerning sermons held by him at different places and times before the times of Zedekiah, and agreeing with those which he had now begun to say to Zedekiah, so that both the equity and constancy of God in his decrees might appear more, as we have already said several times. In this chapter, about to describe the sins which were in men of all ranks, Jeconiah reigning, he begins with the princes. Compare Ezek. 34, 2.

WHO SCATTER AND TEAR THE FLOCK) By their own evil example they are the cause why many of the people are to perish by the hostile sword, by pestilence, and by famine, and many indeed are to be scattered into foreign lands.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII.

Pœna Pastorum gregem Domini dissipantium: in quorum locum fideles ministros, impri- mis vero Messiam justitiam nostram mis- sum iri promittitur, falsorumq; Propheta- rum culpa & pœna indicta, & gloriatione eorum confusa, verbi divini virtus & effi- cacia commendatur.

Vers. 1.

VÆ PASTORIBUS) Hæc omnia usque ad caput 28. commemorationem continent ab Jeremia factam apud Sedeciam, de sermonibus ante Sedeciæ tempora diversis lo- cis ac temporibus à se habitis, ac congruentibus cum iis, quæ nunc Sedeciæ dicere cœperat, ut Dei in decretis suis & æquitas & constantia magis appareret, ut jam aliquoties di- ximus. In hoc capite descripturus peccata quæ erant in o- mnium ordinum hominibus, Jechonia regnante, incipit à principibus. Confer. Ezech. 34, 2.

QUI DISPERDUNT ET DILACERANT GRE- GEM) Malo suo Exemplo causa sunt, cur multi ex populis sint interituri gladio hostili, peste, ac fame, multi vero di- spergendi in terras exteras.

## 23:2
Vers. 2. WHO FEED MY PEOPLE) In name, not in reality.

AND HAVE NOT VISITED THEM) You did not have the care for them which you ought to have had.

BEHOLD I WILL VISIT UPON YOU THE MALICE OF YOUR ENDEAVORS) I will punish. A play on words. For פקד signifies both to care for and to punish.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUI PASCUNT POPVLVM MEUM) No- mine, non re.

ET NON VISITASTIS EOS) Non habuistis eo- tum curam, quam debebatis,

ECCE EGO VISITABO SUPER VOS MALI- TIAM STUDIORUM VESTRORUM) Puniam. Lu- fus ex ambiguo. Nam פקד & curare & punire fignificat.

## 23:3
Vers. 3.

AND I WILL GATHER THE REMNANT OF MY FLOCK.) I will treat those more mildly who sinned by another's example than those who were the authors of sinning for others. Compare what is below in chapter 24 and Zech. 10, 3. AND THEY SHALL GROW AND BE MULTIPLIED) As indeed happened after the return.

Latin:

Verf. 3.

ET EGO CONGREGABO RELIQUIAS GRE- GIS MEI.) Mitius eos tractabo, qui alieno exemplo pec- carunt, quam qui peccandi auctores aliis fuerunt. Confer quæ infra cap. 24. & Zach. 10, 3. ET CRESCENT ET MULTIPLICABUNTUR) Ut fane evenit post reditum.

## 23:4
Vers. 4.

AND I WILL RAISE UP OVER THEM SHEPHERDS, AND THEY SHALL FEED THEM) Good princes, such as Ezra and Nehemiah. THEY SHALL NOT FEAR ANY MORE, AND THEY SHALL NOT BE AFRAID) They will live secure under the most powerful protection of the Kings of Persia. AND NONE SHALL BE SOUGHT FROM THE NUMBER) They will live for a very long time. See Isaiah 65, 20.

Latin:

Verf. 4.

ET SUSCITABO SUPER EOS PASTORES, ET PASCENT EOS) Principes bonos, quales Esdra & Nehemias. NON FORMIDABUNT ULTRA, ET NON PAVEBUNT) Vivent fecuri sub præsidio potentiffimo Re- gum Perfarum. ET NULLUS QUÆRETUR EX NUMERO) Diutiffime vivent. Vide Efaiam 65, 20.

## 23:5
Vers. 5.

BEHOLD THE DAYS COME) They will come after almost two hundred years. AND I WILL RAISE UP DAVID) That is, for David. A JUST BRANCH) Zerubbabel, who is צמח, as he is called here and also in Zechariah 6:12, doubtless because he was like a shoot reborn from the tree of David, as if it had been cut down. Zerubbabel is commended by the name of Justice also in Zechariah 9:9. AND A KING SHALL REIGN, AND SHALL BE WISE) Zerubbabel did not indeed take upon himself the name of King and the insignia of the kingdom, but he was honored by his own people as King, as much as circumstances allowed, being indeed the true offspring of David. And therefore he is called King also in Zechariah 9:9 and here below in 33:7, bearing a sufficiently manifest figure of Christ.

Latin:

Verf. 5.

ECCE DIES VENIUNT) Venient post annos ferme ducentos. ET SUSCITABO DAVID) Id est, Davidi. GERMEN JUSTUM) Zorobabelem, qui צמח, ut hic appellatur ita & Zachariæ 6, 12. nimirum quod velut surculus renatus esset ex arbore Davidis, quasi præcisa. Ju- stitiæ nomine commendatur Zorobabel etiam apud Zacha- riam 9. v. 9. ET REGNABIT REX, ET SAPIENS ERIT) No- men quidem Regis & regni insignia non sumfit sibi Zoroba- bel, sed à suis pro Rege cultus fuit, quantum res ferebant, vera quippe Davidis progenies. Ideoque Rex appellatus etiam apud Zachariam 9, 9. & hic infra 33, 7. figuram ge- rens Christi satis manifestam.

## 23:6
Verse 6.

IN THOSE DAYS JUDAH SHALL BE SAVED) That is, he shall live safely, as the following words explain. AND THIS IS THE NAME WHICH THEY SHALL CALL HIM) Namely, the people. THE LORD OUR JUST) Better: The Lord our justice. I.e., God has done well for us. For צדק is often beneficence to the Hebrews: nor did the Chaldean take it otherwise here. What is said here of the people of Israel is said below of the city of Jerusalem in 33:16. He wishes all these things to be understood of the Shepherds raised up after the Babylonian captivity, and of the multiplication of the people after the return. He followed the Jews, who interpret these things concerning the restoration from the Babylonian captivity. There are those who think that the same things should be explained both of the bodily leading out from the Babylonian captivity and of the spiritual restoration to the Church, and therefore they think the Prophet speaks at once of the type and the antitype. But we have often shown that a double sense of this kind cannot have a place at the same time; that the discourse is about a spiritual restoration alone, the things which follow in the context evidently convince. For it is added in verse 4: They shall fear no more and shall not be dismayed. Grotius rashly seizes upon these as referring to security under the protection of the Persians. For they remove all fear, all dismay. But did not the Jews fear their enemies after the restoration, Sanballat, Tobiah the Ammonite, the Macedonians, the Romans, and others? Therefore it is manifest that spiritual happiness and the removal of all fear from the power of Satan and sin, which is the proper tranquility and salvation of the faithful, is designated. Isa. 11:6, Luke 1:14. NONE SHALL BE SOUGHT FROM THE NUMBER. These do not denote a long life, as Grotius perverts it, for neither do the words bear that, nor is it established that the Jews led a longer life after the return than at other times (the sense of Isa. 65:20 was treated in the vindications of that passage). But they deny that any of the sheep will perish, or will be sought for in vain. And since very many of the Israelites were sought for after the return, and neither were more than two tribes, nor were even those returned in their entirety, what is more certain than that these things are not to be accepted concerning a bodily return, but concerning a spiritual one? For the Prophet deals with the salvation of Judah equally, and of Israel, as is evident from verse 6. Therefore, the discourse concerning the non-loss of the elect, that is to say, that none of them shall perish eternally, John 10:16. For this reason, Jerome rightly understands the shepherds here to be the Apostles, who gathered the remnants of the Lord's flock, the Jews, from the dispersion, so that no sheep might be missing or lacking in the number of the faithful. Blessed Bugenhagen interprets these words differently: NOT TO BE SOUGHT or required, that is, to be punished, when the wicked are visited, so that it may be signified that all will be beloved children of God in this kingdom, over which good shepherds will be set. The same Blessed predecessor of ours has treated this whole prophecy solidly against the Jewish corruptions, which Grotius interpolated, whom it is therefore helpful to hear here. BEHOLD I WILL GATHER THE REMNANTS) The Jews understand these things concerning the reduction from the Babylonian captivity after seventy years, as if God were saying here: with the Kings, Princes, Priests, Prophets, and the impious people lost through the Babylonian captivity, I will again gather for myself a Church from the remnants into these lands, and then I will give them good princes, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel, etc., good priests, Jeshua or JESUS, etc., good prophets, Zechariah, Haggai, Malachi, etc., who may feed the remnants of my people, that is, govern my people according to the law and the word of God. It will indeed be permitted by me that they should explain it thus, but this exposition does not satisfy the promise of God, because here He promises: I will raise up shepherds over my remnants, who will feed them, so that they shall no longer fear or be terrified or be visited, says the Lord, who cannot lie, who will do all these things. Certainly these things were not fulfilled when they were brought back after seventy years from the Babylonian captivity: for it is well known from the history of Ezra and Nehemiah that those remnants feared and were terrified when they were rebuilding those lands and the city of Jerusalem and the temple, even under those shepherds whom I mentioned, that is, the princes, priests, and prophets. How truly those remnants were visited by God for their sin most horribly, the history of the book of Maccabees testifies, when they even began to be seduced from the public preaching of the sincere word of God by impious priests, for whom all things were venal, the priesthood and all sacred things, by the scribes and Pharisees, who began in the time of the Maccabees, by whose traditions the law was obscured, as you see in Matthew 5, the Gospel concerning the promised seed was obscured, so that the scribes and Pharisees could not answer Christ when He asked how David in the Spirit calls Christ his Lord, if Christ is his son? They did not acknowledge their sins from the law but dreamed that they were righteous by the law: they did not know that the promised seed was their righteousness, if they believed in the promised seed, that is, that they had the remission of sins through Christ alone, according to the promise, or according to the Gospel. The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent; in thy seed, O Abraham, shall all the nations of the earth be blessed. This is the misery of miseries, and a very harsh and intolerable visitation of a people (unless blindness were to follow), when God thus allows a people to depart from the faith of the word of God into the horrible darkness of the doctrines of demons, just as Adam and Eve fell, just as we fell under the Pope, of whom Paul predicted: The Spirit says clearly that in the last times, that is, after the Apostolic times and after the doctrine of the Apostles, they will depart from the faith, giving heed to spirits of error and doctrines of demons, in hypocrisy, that is, under the guise of the worship of God, under the name of Christ and faith, speaking lies, etc. Lord God, You visit our sins too horribly when You thus cast us away into errors from Your face. Concerning which visitation and plague and spiritual captivity, which the foolish world that is seduced and led away from God does not see nor feel, the Lord says in Isaiah 52: You were sold for nothing (into the servitude of human traditions), therefore you shall also be redeemed without money. Because thus says the Lord God: My people went down at the first into Egypt to be a sojourner there. And Assur without cause oppressed them. Now therefore what have I here, says the Lord, that my people is taken away for nothing? This is the third captivity, which happens for nothing, that is, through a thing and a plague which is neither seen nor felt. The people remain quiet in their land, and yet invisibly and insensibly, that is, for nothing, they are led away from their God into errors to strange gods through the doctrine of the scribes and Pharisees, from whom afterwards also came the sect of the Epicureans, who called themselves Sadducees, among whom in the time of Christ were Annas, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, the magistrates of the temple, the monstrous heads of that people, who boasted that they were the people of God. Of whom God adds in Isaiah: Its rulers raise up howling (that is, by their doctrine and feigned worship they make evil consciences before God) and my name is continually blasphemed every day. In this worst captivity we also were under the blasphemous Papists. But hear the liberation through Christ: Therefore, He says, my people shall know my name in that day, for behold I myself will speak. Let there be thanks to Christ the liberator forever. For it follows also concerning the preachers of the Gospel: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news upon the mountains, etc. When, therefore, after the Babylonian captivity the people brought back were so afraid, terrified, and visited by the judgment of God with external wars and internal errors, how can these words of Jeremiah, or of God in Jeremiah: I will raise up shepherds over them, who will feed them, so that they shall no longer fear or be terrified or be visited, be understood of that bodily reduction after seventy years of captivity? Add that they were afraid and terrified and visited by a most harsh visitation according to the body, when they were subjugated by the Romans, and when, having received many disasters, they were forced to accept Herod, an alien King, against the law of Deuteronomy 17. Therefore these words in Jeremiah can in no way be understood concerning the bodily return from the Babylonian captivity, unless it be that God is about to provide such things to those returned after the captivity, beginning in their own land, namely at the time of the incarnate Christ. For by these words God promises that He will give them pastors, that is, Prophets and preachers, of whom it is treated here, who may feed, that is, teach the people by the preaching of repentance and the remission of sins, so that the sheep from that pasture or doctrine may have peace forever before GOD, which is completed in Christ alone, who ascending on high, led captivity captive, gave gifts to men, some Apostles, some Prophets, others Evangelists, others pastors and Doctors for the perfecting of the saints in the body of Christ. These preached the remission of sins, and eternal peace through Christ Rom. 5. Being justified by faith we have peace toward God etc. Then many Jews remained in the kingdom of the Persians and Medes, and of Babylon, who did not wish to return. For it is written in Ezra that only those returned, whose spirit God had touched. Likewise many were scattered into almost all nations, who certainly were not gathered again into their folds, that is, as the Jews here explain, into that land, promised to the fathers, from whence they had been cast out by the Babylonian captivity; this you see Acts 2. Jews from every nation, which is under heaven. Here however Christ through the preaching of the Gospel (just as from His resurrection He commands: Go into the whole world, preach the Gospel to every creature, etc.) gathered as a good shepherd the remnants of his flock, that is, those whom the Father chose and loved in Christ before the foundation of the world. From all, he says, the lands to which I had cast them out, namely on account of sin from Paradise from my face. And I will bring them back into their folds, that is, from the kingdom of sin and death (for I will crush the head of the serpent) into the kingdom of heaven, from whence I had cast them out, through the captivity of death, so that they may grow in the faith and knowledge of Christ, and be multiplied throughout the whole world into eternal life. Therefore this is a notable passage concerning Christ and the salvation of all peoples, or concerning the Church of Christ gathered from Jews and Gentiles into one kingdom of heaven, which is the Kingdom of Christ upon earth until the consummation of the age, in which Church through the preachers of the Gospel there is security and eternal peace. Concerning which preachers or shepherds it is said thus in Isaiah 52. How beautiful are the feet upon the mountains of those bringing good news, of those announcing peace, etc. Concerning this spiritual restoration and gathering through Christ we sing to the Holy Spirit: You who through the diversity of all languages gathered the nations in the unity of the faith. And Christ: I have other sheep, which are not of this fold, them I must bring, and there shall be one shepherd and one fold. The Evangelist John in chapter 11 also says thus: Jesus was about to die for the people, and not for the people only, but that he might gather into one the children of God who were scattered. He calls them scattered, who through various sects and idolatries had departed from God throughout the whole world, nay, had been cast away from God on account of sin to the doctrines of demons. By what reason then were they children of God? By the predestination, election, love, or grace of God, by which God chose them and loved or gratified them in Christ from eternity before the foundation of the world, Eph. 1. These were now scattered, i.e., still ungodly according to the condition of time, Rom. 5, etc. Micah 2, God promises this spiritual restoration from the underworld to God through Christ alone. I, he says, will gather all of you, Jacob, and I will bring the remnants of Israel into one, I will gather them together as a Shepherd into one fold, like a flock into its folds, so that the noisy sound of a multitude of men may be heard there. The breaker-through will ascend before them. They will break through and will enter through the gate and will go out: And their King will go before them and the LORD as Leader before them. What he says of all Jacob, this Paul later repeats in Rom. 11 in these words: I do not want you, brothers, to be ignorant of this mystery, that blindness in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles should enter in, and so all Israel should be saved. For not all who are of the flesh of Abraham are children of Abraham, but all who believe as Abraham, whether Jews or Gentiles, are children of Abraham, Rom. 4. Ezek. 34. The same restoration is promised through Christ the one Shepherd. Thus says the Lord: And I will make a covenant with them, and I will exterminate all evil beasts, so that the sheep may dwell securely in the desert and sleep in the woods; read the rest. And ch. 37. Thus says the Lord. Behold I will bring the children of Israel from the nations where they have gone: And I will gather them from every side and will bring them back into their own land and will make of them one people, in the land upon the mountains of Israel, and all together shall have one King (David, that is, Christ from the seed of David). Nor shall they be divided any more into two peoples or two Kingdoms. Nor shall they pollute themselves with their idols and abominations, and manifold sins. From all places in which they have sinned I will rescue them, and I will cleanse them: And they shall be my people and I will be their God and my servant David shall be their King and the one shepherd of them all. And they shall walk in my laws, they shall keep my precepts and shall perform them, and they shall dwell upon the land which I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt, they and their children and their children's children shall dwell in it forever. And my servant David shall be their Prince forever. And I will make with them a covenant of peace, which shall be an eternal covenant with them, and I will preserve and multiply them, and my Sanctuary shall be among them forever. And I will dwell among them, and I will be their God and they shall be my people, so that the nations also may know that I am the Lord, who sanctifies Israel. For my Sanctuary shall be among them forever. These things we allow the Jews to interpret as their being restored from the Babylonian captivity after seventy years, and that God would do good to them in the land of their fathers; but that God then fulfilled this promise, which is expressed in the Prophets in such clear words, that is, that God after seventy years gathered all Jacob or Israel from all lands, and brought them back into the land of Canaan, each to his own inheritance, from whence they had been cast out, and from them constituted an eternal Kingdom under one shepherd and King of righteousness, David, in which Kingdom there is eternal righteousness and peace, just as, as you see, God promises in the Prophets, this the Jews cannot show, except in Christ Jesus the Son of God our Lord, as we have said, who brought back all Israel, that is, all believing Jews and Gentiles and those who will believe, from the captivity of sin and death, from the Kingdom of Satan, to God, to the kingdom of heaven, from whence we had been cast out on account of sin, just as Christ says, I am the way, the truth and the life, no one comes to the Father, except through me. No one has ascended into heaven, except he who came down from heaven, the son of man, who is in heaven. Therefore, to those restored corporally after seventy years of captivity, here is promised a spiritual restoration through Christ, who came as an eternal priest to his holy Temple, Mal. 3, Hag. 2, into the royal city as an eternal King, as Zechariah had predicted: Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold your King comes to you, etc., and there he began a priestly Kingdom, and a royal priesthood in the spirit eternal, which is the kingdom of heaven, the Kingdom of God, the Kingdom of Christ, a holy people, just, in eternal peace before God. This Kingdom begun there and sprinkled with the blood of the immaculate lamb, Christ rising from the dead, spread through good shepherds throughout the whole world, just as he himself said after the resurrection: It behooved Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. Eph. 2. The Law shall go forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. Ps. 110. The Lord shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion. The same things are said in Micah 4, etc. The Jews denied this Christ, our righteousness and life, and therefore the Kingdom of God was taken away from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. They have been laid waste and cast away not only from their land, but also by God, so that now they are not the people of God, but a blasphemy of God, so far is it from the case that they attained the Kingdom of eternal peace, which is promised here, after seventy years in the land of Canaan. The blasphemous Jews and their Rabbis, after they denied Christ, strive with wondrous madness to obscure and corrupt these and other promises concerning Christ. Nor do we wonder, because they have been blinded and cast away by God and delivered into a reprobate mind. But we do wonder at our own people, who do not think they are interpreting the Prophets properly unless they follow the blasphemous corruptions of the Rabbis. THEY SHALL NOT FEAR ANY MORE nor shall they be terrified NOR SHALL THEY BE VISITED; Which, Bugenhagen continues, was so fulfilled in any earthly kingdom, as the Jews cannot show, so also it is done impossible, but in the kingdom of Christ it is fulfilled, where although there is still trembling on account of the flesh and blood of true Christians, because sin still remains in the flesh, nevertheless there is the highest security and eternal peace in the spirit through faith and the greatest certainty of doctrine through the Gospel of good shepherds, so that you no longer fear on account of uncertainty, as under the Doctrines of Demons, or even as under the servitude of the law, where our Pharisees and Papists, as they did not know the grace of God through Christ alone, so they did not preach it. There was dread and terror of consciences, it was unknown who we might please God, and what might please God. Concerning which Christ says in John 6: This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he sent; God was judged not to be a Father but a Judge, etc. Concerning this security and peace Isaiah also speaks in chapter 32. And the work of justice shall be peace, and the worship of justice silence and security even unto eternity: And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace and in the tabernacles of confidence and in a wealthy rest, etc. And chapter 9: His Empire shall be multiplied and of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his Kingdom, to confirm and corroborate it in judgment and justice from henceforth and even unto eternity. And you have read from Ezekiel: And I will make a covenant of peace with them, etc. And Zacharias, the father of John, full of the Holy Spirit, sings: That without fear, delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him in holiness and justice before him all our days. But attend diligently here to what he says: And I will raise up over them Shepherds who shall feed them, etc. Just as Christ also admonishes: Pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send laborers into his harvest. For by this the Prophet says that Christ will reign over the earth and will give eternal peace in his Kingdom through the preaching of the Gospel, so that here in faith we may have peace, and see through a glass in a riddle, until the last day. Christ reigns in the world through his word, that is, the preached Gospel, from which men receive the Holy Spirit, so that they may be enlightened and can believe in JESUS CHRIST the son of GOD and through Christ received by faith become sons of GOD and the Kingdom of eternal peace. Such a kingdom of CHRIST the Prophets promised. And Moses himself predicts in Deuteronomy 18: The Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet from the midst of your brothers, like me; him you shall hear. For I will put my words in his mouth and he will speak them in my name: But whoever will not hear that Prophet, I will be an avenger, says the Lord. That which the Baptist says thus in John 3: He who does not believe in the son, the wrath of God remains upon him. This is what Christ answers to those asking in John 8, 'Who are you?': I speak in the world what I have heard from the Father, that is, God has put his words in my mouth, as Moses predicted: That which he also says thus in John 14: The word which you have heard is not mine, but the Father's who sent me. And elsewhere: I do not speak from myself, etc. That the Kingdom of Christ over the earth is a Kingdom of the word and of faith, the Jews do not believe, the Papists, persecutors of the Gospel and enemies of CHRIST, do not believe today, and yet such a thing God promises here. And I will raise up over them shepherds, who shall so feed the remnants of the people of God gathered from all lands to King Christ, that they may become a Kingdom of eternal security and peace. Thanks be to Christ forever. These are the words of Mr. Bugenhagen, of blessed memory.

Nor indeed can the righteous Branch, which is promised here to be raised up, be understood of any other than the Messiah alone. Not of Zerubbabel, whether he alone is understood here, or Christ is said to be designated at the same time as an antitype under him. For the predicates in no way fit Zerubbabel, but are proper to Christ alone, which are uttered concerning this branch of David. For first, this righteous branch is called so absolutely. Which epithet fits no one else simply, except Christ alone. For there is no man who does not sin, 1 Kings 8:46. There is none who does good, there is not even one, Ps. 14:3. And how would the Prophet call Zerubbabel the righteous branch simply and absolutely above others, when he himself was a man subject to sins, nor entirely alien from all injustice? How can he who is conceived in iniquity be called the RIGHTEOUS BRANCH, by which name original justice is primarily included, because he germinates not in injustice and iniquity, but as a righteous and holy branch, as is held concerning Christ in Luke 1:35: The holy thing which shall be born of you. We will teach in the annotations to the same that the place in Zechariah 6:12 is wrongly dragged to Zerubbabel. Furthermore, when a branch is said to be raised up to David, regard is had to the promises made to David, and to the faithful mercies of David, 2 Sam. 7:14, Isa. 55:3. And therefore it is necessary to understand these things not of Zerubbabel, but of Christ. Thirdly, the name of the branch appropriated to Christ in the promises confirms that these things are to be accepted concerning Christ: which parallel places evidently establish: Isa. 4:1, ch. 11:1, ch. 53:2, Zech. 3:8, ch. 6:12, Luke 1:7, 8. Fourthly, the royal axiom does not fit Zerubbabel, who did not shine with royal dignity and Majesty. But here the discourse is of that branch of David which was to be a King. And therefore the discourse is uniquely not of Zerubbabel, but of Christ the King. Who is described everywhere by Royal Majesty and throne and royal scepter, Ps. 2, 45, 72, 60, Isa. 9, Zech. 9, Luke 1, etc. It is weak, what Grotius says, that Zerubbabel was honored by his own as King, as much as the situation allowed. For neither did the situation allow it, nor does history agree with it. And although he was a true descendant of David, he was not for that reason to be honored as King. Not all were Kings, or were honored as Kings, who drew their origin from David. That he is called King in Zechariah 9:9 is false. For we know from Matthew 21 that not Zerubbabel, but Christ is presented there. Nor was he King for the reason that he bore the figure of Christ, for Prophets and Leaders also bore his figure. Fifth, the King who is to administer justice and judgment is none other than the Messiah, whose Kingdom is celebrated everywhere for justice and judgment, Isa. 9, ch. 11, whereas no other earthly kingdoms deserve this praise absolutely. For there is no kingdom in the world in which some iniquity or injustice does not sprout. Sixth, when he is said to be about to erect justice and judgment IN THE EARTH, a catholic and ecumenical Kingdom is designated, which spreads itself through the whole earth, and is not bound to a certain place. Which belongs to Christ alone, the King of Kings, and Lord of Lords. Seventh, under this King, salvation for Judah and secure habitation for Israel is promised. But that Judah and Israel, or all twelve tribes, obtained salvation and security under Zerubbabel is false. And therefore ἐξ ἀνάγκης [of necessity] it is about the Kingdom of Christ, under which to all the faithful and spiritual subjects from Judah and Israel, i.e. to the universal Church, spiritual salvation and security befalls, Rom. 5, 1. seqq. ch. 14, 17. Eighth, the name which is attributed to this King is proper to the Messiah alone, because this is the name by which everyone shall call him: Jehovah our righteousness. Does this name befit Zerubbabel, or any other ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ [mere man]? But the Messiah is both Jehovah and God blessed above all forever, Rom. 9, 5, and our righteousness, because he was made righteousness for us by God the Father, 1 Cor. 1, 29, and in him is our righteousness, Isa. 45, 24. But it is a most wicked στρεβλότης [distortion] when Grotius drags this name to the people, and perverts it thus: God does good to us. Not the people, but the branch to be raised up for David is the subject matter underlying the Prophecy concerning the name of this one, not that one, that the action had to be taken. Clearly, he whose birth and lineage, whose kingdom and mighty works in administering the government, whose subjects and kingdom are happily described, was the one who had to be described, distinguished, and celebrated by name; not, however, the people of Israel. It will be said of the righteous Branch that he is himself Jehovah our righteousness, inasmuch as he is described as righteous in himself, and is said to be about to execute judgment and righteousness in the earth. Therefore, this cannot be applied to the people. And who is that people who was to be so called? The name of the people did not precede; mention was made of Judah and Israel; but to whom will that name be drawn? To Judah or to Israel? Finally, if that name were to be attributed to the people by others, how will others call the people Jehovah our righteousness? Is the Jewish people righteousness to others? Grotius's glosses, if there were to be room for them, would have had to be formed thus: And this is the name by which they will call him (the people) Jehovah THEIR righteousness, not indeed Jehovah OUR righteousness, i.e., according to Grotius, Jehovah will do good to them. But by what argument, I ask, will it be taught that 'righteousness' here is understood as beneficence, and that the beneficence shown to the Jewish people will be celebrated by others? These glosses smack merely of a private interpretation, and are clearly twisted. Nor does the parallel passage in ch. 33:15 help them in any way; for there it is not Jerusalem, but the Messiah who is distinguished by this name. Finally, to say something also about the authority of the ancients, the explanation of the Fathers, who unanimously accepted the oracle concerning Christ, was not to be neglected, especially because it was firm by the constant sense and consensus of the Church that it was to be understood solely of Christ. Indeed, if Grotius refused to lend his ears to Christians, he ought at least to have listened to the older Jews, who acknowledged that the passage was to be accepted concerning the Messiah. For thus it is held in Bereshith Rabba on Gen. 25:6: 'When Solomon was magnified in your kingdom, they said, perhaps he is the Messiah; immediately they came to him, as it is said (1 Kings 10:1): And the queen of Sheba heard the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, and she came to him. What is meant by "concerning the name of the Lord"? The prophets made for those who prophesied in the name of the Lord their God the words which had been handed down to them, and which came successively to their hand from Abraham, as it is said (Is. 60:6): The multitude of camels shall cover you: the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, all they from Sheba shall come, they shall bring gold and incense: and they shall announce the praises of the Lord God. This is the King Messiah, as it is said (Jer. 23:6): And this is the name by which they shall call him, The Lord our righteousness.' And here Isaiah says (ch. 60:2): 'God shall arise upon you, and his glory shall appear upon you, and they shall go to your light, and Kings to the brightness of your rising.' In Echa Rabbathi on that passage (Lam. 1:16): 'Because the comforter who restores my soul is far from me,' these things are read: 'What is the name of the King Messiah? R. Abba said: Jehovah is his name, by which they shall call him The Lord our righteousness. R. Joshua Ben Levi said: The Branch is his name, as it is said (Zech. 6:12): Behold, the man whose name is the Branch.' In Midrash Tillim on Ps. 22: 'O Lord, in your strength the King shall rejoice.' And what is his name? Jehovah, as it is said Ex. 15:2. And concerning the King Messiah it is written (Jer. 23:6): And this is his name. Similarly, the explanation of the Talmud holds, in which in the book Bava Bathra in the distinction Hammocher and Hassephinah you will find these things: R. Jonathan said: Three are called by the name of the holy and blessed God, and they are these: the righteous, the Messiah, and Jerusalem. The Messiah, as it is written (Jer. 23:6): And this is his name, etc. R. Saadia Gaon on Dan. 7:13: 'Behold, with the clouds of heaven as the Son of man; This is, he says, the Messiah OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.' What of the fact that the Rabbis, as can be seen in Raimundus Martini in the Pugio Fidei part 2, ch. 11, assume this as undoubted and manifest, that these things speak of the Messiah, and urge this against Christians in this way: since the Jews were to be saved in the days of the Messiah, as is MANIFESTLY held in this place from the words of Jeremiah, and such a captivity and such grave evils never happened to them before or after as in the days of Jesus Christ, nor were they so destroyed, dissipated, and dispersed, Jesus Christ can in no way be the Messiah. In Sefer Ikkarim book 2, chapter 28, it is said thus: 'Scripture calls the Messiah God our righteousness (Jer. 23:6), because he is the Mediator of God, through whom we obtain righteousness from God.' Nor does the Chaldean, to whom Grotius appeals in vain, say otherwise. For he rendered it thus: 'Behold, the days are coming, etc., and I will raise up for David a righteous MESSIAH, etc., and this is his name, which they will say to him, etc.' Therefore, it is the name of the Messiah that is expounded here, not the name of the people, according to the Chaldean Interpreter as well as the older Rabbis: even if in the Chaldean the people convert this name to their own use; since it is rendered in this way: 'they themselves will say, or will call him: May justification be for us before God because of reverence for him.' For the Messiah is our righteousness for this reason, that we are justified before God because of him and in him.

And these things concerning the notable oracle of our Prophet, whose continuity with the preceding things Jerome has handed down, and at the same time has briefly embraced most of the arguments brought forward by us, whence we submit his words: 'The shepherds of the synagogue having therefore been cast away, namely the scribes and Pharisees, and the remnants from Israel having been saved, and the Apostles of the Gospel having been appointed in the place of the former leaders: the Shepherd of shepherds, and the Prince of princes, and the King of Kings, and the Lord of Lords is introduced, namely Christ our Savior, who is properly the righteous branch or the righteous rising, of whom we read: Righteousness shall rise in his days. And in another place: Behold, the man whose name is the rising, and he shall rise up under him, and he shall build the temple to the Lord; so that just as in Isaiah he is called Emmanuel, i.e., God with us, so in Jeremiah he receives the name, our righteousness.' Whence also the Apostle speaks: 'Who was made for us by God Righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption.' Contrary to whom is the anti-Christ and his inhabitant the devil, who in Zechariah is called the foolish Shepherd. And he shall execute, he says, judgment and justice in the earth. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son. In those days both the two and the ten tribes: Judah and Israel shall be saved together. And concerning the two rods, according to Ezekiel, they shall become one rod: And his name, if according to the LXX he shall call him Lord, shall be called Josedech, i.e., Lord Just, thus according to the Hebrew, who said, they shall call his name: it shall be said: The Lord our righteousness. For this is signified by יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ: for which Symmachus translates, Lord justify us.

Latin:

Verf. 6.

IN DIEBUS ILLIS SALVABITUR JUDA) Id est, tuto vivet, ut sequentia explicant. ET HOC EST NOMEN QUOD VOCABUNT EUM) Nempe populum. DOMINUS JUSTUS NOSTER) Melius: Dominus justitia nostra. I. e. Deus nobis bene fecit. Nam צדק He- bræis sæpe est beneficentia: neque aliter hic sumfit Chal- dæus. Quod hic de populo Israëlis, idem de civitate Hie- rosolymorum infra dicitur 33, 16. Omnia hæc de Pastoribus excitatis post Ba- bylonicam captivitatem intellecta vult, & de mul- tiplicatione populi post reditum. Sequutus Ju- dæos, qui de reductione ex captivitate Babylonica hæc interpretantur. Sunt qui eadem & de corpo- rali eductione, è Babylonica captivitate explicanda censeant, & de spirituali reductione ad Ecclesiam, adeoque Prophetam simul loqui putent de typo & antitypo. Sed geminum ejusmodi sensum simul locum habere non posse sæpius ostendimus; de so- la spirituali reductione sermonem esse, ea, quæ in contextu sequuntur, evidenter convincunt. Nam additur versu 4. Non formidabunt ultra & non pa- vebunt. Quæ de securitate sub præsidio Perfarum temere arripit Grotius. Removent enim omnem formidinem, omnem pavorem. At annon formida- runt Judæi hostes suos post reductionem, Sanabal- lat, Tobiam Ammonitam, Macedones, Romanos, alios? Ideo manifestum est, spiritualem felicitatem & remotionem omnis formidinis à potestate Sata- næ & peccati, quæ tranquillitas & salus fidelium propria est, designari. Efa. 11, 6. Luc. 1, 14. NUL- LUS QUÆRETUR EX NUMERO. Hæc non vitam diuturnam notant, uti pervertit Gro- tius, nam neque verba id ferunt, neque constat, vi- tam diuturniorem traxisse Judæos post reditum quam alias (de sensu Efa. 65, 20. in vindiciis istius loci actum) Sed negant ullam ex ovibus perituram, aut desideratum iri. Et quum Israëlitarum post reditum plurimi desiderati fuerint, nec nisi duas tantum tribus, nec eas integras reductas esse, quid certius, quã quod non de reditu corporali hæc ac- cipienda sint, sed de spirituali? Agit n. Propheta de Salvatione Iuda pariter, & Israelis ut è v. 6. constat. Quapropter de non perdendis electis sermo, quod sc. nemo eorum æternum periturus sit Joh. 10. v. 16. Ideo per Pastores merito hic intelligit Hieronymus Apostolos, qui reliquias gregis Domini Judæos è di- spersione reliquos congregârunt, ut nulla ovis de- ficiat aut desideretur in fidelium numero. Aliter hæc verba interpretatur B. Bugenhagius: Non QUÆRENDUM vel requirendum aliquem, id est, puniendum, cum mali visitabuntur, ut significetur omnes fore dilectos Dei filios in hoc regno, cui præfici- entur boni pastores. Idem B. Antecessor noster to- tum hoc vaticinium adversus corruptelas Judaicas, quas Grotius interpolavit solide tractavit, quem proinde hic audire juvat. ECCE EGO CON- GREGABO RELIQUIAS) Hæc intelligunt Ju- dæi de reductione ex captivitate Babylonica post se- ptuaginta annos, quasi Deus hic dicat, perditis per captivitatem Babylonicam Regibus, Principibus, Sacerdotibus, Prophetis & populo impio, rursum ex reliquiis congregabo mihi Ecclesiam in has terras, & tunc dabo eis bonos principes Serubabel, Sealthiel &c. bonos sacerdotes, Jesua sive JESUM &c. bo- nos Prophetas Zachariam, Haggæum, Malachiam &c. qui pascant reliquias populi mei, id est, guber- nent populum meum secundum legem & verbum Dei. Per me quidem ita licebit, ut ita exponant, sed hæc expositio non satisfacit promissioni Dei, quia hic promittit: Suscitabo super reliquias meas Pastores, qui pascant eas, ita ut non metuant ultra aut terreantur aut visitentur, dicit Dominus, qui mentiri non potest, qui hæc omnia faciet. Certe hæc non sunt impleta reductis post septuaginta annos ex ca- ptivitate Babylonica: Nam ut sibi metuerint & territæ sint illæ reliquiæ, cum rursum ædificarent il- las terras & civitatem Jerusalem & templum, etiam sub illis, quos dixi, pastoribus, id est, principibus, sacerdotibus & prophetis, notissimum est ex histo- ria Esdræ & Nehemiæ. Quam vero visitatæ sint illæ reliquiæ à Deo propter peccatum valde hor- rende, testatur historia libri Machabæorum, quan- do etiam cœperunt seduci à publica sinceri verbi Dei prædicatione, per impios sacerdotes, quibus omnia erant venalia, sacerdotium & omnia sacra, per scribas & Pharisæos, qui tempore Machabæo- rum cœperunt, per quorum traditiones obscurata est lex, ut vides Matth. 5. obscuratum est Evange- lium de semine promisso, ita ut scribæ & Pharisæi non potuerint respondere Christo interroganti, quomodo Davidi vocat in Spiritu Christum Domi- num suum, si Christus filius ejus est? Non agnosce- bant sua peccata ex lege sed somniabant se ex lege justos: Non sciebant semen promissum esse suam justitiam, si crederent in promissum semen, id est, se habere remissionem peccatorum per solum Chri- stum, secundum promissionem, sive secundum Ev- angelium. Semen mulieris conteret caput serpen- tis, in semine tuo, ô Abraham, benedicentur cun- ctæ cognationes terræ. Hæc est miseria miseria- rum, & valde dura & intolerabilis (nisi cæcitas ac cederet) visitatio populi, quando Deus sic sinit abi- re populum à fide verbi Dei, in tenebras horrendas doctrinarum dæmoniorum, quemadmodum Adam & Eva ceciderunt, quemadmodum nos sub papa cecidimus, de quo prædixit Paulus: Spiritus manife- sto dicit, quod in novissimis temporibus, id est, post Apostolica tempora, & post Apostolorum doctri- nam, deficient à fide, attendentes spiritibus erroris & doctrinis dæmoniorum, in hypocrisi, id est, sub specie cultus Dei, sub nomine Christi & fidei, loquentes mendacium &c. Domine Deus nimium horrende visitas peccata nostra, quando sic nos abjicis in er- rores à facie tua. De qua visitatione & plaga & spiri- tuali captivitate quã stultʉ mundus,qui seducitur& abducitur à Deo non videt,neque sentit,dicit Do- minus Esa, 52.
