Gratis venundati estis (in servitutem traditionum humanarum) ideo & absque pecunia redimemini. Quia hæc dicit Deus Dominus. Popu- lus meus primum descendit in Ægyptum, ut esset ibi peregrinus. Et Assur absque causa vim intulit illi. Verum quid mihi hic fit? dicit Dominus, populus meus gratis abducitur. Hæc est tertia captivitas, quæ fit gratis,id est, per rem & plagam, quæ neque videtur neque sentitur. Populus manet quietus in sua terra,& tamen invisibiliter & insensibiliter, hoc est,gratis, abducitur à Deo suo in errores ad Deos alienos per doctrinam scribarum & Phari- sæorum, ex quibus postea etiam venit secta Epicu- ræorum, qui Saducæos se vocabant,in quibus tem- pore Christi erant Hannas, Caiphas, Johannes, Alexander, magistratus templi, monstrosa capita illius populi,qui se jactitabat esse populumDei.De quibus addit Deus in Esaia: Dominatores ejus ululatus excitant (id est, sua doctrina & fictis cul- tibus faciunt malas conscientias coram Deo) & no- men meum jugiter quotidie blasphematur. In hac ca- ptivitate pessima etiam nos fuimus sub blasphemis Papistis.Sed audi liberationem per Christum:Pro- pterea, inquit, agnoscet populus meus nomen meum in tempore illo,quia ecce ego ipse loquar. Sit Christo liberatori gratia in æternum.Nam & de prædicato- ribus Evangelii sequitur: Quam jucundi sunt su- per montes pedes nunciorum &c. Quando ergo post captivitatem Babylonicam populus reductus ita metuerit,territus fuerit & visitatus judicio Dei bel- lis externis & erroribus internis,quomodo possunt hæc verba Jeremiæ sive Dei in Jeremia: Suscitabo super eas pastores,qui pascant eas, ita ut non metuant ultra,aut terreantur aut visitentur, intelligi de re- ductione illa corporali post septuaginta captivitatis annos? Adde quod metuerint & territi sint & visi- tati durissima visitatione secundũ corpus, quando subjugati sunt Romanis,& quando multis acceptis cladibus coacti sunt suscipere Herodem Regem alienigenam contra legem Deut. 17. Ergo hæc ver- ba in Jeremia nullo modo possunt intelligi de reductio- ne corporali ex captivitate Babylonica, nisi quod re- ductis post captivitatem talia præstaturus est Deus, in terra ipsorum incipiendo, videlicet tempore Christi incarnati. Nam his verbis promittit Deus se daturum eis pastores,id est, Prophetas & prædica- tores,de quibus hic agitur,qui pascant,id est,doce- ant populum prædicatione pœnitentiæ & remissio- nis peccatorum, ita ut oves ex illa pastura seu do- ctrina habeant pacem in æternum coram DEO, quod in solo Christo completum est, qui ascendens in altum, captivam duxit captivitatem, dedit dona hominibus,quosdam Apostolos, quosdam Prophetas, alios Evangelistas,alios pastores & Doctores ad con- summationem sanctorum in corpore Christi. Hi præ- dicaverunt remissionem peccatorum, & pacem æternam per Christum Rom. 5. Justificati ex fide pa- cem habemus erga Deum &c. Tunc multi Judæi manserunt in regno Persarum & Medorum,& Ba- bylonis, qui noluerunt reverti. Nam in Esdra scri- bitur illos reversos solum, quorum Deus tetigerat spiritum. Item multi dispergebantur in omnes fere nationes, qui certe non colligebantur rur- sum in caulas suas, id est, ut Judæi hic expo- nunt,in terram illam, patribus promissam, unde jecti erant per Babylonicam captivitatem; hoc vi- des Actor. 2. Ex omni natione Judæi, quæ sub cælo est. Hic autem Christus per prædicationem Evan- gelii(quemadmodum à resurrectione sua mandat: Ite in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ &c.) congregavit ut pastor bonus reliquias gregis sui, id est, quos Pater elegit & dile- xit in Christo ante mundi constitutionem. Ex o- mnibus, inquit, terris, quo ego ejeceram eas, videlicet propter peccatum ex Paradiso à facie mea. Et re- ducam eas in caulas suas, id est, ex regno peccati & mortis (nam ego conteram caput serpentis) in re- gnum cœlorum, unde ejeceram eas, per captivita- tem mortis, ut crescant in fide & cognitione Chri- sti, & multiplicentur per totum mundum in vitam æternam. Igitur hic est insignis locus de Christo & salute omnium populorum sive de Christi Ecclesia ex Judæis & gentibus congregata in unum regnum cœlorum, quod est Regnum Christi super terram usque ad consummationem seculi, in qua Ecclesia per Evangelii prædicatores est securitas & pax æ- terna. De quibus prædicatoribus sive pastoribus Esa. 52. sic dicitur. Quam speciosi pedes super mon- tes Evangelizantium bona, annunciantium pacem &c. De hac reductione & congregatione spiritua- li per Christum canimus ad Sanctum Spiritum: Qui per diversitatem linguarum cunctarum gentes in unitate fidei congregasti. Et Christus: Alias opes habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, illas oportet me adducere, & fiet unus pastor & unum ovile. Johan- nes Evangelista cap. 11. etiam sic dicit: Jesus erat moriturus pro populo, & non pro populo tantum, sed ut filios Dei, qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Dispersos dicit, qui variis sectis & idololatriis per totum mundum à Deo recesserant, imo à Deo pro- pter peccatum abjecti fuerant ad doctrinas dæ- moniorũ. Qua ratione ergo erant filii Dei? Præde- stinatione, electione, dilectione seu gratia Dei, qua elegit eos Deus & dilexit sive gratificavit eos in Christo ab æterno ante constitutionẽ mundi Eph. 1. Hi erãt nunc dispersi, i. e. adhuc pro temporis ratione impii, Rom. 5. &c. Mich. 2. promittit Deus hanc spiritualem reductionem ex Infernis ad Deum per solum Christum. Ego, inquit, te Jacob totum con- gregabo & reliquias Israël in unum adducam, Ego ut Pastor eos simul in unum ovile colligam, quasi gregem in suas caulas, ut strepens sonus ibi audiatur multi- tudinis hominum. Ascendet perruptor ante eos. I- psi perrumpent & per portam ingredientur & egre- dientur: Et Rex eorum præcedet ipsos & DOMI- NUS Dux ante ipsos. Quod dicit totum Jacob, hoc postea repetit Paulus Rom. 11. his verbis: Nolo vos fratres ignorare mysterium hoc, quod excæ- catio Israëli ex parte accidit, donec plenitudo gen- tium intraret, & sic totus Israël salvus esset. Non e- nim omnes, qui sunt ex carne Abrahæ, sunt filii A- brahæ, sed omnes, qui credunt ut Abraham, sive Iu- dæi sive gentes, sunt filii Abrahæ Rom. 4. Ezech. 34. Eadem reductio promittitur pèr Christum unicum Pastorem. Sic dicit Dominus: Et faciam cum eis fœdus, & exterminabo omnes malas bestias, ut oves secure habitent in deserto & dormiant in silvis; lege reliqua. Et c. 37. Sic dicit Dominus. Ecce ego ad- ducam filios Israël ex gentibus quo abierunt: Et con- gregabo eos undequaq; & reducam eos in terram su- am & faciam ex eis unicum populum, in terra super montes Israël, & omnes simul unicum habebunt Re- gem (Davidem, id est, Christum ex semine Davi- dis) Nec dividentur amplius in duos populos aut duo Regna. Nec polluent sese suis idolis & abominatio- nibus, & multiplicibus peccatis. Ex omnibus locis e- ruam eos, in quibus peccaverunt, & mundabo eos: Et erunt populus meus & ego ero Deus eorum & servus meus David erit Rex eorum & omnium eorum unicus pastor. Et ambulabunt in juribus meis, servabunt mea præcepta & præstabunt, habitabuntq; super terram, quam dedi servo meo Jacob, in qua habitaverunt patres vestri, ipsi & filii eorum & filii filiorum habitabunt in ea in æternum. Et servus meus David in æternum erit Princeps eorum. Et faciam cum eis fœdus pacis, id quod erit fœdus æternum cum eis, & conservabo & multiplicabo eos, & Sanctuarium meum erit inter eos in æternum. Et habitabo inter eos, erog; Deus eorum & ipsi populus meus, ut & gentes cognoscant, quod ego sum Dominus, qui sanctificat Israëlem. Meum enim Sanctuarium erit inter eos in æternum. Hæc permittimus Judæis, ut exponant, se reducendos ex captivitate Babylonica post septuaginta annos, & Deum benefacturum eis in terra patrum ipsorum; sed quod Deus tunc hanc promissionem implevit, quæ in Prophetis tam claris verbis exprimitur, id est, quod Deus post septuaginta annos totum Jacob sive Israelem ex universis terris collegerit, & reduxerit in terram Canaan, quemque ad hæreditatem suam, unde ejecti erant, & ex eis constituerit Regnum æternum sub uno pastore & Rege justitiæ Davide, in quo Regno sit justitia & pax æterna, quemadmodum in Prophetis, ut vides, Deus promittit, hoc Judæi non possunt ostendere, nisi in Christo Jesu filio Dei Domino nostro, ut diximus, qui reduxit totam Israëlem, id est, omnes credentes, & credituros Judæos & gentes ex captivitate peccati & mortis, ex Regno Satanæ, ad Deum, ad Regnum cælorum, unde abjecti eramus propter peccatum, quemadmodum Christus dicit, Ego sum via, veritas & vita, nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Nemo ascendit in cælum, nisi qui venit de cælo, filius hominis, qui in cælo est. Itaque reductis corporaliter post septuaginta captivitatis annos, hic promittitur spiritualis reductio per Christum, qui venit, ut sacerdos æternus ad Templum sanctum suum, Malach. 3. Hagg. 2. in civitatem Regiam ut Rex æternus, ut Zacharias prædixerat: Dicite filiæ Zion: Ecce Rex tuus venit tibi &c. & incepit ibi Regnum sacerdotale, & sacerdotium regale in spiritu æternum, quod est Regnum cælorum, Regnum Dei, Regnum Christi, populus sanctus, justus, in pace coram Dei æterna. Hoc Regnum ibi cœptum & aspersum sanguine agni immaculati resurgens Christus à mortuis dilatavit per bonos pastores per totum mundum, quemadmodum ipse à resurrectione: Oportuit Christum pati & resurgere à mortuis, & prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes, incipiendo à Jerosolyma. Ef. 2. De Zion exibit Lex & verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Ps. 110. Sceptrum regni tui emittet Dominus ex Zion. Eadem dicuntur Michæ 4. &c. Hunc Christum, justitiam & vitam nostram Judæi negaverunt, & ideo ablatum est ab eis Regnum Dei & datum est Genti facienti fructus ejus. Vastati sunt & abjecti non solum à terra sua, sed etiam à Deo, ut nunc non sint populus Dei, sed blasphemia Dei, tantum apest, ut Regnum æternæ pacis, quod hic promittitur, consecuti sint post septuaginta annos in terra Canaan. Blasphemi Judæi & Rabini eorum, postquam negaverunt Christum, student mira insania obscurare & depravare has & alias promissiones de Christo. Nec miramur, quia excæcati abjectique sunt à Deo & traditi in reprobum sensum. Miramur vero de nostris, qui non existimant se commode interpretari Prophetas, nisi sequantur Rabinorum blasphemas depravationes. NON METUENT ULTRA aut terrebitur AUT VISITABUNTUR; Quod in terreno aliquo regno, ita pergit Bugenhagius, impletum, ut Judæi ostendere non possunt, ita etiam fieri ne- quit,in Christi autem regno impletur, ubi licet ad- huc trepidatio sit propter carnem & sanguinem Christianorum verorum, quia adhuc reliquum est peccatum in carne, tamen summa securitas & pax æterna est in spiritu per fidem & maxima doctrinæ certitudo per Evangelium bonorum pastorum, ut jam non metuas propter incertitudinem,quemad- modum sub Doctrinis Dæmoniorum, vel etiam quemadmodum sub servitute legis, ubi Pharisæi & Papistæ nostri gratiam Dei per solum Christum, ut non noverunt, ita non prædicarunt. Ibi erat pa- vor & formido conscientiarum, ignorabatur qui placeremus Deo, & quid placeret Deo. De quo Christus dicit Joh. 6. Hoc est opus Dei, ut credatis in eum,quem ille misit, judicabatur Deus non esse Pater sed Judex &c. De hac securitate & pace dicit etiam Esaias c. 32. Et erit opus justitiæ pax & cultus justitiæ silentium & securitas usq́; in sempiternum: Et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis & in taberna- culis fiduciæ & in requie opulenta &c. Et cap. 9. Multiplicabitur ejus Imperium & pacis non erit fi- nis, super solium David, & super Regnum ejus, ut confirmet & corroboret illud in judicio & justitia à modo & usque in sempiternum. Et ex Ezechiele legisti: Et faciam cum eis pactum pacis &c. Et Za- charias pater Johannis plenus Spiritu Sancto canit: Ut sine timore,de manu inimicorum nostrorum libe- rati serviamus illi in sanctitate & Justitia coram ipso omnibus diebus nostris. Attende vero hic dili- genter, quod dicit; Et suscitabo super eas Pastores qui pascant eas &c. Quemadmodum & Christus admonet: Rogate Dominum messis, ut mittat ope- rarios in messem suam. Nam per hoc Propheta dicit Christum regnaturum super terram & pacem æternam in suo Regno daturum per prædicatio- nem Evangelii, ut hic in fide pacem habeamus,& videamus per speculum in ænigmate,usque ad ex- tremum diem. Christus regnat in mundo per ver- bum suum,id est, Evangelium prædicatum, ex quo homines accipiuntSpiritumSanctum,ut illuminen- tur & credere possunt in JESUM CHRISTUM filium DEI & per Christum fide susceptum fieri fi- lii DEI & Regnum pacis æternæ. Tale re- gnum CHRISTI promiserunt Prophetæ. Et Moses ipse prædicit Deut. 18. Prophetam susci- tabit tibi Dominus Deus tuus de medio fratrum tuo- rum, sicut me illum audies. Ego enim ponam verba mea in os ejus & loquetur ea in nomine meo: Qui autem Prophetam illum non audierit, ego ultor exi- stam dicit Dominus. Id quod Baptista sic dicit Joh. 3. Qui non credit in filium, ira Dei manet super ipsum. Hoc est quod Christus interrogantibus Joh. 8. tu quis es? respondet: Ego quæ audivi à Patre, loquor in mundo, id est, Deus posuit sua verba in os meum,ut Moses prædixit: Id quod & Johan. 14. sic dicit: Sermo quem audistis,non est meus, sed e- jus qui misit me Patris. Et alibi: A me ipso non lo- quor &c. Regnum Christi super terram esse Regnum verbi & fidei non credunt Judæi, non credunt hodie Papistæ Evangelii persecu- tores & hostes CHRISTI, & tamen tale Deus hic promittit. Et suscitabo super eas pastores, qui ita pascant reliquias populi Dei ex omnibus terris ad Regem Christum congregatas, ut fiant Regnum æternæ securitatis & pacis. Sit Christo gratia in æ- ternum. Hæc Dn. Bugenhagius ὁ μακαρίτης.

Neque vero, Germen justum, quod hic excitan- dum promittitur, de alio, quam soloMessia intelligi potest. Non de Zorobabele, sive solus hic in- telligatur,seu Christus tanquam antitypus,sub ipso simul designatus dicatur. Nam nullatenus in Zo- robabelem congruunt prædicata, sed uni Christo propria sunt, quæ de hoc Davidis germine efferūtur. Primum enim hoc germen justum absolute dicitur. Quod epitheton nulli alii ἁπλῶς convenit, nisi uni Christo. Non enim est homo, qui non peccet. 1. Reg. 8, 46. Non est qui bonum faciat, non est usque ad u- num Ps. 14, 3. Et quomodo Zorobabelem simplici- ter & absolute germen justum præ aliis diceret Pro- pheta, quum & ipse homo peccatis obnoxius fue- rit, nec ab omni injustitia plane alienus? Quomodo in iniquitate conceptus GERMEN IUSTUM dici po- test, quo nomine justitia originalis imprimis cōpre- henditur, quod progerminet non in injustitia & iniquitate, sed ceu justum & sanctum germen, uti de Christo habetur Luc. 1, 35. Sanctum quod ex te na- scetur. Locum Zach. 6, 12. perperam ad Zorobabe- lem pertrahi in annotatis ad eundem docebimus. Deinde cum Davidi excitandum germen dicitur, ad promissiones Davidi factas respectus habetur, & ad fidelia David. 2. Sam. 7, 14. Esa. 55, 3. Ideoque non de Zorobabele, sed de Christo hæc intelligere opor- tet. Tertio nomen germinis Christo in promissio- nibus appropriatum, hæc de Christo accipienda es- se confirmat: quod loca parallela evidenter statu- minant Es. 4, 1. c. 11, 1. c. 53, 2. Zach. 3, 8. c. 6, 12. Luc. 1, 7. 8. Quarto axioma Regium Zorobabeli non conve- nit, qui regia dignitate ac Majestate non claruit. At hic de illo germine Davidis sermo est, quod Rex futurum erat. Ideoque non de Zorobabele, sed de Christo Rege unice sermo est. Qui à Regia Maje- state & throno ac sceptro Regio passim describitur Ps. 2. 45. 72. 60. Esa, 9. Zach. 9. Luc. 1. &c. Dilutum est, quod ait Grotius, Zorobabelem à suis pro Rege cultum fuisse, quantum res tulerit. Nam neque res ferebat, neque historiæ id consonat. Etsi vero vera progenies Davidis fuerit, non ideo pro Rege co- lendus erat. Non omnes Rege fuere, aut pro Re- gibus culti sunt, qui ortum traxere è Davide. Apud Zachariam c. 9, 9. Regem appellari, falsum est. Nam ibi non Zorobabelem, sed Christum sisti, è Matth. 21. novimus. Neque ideo Rex fuit, quod figuram Christi gesserit, nam & Prophetæ & Duces figuram ejus gesserunt. Quinto Rex justitiam & judicium administraturus nullus alius est, quam Messias, cu- jus Regnum à justitia & judicio passim celebratur Esa. 9. c. 11. quum alia terrena regna nulla absolute hanc laudem mereantur. Nullum enim est in mun- do, in quo non aliquid iniquitatis aut injustitiæ pro- germinet. Sexto cum erecturus dicitur justitiam & judicium IN TERRA, Regnum catholicum & œcumenicum designatur, quod se per universam terram diffundat, non vero ad certum locū alliga- tum sit. Quod solius Christi est, Regis Regum, & Domini Dominantium. Septimo promittitur sub hoc Rege Judæ salus & Israeli secura habitatio. At sub Zorobabel Judam & Israëlem vel omnes duo- decim tribus salutem & securitatem obtinuisse, fal- sum est. Ideoque ἐξ ἀνάγκης de Christi Regno, sub quo omnibus fidelibus & subditis spiritualibus ex Juda & Israele, h. e. Ecclesiæ universæ salus & se- curitas spiritualis obtingit, Rom. 5, 1. seqq. c. 14, 17. Octavo nomen, quod huic Regi tribuitur, uni Mes- siæ proprium est, quia hoc est nomen, quo vocabit eū unusquisque: Iehovah justitia nostra. Num Zoroba- beli, num ulli alii ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ id nominis con- venit? Messias vero & Jehovah est Deus super omnia benedictus in secula Rom. 9, 5. & justitia nostra, quia factus est nobis à Deo Patre justitia 1. Cor. 1, 29. & in ipso justitia nostra est. Esa. 45, 24. Pessima autem στρεβλότης est, cum Grotius ad populum hoc nomen pertrahit, idque ita pervertit: Deus nobis benefe- cit. Non populus sed germen Davidi excitan- dum hic materia substrata est Prophetiæ. De hujus ergo, non illius nomine agendum erat. Sci- licet is cujus ortus & prosapia, cujus regnum & vir- tutes in administrando regimine, cujus subditi & regnum feliciter describuntur, nomine certo de- scribendus, insigniendus & celebrandus erat; non ve ro populus Israël. Degermine justo dicetur, quod sit ipse Jehovab justitia nostra, utpote quod ut ju- stum per se describitur, & judicium ac justitiam in terra facturum dicitur. Non ergo hoc ad populum trahi potest. Et quis est populus ille, qui ita vocan- dus erat: Nomen populi non præcessit; Judæ & Israelis mentio facta est; ad quemnam vero id no- minis pertrahetur? Num ad Judam an vero ad Israë- lem? Denique si populo id nomen tribuendum ab aliis, quomodo alii vocabunt populum Jehovah ju- stitia nostra? Num aliis justitia est populus Judai- cus? Glossæ Grotii, si locus esse deberet, ita verba fuissent formanda: Et hoc est nomen, quo vocabunt eum (populum) Jehovah Justitia IPSORUM, non vero Jehovah Justitia NOSTRA, h. e. juxta Gro- tium Jehovah ipsis benefaciet. Sed per JUSTITIAM hic beneficentiam intelligi, & beneficentiam populo Judaico exhibitam ab aliis celebratum iri, quo ob- secro argumento docebitur? Glossæ hæ mere ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sapiunt, ac plane contortæ sunt. Ne- que ullatenus eas juvat locus parallelus c. 33, 15. ibi enim non Hierosolyma, sed Messias hoc nomine insignitur. Postremo, ut de autoritate veterum etiam aliquid dicamus, non erat posthabenda Pa- trum explicatio, qui unanimiter de Christo oracu- lum accepere, maxime quia constanti Ecclesiæ sen- su & consensu firmum fuit, de Christo unice intelli- gendum esse. Imo si Christianis aures præbere re- nuit Grotius, Judæos saltim vetustiores audire de- bebat, qui de Messia locũ accipiendun esse, agno- vere. Sic enim habetur in Bereschith Rabba super Genes. 25, 6. Cum magnificatus est Salomo in regno tuo, dixerunt forte ipse est Messias, statimẁ venerunt ad eum, sicut dictum est (1. Reg. 10, 1. Et regina Sa- ba audita fama Salomonis ad nomen Domini veeit ad eum. Quid est dictum in nomen Domini? Pro- phetæ fecerunt iis, qui prophetabant in nomine Domi- ni Dei sui verba, quæ fuerant eis tradita, & quæ ve- nerunt successive ad manum eorum ex Abraham, si- cut dictum est (Es. 60, 6.) Multitudo Camelorum operient te: Dromedarii de Midin & Epha, omnes ipsi de Saba venient, aurum & thus deferent: Et laudes Domini Dei nunciabunt. Hic est Rex Mes- sias, sicut dictum est (Jer. 23, 6.) Et hoc est nomen, quo vocabunt cum, Dominus justitia nostra. Et hic dicit Esaias (c. 60, 2.) Super te orietur Deus, & glo- ria ejus super te apparebit, & ibunt ad lumen tuum, & Reges ad splendorem ortus tui. In Echa Rabba- thi super illud (Thren. 1, 16.) Quia elongatus est à me consolator, reducens animam meam, hæc legun- tur: Quid est nomen Regis Messiæ? Dixit R. Abba יהוה Dominus est nomen ejus, quo vocabunt ipsum Dominus justitia nostra. R. Josua Ben Levi dixit: Germen est nomẽ ejus, sicut dictum est (Zach. 6, 12.) Ecce, vir Germen nomen ejus. In Midrasch Til- lim ad Ps. 22. Domine in virtute tua lætabitur Rex. Et quod est nomen ejus? Iehovah sicut dictum est Ex. 15, 2. Et de Rege Messia scriptum est (Ier. 23, 6. Et hoc nomen ejus. Similiter Talmudis explicatio ha- bet, in qua in libro Bava Bathra in distinctione Hammocher, & Hassephinah hæc reperies: Dixit R. Ionathan: Tres sunt vocati nomine Dei sancti be- nedicti, & sunt hi, justi, Messias, & Jerusalem. Mes- sias sicut scriptum est, (Ier. 23, 6.) Et hoc est nomen ejus &c. R. Saadia Gaon ad Dan. 7, 13. Ecce, cum nubibus cæli tanquam Filius hominis; Hic est, in- quit, Messias IUSTITIA NOSTRA. Quid quod in- Rabbini, ut apud Raimundum Martini in pugione Fidei part. 2. c. 11. videre est, assumant hoc tanquam indubitatum & manifestum, quod haec de Messia lo- quantur, idque urgeant adversus Christianos, hoc modo; cum Judaei salvari debuerint in diebus Mes- siae, ut hoc in loco MANIFESTE habetur ex verbis Jeremiae, & nunquam eis ante, vel post talis captivi- tas tot, & tam gravia mala evenerunt, ut in diebus Jesu Christi, nec ita fuerint destructi, dissipati, atque dispersi, nullatenus Jesus Christus esse poterit Messias. In Sephir Ikkarim libr. 2. cap. 28. ita dicitur: vocat Scriptura Messiam Deum justitiam nostram (Jer. 23, 6.) Quia est Mediator Dei, per quem justitiam a Deo consequimur. Neque aliter Chaldaeus, ad quem frustra provocat Grotius. Ita enim reddidit: Ecce, dies venient &c. & erigam Davidi MESSIAM justum &c. & istud est nomen ejus, quod ipsi dicent ei &c. Nomen ergo Messiae est, quod hic exponi- tur, non nomen populi, juxta Chaldaeum Interpre- tem pariter & Rabinos vetustiores: etsi apud Chal- daeum populus hoc nomen in usum suum conver- tat; cum hoc modo reddatur: ipsi dicent, vel voca- bunt eum: Fiat nobis justificatio coram Deo ob reve- rentiam ejus. Nam ideo Messias est justitia nostra, quod nos ob ipsum & in ipso justificamur cora Deo.

Atq; haec de oraculo insigni Prophetae nostri, cujus συνέχειαν cum superioribus tradidit Hierony- mus, simulque argumenta pleraq; a nobis adducta breviter complexus est, unde verba ejus subjici- mus: Abjectis ergo Pastoribus synagogae, scribis vi- delicet & Pharisaeis, & salvatis reliquiis ex Israel, Apostolisque Evangelii in locum priorum principum constitutis: inducitur Pastor pastorum, & Princeps principum, & Rex Regum, & Dominus Dominan- tium, Christus videlicet Salvator noster, qui proprie est germen justum sive oriens justus, de quo legimus: Orietur in diebus ejus justitia. Et in alio loco: Ec- ce, vir oriens nomen ejus, & subter eum orietur, & aedificabit templum Domino; ut quomodo in Esaia Emmanuel appellatur, h. e. nobiscum Deus, sic in Hieremia nomen accipiat, justitia nostra. Unde & Apostolus loquitur: Qui factus est nobis a Deo Ju- stitia, & sanctificatio, & redemptio. Cui contrarius anti-Christus & ejus habitator diabolus, in Zacha- ria stultus Pastor dicitur. Et faciet, inquit, judi- cium & justitiam in terra. Non enim Pater judicat quenquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio. In diebus illis & duae & decem tribus: Juda & Israel pariter salvabuntur. Et de duabus virgis, juxta Ezechiel, una virga fiet: Nomenq; ejus, si juxta LXX. voca- verit eum Dominus, appellabitur Josedech, i. e. Do- minus Justus, Sic secundum Hebraicum, qui dixe- runt, nomen ejus vocabunt: dicetur: Dominus ju- stitia nostra. Hoc enim significatur יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ : pro quo Symmachus vertit, Domine justifica nos.

## 23:7
Vers. 7. THEREFORE] Even here לָכֵן, you might better translate it 'furthermore'. THEY SHALL NO MORE SAY: THE LORD LIVES, WHO BROUGHT UP THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT] See above 16, 14. The Prophet often said the same things, so that the words might stick more firmly in their minds.

There is no need for לָכֵן to be translated otherwise. For these things cohere conveniently with the preceding, and treat of the same benefit: namely, not of a corporal, but of a spiritual restoration. Nor does the parallel passage, c. 16, 14, treat of any other restoration, where the promise concerning the fishers and hunters, the Apostles, is subjoined, as was said in its explanation: For the sense concerning spiritual restoration is demanded not only by the antecedents in this text, which treat of the kingdom of the Messiah, and of spiritual Israel and Judah, that is, the Church of Christ, to be gathered not only from the Jews or Israelites, but also from the Gentiles which are proclaimed. For this name is proper to the universal Church of the New Testament, in prophetic phraseology, because under the Old Testament the church was contained within the Jewish and Israelitic people, and the nations were added to Israel, and were gathered to the πολιτείαν τῶ Ἰσραὴλ, Eph. 2, 12. But the formula of the oath or confession, of which mention is made here, also requires this sense, inasmuch as it will be solemn in that Judah and Israel, who shall dwell confidently under the righteous Branch, and shall be saved through it. Under the name of the oath, the entire worship of religion and confession is comprehended. It stands thus: The Lord lives, who brought up and brought the seed of the house of Israel from the land of the North, and from ALL LANDS, to which I had cast them there, and they shall dwell in their own land! Israelites according to the flesh were never brought back to Palestine from ALL LANDS to which they were cast, nor will they ever be brought back, or form a polity in it. Therefore, these things cannot be understood of the Israelites according to the flesh, but of those who are to acknowledge and celebrate the Messiah with true faith, Jehovah our Righteousness, and are to obtain salvation through the Messiah, and are to dwell confidently under His Kingdom, are proclaimed, i.e., of all true believers. Although, therefore, an allusion is made to the reduction from the land of the North, promised to others, in a manner solemn to the Prophets, who love to express the spiritual things of the New Testament in the words of the Old Testament, yet they must necessarily be accepted not of a bodily, but of a spiritual reduction, and explained mystically, so that the land of the North, and all the lands to which they had been cast, may indeed look to Chaldea and other lands into which the people had been dispersed on account of sin, and to the captivity and exile of the same, but here is designated the spiritual dispersion and casting away by God, and exile from the face of the Lord, and captivity under sin and the Devil. Because when we are converted to God, we are freed from that exile, from that casting away and dispersion, from that captivity and misery, so that, translated into the kingdom of the Lord, we may enjoy true liberty, security, and tranquility. As Canaan is accustomed to denote the Church, to which we are led: so the constitution in the land of the North and the other lands of exile denotes the state in which we are before conversion; and thus it is signified that we are freed from the captivity of sin and Satan, and are led to the Church, and gathered by the Lord, who is our righteousness, our King, and who sets up righteousness and judgment in the earth. Which sense parallel passages, Ps. 68, 7. Luke 1, 29. Col. 1, 14. confirm, and the pious Ancients support: especially Jerome: This is the sense, that the people of God are by no means delivered from Egypt through Moses, but through Jesus Christ, from the whole world, into which they had been dispersed. Which is in part being completed now in the world, and will be completed in its entirety when they shall come from the East and West, North and South, and shall recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: So that after the fullness of the nations has entered in, then all Israel may be saved. But the ancient Jews also acknowledged that these things look to and designate the reduction to be performed through the Messiah, which is the substance of that exodus from Egypt, as the substance of a type is the Antitype, as is held in the Babylonian Book Berochoth in the distinction Maimathai Korin, expounded by Raimundo Martini part 3. Pug. Fid. dist. 3. cap. 11 p. 610. To which contributes that of the Author of Neve Schalom. l. 10 cap. ult. The exodus from Egypt is an accessory to the advent of the Messiah: because, indeed, the exodus from Egypt is the material cause: but the advent of the Messiah is the final cause, establishing for us an immutable end.

Latin:

Vers. 7. PROPTER HOC] Etiam hic לָכֵן, melius vertas praeterea. NON DICENT ULTRA: VIVIT DOMINUS, QUI EDUXIT FILIOS ISRAEL DE TERRA AEGT- PTI] Vide supra 16, 14. Saepe eadem dixit Propheta, quo magis dicta haererent animis.

Non opus est, ut לָכֵן aliter vertatur. Nam com- mode haec cohaerent antecedentibus, & de eodem beneficio agunt: nempe non de corporali, sed de spirituali reductione. Neq; de alia reductione locus parallelus agit, c. 16, 14. ubi subjungitur promissio de piscatoribus & venatoribus Apostolis, ut in ejus explicatione dictum: Nam sensum de spirituali re- ductione non tantum antecedentia in hoc textu po- stulant, quae de Messiae regno, deque Israele & Juda spirituali, hoc est, Ecclesia Christi, non e Judaeis aut Israelitis tantum, sed etiam e gentibus colligenda prædicantur. Hoc enim nomen Ecelesiae universæ N. T. proprium est, phrasiologia prophetica, quia sub V. T. ecclesia intra populum Judaicum & Israe- liticum continebatur, & gentes adscitæ sunt Israeli, collectæq; sunt ad πολιτείαν τῶ Ἰσραὴλ, Eph. 2, 12. Sed requirit etiam hunc sensum formula juramenti vel confessionis, cujus hic fit mentio, utpote, quæ in Juda & Israële illo solemnis erit, qui sub germine justo habitaturus est confidenter, & per illud salva- bitur. Sub juramenti nomine universus cultus reli- gionis & confessionis comprehenditur. Ità autem habet: Vivit Dominus, qui eduxit & adduxit semen domus Israel de terra Aquilonis, & de CUNCTIS TERRIS, ad quas ejeceram eos illuc, & habitabunt in terra sua! Israëlitæ secundum carnem de CUN- CTIS TERRIS, ad quas ejecti sunt, nunquam re- ducti in Palæstinam sunt, nunquam reducentur, aut politiam in ea formabunt. Non ergo de Israelitis secundum carnem hæc intelligi possunt, sed de illis, qui Messiam vera fide agnituri & celebraturi sint, Jehovah Justitia nostra, & per Messiam salutem consecuturi, ac sub Regno ejus confidenter habita- turi, prædicuntur, h. e. de omnibus veris fidelibus. Etsi ergo allusio fiat ad reductionem de terra Aqui- lonis, aliis promissam, more Prophetis solemni, qui amant res spirituales N. Test. verbis V. Testamenti exprimere, tamen non de corporali, sed spirituali reductione ita necessario accipienda sunt, & mysti- ce explicanda, ut terra Aquilonis, & cunctæ terræ, ad quas ejecti erant, respiciant quidem Chaldæam & alias terras, in quas ob peccatum populus dispersus erat, ac captivitatem & exilium ejusdem, sed desi- gnetur hic spiritualis dispersio & projectio à Deo, atq; exilium à facie Domini, ac captivitas sub peccato, & Diabolo. Quia cum convertimur ad Deum, ab illo exilio, ab ista projectione, ac dispersione, ab ista captivitate & miseria liberamur, ut in regnum Do- mini translati vera libertate, securitate & tranquil- litate fruamur. Ut Canaan notare solet Ecclesiam, ad quam perducimur: Ita constitutio in terra Aqui- lonis & terris exilii cæteris notat statum, in quo ver- samur ante conversionem; adeoq; id significatur, nos à captivitate peccati & Satanæ liberari, & ad Ec- clesiam perduci, atq; colligi per Dominum, qui est ju- stitia nostra, Rex noster, & in terra justitiam & ju- dicium erigit. Quem sensum parallela loca, Ps. 68, 7. Luc. 1, 29. Col. 1, 14. confirmant, piique Veteres ad- struunt: imprimis Hieronymus: Hic est sensus, quod nequaquam per Mosen populus Dei de Ægypto liberetur, sed per Jesum Christum, de omni orbe terra- rum, in quem dispersus fuerat. Quod ex parte & nunc completur in mundo, & ex toto complebitur, quando de Oriente & Occidente, Septentrione & Meridie venient & discumbent cum Abraham, Isaac & Ja- cob: Ut postquam subintraverit plenitudo gentium, tunc omnis Israel salvus fiat. Sed & Judæi prisci a- gnoverunt hæc respicere ac designare reductionem per Messiam præstandum, quæ sit substantia istius e- gressus ex Ægypto, ut typi substantia est Antitypus quemadmodum habetur in Libro Berochoth Baby- lonico in distinctione Maimathai Korin, exponente Raimundo Martini part. 3. Pug. Fid. dist. 3. cap. 11 p. 610. Quo facit illud Auctoris Neve Schalom. l. 10 cap. ult. Exitus ex Ægypto est accessorium adventui Messiæ: quia nimirum exitus ex Ægypto est causa materialis: adventus vero Messiæ est causa finalis constituens nobis finem immutabilem.

## 23:9
Vers. 9. TO THE PROPHETS, MY HEART IS BROKEN WITHIN ME] These cohere better in the Chaldean: Because of the Prophets my heart is broken within me. He calls them prophets, just as before he called them shepherds, who wished to be believed as such: κατὰ δόξαν. He says in these and the following words that he wonders at the impudence of those who would sell themselves under a name not pertaining to them, only to stroke the people, and by nourishing vices to nourish themselves, than which nothing is more wicked.

I HAVE BECOME LIKE A DRUNKEN MAN AND LIKE A MAN OVERCOME WITH WINE, BECAUSE OF THE LORD, AND BECAUSE OF THE WORDS OF HIS HOLINESS] I am clearly stupefied considering the wrath of God, and those things which God most justly threatens them. Vers. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 9. AD PROPHETAS, CONTRITUM EST COR MEUM IN MEDIO MEI] Melius hæc cohærent apud Chaldæum: Propter Prophetas frangitur intra me cor meum. Prophetas autem vocat, sicut antea pastores, qui tales credi volebant: κατὰ δόξαν. Dicit his & sequentibus verbis se mirari illorum impudentiam, qui se venditarent nomi- ad se nihil pertinente, tantum ut populo palpum obtrude- rent, ac vitia nutriendo se nutrirent, quo nihil est sceleratius.

FACTUS SUM QUASI VIR EBRIUS ET QUA- SI MADIDUS A VINO, A FACIE DOMINI, ET A FACIE VERBORUM SANCTORUM EJUS] Plane obstupefio considerans iram Dei, & illa, quæ Deus eis ju- stissime minatur. Vers. 10.

## 23:10
FOR THE LAND IS FILLED WITH ADULTERERS] While those who falsely call themselves prophets connive at vices, and because of the land and the temple of the Lord, promise all prosperous things to those living in such a way, the morals of all are depraved.

BECAUSE OF THE CURSE THE LAND HAS MOURNED, THE PASTURES OF THE DESERT ARE DRIED UP] That is, on account of the oaths (falsely, to wit) the land will be in mourning, all the fields will be without fruit.

THEIR COURSE HAS BECOME EVIL] They will go to the dogs.

AND THEIR STRENGTH IS NOT RIGHT] Not straight. They use the strength they have badly; therefore those strengths will be taken away from them. Vers. 11.

FOR PROPHET AND PRIEST ARE POLLUTED] They have acted impiously. For that is what חנפו signifies.

Latin:

QUIA ADULTERIS REPLETA EST TERRA] Dum illi, qui se Prophetas falso dicunt, ad vitia connivent, & propter terram ac templum Domini, ita viventibus, o- mnia pollicentur prospera, depravantur omnium mores.

A FACIE MALEDICTIONIS LUXIT TERRA, AREFACTA SUNT ARVA DESERTI] Id est, ob juramenta (falsa scil.) terra erit in luctum, campi omnes erunt sine fruge.

FACTUS EST CURSUS EORUM MALUS ] Ibunt εἰς κόρακας.

ET FORTITUDO EORUM DISSIMILIS ] Non recta. Viribus, quas habent male utuntur; ideo eis eripien- tur illæ vires. Vers. 11.

PROPheta NAMQUE ET SACERDOS POL- LUTI SUNT] Impie egerunt. Id enim significat חנפו

## 23:11
AND IN MY HOUSE I HAVE FOUND THEIR EVIL] In the Temple itself they have committed idolatry, 2 Kings 21, 5. above 11, 15. and Ezek. 8, 3. and following.

Latin:

ET IN DOMO MEA INVENI MALUM EO- RUM ] In ipso Templo idololatriam commiserunt, 2. Reg. 21, 5. supra 11, 15. & Ezech. 8, 3. & sequentibus.

## 23:12
Vers. 12. THEREFORE THEIR WAY SHALL BE AS SLIPPERY IN THE DARK: FOR THEY SHALL BE DRIVEN, AND FALL THEREIN] He who walks at night on a slippery path cannot but stumble often, and at last fall. Thus those false prophets will experience to their own harm how falsely they have predicted.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ICCIRCO VIA EORUM ERIT QUASI LUBRICUM IN TENEBRIS : IMPELLENTUR E- NIM, ET CORRUENT IN EA ] Qui nocte in via lu- brica ambulat, fieri, non potest, quin sæpe cespitet, tan- dem & cadat. Sic illi Pseudoprophetæ experientur suo ma- lo, quam falsa prædixerint.

## 23:13
Vers. AND IN THE PROPHETS OF SAMARIA I HAVE SEEN FOLLY] The ו has many uses in the Hebrew language. Here it signifies 'indeed'. For the sense is: in the prophets of Samaria indeed I discovered folly: for prophesying in the name of Baal they deceived the people of Israel. But in those Jerusalemite prophets I discovered horrible things: that is, having much more malice. Vers. 14.

Latin:

Vers. ET IN PROPHETIS SAMARIÆ VIDI FA- TUITATEM] ו multos usus habet in lingua Hebræa. Hic valet quidem. Sensus enim est : in Prophetis quidem Sama- riæ stultitiam deprehendi : nam vaticinantes nomine Baalis deceperunt populum Israel. At in prophetis illis Hieroso- lymitanis deprehendi res horrendas : id est, multo plus ha- bentes malitiæ. Vers. 14.

## 23:14
I HAVE SEEN THE LIKENESS OF THOSE COMMITTING ADULTERY, AND THE WAY OF A LIE] Better: I have seen the horrible things of men committing adultery (with the truth) and walking in a lie. They are so much the worse, because they foster vices not in the name of Baal, but in my name, which are most contrary to my will.

AND THEY HAVE STRENGTHENED THE HANDS OF THE WICKED, THAT EVERY ONE MIGHT NOT TURN FROM HIS MALICE] They flattered vices, promising all things prosperous, on account of the Temple, the house of David, the priesthood, and the rites instituted by God: and in that way they hindered the conversion of many, than which kind of men there is none more destructive. See 2 Tim. 3, 6.

THEY ARE ALL BECOME UNTO ME AS SODOM, AND THE INHABITANTS THEREOF AS GOMORRAH] I do not value them more than the citizens of Sodom and Gomorrah, men who are not evil by some error, but by design.

Latin:

VIDI SIMILITUDINEM ADULTERANTIUM, ET ITER MENDACII] Melius : Vidi horrenda hominum adulterantium (veritatem ) & ambulantium in mendacio. Tanto pejores sunt, quod non in Baalis, sed in meo nomine fovent vitia, meæ voluntati vel maxime adversantia.

ET CONFORTAVERUNT MANUS PESSIMO- RUM, UT NON CONVERTERETUR UNUSQUIS- QUE A MALITIA SUA] Blanditi sunt vitiis, omnia pro- spera promittentes, propter Templum, domum Davidis, sa- cerdotium & ritus à Deo institutos : atque eo modo multo- rum impedierunt conversionem, quo genere hominum nul- lum est exitialius. Vid. 2. Tim. 3, 6.

FACTI SUNT MIHI OMNES UT SODOMA, ET HABITATORES EJUS QUASI GOMORRA] Non pluris eos facio, quam Sodomæ & Gomorræ cives, ho- mines non errore aliquo, sed destinato malos.

## 23:15
Vers. 15. BEHOLD, I WILL FEED THEM WITH WORMWOOD, AND GIVE THEM GALL TO DRINK] See above 9, 15.

FOR FROM THE PROPHETS OF JERUSALEM IS PROFANENESS GONE FORTH INTO ALL THE LAND] For they propagated vices by flattering.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ECCE, EGO CIBABO EOS ABSINTHIO, ET POTABO FELLE] Vide supra 9, 15.

A PROPHETIS ENIM JERUSALEM EGRES- SA EST POLLUTIO SUPER OMNEM TERRAM] Illi enim adulando vitia propagarunt.

## 23:16
Vers. 16. THEY SPEAK A VISION OF THEIR OWN HEART] They speak what seemed good to themselves.

NOT OUT OF THE MOUTH OF THE LORD] By no command of God.

Latin:

Vers. 16. VISIONEM CORDIS SUI LOQUUN- TUR ] Loquuntur quod ipsis visum est.

NON DE ORE DOMINI] Nullo Dei mandato.

## 23:17
Vers. 17. AND TO EVERY ONE THAT WALKETH IN THE PERVERSENESS OF HIS OWN HEART] In the hardness of his own heart. In that sense this word is always taken among the Rabbis and Talmudists.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET OMNI, QUI AMBULAT IN PRA- VITATE CORDIS SUI ] In duritie cordis sui. Eo sensu hæc vox sumitur semper apud Rabbinos & Thalmudistas.

## 23:18
Vers. 18. WHO HATH STOOD IN THE COUNSEL OF THE LORD, AND HATH PERCEIVED AND HEARD HIS WORD, WHO HATH CONSIDERED HIS WORD, AND HEARD IT?] They spoke from conjecture, not from revelation. But conjectures, if they deceive a man in the councils of kings, how much more in the councils of God? Similar to this passage is that to the Romans 11, 34. 35. against the Jews, who by mere conjecture about the will of God affirmed for certain that God did not wish to admit uncircumcised men, but only the pious, to eternal life.

Latin:

Vers. 18. QUIS AFFUIT IN CONSILIO DOMINI, ET VIDIT, ET AUDIVIT SERMONEM EJUS, QUIS CONSIDERAVIT VERBUM ILLIUS, ET AV- DIVIT?] Ex conjectura, non ex revelatione loquebantur. Conjecturæ autem, si in regum consiliis, quanto magis in consiliis Dei, hominem fallunt? Similis est huic loco ille ad Romanos 11, 34. 35. contra Judæos, qui sola conjectura de voluntate Dei pro certo affirmabant, nolle Deum homi- nes incircumcisos, sed pios ad vitam æternam admittere.

## 23:19
Vers. 19. BEHOLD A WHIRLWIND OF THE LORD'S INDIGNATION SHALL GO FORTH] A huge storm, λαῖλαψ, καταιγὶς, κλύδων, by which words סער is usually translated.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ECCE TURBO DOMINICÆ INDIGNA- TIONIS EGREDIETUR ] Procella ingens, λαῖλαψ, κα- ταιγὶς, κλύδων, quibus verbis verti solet סער.

## 23:20
Ver. 20. THE FURY OF THE LORD SHALL NOT RETURN] A similitude taken from a messenger. Thus ἐπιστραφήτω is used also in Matt. 10, 13.

IN THE LATTER DAYS YOU SHALL UNDERSTAND HIS COUNSEL] That is, at length: when the time shall have come.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NON REVERTETUR FUROR DOMINI] Similitudo à nuntio sumpta. Sic ἐπιστραφήτω ponitur & Matth. 10, 13.

IN NOVISSIMIS DIEBUS INTELLIGETIS CON- SILIUM EJUS] Id est, tandem : ubi tempus venerit.

## 23:22
Ver. 22. IF THEY HAD STOOD IN MY COUNSEL] If they had received revelations from me.

AND HAD MADE KNOWN MY WORDS TO THE PEOPLE] And had spoken my commandments, adding nothing, or taking away.

I WOULD SURELY HAVE TURNED THEM FROM THEIR WAY] The interpreter wrote 'they would have turned', as it is also in the Hebrew, and in the Greek and in the Chaldean. They should have given, he says, to the people those counsels through which, being healed from sins, they would have simultaneously escaped punishments.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SI STETISSENT IN CONSILIO MEO] Si à me revelationes accepissent.

ET NOTA FECISSENT VERBA MEA POPULO] Et mea mandata elocuti essent, nihil addendo, aut demendo.

AVERTISSEM UTIQUE EOS A VIA SUA] Scri- psit interpres avertissent, ut & in Hebræo est, & in Græco & in Chaldæo. Dedissent, ait, populo ea consilia, per quæ à peccatis sanati simul & pœnas evasissent.

## 23:23
Verse 23. AM I A GOD AT HAND, SAYS THE LORD, AND NOT A GOD AFAR OFF? Do you think that I only care for heavenly things, and not earthly ones?

Latin:

Vers. 23. PVTASNE DEVS E VICINO EGO SVM, DICIT DOMINVS, ET NON DEVS DE LONGE? Putarisne me tantum cœlestia curare, & non terrestria?

## 23:24
Verse 24. SHALL A MAN HIDE HIMSELF IN SECRET PLACES, AND I SHALL NOT SEE HIM? Will someone so wrap himself in hiding places that I do not see him?

DO NOT I FILL HEAVEN AND EARTH? Both in perspicacity and in efficacy. See Psalm 139, 7. 8. 9. 10.

Although it cannot be denied that these words speak of providence and the care of earthly things and the omnipresent dominion of God in heaven and on earth, they are not, however, to be understood as referring to a bare and abstract essence, as if God were present only by His power and operation, with His substance excluded, which is contained only by heaven, as Grotius accepts the position with the Socinians and some Calvinists. Because they clearly infer both, namely, both the ἀδιαςασίαν (indistancy) and the indistancy of essence, and the divine ἐνέργειαν (energy) and operation. God testifies that He is a God not AFAR OFF, but AT HAND, and teaches that He FILLS heaven and earth. But God would not be AT HAND if He were contained by heaven by reason of ESSENCE, nor would His substance be present outside of heaven. For thus, indeed, the operation of God would be near, yet God Himself would be AFAR OFF, not at hand: just as the King of the Spains is present to the Indies with his power, government, and authority, but resides at Madrid in Castile; he is a King from afar, not at hand. Nor could one be said to FILL heaven and earth equally who were in heaven only by reason of substance, and not truly equally on earth, as Grotius dreams concerning God with the Socinians and some Calvinists. But on the contrary, God says, Do I not fill heaven and earth?

Wherefore that πλήρωσις (filling), although it also implies divine power and operation or efficacy, does not, however, exclude the divine essence. God fills heaven and earth with present power, not with absent nature, says Augustine, book 7, On the City of God, ch. 30. Which the parallel passage from the Psalms confirms: namely, Psalm 139, 7 ff. Whither shall I go from thy Spirit, or whither shall I flee from thy face? If I ascend into heaven, thou art there; if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there: If I take the wings of the morning and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea, even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me; which imply God Himself, not only present divine power. This discourse, asks Anastasius, Patriarch of Antioch, in book 2, On the Uncircumscribed Essence of God, regarding those words of the Psalm, where did he render that meaning of nature separated from the efficacy of operating? For that Divinity permeates and extends through all things, filling the universe with the magnitude of His nature. That was the error of the Stoics, that God is absent from the earth by reason of substance, whom Tertullian notes in his Apologeticus, because they said God was placed outside the world, who like a potter turns this mass from the outside: But Plotinus, Ennead 6, book 5, 4, taught that it is implanted in all human nature to think that God is simultaneously present, and to judge that He is everywhere in His entirety. Cyril of Alexandria, book 2, against Julian, and Jerome, in ch. 66 of Isaiah, noted something similar about the Jews, but that is to be understood only of certain unlearned men among the Jews. For the wise among them did not deny the immensity of the divine essence. R. David Kimchi on v. 7 of Ps. 139, Whither shall I go from thy Spirit, and whither shall I flee from thy face? If I say, he says, that I will do that, I shall not be able. For thou art in every place, and place does not contain thee. Therefore, as Hilary interpreted: No place is without God, nor is any place not in God: He is in the heavens, He is in hell, He is beyond the seas; He is within, He is without; thus He has and is had, nor is He Himself in anything, nor is He not in all things. And thus the author of the book On Foundations, book 2, ch. 17, notes from 1 Kings 8:27, Behold, the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee, and concludes that God does not need a place in which to exist: God alone is blessed, he says, thus it cannot be said that He is somewhere, just as He cannot be said to be in a place. Which are twin to those of Damascene, book 1, On the Orthodox Faith, ch. 14: God is not in a place: for He is His own place, filling all things and existing above all things and Himself containing the universe. And the Sentences of Fulgentius, book against the Sermon of Fastidiosus, ch. 6. This is the immense One, whom no creature can enclose, and because He is immense, He is everywhere whole: because He is neither contained by place, nor extended or contracted by space. With which Gregory the Great agrees, book 2, Morals, ch. 8, on those words of Job 1: Satan went out from the face of the Lord. Whither then does he go from Him, who, while He is nowhere by the mass of a body, is nowhere absent by His uncircumscribed Substance. Nor for any other reason do the Hebrews call God מקום (place), than that He embraces all things. In which manner Maximus in the Scholia to ch. 1 of Dionysius, On the Divine Names: If God, he says, is the place of all things, not in a corporeal way, but as the Maker: since He who fills heaven and earth and all things Himself, and is outside these, it is clear that He is the same as infinity, i.e., a force having no limit. Therefore Maimonides in More Nebuchim, part 1, ch. 8: As often as the word place is said of God, it is truly understood as the degree of His own immense and incomparable essence.

Therefore it is not to be thought that God fills all things, fills heaven and earth, in such a way that He diffuses and expands His essence through all things in heaven and on earth in a corporeal manner, but He fills all things because He is absent from no thing, He is present to all, He contains all things, He is not contained by them. God does not fill all things by being extended with all things, says Athanasius in his book against Sabellius; for this is corporeal, as if one were to say that air has filled whatever lies between heaven and earth. But He contains all things as a force. For He is a force devoid of body, not falling under sight, neither surrounding nor surrounded. Which Gregory the Great explains thus in homily 8 on Ezekiel. Let us place before our eyes what that nature of God is, which holds all things, fills all things, embraces all things, surpasses all things, sustains all things: yet God does not sustain from one part and surpass from another, nor fill from one part and embrace from another, but by embracing He fills, by filling He embraces, by sustaining He surpasses, by surpassing He sustains, ruling what is above without restlessness, sustaining what is below without breadth, penetrating what is within without thinning, surrounding what is without without extension. He is therefore lower and higher without place: He is ample without breadth, He is subtle without thinning, and He who is nowhere through the mass of a body, is nowhere absent through His uncircumscribed substance. And not otherwise S. Aug. Ep. 57. ad Dardan. Thus is God divided through all things, so that He is not a quality of the world, but the creative substance of the world, ruling the world without labor and containing it without burden, yet not through spaces of places, as if by a diffused mass, so that He is half in half the body of the world, and thus whole through the whole, but whole in heaven alone, and whole in earth alone, and whole in heaven and in earth alone, and contained by no place, but everywhere whole in Himself. And libr. 22. de Civit. Dei c. 29. For not because it is said that God is both in heaven and on earth, for He Himself says through the Prophet (Jer. 23.) I fill heaven and earth, are we to say that He has one part in heaven and another on earth, but He is whole in heaven, whole on earth; not at alternating times, but both at once, which no bodily nature can do. Gregory of Nyssa judges this to be childish, if anyone does not acknowledge God to be everywhere present by His essence Catech. libr. 1. cap. 25. Who is of such a childish mind, that looking at the universe he does not believe that in the universe there is God entering into it, containing it, and sitting upon it: And how can divine power be separated from His essence? The being of God, says Anselm in the book de Incarnat. c. 4., is the same as His power. Just as therefore the power of God is always and everywhere, so whatever God is, is everywhere and always. Therefore Cyril of Alexandria l. 11. in Joh. The operation of God and His power

It is fitting for God to be everywhere and in an inexplicable way to fill heaven, to fill the earth, to contain all things, to be contained by none. For God cannot be comprehended by place, nor circumscribed by spaces. Not as if enclosed in heaven by others, says Chrysostom on Ps. 112, he sees from on high what is on earth, but is everywhere present and assisting all.

Latin:

Vers. 24. SI OCCVLTABITVR VIR IN ABSCONDITIS, ET EGO NON VIDEBO EVM) Itane se latebris involvet aliquis, ut ego eum non videam?

NVMQVID NON COELVM ET TERRAM EGO IMPLEO) Tum perspicacia tum efficacia. Vide Psal. 139, 7. 8. 9. 10.

Etsi negandum non sit, hæc de providentia, & cura rerum terrenarum ac omnipræsenti dominio Dei in cœlo & in terra loqui, non tamen de nuda & abstracta essentia intelligenda sunt, quasi sola potentia, & operatione sua Deus præsto esset, exclusa substantia, quæ solum cœlo contineatur, uti cum Socinianis & Calvinianis nonnullis locum accipit Grot. Quia utrumque, puta tum ἀδιαςασίαν & indistantem ad- essentiam, tum ἐνέργειαν & operationem divinam luculenter inferunt. Deus se Deum non de LONGE, sed E VICINO esse testatur, ac cælum & terram se IMPLERE docet. Non autem esset Deus de VICINO, si cælo ratione ESSENTIÆ contineretur, neq́; extra cælum substantia sua præsto esset. Sic enim vicina quidem foret Dei operatio, Deus tamen ipse DE LONGE esset, non de vicino: quemadmodum Hispaniarum Rex cum potestate sua, gubernatione, atq́; imperio adest Indiis, residet autem Madriti in Castilia, de longe Rex est, non de vicino. Neq́; IMPLERE cœlum pariter, & terram dici posset, qui in cœlo solum ratione substantiæ foret, non vero æque in terra, uti de Deo cum Socinianis, & Calvinianis nonnullis somniat Grotius. At ex adverso Deus, numquid, inquit, non cœlum & terram ego impleo?

Quapropter πλήρωσις illa, etsi inferat etiam divinam potentiam & operationem vel efficaciam, non excludit tamen divinam essentiam. Deus implet cœlum & terram præsente potentia, non absente natura inquit Augustinus l. 7. de Civ. Dei c. 30. Quod locus è Psalmis parallelus confirmat: Psal. nempe 139, 7. seqq. Quo ibo à Spiritu tuo, & quo fugiam à facie tua. Si ascendero in cœlos, ibi tu, si stratum fecero in inferno, ecce tu: Si assumsero pennas auroræ & habitavero in novissimo maris, ibi manus tua me ducet & tenebit me dextra tua; quæ Deum ipsum, non tantum divinam potentiam præsentem inferunt. Sermo hic, quærit Anastasius Patriarcha Antiochenus lib. 2. de incircumscripta Dei essentia, ad illa Psalmi verba, ubi significationem illam reddidit naturæ ab efficacia operandi separatæ? Numen etenim illud omnia permeat, ac pertendit, universa adimplens magnitudine suæ naturæ. Stoicorum ille erat error, absentem Deum esse terris ratione substantiæ, quos notat Tertullianus in Apologet. quod positum extra mundum Deum dixerint, qui figuli modo extrinsecus torqueat molem hanc: Sed Plotinus Ennead. 6. lib. 5. 4. id omni humanæ naturæ insitum esse docuit, ut simul esse Deum existimet, etiam ubiq́; esse totum arbitretur. Cyrillus Alex. lib. 2. cont. Julian. Hieron. in c. 66. Es. simile quid de Judæis notarunt, sed id non nisi de rudibus quibusdam inter Judæos intelligendum. Sapientes enim ex ipsis non negarunt immensitatem divinæ essentiæ. R. David Kimchi ad v. 7. Ps. 139. quo ibo à Spiritu tuo, & quo à facie tua fugiam? Si dixero, inquit, me id facturum, non potero. Tu enim es in omni loco, & locus te non capit. Proinde uti Hilarius interpretatus est: Nullus sine Deo, neq́; ullus non in Deo locus est: In cœlis est, in inferno est, ultra maria est, inest interior, excedit interior: ita cum habet, atq́; habetur, neq́; in aliquo ipse, neq́; non in omnibus est. Atq; ita Autor libri de fundamentis l. 2. c. 17. notat è 1. Reg. 8, 27. Ecce, cœli cœlorum non capient te, colligit, Deum non indigere loco, in quo consistat: Deus solus benedictus, inquit, sic est non potest dici esse alicubi, sicut nec esse in loco. Quæ gemina sunt illis Damasceni libro 1. de Fid. cap. 14. Deus in loco non est: ipse enim sibi ipsi locus est im- plens omnia & supra omnia consistens atque ipse conti- nens universa. Et Sententiæ Fulgentii libr. contra Sermon. fastidios. c. 6. Hic est immensus, quem nul- ta potest concludere creatura, & quia immensus, ubi- que totus: quia nec continetur loco, nec distenditur aut contrahitur spatio. Quibus consonat Gregor. M. l. 2. Moral. c. 8. ad illa Job. 1. Egressus est Satan à fa- cie Domini. Quo igitur ab eo exit, qui dum per mo- lem corporis nusquam est, per incircumscriptam Sub- stantiam nusquam deest. Nec alia ratione Ebræi Deum מקום locum vocant, quam quod omnia com- plectatur. Quo pacto Maximus in Scholiis ad cap. 1. Dionys. de Divin. nomin. Si Deus, inquit, omnium est locus, non corporeo modo, sed tanquam opifex: quippe, qui cœlum & terram & omnia implet ipse, & extra hæc est, perspicuum est, eundem esse infinitatem, h. e. vim terminum nullum habentem. Ideo Maimo- nides in More Nebuch. part. 1. c. 8. Quotiescunque vox loci dicitur de Deo, revera intelligitur gradus es- sentiæ ipsius immensæ & incomparabilis.

Non ergo cogitandum, Deum implere omnia, implere cœlum & terram, ita, ut se diffundat & ex- pandat essentia sua per omnia in cœlo & in terra, more corporali, sed omnia implet, quia nulli rei abest omni- b9 adest, omnia continet, non continetur ab iis. Non cum omnibus extensus, inquit Athanasius Libr. adv. Sabellium, complet omnia Deus; hoc enim est corpo- reum, ut si quis aërem dixerit implevisse, quicquid in- ter cœlum ac terram interjacet. Verum tanquam vis omnia continet. Est enim vis corporis expers sub aspe- ctum non cadens, non ambiens, nec ambita. Quod ita explicat Gregorius M. homil. 8. in Ezech. Pona- mus ante oculos, quæ sit illa Dei natura, quæ tenet o- mnia, implet omnia, complectitur omnia, superexce- dit omnia, sustinet omnia: nequaquam autem Deus ex una parte sustinet, atq; ex alia superexcedit, neque ex alia parte implet, atq; ex alia circumplectitur, sed circumplectendo implet, implendo circumplectitur, sustinendo superexcedit, superexcedendo sustinet, sine inquietudine superius regens, sine latitudine inferius sustinens, interius sine extenuatione penetrans, exte- rius sine extensione circumstans. Est itaq; inferior & superior sine loco: est amplus sine latitudine, est sub- tilis sine extenuatione, & qui per molem corporis nus- quam est, per incircumscriptam substantiam suam nusquam deest. Nec aliter S. Aug. Ep. 57. ad Dardan. Sic est De9 per cuncta divisus, ut non sit qualitas mun- di, sed substantia creatrix mundi, sine labore regens & sine onere continens mundum, non tamen per spatia lo- corum, quasi mole diffusa, ita ut in dimidio mundi cor- pore sit dimidius, atq; ita per totum totus, sed in solo cœ- lo totus, & in sola terra totus & in cœlo & in terra totus solus & nullo contentus loco, sed in seipso ubique totus. Et libr. 22. de Civit. Dei c. 29. Non enim quia dicitur Deum & in cœlo esse & in terra, ipse quippe ait per Prophetam (Jer. 23.) Cœlum & terram ego impleo, aliam partem dicturi sumus eum in cœlo habere, & in terra aliam, sed totus in cœlo est, totus in terra; non alternis temporibus, sed utrumq; simul, quod nulla na- tura corporalis potest. Gregorius Nyssenus puerile hoc esse censet, si quis Deum non ubiq; præsentem es- sentia sua agnoscat Catech. libr. 1. cap. 25. Quis tam puerili ingenio est, ut ad universitatem adspiciens in universitate non credat, esse Deum in eam subeuntem, eam continentem & ei insidentem: Et quomodo sepa- rari potest divina potentia ab ejus essentia? Idem est esse Dei, inquit Anshelmus libro de Incarnat. c. 4. & potestas ejus. Sicut itaq; potestas Dei semper & u- biq;, ita quidquid est Deus, ubiq; est & semper. Ideo Cyrill. Alexand. l. 11. in Joh. Operatio Dei ac virtus

Deo conveniens est, esse ubique & inexplicabili modo implere cælum, implere terram, capere omnia, à nullo capi. Non enim comprehendi loco potest Deus, neque spatiis circumscribi. Non tanquam aliis in cælo conclusus, inquit Chrysost. ad Ps. 112. eminens videt, quæ sunt in terra, sed ubiq; præsens & omnib9 assistens.

## 23:27
Verse 27. BECAUSE OF THEIR DREAMS) They were selling prophecies from the trifles of ὀνειροπόλων (dream-interpreters).

Latin:

Vers. 27. PROPTER SOMNIA EORVM) Ex ὀνει- ροπόλων nugis vaticinia venditabant.

## 23:28
Verse 28. THE PROPHET WHO HAS A DREAM AS A DREAM) He who calls himself a Prophet, if he has dreamed anything, let him tell it as a dream, not as a divine revelation. AND HE WHO HAS MY WORD, LET HIM SPEAK MY WORD TRULY) Let him announce in good faith what he has received from God, let him subtract nothing, let him add nothing of his own. WHAT HAVE THE CHAFF TO DO WITH THE WHEAT?) What similarity do such dreams have with divine revelations?

Latin:

Vers. 28. PROPHETA QVI HABET SOMNIVM VT SOMNIUM) Qui se Prophetam dicit, si quid somnia- vit, narret ut somnium, non ut revelationem divinam. ET QVI HABET SERMONEM MEVM, LO- QVATVR SERMONEM MEUM VERE) Bona fide e- nuntiet, quæ à Deo accepit, nihil subtraheat, nihil addat de suo. QVID PALEIS AD TRITICUM?) Quid simile habent talia somnia cum revelationibus divinis?

## 23:29
Verse 29. ARE NOT MY WORDS LIKE FIRE, SAYS THE LORD, AND LIKE A HAMMER THAT BREAKS THE ROCK) Sparing no one, not even the hardest, whereas those false prophets accommodate themselves to the ears and wills of all.

Latin:

Vers. 29. NUMQUID NON VERBA MEA SVNT QVASI IGNIS, DICIT DOMINUS, ET QVASI MALLEUS CONTERENS PETRAM) Nemini parcens, ne durissimo quidem, cum illi Pseudoprophetæ omnium auribus ac voluntatibus se accommodent.

## 23:30
Verse 30. WHO STEAL MY WORDS EVERYONE FROM HIS NEIGHBOR) That is, by their lies they cause men not to give credence to the law and to true Prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 30. QVI FVRANTVR VERBA MEA UNUS- QVISQVE A PROXIMO SVO) Id est, suis mendaciis efficiunt, ne homines legi & veris Prophetis fide adhibeant.

## 23:31
Verse 31. WHO TAKE THEIR TONGUES) They say what comes into their own minds.

Latin:

Vers. 31. QVI ASSVMVNT LINGVAS SVAS) Di- cunt, quod ipsis in mentem venit.

## 23:32
Verse 32. AND IN THEIR MIRACLES) The Chaldean better: by their rashness. The LXX: ἐν τοῖς πλάνοις αὐτῶν (in their deceits). פחת to the Chaldeans is to leap up.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ET IN MIRACULIS SVIS) Chaldæus me- lius: temeritate sua. LXX. ἐν τοῖς πλάνοις αὐτῶν. פחת Chal- dæis est subsilire.

## 23:33
Verse 33. SAYING WHAT IS THE BURDEN OF THE LORD) The Greeks translate משא as λῆμμα (taking/assumption), and thus Chrysostom uses it in this place, that the author of both laws is the same. The Latin well as 'onus' (burden), and Aquila as ἄρμα (chariot). For the Prophets used that title or preface when they were about to publish prophecies that were dire, sad, and heavy to carry. But because this word, on account of the long patience of God not immediately fulfilling his threats, had turned into a mockery among the impious Jews, therefore Jeremiah gravely rebukes them for the mockery of this word. YOU SHALL SAY: YOU ARE THE BURDEN, I WILL CAST YOU AWAY) A play on ambiguity; for heavy and useless burdens are accustomed to be cast away. And God had tolerated those men more than enough. See also shortly 38.

Latin:

Vers. 33. DICENS QVOD EST ONVS DOMINI) משא Græci λῆμμα vertunt, & sic hoc loco utitur Chryso- stomus sermone utriusque legis eundem esse auctorem. Latinus bene onus, & Aquila ἄρμα. Eo enim titulo aut præ- fatione utebantur Prophetæ, ubi vulgaturi erant vaticinia dira atque tristia & gravia portatu. Quia vero hæc vox ob longam patientiam Dei non statim minas suas implentis apud impios Judæos in ludibrium verterat, ideo Jeremias graviter eos de hujus vocis irrisu increpat. DICES: VOS ESTIS ONUS, PROJICIAM QVIPPE VOS) Lusus ex ambiguo; nam onera gravia & inutilia projici solent. Et illos homines Deus plus satis to- leraverat. Vide & mox 38.

## 23:36
Verse 36. FOR THE BURDEN SHALL BE TO EVERYONE HIS OWN WORD) That is, those words of those using the word 'burden' through mockery will turn out very badly for them. AND YOU HAVE PERVERTED THE WORDS OF THE LIVING GOD) For you, he says, have turned the words of the living God into a joke.

Latin:

Vers. 36. QVIA ONVS ERIT UNICUIQVE SER- MO SVVS) Id est, illa verba vocem oneris per risum usur- pantium pessime ipsis cedent. ET PERVERTISTIS VERBA DEI VIVENTIS) Nam vos, inquit, Dei viventis verba in jocum vertistis.

## 23:39
Verse 39. I WILL TAKE YOU CARRYING) I.e., carrying away. Twice here is the verb נשא, from which is derived משא, i.e., burden.

Latin:

Vers. 39. TOLLAM VOS PORTANS) I. e. deportan- dos. Bis hic est verbū נשא, unde derivatur משא, i. e. onu-.

## 23:40
Verse 40. INTO EVERLASTING REPROACH) See above 20, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 40. IN OPPROBRIVM SEMPITERNUM) Vi de supra 20, 11.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV.

A vision concerning two baskets filled with good and bad figs: which is explained, that those who had given themselves up as captives with Jeconiah would fare well, but Zedekiah the oath-breaker, with his people, would perish.

Vers. 1. THE LORD SHOWED ME, AND BEHOLD, TWO BASKETS FULL OF FIGS) That is, He showed me two baskets, or two hampers full of figs. After Jeremiah had reminded King Zedekiah of what he had once said first to the kings, then to the Princes, and afterwards to those who wished to be considered Prophets, he comes to a certain comparison between the king and the princes, and between the people, intending to add final warnings which pertain to the people alone, pursuing the order of things indeed, rather than of times. SET BEFORE THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) Which they had brought to the Temple from the first fruits of the fields of the Lord. AFTER NEBUCHADNEZZAR HAD CARRIED AWAY JECONIAH THE SON OF JEHOIAKIM KING OF JUDAH AND HIS PRINCES) That is, immediately after that had happened which is narrated in 2 Kings 24:10. Thus, at the very beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, the Prophet had foreseen the outcome of that same reign. AND THE CRAFTSMAN AND THE SMITH) See what is said in 2 Kings 24:14.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV.

Visio de duobus calathis ficubus bonis & malis repletis: quæ explicatur, illos, qui cū Jecho- nia se captivos dederint, bene habituros, Ze- dekiā vero fœdifragū cū suis pessum iturū.

Vers. 1. OSTENDIT MIHI DOMINVS, ET ECCE, DUO CALATHI PLENI FICIS) Id est, ostendit mihi duos calathos, aut duo canistra plena ficis. Jeremias post- quam Regi Sedeciæ commemoraverat, quæ olim dixerat re- gibus primum, deinde Principibus, postea his, qui Prophetæ haberi volebant, venit ad comparationem quandam inter regem & principes, interq; populum, postrema monita addi- turus, quæ ad populum solum pertinent, rerum quippe ma- gis, quam temporum ordinem persequens. POSITI ANTE TEMPLVM DOMINI) Quos de primitiis ad Templum tulerant agrorum Domini. POSTQVAM TRANSTVLIT NABVCHODO- NOSOR JECHONIAM FILIVM JOJAKIM REGEM JVDA ET PRINCIPES EJVS) Id est, statim postquam illud acciderat, quod narratur 2. Reg. 24, 10. Ita ipso initio regni Sedeciæ exitum ejusdem regni Propheta prospexerat ET FABRVM ET INCLVSORVM) Vide, qua dicta 2. Reg. 24, 14.

## 24:2
Vers. 2. AS FIGS ARE WONT) For there are certain figs which bear both early and late fruits. Plin. 15, 18. VERY BAD) As was evident from their appearance.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VT SOLENT FICVS ESSE PRIMI TEM- PORIS) Sunt enim ficus quædam, quæ & præcoces & se rotinos fructus ferunt. Plin. 15, 18. MALAS NIMIS) Ut ex aspectu patebat.

## 24:3
Vers. 3. LIKE THESE GOOD FIGS, SO WILL I ACKNOWLEDGE THE CAPTIVITY OF JUDAH, WHOM I HAVE SENT OUT OF THIS PLACE INTO THE LAND OF THE CHALDEANS FOR THEIR GOOD) Just as you approve of those figs, so I will approve of the repentance which those now deported will one day perform, for whom God therefore prolonged their life, because they had sinned by the example of others. Vers. 6. I WILL SET MY EYES UPON THEM) I will look upon them with favor. AND I WILL BUILD THEM, AND NOT DESTROY THEM) I will place them here in a certain seat, which they are happily to obtain. Vers. 7. AND I WILL GIVE THEM A HEART, THAT THEY MAY KNOW THAT I AM THE LORD) I will so bind them with the greatest benefits that they cannot be unmindful of me. Or rather, that they may be converted: because conversion is described by the gift of a new heart and the knowledge of the Lord, both a priori and a posteriori, ch. 31, 31. Ezek. 11, 19. and Jer. 9, 24. whence they are said to be about to repent at the gift of a new heart, and to know the Lord more and more. THAT THEY MAY RETURN TO ME WITH THEIR WHOLE HEART) Better: After they shall have returned to me with their whole heart. Vers. 8. WHO REMAIN IN THIS CITY) Better: Who will remain in this city: namely, after all the deportations. AND WHO DWELL IN THE LAND OF EGYPT) And who will go to dwell in the land of Egypt. Those, namely, of whom 2 Kings 25:26 and below 42, 43, 44. It seems rather to be understood of those who, of their own accord, for greater security, had already fled into Egypt before the capture of Zedekiah, as Castrius and B. Hülsemann explain. Vers. 9. AND FOR A PROVERB) It will be said of a most miserable man: he is as miserable as Zedekiah. Vers. 10. UNTIL THEY ARE CONSUMED FROM THE LAND) That is, they shall perish, never to return to their homeland.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SICVT FICVS HÆ BONÆ, SIC COGNO SCAM TRANSMIGRATIONEM JVDÆ, QVAM E MISI DE LOCO ISTO IN TERRAM CHALDÆO RUM IN BONUM) Sicut tu ficus illas approbas, ita eg approbabo pœnitentiam, quam agent aliquando isti nun deportati, quibus ideo Deus vitam produxit, quia alieno ex- emplo peccaverant. Vers. 6. PONAM OCULOS MEOS SVPER EOS) Favens eos respiciam. ET ÆDIFICABO EOS, ET NON DESTRVAM) Locabo eos hic in certa sede, quam feliciter obtenturi sunt. Vers. 7. ET DABO EIS COR, UT SCIANT, QVIA EGO SVM DOMINVS) Maximis beneficiis ita eos obli- gabo, ut mei immemores esse non possint. IMo ut convertantur: quia cordis novi donatio- ne, & Domini agnitione conversio describitur à priori, & à posteriori, c. 31, 31. Ezech. 11, 19. & Ier. 9, 24. unde ad cordis novi donationem dicuntur acturi pœnitentiam, ac magis magisque cognituri Dominum. QVIA REVERTENTVR AD ME IN TOTO CORDE SVO) Melius: Postquam ad me reversi fuerint in toto corde suo. Vers. 8. QVI REMANSERUNT IN VRBE HAC) Melius: Qui remanebunt in urbe hac: nempe post omnes deportationes. ET QVI HABITANT IN TERRA ÆGYPTI) Et qui habitatum ibunt in terram Ægyptii. Illi scilicet de qui- bus 2. Reg. 25, 26. & infra 42. 43. 44. Videtur potius intelligi, qui sua sponte ad ma- jorem securitatem jam ante captum Zedekiam in Ægyptum profugerant, ut Castrius, & B. Hülse- mann. explicant. Vers. 9. ET IN PARABOLAM) De miserrimo ho- mine dicetur: tam miser est, quam Sedecias. Vers. 10. DONEC CONSVMANTVR DE TERRA) Id est, pereant nunquam in patriam redituri.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV.

A complaint concerning the contempt of the Prophet's sermons with a prediction of the destruction and captivity of seventy years. The cup of wrath is to be given to other nations also, though the beginning is made at the house of the Lord.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV.

Querela de contemtu concionum Prophetæ cũ prædictione excidii, & captivitatis LXX. annorum. Calix iræ aliis etiam populis pro- pinandus, initio tamẽ facto à domo Domini.

## 25:3
Vers. 3. FROM THE THIRTEENTH YEAR OF THE REIGN OF JOSIAH) For Josiah reigned for 31 years. From these subtract 12 and add the 4 years of Jehoiakim, they become the 23 years themselves, during which Jeremiah says he had not ceased with any labor to bring himself and his associates, so that he might lead the people to a better way of life. Vers. 9. THE FAMILIES OF THE NORTH) The Medes and other nations either subject to or allied with the Chaldeans. NEBUCHADNEZZAR THE KING OF BABYLON MY SERVANT) That is, the instrument of my wrath. INTO ASTONISHMENT AND HISSING) Above 18, 16. 19, 8. AND UPON ALL THE NATIONS THAT ARE ROUND ABOUT IT) The neighbors of the Jews, of whom below 20, 21, 22. Vers. 10. AND I WILL DESTROY FROM THEM THE VOICE OF MIRTH, THE VOICE OF THE BRIDEGROOM AND THE BRIDE) Above 7, 34. and 16, 9. THE VOICE OF THE MILLSTONE) The songs of girls grinding at the mill. See Matt. 24, 41. Such a song was that mentioned by Plutarch: ἄλει μύλα, ἄλει. Καὶ γὰρ Πίττακος ἀλει̃ μεγάλας Μιτυλάνας βασιλεύων. AND THE LIGHT OF THE LAMP) He seems to understand torches, with which one went to banquets. Vers. 11. SEVENTY YEARS) A remarkable prediction, because of the exact designation of time. Vers. 12. AND WHEN SEVENTY YEARS HAVE BEEN COMPLETED. The beginning of the Babylonian captivity is fixed here in the fourth year of Jehoiakim: which is also noted by Daniel ch. 1, 1. 2. so that the end of them is to be fixed in the first year of the Monarchy of Cyrus, to which opinion almost all the Fathers agree, observes B. Hülsemann here, and he proves that this was also the later opinion of Jerome from his Commentary on Jeremiah, who is later than his commentary on Haggai, as is evident from the preface. Vers. same. I WILL VISIT UPON THE KING OF BABYLON) I will punish Nabonidus through Cyrus. INTO EVERLASTING SOLITUDES) Long-lasting. Why are the desolations to be understood not as everlasting, but only as long-lasting? Just as Babel ought to have been subject to perpetual devastation. Concerning which Jerome in this place: Just as Jerusalem after seventy years does not receive its former inhabitants, and having completed its punishments, because it obeyed the sentence of God, it enjoys its former happiness: Thus the King of Babylon, who was lifted up in pride, and thought it was of his own strength that he reigned among the nations and not of the Lord's will, would be destroyed by the coming of the Medes and Persians. Finally, to this day, the ruins of the city of Babylon remain solitude, and fulfilled all the words which are contained in the volume of this very Prophet.

Latin:

Vers. 3. A TERTIO DECIMO ANNO REGNI JO- SIÆ) Nam 31. annis regnavit Josias. Ab his deme 12. & ad- de annos 4. Joakimi, fiunt ipsi anni 23. per quos nullo la- bore & se & socios suos abstinuisse ait Jeremias, ut ad melio- rem frugem populum reduceret. Vers. 9. COGNATIONES AQUILONIS) Medos, aliasq; gentes Chaldæis aut subditas, aut federatas. NABUCHODONOSOR REGEM BABYLONIS SERVUM MEVM) Id est, instrumentum iræ meæ. IN STVPOREM ET IN SIBILUM) Supra 18, 16. 19, 8. ET SVPER OMNES NATIONES, QVÆ IN CIRCVITV ILLIVS SVNT) Vicinos Judæorum, de quibus infra 20. 21. 22. Vers. 10, PERDAMQVE EX EIS VOCEM GAVDII, VOCEM SPONSI ET SPONSÆ) Supra 7, 34. & 16, 9. VOCEM MOLÆ) Cantica puellarum molam tru- fantium. Vide Matth. 24, 41. Tale canticum erat illud me- moratum Plutarcho: ἄλει μύλα, ἄλει. Καὶ γὰρ Πίττακος ἀλει̃ μεγάλας Μιτυλάνας βασιλεύων. ET LUMEN LVCERNÆ) Faces intelligere vide- tur, cum quibus ad convivia ibatur. Vers. 11. SEPTVAGINTA ANNIS) Prædictio insignis, ob ita exactam temporis designationem. Vers. 12. CUMQUE IMPLETI FUERINT LXX. ANNI. Initium hic figitur captivitatis Babyl. in quar- to Jojakimi anno: quod & Danieli notatum cap. 1, 1. 2. ut terminus eorum sit in primo Monarchiæ Cy- ri figendus, in quam sententiam consentire fere omnes Patres observat hic B. Hülsemann. eamque etiam posteriorem fuisse sententiam Hieronymi è Comment. in Jer. probat, qui ejus commentario in Haggæum posterior est, ut è præfat. patet. Vers. eod. VISITABO SVPER REGEM BABILO- NIS) Nabonidum puniam per Cyrum. IN SOLITVDINES SEMPITERNAS) Diuturnas. Cur non sempiternæ, sed tantum diuturnæ in- telligendæ desolationes? Sicuti perpetuæ deva- stationi obnoxia Babel esse debuit. De quo Hiero- nymus hoc loco: Sicut Hierusalem post septuaginta annos non recipit pristinos habitatores, & expletis suppliciis, quia obedivit sententiae Dei, felicitate pri- stina perfruitur: Sic Rex Babylonis, qui elatus est in superbiam, & suarum arbitratus est virium, quod regnavit in gentibus & non Domini voluntatis, Me- dis Persisque venientibus destrueretur. Denique usque ho- die urbis Babylonis reliquiae tantum manent. Et po- suit illam Dominus in solitudinem sempiternam, & implevit omnia verba, quae in istius ipsius Prophetae volumine continentur.

## 25:13
Vers. 13. ALL THAT IS WRITTEN IN THIS BOOK) Here follow in the Greek the prophecies of this Prophet against various nations, such as that against the Elymaeans, which we have at 49, 35. Then that against Egypt, which is for us in chapter 46, then against Babylon, which we have in chapters 50 and 51, then those in 47, 48, 49. Afterwards follow those things which are in this chapter from verse 15. I do not disapprove. For these prophecies seem to be indicated when it is said: In this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all nations.

Hence it cannot be solidly proven that the order here must be inverted. For it could rightly be said that it was written in this book, even if it is written below.

Latin:

Vers. 13. OMNE QUOD SCRIPTUM EST IN LI- BRO ISTO) Hic sequuntur in Graeco prophetiae hujus Pro- phetae adversus gentes varias, ut contra Elymaeos ea, quam nos habemus 49, 35. Deinde illa contra Aegyptum, quae nobis est capite 46. tum contra Babylonem, quam nos ha- bemus cap. 50. & 51. deinde illae 47. 48. 49. Postea sequun- tur ea, quae in hoc sunt capite a commate 15. Non improbo. Videntur enim istae prophetiae indicari, cum dicitur: In libro isto, quem prophetavit Jeremias adversus omnes gentes.

Hinc non probari potest solide, ordinem hic invertendum esse. Nam recte poterat dici scriptum esse in libro hoc, etiamsi infra id scriptum sit.

## 25:14
Vers. 14. BECAUSE THEY SERVED THEM, WHEN THEY WERE MANY NATIONS AND GREAT KINGS) Better: For they themselves shall also serve many nations and great kings: namely, the Medes and Persians. But the Greeks do not have these, as Jerome also noted.

It is by no means to be admitted that the Greek version should be preferred to the authentic Hebrew text. Nor does any necessity compel this. For although these prophecies against the nations are not immediately subjoined here, they are not omitted in the Hebrew Codex, but are exhibited in their own place. Which is also noted here by Jerome. He says it signifies that Jeremiah prophesied not only against Babylon, but against the other nations which had been in the army against the Babylonians, and had fought against the Lord's people. Finally, in the following verses, it is said against Egypt and the Philistines and Moab and Ammon and Idumea and Damascus and Cedar, and the Kingdoms of Hazor and Elam, and at the end, against Babylon and the land of Chaldea. The Hebrew text is not to be corrected by the Greek translation, but the Greek translation ought to have been tested against the Hebrew text.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QUIA SERVIERUNT EIS, CUM ESSENT GENTES MULTAE ET REGES MAGNI) Melius: Nam servient & ipsi gentibus multis & regibus magnis: Medis & Persis scilicet. Sed haec Graeci non habent, ut & Hiero- nymus annotavit.

Neutiquam admittendum, ut praeferatur Grae- ca versio textui Ebraeo authentico. Nec ulla id co- git necessitas. Etsi enim hic non subjunguntur sta- tim ista vaticinia contra gentes, non tamen omit- tuntur in Ebraeo Codice, sed suo loco exhibentur. Quod etiam Hieronymo hic notatum. Significat in- quit, quod non solum contra Babylonem prophetarit Hieremias, sed contra caeteras gentes, quae in Babylonios fuerant exercitu, & contra Domini populum dimi- carunt. Denique in sequentibus dicitur contra Aegy- ptum & Philistim & Moab & Ammon & Idumae- am & Damascum & Cedar, & Regna Asor & E- lam, & ad extremum, contra Babylonem terramque Chaldaeam. Non ex Graeca translatione textus E- braeus corrigendus, sed Graeca translatio ad Ebrae- um textum exigenda erat.

## 25:15
Vers. 15.

TAKE THE CUP OF THE WINE OF THIS FURY FROM MY HAND) This was done in a vision. In that cup, which Jeremiah saw, was fuming wine, a sign of divine wrath.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

SUME CALICEM VINI FURORIS HUJUS DE MANU MEA) Hoc factum ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ. In illo ca- lice, quem videbat Jeremias, erat vinum fumigans, signum irae divinae.

## 25:16
Vers. 16. AND THEY SHALL DRINK, AND BE TROUBLED, AND BE MAD FROM THE FACE OF THE SWORD) Cf. Isaiah 51, 17. Great, he says, pain will take away all sense and wisdom from them. For this wrath, coming into one place of the soul, becomes madness to those who possess it, says Cleaenetus.

Latin:
