Vers. 16. ET BIBENT, ET TURBABUNTUR, ET INSANIENT A FACIE GLADII) Conf. Esaiam 51, 17. Magnus, inquit, dolor omnem illis sensum ac sapientiam adimet. Αὕτη γὰρ ὀργήτ᾽ εἰς ἕνα ψυχῆς τόπον, Ἐλθοῦσα μανία τοῖς ἔχουσι γίνεται. ait Cleaenetus.

## 25:19
V. 19. TO PHARAOH KING OF EGYPT) See below 43.

Latin:

V. 19. PHARAONI REGI AEGYPTI) Vide infra 43.

## 25:20
Vers. 20.

AND TO ALL GENERALLY) In the Hebrew: ואת כל הערב, which the LXX translate: and all the mixed multitude with him: Just as in Exodus 12, 38, they translated it mixed multitude. Jerome thinks it refers to the foreigners dwelling in Egypt, the Chaldean: all the neighbors. You would not translate it badly as: And all those Arabs, whose enumeration follows.

LAND OF UZ) Concerning which see the beginning of Job & Gen. 10, 23.

LAND OF THE PHILISTINES) Whose towns follow here. Compare Isaiah 14, 29. and what is below 47.

AND THE REMNANT OF ASHDOD) For that region had been exhausted by the siege of Psammetichus, king of Egypt, as we learn from Herodotus in Euterpe. Therefore Gath is not named here, since it was destroyed in the same war.

EDOMITES) See below 49, 7.

MOABITES) See below 48.

AMMONITES) In the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ET UNIVERSIS GENERALITER) In Hebraeo: ואת כל הערב, quod LXX. vertunt: καὶ πάντας τοὺς συμ- μίκτους αὐτῶ: Sicut Exodi 12, 38. verterunt ἐπίμικτον. Pu- tat Hieronymus intelligi peregrinos in Aegypto morantes, Chaldaeus: omnes vicinos. Non male vertas: Et omnes illos Arabas, quorum scilicet enumeratio sequitur.

TERRAE AUSITIDIS) De qua vide initium Jobi & Gen. 10, 23.

TERRAE PHILISTIIM) Quarum oppida sequun- tur hic. Confer Esaiam 14, 29. & quae infra 47.

ET RELIQUIIS AZOTI) Exhausta enim erat il- la regio obsidione Psammetichi Aegyptii regis, ut ex Hero- doto in Euterpe discimus. Ideo Geth hic non nominatur, quippe eodem bello disjecta.

IDUMAEIS) Vide infra 49, 7.

MOABITIS) Vide infra. 48.

AMMONITIS) Ibidem.

## 25:22
Verse 22.

AND THE KINGS OF THE COASTLANDS, WHICH ARE BEYOND THE SEA) Of the sea adjacent to Syria, See below 49, 23.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET REGIBUS TERRAE INSULARUM, QUI SUNT TRANS MARE) Syriae mari adjacentis, Vide infra 49, 23.

## 25:23
Verse 23.

AND DEDAN) Gen. 25, 13.

TEMA) Gen. 25, 15. AND BUZ) Gen. 22, 21. All these are mixed with the Saracens, as Jerome notes here. AND ALL WHO ARE CLIPPED IN THE HAIR) That is, τροχοκόυραδες. Such as the Saracens. See above 9, 26. Lev. 19, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

ET DEDAN) Gen. 25, 13.

THEMA) Gen. 25, 15. ET BUZ) Gen. 22, 21. Hi omnes mixti sunt Sar- racenis, ut hic notat Hieronymus. ET UNIVERSIS, QUI ATTONSI SVNT IN COMAM) Id est, τροχοκόυραδες. Quales Sarraceni. Vide supra 9, 26. Lev. 19, 27.

## 25:24
Verse 24.

AND ALL THE KINGS OF THE WEST, WHO DWELL IN THE DESERT) Better with the Chaldean: The kings of the Arabs dwelling in the desert, that is, the Scenitae, which the Chaldean also adds. See below 49, 28.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET CUNCTIS REGIBVS OCCIDENTIS, QVI HABITANT IN DESERTO) Melius cum Chaldæo: Regibus Arabum habitantium in deserto, id est, Scenitarum, quod & Chaldæus addit. Vide infra 49, 28.

## 25:25
Ver. 25.

AND ALL THE KINGS OF ZIMRI) From Zimri, named in Gen. 25, 2. These are the Zamareni in Pliny 6, 28. AND ALL THE KINGS OF ELAM) Of Elymais. See Gen. 10, 22. below 49, 34. and what we have said in the first book on the Truth of the Christian Religion. AND ALL THE KINGS OF THE MEDES) Kings and petty kings. This pertains to the war of Cyrus against Astyages.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

ET CUNCTIS REGIBVS ZAMBRI) A Zimra- ne, nominato Gen. 25, 2. Hi sunt Zamareni Plinio 6, 28. ET CUNCTIS REGIBVS ELAM) Elymaidos. Vide Gen. 10, 22. infra 49, 34. & a nobis dicta ad librum primum de Veritate Religionis Christianæ. ET CUNCTIS REGIBVS MEDORUM) Regibus & regulis. Pertinet hoc ad bellum Cyri contra Astyagem.

## 25:26
Ver. 26.

AND ALSO ALL THE KINGS OF THE NORTH FROM NEAR AND FROM FAR, EVERY ONE AGAINST HIS BROTHER) Some will be near the Medes, others will be with Astyages, others with Cyrus, and thus they will clash among themselves. The LXX, however, translate צפון elsewhere as North, but here as ἀφηλιώτην (east-southeast), not badly: for that is the wind between the North and the East, in which position are most of the nations of which we are treating here in relation to Judea. AND THE KING OF SHESHACH SHALL DRINK AFTER THEM) The Chaldean also teaches us that the Babylonian King is signified here: nor was any other King to be named by circumlocution besides him, under whose empire Jeremiah was to live for some time: but the Prophet himself, when he was already living in Egypt, explains this name below 51, 41. The Jews, and Jerome with them, think that ששך is בבל, through that permutation of letters which they call ATBASH, that is, where the last letter of the alphabet is put for the first, the penultimate for the second, and so on. But others prefer to derive this name, with the first letter repeated, from שך, which is the name of one of the goddesses of Babylon, on account of whom he who was called by the Hebrews Mishael, was called by the Babylonians Meshach, Daniel 1, 7. From the same source comes Sacchaea, the name of festival days among the same Babylonians, as Athenaeus teaches from Berosus and Ctesias, 4, 10. Chrysostom also mentions it in his 4th book on the Kingdom: calling it Σακκῶν ἑορτὴν. Compare Junius and Tremellius. B. Hülsemann, however, likes that metathesis of letters. Almost all interpreters agree on the King of Babylon, with the sole exception of Lyranus, who understands the King of Egypt as Shishak, but that name is different.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

CVNCTIS QUOQVE REGIBVS AQVILO- NIS DE PROPE ET DE LONGE, UNICUIQVE CONTRA FRATREM SVVM) Illi Medis vicini, alii A- styagi, alii Cyro aderunt, atq; ita inter se collidentur. LXX. vero צפון, alibi Boream vertunt, at hic ἀφηλιώτην, non ma- le: est enim is ventus inter Aquilonem & Eurum, in quo situ sunt pleræque gentes, de quibus hic agitur ad Judæam. ET REX SESACH BIBET POST EOS) Regem Babylonium hic significari etiam Chaldæus nos docet: nec alius Rex per ambages nominandus erat extra hunc, sub cujus imperio aliquamdiu victurus erat Jeremias: sed & pse Propheta, cum jam in Ægypto viveret, nomen hoc ex- plicat infra 51, 41. Judæi & cum eis Hieronymus putant ששך esse בבל, per eam literarum permutationem, quam אתבש vocant, id est, ubi ultima alphabeti litera pro pri- ma ponitur, penultima pro secunda, & contra, atque ita deinceps. At alii malunt hoc nomen, repetita litera prima, derivare à שך, quod nomen alicui Dearum Babylonis, ob quam is, qui Hebræis vocabatur מישאל, dictus est Baby- loniis מישך, Daniel. 1, 7. Indidem σακχαῖα, nomen fe- storum dierum apud eosdem Babylonios, ut ex Beroso & Ctesia docet Athenæus I 4, 10. Meminit & Chrysostomus 4. de Regno: Σακκῶν ἑορτὴν vocans. Conf. Jun. & Tremell. B. Hülsemanno tamen placet illa literarum metathesis. In Regem Ba- byl. consentiunt omnes pene Interpp. solo Lyrano excepto, qui Regem Ægypti שושך intelligit, sed id nomen diversum est.

## 25:28
Ver. 28.

AND WHEN THEY SHALL REFUSE) Translate even if they refuse.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

CVMQVE NOLVERINT) Verte etiam si nolint.

## 25:29
Ver. 29.

BEHOLD IN THE CITY, IN WHICH MY NAME IS CALLED UPON, I WILL BEGIN TO AFFLICT, AND SHALL YOU BE AS INNOCENT AND UNPUNISHED?) If I did not spare the city of Jerusalem, why should I spare you? Compare Ezek. 9, 16. 1 Pet. 4, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ECCE IN CIVITATE, IN QVA INVOCATUM EST NOMEN MEUM, EGO INCIPIAM AFFLIGE- RE, ET VOS QUASI INSONTES ET IMMUNES ERITIS?) Si urbi Hierosolymorum non peperci, cur vo- bis parcerem? Confer Ezech. 9, 16. 1. Pet. 4, 17.

## 25:30
Ver. 30.

HE SHALL ROAR) Like an angry lion. FROM HIS HOLY HABITATION HE SHALL GIVE HIS VOICE) From heaven He shall call those whose works He wishes to use. ROARING HE SHALL ROAR OVER HIS DWELLING PLACE) Against the temple. A SHOUT AS OF THOSE THAT TREAD) Namely, grapes: as in Is. 16, 10. To these are compared the enemies who press out much blood: as in Is. 63, 3. AGAINST ALL THE INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH) Namely, the punishment will reach them later, as above 29. UNTO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH) To the Red Sea and the Caspian.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

RUGIET) Ut leo iratus. DE HABITACULO SANCTO DABIT VO- CEM SUAM) De cœlo vocabit eos, quorum opera uti volet. RVGIENS RVGIET SUPER DECOREM SVVM) Contra templum. CELEUSMA QVASI CALCANTIUM) Scilicet uvas: ut Ef. 16, 10. His comparantur hostes sanguinem multum exprimentes: ut Es. 63, 3. ADVERSVS OMNES HABITATORES TER- RÆ) Nempe ad illos posterius perveniet pœna, ut supra 29. USQVE AD EXTREMA TERRÆ) Ad mare ru- brum & Caspium.

## 25:31
Vers. 31.

HE HIMSELF IS JUDGED WITH ALL FLESH) He shows to the whole world that he does nothing but most justly. See Isaiah 1, 18. Vers. 33. AND THE SLAIN OF THE LORD SHALL BE) Those whom the Lord has caused to be slain. FROM ONE END OF THE EARTH EVEN UNTO THE OTHER END OF IT) Better: From one end of the earth to the other end. Thus the Chaldean here. The LXX also: ἐκ μέρους τῆς γῆς κτέ ἕως μέρους τῆς γῆς. Thus ἀπ’ ἄκρων ἕως ἄκρων, Matt. 24, 31. THEY SHALL NOT BE LAMENTED) As was said of the Jews above 16, 6. 22, 18. AND THEY SHALL NOT BE GATHERED) They shall not be placed in the monuments of their ancestors. See above 8, 2. NEITHER SHALL THEY BE BURIED) They shall not be buried even in the common manner.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

JUDICATUR IPSE CVM OMNI CARNE) Ostendit toti mundo se nihil nisi justissime facere. Vide Esaiam 1, 18. Vers. 33. ET ERUNT INTERFECTI DOMINI) Quos Dominus interfici curavit. A SUMMO TERRÆ USQVE AD SVMMVM EJVS) Melius: A fine terræ ad finem alterum. Ita hic Chal- dæus. LXX. quoque: ἐκ μέρους τῆς γῆς κτέ ἕως μέρους τῆς γῆς. Sic ἀπ’ ἄκρων ἕως ἄκρων, Matth. 24, 31. NON PLANGENTUR) Ut de Judæis dictum su- pra 16, 6. 22, 18. ET NON COLLIGENTVR) Non collocabun- tur in monumentis majorum. Vide supra 8, 2. NEQVE SEPELIENTUR) Ne plebeio quidem more sepelientur.

## 25:33
INTO THE DUNGHILL) See above 8, 2. 9, 21. 16, 3. Ver. 34. HOWL YE SHEPHERDS) Kings and Senators of the Great Sanhedrin. WALLOW YOURSELVES IN ASHES, YE PRINCIPALS OF THE FLOCK) Judges of the cities. AND YOUR DISPERSIONS) That is, that you may be scattered one here, another there. AND YE SHALL FALL LIKE PRECIOUS VESSELS) Like vessels of crystal, or some gem, which are so fragile that, once dashed against the ground, they shatter into pieces. Ver. 35. AND FLIGHT SHALL PERISH FROM THE SHEPHERDS, AND ESCAPE FROM THE PRINCIPALS OF THE FLOCK) For they are the ones usually sought most for slaughter. Ver. 37. AND THE FIELDS OF PEACE ARE CUT DOWN) Better: And the habitations of peace shall be cut down. It is an allusion to the name Salem, or Jerusalem. Ver. 38. HE HATH FORSAKEN HIS COVERT AS A LION) You will connect these better with the preceding in this manner: Because of the burning wrath of God, like a young lion forsaking his den, namely, to seek his prey. FROM THE FACE OF THE WRATH OF THE DOVE) יונה in Hebrew signifies both a dove and a waster, or enemy, as the Chaldean has it here, or, as the Greeks often translate, θλίβοντα, καταδυνασέυοντα. But the word 'sword' is understood. For the sense is: all things desolate from the fury of a hostile sword. That this is implied appears both from the Chaldean here, and from the passages below 46, 16. 50, 16. where the same matter is treated. The LXX here [translate] ἀπὸ προσώπης τῆς μαχαίρας μεγάλης. But others in those two places [translate] ἀπὸ μαχαίρας ἑλληνικῆς, as if it were a feminine adjective from יון, which signifies Greek. For יונת is in Hebrew the genitive feminine. And Jerome says on Zach. 3 that this passage can also be explained in this way. But if anyone considers all these passages, he will see that Greece has no part here. Those who translate 'dove' say that the dove was the military standard of Semiramis: and that it was afterwards always used by the Assyrians. Indeed, we know that doves were sacred among the Syrians, and dedicated to Venus; Diodorus Siculus was also persuaded that Semiramis was named from the cooing of a dove, as if it were from ימיר, which is a song to the Chaldeans, not from שמי רם, the height of heaven. But here and at 46, 16, it is not a question of the Assyrians, but of the Babylonians. And at 50, 16, of the Persians. But who would believe that the standards of conquered nations were taken by the victors? Wherefore that first interpretation is the best.

The Vulgate must therefore be corrected with its 'dove': the face of the wrath of the oppressor is noted according to R. David Kimchi, Pagninus, Arias, Vatablus, Tigurinus, B. Luther, and others.

Latin:

IN STERQVILINIVM) Supra 8, 2. 9, 21. 16, 3. Vers. 34. ULULATE PASTORES) Reges & Senato- res Magni Synedrii. ASPERGITE VOS CINERE OPTIMATES GREGIS) Judices urbium. ET DISSIPATIONES VESTRÆ) Id est, ut dis- pergamini alius alio. ET CADETIS QVASI VASA PRETIOSA) Ut vasa ex crystallo, aut gemma aliqua, quæ ita tenera sunt, ut semel solo allisa, in partes dissiliant. Vers. 35. ET PERIBIT FUGA A PASTORIBVS, ET SALVATIO AB OPTIMATIBUS GREGIS) Illi enim maxime quæri solent ad cædem. Vers. 37. ET CONTRIVERUNT ARVA PACIS) Melius: Et excidentur habitacula pacis. Est allusio ad no- men Salem, sive Jerusalem. Vers. 38. DERELIQUIT QVASI LEO UMBRA- CULUM SUUM) Melius hæc connectes cum superioribus in hunc modū: Propter iram æstuantem Dei, similis leoni jubeni derelinquenti spelæum suum, nempe ut prædam suam quærat. A FACIE IRÆ COLUMBÆ) יונה in Hebræo & co- lumbam significat & vastatorem, sive inimicum, ut hic ha- bet Chaldæus, aut, ut Græci sæpe vertunt, θλίβοντα, καταδυνα- σέυοντα. Subauditur autem vox gladii. Sensus enim est: o- mnia desolata à furore gladii hostilis. Id subintelligi apparet & ex Chaldæo hic, & ex locis infra 46, 16. 50, 16. ubi de re eadem agitur. LXX. hic ἀπὸ προσώπης τῆς μαχαίρας μεγάλης. At alii duobus illis locis, ἀπὸ μαχαίρας ἑλληνικῆς, quasi esset adjectivum fœmininum à יון, quod Græcum significat. Est enim יונת Hebræis gen. fœminini. Et sic hunc quoque lo- cum explicari posse ait Hieronymus ad Zach. 3. At siquis o- mnes hos locos consideret, videbit Græciæ nullas hic esse partes. Qui columbā vertunt, ajunt Semiramidis signū bel- licum fuisse columbam: idq; postea usurpatum semper ab Assyriis. Sane columbas scimus apud Syros sacras fuisse, & Veneri dicatas, Diodoro quoq; Siculo persuasum Semirami- da dictam à pipitu columbæ, quasi esset à ימיר, quod est canticū Chaldæis, non à שמי רם, cœli altitudine. At hic & 46, 16. non de Assyriis, sed de Babyloniis agitur. At 50, 16. de Persis. Quis autem credat victarum gentium signa sumta à victoribus? quare optima est illa prima interpretatio.

Castiganda ergo Vulgata cum sua columba: fa- cies iræ affligentis notatur juxta R. David Kimchi, Pagnin. Ariam, Vatabl. Tigurin. B. Luther. & alios.

## 25:37
AND FROM THE FACE OF THE WRATH OF THE FURY OF THE LORD) If the wrath of Nebuchadnezzar cannot be escaped, how much less that of God?

Latin:

ET A FACIE IRÆ FURORIS DOMINI) Si Nabuchodonosori ira evadi nequit, quanto minus Dei?

## 25:38
Vers. 38. AND ITS KINGS) Jehoiakim, Jeconiah, Zedekiah.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ET REGIBUS EJUS) Joakimo, Jechoniae, Sedeciae.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

The Prophet, predicting the destruction both of the city and of the temple, unless they should be converted, is offered as a captive to the people by the False Prophets and Priests, and is accused of being guilty of death, but is liberated by the princes, with the examples of Micah and Uriah brought forward.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Propheta excidiū prædicens tum urbis, tūtem- pli, nisi conversi fuerint, à Pseudoprophetis & Sacerdotibus captivus offertur populo, mortisq; reus agitur, sed à principibus libe- ratur prolatis exemplis Micheæ & Uziæ.

## 26:2
Ver. 2. STAND IN THE COURT OF THE LORD'S HOUSE) Namely, in the most important one. Ver. 3. IF SO BE THEY WILL HEARKEN) Jerome: He speaks according to our human affection, so that free will may be preserved for man. AND I MAY REPENT ME OF THE EVIL) See above 18, 8. Ver. 5. I SENT UNTO YOU RISING UP EARLY) That is, with assiduous solicitude, as 7, 13. 11, 7. 25, 3. 4. AND YE HAVE NOT HEARKENED) That is, whom you have not hearkened to. Ver. 6. LIKE SHILOH) See above 7, 12.

The destruction of the city of Shiloh consisted not only in the removal of the tabernacle and divine worship, as it seemed to some, but in its horrendous desolation. Compare v. 9. Ver. 8. THE PRIESTS TOOK HIM) Namely, the captain of the temple, who had the right of arresting in the Temple, with the assent of the priests who were present and the Prophets, and with the people complying. Ver. 10. THE PRINCES OF JUDAH) The senators of the great Sanhedrin, to whom belonged the judgment concerning a true or false Prophet. AND THEY SAT IN THE ENTRY OF THE NEW GATE OF THE LORD'S HOUSE) Built by Jotham, 2 Kings 15, 35. 2 Chronicles 27, 3. The Chaldean here says it was to the East. But Maimonides locates the court of this Sanhedrin to the West. But it is no wonder that the place of this assembly was moved in the second Temple. Ver. 11. JUDGMENT OF DEATH IS FOR THIS MAN, BECAUSE HE HATH PROPHESIED AGAINST THIS CITY) By the crime of sedition, namely, because he who prophesies evil for the fatherland often stirs up the people and gives occasions for either seditions or desperate counsels. Compare Acts 6, 13. Ver. 12. THE LORD SENT ME TO PROPHESY AGAINST THIS HOUSE AND AGAINST THIS CITY) House, that is, the Temple. Jerome notes the prudence of Jeremiah, who, since he declares God to be his author, brought forward a sufficiently valid exception against all laws. Then, he does not say 'against the city,' but 'to the city,' signifying that he serves their own interests, [and that] there is still room for repentance. Ver. 14. AS FOR ME, BEHOLD, I AM IN YOUR HAND: DO WITH ME AS SEEMETH GOOD AND MEET UNTO YOU) Here Jerome observes his humility. He acknowledges in the Sanhedrin the power of life and death. Ver. 15. BUT KNOW YE FOR CERTAIN, THAT IF YE PUT ME TO DEATH, YE SHALL SURELY BRING INNOCENT BLOOD UPON YOURSELVES, AND UPON THIS CITY, AND UPON THE INHABITANTS THEREOF) Here Jerome observes his constancy. See, he says, what you are doing. It is easy for you to take away my life. But by doing this, you will not escape the evils of which I have spoken, but rather, for this very reason, they will be the more grievous. In Hebrew: Ye shall give innocent blood against yourselves, that is, you shall contract the guilt of shedding innocent blood. Compare Matthew 23, 35. ch. 27, 25. Ver. 16. THEN SAID THE PRINCES) The greater part of the Sanhedrin. Jerome: The Prophet would have perished, as far as it depended on the Priests and Prophets, if the accusers themselves had had the power of judgment. From which we understand that those who seemed devoted to religion were more cruel toward the Prophet, out of envy of his holiness, than those who were in charge of public necessities. AND ALL THE PEOPLE) Moved by the authority of the Senators, as before they had been moved by the authority of the Priests. Quickly, says this Jerome, the unlearned common people change their opinion once a reason is received. But the grief of the accusers, especially of the Priests and False Prophets, cannot be changed. And therefore, while they accuse and persevere in their accusation, the people are changed. Vers. 17. THEN THERE ROSE UP CERTAIN OF THE ELDERS OF THE LAND) They are the same whom we saw before called שרים, or princes. Vers. 18. MICAH THE MORASTHITE PROPHESIED IN THE DAYS OF HEZEKIAH) Politicians persuade many things by examples. And in the interpretation of laws, the authority of things previously judged is of great value. Morasthi is a village in the tribe of Judah. This is the same Micah whose prophecy exists. ZION SHALL BE PLOWED LIKE A FIELD) Such is that: And the fields, where Troy was. See Mic. 3, 12. Vers. 19. DID HEZEKIAH KING OF JUDAH PUT HIM AT ALL TO DEATH?) By royal right, as a seditious person. AND ALL JUDAH) Or all Judah. That is, the Sanhedrin, holding the place of the whole people and having cognizance of those who claimed to be Prophets. Vers. 20. AND THERE WAS ALSO A MAN THAT PROPHESIED) With the speech of the Senators concluded, the history of those times is added here: from which it can be understood in how much danger Jeremiah was under an impious king. Jerome, Theodoret, Hugo, Thomas, Lyranus, and most others think more correctly that this contrary example was brought forward by the Elders, so that they might be moved to the detestation of such a heinous crime. See B. Hülsemann on this passage. OF KIRIATH-JEARIM) See Josh. 15, 9. Vers. 22. INTO EGYPT) Where Jehoiakim easily obtained even unjust things, because he had given himself into the faith and clientage of the King of Egypt, 2 Kings 23, 34. Jerome observes this. Vers. 23. HE SLEW HIM WITH THE SWORD) As a seditious person, as we just said. The king had the right over such, unless they claimed to be Prophets. But all royal punishment was by the sword. IN THE GRAVES OF THE COMMON PEOPLE) In the burial place of strangers, as the Chaldean has it here. See 2 Kings 24, 6 and Matt. 27, 7. Vers. 24. NEVERTHELESS THE HAND OF AHIKAM THE SON OF SHAPHAN WAS WITH JEREMIAH) For 'therefore', you will more correctly put 'nevertheless': i.e., although one lived under such a bad king, who had already given such an example of his cruelty. Hand, that is, authority. For Ahikam was among the chief men, whose counsel King Josiah, the father of Jehoiakim, had used very much: as can be seen in 2 Kings 24, 12. THAT HE SHOULD NOT BE GIVEN INTO THE HAND OF THE PEOPLE) Kings often, when they wish a man of clear virtue to perish, prefer that it be done through the sedition of the common people (which it is easy for them to incite) rather than by their own command, so that they may enjoy the crime of another without their own hatred.

Latin:

Vers. 2. STA IN ATRIO DOMUS DOMINI) Nempe maxime. Vers. 3. SI FORTE AUDIANT) Hieronymus: No- stro loquitur affectu, ut liberum homini servetur arbitrium. ET POENITEAT ME MALI) Vide supra 18, 8. Vers. 5. MISI AD VOS DE NOCTE CONSVR- GENS) Id est, sollicitudine assidua, ut 7, 13. 11, 7. 25, 3. 4. ET NON AUDISTIS) Id est, quos non audistis. Vers. 6. SICUT SILO) Supra 7, 12.

Destructio urbis Silo non solum in ablatio- ne tabernaculi, & cultus divini consistebat, uti nonnullis visum, sed in horrenda ejus desola- tione. Confer v. 9. Vers. 8. APPREHENDERVNT EUM SACERDO- TES) Nempe ὁ σραληγὸς τῦ ἱερῦ, cui prehendendi in Tem- plo jus erat, assentientibus sacerdotibus, qui aderant & Pro- phetis, plebe autem obsecundante. Vers. 10. PRINCIPES JUDÆ) Senatores magni Sy nedrii, ad quos pertinebat judicium de Propheta vero aut falso. ET SEDERUNT IN INTROITU PORTÆ DOMUS DOMINI NOVÆ) Ædificatæ à Jothamo 2. Regum 15, 35. 2. Paral. 27, 3. Eam fuisse ad Orientem, ait hic Chaldæus. At Maimonides curiam hujus Synedrii ad Occidentem locat. Verum nihil mirum eum conven- tus locum in Templo secundo fuisse translatum. Vers. 11. JUDICIUM MORES EST VIRO HUIC, QUIA PROPHETAVIT ADVERSUS CIVITATEM ISTAM) Crimine nempe seditionis, quia qui male omina- tur patriæ, plebem sæpe commoves, & occasiones dat aut seditionibus, aut desperatis consiliis. Confer Act. 6, 13. Vers. 12. DOMINVS ME MISIT, UT PROPHETA- REM AD DOMUM ISTAM, ET CIVITATEM HANC) Domum, id est, Templum. Notat prudentiam Je- remiæ Hieronymus, qui cum Deum sibi dicat auctorem, sa- tisvalidam protulit exceptionem contra leges omnes, De- inde non dicit contra civitatem, sed ad civitatem, significans se ipsorum utilitatibus servire, locum adhuc esse pœnitentiæ. Vers. 14. EGO AUTEM, ECCE, IN MANIBVS VE- STRIS SUM: FACITE MIHI, QVOD BONUM ET RECTVM EST IN OCVLIS VESTRIS) Hic humili- tatem ejus observat Hieronymus. Agnoscit in Synedrio vitæ & necis potestatem. Vers. 15. VERUNTAMEN SCITOTE ET COGNO- SCITE, QVOD SI OCCIDERITIS ME, SANGUI- NEM INNOCENTEM TRADETIS CONTRA VOS- METIPSOS, ET CONTRA CIVITATEM ISTAM, ET HABITATORES EJVS) Hic constantiam observat Hieronymus. Videre, ait, quid agatis, Facile vobis est mihi vitam adimere. Sed hoc facto adeo mala, de quibus locutus sum, non evadetis, ut etiā ob id ipsum ea futura sint graviora. In Ebr. Dabitis innocentem sang inem contra vos ipsos, id est, contrahetis reatum effusi sanguinis innoxii. Conf. Matth. 23, 35. c. 27, 25. Vers. 16. ET DIXERUNT PRINCIPES) Major pars Synedrii. Hieronymus: Perierat Propheta, quantum fuit in Sacerdotibus & Prophetis, si accusatores ipsi habuissent judicii potestatem. Ex quo intelligimus crudeliores fuisse in Prophetam per invidiam sanctitatis, qui religioni videbantur dediti, quam qui necessitatibus publicis præerant. ET OMNIS POPVLVS) Motus auctoritate Sena- torum, ut ante motus fuerat auctoritate Sacerdotum. Cito, ait hic Hieronymus, vulgus indoctum accepta ratione mu- tat sententiam. Dolor autem accusantium, præcipue Sacerdotum & Pseudoprophetarum, non potest immutari. Et ideo illis accu- santibus, & in accusatione perseverantibus, populus commutatur. Vers. 17. SURREXERVNT ERGO VIRI DE SE- NIORIBVS TERRÆ) Eidem sunt, quos antea שרים, five principes dictos vidimus. Vers. 18. MICHEAS DE MORASTHI FUIT PRO- PHETA IN DIEBVS EZECHIÆ) Politici multa ex- emplis persuadent. Et in legum interpretatione multum va- let rerum ante judicatarum auctoritas. Morasthi vicus est in tribu Juda. Hic est idem Micheas, cujus prophetia exstat. SION QVASI AGER ARABITUR) Tale illud: Et campos, ubi Troja fuit. Vid. Mich. 3, 12. Vers. 19. NUMQVID MORTE CONDEMNAVIT EVM EZECHIAS REX JUDÆ?) Jure regio, tanquam seditiosum. ET OMNIS JUDA) Aut omnis Juda. Id est, Sy- nedrium gerens totius populi vices, & cognitionem ha- bens de iis, qui Prophetas se dicerent. Vers. 20. FVIT QVOQVE VIR PROPHETANS) Absoluto sermone Senatorum additur hic historia illorum temporum: unde intelligi potest, quanto in periculo Jere- mias fuerit sub rege improbo. Hieronym. Theodoret. Hugo, Thomas, Lyran. & pleriq; alii rectius à Senioribus adferri hoc contra- rium exemplum putant, ut ad detestationem tum nefandi facinoris commoverentur. Vid. B. Hül- semann. in h. l. DE CARIATHIARIM) Vide Jos. 15, 9. Vers. 22. IN ÆGTPTUM) Ubi facile etiam iniqua im- petrabat Jojakimus, ideo, quod se in fidem & clientelam re- gis Ægyptii dedisset, 2. Reg. 23, 34. Observatū hoc Hieron. Vers. 23. PERCUSSIT EUM GLADIO) Tanquam seditiosum, ut modo diximus. In tales rex jus habebat, nisi Prophetas se dicerent. Animadversio autem regia omnis per gladium. IN SEPULCRIS VULGI IGNOBILIS) In se- pulchretum advenarum, ut hic Chaldæus. Vid. 2. Reg. 24, 6. & Matth. 27, 7. Vers. 24. IGITUR MANVS AHICAN FILII SA- PHAN FUIT CUM JEREMIA) Pro igitur, rectius po- nes veruntamen: i. e. quanquam sub tam malo rege vive- retur, qui jam tale sævitiæ suæ exemplum dederat. Manus, id est, auctoritas. Erat enim Ahicam inter præcipuos, quo- rum consilio Josias rex pater Jojakimi plurimum usus fue- rat: Ut videre est 2. Reg. 24, 12. UT NON TRADERETUR IN MANVS PO- PULI) Reges sæpe cum perire volunt hominem claræ vir- tutis, malunt id per seditionem vulgi (quam concitare ipsis facile est) quam suo jussu fieri, ut sine suo odio alieno sce- lere fruantur.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII.

The Prophet is ordered to send a yoke to the five kings in Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon, because they are to be subjugated by Nebuchadnezzar, and he preaches about this in the court of Zedekiah, and before the priests and the people, that they should voluntarily surrender themselves to the Babylonian who is certainly coming, and who will carry away the remaining vessels.

Ver. 1. IN THE BEGINNING OF THE REIGN OF JEHOIAKIM) Just as the prophecy which preceded pertains to the people, so does this one: but this one, according to ancient custom, has signs joined together with the words of things.

Although Grotius is otherwise quite ready to invent errors in Hebrew Codices, it is a wonder that he did not here adopt the opinion of Dr. Behm, if indeed it was known to him, that Jehoiakim was put in place of Zedekiah. Chronol. Manuduct. page 246. But there are no reasons why an error should be posited there. For a prophecy is being delivered, not a history: which Jeremiah kept for himself until the reign of Zedekiah, as the Weimar scholars rightly noted. The Prophet is therefore ordered to send a yoke through the envoys who were TO COME to Zedekiah, ver. 3. And he executed this afterwards, and held the sermon to Zedekiah according to that command which he had received at the beginning of King Jehoiakim's reign, and thus eleven years earlier, (Compare v. 1 with 2 Kings 23:36, ch. 24:6, 8, 18) and that is explained in ver. 12, which was done at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, as is clear from a comparison of ch. 28:1. Therefore, the command of the symbolic prophecy by means of the yoke must be distinguished from the execution of this command. That was given under the auspices of the reign of Jehoiakim: Jer. 27:1; this was done at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, v. 12, ch. 28:1.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII.

Jugum mitti jubetur quinq. Regum in Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyro, & Sidone legatis, quod à Nebucadnezare subjugandi sint, deq. eo in aula Sedekiæ, & apud sacerdotes ac populu concionatur Propheta, ut sponte se dedat Babylonio certo venturo, & reliqua vasa abducturo.

Vers. 1. IN PRINCIPIO REGNI JOAKIM) Sicut quæ antecessit vaticinatio, ad populum pertinet, ita & hæc: Sed hæc cum verbis rerum etiam signa conjuncta habet, more antiquo.

QUum admodum facilis alias Grotius sit in fingendis Codicum Ebræorum sphalmatis, mirum quod hic non assumserit D. Behmii sententiam, si modo ei nota fuit, Joakimum positum esse pro Zedekia. Chronol. Manuduct. pag. 246. Sed rationes cur ibi erratum ponatur, nullæ sunt. Nam prophetia, non historia traditur: quam servavit sibi Jeremias usque ad Zedekiæ regnum, ut recte notarunt Vinarienses. Mittere ergo jubetur Propheta jugum per legatos, qui ad Zedekiam VENTURI erant vers. 3. Et exequutus id est postea, atq; concionem ad Zedekiam, juxta illud mandatum habuit, quod sub initium Regis Jojakim, adeoq; undecennio antea acceperat, (Conf. v. 1. cum 2. Reg. 23, 36. c. 24, 6. 8. 18.) idque exponitur vers. 12. quod factum sub initium regni Zedekiæ, uti è collatione cap. 28, 1. liquet. Distinguatur ergo mandatum prophetiæ Symbolicæ per jugum, ab exequutione hujus mandati. Illud datum est sub auspicium regni Jojakim: Jer. 27, 1. hæc sub exordium regni Zedekiæ facta est, v. 12. c. 28, 1.

## 27:2
Ver. 2. MAKE THEE BONDS AND YOKES) The sense is: Make for yourself several wooden yokes, to be sent to the kings, but one to be worn by you yourself, Jeremiah, in the name of the people. See below 28, v. 2, 10, 13. For מוסרות are the two pieces of wood of the yoke, but מט is the third piece of wood, by which the two are connected, as David Kimchi maintains.

Latin:

Vers. 2. FAC TIBI VINCULA ET CATENAS) Sensus est: Eac tibi juga lignea complura, mittenda ad reges, unum vero gestandum tibi ipsi Jeremiæ, nomine populi. Vide infra 28. v. 2. 10. 13. Nam מוסרות sunt duo ligna jugi, מט vero lignum tertium, quo duo connectuntur, ut vult David Kimchi.

## 27:3
Ver. 3. AND SEND THEM TO THE KING OF EDOM, AND TO THE KING OF MOAB, AND TO THE KING OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON, AND TO THE KING OF TYRE, AND TO THE KING OF SIDON) For all these kings were subjugated by Nebuchadnezzar. See below 48, 49.

IN THE HAND OF THE MESSENGERS WHO CAME TO JERUSALEM TO ZEDEKIAH KING OF JUDAH) Namely, to solicit him to defect from the Chaldean. Concerning which see 2 Chron. 36:13.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET MITTES EAS AD REGEM EDOM, ET AD REGEM MOAB, ET AD REGEM FILIORVM AMMON, ET AD REGEM TYRI, ET AD REGEM SIDONIS) Omnes enim hi reges subjugati à Nabuchodonosoro. Vide infra 48. 49.

IN MANU NUNTIORVM QVI VENERVNT JERUSALEM AD SEDECIAM REGEM JUDA) Nempe ut eum sollicitarent ad defectionem à Chaldæo. De qua vide 2. Paral. 36, 13.

## 27:6
Ver. 6. AND NOW THEREFORE HAVE I GIVEN ALL THESE LANDS) Namely, the ones already named, I have given, that is, I have determined to give.

AND THE BEASTS OF THE FIELD HAVE I GIVEN THEM) Horses, so that the Chaldeans may be carried by them; oxen, so that they may pull machines and supplies.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET NUNC ITAQVE EGO DEDI OMNES TERRAS ISTAS) Nempe jam nominatus, Dedi, id est, constitui dare.

ET BESTIAS AGRI DEDI EIS) Equos, ut iis vehantur Chaldæi; boves, ut machinas & commeatus trahant.

## 27:7
Ver. 7. AND ALL NATIONS SHALL SERVE HIM) Those just mentioned.

AND HIS SON) Evil-merodach, who is corruptly called Ἰλκαρόδαμος in Ptolemy.

AND TO HIS GRANDSON) Laborosoarchod, son of the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar. See what we have collected for Book 3 of the Truth of the Christian Religion. Here, in Ptolemy, it is corruptly written Niricassolassar.

And Grotius perverts the words of the Prophet and confuses the persons in Ptolemy's Canon. For the Prophet did not name the son of the daughter, but the son of the son: who was Nabonidus, called Belshazzar by Daniel, the last in the Babylonian Monarchy. But Ptolemy's Niricassolassar, who reigned for 4 years, is different from Laborosoarchod, who was his son and ruled for only nine months, as Berosus and Megasthenes have in their fragments, who note that he obtained the kingdom as a boy; whence, because he ruled for such a short time and as a boy, he was neglected by Ptolemy; nor did God judge his father Niricassolassar worthy to be named here, inasmuch as he occupied the kingdom tyrannically after killing his King and Lord Evil-Merodach: and the Lord wished here to designate only the natural and hereditary successors of Nebuchadnezzar: namely, that not only his son, but also his son's son would rule over the Kingdom, and that the Assyrian Monarchy would have its end in this: which happened in Nabonidus, or as he is called by Daniel, Belshazzar, Dan. 5, 25. seqq. and vers. 30. 31. For almost all interpreters agree that this Belshazzar was the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar, the son of Evil-Merodach. The Prophet only teaches that the peoples will serve the son and the son's son of Nebuchadnezzar: he does not teach whether these are to succeed one another in immediate order, as B. Hülseman rightly says. UNTIL HIS TIME COMES, AND HIS) The time destined for the destruction of Babylon and the kingdom, as below 22, above 25, 12, below 29, 10. Vers. 8. AND WHOSOEVER WILL NOT BEND HIS NECK UNDER THE YOKE OF THE KING OF BABYLON) An explanation of the symbols. Vers. 9. DO NOT LISTEN TO YOUR PROPHETS) Who feigned divine inspiration. AND DIVINERS) τῶν μαντευομένων [those who divine] in Greek. Understand soothsayers. AND DREAMERS) ὀνειρομάντεις [dream-diviners], who promised the interpretation of dreams by human art. AND AUGURS) Predicting future events from the behavior or taste of birds. AND SORCERERS) Who raised up shades by shedding human blood; νεκυομάντεις [necromancers]. Vers. 10. THAT THEY MAY MAKE YOU FAR FROM YOUR LAND) That here is ἐκβατικὸν [consecutive]. So also below 15. Vers. 11. FURTHERMORE, THE NATION THAT SHALL SUBMIT ITS NECK UNDER THE YOKE OF THE KING OF BABYLON) Namely, by making a surrender before hostile force. Vers. 12. AND TO ZEDEKIAH KING OF JUDAH) This is another section, and pertains to another time, but is joined in argument with the previous one. Compare what we said at v. 1. Vers. 16. BEHOLD THE VESSELS OF THE LORD SHALL RETURN FROM BABYLON) Namely those which had been taken away in the time of Jeconiah. 2 Kings 24, 13. It is a hypotyposis, as if the vessels were already on the way to be brought back into the temple. Vers. 18. LET THEM INTERCEDE WITH THE LORD OF HOSTS) Let them obtain by prayers. THAT THE VESSELS WHICH HAD BEEN LEFT BEHIND MAY NOT COME) Which had not been taken away in the time of Jeconiah, namely as follows, the pillars, the sea, the bases, and other things, which Nebuzaradan took away afterwards, 2 Kings 25, 13. See the description of those vessels in 1 Kings 7. AND IN THE HOUSE OF THE KING OF JUDAH) The furniture of the palace. AND IN JERUSALEM) Of other houses, such as were many and opulent in Jerusalem. Vers. 22. UNTIL THE DAY OF HIS VISITATION) That is, of punishment. Until Cyrus, the victor of Babylon, sends back the vessels of the Temple. Ezra 1, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET SERVIENT EI OMNES GENTES) Modo dictæ.

ET FILIO EJUS) Evilmeroducho, qui apud Ptolemæum corrupte Ἰλκαρόδαμος.

ET NEPOTI EJUS) Laborosoardocho filio filiæ Nabuchodonosori. Vide quæ congesfimus ad Librum 3. de veritate Religionis Christianæ. Ptolomæo hic corrupte Νιρικασσολάσσαρος.

Et Prophetæ verba pervertit Grotius, & personas confundit in Ptolemæi Canone. Nam Prophetan on filium filiæ, sed filii nominavit: qui fuit Nabonadius Danieli Baltasar dictus, ultimus in Monarchia Babylonica. Ptolemei vero Niricassolaffor, qui per 4. annos regnavit, diversus est à Laborosoardocho, qui filius illius fuit, & novem tantum mensibus præfuit, ut Berosus & Megasthenes in fragmentis habent, quem puerum regnum obtinuisse notant; unde quia tam brevi tempore, & ceu puer præfuit, neglectus à Ptolemæo est; neq; patrem ejus Niricassolafforum dignum judicavit Deus, quem hic nominaret, utpote qui tyrannice regnum occupavit interfecto Rege ac Domino suo Evilmerodacho: & volebat Dominus hic naturales & hæreditarios successores Nebucadnezaris tantum designare: quod nempe non tantum filius ejus, sed etiam filii filius Regno præfuturus sit, & in hoc fi- nem habitura Monarchia Assyriaca: quod in Na- bonido evenit, vel ut Danieli vocatur, Baltasare Dan. 5, 25. seqq. & vers. 30. 31. Consentiunt enim omnes ferte Interpp. hunc Baltasarem nepotem fuisse Nebucadnezaris Evilmerodochi filium. Propheta solum docet populos servituros fi- lio, & filio filii Nebucadnezaris: num v. hi imme- diato ordine sibi invicem successuri sint, non do- cet, ut recte B. Hülseman. DONEC VENIAT TEMPUS EJUS, ET IPSIVS) Tempus destinatum excidio Babylonis & regni, ut infra 22. supra 25, 12. infra 29, 10. Vers. 8. ET QVICUNQVE NON CURVAVERIT COLLUM SVVM SVB JUGO REGIS BABYLONIS) Explicatio συμβόλων. Vers. 9. NOLITE AUDIRE PROPHETAS VE- STROS) Qui afflatum divinum simulabant. ET DIVINOS) τῶν μαντευομένων Græci. Aruspices intellige. ET SOMNIATORES) ὀνειρομάντεις, qui humana arte somniorum interpretationem pollicebantur. ET AUGURES) Prædicentes futura ex avium ge- stu gustuve. ET MALEFICOS) Qui sanguine humano effuso umbras excitabant; νεκυομάντεις. Vers. 10. UT LONGE VOS FACIANT DE TER- RA VESTRA) Ut hic est ἐκβατικὸν. Sic & infra 15. Vers. 11. PORRO GENS QVÆ SUBJECERIT CER- VICEM SVAM SUB JUGO REGIS BABYLONIÆ) Nempe deditione facta ante vim hostilem. Vers. 12. ET AD SEDECIAM REGEM JVDÆ) Alia est sectio, & ad aliud tempus pertinens, sed argumen- to conjuncta cum superiori. Conf. quæ ad v. 1. diximus. Vers. 16. ECCE VASA DOMINI REVERTEN- TUR DE BABYLONE) Nempe illa quæ Jechoniæ tem- pore ablata fuerant. 2. Reg. 24, 13. Est hypotyposis, ac si vasa jam in via essent, ut reducerentur in templum. Vers. 18. OCCVRRANT DOMINO EXERCI- TVVM) Precibus impetrent. VT NON VENIANT VASA QVÆ DERELL- CTA FVERANT) Quæ tempore Jechoniæ ablata non fuerant, nempe ut sequitur, columnæ, mare, basis & alia, quæ scilicet postea abstulit Nabuzardan 2. Reg. 25, 13. Eo- rum vasorum descriptionem vide 1. Reg. 7. ET IN DOMO REGIS JUDÆ) Supellex palatii. ET IN JERUSALEM) Domuum aliarum, quales multæ atque opulentæ Hierosolymis. Vers. 22. USQUE AD DIEM VISITATIONIS SVÆ) Id est, punitionis. Usque dum Cyrus Babylonis victor vasa Templi remittat. Esdr. 1, 7.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII.

While Hananiah promises the restoration of the people with the taken vessels and breaks Jeremiah's yoke, Jeremiah threatens the people with an iron yoke in place of the wooden one, and announces the death of Hananiah, who expired in the same year. Vers. 1. AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THAT YEAR) In the same year in which I had said those things which precede to Zedekiah. IN THE BEGINNING OF THE REIGN OF ZEDEKIAH) That is, when that evil which I predicted was still far off: for Zedekiah reigned for eleven years. The explanation of Dionysius and Hugo goes there, as also that of Maldonatus and Cornelius. But here is understood the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, in which, namely, he was newly confirmed in the kingdom by Nebuchadnezzar at Babylon, to which he had gone, Jerem. 51, 59, in the fourth year of the reign he had first begun. IN THE FOURTH YEAR, IN THE FIFTH MONTH) Some understand the fourth year of the week of years, which are reckoned from the Sabbatical year. But the Greeks and the Chaldean understood it of the year of the reign of Zedekiah. Nor does that which preceded in the beginning stand in the way, understood as we have said. PROPHET) Who called himself a prophet. Vers. 2. I HAVE BROKEN) I have decreed to break. See below 4. Vers. 3. STILL TWO YEARS OF DAYS) Completed, περιπλόμενοι ἐνιαυτοὶ [revolving years]. The wonderful wickedness of the man, who without any divine revelation he dared to speak so definitely. And so he deservedly paid the penalty. Verse 6. AMEN SIC FACIAT DOMINVS) Amen here means 'would that'. I would wish, he says, that you speak the truth. So also Micah 2:11. So also 1 Kings 1:26, Nehemiah 5:13. Therefore, there is no need to say with Estius that these things were said ironically by the Prophet: much less to say with the Jews, out of ignorance, that Ananias is a false prophet. Compare chapter 27:14, 18, 21, and the response in verse 7 added here. SUSCITET DOMINUS VERBA TUA) I would wish that God may make those words valid. Verse 8. QUI FUERUNT ANTE ME ET ANTE TE) Joel, Amos, Hosea, Isaiah, Micah, Zephaniah, Nahum, Habakkuk, and others. ET PROPHETAVERUNT) Here also that word is redundant in the Hebrew manner. DE PRÆLIO, ET DE AFFLICTIONE, ET DE FAME) Which, however, sometimes did not happen, repentance intervening. Nor does that detract from the authority of the Prophets, who, having performed their duty by warning, saw the fruit of their duty which they most desired. Verse 9. PROPHET WHO HAS PROPHESIED PEACE) Who predicted prosperous things. CUM VENERIT VERBVM EJVS) If the outcome corresponds. SCIETUR PROPHETA QVEM DOMINVS MISIT IN VERITATE) Hananiah had warned the people of nothing regarding conversion, but had simply predicted happy things, which, if they did not happen, he was then detected as a false prophet. Verse 10. CATENAM) That wooden yoke. See above 27:2, and below 13. DE COLLO OMNIUM GENTIVM) Named above 27:3. Verse 13. FACIES PRO EIS) You, Jeremiah, will show [it] to Hananiah. CATENAS FERREAS) An iron yoke, signifying most harsh servitude. An allusion to the passage in Deuteronomy 28:48. Verse 16. HOC ANNO MORIERIS) A prediction well circumscribed by time, such as shows a true Prophet. See what is at Deuteronomy 18:22.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVIII.

Anania populi cum vasis ablatis restitutionem post biennium promittente, & jugum Jere- miæ confringente, Jeremias loco lignei fer- reum jugum populo minatur, ac Ananiæ mortem indicit, qui eodem anno exspiravit. Vers. 1. ET FACTVM IN ANNO ILLO) Eodem anno, quo ista quæ præcedunt Sedeciæ dixeram. IN PRINCIPIO REGNI SEDECIÆ) Id est, cum adhuc longe abesset malum illud quod prædixi: nam per undecim annos regnavit Sedecias. Abit eo explicatio Dionysii, & Hugonis, ut & Maldonati ac Cornelii. Sed intelligitur hic regni Zedekiæ principium, qua sc. is noviter in regno à Nebucadn. confirmatus est Babylone, quo profe- ctus erat Jerem. 51, 59. anno quarto regiminis pri- mum cepti. IN ANNO QUARTO, IN MENSE QVINTO) Quidam annum quartum intelligunt ἑβδομάδος annorum, qui putantur ab anno Sabbatico. Sed de anno regni Sede- ciæ intellexere Græci, & Chaldæus. Nec obstat id quod præcessit in principio, sic intellectum ut diximus. PROPHETA) Qui prophetam se dicebat. Vers. 2. CONTRIVI) Conterere decrevi. Vide infra 4. Vers. 3. ADHVC DVO ANNI DIERVM) Com- pleti, περιπλόμενοι ἐνιαυτοὶ. Mira improbitas hominis, qui sine ulla divina revelatione ita definite loqui ausus est. Ita- que merito poenas dedit. Vers. 6. AMEN SIC FACIAT DOMINVS) Amen hic valet utinam. Velim, inquit, vera dicas. Sic & Michæ 2, 11. Sic etiam 1. Reg. 1, 26. Neh. 5, 13. Non ergo ironice hæc dicta esse à Propheta, opus est cum Estio dicere: nedum cum Judæis ex ignorantia, quod Ananias sit Pseudo-Propheta. Conf. c. 27, 14. 18. 21. & responsum v. 7. hic additum. SUSCITET DOMINUS VERBA TUA) Velim Deus ea rata faciat. Vers. 8. QUI FUERUNT ANTE ME ET ANTE TE) Joel, Amos, Oseas, Esaias, Micheas, Sophonias, Na- hum, Abacuc & alii. ET PROPHETAVERUNT) Hic & illud abundat more Hebraico. DE PRÆLIO, ET DE AFFLICTIONE, ET DE FAME) Quæ tamen interdum non evenere, interce- dente poenitentia. Neque id Prophetis auctoritatem detra- hit, qui functi officio monendo, fructum quem maxime volebant officii sui, videre. Vers. 9. PROPHETA QVI VATICINATUS EST PACEM) Qui prædixit res prosperas. CUM VENERIT VERBVM EJVS) Si eventus respondet. SCIETUR PROPHETA QVEM DOMINVS MISIT IN VERITATE) Hananias de conversione nihil monuerat populum, sed simpliciter res felices prædixerat, quæ si non evenirent, jam pseudopropheta deprehende- batur. Vers. 10. CATENAM) Jugum illud ligneum. Vide supra 27, 2. & infra 13. DE COLLO OMNIUM GENTIVM) Nomina- tarum supra 27, 3. Vers. 13. FACIES PRO EIS) Tu Jeremia, & Hana- niæ ostendes. CATENAS FERREAS) Jugum ferreum, durissimam servitutem significans. Allusio ad locum Deut. 28, 48. Vers. 16. HOC ANNO MORIERIS) Bene tempo- re circumscripta prædictio, qualis verum Prophetam osten- dit. Vide quæ ad Deut. 18, 22.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX.

A letter sent to the captives in Babylon, so that they might arrange their economy as if they were to remain there for many years, and so that they might not have faith in the prophets persuading them otherwise; with the addition of the sign of the death of the false prophets, along with a prophecy against Shemaiah.

Verse 1. THESE ARE THE WORDS OF THE BOOK) This is the tenor of the letter which Jeremiah sent by Elasah and Gemariah: as follows below. FROM JERUSALEM) He sent it from Jerusalem. TO THE REMNANT OF THE ELDERS OF THE CAPTIVITY) To those who were survivors among the exiles from the Great Sanhedrin. Verse 2. AND THE QUEEN) The honorable mother of Jeconiah, 2 Kings 24:15. Verse 3. WHOM ZEDEKIAH KING OF JUDAH SENT TO NEBUCHADNEZZAR) Having now greater faith in the words of Jeremiah after the death of Hananiah, and therefore striving to reconcile Nebuchadnezzar to himself, but in vain. Verse 5. BUILD HOUSES, AND DWELL) Do everything as if you were to remain long in exile. Verse 6. GIVE YOUR SONS WIVES. By which the right of fathers is signified, which parents have in giving their sons and daughters in marriage, as the interpreters note in Genesis 21:21, chapter 24:3, Exodus 34:16. Verse 7. AND MULTIPLY THERE, AND BE NOT FEW IN NUMBER) Better: That you may multiply, and not be diminished. For so it is in the Hebrew. Verse 7. PRAY FOR IT TO THE LORD: FOR IN ITS PEACE THERE WILL BE PEACE FOR YOU) You will be safe under the protection of that kingdom. Verse 8. YOUR PROPHETS WHO ARE IN YOUR MIDST, AND YOUR DIVINERS) Ezekiel 13:3, 6 shows that there were not a few such even in exile. Verse 10. SEVENTY YEARS) Above 25:12. See the fulfillment in 2 Chronicles 36:21, Daniel 9:2. An excellent argument for divine providence, I WILL RAISE UP MY GOOD WORD OVER YOU) I will perform the promises, provided you on your part fulfill the condition,

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX.

Epistola captivis in Babyloniam missa, ut ita Oeconomiam suam instituant, ac si multis annis ibi permansuri essent, ac ne Prophe- tis aliud persuadentibus fidem habeant; addito signo mortis Pseudo-Prophetarum, cum vaticinio contra Semajam.

Vers. 1. HÆC SUNT VERBA LIBRI) Hic tenor est Epistolæ, quam misit Jeremias per Elasam & Gamariam: ut sequitur infra. DE JERUSALEM) Ex Hierosolymis misit. AD RELIQVIAS SENIORUM TRANSMIGRA- TIONIS) Ad illos qui inter exsules superstites erant de Magno Synedrio. Vers. 2. ET DOMINA) Honesta mater Jechoniæ 2. Reg. 24, 15. Vers. 3. QUOS MISIT SEDECIAS REX JUDA AD NABUCHODONOSOR) Ex morte Hananiæ ma- jorem jam fidem habens verbis Jeremiæ, ideoque Nabucho- donosorum sibi studens conciliare, sed frustra. Vers. 5. ÆDIFICATE DOMOS, ET HABITATE) Omnia agite tanquam diu mansuri in exsilio. Vers. 6. DATE FILIIS VESTRIS UXORES. Quo jus Patrum significari, quod habent pa- rentes in elocandis filiis & filiabus, uti Gen. 21, 21. c. 24, 3. Ex. 34, 16. notant Interpp. Vers. 7. ET MULTIPLICAMINI IBI, ET NOLI- TE PAUCI ESSE NUMERO) Melius: Ut multiplicemi- ni, & non diminuamini. Sic enim in Hebræo. Vers. 7. ORATE PRO EO AD DOMINUM: QVIA IN PACE ILLIUS ERIT PAX VOBIS) Tuti eritis sub illius regni præsidio. Vers. 8. PROPHETÆ VESTRI QUI SUNT IN MEDIO VESTRI, ET DIVINI VESTRI) Quales non paucos fuisse etiam in exsilio ostendit Ezechiel 13, 3. 6. Vers. 10. SEPTUAGINTA ANNI) Supra 25, 12. Im- plementum vide 2. Chron. 36, 21. Daniel 9, 2. Egre- gium divinæ providentiæ argumentum, SUSCITABO SUPER VOS VERBUM MEUM BONUM) Præstabo promissa, modo vos ex vestra parte impleatis conditionem,

## 29:11
Verse 11. THAT I MAY GIVE YOU AN END AND PATIENCE) In the Hebrew: an end and hope: that is, an end such as you hope for, hendiadys.

Those promises were not conditional, but categorical. For simply LXX years were defined, in the divine counsel, for the Babylonian captivity, nor did the resolution of the captivity rest upon the piety of the captives, but upon the grace and mere goodness of God the liberator, so that in this part also the type might correspond to the antitype, the liberation from the Babylonian captivity to the liberation from the captivity of Satan, which was promised to the human race without condition. Furthermore, Grotius fixes the beginning of this epoch, as far as it has been possible to observe, at the deportation of Jeconiah; because he loves to follow the parts of Scaliger in these matters. To whom also, with other most excellent chronologists, Seth Calvisius gave assent, as did also Dr. Behmius. For the latter strives at length to prove in his Manuductio Chronologica, book 2, title 2, chapter 2, that the LXX years are to be begun from the spontaneous abduction of Jeconiah and his companions into the Babylonian captivity, which took place at the end of the 7th year of Nebuchadnezzar and the beginning of the 8th. 2 Kings 24:12. And he seeks the argument for this matter from this 29th chapter of Jeremiah, because the Prophet, intending to console the people abducted with Jeconiah, promises them liberation divinely after the passage of LXX years in verse 10, as if by that very fact he were implying that the LXX years of exile were to be begun from the captivity of Jeconiah. For which opinion he also urges that Jeremiah 24, the basket of good figs designates those deported with Jeconiah, and the bad ones those with Zedekiah, and that to the former a return to their homeland is promised. But that opinion, although it may seem very probable, and may please many learned modern chronologists, is not without significant difficulties, from which not even Scaliger himself could extricate himself. On the contrary, however, that opinion rests upon arguments not light, which fixes the beginning of this epoch in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, and his captivity, which year is the first of the expedition of Nebuchadnezzar into Judea. For first, no evident passage from the Scriptures can be brought forward for that beginning from the deportation of Jeconiah. Nor, because the resolution of the captivity is promised in this 29th chapter after the LXX years are finished, is it indicated that the beginning of the same must be established from the time of this promise, unless one were also to wish for that reason, with some of the ancients, to begin the same years from the 13th year of Josiah, because in that year Jeremiah began to prophesy, promising the resolution of the captivity, so that they might end in the first year of Cyrus. Which could indeed seem more likely, because from the 13th year of Josiah to the first of Cyrus there are precisely LXX years, according to the calculation of the ancients. Which opinion, however, is deservedly rejected by Scaliger.

Furthermore, secondly, the term to which of the captivity does not agree. For how will they be able to designate the seventieth year according to this opinion? For the interval of years in the enumeration of Berosus in Josephus, book 1 against Apion, is 66 years and 9 months, from the first year of Nebuchadnezzar to the last year of the last King of the Babylonians. If, therefore, the years are counted from the voluntary deportation of Jeconiah, which took place at the beginning of the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar, the interval from the 6th year of Nebuchadnezzar to the 17th of Nabonidus the Mede will be only 60 years. Ten years are therefore missing. Here B. D. Behm, a chronologist otherwise accurate, twists himself. First, therefore, he seeks a remedy in Sulpicius Severus: that he makes twelve years out of the two years which Berosus, in Josephus, attributes to Evil-Merodach in his reign: But because the fragment of Berosus, which Scaliger holds in the highest esteem, would not be correct in that way, he then betakes himself to other things, with Scaliger leading the way, Decad 1, observation 6. It is uncertain, he says, (1.) whether Cyrus stormed Babylon exactly in the 16th year of Nabonidus the Mede. Indeed, this is not found in Berosus. For he writes thus: that Cyrus, in the 17th year of Nabonidus, set out from Persia, laid waste all the rest of Asia, and then attacked Babylon. Herodotus writes thus in book 1, chapter 177: When Cyrus had made the whole continent (τὰ πάντα τῆς ἠπείρου ὑποχείρια) subject to his rule, he waged war on the Assyrians. Were these things thus accomplished by Cyrus immediately in one year? (2.) Furthermore, historians testify with what great difficulties the siege and storming of Babylon were connected. It is therefore entirely likely that Cyrus spent one or two years in besieging and storming Babylon (a city, according to Herodotus, ὀνομαστοτάτῳ καὶ ἰσχυροτάτῳ). (3.) It is uncertain whether Cyrus released the Jews from captivity in that very year when he had stormed Babylon. Berosus is indeed a witness that Cyrus, after the storming of Babylon, betook himself to Borsippa, a most fortified place (to which the Mede Nabonidus had fled), and there surrounded Nabonidus with a siege. Strabo, book 15, along with Solinus, chapters 62 and 65, are witnesses that Cyrus, after the storming of Babylon, set out for India, and subjugated the city of Capissa, situated on the Indus river, and other places in India. What if he had returned to Babylon afterwards? (4.) What if God had shortened the term of the 70 years of captivity by one or two years by the power of His mercy! These are the words of the blessed D. Behmius there. Thus, therefore, the supporters of the Scaligerian opinion must finally go so far as to render the very truth of the divine promises, made not hypothetically but absolutely, doubtful; that is, they expose oracles, which are above all exception and entirely infallible, to the hazard of controversy. Thirdly, according to the opinion of Scaliger and his followers, the year of the finished captivity turns out to be clearly uncertain: because they cannot determine the time of Babylon being overcome, let alone the captivity being released, concerning which Scaliger in his Notes to the fragments, p. 16, has this: That he did not immediately possess Babylon after Nabonidus was defeated is testified by Herodotus, who says that the citizens, after that slaughter and the flight of Labynitus, having brought many provisions into the city, awaited the siege. Wherefore, having barely possessed Babylon after much time, he hastened to attack Nabonidus, who was keeping himself within the fortifications of Borsippa: and as he was making a surrender, he needed no less time than labor to subdue the rest of Babylonia. These things we have gathered from Herodotus, Berosus, and others. Therefore, the seventy years were truly completed for Babylon then, when the victor Cyrus returned to Babylon. From which time those Chaldeans instituted a new era for the conqueror of all Asia. Whence he rightly says: The God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. And p. 18: He did not take Babylon immediately after Nabonidus was defeated, as is evident from Herodotus. For the citizens awaited the siege, having brought much food into the city. Nabonidus was defeated in the 206th year of Nabonassar. But we do not know the true time of the captured Babylon because the duration of the siege is unknown to us. That it lasted a long time, both reason teaches and Herodotus: Cyrus, he says, ἀπορίῃσί τε ἐνείχετο, ἅ τε χρόνῳ τε ἐγγινομένῳ συχνῷ &c. These are the words of Scaliger. Thus, therefore, according to him, the true time of the captured Babylon is unknown, as is that of the Babylonian empire of Cyrus, during which he could say, The God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. How, therefore, can the true time of the released Babylonian captivity be known? Fourthly, one must invent, according to that opinion of Scaliger, a new beginning for Cyrus. That there are two other beginnings of the reign of Cyrus is not unknown; even though they are very poorly confused by the Jesuit Pererius, as one less experienced in history. The first is of the Persian Kingdom, which is usually designated primarily in secular history. The second is of the Babylonian Kingdom, which is expressed in sacred writings. In which we have the agreement of Dionysius Petavius the Jesuit, the reviser of the Grotius commentaries: who likewise distinguishes between the epoch

of the Persian Kingdom begun by Cyrus, and the epoch of the Babylonian Empire, at the beginning of which the 70 years of Babylonian misery reached their end. See book X, de temp., ch. 14 and 15. But what of Scaliger? He introduced a third beginning of the reign of Cyrus (I am reciting the words of D. Behmius) into the schools of chronologists, arising from the 28th year of the Persian Kingdom of Cyrus, seven years after the Babylonian reign of Cyrus. For he wishes that Cyrus did not release the captivity to the Jews immediately after Babylon was occupied, but from that time when, after Babylon was occupied, he subjugated to himself in India the city of Capissa, situated on the Indus river, and other places in India, as well as the Bactrians, as Strabo, book 15, and Solinus, chapters 62 and 65, testify. Although these things were not once disapproved of by the blessed D. Behmius, he himself later publicly refuted this opinion. For second thoughts are wiser. Thus, therefore, he has it word for word in his Biblical-Historical-Chronological Theme on the first year of Cyrus: There is no need to multiply entities or distinct beginnings of Cyrus without necessity. Simpler and truer is the opinion which establishes that Cyrus, immediately after the Babylonian kingdom was occupied, promulgated to the Jewish kings the permission to return to their homeland, the Jews urging this from the prophecy of Isaiah. These are the words of the blessed D. Behmius, destroying his own [previous] arguments.

Fifthly, the Canon of Ptolemy, which the Scaligerians venerate as divine and hold more precious than any gold, attributes to Cyrus only 9 years; whence it can be gathered that, since Cyrus reigned in Persia for 38 years, that nine-year period must be assigned to his Babylonian Monarchy, so that in the 21 years prior to the Persian Kingdom of Cyrus, Balthazar and Darius the Mede, who was defeated by Cyrus, held the Babylonian Monarchy. Nor do the historians—Herodotus, Trogus, Justin, and others—disagree, from whose accurate comparison it is evident that Cyrus had not set foot into the Babylonian Kingdom before the 20th year of his Persian reign, so far is it from the case that he could have said, The Lord God has given me all the kingdoms of the earth.

Sixth, if the words of our Prophet are accurately weighed in chapter 25, it will be manifest that the years of the pressure and Babylonian captivity are to be numbered from the fourth year of Jehoiakim, or from the first arrival of Nebuchadnezzar in Judea, by which the first abduction was also made, and from which the most recent Kings of the Jews were constituted vassals of Nebuchadnezzar. For not in vain does Jeremiah repeat how from the 13th year of Josiah up to that 4th year God recalled the people to repentance, and how for 23 whole years he himself diligently invited them to repentance by his proclamation; UP TO THIS DAY, says the Prophet, i.e., therefore now is the time of divine judgment, and up to this day divine μακροθυμία (long-suffering) has invited you. What could be clearer than when the Prophet in the fourth year of Jehoiakim testifies that he had taken the cup from the hand of the Lord, to offer it to all nations, but primarily to Jerusalem, and to the other towns of Judea, and to the Princes, that he might give them into solitude and desolation and into a curse, and into a hissing, AS IT IS THIS DAY v. 17. By which it is indicated entirely that at that time that solitude and devastation had already begun; therefore he also fixes there the years of the misery that would last for LXX. v. 11. And let ALL the captives be compared here in c. 29, 4, not only those who had been transported with Jeconiah, but also those from the first abduction, when the term of LXX. years is again sanctioned for them, viz., from their first transportation. Otherwise, those first deported would have had to remain in exile not only for LXX. years, but for many more. Finally, if the King of Babylon was overcome and conquered by Cyrus in the 21st year of the reign of Cyrus, which the Scaligerians do not deny, it must be that the release of the captivity also happened soon after: because the Prophet joins these things in c. 25, 12. When the LXX. years have been fulfilled, I will visit upon the King of Babylon and upon that nation, says the Lord, their iniquity, and upon the land of the Chaldeans; and so at the same time after the seventy years had elapsed, the Holy Spirit predicts both the liberation for the people and the visitation of the King of Babylon. The calculation agrees perfectly with the seventh. For from the 4th year of Jehoiakim until the 23rd year of the Persian Kingdom of Cyrus, which is the first year of his Monarchy, exactly seventy years have passed. For the first year of Nebuchadnezzar in Judea is connected with the 4th year of Jehoiakim, Jer. 25, 1. That first year of Nebuchadnezzar, however, is the 140th Nabonassar year, from which it follows that the 18th year of Nebuchadnezzar is the 159th Nabonassar year, i.e., the eleventh or last year of King Zedekiah: but the first year of the Monarchy of Cyrus will be the 210th Nabonassar year. Eighth: The calculation can be started thus according to the monarchs of Babylon; since the first year of Nebuchadnezzar concurs with the 4th year of Jehoiakim. But he reigned for 43 years, as Berosus and the Mathematical Canon testify. Evil-Merodach reigned for two years, as Berosus and the canon of Ptolemy testify again from the edition of Calvisius. Neriglissar for four years, Laborosoarchod, or Belshazzar, according to Berosus, reigned alone for 9 months, Nabonidus or Darius the Mede presided over the Kingdom for 17 years by the consent of all; which years collected make 66. Thus 4 years are missing. The reason for this is that Nebuchadnezzar reigned for four years with his parent, which Ptolemy did not count in the years of his reign; about which it is helpful to hear the blessed D. Behmius: It is to be observed, he says in the cited place, Th. 26, that in connecting the years of Nebuchadnezzar with the Nabonassar years, there is a difference of four years between Biblical History and the Mathematical canon of Ptolemy. The former connects the first year of Nebuchadnezzar with the 140th Nabonassar year. The latter with the 144th Nabonassar year. This is the cause of the difference. Biblical history begins the years of Nebuchadnezzar immediately from his first arrival into Syria and Judea, while his parent Nabopolassar was still living, by whom he was sent against the rebels, as Berosus testifies in his golden fragment found in Josephus and Eusebius. But the canon of Ptolemy begins the years of Nebuchadnezzar only from the death of his parent, who reigned for 21 years, from the 123rd to the 144th Nabonassar year. Hence it appears that Nebuchadnezzar, according to the guidance of Scripture, reigned for four years with his parent. And because Ptolemy attributes 43 years to Nebuchadnezzar after the death of his parent, it must be said that the same King of Babylon reigned for 47 years according to Biblical history, four with his parent, 43 alone. This, noted with accurate diligence, contains the foundation of the chronological connection of the Nabonassar Epoch with the Biblical years and the Mathematical canon of Ptolemy. Thus far the blessed D. Behmius. Eusebius also agrees in his Chronicles. for if 60 years are counted from the eleventh year of Zedekiah to the last year of Cyrus, then the interval to the 22nd year of Cyrus will be 52 years. Add to these the 18 years from the first arrival of Nebuchadnezzar to the 11th year of King Zedekiah, and 70 years result. The computation can also be established thus: The destruction of Jerusalem falls, according to Eusebius, in the second year of the 47th Olympiad or the 186th of Iphitus. For the first year of Cyrus is the first year of the 55th Olympiad, or the 217th of Iphitus. We have, therefore, an interval from the destruction to the first year of Cyrus of 32 years; add to these the 22 years of Cyrus, and 53 result. But from the 4th year of Jehoiakim to the destruction of Jerusalem, 17 years are counted, namely the 7 remaining years of Jehoiakim (who reigned for 11 years), the 3 months of Jehoiachin, and the ten years of Zedekiah, because the eleventh concurs with the year of the destruction. Add what Calvisius has on the interval between the destruction of Jerusalem and the beginning of the Babylonian Cyrus, Isag. Chron. c. 33, page 183. But those older chronologists are entirely concerned with demonstrating that this difference is of thirty solid years, and that Cyrus began in the 31st year after the destruction of Jerusalem, and they prove this with several arguments: nevertheless, we can teach the same from the Sabbatical years. Cyrus began, as all historians testify, in the 189th year of Nabonassar, in the third year after a celebrated Sabbatical year; for add three and cast out the sevens, and in the remainder there are three. Now the year of the capture of Jerusalem falls in a Sabbatical year, and from here the following Sabbatical years can be correctly counted. The twenty-eighth year, therefore, after the capture of Jerusalem is also a Sabbatical year, just as the thirty-fifth is. But Cyrus began in the third year after a celebrated Sabbatical year. Therefore he began either in the thirty-first after the capture of Jerusalem, or the thirty-eighth. He could not have begun in the thirty-eighth year, because it would follow that he defeated Darius, King of the Persians, in the eleventh or twelfth year of his reign, when nevertheless the war was appearing most at that time, as historians testify regarding Croesus. Subtract thirty-eight years from the 49 years of the distance between the destruction of Jerusalem and the defeat of Darius, and eleven years remain. Since, therefore, Cyrus did not defeat Darius in the twelfth year of his reign but after another seven years, as the Sabbatical years show, it is necessary that he began in the thirty-first year after the destruction of Jerusalem. If the thirty-first year after that destruction is the 189th year of Nabonassar, in which Cyrus began, then that destruction happened in the 188th year of Nabonassar, a Sabbatical year, as Ezekiel, Clement of Alexandria, Eusebius, Herodotus, and also the distance of 13 years of Hezekiah, and Berosus maintain.

Ninth: Thus its own reason will be established in the first year of Cyrus, 2 Chron. 36, Ezra 1, which according to Scaliger's opinion can be rendered as nothing. For if you say that the captivity was released in the first year of Cyrus, and you understand the first year as nothing other than the Epoch of the released captivity, that will be ridiculous, and the same will be designated by the same. And how can the first year of Cyrus be understood otherwise than as the first year of the reign of Cyrus, according to the customary phrase of Scripture? Indeed, how could the first year after the defeat of Nabonidus in the annals of the Persians themselves, which were kept in the archives of the Empire, have been called the first year of Cyrus, not from the empire of Cyrus, but from the released captivity of the Jews! For thus it is read in those, Ezra 6, 3: In the first year of Cyrus the King, Cyrus the King decreed that the house of God should be built. What is more manifest than that the first year of the Monarchy of Cyrus is designated there? Add the response of the Israelite people, Ezra 5, 13. In the first year of Cyrus King of Babylon, King Cyrus proposed an edict that the house of God should be built: Where everyone sees that the first year of Cyrus is proposed as that of the King of Babylon, or of his Babylonian Monarchy. But concerning this first year of Cyrus, we have said more at the place 2 Chron. 36.

Tenth, Scaliger is not consistent with himself, when in book 6 of De Emendatione Temporum he places the beginning of the 70 years in the first year of Jeconiah, when Ezekiel was carried away with the King and others: and not in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, when Daniel migrated to Babylon with others: But in book 5 he says that Daniel and Ezekiel were brought to Babylon together, no otherwise than if the captivity of Jeconiah and Jehoiakim were one and the same.

Eleventh, we add authorities for this opinion, not only of the Ancients, and the Beroaldists, and others, especially of Dionysius Petavius, the most celebrated Chronologist, James Ussher, as also Robert Baillie, Oper. Chron. & Hist. lib. 1, p. 91. From Jeremiah ch. 25, 10, 11, 12, it appears that their beginning is to be taken from the first year of Nebuchadnezzar; whether finished or current, it matters not; namely, nineteen years before the temple was destroyed and the epoch closed at hand, so that after the destruction of the city and temple, only fifty-one of those 70 years remain, so that it would have been easy for many to have seen both temples, that of Solomon overthrown and the foundations of Zerubbabel laid: which on p. 144, quest. 2, Bailius pursued more fully. But also from the Scaligerian works of the blessed D. D. Behmius. Who, in his Chronological Manuduction, Book 2, Title 2, chapter 3, indeed rejected this opinion in this way: The third year of Jehoiakim is the third year of the 42nd Olympiad. Or the 167th Olympiadic year, according to the reckoning of the ancients; The twentieth of Cyrus is the first of the 60th Olympiad, or the 237th Olympiadic year. If 167 are subtracted from this number, 70 remain. But even this opinion of the ancients (which some modern chronologists, Beroaldus, and others follow) does not hold. For although in the third year of Jehoiakim many of the Jews were led away into Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, King of the Babylonians (among whom was also Daniel, ch. 1, 6), yet Scripture nowhere begins the 70 years of captivity from that captivity, because at that time only adolescents of royal seed and some of the Jewish courtiers were led away, Dan. 1, verses 3, 4. Thus he in the Chronological Manuduction, published in the year 1617. But afterwards in his old age, and after 25 years, having been taught more correctly by more accurate investigation, he did not hesitate to retract that former opinion of his, and to assert ours. Such was the candor of the man; whom I remember St. Augustine often praising, because he did not hesitate to write his books of Retractions; whose example, therefore, he himself also followed eagerly, especially in his Chronological works. It will be helpful to adduce from his cited disputation of the year 1643, held publicly at Königsberg, his own words and foundations, especially for the sake of those who followed the blessed D. Behmius, and still follow him, in assigning the term of the Babylonian captivity according to the Chronological Manuduction: ignorant, as it appears, that he himself had embraced another opinion in later years. They depart, he says, loc. citat. Th. XXI, from the prophet Jeremiah, who begins the 70 years of Babylonian oppression from the 4th year of Jehoiakim and the first arrival of Nebuchadnezzar into Judea, ch. 25. Did not the leading away of the Jews into Babylon begin immediately from that time? Were not the last three Jewish Kings, Jehoiakim, Jeconiah, and Zedekiah, made vassals of the Babylonian Kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar from that time? Did not Judea become tributary to the Babylonian King from that time? Would that those men, having finally laid aside their error, might be wise! Having therefore retained (so he continues) the Eusebian interval of 30 years, from the 4th of Jehoiakim to the first of the Persian Kingdom of Cyrus is an interval of 48 years; with 22 years added, they become 70. Whence we see that Cyrus obtained the Babylonian Kingdom in the 22nd year of his Persian Kingdom, and at that very time released the Jews from captivity, not in the first year of the Persian Kingdom of Cyrus, as Pererius imagines and raves along with many others. Cyrus therefore reigned after the Babylonian Kingdom was occupied for 9 more years, which agrees exactly with the mathematical canon of Ptolemy. From these premises we proceed in this manner. The first year of his Babylonian Kingdom of Cyrus in the mathematical canon of Ptolemy is concatenated with the 210th Nabonassarean year. With the 70 years of the Babylonian captivity subtracted, 140 Nabonassarean years remain. But the years of the captivity are to be begun from the 4th of Jehoiakim, or from the first arrival of Nebuchadnezzar into Syria and Judea, as witnessed by Jerem. ch. 25, 1, as was just noted. The fourth year of Jehoiakim therefore corresponds with the 140th Nabonassarean year shows us an excellent artifice of the connection of the Nabonassarean Epoch with the Biblical years. If the 140th Nabonassarean year is the first of Nebuchadnezzar in Scripture according to Jeremiah. Therefore, the 18th of the same, concatenated with the year of the extermination of the Solomonic temple, will be the 158th Nabonassarean year, exactly corresponding with the 11th of Zedekiah, the last King of Judah. The same artifice is exhibited to us by the Eusebian placement of years, which from the 11th of Zedekiah, or the total destruction of the Solomonic temple, to the last year of Cyrus, has an interval of 60 solid years. The last year of Cyrus in the aforementioned canon of Ptolemy is the 218th Nabonassarean year; with the 60 Eusebian years subtracted, the 158th Nabonassarean year remains, to be connected in truth with the last year of Zedekiah. With this Eusebian interval standing as clearly legitimate and firm, an undoubted argument is derived from it that the term FROM WHICH the 70 years of the Babylonian captivity are to be reckoned is not the total destruction of the Solomonic temple, but one must ascend to the earlier 4th year of Jehoiakim, or the first of Nebuchadnezzar in Scripture. The same concatenation can be confirmed from the passage of Ezekiel ch. 1, 1, which connects the 30th year with the 5th from the spontaneous transportation of Jeconiah: It pleases us, however, to follow the opinion of those who establish that the Prophet, then living in Babylon, denotes the thirtieth year of some Babylonian King, by the example of Nehemiah ch. 1, 1. But that King is not Nebuchadnezzar. For the 5th year from the deported Jeconiah corresponds with the 13th of Nebuchadnezzar in Scripture. Therefore, Nebuchadnezzar's parent will be the one called Nabullassar or Nabopolassar (witnessed by Berosus, Josephus, Ptolemy, Eusebius). His reign arises from the 123rd Nabonassarean year. For his fifth year, confirmed by a celestial character, an eclipse of the moon according to Ptolemy, is the 127th Nabonassarean year. Hence we reason thus: If the first year from Nabopolassar is the 123rd Nabonassarean year: therefore the thirtieth from the same is the 152nd Nabonassarean year, corresponding with the 5th year from the deported Jeconiah, which is at the same time the 5th of Zedekiah. If this is so, his eleventh year will be the 158th Nabonassarean year. Than which concatenation nothing is more pleasant, nothing more exact, nothing more solid. All these things were by D. Behmius, who is now among the saints. We also add the artifice of the connection of the Nabonassarean Epoch with the Biblical years and the mathematical canon of Ptolemy. The artifice, he says, is in this way: Ptolemy in his canon counts 66 years from the first of Nebuchadnezzar to the first of the Babylonian Kingdom of Cyrus exclusively. He attributes 43 years to Nabocolassar (who is Nebuchadnezzar in the Bible). Two to Ilvarodamus (Evil-merodach). Four to Nericassolassar (Belshazzar). Nabonnidus the Mede (Darius the Mede) 17. The sum is 66. With 4 years added according to the Biblical numbering of Nebuchadnezzar's years, they become 70 years. Whence it clearly shines forth that the term A QUO of the 70 years of the Babylonian captivity is not the πα- νωλεθρίαν or extermination of the Solomonic Temple, but one must ascend 18 years earlier, to the fourth year of Jehoiakim, which corresponds, according to the Biblical concatenation, with the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, as Jeremiah testifies in chapter 25, 1. Which passage is to be noted with accurate diligence. Finally, the blessed one concludes in this way: In the truth of the matter, therefore, from the destruction of the Hierosolymitan Temple to the release of the captivity there are 52 years, neither more nor fewer. The year of the destruction of the Solomonic temple corresponds with the 158th Nabonassarean year, as was noted a little before. The captivity of the Jews was therefore released in the 210th Nabonassarean year, which is the first year of the Babylonian Kingdom of Cyrus in the divine canon of Ptolemy. With eight years of Cyrus added, they become 218 years. And yet the 218th Nabonassarean year is the year of Cyrus's death. For the seventh year of Cambyses is marked in the celestial character, by an Eclipse of the Moon in Ptolemy, as the 225th Nabonassarean year. Would that at last the learned, having rejected the dreams of Annianus and the errors of Funccius, would embrace the true and firm concatenation of the Nabonassarean Epoch with the Biblical years! For with this concatenation established, the two other more famous Epochs, of the Olympiad and of the City, can be connected with the Biblical years with easy effort. Which was to be briefly demonstrated. These things thus B. D. Behmius word for word, which, on account of his followers and disciples, we wished on this occasion to bring into the light, for the sake of sacred Chronology: since in these, and others, he confirmed that proverb by his own example: Day teaches day. Verse 12. YOU SHALL CALL UPON ME) That is, call, go, pray, seek. Verse 13. WHEN YOU SHALL SEEK ME WITH ALL YOUR HEART) With a sincere mind. Verse 15. BECAUSE YOU HAVE SAID, THE LORD HATH RAISED UP PROPHETS FOR US IN BABYLON) A transposition. The sense is: After you have said in Babylon, God had raised up for us (already long ago, of course) prophets: truthful ones, indeed, who had predicted all these things which have happened to us.
