Compare Daniel 9, 6. 12. Verse 16. UPON THE THRONE OF DAVID) That is, concerning Zedekiah. Verse 17. THE SWORD AND THE FAMINE, AND THE PESTILENCE) Above 15, 2. LIKE BAD FIGS) As above 24, 8. Verse 18. AND INTO ASTONISHMENT AND A HISSING) Above 18, 16. 19, 8. 25, 18. Verse 19. RISING UP EARLY) Above 25, 3. Verse 21. HE SHALL SMITE THEM) He shall kill them, by fire, as follows. WHOM THE KING OF BABYLON ROASTED IN THE FIRE) קלה is to roast, as the Chaldean has it here. Casting into a furnace was a punishment among the Chaldeans, Dan. 3, 6. Add Amos 4, 2. Verse 23. FOR THAT THEY HAVE DONE FOLLY IN ISRAEL.) A crime, a foul thing, as the Chaldean has it here. By a Greek noun, ἀνομίαν. AND HAVE COMMITTED ADULTERY WITH THE WIVES OF THEIR NEIGHBORS) The Jews wish these to be the same ones who laid snares for the modesty of Susanna: for they think that history to be true: but not everything that we have in the Greek: and it is more credible that they were punished by the king than by the exiled people. If anyone is delighted by fables, let him see what the Gemara narrates concerning the daughter of the Babylonian king, solicited to adultery by that Ahab and Zedekiah, at the title concerning the Sanhedrin, chapter כל ישראל. Jerome indicated more than once that that narrative about Susanna is a fable: and those elders are said to have been stoned, but these were roasted by fire, v. 22. I AM JUDGE AND WITNESS) In the Hebrew: I know and I testify. Verse 24. AND TO SEMEIAH THE NEHELAMITE YOU SHALL SAY) This is to be separated from the preceding. For Jeremiah received this command after the envoys had returned. Verse 25. FOR THAT YOU HAVE SENT IN YOUR NAME LETTERS) That is, epistles to Zephaniah and others. In your name: that is, without my order. Thus ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ is taken in John 5, 43. TO ZEPHANIAH) Who was סגן, that is, second to the High Priest, and his vicar. 2 Kings 25, 18. Verse 26. THE LORD HATH MADE YOU PRIEST INSTEAD OF JEHOIADA THE PRIEST) That is, you ought to imitate the zeal of Jehoiada, concerning whom 2 Kings 11, 18. 2 Chronicles 23, 17. THAT YOU MAY BE A RULER IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) That you may preside over the other priests and command them to seize pseudo-prophets, such as Jeremiah is, by the authority of the captain of the temple. A MAN THAT IS MAD) Who is not incited by the spirit of God, but by demons. See 2 Kings 9, 11. INTO THE STOCKS AND INTO THE PRISON) The former word is the same as above 20, 2. The other is צינק, as most of the Hebrews judge, an iron manacle. ענק signifies to be narrow to the Arabs. There are those who, led by the etymology, think that the punishment of the boats is signified, of which Plutarch makes mention in Artaxerxes. But that punishment was unknown to the Hebrews, and the priests had the right to seize in the Temple, not to punish. Verse 29. ZEPHANIAH THE PRIEST THEREFORE READ THIS BOOK IN THE EARS OF JEREMIAH THE PROPHET) Not wishing to seize one unheard. Verse 32. THERE SHALL NOT BE FOR HIM A MAN SITTING IN THE MIDST OF THIS PEOPLE) That is, dwelling. AND HE SHALL NOT SEE THE GOOD THAT I WILL DO TO MY PEOPLE) The return to the fatherland. BECAUSE HE HATH SPOKEN PREVARICATION AGAINST THE LORD) He hinders the conversion of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 11. UT DEM VOBIS FINEM ET PATIEN- TIAM ) In Hebræo: finem & spem: id est, finem qualem speratis, ἐν διὰ δυοῖν.

PRomissa illa non fuere conditionata, sed cate- gorica. Nam simpliciter LXX. anni definiti erant, in consilio divino, captivitati Babylonicæ, neq; solutio captivitatis nitebatur pietate captivo- rum, sed gratia & bonitate mera Dei liberatoris, ut hac etiam parte typus congrueret antitypo, libera- tio è captivitateBabylonica liberationi è captivita- te Satanæ, quæ generi humano citra conditionem promissa erat. Cæterum Epochæ hujus initium, quantum observare licuit, figit Grotius in deporta- tione Jechoniæ; quia in hisce Scaligeri partes sequi amat. Cui etiam cum aliis Chronologis præstan- tissimis assensum præbuit Sethus Calvisius, ut & Dn. D. Behmius. Hic enim prolixe conatur probare l. 2. Manuduct. Chronol. Tit. 2. c. 2. annos LXX. in- choandos esse à spontanea Jechoniæ & sociorum ejus in Babylonicam captivitatem abductione, fa- cta anno Nebucadnezaris 7. finiente,& 8. ineunte. 2. Reg. 24, 12. Atque argumentum ejus rei petit ex hoc capite 29. Jer. quod Propheta populum cum Jechonia abductum consolaturus, ei post LXX. an- norum decursum liberationem divinitus promit- tat versic. 10. quasi eo ipso LXX. annos exilii, à Je- choniæ captivitate incipiendos esse innueret. In quam sententiam etiam urget, quod Jer. 24. Cala- thi ficuum bonorum deportatos cum Jechonia, malo- rum cum Zedekia, designent, atq; istis reditus in pa- triam promittatur. At sententia illa, etsi valde pro- babilis videatur, ac multis eruditis Chronologis modernis placeat,non caret insignibus difficultati- bus, ex quibus ne Scaliger quidem ipse sese expe- dire potuit. Ex adverso vero argumentis non levi- bus nititur sententia illa, quæ initium hujus Epo- chæ figit in anno quarto Jojakim, ejusque captivatio- ne, qui annus primus est expeditionis Nabuchodono- soris in Judæam. Nam primo nullus evidens locus è Scripturis adferri potest pro initio illo à deporta- tione Jechoniæ. Neque enim quia hoc 29. capite promittitur finitis LXX. annis solutio captivitatis, etiam initium ejusdem ab hujus promissionis tem- pore constituendum esse indicatur, nisi etiam quis ideo cum Veteribus nonnullis ab anno XIII. Josiæ, quia illo Jeremias captivitatis solutionem promit- tens, vaticinari cœpit, eosdem annos inchoare vel- let, ut finiantur in anno Cyri primo. Quod eo ve- ro similius videri posset, quia à 13. Josiæ anno ad primum Cyri præcise sunt LXX. anni, stante vete- rum alligatione. Quæ vero sententia merito à Scaligero reprobatur.

Porro secundo, non convenit terminus ad quem captivitatis. Quomodo enim septuagesimum an- num designare poterunt juxta hanc sententiam? Nam intervallum annorum in Berosi numeratione apud Josephum l. in Appion. est LXVI. annorum IX. mensium, à primo Nebucadnezaris ad ultimum ultimi Babyloniorum Regis annum. Si itaque an- ni, à spontanea Jechoniæ deportatione, facta anno Nebucadnezaris octavo ineunte, numerentur, in- tervallum à VI. Nebucadnezaris anno, ad XVII. Nabonidi Medi, LX. tantum annorum erit. De- sunt ergo X. anni. Torquet hic sese B. D. Beh- mius, Chronologus cæteroquin accuratus. Primo ergo in Sulpitio Severo quærit remedium: quod is ex duobus annis, quos Berosus apud Josephum Evilmerodacho in regno tribuit, duodecim faciat: Sed quia ita Berosi fragmentum, quod Scaliger in summo habet pretio, non recte habebit, ad alia de- inde sese, præeunte Scaligero, recipit Decad. 1. ob- servat. VI. Incertum, inquit, (1.) est, num Cyrus sta- tum anno XVI. Nabonnidi Medi Babylone expugnarit. Siquidem id in Beroso non habetur. Sic enim scribit: Cyrum anno XVII. Nabonnidi ex Perside profe- ctum, reliquam omnem Asiam vastasse, tum Baby- loniam aggressum. Herodotus ita scribit lib. 1. cap. 177. Cum Cyrus continentem universam (τὰ πάντα τῆς ἠπείρε ὑποχείρια) suæ ditionis fecisset, Assyriis bellum intulit. Siccine hæc uno statim anno â Cyro peracta? (2.) Quantis præterea cum diffi- cultatibus Babylonis obsidio & expugnatio conjuncta fuerit, testantur Historici. Omnino ergo verosimile, Cyrum unum vel alterum annum in obsidenda & ex- pugnanda Babylone (civitate secundum Herodotum ὀνομαστοτάτῳ καὶ ἰσχυροτάτῳ) insumpsisse. (3.) In- certum, num Cyrus eo statim anno, cum Babylonem expugnasset, Judæis captivitatem laxarit. Berosus sane testis est, Cyrum post Babylonis expugnatio- nem, ad Borsippum locum munitissimum (quo Na- bonnidus Medus confugerat) se contulisse, ibidem- que Nabonnidum obsidione cinxisse. Strabo lib. 15. cum Solino cap. 62. & 65. testes sunt, Cyrum post Ba- bylonis expugnationem in Indiam profectum, Capis- sam urbem ad Indum fluvium sitam, & alia Indiæ lo- ca sibi subjugasse. Quid si postea Babylonem reversus fuiffet? (4.) Quid si Deus terminum LXX. annorum captivitatis vi suæ misericordiæ uno & altero anno de- curtasset! Hæc ibi B. D. Behmius. Ita ergo eo tan- dem abeundum est Scaligerianæ sententiæ fautori- bus, ut ipsam promissionum divinarum, non hypo- thetice sed absolute factarũ, veritatem dubiam red- dant, hoc est, oracula omni exceptione superiora, & prorsus infallibilia aleæ controversiæ exponant. Tertio juxta Scaligeri & asseclarum sententiam, incertus plane evadit annus finitæ captivitatis: quia non possunt determinare tempus Babylonis supe- ratæ, nedum solutæ captivitatis, de quo Scaliger in Notis ad fragmenta p. 16. ita habet: Victo Nabonni- do nõ statim potitum fuisse Babylone, testis Herodotus, qui dicit cives post cladem illam & fugam Labyniti, comportatis in urbem multorum cibaris obsidionem expectasse. Quare post multum temporis vix tandem Babylone potitus, ad Nabonidum intra Borsippi muni- menta sese continentem, oppugnandum contendit: quo deditionem faciente, ad reliqua Babyloniæ debel- landa non minore temporis spatio, quam labore illi opus fuit. Hæc ex Herodoto, Beroso & aliis collegimus. Itaq; vere tunc completi fuerunt septuaginta anni Ba- byloni, cum victor Cyrus Babylonem regressus est. Ex quo tempore novam æram illi Chaldæi instituerunt to- tius Asiæ triumphatori. Unde merito dicit: Deus cœli dedit mihi omnia regna terræ. Et pag. 18. Non statim victo Nabonido Babylonem cepit, ut patet ex Herodoto. Nam commeatu multo in urbem impor tato, obsidionem cives expectarunt. Victus est Nabo- nidus anno Nabonassari 206. Verum autem captæ Babylonis tempus ideo nescimus, quia duratio obsidio- nis nobis incomperta. Quod autem multum temporis duraverit, & ratio docet, & Herodotus: Κῦρος δὲ, inquit, ἀπορίῃσί τε ἐνείχετο, ἅ τε χρόνᴎτε ἐγγινο- μένᴎ συχνᴎ &c. Hæc Scaliger. Sic ergo juxta ipsũ, nescitur verum tempus captæ Babylonis, & imperii Babylonici Cyri, quo dicere poterat, Deus cœli de- dit mihi omnia Regna terræ. Quomodo itaq; verũ tempus solutæ captivitatis Babylonicæ sciri potest? Quarto fingere oportet, juxta illam Scaligeri sententiam, novum Cyri initium. Duo alias initia regni Cyri esse, non ignotum est; etsi ea à Jesuita Pererio pessime confundantur, utpote in historia minus exercitato. Primum est Regni Persici, quod in historia exotica imprimis designari solet. Alte- rum est Regni Babylonici, quod in sacris exprimitur. In quo habemus consentientem Dionysium Peta- vium Jesuitam, Grotianarum commentationum revisorem: qui distinguit pariter inter Epocham

Persici Regni à Cyro initi, & Epocham Babylonici Imperii, in cujus principio LXX. anni Babylonicæ miseriæ finem assecuti sint. Vid. l. X. de temp. c. 14. & 15. At quid Scaliger? Tertium regni Cyri ini- tium (D. Behmii verba recito) is introduxit in Scho- las Chronologorum, exurgens à 28. anno Cyri Persici Regni septennio post à Babylonico Cyri regno. Vult enim Cyrum non statim ab occupata Babylone Judæis captivitatem laxasse, sed ab eo tempore, quo post occu- patam Babylonem in India Capissam urbem ad Indum fluvium sitam, & alia India loca, ut & Bactrianos sibi subjugavit, Strabone teste l. 15. & Solino cap. 62. & 65. Quæ etsi non improbata olim fuerint B. D. Behmio, hanc tamen sententiam ipse postmodum publice refutavit. δευτέραι enim φροντίδες σοφω- τέραι. Ita ergo αυ᾿τολεξεὶ habet in Themate Biblico- Historico-Chronologico de primo anno Cyri: Non est opus Entia, vel distincta Cyri principia sine necessita- te multiplicare. Simplicior & verior est sententia, quæ statuit, Cyrum statim post occupatum Babyloni- cum regnum Judæis regibus licentiam promulgasse redeundi in patriam, urgentibus id Judæis ex Esaiæ vaticinio. Hæc B. D. Behmius, τὰ ἴδια ἀναιρω̃ν.

Quinto Canon Ptolemæi, quem ceu divinum venerantur Scaligeriani, & quovis auro pretiosio- rem habent, tribuit Cyro tantum annos IX. unde colligere licet, quum Cyrus regnarit in Persia per 38. annos, Novennium illud Monarchiæ ejus Ba- bylonicæ assignandum esse, ut 21. annis prioribus Regni Persici Cyri Babylonicam Monarchiam ob- tinuerint Balthazar, & Darius Medus, qui à Cyro devictus est. Neque dissonant Historici, Herodo- tus, Trogus, Justinus, alii, ex quorum accurata colla- tione id patet, Cyrum ante 20. annum Regni sui Persici in Babylonicum Regnum pedem haud intu- lisse, tantum abest, ut dicere potuerit, Dominus Deus dedit mihi omnia Regna terræ.

Sexto, si verba Prophetæ nostri accurate ex- pendantur cap. 25. manifestum erit annos pressuræ & captivitatis Babylonicæ numerandos esse à quar- to Joackimi, vel à primo adventu Nebucadnezaris in Judæam, quo prima etiam abductio facta, & ex quo Reges Judæorum novissimi constituti sunt Vasalli Nebucadnezaris. Non enim frustra Jeremias re- petit, quomodo à 13. Josiæ anno usq; ad illum 4. an- num Deus ad pœnitentiam revocarit populum, & quomodo per integros 23. annos ipse sedulo eos præconio suo ad pœnitentiam invitarit; USQUE AD HUNC DIEM, inquit Propheta, q. d. jam ergo tempus est judicii divini, utque ad hunc diem μακροθυμία divina vos invitavit. Quid luculentius esse poterat, quam cum Propheta quarto Jojakim anno testatur se calicem accepisse ex manu Domini, ut propinaret omnibus gentibus, imprimis autem Hie- rosolymæ, & cæteris oppidis Judææ, & Principibus, ut daret eos in solitudinem & desolationem & in male- dictionem, & in sibilum, SICUT EST DIES ISTA v. 17. Quo indicatur omnino, isto tempore jam cœ- pisse illam solitudinem, & vastitatem; ideo etiam ibi figit annos duraturæ miseriæ LXX. v. 11. Et com- pellantur hic c. 29, 4. captivi OMNES, non tantum qui cum Jechonia transportati erant, sed etiam è prima abductione, cum terminus denuo sancitur ipsis, LXX. annorum, sc. à prima ipsorum transpor- tatione. Alias illis primum deportatis, non tantum per LXX. annos, sed per multo plures in exilio hæ- rendum fuisset. Deniq; si Rex Babyloniæ supera- tus & victus à Cyro fuit anno 21. Regni Cyri, quod Scaligeriani non diffitentur, oportet, ut etiam solu- tio proxime facta sit captivitatis: quia conjungit hæc Propheta c. 25, 12. Cum impleti fuerint LXX. an- ni, visitabo super Regem Babylonis & super gentem il- lam, dicit Dominus, iniquitatem eorum, & super ter- ram Chaldaeorum; adeoque sub idem tempus post ela- psos nempe LXX. annos, tum liberationem popu- lo, tum visitationem Regis Babylonis praedicit Sp. S. Septimo congruit apprime calculus. Nam a IV. anno Jojakim usque ad XXIII. annum Persici Regni Cyri, qui primus annus Monarchiae ejusdem est, praeterlapsi exacte sunt LXX. anni. Nam primus annus Nebucadnezaris in Judaea, cum IV. anno Jo- jakim connectitur Jer. 25, 1. Annus autem ille Ne- bucadnezaris primus, est annus Nabonassareus CXL. unde consequitur XVIII. annum Nebucadnezaris esse CLIX. Nabonazareum, h. e. annum undeci- mum, vel ultimum Regis Sedekiae: primus autem Monarchiae Cyri erit CCX. Nabonazareus. Octavo Calculus iniri ita potest secundum Mo- narchas Babyloniae; Siquidem primus annus Nabu- chodonosaris cum IV. anno Jojakimi concurrit. Ille autem regnavit XLIII. annis teste vero Beroso, & Canone Mathematico. Evilmerodach duobus re- gnavit annis, ut iterum Berosus, & canon Ptolomei testatur ex editione Calvisii. Neriglissares quatuor annis, Laborosardochus, sive Belsazar, Beroso auto- re, per IX. menses regnavit solus, Nabonidus vel Da- rius Medus XVII. annis omnium consensu Regno praefuit; qui anni collecti efficiunt LXVI. Desi- derantur ita IV. anni. Causa haec est, quod per qua- driennium cum parente regnavit Nebucadnezar, quos non annumeravit Ptolemaeus annis Regiminis ejus; de quo audire juvat B. D. Behmium: Obser- vandum, inquit loco citato, Th. XXVI. in annis Ne- bucadnezaris connectendis cum annis Nabonaza- reis, quadriennii discrimen esse in Biblica Historia & Mathematico Ptolemaei canone. Illa primum Nebu- cadnezaris connectit cum CXL. Nabonazareo. Hic cum CXLIV. Nabonazareo. Causa differentiae haec est. Biblica historia annos Nebucadnezaris incipit statim a primo ejusdem in Syriam & Judaeam adven- tu, facto vivente adhuc parente Nabopolassare, a quo ad rebelles missus est, teste vero Beroso, in aureo suo a- pud Josephum & Eusebium fragmento. Canon vero Pto- lomaei annos Nebucadnezaris demum inchoat a mor- te Parentis, qui per XXI. annos regnavit, a CXXIII. ad CXLIV. Nabonazaraeum. Hinc apparet Nebucad- nezarem ex Scripturae ductu per quadriennium cum parente regnasse. Et quia Ptolomaeus Nebucadneza- ris post Parentis mortem tribuit annos XLIII. dicen- dum, eundem Babyloniae Regem secundum Biblicam historiam regnasse XLVII. annos, quatuor cum Paren- te, XLIII. solum. Quod accurata cum diligentia no- tatum fundamentum continet Chronologicae conne- xionis Epochae Nabonazareae cum annis Biblicis & Mathematico Ptolemaei canone. Haec B. D. Behmius. Consonat etiam Eusebius in Chronic. siquidem nu- merentur ab anno undecimo Zedekiae LX. anni ad ultimum Cyri, adeoque intervallum ad annum XXII. Cyri erit LII. annorum. His adde XVIII. annos a primo adventu Nebucadnezaris ad XI. Regis Sede- kiae & proveniunt LXX. anni. Computus etiam ita institui potest: Excidium Hierosolymitanum inci- dit juxta Eusebium in secundum Olympiadis XLVII. annum vel Iphiti CLXXXVI. Cyri enim annus pri- mus est Olympiadis LV. primus, seu Iphiti CCXVII. Habemus ergo intervallum ab excidio, ad primum Cyri, XXXII. annorum; his adde annos 22. Cyri, prodeunt 53. Ad excidium autem Hierosol. ab an- no IV. Jojakimi numerantur XVII. anni, nempe VII. reliqui Jojakimini (qui regnavit XI. annis) Joja- chim III. menses & decem anni Zedekiae, quia un- decimus concurrit cum anno excidii. Adde quae de intervallo excidii Hierosol. & initii Cyri Babylo- nici Calvisius habet Isag. Chron. c. 33. pag. 183. Eos autem Chronologi antiquiores toti sunt in eo, ut de- monstrent differentiam hanc esse annorum solidorum triginta, & Cyrum cœpisse anno XXXI. post excidium Hierosolymæ, idq; pluribus argumentis præstant : ta- men idem ex annis Sabbathicis docere possumus. Cy- rus cœpit testibus Historicis omnibus, anno Nabonas- saris CLXXXIX. anno tertio post celebratum annum Sabbathicum, adde enim ternarium & abjice septe- naria, in residuo sunt tria. Jam annus captæ Hierso- lymæ incidit in Sabbathicum, & hinc sequentes Sab- bathici recte numerari possunt. Vicesimus igitur octa- vus annus post captam Hierosolymam est etiam Sab- bathicus, quemadmodum & tricesimus quintus. Cy- rus autem cœpit anno tertio post celebratum Sabba- thicum. Ergo cœpit vel tricesimo primo post captam Hierosolymam : aut tricesimo octavo. Anno tricesi- mo octavo incipere non potuit, quia sequeretur eum vicisse Darium Persarum Regem anno undecimo vel duodecimo Regni, cum tamen tum maxime appareret bellum, ut Historici testantur in Cræsum. Subduc an- nos triginta octo ex annis XLIX. ex distantia inter cladem Hierosolymitanam, & victum Darium, su- persunt anni undecim. Cum igitur Cyrus Darium anno duodecimo regni non vicerit sed post annos alios septem, ut Sabbathici monstrant, necesse est, ut cœperit anno tricesimo primo post cladem Hierosolymitanam. Si annus tricesimus primus post illam cladem est an- nus Nabonassaris CLXXXIX. quo Cyrus cœpit, ergo clades illa accidit anno CLXXXVIII. Nabonassaris, anno Sabbathico, ut vult Ezechiel, Clemens Alexan- drinus, Eusebius, Herodotus, distantia item XIII. anni Ezechiæ, & Berosus.

Nono ita sua constabit ratio anno primo Cyri 2. Par. 36. Esr. 1. quæ juxta Scaligeri sententiam nulla reddi potest. Nam si dicas anno primo Cyri solutam esse captivitatem, & annum primum non aliter intelligas, quam de Epocha solutæ captivitatis, ridiculum id erit, atq; idem per idem designabitur. Et quomodo annus primus Cyri aliter, quam de anno primo Regni Cyri intelligi potest, juxta phrasin Scripturæ usitatam, imo quomodo annus primus post devictum Nabonidum in annalibus ipsis Per- sarum, qui in archivis Imperii asservati sunt, primus annus Cyri dictus fuisset, non ab imperio Cyri, sed à soluta Judæorum captivitate! Sic enim legitur in illis Esdr. VI. 3. Anno primo Cyri Regis Cyrus Rex decrevit, ut domus Dei ædificaretur. Quid manife- stius, quam quod ibi annus primus Monarchiæ Cy- ri designetur? Adde responsum populi Israelitici Esdr. 5, 13. Anno primo Cyri Regis Babylonis, Cyrus Rex proposuit edictum, ut domus Dei ædificaretur: Ubi nemo non videt annum primum Cyri proponi tanquam Regis Babylonis, seu Monarchiæ ejus Babylonicæ. Sed de hoc primo Cyri anno plura diximus ad locum 2. Par. 36.

Decimo non constat sibi Scaliger, cum libro 6. de emendatione temporum principium LXX. anno- rum ponit in primo Jechoniæ, quando cum Rege, & aliis Ezechiel abductus est : non v. in quarto Joja- kimi, quando Daniel cum aliis Babylonem migra- vit: At libro 5. Danielem & Ezechielem simul tra- ductos Babylonem ait, non secus ac si una esset atq; eadem captivitas Jechoniæ, & Jojakimi.

Undecimo addimus autoritates pro hac senten- tia non tantum Veterum, & Beroaldistarum, & alio- rum, imprimis Dionysii Petavii Chronologi cele- berrimi, Jacobi Usserii, ut & Rob. Bailii Oper. Chron. & Hist. l. 1. p. 91. Ex Jeremiæ c. 25, 10. 11. 12. appa- ret, eorum initium sumendum à primo anno Nebu- chadnezaris; finito an fluente, nihil refert; annis nimirum novendecim ante destructum templum, & clausam præ manibus Epocham, ita ut post urbis ac templi excidium, 70. istorum annorum tantum quinquaginta & unus restent, adeo ut facile fuerit multis utrumq; templum conspexisse, Salomonis eversa & Zorobabelis jacta fundamenta: quod p. 144. quast. 2. plenius persequutus est Bailius. Sed etiam è Scaligerianis B. Dn. D. Behmii. Qui in Chrono- log. Manuduct. quidem Libr. 2. Tit. 2. cap. 3. hanc sententiam hoc modo reprobavit: Tertius Joja- kim est annus tertius Olympiadis XLII. Sive annus Olympiadicus CLXVII. ex Veterum alligatione; Vigesimus Cyri est primus Olympiadis LX. sive CCXXXVII. Olympiadicus. Ab hoc numero si CLXVII. subtrahantur, LXX. remanent. Verum & hæc veterum opinio (quam nonnulli hodiernorum Chronologorum, Beroaldus, & alii sequuntur) non consistit. Licet enim anno tertio Jojakim à Nebucad- nezare Babyloniorum Rege multi Judæorum in Ba- bylonem abducti sint, (inter quos & Daniel c. 1, 6.) ab ea tamen captivitate scriptura nullibi LXX. capti- vitatis annis inchoat, quia tum temporis non nisi ado- lescentes seminis regii & nonnulli Judaicorum auli- corum abducebantur Dan. 1. vers. 3. 4. Ita ille in Chron. Manuduct. edita Anno 1617. Sed postmo- dum in senectute, & post annos XXV. accuratiori indagatione rectius edoctus, non dubitavit senten- tiam illam suam pristinam retractare, nostramque adserere. Qui viri candor erat; quem subinde laudare S. Augustinum recordor, quod non dubi- tarit Retractationum libros scribere; cujus pro- inde exemplum sequutus etiam προθύμως ipse est, imprimis in Chronologicis. Juvabit adducere è lau- data ejus disputatione Anno 1643. Regiomonti publice nabita, propria ejusdem verba, & funda- menta, ob eos imprimis, qui B. D. Behmium sequu- ti sunt, & adhuc sequuntur, in assignando termino captivitatis Babylonicæ juxta Manuductionem Chronologicam: ignari, ut apparet, quod ipse aliam in posterioribus annis sententiam amplexus fuœrit. Discedunt, inquit loc. citat. Th. XXI. à pro- pheta Jeremia, qui annos LXX. Babylonicæ pressuræ incipit à IV. Jojakimi & primo Nebucadnezaris in Judæam adventu c. 25. Annon ab eo statim tempore in- cepit Judæorum in Babyloniam abductio? Annon ab eo tempore tres ultimi Judæorum Reges Jojakimi, Je- chonia, Zedekia facti sunt Vasalli Babylonici Regni Nebucadnezaris? Annon ab eo tempore Judæa Ba- bylonico Regi facta est tributaria? Utinam vel tan- dem errore deposito homines illi saperent! Retento ergo (ita pergit) Eusebiano XXX. annorum inter- vallo, a IV. Jojakim, ad primum Cyri Persici Regni intervallum est XLVIII. annorum; additis XXII. an- nis, fiunt LXX. Unde videmus, Cyrum Babylonicum Regnum obtinuisse anno XXII. Persici sui Regni, & eo ipso statim tempore Judæis captivitatem laxasse, non primo Cyri Persici Regni, uti Pererius fingit, & deli- rat cum multis aliis. Regnavit ergo Cyrus post occupa tum Babylonicum Regnum adhuc per annos IX. quod cum Mathematico Ptolemæi canone exactè convenit. Ex hisce proauctis hunc in modum progredimur. Pri- mum Cyri Babylonici sui Regni in Mathematico Pto- lomæi Canone, concatenatus est cum CCX. Nabona- zaræo. Subtractis LXX. annis Babylonicæ captivi- tatis remanent CXL. anni Nabonazaræi. Anni ve- ro captivitatis sunt incipiendi à IV. Jojakimi, vel à primo Nebucadnezaris in Syriam & Judæam adven- tu, teste Jerem. Cap. 25, 1. ut modo monitum. Quar- tus ergo Jojakimi conveniens cum CXL. Nabonaza- ræo egregium nobis monstrat artificium connexionis Epochæ Nabonazarææ cum annis Biblicis. Si CXL. Nabonazaræus primus est Nebucadnezaris in scri- ptura secundum Jeremiam. Ergo XVIII. ejusdem con- catenatus cum anno exterminii Salomonici templi erit CLVIII. Nabonazaræus exactè conveniens cũ XI. Ze- dekiæ ultimi Regis Judæ. Idem artificium nobis exhibet Eusebianus annorũ positus, qui ab XI. Zedekiæ s. πανο- λεθρία Salomonici templi ad ultimum Cyri interval- lum habet LX. solidorum annorum. Ultimus Cyri in prænominatu Ptolemæus canone est CCXVIII. Nabo- nazaræus, subtractis LX. annis Eusebianis remanet CLVIII. Nabonazaræus, connectendus in rei verita- te cum ultimo Zedekiæ. Stante hoc Eusebiano inter- vallo plane legitimo & firmo, indubitatum inde argu- mentum desumitur, terminum A QUO LXX. an- norum Babylonicæ captivitatis non esse πανωλε- θρίαν Salomonici templi, sed in anteriora ascenden- dum ad IV. Jojakimi, vel primum Nebucadnezaris in Scriptura. Eadem concatenatio firmari poterit ex E- zechielis loco c. 1, 1. qui XXX. annum connectit cum 5. à spontanea Jechoniæ transportatione: Placet autem nobis eorum sententia, qui statuunt Prophetam Baby- lone tum degentem, tricesimum annum notare Baby- lonici alicujus Regis, exemplo Nehemiæ c. 1, 1. Atqui Rex ille non est Nebucadnezar. Quintus enim à de- portato Jechonia convenit cum XIII. Nebucadneza- ris in Scriptura. Erit ergo Nebucadnezaris Parens Nabullassar vel Nabopollaffar (teste Beroso, Josepho, Ptolomæo, Eusebio) dictus. Hujus regimen exurgit ab anno CXXIII. Nabonazaræo. Ejus enim quintus cælesti charactere, deliquio lunæ apud Ptolomæum, firmatus, est CXXVII. Nabonazaræus. Hinc ita ra- tiocinamur: Si primus à Nabopollaffare est CXXIII. Nabonaffaræus: ergo tricesimus ab eodem est CLII. Nabon. conveniens cum 5. anno à deportato Jecho- nia, qui simul quintus est Zedekiæ. Si hoc, undecimus ejusdem erit CLVIII. Nabonazaræus. Qua conca- tenatione nil jucundius, nil exactius, nil solidius. Hæc omnia D. Behmius ὁ νῦν ἐν ἁγίοις. Addimus etiam artificium connexionis Epochæ Nabonaza- rææ cum annis Biblicis, & Mathematico canone Ptolomæi. Artificium, inquit, tali se modo habet: Ptolemæus in canone à primo Nebucadnezaris ad pri- mum Cyri Babylonici Regni exclusive numerat annos LXVI. Nabocolaffaro (qui in Bibliis est Nebucadne- zar) tribuit XLIII. annos. Ilvarodamo (Evilmęro- dacho) duos. Nericaffolaffaro (Belfchazari) qua- tuor. Nabonnido Medo (Dario Medo) XVII. summa LXVI. Additis IV. annis secundum Biblicam annorum Nebucadnezaris numerationem, fiunt LXX. anni, Unde clare elucescit, terminum A QUO LXX. annorum Babylonicæ captivitatis non esse πα- νωλεθρίαν seu exterminium Salomonici Templi, sed per annos XVIII. in anteriora afcendendum, in quar- tum Jojakimi, convenientem secundum Biblicam con- catenationem, cum primo Nebucadnezaris, Jeremia teste cap. 25, 1. Qui locus accurata cum diligen- tia notandus est. Concludit deniq; ὁ μακαρίτης hoc modo: In rei ergo veritate ab excidio Hierosolymi- tani Templi ad captivitatis laxationem anni sunt LII. non plures nec pauciores. Annus excidii Salo- monici templi convenit cum CLVIII. Nabonazaræo, ut paulo ante monitum. Judæorum ergo captivitas laxata anno CCX. Nabonazaræo, qui primus est Cyri Babylonici Regni in divino Ptolomæi canone. Addi- tis octo annis Cyri fiunt, CCXVIII. anni. Atqui annus CCXVIII. Nabonazaræus est emortualis Cyri. Septi- mus enim Cambysis cælesti charactere, Eclipsi Lunæ apud Ptolemæum, notatus est CCXXV. Nabonaza- ræus. Utinam vel tandem literati rejectis Anniani somniis, & Funccianis erroribus veram firmamque concatenationem Epochæ Nabonarææ cum annis Biblicis amplecterentur! Hac enim concatenatione firmata, duæ reliquæ celebriores Epochæ, Olympiadis & Urbis facili labore cum annis Biblicis connecti pos- sunt. Quod breviter fuit monstrandum. Hæc ita B. D. Behmius αὐτολεξεὶ, quæ ob sectatores & disci- pulos ejus, hac occasione, in apricum producere voluimus, in gratiam sacræ Chronologiæ: quum in his, & aliis suo etiam exemplo illud veriverbium comprobavit: Dies diem docet. Vers. 12. INVOCABITIS ME) Id est, invocate, ite, orate, quærite. Vers. 13. CUM QUÆSIERITIS ME IN TOTO CORDE VESTRO) Animo sincero. Vers. 15. QUIA DIXISTIS, SUSCITAVIT NO- BIS PROPHETAS IN BABYLONE) Transpositio. Sensus est: Postquam dixeritis in Babylone, Deus nobis susci- taverat (jam olim scilicet) Prophe as : veraces nempe, qui hæc omnia prædixerant, quæ nobis evenere. Confer. Daniel 9, 6. 12. Vers. 16. SUPER SOLIUM DAVID) Id est, de Sedecia. Vers. 17. GLADIUM ET FAMEM, ET PESTEM) Supra 15, 2. QUASI FICUS MALAS) Ut supra 24, 8. Vers. 18. ET IN STUPOREM ET IN SIBILUM) Supra 18, 16. 19, 8. 25, 18. Vers. 19. DE NOCTE CONSURGENS) Supra 25, 3. Vers. 21. PERCUTIET EOS) Interficiet, igne, ut se- quitur. QVOS FRIXIT REX BABYLONIS IN IGNE) קלה est torrere, ut hic habet Chaldæus. In caminum con- jectio pœna apud Chaldæos Dan. 3, 6. Adde Amos 4, 2. Vers. 23. PRO EO QVOD FECERINT STVLTI- TIAM IN ISRAEL.) Flagitium, rem fœdam, ut hic Chal- dæus. Græci generis nomine, ἀνομίαν. ET MOECHATI SVNT IN UXORES AMI- CORUM SUORUM) Judæi hos eosdem illos esse volunt, qui Susannæ pudori insidiati sunt: historiam enim illam veram existimant: non autem omnia quæ in Græco habe- mus: & credibilius punitos à rege, quam à populo exsulan- te. Si quis fabulis delectatur, videat quæ de regis Babylo- nii filia Achabo isto, & Sedecia ad stuprum sollicitata, narrat Gemara ad titulum de Synedrio capite כל ישראל. Fabulam esse narrationem illam de Susanna Hieronym. plus vice simplici indicavit: & lapidati dicuntur illi senes, hi vero igne tosti sunt v. 22. EGO SVM JUDEX ET TESTIS) In Hebræo: Ego novi & testificor. Vers. 24. ET AD SEMEJAM NEHESAMITEN DICES) Separandum hoc à superioribus. Hoc enim mun- datum Jeremias accepit, postquam legati redierant. Vers. 25. PRO EO QVOD MISISTI IN NOMINE TUO LIBROS) Id est, epistolas ad Sophoniam & alios. In nomine tuo: id est, meo injussu. Sic ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ sumitur Joh. 5, 43. AD SOPHONIAM) Qui erat סגן, id est, secun- dus à summo Pontifice, ejusque vicarius. 2. Reg. 25, 18. Vers. 26. DOMINUS DEDIT TE SACERDOTEM PRO JOJADA SACERDOTE) Id est, Jojadæ Zelum imitari debes, de quo 2. Reg. 11, 18. 2. Paral. 23, 17. UT SIS DUX IN DOMO DOMINI) Ut cæteris sacerdotibus præeas, jubeasque per στρατηγοῦντᾶ ἱερῦ capi pseudo-prophetas, qualis est Jeremias. VIRVM ARREPTITIVM) Qui non à Dei spiritu, sed dæmonibus incitatur. Vide 2. Reg. 9, 11. IN NERVUM ET IN CARCEREM) Prior vox eadem quæ supra 20, 2. Altera צינק est, ut plerique He- bræorum censent, manica ferrea. ענק Arabibus ar- ctum esse significat. Sunt qui etymo ducti significari pu- tant supplicium illud scapharium, cujus in Artaxerxe Plu- tarchus meminit. Verum id supplicium Hebræis inco- gnitum fuit, & Sacerdotes in Templo prehendendi, non puniendi jus habebant. Vers. 29. LEGIT ERGO SOPHONIAS SACERDOS LIBRUM ISTUM IN AVRIBVS JEREMIÆ PRO- PHETÆ) Nolens prehendere inauditum. Vers. 32. NON ERIT EI VIR SEDENS IN ME- DIO POPULI HVJVS) Id est, habitans. ET NON VIDEBIT BONVM QVOD EGO FACIAM POPVLO MEO) Reditum in patriam. QUIA PRÆVARICATIONEM LOCVTVS EST ADVERSVS DOMINUM) Impedit conversio- nem populi.

## 30:1 Argument
SUBSECTION II. MORE EVANGELICAL AND CONSOLATORY SERMONS. CHAPTER XXX. The Prophet is ordered to consign to a book the words of the Lord, who consoles the people to be freed from captivity with the promise of the Leader Messiah.

Latin:

SUBSECTIO II. CONCIONES MAGIS EVANGELI- CÆ ET CONSOLATORIÆ. CAPUT XXX. Libro consignare jubetur Propheta verba Do- mini, qui consolatur populum è captivitate liberandum cum promissione Ducis Messia.

## 30:2
WRITE TO YOURSELF ALL THE WORDS WHICH I HAVE SPOKEN TO YOU) Which I am now speaking to you. He understands the words which will now follow. IN A BOOK) On parchment, which may last a long time, so that these things written by your hand may be read then, when they are fulfilled, as a sign of my truth.

They were not only to last until the captivity was resolved, but forever. For the word of God was to be consigned to writing, so that it might serve our uses also. Whatever things were written, were written for our sake, as the Apostle testifies, Rom. 15, verse 4.

Latin:

SCRIBE TIBI OMNIA VERBA QUÆ LOCU- TUS SUM AD TE) Quæ jam ad te loquor. Intelligit verba, quæ jam sequentur. IN LIBRO) In membrana, quæ diu duret, ut hæc tua manu scripta legi possint tunc, cum implebuntur, in signum meæ veritatis.

NOn tantum durare debebant donec solvere- tur captivitas, sed in perpetuum. Scriptis enim consignandum erat verbum Dei, ut in usus etiam nostros inserviret. Quæcunque scripta sunt, propter nos scripta sunt, teste Apostolo Rom. 15. vers. 4.

## 30:3
Verse 3.

I WILL TURN THE CAPTIVITY) In the Hebrew: I will turn the transmigration: that is, those who have migrated. Thus both the Chaldean here and the Greeks. We had a similar way of speaking above 29, 1. Moreover, there is an allusion to neighboring words, of which the former is from שוב, the latter from שבה.

OF MY PEOPLE ISRAEL AND JUDA) For although the descendants of Judah and Benjamin, some also returned from other tribes, especially from the Levitical. See Luke 2, 36.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

CONVERTAM CONVERSIONEM) In Hebræo: Convertam transmigrationem: id est, eos qui transmigra- runt. Ita & Chaldæus hic & Græci. Simile loquendi genus habuimus supra 29, 1. Est autem allusio vicinarum vocum, quarum prior est à שוב, altera à שבה.

POPULI MEI ISRAEL ET JUDA) Nam cum Judæ & Benjaminis posteri, nonnulli etiam rediere ex aliis tribubus, maxime ex Levitica. Vide Lucam 2, 36.

## 30:5
Verse 5.

WE HAVE HEARD A VOICE OF TERROR: FEAR AND THERE IS NO PEACE) Evils will last a long time.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

VOCEM TERRORIS AUDIVIMUS: FORMI- DO ET NON EST PAX) Diu durabunt mala.

## 30:6
Verse 6.

INTERROGATE AND SEE, IF A MALE GIVES BIRTH) Translate: whether a male gives birth. Question the wise, search in books, whether that can happen. You will find it cannot.

WHY THEN HAVE I SEEN EVERY MAN'S HAND UPON HIS LOIN AS A WOMAN IN LABOR) For women in labor are accustomed to place their hands on their loins to repress the pain.

AND ALL FACES ARE TURNED INTO PALENESS) They are suffused with a yellowish color, as is accustomed to happen to the jaundiced. This happens from diffused bile.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

INTERROGATE ET VIDETE, SI GE- NERAT MASCULUS) Verte: an pariat mas. Interro- gate sapientes, quærite in libris, an id fieri possit. Reperietis non posse.

QUARE ERGO VIDI OMNIS VIRI MANUM SUPER LUMBUM SUUM QUASI PARTURIENTIS) Nam solent feminæ parturientes lumbis manus apponere ad reprimendum dolorem.

ET CONVERSÆ SUNT UNIVERSÆ FACIES IN AURUGINEM) Luteo colore suffusæ sunt, ut icteri- cis accidere solet. Id fit diffusa bile.

## 30:7
Verse 7.

THAT DAY IS GREAT) The whole time of the exile.

The discourse is not about the whole time of the exile, but about that time when, the city having been captured, the people were led away into captivity. Others explain it regarding the calamities under Antiochus, with whom Osiander agreed in his paraphrase; some accept the prophecy as being about the time of the final destruction of Jerusalem carried out by the Romans, such as Joachim the Abbot, Tostatus, Castro, and Chislerus, who furthermore interpret the promised liberation as the liberation through the final coming of Christ for judgment; but this exposition is foreign: nor does that seem to fit sufficiently. Since the context teaches that it is a matter of the affliction by the Chaldeans.

AND HE SHALL BE SAVED FROM IT) But he shall be saved from it. For after the description of evils, here begins the consolation.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

MAGNA DIES ILLA) Tempus totum exsilii.

Non de toto exsilii tempore, sed de illo tem- pore, quo capta civitate in captivitatem abductus est populus, sermo est. Alii de calamitatibus sub Antiocho explicant, cum quibus fecit Osiander in paraphrasi; nonnulli de tempore ultimæ cladis Hierosolymitanæ per Romanos factæ vaticinium accipiunt, utpote Joachimus Abbas, Tostatus, Castro, Chislerus, qui porro liberationem promissam de li- beratione per ultimum Christi adventum ad judi- cium interpretantur; sed hæc expositio aliena est: neq; illa satis convenire videtur. Siquidem con- textus doceat de Chaldæorum afflictione agi.

ET EX IPSO SALVABITUR) Sed ex ipso salva- bitur. Nam post descriptionem malorum hic incipit con- solatio.

## 30:9
Verse 9.

THEY SHALL SERVE THE LORD THEIR GOD, AND DAVID THEIR KING) That is, Zerubbabel, of whom also above 23, 5. He is called David, both here and in Ezekiel 34, 23 and chapter 37, 24; naturally, just as Ptolemies arose from Ptolemy, and Caesars from Caesar.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SERVIENT DOMINO DEO SUO, ET DA- VID REGI SUO) Id est, Zorobabeli, de quo & supra 23, 5. Is David vocatur, & hic & Ezech. 34, 23. & c. 37, 24. ni- mirum sicut à Ptolemæo orti Ptolemæi, à Cæsare Cæsares.

## 30:10
Verse 10.

AND HE SHALL ABOUND WITH ALL GOOD THINGS, AND THERE SHALL BE NONE WHOM HE FEARS) Above 23, 6.

It is a mistake to understand Zerubbabel by David, who is neither designated anywhere by the name of David, nor ever bore either the royal name or the diadem. And here King David is joined with GOD in worship: They shall serve the Lord and David their King. Wherefore no other can be understood by King David than the Messiah, who is to be followed with divine worship along with God the Father, and to whom religious service is owed. We previously showed that this King, and not Zerubbabel, is pointed out in chapter 23, 6. Ezekiel also calls him by the name of David in chapter 34, 23, 24, and Hosea in chapter 3, 5, because, having sprung from the lineage of David, he obtained the throne of David, Isa. 9, 4, Luke 1, 32, and was prefigured in David as in a notable type. Christian interpreters agree unanimously in this opinion, namely that Christ is to be understood here by David: Grotius alone almost dreams here of Zerubbabel, to whom the name of King in no way applies, nor was it ever attributed. Whence even the ancient Rabbis themselves acknowledged that the Messiah is designated in this place. For the Chaldean translation holds it thus: And they shall serve before the Lord their God, and shall obey the Messiah the Son of David their King, whom I will raise up for them. So also it is read in the Talmud, in the book Sanhedrin, chapter Chelek: The King of Judah said. Rab said: It is to be that the Holy One blessed be He Himself shall raise up or establish for Israel another David. He did not say 'is established,' but 'I will establish.' And in the Jerusalem book Berochoth, in the distinction Hajah Kore: Afterwards the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the Lord their God, and David their King (Hos. 3:5). The Rabbis said: This King Messiah, if he is of the living, David is his name; if of the dead, David is his name. That is, whether he be living or dead, his name is David. Where likewise Jonathan in his translation understood the Messiah, rendering it thus: And after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the worship of the Lord their God, and shall obey the Messiah the son of David their King. Furthermore, although Christian interpreters agree that this prophecy is to be understood concerning the Messiah, they vary not a little, however, as to what time and what liberation is designated in this place! Some accept all these things, which are promised in this chapter concerning the resolution and liberation from captivity, as referring to the time of the coming of the Messiah and spiritual liberation, along with Jerome, Isidore, Rabanus, Hugo, Lyranus, and Vatablus. Others, with Tostatus and Joachim the Abbot, refer it to the end time and liberation through the coming to judgment. But neither seems to correspond sufficiently to the explanation of the context: in which it is primarily certain that it treats of the captivity and calamity at the time of that Babylonian captivity: nor can we deny that liberation from that captivity is promised, when the Prophet threatens destruction to the nations through which the people had been dispersed, but promises grace and liberation to the people to whom a significant distress was about to happen, therefore he is raised up by this consolation, that he is to be liberated from the same, verse 7. Meanwhile, promises concerning spiritual goods and benefits are mixed in with the promises of corporal benefits; not as if the same promises treat both of the type in the literal sense, that is, of the liberation from the Babylonian captivity, and of the antitype in the mystical sense, or spiritual liberation—for hermeneutical laws do not permit that—but that both corporal and spiritual promises are joined, yet with distinct words of the Prophet: and those benefits which are spiritual, they should be understood solely concerning those, and those which are corporal, they should not be accepted as anything but the same, lest the most distinct benefits be confused. Wherefore if the conversion of captivity or transmigration and the reduction into the land of Canaan is promised, which we do not deny in this place, it must be confessed that the end of this reduction is expressed here, namely, that they may serve God and their King the Messiah, whom God is one day to raise up for them, by virtue of the promise made above in chapter 23:6, to whom, that they might serve, they were stirred up by David himself, Ps. 2:12. For the faithful do not serve the Messiah only at the time of the New Testament, but they were bound to serve him at all times. Jesus Christ yesterday, today, the same, and forever, Heb. 13:8. Because of this Messiah their King, a corporal liberation also befell them. The returned ones were able to serve Him and to worship the same, free from the yoke and from the chains in which they were held to serve strangers: Which chains, and which yoke—whether it be understood with some concerning the spiritual yoke of the law and the chains of sin, or concerning the corporal yoke and captivity (one or the other sense must necessarily be admitted, for both cannot have place at the same time)—remains meanwhile that the servitude, for which they were to be liberated, to be rendered to the Lord and King David, is to be taken concerning religious worship, to be exhibited to God and the Messiah: whom, even if they were to expect to be raised up in his own time, they were nevertheless always bound to adhere to with true faith, along with David, who venerated him as his own Lord, Ps. 110:1, and for that end they are liberated from their enemies, that they might be able to be freely at leisure for this religious servitude. Therefore, this spiritual worship is promised, the coming and expectation of the Messiah is promised; and afterwards in verse 22, the gracious reception of the people is promised at the same time, but those spiritual promises, as I have said, are not to be confused with the corporal ones, nor, while place is left for the latter, are the former to be entirely eliminated, but the words of each promise are to be properly weighed, so that what it has in reserve, in its own and literal sense intended by the Holy Spirit, which is only one, may be rightly defined. Blessed Hülsemann agrees in the explanation of this place. For even if he understands the preceding verses 3 and following concerning the Babylonian captivity, comparing verse 8 with chapter 27:8, 11, and through Israel and Judah v. 3. He wishes the Israelites and Jews according to the flesh to be designated, nor does he concede that hypothesis that only two tribes were returned from the Babylonian captivity, both because many Israelites left by Tiglath-Pileser were brought over by Nebuchadnezzar, 2 Chron. 20:11 ff., and because the temporal reduction is promised very often to the remaining Israelites and Jews alike, Jer. 12:14, 15; ch. 16:15; ch. 23:3; ch. 50:17, and because the whole people of Israel is said to have returned, 2 Chron. 36:23, and there is no doubt for him but that those Israelites who had been dispersed through other regions returned into Judea after the temple was rebuilt: and because nowhere is that land of the living described by this epithet, that God gave it to the fathers, which is the perpetual description of the land of Canaan, ch. 15:15; ch. 50:17, 19, etc. He determines, however, that it must be asserted entirely that in this 9th verse a spiritual promise is mixed with bodily liberation, so that by David, Christ the son of David is understood, and he observes that R. D. Kimchi & R. Jonathan explain it thus in the paraphrase, and he urges especially the parallel passages Luc. 1, 52. Ezech. 34, 23. 24. 37, 25. Rom. 9, 11. refuting at the same time Calvin, who thought it could be explained concerning a temporal prince from the seed of David, because the name of David is never read to be attributed to them univocally & simply: but they are said only to be like David, to walk in the ways of David, when they are similar to him in piety & morals 1. Reg. 15, 3. 2. Reg. 18, 3. cap. 22, 25. Jer. 13, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET CUNCTIS AFFLVET BONIS, ET NON ERIT QVEM FORMIDET) Supra 23, 6.

Perperam per Davidem Zorobabel intelligi- tur, qui neque Davidis nomine uspiam indigitatur, neq; Regium aut nomen aut diadema unquam ges- fit. Et conjungitur hic David Rex cum DEO in cultu: Servient Domino & Davidi Regi. Qua- propter non potest alius per Davidem Regem in- telligi, quam Messias, qui cum Deo Patre cultu divi- no prosequendus, & cui servitus religiosa debetur. Hunc Regem indigitatum esse cap. 23, 6. non Zoro- babelem, antea ostendimus. Hunc Davidis nomi- ne etiam Ezechiel vocat cap. 34, 23. 24. & Hoseas cap. 3, 5. quia è Davidis prosapia ortus, solium Da- vidis obtinuit Esa. 9, 4. Luc. 1, 32. & in Davide, ceu insigni typo, præfiguratus fuit. In quam senten- tiam conveniunt Christiani Interpp. ὁμοθυμα- δὸν, per Davidem nempe hic intelligendum esse Christum: solus pene Grotius Zorobabelem hic somniat, cui nomen Regis nullatenus convenit, nec unquam tributum fuit. Unde etiam ipsimet Rabbini veteres agnovere, Messiam hoc loco desi- gnari. Nam ita habet translatio Chaldaica: Et ser- vient coram Domino Deo suo, & obedient Messiae Filio David Regi suo, quem suscitabo illis. Ita etiam in Tal- mud legitur, in libro Sanhedrim, capite Chelek: Dixit Rex Juda. Dixit Rab. Futurum est, quod San- ctus benedictus ipse suscitet vel statuat Israeli alium David. Non dixit statui, sed statuam. Et in libro Be- rochoth Hierosolymitano distinctione Hajah Ko- re: Postea revertentur filii Israel, & quaerent Domi- num Deum suum, & Davidem Regem suum (Hof. 3, 5.) Rabbini dixerunt: Iste Rex Messias si de vivis est, David est nomen ejus, si de mortuis, David est nomen ejus. Hoc est, sive vivus sit, sive mortuus, nomen e- jus est David. Ubi itidem Jonathan in translatione sua Messiam intellexit, ita reddens: Et post hoc re- vertentur filii Israel & quaerent cultum Domini Dei sui, & obedient Messiae filio David Regi suo. Cæte- rum quamvis conveniant in eo Christiani Interpp. de Messia intelligendum esse hoc vaticinium, in eo tamen non parum variant, quodnam tempus, & quæ liberatio hoc in loco designetur! Nonnulli de tempore adventus Messiae & liberatione spirituali omnia hæc accipiunt, quæ de captivitatis solutione ac libera- tione in hoc capite promittuntur, cum Hierony- mo, Isidoro, Rabano, Hugone, Lyrano, Vatablo. Alii cum Tostato, & Joachimo Abbate de tempore novis- simo, & liberatione per adventum adjudicium. Sed neutrum explicationi contextus satis congrue- re videtur: in quo imprimis id certum est, de ca- ptivitate & calamitate tempore captivitatis istius Babylonicæ agi: neque negare possumus, lib. ratio- nem ex ista captivitate promitti, cum consumma- tionem gentibus, per quas dispersus erat populus, minatur Propheta, sed gratiam & liberationem pollicetur populo, cui angustia insignis obventura erat, ideo consolatione hac erigitur, quod ex ea- dem liberandus sit vers. 7. Interim promissionibus corporalium beneficiorum admixtæ sunt promis- siones de bonis & beneficiis spiritualibus; non ac si eædem promissiones tum de typo sensu literali a- gant, hoc est, de liberatione è captivitate Babylo- nica, tum sensu mystico de antitypo, seu spirituali li- beratione, id enim non permittunt leges hermi- neuticæ, sed quod conjungantur promissiones u- træque corporales & spirituales, distinctis tamen verbis Prophetæ: & quæ beneficia spiritualia si- stunt, de illis unice intelligenda sint, quæ corpora- lia, non nisi de iisdem accipi debeant, ne distin- ctissima beneficia confundantur. Quapropter si captivitatis, vel transmigrationis conversio, & redu- ctio in terram Canaan promittatur, quod hoc loco non abnuimus, fatendum est, finem hujus reductionis hic exprimi, ut nempe serviant Deo & Regi suo Messiae, quem olim Deus ipsi excitaturus est, vi promissio- nis supra factæ cap. 23, 6. cui ut serviant, à Davide i- pso excitati sunt Ps. 2, 12. Non enim tantum Novi Testamenti tempore Messiae serviunt fideles, sed servire ei debuere omni tempore. Jesus Christus he- ri, hodie, idem & in secula Ebr. 13. 18. Ob hunc Mes- siam Regem suum obtigit ipsis liberatio etiam cor- poralis. Huic reduces servire, eundemq; colere po- terant, liber à jugo & à vinculis, in quibus peregri- nis servire tenebantur: Quæ vincula, & quod ju- gum sive de spirituali jugo legis & vinculis peccati cum nonnullis, seu de corporali jugo & captivitate intelligatur, (alteruter sensus necessum est admit- tatur, uterq; enim simul locum habere non potest) manet interim servitutem, ob quam liberandi e- rant, Domino & Regi Davidi præstandam, de cul- tu religioso accipienda esse, Deo & Messiæ exhi- bendo: quem etsi suscitandum suo tempore expe- ctare debebant, ei tamen vera fide, cum Davide, qui ipsum ceu Dominum suum venerabatur, Psal. 110, 1. adhærescere semper tenebantur, eoque fine liberantur ad hostibus suis, ut servituti huic reli- giosæ libere vacare possent. Promittitur ergo hic cultus spiritualis, promittitur adventus & expectatio Messiæ; ac postmodum in vers. 22. promittitur si- mul susceptio gratiosa populi, sed promissiones istæ spirituales, uti dixi, non confundendæ sunt cum corporalibus, neque dum his locus relinquitur, illæ prorsus eliminandæ, sed uniuscujusque promif- sionis verba probe ponderanda, ut quid in recessu habeat, proprio, & literali sensu à Spiritu Sancto intento, qui non nisi unicus est, recte definiatur. Consonat B. Hülsemannus in explicatione hujus loci. Etsi enim præcedentia vers. 3. seqq. de captivi- tate Babylonica intelligat, conferens vers. 8. cum cap. 27, 8. 11. & per Israelem & Juda v. 3. Israelitas & Judæos secundum carnem designari velit, neque concedat istam hypothesin, quod duæ solum tribus reductæ sint è captivitate Babylonica, tum quia reli- cti à Tiglathpilassare Israelitæ plurimi traducti à Nebucadnezare 2. Par, 20, 11. seqq. tum quia pro- mittitur sæpissime reliquis Israelitis pariter & Ju- dæis reductio temporalis Jer. 12, 14. 15. cap. 16, 15. cap. 23, 3. cap. 50, 17. tum quia totus populus Israel reversus dicitur 2. Par. 36, 23. & dubium ipsi non est, quin illi Israelitæ, qui per alias Regiones dispersi e- rant, post reædificatum templum in Judæam redie- rint: tum quia nuspiam terra illa viventium hoc e- pitheto describitur, quod Deus eam dederit pa- tribus, quæ perpetua est descriptio terræ Canaan cap. 15, 15. cap. 50, 17. 19. &c. hoc tamen 9. versu promissionem spiritualem liberationi corporali immixtam esse, omnino asserendum statuit, ut per Davidem intelligatur Christus filius Davidis, atque ita R. D. Kimchi & R. Jonathan in paraphrasi ex- ponere observat, urgetque imprimis loca paralle- la Luc. 1, 52. Ezech. 34, 23. 24. 37, 25. Rom. 9, 11. resel- lens simul Calvinum, qui putavit exponi posse de principe temporali ex semine Davidis, quia his nunquam legitur attributum nomen Davidis uni- voce & simpliciter: sed ipsi dicuntur solum esse sicut David, ambulare in viis Davidis, cum ei simi- les sunt in pietate & moribus 1. Reg. 15, 3. 2. Reg. 18, 3. cap. 22, 25. Jer. 13, 13.

## 30:11
Vers. 11. FOR I WILL MAKE A CONSUMMATION AMONG ALL NATIONS) That is, I will punish them once in such a way that nothing further remains to be punished.

I WILL CHASTISE THEE IN JUDGMENT) Moderately, the same manner of speaking as above 10, 24.

THAT THOU MAYEST NOT SEEM INNOCENT TO THYSELF) The Greeks: καθαρίζων ὀ καθαριῶς, that is, I will not leave thee altogether unpunished: for καθαρίζειν often means to free from punishment among the Greeks. But the Chaldean: I will not destroy thee by destroying. The Hebrew נקה signifies both to purge and to cut off.

Latin:

Vers. 11. FACIAM ENIM CONSUMMATIONEM IN CUNCTIS GENTIBVS) Id est, semel eas ita puniam, ut nihil ultra puniendum restet.

CASTIGABO TE IN JUDICIO) Moderate, Idem loquendi genus supra 10, 24.

UT NON VIDEARIS TIBI INNOXIUS) Græ- ci: καθαρίζων ὀ καθαριῶς, id est non omnino te relinquam impunitum: nam καθαρίζειν sæpe Græcis à pœna liberare. At Chaldæus: perdendo non perdam te. נקה Hebræum & purgare & succidere significat.

## 30:12
Vers. 12. THY FRACTURE IS INCURABLE) He speaks to the people as to a woman, which the suffixes demonstrate. So also above 22, 21. He says this: Thy wound will seem desperate. Namely, when thou shalt serve for so many years.

THY PLAGUE IS VERY GRIEVOUS) In the Hebrew: Full of pain.

Latin:

Vers. 12. INSANABILIS FRACTURA TVA) Ad populum tanquam ad feminam loquitur, quod affixa de- monstrant. Sic & supra 22, 21. Hoc dicit: Vulnus tuum desperatum videbitur. Nempe cum per tot annos servies.

PESSIMA PLAGA TUA) In Hebræo: Doloris plena.

## 30:13
Vers. 13. THERE IS NONE TO JUDGE THY JUDGMENT TO BIND UP) There will be no one who may rightly judge the causes of thy wound, and apply a hand to curing it.

THERE IS NO USE OF MEDICINES FOR THEE) You might express it better thus: There will be no remedies for thee for healing.

Latin:

Vers. 13. NON EST QUI JUDICET JUDICIUM TVUM AD ALLIGANDUM) Nemo erit qui de causis tui vulneris recte judicet, ac manum ei curando admoveat.

CURATIONUM UTILITAS NON EST TI- BI) Melius sic exprimas: Nulla tibi erunt remedia ad sa- nationem.

## 30:14
Vers. 14. ALL THY LOVERS HAVE FORGOTTEN THEE) He persists in the likeness of a woman. Lovers; that is, those allies, of whom mention is made in chapter 27.

FOR I HAVE STRUCK THEE WITH THE PLAGUE OF AN ENEMY) That is, severely, as follows.

FOR THE MULTITUDE OF INIQUITY

YOURS, YOUR SINS HAVE BEEN MADE HARSH) That is, punishments. In which sense the Hebrew חַטּאת is often taken. Ver. 15. WHY DO YOU CRY OUT OVER YOUR CONTRITION, YOUR PAIN IS INCURABLE) Better: Over your desperate (namely, humanly speaking) sickness. So that it may be an exposition of the former κατὰ πρόθεσιν. V. 16. THEREFORE ALL WHO EAT YOU SHALL BE DEVOURED) More correctly: Nevertheless all, etc. Then it will appear that I was led to do these things not by hatred, but by justice. AND ALL YOUR PLUNDERERS I WILL GIVE FOR PLUNDER) See Isa. 33, 1. Ver. 17. FOR I WILL BRING A SCAR UPON YOU) But I will bring a scar upon you: that is, I will heal your wound, as follows; אֲרֻכָה translates 'scar' well. It is often found in that sense among the Rabbis as אֲרוּכָה, and in the Chaldean Paraphrast Ps. 147, 3. By metaphor it is also said thus of the repairing of walls. BECAUSE THEY SHALL CALL YOU AN OUTCAST, SION, THIS IS SHE WHO HAS NO ONE SEEKING HER) Better: although (foreigners) have called you an outcast, adding 'Sion is a city for which no one cares.' Ver. 18. I WILL TURN THE CONVERSION) Better: transmigration, as above 3. AND THE CITY SHALL BE BUILT UPON ITS HEIGHT) In its mountainous places. Jerome rightly notes that this was fulfilled in the time of Zerubbabel: and no less rightly does he refer this mystery to the Church. AND THE TEMPLE SHALL BE FOUNDED ACCORDING TO ITS ORDER) In the Hebrew is אַרְמוֹן, that is, a palace, which can be understood as the house of the Prince. But the Chaldean and the Greeks understood it as the Temple. Ver. 19. AND THE VOICE OF THOSE PLAYING) That is, of those singing: as the Greeks and the Chaldean have translated it here. So also the Latins: 'He allowed me to play what I wished on a rustic reed.' Although we do not deny that these things can be accepted regarding the bodily restoration, and that sense seems primarily to be required by the fact that the Prophet prophesies not only about the city being built again on its hills, but also about the temple being constructed according to its former form, yet those joys, nor the multiplication and glorification of those assemblies, encompass only external joys and external polity, but primarily comprehend spiritual joys and the glory and propagation of the Church at the same time. For only thus does praise and the voice of joy go forth from us, only thus are we glorified by the Lord, when we are affected with spiritual joy in the Lord, the Lord is celebrated for the return from Babylon, and we exult and are glorified and exult in the Lord. Moreover, joined to this promise is a promise concerning the Messiah, on account of whom all benefits accrue to the people, and in whom and through whom God is God to us, and we are a people to God, v. 20 and 21. And therefore the Prophet flies away from that bodily promise, according to the custom solemn to the Prophets, to Christ, in whom all promises are Yes and Amen. 2 Cor. 1. Ver. 20. AND HER CHILDREN SHALL BE AS FROM THE BEGINNING) That is, as of old. LXX: as before. THE CROWN SHALL REMAIN.) In the Hebrew: shall be established. AND I WILL VISIT AGAINST ALL THOSE WHO TROUBLE HIM.) The Babylonians, Idumeans, Ammonites shall be punished. Ver. 21. AND HER LEADER SHALL BE FROM HIM, AND A PRINCE SHALL BE PRODUCED FROM THE MIDST OF HIM) The discourse returns to Zerubbabel. They shall have a prince not external, but of their own nation. AND I WILL APPLY HIM) I will hold him most dear. AND HE SHALL APPROACH TO ME. FOR WHO IS HE WHO APPLIES HIS HEART TO APPROACH TO ME, SAYS THE LORD) You would translate more correctly: And whoever is accustomed, whoever has sweetened his heart to approach to me, shall have access to me, says the Lord. מִי is often put for 'whoever.' And the Greeks translate ערב by ἡδύνειν in many places. Ver. 23. AT THE HEAD OF THE WICKED) Of those about whom above 20. Ver. 24. IN THE LATTER DAYS YOU SHALL UNDERSTAND THESE THINGS.) At length. Namely, when the event is present. Repeated from that which is above 23, 20. Most Christian interpreters judge that by that Leader, not Zerubbabel, but Christ is to be understood. Which sense these things confirm. First, because the Holy Spirit is accustomed to turn Himself from bodily promises to Christ and spiritual benefits. Nor would He easily neglect in more significant promises Him who is the basis of all promises. Then, because the same is without doubt understood by the Leader and Prince who is to go forth from this people, who was designated at ver. 9 by David the King to be raised up for him, whom we showed above to be none other than Christ. Thirdly, because there is no one who has applied his heart to the Lord so as to approach to Him, which is said of this prince, except Christ; therefore, of this one the Lord rightly says: 'Who is this who applies his heart to approach to me?' The gloss which Grotius attaches to these words is new. The discourse is not about just anyone else who is to approach to the Lord, but about this Prince; indeed, that gloss is repugnant to the distinction of the Hebrew text; because there is an Athnach on the word אלי YOU SHALL APPROACH TO ME. Osiander explains this oracle thus: 'And the Prince of peace, our Ruler Jesus Christ, shall be produced, or shall arise, from the midst of them.' (For Christ, our leader and prince, derived his origin (according to his humanity) from his Jewish nation: from which the Church was later collected.) 'And I will apply him': i.e. I will constitute him a priest, and he shall approach to me, as the true and supreme Pontiff, and he shall be the mediator of the human race: and by one oblation of his body on the cross he shall reconcile to me all who believe in him (for Christ entered once into the holy places by an eternal redemption found, Hebr. 9). 'For who is this who most promptly applies his heart to approach to me,' says the Lord: i.e., Is not my only-begotten Son the only one who renders supreme obedience to me? namely, even unto death, even the death of the cross, Phil. 2, so that, having been made Mediator between God and men, he may approach to me by his most sacred passion, and obtain pardon for all truly penitent sinners. Fourthly, in Christ and for Christ's sake we attain this, that God becomes God to us, than which promise there is none more sublime, and that we are the people of God, enjoy the grace of God, and serve God alone, and consecrate ourselves as the people of the Lord, λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν. Fifthly, the ancients interpreted this passage from the Rabbis in such a way that they derived from it the name of the Messiah אַדִּירוֹ, his illustrious one, as it is written in the Talmud, in Chelek, where various prophetic names of the Messiah are enumerated. Rabbi said: If he is of the living, he will be like me, as it is said in Jer. 30, 21: 'And his illustrious one shall be from him.' In Midrash Tehillim on Ps. 21, these things are read: R. Berachiah said in the name of R. Samuel: One Scripture said (Daniel 7, 13: 'And he came even to the Ancient of days, and they presented him before him'): And another Scripture said (Jer. 30, 21: 'And I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me.' And behold how: The angels brought him even to the midst of them: but God extended his hand and brought him to himself. These things the Midrash says concerning the Messiah. Nor did the Chaldean [Paraphrast] interpret otherwise, who interpreted these words thus: 'And their King shall nourish himself from them, and their Messiah shall reveal himself from their midst.' Sixthly, some will derive the time of the sending of the Messiah from this passage: Thus Raymundus Martini, Pugio Fidei, part 2, cap. 9, page 313. It is to be noted that from the aforementioned words of Jeremiah, if one diligently attends, it is openly given to be understood that when the state of the sons of the Jews, who were to return from Babylon and build the temple, should be as it was of old, which was in the time of the Maccabees: the Messiah was to be born from them and to be revealed. And this is noted according to the second reward of the Targum, when it is said, 'And his leader shall be from him,' etc. Then it is shown that this would be after the conjunction of the divine and human nature in the Messiah, when it is said, 'And I will cause him to draw near to me,' etc. For since in verse 20 the Prophet says: 'And his children shall be AS FROM THE BEGINNING,' he gathers from it, that at this time he would go forth from them, the Prince Messiah, by whom they were to be brought back to that state in which they once were, when, to wit, they were oppressed under the most grievous servitude in Egypt, because the unhappiness of the people under the coming of the Messiah was no less. And to this also some refer the last words of the chapter: IN THE LATTER DAYS you shall understand, etc. Thus Lyranus and Dionysius. Jerome understands it of the latter days of the people and of the final devastation: BEHOLD THE WHIRLWIND OF THE LORD, A FURIOUS WIND GOING FORTH, etc. The whirlwind of the Lord's fury, and a rushing storm, and a tempest, shall rest upon the head of them, either of the demons or of those who blasphemed the Son of God; and He shall not turn away the anger of His indignation until He does and completes the thought of His heart, and Jerusalem is surrounded by an army and utterly destroyed. But just as an artisan cannot be understood except by the completed work, nor the industry of a physician except after health has been attained: so when the subversion of Jerusalem and the rejection of the former people shall have occurred, then believers will understand that the repulsion of the Jews is the occasion of our salvation. Thus Jerome: to whom it is indubitable that the Messiah was promised here. AND HIS LEADER WAS FROM HIM. There is no doubt, he says, that the Lord and Savior according to the flesh is from the race of Israel. And the Prince was brought forth from his midst. The Father applied Him to Himself, and He approached Him, so that the Son might say: I am in the Father and the Father in me, because no one can so apply his heart to God, nor be so joined to the Father as the Son. And what he says according to the LXX: And you shall be to me for a people, and I will be to you for a God, we see completed in work in part in Israel, and in whole in the multitude of the Gentiles. Our countrymen agree with Jerome that this discourse is about the Messiah. Our blessed Hülsemann, although he explains verse 18, 'the city shall be built upon its own hill' (according to the Hebrew, 'upon its own mound,' as that word is taken in chapter 49:2, Deut. 13:12), as follows: i.e., where now are the mounds and ruins of the ancient city, in the same place the city is to be restored, or even where mounds have been made by industry, the foundations of houses are to be placed; yet he understands verse 20, 'AND HIS LEADER SHALL BE,' of Christ, from the parallel passage in Micah 5:2, and because the consequences do not seem to be able to apply to Zerubbabel.

Latin:

Vers. 14. OMNES AMATORES TVI OBLITI SVNT TVI) Persistit in similitudine feminæ. Amatore; id est, fœderati illi, quorum mentio cap. 27.

PLAGA ENIM INIMICI PERCVSSI TE) Id est, graviter, ut sequitur.

PROPTER MULTITVDINEM INIQVITATIS

TUÆ, DURA FACTA SVNT PECCATA TUA) Id est, pœnæ. Quo sensu sæpe sumitur Hebræum חַטּאת. Vers. 15. QUID CLAMAS SUPER CONTRITIO- NE TUA, INSANABILIS EST DOLOR TUUS) Me- lius: Desperato (nempe humanitus) morbo tuo. Ut sit expo- sitio prioris κατὰ πρόθεσιν. V. 16. PROPTEREA OMNES QVI COMEDENT TE DEVORABUNTUR) Rectius: Veruntamen omnes &c. Tunc apparebit non odio, sed jure me adductum ut ista facerem. CUNCTOSQVE PRÆDATORES TUOS DA- BO IN PRÆDAM) Vid. Est eo sensu sæpe apud Rabbinos אֲרוּכָה, & in Chaldæo Paraphraste Ps. 147, 3. Per metaphoram sic etiam dicitur sarcitura murorum. QVIA EJECTAM VOCABUNT TE SION, HÆC EST QVÆ NON HABEAT REQVIRENTEM) Melius: quanquam (alienigenæ) abjectam te dixerunt, ad- dentes Sion est urbs, cujus nemo curam gerit. Vers. 18. CONVERTAM CONVERSIONEM) Me- lius: transmigrationem, ut supra 3. ET ÆDIFICABITUR CIVITAS IN EXCELSO SUO) In montanis suis locis. Hæc Zorobabelis tempore impleta recte notat Hieronymus: neque minus recte my- sterium hoc ad Ecclesiam refert. ET TEMPLUM JUXTA ORDINEM SVVM FVNDABITVR) In Hebræo est אַרְמוֹן, id est palatium, quod intelligi potest de domo Principis. Sed Chaldæus & Græci Templum intellexerunt. Vers. 19. VOXQUE LUDENTIUM) Id est canentium: quomodo hic verterunt Græci & Chaldæus. Sic & Latini: Ludere quæ vellem calamo permisit agresti. Etsi hæc de reductione corporali accipi posse non abnuamus, eumq; sensum videatur imprimis id requirere, quod non modo de civitate iterum in collibus suis ædificanda, sed etiam de templo secun- dum priorem formam exstruendo vaticinetur Propheta, non tamen illa gaudia, neque multiplica- tio & glorificatio cætuum ipsorum solum externa gaudia & externam politiam complectitur, sed im- primis gaudia spiritualia & gloriam ac propagatio- nem Ecclesiæ simul comprehendit. Nam ita demum egreditur de nobis laus & vox gaudii, ita demum glorificamur à Domino, cum gaudio spirituali in Domino afficimur, Dominus de reditu è Babylone celebratur & nos in Domino exultamus & glorifi- camur atque exultamur. Cæterum huic promis- sioni subjuncta est promissio de Messia, ob quem omnia beneficia populo obtingunt, & in quo & per quem Deus nobis in Deum est, & nos sumus Deo in populum v. 20. & 21. Ideoque avolat Propheta ab ista corporali promissione pro more Prophetis solemni ad Christum, in quo omnes promissiones ne sunt & Amen. 2. Cor. 1. Vers. 20. ET ERVNT FILII EJUS SICUT A PRINCIPIO) Id est, ut olim. LXX. ὡς τοπρότερον. CORONA PERMANEBIT.) In Hebræo: firmabitur. ET VISITABO ADVERSUM OMNES EOS QUI TRIBULANT EUM.) Babylonii, Idumæi, Ammo- nitæ punientur. Vers. 21. ET ERIT DUX EJUS EX EO, ET PRIN- CEPS DE MEDIO EJUS PRODUCETUR) Ad Zoro- babelem redit oratio. Habebunt principem non exter- num, sed suæ gentis. ET APPLICABO EUM) Habebo eum amicissimum. ET ACCEDET AD ME. QVIS ENIM EST, QVI APPLICET COR SVVM, UT APPROPINQVET MIHI, AIT DOMINVS) Rectius vertas: Et ad me adi- tum habebit quisquis solet, quisquis edulcavit cor suum ut ad me accedat, ait Dominus. מִי sæpe ponitur pro quisquis. Et ערב per ἡδύνειν vertunt Græci multis in locis. Vers. 23. IN CAPITE IMPIORVM) Illorum de qui- bus supra 20. Vers. 24. IN NOVISSIMO DIERVM INTELLIGE- TIS EA.) Tandem. Nempe ubi eventus aderit. Repeti- tum ex eo quod supra 23, 20. Per Ducem illum non Zorobabelem, sed Chri- stum intelligendum esse pleriq; Interpretes Chri- stiani censent. Quem sensum hæc firmant. Primo quod Spiritus Sanctus consueverit à promissioni- bus corporalibus sese ad Christum & spiritua- lia beneficia convertere. Neque facile negligat in infignioribus promiffionibus illum, qui bafis eft omnium promiffionum. Deinde quod idem fine dubio intelligatur per Ducem & Principem ex hoc populo egreffurum, qui verf. 9. per Davidem Re- gem ipfi excitandum defignatus eft, quem nul- lum alium effe quam Chriftum fupra oftendimus. Tertio quod nemo fit, qui cor fuum applicarit Do- mino, ut eidem appropinquaret, quod de hoc prin- cipe dicitur, præter Chriftum, de hoc ergo merito Dominus: Quis iste est, qui applicet cor suum, ut mi- hi appropinquet? Gloffa, quam his verbis allinit Grotius, nova eft. Non de quolibet alio acceffuro ad Dominum, fed de hoc Principe fermo eft; imo repugnat ifta gloffa diftinctioni textus Ebræi; quia Athnach habetur in voce אלי ACCEDES AD ME. Ofiander ita exponit hoc oraculum: Et Prin- ceps pacis, Dominator noster Iesus Christus, de me- dio eorum producetur, seu orietur. (Chriftus enim, dux & princeps nofter originem (juxta humani- tatem,) duxit è gente fua Judaica: ex qua poftea collecta eft Ecclefia) Et applicabo eum: i. e. Sacerdotem conftituam eum, & ille accedet ad me, tanquam verus & fummus Pontifex, eritque mediator generis humani: atque una oblatione corporis fui in cruce reconciliabit mihi omnes, qui in ipfum credunt (ingressus est enim Christus semel in sancta æterna redemtione inventa, Hebr. 9.) Quis enim iste est, qui promptissime applicet cor suum, ut appropinquet mihi, ait Dominus: i. e. Nonne uni- genitus Filius meus folus eft ille, qui obedientiam mihi præftat fummam? nimirum usq; ad mortem, mortem autem crucis, Phil. 2. ut Mediator inter Deum & homines factus accedat ad me, facratiffi- ma fua paffione, & impetret veniam omnibus vere pœnitentibus peccatoribus. Quarto in Chrifto & propter Chriftum confequimur id, ut Deus nobis in Deum fit, qua promiffione nulla eft fublimior, & ut nos fimus Dei populus, Dei gratia fruamur, Deoque uni ferviamus, & nos confecremus, ceu populus Domini λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν. Quinto ita è Rabbinis veteres interpretati hunc locum funt, at- que inde nomen Meffiæ depromferunt אַדִּירוֹ in- clytus ejus, uti fcriptum eft in Talmude, in Chelek, ubi varia Meffiæ nomina prophetica recenfentur. Dixit Rab. si est de vivis, erit sicut ego, sicut dictum est Jer. 30, 21.) Et erit inclytus ejus ex eo. In Midrasch Tillim fuper Pf. 21. hæc leguntur: R. Berachia in no- mine R. Samuel dixit: una Scriptura dixit (Daniel. 7, 13. Et usque ad antiquum dierum pervenit, & co- ram eo obtulerunt illum: Et alia Scriptura dixit (Jer. 30, 21.) Et applicabo eum, & accedet ad me, Et ecce qualiter: Angeli introduxerunt usq́; ad medium eorum: Deus autem extendit manum suam & intro- ducit ipsum ad se. Hæc Midrafch de Meffia. Nec ali- ter Chaldæus, qui hæc verba ita interpretatus eft: Et nutriet se Rex eorum ex ipsis, & Messias eorum de me- dio eorum revelabit se. Sexto tempus mittendi Mef- fiæ ex hoc loco erunt nonnulli: Sic Raymundus Martini Pug. Fid. part. 2. cap. 9. pag 313. Notan- dum quod ex prædictis Ieremiæ verbis, si quis dili- genter attendat, aperte datur intelligi, quod quando filiorum Iudæorum, qui de Babylonia erant reversuri, & templum ædificaturi, fuisset status eorum, sicut an- tiquitus, qui fuit tempore Maccabæorum: nasciturus erat ex iis Messias & revelandus. Et hoc notatur se- cundum præmium Targum, cum dicitur, Et erit dux ejus ex eo &c. Deinde ostenditur, quod hoc esset post conjunctionem divinæ & humanæ naturæ in Mes- sia, cum dicitur, Et appropinquavero ad eum, &c. Quum enim versu 20. dicat Propheta: Et erunt filii ejus SICUT A PRINCIPIO, ex eo colligit, isto- tempore egressurum ex ipsis Principem Messiam, quo ad illum statum redigendi erant, in quo olim fuere, cum sc. sub gravissima servitute premerentur in Ægy- pto, quia non minor infelicitas erat populi sub adven- tum Messiæ. Atque eo etiam referunt nonnulli ver- ba postrema capitis. IN NOVISSIMO DIERVM intelligetis &c. Ita Lyranus, & Dionysius. Hierony- mus de novissimis diebus populi, & de novissima de- vastatione intelligit, ECCE TURBO DOMINI EUROR EGREDIENS &c. Turbo furoris Do- mini, & procella ruens, atque tempestas, requiescet in capite eorum, vel dæmonum, vel eorum qui Dei fi- lium blasphemarunt; & non avertet iram indigna- tionis suæ, donec faciat & compleat cogitationem cor- dis sui, & circundetur exercitu Hierusalem & peni- tus deleatur. Quomodo autem artifex non potest intelligi nisi opere completo, nec medici industria, nisi postquam fuerit sanitas consecuta: ita cum u- versio fuerit Hierusalem & prioris populi abjectio, tunc intelligent credentes, quod repulsio Judæo- rum nostræ salutis occasio sit. Hæc Hieronymus: cui indubium est, hic promissum fuisse Messiam. ET FUIT DUX EJUS EX EO. Haud dubium, inquit, quin Dominus & Salvator secundum car- nem ex genere Israel. Et Princeps de medio ejus pro- ductus est. Applicavit eum Pater ad se, & accessit ad eum, ut diceret filius: Ego in Patre & Pater in me, quia nullus potest sic cor suum applicare Deo, nec ita ut Filius Patri esse conjunctus. Quodque dicit juxta LXX. Et eritis mihi in populum: & ego ero vobis in Deum, cernimus opere completum ex parte in I- srael, & ex toto in gentium multitudine. Hieronymo congruunt nostrates, quod hic sermo sit de Messia. B. Hülsemannus noster, etsi versu 18. ædificabitur ci- vitas in excelso suo, juxta Ebr. super tumulum suum, uti vox illa accipitur cap. 49, 2. Deut. 13, 12. ita ex- plicet: q. d. ubi nunc tumuli, & rudera civitatis an- tiquæ sunt, eodem loco restaurandam esse civitatem, vel etiam, ubi tumuli sunt ex industria facti, funda- menta ædium collocanda, versum tamen 20. ET ERIT DUX EJUS de Christo intelligit è loco parallelo Mich. 5, 2. & quod consequentia non vi- deantur Zorobabeli convenire posse.

## 31:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXI.

Concerning the propagation of Israel, and the turning of mourning into joy, where Rachel, bewailing her children, is also affected with consolation, and to the faithful, because of the Messiah who is to arise in a new way, and through the grace of the New Covenant, refreshment and the amplification of the Church is promised.

Ver. 1.

I AM GOD) אלהים, that is, a just Judge. AND THEY SHALL BE TO ME FOR A PEOPLE) To me, that they may obey me as their King,

A notable promise is perverted, which is repeated from the covenant entered into with Abraham in Gen. 17 and confirmed by the Sacrament of circumcision; for it is not justice that is indicated, but the grace of benefits that is promised: when God promises that He will be the God of someone. For to him He offers and promises perennial grace and all manner of benefits, both temporal and spiritual and everlasting, just as is indicated everywhere this promise occurs, whence its effect extends even to the other life, as Christ testifies in Matt. 22 and Apoc. 21, so that not without reason our Brentius pronounced on this passage: there is no greater promise than this: I will be God. And it is to be observed that this promise was made not to the Jewish people, or to two tribes only, but to ALL THE FAMILIES

OF ISRAEL, and thus the same distinction between the Kingdom of Judah and Israel is removed, and it is predicted that both kingdoms are to be held as the same people. Wherefore this promise pertains to the times of the New Testament, even if phrases are employed that are solemn to the time of the Old Testament and bear the appearance of a return from the Babylonian captivity, because under such wrappings of words the Prophets were accustomed to designate spiritual things without a double sense. For it is one thing, as we warn again, that phrases were used which refer to that return, and another that those phrases in this text, from the intention of the Holy Spirit, whether primarily or secondarily, express that return, and that the Prophet is prophesying about the same in this place. The certainty of the promised liberation of the people of God being supposed, the use of such locutions can be admitted, but that these oracles obtain a double sense from the mind and intention of the Holy Spirit is by no means to be believed. Having weighed this observation, we approve the Osiandrian Paraphrase: Again the Prophet (under phrases concerning the return from the Babylonian captivity) prophesies about the Kingdom of grace under the New Testament, and indeed copiously. In that time, says the Lord, I will be a clement and merciful God to all the families of Israel: and they shall be to me for a people. i.e., There will no longer be a distinction between the Kingdom of Judah and the Kingdom of Israel: as there was under the former kings: when the Israelites, who belonged to the Kingdom of Israel, were almost all polluted with impious and idolatrous cults, so that I abhorred them. But now I embrace the whole people of Israel with paternal benevolence, I will acknowledge them as sons and heirs of heavenly goods, and they in turn will show me obedience (This is, whoever shall have repented and believed the Gospel of Christ, shall be saved, from whatever family, tribe, or nation he may be sprung. For the Israelites in the New Testament are all who believe in Christ, Gal. VI.) Finally, even if you refer the promise to the times of Ezra and Nehemiah, its more perfect complement is under the New Testament, which can be established without a double sense of the Prophetic oracle. For God promised grace to His people, which He began to exhibit when He led them back from captivity. For even then He was their God in the promised land, and they were the people of the Lord; but He exhibited it more fully at the time of the N.T. when from that people He gathered a Church, which was to be propagated through the whole world, for then to all the families of Israel, the distinction of the kingdom of Judah and Israel having been removed, saving grace was exhibited, and from them the Church was propagated to all the nations. Blessed Bugenhagen rightly weighed these things, and at the same time noted the coherence with the preceding chapter, fol. 310.
