At that time, or at the same time, namely in the last of the days, when with a violent whirlwind, fury, and terrible power I shall cast away all the impious, contemners, and incredulous Israelites and Jews, who were never the people of God, except through hypocrisy and lying, who were never before God the children of Abraham, or the children of Israel, even if according to flesh and blood they were Rom. 4. Rom. 9. &c. John the Baptist says: God is able of these stones to raise up children of Abraham. Then, he says, I shall not be God without the people of Israel, but I shall be God to all the families of Israel and the families themselves shall be to me a people, that is, the believing children of God, the impious Israelites being cast away &c. And furthermore: That which he adds: To all the families of Israel, and they themselves shall be to me a people, the same not only to the tribe of Judah and Benjamin, which after seventy years were restored to their lands, likewise that afterwards he also makes mention of all Jacob and Ephraim and Samaria, in this promise of grace, certainly shows that he is promising a greater and more ample release from captivity than that Babylonian one. For the ten tribes were not so restored from their own seats and lands, as two. For the land of these two tribes kept a perpetual Sabbath for seventy years, as the history holds: But the land of those others had received the Samaritans two hundred years before the Babylonian captivity was ended, who also remained there, as you see even in the Evangelical history. This is our Bugenhagius.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXI.

De Israelis propagatione, & luctu in gaudium convertendo, ubi Rachel liberos deplorans etiam consolatione afficitur, & fidelibus ob Messiam nova ratione oriturum, & per No- vi fœderis gratiam, refectio, & Ecclesiæ amplificatio promittitur.

Vers. 1.

EGO DEVS) אלהים, id est, Judex justus. ET IPSI ERVNT MIHI IN POPVLVM) Mihi ut Regi suo obedieut,

PErvertitur insignis promissio, quæ è fœdere cű Abrahamo Gen. 17. inito & Sacramento cir- cumcisionis firmato repetitur; Nõ enim justitia in- dicatur, sed gratia benefactorum promittitur: cum Deus se Deum alicujus fore pollicetur. Huic enim perrennem gratiam, & beneficia quævis cum tem- poralia, tum spiritualia & sempiterna offert, ac pro- mittit, quemadmodum passim, ubi hæc promissio occurrit, indicatur, unde etiam ad alteram vitam effectus ejusdem sese porrigit, teste Christo Matth. 22. & Apoc. 21. ut non abs re Brentius noster ad h. l. pronunciarit, non est major promissio, quam hæc: Ego ero Deus. Et observandum, promissionem hanc fa- ctam esse non populo Judaico, vel duabus tribubus tantum, sed UNIVERSIS COGNATIONIBUS

ISRAEL, adeoque tolli eadem discrimen inter Re- gnum Juda & Israel, & prædici, utrumque regnum pro eodem populo habendum esse. Quapropter pertinet hæc promissio ad tempora Novi Testamen- ti, etsi phrases adhibeantur Veteris Testamenti tempori solemnes & reditum à captivitate Babylo- nica præ se ferentes, quia sub talibus involucris ver- borum folebant Prophetæ res spirituales designare citra sensuum διττότητα. Aliud enim est, quod ite- rum monemus, phrases adhibitas esse, quæ reditum illu referant, aliud phrases istas in hoc textu ex in- tentione Spiritus S. sive πρώτως sive δευτέρως redi- tum illum exprimere, ac de eodem Prophetam in hoc loco vaticinari. Supponi certitudinem promif- sæ alias liberationis populi Domini, per usurpatio- nem talium loquutionum, admitti potest, at du- plicem sensum hæc oracula ex mente & intentione Spiritus Sancti obtinere, minime credendum est. Qua observatione pensi habita, probamus Osian- drinam Paraphrasin; Rursus Propheta (sub phrafi- bus de reditu à captivitate Babylonica) vaticinatur de Regno gratiæ sub Novo Testamento & quidem co- piosè. In tempore illo, dicit Dominus, ero clemens & misericors Deus, universis cognationibus Israel: & ipsi erunt mihi in populum. i. e. Non amplius erit discrimen inter Regnum Juda & Regnum Israel: si- cut fuit sub regibus prioribus: quando fere Israelitæ, qui ad Regnum Israelis pertinebant, impiis & idolo- latricis cultibus erant polluti, ita ut eos abominarer. Sed jam totum populum Israel benevolentia paterna complector, agnoscam eos pro filiis & hæredibus cæ- lestium bonorum, & ipsi mihi vicissim obedientiam exhibebunt (Hoc est, quisquis pœnitentiam egerit & crediderit Evangelio Christi, salvus erit, ex qua- cunque familia, tribu aut gente sit oriundus. Israe- litæ enim in Novo Testamento sunt omnes in Chri- stum credentes, Gal, VI.) Deniq; etiamsi promif- sionem referas ad tempora Esdræ & Nehemiæ, per- fectius tamen complementum ejus est sub Nov. Testam. quod statui potest citra διττότητα sensus oraculi Prophetici. Nam promisit Deus gratiam populo suo, quam exhibere cepit, cum reduxit eos è captivitate. Nam & tum ipsorum Deus fuit in ter- ra promissa, & ipsi erant populus Domini; sed ple- nius exhibuit tempore N. T. cum è populo isto collegit Ecclesiam, quæ propaganda erat per totu orbem, tum enim universis cognationibus Israelis sublato discrimine regni Juda & Israel gratia exhi- bita est σωτήριος, & ex illis propagata ad gentes u- niversas Ecclesia. Recte hæc expendit B. Bugenha- gius, simulque cohærentiam cum cap. præcedente notavit fol. 310. In illo tempore, vel in eodem tempore, videlicet in novissimo dierum, quando vehementi turbine, furore & terribili potestate abjecero o- mnes impios, contemptores, & incredulos Israeli- tas & Judæos, qui nunquam fuerunt populus Dei, nisi per hypocrisin & mendacium, qui nunquam fuerunt coram Deo filii Abrahæ, vel filii Israel, etiamsi secun- dum carnem & sanguinem essent Rom. 4. Rom. 9. &c. Johannes Baptista dicit: Potens est Deus de lapidi- bus istis suscitare filios Abrahæ. Tunc, inquit, non ero Deus absq; populo Israel, sed ero Deus omnibus cognationibus Israel & ipsæ cognationes erunt mi- hi populus, id est, credentes filii Dei, abjectis impiis Israelitis &c. Et porro: Quod autẽ addit: Omnibus cognationibus Israel, & ipsæ erunt mihi populus, i- dem non soli tribui Judæ & Benjamin, quæ post septua- ginta annos restitutæ sunt suis terris, item quod postea etiã totius Jacob & Ephraim & Samariæ meminit, in hac gratiæ promissione, certe ostendit se majore & am- pliorem solutione captivitatis, quam illius Babylonicæ promittere. Nam decem tribus non sunt ita restitutæ- suis sedibus & terris, ut duo. Harum enim duarum tribuum terra septuaginta annis perpetuum egit Sab- batum, ut habet historia: Illarum autem terra du- centis annis ante solutam captivitatem Babylonicam Samaritanos acceperat, qui & ibi permanserunt, ut vides etiam in historia Evangelica. Hæc Bugenha- gius noster.

## 31:2
Vers. 2. THE PEOPLE FOUND GRACE IN THE DESERT] God repeats ancient benefits, so that new ones may be the more hoped for. In the desert I provided for them regarding all necessities. Here Jerome rightly observes that the seventy elders read זקנ instead of הרג.

WHO HAD REMAINED FROM THE SWORD) Who had escaped the sword of the Egyptians.

ISRAEL SHALL GO TO HIS REST) Better, he went: that is, the Amalekites, Canaanites, Philistines, and others could not prevent the Jews from arriving at quiet seats. The land of Judea is called κατάπαυσις Ps. 95, 11. Heb. 3, 11.

There is no reason why the tenses should be changed, so that the future becomes the past, and the promise of a new benefit becomes a remembrance of an old one. HE SHALL GO, says the Lord, to the rest of Israel: to whom He had promised before; I will be a GOD to him, and they shall be a people to me. But what stands in the way of our taking the words, as they sound, in the sense of a promise? i.e., Just as the people rescued from Egypt once found grace in the desert, so I will have mercy also on the Israelites who survived the sword or exile; they shall find grace and shall go to their rest. They find grace as it were, that is, they are acceptable to God, who, being established in the horrors and terrors of conscience, hear the sweet voice of the Gospel concerning Christ and believe in the Gospel of Christ.

And since the Israelites returning from Babylon had not much rest in their own country, but were rather mocked and troubled by neighboring nations, as the writings of Ezra and Nehemiah testify, it is manifest that the Prophet is dealing in this place with spiritual rest. Christ speaks of this, saying: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you; Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you shall find rest for your souls Matth. 11. And those who through faith have obtained tranquility of conscience, finally after this life enter into the true and eternal rest, of which the Apostle speaks in the 4th chapter of Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 2. INVENIT GRATIAM IN DESERTO PO- PULUS] Repetit Deus vetera beneficia, quo magis nova sperentur. In deserto prospexi illis de omnibus necessariis. Hic pro הרג LXX. senes legisse זקנ recte observat Hierony- mus.

QUI REMANSERAT A GLADIO) Qui evaserat gladium Ægyptiorum.

VADET AD REQUIEM SUAM ISRAEL) Me- lius, ivit: id est, non potuerunt impedire Amaleckitæ, Cananæi, Philistini, atque alii, quo minus pervenirent Ju- dæi ad sedes quietas. Terra Judæa vocatur κατάπαυσις Ps. 95, 11. Hebr. 3, 11.

Non est cur tempora mutentur, ut è futuro evadat præteritum, & è promissione novi beneficii ve- teris rememoratio. VADET, inquit Dominus, ad requiem Israel: cui antea promiserat; Ero ei DEUS, & ipsi erunt mihi in populum. Quid vero obstat, quo minus verba, uti sonant, sensu promissionis ac- cipiamus? q. d. Quemadmodum olim in deserto gratiam invenit populus ereptus ex Ægypto, ita miserebor & Israelitarum, qui superfuerunt gladio vel exilio; gratiam invenient & vadent ad requiem suam. Inveniunt quasi gratiam, hoc est, sunt Deo accepti, qui in horroribus & terroribus conscientiæ constituti suavem Evangelii vocem de Christo au- diunt & Evangelio Christi credunt.

Et quum Israelitæ redeuntes è Babylone non multum quietis in patria sua habuerint: sed potius à vicinis gentibus fuerint irrisi & tribulati, ut Esdræ & Nehemiæ scripta testantur, manifestum est Pro- phetam hoc loco de spirituali requie agere. De hac loquitur Christus dicens: Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis, ego reficiam vos; Tollite jugum meum super vos & discite à me, quia mitis sum, & humilis corde, & invenietis requiem anima- bus vestris Matth. 11. Et qui per fidem consecuti sunt conscientiæ tranquillitatem, tandem post hanc vitam ingrediuntur veram & æternam re- quiem, de qua Apostolus loquitur Ebr. 4. cap.

## 31:3
Vers. 3. THE LORD APPEARED TO ME FROM AFAR) Formerly the Lord showed Himself to me: namely, as benevolent, as if he were saying not now. These are the words of the Jewish nation, which is set before the eyes here also, as a woman.

AND I HAVE LOVED THEE WITH PERPETUAL CHARITY) God answers the nation. Indeed, I have loved thee with a perennial love. That is, I have never omitted anything that was my part.

THEREFORE I HAVE DRAWN THEE PITYING) I draw thee, that is, I exhort thee to repentance.

Latin:

Vers. 3. LONGE DOMINUS APPARVIT MIHI) Olim Dominus se mihi ostendit: nempe benevolum, quasi di- cat non nunc. Verba sunt gentis Judaicæ, quæ hic etiam, ut femina ob oculos ponitur.

ET IN CHARITATE PERPETUA DILEXI TE) Respondet Deus genti. Imo perenni amare te dilexi. Id est, nunquam quicquam omisi, quod mearum esset partium.

IDEO ATTRAXI TE MISERANS) Attraho te, id est, ad resipiscentiam exhortor.

## 31:4
Vers. 4. AND I WILL BUILD THEE AGAIN) When thou shalt have turned to me, I will cause thee to have houses again.

AND THOU SHALT BE BUILT) And thou shalt possess them safely.

THOU SHALT YET BE ADORNED WITH THY TIMBREL, AND SHALT GO FORTH IN THE DANCE OF THEM THAT PLAY) As women were accustomed to do. 1 Reg. 18, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 4. RVRSVMQVE ÆDIFICABO TE) Ubi con- versa fueris ad me, faciam rursus habeas domos.

ET ÆDIFICABERIS) Et tuto eas possideas.

ADHUC ORNABERIS TYMPANIS TVIS, ET EGREDIERIS IN CHORO LVDENTIVM) Ut feminæ solebant. 1. Reg. 18, 6.

## 31:5
Vers. 5. YOU SHALL PLANT VINEYARDS IN THE MOUNTAINS OF SAMARIA) Demetrius in the Epistle to the Jews, which exists in Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews 13, 5: 'And of the three toparchies which were added to Judea from Samaria, and Galilee and Perea, these I cede to you from now for all time.' Add the same Josephus, 13, 17.

AND UNTIL THE TIME COMES, THEY SHALL NOT VINTAGE) For these words in Hebrew it is 'they shall profane': That is, they shall eat the fruits of the vineyard at the legitimate time. Understand this from the law in Leviticus 19, 25. Compare also Deuteronomy 20, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PLANTABIS VINEAS IN MONTIBVS SA MARIÆ) Demetrius in Epistola ad Judæos, quæ extat apud Josephum Antiquæ Historiæ 13, 5. καὶ τῶν τριῶν τοπαρχιῶν τῶν τῇ Ιυδαίᾳ προσκειμένων Σαμαρείας, καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Πε- ραίας, τάτας παραχωρῶ ὑμῖν ἀπὸ τῦ νῦν εἰς τὸν ἅπαντα χρόνον. Adde eundem Josephum. 13, 17.

ET DONEC TEMPVS VENIAT, NON VINDE- MIABVNT) pro his verbis in Hebræo est profanabunt: Id est, vescentur fructibus vineæ legitimo tempore. Hoc intel- lige ex lege Levit. 19, 25. Confer & Deut. 20, 6.

## 31:6
Vers. 6. THE WATCHMEN SHALL CRY OUT ON MOUNT EPHRAIM) The Jews, who are going to dwell there. Watchmen in Hebrew is נצרים, netzarim, which you may very well draw to a mystical sense concerning the Church: for Christians are even now called by this name by the Jews.

EXULT IN THE JOY OF JACOB) That is, take each your own part in the public joy. For here is Jacob with the lamed, which is often a sign of the genitive.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CLAMABVNT CVSTODES IN MONTE EPHRAIM) Judæi, qui ibi sunt habitaturi. Custodes in He- bræo נצרים, נצרי, quod ad mysticum sensum de Ecclesia optime trahas: nam Christiani à Judæis nunc quoque hoc nomine vocantur.

EXVLTATE IN LÆTITIA JACOB) Id est, in publica lætitia suam quisque partem sumite. Est enim hic Jacob cum ל, quæ nota sæpe genitivi.

## 31:7
Vers. 7. NEIGH AGAINST THE HEAD OF THE NATIONS) That is, utter a clear voice in the sight of all the nations.

SAY: SAVE, O LORD] ἀταντά. Vers. 8. FROM THE LAND OF THE NORTH] From Media, and the surrounding lands. AMONG WHOM SHALL BE THE BLIND AND THE LAME] No one will want to be absent. But the LXX read בַּעֲצָרָה, pesach, that is, as if in the feast of the Passover, in which a very great multitude used to gather. THE PREGNANT AND THE ONE GIVING BIRTH TOGETHER] Neither the womb nor the impending birth shall delay the women. But the LXX wish for the greatest fertility to be signified. A GREAT CONGREGATION] A huge army, as the Chaldean here. Vers. 9. THEY SHALL COME IN WEEPING] Better, they shall go in weeping: namely, when they were being led away. The Chaldean understood it thus. The Greeks: 'they went out in weeping.' AND I WILL LEAD THEM BY THE TORRENTS OF WATERS] In the Hebrew and Chaldean, 'by the brooks of waters': that is, there shall not be lacking to those making the journey that which they may drink. IN A STRAIGHT WAY, AND THEY SHALL NOT STUMBLE IN IT] In a way so level that they shall not be about to stumble in it. Vers. 10. AND EPHRAIM IS MY FIRSTBORN] So dear, as firstborns are wont to be. This is because some of the Israelites of the X tribes returned with the Jews. See Ezra 2, and above 33, 3. V. 11. FOR THE LORD HAS REDEEMED JACOB] He shall redeem. AND HAS DELIVERED.] He shall deliver. Vers. 12. AND THEIR SOUL SHALL BE AS A WATERED GARDEN] Full of joy. AND I WILL INEBRIATE THE SOUL OF THE PRIESTS WITH FATNESS] I will satisfy the priests with fat victims.

Grotius understands all these things concerning bodily benefits. He acknowledges, however, that it is very well drawn to a mystical sense concerning the Church. But there is no trace of a double sense here. That it treats of the Church in the literal sense is not obscure from the preceding, where the subject was designated as Israel, and these promises were made to all the families of Israel: but that all the families of Israel according to the flesh went to rest, were rebuilt again, and adorned, and filled with external joys in their fatherland, and planted vineyards again in the mountains of Samaria, experience loudly protests against. Therefore these things are to be understood concerning the Israelites according to the Spirit, and concerning the Church of Christ in the literal sense: to which is promised spiritual building through the preaching of the Gospel, and adornment and spiritual joy. For the hearts of the pious exult in the consideration of the huge benefits of Christ, and they go out with timbrels and flutes, when they celebrate with Psalms and hymns the mercy of God exhibited in Christ. The Churches of Christ are planted as vineyards and are preserved, so that the ministers of the word who plant may receive spiritual fruit with joy. Whence the Lord Himself exclaims: Exult in the joy of Jacob (my people) and neigh, OVER THE HEAD OF THE NATIONS, (CHRIST, who is not only the Messiah of the Jews, but also the prince and head of the nations) SOUND FORTH, AND SING: AND SAY, save, O Lord, thy people, namely the remnant of Israel. To which pertains that Hosanna, which was acclaimed to Christ, Matthew 21. Through Him the remnants of the people of God are saved. For the number of those who do not believe the Gospel is greater than those who are saved. Whence it is added, HEAR THE WORD OF THE LORD, O YOU NATIONS. For the Gospel of Christ shall be preached to you also, and with joy, and congratulating, announce (the benefits of Christ conferred upon the Church) in the Islands, in various and remote places, which are situated far away, and say: He who once scattered the people of Israel, the Lord our God, He shall gather him again and shall guard him, as a shepherd his flock (For Christ is the good shepherd, who laid down His life for His flock, John 10. He, through the preaching of the Gospel, feeds and cares for the gathered sheep most humanely. Ezekiel 34.) For the Lord Jehovah Christ Jesus shall redeem Jacob, His people, and shall deliver him from the hand of the stronger one. (For Christ overcame that strong and armed one, Satan, Luke 11, and through His death destroyed him who had the power of death, that is,

the Devil, Heb. 2.) And they shall come & shall praise in mount Sion; more correctly: They shall jubilate in the heights of Sion, that is: Those who have heard the Gospel concerning Christ, with great joy will join themselves to the Church shadowed forth by mount Sion & will flow together to share in the goods of the Lord, which the Lord will liberally give to them, and they shall rejoice over the grain & wine & oil & the offspring of the flocks & herds: for they shall have all these things abundantly: and their soul shall be as a watered garden, to which no heat, however great, can do harm: & they shall no longer hunger. Heb. they shall not grieve (i. e. Christians shall be fed & shall be given to drink copiously & liberally with the word of the Gospel, by which their hearts shall be truly exhilarated. They shall also be fed & given to drink in the Holy Supper of the Lord with the body and blood of Jesus Christ, God and man: nor shall anything that pertains to true salvation be lacking to them. Moreover, they shall be anointed with oil, that is, with the gifts of the Holy Spirit: and they shall be prepared for all good works. And, like a garden always watered, they shall bear many good fruits. And if any adversities must be borne, they shall bear them cheerfully, with the joy of the Holy Spirit overcoming the pain, until they are transferred into the heavenly life, where there shall be true, perpetual, & solid joy, and where there shall no longer be any pain or any sadness. As Osiander not inappropriately says here. THEN INDEED THE VIRGIN SHALL REJOICE (singular for plural) IN THE CHOIR &c. He says the virgins, young men and old men rejoice in the Choir: Signifying that the Church rejoices in the communication of heavenly benefits & gifts, by which the members of the Church serve one another: whence they rejoice mutually among themselves. Then indeed this promise will be entirely fulfilled, when, freed from all the evils of this life, we shall enjoy eternal gladness. For then all tears shall be wiped away from our eyes Apoc. 20. AND I WILL SATIATE THE SOUL OF THE PRIESTS WITH FATNESS, i. e. I will feed my priests most liberally, so that they might seem to be satiated as if with fat: AND MY PEOPLE SHALL BE FILLED WITH MY GOOD THINGS, SAYS THE LORD. (And although all Christians are priests before God, 1 Pet. 2, and therefore all are fed largely with the word of the Gospel, by which their minds are refreshed: yet the Lord is accustomed to pour out a richer knowledge of the Gospel upon those who are set over others to teach in the Church: so that they may not only have that by which they themselves are refreshed in conscience, but that they may also be able to provide rich consolations to others.) The commentary of Brentius agrees with this, as does the exposition of the blessed Pappus, who observes that promises of four kinds are handed down here, namely the adoption of the spiritual Israel ver. 1, the propagation of the doctrine of the Gospel ver. 2, up to 7, the defense of the Church against various dangers ver. 7, 8, 9. & the calling of the Gentiles to the Society of the Church ver. 10, up to 14. The same was the mind of St. Jerome, that these things are to be understood according to the literal sense solely concerning the Church. I WILL BUILD THEE AND THOU SHALT BE BUILT, O VIRGIN ISRAEL. Let us understand this properly in the Church. And further. AMONG WHOM SHALL BE THE BLIND AND THE LAME &c. The remnants of the people of Israel are gathered by the Apostles & apostolic men, of whom we read above: The watchmen shall cry on the mount, and to whom it is commanded: Sound, sing, and say, that the remnants of Israel may be saved. That which is written in Hebrew, among whom shall be the blind and the lame and the pregnant and the one giving birth together, this is the great Church of those returning, although it may have been fulfilled according to the letter, that the blind saw, the lame walked, yet it can be better understood according to the Anagoge, that those who were previously blind by perfidy, afterwards believed in the Savior, and those who were lame, to whom Elijah once spoke: How long do you halt between two opinions, afterwards walked: and the people, who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, saw a great light, and the lame ran, and the pregnant woman brought forth sons. Concerning those words, the great Church of those returning to the faith, Jerome has this: The Jews think this was completed when under Ezra after the day of Passover they went out of Babylon, to return to Jerusalem, in which there was a type and not the truth: For they will not be able to prove that at that time all things which we read and are about to read were completed. And afterwards to those words, HEAR THE WORD OF THE LORD: He says the calling of the Gentiles is clearly demonstrated, the scripture saying: Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles that are afar off and say: What do they declare to the Isles that are afar off? That the Lord, who scattered Israel, he will gather him. Therefore it was by no means the power of adversaries that they were scattered, but the will of the Lord. And he shall keep him as a shepherd his flock, for the good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. Because God redeemed Jacob, by the price of his blood, and delivered him from the hand of the stronger or mightier. By which are shown the stronger adversary powers of the nature of human frailty. And as much as there is strength in both, that they are stronger by nature, but we are stronger by faith, if indeed we deserve to be delivered by him, who can bind the strong man and plunder his house. And they shall come, he says, there is no doubt, but that they are freed from the hand of the powerful and shall praise their deliverer on mount Sion, that is, in the Church, and shall flow together to the goods of the Lord, the abundance of all things, which is felt not in the fruits and foods of the flesh itself, but in the variety of virtues. Over the grain, he says, and wine and oil, from which the bread of the Lord is made, and the type of his blood is fulfilled, and the blessing of Sanctification is shown, the scripture saying: God thy God hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. And the offspring of the flocks, who are the simple in the Church, and of the herds, which are horned, and toss the adversaries. But that we may know that these blessings pertain by no means to the body but to the soul, it follows: And their soul shall be as a watered garden, or as a fruit-bearing tree, which is planted by the courses of waters, and the paradise of the Lord in delights. And further, he says, they shall not hunger, not with that hunger of which it is written: Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness, but with that which is changed by satiety and excludes the penury of all things. Then the virgin shall rejoice in the choir, of whom the Apostle writes: For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. And the young men, to whom John speaks: I write unto you, young men, because you have overcome the wicked one. And the old men, to whom the same one testifies in mystical language: I write unto you, Fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. And I will turn, he says, their mourning into joy, so that those whom the cross had terrified, the resurrection may gladden, And I will comfort them and make them rejoice from their sorrow, according to that which the Lord speaks: Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted. And I will inebriate the soul of the priests, who have the knowledge of God, from whose mouth they seek the law of the Lord, who believe in him, to whom the Prophet sings: Thou art a Priest forever according to the order of Melchisedech. But what follows according to the LXX, 'of the sons of Levi', is not held in the Hebrew. And it is clear that this is by no means said of those priests who are sons of Levi, but of those in whose type Melchisedech went before. Moreover, the drunkenness of the Priests is also proven in the Apostles, when they were fervent in faith, and were said to be full of new wine. Whence also the place in which the Lord was seized is called Gethsemani, which in our language means the valley of fatness ness. And when the priests have been fat with the doctrine of the Lord, and having been inebriated at the banquet of Joseph have said: How excellent is your inebriating cup, then will this also be, which the Lord now promises: And my people shall be filled with my good things. All of which are now bestowed in part: but then they shall be given in full, when we shall have seen face to face, and the body of our humility shall have been changed by the glory of the resurrection. Thus Jerome, whose words excellently illustrate our passage. Among the Papists, Cornel. a Lapide acknowledges this sense, who also praises Rabanus, Lyranus, and Vatablus for it. Nor do Maldonatus and Tirinus deny that the passage is to be understood of the Church arising from the Samaritans, Acts 8. Menochius, however, praised by Grotius, uniquely approves that explanation which understands it in the literal sense concerning the conversion of the Samaritans in the time of the New Testament. At verse 5. YOU SHALL YET PLANT VINEYARDS ON THE MOUNT OF SAMARIA: It is necessary to understand these things concerning the conversion of the Samaritans to the faith of Christ, and by vineyards, particular Churches, as if he were saying, I will convert many to you, O Sion, O Church of Christ, in Samaria, through the preaching of the Gospel, so that you may found many Churches of the Samaritans there. It was so done John 4:41, Acts 8:14; for it is certain that the Samaritans, that is, the ten tribes, led away into captivity by the Assyrians, never returned to Samaria. Which is certainly an irrefutable argument that these things cannot be restricted to the return from Babylon according to the proper and direct intention of the Holy Spirit, but that they attained their fulfillment especially in the time of the New Testament. Although, however, these things are so, and this place looks especially to the times of the New Testament and the benefits proper to them, yet because God testifies: I HAVE LOVED YOU WITH AN EVERLASTING LOVE, the benefits which befell the people and Church of God under the Old Testament are not to be excluded, but whatever pertains to the rebuilding of the virgin, that is, the Church of Israel, is to be included, so that it is truly built, as the Prophet speaks. And although temporal joys are not to be dreamed of, just as carnal Jews everywhere dream of them in the Prophetic sayings, as if the striking of timbrels, the going forth to the dance, the singing of pipes, as they sound according to the letter, were to be understood, and that clamor with joy, and the leaping of those rejoicing in a worldly manner, and were to be taken concerning external happiness and gladness, yet that rebuilding of the Virgin of Israel embraces the erection of the Church to be instituted and continued after the captivity is released, even if that building was finally consummated especially under the times of the New Testament; provided that a double sense is not introduced; for which there is no need, if the benefit begun at that time is said to be perfected in this more blessed time of the New Testament. Since that building does not cease, nor will it cease, until the building of the Church of the body of Christ is consummated, Eph. 4:12, Matt. 16:18. Nor is there mention of the mountains of Samaria and Ephraim without cause, since it is taught that that grace is also to be shown to the Samaritans and Ephraimites, because the Church ought to be rebuilt not only from the Kingdom of Judah, but also from the Kingdom of Israel, and in the very lands of Israel God will again gather a people for Himself. Therefore, if the reduction from the land of the North and the gathering from the ends of the earth be taken as the means of this rebuilding, the sense of a bodily reduction could be admitted, provided that the building of the Church is understood (not of material buildings) and is believed to be consummated not through Ezra and Nehemiah, but in the time of the New Testament. Our blessed Pomeranus has executed these things excellently before other interpreters, from whose commentary it is helpful to bring forward some things, even if they are delivered somewhat prolixly, because it is now in the hands of few. He promises peace after the Babylonian captivity into the land of Canaan, which they had possessed before. But how thin that external peace was, not for all Israel but for those who returned from captivity, and how often it was disturbed, the history of Ezra and Nehemiah is witness, and then also the history of the Maccabees and of Josephus. What peace, I ask, did they have when Herod the alien occupied the Kingdom? Even if here we do not look only to external peace in the manner of the Jewish Rabbis, but also much more, as we ought, to that true peace, namely of consciences before God, what peace, I ask, could there be then, when consciences began again to be vexed by human traditions and everything to be laid waste by the doctrines of the Pharisees and Sadducees? Concerning which miserable but spiritual Pharisaic captivity, which was to be in the future after other bodily captivities, the Lord complains in Isaiah 52. Where, therefore, is that notable peace which is promised here to the whole of Israel to be in the land from which they were cast out? I answer, as I said before, God, after seventy years, the captivity being released, began to do them good in their own land, and defended them even in the midst of their adversaries: But lest those glorious promises should be believed to have meant nothing else than this benefit, so thin and both temporal and bodily, toward two tribes, when nevertheless the manifest words promised more, God permitted that they should often be overwhelmed by both external and internal evils, so that the faithful (for others meanwhile were blaspheming) might know that the grace promised was already in some way to be perfected at some time for the whole of Israel, with eternal peace, which was done through Christ. But note here that when the two tribes are cast into Babylon, they receive a prophetic promise from God that God would lead them back after seventy years, so that He might afterwards complete what was promised concerning Christ in those lands. I- and therefore they could expect to receive back those lands of theirs, to establish their polities and the worship of God in the temple, to cultivate their fields and vineyards, etc. Meanwhile, however, for one hundred and thirty years the ten tribes (which are called the Kingdom of Israel, the Kingdom of Ephraim, the Kingdom of Samaria) cast out into certain cities of the Medes by the King of the Assyrians, have no certain promises of being brought back, or that they were to be restored to their lands, except those general ones from the Law, which had the condition of the Law attached, if they should return with their whole heart to God and to the observance of the Law of God, as Lev. XXVI. Until their uncircumcised mind is humbled. Then they shall pray, etc. And Deut. XXX. When therefore they shall come upon you, etc. And those promises from Hosea and other Prophets, concerning Israel being restored to the Kingdom, not of Samaria but of David, without the prescription of a certain time. Which promises the impious easily either neglected or even despised, as despairing after such long times, especially since they did not have such Prophets as God gave to the two tribes in Babylon: For who does not neglect the promises of God, when holy and faithful Prophets or preachers of God are not present? But what were they to hope for concerning Christ, although there was a promise, when some were now mocking the promises concerning Christ, while others dreamed that they had been made void on account of the sins of the people, as even now our Jews are insane? I do not deny, however, that there were some pious ones among them who expected redemption and inculcated it to their children and friends, as is read concerning Tobias, but how despised these were among them, the same history declares. And so, without hope of returning, the ten tribes were cast out, 4 Kings 15 & 17. And so that they might not again be able to hope for the Kingdom of Samaria or that Kingdom of theirs of Israel, or Ephraim, and their polity and their condemned sacred rites, there were substituted for them in Samaria and the cities of Samaria those Gentiles, who were afterwards called Samaritans from that place. The land did not perform a Sabbath or a calling there, as in the Kingdom of Judah under captivity. Because to this place, that is, to the Kingdom of Judah, two tribes were to be restored to the sacred rites of God, to their polities, to their fields and possessions, as you will see also in the following chapter. public edict of Cyrus, King of the Persians, the power and liberty of returning had been granted to all the Jews, to build the temple of God at Jerusalem, they returned, who were from Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, and all whose spirit God had stirred up, as Ezra writes in chapter 1, to whom without doubt some who feared God from the ten tribes added themselves of their own accord, being very desirous of the holy religion of the fathers. Many afterwards, when they saw the ancient religion flourishing again in their own land, returned little by little in such a way that they occupied not only some places in Samaria, where it was permitted by the Samaritans, but also the whole of Galilee, and the places across the Jordan, which is called the land of Gilead, or Galaad, and other places by which one goes to Tyre and Sidon, as even the Gospel history testifies, Matt. 4, Mark 3, John 4, etc. Which places had previously been assigned to the ten tribes by Moses and Joshua, and belonged to the Kingdom of Israel after the death of Solomon. But having returned in this way, they dwell in great confusion, that is, not according to the tribes and according to the order in which Joshua had distributed those lands, but indiscriminately, as each one was able to occupy his own places and some field first. For they could not recover their paternal fields, so that even some from Judah dwelt there with them, who perhaps had returned later from the captivity, just as you read concerning the Virgin Mary and Joseph, that they dwelt in Nazareth, Luke 2, where you also read this, that individuals went to their own city, so that they might register. By which words it is clearly signified that many did not then dwell in the cities of their own lot or their own tribe. Nor did they have princes from among themselves afterwards, much less those glorious temples and the sacred rites condemned before the captivity, but they were ruled by leading men who were in Judah, and by the priests and Levites, and they went every year according to the Law to the Temple of Jerusalem. Thus you look at the bodily things in the ten tribes, that is, in some of the ten tribes having returned in this way, they had and could have the same things among the nations from which they returned, and now the impious Samaritans had better things than the Israelites themselves from the Kingdom of the ten tribes. And yet even this was a great grace to them, that they were thus returning to the God of their fathers, because He wished to be worshipped by the Jews at that time in that land and in that Temple of Jerusalem, concerning which matter some Psalms were made. Just as among us it is a great grace and a benefit of God to be received with thanksgiving, that we worship where the Gospel of Christ is sincerely preached, and the true use of the Sacraments is delivered. It cannot be that the temple of God is not there, that is, a people holy through Christ, etc. But it was a very great grace to them that many of them received Christ present in the flesh in those lands of theirs, just as many from the two tribes also did, as the Gospel history holds, and the history of the Acts of the Apostles declares much more, that Christ, already glorified, was received there by them. And that you may marvel at the clemency of God in Christ, Christ began to preach and heal the elect Jews there first, where the devastation had once been made by the Assyrians, as you read in Matthew 4 from Isaiah 9, so that you may see that they then truly began to be led back to God, who had been led away from God, by that perfect restoration which is promised here in Jeremiah. All others, who were from the elect of Israel and the true

sons of Abraham, received Christ in their other places, where they were dispersed among the nations, through the preaching of the Gospel, which is a spiritual restoration, and a true restoration, without which that bodily one would have done more harm, as it certainly did harm the impious Jews, who even afterwards did not receive Christ but crucified Him. Just as the Prophet Zechariah warns those who returned from captivity to return to God. Being led away from God through infidelity or impiety and contempt, how can they be led back to God except through faith? Concerning this spiritual restoration of Israel I spoke above in chapter 3. The Jews were then dispersed not only among the Assyrians and Persians, but also near Judea in Idumea, Arabia, etc. Then also in Asia, Egypt, Italy, and as you see in Acts 2, and in the whole book of the Acts of the Apostles. Thus God had then multiplied that people, the remnants from the flesh of Israel. From whom many, hardened everywhere, resisted the Gospel, but some believed. And these, having acknowledged their liberty in Christ, did not afterwards delay for a bodily restoration. And lest some should make this necessary for themselves and this scandal should harm even the believing Gentiles, as if all the sacred rites of the Jews were still intact, God devastated everything there through the Romans, so that not a stone remained upon a stone, just as Christ had predicted. Thus there was made one Kingdom of believing Israelites and believing Jews, under one King, Christ, through whom the new Jerusalem, the new temple, the new Kingdom of believing Jews was spread among all nations throughout the whole world. Which nations themselves also, through faith, were made sons of Abraham, men of Israel, Rom. 4 and 9, raised up not from the flesh of Abraham but from the stones, as John the Baptist says. Those who are raised up from the stones certainly cannot be from the flesh of Abraham, yet they are true sons of Abraham, whom Abraham did not make by carnal propagation, but God Himself raised up. John 1: As many as received the King of the Jews, to them He gave the power to become sons of God, to those who believe in His name. This glory of the believing Jews (for what has God to do with the impious and unbelievers?) our Jewish dregs, a brood of vipers, today consider contemptible, and demand that in these and similar Scriptures we show the pomp of the flesh and the glory of the world exhibited to them through Jesus the Savior, not seeing, blind as they are, that by this reasoning they make their own scriptures false, while they can never show from this Prophet and others anything of the sort that they dream of as having been exhibited by God to the twelve tribes. These things, therefore, which we have said from history concerning the even bodily restoration of many of the ten tribes of Israel, you should note most highly for yourself, because almost no expositors have touched upon these; they all speak only of the spiritual restoration, which was brought about for the exiled Israelites by faith in Christ, as it was for us all. And at the same time they manifestly deny that Israel, that is, the ten tribes, have been restored, contrary to the promises of God, which you read here and elsewhere. For it is not only said here that they would return, which could be understood as a true return to God, without which all returns are vain, but also that they will act in the lands of Samaria, etc., so that those things also may be confirmed and performed which were promised to them in those lands concerning Christ and the bodily presence of Christ and concerning the beginning of the Kingdom of Christ spread abroad in the lands. Since, as Paul says, Christ was made a minister of the circumcision, to confirm the promises made to the fathers. And first He began to manifest Himself in Galilee and other places of the ten tribes, according to the prophecy of Micah in Bethlehem, there to be proclaimed by Angels to the shepherds, to be manifested to the Magi, to Simeon, to Anna, and through these to others also in the temple of Jerusalem. But when he had begun, as has been said, to manifest his Kingdom through the Gospel and miracles in Galilee, and thus to reign not with a kingdom of the world, the eternal King and priest (Ps. 110) went away into Jerusalem and Judea, as is said in John 2, and asserted that that temple of God was confessed himself to be the Son of God, and by this authority he cast out of the temple those buying and selling, as the son of David, as the son of God, as King and high priest, in short, as that Messiah promised in the law and the Prophets. There then many believed in him because of the miracles which he was doing. Nor did he despise the Samaritans living in the Kingdom of the ten tribes, when he was returning from Judea into Galilee, as is said in John 3. Lest anyone should say that Christ, the sun of righteousness, had not shone everywhere in those lands; for it had been promised that Christ would come not only to the Jews, but also to those lands which the fathers of the Jews had possessed, and for this reason the Samaritans are also received. All these things our Bugenhagen, who then excellently declares how that ἐναντιοφάνεια in the prophecies of the Prophets, concerning the bringing back and the not bringing back of the Israelites, ought to be reconciled, fol. 318. But from these things which we have said about the reduction of the ten tribes, you will easily judge the Prophecies, and understand what they mean. For sometimes they say they are to be brought back to the land of the Fathers, but sometimes, without any mercy, to be cast away, so that they are never restored. Both are read in Hosea 1 and elsewhere, and thus the Prophets seem to establish two contradictory things at once, which cannot happen, nor are the Prophets so foolish as to intend this, who speak from the mouth of the Lord. Thus therefore the blessed Bugenhagen reconciles the passages that are apparently contrary concerning the reduction of the X. tribes and their perpetual rejection: They were brought back also corporally, although the greater number remained dispersed among the nations. But the Israelites who were brought back, whether they were from the Kingdom of Joseph, or Ephraim, or Samaria, were ruled by the Princes of Judah, so that in this beginning they might begin to return to the Kingdom of David, from which they had been separated with the greatest emulation after the death of Solomon: But that King David promised was not there until JESUS Christ our Lord the true Messiah, under which one head of both Kingdoms the people, as one people, was to be, as was formerly predicted. In these thus gradually brought back was completed what is read concerning the corporal reduction of Israel to the lands of Samaria. Of these, those who were chosen received Christ coming, and thus were truly brought back to God. After whom also other Israelites remaining in the dispersion of the nations were brought back to God through the Gospel, which is a spiritual reduction, promised to all the tribes and performed through Christ; expositors look only to this spiritual reduction of the Israelites, or the ten tribes. But we must also remember that corporal reduction, because of certain words of the Prophets, and because of the history itself, which we have indicated. But when it is read that the ten tribes are not to be brought back, or restored, it is known to those who are accustomed to the sacred scriptures what is understood, as I said in chapter 9, where it is said 'The lairs of dragons' etc., and in chapter 25, where it is said, 'Everlasting solitudes' etc. For Israel is not restored as Judah. For it does not return all at once, but gradually from all the tribes return a few, who nevertheless were multiplied beyond measure within five hundred or four hundred years (for some returned later) up to Christ. Then, they never rise again into a Kingdom and power, and that polity which they had before, but are ruled under Judah, to say nothing of foreign rulers, which was often a common evil for both peoples afterwards, so that they might learn to hope for and desire the promised Messiah. Furthermore, they are not restored to their cities and villages and fields and vineyards, as Judah was. For the Samaritans had occupied all the best things in the Kingdom of Samaria: But they dwell where it was permitted to occupy or buy places without order, without distinction of tribes, as I said above, not as Lords of the land, but as exiles, who desired to be citizens there, which was permitted to them then under the Kingdom of the Persians, nor was it permitted to them alone, but it would have been permitted to the Gentiles then there also, yet this very thing turned out prosperously for them, so that they occupied the whole of Galilee besides other places. From these things you see that the ten tribes were so cast away that they never returned to their former glory, and thus to the fields and possessions of their fathers, so that I may not now repeat again that the greatest part of them never returned to those lands, and thus the words of Josephus are to be understood, which you read in the 10th book of the Antiquities, chapter 5. What thanks, therefore, did they have, having returned in this way? I have already said before that it was a great thanksgiving that they thus returned to the true religion of their God, and thus to the God of their Fathers, and that the chosen among them later received the Lord Christ present in the flesh, according to the word of Christ: 'Blessed are the eyes which see what you see' etc. Wherefore our blessed Predecessor, the faithful supporter of St. Luther, concludes from all these things that these things are to be understood concerning spiritual peace, and that they obtained their fulfillment in the time of the New Testament: Therefore, let anyone understand what is said here concerning the peace of Israel as he wishes, even concerning that however small temporal peace, which they enjoyed after the captivity having returned, and rejoiced that they had returned to their brothers and to the worship of God. But when this peace was often interrupted, as we have said above, and not shown to the whole of Israel, it is certain that by this peace what is promised here was not completely performed. For the end of this chapter declares that the things promised here are eternal, of which those things that are promised as bodily were scarcely a shadow and the beginnings of the benefits of God after the Babylonian captivity. And therefore these things were completed in Christ for the Jews and the Gentiles. Whence Paul says in Eph. 2: Coming, he preached peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near: because through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. And Isaiah chapter 9, in manifest words, calls this peace upon the throne of David and upon his kingdom in Christ eternal, when he says: And of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. Rom. 5: Being justified by faith, we have peace toward GOD through Jesus Christ, etc.

By no means, therefore, is the Grotian gloss to be admitted: I WILL BUILD THEE AGAIN, when you shall have turned to me, I will cause you to have houses again. AND THOU SHALT BE BUILT, and that you may safely possess them. For it is manifest from those things which have been said that the prophecy does not treat of material buildings, but of the edification of the Church and the propagation of the same. These arguments can be gathered from the text: (1.) From the subject to whom the promise was made, ALL THE FAMILIES OF ISRAEL, ver. 11. For not all of them returned corporally. (2.) From the name with which it is adorned, VIRGIN OF ISRAEL, which is significant of the Church. (3.) From the place in which the vineyards are to be planted: thou shalt yet plant vines upon the mountains of Samaria. But not all Israelites planted vines on the mountains of Samaria, which the Gentile Samaritans rather occupied. Wherefore these things are to be understood of a spiritual planting, which was done in Samaria, John 4, Acts 8. (4.) From the rousing of the watchmen: Arise and let us ascend to Zion to the Lord our God. It is established that this exhortation concerns the gathering to the Church and the times of the New Testament from the parallel passages Isa. 2:3, Mic. 4:2. (5.) From the description of joy, which is commanded to the people, for which they invite one another to the Church: EXULT IN JOY O JACOB AND NEIGH OVER THE HEAD OF THE NATIONS, SOUND FORTH AND SING AND SAY: SAVE O LORD THY PEOPLE THE REMNANT OF ISRAEL. Which refer to spiritual joy in the Lord, and a vow for the success of the Kingdom of the Lord, as is clear from the parallel passage Matt. 21. (6.) From the connected calling of the nations, verse 10. HEAR O NATIONS THE WORD OF THE LORD. NATIONS etc. (7.) From the condition of the good things, which are promised here: I WILL BE THEIR GOD, and they shall be my people, their soul shall be as a watered garden, and they shall hunger no more, I will inebriate the soul of the Priests with fatness, and my people shall be filled with good things. (8.) From common and universal joy, and that pure and true: Then the virgin shall rejoice in the dance, young men and old together: and I will turn their mourning into joy and will comfort them and make them rejoice from their sorrow. Such joy does not exist in this world; only joy in the Lord is true, and perfect joy. (9.) From the subjoined prophecy concerning the slaughter at Bethlehem. Which, with other connected matters, pertains to the times of the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 7. HINNITE CONTRA CAPVT GENTIVM) Id est, claram vocem edite in conspectu gentium omnium.

DICITE: SALVA DOMINE] ἀταντά. Verf. 8. DE TERRA AQUILONIS] De Media, ter- risque circumsitis. INTER QUOS ERUNT CÆCUS ET CLAU- DUS] Nemo volet abesse. At LXX. legerunt בעצרה, פסח id est, tanquam in festo Paschatis, quo maxima mul- titudo confluebat. PRÆGNANS ET PARIENS SIMUL] Nec uterus nec partus instans tardabit feminas. At LXX. summam fœ- cunditatem significari volunt. COETUS MAGNUS] Ingens exercitus, ut hic Chal- dæus. Verf. 9. IN FLETU VENIENT] Melius in fletu ibcrunt: nempe cum abducerentur. Ita accepit Chaldæus. Græci ἐν κλαυθμῷ ἐξῆλθον. ET ADDUCAM EOS PER TORRENTES A- QUARUM] In Hebræo & Chaldæo, ad rivos aquarum: id est, non deerit iter facientibus quod bibant. IN VIA RECTA, ET NON IMPINGENT IN EA] In via ita plana, ut in ea impacturi non sint. Verf. 10. ET EPHRAIM PRIMOGENITUS MEUS EST] Ita carus, ut solent esse primogeniti. Hoc ideo, quod nonnulli de Israelitis X. tribuum cum Judæis rediere. Vide Esdr. 2. & supra 33, 3. V. 11. REDEMIT ENIM DOMINUS JACOB] Redimet. ET LIBERAVIT.] Liberabit. Verf. 12. ERITQUE ANIMA EORUM QUASI HORTUS IRRIGUUS] Plena gaudii. ET INEBRIABO ANIMAM SACERDOTUM PINGUEDINE] Satiabo Sacerdotes pinguibus victimis.

De corporalibus beneficiis hæc omnia intelligit Grotius. Agnoscit tamen ad mysticum sensum de Ecclesia optime trahi. At nullum hic vestigium ge- mini sensus est. De Ecclesia agi sensu literali, ex antecedentibus haud obscurum est, ubi subjectum designabatur Israel, & universis cognationibus Israel hæc promissa: universas autem cognationes Israe- lis secundum carnem ad requiem ivisse, rursum ædi- ficatas esse, & ornatas, gaudiisque externis repletas in patria, in montibus Samariæ vineas iterum plan- tasse experientiæ palà reclamat. Ideo hæc de Israe- litis secundum Spiritum, & de Ecclesia Christi intel- ligenda sensu literali sunt: cui promittitur spiritua- lis ædificatio per Evangelii præconium, & ornatus & gaudium spirituale. Exultant enim piorum cor- da consideratione ingentium beneficiorum Chri- sti, & cum tympanis & tibiis egrediuntur, quando Psalmis & hymnis misericordiam Dei in Christo exhibita celebrant. Plantantur Christi Ecclesiæ quasi vineæ & conservantur, ut fructum spiritualem per- cipiant plantantes verbi ministri cum lætitia. Unde acclamat ipse Dominus: Exultate in lætitia Jacob (populi mei) & hinnite, SUPER CAPITE GEN- TIUM, (CHRISTO, qui non modo Judæorum Messias, sed etiam princeps est & caput gentium) PERSONATE, ET CANITE: ET DICI- TE, salva Domine populum tuum, nempe reli- quias Israel. Quo pertinet illud Hosianna, quod Christo acclamatum fuit Matth. 21. Per hunc ser- vantur reliquiæ populi Dei. Major est enim nume- rus eorum, qui Evangelio non credunt, quam eo- rum, qui servantur. Unde additur, AUDITE VERBUM DOMINI VOS GENTES. Nam & vobis prædicabitur Evangelium Christi, & cum gaudio, atque congratulantes annunciate (bene- ficia Christi in Ecclesiam collata) in Insulis, in variis & remotis locis, quæ procul sunt dissita, & dicite: Qui dispersit olim populum Israel, Dominus Deus no- ster, is rursus congregabit eum & custodiet eum, sicut pastor gregem suum (Est enim Christus pastor bo- nus, qui posuit animam suam pro grege suo Johan. 10. Is per Evangelii prædicationem collectas oves humanissime pascit atq; curat. Ezech. 34.) Redimet enim Dominus Jehovab Christus Jesus Jacob, popu- lum suum & liberabit eum de manu potentioris. (Christus enim superavit potentem & armatum il- lum Satanam, Luc. 11. & per mortem (suam) destru- xit eum, qui habebat mortis imperium, id est,

Diabolum, Hebr. 2.) Et venient & laudabunt in monte Sion; rectius: Jubilabunt in excelsis Sion, id est: Qui Evangelion de Christo audierint, magno cum gaudio adjungent se Ecclesiæ per monte Sion adumbratæ & confluent ad bona Domini parti- cipanda, quæ illis Dominus liberaliter donabit, atque lætabuntur super frumento & vino & oleo & fœtu pecorum & armentorum: hæc enim omnia abundanter habebunt: eritque anima eorum quasi hortus irriguus, cui nullus æstus quantumvis ma- gnus, nocere potest: & ultra non esurient. Hebr. non dolebunt (i. e. Christiani pascentur & potabun- tur copiose & liberaliter verbo Evangelii, quo i- psorum corda vere exhilarabuntur. Pascentur e- tiam & potabuntur in Sacra Cœna Domini corpo- re & sanguine Jesu Christi, Dei & hominis: neque illis quicquam, quod ad veram salutem pertinet, deerit. Quin & oleo, hoc est, donis Spiritus Sancti, perfundentur: eruntque ab omnia bona opera præ- parati. Et, ut hortus semper irriguus, multos bo- nos fructus ferent. Et si qua adversa sint ferenda, alacriter perferent, vincente dolore gaudio Spiri- tus Sancti, donec in vitam cœlestem transferantur, ubi erit verum, perpetuum, & solidum gaudium, & ubi nullus erit amplius dolor aut ulla tristitia. Ut hic non incommode Osiander. TUNC VERO LÆTABITUR VIRGO (singulare pro plura- li) IN CHORO &c. Gaudere dicit in Choro virgines, juvenes & senes: Significans, Ecclesiam gaudere communicatione cœlestium beneficio- rum & donorum, quibus Ecclesiæ membra sibi in- vicem inserviunt: unde mutuo inter se gaudent. Tum vero omnino complebitur hæc promissio, cum ab omnibus hujus vitæ malis liberati æterna lætitia perfruemur. Tunc enim absterfæ erunt o- mnes lacrymæ ab oculis nostris Apoc. 20. ET IN- EBRIABO ANIMAM SACERDOTUM PINGUEDINE, i. e. liberalissime pascam meos sa- cerdotes, ut quasi adipe inebriati videri possent: ET POPULUS MEUS BONIS MEIS AD IMPLEBITUR AIT DOMINUS. (Etsi au- tem omnes Christiani sunt coram Deo sacerdotes, 1. Pet. 2. ideoque omnes large pascuntur verbo Ev- angelii, quo ipsorum animi reficiuntur: tamen Dominus in eos, qui aliis docendis in Ecclesia præ- ficiuntur, solet uberiorem Evangelii cognitionem effundere: ut non modo habeant, quo ipsi in con- scientia reficiantur, sed ut aliis etiam uberes con- solationes subministrare queant.) Consonat hic commentarius Brentianus, & enarratio B. Pappi, qui observat quatuor generum promissiones hic tra- di, adoptionem nempe Spiritualis Israelis vers. 1. propagationem doctrinæ Evangelii vers. 2. usque ad 7. Defensionem Ecclesiæ contra varia pericula vers. 7. 8. 9. & Vocationem gentium ad Societatem Ecclesiæ vers. 10. usque ad 14. Eadem mens fuit S. Hierony- mo, hæc intelligenda esse secundum literalem sen- fum unice de Ecclesia. ÆDIFICABO TE ET ÆDIFICABERIS VIRGO ISRAEL. Hoc pro- prie intelligamus in Ecclesia. Et porro. INTER QUOS ERUNT CÆCUS ET CLAUDUS &c. Congregantur reliquiæ populi Israel per Apostolos & apostolicos viros, de quibus supra legimus: Clama- bunt custodes in monte, & quibus præcipitur: Per- sonate, canite, & dicite, ut salvæ fiant reliquiæ Israel. Quod in Hebraico scribitur, inter quos erunt cæ- cus & claudus & prægnans & pariens simul, Eccle- sia magna revertentium hæc, quanquam & juxta literam impletum sit, quod cæci viderint, claudi am- bulaverint, tamen melius juxta Anagogen intelligi potest, quod qui prius erant cæci perfidia, postea cre- diderunt Salvatori, & qui claudi, quibus quondam loquebatur Helias: Vsque quo claudicatis utroque pede, postea ambulaverint: & populus, qui sedebat in tenebris & umbra mortis, magnum lumen aspe- xerint, claudique cucurrerint, & praegnans pepe- rerit filios. De illis verbis Ecclesiam magnam re- vertentium ad fidem ita habet Hier. Judaei putant hoc esse completum, quando sub Esdra post diem Phasa egreffi sunt de Babylone, ut reverterentur Hierusa- lem, in quo typus fuit & non veritas: Neque enim in illo tempore universa quae legimus & lecturi sumus fuiffe completa poterunt approbare. Atque postmo- dum ad illa, AUDITE VERBUM DOMINI: Perspicue inquit, vocatio gentium demonstratur, scriptura dicente: Audite verbum Domini gentes, & annunciate in insulis, quae procul sitae sunt & di- cite: Quid annunciant Insulis, quae procul sitae sunt? Quod Dominus, qui disperfit Israel, ipse congre- gabit eum. Nequaquam ergo ut dispergerentur, po- tentiae fuit adversariorum, sed Domini voluntatis. Et custodiet eum sicut pastor gregem suum, Pastor enim bonus ponit animam suam pro ovibus suis. Quia redemit Deus Jacob, pretio sanguinis sui, & libe- ravit eum de manu potentioris sive fortioris. Per quae ostenduntur fortiores adversariae potestates na- tura fragilitatis humanae. Et quantum in utrisque virium est, illas fortiores esse natura, sed nos fortio- res fide, si tamen mereamur liberari ab eo, qui potest alligare fortem & domum ejus diripere. Et venient, inquit, haud dubium, quin liberati de manu poten- tium & laudabunt liberatorem suum in monte Sion, hoc est, in Ecclesia, & confluent ad bona Domini, rerum omnium abundantiam, quae non in frugibus & cibis carnis ipsius, sed in virtutum varietate sen- titur. Super frumento, inquit, & vino & oleo, de quo conficitur panis Domini, & sanguinis ejus im- pletur typus, & benedictio Sanctificationis ostendi- tur, dicente scriptura: Unxit te Deus Deus tuus oleo laetitiae prae consortibus tuis. Et foeta pecorum, qui in Ecclesia simplices sunt, & armentorum, quae cornuta sunt, & adversarios ventilant. Ut autem sciamus benedictiones has nequaquam ad corpus sed ad animam pertinere, sequitur: Eritque anima eo- rum quasi hortus irriguus, sive quasi lignum fructi- ferum, quod plantatum est secus decursus aquaru, & paradisus Domini in delitiis. Et ultra, ait, non e- surient, Nequaquam ea esurie, de qua scriptum est: Beati qui esuriunt & sitiunt justitiam, sed ea, quae sa- turitate mutatur & rerum omnium excludit penu- riam. Tunc laetabitur virgo in Choro, de qua scri- bit Apostolus: Despondi enim vos uni viro virginem castam exhibere Christo. Et juvenes, ad quos loqui- tur Johannes: Scribo vobis juvenes, quoniam vici- stis malignum. Et senes, ad quos idem mystico sermone testatur: Scribo vobis Patres, quoniam cognovistis eum, qui ab initio est. Et convertam, inquit, luctum eorum in gaudium, ut quos terrue- rat crux, laetificet resurrectio, Et consolabor eos & laetificabo a dolore suo, juxta illud, quod Do- minus loquitur: Beati lugentes, quoniam ipsi conso- labuntur. Et inebriabo animam sacerdotum, qui habent scientiam Dei, de quorum ore interrogant legem Domini, qui credunt in eum, ad quem Prophe- ta canit: Tu es Sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordi- nem Melchisedech. Quod autem sequitur juxta LXX. Filiorum Levi, in Hebraico non habetur. Et perspicuum est nequaquam id dici de his sacerdoti- bus, qui sunt filii Levi, sed de his, in quorum typum praecessit Melchisedech. Ebrietas autem Sacerdo- tum & in Apostolis comprobatur, quando fervebant fide, & musto pleni dicebantur. Unde & locus, in quo comprehensus Dominus est, vocatur Geth- semani, quod in lingua nostra vallem pinguedi- nis sonat. Cumque sacerdotes pingues fuerint doctri- na Domini, & inebriati in convivio Joseph dixe- rint: Calix tuus inebrians quam præclarus est, tunc erit & hoc, quod nunc Dominus pollicetur: Et po- pulus meus bonis meis adimplebitur. Quæ omnia nunc ex parte tribuuntur: tunc autem dabuntur in pleno, quando viderimus a facie ad faciem, & corpus humilitatis nostræ fuerit resurrectionis gloria commu- tatum. Hæc Hieronymus, quæ eximie locum no- strum illustrant. E Pontificiis hunc sensum agnoscit Cornel. a Lapide, qui etiam Rabanum, Lyranum, Vatablum pro eo laudat. Neq; diffitentur Maldonatus, & Tiri- nus de Ecclesia intelligendū esse locum e Samarita- nis oriunda Act. 8. Menochius vero Grotio laudatus, unice probat illam explicationem, quæ literali sen- su intelligit de conversione Samaritanorum tempo- re N. T. Ad vers. 5. ADHUC PLANTABIS VINEAS IN MONTE SAMARIÆ: Oportet hæc intelligere de Conversione Samaritanorum ad fi- dem Christi, & per vineas, particulares Ecclesias, quasi dicat, Multos ad te, o Sion, o Ecclesia Chri- sti, convertam in Samaria, per prædicationem Ev- angelii, ut multas ibi fundes Samaritanorum Ec- clesias. Ita factum est Joh. 4, 41. Act. 8, 14. constat enim Samaritanos, id est decem tribus, ab Assyriis abductos in captivitatem, nunquam in Samariam rediisse. Quod certe argumentum est ἀδιάλυτον, non posse hæc ad reditum e Babylonia restringi secundum propriam & directam intentionem Sp. S. Sed maxime tempore N. T. complementum suum consequuta esse. Quenquam vero hæc ita sese habant, respici hoc loco maxime tempora Novi Testamenti, & be- neficia istis propria, tamen quia Deus testatur: EGO PERPETUA DILECTIONE DILE- XI TE, non excludenda sunt beneficia, quæ po- pulo & Ecclesiæ Dei obtigerunt sub Veteri Test. sed comprehendendum quicquid ad readificatio- nem virginis, hoc est, Ecclesia Israelis pertinet, ut vere sit ædificata, ut Propheta loquitur. Et utut somnianda non sint gaudia temporalia, quemad- modum eadem carnales Judæi ubique somniant in dictis Propheticis, quasi tympanorum percussio, exi- tus ad choream, fistularum cantus, ut sonant secun- dum literam, intelligantur, & clamor ille cum gau- dio, & jubilantium tripudia mundano more, ac de externa felicitate & lætitia accipienda sint, illa ta- men readificatio Virginis Israelis, erectionem Ec- clesiæ complectitur post solutam captivitatem in- stituendam, & continuandam, etsi ædificatio ista maxime sub Novi Testam. tempora demum con- summata sit; modo geminus non invehatur sensus; quo opus non est, si beneficium isto tempore in- choatum hoc beatiori Novi Testamenti tempore perfectum dicatur. Siquidem illa ædificatio non cesset, neque cessatura sit, donec consummetur æ- dificatio Ecclesiæ corporis Christi Eph. 4, 12. Matth. 16, 18. Neque absque causa montium Sa- mariæ & Ephraim mentio fit, siquidem eam gra- tiam etiam Samaritanis & Ephraimitis exhibendam esse doceatur, quod non tantum e Regno Judæ, sed etiam e Regno Israelis reædificari debeat Ecclesia, & in terris ipsis Israelis Deus sibi iterum collectu- rus sit populum. Ideo si reductio e terra Aquilonis & congregatio a finibus terræ accipiatur tanquā me- dium istis reædificationis; admitti posset sensus re- ductionis corporalis, modo ædificatio Ecclesiæ intelligatur (non materialium ædificiorum) & consummanda credatur non per Esdram, & Nehe- miam, sed tempore Novi Testamenti. Exequutus hæc eximie est præ aliis Interpp. B. Pomeranus no- stris ster, è cujus commentario nonnulla, etsi prolixiu- scule tradita, quia nunc in paucorum versatur ma- nibus, adducere juvat. Promittit pacem post capti- vitatem Babylonicam in terram Canaan, quam ante possederant. Verum quam tenuis illa externa pax, non toti Israeli sed reversis illis ex captivitate fuerit, & quam sæpe interturbata, testis est primum historia Esdræ & Nehemiæ, deinde & Machabæorum historia & Josephi. Quã quæso pacem habuerunt Herode alie- nigena occupante Regnũ? Etsi hic non tantum Judai- corum Rabbinorum more respiciamus in externam pacem, sed etiam multo amplius, ut debemus, in pacem illam veram, videlicet conscientiarum coram Deo, quæ pax quæso tunc esse potuit, quando rursum cõscien- tiæ cœperunt vexari traditionibus humanis & omnia vastari doctrinis Pharisæorũ & Saducæorum? De qua misera sed spirituali captivitate Pharisaica, post a- lias corporales captivitates futura, conqueritur Do- minus Esa. 52. Ubi ergo est illa insignis pax, quæ toti Israëli hic promittitur futura in terra, ex qua ejecti funt? Respondeo, quemadmodum antea dixi, Deus post septuaginta annos, soluta captivitate, cœpit eis benefacere in terra sua, & defendit eos vel in medio adversariorum: Ne autem illæ gloriosæ promissiones crederentur nihil aliud voluisse, quam hoc tam te- nue erga duas tribus beneficium & temporale & cor- porale, cum tamen plus promitterent manifesta ver- ba, permisit Deus, ut & externis & internis sæpe obruerentur malis, ut scirent fideles (nam alii interim blasphemabant) Gratiam promissam jam aliquo mo- do quandoque perficiendam toti Israeli, pace æterna, id quod factum est per Christum. Adverte vero hic, quod duæ tribus cum abjiciuntur in Babylonem, pro- missionem Propheticam à Deo accipiunt, quod Deus reducturus sit eos post septuaginta annos, ut compleat postea, quæ de Christo promissa erant in illis terris. I- deoque expectare potuerunt, ut rursum acciperent suas illas terras, instituerent suas Politias & in tem- plo cultum Dei, colerent suos agros & vineas &c. In- terim vero jam centum triginta annos abjectæ de- cem tribus (quæ vocantur Regnum Israel, Regnum Ephraim, Regnum Samariæ) in quasdam civitates Medorum per Regem Assyriorum, non habent cer- tas promissiones de reducendo, vel quod essent resti- tuendæ suis terris, nisi illas generales ex lege, quæ ha- bebant conditionem legis adjectam, si ex toto corde redirent ad Deum & ad Legis Dei observationem, ut Lev. XXVI. Donec erubescat incircumcisa mens eorum. Tunc orabunt &c. Et Deut. XXX. Cum ergo venerint super te &c. Et illas promissiones ex Osea & aliis Prophetis, de Israele restituendo in Re- gnum, non Samariæ sed Davidis, sine certi temporis præscriptione. Quas promissiones impiis facile aut negligebant, aut etiam contemnebant, ut despe- rantes post tanta tempora, maxime cum tales Pro- phetas non haberent, quales Deus dedit duabus tribubus in Babylone: Quis enim non negligit Dei promissiones, quando non adsunt sancti & fideles Dei Prophetæ sive prædicatores? Quid vero spe- rarent de Christo, licet promissio, quando alii promissiones de Christo nunc irridebant, alii au- tem inanes factas, propter peccata populi, somnia- bant, ut etiamnum nostri Judæi insaniunt? Non autem nego inter eos quosdam pios fuisse, qui ex- pectarint redemptionem, & eam suis filiis & ami- cis inculcarint, ut de Tobia legitur, sed hi quam contempti inter ipsos fuerint, eadem historia decla- rat. Itaque sine spe redeundi abjectæ sunt decem tribus 4. Reg. 15. & 17. Et ne rursum possent Regnum Samariæ sive suum illud Regnum Israel, sive E- phraim, & Politiam & sua damnata sacra sperare, subrogati sunt eis in Samariam & Samariæ civitates illi gentiles, qui ex loco postea vocati sunt Samari- tani. Non egit ibi terra Sabbatum sive vocatio- nem, ut in Regno Juda sub captivitate. Quia huc, id est, ad Regnum Juda erant duæ tribus restituen- dæ ad sacra Dei, ad suas Politias, ad suos agros & possessiones, ut videbis etiam capite sequenti. Cùm vero, publico edicto Cyri Regis Persarum, facta esset omnibus Judæis redeundi potestas & libertas, ad ædificandum Dei templum Hierosolymis, redie- runt, qui ex Juda & Benjamin erant & sacerdotes & Levitæ, & omnes quorum suscitavit Deus Spi- ritum, ut scribit Esdras capit. 1. quibus sine dubio quidam timentes Deum ex decem tribubus se ul- tro addiderunt, sanctæ patrum Religionis percupidi. Multi postea, ubi antiquam Religionem rursum in terra sua florere videbant, ita paulatim redibant, ut non solum aliqua loca in Samaria, ubi per Sama- ritanos licebat, sed etiam totam Galileam, & loca trans Jordanem, quæ vocatur terra Gilead, sive Galaad, & alia qua itur ad Tyrum & Sidonem, oc- cuparint, ut vel historia Evangelica testatur Matth. 4. Marc. 3. Joan. 4. &c. Quæ loca ante per Mo- sen & Josua ad decem tribus ordinata fuerant, & ad Regnum Israël, post mortem Salomonis, pertine- bant. Sic autem reversi confusissime habitant, id est, non secundum tribus & secundum ordinem, quo Josua distribuerat illas terras, sed promiscue, ut sua quisque loca & aliquem agrum primum po- tuit occupare. Nam paternos agros non potuerunt recipere, ita ut etiam cum eis illic quidam habita- rent ex Juda, qui forte serius redierant ex capti- vitate, quemadmodum legis de Maria virgine & Joseph, quod habitaverint in Nazareth, Luc. 2. ubi & hoc legis, quod singuli ibant in suam civi- tatem, ut profiterentur. Quibus verbis clare si- gnificatur, plures tunc non habitasse in suæ sortis aut suæ tribus civitatibus. Neque etiam Princi- pes postea ex se habuerunt, multo minus illa glorio- sa Templa & damnata ante captivitatem sacra, sed regebantur à Principibus viris, qui erant in Ju- da, & à Sacerdotibus & Levitis, & ibant singu- lis annis secundum Legem ad Templum Hierosoly- morum. Sic corporalia spectas in decem tribubus, id est, in quibusdam ex decem tribubus sic reversis, eadem habuerunt & habere potuerunt inter gen- tes, ex quibus redierunt, & nunc melius habe- bant impii Samaritani, quam ipsi Israëlitæ ex decem tribuum Regno. Et tamen vel hæc magna Gra- tia erat eis, quod ita revertebantur ad Deum patrum suorum, quia à Judæis tunc coli volebat in terra illa & in illo Templo Hierosolymorum, qua de re aliqui Psalmi facti sunt. Quemadmodum apud nos magna gratia est & beneficium Dei cum gratiarum actione suscipiendum, quod illic agi- mus, ubi sincere prædicatur Evangelium Christi, & verus usus traditur Sacramentorum. Non po- test fieri, ut ibi non sit templum Dei, id est, po- pulus per Christum sanctus &c. Maxima vero erat eis gratia, quod multi ex eis Christum in suis illis terris in carne præsentem susceperunt, sicut & multi ex duabus tribubus, ut habet historia E- vangelica, & multo magis historia Actorum A- postolicorum declarat, illic ab eis Christum jam glo- rificatum, susceptum. Et ut mireris Dei cle- mentiam in Christo, Christus illic primum cœpit prædicare & sanare Judæos electos, ubi primum fa- cta erat olim vastatio per Assyrios, ut legis Matthæi 4. ex Esa. 9. ut videas tunc eos vere cœpisse reduci ad Deum, qui à Deo abducti fuerant, reductione illa perfecta, quæ hic in Jeremia promittitur. A- lii omnes, qui erant ex electis Israëlis & veris

Abrahæ filiis, Christum, in aliis suis locis, quo erant dispersi inter gentes, susceperunt per Evan- gelii prædicationem, quæ est reductio spiritualis, & vera reductio, sine qua illa corporalis plus obes- set, ut certe obfuit impiis Judæis, qui etiam po- stæa Christum non susceperunt sed crucifixerunt. Quemadmodum Zacharias Propheta monet rever- sos ex captivitate, ut revertantur ad Deum. Abducti à Deo per infidelitatem sive impietatem & contemptum, quomodo possunt reduci ad Deum nisi per fidem? De hac spirituali reductione Israe- lis dixi supra cap. 3. Judæi tunc erant dispersi non solum apud Assyrios & Persas, sed etiam prope Iu- dæam in Idumæa, Arabia &c. Deinde etiam in Asia, Ægypto, Italia, & ut vides Act. 2. & in toto libro Actorum Apostolicorum. Ita multipli- caverat tunc Deus illum populum reliquias ex car- ne Israel. Ex quibus multi indurati ubique Ev- angelio resistebant, quidam autem crediderunt. Atque hi agnita sua in Christo libertate, nihil po- stæa morati sunt reductionem corporalem. Et ne hanc aliqui necessariam sibi facerent & hoc scan- dalum obesset etiam credentibus Gentibus, quasi omnia Judæorum sacra adhuc essent integra, Deus per Romanos vastavit illic omnia, ut non mane- ret lapis super lapidem, quemadmodum Christus prædixerat. Factum est itaque unum Regnum cre- dentium Israelitarum & credentium Judæorum, sub uno Rege Christo, per quos nova Jerusalem novum templum, novum Regnum Judæorum cre- dentium dilatatum est in omnes gentes per totum mundum. Quæ gentes & ipsæ per fidem factæ sunt filii Abrahæ, viri Israelitæ Rom. 4. & 9. suscita- ti non ex carne Abrahæ sed ex Lapidibus, ut Johan- nes Baptista ait. Qui ex lapidibus suscitantur, certe ex carne Abrahæ esse non possunt, attamen sunt veri filii Abrahæ, quos non Abraham car- nali propagatione fecit, sed Deus ipse suscitavit. Johan. 1. Quotquot susceperunt Regem Judæorum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, iis qui credunt in nomen ejus. Hanc gloriam credentium Judæorum (quid enim Deo cum impiis & incredulis?) nostra Judaica fex, progenies viperarum, hodie con- temptam ducunt, & postulant ut in his & simi- libus Scripturis pompam carnis & gloriam mundi ostendamus per Jesum Salvatorem ipsis exhibitam, non videntes cæci, quod hac ratione suas scripturas faciunt falsas, dum nihil tale, quale ipsi somniant, ex hoc Propheta & aliis ostendere possunt unquam duodecim tribubus à Deo exhibitum. Hæc ergo quæ diximus ex historia de reductione etiam corpo- rali multorum ex decem tribubus Israel, summe no- tabis tibi, quia nullus fere expositorum hæc attigit, tantum dicunt omnes de spirituali reductione, quæ fide in Christum exulibus Israelitis facta est, ut omni- bus nobis. Et simul manifeste negant Israelem, id est, decem tribus reductas esse, contra promis- siones Dei, quas hic & alibi legis. Nam non so- lum hic dicitur quod reverterentur, id quod intelligi posset de vera reversione ad Deum, sine qua omnes reversiones sunt vanæ, sed etiam quod agent in ter- ris Samariæ &c. ut confirmentur & præstentur e- tiam illa, quæ eis in illis terris de Christo & Chri- sti corporali præsentia & de initio vulgati in terris Regni Christi promissa sunt. Siquidem, ut ait Paulus, Christus factus est minister circumcisio- nis, ad confirmandas promissiones patribus factas. Et primum cæpit se manifestare in Galilæa & aliis locis decem tribuum, secundum prophetiam Mi- chæ in Bethlehem, ibi ab Angelis prædicari pasto- ribus, manifestari Magis, Simeonis, Hannæ, & per hos aliis etiam in templo Hierosolymorum. Ubi vero suum Regnum per Evangelium & miracula manifestare in Galilæa, ut dictum est, cœperat, atque adeo regnare non mundi Regno, abiit æter- nus & Rex & sacerdos (Pfal. 110.) in Jerusalem & Judeam, ut dicitur Joh. 2. & asseruit illud tem- plum Dei esse domum Patris sui. Quo manifeste se filium Dei confessus est, & hac autoritate eje- cit è templo ementes & vendentes, ut filius Davi- dis, ut filius Dei, ut Rex & summus sacerdos, bre- viter, ut Messias ille in lege & Prophetis promissus. Ibi tum multi crediderunt in eum propter miracu- la, quæ faciebat. Nec contemptit Samaritanos in Regno decem tribuum habitantes, ubi reverte- batur ex Judea in Galileam, ut dicitur Joh. 3. Ne quis diceret, non ubique in illis terris patrum illuxisse Christum, solem justitiæ; Nam promis- sum erat, Christum non solum ad Judæos, sed e- tiam ad illas terras, quas patres Judæorum posse- derant, venturum, hac ratione & Samaritani suscipiuntur. Hæc omnia Bugenhagius noster, qui deinde eximie declarat, quomodo ἐναντιο- φάνεια illa in vaticiniis Prophetarum, de redu- cendis, & non reducendis Israelitis, concilia- ri debeat fol. 318. Ex his autem quæ de decem tribuum reductione diximus, facile judicabis Pro- phetias, & intelliges quid velint. Nam quan- doque dicunt reducendas in terram Patrum, quan- doque vero, absque ulla misericordi aita abjicien- das, ut nunquam restituantur. Utrumque legis Ose. 1. & alibi, atque ita videntur Prophetæ simul duo contradictoria statuere, id quod fieri non potest, ne- que adeo stulti sunt Prophetæ, ut hoc velint, qui lo- quuntur ex ore Domini. Sic ergo conciliat loca in speciem contraria de reductione X. tribuum & de perpetua earum abjectione B. Bugenhagius: Reductæ sunt etiam corporaliter, licet major nu- merus manserit inter gentes dispersus. Reducti au- tem Israëlitæ, sive qui erant ex Regno Joseph, si- ve Ephraim, sive Samariæ, regebantur à Princi- pibus Juda, ut hoc initio inciperent redire ad Re- gnum Davidis, à quo maxima æmulatione post mortem Salomonis fuerant separati: Sed non erat ibi ille Rex David promissus usque ad JESUM Christum Dominum nostrum verum Messiam, sub quo uno capite utriusque Regni populus, unus popu- lus futurus, olim prædicabatur. In his ita paula- tim reductis completum est, quod legitur de corporali reductione Israelis ad terras Samariæ.
