Therefore, the promise was made not only to the two tribes, but indiscriminately to the Israelites and the Jews, because from the remnants of these the New Testament was to be produced. The Church, to be enriched by the accession of the Gentiles, with God watching, not that He may pluck up and scatter anymore, as He had previously scattered the Israelite Church, but that He may build and plant the Church. To this also pertains that notable promise, that the Lord wishes to strike a covenant with the house of Israel, concerning the law to be inscribed upon their hearts, and the taking of them into His people, that they may enjoy divine grace and obtain the remission of sins: How, however, the gloss of Grotius holds together, does not appear. Ephraim groans under captivity, as it seems to us, or the Assyrian exile; he grieves that he remains chastised, still like an untamed heifer; he seeks and sighs to the Lord; CONVERT ME, AND I SHALL BE CONVERTED, which cannot be taken in a different sense, as Grotius wishes, as if the former, which Ephraim seeks, concerns the return, and the latter, which he promises himself, pertains to conversion: since it is manifest that Ephraim is seeking conversion to the Lord, so that he may in reality be converted to Him. And thus he testifies that he cannot be converted to the Lord except by the power and grace of the Lord. Whence Jerome rightly concludes: Therefore, that very thing, that we do penance, we cannot fulfill unless we rely on the help of God. For after you have converted me, and I shall have been converted to you, then I shall know that you are the Lord my God, and my errors and sins shall by no means kill me. And after you converted me, I did penance. See how great is the help of God, and how fragile the human condition, that this very thing, by which we do penance, we are by no means able to fulfill unless the Lord has first converted us. And after, he says, you showed me, either penance itself or the knowledge of you, or I knew you, I struck my thigh. Which is a sign of one grieving and lamenting and weeping over his former error, that he strikes his thigh with his hand and confesses that he had been a fool before. I am confounded, he says, and I blushed, or from the day of confusion. For what time is not a time of our confusion, if we remember ancient sins, and take memory of all things which we have done wickedly? Which sense the parallel clearly confirms in Lamentations 5:21. Convert us, O Lord, to you, and we shall be converted. Which Grotius utterly perverts. For when in these words Ephraim desires and expects the grace of conversion, and testifies to his penance by the striking of his thigh, his confusion, and his blushing, Grotius twists them into the contrary sense, as if to say he cannot be free to do penance: Furthermore, when the Lord testifies that Ephraim is precious to Him, that He still remembers him, that the bowels of His mercy are moved over him, that He cannot but have mercy on him: conversely, Grotius understands these things as being about the rejection of Ephraim and the wrath of God against him. But the sense of the Prophet, as also the common consensus of the Church concerning the same, is so obvious and well-known that there is no need to dwell on these. For it is sufficiently manifest, as Jerome also observed here, that this passage is parallel with that in Hosea 11: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Israel? How shall I make you as Admah, and as Zeboim? My heart is turned within me, my bowels are troubled. I will not execute the fury of my wrath and I will not destroy Ephraim. Being merciful I will have mercy, says the Lord. This notable evangelical pericope, most full of consolation concerning the mercy of God, which some understand generally of the Church, shadowed forth through Ephraim, but others, although they acknowledge it was spoken to the Israelites, nevertheless deservedly apply it to any of the faithful, Grotius changed into a legal and judicial sentence, by which all mercy is denied to the Israelites. By which means no promise will remain so clear that it cannot be transformed into a threat.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SI FILIVS HONORABILIS MIHI EPHRAIM, SI PVER DELICATVS) Respondet Deus: Nonne pretiosus filius mihi est Ephraim, nonne natus deliculatus? Certe necesse est credat me ipso carere non posse, quod tam delicatus est, ut pœnitentiam agere nolit, nisi prius obtento reditu.

EX QVO LOCUTUS SVM DE EO, ADHVC RECORDABOR EJVS) Ubi satis cum eo locutus ero, (id est, ubi satis eum admonuero) omnino recordabor ejus, nem- pe meminero istius pertinaciæ.

IDCIRCO CONTVRBATA SVNT VISCERA MEA SVPER EVM) Ob hoc vehementer ei succenseo. Vox viscerum apud Hebræos ad omnem graviorem affe- ctum refertur.

MISERANS MISEREBOR EJVS) Hæc per interro- gationem legenda arbitror. An omnino misereri ejus possem, qui corrigere se non vult, quamdiu in malis est rebus?

Nova sua Interpretatione textum pervertit, neque sibi constat satis Grotius. Nam si hæc de decem tribuum desertione intelligenda, quomodo vers. 21. compellantur duæ tribus, cum oratio ita comparata sit, ut eosdem, non diversos compellari dubitandum non sit? Porro quum è superioribus certi simus,hæc pertinere ad tempora Novi Testa- menti, B. Hulsemannus noster refert hæc ad exci- dium novissimum per Romanos factum. Manifestum est, quodEphraimi & virginis Israelis status misera- bilis ac gemitus hic sistantur, cum Israelitæ, confusi ob scelera, sustinere opprobrium adolescentiæ: quodq; aperianturviscera miserationis divinæ,qua Ephraimum & Israelem consolari & revocare ad pœnitentiam non dedignatus fuerit. Quanquam vero penes plerosq; Israelitas Deus sua gratia fru- stra fuerit, testari tamen eam voluit omnibus, o- mnesque in viam revocare, cujus rei causa etiam novum illud, quod Dominus creaturus erat in ter- ra, proponitur, quum ea fini id creatum, & Filius Dei è virgine prognatus sit, ut quære etur quod perierat, & peccatores ad pœnitentiam vocaren- tur. Neque omnino nullus erit fructus divinæ gra- tiæ: Hæc enim dicit Dominus exercituum, Deus Israel: adhuc dicent verbum istud in terra Iuda. Benedicat tibi Dominus ô habitatio justitiæ! Siquidem non- nullæ reliquiæ è Judæis eripientur, & ex illisChri- stianæ Ecclesiæ primordia orientur, quæ valde de- inde augenda & multiplicanda erit. Ecce dies ve- niunt, dicit Dominus, & seminabo domum Israel & domum Iuda. Non ergo tantum duabus tribubus, sed promiscue Israelitis & Iudæis facta est promif- sio, quia ex istorum reliquiis erat procreanda Novi Testam. Ecclesia, accessione gentium locupletanda, vi- gilante Deo,non ut evellat amplius atque dissipet, quo- modo Ecclesiam Israeliticam antea dissiparat, sed ut ædificet & plantet Ecclesiam. Quo etiam facit in- signis illa promissio, quod fœdus ferire velit Do- minus, cum domo Israel, de lege cordibus ipsorum inscribenda,assumendisque iisdem in populum, ut gratia divina fruantur & remissionem peccatorum consequantur: Quomodo autem glossa Grotii consistat, non apparet. Gemit Ephraim sub captivitate, uti nobis videtur, vel exilio Assyriaco, dolet se castigatum adhuc quasi juvenculum indo- mitum remanere, petit & suspirat ad Dominum; CONVERTE ME, ET CONVER- TAR, quæ non possunt dispari sensu accipi, ut Grotius vult,quasi prius illud,quod petit Ephraim, reditum concernat,posterius,quod promittit sibi, conversionem attineat: quum manifestum sit conversionem ad Dominum petere Ephraimum, ut reapse ad eum convertatur. Adeoque testa- ri, se non posse ad Dominum converti, nisi virtute ac gratia Domini. Unde recte conclu- dit Hieronymus; Ergo id ipsum, quod agimus pœnitentiam, nisi Dei nitamur auxilio, implere non possumus. Postquam enim converteris me, & ad te conversus fuero, tunc cognoscam, quia tu Dominus Deus meus es, & nequaquam ex rores mei, atque peccata interficient me. Et postquam convertisti me, egi pœnitentiam. Vide quantum sit auxilium Dei,& quam fragilis humana conditio, ut hoc ipsum, quo agimus pœnitentiam, ni nos Dominus ante converterit, nequaquam implere valeamus. Et postquam, inquit, ostendisti mihi, vel ipsam pœnitentiam vel tui notitiam, sive cognovi te, percussi femur meum. Quod dolentis & plangentis & super errore pristino ploran- tis indicium est,ut femur manu percutiat & stultum se ante fuisse fateatur. Confusus, inquit, sum & erubui, sive ex die confusionis. Quod enim tempus non est confusionis nostræ, si recordemur an- tiqua peccata, & omnium,quæ male egimus, capia- mus memoriam? Quem sensum parallelus aperte confirmat Thren. 5, 21. Converte nos Domine ad te & convertemur. Quæ prorsus pervertit Gro- tius. Nam quum his verbis Ephraim desideret, atq; expectet gratiam conversionis, ac pœniten- tiam suam testetur, percussione femoris, confusio- ne, & erubescentia sua, in contrarium sensum ea de- torquet Grotius q. d. non posse se vacare agendæ pœ- nitentiæ : Ulterius, quum testetur Dominus, Ephraimum sibi pretiosum esse, se adhuc ejus recor- dari, viscera misericordiæ suæ super ipso commoveri, sese non posse non ejusdem misereri: ex adverso Grotius de abjectione Ephraimi, & ira Dei adver- sus eundem hæc intelligit. Sensus autem Prophe- tæ, ut & communis de eodem consensus Ecclesiæ ita obvius, ac notissimus, ut opus non sit in his hærere. Nam manifestum satis, quod etiam Hie- ronymus hic observavit, locum hunc parallelum esse cum illo Hos. 11. Quid tibi faciam Ephraim? Quid tibi faciam Israel? Quasi Adamam ponam te, & quasi Sebojam. Conversum est in me cor meum, conturbatæ sunt viscera mea. Non faciam furorem iræ meæ & non disperdam Ephraim. Mise- rans miserebor, ait Dominus. Insignem hanc peri- copam Evangelicam, consolationis de misericordia Dei plenissimam, quam nonnulli generaliter de Ecclesia intelligunt, adumbrata per Ephraimum, alii autem etsi Israelitis dictam agnoscant, fidelibus tamen quibusvis merito applicant, in sententiam le- galem & judiciariam commutavit Grotius, qua de- rogetur Israelitis omnis misericordia. Quo pacto nulla tam luculenta supererit promissio, quæ non transformari possit in comminationem.

## 31:21
Vers. 21.

SET UP A WATCHTOWER FOR YOURSELF, PLACE FOR YOURSELF BITTERNESSES] These pertain to the Israelites from the two tribes. The Hebrews have: Set up for yourself markers, place for yourself high heaps, namely, by which roads are accustomed to be marked, so that you may find where you have gone: for you will return by the same way. DIRECT YOUR HEART INTO THE RIGHT WAY IN WHICH YOU HAVE WALKED) Turn your mind to that paved way, through which you have gone. See that you well remember the whole life through which you have been led. RETURN, O VIRGIN OF ISRAEL: RETURN TO THESE CITIES OF YOURS.) That is, I am about to say at some time: return by the same way.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

STATUE TIBI SPECULAM, PONE TIBI AMARITUDINES] Hæc pertinent ad Israelitas ex dua- bus tribubus. Hebræi habent: Statue tibi tiulos, pone tibi altos cumulos, nempe quibus viæ signari solent, ut repe- rias qua iveris : nam eadem redibis. DIRIGE COR TUUM IN VIAM RECTAM IN QUA AMBVLASTI) Adverte animum ad istam viam stra- tam, per quam ivisti. Vide ut totius vitæ, per quam ductus es, bene memineris. REVERTERE VIRGO ISRAEL : REVERTERE AD CIVITATES TVAS ISTAS.) Id est, dicturus sum aliquando : redi eadem via.

## 31:22
Vers. 22.

HOW LONG WILL YOU BE DISSOLVED IN DELIGHTS, O WANDERING DAUGHTER) How long do you withdraw yourself (from me calling you), O rebellious daughter? Why is it that you do not come to me immediately? This exhortation is directed universally to the virgin of Israel, to the wandering daughter. Why it should be restricted to the two tribes does not appear. What is commanded and promised is commanded and promised to all Israelites. I will sow, says the Lord in v. 27, the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of men: And further in v. 32, I will strike a covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Which clearly teach that these things ought not to be limited to the tribe of Judah and Benjamin, as Jerome warned, that from this pericope the former things are to be understood in the advent of the Savior, when both peoples, Israel and Judah, were joined to themselves. Nor is the discourse only about corporal benefits, or the corporal increase and multiplication of the Jews, even if verse 21 were speaking most especially of the return from the Babylonian captivity, although this return cannot be restricted to the Jews alone. For not a few of the other tribes also, especially those who had been left in the promised land and were abducted from there into captivity, returned. For the promised blessing to those returning, for verse 23, THE LORD BLESS THEE, O BEAUTY OF JUSTICE, O HOLY MOUNTAIN, primarily embraces spiritual blessing, and that inebriation of the weary soul, and the satisfying of every hungry soul in verse 25, is spiritual: furthermore, the multiplication and building up in verses 27 and 28 concerns the multiplication and building up of the Church and the faithful, just as is manifest from the covenant which God wishes to strike with the house of Israel and Judah. For this embraces spiritual goods. Add that not a few interpreters wish for those things which are commanded in verse 21, concerning setting up a watchtower, placing bitter things, and directing the heart into the right way, to be understood spiritually concerning the repentance and conversion of the Israelites. Thus Trinus explains: Set up a watchtower for yourself, that is, look out from on high, and place bitter things for yourself, that is, weep bitterly, mourn, be contrite. Weigh how bitter, how sad, how harmful it was to have abandoned the Lord, how happy you were before sin, how miserable after sin. Therefore, having abandoned the crooked way of sinners, the straight way of repentance to turn from captivity into liberty, into your cities of Samaria, which now abound with all spiritual goods through Christ. HOW LONG, O Ephraim, will you wander through delights and life and BE DISSOLVED? You will find nothing there but miseries and eternal perdition. Apply yourself, if you are wise, to the way of virtues, the way of repentance, the way to Christ, and through Christ to God, and into heaven. Thus Menochius: SET UP A WATCHTOWER FOR YOURSELF: as if he were saying, watch and look out, what sin is. SET UP BITTERNESSES FOR YOURSELF. Grieve and mourn bitterly. DIRECT YOUR HEART &c. Apply your heart to retrace the way by which you have walked, so that you may indeed return to Samaria, Zion, and Jerusalem, not the corporal, but the spiritual, namely to the Church. HOW LONG WILL YOU BE DISSOLVED IN DELIGHTS: that is, how long will you be so delicate and soft that you dare not strenuously desert Babylon and the captivity of sin? WANDERING DAUGHTER. You who flee from me and wander, and run to the gods of the nations, and are a rebellious and turning-away king. Our Blessed Bugenhagius takes these words, because GOD orders signs to be set up, in this way: that He wishes them not to forget in what sins and evils they were, lest they fall back into ingratitude, as Paul said to the Corinthians: Know that you were Gentiles, going to dumb idols, as you were led. He explains THE STRAIGHT WAY, not as muddy, not as a way impeded by error and perdition, but as the solid, true way of the Lord, by which one goes straight to God. Blessed Osiander explains it thus: Set up for yourself great monuments of sorrow, that is, bewail your sins from your heart. Direct your heart into the straight way, by which you (formerly) walked when you rendered obedience to God: return to the way, repent, turn back, O virgin (Church) Israel, return to these cities of yours; for you have gone out and begun to wander outside the boundaries of your calling. How long will you be dissolved in delights; Heb. will you go about, O wandering daughter? For those who depart from the way of the word of GOD, they, according to the thoughts and concupiscences of their own heart, wander as if through pathless places and through solitudes, and always depart further from the kingdom of GOD. But when they have returned to the way, grieving from their heart over their errors, they are received by GOD into favor. Do penance, says the Prophet. Jerome also interpreted it concerning penance, but he explained the watchtowers differently, namely, in such a way that he looked toward a corporal return. Set up watchtowers for yourself, set up for yourself &c. How long will you be dissolved in delights, O wandering daughter &c. Where we, he says, have said 'how long will you be dissolved in delights': Symmachus placed; 'How long will you be submerged into the deep?' I have, however, placed both editions in their entirety, so that I might show that this most obscure chapter, which contains the Sacraments of the Church, whether the LXX or whoever else interpreted this Prophet, was either ignored or omitted. He speaks, however, to Ephraim: Set up for yourself watchtowers or watchmen, who may announce to you beforehand that such great happiness of all things is coming. And what follows, bitterness, which in Hebrew are called תמרורים, for which Symmachus interpreted 'transmutations,' indicates this, that she ought to weep either for ancient sins or for the greatness of joy, and be converted with her whole mind to the Lord, and set or direct her heart into the way by which she set out: for from there she is to return. Furthermore, even if you translate the Hebrew words with Grotius, 'set up for yourself titles, set up for yourself high heaps,' the titles and heaps are not therefore to be set up so that the Israelites may know the way by which they were led, nor is it to be drawn to the Jews transported into Chaldea. Brentius understands these things concerning the Israelites in Assyria, that they were to leave behind them statues and monuments of their presence. But if we look at the continuity of the text, that exegesis which wishes repentance to be inculcated here seems to be preferred: Although we do not deny those things,

RETURN TO THESE CITIES OF YOURS, because they speak openly of the Israelite cities to which the virgin Israel ought to return, are to be accepted concerning a corporal return. Because the Lord had promised mercy to Ephraim, verse 20, now therefore, so that he may become a possessor of favor, He excites him to the same repentance and to a return to his cities. Whence, by the force of the context, these things are to be understood concerning the Israelites and Ephraim, that is, concerning the ten tribes, not concerning the Jews. Which was correctly observed by Jerome, who therefore notes the Vulgate (Greek) version here: The Hebrew word צִיֻּנִים is translated either into watchmen or into watchtowers, as Aquila and Symmachus interpreted. Whence I wonder what the Vulgate edition intended for itself, that for צִיֻּנִים, that is, for watchmen, it should place Zion: and disturb the reader's understanding, so that he might think that after Ephraim the speech of GOD was suddenly made to Zion and to the tribe of Judah, when the discourse is perpetually Ephraim, to whom He spoke above; Hearing I have heard Ephraim: And, Ephraim is an honorable son to me, or a delicate boy, to whom He also now speaks: Set up for yourself watchtowers, or watchmen. Brentius also observed the same thing, at the words I WILL SURELY HAVE MERCY. The return of the kingdom of Jeroboam is prophesied in some way, begun after the return of the kingdom of Rehoboam of the two tribes from Babylon, but fulfilled under CHRIST, where the remnants of Israel were saved. But before others, our Blessed Bugenhagius has diligently executed these things, that it is the kingdom of Ephraim that is treated here, which he proves both from those things which precede concerning Israel and Ephraim, and from those which follow, and indeed also from the immediately subjoined prophecy concerning the conception of the Messiah, which he will excellently lead to be restricted here to the land of Israel, fol. 337, rendering this reason for the coherence: Return, O daughter of Israel, or you Ephraim, so that in your land, according to the promises of GOD, you may receive the Messiah not born of man and woman, as all men are now born, but of a woman alone, according to the flesh, that is, of a virgin, for the Lord will create a new thing in the earth. A woman shall compass a man. Blessed Bugenhagius continues afterwards in this way: Our elders before us understood it concerning the mother of the Savior being pregnant, which is the true meaning of this promise, but that which is said, in the land or upon the land, they did not sufficiently attend to. For they understood it generally upon the earth, that is, in the world, although Jeremiah here speaks specifically of the land of Israel, or the Kingdom of Ephraim, as it once was, which matter also adds a singular prophecy concerning the land where CHRIST is to be conceived, and carried in the womb of his mother, and afterwards educated; so that the Jews mocked our Lord JESUS CHRIST in vain, calling him a Nazarene and a Galilean, and slandering him, that he could not be the Messiah, or CHRIST, who had come from Nazareth and from the land of Israel of Galilee, when CHRIST was promised from the land of Judah from Bethlehem, according to the prophecy of Micah. And thou Bethlehem, land of Judah, etc. The blind Jews did not see, just as they do not see even today, this prophecy of Jeremiah concerning CHRIST and his mother, of whom I shall now speak. Return, he says, daughter of Israel, return to these cities of yours, that is, You from the kingdom of Israel, or Ephraim, who have been led away from your land by the Assyrian, who act in despair, as if you were never to be received back by GOD. For you do not have a promise of being brought back, so that you might one day be brought back to your land, from whence the Lord cast you out on account of your iniquities and the contempt of his word: Accept now the promise of GOD. Return to your cities in the land of your fathers. And although he calls her a deserter of father and mother, that is, a harlot and an adulteress, so that she may acknowledge her sins, and believe that she is not received by her own merit but by the grace of GOD alone, yet at the same time He also calls her daughter, and daughter of Israel, so that she may still hope well for the mercy of GOD, especially that those greatest promises concerning the Messiah the liberator, whom GOD had promised to the Jews would come into their land from the flesh of Abraham, had not yet perished before GOD. For the Israelites, already performing penance in captivity, feared that GOD had withdrawn those excellent promises, which however is impossible. For those promises concerning CHRIST were promises of the grace of GOD and gratuitous, not promises of the Law, as we have said sometimes before. How, they say, will that liberator and triumphant Messiah, the Son of Abraham, the son of David, come to us into our land, and into our cities, when we have been cast out from there, and there is no hope for us of returning thither, pressed under servitude in captivity, and the Samaritans occupy everything there? To whom Jeremiah says, Return to these thy cities, how long wilt thou turn away, O backsliding daughter? The Lord will provide for thee in the land, and in thy cities, whatever He promised thee, especially concerning CHRIST, for the Lord will create a new thing, in your land of Israel, or Ephraim, in the Kingdom which you called the Kingdom of Samaria, in the land of the ten tribes. Which thing is called new, and to be created by the Lord, because from the foundation of the world it had not been done or come to pass before, yet it was promised, and was expected by believers, but it will be created new by GOD in your land, from whence you were cast out. Return therefore into your land, GOD will receive you as beloved sons, just as He receives the prodigal and backsliding son, Luke 15. Hasten, speed you backsliders to your land. You have enough in your land, even if you do not receive the fields and paternal possessions, as those who are from the Kingdom of Judah, when Cyrus shall have released, through the grace of GOD towards you, the captivity, do not despise the gift of GOD. Return hither: The promises of GOD concerning CHRIST have not perished, as you foolishly fear. You will receive in the land of Israel, first and before others, those greatest gifts of GOD promised to you, the highest riches, the highest delights, the highest power, liberation from the wrath of God, from your sins, from your death, righteousness and eternal life, namely that man, Christ, CHRIST, who was promised to you. These things B. Bugenhagius, which excellently illustrate the connection of the antecedents and consequents in this context, and contribute not a little to the declaration of the oracle, which follows next.

Verse of the same.

FOR THE LORD HATH CREATED A NEW THING UPON THE EARTH). I am doing a new thing. A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN.) Proverbial. Men are accustomed to woo maidens: not maidens men. Thus it was the people's part to seek God: But God comes of His own accord to the people, and woos their love. Moses Hadarsan also mystically adapts these things to the Messiah at Gen. 41, 21.

A strange gloss, the sense of which I confess I cannot penetrate: If men are ordinarily accustomed to woo maidens, not maidens men, it would have been extraordinary and singular that the people, designated by the woman, should woo and compass God, as a man. Thus the Prophet, according to the Grotian explanation, would invert the matter in this place, since he sells as a mere and singular thing that which is that God woos the people, and comes to them of His own accord. Perhaps Grotius wished to say the contrary, namely that this is indicated, that the people should return again to God, and woo His love, not indeed that God should come of His own accord to the people. Which is the opinion of certain Jews. For although they understand it of a common wife embracing, or bringing back a husband from whom she had departed, and say that this began to be fulfilled in the exile according to Isaiah 4, 1, they nevertheless explain it also of the Israelitic people returning to the Lord,

and performing penance, who had made a divorce from the Lord, as a husband, and had prostituted themselves to many adulterers. Whither also Jonathan seems to go, thus paraphrasing: For behold the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, And the people of the house of Israel shall apply themselves to the law: Where the Paraphrast did not render word for word, as if he understood the law by the man, and to apply themselves by to embrace, but expressed the sense, as he does other times very often, which he believed to be indicated by the Prophet, namely that the people, having turned to the Lord, will apply themselves to the law, and will adhere to the Lord by pious study and obedience to the law. Sanctius at this place gathers from their versions that the Seventy Elders and Theodotion likewise understood this oracle concerning the salutary conversion to God of the Jewish Synagogue, which had been for some time separated from God by spiritual adultery, by which conversion, to be excited beyond hope, she would seek God her husband and her salvation, when the LXX have it thus: ὅτι ἔκτισε κύριος σωτηρίαν εἰς κ̅τ̅ φυτευσιν, ϰ’ ἐν σωτηρίᾳ σὐ περιελεύσονται ἄνθρωποι. Which, however, Theodoret at this place wished to be understood rather of the calling of the Gentiles through the Apostles, writing thus: In this place the Prophet openly shows the cause of the revocation, when through it he prophesies that there will be a new plantation; for this they had brought to the world, who were born from it, the Apostles, which the Prophetic discourse (sc. according to the LXX and Theodoret's version) does not obscurely say, men shall come from everywhere in salvation; for these, passing through all nations, brought salvation to them through the knowledge of God. To which sense also those favor who, among the Christians, accept it concerning the conversion of the Jewish Synagogue to God, from whom it had been turned away and alienated; which is the interpretation of some Papists, Hieron. ab Oleastr. Can. 4. Prooem. in Gen. Johan. Pinedae de Salom. l. 3. cap. 3. Francisc. Sanchez at this place, etc. To whom are almost twin those who understand it of the reduction of the Israelitic people to the communion of the Church, which will be especially in the New Testament, because that Church, having been turned away, having been converted to Christ, to whom she was once betrothed, will embrace the same anew, as her husband. Which sense is defended especially by Pareus l. 2. contr. D. Hunnium p. 166. and Dn. D. Johan. Tarnovius in Exercit. Bibl. pag. 311. seqq. Who indeed narrate it concerning the conversion to God, and his wooing, or embrace through faith, but of the Gentiles under the New Testament, to be brought to Christ. As Theodoret, LXX Interpr. & insisting on the versions of Theodotion, he understands the divine planting and the circuit of the Apostles into all nations, for the sake of their salvation. Franciscus Junius, however, with Tremellius, following the Hebrew sources, say that the woman encompassing the man is the Church of God, which, being bereaved of Israel and the Jews, her own children, on account of their apostasy, as a widow and barren woman, is about to encompass a Man, and to procure for herself sons and daughters from elsewhere, in his notes on this passage. If Grotius wished to say things akin to these, he ought to have explained his mind otherwise. But whatever may be the case regarding that intricate gloss of Grotius, we understand the oracle concerning Christ, not only in a mystical sense, but in a proper and literal one; namely, that the woman Mary, the blessed Virgin, is about to encompass and enclose in her womb not an infant or a boy, but a man, and that without the work of a man, which is truly wonderful. Because Christ, an infant in the womb of his virgin mother, was already גבר, a man and a Hero. John Calvin indeed superciliously laughs at this opinion and exposition, which he acknowledges is almost common to Christians, inasmuch as they have almost with one consent interpreted these things concerning the Virgin Mary, and he brings forth this explanation from the quiver of his wisdom: women will reduce men to straits, so that they will hold them captive. Johannes Piscator of Herborn wanders on the same string in his scholia on this passage: This is the meaning:

You Jews, who are now like weak and despondent women in your defense against the Chaldeans, will be so courageous and bold in the return from the Babylonian captivity that you might even hostilely surround and overwhelm the mighty Chaldeans. Elsewhere, however, Piscator (namely in his Commentary, page 211) paraphrases this passage thus: 'A woman shall encompass a man,' that is, the Christian Church, although before the world she will be like a weak and infirm woman, yet she will dare to resist her powerful persecutors through confession, and will overcome them by faith, 1 John 5:4.

These arguments, which were briefly produced in a festive program for the birthday solemnities of our Savior in the name of the Rector and the Academic Senate of Königsberg in the year 1640, and which we think should be repeated here, though somewhat illustrated, because the copies have been distributed, prove our exposition. (I.) The connection of the text, made by the particle כי: which relates the cause for which the Israelites, now accustomed to the captivity—which the clemency of the Kingdom had made tolerable—with homes fixed here and there throughout the East, and captivated by its delights and riches, might be stirred to desire their homeland, which they had seen exposed to various incursions. But nothing could move and animate the Jews to this, except that it necessarily and solely had to be performed in Judea by the power of divine promises; nor could a more urgent argument be proposed to them than the conception of the Messiah alone in the land of Israel. For the fact that it deals rather with a spiritual conversion than a bodily return, verse 21, is persuaded by the commemoration of the Mercurial statues, the signs pointing the way, and the road by which one went from Judea to Assyria, and the cities to which they are ordered to return, and the conversion of their captivity, as Grotius himself interprets, or the memorable signs to be left in Assyria, as Brentius explains, which no necessity compels to be taken otherwise than according to the letter. (II.) The new Creation, which the Prophet mentions: The word ברא in a more eminent sense imports a creation properly so called, whether immediate or mediate. But no other encompassing can be designated in this place, for the efficiency of which the work of a creation properly so called might be required in detail, except this one, by which Jehovah, out of the infinity of His power, created the human nature of Christ in the womb of the Blessed Virgin, and thus brought it about that she should encompass, or conceive, this man. The name of creation is indeed attributed also to conversion, but in a metaphorical sense: which no reason compels us to admit; nor is it used absolutely, but with an addition, as in Psalm 51:12, the creation of a clean heart, or with some other determination added, which does not occur here. (III.) The designation of novelty. 'New' placed absolutely is to be taken for absolutely new, unless the nature of the thing or the continuity of the text teaches that it is only new in a certain respect. Since this is not the case here, we are entirely urged to understand that new thing as the newest of all new things, which alone is new under the sun, as Damascene says in Book 3, O. F. ch. 1. For all other things that can be brought forward here are not absolutely new, but only new in a certain way. And therefore, insisting on the literal sense, we conclude that the great mystery of godliness concerning the controversy, 1 Timothy 3:16, which alone deserves to be called absolutely new according to Scripture, is designated as the singularly wonderful and wonderfully singular virginal embrace and conception of the eternal Son of God. Which 'New' thing the faithful of the Old Testament uniquely desired, Luke 2:15, 38; ch. 10:24. (IV.) The determination of the place. This newest encompassing is promised to be in the future land, and indeed that which includes the mountains of Samaria and Ephraim, in which

Rama is situated, verses 5, 6, 15. Which is the boundary of Israel, verse 17. And in which are the cities of Israel, verse 22. Therefore, no other encompassing will be denoted than that one of the womanly conception: since all the rest happen even elsewhere outside the land of Israel. We owe this observation concerning the land of the conception of the Messiah primarily to our blessed Bugenhagen, who handed it down in his Commentary, fol. 342. We have said that this does not signify 'in the land' or 'upon the earth' generally in the world, as almost all interpreters before us understood, but only specifically 'upon the land' or 'in the land,' namely in the land of Ephraim, that is, of the ten tribes, whose land after Solomon was called the Kingdom of Israel, the Kingdom of Joseph, the Kingdom of Ephraim, the Kingdom of Samaria, as has been sufficiently said above. For Jeremiah speaks in this place to those ten tribes, which had long since been led away through Assyria and cast out from their land, saying: 'You shall again plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria.' Because there will be a time when the watchmen in the mountains of Ephraim will cry: 'Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.' For I am a Father to Israel; and Ephraim is my firstborn: Likewise, 'I have surely heard Ephraim lamenting, etc. Is Ephraim my precious son, and a desirable child? Return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities. How long wilt thou turn away, O backsliding daughter? FOR THE LORD will create a new thing in the earth. A woman shall encompass a Man': namely, Him who is promised, the crusher of the serpent's head, that seed of the woman, that seed of Abraham, in whom all the families of the earth shall be blessed. For the promises of God concerning Christ have not fallen away because of your sins, as you foolishly fear, but you shall receive the promised Man in your land, that is, in the land of the ten tribes, before He Himself comes into the land of the two tribes, or into the land of Judah. It is indeed promised in the Prophets that an eternal King will arise from the House and family, or lineage, of David, and in the Prophet Micah, that He will be born in Bethlehem, and will come to His holy temple, a Teacher in Zion or Jerusalem: 'And thou, O tower of Eder,' he says, 'which art the stronghold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall come thy golden Rose, the former dominion, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem': and that the Gospel and the kingdom of Christ will go forth from Jerusalem, and will be spread through the whole world, to all nations; 'out of Zion,' he says, 'shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And He shall judge among many peoples, and shall rebuke strong nations in distant regions, etc.' But nevertheless, as the Lord promises here through Jeremiah, in the land of Israel, or Ephraim, that is, of the ten tribes which had been cast away into Assyria and the cities of the Medes, that man, God and man, the crusher of the serpent's head, the blessing of all nations, shall be conceived in a maternal womb, not from the seed of a man, but from a new operation and creation of God, which God shall create as a new thing in the earth, in the land of Ephraim, not in the land of Judah, nor elsewhere in the world. Return, he says, O daughter of Israel, return to these cities, how long will you turn away, O backsliding daughter? You shall receive in your land, which God promised to you, eternal salvation. FOR THE LORD SHALL CREATE A NEW THING IN THE EARTH, namely yours, A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN. He shall be conceived, I say, and carried in the womb of a mother in the land of Israel, until the virgin mother brings him forth in Bethlehem in the land of Judah, according to the prophecy of Micah, as leader and ruler of all Israel. Whence furthermore the Blessed Bugenhagen notes concerning the fulfillment of the prophecy on folio 345: That Joseph and Mary, who were indeed of the house of David and the royal lineage, nevertheless on account of poverty had nothing of their own in Bethlehem, the city and fatherland of David, and were compelled to dwell in a foreign land, namely in Galilee, which belonged to the land of Ephraim, or of the ten tribes, so that this prophecy of Jeremiah might be fulfilled: The Lord will create a new thing in your land, O Ephraim. A woman shall encompass a man, whom, however, she will not bring forth there, but in the land of Judah in Bethlehem, as Micah foretold.

(V.) The designation of the one encompassing, which is called נְקֵבָה. But that word is nowhere in the Holy Scriptures used collectively for any multitude, or for the whole female sex; it always denotes a singular individual, either vague or determined, of the female sex, which an induction of the passages most openly teaches, so that it is a wonder that this is denied. Nor does it precisely imply a female joined to a male as a second principle of generation, in which something is begotten; but it designates a female in general, because she is distinguished from the male by nature, whether she is subordinated to the male for generation or not. Nor is that subordination hinted at in those places where that word occurs; indeed, sometimes it cannot even have a place, as in Lev. 12, 5. 7. There is, therefore, no reason for us to doubt that it is fitting for Mary, the Theotokos, as the most choice workshop of the Holy Spirit from the female sex, and one already destined for marriage and betrothed. Indeed, if one must insist on the proper and customary signification of the scriptures, by which it denotes a singular individual of the female sex, not even another woman could be given who is intended here, besides that blessed virgin.

(VI.) The notation of the encompassing. The word סָבַב in general is to embrace, likewise to surround, and to encompass, just as R. Nathan Mardoch. explains that circumference in his Concordance by הִקִּיף: and it agrees very well with uterine encompassing: by which the fetus is encompassed on all sides by the maternal womb, is circumscribed, and is cherished by a vital embrace. For although a similar example does not occur in the Scriptures where it is applied to conception, yet the general signification can conveniently be applied to the species; and the Rabbis, Chaldeans, and Arabs express the cause by this word; and therefore it fits not badly with causal conservation, such as that of an infant in the womb; nay, the Chaldeans even derive the word סוֹבֵא (menstruum) from it, and the Arab interpreter expressed it in this place by 'he will vivify,' which pertains to the office of the womb, 'having a vital power,' as Basil says. There are, moreover, not a few hapax legomena in the Scriptures: Finally, this conception is also monotropos and singular to that extent. But concerning the complexation by which a woman encompasses a husband, or the Church encompasses God, it not only does not occur anywhere in the scriptures, but it is also clear by any certain document that the word is not to be understood in this way in this place: Indeed, it is easily evident that it is not to be understood so: because if the Lord creates this new thing, how will it be understood concerning the Jews spontaneously encompassing the Lord? And since conversion is by no means of our own powers, how could the Jews have spontaneously encompassed the Lord, who rather sighed: 'Convert us, O Lord, and we shall be converted'? Add that this reasoning becomes tautological: 'Return, O virgin of Israel' through repentance: because 'a woman shall encompass a man': that is, because the Israelites will encompass the Lord; or they are about to do penance and convert themselves to the Lord. See Dn. D. Müller in Judaismo, ch. 19, p. 661.

(VII.) The designation of the one encompassed. He is called גֶּבֶר, which name there is no doubt fits God. Deut. 10, 17. Jer. 32, 28, where he is called גִּבּוֹר (mighty) and Jer. 20, 11, where he is called μαχητὴς (warrior), and the better interpreters understand this of God in this place, and indeed as the bridegroom and husband of the Church, and thus of Christ, who is the bridegroom of the Church: Matt. 9, 15. John 3, 29. 2 Cor. 11, 2. Eph. 5, 23, etc. Who is, moreover, called גִּבּוֹר as a proper name in the prophetic nomenclature, Isa. 9, 6, as also Ps. 45, 4. Indeed, by this very word גֶּבֶר, Zechariah is pointed out

13, 7. Compare Matt. 27, 31. Mark 14, 27. You are in vain if you say that the name גֶּבֶר does not fit Christ in the maternal womb: For it is also applied to a newly born infant in Job 3, 2, as also by Onkelos in Gen. 4, 1, and it is attributed by Isaiah to the newly born child in chapter 9, 6. Add that this name, denoting a hero in a more famous signification, is used here peculiarly and with choice concerning the conception of the Messiah: because he himself was already a hero in his mother's womb, instructed by divine power and virtue, and by the אֶל מֵ֫טְרוֹן, which can be said of no infant enclosed in the womb. Therefore Bugenhagen illustrated these words with such a paraphrase: 'You Israelites will first receive this most strong hero, a powerful man, and indeed a true almighty one, as being God and man, in your land, with GOD creating and making this new thing in your land, that a woman shall encompass a man, that is, a woman shall carry in her womb that strong and almighty hero, the Messiah, whom you have long expected as promised by God.' Concerning which Jerome also warned: 'The Lord will create a new thing upon the earth. Without the seed of a man, without any intercourse and conception, a woman shall encompass a man in the bosom of her womb, who, according to the growth of age, will indeed seem to progress in wisdom and age through crying and infancy, but the perfect man will be contained in the female womb for the usual months.'

(VIII.) The reason of the context. Which is entirely occupied with the benefits of the incarnation of Christ, reconciliation with God, and the blessings arising from the covenant of God, into which the Prophet sprinkles this new thing to be created by the Lord, so that he may recall them to the source and foundation by his death. Compare Jer. 23, 5; ch. 33, 15. Dn. D. Müller explained the coherence of the text more prolixly in Judaismo, part 1, ch. 19. That the Prophet is accustomed in this and the preceding chapter to comfort the Church through the advent of the Messiah, whom he calls David in ch. 30, 9, and therefore excites the people to joy in ch. 31, 7, 13, as prophets are wont to do when they announce the advent of the Messiah, Isa. 9, v. 3, Zech. 9, 9, and brings forward the benefits of the Messiah, our salvation also, the blessing in v. 24, the recreation of the weary in v. 25, the remission of sins in v. 34. Which connection Jerome also indicates: 'Look at what I am about to say, and diligently attend to whence such great blessedness is to be expected by you: Hear what you had never known before: The Lord has created a new thing, etc.'

(IX.) The commemoration of the weeping of Rachel, v. 15, which is referred to the infanticide of Herod at the time of the newly born Christ, Matt. 2, 18. That encompassing is therefore understood which is connected with the slaughter at Bethlehem.

(X.) Nazareth. The dance, and mutual invitation v. 6. where if נוֹצְרִים be taken as a proper patronymic, the remnant of Israel in Nazareth are indicated as rejoicing, and inviting one another to celebrate the Lord on account of Jesus the Nazarene, their fellow countryman, Matt. 2, 23. to which the promise of this new thing to be created in the land of Israel, namely the conception of the Messiah, for which Nazareth was divinely chosen, Luke 1, 26. seems excellently to correspond.

(XI.) The Prophetic definition of the place of conception. For since the Spirit of God has so accurately noted the place of the birth of the Messiah in Micah 5, 2. and of his upbringing in Matt. 2, 23. and of his ministry and preaching in Hagg. 2, 8. Mal. 3, 1. and of his Passion in Zech. 12, 11: and it is not likely that He would not have defined and foretold the place of conception, ecclesiastical writers have diligently inquired, and at length discovered this place, as Mr. Chemnitz observes in his Harmony of the Gospels, chap. 4, col. 37, and it was established by the pious investigation of the blessed Pomeranus.

(XII.) The confession of the better interpreters, who for the most part approve this female embrace and conception of Christ as an exegesis. Among Christians, the same is defended by the older Doctors, Justin in the Dialogue with Trypho, Cyprian in the Sermon on the Nativity of Christ, Augustine in Sermon 9 de tempore on the Nativity of the Lord, Jerome in his Commentary on this passage, Vol. 4, likewise Rabanus, Strabus in the ordinary gloss, and also Bernard by more recent ones from the Papists, Lyranus, Galatinus, and others; from the Calvinists, Oecolampadius, Zwingli, Pellican, Bullinger, etc., in their commentaries on this passage. And most of our own; all, even the Blessed Luther. Although the former in his version inclined toward that opinion which was approved by Calvin, by rendering the passage thus, (as the Bibles of the year 32 published at Wittenberg testify) 'How long will you turn yourself away, you daughter, whom I will bring back? For the Lord will create a new thing in the land, that those who previously acted like women shall be men.' Afterwards, however, having examined the passage and noted the circumstances of the prophetic text, he expunged the former version in an accurate revision of the translation, and substituted the one which copies have today: 'How long will you go astray, you backsliding daughter? For the Lord will create a new thing in the land, a woman shall encompass a man.' He confirmed the opinion in the marginal gloss against the Jews partly by the novelty of this encompassing, partly by the series of the context, which deals entirely with the New Testament: and therefore he commands this new thing, which the Lord was about to create on earth, by which a woman (an incorrupt virgin) is a new and miraculous mother, and thus, because of the Messiah, the son of a virgin, to bury Moses, and to turn oneself into the way of the Lord. Because by this virgin mother conceiving, Moses had to be buried, and Israel had to be converted to Christ. Luke 1:16, 17, 76. And the New Testament took its beginning. But although Megalander also hands down another sense there, namely the meaning or figure of the Apostle in Romans 7:6, that we, having been previously concluded by the law, now embrace the law as it were, which is now not above us, but below us: he nevertheless insinuates that one only as a certain allegorical accommodation: but he accepts and approves the former as proper and literal. Which he also confirmed in the book 'De Schemhamphorasch', Vol. 8, Jena, German, fol. 133, in the year 1543, from the consensus of the Christian world and the emphasis of the words. 'This has been read and understood in the whole of Christendom concerning Christ and the Virgin Mary, his mother, as is right and proper. It shall be a new thing, he says, which has not been before on earth. Children have been born from the beginning, government has existed, evil and good people have lived, improved themselves, and worsened themselves, as it still goes on now, and will go on until the end of the world. But here the new miracle shall happen, which has never happened before, namely a Nekefa, a woman, who is not a man, shall encompass a man, that is: Mary shall conceive and bear God's Son.' For that must be, if our faith is to be right, that Christ our Lord, in the moment when Mary gave her consent to the angel Gabriel and said: 'Be it done to me according to your word,' was at once God and perfect man, in one person, as the dear Fathers in the Council of Ephesus maintained against Nestorius. For where that should not be, she would not be to be called Theotokos, God's mother, nor would Christ be to be called her son. We add to these the testimony of the older Jews. R. Moses Hadarschan in Gen. 41 has it thus: '& he comforted him in a virgin, as it is said in Jer. 31:21, etc. Return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities, until when wilt thou be wayward, O backsliding daughter? For God created a new thing in the earth, a woman shall encompass a man.' R. Huna in the name of R. Idi and R. Joshua Ben Levi said that this is the King Messiah, of whom it is said in Psalm 2:7, I have this day begotten thee. We have therefore the consensus of R. Idi, Rabbi Joshua ben Levi, R. Huna, and R. Moses Hadarschan, to whom R. Hakkadosch also accedes in Gali Razia. See 'Pugio Fidei' by Raimund Martin, part 3, Distinct. 3, chap. 19; Petrus Galatinus, book 7, 'De Arcanis Catholicae Veritatis', chap. 14, col. 414. Blessed Luther stopped the mouths of the more recent Jews, whose sense Grotius seems to have wished to express, in the cited passage. 'He also wants to show his art in the passage of Jeremiah 31, where he says, "A woman shall encompass a man," it should mean as much as: the people of Israel is the woman, God the man: Now Israel has been a whore in idolatry, afterwards she has converted and repented, thereby again encompassing and reconciling the man, that is, God. Even if the words could yield that, as cannot be, how can such a thing be called a new thing created on earth?' Has the people of Israel never been such a whore, and been converted again? Ask the Book of Judges about that. Here it wants to come to this, that what a Rabbi calls new, that is new, what he calls old, that is old, as the rule gives above concerning the left and right hand. He also added another very foolish gloss of the Jews, which we subjoin, so that the blindness of the learned Grotius may be recognized. 'Beyond that, his art is even higher in this place, they say, the woman is to be understood as the whore Israel, but when they have a wedding, they lead the bride three times around the bridegroom, so that they may satisfy this passage of Jeremiah, "A woman encompasses the man." Here Nekefa, the woman, must be called a virgin, there a whore. Why?' Therefore, that the Rabbis cannot err when they say a whore is a virgin, and a virgin a whore, according to the rule: That the left hand is the right, if a Rabbi calls it right. And such new things must also never have happened before, when a woman or bride is led three times around the man, for Jeremiah says: It shall be a new thing created by the Lord on earth; but here a Rabbi has soon helped the matter, and said, what he calls new, that is new, but what he calls old, that is old, etc. In sum, the desperate devilish lying-mouths think nothing else but that the Holy Scripture is their own, like a piece of paper from which they might carve little men, little birds, little houses, little cat-stools, as they wish, and whatever it says, both their Jews and we Christians should accept as right. It has pleased Grotius, therefore, to follow such illustrious teachers and guides. Nor is there any reason why anyone should think that these two diverse opinions can be joined. This fiction in Pareus, although he also appeals to the consensus of Oecolampadius, Zwingli, Pellican, and Bullinger, was refuted by the blessed Hunnius in his Anti-Pareus, page 229. But I, my Pareus, will show myself a diligent spectator and an attentive listener, by what arts you wish to force into one interpretation, or as you say, to join, your opinion, which Calvin ascribes to the Jews: And that of the Christians, who interpret the saying of Jeremiah concerning the conception of a virgin. Concerning those who affect an abundance of speech, when they cannot even once explain a matter aptly, Erasmus of Rotterdam writes somewhere that those inept men heap up certain synonyms so distrustful of one another that they themselves wonder how they could ever agree. The same may be affirmed of Pareus connecting opinions that are utterly unconnected, and so dissident among themselves, that they themselves wonder by whose craftsman's work they have come together into one. If those two opinions are to be joined, then or under the analogy of type and antitype, they will have to be joined or connected simply. In neither way do they allow themselves to be coupled. If you try the former way, this absurd paraphrase will emerge: Just as the Jewish Church, which like a deserter and adulteress had deserted the Lord, will embrace the same by a new miracle as it were, and will constantly adhere to him with true repentance; so at some time a virgin woman will conceive in a virginal womb the Messiah the Lord. Beautiful, charming, elegant, nothing above it. If this composition pleases anyone less, and the other is held, what could be said more inconveniently than that? For it is necessary that the conciliator strike against this rock of most prodigious absurdity, so that the word WOMAN may signify at once and simultaneously that adulterous deserter of God, the Jewish Church, in one sense, and then the most holy mother of God in another sense: then the word to surround may denote at once the conversion in the sense of Pareus, and then the conception of the Son of God from a virgin, in our sense: the word man may at once and simultaneously designate God simply, that is, the whole Trinity, and then (in the other opinion) not the whole Trinity, but only the Son. What kind of method of interpreting the Scriptures this is, whether it has even been heard of in the Church (I will not say received or frequented), let the judgment be most free, not only among friends, but also enemies. These are the words of the blessed Hunnius the elder, which it seemed good to transcribe in full, so that it may be known by this example, and by the judgment of that theologian of the τῶν μακαρίτων, our predecessor, how absurdly those who are accustomed to rub a double sense onto the words of Scripture connect unconnected opinions. Nor do I believe that anyone who has seen how the blessed Hunnius has weakened the same will easily kiss Calvin's opinion. The Prophet, says Calvin, uses the singular number, as if he were to say: one woman will excel many men, that is, individual Jews will excel individual Chaldeans, thus the Jews will be superior, although the strength of the enemies is great and terrible. For thus Calvin had the necessity to transform the first singular into the plural, so that for woman he substituted women, who will reduce men to straits. Then to convert the other noun man also into the plural. Thirdly, to take the word woman again as referring to one. Because he says: this is the sense, one woman will excel many men. Furthermore, to twist these things in such a way, that by women, Jews are to be understood, and by men, Chaldeans; and then these things are to be connected thus: That the Jews, who in respect to the Chaldeans can be considered as women, are about to reduce the Chaldeans to straits: whence our Hunnius not undeservedly asked, who gave Calvin this license to feign anything from anything by metamorphoses that almost surpass those of Ovid, and to transform woman into women, women into Jews, and from man into men, namely Chaldeans. And whether this is something new on earth, or whether the Jews have not often routed innumerable forces of most powerful enemies with a small band. Finally, what annals of histories testify that the captive Jews, either in the very victory of the Persians against the Babylonians, or after the Chaldeans had already been defeated by Cyrus, opposed them with an armed hand, or at least joined their forces with the Persians and Medes in defeating the Babylonians, it is so far from the case that they themselves overcame these in a peculiar conflict and brought them into their own captivity. But these things also regarding the gloss of Calvin. Mr. Theodorus Hacksp. discussed the exceptions and arguments of the blessed Joh. Tarnovius, who adheres to this opinion of Calvin, at this place. The new exposition of the Papist Ludovicus Alcafar is not worthy to be brought forward, let alone to be subjected to examination: because it is ridiculous. For he thinks the mystery of the Eucharist is signified, which contains the body of Christ. How this squares with either the words or the context, no one will perceive unless he excels in Jesuitical acumen.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

USQUEQUO DELITIIS DISSOLVERIS FILIA VAGA) Quousque te subducis, (mihi te vocanti) filia re- bellis? Quid est, quod non statim ad me venis? Parænesis hæc dirigitur universaliter ad vir- ginem Israel, ad filiam vagam. Cur ad duas tribus restringenda sit, non apparet. Quæ mandantur, & promittuntur, omnibus Israelitis mandata & pro- missa sunt. Seminabo, inquit v. 27. Dominus, do- mum Israel & domum Iuda semine hominum: Et porro v. 32. Feriam domui Israel & domui Iuda pactum. Quæ aperte docent, non debere hæc limitari ad tribum Juda & Benjamin, uti monuit Hieronymus, ex hac pericopa esse superiora in ad- ventu Salvatoris intelligenda, quando uterque popu- lus sibi Israel & Iuda copulatus est. Neque de cor- poralibus beneficiis tantum sermo est, aut aug- mento & multiplicatione Judæorum corporali, etiamsi maxime vers. 21. loqueretur de reditu è ca- ptivitateBabylonica, quamvis neque hic reditus ad solos Judæos restringi possit. Siquidem etiam alia- rum tribuum non pauci, cumprimis ex illis, qui in terra promissa relicti erant, & in captivitatem in- de abducti sunt, reversi sint. Redeuntibus enim promissa benedictio Vers. enim 23. BENEDICAT TIBI DOMINUS, PULCHRITUDO JU- STITIÆ MONS SANCTUS, imprimis spi- ritualem benedictionem complectitur, & inebriatio illa animæ lassæ, ac saturatio omnis animæ esurientis vers. 25. spiritualis est : multiplicatio insuper & ædificatio vers. 27. 28. Ecclesiæ & fidelium multi- plicationem & ædificationem concernit, quemad- modum ex fœdere quod Deus cum domo Israel & Juda ferire vult, manifestum est. Hoc enim bona spiritualia complectitur. Adde, quod non pauci Interpp. ea, quæ jubentur vers. 21. de statuenda spe- cula, ponendis amaritudinibus, de dirigendo cor- de in viam rectam, spiritualiter intellecta velint de pœnitentia & conversione Israelitarum. Sic Trinus exponit : Statue tibi speculam, id est, ex alto speculare, & pone tibi amaritudines, id est, amare plora, luge, conterere. Expende quam amarum, quam triste, quam noxium fuerit reliquisse Dominum, quam felix fueris ante peccatum, quam miser post peccatum. Ergo relicta via curva pec- catorum, recta via pœnitentiæconvertere e captivita- te in libertatem, in civitates tuas Samariæ, quæ bonis nunc omnibus spiritualibus affluunt per Christum. USQUE. QUO, o Ephraim per delicias & vita va- gaberis ac DISSOLVERIS? Nil ibi reperies præter miserias & perditionem æternam. Intende, si sapis, viæ virtutum, viæ pœnitentiæ, viæ ad Christum, & per Christum ad Deum, & in cælum. Sic Meno- chius: STATUE TIBI SPECULAM: quasi dicat, vigila, & speculare, quid sit peccatum. PONE TIBI AMARITUDINES. Doleas & amare lu- geas. DIRIGE COR TUUM &c. Applica cor tuum ad retexendam viam, per quam ambulasti, ut nimirum revertaris in Samariam, Sion & Jeru- salem, non corporalem, sed spiritualem, scilicet ad Ec- clesiam. USQUE QUO DELICIIS DISSOL- VERIS: id est, usquequo adeo eris delicata, & mol- lis ut strenue Babylonem, & peccati captivitatem de- serere non audeas? FILIA VAGA. Quæ a me fugis & vagaris, & ad gentium Deos, & reges discur- ris rebellis, & aversatrix. B. Bugenhagius noster hæc, quod DEUS signa erigi jubeat, ita accipit, quod velit, ne obliviscantur, in quibus peccatis, & malis fuerint, ne rursus deficiant ad ingratitudinem, ut Paulus Corinthiis dixit: Scitote, quod gentes fuistis, ad idola muta, ut ducebamini, euntes. VIAM STRATAM explicat, non lutosam, non impiditam erroris & perditionis viam, sed solidam, veram viam Domini, qua itur recta ad Deum. B. Osiander ita exponit: Pone tibi monumenta magna doloris, id est, defle ex animo peccata tua. Dirige cor tuum in viam rectam, ut qua (olim) ambulasti, cum Deo obedientiam præstares: redi in viam, resipi- sce,convertere virgo (Ecclesia) Israel, revertere ad civitates tuas istas; egressa es enim & vagari cœpisti extra terminos vocationis tuæ. Usquequo deliciis dissolveris; Hebr. circuibis o filia vaga? qui enim a via verbi DEI discedunt, ij juxta cordis sui cogita- tiones, & concupiscentias, tanquam per invia, & per solitudines, vagantur, semperque longius a regno DEI discedunt. Cum vero in viam redierint, dolentes ex animo super erroribus suis recipiuntur a DEO in gratiam. Agite pœnitentiam, inquit Propheta. De pœnitentia etiam interpretatus est Hieronymus, sed speculas aliter exposuit, ita nempe, ut ad reditum corporalem respexerit. Statue tibi speculas, pone tibi &c. Usquequo deliciis dissolveris filia vaga &c. Ubi nos, inquit, diximus usquequo deliciis dissolve- ris: Symmachus posuit; Usquequo demergeris in profundum? Utramque autem editionem ex toto posui, ut caput obscurissimum & Ecclesiæ continens Sacramenta, sive LXX. sive quis alius hunc Prophe- tam interpretatus est, aut ignoratum aut omissum ostenderem. Loquitur autem Ephraimo: Statue tibi speculas sive speculatores, qui tibi prænuncient, advenire tantam rerum omnium felicitatem. Quod- que sequitur amaritudines, quæ Hebraice dicuntur תמרורים pro quibus Symmachus interpretatus est, transmutationes, hoc indicat, quod flere debeat vel antiqua peccata, vel gaudii magnitudine, & tota ad Dominum mente converti, & ponere sive dirigere cor suum in viam, per quam profecta est: inde enim illam esse redituram. Porro etiamsi ita vertas cum Grotio Ebræa verba, statue tibi titulos, pone tibi altos cumulos, non tamen ideo ponendi tituli, & cu- muli, ut viam sciant Israelitæ, per quam ducti sint, ne- que ad Iudæos ea trahenda in Chaldæam transpor- tatos. De Israelitis in Assyria ea intelligit Brentius, quod ibi statuas & monumenta præsentiæ suæ post se relicturi sint. Cæterum si textus συνέχειαν respicia- mus, præferenda videtur illa ἐξήγησις, quæ pœni- tentiam hic inculcari vult: Etsi non negemus ista,

REVERTERE AD CIVITATES TUAS ISTAS, quia palam loquuntur de civitatibus Israe- liticis, ad quas reverti virgo Israel debeat, de reditu corporali accipienda esse. Quia miserationem pro- miserat Dominus Ephraimo, versic. 20. nunc ergo ut compos fiat gratiæ, ad pœnitentiam eandem ex- citat, & ad reditum ad civitates suas. Unde vi con- textus, hæc de Israelitis & Ephraim, hoc est, de de- cem tribubus, non de Judæis intelligenda. Quod re- cte animadversum est abHieronymo, qui ideo ver- sionem Vulgatam, (Græcam) hic notat: Verbum Hebraicum צִיֻּנִים vel in speculatores vel in speculas vertitur, ut Aquila & Symmachus interpretati sunt. Unde miror, quid sibi voluit Vulgata editio, ut pro צִיֻּנִים hoc est, pro speculatoribus, Sion poneret: tur- baretq; lectoris intelligentiam, quo putaret post E- phraim ad Sion & ad tribum Judæ repente DEI fa- ctum esse sermonem, cum perpetua oratio sit Ephraim, cui supra locutus est; Audiens audivi Ephraim: Et, filius honorabilis mihi Ephraim, sive puer de- licatus, cui & nunc loquitur: Statue tibi speculas, sive speculatores. Idem etiam observavit Brentius, ad verba MISERANS MISEREBOR. Redi- tum regni Hieroboam prophetatur utcunq;, ceptum post reditum regni Roboami duarum tribuum à Ba- bylone, sed sub CHRISTO impletum, ubi reliquiæ Israelis salvatæ sunt. Sed præ aliis sedulo hæc exe- quutus est B. Bugenhagius Noster, quod de regno Ephraim hic agatur, quod tum ex iis, quæ antece- dunt de Israele & Ephraimo, tum è sequentibus, & quidē etiam ex immediate subjuncto vaticinio de conceptione Messiæ probat, quam hic restringi ad ter- ram Israelis eximie ducet fol. 337. hanc reddens co- hærentiæ rationem: Revertere filia Israel, sive tu Ephraim, ut in terra tua, secundum promissiones DEI, accipias Messiam non ex viro & muliere na- tum, ut nascuntur nunc omnes homines, sed ex sola fæ- mina, secundum carnem, id est, ex virgine, Dominus enim creabit novam rem in terra. Fæmina circum- dabit virum. Pergit postea B. Bugenhagius hoc modo: Majores nostri ante nos intellexerunt de ma- tre Salvatoris prægnante, quæ est vera sententia hujus promissionis, sed illud quod dicitur, in terra vel super terram, non satis attenderunt. Generaliter enim in- tellexerunt super terram, id est, in mundo, cum ta- men Jeremias hic speciatim de terra Israel, sive Re- gno Ephraim, ut olim erat, loquatur, quæ res etiam singularem Prophetiam de terra addit, ubi CHRI- STUS sit concipiendus, & in utero matris gestan- dus, & postea educandus; ut frustra irriserint Ju- dæi Dominum nostrum JESUM CHRISTUM, vocantes eum Nazarenum & Galilæum, & calumni- antes, quod non posset ipse esse Messias, sive CHRI- STUS, qui ex Nazareth & ex Galilæa terra Israel venisset, quando CHRISTUS promissus erat ex terra Juda ex Bethlehem, secundum Prophetiam Micha. Et tu Bethlehem terra Juda &c. Non vi- derunt cæci Judæi, sicut ne hodie quidem vident hanc Prophetiam Jeremiæ de CHRISTO & matre ejus, de qua nunc dicam. Revertere, inquit, filia Israel, revertere ad hasce civitates tuas, id est, Vos ex re- gno Israel, sive Ephraim, qui estis abducti è terra vestra per Assyrium, qui agitis in desperatione, qua- si nunquam sitis recipiendi à DEO. Non enim habetis promissionem de reducendo, ut aliquando re- ducamini ad terram vestram, unde ejecit vos Dominus propter iniquitates vestras & contem- ptum verbi sui: Accipite nunc promissionem DEI. Revertimini ad vestras civitates in ter- ram Patrum vestrorum. Et licet desertricem patris & matris vocet, id est, meretricem & adulteram, ut agnoscat sua peccata, & credat se recipi non suo meri- to, sed sola gratia DEI, tamen simul etiam vocat fi- liam, & filiam Israel, ut bene adhuc speret de miseri- cordia DEI, maxime nondum periisse apud DEUM illas maximas promissiones de Messia libe- ratore, quem promiserat DEUS Judæis ex carne Abrahæ venturum in terram ipsorum. Nam p... Israelitæ jam in captivitate pœnitentiam agentes, me- tuebant DEUM illas egregias promissiones retraxis- se, quod tamen est impossibile. Nam illæ promissione... de CHRISTO, erant promissiones gratiæ DEI & gratuitæ, non promissiones Legis, ut ante quan- doque diximus. Quomodo, inquiunt, veniet ille li- berator & triumphator Messias Filius Abrahæ, fi- lius Davidis ad nos in terram nostram, & in civita- tes nostras, quando inde abjecti sumus, nec ulla spes est nobis illuc redeundi, sub servitute in capti- vitate pressis, & Samaritani illic omnia occupant? Quibus dicit Jeremias, Revertere ad hasce civitates tuas, quousque te avertes filia desertrix? Domi- nus præstabit tibi in terra, & in civitatibus tuis, quicquid promisit tibi, maxime de CHRISTO, Dominus enim creabit novam rem, in terra vestra Israel, sive Ephraim, in Regno, quod vocabatis Regnum Samariæ, in terra decem tribuum. Quæ res nova, & à Domino creanda dicitur, quia à con- dito mundo antehac non fuit vel facta est, erat ta- men promissa, & expectabatur à credentibus, sed creabitur à DEO nova in terra vestra, unde ejecti estis. Revertimini ergo in terram vestram, DEUS suscipiet vos ut dilectos filios, quemadmodum suscipit filium prodigum & desertorem, Luc. 15. Accurrite, properate vos desertores ad terram ve- stram. Satis habetis in terra vestra, etiamsi non re- cipiatis agros & possessiones paternas, ut illi qui sunt ex Regno Juda, cum Cyrus solverit, per DEI erga vos gratiam, captivitatem, ne contemnite donum DEI. Redite huc: Non perierunt promissiones DEI de CHRISTO, ut stulte metuitis. Accipietis in terra Israel, primum & præ aliis, maxima illa dona DEI vobis promissa, summas divitias, summas de- licias, summam potentiam, liberationem ab ira Dei, à peccatis vestris, à morte vestra, justitiam & vitam æternam, videlicet illum virum, Christum, CHRISTUM, qui vobis promissus est. Hæc B. Bu- genhagius, quæ apprime illustrant συνέχειαν an- tecedentium & consequentium in hoc contextu, & ad declarationem oraculi, quod proxime succedit, non parum faciunt.

Vers. eod.

QVIA CREAVIT DOMINVS NOVVM SVPER TERRAM). Rem novam facio. FOEMINA CIRCVMDABIT VIRVM.) Prover- biale. Viri solent ambire puellas: non puellæ viros. Sic populi erat Deum quærere: At Deus ultro ad populum ve. nit, ejusque amorem ambit. Ad Messiam mystice hæc aptat etiam Moses Hadarsan ad Gen. 41, 21.

Mira glossa, cujus sensum me penetrare non posse, fateor: Si viri ordinarie ambire solent puel- las, non puellæ viros, extraordinarium & singulare illud fuisset, populum per fœminam designatum ambire & circundare Deum, ceu virum. Ita Pro- pheta, juxta Grotianam ἐπίλυσιν, rem inverteret hoc loco, cum id pro mero & singulari venditat, quod Deus ambiat populum, & ad ipsum ultro ve- niat. Contrarium forte dicere voluit Grotius, ni- mirum hocce indigitari, quod populus iterum ad Deum revertatur, ejusq; amorem ambiat, non vero, quod Deus ultro ad populum veniat. Quæ Judæo- rum quorundam est sententia. Nam etsi de vulga- ri uxore amplexante, vel reducente maritum à quo discesserat, intelligant, idque impleri inceptum di- cant in exilio juxta Esai. 4, 1. explicant tamen id etiam de populo Israelitico ad Dominum revertente,

& pœnitentiam agente, qui divortium fecerat à Domino, ceu marito, & multis adulteris se prostituerat. Quo etiã abire videtur Jonathan ita παραφράζων: Quia ecce creavit Dominus novum in terra, Et populus domus Israel incumbet legi: Ubi non verbum verbo reddidit Paraphrastes, quasi per virum legem, per complecti incumbere intellexerit, sed sensum, ut alias sæpenumero, expressit, quem à Propheta indigitari credidit, nempe quod populus ad Dominum conversus legi incumbet, Dominoque adhærebit pio legis studio & obsequio. Septuaginta Seniores & Theodotionem pariter de Judaicæ Synagogæ spirituali adulterio aliquandiu à Deo separatæ salutari ad Deum conversione, qua præter spem excitanda, Deum virum suum & salutem suã quæsitura sit, oraculum hoc intellexisse è versionibus eorundem colligit Sanctius ad h. l. quum LXX. ita habeant: ὅτι ἔκτισε κύριος σωτηρίαν εἰς κ̅τ̅ φυτευσιν, ϰ’ ἐν σωτηρίᾳ σὐ περιελεύσονται ἄνθρωποι. Quod tamen de vocatione gentium per Apostolos potius intellectum voluit Theodoretus in h. l. ita scribens: Hoc loco Propheta aperte ostendit causam revocationis, cum per eam vaticinetur futuram novam plantationem; hanc enim mundo attulerant, qui ex ea nati sunt Apostoli, quod non obscure dicit sermo Propheticus (sc. juxta LXX. & Theodor. versionem) undiquaque venient homines in salute; hi enim permeantes omnes gentes per Dei cognitionem illis salutem attulerunt. Cui sensui etiam favent, qui è Christianis de conversione Synagogæ Judaicæ ad Deum, à quo aversa & alienata fuerat, accipiunt; quæ est Pontificiorum nonnullorum, Hieron. ab Oleastr. Can. 4. Procœm. in Gen. Johan. Pinedæ de Salom. l. 3. cap. 3. Francisc. Sanchez ad h. l. &c. interpretatio. Quibus gemini fere sunt, qui de reductione populi Israelitici ad communionem Ecclesiæ potissimum in Novo Testamento futura intelligunt, quod Ecclesia illa aversa, ad Christum, cui erat olim desponsata, conversa, eundem denuo amplexura sit, ceu virum suum. Quem sensum propugnant potissimum Pareus l. 2. contr. D. Hunnium p. 166. & Dn. D. Johan. Tarnovius in Exercit. Bibl. pag. 311. seqq. Qui de conversione quidem ad Deum, ejusque ambitu, vel complexu per fidem, sed gentiliũ sub Novo Testamento, ad Christum adducendorum, enarrant. Quomodo Theodoretus, LXX. Interpr. & Theodotionis versionibus insistens, divinam plantationem, & circuitionem Apostolorum in omnes gentes, salutis ipsarum causa, intelligit. Franciscus vero Junius, cum Tremellio, fontes Ebræos sequuti fœminam virum ambientem dicunt Ecclesiam Dei, quæ, Israele & Judæis propriis suis liberis propter aversionem eorum orbata, tanquam vidua & sterilis Virum ambitura, & filios filiasque aliunde sibi comparatura sit, in not. ad h. l. His si affinia dicere Grotius voluit, mentem suam aliter explicare debuit. Quicquid autem de glossa illa intricata Grotii sit, nos oraculum de Christo intelligimus, non sensu tantum mystico, sed proprio, & literali; quod nempe fœmina Maria, Virgo beata circumdatura sit, & utero conclusura non infantem aut puerum, sed virum, idq; sine virili opera, quod vere est mirabile. Quia Christus infans in utero matris virginis jam erat גבר vir & Heros. Ridet quidem superciliose hanc sententiam & expositionem Johannes Calvinus, quam agnoscit communem fere esse Christianis, utpote qui uno fere consensu hæc interpretati sint de Maria virgine, & hanc promit è pharetra sapientiæ suæ explicationem, redigent fœminæ viros in angustias, ita ut ipsos captivos teneant. Eadem Chorda oberrat Johan. Piscator Herborn. in scholiis ad hunc locum: Disz ist die Meynung:

Ihr Jüden, die ihr jetzund euch gegen die Chaldæer zu wehren gleich seyd, wie blöde und verzagte Wei- ber, werdet in der Widerkehr aus der Babyloni- schen Gefängnuß so wohlgemuth und kühn seyn, daß ihr die mächtigen Chaldæer auch möchtet feindlich umbgeben und überwältigen. Alibi ta- men Piscator, (in Commentar. nempe pag. 211.) ita παραφράζει h. l. Fæmina circumdabit virum, id est, Ecclesia Christiana, etsi coram mundo instar fœminæ debilis ac infirma erit, tamen audebit poten- tibus suis persecutoribus resistere per confessionem, & illos fide vincet 1. Joh. 5, 4.

Nostram autem ἔκθεσιν hæc probant argumen ta, quæ breviter in programmate ἑορτασικῷ in so- lemnia γενεθλιακα Servatoris nostri, nomine Re- ctoris & Senatus Academici Regiomontani, An. 1640. producta, hic repetenda, sed illustrata nonni- hil, censemus, quia exemplaria distracta sunt. (I.) Textus connexio, per particulam כי facta: quæ cau- sam refert, ob quam Israelitæ captivitati, quam to- lerabilem fecerat Regnum clementia, jam adsueti, domiciliis passim per Orientem fixis, ut & deliciis atq; divitiis ejus capti, excitentur, patriam, quam variis irruptionibus exposita viderant, desiderare. Non poterat autem quicquam Judæos ad hoc mo- vere, & animare, præterquã quod necessario & so- lum in Judæa, vi divinarum promissionum, præstan- dum esset; neque urgens magis iis proponi poterat argumentum, quam sola Messiæ in terra Israelis con- ceptio. Quod enim potius de corporali reversione, quam spirituali conversione vers. 21. agatur, statua- rum Mercurialium, signorumq; iter commonstran- tium, & viæ, qua itum est ex Judæa in Assyriam & civitatum, ad quas redire jubentur, & conversionis captivitatis eorum, uti Grotius ipse interpretatur, vel signorum memorabilium in Assyria relinquen- dorum, ut Brentius exponit, commemoratio per- suadet, quæ aliter, quam secundum literam acci- pienda esse, nulla cogit necessitas. (II.) Nova, quam commemorat Propheta, Creatio: Vox ברא significatu eminentiori creationem proprie dictam sive immediatam, sive mediatam importat. Nulla autem hoc loco circumdatio alia designari potest, ad cujus efficientiam creationis proprie dictæ opus sigillatim requiratur, præter hanc, qua Jehovah ex infinitudine suæ potentiæ in utero B. virginis hu- manam Christi naturam creavit, adeoque effecit, ut illa virum hunc circumdaret, seu conciperet. Tri- buitur equidem creationis nomen etiam conversio- ni, sed metaphorico sensu: quam admittere nulla cogit ratio; nec absolute, sed cum addito, ut Psal. 51, 12. creatio cordis mundi, vel alia quadam determi- natione adjecta, quæ hic non occurrit. (III.) No- vitatis designatio. Novum absolute positum, pro absolute novo accipiendũ, nisi rei natura, vel tex- tus συνέχεια novum tantum secundum quid indigi- tari doceant. Quod cum hic non fiat, urgemur o- mnino, ut novum illud novorum omnium novissimum, quod solum est sub sole novum, dicente Damasceno Lib. 3. O. F. c. I. intelligamus. Cætera enim omnia, quæ hic afferri possunt, non absolute, sed certo tantum modo nova sunt. Ideoq; τῷ ῥητῷ insi- stentes, illud circa controversiam magnum pietatis mysterium 1. Timoth. 3, 16. quod unum absolute no- vum, secundum Scripturam, dici meretur, virgina- lem complexum & conceptionem æterni filii Dei sin- gulariter mirabilem, & mirabiliter singularem de- signari concludimus. Quod Novum unice deside- rabant fideles Veter. Testamenti Luc. 2, 15. 38. cap. 10, 24. (IV.) Loci determinatio. Circumdatio hæc novissima in terra futura promittitur, & quidem ea, quæ montes Samron, Ephraim includit, in qua

Rama sita est vers. 5. 6. 15. Quæ terminus Israelis est vers. 17. Et in qua civitates Israelis vers. 22. Nulla itaque alia circumdatio, quam sola illa fami- neæ conceptionis denotabitur: quum reliquæ omnes etiam alibi fiant extra terram Israelis. Hanc de ter- ra conceptionis Messiæ observationem B. Bugen- hagio nostro inprimis debemus, qui in Commenta- rio suo illam tradidit fol. 342. Diximus hic non significari in terra, vel super terram, generaliter in mundo, quemadmodum interpretes ante nos fere omnes intellexerunt, sed specialiter tantum, super terram, vel in terra, videlicet in terra Ephraim, id est, decem tribuum, quarum terra post Salomonem dicta fuit Regnum Israel, Regnum Joseph, Regnum Ephraim, Regnum Samariæ, ut supra satis dictum est. Nam ad illas decem tribus hoc loco loquitur Je- remias, quæ jamdudum per Assyriam erant abductæ & abjectæ è terra sua, dicens : Rursum ædificabis vineas in montibus Samariæ. Quia erit tempus, quando custodes in montanis Ephraim clamabunt: Surgite ascendamus ad Zion, ad Dominum Deum nostrum.
