Sum enim Pater Israelis; & Ephraim est primogenitus meus: Item, vere audivi lamen- tationem Ephraim &c. Nonne Ephraim est pre- tiosus mihi filius, & puer desiderabilis ? Revertere filia Israel, revertere ad hasce civitates tuas. Quo- usque te avertes filia desertrix ? DOMINUS ENIM creabit novam rem in terra. Fœmina cir- cumdabit Virum: videlicet illum, qui promissus est, contritorem capitis serpentis, illud semen mulie- ris, illud semen Abrahæ, in quo benedicentur o- mnes cognationes terræ. Nam ceciderunt promif- siones Dei de Christo, propter peccata tua, ut tu stulte metuis, sed accipies Virum promissum in ter- ra tua, id est, in terra decem tribuum, priusquã ve- niat ipse in terram duarum tribuum, sive in terram Juda. Promissus quidem est in Prophetis, quod ex Domo & familia, sive cognatione Davidis orietur Rex æternus, & in Micha Propheta, quod nascetur in Bethlehem, & veniet ad templum sanctum suum, Do- ctor in Zion sive Jerusalem : Et Tu turris Eder, in- quit, quæ es arx filiæ Zion, usque ad te veniet sua Rosa aurea, prior Magistratus, Regnum filiæ Jeru- salem : & quod Evangelium & regnum Christi e- gredietur ex Jerusalem, & dilatabitur per totum mundum, in omnes gentes, de Zion, inquit, exibit lex, & verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Et ipse judi- cabit inter populos multos, & arguet gentes multas in regionibus longinquis, &c. Sed tamen, ut promit- tit hic Dominus per Jeremiam, in terra Israel, sive Ephraim, id est, decem tribuum, quæ erant abjectæ in Assyrios, & civitates Medorum, ille vir Deus & ho- mo, contritor capitis serpentis, benedictio omnium gentium, concipietur in utero materno, non ex viri semine, sed ex nova operatione & creatione Dei, quæ Deus creabit novam rem in terra, in terra Ephraim, non in terra Juda, neq; alibi in mundo. Revertere, inquit, ô filia Israel, revertere ad hasce civitates, quousque te avertes Filia desertrix ? Accipies in terra tua, quam promisit tibi Deus, salutem æter- nam. DOMINUS ENIM CREABIT NO- VAM REM IN TERRA, videlicet tua, FOE- MINA CIRCUMDABIT VIRUM. Conci- pietur, inquam, & gestabitur in utero matris in ter- ra Israel, donec virgo mater eum pariat in Bethle- hem in terra Juda, secundum Prophetiam Michæ, ducem & Rectorem totius Israelis. Unde porro notat B. Bugenhagius de complemento Prophetiæ fol. 345. Quod Josephus, & Maria qui fuerint qui- dem de domo Davidis & stirpe Regia, tamen propter paupertatem nihil proprium habuerint in Bethlehem civitate & patria David, & coacti sint habitare in aliena terra, videlicet in Galilæa, quæ pertinebat ad terram Ephraim, sive decem tribuum, ut Ieremiæ hæc Prophetia impleretur: Novam rem creabit Dominus in terra tua, ò Ephraim. Fœmina illic circumdabit virum, quem tamen ibi non pariet, sed in terra Iudæ in Bethlehem, ut prædixit Micha.

(V.) Ambientis denominatio, quæ נְקֵבָה dicitur. Ea autem vox nuspiam in sacris literis collective de multitudine aliqua, aut de toto sexu fœmineo dici- tur, semper individuum singulare vel vagum, vel de- terminatum notat sexus fœminei, quod locorum in- ductio apertissime docet, ut mirum sit, hoc negari. Nec vero præcise fœminam mari adjunctam ceu al- terum generationis principium, in quo aliquid gi- gnitur, infert; sed in genere fœminam, quia distin- guitur à mare per naturam, sive subordinetur mari ad generationem, sive non, designat. Neq; sane in- nuitur illa subordinatio in locis iis, ubi vox illa oc- currit, imo interdum ne locum quidem habere potest, ut Lev. 12, 5. 7. Non ergo est, quod ambi- gamus, id Mariæ θεοτόκῳ ceu lectissimæ è sexu fœ- mineo Spiritus Sancti officinæ, adhæc ad conju- gium jam destinatæ, atque desponsatæ convenire. Imo si propriæ & scripturis usitatæ significationi insistendum, qua individuum singulare sexus fœ- minei notat, ne quidē alia dari poterit, quæ hic in- tendatur fœmina, præter Beatam illam virginem.

(VI.) Circumdationis notatio. Vox סָבַב in genere est complecti, item circumdare, & ambire, uti R. Nathan Mardoch. in Concordant. per הִקִּיף ambitum illum explicat: optimeq; congruit uteri- næ circumdationi: qua fœtus undiq; ab utero ma- terno ambitur, circumscribitur, & vitali fovetur complexu. Quanquam enim simile exemplum non occurrat in Scripturis, ubi de conceptione adhi- beatur, commode tamen generalis significatio ad speciem adhiberi potest; & exprimunt Rabbini, Chaldæi, Arabes, hac voce causam; ideoque con- servationi causali, qualis est infantis in utero, non male convenit, quin & vocem סוֹבֵא menstruum Chaldæi inde deducunt, & expressit interpres Arabs eam hoc loco per vivificabit, quod ad offi- cium uteri ζωτικὴν δύναμιν ἐνησης, dicente Basilio, pertinet. Sunt præterea non pauca in Scripturis ἅπαξ λεγόμενα : Denique conceptio hæc quoque μονότροπος & singularis eatenus innuitur. De complexatione vero, qua fœmina maritum, Ecclesia Deum ambit, non modo non occurrit uspiam in scripturis, sed nec hoc loco ita intelligendam esse vocem illam, ullo certo documento patet: Imo non esse intelligendam, facile liquet: quia si Do- minus creat hoc novum, quomodo de Judæis sponte ambientibus Dominum intelligendum id erit? & quum conversio neutiquam sit nostrarum virium, quomodo sponte sua ambire Judæi Dominum po- tuissent, qui potius suspirarunt: converte nos Do- mine & convertemur? Adde, quod ταυτολογικὴ fit illa ratio, revertere virgo Israel per pœnitentiam: quia fœmina circumdabit virum: id est, quia Israeli- tæ ambient Dominum; vel acturi sunt pœnitentiam, seque conversuri ad Dominum. Videatur Dn, D. Müllerus in Judaismo cap. 19. p. 661.

(VII.) Circumdati denominatio. Vocatur is גֶּבֶר, quod nomen Deo convenire dubium non est. Deut. 10, 17. Ier. 32, 28. ubi גִּבּוֹר ἰχυρὸς & Ier. 20, 11 ubi μαχητὴς vocatur, idque de Deo hoc loco intel- ligunt potiores Interpp. & quidem ut Ecclesiæ spon- so, & marito, adeoque de Christo, qui sponsus est Ec- clesiæ: Matth. 9, 15. Ioh. 3, 29. 2. Cor. 11, 2. Ephes. 5 23. &c. Qui præterea גִּבּוֹר vocatur, ceu proprio no- mine in Prophetica nomenclatura Efa. 9, 6. ut & Psal. 45, 4. Imo hac ipsa voce גֶּבֶר indigitatur Zach

13, 7. Confer. Matth. 27, 31. Marc. 14, 27. Frustra es, si dicas, Christo in utero materno nomen גֶּבֶר haud congruere: Nam & de infantulo recens nato adhibetur Iob. 3, 2. ut & ab Onkelo Gen. 4, 1. & ab Esaia recens nato Jesulo tribuitur cap. 9, 6. Adde quod nomen istud famosiori significatu Heroem notans, peculiariter hic adhibeatur & cum delectu, de conceptione Messiæ: quod ipse in utero matris jam fuerit Heros, divina potentia & virtute, 8' אֶל מֵ֫טְרוֹן instructus, quod de nullo infantulo in utero con- cluso dici potest. Ideo Bugenhagius hæc verba tali illustravit paraphrasi; Hunc Heroa fortissimum, virum potentem, atq; adeo verum omnipotentem, ut- pote Deum & hominem accipietis vos Israelitæ pri- mum in terra vestra, creante DEO, & faciente no- vam hanc rem in terra vestra, quod fœmina cir- cumdabit virum, id est, mulier gestabit in utero il- lum fortem & omnipotentem Heroa Messiam, quem à Deo promissum jamdudum expectatis. De quo etiam monuit Hieronymus; novam rem crea- bit Dominus super terram. Absq; viri semine, absq; ullo coitu, atq; conceptu, fæmina circumdabit vi- rum gremio uteri sui, qui juxta incrementa quidem ætatis per vagitus & infantium proficere videbitur sapientia & ætate, sed perfectus vir in ventre fæmi- neo solitis mensibus continebitur.

(VIII.) Contextus ratio. Qui totus occupa- tur in beneficiis incarnatione Christi partis, conci- liatione cum Deo, & benedictionibus è fœdere Dei oriundis, quibus novum istud à Domino creandum inspergit Propheta, ut ad fontem, & fundamentum morte suo revocet. Confer Ier. 23, 5. cap. 33, 15. Pro- lixius textus cohærentiam exposuit Dn. D. Mulle- rus in Judaismo part. 1. cap. 19. Quod Propheta hoc & præcedenti capite Ecclesiam soletur per ad- ventum Messiæ, quem Davidem vocat cap. 30, 9. & populum ideo ad gaudium excitet cap. 31, 7. 13. uti Prophetæ solent, cum adventum Messiæ annun- ciant Esa. 9. v. 3. Zach. 9, 9. & beneficia Messiæ ad- ducat, salutem nostram etiam, benedictionem v. 24. lassorum recreationem v. 25. peccatorum remissionem v. 34. Quem nexum etiam indicat Hieronymus; Respice quod dicturus sum, & unde tibi tanta beati- tudo expectanda sit, diligenter attende: Audi quod nunquam ante cognoveras: Novam rem creavit Dominus &c.

(IX.) Ploratus Rachelis commemoratio v. 15. qui ad infanticidium Herodis recens nati Christi tempore refertur Matth. 2, 18. Ea proinde cir- cumdatio intelligitur, quæ cum clade Bethlehe- mitica connexa.

(X.) Nazareth. tripudium, & mutua invi- tatio v. 6. ubi si נוֹצְרִים ut proprium patronymi- cum accipiatur, reliquiæ Israel in Nazareth læ- tati innuuntur, seque invitare ad celebrandum Do- minum propter Jesum Nazarenum conterraneum suum Matth. 2, 23. cui egregie respondet promis- sio novi hujus in terra Israelis creandi, conceptio- nis nempe Messiæ, ad quam divinitus delecta fuit Nazareth Luc. 1, 26. videntur.

(XI.) Loci conceptionis Prophetica definitio. Nam cum tam accurate Spiritus Dei locum nativi- tatis Messiæ Mich. 5, 2. & educationis Matth. 2, 23. & ministerii, ac prædicationis Hagg. 2, 8. Mal. 3, 1. & Passionis Zach. 12, 11. notarit: neque verisimile sit locum conceptionis haud definivisse, ac prænun- ciaffe, diligenter inquisiverunt Ecclesiastici Scri- ptores, & tandem deprehenderunt hunc locum, ut observat Dn. Chemnitius harm. Evang. cap. 4. col. 37. & è B. Pomerani pia ἐρευνήσει constitit.

(XII.) Interpretum meliorum confessio, qui pleriq; hanc de fœminea Christi complexione, & conceptione approbant ἐξήγησιν. E Christiani eandem propugnant tum antiquiores Doctores, Ju- stinus in Dial. cum Triphon. Cyprianus Serm. de Nat. Christi. Augustinus Serm. 9. de tempore de Nativitate Domini. Hieronymus Comment. in h. l. Tom. 4. Rabanus item, Strabus in glossa ordin. nec non Bernhard. hom. 2. super missus est, & alii; Tum recentiores è Pontificiis, Lyranus, Galatinus, aliiq́; E Calvinianis, Oecolampadius, Zvvinglius, Pelica- nus, Bullingerus &c. in comment, in h. l. E nostri plerique; omnes, etiam B. Lutherus. Quamvis prior versione sua inclinavit in eam sententiam, quæ Cal- vino probata est, sic locum reddendo, (ut Biblia Anno 32. Wittebergæ edita testantur) Wie lang wilt du dich wegkehren du Tochter, die ich wieder bringen wil? daß der HErr wieder ein Neues im Land erschaffen, daß die sich vorhin wie Weiber ge- stellt haben, sollen Männer seyn; Postea tamen loco examinato & animadversis textus Prophetici cir- cumstantiis priorem versionem in accurata trans- lationis recognitione expunxit, & eam, quam ho- die habent exemplaria, substituit: Wie lang wilt du in der irre gehen, du abtrünnige Tochter? Denn der HErr wird ein Neues im Land erschaffen, das Weib wird den Mann umbgeben? Sententiam in glossa marginali adversus Judæos confirmavit par- tim à circumdationis hujus novitate, partim à contex- tus serie, qui totus agat de Novo Testamento: jubeat- quepropter hoc novũ, quod Dominus creaturus erat in terra, quo fœmina (virgo incorrupta) nova miraǵ; mater est, adeoque propter Messiam virginis filium Mosen sepelire, seque in viam Domini convertere. Quia hac matre virgine concipiente Moses sepeli- ri, & Israël ad Christum converti debuit. Luc. 1, 16. 17. 76. Novumque Testamentum initium sumsit. Etsi autem alium etiam sensum ibi tradat Megalan- der, significationem nempe vel figuram Apostoli Rom. 7, 6. quod nos à lege prius conclusi, nunc legem veluti complectamur, quæ jam non supra, sed infra nos: eum tamen solum tanquam accommodationem ali- quam allegoricam insinuat: Priorem vero ceu pro- priam & literalem suscipit, ac probat. Quem etiam libro de Schemhamphorasch Tom. 8. Jen. Germ. fol. 133. Anno 1543. è Consensu Christiani orbis, & verborũ ἐμφάσε confirmavit. Das hat man in der gantzen Christenheit gelesen, und verstanden võ Christo, und der Jungfrauen Maria, seiner Mut- ter, wie recht und billich ist. Es soll ein Neues seyn, spricht er, das nicht gewest ist zuvor auff Erden, Es sind von Anfang Kinder geborẽ, Regiment gewest, böse uñ gute Leute gelebet, sich gebessert, und verbö- sert, wie es noch jetzt gehet, uñ biß an der Welt Ende gehen wird. Aber hier sol das neue Wunder gesche- hen, das vor nie geschehen ist, nemlich eine Nekefa, ein Weib, die nicht ein Mann ist, sol einen Mann umbgebẽ, das ist: Maria sol Gottes Sohn empfa- hen, und gebehren. Denn das muß seyn, so unser Glaube recht seyn sol, daß Christus unser HErr in dem Augenblick, da Maria dem Engel Gabriel ihr Vollwort gab, und sprach: Mir geschehe nach dei- nem Wort, ist zugleich GOtt und vollkommener Mensch gewest, in einer Person, wie das die lieben Vätter im Concilio zu Epheso wider den Nestori- um erhalten haben. Denn wo das nicht seyn solte, so wäre sie nicht Theotocos, Gottes Mutter zu nen- nen, noch Christus ihr Sohn zu nennen. Addimus hisce testimonium Judæorum antiquiorum. R. Mo- ses Hadarschan in Gen. 41. ita habet: & consolatus est eum in virgine, sicut dictum est Jer. 31, 21. &c. Re- vertere virgo Israel, revertere ad civitates tuas istas, usque quo infanies filia apostatrix: Creavit enim Deus novitatem in terra, fœmina circumdabit vi- rum. R. Huna in nomine R. Idi & R. Josua Ben Levi dixerunt, quod iste est Rex Messias, de quo dictum est Psal. 2, 7. Ego hodie genui te. Habemus ergo con- sensum R. Idi, Rabi Josua ben Levi, R. Hune, & R. Mosis Hadarschan, quibus etiam R. Hakkadosch accedit in Gali Razia. Videatur Pugio fidei Rai- mund. Martin. part. 3. Distinct. 3. cap. 19. Petrus Galatin. lib. 7. de arcan. Cathol. Veritatis cap. 14. col. 414. Recentioribus Judæis, quorum sensum videtur exprimere voluisse Grotius, os oppilavit B. Lutherus loco citato. Wil auch wol ihre Kunst im Spruch Jeremia 31. noch anzeigen, da sie sage, Ein Weib wird einen Mann umbgeben, solle heis- sen so viel, das Volck Israel ist das Weib, GOtt der Mann: Nun ist Israel eine Hure gewest in der Abgötterey, darnach hat sie sich bekehret un bereu- et, damit den Mann, das ist, GOtt wieder umbge- ben und versühnet. Wen nun gleich die Worte das könten geben, als nicht seyn kan, wie kan solches ein Neues auff Erden geschaffst heissen? Ist das Volck Israel niemal eine solche Hure gewest, und wieder bekehret worden? Da frage das Buch der Richter um. Hie wils doch dahin komen, daß, was ein Ra- bin neu heisset, das ist neu, was er alt heisset, das ist alt, wie droben die Regul gibt von der lincken und rechten Hand. Adjecit etiam aliam glossam Judæo- rum valde ineptam, quam, ut ductorum Grotii cœ- citatem agnoscere liceat, subjungimus. Uber das ist noch viel höher seiner Kunst, an diesem Ort, sprechen sie, das Weib sey die Hure Israel zu verstehen, wen sie aber Hochzeit haben, führen sie die Braut drey- mal umb den Bräutigã, auff daß sie diese Spruch Jeremia gnug thun, Ein Weib umbgibt den Mann, Hie muß Nekesa, das Weib, eine Jungfrau heissen, dort eine Hure. Warumb? Darumb, daß die Rabinen nicht fehlen können, wenn sie sagen, ei- ne Hure ist eine Jungfrau, und eine Jungfrau eine Hure, nach der Regul: Daß die lincke Hand recht ist, wenn sie ein Rabi recht heisset. Und muß auch vor nie solche neue Dinge geschehen seyn, wenn ein Weib oder Braut umb den Man dreymal gefüh- ret wird, denn Jeremias spricht: Es soll ein Neues seyn auff Erden vom HErrn geschaffen; Aber hie hat ein Rabin der Sachen bald geholffe, un gesagt, was er neu heisse, das ist neu, was er aber alt heisse, das ist alt, œc. Suma, die verzweiffelten Teuffels- Lügenmäuler meynen nicht anders, denn die Heili- ge Schrifft sey ihr eigen, wie ein Papier, darauß sie Männlein, Vögelein, Häuslein, Katzenstülein, schnitzen möchten, wie sie wollen, und was sie sage, das sollen beyde, ihre Jüden, und wir Christen, zu recht annehmen. Hos ergo tam præclaros Doctores & ductores sequi placuit Grotio. Neq; est, quod has duas diversas sententias conjungi posse, quis existi- met. Quod commentum in Pareo, etsi idem etiam ad Oecolampadii, Zvvinglii, Pelicani & Bullingeri con- sensum provocet, ita refutavit B. Hunnius Anti-Pa- reo pag. 229. Ego vero, mi Paree, me & spectatorem præbebo sedulum & auditorem attentum, quibus ar- tibus sub unam interpretationem cogere, seu ut tu lo- queris, conjungere velis sententiam tuam, quam Calvi- nus Judæis adscribit: Et Christianorum, qui dictum Jeremiæ de conceptione virginis interpretantur. De iis, qui copiam orationis affectant, cum ne se- mel quidem rem possint apte explicare, scribit alicubi Erasmus Roterodamus, ineptos illos Sy- nonyma quædam congerere adeo inter se diffi- dentia, ut ipsi mirentur, quo pacto convenirent. Idem affirmare liceat de Pareo sententias connectente prorsus inconnexiles, atque adeo inter se dissidentes, ut mirentur ipsæ, cujus artificis opera in unum conve- nerint. Si conjungendæ sunt duæ istæ sententiæ, tum aut sub analogia typi, & antitypi erunt conjungendæ aut connectendæ simpliciter. Neutro modo patiun- tur se copulari. Priori modo se tentes, hæc prodibit absurda Paraphrasis : Quemadmodum Ecclesia Judaica, quæ tanquam desertrix, & adultera Domi- num deseruerat, novo quasi miraculo eundem am- plexabitur, & vera resipiscentia constanter ei adhæ- rebit; Sic aliquando fœmina virgo in virginali ute, ro concipiet Messiam Dominum. Pulchre, lepide, laute, nihil supra. Si cui hæc compositio minus arri- det, & tenetur altera, quid ea dici poterit inconve- nientius ? Ad hunc enim scopulum prodigiosissimæ absurditatis conciliator allidat, necesse est, ut vox FOEMINÆ simul & semel adulteram illam Dei desertricem, Ecclesiam Iudaicam sensu uno, & dein- de sanctissimam Dei genitricem significet sensu altero: tum verbum circumdare simul notet conversionem sensu Parei, & deinde filiiDei conceptionem ex vir- gine, sensu nostro: Viri vox simul & semel & Deum simpliciter, hoc est,totam Trinitatem, & deinde (in altera sententia) non totam Trinitatem, sed solum filium designet. Quæ ratio interpretandi Scripturas sit ne vel audita saltem in Ecclesia, (non dicam rece- pta aut frequentata :) liberrimum esto judicium, non modo penes amicos, sed etiam inimicos. Hæc Beatus Hunnius, senior, quæ integra ad- scribere visum fuit,ut quam absurde ab illis, qui geminum sensum dictis Scripturæ affricare solent, inconnectiles sententiæ connectantur, hoc etiam exemplo, & Theologi istius τῶν μακαρίτων ante- cessoris nostri judicio innotescat. Neq; credo Calvini sententiam facile exoscu- laturum quemquam,qui quomodo eandē delum- barit B. Hunnius, viderit. Utitur, inquit Calvinus, singulari numero Propheta,quasi dicat : fœmina una præstabit multis viris, hoc est, singuli Judæi præsta- bunt singulis Chaldæis, ita Judæi superiores erunt, quamvis magnum & terribile sit robur hostium.Sic enim transformare necessum habuit Calvinus pri- mum singulare in plurale, ut pro fœmina substituerit fœmine, viros in angustias redigent. Deinde nomen alterum viri etiam in plurale convertere. Tertio fœ- minæ vocem rursus de una accipere. Quia dicit : hunc esse sensum, fœmina una præstabit multis veris.Por- ro hæc ita torquere,quod per fœminas, Judæi, per vi- ros Chald ei intelligendi; & deinceps hæc ita conne- ctenda sunt : Quod Judæi, qui respectu Chaldæo- rum pro fœminis haberi queant,ad angustias reda- cturi sint Chaldæos : unde non immerito quæsivit Hunnius noster, quis Calvino hanc licentiam dede- rit per Metamorphoses, quæ pene Ovidianas illas su- peret, quidvis fingendi ex quolibet, & fœminam in fœminas, fœminas in Judæos transformandi, ex viro viros, nempe Chaldæos. Et anne hoc novum sit in ter- ra annon sæpe Judæi parva manu innumerabiles co- pias potentissimorum hostium profligarint. Denique qui annales bistoriarum testentur, quod Judæi capti- vi vel in ipsa victoria Persarum contra Babylonios, vel post devictos jam à Cyro Chaldæos sese illis armata manu opposuerint, aut vires suas cum Persis ac Me- dis in debellandis Babyloniis conjunxerint saltem,tan- tum abest, ut hosce ipsi peculiari conflictu superarint, & in suam captivitatem redegerint. Sed hæc de glossemate etiam Calvini. B. Joh. Tarnovii hic Cal- vini sententiæ adhærentis exceptiones & argu- menta discussit Dn. Theodorus Hacksp. ad h. l. Lu- dovici Alcafaris Papistæ nova expositio digna non est,quæ adducatur,nedum quæ sub examen revo- cetur : Quia ridicula est. Censet nempe Eucharistiæ mysterium significari,quæ corpus Christi continet. Quæ quomodo vel verbis,vel contextui quadret, nemo nisi Jesuitico acumine excellens, perspiciet.

## 31:23
MAY THE LORD BLESS YOU BEAUTY OF JUSTICE) The dwelling place of justice: that is, the seat of religion. Jerusalem.

MOUNTAIN OF HOLINESS) The Temple.

Latin:

BENEDICAT TIBI DOMINVS PULCHRI- TVDO JVSTITIÆ) Habitaculum justitiæ: id est, reli- gionis sedes. Hierosolyma.

MONS SANCTITATIS) Templum.

## 31:24
Ver. 24.

AND THOSE DRIVING THE FLOCK) In Hebrew: and those who go with the flock, that is, Shepherds.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET MINANTES GREGEM) In Hebræo: & qui eunt cum grege, id est, Pastores.

## 31:25
Ver. 25.

I HAVE INEBRIATED THE WEARY SOUL) See above 14. but these are to be translated by the future.

This blessing is not to be restricted to the Jews alone, let alone to the temporal rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple and the fatness of the sacrifices, by which the priests were to be fattened. The blessing extends itself to the whole Church, and is to be understood primarily in a spiritual sense. Then it treats of the house of Israel equally as of the house of Judah v. 26. and following. Even if therefore Judea is peculiarly raised up, because the seat of the Church was there, and they themselves were to be led into captivity and were in need of comfort, this word will still be said in the land of Judah and its cities, when I shall turn back their captivity: yet the blessing made to the land of Judah and its cities is not terminated within the boundaries of Judea, but is to be explained in such a way that it can befit the whole Church; but it is not to be determined to a material temple, or to the ceremonials proper to Jerusalem. For if he prophesies, as is held at the end of the chapter, how the holy temple and the holy city ought to be dilated into the four parts of the world, and so be sanctified to the Lord, that it may not be violated or laid waste forever: and whereas previously Jerusalem was called holy, and the temple and the worship of God, but not likewise other cities in Judah, now Jeremiah predicts that the whole land of Judah and its cities ought to be called the habitation of justice, and the holy mount, not only Jerusalem, not only the temple, as Grotius perverts it, taking these things concerning Jerusalem and the temple. Wherefore Bugenhagen, on page 351, rightly explains these things concerning the kingdom of Christ. Previously indeed Jerusalem was called the holy city on account of the temple and the worship of God, but not other cities in Judah, but here it is predicted that the whole land of Judah and its cities shall be called and proclaimed: The habitation of justice and the holy mount. What is that land of Judah with its cities, if not the kingdom of Judah, which was promised to David in Christ as eternal? To which kingdom belong the Jews, Israelites, Samaritans, and the nations throughout the whole world, just as it was predicted in Isaiah 49. There shall be spoken or proclaimed the joyful proclamation and the good invocation of the Gospel against the sad and horrendous proclamation and condemnation of the law, namely this: The LORD bless thee: Formerly indeed it was also proclaimed to that people, The Lord bless thee, but that blessing of the Lord was never commanded to be proclaimed without Christ, because the blessing of God was promised to them in Christ alone against the curse of the law, by which all men are condemned, nor was it promised to them alone, but also to all nations, Romans 3. Is he the God of the Jews only, and not also of the Gentiles? For thus God promised to Abraham: In thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. This Christ, the blessing of all the peoples of the earth, whom a woman encompassed, Jeremiah says here is to be exhibited in the land of Judah through blessings, that is, the preaching of the Gospel and mighty works, so that he may come and dilate his kingdom to the whole land of the Jews, and to the Samaritans, and to all nations throughout the whole world, Acts 1. You shall be witnesses to me, that is, preachers of the Gospel concerning me, not only in Jerusalem, but also in all Judea and Samaria, and even to the ends of the earth. For thus in Acts 3 the Apostles explain to the Jews, and declare the promise made to Abraham already exhibited, in thy seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed. To you, they say, God first, when he had raised up his son Jesus, sent him blessing you, that every one of you may turn himself from his iniquities. Therefore the Lord shall bless thee, it shall be heard in the land of Judah, and in its cities, after a woman shall compass a man, that is, the Lord God himself shall be present there, right-hand, happy, and blessings in that omnipotent Man, the crusher of the serpent's head, and the blessing of all the families of the earth, there then you shall hear and see what have long since been promised to you in the Messiah. Blessed are the eyes which see what you see, and blessed are the ears which hear what you hear. Many Kings and Prophets and righteous men have desired to hear what you hear and see, and have not heard, nor seen. Here is heard and seen Christ the blessing of all the families of the earth, against the curse of the law, and the damnation of all men. They shall be blessed through Christ, that is, the Gospel of Christ shall be preached to them, and believers shall be delivered through Christ from their curse, sin, and death, and shall become children of God, gifted with righteousness, a good conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, the fruits of righteousness, and eternal life. This is the first, highest, proper, and eternal blessing in Christ, of which Eph. 1 thus it is said: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, just as he chose us in Christ, before the foundation of the world, etc. Then to us believers, blessed through Christ with an eternal blessing, he has also promised a temporal blessing, daily bread, that is, sustenance in this mortal life, saying: Seek first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added. And in Paul: Godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come. Which Paul explains 1 Cor. 10. That all things are ours, which are the Lord's, who through faith are one with the Lord Christ; he says that Christ is that Lord, whose is the earth and the fullness thereof. For he is the Son of God, Heir of all the Father's goods. Which furthermore the blessed Bugenhagius has thus executed on page 354. But because the kingdom of heaven or the holy and righteous Church of Christ began on the day of Pentecost in the Kingdom of Judah, which was David's, i.e., in Zion and Jerusalem, it is called in the Prophets Zion and Jerusalem, and the eternal Kingdom of Judah, and Zion and Jerusalem became spiritual and heavenly, after that earthly one perished, so that there did not remain there a stone upon a stone. To Paul, Jerusalem, which is above, is our mother; that the Jews may see where they should look for the promises of God, namely that that promised eternal kingdom of David cannot be an earthly kingdom, but shall be the kingdom of heaven, as the Prophets predicted, who all (as Peter says) bear witness to Christ, that through his name whoever believes in him receives remission of sins, i.e., all, whether Jews or Gentiles in the Kingdom of Christ, have remission of sins, or are justified through Christ alone. Ps. 2 God says: But I have set my King upon Zion, my holy hill, I will declare the decree, etc. Is. 60. there are many promises and strong consolations of God, promised to the Church of Christ itself, in which also this is said to the Church or kingdom of Christ, in thy people all shall be righteous, and they shall possess the land forever, as they who are the branch of my planting, and the work of my hands to be glorified. From the least there shall be a thousand, and from a small people a mighty one. There God calls the kingdom of Christ Jerusalem, the city of the Lord, the Zion of the holy one of Israel, certainly the holy hill, the habitation of righteousness, as here Jeremiah, that all who shall be in that kingdom shall be holy and righteous, by the imputation of God through the remission of sins in Christ. The kingdom of Christ is called on earth the holy Hill, and the habitation of righteousness because of the citizens and inhabitants, who all are holy and righteous. Jerusalem was not holy because of Annas and Caiaphas who were never the Church of God, just as neither were the impious Kings, Princes, Priests, and Prophets of old: But as from Adam only the believers were the people of God, so now only the believers are the people of God and the Kingdom of God. For Christ did not come to occupy the cities of Judah and Israel, houses and fields, or gold and silver, and the power of the Gentiles, as the foolish Jews dream for themselves, without the word of God, but to possess men, just as he himself says: The son of man shall come to seek and to save that which was lost. Five thousand men (in which number are not women and children) Christ first received in Jerusalem, the sacred beginnings of his kingdom, as the law of Acts 4, and then daily the number and multitude of believers was increased. These were made first the Church of Christ, the people of God and the kingdom of heaven, meanwhile Annas, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and other High Priests and Priests, the adversaries of Christ, were kept in that earthly Jerusalem for destruction, as chaff for the fire, and in vain they boasted blaspheming: We are the heads of the Church and of the people of Israel. You ought to hear us, and not that crucified Galilean. This multitude of the people of the Saints was dispersed after the stoning of Stephen to the remaining Jews and Samaritans, and to the Gentiles also, as you see in the acts of the Apostles, where they preached the Gospel of Christ, and Jerusalem was dilated into the whole world, the holy Hill and habitation of righteousness. That which Zechariah had predicted c. 2. Jerusalem shall be inhabited without a wall, because of the great multitude of men, i.e., of Jews, and of cattle, i.e., of Gentiles, which shall be in it, Behold I, says the Lord, will be a wall of fire round about it, and I will be in it, etc. I will show myself in the midst of it with glory, Ps. 87. It is founded upon the holy mountains. The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the tabernacles of Jacob. Glorious things are spoken of thee, O City of God. I will make Rahab, i.e., the Egyptians and Babylonians, to be spoken of, that they may know me; behold the Philistines and the Tyrians with the Ethiopians are born there; it shall be said in Zion that everyone is born in her, and that the Most High himself establishes her, etc. And Isa. 60. Arise, shine, for thy light is come, etc. And the Gentiles shall walk in thy light, and the Gentiles in the brightness that rises upon thee; lift up thine eyes, and look round about; all these are gathered together and come to thee, etc. All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall serve thee; they shall be offered upon my well-pleasing altar (which is Christ, Heb. 13). For I will beautify the gift of my glory; who are these, etc. Thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night. That the power of the Gentiles may be brought unto thee, and their kings may be led to thee. For whatever nations or kingdoms will not serve thee shall perish, and those nations shall be utterly wasted, etc. And I will make thy overseers teach, and thy presidents righteousness. Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, nor wasting or destruction within thy borders, but thy walls shall be called salvation, and thy gates praise. The sun shall no more shine upon thee by day, and the brightness of the moon shall not shine upon thee (hear, O Jews, that the Kingdom of Jerusalem is not to be an earthly one), but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down, nor shall thy moon withdraw its light, for the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall have an end, etc. And Isa. 49. It is a small thing that thou shouldst be my servant, etc. In an acceptable time I have heard thee, etc. But Zion says: The Lord has forsaken me, the Lord has forgotten me, etc. Lift up thine eyes round about, etc. You have the holy mountain, the habitation of righteousness, the eternal Kingdom of David, of which they acclaimed Christ on the day

Of Palms; Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, King of Israel, Blessed is that which comes, the Kingdom of our father David, in which kingdom is preached the blessing of all the peoples of the earth, that is, Christ, of whom God promised to Abraham, in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed, may the Lord bless you, he says, O habitation of justice, O holy mountain. And Judah with all its cities, that is, the whole kingdom of Judah promised to David, gathered from Jews and Gentiles to one King, and Shepherd David, i.e., Christ, the Son of David gathered, with all the cities, that is, Churches, shall dwell there in Jerusalem, in the holy mountain, and in the habitation of justice; as also in the Psalm, Lord, who shall dwell in your Tabernacle, or who shall rest in your holy mountain? And it does not answer: He who is circumcised is a Jew, and thus sacrifices. But, He who walks without blemish, and works justice, etc. And it is added, And the farmers, and those who change places with their flock, i.e., shepherds, shall also dwell there in Jerusalem, in the holy mountain, and in the habitation of justice. Tell me, O Jew, will you permit farmers and Shepherds and sheep and beasts of burden to dwell in the holy mountain, in the temple of the Lord? What advantage will there be for them in Jerusalem? How shall Judah dwell with all its cities in the holy mountain and in the habitation of justice? Therefore, by Farmers and Shepherds of the Flock he means the preachers of the Gospel, and the Doctors of the Churches, of whom God promised also above in ch. 22. Behold, I will gather the remnants of my flock from all the lands, whither I had cast them out, and I will bring them back to their folds, that they may grow and multiply. And I will raise up over them Shepherds, who shall feed them, so that they shall not fear any more, nor be terrified or visited, says the Lord. For Paul calls the Preachers farmers, 1 Corinthians 3. God indeed gave to the Jews after the Babylonian captivity fertility of fields and an abundance of sheep and cattle. Because he cares for his children even for bodily food. But here he sets forth the whole of Judah with all its cities, with farmers and shepherds who will dwell in the habitation of justice, i.e., in that kingdom where all are just forever, as Isaiah said, i.e., in the Kingdom of David Christ. FOR I WILL REFRESH. This is the reason why men willingly approach the Kingdom of Christ, that they may become a holy mountain and a habitation of justice. Therefore God says, I will be present in that Man, the crusher of the serpent's head, whom the woman surrounded in Israel, and brought forth in Bethlehem of Judah; For he shall be God and man; And I will refresh in Christ the weary souls, i.e., the penitent, and the anxious souls, namely concerning food, i.e., the needy and hungry sinners. I will satisfy in the Kingdom of Judah of David, i.e., in the Church of Christ, which began in Judah: Hear the man, the crusher of the serpent's head, saying this very thing: The poor were evangelized; Those who were invited were not worthy; Go therefore to the exits of the ways, and whomever you find, the weak, the blind, the lame, bring them in here; There is no need of a physician for those who are well, but for those who are ill. Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you, and you will find rest for your souls. Let the contemptuous Jews hear and see these things, whose the kingdom of heaven is, or of the Messiah, certainly not theirs who expect a Messiah through whom they may become rich in this world, and glorious, but theirs who desire to be healed and freed from sins and death according to the Gospel; The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent. In your seed, Abraham, shall all the families of the earth be blessed: I have preferred to set forth these words of the venerable Predecessor, the faithful assistant, the Great Man Luther, rather than my own, so fully, because they not only serve to explain this prophecy, but also kindle a torch for other similar ones. The Osiandrian [paraphrase] agrees excellently.

Paraphrase. But how well those who believe in the incarnate Son of God shall dwell, the Prophet indicates in the following words: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: They shall yet say this word in the land of Judah, and in its cities, when I shall have turned their captivity: Thus shall the Israelites, that is, the Christians, congratulate the nascent Church: may the Lord bless you, O beauty: In Hebrew, O habitation of justice, O holy mountain, in which is the temple of the living God (that is, may the Lord give you, O Church of Christ, increase, that you may be enlarged, and grow in the number of men, and in the gifts of the Holy Spirit. For you are like a most holy city, in which piety and justice flourish: in you the Lord God dwells presently, especially indeed with his goods and gifts) (For although the Church in these lands has its blemishes: yet it is just before God by the imputation of the justice of Christ. And it is regenerated and sanctified by the Holy Spirit) and Judah, the people of the kingdom of Judah, and all its cities together shall dwell in it: Nay, even farmers and shepherds, leading their flocks, that is, the Church of Christ shall be able to receive all, as many as shall wish to join themselves to it: and it shall be like a most ample city, which can embrace many cities and villages within itself. (This is the Catholic Church of Christ, in which there are not only many cities, but also many Principalities, indeed many kingdoms, and indeed in that universal Church there are also many spiritual farmers and shepherds of the Churches, to whom the agriculture of God is a care, 1 Cor. 3. And to whose faith the sheep to be fed are committed under one supreme shepherd Christ, 1. Peter 5.) Then blessed shall be the citizens of that Church (says Christ) Because I have inebriated: more correctly: I will inebriate (I will abundantly refresh) the weary soul, and every hungry soul: more correctly, the sorrowful, I have satisfied; More correctly, I will satisfy. Thus far Osiander.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

INEBRIAVI ANIMAM LASSAM) Vide supra 14. vertenda autem hæc per futurum.

Non restringenda hæc benedictio ad solos Ju- dæos, nedum ad temporalem Hierosolymæ, & templi reædificationem ac sacrificiorum pinguedinem, qui- bus exatiandi Sacerdotes. Benedictio porrigit sese ad totam Ecclesiam, & sensu spirituali imprimis in- telligenda est. Tum de domo Israel pariter, ac de domo Juda agitur v. 26. & seqq. Etsi ergo Judæa pe- culiariter erigatur, quia ibi sedes erat Ecclesiæ, ipsi- que in captivitatem abducendi solamine indige- bant, adhuc dicetur hoc verbum in terra Judæ & ci- vitatibus ejus, cum vertero captivitatem eorum: be- nedictio tamen terræ Judæ, & civitatibus ejus facta non intra pomœria Judææ terminatur, sed ita ex- plicanda est, ut toti Ecclesiæ convenire queat; Non autem ad materiale templum, aut ceremonialia Hie- rosolymæ propria determinanda. Siquidem vatici- netur, ut in fine capitis habetur, quomodo templum sanctum, & civitas sancta, in quatuor mundi partes dilatari debeat, & ita sanctificari Domino, ut non violetur aut vastetur in æternum: & quum antea Hierosolyma dicta sit sancta, & templum & cultus Dei, non item aliæ civitates in Juda, jam prædicit Jeremias, quod tota terra Judæ & civitates ejus vo- cari debeant habitatio justitiæ, & mons sanctus, non tantum Jerusalem, non solum templum, uti perver- tit Grotius de Hierosolymis & templo hæc acci- piens. Quapropter de regno Christi hæc recte ex- plicat Bugenhagius pag. 351. Antea quidem diceba- tur Jerusalem civitas sancta propter templum & cul- tum Dei, sed non aliæ civitates in Juda, hic autem prædicitur, quod tota terra Judæ, & civitates ejus vo- cabuntur & prædicabuntur: Habitatio justitiæ & Mons sanctus. Quæ est illa terra Juda cum civitati- bus suis, nisi regnum Juda, quod Davidi promis- sum est in Christo æternum? Ad quod regnum pertinent Judæi, Israëlitæ, Samaritæ & gentes per totum mundum, quemadmodum prædictum est Es. 49. Ibi dicetur sive prædicabitur læta prædicatio, & bona imprecatio Evangelii contra tristem & hor- rendam prædicationem & damnationem legis, vide- licet hæc: DOMINUS benedicat tibi: Olim qui- dem etiam est prædicatum illi populo, Dominus be- nedicat tibi, sed illa benedictio Domini nunquam jussa est prædicari sine Christo, quia promissa erat eis benedictio Dei in solo Christo contra maledictio- nem legis, qua damnati sunt omnes homines, nec eis solum erat promissa, sed etiam omnibus gentibus Rom. 3. An Judæorum tantum Deus est, & non e- tiam gentium? Sic enim promisit Deus Abrahæ: In semine tuo benedicentur cunctæ cognationes ter- ræ. Hunc Christum, benedictionem omnium populo- rum terræ, quem Virum fœmina circumdedit, dicit hic Jeremias exhibendam in terra Juda per benedi- ctiones, id est, Evangelii prædicationem & mirabilia facta, ut veniat, & dilatet regnum suum ad totam ter- ram Judæorum, & ad Samaritanos & ad omnes gen- tes per totum mundum, Actor. 1. Eritis mihi testes, id est, prædicatores Evangelii de me, non solum Hie- rosolymis, verum etiam in universa Judæa & Sama- ria, denig; usque ad extrema terræ. Sic enim Actor. 3. Apostoli exponunt Judæis, & declarant jam exhi- bitam promissionem Abrahæ factam, in semine tuo benedicentur cunctæ cognationes terræ, Vobis, inquiunt, primum Deus, cum suscitasset filium suum Jesum, misit eum benedicentem vobis, ut u- nusquisque vestrum convertat se ab iniquitatibus suis. Igitur Dominus benedicat tibi, audietur in terra Juda, & in civitatibus ejus, postquam fœmina circumdederit Virum, id est, Dominus Deus ipse ad- erit ibi dexter, fœlix, & benedictiones in illo Viro o- mnipotente, contritor capitis serpentis, & benedictio omnium cognationum terræ, ibi tum audies & vide- bis, quæ jamdudum tibi promissa sunt in Messia. Bea- ti oculi, qui vident, quæ vos videtis, & beatæ aures, quæ audiunt, quæ vos auditis. Multi Reges & Pro- phetæ & justi voluerunt audire, quæ vos auditis, & videtis, & non audierunt, neq; viderunt. Hic audi- tur & videtur Christus benedictio omnium fami- liarum terræ, contra maledictionem legis, & damna- tionem omnium hominum. Benedicentur per Chri- stum, id est, prædicabitur eis Evangelium Christi, & credentes liberabuntur per Christum à sua maledi- ctione, peccato ac morte, & fient filii Dei, donati ju- stitia, bona conscientia, gaudio in Spiritu Sancto, fru- ctibus justitiæ & vita æterna. Hæc est prima, summa, propria & æterna benedictio in Christo, de qua Eph. 1. sic dicitur: Benedictus Deus & Pater Domini no- stri Jesu Christi, qui benedixit nos omni benedi- ctione spirituali in cœlestibus in Christo, quemad- modum elegit nos in Christo, ante constitutionem mundi &c. Deinde nobis credentibus, benedictis per Christum æterna benedictione etiam promisit tempo- ralem benedictionem, panem quotidianum, id est, vi- ctum in hac mortali vita, dicens: Primum quærite regnum Dei, & justitiam ejus, & hæc omnia adjici- entur. Et in Paulo: Pietas ad omnia utilis est, pro- missionem habens vitæ æternæ, præsentis & futuræ. Quod exponit Paulus 1. Cor. 10. Quod omnia sunt nostra, quæ sunt Domini, qui per fidem sumus u- num cum Domino Christo; Christum dicit esse illū Dominum, cujus est terra & plenitudo ejus. Est enim Filius Dei, Hæres omnium bonorum Patris. Quod porro ita exequutus est B. Bugenhagius pag. 354. Quia vero regnum cælorum sive Ecclesia sancta, & justa Christi cœpit in die Pentecostes in Regno Juda, quod erat Davidis, i. e. in Zion & Jerusalem, voca- tur ipsum in Prophetis Zion & Jerusalem, & Regnum Juda æternum, & Zion & Jerusalem facta est spiri- tualis & cælestis, postquam illa terrena periit, ita, ut non manserit ibi lapis super lapidem. Paulo Jerusa- lem, quæ sursum est, mater nostra est; ut videant Judæi, quo respiciant promissiones Dei, videlicet quod promissum illud æternum regnum Davidis, non potest esse regnum terrenum, sed erit regnum cælorum, ut Prophetæ prædixerunt, qui omnes (ut ait Petrus) Christo testimonium perhibent, remissionem peccato- rum accipere per nomen ejus, quotquot credunt in eum, i. e. omnes, sive Judæi, sive gentes in Regno Chri- sti, habent remissionem peccatorum, sive sunt justifi- cati per solum Christum. Psal. 2. dicit Deus: Ego au- tem constitui Regem meum super Zion, montem san- ctum meum, Prædicabo statutum &c. Es. 60. sunt multæ promissiones & fortes consolationes Dei, ipsi Ecclesiæ Christi promissæ, in quibus & hoc dicitur ad Ecclesiam sive regnum Christi, in populo tuo omnes erunt justi, & in æternum possidebunt terram, ut qui surculus sunt plantationis meæ, & opus ma- nuum mearum ad glorificandum. Ex minimo e- runt mille, & ex exiguo populo potens. Ibi Deus vocat regnum Christi Jerusalem, civitatem Domi- ni, Zionem sancti Israëlis, certe montem sanctum, habitationem justitiæ, ut hic Jeremias, quod omnes, qui in eo regno fuerint, erunt sancti & justi, imputa- tione Dei per remissionem peccatorum in Christo. Re- gnum Christi dicitur in terris Mons sanctus, & habi- tatio justitiæ propter cives & inhabitantes, qui omnes sunt sancti & justi. Non fuit Jerusalem sancta propter Hannam & Caipham qui nunquam fuerunt Ecclesia Dei, ut nec olim impii Reges, Principes, Sacerdotes & Prophetæ: Sed ut olim ab Adam soli credentes fuerunt populus Dei, ita nunc soli credentes sunt populus Dei & Regnum Dei. Non enim venit Christus, ut civita- tes Juda & Israël, domos & agros, vel aurum & ar- gentum, & potentiam Gentium occuparet, ut somni- ant sibi stulti Judæi, sine verbo Dei, sed ut homines possideret, quemadmodum ipse dicit: Veniet filius hominis quærere & salvum facere, quod perierat. Quing; millia virorum (in quo numero non sunt mu- lieres & parvuli) primum suscepit Christus in Jeru- salem, sacra regni sui initia, ut legis Act. 4. & deinde quotidie augebatur numerus & multitudo creden- tium. Hi facti sunt primum Ecclesia Christi, populus Dei & regnum cælorum, interim Hannas, Caiphas, Johannes, Alexander, & alii Pontifices & Sacerdo- tes, adversarii Christi, servabantur in terrena illa Je- rusalem perditioni, ut palea igni, & frustra jactita- bant blasphemantes: Nos sumus capita Ecclesiæ & populi Israël. Nos debetis audire, & non illum Ga- lilæum crucifixum. Hæc multitudo populi Sanctorum dispersa est post lapidationem Stephani ad reliquos Judæos & Samaritas, & ad gentes quoque, ut vides in actis Apostolorum, ubi prædicaverunt Evangelium Christi, & dilatata est Jerusalem in totum orbem ter- rarum, Mons sanctus & habitatio justitiæ. Id quod prædixerat Zacharias c. 2. Jerusalem absq; muro ha- bitabitur, præ maxima multitudine hominum, i. e. Judæorum, & pecorum, i. e. gentilium, quæ erunt in ea, Ecce Ego, dicit Dominus, ero Murus igneus in circuitu ejus, & ero in ea &c. ostendam me in me- dio ejus cum gloria, Psal. 87. Fundata est ipsa super montes sanctos. Dominus amat portas Zion ma- gis, quam omnia tabernacula Jacob. Gloriosa præ- dicantur in te, Civitas Dei, Prædicari facia Rahab, i. e. Ægyptiis & Babyloniis, ut cognoscant me, ecce Philistæi & Tyrii cum Æthiopibus nascuntur ibi, in Zion dicetur, quod quisque nascitur in ea, & quod ipse altissimus ædificat eam, &c. Et Ef. 60. Surge, illuminare, quia venit lux tua, &c. Et ambulabunt gentes in lumine tuo, & Gentes in splendore, qui oritur super te, leva oculos tuos, & respice circum- quaque, isti omnes congregati veniunt ad te, &c. Omnes gregesKedar congregabuntur ad te, arietes Nabajoth servient tibi, offerentur super bene com- placens altare meum (quod est Christus, Hebr. 13.) Donum enim gloriæ meæ decorabo, qui sunt isti &c. Portæ tuæ erunt apertæ jugiter, neq; interdiu, neq; nocte claudentur. Ut potentia gentium addu- catur tibi, & deducantur ad te Reges earum. Quia quæ gentes aut regna noluerint servire tibi, per- ibunt, & gentes illæ penitus desolabuntur, &c. Et faciam, ut Præpositi tui doceant decem, & Præsides tui justitiam. Non audietur ultra in terra tua inju- ria, neq; damnum aut perditio in terminis tuis, sed muri tui vocabuntur salus, & portæ tuæ laus, Sol non lucebit tibi amplius per diem, & splendor lunæ non lucefcet tibi, (auditis Judæi, non terrenum Re- gnum fore Jerusalem terrestrem) Sed Dominus erit lux tibi æterna, & Deus tuus erit Gloria tua. Non occidet ultra sol tuus, nec amittet lumen luna tua, Dominus enim erit tibi lux æterna, & dies luctus tui finem habebunt, &c. Et Ef. 49. Parum est, ut sis mihi servus &c. In tempore accepto exaudivi te&c. AtZion dicit: Dominus dereliquit me, Domin9 est oblitus mei &c. Leva oculos circumquaq; &c. Ha- bes montem sanctum, habitationem justitiæ, Regnum Davidis æternum, de quo acclamarunt Christo in die

Palmarum; Benedictus, qui venit in nomine Do- mini, Rex Israël, Benedictum quod venit Regnum patris nostri David, in quo regno prædicatur benedi- ctio omnium populorum terræ, id est, Christus, de quo promisit Deus Abrahæ, in semine tuo benedicentur cunctæ cognationes terræ, benedicat, inquit, tibi Dominus, tu habitatio justitiæ, tu mons sancte. Et Juda cum omnibus suis civitatibus, id est, totum re- gnum Juda Davidi promissum, ex Judæis & genti- bus congregatum ad unum Regem, & Pastorem Davidem, i. e. Christum, Filium Davidis congre- gatum, cum omnibus civitatibus, id est, Ecclesiis, ha- bitabit ibi in Jerusalem, in monte sancto, & in habi- tatione justitiæ; ut & in Psalmo, Domine, quis ha- bitabit in Tabernaculo tuo, aut quis requiescet in monte sancto tuo; Et non respondet: Qui circum- cisus est Judæus, & sic sacrificat. Sed, Qui ingreditur sine macula, & operatur justitiam &c. Et additur, Et agricolæ, & qui mutant loca cum grege suo, i. e. pastores, habitabunt etiam ibi in Jerusalem, in monte sancto, & in habitatione justitiæ. Dic Ju- dæe, Permittesne agricolis ac Pastoribus & ovibus ac jumentis, ut habitent in monte sancto, in templo Do- mini? Quæ commoditas erit illis in Jerusalem? Quo- modo habitabit Juda cum omnibus civitatibus suis in monte sancto & in habitatione justitiæ? Ergo Agri- colas & Pastores Gregis dicit prædicatores Evangelii, & Doctores Ecclesiarum, de quibus promisit Deus etiam supra c. 22. Ecce, Ego congregabo reliquias gregis mei ex omnibus terris, quo ejeceram eas, & reducam eas ad caulas suas, ut crescant & multipli- centur. Et suscitabo super eas Pastores, qui pascant eas, ita ut non metuant ultra, aut terreantur aut visi- tentur, dicit Dominus. Agricolas enim Paulus vo- cat Prædicatores, 1. Corinth. 3. Dedit quidem Deus Judæis post captivitatem Babylonicam fertilitatem agrorum & abundantiam ovium & pecorum. Quia curat suis filiis etiam cibum corporalem. Sed hic præ- mittit totum Judam cum omnibus civitatibus suis, cum agricolis & pastoribus habituros in habitatio- ne justitiæ, i. e. in eo regno, ubi omnes sunt justi in æter- num, ut dixit Esaias, i. e. in Regno Davidis Christi. EGO ENIM REFICIAM. Hæc est causa, quare homines libenter accedant ad Regnum Christi, ut fiant mons sanctus & habitatio justitiæ. Ergo ait Deus, adero in illo Viro contritore capitis serpentis, quem fœ- mina circumdedit in Israël, & peperit in Bethlehem Juda; Erit enim Deus & homo; Et reficiam in Chri- sto animas lassas, i. e. pœnitentes, & animas solicitas, videlicet de victu, i. e. inopes & esurientes peccatores. Ego saturabo in Regno Juda Davidis, i. e. in Eccle- sia Christi, quæ in Juda incepit: Audi virum contri- torem capitis serpentis, hoc ipsum dicentem: Paupe- res evangelizabantur; Qui invitati erant, non fue- runt digni; Ite ergo ad exitus viarum, & quoscun- que inveneritis, debiles, cæcos, claudos, introdu- cite huc; Non est opus medico bene valentibus, sed male habentibus. Venite ad me omnes, qui labo- ratis & onerati estis, & ego reficiam vos, & invenie- tis requiem animabus vestris. Audiant & videant hæc contemptores Judæi, quorum sit regnum cælo- rum, sive Messiæ, certe non eorum, qui expectant Mes- siam, per quem fiant in hoc mundo divites, ponentes gloriosi, sed eorum, qui cupiunt sanari & liberari à peccatis & morte secundum Evangelium; Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. In semine tuo, Abraham, benedicentur cunctæ cognationes ter- ræ: Huc venerandi Antecessoris, fidelis parastatæ Megalandri Lutheri verbis, quam meis ita plene proponere malui, quod non tantum ad hoc vatici- nium explicandum faciant, sed aliis similibus etiam facem accendant. Consonat eximie Osiandrina

Paraphrasis. Quam bene autem habituri sint in Fi- lium Dei incarnatum credentes, Propheta sequenti- bus verbis indicat: Hæc dicit Dominus exercitu- um, Deus Israël: Adhuc dicent verbum istud in ter- ra Juda, & in urbibus ejus, cum convertero captivi- tatem eorum: Sic gratulabuntur Israëlitæ, hoc est, Christiani, Ecclesiæ nascenti: benedicat tibi Domi- nus pulchritudo: Hebraice, ô habitatio justitiæ, ô mons sanctus, in quo est templum Dei viventis (id est, Dominus det tibi, ô Ecclesia Christi incremen- tum, ut augearis, & crescas numero hominum, & do- nis Spiritus Sancti. Tu enim es instar civitatis san- ctissimæ, in qua vigent pietas & justitia: in te habi- tat Dominus Deus præsenter, inprimis vero bonis & donis suis) (Etsi enim Ecclesia in his terris habet suos nævos: tamen justa est coram Deo imputatione justi- tiæ Christi. Et regeneratur atque sanctificatur Spiri- tu Sancto) & habitabunt in eo Judas, populus regni Juda, & omnes civitates ejus simul: Quin, etiam a- gricolæ & pastores, minantes greges, id est, Eccle- sia Christi poterit capere omnes, quotquot sese ei ad- jungere volent: eritque instar amplissimæ civitatis, quæ multas in se civitates & villas possit complecti. (Hæc est Ecclesia Christi Catholica, in qua multæ sunt non modo urbes, sed etiam multi Principatus, imo multa regna, & quidem in ea universali Ecclesia sunt etiam multi spirituales agricolæ & pastores Ecclesia- rum, quibus curæ est agricultura Dei, 1. Cor. 3. Et quo- rum fidei oves pascendæ sunt commissæ sub uno supre- mo pastore Christo, 1. Petr. 5.) Tunc beati erunt cives istius Ecclesiæ (inquit Christus) Quia inebriavi: re- ctius: inebriabo (large reficiam) animam lassam, & omnem animam esurientem: rectius dolentem, sa- turavi; Rectius saturabo. Hactenus Osiander.

## 31:26
Verse 26. THEREFORE AS IF AWAKENED FROM SLEEP I WAS, AND I SAW, AND MY SLEEP WAS SWEET TO ME] The Prophet speaks: When I arose from this vision, I saw: That is; with pleasure I contemplated what had been revealed to me. And my sleep was sweet to me: That is, I slept sweetly afterwards, which before I was not accustomed to do on account of pain.

He follows the Jews, but Maldonatus observes that they acknowledge the prophecy concerning Christ delivered by the Prophet. Jonathan, R. David, and R. Solomon say it is of the Prophet speaking, who, after he had received this prophecy about the future Christ in dreams, awoke, and was filled with great pleasure. Others refer it to the people; some to God, because it seems to be a certain continuous discourse of the same. Pious, and not unpleasant, is the ἔκθεσις of our blessed Bugenhagen, who wishes these words to be those of the Son of God. For those things which intervene are His own. I will refresh the weary souls, and I will satisfy the anxious souls, as we know from Is. 50:4, 55:2, Matt. 11:28: And to that end Christ both died and was resurrected. I have inebriated (or I will refresh) the weary soul, and I have satisfied every hungry soul. Therefore I was awakened as if from sleep, and I saw, and my sleep was sweet to me. But it is helpful to hear the blessed Pomeranus again. THEREFORE I AWOKE. I, when treating of this in that school, judged that this word 'to awake' should be explained from that which follows, 'and as I watched,' etc. But now I see it is not similar. For there, to watch is to do something with zeal, and to apply oneself to something with all effort. But here, to awake, what else can it be than to be roused from sleep? That which he adds: 'After I had slept sweetly.' It is certain that God Himself speaks here, just as in the preceding words: 'For I will refresh,' etc. I do not, therefore, delay over the corrupters of Scripture; the words are sufficiently clear. Thus the Lord God speaks here: Therefore, or for this reason, namely, that I might be able to refresh the weary souls and satisfy the anxious souls, I awoke. I, God, looked up, where I had slept sweetly in the land of Judah, that is, I, God, in that man promised, whom a woman encompassed, I slept sweetly, that is, I was dead, and I sanctified a happy Sabbath in the sepulchre, I awoke, that is, I lived again and rose again after a sweet sleep, and I looked up, that is, I attended to the miseries of men, to weary souls, that I might help them, as follows below; Thus I will watch over them, that I may build and plant, etc. For rising from death in the land of Judah, I sat at the right hand of the Father, and I sent the Holy Spirit into Jerusalem first, then into the whole world, that I might refresh weary souls, and satisfy anxious souls, for whom I was dead, and rose again, thus I looked up and attended, that reigning at the right hand of the Father, and having power in heaven and on earth, I may be with you, Emmanuel, all the days even unto the consummation of the age, Matt. last. You see what God says here about the death of Christ and the resurrection in the land of Judah, and about the kingdom of Christ through the Gospel and the Holy Spirit, Go, he says, into the whole world, etc. There God himself in that omnipotent man Christ slept sweetly, awoke and looked up, and still looks up forever, sees and attends, acting among us and in us through his Holy Spirit, and the preaching of the Gospel, all the days, even unto the consummation of the age. Paul, Acts 20, says: God acquired his Church for himself with his own blood. That therefore God dies, rises again, and reigns at the right hand of the Father, all things are and are done in that man, whom a woman encompassed, for us, for the salvation of men, that God in Christ and through Christ may refresh weary souls, and satisfy anxious souls. Rom. 8. Christ sits at the right hand of God, and intercedes for us. You have therefore here, that God, or the Son of God Christ, who in the land of Israel took up this our mortal life, finished it in the land of Judah in Jerusalem, and where he had slept sweetly there, he rose again in the same place, and began there to reign through the Holy Spirit, etc. As Christ predicts to the disciples, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things will be finished there, which have been said in the Prophets concerning the son of man. Thus far our Bugenhagius, whose learned and pious opinion I would not rashly disparage. If it does not please anyone, he will be able to follow Osiander, expressing it thus: Therefore, in Hebrew: upon this (as if awakened from sleep) I saw the miseries of my people, and my sleep had been sweet to me: I had indulged in sleep for a very long time, that is: I indeed for a long time seemed to care little for my people; when, namely, after the last Prophets, who prophesied after the return from Babylon, I sent no further Prophet to them. Therefore, the miserable souls almost failed from the lack of pure heavenly doctrine: for they could not seek solid consolations from the sermons of the Pharisees. Wherefore, as if awakening from sleep, I looked upon my Church, and I refresh the troubled consciences with my Gospel, concerning the remission of sins, abundantly and most sweetly. For those who receive the Gospel of Christ by faith find the true refreshment of their souls, according to that: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you, Matt. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 26. IDEO QVASI DE SOMNO SUSCITA- TVS SVM, ET VIDI, ET SOMNVS MEVS DVL- CIS MIHI] Loquitur Propheta: Ubi ab hoc viso, surrexi, vidi: Id est; cum voluptate contemplatus sum, quæ mihi erant revelata. Et somnus meus mihi dulcis fuit: Id est, sua- viter dormivi postea, quod antea præ dolore facere non solebam.

Sequitur Judæos, sed illos agnoscere Prophe- tiam de Christo à Propheta traditam observat Mal- donatus. Jonathas, R. David & R. Salomo dicunt, esse Prophetæ dicentis, se, postquam in somniis hanc de futuro Christo prophetiam accepisset, experge- factum, magnaq; perfusum voluptate. Alii ad po- pulum; nonnulli ad Deum referunt, quod continua quædam ejusdem oratio esse videatur. Pia est, nec injucunda B. Bugenhagii nostri ἔκθεσις, qui hæc ver- ba vult esse Filii Dei. Ejus enim propria sunt, quæ intercedunt. Ego reficiam animas lassas, & solicitas animas saturabo, uti ex Es. 50, 4. 55, 2. Matth. 11, 28. novimus: Et ea fine tum mortuus est, tum resusci- tatus Christus. Inebriavi (vel reficiam) animam lassam, & omnem animam esurientem saturavi. Id- circo quasi de somno suscitatus sum, & vidi, & somnus meus dulcis mihi. Sed juvat iterum B. Pomeranum audire. ICCIRCO EVIGILAVI. Ego quandoq; in scho- la ista tractans, judicavi exponendum hoc verbum evigilandi, ex eo, quod sequitur, & sicut vigilavi &c. Sed nunc video, non esse simile. Nam ibi vigilare, est studio quid agere, & toto conatu ad aliquid incum- bere. Hic autem evigilare, quid aliud esse potest, quam è somno excitari? id quod addit: Postquam suavi- ter dormieram. Certum est hic Deum ipsum loqui, sicut & in præcedentibus verbis: Ego enim reficiam &c. Non moror ergo depravatores Scripturæ, verba sunt satis aperta. Sic loquitur hic Dominus Deus: Idcirco vel propterea, videlicet, ut possim refice- re animas lassas, & animas solicitas saturare, evi- gilavi. Ego Deus, & suspexi, ubi suaviter dor- mieram in terra Juda, id est, Ego Deus in viro illo promisso, quem foemina circumdedit, suaviter dormivi, id est, mortuus sui, & foelix Sabbathum sanctificavi in sepulchro, evigilavi, id est, revixi & resurrexi post suavem somnum, & suspexi, id est, at- tendi ad miserias hominum, ad animas lassas, ut au- xiliarer eis, quemadmodum infra sequitur; Ita vi- gilabo super eos, ut ædificem & plantem &c. Resur- gens enim à morte in terra Iuda, consedi in dextera Patris, & misi Spiritum Sanctum in Ierusalem pri- mum, deinde in totum mundum, ut reficiam animas lassas, & saturem animas solicitas, pro quibus mor- tuus sui, & resurrexi, ita suspexi & attendi, ut in dex- tera patris regnans, & potestatem habens in cælo & in terra, vobiscum sim Emanuel omnibus diebus us- que ad consummationem sæculi, Matth. ult. Vides, quod hic Deus de morte Christi & resurrectione in terra Iuda dicit, & de regno Christi per Evangelium & Spiritum Sanctum, Ite, inquit, in mundum uni- versum, &c. Ibi Deus ipse in viro illo omnipotente Christo suaviter dormivit, evigilavit & suspexit, & adhuc in æternum suspicit, videt & attendit, apud nos, & in nobis agens per suum Spiritum Sanctum, & Ev- angelii prædicationem, omnibus diebus, usq; ad con- summationem sæculi. Paulus Act. 20. dicit: Ec- clesiam suam Deus acquisivit sibi sanguine suo. Quod itaq́; Deus moritur, resurgit, & regnat in dex- tera Patris, omnia sunt & fiunt in isto viro, quem fœ- mina circumdedit, pro nobis, ad salutem hominum, ut Deus in Christo & per Christum reficiat animas lassas, & saturet animas solicitas Rom. 8. Christus sedet ad dexteram Dei, & intercedit pro nobis. Ha- bes itaq́; hic, quod Deus, sive Filius Dei Christus, qui in terra Israel suscepit hanc nostram mortalem vi- tam, consummavit in terra Iuda in Ierusalem, & u- bi suaviter ibi dormierat, resurrexit ibidem, & cœ- pit ibi per Spiritum Sanctum regnare &c. Quemad- modum Christus prædicit discipulis, Ecce, ascendi- mus Hierosolymam, & consummabuntur ibi o- mnia, quæ dicta sunt in Prophetis de filio hominis. Hactenus Bugenhagius noster, cujus eruditam & piam sententiam temere sugillandam haud duxe- rim. Si cui ea nõ placeat, Osiandrum sequi poterit, ita exprimentem: Ideo, Hebraice: super hoc (quasi de somno suscitatus sum) & vidi populi mei mise- rias, & somnus meus dulcis mihi fuerat: diu admo- dum indulseram somno, id est: Ego quidem longo tempore visus sum populum meum parum curare; quando nimirum post ultimos Prophetas, qui post reditum ex Babylone sunt vaticinati, nullum am- plius Prophetam illis misi. Itaque miseræ animæ propemodum defecerunt ex inopia puræ doctri- næ cœlestis: non enim ex Pharisæorum concioni- bus solidas consolationes petere potuere. Quare, quasi de somno evigilans, respexi Ecclesiam meã, & perturbatas conscientias Evangelio meo, de re- missione peccatorum, largiter & suavissime refi- cio. Qui enim Christi Evangelion fide recipiunt, veram animarum suarum refectionem inveniunt, juxta illud: Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis, ac onerati estis, & ego reficiam vos, Matth. 11.

## 31:27
Ver. 27. I WILL SOW THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL] That is, I will fill. Ver. 28. AND AS I HAVE WATCHED] I have been diligent.

To be explained more specifically: what kind of filling, and what these benefits were. Grotius, as it appears, understands it of bodily multiplication. But the scope and context prove that the Prophet is dealing with the propagation of the Church, not with the bodily multiplication of the Israelites, about which the interpreters easily agree among themselves, not even excluding the older Jews. For these say that the calling of the Gentiles is included here; In Midrash R. Nachman it is thus: The seed of man is they are Israel, as it is said Ezek. 34, 31. And you my sheep, the sheep of my pasture are men. And the seed of the beast are they proselytes or converts from the Gentiles. B. Bugenhagius reports these things on this passage: TO SOW. Enough was given to the Jews regarding sustenance, and they were multiplied after the Babylonian captivity in the land of Judah and in the land of Israel, but yet Israel was not returned to its fields and possessions; But here God says that he wishes to raise up again both houses into one kingdom of David, just as it is also said from Micah: I will gather all of you, Jacob, and I will bring the remnants of Israel into one. I, as a shepherd, will gather them together into one fold, as a flock into its pens, so that the noisy sound of a multitude of men may be heard there, etc. Ezekiel also and Jeremiah openly predict concerning one shepherd and King David, as we indicated before. Hos. chap. 3. he says thus: Afterwards the Children of Israel will be converted, and will seek the Lord their God, and their King David, and they will glorify the Lord, and his goodness in the last time. And chap. 2. The number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can neither be measured nor numbered. And it will come to pass, that in the place where it was said, You are not my people, there it shall be said to them: O children of the living God! For the children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together, and will adhere equally to one head. And they will ascend from the land, because that day of Israel will be great, that is, of the seed of God. Concerning which seed of God, and the multiplication of peoples in one kingdom of David, that is, of Christ, Jeremiah also says here, Behold, the days come, says the Lord, namely after my resurrection, that I will sow the house of Israel, and the house of Judah, that is, the whole kingdom of David, of Christ, with much seed, namely both with men and with beasts. There will not be there the seed of men, by which men are sown and generated, nor will there be there the seed of beasts, by which beasts are sown and generated, but it will be my seed, says the Lord, I myself will sow and resow into the whole kingdom of David, men and beasts will be the seed of God there. What is this other than what Hosea says: Israel, that is, the seed of God, and the children of the living God; That this is said of the New Testament, Paul is also a witness, Rom. 9. If men and beasts are to be children of God, of whom he speaks here, it is certain that he is speaking here again of the holy mountain, and of the habitation of righteousness, that is, of the kingdom of Christ, in which all inhabitants are holy and righteous, as was said before, that is, children of God. Therefore he calls men Jews, beasts Gentiles, whom the Jews despised before themselves as beasts. These together will be the seed, that is, children of God, in the kingdom of Christ, John 1. But as many as received him, whether Jews or Gentiles, he gave them power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name, who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. Jacob the Patriarch calls the children of God in the Kingdom of Shiloh, that is, of Christ, the foal of Christ, and the son of Christ's ass, Gen. 49, binding his foal to the vine, and his ass's son to the branch; in Psalm 68. they are called animals and cattle of God; just as flocks of sheep are also often accustomed to be called in the Scriptures. Your animals, he says, will dwell in it, with your goods you console the poor, O God, the Lord gives the word and a great army of Evangelists, etc. Christ openly expressed these things in John 10 thus: I am the good shepherd: The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. I have other sheep, he says, that is, Gentiles, which are not of this fold, that is, they are not Jews, them I must bring, and there will be one shepherd, and one fold. This is Bugenhagen. If it is harsh that the Gentiles are designated by beasts, their multiplication added can be understood, so that it might be expressed that even for the faithful there would not be lacking earthly and bodily blessing: because by beasts of burden every kind of wealth, which was once valued by cattle, whence the name of money arose, can be designated.

Latin:

Vers. 27. SEMINABO DOMUM ISRAEL] Id est, replebo. Vers. 28. ET SICVT VIGILAVI] Sedulus fui.|

Explicandum specjalius: qualis repletio, & quæ beneficia hæc fuerint. De corporali multiplicatione, ut apparet, intelligit Grotius. At de Ecclesiæ pro- pagatione, non de Israë̈litarum corporali multipli- catione agere Prophetam, scopus ac contextus e- vincũt, de quo facile Interpp. inter se consentiunt, ne exceptis quidẽ antiquioribus Judæis. Hi enim vocationem gentium hic comprehendi ajunt; In Midrasch R. Nachman ita habet: Semen hominis est illi sunt Israël, sicut dictum est Ezech. 34, 31. Et vos oves meæ, oves pascuæ meæ homines estis. Et se- men bestiæ illi sunt proselyti sive conversi ex gentibus. B. Bugenhagius ad hunc locum hæc tradit: UT PERSEMINEM. Satis quod ad victum attinet Judæis datum est, & multiplicati sunt post captivi- tatem Babylonicam in terra Juda & in terra Israël, sed tamen Israël non est redditus suis agris & posses- sionibus; Hic autem dicit Deus, quod vult rursum e- rigere utramque domum in unum regnum Davidis, quemadmodum & ex Micha dictum est: Ego te Ja- cob totum congregabo, & reliquias Israël in unum adducam. Ego, ut pastor, eas simul in unum ovile colligam, quasi gregem in caulas suas, ut strepens sonitus ibi audiatur multitudinis hominum &c. Ezechiel quoq; & Jeremias aperte prædicunt de uno pastore & Rege David, ut ante indicavimus. Hos. cap. 3. sic dicit: Postea convertentur Filii Israël, & requirent Dominum Deum suum, & Regem suum David, & glorificabunt Dominum, & gratiam ejus in novissimo tempore. Et cap. 2. Erit numerus fi- liorum Israël ut arena maris, quæ neque mensurari neque numerari potest.Et futurum est,ut in loco, ubi dictum est, Vos non estis populus meus, ibi dicatur ipsis: ô filii Dei viventis! Congregabun- tur enim filii Juda & filii Israël simul, & adhærebunt pariter uni capiti.Et ascendent ex terrâ, quia ma- gnus erit illa dies Israël,id est,seminis Dei. De quo semine Dei, & multiplicatione populorum in uno re- gno Davidis,id est, Christi, etiam hic dicit Jeremias, Ecce, dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, videlicet post resurrectionem meam, ut perseminem domum Is- raël, & domum Juda, id est, totum regnum Davidis, Christi, multo semine, videlicet & hominibus & ju- mentis.Non erit ibi semen hominum, quo semi- nentur & generentur homines, nec erit ibi semen jumentorum, quo seminentur & generentur ju- menta, sed erit semen meum, dicit Dominus, ego ipse seminabo & perseminabo in totum regnum Davidis, semen Dei erunt ibi homines & jumenta, Quid est hoc aliud, quam quod Hosea dicit: Israël, id est, semen Dei, & filii Dei viventis; Quod de No- vo Testamento dictum, testis est etiam Paulus Rom. 9. Si filii Dei erunt homines & jumenta, de quibus hic dicit, certum est, quod hic rursum loquitur de mon- te sancto, & de habitatione justitiæ, id est, de regno Christi,in quo omnes habitatores sunt sancti & ju- sti, ut ante dictum est, id est, filii Dei. Homines er- go dicit Judæos, Jumenta gentes,quas Judæi præ se contemnebant ut bestias. Hi simul erunt semen,id est, filii Dei, in regno Christi, Joh. 1. Quotquot autem susceperunt eum, sive Judai, sive Gentes, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, iis qui credunt in no- men ejus,qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex volun- tate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed exDeo na- ti sunt. Jacob Patriarcha filios Dei in Regno Silo, id est, Christi, vocat pullum Christi, & filium asinæ Christi, Gen. 49. ligans ad vitem pullum suum, & ad palmitem filium asinæ suæ; in Psal.68. vocantur animalia & pecora Dei; sicut & greges ovium sæpe solent in Scripturis vocari. Animalia, inquit, tua habitabunt in ea, tuis bonis pauperem consolaris Deus, Dominus dat verbum & exercitum multum Evangelistarum &c. Christus aperte hæc Ioh. 10. sic expreffit: Ego sum pastor bonus: Bonus pastor a- nimam suam ponit pro ovibus suis. Adhuc alias oves habeo, id est, gentes, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, id est, non sunt Judæi, illas oportet me ad- ducere, & fiet unus pastor, & unum ovile. Hæc Bugenhagius. Si durum per jumenta gentes desi- gnari, eorum multiplicatio addita intelligi po- test, ut exprimeretur, fidelibus etiam non defu- turam terrenam & corporalem benedictionem: quia per jumenta omne genus divitiarum, quæ olim pecudibus æstimabantur,unde nomen pecu- niæ ortum, designari potest.

## 31:29
Verse 29.

THEY SHALL NOT SAY ANY MORE: THE FATHERS HAVE EATEN A SOUR GRAPE, AND THE CHILDREN'S TEETH ARE SET ON EDGE) Ὄμφαξ, that is, a sour grape, has a very astringent power. The Jews used this proverb, as can be seen in Ezekiel 18:2, as if they were saying: You will suffer the sins of your ancestors undeservedly, Roman.

It is not to be doubted that God, the maker of all men, and therefore their Lord, can punish parents who have deserved it in such a way that the exile continues even to their descendants; but His own goodness eventually sets a limit to this supreme right, partly on account of the outstanding virtues of the older parents, and partly on account of the descendants themselves. Note 'in those days': and in Ezekiel: 'if it shall be any more'.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

NON DICENT ULTRA : PATRES COME- DERVNT UVAM ACERBAM, ET DENTES FILIO- RVM OBSTVPVERVNT) Ὄμφαξ, id est, uva acerba, vim habet multum adstringentem. Hoc adagium Judæi usurpabant, ut videre est Ezech. 18, 2. quasi dicerent: Delicta majorum immeritus lues, Romane.

Non dubitandum est, quin Deus, omnium hominum o- pifex, ac propterea Dominus, possit parentes ita meritos punire exsilio etiam ad posteros permanente; sed huic sum- mo juri bonitas ipsius tandem modum imponit, partim propter antiquiorum parentu, partim propter ipsorum posterorum egregias virtutes. Nota in diebus illis : & apud Ezechielem : si erit ultra.

## 31:30
Verse 30.

EVERYONE SHALL DIE IN HIS OWN INIQUITY) Thus in Ezekiel, The soul (that is, the man) that sins, he shall die. Judgments will be exercised so well that it will not be necessary to come to those extraordinary and general punishments. The sense is the same in Isaiah 65:20, where see the notes.

It is not a question of the diversity of God's judgments, as if sometimes innocent children were punished for the sins of their parents, but afterwards were not to be punished any more for their parents, with divine goodness intervening in God's supreme right: But it is about the different judgments of the people of God, either calling them to examination, or complaining about them, or ceasing to complain. For the words 'THEY SHALL NOT SAY ANY MORE' imply a censure of these. The Prophet does not point out what He did before: but what the Israelites judged or said that God had done before. Osiander therefore correctly paraphrases: 'Formerly my people were so blinded in their impiety that they would not acknowledge their sins. But, if I sent any punishments for sins upon them, they would clamor that they were bearing the punishments for sins which not they, but their parents had deserved.' (For this proverb, often and much used among the Jews, is also attested by Ezekiel chapter 18.) And there will not be such stupor of the people in the New Testament. But rather, being chastised for their sins, they will be humbled and will confess that they have been corrected less than their merits deserved, for Christians, understanding this, say with the Psalmist: 'He has not dealt with us according to our sins: nor rewarded us according to our iniquities,' Psalm 103. These are Osiander's words. Whom the Weimar Paraphrasts have also followed. If, however, anyone wishes to refer these things to God, the explanation of our Bugenhagen will have a place: 'THEN IT SHALL NO LONGER BE SAID.' God promises in the New Testament security to all who abandon the errors and sins of their fathers, so that they may not fear that sentence of the law which says, 'I am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.' This very promise and Evangelical sentence is expressed in many words in Ezekiel 18. Read the whole chapter there. 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes,' i.e., have sinned, and provoked God to anger, 'and the children's teeth are set on edge,' that is, we their descendants are punished for the sins of our fathers, just as our Jeremiah also complains in Lamentations, chapter 5, etc. According to the law, children bear the iniquity of the fathers who persevere in the sins of the fathers. But according to the Gospel or the new covenant, which is promised here, children who believe in Christ do not bear the sins of their fathers, but have the remission of all sins, as you will hear here presently. For Christ absolves believers from the curse of the law. But he who does not believe shall be condemned. Which is said here thus: Whoever eats sour grapes, that is, has despised God, and has sinned; his own teeth shall be set on edge, that is, he himself shall be condemned for his own sin. The former explanation, however, seems simpler to us, so that Jeremiah proclaims both that the faithful will acknowledge their sins; and that (as follows in verse 31) by the power of the covenant of grace they will obtain the remission of them.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

UNVSQVISQVE IN INIQVITATE SVA MO- RIETVR) Sic apud Ezechielem, Anima (id est,homo) qui peccaverit,ipse morietur. Judicia tam bene exercebuntur, ut nihil necesse futurum sit ad extraordinarias illas & genera- les pœnas veniri.Idem est sensus Es.65,20. ubi notata vide.
