Non de diversitate judiciorum Dei agitur, qua- si aliquando filii in\u017薔ontes propter parentū pecca- ta puniti sint, deinceps autem puniendi amplius ob parentes non sint,intercedente summo Dei juri di- vina bonitate : Sed de diversis judiciis populi Dei, vel sub examen vocantis, aut de iisdem conquerentis, vel conqueri desinentis. Nam horum censuram im- portant verba : NON DICENT ULTRA. Non quod fecerit antea:sed quid Deum fecisse antea ju- dicaverint, vel dixerint Israëlitæ, Propheta indigi- tat. Recte ergo περιΦραζει Osiander; Olim popu- lus meus ita fuit excæcatus in sua impietate, ut pecca- ta nollet agnoscere. Sed,si quas illis peccatorum pœnas immittebam, clamitabant, se supplicia peccatorum ferre, quæ non ipsi,sed parentes ipsorum essent meriti. (Hoc enim Proverbium sæpe multumq;, inter Judæos usurpatum,testatur etiam Ezechiele cap. 18.) Ac non erit talis stupor populi in Novo Testamento. Sed po- tius propter peccata castigati, humiliabuntur & fa- tebuntur, se minus, quam pro meritis suis fuisse corre- reptos, intelligentes enim Christiani dicunt cum Psal- mista : Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis: neque secundum iniquitates nostras retribuit no- bis, Psal. 103. Hæc Osiander. Quem sequuti etiam sunt Paraphrastæ Vinarienses. Si tamen quis ad Deum hæc referre velit, Bugenhagii nostri expli- catio locum habitura est : TUNC NON AM- PLIUS DICETUR. Promittit Deus in Novo Te- stamento securitatem omnibus, qui errores ac peccata Patrum deserunt,ne metuant illam sententiam legis, quæ dicit, Ego sum Deus zelotes, vindicans iniqui- tatem patrum in filios, usque in tertiam & quartam generationem eorum, qui oderunt me. Hæc ipsa promissio & Evangelica sententia multis verbis ex- pressa est Ezech.18. Lege illic totum caput. Patres comederunt immatura, i. e. peccaverunt, & Deum ad iracundiam concitaverunt, & dentes filiorum obstupescunt,id est, nos posteri eorum punimur pro- pter peccata patrum, quemadmodum etiam queritur in Threnis noster Jeremias, cap. 5. &c. Secundum legem filii portant iniquitatemPatrum,qui in pec- catis Patrum perseverant. Secundum Evangelium autem vel novum pactum,quod hic promittitur,fi- lii,qui credunt in Christum, non portant peccata Patrum, sed habent remissionem omnium pecca- torum, ut mox hic audies. Nam Christus à maledi- ctione legis absolvit credentes. Qui vero non credi- derit,condemnabitur. Quod hic sic dicit : Quisquis comederit immatura,id est,contempserit Deum, & peccaverit; ejusdem dentes stupescent, id est, ipse propter peccatum proprium condemnabitur. Prior tamen explicatio nobis simplicior videtur, ut præ- dicat Jeremias, cum quod agnituri sint fideles pec- cata; tum quòd (veluti sequitur vers. 31.) vi pacti gratiæ remissionem eorum consecuturi sint.

## 31:31
Verse 31.

AND I WILL MAKE A NEW COVENANT WITH THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL, AND WITH THE HOUSE OF JUDAH) I will renew the covenant through my Prophets: See Nehemiah 9:38, chapter 10. But this is usually done when the other party has broken the covenant.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

ET FERIAM DOMVI ISRAEL, ET DOMVI JVDA FOEDVS NOVUM) Renovabo fœdus per Pro- phetas meas: Vide Nehem. 9, 38. c. 10. Solet autem id fieri, ubi pars altera fedus infregit.

## 31:32
Verse 32.

NOT ACCORDING TO THE COVENANT, WHICH I MADE WITH THEIR FATHERS, IN THE DAY THAT I TOOK THEM BY THE HAND, TO BRING THEM OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT.) For that covenant says: I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt. But this benefit will be overshadowed by a greater and more admirable benefit, Is. 43, 28.

WHICH THEY BROKE) By many grievous and long-standing sins, concerning which see Isaiah, this Prophet, and Nehemiah chapter 9.

A notable depravation of a most august promise; which, as it appears, was undertaken for the sake of the Socinians and their like, who attempt to eliminate and expunge the promises of eternal life from the books of the Old Testament, which goal he revealed not obscurely at verse 33; indeed, even for the sake of the Jews, who contend by the force of this oracle that the Old Testament is not to be abrogated, but only to be renewed. For thus R. Isaac explains it in Chiffuk chapter 29, whose Φλυαρίας (trifles) Dr. D. Muller demolished in his Judaism, page 726. For the Prophet treats of a new covenant, and indicates the abrogation of the old when he promises a new one. But Grotius understands it of the old, and wishes it to be indicated that only its renewal is meant. The Prophet clearly implies a different covenant when he says that the Lord will strike a new covenant, not according to the pact which He made concerning the leading out from the land of Egypt on Mount Sinai. But Grotius wishes not a different covenant to be signified, but only a diversity of the benefits of that leading out from Egypt and the leading out from Babylon, by which he falsely thinks the former was shadowed forth as a greater and more admirable benefit. For the benefit of the liberation from Egypt was certainly a greater and more wonderful benefit, joined with many and stupendous prodigies and miracles, with the stupendous passage of the whole Israelite people through the Red Sea, and the horrible suffocation of the entire Pharaonic army in the same, than the liberation of the two tribes of Israel from Babylon. Nor does the passage Is. 43, 18 contribute anything here, so that it might be taught that this liberation is greater and more admirable: because it does not treat of the liberation from the Babylonian captivity, as we have noted in that place. How this notable passage can be urged against the Jews, see Dr. Muller, page 673 et seqq.

Verse the same.

AND I RULED OVER THEM, SAYS THE LORD.) One may translate, And I would have remained their husband. But the LXX, for בעלתי, read בחלתי, and therefore translated, ἐγὼ ἠμέλησα αὐτῶν (I neglected them). There is no reason why we should disapprove of this. They neglected me, I in turn neglected them.

The Greek translation is rashly and perversely preferred to the Authentic text, nor does Buxtorff teach that the LXX Interpreters read otherwise, even if they translated otherwise, in his Vindic. page 675. Nor is there any reason for abandoning the Vulgate version, which is in excellent agreement with the Hebrew source. But the dominion of coercion is understood, just as the Blessed Luther rendered it, with B. Bugenhagen: Which Osiander explains: I RULED OVER THEM, i.e., I had to treat them as servants, not as sons, because of their manifold transgressions and their notable stubbornness. By which periphrasis our people have rightly observed that the nature of the ancient covenant is designated, which is that it was not only impossible to be fulfilled: Just as that was rendered entirely void by the Israelites; but because it is also joined with dominion and coercion, since it forces the unwilling to obedience. For the law of Moses can neither be fulfilled perfectly by anyone, and yet it forces everyone to obedience, and extorts compliance from all under the thunderbolt of a curse. Because it does not confer the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of liberty. Therefore, the works of the law, which are done by the unregenerate, are done by the unwilling and the coerced; whence there was a need for a new covenant, which would both bring the remission of sins, because the law could not be fulfilled, and would confer the Holy Spirit, so that we might render spontaneous obedience to the divine commands. Under the law there is coercion, punishment, and condemnation; under grace there is liberty, obedience, and voluntary worship. But because our blessed Bugenhagen, who was among the first restorers of evangelical doctrine from the word of God, has excellently declared this doctrine concerning the distinction between the Old and New Covenant from this illustrious passage and parallel scriptures, especially from the Epistle to the Hebrews, which treats this passage at length in chapters 8 and 9; it will not be tedious to bring forward his explanation, as it is solid and clear, which he opposed both to the Papists and also to the sectarians and Sacramentarians. For he considers that these men suffer an excellent punishment for their contempt, while they despise the writings and doctrine of the Evangelicals, since they show that they understand nothing about the abolition of the law, which is through faith in Christ, and do not even perceive the terms, so that they might know what is the Old and what is the New Testament. Which we see here also in Grotius. NEW COVENANT: BY SAYING NEW, says our blessed one, he abolishes the old, as the Epistle to the Hebrews also argues, just as among men a later testament abrogates a former one. Which Jeremiah also declares thus in the words of God; For as it was the covenant which I made with their fathers, when I took them by the hand (just as the hand of a little child is taken, so that it may be led) and led them out of Egypt, namely on Mount Sinai. Therefore, this is a different pact than that old one. Since that one was of the old man, and demanded his righteousness before God, which he himself did not have, nor could have, for it was impossible for a man to be justified by the law of commandments, as Paul teaches in the Acts of the Apostles, and in his Epistles, and he himself, already justified through Christ, complains of himself in Rom. 7, etc. What then would you hope for from the law concerning those not justified? God indeed promised, I will be your God, but he adds a condition of the law impossible for us, if you have remained in my commandments. Cursed is he who has not remained in all things which are written in the book of the law, as was said above in chapter 30. This curse of the law and our condemnation Christ transferred to himself, and abolished for believers; he did not only abolish the ceremonies, otherwise, where would be the remission of sins, the imputation of righteousness, the gift of the Holy Spirit and of eternal life, which we have through CHRIST alone, and on account of CHRIST alone, and in Christ alone, having been grafted into him by faith and made children of God? This is the New Testament, but for the new, who are renewed by faith and the Spirit of God, having put off the oldness of the letter, or of the old law. Without this New Testament or covenant, all men, until the end of the world, not only those unbelieving Jews, remain under the law, or the Old Testament. For they are not under grace Rom. 3, even if they have fashioned for themselves a religion of angels, Col. 2. Thus Paul says to the Galatians that Christ was made under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons of God, no longer servants under the law, but free under grace. And Rom. 8. What was impossible for the law, because it was weak through the flesh, this God did by sending his own son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and condemned sin for sin through the flesh, so that the justification of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit, etc. The Old Testament, or the law of God, reveals sin and demands righteousness, but the New Testament or covenant, which is the Gospel, forgives sin and confers righteousness. By the former, all are held guilty of eternal death. By the latter, all are absolved, and receive eternal life. There, the oldness of the letter killed; here, the newness of the Spirit gives life. For consciences are not terrified by the Gospel, as by the law, but receive eternal consolation from GOD. And just as the law, so also the priesthood of the law was useless for purifying consciences before God. It did indeed have propitiation, and remission of sins, but a legal one, that is, an external one. For men who sinned against the prescription of the law by an external work were separated, that is, as we now say, were excommunicated, and again were received back into that external communion of the people and worship of GOD, either by washings or by sacrifices instituted in the law. But Christ, the Priest of the New Testament and Mediator between God and man, truly pacifies and sanctifies in the conscience before GOD forever, so that we may be not only participants of the Saints and of men and of angels, but also partakers of the divine nature through him. This Christ is not a Levitical or legal priest, but an eternal priest, at the right hand of God interceding for us, the blessing of all the families of the earth, but according to the order of Melchizedek, that is, a free Priest, who justifies without the law, and receives sinners freely: Our propitiation Rom. 3. The throne of grace Heb. 4. An advocate with the father 1 John 2, who sits at the right hand of Majesty on high, having made purification of sins by himself, Heb. 1. On account of Christ the law has no right to accuse us, much less does it have the right to condemn; for on his account the transgression of the law, that is, sin, is not imputed to us, and on his account all our things are acceptable to God. Whatever of the law or of works you read to be commended in the Scriptures, do not understand it to please GOD without the mediator Christ: for without faith it is impossible to please GOD. By this confidence in Christ the crusher of the Serpent's head, and the blessing of all nations, those ancients were once justified, and made partakers of this new Testament. For no one could ever be justified otherwise. But the Gospel delivered these things more obscurely: The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent; not the Law, or our work shall crush it; in thy seed, O Abraham, shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed, not in the law, or human works; to say nothing of the Sacrifices, and figures, or significations of the law looking toward Christ. The Prophets, however, or holy Preachers declared these things more clearly, as I said before concerning Adam; especially in the Psalms, that we are saved not by the law, but by the mercy of God, which is in Christ, etc. So that you may see there has always been one justifying faith before God, even among the ancient Fathers, which is also among us. From this, however, it does not follow that the old and new Testament are the same, nor that they differ only in the manner of delivery, as someone recently wrote most unlearnedly. This grace is here promised by God to be spread abroad, and given to the house of Israel, and to the house of Judah, that is, to the whole Kingdom of David, that is, of Christ, which is the kingdom of heaven extended from Jerusalem through the preaching of the Gospel to all nations. Thus Bugenhagen: which blessed Luther has everywhere executed with great Spirit in his golden writings.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

NON SECVNDVM PACTVM, QVOD PEPI- GI CVM PATRIBVS EORVM, IN DIE, QVA AP- PREHENDI MANVM EORVM, VT EDVCEREM EOS DE TERRA ÆGTPTI.) Nam illud pactum dicit: Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui te eduxi de terra Ægypti. Hoc autem beneficium majore ac admirabiliore beneficio obumbrabitur, Es. 43, 28.

QVOD IRRITVM FECERVNT) Multis gravi- bus ac diuturnis peccatis, de quibus vide Esaiam, hunc Pro- phetam, & Nehemiam cap. 9.

Depravatio insignis promissionis augustissi- mæ; Quæ, ut apparet, in gratiam Socinianorum, ac similium, qui è libris Veteris Testamenti promissiones vitæ æternæ eliminare, & expungere conantur, sus- cepta est, quem scopum ad vers. 33. haud obscure prodidit; imo etiam in gratiam Judæorum, qui Ve- tus Testamentum non abrogari, sed tantum reno- vari debere, vi hujus oraculi contendunt. Sic enim explicat R. Isaac in Chiffuk cap. 29. cujus Φλυαρίας disjecit Dn. D. Mullerus in Judaismo pag. 726. Nam de novo fœdere agit Propheta, & abrogationem veteris indicat, cum novum promittit. At Grotius de veteri intelligit, ejusque solum renovationem in- digitari vult. Diversum plane fœdus Propheta in- nuit, cum ait, fœdus novum ferire Dominum, non secundum pactum, quod fecit circa eductionem de terra Ægypti in monte Sinai. At Grotius non di- versum pactum, sed solum diversitatem beneficio- rum eductionis istius ex Ægypto & eductionis è Babylone significari vult, quo ceu majori ac admi- rabiliori beneficio prius adumbratum esse falso pu- tat. Nam majus ac mirabilius utique beneficium fuit, multis ac stupendis prodigiis & miraculis, cum stupenda traductione totius populi Israelitici per mare rubrum, & horrenda suffocatione totius ex- ercitus Pharaonici in eodem, conjunctum, libera- tionis ex Ægypto beneficium, quam liberatio Ba- bylone duarum tribuum Israëlis. Neque locus Es. 43, 18. quicquam huc facit, ut doceatur, hanc libe- rationem majorem ac admirabiliorem esse: quia non agit de liberatione à captivitate Babylonica, ut ibidem monuimus. Quomodo adversus Judæos insignis hic locus urgeri possit, videatur Dn. Mul- lerus pag. 673. seqq.

Vers. eod.

ET EGO DOMINATVS SVM EORVM, DICIT DOMINVS.) Vertere licet, Et ego eorum maritus man- sissem. Sed LXX. pro בעלתי, legerunt בחלתי, ideoque verterunt, ἐγὼ ἠμέλησα αὐτῶν. Nihil causæ est, cur hoc im- probemus. Illi me neglexerunt, ego eos vicissim ne- glexi.

Temere ac perverse translatio Græca præfer- tur textui Authentico, neq; aliter legisse LXX. In- terpp. etsi aliter verterunt, docet Buxtorff. Vindic. pag. 675. Neq; causa est deserendi vulgatam versio- nem, quæ Ebræo fonti apprime consonat. Domi- nium autem coactionis intelligitur, quemadmodum B. Lutherus reddidit, cum B. Bugenhagio: Quod explicat Osiander: DOMINATUS SUM EO- RUM, i. e. necesse habui ipsos, tanquam servos, non tanquam filios tractare, propter ipsorum transgressio- nes multiplices, & insignem eorum pervicaciam. Qua περιφράσει designari naturam fœderis antiqui recte observarunt nostri, quod nempe id non modo im- pleri non possit: Quemadmodum ab Israelitis id irritum omne redditum; sed quod etiam cum do- minatu ac coactione conjunctum sit, quia cogit in- vitos ad obsequium. Lex enim Mosis neque im- pleri ab ullo potest perfecte, & ad obedientiam tamen omnes cogit, omnibus obsequium extor- quet sub fulmine maledictionis. Quia non con- fert Spiritum Sanctum, qui libertatis est Spiri- tus. Ideo opera legis, quæ fiunt à non renatis, ab invitis & coactis fiunt; unde opus erat novo fœde- re, quod & remissionem peccatorum afferret, quia lex impleri non poterat, & Spiritum Sanctum con- ferret, ut mandatis divinis obedientiam sponta- neam præstaremus. Sub lege est coactio, pœna, & damnatio; sub gratia est libertas, obedientia, & voluntarius cultus. Quia vero hanc doctrinam de discrimine Veteris ac Novi fœderis ex hoc lo- co illustri & parallelis scripturis, imprimis etiam ex Epistola ad Hebræos, quæ hunc locum prolixe tractat c. 8. & 9. eximie declaravit B. Bugenhagius noster, qui inter primos fuit Evangelicæ doctrinæ è verbo Dei restauratores; non pigebit ejus expli- cationem, utpote solidam, ac luculentam adduce- re, quam tum Papistis, tum etiam sectariis ac Sacra- mentariis opposuit. Hos enim egregiam pœnam sustinere sui contemptus censet, dum Evangelico- rum scripta & doctrinam contemnant, siquidem ostendunt nihil de abolitione legis, quæ per fidem in Christum est, se intelligere, ac ne vocabula qui- dem percipere, ut sciant, quodnam sit vetus, & quodnam novum Testamentum. Quod hic etiam in Grotio videmus. FOEDUS NOVUM: DICENDO NOVUM, inquit ὁ μακαρίτης no- ster, abolet vetus, ut argumentatur etiam Epistola ad Hebræos, quemadmodum & apud homines testamen- tum posterius abrogat prius. Id quod & Jeremias sic declarat verbis Dei; Nam ut erat fœdus, quod pepigi cum patribus ipsorum, quando apprehendi manum ipsorum (quemadmodum apprehenditur manus parvuli, ut ducatur) & eduxi eos ex Ægy- pto, videlicet in monte Sina. Aliud ergo hic est pactum, quam illud vetus. Siquidem illud erat ve- teris hominis, & justitiam ejus exigebat coram Deo, quam ipse non habebat, nec habere potuit, impossibile enim erat per legem mandatorum hominem justifica- ri, ut Paulus docet in actis Apostolorum, & in Episto- lis suis, & ipse jam justificatus per Christum de se conqueritur Rom. 7. &c. Quid ergo ex lege sperares de non justificatis? Promisit quidem Deus, Ero vester Deus, sed addit conditionem legis nobis impossibilem, si manseritis in meis mandatis. Maledictus qui non manserit in omnibus, quæ scripta sunt in libro le- gis, ut supra dictum cap. 30. Hanc maledictionem le- gis & damnationem nostri transtulit in se Christus, & abolevit credentibus, non tantum abolevit ceremo- nias, alioqui, ubi esset remissio peccatorum, imputatio justitiæ, donatio Spiritus Sancti & vitæ æternæ, quæ habemus per CHRISTUM solum, & propter CHRISTUM solum, & in Christo solo, fide ei inseriti & filii Dei facti? Hoc est novum Testamen- tum, sed novis, qui fide & Spiritu Dei innovantur, exuti vetustate literæ, sive legis veteris. Sine hoc Te- stamento vel pacto novo omnes homines, usque ad fi- nem mundi, non solum illi increduli Judæi, manent sub lege, sive Vet. Test. Non enim sub gratia Rom. 3. eti- am si religionem angelorum sibi finxerint, Col. 2. Sic Paulus ait ad Gal. Christum factum sub lege, ut eos qui sub lege erant, redimeret, ut adoptionem filio- rum Dei reciperemus, non jam servi sub lege, sed liberi sub gratia. Et Rom. 8. Quod impossibile erat legi, quia imbecillis erat per carnem, hoc Deus proprio filio misso sub specie carnis peccati, præ- stitit, ac de peccato condemnavit peccatū per car- nem, ut justificatio Legis impleretur in nobis, qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum Spiritum, &c. Vetus Testamentum, sive lex Dei re- velat peccatum & exigit justitiam, Novum autem Testamentum sive pactum, quod est Evangelium, condonat peccatum, & confert justitiam. Illo omnes rei tenentur morte æterna. Hoc omnes absolvuntur, & accipiunt vitam æternam. Illic vetustas literæ occidebat, hic novitas Spiritus vivificat. Non enim Evangelio, ut lege, terrentur conscientiæ, sed consola- tionem accipiunt à DEO æternam. Et sicut lex, ita & legis sacerdotium inutile erat ad purificandum conscientias coram Deo. Habuit quidem placatio- nem, & remissionem peccatorum, sed legalem, id est, externam. Separabantur enim homines, qui con- tra legis præscriptum opere externo peccabant, id est, ut nunc dicimus, excommunicabantur, & rursum vel ablutionibus, vel sacrificiis in lege institutis reci- piebantur in externam illam populi & cultus DEI communionem. Christus vero novi Test. Sacerdos, & Mediator inter Deum, & hominem, vere in conscientia corã Deo pacificat & sanctificat in æternum, ut simus non solum Sanctorum & hominum & angelorum participes, sed etiam consortes divinæ naturæ per i- psum. Hic Christus non est Sacerdos Leviticus, aut legalis, sed sacerdos æternus, in dextera Dei inter- pellans pro nobis, benedictio omnium cognationum terræ, sed secundum ritum Melchisedec, id est, Sacer- dos liber, qui sine lege justificet, & gratis suscipiat pec- catores: Propitiatorium nostrum Rom. 3. Thronus gratiæ Heb. 4. Advocatus apud patrem 1. Joh. 2. qui sedet ad dextram Majestatis in excelsis purgatione peccatorum per semetipsum facta, Heb. 1. Propter Christum lex non habet jus nos accusandi, tantum abest, ut habeat jus damnandi; Propter eum enim non imputatur nobis transgressio legis, id est, pecca- tum, & propter eum omnia nostra sunt accepta Deo. Quicquid legis, aut operum in Scripturis commenda- ri legeris, non intellige placere DEO sine mediatore Christo: sine fide enim impossibile est placere DEO. Hac fiducia in Christum contritorem Capitis Serpen- tis, & benedictionem omnium gentium, olim veteres illi justificati sunt, & hujus novi Testamenti partici- pes facti. Nemo enim unquam aliter justificari po- tuit. Sed obscurius ista tradebat Evangelium: Se- men mulieris conteret caput serpentis; non Lex, aut opus nostrum conteret; in semine tuo, ô Abra- ham, benedicentur cunctæ cognationes terræ, non in lege, aut operibus humanis; ut taceam Sacrificia, & figuras, sive significationes legis in Christum respi- cientes. Prophetæ autem, sive sancti Prædicatores ista clarius declarabant, ut ante dixi de Adam; ma- xime in Psalmis, quod non lege, sed misericordia Dei, quæ est in Christo, salvamur &c. Ut videas unam semper fuisse fidem justificantem coram Deo, etiam apud veteres Patres, quæ & apud nos est. Hinc autem non sequitur vetus & novum Testamentum idem esse, nec differre, nisi in modo tradendi, ut quidam nuper indoctissime scripsit. Hæc gratia hic à Deo promit- titur divulganda, & danda domui Israel, & domui Juda, id est, toti Regno Davidis, id est, Christi, quod est regnum cælorum à Jerusalem per Evangelii prædicationem dilatatum ad omnes gentes. Hæc Bu- genhagius: quæ passim magno Spiritu B. Luthe- rus in scriptis suis aureis exequutus est.

## 31:33
Vers. 33.

I WILL PUT MY LAW IN THEIR INWARD PARTS; AND WILL WRITE IT IN THEIR HEARTS] I will confer such benefits upon them, that they cannot but remember them. But both this passage and that in Ezekiel 11, 19. 36, 26. indeed had their fulfillment in those times after the return, but because it was paving the way for the Gospel, at which time these had a much more eminent effect, through the indubitable revelation of eternal life, and the immense power of the Spirit poured out upon Christians, even those who were among the common people.

Behold the inept corruption of an illustrious text! I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts, that is, I will confer such great benefits upon them that they cannot but remember them. The Prophet is not speaking of a perpetual memory of benefits, but of the inscription of the divine law into hearts; which are as far apart as the whole heaven. He previously taught that the law could not be kept, and that the old covenant had been rendered void: Now, therefore, he promises that he will write the law into their very hearts. On Mount Sinai, the law was written on tablets of stone: Here, therefore, is promised the inscription of the law into our inward parts and into our hearts; which happens when heavenly doctrine is imprinted upon our hearts by the Holy Spirit, and written as if by the finger of God, so that we may attain saving knowledge of GOD, and true faith, which is effective through love, and may order our life according to the law of God, walking not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit. Osiander paraphrases it thus: Formerly I wrote the moral law, the Decalogue, on stone tablets: but it remained on the stones; it did not penetrate into the hearts in such a way that they would embrace that doctrine with a ready mind, and from the heart order their life according to that norm. (For although a particle of the law, from the first creation, remains in the hearts of men, yet it is meager, and the impenitent strive more to extinguish it than to cherish it) but the manner of the New Testament will be far different, says the Lord. For I, through the ministry of the word, will so write the Gospel into the hearts and inward parts of Christians, that they will embrace it most greedily and most closely, and from it will know that I am a most merciful God. And this recognition of my fatherly goodness (which appears in the benefits of Christ) will move Christians to strive as diligently as possible, so that they may not commit anything that does not befit the people of God. Therefore, they will show me such obedience that they will not hesitate to lay down their lives for my sake. For it is not the doctrine of the law, but of the Gospel, that regenerates the hearts of men, so that they may obey the Lord from the heart. Furthermore, if these promises have attained their effect through the revelation of eternal life and the immense power of the Holy Spirit poured out upon Christians, how will that promise be explained concerning the memory of the benefits of GOD? These are disparate and unconnected expositions. Moreover, there lurks here a Pelagian-Socinian sore, namely, that in ancient times the promise of eternal life was not made, and that the gift of the Holy Spirit was reserved for the times of the New Testament: then that the revelation of eternal life alone induces us sufficiently to the observation of the precepts of God: which postulates we have elsewhere refuted in the Socinians.

AND I WILL BE TO THEM A GOD, AND THEY SHALL BE TO ME A PEOPLE] I, as King, will protect them; they, as to a King, will obey me; see above 7, 23. 11, 4. 24, 7. below 32, 38.

The interpretation of this significant promise is too diluted, for God does not promise protection, but when he promises that he will be the God of someone, he pledges whatever can be expected from God: the remission of sins, grace, righteousness, indwelling, communion with himself, glory, and eternal blessedness, as is evident from the formula of the promise in the Sacrament of circumcision in Gen. 17 and Christ's explanation in Matt. 22, v. 31, and Rev. 21, 7. Nor do some warn without cause that something peculiar, and proper to the New Testament, is promised in the words: I WILL BE THEIR GOD. Namely, that there is a looking toward that unique mode, that the Son wills to be our God through the incarnation, by which he was made Immanuel, GOD with us, Isa. 7, v. 14, chap. 8, v. 8. See D. Muller, loc. cit., p. 677.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

DABO LEGEM MEAM IN VISCERIBUS EO- RVm; AC IN CORDE EORVM SCRIBAM EAM] Tanta in eos beneficiu conferam, ut eorum non possint nõ meminisse. Sed & hic locus & ille apud Ezechielem 11, 19. 36, 26. suum quidem implementum, temporibus illis post reditum habuit, sed quod viam sternebat Evangelio, quo tempore hæc multo eminentiorem effectum habuere, per revelationem non dubitandam vitæ æternæ, & vim ingen- tem Spiritus super Christianos, etiam qui in plebe erant, effusam.

En ineptam textus illustris depravationem! Dabo legem meam in visceribus eorum, & in corde eorum scribam eam, id est, tanta in eos beneficia con- feram, ut eorum non possint non meminisse. Non de beneficiorum perenni memoria, sed de legis divinæ in corda inscriptione loquitur Propheta; quæ toto cœlo distant. Legem servari non potuisse, pactum vetus irritum redditum esse, antea docuit: Nunc ergo promittit, legem sese in corda ipsorum inscri- pturum. In monte Sinai lex in tabulis saxeis inscri- pta fuit: Hic ergo promittitur legis inscriptio in vi- scera nostra, & in corda; quæ fit, cum doctrina cœ- lestis per Spiritum Sanctum cordibus nostris im- primitur, & veluti digito Dei inscribitur, ut cogni- tionem salutarem DEI, & veram fidem, quæ per charitatem efficax est, consequamur, ac secundum legem Dei vitam nostram instituamus, ambulantes non secundum carnem, sed secundum Spiritum. Osiand. ita παραφράζει: Olim scripsi legem moralem Decalogum in tabulis lapideis: sed ea mansit in lapi- dibus; non ita penetravit in corda, ut prompto animo eam doctrinam amplecterentur, & ex animo vitam suam juxta eam normam instituerent. (Etsi enim particula legis, ex prima creatione, manet in cordi- bus hominum, tamen ea exigua est, & magis extin- guere, quam fovere eam student impœnitentes) sed longe erit alia ratio novi Testamenti, inquit Dominus. Ego enim per ministerium verbi ita inscribam Evangelium cordibus & visceribus Christianorum, ut illud avidissime & arctissime sint amplexuri, & ex eo cognituri, quod sim Deus clementissimus. Et hæc agnitio paternæ meæ bonitatis (quæ apparet in be- neficiis Christi) permovebit Christianos, ut quam di- ligentissime sint elaboraturi, ne quid committant, quod populum Dei non deceat. Itaq́; talem mihi ob- edientiam præstabunt, ut etiam vitam mea causa pro- fundere minime dubitent. Non enim legis, sed Ev- angelii doctrina hominum corda regenerat, ut ex ani- mo Domino obediant. Porro si per revelationem vitæ æternæ, & vim ingentem Spiritus Sancti super Christianos effusam hæc promissa effectum suum consequuta sunt, quomodo de beneficiorum DEI memoria illa promissio explicabitur? Sunt hæ ἐκ- θέσεις disparatæ, & inconnectiles. Cæterum latet hic ὕπουλον Pelagio-Socinianum, quod nempe pri- scis temporibus promissio vitæ æternæ facta non sit, quodque donum Spiritus Sancti reservatum fuerit temporibus Novi Testamenti: tum quod revela- tio vitæ æternæ sola ad observationem præcepto- rum Dei nos satis inducat: quæ postulata in Soci- nianis alias profligavimus.

ET EGO ERO EIS IN DEUM, ET IPSI MI- HI ERUNT IN POPULUM] Ego ut Rex eos prote- gam; illi mihi, ut Regi, parebunt: supra 7, 23. II, 4. 24, 7. infra 32, 38.

Nimis diluta est interpretatio insignis promif- sionis, non enim protectionem Deus promittit, sed cum se Deum alicujus fore pollicetur, quicquid à Deo expectari potest, spondet: remissionem pecca- torum, gratiam, justitiam, inhabitationem, commu- nionem cum ipso, gloriam & beatitudinem æternam ut ex formula promissionis in Sacramento circum- cisionis Gen. 17. & explicatione Christi Matth. 22. v. 31. & Apoc. 21, 7. constat. Neq; temere monent nonnulli, hoc loco peculiare quid, & Novo Testa- mento proprium, verbis: EGO ERO DEUS EORUM, promitti. Quod nempe respiciatur modus ille μονότροπος, quod Filius Deus noster esse velit per ἐνσάρκωσιν, quo factus est Immanuel, DEUS nobiscum Esa. 7. v. 14. cap. 8. vers. 8. Vide D. Mullerum l. c. p. 677.

## 31:34
AND NO MORE SHALL EVERY MAN TEACH HIS NEIGHBOR, AND EVERY MAN HIS BROTHER, SAYING: KNOW THE LORD] The sense is: there will be no need for one to urge another to show reverence to GOD. Which the Hebrews often signify by ידע.

FOR ALL SHALL KNOW ME] All will worship and revere me spontaneously, because of such immense benefits.

Grotius takes this concerning the spontaneous worship of God, that there will be no need for mutual excitation, so that one might urge another. But it is a matter of the knowledge of God, not of worship alone. Nor is any affection of worship attended to here, such as the voluntary, or that one should spontaneously revere God without another's urging. But the universal education of all is promised. That all are to be taught of God, as Christ teaches in John 6, 45, from the prophecy of Isaiah chap. 55, 33. By which the abundance and fullness of the time of illumination and knowledge of the New Testament is insinuated, just as it was predicted in Isa. 11, 9, that the earth would be full of knowledge. Yet the medium of the knowledge of the Lord, the ministry of the word, is not removed here when it is said: no more shall a man teach his neighbor: but the knowledge of all the faithful sufficient for salvation is indicated: that they are not rude in knowledge, and needy of information in those things which are necessary to be known for salvation, but that all the faithful are sufficiently instructed; which, however, they will not attain immediately from GOD, without the doctrine of the word or ministry. For that is not looked at here, where only the 'that', that all are to know God, is defined, not the 'how', in what manner, or from where, whether by immediate illumination of God, or by means of the information of the word and ministry! Jeremiah does not say here, nor does he deny, says Bugenhagen on page 365, by what medium God is to do this, namely, through the preaching of the Gospel, and therefore against those despisers of the ministry of the Gospel he said earlier, 'Still there shall be heard in the land of Judah and in its cities, The Lord bless thee there,' etc. Likewise elsewhere concerning the New Testament, 'I will give them pastors,' etc. So also Joel says: 'And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy,' etc. Now, lying Prophet, say that the holy Prophets predict that in the New Testament there will be no public preaching. The Devil himself speaks out of you. For Christ ascended on high for this reason, that he might give gifts to men, Apostles, Prophets, Evangelists, Doctors, Pastors, Eph. 4. But what have we to do with that insanity and blasphemy of the most vain men! God alone gives his law, that is, the Spirit into hearts, but through the preaching of the Gospel. For thus He ordained for His Church, as Paul says in Ephesians 4. Those ignorant of the faith are in need of the doctrine of God through the word of the Gospel, because they do not yet believe, or possess the Spirit; but those who know are in need of exhortation and consolation, and of defense against heretics and fanatical spirits, so that they may persist in the word of God, grow in the knowledge of Christ, and become perpetually stronger in faith; and yet who teaches, who exhorts, reproves, consoles, and comforts, if not God alone by His Spirit, but through the ministry of the word? For the Spirit is effective in us through the word. This is what Paul clearly says against the fanatical enemies of the Spirit, interpreting this passage of Jeremiah in 2 Corinthians 3. You, he says, are the Epistle of Christ, (that is, written by Christ our Prince, of whom we are the scribes and legates) written by our ministry, not with ink, (as is the case among men, and just as both sacred and profane things are written outside of men onto papers; for here you would foolishly say, forsooth, that Paul never wrote with ink) but with the Spirit of the living God (you see that Paul and the Evangelical preachers, by the preaching of the Gospel, write the Epistle of Christ with the Spirit of the living God. For God Himself gives the Spirit and faith, and no one else: but through the ministry of the word, through which we are also absolved from sins. Whence some They explain these things comparatively, that not, as in the time of the Old Testament, do the nations have need to seek saving doctrine from the Jews, but that any peoples whatsoever are to have the knowledge of God under the New Testament. This sense the Ministry of Lübeck, Hamburg, and Lüneburg follows against the new-fangled Prophets in the detailed Report §. 786. This explanation is rightly joined by Osiander: There will not be a small number of those who believe in me, Jesus Christ: but all, as many as have embraced the Gospel by faith, will have a true and saving knowledge of me: so that even children are to believe in me: (This text does not abolish the external ministry of the word, as the Enthusiasts imagine: as if we could obtain the true knowledge of God outside the ministry of the word of God. To this opinion Paul perniciously opposes himself in Rom. 10, affirming that faith comes from hearing: But the magnitude of the knowledge of Christ in the New Testament is compared with that which was in the Old Testament. For today an infant child understands the mystery of our redemption through Christ more explicitly than perhaps some one of the chief priests understood it formerly in the Old Testament. And it is notable that even to the least (as are the most tender infants) in Christianity, this knowledge of Christ is attributed in this place, which is nothing other than faith in Christ. Finally, this knowledge of God is not opposed to the ministry, through which God informs, but to human doctrines, nay, even to the law itself, as the blessed Bugenhagen has learnedly taught. What is said here, no one shall teach another, or brother his brother, know the Lord, is not said about the abolishing of the ministers of the Gospel, as Satan wishes in his Prophets. For even the Lord Jesus himself preached not only to the unbelieving, that they might be converted, but also to those who had already believed and had received that new covenant, that is, to his own disciples. Similarly, it is also written about the faithful in the Acts of the Apostles: They were persevering in the doctrine of the Apostles, etc. These, however, had received the Holy Spirit: thus also Paul preaches and writes even to those who had already believed. And we cannot lack such a ministry, unless we wish to be without consolation, without the word of God, and the Spirit. But properly this is said against human doctrines inventing new opinions, worships, and observances, whence the Lord might be known and God pleased; and against the boasters of the Spirit, who teach their own dreams, not the word of God, and thus even against Moses and the Law this is said, which indeed demands the knowledge of God, but does not provide it. No one under the servitude of the Law, much less under the servitude of human traditions, knows the Lord. For to know the Lord truly is to believe him to be our Father, to whom no one comes, unless he apprehends the New Testament or Covenant, the promise of grace in Christ Jesus, our Lord, just as he himself says: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no one comes to the Father except through me: Likewise, this is eternal life, O Father, that they may know you the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ. This knowledge of God no man teaches, but God alone by his Spirit gives and writes in the hearts and minds of men, although through the word preached or written, so that all may know him who have received from him the law of the Spirit written in the heart, from the least even to the greatest, that is, as much the people as the preachers, or rather as much those gifted with small faith as those with great.

Verse of the same.

FOR I WILL BE MERCIFUL TO THEIR INIQUITY, AND I WILL REMEMBER THEIR SIN NO MORE.] The sense is: because I have shown (by such great benefits, namely) that I have granted them forgiveness of their crimes and do not wish to pursue them further.

The sum of the New Testament is comprehended here, consisting in the gracious remission of sins, as most interpreters have observed, with the Apostle preceding in Heb. 8. The gloss of Grotius, however, is hitherto unheard of, as if the matter were only about the temporal remission of punishment and bodily benefits, by which God demonstrated to the Israelites that he had granted forgiveness of crimes. It is not about the Israelites alone, but about the Church designated by the name of Israel and Judah, and thus all the faithful, especially however under the times of the New Testament, where the knowledge of God will be more illustrious. Nor is the forgiveness of crimes to be inferred from bodily benefits, but the remission of sins is directly promised, and the distinction between the Old and New Testament is established in this, that the Old Testament indeed brings condemnation on account of sins; but the New truly exhibits the remission of sins and grace. Therefore Christ is the mediator of the New Testament, as the Apostle teaches in Heb. 9, 15, so that by his death interceding for the redemption of those transgressions which were under the former Testament, those who have been called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance. The Jews themselves refer these things to the times of the Messiah, and explain them concerning the law or the new doctrine of the Messiah in the book Siphra, which is also called Torath Koharim, and in Midrash Koheleth Eccles. 2, 2. see Pug. Fidei part. 3. distinct. 3. c. 21, 1. & 6. The author of Sepher Ikkarim lib. 3. c. 19. reports these things from the Midrash: And would that he might kiss me with the kiss of his mouth Cant. 1. they said, that was not then, but hereafter according to that of Jer. 31, 31. 32. 33. Behold it has been explained to you, that our doctors judge that all Israelites will hereafter receive another doctrine, as before, from the mouth of God immediately, namely in the time of the Messiah: R. Moses Nachmanides teaches in Deut. sect. נצבים Man will be restored at that time, namely in the days of the Messiah, to that state in which he was before the first man sinned, that is, what the Scripture says Jer. 31, 31. 32. 33. Maimonides in his Talmudic summary tract. on Kings, teaches concerning the times of the Messiah: That hidden and profound things will be open to all.

Latin:

ET NON DOCEBIT ULTRA VIR PROXI- MVM SVVM, ET VIR FRATREM SVVM DI- CENS: COGNOSCE DOMINVM] Sensus est: non opus erit, ut alter alterum moneat ad reverentiam DEO ex- hibendam. Quod sæpe Hebræi per ידע significant.

OMNES ENIM COGNOSCENT ME] Omnes sponte me colent, ac reverebuntur, ob tam ingentia bene- facta.

De spontaneo cultu Dei accipit Grotius, quod opus non sit futurum excitatione mutua, ut alter alterum moneat. At de cognitione Dei, non de solo cultu, agitur. Neque hic ulla cultus affectio, τὸ ἑκούσιον puta, vel quod sponte sine alterius monitu quis Deum revereatur, attenditur. Sed universalis omnium eruditio promittitur. Quod omnes futu- ri sint θεοδίδακτοι, ut Christus docet Joh. 6, 45. è vaticinio Esaiæ cap. 55, 33. Quo illuminationis & cognitionis Novi Testamenti tempore ubertas, & plenitudo insinuatur, uti Esa. 11, 9. prædictum, ter- ram plenam fore cognitione. Neque tamen hic tol- litur medium cognitionis Domini, verbi ministe- rium, cum dicitur; non docebit ultra vir proximum suum: sed fidelium omnium sufficiens ad salutem notitia indicatur: quod non rudes sint notitiæ, & indigi in iis, quæ ad salutem cognitu sunt necessa- ria, informatione, sed sufficienter instructi omnes fideles sint; quam vero non immediate à DEO, sine verbi aut ministerii doctrina, consequentur. Id enim hic non respicitur, ubi solum τὸ ὅτι, quod Deum cognituri sint omnes, definitur, non τὸ πῶς, quomodo, aut unde, num immediata Dei illumina- tione, an mediante verbi & ministerii informatione! Non dicit hic Jeremias, aut negat, inquit Bugenha- gius pag. 365. quo medio Deus hoc sit facturus, videli- cet per prædicationem Evangelii, atque adeo contra istos ministerii Evangelii contemptores ante dixit, Adhuc audietur in terra Juda & in civitatibus ejus, Dominus benedicat ibi &c. Item alibi de Novo Te- stamento, Dabo eis pastores &c. Sic & Joel dicit; Et prophetabunt filii vestri, & filiæ vestræ, &c. nunc Mendax Propheta, & dic sanctos Prophetas prædi- cere, quod in Novo Testamento non erit publica præ- dicatio. Diabolus ipse ex te loquitur. Nam Christus propterea ascendit in altum, ut daret dona homini- bus, Apostolos, Prophetas, Evangelistas, Docto- res, Pastores, Eph. 4. Sed quid nobis cum illa insa- nia & blasphemia vanissimorum hominum! Solus Deus dat legem suam, id est, Spiritum in corda, sed per prædicationem Evangelii. Sic enim ordinavit suæ Ecclesiæ, ut Paulus Ephes. 4. dicit. Ignorantes fidei indigent doctrina Dei per verbum Evangelii, quia nondum credunt, sive habent Spiritum; scientes au- tem indigente exhortatione & consolatione, & contra Hæreticos & phanaticos Spiritus defensione, ut persi- stant in verbo Dei, crescant in cognitione Christi, & fide perpetuo fiant fortiores; Et tamen quis docet, quis exhortatur, arguit, consolatur, confortat, nisi solus Deus suo Spiritu, sed per ministerium verbi? Spiritus enim est in nobis efficax per verbum. Id quod ma- nifeste dicit Paulus contra hostes Phanaticos Spiritus, hunc Jeremiæ locum interpretatus 2. Cor. 3. Vos, in- quit, estis Epistola Christi, (id est, à Christo Principe nostro scripta, cujus nos notarii ac legati sumus) mi- nisterio nostro à nobis conscripta, non atramento, (ut apud homines sit, & quemadmodum & Sacra & prophana extra homines scribuntur in chartas; Hic enim stulte diceres, scilicet, Paulum nunquam atra- mento scripsisse) Sed Spiritu Dei viventis (vides quod Paulus & Evangelici Prædicatores, prædica- tione Evangelii scribunt Epistolam Christi, Spiritu Dei viventis. Nam Deus ipse donat Spiritum & fidem, & nullus alius: sed per ministerium verbi, per quod etiam absolvimur à peccatis. Unde nonnulli συγκριτικῶς hæc explicant, quod non, ut tempo- re Veteris Testamenti, gentes à Judæis doctrinam salutarem expetere opus habeant, sed quod quivis populi cognitionem Dei habituri sint sub Novo Testamento. Quem sensum adversus novellos Prophetas Ministerium Lubecense, Hamburgen- se, & Lunæburgense im ausführlichen Bericht §. 786. sequitur. Quæ explicatio utraq; conjun- gitur recte ab Osiandro: Non erit exiguus nume- rus eorum, qui in me, Jesum Christum credant: sed omnes, quoquot Evangelion fide fuerint amplexi, habebunt veram & salutarem mei agnitionem: ita ut pueri etiam in me sint credituri: (Hic textus non tollit externum verbi ministerium, ut Enthusiastæ opinantur: quasi veram Dei agnitionem extra mi- nisterium verbi Dei consequi possemus. Cui opini- oni pernitiose repugnat Paulus Rom. 10. affirmans fidem esse ex auditu: Sed confertur magnitudo cogni- tionis Christi in Novo Testamento, cum ea, quæ fuit in Veteri Testamento. Etenim hodie puer infans explicatius intelligit Mysterium redemptionis nostræ per Christum, quam olim in Veteri Testamento, for- tasse aliquis ex præcipuis Sacerdotibus intellexit. Et notabile est, quod etiam minimis, (ut sunt tenerrimi infantes) in Christianismo, tribuitur hoc loco agni- tio Christi, quæ nihil aliud est, quam fides in Chri- stum. Denique non opponitur hæc notitia Dei ministerio, per quod informat Deus, sed humanis doctrinis, imo ipsi etiam legi, ut scite docuit B. Bu- genhagius. Quod hic dicitur, non docebit aliquis alium, aut frater fratrem, cognosce Dominum, non dicitur de abrogandis Evangelii ministris, ut Satan vult in suis Prophetis. Nam & ipse Dominus Je- sus prædicavit non solum incredulis, ut converteren- tur, sed etiam iis, qui jam crediderant, & illud pa- ctum novum susceperant, hoc est, discipulis suis. Si- militer & de fidelibus scriptum est in Actis Aposto- lorum; Erant perseverantes in doctrina Apostolo- rum, &c. Hi tamen Spiritum Sanctum acceperant: sic & Paulus prædicat & scribit etiam iis, qui jam crediderant. Et nos tali ministerio carere non pos- sumus, nisi velimus esse absq; consolatione, absq; ver- bo Dei, & Spiritu. Sed proprie hoc dicitur contra doctrinas humanas fingentes novas opiniones, cultus, & observationes, unde cognoscatur Domi- nus, & placetur Deus; & contra jactatores Spiri- tus, qui sua somnia, non verbum Dei docent, atq; adeo etiam contra Mosen & Legem hoc dicitur, quæ exigit quidem cognitionem Dei, sed non præstat. Ne- mo sub servitute Legis, multo minus sub servitute traditionum humanarum cognoscit Dominum. Nam Dominum vere cognoscere, est eum credere, esse Patrem nostrum, quo nemo pervenit, nisi apprehen- dat Nov. Testam. sive Pactum, promissionem gratiæ in Christo Jesu, Domino nostro, quemadmodum ipse dicit; Ego sum via, veritas & vita: nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me: Item, hæc est vita æterna, ô Pa- ter, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, & quem misisti Jesum Christum. Hanc cognitionem Dei nullus homo docet, sed solus Deus suo Spiritu dat & scribit in corda & mentes hominum, licet per ver- bum prædicatum vel scriptum, ut cognoscant ipsum omnes, qui acceperint ab eo legem Spiritus in cor scriptam, à minimo usque ad maximum, id est, tam populi, quam prædicatores, sive potius tam parva fide, quam magna donati.

Vers eod.

QVIA PROPITIABOR INIQVITATI EO- RVM, ET PECCATI EORVM NON MEMORA- BOR AMPLIUS.] Sensus est: quia ostendi, (tantis nem- pe benefactis) me veniam dedisse ipsis criminum neque ul- tra ea velle exsequi.

Summa hic comprehenditur Novi Testamen- ti, consistens in gratiosa peccatorum remissione, ut præeunte Apostolo Ebr. 8. Interpretes plerique observarunt. Glossa autem Grotii hactenus in- audita est, quasi de temporali solum pœnæ remissione, & corporalibus beneficiis res sit, quibus demonstravit Deus Israëlitis, se veniam criminum dedisse. Non de Israëlitis solum sermo est, sed de Ecclesia Israelis & Iudæ nomine designata, adeoq; fidelibus omnibus, imprimis tamen sub Novi Testamenti tempora, ubi illustrior erit Dei cognitio. Neque ex cor- poralibus beneficiis colligenda venia criminum in- digitatur, sed directe remissio peccatorum promitti- tur ac discrimen in eo Veteris & Novi Testamenti constituitur, quod vetus Testamentum quidem condemnationem ob peccata adferat; Novum vero remissionem peccatorum & gratiam exhibeat. Ideo Christus Novi Testamenti, docente Apostolo Ebr. 9, 15. mediator est, ut morte intercedente in redemptio- nem earum prævaricationum, quæ erant sub priori Testamento, repromissionem accipiant, qui voca- ti sunt, æternæ hæreditatis. Judæi ipsi referunt hæc ad tempora Messiæ, & de lege, vel doctrina nova Messiæ explicant in libro Siphra, qui etiam Torath Koharim dicitur, & in Midrasch Koheleth Eccles. 2, 2. vid. Pug. Fidei part. 3. distinct. 3. c. 21, 1. & 6. Au- tor Sepher Ikkarim lib. 3. c. 19. è Midrasch hæc re- fert: Et utinam osculetur me osculo oris sui Cant. 1. dixerunt, id jam non fuit, sed posthac juxta illud Jer. 31, 31. 32. 33. Ecce explicatum tibi est, censere docto- res nostros, omnes Israelitas posthæc accepturos doctri- nam alteram, ut prius, ex ore Dei immediate, tempo- re nimirum Messiæ: docet R. Moses Nachmanides in Deut. sect. נצבים Restituetur homo illo tempore, nempe diebus Messiæ, in eum statum, in quo erat an- tequam peccaret primus homo, hoc est, quod dicit Scri- ptura Jer. 31, 31. 32. 33. Maimonides in summa sua Thalmudica tract. de Regibus, de temporibus Mes- siæ docet: Res occultas & profundas apertas fore omnibus.

Verse 35.

WHO TURBLES THE SEA, AND ITS WAVES SOUND] That is, by whose troubling the waves of the sea resound,

Latin:

Vers. 35.

QVI TVRBAT MARE, ET SONANT FLV- CTVS EJVS] Id est, quo turbante maris fluctus inso- nant,

## 31:36
Verse 36.

IF THESE LAWS SHALL FAIL BEFORE ME] If that whole order of nature shall have ceased, then that also shall come to pass. THEN SHALL THE SEED OF ISRAEL ALSO CEASE] This is the absolute decree of God, and as Paul speaks, ἀμετα- μέλητον, that there may always be, and be known distinctly from others, a great multitude of Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

SI DEFECERINT LEGES ISTÆ CORAM ME] Si totus ille ordo naturæ cessaverit, tunc & illud fiet. TVNC ET SEMEN ISRAEL DEFICIET] Hoc est decretum Dei absolutum, & ut Paulus loquitur, ἀμετα- μέλητον, ut semper & sit, & cognoscatur distincte ab aliis magna Israelitarum multitudo.

## 31:37
Vers. 37.

IF THE HEAVENS ABOVE CAN BE MEASURED] Those heavens which are above the stars. AND THE FOUNDATIONS OF THE EARTH SEARCHED OUT BENEATH] The innermost bowels of the earth. AND I WILL ALSO CAST OFF ALL THE SEED OF ISRAEL FOR ALL THAT THEY HAVE DONE] This God plainly denies that He will ever do. For He wishes to punish the sins of the Jews in such a way that He still wishes some of them always to survive.

These things are in favor of the Jewish nation, as if nothing else were promised than the preservation of the Israelites, so that some great multitude of them, distinct from others, might always survive. The Jews therefore have reason to congratulate themselves on this advocate. But what kind of singular benefit is this, that some from the Jewish nation should survive, who, as exiles and outcasts, desperate and excluded from the Church of God, wander throughout the world! For this is no other than their state, truly most unhappy, so that it would be better for them not to be, or to be born, than to survive for this unhappiness, Matt. 26, 14. But the whole prophecy cries out that these things are not to be understood precisely of the Israelites according to the flesh, but of the Church of God. To this, therefore, is promised perpetual preservation in these lands. That the holy seed shall never be wanting to God it comes to pass, the Church will never completely fail. Bugenhagen rightly embraced it: Israel, he says, has been led away, Judah is to be led away into captivity. Therefore, they say, will the whole race of Israel perish? The Lord answers: No, but in the last time I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and I will give you in your land Christ, the new Testament, the salvation of the whole world. This is the sum of this whole chapter, as if God were saying: I will always have a people of Israel, even in captivity, and after captivity, from Jews and Gentiles, just as Paul looks to Israel according to faith, and the children of Abraham Gal. 6. Rom. 9. And yet God also preserved carnal Israel until Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

SI MENSVRARI POTVERINT CŒLI SVR- SVM] Illi cœli, qui supra astra sunt. ET FVNDAMENTA TERRÆ DEORSVM] In- tima terræ viscera. ET EGO ABJICIAM VNIVERSVM SEMEN ISRAEL PROPTER OMNIA QVÆ FECERVNT] Hoc Deus negat plane se unquam facturum. Ita enim vult punire Judæorum peccata, ut tamen aliquos eorum semper velit superesse.

Hæc in favorem gentis Judaicæ, quasi nihil aliud promittatur, quam Israelitarum conservatio, ut semper aliqua magna eorum supersit, ab aliis di- stincta multitudo. Gratulari ergo sibi de hoc ad- vocato habent Judæi. At quid hoc est beneficii sin- gularis, superesse aliquos è gente Judæa, qui exules & extorres, desperabundi, & exclusi ab Ecclesia Dei per orbem errent! Hic enim non alius ipsorum sta- tus est, sane infelicissimus, ut præstaret ipsos non esse, aut nasci, quam ad hanc infelicitatem superesse Matth. 26, 14. Non autem hæc de Israelitis secun- dum carnem præcise intelligenda esse, sed de Eccle- sia Dei, universum vaticinium clamitat. Huic ergo promittitur perpetua conservatio in his terris. Quod nunquam sanctum semen Deo defuturum fit, nunquam Ecclesia penitus defectura. Recte Bügenhagius illam complexus est: Israël, inquit, est abductus, Iuda est abducendus in captivitatem. Ergo, inquiunt, peribit totum genus Israel? Respon- det Dominus; Non, sed in novissimo tempore Ero Deus cunctis cognationibus Israël, & dabo vobis in terra vestra Christum, novum Testamentum, salutem to- tius mundi. Hæc est summa totius hujus capitis, quasi dicat Deus; Semper habebo populum Israël, etiam in captivitate, & post captivitatem, ex Iudæis & gentibus, quemadmodum Paulus Israelem secun- dum fidem respicit, & filios Abrahæ Gal. 6. Rom. 9. Et tamen etiam Deus carnalem Israëlem servavit usque ad Christum.

FROM THE TOWER OF HANANEEL, ) He describes accurately the whole circuit of the city. The Tower of Hananeel is on the southern side, Nehem. 3, 1. compare with this place the other in Zech. 14, 10.

AS FAR AS THE CORNER GATE] Which is between the East and the North in the portion of Benjamin 2. Kings 14, 13.

VSQUE AD PORTAM ANGULI] Qui inter O- rientem & Septentrionem in parte Benjamini 2. Reg. 14, 13.

## 31:39
Vers. 39.

AND IT SHALL GO FORTH BEYOND THE MEASURING LINE IN HIS SIGHT UPON THE HILL GAREB] He has placed 'norma' here for a line, as elsewhere. The hill Gareb was to the north, but towards the west, so called because lepers used to stay there.

AND IT SHALL CIRCLE GOATHA] The Chaldean says it was a round citadel, perhaps so called because the ascent to it was laborious, from יגע which the Greeks translate as κοπιᾶν and μοχθεῖν: it was to the west and south.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

ET EXIBIT ULTRA NORMA MENSURÆ IN CONSPECTU EJUS SUPER COLLEM GAREB] Nor- mam hic posuit pro linea, ut & alibi. Collis Gareb erat ad septentrionem, sed occasum versus, ita dictus, quod ibi se tenerent leprosi.

ET CIRCVIBIT GOATHA] Arcem rotundam ait fuisse Chaldæus, forte ita dictam quod laboriosus illuc esset ascensus à יגע quod κοπιᾶν & μοχθεῖν vertunt Græ- ci: ea fuit ad occasum & meridiem.

## 31:40
V. 40. AND ALL THE VALLEY OF DEAD BODIES AND OF ASHES] That is, according to the Chaldean interpreter, where the greatest part of those who were with Sennacherib had fallen. That is the very valley of Tophet, in which those sacrificed to Moloch were turned to ashes. Isa. 30, v. 33. This region approaches from the west closer to the south.

AND THE WHOLE REGION OF DEATH] The Greeks retained the Hebrew word השדמות as ἀσαρημώθ. Jerome reads השדמות and derives it from שדה and מות, of which the former signifies region, the latter death. Aquila translates it προάστια, thinking, I suppose, of suburban vines, which are called שדמות. But the Chaldean [translates it as] aqueducts, from the two particles and ש, from רמה and ש רמות, which is to cast. He seems to understand the aqueducts made by Hezekiah.

AS FAR AS THE BROOK CEDRON] Which is nearest to the valley of Tophet.

AND AS FAR AS THE CORNER OF THE EASTERN HORSE GATE] The Chaldean: to the corner of the gate of the Royal stadium, which is to the East. Here the designation returns from the south to the east. Concerning this Horse gate see Neh. 3, 28.

HOLY TO THE LORD] All these places will resound with the praises of God.

IT SHALL NOT BE PLUCKED UP AND SHALL NOT BE DESTROYED ANY MORE FOREVER.] that is, the city will stand for a long time after it has been restored.

Grotius understands everything as referring to the city and the material structure. But the boundaries which the Lord placed here do not fit at first. Grotius indeed attempts to adapt them: but yet everything does not fit in the least. For the Prophet adds, as our Bugenhagius observes, other places outside Jerusalem, such as the hill Gareb and Goath, then also the valley of dead bodies and of ashes, and the whole region or field of death, by which words he signifies Tophet and Gehenna, as far as the brook Kidron, which is a place known even from the Gospel, cf. 2 Kings 1. He says therefore, (so Bugenhagius continues) the city of Jerusalem will indeed now be laid waste by the Babylonians, but it will be rebuilt, as foretold, after the Babylonian captivity. But when the new covenant has been published, through the man whom a woman encompassed, through the crusher of the serpent's head, your Messiah, and the law of God has been written in hearts, sin having been abolished, that is, when the kingdom of the Messiah has come, to which all nations will flow, then there will be a far different Jerusalem. Much more majestic, which will extend and be dilated to the North and to the West, and to all parts of the world, so that places which are now outside Jerusalem may be inside Jerusalem. Read Zech. 2. Do not therefore fear: The people of Israel will be multiplied, and the holy city, or the city of GOD will be greatly dilated, and the holy city and the Sanctuary will be so established by God that it can never be broken and laid waste forever, as it will now be laid waste by the Babylonians. By which words he manifestly describes the dilation of the kingdom of Christ beginning in Judea, but with a carnal description before carnal men. For in the Jerusalem and temple that will be built after the captivity, there did not remain afterwards a stone upon a stone, according to the prophecy of Christ, nor was that Jerusalem ever so dilated. But the Jerusalem which is above is our mother Gal. 4. Heb. 12. to which all nations flow, and dwell Ps. 87. etc. Jerusalem will therefore be wider now than the earthly one ever was or will be. Now before, God was known only in Judea. But now they will come (Matt. 8.) from the east and from the west, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. It will be holy to the Lord, that is, this whole thing will be separated and sanctified to the Lord. Namely, the kingdom of God in Christ; this will not be laid waste, nor will it be violated forever, which cannot be said of the earthly city. This is the eternal kingdom of Christ promised to us in the Prophets and exhibited through the Gospel.

Other interpreters have also observed this: Maldonatus says, Gareb and Goath were two hills outside the city. Therefore, he signifies that it is to be amplified beyond the ancient boundaries, as above verse 24 and Isa. ch. 55, 2. And mystically, the Catholic Church will be much more ample than the Synagogue was; Because he will have dominion from sea to sea Ps. 72, 8. and it extends its branches as far as the sea, and its shoots as far as the river Ps. 79, 12. Verse 40. THE VALLEY of dead bodies. For that was outside Jerusalem, which is therefore believed to have been called the valley of dead bodies, as R. Solomon and Jonathan say, because the corpses of the Assyrians had fallen there, when the angel struck them, 2 Kings 19, 35. And the ashes, והרשן and the ashes, that is, as far as the valley of ashes. Which, as some of the Hebrews think, was so called because the ashes of the sacrifices were thrown into it. Others as far as the valley ודשן of fatness, that is, of olives. Jonathan [says] aqueducts, which made the land fertile. And the whole region of death. Thus our interpreters think the place of punishment was called, such as Montfaucon is at Paris. But Jerome himself confesses that he made two words out of one, השר־מות, which as R. David notes is written with ר and read with ד, and R. Solomon interprets it as all the plains, all the regions as far as the valley of Kidron. There is much mention of this valley in the scriptures: it was situated outside the gate which they called the sheep gate, and it extended as far as the mount of olives, as appears 2 Kings 15, 23. This is Maldonatus.

Furthermore, since all those things are said to be holy to the Lord, it is signified not only that the whole of Jerusalem will resound with the praises of God; but the holiness of the Church, shadowed forth by Jerusalem, is predicted. For what, shall we admit that Jerusalem was ever entirely holy? It is manifest therefore that this is an encomium of the Church, which is properly the communion of Saints. Finally, when the promise is made to it: IT SHALL NOT BE PLUCKED UP, NOR DESTROYED ANY MORE FOREVER: its perennial preservation is hinted at. Which notable promise is perversely corrupted by Grotius: as if only a long-lasting preservation were designated. The words of the Prophet imply perpetuity, not long duration. And therefore they openly teach that these things cannot be accepted concerning the earthly Jerusalem. For that was so overturned by the Romans that not even a stone was left upon a stone Matt. 24. It must therefore be understood of the Church of Christ, which is built upon the rock Christ, against which the gates of hell will not prevail Matt. 16, 17. And these things concerning Chapter 31.

CHAP.

Latin:

V. 40. ET OMNEM VALLEM CADAVERUM ET CINERIS] Id est, Chaldæo interprete, ubi maxima pars ceciderat eorum, qui erant cum Sennacheribo. Ea ipsa est vallis Tophet, in qua Molocho immolati cinefiebant. Esa. 30, v. 33. Hæc regio ab occasu propius ad meridiem accedit.

ET UNIVERSAM REGIONEM MORTIS] Græ- ci Hebræam vocem retinuere השדמות ἀσαρημώθ. Hie- ronymus legit השדמות derivatque à שדה & מות, quorum illud regionem, hoc mortem significat. Aquila ver- tit προάστια, vites puto suburbanas intelligens, quæ dicun- tur שדמות. At Chaldæus aquaductus, à particulis duabus & ש, à רמה & ש רמות, quod est projicere. Videtur in- telligere aquæductus factos ab Ezechia.

USQUE AD TORRENTEM CEDRON] Qui pro- ximus valli Tophet.

ET USQUE AD ANGULUM PORTÆ EQUO- RVM ORIENTALIS] Chaldæus: ad angulum portæ sta dii Regii, qui ad Orientem. Hic designatio à meridie ad o- rientem redit. De hac porta Equorum vide Neh. 3, 28.

SANCTUM DOMINI] Omnia hæc loca persona- bunt Dei laudibus.

NON EVELLETUR ET NON DESTRUE- TUR ULTRA IN PERPETUUM.] id est, diu stabit urbs, postquam erit reperata.

De urbe & structura materiali intelligit omnia Grotius. At non congruunt primo limites, quos hic posuit Dominus. Quos aptare quidem cona- tur Grotius: Sed omnia tamen minime conveni- unt. Addit enim Propheta, observante Bugen- hagio nostro, alia loca extra Ierusalem, ut collem Gareb & Gaath, deinde & vallem cadaverum atq; cinerum, & totam regionem sive agrum mortis, qui- bus verbis significat Tophet & Gehinnon, usque ad torrentem Kidron, qui est notus vel ex Evangelio lo- cus, conf. 1. Reg. 2. Ait ergo, (ita pergit Bugenha- gius) civitas Ierusalem nunc quidem per Babylo- nios vastabitur, sed reædificabitur, ut antedictum, post captivitatem Babylonicam. Ubi autem pactum novum invulgatum fuerit, per virum, quem fæmina circumdedit, per contritorem capitis serpentis, vestru Messiam, & scripta fuerit lex Dei in corda, abolito peccato, hoc est, ubi regnum Messiæ venerit, ad quod confluent omnes gentes, tunc erit adhuc longe alia Ieru- salem. Multo augustior, quæ extendetur & dilatabitur ad Aquilone & ad Occidente, & ad omnes mundi par- tes, ut loca, quæ nunc sunt extra Ierusalē sint intraleru- salē. Lege Zach. 2. Nolite itaq; metuere: Populus Israe multiplicabitur, & civitas sancta, sive civitas DE- valde dilatabitur, & civitas sancta & Sanctuarium ita a Deo firmabitur, ut nunquam in æternum possit rumpi & vastari, ut jam per Babylonios vastabitur. Quibus verbis manifeste describit dilatationem regni Christi in Judæa incipientis, sed carnali descriptione coram carnalibus. Nam in Jerusalem & templo, quod post captivitatem ædificabitur, non mansit po- stea lapis super lapidem, secundum Prophetiam Chri- sti, nec illa Jerusalem sic unquam dilatata est. Jeru- salem autem, quæ sursum est, est mater nostra Gal. 4. Heb. 12. ad quam coufluunt omnes Gentes, & habi- tant Psal. 87. &c. Latior ergo erit nunc Jerusalem, quam terrena unquam fuit, aut erit. Nunc antea in Judæa solum notus erat Deus. Nunc autem veni- ent (Matth. 8.) ab oriente, & ab occidente, & re- cumbent cum Abraham, Isaac & Jacob in regno cœlorum. Sanctum erit Domino, id est, hoc to- tum erit Domino separatum & sanctificatum. Re- gnum videlicet Dei in Christo; Hoc non vastabitur, neque violabitur in æternum, quod de terrena civi- tate dici non potest. Hoc est æternum regnum Christi nobis in Prophetis promissum, & per Evangelium exhibitum.

Hoc etiam alii interpretes observarunt: Mal- donatus, Gareb, inquit, & Goatha, duo colles erant extra urbem. Itaq; significat, amplificandam esse ultra terminos antiquos, ut supra vers. 24. & Isa. c. 55, 2. Et mystice multo ampliorum futuram Ecclesiam Catho- licam, quam fuerit Synagoga; Quia dominabitur a mari usque ad mare Pl. 72, 8. & extendit palmites suos usque ad mare, & usq; ad flumen propagines ejus Psal. 79, 12. Vers. 40. VALLEM cadaverum. Ea enim erat extra Jerosolymam, quæ ideo vallis ca- daverum appellata fuisse creditur, ut ait R. Salomo & Jonathas, quia illic Assyriorum cadavera, percu- tiente angelo, ceciderant, 4. Reg. 19, 35. Et cineres, והרשן & cineres, id est, usque ad vallem cinerum. Quæ, ut quidam Hebræorum putant, ita vocabatur, quod in eam sacrificiorum cineres projicerentur. Alii usq; ad vallem ודשן pinguedinis, id est, olivarum. Ionathas aquæductus, qui terram pinguem redde- bant. Et universam regionem mortis. Sic exi- stimant interpretes nostri appellatum esse locum sup- plicii, qualis est Parisiis mons Falconius. Sed Hie- ronymus ipse fatetur, se ex una dictione duas fecisse, השר־מות, quod ut notat R. David scribitur cum ר & legitur eum ד, & interpretatur R. Salomo omnia campestria, omnes regiones usque ad vallem Ce- dron. De hac valle multa est in scripturis mentio: erat autem sita extra portam, quam gregis appella- bant, & usque ad montem olivarum porrigebatur, ut apparet 2. Reg. 15, 23. Hæc Maldonatus.

Porro cum omnia illa dicantur fore Sanctum Do- mini, non tantum totam Hierosolymam persona- turam Dei laudibus, significatur; Sed sanctitas præ- dicitur Ecclesiæ per Hierosolymam adumbratæ. Quid enim, num Hierosolymam universam san- ctam unquam fuisse admittemus? Manifestum er- go est Ecclesiæ hoc esse elogium, quæ proprie est Sanctorum communio. Denique cum promissio ei fit: NON EVELLETUR, NEQUE DE- STRUETUR ULTRA IN PERPETUUM: perennis ejus conservatio innuitur. Quæ insignis promissio perverse corrumpitur a Grotio: quasi tantum diuturna conservatio designetur. Verba Prophetæ perennitatem, non diuturnitatem infe- runt. Ideoque palam docent, non posse hæc de terrena Hierosolyma accipi. Ea enim ita eversa est a Romanis, ut ne lapis quidem super lapidem sit re- lictus Matt. 24. Intelligenda ergo de Ecclesia Chri- sti, quæ super petram Christum ædificata est adver- sus quam nec portæ inferorum prævalebunt Matt. 16, 17. Atq; hæc de Capite 31.

CAP.

## 32:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXII.

Jeremiah in prison, by the sign of a field bought from a kinsman, seals the return from captivity and promises the propagation of the kingdom of Christ and the gathering of the nations.

Ver. 1.

THIS IS THE EIGHTEENTH YEAR OF NEBUCHADNEZZAR) See above 25, 1. THEN THE ARMY OF THE KING OF BABYLON BESIEGED JERUSALEM) It had already been besieging it for some time, as appears in 2 Kings 25, 1.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXII.

Jeremias in Carcere prædicta Zedekiæ abdu- ctione figno agri à propinquo emti obsignat reditum è captivitate ac promittit regni Christi propagationem & gentium aggre- gationem.

Vers. 1.

IPSE EST ANNUS DECIMUS OCTAVUS NA- BUCHODONOSOR) Vide supra 25, 1. TUNC EXERCITUS REGIS BABYLONIS OB- SIDEBAT JERUSALEM) Jam per aliquod tempus obse- derat, ut apparet 2. Reg. 25, 1.

## 32:2
Ver. 2.

HE WAS SHUT UP IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON WHICH WAS IN THE HOUSE OF THE KING OF JUDA) In the vestibule of the prison, in a slightly milder custody than that in which he had been before. Thus Jerome here: who also translates what is here 'court' as 'vestibule' below in verse 8. This very thing is proven from the passage which is below 37, 15. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ERAT CLAUSUS IN ATRIO CARCERES QUI ERAT IN DOMO REGIS JUDA) In vestibulo carceris, paulo leniore custodia, quam in qua ante fuerat. Ita hic Hieronymus : qui & quod hic atrium, infra 8. vestibulum vertit. Probatur hoc ipsum ex loco qui infra est 37, 15. 20.

## 32:5
Ver. 5.

THERE HE SHALL BE UNTIL I VISIT HIM) Until I take him away from this mortal life.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

IBI ERIT DONEC VISITEM EVM) Donec cum mortali vitæ eximam.

## 32:7
Ver. 7.

THY KINSMAN) In the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek, the son of Shallum thy uncle. BUY THEE MY FIELD THAT IS IN ANATHOTH) Jerome understands this as some suburban garden, such as the Levites could have, but the law of Leviticus 25, 34 stands in the way, which denies that such estates can be sold at all. Therefore, it should rather be taken as some estate that had come from a common grandmother or great-grandmother. For women, if they had no brothers, were heirs of their parents, and if a kinsman did not wish to marry them, they married others. FOR TO THEE IT PERTAINETH OF RIGHT OF KINSHIP THAT THOU SHOULDST BUY IT) The sense is: if I had sold it to others, you would have the right of redemption, by the law of Leviticus 25, 25. Wherefore, to avoid this circuitous process, I offer this field for sale to you before others.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

PATRVELIS TVUS) In Hebræo, Chaldæo, Græco, filius Sellum patrui tui. EME TIBI AGRVM MEUM QUI EST IN A- NATHOTH) Intelligit Hieronymus de horto aliquo sub- urbano, quales habere Levitæ poterant, sed obstat lex Levit. 25, 34. quæ talia prædia omnino negat posse vendi. Ergo potius sumendum de prædio aliquo, quod ab avia, aut pro- avia communi venerat. Nam mulieres, si fratres non ha- berent, hæredes erant parentum, & si propinquus eas duce- re nollet, nubebant aliis. TIBI ENIM COMPETIT EX PROPINQVITA- TE UT EMAS) Sensus est : si alii vendidissem, tibi esset jus redimendi, ex lege Levit. 25, 25. Quare ad evitandum hunc circuitum, tibi ante alios agrum hunc vænale offero.

## 32:8
Ver. 8.

THE INHERITANCE IS THINE) namely, if I were to die without children. AND THOU ART KINSMAN TO POSSESS IT) In the Hebrew: And to thee is the redemption. That is, if I were to sell to others, you would have the right of redeeming. You are גאל, the Greek here is οὐ πρεσβύτερος. That is, the first in order among the agnates. BUT I UNDERSTOOD THAT THIS WAS THE WORD OF THE LORD) God revealed to me that these things were to be done under His direction, so that by my example the people might conceive a certain confidence of their return, seeing me buy a field which was held by the enemy. Florus in book two, chapter six: A small thing to mention, but sufficiently effective for proving the magnanimity of the Roman people, that in those very days in which it was being besieged, the field which Hannibal had occupied with his camp was for sale at Rome, and being put up for auction, it found a buyer.

Latin:

Vers 8.

TIBI COMPETIT HÆREDITAS) nempe si ego sine liberis decederem. ET TV PROPINQUUS ES UT POSSIDEAS) In Hebræo : Et tibi redemtio. Id est, si alii venderem tibi jus foret redimendi. Tu es גאל, ὁ ἀγχιστεύων Græci hic οὐ πρεσβύτερος. Id est, inter agnatos primus ordine. INTELLEXI AUTEM QUOD VERBVM DO- MINI ESSET) Deus mihi revelavit hæc ipso dirigente fieri, ut meo exemplo populus de reditu certam conciperet fidu- ciam, videns a me agrum emi, qui ab hoste teneretur Florus libro secundo capite sexto: Parva res dictu, sed ad magnani- mitatem populi Romani probandam satis efficax, quod illis ipsis, quibus obsidebatur, diebus ager quem Annibal castris insederat, venalis Romæ fuit, hastæque subjectus invenit emptorem.

## 32:9
Verse 9.

SEVEN STATERS AND TEN SILVER PIECES) The Chaldean: seven minas and ten silver coins. For שקלים is interpreted as מנן. Therefore שקר, when it is proposed with silver coins, signifies something else than when it is placed by itself.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SEPTEM STATERES ET DECEM ARGEN- TEOS) Chaldæus: septem minas & decem argenteos num- mos. Nam שקלים interpretatur מנן. Ergo שקר, cum proponitur nummis argenteis, aliud significat, quam cum ponitur per se.

## 32:10
Verse 10.

AND I WROTE IN THE BOOK) I made an instrument of purchase and sale. AND I SEALED) I sealed it closed with a ring. The witnesses did the same. AND I WEIGHED THE SILVER IN THE BALANCE) So that it might appear that the payment had been perfect, and thus the right to the field had passed.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET SCRIPSI IN LIBRO) Feci instrumentum em- tionis & venditionis. ET SIGNAVI) Clausum obsignavi annulo. Idem fecerunt testes. ET APPENDI ARGENTUM IN STATERA) Ut appareret perfectam fuisse solutionem, ac sic jus agri transiisse.

## 32:11
Verse 11.

AND I TOOK THE BOOK OF POSSESSION SEALED, AND THE STIPULATIONS, AND THE RATIFIED, AND THE SIGNS ON THE OUTSIDE) You may translate it best: I took the instrument of sale sealed according to the laws and customs, and open: Supply the other, which was ἴσον, a duplicate, or a copy of that sealed one, as appears below in 14. Jerome in this place: That he may take the books, one sealed, the other open, which custom of purchases is observed even until now: so that what the seals contain closed on the inside, the open volume may exhibit to those desiring to read it. What is called here of possession, is placed for of purchase, as also above in 8. posside קנה is buy, just as the Chaldean also translates.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET ACCEPI LIBRUM POSSESSIONIS SIGNA- TVM, ET STIPULATIONES, ET RATA, ET SIGNA FORINSECUS) vertas optime: Accepi instrumentum ven- ditionis signatum secundum leges & mores, & apertum : Sup- ple alterum, quod erat ἴσον, pariculum, sive exemplum il- lius signati, ut apparet infra 14. Hieronymus hoc loco : Ut assumat libros, unum signatum, alterum apertum,quæ emptio- num consuetudo huc usque servatur: ut quod intrinsecus clau- sum singnacula continent, hoc legere cupientibus apertum volu- men exhibeat. Quod hic dicitur possessionis, positum est pro emtionis, ut & supra 8. posside קנה est eme, quomo- do & Chaldæus vertit.

## 32:12
Verse 12.

BARUCH THE SON OF NERIAH) The chief of his disciples. OF THE WITNESSES WHO WERE WRITTEN IN THE BOOK OF PURCHASE) Whose names were written on the back of the instrument.

AND IN THE EYES OF ALL THE JEWS, WHO WERE SITTING IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON) Namely, of those who had come there to see or to hear Jeremiah.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

BARUCH FILIO NERI) Discipulorum suorum præcipuo. TESTIUM QUI SCRIPTI ERANT IN LIBRO EMPTIONIS) Quorum nomina perscripta erant in tergo instrumenti.

ET IN OCULIS OMNIUM JUDÆORUM, QUI SEDEBANT IN ATRIO CARCERIS) Eorum scilicet, qui ad vivendum aut audiendum Jeremiam eo ve- nerant.

## 32:14
Verse 14.

PUT THEM IN AN EARTHEN VESSEL, THAT THEY MAY REMAIN FOR MANY DAYS) Lest, says Jerome, either placed outside they might be exposed to plunder, or buried in the ground they might be dissolved by the moisture of the earth.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

PONE ILLOS IN VASE FICTILI, UT PER- MANERE POSSINT DIEBVS MULTIS) Ne, inquit Hieronymus, vel foris positi paterent rapinæ, vel humo conditi humore terræ solverentur.

## 32:15
THEY SHALL STILL BE POSSESSED) They shall be bought.

Latin:

ADHUC POSSIDEBUNTUR) Ementur.

Verse 16.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Verse 18.
