Vers. 18.

QUI FACIS MISERICORDIAM IN MILLI- BUS) Ex decalogo.

## 32:19
Verse 19.

GREAT IN COUNSEL, AND INCOMPREHENSIBLE IN THOUGHT) LXX: δυνατὸς τοῖς ἐργοῖς. Nor does the Chaldee say otherwise; עלילות are works, actions.

WHOSE EYES ARE OPEN UPON ALL THE WAYS OF THE SONS OF ADAM) -- ὄχ ἕυδει Διὸς. Ὀφθαλμὸς· ἐγγὺς δ' ἐσὶ καὶ παρὼν πόνῳ.

THAT THOU MAYEST RENDER TO EVERY ONE ACCORDING TO HIS WAYS AND ACCORDING TO THE FRUIT OF HIS DEVICES) Thou who judgest and recompensest not only works but also thoughts.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

MAGNUS CONSILIO, ET INCOMPREHEN- SIBILIS COGITATU) LXX. δυνατὸς τοῖς ἐργοῖς. Nec ali- ter Chaldæus עלילות sunt opera, actiones.

CUJUS OCULI APERTI SUNT SUPER O- MNES VIAS FILIORUM ADAM) -- ὄχ ἕυδει Διὸς. Ὀφθαλμὸς· ἐγγὺς δ' ἐσὶ καὶ παρὼν πόνῳ.

UT REDDAS UNICUIQVE SECUNDUM VIAS SVAS ET SECUNDUM FRUCTUM ADINVEN- TIONUM EJUS) Qui non opera tantum sed & cogitata judicas ac repensas.

## 32:20
Verse 20.

THOU WHO HAST SET SIGNS) Thou hast brought forth.

EVEN UNTO THIS DAY) Celebrated, that is to say.

AND IN ISRAEL, AND IN MEN, AND YOU HAVE MADE A NAME FOR YOURSELF) This is later and redundant in the Hebrew manner. By those deeds you acquired a huge name for yourself, not only among Israel, but also among foreign peoples.

AS IS THIS DAY) As it is today: that is, a name such as it appears you have at this time.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

QUI POSVISTI SIGNA) Edidisti.

USQVE AD DIEM HANC) Celebrata scilicet.

ET IN ISRAEL, ET IN HOMINIBVS, ET FE- CISTI TIBI NOMEN) Hic posterius & abundat more Hebræo. Illis factis ingens tibi nomen comparasti, non apud Israelem tantum, sed etiam apud populos extraneos.

SICUT EST DIES HAEC) Sicut est hodie: id est, nomen quale hoc tempore te habere apparet.

Verse 23.

ALL THINGS WHICH YOU COMMANDED THEM TO DO, THEY HAVE NOT DONE) They have trampled upon all your laws.

Vers. 23.

OMNIA QUÆ MANDASTI EIS UT FACERENT, NON FECERVNT) omnes leges tuas proculcarunt.

Verse 24.

BEHOLD THE FORTIFICATIONS HAVE BEEN BUILT AGAINST THE CITY, SO THAT IT MAY BE TAKEN) The Chaldean here rightly has 'mounds', namely, siege works.

FROM THE FACE OF THE SWORD, AND OF FAMINE, AND OF PESTILENCE) That is, we are being attacked by the fear of the sword, famine, and plague.

Vers. 24.

ECCE MUNITIONES EXSTRUCTÆ SVNT ADVERSVM CIVITATEM, UT CAPIATUR) Aggeres habet hic bene Chaldæus, obsidionales scilicet.

URBS DATA EST IN MANVS CHALDÆO- RUM, QVI PRÆLIANTVR ADVERSUS EAM) Qui eam oppugnant. Ostendisti mihi te nihil opis adferre ur- bi velle.

A FACIE GLADII, ET FAMIS, ET PESTI- LENTIÆ) Id est, metu gladii, famis ac pestis oppugnant nos.

Verse 29. THE CHALDEANS SHALL COME) More correctly, they shall enter, namely the city, having made an assault.

Verse 30.

WHO EVEN UNTIL NOW PROVOKE ME BY THE WORK OF THEIR HANDS) Not even now do they cease to serve idols.

Ver. 31.

IN MY FURY AND IN MY INDIGNATION THIS CITY HATH BEEN MADE TO ME) This city hath been made to me a provocation of anger and fury.

FROM THE DAY THAT THEY BUILT IT) For Solomon completed the structure of the city: the same was the first of the kings to turn himself to idols.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

IN FVRORE ET IN INDIGNATIONE MEA FA- CTA EST MIHI CIVITAS HÆC) Urbs hæc facta est mihi suscitabulum iræ & furoris.

A DIE QUA ÆDIFICAVERUNT EAM) Nam Salomon urbis structuram perfecit: idem primus regum ad idola se vertit.

Ver. 32.

THEIR PROPHETS) Whom they themselves hold for prophets.

Vers. 32.

PROPHETÆ EORVM) Quos ipsi pro Prophetis habent.

Ver. 33.

WHEN I TAUGHT THEM EARLY IN THE MORNING) That is, with the greatest assiduity, as above 29, 19.

Vers. 33.

VERTERVNT AD ME TERGA) Cervicem, in Hebræo. Vide supra 2, 27.

CVM DOCEREM EOS DILUCULO) Id est, summa assiduitate, ut supra 29, 19.

Ver. 34.

IN THE HOUSE WHEREIN MY NAME IS CALLED UPON) In the Temple which is called the House of the Lord 2 Kings 21, 4. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

IN DOMO IN QUA INVOCATVM EST NO- MEN MEVM) In Templo quod vocatur Domus Domini 2. Reg. 21, 4. 5.

## 32:35
Ver. 35. THAT THEY MIGHT INITIATE THEIR SONS IN THE VALLEY OF THE SON OF HINNOM) That they might purify them by passing them through the fire. See what we have said at Deut. 18, 10.

Vers. 35. UT INITIARENT FILIOS IN VALLE FILII ENNOM) Lustrarent trajiciendo per ignem. Vide quæ diximus ad Deut. 18, 10.

Ver. 36. AND NOW THEREFORE THUS SAITH THE LORD) You may translate more correctly: Nevertheless even now saith the Lord.

Vers. 36. ET NVNC PROPTER ISTA DICIT DO- MINVS) Rectius vertas: Attamen jam nunc dicit Dominus.

Verse 37. I WILL MAKE THEM DWELL CONFIDENTLY.) Secure: as above 23, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 37. HABITARE EOS FACIAM CONFIDENTER.) Secure: ut supra 23, 6.

Verse 38. AND I WILL GIVE THEM ONE HEART, AND ONE WAY) I will cause that they may concordantly profess one religion.

Latin:

Vers. 38. ET DABO EIS COR UNUM, ET VIAM UNAM) Faciam ut concorditer unam religionem profiteantur.

## 32:40
Verse 40. AND I WILL STRIKE AN EVERLASTING COVENANT WITH THEM) Above 31, 31.

AND I WILL NOT CEASE TO DO THEM GOOD, AND I WILL PUT MY FEAR IN THEIR HEART, THAT THEY MAY NOT DEPART FROM ME.) The sense is, by many benefits I will excite the reverence of me in their minds. Thus this passage is an interpreter of that which we had above 31, 33.

Latin:

Vers. 40. ET FERIAM EIS PACTUM SEMPITERNUM) Supra 31, 31.

ET NON DESINAM EIS BENEFACERE, ET TIMOREM EORUM DABO IN CORDE EORUM, UT NON RECEDANT A ME.) Sensus est, pluribus be- neficiis reverentiam mei in animis eorum excitabo. Ita locus hic interpres est ejus, quem supra habuimus 31, 33.

## 32:41
Verse 41. AND I WILL REJOICE OVER THEM) With these words must be connected those which follow, with my whole heart, and with my whole soul.

WHEN I HAVE DONE THEM GOOD, AND I WILL PLANT THEM IN THIS LAND IN TRUTH) When I have done them good, that is, I will plant them in this land firmly.

Latin:

Vers. 41. ET LÆTABOR SUPER EIS) Cum his verbis connectenda sunt quæ sequuntur, in toto corde meo, & in tota anima mea.

CUM BENE EIS FECERO, ET PLANTABO EOS IN TERRA ISTA IN VERITATE) Cum bene eis fecero, id est, plantabo eos in terra hac firma.

## 32:43
Verse 43. AND FIELDS SHALL BE POSSESSED) Shall be bought: as above 15.

AND THEY SHALL BE WRITTEN IN BOOKS,) In an instrument. AND A SEAL SHALL BE IMPRESSED) Of the seller, and of the buyer.

Latin:

Vers. 43. ET POSSIDEBUNTUR AGRI) Ementur: ut su- pra 15.

ET SCRIBENTUR IN LIBRIS,) In instrumento. ET IMPRIMETUR SIGNUM) Vendentis, & e- mentis.

## 32:44
AND A WITNESS SHALL BE ADMITTED) Some witnesses, as above 10.

AND IN THE CITIES OF THE PLAIN (שפלה which the Greeks here retain as σεφηλᾶ, signifies a low situation.

AND IN THE CITIES THAT ARE TO THE SOUTH) The Greeks retained נגב ναγεβ. It is often taken for the south, or a southern situation. He describes all parts of Judea. See below 33, 13. Compare Zech. 1, 11, 7.

BECAUSE I WILL TURN THEIR CAPTIVITY) That is, the captives, or exiles. See above 30, 3.

Grotius makes these mere corporal promises: but although in the latter parts the discourse is primarily about the return from captivity; yet God promises in the former words more ample and more significant benefits, and especially spiritual grace. Because, as has been noted several times, that promise, I WILL BE TO THEM A GOD, embraces whatever goods, both earthly and especially heavenly. And that in those words: I WILL GIVE THEM ONE HEART AND ONE WAY, the unity of faith and concord in true religion, so that they may worship God in the unity of the Spirit and serve one another in mutual charity, is contained, not even Grotius could deny.

Finally, this EVERLASTING covenant, which the Lord wishes to strike, cannot be restricted to temporal goods, but embraces primarily the remission of sins in the Messiah, just as is evident from the preceding v. 31 et seqq.

The words: THAT I MAY NOT DEPART FROM THEM, TO DO THEM GOOD, the LXX interpreters render ἧν ὀ μὴ ἀποστρέψω ὄπισθεν αὐτῶν, which (covenant) I will not turn away from after them. In whatever way we translate it, it is certain that it is an explanation of the everlasting Testament, as Maldonatus and the other interpreters here acknowledge. And these things also pertain to Chapter 32.

Latin:

ET TESTIS ADHIBEBITUR) Testes aliquot, ut supra 10.

ET IN CIVITATIBUS CAMPESTRIBUS(שפלה quod hic retinere Græci σεφηλᾶ, situm humilem significat.

ET IN CIVITATIBUS QUÆ AD AUSTRUM SUNT) Ethic Græci retinuere נגב ναγεβ. Id pro meri- die, aut meridiano situ sæpe sumitur. Describit omnes Ju- dææ partes. Vide infra 33, 13. Confer Zach. 1, 11, 7.

QUIA CONVERTAM CAPTIVITATEM EO- RUM) Id est, captivos, sive exules. Vide supra 30, 3.

Mere corporales promissiones has facit Gro- tius: sed quamquam in posterioribus imprimis de reductione è captivitate sermo sit; promittit ta- men Deus verbis prioribus ampliora, & insigniora beneficia, ac maxime gratiam spiritualem. Quia, ut a- liquoties monitum, promissio illa, ERO EIS IN DEUM, quæcunq; bona, tum terrena tũ imprimis cœlestia complectitur. Et in illis: DABO ILLIS COR UNUM ET VIAM UNAM, fidei unitatem & con- cordiam in vera religione, ut Deum in unitate Spi- ritus colant, sibique mutua charitate inserviant, contineri, nec ipse Grotius diffiteri potuit.

Denique pactum istud SEMPITERNUM, quod Dominus ferire vult, non restringi potest ad bona temporalia, sed complectitur præcipue re- missionem peccatorum in Messia, quemadmodum è præced. v. 31. seqq. constitit.

Verba: UT NON DISCEDAM AB HIS, UT BENEFACIAM ILLIS, LXX. Interpp. red- dunt ἧν ὀ μὴ ἀποστρέψω ὄπισθεν αὐτῶν quod (te- stamentum) non avertam post eos. Quocunq; mo- do vertamus illud, certum est explicationem esse sempiterni Testamenti, ut hic Maldonatus, cæteriq; interpretes agnoscunt. Et hæc etiam ad Cap. 32.

## 33:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIII.

An evangelical sermon concerning great things, concerning the healing, cleansing, and glory of the people after the departure, and the voice of joy to be brought back again, and the spiritual kingdom to be erected through the righteous branch of David, and the divine covenant to be perpetuated, and the seed of Jacob to be vehemently multiplied.

Vers. 1. SECONDLY WHEN HE WAS STILL SHUT UP IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON) Secondly, since he was shut up in the vestibule of the prison. Often at other times God had revealed many things to him. But this happened to him a second time in the Palatine prison.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIII.

Evangelica concio de rebus magnis, de sana- tione, mundatione, & gloria populi post exitum, & iterum adducenda voce lætitiæ ac regno spirituali per germen Davidis ju- stum erigendo, ac fœdere divino perpe- tuando, & semine Jacob vehementer mul- tiplicando.

Vers. 1. SECUNDO CUM ADHUC CLAUSUS ESSET IN ATRIO CARCERIS) Secundo, ex quo clausus erat in vestibulo carceris, Sæpe alias multa ei Deus patefecerat. Sed hoc ei alterum contigit in Palatino carcere.

## 33:3
Vers. 3. CALL UNTO ME, AND I WILL ANSWER THEE, AND

I WILL SHOW THEE GREAT AND FIRM THINGS WHICH THOU KNOWEST NOT) That is, and if you pray to me, I will tell you many certain future things.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CLAMA AD ME, ET EXAUDIAM TE, ET

ANNUNTIABO TIBI GRANDIA AC FIRMA QUÆ NESCIS) Id est, & me ores, multa futura certa tibi dicam.

## 33:4
Vers. 4. THUS SAITH THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL CONCERNING THE HOUSES OF THE KING OF JUDAH WHICH ARE DESTROYED, AND CONCERNING THE FORTIFICATIONS, AND CONCERNING THE SWORD OF THOSE COMING TO FIGHT WITH THE CHALDEANS, AND TO FILL THEM WITH THE DEAD BODIES OF MEN) These things are more obscure, which you will best interpret from the sense of the Greeks and the Chaldean thus: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel on the occasion of the houses of this city, even the houses of the kings of Judah, which have been torn down so that a rampart might be made from them (for in besieged cities, where the outer rampart has yielded to the enemy, there is an inner rampart, and for that not only houses but also palaces are torn down. See Nahum 3:14) and of those who, armed with the sword, go to fight with the Chaldeans, namely to fill them (the houses torn down, that is, or their areas) with the dead bodies of men: namely, of their own countrymen. That 'ut' here, as often elsewhere, is not final, but consecutive; for they were not doing this, but this was to be the outcome.

Latin:

Vers. 4. HÆC DICIT DOMINUS DEUS ISRAEL AD DOMOS REGIS JUDÆ QUÆ DESTRUCTÆ SUNT, ET AD MUNITIONES, ET AD GLADIUM VENI- ENTIUM, UT DIMICENT CUM CHALDÆIS, ET IMPLEANT EAS CADAVERIBUS HOMINUM) Hæc obscuriora sunt, quæ sic ex sensu Græcorum & Chaldæi optime interpretaberis: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Israel ex occasione Domuum urbis hujus, etiam domuum regum Judæ, quæ dirutæ sunt, ut inde vallum fieret (nam in obsessis urbi- bus, ubi vallum exterius hosti cessit, sit vallum interius, & in id non domus tantum, sed & palatia diruuntur. Vide Na- hum 3, 14.) & eorum qui gladio armati eunt ut pugnent cum Chaldæis, nempe ut impleant illas (domos scilicet dirutas, aut eorum areas) cadaveribus hominum: popularium scilicet suorum. Illud ut hic, ut alibi sæpe est non τελικὸν, sed ἐκβα- τικόν, non enim hoc agebant, sed hic futurus erat exitus.

## 33:5
WHOM I HAVE SMITTEN IN MY FURY) Whom (the Jerusalemites) I will smite (namely, through the Chaldeans) being angry.

HIDING MY FACE FROM THIS CITY) Withdrawing my favor from them.

Latin:

QUOS PERCUSSI IN FURORE MEO) Quos (Hierosolymita-) percutiam (nempe per Chaldæos) iratus.

ABSCONDENS FACIEM MEAM A CIVITA- TE HAC) Favorem meum ab illis auferens.

## 33:6
Vers. 6. BEHOLD I WILL BRING THEM A SCAR) Above 30:17.

AND HEALTH) So that no reckoning remains. AND I WILL REVEAL TO THEM THE SUPPLICATION OF PEACE AND TRUTH) The sense is, as can be understood from the Greek and Chaldean: I will teach them how they may supplicate for the punishment before me, and obtain firm salvation: namely by correcting their life, as the Chaldean explains here.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ECCE EGO OBDUCAM EIS CICATRICEM) Supra 30, 17.

ET SANITATEM) Ita ut nulla maneat supputatio. ET REVELABO ILLIS DEPRECATIONEM PACIS ET VERITATIS) Sensus est, ut ex Græco & Chaldæo intelligi potest: docebo eos quomodo apud me deprecari supplicium possint, & impetrare salutem firmam: nempe vitam corrigendo, quomodo hic explicatChaldæus.

## 33:7
Vers. 7. AND I WILL TURN THE CAPTIVITY OF JUDAH) I will cause the captives to return, as above 32, 44.

I WILL BUILD THEM AS FROM THE BEGINNING) I will cause them to dwell, as formerly. Thus above 31, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET CONVERTAM CONVERSIONEM JUDA) Redire faciam captivos, ut supra 32, 44.

ÆDIFICABO EOS SICUT A PRINCIPIO) Fa- ciam habitent, ut olim. Sic supra 31, 4.

## 33:8
Vers. 8. AND I WILL CLEANSE THEM FROM ALL THEIR INIQUITY) That is, I will make an end of punishments, as the following explains, for thus טהר and καθαρίζειν are very often taken.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET EMUNDABO ILLOS AC OMNI INIQUI- TATE SUA) Id est, pœnarum finem faciam, ut sequentia explicant, sic enim טהר & καθαρίζειν sumuntur sæpissime.

## 33:9
V. 9. TO ALL THE NATIONS OF THE EARTH) Among all the nations of the earth.

AND THEY SHALL FEAR AND BE TROUBLED IN ALL THE GOOD THINGS AND IN ALL THE PEACE, WHICH I WILL MAKE FOR THEM.) Peace, that is, happiness. But they shall fear because they will recognize the power of God and his benevolence toward the Jews by such manifest signs.

Latin:

V. 9. CUNCTIS GENTIBUS TERRÆ) Apud omnes gentes terræ.

ET PAVEBUNT ET TURBABUNTUR IN UNI- VERSIS BONIS ET IN OMNI PACE, QUAM EGO FACIAM EIS.) Pace, id est, felicitate. Pavebunt autem quia potentiam Dei & in Judæos benevolentiam tam ma- nifestis signis agnoscent.

## 33:10
Vers. 10. WHICH YOU SAY IS DESERTED, BECAUSE THERE IS NO MAN, NOR BEAST) See above 32, 43.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUEM VOS DICITIS ESSE DESERTUM, EO QUOD NON SIT HOMO, NEC JUMENTUM) Vi- de supra 32, 43.

## 33:11
Vers. 11. THE VOICE OF JOY AND THE VOICE OF GLADNESS, THE VOICE OF THE BRIDEGROOM AND THE VOICE OF THE BRIDE) See above 7, 32. 16, 8. 25, 10.

THE VOICE OF THOSE SAYING: CONFESS TO THE LORD OF HOSTS: FOR THE LORD IS GOOD, FOR HIS MERCY IS ETERNAL) These very words taken from Psalm 136. It appears from Ezra 3, 11 that the returning Jews sang them.

OF THOSE BRINGING VOWS) In Hebrew, תודה that is, victims for the praise of God.

FOR I WILL BRING BACK THE CAPTIVITY OF THE LAND AS FROM THE BEGINNING) For I will bring back the captivity (that is, the captives) of the land (of this, so that they may be) as formerly. So that in the same way as formerly, they may live in this very land.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VOX GAUDII ET VOX LÆTITIÆ, VOX SPON- SI ET VOX SPONSÆ) Vide supra 7, 32. 16, 8. 25, 10.

VOX DICENTIUM: CONFITEMINI DOMINO EXERCITUUM: QUONIAM BONUS DOMINUS, QUONIAM IN ÆTERNUM MISERICORDIA EJUS) Hæc ipsa verba sumpta ex Psalmo 136. cecinisse Judæos re- duces apparet Esdræ 3, 11.

PORTANTIUM VOTA) In Hebræo, תודה id est victimas ad laudem Dei.

REDUCAM ENIM CONVERSIONEM TER- RÆ SICUT A PRINCIPIO) Reducam enim captivitatem (id est captivos) terræ (hujus, ut sint) sicut olim. Ut eodem modo sicut olim, in hac ipsa terra vivant.

## 33:12
Vers. 12. A HABITATION OF SHEPHERDS RESTING FLOCKS) see above 31, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 12. HABITACULUM PASTORUM ACCUBAN- TIUM GREGES) vide supra 31, 12.

## 33:13
Vers. 13. IN THE MOUNTAINOUS CITIES) The same as above 32, 44.

THE FLOCKS SHALL PASS BY THE HAND OF HIM THAT NUMBERETH) Virgil: And twice a day they count the flock, and the other the kids. Moreover, striking with a rod each one of the flock as it went out of the fold, they counted them at the same time. Lev. 27, 32.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN CIVITATIBUS MONTUOSIS) Idem quod supra 32, 44.

TRANSIBUNT GREGES AD MANUM NU- MERANTIS) Virgilius: Bisq, die numerant alter pecus alter & hœdos. Virga autem percutientes pecudum quamque caula exeun- tem simul numerabant. Lev. 27, 32.

## 33:14
Vers. 14. I WILL RAISE UP A GOOD WORD) I will make the promises valid.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SUSCITABO VERBUM BONUM) Rata faciam promissa.

## 33:15
DAVID) To David. THE BRANCH OF JUSTICE) Zerubbabel, the branch of David, a man loving equity; we had the same above 23, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DAVID) Davidi. GERMEN JUSTITIÆ) Zorobabelem, germen Davidis, virum æqui amantem, idem habuimus supra 23, 5.

## 33:16
Vers. 16. JUDAH SHALL BE SAVED) He shall be happy.

JERUSALEM SHALL DWELL CONFIDENTLY) Above 23, 37.

AND THIS IS THE NAME WHICH THEY SHALL CALL HIM THE LORD) The same sense as above, ch. 23, 6, except that there it concerns the people, here the city. And therefore there it is יקראו, but here יקרא לה, for which however both the Greeks and the Chaldean read לו, and refer it to Judea. In a more sublime sense, not only Christians, but also Kimchi refers this to the Messiah.

But this most illustrious oracle cannot in any part be drawn to Zerubbabel, but is to be understood solely of Christ. It is entirely parallel to the passage above, Chapter 23, v. 6, which we showed must be accepted only of Christ. Nor did those of the Jews who expounded it of the Messiah understand it otherwise. For that name, Jehovah our righteousness, cannot be applied to any other than Christ: which is attributed to the righteous branch of David. Wherefore, not only in a mystical sense, but according to the letter, both Christians by common suffrage and even the ancient Hebrews expounded this oracle of the Messiah, and not of Zerubbabel, as is evident from the Targum Jonathan, and Bereschit Rabba on Gen. 25, v. 5, and on Gen. 41, v. 44, from Midrash Tillim on Psalm 21, and Echa Rabathi on Lamentations 1, 16, and Bava Bathra ch. Hammocheret Hassephinah, and R. Joseph Albo, or as others will have it R. Moses Egyptian, in the book Ikkarim, can be seen, who all acknowledge that by that King who will rule prosperously and holily, and the Davidic branch, the Messiah is to be understood. Which even Socinus did not deny. Since it is too evident that all these epithets, which are used in these places, befit the Messiah alone. For he is the branch of Zech. 3, v. 8, the Branch of Jehovah of Isa. 4, v. 2, and the shoot of Jesse, Isa. 11, v. 1. Whom God raised up and sent in the fullness of time, Galat. 4, v. 4. That righteous King, Zech. 9, v. 9, born from the seed of David, Rom. 1, 3, the fruit of whose kingdom is salvation, the security of Israel and Judah. Nor can the feminine pronoun יקרא לה move anyone, as if this name, Jehovah our righteousness, were attributed to the city, which Grotius, along with some Jews, Socinians, and Arminians, thinks, but this august oracle and its parallelism with the previous Chapter 23 cries out against it. Indeed, Socinus himself refutes the Enjedini, who contends that the name Jehovah is attributed to Jerusalem, in contr. Wuieck. p. 390, and Crellius in his book on God and Divine attributes. The reason for which is this: Because Jerusalem is included under the number of those whose righteousness is Jehovah: therefore it is not denoted by the name Jehovah itself, who is Righteousness. Now, that this appellation is attributed to the seed of David, that is, the Messiah, and not to Israel, Judah, or Jerusalem, we have proved in Theolog. natur. & revelat. by several arguments on page 305 and following, which may be seen there.

Furthermore, that this name may be rightly vindicated for our Christ, we have determined that it must be accepted by apposition; namely, that Christ is to be called Jehovah, who is our righteousness. Which we now further prove (1.) from the context; because the Messiah is said to be called Jehovah our righteousness in such a way that the reason for this name is given at the same time, that he himself is to be the author of our righteousness: Because he himself shall reign as King, and shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land. Wherefore the Messiah is called Jehovah our righteousness, or the author of our righteousness, as Crellius interprets, because he himself is Jehovah, and the author of our righteousness. Such an argument can be: He who is our righteousness or the author of our righteousness, according to the explanation of this very prophecy itself, is also to be acknowledged and called that Jehovah, our righteousness, or the author of our righteousness, according to this prophecy. But the former is true of the Messiah, by force of the context. Therefore the latter. (2.) From resolution. Those things which are said jointly of any matter by apposition can also be said separately, as Crellius warns, and vice versa, since certain names which can be said separately of any matter or person, which are joined, are rightly said to be joined by apposition, unless a reason is evident from the context which teaches that the expression is elliptical, and the substantive verb is to be understood. But these names can be said separately of the Messiah. We demonstrated that regarding the name Jehovah in its proper place; but regarding the other name, our righteousness, the opposing party concedes it, when it interprets it as the author of our righteousness. For that Christ is the author of our righteousness can in no way be denied. (3.) From Paul's explanation, 1 Cor. 1, v. 30, 31, where Christ is called our righteousness, and likewise the Lord, in whom we ought to glory, and thus Jehovah, from Jerem. 9, v. 23. Compare 1 Cor. 1, v. 13, 2 Corinth. 10, v. 17. Christ is therefore Jehovah our righteousness. (4.) From the resolution of our text. For whether it is resolved thus, he who shall call, or shall convoke Jerusalem, or who shall preach to her, or even who shall be called to her, or whom he shall preach, or commend to her, (the Lord) is, or shall be Jehovah our righteousness, it is most manifest that there is a grammatical apposition in the predicate; similarly also if it is explained with the word 'name' inserted; This is the (name) which shall be called to him, or by her, or by which the Messiah shall be commended to the same, Jehovah our righteousness, the apposition will have the best place. (5.) From the custom of Scripture; For since Crellius himself confesses that a denomination by two words joined together by apposition is far more customary than one made by a complete statement; it is certainly more likely that this compound name was formed according to the more customary mode of denomination: nor is there need for us to have recourse to an ellipsis of the substantive verb, which is certainly not to be admitted unless necessity compels. Our application, therefore, the more customary and simple it is, the more certain and safe it is. (6.) From the attributed work; because the Messiah is proposed here as the branch of righteousness, as the author of salvation and peace. But the author of salvation and peace is not ministerial, but principal, as Grotius acknowledges; Therefore, not undeservedly, he is considered to be called by this name, Jehovah our righteousness, or he who is the author of our righteousness. It is said that Jehovah saves us in Jehovah our God, Hos. 1. v. 7. that is in the Messiah (our God, & our Lord Joh. 20. v. 28.) as the Targum interprets. (7.) From a similar denomination of the Messiah: who is accustomed to be called thus by apposition or another reason by two or more joined names; e.g. Gen. 4. v. 1. Man Jehovah; Isa. 4. v. 2. Branch Jehovah: 2. Sam. 7. v. 19. Man Lord God. Child God mighty His Man companion of God Zach. 13. v. 7. &c. (8.) From parallel passages Isa. 45. v. 24. Every tongue shall confess, certainly in Jehovah our righteousness. Which it is manifest is said of Christ from the Apostolic citation Rom. 14. v. 11. Conf. Phil. 2. v. 10. Christ therefore is Jehovah, who is our righteousness, because in Christ Jehovah is our righteousness. Christ is to be named thus by the faithful, because to him every knee ought to bow, and every tongue to swear by him, Christ is a righteous King, & the author of salvation Jehovah our righteousness. Just as he is introduced by Isaiah asserting: I am a righteous God & a Saviour, & besides me there is no other: turn to me and all the ends of the earth shall be saved: So in this place Jeremiah introduces him: Because he himself will execute righteousness in the earth, & they shall dwell under all the faithful will confidently be saved through him. Thus these passages illustrate one another remarkably. Similarly, Zech. 9:9, the daughter of Zion is commanded to rejoice in the Messiah, the righteous King who is coming: which righteous King is Jehovah himself, as is clear from a comparison with Zech. 3:20. But the same promise is held here concerning the Messiah, the righteous King, under whom Jerusalem will dwell confidently, who is Jehovah our righteousness. (9.) From the absurdity of the opposing opinion. For how would Christ use this symbol, Jehovah (is) our righteousness? Did Christ have need to be freed from the punishment of injustice and to be justified? Is not Christ himself our righteousness, so much so that all the faithful confess him, because they have righteousness in him before God? 2 Cor. 5:21. In symbolic names of persons, such symbols are accustomed to be included which are used by them, or can deservedly be used. But that this has no place here, anyone can see. The gloss of Socinus, that in the time of Christ it will come to pass that that Jehovah, our one God, will justify us through Christ, is: (1.) merely arbitrary, because Socinus will not provide a similar denomination of any person to be explained in that manner. (2.) Built upon a false hypothesis; that justification through Christ will only happen in the New Testament, which is against Peter, Acts 4:12 & Ch. 10:43, Paul, Rom. 3:19, 24, Ch. 5:18, and the Council of Jerusalem, Acts 15:11. (3.) Too jejune: Since Judah and Israel, that is, the faithful, by this appellation do not only wish to indicate what Jehovah will perform through Christ, but directly to address Christ himself in true faith, and to invoke the same, O Jehovah our righteousness, for the reason that they have in him righteousness, salvation, and tranquility of soul. (4.) Adverse to the text: which proposes Christ, not as a secondary or ministerial author of righteousness, but as the principal author of righteousness, who will perform righteousness on earth, and for that name is to be celebrated as the author of righteousness. (5.) Contrary to the whole of Scripture; which ascribes justification and salvation to Christ as the principal author, Acts 3:12, Heb. 2:18, ch. 5:9, ch. 12:2. And therefore it calls him righteousness in the abstract, 1 Cor. 1:30, and salvation, Isa. 49:6, Acts 13:47. (6.) Alien to the mind of the Prophet. For here is expressed a certain name not of God the Father, but of the Messiah himself, and thus the benefit of justification is celebrated, not as it is a benefit of the Father, but as it is of the Messiah, since he is the proper object of this prophecy; indeed, God the Father is rather proposed here as the one who established and raised up this Savior for the Church, and preaches and commends the same to it as Jehovah its justifier.

(10.) From the common naming of Christians. For here the meaning of this name is to be sought not from blind Rabbis with Socinus, but from the true Church of Christ, since it is that which is designated in this place, which is about to name and confess Christ by that name; and therefore its interpretation is rightly taken from the fulfillment of the prophecy. But the Church of the New Testament, just as it calls Christ Jesus, because he himself saves us from our sins, Matt. 1:21, and glories in him, that he is our righteousness, 1 Cor. 1:30, so it constantly and with unanimous voice proclaims, celebrates, and with true faith addresses and invokes Christ with us, that he himself is Jehovah our righteousness; whatever the devil may plot against it, while through his ministers he labors to deprive Christ of this eulogy and honor, namely through Socinus and his followers. Let the argument be such: The name of the Messiah, by which he ought to be called by the faithful of the New Testament, is to be understood as Christ is called by the Church

of the New Testament. Which is evident from the consistency of the prophecy and the fulfillment. But Christ is called by the Church of the New Testament Jehovah, who is our righteousness; and not merely a ministerial author of our justification; which is clearly established from the testimonies of the public doctors of the Church, both immediately θεοπνεύστων (God-breathed), the holy Apostles, and mediately θεοδιδάκτων (God-taught), those disciples, the Holy Fathers of both the Eastern and Western Church. Let the Confession of the Martyrs and other faithful be seen, and especially of the Doctors of the Church after the departure of the Holy Apostles up to the Council of Nicaea, proposed by us here in a public disputation in the year 1658. Therefore, the name of the Messiah is to be understood as that he is Jehovah, who is our righteousness.

Latin:

Vers. 16. SALVABITUR JUDA) Felixerit.

JERUSALEM HABITABIT CONFIDENTER) Supra 23, 37.

ET HOC EST NOMEN QUOD VOCABUNT EUM DOMINUS) Idem sensus, qui supra c. 23, 6. nisi quod ibi de populo, hic de civitate agitur. Et ideo ibi est יקראו, hic vero יקרא לה, pro quo tamen & Græci & Chaldæus legerunt לו, & ad Judæam referunt. Sensu sublimiore non Christiani tantum, sed & Kimchi hoc ad Messiam refert.

Hoc vero oraculum illustrissimum nulla parte ad Zorobabelem trahi potest, sed unice de Christo intelligendum est. Parallelum prorsus est loco superiori Cap. 23. v. 6. quem de Christo so- lum accipiendum esse, ostendimus. Nec aliter intellexerunt, qui è Judæis de Messia exposuere. Non enim de alio, quam Christo nomen illud ef- ferri potest, Jehovah justitia nostra: quod germi- ni Davidis justo tribuitur. Quapropter non mysti- co tantum sensu, sed secundum literam de Messia hoc oraculum exposuere tum Christiani communi suffragio, tum prisci etiam Ebræi, non vero de Zo- robabele, quemadmodum è Targum Jonathan, & Bereschit Rabba super Gen. 25. v. 5. & super Gen. 41. v. 44. è Midrasch Tillim super Psalm. 21. & Echa Rabathi super Thren. 1, 16. & Bava Bathra cap. Hammocheret Hassephinah, & R. Joseph Albo, vel ut alii volunt R. Mose Ægyptio, in libro Ikka- zim videre est, qui agnoscunt omnes, per Regem il- lum prospere, sancteque imperaturum & germen Da- vidicum Messiam intelligendum esse. Quod ne- que Socinus negavit. Siquidem nimis evidens sit, soli Messiæ convenire omnia isthæc Epitheta, quæ his locis adhibentur. Quippe qui est germen Zach. 3. v. 8. Germen Jehovah Esa. 4. v. 2. & surcu- lus Isai, Esa 11. v. 1. Quem Deus excitavit, misitque in plenitudine temporis Galat. 4. v. 4. Rex ille ju- stus Zach. 9. v. 9. ex semine David oriundus, Rom. 1, 3. cujus regni fructus salus est, securitas Israëlis & Judæ. Neq; pronomen fœmininum יקרא לה quem- quam movere potest, ac si civitati hoc nomen tri- buatur, Jehovah justitia nostra, quod cum Judæis nonnullis, Socinianis & Arminianis censet Gro- tius, sed reclamante augusto hoc oraculo ejusdem- que cum superiori Cap. 23. parallelismo. Enje- dinum sane, qui nomen Jehovah Hierosolymæ tribui contendit, refellit Socinus ipse contr. Wuieck. p. 390. & Crellius l. de Deo & attr. Div. Cujus hæc est ratio: Quia Hierosolyma comprehenditur sub eo- rum numero, quorum Justitia est Jehovah: non er- go notatur ipso nomine Jehovah, qui est Justitia. Jam quod semini Davidico, hoc est, Messiæ tribuatur hæc appellatio, non vero Israëli, Judæ, aut Hiero- solymiæ, probavimus in Theolog. natur. & revelat. compluribus argumentis pag. 305. & seqq. quæ ibi videantur.

Porro ut rite hoc nomen vindicetur Christo nostro, per appositionem id accipiendum esse sta- tuimus; quod nempe Christus nuncupandus sit Je- hovah, qui est justitia nostra. Quod nunc ulte- rius probamus (1.) è contextu; quia Messias ita dicitur Jehovah justitia nostra nuncupandus, ut ra- tio simul hujus nominis reddatur, quod ipse futu- rus sit autor justitiæ nostræ: Quia ipse regnabit Rex, & judicium, ac justitiam faciet in terra. Quocir- ca Jehovah justitia nostra, vel autor justitiæ nostræ, ut interpretatur Crellius, dicitur Messias, quod ipse sit Jehovah, & autor nostræ justitiæ. Argumen- tum tale esse potest: Qui est justitia nostra vel au- tor justitiæ nostræ, juxta ipsiusmet hujus vaticinii explicationem, idem etiam agnoscendus & nun- cupandus est Jehovah ille, justitia nostra, vel autor justitiæ nostræ, secundum hoc vaticinium. At de Messia verum est prius, vi contextus. E. & posterius. (2.) E resolutione. Quæ per apposi- tionem junctim de re quapiam dicuntur, ea etiam dici possunt separatim, monente Crellio, & vice versa, cum nomina quædam de re vel persona qua- piam separatim dici possunt, quæ conjunguntur, ea per appositionem conjungi recte dicuntur, nisi evidens sit è contextu ratio, quæ doceat ellipticam esse loquutionem, verbumque substantivum sub- intelligi. Hæc autem nomina separatim de Mes- sia dici possunt. De nomine Jehovah suo loco id demonstravimus; de altero autem nomine, justi- tia nostra, concedit pars adversa, cum interpreta- tur autorem justitiæ nostræ. Christum enim esse au- torem justitiæ nostræ nullo modo negari potest. (3.) E Pauli explicatione 1. Cor. 1. v. 30. 31. ubi Chri- stus dicitur justitia nostra, itemque Dominus, in quo gloriari debemus, adeoque Jehovah, è Jerem. 9. v. 23. Confer. 1. Cor. 1. v. 13. 2. Corinth. 10. v. 17. Est ergo Christus Jehovah justitia nostra. (4.) E textus nostri resolutione. Sive enim ita resolvatur, iste qui vocabit, vel convocabit Hierosolymam, sive qui prædicabit ei, vel etiam qui nuncupabitur ei, aut quem prædicabit, vel commendabit ei, (Domi- nus) est, vel erit Jehovah justitia nostra, manife- stissimum est, appositionem Grammaticam in præ- dicato haberi; similiter quoque si explicetur, inser- ta voce nominis; Hoc est (nomen) quod vocabi- tur illi, vel ab illa, aut quo commendabitur eidem Messias, Jehovah justitia nostra, optime locum habebit appositio. (5.) E Scripturæ consuetudi- ne; Quum enim ipse Crellius fateatur, longe usi- tatiorem esse denominationem duabus vocibus in- ter se junctis per appositionem, quam per integram e- nuntiationem factam; utique vero similius est jux- ta usitatiorem denominationis modum hoc nomen compositum formatum esse: nec opus est, ut re- curramus ad ellipsin verbi substantivi, quæ certe non admittenda, nisi cogat necessitas. Nostra ergo applicatio quo usitatior, quo simplicior, eo certior, atque tutior. (6.) Ex attributo opere; quia proponitur hic Messias germen justitiæ, ut autor salutis ac pacis. Salutis vero pacisque au- tor est non ministerialis, sed principalis, agnoscen- te Grotio; Proinde etiam non immerito cense- tur hoc nomine vocandus, Jehovah justitia no- stra, vel qui est autor justitiæ nostræ. Dicitur nos Jehovah salvare in Jehovah Deo nostro, Ose. 1. v. 7. hoc est in Messia (Deo nostro, & Domino no- stro Joh. 20. v. 28.) ut interpretatur Thargum. (7.) E simili denominatione Messiæ: qui solet ita per appositionem aut alia ratione duobus vel pluribus nominibus conjunctis appellari; v. g. Gen. 4. v. 1. Vir Jehovah; Esa. 4. v. 2. Germen Je- hovah: 2. Sam. 7. v. 19. Homo Dominus Deus. Puer Deus fortis Ejus Vir socius Dei Zach. 13. v. 7. &c. (8.) E locis parallelis Es. 45. v. 24. Omnis lingua confitebitur, utique in Jehovah justitia no- stra. Quod de Christo dici manifestum est ex allegatione Apostolica Rom. 14. v. 11. Conf. Phil. 2. v. 10. Christus ergo est Jehovah, qui est ju- stitia nostra, quia in Christo Jehovah est justitia nostra. Christus ita nuncupandus est à fideli- bus, quia ipsi curvari debet omne genu, omnis- que lingua jurare in ipso, Christus est Rex ju- stus, & salutis autor Jehovah justitia nostra. Perinde uti ab Esaia introducitur asseverans: Ego justus Deus & Salvator, & præter me non est alius: convertimini ad me & salvabimini omnes fines terræ: Ita hoc in loco introducit eum Jerem. Quia justitiam faciet ipse in terra,& habitabunt sub ipso confidenter omnes fideles & salvabuntur per i- psum. Sic egregie sese illustrant mutuo hæc loca. Similiter Zach. 9, 9. lætari jubetur filia Zion in Mes- fia Rege justo adveniente: qui Rex justus est ipse Je- hovah, ut ex collatione Zach. 3, 20. patet. Eadem autem hic habetur promissio de Messia justo Rege, sub quo confidentur habitabit Jerusalem, qui est Jehovah justitia nostra. (9.) ab inconvenientia sententiæ adversæ. Quomodo enim Christus hoc symbolo utetur, Jehovah (est) justitia nostra? An Christus opus habuit,ut ab injustitiæ pœna libera- retur, & justificaretur? Nonne Christus ipse no- stra est justitia, adeo ut fideles omnes ipsum confi- teantur, quod in ipso habeant justitiam coram Deo? 2. Corinth. 5, 21. In nominibus persona- rum Symbolicis ejusmodi symbola comprehendi solent, quæ ab illis usurpantur, vel usurpari merito possunt. Id autem hic locum non habere, quilibet videt. Glossa Socini, tempore Christi futurum, ut Iehovah ille unus Deus noster nos justificet per Chri- stum, est. (1.) mere arbitraria, quia similem per- sonæ alicujus denominationem ista ratione expli- candam haud dabit Socinus. (2.) Hypothesi fal- sæ superstructa; quod in Novo Testamento demum justificatio per Christum futura sit, quod est con- tra Petrum Act. 4. v. 12. & Cap. 10. v. 43. Paulum, Rom.3, 19. 24. Cap. 5, 18. & concilium Hierofoly- mitanum Actor. 15, 11. (3.) Nimis jejuna: Quum Juda, & Israël, hoc est, fideles hac appellatione non tantum indicare velint,quidnam Jehovah per Chri- stum præstiturus sit, sed directe compellare ipsum Christum in vera fide, eundemque invocare, ô Je- hovah justitia nostra, eo quod in ipso habent ju- sticiam, salutem, & tranquillitatem animæ. (4.) Textui adversa: qui Christum proponit, non ut secundarium vel ministerialem justitiæ autorem, sed ceu principalem autorem justitiæ,qui faciet ju- stitiam in terra, eoque nomine celebrandus est, ut justitiæ autor. (5.) Scripturæ universæ contraria; quæ justificationem & salutem adscribit Christo, ceu autori principali Actor.3,12. Ebr.2, 18. c.5, 9. c. 12. vers.2. Ideoque eum in abstracto vocat justitiam, 1. Corinth. 1. v. 30. & salutem, Esa. 49. v. 6. Actor. 13. v. 47. (6.) à mente Prophetæ aliena. Hic enim exprimitur nomen quoddam non Dei Patris, sed ipsius Messiæ, adeoque celebratur beneficium ju- stificationis,non ut Patris est beneficium, sed uti est Messiæ, quippe qui est proprium hujus vaticinii objectum; Imo Deus Pater hic potius proponi- tur, ut is, qui Ecclesiæ hunc constituit & excitat Salvatorem, eidemque prædicat, & commendat eundem ceu Jehovah justificatorem ipsius.

(10.) A communi Christianorum nuncupatione. Hic enim non à cæcis Rabbinis cum Socino, sed ab Ecclesia Christi vera petenda nominis hujus sententia, quippe, quod illa hoc loco designe- tur, quæ Christum isto nomine nuncupatura & confessura sit; ideoque ex complemento vaticinii recte desumitur ejus interpretatio. Ecclesia autem Novi Testamenti uti Christum vocat Jesum, quod ipse salvet nos à peccatis Matth. 1, 21. & in ipso gloria- tur, quod sit nostra justitia 1. Cor. 1 30. Ita constan- ter & unanimi voce Christum deprædicat,celebrat, veraque fide compellat & invocat nobiscum, quod ipse sit Jehovah justitia nostra; quicquid etiam contra machinetur diabolus, dum per ministros suos Christum hoc Elogio, & honore privare alla- borat,utpote per Socinum, ejusque asseclas. Ar- gumentum esto tale: Nomen Messiæ, quo à fide- libus Novi Testamenti appellari debuit, ita intelli- gendum est, uti Christus appellatur ab Ecclesia

Novi Testamenti. Quod ἔνδηλον è consonantia vaticinii & complementi. At Christus ab Eccle- sia Novi Testamenti appellatur Iehovah, qui est ju- stitia nostra; non vero ministerialis autor tantum nostræ justificationis; quod è Testimoniis publico- rum Ecclesiæ doctorum tum immediate θεοπνεύ- ςων, Apostolorum sanctorum, tum mediate θεοδι- δάκτων, istorum discipulorum, S. Patrum utrius- que tam orientalis quam occidentalis Ecclesiæ li- quido constat. Videatur Confessio Martyrum & aliorum fidelium, ac imprimis Ecclesiæ Doctorum post S. Apostolorum excessum usque ad Concilium Ni- cænum Anno 1658. disputatione publica à nobis hic proposita. E. Nomen Messiæ ita intelligendum est, quod sit Jehovah, qui est justitia nostra.

## 33:17
Verse 17. THERE SHALL NOT PERISH FROM DAVID A MAN WHO SHALL SIT UPON THE THRONE OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL.) There shall not be lacking, and ἐκλείψει (shall fail) the LXX, nor does the Chaldean say otherwise. And thus the Greeks translate כרת in many other places.

Latin:

Vers. 17. NON PERIBIT DE DAVID VIR, QVI SEDE- AT SVPER THRONUM DOMVS ISRAEL.) Non deerit, & ἐκλείψει LXX. nec aliter Chaldæus. Et sic Græci כרת vertunt multis aliis in locis.

## 33:18
Verse 18. AND FROM THE PRIESTS AND LEVITES THERE SHALL NOT PERISH A MAN FROM BEFORE ME.) It is a day-word, and it signifies, although most will be returnees from Judah and Benjamin, yet a sufficient number of Priests and Levites will not be lacking, who may care for the sacred things. AND SHALL BURN A SACRIFICE) In the Hebrew: let him burn מנחה (minchah), that is, a part of the cake of fine flour, see Lev. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET DE SACERDOTIBVS ET LEVITIS NON INTERIBIT VIR A FACIE MEA.) Est diem verbum, & significat, quamquam reduces plerique erunt ex Juda &Ben- jamine, tamen etiam numerum sufficientem Sacerdotum & Levitarum non defuturum, qui sacra curent. ET INCENDAT SACRIFICIVM) In Hebræo: adoleat מנחה mara, id est, partem de libo è simila, Vid. Lev. 2.

## 33:20
Verse 20. IF MY COVENANT CAN BE MADE VOID WITH THE DAY, AND MY COVENANT WITH THE NIGHT) Here ברית (berith) signifies law or precept rather than covenant or pact. See our prolegomena to the Gospels. Compare also what we had above 31:36.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SI IRRITVM POTEST FIERI PACTVM MEVM CVM DIE, ET PACTVM MEVM CVM NOCTE) Hic ברית legem sive præceptum potius quam fœdus aut pactum significat. Vide prolegomena nostra ad Evangelia. Confer & quæ supra habuimus 31, 36.

## 33:21
Verse 21. AND MY COVENANT BE ABLE TO BE MADE VOID WITH DAVID MY SERVANT) The promise made to David. 2 Sam. 7, 1 Chron. 17.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET PACTVM MEVM IRRITVM ESSE POTE- RIT CVM DAVID SERVO MEO) Promissio Davidi facta. 2. Sam. 7. 1. Par. 7.

## 33:22
Verse 22. AS THE STARS OF HEAVEN CANNOT BE NUMBERED, THE SAND OF THE SEA MEASURED) It refers to the passages Gen. 15:5, 21:17, 26:4, & 22:17, 32:12.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SICVT ENVMERARI NON POSSVNT STEL- LÆ COELI, METIRI ARENA MARIS) Respicit lo- ca Gen. 15, 5. 21, 17.26, 4. & 22, 17. 32, 12.

## 33:24
Verse 24. WHAT THIS PEOPLE HAS SPOKEN) Synecdoche, that is, some of the people. THE TWO FAMILIES WHICH THE LORD HAD CHOSEN HAVE BEEN REJECTED) That is, the Davidic and the Aaronic: the former royal, the latter pontifical. AND THEY HAVE DESPISED MY PEOPLE, IN THAT THERE IS NO LONGER A NATION BEFORE THEM) Therefore they despised my people, because in their opinion there was to be no nation anymore. For to constitute a republic, primarily are required ἡ κυρία ἀρχὴ (the sovereign authority) and ἡ ἱερωσύνη (the priesthood).

Latin:

Vers. 24. QVID POPVLVS HIC LOCVTVS SIT) Συνεκ- δοχὴ, id est, quidam de populo. DVÆ COGNATIONES QVAS ELEGERAT DO- MINVS ABJECTÆ SVNT) Id est, Davidica, & Aaronica: illa regia, hæc pontificia. ET POPVLVM MEVM DESPEXERVNT, EO QVOD NON SIT VLTRA GENS CORAM EIS) Ideo despexerunt populum meum, quod eorum opinione gens ultra non esse futura. Nam ad rempublicam constituendam im- primis requiruntur ἡ κυρία ἀρχὴ, & ἡ ἱερωσύνη.

## 33:25
VERS. 25. FOR I WILL BRING BACK THE CAPTIVITY) Translate here also 'captivity', as several times above. Nor do the LXX and the Chaldean translate it otherwise here.

This prophecy concerning the preservation of David, who sits upon the throne of the house of Israel, and concerning the Priests and Levites who shall not perish, cannot obtain its truth unless Christ is primarily included under those heirs of the Davidic throne, and by the name of Priests and Levites are understood whosoever care for sacred things, even if they are not Levitical Priests ordained according to the Mosaic constitutions, or from the order of Levites, whom the law had joined to such priests. Because it is certain that the bodily royal heirs of David have long since ceased, and the bodily throne of David has been removed, and such Priests and Levites no longer survive. Wherefore, since the perpetuity of the Davidic Throne and of the Priests is brought forward here in v. 21. If my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night can be made void, so that there be not day and night in their time, then my covenant also can be made void with David my servant, that there be not a son from him who shall reign on his Throne, and the Levites and Priests who are my ministers; which words, clearer than the rays of the sun, teach that the Throne of David shall endure until the consummation of the age, and he who sits upon the Throne, and the ministry of the Priests and Levites: that this is false concerning earthly Kings and legal Priests and Levites, experience testifies, since they have already ceased for sixteen centuries: nothing is clearer and more evident than that by those words, 'so that there be not of him (David) a son who reigns on his throne, and the Levites and Priests my ministers,' Christ is comprehended, of whose kingdom there is no end, and the ministry of the word is to be preserved until the consummation of the age. Whence that multiplication of the seed of David, and of the Levites, ministers of the Lord, so great that it cannot be numbered, just as the stars of heaven cannot be numbered, must necessarily be accepted as meaning that there shall be innumerable Christians; and ministers of the Church of Christ, and princes, whom He receives and promises that He will take from the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the covenant having been entered into, just as He preserves the pact between day and night, and as long as that lasts, are not to be restricted to princes born from the loins of those Patriarchs, such as have long since failed, but are to be understood generally, so that under the name of these princes are also comprehended those who preside over the Church of Christ, who are distinguished by this name, not because they ought to command the flock (which is repugnant to the prohibition of Christ, Luke 22), but because by their gifts, authority, and sacred office they represent princes, and stand out in the Church of Christ as ἡγέμενοι [leaders]. Heb. 13:7. Nor are those two kindreds, which some complained the Lord had cast off, the Davidic and Aaronic families, as Grotius wishes, but the Israelite nation, or the 10 tribes, and the Jewish nation, or the two tribes; As if the Lord had utterly cast off both the kingdom of Judah and of Israel. The Lord therefore protests that He has so far from cast off His people, that He will rather preserve a seed for Himself, while there shall be a covenant of God with day and night, and while the laws of heaven shall exist. Therefore, that He will turn the captivity of the people, and have mercy on them, as being that from which the Church, to be propagated thereafter through the whole world and to be preserved until the end of the world, ought to be produced. For from Zion the law of the Lord was to go forth, and through the Apostles, who are also called Princes in Psalm 45:17 and were the heads of the Church, it was to be propagated through the whole world, and thus disseminated among all nations and peoples. Again, God promises, says our Bugenhagen on fol. 376, liberation and return from captivity: And he adds that after the return, although they might not have kings, they would nevertheless have princes and rulers from the lineage of David, and from Levi and Aaron, Levites and Priests according to the divine promise and institution and according to the law of God. Which commands the people to hope well, not only for the return to that land, but also to God, so that there may be a holy Polity, and a sincere and true worship of God. In Christ, however, the eternal Kingdom was later begun, who is the seed of David, and the Levites and Priests of the law passed away and were changed, not by the propagation of flesh, nor by the mandate of the law, but by the institution of God and of Christ, the eternal King and Priest, into Apostles and holy Doctors of the Gospel, and thus, as many as are incorporated through faith into Christ and the eternal, not legal, Priest, are through Him, and because of Him, a Royal Priesthood and a Priestly Kingdom, 1 Pet. 2. And so those temporal things are promised first here, and then also the eternal in Christ, the eternal King and Priest, and all these things were to be after the Babylonian captivity. Thus, therefore, the temporal principate was changed into a spiritual and eternal one, and passed to Christ, the descendant of David, the eternal King and Priest. Nor does Bugenhagen rashly note that those words in verse 11, 'As from the beginning,' do not look only to the beginning of the kingdom, but are to be understood as they were then, when I first took your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to myself as a people, who were my kingdom, my people, the just sons of God without an earthly kingdom. These things, he says, do not taste good to the avaricious and proud Jews, because they see that the Gentiles can also attain to that justice. Certainly, when it pleased God through faith, Abraham was not a circumcised Jew, but an uncircumcised Gentile. Therefore, Abraham is also the father of us all, both of Jews and of Gentiles, who believe; as Abraham believed Rom. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 25. REDVCAM ENIM CONVERSIONEM) Verte & hic captivitatem, ut supra aliquoties. Nec aliter hic LXX, & Chaldæus.

Non potest hoc vaticinium de conservando Davide,qui sedeat super thronum domus Israel, & de Sacerdotibus & Levitis non interituris, verita- tem suam obtinere,nisi sub illis throni Davidici hæ- redibus imprimis comprehendatur Christus, & Sa- cerdotum ac Levitarum nomine intelligantur qui- cunque sacra curant, etsi non sint Sacerdotes Levi- tici juxta Mosaicas constitutiones ordinati, aut è Levitarum ordine, quos ejusmodi sacerdotibus lex adjunxerat. Quia certum est jam pridem desiisse corporales hæredes Davidis regios,thronumque cor- poralem Davidis sublatum esse, neque superesse amplius Sacerdotes & Levitas ejusmodi. Quapro- pter cum hic perennitas Throni Davidici & Sacerdotũ adferatur v. 21. Si irritum potest fieri pactum meum cum die & pactum meum cum nocte, ut non sit dies, & nox in tempore suo,& pactum meum irritum esse pote- rit, cum Davidservo meo, ut non sit ex eo filius, qui regnet in Throno ejus, & Levitæ & Sacerdotes mini- stri mei; Quæ verba solis radiis clariora docent, us- que ad consummationem sæculi mansurum Thronum Davidis, & qui sedeat in Throno, & ministerium Sa- cerdotum ac Levitarum: quod de terrenis Regibus & legalibus Sacerdotibus ac Levitis falsum esse, ex- perientia testatur,quum per sedecim secula jam es- se desierint: nihil clarius ac luculentius est, quam quod verbis illis, ut non sit ex eo (Davide) filius, qui regnet in throno ejus, & Levitæ & Sacerdotes mi- nistri mei, comprehendatur Christus, cujus regni non est finis, & ministerium verbi conservandum usque ad consummationem sæculi. Unde multiplicatio illa seminis Davidis,& Levitarum ministrorum Domi- ni tanta, ut numerari non possit, quemadmodum numerari non possunt stellæ cœli, sic necessario acci- pienda, quod innumerabiles futuri sint Christiani; & ministri Ecclesiæ Christi, & principes, quos de semine Abrahæ, Isaac & Jacob assumturum se fœ- dere inito recipit ac promittit, æque uti pactum inter diem & noctem conservat, & quoad usque illud durat,non ad principes restringendi sunt,ex isto- rum Patriarcharum lumbis oriundos, quales jam- pridem defecerunt, sed generaliter intelligendi, ut sub horum principum nomine comprehendantur etiam illi,qui Ecclesiæ Christi præsunt, qui hoc no- mine insigniuntur,non quod imperare gregi debe- ant (quod interdicto Christi Luc. 22. repugnat)sed quod donis,autoritate ac munere sacro principes re- ferant,atque in Christi Ecclesia ceu ἡγέμενοι emi- neant. Ebr.13,7. Nec duæ illæ cognationes, quas abje- cisseDominum nonnulli querebantur, sunt familiæ Davidica & Aaronica, uti Grotius vult, sed natio Israelitica, vel 10. tribuum & natio Judaica vel dua- rum tribuum; Quasi Dominus tam regnum Judæ, quam Israelis penitus abjecerit. Protestatur ergo Dominus se adeo non abjecisse populum suum, ut conservaturus potius sit sibi semen,dum erit pactum Deo cum die & nocte,& dum leges cæli erunt. Ideo con- versurum se captivitatem populi, ejusque miserturum, utpote è quo deinde Ecclesia porro propaganda per totum orbem, usque ad finem mundi conservanda, procreari debeat. Nam è Zione lex Domini egre- di debebat, & in totum orbem per Apostolos, qui etiam Psalm 45, 17. Principes vocantur & Ecclesiæ capita fuere,per universum mundum propagari, a- deoque inter gentes & populos omnes disseminari. Rursum promittit Deus, inquit Bugenhagius noster fol. 376. liberationem & reditum ex captivitate: Et addit,quod post reditum,ut maxime non reges, ta- men principes & rectores habituri sint ex stirpe Davidis,& exLevi&Aaron, Levitas & Sacerdotes secundum promissionem & institutionem divinam & secundum legem Dei. Quod jubet,ut bene sperent, populum non solum ad illam terram, sed etiam ad Deum reducendam,ut sit sancta Politia,& sincerus,ve- rusque Dei cultus. In Christo autem postea cæptum est Regnum æternum, qui est semen Davidis, & Levitæ & Sacerdotes legis transsierunt & mutati sunt, non car- nis propagatione, nec legis mandato, sed institutione Dei & Christi, Regis & Sacerdotis æterni, in Apostolos & Doctores Evangelii sacros,atque adeo, quotquot per fidem sunt incorporati Christo & æterno, non legali Sa- cerdoti, sunt per eum, & propter eum, Regale Sacer- dotium & Sacerdotale Regnum 1. Pet. 2. Itaque illa temporalia primum hic, deinde & æterna in Christo æterno Rege & Sacerdote promittuntur, atque hæc o- mnia futura post Babylonicam captivitatem. Sic er- go temporalis principatus mutatus est in Spiritusalem & æternum, & transiit ad Christum posteritatis Da- vidis æternum Regem & Sacerdotem. Nec temere no- tat Bugenhagius illa vers. 11. Sicut à principio, non respicere solum regni principium, sed ita intelligen- da esse, sicut tunc, cum primum Patres vestros Abra- ham, Isaac & Jacob suscipiebam mihi in populum, qui erant regnum meum, populus meus, justi filii Dei sine terreno regno. Hæc, inquit, non sapiunt avaris & superbis Judæis, quia vident ad eam justitiam e- tiam posse pervenire gentes. Certe Abraham cum pla- cuit Deo per fidem, non fuit circumcisus Judæus, sed incircumcisus gentilis, Ergo Abraham etiam est pa- ter nostrum omnium & Judæorum & gentium, cre- dentium; ut Abraham credidit Rom. 4.

## 34:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIV.

Some small consolation for Zedekiah, that although he is to be taken captive once the city is occupied, he shall nevertheless die in peace and be buried honorably, while punishment is announced for the people because the year of liberty was not observed, for whom liberty is announced only for the sword, pestilence, and famine.

Ver. 1.

THE WORD WHICH CAME TO JEREMIAH) Here, by an ἐπάνοδον [recapitulation], he gives the reason for the Prophet, on account of which he had been sent to prison by Zedekiah. For these are the very words on account of which Zedekiah had wished him ill, as we learned in chapter 32.

Indeed, this prophecy is later than that one, because the threatening which is made here looks to that time when Nebuchadnezzar had withdrawn from the first siege, v. 21. But that threatening made in chapter 32 is said to have been made while the first siege of the city was still continuing.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIV.

Solatiolum aliquod Sedekiæ, quod occupata ur- be captivandus in pace tamen moriturus & honeste sepeliendus sit, cum pœna popu- li ob annum libertatis promulgatum non servatum, cui libertas sed ad gladium, pe- stem, & famem intimatur.

Vers. 1.

VERBUM QUOD FACTUM EST AD JERE- MIAM) Hic per ἐπάνοδον causam reddit Prophetæ, ob quam à Sedecia in carcerem missus fuerat. Sunt enim hic ipsa verba, ob quæ Sedecias ei male voluerat, ut didicimus ca- pite 32.

Imo vaticinium hoc illo posterius est, quia comminatio, quæ hic facta, ad tempus illud spe- ctat, quo Nebucadnezar à prima obsidione reces- serat v. 21. Illa autem comminatio cap. 32. facta di- citur adhuc durante prima obsidione urbis.

## 34:5
Ver. 5.

YOU SHALL DIE IN PEACE) Not by the violence of war.

Compare ch. 52, 11.

ACCORDING TO THE BURNINGS OF YOUR FATHERS, THE FORMER KINGS, THEY SHALL BURN YOU, AND ALAS, LORD, THEY SHALL LAMENT YOU) Namely, with the king of Babylon granting that which had not happened to Jehoiakim, above 22, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

IN PACE MORIERIS) Non vi bellica.

Confer c. 52, 11.

SECUNDUM COMBUSTIONES PATRUM TUORUM REGUM PRIORUM COMBURENT TE, ET VÆ DOMINE PLANGENT TE) Nempe conce- dente id rege Babylonis, quod Joakimo non contigerat, Supra 22, 18.

## 34:7
Verse 7. LACHISH) See Joshua 10, 31. 2 Chron. 11, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 7. LACHIS) Vide Josuæ 10, 31. 2. Par. 11, 9.

## 34:8
Verse 8.

AFTER KING ZEDEKIAH HAD MADE A COVENANT WITH ALL THE PEOPLE IN JERUSALEM) By a common decree he had determined that what the law commanded should be fulfilled, but the Jews had not observed it. See Exod. 21, 2. Deut. 15, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

POSTQVAM PERCUSSIT REX SEDECIAS FE- DUS CUM OMNI POPULO IN JERUSALEM) Com- muni decreto statuerat impleri quod lex jubebat, sed Ju- dæi non observaverant. Vide Exod. 21, 2. Deut. 15, 12.

## 34:11
Verse 11.

AND THEY TURNED AFTERWARDS) They changed their opinion when the Chaldeans, having heard the rumor of the arrival of the Egyptian, had lifted the first siege, as we read below 21. & 37, 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. Thus also below this word is taken. 15. 16.

AND THEY BROUGHT BACK THE MENSERVANTS AND MAIDSERVANTS) Into servitude against the law.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET CONVERSI SUNT DEINCEPS) Mutarunt sententiam, cum Chaldæi, audita fama de adventu Ægyptii, obsidionem primam solvissent, ut legimus infra 21. & 37, 4.5.6.7.8. sic & infra hoc verbum sumitur. 15. 16.

ET RETRAXERUNT SERVOS ET ANCILLAS) In servitutem contra legem.

## 34:15
Verse 15.

THAT YOU MIGHT PROCLAIM LIBERTY) You might publish, and that in the Temple, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

UT PRÆDICARETIS LIBERTATEM) Publica- retis, idque in Templo, ut sequitur.

## 34:17
Verse 17.

I PROCLAIM LIBERTY TO YOU, SAYS THE LORD, TO THE SWORD, AND TO THE PESTILENCE, AND TO THE FAMINE) I proclaim liberty against you to the sword and to the pestilence and to the famine.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

EGO PRÆDICO VOBIS LIBERTATEM, AIT DOMINUS, AD GLADIUM, ET AD PESTEM ET AD FAMEM) Ego publico adversus vos libertatem gladio & pesti & fami.

## 34:18
Vers. 18.

THEY HAVE NOT KEPT THE WORDS OF THE COVENANT WHICH THEY AGREED TO IN MY SIGHT) That is, in the Temple.

THE CALF WHICH THEY CUT INTO TWO PARTS, AND PASSED BETWEEN THE DIVISIONS THEREOF) By cutting the calf into two parts, and passing between the divisions thereof. Concerning this custom of ratifying covenants, see Gen. 15, 9, and what we have said at Matth. 26, vers. 28.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

NON OBSERVaVERUNT VERBA FEDERIS, QVIBUS ASSENSI SUNT IN CONSPECTU MEO) Id est, in Templo.

VITULUM QUEM CONCIDERUNT IN DUAS PARTES, ET TRANSIERUNT INTER DIVISIONES EJUS) Vitulum concidendo in duas partes, & transeundo inter divisiones ejus. De hoc more fœderum sanciendorum vide Gen. 15, 9. & quæ diximus ad Matth. 26, vers. 28.

## 34:19
EUNUCHS) Eunuchs.

AND ALL THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND) And all the people of the land. For these things cohere with that which follows, I will give them into the hands, with the conjunction overflowing in the Hebrew manner.

Latin:

EUNUCHI) Eunuchos.

ET OMNIS POPULUS TERRÆ) Et omnem po- pulum terræ. Cohærent enim hæc cum eo quod sequi- tur, Dabo eos in manus, superfluente copula more He- bræo.

## 34:21
Verse 21.

AND INTO THE HANDS OF THE ARMIES OF THE KING OF BABYLON, WHICH HAVE GONE UP FROM YOU) That is, they will return, once it is known that the Egyptian has returned to his own land.

Latin:

Verf. 21.

ET IN MANVS EXERCITUUM REGIS BABYLONIS, QVI RECESSERUNT A VOBIS) Et redibunt scilicet, cognito ad sua rediisse Ægyptium.

## 34:22
Verse 22.

BEHOLD I WILL COMMAND) I am about to command. That is, I will bring it about that those Chaldeans return.

Latin:

Verf. 22.

ECCŒ EGO PRÆCIPIO) Præcepturus sum. Id est, effecturus, ut illi Chaldæi redeant.

## 35:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXV.

The obedience of the Rechabites is proposed to confound the disobedience of the people; to the former a blessing is promised, but to the latter a punishment is denounced.

Verse 1.

THE WORD WHICH CAME TO JEREMIAH FROM THE LORD, IN THE DAYS OF JEHOIAKIM THE SON OF JOSIAH KING OF JUDAH) By way of occasion, he attaches to this place the history of a matter done long before, so that he may show how gravely they offend God who violate his laws of whatever kind, as those had done who had dragged their fellow countrymen back into servitude.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXV.

Rechabitarum obedientia ad confundendam inobedientiam populi proposita benedictio promittitur, huic autem pœna denunciatur.

Verf. 1.

VERBUM QVOD FACTUM EST AD JEREMIAM A DOMINO, IN DIEBUS JOAKIM FILII JOSIÆ REGIS JUDÆ) Ex occasione historiam rei multo ante actæ huic loco attexit, ut ostendat quam graviter Deum offendant, qui leges ejus qualescunque violant, ut illi fecerant, qui in servitutem populares suos retraxerant.

## 35:2
GO TO THE HOUSE OF THE RECHABITES) That is, to the family. It had originated in antiquity from the Kenites, 1 Chron. 2:55.

From the father-in-law of Moses Ex. 3:1, Num. 10:29. They were Kenites Num. 24:21, Judges 1:16. That they were not monks is sufficiently evident, because they neither abstained from marriage, nor were they bound to poverty, or even to indefinite obedience. Compare B. Hülseman on this passage.

ON ONE CHAMBER OF THE TREASURIES) It would have been enough to say chamber; the Greeks say sometimes μίαν τǿν αὐλǿν, sometimes πασφόριον. Jerome, at Isaiah 22, interprets pastophorium as a chamber in which the overseer of the Temple dwells, putting the species for the genus; but because both the vestments of the priests and the vessels were kept in those chambers, therefore it is called here the chamber of the treasuries, and presently the treasury.

Latin:

VADE AD DOMUM RECHABITARVM) Id est, ad familiam. Ea antiquitus ex Cinæis erat orta, 1. Par. 2, 55.

A Socero Mosis Ex. 3, 1. Num. 10, 29. Kenitæ fuere Num. 24, 21. Judicum 1, 16. Non fuisse eos Monachos satis constat, quia nec à matrimonio abstinuere, nec ad paupertatem, aut etiam indefinitam obedientiam adstricti fuere. Conf. B. Hülseman. h. l.

IN UNAM EXEDRAM THESAURORUM) Exedram dicere satis fuerat, Græci modo μίαν τǿν αὐλǿν, modo πασφόριον dicunt. Pastophorium Hieronymus ad 22. Esaiæ interpretatur thalamum, in quo habitat præpositus Templi, speciem ponens pro genere; sed quia in exedris illis & vestes sacerdotum & vasa asservabantur, ideo hic dicitur exedra thesaurorum, & mox gazophylacium.

## 35:4
Ver. 4.

OF THE SONS OF HANAN THE SON OF IGDALIAH THE MAN OF GOD) A prophet, as the Chaldean has it here. Thus the same words are used in 2 Kings 4:7, 25, 40; 6:6, and elsewhere.

BY THE TREASURY OF THE PRINCES) By the chamber in which the chief of the priests used to take food.

OVER THE TREASURY) Over the chamber.

WHO WAS THE KEEPER OF THE THRESHOLD) סף signifies both vessels and threshold: the Chaldean embraces the former meaning here, which has אמרכלין. By that name were called in the Temple the seven treasurers, to whom the money paid per head for the uses of the Temple, and votive and consecrated things, were brought by those who were called גזברין. The Greeks, who have τὸ φυλάσσοντα τὴν ὁδὸν, embrace the latter with the Latin.

Latin:

Verf. 4.

FILIORUM HANAN FILII JEGEDELIÆ HOMINIS DEI) Prophetæ, ut hic Chaldæus. Sic eadem vocabula usurpantur 2. Reg. 4, 7. 25. 40. 6, 6. & alibi.

JUXTA GAZOPHTLACIUM PRINCIPUM) Juxta exedram in qua primi sacerdotum cibum capiebant.

SUPER THESAURUM) Super exedram.

QVI ERAT CUSTOS VESTIBUBI) סף & vasa & limen significat: priorem significatum hic amplectitur Chaldæus, qui habet אמרכלין. Eo nomine dicebantur in Templo septem arcarii, ad quos pecunia in usus Templi capitatim soluta, & res votivæ atque consecratæ deferebantur ab iis qui vocabantur גזברין. Posteriorem cum Latino Græci, qui habent τὸ φυλάσσοντα τὴν ὁδὸν.

## 35:6
Ver. 6.

BECAUSE JONADAB THE SON OF RECHAB OUR FATHER) They call him father who had been their progenitor three hundred years before. For this Jonadab had been a friend of King Josiah, as we see in 2 Kings 10:15.

HE COMMANDED US SAYING: YOU SHALL NOT DRINK WINE) If a progenitor could command this to his descendants, and those who observed it have praise from God: why should not the fathers of the Church be able to command certain things, not necessary in themselves, but useful according to the circumstances of times or places, either to avoid occasions of evil or as aids to virtues?

Latin:

Verf. 6.

QVIA JONADAB FILIUS RECHAB PATER NOSTER) Patrem vocant, qui progenitor eorum fuerat ante annos trecentos. Fuerat enim hic Jonadab amicus regis Josiæ, ut videmus 2. Reg. 10, 15.

PRÆCEPIT NOBIS DICENS : NON BIBETIS VINUM) Si hoc præcipere progenitor posteris suis potuit, & laudem à Deo habent qui id observarunt: cur non Ecclesiæ patres præcipere quædam poterunt, non per se necessariæ, sed pro ratione temporum locorumve utilia, aut ad vitandas mali occasiones aut ad virtutum adminicula?

## 35:7
YOU SHALL DWELL IN TENTS) In tents, according to their ancestral custom, Judges 4:17.

THAT YOU MAY LIVE MANY DAYS UPON THE FACE OF THE LAND, WHERE YOU SOJOURN) For they were not of the stock of Jacob: but for such inhabitants, envy is especially to be avoided.

Latin:

IN TABERNACULIS HABITABITIS) In tentoriis, more ipsis avito, Jud 4, 17.

UT VIVATIS DIEBVS MVLTIS SUPER FACIEM TERRÆ, IN QVA VOS PEREGRINAMINI) Non erant enim de stirpe Jacobi: incolis autem talibus præcipue vitanda invidia est.

## 35:11
Ver. 11.

BUT WHEN NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON HAD ASCENDED INTO OUR LAND) It could be asked, why then do you remain in the city against the prohibition of Jonadab? They meet this accusation, and say that they did it compelled by necessity: because the enemy held all the lands, allowing no one to remain there. Precepts of the kind to which this belonged love ἐπιείκειαν as an interpreter.

AND FROM THE FACE OF THE ARMY OF SYRIA) For the Syrians were allies of the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Verf. 11.

CUM AVTEM ASCENDISSET NABVCHODONOSOR REX BABYLONIS IN TERRAM NOSTRAM) Quæri poterat, cur ergo in urbe moramini contra Jonadabi interdictum? occurrunt huic accusationi, & ajunt necessitate coactos se id fecisse: quod terras omnes hostis teneret, neminem ibi patiens consistere. Præcepta ejus generis, cujus hoc fuit, amant ἐπιείκειαν interpretem.

ET A FACIE EXERCITVS SYRIÆ) Nam Syri socii erant Chaldæorum.

## 35:14
Ver. 14.

THE WORDS OF JONADAB PREVAILED) They had authority among his descendants.

AND THEY HAVE NOT DRUNK UNTIL THIS DAY) For three hundred years, as we have said.

Latin:

Verf. 14.

PRÆVALVERVNT SERMONES JONADAB) Auctoritatem apud posteros habuerunt.

ET NON BIBERVNT VSQVE AD DIEM HANC) Per annos, ut diximus, trecentos.

## 35:16
Ver. 16.

THEREFORE THE SONS OF JONADAB THE SON OF RECHAB ESTABLISHED THE PRECEPT OF THEIR FATHER) They made it ratified.

SECTION II. COMPRISING THE HISTORICAL.

Latin:

Verf. 16.

FIRMAVERVNT IGITVR FILII JONADAB FILII RECHAB PRÆCEPTVM PATRIS SVI) Ratum fecerunt.

SECTIO II. HISTORICA COMPLECTENS.

## 35:19
Verse 19.

THERE SHALL NOT FAIL A MAN OF THE LINEAGE OF JONADAB THE SON OF RECHAB STANDING BEFORE ME ALL THE DAYS) That is, ministering to me, as the Chaldean says, namely by singing the praises of God. Which seems to be gathered from the passage 1 Chron. 2:55, where we also learn this, that they returned from exile.

Latin:

Verf. 19.

NON DEFICIET VIR DE STIRPE JONADAB FILII RECHAB STANS IN CONSPECTU MEO CUNCTIS DIEBUS) Id est, ministrans mihi, ut ait Chaldæus, nempe Dei laudes canendo. Quod colligi videtur ex loco 1. Par. 2, 55. ubi & hoc discimus, rediisse eos ab exsilio.

## 36:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVI.

The Prophet sends threats recorded in a book by Baruch, so that they may be read aloud to the people: which the princes and nobles also take care to have read to themselves, and they indicate the contents to the terrified King Jehoiakim: who cuts up the book read by the Secretary and throws it into the fire; But another is ordered to be made and destruction is announced to the King and his house.

Ver. 1.

THE WORD THAT CAME TO JEREMIAH FROM THE LORD IN THE DAYS OF JEHOIAKIM THE SON OF JOSIAH) Just as Isaiah appended to his prophecies a history of the events by which the truth of his prophecies was proven, in chapters 36, 37, 38, 39, so also does Jeremiah, whose history will begin in the following chapter and will run through several chapters. But before he does that, he prefaces a narrative of a deed done long ago, from which it would be clear that Jeremiah had not only spoken by voice, but had also recorded in writing, and indeed twice, all those things which he will subsequently show to have come to pass.

At the beginning of the fourth year, Jehoiakim was indeed carried away, but he was restored under certain conditions, 1 Kings 24:1. After this restoration, therefore, these things were done.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVI.

Mittit Propheta comminationes libro consignatas per Baruchum, ut populo prælegantur: quas etiam sibi prælegi curant principes & Optimates, ac perterrito Regi Iojakimo contenta indicant: qui librum à Secretario prælectum scindit & in ignem conjicit; Sed alius confici jubetur ac Regi & domui ejus exitium indicitur.

Verf. 1.

VERBUM QVOD FACTUM EST AD JEREMIAM A DOMINO IN DIEBUS JOAKIM FILII JOSIÆ) Sicut Esaias vaticiniis suis subtexuit historiam rerum, per quas probata est vaticiniorum fides, capitibus 36. 37. 38. 39. sic & Jeremias, cujus historia incipiet capite sequenti, & per aliquot capita decurret. Sed priusquam id faciat, præmittit narrationem rei gestæ jam olim, ex qua constaret Jeremiam non voce tantum dixisse, sed & scripto, & quidem bis, consignasse omnia ea, quæ evenisse deinde ostendet.

Anno quarto ineunte abductus quidem Jojakim, sed certis conditionibus restitutus fuit 1. Regum 4, 1. 2. Post hanc ergo restitutionem hæc facta.

## 36:2
Verse 2.

TAKE A ROLL OF A BOOK) Take for yourself as much as is sufficient from the rollable membranes.

The Jews used to write on membranes, which they then rolled up in the manner of a cylinder. Therefore, the wrapping of a book is mentioned in Psalm 40:7.

Latin:

Verf. 2.

TOLLE VOLUMEN LIBRI) Sume tibi de membranis volubilibus quantum satis est.

In membranis scribebant Judæi, quas deinde convolvebant in modum cylindri. Dicitur ergo involucrum libri Psal. 40, 8.

## 36:4
Verse 4.

BARUCH) Chiefly of his disciples, as we noted above in 32:12.

Latin:

Verf. 4.

BARUCH) Discipulorum suorum potissimum, ut supra notavimus 32, 12.

## 36:5
Verse 5.

I AM SHUT UP) I am detained. That is to say, ordered by the king to keep myself at home.

Theodoret, Jerome, and others understand this as his imprisonment. Therefore, what is in verse 19, that he was hidden by the Lord, was done through a miracle, as also in verse 26, which Thomas, Lyranus, Castro, and Maldonatus understand more correctly as a hiding than the Chaldean, Rabanus, and Hugo do as a transportation.

Latin:

Verf. 5.

EGO CLAUSUS SUM) Detineor. Jussus scilicet à rege domi me continere.

De carcere ejus intelligunt Theodor. Hieron. alii. Quod ergo v. 19. absconsus fuit à Domino, per miraculum factum, ut & v. 26. quod de occultatione Thomas, Lyran. Castro Maldon. rectius intelligunt quam de transportatione Chaldæus, Rabanus & Hugo.

## 36:6
Verse 6.

ON THE DAY OF FASTING) Which the king was about to proclaim, below in chapter 9.

This was an extraordinary fast on account of present necessity and fear.

Latin:

Verf. 6.

IN DIE JEJUNII) Quod rex erat indicturus, infra 9.

Erat hoc extraordinarium jejunium ob præsentem necessitatem & metum.

## 36:7
Verse 7.

IF PERCHANCE THEIR PRAYER MAY FALL IN THE SIGHT OF THE LORD) A prayer is said to fall which is made by those prostrating themselves. Thus below 38, 26.

Latin:

Verf. 7.

SI FORTE CADAT ORATIO EORUM IN CONSPECTU DOMINI) Cadere oratio dicitur quæ fit à procumbentibus. Sic infra 38, 26.

## 36:8
Verse 8.

Latin:

Verf. 8.

## 36:9
AND TO THE WHOLE MULTITUDE WHICH HAD FLOWED TOGETHER FROM THE CITIES OF JUDAH INTO JERUSALEM) By the king's edict.

Latin:

ET UNIVERSÆ MULTITUDINI QVÆ CONFLUXERAT DE CIVITATIBUS JUDÆ IN JERUSALEM) Ex regis edicto.

## 36:10
Verse 10.

SCRIBE) Namely of the Temple.

AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE NEW GATE) Concerning which see above 26, 10.

Latin:

Verf. 10.

SCRIBÆ) Nempe Templi.

IN INTROITU PORTÆ NOVÆ) De qua supra 26, 10.

## 36:12
Verse 12.

HE WENT DOWN INTO THE KING'S HOUSE TO THE SCRIBE'S TREASURY) To the chamber of the royal scribe.

AND BEHOLD ALL THE PRINCES WERE SITTING THERE) The chief men of the court. ELNATHAN THE SON OF ACHBOR) Already named above 26, 22.

Latin:

Verf. 12.

DESCENDIT IN DOMUM REGIS AD GAZOPHTLACIUM SCRIBÆ) Ad exedram scribæ regii.

ET ECCE IBI OMNES PRINCIPES SEDEBANT) Primores aulæ. ELNATHAN FILIUS ACHABOR) Nominatus jam supra 26, 22.

## 36:16
Verse 16.

THEY WERE ASTONIED EVERY ONE TO HIS NEIGHBOUR) They looked at one another, struck by the announcement of such grave matters.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

OBSTUPUERUNT UNUSQUISQUE AD PROXIMUM SUUM) Respexerunt se mutuo, perculsi tam gravium rerum denuntiatione.

## 36:18
Verse 18.

HE SPOKE FROM HIS MOUTH, AS IF READING TO ME, ALL THESE WORDS) Distinctly, hesitating at nothing, he dictated all these things to me.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

EX ORE SUO LOQVEBATUR, QVASI LEGENS AD ME, OMNES SERMONES ISTOS) Distincte, nihil hæsitans, omnia ista mihi dictavit.

## 36:19
Verse 19.

GO AND HIDE THOU AND JEREMIAH) These men were not bad, and they foresaw the king's anger. See below 25.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

VADE ET ABSCONDERE TU ET JEREMIAS) Erant hi viri non mali, & prospiciebant regis iram. Vide infra 25.

## 36:21
Verse 21.

THE KING SENT JUDI) A man like the king, and therefore inseparable from him.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

MISIT REX JUDI) Hominem regi similem, eoque ei individuum.

## 36:22
Verse 22.

IN THE WINTER HOUSE) For kings used to change their chambers according to the time of the year. A HEARTH WAS SET) That is, a fire-pan. ἐσχάρα to the Greeks here: otherwise πυραύμη.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

IN DOMO HTEMALI Mutabant enim reges exedras, pro anni tempore. POSITA ERAT ARULA) Id est, batillus. ἐσχάρα Græcis hic: aliter πυραύμη.

## 36:23
Verse 23.

THREE PAGES, OR FOUR) In Hebrew: Doors. Thus are the titles of the sections called. The same is פצין in Chaldean. HE CUT IT WITH THE SCRIBE'S PENKNIFE) With a writing knife, which the Greek epigrammatist calls σμίλην δονάκων ἀκροβελῶν γλυφίδα, another γλυφανῆ καλάμυ πλαστίῳ γλωχῖνα σιδήρῳ, another again χαλκὸν δονάκων τέκτονα λεπταλίων, another σμίλας ὀξυτόμον κοπίδα, another γλυπτῆρα σιδήρεον.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

TRES PAGELLAS, VEL QVATUOR) In Hebræo: Ostia. Sic vocantur tituli sectionum. Idem est פצין in Chaldaico. SCIDIT ILLUD SCALPELLO SCRIBÆ) Cultello scriptorio, quod σμίλην δονάκων ἀκροβελῶν γλυφίδα, vocat Epigrammatarius Græcus, alius γλυφανῆ καλάμυ πλαστίῳ γλωχῖνα σιδήρῳ, rursus alius χαλκὸν δονάκων τέκτονα λεπταλίων, alius σμίλας ὀξυτόμον κοπίδα, alius γλυπτῆρα σιδήρεον.

## 36:24
Verse 24.

AND THEY DID NOT FEAR) So much the worse than those of whom [it is spoken] above 12, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET NON TIMUERUNT) Tanto pejores illis, de quibus supra 12, 16.

## 36:25
Verse 25.

THEY CONTRADICTED THE KING, THAT HE MIGHT NOT BURN THE BOOK) They entreated [him] against it. Thus the Hebrew and the Chaldean have it.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

CONTRADIXERUNT REGI, NE COMBURERET LIBRUM) Deprecati sunt. Sic habet Hebræum, & Chaldæus.

## 36:26
Verse 26.

BUT THE LORD HID THEM) He caused them not to be able to be found.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ABSCONDIT AUTEM EOS DOMINUS) Fecit ne inveniri possent.

## 36:28
Verse 28.

TAKE ANOTHER VOLUME) Take other parchments.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

TOLLE VOLUMEN ALIUD) Sume membranas alias.

## 36:29
Verse 29.

SAYING, WHY HAVE YOU WRITTEN ALL) This is what the king had ordered to be said to Jeremiah, if he had been found: Why have you written to this effect, that the King of Babylon is to come, etc. Kings do not want the truth to be told to them.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

DICENS, QVARE SCRIPSISTI OMNIA) Hoc est, quod rex jusserat dici Jeremiæ, si inventus esset: Cur scripsisti in istam sententiam, venturum Regem Babylonis, &c. Nolunt reges sibi vera dici.

## 36:30
Verse 30.

THERE SHALL NOT BE OF HIM WHO SHALL SIT UPON THE THRONE OF DAVID) That is, his posterity shall not remain on the throne of David. For Jeconiah his son, after a three-month reign, died without children. He went into captivity, 2 Kings 24, but he did not die without children: for seven or eight of his children are listed, 1 Chron. 3:17, and mention is made of his wives, Jer. 22:28. Furthermore, TO SIT upon the throne of David here seems to denote a tranquil and durable rule, as some explain it. AND HIS CORPSE SHALL BE CAST OUT TO THE HEAT BY DAY, AND TO THE FROST BY NIGHT) The same sense as above, 22:18.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

NON ERIT EX EO QVI SEDEAT SVPER SOLIUM DAVID) Id est, non manebit in solio Davidis ejus posteritas. Nam Jechonias filius ejus post trimestre regnum sine liberis decessit. In captivitatem abiit 2. Regum 24. non autem sine liberis obiit: nam recensentur septem vel octo ejus liberi 1. Par. 3, 17. & feminis ejus mentio fit Jerem. 22, 28. Cæterum SEDERE super solium David hic imperium tranquillum & durabile notare videtur uti nonnulli explicant. ET CADAVER EJUS PROJICIETVR AD ÆSTUM PER DIEM, ET AD GELU PER NOCTEM) Idem sensus qui supra 22, 18.

## 36:31
