Ver. 31. WHICH I HAVE SPOKEN TO THEM) In that volume. AND THEY HAVE NOT HEARD) They were unwilling to admit it into their mind.

Latin:

Vers. 31. QVOD LOCUTVS SUM AD EOS) In isto volumine. ET NON AUDIERUNT) Noluerunt in animum admittere.

## 36:32
Ver. 32.

AND MOREOVER THERE WERE ADDED MANY MORE WORDS THAN HAD BEEN BEFORE) In the Hebrew: Like these: that is, of a similar argument.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ET INSUPER ADDITI SUNT SERMONES MULTO PLURES QVAM ANTEA FUERANT) In Hebræo: Ut isti: id est, simili argumento.

## 37:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVII.

Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to pray for him, who, after the Chaldeans left the city because of Pharaoh, prophesies that they will return and burn the city: and intending to leave the city, he is imprisoned, but being consulted by Zedekiah, and predicting captivity to him, he is rescued and kept in the courtyard, and is fed.

Ver. 1.

AND KING ZEDEKIAH THE SON OF JOSIAH REIGNED INSTEAD OF JECONIAH THE SON OF JEHOIAKIM. Josiah had four sons: Jehoiakim, who is also Eliakim; Shallum, of whom Jer. 22:11; Zedekiah; and Johanan the firstborn, of whom see what we observed at 1 Chron. 3:15, so that you do not err here with many interpreters. Concerning the succession or substitution of Zedekiah in the place of Jeconiah, see 2 Kings 24:15, 17.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVII.

Sedekias petit Ieremiam ut pro se oret, qui relicta ob Pharaonem à Chaldais urbe, vaticinatur eos redituros, & urbem exusturos: & egressurus ex urbe incarceratur, sed à Zedekia consultus, eique captivitatem prædicens, ereptus in atrio asservatur, & cibatur.

Vers. 1.

ET REGNAVIT REX SEDECIAS FILIUS JOSIÆ PRO JECHONIA FILIO JOAKIM. Josias quatuor habuit filios, Jojakim qui & Eliakim, Sallum, de quo Jerem. 22, 11. Zedekiam & Johanan primogenitum, de quo vid. quæ ad 1. Par. 3, 15. observavimus, ne cum multis Interpp. hic aberres. De successione vel surrogatione Zedekiæ in locum Jechoniæ vid. 1. Reg. 24, 15. 17.

## 37:3
Ver. 3.

PRAY FOR US TO THE LORD OUR GOD) Uncertain of his plans, he did not know where to turn. FOR THEY HAD NOT YET PUT HIM INTO THE CUSTODY OF THE PRISON) That is, not yet: for afterwards he was put into prison below in chapter 14, and there he had those visions which Jeremiah had already recorded earlier in the prophecies, 32 and 33.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ORA PRO NOBIS DOMINUM DEUM NOSTRUM) Incertus consiliorum, nesciebat quo se verteret. NON ENIM MISERANT EUM IN CUSTODIAM CARCERIS) Id est, nondum: nam postea datus est in carcerem infra 14. & ibi visa illa habuit, quæ jam ante in Prophetias retulit Jeremias 32. & 33.

## 37:4
Ver. 4.

THEY HAD DEPARTED FROM JERUSALEM.) At which time the King and the princes rescinded the decree concerning the freedom of the common people, as we had in 34.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

RECESSERUNT AB JERUSALEM.) Quo tempore Rex & principes resciderunt decretum de popularium libertate, ut habuimus 34.

## 37:6
Verse 6.

BEHOLD THE ARMY OF PHARAOH, WHICH HAS COME FORTH TO YOUR AID, SHALL RETURN TO THE LAND) He did not dare to go against the Babylonian, who for that reason had departed from the siege of Jerusalem, having left garrisons in other towns. See 2 Kings 24:7. Verse 7. AND THE CHALDEANS SHALL RETURN) They shall return to resume the siege.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ECCE EXERCITUS PHARAONIS, QVI EGRESSUS EST VOBIS IN AUXILIUM, REVERTETUR IN TERRAM) Non ausus obviam ire Babylonio, qui ob id ab obsidione Hierosolymorum discesserat, relictis per alia oppida præsidiis. Vide 2. Reg. 24, 7. Vers. 7. ET REDIENT CHALDÆI) Redibunt ad repetendam obsidionem.

## 37:9
Verse 9

EVERY ONE) Of those wounded men. So great is God's anger against you that even a few wounded men are sufficient for your destruction.

Latin:

Vers. 9

SINGULI) Istorum vulneratorum. Tanta est Dei in vos ira, ut vel pauci saucii ad vestram perniciem sufficiant.

## 37:11
Verse 11.

AND THAT HE MIGHT DIVIDE THE POSSESSION THERE IN THE SIGHT OF THE CITIZENS) חלק indeed also signifies to divide: but also to draw out, in which meaning it is often found among the Talmudists: so that the sense is not inconvenient, that he might withdraw himself from the sight of the citizens, namely, the Jerusalemites. Which explanation also commended itself to the LXX, Pagninus, Arias, and B. Hülsemann.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET DIVIDERET IBI POSSESSIONEM IN CONSPECTU CIVIUM) חלק quidem partiri quoque significat: verum etiam extrahere, quo significatu sæpe reperitur apud Thalmudicos: ita ut sensus sit non incommodus, ut subduceret se de conspectu civium, Hierosolymitanorum scilicet. Quæ explicatio LXX. Pagnini, & Ariæ etiam sese probavit B. Hülsemanno.

## 37:12
Verse 12.

SON OF ANANIAH) To whom Jeremiah had predicted death above in 28. The grandson wished to avenge that death as if it had not been predicted, but inflicted by Jeremiah.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

FILII ANANIÆ) Cui mortem prædixerat Jeremias supra 28. Eam mortem quasi non prædicta, sed illata fuisset ab Jeremia, vindicare voluit nepos.

## 37:14
INTO THE PRISON THAT WAS IN THE HOUSE OF JONATHAN THE SCRIBE) One of the court scribes. For this prison was in the court. See above 32. Verse 16. INTO THE HOUSE OF THE PIT, AND INTO THE DUNGEON) Better: into the house of the prison (the inner one, that is) and into the cells. He understands those which they now call gaols: a sad dwelling.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN CARCEREM QVI ERAT IN DOMO JONATHAN SCRIBÆ) Unius ex aulicis scribis. Nam carcer hic in aula erat. Vide supra 32. Vers. 16. IN DOMUM LACI, ET IN ERGASTULUM) Melius: in domum carceris (interiorem scilicet) & in cellulas. Eas intelligit, quas nunc geolas vocant: triste habitaculum.

## 37:16
HE TOOK HIM) He ordered him to be brought to him secretly. IS THERE A WORD FROM THE LORD) Is there (supply, for you) a word from the Lord? Can you now, even at this time, predict something certain for us? Verse 17. FOR YOU HAVE SENT ME INTO THE HOUSE OF THE PRISON) A gloomy and dark place. Verse 20. IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON) Where he could both enjoy the sky and be visited by friends. See above 32. AND THAT A LOAF OF BREAD MIGHT BE GIVEN TO HIM DAILY, EXCEPT FOR THE POTTAGE) And that a piece of bread might be given to him daily from the street of the bakers. Thus the Chaldean: which agrees very well with the Hebrew. Large loaves were accustomed to be made. From them, portions, μέριδες, κλάσματα, were given to individuals. The Vulgate is rightly corrected. There is nothing in the Hebrew about pottage. AND JEREMIAH REMAINED IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON) Until he was transferred to a worse place, as we shall have in the following chapter.

Latin:

TULIT EUM) Jussit clam eum ad se deduci. PUTASNE EST SERMO A DOMINO) An est (supple, tibi) sermo à Domino? An nunc etiam hoc tempore certi aliquid nobis potes prædicere? Vers. 17. QVIA MISISTI ME IN DOMUM CARCERIS) Locum tetrum ac tenebricosum. Vers. 20. IN VESTIBULO CARCERIS) Ubi & cælo frui poterat, & ab amicis adiri. Vide supra 32. ET DARETUR EI TORTA PANIS QUOTIDIE, EXCEPTO PULMENTO) Et daretur ei frustum panis quotidie de vico pistorum. Sic Chaldæus: quæ optime cum Hebræo conveniunt. Panes grandes fieri solebant. Ex iis partes μέριδες, κλάσματα singulis dabantur. Recte corrigitur vulg. Nihil in Ebræo de pulmento. ET MANSIT JEREMIAS IN VESTIBULO CARCERIS) Donec in pejorem locum transferretur, ut habebimus capite sequenti.

## 38:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVIII.

Jeremiah, persuading the people to surrender, is let down into a muddy pit, but is drawn out by Ebed-melech and, remaining in the court of the prison, is consulted by Zedekiah, to whom he advises a voluntary surrender if he wishes to be saved.

Ver. 1. GEDALIAH THE SON OF PASHUR) Of him concerning whom [see] chapter 20. AND JUCAL THE SON OF SHELEMIAH) Of him whose mention [is] above 36, 26.

AND PASHUR THE SON OF MALCHIAH) He is the very same who is named above 21, 1.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVIII.

Ieremias deditionem suadens populo in lacum luteosum demittitur, ab Ebedmelech autem educitur & in vestibulo carceris manens à Zedekia consulitur, cui spontaneam deditionem suadet si servari velit.

Vers. 1. GEDELIAS FILIUS PHASSUR) Illius de quo capite 20. ET JUCHAL FILIUS SEMELLÆ) Ejus cujus mentio supra 36, 26.

ET PHASSVR FILIVS MELCHIÆ) Is ipse est, qui nominatus est supra 21, 1.

## 38:4
Ver. 4.

FOR HE DELIBERATELY WEAKENS THE HANDS OF THE MEN OF WAR, WHO REMAINED IN THIS CITY) In the Hebrew: For by these (namely words) he weakens the hands of the men, &c. He breaks their spirits, by taking away all hope. Those are to be punished who have done anything by which the fickle minds of men might be held by superstition of the divine, as Modestinus teaches in L. Si quis aliquid, D. de pœnis. And to scrutinize the fates of the prince was a capital offense among the Romans: as Tacitus teaches us in Annal. 16. These things are true: but the command of God is above every law, and whatever He commands, He defends.

HE DOES NOT SEEK THE PEACE OF THIS PEOPLE) That is, their salvation.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

DE INDUSTRIA ENIM DISSOLVIT MANUS VIRORUM BELLANTIUM, QVI REMANSERUNT IN CIVITATE HAC) In Hebræo: Nam per ista (nempe verba) debilitat manus virorum, &c. Infringit illis animos, spem omnem adimendo. Puniendi sunt qui aliquid fecerint, quo leves hominum animi superstitione numinis tenerentur, ut docet Modestinus L. Si quis aliquid, D. de pœnis. Et principis fata scrutari capital apud Romanos: Ut Tacitus nos docet Annal. 16. Vera hæc: sed Dei jussus supra omnem legem est, & quicquid imperat, defendit.

NON QVÆRIT PACEM POPULO HUIC) Id est, salutem.

## 38:5
Ver. 5.

BEHOLD HE IS IN YOUR HANDS) In the hands of the Sanhedrin, whose duty it is to judge concerning a true or false Prophet.

FOR IT IS NOT LAWFUL FOR THE KING TO DENY YOU ANYTHING) In the Hebrew: For the King can do nothing against you: namely in that kind of matter, as we explained in book I. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 2, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ECCE IPSE IN MANIBUS VESTRIS EST) In manibus Synedrii, cujus est judicare de Propheta vero aut falso.

NEC ENIM FAS EST REGEM VOBIS QVICQVAM NEGARE) In Hebræo: Nam Rex nihil contra vos potest: nempe in isto rerum genere, ut explicavimus lib. I. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 2, 20.

## 38:6
Ver. 6.

SON OF AMELECH) Of which Amelech mention is made above 36, 26. But the Chaldean and the Greeks have taken it everywhere for the name of a king, thinking that both this Malchiah and that Jerahmeel were sons of some king.

INTO THE PIT IN WHICH THERE WAS NO WATER, BUT MIRE: SO JEREMIAH DESCENDED INTO THE MUD) Which he describes lamentably in his own misery in Lamentations 3, and Isaiah had predicted it 53, 8. Josephus: παραλαβόντες αὐτὸν εἰς τινα λάκκον βορβόρυ πλήρη καθιμήσαντο, ὅπως ἰδίῳ θανάτῳ πνιγεὶς ἀποθάνη. ὁ δὲ πρὸ τῶ αὐχένος ὑπὸ τῶ πλήθει περιεχείτο ἐν τούτοις ἧν.

Concerning the passage of Lamentations in its place. That Isaiah ch. 53 treated of Jeremiah is a Jewish fiction, which we have solidly refuted in the vindications of that chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

FILII AMELECH) Cujus Amelech mentio supra 36, 26. At Chaldæus & Græci urrobique pro nomine regis sumpserunt, putantes & hunc Melchiam & illum Jeremielem alicujus regum fuisse filios.

IN LACUM IN QUO NON ERAT AQVA, SED LUTUM: DESCENDIT ITAQVE JEREMIAS IN COENUM) Quæ hanc miseriam suam flebiliter describit Thren. 3. & prædixerat eam Esaias 53, 8. Josephus: παραλαβόντες αὐτὸν εἰς τινα λάκκον βορβόρυ πλήρη καθιμήσαντο, ὅπως ἰδίῳ θανάτῳ πνιγεὶς ἀποθάνη. ὁ δὲ πρὸ τῶ αὐχένος ὑπὸ τῶ πλήθει περιεχείτο ἐν τούτοις ἧν.

De loco Threnorum suo loco. Esaiam c. 53. de Jeremia egisse commentum est Judaicum, quod in Capit. istius vindiciis solide confutavimus.

## 38:7
Ver. 7.

ABDEMELECH THE ETHIOPIAN) Even then God wished to show from afar how just causes He had for calling foreign nations to salvation. The Ethiopian saves the Prophet whom the Jews were oppressing. The Gentiles believed in Christ, whom the Jews had crucified.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ABDEMELECH ÆTHIOPS) Jam tum eminus ostendere Deus voluit, quam justas causas haberet gentes extraneas ad salutem vocandi. Servat Æthiops Prophetam quem Judæi opprimebant. Gentes in Christum credidere, quem Judæi crucifixerant.

## 38:7
AT THE GATE OF BENJAMIN) Where he was accustomed to hear the requests of the citizens.

Latin:

IN PORTA BENJAMIN) Ubi desideria civium audire solebat.

## 38:9
CASTING HIM INTO THE PIT, THAT HE MAY DIE THERE OF FAMINE: FOR THERE IS NO MORE BREAD IN THE CITY) It is otherwise in the Hebrew: He would have died by himself of famine, because there is no more bread in the city: In this sense; there was no need for those seeking his death to transfer him to such a foul place; for even if they had left him in the vestibule of the prison, death awaited him from hunger, since bread had already failed. The Chaldean: He would have died in his place from famine. In that former place, namely.

Latin:

MITTENTES EUM IN LACUM, UT MORIATUR IBI FAME: NON SUNT ENIM PANES ULTRA IN CIVITATE) Aliter in Hebræo est: Mortuus fuisset per se à fame, quia non est ultra panis in urbe: Hoc sensu; nihil opus erat mortem ejus appetentibus eum transferre in locum tam fœdum; nam etiam si in vestibulo carceris eum reliquissent, ex fame mors eum manebat, quippe cum panes jam defecerint. Chaldæus: Mortuus esset in loco suo præ fame. In loco scilicet illo priore.

## 38:11
Vers. 11.

HE ENTERED THE KING'S HOUSE WHICH WAS UNDER THE CELLAR) אל־תחת signifies sometimes treasures, sometimes storehouses, by which word the Greeks sometimes translated that Hebrew term. It is credible that this place, into which Abdemelech descended, was beneath the storehouse, where rags worn out by use were thrown away.

HE TOOK THENCE OLD RAGS, AND OLD THINGS WHICH HAD ROTTED) In the Hebrew: Old things of drawings and old things of corruptions: That is, rags torn or worn out by use. Concerning this word מלחים see what we have said at Mark 9, 49.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

INGRESSUS EST DOMVM REGIS QVÆ ERAT SVB CELLARIO) אל־תחת modo thesauros, modo apothecas significat, qua voce Hebræam illam interdum verterunt Græci. Credibile est hunc locum, in quem descendit Abdemelech, fuisse subter cellam penuriam, quo peniculi usu detriti abjiciebantur.

TULIT INDE VETERES PANNOS, ET ANTIQVA QVÆ COMPTVRVERANT) In Hebræo: Vetera tractionum & vetera corruptionum: Id est penicillos laceratos vel usu detritos. De voce hac מלחים vide quæ diximus ad Marcum 9, 49.

## 38:12
Vers. 12.

UNDER THE CUBIT OF THY HANDS) Under the armpits of thy hands: that is, of thy arms.

UPON THE ROPES) In the Hebrew: under (those rags, place) the ropes: namely, so that the ropes might not injure the naked or semi-naked man,

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SVB CVBITO MANVVM TVARVM) Sub axillis manuum tuarum: id est, brachiorum tuorum.

SVPER FVNES) In Hebræo: subter (eos peniculos, pone) funes: nempe quo minus funes læderent hominem nudum, aut seminudum,

## 38:13
Vers. 13.

IN THE VESTIBULE OF THE PRISON) Where he had been before, 37, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

IN VESTIBVLO CARCERIS) Vbi ante fuerat, 37, 20.

## 38:14
Vers. 14.

HE TOOK JEREMIAH TO HIMSELF) Take as above 37, 16.

AT THE THIRD ENTRY WHICH WAS IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) At the third entrance which went into the House of the Lord, That is, into the Temple. See 1 Kings 10, 5. 12. 1 Chron. 26, 16. 18. 2 Chron. 9, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

TVLIT AD SE JEREMIAM) Sume ut supra 37, 16.

AD OSTIVM TERTIVM QVOD ERAT IN DOMO DOMINI) Ad introitum tertium qui ibat in Domum Domini, Id est, in Templum. Vide 1. Reg. 10, 5. 12. 1.Par. 26, 16. 18. 2. Par. 9, 11.

## 38:15
Verse 15.

IF I SHALL DECLARE TO THEE) He believed that he would again ask something about the outcome of the siege, which was true,

SHALT THOU NOT PUT ME TO DEATH) That is, surely thou wilt put me to death. He was making that conjecture from the preceding events. See the preceding chapter, and this one in which we now are.

AND IF I SHALL GIVE THEE COUNSEL, THOU WILT NOT HEAR ME) He speaks according to that which was credible, For having been often warned he had become no better.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

SI ANNVNCIAVERO TIBI) Credebat illum iterum de obsidionis eventu aliquid interrogaturum, quod verum erat,

NUMQUID NON INTERFICIES ME) Id est, profecto interficies me. Eam conjecturam faciebat ex rebus antecedentibus. Vide caput præcedens, & hoc in quo nunc sumus.

ET SI CONSILIUM DEDERO TIBI, NON ME AUDIES) Loquitur secundum id quod erat credibile, Nam sæpe monitus nihilo factus erat melior.

## 38:16
Verse 16.

THE LORD LIVETH, WHO MADE US THIS SOUL) That is, who gave us this life. Even evil kings are accustomed to be struck by some fear of the divine in great dangers. See Suetonius Caligula 4, 51.

INTO THE HANDS OF THE MEN) Who were named at the beginning of the chapter, and who through the Sanhedrin, of which they were a part, easily hoped that they could obtain the death of the Prophet.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

VIVIT DOMINUS, QVI FECIT NOBIS ANIMAM HANC) Id est, qui nobis hanc vitam dedit. Solent reges etiam mali in magnis periculis aliquo numinis metu percelli. Vide Suetonium Caligula 4, 51.

IN MANUS VIRORUM) Qui nominati initio capitis, quique per Synedrium, cujus pars erant, facile sperabant obtinere se posse mortem Prophetæ.

## 38:17
Verse 17.

IF THOU SHALT GO FORTH TO THE PRINCES OF THE KING OF BABYLON) That is, if thou shalt go to surrender thyself. He does not say if thou shalt go to the king. For he would not have valued him so much, that he would have wished to admit a violator of a treaty to his presence.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

SI PROFECTUS EXIERIS AD PRINCIPES REGIS BABYLONIS) Id est, si te eas deditum. Non dicit si eas ad regem. Non enim tanti eum fecisset, ut fœderis violatorem admittere ad suum aspectum voluisset.

## 38:20
Verse 20.

THEY SHALL NOT DELIVER THEE) God knows not only those things which are about to happen, but also those which would be about to happen, if this or that were done, partly because all the affections of men are most thoroughly known to Him, and partly because by His omnipotent power He can both turn affections and hinder any effects whatsoever even without it.

Thus in Matt. 11, v. 21, it is intimated that God foresaw that the Tyrians and Sidonians would have done penance if they had seen the miracles of Christ. 1 Sam. 23, 12, that the Keilites would have delivered up David if he had remained among them. God foreknew these things not in effect, which was never to be, but in the cause under a hypothesis, namely, given such or such circumstances: which, however, did not exist; whence it follows that future contingencies, even conditional ones, are of determined truth, and have their being, but a conditional one: and that the decrees of God concerning the fortunate or unfortunate events of men do not infer upon men or secondary causes a necessity of operating in such a way that the event foreseen by God follows therefore, or from the foreknowledge of God or even because of the decree of God, but rather that the decrees were made in God from the foreknowledge of the free human motion, and infer only the certainty of the events, which otherwise were to follow from the motion of secondary causes: which the blessed Hulseman not undeservedly observes here not only against the Calvinists, but also the Papists, who contend that the predetermination of all human acts, whether they be good or evil, is so made by God that they are carried by their own nature toward that end, in the way that God has decreed, nor can they be omitted by man; which the Jesuits, Paul Petr. de Cellis in his peculiar book on the conformity of the doctrine of Calvin, and Bannis, demonstrate to be most Calvinistic. For that appears most clearly from these examples, just as God does not decree that which He perceives men will not do by free will (e.g. that the Chaldeans will not deliver Zedekiah to the Jews) so conversely He decrees that to some certain end, which He foresees will otherwise happen by the free will of men, and thus by His decree He infers no necessitation, if I may so speak, of the human will, nor does He predetermine it so that it must necessarily act in such a way, and cannot not act in such a way, and thus take away its liberty. See Vol. 2, Syst. Theol., ch. 10, q. 6, p. 525.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

NON TE TRADENT) Deus non ea tantum novit quæ eventura sunt, sed & quæ eventura essent, si hoc vel illud fieret, partim quod omnes hominum affectus ipsi perspectissimi sunt, partim quod vi sua omnipotente & affectus vertere, & effectus quosvis etiam sine eo impedire possit.

Sic Matth. 11. v. 21. innuitur Deum prævidisse Tyrios & Sidonios pœnitentiam acturos, si miracula Christi vidissent. 1. Sam. 23, 12. Kegilitas Davidem tradituros fuisse, si penes illos mansisset. Præsciebat hæc Deus non in effectu, qui nunquam erat futurus, sed in causa sub hypothesi, positis sc. talibus vel talibus circumstantiis: quæ vero non extitere; unde sequitur futura contingentia etiam conditionalia esse determinatæ veritatis, & habere suum esse, sed conditionatum: ac decreta Dei de fortunatis vel infortunatis hominum eventibus non inferre hominibus vel causis secundis necessitatem ita operandi, ut eventus à Deo prævisus consequatur ideo, seu ex prævisione Dei vel ob decretum etiam Dei, sed ex prævisione potius liberi motus humani decreta in Deo facta esse, & certitudinem solum eventuum inferre, qui alias ex motione causarum secundarum secuturi erant: quod non tantum contra Calvinianos, sed etiam Pontificios hic non immerito observat B. Hulseman. qui prædeterminationem omnium actuum humanorum sive boni sive mali sint, ita à Deo factam esse contendunt, ut sua natura ferantur in illum finem, quomodo Deus decrevit, nec possint ab homine omitti; quem Jesuitæ, Calvinissimum Paul. Petr. de Cellis demonstravis lib. peculiari de conform. doct. Calvini, & Bannis. Id enim ex istis exemplis apparet luculentissime, quemadmodum Deus non decernit id, quod homines libera voluntate non facturos cernit (v. g. non tradituros Chaldæos Zedekiam Judæis) ita ex adverso eum id decernere ad certum aliquem finem, quod libera hominum voluntate alias eventurum prævidet, adeoque suo decreto nullam inferre voluntatis humanæ necessitationem, ut ita loquar, nec eam prædeterminare, ut necessario ita agat, nec possit non ita agere, adeoque libertatem ejus tollere, Vid. T. 2. Syst. Theol. c. 10. q. 6. p. 525.

## 38:22
Verse 22.

ALL THE WOMEN WHO REMAINED IN THE HOUSE OF THE KING OF JUDAH) Who were either Jehoiakim's or Jeconiah's.

THEY THEMSELVES SHALL SAY: THEY HAVE SEDUCED THEE) They themselves shall say that you were seduced by those whom he will now describe.

THE MEN OF THY PEACE) That is, thy friends, as in Psalm 41, v. 10; understand the Egyptians, the pseudo-prophets, certain of the nobles.

THEY HAVE SUNK THY FEET IN THE MIRE AND IN THE SLIPPERY PLACE) They will say that they were the ones who involved you in inexplicable evils.

AND THEY HAVE DEPARTED FROM THEE) That is, that they indeed have gone back. They immediately led back the army of Egypt, with the false prophets and the nobles, who had been most ready before the dangers, fleeing to the Chaldeans when the danger was pressing: see above 19.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

OMNES MULIERES QVÆ REMANSERUNT IN DOMO REGIS JUDA) Quæ aut Joakimi, aut Jechoniæ fuerunt.

IPSÆ DICENT: SUBDUXERVNT TE) Ipsæ dicent te seductum ab his quos jam describet.

VIRI PACIFICI TUI) Id est, amici tui, ut Psalm 41, v. 10. intellige Ægyptios, Pseudo-prophetas, procerum quosdam,

DEMERSERUNT IN COENO ET IN LUBRICO PEDES TUOS) Dicent illos fuisse, qui te involverunt inexplicabilibus malis.

ET RECESSERUNT A TE) Id est, illos vero retro abiisse. Ægypti Exercitum statim reduxere, Pseudoprophetarum & procerum, qui ante pericula promptissimi fuerant, urgente periculo transfugere ad Chaldæos: supra 19.

## 38:23
Ver. 23. AND ALL THY WIVES, AND THY SONS) The discourse ascends, for it comes nearer and nearer to him himself.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET OMNES UXORES TUÆ, ET FILII TUI) Scandit oratio, propius enim propiusque ad ipsum venit.

## 38:24
Ver. 24. LET NO MAN KNOW THESE WORDS, AND THOU SHALT NOT DIE) That is, if you do not bring these things to the common people, I will keep you safe.

Latin:

Vers. 24. NULLUS SCIAT VERBA HÆC, ET NON MORIERIS) Id est, si hæc in vulgus non proferas, salvum te præstabo.

## 38:26
Ver. 26. I PRESENTED MY SUPPLICATION BEFORE THE KING) That is, with body prostrate I prayed to the king. We had a similar expression above 36, 7.

INTO THE HOUSE OF JONATHAN.) Into that inner and dark prison, of which above 37, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 26. PROSTRAVI EGO PRECES MEAS CORAM REGE) Id est, prostrato corpore regem oravi. Similem locutionem habuimus supra 36, 7.

IN DOMUM JONATHAN.) In carcerem illum interiorem ac tenebricosum, de quo supra 37, 14.

## 38:27
Ver. 27. AND HE SPOKE TO THEM ACCORDING TO ALL THE WORDS, WHICH THE KING HAD COMMANDED HIM) To tell a part of the truth is not to lie.

Therefore these things do not favor Jesuitical equivocations, for it was true that the King had spoken with Jeremiah about that dark prison in the house of Jonathan. If you say: but Jeremiah had not asked here that he might not be sent into it. It can be answered, although this is not mentioned here, it seems nevertheless that he had prayed for this to the King, just as in the preceding chapter, verse 19, he had prayed for the same thing, which Cornel. a Lapide acknowledges. Since the King himself orders it to be indicated to the princes, and Jeremiah had vehemently abhorred this worst of prisons. Not to speak of some matter before an inferior, if a superior Magistrate has forbidden it, if no necessity urges, if no damage or utility follows accordingly, or if the inconvenience which was to result from the revelation was greater than the convenience which underlies the reticence, can neither be called an equivocation, nor a sin, but obedience rendered to the command of the King, with which the equivocations of the Jesuits have nothing in common: which has been observed here by B. Hülsemann correctly against the Jesuit Creswell under the name of Φιλόπατρος against the edict of the Queen of England, section 3, and against Andreas Eudæmon-Joannes in his Apology for Garnet, chapter 11, who abuse this passage of Jeremiah for asserting their own equivocations.

Ver. same. AND THEY CEASED FROM HIM) They did not drag him to the Sanhedrin.

FOR NOTHING HAD BEEN HEARD) Concerning those things which the king had asked him, and which he himself had answered.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET LOCUTUS EST EIS JUXTA OMNIA VERBA, QUÆ PRÆCEPERAT EI REX) Partem veri dicere non est mentiri.

Non ergo hæc favent æquivocationibus Jesui- ticis, verum enim erat, quod Rex cum Jeremia lo- quutus fuerit de illo carcere tenebricoso in domo Jonathan. Si dicas: at non petierat hic Jeremias, ut ne in illum dimitteretur. Responderi potest, etsi hoc non commemoratur hic sit, videri tamen id orai- se Regem, quemadmodum cap. præced. vers. 19. idem oraverat, quod agnoscit Cornel. a Lapide. Siqui- dem Rex ipse id indicare principibus jubeat, & ve- hementer abhorruerit ab hoc pessimo carcere Je- remias. Non loqui rem aliquam coram inferiore, si superior Magistratus interdixerit, si nulla necessitas urgeat, si nullum damnum vel utilitas perinde con- sequatur, vel si incommodum, quod ex revelatio- ne futurum erat, majus fuerit commodo, quod reti- centiæ subest, neque æquivocatio dici potest, neq; peccatum, sed mandato Regis præstita obedientia, cum qua Jesuitarum æquivocationes nihil com- mune habent: quod hic recte adversus Jesuitam Cresvel sub nomine Φιλόπατρος adv. edictum Re- ginæ Angliæ sect. 3. & Andream Eudæmon Johan- nem Apol. pro Garnetto cap. 11. hoc loco Jeremiæ pro æquivocationibus suis adserendis abutentes B. Hülsemanno observatum est.

Vers. eod. ET CASSAVERUNT AB EO) Non tra- xerunt eum ad Synedrium.

NIHIL ENIM FUERAT AUDITUM) De iis, quæ rex eum interrogaverat, quæque ipse responderat.

## 38:28
Ver. 28. BUT JEREMIAH REMAINED IN THE COURT OF THE PRISON) Of which 32, 2. ch. 33. ch. 37, 20.

UNTIL THE DAY THAT JERUSALEM WAS TAKEN.) As appears below 39, 13.

AND IT CAME TO PASS, THAT JERUSALEM WAS TAKEN) These words are better referred to the following chapter, so that the first and second clauses have the force of a parenthesis, and in the third the conjunction is redundant.

The censure is rashly exercised by this Aristarchus of ours upon the authentic text. Why should those not be left to the present chapter? What need is there of a parenthesis, or even of the deletion of the conjunction! However much, therefore, the LXX and some interpreters, Rabanus, Hugo, and Thomas, draw them to the following chapter, there is nevertheless no necessity for deferring or changing the authentic text.

Latin:

Vers. 28. MANSIT VERO JEREMIAS IN VESTIBULO CARCERIS) De quo 32, 2. c. 33. c. 37, 20.

USQVE AD DIEM, QVO CAPTA EST JERUSALEM.) Ut apparet infra 39, 13.

ET FACTUM EST, UT CAPERETUR JERUSALEM) Hæc verba melius ad caput sequens referen- tur, ut primum & secundum comma παρενθέσεως vim ha- beant, & in tertio abundet copula.

Temere censura exercetur ab hoc Aristarcho nostro in textum authenticum. Cur non relinquen- da illa capiti præsenti? Quid opus παρενθέσεως, vel etiam deletione copulæ! Utut ergo LXX. & interpp. nonnulli Raban. Hugo & Thomas ad sequens caput ea trahant, nulla tamen necessitas est deferendi vel immutandi textum authenticum.

## 39:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIX. The city having been stormed, while Zedekiah attempts to flee he is captured, and his children having been killed before his eyes, he himself is deprived of his eyes, and in chains is led away to Babylon; the palace and other buildings having been set on fire, and most of the inhabitants having been led away, while others are made tributary, Jeremiah is preserved, and the safety promised to Ebed-melech is performed.

Ver. 1. IN THE NINTH YEAR OF ZEDEKIAH KING OF JUDAH, IN THE TENTH MONTH CAME NEBUCHADNEZZAR.

This year was the 3414th of the World and the 9th of the Sabbatical reign of Zedekiah. In the 10th month of it, on the 10th day, Nebuchadnezzar and all his forces pitched their camp near Jerusalem, c. 52, 4. 2 Kings 25, in memory of which event an annual fast has been observed by the Jews not only during the time of the captivity, Zech. 8, 19, but even to this very day. On the same day the siege of the city was revealed to Ezekiel in Chaldea, and the Prophet's wife died, whom he is forbidden to follow with mourning, for the sake of signifying the most grievous calamities of the Jews which would exceed all mourning, Ezek. 24, 1. 2. In the same year Jeremiah, by God's command, announces to King Zedekiah that Jerusalem is to be taken and burned by the King of Babylon, but that the King himself is to be led away to Babylon, and dying there is to be buried honorably, Jer. 34, 1. 7. But when, upon the forces of Pharaoh Hophra having gone out from Egypt to bring aid to Zedekiah, the Chaldeans met them, having left Jerusalem—whom the Prophet indicates would return, c. 37, 3. 10—the Jerusalemites, freed from the present fear of the siege, drew back the servants whom they had manumitted in that Sabbatical year according to the prescription of the law; for which reason Jeremiah predicts to them that the siege would be renewed and the city burned, c. 34, 11. 21. And while the Chaldean forces were away, as he was going out of the city, he was struck by the Princes and thrown into the pit of the prison in the house of Jonathan, Jer. 37, 11. 14. Furthermore, the army of Pharaoh having been put to flight, Nebuchadnezzar renewed the Jerusalemite siege in the following year, M. 3415, of the deported Jeconiah, and the 10th of Zedekiah, around the 5th day of the 3rd month, namely 390 days before the city was taken, as can be gathered from the type in Ezek. 5, 5. 8. Then indeed Jeremiah, being consulted by Zedekiah, gave an answer concerning delivering him into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, and was freed from the pit, c. 37, 11. 21. But the siege being continued, Jeremiah, being consulted again by Zedekiah through messengers, returns a similar answer: that both the King and the citizens are to be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar; that those who are to remain in the city will die by the sword, or by famine, or by pestilence, but those who are to go out to the Chaldeans will possess their life in place of spoil, c. 21. On account of which answer he is thrown by the Princes into the pit of Malchiah, which was in the court of the prison, but by the work of Ebed-melech he is led out and consulted again by King Zedekiah, and with the prophecy repeated against Judea, he is kept in the court of the prison until the city was taken, c. 38, 15. 18. Therefore, that time during which the siege was lifted on account of the arrival of Pharaoh must altogether be included in the two-year period of the siege, c. 37, 4. as Jerome and other ancients rightly observed, but the opinion of Hugo, Thomas, Castrius, and others is not to be approved, that the first siege had already been lifted before the ninth year of Zedekiah.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIX. Urbe expugnata, dum effugere conatur Sede- kias capitur, & necatis coram oculis ejus li- beris ejus, oculis privatur ipse, ac vinctus Ba- bylonem abducitur, Regia ædibusque aliis accensis, & abductis plerisque incolis, aliis autem tributariis factis servatur Jeremias, & Ebedmelecho incolumitas promissa præ- statur.

Vers. 1. ANNO NONO SEDECIÆ REGIS JUDA, MENSE DECIMO VENIT NABUCHODONOSOR.

Annus hic erat Mundi 3414. & Sabbatarii regni Sedekiæ 9. Mense ejus 10, d. 10. Nebucadne- zar, & omnes copiæ ejus castra juxta Hierosoly- mam posuerunt, c. 52, 4. 2. Reg. 25. in cujus rei me- moriam non solum captivitatis tempore, Zach. 8, 19. sed etiam ad hodiernum usq; diem jejunium annu- um a Judæis observatum est. Eodem die obsidio ur- bis Ezechieli in Chaldæa revelata est, & uxor Pro- phetæ mortua, quam luctu prosequi vetatur, gra- vissimas Judæorum calamitates luctum omnem su- peraturas innuendi gratia, Ezech. 24, 1.2. Eodem an- no Jeremias, Deo jubente Sedekiæ Regi prənun- ciat Hierosolymam a Rege Babyloniæ capiendam & comburendam, Regem vero ipsum in Babyloni- am abducendum, ibidemque morientem honorifi- ce sepeliendum Jer. 34, 1. 7. Quum vero Pharaonis Hophra copiis Ægypto egressis, ut suppetias fer- rent Zedekiæ, Chaldæi occurrerent relicta Hiero- solyma, quos reversuros Propheta indicat c. 37, 3. 10. Hierosolymitani præsenti obsidionis metu liberati, servos, quos anno illo Sabbatario ex legis præscri- pto manumiserant, retraxere: quibus proinde Je- remias obsidionem redintegrandam, & urbis com- bustionem prædicit c. 34, 11. 21. & dum abessent co- piæ Chaldæorum urbe egrediens a Principibus cæ- sus in foveam carceris in domo Jonathanis conji- citur, Jer. 37, 11. 14. Porro fugato Pharaonis exer- citu Hierosolymitanam obsidionem redintegravit Nebucadnezar anno sequenti M. 3415. Jechoniæ deportati, ac Zedekiæ 10. circa 5. diem 3. Mensis, diebus videlicet 390. ante captam urbem, ut e typo Ezech. 5, 5. 8. colligere est. Tum vero Jeremias a Zedekia consultus, de eo in manus Nebucadneza- ris tradendo responsum dedit, & ex fovea libera- tus est cap. 37, 11. 21. continuata vero obsidione Jere- mias iterum a Sedekia per legatos consultus simile reddit responsum & Regem & cives in manum Ne- bucadnez. tradendos; eos, qui in civitate mansuri sunt, gladio, aut fame, aut peste morituros, eos au- tem, qui ad Chaldæos egressuri sunt, vita sua loco spolii potituros, c. 21. ob quod responsum a Princi- pibus in foveam Malchiæ, quæ erat in atrio carceris, conjicitur, sed opera Ebedmelech eductus a Rege Sedekia denuo consulitur, & repetito vaticinio contra Judæam in atrio carceris usque ad urbem ca- ptam servatur, c. 38, 15. 18. Biennio ergo obsidionis includendum omnino est tempus illud, quo ob ad- ventum Pharaonis obsidio soluta est c. 37, 4. ut re- cte Hieronymus aliique veteres observarunt, non ve- ro probanda Hugonis, Thomæ, Castrii, & aliorum sententia, quod prima obsidio ante nonum Zede- kiæ annum jam soluta fuerit.

## 39:2
Ver. 2. FIFTH MONTH) The error is not of the interpreter, but of the scribe, who wrote 5 instead of 9. For the Hebrew codices, the Greek, and the Chaldaic agree here. Nor do the same codices, and the Latin itself, say otherwise in 2 Kings 25, 3, and below in this book 52, 6.

Why then did the Roman Pontiff not correct but canonize the error? It is strange that Cornelius a Lapide has dared to defend the error even now, and indeed by the authority of the LXX and Hebrew codices, which nevertheless consistently have the ninth, as Grotius admits here. But that in 2 Kings 25, 8, the city is said to have been burned at last on the seventh day of the FIFTH month, is because after it was taken by the occupation of the middle gate on the ninth day of the fourth month, Jer. 39, 3, then the King was caught, v. 5, and led captive to the King of Babylon staying in Riblah, and was condemned there, v. 6. 7, the city was finally burned with fire applied to the buildings, and on the tenth day, which was the Sabbath, the temple and the King's palace were burned with the remaining buildings. Compare Jer. 52, 53, with c. 39, 8. For for those things a monthly space was easily required.

Vers. eod. THE CITY WAS OPENED) That is, as historians speak, the city was laid bare by ruins. Vers. 3. AND ALL ENTERED) They rushed in with force, AND SAT IN THE MIDDLE GATE) Which divided the two parts of the city. To sit here is to fix a station. For Jerusalem was surrounded by two walls, vers. 4. The first wall therefore was already occupied, Vers. eod. NEREGEL - SERESER SEMEGARNABA) Since two are named here by the name Neregel-Sereser, it is credible that they were distinguished here by their offices: סמגר נבו seems to be the guardian of the Temple of Nabo, so that he is in place of ἐπιστάτης. He who is named first here, and prince, Neregel-Sereser, is believed to be Niriglossor, who, after Evil-Merodach was killed, occupied the kingdom. RAB-SARIS) That is, prefect of the eunuchs. RAB-MAG) Prince of the magi. You will find all these names so corrupted in Josephus that you will scarcely recognize the traces. Vers. 4. BY THE WAY OF THE KING'S GARDEN) That is, through some crypt. AND BY THE GATE WHICH WAS BETWEEN THE TWO WALLS) That is, the gate itself was outside the wall, and it itself, as happens in sieges, was obstructed by a wall, whence it was necessary to dig through that wall so that an exit might be open to the king, Ezek. 12, 12. AND THEY WENT OUT BY THE WAY OF THE DESERT) By the level way. The Greeks, having retained the Hebrew word, διὰ τὴν ὁδὸν Ἀραϐά. That is the way toward Jericho, as the following things show. Vers. 5. IN REBLATHA, IN THE LAND OF EMATH) Concerning which see 2 Kings 17, 24. Emath the lesser, afterwards called Epiphania by Antiochus Epiphanes, as Jerome testifies at Amos 6, 2. in the province of Syria, Reblatha, a most pleasant place, where Nebuchadnezzar sat down, so that he might watch the success of the war from a distance, and be nearer to Chaldea, and send reinforcements from there to his own against the Jews. Vers. eod. AND HE SPOKE JUDGMENTS TO HIM) That is, against him, as a breaker of the covenant, he passed sentence, in the way Tullus did to Mettius Fufetius. Vers. 7. HE ALSO PUT OUT THE EYES OF ZEDEKIAH. Thus blinded, he was led to Epiphania, and shut up like a wild beast in a cage to Babylon; which he could not see, as was predicted in Ezek. 12, 13. Thus Zedekiah was punished for infidelity and ingratitude, because, having been made King by Nebuchadnezzar in place of Jehoiachin, he had violated the covenant entered into. Vers. 9. AND THE REMAINDER OF THE PEOPLE, WHO HAD REMAINED IN THE CITY) Except, as he will now say, the very poor, from whom he feared nothing: as the following things show. AND THE FUGITIVES, WHO HAD FLED TO HIM) Concerning whom see above 38, 19. AND THE SUPERFLUOUS OF THE COMMON PEOPLE, WHO HAD REMAINED) That is, those who remained from the smaller towns and fields after such great slaughters. See what has been said on this history in the book of Kings. Vers. 11. BUT NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON HAD COMMANDED CONCERNING JEREMIAH TO NEBUZARADAN THE MASTER OF THE SOLDIERS) Namely, having been taught by the fugitives that he had always been a monitor that the city should be surrendered to the Chaldeans, and for that very reason had been treated very badly by his own countrymen. Vers. 14. THEY DELIVERED HIM TO GEDALIAH) It is an anticipation of that which will be narrated more fully with its circumstances in the following chapter; that Gedaliah was the chief of those who had fled to the Chaldeans. Vers 16. AND THEY WILL BE IN THY SIGHT IN THAT DAY) You will see all those things happen which Jeremiah predicted. Vers. 17. THOU SHALT NOT BE DELIVERED INTO THE HANDS OF THE MEN, WHOM THOU DOST FEAR) Those courtiers of King Zedekiah who are hostile to you, on account of Jeremiah being freed, will be able to do nothing against you: they will have business at home. Vers. 18. THY SOUL SHALL BE TO THEE FOR A SAVING) In the Hebrew: for a spoil: in the Chaldean for a rescue, just as spoils are snatched from enemies, so you will snatch your life from their force. The Greeks translate it εἰς ἕυρημα, both here and 39, 18. and 45, 5. BECAUSE THOU HAST HAD TRUST IN ME) Namely, when you did not fear the anger of powerful men and lent a free voice to the Prophet and to equity. Above 38, 7. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QVINTA MENSIS) Error est non interpretis, sed scribæ, qui 5. scripsit pro 9. Consentiunt enim hic Hebræi codices, Græci, Chaldaici, Nec aliter iidem Codices, & ipse Latinus 2. Reg. 25, 3. & hoc libro infra 52, 6

Cur ergo non correxit sed canonizavit errorem Pontifex Romanus? Mirum quod Cornelius a Lap. adhuc tueri errorem ausus sit, & quidem autoritate LXX. & Ebræor. codicum, qui tamen constanter nonam habent, uti fatetur hic Grotius. Quod autem 2. Reg. 25, 8. Mensis QUINTI die septimo urbs demum incensa dicitur, inde est, quod post- quam quarto mense die nona occupatione portæ mediæ capta est Jer. 39, 3. deinde Rex compre- hensus v. 5. captivus ad Babylonium Regem in Re- blatha commorantem adductus, ibique condemna- tus est v. 6. 7. urbs demum incensa subjecto ædifi- ciis igne, decimo autem die, qui Sabbathi fuit, tem- plum ac palatium Regis exustum fuit cum reliquis ædificiis. Conf. Jer. 52, 53. cum c. 39, 8. Ad illa enim facile spatium menstruum requirebatur.

Vers. eod. APERTA EST CIVITAS) Id est, ut historici lo- quuntur, ruinis nudata urbs erat. Vers. 3. ET INGRESSI SVNT OMNES) Impetu irruperunt, ET SEDERVNT IN PORTA MEDIA) Quæ duas urbis partes dividebat. Sedere hic est stationem figere. Fuit enim Je- rusalem duobus muris cincta vers. 4. Primus ergo murus jam occupatus, Vers. eod. NEREGEL - SERESER SEMEGARNABA) Cum duo hic nominentur nomine Neregel - Sereser, credibile est eos officiis hic distinctos esse: סמגר נבו videtur esse cu- stos Templi Nabo, ut sit vice ἐπιστάτης. Qui hic primus, & princeps nominatur Nere- gel-Sereser, creditur Niriglossor, qui Evilmerodo- cho interfecto regnum occupavit. RAB-SARIS) Id est, præfectus eunuchorum. RAB-MAG) Princeps magorum. Nomina hæc omnia apud Josephum ita corrupta reperies, ut vestigia vix agnoscas. Vers. 4. PER VIAM HORTI REGIS) Id est, per cry- ptam aliquam. ET PER PORTAM QVÆ ERAT INTER DUOS MVROS) Id est, ipsa porta erat extra murum, & ipsa, ut in obsidionibus fit, muro obstructa, unde eum murum perfodi necesse fuit, ut regi pateret exitus, Ezech. 12, 12. ET EGRESSI SVNT PER VIAM DESERTI) Via campestri. Græci, retenta voce Hebræa, διὰ τὴν ὁδὸν Ἀρα- ϐά. Ea est via versus Hierichuntem, ut sequentia ostendunt. Vers. 5. IN REBLATHA, IN TERRA EMATH) De qua vide 2. Reg. 17, 24. Emath minor Epiphania deinde vocata ab Antiocho Epiphane, teste Hieron. ad Amos. 6, 2. in provincia Syriæ Reblatha, loco amœnissimo, ubi consedit Nebucadnezar, ut eminus belli successum spectaret, ac Chaldææ vicinior esset, & suis contra Judæos subsidia inde mitteret. Vers. eod. ET LOCVTVS EST AD EVM JVDICIA) Id est, contra eum, ut fœderis ruptorem, sententiam tulit, quo- modo Tullus in Metium Suffetium. Vers. 7. OCULOS QUOQUE SEDECLÆ ERUIT. Ita excæcatus Epiphaniæ, & instar feræ caveæ inclusus Babylonem ductus est; quam videre non potuit, ut prædictum Ezech. 12, 13. Sic punitus fuit Zedekias ob infidelitatem & ingratitudinem, quod à Nebucadn. loco Jojachin Rex constitutus fœdus initum violasset. Vers. 9. ET RELIQVIAS POPVLI, QVI REMAN- SERANT IN CIVITATE) Exceptis, ut jam dicet, pau- perrimis, à quibus nihil metuebat: ut sequentia ostendunt. ET PERFVGAS, QVI TRANSFVGERVNT AD EVM) De quibus supra 38, 19. ET SVPERFLVOS VVLGI, QVI REMANSE- RVNT) Id est, illos, qui ex minoribus oppidis agrisque post tantas strages restabant. Vide, quæ dicta ad historiam hanc in libro Regum. Vers. 11. PRÆCEPERAT AVTEM NABVCHODONO- SOR REX BABYLONIS DE JEREMIA NABVZAR- DAN MAGISTRO MILITVM) Nempe edoctus è per- fugis eum semper monitorem fuisse, ut Chaldæis urbs de- deretur, & ob id ipsum à suis popularibus tractatum pes- sime. Vers. 14. TRADIDERVNT EVM GODOLIÆ) Est antici- patio ejus, quod uberius narrabitur cum suis circumstantiis capite sequenti, Godolias ille præcipuus fuit eorum, qui ad Chaldæos transfugerant. Vers 16. ET ERVNT IN CONSPECTV TVO IN DIE ILLA) Videbis omnia illa evenire, quæ prædixit Jeremias. Vers. 17. NON TRADERIS IN MANVS VIRORVM, QVOS TV FORMIDAS) Aulici isti Sedeciæ regis tibi infensi, ob Jeremiam liberatum, nihil adversus te poterunt: habebunt domi negotium. Vers. 18. ERIT TIBI ANIMA TVA IN SALVTEM) In Hebræo: per spolio: Chaldæo in ereptionem, Sicut spolia eri- piuntur hoftibus, ita ut vitam ab eorum vi eripies. Græci vertunt εἰς ἕυρημα, & hic & 39, 18. & 45, 5. QVIA IN ME HABUISTI FIDUCIAM) Nem- pe cum virorum potentium iram non veritus Prophetæ & æquitati vocem liberam commodâsti. Supra 38, 7. 8.

## 40:1 Argument
CHAPTER XL.

Jeremiah, restored to liberty in Ramah, returns to Gedaliah, the leader of the people remaining in Judea, against whom ambushes are plotted by Ishmael.

Vers. 1.

THE WORD, WHICH WAS MADE TO JEREMIAH FROM THE LORD) These things are to be referred to those which will follow in chapter 42, 9. The rest are set forth beforehand, so that the time and occasion of that Prophecy may be understood more correctly. This parenthesis, which Lyranus, Maldonatus, and Cornelius establish with the Hebrews, seems too long, nor is it to be agreed with Calvin or Pagninus that these words are interpolated, for which reason perhaps these things will be best referred to those which the prince of the army said to Jeremiah, so that it may be hinted that these things were said with the Lord directing it, not without the Lord, but as the text has it, these things were brought to Jeremiah from the Lord. WHEN HE TOOK HIM BOUND IN CHAINS) Unknown, of course, to him until then. For as soon as he learned that he was Jeremiah, he freed him, and did well by him according to the command of the king, which we had above 39, 11. FROM RAMAH) See what we said above 31, 15.

Latin:

CAPUT XL.

Jeremias in Rama libertati restitutus ad Go- doliam redit, Ducem reliqui in Judæa po- puli, cui insidiæ per Ismael struuntur.

Vers. 1.

SERMO, QVI FACTUS EST AD JEREMIAM A DOMINO) Hæc referenda sunt ad ea, quæ sequentur capite 42, 9. Cætera præmittuntur, ut tempus & occasio ejus Prophetiæ rectius intelligantur. Hæc parenthesis, quam cum Ebræis, Lyran. KNOW, THAT BAALIS KING OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON HATH SENT ISHMAEL THE SON OF NETHANIAH TO SLAY THEE) Certain Greek books have here βασίλισσα βασιλέως ὑιῶν Ἀμμὼν, that is, the queen (mother) of the king of Ammon, holding the guardianship of the boy king. Just as the mother of the king was called גבירה among the Hebrews, so among the Ammonites she was called בעליס. For to put ס for ת is a dialectal variation. Therefore, for שלח they read שלחה. For that know, in the Hebrew it is, dost thou surely know?

that is, did you not understand a matter of such importance? That Ishmael was a Jew, belonging to the royal family of David, as we shall soon see 41, 1. Thus the ancient hatred of the Ammonite Augusta toward the Hebrews, and that Ishmael's hope, which he had conceived from the origin of the Davidic stock, mingled together. To strike the soul is to wound mortally, as in Gen. 37, 12.

Sicut mater regis Hebræis vocabatur גבירה, ita Ammonitis בעליס Nam ס pro ת ponere est dialectus. Pro שלח ergo legerunt שלחה. Pro illo scito, in Hebræo est, an plane scis?

id est, an non intellexisti rem tanti momenti? Ismael iste Ju- dæus erat, ad regiam Davidis familiam pertinens, ut mox videbimus 41, 1. Ita Ammonitarum Augusta vetus in He- bræos odium, Ismael vero ille spem, quam conceperat ex ortu Davidicæ stirpis, una miscuerunt. Percutere animam est vulnerare lethaliter, ut Gen. 37, 12.

## 41:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLI. Ishmael treacherously kills Gedaliah with other Jews, whom Johanan pursues as he is about to lead the remaining captives to the Ammonites, bringing them back while Ishmael escapes.

Verse 1.

AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE SEVENTH MONTH ISHMAEL CAME. That seventh month was not of the year of the destruction of the temple, but of the following year, namely of the World 3417. For when Gedaliah the son of Ahikam had first been appointed by Nebuchadnezzar over those remnants of the people whom Nebuzar-Adan had left in the land of Judah to be vinedressers and farmers (but without any distinguished royal or imperial title, because, as Sulpicius Severus says, there was no dignity in presiding over a few and calamitous people), and Jeremiah had also been brought in chains to Ramah, and there having been freed by Nebuzar-Adan, had been sent to Gedaliah the prefect, chap. 39, 11. 14. c. 40, 1. 6. The leaders and soldiers who had fled by night from Jerusalem with Zedekiah, wandering in the fields, and indeed all the Jews who had betaken themselves to the Moabites, Ammonites, and neighboring nations, had returned to Gedaliah into their country, then at last these things happened, whence it is necessary that not only two months had passed since the destruction, which happened in the fifth month: and so some chronologists rightly observe that these things pertain to the seventh month of the following year.

Verse the same. ISHMAEL OF THE ROYAL STOCK.

Not of the Ammonites, as Lyra, Dionysius, Hugo, and Castro wish, but of the royal seed of the Jews. AND TEN MEN WITH HIM. It is credible that these 10 men are not understood to be all the associates of the treason, but the nobles and the leaders of the rest; for how could 10 men both overcome the Chaldean garrison and kill 80 men? Nor indeed should one rashly resort to a miracle here with Lyranus and Dionysius. The cause, however, of this slaughter was envy, because Gedaliah had been preferred in this prefecture over the Ishmaelites, who were sprung from royal seed. The Jews celebrate a fast in the seventh month on account of the slain Gedaliah, as their Menologies teach.

Verse the same.

THEY ATE BREAD THERE) They were received at a banquet.

Latin:

CAPUT XLI. Ismael dolo occidit Godoliam cum aliis Judæis, quem reliquos captivos ad Ammonitas du- cturum Johanan insequitur, reducens illos Ismaele effugiente.

Vers. 1.

ET FACTUM EST IN MENSE SEPTI- MO VENIT ISMAEL. Mensis ille septimus fuit non anni excidii tem- pli, sed sequentis anni nempe Mundi 3417. Nam cum Gedalias Ahikami filius reliquiis illis de popu- lo, quos Nebuzar-Adan in terra Judæ reliquerat, ut vinitores & agricolæ essent, primum à Nebucad- nezare præfectus fuerit (sed absque ullo insigni regio, aut imperii nomine, quia præcesse paucis & calamitosis Severo Sulpitio dicente nulla digni- tas erat) Jeremias etiam Ramam vinctus catenis ad- ductus, ibique à Nebuzar-Adan liberatus ad Ge- daliam præfectum missus esset cap. 39, 11. 14. c. 40, 1. 6. Duces, & milites, qui cum Sedekia Hierosolymis noctu aufugerant in agris palantes, quin & Judæi omnes, qui ad Moabitas, Ammonitas, & gentes finitimas se receperant, ad Gedaliam reversi es- sent in patriam, tum demum hæc evenerunt, unde non duos menses solum præterlapsos oportet esse ab excidio, quod quinto mense contigit: adeo- que recte observant Chronologi nonnulli hæc ad septimum Mensem sequentis anni pertinere.

Vers. eod. ISMAEL DE STIRPE RE- GALI.

Non Ammonitarum, ut Lyra, Dionysius, Hugo, Castro, volunt, sed è regio semine Judæorum. ET DECEM VIRI CUM EO. Credibile est, hos 10. viros non intelligi universos socios proditionis, sed optimates & cæterorum antesignanos; nam quomodo 10. viri & præsidium Chaldaicum su- perare, & 80. viros interficere potuissent? Ne- que vero temere cum Lyrano & Dionysio ad miraculum hic confugiendum. Causa autem hu- jus cædis invidia fuit, quod Ismaelitæ ex regio se- mine oriundo Godolias prælatus fuerit in hac præ- fectura. Judæi ob occisum Godoliam Mense septimo statum celebrant jejunium, ut Menologia eorum docent.

Vers. eod.

## 41:17
Ver. 17.

THEY SAT DOWN AS SOJOURNERS IN CHAMAAM, WHICH IS NEAR BETHLEHEM) In the Hebrew: They sat down in the habitation of Chimham, which is near Bethlehem. When David had finished the war against Absalom, since he could not bring his friend Barzillai, who was an old man, back with him to Jerusalem, he took his son Chamaam with him, with the intention of rewarding the father's merits in the son: moreover, since David had an estate in the field of Bethlehem, he gave Chamaam the right of dwelling there and of making certain profits for himself; and from that time that field received its name. They sat down there, however, only to prepare themselves for the journey, of which the following verses treat.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

David bello adversus Absolomum patrato, cum Berzel-laium amicum suum senem secum Hierosolyma reducere non posset, filium ejus Chamaamum secum duxit, eo ani-mo, ut patris merita in filio remuneraret: cum autem Da-vid patrimonium haberet in agro Bethlehemitico, jus ibi ha-bitandi & fructus quosdam suos faciendi dedit Chamaa-mo; atque inde id rus nomen accepit. Consederunt autem ibi tantum, ut se pararent itineri, de quo agunt sequentia.

## 42:1 Argument
CHAP. XLII.

CHAPTER XLII.

Johanan with his companions consult the Prophet, whether they ought to betake themselves into Egypt, who warns them to remain in Judea, and unless they do so, threatens them with the sword, famine, and pestilence.

Ver. 1. AND JOHANAN THE SON OF KAREAH) Namely Johanan. LET OUR SUPPLICATION FALL BEFORE THEE) Better: from thy presence: that is, do thou, prostrating thyself, carry our prayers to God. A prayer is said to fall, which is made by those prostrating themselves, as above 36, 7. 38, 26. See also below 9. Most simply the sense is: let our prayer be present to thee and thy care.

Latin:

CAP. XLII.

CAPUT XLII.

Johanan cum sociis consulunt Prophetam, anne in Ægyptum se conferre debeant, qui monet, ut in Judæa subsistant, ac nisi id fecerint, gladium, famem & pestem ipsis minatur.

Vers. 1. ET JOHANAN FILIUS CAREE) Nempe Io- hanan. CADAT ORATIO NOSTRA IN CONSPE- CTU TUO) Melius : à conspectu tuo : id est, tu procum- bens preces nostras ad Deum defer. Cadere oratio dicitur, quæ fit à procumbentibus, ut supra 36, 7. 38, 26. Vide & infra 9. SImplicissime sensus est: sit præsens tibi & curæ oratio nostra.

## 42:2
Ver. 2. WE ARE LEFT BUT A FEW OF MANY) Such is that: The remnants of the Danaans, and of cruel Achilles.

Latin:

Vers. 2. DERELICTI SUMUS PAUCI DE PLURIBUS) Tale illud : Relliquias Danaûm, atque immitis Achilli.

## 42:3

Latin:

## 42:6

Latin:

Vers. 6. SIVE BONUM EST, SIVE MALUM) Id est, sive facile, sive difficile.

Ver. same. IN THIS LAND) Judea. I WILL BUILD YOU) I will give you houses, as above 33, 7. I WILL PLANT YOU) I will make firm seats for you as for trees, which are fixed into the soil. FOR NOW I AM APPEASED CONCERNING THE EVIL, THAT I HAVE DONE UNTO YOU) I am content with those punishments which I have brought upon you, provided you do not add a new fault of disobedience.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SI QVIESCENTES MANSERITIS) Sub imperio Babylonico, cui eos subjici plane Deus voluerat. In Ebr. Si revertendo reversi fueritis. Erant enim Judæi jam in motu, etsi id dissimularint Prophetæ, ut proficiscerentur in Ægyptum, c. 41, 17.

Vers. eod. IN TERRA HAC) Judæa. ÆDIFICABO VOS) Domos vobis dabo, ut su- pra 33, 7. PLANTABO) Firmas sedes vobis faciam ut arbo- ribus, quæ soli infiguntur. JAM ENIM PLACATUS SVM SVPER MA- LO, QVOD FECI VOBIS) Contentus sum iis pœnis, quas vobis intuli, modo ne novam imparentiæ culpam adjiciatis.

## 42:11
Ver. 11. I AM WITH YOU) See at the end of Matthew.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VOBISCUM SVM EGO) Vide ad ultima Matthæi.

## 42:14
Ver. 14. AND THERE WILL WE DWELL) We will not wander, as here, at the whim of the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET IBI HABITABIMUS) Non vagabimur, ut hic, pro arbitrio Chaldæorum.

## 42:15
Ver. 15. IF YE SET YOUR FACES TO ENTER INTO EGYPT) See concerning this manner of speaking at Luke 9, 51. But that they are forbidden to go into Egypt does not come from that passage Deuteronomy 17, 16. The sense of which, other than what is thought by some, we have shown there, but from a special decree of God, for that cause which we brought forward above 10. To set the face denotes stubbornness in a purpose. Conf. v. 17. Dan. 11, 17. Luke 9, 51. In the Hebrew there is emphasis: If you by setting shall set your face to go into Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SI POSVERITIS FACIEM VESTRAM, VT INGREDIAMINI ÆGTPTVM) Vide de hoc loquendi genere ad Lucam 9, 51. Quod autem in Ægyptum ire ve- tantur, non venit ex illo loco Deuteron. 17, 16. Cujus alium quam à nonnullis putatur, sensum esse, ibi oftendi- mus, sed ex speciali decreto Dei, ex causa illa, quam attu- limus sup. 10. Ponere faciem pertinaciam in proposito notat. Conf. v. 17. Dan. 11, 17. Luc. 9, 51. In Ebr. empha- sis est : Si vos ponendo posueritis faciem vestram ad eundum in Ægyptum.

## 42:16
Ver. 16. THE SWORD, WHICH YE FEAR, SHALL OVERTAKE YOU THERE IN THE LAND OF EGYPT) The sword of Nebuchadnezzar. This happened in that expedition in which Nebuchadnezzar went into Africa, of which Megasthenes makes mention, produced by us in book 3 of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Latin:

Vers. 16. GLADIVS, QVEM VOS FORMIDATIS IBI COMPREHENDET VOS IN TERRA ÆGTPTI) Gladius Nabuchodonosoris. Factum hoc ea expeditione, qua in Africam ivit Nabuchodonosor, cujus meminit Me- gasthenes productus à nobis ad librum 3. de veritate reli- gionis Christianæ.

## 42:18
Ver. 18. AS MY FURY IS POURED OUT) Better: is poured out. For נתך is accustomed to be explained by יצק. It rested, the Chaldean: well as to the sense. *It did not rest, but rather was poured out, which is the contrary to that. Metals, while they are smelted and liquefied, are poured out and burst forth with great force like a fiery torrent. Cf. ch. 7, 22. Ez. 22, 21. Nah. 1, 6.

Ver. eod. AND YOU SHALL BE FOR AN OATH) For an execration. It shall be said: may God destroy you, as he destroyed the Jews in Egypt. AND FOR AN ASTONISHMENT) Better: for a desolation: as the Chaldean. The Greeks, εἰς ἄβατον.

AND FOR A CURSE) It shall be said of you: O wicked men. AND FOR A REPROACH) For a mockery. AND YOU SHALL SEE THIS PLACE NO MORE) You shall not return into Judea, like those who were carried away into Babylon.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SICVT CONFLATVS EST FVROR MEVS) Melius : effusus est. Solet enim נתך exponi per יצק. Re- sedit, Chaldæus: bene ad sensum. *Non resedit, sed potius effusus est, quod contrari- um illi. Metalla dum conflantur & liquefiunt, ma- gno impetu instar torrentis ignei effunduntur & erumpunt. Conf. cap. 7, 22. Ez. 22, 21. Nah. 1, 6.

Vers. eod. ET ERITIS IN JVSJVRANDVM) In exsecra- tionem. Dicetur : ita vos perdat Deus, ut Judæos in Ægy- pto perdidit. ET IN STVPOREM) Melius : in desolationem : quomodo Chaldæus. Græci, εἰς ἄβατον.

ET IN MALEDICTIONEM) Dicetur de vobis: o homines scelerati. ET IN OPPROBRIUM) Ludificatui. ET NEQUAQUAM ULTRA VIDEBITIS LO- CUM ISTUM) Non redibitis in Judæam, ut isti, qui in Ba- bylona deportati fuerunt.

Ver. 19.

THE WORD OF THE LORD CONCERNING YOU, O REMNANT OF JUDA) This is what God declares to you through me in order and irrevocably. KNOWING YOU SHALL KNOW, THAT I HAVE TESTIFIED TO YOU THIS DAY) Know, that is, remember that I have testified to you all.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

VERBUM DOMINI SUPER VOS, O RELI- QUIÆ JUDA) Hoc est, quod Deus vobis per me serie & irrevocabiliter denunciat. SCIENTES SCIETIS, QVIA EGO VOS OBTE- STATUS SUM HODIE) Scitote, id est, mementote me contestatum vos omnes.

Ver. 20.

YOU HAVE DECEIVED YOUR SOULS) In the Hebrew: You have deceived (me, namely, whom you wished to use to pray to and consult God) in your souls: that is, against yourselves, to your own harm.

Vers. 20.

## 43:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLIII.

Johanan, not hearing the voice of the Lord, leads Jeremiah and Baruch with the people into Egypt: where the Prophet prophesies that the King of Babylon will lay waste to Egypt with its idols, and will condemn it.

Latin:

CAPUT XLIII.

Non audiens vocem Domini Johanan in Ægy- ptum Jeremiam & Baruch cum populo ab- ducit : ubi vaticinatur Propheta Regem Ba- bylonis Ægyptum cum idolis suis vastatu- rum, eique daminaturum.

## 43:2
Ver. 2.

AZARIAH THE SON OF HOSHAIAH) The author of that counsel concerning the departure into Egypt. He was not a False Prophet, as it seemed to the Tigurines, but one of the warriors, among whom he is placed.

Ver. eod.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

AZARIAS FILIUS OSAIÆ) Auctor consilii illius de profectione in Ægyptum. NonPseudopropheta fuit,ut Tigurinis visum, sed unus è bellatoribus,inter quos collocatur.

Vers. eod.

## 43:3
BARUCH SON OF NERIAH) Who, as a younger servant, spoke those things which he had learned from Jeremiah.

Latin:

BARUCH FILIUS NERIÆ) Qui ut junior servi- dius ea eloquebatur, quæ ab Jeremia didicerat.

## 43:7
Verse 7.

AND THEY CAME EVEN TO TAPHNIS) Daphnae of Pelusium. See Isaiah 30, 4. The Greeks [write] τάφνας. It was a Royal metropolis, where Moses had performed his prodigies in the field of Zoan, or Taphnis, Psalm 77, 43. Numbers 13, 23.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET VENERUNT USQVE AD TAPHNIS) Da- phnas Pelusias. Vide Esaiam 30, 4. Græci τάφνας. Metropolis erat Regia, ubi Moses sua fecerat prodigia in campo Taneos, vel Taphnis, Psal. 77, 43. Num. 13, 23.

## 43:9
Verse 9.

HIDE THEM IN THE CRYPT, WHICH IS UNDER THE BRICK WALL AT THE GATE OF THE HOUSE OF PHARAOH IN TAPHNIS) מלט is without doubt cement. For so both the Chaldeans and Arabs use it, and from them the Italians: and טין signifies the same, which the Chaldean has here. מלבן are bricks, as appears in Exodus 1, 14; 5, 16, 18, 19. And the place where bricks are made. The sense therefore is: place those large stones in the cement, which was in the brick-kiln, namely, so that they might be kept more correctly: because Nebuchadnezzar was to use them to pave the ground upon which he was to place his royal seat.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ABSCONDES EOS IN CRTPTA, QVÆ EST SUB MURO LATERITIO IN PORTA DOMUS PHARAONIS IN TAPHNIS) מלט haud dubie cæmen- tum est. Nam ita usurpant & Châldæi & Arabes, & ab illis Itali: Idemque significat טין, quod hic habet Chaldæus. מלבן sunt lateres, ut apparet Exod. 1, 14. 5, 16. 18. 19. Et locus ubi lateres fiunt. Sensus ergo est: lapides illos magnos cæmento imponito, quod erat in officina lateraria, nempe quo rectius serventur: quia illis usurus est Nabuchodono- sor ad sternendum solum, cui sedem regiam erat impo- siturus.

## 43:10
Verse 10.

AND HE SHALL SET HIS THRONE ABOVE THEM) A tent. For so it is in the Hebrew and Chaldean: Imperial.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET STATUET SOLIUM SUUM SUPRA EOS) Tentorium. Sic enim in Hebræo & Chaldæo: Augustale.

## 43:11
Verse 11.

SUCH AS ARE FOR DEATH, TO DEATH: AND SUCH AS ARE FOR CAPTIVITY, TO CAPTIVITY: AND SUCH AS ARE FOR THE SWORD, TO THE SWORD) To some he will bring pestilence: (from bad food) others he will lead captive: others he will kill: thinking it of little importance to whom the lot of each might fall. We had a similar manner of speaking above at 15, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

QVOS IN MORTEM, IN MORTEM: ET QVOS IN CAPTIVITATEM, IN CAPTIVITATEM: ET QVOS IN GLADIUM, IN GLADIUM) Aliis pestem adferet: (ex malis alimentis) alios captivos aget: alios oc- cidet: parum sua referre existimans,in quem exitum cujus- que fors ceciderit. Simile loquendi genus habuimus su- pra 15, 2

## 43:12
Verse 12.

AND HE SHALL KINDLE A FIRE IN THE TEMPLES OF THE GODS OF EGYPT, AND HE SHALL BURN THEM) Thus the son of Pompey speaking of the Egyptian gods in Lucan: And having placed the gods beneath, I shall burn my head. AND HE SHALL CARRY THEM AWAY CAPTIVE) Tertullian in his Apology: As many triumphs over gods as over nations: as many spoils as there still remain images of captive gods. See what we said in book 3 of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 5, § 2, and in the annotations there. AND HE SHALL WRAP HIMSELF IN THE LAND OF EGYPT, AS A SHEPHERD WRAPS HIMSELF IN HIS CLOAK) The land of Egypt is here an ablative, for the spoils of Egypt, as 'laden with the spoils of the East.' But the Greeks read עטה, which is sometimes to cleanse, and they explain it: he shall so thoroughly cleanse Egypt, as a shepherd cleanses his cloak of lice, that is, he shall search everything and take it away.

Verse of the same.

AND HE SHALL GO FORTH FROM THENCE IN PEACE) He shall go into Africa without harm and safely.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET SUCCENDET IGNEM IN DELUBRIS DEO- RUM ÆGTPTI, ET COMBURET EA) Sic Pompeji filius apud Lucanum de Diis Ægyptiis loquens: Suppositisque Deis uram caput. ET CAPTIVOS DUCET ILLOS) Tertullia- nus Apologetico: Tot de diis, quot de gentibus triumphi: tot manubiæ quot adhuc manent simulacra captivorum deo- rum. Vide, quæ diximus libro 3. de Jure Belli ac Pacis, cap. 5. §. 2. & in Annotatis ibi. ET AMICIETUR TERRA ÆGYPTI, SICUT AMICITUR PASTOR PALLIO SUO) Terra Ægypti, est hic ablativus, pro spoliis Ægypti, ut Spoliis orientis onustum. At Græci legerunt עטה, quod est interdum purgare, & explicant: ita perpurgabit Ægyptum, quomodo pastor ab- ollam suam pediculis repurget, id est, omnia scrutabitur & auferet.

Vers. eod.

ET EGREDIETVR INDE IN PACE) Sine noxa ac tuto ibit in Africam.

## 43:13
Verse 13.

AND HE SHALL BREAK THE STATUES OF THE HOUSE OF THE SUN) בית־שמש. The LXX rendered it word for word very well, ἠλι- οπόλεως. Herodotus in Euterpe records that there was a great πανήγυριν (festival) in Heliopolis in Egypt in honor of the sun. The Greek version of Genesis 41:45 teaches us that this is the place which was once called On.

AND HE SHALL BURN THE TEMPLES OF THE GODS OF EGYPT WITH FIRE) The same as above in 12. It is the custom of the Hebrews to repeat more often those things which are extraordinary and least credible.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET CONTERET STATUAS DOMUS SOLIS) בית־שמש. LXX. verbum verbo optime reddiderunt, ἠλι- οπόλεως. Heliopoli in Ægypto magnam fuisse πανήγυριν in honorem solis memorat Herodotus Euterpe. Eam esse, quæ olim On vocabatur, docet nos Græca versio Ge- nes. 41, 45.

ET DELVBRA DEORVM ÆGYPTI COMBV- RET IGNI) Idem quod supra 12. Mos est Hebræis, ea, quæ eximia & minime credibilia sunt sæpius repetere.

## 44:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLIV.

Jeremiah reproaches the Jews for Egyptian idolatry and denounces punishment: to those objecting that the cause of their calamity was that they did not serve the stars, the Prophet intimates the sword and famine, and the delivery of the King of Egypt himself into the hands of his enemies.

Verse 1.

IN MIGDOL) It is a place not far from the Arabian Gulf, or the Red Sea, as appears in Exodus 14:2.

Herodotus in book 2 and Pliny in book 2, chapter 8, mention a city of Egypt which was a royal seat by the name of Magdalan. Lyranus thinks that palace was so called because Joseph once inhabited it, named by this name on account of its magnificence.

Verse of the same.

AND IN MEMPHIS) In Memphis, which is מֹף to the Hebrews: closer to the Chaldean is מַפֵּס.

AND IN THE LAND OF PATHROS) The name of the Pharusii (so Pliny writes) or Phaurusii (for so Strabo) of the Ethiopians does not go far. We have the Hebrew name פַתְרוֹס both in Gen. 10:14 and Isaiah 11:11.

Interpreters make Pathros a certain province on this side of the Nile, more fertile in crops than the rest, whence the Jews chose it as a seat,

Latin:

CAPUT XLIV.

Judæis Ægyptiacam idololatriam exprobrat Jeremias, pœnamque denunciat: illis oppo- nentibus hanc esse calamitatis suæ causam, quod non servierint sideribus, gladium & famem, ipsiusque Regis Ægypti traditionem in manus hostium, intimat Propheta.

Vers. 1.

IN MAGDALO) Locus est non longe à sinu Ara- bico, sive mari rubro, ut apparet Exod. 14, 2.

Herodotus l. 2. & Plinius l. 2. c. 8. meminerunt urbis Ægypti, quæ Regia sedes fuerit nomine Ma- gdalan. Lyranus palatium illud ita dictum fuisse putat, quod inhabitavit olim Joseph, vocatum hoc nomine ob magnificentiam.

Vers. eod.

ET IN MEMPHIS) In Memphide, quæ מֹף He- bræis: Chaldæo propius מַפֵּס.

ET IN TERRA PHATVRES) Non abit longe nomen Pharusiorum (ita Plinius scribit) aut Phaurusiorum (nam ita Strabo) Æthiopum. Nomen Hebræum פַתְרוֹס habemus & Gen. 10, 14. & Esaiæ. 11, 11.

Provinciam aliquam cis Nilum Patros faciunt interpp. frugibus præ reliquis feraciorem, unde eam Judæi in sedem elegerint,

Ver. 14.

TO WHICH THEY LIFT UP THEIR SOULS) That is, where they hope to come. The same expression in Deut. 24, 15. and above 22, 27. where the LXX. ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχειν τὴν ἐλπίδα. and here: ἐφ' ᾗν αὐτοὶ ἐλπίζυσι ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν. Thus also the more elegant Greeks say μετεωρίζεσθαι.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

## 44:17
Ver. 17.

BUT DOING WE WILL DO EVERY WORD, THAT GOETH FORTH OUT OF OUR MOUTH) That is, whatever we have vowed to do. See below 25. Thus to go forth from the lips is said of a vow in Deut. 23, 23.

THAT WE MAY SACRIFICE TO THE QUEEN OF HEAVEN) That we may burn incense. The Queen of heaven בעלית, Baaltis, the Moon, as was said above 7, 18.

R. Kimchi and Pagninus understand Saturn, Junius and Tremellius the whole host of heaven. Thus the Turks worship the Moon.

Verse of the same.

OUR KINGS, AND OUR PRINCES) Both by others, and especially from Manasseh reigning.

IT WAS WELL WITH US) We were good: that is, in good circumstances.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

SED FACIENTES FACIEMVS OMNE VER- BVM, QVOD EGREDITUR EX ORE NOSTRO) Id est, quicquid nos vovimus facturos. Vide infra 25. Sic egredi de labiis, de voto dicitur Deut. 23, 23.

UT SACRIFICEMUS REGINÆ COELI) Ut adoleamus. Regina cœli בעלית, Baaltis, Luna, ut di- ctum supra 7, 18.

R. Kimchi, & Pagninus Saturnum, Jun. & Tre- mell. universum cœli exercitum intelligunt. Sic Turcæ colunt Lunam.

Vers. eod.

REGES NOSTRI, ET PRINCIPES NOSTRI) Tum aliis, tum maxime è Manasse regnante.

BENE NOBIS ERAT) Fuimus boni: id est, in bo- nis rebus.

## 44:19
Verse 19. DID WE WITHOUT OUR HUSBANDS MAKE THEM CAKES) Popana (sacrificial cakes). Here speak those women, of whom he said above that there was a huge multitude. We did not conduct, they say, private and nocturnal rites, which are accustomed to be suspect to husbands. Openly and with our husbands aware and seeing, we did those things. See Livy concerning the Bacchanalia.

Verse of the same. TO WORSHIP HER.

Cornelius renders the Hebrew להעציבה as to fashion the idol in it: because in their cakes they formed or impressed the image of their idol, namely of the Moon, just as the Turks display its image on banners, tables, and foods.

Verse of the same.

DID NOT THE LORD REMEMBER THE SACRIFICE, WHICH YOU SACRIFICED IN THE CITIES OF JUDAH, AND IN THE STREETS OF JERUSALEM, YOU AND YOUR FATHERS, AND YOUR KINGS, AND YOUR PRINCES, AND THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND) But did not the Lord remember the incense, which you burned in the cities of Judah, and in the (various) regions of Jerusalem, you (I say) and your fathers, and your kings, and your princes, and the common people? That is, did He not repay you with an excellent return for your excellent deeds?

Latin:

Vers. 19. NUMQVID SINE VIRIS NOSTRIS FE- CIMUS EIS PLACENTAS) Popana. Hic loquuntur il- læ mulieres, quarum ingentem fuisse multitudinem supra dixit. Non agitavimus, inquiunt, sacra privata ac nocturna, quæ suspecta viris esse solent. Palam & viris nostris con- sciis ac videntibus ista fecimus. Vide Livium de Baccha- nalibus.

Vers. eod. AD COLENDUM EAM.

Hebræum Cornelius reddit להעציבה ad elabo- randum idolum in ea: quod in suis placentis effor- marint vel impresserint effigiem idoli sui, utpote Lunæ, uti ejus effigiem Turcæ in vexillis, mensis, & cibis præferunt.

Vers. eod.

NUMQVID NON SACRIFICIUM, QVOD SA- CRIFICASTIS IN CIVITATIBUS JUDA, ET IN PLATEIS JERUSALEM, VOS ET PATRES VESTRI, ET REGES VESTRI, ET PRINCIPES VESTRI, ET POPULUS TERRÆ, HORUM RECORDATUS EST DOMINUS) At nonne aromatum, qua adolestis in ur- bibus Iuda, & in (variis) regionibus Hierosolymorum, vos (in- quam) & patres vestri, & reges vestri, & principes vestri, & plebs, recordatus est Dominus? Id est, annon pro egregiis fa- ctis egregiam vobis rependit vicem?

Verse 22.

BECAUSE THERE IS NO INHABITANT) Without an inhabitant. In the Hebrew.

THAT YOU HAVE SACRIFICED) You have burned.

IN THE LAW) In those things which the law itself holds to be honest.

AND IN THE PRECEPTS) In the rituals.

Vers. 25.

Vers. 26.

THAT MY NAME SHALL NO MORE BE CALLED UPON BY THE MOUTH OF ANY MAN OF JUDAH SAYING: THE LORD GOD LIVES IN ALL THE LAND OF EGYPT) That is, I hate them so much that I do not even wish to be named by them: which, so that it may not happen anymore, I will abolish them all.

ECCE, EGO JVRAVI IN NOMINE MEO MA- GNO) Et ego votum feci, quod implebo.

QVIA NEQVAQVAM VLTRA VOCABITVR NOMEN MEVM EX ORE OMNIS VIRI JVDÆI DICENTIS: VIVAT DOMINVS DEVS IN OMNI TERRA ÆGTPTI) Id est, ita eos odi, ut ab iis ne nomina- ri quidem velim: quod ne ultra fiat abolebo omnes.

Vers. 27.

Vers. 28.

AND THEY THAT SHALL FLEE THE SWORD SHALL RETURN FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT INTO THE LAND OF JUDAH, FEW MEN) Connect these with the preceding in this sense: All shall die, except for a very few, who for fear of slaughter shall flee back from Egypt into Judea, which they had left by evil counsel.

OF THEM THAT ENTER INTO THE LAND OF EGYPT) That is, those who have entered into Egypt: both those who shall die there, and those who shall flee away.

WHOSE WORD SHALL BE FULFILLED) It shall stand: that is, it shall be made valid by God.

ET QVI FVGERINT GLADIVM REVER- TENTVR DE TERRA ÆGTPTI IN TERRAM JV- DA VIRI PAVCI) Connecte hæc cum superioribus hoc sensu: Morientur omnes, exceptis admodum paucis, qui metu cædis ex Ægypto in Judæam, quam malo consilio re- liquerant, refugient.

INGREDIENTIVM TERRAM ÆGTPTI) Id est, qui ingressi fuerunt in Ægyptum: tum ii, qui ibi morientur, tum qui aufugient.

CVJVS SERMO COMPLEATVR) Stabit: id est, ratum à Deo fiet.

## 44:29
Vers. 29.

AND THIS SHALL BE A SIGN UNTO YOU) Namely, the preceding. I shall tell of a great thing, which shall happen before you perish. Ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων, as in Matthew 24:8.

THAT I WILL VISIT UPON YOU IN THIS PLACE) By which you may know that I will there exact punishment from you.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ET HOC VOBIS SIGNVM) Nempe antecedens. Dicam rem magnam, quæ prius eveniet, quam vos interea- tis. Ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων, ut Matth. 24, 8.

QVOD VISITEM SVPER VOS EGO IN LO- CO ISTO) Quo cognoscatis me ibi de vobis pœnas ex- acturum.

## 44:30
Vers. 30.

PHARAOH HOPHRA) חפרע in Hebrew: The Greeks have Ὀαφρῆ here, and Clement of Alexandria. Herodotus in Euterpe calls him Ἀπρίην. The Chaldean thinks this Egyptian name has the meaning of a lame man.

R. David and R. Salomo think the name is the same as פרעה with only the prefix מ; others think that name signifies a bare pit, despoiled of all goods, from פרה to dig, and ערה to bare, to despoil. Apries began to reign in the 18th year of Nebuchadnezzar. For in the second year of Apries, Jerusalem was captured, according to Clem. Al. lib. 2. Strom.

IN THE HAND OF HIS ENEMIES, AND IN THE HAND OF THOSE SEEKING HIS SOUL) Into the hand of Amasis, and of those who followed the faction of Amasis. By them he was captured and kept in the city of Sais: and finally killed at the instigation of Amasis by those who did not think themselves safe enough unless he were dead. You have these things in Herodotus, the best interpreter of this passage.

That he was captured and killed not by Amasis, but by Nebuchadnezzar, is evident both from this passage, and from Ez. 29:19, ch. 31:11, 15, 18, as well as from Joseph. lib. 10, ch. 11, and Jerome in ch. 4 of Lamentations. It could have happened, however, that Nebuchadnezzar substituted Amasis for him in the kingdom, whence Herodotus supposed him to have been captured and slain by Amasis.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

PHARAONEM EPHREE) חפרע in Hebræo: Ὀαφρῆ habent hic Græci, & Clemens Alexandrinus. Ἀπρίην vo- cat Herodotus Euterpe. Chaldæus nomen hoc Ægyptium putat significationem habere hominis claudi.

R. David, & R. Salomo putant, nomen idem esse cum פרעה præposito solum מ; alii nomen il- lud significare foveam nudam, omnibus bonis spolia- tam à פרה fodere, & ערה nudare, spoliare. Cœpit Apries regnare anno 18. Nebucadnezar. Nam anno Apries secundo capta est Hierosolyma teste Clem. Al. l. 2. Strom.

IN MANU INIMICORUM EJUS, ET IN MA- NU QUÆRENTIUM ANIMAM ILLIUS) In manum Amasidis, & eorum, qui Amasidis sectam sequebantur. Ab his captus asservatusque est in urbe Sai: & tandem occisus instigantibus Amasim iis, qui nisi morte ejus se satis tutos esse non putabant. Hæc habes apud Herodotum optimum hujus loci interpretem.

Non ab Amasi, sed à Nebucadnez. ipsum captum & occisum esse, tum ex hoc loco, tum ex Ez. 29, 19. c. 31, 11. 15. 18. nec non è Joseph. l. 10. c. 11. & Hieron. in c. 4. Thren. constat. Fieri tamen potuit, ut Na- buchodonosor Amasin ei in regno substituit, un- de ab Amasi eum captum & cæsum Herodotus opinatus sit.

## 45:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLV.

The Lord deals with the troubled Baruch and promises him safety.

Ver. 1. THE WORD THAT JEREMIAH THE PROPHET SPOKE TO BARUCH, THE SON OF NERIAH) Having finished both the prophecies and the histories pertaining to the kings and the Jewish people, he subjoins one that pertains to a single man, namely Baruch: just as to the Epistles of Paul to the Churches are subjoined those that pertain to individuals, even if some of these were written before those. After this, the Prophet will append prophecies that look to other nations, and that will be the end of the whole book. For we shall say where the last chapter belongs when we have come to it.

THESE WORDS) Those words, namely, placed above in 36.

Latin:

CAPUT XLV.

Cum Barucho perturbato agit Dominus, eique incolumitatem pollicetur.

Vers. 1. VERBUM, QUOD LOCUTUS EST JERE- MIAS PROPHETA AD BARUCH, FILIUM NE- RIÆ) Absolutis & Prophetis & historiis ad reges popu- lumque Judæum pertinentibus, subjungit unam, quæ ad u- num hominem, Baruchum scilicet pertinet: Sicut Epistolis Pauli ad Ecclesias subjunguntur illæ, quæ ad singulos per- tinent, etiamsi quædam harum ante illas scriptæ sunt. Post id subnectet Propheta prophetias, quæ spectant ad gentes alias, isque erit totius libri finis. Nam ultimum caput quo pertineat, ubi eo ventum erit, dicemus.

VERBA HÆC) Verba ista, nempe posita supr. 36.

## 45:3
Ver. 3. SORROW TO MY SORROW) Danger to danger, above 36:10, 16, 26.

AND I HAVE FOUND NO REST) A tranquil place of habitation. The Chaldean understands it of the gift of prophecy.

This does not agree with the text, from which it is sufficiently clear that it treats of deliverance from afflictions, not only of a tranquil place.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DOLOREM DOLORI MEO) Periculum ad pe- riculum supra 36, 10. 16. 26.

ET REQUIEM NON INVENI) Locum tran- quillum habitationis. De Prophetiæ dono intelligit Chaldæus.

Non congruit hoc textui, è quo satis patet de li- beratione ab afflictionibus agi, non solum de loco tranquillo.

## 45:4
Ver. 4. BEHOLD, THAT WHICH I HAVE BUILT, I DESTROY) This whole kingdom, begun, nurtured, increased, defended, and adorned with such great care of mine.
