See the same phrase in ch. 1:10, ch. 18:9, ch. 24:6, ch. 33:7, ch. 42:10. The argument is from the greater to the lesser, as in ch. 35:26, 29.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ECCE, QVOD ÆDIFICAVI EGO, DE- STRUO) Regnum hoc totum tanta mea cura inchoatum, educatum, auctum, defensum, ornatum.

Vide eandem phrasin cap. 1, 10. c. 18, 9. c. 24, 6. c. 33, 7. c. 42, 10. Argumentum est à majori ad mi- nus, ut c. 35, 26. 29.

## 45:5
AND DO YOU SEEK for yourself great things? You make great vows. You want a tranquil life outside of dangers, outside of fear. And yet Cato in Lucan: Who would wish to watch the stars and the world falling, himself devoid of fear? &c.

He calls a miraculous deliverance great things, Ps. 106, 21. It is a sign of human weakness to imagine great things for oneself amidst common punishments.

Verse of the same. ABOVE ALL FLESH) Of the Jews, as the preceding things show.

AND I WILL GIVE YOU YOUR LIFE AS A SPOIL) As a spoil. In the Hebrew, as above 39, 16. Let it be enough for you at such a time to have your life saved.

THE SECOND PART OF JEREMIAH, PROPHECIES CONCERNING FOREIGN KINGDOMS AND PEOPLES.

Latin:

ET TU QVÆRIS TIBI GRANDIA) Magna facis vota. Vis tranquillam vitam extra pericula, extra metum. Atqui Cato apud Lucanum: Sidera quis, mundumque velit spectare cadentem, Expers ipse metus? &c.

Grandia vocat miraculosam liberationem, Ps. 106, 21. Indicium est humanæ infirmitatis imagina- ri sibi grandia inter communes pœnas.

Vers. eod. SUPER OMNEM CARNEM) Judæorum, ut præcedentia ostendunt.

ET DABO TIBI ANIMAM TUAM IN SALU- TEM) In spolium. In Hebræo, ut supra 39, 16. Satis tibi sit tali tempore vitam habere salvam.

PARS SECUNDA JEREMIAE, PROPHETIÆ DE EXOTICIS REGNIS ET POPULIS.

## 46:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLVI.

The slaughter and desolation to be brought upon Pharaoh and Egypt by Nebuchadnezzar is announced twice, with the addition of an Evangelical consolation for the sake of the faithful.

Verse 1. AGAINST THE NATIONS) This is the general title of all those things which will follow through six chapters. Then follows a special title to Egypt, that is, against Egypt. These prophecies are arranged by nations, not by times. This prophecy was given to Jeremiah, as follows, in the fourth year of King Jehoiakim. But the Greek books placed these prophecies above, as we have warned elsewhere.

Latin:

CAPUT XLVI.

Pharaoni & Ægypto clades, & desolatio à Nebucadnez. inferenda prænunciatur dua- bus vicibus, addita fidelium causa consola- tione Evangelica.

Vers. 1. CONTRA GENTES) Hic est titulus generalis, o- mnium eorum, quæ per sex capita sequentur. Sequitur de- inde specialis titulus ad Ægyptum, id est, contra Ægy- ptum. Hæ prophetise per gentes digeruntur, non per tem- pora, Hæc prophetia Jeremiæ data est, ut sequitur, anno quarto regis Joakim, At Græci libri has prophetias supra posuere, ut alibi monuimus.

## 46:2
Verse 2. PHARAOH NECHO) Who is Neco to Herodotus. He reigned in Egypt in the times of Nebuchadnezzar, while Josiah first, then Jehoiakim were reigning in Judea. Psammitichus, and Vaphres or Apries, succeeded this Necho in the kingdom of Egypt. Necho provoked Nebuchadnezzar with war. Nebuchadnezzar defeated him in battle at the Euphrates: then he went to avenge that injury, and having entered Coele-Syria, with the Ammonites and Moabites subdued, about whom prophecies will follow, he attacked Egypt and held a great part of it: and from there he set out into Africa, having taken as a pretext for war that the Africans had helped the Egyptians. These are the things which we gather from 2 Kings, chapter 23, near the end, and 24, 7, and from Megasthenes and Strabo, compared with that which we have below in 9, and with Josephus. Nebuchadnezzar's father, Nabopolassar, had already held some part of Egypt before, as we learn from Berosus.

AT CARCHEMISH) Which is Cercusium to Ammianus, as we said at 2 Chron. 35, 20. Egypt claimed that part of Syria for itself, as appears in 2 Kings 35, 20.

Carchemish was a fortress, whose walls the rivers Abora and Euphrates surrounded. Therefore, because the Egyptians had occupied this, they trusted in it too much.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PHARAONIS NECHAO) Qui Necos Herodoto. Regnavit is in Ægypto Nabuchodonosoris temporibus, Jo- sia primum, inde Joakimo regnantibus in Judæa. Huic Ne- chaoni in Ægypti regnum successit Psammitichus, & Va- phres sive Apries. Nechao Nabuchodonoforem bello la- cessivit. Nabuchodonosor eum prælio vicit ad Euphratem: deinde eam injuriam ultum ivit, ingressusque Cœlen Sy- riam perdomitis Ammonitis & Moabitis, de quibus vati- cinia sequentur, adortus Ægyptum, magnam ejus partem tenuit: atque inde in Africam profectus est, prætextu belli sumto, quod Afri Ægyptios adjuvissent. Hæc sunt, quæ colligimus ex 2. Reg. cap. 23. circa finem & 24, 7. & ex Me- gasthene ac Strabone, collatis cum eo, quod infra habemus 9. & cum Josepho. Partem Ægypti aliquam jam ante & Ne- buchodonosoris pater tenuerat Nabopollafarns, ut ex Be- roso discimus.

IN CHARCAMIS) Quod Cercusum Ammiano, ut diximus ad 2. Par. 35, 20. Eam partem Syriæ sibi vindi- cabat Ægyptus, ut apparet 2. Reg. 35, 20.

Carchimis fuit propugnaculum, cujus mœ- nia Abora, & Euphrates flumina ambierunt. Ideo quia Ægyptii hoc occupaverant, nimium ei con- fidebant.

## 46:3
Verse 3. PREPARE THE SHIELD AND BUCKLER, AND ADVANCE TO BATTLE) A mockery, by which that huge preparation and great threats that are about to fall into nothing are indicated.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PRÆPARATE SCUTUM ET CLYPEUM, ET PROCEDITE AD BELLUM) χλευασμός, quo indicatur ingens ille apparatus & magnæ minæ in nihilum casuræ.

## 46:4
Vers. 4. ASCENDITE EQUITES) You horsemen, mount the scythed chariots.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ASCENDITE EQUITES) Vos equites ascendite currus falcatos.

## 46:5
Vers. 5. FUGERUNT CONCITI, NEC RESPEXERUNT) A headlong flight.

Latin:

Vers. 5. FUGERUNT CONCITI, NEC RESPEXERUNT) Effusa fuga.

## 46:6
Vers. 6. NON FUGIAT VELOX) Better: The swift shall not escape. However swift they may be, they shall not escape. Thus also the Chaldean.

NEC SALVARI SE PUTET FORTIS) In the Hebrew: The strong shall not escape. That is, if there is anyone who wishes to resist the enemy, neither shall he find safety. Neither fighting nor fleeing will be of any use.

AD AQUILONEM JUXTA FLUMEN EUPHRATEM) Situated by the Aborras and the Euphrates on the northern side for the Jews. I say on the side: for the Greeks often translate צפון as βορρα̂ν, sometimes Ἀπολιώτην, as we said above 25, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 6. NON FUGIAT VELOX) Melius: Non effugiet ve- lox. Utut veloces sint, non effugient. Sic & Chaldæus.

NEC SALVARI SE PUTET FORTIS) In He- bræo: Fortis non evadet. Id est, si quis erit, qui resistere ho- sti velit, nec ille salutem inveniet. Nec pugnare proderit, nec fugere.

AD AQUILONEM JUXTA FLUMEN EU- PHRATEM) Ad Aborram & Euphraten sita ex parte Se- ptentrionali Judæis. Ex parte dico: nam & צפון Græci sæpe βορρα̂ν vertunt, interdum Ἀπολιώτην, ut diximus supra 25, 26.

## 46:7
Vers. 7. QUIS ISTE, QUI QUASI FLUMEN ASCENDIT, ET VELUTI FLUVIORUM INTUMESCUNT GURGITES EJUS) In the Hebrew: His torrents are turbid. An allusion to the Nile, which both overflows its banks and is turbid with silt.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QUIS ISTE, QUI QUASI FLUMEN ASCENDIT, ET VELUTI FLUVIORUM INTUME- SCUNT GURGITES EJUS) In Hebræo: Turbidi sunt gur- gites ejus. Allusio ad Nilum, qui & ripas transcendit, & turbidus est limo.

## 46:8
Vers. 8. ÆGYPTUS FLUMINIS INSTAR ASCENDIT) That is, the king and the army of Egypt. The Prophet answers himself with the same words with which he had questioned. See a similar instance in Is. 63, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ÆGYPTUS FLUMINIS INSTAR ASCENDIT) Id est, rex & exercitus Ægypti. Respondet sibi ipsi Propheta iisdem verbis, quibus interrogaverat. Simile vide Es. 63, 3.

## 46:9
Vers. 9. ETHIOPIA AND THE LIBYANS HOLDING THE SHIELD, AND THE LYDIANS TAKING AND SHOOTING ARROWS) Namely: - - - All Egypt and the Indians, all the Arabs, all the Sabeans turned their backs in that terror. As Virgil speaks. Libyans in the Hebrew is Phuth. See what we have said in book 1, concerning the truth of the Christian religion. From these African auxiliaries sent into Egypt, the occasion was taken by Nebuchadnezzar, after Egypt, to invade Africa.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ÆTHIOPIA ET LIBYCI TENENTES SCUTUM, ET LYDI ARRIPIENTES ET JACIENTES SAGIT- TAS) Nimirum: - - - Omnis eo terrore Ægyptus & Indi, Omnis Arabs, omnes verterunt terga Sabæi. Ut Virgilius loquitur. Lybici in Hebræo Phuth. Vide, quæ diximus ad lib. 1, de veritate religionis Christianæ. Ex his Afrorum auxiliis in Ægyptum missis occasio sumta Nabu- chodonosoro post Ægyptum invadendi Africam.

## 46:10
Vers. 10. DE INIMICIS SUIS) Of those who had killed Josiah.

VICTIMA ENIM DOMINI DEI EXERCITUUM) God will rejoice in their blood.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DE INIMICIS SUIS) De iis, qui Josiam oc- ciderant.

VICTIMA ENIM DOMINI DEI EXERCI- TUUM) Lætabitur Deus illorum sanguine.

## 46:11
Vers. 11. ASCENDE IN GALAAD, ET TOLLE RESINAM) Namely, to heal the wounds. See what was said above 8, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ASCENDE IN GALAAD, ET TOLLE RE- SINAM) Nempe ad curanda vulnera. Vide quæ dicta supra 8, 22.

## 46:12
Vers. 12. AUDIERUNT GENTES IGNOMINIAM TUAM) Your slaughter.

THE STRONG MAN HAS STRUCK AGAINST THE STRONG MAN AND BOTH HAVE FALLEN TOGETHER) Better: both shall fall in like manner: that is, now the Egyptian: but afterwards the Babylonian under the Medes.

Others more correctly [interpret it] concerning a mutual collision, and the blind impetus of the Egyptians themselves against one another: such as Jud. 7, 22. 1 Sam. 14, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 12. AUDIERUNT GENTES IGNOMINIAM TUAM) Cladem.

FORTIS IMPEGIT IN FORTEM ET AMBO PARITER CONCIDERUNT) Melius: ambo similiter cadent: id est, nunc Ægyptius: postea vero sub Medis Baby- lonius.

Rectius alii de mutua collisione, & cœco im- petu ipsorummet Ægyptiorum in se invicem: qua- lis Jud. 7, 22. 1. Sam. 14, 20.

## 46:13
Ver. 13. AND SHALL STRIKE THE LAND OF EGYPT) Shall invade with war.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET PERCUSSURUS TERRAM ÆGY- PTI) Invasurus bello.

## 46:14
Ver. 14. IN MAGDOL, AND LET IT RESOUND IN MEMPHIS AND IN TAPHNIS) See above, 44, 1.

Migdol is situated to the East, Memphis to the South, Taphne to the North; it is therefore implied that the kingdom is to be laid waste on every side.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN MAGDALO, ET RESONET IN MEMPHIS ET IN TAPHNIS) Vide supra. 44, 1.

Migdal ad Orientem, Memphis ad Meridiem, Taphne ad Septentrionem sita; innuitur ergo un- diquaque vastandum regnum.

## 46:15
Ver. 15. WHY HAS THY STRONG ONE ROTTED) In the Hebrew: he has been driven away.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QVARE COMPUTRUIT FORTIS TUUS) In Hebræo: propulsatus est.

## 46:16
Ver. 16. LET US RETURN TO OUR PEOPLE AND TO THE LAND OF OUR NATIVITY) These are the words of those who had brought aid to the Egyptians, the Lydians, Africans, and Ethiopians. See below, 21.

FROM THE FACE OF THE SWORD OF THE DOVE) Of the devastating sword. We have spoken about this matter above, 25, 38.

Latin:

Vers. 16. REVERTAMUR AD POPULUM NO- STRUM ET AD TERRAM NATIVITATIS NO- STRÆ) Verba sunt eorum qui Ægyptiis auxilium attule- rant, Lydorum, Afrorum, Æthiopum. Vide infra 21.

A FACIE GLADII COLUMBÆ) Gladii vasta- toris. Diximus hac de re supra 25, 38.

## 46:17
Ver. 17. CALL THE NAME OF PHARAOH KING OF EGYPT, A TUMULT HAS BROUGHT THE TIME) Translate: they (namely, the auxiliaries) shall say of Pharaoh king of Egypt: he is a noise, but he lets the opportunity pass. He threatens great things: but when the matter demands it, he does nothing.

B. Luther translates, he has deserted his station. The Hebrew word signifies both place and time.

Latin:

Vers. 17. VOCA NOMEN PHARAONIS REGIS Æ- GYPTI, TUMULTUM ADDUXIT TEMPUS) Verte: dicent illi, (nempe auxiliares) de Pharaone rege Ægypti: strepi- tus est, sed transmittit occasionem. Magna minatur: sed ubi res exigit, nihil agit.

B. Lutherus vertit, deseruit stationem suam. Vox Ebræa tam locum, quam tempus significat.

## 46:18
Ver. 18. FOR AS THABOR IS AMONG THE MOUNTAINS, AND CARMEL BY THE SEA, HE SHALL COME) This is as certain to happen as it is certain that Thabor, or Mount Itabyrium, is enclosed by mountains, and that Carmel, a mountain of Syria, reaches to the sea.

So indeed Jonathan and R. Solomon, Aquila, Theodoret, Tremellius, Piscator. But such a formula of attestation is unusual in the Scriptures: therefore Kimchi, Jerome, Luther, Castro, Cornelius, Maldonatus are more correct: that as Thabor was a fortified place, and Carmel also, because of its situation by the sea and its height, was an inaccessible mountain, so the King of Babylon would approach with insuperable force. Compare Cant. 7, 5. Am. 9, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 18. QVONIAM SICUT THABOR IN MON- TIBUS, ET CARMELUS IN MARI VENIET) Tam certum hoc est eventurum, quam certum Thaborem, sive Itabyrium montibus claudi, & Carmelum Syriæ montem ad mare pertingere.

Ita quidem Jonathan & R. Salomo, Aquila, Theodoret. Tremell. Piscat. Sed formula talis atte- standi in sacris insolita est: Ideo rectius Kimchi, Hieron. Luther. Castro, Corn. Maldonat. uti Tha- bor locus munitus erat, Carmel quoque ob situm ad mare, & altitudinem suam mons inaccessus, ita Regem Babylon. vi insuperabili accessurum. Conf. Cant. 7, 5. Am. 9, 3.

## 46:19
Ver. 19. MAKE THEE VESSELS OF REMOVAL) Gather your vessels, as the Latins say.

Latin:

Vers. 19. VASA TRANSMIGRATIONIS FAC TI- BI) Vasa collige, ut loquuntur Latini.

## 46:20
Ver. 20. EGYPT IS A FAIR AND BEAUTIFUL HEIFER) He alludes to the worship of Apis and Mnevis.

A GOAD SHALL COME UPON HER FROM THE NORTH) A slaughterer. Thus the Chaldean, and קרץ is accustomed to be used among the Talmudists for a slaughterer.

Latin:

Vers. 20. VITULA ELEGANS ATQVE FORMO- SA ÆGYPTUS) Alludit ad cultum Apidos & Mnevis.

STIMULATOR AB AQUILONE VENIET EI) Mactator. Ita Chaldæus, & solet קרץ apud Thalmudistas de victimario dici.

## 46:21
HIRELINGS.

Sc. soldiers hired for pay, ver. 9.

Ver. 21. AS CALVES OF THE STALL) Refer this to the preceding: who were in the midst of her.

Latin:

MERCENARII.

Sc. milites mercede conducti vers. 9.

Vers. 21. QVASI VITULI SAGINATI) Refer hoc ad præcedentia: qui versabantur in medio ejus.

## 46:22
Ver. 22. HER VOICE SHALL SOUND LIKE BRASS) It may seem to be an allusion to sistrums. Thus Virgil: The queen in the midst calls the troops with her native sistrum. But both the Chaldean and the Greeks translate נחש as serpent: so that the sense may be: they shall hiss for fear like a viper.

This does not suit the text, even though it is approved by Tremellius, because the discourse is about the fury of the King, whence the interpretation of the Vulgate, Luther, Castro, Giselerius, and Sanctius concerning brass, and the sound of axes and other instruments of war, is to be preferred. See ver. 23.

THEY SHALL COME WITH AXES AS HEWERS OF WOOD) Armed in the Scythian manner.

Latin:

Vers. 22. VOX EJUS QVASI ÆRIS SONABAT) Allusum videri potest ad sistra. Sic Virgilius: Regina in mediis patrio vocat agmina sistro. Sed & Chaldæus & Græci נחש serpentem vertunt: ut ser- sus sit: sibilabunt præ metu ut vipera.

Non convenit hoc textui, etsi probetur Tre- mellio, quia de furore Regis sermo est, unde præfe- renda Vulg. Luther. Castro, Giselerii, Sanctii inter- pretatio de ære, & sonitu securium & aliorum in- strumentorum bellicorum. Vid. v. 23.

CUM SECURIBUS VENIENT QVASI CÆ- DENTES LIGNA) Armati Scythicum in morem.

## 46:23
Ver. 23. THEY HAVE CUT DOWN HER FOREST, SAITH THE LORD, WHICH CANNOT BE COUNTED) Cut down her forest, saith the Lord, (to the army) which cannot be counted. He persists in the metaphor of the woodcutter begun. The forest is the cities, which were one thousand and twenty in Egypt in those times.

THEY ARE MULTIPLIED ABOVE THE LOCUSTS, AND THERE IS NO NUMBER OF THEM) The Chaldeans are more numerous than locusts, nay, they are innumerable.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SUCCIDERUNT SALTUM EJUS, AIT DOMINUS: QVI SUPPUTARI NON POTEST) Succidite sylvam ejus, ait Dominus, (ad exercitum) qui suppu- tari non potest. Perstat in similitudine cœpta ὑλοτόμυ. Sylva sunt urbes, quæ in Ægypto mille & viginti illis temporibus.

MULTIPLICATI SUNT SUPER LOCUSTAS, ET NON EST EIS NUMERUS) Qui Chaldæi plures sunt quam locustæ, imo innumeri.

## 46:25
Ver. 25. BEHOLD I WILL VISIT UPON THE MULTITUDE OF ALEXANDRIA) In the Hebrew here is אמון מנא, in Nahum 3, 7, נא אמון: It was a most populous city of Egypt, in Pharo, as I think, whence the Chaldean, from the name of a later age, put Alexandria. But מנא is a dialect for אמום of the people: אמון מנא people of No: נא אמון populous No.

Thus the word אמון is understood concerning a multitude, Ez. 30, 14. 15. Mal. 3, 18. Luther, Pagninus, Arias, Junius, and Piscator explain it as 'prefect,' which seems preferable to B. Hülsemann, because the vengeance to be taken upon the King and Kingdom of Egypt follows immediately. But No is that city at the mouth of the Nile, which, having been destroyed by the Chaldeans so that it might not be a bulwark for the invader Alexander, was restored by him and called Alexandria.

AND UPON ITS GODS) Monsters of every kind of god, as Virgil speaks. See above 43, 12. 13.

AND UPON ITS KINGS) Thus he calls the nomarchs. Concerning whom see Strabo and Aristotle, 2 Ethics.

AND UPON PHARAOH) Upon Pharaoh, I say, for the ו is often placed thus, and mention of Pharaoh has already preceded.

AND UPON THOSE WHO TRUST IN HIM) Subjects and allies.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ECCE EGO VISITABO SUPER TUMUL- TUM ALEXANDRIÆ) In Hebræo hic אמון מנא, apud Nahumum 3, 7. נא אמון: Fuit urbs Ægypti popu- losissima, in Pharo, ut puto, unde Chaldæus, ex posterioris ævi nomine Alexandriam posuit. At מנא est dialectus pro אמום populi: אמון מנא populi de No: נא אמון No populosa.

Ita vox אמון de multitudine accipitur Ez. 30, 14. 15. Mal. 3, 18. Lutherus, Pagninus, Arias, Ju- nius, Piscator de præfecto explicant, quod præferen- dum videtur B. Hülsemanno, quia immediate sequi- tur vindicta de Rege & Regno Ægypti sumenda. No autem est urbs illa ad ostium Nili, quæ à Chal- dæis diruta, ne Alexandro invasori propugnacu- lum esset, ab hoc instaurata, & Alexandria vocata.

ET SVPER DEOS EJVS) Omnigenum Deum monstra, ut loquitur Virgilius. Vide supra 43, 12. 13.

ET SVPER REGES EJVS) Sic vocat τές νομάρ- χας. De quibus vide Strabonem & Aristotelem 2. Ethi. corum.

ET SVPER PHARAONEM) Super Pharaonem, in- quam, Nam ו sæpe sic ponitur, & præcessit jam Pharaonis mentio,

ET SVPER EOS QVI CONFIDVNT IN EO) Subditos & socios.

## 46:26
Ver. 26. AND AFTER THESE THINGS IT SHALL BE INHABITED AS IN THE DAYS OF OLD, SAYS THE LORD) Egypt, having been greatly desolated after 40 years, will begin to flourish again and to recover its liberty and commerce. See Ezek. 19, 11. And the restoration falls in the times of Amasis, a contemporary of Cyrus.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET POST HÆC HABITABITVR SICVT DIEBVS PRISTINIS, AIT DOMINVS) Ægyptus val- de desolata post annos 40. incipiet reflorescere, & liber- tatem suam ac commercia recuperare. Vide Ezech. 19, 11. Et ἀποκατάστασις incidit in Amasis tempora, Cyro coævi.

## 46:27
Ver. 27. AND DO NOT THOU FEAR, O MY SERVANT JACOB, AND DO NOT BE DISMAYED, O ISRAEL.) This consolation pertains to those who had been led away into Egypt by King Necho with King Jehoahaz, 2 Chron. 36, 4, whom he says will return to their fatherland, namely, once the affairs of the Egyptians are broken.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET TV NE TIMEAS SERVVS MEVS JACOB, ET NE PAVEAS ISRAEL.) Hæc consolatio pertinet ad eos, qui à Rege Necaone cum Joachazo Rege in Ægyptum abducti erant 2. Paral. 36, 4. quos redituros ait in patriam, nempe fractis Ægyptiorum rebus.

## 46:28
Ver. 28. I WILL CONSUME ALL THE NATIONS TO WHICH I HAVE CAST THEE) That is, I will exhaust them with most grievous disasters, and as it were with slaughter.

I WILL CHASTISE THEE IN JUDGMENT) Moderately, so that you may learn, not so that you may perish. See above 10, 23. ch. 30, 11.

NOR WILL I SPARE THEE AS IF THOU WERE INNOCENT) How these words are best translated, see above 30, 11.

Osiander explains this passage concerning spiritual liberation: Now the Prophet consoles the Church of the people of God, and prophesies concerning the kingdom of Christ: And do not thou fear, O my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, O Israel: be of good courage, O my Church. Because behold, I will save thee (my people) from the land of thy captivity: I will deliver you and your descendants from captivity: even though you may be scattered far and wide. And the people of Jacob will return to their fatherland, and will rest, and will enjoy true tranquility, and will prosper: it will have an abundance of all necessary things: (for that is what the Hebrew word signifies) and there will be no one to terrify it: for it will dwell in great and true security. And although these things appear to be spoken according to the letter concerning the return from the Babylonian exile, yet in truth the Prophet speaks concerning the benefits of the New Testament. For there the Church is gathered through the ministry of the Gospel from the whole world and from distant places: and it enjoys through faith in Christ the tranquility of conscience, Rom. 5. Nay, it is also abundantly fed by the word of the Gospel, and by the Sacrament of the body and blood of Christ, and is secure in faith. For it knows that the gates of hell cannot prevail against it, Matt. 16. (And do not thou, I say, fear, O my servant Jacob, says the Lord: be of tranquil and good courage, my dearest Church: because I am with thee, I will be present with thee in all afflictions, so that I may deliver thee. (If, however, the Lord is with us and for us, who is against us? Rom. 8.) Because I will indeed consume all the nations to which I have cast thee: but thee I will not consume; I will spare thee: for the impious nations are blotted out, but the Church of Christ is not blotted out.) But I will nevertheless chastise thee in judgment (i. e. having applied moderation) nor shall I spare you as if you were innocent: that is, for I cannot spare you entirely: because you are not innocent of every sin. For the Lord corrects His Church, so that it may acknowledge its sins and infirmities: lest it be plunged into carnal security, and be condemned with the world 1. Corinth. 11. Bugenhagius also sets forth the Evangelical promise here, although he wishes the consolation of the Jews to be delivered, because God wishes only to chastise them, as a father does a son, lest they think themselves innocent in their idolatry and contempt of the word of God. A parallel passage is chapter 30, 11. where Osian der thinks that the Church is likewise addressed and that spiritual security and happiness are promised to it. Bugenhagius interpreted those words also, I WILL MAKE A CONSUMMATION IN ALL NATIONS, IN WHICH I HAVE SCATTERED THEE, BUT THEE I WILL NOT MAKE INTO A CONSUMMATION, Chap. 30, in this way: I will destroy all others, but my people, that is, the believers and those serving their King the Messiah, I will not destroy. All other kingdoms will have an end, the kingdom of Christ will have no end. And yet I will first correct my elect with captivity and vexation and terrors of conscience through the preaching of the law, lest they seem to themselves innocent and such as are owed grace for their merits, which is promised. And he expounded that consolation, Do not fear, Chap. 30, in that sense as well. And what will be the fruit of this kingdom of CHRIST for us? Freedom from sin, and joy of conscience before God, which follows thus: therefore Jacob, do not fear: For Behold I, etc. The word I has a most weighty emphasis and intensity, as if God were saying: Not Moses or the law, not you, or your works, or any creature will deliver you, but I, I alone will deliver you from the captivity in which you have been cast far from God. For after the resolution of the Babylonian captivity, there will also be another resolution through Christ of a far greater captivity. I will deliver, he says, then, but under King David, that is, Christ. Those things which follow in this promise also pertain to the security of consciences, that Jacob may return, etc. Not only to those goods which the Jews received on earth. Not to mention that the ten tribes did not receive their fields and possessions, which were nevertheless very meager goods in comparison with those which are promised here, and scarcely their shadow; it is also evident how they were often vexed under foreign Kings, up to Christ, as I said, Chap. 23. The continuity of the text seems to favor this explanation, because the Messiah had been dealt with previously in verse 9. Other interpreters, however, take both parts to refer to liberation from external captivity, to which B. Hülsemann and, among the ancients, St. Jerome also subscribed. Moreover, the Divine discourse promises, and calls its servant Jacob and Israel familiar, just as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are called servants of God. Moses also and other Prophets, and the Apostle Paul in the beginning of his Epistles glories in this title, so that the twelve tribes, that is, the twelve, may know that they are to be saved from a far land, and that the captivity is to be resolved, and peace is to be restored, and they are to be filled with every abundance: according to that which is said in the Psalm: Let there be peace in thy strength, and abundance in thy towers. This, however, will be, because they will enjoy the presence of the Lord, when the opposing nations, which had taken them, will perish, and these will be delivered from the nations. And he teaches that they were by no means handed over for punishment, but for instruction, so that they might be judged as his own; they would not be lost as if they were strangers. The Vinarie Paraphrasts, according to their custom, combine both senses regarding the Israelite people and the kingdom of Christ, even though they acknowledge that the latter is the principal one. Regarding what should be held about this, we have spoken at that place and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 28. CONSVMAM CVNCTAS GENTES, AD QVAS EJECT TE) Id est, gravissimis cladibus, ac velut internecione, eos exhauriam.

CASTIGABO TE IN JVDICIO) Moderate, ut discas, non ut pereas. Vide supra 10, 23. c. 30, 11.

NEC QVASI INNOCENTI PARCAM TIBI ) Quomodo hæc verba optime vertantur, vide supra 30, 11.

De Spirituali liberatione hanc pericopam ex- plicat Osiander : Nunc Propheta Ecclesiam populi Dei consolatur, & de regno Christi vaticinatur : Et tu ne timeas serve meus Jacob, & ne paveas ô Israel: sis bono animo tu Ecclesia mea. Quia ecce ego salva- bo te (populum meum) de terra captivitatis tuæ: ego vos & posteros vestros eripiam de captivitate: licet longe lateque disjecti sitis. Et revertetur populus Jacob in patriam suam, & requiescet, tranquillitate vera fruetur, & prosperabitur: habebit omnium re- rum necessariarum copiam: (id enim Hebræum voca- bulum significat) & non erit, qui exterreat eum: in magna enim & vera securitate deget. Etsi autem hæc juxta literam de reditu ex exilio Babylonico dicta apparent, tamen revera Propheta loquitur de beneficiis novi Testamenti. Ibi enim Ecclesia per ministerium Evangelii colligitur ex orbe terrarum, & longinquis locis: & fruitur per fidem in Chri- stum tranquillitate conscientiæ, Rom. 5. Quin & abunde pascitur verbo Evangelii, & Sacramento corporis & sanguinis Christi, & secura est in fide. Novit enim, quod portæ inferorum adversus ipsam prævalere non possint Matt. 16. (Et tu noli, inquam, timere serve meus Jacob, ait Dominus: sis tranquil- lo & bono animo, mea charissima Ecclesia : quia tecum ego sum, adero tibi in omnibus afflictionibus, ut te eripiam. (Si autem Dominus nobiscum, & pro nobis, quis contra nos? Rom. 8.) Quia ego consu- mam quidem cunctas gentes, ad quas ejeci te: te vero non consumam; tibi parcam: delentur enim impiæ gentes, non deletur autem Ecclesia Christi.) Sed castigabo tamen te, in judicio (i. e. adhibita mode- ratione) nec quasi innocenti parcam tibi: id est, non enim possum tibi omnino parcere: quia non es ab omni peccato innocens. Dominus enim Ecclesiam suam corripit, ut peccata & infirmitates suas agno- scat: ne in carnalem securitatem immergatur, & cum mundo damnetur 1. Corinth. 11. Promissionem etiam Evangelicam hic ponit Bugenhagius, etsi consolationem Judæorum tradi velit, quod eos Deus tantum castigare velit, ut pater filium, ne se innocentes sua Idololatria & verbi Dei comtemtu putent. Locus parallelus est cap. 30, 11. ubi Osian- der itidem Ecclefiam compellari & securitatem ac fe- licitatem spiritualem ipsi promitti existimat. Verba etiam illa FACIAM CONSUMMATIONEM IN OMNIBUS GENTIBUS, IN QUIBUS DISPERSI TE, TE AUTEM NON FA- CIAM IN CONSUMMATIONEM Cap. 30. Bugenhagius ita interpretatus est: Omnes alios perdam, populum autem meum, id est, credentes, & Regi suo Messiæ servientes non perdam. Alia regna omnia habebunt finem, Christi regni non erit finis. Et tamen corripiam primum electos meos captivitate & vexatione & terroribus conscientiarum per prædica- tionem legis, ne videantur sibi innocentes & tales, qui- bus gratia pro meritis debeatur, quæ promittitur. At- que in eam sententiam exposuit etiam illam conso- lationem, Noli timere Cap. 30. Ac quis erit nobis fructus hujus regni CHRISTI? Libertas à pec- cato, & gaudium conscientiarum coram Deo, id quod sic sequitur: ideo Jacob, noli timere: Quia Ecce Ego, &c. dictio Ego Emphasin & Epitasin habet gra- vissimam, quasi dicat Deus: Non Moses aut lex, non vos, aut vestra opera, aut ulla creatura vos libe- rabit, sed ego, Ego solus liberabo vos ex captivita- te, in qua longe abjecti estis â Deo. Nam post ca- ptivitatis Babylonicæ solutionem, etiam alia erit solu- tio per Christum longe majoris captivitatis. Libera- bo, inquit, tunc, sed sub Rege Davide, id est, Christo. Ad securitatem conscientiarum quoque pertinent ea, quæ sequuntur in hac promissione, ut revertatur Jacob &c. Non solum ad ea bona, quæ Judæi in terris acceperunt. Ut non dicam, quod decem tribus non receperunt suos agros & possessiones, quæ tamen bona valde tenuia erant, comparatione eorum, quæ hic promittuntur, & vix eorum umbra; constat etiam, quam vexati sint sæpe sub alienis Regibus, usque ad Christum, ut dixi, Cap. 23. Cui explicationi fave- re videtur συνέχεια textus, quia antea de Messia actum erat vers. 9. Alii tamen interpretes de libe- ratione è captivitate externa utrumque locum acci- piunt, quibus etiam accessit B. Hülsemannus & è veteribus S. Hieronymus. Pollicetur autem sermo Divinus, & familiarem vocat servum suum Jacob & Israel, sicut Abraham, Isaac & Jacob vocantur servi Dei. Moyses quoque & alii Prophetæ, & Apo- stolus Paulus in principio Epistolarum suarum hic ti- tulo gloriatur, ut duæ & decem tribus, id est, duode- cim sciant, se de terra longinqua esse salvandas, & sol- vendam captivitatem, reddendamque pacem, & omni eas replendas abundantia: juxta illud, quod in Psal- mo dicitur: Fiat pax in virtute tua, & abundantia in turribus tuis. Hoc autem erit, quia præsentia Do- mini perfruentur, quando & gentes adversariæ, quæ eos ceperant, disperibunt, & isti liberabuntur ex gen- tibus. Docetque eos nequaquam pœnæ, sed eruditioni traditos, ut judicarentur, quasi proprii; non perde- rentur, quasi alieni. Paraphrastæ Vinarienses pro more suo utrumque sensum de populo Israelitico, & de regno Christi conjungunt, etsi hunc præci- puum esse agnoscant. De quo quid habendum, ad istum locum, & alias diximus.

## 47:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLVII. It is predicted what threatens the Philistines, the Tyrians, the Sidonians, Gaza, and Ascalon.

Vers. 1.

THE WORD OF THE LORD THAT CAME) A transposition for The word of the Lord that came. BEFORE PHARAO SMOTE GAZA) Since either the prophet, or he who collected these prophecies, divided them not by times but by these nations, I understand Pharaoh Necho here: Gaza, a city of the Philistines, was besieged by him after the victory at Megiddo, when now no one dared to contend against him in battle any further. Moreover, this Prophecy is the more notable because it predicted the devastation of the land of the Philistines at a time when all hostile things were expected from the Egyptians alone, but friendly things from the Chaldeans.

Most agree on this with Seder Olam, R. Salom., and Rabbi Kimchi. Lyranus, Castro, Sanctius, and others [agree] that these things happened when Pharaoh Necho came to the aid of the Jews besieged by Nebuchadnezzar, c. 37. 4. Nor does the opinion of Tremellius, Piscator, and the Tigurines, that these things happened a long time after the destruction of Jerusalem, hold up: because Jeremiah speaks of that slaughter which happened in his own time.

Latin:

CAPUT XLVII. Quid Philistinis, Tyriis, Sidoniis, Gazæ, & Ascatoni immineat, prædicitur.

Vers. 1.

QVOD FACTVM EST VERBVM DOMINI) Transpositio pro Verbum Domini quod factum est. ANTEQVAM PERCVTERET PHARAO GA- ZAM) Cum non per tempora, sed per gentes has Prophe- tias dispartiverit, aut propheta, aut is, qui eas collegit, Phara- onem hic intelligo Nechaonem: ab eo autem obsessam Ga- zam Philistinorum urbem post victoriam in Mageddo, cum jam nemo ultra adversus eum prælio certare auderet. Est autem hæc Prophetia eo insignior, quod Philisthinæ terra vastationem prædixit eo tempore, cum à solis Ægyptiis ho- stilia, à Chaldæis vero amica omnia expectarentur.

COnveniunt in eo plerique cum Seder Olam, R. Salom. & Rabbi Kimch. Lyran. Castro, San- ctius, alii tum evenisse hæc, quando Pharao Necho Judæis à Nebucadn. obsessis in subsidium venit, c. 37. 4. neque convenit Tremellii, Piscator. & Tigur. opinio, multo tempore post excidium Hierosol. hæc accidisse: quia loquitur Jeremias de ea clade, quæ suo tempore evenerit.

## 47:2
Vers. 2. BEHOLD WATERS ASCEND FROM THE NORTH: AND THEY SHALL BE AS AN OVERFLOWING TORRENT) As the Egyptians are compared to the Nile, so the Chaldeans are compared to the Euphrates. Moreover, I do not doubt that those things which are predicted here were done through Nebuzaradan, whom Nebuchadnezzar had left behind to subdue the rest of the surroundings after Jerusalem was captured.

The army of the Assyrians is described with the same simile in Isa. 8, 7. 12. 11, 15.

AND ALL SHALL HOWL) The Prophets are accustomed to use the word היליל in the sense of grave mourning. It is translated by ὀλολύζειν, ἀλαλάζειν, θρηνεῖν, πενθεῖν.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ECCE AQVÆ ASCENDUNT AB AQVI- LONE : ET ERUNT QVASI TORRENS INUN- DANS ) Sicut Ægyptii Nilo, sic Chaldæi Euphrati compa- rantur. Ea autem quæ hic prædicuntur, non dubito quin fa- cta sint per Nebuzardanem, quem post capta Hierosolyma, cæteris circum perdomandis, Nabuchodonosor reli- querat.

Eadem similitudine describitur exercitus As- syriorum Esa. 8, 7. 12. 11, 15.

ET ULULABUNT OMNES ) Solent Prophetæ voce היליל uti in significatu luctus gravis. Vertitur per ὀλολύζειν, ἀλαλάζειν, θρηνεῖν, πενθεῖν.

## 47:3
Vers. 3. AT THE NOISE OF THE POMP OF HIS ARMOR AND HIS WARRIORS) From the quadrupedal sound of strong hoofs (that is) of his cavalry.

FROM THE COMMOTION OF HIS CHARIOTS) From the noise of his chariots.

AND THE MULTITUDE OF HIS WHEELS) From the crashing of the wheels.

THE FATHERS HAVE NOT LOOKED BACK TO THEIR CHILDREN) The fathers shall not look back to their children. And connect this with the preceding. Each one will look to his own safety with the utmost haste, regarding no family ties.

See above ch. 6, 24. ch. 38, 4.

WITH HANDS DISSOLVED) All hope will be in the feet, not in the hands.

Latin:

Vers. 3. A STREPITV POMPÆ ARMORVM ET BELLATORVM EJVS ) A quadrupedante sono ungula- rum fortium (id est) equitum ejus.

A COMMOTIONE QVADRIGARVM EJVS) A strepitu quadrigarum ejus.

ET MVLTITVDINE ROTARVM ILLIVS ) Præ fragore rotarum.

NON RESPEXERVNT PATRES FILIOS) Non respicient patres filios. Et connecte cum præcedentibus. Sibi quisque consulet summa festinatione, nullas necessi- tudines respiciens.

Vid. Supra c. 6, 24. c. 38, 4.

MANIBVS DISSOLVTIS) Spes omnis in pedibus erit non in manibus.

## 47:4
Verse 4. FOR THE COMING OF THE DAY) In the Hebrew: The day coming upon: that is, when that day shall have come.

AND TYRE AND SIDON SHALL BE DESTROYED WITH ALL THEIR REMAINING AIDS) That is, the Tyrians and Sidonians, and other auxiliaries of the Philistines.

FOR HE HAS DEPOPULATED) He will depopulate.

THE REMNANTS OF THE ISLAND OF CAPPADOCIA) כפתור They translate as Cappadocia, not only here the Chaldean and the Greeks, but also the Jerusalem interpreter at Deut. 2, 23, and Jerome thinks no differently. Wherefore it is to be held as true that the Philistines came from Cappadocia, which is called an island because it is maritime, and that the city of Idumea, Capatorfa, has its name from them, as we noted at the said place in Deuteronomy. Add Amos 9, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PRO ADVENTV DIEI) In Hebræo: Super- venire diem : id est, cum ille dies venerit.

ET DISSIPABITVR TTRVS ET SIDON CVM OMNIBVS RELIQVIS AVXILIIS SVIS) Id est, Tyrii & Sidonii, aliique auxiliares Philistinorum.

DEPOPVLATVS EST ENIM) Depopulabitur.

RELIQVIAS INSVLÆ CAPPADOCIÆ) כפתור Cappadociam transferunt, non hic tantum Chaldæus & Græci sed & Hierosolymitanus interpres ad Deut. 2, 23. nec aliter censet Hieronymus. Quare pro vero habendum à Cappadocia, quæ insula vocatur quod maritima sit, venis- se Philistinos, & ab iisdem nomen habere Idumææ urbem Capatorfam, ut ad dictum Deuteronomii locum notavi- mus. Adde Amosum 9, 7.

## 47:5
Verse 5. BALDNESS HAS COME UPON GAZA) A sign of mourning, as in Isaiah 3, 24.

This is to be preferred to the explanation of Calvin, Lyranus, and Tostatus concerning the depopulation of crops and temporal goods: as is evident from the end of the verse.

ASCALON HAS BEEN SILENCED) It shall be cut off. Thus the Greeks and the Chaldean.

AND THE REMAINDER OF THE VALLEY OF THEM) More correctly: of them: that is, and other cities of the Philistines situated in the valleys. For the cities which he had already named were more elevated. But the LXX, for עמקם, read ענקים, Enakim. This reading pleases me. For it appears that the remnants of the Enakim were in those places, Num. 13:19.

HOW LONG WILL YOU CUT YOURSELF) In the Hebrew: How long will you cut yourself? that is, how long will you lacerate your arms with knives? which those nations were accustomed to do in mourning, as we said at Lev. 19:28.

See also Deut. 14:1, where incision is indeed forbidden to the Jews, but they nevertheless sometimes employed the rites of neighboring nations in baldness and the shaving of the beard due to excessive mourning.

Latin:

Vers. 5. VENIT CALVITIVM SVPER GAZAM) Luctus signum ut Esaiæ 3, 24.

Præferendum id explicationi Calvini, Lyrani & Tostati de depopulatione frugum & opum tem- poralium: ut è fine versus patet.

CONTICVIT ASCALON) Excidetur. Sic Græci & Chaldæus.

ET RELIQVIÆ VALLIS EARVM) Rectius : eo- rum : id est, & aliæ urbes Philistinorum in vallibus sitæ. Nam quas nominaverat jam urbes, eæ editiores erant. At LXX. pro עמקם legerunt ענקים Ἐνακείμ. Placet mihi hæc lectio. Nam reliquias Enaciin fuisse illis in locis appa- ret Num. 13, 19.

VSQVE QVO CONCIDERIS ) In Hebræo : Quousque te incides? id est, quousque brachia tua cultris lacerabis? quod gentes illæ in luctu facere solebant, ut diximus ad Levit. 19, 28.

Vid. & Deut. 14, 1. ubi Judæis quidem inter- dicta incisio, sed illi quandoque tamen præ nimio luctu ritus gentium vicinarum in calvitio & rasura barbæ adhibuere.

## 47:6
Verse 6. O SWORD OF THE LORD) That is, saying, O sword of the Lord. He imitates the words of those cutting themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 6. O MVCRO DOMINI) Id est, dicens, ò mu- cro Domini. Verba incidentium se imitatur.

## 47:7
Verse 7. HOW RESTING?) The Prophet responds to their lamentation.

WHEN THE LORD HAS COMMANDED IT AGAINST ASCALON) Supply, to go.

AND AGAINST ITS MARITIME REGIONS) Joppa, Jamnia.

AND THERE HE HAS APPOINTED IT. In Hebrew: there he has summoned it, namely, the sword. The Hebrew word denotes a solemn summoning, as the Chaldean and the Rabbis explain, as also B. Luther, with the word bestellen.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVO MODO QVIESCENS? ) Respondet illorum planctui Prophetæ.

CVM DOMINVS PRÆCEPERIT EI ADVER- SVS ASCALONEM ) Supple, ire.

ET ADVERSVS MARITIMAS EJVS REGIO- NES) Joppen, Jamnes.

IBIQUE CONDIXERIT ILLI. In Ebr. ibi convocavit eum, sc. gladium. Vox Ebr. sole- mnem convocationem notat, uti Chald. & Rabbini exponunt, ut & B. Luther, voce bestellen.

## 48:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLVIII.

The devastation of the Moabites predicted on account of their security and pride, but their captivity is to be relaxed in the last days.

Vers. 1. AGAINST MOAB THUS SAITH THE LORD OF HOSTS) We have a prophecy concerning the devastation of the Moabite territory, which came to pass through Shalmaneser, in Isaiah 15 and 16. Here I do not doubt that it treats of that which was done by Nebuzaradan, of which Ezekiel also treats in 5 and 9. These are among those Syrians or Phoenicians whom Berosus narrates were subdued by Nebuchadnezzar. Josephus says this destruction happened to both the Moabites and the Ammonites in the fifth year after Jerusalem was destroyed.

WOE UPON NEBO) See Num. 33, 47. Isaiah 15, 2. Inaba in Ptolemy.

From Num. 33 and Josh. 12 and 13 it appears that this and other principal cities of the Moabites belonged to the Israelites: from whom, therefore, they must have been successively snatched away.

KIRIATHAIM IS TAKEN) Joshua 13, 19. A city consisting of two cities, as the word shows, perhaps the same as Kir-heres. Isaiah 16, 7. Chariatha in Ptolemy.

Latin:

CAPUT XLVIII.

Moabitis vastatio ob securitatem, & super- biam prædicta, sed relaxanda in novissimis diebus captivitas.

Vers. 1. AD MOAB HÆC DICIT DOMINUS EXER- CITUVM) Prophetiam de vastatione Moabitidos, quæ per Salmanassarem evenit, habemus Esaiæ 15. & 16. Hic non dubito quin de ea agatur, quæ per Nabuzardanem facta est, de qua & Ezechiel agit 5, 9. Hi sunt inter illos Syros, aut Phœnices, quos à Nabuchodonosoro subactos narrat Berosus. Evenisse hoc excidium & Moabitis & Ammonitis ait Josephus quinto anno post excisa Hierosolyma.

VÆ SVPER NABO) Vide Num. 33, 47. Esaiam 15, 2. Ἰνάβα Ptolemæo.

ENum. 33. & Jos. 12. & 13. apparet pertinuisse hanc & alias urbes præcipuas Moabitarum ad Israelitas: quibus proinde successive ereptas illas esse oportet.

CAPTA EST CARIATHAIM) Josua 13, 19. Urbs ex duabus urbibus constans, ut vocabulum ostendit, forte eadem quæ Kir-chereseth. Esaiæ 16, 7. Chariatha Ptole- mæo.

## 48:2
Vers. 2. AGAINST HESHBON THEY HAVE DEVISED EVIL) The Chaldeans, of course, saying those things which follow. Concerning Heshbon see Isaiah 15, 4; 16, 8. Esbus in Ptolemy. Hence the Esbonite Arabs in Pliny, as we have said elsewhere.

See concerning Heshbon, which was once the seat of the King of the Amorites, assigned to the Reubenites, Num. 21, 31 ff.; Josh. 13, 19.

THEREFORE SILENT YOU SHALL BE SILENT) Madmen you shall be silent. An allusion to the name Madmen from damam, which is to be silent. You shall not dare to mutter. Madmen is Madiama in Ptolemy. Madaba in Josephus 13, 17, where perhaps it was written medama. For beta and mu are very similar in manuscripts.

The Vulgate is deservedly corrected. For this is a proper name of a city, as appears from other cities similarly designated in this place.

AND THE SWORD SHALL FOLLOW THEE) It shall pursue.

Latin:

Vers. 2. CONTRA ESEBON COGITAVERUNT MALVM) Chaldæi nimirum, dicentes ea quæ sequuntur. De Esebone vide Esaiam 15, 4. 16, 8. Ἐσβῦς Ptolemæo. Hinc Esbonitæ Arabes apud Plinium, ut alibi diximus.

Vid. de Hesbon, quæ sedes fuit quondam Re- gis Amoritarum Rubenitis tributa Num. 21, 31. seqq. Jos. 13, 19.

ERGO SILENS CONTICESCES) Madmen filebis. Allusio ad nomen מדמן à דמם, quod est silere. Mutire non audebis. Madmen Madiama Ptolemæo. Madaba Jo- sepho 13, 17. ubi forte scriptum fuit μηδαμά. Nam β & μ valde similes in manuscriptis.

Corrigitur merito vulgata. Est enim hic no- men urbis proprium, uti ex aliis urbibus similiter designatis hoc loco apparet.

SEQUITVRQVE TE GLADIVS) Insequetur.

## 48:3
Vers. 3. A VOICE OF CRYING FROM HORONAIM) Isaiah 15, 5. Where we said this is the Avara of Ptolemy.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VOX CLAMORIS DE ORONAIM) Esaias 15, 5. Vbi diximus hanc esse Avaram Ptolemæi.

## 48:5
Vers. 5. PER ASCENSVM ENIM LVITH) He repeats the very words of Isaiah in a similar matter, 15, 5. Where we have noted that this is Lusa for Ptolemy.

Alsted, in book 2 of his Theological Precognitions, p. 236, wrongly makes Luchith and Horonaim mimetic words of those wailing. For those cities were, the former on a mountain, the latter in a valley, Is. 15:5. See Eusebius, book 1, Hist. ch. 5, in which the Hebrews and other interpreters agree.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PER ASCENSVM ENIM LVITH) Repe- tit ipsa Esaiæ verba in re simili, 15, 5. Vbi hanc Ptolemæo Lusam esse notavimus.

Perperam Alstedius l. 2. præcogn. Theol. p. 236. Luchit, & Choronaim voces Mimeticas ejulantium facit. Fuere enim urbes illa in monte, hæc in convalle Es. 15, 5. V. Euseb. l. 1. Hist. c. 5. in quo consentiunt Ebræi, aliique Interpp.

## 48:6
Vers. 6. AND YE SHALL BE LIKE THE HEATH IN THE DESERT) Be ye: that is, live in desert and pathless places, as the heath or junipers do: do not trust in walls, as follows. Concerning the word ערוער see above. The Chaldean here takes as a proper name what we ourselves have below in 19.

Thus also the Jews understand the city of Aroer situated by the torrent of Arnon, Josh. 13:9, and this destruction seems to be compared with the destruction of the city of Aroer.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET ERITIS QVASI MTRICÆ IN DE- SERTO) Estote: id est, vivite in desertis, atque inviis lo- cis, ut myricæ faciunt, aut juniperi: ne fidite muris, ut se- quitur. De voce ערוער vide supra. Chaldæus pro proprio nomine hic accipit quod ipsum infra habemus 19.

Sic etiam Judæi intelligunt urbein Aroër sitam ad torrentem Arnon Jos. 13, 9. & videtur compa- rari hoc excidium cum excidio urbis Aroër.

## 48:7
Ver. 7. YOU ALSO SHALL BE TAKEN) Namely, Ar-Moab, the most fortified city of the Moabites, called ἄρη βασιλείαν by Ptolemy. See the cited passage of Ezekiel.

CHEMOSH SHALL GO INTO CAPTIVITY) For when peoples are captured, their gods are also captured, as we said above, 43:12. Chemosh is the god of the Moabites, Num. 21:29, Judg. 11:24.

It is implied that the sacred rites of the Moabites are to be completely abolished. Compare ch. 43:10, ch. 49:3. Jerome, in Isaiah 15, thinks Chemosh is Baal-Peor, 1 Kings 11:7, 2 Kings 23:13, an idol similar to Priapus.

Latin:

Vers. 7. TV QVOQVE CAPIERIS) Nempe Ar- Moab urbs Moabitarum munitissima ἄρη βασιλείαν Ptole- mæo. Vide dictum Ezechielis locum.

IBIT CHAMOS IN TRANSMIGRATIONEM) Nam captis populis & dii capiuntur, ut diximus supra 43, 12. Chamos Deus Moabitarum Num. 21, 29. Jud. 11, 24.

Innuitur Sacra Moabitar. plane abolenda. Conf. c. 43, 10. c. 49, 3. Hieronym. in 15. Esa. putat Chamos esse Baal Pegor 1. Reg. 1, 7. 2. Reg. 23, 13. idolum Priapo simile.

## 48:8
Ver. 8. THE VALLEYS SHALL PERISH) That is, those who dwell in the valley, as the Chaldean has it here.

It is a proverb, the valleys shall perish, and the plains shall be destroyed, signifying the devastation of all parts of the region, Is. 2:14, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 8. PERIBVNT VALLES) Id est, qui habitant in valle, ut hic habet Chaldæus.

Proverbium est, peribunt valles, & dissipabun- tur campestria, significans devaftationem omnium partium regionis Es. 2, 14. 15.

## 48:9
Ver. 9. GIVE A FLOWER TO MOAB, FOR THE FLOWERING ONE SHALL GO FORTH) Give a wing to Moab, that by flying it may escape. ציא for wing is Chaldean, as can be seen in the Chaldean interpreter, Ps. 139:9. The sense is: unless it has wings, it will not be able to escape. Thus Cophen asked whether Alexander could fly.

For the Vulgate, Cornelius and Castro bring forward this explanation: Give a flower to Moab, that it may adorn its funeral with flowers, because it will soon be killed. But Moab was not to be destroyed with any pomp of its own, as the funerals of the rich are wont to be adorned, but was to be slaughtered by a sudden and unexpected sword, v. 10. And therefore that version is deservedly abandoned, even though Aquila, Symmachus, and others also have 'flower,' as if a small flower should not be begrudged to Moab. But that interpretation is convenient for the Hebrews, R. Solomon and Kimchi, the Tigurines, Isidore, Pagninus, Arias, and it is also approved by our B. Luther.

Latin:

Vers. 9. DATE FLOREM MOAB QVIA FLO- RENS EGREDIETVR) Date alam Moabo, ut volando abolet. ציא pro ala Chaldaicum est, ut videre est in Chaldæo interprete Ps. 139, 9. Sensus est: nisi alas habeat non poterit evadere. Sic Cophen interrogabat, an Alexander volare posset.

Pro vulgata Cornel. & Castro hanc explica- tionem adferunt: Date florem Moab, ut ornet funus suum floribus, quia cito interimctur. Sed Moab non erat perdendus cum pompa quadam sua, uti divitum funera ornari solent, sed subito & inspera- to gladio mactandus v. 10. Ideoque merito deseri- tur illa versio, etsi etiam Aquila, Symmachus & alii florem habeant, non invidendum Moabo exiguum florem. Commoda autem est illa Ebræis R. Salom. & Kimchio, Tigurinis, Isidoro, Pagnino, Ariæ, & B. Luthero nostro etiam probata.

## 48:10
Ver. 10. CURSED IS HE WHO DOES THE WORK OF THE LORD DECEITFULLY) That is, ἀμελῶς, as the Greeks have it here, negligently. These are the words of God exhorting the Chaldeans as those sent by Him.

This maxim is nevertheless rightly applied by Jerome, Theodoret, and Gregory the Great in Pastoral Rule, book 3, to diligence in any office.

Latin:

Vers. 10. MALEDICTUS QVI FACIT OPUS DOMI- NI FRAUDULENTER) Id est, ἀμελῶς, uti hic Græci, negligenter. Verba sunt Dei Chaldæos cohortantis, ut à se missos.

Recte tamen hæc gnome ab Hieron. Theodor. & Gregor. M. in Pastor. l. 3. ad diligentiam in quo- vis officio adhibetur.

## 48:11
Verse 11. MOAB HAS BEEN FRUITFUL FROM HIS YOUTH) In the Hebrew: He has been tranquil. The Greeks: ἀνεπαύσατο. The Chaldean: they have been wealthy. From his youth, that is, long since, namely from the times of Shalmaneser.

AND HAS RESTED IN HIS LEES AND HAS NOT BEEN POURED FROM VESSEL TO VESSEL) An excellent comparison taken from wine.

AND HAS NOT GONE INTO EXILE) The 'and' here signifies 'that is'. For these words interpret the allegory.

THEREFORE HIS TASTE HAS REMAINED IN HIM AND HIS SCENT HAS NOT BEEN CHANGED) He returns to the simile, that is, to wine. For wines that are not poured retain their native strength more constantly. So also the Moabites [retained] their pride. Isaiah 16:6.

Latin:

Vers. 11. FERTILIS FUIT MOAB AB ADOLE- SCENTIA SUA) In Hebræo: Tranquillus fuit. Græci: ἀνεπαύσατο. Chaldæus opulenti fuere. Ab Adolescentia sua, id est, jam pridem, à temporibus scilicet Salmanaffari.

ET REQVIEVIT IN FÆCIBUS NEC TRANS- FUSVS EST DE VASE IN VAS) Comparatio egre- gia à vino desumta.

ET IN TRANSMIGRATIONEM NON ABIIT) Illud & hic valet id est. Verba enim hæc allegoriam inter- pretantur.

ICCIRCO MANSIT GUSTUS EJUS IN EO ET ODOR EJUS NON EST IMMUTATUS) Redit ad simile, id est, ad vinum. Nam vina non transfusa vim nativam constantius retinent. Ita & Moabitæ suum fastum. Esaias 16, 6.

## 48:12
Verse 12. I WILL SEND TO THEM POURERS, AND THEY SHALL POUR HIM OUT, AND SHALL EMPTY HIS VESSELS, AND BREAK THEIR BOTTLES) In the Hebrew: I will send to him pourers, who shall pour him out, and empty the casks, and break the bottles. He continues the begun simile. The pourers are the Chaldeans: the casks are the cities: the broken bottles are the slain men.

Latin:

Vers. 12. MITTAM EIS ORDINATORES, ET STATORES LAGUNCULARUM, ET STERNENT EUM, ET VASA EJUS EXHAURIENT, ET LA- GUNCULAS EORUM COLLIDENT) In Hebræo: Mit- tam ei transfusores, qui eum transfundant, & dolia inaniant, & lagenas confringant. Periit in cœpta similitudine. Transfusores sunt Chaldæi: dolia urbes: Lagenæ fractæ, homines interfecti.

## 48:13
Verse 13. AND MOAB SHALL BE ASHAMED OF CHEMOSH) That is, they shall see that their confidence was empty, as follows.

AS THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL WAS ASHAMED) Because of the golden calf.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET CONFUNDETUR MOAB A CHA- MOS) Id est, videbunt inanem fuisse suam fiduciam, ut sequitur.

SICUT CONFUSA EST DOMUS ISRAEL) A vitulo aureo.

## 48:14
Verse 14. MOAB IS WASTED) He is wasted: In the Hebrew. For it is a question of the people.

AND HIS CITIES HAVE ASCENDED) They shall ascend, namely into smoke, having been set on fire. There is here in the Hebrew a construction of a singular verb with a plural noun, as is often the case with collective nouns.

In the Vulgate it is incorrectly held as 'and his cities have cut down', as Christoph à Castro acknowledges.

Latin:

Vers. 14. VASTATA EST MOAB) Vastatus est: In Hebræo. De populo enim agitur.

ET CIVITATES ILLIUS ASCENDERUNT) Ascendent, Nempe in fumum, igne incensæ. Est hic in He- bræo constructio verbi singularis cum nomine plurali ut sæpe in collectivis.

In vulgata perperam habetur & civitates illius succiderunt, ut agnoscit Christoph. à Castro.

## 48:15
AND HIS CHOSEN YOUNG MEN HAVE GONE DOWN TO THE SLAUGHTER) That is, they shall fall slain. There is an antithesis here: the cities shall ascend, the young men shall descend.

Others, the Chaldeans, ascended the Moabite cities, and against them the youths of the Moabites descended into slaughter, as Is. 5, 14. c. 38, 18. c. 42, 10. to which B. Luther's version also goes.

KING. GOD, who has the power of destroying these and other kingdoms. Dan. 4, 14. 28.

Latin:

ET ELECTI JUVENES EJUS DESCENDE- RUNT IN OCCISIONEM) Id est, cadent occisi, Est ἀντίθεσις: urbes ascendent, juvenes descendent.

Alii ascenderunt civitates Moabiticas Chaldæi, & contra descenderunt juvenes Moabitarum in inter- necionem, ut Es. 5, 14. c. 38, 18. c. 42, 10. quo B. Lutheri etiam abit versio.

REX. DEUS, qui imperium habet hæc & alia regna perdendi. Dan. 4, 14. 28.

## 48:17
Vers. 17. COMFORT HER ALL YOU WHO ARE IN HER CIRCUIT) Condole with her in the Hebrew: as also Job 2, 11. The better Greek Codices: κινήσατε αὐτῷ, that is, shake your heads on her account, which is a sign of one condoling Job 42. v. 11.

AND ALL YOU WHO KNOW HER NAME, SAY, HOW IS THE ROD OF STRENGTH BROKEN, THE GLORIOUS STAFF) The better Greek Codices have the same sense πάντες εἰδότες, not ἔκδοτοι. Nor does the Chaldean say otherwise. First the Prophet invites the neighbors to testify to the grief, then also those placed further away, to whom the fame of the Moabites had reached. He calls the people of the Moabites a staff and a rod, because they had been troublesome and terrible to other peoples, as the Chaldean explains here.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONSOLAMINI EAM OMNES QVI ESTIS IN CIRCUITU EJUS) Condolete ei in Hebræo: ut & Jobi 2, 11. Græci Codices meliores: κινήσατε αὐτῷ, id est, capita ejus causa movete, quod signum condolentis Job. 42. v. 11.

ET UNIVERSI QVI SCITIS NOMEN EJUS, DICITE, QVOMODO CONFRACTA EST VIRGA FORTITUDINIS, BACVLVS GLORIOSVS) Græci Codices meliores eodem sensu πάντες εἰδότες, non ἔκδοτοι. Nec aliter Chaldæus. Prius Propheta ad dolorem testan- dum invitat vicinos, deinde & longius positos, ad quos fama Moabitarum pervenisset. Vocat autem populum Moabi- tarum baculum & virgam, quod molestus ac terribilis fuis- set aliis populis, ut hic explicat Chaldæus.

## 48:18
Vers. 18. AND SIT IN THIRST) In arid and desert places, as above 48, 6.

Thirst is opposed to former affluence, and denotes the lack of all things.

DWELLING OF THE DAUGHTER OF DIBON) You who dwell in Dibon Isa. 15, 2. Joshua 13, 17. This is Δίβων in Ptolemy. For ב is often turned into פ.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET SEDE IN SITI) In locis aridis, & de- fertis, uti supra 48, 6.

Sitis opponitur pristinæ affluentiæ, notatque carentiam rerum omnium.

HABITATIO FILIÆ DIBON) Vos qui Dibonæ habitatis Esa. 15, 2. Josuæ. 13, 17. Hæc est Δίβων Ptolemæo. Nam ב per פ sæpe vertitur.

## 48:19
Verf. 19. STAND IN THE WAY AND LOOK OUT. HABITATION AROER) A city of the Ammonites, not far from the land of Moab. See Deut. 2, 36. c. 3, 12. Ask what has happened, and learn from that what fate awaits you also. The same sense is in the following verse.

Latin:

Verf. 19. IN VIA STA ET PROSPICE HABITA- TIO AROER) Urbs Ammonitarum, non longe a Moa- bitide. Vide Deut. 2, 36. c. 3, 12. Interroga quid accide- rit, & inde difce, quæ & te fors maneat. Idem fenfus in commate fequenti.

## 48:20
Verf. 20. MOAB IS CONFOUNDED, FOR IT IS VANQUISHED.) It has lost hope, because of such a great slaughter. For this is הוביש. These will be the words of those fleeing from the slaughter to the Ammonites. Similar to Isa. 16, 2.

Latin:

Verf. 20. CONFVSVS EST MOAB, QVIA VI- CTVS EST.) Spem perdidit, ob tantam cladem. Hoc enim eft הוביש. Hæc erunt verba fugientium è clade ad Ammonitas. Simile Efa. 16, 2.

## 48:21
Verf. 21. AND JUDGMENT IS COME UPON THE PLAIN COUNTRY UPON ELON) Divine vengeance. Helon, the Chaldean: Χαιλὼν, the Greeks. To Ptolemy Alabana, the letter l turned into β, as often. Elon and those which follow are in that plain country.

AND UPON JASA) To Ptolemy Iassa, the letter σ changed into Δ, which is frequent for those peoples.

AND UPON MEPHATH) This is a city not far from Heshbon and Dibon and Kiriathaim, Joshua 13, 18. chap. 21, 37. Mepha, a metropolis to Ptolemy.

Latin:

Verf. 21. ET JVDICIVM PERVENIT AD TER- RAM CAMPESTREM SUPER ELON) Ultio divina. Helon, Chaldæus: Χαιλὼν, Græci. Ptolemæo Αλαβάνα, l litera in β verfa, ut fæpe. Elon & quæ fequentur funt in illa terra campeftri.

ET SVPER JASA) Ptolemæo Ιάσσα litera σ muta- ta in Δ, quod frequens illis gentibus.

ET SVEPR MEPHATH) Eft hæc urbs non longe ab Esbunte & Dibone & Cariathaim Jofue 13, 18. cap. 21, 37. Μηφᾷα metropolis Ptolemæo.

## 48:22
Verf. 22. AND UPON DIBON) Above 18.

AND UPON NEBO) See above 1.

AND UPON BETH-DIBLATHAIM) House is accustomed to be taken for a city, as in this very land of Moab, Badais to Ptolemy is בית עין house of the spring. It is near Nebo, as appears Num. 33, 46. This is Dela to Ptolemy, with the ב omitted and the final addition.

Latin:

Verf. 22. ET SVPER DIBON) Supra 18.

ET SVPER NABO) Vide fupra 1.

ET SVPER DOMVM DEBLATHAIM) Domus pro urbe fumi folet, uti in hac ipfa Moabitide βαδαις Pto- lemæo eft בית עין domus fontis. Eft apud Nabuntem, ut apparet Num. 33, 46. Hæc eft Δέλα Ptolemæo, omiffo ב & additamento finali

## 48:23
Verf. 23. AND UPON KIRIATHAIM) Above 1.

AND UPON BETH-GAMUL) The city of camels, which to Ptolemy, with the letters transposed, is Makkala for Kamala. A similar name is Gaugamela גמל גוא, the village where Darius was finally defeated by Alexander.

AND UPON BETH-MEON) Which is בית מעון by excellence, Isa. 15, 20. Where see what was said by us. To Ptolemy Baelma, with the ת omitted, and the מ changed into ל, because of the neighboring sound.

Latin:

Verf. 23. ET SVPER CARIATHAIM) Supra 1.

ET SVPER BETHGAMAL) Urbem camelorum, quæ Ptolemæo transpofitis literis Μάκκαλα pro Κάμαλα. Simile nomen Gaugamela גמל גוא, vicus ubi poftremo vi- ctus eft ab Alexandro Darius.

ET SUPER BETHAMON) Quæ בית מעון per Excel- lentiam Efa. 15, 20. Ubi à nobis dicta vide. Ptolemæo Βάελμα, omiffo ת, & מ mutato ih ל, ob fonum vicinum.

## 48:24
Verf. 24. AND UPON KERIOTH) This city is named Amos 2, 2. Keriatha to Ptolemy.

AND UPON BOSRAH) Not that city of Idumea, but another of Moab, which is בצר Joshua 21:36. Βόσορ 1 Maccabees 5:36.

Latin:

Verf. 24. ET SVPER CHARIOTH) Nominatur hæc urbs Amos. 2, 2. Κεριάθα Ptolemæo.

ET SUPER BOSRA) Non illam urbem Idumææ, fed aliam Moabitidis, quæ בצר Jofue 21, 36. Βόσορ 1. Macc. 5. verf. 36.

## 48:25
Ver. 25. THE HORN OF MOAB IS CUT OFF) It shall be cut off. קרן is the name of a city, Κάρνα in Ptolemy; but at the same time, by alluding to the name, it is signified that all power, either of harming others or of defending themselves, has been taken away from them. See 1 Samuel 2:1.

AND HIS ARM IS BROKEN, SAITH THE LORD) This is also the name of a city, which is Σάβαρα in Ptolemy. But at the same time, it is an excellent allusion, as above.

Latin:

Verf. 25. ABSCISSVM EST CORNU MOAB) Ab- fcindetur. קרן nomen eft urbis, Κάρνα apud Ptolemæum; Sed fimul alludendo ad nomen fignificatur ablata illis omnis vis, aut nocendi aliis, aut fe defendendi. Vide 1. Sam. 2, 1.

ET BRACHIVM EJUS CONTRITVM EST, AIT DOMINVS) Eft & hoc nomen urbis, quæ Σάβαρα Ptolemæo. Sed fimul egregia allufio, ut fupra.

## 48:26
Ver. 26. MAKE HIM DRUNK, BECAUSE HE HATH LIFTED HIMSELF UP AGAINST THE LORD) You Chaldeans, give him a full cup of divine wrath, so that he may not know where to turn, as above 25:17.

AND MOAB SHALL DASH HIS HAND IN HIS VOMIT) So that he may both vomit and, falling, wound himself. He persists in the comparison begun.

Because of drunkenness. Psalm 107:27. Job 12:25. Isaiah 19:14.

AND HE ALSO SHALL BE IN DERISION) And thus let him be laughed at by others.

Latin:

Verf. 26. INEBRIATE EVM, QVONIAM CON- TRA DOMINVM ERECTVS EST) Vos Chaldæi ple- num ei date poculum iræ divinæ, ita ut nefciat quo fe ver- tat, ut fupra 25, 17.

ET ALLIDET MANVM MOAB IN VOMITV SVO) Ut fimul & vomat & cadens fe fauciet. Perfstat in cœpta comparatione.

Præ ebrietate. Pf. 107, 27. Job. 12, 25. Ef. 19, 14.

ET ERIT IN DERISVM ETIAM IPSE) Et fic ab aliis rideatur.

## 48:27
Ver. 27. FOR ISRAEL HATH BEEN A DERISION UNTO THEE) The people of the ten tribes when they were led into captivity, and some from the tribe of Judah. It is just that you also should be laughed at.

AS IF THOU HADST FOUND HIM AMONG THIEVES) A proverbial expression. See above 2:26 and what is said there.

THEREFORE BECAUSE OF THY WORDS WHICH THOU HAST SPOKEN AGAINST HIM THOU SHALT BE LED CAPTIVE) Because of the many words which thou hast spoken against him (the Israelite people), thou shalt be carried away. Thus the Chaldean, well according to the Hebrew.

Latin:

Verf 27. FVIT ENIM IN DERISVM TIBI ISRAEL) Populus decem tribuum cum abduceretur in captivita- tem, & quidam ex tribu Juda. Æquum eft, ut & tu ri- dearis.

QVASI INTER FVRES REPERISSET EUM) Proverbiale. Vide fupra 2, 26. & ibi dicta.

PROPTER VERBA ERGO TVA QVÆ AD- VERSVS ILLVM LOCVTVS ES CAPTIVVS DVCE- RIS) Propter multa verba quæ contra illum (populum Ifraelicum) locutus es, transmigrabis. Ita Chaldæus, bene ad Hebræum.

## 48:28
Ver. 28. LEAVE THE CITIES AND DWELL IN THE ROCK, YE INHABITANTS OF MOAB) Do not trust in cities, but betake yourselves to lonely and inaccessible places, such as rocks. The same sense as above 5.

AND BE YE LIKE THE DOVE THAT NESTETH IN THE HIGHEST MOUTH OF THE HOLE) Which, of course, for fear of those lying in wait, seeks a nest for itself in some side of a cleft rock. But the Chaldean understands it of a dove descending from its tower, so that it may hide itself in some pit. The former sense agrees better with the preceding.

Latin:

Verf. 28. RELINQVITE CIVITATES ET HABI- TATE IN PETRA HABITATORES MOAB) Ne fidite urbibus, fed in loca fola & inacceffa, quales funt rupes, vos recipite. Idem fenfus qui fupra 5.

ET ESTOTE QVASI COLVMBA NIDIFICANS IN SUMMO ORE FORAMINIS) Quæ fcilicet præ metu infidiantium nidum fibi quærit in aliquo latere fcif- fæ rupis. At Chaldæus intelligit de columba de turre fua defcendente, ut fe in fovea aliqua occulter. Prior fenfus magis congruit antecedentibus.

## 48:29
Verf. 29. WE HAVE HEARD THE PRIDE OF MOAB, HE IS EXCEEDING PROUD) He repeats the words which Isaiah had spoken at a similar time.

HIS SUBLIMITY AND HIS ARROGANCE AND HIS PRIDE AND THE HAUGHTINESS OF HIS HEART) He adds something to the words of Isaiah, to show that the Moabites were not only not corrected, but had even progressed for the worse. He does the same in what follows, so that he may show both the guilt and the punishment to be greater.

Latin:

Verf. 29. AVDIVIMVS SVPERBIAM MOAB, SV- PERBVS EST VALDE) Repetit verba quæ Efaias in fi- mili tempore dixerat.

SVBLIMITATEM EJVS ET ARROGANTIAM ET SVPERBIAM ET ALTITVDINEM CORDIS EJVS) Aliquid addit ad verba Efaiæ, ut oftendat non modo non correctos, fed etiam in pejus profeciffe Moabitas. Sic etiam facit in fequentibus, ut & culpam & pœnam often- dat majorem.

## 48:30
HIS [PRIDE]; AND THAT HIS MIGHT IS NOT ACCORDING TO IT, NOR HAS HE ENDEAVORED TO DO ACCORDING TO WHAT HE COULD) That is, he wanted more than he could do. The sense is the same as in Isaiah 16:6. But augmented. For בדיו this interpreter reads here, after the Greeks, בידיו, which was in his hand: what he could do. In the Chaldean, בדיו are their princes.

Latin:

TIAM EJUS; ET QVOD NON SIT. JVXTA EAM VIRTVS EJVS, NEC JVXTA QVOD POTERAT CONATA SIT FACERE) Id est, plus voluit quam po- tuit. Sensus idem qui apud Esaiam 16, 1. Sed auctus. Pro בדיו legit hic interpres post Græcos בידיו quod in manu ejus erat: quod poterat. Chaldæo בדיו sunt principes eorum.

## 48:31
Vers. 31.

THEREFORE I WILL HOWL OVER MOAB AND I WILL CRY OUT TO ALL MOAB) The same sense as in Isaiah 16:11. He says that he himself, though owing nothing to the Moabites, is nevertheless somewhat moved by such great calamities of theirs.

TO THE MEN OF THE WALL OF BAKED CLAY LAMENTING) Because of the laments of those who dwelt in Kir-hareseth, or Kir-hareseth, which the Latin translates as a wall of baked clay, when it is rather the city of the sun. See also 16:7 & 11, and what we said there. The Greeks here retained the Hebrew word κειρ ἀρεσέθ; wherefore in 16:6 restore the mutilated word κειρ ἀρεσέθ, and in 11, for ἐνεκαίνισας write κειρ ἀράς.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

IDEO SVPER MOAB EJVLABO ET AD MO- AB VNIVERSAM CLAMABO) Idem sensus qui Esaiæ 16, 11. Dicit se quoque ipsum nihil Moabitis debentem, tamen tantis ipsorum calamitatibus nonnihil commoveri.

AD VIROS MVRI FICTILIS LAMENTAN- TES) Ob lamenta eorum qui habitarunt in Kirchareseh vel Kirchareseh quod murum fictilem transfert Latinus, cum potius sit urbs solis. Vide etiam 16, 7. & 11. & ibi à no- bis dicta. Græci hic retinuerunt Hebræam vocem κειρ ἀρεσέθ, quare 16, 6. vocem mutilatam repone κειρ ἀρεσέθ, & 11. pro ἐνεκαίνισας scribe κειρ ἀράς.

## 48:32
Vers. 32.

WITH THE WEEPING OF JAZER I WILL WEEP FOR THEE, O VINE OF SIBMAH) Jazer, Iazea in Ptolemy, with the z changed to ts, which is frequent among the Chaldeans: not far from Heshbon, Joshua 21:39. Hence not far is Sibmah, Saba in Ptolemy, an excellent vineyard. These are joined together also in Isaiah 16, verse 9. From which this passage is taken with an augmentation, as we have said.

THY BRANCHES HAVE PASSED OVER THE SEA) And this is from Isaiah 16:8. Alluding to the vine, by branches or plants he understands the inhabitants, some of whom were sent across the sea, to Cyprus for instance, which island obeyed first the Assyrians, then the Babylonians, and lastly the Persians. See our notes to the third book of the Truth of the Christian Religion.

THEY HAVE REACHED EVEN TO THE SEA OF JAZER) [They have reached] for the men of Jazer, as we have often noted elsewhere.

UPON THY HARVEST, AND UPON THY VINTAGE THE SPOILER IS FALLEN) Nebuzaradan.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

DE PLANCTV JAZOR PLORABO TIBI VI- NEA SABAMA) Jazor Ἰάζεα Ptolemæo, ז in ץ verso quod Chaldæis frequens est: non longe ab Esbunte Josue 21, 39. Hinc non longe Sabama, Σαβὰ Ptolemæo, vinetum opti- mum. Junguntur hæc simul & apud Esaiam 16. vers. 9. De quo hic locus cum augmento depromtus est, ut dixi- mus.

PROPAGINES TVÆ TRANSIERVNT MARE) Et hoc ex Esa. 16, 8. Alludens ad vineam, per propagi- nes, sive plantas habitatores intelligit, quorum quidam trans mare, Cyprum puta missi, quæ Insula primum Assy- riis, deinde Babyloniis ac postremum Persis paruit. Vi- de nostra ad tertium librum de Veritate Religionis Chri- stianæ.

VSQVE AD MARE JAZER PERVENERVNT) Ελεείς pro homines Iazer, qualem & alibi sæpe nota- vimus.

SVPER MESSEM TVAM, ET SVPER VIN- DEMIAM TVAM PRÆDO IRRVIT) Nabuzardan.

## 48:33
Vers. 33.

CONCERNING CARMEL) Concerning cultivated places. For commonly here and elsewhere it is often taken not in its proper sense.

AND I HAVE TAKEN AWAY WINE FROM THE WINEPRESSES) God continues to speak as above in 30. The rest is interjected by the Prophet as if by a parenthesis.

BY NO MEANS SHALL THE TREADER OF THE WINEPRESS SING THE USUAL SONG) And this is from Isaiah 16, 10. See also above 25, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

DE CARMELO) De locis cultis. Communiter enim hic & alibi sæpe, non proprie sumitur.

ET VINVM DE TORCVLARIBVS SVSTVLI) Deus pergit loqui ut supra 30. Cætera à Propheta velut per παρίνθεσιν interjecta.

NEQVAQVAM CALCATOR VVÆ SOLI- TVM CELEVSMA CANTABIT) Et hoc ex Esaia 16, 10. Vide & supra 25, 30.

## 48:34
Ver. 34.

CONCERNING THE CRY FROM HESBON EVEN TO ELEALE AND JAZER) Supply, the sound reaches, as is understood from what follows, that is, from one end to the other. A similar expression is in Isaiah 15, 4. We have already had Heshbon above in 2, and Jazer in 21. We have Eleale also in Isaiah 15, 4 and chapter 16, 9. It seems that אל is the Arabic article, and the name is עלע, Ὑελα in Ptolemy.

FROM ZOAR EVEN TO HORONAIM) We have Zoar also in Isaiah 15, verse 5. It is the very town to which Lot had retreated when Sodom was perishing. Horonaim is above in the same place, and above in 3.

A HEIFER OF THREE YEARS OLD) As a three-year-old heifer. And this is from Isaiah 15, verse 5. In a like matter, like words.

THE WATERS ALSO OF NIMRIM SHALL BE MOST EVIL) They shall be desolate. By waters, understand the pastures situated nearby, as we said regarding the passage in Isaiah 15, verse 6, which is related to this one.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

DE CLAMORE ESEBON VSQVE ELEALE ET JAZE) Supple, pervenit sonus, ut ex sequentibus in- telligitur, id est, à fine uno ad alterum. Similis locutio Esaiæ 15, 4. Esbunta habuimus jam supra 2. & Jasa 21. Elea- le habemus & Esaiæ 15, 4. cap. 16, 9. Videtur אל esse ar- ticulus Arabicus, nomen autem עלע Ὑελα Ptolemæo.

A; SEGOR VSQVE ADORONAIM) Segor ha- bemus & Esaiæ 15. vers. 5. Est id ipsum oppidum quo Loth se receperat, pereuntibus Sodomis. Oronaim supra ibi dem, & supra 3.

VITVLA CONTERNANTE) Tanquam vitu- la trime. Et hoc ex Esaia 15. vers. 5. In re pari paria verba.

AQVÆ QVOQVE NEMRIM PESSIMÆ E- RVNT) Deserta erunt. Per aquas pascua adsita intel- lige, ut diximus ad huic consanguineum Esaiæ locum 15. vers. 6.

## 48:35
Ver. 35.

AND I WILL TAKE AWAY FROM MOAB, SAITH THE LORD, HIM THAT OFFERETH IN THE HIGH PLACES) Because otherwise I could not take away, or thus I will take away. Understand that 'him that offereth' as one offering a whole burnt offering. The Hebrew word demands that. See 2 Kings 3, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

ET AVFERAM DE MOAB, AIT DOMI- NVS, OFFERENTEM IN EXCELSIS) Quia aliter, auferre non potui, vel sic auferam. Offerentem illud, intellige ὁλοκαυτῶντα. Id poscit vox Hebræa. Vide 2. Reg. 3. 27.

## 48:36
Ver. 36.

MY HEART SHALL SOUND FOR MOAB LIKE PIPES) As the heart, that is, the innermost part, resounds with the sound of a pipe, so my heart (says the Prophet) is moved when I imagine such great evils. See above 31.

TO THE MEN OF THE EARTHEN WALL) To the men of Kircher. Above 31.

BECAUSE HE DID MORE THAN HE COULD, THEREFORE THEY PERISHED) Better: for even those who will have been left, will perish. For יתרתו in this sense is taken also in Isaiah 15, 7. Those who will not have been killed by the enemy, will perish by famine and diseases.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

COR MEVM AD MOAB QVASI TIBIÆ RE- SONABIT) Ut cor, id est, intimum tibiæ perstrepit sono, ita cor meum (ait Propheta) commovetur cum tanta mala imaginor. Vide supra 31.

AD VIROS MURI FICTILIS) Ad viros Kirche- res. Supra 31.

QVIA PLVS FECIT QVAM POTVIT, IC- CIRCO PERIERUNT) Melius: nam & qui reliqui erunt facti, peribunt. Nam יתרתו hoc sensu sumitur etiam apud Esaiam 15, 7. Qui occisi ab hoste non fuerint, fame ac mor- bis peribunt.

## 48:37
Ver. 37.

FOR EVERY HEAD SHALL BE BALD) That is, he shall be plucked of hair after the manner of the nation, as above 47, 5. Cicero, Tusculan Disputations 3: 'It is most foolish in grief to pluck out one's hair, as if sorrow were lightened by baldness.' There is also this passage from Isaiah 15, 2: 'AND EVERY BEARD SHALL BE SHAVED.' See what has been said on that same passage of Isaiah. 'IN ALL HANDS A BINDING': In the Hebrew: a cutting. Take hands for arms, as above 38, 12. But refer it to the custom, concerning which see above 47, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

OMNE ENIM CAPVT CALVITIVM) Id est, depilabitur more gentis, ut supra 47, 5. Cicero Tusculana- rum 3. Stultissimum in luctu capillum sibi evellere, quasi calvi- tio mæror levaretur. Est & hic locus ex Esaia 15, 2. ET OMNIS BARBA RASA ERIT) Vide quæ dicta ad eundem Esaiæ locum. IN CUNCTIS MANIBUS COLLIGATIO) In Hebræo: incisio. Manus sume pro brachiis, ut supra 38, 12. refer autem ad morem, de quo supra 47, 5.

## 48:38
Verse 38.

AS A USELESS VESSEL: A displeasing vessel: that is, refuse, as above 22, 28. HOW IS IT OVERTHROWN: How is it dismayed, namely the city of Kir-heres, of which the discourse preceded. AND THEY HAVE HOWLED: So that they howled, namely its citizens.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

SICUT VAS INUTILE) Vas displicens: id est, quis- quiliæ, ut supra 22, 28. QUOMODO VICTA EST) Quomodo conster- nata est, nempe civitas Kir-cheresch, de qua sermo præ- cessit. ET ULULAVERUNT) Ita ut ulularent, nempe cives ejus.

## 48:39
Verse 39.

HOW HATH HE CAST DOWN THE NECK OF MOAB: He turned his neck. That is, he turned his back, as is the custom of those who dare not show their face. AND FOR AN EXAMPLE TO ALL ROUND ABOUT HIM: It has become a terror to all who fear similar things for themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

QUOMODO DEJECIT CERVICEM MOAB) Vertit cervicem. Id est, tergum obvertit, ut solent qui fa- ciem ostendere non audent. ET IN EXEMPLUM OMNIBUS IN CIRCUI- TU SVO) Terrori facta est, omnibus paria sibi metuen- tibus.

## 48:40
Verse 40.

BEHOLD AS AN EAGLE HE SHALL FLY: Nebuzaradan. AND SHALL EXTEND HIS WINGS TO MOAB: As an eagle flies upon small birds. There is, however, a play on the word. For wings are also called military outposts.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

ECCE QVASI AQVILA VOLABIT) Nabu- zardan. ET EXTENDET ALAS SVAS AD MOAB) Ut aquila in minutas aves involat. Est autem lusus in voce. Nam alæ dicuntur etiam militares prætenturæ.

## 48:41
Verse 41.

KIRIOTH IS TAKEN: Kirioth shall be taken suddenly, concerning which see above 23. AS THE HEART OF A WOMAN IN TRAVAIL: Having a difficult birth: δυςτοκέσης.

Latin:

Vers. 41.

CAPTA EST CARIOTH) Capietur subito Ca- rioth, de qua supra 23. SICVT COR MVLIERIS PARTVRIENTIS) Gravem habentis partum: δυςτοκέσης.

## 48:42
Verse 42.

AND MOAB SHALL CEASE TO BE A PEOPLE: By slaughter and dispersion, in the way that cities perish. See what we have said in Book 2 of the Law of War and Peace 9, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 42.

ET CESSABIT MOAB ESSE POPVLVS) Oc- cidione & dispersione, quomodo civitates intereunt. Vide quæ diximus lib. 2. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 9, 3. 4. 5. 6.

## 48:43
Verse 43. FEAR, AND THE PIT, AND THE SNARE: From Isaiah 24, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 43. PAVOR, ET FOVEA ET LAQVEVS) Ex Esaia 24, 17.

## 48:45
Ver. 45.

IN THE SHADOW OF HESEBON THEY STOOD FLEEING FROM THE SNARE) Better: In the shadow of Hesebon they stood: therefore from the fire they flee. They trusted that enemies could be stopped near Esbus, but falsely. FOR FIRE HAS GONE FORTH FROM HESEBON AND A FLAME FROM THE MIDST OF SEHON) The sense is, an old proverb is confirmed by a new event, which is Num. 21:28. Namely, with the enemy poured out from there upon the rest of the Moabites to their destruction. Sehon was the old king of that region, as we learn from the book of Numbers and elsewhere: but here Sehon is said for the city of Sehon, which is Esbus itself, or Hesebon. AND IT SHALL DEVOUR PART OF MOAB) The corner of Moab, in Hebrew: that is, the Moabite territory at the corner, that is, the final end. But the Chaldean reads פאת and explains it as princes: just as the same name is explained concerning the same Moabites, both by others and by the Latin interpreter, Num. 24:17. AND THE CROWN OF THE SONS OF TUMULT) Of the crowds: that is, the most noble of the people, as the Chaldean understood it here.

Latin:

Vers. 45.

IN VMBRA HESEBON STETERVNT DE LAQVEO FVGIENTES) Melius: In umbra Hesebon ste- terunt: ideo à Si fugient. Confisi sunt apud Esbuntem sisti hostes posse, sed falso. QVIA IGNIS EGRESSVS EST DE HESEBON ET FLAMMA DE MEDIO SEHON) Sensum est, novo even- tu comprobatum vetus proverbium, quod est Num. 21, 28. Hoste scilicet inde effuso in cæteros Moabitas ad eorum perniciem. Sehon vetus rex fuit tractus ejus, ut ex libro Nu- merorum, & alibi discimus: Sehon autem hic dicitur pro urbe Sehonis, quæ est ipsa Esbus, sive Hesebon. ET DEVORABIT PARTEM MOAB) Angulum Moab, in Hebræo: id est, Moabitidem ad angulum, id est, fi- nem ultimum. At Chaldæus legit פאת & explicat princi- pes: quomodo idem nomen & de iisdem Moabitis explica- tur tum ab aliis, tum à Latino interprete, Num. 24, 17. ET VERTICEM FILIORVM TVMVLTVS) Tur- bæ: id est, nobilissimos populi, ut hic accepit Chaldæus.

## 48:46
Ver. 46.

WOE TO THEE MOAB, THOU HAST PERISHED O PEOPLE OF CHAMOS) And this is from Num. 22:28.

Latin:

Vers. 46.

VÆ TIBI MOAB, PERIISTI POPVLE CHA- MOS) Et hoc ex Num. 22, 28.

## 48:47
Ver. 47. AND I WILL TURN BACK) Nevertheless I will cause to return. THE CAPTIVITY OF MOAB) That is, the captives. IN THE LATTER DAYS) That is, at length. That the Moabites were restored to their homeland is testified by the rich witness Josephus 13, 17, 21, and elsewhere. THUS FAR THE JUDGMENTS OF MOAB) That is, until that time the vengeance of God upon the Moabites will endure. Thus the Chaldean is good here. Junius and Tremellius, and the Belgian Paraphrasts, as well as Osiander from among our own, explain this concerning conversion to Christ: For the Prophet saw that even some from the Moabites would arrive at the knowledge of Christ. Therefore he says: And I will turn back the captivity of Moab in the latter days, says the Lord: i.e., I will gather some from the posterity of the Moabites into the Church of Christ, so that, freed from sin, they may become partakers of eternal salvation through faith in Christ. For God gathers a Church for Himself from various (even the most impious) peoples through the preaching of the Gospel. The Vinarians and B. Hülsemann follow Osiander, nor does B. Hagius deny it. When, he says, this may have happened, we do not know. But it seems to have happened after the return of the Jews, under the Kings of the Persians. If anyone wishes this to be understood concerning the spiritual reduction to Christ, I will allow it, and it is very true, that afterwards they returned to God through the Gospel, and the Moabites did not raise themselves up against God any further, but humbled themselves under the mighty hand of God, so that they might be exalted in the most holy day of visitation.

Latin:

Vers. 47. ET CONVERTAM) Attamen reverti faciam. CAPTIVITATEM MOAB) Id est, captivos. IN NOVISSIMIS DIEBVS) Id est, tandem. Moa- bitas restitutos in patriam testis est locuples Josephus 13, 17. 21. & alibi. HVC VSQVE JVDICIA MOAB) Id est, ad id usque tempus durabit vindicta Dei in Moabitas. Ita hic Chaldæus bene. De conversione ad Christum explicant Jun. & Tre- mellius, ac Paraphrastæ Belgici, nec non è nostris Osiander: Videbat autem Propheta, etiam ex Moa- bitis aliquos perventuros ad agnitionem Christi. Ita- que ait: Et convertam captivitatem Moab in novis- simis diebus, ait Dominus: i. e. Ex posteritate Moabitarum aliquos colligam in Ecclesiam Christi, ut à peccato liberati, æternæ salutis per fidem in Chri- stum fiant participes. Deus enim ex variis (etiam impiissimis) populis, per Evangelii prædicatio- nem, sibi Ecclesiam colligit. Osiandrum sequun- tur Vinarienses & B. Hülsemannus, neque abnuit B適切hagius. Quando, inquit, hoc factum sit, igno- ramus. Videtur autem factum post reversionem Ju- dæorum, sub Regibus Persarum.
