Si quis hoc voluerit intellectum de reductione spirituali ad Christum, per me licebit, & valde verum est, quod postea per Ev- angelium redierunt ad Deum, & amplius Moabitæ non se erexerunt contra Deum, sed humiliaverunt se ipsos sub potenti manu Dei, ut exaltarentur in die sanctissima visitationis.

## 49:1 Argument
CHAPTER XLIX. Prophecy against the Ammonites, Idumeans, Damascus and the Syrians, Kedar or the Ishmaelites, the Elamites or Persians. Yet the captivity of Ammon and Elam is to be resolved at last.

Ver. 1. TO THE SONS OF AMMON) Those who divided these into chapters gathered into this one chapter five different prophecies, the first of which pertains to the Ammonites, the second to the Idumeans, the third to the Syrians around Damascus, the fourth to the Kedarite Arabs and their neighbors, the fifth to the Elymeans. The event of this prophecy preceded by a little the event of the one we had against the Moabites. That appears also here below in 3. And Ezek. 21:33. Where the slaughter of the Ammonites is connected to the removal of Zedekiah.

HATH ISRAEL NO SONS, OR HATH HE NO HEIR? WHY THEN HATH MELCHAM POSSESSED GAD BY INHERITANCE, AND HIS PEOPLE DWELT IN HIS CITIES) Melcham the God of the Ammonites, the same who is Moloch 2 Kings 23:13. Possessed by inheritance, that is, possessed as if by his own perpetual right. Things become ownerless (ἀδέσποτα) of the occupier. But the goods of those who either have children, or relatives who by law ought to succeed, are not ownerless. Therefore the Ammonites had occupied the land distributed to Israel, such as the region of the Gadites, through injury. The Ammonites had done this, having entered into a pact with Tiglath-Pileser, when he had devastated those parts in war 2 Kings 15:29. For they were neighbors to the strong Gadites, Joshua 13:24, 25. But it was just that those deserted parts should accrue to the Jews who had the same parent, Jacob, with the Gadites. Hence the war between the Jews and the Ammonites mentioned 2 Kings 24:2. We learn from this, although it is commonly said that he who captures certain lands in war becomes their Lord by the law of nations, that if the war is unjust, it does not absolve the captor himself, nor others having a cause from him, before God. See what we have said about this matter in book 3 of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 10. Zephaniah 2:8 touches upon this same invasion.

Latin:

CAPUT XLIX. Prophetia contra Ammonitas, Idumæos, Da- mascum & Syros, Kedar vel Ismaëlitas, Ela- mitas vel Persas. Solvenda tamen tan- dem captivitas Ammon & Elam.

Vers. 1. AD FILIOS AMMON) Qui hæc in capita distri- buerunt, in unum hoc caput compegerunt quinque vatici- nia diversa, quorum primum pertinet ad Ammonitas, alte- rum ad Idumæos, tertium ad Syros circa Damascum, quar- tum ad Cedarenos Arabas, eorumque vicinos, quintum ad Elymæos. Eventus hujus prophetiæ paululum præcessit eventum ejus, quem habuimus contra Moabitas. Apparet id & hic infra 3. Et Ezech. 21, 33. Ubi evectioni Sede- ciæ subnectitur clades Ammonitarum.

NUMQUID NON FILII SUNT ISRAEL, AUT HERES NON EST EI? CUR IGITUR HEREDITA- TE POSSEDIT MELCHAM GAD, ET POPULUS IN URBIBUS EJUS HABITAVIT) Melcham Deus Ammo- nitarum, idem qui Moloch 2. Reg. 23, 13. Hereditate pos- sedit, id est, velut proprio perpetuoque jure possedit. Adé- σποτα fiunt occupantis. Bona autem eorum, qui aut libe- ros habent, aut propinquos qui ex lege debeant succedere, non sunt ἀδέσποτα. Ergo per injuriam Ammonitæ sola Israeli distributa, ut Gaditarum regionem, occupaverant. Fecerant autem hoc Ammonitæ, pactione inita cum The- glathphalasaro, cum ille eas partes bello vastasset 2. Reg. 15, 29. Erant enim contermini Gaditarum forti, Josue 13, 24. 25. Æquum autem erat illas partes desertas, Judæis qui cum Gaditis eundem parentem Jacobum habuerant, accre- scere. Hinc bellum inter Judæos & Ammonitas memora- tum 2. Reg. 24, 2. Discimus hinc, quanquam vulgo dici- tur, qui bello terras aliquas cepit, earum Dominus fieri jure gentium, id tamen si bellum sit injustum, neque ipsum ca- pientem, neque alios causam ab eo habentes apud Deum absolvere. Vide quæ de hac re diximus libro 3. de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 10. Tangit eandem hanc invasionem Sophonias 2, 8.

## 49:2
UPON RABBATH OF THE SONS OF AMMON) This city was the chief of the Ammonite cities, Joshua 13:25, 2 Sam. 11:1. In Polybius it is Ῥαβαθαματὰ. It was called Philadelphia afterwards. Ezekiel 25:5 also predicted the destruction of this city.

HER DAUGHTERS SHALL BE SET ON FIRE) The smaller cities, as also below in 3. The Greeks read בְמוֹת instead of בנות.

AND ISRAEL SHALL POSSESS HIS POSSESSORS) Better: And Israel shall destroy his destroyers: that is, he shall be the cause why they perish. ירש is translated in many places by ἐξολοθρεύειν, ἀπολλύναι, ἐξαναλίσκειν, ἐξαίρειν. See a similar sense in Obadiah 18.

Latin:

SUPER RABBATH FILIORUM AMMON) Erat hæc urbs princeps urbium Ammoniticarum Josue 13, 25. 2. Sam. 11, 1. Polybio Ῥαβαθαματὰ. Philadelphia dicta est postea. Excidium hujus urbis prædixit & Ezechiel 25, 5.

FILIÆ EJUS IGNI SUCCENDENTUR) Urbes minores, ut & infra 3. Græci pro בנות legerunt בְמוֹת.

ET POSSIDEBIT ISRAEL POSSESSORES SUOS) Melius: Et perdet Israel perditores suos: id est, in causa erit cur pereant. ירש pluribus in locis vertitur per ἐξολο- θρεύειν, ἀπολλύναι, ἐξαναλίσκειν, ἐξαίρειν. Vide similem sensum Abdiæ 18.

## 49:3
Ver. 3. HOWL O HESHBON FOR HAI IS WASTED) This Hai is not that one mentioned in the book of Joshua chapter 8, but another, Γαῖα in Ptolemy: for ע is accustomed to be translated by γ; as עמרה Gomorrah. This city being destroyed, Heshbon, which was not far off, had reason to fear for itself. And soon evil reached this one also, as we learned from the preceding chapter.

LAMENT AND GO ABOUT BY THE HEDGES) The Chaldean: Cut yourselves in crowds. שוט is a whip. גדר is a fenced place, such as are village-towns.

MELCHOM SHALL BE CARRIED INTO CAPTIVITY) Similar above 48, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ULULA HESEBON QUONIAM VASTATA EST HAI) Hæc Hai non est illa in Josuæ libro cap. 8. me- morata, sed altera Γαῖα Ptolemæo: nam ע per γ verti solet; ut עמרה Γομόῤῥα. Hac urbe excisa Esbus quæ non longe erat, habebat quod sibi timeret. Et mox ad hanc quoque pervenit malum, ut ex capite præcedenti didicimus.

PLANGITE ET CIRCUITE PER SEPES) Chal- dæus: Incidite vos in turbis. שוט est flagellum. גדר locus sæptus, quales sunt κωμοπόλεις.

MELCHOM IN TRANSMIGRATIONEM DU- CETUR) Simile supra 48, 7.

## 49:4
WHY GLORY THOU IN THE VALLEYS) Very fruitful ones.

Ver. 4. THY VALLEY HATH FLOWED DOWN) It shall flow. Thy valleys shall flow with blood.

DELICATE DAUGHTER) Stubborn, rash: θυγάτηρ τῆς ἰταμίας in the Greeks, in the Chaldean foolish.

Latin:

QUID GLORIARIS IN VALLIBUS) Frugiferis admodum.

Vers. 4. DEFLUXIT VALLIS TUA) Fluet. Valles tuæ sanguine fluent.

FILIA DELICATA) Pervicax, temeraria : θυγά- τηρ τῆς ἰταμίας Græcis Chaldæo insipiens.

## 49:5
Ver. 5. BEHOLD I WILL BRING UPON THEE A TERROR SAITH THE LORD OF HOSTS, FROM ALL THAT ARE ROUND ABOUT THEE) In the Hebrew: from all thy surroundings: that is, from every side.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ECCE EGO INDUCAM SUPER TE TER- ROREM AIT DOMINUS EXERCITUUM, AB OMNI- BUS QUI SUNT IN CIRCUITU TUO) In Hebræo: ab omnibus circuitibus tuis: id est, undique.

## 49:6
Ver. 6. AND AFTER THESE THINGS I WILL CAUSE THE CAPTIVES OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON TO RETURN.) That this also happened is clear from Josephus 12, 12, and elsewhere.

THUS also Lyranus, Dionysius, and Castro explain it with Theodoret: But because Ezech. 25, 11. to tal abolition of the name of the Ammonites is intimated; it is more probable, in the judgment of our B. Hülfemann, that this treats of the reduction to Christ that was to happen in the time of the Apostles, which Jerome, Rabanus, Hugo, Isidore, Saa, Luther, Tremellius, and others have understood. Similarly Osiander: The Prophet, however, subjoins a consolation: And after these things I will make the fugitives return, and I will bring back the captives of the children of Ammon; saith the Lord (i.e., The Gospel of Christ shall be preached even to the posterity of the Ammonites: to which those who shall apply faith will be delivered from the tyranny of Satan:) and they shall be led into the heavenly fatherland. The Weimar Paraphrasts agree, as do the Belgian ones. Bugenhagius has it thus: Since we do not have certain history concerning this, take it in the same way as we said in the previous chapter concerning the return of the Moabites: For thus God casts away all Nations, and the Jews, so that He nevertheless promises that He will receive them, but only through Christ, which is what we said in chapter 31. & others.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET POST HÆC REVERTI FACIAM CA- PTIVOS FILIORUM AMMON.) Hoc quoque factum patet ex Josepho 12, 12. & alibi.

SIc etiam exponunt cum Theodoreto Lyranus, Dionysius & Castro: Sed quia Ezech. 25, 11. to- talis abolitio nominis Ammonitarum intimatur, probabilius est, judice B. Hülfemanno nostro, agi hic de reductione ad Christum tempore Apostolorum futura, quod Hieronymus, Rabanus, Hugo, Isidorus, Saa, Lutherus, Tremellius & alii intellexerunt. Si- militer Osiander: Subjungit autem Propheta con- solationem: Et post haec reverti faciam fugientes, & reducam captivos filiorum Ammon; ait Do- minus (i. e. Praedicabitur Evangelion Christi etiam Ammonitarum posteritati: cui qui fidem adhibue- rint, liberabuntur a tyrannide Satanae:) & in patriam coelestem ducentur. Consonant Paraphrastae Vi- narienses, ut & Belgici. Bugenhagius ita habet: Quando de hoc non habemus certam historiam, acci- pe ita, quemadmodum fuperiori capite de reversione Moabitarum diximus: Sic enim abjicit Deus omnes Gentes, & Judaeos, ut tamen promittat, se eos recepturum, sed per solum Christum, id quod dixi- mus capite 31. & alias.

## 49:7
Ver. 7.

TO IDUMAEA) This prophecy also was completed in the same times as the former ones. See Ezek. 25, 12. and below 12. Many things here are taken from Obadiah, who had predicted the same things concerning the times of Sennacherib. IS THERE NO LONGER WISDOM IN THEMAN?) A city of Idumaea, whence the Themanaei [come], according to Herodotus, as we said at Gen. 36, 15. All Arabs were long ago celebrated for wisdom, as we noted at Matt. 11, 1, especially those sprung from Esau, as appears from the history of Job, and among these very ones the Themanaei were eminent in this praise. Obadiah 8. HAS COUNSEL PERISHED FROM THE CHILDREN) Namely, of wisdom, as Matt. 11, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

AD IDUMÆAM) Haec quoque Prophetia iisdem temporibus completa est quibus priores. Vide Ezech. 25, 12. & infra 12. Multa hic sumta ex Abdia, qui eadem de temporibus Sennacheribi praedixerat. NUMQVID NON ULTRA EST SAPIENTIA IN THEMAN?) Urbe Idumaeae, unde Themanaei Hero- doto, ut diximus ad Gen. 36, 15. Omnes Arabes jam olim sapientia celebres, ut notavimus ad Matth. 11, 1. praeser- tim illi ab Esavo orti, ut ex Jobi historia apparet, & inter hos ipsos eminebant hac laude Themanaei. Abdias 8. PERIIT CONSILIUM A FILIIS) Nempe sapien- tiae, ut Matth. 11, 19.

## 49:8
Ver. 8. DESCEND INTO THE PIT) Into the caves. INHABITANTS OF DEDAN) See Gen. 25, 3. Ezech. 26. ver. 13. These are from the descendants of Keturah, but subdued by the Idumaeans.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DESCENDITE IN VORAGINEM) In specus. HABITATORES DEDAN) Vide Gen. 25, 3. Ezech. 26. vers. 13. Hi sunt ex Cethurae postetis, sed sub- acti ab Idumaeis.

## 49:9
Ver. 9.

IF GRAPE-GATHERERS HAD COME UPON THEE, WOULD THEY NOT HAVE LEFT A CLUSTER) Would they not have left something to glean? The [word] thieves demands this sense. But the Chaldeans will take away everything, even to the dust. These things are taken from Obadiah 5.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SI VINDEMIATORES VENISSENT SUPER TE, NON RELIQVISSENT RACEMUM) Nonne reliquissent aliquid ad racemandum? Hunc sensum exigit fures. At Chaldaei omnia auferent cum pulvisculo. Sumta haec ex Abdia 5.

## 49:10
Ver. 10.

I HAVE REVEALED HIS HIDDEN THINGS) I have brought it about that there was nothing so hidden that the victor would not find it.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

REVELAVI ABSCONDITA EJUS) Effeci ut ni- hil esset tam abditum quod non inveniret victor.

## 49:11
Ver. 11.

LEAVE THY FATHERLESS CHILDREN: I WILL MAKE THEM LIVE, AND THY WIDOWS SHALL HOPE IN ME.) That is, if you leave the fatherless and widows, I will care for them. He says this because neither the fatherless nor the widows were going to survive: which sense the LXX indicate here. Bugenhagius translates it thus: What however shall have remained of thy fatherless children, I will make to live, and thy widows shall hope in Me; And he wishes not only to look to the widows and fatherless of that time, but he understands these things especially concerning the remnants of the Idumaeans to be converted in the time of the New Testament. Having left, he says on page 428, after the slaughter and captivity, I will have mercy on the fatherless and widows in thy land. Provided they shall call upon Me, and shall hope in Me, which could happen there, with the god Malchom confounded: where there were still remnants of holy doctrine from the Fathers, they were offspring from Jacob. For God is not the God of the Jews only, Rom. 3, etc. For in tribulation one sighs to God, whom we do not acknowledge outside of temptation. And God boasts in Scripture that He is the Father of the fatherless and the defender of widows. And Christ says of the Gospel: The poor have the Gospel preached to them. But we must especially understand this concerning the remnants of the Idumaeans to be converted to Christ, to whom none are converted except sinners and the desperate, who are called here the fatherless and widows. Of whom Christ Himself says: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. Similarly Osiander: Although He is truly the Lord, the father of orphans and widows: yet the Prophet looks further in this place. And he hints that it will be that even from the Idumaeans, when properly humbled, some will be converted to Christ: these he understands by the name of fatherless and widows. Maldonatus accepts these in the sense not of a promise, but of a threat, because God would not be saying, 'leave some orphans to me,' but B. Hülsemann refutes this in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

RELINQVE PUPILLOS TUOS: EGO FACIAM EOS VIVERE, ET VIDUÆ TUÆ IN ME SPERA- BUNT.) Id est, si relinquas pupillos & viduas, ego eos curabo. Hoc ideo dicit, quia nec pupilli, nec viduae superfuturae erant: quem sensum hic indicant LXX. Bugenhagius ita vertit: Quod tamen reliquum fuerit de pupillis tuis, ego faciam vivere, & viduae tuae in me sperabunt; Nec solum illius temporis viduas & pupillos respici vult, sed maxime haec de reli- quiis Idumaeorum convertendis tempore Novi Te- stamenti intelligit. Relictis, inquit pag. 428. post cladem & captivitatem pupillis & viduis in terra tua miserebor. Siquidem invocabunt Me, & in Me spe- rabunt, id quod illic fieri potuit, confuso Deo Mal- chom: ubi adhuc erant sanctae doctrinae reliquiae ex Patribus, progenies erant ex Jacob. Non enim Deus solorum Judaeorum Deus est Rom. 3. &c. Nam in tribulatione ad Deum suspiratur, quem extra tenta- tionem non agnoscimus. Et Deus in Scriptura glo- riatur, se esse Patrem pupillorum, & defensorem vi- duarum. Et Christus de Evangelio dicit: Paupe- res Evangelizantur. Maxime vero hoc intelligere debemus de reliquiis Idumaeorum ad Christum con- vertendis, ad quem non convertuntur nisi peccato- res, & desperati, qui vocantur hic pupilli & viduae De quibus ipse Christus ait: Non veni vocare ju- stos, sed peccatores ad poenitentiam. Similiter Osian- der: Etsi revera Dominus est pater orphanorum & viduarum: tamen Propheta hoc loco longius respi- cit. Et innuit, fore, ut etiam ex Idumaeis probe humi- liatis, aliqui ad Christum convertantur: hos pupil- lorum & viduarum nomine, intelligit. Maldonatus ea accipit sensu non promissionis, sed comminatio- nis, quod non dicturus sit Deus, relinque mihi ali- quos pupillos, sed hoc refellit B. Hülsemannus in hoc loco.

## 49:12
Vers. 12. BEHOLD, THEY TO WHOM IT WAS NOT JUDGMENT TO DRINK THE CUP, DRINKING SHALL DRINK) Namely the Jews, who compared with the Idumeans could be considered innocent. משפט guilt, liability, as above 26, vers. 11.

AND THOU AS IF INNOCENT SHALT BE LEFT) In the Hebrew: & shalt thou altogether go unpunished? For that is what נקה most often signifies.

THOU SHALT NOT BE INNOCENT) Thou shalt not go unpunished.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ECCE QVIBUS NON ERAT JUDICIUM UT BIBERENT CALICEM, BIBENTES BIBENT) Nem- pe Judæi, qui comparati cum Idumæis innocentes ha- beri poterant. משפט culpa reatus ut supra 26. vers. 11.

ET TU QVASI INNOCENS RELINQVERIS) In Hebræo: & tu omnino impune feres? Id enim נקה sæ- pissime significat.

NON ERIS INNOCENS) Non impune feres.

## 49:13
Vers. 13. FOR A CURSE SHALL BOSRA BE) Namely Idumea, concerning which see Isa. 63.

We have explained that passage in the annotations to Isaiah, which should be consulted.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN MALEDICTIONEM ERIT BOSRA) Nempe Idumæa, de qua vide Esa. 63.

Locum illum expoluimus in annot. ad Esa- iam, quæ videantur.

## 49:14
Vers. 14. I HAVE HEARD A REPORT FROM THE LORD) A decree as if pronounced by GOD. From Obadiah 1. Concerning which in that place.

AND AN AMBASSADOR IS SENT TO THE NATIONS) An angel of God, who may stir up the Chaldeans.

Theodoret also accepts it as an angel, as do Castro, Tirinus, Menochius, and Gislerius. Bugenhagen understands it generally as God urging and compelling others to the destruction of those whom He wishes to destroy by His own judgment. Similarly Osiander: The Lord sends an ambassador to call the nations against an impenitent people, when He impels peoples by a secret instinct to take up arms and invade those regions which have gravely offended Him by their impiety. The opinion of B. Hülsemann is the simplest, that it concerns any messenger and the convocation of nations among themselves, because the Hebrew word denotes any messenger: the mutual sending of messengers is the usual way to describe the communication of plans. See c. 22, 17. & Compare annotations to Obad. vers. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 14. AUDITUM AUDIVI A DOMINO) Decretum à DEO quasi pronunciatum. Ex Abdia 1. De quo illic loci.

ET LEGATUS AD GENTES MISSUS EST) Angelus Dei, qui excitet Chaldæos.

De angelo Theodoretus etiam accipit, ut & Castro, Tirinus, Menochius, & Gislerius. Bugenha- gius generatim intelligit Deum urgere & cogere alios in perniciem illorum, quos suo judicio perde- re vult. Similiter Osiander: Mittit Dominus lega- tum ad gentes vocandas contra populum impæniten- tem, cum arcano instinctu impellit populos, ut arma capiant, & invadant eas regiones, quæ sua impietate ipsum graviter offenderunt. Simplicissima est B. Hülsemanni sententia, de quovis nuncio, & convo- catione gentium inter se agi, quia vox Ebræa quem- vis nuncium notat: mutua nuntiorum missitatio- ne describi solet consiliorum communicatio. Vide c. 22, 17. & Conf. annot. ad Obad. vers. 1.

## 49:16
Vers. 16. THY ARROGANCE HATH DECEIVED THEE) An idol. For thus מפלצת is taken in 1 Kings 15, 13. Lucilius uses 'terriculas' in a similar sense. For ערץ is to terrify. And these are from Obadiah 3, 4.

THOU THAT DWELLEST IN THE CAVERNS OF THE ROCK) And therefore thou thinkest thyself impregnable, just as those who were in the rock of the Sogdians in Curtius 10. Jerome to Obadiah: The whole southern region of the Idumeans from Eleutheropolis as far as Petra and Aila, this is indeed the possession of Esau, has little dwellings in caves.

AND YOU STRIVE TO GRASP THE HEIGHT OF THE HILL) And you hold the high places of the hills: namely, Seir.

THENCE I WILL DRAG YOU DOWN) By famine, just as Gelimer was dragged down from Mount Aurasius.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ARROGANTIA TUA DECEPIT TE) Idolum. Sic enim מפלצת sumitur 1. Reg 15, 13. Terricu- las simili sensu Lucilius. Nam ערץ est terrere. Et hæc sunt ex Abdia 3, 4.

QVI HABITAS IN CAVERNIS PETRÆ) Ideo- que te in expugnabilem putas, ut illi scilicet qui in petra e- rant Sogdianorum apud Curtium 10. Hieronymus ad Ab- diam: Omnis australis regio Idumæorum de Eleutheropoli usque ad Petram & Hailam, hæc est enim possessio Esau) in specubus habitatiunculas habet.

ET APPREHENDERE NITERIS ALTITUDI- NEM COLLIS) Et tenes celsa collium: Seir scilicet.

INDE DETRAHAM TE) Fame, quomodo ex Aurafio monte detractus fuit Gelimer.

## 49:17
Ver. 17. EVERYONE WHO PASSES BY IT SHALL BE ASTONISHED, AND SHALL HISS AT ALL ITS PLAGUES) It is proverbial, as appears in 1 Kings 9:8.

Latin:

Vers. 17. OMNIS QVI TRANSIBIT PER EAM STUPEBIT, ET SIBILABIT SUPER OMNES PLA- GAS EJUS) Est proverbiale, ut apparet 1. Reg. 9, 8.

## 49:18
Ver. 18. AS SODOM AND GOMORRAH WERE OVERTHROWN, AND THEIR NEIGHBORS) Admah and Zeboim.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SICUT SUBVERSA EST SODOMA ET GOMORRA, ET VICINA EJVS) Adama & Seboim.

## 49:19
Ver. 19. BEHOLD, LIKE A LION HE SHALL COME UP FROM THE PRIDE OF THE JORDAN) Nebuzaradan, the devastator of Judea, shall come up like a lion, whom the overflowing Jordan drove out from the thickets.

TO THE STRONG BEAUTY) In Hebrew: to the strong habitation: Idumea, situated among the rocks.

FOR I WILL SUDDENLY MAKE HIM RUN TO IT) Nebuzaradan to Idumea.

AND WHO SHALL BE THE CHOSEN ONE, WHOM I SHALL APPOINT OVER IT?) We have said elsewhere that מי is often used for whoever. Therefore you will rightly translate, whoever shall be the strongest (among the Chaldeans), him I shall set over it, namely, to devastate it.

WHO IS THIS SHEPHERD, WHO SHALL RESIST MY FACE?) That is, leader.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ECCE QVASI LEO ASCENDET DE SUPERBIA JORDANIS) Nabuzardan Judææ vastator ascendet quasi leo, quem Jordanes exundans lustris expulit.

AD PULCHRITUDINEM ROBUSTAM) In He- bræo: ad habitaculum robustum: Idumæam in rupibus sitam.

QVIA SUBITO FACIAM CURRERE EUM AD ISTAM) Nabuzardanem ad Idumæam.

ET QVIS ERIT ELECTUS, QVEM PRO- PONAM EI.) Diximus alibi מי sæpe poni pro quisquis. Itaque recte verteris, quisquis erit fortissimus (inter Chal- dæos) eum præficiam ei, vastandæ scilicet.

QVIS EST ISTE PASTOR, QVI RESISTAT VULTUI MEO?) Id est, dux.

## 49:20
Ver. 20. IF THE LITTLE ONES OF THE FLOCK DO NOT CAST THEM DOWN) If the least of the flock do not drag them away: supply, lest I be held untruthful. The camp followers, he says, and the servants shall drag them away as captives.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SI NON DEJECERINT EOS PARVU- LI GREGIS) Si non traxerint eos minimi gregis: supple, ne verax habear. Lixæ, inquit, & calones eos captivos trahent.

## 49:21
Ver. 21. A CRY WAS HEARD IN THE RED SEA) For the borders of Idumea reach to the Red Sea. Therefore that sea is called ים אדום, and by the Greeks, rendering word for word, θάλασσα Ἐρυθραία.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CLAMOR IN MARI RUBRO AUDI- TUS EST) Pertingunt enim ad mare rubrum Idumææ fi- nes. Ideo id mare dictum ים אדום, & Græcis verbum verbo reddentibus θάλασσα Ἐρυθραία.

## 49:22
Ver. 22. BEHOLD, LIKE AN EAGLE HE SHALL ASCEND AND FLY AWAY) Nay, he shall fly: that is, Nebuzaradan shall suddenly swoop down upon Idumea.

By that chosen one, Luther and Osiander, along with Lyranus and Dionysius, understand Alexander the Great, as if he were saying, I will rouse that most valiant youth to devastate Idumea. IF THE LITTLE ONES OF THE FLOCK SHALL NOT CAST THEM DOWN: the boys of the shepherds (that is, the soldiers serving the King) shall destroy the cities of the Idumeans: unless they shall have dissipated their dwelling with them: i.e., the soldiers of Alexander the Great shall destroy the fortresses and cities of the Idumeans, together with their inhabitants. At the voice (i.e., at the noise) of their ruin the earth is moved: i.e., Idumea shall horribly collapse: so that the whole earth may seem to be shaken by the force of that ruin: the cry was heard in the Red Sea of its voice: the cry of the Idumeans shall be heard as far as the Red Sea, i.e., their devastation shall be dreadful. Behold, Alexander the Great shall ascend and fly like an eagle, he shall invade Idumea with the greatest speed and fortitude, and shall spread his wings over the city of Bozrah in Idumea, and shall bring it under his power. And the heart of the valiant men, the warriors of Idumea, shall be in that day as the heart of a woman in labor: so that they shall not dare to resist the Macedonians at all because of their anguish of mind. Yet the words themselves do not seem to imply this in a general sense, although they might be understood so. Bugenhagius, however, explains it as the King of Babylon, especially because in chapters 25 and 26 it is spoken of him: The King of Sheshach shall drink after them, and the following two chapters have the same thing, namely, that after the others of whom it is spoken here, the empire of Babylon is to suffer and perish, where in chapter 50, 44 ff. are the very same words that are read here: which passage Osiander himself accepted as referring to the Chaldean. And by these arguments we are easily led to understand the present passage also as referring to Nebuzaradan, with Grotius.

HE SHALL SPREAD HIS WINGS OVER BOZRAH) The same manner of speaking as above at 48, 40.

AND THE HEART OF THE VALIANT MEN OF IDUMEA SHALL BE IN THAT DAY AS THE HEART OF A WOMAN IN LABOR) And we had this in the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ECCE QVASI AQVILA ASCENDET ET AVOLABIT) Imo volabit: id est, involabit Idu- mæam subito Nabuzardan.

Per electum illum intelligit cum Lyrano & Dionysio Lutherus & Osiander Alexandrum M. quasi dicat, excitabo juvenem illum fortissimum, ut Idumæam devastet. SI NON DEJECERINT EOS PARVULI GREGIS : pueri pastorum (hoc est, milites servi Regis) destruent urbes Idu- mæorum : nisi dissipaverint cum eis habitaculum eo- rum : i. e. milites Alexandri Magni arces & civita- tes Idumæorum, una cum habitatoribus delebunt. A voce (i. e. à strepitu) ruinæ eorum commota est terra : i. e. horribiliter corruet Idumæa : ita ut tota terra videatur impetu ruinæ illius concuti : clamor in mari rubro auditus est vocis ejus : audietur cla- mor Idumæorum usque ad mare rubrum, i. e. hor- renda erit ipsorum vastatio. Ecce Alexander Ma- gnus quasi aquila ascendet & advolabit, summa ce- leritate & fortitudine invadet Idumæam, & expan- det alas suas super urbem Bosram in Idumæa, eam- que in suam potestatem rediget. Et erit cor for- tium, bellatorum Idumææ, in die illa, quasi cor mu- lieris parturientis : ita, ut Macedonibus nequa- quam resistere audeant præ animi angustia. Neu- tiquam vero in genere quamvis intelligi verba ipsa innuere videntur. De Rege Babylonio tamen explicat Bugenhagius, maxime, quia cap. 25, 26. dicitur de eo : Rex Sesach bibet post eos, & sequentia duo capita hoc idem habent, videlicet post alios, de quibus hic dicitur passurum & periturum im- perium Babylonis, ubi c. 50, 44. seqq. eadem omnino verba quæ hic leguntur : quem locum de Chaldæo accepit ipse Osiander. Aque his argumen- tis facile inducimur, ut præsentem etiam locum de Nabuzardane cum Grotio intelligamus.

EXPANDET ALAS SVAS SUPER BOSRAM ) Idem loquendi genus supra 48, 40.

ET ERIT COR FORTIVM IDVMÆÆ IN DIE ILLA, QVASI COR MVLIERIS PARTVRIENTIS ) Et hoc ibidem habuimus.

## 49:23
Verse 23.

TO DAMASCUS) Synecdochically, that is, to that Syria in which Damascus is.

HAMATH IS CONFOUNDED) Amathus of Syria. Gen. 10, 18. Num. 13, 21. 2 Sam. 8, 9. 2 Kings 17, 24. 30. 18, 34.

AND ARPAD) It is so written also in 2 Kings 18, 34. But in Gen. 10, 18, אַרְוָדִי, that is, Aradii, as the Greeks have it there. See Pliny in his description of Lebanon.

THEY ARE TROUBLED IN THE SEA) That is, the nearby islanders, for instance, the Antaradii.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

AD DAMASCVM ) Συνεκδοχικῶς, id est, ad Sy- riam illam, in qua est Damascus.

CONFUSA EST EMATH ) Amathus Syriæ. Gen. 10, 18. Num. 13, 21. 2. Sam. 8, 9. 2. Reg. 17, 24. 30. 18, 34.

ET ARPHAD ) Sic scribitur & 2. Reg. 18, 3. At Gen. 10, 18, אַרְוָדִי, id est, Aradii, ut ibi habent Græci. Vide Plinium in Libani descriptione.

TVRBATI SVNT IN MARI ) Id est, insulares proximi, puta Antaradii.

## 49:24
Verse 24.

AS A WOMAN IN LABOR) As above at 22.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

QVASI PARTVRIENTEM ) Ut supra 22.

## 49:25
Verse 25.

HOW THEY LEFT THE PRAISEWORTHY CITY, THE CITY OF JOY) In the Hebrew: Why have they not left the praised city, the (full) town of joy. Why did they wish to defend it? This is the cause of their destruction, as follows. Here the י in the word מְשֻׁוָּשִׁי is merely παραγωγικὴ from the dialect of the Syrians, of whom this treats. Such are גוֹבַי in Nahum 3:17, הֹרִי in Zechariah 14:5, חוֹרִי in Isaiah 19:9, שׁוֹבַי in Isaiah 20:4, אֶרְנִי in Ezekiel 13:9, and certain others elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

QVOMODO RELIQVERVNT CIVITATEM LAVDABILEM, VRBEM LÆTITIÆ ) In Hebræo : Cur non dereliquerunt urbem laudatam, oppidum (ple- num) lætitiæ. Cur eam voluerunt defendere ? hæc est cau- sa exitii eorum, ut sequitur. Hic י in voce מְשֻׁוָּשִׁי est mere παραγωγικὴ ex dialecto Syrorum, de quibus hic agitur. Talia sunt גוֹבַי Nahumi 3, 17. הֹרִי Zachar. 14, 5. חוֹרִי Esa. 19, 9. שׁוֹבַי Esaiæ. 20, 4. אֶרְנִי Ezech. 13, 9. & alia quædam alibi.

## 49:27
Verse 27.

AND IT SHALL DEVOUR THE WALLS OF BEN-HADAD) The palaces of Ben-hadad: the houses of Ben-hadad, just as this same interpreter translates these very two words in Amos 1:4. Ben-hadad was a most powerful king of Syria, 1 Kings 15:18. See what we have said in the third book concerning the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ET DEVORABIT MOENIA BENADAD ) Pala- tia Benadadi: domos Benadadi, quomodo hic ipse inter- pres vertit easdem has duas voces Amosi 1, 4. Benadadus rex Syriæ potentissimus fuit 1. Reg. 15, 18. Vide quæ di- ximus ad tertium lib. de Veritate Religionis Christianæ.

## 49:28
Verse 28.

TO KEDAR) That is, to the Kedarenes, or Cedereni. See on Psalm 120:5. The Greeks form the names of the east in a double way, as Stephanus noted, in ᾶνας or in ηνός. This latter, on account of the plural of those nations which is in ִין.

AND TO THE KINGDOMS OF HAZOR) He calls the provinces kingdoms, to which those people betook themselves from the city of Hazor, which Joshua had destroyed, Joshua 11:13, Judges 4:2.

WHICH NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON SMOTE) He is about to smite; that is, he is about to lay waste with war. This, however, was fulfilled when Nebuchadnezzar

made a great part of Egypt his own, and sent a part of his forces to the neighboring places. THUS SAITH THE LORD: ARISE AND ASCEND TO KEDAR) To the Chaldeans, of course, he will say these things. See also below 31. AND LAY WASTE THE CHILDREN OF THE EAST) Those Arabs who were to the East of the Jews. See what is on Matthew 2:1.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

AD CEDAR ) Id est, ad Cedræos, sive Cede- renos. Vide ad Psal. 120, 5. Græci nomina orientis for- mant duplici modo, ut Stephanus notavit, ἅνας vel in ηνός. Postremum hoc, ob pluralem illarum gentium qui est in ִין.

ET AD REGNA ASOR) Regna vocat provincias, ad quas se contulerunt illi ab urbe Asore, quam diruerat Josue 11, 13. Jud. 4, 2.

QVÆ PERCVSSIT NABVCHODONOSOR REX BABYLONIS ) Percussurus est; id est, bello vasta- turus. Hoc autem impletum est cum Nabuchodonosor

Ægypti magnam partem suam fecit, & partem copiarum misit ad loca vicina. HAEC DICIT DOMINVS: SVRGITE ET A- SCENDITE AD CEDAR) Chaldæis scilicet hæc dicet. Vide & infra 31. ET VASTATE FILIOS ORIENTIS) Arabes il- los qui ad Orientem Judæis. Vide quæ ad Matth. 2, 1.

## 49:29
Verse 29.

THEIR TENTS) For the Kedarenes were a part of the Scenitae. THEIR CURTAINS) Those elegant veils, by which the tents were distinguished. See the Chaldean Paraphrast on Exodus 25, Psalm 114:2. See here above 4:20, 10:19. AND THEIR CAMELS) With which Arabia abounds, as appears from Job and others. AND THEY SHALL CALL UPON THEM TERROR ROUND ABOUT) Formidable soldiers. Metonymy.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

TABERNACVLA EORVM) Erant enim Cedare- ni pars Scenitarum. PELLES EORVM) Vela illa elegantia, per quæ tentoria distingvebantur. Vide Paraphrasten Chaldæum Exod. 25. Psal. 114. v. 2. Vide hic supra 4, 20. 10, 19. ET CAMELOS EORVM) Quibus abundat Ara- bia, ut apparet ex Jobo & aliis. ET VOCABVNT SVPER EOS FORMIDI- NEM IN CIRCVITV) Milites formidandos. Μετωνυ- μία.

## 49:30
Verse 30.

DWELL IN THE DEPTHS) In caves: as above 8. The Greeks in both places βαθύνατε εἰς κάθισιν, seek the depths.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

IN VORAGINIBVS SEDETE) In specubus: ut supra 8. Græci utrobique βαθύνατε εἰς κάθισιν, profunda quærite.

## 49:31
Ver. 31.

TO A QUIET NATION AND DWELLING CONFIDENTLY) Long untouched, and therefore secure. THEY HAVE NEITHER GATES NOR BARS, THEY DWELL ALONE) That is, apart in tents.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

AD GENTEM QVIETAM ET HABITANTEM CONFIDENTER) Pridem intactam, ideoque se- curam. NON OSTIA NEC VECTES EIS, SOLI HA- BITANT) Id est, seorsim in tentoriis.

## 49:32
Ver. 32.

I WILL SCATTER THEM INTO EVERY WIND) To every side. WHO ARE SHORN IN THE HAIR) The Arabs, the τροχοκουράδας. See above 9, 25. and 25, 23. and what was said there.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

DISPERGAM EOS IN OMNEM VENTVM) In omne latus. QVI SVNT ATTONSI IN COMAM) Arabas τροχοκουράδας. Vide supra 9, 25. & 25, 23. & ibi dicta.

## 49:33
Ver. 33.

AND ASOR SHALL BE) That people of whom [I spoke] above in 28.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

ET ERIT ASOR) Populus ille de quo supra 28.

## 49:34
Ver. 34.

WHICH WAS THE WORD OF THE LORD) A transposition, as above 47, 1. AGAINST ELAM) The Elymaeans. See what was said by us in the first book concerning the truth of the Christian Religion. IN THE BEGINNING OF THE REIGN OF KING ZEDEKIAH) That is, long before the event occurred.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

QVOD FACTVM EST VERBVM DOMINI) Transpositio, ut supra 47, 1. ADVERSVS ELAM) Elymæos. Vide quæ dicta à nobis ad primum librum de veritate Religionis Chri- stianæ. IN PRINCIPIO REGNI REGIS SEDECIÆ) Id est, multo antequam res evenirit.

## 49:35
Ver. 35.

BEHOLD I WILL BREAK THE BOW OF ELAM) For they were strong in the bow, as can be seen in Isaiah 22, 6. and in Livy, book 37. It is credible that this happened when the Elymaeans had defected from the king of Media, whose daughter Nebuchadnezzar had in marriage.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

ECCE EGO CONFRINGAM ARCVM ELAM) Arcu enim valebant, ut videre est Esaiæ 22, 6. apud Li- vium lib. 37. Factum hoc credibile est, cum Elymæi de- fecissent à Mediæ rege, cujus filiam in matrimonio habe- bat Nabuchodonosor.

## 49:36
Ver. 36.

AND I WILL BRING UPON ELAM THE FOUR WINDS) Many peoples, the Babylonians, the Medes, and their subjects and allies. AND I WILL FAN THEM INTO ALL THESE WINDS) I will scatter those captured in war.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

ET INDVCAM SVPER ELAM QVATVOR VENTOS) Multos populos, Babylonios, Medos eorum- que subditos ac fœderatos. ET VENTILABO EOS IN OMNES VENTOS ISTOS) Dispergam bello captos.

## 49:38
Verse 38.

AND I WILL SET MY THRONE IN ELAM) My throne, that is, the throne of Cyrus, singularly chosen by me for this purpose. See Isaiah 45:1. For Cyrus, attacking the Medes from Persia, began from Elymais, which is situated among those peoples.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

ET PONAM SOLIVM MEVM IN ELAM) So- lium meum, id est, solium Cyri à me ad hoc singulariter ele- cti. Vide Esaiam 45, 1. Nam Cyrus ex Perside Medos bello impetens incepit ab Elymaide inter illos popu- los sita.

## 49:39
Verse 39.

BUT IN THE LATTER DAYS) That is, at length. I WILL BRING BACK THE CAPTIVES OF ELAM) Through Cyrus, who by that means strengthened his empire over the Medes. Others, Junius, Tremellius, Osiander, and our B. Hülsemann, explain the conversion of the Persians more correctly, as if he were saying: I will send the Apostles and their successors, who shall spread the Gospel concerning Christ even in Persia, so that they too may be gathered into the Church. Compare Acts 2:8, 9. The Weimar and Dutch paraphrasts agree.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

IN NOVISSIMIS AVTEM DIEBVS) Id est, tandem. REVERTI FACIAM CAPTIVOS ELAM) Per Cyrum, qui ea ratione suum in Medos firmavit impe- rium. De Conversione Persarum rectius alii, Junius, Tremellius, Osiander, & B. Hülsemannus noster explicant, quasi dicat: Mittam Apostolos, eorum- que successores, qui Evangelium de Christo etiam in Persia spargant, ut & ipsi colligantur in Ecclesiam. Conf. Act. 2, 8. 9. Consonant Paraphrastæ Vina- rienses & Belgici.

## 50:1 Argument
CHAPTER L. The punishment of impiety and cruelty denounced against the Babylonian kingdom.

Ver. 1.

THE WORD WHICH THE LORD SPOKE CONCERNING BABYLON, AND CONCERNING THE LAND OF THE CHALDEANS, BY THE HAND OF JEREMIAH THE PROPHET) In the last place he sets forth the prophecies concerning Babylon and the Chaldeans, as excellent comforts for the Jews who were to live in exile. Moreover, it is the same matter which is foretold by Isaiah 45, 46, 47, and elsewhere, but the closer the times approached, the more distinctly it was revealed: to which we said the passage of Isaiah 53 refers.

A completely unsuitable comparison of the passages of Isaiah. And it has been shown in individual places that violence was done by Grotius to those prophecies, and especially indeed to chapter 56 of Isaiah.

Latin:

CAPUT L. Impietatis & crudelitatis pœna regno Baby- lonico denunciata.

Verf. 1.

VERBUM QVOD LOCUTUS EST DOMINUS DE BABYLONE, ET DE TERRA CHALDÆO- RUM, IN MANU JEREMIÆ PROPHETÆ) Postremo loco ponit vaticinia de Babylone, & Chaldæis, tanquam egregia judæorum, qui in exilio acturi erant, folatia. Est autem res eadem, quæ prædicitur ab Esaia 45. 46. 47. & alibi, fed quanto tempora accedebant propius, tanto distinctius revelata: quo spectare diximus locum Esaiæ 53.

COllatio prorsus inconveniens locorum E- saiæ. Et vaticiniis illis cumprimis vero cap. Es. 56. vim factam esse à Grotio, singulis locis o- stensum fuit.

## 50:2
Ver. 2.

DECLARE AMONG THE NATIONS) You all, Jews, at the time of the dispersion, sustain one another with this certain hope.

MAKE IT HEARD) That is, spread the report. For thus the Hebrew word השמיע is taken, and ἀκοὴν or ἀκουστὸν ποιεῖν by the Greek interpreters.

SET UP A STANDARD) A sign of approaching joy. For Babylon having been captured by Cyrus was a pledge of their liberation.

BEL IS CONFOUNDED) The idol Bel, that is, of the Sun, which is closer to the Judean Baal: for gutturals are easily elided. Because the same was the first of the gods among the Babylonians, he was called Zeus by the Greeks. When nations are conquered, their gods are also said to be conquered, as we had above concerning the gods of Egypt, concerning Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites.

MERODACH IS BROKEN IN PIECES) The old king of Isaiah 39, reckoned among the gods by the Babylonians.

HER IDOLS ARE CONFOUNDED) The gods of the lesser nations.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ANNUNCIATE IN GENTIBUS) Vos omnes Judæi tempore dispersionis alii alios hac certa spe susten- tate.

AUDITUM FACITE) Id est, famam spargire. Ita enim השמיע fumitur Hebræis, & ἀκοὴν vel ἀκουστὸν ποιεῖν, interpretibus Græcis.

LEVATE SIGNUM) Signum gaudii adventantis. Nam capta à Cyro Babylon erat pignus liberationis ipso- rum.

CONFUSUS EST BEL) Idolum בל, id est Solis, qui propioribus Judææ בעל: nam gutturales facile eli- duntur. Idem quia primus erat deorum apud Babylo- nios, Græcis Ζεὺς dictus. Gentibus victis dicuntur & dii victi, ut de diis Ægypti, de Chamoso Moabitarum, Mel- chomo Ammonitarum deo supra habuimus.

VICTUS EST MERODOCH) Rex vetus Esaiæ 39. à Babyloniis relatus in deos.

CONFUSA SUNT SCULPTILIA EJUS) Dii minorum gentium.

## 50:3
Ver. 3.

A NATION FROM THE NORTH) The Medes, who are northern to the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

GENS AB AQVILONE) Medi Septentrionales Chaldæis.

## 50:4
Ver. 4.

THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SHALL COME, THEY AND THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH TOGETHER) By the children of Israel understand the Levites, and a few from the other tribes, who lived mixed with the tribe of Judah and Benjamin.

THEY SHALL GO WEEPING AND HASTENING, AND THEY SHALL SEEK THE LORD THEIR GOD) The Chaldean provides not a bad version: Walking and weeping they shall go: (formerly when they were being led away) but (now) they shall seek the Lord their God: that is, they shall give thanks to Him.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

VENIENT FILII ISRAEL IPSI, ET FILII JU- DA SIMUL) Per filios Israel Levitas intellige, & ex aliis tribubus paucos, qui Judæi & Benjaminis tribui permixti vivebant.

AMBULANTES ET FLENTES PROPERA- BUNT, ET DOMINUM DEUM SUUM QVÆRENT) Chaldæus non malam versionem præit: Ambulantes & flentes ibarunt: (olim cum adducerentur) at (nunc) Do- minum Deum quærent: id est, gratias ipsi agent.

## 50:5
Ver. 5.

THEY SHALL ASK THE WAY TO SION) That is, the way that leads to Sion.

THITHER SHALL BE THEIR FACES) Concerning this expression see Luke 10:4, above 42:15.

These things are rather to be understood concerning the conversion to the Lord of both the Jews and the Israelites: concerning the weeping of repentance, which is followed by a desire to know the Lord, and concerning the gathering into the Church.

THEY SHALL BE JOINED TO THE LORD BY AN EVERLASTING COVENANT) That is, long-lasting, as often elsewhere. A more sublime sense in the Evangelical covenant which is truly eternal.

There is no need for a double sense. The letter itself is manifest concerning an everlasting covenant, and therefore it is wrongly corrupted, so that it denotes only a long-lasting covenant. What will be left certain in the Scriptures by that agreement? It is much less fitting to take the same word for both long-lastingness and eternity. For both senses cannot exist in one word in the same place. The covenant which the faithful enter into with God is eternal, and although it may be violated by some, yet on the part of God it is ἀμεταμέλητον [irrevocable], nor does the universal Church fall away from the covenant, from which the elect cannot fall away τελικῶς [finally]: It certainly ought to be entered into by all with the intention that it be eternal and immutable.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

IN SION INTERROGABUNT VIAM) Id est, viam quæ fert ad Sionem.

HUC FACIES EORUM) De hac locutione vide Lucæ 10, 4. supra 42, 15.

De conversione ad Dominum tum Judæo- rum tum Israelitarum hæc potius accipienda: de fletu pœnitentiæ, quem sequitur desiderium de co- gnoscendo Domino, & de aggregatione ad Eccle- siam.

APPONENTUR AD DEUM FOEDERE SEM- PITERNO) Id est, diuturno, ut alibi fæpe. Sensus subli- mior in fœdere Evangelico quod vere æternum.

Non opus est gemino sensu. Litera ipsa mani- festa est de fœdere sempiterno, ideoque perperam corrumpitur, ut solum diuturnum fœdus notet. Quid eo pacto certi relinquetur in Scripturis? Multo minus conveniens est, eandem vocem ac- cipere & pro diuturnitate & pro æternitate. Qui uterque sensus uni voci inesse eodem in loco non potest. Fœdus, quod cum Deo ineunt fideles, æternum est, & quanquam à nonnullis id viole- tur, à parte tamen Dei est ἀμεταμέλητον, ne- que universa Ecclesia fœdere excidit, quo nec electi τελικῶς excidere possunt: Eo certe animo ab omnibus iniri debet, ut æternum sit & immu- tabile.

## 50:6
Ver. 6.

THEIR SHEPHERDS HAVE SEDUCED THEM) Kings: when they are removed, they are more curable.

AND THEY HAVE MADE THEM WANDER ON THE MOUNTAINS, FROM MOUNTAIN TO HILL) That is, they were the cause that they were scattered wandering hither and thither. For he persists in the begun similitude of the flock.

THEY HAVE FORGOTTEN THEIR FOLD) Their sheepfold.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PASTORES EORVM SEDUXERVNT EOS) Reges: quibus ablatis sanabiliores funt.

FECERVNTQVE VAGARI IN MONTIBVS, DE MONTE IN COLLEM) Id est causa fuerunt, ut huc il- luc vagi disjicerentur. Perstat enim in cœpta gregis simi- litudine.

OBLITI SVNT CVBILIS SVI) Caula suæ.

## 50:7
Ver. 7. ALL THAT FOUND THEM HAVE EATEN THEM) They despoil.

THEY HAVE SINNED AGAINST THE LORD, THE HABITATION OF JUSTICE) Who was to them a most benign fold. Thus נוה is taken in Ezek. 34:14. It persists in the similitude of a flock. By the fold, however, a refuge is understood.

There is no reason why the Vulgate should be abandoned. For the word נוה signifies beauty and pleasantness, Ps. 45:9. And that interpretation concerning a fold is incongruous. Jerome, Theodoret, Hugo, Dionysius, Lyranus, and others understand by the habitation of justice, Christ, who is said to be so from 1 Cor. 1:30, Jer. 23:6, afterwards. Compare Ps. 45:10, Is. 61:10, who is also afterwards called here the expectation of the fathers. Compare Gen. 49:10, 18, Hag. 2:8.

Latin:

Vers. 7. OMNES QVI INVENERVNT COMEDE- RVNT EOS) Despoliant.

PECCAVERUNT DOMINO DECORI JVSTI- TIÆ) Qui ipsis erat caula benignissima. Sic נוה sumitur Ezech. 34, 14. perstat in similitudine pecoris. Per caulam autem perfugium intelligitur.

Non est causa, cur Vulgata deseratur. Nam vox נוה decorem & amœnitatem significat Psal. 45, 9. Et inconcinna est illa de caula interpretatio. Hie- ronymus, Theodoret. Hugo, Dionys. Lyran. & alii per decorem justitiæ, Christum intelligunt, qui ita è 1. Cor. 1, 30. Jer. 23, 6. dici postea, Confer. Ps. 45, 10. Es. 61, 10. qui etiam postea hic expectatio patrum dictus est. Conf. Gen. 49, 10. 18. Hag. 2, 8.

## 50:8
Ver. 8.

REMOVE OUT OF THE MIDST OF BABYLON) Fly away, let no time pass by: seize the opportunity.

BE AS THE HEE-GOATS BEFORE THE FLOCK) In the Hebrew: birci: who are accustomed to be more lively than other cattle. Such were those companions of Ezra, who went before many others as an example.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

RECEDITE DE MEDIO BABYLONIS) Avolate, nullum tempus abire finite: arripite occasionem.

ESTOTE QVASI HOEDI ANTE GREGEM) In Hebræo: birci: qui aliis pecudibus alacriores esse solent. Tales fuere illi Esdræ comites, qui multis aliis exemplo præivere.

## 50:9
Ver. 9. IT SHALL BE TAKEN) In the Hebrew שׁם, that is, immediately. It shall be seized by force, unexpectedly, says Herodotus.

HIS ARROW, AS OF A MIGHTY MAN A DESTROYER, SHALL NOT RETURN IN VAIN) The Medes and Persians, as we just said concerning their neighbors the Elymaeans, were strong with the bow, which praise passed to their successors the Parthians, as historians and poets testify. See below 14.

Blessed Hülfemann notes here a Hebraism, shall not return in vain: by which is noted the extensive operation of the arrow or the slaughter of many men. Compare 2 Sam. 1:22, Is. 55:1.

Latin:

Vers. 9. INDE CAPIETUR) In Hebræo שׁם, id est, statim. Impetu rapietur, ἐξ ἀπροσδοκήτε, ait Herodotus.

SAGITTA EJUS, QVASI VIRI FORTIS IN- TERFECTORIS, NON REVERTETUR VACUA) Me- di & Persæ, ut modo de vicinis eorum Elymæis diximus, arcu valebant, quæ laus ad successores eorum Parthos tran- siit, testibus historicis & Poetis. Vide infra 14.

Notat hic Ebraismum B. Hülfemannus, non re- vertetur vacua: quo notetur prolixa operatio sa- gittæ seu multorum hominum internecio. Con- fer 2. Sam. 1, 22. Es. 55, 1.

## 50:11
Ver. 11. YOU THAT PLUNDER MY INHERITANCE) You plunderers of my patrimony. God addresses the Chaldeans, who had plundered Judea and Jerusalem itself.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE SPREAD OUT.

In the Hebrew it is, you have grown wanton (Mal. 4, 2. Hab. 1, 8.) like a stall-fed calf, that is, like a sated ox, grazing on herbs.

AND YOU HAVE LOWED LIKE BULLS) צהל signifies every louder sound, says Rabbi Abraham.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DIRIPIENTES HEREDITATEM MEAM) Direptores mei patrimonii. Chaldæos Deus alloquitur, qui Judæam & ipsa Hierosolyma diripuerant.

QVONIAM EFFUSI ESTIS.

In Ebræo est, luxuriatis (Mal. 4, 2. Hab. 1, 8.) sicut vitulus herbæ, id est, sicut bos satur, depascens herbas.

ET MUGISTIS SICUT TAURI) צהל omnem sonum elatiorem significat, ait Rabbi Abraham.

## 50:12
Verse 12. YOUR MOTHER IS CONFOUNDED) She shall be: namely, Babylon.

SHE SHALL BE THE LAST OF THE NATIONS.

That is, despised above the rest. c. 49, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 12. CONFUSA EST MATER VESTRA) Erit: nempe Babylon.

ERIT NOVISSIMA INGENTIBUS.

Id est, contemta præ reliquis. c. 49, 15.

## 50:14
Verse 14. PREPARE YOURSELVES AGAINST BABYLON ROUND ABOUT, ALL YOU) Similar to above 49, 14. & elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PRÆPARAMINI CONTRA BABYLO- NEM PER CIRCUITUM OMNES) Simile supra 49, 14. & alibi.

## 50:15
Verse 15. BECAUSE SHE HAS SINNED AGAINST THE LORD) Against the Lord. By turning the vessels of the Temple to profane uses. Dan. 5, 2. But now how many princes do this, and wish to be called Christians.

SHOUT AGAINST HER: SHE HAS GIVEN HER HAND EVERYWHERE) Shout against her from every side: she has given her hand. That is, Babylon was allied with the Lydians, our enemies: (we learn from Herodotus that this was so) wherefore she is not to be spared. We have Διδόναι δεξιὰς for entering into an alliance in 1 Macc. 11, 50. & Gal. 2, 9. So also to place the hand is used in Levit. 6, 2, to clap the hand in Job 17, 2.

Others [translate] she has given her hand everywhere, that is, she is conquered, from Lam. 5, 6. which is more suitable, and agrees better with the text.

HER FOUNDATIONS HAVE FALLEN, HER WALLS ARE DESTROYED) Let her foundations fall, let her walls be destroyed. For all these things the soldiers are commanded to shout while they make an incursion. And the matter did not happen otherwise. Babylon was thus taken, says Herodotus. But Strabo says: the Persians destroyed parts of the city, and time destroyed others.

AS SHE HAS DONE, DO TO HER) Thus it is said in the Apocalypse concerning Rome: render to her as she also rendered to you 18, 6. Babylon had destroyed many cities, including Jerusalem. Let her suffer the law which she imposed.

We shall speak of the Apocalyptic passage and the application of the Prophet's words, if God permits, when we have arrived at that point.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QVIA DOMINO PECCAVIT) In Dominum. Templi vasa vertendo in usus profanos. Dan. 5, 2. Nunc vero quam multi hoc faciunt principes, & Christiani dici volunt.

CLAMATE ADVERSUS EAM: UBIQVE DE- DIT MANUM SUAM) Clamate adversus eam undique: de- dit manum suam. Id est, Babylon fœderata fuit cum Lydis hostibus nostris: (Id ita fuisse ab Herodoto discimus) quare non est illi parcendum. Διδόναι δεξιὰς pro societatem inire habemus 1. Macc. 11, 50. & Gal. 2, 9. Sic & ponere ma- num sumitur Levit. 6, 2, manum complodere Job. 17, 2.

Alii ubique dedit manum, id est, victa est, è Thren. 5, 6. quod commodius, & textui magis con- venit.

CECIDERUNT FUNDAMENTA EJUS, DE- STRUCTI SUNT MURI EJUS) Cadant fundamenta ejus, destruantur muri ejus. Hæc enim omnia jubentur clama- re milites dum irruptionem faciunt. Nec aliter res se ha- buit. βαβυλὼν μὲν οὕτω ἀνέρητο, ait Herodotus. Strabo vero: κατήριψαν τῆς πόλεως, τὰ μὲν οἱ Πέρσαι, τάδ' ὁ χρόνος.

SICUT FECIT FACITE EI) Sic Gotthis dicitus in Apocalypsi de Roma: ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς κὰι αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν ὑμῖν 18, 6. Babylon multas urbes exciderat etiam Hieroso- lyma. Patiatur legem quam tulit.

De loco Apocalyptico & applicatione verborum Prophetæ dicturi sumus, ἐὰν ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιτρέπει, cum eo devenerimus.

## 50:16
Vers. 16. DESTROY THE SOWER FROM BABYLON AND THE ONE HOLDING THE SICKLE IN THE TIME OF HARVEST) Babylon had a περιγραφήν [description], more of a nation than of a city. Aristot. Polit. 3, 2. Therefore, in the city itself, there is sowing and reaping. Pliny 18, 17. For this reason, there were many farmers in that city. But since victors are usually more merciful in sparing farmers, the Medes and Persians did not do this when they captured Babylon.

Simplicius and others, noting here the description of temporal happiness from a rich harvest and its administrators. Ps. 129, 1. Jer. 9, 22.

FROM THE FACE OF THE DOVE'S SWORD) Of the destroyer. For that is what יונה is here, as we said above 26. 38. & 46, 17.

EVERYONE SHALL TURN TO HIS OWN PEOPLE, AND EACH SHALL FLEE TO HIS OWN LAND) Namely, the auxiliaries hired by the Babylonians.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DISPERDITE SATOREM DE BABYLO- NE ET TENENTEM FALCEM IN TEMPORE MES- SIS) Babylon habuit περιγραφήν, magis ἔθνυς, quam πό- λεως. Aristot. Polit. 3, 2. Itaque in ipsa urbe seritur ac meti- tur. Plinius 18, 17. ob id multi in ea urbe erant agricolæ. Cum vero victores clementiores soleant agricolis parcere: non fecere id Medi ac Persæ, cum Babylonem caperent.

Simplicius alii descriptionem hic notantes felicitatis temporalis à messe opima, ejusque ad- ministris. Pf. 129, 1. Jer. 9, 22.

A FACIE GLADII COLUMBÆ) Vastatoris. Id enim hic est יונה, ut diximus supra 26. 38. & 46, 17.

UNUSQUISQUE IN POPULUM SUUM CON- VERTETUR, ET SINGULI AD TERRAM SUAM FUGIENT) Auxiliares scilicet à Babyloniis conducti.

## 50:17
Vers. 17.

ISRAEL IS A SCATTERED FLOCK: THE LIONS HAVE DRIVEN HIM AWAY) They have scattered him. The lions are kings, as the Chaldean rightly interprets: τό θηρίον βασιλέα δηλοῖ, as we have shown elsewhere.

THE FIRST KING OF ASSYRIA ATE HIM) Shalmaneser, who deported the ten tribes.

NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON HAS PICKED HIS BONES) He took away what remained of the body, that is, Judah and Benjamin.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

GREX DISPERSUS ISRAEL: LEONES EJECE- RUNT EUM) Dispeferunt eum. Leones sunt reges, ut recte interpretatur Chaldæus: τό θηρίον βασιλέα δηλοῖ, ut alibi ostendimus.

PRIMUS COMEDIT EUM REX ASSUR) Sal- manafar, qui decem tribus deportavit.

EXOSSAVIT EUM NABUCHODONOSOR REX BABYLONIS) Quod de corpore reliquum erat, id est, Judam & Benjaminem, abstulit.

## 50:18
Vers. 18.

BEHOLD I WILL VISIT THE KING OF BABYLON) Who holds the place of Nebuchadnezzar, Nabonidus according to Berosus, Labynetus according to Herodotus. For often among the Chaldeans ד and ר are interchanged. The same is Nabannidachus to Abydenus, Nabonadus to Ptolemy.

AS I VISITED THE KING OF ASSYRIA) Namely, Sennacherib, the successor of Shalmaneser.

AND I WILL BRING BACK ISRAEL TO HIS HABITATION) That is, Judah, Benjamin, the Levites, and certain others joined to them.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

ECCE EGO VISITABO REGEM BABYLONIS) Qui Nabuchodonosori locum tenet, Nabonidum Beroso, Labyniturn Herodoto. Nam sæpe apud Chaldæos ד & permutantur. Idem Nabannidachus Abydeno, Nabona- dus Ptolemæo.

SICUT VISITAVI REGEM ASSUR) Nempe Sennacheribum Salmanafaris successorem.

ET REDUCAM ISRAEL AD HABITACULUM SUUM) Id est, Judam, Benjaminem, Levitas, & alios quosdam his adjunctos.

## 50:19
Vers. 19.

AND CARMEL SHALL BE FED) They shall feed. Carmel, as we have shown elsewhere from Tacitus, is a mountain midway between Judea and Syria. Elsewhere כרמל is a common noun: here it is a proper noun.

AND BASHAN) Where the pastures are best.

AND IN MOUNT EPHRAIM) Of Samaria, which was granted to the Jews by Demetrius, as we have demonstrated elsewhere.

AND GILEAD) A part of Galilee. Moreover, Galilee was in that same grant of Demetrius: and as an accession to Judea, no less than Samaria, it was possessed by the Jewish kings, and even by Herod the Great.

HIS SOUL SHALL BE SATISFIED) That is, he himself.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ET PASCETUR CARMELUM) Depascentur. Carmelus, ut alibi ex Tacito ostendimus, mons Judæam inter Syriamque medius. Alibi כרמל est commune: hic proprium.

ET BASAN) Ubi pascua optima.

ET IN MONTE EPHRAIM) Samariæ, quæ con- cessa Judæis à Demetrio, ut alibi demonstravimus.

ET GALAAD) Pars Galilææ. Fuit autem in eadem concessione Demetrii & Galilæa: & ut accessio Judææ, non minus quam Samaria, possessa à regibus Judæis, etiam ab Herode magno.

SATVRABITUR ANIMA EJUS) Id est, ipse.

## 50:20
Ver. 20.

THE INIQUITY OF ISRAEL SHALL BE SOUGHT, AND SHALL NOT BE; AND THE SIN OF JUDAH, AND IT SHALL NOT BE FOUND) A simile taken from debts, which are written in a book, and where they have been accepted as paid, they are erased. Thus the Greeks used to say that sins are written in the folds of the tablets of Zeus, as Euripides testifies in Melanippe.

FOR I WILL BE MERCIFUL TO THEM WHOM I SHALL LEAVE) To those who shall be survivors, I will forgive their sins: that is, I will treat them as if neither they nor their parents had sinned.

Therefore, an all-encompassing forgiveness of sins is described, both because the iniquity is said to be sought and not found, and because the Lord promises that He will be merciful, which phrase embraces not only the forgiveness of temporal punishments but also the remission of sins, and thus that both guilt and punishment are to be remitted. To be merciful to someone is not to treat them as if they had not sinned: which sense of the phrase Grotius drew not from the Holy Scriptures, but from Socinian pits. Some explain the promise concerning the Church and the kingdom of Christ: for although the Lord embraced the Jews, who returned from the Babylonian captivity, with fatherly benevolence, yet the Prophet here looks toward the Kingdom of Christ: where all who believe in Christ obtain the remission of all their sins. Acts 10:43, so that sins are no longer imputed to them: Rom. 4, Ps. 32.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

QVÆRETUR INIQVITAS ISRAEL, ET NON ERIT; ET PECCATVM JUDA, ET NON INVENIE- TUR) Similitudo sumpta à debitis, quæ in libro scribun- tur, & ubi acceptilata sunt, delentur. Sic τὰ ἀδικήμα- τα ἐν Διὸς δέλτω πτυχαῖς γράφεsθαι dicebant Græci, teste Euripide in Melanippe.

QUONIAM PROPITIVS ERO EIS QVOS RELIQVERO) Iis, qui superstites erunt, peccata con- donabo: id est, tractabo eos, quasi nec ipsi, nec parentes eorum peccassent.

Condonatio ergo peccatorum omnimoda describitur, tum quia quærenda dicitur iniqui- tas, non invenienda, tum quia propitium se fo- re promittit Dominus, quæ phrasis non folum pœnarum temporalium condonationem, sed peccatorum etiam remissionem complectitur, a- deoque quod tum culpa, tum pœna sit remitten- da. Propitium esse alicui non est tractare, quasi non peccasset: quem sensum Phraseos non è Scri- pturis sacris, sed è lacunis Socinisticis hausit Gro- tius. De Ecclesia & regno Christi explicant non- nulli promissionem : Etsi enim Dominus Ju- dæos, è captivitate Babylonica reversos, paterna benevolentia est complexus: tamen Propheta hic respicit ad Regnum Christi: ubi omnes qui in Christum credunt, omnium peccatorum suo- rum remissionem consequuntur. Act. 10, 43. ita ut eis peccata non amplius imputentur: Rom. 4. Psal. 32.

## 50:21
Ver. 21.

GO UP AGAINST THE LAND OF THE DOMINATORS) God speaks to a man not yet born, namely Cyrus, and shows what He wishes him to do; He shows also by what route he is to come against Babylon: wherefore I agree with those who understand by the land מרתים here not the land of the dominators, as the Latin here does from the Chaldean, nor of the rebels, as others do, but of the Mardi, who are named in the dual number for the reason that some were on this side of the Tigris, others across the Tigris, as we learn from Ptolemy, and likewise from Pliny and Mela.

AND UPON ITS INHABITANTS VISIT) For visit; the Chaldean has the proper name inhabitants of Pekod, that is, as I think, of the Bactrians.

DISSIPATE AND KILL THOSE WHICH ARE AFTER THEM) That is, take away their posterity, by killing even all the children. Thus the word הרם is used in Dan. 11, 4.

DO ACCORDING TO ALL WHICH I HAVE COMMANDED THEE) Execute my commands, which I have published through Isaiah.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

SVPER TERRAM DOMINANTIVM ASCEN- DE) Loquitur Deus homini nondum nato, Cyro scilicet, ostenditque quid eum velit facere; ostendit autem quo iti- nere venturus sit contra Babylonem: quare assentior iis qui per terram מרתים hic non terram dominantium, ut Latinus hic ex Chaldæo, nec rebellium, ut alii, sed Mardorum intelligunt, qui duali numero ideo nominan- tur, quod alii essent cis Tigridem, alii trans Tigridem, ut ex Ptolemæo discimus, itemque ex Plinio, & Mela.

ET SUPER HABITATORES EJUS VISITA) Pro visita; Chaldæus habet proprium nomen habitatores Pekod, Id est, ut puto, Bactrorum.

DISSIPA ET INTERFICE QVÆ POST EOS SUNT) Id est, posteritatem illis aufer, omnes etiam pue- ros occidendo, Sic vox הרם sumitur Dan. 11, 4.

FAC JUXTA OMNIA QVÆ PRÆCEPI TI- BI) Mandata mea, quæ per Esaiam edidi, exsequere.

## 50:23
Verse 23.

HAMMER OF THE WHOLE EARTH) He calls the Chaldeans so, for the same reason as that for which the Frankish [leader] was indeed called Martellus.

HOW IS BABYLON BECOME A DESERT AMONG THE NATIONS) Better: How has Babylon been a cause of astonishment to the nations? For שמה signifies this also.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

MALLEUS UNIVERSÆ TERRÆ) Sic vocat Chaldæos, pari de causa, ut ob quam Francorum quidem dictus est Martellus.

QVOMODO VERSA EST IN DESERTUM BABYLON IN GENTIBUS) Melius: Quomodo Ba- bylon gentibus stupori fuit? Nam שמה & hoc significat.

## 50:24
Verse 24.

THOU ART TAKEN BABYLON AND THOU DIDST NOT KNOW) Suddenly, suspecting nothing of the sort as yet. See above 8. Herodotus relates, and Aristotle from him, that a part of the city had already been captured, while those who were in the middle of the city were still ignorant of it.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

CAPTA ES BABYLON ET NESCIERAS) Su- bitò, nihil tale adhuc suspicans. Vide supra 8. Narrat He- rodotus & ex eo Aristoteles, jam partem urbis fuisse ca- ptam, cum qui in media essent urbe, id adhuc ignora- rent.

## 50:25
Verse 25.

THE LORD HATH OPENED HIS TREASURY) Namely, He whose treasures you have taken away.

AND HATH BROUGHT FORTH THE VESSELS OF HIS INDIGNATION) He, whose vessels you have profaned: See above 15.

FOR THERE IS A WORK FOR THE LORD GOD OF HOSTS) He has need of such instruments as are the Medes and Persians.

Nay, WORK here is the purpose and the decreed execution of GOD, as in chapter 48, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

APERUIT DOMINUS THESAURUM SUUM) Nempe is cujus thesauros tu abstulisti.

ET PROTULIT VASA IRÆ SUÆ) Is, cujus vasa tu profanasti: Vide supra 15.

QVONIAM OPUS EST DOMINO DEO E- XERCITUUM) Opus illi est talibus instrumentis, quales sunt Medi & Persæ.

Imo OPUS hic est propositum, & decreta exequutio DEI, ut cap. 48, 10.

## 50:26
Ver. 26.

COME TO HER FROM THE FARTHEST BORDERS) From the Caspian and Euxine Sea.

OPEN SO THAT THEY MAY GO FORTH WHO TREAD HER DOWN: REMOVE THE STONES FROM THE WAY, AND REDUCE HER TO HEAPS AND DESTROY HER: AND LET THERE BE NOTHING LEFT) The versions vary here. This seems the best: Open her storehouses and tread her like heaps (of wheat, that is, they are threshed by treading) indeed so destroy her that nothing remains.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

VENITE AD EAM AB EXTREMIS FINIBUS) A Mari Caspin & Euxino.

APERITE UT EXEANT QVI CONCUL- CENT EAM: TOLLITE DE VIA LAPIDES, ET REDIGITE IN ACERVOS ET INTERFICITE EAM: NEC SIT QUICQVAM RELIQVUM) Variant hic versiones. Optima hæc videtur: Aperite apothecas ejus & calcare eam ficut acervi (tritici scilicet, teruntur calcando) quin ita eam delete ut nihil fuperfit.

## 50:28
Ver. 28.

THE VOICE OF THOSE WHO FLEE AND OF THOSE WHO HAVE ESCAPED FROM THE LAND OF BABYLON, TO ANNOUNCE IN ZION THE VENGEANCE OF THE LORD OUR GOD, THE VENGEANCE OF HIS TEMPLE) The flight will be so great that it will carry some even to Judea: who will there narrate what has happened to Babylon.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

VOX FUGIENTIUM ET EORUM QUI EVA- SERUNT DE TERRA BABYLONIS, UT ANNUN- CIENT IN SION ULTIONEM DOMINI DEI NO- STRI, ULTIONEM TEMPLI EJUS) Tanta erit fu- ga, ut quosdam perlatura sit ad Judæam usque: qui ibi narraturi sint quid Babyloni evenerit.

## 50:29
Ver. 29.

ANNOUNCE TO BABYLON TO MANY, TO ALL WHO BEND THE BOW) Summon many against Babylon, who may all bend the bow.

TAKE YOUR STAND AGAINST HER ROUND ABOUT AND LET NO ONE ESCAPE) Place stations on every side, so that no one may escape.

REPAY HER ACCORDING TO HER WORK) Above 15.

BECAUSE SHE HAS BEEN LIFTED UP AGAINST THE LORD) See in the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ANNUNCIATE IN BABYLONEM PLURIMIS, OMNIBUS QUI TENDUNT ARCUM) Convocate con- tra Babylonem multos, qui omnes arcum tendant.

CONSISTITE ADVERSUS EAM PER GYRUM ET NULLUS EVADAT) Stationes ab omni parte ponite, nè quis evadat.

REDDITE EI SECUNDUM OPUS SUUM) Su- pra 15.

QVIA CONTRA DOMINUM ERECTA EST) Vide ibidem.

## 50:30
Ver. 30.

THEY SHALL BE SILENT IN THAT DAY) Better: they shall be cut down: from דמה not from דמם they shall be crushed, the Chaldean. φθήσονται, the Greeks.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

CONTICESCENT IN DIE ILLO) Melius: fuca cidentur: à דמה non à דמם conterentur, Chaldæus. φθή- σονται, Græci.

## 50:31
Verse 31.

BEHOLD I AM AGAINST THEE O PROUD ONE) O proud Chaldean, I come against thee.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

ECCE EGO AD TE SUPERBE) Superbe Chal dæe ad te venio.

## 50:32
Verse 32.

HE SHALL FALL, AND THERE SHALL BE NONE TO RAISE HIM UP) Who may lift him up,

Latin:

Vers. 32.

CORRUET, ET NON ERIT QUI SUSCITET EUM) Qui erigat,

## 50:33
Verse 33.

THEY SUSTAIN OPPRESSION) As they are oppressed. For this is עשק, κατεδυνάσευσαν in the LXX in this place, who elsewhere less appropriately translate it σύκοφαντεῖν, concerning which we have spoken at Luke 3:14.

ALL THAT TOOK THEM CAPTIVE HOLD THEM FAST, THEY REFUSE TO LET THEM GO) As much the Assyrians as the Babylonians: therefore I have need of other men.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

CALUMNIAM SUSTINENT) Ut opprimuntur. Id enim עשק, κατεδυνάσευσαν LXX. hoc loco, qui alibi minus proprie vertunt σύκοφαντεῖν, de quo diximus ad Luc. 3, 14.

OMNES QVI CEPERUNT EOS TENENT, NOLUNT DIMITTERE EOS) Tam Assyrii quam Babylonii : ideo aliis hominibus mihi opus est.

## 50:34
Verse 34.

HE SHALL DEFEND THEIR CAUSE IN JUDGMENT) He shall be an advocate for them. For He sees that they are treated harshly, and mocked, on account of the worship of the one true God.

THAT HE MAY TERRIFY THE EARTH) In the Hebrew: that He may make the Earth rest: that is, that He may render Judea tranquil.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

JUDICIO DEFENDET CAUSAM EORUM) Erit ipsis advocatus. Videt enim dure eos haberi, & il- ludi, ob unius veri Dei cultum.

UT EXTERREAT TERRAM) In Hebræo: ut quiscere faciat Terram : id est, ut tranquillam reddat Ju- dæam.

## 50:35
Verse 35.

TO HIS WISE MEN) Μοῦνοι χαλδαῖοι σοφίαν λάχον. Thus they thought of themselves. Strabo: Ἀφώρισο δ' ἐν τῇ βαβυλωνίᾳ κατοικία τοῖς ἐπιχωρίοις Φιλοσόφοις, τοῖς χαλ- δαῖοις προσαγορευομένοις, οἳ περὶ ἀςρονομίαν εἰσὶ τὸ πλέον.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

AD SAPIENTES EJUS) Μοῦνοι χαλδαῖοι σοφίαν λάχον Ita de se existimabant. Strabo : Ἀφώρισο δ' ἐν τῇ βαβυλωνίᾳ κατοικία τοῖς ἐπιχωρίοις Φιλοσόφοις, τοῖς χαλ- δαίοις προσαγορευομένοις, οἳ περὶ ἀςρονομίαν εἰσὶ τὸ πλέον.

## 50:36
Verse 36.

TO HIS DIVINERS) In the Hebrew: his liars. The Chaldean interprets it as קסם, which name the Chaldean version uses for Balaam. Chaldean seers are mentioned in Curtius, whose remark is also this: If indeed it is an art, and not the mockery of every most vain person. WHO SHALL BE FOOLISH) That is, they shall be detected to be foolish, because they did not foresee these things.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

AD DIVINOS EJUS) In Hebræo: mendaces ejus. Chaldæus interpretatur קסם, quod nomen de Balaamo usurpat Chaldaica versio. Chaldæi vates apud Curtium, cu- jus & hoc : Si modo ars est, & non vanissimi cujusque ludi- brium. QVI STULTI ERUNT) Id est, stulti deprehen- dentur esse, quod ista non præviderint.

## 50:37
Verse 37.

AND THEY SHALL BE AS WOMEN) Fearful: thinking nothing manly.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

ET ERUNT QVASI MULIERES) Pavidi : nihil virile cogitantes.

## 50:38
Verse 38.

ITS DROUGHT IS UPON THE WATERS, AND THEY SHALL DRY UP) Because Cyrus made the bed of the Euphrates passable for himself by diverting the river, as Herodotus narrates in Clio, and Xenophon in book 7 of the Cyropaedia. See also below 51, 32. Semiramis had done the same long ago, and Alexander after Cyrus. Frontinus 3, 7. BECAUSE IT IS A LAND OF GRAVEN IMAGES) This is the reason why God allowed these things to happen. AND THEY GLORY IN PORTENTS) It is the same as above. For אימים are Idols. But the Greeks read אמים: less correctly.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

SICCITAS EJUS SUPER AQVAS, ET ARE- SCENT) Quia abducto flumine alveum Euphratis sibi per- vium fe it Cyrus, narrante Herodoto in Clio, & Xenophon- te libro 7. Institutionis. Vide & infra 51, 32. Idem olim Semiramis fecerat, & post Cyrum Alexander. Fronti- nus 3, 7. QVIA TERRA SCULPTILIUM EST) Hæc causa est, cur Deus ista fieri siverit. ET IN PORTENTIS GLORIANTUR) Idem est quod supra. Nam אימים sunt Idola. At Græci legere אמים: minus recte.

## 50:39
Verse 39.

THEREFORE WILD DRAGONS SHALL DWELL THERE.) Wild beasts, as we said at Isaiah 13, 21. WITH WILD CATS) With wild cats, as in Isaiah 13, 22. The word SICARIIS in the Vulgate is clearly foreign here. AND OSTRICHES SHALL DWELL IN IT) See Isaiah ibid. and 4, 3. EVEN FOR EVER) In the Hebrew: לנצח to the end: that is, until the time appointed by God. EVEN TO GENERATION AND GENERATION) Through two generations. The sense of the prophecy is corrupted: For in it a total and final extermination is expressly predicted. Which those descriptions teach, Ziim and Iim shall dwell in it. Ostriches shall dwell in it. And the negative is placed absolutely: It shall not be inhabited anymore by men, nor shall it be built. Then the express designation of eternal desolation: It shall not be inhabited anymore FOR EVER. For the Hebrew phrase does not signify an appointed time in the Holy Scriptures, but eternity. Furthermore, 'from generation to generation' is added, which phrases, when they are accumulated in this way, never denote the duration of generations, but imply eternity. Finally, lest any doubt remain, another periphrasis of eternal desolation is subjoined from a similar destruction: 'As the Lord overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, so shall no man dwell there (in Babylon) and no son of man shall inhabit it hereafter,' that is, it shall remain uninhabitable forever.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

PROPTEREA HABITABUNT DRACONES SIL- VESTRES.) Feræ, ut diximus ad Esa. 13, 21. CUM FAUNIS SICARIIS) Cum feris felibus, ut Esa. 13, 22. Vox SICARIIS Vulgatæ hic plane aliena est. ET HABITABUNT IN EA STRUTHIONES) Vide Esaiam ibid. & 4, 3. USQVE IN SEMPITERNUM) In Hebræo: לנצח ad finem: id est, ad tempus usque a Deo præstitutum. USQVE AD GENERATIONEM ET GENERA- TIONEM) Per γενεὰς duas. Corrumpitur vaticinii sensus: Nam diserte in eo totale & finale exterminium prædicitur. Quod docent illæ descriptiones, habitabunt in ea Ziim & Iim. Habitabunt in ea struthiones. Et negativa ἁ- πλῶς posita: Non inhabitabitur ultra ab hominibus, nec extruetur. Tum expressa æternæ vastitatis desi- gnatio: Non inhabitabitur ultra in SEMPITER- NUM. Nam Phrasis Ebræa non tempus præstitu- tum sonat in S. literis, sed æternitatem. Additur porro de generatione in generationem, quæ Phrases cum ita cumulantur, nunquam durationem gene- rationum notant, sed æternitatem inferunt. Deni- que ne dubium supersit, alia adhuc æternæ vastita- tis περίφρασις subjungitur ab exitio simili: Sicut subvertit Dominus Sodomam & Gomorram, ita non habitabit deinceps ibi vir (in Babylonia) & non in- colet eam posthac filius hominis, id est, perpetuo ma- nebit inhabitabilis.

## 50:40
Verse 40.

AS THE LORD OVERTHREW SODOM, AND GOMORRAH, AND HER NEIGHBORS) See above 49, 18. BEHOLD A PEOPLE COMES FROM THE NORTH) Medes. AND A GREAT NATION) And here is an ἐξηγητικὸν (explanatory note). The sense: who are a great nation. AND MANY KINGS) Of the Armenians, Hyrcanians, Cadusians, Lydians. See Xenophon, book 5 of the Cyropaedia. FROM THE ENDS OF THE EARTH) See above 26. He often repeats the same things, so that they may stick more firmly in the memory.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

SICVT SUBVERTIT DOMINUS SODOMAM, ET GOMORRAM, ET VICINAS EJUS) Supra 49, 18. ECCE POPULUS VENIT AB AQVILONE) Medi. ET GENS MAGNA) ו hic est ἐξηγητικὸν. Sensus: qui sunt gens magna. ET REGES MULTI) Armeniorum, Hyrcanorum, Cadusiorum, Lydorum. Vide Xenophontem 5. institu- tionis. A FINIBUS TERRÆ) Vide Supra 26. sæpe eadem repetit, quo firmior hæreat memoria.

## 50:42
Verse 42.

THEIR VOICE SHALL ROAR LIKE THE SEA) They shall rage fiercely. LIKE THE VOICE FOR BATTLE) In the Hebrew: Set in order, (that is, set in order) as a man for battle. Such great order, that you would say the whole army is one man. Verse 43. THE KING OF BABYLON HAS HEARD THE FAME OF THEM) Nabonidus.

Latin:

Vers. 42.

VOX EORUM QVASI MARE SONABIT) Sæ- vum frement. SICUT VOX AD PRÆLIUM) In Hebræo: Or- dinatus, (id est, ordinati) tanquam vir ad prælium. Tantus ordo, ut totum agmen virum unum esse dicas. Vers. 43. AUDIVIT REX BABYLONIS FAMAM EORUM) Nabonidus.

## 50:43
AND THEIR HANDS ARE WEAKENED) He was immediately defeated in battle. See Herodotus.

PAIN AS OF A WOMAN IN LABOR) See above 6, 24. 13, 21. 22, 23.

Latin:

ET DISSOLUTÆ SUNT MANUS EORUM) Statim prælio victus est. Vide Herodotum.

DOLOR QVASI PARTURIENTEM) Supra 6, 24. 13, 21. 22, 23.

## 50:44
Verse 44.

BEHOLD AS A LION HE SHALL COME UP) These are the same things we had above concerning Nebuzaradan 49, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 44.

ECCE QVASI LEO ASCENDET) Eadem sunt quæ supra de Nabuzardane habuimus 49, 19.

## 50:45
Verse 45.

WHICH HE HAS CONCEIVED AGAINST BABYLON) As above 49, 19 against Edom. And for 'in the Red Sea,' it is here 'among the nations.' The rest are the same.

Latin:

Vers. 45.

QVOD CONCEPIT ADVERSUS BABYLO- NEM) Sicut supra 49, 19. adversus Edom. Et pro in mari rubro, est hic in gentibus. Cætera eadem.

## 51:1 Argument
CHAPTER LI.

Evils impending over Babylon from the Kings of the Medes are predicted. The book of prophecy is transmitted to Babylon by Seraiah the captive and is cast into the middle of the Euphrates.

Vers. 1.

THUS SAYS THE LORD) It is a continuous discourse with the former.

BEHOLD I WILL RAISE UP AGAINST BABYLON, AND AGAINST ITS INHABITANTS, WHO HAVE LIFTED UP THEIR HEART AGAINST ME AS A PESTILENTIAL WIND) A burning wind. That לב קמי which is translated here, who have lifted up their heart against me, through that frequent transposition of letters among the Chaldeans which is called Atbash, about which we said something above 25, 26, makes כשדים which signifies the Chaldeans. And thus both the Greeks and the Chaldean understood this concealment in this place; nor otherwise did the Rabbis Solomon and Kimchi.

Latin:

CAPUT LI.

Mala à Regibus Medorum Babyloni imminen- tia prædicuntur. Liber prophetiæ per Sara- jam captivum in Babyl. transmittitur & in medium Euphratem projicitur.

Vers. 1.

HÆC DICIT DOMINUS) Est sermo continuus cum priore.

ECCE EGO SUSCITABO SUPER BABYLO- NEM, ET SUPER HABITATORES EJUS, QVI COR SUUM LEVAVERUNT CONTRA ME QVA- SI VENTUM PESTILENTEM) Ventum urentem. Illud לב קמי quod hic vertitur, qui cor suum levaverunt contra me, per literarum transmigrationem illam frequentem Chal- dæis quæ dicitur אתבש, de qua aliquid diximus supra 25, 26. facit כשדים quod Chaldæos significat. Et ita hanc κεύσιν intellexere & Græci & Chaldæus hoc loco; nec ali- ter Rabbini Salomon & Kimchi.

## 51:2
Vers. 2.

AND I WILL SEND INTO BABYLON WINNOWERS AND THEY SHALL WINNOW IT) That is, dispersers. For those who winnow, disperse.

AND THEY SHALL DEMOLISH ITS LAND) They shall despoil. So also the Chaldean.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE COME UPON IT FROM EVERY SIDE, IN THE DAY OF ITS AFFLICTION) Better: When they (the Babylonians themselves) have surrounded it from every side in an adverse time.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET MITTAM IN BABYLONEM VENTILA- TORES ET VENTILABUNT EAM) Id est, disperse- res. Nam qui ventilant, dispergunt.

ET DEMOLIENTVR TERRAM EJVS) Despolia- bunt. Sic & Chaldæus.

QVONIAM VENERVNT SVPER EAM VN- DIQVE, IN DIE AFFLICTIONIS EJVS) Melius: Cum eam undique circumvenerint tempore (ipsi Babylonii) adverso.

## 51:3
Vers. 3.

LET NOT HIM WHO BENDS BEND HIS BOW AND LET HIM NOT ASCEND ARMORED: DO NOT SPARE ITS YOUNG MEN, KILL ALL ITS MILITIA) Better: To him who bends by bending let him bend his bow: and to him who ascends armored: these things, namely, God says which follow: do not spare the youth: kill all its militia. He repeats the word of bending three times, because he wishes the string to be bent as much as possible.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

NON TENDAT QVI TENDIT ARCVM SVVM ET NON ASCENDAT LORICATVS : NOLITE PARCERE JVVENIBVS EJVS, INTERFICITE O- MNEM MILITIAM EJVS) Melius; Ei qui tendit tendendo tendens arcum suum: & ei qui ascendit loricatus: hæc scilicet dicit Deus quæ sequuntur: ne parcite juventuti: omnem mi- litiam ejus interficite. Ter repetit vocem tendendi, quia vult quam maxime tendi nervum.

## 51:4
Vers. 4.

AND THE SLAIN SHALL FALL IN THE LAND OF THE CHALDEANS) A transposition for the slain of the Chaldeans, that is, from the Chaldeans, shall fall into the land.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET CADENT INTERFECTI IN TERRA CHALDÆORUM) Transpositio pro interfecti Chaldæorum, id est, ex Chaldæis, cadent in terram.

## 51:5
Verse 5.

FOR ISRAEL AND JUDAH HAVE NOT BEEN WIDOWED BY THEIR GOD, THE LORD OF HOSTS, BUT THEIR LAND IS FILLED WITH SIN AGAINST THE HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL) For Israel and Judah have not been widowed (abandoned as a widow) by their God, the Lord of hosts; (that is, God remembers the insult brought upon the Jews on account of their religion) and therefore their land (that is, that of the Chaldeans) will be most fully punished by the Holy One of Israel; by God, that is, they will bear a much heavier punishment than the Jews have endured.

It is more correctly explained thus: Israel is not completely abandoned (for to abandon a widow is to abandon her completely, Ps. 109:9, Jer. 15:8, Is. 19:7, Josh. 16:15), although previously he filled his land with sins against the Holy One of Israel, that is, against the holy one, as in ch. 50:29, Is. 54:5, ch. 55:5, which sense Theodoret also rendered.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QVONIAM NON FUIT VIDUATUS ISRAEL ET JUDA A DEO SUO DOMINO EXERCITUVM, TERRA AVTEM EORVM REPLETA EST DELICTO A SANCTO ISRAEL) Nam non à Deo suo Domino exerci- tuum viduati sunt, (derelicti ut vidua) Israel & Iuda: (id est, meminit Deus contumeliæ Judæis illatæ ob religio- nem) ideoque terra eorum (id est, Chaldæorum) plenissime punietur à Sancto Israelis; à Deo, id est, multo graviorem pœnam ferent, quam Judæi pertulerunt.

Rectius ita exponitur, Israel non est plane de- relictus (nam viduam relinquere est plane deserere Psal. 109, 9. Jerem. 15, 8. Es. 19, 7. Jos. 16, 15.) quanquam antea terram suam impleverit delictis à Sancto Israel, id est, contra sanctum, ut cap. 50, 29. Es. 54, 5. cap. 55, 5. quem etiam sensum red- didit Theodoretius.

## 51:6
Verse 6.

FLEE FROM THE MIDST OF BABYLON, AND LET EVERYONE SAVE HIS OWN SOUL) Revelation 18:4 applies this to Rome when it was besieged by the Goths. Nabonidus fulfilled these words. For he fled from Babylon to Borsippa. See the passage of Berosus which we produced for the third book on the truth of the Christian Religion.

DO NOT BE SILENT CONCERNING HER INIQUITY) You might better translate: Do not be cut off because of her guilt, so that it is from דמה and not from דמם, as above 50, 30. And John adopted it in Rev. 18, 4: ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

FUGITE DE MEDIO BABYLONIS, ET SALVET QVISQVE ANIMAM SUAM) Hoc ad Ro- mam à Gotthis oppugnatam applicat Apocalypsis 18, 4. Implevit hæc verba Nabonidus. Fugit enim Babylone in Borsippa. Vide locum Berosi quem produximus ad li- brum tertium de veritate Religionis Christianæ.

NOLITE TACERE SUPER INIQVITATEM EJUS) Melius vertas : Ne succidamini propter culpam ejus, ut sit à דמה non à דמם, quomodo supra 50, 30. Et as- sumsit Johannes in Apoc. 18, 4. ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς.

## 51:7
Verse 7.

BABYLON IS A GOLDEN CUP IN THE HAND OF THE LORD, MAKING ALL THE EARTH DRUNK) The golden cup of Babylon in the hand of God (dispensing) makes all the earth drunk. That is, the very splendid society of Babylon drew many auxiliary peoples to destruction. By the cup is meant society. But indeed, as it is in the Oedipus of Seneca: Blood mixes with golden cups.

Juvenal: ---- no aconite is drunk from earthenware. Then fear those, when you take up jeweled cups, and the Setine wine will burn in broad gold. Thus, those allies of Babylon also drank poison from golden cups. See what we noted above 25, 15.

AND THEREFORE THEY ARE MOVED) Therefore they are insane. For great grief no less than wine takes away the mind from men, as we have already noted several times.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

CALIX AUREUS BABYLON IN MANU DO- MINI, INEBRIANS OMNEM TERRAM) Poculum aureum Babylonis Dei manu (dispensante) inebriat omnem terram.
