Id est, Babylonis societas valde splendida multos auxiliares populos in exitium traxit. Per calicem iniba- tur societas. At vero ut in Oedæo est Senecæ : Aurea miscet pocula sanguis.

Juvenalis: ---- nulla aconita bibuntur Fictilibus. Tunc illa time, cum pocula fumes Gemmata, & lato Setinum ardebit in auro. Sic illi etiam Babylonis socii ex calicibus aureis venenum biberunt. Vide quæ supra 25, 15.

ET IDEO COMMOTÆ SUNT) Ideo insaniunt. Nam & magnus dolor non minus quam vinum hominibus mentem adimit, ut jam aliquoties notavimus

## 51:8
Verse 8.

BABYLON IS SUDDENLY FALLEN, AND IS BROKEN) Truly suddenly, as we said 50, 8 and 23. This is taken from a similar prophecy of Isaiah 21, 9; the Apocalypse 14, 8 uses the same words concerning Rome.

HOWL OVER HER) That is, wail, as is accustomed to be done in mourning. θρηνεῖτε, as the Greeks have it here.

TAKE BALM FOR HER PAIN) Which was accustomed to be applied to wounds, as we said 8, 22 and 46, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SUBITO CECIDIT BABYLON, ET CONTRI- TA EST) Sane subito, ut diximus 50, 8. & 23. Sumptum hoc ex vaticinio simili Esaiæ 21, 9. iisdem verbis de Roma utitur Apocal. 14, 8.

ULULATE SUPER EAM) Id est, ejulate, ut in lu- ctu fieri solet. θρηνεῖτε, ut hic Græci.

TOLLITE RESINAM AD DOLOREM) Quæ ad vulnera adhiberi solebat, ut diximus 8, 22. & 46, 11.

## 51:9
Verse 9.

WE HAVE CURED BABYLON AND SHE IS NOT HEALED) Those allies will say this: we indeed devoted effort to save her, but she could not be saved.

LET US GO EVERYONE TO HIS OWN LAND) As above 50, 16.

HIS JUDGMENT HAS REACHED EVEN TO THE HEAVENS) His crimes. See Jonah 1, 2. Gen. 18, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

CURAVIMUS BABYLONEM ET NON EST SANATA) Hoc dicent illi auxiliares : dedimus quidem o- peram, ut eam servaremus : sed servari non potuit.

EAMUS UNUSQUISQUE IN TERRAM SUAM) Ut supra 50, 16.

PERVENIT USQUE AD COELOS JUDICIUM EJUS) Crimina ejus. Vide Jonam 1, 2. Gen. 18, 12.

## 51:10
Ver. 10.

THE LORD HAS BROUGHT FORTH OUR RIGHTEOUSNESSES) God shows our religion to be true. The deported Jews are speaking.

Concerning the righteousness imputed through faith, of which Jer. 23, 6. Is. 46, 13. ch. 48, 16. Am. 5, 24. the blessed Hülsemann explains not inconveniently, where there was also discussion of spiritual liberation in ch. 50, 20.

LET US DECLARE IN ZION THE WORK OF THE LORD OUR GOD) That is, let us exiles send word to those few who remain in Judea, so that they may know that God has done these such great things for our sake.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

PROTULIT DOMINUS JUSTITIAS NOSTRAS) Ostendit Deus religionem nostram esse veram. Loquun- tur Judæi deportati.

De justitia per fidem imputata, de qua Jerem. 23, 6. Ef. 46, 13. c. 48, 16. Am. 5, 24. explicat non incommode B. Hülsemann. ubi de spirituali libe- ratione actum fuit etiam cap. 50, 20.

NARREMUS IN SION OPUS DOMINI DEI NOSTRI) Id est, nos exsules mittamus ad illos paucos, qui in Judæa restant, ut norint Deum hæc tam magna fe- cisse nostri causa.

## 51:11
Ver. 11.

SHARPEN THE ARROWS, FILL THE QUIVERS) He addresses the Babylonians, as if he were saying: exert yourselves as much as you can, you will accomplish nothing. Similar above 46, 3.

In the Hebrew, for 'fill the quivers' it is 'gather the shields'. Compare 2 Chron. 23, 9. 2 Sam. 8, 7. Ez. 27, 11. Cant. 4, 4. as the Tigurines, Tremellius, Piscator, Castro, Giesler, Tirinus, Menochius, and the blessed Luther explain.

THE LORD HAS STIRRED UP THE SPIRIT OF THE KINGS OF THE MEDES) Of Cyrus, and of the princes who are with him.

THE VENGEANCE OF HIS TEMPLE) Above 50, 28.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ACUITE SAGITTAS, IMPLETE PHARE- TRAS) Alloquitur Babylonios, quasi dicat: molimini quantum potestis, nihil proficietis. Simile supra 46, 3.

In Ebr. pro implete pharetras est congregate clypeos. Conf. 2. Par. 23, 9. 2. Sam. 8, 7. Ez. 27, 11. Cant. 4, 4. uti exponunt Tigur. Tremell. Pisc. Ca- stro, Gieslerius, Tirin. Menoch. & B. Lutherus.

SUSCITAVIT DOMINUS SPIRITUM REGUM MEDORUM) Cyri, & principum qui cum ipso.

ULTIO TEMPLI SUI) Supra 50, 28.

## 51:12
Ver. 12.

UPON THE WALLS OF BABYLON LIFT UP A SIGN) You, O Babylonians, lift up signs from the walls; so that, if there are any outside the city who favor you, they may understand in what state things are.

INCREASE THE GUARD) Watchmen at the gates and walls.

STATION GUARDS) Arrange sentinels outside the gates.

PREPARE AMBUSHES) Send scouts there to explore the forces and plans of the enemy.

BECAUSE THE LORD HAS PLANNED AND IS DOING WHATEVER HE HAS SPOKEN AGAINST THE INHABITANTS OF BABYLON) There is a transposition here as well. The sense: do everything that you wish and are able. Nevertheless (for this is what כי גם signifies), what God has planned, and what He has spoken against the inhabitants of Babylon, He will bring to effect.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SUPER MUROS BABYLONIS LEVATE SI- GNUM) Vos ô Babylonii signa attollite è mœnibus; ut, si- qui extra urbem sint vobis faventes, intelligant quo loco res sint.

AUGETE CUSTODIAM) Vigiles in portis & mœ- nibus.

LEVATE CUSTODES) Disponite procubitores ex- tra portas.

PRÆPARATE INSIDIAS) Mittite eo speculatores, qui hostium vires ac consilia explorent.

QUIA COGITAVIT DOMINUS ET FACIT QUÆCUNQUE LOCUTUS EST CONTRA HA- BITATORES BABYLONIS) Est hic quoque transpo- sitio. Sensus: omnia facite quæ vultis & potestis. Attamen (hoc enim valet כי גם) quæ cogitavit Deus, quæque elo- cutus est contra habitatores Babylonis, dabit effectui.

## 51:13
Verse 13.

YOU WHO DWELL UPON MANY WATERS)

By the Euphrates, the huge trenches, the great lake, concerning which see Abydenus and Herodotus. Here also in שכנתי the Jod is added.

YOUR END HAS COME, THE MEASURE OF YOUR COVETOUSNESS) Your destruction has come, which is the measure (that is, the retribution) of your covetousness. בצע is covetousness, also in Exodus 18:21. The Greeks, for אמת בצעך, read אמן במערך.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

QUÆ HABITAS SUPER AQUAS MULTAS)

Ad Euphratem, fossas ingentes, lacum magnum, de qui- bus vide Abydenum & Herodotum. Hic quoque in שכנתי Jod est adjectitium.

VENIT FINIS TUUS, PEDALIS PRÆCISIO- NIS TUÆ) Venit exitium tuum, quæ est mensura (id est, retributio) avaritiæ tuæ. בצע avaritia etiam Exodi 18, 21. Græci pro אמת בצעך legere אמן במערך.

## 51:14
Verse 14.

THE LORD OF HOSTS HAS SWORN BY HIS OWN SOUL) καθ' ἑαυτοῦ, as the writer to the Hebrews 6:13 interprets this expression.

I WILL FILL YOU WITH MEN AS WITH THE BRUCHUS) The bruchus is a specific kind of locust, as Jerome notes on Nahum 3. Those creatures invade lands in a huge swarm, as that very passage of Nahum shows. See also shortly at 27.

AND A SHOUT SHALL BE SUNG OVER THEE) That is, a triumph.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

JURAVIT DOMINUS EXERCITUUM PER ANIMAM SUAM) καθ' ἑαυτῦ ut hanc locutionem inter- pretatur scriptor ad Hebræos 6, 13.

REPLEBO TE HOMINIBUS QUASI BRUCHO) Bruclus genus est proprium locustarum, ut Hieronymus notat ad 3. Nahum. Ea animantia ingenti agmine terras in- vadunt, ut is ipse locus Nahumi ostendit, Vide & mox 27.

ET SUPER TE CELEUSMA CANTABITUR) Id est, triumphus.

## 51:15
Ver. 15.

WHO MADE THE EARTH BY HIS STRENGTH) He, of course, is the one who says these things, so that you may not doubt that he is able to fulfill them.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

QUI FECIT TERRAM IN FORTITUDINE SUA) Is scilicet est qui hæc dicit, ne dubitetis quin implere possit.

## 51:16
Ver. 16.

WHEN HE UTTERS HIS VOICE, THE WATERS ARE MULTIPLIED IN THE HEAVENS) He repeats these things from chapter 10, 13 above.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

DANTE EO VOCEM, MULTIPLICANTUR AQVÆ IN COELO) Repetit hæc ex capite 10, 13. supra.

## 51:20
Ver. 20.

YOU DASH MY WEAPONS OF WAR) You (Cyrus) are for me like a crushing hammer, like weapons of war. See above 50, 23.

I WILL DASH NATIONS IN YOU) In you, a Hebrew idiom, for by you.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

COLLIDIS TU MIHI VASA BELLI) Tu (Cy- re) mihi pro malleo frangente, pro armis bellicis. Vide supra 50, 23.

EGO COLLIDAM IN TE GENTES) In te, lo- cutio Hebræa, pro per te.

## 51:24
Ver. 24.

AND I WILL REPAY BABYLON) Repeat here that [phrase] by you.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET REDDAM BABYLONI) Repete hic illud per te.

## 51:25
Ver. 25.

BEHOLD I AM AGAINST YOU) Supply, I come, as above 50, 31.

PESTILENTIAL MOUNTAIN THAT CORRUPTEST THE WHOLE EARTH) Babylon is called a mountain, on account of its lofty palace, and as Berosus speaks, very similar to mountains. Pestilential, because it had been a destruction to many nations.

It is not called a mountain from its situation, because it was situated on a plain, nor from its form, but from its power, by a received Hebrew phrase.

I WILL ROLL THEE DOWN FROM THE ROCKS) That is, from thy walls rising two hundred royal cubits in height. Herodotus, Strabo, Diodorus Siculus, and Pliny teach this.

AND I WILL MAKE THEE A MOUNTAIN OF BURNING) That thou mayest be like Etna, and other mountains vomiting fire.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

ECCE EGO AD TE) Supple, venio, ut supra 50, 31.

MONS PESTIFER QUI CORRUMPIS UNI- VERSAM TERRAM) Babylon mons dicitur, ob regiam sublimem, & ut Berosus loquitur, montibus persimilem. Pestifer, quod multis gentibus exitio fuisset.

Non à situ mons dicitur, quia in planitie sita erat, nec à forma, sed à potentia sua phrasi E- bræa recepta.

EVOLVAM TE DE PETRIS) Id est, de muris tuis ducentos cubitos regios in altitudinem assurgentibus. Docent in Herodotus, Strabo, Diodorus Siculus, Pli- nius.

ET DABO TE IN MONTEM COMBUSTIO- NIS) Ut sis Ætnæ similis, aliisque montibus ignem vo- mentibus.

## 51:26
Vers. 26.

THEY SHALL NOT TAKE OF THEE A STONE FOR A CORNER AND A STONE FOR FOUNDATIONS) No stones useful for building will remain for thee. The Chaldean thinks that by the corner stone the king is signified, and by the foundations the prince. Thus in the Church Christ is the corner stone, the Apostles the foundations.

PERDITION FOR EVER) Thou shalt be desolate for a long time. For we have often noted that עולם is taken in that way.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

NON TOLLENT DE TE LAPIDEM IN AN- GULUM ET LAPIDEM IN FUNDAMENTA) Nulli lapides ædificio utiles tibi restabunt. Chaldæus per lapidem angularem regem significari putat, per fundamenta princi- pem. Sic in Ecclesia Christus lapis angularis, Apostoli fun- damenta.

PERDITUS IN ÆTERNUM) Desolatus eris lon- go tempore. Nam ita עולם sumi sæpe notavimus.

## 51:27
Vers. 27.

LIFT UP A STANDARD IN THE LAND) Raise up the sign of war: That is, Ye angels, animate all those nations to war.

SOUND THE TRUMPET AMONG THE NATIONS) The same sense in another translation.

SANCTIFY THE NATIONS AGAINST HER) Prepare the nations against her. Thus the Chaldean here. We have already often had קדש in that sense.

PROCLAIM AGAINST HER) Stir up against her.

REGIBUS ARARATH) The kings of the Cordyæi. קרדו here is Chaldean, as also in the history of the flood, as we said in the annotations to book 1 of the truth of the Christian Religion. By kings, understand both kings and princes.

MENIN) Those who are in Minyas. See the passage of Damascus in the same annotations. Hence Armenia seems to be called ארם מני, the Syria of Minyas. For Strabo notes that Armenia was once included under the Aramean name. The Chaldean here has חורמני, the cavern of Minyas. Thus the Chaldeans call Armenia, because it is enclosed by mountains. It touches Media, as Pliny notes, and their kings were with Cyrus, as we noted in 50, 41.

AND ASCENEZ) The Jerusalem interpreter renders this name by the word Asia in Genesis. In it is Ascania, a part of Phrygia and Mysia, and other places of the same name, which we have collected in the aforementioned annotations. And I think this is true, although the Chaldean in this place has placed חדיב, which is in the Talmudic הדיב, that is, Adjabene; Onkelos in Genesis [has] Carmania, for which the Rabbis perversely understood Germany.

NUMBER AGAINST HER TAPHSAR) Appoint a Satrap over her: make it so that from a kingdom it becomes a satrapy. It is frequent for the Hebrews to transpose letters in foreign words, as we noted at Mark 14:3. And so from Satrapa was made Taphsar here and in Nahum 3:17. The Persians called them אחשדרפנים as can be seen in Esther 9:13. Hence Theopompus made ἐξατράπην: other Greeks [made] σατράπην, as we said at Matthew 18:10. And because angels, as we said in the same place, are like Satraps of God: therefore the word טפסר is also used for Satrap by Jonathan at Deuteronomy 28:12. Which appears by comparing the same place of Jonathan at Genesis 30:22.

BRING THE HORSE AS A PRICKLY LOCUST) Bring (supply against him, which the Greeks add here) the horse like a bristling locust. Enallage of the singular for the plural. סמר is to devastate; but to put ס for ש is a Chaldaism. Locusts devastate lands, Nahum 3:1, Joel 1:4, 11, 25. The Chaldean horsemen did the same.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

LEVATE SIGNUM IN TERRA Belli signum attollite: Id est, Vos angeli omnes illas gentes ad bellum animate.

CLANGITE BUCCINA IN GENTIBUS) Idem sensus alia translatione.

SANCTIFICATE SUPER EAM GENTES) Præ- parate contra eam gentes. Ita hic Chaldæus. Habuimus jam sæpe קדש eo sensu.

ANNUNCIATE CONTRA ILLAM) Concitate contra eam.

REGIBUS ARARATH) Reges Cordyæos. קרדו hic Chaldæus, ut & in diluvii historia, sicut diximus in an- notatis ad librum 1. de veritate Religionis Christianæ. Re- ges intellige, tum reges, tum principes.

MENIN) Qui in Minyade. Vide Damasceni locum in iisdein annotatis. Hinc dicta videtur Armenia, ארם מני Syria Minyados. Nam Armeniam sub nomine Aramæo olim comprehensam notat Strabo. Chaldæus hic habet חורמני cavernam Minyados. Sic Chaldæi Armeniam vo- cant, quia montibus clauditur. Tangit Mediam, ut Pli- nius notat, & reges eorum cum Cyro fuere, ut notavi- mus 50, 41.

ET ASCENEZ) Hoc nomen voce Asiæ reddit Hie- rosolymitanus interpres ad Genesin. In ea est Ascania pars Phrygiæ & Mysiæ, & alia loca paris nominis, quæ con- geffimus in dictis annotatis. Idque verum puto, quan- quam Chaldæus hoc loco posuit חדיב, quæ Thalmudicis הדיב, id est, Adjabene, Onkelos in Genesi Carmaniam pro qua Germaniam perverse intellexerunt Rabbini.

NVMERATE CONTRA EAM TAPHSAR) Præficite ei Satrapam : facite ut ex regno satrapia fiat. Fre- quens est Hebræis in barbaris vocibus literas transpone- re, ut notavimus ad Marcum 14, 3. Itaque ex Satrapa fa- ctum est Taphsar hic & Nahumi 3, 17. Persæ eos vocabant אחשדרפנים ut videre est Esther 9, 13. Hinc ἐξατράπην fecit Theopompus : Græci alii σατράπην, ut diximus ad Matth. 18, 10. Et quia angeli, ut ibidem diximus, sunt ve- luti Satrapæ Dei: Ideo vox טפסר etiam pro Satrapa poni- tur à Jonathane ad Deuteron. 28, 12. Quod apparet col- lato ejusdem Jonathanis loco ad Gen. 30, 22.

ADDVCITE EQVVM QVASI BRVCHVM ACVLEATVM) Adducite (supple contra eum, quod hic addunt Græci) equum veluti bruchum hastantem. E- nallage singularis pro plurali. סמר est vastare; pro שׁ au- tem ponere ס est Chaldaismus. Bruchi terras devastant Nahum 3, 1. Joel. 1, 4. 11. 25. Idem faciebant Chaldæi equites.

## 51:28
Verse 28.

KINGS OF MEDIA) The king and the princes as above [in chapter] 27.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

REGES MEDIÆ) Regem ac principes ut su- pra 27.

## 51:29
Verse 29.

THE EARTH SHALL BE MOVED AND SHALL BE TROUBLED) The earth, moved (Chaldean), shall grieve. BECAUSE THE THOUGHT OF THE LORD SHALL AWAKE AGAINST BABYLON) When the thought of the Lord shall be established (that is, shall have its outcome) against Babylon.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

COMMOVEBITVR TERRA ET CONTVR- BABITVR) Terra commota (Chaldaica) dolebit. QVIA EVIGILABIT CONTRA BABYLONEM COGITATIO DOMINI) Cum firmabitur (id est, even- tum habebit) contra Babylonem cogitatio Domini.

## 51:30
Verse 30.

THE MIGHTY MEN OF BABYLON HAVE CEASED FROM BATTLE) They did not dare to defend the city. THEY HAVE DWELT IN STRONGHOLDS) In fortified places. That is, they retreated into Borsippa, a fortified city. See the passage of Berosus. THEIR STRENGTH IS DEVOURED) Their fortitude failed. THEY ARE BECOME AS WOMEN) Fearful, as above 50:37. HER TABERNACLES ARE BURNT) Houses, as the Chaldean [has] here. HER BARS ARE BROKEN) They are shattered. By bars understand the gates.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

CESSAVERVNT FORTES BABYLONIS A PRÆLIO) Non ausi sunt urbem defendere. HABITAVERVNT IN PRÆSIDIIS) In locis mu- nitis. Id est, receperunt se in Borsippa urbem munitam. Vide Berosi locum. DEVORATVM EST ROBVR EORVM) Defecit eorum fortitudo. FACTI SVNT QVASI MVLIERES) Pavidi, ut supra 50, 37. INCENSA SVNT TABERNACVLA EJVS) Domus, ut hic Chaldæus. CONTRITI SVNT VECTES EJVS) Fracti sunt. Per vectes portas intellige.

## 51:31
Verse 31.

ONE RUNNER SHALL COME TO MEET ANOTHER, AND A MESSENGER TO MEET A MESSENGER) Messengers of evil things shall follow one another. TO ANNOUNCE TO THE KING OF BABYLON THAT HIS CITY IS TAKEN FROM END TO END) In the Hebrew: from the end. That is, in one part, περὶ τὰ ἔσχατα τῆς πόλιος, as Herodotus [says]: which those who were with the king in the middle of the city did not yet know, as we just reported from the same Herodotus and Aristotle.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

CVRRENS OBVIAM CVRRENTI VENIET, ET NVNCIVS OBVIAM NVNCIANTI) Nuncii rerum malarum aliis alios consequentur. VT ANNVNCIET REGI BABYLONIS QVIA CAPTA EST CIVITAS EJVS A SVMMO VSQVE AD SVMMVM) In Hebræo : à fine. Id est, in una parte περὶ τὰ ἔσχατα τῆς πόλιος, ut Herodotus: quod adhuc nesciebant illi qui cum rege in media erant urbe, ut ex eo- dem Herodoto & Aristotele modo retulimus.

## 51:32
Verse 32.

AND THE FORDS ARE SEIZED) A passage was found through the diverted channel of the Euphrates. AND THE MARSHES ARE SET ON FIRE WITH FIRE) That is, the fortifications, τὰ ἕλεη, of which ἕλεη Herodotus makes mention. Those fortifications are τὰ ἔξω τῆς πόλεως τείχη, according to Berosus.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ET VADA PRÆOCCVPATA SVNT) Inventus transitus per abacti Euphratis alveum. ET PALVDES INCENSÆ SVNT IGNI) Id est, munimenta, τὰ ἕλεη, cujus ἕλεη meminit Herodotus. Ea munimenta sunt τὰ ἔξω τῆς πόλεως τείχη, Beroso.

## 51:33
Verse 33.

DAUGHTER OF BABYLON AS A THRESHING FLOOR: THE TIME OF HER THRESHING: YET A LITTLE WHILE: AND THE TIME OF HER HARVEST WILL COME) Distinguish and translate these thus: Daughter of Babylon as a threshing floor. The time for her threshing is yet a little while, for the time of her harvest has arrived. The harvest is the slaughter of the citizens. The threshing which follows the harvest is the dissipation of the city.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

FILIA BABYLONIS QVASI AREA: TEMPVS TRITVRÆ EJVS: ADHVC MODICVM: ET VE- NIET TEMPVS MESSIONIS EJVS) Hæc sic distingue, & verte: Filia Babylonis quasi area. Tempus ad trituram ejus adhuc modicum, nam adventavit tempus messionis ejus. Mes- sis est interfectio civium. Tritura quæ messem sequitur, dis- sipatio urbis.

## 51:34
Verse 34.

HE HAS EATEN ME, HE HAS DEVORED ME NEBUCHADNEZZAR) Jerusalem is speaking, as will immediately appear. HE HAS SWALLOWED ME AS A DRAGON) As a whale. HE HAS FILLED HIS BELLY WITH MY DELICACY) With my delights. AND HE HAS CAST ME OUT) He has vomited me out. That is, after he filled all his storehouses with my goods, afterwards he drove me out from this land. Thus the Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

COMEDIT ME, DEVORAVIT ME NABVCHO- DONOSOR) Loquitur Jerusalem, ut statim apparebit. ABSORBVIT ME QVASI DRACO) Quasi balæna. REPLEVIT VENTREM SVVM TENERITVDI- NE MEA) Deliciis meis. ET EIEGIT ME) Evomuit me. Id est, postquam omnes apothecas suas implevit bonis meis, postea me ex hac terra depulit. Ita Chaldæus.

## 51:35
Verse 35.

INIQUITY AGAINST ME, AND MY FLESH UPON BABYLON) For my flesh, put my flesh. The sense is: may the evil which Babylon has brought upon me and my other fellow-citizens come upon her herself.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

INIQVITAS ADVERSVM ME, ET CARO MEA SVPER BABYLONEM) Pro caro mea, pone car- nem meam. Senfus est: malum quod Babylon mihi & aliis popularibus meis intulit, ipsi superveniat.

## 51:36
Verse 36.

Verse 37. AND BABYLON SHALL BE INTO MOUNDS) Isaiah 25, 2.

Vers. 37. ET ERIT BABYLON IN TUMULOS) Esaias 25, 2.

## 51:38
Verse 38.

AS LIONS THEY SHALL ROAR, THEY SHALL SHAKE THEIR MANES LIKE LION'S WHELPS) In the Hebrew: They shall roar like the whelps of lionesses: That is, they shall celebrate the feast with a great clamor at that very time when the city is captured. Herodotus: τυχεῖν γάρ σφι ἐοῦσαν ὀρτήν.

They are more correctly said to be about to roar on account of distress, Ps. 38, 9. because this treats of the afflictions of Babylon, as Arias, Maldonatus, Castro, Saa, Cornelius, Gislerus, and B. Luther explain.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

SIMUL UT LEONES RUGIENT, EXCU- TIENT COMAS VELUTI CATULI LEONUM) In Hebræo: Frement ut catuli leanarum: Id est, magno clamo- re festum agent diem eo ipso tempore, cum urbs capietur. Herodotus: τυχεῖν γάρ σφι ἐοῦσαν ὀρτήν.

Rectius præ ægritudine rugituri dicuntur, Ps. 38, 9. quia de afflictionibus Babyl. hic agitur, ut Arias, Maldon. Castro, Saa. Cornel. Gislerus. & B. Luther. explicant.

## 51:39
Verse 39.

IN THEIR HEAT) That is, when they have become heated with wine. For they were accustomed to hold banquets on feast days: and Xenophon narrates that this happened in Babylon when the city was captured. Herodotus says they were in ἐμπαθείῃσιν.

I WILL SET THEIR DRINKS, AND I WILL MAKE THEM DRUNK) I will give them something else to drink, and from which they may be made drunk: the cup of my wrath as in Isaiah 51, 17. and following. See above 25, 15. and following. 49, 11. Lamentations 4, 21.

THAT THEY MAY SLEEP) So also the Greeks: ὅπως καρωθῶσι. They read, of course, not יעלזו which is 'they shall exult,' as we have it, but ועלפו, just as the Chaldean also reads.

AND THEY SHALL SLEEP AN EVERLASTING SLEEP) The sleep of death. The Chaldean refers these things in a more sublime sense to the second death. They shall die, he says, the second death, and shall not live in the world to come. Compare Revelation 20, 6. 14. 21, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

IN CALORE EORUM) Id est, ubi vino incalue- rint. Solebant enim diebus festis convivia agitari: & hoc Babylone factum, cum urbs caperetur narrat Xenophon. Fuisse eos in ἐμπαθείῃσιν Herodotus.

PONAM POTUS EORUM, ET INEBRIABO EOS) Dabo illis aliud quod bibant, & unde inebrientur: calicem iræ meæ ut Esa. 51, 17. & sequentibus. Supra 25, 15. & sequentibus. 49, 11. Thren. 4, 21.

UT SOPIANTUR) Sic & Græci: ὅπως καρωθῶσι. Legerunt scilicet, non יעלזו quod est exsultent, ut nos ha- bemus, sed ועלפו, quomodo & Chaldæus legit.

ET DORMIANT SOMNUM SEMPITERNUM) Somnum mortis. Chaldæus sensu sublimiore hæc refert ad mortem secundam. Moriantur, ait, morte secunda, & non vivant in sæculo futuro. Confer. Apoc. 20, 6. 14. 21, 8.

## 51:40
Verse 40.

I WILL BRING THEM DOWN LIKE LAMBS TO THE SLAUGHTER, AND LIKE RAMS WITH THE KIDS) There is a transposition: I will bring them down to the slaughter, as lambs, rams, and he-goats are led. But for כרים the Chaldean reads שרים bulls.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

DEDUCAM EOS QVASI AGNOS AD VICTI- MAM, ET QVASI ARIETES CUM HOEDIS) Est transpositio: Deducam eos ad occisionem, sicut ducuntur a- gni, arietes, hirci. Sed pro כרים Chaldæus legit שרים tauri.

## 51:46
Verse 46.

AND LEST PERCHANCE YOUR HEART GROW SOFT, AND YOU FEAR THE REPORT THAT SHALL BE HEARD IN THE LAND) I do not want you, he says, to flee immediately at the first rumor of war. I will tell you the time.

A REPORT SHALL COME IN ONE YEAR) In the first year there will be a rumor that Cyrus is preparing war against the Babylonians.

AND AFTER THIS YEAR A REPORT) With Cyrus already having advanced into Assyria and tearing the river Gyndes into many streams.

AND INIQUITY IN THE LAND) In the third year the land of Babylon shall bear its punishments, which the Hebrews call חמס, as can be seen in Psalm 7:17.

AND RULER OVER RULER) That is, Cyrus shall expel Nabonidus.

Balthasar is predicted to be conquered by Cyrus: as Theodor., Hugo, Lyr., Dionysius & Luther, who is Nabonidus Dan. 5, 3. Verse 47. THEREFORE BEHOLD THE DAYS COME, AND I WILL VISIT UPON THE GRAVEN IMAGES OF BABYLON) Clarius thus: Because then (in that third year) the time will have come when I shall take vengeance upon the idols of Babylon. AND ALL HER LAND SHALL BE CONFOUNDED) That is, it shall have no strength. AND ALL HER SLAIN SHALL FALL IN THE MIDST OF HER) You will translate better: And all her dancers shall fall in the midst of her. Thus חלל is taken in Jud. 21, 21. 23. 1 Sam. 18, 6. 21, 11. 1 Kings 1, 40. In which places the Greeks have placed χορεύειν. Herodotus, however, where he describes Babylon as captured by Cyrus: 'For it happened that there was a festival for them, and they were dancing at that time and were in luxury.' Verse 48. AND THEY SHALL PRAISE OVER BABYLON) Because of Babylon they shall praise, namely God. THE HEAVENS) The angels. AND THE EARTH) The Jews and other nations badly treated by the Chaldeans. FOR FROM THE NORTH SHALL COME SPOILERS TO HER) When from the North shall come destroyers to her. For that is properly שודדים. Verse 49. AS BABYLON HATH CAUSED, THAT THE SLAIN SHOULD FALL IN ISRAEL) The justice of God is shown, for which praises and thanks will deservedly be sung to Him. SO FROM BABYLON SHALL FALL THE SLAIN IN ALL THE EARTH) Namely the Chaldean. Verse 50. YE THAT HAVE FLED THE SWORD) You Jews, when according to these warnings you shall have fled from Babylon for fear of the Persian sword. COME, DO NOT STAND) Go as far away as possible. REMEMBER FROM AFAR THE LORD, AND LET JERUSALEM ASCEND INTO YOUR HEART) Meanwhile, while fleeing, be mindful of the temple and the city, and say among yourselves: what follows. Verse 51. WE ARE CONFOUNDED BECAUSE WE HAVE HEARD OUR REPROACH) We were ashamed as often as the Chaldeans cast our servitude in our teeth. SHAME HATH COVERED OUR FACES: FOR STRANGERS HAVE COME UPON THE SANCTIFICATION OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) But especially when they cast in our teeth that they had burned the temple, as if our religion were a thing of nothing. Verse 52. THEREFORE) Because of these complaints of the Jews. THE DAYS COME SAITH THE LORD) they are approaching. AND I WILL VISIT UPON HER GRAVEN IMAGES) That I may exercise vengeance upon their gods, and show that I indeed have punished those who had neglected me, but that those gods were unable to provide salvation to those who had worshipped them as much as possible. AND IN ALL THE LAND THE WOUNDED SHALL GROAN) Everywhere the wounded shall lie groaning. Verse 53. IF BABYLON SHOULD ASCEND INTO HEAVEN) Even if it should ascend. An exaggeration. AND SHOULD STRENGTHEN THE POWER OF HER STRENGTH IN THE HIGH) If she should make for herself fortresses in the highest part of heaven. Verse 55. HE HATH DESTROYED FROM HER THE GREAT VOICE) He has taken away their roaring. AND THEIR WAVES SHALL SOUND AS MANY WATERS) Their calamities shall cause them to emit a far different sound, such as waves mourning the shores. See above v. 42. Verse 56. THE SPOILER) The destroyer, as above. HER STRONG MEN ARE TAKEN) They are caught, when they least thought of it. AND THEIR BOW HATH WITHERED) That is, their strength is broken. Verse 57. I WILL MAKE DRUNK HER PRINCES) Thus above 49, 39. and here 23. AND THEY SHALL SLEEP A PERPETUAL SLEEP) See above v. 39. Verse 58. THIS BROADEST WALL OF BABYLON SHALL BE DUG UP WITH DIGGING) In the Hebrew: Walls, for there were three walls surrounding the inner city, and as many the outer, as Berosus teaches us. But 'broadest' is well added. For they were fifty cubits thick, as we learn from Herodotus, Strabo, Diodorus Siculus; Pliny says they were fifty feet wide, by each foot three fingers larger in measure than the Roman one.

Vers. 46.

ET NE FORTE MOLLESCAT COR VESTRUM, ET TIMEATIS AVDITUM QVI AVDIETUR IN TERRA) Nolo, inquit, ad primum rumorem belli sta- tim fugiatis. Dicam vobis tempus.

VENIET IN VNO ANNO AVDITIO) Primo anno erit rumor Cyrum parare bellum in Babylonios.

PROPTEREA ECCE DIES VENIVNT, ET VISITABO SVPER SCVLPTILIA BABYLONIS) Clarius sic : Quia tunc (tertio illo anno) venerit tempus quo vindictam sum sumturus de idolis Babylonis. ET OMNIS TERRA EJVS CONFVNDETVR) Id est, nihil virium habebit. ET VNIVERSI INTERFECTI EJVS CADENT IN MEDIO EJVS ) Melius vertes : Et omnes saltatores ejus in medio ejus cadent. QVI FVGISTIS GLADIVM) Vos Judæi, ubi secun- dum hæc monita fugeritis è Babylone metu gladii Persici. VENITE, NOLITE STARE) Ite quam longis- sime. RECORDAMINI PROCUL DOMINI, ET JE- RVSALEM ASCENDAT IN COR VESTRVM) In- terim fugientes estote memores templi & urbis, ac dicite apud vos : quæ sequuntur. Vers. 51. ET VISITABO SVPER SCVLPTILIA EJVS) Ut vindictam exerceam de eorum diis, & ostendam me qui- dam puniisse qui me neglexerant, illos autem deos salutem præstare nequisse iis, qui ipsos quam maxime coluerant. ET IN OMNI TERRA MVGIET VVLNERA- TVS) Ubique jacebunt saucii gementes. Vers. 53. SI ACCENDERIT BABYLON IN COELUM) Etiamsi ascenderet. Exaggeratio. ET FIRMAVERIT IN EXCELSO ROBVR SVVM) Arces sibi in summa cœli parte faceret. Vers. 55. PERDIDIT EX EA VOCEM MAGNAM) Ron- chos illis abitulit. ET SONABVNT FLVCTVS EORVM QVASI AQVÆ MVLTÆ) Calamitates ipsorum efficient, ut lon- ge alium edant sonum, qualem plangentes littora fluctus. Vide supra v. 42. Vers. 56. PRÆDO) Vastator, ut supra. APPREHENSI SVNT FORTES EJVS) Depre- hensi sunt, cum minime id cogitarent. ET EMARCVIT ARCVS EORVM) Id est, fra- ctæ vires. Vers. 57. INEBRIABO PRINCIPES EJVS) Sic supra 49, 39. & hic 23. ET DORMIENT SOMNVM SEMPITERNVM) Vide supra v. 39. Vers. 58. MVRVS BABYLONIS ISTE LATISSIMVS SVFFOSSIONE SVFFODIETVR) In Hebræo : Muri, Erant enim terna mœnia circumdata urbi interiori, exteriori totidem, ut Berosus nos docet. Bene autem additum latissi- mi. Crassi enim erant quinquaginta cubitos, ut ex Herodo- to, Strabone, Diodoro Siculo discimus, Plinius dicit latos fuisse quinquagenos pedes, in singulos pedes tribus digitis mensura ampliore, quam erat Romana.

## 51:58
AND HER HIGH GATES SHALL BE BURNED WITH FIRE) See above v. 30.

AND THE LABOURS OF THE PEOPLES TO NOTHING, AND OF THE NATIONS SHALL BE IN THE FIRE AND THEY SHALL PERISH) That last word signifies rather, they are wearied. But there is a transposition, which will be best explained thus: The labours of the peoples and nations which wearied themselves (by building the wall) shall fall into nothing through fire.

Latin:

ET PORTÆ EJUS EXCELSÆ IGNI COMBU- RENTUR) Vide supra v. 30.

ET LABORES POPULORUM AD NIHILUM, ET GENTIUM IN IGNEM ERUNT ET DISPE- RIBUNT) Postremum illud magis significat, lassati sunt. Est autem transpositio, quæ sic optime exponetur: Labo- res populorum & gentium quæ se fatigarunt (muro struendo) in nihilum per ignem recident.

## 51:59
Verse 59.

WHEN HE WENT WITH SEDECIA THE KING INTO BABYLON) The particle אֵת often signifies 'from', as Gen. 44, 4. Therefore translate: When he himself went from Sedecia the king (sent, that is) to Babylon. Thus the LXX, παρὰ Σεδεκίυ. The Chaldean in the same sense in the embassy of Sedecia.

Why not with Sedekia? That meaning of the particle is certainly more common, which the Vulgate and B. Luther expressed.

IN THE FOURTH YEAR OF HIS REIGN) This is not added rashly, so that it may appear that the ruin of Babylon was predicted by Jeremiah a full six years before the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem, and this prediction was consigned in writing and at the same time by a certain conspicuous action.

We have spoken before about the chronology and sense of this passage.

BUT SARAIAS WAS PRINCE OF PROPHECY) Both the Greeks and the Chaldean did not read מְנוּחָה, but מִנְחָה. For they translate ἄρχων δώρων, prince of gifts: that is, he was the companion of sacred largesses. מִנְחָה μανὰὰ is indeed often taken for a gift which is offered to God, but it is also used for that which men give to men, as Gen. 32, 13. 20. 21. 2 Kings 8, 18. Psalm 45, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 59.

CUM PERGERET CUM SEDECIA REGE IN BABYLONEM) אֵת particula sæpe à significat, ut Gen. 44, 4. Itaque verte: Cum ipse iret à Sedecia rege (missus scilicet) Babylonem. Sic LXX. παρὰ Σεδεκίυ. Chaldæus eodem sensu in legatione Sedeciæ.

Cur non cum Sedekia? Usitatior certe est illa particulæ significatio, quam Vulgatus, & B. Lu- therus expressit.

IN ANNO QVARTO REGNI EJUS) Non teme- re id adjectum est, ut appareat Babylonis ruinam ab Jere- mia prædictam totis sex annis antequam Babylonii Hiero- solyma exscinderent, & hanc prædictionem, scripto simul- que conspicua quadam actione consignatam.

De Chronologia & sensu hujus loci diximus antea.

SARAIAS AUTEM ERAT PRINCEPS PRO- PHETIÆ) Et Græci & Chaldæus non מְנוּחָה legerunt, sed מִנְחָה. Vertunt enim ἄρχων δώρων, princeps munerum: id est, fuit comes sacrarum largitionum. מִנְחָה μανὰὰ sæ- pe quidem sumitur de munere, quod Deo offertur, sed & de eo quod homines hominibus dant usurpatur, ut Gen. 32, 13. 20. 21. 2. Reg. 8, 18. Psalm. 45, 13.

THAT THERE BE NONE TO DWELL IN IT) So that no one is to dwell in it.

NE SIT QVI IN EO HABITET) Ita ut nemo in eo sit habitaturus.

ET PROJICIES ILLUM IN MEDIUM EU- PHRATEM ET DICES: SIC SVBMERGETVR BA- BYLON, ET NON CONSVRGET) Simile illud Ho- ratii:

THUS SHALL SINK) With calamities. See above 55.

THUS FAR THE WORDS OF JEREMIAH) This is a closing clause pertaining not only to this part, but to the whole book: as will appear from those things which we shall now say.

HVCVSQVE VERBA JEREMIÆ) Hæc est clausula non ad hanc tantum partem, sed ad totum librum perti- nens: ut apparebit ex iis quæ jam dicemus.

## 52:1 Argument
CHAPTER LII. & the last. A description of the destruction of the holy city, the captivity of Zedekiah, the burning of the temple, the devastation of the city, the abduction of the people and the vessels and the priests: the various transportations, and the sum of those abducted in them. Finally, the exaltation of Evil-merodach brought out of prison.

Verse 1.

ZEDEKIAH WAS TWENTY-ONE YEARS OLD) It ought to be held for certain that this chapter was not added to this place by Jeremiah: for he would not have repeated in the same book a history already set forth, and indeed in its proper place in chapters XXXV and XL. Furthermore, this history is woven on to the reign of Evil-merodach and even to the end of Jeconiah, which are times posterior to Jeremiah. Wherefore it ought not to be doubted that the leaders of the captives in the Babylonian kingdom, whom they called רָאשֵׁי גָלִיּוֹת αἰχμαλωτάρχας, wrote these things, so that there might be an εἰσαγωγὴ to the book which was accustomed to follow the Prophecies of Jeremiah; that is, to the Lamentations of Jeremiah. For the argument of those dirges is contained in these words, which are almost all taken from the end of the latter book of Kings, with some things added from the history of the temple built by Solomon. A son of XXI years, for, born XXI years. A Hebraism sufficiently well known. These first three verses are taken from the end of chapter XXIV of 1 and 2 Kings.

The words of Jeremiah chapter 51. The prophecies are concluded, the fulfillment of which, concerning the principal prophecy regarding the Jews, is historically appended in the last chapter; or up to this point are the words of Jeremiah against Babel, as in chapters 48 and 47. That the last chapter was not added by Jeremiah, but by another, although Paulus Burgensis and Christophorus à Castro think so, most interpreters nevertheless disagree. A few things touched upon above are here fully recounted. If anything was added by another, verses 31, 32, 33, 34 were added.

Latin:

CAPUT LII. & postremum. Descriptio excidii urbis sanctæ, captivitas Se- deciæ, templi exustio, urbis vastatio, populi & vasorum ac sacerdotum abductio: di- versæ transportationes, & abductorum in iis summa. Denique Evilmerodachi ex carcere educti exaltatio.

Vers. 1.

FILIVS VIGINTI ET VNIVS ANNI ERAT SEDE- CIAS) Pro certo haberi debet, hoc caput non fuisse ab Je- remia huic loco additum: neque enim in eodem libro repe- tiisset historiam ante positam, & quidem suo loco c. XXXV. & XL. Præterea pertexitur hæc historia ad regnum Evil- meradachi & finem usque Jechoniæ, quæ posteriora sunt temporibus Jeremiæ. Quare dubitari non debet, quin pri- mores captivorum in regno Babylonico, quos vocabant רָאשֵׁי גָלִיּוֹת αἰχμαλωτάρχας, hæc scripserint, ut esset εἰσό- γαγὴ ad librum, qui sequi Prophetias Jeremiæ solebat; id est, ad Threnos Jeremiæ. Argumentum enim illorum planctuum his verbis continetur, quæ desumpta sunt fere omnia ex fine posterioris libri Regum, additis quibusdam ex historia structi à Salomone templi. Filius annorum XXI. pro, annos natus XXI. Hebraismus notus satis. Prima hæc tria commata sumpta de fine capitis XXIV, 1, 2, Regum.

Verba Jeremiæ cap. 51. Prophetica conclu- duntur, quorum complementum quoad vatici- nium præcipuum Judæos concernens historice cap. ultimo subjungitur; vel hucusque verba Jeremiæ contra Babel, ut cap. 48, 47. Postremum caput à Jeremia additum non esse, sed ab alio etsi censeant Paulus Burgensis & Christophorus à Castro, dissen- tiunt tamen plerique interpretes. Pauca quædam supra tacta sunt, quæ hic plene recensentur. Si quid adjectum ab alio, vers. 31. 32. 33. 34. adjecti sunt.
