Vers. 3. ET FACTA EST SVPER EVM IBI MA- NVS DOMINI) Potenter in me egit Deus. Infra 3, 14.

## 1:4
Verse 4. AND I SAW.) The Hebrews call this vision that follows מרכב, that is, a chariot, and by this name they designate the more secret Theology concerning God and the angels, just as they call Physics ברשית, the name being taken from the beginning of Genesis. However, the Jews do not want these two parts of Scripture to be read, except by men of advanced age. Jerome says there are many synagogues in the explanation of this place. Moses Maimonides in the Guide for the Perplexed refers the things that are here partly to the angels, the movers of the spheres, and partly to the spheres themselves, that is, the primum mobile, the five planets, the Sun and the Moon, and thence the sublunar things. But if anyone diligently compares these things with those which we have in Exodus 25:18 and Isaiah 6, he will see that it is a matter of the properties and actions of God concerning His people. This vision pertains to this end, that the Jews deported in their evils might acknowledge the justice of God, and conceive hope, if ever they should correct themselves, of better things.

Dismissing the fables of the Jews, to which some Papists partly accede, explaining the four living creatures as the 4 Archangels, Prado, Villalpandus, and Cornelius: there does not appear to be a reason why we should depart from the exposition of the Fathers, who acknowledge that the kingdom of Christ was foreshadowed, and with great consensus assert that the four living creatures figure the four Evangelists, with Irenaeus leading the way in book 3, chapter 21: Athanasius in the Synopsis, Jerome in his Commentary, Augustine in book 1, On the Harmony of the Gospels, chapter 6, Gregory the Great, sermon 3 on Ezekiel, Ambrose, Bede on Apocalypse 4, and others. To whom Blessed Luther agrees, even though he maintains that the doctors of the Church are comprehended in general: concerning whom the quaternary number could be employed, not so much as a finite number for an infinite one, as that it might simultaneously look toward that holy quadriga of the Evangelists, this finite number being assumed (for others could have been assumed, but the quaternary number pleased not without mystery). God therefore indeed wished to exhibit His Majesty in this illustrious vision, but as the occasion of it suggested, with a certain scope and peculiar symbolic significance, because the Prophet was to be confirmed for his office, both concerning the people being liberated from captivity, and especially concerning the end of that liberation, that the Church and the kingdom of Christ might be propagated, which in the time of the New Testament was to be propagated throughout the whole world. The opinion of Apollinaris and Polychronius agrees that by this vision the providence and administration of God, both concerning human affairs in general and concerning the Church in particular, is designated. So also Francis Junius: The sum of the vision is that Jehovah testifies that His glory is most present to His servants, and explains it in heaven and on earth by the most powerful administration of His providence. But especially in Christ, to whom He gave all power, because He is the son of man: With which power the Lord, while He rules all things by His own will, also presides over His Church, and instructs His prophets and His servants, and endows them with the Spirit for the building up of the body of Christ, Eph. 4.

Therefore, it is not the chariot of an angry God, hastening to the punishment of the Jews, but the chariot of the Gospel or the kingdom of Christ that is exhibited, to be carried through the whole world. For the magnificence of God and of Christ is described by the chariot in Psalm 68:18, Song of Solomon 1:9. And the occasion for declaring the glory of the kingdom of Christ in the New Testament seems here to be taken from the Babylonian captivity, and the liberation from the same to be announced by the Prophet, which is a type of the liberation of Christ, and provided the cause for the propagation of the kingdom of Christ.

AND BEHOLD A WHIRLWIND CAME OUT OF THE NORTH.) Most grievous evils from the Chaldeans.

AND A GREAT CLOUD.) The army of the Chaldeans, Jer. 4:13.

AND FIRE WRAPPING ITSELF. ) Turning itself in a circle. The vengeance of God reaching all the Jews.

AND BRIGHTNESS ROUND ABOUT IT. ) The most manifest Justice of God.

Jerome brings forward a similar explanation: Those who read it as wind and the state of a storm, understand this, that the wrath and fury of God are coming from the North, that is, Nebuchadnezzar, and that Jerusalem is to be captured six years after this vision. For the vision is seen in the fifth year of the transmigration of King Jehoiachin, who was also the fifth year of Zedekiah reigning in Jerusalem, whom we read was led into Babylon after similarly six years, that is, in the eleventh year of his reign, when the city was captured. To those, therefore, who were dwelling near the river Chebar, and had voluntarily surrendered themselves to the King, it is revealed that they did well to obey the sentence of God. And in short, that both the province of Judea and the city of Jerusalem were to be captured. And because a great cloud is described, we understand it to carry showers of overthrows upon Judea, and rains of dashings. And the wrapped fire shows the coming punishments and the evils of captivity; and the brightness in its circuit signifies the manifest judgments of God. But since it is evident from the following revelation that the manifestation of the glory of Christ is exhibited under the New Testament, Osiander assigns not badly another reason also, why the wind of the whirlwind was a precursor. For just as before the promulgation of the law a thick cloud and fire in the clouds preceded it, Exod. 19, by which majesty God wished to reconcile authority to His law, not only worldly but heavenly: so that the Gospel suddenly coming upon the world, as a sudden (yet saving) storm, might be promulgated and propagated with great astonishment and admiration. Whence also on the day of Pentecost, when God was about to send the Holy Spirit to the Apostles to divulge the Gospel of Christ, there was suddenly made from heaven a sound, as of a vehement spirit coming, Acts 2. For if the ministry of death (the Law that kills) was in glory: how shall not the ministry of the Spirit (the Gospel through which the Spirit is given) be more in glory? 2 Cor. 3. Which cause can well consist with the former, namely, the wind of the whirlwind was coming from the North, because evil was to come from the North before the glory of the Lord was to appear, who, having shaken off the whirlwind of the wind, will one day carry the chariot of His kingdom through all the regions of the world and restore His people, so that from there the chariot of the living creatures (the Evangelists) can go out into the whole world, whose Gospel passed through the whole world from Judea. Nor indeed does the Gospel find a place, unless we are first shaken by the wind of the whirlwind, namely, by the law, promulgated in a storm and among thunders, driving and terrifying our hearts like a whirlwind. As there can be several causes for one thing, so there can be and can be established diverse reasons for this apparition arranged in that order: meanwhile, primarily the order looks to the storm about to precede from the North, whence the sight of the mystical chariot is more pleasing and more desired, because it may be permitted to understand that it is so far from the case that the chariot of the kingdom of Christ can be clearly checked by that storm, that rather it is to be carried through the whole world in its own time, with Christ as leader, by the impulse of the Holy Spirit.

AND FROM THE MIDST OF IT AS IT WERE THE APPEARANCE OF AMBER.) Namely, the form of the square vehicle, by which the Israelitic people were represented, similar to amber in this, that just as amber is not consumed in fire, so neither was he [the people] about to perish in such great evils; but having undergone a refining, was about to emerge purer.

THAT IS, FROM THE MIDST OF THE FIRE.) Pressed on all sides by punishments sent divinely.

The Hebrew word חשׁמל is explained in various ways. It does not occur elsewhere in the Code: nor do the Hebrews have anything to say about it. Therefore, the Chaldean retained this word, as if despairing of its interpretation. Jerome rendered it amber, but he says it is more excellent than gold and silver. But what that amber is, which is not consumed in fire, is certain. For it is known that amber [succinum] is not consumed by fire. However, it is not splendor that is noted, as Grotius thinks with some, but a Person is designated by the word Chasmal, because he who manifested himself in this vision had to be expressed. For never has a manifestation of attributes and works been made without mention of a person, nor do properties appear without a subject, nor are actions manifested without an acting or operating cause. Nor should the cause of the principal ministry, which directs it, be omitted, since the ministry is designated through living creatures. It is not likely, says B. Hülsemann, in excerpts from Ezekiel, in that vision by which the splendor of the Majesty of Christ, the effect of divine grace, or the chariot of the Gospel is described by its speed, by its administrators v. 5 seqq., by its fruit and efficacy v. 20, 21, in that vision, I say, that no mention is made of the principal efficient and the primary object, which is Christ, who sends those chariots and wheels from Eph. 4:8 seq., Ps. 68:18 seqq. Therefore, since neither another derivation nor another explanation of the word חשׁמל can be given, which better suits any subject than the Messiah, I say that this word is not indeed a proper name of the Messiah, but yet denotes no other subject than the person of the Messiah, who sends the Apostolic chariots. Which is confirmed especially from the collation of v. 26 and 28, which explain each other. And upon the likeness of the throne was as the appearance of a man: and I saw as it were the appearance of Chasmal. By the appearance of Chasmal, therefore, the same is denoted as by the appearance of a man. Furthermore, the personal actions of the Messiah are also attributed to him. For this same one, who was seen by the Prophet, is said to have spoken to him; c. 1 v. ult., c. 11 v. 1, 2. And chap. 8 v. 2. Where, since nothing else is had by which the subject of the vision is expressed, it must be that it is expressed by the word Chasmal. For the other name, son of man, is omitted, and this alone (Chasmal) is expressed, and yet the very description of the son of man delivered in chapter 1 is held. From the identity of which description and apparition, the identity of the subject is also gathered. For such are the subjects as they are permitted to be by the predicates. What of the fact that in chap. 10:19, 20, the same one who in chap. 1 is designated by the name of son of man, and by τῷ Chasmal, and in chap. 12 by this latter alone, is called the God of Israel: It is the animal (or they are the animals, the singular being put for the plural) which I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chobar. Finally, not only the Rabbis and Lyranus, but also Gregory Hom. 11, Dionysius the Carthusian, and Oecolampadius, who explains it of Christ, accept this word as referring to a person. The head of the Church, he says, is Chasmal, the Man called the elder below, who sits upon the throne. And to chap. 10: With the best right is he called Chasmal, because we speak of him with wondering silence and through arcane thoughts, having admired the work of God in him.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET VIDI.) Visum hoc quod sequitur מרכב, id est, currum vocant Hebræi, & hoc nomine appellant se- cretiorem Theologiam de Deo & angelis, sicut Physicam appellant ברשית, ab initio Geneseos desumpto nomine. Nolunt autem Judæi has duas Scripturæ partes legi, nisi ab hominibus provectæ ætatis. Multas in hujus loci explicatio- ne synagogas ait esse Hieronymus. Moses Maimonides in Duce dubitantium ea quæ hic sunt partim ad angelos refert motores sphærarum, partim ad ipsas sphæras, id est, primum mobile, planetarum quinque, Solis ac Lunæ, inde subluna- tium. At si quis diligenter hæc contulerit cum iis, quæ ha- bemus Exod. 25, 18. & Esa. 6. videbit agi de Dei proprietati- bus, & actionibus circa populum suum. Pertinet autem eo hoc visum, ut Judæi deportati in suis malis Dei justi- tiam agnoscerent, & spem conciperent, si quando se corri- gerent, terum meliorum.

Missis Judæorum commentis, quibus ex parte accedunt Papistæ nonnulli, quatuor animalia de Archangelis 4. explicantes, Prado, Villalpandus, & Cornelius: non apparet causa, cur à Patrum exposi- tione discedamus, qui regnum Christi adumbra- tum esse agnoscunt, & magno consensu quatuor animalia figurare quatuor Evangelistas, præeunte Ireneo lib. 3. c. 21. asserunt: Athanasius in Synops. Hieronymus in Comment. Augustinus lib. 1. de Cons. Evang. c. 6. Gregorius M. serm. 3. in Ezechielem, Ambrosius, Beda in Apoc. 4. & alii. Quibus an- nuit B. Lutherus, etsi doctores Ecclesiæ in univer- sum comprehendi statuat: de quibus numerus quaternarius adhiberi potuit, non tam ut finitus pro infinito, quam ut simul ad sanctam illam qua- drigam Evangelistarum, hoc numero finito assum- pto, (poterant enim alii assumi, sed placuit numerus quaternarius non absque mysterio) respiceretur. Exhibere ergo quidem voluit Deus Majestatem suam illustri hac visione, sed ut occasio ejus ferebat, certo scopo, & peculiari symbolica significatione, quia confirmandus erat ad munus suum Propheta, tum de liberando è captivitate populo, tum imprimis de fine istius liberationis, ut Ecclesia & regnum Christi propagaretur, quod tempore Novi Testa- menti per totum orbem erat propagandum. Con- sonat Apollinaris & Polychronii sententia, visione hac providentiam & administrationem Dei, tum de re- bus humanis in genere, tum de Ecclesia in specie, designari. Sic etiam Franciscus Junius: Summa visionis est, Jehovam gloriam suam Servis suis præ- sentissimam testificari, atque exponere in cælo & in terra potentissima administratione providentiæ suæ. Imprimis vero in Christo, cui dedit omnem potesta- tem, quia filius hominis est: Qua potestate Dominus cum omnia regit arbitratu suo, tum præest Ecclesiæ suæ, & instruit Prophetas & servos suos, eosque donat Spiritu ad coagmentationem corporis Christi, Eph. 4.

Non ergo currus Dei irati, properantis ad pœnam Judæorum, sed currus Evangelii vel regni Christi exhibetur, vehendus per totum orbem. Describi- tur enim magnificentia Dei, & Christi per currum Psal. 68, 18. Cant. 1, 9. Et occasio ad declarandam regni Christi gloriam in novo Testamento, desum- ta hic videtur à captivitate Babylonica, & liberatio- ne ex eadem à Propheta annuncianda, quæ typus est liberationis Christi, & causam propagationi re- gni Christi præbuit.

ET ECCE VENTUS TURBINIS VENIEBAT AB AQVILONE. ) Gravissima mala à Chaldæis.

ET NVBES MAGNA.) Exercitus Chaldæorum Jer. 4, 13.

ET IGNIS INVOLVENS. ) In gyrum se agens. Dei ultio ad omnes Judæos perveniens.

ET SPLENDOR IN CIRCVITV EJVS. ) Aper- tissima Dei Justitia.

Similem explicationem adducit Hieronymus: Qui ventum & statum tempestatis legunt, hoc sen- tiunt, iram & furorem Dei venire ab Aquilone, hoc est, Nabuchodonosor, & Hierusalem post sex annos hujus visionis esse capiendam. Cernitur n. visio quinto anno transmigrationis Regis Joachin, qui & Sedethia regnanti in Hierusalem quintus erat, quem legimus post sex similiter annos, id est, anno undecimo imperii sui, urbe capta ductum in Babylonem. His ergo qui ha- bitabant juxta flumen Chobari, & sponte se Regi tra- diderant, revelatur, quod benefecerint obedire senten- tiæ Dei. In brevin. & Judæam provinciam, & urbem Hierusalem esse capiendam. Quodque nubes magna describitur, intelligimus eam imbres eversionum super Judæam, pluviasque allisionum portare. Et involutus ignis monstrat ventura supplicia, & captivitatis mala; Splendorque in tircuitu ejus significat Dei aperta ju- dicia. Sed cum è sequenti revelatione pateat, mani- festationem gloriæ Christi sub Novo Testamento exhiberi, non male causam etiam aliam, cur ventus turbinis prævius fuerit, assignat Osiander. Ut n. ante promulgationem legis densa nubes, & ignis in nu- bibus præcedebant Exod. 19. qua majestate Deus legi suæ autoritatem conciliare voluit, non tantum mundanam, sed cœlestem: ut subito Evangelium superveniens mundo, tanquam subitanea (salutaris tamen) tempestas, cum ingenti stupore & admira- tione promulgaretur & propagaretur. Vnde & in die Pentecostes, cum Deus missurus esset Spiritum sanctum Apostolis ad divulgandum Evangelium Christi, factus est repente de cœlo sonus, tanquam advenientis spiritus vehementis Act. 2. Si n. mini- sterium mortis (Lex occidens) fuit in gloria: quo- modo non magis ministerium Spiritus (Evangeli- um per quod datur Spiritus) erit in gloria. 2. Corin. 3. Quæ causa cum priori consistere probe potest, ni- mirum ab Aquilone veniebat ventus turbinis, quia ab aquilone malum prius venturum erat, quam ap- paritura gloria Domini, qui currum regni sui dis- cusso venti turbine olim per universas mundi pla- gas vecturus populum suum restituet, ut inde in omnem orbem exire possit quadriga animantium (Evangelistarum) provectus, quorum Evangelium è Judæa totum orbem pertransiit. Neque vero E- vangelium locum invenit, nisi prius vento turbinis concutiamur, lege nempe, in tempestate, & inter tonitrua promulgata, instar turbinis corda nostra perpellente, ac perterrefaciente. Vti unius rei plu- res possunt esse causæ, ita apparitionis hujus isto or- dine pactæ diversæ possunt esse ac statui rationes: interim πρώτως ordo intuitur antegressuræ ab A- quilone tempestatis, unde gratior & exoptatior est conspectus currus mystici, quod intelligere liceat tantum abesse, ut per illam tempestatem currus regni Christi plane sufflaminari possit, ut potius suo ille tempore per totum orbem provehendus sit, duce Christo, impulsu Spiritus S.

ET DE MEDIO EJVS QVASI SPECIES ELE- CTRI.) Nempe forma vehiculi quadrati, quo repræfenta- bator populus Israeliticus, electro in hoc similis, quod sicut electrum in igne non consumitur, ita nec ipse in tantis malis erat interiturus; sed excoctione facta exsititurus purior.

ID EST, DE MEDIO IGNIS.) Vndique pressus pœnis divinitus immissis.

Vox Ebræa חשׁמל diversimode explicatur. Non occurrit alias in Codice: nec Ebræi habent, quod de ea dicant. Ideo Chaldæus hanc vocem re- tinuit, tanquam desperans de ejus interpretatione. Hieronymus electrum reddidit, sed id auro & ar- gento præstantius dicit. Quodnam vero illud ele- ctrum sit, quod in igne non consumatur, constat. Succinum enim igne non consumi notum est. Non autem notatur splendor, ut cum nonnullis putat Grotius, sed Persona designatur voce Chasmal, quia exprimendus erat, qui in hoc viso se manifestavit. Nunquam enim manifestatio tantum attributorum, & operum facta est, sine mentione personæ, ne- que proprietates sine subjecto comparent, aut a- ctiones manifestantur sine causa agente, vel ope- rante. Neque omittenda causa ministerii princi- palis, quæ id dirigit, cum per animantia ministe- rium designatum sit. Verisimile non est, inquit B. Hülsemannus, in excerptis ex Ezechiele, in visione illa, qua splendor Majestatis Christi, effectus gratiæ divinæ, seu currus Evangelii descriptus à velocitate sua, ab administris v. 5. seqq. à fructu & efficacia sua v. 20. 21. in illa, inquam, visione, nullam fieri mentio- nem efficientis principalis, & objecti primarii, quod est Christus, qui mittit illos currus, & rotas ex Eph. 4, 8. seq. Psal. 68, 18. seqq. Itaque cum neque alia deriva- tio, neque alia explicatio vocis חשׁמל dari possit, quæ ulli subjecto melius competat, quam Messiæ, dico hanc vocem non quidem esse nomen proprium Messiæ, sed non aliud subjectum tamen denotare, quam personam Messiæ, mittentis currus Apostolicos. Quod confir- mator imprimis è collatione v. 26. & 28. qui se mu- tuo explicant. Et super similitudinem throni erat quasi aspectus hominis: & vidi quasi speciem Chaf- mal. Per speciem Chafmal ergo idem notatur, quod per aspectum hominis. Porro tribuuntur ipsi etiam actiones personales Messiæ. Nam hic idem, qui visus est Prophetæ, dicitur ei loquutus esse; c. 1. v. ult. c. II, v. 1. 2. Et cap. 8. v. 2. Ubi quum nihil aliud ha- beatur, quo subjectum visionis exprimatur, voce Chasmal id expressum sit, necesse est. Omittitur enim alterum nomen filii hominis, & hoc tantum (Chasmal) exprimitur, & habetur tamen ipsa de- scriptio filii hominis cap. 1. tradita. E qua descri- ptionis & apparitionis identitate colligitur etiam identitas subjecti. Talia enim sunt subjecta, qualia permittuntur esse à prædicatis. Quid quod cap. 10, 19. 20. idem qui cap. 1. nomine filii hominis, & τῷ Chasmal & cap. 12. solo hoc posteriori designatus est, dicatur Deus Israel: Ipsum est animal (vel ipsa sunt animalia, singulari posito pro plurali) quod vi- di subter Deum Israel juxta fluvium Chobar. Deni- que de persona hanc vocem accipiunt, non tantum Rabini & Lyranus, sed etiam Gregorius Hom. 11. Dionysius Carthufianus, & Oecolampadius, qui de Christo exponit. Ecclesiæ, inquit, caput est Chaf- mal, Vir infra senex dictus, qui sedet super thronum. Et ad cap. 10. Optimo jure Chasmal dicitur, quod de eo admirabunda taciturnitate, & per cogitationes ar- canas magnifica loquamur, opus Dei in illo admi- raves.

## 1:4
Ver. 4.

AND I HEARD THE SOUND OF THE WINGS, AS THE SOUND OF MANY WATERS, AS THE SOUND OF THE SUBLIME GOD: WHEN THEY WALKED AS THE SOUND WAS OF A MULTITUDE, AS THE SOUND OF A CAMP.) Translate: as the sound of a battle: That is, the sound of a Camp. He says that those wings were not moved without a great noise, which he explains by three similitudes: of the roaring sea, of the thundering heaven (for the voice of God is called thunder, Ps. 29, 3; below 10, 5), and of a bellowing army. This signifies that those commands of God, of which the angels are the ministers, were atrocious and horrible.

That sound, as I said, does not here denote the judgment of God, but the sound of the word. For when the Apostles and their successors preached and propagated the Gospel with great Zeal, in truth the voice of God speaking was heard and the voice of thunder was heard. Whence also the Apostles were called sons of thunder: And many peoples (designated by the multitude of waters) embraced the Gospel and confessed the word of the Gospel everywhere before the world (with the perturbation of the impious), as if you were hearing many peoples simultaneously with one mouth proclaiming the praises of Christ the Redeemer with great majesty (like thunder); for the confession of truth is required both from hearers and from preachers, 1 Pet. 1. WHEN THE LIVING CREATURES STOOD, THEIR WINGS WERE LET DOWN. For when (the Lord permitting) the Ministry of the word of God is hindered for a time either by the cruelty of Tyrants or by the ingratitude and malice of the hearers; then the ministers of the Church, with dejected spirits, mourn, and in a certain way remit something of their Zeal; for they perform their office groaning, Heb. 13. AND THERE WAS A VOICE ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT, THAT WAS OVER THEIR HEAD, when THEY STOOD AND LOWERED THEIR WINGS. That is, when the living creatures were brought to a standstill, thunders were heard from above, for God is angered when the ministry is hindered, and a hindered ministry is a sign and testimony of horrible divine wrath.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET AVDIEBAM SONVM ALARVM, QVASI SONVM AQVARVM MVLTARVM, QVASI SO- NVM SVBLIMIS DEI: CVM AMBVLALENT QVASI SONVS ERAT MVLTITVDINIS, VT SO- NVS CASTRORVM.) Verte: quasi sonus prælii: Id est, sonus Castrorum. Dicit alas illas non fuisse motas sine ma- gno strepitu, quem tribus similitudinibus explicat: maris clangentis, cæli tonantis (tonitru enim vox Dei dicitur Ps. 29, 3. infra 10, 5.) & exercitus barrientis. Significatur hoc atrocia & horribilia fuisse Dei ista mandata, quorum mini- stri angeli.

Sonus ille, ut dixi, non hic notat judicium Dei, sed sonum verbi. Cum enim Apostoli, eorumque suc- cessores magno Zelo prædicarent, & propagarent Evangelion, revera audita est vox Dei loquentis & audita est vox tonitrui. Unde & Apostoli filii toni- trui dicebantur: Et multi populi, (per multitudinem aquarum designati) amplexi sunt Evangelion & coram mundo verbum Evangelii (cum perturba- tione impiorum) passim confessi sunt, quasi audires multos populos simul uno ore laudes Christi Re- demptoris, magna cum majestate (instar tonitrui) deprædicare; Confessio enim veritatis, tum ab au- ditoribus, tum à concionatoribus exigitur 1. Pet. 1. CVM STARENT ANIMALIA, DEMITTE- BANTUR ALÆ EORUM. Cum enim (per- mittente Dn.) ad tempus impeditur Ministerium verbi Dei vel Tyrannorum sævitia, vel audito- rum ingratitudine & malitia; tum Ecclesiæ mini- stri, dejectis animis, lugent, & quodammodo de Zelo suo aliquid remittunt; faciunt enim offici- um suum gementes Ebr. 13. ET FIEBAT VOX SUPRA FIRMAMENTUM, QUOD ERAT SUPER CAPUT EORUM, cum STABANT ET SUBMITTEBANT ALAS SUAS. Id est, cum sistebantur animalia, superne audiebantur to- nitrua, Deus enim irascitur, cum ministerium im- peditur, & impeditum ministerium est signum & testimonium horribilis iræ divinæ.

## 1:5
Vers. 5. AND IN THE MIDST OF IT.) In that vehicle.

THE LIKENESS OF FOUR ANIMALS.) That is, of the two Cherubim, who individually had the parts of the four animals.

AND THIS WAS THEIR APPEARANCE, THE LIKENESS OF A MAN, IN THEM.) That is, the face bore the likeness of a man.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET IN MEDIO EJVS.) In illo vehiculo.

SIMILITVDO QVATVOR ANIMALIVM.) Id est, duorum Cherubinorum, qui singuli partes habebant quatuor animalium.

ET HIC ASPECTVS EORVM, SIMILITVDO HOMINIS, IN EIS.) Id est vultus hominem præferebat.

## 1:6
Vers. 6. FOUR FACES TO ONE) פנים here more correctly explaining forms, or likenesses, as the Chaldean: the form of a man, as has already begun to be said, the form of an eagle, the form of a bull, the form of a lion. AND FOUR WINGS TO ONE) Two for flying; two for covering those things which ought to be covered. In Isaiah, two are added besides for covering the face, because there they stand by the throne, but here they are under the throne. There is consultation: here is execution.

Latin:

Verf. 6. QVATUOR FACIES UNI) פנים hic rectius ex- ponens formas, sive similitudines, ut Chaldæus: forma ho- minis, ut jam dici cœpit, forma aquilæ, forma tauri, for- ma leonis. ET QVATUOR PENNÆ UNI) Duæ ad volan- dum; duæ ad tegenda ea quæ tegi debent. Apud Efaiam adduntur præterea duæ ad regendum vultum, quia ibi ad- stant throno, hic vero sub throno. Ibi consultatio est: hic exsecutio.

## 1:7
Vers. 7. THEIR FEET, STRAIGHT FEET) That is, legs equal, bulging in no part: all actions straight. The Hebrews call the foot everything that is under the belly. AND THE SOLE OF THEIR FOOT AS THE SOLE OF THE FOOT OF A CALF) That is, the feet themselves are bovine. Thus also the Greeks say βοείω ποδὶ [with an ox-foot], when they signify that something is done slowly and heavily. AND SPARKS AS THE APPEARANCE OF GLOWING BRASS) In the Hebrew: and shining like the color of polished brass: that is, χαλκολιβάνω, as it is in Apoc. 1:15, 2:18, which most interpret as aurichalcum. It signifies that in those actions the purity of God appears, namely, that he waited so long and so patiently for the repentance of the Jews.

Latin:

Verf. 7. PEDES EORUM, PEDES RECTI) Id est, crura æqualia, nulla parte extuberantia: omnes actiones rectæ. Hebræi pedem vocant totum illud quod sub ventre est. ET PLANTA PEDIS EORUM QVASI PLAN- TA PEDIS VITULI) Id est, pedes ipsi bovini. Sic & Græci βοείω ποδὶ dicunt, cum tarde ac graviter agi aliquid significant. ET SCINTILLÆ QVASI ASPECTUS ÆRIS CANDENTIS) In Hebræo: & fulgentes ut color æris politi: id est, χαλκολιβάνω, ut est in Apoc. 1, 15. 2, 18. quod pleri- que aurichalcum interpretatur. Significat in illis actioni- bus apparere Dei puritatem, nempe quod tam diu ac tam patienter Judæorum resipiscentiam exspectaverit.

## 1:8
Verf. 8. AND THE HAND OF A MAN UNDER THEIR WINGS ON THE FOUR SIDES) That is, the wings had joints, such as the hand of a man. This signifies that even in the swiftest actions, all things are performed distinctly and in an orderly manner. AND THEY HAD FACES AND WINGS ON THE FOUR SIDES.) He repeats what he had said above, so that it may be more firmly fixed in the memory: that each Cherub had not only four wings, but also four forms.

Latin:

Verf. 8. ET MANUS HOMINIS SUB PENNIS EORUM IN QVATVOR PARTIBUS) Id est, pennæ alarum articulos habebant, quales manus hominis. Hoc signi- ficat etiam in celerrimis actionibus omnia distincte ordina- teque peragi. ET FACIES ET PENNAS PER QVATUOR PARTES HABEBANT.) Repetit quod supra dixerat, quo magis infigatur memoriæ: fuisse cuique Cherubino ut quatuor alas, ita formas quatuor.

## 1:8
Vers. 8. AS THE APPEARANCE OF THE BOW THAT IS IN THE CLOUD IN THE DAY OF RAIN, THIS

THE APPEARANCE OF THE SPLENDOR WAS THROUGH (GTRUM) As is the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud on a rainy day, such was the form around that splendor: namely, of that fire. The rainbow is a symbol of God's covenant, Gen. 9, 13. The judgments of God, however severe they may seem, do not abolish in God the memory of the covenant made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in which this also is included, that their posterity may always remain. Isaiah 54, 10. Jeremiah 33, 20. 21. 26.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VELVT ASPECTVM ARCVS CVM FVERIT IN NVBE IN DIE PLVVIÆ, HIC

ERAT ASPECTUS SPLENDORIS PER GTRUM) Qualis est species Iridos in nube die pluvio, talis erat forma circum illum splendorem: ignis illius scilicet. Iris fœderis Dei symbolum Genes. 9, 13. Judicia Dei, utcunque severa videantur, non abolent in Deo memoriam fœderis facti cum Abrahamo, Isaaco, Jacobo, in quo & hoc est, ut sem- per maneat eorum posteritas. Esaias 54, 10. Jerem. 33, 20. 21. 26.

## 1:9
Verf. 9. THEIR WINGS WERE JOINED ONE TO ANOTHER) Namely, as in the Sanctuary, Ex. 25, 20. This signifies that the actions of God all agree wonderfully among themselves, and with His purpose. THEY DID NOT TURN WHEN THEY WENT) They did not look back when they moved the vehicle. For Puhal is here, as often, used for Hiphil. To look back is to be led by repentance. See what is said at Luke 17, 31. This signifies constancy in executing the purpose of God. BUT EVERY ONE WENT STRAIGHT FORWARD) It moved the vehicle wherever it looked, as if by a nod.

Latin:

Verf. 9. JUNCTÆ ERANT PENNÆ EORUM AL- TERIUS AD ALTERUM) Nempe ut in Sanctuario, Ex. 25, 20. Id significat actiones Dei mire convenire inter se omnes, & proposito. NON REVERTEBANTUR, CUM INCIDE- RENT) Non retro spectabant, cum moverent vehiculum. Nam Puhal hic, ut sæpe, pro Hiphil ponitur. Respectare est pœnitentia duci. Vide quæ ad Lucam 17, 31. Significatur hic constantia in exequendo Dei proposito. SED UNUMQUODQVE ANTE FACIEM SUAM GRADIEBATUR) Movebat vehiculum quioquo spectabat, velut nutu.

## 1:10
Verf. 10. AND THE LIKENESS OF THEIR FACES) Translate: And the likeness of its forms. He explains more clearly what he had begun to say in v. 6. THE FACE OF A MAN) Form: and so in the following. THE FACE OF A LION ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THEM FOUR: AND THE FACE OF AN OX ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THEM FOUR.) It is a Hebrew brevity: The sense is: that there were both on the right and on the left, and the form of a lion in the manes, and of an ox in the feet; and that those forms were of the four forms. THE FACE OF AN EAGLE ABOVE THEM FOUR) That is, the form of an eagle was one of the four, in the wings.

Latin:

Verf. 10. SIMILITUDO AUTEM VULTUS EORUM) Verte: Similitudo autem formarum ejus. Explicatius dicit, quod dicere cœperat v. 6. FACIES HOMINIS) Forma: & sic in sequentibus. FACIES LEONIS A DEXTRIS IPSORUM QVATUOR: FACIES AUTEM BOVIS A SINISTRIS IPSOSUM QVATVOR.) Est breviloquentia Hebraica: Sensus est: tam à dextra, quam à sinistra fuisse, & for- mam Leonis in jubis, & bovis in pedibus; easque for- mas fuisse de formis quatuor. FACIES AQVILÆ DESUPER IPSORUM QUATUOR) Id est, forma aquilæ, una ex quatuor erat, in alis.

## 1:11
Verf. 11. THEIR FACES AND THEIR WINGS WERE STRETCHED UPWARD) The sense is: such as I have said were the forms, and the wings which were above the bodies. TWO WINGS OF EVERY ONE WERE JOINED) He explains more distinctly what he had said above in v. 9, that the wings of the Cherubim were contiguous to one another. It is to be understood of the flying wings, not of the wings covering the body.

Latin:

Verf. 11. FACIES EORUM ET PENNÆ EORUM EXTENTÆ DESUPER) Sensus est: tales quales dixi erant formæ, & alæ quæ super corpora erant. DUÆ PENNÆ SINGULORUM JUNGEBAN- TUR) Distinctius explicat, quod supra dixerat v. 9. alas Cherubinorum fuisse inter se contiguas. Intelligendum de alis volantibus, non de alis tegenda tegentibus.

## 1:12
Verf. 12. AND EVERY ONE WENT STRAIGHT FORWARD) Wherever it looked, thither it moved the vehicle. Repeated from that which was above in v. 9. WHITHER THE SPIRIT WAS TO GO, THEY WENT) In the Hebrew: Whithersoever there was a will to move, thither they moved: namely, with greater ease than the will of a man moves his own limbs. AND THEY DID NOT TURN WHEN THEY WENT) And they did not look back while moving, as above in v. 9.

Latin:

Verf. 12. ET UNUMQVODQVE CORAM FACIE SUA AMBULABAT) Quoquo spectabat, eo movebat vehiculum. Repetitum ex eo quod supra v. 9. UBI ERAT IMPETUS SPIRITUS, ILLUC GRADIEBANTUR) In Hebræo: Quocunque erat moven- di voluntas, eo movebant: nempe majori facilitate, quam vo- luntas hominis sua membra movet. NEC REVERTEBANTUR, CUM AMBULARENT) Nec retro spectabant inter movendum, ut supra v. 9.

## 1:13
Verf. 13. AND THE LIKENESS OF THE LIVING CREATURES) That is, this was the composition of each Cherub, consisting of those four forms of living creatures. THEIR APPEARANCE) Color. AS OF BURNING COALS OF FIRE) After the long patience of God, all things looked toward vengeance. Patience itself had become fury. AND AS THE APPEARANCE OF LAMPS.) With divine justice and purity shining forth everywhere. THIS WAS THE VISION RUNNING IN THE MIDST OF THE LIVING CREATURES) That is, such as I have said was the color in all parts.

SPLENDOR OF FIRE) Fiery. AND COMING FORTH FROM THE FIRE LIGHTNING) The burning of the city and the temple. An allusion to the history of Sodom.

Latin:

Verf. 13. ET SIMILITUDO ANIMALIVM) Id est, hæc erat compositio Cherubini cujusque constantis ex quatuor illis animalium formis. ASPECTUS EORVM) Color. QVASI CARBONVM IGNIS ARDENTIVM) Post longam Dei patientiam omnia ad ultionem specta- bant. Ipsa patientia furor erat facta. ET QVASI ASPECTVS LAMPADARVM.) Elucescente ubique divina justitia ac puritate. HÆC ERAT VISIO DISCVRRENS IN MEDIO ANIMALIVM) Id est, talis qualis dixi color erat in parti- bus omnibus.

SPLENDOR IGNIS) Igneus. ET DE IGNE EGREDIENS FULGUR) In- cendium urbis ac templi. Allusio ad Sodomorum hi- storiam.

## 1:14
Verse 14.

AND THE LIVING CREATURES WENT, AND RETURNED) That is, when they had arrived where they wished, they began another journey. Thus this does not conflict with that which is above 9, 12. IN THE LIKENESS OF FLASHING LIGHTNING) That is, very suddenly. See Matt. 24, 27. Luke 10, 18. 17, 24. So the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET ANIMALIA IBANT, ET REVERTEBAN- TUR) Id est, cum pervenissent quo vellent, aliud institue- bant iter. Ita hoc nihil pugnat cum eo, quod supra 9, 12. IN SIMILITUDINEM FULGURIS CORUSCAN- TIS) Id est, subito admodum. Vid. Matth. 24, 27. Luc. 10, 18. 17, 24. Sic Chaldæus hic.

## 1:15
Verse 15.

AND AS I LOOKED AT THE LIVING CREATURES) In the Hebrew: And I saw the living creatures, that is, I saw such Cherubim bearing the forms of four living creatures. It is a conclusion of the preceding, and a transition to the wheels. THERE APPEARED ONE WHEEL UPON THE EARTH) That is, I saw first one of the wheels, soon looking more diligently, I saw three others similar, as both the following and that which is below 10, 9 show. BESIDE THE LIVING CREATURES) Interpret as above. HAVING FOUR FACES) That is, the same form for those four wheels: which the following also explain more clearly.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

CUMQUE ASPICEREM ANIMALIA) In He- bræo: Et vidi animalia, id est, tales vidi Cherubinos qua- tuor animalium formas præferentes. Est conclusio præce- dentium, & transitus ad rotas. APPARUIT ROTA UNA SUPER TERRAM) Id est, vidi primo unam è rotis, mox diligentius intuens, vidi tres alias similes, ut ostendunt & sequentia & illa quæ infra 10, 9. JUXTA ANIMALIA) Interpretare ut supra. HABENS QUATUOR FACIES) Id est, forma ea- dem illis quatuor rotis: quod & sequentia clarius expli- cant.

## 1:16
Verse 16.

THE APPEARANCE OF THE WHEELS) Color. As above 13. AS THE VISION OF THE SEA) As if the color of the Ocean. That is, Hyacinthine as Symmachus translates. See Apoc. 9, 17. It does not differ much from the color of an Emerald. See Pliny 37, 9. It is signified by this, that just as the Ocean, although flowing, nevertheless has fixed and ordered cycles from God, so also the Jewish people. AND ONE LIKENESS OF THE FOUR) Form as we have already said. AND THE WORK AS IF A WHEEL WERE IN THE MIDST OF A WHEEL) The construction of them as a wheel in a wheel. That is: each wheel consisted of two intersecting each other, and thus it was as if spherical. This pertained to the fact that by the command of the Cherubim that vehicle could without difficulty be turned in four directions. By this was signified the deportation of the Jews to the North and South, East and West. Isa. 43. v. 5. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ASPECTUS ROTARUM) Color. Ut supra 13. QUASI VISIO MARIS) Tanquam color Oceani. Id est, Hyacinthinus ut vertit Symmachus. Vide Apoc. 9, 17. Non multum à Smaragdi colore distat. Vide Plinium 37, 9. Significatur eo, sicut Oceanus, quanquam fluxus, vices ta- men statas atque ordinatas à Deo habet, sic & populum Judaicum. ET UNA SIMILITUDO IPSARUM QUATUOR) Forma ut jam diximus. ET OPERA QUASI SIT ROTA IN MEDIO ROTÆ) Fabrica ipsarum ut rota in rota. Id est: quoque rota ex duabus constabat se mutuo decussantibus, ac sic erat quasi sphærica. Id eo pertinebat, ut jussu Cherubinorum vehiculum illud nullo negotio possit verti in partes qua- tuor. Significabatur autem eo deportatio Judæorum in Septentrionem & Meridiem, Ortum & Occasum. Esa. 43. v. 5. 6.

## 1:17
Verse 17.

THEY WENT THROUGH THEIR FOUR PARTS) That is, they could be moved to the four sides. AND THEY DID NOT RETURN WHEN THEY WALKED) Unless their course was completed, as we just said. Thus also all the deportations destined by God had their effect.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

PER QUATUOR PARTES EARUM EUNTES IBANT) Id est, in quatuor latera poterant moveri. ET NON REVERTEBANTUR CUM AMBU- LARENT) Nisi cursu suo peracto, ut modo diximus. Sic & omnes deportationes à Deo destinatæ suum effectum habuere.

## 1:18
Verse 18.

ALSO THERE WAS STATURE AND HEIGHT) That is, their rims were high. AND A TERRIBLE APPEARANCE) So that they were a horror to the beholder. THE WHOLE BODY FULL OF EYES ROUND ABOUT THE FOUR) But in the Hebrew: Their four rims full of various colors round about. An eye is put for a color. Num. 11, 16. So also below 22. The rims are high and terrible, because by them are signified the Kings, through whom God carried out those deportations. And multicolored, because some were Assyrians, others Egyptians, others Chaldeans: As varied in languages, habit, as in dress and arms.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

STATURA QUOQUE ERAT ET ALTITUDO) Id est, absides earum altæ erant. ET HORRIBILIS ASPECTUS) Ita ut spectanti horrori essent. TOTUM CORPUS OCULIS PLENUM IN CIRCUITU IPSARUM QUATUOR) At in Hæbreo: Absides earum quatuor plenæ variis coloribus circumquaque. Oculus pro colore ponitur. Num. 11, 16. Sic & infra 22. Absides altæ sunt & terribiles, quia per eas significantur Re- ges, per quos Deus deportationes illas exsequebatur. Et versicolores, quia alii Assyrii, alii Ægyptii, alii Chaldæi: Tam varii linguis, habitu quam vestis & armis.

## 1:19
Verse 19.

AND WHEN THE LIVING CREATURES WALKED) They moved, they made them go, as we have just said, and that by their Spirit, that is, by divine power and efficacy, as will follow. THEY WALKED LIKEWISE AND THE WHEELS BESIDE THEM) They proceeded, in whatever way it seemed good to them.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

CUMQUE AMBULARENT ANIMALIA) Mo- verent, incedere facerent, ut modo diximus, idque Spiritu suo, id est, divina vi, atque afficacia, ut sequetur. AMBULABANT PARITER ET ROTÆ JUX- TA EA) Procedebant, quomodo visum illis esset.

## 1:19
AND WHEN THE LIVING CREATURES WERE LIFTED UP FROM THE EARTH, THE WHEELS WERE LIFTED UP TOGETHER.) That is, when they wished, the transport ceased. WHEREVER THE SPIRIT WENT, THITHER THE SPIRIT GOING, THE WHEELS LIKEWISE WERE LIFTED UP, FOLLOWING IT: FOR THE SPIRIT OF LIFE WAS IN THE WHEELS.) The spirit of the living creature, that is, of the Cherub, reached to the wheels. Thus the Chaldean here most excellently. As ships to the wind, so those wheels proceeded or were lifted up according to the Spirit of the Cherubim.

Grotius wishes nothing else to be designated by this vision than the deportation of the Jews. But in this way, most things in the vision do not agree with the event. For example: That the vehicle tended toward the four quarters, by which he wishes the deportation of the Jews into the North and South, East and West to be signified. To which, however, the Jews were not deported, having been led into Babylonia.

(The passage Isa. 43, 5. 6. is irrelevant; for there the universal calling to the Church is predicted) nor is it fitting to understand by the four living creatures two Cherubim, each of whom had the form of those living creatures, nor is this vision rightly compared with that which Isaiah had in chapter 6, which are entirely distinct. Not to mention other things in that Grotian interpretation. Our application to the kingdom of Christ and the light of the Gospel is more correct. The blessed Luther embraced the summary in his Preface to Ezekiel: The vision of Ezekiel in the first part is nothing else, in my understanding (let another do better), than a revelation of the kingdom of Christ in faith here on earth in all four corners of the whole world, Ps. 19, v. 5. Their sound has gone out into all the earth. For there can be no prophet unless he has the Spirit of Christ, etc. Thus Megaland. Osiander followed him in his Paraphrase, applying everything more conveniently than Grotius: By the four living creatures he understands the Apostles and their legitimate successors, the sincere ministers of the Gospel, through whom Christ, triumphing over the devil, death, the world, sin, and hell, is carried in his triumphal chariot (as if by horses) through the world to the four quarters of the earth. Their feet are straight, not crooked, nor lame, but directed for walking; for the Gospel contains a doctrine that is by no means ambiguous or double-tongued: (such as most Delphic oracles were of old: or such as the dogmas of fanatical men are today:) but open and plain: Thus the ministers of the Gospel ought to walk with a straight foot: That they may propose and preserve the truth of the Gospel sincere: And neither attribute anything to the pleasures or desires of men, nor suffer anything to be detracted from its sincerity, or anything of its rectitude to be bent, Galat. 1, 1. THE SOLE OF THE FOOT (of each) is round, as it is held in the Hebrew, so that, of course, like globes, they could be moved most easily to all parts of the world. They (the feet) sparkle like the appearance of polished bronze: Which Grotius drags to the purity of the actions of God: But the feet of God are not described: But the discourse is about the four living creatures; And therefore it notes rather how splendid and pleasant the announcement of the Gospel is to troubled consciences, according to that: How beautiful are the feet of those who evangelize peace, who evangelize good things! Isa. 52. Nah. 1. Rom. 10. THE HAND OF A MAN appears under their wings in the four parts: which Osiander explains thus: Ministers, as they themselves must be faithful workers: So let them teach such faith in Christ as is effective through works of charity: Gal. 5. Because faith, which has no hand (doing good works), is not true faith. If you wish to explain with Grotius that all things are performed quickly, distinctly, and in an orderly manner, that likewise agrees with the faithful ministers of the word. THE FACES, AND THE WINGS, AND THE FOUR PARTS, looking toward the four quarters of the world, express the readiness of the Apostles to announce the Gospel in the whole world. THE WINGS JOINED one to another notes that Christian doctrine is not dissipated (as are the fanatical dogmas of heretics, which are like loose brooms) but is consistent with itself from all parts. THEY DO NOT TURN THEMSELVES WHEN THEY WALK, BUT EACH ONE GOES STRAIGHT BEFORE ITS FACE. BECAUSE wherever God directs the course of the Gospel, it penetrates there with an expeditious step. Fanatical teachers, however, walk with a bent motion, like serpents, and circumvent unwary men with oblique arts, and entangle them in their errors, as if with coils. AND THE LIKENESS OF THEIR FACES WAS THE FACE of a man, and the face of a lion on their right, but the face of an ox on the left of the four, and the face of an eagle of the four. That is, each animal seemed to consist of four parts, because it had four faces; and of the two faces which were on the right, one had the likeness of a human face, the other of a lion's face; but those which were on the left, one of them was like the face of an ox, the other of an eagle. These four faces designated what kind of persons the Apostles (and their legitimate successors) would be in their ministry toward the Church of God. The face of a man expresses humanity, by which the weak in faith ought to be treated most humanely. Rom. 10. chap. The face of a Lion denotes an unbroken spirit against dangers of every kind: so that they do not hesitate even to pour out their life for the Gospel of Christ. Matth. 10. chap. The face of an ox designates the tolerance of labors which the ministry requires: Whence Paul says of the Ministers of the Church: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn 1. Cor. 9. The face of an eagle warns that human traditions, or philosophical or earthly speculations, are not to be proposed: But heavenly doctrine, which surpasses all grasp of human reason, Col. 2. 2. Corint. 10. AND THEIR FACES AND THEIR WINGS WERE DISTINCT ABOVE. That is, neither the faces nor the wings were confused (for the Holy Spirit is not a Spirit of confusion, but of discretion: teaching ministers what it is fitting to do with individuals at any given time) Two feathers (more correctly wings) of each (namely the upper wings) were joined. (These wings designate pious Zeal in propagating the Gospel: in which endeavor sincere ministers agree and join their efforts.) And two wings covered their bodies, in a way warming their bodies (for good Evangelical ministers embrace and warm the members of the Church with great charity: just as a hen warms her chicks.) AND THE LIKENESS OF THE ANIMALS (AND) THEIR APPEARANCE WAS LIKE BURNING COALS OF FIRE (AND) LIKE THE APPEARANCE OF LAMPS: THIS WAS (The vision) RUNNING IN THE MIDST OF THE ANIMALS. The splendor of fire went out from the animals: AND FROM THE FIRE LIGHTNING was GOING FORTH, that is, the animals were ignited and glowing: and between the animals were seen clear flames: And splendor went out from that fire, and from the aforementioned flames went out lightnings. For the Apostles (and their legitimate successors) are illuminated by the fire of the Holy Spirit: and (in the eyes of the Church of Christ) they are illustrious persons, very bright with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. And there is present with them the power and efficacy of the Holy Spirit to illuminate and soften the hearts of the hearers. Whence also on the day of Pentecost the tongues of the Apostles appeared fiery, or flame-like Act. 2. Moreover, the running lightning signified that the Gospel of Christ would penetrate and illuminate the whole world with admirable speed. Furthermore, the WHEELS signify the ministry of the word and Sacraments itself. THEIR STRUCTURE IS LIKE SAPPHIRE GEMS, which reflect the color of the sky when it is most serene; Because in the word of the Gospel and in the Sacraments (although it is preached and administered on earth) heavenly Mysteries and heavenly Treasures are proposed and exhibited to us: THE LIKENESS OF THE WHEELS notes that the word of the Gospel, which is preached in the various Churches of Christ, is the same. THE RIM AND HEIGHT OF THE WHEELS, AND THEIR TERRIBLE APPEARANCE. That is, the uppermost parts of the wheels of unusual and

stupendous height indicate that the dignity and majesty of the word and Sacraments is greater. Those summits of the wheels (the rims) full of eyes denote this: that the ministry confers upon believers an abundant and salutary knowledge of God, and a most rich cognition of heavenly mysteries. AND WHEN THE ANIMALS WALKED, THE WHEELS ALSO WALKED (likewise) BESIDE THEM: The wheels accompanied the animals, just as chariots accompany horses. For the Apostolic office (or the ministry of the word) is not to sit in the midst of pleasures and to indulge one's genius in leisure; which most Roman Pontiffs do; but it requires: that those who boast of that office be occupied in the Ministry of the word and sacraments. For a Pastor of the Church without a Ministry is a name without a thing. AND WHEN THE ANIMALS WERE LIFTED UP FROM THE EARTH, THE WHEELS WERE LIFTED UP (at the same time). For sometimes the Ministry and Ministers (even in worldly kingdoms) are in dignity. And he who magnifies the ministers, also magnifies the ministry. Just as on the contrary, those who despise pious and sincere Ministers, also despise the Ministry in their heart; whatever they may boast with their mouth. WHEREVER THE SPIRIT WENT, or the wind, THITHER THE SPIRIT GOING, (that is, the wind standing and impelling) the wheels and animals went. For the ministry is impelled and governed by the Spirit of God. FOR THE SPIRIT OF LIFE (that is, living and life-giving) WAS IN THE WHEELS. Because the Holy Spirit is present with the ministry, so that it may be taught with fruit. All of which our blessed Hülsemann similarly explains, rightly warning that the divine majesty is signified by this vision, both in vindicating the Jews and in convening the Christians, and that this sense is taken from the last verse of chap. 1. That the occasion of demonstrating this glory both toward the Jews and toward the Church was indeed the captivity and the Babylonian liberation, on account of which the wind of the whirlwinds and the cloud is said to have come from the North, by which region of the world it is established that Babylon is signified Jer. 1. v. 13. and 14. c. 4, 6. But that the Prophet's discourse is not about a Babylonian captivity still to come, is evident from this: because he himself was already held captive in Babylon v. 1.3. For although many Jews still remained to be taken captive under King Zedekiah and the temple to be destroyed, yet the deportation itself was already in motion, and so it is hardly credible that such august visions were shown to the Prophet concerning that alone.

Latin:

ET CUM ELEVARENTUR ANIMALIA DE TERRA, ELEVABANTUR SIMUL ROTÆ.) Id est, cum vellent, cessabat deportatio. QUOCUNQUE IBAT SPIRITUS, ILLUC EUNTE SPIRITU ET ROTÆ PARITER ELEVA- BANTUR, SEQVENTES EUM: SPIRITUS ENIM VITÆ ERAT IN ROTIS.) Spiritus animantis, id est, Cherubini, cujusque pertingebat ad rotas. Ita hic optime Chaldæus. Sicut naves ad ventum, ita rotæ istæ ad Spiri- tum Cherubinorum procedebant aut attollebantur.

Nihil aliud hac visione designari vult Grotius, quam deportationem Judæorum. At ita pleraq; non congruent in visione eventui. Exempli grat. Quod vehiculum tenderit in quatuor plagas, quo deporta- tionem Judæorum in Septentrionem & Meridiem, Ortum & Occasum significatam vult. Quo tamen deportati Judæi non sunt, in Babyloniam traducti

(Locus Ef. 43, 5. 6. ὀὐδὲν πρὸς ἔπος; eo enim vocatio ad Ecclefiam univerfalis prædicitur) neque conve- niens est per animalia quatuor Cherubinos duos in- telligere, quorum quisq; formam illorum animan- tium habuerit, neque recte comparatur hæc vifio cum illa, quam habuit Efaias cap. 6. quæ prorfus di- stinctæ funt. Ut alia in illa ἐπιγνώσει Grotiana tace- am. Rectius se habet nostra applicatio ad regnum Christi, & lumen Evangelii. Summam comple- xus est B. Lutherus Præfat. in Ezech. Das Ge- ficht Hefcckiels im ersten Theil/ist nichts anders/ meines Verstands (ein ander mache es besser) denn eine Offenbahrung deß Reichs Christi im Glau- ben hie auff Erden in allen vier Orten der ganzen Welt/Pfal. 19. v. 5. In omnem terram exivit fonus eorum. Denn es kan kein Prophet seyn/ er habe denn den Geist Christi œc. Hæc Megaland. Sequu- tus est eum in Paraphrafi Ofiander, omnia conveni- entius applicens quam Grotius: Per quatuor anima- lia intelligit Apoftolos, eorumque legitimos succef- fores, sinceros Evangelii ministros, per quos Chri- stus triumphans de diabolo, morte, mundo, peccato & inferno in curru suo triumphi (tanquam equis) vehitur per orbem terrarum, ad quatuor mundi plagas. Pedes eorum recti funt, non curvi, neq; clau- di sed ad incedendum directi, ut enim Evangelion continet minime flexiloquam aut ambiguam do- ctrinam: (qualia erant olim Delphica pleraque o- racula: aut qualia sunt hodie phanaticorum homi- num dogmata:) sed apertam & planam: Ita mini- stri Evangelii debent recto pede incedere: Ut ve- ritatem Evangelii sinceram proponant, ac confer- vent: Neque hominum placitis aut cupiditatibus aliquid tribuant, neque quicquam de ejus sinceri- tate detrahi, aut de rectitudine ejus aliquid incur- vari patiantur, Galat. 1, 1. PLANTA PEDIS (cujus- que) rotunda est, ut in Ebræo habetur, ut nimirum tanquam globi ad omnes mundi partes moveri fa- cillime possent. Coruscant (pedes) quasi afpectus æris politi: Quæ ad puritatem actionum Dei rapit Grotius: At non pedes Dei defcribuntur: Sed de quatuor animantibus fermo est; Ideoque notat potius, quam splendida & jucunda sit annunciatio Evangelii perturbatis conscientiis, juxta illud: Quam fpeciofi funt pedes Evangelizantium pacem, Evangelizantium bona! Efa. 52. Nah. 1. Rom. 10. MANVS HOMINIS fub alis eorum in quatuor partibus apparent: quod ita explicat Ofiander: Ministri, ut ipfi fideles operari esse debent: Ita ta- lem fidem in Chriftum doceant, quæ per opera chari- tatis fit efficax: Gal. 5. Quia fides, quæ nullam ma- num (bona operantem) habet: non est vera fi- des. Si malis cum Grotio explicare, quod omnia celeriter, distincte, & ordinate peragantur, id pari- ter congruit fidelibus verbi ministris. FACIES, ET ALÆ, ET QVATVOR PARTES, re- spicientes ad quatuor Mundi plagas promptitudi- nem Apostolorum exprimunt ad annunciandum Evangelium in universo orbe. ALÆ JVNCTÆ una ad alteram notat, doctrinam Christianam non esse dissipatam, (ut sunt hæreticorum dogmata fa- natica, quæ scopæ dissolutæ) sed ex omnibus par- tibus sibi constare. NON VERTVNT SE, CVM INCEDVNT, SED VNVMQVOD- QVE ANTE FACIEM SVAM (recta) GRA- DITVR. QVIA quocunque Deus Evangelii curfum dirigit, eo penetrat expedito gradu. Fa- natici vero Doctores, inflexo motu, tanquam ser- pentes, incedunt, & obliquis artibus incautos ho- mines circumveniunt, atque erroribus fuis eos, tanquam spiris implicant. SIMILITVDO AVTEM VVLTV EORVM FACIES HOMINIS, ET FACIES LEONIS A DEX- TRIS IPSORUM QUATUOR, FACIES AUTEM BOVIS A SINISTRIS IPSO- RUM QUATUOR, ET FACIES AQUILAE IPSORUM QUATUOR. Id est, unumquod- que animal videbatur quasi ex quatuor partibus constare, quia quatuor facies habebat; & duarum facierum, quae a Dextris erant, altera habebat simi- litudinem humanae faciei, altera Leoninae faciei; quae vero a Sinistris erant, earum altera similis erat faciei bovinae, altera aquilinae. Hae quatuor facies designabant, quales Apostoli (& eorum legitimi successores) futuri essent in ministerio suo, erga Ecclesiam Dei. Facies hominis exprimit humani- tatem, qua infirmi in fide humanissime tractari de- bent. Rom. 10. cap. Facies Leonis denotat infra- ctum animum adversus omnis generis pericula: ita ut etiam vitam pro Evangelio Christi profundere non dubitent. Matth. 10. cap. Facies bovis de- signat tolerantiam laborum, quos ministerium re- quirit: Unde Paulus de Ministris Ecclesiae dicit: Trituranti bovi os non obligabis 1. Cor. 9. Facies aquilae admonet, non proponendas esse humanas traditiones, aut Philosophicas, aut terrenas specu- lationes: Sed coelestem doctrinam, quae omnem rationis humanae captum superat, Col. 2. 2. Corint. 10. ET FACIES EORUM ET ALAE EO- RUM DISTINCTAE ERANT SUPRA. Id est, nec facies, nec alae erant confusae (Spiritus enim sanctus non est Spiritus confusionis, sed discretio- nis: docens ministros: quid quolibet tempore cum singulis agi conveniat) Duae pennae (rectius alae) singulorum (superiores nimirum alae) junge- bantur. (Hae alae pium Zelum in propagando Ev- angelio designant: in quo studio sinceri ministri concordant, operasque suas conjungunt.) Et duae alae tegebant corpora eorum, foventes quodammodo corpora (boni enim ministri Evangelici magna charitate complectuntur & fovent Ecclesiae mem- bra: quasi gallina pullos suos fovet.) ET SIMI- LITUDO ANIMALIUM (&) ASPECTUS EORUM QUASI CARBONUM IGNIS AR- DENTIUM (&) QUASI ASPECTUS LAM- PADARUM: HAEC ERAT (Visio) DIS- CURRENS IN MEDIO ANIMALIUM. Splen- dor ignis exibat de animalibus: ET DE IGNE FULGUR erat EGREDIENS, id est, ani- malia erant ignita & candentia: & inter animalia videbantur clarae flammae: Et splendor ex illo igne egrediebatur, atque ex flammis praedictis exibant ful- gura. Apostoli enim (eorumque legitimi succes- sores) igne Spiritus sancti sunt illuminati: & (in oculis Ecclesiae Christi) sunt illustres personae, donis SpiritusSancti admodum clari. Et adest illis vis, & efficacia Spiritus sancti, ad illuminanda & emollien- da corda auditorum. Unde & in die Pentecostes linguae Apostolorum igneae, seu flammeae apparebant Act. 2. Discurrens autem fulgur significabat, Evangelion Christi admiranda celeritate pervasu- rum & illuminaturum orbem terrarum. Porro ROTAE significant ipsum ministerium verbi & Sa- cramentorum. STRUCTVRA earum est QVA- SI GEMMAE SAPPHIRI, quae colorem caeli referunt, cum serenissimum est; Quia in verbo Evangelii & in Sacramentis (licet in terris praedi- cetur & administrentur) proponuntur & exhiben- tur nobis caelestia Mysteria, & caelestes Thesauroi: SIMILITUDO ROTARVM notat, quod ver- bum Evangelii, quod in variis ChristiEcclesiis prae- dicatur, idem sit. ROTARVM GIBBVS ET ALTITVDO, ET HORRIBILIS ASPE- CTVS. Id est, supremae rotarum partes inusitatae &

stupendæ altitudinis indicant majorem esse digni- tatem & majestatem verbi & Sacramentorum. Sum- mitates illæ rotarum (die Felgen) plenæ oculis id notant: quod ministerium conferat credentibus copiosam & salutarem agnitionem Dei, & cognitio- nem uberrimam cælestium mysteriorum. CVM- QUE AMBULARENT ANIMALIA, AM- BULABANT (paritér) ET ROTÆ JUXTA EA: Rotæ comitabantur animalia, sicut currus equos. Officium enim Apostolicum (seu mini- sterium verbi) non est sedere in mediis voluptati- bus, & in otio indulgere genio; quod faciunt ple- rique Pontificis Romani; sed requirit: ut qui de eo officio gloriantur, in Ministerio verbi & sacramen- torum sint occupati. Pastor enim Ecclesiæ sine Ministerio est nomen sine re. ET CUM ELE- VARENTUR ANIMALIA DE TERRA, ELEVABANTUR (simul) ET ROTÆ. Quan- doque enim Ministerium & Ministri (etiam in mundanis regnis) sunt in dignitate. Et qui mini- stros magnificat, etiam ministerium magnificat. Sicut contra, qui pios & synceros Ministros con- temnunt, etiam Ministerium in corde suo con- temnunt; quicquid ore jactent. QUOCUN- QUE IBAT SPIRITUS, seu ventus, ILLUC EUNTE SPIRITU, (id est, stante & impellente vento) ibant rotæ & animalia. Impellitur enim ministerium & gubernatur Spiritu Dei. SPIRI- TUS ENIM VITÆ (id est, vivus & vivificans) ERAT IN ROTIS. Quia Spiritus Sanctus adest ministerio, ut cum fructu doceatur. Quæ omnia si- militer explicat B. Hülsemannus noster, recte mo- nens, significari visione hac majestatem divinam tum in vindicando Judæos, tum in convocando Christianos, eumque sensum sumi ex versu ultimo cap. 1. Oc- casionem quidem hujus gloriæ tum erga Judæos, tum ergaEcclesiam demonstrandæ fuisse captivita- tem, & liberationem Babylonicam, ob quam ven- tus turbinum & nubes venisse dicitur ab Aquilone, qua mundi plaga Babylonem significari constat Jer. 1. v. 13. & 14. c. 4, 6. Non esse autem sermonem Prophetæ de captivitate Babylonica adhuc futura, exinde patescere: quia ipse in Babylone jam capti- vus tenebatur v. 1.3. Quanquam enim plures ad- huc Judæi sub Zedekia Rege captivandi & tem- plum destruendum restaret, deportatio tamen ipsa jam in motu erat, adeoque de illa tantum tam au- gustas visiones Prophetæ monstratas esse, vix credibile est.

## 1:20
Verse 20.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

## 1:22
Vers. 22.

AND THE LIKENESS OVER THE HEADS OF THE LIVING CREATURES OF THE FIRMAMENT, AS THE APPEARANCE OF THE TERRIBLE CRYSTAL.) There appeared over the heads of the Cherubim a canopy of the appearance of wondrous Crystal. A canopy is the roof of a vehicle, as Servius teaches us: It is in Hebrew רָקִיעַ that is, an expansion, by which name also the heaven is called. Thus also to the Greeks ὠράνιον is a parasol, under which Kings sit. Not even the Angels gaze directly upon the properties of God, but through an expansion, yet clearly as those who see something through crystalline mirrors. Thus this crystalline canopy performs the same thing here, which in Isaiah the wings covering the face do.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET SIMILITVDO SUPER CAPITA ANIMA- LIUM FIRMAMENTI, QVASI ASPECTUS CRY- STALLI HORRIBILIS.) Apparebat super capita Cherubino- rum tympanum specie admirabilis Crystalli. Tympanum est tectum vehiculi, ut nos docet Servius: Id Hebraice רָקִיעַ id est, expansio, quo nomine & cælum appellatur. Sic & Græcis ὠράνιον est umbella, sub quaReges resident. Di- recte proprietates Dei ne Angeli quidem intuentur, sed per oppansum, lucide tamen ut qui per crystallina specularia aliquid vident. Ita idem hic præstat tympanum crystalli- num, quod apud Esaiam alæ faciem tegentes.

## 1:23
Vers. 23.

AND UNDER THE FIRMAMENT, ) Under that canopy. THEIR WINGS STRAIGHT THE ONE TOWARD THE OTHER.) That is, the upper wings were so expanded that they touched one another. EVERY ONE WITH TWO WINGS COVERED HIS BODY, AND THE OTHER WAS LIKEWISE COVERED.) With the other wings they covered what was to be covered, exactly as one of the Cherubim, so the other. These things are repeated from the above, so that they do not slip from the readers. Trifles more vain than Sicilian nonsense: there is no discourse here about Cherubim, that is, angels, none about crystalline mirrors: None about a canopy or roof over the heads of the angels. And that the angels do not behold the properties of God directly through the expanse, yet clearly and through crystalline mirrors, whence Grotius has it, unless perhaps from a Papistical mirror? And the comparison with a place entirely different, Isa. 5, which we previously noted, is rash. By רקיע, as has been said, the firmament is understood, but above the heads of the living creatures was as it were the appearance of admirable crystal; which signifies divine protection over the ministers and the ministry, if they are defended and preserved against the insults of the devil and the world. Moreover, the individual living creatures raise two wings on high, and with the other two they cover their bodies; the upper wings denote the concordant zeal of the ministers in propagating the Gospel, the lower ones denote the charity of the ministers toward the Church. If the angels cover their faces with their wings, lest they behold God, why do they lower their wings afterwards, verse 25? Is not the august Majesty of God always to be trembled at by them?

Latin:

Vers. 23.

SUB FIRMAMENTO AUTEM, ) Sub isto tym- pano. PENNÆ EORUM RECTÆ ALTERIUS AD ALTERUM.) Id est alæ superiores ita expansæ erant, ut se mutuo contingerent. VNVMQVODQVE DVABVS ALIS VELA- BAT CORPVS SVVM, ET ALTERVM SIMILITER VELABATVR.) Alteris alis obtegebant obtegenda, plane ut unus, sic alter Cherubinorum. Repetita hæc ex superioribus, ne lectoribus excidant. Nugæ gerris Siculis vaniores: de Cherubinis, h. e. angelis, nullus hic sermo, nullus de crystallinis specularibus: Nullus de tympano vel tecto super ca- pita angelorum. Et angelos per oppansum non di- recte Dei proprietates intueri, lucide tamen & per Crystallina specularia, unde habet Grotius, nisi forte ex speculo Papistico? & temeraria est collatio cum loco prorsus diverso Esa. 5. quod antea mo- nuimus. Per רקיע ut dictum est, firmamentum in- telligitur, sed super capita animalium quasi aspectus admirabilis Crystalli; quod significat protectionem divinam super ministros & ministerium, si contra insultus diaboli & mundi defenduntur & conser- vantur. Singula autem animalia duas alas in subli- me erigunt, reliquis duabus corpora sua tegunt su- periores alæ concordem zelum ministrorum in propagando Evangelio, inferiores charitatem mi- nistrorum erga Ecclesiam notant. Si angeli tegunt alis faciem, ne intueantur Deum, cur submittunt postea alas, vers. 25. Annon semper tremenda ipsis est augusta Dei Majestas?

## 1:25
Ver. 25. FOR WHEN THE VOICE WAS MADE ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT THAT WAS OVER THEIR HEAD) ו here rather signifies 'but': and the sense is: but truly as often as the voice was heard from the throne, which were above the firmament: (namely, for a retreat: τὸ ἀνακλητικὸν. THEY STOOD, AND LOWERED THEIR WINGS) They stood with wings resting. For רפה generally signifies this: nor did the Chaldean and the LXX take it otherwise here. By God's command the ministries were resting: there was a cessation from the deportations. Ver. 26. AND ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT THAT WAS IMMINENT OVER THEIR HEAD.) Above that firmament. AS THE APPEARANCE OF A SAPPHIRE STONE THE LIKENESS OF A THRONE. There is a transposition here. The sense: There was there the form of a throne with a sapphire color. The throne signifies the judgments of God, 21.0, 5.+7, 9.97,.. Isa. 6, 1. Dan. 7, 9. Often in the Apocalypse. Sapphire, with its sky-blue color and golden dots, signifies the heaven where the throne of God is. Apocal. 4, 2. AND ABOVE THE LIKENESS OF THE THRONE, THE LIKENESS AS THE APPEARANCE OF A MAN FROM ABOVE.) That is: And above the appearance of the throne a certain human appearance. The One sitting upon His throne is not compared to a Lion, or a bear, or a Whale, but to a man, whose property is justice, as Hesiod says: 'For to fishes and beasts and winged birds He gave to eat one another, since justice is not among them; but to men He gave justice, which is by far the best.' It is signified, therefore, that God judges the affairs of the Jewish people with most equitable judgments.

The throne of God does not always denote the judgments of God punishing, but the Majesty of the government of God, whence Christ is said to be raised to the throne of God, or of divine Majesty and glory, when, exalted to the right hand of God, He received all power in heaven and on earth, and was made the head of His body, Heb. 1 and 12, Apoc. 3. By the son of man, not the humanity and kindness of God, but Christ, to whom this name 'son of man' is appropriated, is denoted, who was also called so by Daniel, chap. 7. Nor is the image of God's decree concerning the Jewish people presented here, but that of the kingdom and majesty of Christ, to whom all things more rightly correspond, who, residing on the seat of divine Majesty, governs the evangelical chariot. That throne is established above the firmament: Because Christ is even more sublime than the heavens by His Majesty and power, Heb. 7. Not by local position, but by the magnitude of glory. Which Junius also acknowledges, that the omnipotence of Christ and the position of the Son are exhibited. The position indeed, because the seat is said to have been placed above that expanse, and above the head of the living creatures, that is (as the Apostle commonly speaks, ἐν τοῖς ὑπερερανίοις, in the supercelestial places (so to speak), above every name and power, as also Eph. 1. For thus we acknowledge the majesty of Christ to obtain infinite empire over all created things, celestial, terrestrial, animate, inanimate. The appearance, however, explains that same majesty further, when it is said that the seat had the appearance of Sapphire, which stone indeed approaches most closely to the Beryl in sea-green color, but has less of that marine greenness, and prefers the brightness of gold in a blue color: By which reason we are taught that the glory of the heavens themselves, and of all celestial things, is surpassed in all respects by the glory of Christ, just as the blue and Sapphire color surpasses the wave-like and sea-green color. These are the words of Junius. The Son of Man, however, is placed upon that throne, because Christ was to be placed at the right hand of God, on the throne of majesty, so that through the ministry of the word he might gather and govern the Church in the world. Furthermore, there appears as it were the appearance of Chasmal, like the appearance of fire within it round about, from his loins upward, and from his loins even downward as it were the appearance of shining fire round about. That man (Jesus Christ) from behind (upward and downward) has a most bright fire, which casts forth an admirable splendor from itself. For Christ dwells in Majesty, and in ineffable light, as Osiander explains. A rainbow, however, appears around that light, so that we may be taught that this majesty of Christ is salutary to the human race, inasmuch as all who believe in this θεάνθρωπον are reconciled with the heavenly Father, and are received into grace.

Latin:

Vers. 25. NAM CVM FIERET VOX SVPER FIR- MAMENTVM QVOD ERAT SVPER CAPVT EO- RVM) ו hic potius at valet: & sensus est: at vero quoties ex throno, qui erant super tympanum, vox audiebatur: (nempe receptui: τὸ ἀνακλητικὸν. STABANT, ET SVBMITTEBANT ALAS SVAS) Stabant alis quiescentibus. Idenim רפה plerunqui significat: nec aliter hic sumsit Chaldæus & LXX. Deo ju- bente quiescebant ministeria: cessabatur à deportationibus. Vers. 26. ET SVPER FIRMAMENTVM QVOD ERAT IMMINENS CAPITI EORVM.) Super illud tympanum. QVASI ASPECTVS LAPITIS SAPPHIRI SI- MILITVDO THRONI. Est hic transpositio. Sensus: Erat ibi forma throni colore sapphirino. Thronus significat judicia Dei 21.0, 5.+7, 9.97,.. Es. 6, 1. Dan. 7, 9. In Apo- calypsi sæpe. Sapphirus colore cæruleo, & aureis pun- ctis cælum significat, ubi thronus Dei. Apocal. 4, 2. ET SVPER SIMILITVDINEM THRONI, SI- MILITUDO QVASI ASPECTVS HOMINIS DE- SUPER.) Id est: Et super speciem throni species quædam humana. Decus throno suo insidens, non Leoni, aut urso, aut Balænæ comparatur, sed homini, cujus propria est justi- tia, ut ait Hesiodus: Ἰχθύσι γὰρ κὴ θηρσὶ κὴ οἰωνοῖς πετεηνοῖς Ἐσθίμεν ἀλλήλους, ἐπεὶ ὀ δίκη ἐςὶ μετ᾿ αὐτῶν· Ἀνθρώποισι δ᾽ ἔδωκε δίκην ἣ πολλὸν ἀρίστη. Significatur ergo Deum æquissimis arbitriis res Judaici po- puli dijudicare.

Thronus Dei non semper judicia Dei punientis, sed Majestatem regiminis Dei notat, unde Chri- stus ad thronum Dei, seu Majestatis & gloriæ divi- næ evectus dicitur, cum exaltatus ad dextram Dei, omnem potestatem accepit in cœlo & in terra, & caput factus est corporis sui Ebr. 1. & 12. Apoc. 3. per filium hominis, non humanitas & benignites Dei, sed Christus, cui appropriatur hoc nomen fi- lius hominis, notatur, qui â Daniele etiam ita voca- tus est cap. 7. Neque hic imago decreti Dei de populo Judaico, sed regni & majestatis Christi exhibetur, cui omnia rectius congruunt, qui in solio Majesta- tis divinæ residens currum Evangelicum guber- nat. Thronus ille super firmamentum constitutus est: Quia Christus Majestate & potestate sua etiam cœlis sublimior est, Ebr. 7. Non positu locali, sed magnitudine gloriæ. Quod agnoscit etiam Junius, quod omnipotentia Christi & situs filii exhibeatur. Si- tus quidem, quod solium dicitur fuisse positum super expansum illud, & supra animalium caput, id est, (ut vulgo loquitur Apostolus, ἐν τοῖς ὑπερερανίοις, in locis supercœlestibus (ut ita loquamur) supra omne no- men & potestatem, ut & Eph. 1. Sic enim agnosci- mus majestatem Christi in omnes res creatas, cœlestes, terrestres, animatas, inanimas in, infinitum imperium obtinere. Species vero eandem majestatem amplius explicat, q um dicitur solium Speciem habuisse Sap- phiri, qui lapis ad Berillum quidem thalassium colore accedit proxime, sed eo minus marinæ viriditatis ha- bet, & auri fulgorem in cyaneo colore præfert: Quæ ratione docemur ipsam cælorum, rerumque omnium cœlestium gloriam, omnibus numeris à gloria Christi superari, ut cymatilem colorem, atque thalassium su- perat cyaneus & Sapphirinus. Hæc Junius. Colloca- tus autem est Filius hominis super illo throno, quia Christus collocandus erat ad dextram Dei, in thro- no majestatis, ut per ministerium verbi Ecclesiam in orbe terrarum colligeret & gubernaret. Porro videtur quasi species Chasmal, velut aspectus ignis in- trinsecus ejus per circuitum, à lumbis ejus desuper, & à lumbis ejus usque deorsum quasi species ignis splen- dentis in circuitu. Homo ille (Jesus Christus) à tergo (iursum & deorsum) habet lucidissimum ignem, quod admirandum de se splendorem ejicit. Chri- stus enim habitat in Majestate, & luce ineffabili, ut OSIANDER explicat. Iris autem apparet circa illam lucem, ut doceamur, hanc majestatem Christi salutarem esse generi humano, siquidem omnes in hunc θεάνθρωπον credentes cum patre cœlesti re- conciliantur, & in gratiam recipiantur.

## 1:27
Vers. 27. AND I SAW AS IT WERE THE APPEARANCE OF AMBER, LIKE THE APPEARANCE OF FIRE WITHIN IT ROUND ABOUT; FROM HIS LOINS, AND UPWARD, AND FROM HIS LOINS EVEN DOWNWARD I SAW AS IT WERE THE APPEARANCE OF SHINING FIRE ROUND ABOUT) This is an ἔκθεσις correctly noted by the seventy elders from a comparison of the passage which is below, 8, 2. Therefore this passage is to be rendered: I saw the color of amber, and the form like fire inside and out. (For this is בית לה סביב) from the appearance of the loins to the parts above: (amber:) from the appearance of the loins even to the lowest parts, the appearance of fire, and of its shining round about. This is an image not of the divine nature, but of its decrees concerning the Jewish people, which correspond clearly with the execution. By fire, that is, by calamities, the people will not perish, but will be refined and purged: many will perish: the rest will survive.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET VIDI QVASI SPECIEM ELECTRI, VELUT ASPECTUM IGNIS INTRINSECVS EJUS PER CIRCUITUM; A LUMBIS EJUS, ET DESU- PER, ET A LUMBIS EJUS USQVE DEORSUM VIDI QVASI SPECIEM IGNIS SPLENDENTIS IN CIRCVITV) Est hic ἔκθεσις recte animadversa senibus LXX. ex collatione loci, qui infra est 8, 2. Reddendus ergo fic locus: Vidi colorem electri, & formam velut ignis intus atque extra. (Hoc enim est בית לה סביב) à specie lumbo- rum ad superna: (electrum:) à specie lumborum ad infima us- que, speciem ignis, ejusque splendentis circumquaque. Est hæc imago non naturæ divinæ, sed decretorum ejus de populo Judaico, quæ plane cum executione respondent. Igne, id est, calamitatibus non interibit populus, sed excoquetur & purgabitnr: multi peribunt: reliqui supererunt.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. The prophet, being terrified, is strengthened so that he may fearlessly rebuke the rebellious sons of Israel, if by any means they might finally repent, and he is commanded to eat a book written within and without, in which were lamentations and woe.

Ver. 1. THIS VISION OF THE LIKENESS OF THE GLORY OF THE LORD) This verse coheres better in the Hebrew and Greek with the preceding ones. He calls the divine attributes the glory of God, justice, wisdom, which were understood through such an image.

IF the glory of God represented by these are the divine attributes, justice, equity, the wisdom of God, then that image will certainly be of the divine nature, not of his decrees concerning the Jewish people. Because those attributes are natural to God, justice, truth, and wisdom. Therefore, Grotius is not sufficiently consistent with himself. But, as I have said, the Prophet signifies that by that reason some likeness of the majesty of the Son of Man, Christ, was shadowed forth, who is the Lord of glory, 1 Corinthians 2, 8. The brightness of the Father's glory and the image of his substance, Heb. 1, 3. Moreover, Grotius's own confession contributes to the confirmation of our opinion, who observes at chapter 3, 6: That God tacitly intimates that he would sometime, in the calling of the Apostles to many peoples of deep speech and unknown language, send and find those who would obey. Why then could not the time of the New Testament also be looked to here, in which the chariot of the Gospel was to be carried by the Apostles through the whole world?

Ver. same. AND I SAW, AND I FELL UPON MY FACE) That is, seeing, I fell upon my face, struck by the consideration of such great things. Daniel 8, 17. See what is at Matthew 17, 6.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Propheta exterritus roboratur, ut intrepide arguat rebelles filios Israël, si quo modo tandem resipiscant, & jubetur comedere li- brum scriptum intus, & foris, in quo erant lamentationes & væ.

Vers. 1. HÆC VISIO SIMILITUDINIS GLORIÆ DOMINI) Melius hoc comma in Hebræo & Græco cum superioribus cohæret. Gloriam Dei vocat divinas proprie- tates, justitiam, sapientiam, quæ per talem imaginem intel- ligebantur.

SI gloria Dei his repræsentata, divinæ proprieta- tes sunt, justitia, æquitas, sapientia Dei, imago uti- que illa naturæ divinæ, non decretorum ejus de popu- lo Judaico erit. Quia istæ proprietates Deo sunt na- turales, justitia, veritas & sapientia. Itaque non satis sibi constat Grotius. Sed, uti dixi, significat Prophe- ta ea ratione aliquam similitudinem adumbratam majestatis filii hominis Christi, qui est Domi- nus gloriæ 1. Corinth. 2, 8. Splendor gloriæ patris & imago substantiæ ejus Ebr. 1, 3. Facit autem ad sen- tentiæ nostræ confirmationem propria Grotii con- fessio, qui ad cap. 3, 6. observat: Deum innuere tacite, se aliquando in vocatione Apostolorum ad po- pulos multos profundi sermonis, & ignotæ linguæ mis- surum & inventurum, qui pareant. Quidni ergo hic etiam respici potuerit tempus Novi Testamen- ti, quo currus Evangelii per Apostolos vehendus erat per totum orbem?

Vers. eod. ET VIDI, ET CECIDI IN FACIEM MEAM) Id est, videns cecidi in faciem meam, tantarum rerum conside- ratione perculsus. Daniel 8, 17. vide quæ ad Matth. 17, 6.

STAND UPON YOUR FEET) That is, arise. Thus in Matthew: ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε (arise and do not be afraid).

Ver. 4. AND SONS OF A HARD FACE.) σκληροπρόσωποι (hard-faced): that is, impudent, as the Chaldean interprets it here.
