## 2:5
Ver. 5. IF PERCHANCE THEY WILL HEAR, AND IF PERCHANCE THEY WILL CEASE AND THEY SHALL KNOW THAT A PROPHET WAS IN THE MIDST OF THEM) The best translation will be: that whether they hear, or whether they refrain (from hearing)—for it is a rebellious house—they shall certainly remember that a Prophet was sent to them. If they correct themselves, rightly: If not (which is more credible about them thus far, on account of their extreme stubbornness), they will be without excuse. Jerome on this passage: God speaks this with the affection of one who is in doubt, so that he may show the free will of man.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SI FORTE VEL IPSI AUDIANT, ET SI FORTE QVIESCANT ET SCIENT QVIA PRO- PHETA FUIT IN MEDIO EORUM) Optima erit ver- sio: ut sive audiant, sive abstineant (audire) est enim domus refractaria, certe meminerint Prophetam ad se missum. Si se corrigunt, recte: Si non (quod hactenus magis de illis credibile est, ob summam pertinaciam) erunt inexcusati. Hieronymus hoc loco: Loquitur autem hæc Deus ambigen- tis affectu, ut liberum hominis monstret arbitrium.

## 2:6
NEITHER FEAR THEIR WORDS) Counsels.

BECAUSE THEY ARE UNBELIEVERS AND SUBVERTERS WITH YOU AND YOU DWELL WITH SCORPIONS) Although they are contumacious, and thorny against you, nay (as it were) you dwell with scorpions. Thorny, that is, seeking to harm: Scorpions, that is, murderers.

BECAUSE IT IS AN EXASPERATING HOUSE) Although it is a refractory House.

Latin:

Vers. 6. NEQUE SERMONES EORUM METUAS) Consilia.

QUONIAM INCREDULI ET SUBVERSORES SUNT TECUM ET CUM SCORPIONIBUS HA- BITAS) Quanquam contumaces sunt, & spinei adversum te, imo (quasi) cum scorpionibus habitas. Spinei, id est nocere quærentes: Scorpiones, id est homicidæ.

QVIA DOMUS EXASPERANS EST) Quan- quam est Domus refractaria.

## 2:7
THEREFORE YOU SHALL SPEAK MY WORDS TO THEM) Do not refrain from speaking what has been entrusted to you: I will protect you.

IF PERCHANCE THEY HEAR AND CEASE) Whether they hear you, or refrain. Be secure, that is to say.

BECAUSE THEY ARE PROVOKERS) Although it (the people) is pleased with its own pertinacity: Yet they shall not be able to harm you.

Latin:

Vers. 7. LOQVERIS ERGO VERBA MEA AD EOS) Ne abstine tibi commissa eloqui: Ego te tuebor.

SI FORTE AUDIANT ET QVIESCANT) Si- ve te audiant, sive abstineant. Securus esto scilicet.

QVONIAM IRRITATORES SUNT) Quan- quam pertinaciæ ei (populo, placet:) Non poterunt tamen tibi nocere.

## 2:8
AND DO NOT BE EXASPERATING, AS THE EXASPERATING HOUSE) Do not you also be refractory, such as they are.

AND EAT WHATEVER I GIVE TO YOU) Admit it deeply into your mind. For Maimonides rightly noted in the Guide for the Perplexed 1. 2, that this is very often signified by the word אכל. Thus also the Latins say to turn into blood and juice.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET NOLI ESSE EXASPERANS, SICUT DOMUS EXASPERATRIX) Noli & tu esse refractarius, quales sunt illi.

ET COMEDE QVAECUNQVE EGO DO TI- BI) In animum penitus admitte. Id enim voce אכל saepif- sime significari recte notavit Maimonides Ductoris dubi tantium 1. 2. Sic & Latini dicunt in sanguinem & succum vertere.

## 2:9
IT WAS WRITTEN WITHIN AND WITHOUT) Such as that: Orestes written on the back and not yet finished. That is, the prophecy will be long, containing a long series of evils, as the following things explain: It will be a whole Iliad, the Greeks would say.

AND A SONG) Namely, a mournful one. For the subject matter requires that. Otherwise it is a general word, which signifies everything meditated upon. Thus μέλος is said to be from μελετᾶν. Thus also in Ps. 5, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ERAT SCRIPTUS INTUS ET FORIS) Tale illud: Scriptus & in tergo necdum finitus Orestes. Id est, Prophetia erit longa, longam seriem continens ma- lorum, ut explicant sequentia: Erit tota ilias, dicerent Graeci.

ET CARMEN) Nempe lugubre. Id enim requirit materia. Est alioqui vox generalis, quae omne meditatum significat. Sic μέλος dictum ἀπὸ τοῦ μελετᾶν. Sic & in Ps. 5, 1.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

The book having been eaten, the Prophet is given an adamantine face to rebuke the most hardened sons of Israel established in captivity, and he himself is appointed as a watchman of the people: and the glory of the Lord having been seen, he is commanded to sit bound and mute in his house.

Ver. 1.

EAT) Meditate, and receive it as true. Thus the Chaldean rightly here. The interpretation is subjoined below in com. 10.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Comesto libro datur Prophetae facies adaman- tina ad redarguendos durissimos filios Israel in captivitate constitutos, & ordinatur ipse in speculatorem populi: ac visa gloria Do- mini jubetur vinctus ac mutus in domo sua sedere.

Vers. 1.

COMEDE) Meditare, & ut verum suscipe. Ita hic Chaldaeus recte. Interpretatio infra subjicitur com. 10.

## 3:3
Ver. 3.

YOUR BELLY SHALL EAT, AND YOUR BOWELS SHALL BE FILLED WITH THIS ROLL) Let your belly eat, and your bowels be filled. Explain from the preceding.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

VENTER TUUS COMEDET, ET VISCERA TUA COMPLEBUNTUR VOLUMINE ISTO) Venter tuus comedat, & viscera tua compleantur. Explica ex prae- cedentibus.

## 3:3
IT WAS IN MY MOUTH AS SWEET HONEY) Where I rightly grasped the whole sense of those images which I had seen, I approved with my whole soul the divine justice in those matters.

Latin:

FACTUM EST IN ORE MEO QVASI MEL DULCE) Ubi omnem earum imaginum, quas videram, sensum recte comprehendi, toto animo approbavi justi- tiam divinam in illis rebus.

## 3:4
Ver. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

## 3:5
Ver. 5.

FOR YOU ARE NOT SENT TO A PEOPLE OF DEEP SPEECH AND OF AN UNKNOWN TONGUE, TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) This is an ἐπείφεσις of the adversative particle. The sense: You are not sent to a ἑτερόγλωσσον people, but to your own people of your own speech. You are not sent to Nineveh, as Jonah was: therefore fear nothing.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NON ENIM AD POPULUM PROFUNDI SER- MONIS, ET IGNOTAE LINGUAE TU MITTERIS, AD DOMUM ISRAEL) Est ἐπείφεσις voculae adversan- tis. Sensus: Non ad populum ἑτερόγλωσσον mitteris, sed ad populum tuum tui sermonis. Non mitteris ad Nini- ven, ut Jonas: quare nihil metue.

## 3:6
Ver. 6.

NOR TO MANY PEOPLES OF DEEP SPEECH AND OF AN UNKNOWN TONGUE, WHOSE WORDS YOU CANNOT HEAR) He tacitly hints that he will do this at some time in the calling of the Apostles: and will find those who will obey.

AND IF YOU WERE SENT TO THEM, THEY WOULD HEAR YOU) That is, there is more hope that they would obey your words than the Israelites: they are so corrupt. See a similar passage in Matt. 11, 23.

In the Hebrew text there is a difficulty on account of the negative particle, which seems to be redundant, concerning which see Glassius, Philol. Sacra, book 1, Tract. p. 138.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

NEQVE AD POPULOS MULTOS PRO- FUNDI SERMONIS ET IGNOTAE LINGUAE, QVORUM NON POSSIS AUDIRE SERMONEM) Tacite innuit se hoc aliquando facturum in vocatione Apo- stolorum: & inventurum, qui pareant.

ET SI AD ILLOS MITTERERIS, IPSI AU- DIRENT TE) Id est, propius spei est, ut illi tuis dictis pareant, quam ut Israelitae: adeo sunt corrupti. Simile vide Matth. 11, 23.

In Ebraeo textu ob particulam negativam, quae redundare videtur, difficultas est, de qua vide Glassium Philol. Sacra lib. 1. Tract. p. 138.

## 3:7
Ver. 7.

WITH A BRAZEN BROW) With a rubbed-hard brow. See above 2, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ATTRITA FRONTE EST) Fronte perfricta. Vide supra 2, 4.

## 3:8
Ver. 8.

BEHOLD I HAVE MADE THY FACE STRONGER THAN THEIR FACES, AND THY FOREHEAD HARDER THAN THEIR FOREHEADS) Provided you prepare yourself with obedience, I will add courage to you, by which you may despise their attacks.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ECCE DEDI FACIEM TUAM VALENTIO- REM FACIEBUS EORUM, ET FRONTEM TUAM DURIOREM FRONTIBUS EORUM) Modo te pares obsequio, animum tibi addam, quo eorum impetus con- temnas.

## 3:9
Ver. 9.

AS AN ADAMANT AND AS A FLINT HAVE I MADE THY FACE) In the Hebrew: I will make thy forehead as an adamant, which is harder than a rock. For there is a proverb שמירא תקיף מטינרא, an adamant harder than a rock. See Jer. 17. ver. 1.

FOR IT IS A PROVOKING HOUSE) Although it is a refractory house. Thus כי is often taken, as we have already noted several times.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

UT ADAMANTEM ET UT SILICEM DEDI FACIEM TUAM) In Hebraeo: Frontem tuam faciam ut adamantem, qui durior est rupe. Est enim proverbium שמירא תקיף מטינרא, adamas rupe durior. Vide Jer. 17. vers. 1.

QVIA DOMUS EXASPERANS EST) Quamvis est domus refractaria. Sic כי saepe sumitur, ut jam aliquo- ties notavimus.

## 3:11
Ver. 11.

TO THE CAPTIVITY) To those dispersed by the first deportation made by the Chaldeans, of whom you also were one.

THUS SAITH THE LORD GOD: IF PERADVENTURE THEY WILL HEAR, AND WILL FORBEAR) Better: Whether they hear, or whether they forbear to hear. As above 2, 5. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

AD TRANSMIGRATIONEM) Ad illos dispersos prima deportatione per Chaldaeos facta, quorum & tu fuisti.

HAEC DICIT DOMINUS DEUS: SI FORTE AUDIANT, ET QVIESCANT) Melius: Sive audiant, sive abstineant audire. Ut supra 2, 5. 7.

## 3:12
Ver. 12. AND THE SPIRIT TOOK ME UP) That is, compelled me to go to my countrymen. Both the preceding and following context imply this sense. AND I HEARD BEHIND ME THE VOICE OF A GREAT COMMOTION) Of a great noise: for that is what רעש means. He wishes to be understood as the choir of Angels approving the judgments of God. BLESSED BE THE GLORY OF THE LORD FROM HIS PLACE) That is, the praise of God is celebrated by the Angels. Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ. Luke 2:14.

Latin:

Verf. 12. ET ASSVMSIT ME SPIRITVS) Id est, compulit me, ut irem ad populares meos. Hunc sensum & præceden- tia & sequentia insinuant. ET AVDIVI POST ME VOCEM COMMO- TIONIS MAGNÆ) Magni strepitus: Id enim רעש. Intel- ligi vult chorum Angelorum Dei judicia approbantium. BENEDICTA GLORIA DOMINI DE LOCO SVO) Id est, laus Dei celebratur ab Angelis. Δόξα ἐν ὑψί- στοις Θεῷ. Luc. 2, 14.

## 3:13
Ver. 13. AND THE VOICE OF THE WINGS STRIKING ONE AGAINST ANOTHER) For those wings were both touching each other and were being struck with a great sound in that vision which Ezekiel had seen. See above 1:24. This interpreter often puts 'voice' for 'noise'. However, it is signified that great and atrocious things are being prepared. AND THE VOICE OF THE WHEELS FOLLOWING THE ANIMALS) The noise of the wheels, as the Cherubim were moving: that is, more severe deportations impending than the first. AND THE VOICE OF A GREAT COMMOTION) Great groans and lamentations. A little before, by the voice of a great commotion, Grotius understood the choir of angels, v. 12. Now, great groans and lamentations. But because that sound is excited by the motion of the wheels and the living creatures, the course of the word of God is noted. For Ezekiel was also a Prophet, not only the Apostles, and he was governed by the same Spirit, and was impelled to teach, as the Apostles were: But he also preached the same Christ: Acts 10:45, Heb. 13:8. And therefore the Vision proposed above in chapter 1 is also deservedly accommodated to his own ministry.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET VOCEM ALARVM PERCVTIENTIVM ALTERAM AD ALTERAM) Alæ enim illæ & contin- gebant se, & magno sono concutiebantur in imagine ea, quam viderat Ezechiel. Vide supra 1, 24. Vocem pro stre- pitu sæpe ponit hic interpres. Significatur autem, magna & atrocia parari. ET VOCEM ROTARVM SEQVENTIVM A- NIMALIA) Strepitum rotarum, motantibus Cherubinis: id est, deportationes graviores prima imminentes. ET VOCEM COMMOTIONIS MAGNÆ) Ma- gnos gemitus & lamenta. Paulo ante per vocem commotionis magnæ, Cho- rum angelorum intelligebat Grotius v. 12. Jam ma- gnos gemitus ac lamenta. Quia vero sonitus ille ex- citatur à rotarum & animantium motu, cursus ver- bi Dei notatur. Ezechiel enim etiam Propheta e- rat, non Apostoli tantum, & eodem Spiritu rege- batur, & ad docendum impellebatur, quo Apostoli: Sed & eundem Christum prædicabat: Actor. 10, 45. Ebr. 13, 8. Ideoq; Visio supra cap. 1. proposita etiam ad ipsius ministerium merito accommodatur.

## 3:14
Ver. 14. THE SPIRIT ALSO LIFTED ME UP, AND TOOK ME) And here ו is for 'but'. Although I saw these things, which terrified me, yet God compelled me to proceed to those who were deported. AND I WENT IN BITTERNESS IN THE INDIGNATION OF MY SPIRIT) In the Hebrew: Bitter in the heat of my spirit. That is, very sad, on account of those impending evils, of which I was ordered to be a 'bad messenger'. FOR THE HAND OF THE LORD WAS WITH ME STRENGTHENING ME) And here ו is for 'but'. The sense is: I was sad, but the power of God added courage to me, and the consciousness of my duty raised me up, as the following things show.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SPIRITVS QVOQVE LEVAVIT ME, ET AS- SVMSIT ME) ו hic est pro autem. Quanquam hæc vide- bam, quæ me terrebant, tamen Deus me compulit pergere ad illos deportatos. ET ABII AMARVS IN INDIGNATIONE SPI- RITUS MEI) In Hebræo: Amarus in æstu spiritus mei. Id est, valde tristis, ob mala illa imminentia, quorum esse jubebar κακὸς ἄγγελος. MANVS ENIM DOMINI ERAT MECVM CONFORTANS) Et hic ו est pro autem. Sensus est: tristis eram, sed vis Dei mihi addebat animum, ac me erigebat conscientia debiti officii, ut sequentia ostendunt.

## 3:15
Ver. 15. AND I CAME TO THE TRANSMIGRATION) To those Jews deported with me. TO THE HEAP OF NEW FRUITS) To Tel-abib. A name, but derived from the fertility of a place rising into hills. Thus also the Chaldean understood it: nor did Symmachus, Aquila, or Theodotion understand it otherwise, as Jerome teaches us in this place. This very place is Thelda, according to Ptolemy in Mesopotamia. AND I SAT, WHERE THEY SAT) That is, I stopped, in the part where the greatest part of them had their dwellings. For the interpreters followed the reading of the margin, which is ואשב. The text has ואשר, where perhaps it was ואשרנ, so that the sense might be that he had come to that region which is between the Chaboras and another river, which Ptolemy calls Σασκόραν, in which part they were dwelling. If it is lawful to indulge in such conjectures, and to correct the words of the Hebrew text, what will human audacity not take upon itself? But that place, which Grotius designates just now, confirms the opinion of Junius touched upon in the preface, about which let Junius be seen here. Namely, that the vision of the Prophet took place in Mesopotamia, and in that part of it which is across the Chaboras, surrounded on the West by the river Chaboras, and on the East by the Sascora. But above in the proem, Grotius had designated another place for the vision. AND I REMAINED THERE SEVEN DAYS MOURNING IN THE MIDST OF THEM) משמים, which is translated here as 'mourning', you would more correctly translate as 'solitary'. Aquila had translated it ἠρεμίζων, that is, says Jerome, resting and placed apart: namely, observing their life and actions, so that according to their manner he might utter threats more severely or more leniently.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET VENI AD TRANSMIGRATIONEM) Ad illos Judæos mecum deportatos. AD ACERVVM NOVARVM FRVGVM) Ad Te- labib. Nomen, sed ductum à loci in colles assurgentis ferti- litate. Sic & Chaldæus accepit: nec aliter Symmachus, A- quila, Theodotio, ut nos docet hoc loco Hieronymus. Hic ipse locus est Thelda, Ptolemæo in Mesopotamia. ET SEDI, VBI ILLI SEDEBANT) Id est, sub- stiti, qua in parte maxima pars illorum sedes habebat. Nam interpretes secuti sunt lectionem marginis, quæ est ואשב. Textus habet ואשר, ubi forte fuerit ואשרנ, ut sensus sit, venisse ad regionem illam, quæ est inter Chaboram & flu- men alterum, quod Ptolemæus vocat Σασκόραν, qua in par- te illa morabantur. Si talibus conjecturis indulgere fas est, & cor- rigere voces textus Ebræi, quid non sibi sumet au- dacia humana? Locus autem ille, quem designat modo Grotius, confirmat sententiam Junii in præ- fatione tactam, de qua hic videatur Junius. Quod nempe in Mesopotamia, ejusque ea parte facta sit visio Prophetæ, quæ trans Chaboram est circumfu- sa ab Occidente fluvio Chabora, ab Oriente Sascora. Supra autem in proœmio alium locum visionis designarat Grotius. ET MANSI IBI SEPTEM DIEBVS MOERENS IN MEDIO EORVM) משמים, quod hic vertitur mœ- rens, rectius vertas, solitarius. Aquila verterat ἠρεμίζων, id est, ait Hieronymus, quiescens & seorfim positus: nempe observans eorum vitam, & actiones, ut pro earum modo minas gravius aut remissius eloqueretur.

## 3:16
Ver. 16. AND WHEN SEVEN DAYS HAD PASSED) Which could have been sufficient for Ezekiel to know their vices.

Latin:

Vers. 16. CVM AVTEM PERTRANSISSENT SEPTEM DIES) Qui sufficere poterant Ezechieli ad cognoscenda illorum vitia.

## 3:17
Ver. 17. I HAVE GIVEN THEE A WATCHMAN TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) God sharply stimulates the hesitating man to fulfill his duty, comparing the Prophet to a man set on a watchtower by a king, who, if he sees danger from afar and does not announce it, falls into danger himself.

AND THOU SHALT HEAR THE WORD FROM MY MOUTH, AND SHALT ANNOUNCE IT TO THEM FROM ME) So that what you hear from me, you may announce to them in my name.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SPECVLATOREM DEDI TE DOMVI ISRAEL) Cunctantem Deus ad officium implendum acriter exstimu- lat, Prophetam comparans homini in specula constituto à rege, qui si eminus periculum videns non annuntiaverit, ipse in periculum incidit.

ET AVDIES DE ORE MEO VERBVM, ET ANNVNTIABIS EIS EX ME) Vt quod de me audies, id ipsis meo nomine annunties.

## 3:18
Ver. 18. IF WHEN I SAY TO THE WICKED: THOU SHALT SURELY DIE) When it is commanded to be said: absolutely, if you continue thus, destruction hangs over you. For the following things show that this is to be understood with a tacit condition: That he may turn from his wicked way, and live. There is a broader explanation of these words below in chapter 18.

THE SAME WICKED MAN SHALL DIE IN HIS INIQUITY) Because of his sins.

BUT HIS BLOOD I WILL REQUIRE FROM THY HAND) That is, you will be guilty of his death, no less than he himself. Blood, among the Hebrews, with the species taken for the genus, is called every destruction. See Gen. 9:5.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SI DICENTE ME AD IMPIVM: MORTE MO- RIERIS) Jubente dici: omnino, si ita pergis, exitium tibi imminet. Nam cum conditione tacita hoc intelligendum ostendunt sequentia: Vt avertatur à via sua impia, & vivat. Est horum verborum latior explicatio infra c. 18.

IPSE IMPIVS IN INIQVITATE SVA MO- RIETVR) Ob peccata sua.

SANGVINEM AVTEM EJVS DE MANV TVA REQVIRAM) Id est, tu de morte ipsius reus eris, non mi- nus quam ipse. Sanguis Hebræis, specie sumta pro genere, vocatur omnis interitus. Vide Gen. 9, 5.

## 3:19
Ver. 19. BUT YOU HAVE DELIVERED YOUR SOUL) You will have delivered yourself.

Latin:

Vers. 19. TV AVTEM ANIMAM TVAM LIBERASTI) Tu temet liberaveris.

## 3:20
Ver. 20. BUT IF THE JUST MAN SHALL HAVE TURNED) He shall have turned himself away from the right path. See below 18, 24.

I WILL PLACE A STUMBLING BLOCK BEFORE HIM) I will cause him to fall.

AND HIS JUSTICES SHALL NOT BE IN REMEMBRANCE) So far is it, namely, that the virtues of parents absolve wicked men.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SED ET SI CONVERSVS JVSTVS A JVSTITIA SVA FVERIT) Averterit se à via recta. Vide infra 18, 24.

PONAM OFFENDICVLVM GORAM EO) Fa- ciam ut ruat.

ET NON ERVNT IN MEMORIA JVSTITIÆ EJVS) Tantum abest, scilicet ut homines sceleratos ab- solvant parentum virtutes.

## 3:21
Ver. 21. BUT IF YOU SHALL HAVE ANNOUNCED TO THE JUST, THAT THE JUST MAN MAY NOT SIN) That is, you shall have warned a good man, that he may not follow the examples of so many evils.

AND HE SHALL NOT HAVE SINNED) He shall not have sinned, take this here in a more serious sense, that is, knowingly, and with deliberate intent he shall not have stumbled against the law.

LIVING HE SHALL LIVE) He shall certainly be preserved in life.

Latin:

Vers. 21. SI AVTEM ANNVNCIAVERIS JVSTO, VT NON PECCET JVSTVS) Id est, monueris virum bonum, ne tot malorum sequatur exempla.

ET ILLE NON PECCAVERIT) Non peccaverit, hic sume in sensu graviore, id est, sciens, ac deliberato non impegerit in legem.

VIVENS VIVET) Certo in vita conservabitur.

## 3:22
Ver. 22. AND THE HAND OF THE LORD WAS UPON ME) Again, that is to say. See above 1, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET FACTA EST SVPER ME MANVS DO- MINI) Iterum scilicet. Vide supra 1, 3.

## 3:23
Ver. 23. AND BEHOLD, THERE THE GLORY OF THE LORD) The image of a man partly fiery, partly of electrum, as above and below in chapter 8.

Osiander more correctly: The Son of God to be incarnate appeared to me, in the form of a man, in that majesty which I had seen when the four living creatures and the four wheels appeared to me, which vision is described at length above in the first chapter. The Lord signified, however, by the repetition of that vision, that He would multiply the subjects of His heavenly kingdom through the ministry of the Prophet Ezekiel. For it would come to pass that, having heard the sermons of the Prophet, some would be converted and believe in the Messiah. For Ezekiel prophesied excellently concerning Christ the Savior, as we shall see below (especially in chapter 34). For the Lord is present to the ministry of the word, and works through the Holy Spirit, so that the hearers may believe and be saved.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ECCE, IBI GLORIA DOMINI) Ima- go hominis partim ignea, partim ex electro, ut supra & infra c. 8.

Rectius Osiander: Apparuit mihi filius Dei in- carnandus, in forma hominis, in majestate illa, quam videram, cum mihi quatuor animalia, & quatuor rotæ apparerent, quæ visio, supra capite primo pro- lixe est descripta. Significabat autem Dominus per repetitionem illius visionis, se per ministerium Prophetæ Ezechielis, subditos cœlestis sui regni multiplicaturum. Futurum enim, ut auditis con- cionibus Prophetæ, aliqui converterentur, atque in Messiam crederent. Ezechiel enim de Christo Servatore præclare est vaticinatus, ut infra (præ- sertim cap. 34.) videbimus. Dominus enim adest ministerio verbi, & operatur per Spiritum San- ctum, ut Auditores credant & salventur.

## 3:24
Ver. 24. GO IN, AND SHUT YOURSELF UP IN THE MIDST OF YOUR HOUSE) Do not go out from there before I have revealed to you future things, both by signs and by words, which is done in the following chapters, up to the eleventh. This image was of a besieged city.

Latin:

Vers. 24. INGREDERE, ET INCLVDERE IN MEDIO DOMVS TVÆ) Ne inde exeas, priusquam tibi res futu- ras tum per signa, tum per verba revelaverim, quod fit se- quentibus capitibus, usque ad undecimum. Imago hæc erat obsessæ urbis.

## 3:25
Ver. 25. BEHOLD, BONDS HAVE BEEN GIVEN UPON YOU, AND THEY SHALL BIND YOU IN THEM) The future for the imperative. Let them place bonds upon you, and let them bind you: your own household, that is, so that you may also bear the image of the future captivity.

AND YOU SHALL NOT GO OUT FROM THE MIDST OF THEM) In the Hebrew; Into the midst of them: that is, into the crowd.

Latin:

Vers 25. ECCE DATA SVNT SVPER TE VINCV- LA, ET LIGABVNT TE IN EIS) Futurum pro Impe- rativo. Imponant tibi vincula, & legent te: domestici scili- cet tui, ut sic quoque captivitatis futuræ geras imaginem.

ET NON EGREDIERIS DE MEDIO EORVM) In Hebræo; In medium eorum: id est, in turbam.

## 3:26
Ver. 26. AND MAKE YOUR TONGUE CLEAVE TO YOUR PALATE, AND YOU SHALL BE MUTE) That is, as if mute, for no one at that time will approach you.

NOR AS A MAN REBUKING) In the Hebrew: You shall not be for a man arguing. There will be no one whom you may chastise with words.

BECAUSE IT IS A REBELLIOUS HOUSE) Refractory. Although they know that you are here and are a Prophet, they will not care, however, to learn from you what is salutary.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET LINGVAM TVAM ADHÆRERE FACIEM PALATO TVO, ET ERIS MVTVS) Id est, quasi mu- tus, nemo enim isto tempore ad te accedet.

NEC QVASI VIR OBJVRGANS) In Hebræo: Non eris in virum arguentem. Nemo erit, quem verbis castiges.

QVIA DOMVS EXASPERANS EST) Refrattaria. Cum norint, te hic esse & esse Prophetam, non curabunt tamen à te discere, quæ sunt salutaria.

## 3:27
Ver. 27. BUT WHEN I SHALL HAVE SPOKEN TO YOU) When I shall have explained all future things to you.

I WILL OPEN YOUR MOUTH) I will give you the power of going out and speaking to them what you shall have learned from me.

HE WHO HEARS, LET HIM HEAR, AND HE WHO REFRAINS, LET HIM REFRAIN) He who wishes to abstain from hearing, let him abstain at his own peril.

Latin:

Vers. 27. CVM AVTEM LOCVTVS FVERO TIBI) Ubi omnia futura tibi exposuero.

APERIAM OS TVVM) Faciam tibi potestatem exeundi & loquendi ad eos, quæ à me didiceris.

QVI AVDIT, AVDIAT, ET QVI QVIESCIT QVIESCAT) Qui abstinere ab audiendo vult, abstineat suo periculo.

## 4:1 Argument
SECTION I. THREATS AGAINST THE JEWS. CHAPTER IV.

The prophet is commanded to represent the siege of Jerusalem, and to sleep upon his left side for 390 days, and upon his right for 40 days, and to eat vile and foully prepared food because of the sins of so many years of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, to designate the calamity of the children of Israel and the siege and affliction of Jerusalem.

Ver. 1.

TAKE THEE A BRICK) Not baked, that is, clay.

AND SHALT PORTRAY UPON IT THE CITY OF JERUSALEM) Namely, by the plastic art, which this prophet, as one most skilled in architecture, had learned. Jerome, following Symmachus, thinks that πλινθίον is a tablet, and a sketch made in the dust.

Latin:

SECTIO I. COMMINATIONES ADVERSVS JUDÆOS. CAPUT IV.

Propheta figurare jubetur obsidionem Jerusa- lem, ac dormire super latus sinistrum 390. super dexterum 40. diebus, & vilem ac fœ- de confectum cibum comedere ob peccata tot annorum domus Israëlis, & domus Ju- da, ad designandam calamitatem filiorum Israël & obsidionem atque afflictionem Hierosolymæ.

Vers. 1.

SVME TIBI LATEREM) Non coctum, id est, argillam.

ET DESCRIBES IN EO CIVITATE JERV- SALEM) Nempe plastica arte, quam hic Propheta, ut ar- chitecturæ peritissimus, didicerat. Hieronymus ex Symma- cho putat πλινθίον esse abacum, & in pulvere factam σκια- γραφίαν.

## 4:2
Ver. 2.

AND SHALT SET A SIEGE AGAINST IT) Fashion a figure of a siege around the city,

AND SHALT BUILD FORTS) In Hebrew דיק, a wooden tower: concerning which see Vegetius 4, 17. Josephus in his description of this siege: 'The Babylonian, having built great towers of earthworks, from them kept off those who were standing on the walls.' And shortly after: 'They were destroyed by the missiles which the enemies hurled at them from the towers.'

AND SHALT CAST A MOUNT) Josephus in the aforementioned place: 'And he raised many mounds around the whole circuit, equal in height to the walls.'

AND SHALT SET CAMP AGAINST IT.) You shall figure a camp surrounded by the city.

AND SHALT SET BATTERING RAMS AGAINST IT) כרים, which is here in the Hebrew, signifies rams: but by rams, the Chaldean understands the leaders of the camps, whom David Kimchi follows. Others, engines of war. And indeed, if Epeus invented the ram as an engine of war at the Trojan War, it will not be surprising if its use was frequent so much later. But Vitruvius attributes the beginning of its invention to the Carthaginians in the siege of Gades: its perfection to Cetra the Chalcedonian. You have כרים for leaders in 2 Kings 11:4, 18. And thus the Chaldean translates it also below in 21:22, where the LXX have χάρακας, and here, βελοστάσεις.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET ORDINABIS ADVERSVS EAM OBSIDIO- NEM) Effinge figuram obsidionis circum urbem,

ET ÆDIFICABIS MVNITIONES) In Hebræo דיק, turrim ligneam: de qua vide Vegetium 4, 17. Josephus in descriptione hujus obsidii: ὁ Βαβυλώνιος πύργες μεγά- λων οἰκοδομήσας χωμάτων, ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ἀνεῖργε τὲς τοῖς τείχεσιν ἐφεστῶτας. Et mox: διεφθάρησαν ὑπὸ τῶν βελῶν ἅπερ ἀπὸ τῶν πύργων εἰς ἀυτὲς ἠκόντιζον οἱ πολέμιοι.

ET COMPORTABIS AGGEREM) Josephus di- cto loco: κὴ πολλὰ περὶ τὸν κύκλον ὅλον ἤγειρε χώματα τοῖς τείχεσι τὸ ὕψος ἶσα.

ET DABIS CONTRA EAM CASTRA.) Figu- rabis castra urbi circumdata.

ET PONES ARIETES IN GTRO) כרים, quod hic in Hebræo est, arietes significat: sed per arietes, castro- rum duces intelligit Chaldæus, quem sequitur David Kim- chi. Alii machinas. Et sane si arietem machinam bello Tro- jano invenit Epeus, non mirum erit, si tanto post tempore frequens ejus fuerit usus. At Vitruvius Carthaginiensibus in Gadium oppugnatione initium reperti tribuit: consumma- tionem Cetræ Chalcedonio. כרים pro ducibus habes 2. Reg. 11, 4. 18. Et sic vertit Chaldæus etiam infra 21, 22. ubi LXX. χάρακας, qui hic, βελοστάσεις.

## 4:3
Ver. 3.

AND TAKE TO THYSELF AN IRON PAN) Black and hard, such as were the sins of the Jews.

AND SETTING IT AS AN IRON WALL BETWEEN THEE, AND BETWEEN THE CITY) The prophet in this matter represents God, who is hindered by intervening sins from regarding the people. See Isaiah 59, 2.

AND THOU SHALT SET THY FACE TOWARD IT) The pan. Thou shalt look upon it with an angry countenance, just as God does the sins of the Jews.

AND IT SHALL BE FOR A SIEGE AND THOU SHALT COMPASS IT) Proceed in figuring the siege, as one that is to last a long time.

IT IS A SIGN TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) To all the descendants of Jacob.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET SVME TIBI SARTAGINEM FERREAM) Atram & duram, qualia erant peccata Judæorum.

ET PONENS EAM IN FERREVM MVRVM INTER TE, ET INTER CIVITATEM) Propheta in hac re Deum repræsentat, qui peccatis intercedentibus im- peditur, quo minus populum respiciat. Vide Esaiam 59, 2.

ET OBFRMABIS FACIEM TVAM AD EAM) Sartaginem. Irato vultu eam aspicies, quomodo Deus pec- cata Judæorum.

ET ERIT IN OBSIDIONEM ET CIRVCM- DABIS SAM) Perge in figuranda obsidione, ut quæ diu sit duratura.

SIGNVM EST DOMVS ISRAËL) Omnibus Ja- cobi posteris.

## 4:4
Ver. 4.

AND THOU SHALT SLEEP UPON THY LEFT SIDE) Thou shalt lie down. This lying down of Ezekiel signifies the supreme patience of God, and how burdensome it is to God to behold sins. The left side, as being less worthy, signifies the people of the ten tribes. The right side, as being more worthy, are Judah and Benjamin, in whose territory alone was the Temple.

AND THOU SHALT LAY THE INIQUITIES OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL UPON IT ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF THE DAYS, WHEREIN THOU SHALT SLEEP UPON IT) Thou shalt lie down: that is, from the days thou shalt understand for how many years I have silently endured their sins. For days were given to Ezekiel for as many years of divine patience, as will immediately follow.

AND THOU SHALT BEAR THEIR INIQUITY) Thou shalt carry it in a sign.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET TV DORMIES SVPER LATVS TVVM SI- NISTRVM) Cubabis. Cubatio hæc Ezechielis patientiam Dei summam, ac Deo molestissimam in spectandis pecca- tis significat. Latus sinistrum, ut minus dignum, significat populum decem tribuum. Latus dextrum, utpote dignius, sunt Judas & Benjamin, in quorum solo Templum.

ET PONES INIQVITATES DOMVS ISRAEL SVPER EO NVMERO DIERVM, QVIBVS DOR- MIES SVPER ILLVD) Cubabis: id est, ex diebus intel- liges per quot annos ego illorum peccata tacitus pertule- rim. Nam dies Ezechieli dati sunt pro totidem annis di- vinæ patientiæ, ut statim sequetur.

ET ASSVMES INIQVITATEM EORVM) Feres in signo.

## 4:5
Ver. 5.

THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY DAYS) So many years are from the fall of Solomon to the deportation of the ten tribes by Shalmaneser, through which the men of those tribes ceased to be a nation.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

TRECENTOS ET NONAGINTA DIES) Tot anni sunt à lapsu Solomonis ad deportationem decem tri- buum per Salmanaffarem, per quam illarum tribuum ho- mines gens esse desierunt.

## 4:6
Ver. 6.

YOU SHALL SLEEP UPON YOUR RIGHT SIDE

SECONDLY.) A transposition, for: you shall lie on the other side, and that on the right side.

YOU SHALL BEAR THE INIQUITY OF THE HOUSE OF JUDAH) You shall carry it in a sign, as above.

FORTY DAYS) How many years there are from the covenant renewed by Josiah to the destruction of the city and the temple.

The first and most serious doubt here is, whether the years of the offending that continues are to be understood, or rather the years of the punishment of iniquity to be borne? For the words of the text seem to imply this latter, which Jerome, the Ordinary Gloss, Pradus, Maldonatus, Tirinus, Menochius, Cornelius, as well as B. Hülsemannus, have also assumed, and Jerome calculated it at length, whom the others also follow.

If, however, you should judge that the time of bearing the iniquity is expressed, which Chronologists especially think, and which we do not entirely deny, the calculation of Grotius will not hold up at all. For from the fall of Solomon to the deportation by Shalmaneser, 390 years are not counted; since not even three hundred years have passed from the beginning of Solomon's reign until that deportation. Therefore, Tremellius indeed begins these 190 years from the time when Solomon fell into idolatry, 1 Kings ch. 11, which he assigns to the 27th year of his reign. But he ends it not at the deportation of Shalmaneser, but in the 23rd year of Nebuchadnezzar, or the fifth from the devastation of the temple. But Scaliger, Buntingus, Calvisius, Johannes Temporarius, D. Behm, and Clemens Schubertus more correctly begin these years from the death of Solomon, or rather from the beginning of the apostasy of the ten tribes, and end them at the final siege of Jerusalem, which took place in the last times of Zedekiah. For they think the term from which is expressly defined here, when they are called the years of the INIQUITIES OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL: by which is designated the notable sin of the whole house of Israel. But no sin in the history of the Israelite kings is as famous as the defection of Jeroboam, when by erecting golden calves in Dan and Bethel, he both sinned himself and caused the whole kingdom of Israel to sin, which is everywhere most gravely exaggerated by Holy Scripture: 1 Kings 12, 20. 28. ch. 13, 34. ch. 14, 9. 16. ch. 15, 26. But the term to which becomes clear from the intention of this prophecy; for this was to describe the siege of Jerusalem, and therefore the time of it is defined. Because for 390 days the Prophet is commanded to bear the sins of Israel, which days, if each is computed for each year, end with the time of the siege. Calvisius collects the years in Isag. Chronolog. 140. p. 202. with the beginning made from Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin, at the beginning of his reign, immediately after the death of Solomon, in the year of the world 2969.

Some, however, begin the years of the sins of the House of Judah from the 19th year of Josiah, and end them in the 23rd of Nebuchadnezzar, in which Nebuzar-adan led away the remnants of the Jewish people. But by others these years are ended, just as the preceding ones, at the devastation of the first temple; to which Ezekiel manifestly looks in his vision of the siege: and so these 40 years must be begun from the 13th year of Josiah. For Zedekiah reigned 11 years. Jehoiachin 11. To these let there be added, to complete the 40 years, 18 years subtracted from the 31 years of Josiah, and there will remain the 13th year of Josiah, in which Jeremiah began to prophesy, Jer. 1, verse 2. ch. 25, 3. When in the preceding twelfth year of Josiah the kingdom had been purged from idol-mania, 2 Chron. 34, 3. and following. But the Jews, at this purging and the sermons of Jeremiah, were made no better, as Jeremiah himself complains in ch. 25, 3. To which place of Jeremiah, Ezekiel, who was most familiar with Jeremiah, in the definition of the 40 years of the sins of the house of Judah, in the judgment of D. Behm, undoubtedly looked. Nevertheless, a more accurate account of the sacred chronicle teaches that a calculation must be added to the former opinion, so that the beginning may be taken from the eighteenth year, in which both the reformation of Josiah and the renewal of the divine covenant truly took place, as can be seen in the Chronological tables, but the end should be established not in the πανωλεθρίᾳ (total destruction) of the temple in the thirty-sixth year from that reformation, but in the most recent deportation of the Israelites carried out by Nebuzaradan in the 23rd year of Nebuchadnezzar, Jer. 52, 30. If you say that the words of the Prophetic text do not refer to the years of the duration of the offense, but to the bearing of the iniquity of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, I answer: the words of the text flow according to the fountains of truth thus: And you, lie upon your left side, and place the INIQUITY of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of days that you shall lie upon it, you shall bear their iniquity. And I have given you the YEARS OF THEIR INIQUITY according to the number of days, three hundred and ninety days, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel. From which it is manifest, if the words are accurately weighed, that both the years of iniquity are expressed, namely how long it lasted and was tolerated by God, and that in place of those years as many days were given for the iniquity to be borne by the Prophet, which is a symbol, as some judge, that the city is to be besieged for so many days, which number they gather from a comparison of chapter 39, v. 2, 3, Jerem. 52, 6, with chapter 32, 1, c. 34, 18, c. 37, 6. Namely, that Jerusalem began to be besieged in the 9th year of Zedekiah in the 10th month, and the siege lasted until the 11th year, 4th month of Zedekiah, that is, for 18 full months: but from these must be deducted those months in which Nebuchadnezzar was forced to dissolve the siege due to Egyptian relief, Jerem. 32, 1, chapter 33, 1. Therefore, this siege lasted for 14 months, which according to the Jewish calculation, assigning 28 days to a month, make 390. Grotius will now suggest another calculation of the days. Regarding the remaining 40 days of bearing the iniquity of the house of Judah, there is another reason. For they gather that these were not a symbol of the duration of the siege from the fact that the Prophet is not ordered to eat the kind of bread with them that he was to live on for the 390 days of bearing the iniquity of the house of Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

DORMIES SVPER LATVS TVVM DEXTRVM

SECVNDO.) Transpositio, pro: alterum cubabis, idque in dextrum latus.

ASSVMES INIQVITATEM DOMVS JVDÆ) Feres in figno, ut fupra.

QVADRAGINTA DIEBVS) Quot anni sunt à renovato per Josiam fœdere, ad excidium urbis & templi.

Dubium hic primo gravissimum est, Num anni durantis offensionis, an vero portandæ pœnæ iniquita- tis intelligantur? Nam hoc posterius videntur ver- ba textus inferre, quod etiam assumsit Hieronymus, Glossa ordinaria, Pradus, Maldonatus, Tirinus, Menochius, Cornelius, ut & B. Hülsemannus, cal- culumque duxit prolixe Hieronymus, quem & sequuntur cæteri.

Si tamen tempus portandæ iniquitatis expressum esse censeas, quod imprimis Chronologi putant, neque omnino abnuimus, minime sibi constabit Calculus Grotii. A lapsu enim Salomoneo, ad de- portationem Salmanassaris non numerantur 390. anni; Quum ne quidem trecenti anni lapsi sint ab initio regiminis Salomonei usque ad illam depor- tationem. Ideo Tremellius inchoat quidem hos 190. annos, ab eo tempore, quo Salomon in ido- lolatriam prolapsus est, 1. Reg. 11. cap. quod in 27. annum regni ejus rejicit. Sed finit id non in de- portatione Salmanassaris, sed in anno 23. Nabucho- donosoris, vel quinto à devastatione templi. Rectius vero Scaliger, Buntingus, Calvisius, Johannes Tempo- rarius, D. Behm. Clemens Schubertus annos hosce in- choant à morte Salomonis, vel potius initio ἀποστα- σίας decem tribuum, finiunt in ultima Hierosoly- mæ obsidione, Zedekiæ temporibus ultimis facta. Terminum enim à quo expresse hic definitum pu- tant, cum vocantur anni INIQUITATUM DO- MUS ISRAEL: quo designatur peccatum insigne tatius domus Israël. Nullum autem in Historia Regum Israëliticorum adeo celebre est ac Jeroboa- mi defectio, cum aureos vitulos in Dan & Bethel erigendo, & peccavit ipse, & totum Israëlis re- gnum peccare fecit, quod passim à Sacra Scriptura exaggeratur gravissime: 1. Reg. 12, 20. 28. cap. 13, 34. cap. 14, 9. 16. cap. 15, 26. Terminus autem ad quem ex intentione hujus Prophetiæ elusescit; Hæc enim erat obsidionem Hierosolymæ descri- bere, ideoque tempus ejusdem definitur. Quia 290. diebus Propheta jubetur portare peccata Israëlis, qui dies, si singuli pro annis singulis com- putentur, finiuntur cum obsidionis tempore. An- nos colligit Calvisius Isag. Chronolog. 140. p. 202. initio facto à Jeroboam, qui peccare fecit Israël, sub initium regni sui, statim ab obitu Salomonis, Anno mundi 2969.

Annos autem peccatorum Domus Judæ nonnul- li quidem à 19. Josiæ anno inchoant, finiuntque in 23. Nebucadnezaris, quo Nebusar-Adan reliquias populi Judaici abduxit. Ab aliis vero hi anni fini- untur, perinde ut præcedentes, in devastatione templi prioris; ad quam Ezechiel in sua obsidionis visione manifeste respicit: adeoque inchoandi erunt 40. hi anni à Josiæ 13. Nam Zedekias regna- vit 11. annis. Jechonias 11. His addantur ad com- plendos 40. annos. 18. anni detracti ab annis 31. Jo- siæ, relinquetur 13. annus Josiæ, quo Jeremias pro- phetare cœpit, Jerem. 1. vers. 2. c. 25, 3. Quum anno præcedente duodecimo Josiæ regnum ab Idolo- mania repurgatum esset 2. Chron. 34, 3. & seqq. At Judæi ad hanc repurgationem & Jeremiæ concio- nes nihil meliores facti, ut Jer. 25, 3. ipse conque- ritur. Ad quem Jerem. locum Ezechiel Jeremiæ fa- miliarissimus, in definitione 40. annorum peccato- rum domus Judæ, D. Behmio judice, procul dubio respexit. Accuratior tamen Chronici sacri com- putus priori sententiae Calculum adjiciendum esse docet, ut initium a decimo octavo capiatur, quo & reformatio Josiae, & renovatio foederis divini reve- ra facta, ut in tabellis Chronologicis videre est, finis autem constituatur non in templi πανωλεθρίᾳ tri- gesimo sexto anno ab illa reformatione facta, sed in novissima Israelitarum deportatione per Nebuza- radan facta anno Nebucadnezaris 23. Jer. 52, 30. Si dicas, verba textus Prophetici non annos durantis offensionis, sed portandae iniquitatis domus Israelis & domus Juda inferre, respondeo; verba textus juxta fontes veritatis ita fluunt: Et tu cuba super latus tuum sinistrum, & pone INIQVITATEM domus Israel super illud: secundum numerum dierum, quibus jacueris super illud, portabis iniquitatem eorum. Et ego dedi tibi ANNOS INIQVITATIS eorum ad numerum dierum, trecentos & nonaginta dies, & portabis iniquitatem domus Israel. E quibus manife- stum est, si verba accurate expendantur, & Annos iniquitatis expressos esse, quot nempe illa durarit, & tolerata a Deo fuerit, & loco istorum annorum totidem datos fuisse dies portandae a Propheta ini- quitatis, quod Symbolum, quod tot diebus obsiden- da urbs sit, fuisse nonnulli censent, quem numerum colligunt e collatione cap. 39, v. 2. 3. Jerem. 52, 6. cum cap. 32, 1. c. 34, 18. c. 37, 6. Quod nempe Jerusa- lem obsideri coeperit anno 9. Zedekiae mense 10. & obsidio durarit usque in annum 11. Mensem 4. Ze- dekiae, h. e. integris 18. mensibus: quibus vero de- mendi menses illi, quibus ob succursum Aegyptia- cum Nebucadnezar dissolvere obsidionem coactus fuit, Jerem. 32, 1. cap. 33, 1. Durasse ergo hanc obsi- dionem mensibus 14. qui juxta calculum Judaicum, mensi assignando 28. dies, efficiunt 390. Alium cal- culum dierum jam suggeret Grotius. De reliquis 40. diebus portandae iniquitatis domus Juda alia ra- tio est. Hos enim symbolum non fuisse durationis obsidionis ex eo colligunt, quod non jubetur Pro- pheta illis ejusmodi panes comedere, quibus vi- ctitandum ipsi erat per 390. dies portandae iniqui- tatis domus Israelis.

## 4:7
Vers. 7.

AND YOU SHALL TURN YOUR FACE TOWARD THE SIEGE OF JERUSALEM, AND YOUR ARM SHALL BE EXTENDED) Let it be bared. Which was the custom for combatants at that time. You shall imitate the attackers as much by a fierce countenance turned toward that region in which the city of Jerusalem is, as by a bared arm.

AND YOU SHALL PROPHESY AGAINST IT) That is, by these signs you shall pre-signify future things,

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET AD OBSIDIONEM JERVSALEM CON- VERTES FACIEM TVAM, ET BRACHIVM TVVM ERIT EXTENTVM) Esto nudatum. Qui mos pugnanti- bus illo tempore. Tam vultu atroce obverso in eam regio- nem, in qua est urbs Hierosolyma, quam brachio nudato oppugnatores imitaberis.

ET PROPHETABIS ADVERSVS EAM) Id est, signis istis res futuras praesignificabis,

## 4:8
Vers. 8.

BEHOLD, I HAVE SURROUNDED YOU WITH BONDS) I want you to remain in those bonds which your household members have placed upon you by my command, so that in this way also you may express the besieged city:

AND YOU SHALL NOT TURN YOURSELF FROM YOUR SIDE TO ANOTHER SIDE) So that you may express divine patience in this way.

UNTIL YOU COMPLETE THE DAYS OF YOUR SIEGE) Those 340 days which correspond to the days during which the scarcity of necessary things began to press upon the besieged city (for the siege itself lasted for almost two years, 1 Kings 25, 1, 2). See Jer. 37, 20, 38, 9. See also Josephus 12. He says 'your siege' because the necessity of remaining at home and not turning oneself, and the bonds, had the form of a siege. Now, the thing signifying is accustomed to be expressed by the name of the thing signified. But just as the scarcity lasted there for 390 days, so the burning of the city and Temple lasted for 40 days.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ECCE, CIRCVMDEDI TE VINCVLIS) Volo maneas in istis vinculis, quae tibi domestici meo jussu im- posuere, ut sic quoque urbem obsessam exprimas:

ET NON CONVERTES TE A LATERE TVO IN LATVS ALIVD) Ut divinam patientiam hoc modo exprimas.

DONEC COMPLEAS DIES OBSIDIONIS TVAE) Dies illos 340. qui respondent diebus, per quos urbem ob- sessam (ipsa enim obsessio duravit ferme per biennium, 1. Regum 25, 1. 2.) premere coepit rerum necessariarum pe- nuria. Vide Jer. 37, 20. 38, 9. Vide & Josephum 12. Obsi- dionis tuae dicit, quia domi manendi, neque se convertendi necessitas, & vincula obsidionis habebant figuram. Solet autem res figurans rei figuratae vocabulo exprimi. Sicut au- tem egestas ibi duravit per dies 390. ita incendium urbis ac Templi per dies 40.

## 4:9
Vers. 9. TAKE FOR YOURSELF WHEAT) That is, grain, as the Chaldean and the Greeks here.

AND BARLEY, AND BEANS, AND LENTILS, AND MILLET) For in besieged cities, bread is not usually made from wheat alone, but with many other things mixed in, so that the food may be drawn out longer.

AND VETCH) The Greeks translate כסמים as ὀλύραν (spelt). It is a kind of ζειᾶς (spelt), according to Herodotus. We learn from Homer that it was accustomed to be given to horses. Nevertheless, Herodotus teaches that among destitute nations, bread was also made from it. The Chaldean has כונתין, which signifies spelt: as can be seen in Exodus 9:32.

AND YOU SHALL PUT THEM INTO ONE VESSEL) You will make a mixture from it. AND YOU SHALL MAKE FOR YOURSELF BREAD ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF DAYS, DURING WHICH YOU SHALL SLEEP ON YOUR SIDE) that is, which may suffice for the time of 390 days, as follows. FROM TIME TO TIME YOU SHALL EAT IT) Just as much also per day.

Latin:

Vers. 9. SVME TIBI FRVMENTVM) Id est, triti- cum, ut hic Chaldaeus & Graeci.

ET HORDEVM, ET FABAM, ET LENTEM, ET MILIVM) Nam in obsessis urbibus non solent panes ex solo tritico, sed multis rebus aliis admixtis fieri, quo diu- tius protrahantur alimenta.

ET VICIAM) כסמים ὀλύραν vertunt Graeci. Est genus ζειᾶς, teste Herodoto. Equis solitum dari ex Homero discimus. Tamen apud gentes inopes etiam panem inde factum docet Herodotus. Chaldaeus habet כונתין, quod zeam significat: ut videre est Exod. 9, 32.

ET MITTES EAS IN VAS VNVM) Farragi- nem inde facies. ET FACIES TIBI PANES NVMERO DIERVM, QVIBVS DORMIES SVPER LATVS TVVM) id est, qui sufficere possint in tempus dierum 390. ut sequitur. A TEMPORE VSQVE AD TEMPVS COME- DES ILLVD) Tantundem quoque die.

## 4:10
BUT THE FOOD WHICH YOU SHALL EAT, SHALL BE IN WEIGHT TWENTY STATERS A DAY) That is, there shall be bread for you for the day, which might sometimes weigh less than a pound: since for those thrown into prison according to the law of the Twelve Tables, a pound of grain was given per day.

Latin:

CIBVS AVTEM QVO VESCERIS, ERIT IN PONDERE VIGINTI STATERES IN DIE) Id est, pa- nis in diem tibi erit, qui minus aliquando libra pendat: cum in nervum conjectis ex lege duodecim tabellarum libra farris in diem daretur.

## 4:11
AND YOU SHALL DRINK WATER BY MEASURE) The enemies cut off whatever veins of water they could, so that there was a scarcity of that thing also for the besieged.

Latin:

ET AQVAM IN MENSVRA BIBES) Hostes quascunque poterant aquarum venas intersciderunt, ita ut ejus quoque rei penuria esset obsessis.

## 4:12
Verse 12. AND AS A BARLEY CAKE YOU SHALL EAT IT) In the Hebrew: Furthermore, you shall eat a cake made of barley. Namely, during those forty days of the second lying down, so that the Jews may understand what they are to expect once the siege is finished.

AND WITH DUNG, WHICH COMES OUT OF A MAN, YOU SHALL COVER IT IN THEIR SIGHT) In the Hebrew: you shall bake. There will be such a scarcity of both cattle and wood, that they will make a fire from excrement, just as certain nations do from the dung of oxen.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET QVASI SVBCINERICIVM HORDEA- CEVM COMEDES ILLVD) In Hebræo: Præterea libum ex hordeo comedes. Nempe quadraginta illos diebus secundæ cubationis, ut intelligant Judæi, quid peracto obsidio ex- spectandum habeant.

ET STERCORE, QVOD EGREDITVR DE HOMINE, OPERIES ILLVD IN OCVLIS EORVM) In Hebræo: coques. Tanta erit & pecoris & ligni egestas, ut ex oleto ignem facturi sint, sicut quædam gentes ex boum egestu.

## 4:13
Verse 13. SO SHALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL EAT THEIR BREAD POLLUTED) From the contraction of the camp, Deut. 23:14. Jerome: To this day this opinion is kept among the people of the Jews, that they do not eat their bread with human dung.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SIC COMEDENT FILII ISRAEL PANEM SVVM POLLVTVM) Ex contractu oleri, Deut. 23, 14. Hieronymus: Vsque hodie in populo Iudæorum servatur ista sententia, ut non comedant panem suum in humano stercore.

## 4:14
AH AH LORD GOD) אהה is an interjection of supplication. The Chaldean: Receive my supplication. The LXX & Symmachus: Μηδαμῶς. Theodotion: ἆ.

CARCASS) A beast that has died by its own fate. See Deut. 14, 21.

AND TORN BY BEASTS) Exod. 22, 31. Levit. 17, 5.

FROM MY YOUTH) From my youth: from the time I began to use reason.

AND NO UNCLEAN FLESH HATH ENTERED INTO MY MOUTH) κρέας βέβηλον. That is, I have eaten nothing forbidden by the law. See a similar passage in Acts 10, 14. He means to say: If I have abstained from things unclean by the law, I should not be forced to use a thing unclean by nature. In certain Greek books it is κρέας ἑωλον, and in Theodoret, κρέας ἕωλον ἢ βέβηλον. Namely, concerning sacrifices for giving thanks to God, it is forbidden to eat of the previous day's food, Exod. 22, 29.

Latin:

A A A DOMINE DEVS) אהה est interjectio de- precativa. Chaldæus: Suscipe deprecationem meam. LXX. & Symmachus: Μηδαμῶς. Theodotion: ἆ.

MORTICINIVM) Pecudem fato suo mortuam. Vide Deut. 14, 21.

ET LACERATVM A BESTIIS) Exod. 22, 31. Levit. 17, 5.

A PVERITIA MEA) A juventute mea: ex quo ratione uti cœpi.

ET NON EST INGRESSA IN OS MEVM O- MNIS CARO IMMVNDA) κρέας βέβηλον. Id est, nihil edi lege vetitum. Vide simile Act. 10, 14. Vult dicere: Si cæ- teris abstinui per legem immundis, ne cogar, uti re per na- turam immunda. In quibusdam libris Græcis est, κρέας ἑω- λον, & apud Theodoretum, κρέας ἕωλον ἢ βέβηλον. Nempe de sacrificiis pro gratiis Deo agendis, vetitum pridianis vesci, Exod. 22, 29.

## 4:15
Vers. 15. BEHOLD, I HAVE GIVEN THEE COW'S DUNG FOR MAN'S DUNG) Namely, in such a way that the excrement of oxen shall signify filth.

AND THOU SHALT PREPARE THY BREAD UPON IT) That is, thou shalt bake, as above.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ECCE, DEDI TIBI FIMVM BOVM PRO STERCORIBVS HVMANIS) Nempe ita ut boum ege- stus significaturus sit oletum.

ET FACIES PANEM TVVM IN EO) Id est, coques, ut supra.

## 4:16
Vers. 16. BEHOLD, I WILL BREAK THE STAFF OF BREAD IN JERUSALEM) That is, bread, which is the sustenance of man. I will cause that which sustains the body to be lacking. Here the LXX have Στήριγμα, Symmachus and Theodotion have σερέωμα. See Lev. 26, 26. This is an explanation of the preceding types.

THEY SHALL EAT BREAD BY WEIGHT) Weighed out, and indeed sparingly.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ECCE, EGO CONTERAM BACVLVM PANIS IN JERVSALEM) Id est, panem, qui est susten- taculum hominis. Faciam ut desit, quo corpus sustentatur. Στήριγμα hic LXX. Symmacho & Theodotioni σερέωμα. Vide Lev. 26, 26. Hic est explicatio typorum præcedentium.

COMEDENT PANEM IN PONDERE) Appen- sum & quidem tenuiter.

## 4:17
SO THAT BREAD AND WATER FAILING) Finally, after long, meager meals.

EVERY ONE SHALL FALL TOWARD HIS BROTHER) Here and there he shall fall lifeless from hunger and thirst.

AND THEY SHALL PINE AWAY IN THEIR INIQUITIES) That is, or if any remain, they shall scarcely cling to their bones. In their iniquities, that is, on account of their sins.

Latin:

VT DEFICIENTIBVS PANE ET AQVA) Po- stremo, post longos pastus tenues.

CORRVAT VNVSQVISQVE AD FRATREM SVVM) Hic & illic exanimis cadat præ fame ac siti.

ET CONTABESCANT IN INIQVITATIBVS SVIS) Id est, aut si qui superfint, ii vix ossibus hæreant. In iniquitatibus suis, id est, ob peccata sua.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

By the shorn hairs of the head and beard of the Prophet, consumed in various ways, are designated the Jews who, on account of their sins, are to be consumed by famine and sword, or so that fathers may eat their sons, and sons their fathers, while the rest are to be led into captivity, where they shall be a reproach and a wonder to the nations, whose crimes they shall exceed.

Verse 1.

TAKE TO YOURSELF A SHARP SWORD) That is, a razor; for everything that cuts is in Hebrew חרב. The following addition demands this sense.

AND YOU SHALL PASS OVER YOUR HEAD, AND OVER YOUR BEARD) Cause it to shave off for you both the hairs of your head and the hairs of your beard. This is another very exact type of future events.

The prophet himself had to shave his beard and head to signify divine severity against his own body and the Jewish people.

Verse same.

AND YOU SHALL TAKE TO YOURSELF A BALANCE OF WEIGHT, AND YOU SHALL DIVIDE THEM) The balance is a symbol of divine justice, which measures out to each what is fair. The razor is divine vengeance. The balance, its equity. The hairs are the Jews: the division, the punishments attributed to each.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Per detonsos capitis & barbæ Prophetæ pilos varieque consumtos designantur Iudæi pro- pter sua peccata fame & gladio consumen- di, seu ut patres filios, & filii patres come- dant, reliqui vero in captivitatem ducendi, ubi sint opprobrium, & stupor gentium, qua- rum superabunt scelera.

Vers. 1.

SVME TIBI GLADIVM ACVTVM) Id est, no- vaculam; nam omne, quod abscincit, Hebræis est חרב Hunc sensum exigit adjectio sequens.

ET DVCES PER CAPVT TVVM, ET PER BARBAM TVAM) Fac ut & capillos & barbæ pilos tibi altondeat. Est hic alter typus valde exactus rerum futu- rarum.

Propheta ipse barbam & caput radere debuit ad significandam divinam severitatem in corpus suum & populum Judaicum.

Vers. eod.

ET ASSVMES TIBI STATERAM PONDERIS, ET DIVIDES EOS) Statera Symbolum divinæ justitiæ, quæ cuique admetitur,quod æquum est. Novacula est ultio divina. Statera, æquitas ejus. Pili sunt Judæi : divisio, pœ- næ cuique attributæ.

## 5:2
Verse 2.

YOU SHALL BURN A THIRD PART WITH FIRE IN THE MIDST OF THE CITY ACCORDING TO THE COMPLETION OF THE DAYS OF THE SIEGE) The seventy elders here make four parts, and for that reason they do not agree in many parts with the Hebrew which we indeed now have. That shows a discrepancy in older codices in matters not pertaining to the sum of piety. We shall follow the Masoretic Hebrew. Fire in this place signifies divine wrath, effective in various ways, and here especially through plague and famine, as these words are explained below in verse 12. For both plague burns, and famine burns. In the midst of the city: that is: you shall do this in that very model of the city which you have made for yourself out of clay. According to the completion of the days of the siege: That is, this will signify that which is to be, as long as the siege shall last.

It is not a sufficiently firm argument to be sought from the diverse interpretation of the LXX Interpreters to collect a diverse reading of the Hebrew Codices, as has been warned more often. Jerome corrects this LXX Interpreter here, and refutes that addition of a fourth part from the text. They sometimes added something of their own, so that they might express the sense according to their own judgment, not precisely rendering word for word. Theodotion and Aquila rendered it as it is in the Hebrew, τριτον. Jerome includes famine and plague in the punishment of fire, as is explained in verse 12, because they no less burn, migrate, and destroy men than fire, Lamentations 4:7, nor does Grotius deny it.

Verse same.

AND YOU SHALL TAKE A THIRD PART, AND YOU SHALL CUT WITH THE SWORD IN THE CIRCUIT OF IT) He designates those who were making a sortie from the City into the camps. See below verse 12.

Not only them, even if Pradus, Tremellius, and Cornelius might wish it, but also those who were led out of the city and slaughtered: for they are opposed to those who perished in the midst of the city. The other third part was consumed by plague and famine in the city, as is explained in verse 12; concerning the third, it is now added that it is to be scattered into exile.

Verse of the same.

AND A THIRD PART YOU SHALL SCATTER INTO THE WIND) That is, the third part shall be driven into exile, like chaff, which is scattered by the wind.

AND I WILL DRAW OUT A SWORD AFTER THEM) That is, I will cause them to be in perpetual fear, exposed to the violence and injuries of all. See below v. 12.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

TERTIAM PARTEM IGNI COMBVRES IN ME- DIO CIVITATIS JVXTA COMPLETIONEM DIE- RVM OBSIDIONIS) LXX. senes hic quatuor partes faci- unt, ac ob id cum Hebr. quòd quidem nos nunc habemus multis partibus non congruunt. Monstrat id codicum anti- quiorum, in rebus nihil ad pietatis summam spectantibus discrepantiam. Nos Hebræum Masoriticum sequemur.Ignis hoc loco iram divinam significat, variis modis efficacem, & hic maxime per pestem & famem, ut infrà hæc verba ex- plicantur v. 12. Nam & pestis urit, & fames urit. In medio civitatis: id est : facies hoc in ipsa illa formula urbis, quam tibi de argilla fecisti. Iuxta completionem dierum obsidionis: Id est, significabit hoc id, quod futurum est, quamdiu du- rabit obsidio.

Non satis firmum argumentum peti à diversa in- terpretatione LXX. Interpretum ad colligendam diversam Codicum Ebræorum lectionem sæpius monitum. Corrigit autem hic LXX. Interpret. Hieronymus, & προσθηκην illam quartæ partis è textu refellit. Addiderunt illi quandoque aliquid de suo, ut sensum exprimerent suo judicio, non præcise verbum verbo reddidere. Theodotion & Aquila reddidere, ut in Ebræo est τριτον. Includit autem Hieronymus supplicio ignis famem & pe- stem,uti explicatur v. 12. quia non minus exurunt, demigrant & perdunt homines, quam ignis, Thren. 4, 7. nec abnuit Grotius.

Vers. eod.

ET ASSUMES TERTIAM PARTEM, ET CON- CIDES GLADIO IN CIRCVITV EJVS) Eos desi- gnat, qui ex Urbe in castra eruptione faciebent. Vide infra v.12.

Non eos tantùm, etsi id Pradus etiam, Tremel- lius, & Cornelius velint, sed etiam eos, qui educti ex urbe trucidati sunt: opponuntur enim iis illi, qui in medio urbis periere. Altera tertia pars peste & fame absumta in urbe, ut v. 12. explicatur, de tertia additur jam, quod in exilium spargenda sit.

Vers. eod.

TERTIAM VERO ALIAM DISPERGES IN VENTVM) Id est, tertia pars propelletur in exsilium, ut paleæ, quæ à vento disperguntur.

ET GLADIVM NVDABO POST EGO) Id est, efficiam, ut in perpetuo sint metu, expositi omnium vio- lentiæ & injuriis. Vide infra v. 12.

## 5:3
Verse 3.

AND YOU SHALL TAKE A SMALL NUMBER FROM THERE, AND BIND THEM IN THE SKIRT OF YOUR MANTLE) Here are designated those who, by the permission of Nebuzaradan, remained in very small numbers in Judea. Those edges of the mantle signify that last point to which the goodness of God could extend itself, yet it was greatly despised by those remnants, to their own greatest harm. It must be small, that which is gathered in the fringes.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET SVMES INDE PARVVM NVMERVM, ET LIGABIS EOS IN SVMMITATE PALLII TVI) Hic illi designantur, qui permissu Nabuzardanis pauci admo- dum in Judæa mansere. Oræ istæ pallii significant ultimum illud, quo Dei bonitas extendere se poterat, valde tamen ab illis reliquis contemta. maximo ipsarum malo. Parvum sit oportet, quod in laciniis colligitur.

## 5:4
Verse 4.

AND YOU SHALL TAKE AGAIN FROM THEM, AND CAST THEM INTO THE MIDST OF THE FIRE, AND BURN THEM WITH FIRE: AND FROM IT A FIRE SHALL GO FORTH INTO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) The fire is the divine wrath, as we have just said, and as appears in many other places. That wrath, however, exerted itself upon those small remnants of the Jews in Judea through a certain civil war among them, some following the side of Gedaliah, a good man and a friend to the Chaldeans, others following Ishmael, a wicked man, but of the royal blood of David. These disturbances gave the Chaldeans the opportunity to remove from Judea even the very least of them, and to leave no one, so that there would be no seeds of rebellion. See Jer. 52, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET EX EIS RVRSVM TOLLES, ET PROJICIES EOS IN MEDIO IGNIS, ET COMBVRES EOS IGNI: ET EX EO EGREDIETVR IGNIS IN DOMVM ISRAEL) Ignis est ira divina, ut modo diximus, & multis aliis in locis apparet. Ea autem ira se exseruit in illas exi- guas Judæorum in Judæa reliquias per bellum quoddam in- ter ipsos civile, aliis Godoliæ, viri boni & Chaldæis amici, aliis Ismaelis, hominis scelerati, sed ex Regio Davidis san- guine, partes sequentibus. Qui motusChaldæis occasionem præbuere auferendi è Judæa etiam minimum quemque, nec quemquam relinquendi, ut ne ulla essent rerum no- varum semina. Vide Jer. 52, 30.

## 5:5
Verse 5.

THUS SAYS THE LORD GOD) An explanation of the preceding figure.

THIS IS JERUSALEM) These hairs signify the inhabitants of Jerusalem in particular.

I HAVE SET IT IN THE MIDST OF THE NATIONS, AND THE LANDS AROUND IT) Namely, so that the Egyptians, Syrians, Arabs, Africans, Greeks, and thus gradually others, might take from it an example of piety for themselves.

Therefore, one cannot conclude from this, as the Papist interpreters do, that Jerusalem was situated in the middle of the habitable world, but rather in a place where nations flocked from all sides, and from which place the doctrine of the Word was to shine forth to the whole world, as Theodoret holds. Deut. 4, 6. Ps. 48, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

HÆC DICIT DOMINUS DEUS) Explicatio figuræ antecedentis.

ISTA EST JERUSALEM) Isti pili Hierosolymitas præcipue significant.

IN MEDIO GENTIUM POSUI EAM, ET IN CIRCUITU EJUS TERRAS) Nempe ut exemplum in- de sibi sumerent pietatis Ægyptii, Syri, Arabes, Afri, Græci, atque ita gradatim alii.

Non ergo hinc colligere licet cum Pontificiis Interpp. Hierosolymam in medio orbis habitabilis sitam fuisse, sed illic, quo undique confluebant gentes, & ex quo loco doctrina verbi toti orbi lu- cere debebat,ut habet Theodor. Deut. 4,6. Pf. 48, 2.

## 5:6
Ver. 6.

AND SHE HATH DESPISED MY JUDGMENTS, SO THAT SHE WAS MORE WICKED THAN THE NATIONS) (משפטים here are those things which pertain to the amending of morals. But the nations, he says, are more moral than they themselves. A great and just reproach.

AND MY STATUTES MORE THAN THE LANDS, THAT ARE ROUND ABOUT HER) חקות are ritual matters. The nations keep their own rites, invented by men, better than these men keep those given by God.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET CONTEMSIT JUDICIA MEA, UT PLUS ESSET IMPIA QVAM GENTES) (משפטים sunt hic ea,quæ ad mores emendandos pertinent. Gentes autem,in- quit, ipsis sunt moratiores. Magna & justa exprobratio.

ET PRÆCEPTA MEA ULTRA QVAM TER- RE, QVÆ IN CIRCUITU EJUS SUNT) חקות sunt ritualia. Gentes ritus suos ab hominibus inventos me- lius retinent, quam isti datos divinitus.

## 5:7
Ver. 7.

AND ACCORDING TO THE JUDGMENTS OF THE NATIONS, THAT ARE ROUND ABOUT YOU, YE HAVE NOT DONE) Ye have not even fulfilled that measure of the more moral nations; from whom Pythagoras drew so many things worthy of praise, and brought them into Greece.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET JUXTA JUDICIA GENTIUM, QVÆ IN CIRCUITU VESTRO SUNT, NON ESTIS OPERA- TI) Ne illam quidem mensuram implestis gentium mora- tiorum; à quibus quam multa laudanda hausit Pythago- ras, & in Græciam attulit.

## 5:8
Ver. 8. BEHOLD I, EVEN I, AM AGAINST THEE) I come, as I have several times before.

I, EVEN I, WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS IN THE MIDST OF THEE IN THE SIGHT OF THE NATIONS) I will vindicate my laws from contempt, as great kings are wont to do. Why should I suffer it to be said: Behold those who profess that they alone worship the true God, how do they live?

Latin:

Vers. 8. ECCE EGO AD TE) Venio, ut antehac aliquoties.

IPSE EGO FACIAM IN MEDIO TUI JUDI- CIA IN OCULIS GENTIUM) Ego leges meas à con- temptu vindicabo, ut solent facere magni reges. Cur pa- tiar ut dicatur: Ecce illi, qui soli verum Deum se colere profitentur, quomodo vivunt?

## 5:9
Ver. 9.

AND I WILL DO IN THEE THAT WHICH I HAVE NOT DONE, AND WHEREUNTO I WILL NOT DO ANY MORE THE LIKE) It is just that those should be punished more severely to whom greater benefits have fallen. See Luke 12:48.

BECAUSE OF ALL THINE ABOMINATIONS) Most grave crimes, which the Prophets accuse them of everywhere.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET FACIAM IN TE, QVOD NON FECI, ET QVIBUS SIMILIA ULTRA NON FACIAM) Æquum est puniri gravius, quibus majora contigerunt beneficia. Vide Lucam 12, 48.

PROPTER OMNES ABOMINATIONES TUAS) Scelera gravissima, quæ passim accusant Prophetæ.

## 5:10
Ver. 10.

THEREFORE THE FATHERS SHALL EAT THE SONS IN THE MIDST OF THEE, AND THE SONS SHALL EAT THEIR FATHERS) In severe famine it is hardly possible that such things should not come to pass. See Deut. 28:53. Lam. 2:20, 4:10. Add 2 Kings 6:28, and Josephus, Jewish War 7:8.

AND I WILL WINNOW ALL THY REMNANTS INTO THE WIND) That is, I will scatter, as above 2. & often elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

IDEO PATRES COMEDENT FILIOS IN ME- DIO TUI, ET FILII COMEDENT PATRES SUOS) In gravi fame vix est, ut non talia eveniant. Vide Deuter. 28, 53. Thren. 2, 20. 4, 10. Adde 2. Regum. 6, 28. & Josephum Belli Judaici 7, 8.

ET VENTILABO UNIVERSAS RELIQVIAS TUAS IN VENTUM) Id est, dispergam, ut supra 2. & alibi sæpe.

## 5:11
Vers. 11. BECAUSE THOU HAST DEFILED MY HOLY THING IN ALL THINE OFFENSES, AND IN ALL THINE ABOMINATIONS) Holy thing or sanctuary is the Temple. Moreover, שקוץ & תועבה are of the same value. For by both words idols or idolatry are signified. But the Hebrews love to use tautology in exceptional matters.

I ALSO WILL DIMINISH) In the Hebrew: I will diminish. That is, I will strip away all honor from thee, as thou, as much as was in thee, didst strip it away from me.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QVOD SANCTUM MEUM VIOLASTI IN OMNIBUS OFFENSIONIBUS TUIS, ET IN CUN- CTIS ABOMINATIONIBUS TUI) Sanctum sive san- ctuarium est Templum. Idem autem valent שקוץ & תועבה. Utraque enim voce idola aut idolatolatria signifi- cantur. Sed amant Hebræi in rebus eximiis ταυτολογεῖν.

EGO QVOQVE CONFRINGAM) In Hebræo : Diminuam. Id est, honorem tibi omnem detraham, ut tu mihi, quantum in te erant, detraxisti.

## 5:12
Vers. 12.

A THIRD PART SHALL DIE BY THE PESTILENCE) An explanation of that which God had commanded to be done concerning the hairs.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

TERTIA PARS IN PESTE MORIETUR) Ex- plicatio ejus, quod de pilis fieri Deus jusserat.

## 5:13
Vers. 13.

I WILL CAUSE MY INDIGNATION TO REST UPON THEM) That is, I will satisfy it. See Is. 1, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

REQVIESCERE FACIAM INDIGNATIONEM MEAM IN EIS) Id est, satiabo. Vid. Es. 1, 24.

## 5:15
Vers. 15.

AND THOU SHALT BE A REPROACH AND A BLASPHEMY) All shall speak evil of thee.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET ERIS OPPROBRIUM ET BLASPHEMIA) Maledicent tibi omnes.

Vers. 16.

THE ARROWS OF FAMINE) Hail, rains, mice, blight, mildew, locusts.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

SAGITTAS FAMIS) Grandinem, imbres, mures, uredinem, rubiginem, locustas.

## 5:16
I WILL BREAK THE STAFF OF BREAD AMONG YOU) Above 4, 16.

CONTERAM IN VOBIS BACULUM PANIS) Supra 4, 16.

Vers. 17.

Vers. 17.

## 5:17
AND THE WORST BEASTS) As is accustomed to happen in devastated places. Deut. 26, 22.

EVEN TO DESTRUCTION) In the Hebrew: That they may make you childless.

BLOOD) Slaughter by the enemy.

THEY SHALL PASS THROUGH YOU) They shall invade you.

AND I WILL BRING A SWORD UPON YOU) Civil wars.

CHAP. VI.

Latin:

ET BESTIAS PESSIMAS) Ut soler fieri in locis vastatis. Deut. 26, 22.

USQVE AD INTERNECIONEM) In Hebræo: Vt te orbam faciant.

SANGUIS) Cædes ab hoste.

TRANSIBUNT PER TE) Invadent te.

CAP. VI.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

Because of manifold idolatry, the cities of the Israelites and the high places are to be destroyed: and those who have escaped the plague, the sword, and the famine are to be scattered among the nations, where, pressed by evils, they shall turn to the Lord. Therefore, the Prophet is commanded to cry out and marvel at the destruction and desolation because of the abominations of Israel by the striking of the hand and the stamping of the foot.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Ob multiplicem Idololatriam urbes Israëlita- rum & excelsa dissipanda: & qui pestem, gladium, & famem evaserint, dispergendi inter gentes, ubi malis pressi convertentur ad Dominum. Ideo percussione manus & allisione pedis ad abominationes Israel ex- clamare & mirari interitum, ac desolatio- nem jubetur Propheta.

## 6:2
Ver. 2.

SET THY FACE TOWARD THE MOUNTAINS OF ISRAEL) Turn your face toward that part where Judea is situated: in which there are very many mountains. Exod. 11, 17. Deut. 11, 11.

But especially where the mountains have been contaminated by idolatry, Is. 57, 3. Jer. 3, 6. c. 9, 10. Hos. 4, 13.

Ver. same.

AND PROPHESY UNTO THEM) Address them: a prosopopoeia not unlike that one: You white mounds and groves.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

PONE FACIEM TVAM AD MONTES ISRAEL) Faciem verte in eam partem, ubi sita est Judæa: in qua sunt montes plurimi. Exod. 11, 17. Deut. 11, 11.

Sed imprimis, qua montes idololatria contami- nati sunt, Es. 57. 3. Jer. 3, 6. c. 9, 10. Hos. 4, 13.

Vers. eod.

ET PROPHETABIS AD EOS) Alloquere eos: προσωποποιΐα non dissimilis illi: Vos albani tumuli atq; luci.

## 6:3
Ver. 3.

TO THE ROCKS AND TO THE VALLEYS) In Hebrew: to the brooks and to the valleys. Among the idolaters, even springs are among the divinities.

Pintus understands the primates of the Jews by rocks and hills: but he is misled by the Vulgate version.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

RUPIBUS ET VALLIBUS) In Hebræo: rivis & vallibus. Idololatris inter numina etiam fontes.

Pintus per rupes & colles primates Judæorum in- telligit: sed seductus est à Vulg. versione.

## 6:4
Ver. 4.

I WILL CAST DOWN YOUR SLAIN BEFORE YOUR IDOLS) The Chaldean will do this, which Pyrrhus does in Virgil: Who slaughters the son before the father's face, the father at the altars.

Regarding the word חמנים, the interpreters dispute much, but it is better to understand it as images in general, as in Leviticus 26:30, Isaiah 17:8, chapter 27:9, etc. Some, with Munster, understand it as the sun. Compare Jeremiah 44:17.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

DEJICIAM INTERFECTOS VESTROS ANTE IDOLA VESTRA) Hoc faciet Chaldæus, quod apud Virgilium Pyrrhus: Natum ante ora patris, patrem qui obtruncat ad aras.

De voce חמנים multum disputant Interpp. sed præstat simulachra in genere intelligere, ut Levit. 26, 30. Es. 17, 8. c. 27, 9. &c. Nonnulli solem intelli- gunt cum Munsterio. Conf. Jer. 44, 17.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

AND THE SLAIN SHALL FALL IN THE MIDST OF YOU) An enallage of number. Therefore, both the Chaldean and the Greeks have placed the plural here.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET CADET INTERFECTUS IN MEDIO VE- STRI) Enallage numeri. Ideo pluralem hic posuere tum Chaldæus, tum Græci.

## 6:8
Verse 8.

AND I WILL LEAVE AMONG YOU THOSE WHO HAVE ESCAPED THE SWORD AMONG THE NATIONS, WHEN I HAVE SCATTERED THEM IN THE LANDS) I will cause some to survive by escaping the sword of the nations, whom I will scatter into various lands.
