Vers. 8.

ET RELINQVAM IN VOBIS EOS, QVI FV- GERINT GLADIVM IN GENTIBUS, CVM DIS- PERSERO EOS IN TERRIS) Faciam, ut quidam super- sint evadendo gladium gentium, quos in varias terras disper- gam.

## 6:9
Verse 9. AND YOUR LIBERATED ONES SHALL REMEMBER ME AMONG THE NATIONS) Those who have escaped the sword.

BECAUSE I HAVE BROKEN THEIR WHORING HEART) That I have been broken (that is, affected with grief) by their harlot-like heart. But the LXX did not read נשברתי, but נשבעתי, ὀμώμοκα. The Chaldean, however, takes the Niphal for the Pehal: I will break their foolish heart.

THEIR EYES WHORING AFTER THEIR IDOLS) For they are captured by the appearance and worship of idols, like Helen of Paris,

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET RECORDABVNTVR MEI LIBERATI VESTRI IN GENTIBVS) Illi, qui gladium evaserint.

QVIA CONTRIVI COR EORVM FORNICANS) Me fractum fuisse (id est, dolore affectum) corde eorum me- retricio. At LXX. non נשברתי legerunt, sed נשבעתי ὀμώμοκα. Chaldæus autem Niphal sumit pro Pehal: con- fringam cor eorum insipiens.

OCVLOS EORVM FORNICANTES POST IDOLA SVA) Capiuntur enim specie & cultu idolorum, ut Paridis Helena,

## 6:10
Verse 10.

AND THEY SHALL KNOW THAT I THE LORD HAVE NOT SPOKEN IN VAIN) That is, not without grave cause have I decreed to inflict these evils upon them.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET SCIENT, QVIA EGO DOMINVS NON FRVSTRA LOCVTVS SVM) Id est, non sine gravi cau- sa decrevi hæc mala ipsis inferre.

## 6:11
Verse 11.

SMITE YOUR HAND AND STAMP YOUR FOOT) That is, extend your hand toward Judea, as if about to strike, and shake off the dust of the earth with your foot, so that you may figure that which I am about to do. The things which follow immediately in verse 14 demand this sense.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

PERCVTE MANVM TVAM ET ALLIDE PE- DEM TVVM) Id est, manum tuam extende versus Ju- dæam, tanquam percussurus, & terræ pulverem pede discu- te, ut figures id quod ego facturus sum. Hunc sensum exi- gunt, quæ mox sequentur v. 14.

## 6:12
Verse 12.

HE WHO IS FAR) Namely from the enemy, as the following indicates.

AND HE WHO SHALL BE LEFT, AND BESIEGED) Better: He who shall be left, and preserved. For נצר among other things means to preserve. He who shall be left from the plague, and preserved from the sword, shall perish by famine.

I WILL COMPLETE MY INDIGNATION UPON THEM) As above, verse 13.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QVI LONGE EST) Nempe ab hoste, ut sequen- tia indicant.

ET QVI RELICTVS FVERIT, ET OBSES- SVS) Melius: Qui relictus fuerit, & servatus. Nam נצר in- ter alia est servare. Qui relictus fuerit à peste, & servatus à gladio, fame inter ibit.

COMPLEBO INDIGNATIONEM MEAM IN EIS) Ut supra 5. v. 13.

## 6:14
Verse 14.

AND I WILL MAKE THE LAND DESOLATE AND DESTITUTE FROM THE DESERT TO DEBLATHA) Jerome suspects that a ד crept in for a ר, and that it was formerly written רבאתה, so that it is the same Reblatha, of which Jeremiah 39 makes mention. But the Chaldean and the Greeks favor the received reading; it seems to me that certain interpreters translate it best: I will make the land (Judea) more desolate and more wasted than Deblatha, which is the Moabitic desert, of which mention is made in Num. 33, 47; Jerem. 48, 22. It is a part of that horrible desert, of which Moses makes mention in Deut. 8, 15.

Rightly does Grotius vindicate the Hebrew text (which Papists here, especially Pradus, Estius, Cornelius, and others, call into question), whose authority and integrity, if he had always left it inviolate, would have allowed us to dispense with corrective work in many places.

Verse of the same.

AND THEY SHALL KNOW, THAT I AM THE LORD) So that they may know that I am constant in fulfilling my words.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET FACIAM TERRAM DESOLATAM ET DESTITVTAM A DESERTO DEBLATHA) Hiero- nymus suspicatur irrepsisse ד pro ר, & scriptum olim fuisse רבאתה, ut sit eadem Reblatha, cujus meminit Jeremias 39. At receptæ lectioni favent Chaldæus & Græci, viden- tur mihi optime quidam interpretes vertere: Faciam terram (Judæam) desolatiorem & vastiorem Deblatha, quod est desertum Moabiticum, cujus mentio Num. 33, 47. Jerem. 48, 22. Est pars deserti illius horribilis, cujus meminit Moses Deut. 8, 15.

Merito vindicat Ebræum textum. (quem hic solicitant imprimis Papistæ Pradus, Estius, Corne- lius, alii) Grotius, cujus autoritatem & integrita- tem si intemeratam semper reliquisset, in multis opera castigatoria supersedere nobis licuisset.

Vers. eod.

ET SCIENT, QVIA EGO DOMINVS) Ut no- rint me esse constantem in dictis meis præstandis.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII.

The extreme and inevitable devastation of the whole land of Judah is denounced as being imminently near because of their crimes: which is confirmed by chains.

Latin:

CAPUT VII.

Denunciatur totius terræ Judæ extrema & in- evitabilis vastatio proxime imminens pro- pter scelera ipsorum: quæ catenis confir- matur.

## 7:2
Verse 2.

THE END IS COME) That is, the supreme vengeance, as the Chaldean here. UPON THE FOUR CORNERS OF THE LAND,) That is, upon all Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

FINIS VENIT) Id est, suprema ultio, ut hic Chaldæus. SUPER QVATVOR PLAGAS TERRÆ,) Id est, super totam Judæam.

## 7:3
Ver. 3.

I WILL JUDGE THEE ACCORDING TO THY WAYS) That is, I will punish according to merits. I WILL LAY UPON THEE ALL THINE ABOMINATIONS) I will cause them to fall back upon thy head.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

JVDICABO TE JVXTA VIAS TVAS) Id est, puniam pro meritis. PONAM CONTRA TE OMNES ABOMINA- TIONES TVAS) Faciam, ut in caput tuum recidant.

## 7:4
Ver. 4.

THINE ABOMINATIONS SHALL BE IN THE MIDST OF THEE) The punishment of sins shall be with thee everywhere. Thus the Chaldean rightly here.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ABOMINATIONES TVÆ IN MEDIO TUI ERUNT) Pœna peccatorum ubique tibi aderit. Ita hic Chaldæus recte.

## 7:6
Ver. 6.

IT IS WAKED AGAINST THEE) Vengeance has rushed upon thee wide awake.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

EVIGILAVIT ADVERSVM TE) Pervigil irruit in te ultio.

## 7:7
Ver. 7.

THE MORNING IS COME UPON THEE) That morning has come upon thee. That is, Judgment: for in the morning judgments were exercised. Moreover, צפירת for morning is a Chaldean word. The LXX, who call it πλοκὴν, looked to the Arabic language. For ضمار is πλοκή. THE DAY OF SLAUGHTER, AND NOT OF THE JOYFUL SHOUTING OF THE MOUNTAINS) In the Hebrew: The day of tumult, and not of the song of the gatherers on the mountains. See Isaiah 16, 9. and 10. where the word is the same.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

VENIT CONTRITIO SVPER TE) Venit mand illud in te. Id est, Judicium: nam mane judicia exerceban- tur. Est autem צפירת pro mane vox Chaldaica. LXX. qui πλοκὴν vocant, Arabicam linguam respexere. Nam ضمار est πλοκή. DIES OCCISIONIS, ET NON GLORIÆ MONTIUM) In Hebræo: Dies tumultus, & non carminis venitorum in montibus. Vide Esaiam 16, 9. & 10. ubi vox eadem.

## 7:10
Ver. 10.

THE MORNING IS GONE FORTH) That morning has appeared. As above. THE ROD HATH BLOSSOMED) That is, the tribe of Judah, for מטה signifies both a rod and a tribe. It hath blossomed, it was in prosperous circumstances. Others render: your evil is in the flower: so that the rod is taken for an instrument of punishment, Is. 9, 4.

Ver. the same.

PRIDE HAS BUDDED) It has brought forth pride: that fruit has followed the flowers. INIQUITY HAS RISEN INTO A ROD OF WICKEDNESS) Violence (that is, the violent Chaldean) has readied itself against that impious rod, that is, he is present, who may cut it out by the roots.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

EGRESSA EST CONTRITIO) Mane illud ap- paruit. Ut supra. FLORVIT VIRGA) Id est, tribus Judæ, nam מטה & virgam & tribum significat. Floruit, fuit in rebus pro- speris. Alii reddunt: malum vestrum in flore est: ut virga sumatur pro instrumento supplicii, Es. 9, 4.

Vers. eod.

GERMINAVIT SVPERBIA) Protulit superbiam: Is fructus flores secutus est. INIQVITAS SVRREXIT IN VIRGA IMPIETA- TIS) Violentia (id est, Chaldæus violentus) se expedivit adversus virgam istam impiam, Id est, adest, qui eam exscin- dat radicitus.

## 7:11
Vers. 11.

NOT FROM THEM) Supply, anyone will be immune from evil. NOT FROM THE PEOPLE) Nor from the common folk. NOR FROM THE SOUND OF THEM) Nor from their clamors. That is, the leaders. The word is frequent among the Chaldeans. AND THERE SHALL BE NO REST IN THEM) In the Hebrew: There shall be no mourning for them. It will be empty for no one to mourn the dead. Jer. 16, 4. 5. 6. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

NON EX EIS) Supple, quisquam immunis à ma- lo erit. NON EX POPULO) Neque ex plebe. NEQVE EX SONITV EORVM) Neque ex stre- pitibus eorum. Id est, primoribus. Verbum est frequens Chaldæis. ET NON ERIT REQVIES IN EIS) In Hebræo: Non erit de illis luctus. Nemini vacabit lugere mortuos. Jer. 16, 4. 5. 6. 7.

## 7:12
Vers. 12.

HE WHO BUYS, LET HIM NOT REJOICE, AND HE WHO SELLS, LET HIM NOT MOURN) Let him not grieve. Those who have bought something well are accustomed to rejoice, and those who are forced to sell their own are accustomed to grieve. Now the lot of both will be equal. Both the buyer and the seller will be disturbed from their fatherland, and will be carried away captive.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QVI EMIT, NE LÆTETUR, ET QVI VEN- DIT, NON LVGEAT) Ne doleat. Solent gaudere, qui bene rem emerunt, & dolere, qui vendere sua coguntur. Nunc par utriusque erit sors. Uterque & emtor, & venditor turbabitur è pa- tria sua, & captivus auferetur.

## 7:13
Vers. 13.

FOR HE WHO SELLS SHALL NOT RETURN TO THAT WHICH HE SOLD, AND YET IN THE LIVING IS THEIR LIFE) The sense is: He who has sold a thing, even if he lives (namely, up until the Jubilee), he shall not, however, recover the thing sold: because both he and his estates will be in the power of others. FOR THE VISION) The prophecy. TO ALL THE MULTITUDE) Concerning all this people.

Verse of the same.

IT SHALL NOT RETURN) It shall not be void. Thus Isa. 55, 11. AND THE MAN IN THE INIQUITY OF HIS LIFE SHALL NOT BE STRENGTHENED) Lest anyone think that by acting wickedly he will be safe. The LXX read עון, not עון: which was also noted by Jerome. Jerome did not note a diversity of codices, but a παρόραμα (oversight) of the LXX Elders. The ambiguity, he says, of the Hebrew letters ו and י, which are distinguished only by size, caused some to interpret it as iniquity, others as eyes. Because, namely, these wrongly thought it was a Jod, when a ו is held in the text.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

QVIA QVI VENDIT AD ID QVOD VEN- DIDIT, NON REVERTETVR, ET ADHVC IN VI- VENTIBVS VITA EORVM) Sensus est: Qui rem ven- didit, etiamsi vivat (nempe ad Jubilæum usque) non tamen repetet rem venditam: quia in potestate erit aliorum, & ipse & prædia. VISIO ENIM) Prophetia. AD OMNEM MVLTITVDINEM) De omni hoc populo.

Vers. eod.

NON REVERTETVR) Non erit irrita. Sic Ef. 55, 11. ET VIR IN INIQVITATE VITÆ SVÆ NON CONFORTABITVR) Ne quis se male agendo putet tu- tum fore. LXX. legerunt עון, non עון: quod & Hierony- mo notatum. Non diversitatem Codicum notavit Hierony- mus, sed παρόραμα LXX. Senum. Ambiguitas, in- quit, Hebraicarum literarum ו & י, quæ tantum magnitudine discernuntur, fecit alios iniquitatem, alios oculos interpretari. Quia scilicet hi male Jod esse putarunt, cum ו habeatur in textu.

## 7:14
Verse 14.

BLOW THE TRUMPET, LET ALL BE PREPARED) Attempt whatever you will. AND THERE IS NONE THAT GOETH TO BATTLE) Yet there will be no one who dares to fight. See below 17.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

CANITE TVBA, PRÆPARENTVR OMNES) Quidvis molimini. ET NON EST, QVI VADAT IN PRÆLIVM) Attamen nemo erit, qui pugnare audeat. Vide infra 17.

## 7:16
Verse 16.

AND THEY THAT SHALL FLEE OF THEM SHALL BE SAVED, AND THEY SHALL BE IN THE MOUNTAINS LIKE DOVES OF THE VALLEYS) But those of them who escape safe (from those evils already mentioned), they shall be in the mountains, like doves in the valleys. That is, they shall tremble. ALL TREMBLING EVERY ONE IN HIS INIQUITY) In the Hebrew: Moaning every one because of his punishment. To moan is properly said of doves or turtledoves.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET SALVABVNTVR, QVI FVGERINT EX IIS, ET ERVNT IN MONTIBVS QVASI COLVM- BÆ CONVALLIVM) At qui eorum sospites (ab illis malis jam dictis) evadent, illi erunt in montibus, sicut columbæ in vallibus. Id est, trepidabunt. OMNES TREPIDI VNVSQVISQVE IN IN- IQVITATE SVA) In Hebræo: Gementes quisque ob pœnam suam. Gemere proprie de columbis aut turturibus dicitur.

## 7:17
Verse 17.

ALL HANDS SHALL BE DISSOLVED) Strength shall fail. AND ALL KNEES SHALL FLOW WITH WATERS) They shall flow with urine from fear. LXX: all thighs shall be defiled with moisture. Jerome in his commentary: Knees shall flow with urine.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

OMNES MANVS DISSOLVENTVR) Vires de- ficient. ET OMNIA GENVA FLUENT AQVIS) Perfluent lotio præ metu. LXX. πάντες μηροὶ μολυνθήσονται ὑγρασίᾳ. Hieronym. in commentario: Vrina perfluent genua.

## 7:18
Verse 18.

THEY SHALL GIRD THEMSELVES WITH SACKCLOTH) As in the deepest grief. AND FEAR SHALL COVER THEM) Horror shall seize them on every side. AND ON ALL THEIR HEADS SHALL BE BALDNESS) Isa. 3, 17. Jer. 48, 37. Mic. 1, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

ACCINGENT SE CILICIIS) Ut in summo mœrore. ET OPERIET EOS FORMIDO) Horror eos un- dique invadet. ET IN VNIVERSIS CAPITIBVS EORVM CALVITIVM) Ef. 3, 17. Jerem. 48, 37. Mich. 1, 16.

## 7:19
Verse 19. THEIR SILVER SHALL BE CAST FORTH) By themselves, because they will see that they cannot keep it for themselves. And so they will do this, so that it does not reach the enemy, if only that can be done. AND THEIR GOLD SHALL BE FOR A DUNGHILL) It shall be buried somewhere. In the Hebrew: It shall be despised as an unclean thing: Greeks: it shall be held in contempt. Nor does the Chaldean say otherwise. THEIR SILVER AND THEIR GOLD SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO DELIVER THEM IN THE DAY OF THE WRATH OF THE LORD) For they shall not be theirs, but in the power of the victor. THEY SHALL NOT SATISFY THEIR SOUL) That is, themselves, by a Hebrew idiom. AND THEIR BELLIES SHALL NOT BE FILLED) They shall be fed meagerly, as servants are accustomed to be. BECAUSE THE STUMBLING BLOCK OF THEIR INIQUITY HAS BEEN MADE) The sense is: Therefore gold and silver will not profit them, because they used it for idolatry. The following verses show this: and Jerome rightly saw this in his Commentaries.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ARGENTVM EORVM FORAS PROJI- CIETVR) Ab ipsis, quia videbunt se id sibi servare non posse. Itaque id agent, ne ad hostes perveniat, si modo id fieri possit. ET AVRVM EORVM IN STERQVILINIVM ERIT) Defodietur alicubi. In Hebræo: Spernetur ut res immunda: Græci: ὑπεροφθήσεται. Nec aliter Chaldæus. ARGENTVM EORVM ET AVRVM EORVM NON VALEBIT LIBERARE EOS IN DIE FURO- RIS DOMINI) Neque enim erunt ipsorum, sed in victoris potestate. ANIMAM EORVM NON SATVRABVNT) Id est, semetipsos, locutione Hebræa. ET VENTRES EORVM NON IMPLEBVN- TVR) Tenuiter pascentur, ut servi solent. QVIA SCANDALVM INIQVITATIS EORVM FACTVM EST) Sensus est: Ideo aurum & argentum ipsis non proderit, quia eo usi sunt ad idololatriam. Osten- dunt hoc sequentia: & recte id vidit in Commentariis Hie- ronymus.

## 7:20
Verse 20.

AND THEY SET THE ORNAMENT OF THEIR JEWELS IN PRIDE, AND THEY MADE THE IMAGES OF THEIR ABOMINATIONS, AND OF THEIR IDOLS OUT OF IT) That which had been given to them for becoming ornament and splendor: (for here the verb is used impersonally for the passive) out of that they made their abominable and filthy images. Out of that gold and silver by which they could be beautiful among their neighbors. FOR THIS CAUSE I HAVE GIVEN IT UNTO THEM FOR UNCLEANNESS) Therefore I caused them to cast these things away. Here is the same noun as above 19, נדה, which this interpreter had there translated as dunghill.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ET ORNAMENTVM MONILIVM SVORVM IN SVPERBIAM POSVERVNT, ET IMAGINES ABOMINATIONVM SVARVM, ET SIMVLACHRO- RVm FECERVNT EX EO) Quod in decorum ornatum, & splendorem datum erat ipsis: (est enim hic verbum imper- sonaliter positum pro passivo) de eo imagines suas abominabi- les ac spurcas fecere. De isto auro & argento quo speciosi esse poterant apud vicinos. PROPTER HOC DEDI EIS ILLVD IN IM- MVNDITIEM) Propterea feci, ut ipsi hæc abjicerent. Est hic nomen idem, quod supra 19, נדה, quod ibi sterqui- linium verterat hic interpres.

## 7:21
Vers. 21.

AND THEY SHALL POLLUTE IT) They shall turn it to vile uses. You receive the burden of the belly in gold, wretch, and you are not ashamed. Clement of Alexandria in book 2 of the Paedagogus, chapter 3, says that women were accustomed to make χρυσᾶ, the vessels for excrement. But we are taught that the common vessels of women were silver from Ulpian, Law Quintus, Mucius, Book 2, and from Martial.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ET CONTAMINABVNT ILLVD) Ad viles usus vertent. Ventris onus misero, nec te pudet, excipis auro. Clemens Alexandrinus libro 2. Pædagogi cap. 3. mulieres ait solitas χρυσᾶ ποιεῖν, τῶν ἐκκρίσεως τὰ ἐνδοχεῖα. Mulie- rum autem vulgo scaphia fuisse argentea docemur ex Ul- piano L. Quintus. Mucius Libro 2. & ex Martiali.

## 7:22
Vers. 22.

AND THEY SHALL VIOLATE MY SECRET) The Chaldeans, that is. He calls the inner sanctuary of the Temple a secret: which the LXX call τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν, because God there displayed the signs of His majesty.

AND THE ROBBERS SHALL ENTER INTO IT) Robbers, he says, shall come into that inner chamber, into which it is a sin for the Israelites, for the Levites, for the Priests, except for the high priest, to enter.

AND THEY SHALL POLLUTE IT) They shall value it no more than a profane place. When places are captured by enemies, all things cease to be sacred, says Pomponius in Law Cum loca, Digest on Religious Matters. Cicero, Fourth Verrine: The victory had made the sacred things of Syracuse profane.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET VIOLARVNT ARCANVM MEVM) Chal- dæi scilicet. Arcanum vocat adytum Templi: quod LXX. vocant τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν, quia Deus ibi signa exhibebat suæ majestatis.

ET INTROIBVNT ILLVD EMISSARII) Latrones, inquit, venient in illud penetrale, quo Israëlitæ, quo Levitæ, quo Sacerdoti, extra summum, nefas est intrare.

ET CONTAMINABVNT ILLVD) Non pluris facient, quam locum profanum. Cum loca capta sunt ab hostibus, omnia desinunt sacra esse ait Pomponius in L. Cum loca. D. de Religiosis. Cicero Verrina quarta: Sacra Syracusarum victoria profana fecerat.

## 7:23
Vers. 23.

MAKE A CHAIN) That is, a chain: for that is what רתק is to the Hebrews and Chaldeans. By this sign he shows that captivity is coming.

Jerome's interpretation concerning a rhetorical conclusion is not appropriate: even though the Papists follow it.

FOR THE LAND IS FULL OF THE JUDGMENT OF BLOOD) That is, it is held by crimes which the law requires to be paid for with death.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

FAC CONCLVSIONEM) Id est, catenam: id enim est רתק Hebræis & Chaldæis. Hoc signo ostendit futuram captivitatem.

Non convenit Hieronymi interpretatio de conclusione Rhetorica: etsi eam Papistæ sequantur.

QVONIAM TERRA PLENA EST JVDICIO SANGVINIS) Id est, tenetur criminum, quæ lex morte vult lui.

## 7:24
Verse 24.

AND I WILL MAKE THE PRIDE OF THE MIGHTY TO CEASE) That is, to stop, as it is in the Hebrew and Chaldean.

Verse of the same.

AND THEY SHALL POSSESS THEIR SANCTUARIES) The Hebrew text, the Chaldean, and the Greek: And their sanctuaries shall be profaned. The three parts of the temple: God says 'theirs': because the Temple, having been polluted by them, He no longer held as His own.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET QVIESCERE FACIAM SVPERBIAM POTENTIVM) Id est, cessare, ut est in Hebræo & Chaldæo.

Vers. eod.

ET POSSIDEBVNT SANCTVARIA EORVM) Hebræus textus, Chaldæus, & Græcus: Et profanabuntur sanctuaria ipsorum. Tres partes templi: ipsorum dicit Deus: quia Templum ab ipsis pollutum pro suo amplius non habebat.

## 7:25
Verse 25. DISTRESS COMING UPON) קפדה, for which the LXX read כפרה.

THEY SHALL SEEK PEACE) They shall seek safety.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ANGUSTIA SVPERVENIENTE) קפדה, pro quo LXX. legerunt כפרה.

REQVIRENT PACEM) Quærent salutem.

## 7:26
Verse 26. RUMOR UPON RUMOR) Bad news one after another. Thus ἀκοὴ is taken in Matthew 24:6 and elsewhere.

AND THEY SHALL SEEK A VISION FROM THE PROPHET) They will desire to hear some consolation from the Prophet. See Jeremiah chapters 37 and 38.

AND THE LAW SHALL PERISH FROM THE PRIEST) The priests in such great distress will not be able to fulfill the solemnities of the law: cattle, fine flour, wine, and incense will be lacking.

AND COUNSEL FROM THE ELDERS) Not even the wisest will be able to suggest anything that is to the purpose.

Latin:

Vers. 26. AVDITVS SVPER AVDITVM) Mali nuntii alii super alios. Sic ἀκοὴ sumitur Matth. 24, 6. & alibi.

ET QVÆRENT VISIONEM DE PROPHETA) Optabunt aliquam consolationem audire à Propheta. Vide Jerem. 37. 38. capp.

ET LEX PERIBIT A SACERDOTE) Sacerdotes in tantis angustiis solennia legis implere non poterunt: deerunt pecudes, simila, vinum, suffitus.

ET CONSILIVM A SENIORIBVS) Ne sapientissimi quidem quicquam, quod è re sit, suadere poterunt.

## 7:27
Verse 27. THE KING SHALL MOURN) He will be in the greatest anxiety. See the places of Jeremiah already mentioned.

AND THE PRINCE SHALL BE CLOTHED WITH SORROW) Stupor shall surround the prince. The same as what preceded, in other words.

AND THE HANDS OF THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND SHALL BE TROUBLED) The same sense as above 17.

ACCORDING TO THEIR WAY I WILL DO UNTO THEM) They themselves profaned the Temple: I will cause it to be profaned by the Chaldeans.

ACCORDING TO THEIR JUDGMENTS I WILL JUDGE THEM) They oppressed the poor, they did not give liberty to their fellow countrymen: I will cause that they themselves also be oppressed, and lose their liberty.

AND THEY SHALL KNOW, THAT I AM THE LORD) As above 6, 14.

THE SECOND APPEARANCE OF THE LORD.

Latin:

Vers. 27. REX LVGEBIT) Erit in summa anxietate. Vide dicta jam Jeremiæ loca.

ET PRINCEPS INDVETVR MOERORE) Stupor principem circumdabit. Idem quod præcessit verbis aliis.

ET MANVS POPVLI TERRÆ CONTVRBA- BVNTVR) Sensus idem, qui supra 17.

SECVNDVM VIAM EORVM FACIAM EIS) Profanarunt ipsi Templum: ego faciam, ut profanetur à Chaldæis.

SECVNDVM JVDICIA EORVM JVDICABO EOS) Oppresserunt pauperes, libertatem non dederunt popularibus: faciam ut & ipsi opprimantur, & libertatem amittant.

ET SCIENT, QVIA EGO DOMINVS) Ut supra 6, 14.

SECVNDA DOMINI APPARITIO.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

Ezekiel, after having seen the likeness of God, being caught up by the Spirit into Jerusalem, sees the worst idolatries of the Jews under various figures. 1. In the outer vestibule of the idol, 2. in the vestibule of the Levites, of great abominations, 3. in the vestibule of the Priests, of women weeping for Tammuz, 4. in the inner court of the house of the Lord, of 25. men worshipping the sun, whence the Lord threatens that He will not spare them, nor hear their prayers.

Ver. 1.

AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE SIXTH YEAR) Namely from the deportation of Jeconiah, as above 1, 2. After the completion of the lying down of 390 and 40 days.

I WAS SITTING IN MY HOUSE) By the Chebar.

AND THE ELDERS OF JUDAH WERE SITTING BEFORE ME) Their leaders, who had been deported with Jeconiah.

AND THE HAND OF THE LORD GOD FELL THERE UPON ME) As above 1, 3.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Ezechiel post visam Dei similitudinem Spiritu raptus in Jerusalem videt pessimas Judæorum idololatrias sub variis figuris. 1. In exteriori vestibulo idoli, 2. in vestibulo Levitarum, magnarum abominationum, 3. in vestibulo Sacerdotum, mulierum Thamus plangentium, 4. in atrio domus Domini interiori, 25. virorum solem adorantium, unde minatur Dominus, se eis non parciturum, nec orationes exauditurum.

Vers. 1.

ET FACTVM EST IN ANNO SEXTO) Nempe à deportato Jechonia, ut supra 1, 2. Post impletam cubationem 390. & 40. dierum.

EGO SEDEBAM IN DOMO MEA) Apud Chaboram.

ET SENES JVDÆ SEDEBANT CORAM ME) Primores eorum, qui cum Jechonia fuerant deportati.

ET CECIDIT IBI SVPER ME MANVS DOMINI DEI) Ut supra 1, 3.

## 8:2
Ver. 2.

AND BEHOLD A LIKENESS AS THE APPEARANCE OF FIRE: FROM THE APPEARANCE OF HIS LOINS, AND AS IT WERE DOWNWARD FIRE: AND FROM HIS LOINS, AND UPWARD, AS THE APPEARANCE OF BRIGHTNESS AS THE VISION OF AMBER) The same ὀπτασία which is above 1, 27, signifying God's judgments which would refine the Jewish people through very harsh things, yet with certain remnants saved.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET ECCE SIMILITUDO QUASI ASPECTUS IGNIS: AB ASPECTU LVMBORVM EJVS, ET QUASI DEORSUM IGNIS: ET A LVMBIS EJVS, ET SVRSVM, QUASI ASPECTUS SPLENDORIS VT VISIO ELECTRI) Eadem ὀπτασία quæ supra 1, 27. si- gnificans Dei judicia per res durissimas excoctura populum Judæum, salvis tamen reliquiis quibusdam.

## 8:3
Ver. 3.

AND THE LIKENESS OF A HAND WAS SENT FORTH AND TOOK ME BY A LOCK OF MY HEAD, AND THE SPIRIT LIFTED ME UP BETWEEN THE HEAVEN AND THE EARTH) The elders saw the figure of that hand, and the Prophet suspended by its power. But the vision which follows the Prophet saw alone, clearly as if he were present in the Temple. The cause of the vision, that the most just causes of those judgments, of which we have spoken, might be revealed to him.

AND BROUGHT ME INTO JERUSALEM IN THE VISION OF GOD) Not translated in body, but in such a way that he might behold all the things of the Temple with his own eyes as if present.

BY THE INNER DOOR, WHICH LOOKED TOWARD THE NORTH) Where one entered into the great open court, which was the people's, in which the altar was placed in the times of Ahaz: similar to the Damascene one 2 Kings 16, 11.

WHERE WAS THE SET IDOL) Of Baal, namely one of those which Manasseh had made 2 Kings 21, 7. 2 Chron. 33, 3. Josiah had destroyed 2 Chron. 34, 4. The following kings had replaced it. See 2 Kings 23, 37. 2 Chron. 36, 12.

OF JEALOUSY TO PROVOKE EMULATION) That is, by which God was provoked as a husband to whom an adulterer is brought before his eyes.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET EMISSA SIMILITUDO MANUS APPRE- HENDIT ME IN CINCINNO CAPITIS MEI, ET E- LEVAVIT ME SPIRITUS INTER COELVM ET TERRAM) Manus istius figuram, & Prophetam ejus vi suspensum, videre illi seniores. Visum autem quod sequi- tur vidit Propheta solus, plane quasi præsens esset in Tem- plo. Causa visi, ut judiciorum eorum, de quibus dixi- mus, causæ justissimæ ipsi patesierent.

ET ADDVXIT ME IN JERVSALEM IN VISI- ONE DEI) Non corpore translatum, sed ita ut oculis suis cunctas res Templi velut præsens aspiceret.

JVXTA OSTIVM INTERIVS, QVOD RESPI- CIEBAT AD AQVILONEM) Ubi intrabatur ad subdia- le maximum, quod erat populi, in quo altare positum erat Achazi temporibus: simile Damasceno 2. Reg. 16, 11.

VBI ERAT STATVTVM IDOLVM) Baalis, nem- pe unum ex iis, quæ fecerat Manasses 2. Reg. 21, 7. 2. Par. 33, 3. destruxerat Josias 2. Par. 34, 4. reposuerant reges sequentes. Vide 2. Reg. 23, 37. 2. Par. 36, 12.

ZELI AD PROVOCANDAM ÆMVLATIO- NEM) Id est, quo Deus provocabatur tanquam maritus cui ob oculos adulter adducitur.

## 8:4
Ver. 4.

AND BEHOLD THE GLORY OF GOD WAS THERE, ACCORDING TO THE VISION WHICH I HAD SEEN IN THE PLAIN) See above 3, 22. And understand both the vehicle and the throne: the vehicle to signify the deportation; the throne to figure all the judgments of God.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET ECCE IBI GLORIA DEI, SECUNDVM VISIONEM QVAM VIDERAM IN CAMPO) Vide supra 3, 22. Et vehiculum & thronum intellige: vehicu- lum ad significandam deportationem; thronum ad omnia judicia Dei figuranda.

## 8:5
Ver. 5.

THE IDOL OF JEALOUSY) That of which he had begun to speak.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

IDOLUM ZELI) Illud de quo dicere cœperat.

## 8:6
Verse 6.

DO YOU THINK YOU SEE?) In Hebrew: You do not see.

THAT I MAY GO FAR FROM MY SANCTUARY) That I may abandon the care of this Temple.

AND YET TURNED) Into other parts of the Temple.

YOU WILL SEE GREATER ABOMINATIONS) It could have sufficed what you saw, but you will see graver things.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PUTASNE VIDES TU) In Hebræo: Non vides tu.

VT PROCUL RECEDAM A SANCTUARIO MEO) Ut deseram hujus Templi curam.

ET ADHVC CONVERSVS) In partes Templi alias.

VIDEBIS ABOMINATIONES MAJORES) Suffi- cere poterat quod vidisti, sed videbis graviora.

## 8:7
Verse 7.

HE BROUGHT ME TO THE DOOR OF THE COURT) Namely, the Levitical one, to which at that time even those who were not Levites were admitted against the law.

AND BEHOLD ONE HOLE IN THE WALL) A certain small window, through which I might see what was being done inside the cells of the Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

INTRODUXIT ME AD OSTIUM ATRII) Nem- pe Levitici, quo passim tunc & ii qui Levitæ non erant ad- missi contra legem.

ET ECCE FORAMEN VNVM IN PARIETE) Fenestella quædam, per quam videre possem quæ intra cellas Levitarum peragebantur.

## 8:8
Verse 8.

AND HE SAID TO ME: SON OF MAN, DIG THE WALL) For God had said to me, son of man, dig through the wall. He gives the reason whence that small window was made.

AND WHEN I HAD DUG THE WALL) Namely in the vision, but clearly as if the thing were truly being done.

ONE DOOR APPEARED) That small window had existed. For every opening is called פתח by the Hebrews: and therefore the Greeks sometimes translate it ἄνοιγμα.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET DIXIT AD ME: FILI HOMINIS, FODE PARIETEM) Nam dixerat ad me Deus fili hominis perfode parietem. Causam reddit, unde facta sit ista fenestella.

ET CVM FODISSEM PARIETEM) Nempe in visione, sed plane quasi res vere ageretur.

APPARVIT OSTIVM VNVM) Exstiterat illa fe- nestella. Nam omnis apertura Hebræis פתח dicitur: ideo- que Græci nonnunquam vertunt ἄνοιγμα.

## 8:10
Verse 10.

AND BEHOLD EVERY LIKENESS OF CREEPING THINGS AND ANIMALS, ABOMINATION) That is, which the Egyptians and others worship.

AND ALL THE IDOLS OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL DEPICTED ON THE WALL ROUND ABOUT) They thought they were sinning less because they had not raised figures, but painted ones. But even the paintings of those forms which were proper to idolaters were forbidden. This appears in Leviticus 26:1, Numbers 33:52 in the Hebrew. It was the custom of the Troglodytes to paint such forms on walls, as Philastrius relates.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET ECCE OMNIS SIMILITUDO REPTILIVM ET ANIMALIVM, ABOMINATIO) Id est, quæ colunt Ægyptii, aliique.

ET VNIVERSA IDOLA DOMVS ISRAEL DE- PICTA IN PARIETE IN CIRCVITV PER TOTVM) Putabant se minus peccare, quod non eminentes sed pictas haberent figuras. Verum etiam picturæ vetitæ earum for- marum quæ propriæ erant idololatris. Apparet id Levit. 26, 1. Num. 33, 52. in Hebræo. Pingere tales formas in parie- tibus mos erat Troglodytarum, narrante Philastrio.

## 8:11
Verse 11.

AND SEVENTY MEN OF THE ELDERS OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) That is, those seventy who stood out among all the judges with supreme power; they had both approached where it was not lawful for them to be, and were seeing things which it was their duty to remove.

AND JEZANIAH THE SON OF SHAPHAN STOOD IN THE MIDST OF THEM) He is named in 2 Kings 22:9. It is credible that he was the prince of the Senate.

IN THE MIDST OF THEM STANDING BEFORE THE PICTURES) Of the Levites.

AND EVERY ONE HAD A CENSER IN HIS HAND) He does not say that those seventy offered incense in honor of the idols: but if it was not lawful to have such pictures, it was even less lawful to worship God near them.

Saa and Maldonatus think these things were represented to the mind of the Prophet only in a vision; but others more correctly judge that the thing itself was seen: because in Ezekiel 5:11, Jeremiah 7:30, and chapter 32:34, idols are said to have been placed in the temple: and not only the priests, but also other prominent men had their chambers, Jeremiah 35:15, Ezekiel 16:38. That women truly burned incense to idols is clear from Jeremiah 44:15.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET SEPTVAGINTA VIRI DE SENIORIBVS DO- MIS ISRAEL) Id est, illi septuaginta, qui inter judices omnes eminebant summa cum potestate, tum eo acces- serant quo fas ipsis non erat, tum ea videbant quæ tollere ipsorum erat officii.

ET JEZONIAS FILIVS SAPHAN STABAT IN MEDIO EORVM) Nominatur 2. Reg. 22 9. Eum credi- bile est fuisse Senatus principem.

IN MEDIO EORVM STANTIVM ANTE PI- CTURAS) Levitarum.

ET VNVSQVISQVE HABEBAT THVRIBV- LVM IN MANV SVA) Non dicit illos LXX. suffitum fecisse in honorem idolorum: sed si picturas tales habere non licebat, minus etiam licebat apud eas Deum colere.

In visione tantum haec animo Prophetae re- praesentata Saa, & Maldonatus putant; at alii re- ctius rem ipsam visam censent: quia Ezech. 5, 11. Jerem. 7, 30. cap. 32, 34. idola in templo collocata dicuntur: & cellas suas habuere non solum Sacer- dotes, sed & praecipui alii Jerem. 35, 15. Ezech. 16, 38. Mulieres revera adolevisse idolis, liquet e Jer. 44. v. 15.

## 8:12
Verse 12.

IN THE DARK) For all those chambers were diligently obstructed, so that they could not be seen unless the wall was pierced.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

IN TENEBRIS) Omnia enim illarum cellarum di- ligenter obstructa erant, ut nisi forato pariete inspici ne- quirent.

## 8:14
AND BEHOLD THERE WOMEN WERE SITTING WEEPING FOR ADONIS) In Hebrew it is תמוז. Some think it is Osiris, who is called Ammuz by a similar sound in Herodotus and Plutarch. But Maimonides, Kimchi, and other Hebrews say he was a notable magician, about whom they tell wondrous things. Jerome, however, seems to have put Adonis there because in the same way Adonis was mourned by the Assyrians: on which matter see Macrobius, Saturnalia 1, 21. And by their example by the Egyptians, as the Adoniazousai of Theocritus teach: and by the Greeks, as Bion: and that Thammuz of the Chaldeans, who also gave the name of one of the months from him.

Latin:

ET ECCE IBI MVLIERES SEDEBANT PLAN- GENTES ADONIDEM) In Hebraeo est תמוז. Quidam Osirim esse putant, qui vicina voce Ammuz Herodoto & Plutarcho. Sed Maimonides, Kimchi, & Hebraeorum alii magum aiunt fuisse insignem, de quo mira narrant. Hieron. autem Adonidem ideo posuisse videtur, quod quo modo Adonis lugebatur ab Assyriis: qua de re vide Macrobium Saturnalium 1, 21. & eorum exemplo ab Aegyptiis, ut do- cent Αδωνιαζουσαι Theocriti: & a Graecis, ut Bion: eo & Thammuz ille Chaldaeis, qui & mensium uni nomen ab eo dedere.

## 8:16
Verse 16. AND HE BROUGHT ME INTO THE INNER COURT OF THE LORD'S HOUSE) The priestly one.

AT THE DOOR OF THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD BETWEEN THE PORCH AND THE ALTAR) That door through which one went from the portico of the Temple (for that is אולם to the Hebrews, see 1 Kings 6, 3.) to the altar of burnt offerings.

ABOUT TWENTY-FIVE MEN) Lest one or another might be thought to do it.

HAVING THEIR BACKS TOWARD THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) Turned away from that part in which was the sanctuary, which is here the Temple, because it is the more worthy part of the Temple.

AND THEIR FACES TOWARD THE EAST, AND THEY WERE WORSHIPPING TOWARD THE RISING OF THE SUN) Turned toward the East after the manner of the Chaldeans, not toward the West, which is the custom of the Jews. See Dan. 6, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET DVXIT ME IN ATRIVM DOMVS DOMINI INTERIVS) Sacerdotale.

IN OSTIO TEMPLI DOMINI INTER VESTI- BVLVM ET ALTARE) Ostium illud per quod ex por- ticu Templi (id enim אולם Hebraeis, vide 1. Reg. 6, 3.) ibatur altare holocaustorum.

QVASI VIGINTI QVINQVE VIRI) Ne unus aut alter id facere putaretur.

DORSA HABENTES CONTRA TEMPLVM DOMINI) Aversi ab ea parte in qua erat adytum quod hic Templum, quia pars Templi dignior.

ET FACIES AD ORIENTEM, ET ADORA- BANT AD ORTVM SOLIS) Ad Orientem versi more Chaldaeorum, non ad Occidentem, qui mos Judaeorum. Vide Dan. 6, 10.

## 8:17
Verse 17. AND BEHOLD THEY PUT THE BRANCH TO THEIR NOSE) It is indeed written זמרה, but the Hebrews testify that it was formerly written זמרי, and that זמורה, that is, a song, is ridiculously called a fart: in which sense that word is also found in the Aruch. God therefore (as Solomon and David Kimchi judge) says that they are offering obscene blasts to Him; namely, because they turned their back to God, as we have already said. Because that seemed to be said less decorously, it was changed by the writers of a later age. Similar changes were made in eighteen other places.

There is no cause for that change. Nor are the Hebrews to be listened to here, by whom Grotius is very often misled; the ordinary reading is consistent with itself. For זמורה does not signify a stench anywhere: but a branch, as the Concordances of R. Mordecai Nathan also testify. The root is זמר, he pruned. Jerome expresses the sense. It signifies, however, the twenty-five men, who are established in the square station accustomed to them: and from the five senses, through five times five they make the figure of a square, not only to have the temple behind their back, but like idols to apply a branch to their noses, there is no doubt, that of palms, which they call τα βαια in the Greek language, so that by this it signifies that they are worshipping idols. Finally, Job also says that among other virtues he had this: that he never looking at the heaven and the sun, and the moon, and the shining stars, kissed his hand, that is, worshipped creatures. Let Glassius, Philologia Sacra, book 1, tract 1, p. 49, be consulted. Because most nations worshipped the rising Sun, therefore the Holy of Holies looked toward the west, so that the Jews would not follow the custom of the nations.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET ECCE APPLICANT RAMVM AD NA- RES SVAS) Scribitur quidem זמרה, sed olim זמרי scri- ptum fuisse testantur Hebraei, & זמורה, id est, canticum ridicule vocari ventris crepitum: quo sensu ea vox & in Aruch reperitur. Deus igitur (ut censet Salomo & David Kimchi) ait eos sibi opponere flatus obscoenos; nempe quod tergumDeo obverterent, ut jam diximus. Quod quia minus decore dici videbatur, mutatum est a posterioris aevi scripto- ribus. Similes mutationes factae in aliis locis octodecim.

Mutationis istius nulla causa est. Neque audi- endi hic Ebraei, a quibus saepissime seducitur Gro- tius; Recte sibi constat lectio ordinaria. Neque e- nim זמורה fatorem uspiam significat: Sed palmi- tem, quod etiam Concordantiae R. Mardochai Na- than testantur. Radix est זמר amputavit. Sensum exprimit Hieronym. Significat autem viginti quin- que viros, qui in quadrum solita statione fundati sunt: & a quinque sensibus, per quinquies quinque quadran- guli figuram efficiunt, non solum templum habere post tergum, sed instar Idolorum applicare ramum ad na- res suas, haud dubium, quin palmarum, quas Graeco sermone τα βαια vocant, ut per hoc eos idola adorare significet. Denique & Job inter caeteras virtutes etiam hoc habuisse se dicit: quod nunquam aspiciens coelum & solem, & lunam, & astra fulgentia osculatus sit manum suam, id est adoraverit creaturas. Conse- ratur Glassius Phil. sacra lib. 1. tract. 1. p. 49. Quia pleraeque gentes orientem Solem adorabant, ideo Sanctum Sanctorum occidentem respiciebat, ut Judaei gentium morem non sequerentur.

## 8:18
Verse 18.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

## 8:18
Verse 18. THEREFORE I ALSO WILL DEAL IN FURY) I will do the same to them; I will turn my back to those praying. God gives the reasons why He is going to allow the Temple to be cut off.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ERGO ET EGO FACIAM IN FURORE) Idem ipsis faciam; tergum obvertam orantibus. Reddit Deus causas cur Templum exscindi sit passurus.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX. Six men appearing are all ordered to slaughter in Jerusalem those who are not marked with a sign by the man clothed in linen: which being done, the Lord answers the exclaiming Prophet that this will happen because of their own crimes.

AND HE CRIED IN MINE EARS) God, that is to say. THE VISITATIONS OF THE CITY HAVE DRAWN NEAR) That is, the Prefects of the city: whom God, of course, set over the city to be destroyed, the leaders of the army of Nebuchadnezzar, who attacked the city from six sides. He calls those prefects of the city by way of mockery, such as we have had elsewhere. It is common, however, for the Hebrews to say prefectures instead of prefects, as here, and similar things. AND EVERY MAN HAS A WEAPON OF SLAUGHTER IN HIS HAND) The instrument of the destroyers: as the Chaldean has it here, which the LXX interpret as an axe, not badly. FROM THE WAY OF THE UPPER GATE, WHICH LOOKETH TOWARD THE NORTH) This way was between the north and the east, which is the location of the nation of the Chaldeans in relation to Judea. Verse 2. AND ONE MAN IN THE MIDST OF THEM WAS CLOTHED WITH LINEN) In the Greek: clothed in a long garment, namely of the finest linen, such as was that of the high priest, Leviticus 6:10, 16:4, 23, 32. The same attire is given here, and in Dan. 10:5, 12:6, 7, to the angel, as to the high priest. For both are ministers of God. AND A WRITER'S INKHORNS BY HIS LOINS) Namely, so that he might write that which is said below in verse 4. For קסת, Aquila and Theodotus placed κάσυ, and Jerome says that he learned from the Hebrews that by that word an inkhorn or inkstand is signified. Nor did the Chaldean take it otherwise here. But the LXX interpret קסת as a girdle, and for ספר they read ספיר, wrongly. AND THEY WENT IN) Both into the city and the temple. AND STOOD BESIDE THE BRAZEN ALTAR) Of burnt offerings, namely as those who were about to prepare many victims for God. For thus are the wicked wont to be called, from whom God wishes to take vengeance, Isa. 34:6, Jer. 12:3, 46:10. Below 21:9, 10, 39:17, Dan. 7:11. See what was said at Mark 9:49. Verse 3. AND THE GLORY OF THE GOD OF ISRAEL) A certain brightness, such as sometimes appeared above the Cherubim in the sanctuary. WAS GONE UP FROM THE CHERUB, WHEREUPON HE WAS) It is more correctly translated from the Hebrew, upon which he had been: that is, upon which he had been. That brightness passed from the vehicle to the threshold of the priestly basilica, which looked from nearby upon the altar of burnt offerings. Verse 4. AND THE LORD SAID UNTO HIM.) That is, the voice of some greater Angel sounded from that brightness, speaking in the name of God. GO THROUGH THE MIDST OF THE CITY, THROUGH THE MIDST OF JERUSALEM,) That is: through the middle of the city of Jerusalem.

That the Holy Spirit teaches that that man was not a created angel, but the Son of God, our only High Priest, is shown by the priestly attire, because no angel ever appeared in priestly attire, nor performed the office of a high priest. Which office the Holy Spirit teaches belongs to men, not to angels, Heb. 5:1. He who appeared in Daniel 10:5, 12:6, 7, was by no means a created angel, but the Son of God himself, as is evident from a comparison with Rev. 1:13. For that long linen garment was the priestly attire, with which the Levitical priests were clothed in the time of atonement and intercession for the people. Exod. 28:16, Lev. 6:10, 16:4, 23, 32. Nor does Grotius deny this. Furthermore, since it is the proper office of Christ to deliver from destruction, which was done here by the angel, Christ is deservedly understood to be that angel of the new covenant, who marked his own, so that they might be exempted from slaughter. And the description of the Prophet testifies that he was not from the order of other angels: who separates him from the six other men, in whose midst he was placed, having the others as his attendants, from whom he is distinguished both by dignity and by the function of his office. Furthermore, that man is shown having a writer's inkhorn at his loins. The LXX translated it as ζωνην σαφφειριν, a sapphire girdle; which the Ancients apply likewise to Christ, especially Jerome: inasmuch as the Prince of Priests wore such a Sapphire Girdle. We have, therefore, the ancients agreeing that that man is Christ, our High Priest. See Irenaeus, book 4, chapter 14.

Jerome on this passage, who also praises others for this opinion; Gregory the Great, Rupert, etc. To which opinion also most of the Calvinist Interpreters agree: Junius, Tremellius, Piscator, Polanus, Marloratus on the Apocalypse. And also from the Pontificals, Saa, Gislerius, Pintus, Estius, Sanctius, Fradus, etc. Nor does it stand in the way (which some here urge with Cornelius à Lapide) that that man says: I have done as thou hast commanded me, because Christ is presented not according to the essence of his divinity, but according to the economy and by reason of his priestly office: which befits him as God-man, not in the simple nature of the Deity. Compare Ps. 40:2, John 14:31, chapter 17:2. The blessed Lord Dr. Hulsemann pursues these things at greater length in his Commentary, and especially the blessed Lord Dr. Caelestinus Myslenta, our colleague, fellow-godparent, and formerly most intimate Brother, in Disputation 1 on the foundations of the errors of the Papacy. The Weimar Paraphrasts agree, as do most others of our own, the blessed Dr. Pappus: through this man, he says, we must without controversy understand the one mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ. For he is clothed in linen garments to signify both his priesthood and to testify to his innocence. For linen garments were white, the vestments of priests, which would admonish them of purity of life and innocence. But the other priests could neither offer a true propitiatory sacrifice, nor were they immune from sins. Our Savior, however, mocked in a white garment by Herod, is our true Priest, who by the one sacrifice of his own body perfected forever those who are to be sanctified, and who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth. He has, moreover, an inkhorn at his loins, so that he may mark the foreheads of those to be saved, not with the blood of the Paschal lamb, as the Hebrews once did their doorposts in Egypt; but with his own blood, which cleanses us from all sin.

Latin:

CAPUT IX. Apparentes sex viri omnes in Ierusalem truci- dare jubentur, qui a viro lineis vestito signo notati non sunt: quo facto Dominus excla- manti Prophetae respondet id futurum exi- gentibus ipsorum criminibus.

Vers. 1. ET IN AURIBUS MEIS CLAMAVIT) Deus scilicet. APPROPINQUAVERUNT VISITATIONES UR- BIS) Id est, Praefecti urbis: quos scilicet Deus urbi destruen- dae praefecit, duces exercitus Nabuchodonosoris, qui ex sex partibus urbem oppugnarunt. Eos praefectos urbis vo- cat per χλευασμὸν, qualem & alibi habuimus. Frequens autem est Hebraeis pro praefectis dicere praefecturas, ut hic, & similia. ET UNUSQUISQUE VAS INTERFECTIONIS HABET IN MANU SUA) Instrumentum destructorum: ut hic habet Chaldaeus, quod LXX. interpretantur securim, non male. DE VIA PORTIS SUPERIORIS, QUAE RE- SPICIT AD AQUILONEM) Erat haec via inter septen- trionem Orientemque media, qui situs est gentis Chaldaeo- rum ad Judaeam. Vers. 2. VIR QUOQUE UNUS IN MEDIO EO- RUM VESTITUS ERAT LINEIS) In Graeco: ἐνδεδυκὼς ποδήρη, nempe ex lino tenuissimo, qualis erat Pontificis ma- ximi Levit. 6, 10. 16, 4. 23. 32. Idem habitus hic, & in Dan. 10, 5. 12, 6. 7. datur angelo, qui Pontifici maximo. Ambo enim ministri Dei. ET ATRAMENTARIUM SCRIPTORIS AD RE- NES EJUS) Nempe ut scriberet id quod infra dicitur 4. Pro קסת, κάσυ posuerunt Aquila & Theodotio, eaque vo- ce calamarium aut atramentarium significari ab Hebraeis se dedicisse ait Hieronymus. Nec aliter hic sumsit Chaldaeus. At LXX. קסת interpretantur zonam, & pro ספר legunt ספיר, male. ET INGRESSI SUNT) Tam urbem, quam templum. ET STETERUNT JUXTA ALTARE AENEUM) Holocaustorum, nempe ut qui multas Deo paraturi erant victimas. Ita enim appellari solent scelerati, de quibus Deus sumere vult ultionem, Esa. 34, 6. Jerem. 12, 3. 46, 10. Infra 21, 9. 10. 39, 17. Dan. 7. 11. Vide quae dicta ad Marc. 9, 49. Vers. 3. ET GLORIA DOMINI ISRAEL) Fulgor quidam, qualis interdum super Cherubinos in adyto appa- rebat. ASSUMTA EST DE CHERUB, QUAE ERAT SUPER EUM, AD LIMEN DOMUS) Hebraeum re- ctius vertitur, quem erat super eum: id est, super quem fue- rat. Fulgor ille transiit a vehiculo ad limen basilicae sa- cerdotalis, quod de proximo spectabat altare holocau- storum. Vers. 4. ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD EUM.) Id est, vox majoris Angeli alicujus sonuit de illo fulgore, Dei nomine loquens. TRANSI PER MEDIAM CIVITATEM IN ME- DIO JERUSALEM,) Id est: per mediam urbem Hie- rosolymorum.

Virum illum non angelum fuisse creatum, sed Fi- lium Dei, Pontificem nostrum unicum docet habi- tus sacerdotalis, quia nullus nuquam angelorum aut sacerdotali habitu apparuit, aut pontificis munere functus est. Quod officium hominum esse docet Spiritus Sanctus, non angelorum Ebr. 5, 1. Qui Da- niel. 10, 5. 12, 6. 7. apparuit, minime creatus angelus fuit, sed ipse Filius Dei, ut e collatione Apoc. 1, 13. constat. Vestis enim illa talaris linea habitus sacer- dotalis erat, quo induebantur Levitici Sacerdotes in tempore expiationis, & intercessionis pro popu- lo. Exod. 28, 16. Lev. 6, 10. 16, 4. 23. 32. Neque id diffite- tur Grotius. Porro cum officium Christi proprium sit ab exitio liberare, quod hic ab angelo factum est, merito Christus angelus ille foederis novi intelli- gitur, qui signabat suos, ut ab occisione eximeren- tur. Neque ex aliorum angelorum ordine hunc fuisse, descriptio Prophetae testatur: Qui eundem a sex viris aliis separat, in quorum medio constitu- tus ille caeteros ceu stipatores habuit, a quibus & dignitate, & officii munere discriminatur. Praete- rea exhibetur vir ille habens atramentarium scri- ptoris in lumbis suis. LXX. verterunt ζωνην σαφφει- ριν Zonam seu cingulum sapphirinum; Quod pariter ad Christum applicant Veteres, imprimis Hiero- nymus: Siquidem Princeps Sacerdotum ejus- modi Zonam Sapphirinam gestavit. Habemus ergo consentientes veteres, quod vir ille Christus sit Pontifex noster. Videatur Irenaeus lib. 4. cap. 14

Hieronymus in hunc locum, qui alios etiam in eam sententiam laudat; Gregorius Magnus, Rupertus &c. Cui sententiæ etiam suffragantur Calviniani Inter- pretes plerique omnes Junius, Tremellius, Pisca- tor, Polanus, Marloratus in Apoc. Nec non è Pon- tificiis Saa, Gislerius, Pintus, Estius, Sanctius, Fra- dus &c. neque obstat (quod hic cum Cornelio à La- pide nonnulli urgent,) quod vir ille dicat: Feci sicut præcepisti mihi, quia sistitur Christus non κατ’ ὐσίαν divinitatis, sed κατ’ ὀικονομίαν & ratione muneris sa- cerdotalis: quod ipsi convenit ut θεανθρώπῳ, non in simplice Deitatis natura. Confer. Ps. 40, 2. Job. 14, 31. cap. 17, 2. Pluribus hæc exsequuntur B. Dn. D. Hulsemannus in Comment. & cumprimis B. Dn. D. Cælest. Myslenta collega, compater, & Frater no- ster quondam conjunctissimus, in Disput. 1. de fun- damentis errorum Papatus. Consentiunt Paraphra- stæ Vinarienses, ut & alii plerique è nostris B. D. Pappus: per hunc virum, inquit, sine controversia u- num mediatorem Dei & hominum, hominem Je- sum Christum debemus intelligere. Ille enim lineis indu- tus est vestibus ad significandum & sacerdotium suum, & innocentiam suam testandam. Erant enim vestes lineæ candidæ, sacerdotum gestamina, quæ illos de vitæ puritate & innocentia admonerent. At cæteri quidem Sacerdotes neque verum ἱλαστικὸν sacrificium pote- rant offerre, neque à peccatis immunes erant. Servator autem noster in veste candida ab Herode illusus verus Sacerdos noster est, qui uno sacrificio sui ipsius corporis omnes in æternum sanctificandos consummavit, quique peccatum nullum fecit, neque dolus in ore ejus reper- tus est. Habet autem & ad lumbos atramentarium, ut frontes salvandorum signet, non agni Paschalis sangui- ne, sicut olim in Ægypto Hebræi suos postes; sed proprio sanguine, qui nos emundat ab omni peccato.

## 9:4
AND MARK THAU UPON THE FOREHEADS OF THE MEN THAT SIGH AND THAT CRY FOR ALL THE ABOMINATIONS.) The letter ת from which the word תּוֹרָה begins, signified that they had been devoted to the Law. It was customary for servants to have the name of their master on their forehead. See Hesychius, ἱεριάνα, & Σαμίων δημῶ. Both the Chaldean and Theodotion felt that not just any sign, but the letter Thau was signified here. Jerome says in his commentaries on this passage that that letter, in the ancient Hebrew characters which the Samaritans used, had the likeness of a cross. Scaliger denies this in his Eusebian works, though he does not deny that the Samaritan alphabet was known to Jerome. I do not see what prevents there having been several figures of one letter among the Samaritans and the ancient Hebrews. We mark what we wish to be well guarded. Thus God wished to save those who revered the Law from the slaughter, which is a figure of those who will be saved from the common destruction of the world.

That the letter ת was inscribed on the foreheads of those marked is asserted without solid foundation, and therefore the meaning is vainly sought from the word תּוֹרָה, which begins with ת. In the Hebrew text, it is generally named only as a sign, וְהִתְוִיתָ תָּו, and you shall mark a mark: by a very well-known Hebraism, that is: mark diligently: as in ch. 3, 8, eating you shall eat: Lam. 1, 2, weeping she weeps, etc. And thus the LXX, Aquila, Symmachus, Rabbi Solomon, and many Christians, Chrysostom Hom. 18 to the people of Antioch, and others interpret it. And Sanctius admits that this is the interpretation of the ancients concordant before Jerome. And although in v. 6 it is said, upon whom is the תָּו sign, do not root him out. Whence it is gathered that the same character was marked, yet it is by no means to be admitted that that character was a letter impressed upon the foreheads, as the Chaldean and Theodotion wished, since that name תָּו is used appellatively in the Code, and it does not occur anywhere as the proper name of a letter: see Num. 34, 7, 8, 10; Job 31, v. 35. Nor does any letter of the alphabet occur anywhere in the sacred code τεχνικῶς, or used for itself and its external form. What Mejerus urges, that unless the letter ת is understood, the Prophet could not have known what he ought to paint as a sign, it is answered: The Prophet was not to paint the sign, but a man clothed in linen. Grotius, however, favors the Papists, who contend with great zeal that it was the letter ת, and they wish it to have signified the Cross of Christ: from which they further conclude that the sign of the Cross of Christ is a salutary remedy against the evils of body and soul. Although this consequence is entirely futile, unless one also equally leads oneself to conclude that the figure of the serpent is a salutary remedy today, because formerly the figure of the bronze serpent was used by God as a sign and means of salvation. Nevertheless, we think the antecedent should by no means be conceded to the Papists. Because it can neither be proven that the letter ת is understood here, nor did that letter ever have the shape of a cross, much less signify the Cross of Christ. Although Grotius would gladly help the Papists; yet he can bring forward nothing for the shape of the cross, except that Jerome says, in the ancient Hebrew letters, which the Samaritans used, the letter ת had a resemblance to a cross. And nothing prevents there having been several shapes of one letter among the Samaritans and the ancient Hebrews. Even if this is admitted, it cannot immediately be concluded that precisely this shape, whether among the Samaritans or among the Hebrews, was the one by which the Papists wish the Cross of Christ to be shadowed forth. Nor does Jerome speak from his own mind, but from the opinion of the Samaritans, who boasted that they retained the entire Hebrew letters, as is evident from his commentary on chapter 40 of Ezekiel. Then, if that shape of the letter ת was impressed on foreheads, which God used on the stone tablets, Jerome acknowledges in q. 1 to Hedibia that that shape still exists in our codices. Which, however, does not represent the form of a cross. Nor could Sanctius show, either in our memory or that of the Jews, that the letter ת had the form of a cross, or that it could be proven from ancient monuments, stones, or coins of the Jews. And Gretser acknowledges in lib. 1 de cruc., Bartholomaeus Majerus in part 1 of Philosophia Sacra, chapter 2, and Schickard in Bechenoth Happeruschim, page 80, and in the tract on the law of the Hebrew Kings, 4, c. 6, that the ancient Hebrew Thau did not correspond to the T of the Latins and Greeks. They think rather that it was analogous to the capital X of the Greeks and the X of the Latins, the form of which kind of wood the cross of Christ also had, as Lipsius thinks in lib. 1 de cruce c. 2, Baronius in Tom. 1 of the annals for the year 34, n. 132, and others. And therefore it is necessary that they first settle among themselves which shape was the ancient letter Thau, and which one corresponds to the cross of Christ! What of the fact that from the Pontificians themselves, Hector Pintus, Pradus, and Villalpandus plainly reject that opinion about the similarity of the wood of the cross and the character of the Hebrew letter Thau? The Samaritan characters certainly (although there is no commerce with them by the Hebrews), which Crinesius exhibits in his discourse on the Confusion of languages, have nothing in common with the form of a Cross. Nor does it correspond to the T of the Latins and Greeks; which Estius in annotations to CIX. 4 and Genebrardus to Ps. 67, 47 imagine to have been the twin of the Hebrew Thau. If indeed the cross was verticillated. But T lacks any vertex, and is more like a crossbar than a cross. That the characters of the ancient Hebrews were Samaritan is also denied by Schickard in Im Trichter, p. 21. Who proves that the modern Hebrew characters were in use at the time of Christ from Matt. 5, 18, because the letter Jod is the smallest in the Hebrew character, not the Samaritan. That they were also in use before Christ, indeed in the time of Moses, is taught both from Ex. 26, v. 10, because the hooks are called וויו on account of the similarity they have with the letter Vau, which the Hebrew character, not the Samaritan, exhibits: and from various ancient readings, which the conformity of the letters produced, which indeed are all very dissimilar among the Samaritans: and because the Samaritans lack three letters דחף

with these missing, how could the Pentateuch have been written? Compare on this passage D. Könnig in Vind. locor., locus CXI.

Latin:

ET SIGNA THAU SUPER FRONTES VIRO- RUM GEMENTIUM ET DOLENTIUM SUPER CUN- CTIS ABOMINATIONIBUS.) Lit. ת unde incipit vox תוֹרָה, significabat illos fuisse legi addictos. Solebant in rienote servi in fronte habere nomen domini. Vide Hesy- chium ἱεριάνα, & Σαμίων δημῶ. Non qualecunque signum, sed literam Thau hic significari sensit & Chaldæus & Theodo- tio. Eam literam in antiquis Hebræorum literis, quibus ute- bantur Samaritani, crucis habuisse similitudinem, dicit in commentariis in hunc locum Hieronymus. Negat id in Eu- sebianis Scaliger, qui tamen Hieronymo cognitum fuisse Alphabetum Samaritanum non negat. Non video, quid obstet, quo minus apud Samaritas & Hebræos Veteres unius literæ plures figuræ fuerint. Signamus quæ bene cu- stodita volumus. Sic Deus illos legis reverentes servare vo- luit ab occidione, quæ figura est eorum, qui à communi mundi exitio servabuntur.

Literam ת frontibus inscriptam fuisse signato- rum, sine solido fundamento asseritur, ideoque fru- stra significatio è vore תוֹרָה, quæ à ת incipit, peti- tur. In Ebræo textu generatim tantum signum no- minatur וְהִתְוִיתָ תָּו & signabis signum: per Ebrais- mum notissimum, id est: deligenter signa: uti c. 3, 8. comedendo comedes: Thren. 1, 2. Plorando plorat &c. Atque ita interpretantur LXX. Aquila, Sym- machus, Rabbi Salomo, & multi è Christiani, Chrysostomus Hom. 18. ad popul. Ant. & alii. Ac fa- tetur, Sanctius, concordem eam esse veterum ante Hieronymum interpretationem. Et quanquam v. 6. dicatur, super quo תָּו signum, illum ne eradice- tis. Unde colligitur, eundem characterem signa- tum fuisse, minime tamen admittendum literam illnm characterem fuisse forontibus impres- sum, uti Chaldæus, & Theodotio voluit, siquidem nomen illud תָּו in Codice appellative usurpa- tur, non vero uspiam ut nomen literæ proprium occurrit: vide Num. 34, 7. 8. 10. Job. 31. v. 35. Ne- que ulla Alphabeti litera τεχνικῶς in codice sacro uspiam occurrat, vel pro se, & forma externa usur- pata. Quod Mejerus urget, nisi litera ת intelliga- tur Prophetam scire non potuisse, quale deberet fignum pingere, Respondetur: Non Propheta de- buit pingere fignum, sed vir lineis indutus. Velifica- tur autem Grotius Papistis, qui magno studio id contendunt literam ת fuisse, eamque Crucem Chri- sti significasse volunt: ex quo porro concludunt fi- gnum Crucis Christi esse remedium salutare adversus mala corporis & animæ. Quæ consequentia etsi fu- tilis prorsus sit, nisi etiam pariter quis colligendum ducat figuram serpentis remedium hodie salutare esse, quia olim à Deo figura ænei serpentis, ceu salutis signum & medium adhibita est. Antecedens tamen Papistis minime concedendum arbitramur. Quia neque probari potest literam ת hic intelligi, neque litera illa figuram crucis unquam habuit, nedum crucem Christi significavit. Grotius etsi juvare Papistas li- benter velit; nihil tamen proferre potest pro figura crucis, nisi quod Hieronymus dicat, in antiquis He- bræorum literis, quibus usi Samaritani sint, literam ת crucis habuisse similitudinem. Atque nihil obstat, quo minus apud Samaritas & Hebræos veteres, unius literæ plures figuræ fuerint. Quod etiamsi admittatur, non statim concludi potest, præcise hanc figuram seu a- pud Samaritanos seu apud Ebræos obtinuisse, qua Christi crucem adumbratam volunt Papistæ. Neq; Hieronymus ex propria mente loquitur, sed Samari- tanorum opinione, qui jactabant, se integras Ebræo- rum literas retinere, ut ex commentario ejus in c. 40. Ezech. constat. Tum si ea figura literæ ת im- pressa frontibus fuit, qua usus Deus est in tabulis lapideis, agnoscit Hieronymus q. 1. ad Hedib. eam figuram adhuc extare in nostris codicibus. Quæ vero non repræsentat formam crucis. Nec ostendere potuit Sanctius, vel nostra, vel Judæorum memoria literam ת habuisse crucis formam, aut è veteribus solum monumentis, saxis vel nummis Judæorum id probari. Et agnoscit Gretserus lib. 1. de cruc. Bar- tholomæus Majerus part 1. Philos. Sacræ cap. 2. Schi- ckard, in Bechenoth Happeruschim pag. 80. & tract. de jure Regum Ebr. 4, c. 6. Thau antiquum Ebræum non respondisse T Latinorum & Græcorum. Putant autem potius analogum fuisse X majusculo Græco- rum, & X Latinôrum, cujus modi etiam formam li- gnum crucis Christi habuisse Lipsius lib. 1. de cruce c. 2. Baronius Tom. 1. annal. ad annum 34. n. 132. & alii arbitrantur. Ideoque necessum est, ut prius de eo transigant, utra forma fuerit literæ Thau an- tiqua, utra cruci Christi conveniat! Quid quod ex ipsis Pontificiis Hector Pintus, Pradus, Villalpandus plane reprobent istam opinionem de similitudine ligni crucis, & characteris Ebraicæ literæ Thau. Samaritani certe Characteres, (quamvis nihil cum illis commercii sit Ebræis) quos Crinesius in discur- su de Confus. linguarum exhibet, nihil commune habent cum forma Crucis. Neque Latinorum & Græcorum T illi respondet; quibus geminum Thau Ebræorum fuisse Estius in annot. ad CIX. 4. & Genebrardus ad Ps. 67, 47. fingit. Siquidem crux verticillata fuerit. T autem omni careat vertice, & antennæ potius, quam cruci similis sit. Characte- res Ebræorum antiquorum Samaritanos fuisse, etiam à Schickardo negatur im Trichter p. 21. Qui pro- bat, modernos Characteres Ebræorum tempore Christi in usu fuisse è Matth. 5, 18. quia litera Jod Charactere Hebræo, non Samaritano minima sit. Quod autem & ante Christum, imo Mosis tempore in usu fuerint, docet tum à cap. 26. Ex. v. 10. quod uncini וויו vocentur ob similitudinem, quam habent cum litera Vau, quam Character Ebræus, non Sa- maritanus exhibet: Tum è variis lectionibus anti- quis, quas peperit conformitas literarum, qui ve- ro apud Samaritanos omnes valde dissimiles sunt: Tum quod Samaritani careant tribus literis דחף

quibus deficientibus quomodo Pentateuchus exa- rari potuit? Confer de hoc loco D. Könnig in Vind. locor. loco CXI.

## 9:5
Vers. 5. AND TO THEM HE SAID) To the Chaldean leaders.

## 9:6
Vers. 6. OLD MAN, YOUNG MAN, AND VIRGIN, AND LITTLE ONES AND WOMEN) See 2 Par. 36, 17.

AND BEGIN AT MY SANCTUARY) Slaughter those first who are in the Temple.

SO THEY BEGAN WITH THE ELDERLY MEN, WHO WERE BEFORE THE FACE OF THE HOUSE) With those seventy who were in the cells surrounding the Temple 8, 11.

Vers. 6. SENEM JUVENEM, ET VIRGINEM, PAR- VVLOSQVE ET FEMINAS) Vide 2. Par. 36, 17.

ET A SANCTVARIO MEO INCIPITE) Illos primum trucidate qui in Templo sunt.

COEPERVNT ERGO A VIRIS SENIORIBVS, QVI ERANT ANTE FACIEM DOMVS) Illis LXX. qui erant in cellulis circumjectis Templo 8, 11.

Vers. 7. DEFILE THE HOUSE) Pollute the Temple, forsaken by God, with blood.

AND THE CITY IS FILLED WITH AVERSION) Idolatry.
