ET CIVITAS REPLETA EST AVERSIONE) Idololatria.

DIXERVNT ENIM: DERELIQVIT DOMINVS TERRAM, ET DOMINVS NON VIDET) Non curat res humanas.

## 9:11
Verse 11. I HAVE DONE AS THOU HAST COMMANDED ME) As centurions in Rome were accustomed to say to the Emperors: It is done what you commanded. The sense is this: it is provided that the pious be spared.

Latin:

Vers. 11. FECI SICVT PRÆCEPISTI MIHI) Ut cen- turiones Romæ Imperatoribus dicere solebant: Factum est quod imperasti, Sensus hic est: provisum ut piis parcatur.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

A man clothed in linen pours out coals of fire taken from the midst of the wheels: And again the glory of the Lord is seen in the Cherubim & wheels.

Verse 1. IN THE FIRMAMENT THAT WAS ABOVE THE HEAD OF THE CHERUBIM) In the vault of the vehicle, as we said 1, 26.

AS IT WERE A SAPPHIRE STONE, AS THE APPEARANCE OF THE LIKENESS OF A THRONE APPEARED ABOVE IT) Above that vault, under which were the Cherubim. Many think τὰ χερυβεὶμ is said in the neuter gender and plural number: Jerome says at this place. It is signified here by the repeated vision that those horrible judgments of God are approaching nearer and nearer.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Vir lineis vestitus prunas ignis de medio ro- tarum acceptas effundit: Iterumque vide- tur Domini gloria in Cherubim & rotis.

Vers. 1. IN FIRMAMENTO QVOD ERAT SVPER CAPVT CHERVBIM) In tympano vehiculi, ut diximus 1, 26.

QVASI LAPIS SAPPHIRVS, QVASI SPECIES SIMILITVDINIS SOLII APPARVIT SVPER EA) Su- per illud tympanum, sub quo erant Cherubini. Plerique τὰ χερυβεὶμ neutrali genere, numeroque plurali dici putant: ait Hieronymus ad hunc locum. Significatur hic repetito viso propius propiusque appropinquare horrenda illa Dei ju- dicia.

## 10:2
Verse 2. AND HE SAID TO THE MAN WHO WAS CLOTHED IN LINEN) To that angel, the minister of his command, of whom above 9, 2.

GO IN INTO THE MIDST OF THE WHEELS) Into the middle of the vehicle.

FILL THY HAND WITH COALS OF FIRE, WHICH ARE BETWEEN THE CHERUBIM, AND SCATTER THEM OVER THE CITY) For fire surrounded the whole vehicle 1, 4. 13. It is signified that it will shortly come to pass that the city shall be set on fire.

Although not a few interpreters, and our B. Hülsemann in his Commentary αι̉νιγ́δοτω̃ς (enigmatically) wish the scattering of fiery coals to signify the burning of the city, nevertheless some interpret it in a good sense; Osiander, and the Weimar Paraphrasts, and others. Namely, our Osiander wishes it to be shown to Ezekiel anew the chariot of the Gospel, in which the savior of the world was one day to be carried through the whole world, and at the same time to be taught; that after the preaching of the Gospel the ruin of the Jewish polity would follow, and since words had been spoken concerning the former devastation of the city of Jerusalem, now it is a matter of the second destruction. Therefore, coals are to be taken from the fire which is between the wheels of the Gospel chariot, and they are to be cast into the city. Because the Gospel is to be preached in Jerusalem with great and clearly fiery power of penetrating and illuminating through the Apostles, just as also the Holy Spirit was sent into Jerusalem in the form of tongues of fire Act. 2. The cloud, therefore, or mist signified, according to the Jews themselves, that they would be blinded by the preached Gospel, and that this would happen especially to the High Priests, Priests, scribes, and Pharisees. But that the court was filled with the splendor of the Lord, [signified] that there would nevertheless be some among the Jews, the Elect, who were to be illuminated by the same Gospel for their salvation. And since the sound of the wings of the Cherubim was added even to the outer court, [it signifies] the sound of the Gospel through The Apostles of preaching were also to be heard among the nations designated by the outer court. Grotius himself, at v. 21, seems to have hinted that this refers to the times of the New Testament; he says, he often repeats it, so that the people, about to live without a temple, might have the mysteries of the example in place of a temple, and thus be much better prepared for the covenant. One must live without a temple especially under the New Testament, where there is no use for an ample Levitical and shadowy temple. However, there is no mention of the Son of Man in this vision of the glory of the Lord, as in ch. 1, 26, above. Because Christ was being presented in his priestly office, in the habit of a man clothed in linen garments, and not, as there, on a majestic throne. Nor does it detract anything from the dignity of the Son of God that in v. 7 fire was given to him by the Cherub to be cast into the city. Because, although the Apostles and Evangelical Doctors scatter the Gospel through the Church, nevertheless it must be scattered by the hands of Christ the mediator and unique High Priest, and it has all its force and virtue from him. To this end, much incense was also given to him in Rev. 8, 3, namely, to reconcile force and efficacy to them. Although it must also be noted that in such mystical and significative visions, just as in parables, it is difficult to apply all the circumstances, and not everything is to be referred to the life, or certainly the reason for everything cannot always be rendered by us. Many things remain mystical. It is enough if we understand the scope of the visions, even if we cannot explain all the τὰ περιςατικὰ.

AND HE ENTERED INTO THE SIGHT OF IT) He stood near the wheels.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET DIXIT AD VIRVM QVI INDVTVS ERAT LINEIS) Ad illum Angelum imperii sui ministrum! de quo supra 9, 2.

INGREDERE IN MEDIO ROTARVM) Adda vehiculo medio.

IMPLE MANVM TVAM PRVNIS IGNIS, QVÆ SVNT INTER CHERVBIM, ET EFFVNDE SVPER CIVITATEM) Ignis enim ambiebat omne vehiculum 1,4. 13. Significatur fore brevi ut urbs incendatur.

Etsi non pauci interpretes, & B. Hülsemannus noster in Commentario αι̉νιγ́δοτω̃ς effusionem pruna- rum ignearum incendium urbis significare velint, nonnulli tamē eam in bonam partem interpretantur; Osiander, & Paraphrasta Vinarienses, & alii. Nimi- rum ostendi denuo Ezechieli vult Osiander noster currum Evangelii, in quo mundi servator aliquando vehendus erat per universum terrarum orbem, fi- mulque doceri; post prædicationem Evangelii se- quuturam esse ruinam politiæ Judaicæ, & quum de vastatione priore urbis Jerusalem verba facta fue- rint, jam agi de secundo excidio. Sumendas ergo prunas de igne, qui inter rotas currus Evangelici est, & projiciendas illas in urbem. Quod Evangeli- um magna, & plane ignea virtute penetrandi & il- luminandi per Apostolos prædicandum sit in Jeru- salem, quemadmodum etiam in Jerusalem missest Spiritus Sanctus in specie linguarum ignearumAct. 2. Nubes ergo seu nebula significabat juxta ipsum Iu- dæos excæcatum iri prædicato Evangelio, idque præci- pue futurum in Pontificibus, Sacerdotibus, scribis & Pharisæis. Quod vero atrium splendore Domini repletum, fore tamen aliquos inter Judæos Electos, qui eodem Evangelio ad salutem suam illuminan- di sint. Et quum sonitus alarum Cherubim additus sit usque ad atrium exterius, sonum Evangelii per Apostolos prædicandi exauditum etiam iri inter gentes per exterius atrium designatas. Ad N. Test. tempora spectare hæc, ipse Grotius ad v. 21. innuısse videtur; sæpe, inquit, id repetit, ut populus fine tem- plo vičturus, eœmpli mysteria pro templo haberet, & sic ad fœdus multo melius pararetur. Sine templius vivendum imprimis sub N. T. ubi nullus amplo templo Levitico & umbratili usus. Nou autem sit in hac visione gloriæ Domini mentio filii hominis uti c. 1, 26, supra. Quia Christus exhibebatur in officio sa- cerdotali, sub habitu viri lineis vestibus induti, non vero, ut illic, in throno majestatico. Neque dignitati Filii Dei decedit quicquam, quod v. 7. illi à Cherub ignis datus in urbem projiciendus. Quia, etsi Apostoli & Dočtores Evangelici Evangelium spargant per Ecclesiam, tamen per manus Christi mediatoris & Pontificis unici id spargendum est, & ab illo omnem vim & virtutum suam habet. Hoc fine data etiam illi sunt Apoc. 8, 3. incensa multa, ut scilicet illis vim & efficaciam conciliaret. Quanquam & id monen- dum sit, in talibus visionibus mysticis & significati- vis, æque ut in parabolis, difficile esse omnes cir- cumstantias applicare, nec omnia ad vivum refe- canda esse, aut certe non omnium rationem sem- per à nobis reddi posse. Multa manent mystica. Satis est, si scopum visionum intelligamus, etiamsi τὰ περιςατικὰ omnia expedire nequeamus.

INGRESSVSQVE EST IN CONSPECTVMEO) Prope rotas constitit.

## 10:3
Ver. 3. BUT THE CHERUBIM WERE STANDING ON THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE HOUSE) On the Southern side, as the Chaldean has it. As far as possible from those places where those cells were, and the weeping for Thammuz: these things up to that of the Almighty speaking are said by way of parenthesis.

AND THE CLOUD FILLED THE INNER COURT) The priestly court: where that image of God referring to judgments was going or standing. The splendor preceded, the cloud followed. The splendor signifies clarity in judging: the cloud signifies huge storms of adversities.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CHERVBIM AVTEM STABANT A DEX- TRIS DOMVS) Ad partem Australem, ut habet Chal- dæus. Quam longissime ab illis locis, ubi erant illæ cellulæ, & plančtus de Thamuso: hæc usque ad illa Omnipotentis lo- quentis, dicuntur per παρένθεσιν.

ET NVBES IMPLEVIT ATRIVM INTERIVS) Atrium sacerdotale: quo ibat, aut stabat imago illa Dei judicia referens. Antecedebat splendor, sequebatur nubes. Splendor claritatem in judicando significat: nubes ingen- tes procellas adversorum.

## 10:4
Ver. 4. AND THE GLORY OF THE LORD WAS LIFTED UP ABOVE THE CHERUB) It descended from the vehicle, under which were the Cherubim, gradually deserting the Temple.

AT THE THRESHOLD OF THE HOUSE) At that gate which looked from the priestly basilica to the open-air court of the people.

AND THE HOUSE WAS FILLED WITH THE CLOUD) That very priestly basilica, which was as it were behind that image.

AND THE COURT WAS FILLED WITH THE SPLENDOR OF THE GLORY OF THE LORD) The court or open-air space of the people, which was before the image.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET ELEVATA EST GLORIA DOMINI SVPER CHERVB) De vehiculo descendit, sub quo erant Cherubini, paulatim Templum deserens.

AD LIMEN DOMVS) Ad illam portam quæ à ba- silica sacerdotali spectabat ad subdiale populi.

ET REPLETA EST DOMVS NVBE) Ipsa illa ba- silica sacerdotalis, quæ velut à tergo erat imagini isti.

ET ATRIVM REPLETVM EST SPLENDORE GLORIÆ DOMINI) Atrium sive subdiale populi, quod erat ante imaginem.

## 10:5
Ver. 5. AND THE SOUND OF THE WINGS OF THE CHERUBIM WAS HEARD EVEN TO THE OUTER COURT) It resounded through all that open-air space of the people.

AS THE VOICE OF GOD ALMIGHTY SPEAKING) That is, as thunder, as Symmachus and Theodotion explained. See above 1, 24. They signify, as we said there, the horrible commands of God.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET SONITVS ALARVM CHERVBIM AV- DIEBATVR VSQVE AD ATRIVM EXTERIVS) Per- sonabat per omne illud populi subdiale.

QVASI VOX DEI OMNIPOTENTIS LOQVEN- TIS) Id est, quasi tonitru, ut explicarunt Symmachus & Theodotion. Vide supra 1, 24. Significantur, ut ibi diximus, horribilia Dei mandata.

## 10:6
Ver. 6. AND WHEN HE HAD COMMANDED THE MAN) He repeats the discourse he had begun.

TAKE FIRE) The Cherub reaching it out, as will be said now, thus lesser angels are instructed by greater ones.

IT STOOD BESIDE THE WHEEL) Beside the interval of the wheels.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CVMQVE PRÆCEPISSET VIRO) Repetit cœptum sermonem.

SVME IGNEM) Porrigente Cherubino, ut jam di- cetur, Sic Angeli minores à majoribus instruuntur.

STETIT JVXTA ROTAM) Juxta intervallum ro- tarum.

## 10:7
Ver. 7. AND THE CHERUB STRETCHED FORTH HIS HAND FROM THE MIDST OF THE CHERUBIM) That is, one of the Cherubim stretched out a wing articulated in the manner of a hand.

AND THE FIRE THAT WAS BETWEEN THE CHERUBIM) Which surrounded the whole vehicle.

AND HE TOOK AND GAVE INTO THE HANDS OF HIM WHO WAS CLOTHED IN LINEN: WHO TAKING IT WENT OUT) To set the city on fire.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET EXTENDIT CHERVB MANVM DE MEDIO CHERVBIM) Id est, alter ex Cherubinis alam ad manus modum articulatam extendit.

ET IGNEM QVI ERAT INTER CHERUBIM) Qui vehiculum omne ambiebat.

ET SVMSIT ET DEDIT IN MANVS EJVS QVI INDVTVS ERAT LINEIS : QVI ACCIPIENS EGRESSVS EST) Ad urbem incendendam.

## 10:8
V. 8. AND THERE APPEARED IN THE CHERUBIM THE LIKENESS OF A MAN'S HAND UNDER THEIR WINGS) The wings had joints, like a human hand, see 1, 8.

Latin:

V. 8. ET APPARVIT IN CHERVBIM SIMILITV- DO MANVS HOMINIS SVBTVS PENNAS EORVM) Pennæ articulos habebant, ut manus humana, vide 1,8.

## 10:9
Ver. 9. AND I SAW, AND BEHOLD FOUR WHEELS BESIDE THE CHERUBIM) By which the vehicle was moved, in which the Cherubim were. See 1, 15. 16.

ONE WHEEL BESIDE ONE CHERUB: AND ANOTHER WHEEL BESIDE ONE CHERUB) It is an enallage: for he wishes to speak of two wheels, which were on two sides, that each was so close to the Cherub of its side that it was touched by him.

AND THE APPEARANCE OF THE WHEELS WAS AS THE VISION OF A CHRYSOLITE STONE) As the color of the Ocean, 1, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET VIDI, ET ECCE QVATVOR ROTÆ JVXTA CHERVBIM) Quibus vehiculum movebatur, in quo erant Cherubini. Vide 1, 15. 16.

ROTA VNA JVXTA CHERVB VNVM: ET ROTA ALIA JVXTA CHERVB VNVM) Enallage est: vult enim dicere de binis rotis, quæ in binis erant lateribus, utramque tam propinquam fuisse Cherubino ejus lateris, ut ab eo tangeretur.

SPECIES AVTEM ROTARVM QVASI VISIO LA- PIDIS CHRTSOLITHI) Tanquam color Oceani, 1, 16.

## 10:10
Ver. 10. AND AS FOR THEIR APPEARANCE, THERE WAS ONE LIKENESS TO ALL FOUR) The wheels were equal and similar.

AS IT WERE A WHEEL IN THE MIDST OF A WHEEL) We have said 1, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET ASPECTUS EORUM SIMILITUDO UNA QVATUOR) Pares erant ac similes rotæ.

QVASI SIT ROTA IN MEDIO ROTÆ) Dixi- mus 1, 16.

## 10:11
Ver. 11. AND WHEN THEY WENT, THEY WENT IN THE FOUR DIRECTIONS) Wherever the Cherubim wished. See the sense 1, 17.

AND THEY DID NOT TURN BACK AS THEY WALKED) Unless the course was completed, as in 1, 17.

BUT TO THE PLACE TO WHICH IT WAS GOING IT TURNED, WHICH WAS THE FIRST, AND THE OTHERS FOLLOWED, AND THEY DID NOT TURN) Here also 'the first' is said for the two former. 'The others', that is, the two latter. Moreover, there were former and latter, in turns, as the Cherubim had willed.

Latin:

Vers. 11. CUMQVE AMBULARENT, IN QVA- TUOR PARTES GRADIEBANTVR) Quocunque vel- lent Cherubini. Sensum vide 1, 17.

ET NON REVERTEBANTUR AMBULANTES) Nisi peracto cursu, ut 1, 17.

SED AD LOCUM AD QVEM IRE DECLINA- BAT QVÆ PRIMA ERAT, SEQVEBANTUR ET CÆTERÆ, NEC CONVERTEBANTUR) Hic quoque prima dičtum pro duæ priores. Cæteræ, id est, posteriores duæ. Erant autem priores & posteriores, vicibus, ut voluerant Cherubini.

## 10:12
Vers. 12. AND THEIR WHOLE BODY) Theirs: namely, of the Cherubim, as the Chaldean here [notes],

AND THEIR NECKS, AND THEIR HANDS, AND THEIR WINGS, AND THE WHEELS, WERE FULL OF EYES) That is, of colors. This was added to that vision which we had in the first chapter, or it is now observed more exactly by the Prophet.

ROUND ABOUT THE FOUR WHEELS) Better: Round about, and the four wheels: so that that 'round about' may be referred to the preceding, and it may be added in like manner that the wheels also were variegated, that is, the rims of the wheels, which had also been said in the first chapter, v. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET OMNE CORPUS EARUM) Eorum: Chrubinorum scilicet, ut hic Chaldæus,

ET COLLA, ET MANUS, ET PENNÆ, ET CIRCULI, PLENA ERANT OCULIS) Id est, coloribus. Hoc accessit viso illo, quod in primo capite habuimus, aut nunc exačtius à Propheta observatum est.

IN CIRCUITU QVATVOR ROTARUM) Me- lius: Circumquaque, & quatuor rotæ: ut illud circumquaque ad præcedentia referatur, addaturque pari modo versicolo- res fuisse & rotas, id est, rotarum absides, quod & capite pri- mo, dičtum fuerat v. 18.

## 10:13
V. 13. AND HE CALLED THOSE WHEELS VOLUBILES [WHIRLING] IN MY HEARING) Better: And in my hearing he called out (namely, one of the Cherubim) to those wheels, that is, to each of the wheels: it is resolved, so that there is a deficiency of ה at the end, which is frequent in such words.

Latin:

V. 13. ET ROTAS ISTAS VOCAVIT VOLUBILES AUDIENTE ME) Melius: Et audiente me in clamavit (nem- pe ex Cherubinis alter) rotis illis, id est, cuique rotarum: fol- vitor, ut sit defectus ה in fine, qui verbis talibus frequens.

## 10:14
Vers. 14. AND EVERY ONE HAD FOUR FACES) That is, each of the two Cherubim consisted of four forms.

THE FIRST FACE WAS THE FACE OF A CHERUB) That is, of an ox or a calf. From this part that whole [creature] received its name: and not undeservedly: for the others were as it were additions to this. The Hebrews always valued the ox highly: for that reason Joseph, who deserved very well of them, was called by that surname; and was shadowed forth by that species, as we have said elsewhere.

THE SECOND FACE WAS THE FACE OF A MAN) A human form in the countenance.

AND IN THE THIRD) That is, the third.

THE FACE OF A LION) The form of a lion in the manes.

AND IN THE FOURTH) That is, the fourth.

FACE OF AN EAGLE) The form of an eagle on the wings.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QVATUOR AUTEM FACIES HABEBAT UNUM) Id est, de duobus Cherubinis quisque ex formis constabat quattuor.

UNA FACIES CHERUB) Id est, bovis sive vituli. Ex hac parte totum illud nomen suum accepit: nec immerito: nam cætera hujus velut additamenta erant. Bovem magni semper fecere Hebræi: ideo quod Josephus de ipsis optime meritus, eo cognomine sit appellatus; eaque specie adum- bratus, ut diximus alibi.

FACIES SECUNDA FACIES HOMINI) Forma humana in vultu.

ET IN TERTIO) Id est, tertio.

FACIES LEONIS) Forma leonis in jubis.

ET IN QVARTO) Id est, quarto.

FACIES AQVILÆ) Forma aquilæ in alis.

## 10:15
Verse 15. AND THE CHERUBIM WERE LIFTED UP) That is, the deportation was still inhibited for a short time.

IT IS THE ANIMAL) Now he calls it an animal, now animals: because each animal was composed of the forms of four animals. And again it is an enallage: for he names one, when there were two.

WHICH I HAD SEEN BY THE RIVER CHEBAR) On the bank. Concerning which, chapter 1.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET ELEVATA SUNT CHERUBIM) Id est, deportatio adhuc inhibita ad modicum tempus.

IPSUM EST ANIMAL) Modo animal vocat, modo animalia: quia ex quatuor animalium formis animal quod- que erat compositum. Et rursus est enallage: nam unum no- minat, cum duo essent.

QVOD VIDERAM JUXTA FLUVIUM CHO- BAR) In ripa. De quo capite 1.

## 10:16
Verse 16. AND WHEN THE CHERUBIM WALKED) When they moved, as we said at the first chapter.

AND WHEN THE CHERUBIM LIFTED UP THEIR WINGS, TO BE EXALTED FROM THE EARTH, THE WHEELS DID NOT REMAIN.) Namely, they did not stick to the earth.

BUT THEY ALSO WERE BESIDE) That is, they were lifted up likewise, as the following explains.

Latin:

Vers. 16. CUMQVE AMBULARENT CHERUBIM) Cum moverent, ut diximus ad primum caput.

ET CUM ELEVARENT CHERUBIM ALAS SUAS, UT EXALTARENTUR DE TERRA, NON RESIDE- BANT ROTÆ.) Nempe non hærebant terræ.

SED ET IPSÆ JUXTA ERANT) Id est, parites attollebantur, ut sequentia explicant.

## 10:17
Verse 17. FOR THE SPIRIT OF LIFE WAS IN THEM) The spirit of the living creature (that is, of the Cherub) reached to them, supply 'pertained'. See what is in chapter one, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SPIRITUS ENIM VITÆ ERAT IN EIS) Spiritus animantis (id est, Cherubini) ad eas, supple pertin- gebat. Vide quæ capite primo 20.

## 10:18
Verse 18. AND THE GLORY OF THE LORD WENT OUT FROM THE THRESHOLD OF THE TEMPLE) Where it had stood somewhat above, verse 4.

AND STOOD ABOVE THE CHERUBIM) Above that drum of the vehicle, so that it might decree concerning the deportation.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET EGRESSA EST GLORIA DOMINI A LIMINE TEMPLI) Ubi constiterat nonnihil supra v. 4.

ET STETIT SUPRA CHERUBIM) Super tym- panum illud vehiculi, ut de deportatione decerneret.

## 10:19
Verse 19. AND THE CHERUBIM LIFTING UP THEIR WINGS, WERE EXALTED FROM THE EARTH BEFORE ME, AND AS THEY WENT OUT THE WHEELS ALSO FOLLOWED) That is, as they themselves rose, the wheels also rose. To rise here is to inhibit the deportation. For many things were done, and at many intervals.

AND IT STOOD AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE EASTERN GATE OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) That vehicle, namely, upon which the image of the judgments of God was sitting, as those things which follow signify; it stood at the progress from the innermost parts of the Temple where the exit was, so that the Temple might be understood to be plainly deserted by divine protection.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET ELEVANTIA CHERUBIM ALAS SU- AS, EXALTATA SUNT A TERRA CORAM ME, ET ILLIS EGREDIENTIBUS ROTÆ QVOQVE SUB- SECUTÆ SUNT) Id est, ipsis surgentibus surgebant & rotæ. Surgere hoc est deportationem inhibere, Fačta enim sunt multæ, & multis intervallis.

ET STETIT IN INTROITU PORTÆ DOMUS DOMINI ORIENTALIS) vehiculum illud scilicet, cui ima- go judiciorum Dei insidebat, ut quæ sequuntur significant, progressum ab intimis Templi stetit ubi erat exitus, ut Tem- plum plane desertum à divina tutela intelligeretur.

## 10:20
Vers. 20. IT IS THE SAME ANIMAL WHICH I SAW UNDER THE GOD OF ISRAEL BY THE RIVER CHOBAR) Again an enallage, as above 15. For it is called an animal, although there were two, but indistinct. Wherefore the Chaldean here used the plural.

AND I KNEW THAT THEY WERE CHERUBIM) The Prophet often saw the same thing, so that he might consider more closely, and understand that these forms were the same as those which were above the ark: which he could have understood at some time from the High Priest.

Latin:

Vers. 20. IPSVM EST ANIMAL QVOD VIDI SVB- TER DEVM ISRAEL JVXTA FLVVIUM CHOBAR) Iterum enallage, ut supra 15. nam animal dicitur, cum duo essent, sed indiscreta. Quare plurali hic posuit Chaldæus.

ET COGNOVI CHERVBIM EA ESSE) Sæpe idem vidit Propheta, ut consideraret propius, & intelligeret has formas easdem esse quæ supra arcam erant: positæ quod ex summo Pontifice intellexisse aliquando potuerat.

## 10:21
Vers. 21. FOUR FACES TO ONE) Four forms in each. He often repeats this, so that the people without a temple might live, might hold the mysteries of the Temple as the Temple itself, and thus be much better prepared for the covenant.

AND FOUR WINGS TO ONE) That is, to each one there were. Two wings were flying, two were covering the lower parts.

AND THE LIKENESS OF THE HAND OF A MAN UNDER THEIR WINGS) The feathers were articulated in the place of hands, as we said above.

Latin:

Vers. 21. QVATVOR VVLTVs VNI) Quatuor for- mæ in singulis. Sæpe id repetit, ut populus sine templo vi- cturus, Templi mysteria pro Templo haberet, & sic ad fedus multo melius pararetur.

ET QVATUOR ALÆ UNI) Id est, singulis erant. Duæ alæ volabant, duæ tegebant inferiora.

ET SIMILITUDO MANUS HOMINIS SUB ALIS EORUM) Pennæ articulatæ manuum in vicem, ut supra diximus.

## 10:22
Ver. 22. AND THE LIKENESS OF THEIR FACES, THE VERY FACES WHICH I HAD SEEN BY THE RIVER CHOBAR) The appearance of those four parts was clearly the same as he had seen on the bank of the Chaboras.

AND THEIR APPEARANCE) The same color of the parts: for that is מַרְאֶה.

AND THE IMPETUS OF EACH ONE TO GO BEFORE THEIR FACE) In the Hebrew; And each of them moved where they were looking. For יֵלֵכוּ, as we have said elsewhere, is Pahal, or Pihel for Hiphil, by a not infrequent mutation.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET SIMILITUDO VULTUUM EORUM, IPSI VULTUS QVOS VIDERAM JUXTA FLUVI- UM CHOBAR) Species illarum quatuor partium plane eadem quam viderat in Chaboræ ripa.

ET INTUITUS EORUM) Color idem partium: id enim מַרְאֶה.

ET IMPETUS SINGULORUM ANTE FACIEM SUAM INGREDI) In Hebræo; Et ipsorum singuli quo spe- ctabant eo movebant. Nam יֵלֵכוּ ut alibi diximus, est Pahal, aut Pihel pro Hiphil, minime frequenti mutatione.

## 11:1 Argument
REVELATION III. CHAPTER XI.

The Prophet prophesies against the counsels of Iezoniah and Pheltiah: Pheltiah dies suddenly: yet to the rest of Israel a return and conversion is promised.

Ver. 1. AND THE SPIRIT LIFTED ME UP) More correctly: The Spirit had lifted me up, that is, had held me suspended. For he repeats that which we said about those things in ch. 25, above 8, 6, for he had interrupted that discourse to turn to greater matters.

AND HE BROUGHT ME TO THE EASTERN GATE OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) He had made me see those parts, as if I were present. He understands that gate of the priestly basilica looking into the open court of the people. ch. 8, 16.

AND BEHOLD AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE GATE) Where one goes into the gate, between the gate and the altar of burnt offerings. above 8, 16.

AND I SAW IN THE MIDST OF THEM) Among them. A Hebrew idiom.

JEZONIAH THE SON OF ASSUR) Not that son of Shaphan, who had sinned.

AND PHELIAS THE SON OF BENAIAH) Another of the princes, as follows.

Latin:

REVELATIO III. CAPUT XI.

Adversus Iezoniæ & Pheltiæ consilia vatici- natur Propheta: Pheltia moritur subito: reliquis tamen Israelis promittitur redu- ctio & conversio.

Vers. 1. ET ELEVAVIT ME SPIRITUS) Rectius: Elevarat me Spiritus, id est, suspensum me tenuerat. Repe- tit enim id quod diximus de illis c. 25. supra 8, 6. nam il- lum sermonem ad convertendas res majores interruperat.

ET INTRODUXIT ME AD PORTAM DOMUS DOMINI ORIENTALEM) Videre me fecerat illas par- tes, quasi præsentem. Portam intelligit illam basilicæ sa- cerdotalis spectantem in subdiale populi. c. 8, 16.

ET ECCE IN INTROITU PORTÆ) Qua in portam itur, inter portam & altare holocaustorum. supra 8, 16.

ET VIDI IN MEDIO EORUM) Inter eos. Lo- cutio Hebræa.

JEZONIAM FILIUM ASSUR) Non illum filium Saphan, qui peccaverat.

ET PHELIAM FILIVM BENAIÆ) Alterum ex principibus, ut sequitur.

## 11:2
Ver. 2. AND HE SAID TO ME) That image standing at the same gate had said to me 10, 4.

SON OF MAN, THESE ARE THE MEN WHO DEVISE INIQUITY, AND GIVE WICKED COUNSEL IN THIS CITY) Namely, by adapting themselves to Chaldean superstitions, in order to merit the favor of that nation in that way. The covenant which Zedekiah had wickedly broken, they wished to mend wickedly.

Latin:

Vers. 2. DIXITQVE AD ME) Dixerat ad me illa imago stans ad eandem portam 10, 4.

FILI HOMINIS, HI SVNT VIRI QVI COGI- TANT INIQVITATEM, ET TRACTANT CONSI- LIVM PESSIMVM IN VRBE ISTA) Nempe aptandi se ad superstitiones Chaldaicas, ad eo modo demerendam ejus gentis gratiam. Fœdus quod Sedecias male ruperat, illi male sarcire volebant.

## 11:3
Ver. 3. SAYING, ARE NOT THE HOUSES RECENTLY BUILT) Is the city newly made?

THIS IS THE CALDRON, AND WE ARE THE FLESH) Recently made caldrons are more suitable for cooking meat. Thus they mocked Jeremiah, who had compared the city to a caldron and the men to flesh 1, 15. See also what is below 24, where against this saying Ezekiel says that the rust of the pot will not prevent the pot from cooking some flesh and casting out other.

The meaning is, says B. Hulsemannus, This city is a pot, our receptacle and protection, and we are the flesh enclosed: just as meat is preserved in its pot until perfect cooking, so we shall remain here until extreme old age. Osiander explains it thus: This holy city is as it were a caldron, in which holy flesh (the remains of sacrifices) is cooked to the praise of God; and we are the holy flesh, the people consecrated and devoted to the God of Israel. Therefore the Lord will preserve both the flesh and the caldron, that is, the people and the city.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DICENTES, NONNE DVDVM ÆDIFICA- TÆ SVNT ÆDES) In noviter facta est urbs?

HÆC EST LEBES, NOS AVTEM CARNES) Recenter facti lebetes aptiores sunt ad coquendas carnes. Sic irridebant Jeremiam, qui urbem lebeti, homines carni- bus comparaverat 1, 15. Vide & quæ infra 24. ubi contra hoc dictum dicit Ezechiel, rubiginem ollæ nihil obsi- turam quo minus olla alias carnis coquat, alias ejiciat.

Sensius est, inquit B. Hulsemannus, Hæc civitas est olla, receptaculum & præsidium nostrum, nos autem inclusæ carnes: quemadmodum carnes con- servantur in olla sua, usque ad perfectam deco- ctionem, ita nos hic manebimus ad ultimam usque senectutem. Osiander ita exponit: Hæc sancta urbs est quasi lebes, in quo sanctæ carnes (sacrificiorum reliquiæ) coquuntur ad laudem Dei; nos autem sumus carnes sanctæ, populus Deo Israelis conse- cratus & addictus. Itaque Dominus simul & car- nes & lebetem, hoc est, populum & urbem con- servabit.

## 11:4
Ver. 4. THEREFORE PROPHESY AGAINST THEM, PROPHESY O SON OF MAN) Say what things are going to happen to them, far different from what they think.

Latin:

Vers. 4. IDCIRCO VATICINARE DE EIS, VATI- CINARE FILI HOMINIS) Dic quæ illis sunt eventura longe alia quam putant.

## 11:5
Ver. 5. YOUR SLAIN WHOM YOU HAVE LAID IN THE MIDST OF IT, THESE ARE THE FLESH, THIS IS THE CALDRON) For them this city served as a caldron; for you it shall not.

Latin:

Vers. 5. INTERFECTI VESTRI QVOS POSVISTIS IN MEDIO EJVS, HI SVNT CARNES, HÆC EST LEBES) Illis hæc urbs fuit pro lebete, vobis non erit.

## 11:8
Ver. 8. YOU HAVE FEARED THE SWORD) The Chaldean, that is to say, so much so that for its sake you wished to abandon sacred things.

AND I WILL BRING A SWORD UPON YOU) That very same one which you feared.

Latin:

Vers. 8. GLADIVM METVISTIS) Chaldaicum scili- cet, ita ut ejus causa sacra deserere velletis.

ET GLADIVM INDVCAM SVPER VOS) Eun- dem illum quem metuistis.

## 11:9
Ver. 9. AND I WILL CAST YOU OUT OF THE MIDST OF IT) You shall go outside the city.

AND I WILL GIVE YOU INTO THE HAND OF ENEMIES) You will go not as free men, but as captives.

AND I WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS AMONG YOU) By means of the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET EJICIAM VOS DE MEDIO EJVS) Extra urbem ibitis.

DABOQVE VOS IN MANV HOSTIVM) Non liberi, sed captivi ibitis.

ET FACIAM IN VOBIS JUDICIA) Per Chaldæos.

## 11:10
Ver. 10. IN THE BORDERS OF ISRAEL I WILL JUDGE YOU) In Riblah 2 Kings 25:20, Jeremiah 52:9.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN FINIBUS ISRAEL JUDICABO VOS) In Reblatha 2. Reg. 25, 20. Jerem. 52, 9.

## 11:13
Ver. 13. PELATIAH THE SON OF BENAIAH DIED) As a pledge of that which is to happen to those other 25.

WILL YOU MAKE A FULL END OF THE REMNANT OF ISRAEL) Do you intend to destroy everyone just like that Pelatiah?

Latin:

Vers. 13. PHELIAS FILIUS BENAIÆ MORTUUS EST) In arrham ejus, quod aliis illis 25. eventurum est.

CONSUMMATIONEM TU FACIES RELIQVIA- RUM ISRAEL) Itane omnes vis perdere ut istum Pheltiam.

## 11:15
Ver. 15. THY BRETHREN THY KINSMEN) גאֻלָּתֶךָ : The LXX read גָּלוּתֶךָ , that is, your deportations: that is, those deported with you: the verb 'are' is missing.

TO WHOM THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM HAVE SAID), those who were left in the city, when Jeconiah and others with him were deported.

GET YOU FAR FROM THE LORD) Better: They have gone far from the Lord. Those who are being deported have sinned much more grievously than we.

UNTO US IS THE LAND GIVEN IN POSSESSION) For we shall possess this land so much more spaciously now that they have gone.

Latin:

Vers. 15. FRATRES TUI VIRI PROPINQVI) גאֻלָּתֶךָ : LXX. legerunt גָּלוּתֶךָ , id est, deportationes tuæ: id est, tecum deportati: deficit verbum sunt.

QVIBVS DIXERUNT HABITATORES JERU- SALEM), illi qui relinquebantur in urbe, deportato Je- chonia, & aliis cum eo.

LONGE RECEDITE A DOMINO) Melius: Lon- ge recesserunt a Domino. Illi qui deportantur multo gravius quam nos peccarunt.

NOBIS DATA EST TERRA IN POSSESSIO- NEM) Nam nos possidebimus hanc terram tanto laxius ex quo illi abiere.

## 11:16
Ver. 16. BECAUSE I HAVE CAST THEM FAR OFF AMONG THE HEATHEN, AND BECAUSE I HAVE SCATTERED THEM AMONG THE COUNTRIES) Those deported with Jeconiah, among whom is Ezekiel.

I WILL BE TO THEM AS A LITTLE SANCTUARY IN THE COUNTRIES WHERE THEY SHALL COME) And I was to them a sanctuary for a little time, in the countries where they came. That is: and because at this time, since they were deported, they have no Temple: I am to them instead of a temple: they worship me within the inner chamber of the soul, as Christians are one day to do.

Latin:

Vers. 16. QVIA LONGE FECI ILLOS IN GENTI- BUS, ET QVIA DISPERSI EOS IN TERRIS) Illos cum Jechonia deportatos, in quibus Ezechiel.

ERO EIS IN SANCTIFICATIONEM MODI- CAM IN TERRIS AD QVAS VENERUNT) Et fui eis in sanctuarium ad tempus modicum, in terris ad quas venerunt. Id est: & quia hoc tempore ex quo deportati sunt, Tem- plum non habent: ego illis sum pro templo: intra animi penetrale me colunt, ut olim facturi sunt Christiani.

## 11:17
Ver. 17. THEREFORE SAY, THUS SAITH THE LORD: I WILL EVEN GATHER YOU FROM THE PEOPLE) That 'therefore' coheres with 'I will gather'. For because you, having been deported, have not forgotten me, therefore I will bring you back. There is a transition from the third person to the second, and again from the second to the third, in the Hebrew manner.

Latin:

Vers. 17. PROPTEREA LOQVERE HÆC, DICIT DOMINUS: CONGREGABO VOS DE POPULIS) Illud propterea cohæret cum congregabo. Nam quia vos de- portati mei obliti non estis, ideo vos reducam. Transitur de persona tertia in secundam, & rursum de secunda in tertiam, more Hebræo.

## 11:18
Vers. 18. AND THEY SHALL TAKE AWAY ALL THE OFFENSES, AND ALL THE ABOMINATIONS THEREOF FROM IT) They shall live without idolatry, with eminent men leading the way, Ezra, Nehemiah, Zerubbabel, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, Mordecai, and other men of τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς μεγάλης.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET AUFERENT OMNES OFFENSIONES, ET CUNCTAS ABOMINATIONES EJUS DE ILLA) Vivent sine idololatria, præeuntibus viris egregiis, Esdra, Nehemia, Zorobabele, Aggæo, Zacharia, Malachia, Mardochæo, & aliis viris τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς μεγάλης.

## 11:19
Vers. 19. AND I WILL GIVE THEM ONE HEART) I will bring it about by the greatest benefits, that they may worship me with a concordant mind. Compare Jer. 31, 37. below 36, 26.

These things are not to be restricted to the times of Ezra and the latest Prophets, much less to corporal benefits, namely the restoration into Judea: but they extend more broadly, to the Ecclesiastical congregation, the abdication of any abominations whatsoever, mystical communion, concord and spiritual unity of faith, regeneration and renewal, and sanctification, the gracious indwelling of God, and of any divine benefits whatsoever, not only through those times of the O.T., but especially also in the time of Christ and the Apostles: as is manifest both from the emphasis of the words of this promise, and from similar Evangelical promises in Ezek. 36, Jer. 31, etc., that these pertain especially to the times of the N.T. One heart in respect to God is simple and pure, and is opposed to a double, divided, and not at all sincere heart, Syr. 2, 14. Hos. 10, 2. Zeph. 3, 9. in respect to others it denotes a concordant heart, Acts 4, 32. Jerome and Theodoret agree with our interpretation, as do Augustine in his book on grace and free will, ch. 25, and most others, even Papist interpreters, whom Grotius favors greatly.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET DABO EIS COR UNUM) Efficiam maximis beneficiis, ut concordi animo me colant. Confer Jerem. 31, 37. infra 36, 26.

Non restringenda hæc ad tempora Esdræ, & Prophetarum ultimorum, nedum ad beneficia cor- poralia, reductionem nempe in Judæam: sed la- tius se porrigunt, congregationem Ecclesiasticam, abdicationem quarumvis abominationem, commu- nionem mysticam, concordiam & unitatem fidei spi- ritualem, regenerationem & renovationem, ac san- ctificationem, inhabitationem Dei gratiosam, & bene- ficiorum quorumvis divinorum non solum non modo per illa V. Test. tempora, sed imprimis etiam tempore Christi & Apostolorum: ut cum ex emphasi verbo- rum promissionis hujusce, tum e similibus promis- sionibus Evangelicis Ezech. 36. Jer. 31. &c. manife- stum est, hæc maxime ad tempora N. T. pertinere. Cor unum respectu ad Deum est simplex & purum, ac opponitur cordi duplici, diviso, minimeque sincero, Syr. 2, 14. Hos. 10, 2. Zeph. 3, 9. in respectu ad alios cor concors notat, Act. 4, 32. Consonant no- stræ interpretationi Hieron. & Theodor. ut & Augu- stin. l. de grat. & liber. arbitr. c. 25. & plerique alii, etiam Pontificii Interpp. quibus impense favet Grotius

## 11:21
Vers. 21. WHOSE HEART AFTER THE OFFENSES) In the Hebrew: to the contaminations, that is, idolatry.

THEIR WAY I WILL RECOMPENSE UPON THEIR OWN HEAD) They deserted me, and I will desert them: they profaned the Temple, and I will profane it through the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 21. QVORUM COR POST OFFENDICULA) In Hebræo: ad contaminationes, id est, idololatriam.

HORUM VIAM IN CAPITE SUO PONAM) Deseruerunt me, & ego eos deseram: Templum profana- runt, & ego profanabo per Chaldæos.

## 11:22
Vers. 22. AND THE CHERUBIM LIFTED UP THEIR WINGS, AND THE WHEELS WITH THEM) For the time of deportation was not yet present.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET ELEVARUNT CHERUBIM ALAS SUAS, ET ROTÆ CUM EIS) Nondum enim aderat tempus deportationis.

## 11:23
Vers. 23. AND THE GLORY OF THE LORD WENT UP FROM THE MIDST OF THE CITY) Just as that image had gone out from the temple into the city, so now it also deserts the city, and stands ready to exercise judgments from that place from which the greatest force of hostile missiles was about to reach the city.

AND STOOD UPON THE MOUNTAIN WHICH IS TO THE EAST OF THE CITY) The Mount of Olives, as it is named in 2 Sam. 15, 30. That it is the same mountain which was to the east of the city appears in Zech. 14, 4. Thus also Christ ascended into his kingdom from that mountain, about to exercise judgments upon the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ASCENDIT GLORIA DOMINI DE MEDIO CIVITATIS) Sicut de templo in urbem exierat illa imago, sic nunc & urbem deserit, statque parata ad exercenda judicia ex illo loco, unde maxima vis telorum hostilium in urbem erat perventura,

STETITQUE SUPER MONTEM QVI EST AD ORIENTEM URBIS) Montem Oliveti, ut nominatur 2. Sam. 15, 30. Eundem esse montem, qui ad orientem ur- bis erat, apparet Zach. 14, 4. Sic & Christus ex eo monte in regiam suam ascendit, judicia in Judæos exerciturus.

## 11:24
Verse 24. AND THE SPIRIT LIFTED ME UP, AND BROUGHT ME INTO CHALDEA TO THEM OF THE CAPTIVITY, IN A VISION, BY THE SPIRIT OF GOD) Transposition: The Spirit who had lifted me up in a vision, that is, in the spirit of God, restored me into Chaldea to the deported. For because he had seen all things that were being done at Jerusalem as if present, he is said to have been present there in spirit, and soon to have returned to his own countrymen. AND THE VISION THAT I HAD SEEN WENT UP FROM ME) It ceased, it disappeared, as in Gen. 17, 22. Verse 25. AND I SPOKE TO THE CAPTIVITY ALL THE WORDS OF THE LORD, WHICH HE HAD SHEWED ME) All things. To the captivity: that is, to those elders of the deported, of whom above 8, 1.

the carrying of baggage: Where other Papists defend the error of the Vulgate in vain: for Zedekiah was not carried on shoulders, but he himself, as a fugitive, carried his own baggage. Compare Jer. 13, 18. IN THE DARKNESS THOU SHALT BE CARRIED FORTH) Thou shalt carry thyself forth. For Zedekiah went out by night 39, 4. 52, 7. THOU SHALT COVER THY FACE AND SHALT NOT SEE THE GROUND) Cover your eyes, lest you look upon this Babylonian ground, in which you live, just as Zedekiah is not about to see it because of the blindness which is shadowed forth by covered eyes, below 12. I HAVE SET THEE FOR A SIGN UNTO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) By your deeds I wish to show what is about to happen to the Jews, especially however to the king, as follows. Verse 7. CARRIED UPON SHOULDERS) Nay rather, you shall carry, namely provisions, as we have said.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET SPIRITUS LEVAVIT ME, ADDUXITQVE IN CHALDÆAM AD TRANSMIGRATIONEM IN VISIONE IN SPIRITU DEI) Transpositio: Spiritus qui me levaverat in visione, id est, in spiritu Dei, me in Chaldæam restituit apud deportatos. Nam quia omnia quæ Hierosolymis agebantur, ut præsentia viderat, ibi spiritu præsens fuisse dicitur, ac mox rediisse ad suos populares. ET SUBLATA EST A ME VISIO QVAM VIDERAM) Cessavit, disparuit, ut Gen. 17, 22. Vers. 25. ET LOCUTUS SUM AD TRANSGRATIONEM OMNIA VERBA DOMINI, QVÆ OSTENDERAT MIHI) Res omnes. Ad transmigrationem: id est, ad seniores illos deportatorum, de quibus supra 8, 1.

cinarum portatione: Ubi frustra alii Papistæ Vulgatæ errorem tuentur: non enim humeris portatus est Sedekias, sed fugitivus portavit ipse sarcinas suas. Conf. Jer. 13, 18. IN CALIGINE EFFERERIS) Efferes temetipsum. Nam noctu exiit Sedecias 39, 4. 52, 7. FACIEM TVAM VELABIS ET NON VIDEBIS TERRAM) Oculos tuos vela, ne aspicias terram hancBabylonicam, in qua vivis, sicut eam ob cæcitatem, quæ velatis oculis adumbratur, visurus non est res Sedecias infra 12. PORTENTUM DEDI TE DOMUI ISRAEL) Tuis factis ostendere volo quid Judæis sit eventurum, præsertim autem regi, ut sequitur. Vers. 7. IN HUMERIS PORTATUS) Imo portabi, nempe alimenta, ut diximus.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

Ezekiel, having made the vessels of captivity, by migrating at night, portends the captivity of the city and the King, with the rest consumed by the sword, pestilence, and famine: and that it is not to be deferred for long.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Ezechiel factis vasis transmigrationis noctu transmigrans portendit urbis & Regis cap- tivitatem, reliquis gladio, peste & fame consumtis: nec eam in longum differendam.

## 12:2
Verse 2. IN THE MIDST OF A REBELLIOUS HOUSE THOU DWELLEST) A house of contumacy. THEY HAVE EYES TO SEE, AND SEE NOT) Like that: -- I see the better things, and approve them, I follow the worse. That one, destitute of the word of GOD, did not have eyes to see: these, however, could see the light of the word shining clearly to them through the proclamations of the Prophets; but they were closing their eyes to such great light, and allowing themselves to be blinded, Isa. 6, 9. John 12, 40. 2 Cor. 4, 4. AND EARS TO HEAR, AND HEAR NOT) That is, they do not wish to be taught. That is indicated by a received phrase of scripture, to whom divine grace is not lacking to perceive the true nor to do the good, and yet they do not know, nor do they obey. For the eye denotes understanding, the hearing denotes obedience. Deut. 29, 4. Jerem. 5, 21. Prov. 20, 21. Matt. 13, 9. The opinion of Maldonado, and Tremellius, Polanus and Piscator is inept, who take 'eyes to see' and 'ears to hear' as referring to the senses of the body, and 'not to hear, not to see' as referring to a defect of the senses of salvation: since thus the brooms are loosened, and no reason for reproaching is left: For what is this, if one should say: You can see the sun with the eyes of the body, but you do not wish to see the Sun of righteousness with the eyes of the soul? That a spiritual power of seeing and hearing is presupposed, not even the Jesuits themselves, Cornelius, Saa, and others, deny. It is clear therefore from this that sufficient grace is given to some, who can understand things to be learned, and do things to be done, which however they themselves abuse. Compare Isa. 5, 4. 5. Jerem. 7, 13. Ezech. 3, 6. Matt. 11, 23. Ch. 23, 37. B. Hulsemannus has treated this more broadly here against the Calvinists and the Papists Bellarmine and Alvarez. Verse 3. PREPARE THEE STUFF FOR REMOVING) That is, collect your little bundles, as Juvenal speaks. Martial describes such a migration in that Epigram: I saw, Vacerra, I saw your bundles. Vessels are also called 'stuff' in Latin; for from there comes 'to pack up'. AND THOU SHALT REMOVE BY DAY IN THEIR SIGHT) That is, migrate in the clear day while they are watching: express by signs the thing that is about to happen to them. The preparation for departure and the carrying out of the bundles was done for a long time; but the migration by night. IF SO BE THEY WILL SEE) That is, if perhaps they might be moved by this sight. FOR THEY ARE A REBELLIOUS HOUSE) Although it is a rebellious house: namely so that it is incredible that even by this spectacle they will return to a good mind. Verse 4. AND THOU SHALT BRING FORTH THY STUFF) You shall send ahead your bundles, yourself about to follow. Verse 5. DIG THOU THROUGH THE WALL, AND CARRY OUT) Just as King Zedekiah himself was about to go out through a dug-through wall, as is explained below 12. See what has been said on Jerem. 39, 4. Verse 6. IN THEIR SIGHT SHALT THOU BEAR IT UPON THY SHOULDERS) Nay rather, you shall carry; namely, things necessary for sustenance. YOU SHALL BE CARRIED ON SHOULDERS. In the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Syriac, according to Jerome, Pagninus, Arias, and the Complutensian [Polyglot], it is the active [form] 'you shall carry' concerning the load-

Latin:

Vers. 2. IN MEDIO DOMUS EXASPERANTIS TU HABITAS) Domus contumacis. OCULOS HABENT AD VIDENDUM, ET NON VIDENT) Ut illa: -- Video meliora, proboque Deteriora sequor. Illa verbo DEI destituta oculos non habuit ad videndum: hi vero lucem verbi videre poterant ipsis per præconia Prophetarum clare fulgentem; sed oculos ad tantam lucem claudebant, seque excæcari patiebantur, Esa. 6, 9. Job. 12, 40. 2. Cor. 4, 4. ET AURES AD AUDIENDUM, ET NON AUDIUNT) Id est, doceri nolunt. Id indigitatur, phrasi scripturæ recepta, quibus non deest divina gratia ad percipiendum verum neque ad faciendum bonum, nec tamen cognoscunt, nec obsequuntur. Oculus enim intelligentiam, auditus obsequium notat. Deut 29, 4. Jerem. 5, 21. Prov. 20, 21. Matth. 13, 9. Inepta est Maldonati, & Tremellii, Polani ac Piscatoris sententia, qui oculos ad videndum, & aures ad audiendum de sensibus corporis, τό non audire, non videre de defectu sensuum salutis accipiunt: quum sic scopæ dissolutæ sint, nec ratio exprobrandi relinquatur: Quid enim hoc, si quis dicat; Vos potestis solem videre oculis corporis, sed non vultis Solem justitiæ videre oculis animi? Videndi & audiendi spiritualem potentiam præsupponi, nec ipsi Jesuitæ Cornelius, Saa, alii diffitentur. Patet ergo hinc dari aliquibus sufficientem gratiam, qui possint discenda intelligere, & facienda facere, qua tamen ipsi abutantur. Conf. Esa. 5, 4. 5. Jerem. 7, 13. Ezech 3, 6. Matth 11, 23. C. 23, 37. Quod contra Calvinianos & Pontificios Bellarmin. & Alvarez hic latius exequutus est B. Hulsemannus. Vers. 3. FAC TIBI VAS TRANSMIGRATIONIS) Id est, collige sarcinulas, ut Juvenalis loquitur. Describit talem commigrationem Martialis isto Epigrammate: Vidi, Vacerra, sarcinas tuas vidi. Vasa pro sarcinis etiam Latine dicuntur;nam inde convafare. ET TRANSMIGRABIS PER DIEM CORAM EIS) Id est, migra claro die ipsis spectantibus: rem ipsis eventuram signis exprime. Diu fiebat præparatio abitus, & exportatio sarcinarum; transmigratio autem noctu. SI FORTE ASPICIANT) Id est, si forte moveantur isto conspectu. QVIA DOMUS EXASPERANS EST) Quanquam domus est contumax: nempe ut incredibile sit vel hoc spectaculo redituram esse ad bonam mentem. Vers. 4. ET EFFERES FORAS VASA TVA) Præmittes sarcinas tuas ipse secuturus. Vers. 5. PERFODE TIBI PARIETEM, ET INGREDJERIS PER EUM) Sicut Rex ipse Sedecias perfosso muro erat exiturus, ut explicatur infra 12. Vide quæ dicta sunt ad Jerem. 39, 4. Vers. 6. IN CONSPECTU EORUM IN HUMERIS PORTABERIS) Imo portabis: nempe ad victum necessaria. IN HUMERIS PORTABERIS. In Ebr. Chald. Syr. apud Hieron. Pagninum, Ariam, Complutenses activum est portabis de sar-

## 12:10
Verse 10. UPON THE PRINCE THIS BURDEN) משא is he who is a prince among the people, as in the kingdoms of the east. And so above we have מלך and נשיא in the same sense: and therefore the LXX sometimes translate נשיא as βασιλέα. Verse 11. THIS BURDEN) משא, that is, a dire prophecy. I AM YOUR SIGN) Thus Isaiah 8, 18. Verse 12. HIS FACE SHALL BE COVERED) With blindness. So it happened, that he was led into Babylon, which Jeremiah had predicted, and he did not see it, which Ezekiel had said. Which two things Zedekiah had believed to be in conflict with each other: and therefore he had not had faith in the Prophets, as Josephus narrates. Verse 13. AND I WILL SPREAD MY NET UPON HIM, AND HE SHALL BE TAKEN IN MY SNARE) I will block every escape for him. See 2 Kings 25, 5. Jer. 39, 5. 52, 8. Verse 14. AND ALL THAT ARE ABOUT HIM, HIS HELP, AND ALL HIS BANDS) Courtiers, guards, soldiers. I WILL SCATTER INTO EVERY WIND) Which was signified by the four motions of the wheels. We gave another meaning above. AND I WILL DRAW OUT THE SWORD AFTER THEM) I will cause some to fear for themselves from the victor's sword, and to live in trepidation, as above 5, v. 2. 12. Verse 16. AND I WILL LEAVE OF THEM A FEW MEN FROM THE SWORD, AND FROM THE FAMINE, AND FROM THE PESTILENCE) Survivors of so many evils. THAT THEY MAY DECLARE THEIR ABOMINATIONS AMONG THE GENTILES) That they may tell the causes for which the Temple and the city will have been destroyed. Verse 18. EAT THY BREAD WITH QUAKING, AND DRINK THY WATER WITH TREMBLING) Better in trepidation and sorrow. Verse 19. THEY SHALL EAT THEIR BREAD WITH CAREFULNESS) Namely in exile. THAT THE LAND MAY BE DESOLATE FROM ALL THAT IS THEREIN) When the land shall be desolate. Verse 22. THE DAYS ARE PROLONGED, AND EVERY VISION FAILETH) Here 'and' is for 'or': for those men were saying: either those things which are predicted will happen long after us, or they will plainly vanish, διαπίπτουσι, as Symmachus translates. God answers both members. Verse 24. FOR THERE SHALL BE NO MORE ANY VAIN VISION, NOR FLATTERING DIVINATION WITHIN THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL) There shall no longer be a lying prophecy, and a flattering divination. For all those false Prophets shall be cast out 13, 23. Verse 25. IN YOUR DAYS) While you are living. Similar to Matt. 24, 34. Hence interpret the following as well.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SUPER DUCEM ONUS ISTUD) משא est qui princeps est in populo, ut in regnis •e•. Itaque supra eodem sensu habemus מלך & נשיא: deoque LXX. נשיא interdum vertunt βασιλέα. Vers. 11. ONUS ISTUD) משא, id est, dirum vaticinium. EGO PORTENTVM VESTRUM) Sic Esaias 8, 18. Vers. 12. FACIES EJUS OPERIETUR) Cæcitate. Ita factum, ut ductus sit in Babyloniam, quod prædixerat Jeremias, & eam non viderit, quod dixerat Ezechiel. Quæ duo inter se pugnare crediderat Sedecias: Ideoque Prophetis fidem non habuerat, narrante Josepho. Vers. 13. ET EXTENDAM RETE MEUM SUPER EUM, ET CAPIETUR IN SAGENA MEA) Omne effugium ei præcludam. Vid. 2. Reg. 25, 5. Jer. 39, 5. 52, 8. Vers. 14. ET OMNES QVI CIRCA EUM SUNT, PRÆSIDIUM EJUS, ET AGMINA EJUS) Aulicos, satellites, milites. DISPERGAM IN OMNEM VENTUM) Quod significatum per quatuor motus rotarum. Aliam significationem supra dedimus. ET GLADIUM EVAGINABO POST EOS) Faciam ut aliqui metuant sibi à victoris gladio, trepidique vivant, ut supra 5, v. 2. 12. Vers. 16. ET RELINQVAM EX EIS VIROS PAUCOS A GLADIO, ET FAME, ET PESTILENTIA Superstites tot malorum. UT ENARRENT SCELERA EORUM IN GENTIBUS) Ut dicant causas, propter quas excisum erit Templum & civitas. Vers. 18. PANEM TUUM IN CONTURBATIONE COMEDE, SED ET AQVAM TUAM IN MOERORE BIBE) Melius in trepidatione & mærore. Vers. 19. PANEM SUUM IN SOLLICITUDINE COMEDENT) Nempe in exsilio. UT DESOLETUR TERRA A MULTITUDINE SUA) Cum desolata erit terra. Vers. 22. IN LONGUM DIFFERENTUR DIES, ET PERIBIT OMNIS VISIO) Est hic & pro aut: dicebant enim illi homines: aut ea quæ prædicuntur, multo post nos evenient, aut plane evanescent, διαπίπτουσι, ut vertit Symmachus. Utrique membro respondet Deus. Vers. 24. NON ENIM ERIT ULTRA OMNIS VISIO CASSA, NEQVE DIVINATIO AMBIGUA IN MEDIO FILIORUM ISRAEL) Non ultra erit prophetia mendax, & divinatio blandiens. Ejicientur enim omnes illi falsi Prophetæ 13, 23. Vers. 25. IN DIEBUS VESTRIS) Vobis viventibus. Simile Matth. 24, 34. Hinc interpretare & sequentia.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.

The Lord threatens the false prophets who preach peace and seduce the people: as also those of faithful Israel who prophesy from their own heart, and who put cushions under every elbow.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Pseudo Prophetis pacem prædicantibus & populum seducentibus minatur Dominus: ut & fidelibus Israël de corde de suo prophetantibus, & pulvillos cubito supponentibus.

## 13:2
Verse 2. SON OF MAN, PROPHESY AGAINST THE PROPHETS OF ISRAEL) Send this letter to those who falsely call themselves prophets. Verse 3. WHO PROPHESY FROM THEIR OWN HEART) According to the pleasure of their own mind, which he will soon state, 'who follow their own spirit.' AND SEE NOTHING, Since they have seen nothing; that is, they have had no ὀπτασίαν [vision]. Verse 4. AS FOXES IN THE DESERTS WERE THY PROPHETS, O ISRAEL) Better: are. In desert places: that is, where there is nothing to eat, for such beasts are famished: those false prophets are of the same kind. Foxes never stay in one place, but creeping secretly now here, now elsewhere, they cunningly prepare dens for themselves; so also do the false prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 2. FILI HOMINIS VATICINARE AD PROPHETAS ISRAEL) Mitte ille falso se dicentibus Prophetas hanc epistolam. Vers. 3. PROPHETANTIBUS CORDE SUO) Pro lubitu animi sui, quod mox dicet, qui sequuntur Spiritum suum. ET NIHIL VIDENT, Cum nihil viderint; id est, nullam habuerint ὀπτασίαν. Vers. 4. QVASI VULPES IN DESERTIS PROPHETÆ TUI ISRAEL ERANT) Melius: sunt. In locis desertis: id est, ubi nihil est quod edant, Tales enim feræ famelicæ sunt: ejusdemmodi illi falsi Prophetæ. Vulpes nuspiam subsistunt, sed nunc hic nunc alibi occulte repentes, foveas sibi parant callide, ita & Pseudo Prophetæ.

## 13:5
Verse 5.

YOU HAVE NOT GONE UP INTO THE BREACH, NEITHER HAVE YOU BUILT UP THE WALL FOR THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) Meanwhile you have not stood in the broken part of the wall, nor have you set up a fortification for the house of Israel. Where an enemy attacks a city and has demolished a part of the walls with battering rams, two things are usually done: men are set in opposition to defend the gaps, and the interior parts are fortified. Thus, when God is angry, those who wish to be called prophets ought to set up counsels and warnings in opposition. The former expression is taken from Ps. 106:23 and Psalm 30. See below 23:30.

Indeed, by their prayers, pious prophets set themselves like a wall against divine punishments.

THAT YOU MIGHT STAND IN THE BATTLE IN THE DAY OF THE LORD) Better: that that House, that is, the city, may stand in the battle in the day of the Lord: for it stands in the day of the assault which God makes. Against it there is no defense, except in repentance and pious prayers.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NON ASCENDISTIS EX ADVERSO, NE- QVE OPPOSVISTIS MVRVM PRO DOMO ISRAEL) Interea non stetistis in capta parte muri, neque opposuistis mu- nimentum pro domo Israel. Ubi hostis urbem oppugnat, & mœnium partem arietibus disjecit, duo fieri solent: opponi homines, qui hiantia defendant, & muniri interiora. Sic Deo irato, ii qui Prophetæ dici volunt, debent opponere consilia & monita. Locutio prior sumpta ex Pf. 106, 23. & Psalm 30. Vide infra 23, 30.

Imo precibus se Prophetæ pii veluti murum pœnis divinis opponunt.

VT STARETIS IN PRÆLIO IN DIE DOMI- NI) Melius: ut ea Domus, id est, urbs, stet in prælio in die Domini: pro stet in die oppugnationis quam Deus fa it. Adversus eam nulla est defensio, nisi in resipiscentia & piis precibus.

## 13:6
Verse 6. THEY SEE VANITY) They fashion dreams for themselves.

AND DIVINE A LIE) In the Hebrew: and a lying divination.

SAYING, THE LORD SAYS) They add a huge crime to their lie by ascribing it to God as the author.

WHEN THE LORD HAS NOT SENT THEM) To send is to give a command.

AND THEY HAVE PERSEVERED TO CONFIRM THE WORD) And they make (the people) hope that what they say will come to pass. They entice the people with false hope.

Thus the Hebrews, the Chaldean, Pagninus, Pradus, Tremellius: Others, however, with the Vulgate, LXX, Sanctius, Tirinus, as also B. Luther, and Rabbi Solomon, deriving the word from חלל or חול, which is to labor, to act solicitously, explain it as them acting solicitously to confirm their word. Which sense is not bad.

Latin:

Vers. 6. VIDENT VANA) Ipsi sibi somnia fingunt.

ET DIVINANT MENDACIVM) In Hebræo: & divinationem mendacem.

DICENTES, AIT DOMINVS) Mendacio ingens addunt crimen, Deum auctorem inscribendo.

CVM DOMINVS NON MISERIT EOS) Mitte- re est mandatum dare.

ET PERSEVERAVERUNT CONFIRMARE SER- MONEM) Et spem faciunt (populo) ratum fore quod di- xunt. Falsa spe lactant populum.

Sic Ebræi, Chaldæus, Pagninus, Pradus, Tremel- lius: Alii tamen cum Vulg. LXX. Sanctio, Tirino, ut & B. Luthero, & Rab. Salom. a חלל vel חול vocem deducentes, quod est laboravit, solicite egit, exponunt solicite id agere eos, ut confirment ser- monem suum. Qui sensus non malus.

## 13:8
Verse 8. I AM AGAINST YOU) That is, I am coming.

Latin:

Vers. 8. EGO AD VOS) Venio scilicet.

## 13:9
Verse 9. IN THE COUNCIL OF MY PEOPLE THEY SHALL NOT BE) The returning people will not use their counsel, as they did before.

Others explain it concerning the Church, or the congregation of the Saints, Jerome, Theodoret, Lyranus, B. Luther, etc., from Jer. 23:18, Ps. 1:2, 5.

IN THE WRITING OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL SHALL THEY NOT BE WRITTEN) What is more, their name shall not be in the catalog of those returning.

Some understand the catalog of the faithful, from which they are to be blotted out, as that 'not being written' is taken in Jer. 17:13, Ps. 69:30, with Jerome and Theodoret; others, with the Chaldean and R. David, understand it as the book of life. The Osiandrine Paraphrase favors the Grotian sense.

NEITHER SHALL THEY ENTER INTO THE LAND OF ISRAEL) Either dead beforehand, or excluded by the pious.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN CONSILIO POPVLI MEI NONE- RUNT) Populus rediens illorum consilio non utetur, ut antea.

Alii de Ecclesia, vel congregatione Sanctorum exponunt, Hieronymus, Theodor. Lyran. B. Luther. &c. è Jer. 23, 18. Pf. 1, 2. 5.

IN SCRIPTVRA DOMVS ISRAEL NON SCRI- BENTVR) Quod plus est, non erit nomen illorum in cata- logo redeuntium.

Catalogum fidelium, ex quo delendi sint, ut illud non scribi accipitur Jer. 17. 13. Pf. 69, 30. cum Hieronymo & Theodor. nonnulli intelligunt; alii cum Chald. & R. David de libro vitæ. Grotiano sen- sui favet Paraphrasis Osiandrina.

NEC IN TERRAM ISRAEL INGREDIENTVR) Aut ante mortui, aut à piis exclusi.

## 13:10
Verse 10. SAYING PEACE, AND THERE IS NO PEACE) Saying all things are safe, when nevertheless they are not safe.

AND HE HIMSELF WAS BUILDING A WALL) He (the people) builds a wall: that is, he accumulates evil morals.

BUT THEY) The false prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DICENTES PAX, ET NON EST PAX) Dicentes salva omnia, cum tamen salva non sint.

ET IPSE ÆDIFICABAT PARIETEM) Ipse (po- pulus) ædificat parietem: id est, malos mores accumulat.

ILLI AVTEM) Falsi Prophetæ.

## 13:11
Verse 11. THEY DAUBED IT WITH UNTEMPERED MORTAR) In the Hebrew: They daub with inept, supply plaster, such as mud without straw usually is, or without any tempering. They wish to bring it about that the foulness of vices does not appear: but they take useless pains.

FOR THERE SHALL BE AN OVERFLOWING RAIN) Which easily dissolves mere mud.

AND I WILL GIVE GREAT STONES FALLING DOWN FROM ABOVE) In the Hebrew: And you, O Elgabish stones, shall fall. Gabish is crystal, as stated in Job 28:18. El is indeed the Arabic article; the sense is: fiery stones similar to crystal shall fall from heaven.

The word אלגבש is not read except here in verse 13 and Ezek. 38:22, where it is joined to pestilence and a stormy wind, so that it denotes something harmful or heavy, whence the LXX render it 'stones of hail' and B. Hulseman; here the great hopes of the Jews seem to be understood, which shall fall like stones upon their own heads.

AND A STORMY WIND RENDING IT) And a stormy wind shall dissipate, namely, the wall.

Latin:

Vers. 11. LINIEBANT EVM LVTO ABSQVE PA- LEIS) In Hebræo: Linunt inepto, supple tectorio, quale esse solet lutum sine paleis, aut sine ulla temperatura. Effi- cere volunt ut fœditas vitiorum non appareat: sed inutilem sumunt operam.

ERIT ENIM IMBER INUNDANS) Qui lutum merum facile dissolvit.

ET DABO LAPIDES PRÆGRANDES DESV- PER IRRVENTES) In Hebræo: Et vos ô Lapides Elgabis cadetis. Gabis est pyropus, ut dictum Job. 28, 18. El verò articulus Arabicus, sensus est: cadent de cœlo igniti lapi- des similes pyropo.

Vox אלגבש non legitur, nisi hic v. 13. & Ez. 38, 22. ubi pesti & vento procelloso jungitur, ut notet aliquid noxium, seu grave, unde LXX. reddunt λί- θες πετροβόλες & B. Hulseman. videntur hic magnæ Judæorum spes intelligi, casuræ velut lapides super ipsorum vertices.

ET VENTVM PROCELLÆ DISSIPANTEM) Et ventus procellosus dissipabit, parietem scilicet.

Vers. 14. AND OF THE WALL) They shall fall with their customs.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DE TRVAM PARIETEM) Cadent illi cum suis moribus.

AGAINST THE DAUGHTERS OF THY PEOPLE WHO PROPHESY OUT OF THEIR OWN HEART) Because among the people of God sometimes even women had been gifted with prophesying, such as Deborah and Huldah: Therefore other women also arrogated this honor to themselves, God not giving it.

Latin:

CONTRA FILIAS POPULI TVI QVÆ PRO- PHETANT DE CORDE SVO) Quia in populo Dei in- terdum etiam fœminæ prophetando donatæ fuerant, ut Debora & Olda: Ideo & aliæ mulieres hunc honorem sibi arrogabant, Deo non dante.

## 13:18
Vers. 18. THEY SEW PILLOWS UNDER

EVERY ELBOW OF THE HAND) Upon which men may rest sweetly. It is a Hebrew idiom to say hand for arm. AND MAKE KERCHIEFS UNDER THE HEAD OF EVERY STATURE) מִסְפָחוֹת David Kimchi says these are veils, with which women veil their faces. The Greeks here call them ἐπιβόλαια. Thus those prophetesses suggested pretexts to great and small for covering up their vices. AND TO CATCH SOULS) That is, to hunt souls, to entice men into their love. AND WHEN THEY CAUGHT THE SOULS OF MY PEOPLE, THEY KEPT THEM ALIVE) In the Hebrew: Do you not hunt the souls of my people, and where yours are, you promise them life? For among the Hebrews, words of declaring are also called by the names of doing.

Latin:

Vers. 18. CONSVVNT PVLVILLOS SVB OMNI

CVBITO MANVS) Quibus homines suaviter innitantur. Manum pro brachio dicere Hebræorum est. ET FACIVNT CERVICALIA SVB CAPITE VNIVERSÆ STATVRÆ) מִסְפָחוֹת David Kimchi ait esse velamina, quibus mulieres faciem velant. Græci hîc dicunt ἐπιβόλαια. Sic illæ Prophetides magnis & parvis sug- gerebant prætextus ad obtegenda vitia. AC CAPIENDAS ANIMAS) Id est, ad venandum animas, ad homines alliciendos in sui amorem. ET CVM CAPERENT ANIMAS POPVLI MEI, VIVIFICABANT ANIMAS EORVM) In Hebræo: Non- ne venamini animas populi, & ubi vestræ sunt, eis vitam promit- titis. Nam apud Hebræos etiam declarandi verba faciendi vocabulis appellantur.

## 13:19
Vers. 19.

AND THEY PROFANED ME AMONG MY PEOPLE) In the Hebrew: And you profaned me to my people. That is, you falsely usurped my name. FOR A HANDFUL OF BARLEY, AND A FRAGMENT OF BREAD) For the sake of sustenance only. Mich. 3, 5. Very similar is that of Cato: He can be hired for a crust of bread, either to be silent or to speak. TO SLAY THE SOULS THAT SHOULD NOT DIE) To slay the souls that will not die. That is, to predict destruction to the pious prophets whom I will save. Not only to the prophets, but also to others who are pious, who rebuke idolatry and crimes, and acknowledge the impending punishments; whom they condemn for error and impiety, and adjudge to eternal death (by their own false opinions): and on the contrary, they absolve impious idolaters and wicked men, and promise them earthly and heavenly happiness. AND TO KEEP ALIVE THE SOULS THAT SHOULD NOT LIVE) To keep alive the souls that will not live. To promise salvation to those whom I have determined to destroy.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ET VIOLABANT ME IN POPVLO MEO) In Hebræo: Et profanatis me ad populum meum. Id est nomen meum falso usurpatis. PROPTER PVGILLVM HORDEI, ET FRA- GMEN PANIS) Victus causam tantummini. Mich. 3, 5. Per- simile illud Catonis: Frusto panis conduci potest, vel uti taceat, vel uti loquatur. VT INTERFICERENT ANIMAS, QVÆ NON MORIVNTVR) Ad interficiendas animas, quæ non morien- tur. Id est, ad prædicendum exitium piis Prophetis quos ego servabo. Non Prophetis tantum, sed etiam aliis piis, qui idololatriam & scelera reprehendunt, & impen- dentes pœnas agnoscunt; quos erroris, & impieta- tis damnant, atque morti æternæ (suis falsis senten- tiis) adjudicant: & contra homines impios idolola- tras, & sceleratos absolvunt, iisque terrenam & cœlestem felicitatem promittunt. ET VIVIFICARENT ANIMAS QVÆ NON VI- VVNT) Ad vivificandas animas, quæ non vivent. Ad salu- tem promittendam iis quos ego perdere statui.

## 13:20
Vers. 20. WHEREWITH YOU CATCH THE SOULS THAT FLY) Wherewith you hunt souls to the flower, namely your own: for you will attract them caught by your love; פָּרַח is a flower and metaphorically the flower of youth in Baal Aruch and elsewhere. That word denotes to flourish: The sense according to B. Hulsem. is, the souls of the Jews deceived by false promises to this end, that they might as it were flourish in the midst of evils, that is, think themselves happy or blessed, Psal. 92, v. 8. & 12.

Latin:

Vers. 20. QVIBVS VOS CAPITIS ANIMAS VO- LANTES) Quibus vos venamini animas ad pubem, scilicet vestram: eo enim illos amore vestro captos attrahetis, פָּרַח est flos & metaphorice pubes in Baal Aruch & alibi. Verbum illud notat virere: Sensus juxta B. Hulsem. est, animas Judæorum deceptas falsis pro- missionibus hoc fine, ut in mediis malis quasi vire- ant, id est, felices seu beatas se putent, Psal. 92, v. 8. & 12.

## 13:21
Vers. 21. AND I WILL TEAR YOUR KERCHIEFS) The veils of the faces. More correctly Osiander: I will tear your kerchiefs, with which sinners have hitherto slept securely; I will cause that their lethargy be shaken off, so that they may at last feel their evils, do penance, and be saved. NEITHER SHALL THEY BE ANY MORE IN YOUR HANDS TO BE DELIVERED) And they shall no longer be subject to your hunters.

Latin:

Rectius Osiander: Dirumpam cervicalia vestra, quibus secure hactenus peccatores indormie- runt; efficiam, ut illis veternus excutiatur, ut tan- dem mala sua sentiant, pœnitentiam agant, & sal- ventur. NEQVE ERVNT VLTRA IN MANIBVS VE- STRIS AD PRÆDANDVM) Et non erunt ultra obnoxia vestris venantibus.

Vers. 22.

BECAUSE WITH LIES YOU HAVE MADE THE HEART OF THE RIGHTEOUS SAD) That is, by your calumnies. YOU HAVE STRENGTHENED THE HANDS OF THE WICKED) You have added courage to him. THAT HE SHOULD LIVE) In the Hebrew: by keeping him alive: That is, by promising him life.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV.

The hypocrisy of certain elders having been detected, God threatens punishments to idolaters consulting false prophets, and likewise to the false prophets themselves, and that the contempt of the Lord shall be avenged by famine, wild beasts, sword, and pestilence, even if the holiest of men should intercede with prayers.

Ver. 1.

AND THE MEN OF THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL CAME UNTO ME) Concerning the elders of Israel, Seraiah and those who were sent with him by Zedekiah to Babylon. 51, 59 These men deemed it necessary to address Ezekiel, who was famous for his prophecy, on their journey.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV.

Detecta Seniorum quorundam hypocrisi mina- tur Deus idololatris Pseudoprophetas consu- lentibus pœnas, ac similiter ipsis falsis Pro- phetis, & contemtum Domini vindicandum fame, feris, gladio, peste, etiamsi sanctissi- mi quique precibus interveniant.

Vers. 1.

ET VENERVNT AD ME VIRI SENIORVM ISRAEL) De senioribus Israel, Serajas & qui cum eo à Se- decia missi Babylonem. 51, 59 Hi Ezechielem Prophetia fama celebrem, in itinere compellandum sibi duxere.

## 14:3
Ver. 3. THEY HAVE SET UP THEIR STUMBLINGBLOCKS IN THEIR HEART) That is, they carry idolatry with their whole soul.

In Hebrew: They made their dung-gods (גלולים. Cf. ch. 8, 10; ch. 20, 7; ch. 22, 3; 1 Kings 21, 11. 21; 1 Macc. 13, 47. 48.) ascend upon their hearts. The LXX, Jerome, Sanctius, Pradus, Pintus, and Cornelius render it as 'wicked thoughts.' Maldonatus, however, and Saa explain it as referring to idols.

AND HAVE SET THE STUMBLING BLOCK OF THEIR INIQUITY BEFORE THEIR FACE) That is, the idols are daily before their eyes.

SHOULD I BE INQUIRED OF AT ALL BY THEM?) That is, should I give counsel? It is not right.

Latin:

Vers. 3. POSVERVNT IMMVNDITIAS SVAS IN CORDIBVS SVIS) Id est, idololatriam toto animo ge- stant.

In Ebr. Fecerunt ascendere deos stercoreos (גלולים. Conf. c. 8. 10. c. 20, 7. c. 22, 3. 1. Reg. 21, 11. 21. 1. Macc. 13. 47. 48.) suos super corda sua. LXX. Hier. Sanctius, Pradus, Pintus, Cornelius reddunt pravas cogitationes. Maldonat. tamen & Saa de idolis ex- ponunt.

ET SCANDALVM INIQVITATIS SVÆ STA- TVERVNT CONTRA FACIEM SVAM) Id est, idola quotidie illorum oculis obversantur.

NVMQVID INTERROGATVS RESPONDE- BO EIS?) Id est, consilium darem? non ex æquum.

## 14:4
Verse 4. MAN, MAN) That is, whoever he may be.

I THE LORD WILL ANSWER HIM IN THE MULTITUDE OF HIS ABOMINATIONS) In the Hebrew: I will answer him: he comes in the multitude of his abominations. Behold, he dares to come to me, having a mind full of idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 4. HOMO, HOMO) Id est, quisquis fuerit.

EGO DOMINVS RESPONDEBO EI IN MUL- TITVDINE IMMVNDITIARVM SVARVM) In He- bræo: Respondebo ei: venit in multitudine immunditiarum suarum. Ecce ille ad me venire audet, animum habens idolatriæ plenum.

## 14:5
Verse 5. THAT THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL MAY BE TAKEN IN THEIR OWN HEART) That the house of Israel may be reproved (that is, convicted) in their own heart.

Latin:

Vers. 5. VT CAPIATVR DOMUS ISRAEL IN COR- DE SVO) Vt reprehendatur (id est, convincatur) domus Israel in corde suo.

## 14:7
Verse 7. AND OF THE PROSELYTES WHOSOEVER SOJOURNETH IN ISRAEL) Or of the inhabitants who dwell in the land of Israel. For even foreigners who lived among the Israelites, even if they had not subjected themselves to the Law, were nevertheless bound to abstain from idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET DE PROSELTTIS QVICVMQVE AD- VENA FVERIT IN ISRAEL) Aut de incolis qui incolunt terram Israel. Nam & extranei qui inter Israelitas vivebant, etiamsi legi se non subjeciffent, tenebantur tamen ab idolo- latria se abstinere.

## 14:9
Verse 9. I THE LORD WILL ANSWER HIM BY MYSELF) I will answer him by my deeds.

AND IF THE PROPHET BE DECEIVED) When he has been seduced, namely by the hope of gain.

AND HATH SPOKEN A WORD) As if it were commanded to him by God.

I THE LORD HAVE DECEIVED THAT PROPHET) I will deceive. Bringing upon him an end which he did not expect.

Oecolampadius explains this as a positive seduction of the false prophet, in that the Lord impels him by depraving his reason and inciting his affections. But the Belgian Paraphrasts acknowledge this to be erroneous on this passage, since God does not seduce anyone through the suggestion of evil thoughts; they therefore explain it negatively, that this happens when God does not provide the grace to resist. Most of the Papists explain it in this way: that God seduces by suggesting an occasion, regarding which not only is a fall easy, but also, from God's foreknowledge, it is infallible. But there is no need for God to present such occasions, which the world, the devil, and our own flesh suggest continually. James 1:13; 1 John 2:15. Nor is it of God to concur in such a way. Wherefore, having refuted those heterodox expositions, B. Hülsemann judges it more consistent with the text if it is understood concerning the permission of the fall into various misfortunes, with the evils of fault abstracted. Compare Jer. 20:7, Prov. 20:12, ch. 24:18. See his excerpts on this passage. We have Grotius agreeing here.

Latin:

Vers. 9. EGO DOMINVS RESPONDEBO EI PER ME) Factis ei respondebo.

ET PROPHETA CUM ERRAVERIT) Cum se- ductus fuerit, nempe spe lucri.

ET LOCVTVS FVERIT VERBUM) Quasi à Deo sibi imperatum.

EGO DOMINVS DECEPI PROPHETAM ILLVM) Decipiam. Exitum illi inferens, quem non exspectabat.

Oecolampadius explicat de positiva seductione Pseudo Prophetæ, quod Dominus rationem depra- vando, affectus incitando impellat. Sed hoc errone- um esse agnoscunt Paraphrastæ Belgici, ad hunc lo- cum, siquidem Deus non seducat quenquam per suggestionem malorum cogitationum : qui proin- denegative explicant quod id fiat cum DEUS non suppeditat resistendi gratiam. E Pontificiis plerique explicant hoc modo, quod Deus seducat suggeren- do occasionem, circa quam non solum facilis est la- psus, sed etiam ex prævisione Dei est infallibilis: Verum opus non est, ut Deus tales occasiones obji- ciat, quas mundus, diabolus & caro nostra subinde suggerunt. Jacob. 1, 13. 1. Job. 2, 15. Neque hoc Dei est, ita concurrere. Quapropter profligatis istis hete- rodoxis expositionibus B. Hülsemannus textui ma- gis consentaneum judicat, si de permissione lapsus in varia infortunia, abstractis malis culpæ, intelligatur. Confer. Jer. 20, 7. Prov. 20, 12. c. 24, 18. Vide ex- cerpta ejus ad hunc locum. Habemus hic Gro- tium consentientem.

## 14:10
Ver. 10. ACCORDING TO THE INIQUITY OF HIM THAT INQUIRETH, SO SHALL THE INIQUITY OF THE PROPHET BE) That is, they shall feel the punishments equally, both those who buy prophecies and those who sell them.

Vers. 10. JVXTA INIQVITATEM INTERROGAN- TIS, SIC INIQVITAS PROPHETÆ ERIT) Id est, pœnas pariter sentient & qui emunt vaticinia, & qui vendunt.

## 14:11
Ver. 11. THAT THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL MAY GO NO MORE ASTRAY) Seduced, that is, by those false prophets.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VT NON ERRET VLTRA DOMVS ISRA- EL) Seducta scilicet à pseudoprophetis illis.

## 14:13
Ver. 13. THAT IT SHOULD TRESPASS A TRESPASS) מעל מעל is a change of the worship of the Lord.

I WILL BREAK THE STAFF OF THE BREAD THEREOF) Above 4:16, 5:16.

Latin:

Vers. 13. VT PRÆVARICETVR PRÆVARICANS) מעל מעל est mutatio cultus Domini.

CONTERAM VIRGAM PANIS EJVS) Supra 4, 16. 5, 16.

## 14:14
Ver. 14. NOAH) Who rescued eight people from the flood.

DANIEL) Who delivered the Chaldean magi from imminent death.

AND JOB) Who obtained pardon for those who had offended him.

BY THEIR OWN RIGHTEOUSNESS) Because of their virtues.

THEY SHALL DELIVER THEIR OWN SOULS) Only moderately are the wicked sometimes spared for the sake of the pious, not so for the stubbornly flagitious.

Maldonatus and others ineptly prove from this that the Saints in heaven pray for us. For God speaks openly about the presence of these saints and their dwelling among sinners, and it is a hypothetical statement. What, therefore, does that have to do with saints praying in heaven? And it is certain that Daniel was alive at that time, having been taken to Babel in the 3rd year of Jehoiakim. The Prophet therefore means this: if Noah and Job were also living on earth with Daniel, and were praying for the people, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 14. NOE) Qui octo homines diluvio eripuit.

DANIEL) Qui Chaldæos magos ab imminente morte liberavit.

ET JOB) Qui veniam impetravit iis, qui ipsum ossenderant.

JVSTITIA SVA) Ob suas virtutes.

LIBERABVNT ANIMAS SVAS) Tantum medio- criter malis ob pios interdum parcitur, non ita contuma- citer flagitiosis.

Inepte Maldonatus & alii hinc probant, Sanctos in cælis pro nobis orare. Loquitur enim aperte Deus de præsentia horum sanctorum, & habitatione in- ter peccatores, estque hypothetica loquutio Quid ergo illa ad sanctos in cœlo orantes? Etvixisse tunc Danielem, utpote anno 3. Jojakimi in Babel trans- latum, certum est. Id ergo vult Propheta, si cum Daniele etiam Noah, & Job in terris agerent, & pro populo orarent, &c.

## 14:15
Ver. 15. THAT I MAY LAY IT WASTE) About to bereave it. Ver. 19. PESTILENCE) θάνατον, the Greeks. See what was said on Matt. 24:7. IN BLOOD) That is, with great slaughter of men, as the Chaldean here. For to the Hebrews, blood is every kind of untimely death. Ver. 22. YET BEHOLD, THEREIN SHALL BE LEFT A REMNANT THAT SHALL BE BROUGHT FORTH, BOTH SONS AND DAUGHTERS) And if some survivors remain, who bring forth sons and daughters with them: THEY SHALL COME FORTH UNTO YOU) They also shall be deported to you who have been deported. AND YE SHALL SEE THEIR WAY AND THEIR DOINGS) That is, so that by the testimony of those who come to you, it may be known what kind of people they were whom I delivered to famine, pestilence, sword, and beasts. To see, among the Hebrews, is to obtain knowledge of something in any way. AND YE SHALL BE COMFORTED CONCERNING THE EVIL THAT I HAVE BROUGHT UPON JERUSALEM) You will grieve less when you see that the vengeance was so just.

Vers. 15. VT VASTEM EAM) Orbaturus eam. Vers. 19. PESTILENTIAM) θάνατον, Græci. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 24, 7. IN SANGVINE) Id est, cum multa hominum stra- ge, ut hîc Chaldæus. Nam omne mortis immaturæ genus sanguis Hebræis. Vers. 22. TAMEN RELINQVETVR IN EA SAL- VATIO EDUCENTIVM FILIOS ET FILIAS) Et se ma- neant aliqui superstites, qui filios ac filias secum educant: IPSI INGREDIENTVR AD VOS) Illi ad vos de- portatos ipsi quoque deportabuntur. ET VIDEBITIS VIAM EORVM, ET ADIN- VENTIONES EORVM) Id est, ut illorum qui ad vos ve- niunt testimonio cognoscatur quales illi fuerint, quos fami, pesti, gladio, bestiis tradidi. Videre apud Hebræos, est co- gnitionem alicujus rei quovis modo adipisci. ET CONSOLABIMINI SUSER MALO QVOD INDVXI IN JERVSALEM) Minus dolebitis cum vide- ritis tam justam fuisse ultionem.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

Just as wood cut from the vine serves only for the fire, so he predicts that the Jews, because of their inveterate sins, are to be burned along with Jerusalem.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Sicut lignum de vite præcisum soli servit igni, ita Iudæos ob inveterata peccata cum Ieru- salem prædicit exurendos.

## 15:2
Vers. 2. WHAT SHALL BECOME OF THE WOOD OF THE VINE) You translate correctly: What will there be in which the vine excels other plants, if its branch is equal to forest trees? That is, it brings forth no fruits. The vine is a figure of the Jewish people, Is. 5, Jer. 2, 21, Ps. 80, 9, Matt. 21, 33. Vers. 3. SHALL WOOD BE TAKEN FROM IT, TO DO WORK) As from other forest trees are made masts of ships, beams, tables. OR SHALL A PIN BE MADE FROM IT.) Not even for this are the twigs firm enough. Vers. 4. BEHOLD IT IS GIVEN TO THE FIRE FOR FOOD) It is given to the fire to be consumed. That alone remains. Matt. 3, 10. BOTH ENDS OF IT) Both its outer parts. THE FIRE HATH CONSUMED) It will consume. The LXX ineptly explain: and after a year of purging the fire consumes it. Cf. Jerome. AND THE MIDST OF IT IS REDUCED TO ASHES) In the Hebrew: The middle of it is scorched. SHALL IT BE USEFUL FOR WORK?) That is, so that for that reason any care should be taken of it. Nothing less. Vers. 6. SO WILL I DELIVER THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM) Men of no use. V. 7. AND I WILL SET MY FACE AGAINST THEM) I will look upon them with a stern countenance, as Jer. 21, 10, 44, 11, 27, above 13, 17. THEY SHALL GO OUT FROM THE FIRE, AND THE FIRE SHALL CONSUME THEM) Fire here signifies every kind of evil. Ps. 66, 12, and elsewhere: one evil avoided, they will fall into another. B. Luther explained it negatively: They shall not escape the fire. But almost all other interpreters [explain it] in this way: although they go out from one fire, yet (another) fire shall devour them. Cf. c. 7, 16, Isa. 20, last, Jer. 4, 19, 20. So Jerome, Theodoret, Polychronius, Lyra, and others. Vers. 8. BECAUSE THEY HAVE BEEN TRANSGRESSORS) There is here again in the Hebrew מעל. Jerome in his Commentary on this place: For they have not been sinners like other nations, but transgressors. For it is one thing to neglect what you are ignorant of, another to despise what you have worshipped.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QVID FIET DE LIGNO VITIS) Verteris re- cte: Quid erit in quo vitis præstet aliis plantis, si palmes ejus sit par sylvestribus arboribus? Id est, nullos fructus proferat. Vitis figura populi Judaici Es. 5. Jer. 2, 21. Ps. 80, 9. Matt. 21, 33. Vers. 3. NVMQVID TOLLETVR DE EA LIGNVM, VT FIAT OPVS) Ut ex aliis arboribus silvaticis fiunt mali navium, trabes, mensæ. AVT FABRICABITVR DE EA PAXILLVS.) Ne in hoc quidem satis firma sunt sarmenta. Vers. 4. ECCE IGNI DATVM EST IN ESCAM) Debitur igni absumendum. Id unum restat. Matt. 3, 10.
