VTRAMQVE PARTEM EJVS) Extima ejus utraque. CONSVMPSIT IGNIS) Consumet. LXX. inepte exponunt: & post annum purga- tionem ejus absumit ignis. Conf. Hieronym. ET MEDIETAS EJVS REDACTA EST IN FA- VILLAM) In Hebræo: Medium ejus ustulatum est. NVMQVID VTILE ERIT AD OPUS?) Ut scilicet propterea cura ejus aliqua sumi debeat. Nihil minus. Vers. 6. SIC TRADAM HABITATORES JERVSA- LEM) Nulli usui homines. V. 7. ET PONAM FACIEM MEAM IN EOS) Aspici- am eos vultu torvo, ut Jer. 21, 10. 44, 11. 27. supra 13, 17. DE IGNE EGREDIENTVR, ET IGNIS CON- SVMET EOS) Ignis hîc omne malorum genus significat. Ps 66, 12. & alibi: uno malo vitato, in aliud incident. B. Luther. negative exposuit: Sie sollen dem Feuer nicht entgehen. Alii vero Interpretes pleri- que omnes h. m. quanquam ex uno igne egrediun- tur, devorabit tamen eos (alius) ignis. Conf. c. 7, 16. Esa. 20. ult. Jer. 4, 19. 20. Ita Hieron. Theod. Po- lychron. Lyr. alii. Vers. 8. EO QVOD PRÆVARICATORES EXSTI- TERINT) Est hîc rursus in Hebræo מעל. Hieronymus in Commentario ad hunc locum: Non enim peccatores sicut cæ- teræ gentes, sed prævaricatores extiterunt. Aliud est enim ne- gligere quod ignores, aliud contemnere quod colueris.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI.

Jerusalem, previously most abject, having been exalted by God to an excessive degree, because of her manifold spiritual fornication, by which she surpassed both Samaria and Sodom, is to be delivered to devastation and the reproach of all nations, yet with the covenant preserved for the remnant of the Lord.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI.

Ierusalem prius abjectissima nimium in mo- dum à Deo exaltata, ob fornicationem spiri- tualem multiplicem, qua & Samariam & Sodomam superavit in vastationem omni- umque gentium opprobrium tradenda, ser- vato tamen pacto reliquiis Domini.

## 16:2
Vers. 2. MAKE KNOWN TO JERUSALEM HER ABOMINATIONS) Namely, by a letter, which he was to send to the Jews living in their homeland. There is, moreover, in this whole chapter a wonderful δέινωσις (vehemence), excellently pursuing that similitude of adultery and idolatry. Vers. 3. THY ROOT AND THY HABITATION IS OF THE LAND OF CANAAN) The first habitation of your parents, from whence you had your origin, was the land of Canaan, most corrupt in its morals, from which you drew much more than from the virtues of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Latin:

Vers. 2. NOTAS FAC JERVSALEM ABOMINATIO- NES SVAS) Nempe per epistolam, quam mittere debebat ad Judæos in patria agentes. Est autem hujus totius capitis mira δέινωσις, egregie persequens illam similitudinem adul- terii & Idololatriæ. Vers. 3. RADIX TVA ET HABITATIO TVA DE TER- RA CHANAAN) Habitati prima parentum tuorum, un- de ortus est tibi, fuit terra Chanaan, corruptissima mori- bus, unde multo plus hausisti, quam de virtutibus Abraha- mi, Isaaci & Jacobi.

## 16:3
THY FATHER WAS AN AMORITE, AND THY MOTHER A HITTITE) He calls them father and mother not by nature but by habitation, those who previously held the same land, and whose customs their successors in the land followed. Thus the yennata are called successors, as we said at Luke 3.

Latin:

PATER TVUS AMORRHÆVS, ET MATER TVA CETHÆA) Patrem & matrem vocat non natura sed habitatione eos qui prius eandem terram tenuere, & quorum mores eorum in terra successores sequebantur. Sic yennata dicuntur successores, ut ad 3. Lucæ diximus.

## 16:4
THY NAVEL WAS NOT CUT) From that intestine through which the infant adheres to the mother: That is, you were a most despised people when you were born in Egypt. Namely, infants who are despised are accustomed to be cast away, with no care from their parents for them. See the Title of the Code concerning exposed infants, where it is in Law 2. For no one could call his own, him whom he despises while perishing.

AND THOU WAST NOT WASHED IN WATER UNTO HEALTH) Infants are washed from blood with water, as Jerome well notes here.

NOR SALTED WITH SALT) For the moisture of the bodies of little ones, as the same man says, is dried by the addition of salt.

NOR SWADDLED IN CLOTHS) With swaddling bands, which this Jerome testifies that the barbarians observed both longer and more diligently than the Romans: and therefore the bodies of the barbarians are straighter.

Osiander on this passage. Although the Holy Scriptures wished to signify by these words how despised the Israelite nation once was, especially when it served in Egypt; yet even by this description of filth he depicted the spiritual uncleanness of original sin, which we bring with us from the maternal womb into this world. That must be washed away by the water of Baptism, lest it be imputed to us. And the Lord is accustomed to use the salt of the cross and of afflictions to overcome the old Adam; nevertheless, its remnants remain until all that filth of man is abolished in the sepulcher. Which allegory is not inappropriate: especially because that original filth is to be considered the fountain and origin of all evil, even that which is properly described here.

Latin:

NON EST PRÆCISVS VMBILICVS TVVS) Ab intestino illo per quod matri infans adhæret: Id est, contem- tissimus fuisti populus cum nascereris in Ægypto. Scilicet infantes qui contemnuntur abjici solent, nulla parentum de iis cura. Vide Titulum Codicis de infantibus expositis, ubi est in L. 2. Nec enim suum quis dicere potuerit, quem per- euntem contemnit.

ET AQVA NON ES LOTA IN SALVTEM) Aqua abluuntur infantes à sanguine, ut hic bene nota Hieronymus.

NEC SALE SALITA) Humor enim corporum parvulorum, ut idem ait, salis adjectione siccatur.

NEC INVOLVTA PANNIS) Fasciis, quod barba- ros & diutius & diligentiùs observasse quam Romanos te- statur hic Hieronymus: ideoque & corpora barbarorum esse rectiora.

Osiander h. l. Etsi S.S. significare his verbis voluit, quam contempta aliquando fuerit gens Israëlitica, præsertim cum in Ægypto serviret; tamen etiam hac fœditatis descriptione depinxit spiritualem immunditiem originalis peccati, quod ex utero ma- terno in hunc mundum nobiscum afferimus. Id abluendum est aqua Baptismi, ne nobis impute- tur. Et solet Dominus ad expugnandum vete- rem Adamum uti sale crucis & afflictionum; ma- nent tamen nihilominus ejus reliquiæ, donec in sepulcro tota illa hominis fœditas aboleatur. Quæ allegoria non inconcinna est: imprimis quia origi- naria illa fœditas fons & origo mali omnis, etiam quod hic proprie describitur, censenda est.

## 16:5
Verse 5. AND NO EYE SPARED THEE, TO DO ANY OF THESE THINGS UNTO THEE, HAVING COMPASSION UPON THEE,) He signifies the hardness of the Egyptians, who ought to have been like parents to them, on account of the merits of Joseph, as the Chaldean rightly observes here.

BUT THOU WAST CAST OUT UPON THE FACE OF THE EARTH) Exposed. Those who cast away infants, says the law Sancimus in the Code concerning exposed infants. They cast them out, says Turtius Clodius in the same matter in Seneca, book IV of the Controversies, XXXIII. Such infants are called argorintoi by Harmenopulus.

IN THE ABJECTION OF THY SOUL) That is, with danger to thy life. About to perish unless they are taken away: Labienus in the same controversy.

IN THE DAY THAT THOU WAST BORN) For the people were born in Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 5. NEC PEPERCIT SVPER TE OCVLVS, VT FACERET TIBI VNVM DE HIS, MISERTVS TVI,) Ægyptiorum, qui quasi parentes illis esse debebant, ob Jose- phi merita, duritiam significat, ut recte hic observat Chal- dæus.

SED PROJECTA ES SVPER FACIEM TER- RÆ) Exposita. Qui infantes abjecerunt, ait lex Sancimus C. de Infantibus expositis Projiciunt, ait in eadem re Turtia- nus Clodius apud Senecam lib. IV. controversiarum XXXIII. Tales infantes argorintoi Harmenopulo.

IN ABJECTIONE ANIMÆ TVÆ) Id est, cum periculo vitæ tuæ. Perituros nisi auferantur: Labienus in eadem controversia.

IN DIE QVA NATA ES) Populus enim in Ægy- pto natus est.

## 16:6
Verse 6. AND WHEN I PASSED BY THEE) Passing by thee: as is accustomed to happen.

I SAW THEE TRAMPLED IN THY BLOOD) Reddening from the sea (so Juvenal speaks of being trodden by feet). In the said title of the code it is added: And concerning those who received blood-stained ones to be nourished. The second law uses the same word in the Code concerning fathers who sold their sons: And Donatus in the Andria: and Prudentius against Symmachus: Lactantius called infants from the blood.

LIVE IN THY BLOOD) Although thou art foul with blood, I wish thee to live.

Latin:

Vers. 6. TRANSIENS AVTEM PER TE) Te præte- riens: ut fieri solet.

VIDI TE CONCVLCARI IN SANGVINE) Rubentem à mare (ita Juvenalis loquitur pedibus teri. In di- cto titulo codicis additur: Et de his, qui sanguinolentos nutri- endos acceperunt. Eadem voce utitur Lex secunda, Codice de patribus qui filios suos distraxerunt: Et Donatus in Andria: & Prudentius adversus Symmachum: Lactantius infantes à sanguine dixit.

IN SANGVINE TVO VIVE) Quanquam fœda es sanguine, volo te vivere.

## 16:7
Vers. 7. I HAVE CAUSED THEE TO MULTIPLY AS THE BUD OF THE FIELD, AND THOU ART MULTIPLIED AND BECOME GREAT) Better: I have made thee grow, as the bud of the field, and by growing thou art become great. That the discourse may continue concerning the girl, under whose person the Jewish nation is described.

AND THOU ART COME TO WOMANLY ORNAMENT) Better: and thou art come to pass through transitions: that is, that from an infant thou mightest become a young woman. עבר among other things means to pass through. There can be no mention here of ornaments or attire, because she is still depicted as naked. The following words, however, explain that transition.

THY BREASTS ARE FASHIONED) Thy breasts have swelled. See Cant. 8, 8.

AND THY HAIR IS GROWN) Puberty. Macrobius, book on the dream, chapter 6: After twice seven years, the necessity of age itself reaches puberty. The same, Saturnalia 7, 1: Natural moisture in the body, when age passes childhood, becomes harder and is sharpened into hairs, therefore then also puberty. Tertullian on the veiling of virgins: Now also the voice has changed, and the limbs are complete, and shame is clothed everywhere, and the months pay their tribute. The Hebrews also judged of age by inspecting the body.

AND THOU WAST NAKED AND FULL OF CONFUSION) In the Hebrew: Naked and uncovered: that is, lacking clothing, or thinly clad. Thus is expressed the misery of the nation in Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MVLTIPLICATAM QVASI GERMEN A- GRI DEDI TE, ET MVLTIPLICATA ES GRANDIS EFFECTA) Melius: Crescere feci te, ut germen agri, & cre- scendo grandis facta es. Ut duret sermo de puella, sub cu- jus persona gens Judaica describitur.

ET PERVENISTI AD MVNDVM MVLIEBREM) Melius: & pervenisti ut transires transitiones: id est, ut ex infante fieres adolescentula. עבר inter alia est transire. Mundi aut ornamentorum nulla hic esse potest mentio, quia adhuc nuda fingitur. Transitum autem istum expli- cant sequentia.

VBERA TVA INTVMVERVNT) Mammæ soro- riarunt. Vid. Cant. 8, 8.

ET PILVS TVVS GERMINAVIT) Pubes. Macro- bius lib. de somnio cap 6 Post annos autem bis septem ipsa æ- tatis necessitatem pubescit. IdemSaturnal. 7, 1. Humor natura- lis in corpore, quando ætas transit pueritiam, fit durior & acui- tur in pilos, ideo tunc & pubes. Tertullianus de virginibus ve- landis: Iam & vox obsolefacta est & membra completa sunt, & pudor ubique vestitur, & menses tributa dependunt. Hebræi etiam corpore inspecto de ætate judicabant.

ET ERAT NVDA ET CONFVSIONE PLE- NA) In Hebræo: Nuda & reteda: id est, vestitu carens, aut tenuiter vestita. Sic exprimitur miseria gentis in Ægypto.

## 16:8
Vers. 8.

AND I PASSED BY THEE, AND LOOKED UPON THEE) Passing by thee, I beheld thee.

AND BEHOLD THY TIME, THE TIME OF LOVERS) Of loves: that is, Now ripe for a husband, now in full marriageable years.

AND I SPREAD MY SKIRT OVER THEE) A rite in taking a wife: Ruth 3, 9. Thus Euripides: Ὅταν δ' ὑπ' ἀνδρὸς χλαῖναν ἐυγενῶς πέσῃς.

AND I COVERED THY SHAME) I clothed thee with garments.

AND I SWARE UNTO THEE, AND ENTERED INTO A COVENANT WITH THEE) At Sinai.

AND YOU BECAME MINE

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET TRANSIVI PER TE, ET VIDI TE) Præteri- ens te aspexi.

ET ECCE TEMPVS TVVM, TEMPUS AMAN- TIVM) Amorum: id est, Iam matura viro, jam plenis nubilis annis.

ET EXPANDI AMICTUM MEVM SVPER TE) Ritus in sumenda uxore: Ruth. 3, 9. Sic Euripides: Ὅταν δ' ὑπ' ἀνδρὸς χλαῖναν ἐυγενῶς πέσῃς.

ET OPERVI IGNOMINIAM TVAM) Vestibus te indui.

ET JVRAVI TIBI, ET INGRESSVS SVM PA- CTVM TECUM) In Sinai.

ET FACTA ES MIHI) Mea.

## 16:9
Verse 9.

AND I WASHED YOU WITH WATER AND CLEANSED YOUR BLOOD FROM YOU) I prepared baths for you, in which you might be cleansed from the flow, as is the custom for women, Lev. 12, 28. It signifies the cleansings instituted in the law.

AND I ANOINTED YOU WITH OIL) As is the custom for those newly wed, Ruth 3, 3; Judith 5, 3. The priesthood is signified.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET LAVI TE AQVA ET EMUNDAVI SAN- GVINEM TVVM EX TE) Balnea tibi paravi, in quibus ex profluvio mundareris, ut mos fœminis, Lev. 12, 28. si- gnificat mundationes in lege institutas.

ET VNXI TE OLEO) Ut mos fieri noviter nu- ptis Ruth. 3, 3 Judith. 5, 3. significatur sacerdotium.

## 16:10
Verse 10.

AND I CLOTHED YOU WITH VARICOLORED GARMENTS) New brides also used to take better, multicolored garments. In the Hebrew: I clothed you with needlework. All these things signify the various ceremonies of the law.

AND I SHOD YOU WITH HYACINTHINE) In the Hebrew: With badger skin. On feast days the Hebrews had shoes made of badger skins. The Talmudists mention this.

AND I GIRDED YOU WITH FINE LINEN) In the Hebrew: I covered you with fine linen. I gave you bedspreads of fine linen.

AND I CLOTHED YOU WITH FINE FABRICS) In the Hebrew: I girded you with silk, that is: of silk I made for you bed coverings. Here are signified the ornaments of the sacred tent, which is to God as a nuptial bed.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET VESTIVI TE DISCOLORIBVS) Novæ nu- ptæ etiam vestes meliores sumebant versicolores. In He- bræo: Vestivi te acupictis. Hæc omnia significant varias legis ceremonias.

ET CALCEAVI TE JANTHINO) In Hebræo: Melinis. Hebræi diebus festis calceos habebant de melium pellibus. Meminere Thalmudici.

ET CINXI TE BTSSO) In Hebræo: Instravite bys- so. Stragulas lectorum tibi dedi è bysso.

ET INDVI TE SVBTILIBVS) In Hebræo: Cinxi te ferico, id est: è serico feci tibi lecti περιστρώματα. Hic si- gnificantur ornamenta sacri tentorii, quæ Deo velut nu- ptialis lectus.

## 16:11
Verse 11. AND I ADORNED YOU WITH ORNAMENT) That is, I gave you every feminine ornament: which generality is then explained by its species. The immense riches of the people are signified, especially under David and Solomon.

Grotius understands all these things as referring to corporal benefits. And although God also enumerated such things in this catalog of benefits, it cannot, however, be believed in any way that He was entirely silent about the more important, i.e., spiritual benefits: whence it is better with others to understand these as referring to a gracious upbringing up to womanly perfection (because the Israelite Church is presented under the form of a woman), that is, as the blessed Hülsemann explains, up to the perfection of divine grace in this life; v. 7, concerning spiritual betrothal; v. 8, concerning gracious regeneration and sanctification; v. 9. And thus Osiander explains those words, I WASHED YOU WITH WATER AND CLEANSED YOUR INIQUITY FROM YOU, as concerning cleansing from spiritual iniquity, and the following words, I ANOINTED YOU WITH OIL, as concerning the gift of the Holy Spirit, the oil of gladness. Similarly the Weimar Paraphrasts and Vatablus, and among the ancients, Origen, Theodoret, and others.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET ORNAVI TE ORNAMENTO) Id est omnem ornatum muliebrem tibi dedi: quæ generalitas de- inde per suas species explicatur. Significantur ingentes di- vitiæ populi, sub Davide maxime & Salomone.

Hæc omnia de corporalibus beneficiis intelligit Grotius. Et quamquam Deus etiam talia in hoc beneficiorum catalogo recensuerit, non potest ta- men ullo modo credi, eum potiora, h. e. spiritua- lia beneficia prorsus tacuisse: unde præstat cum a- liis hæc de gratiosa educatione usque ad perfectionem muliebrem (quia sub forma mulieris exhibetur Ec- clesia Israelica) intelligere, hoc est, ut explicat B. Hülsemannus, usque ad perfectionem gratiæ divinæ in hac vita v. 7. de spirituali desponsatione v. 8. de gratiosa regeneratione & sanctificatione v. 9. Atque ita Osiander illa LAVI TE AQVA ET EMVN- DAVI INIQUITATEM TUAM A TE, de emundatione ab iniquitate spirituali, ac sequentia UNXI TE OLEO de donatione Spiritus sancti olei lætitiæ explicat. Similiter Paraphrastæ Vinari- enses & Vatablus, & è veteribus Origenes, Theodore- tus & alii.

## 16:12
Verse 12.

AND I PUT A RING UPON THY NOSTRIL) A jewel upon thy nose. That custom existed among those nations. See what is said in Job 11, 12. Prov. 11, 22. Jerome, who lived in those regions: Even to this day among other ornaments of women, golden rings are accustomed to hang from the forehead over the mouth, and to overhang the nostrils.

AND RINGS UPON THINE EARS) Golden rings in the ears.

AND A CROWN OF BEAUTY UPON THINE HEAD) A crown was also placed upon those being married, Cant. 4, 8. Royal dignity is signified.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET DEDI INAVREM SVPER OS TVVM) Moni- le super nasum tuum. Is mos erat illis gentibus. Vide quæ di- cta Job. 11, 12. Prov. 11, 22. Hieronymus, qui in illis locis vixit: Vsque hodie inter cætera ornamenta mulierum, solent aurei circuli in os ex fronte pendere, & imminere naribus.

ET CIRCVLOS AVRIBVS TVIS) Annulos au- reos in auribus.

ET CORONAM DECORIS IN CAPITE TVO) Etiam corona imponebatur nubentibus Cant. 4, 8. signi- ficatur dignitas regia.

## 16:13
Vers. 13. AND THOU WAST CLOTHED WITH FINE LINEN, AND BROIDERED WORK, AND MANY COLORS) With fine linen, and silk, and needlework. The wives of the wealthy are accustomed to have many sets of garments.

THOU DIDST EAT FINE FLOUR AND HONEY AND OIL) Not onions and garlic, as in Egypt. It was customary for most sweet cakes to be made with these three mixed together.

AND THOU WAST MADE EXCEEDING BEAUTIFUL) Being treated so delicately, thou didst become more beautiful day by day. The magnificence of the temple is signified.

AND THOU DIDST PROSPER INTO A KINGDOM) Thou didst prosper in the kingdom, that is, in majesty. The dominion acquired over neighboring nations is signified, as the Chaldean rightly notes here.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET VESTITA ES BTSSO, ET POLTMI- TO, ET MVLTIS COLORIBVS) Bysso, & serico, & a- cupictis. Opulentorum uxores multas habere solent vestium syntheses.

SIMILAM ET MEL ET OLEVM COMEDISTI) Non cepas & allia, ut in Ægypto. Solebant tribus his mistis suavitissimæ fieri placentæ.

ET DECORA FACTA ES NIMIS) Ita delicate habita speciosior in dies evasisti. Significatur templi ma- gnificentia.

ET PROFECISTI IN REGNUM) Profecisti in re- gno, id est, in majestate. Significator imperium quæsitum in gentes vicinas, ut recte hic notat Chaldæus.

## 16:15
Vers. 15. AND HAVING CONFIDENCE IN THY BEAUTY, THOU HAST PLAYED THE HARLOT) But being proud because of thy form, thou hast committed adultery. There is a conflict between great beauty and chastity. He now begins to touch upon all the scandals of the nation from the times of Solomon onwards. IN THY NAME) As if thou wert of thine own right, and not in the power of a husband. AND HAST EXPOSED THY FORNICATION TO EVERY ONE THAT PASSED BY) That is, thou hast prostituted thy lusts.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET HABENS FIDVCIAM IN PVLCHRITVDI- NE TVA, FORNICATA ES) Sed superbiens ob formam suam, mœchata es. Lis est cum forma magna pudicitiæ. Incipit jam attingere omnia gentis flagitia à Salomonis us- que temporibus. IN NOMINE TVO) Quasi tui juris esses, & non in mariti potestate. ET EXPOSVISTI FORNICATIONEM TVAM OMNI TRANSEVNTI) Id est, prostıtuisti libidines tuas.

## 16:16
Vers. 16. AND TAKING OF THY GARMENTS) Fine linen, silk, embroidered work. THOU HAST MADE TO THYSELF HIGH PLACES) That is, tents on high places, in the Babylonian manner. PATCHED ON EVERY SIDE) טלאות, they are variegated, with broader stripes.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET SVMENS DE VESTIMENTIS TVIS)Byssum, sericum, acupicta. FECISTI TIBI EXCELSA) Id est, Tentoria in ex- celsis, more Babylonico. HINC INDE CONSVTA) טלאות, sunt segmen- tata, plagis latioribus.

## 16:17
Vers. 17. THE VESSELS OF THY BEAUTY) Womanly ornaments. THOU HAST MADE TO THYSELF MASCULINE IMAGES) Baalim. AND HAST PLAYED THE HARLOT WITH THEM) With them thou hast committed adultery.

Latin:

Vers. 17. VASA DECORIS TVI) Ornamenta muliebria. FECISTI TIBI IMAGINES MASCVLINAS) Baa- limos. ET FORNICATA ES IN EIS) Cum eis mœcha- ta es.

## 16:18
AND THOU HAST COVERED THEM) The images. Vers. 18. AND MY OIL) My lamps. AND MY INCENSE) The incense owed to me.

Latin:

ET OPERVISTI ILLAS) Imagines. Vers. 18. ET OLEVM MEVM) Lychnos meos. ET THTMIAMA MEVM) Suffitus mihi debitos.

## 16:19
Vers. 19. AND MY BREAD WHICH I GAVE THEE) By the name of bread the Hebrews understand everything by which we are nourished. This generality is explained by what follows. FINE FLOUR, OIL AND HONEY, WHEREWITH I FED THEE, THOU HAST SET BEFORE THEM FOR A SWEET SAVOUR) That is, thou hast made thereof a מנחה, mana, the description of which is in Leviticus 2. AND IT CAME TO PASS) These things were done exactly so; nothing of these can be denied.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET PANEM MEVM QVEM DEDI TIBI) Panis nomine Hebræi omne id quo nutrimur intelligunt. Hæc generalıtas per subsequentia explicatur. SIMILAM, OLEVM ET MEL, QVIBVS ENV- TRIVI TE, POSVISTI IN CONSPECTV EORVM IN ODOREM SVAVITATIS) Id est, fecisti inde מנחה, μαναὰ, cujus descriptio Levit 2. ET FACTVM EST) Hæc omnino sic facta sunt; negari nihil horum potest.

## 16:20
Vers. 20. AND THOU HAST SACRIFICED TO THEM TO BE DEVOURED) Thou hast given them to be consumed by fire. IS THY FORNICATION A SMALL MATTER?) Do you think there is little wickedness in those sacrilegious rites?

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET IMMOLASTI EIS AD DEVORANDVM) I- gne consumendos dedisti. NVMQVID PARVA EST FORNICATIO TVA?) An parum sceleris esse putatis in sacrilegis illis sacris?

## 16:21
Vers. 21. THOU HAST SACRIFICED MY SONS, AND GIVEN THEM CONSECRATING) He repeats the same in other words, so that the indignity of the matter may the more cling to the mind.

Latin:

Vers. 21. IMMOLASTI FILIOS MEOS, ET DEDISTI IL- LOS CONSECRANS) Idem aliis verbis repetit, ut ma- gis hæreat animo rei indignitas.

## 16:24
Vers. 24. THOU HAST BUILT THEE A BROTHEL, AND HAST MADE A PROSTITUTE SIGN IN ALL STREETS.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ÆDIFICASTI TIBI LVPANAR, ET FE- CISTI SIGNVM PROSTIBVLVM IN CVNCTIS PLATEIS.

## 16:25
Vers. 25. AT EVERY HEAD OF THE WAY THOU HAST BUILT A SIGN OF THY PROSTITUTION) Such as that: 'At all the crossroads and alleys, she peels the noble descendants of Remus.' Truly, shameless women at last find the newest pleasure in the magnitude of their infamy, to use the words of Tacitus. Such was Messalina. 'Daring to prefer a mat to the Palatine bed, the Augusta, a harlot, to take on nocturnal hoods, she left with no more than one maid as a companion: but with a yellow wig hiding her black hair, she entered the warm brothel with an old patchwork quilt, and her own empty cell.'

By brothels understand altars raised here and there. Just as there were altars on the hills, so also were there brothels. Therefore he uses the word רמה and below גב, which suits both the comparison and the thing compared.

AND THOU HAST MADE THY BEAUTY ABOMINABLE) Thy beauty has made thee deformed.

AND THOU HAST DIVIDED THY FEET TO EVERY ONE THAT PASSED BY) The Latins would say, thou hast lifted thy feet: as we have noted elsewhere, the Greeks say διήγαγες τὰ σκέλη σε.

Latin:

Vers. 25. AD OMNE CAPVT VIÆ ÆDIFICASTI SIGNVM PROSTITVTIONIS TVÆ) Tale illud: Cunctis in triviis & angiportis Glubit Magnanimos Remi Nepotes. Nimitum fœminæ impudicæ tandem noviffimam volupta- tem habent in magnitudine infamiæ, ut Taciti utar verbis. Talis Messalina. Ausa Palatino tegetem præferre cubili, Sumere nocturnos meretrix Augusta cucullos, Linquebat comite ancilla non amplius una: Sed nigrum flavo crinem abscondente galero Intravit calidum veteri centone lupanar, Et cellam vacuam atque suam.

Per lupanaria aras intellige passim excitatas. Sicut in colli- bus erant aræ, ita & lupanaria. Propterea utitur voce רמה & infra גב quod & comparationi convenit, & rei comparatæ.

ET ABOMINABILEM FECISTIS DECOREM TVVM) Pulchritudo tua informem te fecit.

ET DIVISISTI PEDES TVOS OMNI TRANS- EVNT) Latini dicerent, sustulisti pedes: ut alibi notavimus Græci διήγαγες τὰ σκέλη σε.

## 16:26
Vers. 26. AND THOU HAST MULTIPLIED THY WHOREDOMS) Like her of whom Martial writes: Since she had given herself freely in all ways. Likewise: Thou deniest no one, Thais; but if thou art not ashamed of that: at least be ashamed, Thais, of denying nothing.

AND THOU HAST PLAYED THE WHORE ALSO WITH THE EGYPTIANS THY NEIGHBOURS, GREAT OF FLESH) That is, well-endowed. It signifies idolatry after the example of the Egyptians, who were great idolaters. See what we have said on chapters 30 and 31 of Isaiah.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET MVLTIPLICASTI FORNICATIONES TVAS) Ut illa de qua Martialis: Cum se dediffet omnibus modis largam. Item: Nulli, Thai, negas; sed si te non pudet istud: Hoc saltem pudeat, Thai, negare nihil.

ET FORNICATA ES CVM FILIIS ÆGYPTI VICINIS TVIS MAGNARVM CARNIVM) Id est, be- ne vasatis. Significatur Idololatria ad exemplar Ægyptio- rum, qui magni erant idololatræ. Vide quæ diximus ad E- saiam 30. 31. Capp.

## 16:27
V. 27. BEHOLD, THEREFORE I HAVE STRETCHED OUT MY HAND OVER THEE, AND HAVE DIMINISHED THINE ORDINARY FOOD) And when I stretched out my hand against thee, and diminished thy measure, that is, took away something of the opulence which thou wast abusing.

AND I WILL DELIVER THEE UNTO THE WILL OF THEM THAT HATE THEE

THE DAUGHTERS OF THE PHILISTINES) And I would leave thee to the will of thine enemies, the Philistines. He uses the feminine noun so that he may better continue the allegory. This, and what follows, happened in the times of Ahaz. See 2 Chron. 28:16, 18; 2 Kings 16:7, 10.

WHICH ARE ASHAMED OF THY LEWD WAY) They were ashamed. The Philistines, although evil, did not dare to imitate thy deeds: they remained with their own gods, Jer. 2:11.

Latin:

V. 27. ECCE EGO EXTENDAM MANVM MEAM SVPER TE, ET AVFERAM JVSTIFICATIONEM TVAM) Et cum ego manum meam contra te extenderem, & diminuerem dimensum tuum, Id est auferrem aliquid de opulentia, qua abutebaris.

ET DABO TE IN ANIMAS ODIENTIVM TE

FILIARVM PALÆSTINORVM) Et permitterem te arbi- trio inimicarum tuarum Palæstinarum. Fœmininum nomen usurpat, ut melius continuet allegoriam. Factum est hoc, & quod sequitur Achazi temporibus. vid. 2. Par. 28, 16. 18. 2. Reg. 16, 7. 10.

QVÆ ERVBESCVNT IN VIA TVA SCELE- RATA) Erubescebant. Palæstini, quamvis mali, tua facta imitari non audebant: manebant penes Deos suos, Jerem. 2. vers. 11.

## 16:28
Vers. 28.

THOU HAST PLAYED THE WHORE ALSO WITH THE ASSYRIANS) For they generally imitated the worship of those whose friendship they sought, as we have noted more than once regarding Isaiah.

AND YET THOU HAST NOT BEEN SATISFIED EVEN WITH THIS) Like Messalina: And wearied by men, she departed not yet satisfied.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

ET FORNICATA ES IN FILIIS ASSTRIO- RVM) Nam plerumque quorum amicitiam ambiebant, eorum cultus imitabantur, ut ad Esaiam plus semel nota- vimus.

ET POSTQVAM FORNICATA ES, NEC SIC ES SATIATA) Ut Messalina: Et lassata viris, nondum satiata recessit.

## 16:29
Vers. 29.

THOU HAST MOREOVER MULTIPLIED THY FORNICATION IN THE LAND OF CANAAN UNTO CHALDEA) He adds in the land of Canaan, so that it may be understood that this was done before the deportation: this began to happen already from the times of Jehoiachin.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ET MVLTIPLICASTI FORNICATIONEM TVAM IN TERRA CHANAAN CVM CHALDÆIS) Addit in terra Chanaan, ut intelligatur hoc factum ante deportationem : fieri hoc cœpit jam à Joachini tempo- ribus.

## 16:30
Vers. 30.

IN WHAT SHALL I CLEANSE THY HEART, SAITH THE LORD GOD) How infirm has thy heart become? That is, sick from lust.

OF A HARLOT AND WANTON WOMAN) In the Hebrew: of a free harlot: that is, one not having a husband. The LXX: παρρησιαζομένης.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

IN QVO MVNDABO COR TVVM, AIT DO- MINVS DEVS) Quam infirmum factum est cor tuum? Id est, ægrum præ libidine.

MVLIERIS MERETRICIS ET PROCACIS) In Hebræo: meretricis liberæ: id est, maritum non habentis. LXX. παρρησιαζομένης.

## 16:31
Ver. 31.

AND THOU HAST NOT BECOME AS A HARLOT INCREASING THE PRICE BY DISDAIN) As a harlot, who makes herself cheap for the sake of payment. Something must be pardoned to those who prostitute themselves, so that they may have wherewith to live. Terence: My Pamphilus, you see her beauty and her age; nor is it hidden from you how both these things are now useful to her, both for modesty and for protecting her estate.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

NEC FACTA ES QVASI MERETRIX FASTI- DIO AVGENS PRETIVM) Quasi meretrix, quæ vilem se facit ob mercedem. Condonandum aliquid iis, quæ se vul- gant, ut habeant unde vivant. Terentius: Mi Pamphile hujus formam atque ætatem vides; Nec clam te est, quam illi utræque res nunc utiles, Et ad pudicitiam, & ad tutandam rem sient.

## 16:32
Ver. 32.

BUT AS AN ADULTEROUS WOMAN, WHO BRINGS IN STRANGERS OVER HER HUSBAND) For her husband: by whom she is loved and well provided for, as this Chaldean [interpreter] says.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

SED QVASI MVLIER ADVLTERA, QVÆ SVPER VIRVM SVVM INDVCIT ALIENOS) Pro vi- ro suo : à quo diligitur ac bene educatur, ut hic Chaldæus.

## 16:33
Ver. 33.

BUT THOU HAST GIVEN REWARDS) Like that old woman in the Plutus of Aristophanes.

THOU GAVEST GIFTS TO THEM) He understands great gifts sent to the Egyptians, Assyrians, and Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

TV AVTEM DEDISTI MERCEDES) Vt anus illa in Pluto Aristophanis.

DONA DABAS EIS) Magna munera intelligit mis- sa ad Ægyptios, Assyrios & Chaldæos.

## 16:34
Ver. 34. THAT THEY MIGHT ENTER UNTO THEE) Into thy bedchamber.

AND AFTER THEE THERE SHALL NOT BE FORNICATION) Of such abandoned lust.

Latin:

Vers. 34. VT INTRARENT AD TE) In cubile tuum.

ET POST TE NON ERIT FORNICATIO) Tam projectæ libidinis.

## 16:36
Ver. 36.

BECAUSE THY BRASS WAS POURED OUT) Thy filthiness was poured out: That is, poison, as Virgil speaks of mares.

نجس is filthiness to the Arabs. Compare Jer. 13, 27.

THY SHAME IS REVEALED) Thy private parts are exposed.

UPON THY LOVERS) Before thy lovers.

AND UPON THE IDOLS OF THINE ABOMINATIONS) Because of thine abominable idols.

IN THE BLOOD OF THY CHILDREN, WHOM THOU HAST GIVEN UNTO THEM) And just as thou hast given the blood of thy children unto them: Namely, I also will give thy blood, as follows. Here begins the first apodosis of the comparison.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

QVIA EFFVSVM EST ÆS TVVM) Effusa est spur- citia tua : Id est virus, ut loquitur Virgilius de equabus.

نجس Arabibus spurcitia. Confer Jer. 13, 27.

REVELATA EST IGNOMINIA TVA) Fatuere partes pudendæ.

SVPER AMATORES TVOS) Coram amatoribus.

ET SVPER IDOLA ABOMINATIONVM TVA- RVM) Propter Idola tua abominanda.

IN SANGVINE FILIORVM TVORVM, QVOS DEDISTI EIS) Ac sicut sanguinem filiorum tuorum dedisti eis: Nempe & ego tuum sanguinem dabo, ut sequitur. Hic incipit prima απόδοσις comparationis.

## 16:37
Ver. 37.

I WILL GATHER ALL THY LOVERS) The Chaldeans with the Assyrian auxiliaries.

WITH ALL WHOM THOU HAST HATED) The Edomites and Philistines.

AND I WILL DISCOVER THY SHAME BEFORE THEM) I will expose thee to public infamy: παραδειγματίσω σε.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

CONGREGABO OMNES AMATORES TVOS) Chaldæos adjutoribus Assyriis.

CVM VNIVERSIS QVOS ODERAS) Idumæis & Palæstinis.

ET NVDABO IGNOMINIAM TVAM CORAM EIS) Publicæ infamiæ te exponam : παραδειγματίσω σε.

## 16:38
Ver. 38.

AND I WILL JUDGE THEE BY THE JUDGMENTS OF ADULTERESSES AND THOSE WHO SHED BLOOD) That is, partly thou shalt be stoned, partly thou shalt be slaughtered by the sword, as follows below in 40. We have spoken of adulteresses being stoned at certain times at John 8, v. 5. Jerusalem was stoned when stones were cast into it from the engines of the Chaldeans. The punishment of the sword is proper to murderers, such as they had been against their own children.

I WILL GIVE THEE INTO THE BLOOD OF FURY AND ZEAL) That is: into the punishment, such as jealous husbands exercise upon an adulteress. See above 14, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

ET JVDICABO TE JVDICIIS ADVLTERA- RVM ET EFFVNDENTIVM SANGVINEM) Id est, partim lapidaberis, partim gladio trucidaberis, ut sequitur infra 40. Lapidatas aliquibus temporibus adulteras dixi- mus ad Joannem 8. v. 5. Lapidata est Jerusalem, cum ex ba- sistis Chaldæorum saxa in eam jacta sunt. Gladii pœna propria homicidarum, quales illi in liberos suos fuerant.

DABO TE IN SANGVINEM FVRORIS ET ZELI) Id est: in pœnam, qualem zelotypi mariti in adulteram exercent. Vid. supra 14, 19.

## 16:39
Ver. 39. THEY SHALL DESTROY THY LUPANAR) The temple from which thou hast made an idol-shrine.

AND THEY SHALL DEMOLISH THY BROTHEL) In the Hebrew: thy high places: See above, 24.

AND THEY SHALL STRIP THEE OF THY GARMENTS) They shall pull down thy walls.

AND THEY SHALL TAKE AWAY THE VESSELS OF THY ORNAMENT) The vessels of the temple, 2 Kings 25, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 39. DESTRVENT LVFANAR TVVM) Tem- plum ex quo Idolium fecisti.

ET DEMOLIENTVR PROSTIBVLVM TVVM) In Hebræo : excelsa tua: Vid. supra, 24.

ET DENVDABVNT TE VESTIMENTIS TVIS) Muros tibi detrahent.

ET AVFERENT VASA DECORIS TVI) Vafa templi 2. Reg. 25, 13.

## 16:41
Verf. 41. AND THEY SHALL BURN THY HOUSES WITH FIRE) As the law commands to be done to a city of idolaters. Deut. 13, 16.

AND THEY SHALL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS UPON THEE IN THE SIGHT OF MANY WOMEN) That is, of the neighboring nations.

AND THOU SHALT GIVE HIRE NO MORE) There will be nothing from which thou mayest give.

Latin:

Verf. 41. ET COMBVRENT DOMOS TVAS IGNI) Ut lex fieri præcipit in urbem Idololatrarum. Deut. 13, 16.

ET FACIENT IN TE JVDICIA IN OCVLIS MV- LIERVM PLVRIMARVM) Id est, vicinarum gentium.

ET MERCEDES VLTRA NON DABIS) Non erit unde des.

## 16:42
Verf. 42. AND MY INDIGNATION SHALL REST IN THEE, AND MY JEALOUSY SHALL DEPART FROM THEE, AND I WILL BE QUIET, AND WILL BE NO MORE ANGRY) That is, with these punishments I shall satisfy my wrath.

Latin:

Verf. 42. ET REQVIESCET INDIGNATIO MEA IN TE, ET AVFERETVR ZELUS MEUS A TE, ET QVIESCAM, NE IRASCAR AMPLIVS) Id est, istis pœnis exsatiabo iram meam.

## 16:43
Verf. 43. I HAVE RECOMPENSED THY WAYS UPON THY HEAD) Thou hast despised me, I will despise thee: thou hast brought grief upon me, and I will bring it upon thee.

AND I HAVE NOT DONE ACCORDING TO THY WICKEDNESS IN ALL THINE ABOMINATIONS) That is, concerning idols. I have not done as much as the sins demanded. Jerome reads עשׂיתי, as also the LXX. Others read עשׂית, and they explain it: Thou hast not made a thought (for זמה signifies both a thought and a crime) concerning all thine abominations, namely, to repent. Thus the Chaldean.

Latin:

Verf. 43. IRAS TVAS IN CAPITE TVO DEDI) Sprevissti me, ego spernam te: dolorem mihi intulisti, & ego tibi inferam.

ET NON FECI JUXTA SCELERA TVA IN OMNIBVS ABOMINATIONIBVS TVIS) Id est, circa idola. Non feci quantum peccata exigebant. Legit Hieron. עשׂיתי, ut & LXX. Alii עשׂית, & exponunt: Non fecisti cogitationem (nam זמה & cogitationem & fcelus fignificat) de omnibus abominationibus tuis, nempe ad resipiscendum. Sic Chaldæus.

## 16:44
Verf. 44. AS IS THE MOTHER, SO IS HER DAUGHTER) Thus Juvenal:

- - Do you expect that the daughter of Larga will not be an adulteress, who will never be able to name her mother's adulterers so quickly nor string them together in such a rush, that she does not take a breath thirteen times?

He calls the Canaanites the mother, and other nations, who had held the same land before, as we said above 16, 3.

Latin:

Verf. 44. SICVT MATER ITA ET FILIA EJVS) Sic Juvenalis:

- - Exspectas ut non sit adultera Largæ Filia, quæ nunquam maternos dicere mœchos Tam cito nec tanto poterit contexere cursu, Ut non terdecies respiret?

Matrem vocat Chananæos, & alias gentes, quæ terram ean- dem ante tenuerant, ut diximus supra 16, 3.

## 16:45
Vers. 45. WHO HATH CAST OFF HER HUSBAND, God, whom they had learned of from Noah.

AND HER SONS) Whom she gave to death in honor of Saturn. For that was originally the custom of the Phoenicians, i.e., the Canaanites.

AND YOU ARE THE SISTER OF YOUR SISTERS, also similar in character to those whom you touch by blood.

WHO HAVE CAST OFF THEIR HUSBANDS) They are sisters of Sodom, and the Ammonites and Moabites, whose origin is from Sodom: And Samaria, the chief city of the ten tribes. The Ammonites and Moabites had received the Chaldean gods in place of their ancient gods Moloch and Chemosh, and the Samaritans in place of their calves, which however profited them nothing. See Jerem. 48. 49. Moreover, the Samaritans were kinsmen of the Jews through Jacob, the Ammonites and Moabites through Terah.

Latin:

Vers. 45. QVÆ PROJECTT VIRVM SVVM, Deum, quem a Noe didicerant.

ET FILIOS SVOS) Quos neci dedit in honorem Sa- turni. Is enim primitus mos Phœnicum, i. e. Chananæorum.

ET SOROR SORORVM TVARVM ES TV, E- tiam ingenio similis iis quos attingis sanguine.

QVÆ PROJECERVNT VIROS SVOS) Sorores funt Sodoma, & Ammonitæ & Moabitæ, quorum origo è Sodomis: Et Samaria princeps civitas decem tribuum. Am- monitæ & Moabitæ pro veteribus diis suis Molocho & Cha- moso, Samaritæ pro vitulis suis deos Chaldæos receperant, quod tamen ipsis nihil profuit. Vide Jerem. 48. 49. Erant autem Samaritæ cognati Judæorum ex Jacobo, Ammonitæ & Moabitæ ex Thare.

## 16:46
Vers. 46. YOUR ELDER SISTER SAMARIA, SHE AND HER DAUGHTERS) Smaller towns, whose kings dwelt in Samaria. She is called the elder sister who is connected by closer blood, as the ten tribes, who are from Jacob: Sister; that is, a kinswoman, the younger, who is more remote by blood.

WHO DWELL AT YOUR LEFT HAND) That is, to the North. A Hebrew idiom. This is said with reference to the temple, if you look from there toward the rising sun.

WHO DWELLS AT THE RIGHT HAND) That is, to the South. See Gen. 13, 3. and the Chaldeans there.

SODOM AND HER DAUGHTERS) The Ammonites and Moabites.

Latin:

Vers. 46. SOROR TVA MAJOR SAMARIA, IPSA ET FILIÆ EJVS) Minora oppida, quorum Reges Samariæ habitabant. Soror major dicitur, quæ propiori sanguine connectitur, ut decem tribus, quæ ex Jacobo: Soror; id est, consanguinea, minor, quæ remotior sanguine.

QVÆ HABITANT AD SINISTRAM TVAM) Id est, ad Septentrionem Locutio Hebraica. Dicitur hoc ra- tione templi, si inde solem orientalem respicias.

QVÆ HABITAT A DEXTRIS) Id est ad Meri- diem. Vide Genes. 13, 3. & ibi Chaldæos.

SODOMA ET FILIÆ EJVS) Ammonitis & Moa- bitis.

## 16:47
Vers. 47. NOR HAVE YOU DONE ACCORDING TO THEIR WICKEDNESSES A LITTLE LESS) Nor have you done according to their wickedness: This would have been very little: Supply for yourself: Thus the Chaldean here.

YOU HAVE DONE ALMOST MORE WICKED THINGS) You have done more wicked things: For that 'almost' has been transferred here from the previous clause.

Latin:

Vers. 47. NEQVE SECVNDVM SCELERA EO- RVM FECISTI PAVX'LLUM M. NVS) Neque secundum scelera earum fecisti: Perpaulum hoc fuisset: Supple tibi: Ita hic Chaldæus.

PÆNE SCELERATIORA FECISTI) Sceleratiora fecisti: Nam illud pæne ex superiori membro huc transla- tum est.

## 16:49
V. 49 BEHOLD THIS WAS THE INIQUITY OF SODOM YOUR SISTER PRIDE) The peculiar vice of the Ammonites and Moabites Isa. 16, 6. Jerem. 48, 27. 49, 21. If he had been dealing with the ancient Sodomites, he would have added their nefarious lusts.

FULNESS OF BREAD AND ABUNDANCE AND IDLENESS) That is, pride born from the fertility of the land, an abundance of all things, and long peace. Jerem. 48, 11. 49, 4. Philo in his book on Abraham, where he treats of the Sodomites: ὕπαγ φιλῶ, κόρ ὕβριν ἐγέννησε.

AND THEY DID NOT STRETCH OUT THEIR HAND TO THE NEEDY AND POOR) Namely, to the Jews driven there. See what was said at Isaiah 16, 2. 36. Jerem. 48, 27. 49, 1.

Latin:

V. 49 ECCE HÆC FVIT INIQVITAS SODOMÆ SORORIS TVÆ SUPERBIA) Proprium vitium Amoni- tarum & Moabitarum Isa. 16, 6. Jerem. 48, 27. 49, 21. Si de veteribus Sodomitis egisset, adjecisset nefarias libidines.

SATVRITAS PANIS ET ABVNDANTIA ET QTIVM) Id est, superbia nata ex fertilitate terræ, rerum omnium copia, longa pace. Jerem. 48, 11. 49, 4. Philo in libro de Abrahamo, ubi de Sodomitis agit: ὕπαγ φιλῶ, κόρ ὕβριν ἐγέννησε.

ET MANVM EGENO ET PAVPERI NON FORRIGEBANT) Nempe Judæis illuc depulsis. Vide quæ dicta ad Esaiam 16, 2. 36. Jerem. 48, 27. 49, 1.

## 16:50
Vers. 50. AND THEY WERE LIFTED UP) They became puffed up by prosperous circumstances.

AND I REMOVED THEM AS YOU SAW) That is, many of them through Shalmaneser. See Isa. 15 & 16 & what is said there.

Latin:

Vers. 50. ET ELEVATÆ SVNT) Intumuerunt rebus fecundis.

ET ABSTVLI EAS SICUT VIDISTI) Id est, mul- tos eorum per Salmanasarem. Vide Esa. 15. & 16. & ibi dicta.

## 16:51
Ver. 51.

YOU HAVE JUSTIFIED YOUR SISTERS) By comparison with you, you made them appear righteous. Jer. 2, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 51.

JVSTIFICASTI SORORES TVAS) Comparatio- ne tui fecisti eas probas videri. Jer. 2, 5.

## 16:52
Ver. 52. BEAR YOUR CONFUSION) I wish you to bear punishment joined with ignominy.

YOU WHO HAVE SURPASSED YOUR SISTERS IN YOUR SINS) In the Hebrew: you who have anticipated judgment against your sister. That is: you said concerning the ten tribes that they were justly punished. See Luke 13, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 52. PORTA CONFUSIONEM TVAM) Volo feras pœnam cum ignominia conjunctam.

QVÆ VICISTI SORORES TVAS PECCATIS TVIS) In Hebræo: quæ judicium præoccupasti adversus soro- rem tuam. Idest: dixisti de decem tribus juste punitas, Vide Luc. 13, 2.

## 16:53
V. 53. AND I WILL TURN BACK, RESTORING THEM BY THE CONVERSION OF SODOM WITH HER DAUGHTERS, AND BY THE CONVERSION OF SAMARIA, AND HER DAUGHTERS, AND I WILL TURN BACK YOUR CAPTIVITY IN THE MIDST OF THEM) And I will cause their captives to return, namely the captives of Sodom, that is, of its offspring: And the captives of Samaria, that is, of its offspring, & the captives who from yours were taken captive equally with them. You will indeed return at some time, but also with you will return the Ammonites & Moabites, & some from the ten tribes, as many as shall have corrected themselves. See Jerem. 48, 47. & 49, 30.

Latin:

V. 53. ET CONVERTAM RESTITUENS EAS CON- VERSIONE SODOMORVM CVM FILIABVS SUIS, ET, CONVERSIONE SAMARIÆ, ET FILIARVM EJUS, ET CONVERTAM REVERSIONEM TVAM IN MEDIO EARUM) Et redire faciam captivos illorum, captivos scilicet Sodoma, id est propaginum ejus: Et captivos Sa- mariæ, id est propaginum ejus, & captivos qui ex vestris capti funt pariter cum ipsis. Redibitis quidem aliquando, fed & vobiscum redibunt Ammonitæ & Moabitæ, & quidam ex decem tribubus, quotquot se correxerint. Vide Jerem. 48, 47. & 49, 30.

## 16:54
Ver. 54. THAT YOU MAY BEAR YOUR IGNOMINY, AND BE CONFOUNDED IN ALL THAT YOU HAVE DONE, CONSOLING THEM) That is, that you may be ashamed to be held equal to those whom you so greatly despised, & who in long exile will have consolation from you.

Latin:

Vers. 54. VT PORTES IGNOMINIAM, ET CON- FUNDARIS IN OMNIBVS QVÆ FECISTI CON- SOLANS EAS) Id est, ut te pudeat parem te haberi iis, quos tantopere contempsisti, & qui in longo exilio ex te habebunt solatium.

## 16:55
Ver. 55.

AND YOUR SISTER SODOM, AND HER DAUGHTERS SHALL RETURN TO THEIR ANTIQUITY: AND SAMARIA AND HER DAUGHTERS SHALL RETURN TO THEIR ANTIQUITY: AND YOU AND YOUR DAUGHTERS SHALL RETURN TO YOUR ANTIQUITY) When your sister Sodom, that is, her offspring, shall return to the places of their origin: & Samaria, that is, her offspring, shall return to the places of their origin: then also you, that is, your offspring, shall return to the places of your origin. Not before, lest you be pleased with yourself.

It is not indicated that Sodom itself is to be converted, but nations similar to it. See Osiander in the paraphrase at this place.

Latin:

Vers. 55.

ET SOROR TVA SODOMA, ET FILIÆ EJVS REVERTENIVR AD ANTIQVITATEM SVAM: ET SAMARIA ET FILIÆ EJVS REVERTENTVR AD ANTIQVITATEM SVAM: ET TV ET FILIÆ TVÆ REVERTEMINI AD ANTIQVITATEM VESTRAM) Cum soror tua Sodoma, id est, propagines ejus, ad loca originis suæ revertentur: & Samaria, id est propagines ejus, revertentur ad loca suæ originis: tunc & tu, id est propagines tuæ, reverten- tur ad loca suæ originis. Non ante, ne tibi placeas.

Non indicatur ipsam Sodomam converten- dam, sed gentes ei similes. Vid. Osiander in para- phras. ad h. l.

## 16:56
Ver. 56. BUT WAS NOT SODOM YOUR SISTER HEARD IN YOUR MOUTH IN THE DAY OF YOUR PRIDE) You held the Ammonites & Moabites expelled from their places in such contempt that you did not even deem them worthy to be named.

Latin:

Vers. 56. NON FVIT AVTEM SODOMA SOROR TVA AVDITA IN ORE SVO IN DIE SVPERBIÆ TVÆ) Adeo despectui habuisti Ammonitas & Moabitas de suis locis expulsos, ut ne dignos quidem arbitrareris, quos nominares.

## 16:57
Ver. 57. BEFORE YOUR MALICE WAS REVEALED) Before the punishment of your malice appeared.

AS AT THIS TIME TO THE REPROACH OF THE DAUGHTERS OF SYRIA, AND OF ALL THE DAUGHTERS OF THE PHILISTINES ROUND ABOUT THEE, WHICH COMPASS THEE ROUND ABOUT) Which now shall so come to pass, that as thou hast despised the Ammonites and Moabites, so shall both the Syrians and Philistines, who are clearly ἀμόφυλοι, hold thee in contempt.

Latin:

Vers. 57. ANTEQVAM REVELARETVR MALI- TIA TVA) Antequam malitiæ tuæ pœna appareret.

SICUT HOC TEMPORE IN OPPROBRIVM FI- LIARVM STRIÆ, ET CVNCTARVM IN CIRCVL- TV TVO FILIORVM PALÆSTINARVM, QVÆ AM- BIVNT TE PER GTRVM) Quod nunc ita fiet, ut ficut tu sprevisti Ammonitas & Moabitas, ita te despectui sint ha- bituri tam Syri quam Philisthini, qui sunt plane ἀμόφυλοι.

## 16:58
Vers. 58. THY WICKEDNESS AND THY IGNOMINY THOU HAST BORNE) in the dual number. You bear the ignominy, which is the punishment of wickedness.

Latin:

Vers. 58. SCELVS TVVM ET IGNOMINIAM TVAM TV PORTASTI) in diæ duoir. Portatis ignomiam, quæ est sceleris pœna.

## 16:59
Vers. 59.

AND I WILL DO UNTO THEE AS THOU HAST DESPISED THE OATH, TO MAKE VOID THE COVENANT) As thou hast despised the covenant by breaking it, so will I despise thee.

Latin:

Vers. 59.

ET FACIAM TIBI SICUT DESPEXISTI JU- RAMENTVM, VT IRRITVM FACERES PACTVM) Sicut tu despexisti pactum infringendo, sic ego te despi- ciam.

## 16:60
Vers. 60. AND I WILL REMEMBER) Nevertheless I will remember at some time.

AND I WILL ESTABLISH UNTO THEE AN EVERLASTING COVENANT) I will renew with thee a covenant that will endure for a long time. Neh. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 60. ET RECORDABOR EGO) Attamen recor- dabor aliquando.

ET SVCITABO TIBI PACTVM SEMPITER- NVM) Renovabo tecum fœdus diu duraturum. Neh. 10.

## 16:61
Vers. 61. AND THOU SHALT REMEMBER THY WAYS) When thou shalt have remembered thy ways. And 'et' for 'cum' is frequent.

AND SHALT BE CONFOUNDED) And shalt do penance.

WHEN THOU SHALT RECEIVE THY SISTERS GREATER THAN THEE WITH THY LESSER) That is, thou shalt return in their company.

AND I WILL GIVE THEM UNTO THEE FOR DAUGHTERS) I will cause them to obey thee, as daughters obey a mother. For the Jews made many of the Ammonitesses and Moabitesses their own by arms, as we have observed elsewhere from Josephus 10, 12, and from 1 Maccab. 5. And Samaria was given to them, Jos. 13, 5.

BUT NOT BY THY COVENANT) By metonymy for that which thou wouldst say: not that thou on thy part didst stand by the covenant. So the Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 61. ET RECORDABERIS VIARVM TVA- NVM) Vibi turecordata fueris viarum tuarum. Et pro cum fatis frequens.

ET CONFVNDERIS) Et pœnitentiam egeris.

CVM RECEPERIS SORORES TVAS TE MA- JORES CVM MINORIBVS TVIS) Id est, in illarum comitatu redieris.

ET DABO EAS TIBI IN FILIAS) Faciam ut tibi pareant, sicut filiæ matri. Nam & Ammonitidos & Moabi- tidos multa Judæi sua armis fecerunt, ut alibi observavimus ex Josepho 10, 12. & ex 1. Maccab. 5. Et Samaria ipsis do- nata est Jos. 13, 5.

SED NON EX PACTO TVO) Μετωνυμίᾳ pro eo quod diceres: non quod tu ex tua parte pacto steteris. Ita Chaldæus.

## 16:62
Vers. 62. AND I WILL ESTABLISH MY COVENANT WITH THEE) Therefore I will renew the covenant, because thou didst not stand by the covenant.

Latin:

Vers. 62. ET SVSCITABO EGO PACTVM MEUM TECVM) Ideo novabo fœdus, quia fœderi non stetisti.

## 16:63
Ver. 63. THAT THOU MAYEST REMEMBER AND BE CONFOUNDED, AND NEVER OPEN THY MOUTH ANY MORE BECAUSE OF THY SHAME) That thou mayest acknowledge perpetually how greatly thou hast sinned,

WHEN I AM PACIFIED TOWARD THEE FOR ALL THAT THOU HAST DONE) After I shall have shown, by entering into a new covenant, that I forgive those things so grievous and great.

The everlasting covenant is rashly explained as that which lasts a long time in verse 60. And Grotius acknowledges in the last verse that it concerns the new covenant. Which is perpetual and truly everlasting. Therefore our own [commentators] have expressed the sense more happily, from whom we cite Osiander: I will remember my covenant, which I made with thee in the days of thy youth, when I brought thee out of Egypt and promised thee the land of Canaan,

and in turn you would bind your obedience and faith to me. Therefore I will not utterly cast you away: but rather I will strike a covenant with you anew: and I will raise up or set up for you an everlasting covenant: I will institute a New Testament, in which (on account of my only-begotten Son) I will receive you into grace and make you an heir of eternal life. (Now the New Testament, whose author is the Son of God Jesus Christ, is truly eternal: because no other is to be expected. And the vigor of this Testament will endure for all eternity: for God will never change anything in it) And you will then remember your ways, i.e., your past impious life, and you will be confounded before yourself (For the pious, when they remember their committed sins and their former impiety, are confounded and give glory to God) This (I say) will happen, when you shall have received at some time your sisters who are older than you, with your younger ones: i.e., when you will gather to yourself many nations, which together with you will embrace the Gospel of Christ (for he says older and younger sisters, (not older and younger) so that it may be understood that very many and various nations pertain to the kingdom of Christ) For I will give them to you as daughters, but not by your covenant. I.e., You will embrace the converted nations with great love, not only as sisters, but also as far dearest daughters. But that covenant, of which they will become participants together with you, will not be the Old Testament, which was once covenanted with you, but a new one. (For the old covenant of the Israelite people promised salvation only to those who would satisfy the divine Law: but the New Testament, (in which converted Jews and peoples gathered from the nations are saved) promises eternal life, not to those working, but to those believing in him who justifies the ungodly, Rom. 4. But while he calls the converted nations daughters, he admonishes Christians that they should embrace one another with sincere love) And I will raise up or set up (as I said) my covenant with you: and you will know or acknowledge, because (for which) I am the Lord your God, a most kind father: who deals with the elect not according to merits, but according to my mercy: That you may remember with shame your past life, and be confounded before yourself, and it may not be lawful for you to open your mouth anymore, because of your confusion: you will not then boast of any of your merits: but you will rather confess that you have deserved eternal damnation: When I shall have been appeased toward you in all things which you have done: when I shall have forgiven you all your sins through faith on account of Christ, says the Lord God. The Vinarienses agree, B. Hülsemann. The Belgian, as also most Papist Interpreters.

Latin:

Vers. 63. VT REÇORDERIS ET CONFVNDARIS, ET NON SIT TIBI VLTRA APERIRE OS PRÆ CONFVSIONE TVA) Vt agnoscas perpetuo, quanta pec- caveris,

CVM PLACATVS TIBI FVERO IN OMNIBVS QVÆ FECISTI) Postquam novum fœdus ineundo often- dam me illa tam gravia ac magna condonare.

Pactum fempiternum temere explicatur de diu duraturo verf. 60. Et agnoscit Grotius Vers. ult. de novo fœdere agi. Quod perpetuum ac vere sempiternum est. Sensum ergo felicius expresse- runt nostri, è quibus Osiandrum adducimus: Re- cordabor ego pacti mei, quod olim pepigi tecum in diebus adolescentiæ tuæ, cum te educerem ex Æ- gypto tibique terram Chanaan promitterem,

& vicissim tu mihi obedientiam & fidem tuam ob- stringeret. Itaque non plane te abjiciam : sed de novo potius fœdus tecum feriam : & suscitabo seu erigam tibi pactum sempiternum : Novum Testamentum insti- tuam, in quo (propter unigenitum Filium meum) te in gratiam recipiam teque vitæ æternæ hæredem fa- ciam. (Novum autem Testamentum, cujus autor est Filius Dei Jesus Christus, vere æternum est: quia nullum aliud est expectandum. Et hujus Testa- menti vigor durabit in omnem æternitatem : ne- que enim Deus quicquam in eo unquam mutabit) Et recordaberis tunc viarum tuarum, i. e. anteactæ impiæ vitæ, & confunderis coram te ipsa (Pii enim cum commissorum peccatorum, & pristinæ impie- tatis suæ recordantur, confunduntur, & Deo glo- riam dant) Hoc (inquam) fiet, cum receperis aliquan- do ad te sorores tuas te majores, cum minoribus tuis: i. e. cum tibi multas gentes aggregabis, quæ una tecum Evangelion Christi amplectentur (sorores enim majores & minores, (non majorem & mino- rem) dicit : ut intelligatur, plurimas & varias gen- tes pertinere ad regnum Christi) Etenim dabo eas tibi in filias, sed non ex pacto tuo. I. e. Tu complecteris gentes conversas magno amore, non modo ut so- rores, sed etiam ut filias longe charissimas. Pactum autem illud, cujus una tecum participes fient, non erit Testamentum Vetus, quod olim tecum pactum fuit, sed novum. (Vetus enim pactum populi I- sraëlitici promittebat salutem non nisi iis, qui Legi divinæ satisfacerent : Novum vero Testamentum, (in quo conversi Judæi, & populi ex gentibus colle- cti salvantur) promittit vitam æternam, non ope- rantibus, sed credentibus in eum, qui justificat im- pium, Rom. 4. Dum autem gentes conversas filias vocat, admonet Christianos, ut se invicem syncero amore complectantur) Et suscitabo seu erigam ego (ut dixi) pactum meum tecum : & scies sive agno- sces, quia (pro quod) ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, benignissimus pater : qui non pro meritis, sed juxta misericordiam meam cum electis ago : Ut recorde- ris cum pudore antedeactæ tuæ vitæ, & confunda- ris coram te ipsa, & non sit tibi ultra fas aperire os tuum, præ confusione tua : non jactabis tunc ulla tua merita : fateberis autem potius te æternam damnationem esse commeritam : Cum placatus tibi fuero in omnibus, quæ fecisti : quando tibi per fidem propter Christum remisero omnia peccata tua, ait Dominus Deus. Consonant Vinarienses, B. Hülse- mann. Belgici, ut & Pontificii plerique Interpretes.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

By the parable of the two eagles and the planted and growing vine, which will not prosper, it is declared that the King of Babylon, having transferred King Jeconiah to Babylon, appointed Zedekiah in his place, who, having broken the covenant and fleeing to the King of Egypt, is to be delivered into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar and to be led away to Babylon: with the addition of a promise concerning Christ as a shoot to be planted on the mountain, which will bear fruit and extend itself greatly.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII.

Per parabolam de duabus aquilis & plantata, & crescente vinea, quæ non prosperabitur, declaratur, quod Rex Babylonis translato in Babyloniam rege Jechonia, Zedekiam pro eo constituit, qui rupto fœdere ad Regem Ægypti transfugiens tradendus in manus Nebucadnezaris, & traducendus in Baby- lonem : addita promissione ad Christo ceu surculo in monte plantando fructus laturo, seque valde extensuro.

## 17:2
Ver. 2.

PROPOSE A RIDDLE) αἴνιγ. Such as that one in Hesiod concerning the hawk. You have this passage in Greek in Chrysostom 19, on the statues.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

PROPONE ÆNIGMA) αἴνιγ. Qualis ille apud He- siodum de accipitre. Habes hunc locum Græce apud Chry- sostomum 19. de statuis.

## 17:3
Ver. 3.

A GREAT EAGLE) Nebuchadnezzar, as can be seen in Jer. 48, 40. 49, 22.

OF GREAT WINGS) Having great forces with him, Jer. 48, 4.

LONGO MEMBRORVM DVCTV) μακρὸς τῇ ἐκτάσει. LXX. אבר members to the Chaldeans. All the interpreters followed this, not the Hebrew meaning, which signifies a wing: for that had been fated to happen. It signifies that Nebuchadnezzar ruled widely. PLENA PLVMIS ET VARIETATE) In the Hebrew: full of feathers, in which there was variety. Having various peoples under him in language and dress.

VENIT AD LIBANVM) By the name of Lebanon, both the temple and the city of Jerusalem are called, because it consisted almost entirely of the cedars of Lebanon. It is agreed among the Jews that the temple is signified by the name of Lebanon, as Eusebius says in his demonstration.

TVLIT MEDVLLAM CEDRI) צמרת, which the Chaldean translates as branch. For that is what עברנא is. He understands the good part of the people, 2 Kings 24:14.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

AQVILA GRANDIS) Nabuchodonosor, ut vide- re est Jer. 48, 40. 49, 22.

MAGNARVM ALARVM) Magnas secum copias habens, Jer. 48, 4.

LONGO MEMBRORVM DVCTV) μακρὸς τῇ ἐκτάσει. LXX. אבר membram Chaldæis, Hoc secuti sunt interpretes omnes, non Hebræum significationem, quæ a- lam significat: Id enim fatis præcesserat. Significatur Na- buchodonosor late imperasse. PLENA PLVMIS ET VARIETATE) In Hebræo: plena plumis, in quibus erat varietas. Varios lingua & ha- bitu sub se populos habens.

VENIT AD LIBANVM) Libani nomine vocatur & templum & urbs Hierosolyma, quod ferme tota ex ce- dris Libani constaret. Libani nomine templum significari constat apud Judæos, ut ait in demonstratione Eusebius.

TVLIT MEDVLLAM CEDRI) צמרת, quod Chaldæus vertit ramum. Id enim est עברנא. Intelligit bonam partem de populo, 2.Reg. 24, 14.

## 17:4
Vers. 4.

SVMMITATEM FRONDIVM EJVS AVVLSIT) The head of its tender branches. King Jeconiah, only 18 years old.

TRANSPORTAVIT EAM IN TERRAM CHANAAN) Into the land of merchants. For such is Babylon, navigable by the greatest rivers: כנען is translated as merchants, Is. 23:8.

IN VRBE NEGOTIATORVM) I praise those who translated it also as of the spice-merchants. For to the Chaldeans רכליס properly signifies that. Babylon was full of spices from trade with the Arabs, Persians, and Indians. From there the Babylonians made incense for their gods most lavishly, so that the whole city seemed to smoke.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

SVMMITATEM FRONDIVM EJVS AVVLSIT) Caput tenerorum ramorum ejus. Jechoniam Regem natum annos tantum 18.

TRANSPORTAVIT EAM IN TERRAM CHA- NAAN) In terram mercatoriam. Talis enim Babylonia, maximis amnibus navigabilis: כנען vertitur ἐμπορῶν, Es. 23, 8.

IN VRBE NEGOTIATORVM) Laudo, qui verte- runt & aromatariorum. Nam Chaldæis רכליס id proprie significat. Plena autem aromatum erat Babylon ex com- mercio cum Arabibus, Persis & Indis. Inde suffitus diis lar- gissime faciebant Babylonii, ita ut urbs tota fumare vide- retur.

## 17:5
Vers. 5. ET TVLIT DE SEMINE TERRÆ) Zedekiah, a man of royal stock.

ET POSVIT ILLVD IN TERRA PRO SEMINE) To make a sowing: the Chaldean here. So that the royal family might endure through him.

VT FIRMARET RADICEM) It is not in the Hebrew.

SVPER AQVAS MVLTAS) Beside many waters. In the best soil, Eccl. 40:1.

IN SVPERFICIE POSVIT ILLVD) צפצפה, which is to look at, he believed to be the doubled form מצפצפה, as also the LXX, who translate it as ἐπιβλεπόμενον. Thus the Babylonian placed Zedekiah, so that he might be looked at, that is, that he might indeed be looked up to by the Jews, but that he might depend upon him himself, as follows. صفصاف to the Arabs, and צפצפה to the Chaldeans is a kind of willow. Hence the sense would be: he placed him as if he were a willow. For willows love waters, Plin. 16:19, Ps. 137:2, Is. 44:4.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET TVLIT DE SEMINE TERRÆ) Sede- cia m Regiæ stirpis virum.

ET POSVIT ILLVD IN TERRA PRO SEMI- NE) Ad sementem faciendam: Chaldæus hic. Ut familia regia per eum duraret.

VT FIRMARET RADICEM) Non est in Hebræo.

SVPER AQVAS MVLTAS) Iuxta aquas multas. In solo optimo, Eccl. 40, 1.

IN SVPERFICIE POSVIT ILLVD) צפצפה, quod est conspicere, factum credidit geminatum מצפצפה, ut & LXX. qui vertunt ἐπιβλεπόμενον. Ita Sedeciam posuit Baby- lonius, ut aspici posset, id est à Judæis quidem suspicere- tur, ab ipso autem penderet, ut sequitur. صفصاف Arabibus, & Chaldæis צפצפה est salicis genus. Hinc sen- sus esset: posuit quasi saliles. Nam salices aquas amant Plin. 16, 19. Psal. 137, 2. Es. 44, 4.

## 17:6
Ver. 6. AND WHEN IT HAD GERMINATED IT GREW INTO A WIDER VINE) Extending itself widely, or luxuriating: for that is properly סרחת.

OF LOW STATURE WITH ITS BRANCHES LOOKING TOWARDS IT) Its branches, that is, its shoots: towards it, supply the eagle. The sense will be: The king was sufficiently opulent and happy, but obliged to look up to the Babylonian King, and to venerate him, as partly a subject, or as a client.

AND ITS ROOTS WERE UNDER IT) That is, the firmness of his kingdom depended upon the Babylonian.

THEREFORE THE VINE BECAME) It became, I say, a vine. For he repeats what he had said.

AND BROUGHT FORTH FRUIT IN BRANCHES, AND SENT OUT SHOOTS) He begat sons, Jer. 52, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CVMQVE GERMINASSET CREVIT IN VINEAM LATIOREM) Late se extendentem, sive luxu- riantem: id enim proprie est סרחת.

HVMILI STATVRA RESPICIENTIBVS RAMIS EJVS AD EAM) Ramis, id est, palmitibus: ad eam, sup- ple aquilam. Sensus erit: Erat rex satis opulentus & felix, sed obligatus suspicere Regem Babylonium, ac venerari, ut partim subditus, aut ut cliens.

ET RADICES EJVS SVB ILLA ERANT) Id est, firmitas regni ipsius à Babylonico pendebat.

FACTA EST ERGO VINEA) Facta est, inquam, vinea. Repetit enim, quod dixerat.

ET FRUCTIFICAVIT IN PALMITES, ET E- MISIT PROPAGINES) Filios genuit, Jer. 52, 10.

## 17:7
Ver. 7.

AND IT CAME TO PASS) It was, moreover: ויהי.

ANOTHER GREAT EAGLE) The Egyptian King, this is explained below in 15, and Chrysostom well acknowledged it in the said place. That King seems to have been Apries, whom Jeremiah and Herodotus mention.

WITH GREAT WINGS, AND MANY FEATHERS) Having armies and various peoples under him.

AND BEHOLD THIS VINE) Zedekiah.

AS IF SENDING ITS ROOTS TOWARDS IT) In the Hebrew: It bent its roots towards it. It sought firmness from him himself: it wished to betake itself to his clientage. Jerem. 37, 38. 2. Kings 24, 7. 2. Chron. 36, 13.

By roots Maldonatus understands ambassadors: but the Grotian interpretation is simpler.

Verse the same.

THAT IT MIGHT WATER IT FROM THE BEDS OF ITS SPROUTS) That is, with that hope, that it might receive great auxiliary forces from him. שקה signifies not only to water, but often also to make fat, and it is taken here for to bestow.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET FACTA EST) Fuit autem: ויהי.

AQVILA ALTERA GRANDIS) Rex Ægyptius, Infra hoc explicatur 15. & bene agnovit dicto loco Chry- sostomus. Is Rex videtur fuisse Apries, cujus Jeremias & Herodotus meminere.

MAGNIS ALIS, MVLTISQVE PLVMIS) Ex- ercitus & populos varios sub se habens.

ET ECCE VINEA ISTA) Sedecias.

QVASI MITTENS RADICES SVAS AD EAM) In Hebræo: Inflexit radices suas ad eam. Ab ipso firmitatem petiit: ad ejus clientelam conferre se voluit. Jerem. 37, 38. 2. Reg. 24, 7. 2. Paral. 36, 13.

Per radices Maldonatus legatos intelligit: sed simplicior est interpretatio Grotiana.

Vers. eod.

VT IRRIGARET EAM DE AREOLIS GER- MINIS SVI) Id est, ea spe, ut auxiliares copias magnas ab ipso acciperet. שקה non irrigare tantum, sed sæpe & pin- guefacere significat, sumiturque hic pro conferere.

## 17:8
Verse 8.

IN A GOOD LAND BY MANY WATERS IT WAS PLANTED, THAT IT MIGHT BRING FORTH BRANCHES, AND BEAR FRUIT, THAT IT MIGHT BE A GOODLY VINE) He repeats what he had said, so that from the greatness of the benefits the guilt of an ungrateful mind might be the more grievous,

Latin:

Vers. 8.

IN TERRA BONA SVPER AQVAS MVLTAS PLANTATA EST, VT FACIAT FRONDES, ET PORTET FRVCTVM, VT SIT IN VINEAM GRAN- DEM) Repetit quæ dixerat, ut ex beneficiorum magnitu- dine gravior sit culpa animi ingrati,

## 17:9
Vers. 9. SHALL HE THEREFORE PROSPER?) Could it be that God would grant prosperous things to both an ungrateful and a treacherous man? Faith must be kept by the law of nations, even to that to which one has come by some necessity of war. See book 3 of The Law of War and Peace, 19, 11. But Zedekiah, besides his faith, was also bound by benefits, owing all he had to the Babylonian.

SHALL HE NOT PULL UP THE ROOTS THEREOF?) The Babylonian will overturn his state.

IT SHALL STRIP OFF THE FRUIT THEREOF?) He will cut off the children of Zedekiah.

AND SHALL DRY UP ALL THE LEAVES OF HER SPRING, AND IT SHALL WITHER) Better: And it shall wither (the vine itself) and the leaves of its spring shall wither likewise. To wither is to lose the living sap, to pine away, as those are wont to do who are in miserable servitude, Levit. 26, 19. The leaves are the princes and the common people.

AND NOT WITH A GREAT ARM, NOR WITH MUCH PEOPLE, AND HE SHALL PLUCK IT UP BY THE ROOTS) Namely, that which the Chaldean adds here will come. He will have no need to use the whole strength of his kingdom against a King so powerless.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ERGONE PROSPERABITUR) Fierine pote- rat, ut Deus res prosperas daret, & ingrato & perfido? Fides servanda jure gentium, etiam ad quam belli aliqua necessi- tate deventum est. Vid. lib. 3. de jure belli ac pacis 19, 11. At Sedecias præter fidem, etiam beneficiis erat obligatus, omnia sua Babylonio debens.

NONNE RADICES EJUS EVELLET) Statum ejus evertet Babylonius.

FRUCTUS EJUS DISTRINGET) Excidet libe- ros Sedeciæ.

ET SICCABIT OMNES PALMITES GERMI- NIS EJUS, ET ARESCET) Melius : Et arescet (ipsa vi- nea) & palmites germinis ejus arescent pariter. Arescere est succum vividum amittere, tabescere, ut solent, qui in misera sunt servitute, Levit. 26, 19. Palmites sunt principes & po- pulares.

ET NON IN BRACHIO GRANDI, NEQVE IN POPULO MULTO, ET EVELLERET EAM RA- DICITUS) Veniet scilicet, quod hic addit Chaldæus. Non opus illi erit totus regni sui viribus uti adversus Regem tam impotentem.

## 17:10
Vers. 10. BEHOLD, BEING PLANTED) Be it so: it was well planted.

SHALL IT NOT, WHEN THE EAST WIND TOUCHETH IT?) In the Hebrew: the east wind. For the peoples who were of the Chaldean empire lay partly to the East and partly to the North of the Jews, as has been said elsewhere.

AND IT SHALL WITHER IN THE FURROWS WHERE IT GREW) He will be captured at Jericho.

In the same place where it grew, according to Maldonatus, which is simpler. That place, however, was specifically the plain of Jericho, 2 Kings 25, 5; Jer. 52, 7, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ECCE PLANTATA EST) Esto: bene plan- tata erat.

NONNE CUM TETIGERIT EAM VENTUS URENS) In Hebræo: ventus orientalis. Nam populi, qui Chaldæici erant imperii, partim Judæis ad Orientem, partim ad Septentrionem objacebant, ut dictum est alibi.

ET IN AREIS GERMINIS SUI ARESCET) Apud Jerichuntem capietur.

In eodem loco, quo crevit, ut Maldonatus, quod simplicius. Locus tamen ille speciatim erat cam- pus Jericho, 2. Reg. 25, 5. Jer. 52, 7. 8.

## 17:12
Vers. 12. BEHOLD, THE KING OF BABYLON IS COME) This is the epimythium of the Apologue.

HE SHALL TAKE THE KING) He took King Jeconiah.

HE SHALL BRING THEE) He brought him. Thus also the Chaldean translates all these things in the past tense.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ECCE VENIT REX BABYLONIS) Hoc est Apologi ἐπιμύθιον.

ASSUMET REGEM) Cepit regem Jechoniam.

TE ADDUCET) Adduxit. Sic & Chaldæus hæc omnia per præterita vertit.

## 17:13
Ver. 13. AND HE SHALL TAKE)

AND HE SHALL STRIKE) He struck.

A COVENANT WITH HIM) Namely an unequal one, because Zedekiah was bound to perform certain commanded things.

AND HE SHALL TAKE AN OATH FROM HIM) He took it, which alone ought to have sufficed to keep him in faith.

BUT HE SHALL ALSO TAKE THE MIGHTY OF THE LAND) He took them away, as hostages of the covenant.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET TOLLET) Tulit.

FERIETQVE) Feriitque.

CUM EO FEDUS) Nempe inæquale, quod Sede- cias imperata quædam facere teneretur.

ET AB EO ACCIPIET JUSJURANDUM) Ac- cepit, quod vel solum sufficere debebat ad eum retinen- dum in fide.

SED ET FORTES TERRÆ TOLLET) Abstulit, velut obsides federis.

## 17:14
Ver. 14. THAT THE KINGDOM MIGHT BE HUMBLE, AND THAT IT MIGHT NOT LIFT ITSELF UP, BUT THAT IT MIGHT KEEP HIS COVENANT, AND THAT IT MIGHT OBSERVE IT) That by that as a bridle Judea might be kept in obedience.

Latin:

Vers. 14. UT SIT REGNUM HUMILE, ET NON ELEVETUR, SED CUSTODIAT PACTUM EJUS, ET SERVET ILLUD) Ut illo velut fræno Judæa reti- neretur in obsequio.

## 17:15
Ver. 15. HE SENT AMBASSADORS TO EGYPT) See above v. 7.

THAT HE MIGHT GIVE HIM HORSES) In which Egypt was especially strong, Deut. 17, 16.

AND SHALL HE THAT HATH BROKEN THE COVENANT ESCAPE?) Shall he bear the broken covenants with impunity?

Latin:

Vers. 15. MISIT NUNCIOS AD ÆGYPTUM) Vide supra v. 7.

UT DARET SIBI EQVOS) Qubus maxime va- lebat Ægyptus, Deut. 17, 16.

ET QVI DISSOLVIT PACTVM NUMQVID EFFUGIET?) An impune feret rupta federa?

## 17:16
Ver. 16. IN THE PLACE OF THE KING) In the Royal city: Babylon, as follows now.

Latin:

Vers. 16. IN LOCO REGIS) In urbe Regia : Baby- lone, ut jam sequitur.

## 17:17
AND NEITHER SHALL PHARAOH WITH A GREAT ARMY AND WITH MUCH PEOPLE MAKE BATTLE AGAINST HIM) Better: He shall make battle against Pharaoh himself, namely the Chaldean. There will be no need for him to contend with the Egyptian with the whole strength of the kingdom. For the Egyptian, having heard of his arrival, will withdraw.

Ver. 17. BY CASTING UP A MOUNT, AND BY BUILDING FORTS) Supply, there will be enough strength to take the city. There is no need for greater forces than those that take the camps placed at the city.

THAT HE MAY KILL MANY SOULS) First with missiles, then with the city captured, with swords.

Latin:

ET NON IN EXERCITV GRANDI, NEQVE IN POPULO MULTO FACIET CONTRA EUM PHARAO PRÆLIUM) Melius: Faciet contra ipsum Pha- raonem prælium, nempe Chaldæus. Non opus erit, ut to- tis viribus regni cum Ægyptio certet. Nam Ægyptius au- dito ejus adventu recedet.

Vers. 17. IN JACTU AGGERIS, ET IN EXSTRU- CTIONE VALLORUM) Supple, satis erit virium ad ur- bem capiendam. Non majoribus copiis opus est, quam castra ad urbem posita capiant.

UT INTERFICIAT ANIMAS MVLTAS) Telis primum, deinde urbe capta, gladiis.

## 17:18
Ver. 18. AND BEHOLD, HE GAVE HIS HAND) And yet he had given his hand, by confirming the covenant, as was the custom. See what we said at Jer. 50, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET ECCE, DEDIT MANUM SUAM) At- qui dederat manum suam, firmando federi, ut moris erat. Vide quod diximus Jer. 50, 15.

## 17:19
Ver. 19. AND THE COVENANT, WHICH HE HATH VIOLATED) In the Hebrew: my covenant, which he broke. Namely, sworn in my name.

I WILL LAY UPON HIS HEAD) I will cause it to turn out badly for him.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET FOEDUS, QVOD PRÆVARICATVS EST) In Hebræo: fœdus meum, quod rupit. Juratum sci- licet in meo nomine.

PONAM IN CAPITE EJVS) Faciam, ut illi male vertat.

## 17:20
Ver. 20. AND I WILL SPREAD OVER HIM MY NET, AND I WILL CATCH HIM IN MY DRAGNET) Above 12, 13. Below 32, 3.

IN THE VIOLATION, WHEREBY HE HATH DESPISED ME) From the law of Exodus 20, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET EXPANDAM SVPER EVM RETE MEVM, ET COMPREHENDAM EVM IN SAGENA MEA) Supra 12, 13. Infra 32, 3.

IN PRÆVARICATIONE, QVA DESPEXIT ME) Ex lege Exodi 20, 7.

## 17:21
Ver. 21.

AND ALL HIS FUGITIVES) Companions of his flight.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ET OMNES PROFVGI EJVS) Comites fugæ.

## 17:22
Ver. 22. AND I WILL TAKE OF THE PITH OF THE HIGH CEDAR AND WILL SET IT) From the branches of the cedar: i.e., I will place many of the people in their own seats.

FROM THE TOP OF HIS BRANCHES I WILL CROP OFF A TENDER ONE) From his highest tender branches I will take away a tender one (one): Namely, from the captivity. The highest branches are those which were of the Davidic house: tender, because of small strength. Zerubbabel is designated.

AND I WILL TAKE) The matter will succeed better for me than for Nebuchadnezzar.

AND I WILL PLANT IT UPON A MOUNTAIN HIGH AND EMINENT) At Jerusalem, a great part of which city is mountainous.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET SVMAM EGO DE MEDVLLA CE- DRI SUBLIMIS ET PONAM) De ramis cedri: i. e. mul- tos populi in suis sedibus collocabo.

DE VERTICE RAMORUM EJUS TENERUM DISTRIHGAM) De summis ramis ejus teneris tenerum (unum) auferam: Nempe e captivitate. Summi rami sunt, qui erant de domo Davidica: teneri, quia viribus exiguis. Zorobabel designatur.

ET SUMAM EGO) Melius mihi res succedet, quam Nabuchodonosori.

ET PLANTABO SUPER MONTEM EXCEL- SUM ET EMINENTEM) Hierosolymis, cujus urbis pars magna montana.

## 17:23
Ver. 23. AND IT SHALL BURST FORTH INTO A SPROUT, AND SHALL PRODUCE FRUIT) From the sprout of the heart it shall bring forth the best fruits of piety. Truly this is said of Zerubbabel.

AND IT SHALL BECOME A GREAT CEDAR) Through him the Jewish nation shall be powerful.

AND ALL BIRDS SHALL DWELL UNDER IT, AND EVERY FOWL SHALL NEST UNDER THE SHADOW OF ITS BRANCHES) That is, other nations shall betake themselves under his protection. A similar expression in Dan. 4:9. See what is said in Matt. 13:32. Among these were the Nabataeans. See 1 Macc. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ERUMPET IN GERMEN, ET FACIET FRUCTUM) E cordis germine optimos proferet fructus pietatis. Vere hoc dictum de Zorobabele.

ET ERIT IN CEDRUM MAGNAM) Per illum gens Judæa potens erit.

ET HABITABUNT SUB EA OMNES VOLU- CRES, ET OMNE VOLATILE SUB UMBRA FRON- DIUM SJUS NIDIFICABIT) Id est, gentes aliæ sub ejus tutelam se conferent. Similis locutio Dan. 4,9. Vide, quæ dicta Matth. 13,32. In his fuere Nabathæi. Vid. 1. Macc. 5.

## 17:24
Ver. 24. AND ALL THE TREES OF THE REGION SHALL KNOW) All trees everywhere: that is, the nations.

I HAVE HUMBLED THE HIGH TREE) I shall bring down the Babylonians. For these past tenses have the sense of the future. He speaks as a witness, because he was living under the Babylonians.

But are not other prophecies uttered against Babylon in Babylon itself sufficiently clear? That parabolic manner of speaking is, as is known, familiar to the Prophets.

I HAVE EXALTED THE LOW TREE) I shall raise up the depressed Jews.

AND I HAVE DRIED UP THE GREEN TREE) I shall wither it. That is, I shall despoil of its wealth Babylon, which has flourished for a long time.

AND I HAVE MADE THE BRANCHES A DRY TREE) Jerusalem, which had been destroyed, I shall restore, and I shall give them wealth.

AND I HAVE DONE) I shall do.

These cannot be explained of Zerubbabel, as Grotius opines along with certain Jews. For he did not grow into such a great Cedar that all birds and every fowl dwelt under the shadow of its branches, i.e., that all nations betook themselves under his protection; which is his own explanation, even though he neglects the universal particle ALL repeated twice, which is not to be neglected. Therefore Cornelius à Lapide, even though he also desires to snatch these for Zerubbabel, is forced to admit that these do not fit Zerubbabel. Nor was Zerubbabel a King: which Maldonado also urges here, he was neither a King, nor was his dominion perpetual. Nor did all birds rest under his shadow, unless hyperbolically; therefore Cornelius provides this sense: God here opposes Himself to Nebuchadnezzar. As if to say: He appointed Zedekiah king from the royal seed, but he shall reign for a short time. For he shall be treacherous, and therefore he shall be blinded by the Chaldean, and deprived of his kingdom. But God from the same seed of David established, as He promised, Christ the King, that He might reign over Sion His holy mountain, that is, in the house of Jacob forever: for of His kingdom there shall be no end. Although indeed the breadth of the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar is also described thus in Dan. 4, 17. 18. 19., yet by no proportion, as the blessed Hülsemann rightly warns here, was the kingdom of Zerubbabel to be compared to it, and in the N.T. it is often explained concerning the breadth of the Church and the grace of Christ, because under this the birds of the air are to dwell, Matt. 13. 32. c. 22, 37. Cornelius also seeks the mystery of the cross in the LXX Version, along with Theodoret, but that does not agree with the authentic text. AND I WILL PLANT (this tender branch of the Cedar and the top, i.e., Christ) UPON A MOUNTAIN HIGH AND EMINENT) that is, in Sion, that is, the Church. The Septuagint translate: I will hang him on the high mountain of Israel, i.e., as Theodoret says, I will crucify Christ on the mount of Calvary, so that afterwards He may bring forth fruit, and the immortal germ of Christians in the whole world. Which note against the Jews. Who deny the cross and death of Christ; because they think the Messiah will be one with pomp and pride, as if a new Solomon.

Furthermore, the Septuagint translate it aptly. For instead of וְהִתְלוֹל i.e., & suspended on high, that is, eminent, as the Vulgate translates, they themselves read אֶתְלוֹל, i.e., I will suspend. For it is properly said that something, or someone, is suspended on a mountain, but not that the mountain itself is suspended. Add that, by the change of a single point, it can be read וְהִתְלַלְ vetalol, i.e., & to suspend, that is, & I will suspend. This is Cornelius. But the sense of the original text is in the open, whatever the LXX interpreters may have read or rendered. Others among the Papists follow Cornelius in this, that a prophecy concerning Christ is held here. Which opinion, even after Jerome and Theodoret, is that of our B. Luther, and of our paraphrasts Osiander and the Vinians, as also of the commentators B. Pappus, B. Hülsemann, and not least the Belgian paraphrasts and others from the Reformed. What of the fact that the Chaldean interpreter understood it concerning the Messiah, and that among the Rabbis, R. Solomon also rendered it thus: I will take the King Messiah, and I will plant him upon a high mountain. Let Galatinus, De arcanis Catholicae veritatis, lib. 3, cap. 21, be compared. Jerome interprets those things concerning the humiliation of the sublime tree and the exaltation of the humble tree thus: This is he who once humbled the sublime tree of Israel, and exalted the humble people of the nations: who dried up the green tree of the Jews, flourishing and budding in the Law and the Prophets, and made the dry tree of the nations to leaf; so that what he had always spoken, he might fulfill with his mouth. The words of Simeon in the Gospel signify this same thing, saying: Behold, this one is set for the ruin and resurrection of many. And the mustard seed, which, though it be the least of all seeds, after it has grown, is a dwelling place for the birds. Thus far Jerome. He also adds another explanation concerning Christ: Some interpret the sublime tree humbled and the humble tree exalted otherwise: referring it to the passion of the Lord Savior. Who, when he was in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal to God: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant: And after the resurrection, the tree itself was subsequently made sublime: which, previously green, was dried up by death: and afterwards reviving, received its former vigor.
