But we can easily admit that the depressed Jews are to be understood, whom God wishes to raise up, and that the kingdom of Jeconiah is designated, who, having already been captured in Babylon, seemed to have withered, with no hope of offspring to reign, but was raised up, not so much when he himself was exalted by Evil-Merodach, or in his grandson Zerubbabel (who was truly not the grandson of Jeconiah, who had no sons and was not of the Solomonic line, but descended from David through the line of Nathan), as when Christ, the Lord of the whole earth, came forth from his own lineage; whence Cornelius again acknowledges that these things properly apply to Christ, and that this is what Isaiah says in ch. 11, 1: A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse (which now seems to have withered) and a flower shall ascend from his root. Let Franciscus Junius be compared in his commentary on this place. B. Hülsemann has it thus on this place, perhaps following Jerome and Osiander, who explains it in almost the same way: The literal sense is that, from the abrogation of the Israelite kingdom, the kingdom of Christ would appear by substitution, because God was also going to elevate the humble and abject figure of Christ and the nature of the Gentiles, and was going to substitute them in the place of the Jews, as the Apostle explains, using the same allegory of the vine and the olive, Rom. 11, 15. Thus Jeconiah is called an abject and dry man, Jer. 22, 30. Christ in the state of emptying himself calls himself the green tree, and the imperfect disciples the dry one, Luke 23, 13. See the same phrase used of men, Is. 56, 4; Sir. 3, 3; Job 29, 1. Here therefore v. 24. AND ALL THE TREES OF THE FIELD SHALL KNOW, he wishes the final cause to be implied, why God is about to perform such a metamorphosis, namely, that all nations might acknowledge that it was necessary for the secular kingdom of Israel to pass into the spiritual kingdom of Christ, as into an antitype. We prefer, however, to understand the Babylonians rather than the Jews by the sublime and green tree: for the latter are included under the humble tree, not indeed that they are to recover their flower and corporal sublimity, as Grotius wishes, but that they are to be exalted spiritually in Christ, and ought to flourish, both in their remnants and in those who will come to them and be grafted into this olive tree, Rom. 11, 24, and are supported by their root, verses 17, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET SCIENT OMNIA LIGNA REGIONIS) Omnes ubivis arbores: id est, gentes.

HUMILIAVI LIGNUM SUBLIME) Deprimam Babylonios. Præterita enim hæc futuri habent sensum. Teste loquitur, quia vivebat sub Babyloniis.

At annon satis aperta alia sunt contra Babylo- nem in ipsa Babyl. prolata vaticinia? Est modus ille loquendi parabolicus Prophetis, ut notum, fa- miliaris.

EXALTAVI LIGNUM HUMILE) Depressos Ju- dæos erigam.

ET SICCAVI LIGNUM VIRIDE) Arefaciam. Id est, suis opibus spoliabo Babylonem, quæ diu floruit.

ET FRONDES FECI LIGNUM ARIDUM) Hiero- solyma, quæ destructa fuere, restituam, opesque ipsis dabo.

ET FECI) Faciam.

De Zorobabele hæc explicari non possunt, uti cum Judæis quibusdam opinatur Grotius. Nam is in tam magnam Cedrum non evasit, ut habitarent sub umbra frondium ipsius omnes volucres, & omne volatile, i. e. omnes gentes sub tutelam ejus se recepe- rint; quæ ipsius est explicatio, etsi ille universalem particulam OMNES bis repetitam negligat, quæ negligenda non est. Ideo Cornelius à Lapide, etsi etiam ad Zorobabelem hæc abripere cupiat, fateri cogitur, Zorobabeli hæc non congruere. Nec Zo- robabel Rex fuit: quod hic urget etiam Maldona- tus, nec Rex fuit, nec dominatio ejus perpetua. Nec sub ejus umbra omnes volucres requieverunt, nisi hy- perbolice; itaque hunc sensum tradit Cornelius: Op- ponit se hic Deus Nabuchodonosori. q. d. Ille regem ex semine regio constituit Sedeciam. sed modico tempore regnabit. Perfidus enim erit, ideoque à Chaldæo exæ- cabitur, & regno privabitur. At Deus ex eodem Davi- dis semine constituit, uti promisit, Regem Christum, ut regnet super Sion montem sanctum ejus, puta in do- mo Jacob in æternum: regni enim ejus non erit fi- nis. Quanquam vero etiam latitudo regni Nebu- cadnezaris ita describatur Dan. 4, 17. 18. 19. nulla tamen proportione, quod recte hic monet B. Hül- semannus, regnum Zorobabel illi fuit comparan- dum, & in N. T. sæpe explicatur de latitudine Eccle- siæ & gratiæ Christi, quod sub hac aves cœli habita- turæ sint Matth. 13. 32. c. 22, 37. Quærit etiam myste- rium crucis Cornelius in Versione LXX. cum Theo- doreto, sed id textui authentico non congruit. ET PLANTABO (tenerum hunc Cedri ramum & verticem, i. e. Christum) SUPER MONTEM EXCELSUM ET EMINENTEM) puta in Sion, id est, Ecclesia. Septuag. vertunt: suspendam illum in monte sublimi Israël, i. e. ut Theodoretus, crucifi- gam Christum in monte Calvariæ, ut postea proferat fructum, & germen Christianorum immortale in toto mundo. Quod nota contra Judæos. Qui negant Chri- sti crucem & mortem; quia putant Messiam futu- rum cum pompa & fastu, quasi novum Salomonem.

Porro apte vertunt Septuag. Nam pro וְהִתְלוֹל i. e. & suspensum in alto, h. e. eminentem, ut vertit Vulga- tus, ipsi legerunt אֶתְלוֹל, i. e. suspendam. Proprie e- nim dicitur quid, vel quis in monte suspensus, non au- tem ipse mons suspensus. Adde, sola unius puncti muta- tione, legi posse וְהִתְלַלְ vetalol, i. e. & suspendere, h. e. & suspendam. Hæc Cornel. Sed sensus textus origina- lis in aprico est, quicquid legerint, aut reddiderint LXX. Interpp. Sequuntur Cornelium in eo alii è Pontificiis, quod hic de Christo vaticinium habea- tur. Quæ sententia etiam post Hieronymum, & Theo- doretum est B. Lutheri nostri, & Paraphrastarum no- strorum Osiandri ac Vinariensium, ut & Commenta- torum, B. Pappi, B. Hülsemanni, nec non Paraphra- starum Belgicorum & aliorum è Reformatis. Quid quod Chaldæus Interpres de Messia intellexerit, quodque è Rabinis etiam R. Salomo sic reddiderit: Accipiam ego Regem Messiam, & plantabo illum su- per montem excelsum. Conferatur Galatinus de arca- nis Catholicæ veritatis lib. 3. cap. 21. Illa de humilia- tione ligni sublimis, & exaltatione ligni humilis ita interpretatur Hieronymus: Iste est, qui Israël quon- dam sublime lignum humiliavit, & exaltavit homi- lem gentium populum: qui exsiccavit lignum viride Judæorum, florens & germinans in lege & Prophetis, & frondere fecit lignum aridum nationum; ut quod si semper locutus est, ore compleret. Hoc idem signifi- cant Simeonis in Evangelio verba, dicentis: Ecce, hic positus est in ruinam, & resurrectionem multorum. Et granum sinapis, quod cum minimum sit omnibus seminibus, postquam creverit, avium habitaculum est. Hactenus Hieronym. Addit & aliam de Christo explicationem: Quidam aliter interpretantur li- gnum sublime humiliatum, & humile exaltatum: re- ferentes ad passionem Domini Salvatoris. Qui cum in forma Dei esset, non est rapinam arbitratus æqua- lem se esse Deo: sed exinanivit se, formam servi ac- cipiens: Et post resurrectionem, ipsum lignum postea sublimatum est: quod prius virens morte siccatum est: & postea reviviscens, pristinum recepit vigorem. Sed admittere facile possumus, quod depressi Judæi intelligendi, quos Deus erigere velit, quodque regnum Jechoniæ designetur, qui jam in Babylone captus aruisse videbatur, nulla spe regnaturæ pro- lis, sed erectus fuit, non tam ubi exaltabatur ipse ab Evilmerodacho, aut in nepote suo Zorobabele, (qui vero non Jechoniæ nepos, qui filios non habebat nec ex linea Salomonea erat, sed per lineam Natha- nis à Davide descendebat) quam cum Christus ex ipsius cognatione prodiret totius terræ Dominus; unde iterum agnoscit Cornelius hæc Christo pro- prie competere, atque hoc esse, quod ait Es. c. 11, 1. Egredietur virga de radice Jesse (quæ jam aruisse vi- detur) & flos de radice ejus ascendet. Conferatur Franciscus Junius in commentario in hunc locum. B. Hulsemannus in hunc locum ita habet, Hierony- mum forte sequutus & Osiandrum, qui eadem fere ratione explicat: Sensus literalis est, ex abrogatione regni Israëlitici, surrogatione regni Christi apparitu- rum esse, quod Deus etiam humilem Christi figuram, & abjectam gentilium naturam elevaturus, & in lo- cum Judæorum substiturus esset, ut Apostolus expli- cat, eadem Allegoria de vite & oleo, Rom. 11, 15. Ita Jechonias vocatur vir abjectus & aridus, Ier. 22, 30. Christus in statu exinanitionis se lignum viride, imperfectos discipulos aridum vocat Luc. 23, 13. Vide eandem phrasin de hominibus usurpatum, Es. 56, 4. Syr. 3, 3. Iob. 29, 1. Hic ergo v. 24. ET SCIANT OMNIA LIGNA REGIONIS, cau- sam finalem innui vult, cur Deus tantam Metamor- phosin facturus sit, videlicet ut omnes gentes agno- scant, oportuisse ut seculari Israëlis regnum transiret in regnum Christi spirituale, tanquam in Antitypum. Malumus tamen per lignum sublime, & viride in- telligere Babylonios quam Judæos: hi enim sub li- gno humili comprehenduntur, non quidem quod florem & sublimitatem corporalem, ut Grotius vult, recuperaturi, sed quod in Christo spiritualiter exaltandi sint, & florere debeant, tum in reliquiis suis, tum in iis, qui ipsis accedent, & oleæ huic inse- rentur, Rom. 11, 24. & à radice eorum portantur, vers. 17. 18.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII.

A divine protest against the proverb of the Jews, that the son is not to bear the iniquity of the father, nor the father that of the son, but that the impious man is to be saved if he performs repentance, and the just man is to be condemned if he abandons his justice: with an exhortation to repentance and the renewal of the heart.

Vers. 1. THE FATHERS HAVE EATEN A SOUR GRAPE, AND THE CHILDREN'S TEETH ARE SET ON EDGE) A frequent adage in those times, as appears in Jer. 31, 29. Similar to that Horatian one: The sins of the ancestors, O Roman, you shall pay for, though undeserving. They wanted to be believed innocent, when they were by no means such.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII.

Protestatio divina contra proverbium Judæo- rum, quod filius non portaturus sit iniqui- tatem Patris, nec Pater filii, sed impius sal- vandus sit, si pœnitentiam agat, justus si ju- stitiam suam deserat, damnandus: cum ad- hortatione ad pœnitentiam & cordis inno- vationem.

Vers. 1. PATRES COMEDERUNT UVAM ACER- BAM, ET DENTES FILIORVM OBSTUPESCUNT) Frequens illis temporibus adagium, ut apparet Jer. 31, 29. Simile illi Horatiano: Delicta majorum immeritis lues Romane. Volebant credi innocentes, cum minime tales essent.

## 18:3
Vers. 3. AS I LIVE) It is a charientismos for 'may I not live.' IF THIS PARABLE SHALL BE A PROVERB AMONG YOU ANY MORE) God, the Lord of the life and death of all, can, because of the sins of parents, inflict either premature death or servitude upon their descendants: and when he does that, as he has done several times, he does injury to no one. But to kings, who do not have such dominion, the law has deservedly forbidden it. Furthermore, with the time of the Gospel now approaching, God wished his justice to appear more exactly, and therefore he willed that all the impious should perish by the sword, pestilence, and famine, that the less evil should die in servitude, and that the good should return free to their homeland.

Although God, as Lord of life and death, by His absolute power has the right to determine concerning us and ours, concerning our life and fortune, and thus to inflict premature death or servitude, as He wills, and upon whom He wills by the vigor of His supreme power, yet He does not wish to be regarded according to absolute right and dominion, nor is it right to separate that from divine justice: Because God can design nothing against justice. Nor was the justice of God revealed only under the New Testament, but as it is essential and natural to God, so also He made it conspicuous at every time. Nowhere have the Holy Scriptures handed down this distinction between the times of the Old and New Testament, that He wished His justice to appear more exactly in punishing the impious and delivering the good under the New Testament: which Grotius ought not to have asserted or assumed as an ὁμολογούμενον, but to have proved and demonstrated from Holy Scripture. He would have spoken more correctly had he said that God wished His grace to appear more exactly under the New Testament; because then the χάρις σωτήριος ἐπεφάνη, Tit. 2, 14, and the Gospel concerning the remission of sins was announced throughout the whole world. Nor indeed does God punish anyone for the sins of parents alone: since no one is entirely innocent before God and every punishment presupposes guilt, not in another, but in him who is to be affected by the punishment. The passage in Exod. 20, 5, that God visits the sins of parents upon children, is ambiguous in the Vulgate version; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon their children, who hate me; as if the relative EORUM should be referred to the parents, which by the force of the Hebrew text must be referred to the children, so that it is clear that those children are designated who hate the Lord, whence Papist interpreters here rashly twist themselves and this limitation is manifest from this passage of Ezekiel, that children are to be chastised for the sins of parents, if indeed the children imitate the iniquities of the parents, and insist upon their wicked footsteps, for those who do not imitate the sins of the parents are not to be punished for the parents' transgres- sion λευκά δὶ Φωνη̃ God here declares in verse 14. Because Socinus urges in his Defensio fidei Catholicae de satisfactione Christi, ch. 4, p. 54, that some are sometimes punished, not only for their own sins, by reason of which they were guilty, but also for the sins of others, and thus are punished even when they were not guilty: To this I answer, that this was done not because they were punished even when not guilty, but because they had accumulated the crimes of others, and had not shrunk from their known and perceived wickedness, nor feared the punishments either inflicted or announced upon their wicked parents or others, which is the cause of the aggravation of the punishment designated below in ch. 20, 18; Jer. 7, 14; ch. 22, 27; ch. 44, 21; Hos. 7, 9; Amos 8, 7. Indeed, it is even indicated here in v. 14. The son seeing the crimes of the father. For it concerns manifest and obvious crimes, v. 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. Therefore, the opinion of Grotius, which he defends in the cited place, is not to be borne. By the words of the Prophet in this place, v. 20, 'The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son,' it is not taught what God must necessarily do, but what He has freely decreed to do; that is, it does not concern a perpetual and immutable law, but the ordinary course of divine providence: This opinion, I say, is not to be admitted; because that flows from the justice of God, which is natural and essential to Him: And therefore it concerns a perpetual and immutable law of God. Which is also designated by the divine law in Deut. 24, 16. For if the Lord were only dealing with what He wishes to use hereafter against the Jews in the ordinary course of His providence, as Grotius wishes, and not what is consistent with law and justice, why did He sanction this maxim of law there: 'The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: but every man shall be put to death for his own sin'? There is no exception for Grotius, that this law was in part positive, laid down by God for men, by which God is not bound, as He never imposed it upon Himself, nor indeed could be bound by any law: because as He fixed the law for others there, so God Himself declares here concerning Himself: 'The soul that sinneth, it shall die': not imposing a law upon Himself, but decreeing what is consistent with His own justice. Which comparison teaches that these are entirely matters of perpetual and immutable law, and not merely positive. Because divine justice does not permit that he who is entirely innocent should be punished. Although, therefore, God is bound by no law, He is nevertheless a law unto Himself, nor can He depart from His own justice, or deny Himself. The Jews themselves in the Gemara Berachot acknowledge that the passage in Exod. 20, 4 must be taken with a limitation: namely, that God only then, when the children imitate the wickedness of their parents, punishes in them not only their own, but also their parents' offenses; otherwise, the son does not die for the sins of the parent. For which reason Jonathan and Onkelos translated it as בנין מרדין, 'rebellious children,' notes R. Menasse Ben Israel in Exod. 33, because they thus showed that the sins of the fathers are punished only in wicked children. Similarly R. Salom. and Aben Esra; when the son, grandson, and great-grandson persist in wickedness, looking at all the sins, He extirpates the fourth generation. And that the sins of parents are not punished in children is sufficiently evident from the examples of Hezekiah and Josiah, who, though born of impious parents, experienced divine blessing. Because they did not follow the impious footsteps of their parents. That children are punished for the deed of Achan, Josh. 7, 14, the Rabbis respond from Pirke R. Eliezer ch. 38, that they themselves were participants in the crime, because, having noticed the theft, they did not report it, but concealed it. That children and grandsons were hanged for the deed of Saul, 2 Sam. 21, 8, R. David Kimchi responds that they themselves were also among the destroyers of the Gibeonites. They certainly did not disapprove of that deed. Since for the deed of Ham, Canaan is subjected to a curse, Gen. 9, 25; for the deed of Jeroboam, his posterity,

1 Kings 14, 10, this does not happen without regard and foreknowledge of their own impiety, by which God even then foresaw that the descendants would imitate their ancestors. Finally, when 70,000 perish for the deed of David, and David exclaims: 'I have sinned and done wickedly, but these sheep, what have they done?', this must be understood in a certain sense: namely, that they were innocent with respect to that crime which David had committed, but whom divine justice could indeed exterminate for other crimes. For why did He will that these precisely, who were killed then, should be killed, and not others, unless because He judged by just judgment that they deserved it? For no absolute decree is to be imagined here. And the observation of R. David Kimchi is entirely to be approved here (which was also approved by R. Aben Esra) when he provides the reason for the history of the sons of Saul, why God Himself punishes children for the offenses of their parents, so that judges should not condemn a father for the son, or the latter for the former, because, namely, God, looking into the minds of men, when He knows that a son is an emulator of paternal wickedness, can punish him, but it is not permitted for men, who are easily deceived, to do the same: For often what they judge to be worst, God approves.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VIVO EGO) Est χαριεντισμός pro ne vivam. SI ERIT ULTRA VOBIS PARABOLA HÆC IN PROVERBIUM) Deus vitæ necisque omnium Domi- nus potest ob peccata parentum etiam posteris aut imma- turam mortem, aut servitutem immittere: & cum id facit, ut fecit aliquoties, nemini facit injuriam. Regibus autem qui tale dominium non habent, merito id lex interdixit. Cæterum appropinquante jam Evangelii tempore, Deus exactius justitiam suam apparere, ideoque impios omnes gladio, peste, fame interire voluit, minus malos mori in servitute, bonos redire liberos in patriam.

ETsi Deus ceu vitæ necisque Dominus pro absolutâ sua potestate de nobis & nostris statuere habe- at, de vita & fortuna nostra, adeoque immaturam mortem aut servitutem immittere, uti vult, & qui- bus vult vigore supremæ potestatis suæ, possit, non tamen secundum jus & dominium absolutum spe- ctari vult, nec illud fas est à justitia divina separare: Quia Deus nihil potest designare adversus justi- tiam. Nec justitia Dei solum sub Novo Testamen- to revelata est, sed uti Deo essentialis & naturalis est, ita etiam omni tempore eandem conspicuam fecit. Nuspiam sacræ Literæ inter Veteris & Novi Testam. tempora hoc discrimen tradidere, quod exactius justitiam suam in impiis puniendis, & bonis liberandis apparere voluerit sub Novo Testamento: quod non asserere aut supponere tanquam ὁμολο- γόμενον debebat Grotius, sed ex sacra Scriptura probare atque demonstrare. Rectius dixisset, gra- tiam suam Deum exactius apparere voluisse sub Novo Testamento; quia tum χάρις σωτήριος ἐπεφάνη, Tit. 2, 14. & per totum orbem annunciatum fuit E- vangelium de remissione peccatorum. Neq; vero quenquam Deus ob sola parentum peccata punit: quum nemo coram Deo prorsus innocens sit & o- mnis pœna præsupponat culpam, non in alio, sed in eo, qui pœna afficiendus est. Locus in Exod. 20, 5. quod Deus visitet peccata parentum in filiis, in vul- gata versione ambiguus est; visitans iniquitatem pa- trum in filios eorum, qui oderunt me; ac si relativum EORUM referendum sit ad parentes, quod vi tex- tus Ebræi referri debet ad filios, ut eos designari constet filios, qui oderunt dominum, unde temere se hic torquent Papistici interpretes & manifesta est hæc limitatio ex hoc Ezechielis loco, filios ob peccata parentum castigandos, si nempe filii imitentur parentum iniquitates, eorumque sceleratis vestigiis in- sistant, nam qui non imitantur parentum peccata, eos non puniendos esse ob parentum prævarica- tionem λευκά δὶ Φωνη̃ Deus hic pronunciat vers.14. Quod urget Socinus defens.fid. Cathol. de satisfact. Christi c. 4. p. 54. punitos aliquos nonnunquam, non ob sua tantum peccata, quorum ratione nocentes fue- rint, sed insuper ob aliena, adeoque punitos etiam, qua non fuere nocentes: Ad id respondeo, id ideo factum, non quod puniti etiam qua non nocentes, sed quod accumularint scelera aliorum, neque abhor- ruerint à cognita & perspecta eorum turpitudine, nec metuerint à suppliciis sceleratis parentibus, aut aliis vel illatis, vel annunciatis, quæ causa aggrauan- di supplicii designatur infra c. 20, 18. Ier. 7, 14. c. 22, 27. cap. 44, 21. Hos 7, 9. Amos 8, 7. Imo etiam hic v. 14. indicata est. Filius videns scelera patris. Agitur enim de manifestis & in oculos incurrentibus facinoribus, v. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. 11. 12. 13. Quapropter non ferenda Grotii sententia, quam loco citato tuetur. Verbis Prophetæ hoc loco v. 20. Anima, quæ peccavit, ipsa morietur: Filius non portabit iniquitatem patris, ne- que pater portabit iniquitatem filii, non doceri, quid necessario Deo faciendum sit, sed quid facere libere decreverit, h. e. non agi de jure perpetuo & immuta- bili, sed de ordinario providentiæ divinæ cursu: Hæc inquam sententia admittenda non est; quia fluit illud ex justitia Dei, quæ ipsi naturalis atque essen- tialis est: Ideoque jus perpetuum & immutabile Dei concernit. Quod etiam lege divina Deut. 24, 16. designatur. Nam si tantum de eo ageret Dominus, quod posthac adversus Judæos uti velit ordinario providentiæ suæ cursu, uti Grotius vult, non vero, quid juri & justitiæ consentaneum sit, cur hanc ibi juris maximam lege sancivit: Ne morte afficia- tur partes pro filiis, neque filii pro patribus: sed quis- que ob peccatum suum morte afficietur. Nulla est Gro- tii exceptio, legem hanc esse ex parte positivam latam hominibus a Deo, qua Deus non adstringatur, ut qui eam sibi nusquam tulerit, neque vero ulla lege adstrin- gi possit: quia ut ibi aliis legem fixit, ita de se hic Deus ipse pronunciat: Anima, quæ peccavit, ipsa mo- rietsr: non sibi legem ferens, sed quid justitiæ suæ consentaneum sit decernens. Quæ collatio docet, omnino hæc juris esse perpetui, & immutabilis, non autem positivi tantum. Quia justitia divina non per- mittit, ut is, qui prorsus innocens sit, pœna afficia- tur. Etsi ergo nulla lege adstringatur Deus, sibi ipsi tamen lex est, nec justitiam suam migrare, aut seipsum abnegare potest. Agnoscunt ipsimet Judæi in Gemara Berachot locum Exod. 20 4. limitate ac- cipiendum esse: Deum scilicet tum demum, quan- do libri parentum pravitatem imitantur, in illis non propria modo, verum & parentum delicta punire, alias filium ob parentis peccata non mori. Quam ob causam Jonathan & Onkelos transtulisse בנין מרדין filii rebelles notat R. Menasse Ben Israel in Exod. 33. quod ita ostenderint, solum in pravis filiis delicta pa- trum castigari. Similiter R. Salom. & Aben Esra; quando filius. nepos & abnepos in pravitate perseve- rant, respiciens universa peccata, quartam generatio- nem exstirpat. Et quod non puniantur peccata pa- rentum in filiis, vel exemplis Hiskiæ & Josiæ satis constat, qui è parentibus impiis procreati divinam benedictionem sensere. Quia parentum impiis ve- stigiis non institerunt. Quod ob factum Achanis filii puniuntur, Jos. 7, 14. respondent Rabbini è Pir- que R. Eliezer c. 38. quod sceleris participes ipsi fue- rint, quia furto animadverso, illud non annuncia- verunt, sed occultarunt. Quod ob factum Saulis su- spensi filii & nepotes, 2. Sam. 21, 8. respondet R. Da- vid Kimchi, quod ipsi etiam fuerint inter eversores Gibeonitarum. Factum certe illud non improba- runt. Cum ob Chami factum execrationi Chanaan subjicitur Gen. 9, 25. ob Jeroboami ejus posteritas,

1. Reg. 14, 10. non id fit sine respectu & prævisione propriæ impietatis, qua Deus jam tum prævidit, posteros imitaturos majores suos. Denique cum ob factum Davidis pereunt LXX. millia, & exclamat David: Ego peccavi & inique feci, hæ oves quid fece- runt, hoc secundum quid intelligendum: quod nem- pe istius criminis, quod David commiserat, respe- ctu innocentes fuerint, quos vero potuit divina ju- stitia ob alia crimina exterminare. Cur enim istos præcise, qui occisi tum sunt, occisos voluit, non ve- ro alios, nisi quod ipsos id mereri judicarit justo ju- dicio? Nullum enim hic absolutum decretum fin- gendum est. Et probanda omnino hic observatio R. David Kimchi est (quæ etiam R. Aben Esræ pro- bata fuit) cum is ad historiam filiorum Saulis cau- sam tradit, cur Deus liberos ob parentum delicta ipse puniat, ut judices patrem filii, aut hunc illius causa non condemnare debeant, quia scilicet Deus introspiciens animos hominum, quando cognoscit fi- lium paternæ pravitatis æmulum esse, castigare eum potest, at hominibus, qui facile falluntur, idem non licet: Nam sæpe quod pessimum illi judicant, Deus probat.

## 18:4
Verse 4. ALL SOULS ARE MINE) All men are in my power.

Latin:

Vers. 4. OMNES ANIMÆ MEÆ SVNT) Omnes homines in mea sunt potestate.

## 18:5
V. 5. HATH EXECUTED JUDGMENT) By rendering to each his own.

AND JUSTICE) He has exercised beneficence; as is explained more fully shortly.

Latin:

V. 5. FECERIT JVDICIVM) Cuique suum tribuendo.

ET JVSTITIAM) Beneficentiam exercuerit; ut mox latius explicatur.

## 18:6
Verse 6. HATH NOT EATEN UPON THE MOUNTAINS) It was the custom to feast after sacrifices, and indeed in the same places where the sacrifice had been made.

HATH NOT LIFTED UP HIS EYES TO THE IDOLS) A gesture of those praying, Ps. 121, 1.

HIS NEIGHBOR'S WIFE) The Israelites.

AND HAS NOT APPROACHED A MENSTRUOUS WOMAN) According to the most wise law, Lev. 20, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 6. IN MONTIBVS NON COMEDERIT) Post sacrificia epulari mos erat, & quidem iisdem in locis ubi sa- crificatum fuerat.

OCVLOS SVOS NON LEVAVERIT AD IDO- LA) Gestus precantium, Psal. 121, 1.

VXOREM PROXIMI SVI) Israelitæ.

ET AD MVLIEREM MENSTRVATAM NON ACCESSERIT) Ex lege sapientissima, Lev. 20, 19.

## 18:7
AND HAS NOT OPPRESSED A MAN) Has not oppressed a man. For that is what ינה means, as both the Chaldean and the LXX understood.

Ver. 7. HAS RETURNED THE PLEDGE TO THE DEBTOR) Namely such a one, which the debtor cannot be without, without serious inconvenience. Exod. 22, 26.

HAS TAKEN NOTHING BY VIOLENCE) In the Hebrew: Has not committed robbery. See Lev. 19, 3.

HAS GIVEN HIS BREAD TO THE HUNGRY) After the duties of judgment, that is, of justice, he comes to the duties of beneficence, which the Hebrews often call justice: and he paves the way for the Gospel, just as Isaiah had done 58, 7. See Matth. 3, 11.

Here recurs the Socinian and Papistic error concerning the precepts of perfection under the New Testament, as if such duties of beneficence had not been required in the Old Testament: the contrary of which Grotius could have learned even from this passage and the parallel in Is. 58, 7 (to say nothing of other similar ones). For the way was not being paved for the Gospel by such things: whose purpose is not to deliver precepts, but to announce grace and the remission of sins; but the law was being explained, and the duties owed according to the law were being declared.

AND HAS COVERED THE NAKED WITH A GARMENT) This is also in Isaiah at the aforementioned place. Compare Matth. 25, 35.

Latin:

ET HOMINEM NON CONTRISTAVERIT) Hominem non oppresserit. Id enim est ינה, quomodo & Chaldæus & LXX. intellexere.

Vers. 7. PIGNVS DEBITORI REDDIDERIT) Nem- pe tale, quo debitor sine gravi incommodo carere non pos- sit. Exod. 22, 26.

PER VIM NIHIL RAPVERIT) In Hebræo: Ra- pinam non rapuerit. Vide Lev. 19, 3.

PANEM SVVM ESVRIENTI DEDERIT) Post officia judici, id est, justitiæ, venit ad officia beneficentiæ, quam Hebræi sæpe justitiam vocant: & Evangelio viam struit, ut & Esais fecerat 58, 7. Vide Matth. 3, 11.

Recurrit hic error Socinianus, & Papisticus de perfectionibus præceptis sub Novo Testamento, quasi talia beneficentiæ officia in Veteri Testamento re- quisita non fuerint: cujus contrarium vel ex hoc loco & parallelo Es. 58, 7. (ut alia similia taceam) di- scere poterat Grotius. Non enim talibus via Evan- gelio sternebatur: cujus non est præcepta tradere, sed gratiam & remissionem peccatorum annuncia- re; sed lex explicabatur, & officia juxta legem de- bita declarabantur.

ET NVDVM OPERVERIT VESTIMENTO) Est & hoc apud Esaiam dicto loco Confer Matth. 25, 35.

## 18:8
Ver. 8.

HAS NOT LENT AT USURY) He used 'to lend' for 'to give a loan'; for these are related. Usury is properly said of money.

AND HAS NOT TAKEN MORE) תרבית, πλεονασμόν (excess). Thus is said whatever one has gained in other things besides money over the amount given as a loan, Levit. 25, 36. Jerome in his Commentaries on this passage: Some think that usury is only in money, which the divine Scripture foreseeing, takes away the superabundance of every thing, so that you do not take more than you gave. It is customary in fields for usury of grain and millet, wine and oil, and other species to be exacted, or, as the divine language calls it, superabundances: for example, that in the winter time you take ten modii. Is it not just that I should take half a modius more of my own when he has nine and a half of mine through my liberality? Do not err, says the Apostle, God is not mocked.

HAS TURNED HIS HAND AWAY FROM INIQUITY) עול is evil deceit.

AND SHALL JUDGE BETWEEN MAN AND MAN) Whether a judge appointed, or an arbiter chosen.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

AD VSVRAM NON COMMODAVERIT) Com- modare pro mutuum dare posuit; sunt enim hæc affinia. Usura de pecunia proprie dicitur.

ET AMPLIVS NON ACCEPERIT) תרבית πλεονασμόν. Ita dicitur, quicquid in rebus aliis præter pecu- niam lucrint super quantitatem mutuo datam, Levit. 25, 36. Hieronymus in Commentariis ad hunc locum: Putant qui- dam, usuram tantum esse in pecunia, quod prævidens Scriptura divina omnis rei aufert superabundantiam, ut plus non accipias quam dedisti Solent in agris frumenti & milii, vini & olei, cæ- terarumque specierum usuræ exigi, sive, ut appellat sermo divi- nus, superabundantiæ: verbi gratia, ut hyemis tempore demas decem modios,. Nonne justum est, ut medium modium de meo plus accipiam cum ille mealiberalitate novem & semis de meo habeat? Noli errare, inquit Apostolus Deus non irridetur.

AB INIQVITATE AVERTERIT MANVM SVAM( עול est dolus malus.

ET JVDICIVM FECERIT INTER VIRUM ET VIRVM) Sive judex constitutus, sive lectus arbiter.

## 18:9
Vers. 9. THAT HE MAY DO TRUTH) Thus the Hebrews call whatever is right. HE SHALL LIVE THE LIFE) He shall be preserved from the sword, pestilence, and famine. Vers. 10. A ROBBER) Properly פריץ is a breaker-in, but it is usually taken more broadly. SHEDDING BLOOD) Namely, innocent blood. HE HAS DONE ONE OF THESE) Of the evil things which we have recounted, which he soon repeats. Vers. 11. AND INDEED NOT DOING ALL THESE) He who has not done all these (namely, the good things mentioned before). Vers. 12. DOING ABOMINATION) Thus he calls intercourse with a woman at a forbidden time. Vers. 13. HE SHALL DIE THE DEATH) Untimely; before his day, as the poets say. HIS BLOOD SHALL BE UPON HIM) The guilt of death. As this Chaldean [version] has it. Vers. 14. HE SHALL HAVE FEARED: AND SHALL NOT HAVE DONE) Seeing, I say, yet he shall not have done like them. He shall not have allowed himself to be drawn by his father's example. Vers. 18. HIS FATHER, BECAUSE HE HAS OPPRESSED, AND HAS DONE VIOLENCE TO HIS FATHER) Because he oppressed with oppression, and committed robbery. HE SHALL DIE IN HIS INIQUITY) He shall die on account of his sin. Vers. 19. AND YOU SAY: WHY HAS THE SON NOT BORNE THE INIQUITY OF THE FATHER?) Better thus: Yet you say why? That is, why do you affirm this so generally? Does not the son bear the iniquity of his Father? i.e., are we not beaten on account of the faults of our parents? God answers this objection. NAMELY BECAUSE THE SON HAS DONE JUDGMENT AND JUSTICE) Rather, if the son has exercised justice and beneficence. ALL MY PRECEPTS) See what is at Luke 1:6. HE SHALL LIVE THE LIFE) A happy one.

Regarding a happy life here: v. 10, Grotius explained it as preservation from sword, pestilence, and famine, just as he explains the threat in v. 13, 'He shall die the death,' as an untimely death, before his day. But these promises and threats are to be understood not only of temporal life and bodily or merely untimely death, but of eternal death and life. Because the promises were made to the penitent not only of temporal and bodily goods, but especially of spiritual goods, the remission of sins, and eternal life. For what else do these words imply than the remission of sins, 'I will not remember all his iniquities which he has done'? What is more certain than that eternal life and salvation are promised when God testifies, 'I do not desire the death of the wicked, but that he may turn and live'? Through repentance and conversion we do not escape temporal death, but eternal: nor do we attain only a happy life in this age, but a blessed life in the other age. A happy life in this age is sometimes common to the pious and the impious, and the impious not infrequently enjoy temporal happiness more than the faithful and the pious, Ps. 37 and 73. Temporal death is also common to the pious and the impious, and the pious are not infrequently snatched away by an untimely death, while the impious survive. And indeed the pious, such as Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and others, suffered unhappy fates, captivity, exile, and other things equally with the reprobate among the people. Wherefore these things cannot be understood of temporal death and affliction alone. V. 20. THE JUSTICE OF THE JUST SHALL BE UPON HIM) The reward of justice is here called justice, just as punishment is called iniquity. Vers. 21. HE SHALL HAVE REPENTED OF ALL HIS SINS) In the Hebrew: He shall have turned away from all his sins: That is: having put off vices, he shall have devoted himself to virtue. In the Hebrew it is held otherwise: But when the impious shall have turned or been converted from all his sins. Those things which treat of repentance, not of the pursuit of virtue, are the fruit of repentance. It is evident, however, from this that the impious can be recalled to repentance, against the Novatians. Vers. 22. OF ALL HIS INIQUITIES WHICH HE HAS DONE, I WILL NOT REMEMBER) There was something good in the deportation: for while the Republic stood, whoever had committed those graver sins, once the matter was brought to the notice of the judges, would die. In exile, with the laws' judgments ceasing, time was given for repentance, and through repentance, impunity was received. Thus, little by little, minds were prepared for the Gospel.

A most vain gloss, by which an illustrious promise is enervated. For here is promised to the truly penitent the remission of all iniquities, so much so that God wills not to remember them any longer. Grotius, on the contrary, twists these things toward impunity in forensic judgments, which did not exist in exile, for there was no lack of judges who would drag transgressors to punishment. This is not merely a preparation of minds for the Gospel: but it is a signal Evangelical promise. And we know from this promise that the Pelagian-Socinian hypothesis is most false, that in the writings of the Old Testament promises concerning the remission of sins were not handed down: Indeed, Peter testifies that ALL the Prophets bear witness to him, that all who believe in him receive remission of sins in the name of Christ, Acts 10:43. From that 'I WILL NOT REMEMBER,' some formerly gathered that God is not omniscient; but the words denote the affection and effect of knowledge in God: He does not wish to remember with a hostile affection, for the sake of punishment: because when a judge forgets an evil or a crime, he does not remember it, and the punishment perishes. God is said not to remember the impious when He does not show them benefits: He is said to remember the pious when He shows a benefit: of those who were impious but are converted, He is said not to remember, i.e., not to punish, as Hackspan has it here. Whence is refuted the error of the Papists that God does not pardon the punishment, but the guilt, and that the former must be suffered even after this life. Compare Jer. 31:34. But it is irrelevant what Becanus objects here from chapter 32:34 of Exodus, because there it is not a question of the penitent, but of the impious persevering in their impiety.

I WILL NOT REMEMBER) That is, I will not inflict punishments. IN HIS JUSTICE, WHICH HE HAS DONE, HE SHALL LIVE) Which he is doing. To which he devotes effort.

Latin:

Vers. 9. UT FACIAT VERITATEM) Ita Hebræi vo- cant, quidquid rectum est. VITA VIVET) Servabitur à gladio, peste, fame. Vers. 10. LATRONEM) Proprie פריץ est effractor, sed solet sumi latius. EFFUNDENTEM SANGUINEM) Nempe inno- xium. FECERIT UNUM DE ISTIS) De malis rebus, quas recensuimus, quas mox repetit. Vers. 11. ET HÆC QUIDEM OMNIA NON FA- CIENTEM) Qui omnia hæc (nempe bonas res ante dictas) non fecerit. Vers. 12. ABOMINATIONEM FACIENTEM) Sic vocat congressum cum femina vetito tempore. Vers. 13. MORTE MORIETUR) Immatura; ante diem, ut dicunt Poëtæ. SANGUIS EJUS IN IPSO ERIT) Reatus mor- tis. Ut hic Chaldæus. Vers. 14. TIMUERIT: ET NON FECERIT SIMI- LE EIS) Videns, inquam, tamen simile illis non fecerit. Ex- emplo paterno trahi se passus non sit. Vers. 18. PATER EJUS, QVIA CALUMNIATUS EST, ET VIM FECIT PATRI) Quia oppressit oppressio- ne, & rapinam rapuit. MORTUUS EST IN INIQVITATE SVA) Mo- rietur ob peccatum suum. Vers. 19. ET DICITIS: QVARE NON PORTAVIT FILIUS INIQVITATEM PATRIS?) Melius sic: Attamen dicitis cur? Id est, cur hoc ita generaliter affirmas? Non ne por- tat filius iniquitatem Patris sui? i. e. nonne ob parentum de- licta nos vapulamus? Respondet huic objectioni Deus. VIDELICET QVIA FILIVS JUDICIUM ET JUSTITIAM OPERATUS EST) Imo si filius jus & bene- ficentiam exercuerit. OMNIA PRÆCEPTA MEA) Vide quæ ad Luc. 1, 6. VIVET VITA) Felice.

De vita felice hic: v. 10. de conservatione à gladio, peste, fame, exposuit Grotius, quemadmodum ex ad- verso comminationem v. 13. Morte morietur, de morte immatura, ante diem explicat. At non de vita tantum temporali, & morte corporali vel immatura solum, sed de morte, & vita æterna hæ tum promis- siones, tum comminationes accipiendæ. Quia pœ- nitentibus promissiones factæ sunt non tantum temporalium & corporalium, sed maxime spirituali- um bonorum, remissionis peccatorum, & vitæ æternæ. Quid enim hæc aliud, quam remissionem peccatorum inferunt, omnium iniquitatum ejus, quas operatus est, non recordabor? Quid certius, quam quod vita & salus æterna promittatur, cum Deus testatur, nolo mortem impii, sed ut convertatur & vivat? Per pœni- tentiam & conversionem non effugimus mortem tem- poralem, sed æternam: neque vitam solum felicem in hoc sæculo consequimur, sed vitam beatam in altero sæculo. Vita felix in hoc seculo piis & impiis non- nunquam communis est, & fruuntur impii non ra- ro temporali felicitate præ fidelibus, & piis Ps. 37. & 73. Communis etiam est temporalis mors piis & im- piis, ac præripiuntur non raro morte immatura pii, superant impii. Et patiebantur sane infelicia fata, captivitatem, exilium & alia æque pii, Jeremias, E- zechiel aliique, ac reprobi in populo. Quapropter hæc accipi non possunt de sola morte & afflictione temporali. V. 20. JUSTITIA JUSTI SUPER EUM ERIT) Mer- ces justitiæ hic vocatur justitia, sicut pœna dicitur iniquitas. Vers. 21. EGERIT POENITENTIAM AB OMNIBUS PECCATIS SUIS) In Hebr. Aversus fuerit ab omnibus pecca tis suis: Id est: exutus vitiis virtuti se dederit. In Ebr. aliter habetur: At impius cum aversus vel conversus fuerit ab omnibus peccatis suis. Quæ de pœ- nitentia agunt, non de virtutis studio, fructu pœni- tentiæ. Patet autem hinc impiam revocari posse ad pœnitentiam contra Novatianos. Vers. 22. OMNIUM INIQVITATUM EJUS, QVAS OPERATUS EST, NON RECORDABOR) Aliquid bon erat in deportatione: nam stante Republica, qui illa gravio ra peccasset, re ad notitiam judicum perducta moriebatur In Exilio cessantibus ex lege judiciis, tempus dabatur a pœnitentiam, ac per pœnitentiam accipiebatur impunita Ita paulatim ad Evangelium præparabantur animi,

Vanissima glossa, qua promissio illustris enervatur. Nam promittitur hic vere poenitentibus omnium iniquitatum remissio, adeo, ut Deus earum non re- cordari velit amplius. Grot. ex adverso haec de- torquet ad impunitatem in judiciis forensibus, quae nulla erat in exilio, nam non deerant judices, qui praævaricatores ad supplicia raperent. Non hic tan- tum praeparatio animorum ad Evangelium est: sed insignis Evangelica est promissio. Et falsissimam esse istam Hypothesin Pelagio-Socinianam, quod in V. Test. scriptis non traditae sint promissiones de re- missione peccatorum, etiam ex hac promissione novimus: Imo testatur Petrus, quod OMNES Pro- phetae testimonium de eo perhibent, quod in nomine Christi remissionem peccatorum consequantur omnes, qui credunt in eum, Act. 10, 43. Ex illo NON RECOR- DABOR olim quidam colligebant, Deum non esse omniscium; sed verba notitiae affectum & effectum in Deo notant: non vult recordari affectu hostili, ad poenam: quia cum judex mali vel delicti oblivisci- tur, non recordatur, perit poena. Impiorum dicitur Deus non recordari, cum ipsis beneficia non exhi- bet: piorum dicitur recordari, cum beneficium exhibet: eorum, qui fuerunt impii, sed convertun- tur, dicitur non recordari, i. e. non punire, ut hic Hacksp. habet. Unde refellitur error Pontificior. quod Deus non condonet poenam, sed culpam, quodq; illa etiam post hanc vitam luenda sit. Conf. Jer. 31, 34. Alienum aute est, quod Becan. hic objicit e cap. 32, 34. Ex. quia ibi non de poenitentibus, sed impiis in sua impietate perseverantibus agitur.

NON RECORDABOR) Id est, non infligam poenas. IN JUSTITIA SUA, QUAM OPERATUS EST, VIVET) Quam operatur. Cui dat operam.

## 18:23
Vers. 23. IS IT OF MY WILL THAT THE IMPIOUS SHOULD DIE, AND NOT THAT HE SHOULD BE CONVERTED FROM HIS WAYS, AND LIVE) These comparisons are to be taken as in Hosea 6:6. For the sense is: I prefer that a man should turn himself away from his impiety and profit himself, rather than that, persisting in evil deeds, he should summon punishment upon himself.

Nay, these are to be understood not comparatively, but absolutely. For they sound absolutely. Nor is there any reason why one should depart from the native sense. Simply, therefore, God wills that man be converted and live. He does not merely prefer life to death. And concerning this philanthropy of His, He testifies most holily, insomuch that by interposing an oath He makes us more certain of His most gracious will, c. 33, 11. Cf. Heb. 6, 17. That which is had in v. 25, that the wicked man will die in his wickedness, that is explained by the distinction of the antecedent and consequent will of God. He does not will the death of the wicked, but that he be converted and live, as regards the antecedent will. But if the wicked man refuses to be converted, God wills that he die in his wickedness by His consequent will. These are not opposites: because the former will was not absolute, but ordered by a certain arrangement of means, which being neglected, the execution of divine judgment follows. Concerning which Damascene speaks thus, lib. 2. de Orthod. fid. c. 29. It is necessary to know that God προηγουμένως (by antecedent will) wills all to be saved and to attain His kingdom. For He did not form us to punish us, but that He might make us partakers of His goodness, as He is good. But He wills to punish those who sin, as He is just. Therefore the first is called the preceding will and acceptance, existing from Himself. The second, however, is the will and promise, existing from our cause. If these are to be taken only comparatively, as if God has only a greater delight when the wicked man is converted than when, persisting in evil deeds, he brings punishment upon himself, will it not follow from that, that God nevertheless has some delight in the damnation of the wicked, which openly contradicts the scope of this divine protestation?

Latin:

Vers. 23. NUMQVID VOLUNTATIS MEAE EST MORS IMPII, ET NON UT CONVERTATUR A VIIS SUIS, ET VIVAT) Comparate haec sumenda, ut Oseae 6, 6. Sensus enim est: Malo ut homo ab impietate sua se avertat, & sibi prosit, quam ut perstans in malis factis poe- nam in se accersat.

Imo non comparate, sed absolute haec intelligenda. Nam absolute sonant. Nec causa est, cur a sensu na- tivo discedatur. Simpliciter ergo vult Deus, ut ho- mo convertatur, & vivat. Non tantum mavult vitam quam mortem. Et de hac Φιλανθρωπίᾳ sua testatur sanctissime, adeo ut jurejurando interposito nos certiores reddat de gratiosissima voluntate c. 33, 11. Conf. Ebr. 6, 17. Quod a. v. 25. habetur, Impium in im- pietate sua moriturum, id expeditur distinctione voluntatis Dei antecedentis & consequentis. Non vult mortem impii, sed ut convertatur & vivat, quoad ante- cedentem voluntatem. At si impius converti renuat, vult Deus, ut in impietate sua moriatur voluntate consequente. Quae opposita non sunt: quia voluntas prior non erat absoluta, sed certa mediorum τάξει ordinata, quibus neglectis, sequitur judicii divini exequutio. De quo ita Damasc. lib. 2. de Orthod. fid. c. 29. Scire oportet Deum προηγουμένως (voluntate antecedente) velle omnes salvari, & regnum suum consequi. Non enim ad puniendum nos plasmavit, sed ut efficiat nos bonitatis suae participes, ut bonus. Pec- cantes autem punire vult ut justus. Dicitur igitur pri- ma praecedens voluntas & acceptatio ex ipso ex- istens. Secunda vero voluntas & promissio ex nostra causa existens. Si comparative tantum haec accipien- da, quasi Deus majorem solum delectationem ha- beat, cum impius convertitur, quam cum persistens in malis factis, poenam in se accersit, annon inde se- quetur, quod Deus aliquam tamen delectationem in damnatione impiorum habeat, quod aperte hu- jus protestationis divinae scopo repugnat?

## 18:24
Vers. 24. ALL HIS RIGHTEOUSNESSES WHICH HE HAD DONE SHALL NOT BE REMEMBERED) As he in Valerius Maximus said: You were Manlius to me when you were driving the Senones headlong: after you began to change, you became one of the Senones.

Thucydides well says: They deserve double punishment because instead of good they have become evil. Those teachers are pestilential who deny that what God testifies can both be done and be severely punished by Him, can be done.

IN TRANSGRESSION) On account of transgression. Thus shortly after in them, because of them. For the particle ב among the Hebrews has various meanings.

From this passage it is clear that a just man can fall from grace. Calvinists deny this: objecting in vain with Polanus and Amesius that the discourse here is about hypocrites: since indeed the just man is here manifestly opposed to the impious, and is said to live in justice if he perseveres, whence Wendelin himself acknowledges that this concerns a truly just man: But what the same person objects, that these things were said only conditionally, does not fit the text so well, in which there is not the condition IF, but when: nor does that rule have a place here. A condition posits nothing in being: because this is valid concerning a condition which is not given, nor can be given. But that this condition is posited as entirely possible is manifest. Therefore they distinguish between conditions which are used only for augmentation, and those which are posited for the sake of admonition. For in the latter it is necessary that the thing be possible to do: in the former, possibility is not always required. See the writings of the Remonstrants at Dordrecht, p. 218 et seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 24. OMNES JUSTITIAE EJUS, QVAS FECE- RAT NON RECORDABUNTUR) Ut ille apud Valer. Maximum dicebat: Manlius er as mihi, cum præcipites agebas Senonas: postquam mutari cœpisti, unus factus es ex Senonibus.

Bene Thucydides : Διπλασίας ζημίας ἀξιούς εἶσιν ὅτι ἀντ᾿ ἀ- γαθῶν κακοὶ γεγένηνται. Pestilentes sunt magistri, qui negant id fieri posse, quod Deus & fieri posse, & graviter a se puniri testatur.

IN PRÆVARICATIONE) Ob prævaricationem. Sic mox in eis, propter eas. Nam particula ב apud Hebræos varias habet significationes.

Ex hoc loco patet justum excidere posse gratia. Quod negant Calviniani: frustra excipientes cum Polano, & Amesio de hypocritis hic sermonem esse: siquidem manifeste hic justus opponatur impio, & in justitia vivere dicatur, si perseveret, unde Wende- linus ipse agnoscit de vere justo hic agi: Quod vero idem obvertit conditionaliter hæc tantum dicta es- se, neque textui adeo convenit, in quo non est con- ditio SI, sed cum: neque locum habet hic illa regula. Conditio nihil ponit in esse: quia hæc valet de con- ditione, quæ non datur, nec dari potest. Hanc vero conditionem ut omnino dabilem poni, manifestum est. Ideo distinguunt inter conditiones, quæ ad αυ- ξησιν tantum adhibentur, & quæ admonitionis cau- sa ponuntur. In his enim necesse est, rem esse factu possibilem: in illis non semper requiritur possibili- tas. Vid. sciptaRemonstrant. Dordrac. p. 218. seqq.

## 18:27
Ver. 27. HE HIMSELF SHALL QUICKEN HIS SOUL) That is, he shall save himself from an evil death, as the LXX rightly explain here. Verbs in Hiphil often have such a meaning.

Also in Piel permission is sometimes meant in the third [person], as Ex. 1:17, 1 Sam. 27:7, they permitted to live, they did not kill. Thus also Num. 31:15. Therefore, to quicken here is not to influence positively by some principle of vital operation, but to take care that he does not kill the soul which he could have killed in the meantime.

Latin:

Vers. 27. IPSE ANIMAM SVAM VIVIFICABIT) Id est, seimet servabit à mala morte, ut recte hic exponuntLXX. Verba in Hiphil sæpe talem significationem habent.

Etiam in Piel permissio tantum quandoque in tertia, ut Ex. 1, 17. 1. Sam. 27, 7. permiserunt vivere, non interfecerunt. Sic & Num. 31, 15. Non ergo vivifica- re hic est per principium aliquod operationis vita- lis positive influere, sed cavere ne quam interimere poterat, animam interimat.

## 18:30
V. 30. ACCORDING TO HIS WAYS) Present, not past.

BE CONVERTED) Turn yourselves to me.

AND DO PENANCE FROM ALL YOUR INIQUITIES) In the Hebrew: Turn yourselves away from all your impieties.

AND INIQUITY SHALL NOT BE TO YOU FOR RUIN) Lest it be to you for ruin.

Latin:

V. 30. JVXTA VIAS SVAS) Præsentes non præteritas.

CONVERTIMINI) Vertite vos ad me.

ET AGITE POENITENTIAM AB OMNIBVS INIQVITATIBUS VESTRIS) In Hebræo: Avertite vos ab omnibus impietatibus vestris.

ET NON ERIT VOBIS IN RUINAM INIQVI- TAS) Ne sit vobis in ruinam.

## 18:31
Ver. 31. MAKE TO YOURSELVES A NEW HEART, AND A NEW SPIRIT) The same act is elsewhere ascribed to God, elsewhere to man: to God as the primary cause, to man as one who freely follows God.

This gloss favors the Socinians, Arminians, and Papists, as if the cooperation of free will were established in the conversion of man to God. But the answer was already given by Augustine to the Pelagians who gathered similar things, in 'On Grace and Free Will' ch. 15, 16. That an admonition of duty is not a testimony concerning the powers implanted in our nature: We remember it is said to God, but 'be converted and you shall live': to whom it is said: 'convert us, O God.' We remember God saying: 'Cast away from you all your impieties': when He Himself justifies the impious. We remember Him saying: 'Make to yourselves a new heart and a new spirit': who says: 'I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will give you.' How therefore does He who says: 'make to yourselves,' say this: 'I will give to you'? Why does He command, if He Himself is about to give? Why does He give, if man is about to do it, unless because He gives what He commands, and helps him to do what He commands him. For to this end is valid what is written: 'If you will, you shall keep the commandments': so that man, who has willed and has not been able, may know that he does not yet fully will, and may pray that he may have such a will as suffices to fulfill the commandments. For thus he is helped to do what is commanded: for then it is useful to will, when we are able: and then it is useful to be able, when we will. For what does it profit if we will what we cannot, or if we do not will what we can. It is certain that we will when we will, but He makes it so that we will the good, of which it was said, which I placed a little before, that the will is prepared by the Lord, of which it was said: 'The steps of a man shall be directed by the Lord, and he shall will his way': of which it was said: 'It is God who works in us both to will and to do.' It is certain that we act when we act, but He acts so that we may act, by offering most effective powers to the will, He who said: I will cause that you walk in my justifications, and observe my judgments, and do them. When He says: I will cause that you do: what else does He say, but I will take away from you the heart of stone, from which you were not doing, and I will give a heart of flesh, so that you may do? And what is this, but I will take away the hard heart, from which you were not doing, and I will give an obedient heart, from which you may do. These are the words of St. Augustine. Furthermore, these things were said to the circumcised Israelites established in the Church of God, who had eyes to see, and ears to hear, that is, the preventing and present grace of God, which they could admit, and through it, once admitted, they themselves also could subsequently work, Jer. 12, 2. Moreover, when men converted by God are said to convert themselves, the continuation of conversion is noted, by the amendment of daily life. Compare Deut. 10, 16. Ezech. 38, 18. Joel. 2, 12. Finally, it is a non-sequitur to gather the faculties and powers of man from divine commands. Who will admit that in Lazarus there were powers to raise himself and to come forth, because he was ordered to come forth, Lazarus come out. Therefore, such an inference is not to be granted: That which God commands us to do, that is produced by our own free motion. We are commanded to rise from spiritual death, Eph. 5, 10, yet that is not placed within our power. But just as we can contribute nothing to our bodily resuscitation, so we can contribute equally nothing at all to our spiritual resuscitation and conversion. Wherefore, by such sayings our inability is demonstrated and the desire for grace is sharpened in us; indeed, grace itself is conferred by such Evangelical exhortations, which have attached to them the promises of grace, as an effective means of the Holy Spirit. Nor is anything else required of us, than that we do not neglect the means of conversion, and that we do not resist the divine grace intending the same.

WHY WILL YOU DIE) Why would you die? why would you voluntarily approach death?

Latin:

Vers. 31. FACITE VOBIS COR NOVVM, ET SPI- RITVM NOVM) Idem actus alibi Deo, alibi homini ad- scribitur: Deo ut causæ præcipuæ, homini, ut Deum libere sequenti.

Favet hæc glossa Socinianis, Arminianis, & Pa- pistis, quasi cooperatio liberi arbitrii adstruatur in conversione hominis ad Deum. Responsum au- tem jam ab Augustino Pelagianis similia colligen- tibus, de gratia & libero arbitrio c. 15. 16. Admoni- tionem officii non esse testimonium de viribus na- turæ nostræ insitis: Meminerimus Deum dicitur, sed convertimini & vivetis: cui dicitur: converte nos Deus. Meminerimus Deum dicere: Projicite à vo- bis omnes impietates vestras: cum ipse justificet impium. Meminerimus ipsum dicere, facite vobis cor novum & spiritum novum: qui dicit: dabo vo- bis cor novum, & spiritum novum dabo vobis. Quomodo ergo quod dicit: facite vobis: hoc dicit, dabo vobis? Quare jubet, si ipse daturus est? Quare dat, si homo facturus est, nisi quia dat, quod jubet, & adjuvat ut faciat cui jubet. Ad hoc enim valet quod scriptum est: Si volueris, conservabis mandata: ut homo, qui voluerit & non potuerit, nondum se ple- ne velle cognoscat, & oret, ut habeat tantam volun- tatem, quanta sufficit ad implenda mandata. Sic quippe adjuvatur, ut faciat, quod jubetur: tunc e- nim utile est velle, cum possumus: & tunc utile est posse, cum volumus. Nam quid prodest, si quod non possumus, volumus, aut si quod possumus, nolumus. Certum est nos velle cum volumus, sed ille facit, ut velimus bonum, de quo dictum est, quod paulo ante po- sui, quod preparatur voluntas à Domino, de quo di- ctum est; A Domino gressus hominis dirigentur, & viam ejus volet: de quo dictum est: Deus est, qui operatur in nobis vellet & operari. Certum est nos facere cum facimus, sed ille facit ut faciamus, præ- bendo vires efficacissimas voluntati, qui dixit: Fa- ciam ut in justificationibus meis ambuletis, & judi- cia mea observatis,& faciatis. Cum dicit: Faciam ut faciatis: quid aliud dicit, nisi auferam à vobis cor la- pideum, unde non faciebatis, & dabo cor carneum, ut faciatis? Et hoc quid est, nisi auferam cor durum, unde non faciebatis & dabo cor obediens, unde facia- tis. Hæc S. Augustinus. Præterea dicta hæc sunt ad Israëlitas circumcisos & in Ecclesia Dei constitu- tos, qui habebant oculos ad videndum, & aures ad au- diendum, id est, prævenientem & præsentem Dei gra- tiam, quam poterant admittere, per eamque admis- sam ipsi quoque deinceps operari, Jer. 12, 2. Porro cum homines conversi à Deo seipsos convertere dicuntur, conversionis notatur continuatio, quotidia- næ vitæ emendatione. Confer Deut. 10, 16. Ezech. 38, 18. Joel. 2, 12. Denique ἀνανόλιθον est, ex mandatis divinis colligere facultates, & vires hominis. Quis admittet, in Lazaro vires fuisse se suscitandi & pro- deundi, quia jussus est prodire, Lazare veni foras. Itaque non concedenda ejusmodi illatio: Quod Deus nos facere jubet, id à motu nostro libero pro- ducitur. Jubemur surgere à morte spirituali, Ephes. 5, 10. nec tamen id in facultate nostra situm est. Sed uti nihil cooperari possumus ad corpora- tem nostri resuscitationem, ita æque nihil prorsus ad spiritualem resuscitationem & conversionem no- stri cooperari possumus. Quapropter dictis ejus- modi ἀδυναμία nostra demonstratur ac desideri- um gratiæ in nobis acuitur, imo gratia etiam ejus- modi Evangelicis cohortationibus, quæ annexas ha- bent gratiæ promissiones, tanquam medio efficaci Spiritus Sancti confertur. Neque à nobis quic- quam aliud requiritur, quam ut media conversio- nis non negligamus, divinæque gratiæ eandem in- tendenti ne resistamus.

QVARE MORIEMINI) Quare moreremini? cur ultro accederetis mortem?

## 18:32
V. 32. I DESIRE NOT THE DEATH OF HIM WHO DIES) Comparatively, as we have just said, that is, the life of one changed for the better pleases me more than the punishment of the obstinate. This does not prevent there being some limit of mercy with God, as appeared in Pharaoh, the Canaanites, and others. See 1 Sam. 2, 25. 2 Chron. 36, 16.

We have shown before that this comparative sense is too diluted. But concerning a limit of the mercy of God, there is nothing in the scriptures: which everywhere proclaim the supreme mercy of God, having no end; nowhere is a limit fixed for it, but we are commanded to hear the voice of God graciously calling us, the end of which is our gracious conversion. Exhort yourselves EVERY DAY, while it is called TODAY, that none of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin, Heb. 3, 13. Pharaoh was exhorted by God by a living voice and by miracles to repentance up to the final term of his life. For even then, when the Israelite was seen to cross through the Red Sea on dry ground, there was still time to return to a sounder mind, to desist from their persecution, and from warring against God. Nor were the Canaanites excluded from mercy by any absolute decree: rather, they could have humbled themselves and obtained grace after seeing and hearing the miracles, which is evident from the example of Rahab and the Gibeonites. What is held in 1 Sam. 2, 25 concerning the sons of Eli, that the Lord willed to kill them, does not teach that all grace was denied to them by some absolute decree, but that their guilt was so constituted that their own obstinacy rendered the intercessions of others fruitless: since they did not listen to the voice of their Father at all, כִי, that is, although (for we judge that this particle should be rendered thus, and Mr. Tarnovius shows this in Exerc. Bibl.) GOD willed to kill them. That in the Jewish people 2 Chron. 36, 16 there remained no remedy, that is not a denial of divine mercy, but impenitence and obstinacy made the desperate and incurable evil of the nation. For this is understood either concerning the curing of guilt and obstinacy, because it could be amended by no warnings, by no threats, or concerning the curing of punishment and the averting of divine wrath, which sense, if it holds, the reason why the wrath of God could no longer be averted was already rendered, because, to wit, they were unwilling to hear the Prophets of the Lord, and by that contumacious disobedience they kindled the fury of God, and irritated him more and more.

Latin:

V. 32. NOLO MORTEM MORIENTIS) Comparatè, ut modo diximus, id est, magis me juvat vita mutati in me- lius, quam contumacium pœna. Hoc non obstat, quin sit apud Deum limes aliquis misericordiæ, ut apparuit in Pha- raone, Cananæis & aliis. Vide 1. Sam, 2, 25. 1. Paralip. 35, 16.

Comparatum istum sensum nimis dilutum esse antea ostendimus. De limite autem misericordiæ Dei nihil in scripturis: quæ undiquaque misericor- diam Dei summam nullumque finem habentem deprædicant; nuspiam limes ei figitur, sed vocem Dei nos gratiose vocitantis audire jubemur, cujus finis est, nostra gratiosa conversio. Adhortamini vosmet ipsos per SINGULOS DIES, donec HODIE cognominatur, ut non obduretur quis ex vobis falla- cia peccati, Ebr. 3, 13. Pharao hortatus à Deo vi- va voce & miraculis ad pœnitentiam fuit usque ad extremum vitæ terminum. Nam etiam tunc ubi transire per mare rubrum sicco pede videbat Israelita, adhuc tempus erat ad saniorem mentem redeundis, à persecutione eorum desistendi, & con- tra Deum belligerandi. Neque Cananæi absoluto aliquo decreto à misericordia exclusi erant: quin potuerint visis & auditis miraculis sese humiliare & gratiam consequi, quod exemplo Rahabi & Gibeo nitarum constat. Quod 1. Sam. 2, 25. de filiis Heli ha- betur, quod eos Dominus occidere voluerit, non docet omnem gratiam ipsis absoluto quodam decreto de- negatam, sed culpam ita comparatam fuisse, ut alio- rum intercessiones frustraneas reddiderit ipsorum pertinacia: siquidem vocem Patris nullatenus au- dierint, כִי, id est, quamvis (sic enim particulam hanc reddendam censemus, & ostendit id Dn. Tarnovius in Exerc. Bibl.) occidere eos DEUS voluerit. Quod in populo Judaico 2. Paralip. 36, 16. nulla superfuit curatio, id non misericor- diæ divinæ abnegatio, sed impænitentia & perti- naciæ malum desperatum & inemendabile fecit. Nam id vel de curatione culpæ & pertinaciæ intelli- gitur, quod illa nullis monitionibus, nullis minis emendari potuerit, vel de curatione pœnæ & aversio- ne iræ divinæ, qui sensus si obtineat, causa cur averti amplius ira Dei nequeat, jam reddita fuit, quia sci- licet Prophetas Domini audire nolebant, & contu- maci illa inobedientia furorem Dei incendebant, & magis magisque irritabant.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX. The Prophet's lamentation for the captivity of the lioness and the lion's whelps, the queen, the mother, and the sons Joahaz and Joakim, and for Jerusalem, which had been a wide vine, to be laid waste.

Ver. 1. TAKE UP A LAMENTATION) Utter laments. OVER THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL) נשיאי, that is, kings, as above 7, 27. Ver. 2. WHY DID THY MOTHER A LIONESS LIE DOWN AMONG LIONS) Better: What (was) thy mother? (The Jewish nation) a lioness lying down among lions. That is, living safely among so many neighboring kings. Allusion is made to the place Gen. 49, 9. IN THE MIDST OF THE LION'S WHELPS SHE BROUGHT UP HER WHELPS) She was fruitful, to the envy of her neighbors. Ver. 3. AND SHE BROUGHT UP ONE OF HER WHELPS: IT BECAME A LION, AND LEARNED TO CATCH THE PREY, AND TO DEVOUR MEN) Joahaz became cruel, 2 Kings 23, 32. Ver. 4. AND NOT WITHOUT ITS WOUNDS THEY TOOK HIM) In the Hebrew: In their pit he was taken. THEY BROUGHT HIM IN CHAINS INTO THE LAND OF EGYPT) In the Hebrew: with hooks. But by that metaphor are signified fetters, 2 Kings 23, 33. Ver. 5. WHICH WHEN SHE HAD SEEN THAT SHE WAS WEAKENED, AND HER EXPECTATION PERISHED) Which (the Jewish nation) seeing when she had expected (for some time) that her hope had perished: that is, that Joahaz was not returned by her prayers from the Egyptian. SHE TOOK ONE OF HER WHELPS, SHE MADE HIM A LION) She acknowledged Eliakim or Joachim as king by the consent of the kings of the Egyptians, 2 Kings 23, 30. 2 Chron. 36, 4. Ver. 6. WHO WALKED AMONG LIONS) He lived in royal fashion. AND LEARNED TO CATCH PREY, AND TO DEVOUR MEN) He himself also became cruel. See 2 Kings 23, 37. 2 Chron. 36, 5. Ver. 7. HE LEARNED TO MAKE WIDOWS) The Chaldean reads ידע אלמנותיו, he corrupted their palaces. Most excellent. The Chaldean interpretation is preferred to the Hebrew text, but the Hebrew text holds itself correctly. For אלמנה denotes a widow. And although it may also occur concerning widowed places, Lam. 1, 1. 2 Chron. 32, 19. Nevertheless, that sense, he knew widowed places, is null. He is said to have known widows, because he may have plotted against their fortunes, and perhaps their chastity, but not widowed places. It seems that the error of the Chaldean gave the occasion, because it is added AND HE DEVASTATED THEIR CITIES. Maldonatus observes that ידע also signifies to crush, and so the Chaldean did not read otherwise than it is now held, even if he translates: he destroyed his palaces. But for the Vulgate he notes that the text can be explained thus: He knew his widows, to wit, of the man whom he killed. Because he had said before, that he devoured men: That he experiences many widows, if indeed he kills their husbands.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX. Planctus Prophetæ ob leænæ & leunculorum, reginæ, matris, & filiorum Joachaz, & Jo- jakim, captivitatem, & Jerusalem, quæ vi- nea lata fuerat, vastandam.

Vers. 1. ASSVME PLANCTVM) Profer lamenta. SVPER PRINCIPES ISRAEL) נשיאי, id est, re- ges, ut supra 7, 27. Vers. 2. QVARE MATER TVA LEÆNA INTER LEONES CVBAVIT) Melius: Quid (fuit) mater tua? (Judæa ge s) leæna cubans inter leones Id est, tuta vivens in- ter tot vicinos reges. Alluditur ad locum Gen. 49, 9. IN MEDIO LEVNCVLORVM ENTRIVIT CATVLOS SVOS) Fœcunda fuit, invi.entibus vicinis. Vers. 3. ET EDVXIT VNVM DE LEVNCVLIS SVIS: LEO FACTVS EST, ET DIDICIT CAPERE PRÆDAM, HOMINEMQVE COMEDERE) Joacha- zus crudelis factus, 2. Reg 23, 32. Vers. 4. ET NON ABSQVE VVLNERIBVS SVIS CEPERVNT EVM) In Hebræo: In scrobe eorum captus est. ADDVXERVNT EVM IN CATENIS IN TER- RAM ÆGYPTI) In Hebræo: hamis. Sed per eam meta- phoram significantur compedes, 2. Reg. 23, 33. Vers 5. QVÆ CVM VIDISSET QVONIAM IN- FIRMATA EST, ET PERIIT EXPECTATIO EJVS Quæ (gens Judæa) videns cum expectasset (aliquandi) periis- se spem suam: id est, non reddi suis precibus ab Ægyptio Joachazum. TVLIT VNVM DE LEVNCVLIS SVIS, LEO- NEM FECIT EVM) Eliachimum sive Joachimum regis Ægyptiorum concessu regem agnovit, 2. Reg. 23, 30. 2. Pa- ralip. 36, 4. Vers. 6. QVI INCEDEBAT INTER LEONES) Re- gio more vivebat. ET DIDICIT PRÆDAM CAPERE, ET HO- MINEM DEVORARE Factus est & ipse crudelis. Vid. 2. Reg. 23, 37. 2. Paralip. 36, 5. Vers. 7. DIDICIT VIDVAS FACERE) Chaldæus le- git ידע אלמנותיו, corrupit palatia eorum. Optime. PRæfertur ita Chaldæa interpretatio Ebræo tex- tui, sed recte se habet Ebræus textus. Nam אלמנה viduam notat. Etsi autem de locis viduatis etiam occurrat, Thr. 1, 1. 2. Chron. 32, 19. Nullus ta- men sensus ille, cognovit loca viduata. Viduas co- gnovisse dicitur, quod earum fortunis, forte & pu- dicitiæ insidiatus fuerit, non autem loca viduata. Viedtur παραράματι Chaldæi occasionem dedisse, quod adjiciatur ET CIVITATES EORUM DEVASTAVIT. Maldonatus observat ידע etiam significate conte- rere, adeoque Chaldæum non legisse aliter, quam nunc habetur, etsi vertat; destruxit palatia ejus. Pro Vulgata vero notat, ita textum exponi posse: Novit viduas ejus scil. hominis, quem occidit. Quia dixerat antea, ipsum homines devorare: Quod experiatur multas viduas, siquidem viros eorum occidat.

## 19:7
Ver. same. AND THE LAND AND THE FULNESS THEREOF IS MADE DESOLATE AT THE VOICE OF HIS ROARING) His fulness, supply fled. The fulness of the land are the men; these were fleeing for fear of the cruel master.

Latin:

Vers. eod. ET DESOLATA EST TERRA ET PLENITV- DO EJVS A VOCE RVGITVS ILLIVS) Plenitudo ejus, supple fugit. Plenitudo terræ sunt homines; hi præ metu crudelis domini fugiebant.

## 19:8
Ver. 8. THE NATIONS CAME TOGETHER AGAINST HIM FROM EVERY SIDE) The Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, Ammonites, 2 Kings 24, 2. IN THEIR WOUNDS HE WAS TAKEN) In their pit, as above 4. Ver. 9. IN CHAINS) With hooks, as above 4.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CONVENERVNT ADVERSVS EVM GENTES VNDIQVE) Chaldæi, Syri, Moabitæ, Ammonitæ, 2. Reg. 24, 2. IN VVLNERIBVS EARVM CAPTVS EST) In scrobe earum, ut supra 4. Vers. 9. IN CATENIS) Hamis, ut supra 4.

## 19:9
Ver. same. TO THE KING OF BABYLON) 2 Chron. 36, 6. THAT HIS VOICE MIGHT NO MORE BE HEARD UPON THE MOUNTAINS OF ISRAEL) That he might no longer be a terror to anyone, as above 7. Ver. 10. THY MOTHER) Another comparison, pertaining to the same Jewish nation. IN THY BLOOD) In thy quiet: that is, when thou Ezekiel and others with thee were living quietly at home. THOU ART PLANTED BY THE WATER) As above 17, 8. HER FRUIT) The people grew. AND HER BRANCHES) Her riches were increased. Ver. 11. AND THERE WERE MADE IN HER STRONG RODS INTO SCEPTRES OF THEM THAT BEAR RULE) From the family of David, now this one, now that one, arrived at the kingdom. AND HER STATURE WAS EXALTED AMONG THE BRANCHES) The stock itself grew among its branches. Ver. 12. AND SHE WAS PLUCKED UP) But she was plucked up: the nation deported. AND CAST DOWN TO THE GROUND) Held in contempt. A BURNING WIND) An Eastern wind, as above 17, 10. DRIED UP HER FRUIT) He killed many of the people. HER STRONG RODS WITHERED, AND WERE DRIED UP) The kings were captured. FIRE HATH CONSUMED IT) Divine wrath pursued the kings even to destruction. Ver. 13. AND NOW SHE IS TRANSPLANTED INTO THE DESERT, IN A LAND NOT PASSED THROUGH AND DRY) The worst of the Chaldean lands were given to them to cultivate. Ver. 14. AND FIRE IS GONE OUT FROM A ROD OF HER BRANCHES, WHICH HATH CONSUMED HER FRUIT) Divine wrath, because of the crime of Zedekiah, gave the people over to slaughter. AND THERE IS NO MORE IN HER A STRONG ROD, A SCEPTRE OF SUCH AS BEAR RULE) There are no longer any kings from her. IT IS A LAMENTATION, AND IT SHALL BE FOR A LAMENTATION) This is the Prophecy of a lamentation that will truly come to pass.

Latin:

Vers. eod. AD REGEM BABYLONIS) 2. Paralip. 36, 6. NE AUDIRETVR VOX EJUS ULTRA SUPER MONTES ISRAEL) Ne cui ultra terrori esset, ut supra 7. Vers. 10. MATER TUA) Altera comparatio, ad ean- dem gentem Judæam pertinens. IN SANGUINE TUO) In quiete tua: id est, cum tu Ezechiel & alii tecum quiete domi viveretis. SUPER AQVAM PLANTATA ES) Ut supra 17, 8. FRUCTUS EJUS) Crevit populus. ET FRONDES EJUS) Auctæ opes. Vers. 11. FACTÆ SUNT EI VIRGÆ SOLIDÆ IN SCEPTRA DOMINANTIUM) Ex familia Davidis mo- do hic, modo ille ad regnum pervenere. ET EXALTATA EST STATVRA EJUS INTER FRONDES) Stirps ipsa inter suas frondes crevit. Vers. 12. ET EVULSA EST) Sed evulsa est: gens deportata. IN TERRAMQVE PROJECTA) Contemtui habita. VENTUS URENS) Ventus Orientalis, ut sup. 17, 10. SICCAVIT FRUCTUM EJUS) Multos de popu- lo occidit. MARCVERUNT, ET AREFACTÆ SVNT VIRGÆ ROBORIS EJUS) Reges capti. IGNIS COMEDIT EAM) Ira divina reges ad ex- itium usque persecuta est. Vers. 13. ET NUNC TRANSPLANTATA EST IN DESERTUM IN TERRA INVIA ET SITIENTE) Pes- sima terræ Chaldaicæ illis data sunt excolenda. Vers. 14. ET EGRESSUS EST IGNIS DE VIRGA RA- MORUM EJUS, QVI FRUCTVM EJUS COMEDIT) Ira divina ob crimen Sedeciæ, populum occidioni de- didit. ET NON FUIT IN EA VIRGA FORTIS SCE- PTRVM DOMINANTIUM) Nulli ultra ex ea sunt reges. PLANCTUS EST, ET ERIT IN PLANCTUM) Hæc est Prophetia planctus vere eventuri.

## 20:1 Argument
THE FOURTH REVELATION. CHAPTER XX.

The Lord denies that he will answer the elders, because the children of Israel have transgressed both in Egypt, and in the desert, and in the land of promise. He promises, however, that he will finally recall them into their own land, in which they may serve him: he also commands him to prophesy against the southern forest.

Ver. 1. THE MEN OF THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL CAME) Those legates sent by Zedekiah, of whom above c. 14. this happened upon the return of the legates. TO ASK THE LORD) To seek counsel concerning their affairs. Ver. 4. IF THOU JUDGEST THEM, IF THOU JUDGEST, SON OF MAN) Whether thou wouldst plead for them, whether thou wouldst plead for them, son of man? That is, wouldst thou wish to defend the cause of such wicked men? For שפוט is often to plead, and את not rarely signifies for. THE ABOMINATIONS OF THEIR FATHERS) Which they themselves also have followed. Ver. 5. I LIFTED UP MY HAND) I swore to them, Exod. 3, 6. Thus this expression is also placed below 15. I APPEARED TO THEM IN THE LAND OF EGYPT) I was known to them through miracles. Ver. 7. THE OFFENCES OF THEIR EYES) In the Hebrew: The abominations of their eyes: that is, the idols to which eyes are lifted up, as we had above 18, 6. Ver. 8. AND I SAID: THAT I WOULD POUR OUT MY INDIGNATION UPON THEM) I had said that I would also pour it out. So also below 13. I had threatened them with pestilence or the sword while they were still in Egypt, Exod. 5. 3. Vers. 9. AND I DID) Nevertheless I did. Well for them, to be sure. FOR MY NAME’S SAKE) Because Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, had been called mine. Vers. 11. I BROUGHT THEM FORTH THEREFORE OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT) I caused them to go out. Vers. 11. MY STATUTES) they are חקים, which bind for this reason, because they have been so ordained.

Latin:

QVARTA REVELATIO. CAPUT XX.

Dominus negat se senioribus responsurum, quia & in Ægypto, & deserto, & in terra promissionis, prævaricati sunt filii Israel. Promittit tamen denique se eos in terram suam revocaturum, in qua sibi serviant: ju- bet etiam prophetare contra saltum meri- dianum.

Vers. 1. VENERVNT VIRI DE SENIORIBVS ISRAEL) Legati illi à Sedecia missi, de quibus supra c. 14. factum hoc in reditu legatorum. UT INTERROGARENT DOMINVM) Ut con- silium exposcerent de rebus suis. Vers. 4. SI JUDICAS EOS, SI JUDICAS, FILI HO- MINIS) An pro eis litigares, an pro eis litigares, fili hominis? Id est, vellesne tam improborum causam defendere? Nam שפוט sæpe est litigare, & את non raro pro significat. ABOMINATIONES PATRUM EORUM) Quas & ipsi secuti sunt. Vers. 5. LEVAVI MANVM MEAM) Juravi eis, Exod. 3, 6. Sic locutio hæc & infra ponitur 15. APPARVI EIS IN TERRA ÆGYPTI) Cogni- tus eis sum per miracula. Vers. 7. OFFENSIONES OCULORUM SUORUM) In Hebræo: Abominationes oculorum: id est, idola ad quæ attolluntur oculi, ut supra habuimus 18, 6. Vers. 8. ET DIXI: UT EFFUNDEREM INDIGNATIO- NEM MEAM SUPER EOS) Dixeram & me effusurum. Sic & infra 13. Minatus illis eram pestem aut gladium cum in Ægypto adhuc essent, Exod. 5. 3. Vers. 9. ET FECI) Attamen feci. Bene illis scilicet. PROPTER NOMEN MEUM) Quia Abrahamus, Isaac us, Jacobus, mei vocati fuerant. Vers. 10. EJECI ERGO EOS DE TERRA ÆGYPTI) Egredi feci. Vers. 11. PRÆCEPTA MEA) חקים sunt, quæ ideo obligant, quia ita constituta sunt.

## 20:11
AND MY JUDGMENTS) משפטי, are those which contain natural equity in themselves.

WHICH IF A MAN DO, HE SHALL LIVE IN THEM) A long and happy life, which was promised to those fulfilling the law; the Chaldean refers these and other things to eternal life: naturally, because they hoped for it, though not by the covenant of the law.

Why not by the covenant of the law? For in the law, eternal life was certainly promised to those observing it, just as, conversely, eternal death was pronounced upon those violating it. And how could they even hope for it without a divine promise, since the foundation of hope is solely the promise of God, or how would the Chaldean have interpreted it concerning eternal life, unless he had believed that the same was promised in part? See what we said at Leviticus 19:5.

Latin:

ET JUDICIA MEA) משפטי, sunt ea quæ natu- ralem in se æquitatem continent.

QVÆ FACIENS HOMO VIVET IN EIS) Vi- tam longam ac felicem, quæ promissa legem implentibus, Chaldæus hæc & alia ad vitam æternam refert: nimirum, quia eam sperabant, non tamen ex legis pacto.

QVidni ex legis pacto? nam in lege utique pro- missa erat observantibus eam vita æterna, uti ex adverso eam violantibus indicta æterna mors. Et quomodo vel sperare eam poterant sine pro- missione divina, quum spei fundamentum pro- missio Dei unice sit, vel Chaldæus de æterna vita in- terpretatus esset, nisi eandem ex parte promissam credidisset. Vide quæ ad Levit. 19, 5. diximus.

## 20:12
Verse 12. MOREOVER ALSO I GAVE THEM MY SABBATHS) That is, the law concerning the rest to be observed on the Sabbaths.

THAT THEY MIGHT BE A SIGN BETWEEN ME AND THEM) So that they might also be distinguished by the matter from other peoples, to whom some tradition of the Sabbath had indeed reached, but not with that law of rest, as we said in book 5 of the truth of the Christian religion.

AND THAT THEY MIGHT KNOW THAT I AM THE LORD THAT SANCTIFIETH THEM) That they might assemble on the Sabbath day, and proclaim my benefits toward them.

Latin:

Vers. 12. INSUPER ET SABBATA MEA DEDI EIS) Id est, legem de quiete observanda in Sabbatis.

UT ESSENT SIGNUM INTER ME ET EOS) Ut etiam re à populis aliis discriminarentur, ad quos aliqua quidem Sabbati traditio pervenerat, sed non cum illa quie- tis lege, ut diximus ad librum 5. de veritate religionis Christianæ.

ET SCIRENT QVIA EGO DOMINUS SAN- CTIFICANS ILLOS) Ut die Sabbati convenirent, & mea in se beneficia prædicarent.

## 20:13
Verse 13. THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL PROVOKED ME IN THE WILDERNESS) Not only in Egypt, but also when they had already been led out, they provoked me both more often and in many ways.

Latin:
