Vers. 13. IRRITAVERUNT ME DOMUS ISRAËL IN DESERTO) Non in Ægypto tantum, sed etiam cum jam educti essent, & sæpius & multis modis me irritarunt.

## 20:14
Verse 14. I LIFTED UP MY HAND UNTO THEM IN THE WILDERNESS) I swore against them. See Psalm 95:11.

Latin:

Vers. 14. LEVAVI MANUM MEAM SUPER EOS IN DESERTO) Contra eos juravi. Vide Psal. 95, 11.

## 20:16
Verse 16. FOR THEIR HEART WENT AFTER THEIR IDOLS) Especially in the land of Midian. Numbers 25.

Latin:

Vers. 16. POST IDOLA ENIM COR EORUM GRADIEBATUR) Maxime in terra Madian. Num. 25.

## 20:17
Verse 17. NEITHER DID I MAKE AN END OF THEM IN THE WILDERNESS) That is, I did not extinguish the whole nation.

Latin:

Vers. 17. NEC CONSUMPSI EOS IN DESERTO) Id est, gentem totam non extinxi.

## 20:21
Verse 21. AND THE CHILDREN REBELLED AGAINST ME) Even the children. This is to be referred to the times of the judges.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET EXACERBAVERUNT ME FILII) Etiam filii. Referendum hoc ad judicum tempora.

## 20:22
Verse 22. NEVERTHELESS I WITHDREW MINE HAND) I restrained myself, so that I would not destroy them.

Latin:

Vers. 22. AVERTI AUTEM MANUM MEAM) Continui me, ne eos perderem.

## 20:23
VERS. 23. I LIFTED UP MY HAND AGAIN TO THEM IN THE WILDERNESS) And yet I had sworn to them in the desert: namely, I had denounced grave threats against them, if they should spurn the law. Deut. 11 & 28.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ITERUM LEVAVI MANUM MEAM IN EOS IN SOLITUDINE) Atqui adhuc in deserto illis jura- veram: nempe minas graves illis denuntiaveram, si legem spernerent. Deut. 11. & 28.

## 20:25
VERS. 25. AND I GAVE THEM STATUTES THAT WERE NOT GOOD, AND JUDGMENTS WHEREBY THEY SHOULD NOT LIVE) I took away their understanding, so that, having despised my laws, they made for themselves laws that were harsh and deadly. Thus the Chaldean here.

Compare Hackspan on the various interpretations of this passage in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET EGO DEDI EIS PRÆCEPTA NON BONA, ET JUDICIA IN QVIBUS NON VIVENT) Mentem ipsis ademi, ita ut meis legibus contemtis, ipsi sibi leges facerent duras atque mortiferas. Ita Chaldæus hic.

Conf. de variis interpretationibus hujus loci Hackspanius in h. l.

## 20:26
VERS. 26. AND I POLLUTED THEM IN THEIR OWN GIFTS) I permitted them to perform sacrilegious rites.

IN THAT THEY CAUSED TO PASS THROUGH THE FIRE ALL THAT OPENETH THE WOMB) I had willed that the firstborn be redeemed: they imposed upon themselves that they should offer them to Moloch for death.

BECAUSE OF THEIR TRANSGRESSIONS) I directed this in such a way that it might appear how, having forsaken a good God, they adopted for themselves evil ones.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET POLLUI EOS IN MUNERIBUS SUIS) Permisi ut sacrilega sacra facerent.

CUM OFFERRENT OMNE QVOD APERIT VULVAM) Ego primogenitos redimi volueram: illi sibi imposuerunt, ut Molocho eos ad mortem offerrent.

PROPTER DELICTA SUA) Hoc ita direxi, ut appareret quam bono Deo deserto, quam malos sibi ipsi adsciscerent.

## 20:27
VERS. 27. YET IN THIS YOUR FATHERS HAVE BLASPHEMED ME) Yet further they treated me with reproaches. Even those who did not perform rites to the gods of the nations performed rites to me in forbidden places.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ADHUC ET IN HOC BLASPHEMA- VERUNT ME PATRES) Adhuc amplius probris me affe- cere. Etiam qui Diis gentium sacra non fecere, mihi sacra fecerunt in locis vetitis.

## 20:28
VERS. 28. THEY SAW EVERY HIGH HILL) Those hills pleased them. Isa. 57, 7.

THEY OFFERED THERE THE SAVOUR OF THEIR SWEETNESS) They made incense from aromatics.

Latin:

Vers. 28. VIDERUNT OMNEM COLLEM EXCEL- SUM) Placuerunt eis colles isti. Esa. 57, 7.

TE POSUERUNT IBI ODOREM SUAVITA- TIS SUÆ) Suffitus ex aromatis fecere.

## 20:29
VERS. 29. AND I SAID UNTO THEM: WHAT IS THE HIGH PLACE WHEREUNTO YE GO) In Hebrew: במה. Now the neighboring nations called their altars by this name: whence also the Greek βωμοὶ. Why do you go there rather than into my temple: what do you see in it that is excellent? I have often warned them of this through the prophets.

AND THE NAME THEREOF IS CALLED HIGH PLACE UNTO THIS DAY) Nevertheless, even today it is called במה: That is, both the custom and the very word taken from profane nations remain, whereas I have called the altar consecrated to me מזבח.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ET DIXI AD EOS: QVID EST EX- CELSUM AD QVOD VOS INGREDIMINI) In Hebræo: במה. Sic autem gentes vicinæ vocabant suas aras: unde & Græcum βωμοὶ. Cur illuc potius itis, quam in templum meum: quid in eo videtis eximii? Hæc per pro- phetas eos sæpe monui.

ET VOCATUM EST NOMEN EJUS EXCEL- SUM, USQVE AD HANC DIEM) Attamen adhuc ho- die במה dicitur: Id est, manet & mos, & ipsum vocabu- lum à profanis gentibus desumtum, cum ego altare mihi sacratum מזבח appellaverim.

## 20:31
VERS. 31. WHEN YE MAKE YOUR SONS PASS THROUGH THE FIRE) You purify them: a custom which had succeeded in place of burning.

AND I WILL ANSWER YOU) I will give counsel.

Latin:

Vers. 31. CUM TRADUCITIS FILIOS VESTROS PER IGNEM) Lustratis eos: qui mos in locum combu- stionis successerat.

ET EGO RESPONDEBO VOBIS) Consilium dabo.

## 20:32
Vers. 32. WE SHALL BE LIKE THE NATIONS, AND LIKE THE FAMILIES OF THE EARTH) By the similarity of worship we shall live more tranquilly and more amicably with them.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ERIMUS SICUT GENTES, ET SICUT COGNATIONES TERRÆ) Similitudine cultus com- mendati tranquillius & amicius cum ipsis vivemus.

## 20:34
Vers. 34. I WILL BRING YOU OUT FROM THE PEOPLES, AND

I WILL GATHER YOU FROM THE LANDS, IN WHICH YOU ARE SCATTERED) I will bring you far from those among whom you now live intermingled, and whose examples you imitate—from the Phoenicians, Ammonites, Moabites, whose borders you touch. Vers. 35. AND I WILL BRING YOU INTO THE DESERT OF THE PEOPLES) I will lead you into places deserted by peoples, as above 19, 13. AND I WILL BE JUDGED WITH YOU FACE TO FACE) I will cause it to appear that I have done these things justly. Vers. 36. IN THE DESERT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT) Touching Egypt. Vers. 37. AND I WILL SUBJECT YOU TO MY SCEPTER, AND I WILL BRING YOU INTO THE BONDS OF THE COVENANT) Namely, by taking away the wicked and leaving a few who are curable. Vers. 38. FROM THE LAND OF THEIR SOJOURNING) where they dwell for a time: namely, from Judea, which they boasted would remain theirs forever, AND THEY SHALL NOT ENTER INTO THE LAND OF ISRAEL) Those wicked ones shall not return home. Vers. 39. EACH ONE GO AFTER YOUR IDOLS, AND SERVE THEM) Be open idolaters rather than mix my worship, which ought to be pure, with the rites of profane nations. BUT IF EVEN IN THIS YOU DO NOT HEAR ME, AND POLLUTE MY HOLY NAME FURTHER WITH YOUR GIFTS, AND WITH YOUR IDOLS) You may translate best from the Hebrew: For then you will clearly not hear me, nor will you further pollute my holy name through your gifts and your marble idols. That is, if you do this, you will clearly show that you do not belong to me, nor will you unjustly usurp my name by offering illegitimate oblations on those marble altars, fashioned after the example of the nations. Vers. 40. ON MY HOLY MOUNTAIN, ON THE HIGH MOUNTAIN OF ISRAEL, SAITH THE LORD GOD, THERE SHALL ALL THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL SERVE ME) That is, they ought to serve. If anyone wishes to offer me anything, he ought to do it in the Temple chosen by me for that purpose. ALL, I SAY, IN THE LAND, IN WHICH THEY SHALL BE PLEASING TO ME) Translate: all, I say, who are in that very land, there I will hold those (things which they offer) as thanks, not elsewhere. AND THERE I WILL SEEK YOUR FIRSTFRUITS) I will approve your oblations. For תרומה is a general word pertaining to all things that are offered; it is spoken especially of tithes. AND THE BEGINNING OF YOUR TITHES) In the Hebrew: The beginning of your elevations. That is, the beginning of the fruits which you take from the land, the firstfruits, Exod. 15, 20. 23, 19. Deut. 26, 2. IN ALL YOUR SANCTIFICATIONS I WILL ACCEPT YOU IN THE ODOR OF SWEETNESS) That is, all your sacrifices will be pleasing to me. A manner of speaking such as Gen. 8, 21. Vers. 41. WHEN I SHALL HAVE BROUGHT YOU OUT FROM THE PEOPLES) A new sense begins. When I shall have brought you back from exile. AND I SHALL BE SANCTIFIED IN YOU IN THE EYES OF THE NATIONS) And then it shall be. Then it shall be that all peoples shall acknowledge my powers, which I shall have shown in bringing you back.

This is more correctly explained by our people concerning the holy mountain of the Church. Osiander has it thus: There follows now a consolation concerning the kingdom of Christ. But on my holy mountain, in Jerusalem on the high mountain of the people of Israel (i.e., in the Church of Christ, which shall become known by the preaching of the Gospel, and shall be eminent in the world), saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel serve me: there all who believe in the Messiah shall worship me: all (I say) in that land shall serve me: in which they shall be pleasing to me: more correctly, there they shall be acceptable to me. But the true Israelites today are not the Jews, but all who believe in Christ, Gal. 6, 16. And there I will seek your firstfruits and the beginning of your tithes, in all your sanctifications I will accept you in the odor of sweetness. Heb. And there I will require (from you, and will kindly accept) your elevations (i. e. oblations) and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all things which you shall have sanctified (to me) (that is, which you shall have given for holy uses) I will be appeased toward you through the odor of sweetness: when I shall have at some time brought you out from the profane peoples, among whom you are in exile, and shall have gathered you again from the lands, into which you were scattered. And although some Israelites returned from exile to their homeland, and with the Jerusalem temple restored, there they offered to God grateful sacrifices: nevertheless the Lord looks further in this promise, namely to the spiritual kingdom of Christ: as we have often warned. The sacrifices of Christians, however, are not the offerings of beasts, nor the offering of the body and blood of Christ in the Mass: concerning which the Lord commanded nothing: But rather the mortification of the Old Adam Rom. 12, prayers and acts of thanksgiving Heb. 13, beneficence toward brothers, especially the needy Heb. 13, Phil. 4. These sacrifices, if they proceed from faith, please God. But the Lord is reconciled to us when we apply to ourselves by faith the sacrifice of Christ performed on the cross, Rom. 3 & 4. And I shall be sanctified i.e. I shall be glorified in you, in the eyes of the nations: That is, the nations will see how powerful and kind a God I am, when I restore you (beyond the expectation of many) to liberty. Here the Papist Interpreters, Cornelius, Maldonatus, Prado, and others, also understand the Church by the holy mountain of the Lord, as do also from the Reformed Oecolampadius, Piscator, Junius, &c.

Latin:

Vers. 34. EDUCAM VOS DE POPULIS, ET

CONGREGABO VOS DE TERRIS, IN QVIBUS DIS- SPERSI ESTIS) Educam vos longè ab illis, quibus nunc permixti vivitis, & quorum exempla imitaminis à Phœni- cibus, Ammonitis, Moabitis, quorum fines attingitis. Vers. 35. ET ADDUCAM VOS IN DESERTVM POPULORUM) Ducam vos in loca à populis deserta, ut supra 19, 13. ET JUDICABOR VOBISCUM FACIE AD FA- CIEM) Efficiam, ut appareat me hæc juste fecisse. Vers. 36. IN DESERTO TERRÆ ÆGYPTI) Attin- gente Ægyptum. Vers. 37. ET SUBJICIAM VOS SCEPTRO MEO, ET INDUCAM VOS IN VINCULIS FŒDERIS) Nem- pe auferendo malos, paucos sanabiles relinquendo. Vers. 38. DE TERRA INCOLATUS EORUM) ubi ad tempus habitant: de Judæa scilicet, quam ipsi in per- petuum sibi mansuram fuisse gloriabantur, ET IN TERRAM ISRAËL NON INGREDIBN- TUR) Illi impii domum non redibunt. Vers. 39. SINGULI POST IDOLA VISTRA AM- BULATE, ET SERVITE EIS) Aperte potius estote ido- lolatræ, quam ut cultum meum, qui purus esse debet, cum profanarum gentium ritibus misceatis. QVOD SI ET IN HOC NON AUDIERITIS ME, ET NOMEN MEUM SANCTUM POLLUERITIS UL- TRA IN MUNERIBUS VESTRIS, ET IN IDOLIS VESTRIS) Ex Hebræo vertas optimè: Tunc enim plane me non audietis, neque polluetis ultra nomen meum sanctum per munera & marmora vestra. Id est, si id faciatis, ostende- tis plane vos ad me non pertinere, neque nomen meum in- juste usurpabitis, offerendo oblationes non legitimas in aris istis marmoreis, exemplo gentium fabricatis. Vers. 40. IN MONTE SANCTO MEO, IN MON- TE EXCELSO ISRAEL, AIT DOMINUS DEUS, IBI SERVIET MIHI OMNIS DOMUS ISRAEL) Id est, servire debet. Si quis mihi offerre quid velit, in Templo ad id à me electo id facere debet. OMNES INQVAM, IN TERRA, IN QVA PLA- CEBUNT MIHI) Verte: omnes, inquam, qui sunt in ipsa terra, ibi illa (quæ offerent) grata habebo, non alibi. ET IBI QVÆRAM PRIMITIAS VESTRAS) Ap- probabo oblationes vestras. Est enim תרומה vox generalis ad omnia quæ offeruntur pertinens, Eximie de decimis dicitur. ET INITIUM DECIMARUM VESTRARUM) In Hebræo: Initium elevationum vestrarum. Id est, initium fructuum, quos de terra tollitis, primitias, Exod. 15, 20. 23, 19. Deut. 26, 2. IN OMNIBUS SANCTIFICATIONIBUS VESTRIS IN ODOREM SUAVITATIS SVSCIPIAM VOS) Id est, omnia sacrificia vestra mihi erunt grata. Loquendi genus, quale Gen. 8, 21. Vers. 41. CUM EDUXERO VOS DE POPULIS) Novus sensus incipit. Ubi vos reduxero ab exsilio. ET SANCTIFICABOR IN VOBIS IN OCU- LIS NATIONUM) Et pro tunc. Tunc siet ut populi omnes meas vires, quas in vobis reducendis ostenderim, agnoscant.

Rectius hoc de monte sancto Ecclesiæ à nostris explicatur. Osiander ita habet: Sequitur nunc consolatio de regno Christi. In monte autem sancto meo, Hierofolymis in monte excelso populi Israel (i. e. in Ecclesia Christi, quæ prædicatione Evangeli in- notescet, & eminebit in orbe terrarum) ait Domi- nus Deus, ibi serviet mihi omnis domus Israel: ibi omnes in Messiam credentes me colent: omnes (in- quam) in terra illa servient mihi: in qua placebunt mihi: rectius, ibi mihi accepti erunt. Veri autem Israelitæ hodie sunt non Judæi, sed omnes in Chri- stum credentes, Gal. 6, 16. & ibi quæram primitias vestras & initium decimarum vestrarum, in omni- bus sanctificationibus vestris, in odorem suavitatis suscipiam vos. Heb. Et ibi requiram (à vobis, & benigne accipiam) Levandas, (i. e. oblationes) ve- stras, & primitias oblationum vestrarum, cum omni- bus, quæ (mihi)sanctificaveritis (hoc est, ad usus sanctos donaveritis) per odorem suavitatis placabor vobis: cum aliquando eduxero vos de populis pro- phanis, inter quos exulatis, & congregavero vos rur- sum de terris, in quas dispersi estis. Etsi autem Israe- litæ aliqui ab exilio in patriam redierunt, & restau- rato templo Hierofolymitano, ibi Deo grata sacri- ficia retulerunt: tamen Dominus hac promissio- ne longius, nempe in regnum Christi spirituale re- spicit: ut saepe monuimus. Sacrificia autem Chri- stianorum sunt, non oblationes pecudum, neque oblatio corporis & sanguinis Christi in Missa: de qua Dominus nihil praecepit: Sed potius morti- ficatio Veteris Adami Rom. 12. preces & gratiarum actiones Heb. 13. beneficentiam erga fratres, praesertim egentes Heb. 13. Phil. 4. Haec sacrificia, si ex fide proficiscantur, Deo placent. Reconciliatur au- tem nobis Dominus, cum sacrificium Christi in cruce peractum, fide nobis applicamus, Rom. 3. & 4. Et sanctificabor i. e. glorificabor in vobis, in ocu- lis nationum: Id est, gentes videbunt, quam sim po- tens & benignus Deus, cum vos (praeter expecta- tionem multorum) libertati restituam. Hic Ec- clesiam etiam intelligunt per montem sanctum Do- mini Pontificii Interpretes, Cornelius, Maldonatus, Prado, & alii, nec non e Reformatis Oecolampadius, Piscator, Junius, &c.

FOR MY NAME'S SAKE) See above 9.

AND NOT ACCORDING TO YOUR EVIL WAYS, NOR ACCORDING TO YOUR MOST WICKED CRIMES) Which you who are now living in that land commit, Above 16. v. 61.

PROPTER NOMEN MEVM) Vide supra 9.

ET NON SECUNDUM VIAS VESTRAS MA- LAS, NEQVE SECUNDUM SCELERA VESTRA PESSIMA) Quae nunc in illa terra viventes admittitis, Su- pra 16. v. 61.

## 20:46
Vers. 46. SET THY FACE AGAINST THE WAY OF THE SOUTH) Here the beginning of the following chapter ought to have been placed: for those things which we have at 21, 1 contain a bare exposition of these words. To the Prophet acting at the Chaboras, Judea was partly to the south. The prophets turned themselves toward those about whom they were to prophesy.

DROP TOWARD THE SOUTH) That is, prophesy, as the Chaldean has it here. So also Amos 7, 16. Micah 2, 6. Prophecy comes from heaven, like rain.

Latin:

Vers. 46. PONE FACIEM TVAM CONTRA VIAM AUSTRI) Hic debuerat initium poni sequentis capitis: nam illa quae nos habemus 21, 1. nudam expositionem horum verborum continent. Prophetae agenti ad Chabo- ram Judaea partim erat ad meridiem. Prophetae de qui- bus vaticinaturi erant de eos se vertebant.

STILLA AD AFFRICUM) Id est, vaticinare, ut hic habet Chaldaeus. Sic & Amos 7, 16. Micheae 2, 6. Pro- phetia de coelo venit, ut imber.

## 20:47
Vers. 47. TO THE FOREST OF THE SOUTH) For Judea is woody.

BEHOLD I WILL KINDLE A FIRE IN THEE) In Jerusalem, and in other towns and villages. This fire signifies not only a conflagration, but everything that consumes, as above 19. v. 12.

AND I WILL BURN IN THEE EVERY GREEN TREE, AND EVERY DRY TREE) In Hebrew: It shall devour in thee: that is, it shall cause that neither good nor bad shall appear, See 21, 3. 4.

THE FLAME OF KINDLING SHALL NOT BE EXTINGUISHED) The evils sent shall not cease, unless those things which I will are accomplished. See 21, 5.

AND EVERY FACE SHALL BE BURNED IN IT FROM THE SOUTH EVEN TO THE NORTH) Every man: that is, many everywhere in places, from one end to the other.

Latin:

Vers. 47. SALTUI MERIDIANO) Nemorosa enim Judaea.

ECCE EGO SUCCENDAM IN TE IGNEM) Hierosolymis, & in oppidis aliis, villisque. Ignis hic non incendium tantum significat, sed omne quod absumit, ut supra 19. v. 12.

ET COMBURAM IN TE OMNE LIGNUM VIRIDE, ET OMNE LIGNUM ARIDUM) In He- braeo: Devorabit in te: id est, efficiet ne compareant aut boni aut mali, Vide 21, 3. 4.

NON EXSTINGUETUR FLAMMA SUCCEN- SIONIS) Non cessabunt immissa mala, nisi peractis quae volo. Vide 21, 5.

ET COMBURETUR IN EA OMNIS FACIES AB AUSTRO USQVE AD AQVILONEM) Omnis homo: id est, multi ubique locorum, ab uno fine ad al- terum.

## 20:49
THEY SAY OF ME) They will say of me, if I have declared these things to them in that manner.

IS THIS MAN NOT SPEAKING IN PARABLES) That is: is this man not always a speaker of riddles?

Vers. 49. IPSI DICUNT DE ME) Dicent de me, si haec ipsis eo modo enuntiaverim.

NUMQVID NON PER PARABOLAS LO- QVITUR ISTE) Id est: nonne iste homo semper est perpexiloquus?

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI. Concerning the manifold sword against Jerusalem, and the King, as also against the children of Ammon, about to come from the King of Babylon.

SON OF MAN SET THY FACE AGAINST JERUSALEM) What God had proposed under allegory, He now explains more openly and clearly for the sake of the Prophet, who was saying that it would come to pass that he would be considered a speaker of riddles.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI. De gladio multiplici contra Ierusalem, & Re- gem, ut & contra filios Ammon a Rege Ba- bylonis venturo.

Vers. 1. FILI HOMINIS PONE FACIEM TUAM AD JERUSALEM) Quae sub allegoria proposuerat Deus, ea jam apertius & enucleatius explicat in Prophetae gratiam, qui fore dicebat, ut pro perplexiloquo haberetur.

## 21:2
DROP TOWARD THE SANCTUARIES) Toward the three parts of the Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 2. STILLA AD SANCTUARIA) Ad tres partes Templi.

## 21:3
I WILL DRAW MY SWORD OUT OF ITS SHEATH) This sword is the same as the fire just mentioned, everything that consumes.

AND I WILL CUT OFF FROM THEE THE RIGHTEOUS AND THE WICKED) In the Hebrew it is, I will cut off: that is, I will take away from the earth, namely by sending the good into exile, and by destroying the wicked evilly. So also here the Chaldaean, which things agree with those which we said at the beginning of chapter 18. Compare also those things which are above 9, 4. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 3. EJICIAM GLADIUM MEUM DE VAGI- NA) Gladius hic idem quod modo ignis, omne quod absumit.

ET OCCIDAM IN TE JUSTUM ET IMPIUM) In Hebraeo est, exscindam: id est, auferam a terra, nempe bo- nos in exsilium mittendo, malos male perdendo. Ita & hic Chaldaeus, quae congruunt cum iis quae ad initium capitis 18. diximus. Confer. & quae supra 9, 4. 6.

## 21:4
BUT FOR THAT I CUT OFF FROM THEE THE RIGHTEOUS AND THE WICKED) That I may cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked.

Latin:

PRO EO AVTEM QVOD OCCIDI IN TE JUSTVM ET IMPIVM) Ut exscindam ex te justum & impium.

## 21:6
Ver. 6.

SIGH WITH THE BREAKING OF THY LOINS) Sigh deeply, like those who suffer from pleurisy.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

INGEMISCE IN CONTRITIONE LUMBO- RUM) Altum ingeme, ut illi qui pleuritide laborant.

## 21:7
Ver. 7.

FOR THE HEARING) Because of that which I understand will happen. EVERY HEART SHALL MELT) It will fail. AND ALL KNEES SHALL FLOW WITH WATER) Interpret, as above 7, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

PRO AUDITU) Ob id quod futurum intelligo. TABESCET OMNE COR) Linquet. ET PER CUNCTA GENUA FLUENT AQUÆ) Interpretare, ut supra 7, 17.

## 21:9
Verse 9.

THE SWORD, THE SWORD IS SHARPENED AND POLISHED) It is sharpened and wiped clean. The sword of the Chaldeans and the Ammonites. Thus here the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

GLADIUS GLADIUS EXACUTUS EST ET LIMATUS) Exacutus est & tersus. Gladius Chaldæorum & Ammonitarum. Ita hic Chaldæos.

## 21:10
Verse 10.

THAT IT MAY SLAY VICTIMS IT IS SHARPENED) In the Hebrew: That it may slaughter those to be slaughtered. A soldier in Plautus: I want to comfort this sword of mine, so that it does not lament, nor lose heart, because I have kept it idle for so long, which miserably longs to make stuffing out of the enemy. THAT IT MAY SHINE IT IS POLISHED) It is wiped clean: So that when the time for use comes, in a close-packed hand, it may dazzle the sight of the eyes in the battle against the enemies. YOU WHO MOVE THE SCEPTER OF MY SON, YOU HAVE CUT DOWN EVERY TREE) Wonderful words, in which the interpreters twist themselves wonderfully. It appears the LXX read otherwise: namely, if I am not mistaken, אל כשל זבח בה מאסת כל־עץ : for they translate ἑτοίμη εἰς παράλυσιν σφάζε, ἐξουθένει, ἀπόδε πᾶν ξύλον. Those former things pertain to the preceding sense: It is polished for dissolution: so that it may easily break everything. Then follows the command of God to the sword: Slay, despise, and hold in no place every tree. That is, spare no man. See above 20, 47.

Little attention should be paid to what the LXX read, or why they rendered it in this way. Nor do bare conjectures make us certain either about the causes of the translation or about a better reading. We persist in the received reading of the Hebrew text, as the royal road, nor do we have cause to depart from it. Maldonatus says he strongly suspects that Jerome did not read נשיש but נשיא, 'will take away,' or נושא, 'taking away.' Others will dream other things. What then remains certain, or who will instruct us about the genuine letter, if you depart from the modern Hebrew text? Piscator rendered the Hebrew thus: Should we nevertheless be joyful! It is the rod of my son, which despises all wood, that is, it is much harder and tougher. The Genevans in almost the same way, except that they understand the rod to despise all wood, because it has the power of penetrating through all wood. Pagninus translated it thus: Or shall we rejoice over the rod of my son, despising every tree. R. Solomon, as Oecolampadius notes, reads it as an exclamation: Is there reason for us to rejoice? Is the rod, with which I punish my son, harder than other sticks and clubs? Truly, just like the remaining wood, it will also despise this rod. Oecolampadius explains it thus: The sword is sharpened, that it may slay you; it is polished, that it may be with a vibrating brightness that dazzles the eyes. Shall we rejoice? By no means should we rejoice, as if it were drawn against enemies: but it will cut down the staff of my son, i.e., the strength of Judah and Benjamin. Thus, therefore, some refer that 'shall we rejoice' to God, others to men, with whom B. Luther agrees. But what does the plural number mean to you, if those are the words of God? Johannes Coccejus in his Commentary on Hos. ch. 12, v. 5, understands the plural as referring to God the Father and the Son: or we shall be glad, namely I and my Son. B. Glassius in Rhet. Sacra, page 163, explains it thus: Or let us rejoice! (that these may be the words of the Prophet, and the Lord may answer:) The rod of my Son (Christ) despising every tree (is present or is prepared.) Which sense the Belgian Paraphrasts do not reject, proposing both explanations concerning the eternal Son of God, and concerning the people called the son of God. Whatever difficult interpretation is chosen, it will be better than if we correct the Hebrew text here from the LXX Interpreters, i.e., prefer a version everywhere corrupted to the purest sources. AND I HAVE GIVEN IT TO BE POLISHED) He gave it to be scoured: namely, the Chaldean king.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

UT CÆDAT VICTIMAS EXACVTUS EST) In Hebræo: Ut mactet mactandos. Miles apud Plautum: Ego hanc macharam mihi consolari volo, Ne lamentetur, neve animum despondeat, Quia se jam pridem feriatam gestitem Quæ misere gestit fartum facere ex hostibus. UT SPLENDEAT LIMATUS EST) Tersus est: Ut ubi usus veniat contra conferta manu Oculorum præstringat aciem in acie hostibus. QVI MOVES SCEPTRUM FILII MEI, SUC- CIDISTI OMNE LIGNUM) Mira verba, in quibus mire se torquent interpretes. LXX. aliter legisse apparet: ni- mirum, ni fallor, אל כשל זבח בה מאסת כל־עץ : vertunt enim ἑτοίμη εἰς παράλυσιν σφάζε, ἐξουθένει, ἀπόδε πᾶν ξύλον. Priora illa ad sensum præcedentem pertinent: Tersus est ad dissolutionem : ut facile disrumpat omnia. Se- quitur deinde Dei imperium ad gladium: Interfice, con- temne nulloque loco habe omne lignum. Id est nulli homini parce. Vide supra 20, 47.

PArum attendendum, quid legerint, aut cur hoc pacto reddiderint LXX. Neque etiam conjectu- ræ nudæ vel de causis translationis certos nos red- dent, vel de meliori lectione. Persistimus in lectio- ne recepta Ebræi textus, ceu via regia, nec habemus causam ab ea discedendi. Maldonatus valde se su- spicari ait, Hieronymus non legisse נשיש sed נשיא, auferet vel נושא auferens. Alii alia somniabunt. Quid ergo certi super est, aut quis de genuina lite- ra, si abeas à textu Ebræo moderno, nos edocebit? Ebræa Piscator ita reddidit: Solten wir dennoch frölich seyn! Es ist die Ruthe meines Sohnes/ welche alles Holtz verachtet/das ist viel härter und zeher ist. Genevenses eodem fere modo, nisi quod virgam omne lignum spernere intelligant, quod vim penetrandi habeat per omne lignum. Pagninus ita transtulit: Vel gaudebimus de virga filii mei, sper- nente omne lignum. R. Salomo, notante Oecolam- padio, per admirationem legit: Estne quod læte- mur? Nunquid virga, qua filium meum castigo, du- rior est cæteris fustibus & clavis? verum sicut reli- qua ligna, & hanc quoque virgam contemnet. Oeco- lampadius ita exponit: Acutus est gladius, ut vos mactet, expolitus est, ut sit vibrante oculos perstrin- genteque fulgore. An lætabimur? Nequaquam gau- dendum, tanquam in hostes stringeretur: sed bacu- lum filii mei, h. e. robur Jude, & Benjamin disseca- bit. Sic ergo illud letabimur alii ad Deum, alii ad homines referunt, cum quibus B. Lutherus facit. Sed quid pluralis numerus tibi vult, si verba illa Dei sunt? Johannes Coccejus in Commentario in Hos. c. 12. v. 5. pluralem de Deo Patre & Filio intelligit: vel hilarabimur, ego scilicet, & Filius meus. B. Glassius Rhet. Sacra pag. 163. ita explicat: Aut gaudeamus! (ut hæc sint verba Prophetæ, & re- spondeat Dominus:) Virga Filii mei (Christi) sper- nens omne lignum (aderit vel parata est.) Quem sensum non reprobant Paraphrastæ Belgici utram- que explicationem de Filio Dei æterno, & de populo filio Dei dicto proponentes. Quæcunque in loco- difficili eligatur interpretatio, satius erit, quam hic è LXX. Interpp. Ebræum textum corrigamus, h. e. versionem undiquaque turbatam fontibus purissi- mis præferamus. ET DEDI EVM AD LÆVIGANDVM) Dedit eum ad tergendurn: nempe rex Chaldæus.

## 21:11
Vers. 11. THAT IT MAY BE HELD) That it may now offer itself for use. THAT IT MAY BE IN THE HAND OF THE SLAYER) The Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VT TENEATVR MANV) Vt jam jam usum suis præbeat. VT SIT IN MANV INTERFICIENTIS) Chal- dæi.

## 21:12
Vers. 12. FOR THIS IS MADE IN MY PEOPLE) That is, it is prepared against my people. THIS AGAINST ALL THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL) Against the king and the princes. THEY WHO FLED ARE DELIVERED TO THE SWORD WITH MY PEOPLE) In the Hebrew: There shall be fears because of the sword for my people. THEREFORE CLAP UPON THE THIGH) A sign of one grieving. Jerem. 31, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QVIA HIC FACTVS EST IN POPVLO MEO) Id est, paratus est adversus populum meum. HIC IN CVNCTIS DVCIBVS ISRAEL) Con- tra regem ac principes. QVI FVGERVNT GLADIO TRADITI SVNT CVM POPVLO MEO) In Hebræo: Timores ob gladium erunt populo meo. IDCIRCO PLAVDE SVPER FEMVR) Dolentis signum. Jerem. 31, 19.

## 21:13
Vers. 13. FOR IT IS PROVED AND WHAT IF IT SHALL OVERTHROW THE SCEPTRE, AND IT SHALL NOT BE) The sense seems to be: That sword will then have proved its work to me, when it has so overthrown the tribe of Judah (for that is שבט), that nothing of it remains. SMITE HAND TO HAND) Do not grieve any longer, but rather rouse the Chaldeans, that they may execute my judgments which are so just: thus the same expression is taken within 17.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVIA PROBATVS EST ET HOC CVM SCEPTRVM SVBVERTERIT, ET NON ERIT) Sen- sus videtur esse: Gladius ille tunc mihi suam operam ap- probaverit, ubi tribum Judæ (id enim שבט) ita everterit, ut ejus nihil restet. PERCVTE MANV AD MANVM) Noli amplius dolere, sed excita potius Chaldæos, ut judicia mea adeo justa exsequantur: sic eadem locutio intra sumitur 17.

## 21:14
Ver. 14. AND LET THE SWORD BE DOUBLED, AND TRIPLED) That it may be doubled and tripled. That is, you may wish that my judgments be satisfied. The first calamity is the capture of Zedekiah: the second, the capture of the city: the third, of all the remnants that were deported, who had been with Gedaliah. OF THE SLAIN) Understand, and of the devastated, from that which is below in verse 15. WHICH MAKES THEM ASTONISHED) So both the Greeks and the Chaldean. They read therefore החדרת, not as we do החודרת, in the chambers. The sense in the Hebrew text is by no means obscure: The sword of the slain is great החֹדֶרֶת לָהֶם which will enter their inner chambers: which Blessed Luther expressed: Das sie auch treffen wird in den kamern/ Dahin sie fliehen. For Buxtorf rightly notes in *Vindic. Veritat. Ebræ.* page 785, that the Chaldean did not read otherwise; but so understood it for החררת through the metathesis frequent in this language: which was also observed by R. David Kimchi. See similar examples adduced there by Buxtorf. Ludovic. de Dieu, because the word of the Hebrews is not read elsewhere, recurs to the Ethiopic language, where the word ኀደረ is to remain, to dwell, and thus he translates: This is the sword of great slaughter, which remains for them, that is, which is reserved for them as if stored in a chamber.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DVPLICETVR GLADIVS, ET TRIPLI- CETVR) Vt duplicetur, & triplicetur. Id est, optes judiciis meis satisfiat. Prima calamitate capti Sedeciæ: Secunda captæ urbis: tertia omnium reliquiarum deportatarum, quæ cum Godolia fuerant. INTERFECTORVM) Intellige, & vastatorum ex eo quod infra 15. QVI OBSTVPESCERE EOS FACIT) Sic & Græci & Chaldæus. Legerunt ergo החדרת, non ut nos החודרת, in cubiculis. Sensus in Ebræo textu minime obscurus est: Gladius interfectorum magnus החֹדֶרֶת לָהֶם qui in- gredietur penetralia eorum: quem expressit B. Lu- therus: Das sie auch treffen wird in den kamern/ Dahin sie fliehen. Recte enim notat Buxtorffius vindic. Veritat. Ebræ. pag. 785. quod non legerit Chaldæus aliter; sed ita acceperit pro החררת per Mathesin in hac lingua frequentem: quod etiam R. David Kimchio observatum. Vide similia ibi- dem à Buxtorffio adducta. Ludovic. de Dieu, quia verbum Ebræorum alibi non legitur, ad linquam Æthiopicam recurrit, ubi verbum, ኀደረ est mane- re, habitare, adeoque ita vertit: Iste est gladius in- terfectionis magnæ, qui manet ipsos, id est, qui quasi in conclavi repositus, reservatur ipsis.

## 21:15
Vers. 15. AND MULTIPLIES RUINS) It causes many to fall. THE CONSTERNATION OF THE SHARP SWORD) Fear from the sword. AND POLISHED TO SHINE) Scoured. CLOTHED FOR SLAUGHTER) Better: sharpened. For עטה signifies a stylus. Job 9, 24. Jerem. 17, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET MVLTIPLICAT RVINAS) Facit ut multi cadant. CONTVRBATIONEM GLADII ACVTI) Me- tum à gladio. ET LIMATI AD FVLGENDVM) Extersi. AMICTI AD CÆDEM) Melius: mucronati. Nam עטה stylum significat. Job. 9, 24. Jerem. 17, 1.

## 21:16
Vers. 16. SHARPEN, GO TO THE RIGHT, OR TO THE LEFT) An apostrophe to the sword, such as above 10. In the word התאחדי all interpreters take א as epenthetic: not badly. WHITHERSOEVER THE APPETITE OF THY FACE IS) In the Hebrew: Whithersoever thy face is prepared. That is, whithersoever you are drawn, go, kill.

Latin:

Vers. 16. EXACVERE, VADE AD DEXTERAM, SIVE AD SINISTRAM) Apostrophe ad gladium, qualis supra 10. In voce התאחדי omnes interpretes א sumunt pro ἐπενθετικῷ: non male. QVOCVMQVE FACIEI TVÆ APPETITVS EST) In Hebræo: Quocunque facies tua parata. Id est, quo- cumque stringeris, perge, occide.

## 21:17
Vers. 17. YEA, I WILL CLAP HAND TO HAND) That is, I will favor the slayers, as above 14.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QVIN ET EGO PLAVDAM MANV AD MA- NVM) Id est, favebo interfectoribus, ut supra 14.

## 21:19
Vers. 19. SET THEE TWO WAYS) On a tablet paint a fork in the road. See above 4, 1. THAT THE SWORD OF BABYLON MAY COME) Through which the Babylonian army may be able to go. OUT OF ONE LAND SHALL BOTH COME FORTH) From one way, which comes from Arabia, these two ways are divided, one to Jerusalem, the other to Rabbath, the chief city of the Ammonites. The Prophet foresees, however, that it will happen that Nebuchadnezzar, undoubtedly by the instinct of God, will hesitate at that fork in the road as to where he should go most of all.

Latin:

Vers. 19. PONE TIBI DVAS VIAS) In tabula pinge bi- vium. Vide supra 4, 1. VT VENIAT GLADIVS BABYLONIS) Per quas ire possit exercitus Babylonicos. DE VNA TERRA EGREDIENTVR AMBÆ) Ex una via, quæ ex Arabia venit, duæ istæ viæ dividuntur, al- tera ad Hierosolyma, altera ad Rabbatham principem ur- bem Ammonitarum. Prævidet autem Propheta futurum, ut Nabuchodonosor, Dei haud dubie instinctu, in isto bivio dubitet quo potissimum sit iturus.

## 21:21
Vers. 21.

SEEKING DIVINATION, MIXING ARROWS) Jerome on this passage: By the rite of his nation he will consult an oracle, that he may cast his arrows into a quiver and mix them inscribed, or marked with the names of individuals, that he may see whose arrow comes out, and which city he ought to attack first. The Greeks call this belomancy or rhabdomancy. The same on Hosea 4. Whence also the Prophet speaks as if astonished and wondering: my people, who were once called by my name, asked wood and a rod, which kind of divination the Greeks call rhabdomancy. Whence we read in Ezekiel that Nebuchadnezzar mixed his rods against Ammon and Jerusalem, and the rod came out against Jerusalem. The scholiast of Nicander from Dio: Magi and Scythians divine with a tamarisk rod. For indeed in many places they divine with rods. Understand here the Chaldean Magi, as in Claudian: --- and the Magi laid low the bullocks with Chaldean rite. The Scythians, moreover, bordered on the Median empire: a part of them were the Alani, concerning whom Ammianus writes in book 31. They predict the future in a wonderful way: for the women, gathering straight rods and separating them with certain secret incantations at a predetermined time, know openly what is portended. We have two witnesses that this custom flowed to the Slavs, neighbors of the Scythians: Moses of Coucy in the History of the Jubilee 52, and Adam of Bremen in chapter 6 of his Ecclesiastical History. The Germans drew it from the Slavs: concerning whom Tacitus writes: The custom of lots is simple. They cut a rod from a fruit-bearing tree into small twigs, and having distinguished them with certain marks, they scatter them at random and by chance upon a white garment. Presently, if it is consulted publicly, the priest, or if privately, the father of the family himself, prays to the gods, and looking up to the sky, he picks them up three times, one by one: having picked them up, he interprets them according to the mark previously impressed. You have another custom of ῥαβδομαντείας (rod-divination) among the Persians in Strabo 15. and Athenaeus 12, from Phoenix of Colophon: another of βελομαντείας (arrow-divination) in Paul the Venetian [Marco Polo] in his work on the affairs of the Tartars, book 1, 43. We read that the Africans also used it, who are in Caesarea in Mauretania, that is, Algiers.

HE CONSULTED IDOLS) Teraphim, that is, speaking images, of which Thammuz had made not a few.

HE CONSULTED THE ENTRAILS) In the Hebrew: The liver. Namely, in which direction that part of the liver flickered which is called the hostile part. Cicero mentions this in his work On Divination, Lucan in book 1, and Seneca in his Oedipus. Nor do I think it is to be doubted that those arts came from the Chaldeans to the Lydians, and from the Lydians to the Etruscans.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

DIVINATIONEM QVÆRENS, COMMI- SCENS SAGITTAS) Hieronymus ad hunc locum: Ritu gentis suæ oraculum consulet, ut mittat sagittas suas in phare- tram & commisceat eas inscriptas, sive signatas nominibus sin- gulorum, ut videat cujus sagitta exeat, & quam prius civitatem debeat oppugnare. Hanc autem Græci βελομαντίαν sive ῥαβδο- μαντίαν vocant. Idem ad Oseæ 4. Vnde & Propheta, quasi stupens & mirabundus eloquitur: populus meus, qui quondam meo vocabatur nomine, lignum interrogavit & virgam, quod ge- nus divinationis Græci ῥαβδομαντίαν vocant. Vnde in Ezechiele legimus, quod virgas suas miscuerit Nabuchodonosor contra Ammon & Ierusalem, & exierit virga contra Ierusalem. Scho- liastes Nicandri ex Dione: μάγοι κὴ Σκύθαι μυρικίνῳ μαν- τεύονται ξύλῳ. Καὶ γὰρ ἐν πολλοῖς τόποις ῥάβδοις μαντεύονται, Magos hic intellige Chaldæos, ut apud Claudianum: --- rituque juvencos Chaldæo stravere Magi. Scythæ autem Medicum tangebant imperium: eorum pars Alani, de quibus Ammianus lib. 31. Futura miro præsagiunt modo: nam rectiores virgas feminæ colligentes, easque cum in- cantamentis quibusdam secretis præstituto tempore discernentes, aperte quid portendatur norunt. Ad Slavos Scytharum vici- nos hunc manasse morem duos habemus testes, Mosem de Kotzi in Historia Jubilæi LII. & Adamum Bremensem nar- rationis Ecclesiasticæ cap. 6. A Slavis hausere Germani: de quibus Tacitus: Sortium consuetudo simplex. Virgam fru- giferæ arbori decisam in surculos amputant, eosque notis quibus- dam discretos super candidam vestem temere ac fortuito spar- gunt. Mox, si publice consulatur, sacerdos, sin privatim, ipse pater familiæ precatur Deos, cælumque suspiciens, ter singulos tollit: sublatos secundum impressam ante notam interpretatur. Alium morem ῥαβδομαντείας apud Persas habes apud Strabonem 15. & Athenæum 12, ex Phœnice Colophonio: alium βε- λομαντείας apud Paulum Venetum in Tartarorum rebus lib. 1, 43. Legimus eo usos & Afros, qui sunt Cæsareæ in Mau- ritania, id est, Algerii.

INTERROGAVIT IDOLA) Teraphim, id est, imagines loquentes, quales non paucas Thammuz fecerat.

EXTA CONSVLVIT) In Hebræo: Iecur. Nempe quam in partem micaret pars illa jecoris quæ hostiles dici- tur. Meminere Cicero de Divinatione, Lucanus 1. Seneca Oedipode. Nec dubitandum puto quin artes illæ à Chal- dæis ad Lydos, à Lydis ad Hetruscos venerint.

## 21:22
Verse 22.

AT HIS RIGHT HAND DIVINATION WAS MADE) All kinds of divinations, with God providing and ruling, persuade him to insist on the right-hand path, and to seek Jerusalem, and that is clear from what follows.

TO SET BATTERING RAMS) Leaders: the Chaldean, as above 4, 2, where see what is said. To set, namely, in battle array.

TO OPEN THE MOUTH IN SLAUGHTER) The edge of the sword is called the mouth by the Hebrews. Joshua 6, 21, and elsewhere.

TO LIFT UP THE VOICE IN SHOUTING) To raise a military war cry, as is accustomed to happen when cities are besieged.

TO SET BATTERING RAMS AGAINST THE GATES) To set leaders against the gates, as were the seven against Thebes. See Aeschylus in the tragedy of that name, and the Phoenissae of Euripides.

TO HEAP UP A MOUND) A siege rampart, χώματα περὶ τὸν κύκλον (mounds around the circuit), according to Josephus in the fulfillment of the prophecy.

AND TO BUILD FORTIFICATIONS) In the Hebrew: Wooden towers. πύργους (towers), says Josephus. See above 17, 17. The Septuagint in both places said βελοστάσεις (engine-stands), which word the writer of the first book of Maccabees also uses in 6, 21, 51.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

AD DEXTERAM EJVS FACTA EST DIVINA- TIO) Omnia divinationum genera, Deo provide regente, suadebent ut dextrum iter insistat, & Hierosolyma petat, ac ea patet quæ sequuntur.

VT PONAT ARIETES) Duces: Chaldæus, ut supra 4, 2. ubi dicta vide. Ut ponat, nempe in acie.

UT APERIAT OS IN CÆDE) Os vocatur He- bræis acumen gladii. Jos. 6, 21. & alibi.

UT ELEVET VOCEM IN EJVLATU) Bar- ritum edat militarem, ut solet fieri ubi oppugnantur urbes.

VT PONAT ARIETES SVPER PORTAS) Con- tra portas ponat duces, ut positi οἱ ἑπτὰ ἐπὶ Θήβαις. Vi- de Æschylum ejus nominis tragœdia, & Phœnissas Eu- ripidis.

VT COMPORTET AGGEREM) Vallum obsi- dionale, χώματα περὶ τὸν κύκλον, Josepho in implemento prophetiæ.

ET ÆDIFICET MVNITIONES) In Hebræo: Turres ligneas. πύργους Josephus. Vide supra 17, 17. LXX. utrobique dixere βελοστάσεις, qua voce utitur & primi Mac- cabæorum scriptor 6, 21. 51.

## 21:23
Verse 23.

AND HE SHALL BE AS ONE CONSULTING AN ORACLE IN VAIN IN THEIR EYES, AND IMITATING THE REST OF THE SABBATHS) The ambassadors sent by Zedekiah will think he is idling, as is wont to happen on the sabbaths. Others explain שבעי שבעות as belonging to them, of those who had sworn oaths to them (the Chaldeans): That is, of the Jews, who had long since given themselves into the faith of the Chaldeans, so that this very thing is that iniquity, concerning which are the following words. But the Chaldean interpreter interprets that שבעי שבעות as seven times seven times. For he thinks Nebuchadnezzar consulted about the journey that many times.

BUT HE SHALL REMEMBER THE INIQUITY TO TAKE) He meanwhile Nebuchadnezzar, while he consults his idols, will remember that he swore by those same idols to Zedekiah: but that he himself broke the covenant: for which cause, being stirred up, Nebuchadnezzar will burn for his destruction. Nebuchadnezzar had kept the faith given through idols; Zedekiah had not kept the faith given through the true God. This indeed pertained greatly to the reproach of the true God, and therefore it was fitting for God to avenge it.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

ERITQVE QVASI FRVSTRA CONSVLENS ORACVLVM IN OCULIS EORVM, ET SABBA- TORVM OTIVM IMITANS) Legati à Sedecia missi cogitabunt eum otiari, ut in sabbatis fieri solet. Alii שבעי שבעות להם exponunt, eorum qui illis (Chaldæis) juramenta juraverant: Id est, Judæorum, qui se pridem in Chaldæorum fidem dederant, ut hoc ipsum sit illa iniquitas, de qua sunt, verba sequentia. At interpres Chaldæus illud שבעי שבעות interpretatur septies septenis vicibus. Toties enim putat de itinere consultasse Nabuchodono- sorem.

IPSE AVTEM RECORDABITVR INIQVITA- TIS AD CAPIENDVM) Ipse interim Nabuchodo- nosor, dum idola sua consulit, reminiscetur per eadem idola se jurasse Sedeciæ : ipsum autem rupisse fœdus: qua causa excitatus Nabuchodonosor ardebit in ejus exitium. Nabu- chodonosor per idola fidem datam servaverat, Sedecias per verum Deum datam non servaverat. Id vero ad Dei veri contumeliam plurimum pertinebat, ideoque Deum dece- bat id uscisci.

## 21:24
Verse 24.

FOR THAT YOU HAVE REMEMBERED YOUR INIQUITY) Better: You also remember your iniquity. Just as, namely, Nebuchadnezzar remembered his, not without the diminution of divine majesty. AND YOU HAVE REVEALED YOUR TRANSGRESSIONS, AND YOUR SINS HAVE APPEARED IN ALL YOUR THOUGHTS) For you have made your wickedness publicly known, so that it might appear in all your actions. This is a parenthesis. FOR THAT I SAY YOU HAVE REMEMBERED) That I say you may remember. YOU SHALL BE TAKEN BY THE HAND) Namely, through the just wrath of Nebuchadnezzar.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

PRO EO QVOD RECORDATI ESTIS INI- QVITATIS VESTRÆ) Melius: Vivos quoque recordemi- ni iniquitatis vestræ. Sicut scilicet Nabuchodonosor ejus non sine majestatis divinæ diminutione recordatus est. ET REVELASTIS PRÆVARICATIONES VE- STRAS, ET APPARVERVNT PECCATA VE- STRÆ IN OMNIBVS COGITATIONIBVS VE- STRIS) Nam publice notas fecistis malitias vestras, ita ut in omnibus actionibus vestris apparerent. Hæc est pa- renthesis. PRO EO INQVAM QVOD RECORDATI ESTIS) Vt inquam recordemini. MANV CAPIEMINI) Nempe per justam iram Nabuchodonosoris.

## 21:25
Verse 25.

BUT YOU, PROFANE, WICKED PRINCE OF ISRAEL) He addresses Zedekiah, with whom Jeremiah deals more submissively: here more freely, because he was not under the rule of Zedekiah. WHOSE DAY HAS COME IN THE TIME OF PREDESTINED INIQUITY) Better by transposition, which the Chaldean observes here: Whose last day has arrived at an opportune time for punishment: as if God were saying: I have long been waiting for an opportunity to punish you through those to whom you gave the opportunity to despise my name.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

TV AVTEM PROFANE IMPIE DVX ISRAEL) Sedeciam alloquitur, cum quo submissius agit Jeremias: hic liberius, quia non erat sub imperio Sedeciæ. CVJVS VENIT DIES IN TEMPORE INI- QVITATIS PRÆFINITA) Melius per transpositio- nem, quem hic observat Chaldæus: Cujus ultimus dies ad- venit in tempore opportuno ad pœnam: quasi dicat Deus: Jamdudum occasionem exspecto, ut te puniam per eos, quibus tu occasionem mei nominis contemnendi de- disti.

## 21:26
Verse 26.

REMOVE THE MITER) The cidaris, which the Latin translator here placed from the Greeks, is πῖλος βασιλικὸς, as Curtius, Plutarch, Artaxerxes & Antony, and Hesychius teach us. It seems to be a Chaldean word, signifying a rounded, that is, a hemispherical shape. TAKE AWAY THE CROWN) The ornament placed around the miter in the manner of a crown. IS NOT THIS THAT WHICH HAS LIFTED UP THE LOWLY) When it was imposed upon you, a weak man, by Nebuchadnezzar, 24, 17. AND HAS HUMBLED THE EXALTED) He will humble. The cause will be why you are brought low: - - - they are lifted on high, That they may fall with a heavier crash.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

AVFER CIDARIM) Cidaris quod hic ex Græcis Latinus posuit, est πῖλος βασιλικὸς, ut nos docent Curtius, Plutarchus, Artaxerxe & Antonio, & Hesychius. Videtur esse vox Chaldaica, rotundatam, id est, semisphæricam formam significans. TOLLE CORONAM) Ornamentum circumposi- tum cidari in coronæ modum. NONNE HÆC EST QVÆ HVMILEM SVB- LEVAVIT) Cum tibi homini invalido à Nabuchodono- sore imponeretur, 24, 17. ET SVBLIMEM HVMILIAVIT) Humiliabit. Causa erit cur deprimaris: - - - tolluntur in altum, Vt lapsu graviore ruant.

## 21:27
Verse 27.

INIQUITY, INIQUITY, INIQUITY I WILL MAKE IT) Oblique, oblique, oblique I will make it. That is, I will turn the miter into a tiara, namely on the head of Jeconiah in Babylon, so that he may be among the petty kings of the Chaldean kingdom, 4 Kings 25, 27. 28. The kings of the Persians, who drew much from the Chaldeans, had an upright cap, the satraps an inclined one. Herodotus is the witness. The former was called cidaris, the latter tiara. See Hesychius, and the Etymologicum Magnum. AND THIS HAS NOT BEEN DONE) There will not be such a one: namely, a tiara in the Davidic house. UNTIL HE COMES WHOSE IS THE JUDGMENT, AND I WILL GIVE IT TO HIM.) Until he comes, to whom it belongs by right, and I will give it to him, namely the tiara. But he is Zerubbabel. The Chaldean draws these things to Gedaliah and Ishmael, less correctly, as I think.

It is not correctly drawn to Gedaliah and Ishmael, nor to Zerubbabel. For the Messiah is understood. For he is the one to whom the crown belonged by right, and to whom it was to be given. It is rash to distinguish between the miter and the tiara, that the former is upright, the latter oblique. These are more subtle than solid. And he commands the miter, or royal diadem, and the royal crown to be taken from the head: because the royal majesty will no longer endure. Osiander expressed the sense excellently from the Hebrew source, correctly with B. Luther, word for word: But you, Prince of Israel (King Zedekiah) who are profaned and condemned (i.e., whom King Nebuchadnezzar has already judged in his council to be unworthy of the kingdom, as one convicted of perfidy and rebellion) when the day comes, when the time of iniquity is finished (i. e. the time of your calamity will come, when you have filled the measure of your crimes.) Thus says the Lord God, put off the Miter (the royal diadem) & take away (from your head) the crown: because it will not be so any longer, as it was before: It will gain another meaning, for that which had been exalted will be humbled, and the humble will be exalted: vain, vain, vain (I say) I will make it (the crown). And this will not yet be done (namely, that the kingdom be given to another) until he comes, to whom it is owed by right (the crown) and I will give it to him (the crown, i.e., the kingdom.) With the Jewish kingdom overturned, Jesus Christ will obtain the Empire. There is nothing here about the miter being turned into a tiara, or an upright cap being changed into an inclined one. Nothing about the dignity of Kings being exchanged with the status of Satraps. Nor is it certain that the tiara was proper to satraps. Both the miter and the crown are said to be overturned. But it is to be given finally to him, whose is the judgment, that is, to Christ. Thus Jerome, as also Theodoret: this, he says, will be more grievous than the former assaults, yet I will not utterly extinguish the spark of the royal lineage, until he comes to whom it pertains, and to whom it is fitting, and I shall deliver the kingdom to him. St. Paul says the same thing, until the seed should come to whom he had promised, ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator, and Jacob the same Patriarch, blessing Judah, said, the prince shall not fail from Judah, nor the leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it is reserved, and he is the expectation of the nations. Therefore, he also hints here at the kingdom of the Lord Christ, when he said, neither will this be such, until he comes to whom it is fitting, and I shall deliver it to him. He explains, therefore, concerning the most recent devastation, in this way: Neither will this be such, (the desolation) namely, as that which is to be (inflicted by the Romans), for I will preserve the race, until he comes to whom it is fitting, and I shall deliver it to him. For when he shall have appeared, to whom the promises are referred, then, the kingdom having been delivered to him, I will exterminate these. Others interpret it concerning the overturning of the crown, done by the Babylonians, not to be restored except by the advent of Christ: Thus the Weimar Paraphrasts from among our own: as also from the Reformed, Oecolampadius, rendering: until he comes who shall judge, and I will give it, that is, until he shall have come, who was to come, Christ Jesus, to whom the Father gave the power of executing judgment: To him he gave an eternal kingdom: as also Piscator, and likewise the Belgian Paraphrasts, and also Junius and Tremellius in their notes, who understand the humble Jeconiah to be exalted, 2 Kings 25:30, Jer. 52:31, and the high Zedekiah to be brought low: and they interpret verse 32 thus: I will render it perverse, perverse, perverse, that is, the kingdom will be utterly overturned and prostrated, and deleted, and by my judgment, by repeated and reiterated disasters through the Babylonian: as it is said in verse 19. ALSO THIS SHALL NOT BE, UNTIL HE COMES WHOSE THE RIGHT ITSELF IS, AND I HAVE DELIVERED IT: also this, namely the crown of Jeconiah: that is, the kingdom so overturned will never emerge from such great perdition, except by the advent of Christ, to whom the right of the kingdom, both by the order of nature and by my calling, is to come. For however much the remnants were gathered, the republic established, and princes named, after the edict of Cyrus, all things were nevertheless most tenuous and most disturbed, as the history of Ezra, Nehemiah, and the Maccabees, and the prophecy of Daniel in the last two chapters show. Thus Junius and Tremellius. Similarly Cornelius à Lapide, TO WHOM THE JUDGMENT IS, That is, the right and this kingdom: For he is not Nebuchadnezzar, as Lyranus and Pintus wish, as also Menochius. Not Zerubbabel, as Polychronius, but Christ, to whom the Father gave all judgment, John 5:22. Because those who were Kings of the Jews after Zedekiah from the Maccabees, such as Alexander, Aristobulus, and Hyrcanus, obtained the kingdom not so much by hereditary right as by force, says St. Jerome. Tirinus agrees with Cornelius, as does Maldonatus. By the three- fold repetition some understand a triple overthrow: the first made by Nebuchadnezzar, the second by Antiochus and the Greeks, the third by Titus and the Romans; others wish the certainty and perfection of the overthrow to be denoted.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

INIQVITATEM, INIQVITATEM, INIQVI- TATEM PONAM EAM) Obliquam, obliquam, obli- quam ponam eam. Id est, cidarim vertam in tiaram, nempe in capite Jechoniæ in Babylonia, ut sit inter regulos regni Chaldaici, 4. Reg. 25, 27. 28. Persarum, qui mul- ta à Chaldæis hausere, reges habebant pileum rectum, satrapæ inflexum. Testis Herodotus. Illud cidaris, hoc tiara vocabatur. Vide Hesychium, & Etymologicum magnum. ET HOC NON FACTVM EST) Non erit talis: nempe tiara in domo Davidica. DONEC VENIRET CVJVS EST JVDICIVM, ET TRADAM EI.) Donec ille veniat, ad quem jure pertinet, & ei tradam, nempe tiaram. Is autem est Zoro- babel. Chaldæus hæc trahit ad Godoliam & Ismaelem, minus recte, ut arbitror.

Neque ad Godaliam & Ismaelem, neque ad Zoro- babelem recte trahitur. Nam intelligitur Messias. Nam ille est, ad quem jure pertinebat corona, & cui tradenda erat. Temere distinguitur inter cidarim & tiaram, quod illa recta, hæc obliqua. Argutiora hæc quam solidiora. Et cidarim, seu diadema Re- gium, & coronam Regiam de capite tolli jubet: quod non amplius majestas Regia duratura sit. Sensum egregie è fonte Ebræo ira recte cum B. Luthero expressit κτ' πόδα Osiander: Tu autem Dux Israel (Rex Sedechia) qui prophanatus & damnatus es (i. e. quem jam Rex Nabuchodonosor in suo con- silio judicavit regno indignum, quippe perfidiæ & rebellionis convictum) cum dies venit, quando tempus iniquitatis finitur (i. e. veniet tempus cala- mitatis tuæ, quando mensuram scelerum implevi- sti.) Sic dicit Dominus Deus, depone Cidarim (dia- dema regium) & tolle (de capite tuo) coronam : quia non ultra sic erit, ut antea: Es wird ein ander Meynung gewinnen, quod enim exaltatum fuerat, humiliabitur, & humile exaltabitur: vanam, va- nam, vanam (inquam) faciam eam (coronam) Et hoc nondum fiet (ut scilicet detur regnum alteri) donec veniat, cui jure debetur (corona) & dabo ei (coronam i. e. regnum.) Regno Judaico everso, Imperium Jesus Christus consequetur. Nihil hic de cidari vertenda in tiaram, aut pileo recto mutan- do in inflexum. Nihil de Regum dignitate com- mutanda cum axiomate Satraparum. Neque con- stat tiaram fuisse satrapis propriam. Evertenda di- citur & cidaris, & corona. Tradenda autem est novissime ei, cujus est judicium, hoc est Christo. Sic Hieronymus, ut & Theodoreus : superiorum op- pugnationum, inquit, hæc gravior erit, non tamen penitus extinguam regiæ cognationis scintillam, quo- ad venerit, ad quem attinet, cuique convenit, & ipsi tradam regnum. Hoc idem D. Paulus ait, donec veniret semen, cui promiserat, ordinata per angelos in manu mediatoris, & Jacob idem Patriarcha Judæ benedicens dixit, non deficiet princeps ex Juda, & dux de femoribus eis, donec veniat, cui repositum est, & ipse expectatio gentium. Igitur hic quoque Domini Christi regnum innuit, cum dixit, neque hæc talis erit, donec venerit, cui congruit & tradam ei. Explicat ergo de novissima devastatione, hoc modo: Neque hæc talis erit, (solitudo) qualis scili- cet futura (à Romanis inferenda) servabo enim genus, donec veniat, cui convenit, & tradam ei. Cum enim apparuerit ille, in quem pollicitationes referun- tur, tunc tradito ipsi regno, istos exterminabo. Alii de eversione coronæ, per Babylonios facta, inter- pretantur, non restituenda nisi adventu Christi: Sic Paraphrastæ Vinarienses è nostris: nec non è Reformatis Oecolampadius, reddens: donec ve- niat is, qui judicet, & dabo eam, id est, donec venerit, qui venturus erat Christus Jesus, cui pater dedit potestatem judicium faciendi: Huic dedit regnum æternum: ut & Piscator, nec non Paraphrastæ Bel- gici, itemque Junius ac Tremellius in not. qui humi- lem exaltandum intelligunt Jechoniam 2. Reg. 25, 30. Jer. 52, 31. & altum deprimendum Zedekiam: & versum 32. ita interpretantur: Perversam, per- versam, perversam reddam illam, id est, funditus eversum & prostratum erit regnum, deletumque & ju- dicio meo, iteratis & repetitis cladibus per Babylo- nium: ut dictum est verf. 19. ETIAM HÆC NON FUTURA EST, DONEC VENE- RIT IS, CUJUS EST JUS IPSUM, ET TRADIDI ILLUD: etiam hæc nempe corona Jechoniæ: id est, regnum ita eversum nunquam emerget è tanta perditione, nisi adventu Christi, ad quem jus regni, & ordine naturæ, & vocatione mea perventurum est. Nam utcunque congregatæ fue- rint reliquiæ, respublica instituta, & principes di- ctæ, post edictum Cyri, omnia tamen fuerunt te- nuissima & conturbatissima, ut historia Hezræ, Ne- hemiæ & Maccabæorum, prophetiaque Danielis ostendunt duobus ultimis capitibus. Ita Junius & Tremellius. Similiter Cornelius à Lapide, CUI EST JUDICIUM, Id est, jus & regnum hoc: Is enim non Nabuchodonosor, ut vult Lyranus, & Pin- tus, ut & Menochius. Non Zorobabel, ut Polychro- nius, sed Christus, cui pater omne judicium dedit Joan. 5, 22. Quia, qui post Sedeciam Judæorum fuerunt Reges ex Machabæis, uti Alexander, Ari- stobulus & Hircanus, non tam jure hæreditario, quam vi regnum adepti sunt, ait S. Hieronymus. Corne- lio consonat Tirinus, ut & Maldonatus. Per tri- nam re petitionem nonnulli intelligunt triplicem eversionem, primam à Nabuchodonosore,alteram ab Antiocho & Græcis, tertiam à Tito & Romanis fa- ctam: alii certitudinem & perfectionem eversionis notari volunt.

## 21:28
Verse 28.

AND THOU SON OF MAN PROPHESY) A new chapter pertaining to the Ammonites ought to have begun here.

AND FOR THEIR REPROACH) And concerning their taunts. For the Ammonites, allies of the Chaldeans, mocked the Jews when they were being treated badly. See Jeremiah 49:1, below 25:6, Zephaniah 2:8.

SWORD, SWORD IS DRAWN TO KILL, POLISH THYSELF THAT THOU MAYEST SLAY, AND SHINE) In the Hebrew: A sword, a sword is drawn, polished to consume by its very brightness. The words are repeated from the preceding verses 9 and 16. This slaughter befell the Ammonites five years after Jerusalem was overthrown, as we said at Jeremiah 48:1, namely because Ishmael, supported by the help of the Ammonites, had invaded the leadership of Judea against the will of the Babylonian. 2 Kings 25:25, Jeremiah 41:15.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

ET TV FILI HOMINIS PROPHETA) No- vum hic caput inchoari debuit ad Ammonitas perti- nens.

ET AD OPPROBRIVM EORVM) Et de expro- brationibus eorum. Nam Ammonitæ Chaldæorum socii ir- risere Judæos,cum male haberentur. Vide Jeremiam 49, 1. infra 25, 6. Sophon. 2, 8.

MVCRO, MVCRO EVAGINA TE AD OCCI- DENDVM, LIMA TE VT INTERFICIAS, ET FVLGEAS) In Hebræo: Mucro, mucro evaginatus est, tersus ad consumendum ipso fulgore. Verba repetita ex supe- rioribus v. 9. 16. Hæc cladesAmmonitis evenit, quinquen- nio post eversa Hierofolyma, ut diximus ad Jerem. 48, 1. nempe quia Ammonitarum ope suffultus Ismaël contra voluntatem Babylonii principatum Judææ invaserat. 2. Reg. 25, 25. Jerem. 41, 15.

## 21:29
Verse 29.

WHILE THEY SAW VANITY UNTO THEE, AND DIVINED LIES) While vain prophecies are brought to thee, O Ammon, and lies are predicted, meanwhile, of course, the sword is being prepared.

TO LAY THEE UPON THE NECKS OF THEM THAT ARE SLAIN, OF THE WICKED) That He may place thee with the necks of the profane wicked. That is, that He may treat thee just as the Jews, who had been treacherous before, were treated. He repeats the words from the preceding verse 25.

WHOSE DAY IS COME, WHEN THEIR INIQUITY SHALL HAVE AN END) When the final day shall arrive at the time opportune for punishment: as above in 25, from where this is taken. In a like matter, like words.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

CVM TIBI VIDERENTVR VANA, ET DI- VINARENTVR MENDACIA) Dum tibi, ô Ammon, vanæ prophetiæ afferuntur, & mendacia prædicuntur, in- terim scilicet paratur gladius.

VT DARETIS SVPER COLLA VVLNERATO- RVM IMPIORVM) Vt ponat te cum collis profanorum impiorum. Id est, ut te tractet sicut Judæi, qui priores perfidi fuerant, tractati sunt. Verba repetit ex superio- ribus v. 25.

QVORVM VENIT DIES IN TEMPORE INI- QVITATIS PRÆFINITÆ) Cum dies ultimus adveniet in tempore opportuno ad pœnam: ut supra 25. unde hoc tran- sumtum est. In re pari paria verba.

## 21:30
Verse 30.

RETURN INTO THY SHEATH) Thou, O sword, that is, the Chaldeans, after thou shalt have executed this, I wish thee to return home; there I will judge thee.

IN THE PLACE WHERE THOU WAST CREATED, IN THE LAND OF THY NATIVITY WILL I JUDGE THEE) I will punish thee in thy home.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

REVERTERE AD VAGINAM TVAM) Tu, ô gladie, id est, Chaldæ, postquam hoc exsequutus fueris, volo domum redeas, ibi te inveniam.

IN LOCO IN QVO CREATVS ES, IN TER- RA NATIVITATIS TVÆ JVDICABO TE) Domi tuæ te puniam.

## 21:31
Verse 31.

AND I WILL GIVE THEE INTO THE HANDS OF FOOLISH MEN) The hands of the raging, as Papinius says of Capaneus. The LXX [say] βαρβάρων [barbarians]. He understands the Medes and Persians.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

DABOQVE TE IN MANVS HOMINVM IN- SIPIENTIVM) Manus insanientium, ut de Capaneo dicit Papinius. LXX. βαρβάρων. Medos & Persas intelligit.

## 21:32
Verse 32. THOU SHALT BE FOOD FOR THE FIRE) Thy city shall be set on fire.

THY BLOOD SHALL BE IN THE MIDST OF THE LAND) That is, it shall appear shed everywhere throughout the land.

THOU SHALT BE DELIVERED TO OBLIVION) For a long time, that is. See on this matter Isaiah 47, Jeremiah 50, 21, above 17, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 32. IGNI ERIS CIBVS) Vrbs tua incen- detur.

SANGVIS TVVS ERIT IN MEDIO TERRÆ) Id est, ubique per terram fusus apparebit.

OBLIVIONI TRADERIS) Diu scilicet. Vide de hac re Esaiam 47. Jerem. 50, 21. supra 17, 24.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII. The various crimes of the Israelites, of the Priests, of the Princes, of the False Prophets, and of the people of the land, so that no one was found who would oppose himself to the Lord to avert His fury.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII. Variæ scelera Israë̈litarum, Sacerdotum, Prin- cipum, Pseudo-Prophetarum, ac populi ter- ræ, ut nullus inventus sit, qui pro averten- do furore Domino se opponeret.

## 22:2
Verse 2.

WILT THOU NOT JUDGE, WILT THOU NOT JUDGE THE CITY OF BLOOD) Whether thou wouldst plead the cause, or plead the cause of the bloodthirsty city? as above 20, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

NONNE JVDICAS, NONNE JVDICAS CI- VITATEM SANGVINVM) An causam ageres, an causam ageres civitatis sanguinariæ? ut supra 20, 4.

## 22:3
AND SHOW HER ALL HER ABOMINATIONS) Nay, show her all her own crimes.

Verse 3.

SHEDDING BLOOD IN THE MIDST OF IT) That is, everywhere.

THAT HER TIME MAY COME) That she may summon swift punishment upon herself. Here 'that' is ἐκϐατικὸν [consecutive/resultative]. Compare what follows in 4.

AND THE IDOLS WHICH SHE MADE AGAINST HER- SELF, THAT SHE MIGHT BE POLLUTED) A transposition for, the idols which she made, by the worship of which she polluted herself, and that to her own greatest harm.

Latin:

ET OSTENDES EI OMNES ABOMINATIO- NES SVAS) Quin ostende ei omnia scelera ipsius.

Vers. 3.

EFFVNDENS SANGVINEM IN MEDIO SVI) Id est, passim.

VT VENIAT TEMPVS EJVS) Ut sibi pœnam accersat celerem. Hic ut est ἐκϐατικὸν, Confer quod sequitur 4.

ET QVÆ FECIT IDOLA CONTRA SEMET- IPSAM, VT POLLVERETVR) Transpositio pro, quæ fecit idola, quorum cultu se pollueret, idque suo malo maximo.

## 22:4
Ver. 4.

IN THY BLOOD, WHICH WAS SHED BY THEE, THOU HAST SINNED) That is, thou art proven guilty.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

IN SANGVINE TVO, QVI A TE EFFVSVS EST, DELIQVISTI) Id est, rea perageris.

## 22:5
Ver. 5.

THE FILTHY, NOBLE, GREAT IN DESTRUCTION SHALL TRIUMPH OVER THEE) They shall cry out against thee, O infamous one, who hast killed many. סמם is often translated by this very interpreter as to kill.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

TRIVMPHABVNT DE TE SORDIDA, NOBILIS, GRANDIS INTERITV) Clamabunt adversum te ô insa- mis, quæ multos occidisti. סמם sæpe ab hoc ipso interprete vertitur occidere.

## 22:6
Ver. 6.

BEHOLD THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL, EVERY ONE ACCORDING TO HIS ARM, WERE IN THEE) The LXX, having changed the vowel in זרעו, [translate] πρὸς τὸς συγγενεῖς ἀυτᾶ, that is, they were contrary to their own kinsmen, whom the Hebrews call זרו, as also בשר in Isaiah 48:7, and the following words confirm this. The version of the LXX is perversely preferred to the Hebrew text, which is clear and stands very well in this manner: the princes, every one according to his arm, that is, according to his ability, each one harmed his neighbor. But that translation concerning kinsmen is foreign to this place.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ECCE PRINCIPES ISRAEL SINGVLI IN BRA- CHIO SVO FVERVNT IN TE) LXX. mutata vocali in זרעו πρὸς τὸς συγγενεῖς ἀυτᾶ, id est, consanguineis suis contrarii fuere, quos Hebræi זרו vocant, ut & בשר Esai. 48, 7. idque firmant sequentia. PErversè præfertur versio τῶν ὁ Ebræo textui, qui luculentus est, & optime se habet h. m. principes singuli secundum brachium suum, id est, pro facultate sua, quisque læsit proximum suum. Illa vero translatio de consanguineis aliena est hoc loco.

## 22:8
Ver. 8.

THOU HAST DESPISED MY SANCTUARIES) That is, thou hast profaned them with the worship of idols.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SANCTVARIA MEA SPREVISTI) Id est, pro- fanasti cultu idolorum.

## 22:9
Ver. 9.

MEN WHO WERE SLANDERERS WERE IN THEE TO SHED BLOOD) Slandering unto blood, as the Latins say. THEY HAVE COMMITTED WICKEDNESS IN THE MIDST OF THEE) They prostituted their daughters to Venus, in honor of the gods, after the Babylonian custom. Leviticus 19:29.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

VIRI DETRACTORES FVERVNT IN TE AD EFFVNDENDVM SANGVINEM) In sanguinem calu- mniantes, ut loquuntur Latini. SCELVS OPERATI SVNT IN MEDIO TVI) Prostituerunt filias in Venerem, in honorem deorum, more Babylonico. Levit. 19, 29.

## 22:10
Ver. 10.

THEY HAVE UNCOVERED THE SHAMEFUL PARTS OF THE FATHER IN THEE) Daughters have lain with their fathers after the manner of the Arabs. THEY HAVE HUMBLED THE UNCLEANNESS OF THE MENSTRUOUS WOMAN IN THEE) That is, they have oppressed virgins at the very time in which they were being cleansed. We have said that ענה is taken thus at Deut. 21, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

VERECVNDIORA PATRIS DISCOOPERVE- RVNT IN TE) Filiæ cum patribus concubuere more Arabum. IMMVNDITIAM MENSTRVATÆ HVMILIA- VERVNT IN TE) Id est, oppresserunt virgines ipso tempore quo purgabantur. Ita ענה sumi diximus ad Deut. 21, 14.

## 22:11
Vers. 11. THE WIFE OF HIS NEIGHBOUR) The Israelites. HE HATH COMMITTED ABOMINATION) That is, they have abused them most foully. For that is properly תועבה. See Levit. 18, vers. 22. LEWDLY) In honor of the gods, as above 9. HIS SISTER THE DAUGHTER OF HIS FATHER) Of the same family name. See Gen. 20, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VXOREM PROXIMI SVI) Israëlitæ. FECIT ABOMINATIONEM) Id est, fœdissime illis abusi sunt. Id enim proprie תועבה. Vide Levit. 28. vers. 22. NEFARIE) In honorem deorum, ut supra 9. SOROREM SVAM FILIAM PATRIS SVI) Ejusdem familiæ nominis. Vide Gen. 20, 12.

## 22:12
Vers. 12.

THEY HAVE TAKEN GIFTS IN THEE TO SHED BLOOD) Which is punished by the Cornelian law concerning assassins among the Romans, L. 1. §. præterea, D. ad L. Corneliam. THOU HAST TAKEN USURY AND INCREASE) See what was said at chapter 18, 8. AND HAST GREEDILY CALUMNIATED THY NEIGHBOURS) Thou hast coveted the property of thy neighbour through concupiscence. בצע to covet, is elsewhere translated by the LXX as πλεονεκτεῖν, which is excellent for the sense.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

MVNERA ACCEPERVNT APVD TE AD EF- FVNDENDVM SANGVINEM) Quod lege Cornelia de Sicariis punitum apud Romanos L. 1. §. præterea, D. ad L. Corneliam. VSVRAM ET SVPERABVNDANTIAM ACCE- PERVNT) Vide quæ dicta ad caput 18, 8. ET AVARE PROXIMOS TVOS CALVMNIA- BARIS) Appetivisti (rem) proximi tui per concupiscentiam. בצע appetere, à LXX. alibi vertitur πλεονεκτεῖν, ad sensum optime.

## 22:13
Vers. 13.

BEHOLD I HAVE CLAPPED MY HANDS AT THY COVETOUSNESS) That is, as a punishment for your covetousness, when goods shall be taken away, and of slaughter, when thou shalt be laid waste with slaughters. I will clap my hands, that is, I will applaud, as above 21, 17. I will make a clapping, says Plautus.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ECCE COMPLOSI MANVS MEAS SVPER AVARITIAM TVAM) Id est, ob pœnam avaritiæ vestræ, cum bona auferentur, & cædium, cum cædibus vastaberis. Complodam manus, id est, applaudam, ut supra 21, 17. Fa- cebo sapulanti, ait Plautus.

## 22:14
Vers. 14. CAN THINE HEART ENDURE) Will not thy heart fail thee, when thou shalt have fallen into these evils?

Latin:

Vers. 14. NVMQVID SVSTINEBIT COR TVVM) An non linquet tibi cor, ubi in ista mala incideris?

## 22:15
Vers. 15.

I WILL SCATTER INTO THE LANDS) As chaff. Above 20, 23. AND I WILL MAKE THY FILTHINESS TO CEASE FROM THEE) Thou shalt cease to be fruitful by retaining thy monthly periods. For it persists in the likeness of a woman. See Levit. 15, 25. Where the word טמאה is in the same sense. The punishment corresponds to the sin, of which above v. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

VENTILABO IN TERRAS) Vt paleam. Supra 20, 23. ET DEFICERE FACIAM IMMVNDITIAM TV- AM A TE) Desines esse fœcunda retentis mensibus. In similitudine n. fœminæ persistat. Vide Levit. 15, 25. Vbi vox טמאה eodem sensu. Respondet pœna peccato, de quo supra v. 10.

## 22:16
Vers. 16.

AND I WILL BE PROFANED IN THEE IN THE SIGHT OF THE NATIONS) In the Hebrew it is a verb of the second person, and I think it is more correctly translated: Thou shalt be polluted in thyself: from חלל not from נחל, so that it may persist in that which he said. Thou shalt retain thy uncleannesses within thee, and that shall appear from thy face. The sense is allegorical: Thou shalt not only be unfruitful, but also foul to look upon.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET POSSIDEBO TE IN CONSPECTv GEN- TIVM) In Hebræo est verbum secundæ personæ, & puto rectius verti: Polluta eris in te: à חלל non à נחל, ut per- stet in eo quod dixit. Immunditias tuas intra te retinebis, idque ex facie apparebit. Sensus est allegoricus: Non in- fœcunda tantum eris, sed & fœda adspectu.

## 22:18
Vers. 18.

THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL IS BECOME DROSS UNTO ME) It seems to me that סוג or סיג is not merely dross, that is, the refuse or excrement of silver, but everything that is mixed with silver and ought to be separated from it. I am led to this by the following words in this passage and the origin of the word from סוג, which means to depart, and the authority of the LXX interpreters, who translated it ἀναμεμιγμένοι. ALL THEY ARE BRASS, AND TIN, AND IRON, AND LEAD, IN THE MIDST OF THE FURNACE: THEY ARE EVEN THE DROSS OF SILVER) Namely, a mixture of baser metals, as we have already said. It seems that כור is a crucible rather than a furnace. See 1 Kings 8:51, and that the series of this place demands. For it is a mixture before it is cast into the fire.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

VERSA EST MIHI DOMVS ISRAEL IN SCO- RIAM) Videtur mihi סוג sive סיג non esse scoria tantum, id est, retrimentum aut stercus argenti, sed omne id quod admixtum argento separari inde debet. Eo me trahunt se- quentia hoc in loco & origo vocis à סוג, quod est absce- dere, & auctoritas LXX. interpretum, qui verterunt ἀναμε- μιγμένοι. OMNES ISTI ÆS, ET STANNVM, ET FER- RVM, ET PLVMBVM IN MEDIO FORNACIS: SCORIA FACTI ARGENTI SVNT) Mixtura scilicet viliorum metallorum, ut jam diximus. Videtur כור potius esse catinus quam fornax. Vide 1. Reg. 8, 51. idque series hujus loci postulat. Mixtura enim est antequam in ignem mittatur.

## 22:19
Ver. 19.

I WILL GATHER YOU IN THE MIDST OF JERUSALEM) Just as that mass of silver and baser material, having been gathered, is cast into the crucible.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

CONGREGABO VOS IN MEDIO JERVSA- LEM) Sicut illa massa ex argento, & viliori materia con- gregata in catinum conjicitur.

## 22:20
THAT I MAY KINDLE A FIRE IN IT TO MELT) To smelt: that is, to separate from the others. The silver are the few pious ones, whom God is about to save.

Ver. 20.

AND I WILL REST, AND I WILL MELT YOU) And having placed you (there), I will smelt you.

Latin:

VT SVCCENDAM IN EA IGNEM AD CON- FLANDVM) Ad fundendum: id est, ad separandam a cæ- teris. Argentum sunt pauci pii, quos Deus servaturus est.

Vers. 20.

ET REQUIESCAM, ET CONFLABO VOS) Et collocatos (ibi) vos fundam.

## 22:24
Ver. 24.

THOU ART AN UNCLEAN LAND, AND NOT RAINED UPON IN THE DAY OF INDIGNATION) He calls rocks and other things that are of no use an unclean land, no more than the unclean animals. Men of no worth are compared to this. Thou art not rained upon, that is, thou hast not admitted the rain, by which prophecy is signified, as we said 21, 2. in the day of indignation, that is, not even then, when I was threatening the most grievous things to thee.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

TV ES TERRA IMMVNDA, ET NON COM- PLVTA IN DIE FVRORIS) Terram immundam vocat rupes & alia quæ nulli sunt usui, non magis quam anima- lium immunda. Huic comparantur homines nullius frugis Non es compluta, id est, pluviam non admisisti, per quam significatur prophetia, ut diximus 21, 2. in die indignatio- nis, id est, ne tum quidem, cum gravissima tibi minarer.

## 22:25
Ver. 25.

CONSPIRACY OF THE PROPHETS) Of the false ones. The Chaldean understands scribes, that is, interpreters of the law, here and elsewhere.

THEY HAVE DEVOURED SOULS) That is, they have raged even unto blood.

THEY HAVE TAKEN WEALTH AND PRICE) For good predictions. See above 13.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

CONJVRATIO PROPHETARVM) Falsorum. Scribas, id est, legis interpretes intelligit hic & alibi Chal- dæus,

ANIMAS DEVORAVERUNT) Id est, sævierunt etiam in sanguinem.

OPES ET PRETIVM ACCEPERVNT) Pro bonis prædictionibus. Vide supra 13.

## 22:26
Vers. 26.

HER PRIESTS HAVE DESPISED MY LAW) They violated it, whose primary duty it was to teach the law. Malach. 2, 7.

AND HAVE PROFANED MY SANCTUARIES) With idolatrous rites. Above 8.

THEY HAVE HAD NO DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE HOLY AND THE PROFANE, AND HAVE NOT UNDERSTOOD BETWEEN THE POLLUTED AND THE CLEAN) They did not make them understand, namely the distinction, ἀπὸ κοινᾶ. The words themselves are from Levit. 10, 10, where they are commanded to do what they are said here to have neglected. Holy is that which is dedicated to God: profane is that which is in common use. Polluted is that which is forbidden to be eaten: clean is that which is permitted to be eaten.

AND THEY HAVE TURNED AWAY THEIR EYES FROM MY SABBATHS) They do not care if the people violate the sabbaths. Jerem. 17. vers. 27.

AND I WAS PROFANED IN THE MIDST OF THEM) They abuse my name for false or iniquitous things.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

SACERDOTES EJVS CONTEMPSERVNT LE- GEM MEAM) Violaverunt illi, quorum erat præcipuum munus legem docere. Malach. 2, 7.

ET POLLVERVNT SANCTVARIA MEA) Ido- lolatricis ritibus. Supra 8.

INTER SANCTVM ET PROFANVM NON HABVERVNT DISTANTIAM, ET INTER POL- LVTVM ET MVNDVM NON INTELLEXERVNT) Non intelligere fecerunt, nempe distantiam ἀπὸ κοινᾶ Verba ipsa sunt ex Levit. 10, 10. ubi facere jubentur quos hic dicuntur neglexisse. Sanctum quod Deo dicatum est: profanum quod in usu communi. Pollutum quod vesci vetitum : mundum quod vesci licet.

ET A SABBATIS MEIS AVERTERVNT OCV- LOS) Non curant, si populus sabbata violet. Jerem. 17. vers. 27.

ET CONQVINABAR IN MEDIO EORVM) Nomine meo ad res falsas aut iniquas abutuntur.

## 22:27
Vers. 27.

HER PRINCES IN THE MIDST OF HER, AS WOLVES RAVENING THE PREY) He walks through all the orders, noting individual vices. Compare Jerem. 8. & 23.

As the rapacity of the false prophets is compared to lions, so the tyranny of the princes is compared to wolves. Zeph. 3, 3. Gen. 49, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

PRINCIPES EJVS IN MEDIO ILLIVS, QVASI LVPI RAPIENTES PRÆDAM) Per omnes ordines am- bulat, vitia singula notans. Confer. Jerem. 8. & 23.

Ut Pseudo-Prophetarum rapacitas cum leoni- bus, ita Principum tyrannis cum lupis confertur Zeph. 3, 3. Gen. 49, 27.

## 22:28
Vers. 28.

THEY DAUBED THEM WITHOUT TEMPERING) With inept plaster. As above 13, 11.

SEEING VAIN THINGS) This also and what follows are repeated from chapter 13.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

LINIEBANT EOS ABSQVE TEMPERAMEN- TO) Inepto tectorio. Vt supra 13, 11.

VIDENTES VANA) Hoc quoque & quæ sequun- tur sunt repetita ex capite 13.

## 22:29
Ver. 29. PEOPLE OF THE LAND) The common people.

THEY OPPRESSED WITH CALUMNY WITHOUT JUDGMENT) Without cause: for that is what מִשְׁפָּט means here.

Denied public justice is denoted. Harac. 1. ver. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 29. POPVLI TERRÆ) Plebs.

OPPRIMEBANT CALVMNIA ABSQVE JV- DICIO) Absque causa: id enim hic מִשְׁפָּט.

Denotatur denegata publica justitia. Harac. 1. vers. 3.

## 22:30
Ver. 30.

WHO MIGHT INTERPOSE A HEDGE) Who might fortify the interior: as is accustomed to be done, where a part of the wall has been torn down by the enemy.

AND MIGHT STAND OPPOSED AGAINST ME FOR THE LAND) In the Hebrew: And might stand in the breach of the wall. He might defend the gaps. Both similitudes are also placed above in chapter 13, 5. With God attacking the wall, he fortifies the interior who urges the people to a better way. He stands in the ruin who prays for the people, as Moses in Exodus 22. ver. 11. Aaron. Num. 12, 48.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

QVI INTERPONERET SEPEM) Qui interio- ra muniret: ut fieri solet, ubi pars muri disjecta est ab hoste.

ET STARET OPPOSITVS CONTRA ME PRO TERRA) In Hebræo: Et staret in rupta parte muri. Hiantia defenderet. Utraque similitudo etiam supra posita est ca- pite 13, 5. Deo murum oppugnante, interiora munit qui hortatur populum ad viam meliorem. Stat in ruina qui precatur pro populo, ut Moses Exodi 22. vers. 11. Aaron. Num. 12, 48.

## 22:31
Ver. 31. THEIR WAY UPON THEIR HEAD I HAVE RENDERED) I will render. As above 7, 4. 27. chap. 9, 10. c. 16, 43. below 24. ver. 14.

Latin:

Vers. 31. VIAM EORVM IN CAPVT EORVM REDDIDI) Reddam. Vt supra 7, 4. 27. cap. 9, 10. c. 16, 43. infra 24. vers. 14.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII.

The manifold whoredom of Aholah, that is, Samaria, and Aholibah, that is, Jerusalem, whence they fall into the reproach of the nations whose idolatry they chose.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII.

Stuprum multiplex Abalæ, id est, Samariæ, & Abalibæ, id est, Ierusalem, unde cedunt in opprobrium gentium quarum idolola- triam elegerunt.

## 23:2
Ver. 2.

TWO WOMEN THE DAUGHTERS OF ONE MOTHER WERE) Two nations sprung from Sarah.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DUÆ MVLIERES FILIÆ MATRIS VNIVS FUERVNT) Duæ gentes ortæ ex Sara.

## 23:3
Ver. 3.
