AND THEY PLAYED THE HARLOT IN EGYPT) Already then they drank in the seeds of idolatry, from which Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had been most alien. See above 20, 8.

IN HER YOUTH THEY PLAYED THE HARLOT) What he translates here as youth, in Hebrew is נער, which in females signifies the age that is before the twelfth year: as if he were to say, they did not remember that they had been virgins: they were defiled with their equals, as Petronius says. A wonderful deίνωσις (amplification).

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET FORNICATÆ SVNT IN ÆGTPTO) Jam tum hauserunt semina idololatriæ, à qua Abrahamus, Isaa- cus, Jacobus fuerant alienissimi. Vide supra 20, 8.

IN ADOLESCENTIA SVA FORNICATÆ SVNT) Quod hic transfert adolescentiam, in Hebræo est נער, quod in feminis significat ætatem, quæ est ante annum duodecimum: quasi dicat, non meminerunt se virgines fuisse: pares cum paribus inquinatæ sunt, ut loquitur Pe- tronius. Mira deίνωσις.

## 23:4
Ver. 4.

OOLLA THE ELDER) Elder in the number of the tribes, which were ten with Samaria. אָהֳלָה, as Jerome and others have well interpreted, that people is called, because it had made for itself places of divine worship, which are called by the name אֹהֶל, that is, a tent, because the first worship of God among the Israelites was in a tent. אָהֳלָה, that is, her tent for herself.

AND OOLIBA HER SISTER THE YOUNGER) אָהֳלִיבָה, my tent in her: for God had placed His temple there, which is called by the name of a tent, not only for the reason we have stated, but also because God could take away that Temple as easily (concerning which they boasted irrelevantly) as men can a tent.

Polychronius and the old Scholiast think these were the proper names of two famous Egyptian harlots. Others think God had regard for Esau's wife Ahalibama, Gen. 36, 2. But Jerome's opinion is to be preferred, that these names were imposed by the will of God, because Samaria had built her tabernacle for herself out of superstition, whereas in Jerusalem was the tabernacle of the Lord. Compare 1 Kings 12, 16; Job 4, 20.

AND I HAD THEM) They became mine. I joined them to myself in marriage.

THEIR NAMES SAMARIA, OOLLA AND JERUSALEM OOLIBA) He explains what he had said more obscurely.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

OOLLA MAJOR) Major numero tribuum, quæ pe- nes Samariam decem fuere. אָהֳלָה, ut Hieronymus, & alii bene sunt interpretati, vocatur ille populus, ideo quòd sibi fecisset loca divini cultus, quæ אֹהֶל, id est, tentorii no- mine vocantur, quia primus Dei cultus apud Israëlitast fuit in tentorio. אָהֳלָה, id est, tentorium suum sibi.

ET COLIBA SOROR EJUS MINOR( אָהֳלִיבָה, tentorium meum ibi: Deus enim ibi collocaverat templum suum, quod tentorii nomine appellar, non tantum ob eam quam diximus causam, verum etiam quia tam facile Deus illud Templum auferre poterat, (de quo præter rem glo- riabantur) quam homines tentorium.

Polychronius & Scholiastees vetus putant no- mina hæc propria fuisse meretricum duarum in- signium Ægyptiacarum. Alii Deum respectum habuisse ad Esavi uxorem Ahalibama Gen. 36, 2. Sed præferenda Hieronymi sententia, nomina hæc arbitrio Dei esse imposita, quod Samaria sibi ex superstitione tabernaculum suum exstruxerit, Hierosolymis vero fuerit tabernaculum Domini. Conf. 1. Reg. 12, 16. Job. 4, 20.

ET HABVI EAS) Mæ factæ sunt. Ego eas mihi conjugio copulavi.

EARVM NOMINA SAMARIA, OOLLA ET JERVSALEM OOLIBA) Explicat quod obscurius di- xerat.

## 23:5
Ver. 5.

THEREFORE OOLLA PLAYED THE HARLOT AGAINST ME) In the Hebrew: Under me: that is, when she was under my hand and power, that is, she committed adultery. Solomon indeed had begun to permit privately what he ought not. But the ten tribes instituted worship publicly against the law, having set up calves.

AND SHE DATED IN HER LOVERS THE ASSYRIANS DRAWING NEAR) Made neighbors to themselves through Syria, a good part of which they had occupied. See 2 Kings 15, 19; Isaiah 7, 8. Judea is said to have committed adultery with those whose rites she imitated. We have often noted that many of the Hebrews, unmindful of the law and the benefits of God, whose friendship they greatly coveted, flattered them by the imitation of their rites. The history of the events which begins in 1 Kings 16, 31 and continues in 2 Kings 15, 20 is touched upon here.

The word עגב is to burn, or to be inflamed with lust, and to behave oneself quite immoderately or to be insane, v. 7, 9, 12, 16, 20. But the word for drawing near from v. 12 is explained more correctly as referring to those coming to her, rather than the proximity of the province, as R. Solomon and Grotius, following Tremellius, do.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

FORNICATA EST IGITVR SVPER ME OOL- LA) In Hebræo: Sub me: id est, cum sub mea esset manu ac potestate, id est, mœchata est. Solomon quidem pri- vatim cœperat permittere, quæ non debebat. At de- cem tribus publice contra legem cultum instituere, vitu- lis excitatis.

ET INSANIVIT IN AMATORES SVOS IN AS- STRIOS PROPINQVANTES) Vicinos sibi factos per Sy- riam, cujus bonam partem occupaverant. Vide 2. Reg. 15, 19. Esai. 7, 8. Dicitur Judæa mœchata cum illis, quorum ritus imitata est. Sæpe jam id notavimus Hebræorum mul- tos immemores legis & beneficiorum Dei, quorum ami- citiam valde ambiebant, eis blanditos rituum imitatione. Tangitur hic historia rerum quæ incipit 1. Reg. 16, 31. continuatur 2. Reg. 15, 20.

Verbum עגב est ardere, seu æstuare libidine, & plane immoderate se gerere seu insanire v. 7. 9. 12. 16, 20. Verbum autem propinquandi è v. 12. de ve- nientibus ad se rectius explicatur, quam de vici- nitate provinciæ, ut R. Salom. & Tremellium sequu- tus Grotius.

## 23:6
Verse 6.

PRINCES AND MAGISTRATES CLOTHED IN HYACINTH, YOUTHS OF CUPID, ALL HORSEMEN RIDING HORSES) Just as women are accustomed to be inflamed by the luxury of garments, by titles of honor, by youthful age, by a vigorous body, so the power of the Assyrians had enticed the Israelites. See 2 Kings 8:24, Isaiah 10:8.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

VESTITOS HYACINTHO PRINCIPES ET MAGISTRATVS, JVVENES CVPIDINIS, UNI- VERSOS EQVITES ASCENSORES EQVORVM) Sicut feminæ incendi solent luxu vestium, honorum nominibus, juvenili ætate, corpore vegeto, sic Israe- litas pellexerat Assyriorum potentia. Vide 2. Reg. 8, 24. Esai. 10,8.

## 23:7
AND SHE BESTOWED HER WHOREDOMS UPON THEM) With them, that is, she prostituted herself to them. ELECTOS) The chosen ones, i.e., young men.

Ver. 7.

AND WITH ALL WHOM SHE DATED AFTER IN THEIR UNCLEANNESSES SHE WAS DEFILED) In Latin we would say: in the lusts of all those after whom she doted, she was defiled. The sense is: she never denied anything to her lovers: and there is force in the word גלולים, which signifies both filth and idols.

Latin:

ET DEDIT FORNICATIONES SUAS SUPER EOS) Cum illis, id est, prostituit se illis. ELECTOS) Iuvenes.

Vers. 7.

ET IN OMNIBUS IN QVOS INSANIVIT IN IMMUNDITIIS EORUM POLLUTA EST) Lati- nine diceremus: in libidinibus eorum omnium in quos insanivit, polluta est. Sensus est: nihil unquam amatori- bus negavit: & vis est in voce גלולים, quæ & sordes & idola significat.

## 23:8
Ver. 8.

MOREOVER SHE LEFT NOT HER WHOREDOMS BROUGHT FROM EGYPT) She returned to those rites, so that she might incite the Egyptians against the two tribes. 2 Chron. 12, 2. 3. 4.

FOR THEY LAY WITH HER IN HER YOUTH, AND THEY BRUISED THE BREASTS OF HER VIRGINITY, AND POURED THEIR WHOREDOM UPON HER) Better: They had lain, they had handled, they had poured out their whoredom. That is, pleasure, as Hyginus speaks in the fable of Erichthonius.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

INSUPER ET FORNICATIONES SUAS, QVAS HABUERAT IN ÆGYPTO NON RELIQVIT) Ad eos ritus rediit, ut Ægyptios incitaret contra duas tribus. 2. Paralip. 12, 2. 3. 4.

NAM ET ILLI DORMIVERUNT CUM ILLA IN ADOLESCENTIA EJVS, ET ILLI CONFREGE- RUNT UBERA PUBERTATIS EJUS, ET EFFUDE- RUNT FORNICATIONEM SUAM SUPER EAM) Melius: Dormierant, contrectaverant, effuderant suam for- nicationem. Id est, voluptatem, ut Hyginus loquitur in fabula Erichthonii.

## 23:9
Ver. 9.

INTO THE HANDS OF THE SONS OF ASSUR) Pul, Tiglath-pileser, Shalmaneser.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

IN MANUS FILIORUM ASSUR) Phulis, Ti- glathphilasfari Salmanasari.

## 23:10
Ver. 10.

THEY DISCOVERED HER NAKEDNESS) They left her naked.

AND SHE BECAME FAMOUS AMONG WOMEN, AND THEY EXECUTED JUDGMENTS UPON HER) Her name became (infamous, that is) among women, after (the Assyrians) executed the judgments (of God) against her.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

IPSI DISCOOPERVERUNT IGNOMINIAM EJUS) Nudam destituerunt.

ET FACTÆ SUNT FAMOSÆ MULIERES, ET JUDICIA PERPETRAVERUNT IN EA) Fuit nomen (ejus, infame scilicet) inter mulieres, postquam (Assyrii) judicia (Dei) exercuerunt adversus eam.

## 23:12
Ver. 12.

PRÆBUIT IMPUDENTER) He gave, Martial would say.

INDUTIS VESTE VARIA) Adorned with a crown. For מכלולא among the Chaldeans, and perhaps the Assyrians, is a crown. Nor did the Syrian understand it otherwise in Psalm 52. It was the custom for lovers to approach their beloveds with a crown.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

PRÆBUIT IMPUDENTER) Dedit, diceret Mar- tialis.

INDUTIS VESTE VARIA) Redimitis corona. Nam מכלולא Chaldæis, forte & Assyriis, corona. Nec aliter accepit Syrus Psal. 52. Mos erat amantibus amicas adire cum corona.

## 23:14
Vers. 14.

CUMQVE VIDISSET VIROS PICTOS IN PARIETE) Claudian: Let the painting go through the countless household gods. Thus Paris desired Helen: And he burned with love for the girl he had never seen.

EXPRESSAS COLORIBUS) With sinopia. See Jerem. 22, 14.

Maldonatus, Sanctius, Cornelius, and Pintus understand the heroes and princes of the Chaldeans, whose images and deeds the Jews venerated. B. Hulsemann thinks rather that the likenesses of idols depicted on the walls of the Jews should be understood. See ch. 8, 3. 5. 10. ch. 16, 17. But Osiander's explanation seems simpler and more consistent with the text, concerning the Babylonian princes depicted in their native attire and most majestic form, from which the Jews had been enticed into treaties, communion, and further into their idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

CUMQVE VIDISSET VIROS PICTOS IN PA- RIETE) Claudianus: Lena per innumeros iret pictura penates. Sic Paris Helenam concupivit: Et nunquam visa flagravit amore puellæ.

EXPRESSAS COLORIBUS) Sinopide. Vide Jerem. 22, 14.

Maldonatus, Sanctius, Cornelius, Pintus He- roas & principes Chaldæorum intelligunt, quo- rum imagines & res gestas venerati fuerint Judæi. B. Hulsemanm. videntur potius idolorum simula- cra intelligenda esse in parietibus Judæorum de- picta. V. c. 8, 3. 5. 10. cap. 16, 17. Simplicior autem videtur Osiandri explicatio, textuique magis con- veniens de principibus Babylonicis in patrio ha- bitu, & augustissima forma depictis, unde ad fœ- dera, & communionem ac porro ad idololatriam eorum pellecti fuerant Judæi.

## 23:15
Vers. 15.

ACCINGEBAT BALTEIS RENES) In military attire. It is iron that they love, this makes them Hyacinths.

ET TIARAS TINCTAS IN CAPITIBUS EORUM) Helmets, the Chaldean. Understand 'tinctas' as adorned with various feathers. The Greeks: παραβαπτά ἐπὶ τῶν κεφαλῶν ἀυτῶν.

ET FORMAM DUCUM OMNIUM) In the Hebrew: Every form of protectors. See what we said at Exodus 15, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ACCINGEBAT BALTEIS RENES) Militari ha- bitu. Ferrum est quod amant, facit hoc illos Hyacinthos.

ET TIARAS TINCTAS IN CAPITIBUS EO- RUM) Galeas, Chaldæus. Tinctas intellige, ornatas variis plumis. Græci παραβαπτά ἐπὶ τῶν κεφαλῶν ἀυτῶν.

ET FORMAM DUCUM OMNIUM) In He- bræo: Omnis forma protectorum. Vide quæ diximus ad Exodi 15, 4.

## 23:16
Vers. 16.

ET MISIT NUNTIOS AD EOS IN CHALDÆAM) He courted them of his own accord.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET MISIT NUNTIOS AD EOS IN CHAL- DÆAM) Ultro ambivit.

## 23:17
Verse 17.

TO THE BED OF THE BREASTS) What she calls the bed of the breasts can be understood from those things which we said at 23, 2. A bed, that is, בית מקום, as the Talmudists speak.

AND SHE WAS SATIATED WITH THEIR SOULS)

Satiated with their intercourse, she turned herself again to the Egyptians. 2 Kings 14, 7. For children are not changed by their parents as much as they are by an unchaste adulteress: says Agrippina in Tacitus. They call the adultery of one person a marriage, says Seneca.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

AD CUBILE MAMMARUM) Quid cubile mam- marum vocet, intelligi potest ex iis quæ diximus 23, 2. Cubile, id est, בית מקום, ut loquuntur Talmudici.

ET SATIATA EST ANIMÆ EJUS AB ILLIS)

Illorum concubitu satiata ad Ægyptios iterum se vertit. 2. Reg. 14, 7. Neque enim perinde à parentibus liberi, quam ab impudica adulteri mutantur: ait apud Tacitum Agrippi- na. Unius adulterium matrimonium vocant, ait Seneca.

## 23:18
Verse 18. SHE ALSO STRIPPED NAKED HER WHOREDOMS, AND DISCOVERED HER SHAME) It coheres with the above, in this sense: She was satiated, after she had made her lust so known to them, that she voluntarily thrust before their sight those things which ought to be covered.

MY SOUL DEPARTED FROM HER) It could no longer endure the adulteress, both impudent and fickle.

Latin:

Vers. 18. DENUDAVIT QVOQVE FORNICA- TIONES SUAS, ET DISCOOPERUIT IGNOMINIAM SUAM) Cohæret cum superioribus, hoc sensu: Satiata est, postquam libidinem suam ita cognitam ipsis fecerat, ut ultro aspectui ingereret quæ tegi debent.

RECESSIT ANIMA AB EO) Ultra ferre non po- tuit mœcham, & impudentem, & desultoriam.

## 23:19
Verse 19. FOR SHE MULTIPLIED HER WHOREDOMS) As that woman in Ausonius: Lest she should leave anything untried, about to die in vain.

REMEMBERING THE DAY OF HER YOUTH.

Having imitated her former lust in Egypt. Pagninus, Pradus, Sanctius, and Maldonatus, along with Theodoret, wrongly refer that 'remembering' to GOD. B. Luther, Münster, R. David Kimchi, and Tremellius are more correct. Hector Pintus refers it to Judea multiplying her whoredoms. So also Osiander and D. Hulsemann.

Latin:

Vers. 19. MULTIPLICAVIT ENIM FORNICA- TIONES SUAS) Ut illa apud Ausonium: Ne quid inexpertum frustra moritura relinquat.

RECORDANS DIEI ADOLESCEN- TIÆ.

Imitata pristinam libidinem in Ægypto. Per- peram illud recordari ad DEUM referunt Pa- gninus, Pradus, Sanctius, Maldonatus cum Theo- dor. rectius B. Luther. Münsterus, R. David Kimch. Tremellius. Hector Pintus ad Judæam mul- tiplicantem fornicationes suas. Sic etiam Osian- der & D. Hulsemannus.

## 23:20
Verse 20. WHOSE FLESH IS AS THE FLESH OF ASSES) He calls the Egyptians well-endowed, that is, excellent in the worship of idols. We had a similar one above at 12, 26. The ὄνος was consecrated to Priapus: and the Greeks call the masculine part ὄνον, according to Favorinus.

AND THEIR ISSUES ARE AS THE ISSUES OF HORSES) Venom, as Virgil speaks.

Latin:

Vers. 20. QVORUM CARNES SUNT UT CARNES ASINORUM) Ægyptios dicit bene vasatos, id est, in ido- lorum cultu eximios. Simile habuimus supra 12, 26. ὄνος Priapo consecratus: & Græci masculinam partem ὄνον vo- cant, teste Favorino.

ET SUNT FLUXUS EQVORUM FLUXUS EO- RUM) Virus, ut Virgilius loquitur.

## 23:21
Verse 21.

AND THE BREASTS OF THY PUBERTY ARE BROKEN) Worn away.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ET CONFRACTÆ SUNT MAMMÆ PUBER- TATIS TUÆ) Attritæ.

## 23:22
Verse 22.

BEHOLD I WILL CALL TOGETHER ALL THY LOVERS) 'All' is not in the Hebrew.

OF WHOM THY SOUL IS SATIATED) Whom thou hast loathed.

Satisfied, to wit, by thy lust.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ECCE EGO SALUTABO OMNES AMATORES TUOS) Omnes non est in Hebræo.

DE QVIBUS SATIATA EST ANIMA TUA) Quos fastidiisti.

Expleta sc. tua libidine.

## 23:23
Verse 23.

NOBLES, AND TYRANTS AND PRINCES) The LXX, Symmachus, Theodotion retain the Hebrew words as if they were proper names of nations, Φακὸδ, σοὺ, κοὺθ, and the Chaldean no differently. We have the first of these called פקוד also in Jeremiah 50:21, and we said they were the Bactrians. שוע is Σουὲ in the interpreters, as I said, Σίαχ in Armenia according to Ptolemy: תקוע is Choana of Media, according to the same Ptolemy.

ALL THE SONS OF THE ASSYRIANS) The peoples whom he names were either subjects of the Assyrians at that time, or federated.

Although the Greeks and the Chaldean retain the proper names, they think nevertheless that this is done because they did not know how to render them, not because they took them for names of nations, as Grotius does with Tremellius, just as the names of military offices are for the most part foreign. Aquila, however, rendered them. That those who are confederated with them are called sons of the Assyrians will hardly be taught by similar examples; but those peoples whom Grotius said belonged to the Assyrians, not even he dared to say.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

NOBILES, TTRANNOSQVE AC PRINCIPES) LXX. Symmachus, Theodotio, Hebræas voces velut proprias gentium retinent, Φακὸδ, σοὺ, κοὺθ, nec aliter Chaldæus. Horum primos פקוד dictos habemus & apud Jeremiam 50, 21. diximusque esse Bactrianos. שוע Σουὲ LXX, ut dixi, interpretibus, Σίαχ in Armenia apud Pto- lemæum : תקוע Choana Mediæ, apud eundem Ptole- mæum.

OMNES FILIOS ASSTRIORUM) Populi quos nominat, aut subditi tunc erant Assyriorum, aut fæde- rati.

Etsi nomina propria retineant Græci & Chald. putant tamen id fieri, quod reddere ea nesci- verint, non quod habuerint pro gentium nomi- nibus, uti cum Tremellio Grotius, quomodo & nomina officiorum militarium plerumque pe- regrina sunt. Aquila tamen ea reddidit. Filios Assyriorum dici, qui confederati illis sunt, vix ex- emplis similibus docebitur; populos autem illos, quos dixit Grotius ad Assyrios pertinuisse, nec ipse ausus est dicere.

## 23:24
Verse 24. AND THEY SHALL COME UPON THEE EQUIPPED WITH CHARIOT AND WHEEL) LXX: μεθ' ὅπλων κὶ ἁρμάτων κὶ τρο- χῶν. And the Chaldean no differently; clearly all these took the ה in הצן for an article, or certainly a mark of a derivative, and in וגלגל which is often translated ὅπλον. From which origin is also צנה, which will now follow. In order that these two may be distinguished, some understand by הצן iron-clad chariots, that is, scythed ones.

The Hebrews say the name זין is foreign, and a term of military art, such as we noted in verse 23.

AND I WILL SET JUDGMENT BEFORE THEM) That is, I will give them the power of deciding concerning thee.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET VENIENT SVPER TE INSTRUCTI CURRU ET ROTA) LXX. μεθ' ὅπλων κὶ ἁρμάτων κὶ τρο- χῶν. Nec aliter Chaldæus; nimirum hi omnes in הצן sumfere pro articulo, aut certe nota derivativi, & in וגלגל quod sæpe vertitur ὅπλον. Ex qua origine est & צנה, quod jam sequetur. Ut hæc duo distinguantur, quidam per הצן intelligunt currus ferratos, id est, falcatos.

Ebræi nomen זין peregrinum esse, & voca- bulum artis militaris ajunt, qualia v. 23. notavi- mus.

ET DABO CORAM EIS JUDICIUM) Id est, dabo eis de te decernendi facultatem.

## 23:25
Ver. 25. AND I WILL SET MY JEALOUSY UPON THEE) I will strike my jealous spirit upon thee.

WHICH THEY SHALL EXERCISE UPON THEE IN FURY) Which (those Chaldeans) shall pursue thee wrathfully: namely as my ministers.

THEY SHALL CUT OFF THY NOSE AND THINE EARS) As jealous husbands are wont to do to unchaste wives, or to their adulterers. Martial:

Who persuaded thee to cut off the nostrils of the adulterer? By this similitude, however, he signifies Princes and judges.

Jerome on this passage notes that the noses of adulterous women were cut off in his age, so that they might no longer please adulterers, and he understands the King by the nose here, and the nobles by the ears: by which Oecolampadius and others prefer to understand priests.

AND WHAT REMAINS SHALL FALL BY THE SWORD) Namely those lower parts, by which the common people are signified here.

AND YOUR LATTER END SHALL BE DEVOURED BY FIRE) Whatever the captives shall leave behind in the city when they are carried away.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET PONAM ZELUM MEUM IN TE) Zelotypum animum meum in te impingam.

QVEM EXERCENT TECUM IN FURORE) Quem (illi Chaldæi) iracunde exfequantur: nempe ut mi- nistri mei.

NASUM TUUM ET AURES TUAS PRÆCI- DENT) Ut mariti zelotypi uxoribus impudicis, aut ea- rum mœchis facere solent. Martialis:

Quis tibi persuasit nares abscindere mœcho? Significat autem hac similitudine Principes & judices.

Hieronymus in h. 1. notat nares fœminis ad- ulteris præcisas sua ætate fuisse, ne deinceps mœchis placerent, & per nasum hic Regem, per aures proceres intelligit: per quas Oecolampad. aliique sacerdotes malunt intelligere.

ET QVÆ REMANSERINT GLADIO CONCI- DENT) Nempe partes illas inferiores, per quas hic plebs significatur.

ET NOVISSIMUM TUUM DEVORABITUR IGNI) Quidquid captivi cum avehentur in urbe relin- quent.

## 23:26
Vers. 26.

AND THEY SHALL STRIP YOU OF YOUR GARMENTS) As is accustomed to be done to captives.

AND THEY SHALL TAKE YOUR VESSELS OF GLORY) A Hebrew circumlocution, which signifies ornaments.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ET DENUDABUNT TE VESTIMENTIS TUIS) Ut captis fieri solet.

ET TOLLENT VASA GLORIÆ) Circumlocu- tio Hebræa, quæ significat ornamenta.

## 23:27
Vers. 27.

AND I WILL MAKE YOUR WICKEDNESS TO CEASE FROM YOU) I will ensure that it never pleases you to imitate the Chaldeans.

AND YOUR WHOREDOM FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT) That is to say, brought down from there.

NEITHER SHALL YOU LIFT UP YOUR EYES UNTO THEM) You will be afraid to look upon the Chaldeans.

AND YOU SHALL REMEMBER EGYPT NO MORE) Just as Egypt was not mindful of you in your perils.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ET REQVIESCERE FACIAM SCELUS TUUM DE TE) Faciam ne tibi unquam libeat Chaldæos imitari.

ET FORNICATIONEM TUAM DE TERRA ÆGYPTI) Deductam scilicet.

NEC LEVABIS OCULOS TUOS AD EOS) Me- tues aspicere Chaldæos.

ET ÆGYPTI NON RECORDABERIS AMPLIUS) Sicut Ægyptus tui memor non fuit in tuis periculis.

## 23:28
Vers. 28.

INTO THE HANDS OF THOSE WITH WHOM YOUR SOUL WAS SATIATED) Whom you loathed: as above v. 22.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

IN MANUS DE QVIBUS SATIATA EST ANIMA TUA) Quos fastidisti: ut supra v. 22.

## 23:29
Vers. 29.

AND THE SHAME OF THY FORNICATIONS SHALL BE REVEALED) As is wont to happen to captive women. Allegorical sense: All thy filthinesses shall appear.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ET REVELABITUR IGNOMINA FORNICA- TIONUM TUARUM) Ut solet fieri fœminis captivis. Sensus allegoricus: Omnes fœditates tuæ apparebunt.

## 23:30
Vers. 30.

THEY HAVE DONE THESE THINGS UNTO THEE) They shall do, that is, I will permit them to do so because of thy crimes.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

FECERUNT HÆC TIBI) Facient, id est, ego permittam ut faciant ob tua crimina.

## 23:32
Vers. 32.

THOU SHALT BE FOR DERISION AND SCORN, WHICH IS MOST CAPACIOUS) There is a transposition: Most capacious (cup from the preceding) so that thou mayest be for derision and mockery: As they are wont to be who have drained great cups.

Osiander renders for 'most capacious': it shall be much to bear: that is, the contumely which thou art forced to bear shall seem intolerable to thee. R. David Kimchi, thou shalt be multiplied, that is, inebriated with much wine of punishments. Yet transposition is not infrequent among the Hebrews. Concerning the outcome of the mockery see 2 Kings 21:13, Lamentations 2:15.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ERIS IN DERISUM ET SUBSANNATIONEM, QVÆ EST CAPACISSIMA) Est transpositio: Capacis- simum (calicem ex superioribus) ut sis irrisui ac ludibrio: Sicut solent esse qui magnos calices exhausere.

Osiander pro capacissimum reddit: multa erit ad ferendum: id est, intolerabilis tibi videbitur contumelia, quam ferre cogeris. R. David Kim- chi, eris multiplicata, id est, inebriata multo vi- no suppliciorum. Non infrequens tamen est E- bræis trajectio. De subsannationis eventu vid. 2. Reg. 21, 13. Thr. 2, 15.

## 23:34
Vers. 34.

AND THOU SHALT DRINK IT EVEN TO THE DREGS) In Hebrew: Thou shalt suck out; there shall be nothing of punishments that thou shalt not taste.

Concerning the draining even to the bottom, that is, the toleration of all the punishments of GOD, Isaiah 51:17, Psalm 75:9.

AND THOU SHALT DEVOUR THE FRAGMENTS THEREOF) As drunkards often do.

Thou shalt swallow the remnants or clots. גרם whence clots, as noted by Forster and Avenarius.

AND YOU SHALL TEAR YOUR BREASTS) Out of madness.

That is out of sorrow and desperation. For such a gesture was a sign of this. Mention is made of the breasts, because fornication is committed with this member.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

ET EPOTABIS VSQVE AD FÆCES) In He- bræo: Exsuges; nihil erit pœnarum quod non gustes.

De exhaustione usque ad fundum, id est, to- leratione omnium suppliciorum DEI Ef. 51, 17. Ps. 75, 9.

ET FRAGMENTA EJVS DEVORABIS) Ut sæ- pe faciunt ebrii.

Reliquias vel grumos degluties. גרם unde grumi notante Forstero & Avenario.

ET VBERA TVA LACERABIS) Præ rabie.

Id præ mœrore, & desperatione. Hujus enim indicium erat talis gestus. Uberum fit men- tio, quia hoc membro fit fornicatio.

## 23:35
Vers. 35.

YOU HAVE CAST ME BEHIND YOUR BODY) The same locution in 1 Kings 14:9, Ezekiel 23:35 [9:26], and elsewhere.

It is a solemn phrase, to cast someone behind oneself. But here 'body' or 'substance' is added to denote the spiritual union which was between GOD and the Jewish Church.

BEAR YOUR WICKEDNESS) The punishments of wickedness.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

PROJECTISTI ME POST CORPUS TUUM) Lo- cutio eadem 1. Regum 14, 9. Ezech. 9, 26. & alibi.

Solemnis est phrasis, aliquem post se proji- cere. Additur autem hic corpus vel substantia ad denotandam spiritualem copulam, quæ erat inter DEUM & Ecclesiam Judaicam.

PORTA SCELVS TVVM) Sceleris pœnas.

## 23:36
Vers. 36.

WILL YOU JUDGE OOLAH AND OOLIBAH) Would you plead the case of Oolah and Oolibah? as above 20:4, 22:2.

AND DECLARE TO THEM THEIR WICKEDNESSES) Indeed, show them their wickedness; as in the cited place 22:2.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

NVMQVID JVDICAS OOLLAM ET OOLI- BAM) An tu causam ageres Oollæ & Oolibæ? ut supra 20, 4. 22, 2.

ET ANNUNCIAS EIS SCELERA EORVM) Quin ostende eis sua scelera; ut dicto loco 22, 2.

## 23:37
Vers. 37.

THEIR SONS WHOM THEY BORE TO ME) Who ought to have been mine.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

FILIOS SVOS QVOS GENVERVNT MIHI) Qui mei esse debuerant.

## 23:38
Vers. 38.

THEY HAVE POLLUTED MY SANCTUARY IN THAT DAY) On the same day. Coming from those sacrilegious rites, they approach My Temple. The things that follow indicate this meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

POLLVERVNT SANCTVARIVM MEVM IN DIE ILLO) Eodem die. Ab illis sacrilegis sacris venientes Templum meum accedunt. Hunc sensum indicant quæ sequuntur.

## 23:39
Vers. 39.

THEY HAVE ALSO DONE THIS IN THE MIDST OF MY HOUSE.

IN Heb. And behold they have done these things &c. in the Midst of the house, that is, publicly with everyone watching, chap. 18, 18. c. 21. v. last. or even in the temple itself, just as the idolatry of Manasseh was practiced in the temple. 2 Kings 21, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

ETIAM HOC FECERUNT IN ME- DIO DOMUS MEÆ.

IN Ebr. Et ecce hæc fecerunt &c. in Medio domus, id est, publice omnibus spectantibus cap. 18, 18. c. 21. v. ult. vel etiam in ipso templo, uti Ma- nassis idololatria in templo exercita est. 2. Reg. 21, 4.

## 23:40
Vers. 40.

THEY SENT TO MEN COMING FROM AFAR) He repeats the same words often with few changes, so that they may stick more in the mind.

FOR WHOM YOU HAVE WASHED YOURSELF) For whose sake you have used baths.

AND YOU HAVE PAINTED YOUR EYES WITH ANTIMONY) He translates well; for כחל is to the Chaldeans what פוך is to the Hebrews, antimony. Concerning antimony, see what was said at 2 Kings 9, 30. Jeremiah 9, 30.

YOU ARE ADORNED WITH WOMANLY FINERY) With adornment. For if we wish to speak purely, mundus is that by which a woman is clean (munda): adornment is that by which she is adorned. Thus Varro book 4 de Lingua Latina, and Ulpian in L. argumento. §. ornamento. D. De auro, argento & mundo.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

MISERUNT AD VIROS VENIENTES DE LON- GE) Repetit saepe eadem verba paucis mutatis, quo ma- gis animo haereant,

QVIBUS TE LAVISTI) In quorum gratiam bal- neis usa es.

ET CIRCUMLINISTI STIBIO OCULOS TUOS) Bene vertit; nam כחל Chaldaeis est quod פוך Hebraeis stibium. De stibio vide quae dicta 2. Regum 9, 30. Je- rem. 9, 30.

ORNATA ES MUNDO MULIEBRI) Ornatu. Nam pure si loqui velimus, mundus est, per quem munda est foemina: ornatus per quem ornata. Sic Varro lib. 4. de Lingua Latina, & Ulpianus in L. argumento. §. ornamen- to. D. De auro, argento & mundo.

## 23:41
Vers. 41.

YOU SAT ON A MOST BEAUTIFUL COUCH, AND A TABLE WAS SET BEFORE YOU) For the custom of dining on couches had come from the Assyrians or Chaldeans to the Jews, of which custom you have testimony in the Chaldean paraphrase, Amos 2, 8.

Chap. 3, 12. c. 6, 4. 2 Kings 11, 2. Esth. 1, 6. chap. 7, 8. See Plin. book 15, chap. 16. Cael. Rhodigin. book 27, antiq. lect. chap. 27.

MY INCENSE, AND MY OINTMENT YOU HAVE PLACED UPON HIM) That is, you have given to idols what was owed to me. See above 16, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 41.

SEDISTI IN LECTO PULCHERRIMO, ET MEN- SA ORNATA EST ANTE TE) Mos enim in lectis epulandi ab Assyriis aut Chaldaeis ad Judaeos devenerat, cujus moris testimonium habes in Chaldaica paraphrasi, Amos 2, 8.

Cap. 3, 12. c. 6, 4. 2. Reg. 11, 2. Esth. 1, 6. cap. 7, 8. Vid. Plin. l. 15. c. 16. Cael. Rhodigin. l. 27. an- tiq. lect. c. 27.

THTMIAMA MEUM, ET UNGUENTUM MEUM POSUISTI SUPER EUM) Id est, idolis dedisti, mihi debita. Vide supra 16, 18.

## 23:42
Ver. 42.

THE VOICE OF A MULTITUDE EXULTING WAS IN IT) Everything was resounding with hymns to the gods.

AND UPON THE MEN WHO WERE BROUGHT FROM THE MULTITUDE OF MEN, AND CAME FROM THE DESERT, THEY PLACED BRACELETS ON THEIR HANDS, AND BEAUTIFUL CROWNS ON THEIR HEADS) In the Hebrew: Sabeans were brought from the desert. Not content with princes and handsome men, these women also bought for themselves, with bracelets and crowns given, foul men from the common people of Arabia for intercourse.

Concerning crowns placed upon heads as a sign of joy 1 Sam. 23, 26. Ps. 5, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 42.

VOX MULTITUDINIS EXULTANTIS ERAT IN EA) Omnia hymnis deorum perstrepebant.

ET IN VIRIS QVI DE MULTITUDINE HO- MINUM ADDUCEBANTUR, ET VENIEBANT DE- DESERTO, POSUERUNT ARMILLAS IN MANI- BUS EORUM, ET CORONAS SPECIOSAS IN CAPI- TIBUS EORUM) In Hebraeo: Adducebantur Sabaei de deserto. Non contentae viris principibus, & speciosis, istae foeminae etiam de plebe Arabiae foedos homines, armillis coronisque datis, ad concubitum emercatae sunt.

De coronis impositis capitibus in signum lae- titiae 1. Sam. 23, 26. Ps. 5, 13.

## 23:43
Ver. 43.

AND I SAID TO HER) Although I said.

WHO IS WORN OUT IN ADULTERIES) Who has become an old woman by whoring: he is speaking of Judea.

NOW SHE WILL COMMIT WHOREDOM IN HER WHOREDOM EVEN THIS ONE) Now at last her lusts will cease. But she herself, she was persisting, of course: Martial:

When you, Vetustilla, consult your recent [mirror] / And there are three hairs and four teeth, / And afterwards: / You dare to want to marry after two hundred deaths, / And, mad woman, you seek a husband for your ashes / To itch. Why, if you wish to rage, [do you not seek] a rock?

There are also other epigrams in the same poet against lustful old women. See the character of such a woman in the Plutus of Aristophanes.

That Hebrew pleonasm 'to whore whoredoms' brings in another meaning, namely the continuation of the crime, not the end. Hos. 1, 2. Ez. 16, 28. Thus Jerome, Theodoret, B. Luther, Osiander, and others, whom those things that follow in v. 44 favor.

Latin:

Vers. 43.

ET DIXI EI) Quamvis dicerem.

QVAE ATTRITA EST IN ADULTERIS) Quae moechando vetula facta est: de Judaea loquitur.

NUNC FORNICABITUR IN FORNICATIO- NE SUA ETIAM HAEC) Iam tandem definent libidines ejus. At ipsa, perseverabat scilicet: Martialis:

Cum tibit recenti consules Vetustilla Et tres capilli quatuorque sint dentes, Et postea: Audes ducentas nupturire post mortes, Virumque demens cineribus tuis quaeris Prurire. Quid furire si velis saxum?

Sunt apud eundem Poëtam & alia epigrammata in anus li- bidinosas Characterem talis foeminae vide in Pluto Aristo- phanis.

Alium sensum pleonasmus ille Ebraeor. forni- cari fornicationes infert, nimirum continuationem sceleris, non finem. Hos. 1, 2. Ez. 16, 28. Ita Hier. Theodoret. B. Luther. Osiand. alii, quibus favent quae sequuntur v. 44.

## 23:44
Ver. 44. AND THEY WENT IN UNTO HER) Nevertheless they went in unto her. To the old woman, that is to say.

Latin:

Vers. 44. ET INGRESSI SUNT AD EAM) Attamen ingressi sunt ad eam. Jam anum scilicet.

## 23:45
Ver. 45. THE RIGHTEOUS MEN, THEY SHALL JUDGE THEM AFTER THE MANNER OF ADULTERESSES) In the Hebrew: But righteous men shall punish them with the punishment of adulteresses. He calls the Chaldeans righteous, as ministers of divine vengeance.

AND AFTER THE MANNER OF THEM THAT SHED BLOOD) The punishment of murderers. See above 16, 38.

Latin:

Vers. 45. VIRI ERGO JUSTI SUNT, HI JUDICA- BUNT EAS JUDICIO ADULTERARUM) In Hebraeo: At viri justi punient eas poena adulterarum. Justos vocat Chaldaeos, ut divinae ultionis ministros.

ET JUDICIO EFFUNDENTIUM SANGUINEM) Poena homicidarum. Vide supra 16, 38.

## 23:46
Ver. 46. BRING UP A COMPANY AGAINST THEM) Call together an assembly of them. קהל is usually understood as a council of judges, who pronounce upon the life of the accused. Here, however, it is to be understood by ἀλληγορίαν as the army of the Chaldeans.

AND DELIVER THEM TO BE REMOVED) Deliver them to a crowd.

AND SPOIL) And let them be carried away, to the place of punishment, that is to say. For all this translation is taken from judicial proceedings.

Latin:

Vers. 46. ADDUC AD EAS MULTITUDINEM) Convoca de illis coetum. קהל solet intelligi consessus judi- cum, qui de reorum capite pronunciant. Hic vero per ἀλ- ληγορίαν intelligendus exercitus Chaldaeorum.

ET TRADE EAS IN TUMULTUM) Trade eas turbae.

ET IN RAPINAM) Et abripiantur, ad poenae locum scilicet. Omnis enim haec translatio à judiciis sumpta.

## 23:47
Ver. 47. AND THEY SHALL STONE THEM WITH STONES) See the aforementioned place.

Latin:

Vers. 47. ET LAPIDENTUR LAPIDIBUS POPU- LORUM) Vide dictum locum.

## 23:48
Ver. 48. AND I WILL CAUSE LEWDNESS TO CEASE OUT OF THE LAND) Filthy things.

AND ALL WOMEN SHALL LEARN) That is, the nations, which are designated under the name of women.

In Hebrew & they shall be chastised; for the end of the punishments of GOD is the amendment of others.

ACCORDING TO THEIR WICKEDNESS) Foul things: as above.

Latin:

Vers. 48. ET AUFERAM SCELUS DE TERRA) Res foedas.

ET DISCENT OMNES MVLIERES) Id est, gentes, quæ sub mulierum nomine designantur.

In Ebr. & castigabuntur; finis enim supplicorum DEI est emendatio aliorum.

SECVNDVM SCELVS EARVM) Res fœdas: ut supra.

## 23:49
Verse 49.

AND YOU SHALL BEAR THE SINS OF YOUR IDOLS) A double καταγυλα, for the punishments of idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 49.

ET PECCATA IDOLORVM PORTABITIS) Duplex καταγυλα, pro pœnas idololatriæ.

## 24:1 Argument
THE FIFTH REVELATION. CHAPTER XXIV.

Under the figure of a pot full of the choicest pieces of meat and bones, and placed upon the fire, and under the figure of the death of the Prophet's wife, for whom he was commanded to make no mourning, it is signified that the house of Israel is to be delivered to destruction, and its sons to be slaughtered with no mourning following because of the stupor of the mind.

Latin:

QVINTA REVELATIO. CAPUT XXIV.

Sub figura ollæ electioribus carnium partibus, ac ossibus plenæ, ignique admotæ, & sub figura mortis uxoris Prophetæ, pro qua jussus est nullum facere luctum, significatur domum Israel in exitium tradendam, filiosque ejus trucidandos nullo sequente luctu præ animi stupore.

## 24:2
Verse 2.

IN WHICH THE KING OF BABYLON WAS CONFIRMED AGAINST JERUSALEM) He surrounded Jerusalem: in this sense סמך is taken in Psalm 88:8. The LXX here use ἀπεστηρίσατο, that is, he fixed his camp: and the history which is in 2 Kings 25, Jeremiah 52:4 demands this sense. It was easy for God to show things that were being carried out so far away at the very time to the Prophet, since even demons, with God permitting, have done this, just as the whole series of the Pharsalian battle was shown to Cornelius the Priest while he was acting in Venice, as witnessed by Lucan and Gellius, and indeed the slaughter of Domitian to Apollonius of Tyana.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

IN QVA CONFIRMATVS EST REX BABYLONIS ADVERSVS JERUSALEM) Circumdædit Ierusalem: hoc sensu סמך sumitur Psal. 88, 8. LXX. hic ἀπεστηρίσατο, id est, castra fixit: eumque sensum postulat historia quæ est 2. Reg. 25. Jerem. 52, 4. Facile Deo fuit res quæ tam longe gerebantur, sub ipsum tempus Prophetæ ostendere, cum id etiam dæmones Deo sinente fecerint, sicut Cornelio Sacerdoti in Venetis agenti ostensa fuit tota series Pharsalici prælii, teste Lucano & Gellio, Apollonio vero Tyanæo cædes Domitiani.

## 24:3
Verse 3.

AND YOU SHALL SPEAK BY A PROVERB) That is, by an allegory, signify not only by words but also by things. The cauldron is Jerusalem: the meat and limbs put into it are its citizens: the fire and boiling water are the evils which they will suffer.

By water and fire, the vehemence of the chastisement and the multitude of the enemies are noted, Psalm 66:12, Isaiah 8:7, Apocalypse 17:11, Lamentations 1:3. By the shoulder, the King, of whom it was the portion, 1 Samuel 9:23; by the thigh, the most delicate part, by which strength is also usually noted, the magnates and warriors; by the choice bones, the leaders of the people are noted.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET DICES PER PROVERBIVM) Id est, per allegoriam, non verbis tantum sed & rebus significa. Lebes Hierosolyma: carnes & membra ei indita cives ejus: ignis & aqua fervens, mala quæ patientur.

Per aquam, & ignem vehementia castigationis, & multitudo hostium notata Psal. 66, 12. Esaie 8, 7. Apoc. 17, 11. Thren. 1, 3. Per armum Rex, cujus ille portio erat 1. Sam. 9, 23. per femur partem delicatissimam, qua notari etiam robur solet, magnates, & bellatores, per electa ossa primores populi notantur.

## 24:4
Vers. 4.

EVERY GOOD PART, THE THIGH AND THE SHOULDER) The leading citizens.

CHOICE PIECES AND FULL OF BONES) Fill it with the choicest bones. These are the most robust of the common people.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

OMNEM PARTEM BONAM, FEMVR ET ARMVM) Civium primores.

ELECTA ET OSSIBVS PLENA) Imple ossibus lectissimis. Hi sunt de plebe robustissimi.

## 24:5
Vers. 5.

TAKE THE CHOICEST OF THE FLOCK) Taken from the fattest of the flock, namely those bones.

ALSO PILE UP THE HEAPS OF BONES UNDER IT) Burn the bones under it: that is, place fire under the cauldron, which may boil the bones.

ITS BOILING HAS BOILED OVER) Its boiling has bubbled up, namely that of the cauldron.

AND THE BONES OF IT ARE BOILED IN THE MIDST OF IT) So that the bones which are inside the cauldron may be boiled.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PINGUISSIMVM PECVS ASSVME) Sumpta de pinguissimo pecore, nempe ossa illa.

COMPONE QVOQVE STRVES OSSIVM SVB EA) Incende ossa sub eo: id est, lebeti ignem subjice, qui ossa decoquat.

EFFERBVIT COCTIO EJVS) Ebulliit bullitio ejus, nempe lebetis.

ET DISCOCTA SVNT OSSA ILLIVS IN MEDIO EJVS) Vt coquantur ossa quæ sunt intra lebetem.

## 24:6
Vers. 6.

THEREFORE THUS SAYS THE LORD GOD) Concerning this matter (that is, concerning this symbol) the Lord God speaks thus. Thus He Himself explains those enigmas.

WHOSE RUST IS IN IT) חלא signifies vinegar to the Chaldeans, and خل to the Arabs: figuratively it signifies everything corrupt, such as the rust in the cauldron which the LXX here called ἰὸν. By it, however, malice is hinted at.

PIECE BY PIECE AND PIECE BY PIECE CAST IT OUT) Empty it out piece by piece.

Some wish to indicate a successive punishment under Jehoiakim, Jeconiah, and Zedekiah: but the former had already occurred: here it is only about the final prophecy. Moreover, even after that, the surviving Jews were consumed one by one. See Jer. 44, 12. et seqq.

NON CECIDIT SVPER EAM SORS) Let not the lot fall upon it. In the earlier deportations a lot was drawn, as to who should leave or remain: now all are to be cast out.

It is an ancient and strong custom regarding those to be captured or killed. See Orosius b. 7. ch. 25. Eutropius b. 9. Baronius to the year of Christ 197. num. 8. 9. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PROPTEREA HEC DICIT DOMINVS DEVS) De hac re (id est, de hoc symbolo) sic loquitur Dominus Deus. Sic ipse explicat ambages illas.

CVJVS RVBIGO IN EA EST) חלא Chaldæis, & خل Arabibus acetum significat: translate significat omne corruptum, quale est in lebete ærugo quam ἰὸν hic dixere LXX. per eam vero malitia innuitur.

PER PARTES ET PER PARTES SVAS EJICE EAM) Particulatim eam exinani.

Nonnulli successivam punitionem sub Jojakimo, Jechonia, & Zedekia indigitati volunt: sed priores jam contigerant: hic solum de postrema Prophetia sit. Cæterum etiam post illam superstites Judæi sigillatim consumti sunt. Vid. Jer. 64, 12. seqq.

NON CECIDIT SVPER EAM SORS) Ne cadat super eam sors. In prioribus deportationibus sors ducta, qui exirent aut manerent: nunc omnes ejiciendi.

Antiquus est fortis mos super captivos aut occidendos. Vid. Orosius l. 7. cap. 25. Eutropius l. 9. Baronius ad ann. Christ. 197. num. 8. 9. 10.

## 24:7
Vers. 7.

SVPER LIMPIDISSIMAM PETRAM EFFVDIT ILLVM) Upon a high rock, so that all might see.

NON EFFVDIT ILLVM SVPER TERRAM, VT POSSIT OPERIRI PVLVERE.) As those are accustomed to do who are ashamed of their deed.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

SVPER LIMPIDISSIMAM PETRAM EFFVDIT ILLVM) In sublimem petram, ut omnes aspicerent.

NON EFFVDIT ILLVM SVPER TERRAM, VT POSSIT OPERIRI PVLVERE.) Vtilli facere solent, quos pudet facti.

## 24:8
Vers. 8.

DEDI SANGVINEM EJVS SVPER PETRAM LIMPIDISSIMAM) Upon a high rock: I will return like for like. He had sinned openly, he shall be punished openly.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

DEDI SANGVINEM EJVS SVPER PETRAM LIMPIDISSIMAM) In sublimem petram: par pari referam. Palam peccaverat, palam punietur.

## 24:9
Vers. 9.

CVJVS EGO GRANDEM FACIAM PTRAM) He shows more openly what that fire under the cauldron signifies. Then, after the ἀπόδοσιν, he returns to the ἀναγωγίαν, which is now becoming more evident.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

CVJVS EGO GRANDEM FACIAM PTRAM) Ostendit apertius quid ille sub lebete ignis significet. Deinde post ἀπόδοσιν ad ἀναγωγίαν jam magis patescentem redit.

## 24:10
Vers. 10.

CONGERE OSSA) In the Hebrew עצים [wood]. Nor do the Chaldean and the Greeks say otherwise. But the Latin reads עצמים [bones].

WHICH I SHALL KINDLE WITH FIRE) Kindle the fire. He commands the type to be repeated.

THE FLESH SHALL BE CONSUMED) Consume the flesh. ὅπως τακῇ τὰ κρέα. LXX.

AND THE WHOLE COMPOSITION SHALL BE BOILED) The mixture: that is, let the broth be reduced, ἐλαττωθῇ ὁ ζωμός. The more fervent the fire is, the more the liquid is reduced to a concentrate. Virgil: - - Volcani decoquit humorem, Et foliis undam tepidi despumat aheni.

AND THE BONES SHALL BE BURNED) So that the bones also may melt: that is, even the most robust may be dissolved. See above 4.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

CONGERE OSSA) In Hebræo עצים ligna. Nec aliter Chaldæus & Græci. At Latinus legit עצמים.

QVÆ IGNE SUCCENDAM) Succende ignem. Jubet repeti typum.

CONSVMENTUR CARNES) Consume carnem. ὅπως τακῇ τὰ κρέα. LXX.

ET COQVEIVR VNIVERSA COMPOSITIO) Mixtum: id est, jusculum attenuetur, ἐλαττωθῇ ὁ ζωμός. Quo ferventior est ignis, hoc magis liquor in summam redigitur. Virgilius: - - Volcani decoquit humorem, Et foliis undam tepidi despumat aheni.

ET OSSA COMBVRENIVR) Vt & ossa lique- fiant: id est, dissolvantur etiam robustissimi. Vide supra 4.

## 24:11
Ver. 11.

SET IT ALSO EMPTY UPON THE COALS) That is, place the hottest coals under the cauldron itself, after the flesh and bones have been cast out.

THAT IT MAY GROW HOT AND ITS BRASS MAY MELT) That is, that with the citizens cast out, the city may burn.

AND ITS FILTH MAY BE MELTED IN THE MIDST OF IT, AND ITS RUST MAY BE CONSUMED) The sense is, that even thus they might be corrected.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

PONE QVOQVE EAM SVPER PRVNAS VA- CVAM) Id est, ipsi lebeti, post ejectas carnes & ossa, subde prunas ardentissimas.

VT INCALESCAT ET LIQVEFIAT ÆS EJVS) Id est, ut ejectis civibus, urbs ardeat.

ET CONFLETVR IN MEDIO EJVS INQVI- NAMENTVM EJVS, ET CONSVM ATVR RVBIGO EJVS) Sensus est, ut vel sic corrigantur.

## 24:12
Ver. 12.

IT HAS SWEATED WITH MUCH LABOR) It is labored in vain.

AND ITS GREAT RUST HAS NOT GONE OUT OF IT, NOR BY FIRE) In the Hebrew: Its great rust has not gone out of it, by fire (I say) its rust has not gone out. Such was the malice, that it was not purged even by the burning of the city.

These things are not, therefore, to be explained as Jerusalem macerating herself so that she may be free from sin, with Kimchi, Arias, Pagninus, the English, Italian, Spanish, and Mercerus, but as GOD purging her in vain, with Jerome, Theodoret, Tremellius, Sanctius, Maldonatus, Luther, Osiander, and others, as Grotius rightly [holds].

Latin:

Vers. 12.

MVLTO LABORE SVDATVM EST) Frustra laboratur.

ET NON EXIVIT DE EA NIMIA RVBIGO EJVS, NEQVE PER IGNEM) In Hebræo: Non exiit de ea multa ærugo ejus, per ignem (inquam) ærugo ejus non exiit. Tanta fuit malitia, ut ne incendio quidem urbis expurgata sit.

Non ergo de Jerusalem seipsam macerante, ut libera fiat a peccato cum Kimchio, Aria, Pagrino, Angl. Ital. Hisp. & Mercero explicanda hæc sunt, sed de DEO nequicquam eam expurgante, cum Hier. Theod. Tremell. Sanctio, Maldon, Luthero, Osiandro, aliis, ut recte Grotius.

## 24:13
Vers. 13.

UNTIL I SHALL CAUSE MY INDIGNATION TO REST UPON THEE) Until I shall have satisfied my wrath with the most grievous evils of exile.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

DONEC QVIESCERE FACIAM INDIGNATIO- NEM MEAM IN TE) Donec gravissimis exsilii malis iram satiavero.

## 24:14
Vers. 14.

ACCORDING TO THY WAYS AND ACCORDING TO THY DEVICES I WILL JUDGE THEE) The Greeks, whom this interpreter follows, read שפטוך. But our text and the Chaldean read שפטיך, they shall punish thee: namely, the Chaldeans by my command.

He collects a different reading, relying according to his custom upon a hypothesis that is by no means certain and indubitable, as if the Greeks had rendered the words one by one κατὰ πόδα, who, content to have expressed the sense, not rarely used different words by design. The sense, however, is the same, whether it be said that God judges by punishing, or the Chaldeans by divine command. At least the ministerial cause is expressed here, but the principal cause there.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

JVXTA VIAS ET JVXTA INVENTIONES TVAS TE JVDICABO) Græci quos hic interpres sequitur legerunt שפטוך. At noster textus & Chaldæus שפטיך, punient te: nempe Chaldæi meo jussu.

Diversam lectionem colligit, innixus pro more suo hypothefi minime certæ ac indubitatæ, quasi verba singula κ ποδα reddiderint Græci, qui sensum expressisse contenti, verbis non raro ex instituto diversis usi sunt. Sensus autem idem est, seu dicatur Deus judicare, puniendo, seu Chaldæi jussu divino. Saltem exprimitur hic causa ministerialis, ibi vero principalis.

## 24:16
Vers. 16.

I TAKE AWAY FROM THEE THE DESIRE OF THINE EYES WITH A STROKE) By a sudden plague I will take away thy wife from thee, and I do not want thee to mourn her, so that thou mayest signify that in the greatest evils they will not have leisure to mourn.

Compare Num. 16, 13. Jerem. 22, 18. The fatal death of the Jewish Church is prefigured, which had been as it were the spouse of GOD c. 16, 8.

THOU SHALT NOT LAMENT) Thou shalt not strike thyself. Seneca in Troades: The furious hand is free for the beating of the breast.

NEITHER SHALT THOU WEEP) To weep is to cry out. See Festus. An old poet: Alas, that I should utter a virginal lament with my mouth.

NEITHER SHALL THY TEARS FLOW) Ennius: Do not adorn me with tears, nor make a weeping at my funeral.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

EGO TOLLO A TE DESIDERABILE OCV- LORVM TVORVM IN PLAGA) Subita peste auferam tibi uxorem tuam, & eam nolo lugeas, ut significes in maximis malis non vacaturum ipsis ut lugeant.

Confer Num. 16, 13. Jerem. 22, 18. Præfigura- tur mors funesta Ecclesiæ Judaicæ, quæ fuerat quasi conjux DEI c. 16, 8.

NON PLANGES) Non temet percuties. Seneca in Troatibus: Vacat ad crebri berbera planctus Furibunda manus.

NEQVE PLORABIS) Plorare est clamare. Vide Festum. Vetus poëta: Heu virginalem me ore ploratum edere.

NEQVE FLVENT LACHRYMÆ TVÆ) En- nius: Ne me condecores lachrymis, neque funere fletum Faxis.

## 24:17
Vers. 17.

GROAN IN SILENCE) דָּנַק is translated σενάζειν, אֲנָקָה is a groaning. Groan in such a way that no stranger may hear.

THOU SHALT NOT MAKE MOURNING FOR THE DEAD) He speaks generally, which he then explains through species.

LET THY CROWN BE BOUND ABOUT THEE) The Greeks here interpret פְּאֵר as curls, as in Isaiah 61, 10. A mitre, as also here the Chaldean עִטְרוֹנָא. Those mourning were accustomed to go with a bare head. Levit. 13, 14.

AND THY SHOES SHALL BE ON THY FEET) For those mourning used to walk with bare feet. 2 Samuel 15, 30.

NEITHER SHALT THOU COVER THY LIPS) Those mourning (among whom were also lepers) used to cover their mustache for themselves Levit. 13, 45. Micah 3, 7. שָׂפָם or שָׂפָה is properly the mustache, as appears in 2 Samuel 19, 24; for this the Chaldean here said upper lip, in the same sense.

NEITHER SHALT THOU EAT THE FOOD OF MOURNERS) περίδειπνα are funeral feasts which friends used to send to those mourning Jer. 16, 7. Jerome there and here.

Although these were signs of mourning, which was forbidden to the Prophet, yet it must be said that the same thing signified something else, if the interpretation of Grotius on v. 22 & 23 is to be admitted.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

INGEMISCE TACENS) דָּנַק vertitur σενάζειν, אֲנָקָה στεναγμός. Ita geme ut alienus nemo audiat.

MORTVORVM LVCTVM NON FACIES) Ge- neraliter dicit, quod deinde per species explicat.

CORONA TVA CIRCVMLIGATA SIT TIBI) Græci hic פְּאֵר cincinnos interpretantur, ut Esaïæ 61, 10. μίτραν, ut & hic Chaldæus עִטְרוֹנָא. Lugentes nudo capite ire solebant. Levit. 13, 14.

ET CALCEAMENTA TVA ERVNT IN PEDI- BVS TVIS) Nam mœrentes nudis incedebant pedibus. 2. Samuel. 15, 30.

NEC AMICTU ORA VELABIS) Lugentes (in quibus & leprosi) obvelabant sibi mystacem Levit. 13, 45. Mich. 3, 7. שָׂפָם vel שָׂפָה proprie est mystax, ut apparet 2. Samuel. 19, 24. pro eo labium superius hic dixit Chal- dæus, sensu eodem.

NEC CIBOS LVGENTIVM COMEDES) περί- δειπνα sunt parentalia quæ amici mittebant lugentibus Jer. 16, 7. Hieronymus ibi & hic.

Hæc quamvis luctus signa erant, qui prohi- bitus est Prophetæ, tamen aliud quid eadem si- gnasse dicendum erit, si admittenda Grotiana ad v. 22. & 23. evolutio.

## 24:18
Vers. 18.

I SPOKE TO MY PEOPLE, AND MY WIFE DIED IN THE EVENING) When I had spoken to the people in the morning, (the deportees) that very evening my wife died. That is, very suddenly.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

LOCVTVS SVM EGO AD POPVLVM MEVM, ET MORTVA EST VXOR MEA VESPERE) Cum mane allocutus essem populum, (deportatos) ipso vespere uxor mea mortua est. Id est, subito admodum.

## 24:21
Vers. 21.

SPEAK TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) Signify by letters to those who are in Jerusalem.

BEHOLD I WILL PROFANE MY SANCTUARY) I am about to expose it to the lust of profane nations.

THE PRIDE OF YOUR POWER) That is, of your kingdoms.

AND THE DESIRE OF YOUR EYES) Wives, as above 16.

AND THAT UPON WHICH YOUR SOUL FEARETH) That which pleases you. جَمَلَ means to please to the Arabs, and thence Camaïeul, that is, a precious thing.

YOUR SONS AND YOUR DAUGHTERS, WHOM YOU HAVE LEFT) He understands those who had remained with Gedaliah.

See Jer. 41. et seq.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

LOQVERE DOMVI ISRAEL) Significa per lite- ras illis qui sunt Hierosolymis.

ECCE EGO POLLVAM SANCTVARIVM MEVM) Expositurus sum libidini profanarum gentium.

SVPERBIAM IMPERII VESTRI) Id est, re- gnorum.

ET DESIDERABILE OCVLORVM VESTRO- RVM) Uxores, ut supra 16.

ET SVPER QVO PAVET ANIMA VESTRA) Id quod placet vobis. جَمَلَ placere Arabibus, & inde Camaïeul, id est, res pretiosa.

FILII VESTRI ET FILIÆ VESTRÆ, QVAS RELIQVISTIS) Intelligit illos qui cum Godolia man- serant.

Videat Jer. 41. seq.

## 24:22
Vers. 22.

YOU SHALL NOT COVER YOUR FACES WITH A CLOAK) So that you may better see where you must go.

YOU SHALL NOT EAT THE FOOD OF MOURNERS) There will be no one who has the means to send you περίδειπνα [funeral feasts], in that migration of yours.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ORA AMICTU NON VELABITIS) Ut melius introspiciatis quo eundum sit.

CIBOS LVGENTIVM NON COMEDETIS) Ne- mo erit cui copia sit mittendi vobis περίδειπνα, in ista migratione.

## 24:23
Verse 23.

YOU SHALL HAVE CROWNS ON YOUR HEADS) Turbans, as is the custom for those who travel against the sun or rain.

AND SHOES ON YOUR FEET) Against the striking of stones.

These glosses are ingenious: but since in the portent of Ezekiel these occur only as signs of restrained mourning: and here in the application and fulfillment they are explained thus, you shall not lament nor weep, Osiander and others more correctly take them as referring to not mourning over the burned temple and the slain children, lest the cruel enemy be further provoked.

YOU SHALL NOT LAMENT, NOR WEEP) Lest you provoke the victor.

BUT YOU SHALL PINE AWAY IN YOUR INIQUITIES) In your punishments. Taken from Leviticus 26:39.

AND EVERYONE SHALL GROAN TO HIS BROTHER) So that no stranger may hear. Lucan: --- Now there is power to weep while the fortune of the leaders hangs in the balance: when one has conquered, one must rejoice. Women accused because of tears. You have that in Tacitus, Annals 6, who also narrates that the sons of Mithridates were slaughtered because they had wept at the killings of their parents. The same in Agricola: When our sighs were being recorded, when that savage countenance was sufficient for noting the pallor of so many men.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

CORONAS HABEDITIS IN CAPITIBVS VE- STIS) Mitellas, ut solent qui iter faciunt contra solem aut pluviam.

ET CALCEAMENTA IN PEDIBVS) Contra la- pidum offensiones.

Ingeniosæ sunt hæ glossæ: sed quum in porten- to Ezechielis ista non nisi ut signa luctus inhibiti occurrant: & hic in applicatione & complemento sic explicentur, non plangetis neque flebitis, rectius Osiander & alii de non lugendo super exusto tem- plo, & interfectis liberis, ne hostis crudelis magis irritetur, ea accipiunt.

NON PLANGETIS, NEQVE FLEBITIS) Ne ir- ritetis victorem.

SED TABESCETIS IN INIQVITATIBVS VE- STRIS) In pœnis. Sumtum ex Levit. 26, 39.

ET VNVSQVISQVE GEMET AD FRATREM SVVM) Ita ut nemo alienus exaudiat. Lucanus: - - - Nunc flere potestas Dum pendet fortuna ducum: cum vicerit alter Gaudendum est. Fœminæ ob lachrymas accusatæ. Habes id apud Tacitum Annalium 6. qui & filios Mithradatis trucidatos narrat, quod cædibus parentum illachrymassent. Idem in Agricola: Cum suspiria nostra subscriberentur, cum denotandis tot hominum palloribus sufficeret sævus ille vultus.

## 24:24
Verse 24. AND EZEKIEL SHALL BE A PORTENT TO YOU) By his deeds he prefigures what is to happen to you, as in Isaiah 8:18 and above 12:6.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ERITQVE EZECHIEL VOBIS IN PORTENTVM) Suis factis præmonstrat quid vobis sit eventurum, ut Esaiæ 8, 18. & supra 12, 6.

## 24:25
Verse 25. IN THE DAY THAT I TAKE FROM THEM THEIR STRENGTH) The kingdom, as above 21. AND THE JOY OF THEIR GLORY) The joy of their glory: that is, the Temple. AND THE DESIRE OF THEIR EYES) Their wives. UPON WHICH THEIR SOULS REST) The delights of their eyes: that is, their most precious things; above 21.

Latin:

Vers. 25. IN DIE QVA TOLLAM AB EIS FORTITVDINEM EORVM) Regnum, ut supra 21. ET GAVDIVM DIGNITATIS) Gaudium gloriæ: id est, Templum. ET DESIDERIVM OCVLORVM EORVM) Uxores. SVPER QVO REQVIESCVNT ANIMÆ EORVM) Deliciæ oculorum eorum: id est, res pretiosissimæ; supra 21.

## 24:26
Verse 26. IN THAT DAY) That is, when the siege is finished, the city and Temple burned. WHEN A FUGITIVE SHALL COME TO YOU, TO ANNOUNCE TO YOU) See the fulfillment below 33:3.

Latin:

Vers. 26. IN DIE ILLA) Id est, peracto obsidio, exusta urbe ac Templo. CVM VENERIT FVGIENS AD TE, VT ANNVNCIET TIBI) Implementum vide infra 33, 3.

## 24:27
Ver. 27. THY MOUTH SHALL BE OPENED WITH HIM THAT ESCAPETH) His testimony, agreeing with your predictions, will give you authority to speak and will win faith for your new prophecies. AND THOU SHALT BE A SIGN UNTO THEM) Then they will say that you had foretold their fate by the very events themselves. See chapter 33, 3.

SECTION II. PREDICTIONS AGAINST FOREIGNERS.

Latin:

Vers. 27. APERIETVR OS TVVM CVM EO QVI FVGIT) Illius testimonium tuis prædictionibus congruens, auctoritatem tibi dabit loquendi, & fidem conciliabit novis prophetiis. ERISQVE EIS IN PORTENTVM) Tunc dicent te rebus ipsis præmonstrasse ipsorum sortem. Dicto capite 33, 3.

SECTIO II. PRÆDICTIONES ADVERSUS EXTEROS.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV.

The Lord threatens destruction to the regions of Ammon, Moab, Idumea, and Palestine, for the reason that they afflicted the children of Israel and exulted in their affliction.

Ver. 1. AND THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME UNTO ME) After the predictions concerning Jewish affairs, those follow which pertain to other nations, as in Jeremiah.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV.

Regionibus Ammon, Moab, Idumææ & Palæstinæ minatur Dominus exitium, eo quod filios Israel afflixerint, & de ipsorum afflictione exultaverint.

Vers. 1. ET FACTVS EST SERMO DOMINI AD ME) Post prædictiones de rebus Judaicis, sequuntur illæ quæ ad alias gentes pertinent, ut apud Jeremiam.

## 25:2
Ver. 2. SET THY FACE AGAINST THE CHILDREN OF AMMON) A manner of speaking such as above 6, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PONE FACIEM TVAM CONTRA FILIOS AMMON) Loquendi genus quale supra 6, 2.

## 25:3
Ver. 3. AGAINST MY SANCTUARY WHICH WAS PROFANED) Since it had been profaned. Take the following in this way also.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SVPER SANCTVARIVM MEVM QVOD POLLVTVM EST) Cum pollutum esset. Sic etiam sume sequentia.

## 25:4
Ver. 4. I WILL DELIVER THEE TO THE MEN OF THE EAST FOR A POSSESSION) Into the possession of the Chaldeans. We have said at Jer. 48, 1 and above 21, 28 that these things happened to the Ammonites and Arabs in the fifth year after Jerusalem was overturned.

AND THEY SHALL SET THEIR FOLDS IN THEE) In Hebrew: ades.

AND THEY SHALL PLACE IN THEE THEIR TENTS) In Hebrew: Dwellings. So also the Chaldean, which is the more to be noted because from the mention of tents some have wished the Arabs to be understood, which does not agree with Jeremiah.

Theodoret, Polychronius, and Maldonatus understand the Arabs. But the fixing of tents is expressly attributed to the Chaldeans in Jer. 6, 2, 3, 4.

THEY SHALL EAT THY FRUITS. This exegesis, as noted by B. Hulseus, easily declares the duties of shepherds, what kind of shepherds, and what kind of causes are to be understood, namely grazing and laying waste, not feeding.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TRADAM TE FILIIS ORIENTALIBVS IN HEREDITATEM) In possessionem Chaldæis. Evenisse hæc Ammonitis & Arabibus, quinto anno post eversa Hierosolyma, diximus ad Jer. 48, 1. & supra 21, 28.

ET COLLOCABVNT CAVLAS SVAS IN TE) In Hebræo: ades.

ET PONENT IN TE TENTORIA SVA) In Hebræo: Habitacula. Sic & Chaldæus, quod eo magis notandum, quod ex tentoriorum mentione quidam Orientales voluere intelligi Arabas, quod cum Jeremia non convenit.

Arabes intelligit Theodoretus, Polychronius, & Maldonat. Atfixio tentoriorum diserte Chaldæis Jer. 6, 2. 3. 4. tribuitur.

IPSI COMEDENT FRVGES TVAS. Hæc Exegesis notante B. Hulseo. officia pastorum facile declarat, quales pastores, quales causæ intelligantur, depascentes sc. & vastantes, non pascentes.

## 25:5
Verse 5.

AND I WILL GIVE RABBATH) The chief city of the Ammonites, which was later called Philadelphia. See Jerem. 49, 3. here above 21, 20. INTO A DWELLING PLACE FOR CAMELS) Doubtless the Chaldeans and Bactrians had many camels. See Pliny. Palaces are said to be turned into stables, not of domestic, but of hostile beasts of burden. AND THE CHILDREN OF AMMON INTO A FOLD FOR FLOCKS) Better, of the children of Ammon, supply the land, with colonies having been led there from the lands of the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

DABOQVE RABBATH) Urbem principem Ammonitarum, quæ Philadelphia dicta postea. Vide Jerem. 49, 3. hîc supra 21, 20. IN HABITACLVM CAMELORVM) Nimirum Chaldæi multos habebant Camelos & Bactriani. Vide Plinium. Palatia dicuntur vertenda in stadula non domesticorum, sed hostilium jumentorum. ET FILIOS AMMON IN CVBILE PECORVM) Melius, filiorum Ammon, supple terram, deductis scilicet eo coloniis è Chaldæorum terris.

## 25:6
Verse 6.

BECAUSE YOU CLAPPED YOUR HAND) A sign of one rejoicing. Above 21, 17. AND STAMPED WITH YOUR FOOT) The ground, that is, by dancing and leaping.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PRO EO QVOD PLAVSISTI MANV) Signum gaudentis. Supra 21, 17. ET PERCVSSISTI PEDE) Terram scilicet, saltando ac tripudiando.

## 25:8
Verse 8.

BECAUSE MOAB AND SEIR SAID) He joins the neighboring Idumeans with the Moabites. Concerning the evils of the Moabites see Jeremiah in the cited chapter. Concerning the evils of the Idumeans, the same 49, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

PRO EO QVOD DIXERVNT MOAB ET SEIR) Conjungit cum Moabitis vicinos Idumæos. De Moabitarum malis vide Jeremiam dicto capite. De malis Idumæorum eundem 49, 7.

## 25:8
BEHOLD AS ALL THE NATIONS THE HOUSE OF JUDA) It profits them nothing to have worshipped the true God. I WILL OPEN THE SHOULDER OF MOAB) The side. For כתף is often taken thus, as appears in Exodus 28, 7. Num. 39, 11. below 47, 1. 2. The side is said to be opened because it is exposed to blows. God was about to open the sides or borders of the region to the incursion of enemies: as with B. Luth. and R. Dav. Kimchi. B. Hülsem. Others, however, wrongly understand power by the shoulder, with R. Salom. OF THE CITIES, OF THE CITIES I SAY OF IT) ער indeed signifies a city: but here he repeated the word for this reason, with the pronoun 'of it' added, to indicate that they are proper names of cities which were called Har and Haroher Num. 21, 28. Isaiah 16, 1. Deut. 2, 35. So also Tremellius. But because the Prophet is still engaged in a general description of the cities, that they are bordering, that they are renowned, with the Chald. and Rabb. and other interpreters. it is better for all to take these words appellatively, so that the Epizeuxis may hint at the certainty of the event and the severity of God the avenger. AND FROM ITS BORDERS THE RENOWNED OF THE LAND) And from the borders to the most joyful lands. In the borders were fortified places; in the middle places were the most fertile lands. BETHIESIMOTH) Joshua 13, 20. Ziza in Ptolemy, זיזא in the verso. AND BEELMEON) See what was said in Isaiah 16, 2. and Jer. 48, 23. AND CHARIATHAIM) Jerem. 48, 1. 23.

Latin:

ECCE SICVT OMNES GENTES DOMVS JVDA) Nihil prodest illis verum Deum coluisse. APERIAM HVMERVM MOAB) Latus. Nam כתף sæpe sic sumitur, ut apparet Exodi 28, 7. Num. 39, 11. infra 47, 1. 2. Latus apertum dicitur, quod ictibus obnoxium est. Latera seu confinia regionis DEUS aperturus erat irruptioni hostium: uti cum B. Luth. & R. Dav. Kimchi. B. Hülsem. Perperam autem alii per humerum potentiam intelligunt, cum R. Salom. DE CIVITATIBVS, DE CIVITATIBVS INQVAM EJVS) ער civitatem quidem significat: sed hic ideo vocem repetiit, addito pronomine ejus, ut indicaret nomina propria esse urbium quæ dicebantur Har & Haroher Num. 21, 28. Esai. 16, 1. Deut. 2, 35. Ita & Tremellius. Sed quia Propheta adhuc versatur in generali descriptione urbium, quod sint finitimæ, quod sint inclytæ, cum Chald. & Rabb. aliisque Interpp. omnibus præstat has voces appellative accipere, ut Epizeuxis certitudinem eventus, & severitatem DEI vindicis innuat. ET DE FINIBVS EJVS INCLYTAS TERRÆ) Et à finibus ad terras lœtissimas. In finibus erant loca munita; in mediis locis terræ fertilissimæ. BETHIESIMOTH) Josue 13, 20. Ζίζα Ptolemæo, זיזא in ע verso. ET BEELMEON) Vide quæ dicta Esai. 16, 2. & Jer. 48, 23. ET CHARIATHAIM) Jerem. 48, 1. 23.

## 25:9
Verse 9.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

## 25:10
Verse 10.

TO THE CHILDREN OF THE EAST) To the Chaldeans. This depends on what he said, I will open the side. WITH THE CHILDREN OF AMMON, AND I WILL GIVE IT FOR A POSSESSION, THAT THE MEMORY OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON MAY NOT BE ANY MORE AMONG THE NATIONS) After the children of Ammon, that is, when I have given it (the land) as a possession to the Chaldeans, so that the memory of the children of Ammon may not survive among the nations. Thus the sense is excellent: for the former was laid waste by the Chaldeans, the Ammonites: the latter by the Moabites, as we noted at Jerem. 49.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

FILIIS ORIENTIS) Chaldæis. Pendet hoc ab eo quod dixit, Aperiam latus. CVM FILIIS AMMON, ET DABO EAM IN HEREDITATEM, VT NON SIT VLTRA MEMORIA FILIORVM AMMON IN GENTIBVS) Post filios Ammon, id est, ubi dedero eam (terram) in proprietatem Chaldæis, ita ut filiorum Ammon in gentibus memoria non supersit. Ita sensus sit optimus: nam prior à Caldæis vastata est Ammonitis: posterior Moabitis, ut notavimus ad Jerem. 49.

## 25:11
Ver. 11. AND IN MOAB I WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS

I will also take vengeance on the Moabites. FOR THAT IDUMAEA HATH TAKEN VENGEANCE, BY REVENGEING HERSELF OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDA) Because she executed an old hatred when the opportunity was given. Ps. 137, 7. See a similar passage in Obadiah 1, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET IN MOAB FACIAM JVDICIA)

Etiam de Moabitis sumam ultionem. PRO EO QVOD FECIT IDVMÆA VLTIONEM, UT SE VINDICARET DE FILIIS JVDA) Quia vetus odium data occasione exsecuta est. Psal. 137, 7. Simile vide Abdiæ 1, 10.

## 25:12
V. 12. I WILL MAKE IT DESERT FROM THE SOUTH

תימן indeed also signifies the South. But here it is the name of a region called Theman from the grandson of Esau, Gen. 36, 15. Jer. 49, 7. Obadiah 8. See what we have said regarding that passage of Genesis.

Latin:

V. 12. FACIAM EAM DESERTAM AB AUSTRO)

תימן quidem etiam Austrum significat. Sed hic nomen est regionis dictæ Theman à nepote Esavi Genes. 36, 15. Jer. 49, 7. Obadiæ 8. Vide quæ ad illum Geneseos locum diximus.

## 25:13
Vers. 13. AND THEY THAT ARE IN DEDAN) And Dedan

shall even fall by the sword. He names two boundaries, Theman to the South, and Dedan to the North: concerning which see what is said at Jer. 49, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET QVI SVNT IN DEDAN) Et Dedanem

usque gladio cadent. Duos terminos nominat, Themanem ad Austrum, & Dedanem ad Septentrionem: de qua vide quæ ad Jer. 49, 9.

## 25:14
Vers. 14. AND I WILL LAY MY VENGEANCE UPON IDUMAEA BY THE HAND OF MY PEOPLE ISRAEL)

First I will punish it through the Chaldeans: then also through the Jews in the times of Judas Maccabaeus. See what is said at Isaiah 63.

The passage in Is. 63 is irrelevant; see however 1 Macc. 5, 14, 15; 2 Macc. 10, 29; ch. 12, 32; and Josephus, Antiq. book 13, ch. 17, concerning the victory of Hyrcanus reported over the Idumaeans.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DABO ULTIONEM MEAM SVPER IDVMÆAM PER MANUM POPULI MEI ISRAEL)

Primum per Chaldæos eam puniam: deinde & per Judæos temporibus Judæ Maccabæi. Vide quæ ad Esai. 63.

Alienus est locus Es. 63. vid. autem 1. Maccab 5. 14. 15. 2. Macc. 10, 29. c. 12, 32. & Joseph. l. 13. Antiq. c. 17. de victoria Hircani ab Idumæis reportata.

## 25:15
Vers. 15. PALAESTINI) Who are the same elsewhere as the Philistines. For the Greeks transfer the Hebrew פ into π, as Jerome noted here.

AND EXECUTING VENGESANCE BY REVENGE) See 1 Sam. 13 and 42.

Latin:

Vers. 15. PALAESTINI) Qui iidem alibi Philistini. Nam פ Hebræum Græci in π transferunt, ut hic notavit Hiero- nymus.

ET IMPLENTES INIMICITIAS VETERES ) Vide 1. Sam. 13. & 42.

## 25:16
Vers. 16. I WILL DESTROY THE DESTROYERS) כרתים is the proper name of a part of the Philistines, as appears in 1 Samuel 30, 14. From these David enlisted a legion for himself, and from the same the Cretans seem to have originated: whence the LXX here and in Zeph. 2, 4 have placed Κρῆτας.

Thus indeed with Kimchi and Mercerus, Pradus, Pintus, Maldonat. But from v. 7 and the preceding word, it is certain that the punishment of retaliation is designated, and the Chaldean, Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion, and Jerome render it appellatively.

AND I WILL DESTROY THE REMNANTS OF THE MARITIME REGION) He says remnants, because that maritime region near Azotus had been much devastated by Psammetichus, as we said at Jerem. 25, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 16. INTERFICIAM INTERFECTORES ) כרתים nomen est proprium partis Philistinorum, ut ap- paret 1. Samuel. 30, 14. Ex his legionem sibi conscripsit David, & ab iisdem orti Cretes videntur: unde LXX. hic & Soph. 2, 4. Κρῆτας posuere.

Ita quidem cum Kimchio & Mercero Pradus, Pintus, Maldonat. Sed e v. 7. & verbo anteceden- te pœnam talionis designari certum est, & appel- lative reddunt Chald. Aquila, Symmach. Theodotio, Hieronymus.

ET PERDAM RELIQVIAS MARITIMÆ RE- GIONIS) Reliquias dicit, quia maritima illa regio apud A- zotom multum vastata fuerat à Psammeticho, ut diximus ad Jerem. 25, 20.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

The overthrow of Tyre is predicted, because it exulted over the devastation of Jerusalem.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Tyri eversio prædicta, quod super vastatione Hierosolymæ exultarit.

## 26:1
AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE ELEVENTH YEAR) From the deportation of Jeconiah, from which Ezekiel is accustomed to reckon times.

THE FIRST OF THE MONTH) Namely, of that which followed the capture of Jerusalem, which the following things imply.

Others prefer that these things were spoken prophetically before Jerusalem was captured, from a foresight of the impending boasting of the Tyrians. For otherwise, if that boasting had already been commonly known, what need was there for the Prophet to be taught this matter by a divine oracle.

Latin:

ET FACTVM EST IN VNDECIMO ANNO) A deportatione Jechoniæ, unde tempora putare solet E- zechiel.

PRIMA MENSIS) Nempe ejus qui secutus est capta Hierosolyma, quod sequentia innuunt.

Alii malunt ante captam Hieros. hæc pro- phetice dicta, ex prævisione instantis gloriationis Tyriorum. Alias enim si gloriatio illa vulgo jam agnita fuisset, quid opus erat Prophetam oraculo divino hanc rem edoceri.

## 26:2
Vers. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

## 26:2
Vers. 2.

THE GATES OF THE PEOPLES ARE BROKEN) In the Hebrew, the singular of the verbs with a plural noun, which you may explain thus: That city is broken, which offered a wide entrance to foreign peoples.

IT IS TURNED TO ME) It turns itself to me: namely, that market of grain, wine, oil, and balsam.

I SHALL BE FILLED, IT IS DESERTED) I shall grow from its ruins. But the Greeks and the Chaldean read המלאת, or took א for ה: for they translate, that which had been full, is deserted.

The original text is more convenient: which we acknowledge as uniquely authentic: and the Vulgate translation is correct. For neighboring markets are accustomed to take growth from the ruin of others. For there too the corruption of one is the generation of another.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CONFRACTÆ SVNT PORTÆ POPVLORVM) In Hebræo verborum singulare cum nomine plurali, quod sic explices: Fracta est urbs illa, quæ populis externis latum præbebat aditum.

CONVERSA EST AD ME) Ad me se vertit: fo- rum scilicet illud frugum vini, olei, balsami.

IMPLEBOR, DESERTA EST) Ego ex illius rui- nis crescam. At Græci & Chaldæus legerunt המלאת, aut א sumserunt pro ה: vertunt enim, quæ plena fuerat, deserta est.

Convenientior est textus originalis: quem uni- ce authenticum agnoscimus: & recte habet se vul- gata translatio. Solent enim vicina emporia ex aliorum ruina incrementa capere. Nam & ibi unius corruptio est alterius generatio.

## 26:3
Vers. 3. BEHOLD I AM AGAINST THEE TYRE) I come against thee.

AND I WILL CAUSE MANY NATIONS TO COME UP AGAINST THEE) Against thee.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ECCE EGO SVPER TE TTRE) Contra te venio.

ET ASCENDERE FACIAM AD TE GENTES MVLTAS) Contra te.

## 26:4
Vers. 4. AND THEY SHALL DESTROY THE WALLS OF TYRE, AND BREAK DOWN HER TOWERS) Josephus produces the acts of the Phoenicians, which we also cited in the third book on the truth of the Christian Religion: from which it appears that Tyre was besieged by Nebuchadnezzar for 13 years, and it is necessary that a city secluded from commerce for so long a time was reduced to great poverty; many things of the city were also scattered. Those acts do not say what the outcome of the siege was. I do not doubt that the city, tamed by so many evils, surrendered itself to the faith of the Babylonians. It was, however, sometimes under kings, sometimes under judges, that is, interreges, but who observed the Babylonian majesty, to such an extent that it sometimes sought kings from Babylon, from those who were held there as hostages. Which we learn from those acts. And by the same right that Tyre had been under the Babylonians, it remained afterwards under the Persians, the victors of Babylon, until the city was captured by Alexander. But we learn below in v. 7 and c. 29, 19 that the things said here pertain to the times of Nebuchadnezzar, and not to those of Alexander. Nor did Jerome think otherwise in his commentaries on this place.

AND I WILL SCRAPE HER DUST FROM HER) The Latins would say: I will scrape away everything down to the dust.

AND I WILL MAKE IT INTO THE MOST BARE LAND) Like a lofty rock: for these are the same words as above 24, 7. The sense is: I will make you bare like a cliff. Seneca, relegated to Corsica: That once great citizen of yours, your glory, shall be fixed to a rock.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET DISSIPABVNT MUROS TTRI, ET DESTRVENT TVRRES EJVS) Producit acta Phœnicum Josephus, quæ & nos citavimus ad tertium de veritate Re- ligionis Christianæ: unde apparet à Nabuchodonosore Ty- rum obsessam per annos 13. tanto tempore seclusam à com- merciis urbem, ad magnam inopiam redactam esse necesse est; multa etiam urbis disjecta. Exitus quis fuerit obsidio- nis illa acta non dicunt. Ego non dubito quin tot malis do- mita urbs, in fidem se Babyloniorum dederit. Fuit tamen modo sub regibus, modo sub judicibus, id est, interregibus, sed qui majestatem Babylonicam observarent, adeo ut & à Babylone, ex iis qui ibi obsides habebantur, reges interdum peteret. Quod ex illius actis discimus. Quo autem jure sub Babyloniis Tyrus fuerat, eodem postea mansit sub Persis Babylonis victoribus, donec ab Alexandro urbs capta est. Quæ autem hic dicuntur, ad Nabuchodonosoris, non autem ad Alexandri tempora pertinere discimus infra v. 7. & c. 29, 19. Nec aliter sensit Hieronymus in commentariis ad hunc locum.

ET RADAM PVLVEREM EJVS DE EA) Lati- ni dicerent: abradam omnia cum pulvisculo.

ET DABO EAM IN LIMPIDISSIMAM TER- RAM) Tanquam sublimem petram: sunt enim voces ea- dem quæ supra 24, 7. Sensus est: faciam te nudam ut sco- pulum. Seneca in corsicam relegatus: Ille tuus quondam magnus, tua gloria, civis Infigar scopulo.

## 26:5
Ver. 5.

THE DRYING OF NETS SHALL BE IN THE MIDST OF THE SEA) It shall be like deserted shores, offering no other use than for drying nets. Institutes, on the division of things, § 5. The use of shores is also public by the law of nations, just as that of the sea itself, and for that reason it is free for anyone to place a hut there, into which you may withdraw, just as to dry nets and draw them from the sea.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

SICCATIO SAGENARVM ERIT IN MEDIO MARIS) Erit sicut littora deserta, nec alium præbentia usum, quam retibus siccandis. Institution. de rerum divi- sione §. 5. Littorum quoque usus publicus est juris gentium, sicut & ipsius maris, & ob id cuilibet liberum est casam ibi ponere, in quam te recipias, sicut retia siccare & ex mari deducere.

## 26:6
Ver. 6.

HER DAUGHTERS ALSO, WHICH ARE IN THE FIELD) Lesser towns and villages. By them, however, the inhabitants are to be understood, as the Chaldean notes here.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

FILIÆ QVOQVE EJVS, QVÆ SVNT IN AGRO) Minora oppida & vici. Per eos autem intelli- gendi habitatores, ut hic notat Chaldæus.

## 26:7
Ver. 7.

KING OF KINGS) The Babylonian Kings deservedly called themselves thus, who also ruled over certain Kings. See 2 Kings 22, 8; Jeremiah 52, 32; the Persian Kings followed this. Aeschylus concerning kings, under Xerxes: Βασιλῆς Βασιλέως ὕποχοι μεγάλες. Thus the Armenian King was under Cyrus; and Evagoras, King of Cyprus, under the successors of Cyrus, and many others, as we said at Jeremiah 50, 41.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

REGEM REGVM) Merito sic se appellarunt Baby- lonii Reges, qui & Regibus quibusdam imperabant. Vide 2. Reg. 22, 8. Jerem. 52, 32. secuti id Persæ Reges. Æschi- lus de regibus, sub Xerxe: Βασιλῆς Βασιλέως ὕποχοι μεγάλες. Sic Armenius Rex sub Cyro fuit; Et Evagoras Rex Cypri sub Cyri successoribus multique alii, ut diximus ad Je- rem. 50, 41.

## 26:8
Ver. 8.

THY DAUGHTERS WHICH ARE IN THE FIELD) He repeats what he had said above, so that it may be better retained.

AND SHALL COMPASS THEE WITH FORTS) A tower, that is, he will set towers against you. See 2 Kings 25, 1.

AND SHALL CAST A MOUNT AGAINST THEE) He will surround you with a military rampart.

AND SHALL LIFT UP THE SHIELD AGAINST THEE) He will attack you with a tortoise made of ladders. The LXX well describe the tortoise by saying, περίσασιν ὅπλων.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

FILIAS TVAS QVÆ SVNT IN AGRO) Repe- tit quod supra dixerat, quo melius retineatur.

ET CIRCVMDABIT TE MVNITIONIBVS ) Turrem, id est, turres tibi opponet. Vid. 2. Reg. 25, 1.

ET COMPORTABIT AGGEREM IN GTRO) Vallo castrensi te cinget.

ET ELEVABIT CONTRA TE CLTPEVM ) Testudine ex scalis facta te oppugnabit. LXX. bene testu- dinem circumscribunt dicendo, περίσασιν ὅπλων.

## 26:9
Verse 9.

AND HE WILL DIRECT HIS BATTERING RAMS AGAINST THY WALLS) And he will give a blow directly against thy wall. For מחו is to strike among the Chaldeans, whence מחו are blows. קבל, however, among the same Chaldeans, as also among the Arabs, is over against. The Chaldean expressed the sense well when he said, the striking of engines.

AND HE WILL DESTROY THY TOWERS WITH THY WEAPONS) חרב is whatever is made of iron. And so, it is translated now as swords, now as lances, now as hammers. Sometimes the LXX simply put σιδήρον for it. But here the Chaldean well interprets it as iron stones (that is, balls), namely those which were thrown from ballistae.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET VINEAS ET ARIETES TEMPERABIT IN MVROS TVOS) Et ictum ex directo dabit contra murum tuum. Nam מחו Chaldæis est verberare, unde מחו ver- bera. קבל autem iisdem Chaldæis, ut & Arabibus, est ex adverso. Sensum bene expressit Chaldæus, cum dixit, percussionem tormentorum.

ET TVRRES TVAS DESTRVET IN ARMA- TVRA TVA) חרב est, quicquid ex ferro sit. Itaque mo- do gladii, modo lanceæ, modo mallei voce vertitur. In- terdum LXX. simpliciter pro eo ponunt σιδήρον. At hic Chaldæus bene interpretatur lapides (id est globos) fer- reos, nempe qui e balistis jaciebantur.

## 26:10
Verse 10.

BY REASON OF THE ABUNDANCE OF HIS HORSES THEIR DUST SHALL COVER THEE) He said inundation for multitude: which word is here in the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek. So great will be the dust from the running of the horses that it will cover the city like a cloud.

AT THE NOISE OF THE HORSEMEN AND OF THE WHEELS, AND OF THE CHARIOTS THY WALLS SHALL SHAKE) For houses are accustomed to tremble when many chariots and horses run about nearby, because of the cohesion of the ground.

WHEN HE SHALL ENTER INTO THY GATES AS BY THE ENTRANCE OF A CITY WHICH IS BROKEN UP) Such as is the entrance of a broken-up city. With as much security will he enter thy gates (surrender having been made) as a city deserted by its citizens is accustomed to be entered. To such an extent will he fear no one.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

INVNDATIONE EQVORVM EJVS OPERIET TE PVLVIS EORVM) Inundationem dixit pro multitu- dine: quæ vox hic est in Hebræo, Chaldæo, & Græco. Tantus erit pulvis ab equorum cursu, ut nubis modo ur- bem operiat.

A SONITV EQVITVM ET ROTARVM, ET CVRRVVM MOVEBVNTVR MVRI TVI) Solent enim ædes tremere, ubi in propinquo multi cursitant currus & equi, propter soli cohærentiam.

CVM INGRESSVS FVERIT PORTAS TVAS QVASI PER INTROITVM VRBIS DISSIPATÆ) Qualis est introitus urbis dissipatæ. Tanta securitate intra- bit portas tuas (deditione facta) quanta intrari solet urbs a civibus deserta. Adeo neminem metuet.

## 26:11
Verse 11.

HE SHALL SLAY THY PEOPLE WITH THE SWORD) Many of the people.
