AND THY STRONG GARRISONS SHALL FALL DOWN TO THE GROUND) And מצבה and קמא, which the Chaldean has here, everywhere signifies a statue. Wherefore I should think this is said, that the city having been surrendered, it will come to pass that the statues erected to the Kings of Egypt, and to other allies of Tyre and enemies of the Chaldeans, will be cast down. For images of those to whom things turn out unhappily are accustomed to be cast down. You have many examples in Roman history.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

POPLVVM TVVM GLADIO CÆDET) Multos de populo.

ET STATVÆ TVÆ NOBILES IN TERRAM CORRVENT) Et מצבה & קמא quod hic habet Chal- dæus, ubique statuam significat. Quare putem hoc dici, dedita urbe fore ut dejiciantur statuæ erectæ Ægypti Regi- bus, aliisque fœderatis Tyri & Chaldæorum hostibus. So- lent enim imagines dejici eorum, quibus res infeliciter cedunt. Multa exempla habes in historia Romana.

## 26:12
Verse 12.

THEY SHALL MAKE A SPOIL OF THY RICHES) In the fields.

THEY SHALL PLUNDER THY NEGOTIATIONS) They shall prepare the way for commerce.

AND THY DUST IN THE MIDST OF THE WATERS THEY SHALL PLACE) They shall cast the ruins into the sea. Thus both the Greeks and the Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

VASTABVNT OPES TVAS) In agris.

DIRIPIENT NEGOTIATIONES TVAS) Aditum commerciis præstruent.

ET PVLVEREM TVVM IN MEDIO AQVA- RVM PONENT) Rudera in mare projicient. Sic & Græ- ci & Chaldæus.

## 26:13
Ver. 13.

AND I WILL CAUSE THE MULTITUDE OF THY SONGS TO CEASE, AND THE SOUNDS OF THY HARPS SHALL BE HEARD NO MORE) The signs of joy shall cease. See Jer. 7, 34.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET QVIESCERE FACIAM MVLTITVDINEM CANTICORVM TVORVM, ET SONITVS CI- THARARVM TVARVM NON AVDIENTVR AM- PLIVS) Signa lætitiæ cessabunt. Vid. Jer. 7, 34.

## 26:14
Ver. 14.

AND I WILL MAKE THEE A MOST CLEAR ROCK) Into a high cliff. Thou shalt be like a crag, as above in 4.

THOU SHALT BE A DRYING PLACE FOR NETS) See above verse 4.

AND THOU SHALT NOT BE BUILT ANY MORE) Thou shalt not return to thy former fortune. For to build is, for the Hebrews and Syrians, both to multiply offspring and to grow rich. Understand this, however, within a long time, having compared the histories of the times of Alexander.

Blessed Jerome reconciles this passage with Is. 23, 17 in this way, that the sense here is concerning not restoring such a government as existed under Hiram and other Kings, so that Tyre might become a peculiar kingdom. Theodoret thus: that it is not to be restored to its pristine splendor; Kimchi, that it is not to be rebuilt in the same, but in another place. All these things can have a place at the same time.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET DABO TE IN LIMPIDISSIMAM PETRAM) In altam rupem. Scopuli instar eris, ut supra 4.

SICCATIO SAGENARVM ERIS) Vide supra vers. 4.

NEC ÆDIFICABERIS VLTRA) Non redibis ad veterem fortunam. Ædificare enim est Hebræis & Syris tum sobolescere tum ditescere. Intellige autem hoc intra lon- gum tempus, collatis historiis temporum Alexandri.

B. Hieronym. locum hunc cum Ef. 23, 17. sic conciliat, quod hic sensus sit, de non restituet- do tali regimine, quale fuit sub Hiram aliisque Regibus, ut Tyrus quasi regnum peculiare fiat. Theodoretus ita: non effe pristino splendori resti- tuendam; Kimchi, non esse eodem, sed alio loco ræædificandam. Possunt omnia ista simul locum habere.

## 26:15
Ver. 15.

THY RUINS) That is, of the parts of thy city.

THE ISLES SHALL BE MOVED) That is, all the seacoast.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

RVINÆ TVÆ) Id est, partium urbis tuæ.

COMMOVEBVNTVR INSVLÆ) Id est, omnis ora maritima.

## 26:16
Verse 16.

ALL THE PRINCES OF THE SEA SHALL DESCEND FROM THEIR THRONES) The Carthaginians, the Gaditanians, and others born of Tyre and powerful at sea. To descend from one's seat is the custom of those mourning. Jonah 2:6.

THEY SHALL TAKE OFF THEIR ROBES) Their outer garments. Exodus 28:4; 31:11; 5:1; 1 Samuel 18:4; 2 Samuel 13:18.

AND THEY SHALL CAST AWAY THEIR VARIEGATED GARMENTS) Embroidered with a needle: for this too is the custom of those mourning, to change their clothes. See the aforementioned passage of Jonah. Cicero in more than one place narrates that the senate changed their clothing on his account.

AND THEY SHALL BE CLOTHED WITH ASTONISHMENT) You have similar figures of speech above 7:27, 51; Psalm 132:18, and elsewhere. The sense is: they shall be surrounded by fear.

THEY SHALL SIT ON THE GROUND) This is also a custom of those grieving. Job 2:13.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

DESCENDENT DE SEDIBVS SVIS OMNES PRINCIPES MARIS) Carthaginenses, Gaditani, aliique Tyro orti & potentes mari. Descendere de sede mos lugen- tium. Jon. 2, 6.

AUFERENT EXUVIAS SUAS) Vestes extimas. Exod. 28, 4. 31. 11, 5. 1. Sam. 18, 4. 2. Sam. 13, 18.

ET VESTIMENTA SVA VARIA ABJICIENT) Acu picta: nam & hic mos lugentium, mutare vestes. Vide dictum Jonæ locum. Cicero non uno loco propter se a senatu mutatam vestem narrat.

ET INDVENTVR STVPORE) Loquendi gene- ra similia habes supra 7, 27.51. Ps. 132, 18. & alibi. Sen- sus est: circumdabuntur metu.

IN TERRA SEDEBVNT) Mos & hic mœrentium. Job. 2, 13.

## 26:17
Verse 17.

YOU WHO DWELL IN THE SEA) In the Hebrew: Inhabited by the seas: That is, to which strangers came from every sea.

YOU WHO WERE STRONG IN THE SEA) See what was said at Isaiah 23.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

QVÆ HABITAS IN MARI) In Hebræo: Habitata a maribus: Id est ad quam ab omni mari advenæ veniebant.

QVÆ FVISTI FORTIS IN MARI) Vide quæ dicta ad Esa. 23.

## 26:18
NOW THE SHIPS SHALL BE ASTONISHED IN THE DAY OF YOUR TERROR) In the Hebrew and Greek, the islands: It is the same noun that follows in the other member, except that here the ending is Chaldaic, there Hebrew. Moreover, an island to the Hebrews is any maritime coast. But Jerome in his commentary affirms that in the Hebrew it was ships. Therefore he reads אניה.

AND THE ISLANDS SHALL BE TROUBLED IN THE SEA) The islands, I say, in the sea shall be troubled. Note here the repeated word.

BECAUSE NO ONE GOES OUT FROM YOU) In the Hebrew, in the day of your departure: That is, when hostages are taken from you to Babylon. See what we said at the beginning of the chapter.

Latin:

NVNC STVPEBVNT NAVES IN DIE PAVO- RIS TVI) In Hebræo & Græco, Insulæ: Est idem nomen, quod in altero membro sequitur, nisi quod hic terminatio est Chaldaica, ibi Hebraica. Insula autem Hebræis est omnis ora maritima. At Hieronymus in commentario affirmat in Hebræo fuisse naves. Legit ergo אניה.

ET TVRBABVNTUR INSVLÆ IN MARI) Insu- læ, inquam, in mari turbabuntur. hic nota repetitæ vocis.

EO QVOD NVLLVS EGREDIATVR EX TE) In Hebræo, in die exitus tui: Id est ubi obsides ex te aufe- rentur Babylonem. Vide quæ diximus initio capitis.

## 26:19
Ver. 19.

WHEN I SHALL HAVE MADE THEE A DESOLATE CITY, AS CITIES WHICH ARE NOT INHABITED) As destitute of commerce as are cities empty of men.

AND SHALL HAVE BROUGHT UPON THEE THE ABYSS, AND MANY WATERS SHALL HAVE COVERED THEE) A part of thee, which is wont to happen when fortifications are scattered.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

CVM DEDERO TE VRBEM DESOLATAM, SICVT CIVITATES, QVÆ NON HABITANTVR) Tam destitutam a commerciis, quam sunt urbes hominum vacuæ.

ET ADDVXERO SVPER TE ABTSSVM, ET OPERVERINT TE AQVÆ MVLTÆ) Partem tui, quod fieri solet disjectis munimentis.

## 26:20
Ver. 20.

AND SHALL HAVE BROUGHT THEE DOWN WITH THEM THAT DESCEND INTO THE PIT TO THE EVERLASTING PEOPLE) Into the grave. For that is often called בור. In Greek βόθρον both here and below 31, 14. 32, 18. 23. 24, 28. 29. τὰ θεμέλια τῆς γῆς, Isa. 12, 15. The same is said here of Tyre, as in the Gospel of Capernaum, thou shalt be brought down to hell. The life of cities is liberty, commerce, wealth. For: ᾿Αργύριόν ἐσιν αἷμα κὶ ψυχὴ βροτοῖς. The everlasting people are the dead, by whom one perpetual night is slept.

AND SHALL HAVE SET THEE IN THE LOWEST PARTS OF THE EARTH) In the Hebrew: In the land of the lower ones. Thou shalt be as if buried. AS THE ANCIENT DESOLATIONS) Here both the Greeks and the Chaldean read ב for כ, or certainly כ, as if they interpreted it as ב. You will be a part of places desolate from every age. Anyone sees that there is no need for us to invent a different reading, since they could have interpreted ב as כ: such things are met with everywhere. But we have here Grotius, who does not disagree. He who also in chapter 27, 6, and verses 13, 18, ought to have determined [this], but not to have descended to other readings on account of either the Greek or the Latin version. WITH THOSE WHO ARE BROUGHT DOWN INTO THE PIT) He repeats what he had said, as he often does. THAT YOU MAY NOT BE INHABITED) That is, That you may not be inhabited as before. WHEN I SHALL HAVE GIVEN GLORY IN THE LAND OF THE LIVING) Not even then, when Judea shall flourish again. Judea is called the land of the living, that is, of happy men: for to live is often for the Hebrews to lead a life happily. Tremellius, the Belgian [translators], and the Polani of the Bibles understand the glory of the Church of the Jews and especially of the N.T. annotators, explaining the land of the living as the Church, both militant and triumphant. Therefore, the spiritual happiness of the Church is regarded rather than the temporal happiness of Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ET DETRAXERO TE CVM HIS, QVI DE- SCENDVNT IN LACVM AD POPVLVM SEMPI- TERNVVM) In sepulchrum. Id enim sæpe בור dicitur. Græce βόθρον & hic & infra 31, 14. 32, 18. 23. 24, 28. 29. τὰ θε- μέλια τῆς γῆς, Esa. 12, 15. Idem dicitur hic de Tyro, quod in Evangelio de Capharnaumo, ἕως ἅδε καταβιβασθήσῃ. Vi- ta urbium est libertas, commercia, opes. Nam: ᾿Αργύριόν ἐσιν αἷμα κὶ ψυχὴ βροτοῖς. Populus sempiternus sunt mortui, quibus nox una perpe- tua dormitur.

ET COLLOCAVERO TE IN TERRA NO- VISSIMA) In Hebræo: In terra inferiorum. Eris quasi sepulta. SICVT SOLITVDINES VETERES) Hic & Græci & Chaldæus pro כ legerunt ב, aut certe כ, tanquam ב funt interpretati. Eris pars locis ab omni ævo defertis. Quivis videt, opus non esse, ut diversam lectionem fingamus, quam ב tanquam כ interpretari potuerint: qualia plurima passim obvia. Sed habemus hic non refragantem Grotium. Qui idem etiam cap. 27, 6. & vers. 13. 18. statuere, non vero in alias lectiones sive ob Græcam, sive ob Latinam versionem pedibus descendere debuisset. CVM HIS QVI DEDVCVNTVR IN LACVM) Repetit quod dixerat, ut sæpe. VT NON HABITERIS) Id est, Ut non ut ante habiteris. CVM DEDERO GLORIAM IN TERRA VIVENTIVM) Ne tum quidem, cum Judæa iterum florebit. Judæa dicitur terra viventium, id est, hominum felicium: nam vivere sæpe Hebræis est beate vitam agere. Gloriam Ecclesiæ Judæorum & imprimis N. T. intelligunt Tremell. Belgic. & Polani Biblior. annotatores, terram viventium de Ecclesia tum militante, tum triumphante explicantes. Felicitas ergo spiritualis Ecclesiæ potius, quam Judææ temporalis felicitas respicitur.

## 26:21
Ver. 21.

I WILL BRING YOU TO NOTHING) I will give terrors in you. AND YOU SHALL NOT BE) Namely, what you were. Tyre, some time after Jerusalem was destroyed, received this slaughter, as we learned above in v. 2. Therefore, the 70 years of the exile of the Jews ended before the 70 years after which, according to Jeremiah's prediction, Tyre was to return to its old fortune. AND YOU SHALL BE SOUGHT AND NOT BE FOUND ANY MORE) Men will ask where that city is now, which sent out so many colonies, which ruled so widely over the sea. FOREVER) For a long time, as we have now often said. 70 years is a common measure of human life. Others prefer to understand these things concerning the final destruction of Tyre made by Alexander the Great. See Osiander in the Paraphrase. Which fits the emphasis of the words in this last part better.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

IN NIHILVM REDIGAM TE) Terrores dabo in te. ET NON ERIS) Nempe quod fuisti. Tyrus aliquanto post destructa Hierosolyma hanc cladem accepit, ut supra didicimus v. 2. itaque LXX. anni exsilii Judæorum prius exiere quam LXX. anni, post quos in veterem fortunam, ex Jeremiæ prædictione, reditura erat Tyrus. ET REQVISITA NON INVENIERIS VLTRA) Quærent homines ubi nunc illa est urbs, quæ tam multas misit colonias, quæ tam late mari imperavit. IN SEMPITERNVM) In Longum tempus, ut jam sæpe diximus. LXX. anni mensura communis vitæ humanæ. Alii hæc de ultimo excidio Tyri facto per Alex. M. intelligere malunt. Vid. Osiander in Paraphr. Quod emphası verborum in postrema hac parte magis convenit.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII. The ruin of the maritime and most opulent city of Tyre is bewailed, with the goods recounted which were accustomed to be brought to it from every region, and its insane luxury.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII. Tyri urbis maritima ac opulentissima ruina defletur enarratis mercibus, quæ à quaque regione ad eam deferri consueverant, & luxu ejus insano.

## 27:3
Ver. 3.

WHO DWELLS AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE SEA) At the port of the sea: supply 'excellent'. TRADING WITH THE PEOPLES TO MANY ISLANDS) Trading with peoples even to many shores. AND SITUATED IN THE HEART OF THE SEA) In the Hebrew: In the heart of the sea are your borders. For what the Latin refers to as 'your neighbors' to the following sense, the Chaldean and our Greek codices more correctly draw to this member, in the sense I have mentioned. This is what it means: your empire is not contained by land, but spreads itself widely through the sea, so that the Tyrian seas have passed into a proverb. The books of the LXX, for τὰ ὄρια, had τῷ βεελείμ. Perhaps they had written γεβολίμ.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

QVÆ HABITAT IN INTROITV MARIS) Ad portum maris: supple egregium. NEGOTIATIONI POPVLORVM AD INSVLAS MVLTAS) Negotianti cum populis ad oras usque multas. ET IN CORDE MARIS SITA) In Hebræo: In corde maris termini tui. Nam quod Latinus finitimi tui ad sequentem sensum refert, in Chaldæus & Græci nostri codices rectius ad hoc membrum trahunt, eo quo dixi sensu. Hoc vult: imperium tuum non terra continetur: sed late per mare se spargit, ita ut Tyria maria in proverbium abierint. Libri LXX. pro τὰ ὄρια, habuerunt τῷ βεελείμ. Forte scripserant γεβολίμ.

## 27:4
Ver. 4.

WHO BUILT YOU) The Sidonians. THEY HAVE FILLED YOUR BEAUTY) They have perfectly adorned you.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QVI TE ÆDIFICAVERUNT) Sidonii. IMPLEVERVNT DECOREM TVVM) Perfecte te ornarunt.

## 27:5
Ver. 5.

WITH FIR TREES FROM SANIR THEY HAVE BUILT YOU WITH ALL THE PLANKS OF THE SEA) With fir trees from Sanir (that is, from Hermon, Deut. 3, 9) they built for you all the planks of the sea. That is, bridges, as the Chaldean interprets it very well, who no less than the Latin reads לחתים in the Hebrew. On the contrary, the LXX, for את כל, read it as one word אתכל, for they translate it as ταινίας, that is, ribbons. But תכל is a linen cloth. Nor do we acknowledge a different reading here. Even if the Vulgate took the word differently and read it in its own mind, because it did not think of the dual form used here, or did not grasp its sense. And why is not another reading also ascribed to the Chaldean? For it could be said that he himself read לְחֹתֶיךָ, because he translates 'all his bridges', when in the Hebrew there is no suffix, but a simple dual לֻחֹתַיִם. Why should the LXX not be said to have read it differently as well? For they translated it differently: Thus, as many readings as versions must often be invented, which is absurd.

THEY TOOK A CEDAR FROM LEBANON, TO MAKE A MAST FOR YOU) A noble daughter of the forest: as Horace says.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ABIETIBVS DE SANIR EXTRVXERVNT TE CVM OMNIBVS TABVLATIS MARIS) Abietibus de Sanir (id est, de Hermone Deut. 3, 9.) ædificaverunt tibi omnia tabulata maris. Id est, pontes, ut optime interpretatur Chaldæus, qui non minus quam Latinus in Hebræo legit לחתים. contra LXX. pro את כל, legerunt una voce אתכל, vertunt enim ταινίας, id est, aplustria. Est autem תכל carbafus. Neque hic diversam lectionem agnoscimus. Etsi vulgatus diversim acceperit vocem & legerit in sua mente, quia de forma duali hic adhibita non cogitavit, vel sensum ejus assecutus non est. Et cur non etiam alia lectio adscribitur Chal- dæo? Posset enim dici ipsum legisse לְחֹתֶיךָ, quia vertit omnes pontes suos, quum inEbræo nullum ha- beatur suffixum, sed simplex duale לֻחֹתַיִם. Cur non LXX. itidem aliter legisse dicendi? verterunt enim aliter: Ita tot lectiones, quot versiones sæpe fingendæ, quod ἄτοπον.

CEDRVM DE LIBANO TVLERVNT, VT FACERENT TIBI MALUM) Silvæ filia nobilis: ut ait Horatius.

## 27:6
Ver. 6.

THE OAKS OF BASHAN THEY HAVE HEWN FOR THY OARS) אַלּוֹנִים some translate as oaks, others as elms or pines. But the Chaldean has בַּלּוֹטִין, which word signifies oaks to both the Chaldeans and the Arabs.

AND THY BENCHES THEY HAVE MADE FOR THEE OF INDIAN IVORY) From the tooth, in the Hebrew: But by that word they denote ivory, as can be seen in 1 Kings 10:18, 22:39, 2 Chronicles 9:17, Amos 3:5, and elsewhere. The Chaldean understands it as boxwood inlaid with ivory. For קַרְשֵׁךְ, thy benches, the Greeks read קָדְשֵׁךְ, thy holy things.

AND LITTLE PRÆTORIA FROM THE ISLANDS OF ITALY) This passage is translated in various ways. I hold it for certain that אַשּׁוּרִים here is the name of a tree, which is תְּאַשּׁוּר, Isaiah 41:19, where the Chaldean translates it as boxwood. The prætorium which Jerome mentioned here, the Hebrews call תָּא, that is, a cabin in the prow of a ship. For the islands of Italy, in the Hebrew and Greek it is ἀπὸ νήσων τῶν χεττιείμ. Cyprus is properly called by this name. Then, figuratively, other overseas places, especially Macedonia, as in 1 Maccabees 1:1; Pliny teaches us that boxwood was sought from there.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

QVERCUS DE BASAN DOLAVERUNT IN REMOS TVOS) אַלּוֹנִים alii quercus vertunt, alii ul- mos, aut pinus. Sed Chaldæus habet בַּלּוֹטִין quæ vox & Chaldæis & Arabibus significat quercus.

ET TRANSTRA TVA TIBI FECERVNT EX EBORE INDICO) Ex dente, in Hebræo: Sed ea voce ebur notant, ut videre est 1. Reg. 10, 18. 22, 39, 2. Paral. 9, 17. Amos 3, 5. & alibi. Chaldæus intelligit buxum intextam ebore. Pro קַרְשֵׁךְ transtra tua, Græci legerunt קָדְשֵׁךְ, τὰ ἱερά σε.

ET PRÆTORIOLA DE INSVLIS ITALIÆ) Varie hic locus vertitur. Ego pro certo habeo אַשּׁוּרִים hic arboris esse nomen, quæ תְּאַשּׁוּר, Es. 41, 19. ubi buxum vertit Chaldæus. Prætorium quod hic dixit Hie- ronymus, Hebræi תָּא, id est, conclave in navis prora. Pro Italiæ insulis, in Hebræo & Græco est ἀπὸ νήσων τῶν χεττιείμ. Proprie sic vocatur Cyprus. Deinde transla- te alia loca transmarina, præsertim Macedonia, ut 1. Macc. 1, 1. inde autem petitam buxum, docet nos Plinius.

## 27:7
Ver. 7.

FINE LINEN WITH EMBROIDERED WORK FROM EGYPT WAS MADE FOR THEE INTO A SAIL, THAT IT MIGHT BE SET ON THE MAST) And with Egyptian multicolored fine linen an expansion was made for thee, which might serve as a sail.

BLUE AND PURPLE FROM THE ISLANDS OF ELISHA WAS THY COVERING) Understand hyacinth, which Persius calls hyacinthine, wool of the same color as the violet. The islands of Elisha are the maritime places of the Aeolians, who are the best dyers of wool.

By covering, some understand wrappings, with which in a triumph, or upon the arrival of ships, the decks and the curved parts of a ship are accustomed to be covered, and more precious merchandise to be wrapped.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

BYSSUS VARIA DE ÆGYPTO TEXTA EST TIBI IN VELVM, VT PONERETVR IN MALO) Et bysso versicolore Ægyptia facta tibi expansio, quæ pro velo serviret.

HYACINTHVS ET PVRPVRA DE INSVLIS ELISA FACTVM EST OPERIMENTVM TVVM) Hyacinthon intellige, quæ Hyacinthina Persius vocat, la- nam violæ concolorem. Insulæ Elisa, sunt maritima loca Æolum, qui optimi lanarum tinctores.

Per operimentum involucra nonnulli intelli- gunt, quibus in triumpho, vel appulsu navium ta- bulata, & convexa navis solent tegi, mercesque pretiosiores involvi.

## 27:8
THE INHABITANTS OF SIDON AND THE ARADIANS WERE THY ROWERS) So great was the wealth of the Tyrians that they delegated the more menial tasks to foreigners. Concerning Aradus, see Genesis 10:4. The Sidonians were πολύτεχνοι (skilled in many arts) to Strabo.

THY WISE MEN, O TYRE, WERE MADE PILOTS) Thy wise men were in thee: they themselves were thy pilots: That is: experts in naval affairs, whom thou wouldst set over fleets and ships, thou hadst from thyself, thou didst not seek them from elsewhere.

Latin:

HABITATORES SIDONIS ET ARADII FVE- RVNT REMIGES TVI) Tanta erat Tyriorum opulen- tia, ut viliora ministeria externis delegarent. De Arado vide Gen. 10, 4. Sidonii πολύτεχνοι Straboni.

SAPIENTES TVI TTRI FACTI SVNT GV- BERNATORES) Sapientes tui fuerunt in te: ipsi guberna- tores tui: Id est: peritores rei navalis, quos classibus navi- busque præficeres, de te habebas, non petebas aliunde.

## 27:9
Ver. 9.

THE ELDERS OF GEBAL AND THE WISE MEN THEREOF WERE IN THEE TO MEND THE CHINKS OF THY VARIOUS WARES) The elders of Gebal, and indeed the most skilled of them, were with thee to mend the fissures: That is, to make the joints of the ships, which later Greeks and from them we call καλαφατεῖν (to caulk). The Gebalites were excellent craftsmen. See 1 Kings 5:18. Their region is Gabala to Pliny and Ptolemy; in the books of the LXX, βιβλίων is read instead of Γιβλίων by an error of the scribes.

ALL THE SHIPS OF THE SEA, AND THEIR SAILORS WERE IN THE PEOPLE OF THY MERCHANDISE) That is, from all lands ships and sailors came to thee for the sake of trade.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SENES GIBLII ET PRVDENTES EJVS HABV- ERVNT NAVTAS AD MINISTERIVM VARIÆ SV- PELLECTILIS TVÆ) Senes Giblii & quidem eorum peri- tissimi, tibi aderant ad scissuras sarciendas: Id est, ad facien- das navium commissuras, quod Græci posteriores & inde nos καλαφατεῖν dicimus. Erant Giblii fabri optimi. Vid. 1. Reg. 5, 18. Horum regio Gabala Plinio ac Ptolemæo; in libris LXX. βιβλίων legitur pro Γιβλίων errore scriba- rum.

OMNES NAVES MARIS, ET NAVTÆ EA- RVM FVERVNT IN POPVLO NEGOTIATIONIS TVÆ) Id est, ab omnibus terris ad te veniebant naves & nautæ mercaturæ causa.

## 27:10
Vers. 10.

THE PERSIANS AND LYDIANS AND LIBYANS WERE IN THY ARMY) In thy garrisons. Xenophon says that the Lydians flourished with military renown before the times of Croesus. The Libyans also, or Africans, were among the auxiliaries. Jerem. 49, 9. The Persians have been known for their arrows from every age.

THY MEN OF WAR) Mercenary soldiers, such as cities dedicated to trade use much, as also did the daughter of Tyre, Carthage.

THEY HANGED THE SHIELD AND HELMET IN THEE) Namely, those who were off duty from their watches.

FOR THY BEAUTY) In the Hebrew: They were an ornament to thee. It was magnificent for thee to have so many nations hired.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

PERSÆ ET LTDII ET LIBTES ERANT IN EXERCITV TVO) In Præsidiis tuis. Lydos ante Crœ- si tempora laude militari floruisse dicit Xenophon. Libyes quoque sive Afri in auxiliis erant. Jerem. 49, 9. Persiæ sa- gittis noti ab omni ævo.

VIRI BELLATORES TVI) Milites Mercenarii, qualibus multum utuntur civitates mercatui deditæ, ut & filia Tyri Carthago.

CLTPEVM ET GALEAM SVSPENDERVNT IN TE) Nempe qui eorum ab excubiis vacabant.

PRO ORNATV TVO) In Hebræo: Ipsi tibi e- rant decori. Magnificum erat tibi tot gentes habere con- ductas.

## 27:11
Verse 11.

THE SONS OF ARAD WITH THY ARMY WERE UPON THY WALLS ROUND ABOUT) That is, they were mingled with the city's soldiers. AND THE PYGMAEANS WHO WERE IN THY TOWERS HUNG THEIR QUIVERS UPON THY WALLS ROUND ABOUT) Well, if there was a war to be fought against cranes. Otherwise, why choose them for military service, whose whole cohort is not taller than one foot? The opinion of those who think the inhabitants of Ancon are meant, the Phoenicians, is probable: for Ancon is ענק. But the LXX, omitting the ע, read מדים, Medes. The Chaldean, however, the second letter having been changed, seems to have read גמרים. For he interprets it as Cappadocians. Aquila has πυγμαίες, but not from a cubit's stature, but rather, as Theodoret explains, ἀπὸ τῆς πυγμῆς, from the fist or skill in fighting. Junius, Tremellius, Piscator, the Italian and Genevan versions, the Dutch, and Sixtus. Amama interprets them as the Gammatheans or the people of Phoenicia, so called from the situation of the place, because their island is projected into the sea in the shape of a cubit, as Pliny testifies, book 2, chapter 21, 93.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

FILII ARADII CUM EXERCITU TUO E- RANT SUPER MUROS TUOS IN CIRCUITU) Id est, permixti erant urbano militi. ET PTGMÆI QUI ERANT IN TURRIBUS TUIS PHARETRAS SUSPENDERUNT IN MURIS TUIS PER GYRUM) Bene si cum gruibus bellandum fuit. Alioqui quorsum ad militiam deligere eos, Quorum tota cohors pede non est altior uno? Probabilis est eorum sententia, qui intelligi putant habi- tatores Anconis Phœnices: Nam Ancon est ענק. At LXX. ע omisso, legere מדים, μῆδοι. Chaldæus vero, secunda litera mutata, videtur legisse גמרים. Interpretatur enim Cappadoces. Aquila πυγμαίες habet, sed non à statura cu- bitali, verum ut Theodoret. exponit ἀπὸ τῆς πυ- γμῆς à pugno seu pugnandi peritia. Junius, Tre- mellius, Piscator, Ital. & Genev. versio, Belgæ, & Sixt. Amama Gammathæos seu populum Phœ- niciæ interpretantur, sic dictos à situ loci, quia Insula ipsorum in formam cubiti projecta in mare, teste Plin. l. 2. c. 21, 93.

## 27:12
Verse 12.

THE CARTHAGINIANS WERE THY MERCHANTS) תרשיש, we have noted elsewhere how those who are called Tartessians by the Greeks are named. But Carthage is near to them, whence the LXX placed 'Carthaginians' here, for which 'Chalcedonians' is wrongly written in some codices. WITH SILVER) Silver is most beautiful in Spain. Pliny 32, 6. WITH IRON) Martial: The dagger which the short curved orbit of Sena marks: the soil tempered this hissing one with cold waters. The glory of Bilbilis is ennobled by iron. Pliny 34, 14. WITH TIN) It is born with silver. Pliny 34, 16. AND WITH LEAD) Opposite Celtiberia there are many islands, called the Cassiterides by the Greeks from the fertility of lead. Pliny 4, 22. Mela has the same in book 5, 3. THEY FILLED THY FAIRS) They placed in thy storehouses, the Chaldean: which I praise. For עזב is to close.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

CARTHAGINENSES NEGOTIATORES TUI) תרשיש, quomodo vocari illos qui Tartessii dicuntur Græcis notavimus alibi. Illis autem vicina Carthago, unde LXX. καρχηδόνιοι hic posuere, pro quo male scribitur in quibusdam codicibus χαλκηδόνιοι. ARGENTO) Argentum in Hispania pulcherri- mum. Plin. 32, 6. FERRO) Martialis: Pugio quem curva signat brevis orbita Sena: Stridentem gelidis hunc sola tinxit aquis. Bilbilis gloria ferri nobilitatæ. Plin. 34, 14. STANNO) Nascitur cum argento. Plinius 34, 16. PLUMBOQVE) Ex adverso Celtiberiæ complu- res sunt insulæ, Cassiterides dictæ à Græcis à fertilitate plumbi. Plin. 4, 22. Idem habet Mela lib. 5, 3. REPLEVERUNT NUNDINAS TUAS) Posuerunt in apothecis tuis, Chaldæus: quod laudo. Nam עזב est claudere.

## 27:13
Verse 13.

GREECE) Ionia יון. THUBAL) The Asiatic Iberians, and Albanians, whose city Thabilaca is mentioned by Ptolemy. We spoke of this in the first book on the truth of the Christian Religion. AND MOSOCH) The Cappadocians, whose city is Mazaca, along with the Moschi or Moscheni. We spoke of this in the same place. THEY WERE THY MERCHANTS) They traded with thee. PERSONS) In the souls of men. But you should know that household slaves are spoken of in this way: and do not take it otherwise, ψυχαὶ ἀνθρώπων, Rev. 18:13. Thus also for the later Greeks, ψυχάρια are slaves, as Meursius, who deserved well of those letters, noted. For the word σωμάτων, which precedes in the Apocalypse, is to be referred to free men who either prostituted themselves for a price or surrendered themselves to the arena; for Pollux says that σώματα, without an addition, is not used for slaves. AND THEY BROUGHT BRASS VESSELS TO THY PEOPLE) To thy market: מערבך. Thus the Greeks and the Chaldean. The Latin seems to have read מעמך. The fame of brass in Asia. Pliny 34, 2. OF THE HOUSE OF THOGORMA) You will understand that it was a region near Galatia from those things which are below in 38:6. Josephus interprets them as Phrygians, to whom the city of Mysia, Germa, is near according to Ptolemy, as also in Galatia, Germanopolis. And it is clear that the Chaldean meant nothing else, who placed here גרממיא. The Jewish Rabbis call the Turks תורגמים, namely because the Turks first began to appear to the men of the Roman Empire around those parts, which is most true. See Chalcocondylas and Leunclavius.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

GRÆCIA) Jonia יון. THUBAL) Iberi Asiatici, & Albani, quorum urbs Thabilaca apud Ptolemæum. Diximus ad librum primum de veritate Religionis Christianæ. ET MOSOCH) Cappadoces, quorum urbs Ma- zaca, cum Moschis sive Moschenis. Diximus ibidem. IPSI INSTITORES TUI) Tecum negotia- bantur. MANCIPIA) In animabus hominum. Sed noris ita dici servulos vernas: neque vero aliter accipe, ψυχαὶ ἀνθρώπων Apoc. 18, 13. Sic & Græcis posterioribus ψυχάρια sunt servi, ut notavit bene de illis literis meritus Meursius. Nam vox σωμάτων, quæ in Apocalypsi præcedit, referenda ad ingenuos, qui pretio se aut prostituebant, aut addicebant arenæ; quippe σώματα, sine additamento, de servis non dici ait Pollux. ET VASA ÆREA ADDUXERUNT POPULO TUO) Mercatui tuo: מערבך. Sic Græci & Chaldæus. Vi- detur Latinus legisse מעמך. Celebritas æris in Asia. Pli- nius 34, 2. DE DOMO THOGORMA) Fuisse regionem Ga- latiæ propinquam intelliges ex his quæ infra 38, 6. Jose- phus Phrygas interpretatur, quibus vicina urbs Mysiæ Germa Ptolemæo, ut & in Galatia Germanopolis. Nec aliud voluisse Chaldæum patet, qui hic posuit גרממיא- Ju- dæi Rabbini Turcas vocant תורגמים, nempe quod Turcæ primum circa illas partes apparere Romani Imperii homi- nibus cœperint, quod verissimum. Vide Chalcocondylam ac Leunclavium.

## 27:14
Verse 14.

HORSES AND HORSEMEN) Claudian on the horse of Arcadius: Whether the grasses in the Armenian fields nourished him, or the turbulent Halys washed him with Argæan snow. AND MULES) They are best from the wild ass and the she-ass. Wild asses are especially found in Phrygia and Lycaonia. Pliny 117, 44 records both.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

EQVOS ET EQVITES) Claudianus de equo Arcadii: Sive illum Armeniis aluerunt gramina campis, Turbidus Argæa seu nive lavit Halys. ET MULOS) Optimi sunt ex Onagro & Asina. O- nagri in Phrygia & Lycaonia præcipui. Utrumque tradit Plinius 117, 44.

## 27:15
Verse 15.

THE SONS OF DEDAN WERE THY MERCHANTS) The LXX: υἱοὶ ῥοδίων: for they read רדן, as also in Gen. 10:4. But from the wares which are named immediately, it is credible that those mentioned in Gen. 10:4 are not meant, but others situated in Arabia, and descended from Keturah, Gen. 25:2. Their city is Thoata according to Ptolemy.

Jerome rightly corrects the LXX interpreters; Villalpandus foolishly defends them, having invented the idea that the island of Rhodes was once called Dedan.

MANY ISLANDS) Many inhabitants of the Red Sea. THE TRADING OF THY HANDS) That is, they came to buy the works of thy hands.

IVORY TEETH) In the Hebrew: horns of the tooth. And indeed, what we call elephant's teeth, King Juba called horns, as Pliny testifies. But the Chaldean distinguishes, and by horns understands the horns of wild goats, from which the Talmudists relate that trumpets were made: by teeth, ivory. These wild goats lived in the rocks, whence there were many such in Arabia. There were also many elephants among the Troglodytes. Pliny mentions this in more than one place.

AND EBONY) He followed the sound of the Hebrew word הובנים. But the Chaldean interprets it as peacocks, which it is established were brought to the Red Sea from 2 Chronicles 9:21.

THEY EXCHANGED IN THY PRICE) They rendered to thee in return for the price: namely, to compensate for those works of the Tyrians. In an exchange, both are merchandise and price: but that is called merchandise whose use is more frequent.

The Hebrew word שכר (inebriated) reproaches the Tyrians for their gluttony, because they spent their wealth on intoxicating drink. The LXX, reading Sin for Schin, rendered it as wages.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

FILII DEDAN NEGOTIATORES TUI) LXX. υἱοὶ ῥοδίων: legerunt enim רדן, ut & Gen. 10, 4. sed ex mer- cibus quæ statim nominantur, credibile est non illos Gen. 10, 4. dictos intelligi, sed alios in Arabia positos, & ortos ex Cethura Gen. 25, 2. Horum urbs Θοάτα Ptolemæo.

Recte LXX. Interpp. castigat Hieron. inepte tuetur Vilalpandus, Rhodum insulam olim Dedan dictam commentus.

INSULAE MULTAE) Multi accolae mari rubri. NEGOTIATIO MANUS TUAE) Id est, veniebant emptum, manus tuae opera.

DENTES EBURNEOS) In Hebraeo: cornua dentis. Et sane quos dentes Elephanti dicimus, eos Rex Juba dice- bat cornua, teste Plinio. At Chaldaeus distinguit, & per cornua intelligit cornua caprearum, ex quibus buccinas fa- ctas narrant Thalmudici: per dentes, Ebur. Vivebant istae capreae in rupibus, unde multae tales in Arabia. Elephan- tes quoque multi apud Troglodytas. Meminit Plinius non uno loco.

ET HEBENINOS) Sonum secutus est vocis He- braeae הובנים. At Chaldaeus pavos interpretatur, quos in Rubrum mare advectos constat ex 2. Paral. 9, 21.

COMMUTAVERUNT IN PRETIO TUO) Red- diderunt tibi pro pretio: nempe ad repensanda illa opera Tyriorum. In permutatione utrumque & merx est & pretium: sed merx dicitur, cujus usus est frequentior.

Verbum Ebr. שכר inebriavit ingluviem Tyriis exprobat, quod divitias suas pro potu inebrian- te erogarint. LXX. Sin pro Schin legentes merce- dem reddidere.

## 27:16
Verse 16.

SYRIA WAS THY MERCHANT BY REASON OF THE MULTITUDE OF THY WORKS) In order to acquire for himself the works made by thee, he brought to thee his merchandise, which will now be mentioned. The Syrians were great merchants, as Jerome notes here. Horace: 'to exchange with Syrian merchandise.' The LXX, instead of אדם, wrongly read ארם, which Jerome also observes.

GEM) A carbuncle, as in Exodus 28:18.

AND BROIDERED WORK) Needle-painted: as the Chaldean has it here: so also Exodus 35:23, 38:33. See also Exodus 26:36, 28:39, 36:35, 38:18, 39:29, Judges 5:30.

AND BYSSUS) It corresponds to the Hebrew בוץ, which the Greeks translate as Byssus both here and elsewhere: the Chaldean adds an epithet of color, because it is more precious.

AND SILK) ראמת are corals, as stated in Job 27:18.

AND THEY OFFERED CHOLCHOD IN THEIR MARKET.) He retained the word, which is in the Hebrew text, as did the Greeks. Most wish it to be a type of stone. Let us see whether it is the same stone which in the Apocalypse is called χαλκηδὼν, and commonly now also Chalcedony.

Jerome in this place confesses that he could not find what Cholcod signifies: but that the Hebrews say that all most precious wares are signified by this name; or that it is a certain species of most precious wares, which the Roman language does not echo.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

SYRUS NEGOTIATOR TUUS PROPTER MULTITUDINEM OPERUM TUORUM) Ut opera abs te facta sibi compararet, merces suas, quae jam di- centur, tibi attulit. Syri magni negotiatores, ut hic no- tat Hieronymus. Horatius: Syra reparare merce. LXX. pro אדם male legere ארם, quod & idem observat Hiero- nymus.

GEMMAM) Carbunculum, ut Exod. 28, 18.

ET SCUTULATA) Acu picta: quomodo hic Chal- daeus: Sic & Exod. 35, 23.38, 33. Vide & Exod. 26, 36. 28, 39. 36, 35. 38, 18. 39, 29. Jud. 5, 30.

ET BYSSUM) Respondet Hebraeo בוץ quod Bys- sum vertunt Graeci & hic & alibi: discoloris επίθετον addit Chaldaeus, quod ea pretiosior.

ET SERICUM) ראמת sunt coralia, ut dictum Job. 27, 18.

ET CHOLCHOD PROPOSUERUNT IN MER- CATU SUO.) Retinuit vocem, quae est in textu Hebraeo, ut & Graeci. Lapidis esse genus plerique volunt. Videa- mus an idem sit lapis, qui in Apocalypsi dicitur χαλκηδὼν, & vulgo nunc quoque Chalcedonius.

Hieron. in h. l. fatetur se invenire non po- tuisse, quid Cholcod significet: Ebraeos autem dicere, omnes pretiosissimas merces hoc nomine significari; vel speciem quandam esse pretiosissi- marum mercium, quam Romanus sermo non re- sonet.

## 27:17
Ver. 17.

IN THE FIRST WHEAT) That is, the best, as the Chaldean has it, so called from the region Minnith named in Jud. 11, 33, which is at the border of the Ammonites.

B. Hülsemann prefers to take it appellatively concerning the best wheat, for since kingdoms are distinguished by native wares, this wheat cannot derive its denomination from a field situated outside Judea among the Ammonites.

BALSAM) In Hebrew it is צרי, which is Balsam also to the Chaldeans. Μύρον to the Greeks. David Kimchi, who said it was a sweet herb, I do not doubt had in mind the panax, which whether it was already known in the time of Ezekiel, can be doubted. Others think that a ware is not signified, but a region, like Minnith, from where the wheat came. If it is a region, it will be none other than Phoenice, as that which was the land of כנען to the Hebrews and to the Phoenicians themselves was already called by the Greeks at that time. That many Greek words had penetrated into the East at this time will appear from Daniel. Pliny praises Syrian wheat.

But why should the vulgate interpretation not be retained? Which not only the Chaldean, the LXX, but also Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion, and Luther approve, along with St. Jerome. Because that oil is native only to Judea, as attested by Pliny book 12, chapter 15, Josephus book 8, Antiquities chapter 2, and Jerome in Exodus 28, he noted as an author, that the blood of Christ as balsam and an antidote for sins was to be poured out in that region.

AND RESIN) For medicines for wounds. See Jer. 8, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

IN FRUMENTO PRIMO) Id est, optimo, ut ha- bet Chaldaeus, ita dicto a regione Minnith nominata Jud. 11, 33. est ad finem Ammonitarum.

B. Hülsem. mavult appellative accipere de o- ptimo frumento, quum enim regna a mercibus nativis distinguantur, non posse hoc triticum ab agro extra Judaeam inter Ammonitas sito denomi- nationem fortiri.

BALSAMUM) In Hebraeo est צרי, quod Balsamum etiam Chaldaeis. Μύρον Graeci. David Kimchi, qui herbam dulcem esse dixit, non dubito quin in animo habuerit pa- nici, quae an jam Ezechielis tempore cognita fuerit, dubi- tari potest. Alii putant non mercem fingnificari, sed regio- nem, ut Minnith, unde frumentum venerit. Si regio est, alia non erit quam Phoenice, quomodo Graecis vocabatur jam eo tempore ea, quae terra כנען Hebraeis & ipsis Phoe- nicibus. Multa autem Graeca vocabula in orientem hoc tempore penetrasse ex Daniele apparebit. Triticum Syrium laudat Plinius.

Cur vero non retineatur vulgata interpreta- tio? quam non modo Chald. LXX. sed etiam A- quila, Symmachus, Theodotion, Luther. probant, cum S. Hieronymo. Quod oleum soli Judaeae nati- vum teste Plinio l. 12. c. 15. Joseph. l. 8. Ant. c. 2. Hieronymo in Exod. 28. autore notavit, sangui- nem Christi ceu balsamum & alexipharmacon peccatorum in ista regione effundendum.

ET RESINAM) Ad vulnerum medicamenta. Vide Jer. 8, 22.

## 27:18
Verse 18.

IN THE MULTITUDE OF THY WORKS) For comparing the works which are done at Tyre.

IN THE MULTITUDE OF VARIOUS WEALTH) And for comparing monies.

IN FAT WINE) The Greeks, considering it a proper noun, placed οἶνον ἐκ Χελβὼν: that is, from Chalybonitis, as Ptolemy names that part of Syria, with the כ changed into ח, a letter of similar sound and shape.

IN WOOLS OF THE BEST COLOR) Jerome in his Commentaries thinks it was the proper name Soor, from where wool was brought similar to Milesian, which name the LXX placed here. He adds: It signifies, however, that among the other trades of Tyre, the richest wine and excellent wool were brought to its markets from Damascus, which we see even to this day. Soor in Ptolemy is Σούρα.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

IN MULTITUDINE OPERUM TVORVM) Ad comparanda opera quæ Tyri fiunt.

IN MULTITUDINE DIVERSARVM OPUM) Et ad pecunias comparandas.

IN VINO PINGVI) Græci vocem propriam censentes posuere οἶνον ἐκ Χελβὼν: id est, ex Chalybonitide, ut Ptolemæus illam Syriæ partem nominat, כ mutato in ח, vicini soni, ductusque literam.

IN LANIS COLORIS OPTIMI) Hieronymus in Commentariis nomen censet esset proprium Soor, unde lana afferebatur similis Milesiæ, quod nomen posuere hic LXX. Addit: Significat autem quod inter cæteras negotiationes Tyri, ad nundinas ejus de Damasco deferebatur vinum pinguissimum, & lana præcipua, quod usque hodie cernimus. Soor apud Ptolemæum est Σούρα.

## 27:19
Verse 19.

DAN AND GREECE AND MOSEL IN THY MARKETS SET FORTH WROUGHT IRON) In the Greek [texts], which we use, it is Δὰν καὶ Ἰαυὰν καὶ Μοόζηλ. But Jerome relates that these were missing in the LXX, but were added from Theodotion. Certainly Dan can hardly have a place here for Israel, the ten tribes having been led away long ago: and the mention of Greece has already preceded, which that Theodotion did not understand here is apparent from the fact that, above, for יון he placed Ἑλλάς, but here Ἰαυὰν, as we have said. Then indeed he would be much mistaken who seeks stacte or aromatic reed either in the land of Israel or in Greece. Theodotion takes Moozel as a proper name: the Chaldean takes it as a common noun, who translates it in troops: that is, for caravans, from אזל which is to make a journey. I would believe that Taprobane is indicated here, that is, the island of Ceylon, fertile in aromatic reed, and other scents, and not lacking in metals, in which there were the cities of Dana and Ioganna and Modutu, as Ptolemy has it, where perhaps it should be written Μοδόυλα.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

DAN ET GRÆCIA ET MOSEL IN NVNDINIS TVIS PROPOSVERVNT FERRVM FABREFACTVM) In Græcis, quibus nos utimur, est Δὰν καὶ Ἰαυὰν καὶ Μοόζηλ. At ista in LXX. defuisse, adjecta vero ex Theodotione narrat Hieronymus. Certe Dan Israelis locum habere hic vix potest, deductis pridem decem tribubus: & Græciæ mentio jam præcessit, quam hic non intellexisse Theodotionem, hinc apparet quod, supra pro יון posuit Ἑλλάς, hic vero Ἰαυὰν, ut diximus. Tum vero multum fallatur, qui stacten sive calamum aromaticum, aut in Israelis terra aut in Græcia quærat. Moozel pro nomine proprio sumit Theodotio: pro communi Chaldæus, qui vertit turmatim: id est, pro caravanas, ab אזל quod est iter facere. Credam ego Taprobanen hic indicari, id est, Zeilanam insulam, feracem calami odoriferi, & odorum aliorum, & metallorum non inopem, in qua fuere urbes Dana & Ioganna & Modutu, ut habet Ptolemæus, ubi forte scribendum Μοδόυλα.

## 27:20
Verse 20.

DEDAN THY MERCHANTS IN CLOTHS FOR SITTING) The Chaldean translates for riding, that is, for horse-blankets. This is a different Dedan from the one above in [verse] 15. That one [was] from Keturah, this one from the sons of Cush. Gen. 10, 7. The names which follow here show this, which also cohere with the name of Dedan in Genesis. Both are peoples in Arabia, but at a long distance. Of these seems to be Adidos, a village in Ptolemy.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

DEDAN INSTITORES TVI IN TAPETIBVS AD SEDENDUM) Ad equitandum vertit Chaldæus, id est, ad strata equorum. Est hic alius Dedan ab illo qui supra 15. Ille ex Cethura, hic ex Chusi filiis. Gen. 10, 7. Ostendunt id nomina quæ hic sequuntur, quæ & in Genesi nomini Dedanis cohærent. Sunt in Arabia utrique populi, sed longo intervallo. Horum videtur esse Αδίδος, vicus apud Ptolemæum.

## 27:21
Verse 21.

PRINCES OF KEDAR) The Kedarites. See Psalm 120:5, Jeremiah 49:28.

WITH LAMBS, AND RAMS, AND GOATS THEY CAME UNTO THEE) For that region, which in Jerome's time was called the land of the Saracens, abounds in livestock. See also Jeremiah 49:29.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

PRINCIPES CEDAR) Cedareni. Vide Psalm 120, 5. Jerem. 49, 28.

CVM AGNIS, ET ARIETIBVS, ET HOEDIS VENERVNT AD TE) Abundat enim pecore regio illa, quæ Saracenorum Hieronymi tempore dicebatur. Vide & Jerem. 49, 29.

## 27:22
V. 22. THE MERCHANTS OF SHEBA AND RAAMAH) These are peoples of Arabia Felix, where Regma is found in Ptolemy, with the ע changed into a γ, and the town of Saba.

WITH ALL THE CHIEF SPICES) Especially frankincense.

AND PRECIOUS STONE) Such as Lygdinus. Pliny 36:8.

AND GOLD) Of which there is a great abundance among the Arabs, 2 Chronicles 9:14.

Latin:

V. 22. VENDITORES SABA ET REEMA) Ethi populi Arabiæ felicis, ubi Regma Ptolemæo ע in γ mutato, & Saba oppidum.

CVM VNIVERSIS PRIMIS AROMATIBVS) Thure maxime.

ET LAPIDE PRETIOSO) Ut Lygdino. Plinius 36, 8.

ET AVRO) Cujus magna penes Arabes copia 2. Paralip. 9, 14.

## 27:23
Ver. 23.

HARAN) Carrhae, as we have said in the first book on the truth of the Christian religion.

AND CANNEH) In the Hebrew word כנה, either the letter ל was omitted through the carelessness of a scribe, or the pronunciation changed over time. For neighboring places show it to be the same as Calneh, Genesis 10:10 and Amos 6:2, which it is highly credible from Ammianus is Callinicum.

That the pronunciation has changed can be admitted. That a letter was dropped through the carelessness of a scribe should not be admitted. Others think it is a different city. The Septuagint judged it to be the land of Canaan, as their reading now has it. Theodoret, however, read Chalam, and thought it was the place where the tower was built. Jerome took it for a certain province of Mesopotamia, which is called Chalcetis. Villalpandus thinks the name comes from the celebrity of the name.

AND EDEN) It is a part of Babylonia. See what we wrote on Genesis 2.

SHEBA) This Sheba (שבא) is also different from that one above in verse 22; that one is named in Genesis 10:7, but this one in Genesis 25:3. In Pliny, the port of Sheba in Arabia on the sea, 5:23, which Strabo also mentions. Elsewhere the Sabaeans are noble for frankincense, 6:28; Ptolemy also distinguishes them.

ASSUR) Affurii. AND CHELMAD) The Chaldean interprets it as Media. It is a compound word, and I do not think any other place is designated than Gaala of Media, named by Ptolemy. Certain Greek codices have Χαρμὰν, that is, Carmani.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

HARAN) Carræ, ut diximus ad librum primum de veritate religionis Christianæ.

ET CHENE) In Hebræa voce כנה, aut litera ל per scribæ incuriam omissa est, aut cum tempore mutata pronunciatio. Ostendunt enim vicina loca idem esse quod כלנה Gen. 10, 10. & Amos 6, 2. quod esse Callinisum Ammiano perquam credibile est.

Pronunciationem mutatam esse, admitti potest. Excidisse literam per scribæ incuriam, admitti non debet. Alii aliam urbem esse putant. LXX. terram Chanaan esse censuerunt, uti nunc eorum lectio habet. Theodoretus tamen legit Chalam, & putavit locum esse, ubi turris ædificata fuit. Hieronymus habuit pro provincia quadam Mesopotamiæ, quæ chalcetis vocatur. Villalpandus putat appellationem esse à celebritate nominis.

ET EDEN) Pars est Babyloniæ. Vide quæ ad 2. Geneseos.

SABA) Hic quoque שבא diversus ab illo qui supra v. 22. ille nominatus Gen. 10, 7. hic vero Gen. 25, 3. Plinio Sabæ portus Arabiæ ad mare 5, 23. cujus & Strabo meminit. Alibi Sabæi thure nobiles 6, 28, distinguit & Ptolemæus.

ASSUR) Affurii. ET CHELMAD) Mediam interpretatur Chaldæus. Est vox composita, nec alium locum designari puto, quam Gaala Mediæ Ptolemæo nominata. Græci quidam codices Χαρμὰν habent, id est, Carmani.

## 27:24
Verse 24.

THY MERCHANTS THEMSELVES IN MANY WAYS WITH WRAPPINGS OF HYACINTH) The LXX here retained two Hebrew words, ἐν Μοχαλὴμ καὶ Γαλίμε. I approve the Chaldean version: in most perfect things, namely in hyacinthine cloaks, etc., from which Aquila and Symmachus did not depart, as we know from Jerome and Theodotion. AND OF EMBROIDERED WORK) And needle-painted. AND OF PRECIOUS TREASURES) And with collections of precious garments. גנזי from גנז which is to store away. Joseph Kimchi says that כרומים are also precious garments to the Arabs. WHICH WERE WRAPPED AND BOUND WITH CORDS) In the Hebrew: bound with cords: namely, likewise precious, that is, of fine linen, as the Chaldean wishes. THEY SHALL ALSO HAVE CEDARS) And with cedars, that is, in cedar chests, so that they might last longer. The Chaldean placed myrtle chests. IN THY MERCHANDISE) For thy market.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

IPSI NEGOTIATORES TUI MULTIFARIAM INVOLUCRIS HYACINTHI) LXX. hic voces duas He- bræas retinuere, ἐν Μοχαλὴμ καὶ Γαλίμε. Probo Chaldæi ver- sionem: in rebus perfectissimis, nempe in palliis hyacinthinis, &c. à qua non abiere Aquila & Symmachus, ut ex Hieronymo & Theodotione cognoscimus. ET POLYMITORUM) Et acupictis. GAZARUMQVE PRETIOSARUM) Et Synthesi- bus vestium pretiosarum. גנזי à גנז quod est reponere. כרומים etiam Arabibus esse vestes pretiosas, ait Joseph Kimchi. QVÆ OBVOLUTÆ ET ASTRICTÆ ERANT FUNIBUS) In Hebræo: ligatarum funibus: nempe itidem pretiosis, id est, byssinis, ut vult Chaldæus. CEDROS QVOQVE HABEBUNT) Et cedris, id est, in capsis cedrinis, quo magis durarent. Myrtinas capsas posuit Chaldæus. IN NEGOTIATIONIBUS TUIS) Ad mercatum tuum.

## 27:25
Verse 25.

SHIPS OF THE SEA) In the Hebrew: תרשיש: that is, of the Ocean. PRINCES IN THY MERCHANDISE) Chief to thee in thy merchandise: For there is a feminine word in the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

NAVES MARIS) In Hebræo: תרשיש: id est, Oceani. PRINCIPES IN NEGOTIATIONE TUA) Præ- cipuæ tibi in negotiatione tua: Est enim in Hebræo vox fe- minina.

## 27:26
Verse 26.

THY ROWERS HAVE BROUGHT THEE INTO MANY WATERS) Comparing the city to a ship, as Horace does Rome, he says it has been led into a very turbulent sea. The rowers are men of the common people. The sea is the war with the Chaldeans. THE SOUTH WIND) In the Hebrew: Eastern. That wind signifies the Chaldeans coming from the East.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

IN AQVIS MULTIS ADDUXERUNT TE RE- MIGES TUI) Urbem navi comparans, ut Romam Ho- ratius, ait eam perductam in mare valde fluctuosum. Remi- ges sunt homines de plebe. Mare, bellum cum Chaldæis. VENTUS AUSTER) In Hebræo: Orientalis. Is ventus Chaldæos significat ab Oriente venientes.

## 27:27
Verse 27.

WHO HELD THY FURNITURE) In the Hebrew: who mend thy rents. As above 9. AND WERE OVER THY PEOPLE) In the Hebrew: The handlers of thy business: that is, the agents and masters. THEY SHALL FALL IN THE HEART OF THE SEA) They shall fall in the slaughter of war.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

QVI TENEBANT SUPELLECTILEM TUAM) In Hebræo: qui scissuras tuas sarciunt. Ut supra 9. ET POPULO TUO PRÆERANT) In Hebræo: Tractatores negotiorum tuorum: id est, institores & magistri. CADENT IN CORDE MARIS) Bellica clade con- cident.

## 27:28
Verse 28.

AT THE SOUND OF THE CRY OF THY PILOTS THE FLEETS SHALL BE TROUBLED) The suburbs shall tremble. So great will be the cry of those who will be wounded in the sea by the Chaldeans and their Phoenician allies, that not only the island of Tyre, but also the nearby mainland, hearing it, shall tremble.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

A SONITU CLAMORIS GUBERNATORUM TUORUM CONTURBABUNTUR CLASSES) Contre- miscent suburbana. Tantus erit clamor eorum, qui in mari à Chaldæis eorumque sociis Phœnicibus vulnerabuntur, ut non insula tantum Tyros, sed & proxima continens, eo audito contremiscat.

## 27:29
Verse 29.

AND ALL WHO HELD THE OAR SHALL DESCEND FROM THEIR SHIPS) That is, they will all betake themselves into the boats, so that they may reach land as soon as possible, and thus escape the evil. THEY SHALL STAND ON THE LAND) As if cast out. To stand on the land is the gesture of mourners lowering themselves from a higher place to a lower one. See Is. 47, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ET DESCENDENT DE NAVIBUS SUIS O- MNES QVI TENEBANT REMUM) Id est, omnes in scaphas se dabunt, ut terram quamprimum arripiant, & sic malum evadant. IN TERRA STABUNT) Velut ejecti. In terra stare gestus lugentium demittentium sese ex loco superiori in interiorem. Vid. Es. 47, 1.

## 27:30
Vers. 30.

AND THEY SHALL CAST DUST UPON THEIR HEADS AND SHALL BE SPRINKLED WITH ASHES) A custom of those mourning, Joshua 7, 6. Job 2, 12. Jerem. 6, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

ET SUPERJACIENT PULVEREM CAPITIBUS SUIS ET CINERE CONSPERGENTUR) Mos dolen- tium Josuæ 7, 6. Job. 2, 21. Jerem. 6, 26.

## 27:31
Vers. 31.

AND THEY SHALL SHAVE BALDNESS OVER THEE) After the manner of the Phoenicians, Deut. 14, 1. AND THEY SHALL BE GIRDED WITH SACKCLOTH) With the vilest clothing. And this is a custom of the East. Jonah 3, 6. שקים The Latin calls them sometimes sacks, sometimes haircloth. It matters little. See what was said at Matt. 11, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

ET RADENT SUPER TE CALVITIUM) Mo- re Phœnicum Deut. 14, 1. ET ACCINGENTUR CILICIIS) Vestitu vilissimo. Et hic mos Orientis. Jonæ 2, 6. שקים Latinus modo sac- cos vocat, modo cilicia. Parum refert. Vide quæ dicta Matth. 11, 21.

## 27:32
Vers. 32.

AND THEY SHALL TAKE UP A MOURNFUL SONG OVER THEE) They shall lift up a lamentation over thee in their complaints. But the LXX, with different pointing, interpret בניהם as οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν. WHO IS LIKE TYRE, WHICH HATH BEEN SILENCED IN THE MIDST OF THE SEA) Better: What city was like Tyre? What maritime city could be compared to it, so that it is רמה from דמה, not from דמם. It appears the Chaldean took it as we say, and the discourse coheres better: for in adverse fortune they commemorate that former state.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

ET ASSUMENT SUPER TE CARMEN LUGU- BRE) Tollent super te in querimonias suas lamentum. At LXX. aliis punctis בניהם interpretantur οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν. QVÆ EST UT TYRUS, QVÆ OBMUTUIT IN MEDIO MARIS) Melius: Quæ fuit urbs qualis Tyrus? quæ urbs maritima ei comparari potuit ut sit רמה à דמה non à דמם. Apparet Chaldæum sumpsisse ut dicimus, & oratio melius cohæret: nam in adversa fortuna commemo- rant illam priorem.

## 27:33
Vers. 33.

WHICH IN THE GOING FORTH OF THY MERCHANDISE) By long voyages into India, Spain, Africa, Pontus. THOU DIDST FILL MANY PEOPLES) With merchandise. WITH THE MULTITUDE OF THY RICHES) Of money.

AND OF THY PEOPLES) Of thy merchandise. THOU HAST ENRICHED THE KINGS OF THE EARTH) From the customs duties.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

QVÆ IN EXITU NEGOTIATIONUM TUA- RUM) Longinquis navigationibus in Indiam, Hispaniam, Africam, Pontum. IMPLESTI MULTOS POPULOS) Mercibus. MULTITUDINE DIVITIARUM TUARUM) Pecuniarum.

ET POPULORUM TUORUM) Mercimoniorum tuorum. DITASTI REGES TERRÆ) Ex vectigalibus.

## 27:34
Verse 34.

NOW THOU ART BROKEN BY THE SEA) See above v. 26. IN THE DEPTHS OF THE WATERS THY WEALTH) A great force of thy wealth is submerged in the sea. AND ALL THY MULTITUDE WHICH WAS IN THE MIDST OF THEE) The Chaldean: Thy army: that is: the marines.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

NUNC CONTRITA ES A MARI) Vide supra v. 26. IN PROFUNDIS AQVARUM OPES TUÆ) Magna vis opum tuarum in mari demersa est. ET OMNIS MULTITUDO TUA QVÆ ERAT IN MEDIO TUO) Chaldæus: Exercitus tuus: id est: milites Epibatæ.

## 27:35
Verse 35. ALL THE INHABITANTS OF THE ISLANDS) Of the maritime regions. AND THEIR KINGS STRUCK WITH A STORM) With bristling hair: thus the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 35. OMNES HABITATORES INSULARUM) Regionum maritimarum. ET REGES EORUM TEMPESTATE PERCUL- SI) Horrentibus pilis: ita Hebræum.

## 27:36
Verse 36. THEY HAVE HISSED AT THEE) Out of astonishment, as 1 Kings 9:8. THOU ART BROUGHT TO NOTHING) Namely, if this state is compared with the former. THOU SHALT NOT BE FOREVER) עד עולם is for a long time, as we have also noted elsewhere, and Jerome here. Not only a long time, but perpetuity is inferred by the literal sense.

Latin:

Vers. 36. SIBILAVERUNT SUPER TE) Præ stupore, ut 1. Reg. 9, 8. AD NIHILUM REDACTA ES) Nempe si com- paretur hic status cum priore. NON ERIS USQVE IN PERPETUUM) עד עולם est ad longum tempus, ut & nos annotavimus alibi, & hic Hieronymus. Non longum tantum tempus, sed perpetuitas τῷ ῥητῷ infertur.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII. The ruin of the King of Tyre, previously exalted in greatest glory, on account of his excessive pride and other iniquities, as also the devastation of Sidon, and likewise the restoration of the children of Israel, their enemies having been devastated.

Verse 1.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVIII. Ruina Regis Tyri maxima gloria prius exalta- ti, ob nimiam ipsius superbiam, aliasque ini- quitates, ut & vastatio Sidonis, nec non redu- ctio filiorum Israel hostibus eorum vastatis.

Vers. 1.

## 28:2
SAY TO THE PRINCE OF TYRE) To Ithobal. For so he is called in the Tyrian records. The foolish Rabbis imagined that Hiram lived for a thousand years, as Jerome notes here.

Verse 2.

AND THOU HAST SAID: I AM GOD) That is, as if a certain God, as Isaiah 14:4. AND I HAVE SAT IN THE CHAIR OF GOD IN THE HEART OF THE SEA) Again, understand 'as if'. Just as God is safe from every injury in a heavenly citadel, so the sea defends me. WHEN THOU ART MAN) Subject to every human lot. AND NOT GOD) By no means impregnable. THOU HAST GIVEN THY HEART AS THE HEART OF GOD) Thou thinkest of thyself as if all things ought to obey thee.

Latin:

DIC PRINCIPI TYRI) Ithobalo. Ita enim voca- tur in actis Tyriis. Stolidi Rabbini Hiramum fingebant per mille annos vixisse, ut hic notat Hieronymus.

Vers. 2.

ET DIXISTI: DEUS EGO SUM) Id est, quasi Deus quidam, ut Esa. 14, 4. ET IN CATHEDRA DEI SEDI IN CORDE MARIS) Rursum subintellige quasi. Sicut Deus ab omni injuria tutus est in arce cœlesti, sic me defendit mare. CUM SIS HOMO) Omni humanæ sorti obnoxius. ET NON DEUS) Minime inexpugnabilis. DEDISTI COR TUUM QVASI COR DEI) Ita de te cogitas, quasi omnia tibi parere debeant.

## 28:3
Verse 3.

BEHOLD THOU ART WISER THAN DANIEL) So thou seemest to thyself. The fame of Daniel was celebrated then throughout Chaldea. Above 14:20. Dan. 1:17. 2:48. 6:26.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ECCE SAPIENTIOR ES TU DANIELE) Ita ti- bi videris. Celebris erat tunc per Chaldæam fama Danie- lis. Supra 14, 20. Dan. 1, 17. 2, 48. 6, 26.

## 28:4
Verse 4.

YOU HAVE MADE STRENGTH FOR YOURSELF) You have acquired wealth.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

FECISTI TIBI FORTITUDINEM) Opes parasti.

## 28:7
Verse 7.

THE MOST ROBUST OF THE NATIONS) Such as the Chaldeans were then, above 26. 7. THEY SHALL DRAW THEIR SWORDS AGAINST THE BEAUTY OF YOUR WISDOM) Against the most beautiful buildings, which you constructed with great art. AND THEY SHALL POLLUTE YOUR COMELINESS) Your splendor: that is, your kingdom. THEY SHALL KILL AND DRAG YOU DOWN) They shall make you descend to the depths, that is, to the bottom of the sea, in a naval battle.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ROBUSTISSIMOS GENTIUM) Quales tunc erant Chaldæi, supra 26. 7. NUDABUNT GLADIOS SUOS SUPER PUL- CHRITUDINEM SAPIENTIÆ TUÆ) Super pulcherri- ma ædificia, quæ magna arte struxisti. ET POLLUAM DECOREM TUUM) Splendo- rem tuum: id est regnum tuum. INTERFICIENT ET DETRAHENT TE) Ad ima descendere te facient, id est, ad fundum maris, in navali prælio.

## 28:9
Verse 9.

WILL YOU SAY WHEN YOU SPEAK) Will you then say, SINCE YOU ARE A MAN) ---- Death alone confesses how small are the little bodies of men.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

NUMQVID DICENS LOQVERIS) An tunc dices, CUM SIS HOMO) ---- Mors sola fatetur Quantula sint hominum corpuscula.

## 28:10
Verse 10.

YOU SHALL DIE THE DEATH OF THE UNCIRCUMCISED) You mocked the circumcised: therefore I will that the uncircumcised bring death upon you: The death of the uncircumcised, as in Virgil: Slow from the wound of Ulysses; given by Ulysses.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

MORTE INCIRCUMCISORUM MORIERIS) Risisti circumcisos: ideo volo ut incircumcisi tibi mortem inferant: Mors in circumciforum, ut apud Virgilium: Vulnere tardus Ulyssi; ab Ulysse dato

## 28:12
Verse 12.

YOU ARE THE SEAL OF LIKENESS) A signet ring (excellently) figured. Elsewhere they translate חותם as δακτύλιον, elsewhere σφραγὶς, elsewhere ἀποσφράγισμα, with the same meaning. תכנית is figure. And thus the Chaldean takes it here: the sense is, you were guarded most diligently like a splendid ring of great art. Compare Jerem. 22, 24.

They wrongly interpret these things concerning the Devil: Origen hom. 13 on Ezech., Tertullian book 2 against Marcion ch. 10, Ambrose book 2 on Paradise, Augustine book 11 on Genesis literally ch. 22, Gregory book 28 of Morals ch. 18, and others, especially Jerome on ch. 14 of Isaiah and Epistle 146 to Damasus. Likewise the Papists, snatching these things to the Devil in an allegorical sense: For the whole chapter treats of the King of Tyre. Nothing here is about Satan.

FULL OF WISDOM) That is, made with art, as we have already said.

AS PERFECT IN BEAUTY) Shiningly beautiful.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

TU SIGNACULUM SIMILITUDINIS) Annulus signatorius (optime) figuratus. חותם alibi vertunt δακτύ- λιον, alibi σφραγὶς, alibi ἀποσφράγισμα, sensu eodem. תכנית figura. Et sic accipit hic Chaldæus: sensus est, di- ligentissime custodiebaris ut annulus splendidus multæ ar- tis. Confer Jerem. 24, 24.

Perperam de Diabolo hæc accipiunt Origenes hom. 13. in Ezech. Tertul. l. 2. c. Marcion. c. 10 Ambros. l. 2. de Parad. Augustin. l. 11. de Gen. ad liter. c. 22. Gregor. l. 28. Moral. c. 18. & alii, in- primis Hieronym. in c. 14. Ef. & Epist. 146. ad Damas. Papistæ item, sensu allegorico ad Diabo- lum hæc rapientes: Nam de Rege Tyri totum ca- put agit. Nihil hic de Satana.

PLENUS SAPIENTIA) Id est, arte factus, ut jam diximus.

UT PERFECTUS DECORE) Pulchrum fulgens.

## 28:13
Vers. 13.

IN THE DELIGHTS OF THE PARADISE OF GOD YOU WERE) Everything flowed to you, as once to Adam in the garden of Eden, which God had granted to him.

EVERY PRECIOUS STONE WAS YOUR COVERING) Your garment was interwoven with gems.

SARDIUS) אדם signifies red. Such, moreover, is the Indian Sardius in Pliny 37, 7. The Greeks also have σάρδιον here. The Chaldean has סמקן from סמק which means to be red.

TOPAZ) The Greeks translate פטרה as τοπάζιον, both in Exodus and in Job 28, 19. The Chaldean translates it ירקן. To them ירק means to be green. The Topaz is therefore Arabian, to which Pliny 37, 8 attributes a green color.

AND JASPER) יהלם is from הלם which means to break: therefore this name suits the diamond no less than the jasper. And the Chaldean interprets it as diamond both here and in Exodus. Arabian diamonds, according to Pliny 37, 7, so resist a blow that iron splits on both sides, and even the anvils themselves fly apart.

CHRYSOLITE) תרשיש is the Ocean and the color of the Ocean. This name suits the beryl very well, which imitates the greenness of the clear sea, Pliny 37, 5. The Greek interpreters vary: for they translate it as χρυσόλιθον, άνθρακα, ὑάκινθον.

AND ONYX) Almost all the Rabbis agree that the stone is in the shape of a human fingernail, that is, an onyx, and thus it is translated by the Greeks in Job 28, 16. And I prefer this to what is translated elsewhere as πράσινον, elsewhere σμάραγδος, elsewhere σάπφειρος, elsewhere σάρδιον, and elsewhere, as also by the Chaldeans, βηρύλλιον.

AND BERYL) ישפה in its very sound approaches jasper. And so the Greeks here. But elsewhere it is ὀνύχιον, the Chaldean פנתרין, that is, panther-like. I believe that kind of jasper is so called, which Pliny 38, 81 says is composed as if from many gems, from the panther, an animal of varied color.

SAPPHIRE) There is no doubt that it is σάπφειρος, with the name unchanged. And thus the Greeks translate it consistently in Exodus, Job, and elsewhere. Arabia retains the name, with a Nun interposed. سلفير

AND CARBUNCLE) Jerome also translates נפך as carbuncle in Exodus 28, 18, where it is also ἄνθραξ to the Greeks. The Hebrews say that נפך is black. But Pliny also says that Carchedonian carbuncles are of a blacker appearance.

AND SMARAGDUS) ברקת comes from ברק, which means to flash, to sparkle. That name would fit the Chrysolite best, which has a golden color; the Greeks, however, translate it as σμάραγδος and here ὀνύχιον. The Chaldean used a neighboring word ברקן which I see is taken for a carbuncle.

GOLD THE WORK OF THY BEAUTY, AND THY PERFORATIONS IN THE DAY THAT THOU WAST CREATED WERE PREPARED) Better thus: And gold, you may refer to the previous sense. Then translate with Symmachus: Thy timbrels, and thy perforations in the day that thou wast formed, had been prepared. When you were still being formed in the womb, even then were being prepared for you timbrels (so are called the pearls which have only one face, and from it a roundness, with a flatness on the reverse, according to Pliny 9, 35) and perforated ones, that is, strings of pearls, as Scaevola and Martial call them. Similar is that of Claudian concerning Honorius: His mother leaning on gold, flowing with gems, brought him forth on Tyrian couches.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

IN DELICIIS PARADISI DEI FUISTI) Omnia tibi affluebant, ut olim Adamo in horto Hedenis, quem ei Deus concesserat.

OMNIS LAPIS PRETIOSUS OPERIMENTUM TUUM) Vestis tua gemmis erat intexta.

SARDIUS) אדם rubrum significat. Talis autem est Sarda Indica Plinio 37, 7. σάρδιον habent hic & Græci. Chaldæus סמקן à סמק quod est rubere.

TOPAZIUS) פטרה τοπάζιον vertunt Græci, tum in Exodo tum Jobo 28, 19. Chaldæus vertit ירקן. Est illis ירק virere. Est ergo Topazius Arabica, cui virorem attri- buit Plinius 37, 8.

ET JASPIS) יהלם est ab הלם quod est frangere: ideo non minus convenit adamanti hoc nomen, quam ja- spidi. Et adamantem tum hic tum in Exodo interpretatur Chaldæus. Adamantes Arabici Plinio teste 37, 7. ita re- spuunt ictum, ut ferrum utrinque dissultet, incudesque etiam ipsæ dissiliant.

CHRTSOLITHUS) תרשיש est Oceanus & Oceani color. Beryllo id nomen optime convenit, qui viriditatem puri maris imitatur, Plinius 37, 5. Græci interpretes variant: interpretantur enim χρυσόλιθον, άνθρακα, ὑάκινθον.

ET ONYX) שהם Rabbini fere omnes consentiunt lapidem esse forma unguis humani, id est, onychem, & sic à Græcis vertitur Joh. 28, 16. Atque id malo, quam quod alibi vertitur πράσινον, alibi σμάραγδος, alibi σάπφειρος, alibi σάρδιον, alibi ut & à Chaldæis βηρύλλιον.

ET BERYLLUS) ישפה ipso sono accedit ad jaspi- dem. Et ita hic Græci. At alibi ὀνύχιον, Chaldæus פנתרין, id est, pantherinum. Ita vocari credo id jaspidum genus, quod è multis veluti gemmis compositum dicit Plinius 38, 81. à panthera varii coloris animante.

SAPPHIRUS) ספיר non est dubium quin sit σάπφει- ρος, nihil mutato nomine. Et sic constanter vertunt Græci in Exodo, Jobo, & alibi. Retinet nomen Arabia, Nun in- terposito. سلفير

ET CARBUNCULUS) נפך Carbunculum etiam Exodi 28, 18. vertit Hieronymus, ubi & Græcis est ἄνθραξ. Ajunt Hebræi נפך esse nigrum. Sed & Plinius carbuncu- los Carchedonios nigrioris esse aspectus dicit.

ET SMARAGDUS) ברקת est à ברק, quod est fulgurare, coruscare. Optime id nomen conveniret Chry- solitho, cui color aureus; vertunt tamen Græci σμάραγδος & hic ὀνύχιον. Chaldæus vicinam vocem posuit ברקן quod pro carbunculo accipi video.

AURUM OPUS DECORIS TUI, ET FORAMI- NA TUA IN DIE QUA CONDITUS ES PRÆPA- RATA SUNT) Melius illa: Et aurum, ad priorem sensum referas. Deinde vertas cum Symmacho: Tympana tua, & foramina tua in die qua formatus es, præparata fuerant. Cum adhuc in utero formateris, jam tum tibi parabantur tympa- na (sic vocantur margaritæ quibus una tantum est facies, & ab ea rotunditas, inversis planities, teste Plinio 9, 35.) & forata, id est, margaritarum lineæ, ut eas vocat Scævola & Martialis. Simile illud Claudiani de Honorio: Acclinis genitrix auro, circumflua gemmis In Tyrios enixa thoros.

## 28:14
THOU CHERUB EXTENDED AND PROTECTING) He compares him to the other of the Cherubim who were extended over the ark, and covered it. So also he [covered] his own people. Jerome seems to have read ממשך and not ממשח, the sense is thus better.

Cf. B. Glassius, dedicatory preface to the Exegesis of the Epistles.

AND I HAVE SET THEE IN THE HOLY MOUNT OF GOD) Understand, as it were. Just as those were in the sanctuary of the temple (which is called the holy mount), so you were in a place that seemed inaccessible to all force.

IN THE MIDST OF THE FIERY STONES THOU HAST WALKED) Just as the High Priest approached the Cherubim with twelve gleaming stones, so also those who were around you entered with equal adornment.

Latin:

TU CHERUB EXTENTUS ET PROTEGENS) Comparat eum Cherubinorum alteri qui super arcam ex- tendebantur, eamque obtegebant. Sic & ille populum suum. Videtur Hieronymus legisse ממשך non, ממשח, sensus sic est melior.

Conf. B. Glassii præf. dedic. Exeg. Epistolic.

ET POSUI TE IN MONTE SANCTO DEI) Subaudi, quasi. Sicut illi in templi adyto erant (quod vo- catur mons sanctus) ita tu in loco qui videbatur ad omnem vim inaccessus.

IN MEDIO LAPIDUM IGNITORUM AMBU- LASTI) Sicut Pontifex cum duodecim lapidibus mican- tibus accedebat Cherubinum, ita & qui circum te erant, in- trabant pari ornatu.

## 28:15
Verse 15.

PERFECT IN THY WAYS FROM THE DAY OF THY CREATION) You were happy in all your actions, from the time you were formed.

UNTIL INIQUITY WAS FOUND IN THEE) Until you began to practice piracy, as the following verses explain.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

PERFECTUS IN VIIS TUIS A DIE CONDI- TIONIS TUÆ) Felix fuisti in omnibus actionibus tuis, ex quo formatus es.

DONEC INVENTA EST INIQVITAS IN TE) Donec cœpisti exercere piraticam, ut sequentia ex- plicant.

## 28:16
Vers. 16. IN THE MULTITUDE OF THY MERCHANDISE) Since you could easily have made wealth from just commerce. THY INWARD PARTS ARE FILLED) That is, your treasures, as the Chaldean here. WITH INIQUITY) With things seized. I CAST THEE OUT FROM THE MOUNTAIN OF GOD) From Tyre, which was like a sanctuary, as we have said.

Latin:

Vers. 16. IN MULTITUDINE NEGOTIATIONIS TUÆ) Cum ex justis commerciis rem facile posses facere. REPLETA SUNT INTERIORA TUA) Id est, Thesauri tui, ut hic Chaldæus. INIQUITATE) Rebus raptis. EJECI TE DE MONTE DEI) De Tyro, quæ ve- lut adytum erat, ut diximus.

## 28:17
Vers. 17. AND THINE HEART WAS LIFTED UP) For your mind had become proud. I CAST THEE TO THE GROUND) That is, I prostrated you. I LAID THEE BEFORE KINGS THAT THEY MIGHT BEHOLD THEE) I set you before kings as an example. So the Chaldean and the LXX.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET ELEVATUM EST COR TUUM) Nam superbierat tibi animus. IN TERRAM PROJECI TE) Id est, prostravi te. ANTE FACIEM REGUM DEDI TE UT CER- NERENT TE) Te proposui regibus in exemplum. Ita Chaldæus & LXX.

## 28:18
Vers. 18. IN THE MULTITUDE OF THINE INIQUITIES) By many things obtained through force. AND IN THE INIQUITY OF THY MERCHANDISE) And through contracts extorted from strangers. THOU HAST DEFILED THY SANCTUARIES) Your sanctuaries. You filled the temples of Bel, whom the Greeks call Jupiter, of Melcart, whom they call Hercules, and of Astarte, with things ill-gotten. I WILL BRING FORTH A FIRE FROM THE MIDST OF THEE) Punishment will follow guilt as a companion. AND I WILL BRING THEE TO ASHES UPON THE EARTH) Like ashes. The Chaldean is good here. Enemies will not value you more than ashes scattered on the ground.

Latin:

Vers. 18. IN MULTITUDINE INIQUITATUM TUARUM) Rebus multis per vim partis. ET INIQUITATE NEGOTIATIONIS TUÆ) Et per contractus extortos advenis. POLLUISTI SANCTIFICATIONEM TUAM) Sanctuaria tua. Templa Beli quem Jovem Græci vocant, Melcarti, quem illi Herculem, Astartes, implesti rebus male partis. PRODUCAM EGO IGNEM DE MEDIO TUI) Culpam pœna premet comes. ET DABO TE IN CINEREM SUPER TER- RAM) Quasi cinerem. Bene hic Chaldæus. Hostes non pluris te facient, quam cinerem sparsum humi.

## 28:19
Vers. 19. ALL THEY THAT BEHOLD THEE) They had known you before: as the Chaldean says here. THOU ART BROUGHT TO NOTHING) Symmachus is accustomed to translate כלהות as non-existence. The Chaldean in this place expressed the same sense: I will make you as if you had never been. That is, not even a burial will fall to your lot. LXX: you have become destruction. AND NEVER SHALT THOU BE ANY MORE) That is, your body will never be found. Here עדי עולם requires the time to be taken as the end of the end. It has often appeared that it is taken differently elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 19. OMNES QUI VIDERINT TE) Antehac te noverant: ut Chaldæus hic. NIHILI FACTUS ES( כלהות ἀνυπαρξίαν solet ver- tere Symmachus. Chaldæus hoc loco eundem sensum ex- pressit: Ponam te quasi nunquam fuisses. Id est, ne sepultura tibi quidem continget. LXX. ἀπώλεια ἐγένου. ET NON ERIS IN PERPETUUM) Id est, corpus tuum nunquam reperietur. Hic עדי עולם fine fine accipi tempus postulat. Alibi aliter sumi sæpe apparuit.

## 28:22
Vers. 22. BEHOLD, I AM AGAINST THEE, O ZIDON) The histories have perished for us from which we could interpret these things. But it is credible that the Sidonians, from whom Tyre had arisen, had provided aid to the Tyrians, and afterwards paid the penalty to the Chaldeans: for we learn from the writers of the affairs of Alexander that the ancient house of the Sidonian kings had long since been depressed to a plebeian lot. Therefore, these also were made no less than the Tyrians subject to the power of the Chaldeans first, and then of the Persians. See a similar prophecy, but pertaining to more ancient times, concerning Tyre and Sidon in Isaiah 23:4.

AND I SHALL BE SANCTIFIED IN HER) That is, I shall be praised by all on the occasion of her punishments.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ECCE EGO AD TE SIDON) Perierunt nobis historiæ, ex quibus hæc possemus interpretari. Sed credibile est Sidonios, unde orta erat Tyros, Tyriis auxi- lium præbuisse, & postea Chaldæis dedisse pœnas: nam do- mum veterem Sidoniorum regum ad plebejam sortem de- pressam jam olim fuisse discimus ex scriptoribus rerum A- lexandri. Facti ergo & hi non minus quam Tyrii sub po- testate Chaldæorum primum, deinde Persarum. Simile va- ticinium, sed ad tempora vetustiora pertinens de Tyro & Sidone vide apud Esaiam 23, 4.

ET SANCTIFICATUS FUERO IN EA) Id est, occasione pœnarum ejus ab omnibus laudatus fuero.

## 28:23
Vers. 23. AND I WILL SEND PESTILENCE) Which is accustomed to accompany sieges from corrupted food and infected air.

BY THE SWORD) The Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET IMMITTAM PESTILENTIAM) Quæ obsidiones comitari solet ex corruptis alimentis, infecto- que aëre.

GLADIO) Chaldæico.

## 28:24
Vers. 24. AND THERE SHALL BE NO MORE UNTO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL A PRICKING BRIAR) Harmful feelings.

ROUND ABOUT THEM) With the Tyrians, Sidonians, Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites repressed. This is to be referred to the time which he will now describe, when the Jews shall have returned to their homeland. For they lived for a long time unmolested.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET NON ERIT ULTRA DOMUI I- SRAEL OFFENDICULUM AMARITUDINIS) Sentis noxia.

UNDIQUE PER CIRCUITUM EORUM) Re- pressis Tyriis, Sidoniis, Ammonitis, Moabitis, Idumæis. Referendum hoc ad tempus quod jam describet, ubi Judæi in patriam reversi fuerint. Diu enim illæcessiti vixere.

## 29:1 Argument
SIXTH REVELATION. CHAPTER XXIX.

Against the King of Egypt and his kingdom to be reduced to solitude, yet to be recalled after 40 years, though not to its former glory. The land of Egypt (which is the SEVENTH REVELATION) is given to Nebuchadnezzar, because he labored with his army in devastating Tyre.

Vers. 1. IN THE TENTH YEAR) From the deportation of Jeconiah. These prophecies are arranged not by times, but by nations, and they begin from those nearest to the land of Judea.

Latin:

SEXTA REVELATIO. CAPUT XXIX.

Adversus Regem Ægypti ac regnum ejus in so- litudinem redigendum, post 40. tamen annos revocandum, licet non ad pristinam gloriam. Terra Ægypti (quæ est SEPTI- MA REVELATIO) datur Nebucad- nezari, eo quod cum suo exercitu labora- verit devastando Tyrum.

Vers. 1. IN ANNO DECIMO) A deportatione Jechoniæ. Vaticinia hæc non per tempora, sed per gentes sunt ordi- nata, & à propinquioribus terræ Judææ incipiunt.

## 29:2
Vers. 2. AGAINST PHARAOH KING OF EGYPT) Who is חפר in Hebrew, Ουαφρῆς in Greek, Ephree in Latin. Jerem. 45, 30. Apries in Herodotus: where see what has been said by us: for the matter is the same which is touched upon here.

Latin:

Vers. 2. CONTRA PHARAONEM REGEM ÆGTPTI) Qui חפר in Hebræo, Ουαφρῆς in Græco, Ephree in Lati- no. Jerem. 45, 30. Ἀπρίης Herodoto: ubi à nobis dicta vide: res enim est eadem, quæ hic tangitur.

## 29:3
Vers. 3. GREAT DRAGON) The word תנים often signifies a huge fish, and here perhaps a crocodile.

For the Nile abounded in crocodiles, as Jerome, Pintus, Maldonatus, Tremellius, Piscator, B. Hülsemann [note]. Conf. P. 74, 13. WHO LIEST IN THE MIDST OF THY RIVERS) In so many mouths of the Nile. AND SAYEST: THE RIVER IS MINE) That is, this Egyptian kingdom is mine. I HAVE MADE MYSELF) That is, the king. He was the most fortunate of kings for 25 years, as Herodotus testifies, and puffed up by fortune he said, that not even a god could remove him from his kingdom. Others, And I made for myself, viz. it, the river. So also B. Luther.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DRACO MAGNE) Vox תנים piscem ingentem sæ- pe significat, & hic forte crocodilum.

Nilus enim Crocodilis abundabat, ut Hierony- mus, Pintus, Maldon. Tremell. Piscator, B. Hülsemann. Conf. P. 74, 13. QUI CUBAS IN MEDIO FLUMINUM TUO- RUM) In tot Nili ostiis. ET DICIS: MEUS EST FLUVIUS) Id est, meum est hoc regnum Ægyptium. EGO FECI MEMET IPSUM) Regem scilicet. Fe- licissimus regum fuit per annos 25. ut testatur Herodotus, & fortuna elatus dicebat, μηδ' ἄνθεόν μιν μηδένα δύνασθαι παῦσαι τῆς βασιληΐης. Alii, Et ego feci mihi, sc. illum, fluvium. Sic etiam B. Lutherus.

## 29:4
Vers. 4. I WILL PUT A BRIDLE IN THY JAWS) A hook. See Job 11, 19. 20. That hook is Amasis. I WILL STICK THE FISH OF THY RIVERS TO THY SCALES) You will have many who will be with you against Amasis. I WILL DRAW THEE OUT OF THE MIDST OF THY RIVERS) I will strip you of all your dignity. AND ALL THE FISH OF THY RIVERS SHALL STICK TO THY SCALES) And to all the fish that are to stick to your scales. Whoever will be of your sect, will also be participants in the calamity. AND I WILL CAST THEE INTO THE DESERT) Into the dry land where fish cannot live; which he will say presently, upon the face of the earth. By this figure a prison is hinted at. THOU SHALT NOT BE GATHERED NOR COLLECTED) That is, you will not return into the river. For he persists in the likeness of a fish. I HAVE GIVEN THEE TO THE BEASTS OF THE EARTH AND THE FOWLS OF THE HEAVEN TO BE DEVOURED) The sense of the allegory is: I have given power to wild and rapacious men to strip you of your kingdom, liberty, goods, and finally also your life.

Herodotus 1. 2 teaches that Pharaoh Apries was captured and strangled by Amasis his minister; but because destruction is also predicted by fish sticking to his scales, these things are more correctly accepted concerning the slaughter of Pharaoh Necho at the borders of Carchemish, Jerem. 46, 3, than concerning the strangulation of one individual, about which Jer. 44, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PONAM FRÆNUM IN MAXILLIS TUIS) Hamum. Vide Job. 11, 19. 20. Is hamus est Amasis. AGGLUTINABO PISCES FLUMINUM TUO- RUM SQUAMMIS TUIS) Multos habebis qui tibi ad- sint contra Amasim. EXTRAHAM TE DE MEDIO FLUMINUM TUORUM) Omnem dignitatem tibi detraham. ET UNIVERSI PISCES TUI SQVAMIS TUIS ADHÆREBUNT) Et cunctis piscibus qui squammis tuis ad- hæsuri sunt. Quicunque tuæ erunt sectæ, etiam calamita- tis erunt participes. ET PROJICIAM TE IN DESERTUM) In sic- cum ubi pisces vivere nequeunt; quod modo dicet, super faciem terræ. Hæc figura carcer innuitur. NON COLLIGERIS NEQVE CONGREGABE- RIS) Id est, non redibis in flumen. Persitat enim in piscis similitudine. BESTIIS TERRÆ ET VOLATILIBUS COELI DEDI TE AD DEVORANDUM) Sensus allegoriæ est: hominibus feris ac rapacibus potestatem dedi exuendi te regno, libertate, bonis, postremum & vita.

Herodot. 1. 2. Pharaonem Apros ab Amasi mi- nistro suo captum & strangulatum docet; sed quia etiam piscibus squamis adhærentibus interi- tus prædicitur, de Pharaonis Necho clade ad Car- chemis fines desertorum Jerem. 46, 3. hæc rectius accipiuntur quam de strangulatione unius indivi- dui, de qua Jer. 44, 30.

## 29:7
Vers. 7. THOU HAST TORN ALL THEIR SHOULDER) He said shoulder for arm synecdochically. AND HAST DISSOLVED ALL THEIR LOINS) Better, their loins: the Greeks [wrote] συνέκλασας ἀυτῶν πᾶσαν ὀσφύν. Therefore both they and the Latin, and indeed the Chaldean also, read עמדת not ערכת, undoubtedly better. The sense of the allegory is: you were a destruction to those of Israel expecting help from you. See the matter in Jerem. 37, 6. 41, 17. 43, 10. 2 Kings 24, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 7. LACERASTI OMNEM HUMERUM EORUM) Humerum dixit pro Brachio συνεκδοχικῶς. ET DISSOLVISTI OMNES RENES EORUM) Melius, Lumbos eorum: Græcis συνέκλασας ἀυτῶν πᾶσαν ὀσφύν.
