Legerunt ergo & hi & Latinus, imo & Chaldæus עמדת non ערכת, melius haud dubie. Sensus allegoriæ est: Israelis abs te auxilium exspectantibus exitio fuisti. Rem vide Jerem. 37, 6. 41, 17. 43, 10. 2. Reg. 24, 7.

## 29:8
Vers. 8. I WILL BRING A SWORD UPON THEE) First civil wars, then also the arms of Nebuchadnezzar, as he will say presently v. 19. See Jerem. 42, 16. And what is said there. I WILL CUT OFF FROM THEE MAN AND BEAST) Many men, and many living creatures.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ADDUCAM SUPER TE GLADIUM) Primum bella civilia, deinde & arma Nabuchodonosori,ut mox di- cet v. 19. Vide Jerem. 42, 16. Et ibi dicta. INTERFICIAM IN TE HOMINEM ET JU- MENTUM) Multos homines, & animantia multa.

## 29:9
Vers. 9. AND THE LAND OF EGYPT SHALL BE INTO A DESERT) These things are to be understood synecdochically concerning the part of Egypt devastated by wars.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET ERIT TERRA ÆGTPTI IN DESERTUM) Hæc συνεκδοχικῶς de parte Ægypti vastata bellis sunt intel- ligenda.

## 29:10
Vers. 10. FROM THE TOWER OF SYENE) Better: from Migdol and Syene. Migdol is a city of Egypt by the Red Sea, Jerem. 44, 1. 46, 14. Syene is above Alexandria by five thousand stadia. Pliny 2, 75. It is at the cataracts of the Nile, on the eastern side of the Nile, which faces Arabia, as appears from Pliny 5, 9 and others. EVEN TO THE BORDER OF ETHIOPIA) If you rightly pay attention, from these borders you will see a part of Egypt indicated, not the whole of Egypt, which the following will also confirm.

Latin:

Vers. 10. A TURRE STENES) Melius: à Magdalo & Syene. Magdalum est urbs Ægypti ad mare rubrum Jerem. 44, 1. 46, 14. Syene supra Alexandriam est quinque millibus sta- diorum. Plinius 2, 75. Est ad cataractas Nili, in orientali Nili latere, quod Arabiæ obvertitur, ut apparet ex Plinio 5, 9. & aliis. USQVE AD TERMINUM ÆTHIOPIÆ) Si recte animum advertas, ex his terminis videbis partem Ægypti indicari, non totam Ægyptum, quod & fequentia con- firmabunt.

## 29:11
Vers. 11. IT SHALL NOT BE INHABITED FOR FORTY YEARS) Amasis, by a long reign, gradually restored the affairs of Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 11. NON HABITABITUR QVADRAGINTA AN- NIS) Amasis longo regno paulatim restituit res Æ- gypti.

## 29:12
Vers. 12. AND I WILL DISPERSE THE EGYPTIANS AMONG THE nations) Many of the Egyptians who, for fear of war, betake themselves into Arabia or Ethiopia, and are then to return, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET DISPERGAM ÆGYPTIOS IN NATIO- NES) Multos Aegyptiorum qui belli metu in Arabiam se aut Aethiopiam recipient, ac deinde redituri sunt, ut sequitur.

## 29:14
Verse 14.

AND I WILL SET THEM IN THE LAND OF PATHROS) We have said in Book 1 of the Truth of the Christian Religion that פתרסים, who are mentioned in Gen. 10:14, seem to us to be those Ethiopians who are the Pharusii to Pliny, and the Pharusii to Ptolemy. But a part of Egypt is also so called in Isa. 11:11. And here below in 30:14. Having its origin, no doubt, from those Ethiopians, as Ezekiel will now say. The Jerusalem interpreter of Genesis thinks they are the Pelusians.

AND THEY SHALL BE THERE A LOWLY KINGDOM, 15. IT SHALL BE THE LOWLIEST AMONG THE OTHER KINGDOMS: AND IT SHALL NOT EXALT ITSELF ANY MORE ABOVE THE NATIONS: AND I WILL DIMINISH THEM THAT THEY SHALL NOT RULE OVER THE NATIONS) With the empire of the Chaldeans, and then of the Persians, being predominant, they will dare to move nothing until the times of the Lagidae. Cf. Jer. 46:26.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET COLLOCABO EOS IN TERRA PHATURES) Diximus ad librum 1. de veritate religionis Christianae פתרסים, qui dicuntur Gen. 10, 14. videri nobis esse il- los Athiopas, qui Pharusii Plinio, Pharusii Ptolemaeo. At pars etiam Aegypti sic dicta Esa. 11, 11. Et hic infra 30, 14. Ab Aethiopibus illis nimirum ortum habens, ut jam dicet Ezech. Eos esse Pelusios sentit interpres Geneseos Hiero- solymitanus.

ET ERUNT IBI IN REGNUM HUMILE, 15. INTER CAETERA REGNA ERIT HUMILLIMA: ET NON ELEVABITUR ULTRA SUPRA NATIO- NES: ET IMMINUAM EOS NE IMPERENT GEN- TIBUS) Praepollente Chaldaeorum, ac deinde Persarum imperio, nihil movere audebunt ad tempora usque Lagi- darum. Conf. Jerem. 46, 26.

## 29:16
Verse 16.

AND THEY SHALL NO MORE BE TO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL FOR A CONFIDENCE) The Israelites will no longer have trust in them, as heretofore.

TEACHING INIQUITY) That is, they will no longer, by the hope of help, entice the Israelites to the idolatry of their gods, as they have done heretofore.

THAT THEY MAY FLEE AND FOLLOW THEM) In the Hebrew: that is to say, that these Israelites may look to those Egyptians: that they may hang upon their soldiers, and be prepared to do everything for their sake.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

NEQVE ERUNT ULTRA DOMUI ISRAEL IN CONFIDENTIA) Non ultra Israelitae in illis habe- bunt fiduciam, ut antehac.

DOCENTES INIQVITATEM) Id est, non ultra spe auxilii allicient Israelitas ad Idololatriam suorum deo- rum, ut antehac fecerunt.

UT FUGIANT ET SEQVANTUR EOS) In Hebraeo: ut scilicet hi Israelitae ad illos Aegyptios respiciant: ut pendeant ab ipsorum militibus, nihilque non parati sint facere ipsorum causa.

## 29:17
Verse 17.

AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE TWENTY-SEVENTH YEAR IN THE FIRST MONTH, THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME UNTO ME, SAYING) This is connected with the preceding, not in the time of revelation: for it is a long interval, but by the coherence of events. For at the time when Jerusalem was besieged, captured, and burned, and after Gedaliah was killed, the remnants of the Jews who had remained in the country in meager circumstances were deported; then in the fifth year after Jerusalem was captured, the Ammonites and Moabites and neighboring regions were devastated by the Chaldeans; after that, Tyre was besieged for 13 years, soon Sidon and other cities; during all this time, I say, Egypt was agitated by seditions and civil wars. But when that time had elapsed, when the time for Nebuchadnezzar to come into Egypt was now approaching, God revealed to the Prophet more pressingly and distinctly what He had said generally. Cf. Jer. 46:26.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ET FACTUM EST IN VIGESIMO ET SEPTI- MO ANNO IN PRIMO IN UNA MENSIS FACTUM EST VERBUM DOMINI AD ME, DICENS) Hoc cum superioribus nectitur, non revelationis tempore: est enim longum intervallum, sed per rerum cohaerentiam. Nam quo tempore Hierosolyma obsessa, capta, exusta sunt, & post Godoliam interfectum deportatae, quae in patria te- nues resederant Judaeorum reliquiae, deinde quinto post capta Hierosolyma anno, a Chaldaeis vastata Ammonitis & Moabis, vicinaeque regiones; post id Tyros obsessa per an- nos 13. mox Sidon aliaeque urbes, omni hoc, inquam, tem- pore Aegyptus seditionibus bellisque civilibus fuit agitata. Eo vero elapso tempore, cum jam appropinquaret tempus venturi in Aegyptum Nabuchodonosoris, Deus quae gene- raliter dixerat, ea jam pressius signatiusque Prophetae aperuit. Conf. Jer. 46, 26.

## 29:18
Verse 18.

NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON CAUSED HIS ARMY TO SERVE A GREAT SERVICE AGAINST TYRE) God says this. Nebuchadnezzar spent a full 13 years in punishing the Tyrians, and in that matter he performed a service that was thanks-worthy to me. I do not wish it to be without a great reward. And so, for that service, I will give him a good part of Egypt. For he had not plundered Tyre, but had joined it to himself on conditions. See Jerome on this passage.

EVERY HEAD IS MADE BALD.

From the long duration of so troublesome a siege, the weight of the helmets, etc., some argue that Nebuchadnezzar had made a vow and bound himself with ceremonies, from Jer. 33, 16.

EVERY SHOULDER IS STRIPPED) It is worn away. Namely, by carrying baskets to make mounds, as Jerome rightly explains here.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

NABUCHODONOSOR REX BABYLONIS SER- VIRE FECIT EXERCITUM SUUM SERVITUTE MAGNA ADVERSUS TYRUM) Hoc dicit Deus. Na- buchodonosor totos annos 13. impendit in puniendis Ty- riis, eaque in re gratam mihi operam praestitit. Nolo id sit sine magna mercede. Itaque pro ista opera bonam par- tem Aegypti ipsi dabo. Nam Tyrum non diripuerat, sed conditionibus sibi adjunxerat. Vide Hieronymum ad hunc locum.

OMNE CAPUT DECALVATUM EST.

Diuturnitate tam molestae obsidionis, ponde- re galearum, &c. nonnulli vovisse Nebucadne- zar, & caeremoniis se obstrinxisse e Jerem. 33, 16. arguunt.

OMNIS HUMERUS DEPILATUS EST) Attri- tus est. Nempe portando cophinos ad aggeres faciendos, ut recte hic explicat Hieronymus.

## 29:19
Ver. 19.

HE SHALL TAKE HER MULTITUDE) He shall lead away many captives from Egypt.

AND HE SHALL PLUNDER HER SPOILS) He shall despoil her spoils. ἄξει λάφυρα ἀπὸ λαφύρων, as the Aetolians used to say. Just as the Egyptians have plundered others, so the Chaldeans shall plunder them.

AND IT SHALL BE WAGES FOR HIS ARMY) Rightly. For the booty of a city surrendered belongs to the commanders, that of a city taken by storm to the soldiers, as the Flavians say in Tacitus, Histories 3.

Tyre was indeed most opulent, but Jerome testifies that when the inhabitants saw that the preservation of the city was hopeless, they transported themselves and their valuables to Carthage by ships.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ACCIPIET MULTITUDINEM EJUS) Multos adducet captivos ex Aegypto.

ET DEPREDABITUR NANUBIAS EJUS) Spoliabit spolia ejus. ἄξει λάφυρα ἀπὸ λαφύρων, ut dicebant Aetoli. Sicut Aegyptii alios sunt populati, ita ipsos popula- buntur Chaldaei.

ET ERIT MERCES EXERCITUI EJUS) Recte. Nam deditae urbis praeda ad duces, expugnatae ad militem pertinet, ut ajunt Flaviani apud Tacitum histor. 3.

Tyrus opulentissima quidem fuit, sed incolae ubi videre urbis conservationem desperatam esse, se suaque pretiosa Carthaginem navigiis transtu- lisse testatur Hieronymus.

## 29:21
Ver. 21.

IN THAT DAY I WILL CAUSE THE HORN TO BUD FOR THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) That is, Daniel shall be promoted to the greatest dignity, like Joseph, to whom for that reason a horn is attributed in Deut. 33, 17. See Dan. 6, 2.

Others refer the Hebrew 'I will cause to bud a horn for the house of Israel' more correctly to the restoration, both through Zerubbabel and especially through Christ, with Jerome. Compare 2 Kings 25, 30; Jer. 23, 3, 15; Zech. 6, 11; Ps. 132, 17.

AND I WILL GIVE THEE AN OPEN MOUTH IN THE MIDST OF THEM) When so many things have come to pass as predicted by you to the Jews, and by Daniel to the Chaldeans, your words will now have greater authority among the people. See above 24, 27, and what is said there.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

IN DIE ILLO PULLULABIT CORNU DOMUI ISRAEL) Id est, ad maximam dignitatem provehetur Da- niel, instar Josephi, cui ob id cornu tribuitur Deut. 33, 37. Vide Dan. 6, 2.

Alii Ebr. pullulare faciam cornu Domui I- Israel, rectius ad inftaurationem tum per Zoroba- bel, tum præcipue per Christum referunt cum Hie- ron. Conf. 2. Reg. 25, 30. Jerem. 23, 3. 15. Zach. 6, 11. Pf. 132, 17.

ET TIBI DABO APERTVM OS IN MEDIO EORUM) Ubi tam multa abs te Judæis, à Daniele Chal- dæis, prædicta evenerint, auctoritatem jam majorem di- cta tua apud populum habebunt. Vide supra 24, 27. & ibi dicta.

## 30:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXX. All the cities of Egypt will be devastated by the King of Babylon.

Vers. 1.

AND THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME TO ME) The three following chapters pertain to the same thing as the end of the preceding chapter: namely, to the war of Nebuchadnezzar in Egypt, and the part that touched Ethiopia.

Latin:

CAPUT XXX. Omnes urbes Ægypti per Regem Babylonis va- stabuntur.

Vers. 1.

ET FACTUM EST VERBUM DOMINI AD ME) Tria quæ sequuntur capita eodem pertinent, quo finis capitis præcedentis: nempe ad bellum Nabuchodonosoris in Ægypto, & parte quæ Æthiopiam attingebat.

## 30:3
Vers. 3.

DAY OF THE CLOUD) A black day, as the Latins say.

TIME OF THE GENTILES) Namely, for punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

DIES NUBIS) Atra dies, ut dicunt Latini.

TEMPUS GENTIVM) Nempe ad pœnam.

## 30:4
AND TERROR IN ETHIOPIA) In those parts which were allied to Egypt.

AND HER FOUNDATIONS DESTROYED) Cities demolished.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET PAVOR IN ÆTHIOPIA) In illis parti- bus, quæ fœderatæ erant Ægypto.

ET DESTRUCTA FUNDAMENTA EJUS) Ur- bes dirutæ.

## 30:5
Vers. 5. AND LIBYA) For the Africans were also among the allies of Egypt, Jer. 46, 9. And from this Nebuchadnezzar took a pretext for war in Africa, as we have said elsewhere.

AND THE LYDIANS) These also were allies of the Egyptians, Jer. 46, 9.

AND ALL THE REST OF THE COMMON PEOPLE) Mercenary soldiers recruited from many nations. LXX. οἱ ἐπίμικτοι.

AND CHUB) The Cubii in Mareotis according to Ptolemy.

AND THE SONS OF THE LAND OF THE COVENANT) Many Jews will be involved in the same calamity. Jerem. 42, 21. 44, 14. LXX. ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν τῆς διαθήκης μꝰ, Nor does Jerome take it otherwise in his commentary.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET LYBIA) Nam & Afri inter socios Ægypti Jerem. 46, 9. Et hinc belli in Africam prætextum sumsit Nabuchodonosor, ut alibi diximus.

ET LYDI) Socii & hi Ægyptiorum Jer. 46, 9.

ET OMNE RELIQVUM VULGUS) Miles mer- cenarius ex multis gentibus allectus. LXX. οἱ ἐπίμικτοι.

ET CHUB) Cubii in Mareotide apud Ptolemæum.

ET FILII TERRÆ FOEDERIS) Judæi multi ea- dem calamitate involventur. Jerem. 42, 21. 44, 14. LXX. ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν τῆς διαθήκης μꝰ, Nec aliter accipit in commen- tario Hieronymus.

## 30:6
Ver. 6. THE SUPPORTERS OF EGYPT SHALL FALL) Allies and auxiliaries.

FROM THE LAND OF SYENE) From Migdol and Syene: as above 29, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CORRUENT FULCIENTES ÆGYPTIJM) Socii & auxilia.

A TERRA SYENES) A Magdalo & Syene: ut supra 29, 12.

## 30:7
Ver. 7. AND THEY SHALL BE DESOLATE IN THE MIDST OF THE COUNTRIES THAT ARE DESOLATE) They shall be desolated as much as possible. A similar manner of speaking as above 29, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET DISSIPABUNT IN MEDIO TERRA- RUM DESOLATARUM) Desolabuntur ut qui maxime. Si- mile loquendi genus supra 29, 12.

## 30:8
Ver. 8. WHEN I HAVE SET A FIRE IN EGYPT) By the conflagration of war.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CUM DEDERO IGNEM IN ÆGYPTO) Incendio bellico.

## 30:9
Ver. 9. IN SHIPS) Through the Nile. Concerning the ships, see Isaiah 33, 21.

Ver. same. IN THE DAY OF EGYPT. In the Hebrew it is: According to the day of Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN TRIERIBUS) Per Nilum. De trieribus vide Esaiæ 33, 21.

Vers. eod. IN DIE ÆGYPTI. In Ebræo est: Secundum diem Ægypti.

## 30:10
Ver. 10. I WILL MAKE THE MULTITUDE OF EGYPT TO CEASE) I will greatly diminish its crowd.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CESSARE FACIAM MULTITUDINEM ÆGYPTI) Turbam ejus multum imminuam.

## 30:12
AND I WILL MAKE THE RIVERS DRY) The canals of the Nile, as Jerome says here in his commentary. Sextus Aurelius called them ditches: the streams, the only law in the Code concerning the embankments of the Nile.

THE LAND AND THE FULNESS THEREOF) The crops.

Latin:

ET FACIAM ALVEOS FLUMINUM ARIDOS) Nili διώρυχας, ut hic in Commentario Hieronymus. Fossas dixit Sextus Aurelius: fluenta lex unica C. de Nili aggeribus.

TERRAM ET PLENITUDINEM EJUS) Fruges.

## 30:13
Ver. 13. THE IDOLS FROM MEMPHIS) From Memphis. Tibullus: Thee sings and admires its own offspring Osiris, the barbarian, taught to mourn the Memphian ox.

Ovid: Nor flee the sacred rites of the Nile-bearing heifer.

That Noph is Memphis is stated in Isaiah 19:13.

Today it is called Alcair, which the Turk captured in the year 1516, having destroyed the empire of the Egyptians.

A PRINCE FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT SHALL BE NO MORE) That is, a king ruling over all Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IDOLA DE MEMPHIS) De Memphide. Tibullus: Te canit atque suum proles miratur Osirim Barbara, Memphitem plangere docta bovem.

Ovidius: Neu fuge Niligeræ Memphitica sacra juvencæ.

Noph esse Memphidem dictum Esaiæ 19, 30.

Hodie Alcair dicitur, quam Turca Anno, 1516. cepit deleto Ægyptiorum imperio.

DUX DE TERRA ÆGYPTI NON ERIT AM- PLIUS) Id est, rex toti Ægypto imperans.

## 30:14
Verse 14. AND I WILL DESTROY THE LAND OF PATHROS) See what was said above at 19:14.

I WILL SET FIRE IN TAPHNIS) It should have been said Tanis, as the LXX and the Chaldean have here. For that is צען Numbers 13:22. See what we said at Matthew 1:21.

AND I WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS IN ALEXANDRIA) Jerome says in his Commentary that he used this name by anticipation, which is called πρόληψις, because Alexandria was founded where No had been. We spoke at Isaiah 46:25.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DISPERDAM TERRAM PHATU- RES) Vide quæ dicta supra ad 19, 14.

DABO IGNEM IN TAPHNIS) Dicendum fuerat Tanis, ut hic habent LXX. & Chaldæus. Ea enim est צען Num. 13, 22. Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. 1, 21.

ET FACIAM JUDICIA IN ALEXANDRIA) Di- cit in Commentario Hieronymus hoc nomen se posuisse per anticipationem, quæ πρόληψις dicitur, quia Alexandria condita est ubi Novetus fuerat. Diximus ad Es. 46, 25.

## 30:15
Verse 15.

AND I WILL POUR OUT MY INDIGNATION UPON PELUSIUM) סין in Hebrew. That city is believed to be so called because it was set against those coming from the desert of Sin. But what if, by changing one vowel point, we interpret it as Sain with the LXX.

But what necessity is there for changing the authentic text, when it is correct as it stands? See Jerome here.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET EFFUNDAM INDIGNATIONEM MEAM SUPER PELUSIUM) סין in Hebræo. Ita urbs illa dicta creditur quod objecta esset à deserto Sin venientibus. Sed quid si uno puncto mutato Sain interpretemur cum LXX.

Quæ vero necessitas immutandi textum av- thenticum, quum recte is sese habeant. Vid. hic Hieronymus.

## 30:17
Vers. 17. THE YOUNG MEN OF HELIOPOLIS) און, in the Hebrew text, which can be correctly read as On, and is thus written in Gen. 41:45. These are the Onii in the Heliopolitan Nome according to Ptolemy. AND BUBASTI) Bubastus, the city from which the Bubastite Nome [comes], is the same name as that which is written in Hebrew פי־בסת. Bubastus is placed by geographers in the first position among the mouths of the Nile: where the cult of Diana is said to flourish even today.

Latin:

Vers. 17. JUVENES HELIOPOLEOS) און, in Hebræo tex- tu, quod recte legi potest On, & sic scribitus Genes. 41, 45. Hi sunt Onii in Heliopolitano Nomo apud Ptolemæum. ET BVBASTI) Bubastus, urbs unde Bubastites No- mos, idem est nomen quod Hebraice scribitur פי־בסת. Bubas primo loco inter ostia Nili à Geogra- phis locatur: ubi cultus Dianæ hodieque vigere dicitur.

## 30:18
Vers. 18. AND IN TAPHNIS) In the Pelusian Daphnis. See what [is written] at Isaiah 30:4 and Jeremiah 43:7, 8. THE DAY SHALL GROW DARK) See what [is written] at Matthew 24:29. A CLOUD SHALL COVER IT) See above [at] 3.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET IN TAPHNIS) In Daphnis Pelusiis. Vide quæ ad Esaiam 30, 4. & Jerem. 43, 7. 8. NIGRESCET DIES) Vide quæ ad Matth. 24, 29. IPSAM NVBES OPERIET) Suprav. 3.

## 30:20
Vers. 20. AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE ELEVENTH YEAR) Not long after that revelation which was written down in chapter 29.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET FACTVM EST IN UNDECIMO ANNO) Non multo post illam revelationem, quæ perscripta est capite 29.

## 30:21
Vers. 21. I HAVE BROKEN THE ARM OF PHARAOH KING OF EGYPT) I have now begun to execute my decrees against Apries, with the Cyrenians stirred up against him,

Latin:

Vers. 21. BRACHIVM PHARAONIS REGIS ÆGYPTI CONFREGI) Incepi jam exequi decreta mea contra Aprien, Cyrenæis in eum concitatis,

## 30:22
Vers. 22. HIS STRONG ARM) The LXX [read] τοὺς βραχίονας αὐτοῦ τοὺς ἰσχυροὺς καὶ τεταμένους, where Jerome notes here that τεταγμένους had been wrongly written in some codices. IT IS NOT BOUND UP, TO RESTORE HEALTH TO IT) His evil will not only not be alleviated, but will also grow worse day by day,

Latin:

Vers. 22. EJVS BRACHIVM FORTE) LXX. τὺς βραχίο- νας αὐτῆ τὺς ἰχυρὺς κὶ τεταμένυς, ubi τεταγμένυς male fuisse in codicibus nonnullis scriptum notat hic Hieronymus. NON EST OBVOLVTVM, VT RESTITVERE- TVR EI SANITAS) Malum ejus non modo non leva- bitur, sed & magis ingravescet in dies,

## 30:24
Vers. 24. AND I WILL STRENGTHEN THE ARM OF THE KING OF BABYLON) Civil war will be followed by foreign [war]. THEY SHALL GROAN WITH THE GROANINGS OF THE SLAIN) As one who is wounded unto death is accustomed to groan.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET CONFORTABO BRACHIVM REGIS BA- BYLONIS) Civile bellum excipietur ab externo. GEMENT GEMITIBVS INTERFECTI) Ut ge- mere soletis, qui ad mortem vulneratus est.

## 31:1 Argument
THE EIGHTH REVELATION. CHAPTER XXXI.

The loftiness of King Pharaoh is compared with Assur, and the similar destruction of both is indicated.

Vers. 1. IN THE THIRD MONTH) This revelation was made two months later than the one which immediately preceded it.

Latin:

OCTAVA REVELATIO. CAPUT XXXI.

Sublimitas Regis Pharaonis cum Assur com- paratur, & utriusque similis interitus de- signatur.

Vers. 1. TERTIO MENSE) Duobus mensibus poste- rius hæc revelatio facta est, quam ea quæ proxime præ- cessit.

## 31:2
Vers. 2. TO WHOM ART THOU BECOME LIKE IN THY GREATNESS) Namely, to the Assyrian king, who was equally arrogant, who, just as he was treated very badly by the Chaldeans, so too will the King of Egypt be treated by the same. He then illustrates the very pride and ruin of the Assyrian with other comparisons, so that the Egyptian may the better understand what he is to expect for himself.

Latin:

Vers. 2. CVI SIMILIS FACTVS ES IN MAGNITVDI- NE TVA) Nempe regi Assyrio perinde fastuoso, qui sicut à Chaldæis pessime tractatus est, ita & ab eisdem tra- ctabitur rex Ægypti, Ipsam deinde Assyrii superbiam ac cladem aliis comparationibus illustrat, quo magis intelli- gat Ægyptius quid sibi sit expectandum.

## 31:3
Vers. 3. AS A CEDAR IN LEBANON) Kings are accustomed to be compared to tall trees. Dan. 4:17, 18, 19. Above 17:3.

The Assyrian Kingdom is compared to a Cedar because of the loftiness or majesty of its empire; likewise because of its firmness, because a cedar is not damaged by moths and rot; and because many peoples had sought tranquility under that kingdom, as if under its shadow. The Assyrian kingdom was previously distinct from the Chaldean or Babylonian. But once the Assyrian was conquered, the Babylonians and Chaldeans themselves were called [by these names] indiscriminately. See 2 Kings 19:37, Is. 10:21, 36:38, Ezra 4:2, 3.

AND LEAFY WITH BRANCHES. In Hebrew it is singular: and with a branch making shade. A thicket is noted, both tender and dense, by the Hebrew word, suitable for covering men and cattle, so that both the tenderness or excellence of the King and his power to protect his subjects may be intimated. Cornelius à Lapide wrongly understands Pharaoh by Assur, whom it is too manifest that the Prophet compares with the Assyrian, and therefore is distinct from him.

ITS TOP WAS RAISED AMONG THE DENSE BRANCHES) Its top reached to the clouds. For עב also signifies a cloud, LXX. into the midst of the clouds.

Latin:

Vers. 3. QVASI CEDRVS IN LIBANO) Solent Reges excelsis arboribus comparari. Dan. 4, 17. 18. 19. Supra 17, 3.

Comparatur Regnum Assyriacum Cedro pro- pter sublimitatem seu majestatem ejus impe- rii; item propter firmitatem, quia cedrus à tineis, & carie non læditur; & quod multi populi sub eo regno, tanquam sub umbra tranquillitatem quæ- sierant. Fuit Assyrium regnum antea à Chaldæo vel Babylonio distinctum. Sed devicto Assyrio promi- scue ipsimet Babylonii, & Chaldæi dicti sunt. Vid. 2. Reg. 19, 37. Es. 10, 21. 36, 38. Esd. 4, 2. 3.

ET FRONDIBUS NEMOROSUS. In Ebr. singulare est: & fronde umbram fa- ciente. Notatur virgultum & tenerum & densum voce Ebræa, aptum tegendis hominibus & peco- ribus, ut innuatur & teneritas seu excellentiaRe- gis & potentia ejus ad protegendos subditos. Per- peram autem per Assur Cornel. à Lapide Pharao- nem intelligit, quemProphetam cum Assyrio com- parare, adeoque ab illo distinctum esse, nimis ma- nifestum est.

INTER CONDENSAS FRONDES ELEVATVM EST CACVMEN EJVS) Ad nubes pervenit cacumen ejus. Nam עב etiam nubem significat, LXX. εἰς μέσον νεφελῶν.

## 31:4
Ver. 4. THE WATERS NOURISHED IT) A huge abundance of waters, such as in the Tigris and the Nile.

The riches and revenues of the Assyrian kingdom are noted.

AND IT SENT OUT ITS RIVULETS TO ALL THE TREES OF THE REGION) It is a metaphor: For by the rivulets he understands the offshoots of the trees; but by the offshoots, anagogically, colonies.

Osiander rightly: the kingdom was so powerful and opulent that it rendered its nobles and princes quite powerful.

Latin:

Vers. 4. AQVÆ NVTRIERVNT ILLVM) Ingens aquarum abundantia, qualis in Tygride & Nilo.

Notantur divitiæ & proventus regni Assyriaci.

ET RIVVLOS SVOS EMISIT AD VNIVERSA LIGNA REGIONIS) Est Metaphora: Nam per rivulos intelligit arborum traduces; per traduces vero ἀναγωγικῶς colonias.

Recte Osiander: adeo potens erat regnum, atque opulentum, ut optimates & Principes suos admodum potentes redderet.

## 31:5
Ver. 5.

THEREFORE ITS HEIGHT WAS RAISED) It became proud. See below 10. For often here and elsewhere in the Prophets the same thing is repeated.

This can still be understood concerning the exaltation of the kingdom, namely that it surpassed all other kingdoms in sublimity and eminence.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PROPTEREA ELEVATA EST ALTITVDO EJVS) Superbiit. Vide infra 10. Nam sæpe hic & alibi in Prophetis res eadem repetitur.

Potest hoc adhuc accipi de exaltatione regni, quod nempe superarit omnia alia regna sublimitate & eminentia.

## 31:6
Ver. 6.

IN ITS BRANCHES ALL THE BIRDS OF THE HEAVENS MADE THEIR NESTS) Many nations fled to its protection. Above 18, 23. Dan. 4, 9. 19.

AND UNDER ITS BRANCHES ALL THE BEASTS OF THE FIELD BROUGHT FORTH) Peoples grew, with auspicious offspring.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

IN RAMIS EJVS FECERVNT NIDOS OMNIA VOLATILIA COELI) Multæ gentes ad ejus tutelam confugerunt. Supra 18, 23. Dan. 4, 9. 19.

ET SVB FRONDIBVS EJVS GENVERVNT OMNES BESTIÆ SALTVVM) Crevere populi, fausta sobole.

## 31:8
Ver. 8.

IN THE PARADISE OF GOD) A manner of speaking the same as above 28, 12.

EVERY TREE OF THE PARADISE OF GOD) That is, of Babylon, where once the paradise had been given to Adam.

Osiander explained it thus; every tree of the paradise of God is not likened to it, that is, no King of the people of God (for the Church is the garden of God and Paradise) was equal to this one.

AND THE PLANE TREES) ערמנים or ערמנין in the Chaldean are chestnut trees.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

IN PARADISO DEI) Loquendi genus idem quod supra 28, 12.

OMNE LIGNVM PARADISI DEI) Id est, Babyloniæ, ubi quondam paradisus fuerat Adamo datus.

Osiander ita exposuit; omne lignum paradisi Dei non est assimilatum illi, id est, nullus Rex populi Dei (Ecclesia enim est hortus Dei & Paradisus) fuit huic æqualis.

ET PLATANI) ערמנים sive ערמנין Chaldæis sunt castaneæ.

## 31:9
Ver. 9. AND ALL THE TREES OF PLEASURE EMULATED IT) The most delicate trees envied it.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET ÆMVLATA SVNT EUM OMNIA LIGNA VOLVPTATIS) Inviderunt ei arbores delicatissimæ.

## 31:11
Ver. 11.

INTO THE HAND OF THE MIGHTIEST OF THE NATIONS) The Chaldeans.

DOING HE SHALL DO TO HIM) He shall treat him according to his pleasure.

I HAVE CAST HIM OUT) From his empire.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

IN MANV FORTISSIMI GENTIVM) Chaldæi.

FACIENS FACIET EI) Tractabit eum pro libitu.

EJECI EVM) De imperio.

## 31:12
Ver. 12. AND STRANGERS SHALL CUT HIM DOWN) Strangers shall cut him down: that is, the Chaldeans.

AND THE MOST CRUEL OF THE NATIONS) Terrible among the nations. עריצים, the Greeks translate sometimes as δυνατοὶ, sometimes as ἀνόμοι, sometimes otherwise.

AND THEY SHALL CAST HIM UPON THE MOUNTAINS) As is wont to happen to trees, which, placed on the highest ridges, are cut down.

AND IN ALL THE VALLEYS) Subject to the mountain.

AND HIS SHRUBS SHALL BE BROKEN IN ALL THE CLIFFS OF THE EARTH) אפיקים, sometimes signifies torrents, sometimes by metonymy, depressed places. The LXX here: in every plain.

AND ALL THE PEOPLES OF THE EARTH SHALL DEPART FROM HIS SHADE) He mixes the apodosis of the comparison, as often both here and other writers do. See what we have said at Matt. 23, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET SVCCIDENT EVM ALIENI) Succident eum extranei: id est, Chaldæi.

ET CRVDELISSIMI NATIONVM) Terribiles in gentibus. עריצים, Græci modo vertunt δυνατοὶ, modo ἀνόμοι, interdum aliter.

ET PROJICIENT EVM SVPER MONTES) Ut solet fieri arboribus, quæ in summis jugis positæ exscinduntur.

ET IN CVNCTIS CONVALLIBVS) Monti subjectis.

ET CONFRINGENTVR ARBVSTA EJVS IN VNIVERSIS RVPIBVS TERRÆ) אפיקים, modo torrentes significat, modo per μετωνυμίαν locos depressos. LXX. hic: ἐν πάντι πεδίῳ.

ET RECEDENT DE VMBRACVLO EJVS OMNES POPVLI TERRÆ) Permiscet comparationis ἀπόδοσιν, ut sæpe & hic & alii Scriptores. Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. 23, 27.

## 31:13
Vers. 13. IN HIS RUIN ALL THE BIRDS OF THE HEAVEN HAVE DWELT) He returns to the comparison. He wishes to say this: birds and wild beasts have insulted his trunk. It is an allegory: he was held in contempt by all.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN RVINA EJVS HABITAVERUNT OMNIA VOLATILIA COELI) Redit ad comparationem. Hoc vult dicere: trunco ejus insultarunt volucres & feræ. Allegoria est: contemtur fuit ab omnibus.

## 31:14
Vers. 14. WHEREFORE THEY SHALL NOT BE EXALTED) Let them not be exalted.

NOR SHALL THEY PLACE THEIR SUBLIMITY AMONG THE WOODED AND LEAFY) Let them not lift themselves up on high into the clouds. See above v. 4.

NOR SHALL THEY STAND IN THEIR SUBLIMITY) Let them not trust in their tallness.

ALL ARE DELIVERED UNTO DEATH) He returns to the apodosis concerning those high-ranking Assyrian men who had been with Sennacherib: from which the Egyptian might gather what he is to expect for himself.

TO THE LOWEST EARTH) To the lower parts of the earth, where the graves are: εἰς τὰ κατώτερα τῆς γῆς. Ephes. 4. v. 9.

IN THE MIDST OF THE CHILDREN OF MEN, TO THEM THAT GO DOWN INTO THE PIT) like commoners who are cast into a pit. בני אדם to the Hebrews are men of the common people. We had that expression in the midst above in ch. 29 and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QVAMOBREM NON ELEVABVNTVR) Ne elevantor.

NEC PONENT SVBLIMITATEM SVAM INTER NEMOROSA ATQVE FRONDOSA) Ne in sublime se efferant intra nubes. Vide supra v. 4.

NEC STABVNT IN SVBLIMITATE SVA) Ne proceritati suæ fidant.

OMNES TRADITI SVNT IN MORTEM) Redit ad ἀπόδοσιν de Assyriis illis viris summatibus, qui cum Senacheribo fuerant: unde colligere possit Ægyptius quid sibi expectandum sit.

AD TERRAM VLTIMAM) Ad infera terræ, ubi sunt sepulchra: εἰς τὰ κατώτερα τῆς γῆς. Ephes. 4. v. 9.

IN MEDIO FILIORVM HOMINVM, AD EOS QVI DESCENDVNT IN LACVM) instar plebejorum qui dejiciuntur in foveam. בני אדם Hebræis homines de plebe. Locutionem illam in medio habuimus supra c. 29. & alibi.

## 31:15
Vers. 15. IN THE DAY WHEN HE WENT DOWN TO THE LOWER WORLD) Sennacherib himself killed by his sons, 2 Kings 19, 37. Why is it not permitted here to take the word שׁאול as referring to infernal punishment, to which the Assyrian was altogether carried off?

I HAVE BROUGHT MOURNING) In all Assyria.

I COVERED HIM WITH THE ABYSS, AND RESTRAINED HIS RIVERS AND HELD BACK THE MANY WATERS) I caused the abyss (a huge abundance of rivers) to cover itself over him. To cover oneself is characteristic of those who mourn. By waters, however, understand peoples, Apocal. 17, 15.

LEBANON WAS SADDENED OVER HIM) That is, Syria, which had been allied to the Assyrians. See 2 Kings 18, 34. In the Hebrew it is: I caused Lebanon to be clothed in black on his account.

AND ALL THE TREES OF THE FIELD WERE SHAKEN) That is, all the princes round about. See above 3.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IN DIE QVANDO DESCENDIT AD INFEROS) Sennacheribus ipse à filiis occisus, 2. Reg. 19, 37. De infernali pœna vocem שׁאול hic cur non liceat accipere, ad quam omnino abreptus est Assyrius?

INDVXI LVCTVM) In omni Assyria.

OPERVI EVM ABYSSO, ET PROHIBVI FLV- MINA EJVS ET COERCVI AQVAS MVLTAS ) Feci ut de eo abyssus (ingens fluminum abundantia) se ope- riat. Operire se est lugentium. Per aquas autem populos intellige Apocal. 17, 15.

CONTRISTATVS EST SVPER EVM LIBA- NVS) Id est, Syria, quæ fœderata Assyriis fuerat. Vide 2. Reg. 18, 34. In Hebræo est: Atris indui feci Libanum ejus causa.

ET OMNIA LIGNA AGRI CONCVSSA SVNT) Id est, omnes circum principes. Vide supra 3.

## 31:16
Vers. 16.

AND ALL THE TREES WERE CONSOLED IN THE LOWEST EARTH) That is, they were in need of consolation, as those who mourn are wont to be: in the earth, supply, sitting, which is the custom of those who mourn, Job 2, 13. He mixes the comparison and the ἀπόδοσις again.

Others more correctly [say] that others received consolation from this destruction: Which also pleased the blessed Hülseman. Osiander; The nobles and kings of the Israelite Kingdom congratulated themselves that the Assyrian Monarchy had collapsed.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET CONSOLATA SVNT IN TERRA INFI- MA OMNIA LIGNA) Id est, eguerunt consolatione, ut solent lugentes: in terra, supple, sedentes, qui mos lu- gentium, Job. 2, 13. Permiscet iterum comparationem & ἀπόδοσιν.

Rectius alii, consolationem accepisse alios ex hoc interitu: Quod etiam B. Hülseman. placuit. Osiander; Gratulati sibi sunt Israëlitici Regni pro- ceres & Reges, quod Assyriaca Monarchia cor- ruisset.

## 31:17
Vers. 17.

FOR THEY ALSO SHALL DESCEND WITH HIM INTO HELL TO THOSE SLAIN BY THE SWORD, AND THE ARM OF EACH ONE SHALL DWELL UNDER HIS SHADOW IN THE MIDST OF THE NATIONS) The copula placed here for a relative pronoun, which is not infrequent among the Hebrews, obscures the sense. But you may rightly translate: For they also shall descend with him to the grave (where those are who have been slain by the sword), whoever among those nations submitted their strength to his protection. With the affairs of the Assyrians broken, it was easy for the Chaldeans to afflict the Syrians and their neighbors with the greatest disasters. Isaiah 17, 4.

Osiander has it thus in this place: For they also shall descend with him to hell, to many others slain by the sword: For they dwelt under his arm, under his shadow in the midst of the nations. Furthermore, since all the Israelite Kings (Israelite, I say) were impious, and many (in the kingdom of Israel) subjects followed the same impiety; there is no doubt but that they also truly descended with the impious Assyrians into hell with their souls. This is Osiander.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

NAM ET IPSI CVM EO DESCENDENT IN INFERNVM AD INTERFECTOS GLADIO, ET BRACHIVM VNIVSCVJVSQVE SEDEBIT SVB VMBRACVLO EJVS IN MEDIO NATIONVM ) Copula hic posita pro relativo pronomine, quod Hebræis non infrequens sensum obscurat. Recte autem vertas: Nam & illi cum eo ad sepulchrum descendent (ubi sunt qui gla- dio sunt interfecti) quicunque in illis gentibus suam vim illius tu- tela submiserunt. Fractis Assyriorum rebus, facile fuit Chal- dæis Syros eorumque vicinos cladibus maximis afficere. Esaiæ 17, 4.

Osiander ita h. l. habet: Nam & ipsi cum eo de- scendent ad infernum, ad alios multos interfectos gladio: Etenim sub brachio ejus habitarunt, sub um- bra ejus in medio gentium. Cæterum cum omnes Reges Israëlitici (Israëlitici, inquam) impii fue- rint, multique (in regno Israëlis) subditi eandem impietatem sint sequuti; non dubium est, quin il- li etiam vere cum Assyriis impiis in infernum ani- mabus suis descenderint. Hæc Osiander.

## 31:18
Vers. 18.

TO WHOM ARE YOU LIKENED O RENOWNED ONE) Do you understand, King of Egypt, to whom you are to be like? I have shown you a living image of your fortune.

BEHOLD YOU ARE BROUGHT DOWN) You shall be brought down.

IN THE MIDST OF THE UNCIRCUMCISED YOU SHALL SLEEP.) Because circumcision was a mockery to you, the uncircumcised shall enclose you on all sides and bring death upon you. See a similar passage above 28, 10.

HE IS PHARAOH AND ALL HIS MULTITUDE) LXX. ὕτως ὁ Φαραὼν κὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς ἰχύος αὐτῶ. Thus Pharaoh, supply, shall be. He shall find such an end with his own, as I have depicted under the example of the Assyrian.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

CVI ASSIMILATVS ES O INCLYTE) Intel- ligisne rex Ægypti cui futurus sis similis? exhibui tibi vivam fortunæ tuæ imaginem.

ECCE DEDVCTVS ES) Deduceris.

IN MEDIO INCIRCVMCISORVM DORMIES.) Quia circumcisio tibi ludibrio fuit, incircumcisi te undi- que claudent, mortemque tibi inferent. Vide simile supra 28, 10.

IPSE EST PHARAO ET OMNIS MVLTITVDO EJVS) LXX. ὕτως ὁ Φαραὼν κὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς ἰχύος αὐτῶ. Sic Pharao, supple, erit. Talem cum suis inveniet exitum, qualem sub Assyrii exemplo depinxi.

## 32:1 Argument
NINTH REVELATION. CHAPTER XXXII.

Pharaoh, however sublime, is to be crushed by the King of Babylon: at whose devastation very many Kings shall be astonished: and more nations shall be brought down with him into the abyss.

Ver. 1.

IN THE TWELFTH YEAR IN THE TWELFTH MONTH) From the deportation of Jeconiah, as Ezekiel counts. This is indeed, with Jerusalem already cut off, around which time

King Amasis (to whom this prediction pertains) began to rise up against Apries.

Latin:

NONA REVELATIO. CAPUT XXXII.

Pharao, quantumvis sublimis, conterendus est à Rege Babylonis: cujus vastatione plurimi Reges obstupescent: pluresque na- tiones cum eo in abyssum deducentur.

Vers. 1.

DVODECIMO ANNO IN MENSE DVODE- CIMO) A deportatione Jechoniæ, ut numerat Ezechiel. Id vero est, excisis jam Hierosolymis, circa quod tempus

Rex Amasis (ad quem hæc prædictio pertinet) contra A- prien se cœpit erigere.

## 32:2
Ver. 2.

TO THE DRAGON THAT IS IN THE SEA) To the whale. For this also is called תנין.

YOU PUSHED WITH YOUR HORN IN YOUR RIVERS, AND TROUBLED THE WATERS WITH YOUR FEET, AND FOULED THEIR RIVERS) Coming out of the sea into the rivers you troubled the waters with your feet, and indeed you trampled the whole rivers. The simile seems taken from the Hippopotamus, which has hooves like an ox. The sense is: going forth from your empire, you trampled neighboring cities and whole nations. We derived תגח from גוח. But the LXX from נגח. For they translate ἐκεράτιζες, that is, you butted, namely the smaller fish.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DRACONI QVI EST IN MARI) Balænæ. Nam & hæc תנין dicitur.

VENTILABAS CORNV IN FLVMINIBVS TVIS, ET CONTVRBABAS AQVAS PEDIBVS TVIS, ET CONCVLCABAS FLVMINA EARVM) Prodiens è mari in flumina turbabas aquas pedibus, quin & to- ta flumina conculcabas. Videtur similitudo ab Hippopotamo sumta, cui ungulæ quales bovi. Sensus est: ex imperio tuo egrediens, vicinas civitates, gentesque totas proterebas. Derivavimus תגח à גוח. At LXX. à נגח. Vertunt enim ἐκεράτιζες, id est, arietabas, nempe minores pisces

## 32:3
I WILL SPREAD MY NET OVER THEE) I will bring others who shall press thee on every side. Supra 12, 13. 17, 10.

I WILL DRAW THEE OUT IN MY NET) I will lead thee out from safe places.

Latin:

EXPANDAM SVPER TE RETE MEVM) Alios adducam qui te premant undique. Supra 12, 13. 17, 10.

EXTRAHAM TE IN SAGENA MEA) Educam te è locis tutis.

## 32:4
Ver. 4.

AND I WILL CAST THEE UPON THE LAND) I will take away thy vigor, as a fish drawn onto the land. Supra 29, 5.

I WILL MAKE ALL THE FOWLS OF THE HEAVEN TO DWELL UPON THEE, AND I WILL SATIATE THE BEASTS OF ALL THE EARTH WITH THEE) Fierce and rapacious men shall invade Egypt, and shall plunder it. See supra 29, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET PROJICIAM IN TERRAM) Vigorem tibi auferam, velut pisci in terram tracto. Supra 29, 5.

HABITATE FACIAM SVPER TE OMNIA VOLATILIA COELI, ET SATVRABO DE TE BESTIAS VNIVERSÆ TERRÆ) Homines feri ac rapaces Ægyptum invadent, ac deprædabuntur. Vide su- pra 29, 5.

## 32:5
Ver. 5.

AND I WILL LAY THY FLESH UPON THE MOUNTAINS) The flesh of thy men, whom the Chaldeans shall kill.

WITH THY CORRUPTION) That is, of thy people.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET DABO CARNES TVAS SVPER MON- TES) Carnes hominum tuorum, quos interficiens Chaldæi.

SANIE TVA) Id est, tuorum.

## 32:6
Ver. 6.

THE VALLEYS SHALL BE FILLED WITH THEE) With thy people. For the king and the people are considered the same.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

VALLES IMPLEBVNTVR EX TE) Tuis. Nam rex & populus idem censentur.

## 32:7
Ver. 7.

AND I WILL COVER WHEN THOU SHALT BE EXTINGUISHED THE HEAVEN) When thou shalt be extinguished, that is, when thy splendor shall have been taken away. Job 18, 4. But what is said, that the heaven shall be covered, that the stars shall be black, the sun veiled by a cloud, the moon dark, is indeed accustomed to have a signification of sadness, as we have said at Matt. 24, 29. But it seems to be added here, moreover, that there shall be such a slaughter (for that which follows, when thy wounded shall have fallen, pertains to this) that the vapors which the corpses shall emit shall take away the sight of the heaven and the stars. Lucan to Caesar:

But the wasting peoples snatch the Pharsalian fields from you, and hold the plains, the victor having been put to flight.

Seneca in Oedipus: Phoebe's sister glides through the dark sky, and the sad world grows pale with a new cloud. No star shines in the serene nights: but a heavy and black vapor broods over the lands, an infernal face has covered the citadels of the heavenly ones and the highest houses.

See a similar passage in Isaiah 34:4, and what is said there.

However, the blessed Hulseman warned here that these are not to be snatched up as signs of the second coming of Christ, as Stella and Toletus do at Luke 21:25, because the discourse here is about Pharaoh and Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET OPERIAM CVM EXSTINCTUS FVERIS COELVM) Cum exstinctus fueris, id est, cum splendor tibi adeptus fuerit. Job. 18, 4. Quod autem dicitur cælum opertum iri, stellas atras fore, solem obductum nube, lunam obscuram, solet quidem mœstitiæ habere significationem ut diximus ad Matth. 24, 29. Sed addendum insuper hic videtur, tantam stragem fore, (nam huc illud pertinet quod sequitur, cum ceciderint vulnerati tui) ut vapores quos emittent cadavera ademturi sint cæli siderumque conspe- ctus. Lucanus ad Cæsarem:

Sed tibi tabentes populi Pharsalica rura Eripiunt, camposque tenent, victore fugato.

Seneca Oedipode: Obscura cælo labitur Phœbi soror, Tristisque mundus nubilo pallet novo. Nullum serenis noctibus sidus micat: Sed gravis & ater incubat terris vapor, Obtexit arces cælitum ac summas domos Inferna facies.

Vide similem locum Esaiaæ 34, 4. & ibi dicta.

Non autem cum Stella & Toleto ad Luc. 21, 25. hæc ad signa secundi adventus Christi rapienda esse, monuit hic B. Hulseman. quia de Pharaone hic sermo est, & Ægypto.

## 32:9
AND I WILL PROVOKE THE HEART OF MANY PEOPLES) I will move, as the Chaldean has it here: I will shake with grief: for כעס is also accustomed to be translated by ἀθυμεῖν, and הכעים by ἀθυμίαν, by a certain catachresis.

WHEN I SHALL BRING THY DESTRUCTION AMONG THE NATIONS UPON THE LANDS WHICH THOU KNOWEST NOT) Where the captive Egyptians, having been led into distant lands, brought certain news of the slaughter. Thus the LXX rightly here.

Latin:

ET IRRITABO COR POPVLORVM MVL- TORVM) Commovebo, ut hic Chaldæus: mœrore con- cutiam: nam כעס per ἀθυμεῖν, & הכעים per ἀθυμίαν e- tiam verti solet, per κατάχρησιν quandam.

CVM INDVXERO CONTRITIONEM TVAM IN GENTIBVS SVPER TERRAS QVAS NESCIS) Vbi captivi Ægyptii in terras longinquas adducti certum attulerint nuncium cladis. Ita hic LXX. recte.

## 32:10
Verse 10.

AND I WILL MAKE MANY PEOPLES ASTONISHED AT THEE, AND THEIR KINGS SHALL BE AFRAID WITH GREAT HORROR FOR THEE, WHEN MY SWORD SHALL BEGIN TO FLY OVER THEIR FACES) Understand the African peoples and kings, to whom the Chaldeans came through Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET STVPESCERE FACIAM SVPER TE PO- PVLOS MVLTOS, ET REGES EORVM HOR- RORE NIMIO, FORMIDABVNT SVPER TE CVM VOLARE COEPERIT GLADIVS MEVS SVPER FA- CIES EORVM) Populos & reges Afros intellige, ad quos per Ægyptum venere Chaldæi.

## 32:13
Verse 13.

AND I WILL DESTROY ALL ITS BEASTS THAT WERE UPON THE MANY WATERS AND THE FOOT OF MAN SHALL NOT TROUBLE THEM ANY MORE, NEITHER SHALL THE HOOF OF BEASTS TROUBLE THEM) Just as men crossing through fords, and horses when they are led to water, make the waters turbid: so the infantry and cavalry of the Egyptians were accustomed to trouble the neighboring peoples, who are signified under the name of waters (as above 2).

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET PERDAM OMNIA JVMENTA EJVS QVÆ ERANT SVPER AQVAS PLVRIMAS ET NON CONTVRBABIT EAS PES HOMINIS VL- TRA, NEQVE VNGVLA JVMENTORVM TVR- BABIT EAS) Sicut homines per vada transeuntes, & equi ubi aquatum ducuntur, turbidas faciunt aquas: ita Ægy- ptiorum pedites & equites populos vicinos, qui sub aqua- rum significantur nomine, (ut supra 2.) solebant con- turbare.

## 32:14
Verse 14.

Vers. 14. THEN I WILL MAKE THEIR WATERS PURE AND I WILL MAKE THEIR RIVERS FLOW LIKE OIL) That is, those peoples will rest from the Egyptian violence, as the Chaldean well explains here. See above 29, 9. In Hebrew: Then I will make them subside: and afterwards: I will make them walk or flow like oil. Pharaoh, like a dragon, had troubled many waters: v. 2. now there will be malakia and tranquility, of which oil is the symbol, figuring gentleness and meekness; Ps. 55, 22. Prov. 5, 3. 6. 21, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

Vers. 14. TVNC PVRISSIMAS REDDAM AQVAS EO- RVM ET FLVMINA EORVM QVASI OLEVM AD- DVGAM) Id est, quiescent illi populi a vi Ægyptia, ut bene hic explicat Chaldæus. Vide supra 29, 9. In Ebr. Tunc subsidere faciam: & postea: quasi oleum ambulare vel fluere faciam. Pharao Draco- nis instar aquas plurimas turbarat: v. 2. jam μαλα- xía & tranquillitas erit cujus symbolum est oleum, lenitatem & mansuetudinem figurans; Psal. 55, 22. Prov. 5, 3. 6. 21, 17.

## 32:16
Vers. 16. IT IS A LAMENTATION AND THEY SHALL LAMENT HER) The sense is the same as above 15. at the end. This prophecy is lamentable: yet it will happen thus. THE DAUGHTERS OF THE NATIONS SHALL LAMENT HIM) They will use similar words, having known the evils of Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 16. PLANCTVS EST ET PLANGENT EAM) Sen- sus idem qui supra 15. in fine Lamentabilis est hæc Pro- phetia: tamen sic eveniet. FILIÆ GENTIVM PLANGENT EVM) Verbis similibus utentur cognitis Ægypti malis.

## 32:17
Vers. 17. IN THE FIFTEENTH OF THE MONTH) Said before: that is, not many days after the revelation which preceded.

Latin:

Vers. 17. IN QVINTA DECIMA MENSIS) Dicti ante: id est, non multis diebus post revelationem quæ præ- cessit.

## 32:18
Vers. 18. AND DRAW HER DOWN, HER AND THE DAUGHTERS OF THE MIGHTY NATIONS TO THE LOWEST EARTH) The lowest. That is, sing a song for Egypt as if she were dead, such as is wont to be sung for those who are let down into the grave. Moreover, this whole song is a prosopopoeia clearly similar to the other, which is about the Assyrian in Isaiah 14, 10. Just as poets and prophets are said to do what they sing.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET DETRAHE EAM IPSAM ET FILIAS GENTIVM ROBVSTARVM AD TERRAM VLTI- MAM) Infimam. Id est, cane Ægypto velut mortuæ car- men, quale cani solet iis, qui in sepulchrum demittuntur. Est autem totum hoc carmen προσωποποΐϊα plane similis alteri, quæ est de Assyrio apud Esaiam 14, 10. Sicut Poë- tæ it & Prophetæ facere dicuntur quæ canunt.

## 32:19
Vers. 19. WHOM DO YOU SURPASS IN BEAUTY?) In what are you better, namely than other nations who have received equal disasters, having also lost their empire, which is life to nations. DESCEND AND SLEEP WITH THE UNCIRCUMCISED) Since you have despised the circumcised. See above 31. vers. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 19. QVO PVLCRIOR ES) In quo melior es, aliis scilicet gentibus quæ pares clades accepere, amisso etiam imperio, quæ vita est gentibus. DESCENDE ET DORMI CVM INCIRCV- CISIS) Quandoquidem circumcisos sprevisti. Vide supra 31. vers. 18.

## 32:20
Vers. 20. IN THE MIDST OF THOSE SLAIN BY THE SWORD THEY SHALL FALL) The Egyptians have fallen. For he speaks now as if the matter were present. Similar is that of Lucan: - - - - But them. A great slaughter presses, and the corpses perform a part of the slaughter: living trunks crush the heavy bodies. Moreover, the middle signifies not only that the judgment will be public and manifest, but also the common condition of all. THE SWORD IS GIVEN) Egypt is given to the sword. So the Chaldean. THEY HAVE DRAWN HER AND ALL HER PEOPLES) Draw her down, namely into the grave. He speaks as if to the undertakers.

Latin:

Vers. 20. IN MEDIO INTERFECTORVM GLA- DIO CADENT) Cecidere Ægyptii. Loquitur enim jam quasi in re præsente. Simile illud Lucani: - - - - Sed illos. Magna premit strages, peraguntque cadavera partem Cœdis: viva graves elidunt corpora trunci. Medium autem non solum in publico & ma- nifestum fore judicium, sed etiam communem omnium conditionem significat. GLADIVS DATVS EST) Gladio data est Ægy- ptus. Ita Chaldæus. ATTRAXERVNT EAM ET OMNES POPV- LOS EJVS) Detrahite eam, nempe in sepulchrum. Lo- quitur quasi ad libitinarios.

## 32:21
Vers. 21. THEY SHALL SPEAK TO HIM) They will congratulate his arrival. See the place already mentioned of Isaiah. Namely, chapter 14, where the Prophet in an elegant and figurative speech introduces the dead Kings, who in the underworld receive the arriving Babylonian King.

Latin:

Vers. 21. LOQVENTVR EI) Gratulabuntur adven- tum. Vide locum jam dictum Esaiæ. Nimirum cap. 14. ubi Propheta oratione ele- ganti & figurata introducit Reges mortuos, qui apud inferos excipiunt Regem Babylonicum ad- ventantem.

## 32:22
Vers. 22. ROUND ABOUT HIM ARE HIS GRAVES) That is, they lie in the crowd of the dead. So also take the same words repeated.

Latin:

Vers. 22. IN CIRCVITV ILLIVS SEPVLCHRA EJVS) Id est, jacent in turba mortuorum. Sic & eadem verba repetita sume.

## 32:23
Vers. 23. WHOSE GRAVES ARE GIVEN IN THE LOWEST PARTS OF THE PIT) Whose graves are in some part of the pit: common, namely, to many. Osiander rightly expresses the sense. All the Assyrians who were slaughtered will lie buried around their kingdom, who were once formidable to the world. Assur is a most eminent example of prostrate power.

Latin:

Vers. 23. QVORVM DATA SVNT SEPVLCHRA IN NOVISSIMIS LACI) Quorum sepulchra sunt in parte aliqua foveæ: communis scilicet multis. Recte sensum exprimit Osiand. Omnes Assyrii qui trucidati sunt, jacebunt sepulti circa regnum suum, qui aliquando orbi terrarum erant formi- dabiles. Assur eminentissimum exemplum pro- stratæ potentiæ.

## 32:24
Vers. 24. THERE IS ELAM) The Elymaeans. He names those nations which had been in the auxiliaries to the Assyrian. AND THEY HAVE BORNE THEIR SHAME) The punishment of pride, partly prostrated by God at the walls of Jerusalem, partly conquered by the Babylonians.

Latin:

Vers. 24. IBI ELAM) Elymæi. Gentes illas nominat, quæ in auxiliis Assyrio fuerant. ET PORTAVERVNT IGNOMINIAM SVAM) Pœnam superbiæ, partim à Deo prostrati ad mœnia Hie- rosolymorum, partim victi à Babyloniis.

## 32:25
Vers. 25. IN THE MIDST OF THE SLAIN THEY HAVE SET HIS BED) His sepulchral ark. AMONG ALL HIS PEOPLES, ROUND ABOUT HIS GRAVE IS HIS SEPULCHRE) So that all that crowd might be around his grave. So also take it below v. 26.

Latin:

Vers. 25. IN MEDIO INTERFECTORVM POSVE- RVNT CVBILE EJVS) Arcam sepulchralem. IN VNIVERSIS POPVLIS EJVS, IN CIRCVI- TV EJVS SEPVLCHRVM ILLIVS) Vt turba tota illa esser circa sepulchrum ejus. Sic & infra sume v. 26.

## 32:26
Vers. 26. THERE IS MOSOCH) The Cappadocians and their neighbors. See above 27, 13. THUBAL) The Asiatic Iberians. See in the same place. See concerning these below c. 38, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 26. IBI MOSOCH) Cappadoces eorumque vicini. Vide supra 27, 13. THVBAL) Iberi Asiatici. Vide ibidem. Vide de his infra c. 38, 1.

## 32:27
Vers. 27. AND THEY SHALL NOT LIE WITH THE MIGHTY) These all pay the penalty for their sloth: they do not lie separately, but are heaped together into some one pit, as is wont to be done to the vanquished. Lucan after the battle of Pharsalus: - - - we seek not individual tombs, and separate pyres; one fire for the nations.

AND WITH THE FALLEN AND THE UNCIRCUMCISED) Who were indeed uncircumcised and impious, yet brave and magnanimous.

Thus v. 28. they are said to be in the midst of the uncircumcised, who are affected with a like punishment as they. Compare what is said at v. 20.

WHO WENT DOWN TO HELL WITH THEIR WEAPONS, AND LAID THEIR SWORDS UNDER THEIR HEADS) That is, they had them laid. Victors not only had individual sepulchres, but were also buried with their weapons in honor of their valor, 1 Maccab. 13. vers. 29.

To others, to lay swords under their heads is the same as to renounce their use, as soldiers are wont to do when going to bed, Judith 10.

AND THEIR INIQUITIES WERE UPON THEIR BONES) Better: and dwellings for their bones: that is, excellent ones were given, or solaces, for صون among the Arabs is solace. Statius: He gives solaces to great tombs. Their valor was attested by illustrious monuments.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET NON DORMIENT CVM FORTI- BVS) Hi omnes ignaviæ suæ pœnas dant: non seorsim jacent, sed in unam aliquam fossam congesti, ut victis fieri solet. Lucanus post prælium Pharsalicum: - - - petimus non singula busta, Discretosque rogos; unum de gentibus ignem.

CADENTIBVSQVE ET INCIRCVCISIS) Que incircumcisi quidem erant & impii, attamen fortes & ma-gnanimi.

Sic v. 28. in medio incircumcisorum esse dicun-tur, qui pari cum eis supplicio afficiuntur. Conf. quæ ad v. 20.

QVI DESCENDERVNT AD INFERNVM CVM ARMIS SVIS, ET POSVERVNT GLADIOS SVOS SVB CAPITIBVS SVIS) Id est, positos habuerunt. Victo-res non singula tantum habebant sepulchra, sed & in vir-tutis honorem cum armis suis sepeliebantur, 1. Maccab. 13. vers. 29.

Aliis ponere gladios sub capitibus idem est, quod abdicare eorum usum, uti solent milites cubitum ituri, Judith. 10.

ET FVERVNT INIQVITATES EORVM IN OSSIBUS EORVM) Melius: & habitacula pro ossibus eo-rum: data sunt scilicet egregia, aut solatia, nam صون de Arabibus est solatium. Statius: Dat Solatia grandibus sepulchris. Illustribus monumentis testata est eorum virtus.

## 32:28
Vers. 28. AND THOU THEREFORE IN THE MIDST OF THE UNCIRCUMCISED) But thou (Egypt) shalt lie in the crowd of the impious: as the vanquished are wont to do.

THOU SHALT SLEEP WITH THEM THAT ARE SLAIN BY THE SWORD) Not with the victors.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ET TV ERGO IN MEDIO INCIRCVM-CISORVM) At tu (Ægypte) in turba impiorum jacebis: ut victi solent.

DORMIES CVM INTERFECTIS GLADIO) Non cum victoribus.

## 32:29
Vers. 29. THERE IS IDUMEA) The Idumeans, likewise allies of the Assyrians.

Circumcised in body indeed, but who had uncircumcised hearts, and often grievously afflicted their kinsmen the Israelites.

WHO ARE GIVEN WITH THEIR ARMY WITH THEM THAT ARE SLAIN BY THE SWORD) Who were themselves also among the vanquished.

AND WITH THEM THAT GO DOWN INTO THE PIT) Among those who are indiscriminately cast into a common trench.

Latin:

Vers. 29. IBI IDVMÆA) Idumæi, socii itidem Assy-riorum.

Corporibus quidem circumcisi, sed qui corde da habebant incircumcisa, & consanguineos Israë-litas graviter sæpe affligebant.

QVI DATI SVNT CVM EXERCITV SVO CVM INTERFECTIS GLADIO) Qui & ipsi inter vi-ctos fuere.

ET CVM HIS QVI DESCENDVNT IN LA-CVM) Inter eos qui promiscue in communem foveam de-jiciuntur.

## 32:30
V. 30. THERE ALL THE PRINCES OF THE NORTH) The Tyrians who were to the north of the Jews, conquered in many battles by the Chaldean, and reduced to surrender. Above, chapters 26, 27, 28.

AND ALL THE HUNTERS) You will take it better as a proper noun, and translate it as Sidonians: for these too were conquered by the Chaldeans. Above, 28, 21. Nor does the Chaldean interpret it otherwise.

WHO WENT DOWN WITH THE SLAIN) Correctly. But the LXX, for נשת, read אשור, Assyrians.

Latin:

V. 30. IBI PRINCIPES AQVILONIS OMNES) Ty-rii qui Judæis ad Aquilonem, victi multis præliis à Chaldæo, & ad deditionem redacti. Supra 26. 27. 28. capp.

ET VNIVERSI VENATORES) Melius sumes pro nomine proprio, & vertes Sidonii: nam & hi victi à Chaldæis. Supra 28, 21. nec aliter h. c Chaldæus.

QVI DEDVCTI SVNT CVM INTERFECTIS) Recte. At LXX. pro נשת legere אשור Ἀσσύρ.

## 32:31
Ver. 31. PHARAOH SHALL SEE THEM AND SHALL BE COMFORTED) In the Hebrew: Pharaoh shall see them (at some time). When Amasis dies, he shall see so many others badly treated by the Assyrians. It is again a prosopopoeia, by which sense is attributed to the dead.

Latin:

Vers. 31. VIDIT EOS PHARAO ET CONSOLA-TVS EST) In Hebræo: Videbit eos (aliquando) Pharao. Ubi morietur Amasis, videbit tot alios ab Assyriis male tra-ctatos. Est iterum προσωποποιϊα, qua mortuis sensus affin-gitur.

## 32:32
Ver. 32. FOR I HAVE GIVEN MY TERROR IN THE LAND OF THE LIVING) So it is read in the margin. But the text has תתיתו, his terror, and φόβον ἀυτῶ, the LXX: Because I permitted that Egypt in the time of Necho should be a terror to the Jews. The land of the living is Judea, above 26, 20. The Chaldean also understands it thus.

HE SHALL SLEEP) He shall die. LXX. κοιμηθήσεται: that is, he shall lie with the dead.

IN THE MIDST OF THE UNCIRCUMCISED WITH THEM THAT ARE SLAIN BY THE SWORD) For the body of Amasis after death was taken from the monument and burned with fire: which the Egyptians consider shameful. Herodotus, Thalia.

Latin:

Vers. 32. QVIA DEDI TERROREM MEVM IN TERRA VIVENTIVM) Ita legitur in margine. At tex-tus habet תתיתו terrorem ejus, & φόβον ἀυτῶ, LXX: Quia permisi, ut Ægyptus tempore Necaonis terrori esset Ju-dæis. Terra viventium Judæa supra 26, 20. Sic accipit & Chaldæus.

DORMIVIT) Morietur. LXX. κοιμηθήσεται: id est; jacebit cum mortuis.

IN MEDIO INCIRCVMCISORVM CVM IN-TERFECTIS GLADIO) Nam corpus Amasis post mor-tem exemtum monumento & igne crematum est: quod turpe censent Ægyptii. Horodotus Thalia.

## 33:1 Argument
PART II. EXHIBITING CONSOLATORY SERMONS. CHAPTER XXXIII.

Concerning the watchman who is bound to announce impending evil, and the wicked man, if he be converted, being saved: with a dissuasion, that they should not trust in the land given to them in promise, since because of their iniquities they shall be destroyed, and the land shall be reduced to a wilderness, unless they repent.

Latin:

PARS II. CONCIONES CONSOLATO- RIAS EXHIBENS. CAPUT XXXIII.

De speculatore qui imminens malum annun- ciare tenetur, & impio, si convertatur sal- vando: cum dehortatione, ne confidant de terra sibi data in promissionem, quoniam propter suas iniquitates perdentur, terra in solitudinem redigetur, nisi pœnituerint.

## 33:2
Ver. 2.

SPEAK TO THE CHILDREN OF THY PEOPLE, AND THOU SHALT SAY) To those, namely, who had already been deported with Zedekiah. It is the same sense as above 3, 17. But it is repeated for the necessity of the times.

WHEN I BRING A SWORD UPON THE LAND) A transposed expression in the Hebrew manner: for, when I bring a sword (hostile) upon some region: that is, when enemies approach a region, which does not happen without my decree or permission.

AND THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND TAKE A MAN FROM AMONG THEIR LAST) Should someone appointed by the people owe as much diligence as he who is appointed by God?

Latin:

Vers. 2.

LOQVERE AD FILIOS POPVLI TVI, ET DI- CES) Illis scilicet, qui jam cum Sedecia erant deportati. Est idem sensus qui supra 3, 17. Sed pro necessitate tempo- rum repetitur.

TERRA CVM INDVXERO SVPER EAM GLA- DIVM) Locutio transposita more Hebræo: pro, ubi gla- dium (hostilem) super regionem aliquam introduxero: id est, ubi hostes regioni appropinquant, quod sine meo decre- to aut permissu non fit.

ET TVLERIT POPVLVS TERRÆ VIRVM V- NVM DE NOVISSIMIS SVIS) Sitantam diligentiam de- bet aliquis à populo constitutus, quantam is qui à Deo?

## 33:4
Ver. 4. AND HE DOES NOT KEEP WATCH) He does not take heed for himself.

HIS BLOOD SHALL BE UPON HIS OWN HEAD) To him, and indeed to him alone, shall the evil that befalls him be imputed.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET NON SE OBSERVAVERIT) Non sibi caberit.

SANGVIS IPSIVS SVPER CAPVT EJVS ERIT) Ipsi, & quidem soli, imputabitur malum, quod ei evenit.

## 33:6
Ver. 6.

AND TAKES FROM AMONG THEM A SOUL) Someone.

HE INDEED IN HIS INIQUITY) By his own fault. Because those who are in war must always take heed for themselves.

BUT HIS BLOOD I WILL REQUIRE FROM THE HAND OF THE WATCHMAN) He too shall be punished, who ought to have roused those who were negligent. Even the crime of sloth is a transgression in a soldier. L. omne. D. de re militari.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET TVLERIT DE EIS ANIMAM) Aliquem.

ILLE QVIDEM IN INIQVITATE SVA) Culpa sua. Quia perpetuo sibi cavere debent qui in bello sunt.

SANGVINEM AVTEM EJVS DE MANV SPE- CVLATORIS REQVIRAM) Punietur & ille, qui quam- vis negligentes excitare debuit. Etiam segnitiæ crimen in milite delictum est. L. omne. D. de re militari.

## 33:7
Ver. 7.

AND YOU, SON OF MAN) O son of man. אדם in place of the vocative.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET TV FILI HOMINIS) O fili hominis. אדם vice vocativi.

## 33:8
Ver. 8. O WICKED MAN, YOU SHALL SURELY DIE) For there is a tacit condition underlying this, if you remain such: above 18, and presently 10, you shall surely die: that is, you shall perish by an evil death before your time.

These things are to be understood rather of eternal death, as the punishment of sin, when the unfaithful persevere in impiety and depart without repentance. Compare v. 11 and what was said at chapter 18, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 8. IMPIE MORTE MORIERIS) Subest enim tacita conditio, si maneas talis: supra 18. & mox 10. morte morieris: id est mala morte peribis ante diem.

DE morte potius æterna, ceu peccati pœna, cum in impietate perseverant infideles, & sine pœnitentia decedunt, hæc intelligenda. Conf. v. 11. & quæ ad cap. 18, 19.

## 33:9
YOU HAVE DELIVERED YOUR SOUL) That which he said above: he shall save. You have preserved your life.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ANIMAM TVAM LIBERASTI) Quod su- pra dixit salvabit. Vitam tuam servasti.

## 33:10
OUR INIQUITIES AND OUR SINS ARE UPON US) God wishes that we pay the penalties for our crimes. What is done cannot be undone.

AND WE PINE AWAY IN THEM) Namely, by the edict of the law, Lev. 26:39.

Latin:

Vers. 10. INIQVITATES NOSTRÆ ET PECCATA NOSTRA SVPER NOS SVNT) Vult Deus ut criminum pœnas luamus. Factum, infectum fieri nequit.

ET IN IPSIS NOS TABESCIMVS) Nempe ex legis edicto Levit. 26, 39.

## 33:11
I DO NOT DESIRE THE DEATH OF THE WICKED) Compare the statement. The sense is the same as above, 18:23, 32.

No note of a compared sense appears here. This sentiment pertains to the antecedent will of God, according to which God in no way desires the death of man, but rather his conversion and life, as he is one for whose sake, and for whom, the Son of God himself underwent death: whence the absolute decree of Calvin is most solidly refuted. But as for what some among the Reformed—Calvin, Pareus, Polanus, Chamier, Panstrat. Cath. Tom. 3, lib. 3, cap. 6, § 10—except, that in the Hebrew it is not that God does not desire the death of the wicked, but that he does not take pleasure in the death of the wicked: I reply that the word חפץ in general denotes 'to will,' Ps. 5:5, Ps. 115:3, Cant. 2:7; furthermore, their delight is in those things which we will: If, therefore, God does not take pleasure in the death of the wicked, he certainly does not will it; for if he willed it, he would take pleasure in it. That this word introduces the will of good pleasure, Ps. 40:9, Ps. 50:17, Mal. 2:17, Isa. 55:11 openly teach. Add also Num. 14:8, 1 Kings 9:1, 2 Kings 22:20. The Remonstrants, regarding this exception of Calvin—that God does not indeed desire the death of the perishing, insofar as he does not take pleasure in the destruction of the creature, and insofar as he approves of the conversion of men, not insofar as he wills to effect it in all—respond in Script. Dordrac. p. 241: If God approves of the life and conversion of all, why has he absolutely decreed the destruction of most? And they say this is similar to if, to Hezekiah seeking a prolongation of life, the answer had been: 'Be of good courage, O King: For God wills that you live, namely as regards approval, exhortation, and external means: But God is not about to continue for you the life-preserving power, except for a few hours.' Would this have been to console, or rather to mock, a most pious Prince?

Then they except: that God does not desire the death of the sinner, i.e., of the one repenting; and thus the discourse is not about every wicked person, but about him who is converted. But this is inept, and openly alien to the words of God. For what need is there for that protestation concerning the death of the wicked man, that God does not desire it, but THAT THE WICKED MAY BE CONVERTED and live, if it means nothing else than that God does not desire the death of him who is converted? Why does God so distinctly testify that he does not even desire the death of the dying sinner, and distinctly asserts both: that he wills that the sinner repent, and that he wills that he not die? Why does he complain so sorrowfully about the stubbornness of his people, that he wills them to die—not that he desires their death, but that they persist in that way by which the mercy of God is hindered by the actual and obstinate impenitence of the people, and thus they procure death for themselves? Add that divine adjuration: 'Why will you die, O house of Israel?' shows sufficiently that there is no cause for despair, because God, as the injured party, as the plaintiff, and as the judge, does not desire the death of sinners, v. 23; nay, he is prepared to provide the means necessary for conversion, v. 30. What of the fact that 'to will' in this place not only denies the good pleasure of damnation or the delight in death in God, but also introduces the contrary delight in the salvation of the penitent, so that, according to the opinion of the blessed Dn. D. Hülsemann on this passage, it is not necessary for the exposition of this passage to have recourse to the distinction of the divine will into antecedent and consequent. For neither by a consequent will does God take pleasure in the destruction of the wicked, as the Jews slandered, but he is compelled, as it were against his will, by the necessity of the office of Judge to pass sentence. See Lam. 3:33.

As for what they thirdly except, that the discourse is not about eternal death, but temporal, concerning which Sanctius also explains it: that has already been refuted before; because just as eternal life is promised to the righteous, so by the force of opposites, not temporal, but eternal death is understood, which God does not desire with respect to the wicked; nor can the wicked man escape temporal death by his conversion, but eternal. Therefore, Jerome, Dionysius the Carthusian, Lyranus, Hugo, and other ancients, even by the admission of Sanctius himself, interpret these things concerning eternal death.

THAT HE MAY BE CONVERTED) That he may enter upon another life. WHY WILL YOU DIE) Above 18:31. THE RIGHTEOUSNESS OF THE RIGHTEOUS) All these things also are transferred from chapter 18.

Latin:

Vers. 11. NOLO MORTEM IMPII) Comparate di- ctum. Sensus idem qui supra 18, 23.32.

Nulla hic comparet nota sensus comparati.Per- tinet hæc sententia ad voluntatem Dei antecedentem, juxta quam Deus minime vult mortem hominis, sed potius conversionem & vitam, utpote cujus gratia, & pro quo ipse Dei filius mortem subiit: unde solidissime profligatur absolutum Calvin. de- cretum. Quod vero excipiunt nonnulli è Refor- matis, Calvin. Pareus, Polanus, Chamier Panstrat. Cath. Tom.3.l.3. cap.6. §.10. in Ebræo non esse Deum non velle mortem impii, sed non delectari morte im- pii: resp. vocem חפץ in genere notare voluit, Pf. 5,5. Pf. 115.3. Cant. 2, 7. porro delectatio eorum est, quæ volumus: Si ergo morte impii non delecta- tur Deus, utique non vult eam: nam si vellet,dele- ctaretur eadem. Voluntatem beneplaciti verbum hoc inferre Pf. 40, 9. Pf. 50, 17. Mal. 2, 17. Ef. 55, 11. aperte docent. Adde & Num. 14, 8. 1. Reg. 9, 1. 2. Reg. 22, 20. Remonstrantes ad hanc Calvin. exce- ptionem Deum nolle quidem mortem pereuntis, quatenus non delectatur interitu creaturæ, & qua- tenus conversionem hominum approbat,non qua- tenus efficere in omnibus vult: respondent in Script. Dordrac. p. 241. Si approbat Deus omnium vitam & conversionem, qui absolute decrevit plero- rumque interitum? ac simile hoc esse ajunt, ac si Ezechiæ vitæ prorogationem expetenti respon- sum fuisset: Bono animosis ô Rex: Nam Deus vult ut vivas nimirum quoad approbationem, cohortatio- nem & media externa: Sed vim vitæ conservatricem non est tibi Deus, nisi ad paucas horas continuaturus. Hoc cine fuisset consolari, an deridere potius piissi- mum Principem?

Deinde excipiunt: Deum nolle mortem peccato- ris sc. resipiscentis: adeoque sermonem non esse de omni impio, sed se eo qui convertitur: At hoc in- eptum, & à verbis Dei aperte alienum. Quid enim protestatione illa opus de hominis impii morte, quod Deus eam non velit, sed UT CONVER- TATUR impius, & vivat, si nihil aliud ea sibi velit, quam quod Deus non velit ejus, qui conver- titur, mortem: Cur Deus tam diferte testatur, ne morientis quidem peccatoris mortem se velle, & utrumque distincte perhibet: velle sese, ut peccator resipiscat, & velle se, ut non moriatur. Cur tam dolen- ter de populi sui pertinacia conqueritur, quod mori velit, non quod mortem optet, sed quod eam viam insistat, qua misericordia Dei impediatur ob actua- lem & praefractam populi impoenitentiam, sibique ipsi ita mortem conciliet. Adde quod obtestatio illa divina; quare moriemini domus Israël? ostendat satis, nullam esse causam desperationis, quia Deus tanquam pars laesa, tanquam actor, & tanquam judex nolit mortem peccatorum vers. 23. imo paratus sit sufficere media ad conversionem necessaria, v. 30. Quid quod τὸ nolle in h. l. non solum neget benepla- citum damnationis seu delectationis mortis in Deo, sed contrariam etiam delectationem salutis poeniten- tium inferat, adeo, ut ex sententia B. Dn. D. Hülse- manni ad h. l. necessum non sit pro expositione hujus loci decurrere ad distinctionem voluntatis divinae in antecedentem, & consequentem. Nam neque con- sęquente voluntate Deus delectatur interitu impii, quomodo Judaei calumniabantur, sed ex necessitate of- ficii Judicis, & q. invitus cogitur ad ferendam senten- tiam. Vid. Thren. 3, 33.

Quod porro tertio excipiunt, sermonem esse non de morte æterna, sed temporali, de qua etiam Sanctius explicat: id antea jam refutatum est: quia uti vita æterna justo promittitur, ita vi contrario- rum non temporalis, sed æterna mors intelligitur, quam Deus non vult respectu impii: neq; mortem temporalem effugere conversione sua potest im- pius, sed æternam. Ideo Hieronymus, Dionyf. Car- thus. Lyranus, Hugo & alii veteres fatente ipso San- ctio de morte æterna hæc interpretantur.

VT CONVERTATVR) Aliam ineat vitam. QVARE MOREREMINI) Supra 18, 31. JVSTITIA JVSTI) Hæc quoque omnia tranfumta ex capite 18.

## 33:12
Verse 12. IN WHATEVER DAY HE SHALL HAVE SINNED) עזב is to forsake God or the ways of God.

Latin:

Vers. 12. IN QVACVNQVE DIE PECCAVERIT) עזב est Deum aut Dei vias deserere.

## 33:17
Verse 17. THE WAY OF THE LORD IS NOT OF EQUAL WEIGHT) In the Hebrew: Is not equal: As also above 18:25, and here below, 20. Way, that is, the manner of acting.

Latin:

Vers. 17. NON EST ÆQVI PONDERIS VIA DO- MINI) In Hebræo: Non est æqua: Ut & supra 18, 25. & hic infra. 20. via, id est, agendi ratio.

## 33:21
Ver. 21. AND IT CAME TO PASS IN THE TWELFTH YEAR, IN THE TENTH MONTH, IN THE FIFTH OF THE MONTH) In a year and four months, and some days, after the city was taken, so that a messenger could conveniently arrive at Babylon. This happened before the final revelation concerning Egypt. The Prophet did not wish to interrupt the matters pertaining to Egypt, but followed the sequence of events, which historians also often do.

HE THAT HAD ESCAPED OUT OF JERUSALEM CAME UNTO ME) Just as God had predicted to him, above 24, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET FACTVM EST IN DVODECIMO ANNO, IN DECIMO MENSE, IN QVINTA MEN- SIS) Anno & quatuor mensibus, diebusque aliquot, post captam urbem, ita ut commode nuncius Babylonem per- venire potuerit. Accidit hoc ante postremam revelationem de Ægypto. Res ad Ægyptum pertinentes interrumpere Propheta noluit, sed seriem rerum secutus est, quod & historici sæpe faciunt.

VENIT AD ME QVI FVGERAT DE JERV- SALEM) Ita ut Deus ei prædixerat, supra 24, 26.

## 33:22
Ver. 22. AND HE OPENED MY MOUTH) God had commanded me that I should speak freely and with authority. Above 24, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 22. APERVITQVE OS MEVM) Præceperat mihi Deus, ut libere & cum authoritate loquerer. Supra 24, 27.

## 33:24
Ver. 24. YE THAT DWELL IN THESE WASTES UPON THE LAND OF ISRAEL) In the ruins of the city and the towns with Gedaliah.

ABRAHAM WAS ONE AND HE INHERITED THE LAND) That is, the right of dwelling in it and pasturing cattle.

BUT WE ARE MANY, THE LAND IS GIVEN TO US FOR POSSESSION) If he, with three hundred servants, could protect himself among so many hostile men, much more shall we, being so many more, retain our right.

Latin:

Vers. 24. QVI HABITANT IN RVINOSIS HIS SVPER HVMVM ISRAEL) In ruinis urbis & oppido- rum cum Godolia.

VNVS ERAT ABRAHAM ET HEREDITATE POSSEDIT TERRAM) Id est, jus in ea habitandi ac pecora pascendi.

NOS AVTEM MVLTI SVMVS, NOBIS DA- TA EST TERRA IN POSSESSIONEM) Si ille cum vernis trecentis se inter tot infestos homines tutari potuit, multo magis nos tanto plures jus nostrum retinebimus.

## 33:25
Ver. 25. YE THAT EAT WITH THE BLOOD) Contrary to the law of Levit. 9, 26, and one given to all men much earlier. Gen. 9, 4.

YE LIFT UP YOUR EYES) As those praying are accustomed to do. Above 18, 6.

TOWARD YOUR ABOMINATIONS) Toward the Idols.

AND YE SHED BLOOD) You commit murders.

SHALL YE POSSESS THE LAND BY INHERITANCE) It had been promised to you under a condition, which you do not fulfill. Abraham was not such as this. See John 8, verse 39.

Latin:

Vers. 25. QVI IN SANGVINE COMEDITIS) Contra legem Levit. 9, 26. & multo antiquiorem omni- bus hominibus datam. Gen. 9, 4.

OCVLOS VESTROS LEVATIS) Ut solent pre- cantes. Supra 18, 6.

AD IMMVNDITIAS VESTRAS) Ad Idola.

ET SANGVINEM FVNDITIS) Homicidia per- petratis.

NVMQVID TERRAM HEREDITATE POSSI- DEBITIS) Promissa fuerat vobis sub conditione, quam non impletis. Non talis fuit Abraham. Vide Johan. 8. vers. 39.

## 33:26
Verse 26. YOU HAVE RELIED ON YOUR SWORDS) Confident in your own strength, you dare everything. Thus the Chaldean here. These things pertain to homicides. YOU HAVE DONE ABOMINATIONS) This pertains to idolatry. AND EVERYONE HAS DEFILED HIS NEIGHBOR'S WIFE) There is hardly anyone who restrains himself from adulteries.

Latin:

Vers. 26. STETISTIS IN GLADIIS VESTRIS) Con- fisi viribus vestris, nihil non audetis. Ita hic Chaldæus. Hæc ad homicidia pertinent. FECISTIS ABOMINATIONES) Hoc ad Idolo- latriam. ET VNVSQVISQVE VXOREM PROXIMI SVI POLLVIT) Vix quisquam est qui ab adulteriis se temperet.

## 33:27
Verse 27. THOSE WHO DWELL IN RUINS) In those ruins of either the city or the towns. THEY SHALL FALL BY THE SWORD) Partly the sons of Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, partly those avenging the slaughter of Gedaliah by the Chaldeans, 2 Kings 25:23 and following. AND HE WHO IS IN THE FIELD SHALL BE GIVEN TO THE BEASTS TO BE DEVOURED) Above 5:17, 14:15, 21. BUT THOSE WHO ARE IN STRONGHOLDS AND CAVES) He understands by strongholds fortified places, into which, as also into caves, neither enemies nor beasts easily penetrate. THEY SHALL DIE BY PESTILENCE) This agrees with those places just cited from the preceding.

Latin:

Vers. 27. QVI IN RVINOSIS HABITANT) In ruinis illis aut urbis aut oppidorum. GLADIO CADENT) Partim Ismaëlis filii Natha- niæ, partim Chaldæorum Godoliæ necem ulcifcentium 2. Reg. 25, 23. & sequentibus. ET QVI IN AGRO EST BESTIIS TRADE- TVR AD DEVORANDVM) Supra 5, 17. 14, 15. 21. QVI AVTEM IN PRÆSIDIIS ET SPELVN- CIS SVNT) Præsidia intelligit loca munita, ad quæ, ut & ad speluncas, neque hostes neque bestiæ facile penetrant. PESTE MORIENTVR) Convenit hoc cum illis lo- cis modo citatis ex superioribus.

## 33:28
Verse 28. AND I WILL RENDER THE LAND A DESOLATION) Namely, with men consumed by so many deaths and captivities. Jeremiah 4:27, 12:11, 18:16. BECAUSE THERE IS NO ONE WHO PASSES THROUGH THEM) So that there is no one who passes through them (the mountains). Not only will no one dwell there, but not even any traveler will dare to take a journey through that place for fear of wild beasts and the pestilential climate.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ET REDDAM TERRAM IN SOLITV- DINEM) Nempe absumtis per tot mortes ac captivitates hominibus. Jerem. 4, 27. 12, 11. 18, 16. EO QVOD NVLLVS SIT QVI PER EOS TRANSEAT) Ita ut nullus sit qui per eos (montes) transeat. Non modo nullus ibi habitabit, sed nec viator quisquam iter isthac capere audebit metu ferarum & cœli pestilentis.

## 33:30
Verse 30. THEY SPEAK OF YOU BY THE WALLS) Within the walls. He speaks of the deported. AND IN THE DOORS OF THE HOUSES) That is, the vestibules. AND THEY COME TO YOU AS IF THE PEOPLE WERE ENTERING) Just as crowds of disciples are accustomed to come to teachers. Thus the Chaldean here. AND MY PEOPLE SIT BEFORE YOU) That is, as if they were my people; as if they were mine, when they are not. AND THEY HEAR YOUR WORDS AND DO NOT DO THEM) They do not correct themselves any the more. THEY TURN THEM INTO A SONG OF THEIR MOUTH) They care no more for your words than if someone were playing to a flute: for that is עגב. See Genesis 4:21. AND THEIR HEART FOLLOWS THEIR GREED) While you are speaking, they are thinking about making profit through dishonest arts.

Latin:

Vers. 30. LOQVVNTVR DE TE JVXTA MVROS) Intra parietis. De deportates loquitur. ET IN OSTIIS DOMORVM) Id est, vestibulis. ET VENIVNT AD TE QVASI SI INGRE- DIATVR POPVLVS) Sicut discipulorum catervæ ad Do- ctores venire solent. Ita hic Chaldæus. ET SEDENT CORAM TE POPVLVS MEVS) Id est, quasi essent populus meus; quasi essent mei, cum non sint. ET AVDIVNT SERMONES TVOS ET NON FACIVNT EOS) Non eo magis se corrigunt. IN CANTICVM ORIS SVI VERTVNT IL- LOS) Non magis verba tua curant, quam si ad tibiam ali- quis caneret: id enim עגב. Vide Gen. 4, 21. ET AVARITIAM SVAM SEQVITVR COR EORVM) Dum tu loqueris, illi de quæstu per artes ini- quas faciendo cogitant.

## 33:32
Verse 32. AND YOU ARE TO THEM AS A MUSICAL SONG WHICH IS SUNG WITH A SWEET AND PLEASANT SOUND) You are to them like the song of a sweetly sounding flute, or one skilled in playing the psaltery. They praise your eloquence: they do not care for the matter: Such are many even today in the Churches, says Jerome on this passage, who say, come let us hear him, and him loosening the words of his preaching with wonderful eloquence, and many are moved and shout aloud, and toss their hands.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ET ES EIS QVASI CARMEN MVSICVM QVOD SVAVI DVLCIQVE SONO CANITVR) Es eis quasi cantus tibiæ dulce sonantis, aut periti psallere. Elo- quentiam tuam laudant: res non curant: Tales sunt usque hodie multi in Ecclesiis, ait ad hunc locum Hieronymus, qui ajunt, venite audiamus illum, & illum mira eloquentia prædicationis suæ verba solventem, plurimique commovent & vociferantur, & jactant manus.

## 33:33
Verse 33. AND WHEN THAT WHICH WAS PREDICTED HAS COME) But now when that which you predicted (concerning the destruction of the city) has come. BEHOLD INDEED IT COMES) For it certainly happens. THEN THEY SHALL KNOW THAT A PROPHET HAS BEEN AMONG THEM) They will not be able to deny that you were sent to them by me. They will be able to offer no veil of ignorance for their sins.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ET CVM VENERIT QVOD PRÆDI- CTVM EST) At nunc cum quod prædixeras (de urbis ex- cidio) venerit. ECCE ENIM VENIT) Certo enim evenit. TVNC SCIENT QVOD PROPHETES FVERIT INTER EOS) Negare non poterunt te ad ipsos à me fuisse missum. Ignorantiæ velum culpis suis nullum po- terunt obtendere.

## 34:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIV.

From the hands of the shepherds, who, having neglected the flock, seek only their own, the Lord says that He will deliver His sheep: and that He will feed them in judgment, and that He will raise up over them His servant, he teaches is the Messiah, under whom they will feed securely in all the fruitfulness of the earth, and he shows that His flock is the people of Israel, and that He is their God.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIV.
