Ex manibus pastorum, qui neglecto grege sua tantum quærunt, Dominus dicit se oves suas liberaturum: quodque eas in judicio pascet, suscita turus super eas servum suum docet Messiam, sub quo in omni terræ ubertate secure pascentur, ostenditque gregem suum esse populum Israel, & se Deum ipsorum.

## 34:2
Verse 2. CONCERNING THE SHEPHERDS OF ISRAEL) With the city now destroyed, the Prophet commemorates the causes of the destruction, the crimes of the princes: (who are called shepherds, Jeremiah 2:18, 3:15, 10:21, 22:22, 23:1, 25:35, 36. And Plato, Republic 4.) and then also of the people. WHO WERE FEEDING THEMSELVES) They did this one thing, that they themselves might grow rich. ARE NOT FLOCKS FED BY THE SHEPHERDS?) That is, is it not the duty of shepherds to feed the flock?

Latin:

Vers. 2. DE PASTORIBVS ISRAEL) Excisâ jam ur- be, causas Prophetæ excidii commemorat principum crimi- na: (qui pastores dicuntur Jerem. 2, 18. 3, 15. 10, 21. 22, 22. 23, 1. 25, 35. 36. Et Platoni de Rep. 4.) deinde & populi. QVI PASCEBANT SEMETIPSOS) Hoc unum agebant ut ipsi ditescerent. NONNE GREGES A PASTORIBVS PASCVN- TVR?) Id est, nonne id officium est pastorum gregem pascere?

## 34:3
Verse 3. YOU WERE EATING THE MILK AND CLOTHING YOURSELVES WITH THE WOOL) You were exacting great tributes from the people. He milks twice in an hour; says Virgil. AND YOU WERE SLAUGHTERING THAT WHICH WAS FAT)

You were killing the rich through calumny, so that you might take possession of their goods.

BUT YOU WERE NOT FEEDING MY FLOCK) You had no care for it. See what was said on John 10:12.

Latin:

Vers. 3. LAC COMEDEBATIS ET LANIS OPE- RIEBAMINI) Magna tributa exigebatis à populo. Bis mulget in hora; ait Virgilius. ET QVOD CRASSVM ERAT OCCIDEBATIS)

Divites occidebatis per calumniam, ut bonis eorum poti- remini.

GREGEM AUTEM MEUM NON PASCEBA- TIS) Nullam ejus habebatis curam. Vide quæ dicta ad Johan. 10, 12.

## 34:4
Ver. 4. THAT WHICH WAS WEAK YE HAVE NOT STRENGTHENED) Ye have not fortified the languid cattle: with good nourishment, that is.

THAT WHICH WAS SICK YE HAVE NOT HEALED) For cattle also have their own ills and remedies.

THAT WHICH WAS BROKEN YE HAVE NOT BOUND UP) Ye have not bound the wounds perhaps made by wolves.

THAT WHICH WAS CAST AWAY YE HAVE NOT BROUGHT AGAIN) If any had fallen into a pit, ye did not lead it out. See Matt. 12, 11.

THAT WHICH WAS LOST YE HAVE NOT SOUGHT) If any had wandered from the flock Matt. 15, 24. Luke 15, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 4. QVOD INFIRMUM FUIT NON CONSO- LIDASTIS) Pecudem languidam non roborastis: bonis ali- mentis scilicet.

QVOD ÆGROTVM NON SANASTIS) Sunt enim & sua pecudibus mala & medicamina.

QVOD CONFRACTVM EST NON ALLI- GASTIS) Non obligastis vulnera à lupis forte facta.

QVOD ABJECTVM EST NON REDVXISTIS) Si quæ in foveam lapsa erat, non eduxistis. Vide Matth. 12, 11.

QVOD PERIERAT NON QVÆSISTIS) Si quæ à grege aberraverat Matth. 15, 24. Luc. 15, 6.

## 34:5
Ver. 5. AND MY SHEEP WERE SCATTERED) Hither and thither, some one way, some another. Matt. 26, 31. Mark 14, 27. He rightly said my sheep: for the people were not in the patrimony of the princes.

BECAUSE THERE WAS NO SHEPHERD) A good one, that is, and one who loves the flock.

AND THEY BECAME MEAT TO ALL THE BEASTS OF THE FIELD) They were prey to the Syrians, Ammonites, Moabites, Assyrians, Egyptians, Chaldeans.

AND THEY WERE SCATTERED) The Israelites were led away into various lands.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET DISPERSÆ SVNT OVES MEÆ) Huc illuc, aliæ alio. Matth. 26, 31. Marc. 14, 27. Bene dixit oves meæ: neque enim erat in principum patrimonio po- pulus.

EO QVOD NON ESSET PASTOR) Bonus sci- licet & gregis amans.

ET FACTÆ SUNT IN DEVORATIONEM OMNIVM BESTIARVM AGRI) Prædæ fuere Syris, Ammonitis, Moabitis, Assyriis, Ægyptiis, Chaldæis.

ET DISPERSÆ SVNT) Abducti in terras varias Israëlitæ.

## 34:6
Ver. 6. MY FLOCKS WANDERED UPON ALL THE MOUNTAINS AND UPON EVERY HIGH HILL) In idolatrous worships, which were accustomed to be practiced in elevated places.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ERRAVERVNT GREGES MEI IN CVN- CTIS MONTIBVS ET IN UNIVERSO COLLE EX- CELSO) In cultibus idololatricis, qui in locis eminen- tibus exerceri solebant.

## 34:10
Ver. 10. BEHOLD I MYSELF WILL REQUIRE MY FLOCK AT THE HAND OF THE SHEPHERDS) I have required. That is, on that account I most severely punished Zedekiah and his children, and other princes.

I WILL CAUSE THEM TO CEASE) I have caused them to cease.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ECCE EGO IPSE SVPER PASTORES REQVIRAM GREGEM MEUM) Requisivi. Id est, pro- pterea Sedeciam liberosque ejus, & principes alios gravis- sime punivi.

CESSARE FACIAM EOS) Cessare feci eos.

## 34:11
Vers. 11. BEHOLD I MYSELF WILL SEEK MY SHEEP) I myself will take special care of them, by inviting them through the Prophets to a better life. דרש is often to take care.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ECCE EGO IPSE REQVIRAM OVES MEAS) Ipse eorum curam geram peculiarem, per Prophe- tas eos invitando ad vitam meliorem. דרש sæpe est cu- ram gerere.

## 34:12
Vers. 12. AS A SHEPHERD VISITS HIS FLOCK) He inquires everywhere.

I WILL DELIVER THEM OUT OF ALL PLACES) I will bring back the Jews from all places of the Babylonian empire, nay, even from Egypt, and elsewhere.

IN WHICH THEY HAD BEEN SCATTERED IN THE DAYS OF CLOUD AND THICK DARKNESS) In a black and gloomy time: that is, full of miseries. Thus above 30, 3.

Grotius understands this as the vindication of the Jews from the places of their exile, and wishes to designate by the shepherds in verse 10 Zedekiah, his children, and other Princes. But the Shepherds of Israel here are not Princes; because the antithesis of the good shepherd in v. 23 et seqq. and his actions and duties teach that the discourse is about Ecclesiastical Shepherds. And when the flocks are said to have wandered on all the mountains, and on every high hill v. 7, idolatrous worship is noted, as Grotius himself admits, and they are made for the devouring of all the beasts of the field, not only tyrants are understood, but also heretics. Which sense is also confirmed by the parallel passages Jer. 23. 3. 4. John 10, 13. Therefore God himself requires his flock from the hand of the shepherds, not when he requires Princes for punishment, but when he requires an account of the flock from Ecclesiastical shepherds, whom he removes and causes to cease, so that they may no longer feed his free flock. Which was not done when they were restored from the Babylonian captivity, but in the time of the New Testament, when the Jewish Synagogue was rejected, and the Israelites were freed from the Yoke of Moses and the abuse of the law. Therefore, it is a matter of the spiritual care of the sheep, not of bodily benefits, which they acknowledge along with Jerome, Cornelius à Lapide, Hector Pintus, and among our own Osiander, the Weimar theologians, B. Pappus, and others. From the Reformed, Oecolampadius, Junius, Piscator, and the Dutch; although these, along with the Weimar theologians and Cornelius, understand it both of the return from the Babylonian captivity and of the conversion from Gentilism. By the day of cloud, says Oecolampadius, and of thick darkness, he understands every adverse time, when the darkness of either errors or afflictions falls, as they were for the Jews a time of such neglected discipline and doctrine of the law, as well as an exile of captivity. Such was the time when Christ appeared on earth. The sheep are said to be led out from the peoples, by which phrase is denoted the calling of the faithful to the Church from every land, Isa. 49, 7. 23, 3, and thus the minds of Israel in which they are to be pastured are to be understood as the mountains of the Church. Whence it is added, AND IN ALL THE DWELLINGS OF THE EARTH, so that it may be clear that not Palestine alone is designated, but the whole world, through which the Church is to be disseminated. Compare Psalm 68, 16. Isa. 2, 23. Those things which are promised below concerning one shepherd will more fully establish this sense. IN RIVIS) By the streams. Ps. 23, 2. AND IN ALL THE DWELLINGS OF THE EARTH) In the folds. Vers. 14. I WILL FEED THEM IN THE RICHEST PASTURES.) Ps. 33, v. 1. Vers. 15. I WILL MAKE THEM LIE DOWN.) Virgil: He, his snowy side supported by soft hyacinth, beneath the dark holm-oak, chews the cud of herbs. Vers. 16. AND THAT WHICH IS FAT AND STRONG I WILL GUARD.) I will keep in good health. Grotius savors of things merely carnal. But spiritual things are of a better sort. Nor should it be thought that God wished to nourish the hope of the faithful with carnal promises alone, since such earthly things are inconstant, perishable, and temporal. Therefore, one must understand the streams and fat pastures spiritually, as in Ps. 23, 2; John 10, 10. And so with the rest. I will feed my sheep with the fodder of the word, and I will make them lie down, I will provide them security and rest, so that they may be safe under my protection: That which was lost, I will seek: Because Christ was sent to seek and heal the lost sheep of Israel, Matt. 15, 24, that he might seek that which was lost, Luke 19, 10, etc. That the discourse is about Christ is also confirmed by the judgment which he himself executes between the other sheep and the goats, not only in this age, but also on the final day of universal judgment, Matt. 25. Jerome has it thus in this place: AND NOT ONLY ON THE MOUNTAINS, but by the streams, and in all the dwellings of the earth, in the richest pastures, and on the high mountain, of which Isaiah and Micah prophesy more fully: or on the high mountains of Israel: There they shall rest in green herbs and shall say: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing; in a place of pasture he has placed me; he has brought me up over the waters of refreshment. And they shall be fed in the fattest pastures upon the mountains of Israel. It is an infinite promise and hope of blessedness, when the Lord himself promises, saying: I will feed my sheep, and I will by no means commit them to evil shepherds, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord God: that they may rest in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Then that which had perished among the peoples of the nations will be sought, and that which had wandered in the persuasion of heretics will be brought back, and that which had been broken will be bound up, and that which was crushed and weak will be strengthened: that what is written may be fulfilled: Who heals their infirmities, and binds up their bruises. That אשמיד v. 26 is 'I will destroy,' as the Targum renders it אשיצי 'destroying,' Vatablus, Pagninus, Arias, Oecolampadius, Piscator, Junius, the Genevans, the Belgians, Sixtinus Amama, the new Bible of Toussain, published at Frankfurt, the Vinarians, B. Hülsemann, which sense as it agrees with the Hebrew word (Compare Deut. 32, 15. Ps. 22, 30. Isa. 5, 17. c. 10, 16. Amos 4, 1) is thus confirmed by a comparison with v. 20. And here is delivered both the consolation of the pious sheep and the refutation of the reprobate. Therefore, it cannot be explained as 'preservation in good health' with Grotius. The German version of B. Luther followed the LXX. Interpreters who rendered it Φυλάξω, and the Vulgate Latin which rendered it CUSTODIAM. But there is no reason why we should admit with the Papists that the sources are corrupted here, and believe that אשמור 'I will guard' ought to be read.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SICVT VISITAT PASTOR GREGEM SVVM) Ubique inquirit.

LIBERABO EAS DE OMNIBVS LOCIS) Re- ducam Judæos ex omnibus locis imperii Babylonici, imo & ex Ægypto, & aliunde.

IN QVIBUS DISPERSÆ FVERANT IN DIE- BVS NVBIS ET CALIGINIS) Tempore atro ac tene- broso: id est, pleno miseriis. Sic supra 30, 3.

DE vindicandis Judæis è locis exilii intelligit Grotius, & per pastores vers. 10. designari vult Sedeciam, liberosque ejus & Principes alios. Sed Pa- stores Israelis hic non sunt Principes; Quia anti- thesis boni pastoris v. 23. seqq. ejusque actiones & officia docent de Ecclesiasticis Pastoribus sermo- nem esse. Et cum greges aberraffe dicuntur in cun- ctis montibus, & in universo colle excelso v. 7. Idolola- trici cultus notantur, uti fatetur ipse Grotius, & fa- ctæ in devorationem omnium bestiarum agri, non ty- rannorum solum intelliguntur, sed & hæretico- rum. Quem sensum firmant etiam loca parallela Jer. 23. 3. 4. Joh. 10, 13. Requirit ergo Deus ipse su- per pastores gregem suum de manu eorum, non cum requirit Principes ad pœnam, sed cum rationem de grege requirit à pastoribus Ecclesiasticis, quos remo- vet ac cessare facit, ut ultra non pascant liberum gregem suum. Quod non factum cum è Babylonicâ captivitate restituti sunt, sed tempore Novi Testa- menti, cum Synagoga Judaica rejecta, & Israëlitæ à Jugo Mosis & abusu legis liberati sunt. De curâ ergo spirituali ovium agitur, non de corporalibus be- neficiis, quod agnoscunt cum Hieronymo, Corne- lius à Lapide, Hector Pintus, & è nostris Osiander, Vinarienses, B. Pappus, aliique. E Reformatis, Oeco- lampadius, Junius, Piscator, & Belgæ; quanquam hi cum Vinariensibus, & Cornelio tum de reductio- ne è captivitate Babylonica, tum de conversione ex gentilismo intelligant. Per diem nubis, inquit Oeco- lampadius, & caliginis adversum tempus omne intel- ligit, ubi tenebræ vel errorum, vel afflictionum inci- dunt, ut erant judæis tempus tam neglectæ disciplinæ ac doctrinæ legis, quam captivitatis exilium. Cujus- modi tempus fuit quando Christus in terris com- paruit. Educendæ dicuntur oves de populis, qua Phrasi denotatur vocatio fidelium ad Ecclesiam ex omni terra Esa. 49, 7. 23, 3. adeoque mentes Israel in quibus pascendæ sunt, de montibus Ecclesiæ intel- ligendi. Unde additur, ET IN CUNCTIS SE- DIBUS TERRÆ, ut constet, non Palestinam solam designari, sed orbem totum, per quam disse- minanda Ecclesia. Confer Psalmum 68, 16. Esa. 2, 23. sensum hunc uberius statuminabunt ea, quæ de uno pastore infra promissa sunt. IN RIVIS) Ad rivos. Psal. 23, 2. ET IN CVNCTIS SEDIBVS TERRÆ) In caulis. Vers. 14. IN PASCVIS VBERRIMIS PASCAM EAS.) Psal. 33. v. 1. Vers. 15. EGO EAS ACCVBARE FACIAM.) Vir- gilius: Ille latus niveum molli fultus hyacintho, Ilice sub nigra pallente ruminat herbas. Vers. 16. ET QVOD PINGVE ET FORTE CV- STODIAM.) Servabo in bona valetudine. Merè carnalia sapit Grotius. At Spiritualia po- tioris commatis sunt. Neque putandum Deum carnalibus tantum promissionibus fidelium spem nutrire voluisse, quum corporalia ejusmodi terre- na, inconstantia, caduca & temp alia sint. Rivos ergo & pascua pinguia spiritualiter intelligere opor- tet ut Psalm. 23, 2. Joh. 10, 10. Atque ita de cæteris. Ego pascam oves meas verbi pabulo, & Ego faciam accubare eas, securitatem & quietem ipsis præstabo, ut tutæ sint sub mea protectione: Quod perierat, requiram: Quia missus est Christus ad perditas ovi- culas Israel requirendas & curandas Matth. 15, 24. ut quæreret quod perierat Luc. 19, 10. &c. De Chri- sto sermonem esse, etiam judicium, quod exequitur ipse inter pecudes alias, & hircos non tantum in hoc seculo, sed etiam in novissimo die pantocritico Matth. 25. confirmat. Hieronymus ita habet in hoc loco: ET NON SOLUM IN MONTIBUS, sed in rivis, & in cunctis sedibus terræ, in pascuis uber- rimis, & in monte excelso, de quo Esaias & Michæas plenius vaticinantur: sive in montibus excelsis Israel: Ibi requiescent in herbis virentibus & dic ent: Domi- nus pascit me, & nihil mihi deerit, in loco pascuæ ibi me collocavit; Super aquas refectionis educa- vit me. Et pascentur in pascuis pinguissimis super montes Israel. Est infinita promissio spesque beatitudi- nis, quando ipse Dominus pollicetur dicens: Ego pa- scam oves meas, & nequaquam eas committam malis pastoribus, & ego eas accubare faciam, dicit Domi- nus Deus: ut requiescant in sinu Abraham, Isaac & Jacob. Tunc quod perierat in gentium populis, re- quiretur, & quod erraverat in hæreticorum perfua- sione, reducetur, & quod confractum fuerat, alliga- bitur, & quod contritum atque infirmum, consoli- dabitur: ut impleatur quod scriptum est: Qui sanat infirmitates, & alligat contritiones eorum. Illud אשמיד v. 26. est perdam, ut Targum reddens אשיצי perdens, Vatablus, Pagninus, Arias, Oecolampadius, Piscator, Junius, Genevenses, Belgæ, Sixtin. Ama- ma, Biblia nova Tossani, Francofurt. edita, Vinari- enses, B. Hülsemann. qui sensus uti voci Ebrææ con- venit (Conf. Deut. 32, 15. Psal. 22, 30. Esa. 5, 17. c. 10, 16. Amos. 4, 1. ita firmatur è collatione v. 20. Et traditur hic tum ovium piarum consolatio, tum re probarum redarguitio. Non ergo de conservatione in bona valetudine cum Grotio explicari potest. Germanica versio B. Lutheri sequuta est LXX. In- terp. qui Φυλάξω, & Vulgatum Latinumque qui CUSTODIAM reddidere. Non autem causa est, cur cum Pontificiis fontes corruptos hic esse admit- tamus, & אשמור Custodiam, legi debere credamus.

## 34:16
AND I WILL FEED THEM IN JUDGMENT) That is, as is fitting.

Latin:

ET PASCAM ILLAS IN JUDICIO) Id est, ut oportet.

## 34:17
Vers. 17. BUT YOU, O MY FLOCKS) God comes to the sins of the people.

BEHOLD I JUDGE BETWEEN CATTLE AND CATTLE, OF THE RAMS AND OF THE GOATS.) I will determine what is just concerning all: even concerning those who are most eminent among the people, who are included under the name of goats and rams.

Latin:

Vers. 17. VOS AVTEM GREGES MEI) Venit Deus ad peccata populi.

ECCE EGO JUDICO INTER PECUS, ET PECUS ARIETVM ET HIRCORVM.) De omnibus quod jus est statuam: etiam de iis, qui in plebe maxime eminent, qui sub hircorum & arietum nomine comprehenduntur.

## 34:18
Vers. 18. WAS IT NOT ENOUGH FOR YOU TO FEED ON THE GOOD PASTURE?) This pertains especially to the rams and goats, that is, to the wealthy among the people. See James 2, 6.

MOREOVER, YOU HAVE TRAMPLED THE REST OF YOUR PASTURES WITH YOUR FEET) With heavy usury you drive away the resources of the poor. See above c. 18 and 22, 12. Jerem. 24.

YOU TROUBLED WITH YOUR FEET.) He says the same thing with another simile.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NONNE SATIS VOBIS ERAT PASCVA BONA DEPASCI?) Hoc ad arietes & hircos maxime pertinet, id est, ad opulentos in plebe. Vid. Jacob. 2, 6.

INSVPER ET RELIQVIAS PASCVARVM VESTRARVM CONCVLCASTIS PEDIBVS VESTRIS) Gravi fœnore exfugitis pauperum facultates. Vide supra c. 18. & 22, 12. Jerem. 24.

PEDIBUS VESTRIS TVRBABATIS.) Alia similitudine idem dicit.

## 34:19
Vers. 19. AND MY SHEEP FED ON THAT WHICH HAD BEEN TRAMPLED BY YOUR FEET) Scantily, that is.

AND WHAT YOUR FEET HAD TROUBLED, THESE THEY DRANK) Full of sorrow.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET OVES MEÆ HIS QVÆ CONCVLCATA PEDIBVS VESTRIS FVERANT, PASCEBANTVR) Tenuiter scilicet.

ET QVÆ PEDES VESTRI TVRBAVERANT, HÆC BIBEBANT) Mœrore pleni.

## 34:20
Verse 20. BETWEEN THE FAT AND THE LEAN CATTLE) Between the rich and the poor. I will vindicate these, I will punish those.

Latin:

Vers. 20. INTER PECVS PINGVE ET MACILENTVM) Inter divites & pauperes. Hos vindicabo, illos puniam.

## 34:21
Verse 21. BECAUSE YOU PUSHED WITH SIDES AND SHOULDERS, AND WITH YOUR HORNS VENTILATED ALL THE WEAK CATTLE) You butted: for that is what κερατίζειν means. Beware of running against a goat, he strikes with his horn. He put shoulders for arms. Smaller cattle are accustomed to be shoved and attacked by larger ones.

UNTIL THEY WERE SCATTERED ABROAD.) Until the time of the deportation.

Latin:

Vers. 21. PRO EO QVOD LATERIBVS ET HVMERIS IMPINGEBATIS, ET CORNIBVS VESTRIS VENTILABATIS OMNIA INFIRMA PECORA) Arietabatis: id enim est κερατίζειν. Occursare capro, cornu ferit ille, caveto. Humeris posuit pro armis. Solent pecudes minores à majoribus trudi atque incursari.

DONEC DISPERGERENTVR FORAS.) Ad tempus usque deportationis.

## 34:22
Verse 22. I WILL SAVE MY FLOCK) The same sense as above in verse 13.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SALVABO GREGEM MEVM) Idem sensus qui supra vers. 13.

## 34:23
Verse 23. AND I WILL RAISE UP OVER THEM ONE SHEPHERD, WHO SHALL FEED THEM, MY SERVANT DAVID.) Zerubbabel, who is called by the name of David his progenitor. See Jer. 23, 5. 33, 15.

That this prophecy does not speak of Zerubbabel, but is to be understood of Christ according to the literal sense, is taught by (1.) The appellation of David: which is never attributed to Zerubbabel, but to Christ, of whom David was a type. Concerning whom Ambrose, book 7, Epistle 47: David was indeed a King already deceased, and therefore the true David, the true humble one, the true meek one, the true strong Son of God, is announced by this name. Compare Hos. 3, 5. (2) The denomination of one Shepherd. Which here does not lack reason, but is called ONE Shepherd for this reason, that the Shepherd who is most unique, one and singular, might be designated, such as Zerubbabel is not, but Christ, to whom no one is similar, who is called Shepherd κατ’ ἐξοχὴν (by way of excellence) and by an eminent reason, even the prince of shepherds and the Arch-Bishop of our souls, 1 Pet. 2, Heb. 13. (3) The title of Servant. For He calls His servant κατ’ ἐξαίρετον λόγον (by a special reason): I will raise up over them one shepherd, my servant; where it is manifest that the discourse is about a singular servant of God, to whom this name is proper by a peculiar reason on account of his all-manner and most perfect obedience. Who is no other than that just servant of the Lord, who alone of all fulfilled the will of God, whom Isaiah proclaims in chapter 53. He refers indeed to the time when he willed to assume the form of a servant, fulfilled the law for us, and bore the punishments of our sins, and also became a minister of the circumcision, Rom. 15, 8. (4) The designation of the flock. For he is said to be raised up over the universal flock, which is to be gathered from all the seats of the earth. For that ecumenical shepherd of the whole united flock is none other than Christ. (5) The collation of other places. Grotius makes parallels to Jer. 23, 5. 33, 15. which we have shown before to treat of Christ. The passage Zech. 13, 7 must be added, in which likewise that shepherd of the Lord is introduced: whom we know to be Christ from Matt. 26, 31, Mark 14, 27. (6) The condition of the covenant of peace. For it is not a political covenant, nor a Mosaic one, that is understood, but an Evangelical one, which is truly a covenant of peace is the institution, therefore, of the new covenant designated, made in this David, because in Christ the Evangelical covenant was instituted, in which the forgiveness of all sins is placed, so that, justified through faith, we may have peace with God, Rom. 5,1. Concerning this covenant of peace see Eph. 1,10. Eph. 2,17. Col. 1,20. Rom. 14,17. (7) Cessation of beasts. That these things are not to be understood corporally is evident also from the fact that beasts ought to cease from the earth. For that has never been fulfilled among brute animals, nor regarding a corporal kingdom among tyrants. But in the spiritual kingdom of Christ, the beasts that lie in wait for the flocks cease, because the faithful rejoice in spiritual security, without danger. Nor are they harmed by wild beasts, but they know that they will be preserved under that one shepherd, Christ, for eternal life, Rom. 8. See similar passages Is. 11,6. 65,25. Hos. 2,20. The perfect completion, however, will be in the other life, Apocal. 21,25. Grotian Gloss: AND I WILL MAKE THE WORST BEASTS CEASE FROM THE EARTH: which is wont to happen where the land is much inhabited and cultivated, [and] is too cold. (8) The calling of the Gentiles: AND THEY WHO DWELL IN THE DESERT, SHALL SLEEP SECURELY IN THE FORESTS. Who are those who dwell in the desert, if not the Gentiles, who are wont to be described in this way, as being destitute of divine grace? Is. 49,45. Cant. 8,5. (9) Spiritual blessing. Which is designated in v. 26: AND I WILL MAKE THEM A BLESSING AROUND MY HILL. By which phrase an abundance of benefits is expressed. Since to make someone a blessing is to heap him with such great goods that he is, as it were, an example and a sign from which others may derive an argument of divine glory. Compare similar idioms Ps. 21,7. Zach. 3,9. Ruth 4,14. I WILL BRING DOWN THE RAIN IN ITS TIME, AND THERE SHALL BE SHOWERS OF BLESSING. By which is meant the rain of the word and the shower of the Gospel, which brings true blessing Is. 55,11. Ps. 68,10. Concerning which blessing the Apostle [says] Rom. 15,29: I know that when I come to you, I shall come in the abundance of the blessing of Christ. And Ephes. 1,3: Blessed be GOD and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ. (10) Spiritual liberation. The bonds of the yoke are said to be broken, and they themselves are to be liberated from the hand of those ruling over them. But there is no heavier bond of a yoke than that of spiritual servitude, from which Christ restores us into true liberty Joh. 8,36. Rom. 8,2. Compare Is. 9,6. Act. 15,10. Similarly, they are to be liberated from famine. THEY SHALL NOT BE DIMINISHED BY FAMINE (They shall not be consumed by famine IN THE LAND.) Which cannot be understood of the famine of the body: for the faithful are not rarely pressed by this, but of the famine of the soul. Am. 8,11. Because Christ feeds abundantly with the word of the Gospel. Furthermore, they are to be liberated from all reproach. NOR SHALL THEY BEAR THE REPROACH OF THE GENTILES ANY MORE. Which will be fulfilled in the faithful perfectly only in the other life, where no ignominy will have a place, but they shall shine with heavenly glory Dan. 12,1. Matth. 13,43. (11) Indication of this most celebrated Branch. AND I WILL RAISE UP FOR THEM A RENOWNED BRANCH, or rather CELEBRATED, that this is Christ, celebrated under the notion of a Branch to be raised up by God, is evident from Jer. 23,5. c. 33,15. Zach. 2 & 6. Which was a truly celebrated branch in the promises of the Old Testament. But more celebrated in the Confessions under the New Testament, whose name and deeds are celebrated in the whole world, and are sung by the proclamation of the word and the confession of the martyrs. Grotius drags this to posterity under the time of the Maccabees, but without any foundation. (12) Explanation of Christ. Who when Joh. 10. had preached about the reprobate shepherds being rejected, he testified that he himself was that one good shepherd, who is here opposed by Ezekiel to the reprobate shepherds, so that, with them rejected, he might take care of his flock: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, I am THAT SHEPHERD THAT GOOD [ONE], with that double article, as if pointing with an extended finger to that good Shepherd predicted by Ezekiel. Induced, therefore, by these arguments, Christian Doctors have accepted this prophecy concerning Christ with great consensus, both the ancients, Ambros. lib. 7. Epist. 47. Theodoret, and Hieron. in h. l. August. lib. de octo quæst. quæst. 5. and others; and the more recent ones, who here with one voice, Papists, Ours, and Reformed, acknowledge that the prophecy is held to be about Christ. Nor do the Hebrews deny this. For both the Targum Jonathan explained it of the Messiah, and R. David Kimchi in h. l. confesses that it is so explained by God. Grotius alone, with certain more recent Jews, understands these things of Zerubbabel, and believed that nothing but merely carnal and corporal things were proposed—about the land being purged of wild beasts, being filled with men, about fertile trees, and abundant fruits, and things similar to these. Compare what [he says] on chapter 37.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET SVSCITABO SUPER EAS PASTOREM VNVM, QVI PASCAT EAS, SERVVm MEVM DAVID.) Zorobabelem, qui Davidis progenitoris sui nomine appellatur. Vid. Jer. 23, 5. 33, 15.

Hanc Prophetiam non de Zorobabele, sed de Christo secundum literalem sensum loqui & accipiendam esse, docet (1.) Davidis apellatio: quæ nunquam Zorobabeli tribuitur, sed Christo, cujus typus David fuit. De quo Ambrosius l. 7. Epist. 47. David utique Rex jam defunctus erat, & ideo verus David, verus humilis, verus mansuetus, verus fortis Dei filius, hoc annunciatur nomine. Confer. Hos. 3, 5. (2) Pastoris unius denominatio. Quæ hic non caret ratione, sed ideo UNUS Pastor dicitur, ut designetur Pastor μονώτατος unus & singularis, qualis non est Zorobabel, sed Christus, cui nullus similis est, qui κατ’ ἐξοχὴν & eminenti ratione Pastor dicitur, Pastorum etiam princeps & Archi-Episcopus Animarum nostrarum, 1. Pet. 2. Ebr. 13. (3) Servi nuncupatio. Nam servum suum vocat κατ’ ἐξαίρετον λόγον: Excitabo super eas pastorem unum, servum meum; ubi manifestum est, de singulari Dei servo sermonem esse, cui hoc nomen peculiari ratione proprium ob omnimodam & perfectissimam obedientiam. Qui nullus alius est, nisi justus ille servus Domini, qui unus omnium Dei voluntatem implevit, quem deprædicat Es. c. 53. Respicit nempe tempus, quo formam servi assumere voluit, legem pro nobis implevit, & pœnas peccatorum nostrorum tulit, ac minister factus quoque est circumcisionis, Rom. 15, 8. (4) Gregis designatio. Dicitur enim excitandus super universum Gregem, qui de cunctis sedibus terræ congregandus. Oecumenicus quippe ille pastor totius gregis uniti alius non est, nisi Christus. (5) Aliorum locorum collatio. Parallela facit Grotius Jer. 23, 5. 33, 15. quæ de Christo agere antea ostendimus. Addendus locus Zach. 13, 7. quo itidem pastor ille domini introducitur: quem Christum esse è Matth. 26, 31. Marc. 14, 27. novimus. (6) Fœderis pacis conditio. Non enim fœdus Politicum, neque Mosaicum, sed Evangelicum intelligitur, quod vere fœdus pacis- est. Institutio ergo novi fœderis designatur, in hoc Davide facta, quia in Christo fœdus Evangeli- cum institutum, in quo omnium peccatorum con- donatio posita, ut justificati per fidem, pacem habea- mus cum Deo, Rom. 5,1. De hoc pacis pacto vide Ef. 11,10. Eph. 2, 17. Col. 1,20. Rom. 14,17. (7) Bestiarum cessatio. Non corporaliter esse hæc intelligenda vel ex eo constat, quod cessare bestiæ de terra de- beant. Nam neque in brutis animantibus id unquam impletum, neq; quoad regnum corporale in tyran- nis. In spirituali autem Christo regno cessant be- stiæ, quæ gregibus insidiantur, quia fideles gaudent spirituali securitate, absque periculo. Neq; à feris bestiis læduntur, sed sciunt se sub pastore illo uno, Christo, conservatum iri ad vitam æternam, Rom. 8. Vide loca similia Es. 11,6. 65,25. Hos. 2,20. Perfe- ctum tamen complementum erit in altera vita A- pocal. 21,25. Glossa Grotiana: ET CESSARE FA- CIAM BESTIAS PESSIMAS DE TERRA: quod fieri solet, ubi terra multum habitatur & colitur, nimis frigida est. (8) Gentium vocatio: ET QUI HABITANT IN DESERTO, SECURE DOR- MIENT IN SALTIBUS. Quinam illi sunt, qui in deserto habitant, nisi gentiles, qui ita describi so- lent, utpote gratia divina destituti? Es. 49,45. Cant. 8,5. (9) Spiritualis benedictio. Quæ v. 26. designa- tur: ET PONAM EOS IN CIRCUITU COLLIS MEI BENEDICTIONEM. Qua phra- si beneficiorum copia exprimitur. Quum dare ali- quem in benedictionem sit tantis ipsum cumulare bonis, ut quasi exemplum & signum sit, ex quo alii argumentum divinæ gloriæ depromant. Conf. si- miles Idiotismos Ps. 21,7. Zach 3,9. Ruth. 4,14. DE- DUCAM IMBREM IN TEMPORE SUO, ET PLUVIÆ BENEDICTIONIS ERUNT. Quo respicitur imber verbi & pluvia Evangelii, quæ ve- ram benedictionem adfert Es. 55, 11. Ps. 68, 10. De qua benedictione Apostolus Rom. 15, 29. Scio quoniam veniens ad vos, in abundantia benedictionis Christi veniam. Et Ephes. 1, 3. Benedictus DEUS & pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione spirituali, in cælestibus in Christo. (10) Spiritualis liberatio. Dicuntur vin- cula jugi conterenda, ac liberandi ipsi de manu im- perantium sibi. Nullum autem gravius vinculum jugi est, quam spiritualis servitutis, è qua in veram libertatem nos restituit Christus Joh. 8,36. Rom. 8, 2. Confer Es. 9,6. Act. 15,10. Similiter à fame li- berandi sunt. NON ERUNT IMMINUTI FA- ME (Non consumentur fame in TERRA.) Quod non de fame corporis intelligi potest: hac enim premuntur non raro fideles, sed de animæ fame. Am. 8,11. Quia Christus pascit abunde verbo Evan- gelii. Porro liberandi sunt ab opprobrio omni. NEQUE PORTABUNT ULTRA OPFRO- BRIUM GENTIUM. Quod implebitur in fide- libus perfecte demum in altera vita, ubi nulla igno- minia locum habebit, sed gloria cælesti fulgebunt Dan. 12,1. Matth. 13,43. (11) Germinis hujus celebra- tissimi indicatio. ET SUSCITABO EIS GER- MEN NOMINATUM, vel potius CELEBRE, quod esse Christum, celebratum sub germinis à Deo suscitandi notione è Jer. 23, 5. c. 33, 15. Zach. 2. & 6. constat. Quod vere celebre germen erat in promissionibus Vet. Testamenti. Sed magis ce- lebre in Confessionibus sub Novo Testamento, cu- jus nomen & res gestæ in toto terrarum orbe cele- brantur, & præconio verbi ac confessione marty- rum decantantur. Ad posteritatem sub Maccabæo- rum tempore hæc rapit Grotius, sed sine ullo fun- damento. (12) Christi explicatio. Qui quum Joh.10. de pastoribus reprobis rejiciendis concionatus ef- fet, se unum pastorem illum bonum esse, qui hic ab Ezechiele reprobis pastoribus opponebatur, ut istis rejectis, curam gregis sui ageret, testatus est: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, Ego sum ILLE PA- STOR ILLE BONUS, articulo isto gemino, quasi exerto digito demonstrans Pastorem illum bonum ab Ezechiele prædictum. His ergo argumen- tis inducti Doctores Christiani, magno consensu, de Christo hoc vaticinium accepêre, tum veteres Ambrof. lib. 7. Epist. 47. Theodoret, & Hieron. in h. l. August. lib. de octo quæst. quæst. 5. & alii ; tum recentiores, qui hic uno ore, Pontificii, Nostri, & Re- formati Prophetiam de Christo haberi agnoscunt. Neque id diffitentur Ebræi. Nam & Targum Jonathan de Messia exposuit, & fatetur R. David Kimchi in h. l. ita exponi Deum. Solus Grotius cum Judæis quibusdam recentioribus de Zoroba- bele hæc intelligit, nec nisi mere carnalia, & corpora- lia de terra à feris purganda, hominibus replenda, de arboribus fertilibus, & frugibus uberibus, & quæ his similia proponi credidit. Confer quæ ad cap. 37.

## 34:25
Vers. 25.

AND I WILL MAKE A COVENANT OF PEACE WITH THEM] I will renew my covenant with them through the Prophets. See Neh. 10.

AND I WILL MAKE THE WORST BEASTS CEASE FROM THE EARTH] Which is wont to happen where the land is much inhabited and cultivated.

AND THEY WHO DWELL IN THE DESERT, SHALL SLEEP SECURELY IN THE FORESTS] In the Hebrew: And they shall dwell in the desert confidently, and shall sleep in the woods. Thus all things shall be full of men.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

ET FACIAM CUM EIS PACTUM PACIS] Fœdus meum per Prophetas cum illis innovabo. Vide Neh. 10.

ET CESSARE FACIAM BESTIAS PESSIMAS DE TERRA] Quod fieri solet, ubi terra multum & ha- bitatur & colitur.

ET QUI HABITANT IN DESERTO, SECURI DORMIENT IN SALTIBUS] In Hebræo: Et habi- tabunt in deserto confidenter, & in sylvis dormient. Ita omnia plena erunt hominibus.

## 34:26
Vers. 26. AND I WILL MAKE THEM A BLESSING AROUND MY HILL] In the Hebrew: And I will give to them (the woods) and to all (the places) which are around my hill, (in the circuit of Jerusalem) most prosperous things.

AND I WILL BRING DOWN THE RAIN IN TIME] I will send down.

THERE SHALL BE SHOWERS OF BLESSING] That rain shall be prospering their affairs.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET PONAM EOS IN CIRCUITU COL- LIS MEI BENEDICTIONEM] In Hebræo: Et dabo il- lis (sylvis) & omnibus (locis) quæ sunt circa collem meum, (in circuitu Hierosolymorum) res prosperrimas.

ET DEDUCAM IMBREM IN TEMPORE] Demittam.

PLUVIÆ BENEDICTIONIS ERUNT] Is imber erit prosperans res ipsorum.

## 34:27
Ver. 27. AND THE TREE OF THE FIELD SHALL YIELD ITS FRUIT] The trees shall be fertile: which usually happens in soil previously exhausted.

AND THE EARTH SHALL YIELD ITS INCREASE] Crops.

WHEN I HAVE BROKEN THE BANDS OF THEIR YOKE] Shackles. See Isaiah 58, 6. & 9.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET DABIT LIGNUM AGRI FRUCTUS SUOS] Arbores erunt fertiles: quod plerumque evenit in solo pridem exhausto.

ET TERRA DABIT GERMEN SUUM] Fruges.

CUM CONTRIVERO CATENAS JUGI EO- RUM] Numellas. Vide Esaiam 58, 6. & 9.

## 34:28
Ver. 28.

THEY SHALL DWELL SAFELY] Which was certainly most true, not a short time after the return.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

HABITABUNT CONFIDENTER] Quod certe verissimum fuit, non exiguo post reditum tempore.

## 34:29
Ver. 29.

AND I WILL RAISE UP FOR THEM A RENOWNED PLANT] A most celebrated posterity: which happened especially in the time of the Maccabees. See Isa. 60, 21.

AND THEY SHALL NO MORE BE CONSUMED WITH HUNGER IN THE LAND] They shall no more pine away with hunger, namely as formerly. Above 5, 1. 2. 10. ch. 6, 11. 12. ch. 7, 6. 15. ch. 12, 16. & elsewhere.

NEITHER SHALL THEY BEAR THE REPROACH OF THE GENTILES ANY MORE] They shall not be a laughingstock.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ET SUSCITABO EIS GERMEN NOMINA- TUM] Posteritatem celeberrimam : quod maxime conti- git Maccabæorum tempore. Vid. Esa. 60, 21.

ET NON ERUNT ULTRA IMMINUTI FA- ME IN TERRA] Non ultra tabescent fame, nempe ut olim. Supra 5, 1. 2. 10. c. 6, 11. 12. c. 7, 6. 15. c. 12, 16. & alibi.

NEQUE PORTABUNT ULTRA OPPROBRIUM GENTIUM] Non erunt ludibrio.

## 34:30
Ver. 30.

WITH THEM] A supporter and helper to them.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

CUM EIS] Ipsis fautor & adjutor.

## 34:31
Verse 31.

BUT YOU, MY FLOCKS, THE FLOCKS OF MY PASTURE, ARE MEN] That is, what I have represented in cattle, these pertain not to cattle, but to men, and indeed to the Jews. Those cattle are men, just as the cows are years, Gen. 41, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

VOS AUTEM GREGES MEI, GREGES PA- SCUÆ MEÆ HOMINES ESTIS] Id est, quæ in pe- cudibus figuravi, hæc non ad pecudes, sed ad homines, & quidem Judæos, pertinent. Istæ pecudes sunt homines, sicut boves sunt anni, Gen. 41, 26.

## 35:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXV. The devastation of Mount Seir or the Idumeans, because they afflicted the people of God.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXV. Montis Seir sive Idumæorum vastatio, eo quod populum Dei afflixerint.

## 35:2
Verse 2. SET THY FACE. A phrase of the Vulgate, says B. Hülsem., for a hostile or threatening posture against someone. See ch. 29, 2. ch. 28, 21. ch. 25, 2. Osiand. Prepare to prophesy against the Idumeans, who dwell in the mountains of Seir, and that let the listeners understand that you are dealing with a serious matter, turn your face toward that region. Alexander the Great, whom Jeremiah therefore calls a YOUTH, carried out this Prophecy, as is also the case in Jer. 49, but Judas Maccabeus also afflicted the Idumeans, 1 Macc. 5.

Verse same. AGAINST MOUNT SEIR] Which is Idumea, Gen. 36, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PONE FACIEM TUAM. Phrasis Vulgatæ, inquit B. Hülsem. pro habitu ini- mico seu comminatorio adversus aliquem. V. c. 29, 2. c. 28, 21. c. 25, 2. Osiand. Para ad vaticinandum con- tra Idumæos, qui habitant in montanis Seir, & ut intelligant auditores, te rem seriam agere, vertes faciem tuam adversus illam regionem. Hanc autem Prophetiam qualis etiam Jerem. 49. est, exequutus Alexand. M. quem Jeremias propterea JUVE- NEM vocat, sed & Judas Maccabeus Idumæos af- flixit, Macc. 5.

Vers. eod. ADVERSUS MONTEM SEIR] Quæ est Idumæa, Gen. 36, 9.

## 35:3
Verse 3. BEHOLD, I AM AGAINST THEE MOUNT SEIR] Namely, I am coming: as has been said often above. I WILL MAKE THEE MOST DESOLATE] It is the same as what is predicted in Jer. 49, 7. where see it.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ECCE, EGO AD TE MONS SEIR] Venio nempe: ut jam sæpe supra. DABO TE DESOLATUM ATQUE DESER- TUM] Idem est, quod prædicitur Jer. 49, 7. ubi vide.

## 35:5
Verse 5. BECAUSE THOU HAST HAD A PERPETUAL HATRED] An heir to the hatred which Esau bore toward Jacob.

Verse same. AND HAST SHED THE BLOOD OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL BY THE FORCE OF THE SWORD] That is, you denied them refuge when they were being pressed by the Assyrians, and then by the Chaldeans. However, these things do not pertain to the siege of Jerusalem carried out simultaneously by the Idumeans and Babylonians, as Lyra, Hugo, and Dionysius maintain.

Verse same. IN THE TIME OF THEIR CALAMITY] The same expression as above 21, 25. 29. when the time of the Jews' punishment had come.

Latin:

Vers. 5. EO QUOD FUERIS INIMICUS SEMPITER- NUS] Heres odii, quod Esau in Jacobum gessit.

Vers. eod. ET CONCLUSERIS FILIOS ISRAEL IN MA- NIIS GLADII] Id est, perfugium ipsis negaveris, cum ab Assyriis, ac deinde à Chaldæis premerentur. Non autem hæc pertinent ad obsidionem Hie- rosol. simul ab Idumæis & Babyloniis factam, ut Lyrn, Hugo & Dionys. volunt.

Vers. eod. IN TEMPORE INIQUITATIS EXTREMÆ] Locutio eadem, quæ supra 21, 25. 29. cum pœnæ Judæo- rum tempus venisset.

## 35:6
Verse 6. I WILL PREPARE THEE UNTO BLOOD] In the Hebrew: I will make thee into blood: I will expose you to slaughter. AND BLOOD SHALL PURSUE THEE] Slaughter. AND SINCE THOU HAST NOT HATED BLOOD] In the Hebrew: because you have not hated blood: that is, you loved a bloodthirsty life. Glassius, lib. 4, Phil. p. 462, does not connect the particles 'if' with the preceding: As I live, unless you have hated blood, blood also shall pursue you.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SANGUINI TRADAM TE] In Hebræo: In san- guinem faciam te: cædi te exponam. ET SANGUIS TE PERSEQUETUR] Cædes. ET CUM SANGUINEM ODERIS] In Hebræo: quia odisti non sanguinem: id est, vitam amasti sanguinariam. Glaffius l. 4. Phil. p. 462. particulas fi non con- nectit cum prioribus: Vivo ego, nisi quia sangui- nem oderis, etiam sanguis persequetur te.

## 36:23
Vers. 23. I WILL SANCTIFY MY GREAT NAME] I will cause my power to appear. BEFORE THEM] Thus both the Chaldean and the Greeks, who all read לעיניהם, not as we have it, לעיניכם. At this place, the observation of Junius-Tremellius is to be noted. This reading, he says, the Chaldean Paraphrast preserves, and a manuscript book has it; although in the Vulgate copies it is read BEFORE YOUR EYES, contrary to the testimony of the Masoretes themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SANCTIFICABO NOMEN MEVM MAGNVM] Efficiam ut appareat potentia mea. CORAM EIS] Sic & Chaldæus & Græci, qui o- mnes legère לעיניהם, non ut nos habemus, לעיניכם. Ad hunc locum notanda observatio Junio- Tremelliana. Hanc lectionem, inquit, servat Chal- dæus Paraphrastes, & habet liber manuscriptus; etsi in Vulgate exemplaribus legitur ANTE OCU- LOS VESTROS, præter ipsum Massoretarum te- stimonium.

## 36:24
Vers. 24. I WILL GATHER YOU FROM ALL THE GENTILES] Of the Babylonian empire, and from elsewhere. Above 34:12.

Latin:

Vers. 24. CONGREGABO VOS DE VNIVERSIS GENTI- BVS] Babylonici imperii, & aliunde. Supra 34, 12.

## 36:25
Vers. 25. I WILL POUR CLEAN WATER UPON YOU] The pious warnings of the Prophets, which will not cleanse the body, as that water of sprinkling mentioned in Num. 19, but the soul. These are preparations for the Gospel and for Baptism. The Jews wrongly refer these to the time after the resurrection.

Not only preparations for the Gospel, but true Evangelical promises are exhibited here. Therefore, they are to be explained concerning the benefits of the New Testament. This is confirmed by (1) the universal calling, verse 21. I WILL GATHER YOU FROM ALL NATIONS. Grotius rashly restricts this, since it sounds universal. The discourse here is about gathering from all nations, not just from some. (2) The pouring out of clean water. Which cannot be understood as the pious admonitions of the Prophets; for the soul is not purged by admonitions, but by faith, Acts 15:21, and by the blood of Christ, 1 John 1:7, Heb. 9:15, 1 Cor. 6:11. And also by the word of the Gospel and the Sacraments, Eph. 5:26. The effect of this sprinkling of water is liberation from sins. But cleansing from iniquities and the remission of sins comes to us not through the law and legal admonitions, but through the word of grace, apprehended by true faith: that those who believe in Him obtain remission of sins in the name of Jesus is confirmed by the testimony of all the Prophets, Acts 10:43. Therefore, Ambrose, Jerome, Augustine, Hugo, Isidore, and others explain this as the benefits of the New Testament: by the name of clean water, by which we are cleansed from iniquity, the sprinkling or pouring of which ought to have taken place in the New Testament, some understand Baptism, by the force of the sayings in Eph. 5:26, Heb. 10:22; some the Holy Spirit, who was to be poured out like water, John 7:38; some in general the Evangelical grace of the New Testament. These opinions are subordinate if they are accepted in such a way that a large pouring out of grace and the gift of the Holy Spirit is promised, which occurred both invisibly in Baptism and visibly upon the Apostles at the feast of Pentecost. Moreover, the name of water is used because God sometimes willed to use this medium for spiritual purification: which was also signified by the Levitical sprinklings and washings in the Old Testament. (3) The gift of a new heart and spirit. Which brings about regeneration and renewal, when the heart of stone is taken away and a heart of flesh is given to us, which Paul teaches happens both through the word of truth and also in Baptism, Tit. 3:6. But this gift of regeneration and renewal is not a preparation for the Gospel, but an effect of the Gospel: inasmuch as it is the power of God unto salvation, Rom. 1:16. (4) The bestowing of the Holy Spirit. AND I WILL PUT MY SPIRIT WITHIN YOU: this is not to be taken only concerning the Prophetic Spirit, by which the Prophets were instructed especially under the Old Testament, much less restricted to Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, but it embraces any gifts of the Spirit, both ministering and especially sanctifying, because it is added, AND I WILL MAKE YOU WALK IN MY STATUTES. Therefore, the discourse is about that gift of the Spirit by which it comes to pass that we walk in the statutes of the Lord. Which is the Spirit of sanctification. (5) Spiritual salvation, concerning which see verse 29. And I will save you from all your uncleannesses: that is, not only from idolatrous worship, but from any sins whatsoever, which are uncleannesses and pollutions. Whence we are said to be cleansed from sin, 1 John 1:7. Nor is only the washing away of punishments noted by that phrase, as Grotius wishes at verse 33, but also the forgiveness of guilt. Jerome also urges the promise, verse 11. And I will fill you with men and beasts, and they shall multiply and increase: and I will make you dwell as at the beginning, and I will bestow upon you greater goods than you had from the beginning. Some of the Jews, he says, think these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel, but how can this stand, which is said: And I will make you dwell as at the beginning, and I will bestow upon you greater goods than you had from the beginning? For under Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah, few of the people were brought back, and they themselves served the Medes, and Persians, and subsequently the Macedonians and Egyptians, and the Romans, up to Titus and Vespasian, kings of different nations, and they serve even to this day, so that this which the prophecy says at the end cannot stand at all: and you shall no longer bear the reproach of the nations, and you shall not lose your nation any more. Although we may admit that promises concerning temporal things are also intermingled, and the return to the land of Canaan, and the blessing of trees and fields, as well as the multiplication of the Israelite nation, verses 29, 30, 33, etc. Nevertheless, the spiritual benefits of calling, regeneration, justification, and sanctification are primarily promised here: And the Lord promised the return of the people to the land of Canaan for this reason, that divine worship might be restored there, and the Israelites might be a people to the Lord, and He might be a God to them, and thus the kingdom of Christ might be propagated, which is prophesied to be propagated most of all in the fullness of time, with the waters of cleansing poured out and the mission of the Holy Spirit. See Osiander and Pappus on this passage. Jerome has it thus in this passage; delivering not his private, but, as he speaks, an ECCLESIASTICAL UNDERSTANDING: The house of Israel, that is, the people of the Jews, once dwelt in their land, that is, in the land of Judea, when it was led out of Egypt: but they polluted it in their ways and in their pursuits, or their idols, and they were so polluted that they were compared to the uncleanness of a menstruous woman. On account of which God poured out His indignation upon them, for the blood of the Prophets and righteous men, which they had shed upon the earth, the Savior saying in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the Prophets: and stone those who are sent to you. And again: Amen, Amen, I say to you: the blood which has been shed shall be required from this generation, from the blood of righteous Abel, unto the blood of Zechariah, son of Berechiah, whom they shed between the altar and the temple. But they not only shed blood, but also polluted the land with their crimes. Wherefore He scattered them, either under the Babylonian captivity or under the Roman: when they truly shed the blood of Christ: and they were winnowed into lands, as chaff is winnowed, and judged according to their ways and their worst inventions, so that even among the nations to which they had been led captive, they polluted the holy name of God: in that all nations would say by way of mockery: Behold, this is the people of God, who boasted that they properly knew the worship of God: Which when I had seen, he says, not for their sake, but for my holy name. For I am the Creator of all, I have spared them, and I have sanctified them: and I have restored them to their pristine glory, so that upon those believing and converted from error I might pour out the clean water of saving Baptism, and I might cleanse them from their abominations, and from all the errors by which they had been occupied: and I might give them a new heart, that they might believe in the Son of God: and a new spirit, of which David speaks: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right Spirit within my bowels. And it is to be considered, that a new heart and a new Spirit is given through the pouring out and sprinkling of water. But when a new heart and a new Spirit shall have been given, then all hardness, which is compared to a stone, shall be taken away from the Jewish heart, so that in place of a stony heart there may be a heart of flesh, soft and tender, which may be able to receive the Spirit of God within itself and to be inscribed with saving letters. Then they shall walk in the precepts of the Lord, and they shall keep his judgments, and they shall dwell in the land of confession, which he had given to their Fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and to all the saints and Prophets: and they shall be a people of God, and the Lord shall be to them for GOD, which is proven in the present time. Finally, he also explains the last part of verse 33, concerning the restoration of Judea to its entirety, in such a way that its fulfillment,

(although it may be begun by Zerubbabel) it must be placed in the times of the New Testament, and he hands down that this is the ecclesiastical understanding: But after He has cleansed the people of believers from among the Jews from their iniquities, and has caused the cities of the Church to be inhabited: and has restored the ruined things, which had fallen in the synagogues: and the land of confession has been cultivated with the ceremonies of God, which once seemed desolate to all the saints, who pass over the works of earthly conversation; Then all shall say: That the land of Judea, which once had been uncultivated, now has the likeness of the paradise of God, and the cities of Judea, which had been deserted, and destitute, and undermined by their own unbelief, are now erected and fortified in the confession and name of the Lord the Savior, so that every creature may know; and the multitudes of angels, which surround the land of Israel, that the Lord has built up the dissipated cities: and has planted the uncultivated regions; and that which He had promised through the Prophets, He has completed in deed. Nor will He be content with this gift of His liberality toward the people whom He has saved, but He will provide many greater things. For there shall be found by the house of Israel, that which had been sought for a long time, and not found. And after He has found it, He will multiply them like sheep: not of brute animals, but of men, who are full of reason and confession: like holy sheep and the flocks of Jerusalem: in which is properly the worship of God, and the vision of peace, in its solemnities: when we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth: and we feed on the flesh of the lamb and are watered with its blood, and in the seven weeks and in the tabernacles of this age we celebrate the Lord's feasts, so that the cities once deserted may become full of flocks of men, so that by this reason they may know, that He Himself is the Lord, who has provided all things. Let it suffice to have said briefly, according to the truth of history, nay, according to the faith of Prophecy: how the people of Israel is restored to an integral state, and the remnants of the people of the Jews, as the Apostle Paul teaches, are saved in the Apostles, and in all who from among the Jews believed in the beginning, and even to this day return to the Church. And Jerome wishes this to be the literal sense. For he expounds it according to the truth of History and the faith of Prophecy. Finally, he adds the tropological sense there. Nor could Grotius himself entirely deny that these things are to be referred to the times of the New Testament, although according to his custom he asserts that this is done in a more sublime sense, i.e., mystical, not literal, at v. 29. Even the ancient Jews acknowledged that these benefits belong to the Messiah, and that it is the Messiah who was to sprinkle clean waters, by the power of this Prophet: Since in Bereschit Ketanna on Gen. 49, 11. it is held thus: This is He, of whom it is written (Zach. 9, 9.) Poor and riding upon an ass and upon a colt the foal of asses. And He is the one who was planting Israel, like שורק, i.e., like a choice vine. And in what manner will He be acting? As it is said (Ezech. 36. v. 25.) And I will sprinkle clean waters upon you, and you shall be cleansed from all your uncleannesses. For that Christ is understood in Zach. 9, and it cannot be taken of another, R. Solomon confesses expressly in the gloss cited above: Behold, thy King cometh: It is not possible, he says, to explain this, except of King Messiah.

Latin:

Vers. 25. EFFVNDAM SVPER VOS AQVAM MVN- DAM] Pia Prophetarum monita, quæ non corpus purga- bunt, ut aqua illa aspersionis memorata Num. 19. sed ani- mum. Præparamenta hæc sunt ad Evangelium & ad Ba- ptismum. Male Judæi hæc referunt ad tempus post re- surrectionem,

Non præparamenta tantum ad Evangelium, sed veræ Evangelicæ promissiones hic exhibentur. Ideo explicandæ de beneficiis N. Testamenti. Quod confirmat (1) universalis vocatio vers. 21. CONGREGABO VOS DE UNIVERSIS GENTIBUS. Hoc temere restringit Grotius, quum universaliter sonet. De universis gentibus congregandis hic sermo est, non de quibusdam tantum. (2) Aquæ mundæ effusio. Quæ non potest de piis Prophetarum monitis intelligi; nam anima monitis non purgatur, sed fide Actor. 15, 21. & sanguine Christi, 1. Joh. 1, 7. Ebr. 9, 15. 1. Corinth. 6, 11. Nec non verbo Evangelii, & Sacramentis Ephes. 5, 26. Effectus aspersionis aquæ hujus est liberatio à peccatis. At emundatio ab iniquitatibus, & peccatorum remissio non per legem & monita legalia, sed per verbum gratiæ, vera fide apprehensum nobis obtingit: In nomine Jesu remissionem peccatorum obtinere eos, qui credunt in ipsum, omnium Prophetarum testimonio constat, Act. 10, 43. Ideo de beneficiis Novi Testamenti exponunt Ambrosius, Hieronymus, Augustinus, Hugo, Isidorus aliique: Aquæ mundæ nomine, qua emundamur ab iniquitate, cujus aspersio vel effusio fieri debuit in Novo Testamento, nonnulli Baptismum intelligunt, vi dictorum Eph. 5, 26. Ebr. 10, 22. nonnulli Spiritum Sanctum, qui effundendus instar aquæ erat Joh. 7, 38. Nonnulli in genere gratiam Evangelicam Novi Testamenti. Quæ sententiæ subordinatæ sunt, si ita accipiantur, quod promittatur larga effusio gratiæ, ac donum Spiritus Sancti, quæ tum in Baptismo fit invisibili, tum in festo Pentecostes visibili modo super Apostolos facta est. Aquæ autem nomen adhibetur, quia Deus aliquando hoc medium adhibere voluit ad purgationem spiritualem: quod etiam per aspersiones & lotiones Leviticas in Veteri Testamento significatum fuit. (3) Cordis & Spiritus novi donatio. Quæ regenerationem & renovationem infert, cum cor lapideum tollitur, & cor carneum donatur nobis, quod tum per verbum veritatis fit, tum etiam in Baptismo fieri Paulus docet Tit. 3, 6. Hoc autem donum regenerationis, & renovationis, non præparatio ad Evangelium, sed Evangelii effectus est: utpote quod potentia Dei est ad salutem, Rom. 1, 16. (4) Spiritus Sancti largitio. ET SPIRITUM MEUM PONAM IN MEDIO VESTRI: id non de Spiritu Prophetico solum accipiendum, quo instructi fuêre cumprimis sub Veteri Testamento Prophetæ, nedum restringendum ad Haggæum, Zachariam, Malachiam, sed quævis dona Spiritus tum ministrantia, tum maxime etiam sanctificantia complectitur, quia additur, ET FACIAM UT IN PRÆCEPTIS MEIS AMBULETIS. De ea ergo Spiritus donatione sermo est, qua fit, ut in præceptis Domini ambulemus. Qui est Spiritus sanctificationis. (5) Spiritualis salvatio, de qua v. 29. Et salvabo vos ex universis inquinamentis vestris: hoc est, non tantum à cultibus idololatricis, sed à peccatis quibusvis, quæ inquinamenta & pollutiones sunt. Unde à peccato mundari dicimur, 1. Joh. 1, 7. Neque tantum pœnarum ablutio ea phrasi notatur, ut Grotius vult ad vers. 33. sed culpæ etiam condonatio. Urget etiam Hieronymus promissionem, v. 11. Et replebo vos hominibus & jumentis, & multiplicabuntur & crescent: & habitare vos faciam sicut à principio, bonisq́; donabo majoribus, quam habuistis ab initio. Arbitrantur, inquit, nonnulli è Judæis hæc sub Zorobabele esse completa, sed quomodo stare poterit hoc, quod dicitur: Et habitare vos faciam sicut à principio, bonisque donabo majoribus, quam habuistis ab initio. Sub Zorobabel enim, Esdra & Nehemia pauci de populo sunt reducti, & ipsi obedientes Medis, ac Persis, & deinceps Macedonibus & Aegyptiis, atq́; Romanis, usq́; ad Titum & Vespa- sianum diversarum gentium Regibus servierunt, & us- que hodie serviunt, ut stare omnino non possit hoc, quod in extrema dicit Prophetia: & opprobrium popu- lorum nequaquam portabis, & gentem tuam non amittes amplius. Quamquam vero admitta- mus, admisceri etiam promissiones de rebus tempora- libus, & reductione in terram Canaan, ac benedictione arborum & agrorum, nec non multiplicatione gentis Israëliticae v. 29. 30. 33. seqq. Spiritualia tamen benefi- cia vocationis, regenerationis, justificationis, sanctifica- tionis imprimis hic promittuntur: Et reductionem populi in terram Canaan ideo pollicitus est Domi- nus, ut ibi restauretur cultus divinus, & Israëlitae sint Domino in populum, & ipse iis sit in Deum, adeoq; propagetur regnum Christi, quod maxime in ple- nitudine temporis propagatum iri vaticinatur, ef- fusis aquis mundis & missione Spiritus Sancti. Videa- tur Osiander, & Pappus in h. l. Hieronymus ita ha- bet in hac pericopa; non suam privatam, sed Eccle- siasticam, ut loquitur, tradens INTELLIGEN- TIAM: Domus Israël, hoc est, populus Judaeorum ha- bitavit quondam in terra sua, hoc est, in terra Judaea, quando educta est de Aegypto: sed polluerunt eam in viis & in studiis, sive Idolis suis, & in tantum extitere polluti, ut immunditiae mulieris menstruata compa- rati sint. Propter quod Deus effudit indignationem suam super eos, pro sanguine Prophetarum atq́; justo- rum, quem fuderant super terram, dicente in Evan- gelio Salvatore: Hierusalem, Hierusalem, quae occi- dis Prophetas: & lapidas eos, qui ad te missi sunt. Et iterum: Amen, Amen, dico vobis: requiretur san- guis, qui effusus est, a generatione hac, a sanguine Abel justi, usque ad sanguinem Zachariae, filii Bara- chiae, quem effuderunt inter altare & templum. Non solum autem effuderunt sanguinem, sed & pol- luerunt terram sceleribus suis. Quamobrem dispersit eos, vel sub Babylonica captivitate, vel sub Romana: quando vere effuderunt sanguinem Christi: & ventila- ti sunt in terras, quomodo paleae ventilantur, & juxta vias suas & inventiones pessimas judicati, ita ut in gentibus quoq; ad quas captivi ducti fuerant, polluerent nomen sanctum Dei: eo quod per irrisio- nem dicerent universae nationes: Ecce populus Dei iste est, qui jactabat se proprie nosse cultum Dei: Quod cum vidissem, ait, non propter eos, sed pro- pter nomen meum sanctum. Creator enim o- mnium sum, peperci eis, & sanctificavi illos: & glo- riae pristinae restitui, ita ut super credentes, & ab errore conversos effunderem aquam mundam Baptismi salutaris, & mundarem eos ab abominationibus suis, & ab universis erroribus, quibus fuerant occu- pati: & darem eis cor novum, ut crederent in filium Dei: & spiritum novum, de quibus David loquitur: Cor mundum crea in me Deus: & Spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis. Et considerandum, quod cor novum, & Spiritus novus detur per effusionem & aspersonem aquae. Quando autem cor novum & Spi- ritus novus datus fuerit, tunc auferetur de corde Ju- daico omnis duritia, quae lapidi comparatur, ut pro lapideo corde sit cor carneum, molle & tenerum, quod Spiritum Dei possit in se recipere & inscribi li- teris salutaribus. Tunc ambulabunt in praeceptis Domini, & custodient judicia ejus, & habitabunt in terra confessionis, quam dederat Patribus eorum, Abraham, Isaac & Jacob, & cunctis sanctis atque Prophetis: & erunt in populum Dei, & Dominus erit eis in DEUM, quod praesen- ti tempore comprobatur. Denique postremam etiam partem vers. 33. de restitutione Judaeae in integrum ita explicat, ut complementum ejus,

(etsi inchoetur à Zorobabele) ponendum sit in tempora Novi Testamenti, eamque Ecclesiasticam intelligentiam esse tradit: Postquam autem munda- verit credentium ex Judæis populum ab iniquitatibus suis, & habitari fecerit urbes Ecclesiæ: & restaura- verit ruinosa, quæ in Synagogis conciderant: & ter- ræ confessio nis fuerit exculta ceremoniis Dei, quæ quondam visa est desolata omnibus sanctis, qui terre- næ conversationis opera prætereunt; Tunc omnes di- cent: Quod terra Judææ, quæ quondam fuerat inculta, nunc habet similitudinem paradysi Dei, & civitates Judææ, quæ desertæ fuerant, & destitutæ & sua incredulitate suffossæ, nunc erectæ & munitæ sunt in confessione & nomine Domini Salvatoris, ita ut omnis creatura cognoscat; & multitudines angelorum, quæ terram ambiunt Israël, quod Do- minus dissipatas ædificaverit civitates: & incultas plantaverit regiones; & quod pollicitus fuerat per Prophetas, opere compleverit. Ne hoc erit libera- litatis suæ in populum, quem salvarit, contentus mu- nere, sed multa majora præstabit. Invenietur enim à domo Israël, qui multo tempore quæsitus fuerat, & non inventus. Et postquam invenerit eum, mul- tiplicabit eos sicut oves: non brutorum animan- tium, sed hominum, quæ rationis & confessionis sunt plenæ: sicut oves sanctas & greges Hierusalem: in quæ proprie Dei cultus, & visio pacis est, in solemnita- tibus ejus: quando comedimus azyma sinceritatis & veritatis: & agni carnibus vescimur & cruore pota- mur, & in septem hebdomadibus & in tabernaculis hujus seculi dominica festa celebramus, ut civitates quondam desertæ plenæ fiant gregibus hominum, ut hac ratione cognoscant, quod ipse sit Dominus, qui cuncta præstiterit. Hæc juxta historiæ veritatem, imo juxta Prophetiæ fidem: quomodo populus Israel restituatur in integrum statum, & reliquiæ populi Ju- dæorum, Apostolo Paulo docente, salvæ sint in Apo- stolis, & in omnibus, qui ex Judæis in principio cre- diderunt, & usq; hodie redeunt ad Ecclesiam, brevi- ter dixisse sufficiat. Atque hunc sensum literalem esse vult Hieronymus. Nam juxta Historiæ verita- tem & Prophetiæ fidem exponit. Postremum de- mum sensum tropologicum ibi subjungens. Neq; referenda hæc esse ad tempora Novi Testamenti, omnino diffiteri potuit ipse Grotius, etsi pro more suo sensu sublimiori id fieri, h. e. mystico, non litera- li, asserat, ad v. 29. Judæi etiam veteres agnoverunt hæc beneficia Messiæ convenire, ac Messiam esse, qui sparsurus erat aquas mundas, vi hujus Prophe- tæ: Siquidem in Bereschit Ketanna ad Gen. 49, 11. ita habeatur: Hic est ille, de quo scriptum est (Zach. 9, 9.) Pauper & equitans super asinum & super pul- lum filium asinarum. Et ipse est, qui erat plantans Israelem, sicut שורק, i. e. sicut Sarmentum electum. Et qualiter ipse erit agens? sicut dictum est (Ezech. 36. v. 25.) Et spargam super vos aquas mundas, & mundabimini ab omnibus immunditiis vestris. Nam quod Zach. 9. Christus intelligatur, nec de alio accipi possit, διαῤῥήδην fatetur R. Salomo in glossa supra allata: Ecce, Rex tuus venit: Non est, inquit, possibile exponi hoc, nisi de Rege Messia.

## 37:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVII.

In the figure of the dry bones coming back to life, the resurrection of the dead is signified, and by the two joined sticks, the union of the kingdom of the Jews and of Israel, who under one King and Shepherd David (the Messiah, Son of David) shall observe the commandments of the Lord, who will make an everlasting covenant with them.

Vers. 1.

AND HE BROUGHT ME OUT IN THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD] Better, the Lord; it signifies that he was not transported in body, but saw these things in a vision, as above 8, 3. See 2 Cor. 12, 2.

IN THE MIDST OF A PLAIN, WHICH WAS FULL OF BONES] A people led into captivity ceases to be a people, and therefore is best compared to bones or a dead body. See our work on the Law of War and Peace 2. c. 9. Thus Sulpicius called the corpses of towns in his letter to Cicero. This plain refers to Mesopotamia and the neighboring places.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVII.

In figura aridorum ossium reviviscentium mortuorum resuscitatio, & duorum li- gnorum conjunctorum regni Judæorum & Israëlis conjunctio significatur, qui sub uno Rege ac Pastore David (Davidis Filio Messia) observaturi sint mandata Domi- ni, qui cum ipsis pactum faciet sempiter- num.

Vers. I.

ET EDVXIT ME IN SPIRITV DOMINI] Me- lius, Dominus; significat non corpore se translatum, sed hæc vidisse ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ, ut supra 8, 3. Vid. 2. Cor. 12, 2.

IN MEDIO CAMPI, QVI ERAT PLENVS OSSIBVS] Populus in captivitatem deductus desinit esse populus, ideoque optime comparatur ossibus aut corpo- ri mortuo. Vide nostra de jure Belli ac Pacis 2. c. 9. Sic oppidorum cadavera dixit Sulpitius in Epistola ad Cicero- nem. Campus hic Mesopotamiam refert, & loca vicina.

## 37:12
Verse 12.

I WILL OPEN YOUR GRAVES] I will cause the graves to be opened for you; I will restore your civil life to you.

A triple sense of this passage is handed down by Jerome. Some explain it as referring to the universal resurrection: which opinion Jerome expounded thus: Those who think the word of God is about the resurrection, which is believed by all, both Jews and Christians, are accustomed to say: The hand of the Lord was upon the Prophet, that is, the Lord and Savior, through whom the Father wrought all things: For all things were made through him, and without him was made nothing that was made. And he brought me out, he says, in the spirit of the Lord, the hand of the Lord being understood. He led him out, however, in the Spirit, not in the body, but outside the body: and placed him or set him down in the middle of a field, which was full of human bones: nor did He allow him to rest: But He made him go around all the bones, which were not covered with earth, but lying upon the field: and not only many, but too many, and because of the age of time arid, and vehemently dry, and having no moisture in them. And when the divine word had asked him whether he thought these bones could live, he answered; Lord God, You know, who have full knowledge of future things. And the Lord said to him: Prophesy concerning the bones, or over these bones: and you shall say to them: Dry bones hear the word of the Lord. In which it is to be wondered at, how He spoke to dry bones, which before nerves, flesh, and skin, and the life-giving spirit, could hear the word of God. And first the bones are joined with other bones by the bonds of nerves, then they are filled with flesh, and above them for beauty the skin is stretched, which might cover the foulness of the bare flesh, and then they receive the Spirit, which makes them live, and after they have lived, then they know that He is the Lord. The Prophet therefore saying what had been commanded to him, immediately a commotion was made, and the bones were applied to their own framework: Bound with nerves, full of flesh, covered with skin: and human bodies were lying there not having a spirit. Therefore the Prophet prophesies to the Spirit, and says: Thus says the Lord God: From the four winds come O Spirit: from the four quarters of the world, namely, so that just as in the first condition of man God breathed into his face, and he was made into a living soul: so also the second condition, that is, the resurrection of the dead, might be enlivened by the breathing Spirit. Which entered into the human bodies, and immediately they lived, and stood upon their feet. Whence also the resurrection of the dead is called a gathering, or a great Church, and as it is held in the Hebrew, a great army: and it is completed at the time: Send forth Your Spirit, and they shall be created, and You shall renew the face of the earth. These things from the first explanation of Jerome. Which was the opinion of Tertullian concerning the resurrection of the flesh, chapter 30, where he argues that it is more religious if it is believed that the Prophet is dealing with the resurrection, as the letter sounds, than if it is explained allegorically; because it was a matter of religion for him to depart from the literal sense. But it is more religious, he says, that the truth be defended from the authority of its own simplicity, than the sense of the divine proposition demands. For if this vision looked to Jewish affairs, immediately upon revealing the location of the bones he would have added: These bones are the whole House of Israel, etc. But when the bones were shown, concerning the own hope of those of whom he speaks, with Israel not yet named, and he tests the faith of the Prophet: Son of man, if these bones shall live, so that he also might answer, Lord, You know, God would not have tested the faith of the Prophet concerning that thing which was not to be, which Israel had never heard, which ought not to be believed: etc.

A second interpretation, that here in this vision of the Prophet is exhibited the restoration of the people corporally from the Sepulchers of captivity and the bonds by which they were held bound in Babylonian servitude, which the Jews say was fulfilled under Zerubbabel, when a great commotion was made, and the kingdom of the Chaldeans was transferred to the Medes and Persians. Although others hope for it only in the presence of their Christ, whom they think is to come, as Jerome observes here. Grotius joins himself to these, explaining it entirely concerning the corporal liberation from the Babylonian captivity. The third is the exposition of Jerome himself. Who does not indeed deny that these things began to be fulfilled also in the faithful under Zerubbabel, with the Israelite Church gathered again, but refers the complement to the times of the New Testament. But we, he says, record them as fulfilled spiritually after the cross of the Lord Savior, and that it happens daily in those, most especially, who like Lazarus, bound by the bandages of their sins, are raised at the voice of the Lord: and truly are the House of Israel, once parched, and having no hope of salvation: but with the Spirit of grace entering into them, and the Lord reaching out His hand, they are liberated from the depth of the underworld.

Our opinion is that the resurrection of the dead was exhibited to the Prophet by the Lord in this illustrious vision, but that the occasion, cause, and scope of this vision was the restoration of the Israelite people: not so much to the former form of polity, as to restoring the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy, and the divine worship to be erected in turn, which was indeed restored in part under Zerubbabel, but especially brought to perfection at the time of the advent of Christ. Now that the resurrection of the dead was represented by this vision, these things confirm. First, that the literal sense clearly implies the resurrection of the dead itself, which is nowhere else so clearly and part by part exposed as in this vision, as we have previously brought it forward from Jerome. From this literal opinion, however, it ought deservedly to be a matter of religion for us to depart. Those who, having clearly abandoned the literal sense with Grotius, pursue a mere allegory, which was also done by heretics denying the resurrection of the flesh, cannot be absolved of rashness, nor do they treat the discourse religiously enough, in the judgment of Tertullian. This preaching, he says in chapter 30 of the resurrection of the flesh, I know how they shake into an argument of allegory: because by saying, these bones are the whole House of Israel, he made them into an image of Israel, and transferred them from their own condition: and thus that it is a figurative, not a true preaching of the resurrection. For the state of the Jews is deformed, in a way dead and dried up and scattered in the field of the world. Therefore also the image of the resurrection is allegorized into it, because it is to be gathered again, and re-joined bone to bone, i.e., tribe to tribe, and people to people, and to be re-incorporated with the flesh of faculties, and the nerves of the kingdom: and thus to be led out of the sepulchers, i.e., out of the most sad and most foul habitations of captivity, and to breathe in the name of refreshment, and to live from then on in their own land of Judea. And what after these things? They will die without doubt. And what after death? No resurrection I suppose, if this will not be the very one which is revealed to Ezekiel. But indeed another resurrection is also preached; therefore this one will also be: They convert it into the state of Jewish affairs.

Furthermore, that calling of the Spirit from the four winds of the world does not fit the Grotius sense of a mere restoration from the mounds of captivity. Because the Jews were collected from Babylon alone, not from the four winds of the world, they are Zerubbabel. Which argument also seems to have moved Jerome, so that he would not admit that the prophecy was fully completed at that time. But in the universal resurrection from the four winds of the world, they will be gathered from the ends of the heavens to the ends of them, Matt. 24, 31. Mark 13, 27. Add that the great army seen by Ezekiel is said to have been resurrected. But the army led back by Zerubbabel was not so great. Theodoret on v. 9 teaches us, he says, this discourse, how easy all things are to divine power, and that all things are in his hand: for in his hand, he says, is the soul of all living things. Therefore he commands the Prophet to order all souls, wherever they may be, to return and inhabit their bodies again. Having announced, he says, the divine command from me, the bound bones came to life and attained resurrection, and the multitude of those who rose was not small.

Thirdly, since the purpose of the Prophet was to lift up and console the faithful under captivity, the confirmation of faith, taken from the resurrection of faith, which could be hoped for without doubt by all the faithful, certainly contributed more to his consolation than the promise of a future liberation after the passing of LXX years of captivity, which many of the faithful did not reach, being snatched away by death, and which offered very little solid comfort: since they were no less exposed to various calamities in the polity than in exile.

Fourthly, the Grotian gloss is too meager, that a people deprived of polity or captive men are called bones, and that the Spirit sent in denotes nothing other than the restoration of liberty and status. That the sound which the Prophet heard made was the edict of Cyrus. (Whereas the Prophet rather testifies that the commotion made from it was that bone approached bone,) that the opening of the mounds is nothing other than the restoration of Civil life. Which, as they are brought forward rashly without reason, are rejected with the same ease.

Fifthly, on the contrary, all things fit excellently with the resurrection of the dead, just as it is described elsewhere in the sacred writings. Dry bones deprived of spirit are the corpses of the deceased. They hear the Word of the Lord, whose voice those who sleep in their monuments are said to be about to hear, John 5. The Spirit is introduced into them when bodies are animated. Because this will be in the resurrection. The Lord puts nerves upon them, and makes flesh grow, and extends skin over them. Which do not fit any work of God more aptly than the resurrection of the dead. Cf. Job 19, 25.

Sixthly, the context does not object. For nothing in what follows v. 11 stands in the way of this interpretation. Son of man, these bones are the whole House of Israel: they say, our bones have dried up, and our hope has perished, and we are cut off. Therefore prophesy, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your mounds, and I will lead you out of your sepulchers, my people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel. The ancients, whom Jerome cited, he himself explained how they wished to reconcile them: But what follows: And he said to me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: seems to create a question: in that it is not spoken of a general resurrection but properly of the resurrection of the house of Israel, which says: Our bones have dried up, and our hope has perished, and we are cut off from our land, or we have despaired entirely: with them saying these things, Ezekiel is compelled to prophesy a third time, and to say to the dry bones: Thus says the Lord God: I will open your mounds. In which it is asked: If he opens the mounds, how did he say above: But they were very many upon the face of the field, and very dry. And I will lead you, he says, out of your sepulchers, my people, according to that which is written in the Gospel: The hour comes, when those who are in the sepulchers will hear the voice of the Son of God, and will come forth, those who have done good, into the resurrection of life. And again: those who have heard, will live. And if, as some think, the divine discourse speaks of a general resurrection, what need was there to say specifically: And I will bring you into the land of Israel: Since the dead ought to rise in every part of the world from those places in which they are buried. And when, he says, I have led you out of your mounds, and have given my Spirit in you, and you have lived, then I will make you rest upon your soil, so that after you have rested in the land of Israel, then you may know that I am the Lord, who have completed the promises by my work. Those, therefore, who understand these things said about the general resurrection, refer that which seems to create a question: 'These bones are the whole House of Israel,' to the resurrection of the Saints, of which the Apostle John also speaks in the Apocalypse: 'Blessed and Holy is he who has a part in the first resurrection; over him the second death has no power'; namely, that the resurrection of the saints is one thing, and that of sinners another. Whence it is also said in the first Psalm: 'The ungodly shall not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the council of the just.'
