Moreover, they confirm that the land of Israel, which the Lord promises to those who rise, is that of which it is written: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land,' and: 'I will please the Lord in the land of the living.' These things are said by those who, as we have said, suppose that Ezekiel wrote about the general resurrection. Others admit that the Israelite restoration is intended by this vision, but in such a way that a comparison is established with the resurrection of the dead, and thus the latter is assumed as certain. In this way, Tertullian adopts that opinion κατ' ἄνθρωπον: 'Finally,' he says, 'by the very fact that the revival of the Jewish state is figured by the re-embodiment and re-uniting of bones, it is proved that this will also happen to bones. For a figure could not be composed from bones if the same thing were not to happen to bones. For even if the fiction of truth is in the image, the image itself is in the truth of itself; it is necessary that there be a prior reality to which others are configured. A likeness does not fit from a vacuum; a parable does not suit from nothing. Thus, it will also be necessary to believe in the revival and breathing again of bones, such as is described, from which the reformation of Jewish affairs, such as is depicted, can be expressed.' Jerome, however, approves this opinion, and thus maintains that the restoration of the Israelite people, who were at that time captive in Babylon, is prophesied through the parable of the resurrection. But he adds the reason why the resurrection can still be argued from it: 'A likeness of the resurrection,' he says, 'would never be used to signify the restoration of the Israelite people unless the resurrection itself stood firm and were believed to be future; because no one confirms uncertain things by means of things that do not exist.' But since the question still remains whether this discourse on the vivification of bones presents the resurrection of the dead, or whether it ought to be understood solely as the restoration of the Israelite people figured by this vision? it must be said entirely that the resurrection of the dead is not assumed—as if it were merely handed down elsewhere and believed among the people—to establish the restoration of the people, but that it was directly shown and exhibited by that very vision. Yet the cause of this exhibition is added, which the following speech explains in verse 11. Namely, that the resuscitation of the dead was represented for this reason: that God wished this representation to be employed as a figure and confirmation of the restoration of the people. Not only to show the possibility, because since the bones truly dry, and entirely devoid of the vital Spirit can recover life and spirit, much more can those who are by analogy dry bones, and who cling as if in tombs, receive life and liberty. But also, that by that reason he might shadow forth, through a certain representation, the condition and state both present and subsequently to follow, that they are to be raised as if from the dead, when the Ecclesiastical polity shall be restored and public worship shall be established. Jerome does not deny this intention and mind of the Prophet: Indeed, he says, our whole assertion tends to this, how it seems incredible that a future resurrection is promised to dry bones consumed by great age, and yet what is promised is to be, so also the restoration of the people of Israel, who were led into captivity and dispersed throughout the whole world, seems indeed incredible to those who do not know the power of God, but yet it is to be: because I, says the Lord, have spoken: and I will do as I have promised. Similar things are held in Epiphanius, book 2, Tome 2, last heresy. That God can set up a body by himself before himself, was declared through Ezekiel, even if that thing was done through a parable: But the species itself was then fulfilled and perfected according to the allegory of truth. That bone is to be gathered to bone, harmony to harmony, and when the bones were dry, and neither soul nor moving Spirit was yet in them, bodies were immediately joined and, according to the words of the Prophet, solidified. Justin also teaches both scopes of this vision in Questions and Answers to the Orthodox, question 45, namely that in the first place it was indeed the resurrection of the dead, but that it was shadowed forth to this end, that they might not only take consolation from it, but also be confirmed at the same time concerning their own future restoration. Otherwise, he says, in Ezekiel, everything was a vision, both the bones and their resurrection. But this vision was exhibited to the holy Seer by God, principally indeed, that through it might be indicated the future universal resuscitation of all the dead in the whole world through Christ: but secondly, for the consolation of the Israelites, who had cut off from themselves by despair the hope of liberation from the dominion of the Babylonians, and of that servitude in which they were detained. For just as deceased bodies, placed in monuments, do not have the hope of resuscitation: so they thought themselves to be in Babylon, without hope of return and restoration. The Prophet himself declares this, when he says: And the word of the Lord was made to me, saying: Son of man, all these bones are the house of Israel. They say; Our bones have dried up, our hope has perished, and what follows. Thus there is no need, as with Cornelius à Lapide and other Papists, for us to invent various senses of the same words here; who are very tricky and perplexed in this place. Cornelius à Lapide says now grammatically, as if the resurrection of the dead were signified in the bark of the letter, and under this as if a parable the liberation of the Jews from captivity; now again under the type of liberation he wants to be understood PROPERLY AND LITERALLY the resuscitation of sinners, who are held captive in sin as if dry bones without spirit and grace, through the breathing of the Spirit and the grace of Christ; and thus he doubles here as if the Parable, and wants there to be a double literal sense. But the discourse is thus confused. For in the former part up to verse 10, it treats of the resurrection of the dead according to the letter: and that is the unique sense of that discourse. But lest the proximate cause should be hidden from the Prophet, why God wished to exhibit this resurrection of the dead to him, another discourse follows in v. 11 seq., in which the words of the former discourse are not explained nor is the apodosis of the parable rendered, but the scope of this preceding vision is exhibited, through the analogy which restoration has with bodily resuscitation. Thus Theodoret explains in this place, he accepts revelations consistent with things: for when, because of the perfidy with which they were afflicted as a disease, those Jews who had been led away captive from Judea had despaired of better things, God, the author of all things, shows them his power, and indicates to the Prophet the resurrection of dead bodies, which is far more difficult than their restoration to their former state: through whom he teaches all the people that all things are easy to him who wills. Therefore he taught the Jews and other Israelites through this: that it is very easy for God, who wills it, to vindicate those reduced to servitude into their former liberty; but to us and to all absolutely, who have received the Evangelical proclamation with faith, he shows the facility of the resurrection of our bodies, and that Nature obeys the divine word and the nod of things. And to v. 11. If I have shown that what seems much more difficult to you can be done by me quite easily, it is certainly clear that I will also do this very easily and with no trouble, I who will lead you out of the bonds of captivity as if from certain tombs and bring you back into your own country. Nor do the Jews indeed deny that there is a discourse here about the resurrection of the dead. R. Simai brought forward a saying to that effect in Gal. lib. 12. c. 2. R. Menasse Ben Israel makes this testimony superior to every exception, and praises the ancient Jews for that opinion in book 1, concerning the resurrection of the Dead, c. 11, page 22. This text, he says, is express, and greater than every exception for the resurrection of the dead. Nor does it matter that the Talmudic Rabbis dispute over this place, whether it is to be understood figuratively, or truly and properly according to the letter, that which is said by Ezekiel to be about to happen, that he should recall the dead to life? For however that may be, it is certain that God wished to indicate to Ezekiel by this Vision the future resurrection of the dead. Therefore it is said in the ancient Pirque R. Eliezer: The Israelites stood, and wept saying: We hoped for light and behold darkness. Then the Lord addressed the Prophet and said, the Lord lives, if I do not resuscitate you, when the dead shall rise, and when I shall gather with Israel: Which is the same as that: I will open your graves. It is clear therefore that they believed that the resurrection of the dead had been represented in that prophecy. Let those things be compared which we said in Sotinismo profligato page 1067. and those things which B. Gerhardus on the resurrection of the dead §. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

APERIAM TUMULOS VESTROS] Faciam vobis quasi tumulos aperiri ; vitam civilem vobis reddam.

Triplex sensus hujus Pericopes traditur penes Hieronymum. Nonnulli eandem de resurrectione universali explicant: quam sententiam ita expo- suit Hieronymus: Qui putant de resurrectione, quæ ab omnibus, & Judæis & Christianis creditur, Dei esse sermonem, hæc solent dicere : Facta est super Pro- phetam manus Domini, hoc est, Dominus atq; Sal- vator, per quem Pater cuncta operatus est: Omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt, & sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est. Et eduxit me, inquit, in spiritu Domini, subauditur manus Domini. Edu- xit autem eum in Spiritu, non in corpore, sed extra corpus: & posuit illum sive dimisit in medio campi, qui plenus erat humanis ossibus : nec eum est passa requiescere : Sed fecit ossa omnia circumire, quæ non erant operta humo, sed super campum jacen- tia : nec solum multa, sed multa nimis, & propter temporis vetustatem arida, siccaque vehementer, & nihil in se humoris habentia. Cumq; interrogasset eum sermo divinus, utrum existimaret hæc ossa posse vivere, respondit; Domine Deus, tu nosti, qui ple- nam habes scientiam futurorum. Dixitq; ad eum Dominus : Vaticinare de ossibus, sive super ossa hæc : & dices ad ea : Ossa arida audite verbum Do- mini. In quo mirandum, quomodo ad ossa arida locu- tus sit, quæ ante nervos, carnes, & cutem, & spiritum vivificantem, Dei possent audire sermonem. Pri- mumque ossa cum aliis ossibus nervorum vinculis colligantur, deinde implentur carnibus, & desuper ob pulchritudinem extenditur cutis, quæ nudaram carnium operiat fœditatem, & tunc accipiunt Spi- ritum, qui vivere ea faciat, & postquam vixerint, tunc cognoscant, quod ipse sit Dominus. Dicente itaq; Propheta, quod ei fuerat imperatum, statim facta commotio, ossaque in suam sunt applicata compagem : Astricta nervis, plena carnibus, pelle cooperta : jacebantque humana corpora spiritum non habentia. Idcirco Propheta vaticinatur ad Spiri- tum, & ait : Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: A qua- tuor ventis veniSpiritus : à quatuor videlicet mun di plagis, ut quomodo in prima conditione hominis in- sufflavit Deus in faciem ejus, & factus est in animam viventem : sic & secunda conditio, id est, resurrectio mortuorum, insufflante Spiritu vivificetur. Qui in- gressus est humana corpora, statimque vixerunt, steteruntq; super pedes suos. Unde & resurrectio di- citur mortuorum congregatio, sive Ecclesia multa, & uti in Hebræo habetur, grandis exercitus: eog; completur tempore : Emitte Spiritum tuum, & crea- buntur, & renovabis faciem terræ. Hæc de prima explicatione Hieronymus. Quæ sententia Tertul- liani fuit de resurrectione carn. cap. 30. ubi dispu- tat, magis religiosum esse si credatur agere Prophetam de resurrectione, prout litera sonat, quam si allegorice explicetur ; quia religio ipsi fuit à literali sensu dis- cedere. Sed magis, inquit, religiosum est veritatem de suæ auctoritate simplicitatis defendi, quam sensus divinæ propositionis expostulat. Si enim ad res Iu- daicas spectaret hæc visio, statim revelato situ ossium subjecisset: Ossa ista omnis Domus Israël est &c. At cum ostensis ossibus, de propria spe eorum, qui ob- loquitur, nondum nominato Israële, & fidem tentat Prophetæ: Fili hominis, si vivent ossa hæc, ut & ille responderet, Domine, tu scis, non utiq; Deus Pro- phetæ fidem de ea re tentasset, quæ futura non esset, quam nunquam Israël audisset, quam credi non opor- teret: &c.

Altera interpretatio, quod hic exhibeatur in vi- sione ista Prophetæ restitutio populi corporalis è Se- pulchris captivitatis & vinculis, quibus servitute Ba- bylonica tenebantur adstricti, quam sub Zoroba- bele expletam dicunt Judæi, quando magna est facta commotio, & regnum Chaldæorum in Medos, Per- sasq; translatum. Quamvis alii eam demum adhuc sperent in præsentia Christi sui, quem putant esse ven- turum, ut observat hic Hieronymus. Istis se adjun- git Grotius de corporali liberatione è captivitate Babylonica in solidum explicans. Tertia Hieronymi ipsius est expositio. Qui non negat quidem cepisse etiam impleri ea in fidelibus sub Zorobabele, colle- cta iterum Ecclesia Israëlitica, sed complementum refert ad tempora N. Testamenti. Nos autem, inquit, spiritualiter post crucem Domini Salvatoris completa memoramus, & quotidie fieri in his, vel maxime, qui instar Lazari peccatorum suorum fasciis colligati, ad vocem Domini suscitantur: & vere sunt Domus Israël, arens quondam, & nullam spem habens sa- lutis: sed intrante in se Spiritu gratiæ, & porrigente Domino manum de profundo inferi liberantur.

Nostra sentenia est, à Domino in hac illustri vi- sione exhibitam fuisse Prophetæ resurrectionem mor- tuorum, sed occasionem, causam, scopum hujus vi- sionis fuisse restitutionem populi Israëlitici: non tam in politiæ formam pristinam, quam ad restauran- dam Hierarchiam Ecclesiasticam, cultumq; divinum vicissim erigendum, quæ sub Zorobabele quidem ex parte restaurata, sed imprimis tempore adventus Christi ad perfectionem perductu. Jam quod resur- rectio mortuorum hac visione repræsentata fuerit, hæc confirmant. Primo, quod τὸ ῥητὸν clare ipsam mortuorum resurrectionem inferat, quæ nuspiam fere tam luculenter & per partes exposita est, quam hac visione, ut ex Hieronymo eam antea adduximus. Ab hac autem literali sententia discedere merito nobis religio esse debet. Qui relicto plane τῷ ῥητῷ cum Grotio meram allegoriam sectantur, quod etiam ab hæreticis factum resurrectionem carnis neganti- bus, à temeritate absolvi non possunt, nec satis re- ligiese sermonem tractant, judicio Tertulliani. Hanc prædicationem, inquit c. 30. de resurrect. carn. scio qualiter concutiant in allegoriæ argumentatio- nem: quia dicendo, ossa ista omnis Domus Israël est, in imaginem ea fecerit Israël, & à propria conditione transtulerit: atq; ita figuratam esse, non veram resur- rectionis prædicationem. Statum enim Judæorum de- formari, quodammodo emortuum & exaridum & di- sfersum in campo orbis. Itaq; & imaginem resurre- ctionis in illum allegorizari, quia recolligi habeat, & recompingi os ad os, i. e. tribus ad tribum, & popu- lus ad populum, & reincorporari carnibus facultatum, & nervis regni: atq; ita de sepulchris, i. e. de habita- culis captivitatis tristissimis atq; teterrimis educi, & refrigerii nomine respirare, & vivere exinde in ter- ra sua Iudæa. Et quid post hæc? morientur sine dubio. Et quid post mortem? Nulla opinor resuscitatio, si non hæc erit ipsa, quæ Ezechieli revelatur. Sed enim & alias prædicatur resurrectio; etgo & hæc erit: Ste- mere in statum eam Iudaicarum rerum convertunt.

Deinde non congruit sensui Grotiano de sola reductione e captivitatis tumulis illa Spiritus a quatuor mundi ventis vocatio. Quia e Babylone solum, non e quatuor ventis mundi collecti sunt Judæi, sunt Zorobabel. Quod argumentum etiam movisse videtur Hieronymum, quo minus admit- teret, plene completum vaticinium fuisse isto tem- pore. At in universali resurrectione à quatuor mundi ventis, à summis cœlorum usque ad termi- nos eorum colligentur omnes Matth. 24, 31. Marc. 13, 27. Adde quod exercitus grandis nimis valde re- suscitatus visus Ezechieli sit. Reductus autem per Zorobabelem non adeo grandis fuerit exercitus. Theodoretus ad v. 9. docet nos, inquit, hæc oratio, quam facilia omnia divinæ sint potestati, omniaque in manu ejus esse: in manu enim ejus anima, inquit, o- mnium viventium. Idcirco Prophetæ præcipit, ut jubeat omnes animas, ubicunque sint, redire, & sua rursus cor- pora habitare. Renunciatà, inquit, à me divino præcepto, revixerunt ossa devincta, & resurrectio- nem consecuta, neque exigua erat eorum, qui re- surrexère, multitudo.

Tertio cum propositum Prophetæ fuerit, fi- deles sub captivitate erigere, & consolari, magis certe ad consolationem ejus fecit confirmatio fi- dei, desumta à resurrectione fidei, quæ ab omnibus fidelibus indubitato sperari potuit, quam promis- sio aliquando post decursum LXX. annorum ca- ptivitatis futuræ liberationis, quam multi fidelium non attingerunt, morte prærepti, quæque solidum solatium minime præbebat: quum non minus calamitatibus variis expositi fuerint in politia, quam in exilio.

Quarto nimis jejuna est Grotiana glossa, po- pulum politia destitutum, vel homines captivos dici ossa, Spiritum immissum nihil aliud notare, quam libertatis & status restitutionem. Sonitum, quem factum audivit Propheta, esse Cyri edictum. (Quum potius testetur Propheta commotionem factam ex eo esse, quod ossa ad ossa accesserint,) a- pertionem tumulorum nihil aliud esse, quam reddi- tionem vitæ Civilis. Quæ uti temere sine ratione af- feruntur, ita eadem facilitate rejiciuntur.

Quinto ex adverso congruunt omnia egre- gie resurrectioni mortuorum, prout etiam alias in sacris descripta est. Ossa arida spiritu destituta cada- vera sunt defunctorum. Audiunt Verbum Domini, cujus vocem audituri dicuntur, qui dormiunt in monumentis suis Joh. 5. Intromittitur in illa Spiri- tus, cum animantur corpora. Quia hoc futurum in resurrectione. Dat Dominus super ipsos nervos, & succrescere facit carnes, & super extendit cutem. Quæ non conveniunt aptius ulli Dei operi, quam resurrectioni mortuorum. Conf. Job. 19, 25.

Sexto non reclamat contextus. Nihil enim in- terpretationi huic obstant, quæ sequuntur v. 11. Fili hominis, ossa hæc universa Domus Israël est: ipsi di- cunt, aruerunt ossa nostra, & periit spes nostra, & ab- scissi sumus. Propterea vaticinare, & dices ad eos: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Ecce, ego aperiam tumu- los vestros, & educam vos è sepulchris vestris, populus meus, & inducam vos in terram Israël. Veteres, quos adduxit Hieronymus, quomodo ea conciliare vo- luerint, ipse exposuit: Quod autem sequitur: Et di- xit ad me, Fili hominis, ossa hæc universa est domus Israël: videtur facere quæstionem: eo quod non de ge- nerali resurrectione sed propriè de resurrectione dica- tur domus Israël, quæ dicat: Aruerunt ossa nostra, & periit spes nostra, & abscissi sumus à terra nostra, sive omnino desperavimus: quibus ista dicentibus, tertio Ezechiel prophetare compellitur, & dicere os- sibus aridis: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Ego ape- riam tumulos vestros. In quo quæritur: Si aperiat tumulos, quomodo supra dixerit: Erant autem mul- ta valde super faciem campi, siccaq; vehementer. Et educam, inquit, vos de sepulchris vestris populus meus, secundum illud, quod scriptum est in Evangelio: Venit hora, quando qui in sepulchris sunt, audient vocem Filii Dei, & exibunt, qui bona egerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ. Et iterum: qui audierint, vivent. Et si, sicut nonnulli arbitrantur, de gene- rali resurrectione dicit sermo divinus, quid necesse fuit specialiter dici: Et inducam vos in terram Israël: Cum in omni orbe terrarum resurgere debeant mortui ex his locis, in quibus sepulti sunt. Cumque, ait, e- duxero vos de tumulis vestris, & dedero Spiritum meum in vobis, & vixeritis, tunc requiescere vos faciam super humum vestram, ut postquam requie- veritis in terra Israël, tunc cognoscatis, quod ipse sim Dominus, qui promissa opere compleverim. Qui ergo de generali resurrectione hæc dicta intelli- gunt, illud quod videtur facere quæstionem: Ossa hæc universa Domus est Israël: ad Sanctorum resurre- ctionem referunt, de qua & Apostolus Johannes in Apocalypsi loquitur: Beatus & Sanctus, qui habet partem in resurrectione prima, super eum secunda mors non habet potestatem; quod videlicet alia san- ctorum, alia peccatorum sit resurrectio. Unde & in Psalmo primo dicitur: Non resurgent impii in ju- dicio. Neq; peccatores in consilio justorum. Ter- ram autem Israel, quam resurgentibus Dominus pol- licetur, illam esse confirmant, de qua scriptum est: Beati mites: quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram: Et: Placebo Domino in regione viventium. Hæc lo- quuntur, qui de generali, ut diximus, resurrectio- ne Ezechielem scripsisse autumant. Alii admittunt hac visione intendi restitutionem Israëliticam, sed ita ut comparatio instituatur cum mortuorum re- surrectione, adeoq; hæc tanquam certa supponan- tur. Quo pacto assumit κατ' ἄνθρωπον Tertull. eam sententiam: Deniq; hoc ipso, inquit, quod recidi- vatus Judaici status de recorpordtione, & readunitio- ne ossium figuratur, id quoq; eventurum ossibus proba- tur. Non enim posset de ossibus figura componi, sinon idipsum & ossibus eventurum esset. Nam et si figmentum veritatis in imagine est, imago ipsa in veritate est sui, ne- cesse est esse prius sibi, quo alii configurentur. De vacuo similitudo non competit: de nullo parabola non conve- nit. Ita quoq; oportebit ossium quoq; credi reviviscan- tionem & respirationem, qualis dicitur, de qua possit exprimi Judaicarum rerum reformatio, qualis affin- gitur. Hieronymus vero probat hanc sententiam, adeoque vult, per resurrectionis parabolam de resti- tutione Israel prophetari, qui eo tempore captivus erat in Babylone: Sed addit, qua ratione inde ad- strui adhuc possit resurrectio. Nunquam poneretur, inquit, similitudo resurrectionis ad restitutionem Is- raëlitici populi significandam, nisi staret ipsa resurre- ctio, & futura crederetur: quia nemo de rebus non extantibus incerta confirmat. Quia vero adhuc ita quæstio superest, an hæc de ossium vivificatione con- cio exhibeat mortuorum resurrectionem, an vero unice de restitutione Israëlitici populi hac visione figurata intelligi debeat? dicendum omnino est, resurre- ctionem mortuorum, non ut alibi saltem tradi- tam, & penes populum creditam assumi, ad stabi- liendam populi restitutionem, sed ipsa illa visione directe ostensam & exhibitam fuisse: Addita ta- men exhibitionis hujus causa, quam subjuncta o- ratio explicat vers. 11. Quod nempe ideo repræ- sentata fuerit mortuorum resuscitatio, quod Deus hanc repræsentationem voluerit adhibitam, in fi- guram & confirmationem restitutionis populi. Non solum, ut possibilitatem ostenderet, quod quia of- sa-revera arida, & Spiritus vitalis prorsus expertia possint vitam & spiritum recuperare, multo magis illi, qui κατ᾽ ἀναλογίαν sunt ossa arida, & velut in sepulcris hærent, vitam & libertatem recipere possint. Sed etiam, ut ea ratione conditionem ac statum tùm præsentem, tum deinceps sequuturum per quandam ὑποτύπωσιν adumbraret, quod veluti è mortuis excitandi sint, cum restituetur politia Ecclesiastica & cultus publicus instaurabitur. Quam Prophetæ intentionem ac mentem non dif- fitetur Hieronymus: Imo tota nostra illo, inquit, tendit assertio, quomodo videtur incredulum, quod of- fibus aridis & multa vetustate confectis futura resur- rectio promittatur, & tamen futurum est, quod promittitur, sic & restitutio populi Israël, qui ductus est in captivitatem, & in toto orbe dispersus, vide- tur quidem incredibilis his, qui Dei non norunt po- tentiam, sed tamen futura est : quia ego, inquit Dominus, locutus sum: & faciam sicut pollicitus sum. Similia habentur apud Epiphanium lib. 2. Tom. 2. hæref. ult. Quod corpus per seipsum ante se statue- re possit Deus, per Ezechielem declaratum est, etsi per parabolam res ea facta sit: At species ipsa ad allego- riam veritatis tunc impleta perfecta est. Quod con- gregandum est os ad os, harmonia ad harmoniam, & cum ossa sicca essent, & nondum anima, neq; Spiritus moyens in ipsis esset statim coacta sunt corpora, & jux- ta Prophetæ verba solidata. Utrumque scopum hu- jus visionis docet etiam Justin. qq. & Resp. ad Orth. quæst. 45. quod nempe primo quidem resur- rectio mortuorum sed ea hac fini adumbrata fuerit, ut non tantum consolationem arriperent inde, sed confir- marentur simul etiam de futura sui restitutione. Cæte- rum apud Ezechielem, inquit, omnia visio fuere, & of- sa, & horum resurrectio. Exhibita autem sancto Vati à Deo ista visio est, præcipue quidem, ut per eam indi- caretur futura per Christum universalis omnium in to- to mundo mortuorum resuscitatio: deinde vero propter Israëlitarum consolationem, qui & eam, in qua de- tinebantur, servitutem, de liberatione ex Babylonio- rum dominatu, spem sibi ipsis desperatione præciderant. Nam sicuti defuncta corpora, in monumentis sita, spem resuscitationis non habent: sic illi se Babylone esse re- bantur, absq; spe reditus & restitutionis. Declarat hoc Propheta ipse, cum dicit: Et factus est sermo Domi- ni ad me, dicens: Fili hominis, ossa hæc universa, domus Israël est. Ipsi dicunt; Exaruerunt nostra ossa, periit spes nostra, & quæ sequuntur. Ita opus non est, ut cum Cornelio à Lapide, aliisq; Papistis varios sensus hic fingamus eorundem verborum; qui valde tricofi, & perplexi in hoc loco sunt. Cor- nelius à Lapide modo Grammatice dicit, quasi in cortice literæ significari resurrectionem mortuorum, & sub hac quasi parabola liberationem Judæorum è captivitate; modo rursus sub typo liberationis PRO- PRIE ET AD LITERAM intelligi vult peccato- rum, qui quasi ossa arida sine spiritu & gratia in peccato captivi tenentur, resuscitationem, per affla- tum Spiritus & gratiæ Christi; adeoque geminat hic quasi Parabolam, & geminum sensum literalem ef- se vult. Sed confunditur ita diversa oratio. Nam in priori usq; ad versum 10. de resurrectione mortuorum secundum literam agitur: atque istius orationis unicus ille sensus est. Sed ne lateret Prophetam causa proxima; cur Deus ipsi hanc exhibere volue- rit resuscitationem mortuorum, subsequitur altera oratio v. 11. seq. in qua non verba explicantur prio- ris orationis aut Ἀπόδοσις redditur parabolæ, sed sco pus istius præcedaneæ visionis exhibetur, per ἀνα- λογίαν, quam restitutio habet cum corporali resusci- tatione. Sic explicat Theodorecus in h. l. consenta- neas rebus accipit revelationes: cum enim propter per- fidiam, cujus morbo laborabant, meliora desperassent Judæi illi, qui ex Judæa captivi abducti fuerant, suam ipsis auctor omnium rerum Deus potentiam ostendit, & longe difficiliorem illa in pristinum statum ipsorum re- stitutione, mortuorum corporum resurrectionem indi- cat Prophetæ: per quem omnem populum docet, o- mnia sibi esse facilia volenti. Judæos igitur & alios Israelitas per hunc docuit: facillimum esse volenti Deo in servitutem redactos in pristinam libertatem vindi- care; nobis autem & omnibus omnino, qui præconium Evangelicum cum fide excepimus, resurrectionis corpo- rum nostrorum ostendit facilitatem, divinoque verbo ac nutui rerum obsequi Naturam. Et ad v. 11. Si id quod vobis multo difficilius videtur, admodum facile à me fieri posse ostendi, sane perspicuum est, hoc i- tem me facillime ac nullo negotio facturum, qui vos è captivitatis vinculis veluti è quibusdam sepulchris eductos in propriam patriam reducam. Neque dif- fitentur sane Judæi de resurrectione mortuorum hic sermonem esse. R. Simai dictum in eam senten- tiam adduxit Gal. lib. 12. c. 2. R. Menasse Ben Israel o- mni exceptione superius hoc testimonium facit, & veteres eam in sententiam laudat Judæos lib. 1. de resurrectione Mortuorum c. 11. pag. 22. Textus hic, inquit, expressus, & omni exceptione major est pro resurrectione mortuorum. Nec refert, quod super hoc loco Rabbini Talmudici disputent, sitne figurate, an vero proprie secundum literam intelligendum, id quod ab Ezechiele dicitur futurum, ut defunctos in vitam revocet? Utut enim sit, certum est Deum ista Vi- sione indicare voluisse Ezechieli, futuram aliquando resurrectionem mortuorum. Idcirco in antiquis di- citur in Pirque R. Eliezer: Consistebant Israelitæ, plorabantq́; dicentes: Speravimus lucem & ecce te- nebræ. Tum alloquutus est Dominus Prophetam & ait, vivit Dominus, si vos non resuscitem, cum mortui resurgent, & cum Israele recolligam: Quod idem est atq́; illud: Aperiam vestra sepulchra. Liquet igitur, credidisse illos, in ista Prophetia repræsentatam fuisse resurrectionem mortuorum. Conferantur quæ in Sotinismo profligato diximus pag. 1067. & quæ B. Gerhardus de resurrectione mortuorum §. 13.

## 37:16
Vers. 16. TAKE THEE ONE STICK] A tablet, as the Chaldean here. OF JUDAH AND OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HIS COMPANIONS] that is, and of Benjamin. UPON IT FOR JOSEPH] That is, upon the tablet dedicated to the descendants of Joseph. EPHRAIM] Because the kingdom was in that tribe. AND ALL THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL] The other tribes. AND HIS COMPANIONS] Write his companions, by way of explanation of the preceding: for the rest of the house of Israel were companions to Ephraim in the same way that Benjamin was a companion to Judah.

Latin:

Vers. 16. SUME TIBI LIGNUM UNUM] Tabellam, ut hic Chaldæus. JUDÆ ET FILIORUM ISRAEL SOCIORUM EJUS] id est, & Benjaminis. SUPER ILLUD JOSEPH] Id est, super tabellam Josephi posteris dicatam. EPHRAIM] Quia in ea tribu regnum fuit. ET CUNCTÆ DOMUS ISRAEL] Tribubus aliis. SOCIORUMQUE EJUS] Scribe sociorum ejus, per ἐξήγησιν præcedentis: nam reliqua domus Israel ita socit erant Ephraimo, quomodo Benjamin Judæ erat socius.

## 37:19
Vers. 19. BEHOLD I WILL TAKE THE STICK OF JOSEPH, WHICH IS IN THE HAND OF EPHRAIM, AND THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL, WHICH ARE JOINED UNTO HIM, AND WILL PUT THEM TOGETHER WITH THE STICK OF JUDAH, AND WILL MAKE THEM ONE STICK] That which was in the hand of Ephraim, that is, which part was ruled by the descendants of Ephraim. This prophecy would have had its full effect in those tribes if they had seriously converted themselves to God: now because few did so, it profited few. See what we shall say at chapter 49, 15. Ezekiel himself said that a tacit condition underlies all the promises and threats of God, 37, 13: and Jerem. 18, 9. AND THEY SHALL BE ONE IN HIS HAND] In the Hebrew: In my hand: under my protection. Thus the Chaldean.

He rashly makes this prophecy conditional. For there is nothing in the text which teaches that what has been predicted absolutely is to be understood as conditional. Nor is it true that ALL promises have a tacit condition. For absolute promises are also given, such as that concerning the manifestation of the Messiah, concerning the New Testament, etc. Nor are all threats, which are read in the Prophets, ditional. Such as those were concerning the extermination of the Canaanites, concerning the Babylonian captivity, in which it must by no means be said that a tacit condition lay hidden. That a condition underlies certain promises and threats, the passages of Ezekiel and Jeremiah testify; that it is to be understood in all and always, they do not testify. Wherefore, since this prophecy concerning the kingdoms of Judah and Israel being joined into one has never been fulfilled in the Jews and Israelites according to the flesh, it must necessarily be understood of the Jews and Israelites according to the Spirit. Just as those things which are added concerning the ONE KING of all openly do not treat of any earthly king, but of a spiritual king, of the Messiah: so these things also are to be accepted not of an earthly kingdom, but of a spiritual kingdom.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ECCE EGO ASSUMAM LIGNUM JOSEPH, QUOD EST IN MANU EPHRAIM, ET TRIBUS IS- RAEL, QUÆ SUNT EI ADJUNCTÆ, ET DABO EAS PARITER CUM LIGNO JUDA, ET FACIAM EAS IN LIGNUM VNUM] Quod fuit in manu Ephraim, id est, quæ pars regnata fuit ab Ephraimi posteris. Hæc Prophetia plenum in illis tribubus effectum habuisset, si illæ ad Deum serio se convertissent: nunc quia pauci id fecere, paucis profuit. Vide, quæ dicemus ad caput 49, 15. In omnibus promissis & minis Dei tacitam subesse condi- tionem ipse dixit Ezechiel 37, 13: & Jerem. 18, 9. ET ERUNT VNUM IN MANU EJUS] In He- bræo: In manu mea: sub mea tutela. Sic Chaldæus.

Temere hanc Prophetiam facit conditionatam. Nihil enim in textu est, quod doceat, quæ absolute prædicta sunt, sub conditione intelligenda esse. Neq; verum est, OMNES promissiones tacitam habere conditionem. Nam dantur etiam abso- lutæ promissiones, qualis erat illa de Messia exhi- bendo, de Novo Testamento &c. Nec omnes comminationes, quæ in Prophetis leguntur, con- ditionatæ sunt. Quales erant de Canaanæis ex- terminandis, de captivitate Babylonica, in quibus tacitam conditionem latitasse, minime dicendum. In quibusdam promissionibus & minis subesse con- ditionem loca Ezechielis & Jeremiæ testantur, in omnibus & semper subaudiendam esse, non testan- tur. Quâpropter cum hæc Prophetia, de regnis Juda & Israel in unum colligandis, nunquam imple- ta sit in Judæis, & Israëlitis secundum carnem, in- telligenda ea necessario est de Judæis & Israëlitis secundum Spiritum. Quemadmodum ea, quæ de REGE omnium UNO adduntur, palam non de re- ge aliquo terreno agunt, sed de rege spirituali, de Messia: ita hæc etiam non de regno terreno, sed de regno spirituali accipienda.

## 37:22
Verse 22.

AND ONE KING SHALL BE RULING OVER ALL] Zerubbabel, of whom above 34, 23. For he, although he did not assume the royal name out of reverence for the Persian empire, was nevertheless held by his own people as king.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET REX UNUS ERIT OMNIBUS IMPERANS] Zorobabel, de quo supra 34, 23. Is enim, quanquam regium nomen ob reverentiam Persici imperii non assum- sit, à suis tamen pro rege habitus fuit.

## 37:23
Verse 23. NEITHER SHALL THEY BE POLLUTED ANY MORE WITH THEIR IDOLS] Above 36, 27.

AND I WILL CLEANSE THEM] I will take away the punishments, as above 36, 33.

Latin:

Vers. 23. NEQUE POLLUENTUR ULTRA IN I- DOLIS SUIS] Supra 36, 27.

ET EMUNDABO EOS] Pœnas auferam, ut su- pra 36, 33.

## 37:24
Verse 24. AND MY SERVANT DAVID KING OVER THEM] Thus Zerubbabel is called, because he was of the blood of David, and an imitator of his virtues. See above 34, 34.

The illustrious prophecy concerning the kingdom of Christ is again perverted, and those things which were predicted concerning the Messiah as the one King of all Israel are twisted toward Zerubbabel. Which, however, is not to be conceded, since in the first place the kingdom of Ephraim had to coalesce with the kingdom of Judah into one body, I WILL MAKE THEM (the tribes) INTO ONE STICK. That, however, was never fulfilled in the bodily kingdom of Ephraim and Judah, much less under Zerubbabel: but in the kingdom of Christ; under whom both Israelites and Jews coalesced into one mystical body. It is to be observed, however, primarily, that mention is made not only of the tribe of Judah and the sons of Israel his companions, by whom are understood those who in the first schism under Rehoboam 1 Kings 12 followed the parts of Judah, along with the tribe of Benjamin, and Levi, such as were some from all the tribes, then those who from the tribe of Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon, betook themselves to Asa the grandson of Solomon; See 2. Chronicles 11, 16. et seqq. chapter 15, 8. et seqq. as well as those who under Hezekiah came from the tribes of Asher, Manasseh, Zebulun, and Issachar 2 Chronicles 30, 5. 11. 18. chapter 31, 1. Compare Josephus book 8 of Antiquities, chapter 3. But that also the whole house of Israel, and his companions are commemorated v. 16. The entire tribes of Israel, because they had to coalesce into one with the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, namely into one ecclesiastical city. To whom indeed it is to be referred that they are Israelites according to the Spirit, who are to be thought of as being restored to favor not by respect of nation, but of faith, is gathered from Hosea 3, 4. 5. Jeremiah 3, 18. Romans 9, 5. 6. For the entire tribes of Israel were never restored into one polity and Republic with the Jews, because the ten tribes are openly said to have remained in perpetual captivity 2 Kings 17, 23. 41. and to that extent only the Jewish tribe with its adherents is said to have been brought back here and there: concerning which also Josephus book 11 of Antiquities, chapter 5. Only two tribes, he says, dwell under the Roman Empire throughout Asia and Europe. The ten tribes are now also beyond the Euphrates, infinite thousands of men. Which it is hardly possible to comprehend by number. Cyrus certainly permitted to all Israelites who were under his empire the power of returning, as did Artaxerxes, as their own documents testify Ezra 1. 2. 3. 4. as also v. 12. 13. and those who were dismissed and returned are called by the common name of Israel Ezra 1, 5. chapter 2, 3. 59. 70. chapter 6, 21. chapter 10, 1. and mention of all Israel is made chapter 2, 70. chapter 10, 5. Nehemiah 7, 20. chapter 12, 47. and Ezra transmitted a copy of the documents of liberty promulgated by Cyrus to the Israelites staying in Media, as Josephus testifies book 11, chapter 5. Ezra summoned Levites from Caspia Ezra 8, 15. nor is there doubt that others also could have returned from there, indeed when 12 rams were offered for sacrifices, according to the number of the 12 tribes of Israel Ezra 8, 35. it seems not obscure that some from all the tribes had returned: Furthermore, since Scripture assigns in this a distinction of the two tribes and the ten tribes, or of the Jews and the Israelites, that the Jews were indeed to be brought back, but not likewise the Israelites; and openly testifies that the Israelites remained perpetually in Media, and were cast out from the face of the Lord, just as He had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets 2 Kings 17, 21. et seqq. and the entire tribes of Israel never returned, just as this prophecy makes mention of the tribes: it does not appear how it can be said that this prophecy had its full complement in the reduction and bodily return of the tribes of Israel and Judah, which never again coalesced into one kingdom, just as before the division under Solomon all 12 tribes constituted one kingdom and one polity. Wherefore, however much it may be admitted that by such prophecies that benefit of the liberty of returning to the fatherland was to be opened to all, and that many from all the tribes would eventually return to restore the assembly of the people of God in the land of Canaan; yet the sense of prophecies of this kind, which imply something more, is not exhausted; namely, that it was integral for all Israelites to be aggregated to the people of God, and that they were all called not so much by the edict of Cyrus as by the universal proclamation of the Gospel, by which liberty and power of collection to the Church was made for all, and all throughout the whole world were called to the people of God, whom He had led back from the Babylonian captivity, in the New Testament, after Christ Himself had presented Himself to this people, and had gathered the same through the word, who also died for the Jewish nation, nay, not for that nation only, but that He might gather together in one the children of God who were scattered, John 11:52. The sum is: it is treated here of the convocation to the Church, not of the collection to the Polity; of the unity of the Mystical body, not of civil unity: of unity under the heavenly King Messiah, not under an earthly one. Which convocation began in the time of Cyrus, but is completed in the time of the New Testament up to the consummation of the age, in which God extended His hand first to the Israelites, as the chosen people of God, to whom God once revealed His word, and willed them to be recalled to their native land for the sake of restoring public worship and the Ecclesiastical assembly, who did not fly together in a small number in the time of Cyrus, and more of them were aggregated in the succession of time, when Christ the promised Messiah and Savior of the world, at His coming, preached αὐτοπροσώπως (in person) to all the tribes in the land of Israel, and restored the Church from all the tribes; then indeed, through the Apostles, He took care that the universal nations be aggregated to the Israelite Church, the middle wall of partition being broken down, and made one body out of all, these also being reckoned for Israelites who were aggregated to the same, and were grafted into the good olive tree, even if cut out from the natural wild olive, Rom. 11:24. Rightly, therefore, the blessed Chytreus in his Commentary on the Apocalypse in German, ch. 20, observes that there are three degrees of the restoration of the Israelite people, of which Ezekiel and other Prophets speak: The first under Cyrus and Darius, when, having been led back into Judea, they rebuilt their city and temple. The second, which was made through Christ the King and Shepherd of the sheep of Israel dispersed everywhere throughout the world, who propagates Mount Zion and the kingdom of David to the whole world, and through the proclamation of the Gospel erects a new and eternal city and Church, and a new and eternal justice; which will be completed and consummated in the third perfect restoration of Israel in the new and heavenly Jerusalem after the resurrection. Therefore, according to Chytraeus, the Prophet promises to the Jews captive in Babylon and dispersed throughout the world a return to Judea and the restoration of the city and the temple so that the restoration of the temple ought not to be excluded from this prophecy, nor should that alone exhaust its Majesty, but primarily the august kingdom of Christ should be intended.

Nor indeed is the refuge of the Judaizing Grotius to be admitted again, that this prophecy was only conditional, made under the hypothesis of a serious conversion: For with equal ease the Jews will also say that the promise concerning the Messiah is conditional, and that the condition not being fulfilled, even what was promised is not fulfilled. Thus cold water is poured upon the blinded Jews. We do not deny that a tacit condition underlies some promises, but that a condition is to be understood in all, is by no means to be conceded.

Furthermore (2) the children of Israel are said to be gathered not from a certain land but from the whole world: v. 21. Behold I will take the children of Israel from the midst of the nations, to which they have gone, and I will gather them from every side, and I will bring them to their own land. Since this has never been fulfilled, at least as far as all the Israelites from the midst of any nations, gathered from every side into one political body, it must necessarily be understood concerning the convocation and collection to the Church.

Thirdly, when God promises that He will make one nation in the land on the mountains of Israel, if this is to be accepted concerning political unity in one Republic or one kingdom, let the Jews, and their advocate Grotius, and those who wish to defend his side, show where all the Israelites have been gathered into one body, into one political nation on the mountains of Israel. Therefore, it is necessary to understand this concerning the mystical unity of the Israelites, who have been called from all nations to the Church, as well as those who, according to the promise, are reckoned as Israelites, and thus are called Israel according to the Spirit, of whom all there is one heart and one soul, Acts 4:15. Compare Isa. 11:6 seqq. Gal. 3:28. Eph. 2:14. Col. 3:11. There will not be, he says, two nations any longer, nor will they be divided anymore into two kingdoms. That certainly has never been fulfilled in the Israelites according to the flesh and the Jews, that they were so joined into one kingdom, and into one nation, as regards political government. Therefore they are said to be one IN THE HAND of the Lord, as it is held in the Hebrew, because Christ took away the emulation and contention between the Jews and the Samaritans, and joined both to Himself and to God in the Church, John 4:21. Concerning which Jerome says: truly at the advent of the Savior two rods, and as it is placed in the Hebrew, two sticks were joined into one scepter, and in the Baptism of Christ those long separated are associated: so that they may become one new man: and one nation: nor be polluted any longer by idols and abominations: But by the washing of the world they may be the people of God: and Christ may rule over them: and they may dwell upon the land of the meek, the land of the living, which He had given to His servant Jacob: who supplanted the people of Israel in his mother's womb. He also adds an explanation of others, which I am pleased to subjoin: But if we wish, according to the prophecy of Hosea, which is almost entirely directed to the ten tribes, that is, to Joseph and Ephraim, and Samaria and Israel, to understand the knowledge falsely so called, and the diverse mobs of heretics: we will say this, that in the last time, when the fullness of the nations shall have entered in, and all Israel shall have been saved: then also the adversaries of the people, who fought against the house of Judah and the confession of the Church, shall surrender themselves to the Ecclesiastical faith: and having abandoned all errors and the princes of this world, who are being destroyed: and their Patriarchs, who led them into the abyss of blasphemies: they shall rise up and leave their idols, and the abominations, which they had fashioned from their own heart: and from all their seats, in which they sinned, they shall pass over to the Ecclesiastical faith and be cleansed, and be the people of Christ, and He Himself shall be their God.

Therefore by the Mountains of Israel, the mountains of the Church, by a Prophetic phrase, are understood. Because the mountains of Israel could neither contain all, nor did all return to them.

Fourthly, whenever justification and liberation from all abominations is promised, and there is talk of such a king, government, and kingdom, under which, and in which the subjects are to be spiritually cleansed, it is manifest that it is about a spiritual, not a terrestrial, kingdom and king. For there is no people under the earth, no kingdom, that is entirely so holy and pious perpetually from idols and abominations and iniquities, as is promised here: Nor shall they be polluted ANY LONGER by their idols, and their abominations and all their iniquities, and I will make them safe from all their dwelling places, in which they have sinned, and I will CLEANSE them, and they shall be my people, and I will be their GOD. It is manifest that these things are to be understood concerning the Church, which God purifies and sanctifies for Himself, and the kingdom of Christ.

Fifthly: Like people, like King: Therefore a terrestrial King is not promised, but the Messiah King established by God on mount Zion Ps. 2:6. That Righteous Branch of David, under whom Judah and Israel dwell confidently Jer. 23:6. c. 33:16. To whom the name David is attributed, because He drew His origin from David, and occupied the throne of David, and David was His notable type. Therefore Theodoret: David, however, calls Christ Lord, as arising from David according to the flesh: but servant on account of His human nature. For when He was in the form of God, He took the form of a servant; the Prophetic speech therefore teaches that impiety will be extinguished, and the error of worshipping idols, and the division of kingdoms will at last be terminated by one empire, under which those living, who are also signified by one shepherd, will acknowledge both their Lord and God. These things Theodoret. Concerning which we spoke at Ezek. 34.

Sixth, one King of all who are to be gathered from all nations is appointed, one Shepherd of those sheep; which cannot be understood of Zerubbabel, who neither shone with royal dignity, nor ruled over all the Israelite tribes; nay, since the office of this King is described here by the remission of sins and sanctification, it is manifest that it applies to no earthly King, as Theodoret rightly noted. The discourse is about such a King, under whom all are to walk in justice, and all subjects are to be holy. And my servant David shall be King over them and one shepherd of them all: they shall walk in my judgments and keep my commandments and do them. This, indeed, happened in no earthly King, but is proper to the kingdom of Christ, the Church of God, which is the communion of saints.

Seventh, it is treated here of a perpetual and everlasting King, who, namely, is to reign forever, whose kingdom shall have no end. And they shall dwell upon it, both they and their children, and their children's children FOREVER, and David my servant shall be their prince FOREVER. This, indeed, in no way suits Zerubbabel. For is he the perpetual King of Israel? But if anyone wishes, with Grotius, to pervert it, that the words forever signify nothing else than a long time, the things which are held here do not allow it: and they shall dwell upon it, they and their children, and their children's children FOREVER. For these words speak of all their posterity, the children of children, and those who will be born from them. But how was Zorobabel the King of all of them, of the entire Israelite posterity? Indeed, it is said of all these: AND DAVID MY SERVANT SHALL BE THEIR PRINCE forever. Theodoret urges this argument against the Jews: Let the Jews say, who is their eternal King, who is called David? For they themselves will also confess that such appellations by no means fit Zorobabel. For first, he did not reign, but was a leader of the people; then, even that very rule was ended by death: but if they understand this eternal one to be of the Davidic lineage, let them show the Davidic lineage reigning, which if, besides the kingdom, the lineage itself also the Davidic lineage is uncertain, in the present case one of two things is necessary: either to think the Prophecy false, or to adore the kingdom of the Lord Christ, born of David according to the flesh; but they themselves will likewise confess that the Prophecy is free from falsehood. But if it is true, how then is it free from falsehood, when we see neither another kingdom of the Jews, nor even the lineage of David itself, it is clear and manifest that He Himself reigns, as from David according to the flesh, but Son of God according to divinity, and He obtains an eternal empire; their delusion and perfidy are clear and open, and our knowledge of God. This is Theodoret.

Then, lest we doubt that that principality truly lasts forever, a covenant of peace forever is promised to this kingdom. That eternity, therefore, is promised to this David, which is of the covenant of peace, struck with him and his kingdom. But this is not an eternity of long time, but a perpetual one. Which is our eighth argument concerning the covenant of peace and this eternal King. Concerning which Theodoret again: Let them (the Jews) therefore show us either a covenant of peace or an eternal one: They will not be able, since they are deprived of both. But the Lord has given us both, for He has promised us eternal goods, and has bestowed this upon us, that we might be reconciled with Him. For He Himself is our peace, just as the divine Apostle is the author, and again the one and Mediator, God and man, Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a redemption for all.

The ninth argument is provided by the perpetual preservation of the sanctuary and tabernacle of the Lord in this Israel and under this King, v. 24. I WILL ESTABLISH THEM, AND WILL MULTIPLY THEM, AND WILL GIVE MY SANCTIFICATION IN THE MIDST OF THEM, AND MY TABERNACLE SHALL BE IN THEM, AND I WILL BE THEIR GOD, AND THEY SHALL BE MY PEOPLE. AND THE GENTILES SHALL KNOW THAT I THE LORD AM THE SANCTIFIER OF ISRAEL, WHEN MY SANCTIFICATION SHALL BE IN THE MIDST OF THEM FOREVER. This frequent repetition of the words FOREVER, and ETERNALLY; AN ETERNAL COVENANT, which are repeated five times in express words and several times more κατ' διάνοιαν (in meaning), confirm at length that not some long time, but a simple perpetuity is denoted, and that this King David will be eternal, just as his kingdom will be eternal, his eternal covenant of peace, his eternal people, and his eternal tabernacle in them, the eternal sanctification of the Lord in their midst, God will be eternal to them as God, which is to be understood of Christ the eternal King, and his eternal kingdom, which in this age is the kingdom of grace, in the other the kingdom of glory, the same kingdom, but a different manner of reigning, in which there is eternal peace, eternal sanctification, eternal tabernacles, and in them the eternal glory of the Lord. Whence it is taught that these things are also to be understood of the eternal heavenly Jerusalem, Apoc. 21, 3. Which Theodoret inculcates and urges against the Jews (and likewise against the Judaizing Grotius): But the temple is deserted, and what were holy things of old, how then did He promise that He would place His holy things in their midst for an age, and His tabernacle in them? Therefore, since we see neither the outcome of these things according to the opinion of the Jews, and we know the truth of spiritual words, let us understand these things in such a way that they correspond to those which we have interpreted before; for we have also the consenting testimony of the things themselves: For not only the holy house of God, but also the divine altars have been given to all men. Similarly Jerome: The Jews interpret it concerning the temple which was built under Zorobabel. But how can this stand, which is said forever, when that temple, which was built under Zorobabel, and afterwards restored by many, was burned by Roman fire? All of which things are to be referred to the Church, and to the times of the Savior, when His tabernacle was placed in the Church: where He has become our God: and we His people, and the progress of all is that they may know that He Himself is God, and He Himself sanctifies Israel, not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit: when His sanctification was made in the midst of believers forever.

The tenth argument is provided by the calling of the Gentiles: AND THE GENTILES SHALL KNOW, THAT I THE LORD AM THE SANCTIFICATION IN THE MIDST OF THEM FOREVER. Which teach that the Gentiles are to be brought to the knowledge of the one true God and to the Church of Israel: concerning which Theodoret: Truly, through those who believed from among the Jews, the Gentiles also received the light of the knowledge of God: for from the Jews came the Divine Apostles and the first disciples of the Apostles, and from the Prophetic foods, which were kept among the Jews, perceiving those things which pertain to our Savior Christ, the Gentiles believed through divine proclamation: for which reason the Divine Apostle also said that those who believed from among the Gentiles were grafted into the pious root of the Jews, and that those who did not believe from among the Jews were broken off and separated from this root. Therefore, salvation having been provided first to the Jews, he says, the Gentiles shall know that I am the Lord sanctifying them: For from the Jews is the Lord Christ according to the flesh, among the Jews the cross, the sepulcher, the resurrection, from the Jews the Apostles, and the first heralds; deservedly, therefore, the nations obtain salvation through them. Finally, the Rabbis themselves acknowledge that by David here the Messiah is understood: comparing what is said here about King David being for eternity with those things which are held concerning the eternal Throne of the Messiah in Psalm 45, 'Thy throne, O GOD, is for ever,' as is evident from Rabbi Aben Ezra on the aforementioned Psalm. R. Lusitanus in the Mittelburg Colloquy, fol. 122, admits that the Messiah is called here 'David my servant,' from which (although ἀπαιδεύτως [ignorantly]) he concludes that he is not God.

IN MY JUDGMENTS THEY SHALL WALK, AND MY COMMANDMENTS THEY SHALL KEEP, AND THEY SHALL DO THEM] See Isaiah 65:20.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET SERVUS MEUS DAVID REX SU- PER EOS] Ita dicitur Zorobabel, quia ex Davidis erat Sanguine, & virtutum ejus imitator, Vide supra 34, 34.

Pervertitur iterum illustris Prophetia de regno Christi & quæ de Messia uno Rege totius Israëlis præ- dicta, ad Zorobabelem detorquentur. Quod vero non concedendum, siquidem primo regnum Ephra- im cum regno Judæ in unum corpus coalescere debue- rit, FACIAM EAS (tribus) IN LIGNUM U- NUM. Id vero nunquam impletum est in cor- porali regno Ephraim & Juda, nedum sub Zoroba- bele: sed in regno Christi; sub quo & Israëlitæ & Judæ in unum mysticum corpus coaluêre. Obser- vandum autem imprimis, quod non tantum tribus Judæ & filiorum Israël sociorum ejus mentio fiat, per quos intelliguntur, qui in primo schismate sub Rehabeam 1. Reg. 12. partes Judæ sequuti sunt, cum tribu Benjamin, & Levi, quales erant ex omnibus tribubus aliqui, tum qui ex tribu Ephraim, Manaf- se & Simeon, ad Assum Nepotem Salomonis sese re- cepere; Vide 2. Chron. 11, 16. seqq. c. 15, 8. seqq. nec non qui sub Ezechia accesserunt è tribubus Asser, Menasse, Sebulon, & Isaschar 2. Chron. 30, 5. 11. 18. cap. 31, 1. Conf. Josephus l. 8. Antiquitat. c. 3. Sed quod etiam cuncta domus Israel, & socii ejus com- memorentur v. 16. Tribus Israel integræ, quod in u- num coalescere debuerunt cum tribubus Judæ & Ben- jamin, in unam nempe civitatem Ecclesiasticam. Ad quos vero referendos esse Israelitas secundum Spiritum, qui pro Israelitis restituendis in gratiam putandi erunt non gentis, sed fidei respectu ex Hos. 3, 4. 5. Ier. 3, 18. Rom. 9, 5. 6. colligitur. Neq; enim integræ tribus Israelis restitutæ unquam fuêre in unam politiam & Rempublicam cum Judæis, quia mansisse in perpetua captivitate aperte dicuntur decem tribus 2. Reg. 17, 23. 41. & eatenus sola tribus Judaica cum adhærentibus reducta dicitur passim: quo de etiam Josephus lib. 11. Ant. c. 5. Duæ tantum, inquit, tribus, per Asiam & Europam sub Romano Imperio degunt. Decem tribus nunc quoque ultra Euphratem sunt infinita hominum millia. Quæ vix est numero comprehendere. Permisit sane Cyrus Is- raëlitis omnibus potestatem redeundi, qui sub imperio suo erant, ut & Artachsastha, testibus diplo- matibus ipsorum Esdr. 1. 2. 3. 4. ut & v. 12. 13. & qui di- missi ac reversi sunt, vocantur communi Israelis no- mine Esdr. 1, 5. c. 2, 3. 59. 70. c. 6. 21. c. 10, 1. ac totius Israe- lis mentio fit c. 2, 70. c. 10, 5. Neh. 7, 20. c. 12, 47. & transmisit Esra diplomatis libertatis à Cyro pro- mulgati copiam Israelitis in Media hærentibus, te- ste Iosepho lib. 11. C. 5. accersivit Esdra è Caspia Le- vitas Efr. 8, 15. neq; dubium est, alios etiam inde re- dire potuisse, imo quum in sacrificia 12. arietes obla- ti sint, secundum numerum 12. tribuum Israel Efr. 8,35. haud obscurum esse videtur ex omnibus tribu- bus nonnullos reversos fuisse : Cæterum quum Scri- ptura in eo discrimen duarum tribuum, & decem tribuum, vel Iudæorum & Israelitarum assignet, quod Judæi reducendi quidem fuerint, non item Israelitæ; & Israelitas in Media perpetuo mansisse, ac projectos esse à facie Domini, sicut loquutus fue- rat in manu omnium servorum suorum Propheta- rum, aperte testetur 2. Reg. 17, 21. & seqq. neque unquam reversæ sint integræ tribus Israelus, quem- admodum hoc vaticinium tribuum mentionem fa- cit: non apparet, quomodo dici possit, hoc va- ticinium plenum complementum suum habuisse in reductione, & reditu corporali tribuum Israë- lis, & Judæ, quæ nunquam iterum in unum re- gnum coaluere, quemadmodum ante divisionem sub Salomone unum regnum & unam politiam o- mnes 12. tribus constituere. Quapropter utut vati- ciniis talibus illud beneficium libertatis redeundi in patriam omnibus apertum iri, multosque ex o- mnibus tribubus aliquando redituros ad cœtum populi Dei in terra Canaan restaurandam, admitti queat; non exhauritur tamen ita sensus ejusmodi Prophetiarum, quæ aliquid amplius inferunt; quod nempe Israelitis omnibus integrum fuerit ad populum Dei aggregari, quodq; convocati omnes sint non tam edicto Cyri, quam universali Evangelii præconio, quo omnibus libertas, ac potestas facta collectionis ad Ecclesiam, omnesque per totum or- bem ad populum Dei, quem reduxerat è captivita- te Babylonica, vocati sunt in Novo Testamento, postquam Christus ipse huic populo sese stiterat, eundemque per verbum congregarat, qui etiam mortuus est pro gente Iudaica, imo non pro gente tantum illa, sed ut filios Dei, qui erant dispersi, con- gregaret in unum, Ios. 11, 52. Summa est; agi hic de convocatione ad Ecclesiam, non de collectione ad Po- litiam; de unitate corporis Mystici, non de unita- te civili : de unitate sub Rege cælesti Messia, non sub terreno. Quæ convocatio cœperit tempore Cy- ri, sed compleatur tempore N. Test. usq; ad con- summationem seculi qua ad Israëlitas primum, ceu populum Dei electum, cui revelavit quondam Deus verbum suum, extendit Deus Manum suam, eosq; in terram patriam restaurandi cultus publici & cœtus Ecclesiastici causa revocatos voluit, qui non in exiguo numero tempore Cyri convolarunt & successu temporis aggregati plures eorum sunt, u- bi Christus promissus Messias, & Salv. mundi sub ad- ventum suum in terra Israelis αὐτοπροσώπως omnibus tribubus prædicavit, & ex omnibus tribubus Ecele- siam restauravit; tum vero per Apostolos ad Israeliti- cam Ecclesiam gentes universas aggregari, diruto pariete intergerino, curavit, & ex omnibus unum corpus fecit, hisce etiam pro Israelitis putatis, qui ad eosdem aggregabantur, & in bonam olivam, etsi ex naturali excisi oleastro, inserebantur, Rom. 11, 24. Recte itaque B. Chytreus in Comment. in Apoc. Germ. c. 20. observat tres esse gradus restitutionis populi Israelitici, de quibus Ezechiel, & alii Pro- phetæ: Primam sub Cyro & Dario, cum in Judæam reducti civitatem suam & templum reædificarunt. Alteram quæ per Christum Regem & Pastorem ovium Israelis undiq; per orbem dispersarum facta est, qui montem Zion & regnum Davidis in totum orbem propagat, & per præconium Evangelii novam & æternam civitatem & Ecclesiam erigit, & novam & æternam justitiam inchoat; quæ in tertia perfecta restitutione Israëlisin nova & cælestis Hierosolyma post resurrectionem complebitur, & consummabitur. Promittit ergo, juxta Chytreum, Prophetà Judæis in Babylone captivis & per orbem dispersis redi- tum in Judæam & restaurationem civitatis & tem- pli, & gloriosi atque æterni regni Davidis: ut nec excludi restauratio templi ex hoc vaticinio de- beat, nec ea sola Majestatem ejus exhauriat, sed im- primis augustum Christi regnum intendatur.

Neque vero admittendum iterum Judaizan- tis Grotii κρησφύγετον, quod hæc Prophetia tan- tum conditionata fuerit sub hypothesi seriæ conversio- nis facta: Nam parili facilitate etiam Judæi dicent promissionem de Messia conditionatam esse, ac con- ditione non præstita, etiam, quæ promissa sint, non impleri. Sic frigida affunditur excæcatis Ju- dæis. In promissionibus vero nonnullis tacitam conditionem subesse non diffitemur, sed in omnibus conditionem subintelligendam, minime conce- dendum est.

Porro (2) congregandi dicuntur filii Israël non ex terra certa sed è toto orbe: v. 21. Ecce ego assu- mam filios Israël de medio nationum, ad quas abie- runt, & congregabo eos undiq;, & adducam eos ad hu- mum suam. Quod cum nunquam impletum sit, quantum quidem ad universos Israëlitas è medio quarumvis nationum, undiq; collectos in unum poli- ticum corpus, de convocatione & collectione ad Eccle- siam intelligendum necessario est.

Tertio cum promittit Deus se gentem unam in terra in montibus Israël facturum, si de Politica unitate in Republica una vel regno uno id accipien- dum, ostendant Judæi, & advocatus eorum Gro- tius, & qui ejus partes tueri velint, ubi in unum corpus, in unam gentem politicam Israëlite omnes in montibus Israël collecti sint. Ideoq; de unitate my- stica Israëlitarum, qui convocati ex omnibus natio- nibus sunt ad Ecclesiam, tum eorum, qui secundum promissionem putati pro Israëlitis sunt, adeoque Israël dicuntur secundum Spiritum, intelligere hæc oportet, quorum omnium cor unum & una anima est Actor. 4,15. Confer. Esa. 11, 6. seqq. Galat. 3, 28. Eph. 2, 14. Col. 3, 11. Non erunt, inquit, tum ultra duæ gentes, nec dividentur amplius in duo regna. Id certe nunquam impletum est in Israëlitis secundum car- nem & Judæis, quod ita copulati sint in unum re- gnum, & in unam gentem, quoad gubernationem politicam. Ideo dicuntur unum esse IN MANU Domini, ut in Ebræo habetur, quia Christus sustu- lit æmulationem ac contentionem inter Judæos & Samaritanos, ac utrosque in Ecclesia sibi ac Deo junxit Joh. 4, 21. Quo de Hieronymus: vere in ad- ventu Salvatoris duæ virgæ, & ut in Hebræo positum est, duo ligna in unum juncta sunt sceptrum, & in Baptismate Christi dudum separata sociantur: ut fiant in unum novum hominem: & in unam gentem: neq; polluantur ultra in Idolis & abominationibus: Sed mundi lavacro sint populus Dei: & imperet eis Christus: & habitent super terram mitium, terram viventium, quam dederat servo suo Jacob: qui popu- lum Israël in matris utero supplantavit. Addit & alio- rum explicationem, quam etiam subjicere placet: Sin autem voluerimus juxta prophetiam Osee, quæ pene omnis ad decem tribus dirigitur, id est, ad Joseph & Ephraim, & Samariam & Israël, intelligere falsi nominis scientiam, & diversas turbas hæreticorum: hoc dicemus, quod in ultimo tempore, quando subin- traverit plenitudo gentium, & omnis Israël salvus fuerit: tunc etiam adversarii populi, qui contra do- mum Judæ & confessionem Ecclesiæ pugnaverunt, tradant se Ecclesiasticæ fidei: & universis erroribus derelictis & principibus mundi istius, qui destruuntur : & Patriarchis suis, qui eos in blasphemiarum bara- thrum deduxerunt : consurgant & relinquant Idola sua, & abominationes, quas de suo corde confinxe- rant : & de cunctis sedibus suis, in quibus peccave- runt, transeant ad Ecclesiasticam fidem & munden- tur, & sint populus Christi, & ipse sit Deus eorum.

Per Montes ergo Israel montes Ecclesiæ, Phra- si Prophetica, intelliguntur. Quia montes Israel, nec capere possent omnes, nec ad illos reversi o- mnes sunt.

Quarto quandocunque justificatio & libera- tio ab omnibus abominationibus promittitur, ac de tali rege, regimine & regno sermo est, sub quo, & in quo subditi spiritualiter mundandi sint, de regno & rege spirituali, non terreno agi manifestum est. Nullus enim sub terra populus est, nullum re- gnum, quòd totum ita sanctum & pium perpetuo sit ab idolis & abominationibus & iniquitatibus, quemadmodum hic promissum est: Neǵ; pollue- tur ULTRA in idolis suis, & abominationibus suis & cunctis iniquitatibus suis, & salvos eos faciam de u- niversis sedibus suis, in quibus peccaverunt, & E- MUNDABO eos, & erunt mihi populus, & ego ero eis DEUS. Quæ de Ecclesiâ, quam sibi Deus puri- ficat & sanctificat, & regno Christi intelligenda es- se, manifestum est.

Quinto: Qualis populus, talis Rex: Ideo non promittitur terrenus Rex, sed Messias Rex in mon- te Zion à Deo constitutus Ps. 2, 6. Germen illud Ju- stum Davidis, sub quo Juda & Israel confidenter ha- bitant Jerem. 23, 6. c. 33, 16. Cui nomen David tri- buitur, quod ex Davide originem traxerit, & thro- num David occuparit, ac David insignis ejus typus fuerit. Ideo Theodorets; David autem Domi- nus dicit Christum, ut ex David secundum carnem oriundum: servum autem propter humanam natu- ram. Quum enim in forma Dei esset, formam ser- vi accepit; docet igitur Prophetica oratio impietatem extinctum iri, & colendorum Idolorum errorem, regnorumq́; divisionem uno tandem imperio termi- nandam, sub quo degentes ii, qui etiam ab uno pasto- re significantur, suum & dominum & Deum agnoscent. Hæc Theodoretus. Quo de ad Ezech. 34. dixi- mus.

Sexto unus Rex omnium convocandorum ex omnibus nationibus constituitur, unus Pastor o- vium istarum; quod de Zorobabele intelligi non potèst, qui neque regia dignitate fulsit, neque o- mnibus Israëliticis tribubus imperavit; imo cum Regis hujus officium hic describatur à remissione peccatorum & sanctificatione, manifestum est, in nullum Regem terrenum id competere, ut recte notavit Theodoretus. De tali Rege sermo est, sub quo omnes ambulaturi in justitia, omnesque subditi sancti futuri sunt. Et Servus meus David Rex super eos & pastor unus omnium erit eorum: in judiciis meis ambulabunt & mandata mea custodient & fa- cient ea. Id vero in nullo terreno Rege contigit, sed proprium est regni Christi, Ecclesiæ Dei, quæ sanctorum est communio.

Septimo de Rege perpetuo & sempiterno hic a- gitur, qui scilicet in perpetuum regnaturus sit, cu- jus regni nullus sit finis. Et habitabunt super eam & ipsi & filii eorum, & filii filiorum eorum USQUE IN SEMPITERNUM, & David servus meus prin- ceps eorum in SEMPITERNUM. Id vero nul- latenus convenit Zorobabeli. Num enim ille Rex perpetuus Israëlis? Si vero pervertere quis cum Grotio id velit, verba in sempiternum nihil a- liud significare, quam diuturno tempore, non pa- tiuntur id ea, quæ hic habentur: & habitabunt super eam ipsi & filii eorum, & filii filiorum eorum US- QUE IN SEMPITERNUM. Nam ea sonant de omni posteritate eorum, natorum natis, & qui na- scentur ab illis. Quomodo vero illorum omnium Rex Zorobabel fuit, totius posteritatis Israëliticæ? Quin de his omnibus dicitur: ET DAVID SER VUS MEUS PRINCEPS EORUM in perpe- tuum. Quod argumentum urget adversùs Ju- dæos Theodoretus: Dicant Judæi, quis sempiternus ipsorum Rex fit, qui David appelletur? Nequaquam enim Zorobabeli hujuscemodi appellationes convenire, ipsi quoq; confitebuntur. Primum enim haud regna- vit ille, sed populi ductor fuit, deinde etiam illud ipsum imperium morte finitum est: quod si de genere Davidi- co hunc sempiternum intelligunt, ostendant David ge- nus regnare, quod si præter regnum ipsum quoq; David genus incertum est, in præsenti duorum alterum ne- cesse est, vel falsam Prophetiam opinari, vel Do- mini Christi ex David secundum carnem nati re- gnum adorare, verum à mendacio vacuam esse Pro- phetiam, ipsi itidem fatebuntur. Quod si vera est, quemadmodum igitur mendacii expers est, neq; vide- mus aliud Judæorum regnum, neq; insuper ipsum ge- nus David, clarum est & perspicuum, & ipse regnat, ut ex David secundum carnem, filius autem Dei se- cundum divinitatem, etiam sempiternum obtinet imperium; Perspicua & aperta est & illorum deli- ratio, perfidiaq́; & nostra Dei cognitio. Hæc Theo- doretus.

Tum ne ambigamus vere in sempiternum du- rare illum principatum, fœdus pacis sempiternum huic regno promittitur. Ea ergo sempiternitas huic Davidi promissa est, quæ fœderis pacis est, cum illo, & regno ejus percutitur. At hæc non est sempiternitas diuturni temporis, sed perpetua. Quod nobis octavum argumentum est de fœdere pacis, & hoc Rege sempiterno. De quo iterum Theodoretus: Ostendant igitur nobis (Iudæi) vel pacis vel sempiternum testamentum: Non poterunt, cum utroq; privati sint. Nobis autem utrumq; dedit Dominus, namq; & sempiterna nobis bona pollicitus est, & id nobis est elargitus, ut cum ipso reconciliare- mur. Ipse enim est pax nostra, sicut auctor est divus Apostolus, & rursus unus ac Mediator, Deus & ho- mo, Christus Jesus, qui dedit seipsum redemptionem pro omnibus.

Nonum argumentum perpetua sanctuarii & tabernaculi Domini in hoc Israële & sub hoc Rege conservatio suppeditat v. 24. FUNDABO EOS, ET MULTIPLICABO, ET DABO SAN- CTIFICATIONEM MEAM IN MEDIO EORUM, ET ERIT TABERNACULUM MEUM IN EIS, ET ERO EIS DEUS, ET IPSI ERUNT MIHI POPULUS. ET SCIENT GENTES QUIA EGO DOMINUS SANCTIFICATOR ISRAEL CUM FUERIT SANCTIFICATIO MEA IN MEDIO EO- RUM IN PERPETUUM. Hæc crebra re- petitio vocum IN PERPETUUM, atque IN SEMPITERNUM; PACTUM SEMPITER- NUM, quæ quinquies expressis verbis & adhuc aliquoties κατ' διάνοιαν repetuntur, confirmant prolixe, non diuturnum aliquod tempus, sed sim- plicem perpetuitatem notari, & æternum fore hunc Regem Davidem, æque ut æternum erit regnum ejus, æternum fœdus pacis, æternus ejus populus, & æternum ejus tabernaculum in eis, æterna in medio eorum sanctificatio Domini, æternus ipsis erit Deus in Deum, quæ intelligenda de Christo æterno Rege, & æterno ejus regno, quod in hoc seculo regnum est gratiæ, in altero regnum gloriæ, idem regnum, sed diversa regnandi ratio, in quo æ- terna pax, æterna sanctificatio, æterna tabernacula, & in eis æterna Domini gloria. Unde hæc de æ- terna Hierosolyma cœlesti etiam intelligenda esse docetur Apoc. 21, 3. Quæ adversus Judæos (& pa- riter adversus Grotium Judaizantem) ita inculcat, urgetque Theodoretus: Atqui desertum templum, & quæ antiquitus sancta erant, quomodo igitur pro- misit, se positurum sancta sua in medio ipsorum in se- culum, & tabernaculum suum in ipsis? igitur cum neq́; horum cernamus eventum secundum Judæorum sententiam, noverimusq́; spiritualium verborum veri- tatem, ita hæc intelligamus, ut iis congruant, quæ an- te interpretati sumus; habemus enim etiam rerum i- psarum consenticus testimonium: Neq́; enim solum sancta domus Dei, sed etiam divina altaria omnibus hominibus donata sunt. Similiter Hieronymus: Iu- dæi de templo interpretantur, quod sub Zorobabel ex- tructum est. Sed quomodo stare poterit hoc, quod di- citur in perpetuum, cum templum illud, quod sub Zoro- babel extructum est, & postea à multis instauratum, Romano igne succensum sit? Quæ omnia referenda sunt ad Ecclesiam, & ad tempora Salvatoris, quando tabernaculum ejus positum est in Ecclesia: ubi factus est Deus noster: & nos populus ejus, profectusq́; o- mnium est, ut sciant quod ipse sit Deus, & ipse san- ctificet Israel, non juxta carnem, sed juxta Spiritum: quando sanctificatio ejus in medio credentium facta est in perpetuum.

Decimum argumentum gentium vocatio sub- ministrat: ET SCIENT GENTES, QUIA E- GO DOMINUS SANCTIFICATIO IN ME- DIO EORUM IN PERPETUUM. Quæ gentes ad notitiam unius veri Dei & ad Ecclesiam Israelis adductum iri docent: de quo Theodore- tus: Revera per eos, qui ex Judæis credidére, etiam gentes cognitionis Dei lumen excepêrunt: ex Judæis enim Divi Apostoli & primi Apostolorum discipuli, & ex Propheticis cibis, qui apud Judæos custodieban- tur, quæ ad Salvatorem nostrum Christum pertinent, percipientes divino præconio gentes credidere: quam- obrem Divus quoq́; Apostolus inseri, qui ex gentibus crederent, dixit in pia Judæorum radice, frangiq́; & ab hac radice separari eos, qui è Judæis minime cre- derent. Salute igitur Indæis, inquit, primum suppe- ditata cognoscent gentes, quia ego sum Dominus san- ctificans eos: Ex Iudæis enim Dominus Christus se- cundum carnem, apud Iudæos crux, sepulchrum, resurrectio, ex Iudæis Apostoli, primią; præcones, merito igitur gentes per hos salutem consequuntur. Postremo agnoscunt Rabbini ipsi, per Davidem hic Messiam intelligi: Conferentes, quæ hic de Davide Rege in sempiternum futuro dicuntur, cum iis, quæ de Throno Messiæ sempiterno ha- bentur Psal. 45. Thronus tuus DEUS in æternum, ut ex Rab. Aben Esra in prædictum Psalmum con- stat. R. Lusitanus in Colloq. Mittelburg. f. 122. admittit, quod Messias hic dicatur David servus Do- mini, ex quo (licet ἀπαιδεύτως) concludit, quod non sit Deus.

IN JUDICIIS MEIS AMBULABUNT, ET MANDATA MEA CUSTODIENT, ET FACIENT EA] Vide Esaiam 65, 20.

## 37:25
Ver. 25.

FOR EVER] עַד-עוֹלָם, that is, for a very long time.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

USQUE IN SEMPITERNUM] עַד-עוֹלָם, id est, longissimo tempore.

## 37:26
Ver. 26.

COVENANT OF PEACE] Above 34:25. AND I WILL SET MY SANCTIFICATION IN THE MIDST OF THEM] Sacred things and ceremonies. Thus also shortly [in verse] 28.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

FOEDUS PACIS] Supra 34, 25. ET DABO SANCTIFICATIONEM MEAM IN MEDIO EORUM] Sacra ceremoniasque. Sic & mox 28.

## 37:27
Ver. 27.

AND MY TABERNACLE SHALL BE IN THEM] In the Hebrew: My dwelling-place. Thus also the Chaldean; the LXX [Septuagint]: κατασκήνωσις [dwelling]. Thus the temple is called in Ps. 131:5.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ET ERIT TABERNACULUM MEUM IN EIS] In Hebræo: Habitaculum meum. Sic & Chaldæus; LXX. κατασκήνωσις. Ita vocatur templum Ps. 131, 5.

## 38:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVIII. Consolation against the most grievous persecutions of the Church by Gog, who will strike the greatest terror, because the Lord is about to summon the sword against him and to punish him in various ways.

Vers. 1. SET THY FACE AGAINST GOG] He designates Antiochus from the peoples whom he possessed. Therefore, the best version is to Gog and Magog, the prince of the land.

That Grotius refers these two chapters to the times of the Maccabees proceeds from a preconceived opinion; namely, that the preceding prophecy deals with Zerubbabel and the preservation of the Jewish polity for a long time, as if God wished to warn the Jews not to promise themselves mere happiness from it, and that calamities would not be lacking. That foundation is slippery, nay, null. For the preceding prophecy did not deal with Zerubbabel, but with the Messiah. We do not deny, however, that this prophecy concerning Gog and Magog is very obscure and subject to various expositions by authors, most of which Bellarmine reviews in book III de Rom. Pont. cap. 17. Of these, those are inept in the first place who thought that the battles of the Devil and his angels with the good angels in heaven are noted in Jerome, since the prophecy is proposed concerning future things; and the battles are shown to be waged not between angels, but between men. Those who, according to Maldonatus, refer these to the battles of the Devil, which will one day occur in the heavens against the elect and the glorified, and understand by the different nations different orders of devils, do not depart much from them; these trifles we leave to their authors.

Nor, secondly, is the interpretation of St. Augustine suitable, who understands by Gog the Devil, and by Magog the army of the Antichrist: because Gog is some earthly Prince, a leader of an army, subject to death.

Thirdly, the opinion of the Jews, that the Messiah as an earthly King, whose coming they still await, is about to wage a corporal war against Gog and Magog, and is about to effect this notable slaughter of them, which is laboriously described by Ezekiel, is easily refuted from the text itself; because there is absolutely no mention of the Messiah here throughout two entire chapters which deal with the Gogitic battle, nor is any earthly Messiah, such as the Jews imagine, set up, but Jehovah is established in the battle line against Gog, c. 38, 21. c. 39, 2. 3. 4. 22. Since, therefore, the destroyer of this most grievous enemy of the Lord's people, whom the Prophet introduces, is Jehovah, the Jews must acknowledge that the Messiah is Jehovah, if they wish him to be opposed to the same here. For no one else is opposed to him in express words by the Prophet, except Jehovah. I pass over those things which the Jews have invented here concerning a double Messiah, one the son of Joseph, whose name is Nehemiah the son of Husiel, the other the son of David, of whom the former is to be killed in this Gogitic battle: the latter, succeeding him, is to occupy the kingdom: concerning which one may read in the Targum on Cant. 4, in Abenezra on Zach. 9, 1, and elsewhere passim. The author of Askath Rochel under the ninth sign expands his dreams about these thus: Michael will sound a great blast, by which the sepulchres of the dead will be opened in Jerusalem, and God Blessed will restore them to life.
