For the Messiah Ben David, and with him the Prophet Elijah, will raise from the dead the Messiah Ben Joseph, who was kept under the gates of Jerusalem. Then they will send the Messiah Ben David to collect the remnants of the Jews dispersed in all lands. And immediately all the Kings of the nations of the whole world will bring the Israelites, placed upon their shoulders, to God, etc. These also are of the same: But the Rabbis say in m. that the Messiah Ben Joseph will come first to collect the captivities, and then there will be the wars of Gog and Magog, just as they explain in cap. Roch. exalted above all as head (from 1 Chron. 29, 11.) Exalted as head, these are the wars of Gog and Magog, according to that of Ezek. 38, 3. Behold me against thee: And Gog and Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Thus in cap. Hachalil they explain concerning this time the Scripture which exists in Zach. 12, 11. Every family shall mourn apart, etc., namely, on account of the death of the Messiah Ben Joseph, who will be killed. And in cap. 1 of the same Megilla, that which is said in verse 11 is referred to the same: On that day there will be a great mourning in Jerusalem, etc. Other portents concerning these are proposed thus by R. Manasse Ben Israel in the book Hope of Israel p. 78. At that time the X tribes will come to Jerusalem, under the leadership of a prince, whom some Rabbis in the Talmud, and the Chaldean Paraphrase in some places, call the Messiah son of Joseph; and elsewhere the Messiah son of Ephraim, who, slain in the last war of Gog and Magog, will show himself to be (perhaps it should be read not to be) the Messiah son of David, who will be, as Hosea and Ezekiel say, the eternal prince of all 12 Tribes. The wise men make mention of this Messiah son of Ephraim in many places, but especially in the Babylonian Talmud in the tractate Suca c. 5, where they say he will die in the last war of Gog and Magog, and thus they explain c. 13 of the Prophet Zechariah: And they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one is wont to mourn for an only son. They also add that the four leaders, of whom the same Prophet speaks in chapter 11, are the Messiah son of David, the Messiah son of Joseph, the Prophet Elijah, and the high priest, which are the four dignities that will show their power in that blessed age. Note, however, that sometimes they call the Messiah the son of Ephraim, sometimes of Joseph: for he will come forth from the tribe of Ephraim, and will be the leader of all the ten tribes that give their name to Ephraim, because their first King, Jeroboam, was from that tribe. Not without reason do they call him the son of Joseph; for he himself was a true type for the house of Israel because of his imprisonment and subsequent happiness. Add that he remained hidden from his brothers for so long that he was completely unknown to them: just as today the ten tribes, who, however much they may call themselves captive, will nevertheless afterwards ascend to the highest pinnacle of happiness in the same way as Joseph. This Messiah of Joseph will die in the battle of Gog and Magog, and afterwards will rise again, so that he may discharge that dignity, not indeed with the scepter of a King, but only with the office of a viceroy, as Joseph was in Egypt, for the reason that the empire of the house of Israel, which fell under the reign of Hoshea son of Elah, will not rise again, as the Prophet Amos says in chapter 5, verse 2. Therefore, the kingdom of the ten tribes will not be restored, as Ezekiel warns in chapter 37, under the empire of the Messiah son of David, who will be eternal, and through the death of the Messiah, son of Joseph, the ten tribes will acknowledge that God does not wish them to have more than one prince; etc. The same Menasseh in book 3 of the Resurrection, chapter 5, hands down these things; all the Rabbis agree on this, that the Israelites, after their return to their homeland, which will happen at the time of redemption, will not fully and perfectly enjoy all tranquility and peace, until finally after the completion of the last and final war of Gog and Magog. For it will come to pass that after the Israelites have returned to Palestine, that nation of Gog and Magog will come to invade and occupy that land, and indeed with a huge multitude of men and infinite forces of soldiers, with the hope and intention that it may claim that kingdom and empire for itself, no differently than the Goths and Vandals of old, accompanied by a vile crowd, subjected the most opulent kingdoms to themselves and triumphed over them. And although they may perhaps be persuaded that this Jewish Monarchy was erected by no other than singular divine providence, perhaps they will nevertheless think that it will last only for some time; and therefore that it can be overturned by them no less then and subjugated, than it was once overturned or subjugated by Nebuchadnezzar and Titus Vespasian. Armed with this hope and confidence, those nations will invade the Holy Land, and, having expelled the Israelites again, will attempt to bring it under their own power. This he attempts to prove primarily from this prophecy. But this battle, says Manasseh, will be joined at the end of the world; for on its very last and final day the whole earth will be shaken, and dissolved into parts, it will be dissipated by floods, earthquakes, and other ruins of that kind. And then all things will be destroyed, Gog will be wiped out with all the nations, and from their slaughter the earth will be filled with so many corpses that it will take seven months to bury the corpses and cleanse the land.

But to have recited these incoherent inventions, more absurd than old wives' tales, is to have refuted them most soundly. And we see here openly that, out of sheer desperation, Manasseh pushes the coming of the Messiah to the end of the world. In this way, the earthly Messiah, for whom they have hoped for so many centuries, will be of no use to them, nor will those things which they dream are predicted here concerning his battle be able to hold together in any way. If the construction of the third temple, which the Jews dream of, is to be joined with the coming of the Messiah, how can it be pushed here to the end of the world and coincide with it, unless perhaps they wish to say that the material temple is to be built only after the resurrection of the dead and the final judgment? Manasseh indeed says this in book 3 of De Resurrect. c. 8, but everyone understands how absurd and discordant that is.

But, so that the texture and origin of that fable concerning the meeting of the twin Messiahs with Gog may be more fully understood, it is pleasing to append some things from the author of As kath Rochel, edited by Hulsius. Now, under the seventh sign of the Messiah, page 51, it is held thus: God, the worker of wonders, will show a prodigy in the world: they say that at Rome there is a marble stone representing the form of a most beautiful girl, which was not made by hand, but was created by divine power; to this stone the most wicked of the nations of the world will gather, and warming it, they will lie with it; God, however, will preserve the drops of their seed in the middle of the stone, and will create a creature in it, and will form the appearance of an infant; finally, the stone being broken, he will bring forth the form of a man, whose name will be Armillus, who will be the adversary, and the nations will call him Antichrist. His height will be twelve cubits, and between his two eyes there will be the space of a span; with deep and glowing eyes, the hair of his head will be like the color of gold, the soles of his feet will be green, and he will have two crowns. He will approach the impious and say to them: I am the Messiah, I am your God, and they will immediately believe in him and will thus appoint him king; all the descendants of Esau will associate themselves with him. Against him, it is said, the Messiah Ben Joseph, who is Nehemiah the son of Husiel, is to go forth into battle with thirty thousand of Israel, and at first indeed successfully, but in the second battle they are to lose the leader himself, the Messiah, whose body the angels of the ministry are to take up and keep with the Patriarchs: after him will follow the Messiah Ben David, together with Elijah, to whom the rest among the Jews will gather themselves, and will resist Armillus. God, however, will not compel the Messiah to enter into war, but will say to him only, sit at my right hand. Ps. 110:1. And he himself will say to the Israelites, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which will be prepared for you today. And immediately God himself will fight with the enemies, which is said in Zech. 14:3. And God will go forth and fight with those nations, as on the day when he fought, the day of conflict. And God will send down fire and brimstone from heaven, which is what is said in Ezek. 38:22. And I will contend with him with pestilence and blood, and I will rain down upon him huge hailstones, fire, and brimstone. And immediately the impious Armillus will die with his whole army and all the impious who laid waste the House of our God and deported us from our land. In that very hour the Israelites will take vengeance upon them, because it is said in Obad. 1:18. And the house of Jacob will be as fire, and the house of Joseph as a flame, but the house of Esau as stubble, etc. Then Michael will sound a great blast: and what follows thereafter, cited above. But enough of trifles, and perhaps more than enough.

The fourth opinion of certain ancient Chiliasts is that, after the Antichrist has been killed and the resurrection has taken place, the Saints will reign with Christ for a thousand years on this earth in supreme peace, but when those are finished, the devil will be released and will stir up war against the Saints, concerning which Ezekiel treats here, and John in Rev. 20. Although this opinion is that of many ancients, such as Papias, Justin, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Apollinaris, etc., as Jerome reports in ch. 37 of Ezekiel, and Eusebius in book 2 of Ecclesiastical History, the last chapter, Bellarmine rightly says that it has long since been exploded as a proven error. Because the bodily resurrection of the dead will not happen except once at the end of the world, and the destruction of the Antichrist is connected with the very consummation of the age and the coming of Christ, 2 Thess. 2.

Nor is there any reason for us to be much concerned about the fifth, the opinion of Eusebius in book 9 of Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. 3, who posits that Gog is the Roman Emperor and Magog is his Empire, because it rests on no other foundation than a foreign translation of the passage in Num. 24, among the LXX Interpreters, who rendered Agag as Gog. Gog will be exalted, and his kingdom will be increased. In the Hebrew it is: He will be exalted more than Agag his King, that is, the Kings of the Hebrews will be more powerful than neighboring kings, and most powerful ones, such as Agag was.

Regarding the sixth point to the Papists, who interpret their utopian Antichrist as about to appear against the Church of Christ, whom Bellarmine approves, Cornelius a Lapide the Jesuit refutes his own associates with these arguments: because Gog is not the Antichrist, because Gog ought to have been buried in the land of Israel to the east of the sea, whereas the Antichrist is to be snatched away alive to the underworld; Gog is called the Prince of Meshech and Tubal; but the Antichrist is the prince of many more nations. Valentianus, however, still feigns that for that Jewish Antichrist of his, the armies of Gog and Magog will come to Jerusalem, so that in it, and in all of Judea, they may destroy the Christians who are to flock there to hear Elijah and Enoch preaching. These inventions are of the same currency as Rabbinical fables, and will find belief only when it is demonstrated that the Antichrist will arise from the tribe of Dan, and that the resurrection of Elijah and Enoch will take place before the end of the world.

Seventh, Jerome, and those who follow him, both Tyconius in homily 17, Haymo, Bede in Apocalypse 20, Prosper of Aquitaine with others, and also Augustine in book 20 of The City of God, chapter 21, mystically interpret the individual words, which denote specific peoples. Searching according to etymology for a certain spiritual meaning; as, for example, because Gog sounds like 'roof,' heresiarchs, who are like a raised and proud roof, are noted. Magog, which is interpreted as 'from the roof,' signifies those who believe the heretics, and so on. But it is too manifest that a certain kingdom and certain peoples are being described, whose names, provinces, and location the Holy Spirit has expressed, and not in such an elaborate description of peoples, from gentile and patronymic names, all those things can be explained allegorically, unless we wish to do significant violence to the text.

Eighth. Some wish for him to be described here, following Galatinus, as the enemies of the Church in general. This opinion also pleased Johann Hornbeck in his work on the conversion of the Jews, Book III, chapter 11, page 252. In my opinion, no specific person is designated here by Gog, the prince of Meshech and Tubal; but under that name, the enemies of the Church in general, and how GOD is going to restrain them and destroy them. Therefore, I believe that not only Antiochus and his persecutions, or the Roman Anti-Christ, but whoever are the mimics and adversaries of the Church are denoted under that name, and how both they are going to wage war against the Church, and GOD is going to wage war for the Church against them, and destroy them. But the individuating conditions, by which Gog and the peoples fighting against the Church, and their auxiliary peoples attacking the Church here and now, and the war itself, and the place and outcome of the war are defined, compel us to understand specific peoples, unless we wish to depart from the literal sense to a certain allegorical and etymological interpretation and allusion, contrary to the custom and habit of this Prophet and other similar prophecies, and contrary to the laws of sound interpretation.

Ninth. The blessed Ambrose, in Book II of 'On the Faith', last chapter, wishes Gog to be the Goths, which opinion St. Jerome left in the middle in his Hebrew Questions on Genesis, chapter 10. But our blessed Hülsemann, in his unpublished commentary on Ezekiel, argues at length (even if he acknowledges that Ambrose strayed from the mark in point of time regarding the fulfillment of the prophecy) and brings forward as those of the same mind as Ambrose: Proclus of Constantinople in Socrates, Book VII, chapter 41; Nicephorus, Book XIV, chapter 38; Isidore of Seville in the etymology of the name Gog; Arethas on chapter 20 of the Apocalypse; that by these tyrants are understood the Goths and Vandals, who in the centuries of Theodosius, Valens, Gratian, and succeeding Emperors, twelve hundred years ago, ravaged the Church in Thrace, Italy, Africa, and a certain part of Asia, and likewise in Spain. Our opinion, he says, is that primarily and radically by Gog and Magog are to be understood the Goths, the peoples of Sweden. He proves this from the fact that (1.) The Goths are said to be named from Gog, by the consensus of ancient historians. (2.) That ancient and recent historians alike establish Magog, the grandson of Noah, as the first king of the Swedes. (3.) That the empire of the Goths once extended to European Scythia, which is today under the empire of the Turks. Indeed, even today the borders of Karelia and Ingria extend into both Moscovies, that is, into European and Asiatic Scythia, as witnessed by Johannes Magnus in the preface to his History, chapter 4, and in History, Book I, chapter 1, and Book VI, 12. And that the Goths and Swedes, already some thousands of years ago, coalesced into one nation, whence the Scythians, Libyans, and Ethiopians are touched upon here as allies of the battle of Magog, because they are neighbors of the Goths, were once under their power before the age of Constantine the Great, and dwell in the same continent with them, namely towards the East and the North. (4.) Since more than 30 peoples erupted in different centuries from the region of the Goths, who, longing for the richer property of other kingdoms, fixed their seats in Asia, Africa, and various kingdoms of Europe, it is not a wonder if the Prophet establishes the Goths as the first authors of the incursion into the lands of the faithful, to whom then other Northern Barbarians, invited by the progress of the Goths, joined themselves. He brings forward at length examples of these incursions made by the Goths from Johannes Magnus, and confirms with various testimonies that they occupied Rome itself, and what calamities they often created in the Church before they were converted to the faith of Christ. (5) He observes that that Gog is rightly called the prince and head of them, or the chief Meshech, whether the word Meshech is understood of the Cappadocians with Jerome and Josephus, or of the Muscovites with Tirinus and Menochius, or of the Scythians themselves living by the Maeotic Marshes, because, as Johannes Magnus testifies, the Goths occupied these kingdoms of Asia and Europe, and left their descendants there: for the same reason he understands the prince Tubal to be called either the Spaniards, Portuguese, or Iberians or Castilians with Prado, Saa, Sanctius, and Maldonado, or with Bellarmine those Spaniards who migrated into America and the kingdom of Peru, because the most powerful part of the current inhabitants of Spain arose from the Goths, as the same Johannes Magnus teaches. Although indeed the blessed Hülsemann wishes the Goths to be understood primarily and radically by Gog and Magog, because the first incursions into the lands of the faithful, and the most grievous persecutions and devastations were made by the pagan Goths, and other Barbarians were invited by their example, he nevertheless refers the most recent persecution, which he judges to be designated by Ezekiel, to the Roman Anti-Christ at the same time: concerning whom he writes thus on chapter XXXVIII, verse 1. The tenth opinion, which Bellarmine makes his own, and which most modern Papists follow (though not all), explaining Gog as the Anti-Christ and Magog as his people or army, is so far from being opposed to us that we believe the Roman Pontiff, having at some time taken on Northern Barbarians—Turks, Tartars, Muscovites, and other peoples who inhabit Scythia today—will afflict the Church with reinforcements: because that persecution from Gog and Magog, of which Revelation 20 speaks, will be the very last of all before the end of the world, as the connection of the prophecies with the Apocalypse easily shows, and Jerome and Augustine rightly noted. But that the seat or place of the Anti-Christ will be in the sides of the North, by the force of these prophecies of Ezekiel 38, verse 15, and chapter 39, verse 2, or that the Anti-Christ himself is Gog, are mere trifles clothed in no appearance of probability: wherefore they do not even deserve a refutation.

These things our late lamented one, whose arguments concerning Gog and Magog also provide conviction, which L. Paulinus Gothus, Theologian and Bishop of Strängnäs, in his Historia Arctoa concerning the deeds of the Swedish and Gothic Emperors, from Magog onwards, both internal and external, up to the end of the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy and the Visigothic in Spain, has handed down: The Swedish-Gothic Monarchy, he says, acknowledges as the author of its origin Magog, the grandson of Noah through his son Japheth: Genesis 10, verse 2. Magog, therefore, heading from the mouths of the river Tanais towards the North, first ruled in that part of Scythia which is now called Finland, otherwise Finningia. Then, having crossed the Venedic gulf of the Bothnian sea, he arrived in the peninsula of Scandia, containing three very large kingdoms, namely Sweden, Gothia, and Norway, carried with a great multitude of people in serrated ships, and he named those peoples after his own name, as Josephus is the author, Magogae, upon whom later both the Latins and the Greeks imposed the name of Scythians. These things he.

L. Paulinus Gothus makes Suennon, son of Magog, the second ruler and propagator of the Swedish nation, who gave the appellation to the peoples subject to him and to the land of Sueconia or Sweden: but the third, GETHAR (the second-born of Magog), otherwise Gog, who took care that his name should be adapted to the Geths, or Goths, over whom he presided.

However, since I do not fully grasp the mind of my blessed father-in-law regarding the fulfillment of the prophecy of this prediction concerning Gog and Magog, to tell the truth, nor does it appear how that opinion concerning the Goths can be adapted to the latest times and the latest persecution, which he considers to be described here and in Apoc. 20, if the Turks, Tartars, and Muscovites, who have most recently afflicted the Church, are understood, I leave the judgment concerning the same, and concerning the prince Tyrant Goth, to others. I add this, however: that the blessed Philipp Nicolai, although in Book II of the Kingdom of Christ, Vol. II of his works, p. 137, understands by Gog the greater, external Anti-Christ, Mahomet, and his precursors, through whom he burst in from the sides into the kingdoms and principalities of the Christian Goths, Vandals, Alans, Heruli, Huns, etc. He subjoined this Apology for that explanation, p. 186. Moreover, if it has troubled anyone here that I reckon wars moved not only by the Turks and Tartars, but also by the Huns, Goths, Vandals, Alans, Heruli, Lombards, Bulgars, Slavs, English, French, Germans, and Burgundians, and formerly against the Roman Empire and the Christians, to the Gogitic expedition onto the mountains of Israel: let him diligently look at the catalog of nations assisting the Gogites, and let him remember that the sides of the North are not without cause called the place of Gog, since Gog obtained from there such a multitude of peoples, vigorously promoting his own efforts, and those nations, partly of Henetic and partly of Germanic origin (before they were brought to Christ), some attacked the Church of the Lord from the outside with pagan fury; others patronized Arianism, and thus all, placed outside the Church of Christ, fostered and aided the spirit of the greater Anti-Christ, that is, Mahomet, as his forerunner. Nor is there any reason to object: If those ancient nations, tracing their lineage from the Heneti and Germans, are therefore to be numbered among the Gogites because they hostiley infested the churches of the Roman Empire with fury and ethnic blindness: then by the same argument the Roman Emperors themselves, the Neros, Trajans, Commodi, Heliogabali, Valerians, Maximini, Diocletians, and others still immersed in pagan superstitions (who afflicted the Church) should be reduced to the same order, so that they are considered to have provided fodder and nourishment to the Gogitic Spirit with blind impetus. A ready solution occurs: that there is a difference between the persecution moved by ethnic Emperors and that which those ancient nations excited. For the pagan Caesars afflicted the Church of Christ, accustomed to the slaughter and calamities of continuous persecutions: But the Huns, Heruli, Lombards, Franks, English, Picts, Slavs, Bulgars, and Ruthenians (while they still defended Paganism) tyrannically vexed and harassed the churches of the provinces of the Roman Empire, no longer exposed to the furies of gentile emperors, but having emerged from them and enjoying public peace. Ezekiel and Daniel, however, testify together that those are led by the Gogitic Spirit who attack the Church from the outside at a time when the yoke of persecution has been removed, the sacrifice [has been restored], and when the Israelites, the dispersion of the holy people having ended, have breathed again, and thus, having been gathered from the sword, have lived securely and confidently. Whence it is plain that, although ethnic

Emperors, no less than our Northern ancestors, still laboring under gentile blindness, atrociously persecuted the Church from the outside, nevertheless both are not to be reckoned among the Gogites, but only these latter ones who Mahometanized, who harassed with slaughters and rapine the Israelites or Christians, freed from the sword of persecution and placed in public tranquility. Thus far the blessed Phil. Nicolai.

Theodor Bibliander provided the occasion for the tenth explanation, which Bellarmine (following his own order) recounts thus: The fifth, he says, is that of Theodor Bibliander, whom Chytræus follows in his commentary on c. 20 of the Apocalypse. Therefore, Bibliander, in table 14 of his Chronology, where he accurately discusses Gog and Magog, and finally teaches that the prophecy of Ezekiel and John does not pertain to the same time, but that the prediction of Ezekiel was indeed fulfilled in the time of the Maccabees, and that Gog and Magog were Alexander the Great and his successors, the Kings of Syria and Egypt, who engaged in many battles with the Jews and were finally overcome by the Maccabees. But the prophecy of John was fulfilled in the time of Pope Gregory VII and some following Pontiffs: And that Gog and Magog were the Pontiffs and the armies that fought for a long time against the Saracens for the recovery of the Holy Land and the Sepulcher of the Lord. These things Bellarmine: who, however, explained that opinion less faithfully regarding the battle against the Saracens, so that he might the more easily refute it, since the battle of Gog and Magog is to be outside the camp of the Saints, that is, the beloved city, or against the true Church of God: But the war of the Christians was conducted for the recovery of the Holy Land. The blessed Chytræus, following Bibliander in Apoc. c. 20, explained his mind far otherwise, whose exposition we bring forward, because it is not easily accessible. That John says, however, when the thousand years are finished, Satan will be loosed again, to seduce all the nations, Gog and Magog, that he may gather them for battle, etc., means that the Devil will again rage in the world much more severely and violently, and that the Antichrist will extend his kingdom much further than could have happened in these thousand years before. The thousand years, however, Theodore Bibliander begins, in the 13th table of his chronology, not from the resurrection of Christ, but from the completion of the preaching of most of the apostles, namely around the year 73 after the birth of Christ, in which year Gregory VII Hellebrandus was Pope at Rome, who with Antichristian tyranny and persecution of Christendom, but especially of the German lands, far surpassed all previous Popes. And at that very time the Turks also devastated the most prominent churches in Asia, having taken Antioch, Nicaea, and other cities as well. Soon thereafter, the expedition into Asia and Palestine was undertaken at the instigation of the Pope, who, although he pretended in words as if he wanted to protect the churches in the Orient, in truth intended nothing else by it than that he would gladly have extended his primacy and kingdom over the Asian churches as well. In which expedition, countless Christians were slain by the Saracens and Turks, from the year of Christ 1096, in which Godfrey, the Duke of Lorraine, with his brother Baldwin and other princes, first sailed into Asia: until the year after Christ's birth 1290, at which time Mulech, the Saracen Sultan, tore down and razed the cities of Tripoli, Tyre, Sidon, Beirut, and Ptolemais (which the Christians alone still held at that time). And thus the beloved city and camp of the saints or of the Church of God was surrounded in the east and west, and terribly devastated and plagued by the Anti-Christ, Saracens, and Turks, who have since then oppressed almost all Christians in Asia, Africa, and the greater part of Europe. These barbaric peoples, but especially the Saracens and Turks, who wage such terrible and bloody wars against the Churches of God, are (as almost all Christian teachers unanimously hold) signified by the words Gog and Magog. Therefore they did not make the Mohammedans and Saracens the true Church of God and the camp of the saints, as Bellarmine slanders, but they wish for them to be signified by the name of Gog and Magog, not excluding the Roman Anti-Christ.

B. Cramer also applied this to this prophecy of Ezekiel in his Bible and treated it more fully. To which Mr. Dr. Moller in his Refuted Judaism seems not to deny his support at all, book 1, ch. 22, p. 928. When this defeat is to happen, whether it has happened or is still in the future, I would rather hear others speak of it than speak myself. Yet, so as not to forestall anyone, I will state my opinion on this simply, and nevertheless leave everyone to their own opinion. If one says that such a terrible defeat, where the Turk, as some claim, is to be completely crushed shortly before the Last Day, is still to come: what is that other than to make people secure, not to believe in the arrival of Christ, rather than that this has been put into effect? And where does that leave Daniel, who says that he will retain the victory until the Ancient of Days holds the judgment? Therefore, I hold that this defeat has already occurred, and indeed in the year that was written, after Christ's birth, one thousand and ninety-six, when the Turkish Mahumeth had already raged and stormed for almost five hundred years from his beginning. For then the Roman Empire sent the mighty and brave hero Godfrey, Prince and Duke of Lorraine, together with his brothers and many other brave princes and great lords, into the Promised Land, with six hundred thousand men on foot and one hundred thousand armored men on horseback, against whom Gog and Magog brought such a force into the field that Bonfinius writes of it: innumerabilem Turcarum & Saracenorum multitudinem fuisse, it was an uncountable multitude, like a cloud, as Ezekiel says, or the sand on the sea, as St. John says, of Turks and Saracens who had marched against them under Solyman: as to how it turned out, Bonfinius says further: Inaudita Barbarorum cædes edita, præda incredibilis inde relata. It was an unheard-of slaughter of the heathens that occurred, over which they obtained an incredibly great booty: just as they also conquered so blissfully that so many glorious cities were taken from him by force and captured: such as Nicaea, Antioch, Jerusalem, Tarsus, Tripoli, Joppa, Ascalon, Porphyria, Tiberias, in sum all of Cilicia, Syria, Mesopotamia, but drove the Turks to Egypt, and also brought their victory so high that Godfrey was publicly crowned King of Jerusalem, yet with a crown of thorns in honor of Christ. Which kingdom the Christians also possessed peacefully for a full ninety years from the conquest of the city of Nicaea, and obtained manifold victories against the hereditary enemy. From this also arose the holy orders of the Knights Hospitaller and the Rhodians, and the Templars, all of which were directed against the Turk, as can still be read about this in William of Tyre, Antonius Bonfinius, Henricus Pantaleon, Albert of Aachen, Melanchthon, Funck, Lonicer, and others more. Now, if one looks at the text of the prophet, it fits perfectly here without any strain. For 1. the power of the Turk had risen greatly at that time and had exercised great tyranny against the Christians for several hundred years. 2. His great multitude of armies and the support of the peoples coincide with it. 3. His equipment. 4. As far as the place is concerned, it happened precisely on the mountains of Israel, which is the land that has been brought back from the sword: for it certainly happened after the Roman destruction of the city of Jerusalem. 5. It happened through the people of Israel, that is, the Christians, who are of the faith of Israel, and yet are such an Israelite people, which has been brought back from many peoples (Jews and heathens through faith). 6. It was such a defeat that one could well have had enough wood for seven years from the shields, arrows, and bows in that same region: without the numerus finitus being able to be taken for an indefinite one, for if the Christians were six hundred thousand, without those whom they found there for themselves in the Promised Land, then there were at the very least just as many Gogites, Turks, and Saracens again; let one consider what kind of battle that was, and whether there were not over a thousand times a thousand pieces to count in shields, bucklers, and arrows, and whether the Christians of that place could not have had fuel from it for a long time in the warm lands, and the animals and birds under the heavens would have found good pickings, according to the letter. And I do not see what can be brought up against this from the text, other than that one might say that GOD nevertheless promises here to turn the captivity of Jacob, and that they would dwell securely in the land after such a battle: now the Turk has nevertheless become powerful again. The answer to this is that these words are to be compared (indeed, in sound they are the very same) with those by which GOD promised the return and security to his people after the Babylonian captivity: Therefore our fortune cannot be otherwise than that of the Jews after the Babylonian captivity was, when they were indeed brought back and dwelt securely, but yet so that they did not remain without great opposition from the enemies from whom they had been rescued, as can be seen from Ezra and Nehemiah, and from the histories of the Maccabees: For the cross must be included, and just as GOD destroyed the Canaanites, and yet the Israelites had to have a rod of discipline in those who remained, Jud. c. 2. v. 3. and c. 3. v. 4. GOD deals likewise with his Christians, and we have God to thank that, although the Christians on the borders are not unmolested by the Turks, that nevertheless the greatest crowd of Christians in Spain, Italy, France, for the most part German lands, Poland, Muscovy, Sweden, Denmark, England, the Netherlands, yes, even in Turkey itself, can still live, God be praised, and have lived quite securely from him. And so much for the B battle already happened six hundred years ago, and this time was already called the last time by the prophets back then, and St. John soon thereafter set the white throne, it is therefore infallibly to be concluded that the dear Last Day must be near at the door: It is also useful to consider how gloriously God spread the name of Christ there among the heathens, and made himself known against the blasphemous Mahometan crowd, in all places of the world. These things [are from] the blessed Cramer, and from him Mr. Dr. Müller.

Others, however, in the eleventh [place] admit that the Turks are indeed pointed to by the Prophet, but they prefer that this prophecy is not yet fulfilled, but remains to be fulfilled in these last times. Which opinion is that of the Magdeburg Centuriators, Cent. 1, book 2, ch. 4, column 435, and of Osiander in his Paraphrase, which explanation was also that of the blessed Luther in his marginal glosses, and seems preferable to the others. Philipp Nicolai, however, provided a completely peculiar and entirely mystical interpretation, which can be read in the cited place.

Twelfth, Theodoret in ch. 38 of Ezekiel, and Bibliander, as well as Sanctius among the Papists, and Tremellius, Junius, Piscator, and Polanus among the Calvinists, explain it concerning Antiochus: which opinion this Grotius interpolated.

Some in the thirteenth [place] join this and the preceding explanation, and wish for the Prophet to be prophesying both about the tyranny of Antiochus against the Israelites and about that of the Mahometans or Turks against the Christian Church, such as the blessed Pappus and the Weimar Paraphrasts.

Others in the fourteenth [place] explain it partly concerning Antiochus, partly concerning the Roman Anti-Christ, of whom the former was a type. Which exposition was approved by the Belgian Paraphrasts. But since a diverse and disparate meaning must be introduced into most of the words and phrases by such a double sense, it deserves no consideration, to say nothing of its other inconveniences.

But the explanation of the blessed Luther is simpler, more certain, and clearer, as will be evident in the progress. It suffices here to note only a few things against the Grotian interpretation, which stand in the way of our judging that it should be subscribed to.

But first, that connection which he lays down as a foundation with the preceding chapter does not exist: which relies on a false interpretation, as if deliverance from the Babylonian captivity were predicted in the preceding words, but now the dangers to which the Jews in the land are to be exposed are described. But since the antecedent has already been demonstrated to be false, the consequent is rashly inferred.

Next, the version which Grotius calls the best: 'Set thy face toward Gog & Magog, the prince of the land,' is less appropriate: for in the Hebrew it is 'toward Gog, the land of Magog' המגוג. Nor do the accents, or a comparison of chapter 39, 1, permit us to draw 'prince' נשיא back to the preceding words, as if it were said 'Prince of the land of Magog,' since it pertains to the following ones. It is also indicated that 'Gog and Magog' are distinct in Rev. 20:8, where each word is taken for a people. Therefore, one should not believe with Grotius that a single Antiochus is designated as the prince of the land of Magog. Thirdly, it is too precarious and less consistent that he derives the name of Gog from the Gygaean Lake, and furthermore resorts to Gyges, who had possessed Lydia and the neighboring places of Asia. Because, forsooth, Lydia was in the part of the Lagidae, from whose lineage Antiochus came. Fourthly, he makes the land of Magog Syria, because in it there is a Hieropolis called Magog by Pliny. But the interpreter of Pliny, Sigismund Gelenius, Lipsius, Dalecampius, Casaubon, and Johannes Annius of Viterbo in his Commentary on Berosus deny that his words should be taken as if Hieropolis were called Magog in the Syrian language. Since Josephus, who was very close to that province, would not have been silent about that name. To some it seems that by Magog, Pliny designated some idol worshipped at Hieropolis. Then, if any city of Syria is called so at all, it cannot be understood here. Because Syria is to the South of Chaldea, in which Ezekiel had this vision, not to the North. But Magog is established here toward the North. Furthermore, not only a city is noted here, but a land, that is, some province or kingdom, by Magog. Therefore, Hieropolis cannot be understood. Wherefore, by the land of Magog, a province or the people of Magog is significantly indicated. However, it is agreed that to Magog both Scythias, European and Asiatic, that is, all the Northern kingdoms, Armenia, Tartary, Muscovy, Lithuania, Finland, Sweden, Gothia, Denmark, Norway, were granted to be inhabited and governed. And therefore, B. Luther and others of our theologians not without reason judge that this prophecy directed to 'Gog, the land of Magog' refers to the Eastern Anti-Christ, the Turk, and the peoples of Tartary; Josephus is the author who states that the Scythians were called Magog, lib. 1, c. 11. But that the Turks are among the peoples of the Scythians, there is no doubt, see Pliny, lib. 6, c. 7. The Jews themselves understand the Scythian nations, as witnessed by Jerome on this passage, nor does Jerome deny it in his 17th question, and he also hands down that Magog is Scythian.

Fifthly, that by Meshech, Cappadocia is to be understood, although it seems so to Jerome, as also to Josephus, lib. 1, cap. 11. Others, however, prefer to understand it as the Muscovites, to whom the name also corresponds. Grotius wishes Tubal to be designated as Asiatic Iberia; others as the Spaniards or Portuguese or Castilians; others as the Armenians; but since all circumstances show that the Northern peoples who verge toward the East are to be understood in this place, Osiander maintains that the Wallachians are to be understood by Tubal: 'I think, therefore,' he says, 'that by Gog the Turk, by Magog the Tartar, by Meshech the Muscovites, by Tubal the Wallachians ought to be understood, so that the Turk and the Tartar hold the primary place in that expedition.' For John in the Apocalypse distinguishes Gog and Magog: And yet the supreme power will then be in the hands of Gog (the Turk): For he is called 'prince of the head' נשיא ראש, or chief, just as in Zech. 4:7, 'the headstone,' that is, the chief. Ps. 141:5, 'the oil of the head,' that is, the best balsam: B. Luther in the Marginal Gloss: 'Meshech and Tubal are also Tartars and the people behind them, whom one calls Scythians or Scots, although Meshech sounds as if the Muscovites come from them, that is, the Russians.' Johannes Cluverus, in Apoc. cap. 20, proves this opinion, which he says is that of the Magdeburg Centuriators and many others of our people, that Gog is the Prince of the Scythians, the Sultan of the Turks, of whom Magog are all those Scythian peoples who acknowledge the Turkish empire: He adds that some believe the Anti-Christ is Gog, that concerning the Eastern one it is true, who openly attacks the Church with war, not of the Western one, whom we have seen described under the name of the beast, who is clearly distinguished from Gog, and speaks lies under the horns of the lamb, and dominates in the very temple of God, that is, the Church. Philippus Nicolai understands Mahomet by Gog, the whole of Turkey by the land of Magog, the Muscovites and Spaniards by Mosoch and Thubal, and wishes him to be called their prince, because he exists in the place of the prince of tyranny before them, who themselves also hostiley infest the orthodox Church.

Sixth, as to the remaining peoples who are enumerated here, although some of them may have been in the army of Antiochus; yet because the rest do not fit Antiochus, in that he comes from the sides of the North, and in the latter years, others explain it more correctly as the forces of the Turks. B. Luther: 'Persians border on the Kingdom of Arabia, therefore the Turk will also have some of them; I consider Gomer and Togarmah to be the Wends, for at the Turkish court one speaks Wendish. Dedan is a piece of the Kingdom of Arabia, for the Mahomet lies buried in the Kingdom of Arabia at Mecca.' Osiander has this Paraphrase: 'In your army (O Gog) will be the Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans with them, all shielded and helmeted, because Gomer also (some think the Vandals descended from this grandson of Japheth) and all his hosts: the house of Togarmah, the sides of the north and all his strength (or army): i.e., there will also be present with you peoples who have sprung from Togarmah (grandson of Japheth): who dwell towards the North: and many and various peoples will be with you in that expedition against the Christians.' Although the Turk does not today immediately rule over all the aforementioned peoples: it can nevertheless happen that he gathers a huge army from all those regions. For Germans also serve in the armies of other nations, whose rule they do not yet acknowledge. B. Cluverus has it thus: 'Ezekiel brings forth Gog from the land of Magog, which is that of the Scythians, but he joins to them Paras, that is, the Persians, who are to the East: Cush, that is, the Ethiopians: indeed also certain Arabs, as the Midianites were once called Cush. Put, that is, the Libyans to the south: Gomer, who are the Galatians according to Josephus. Togarmah, who are the Phrygians, whom he places at the sides of the north, namely with respect to Judea, likewise Seba and Dedan, who are the Sabaean Arabs, and inhabitants of Petraea, Gen. 10, 7 and 25, v. 3. It is certain that these nations have finally been collected under one Turkish Empire, in which Magog, that is, the Turks and Tartars, dominate.' Josephus wishes Mesech to be the Cappadocians, and from them the Ottoman made the beginning of his empire, having set out from Bithynia and Cappadocia to occupy the rest of Asia, so that he is rightly called Prince of Mesech and Thubal, that is, of the Iberians; not of the Spaniards, but of those who are neighbors to the Pontus and Colchis, whom the Moschici mountains separated from Armenia, as Strabo writes in book 1. And undoubtedly from Mesech or these Moschici mountains, the Muscovites drew their name, who are to be considered either Scythians or not unlike the Scythians. Philippus Nicolai is almost similar, who however makes Gomer the Germans and Heneti, and the house of Togarmah the nation of the Tartars: he understands the sides of the North as those dwelling towards the North with all their strength, with all their hordes or armies. He thinks, however, that the Germans and Heneti are pointed out by the Arian, Macedonian, Anabaptist, Calvinist, and similar heresies preparing the way for the Mahometans. B. Hülfemannus observes that all interpreters understand the northern peoples by Gomer and Togarmah, but the southern ones by verse 5, and that they are the Vandals. Therefore Gomer are not the Galatians, nor are the House of Togarmah the Phrygians or Paphlagonians, as Grotius wishes with Junius, Polanus, Piscator, Sanctius, Tirinus, and Maldonado, because the Galatians, a people of Asia, and the inhabitants of Phrygia in lesser Armenia do not occupy the side of the North of the terrestrial sphere, but of the East and South. Whence R. Jonathan, and the Jerusalem Targum, as also Emanuel Saa and Menochius, understand the Germans here.

Seventh, therefore, the situation of the place does not fit the Grotian interpretation. For the fact that he takes the peoples to the North, with respect to Judea, does not fit at all. Because the prophecy was established in Chaldea, not in Judea. And therefore the designation of places towards the South, and to the sides of the North, must be understood with respect to Chaldea, and with respect to the whole terrestrial sphere, not by reason of Judea. Add that St. John, who was established in Patmos, an Asian island, defines the dimensions of the places of the prophecies in the same way in chapter 20, although Ezekiel was established under a far different region of the sky, from which it is manifest that the partition of the whole sphere is regarded. It is therefore not to the point that the Galatians and Phrygians are considered northern by reason of Judea, because the discourse is about those who are northern with respect to Chaldea, or the whole sphere.

Eighth, the place of invasion is not Palestine precisely, as the Grotian opinion infers, but by the mountains of Israel are understood the dwellings of the Church, and by the Israelites the Christians, as is evident from the sanctification and glorification of all the faithful without exception; who can by no means be restricted to the Jews, c. 39, 24, as also from the parallel passages of the Prophet, who, when he prophesies about future benefits, never understands the Judean Palestinians adequately by the mountains of Israel or the land of Israel, but the descendants of the Church of Israel, Rom. 5, 6, seqq., Gal. 4, 18. Compare c. 36, 23, c. 37, 21, seqq.

Ninth, the calculation of time does not agree. For these things are said to be about to happen IN THE LATTER YEARS, IN THE LATTER DAYS c. 38. 8, 16. which is likewise to be taken universally, not with regard to a specific people. In the latest time of the whole world, not long before the final day. It is false, what Grotius affirms: that this Hebrew expression signifies nothing other than AT LENGTH. For he could bring forward no parallel passage: and therefore he retreated to this evasion in vain; since it is in the open that by this phrase the latest ages are understood, where no determination is held in the text. Therefore, it is not permitted to refer this to the times of Antiochus, which in no way can be considered the latest. For the blessed Hülsemann notes the singular periphrasis of this time, which is, namely, such that not one or another of the Prophets, but all from ancient days have predicted it, such a periphrasis is never added to a particular disaster of the kind that was that which happened under the Maccabees, but is proper to events about to be under the New Testament Luc. 1, 70. Act. 3, 18. 21. c. 10, 43. Compare Dan. 9, 10.

Tenth, the persecution of Antiochus was not as great as the Prophet predicts here: See v. 23. & compare Ez. 29, 4. Ier. 12, 41. Most ineptly are these drawn by Sanchez and his followers, in the judgment of the blessed Hülsemann, to the persecution of Antiochus, in the time of the Maccabees 2. Macc. 9, 12. For this hyperbole is too vehement to be accommodated to that storm, concerning the casting away of the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the beasts of the field, and all reptiles.

Eleventh, the slaughter of Antiochus does not correspond to the present prophecy: For neither did the allies of Antiochus consume themselves in internal strife, as is said here: The sword of each one shall be directed against his brother, nor were they destroyed by heavenly fire and brimstone, nor those things which are predicted in chapter XXXIX. verse 7. following, concerning Gog, or those which in verse 9. following, concerning the inhabitants in the cities of Israel preparing fire to consume the weapons that are held, they agree with the slaughter of Antiochus; whence this Sanctius stuck in the water. The Jesuit Sanctius indeed twists that burning of weapons to the victory of the Jews over Nicanor, 2 Macc. 8:27, but there the weapons and spoils of the enemies are said to be gathered and divided among the widows, not indeed burned: nor was such a great slaughter of peoples made then, or such a great quantity of weapons acquired, which might in any way correspond to this hyperbole. B. Osiander, from a comparison with Rev. 20 concerning the sending of divine fire, concludes that Gog is to be destroyed by tempests rather than by weapons.

Twelfth, the arrival of Gog, through the land which is without a wall, ch. 38:11, is taken metaphorically and comparatively without sufficient reason: which has no fortifications, namely such as could resist so many forces and machines: and therefore Sanctius takes it concerning Judea after the devastation of Nebuchadnezzar, being destitute of fortified citadels and cities: but it is sufficiently evident from Neh. 4 that the city of Jerusalem had been fortified. Other towns were also fortified: 1 Macc. 5:27. Wherefore Osiander paraphrases it thus: I will ascend to the land of Israel (of the Christians) which is without a wall: I will invade them in those regions which do not have many cities and fortified citadels: (such is Poland) I will come suddenly and beyond expectation, upon those resting and dwelling securely: I will oppress them, fearing nothing of the sort: (these) for all dwell without a wall, the bars and gates are not to them such as could sustain the attack of so great an enemy.

Thirteenth, the place of the Gogitic slaughter is wrongly established at Jerusalem. Of which no trace is found here. Therefore that new translation of verse 16 by Grotius is vain: The name of the city is Amona, and they shall cleanse the land: That multitude (of the slain) will give a name to the city (of Jerusalem) after the land shall have been cleansed. Since bones will no longer be seen testifying to the victory, the city of Jerusalem will nevertheless obtain fame from it, as the victor of the nations. Which, as being merely precarious, is deservedly rejected. B. Gesner, Disput. de Turc. 3, p. 210, has this to say about that place: The place will be within the Christian world in a valley, where travelers make their journey to the sea, or the Ocean of the East, which from the event will then also obtain a name and be called Geh Hamon Gog, that is, the valley of the Gogitic multitude. To inquire for more and clearer things about that most foul valley, and the sepulcher of the Turkish dogs, and about the city of Hamona, is of an idle and curious mind, since these and things of this kind cannot be known before they happen.

Fourteenth, the illuminated day, in which the Lord is glorified, ch. 39:13, is rashly transferred to the day of the dedication. For the day of punishment to be taken from Gog is called the day of the glorification of the Lord, because then the illustrious glory of divine justice appeared.

Fifteenth, the promise concerning the reduction and conversion of the captivity of the people and of all Israel, which is subjoined toward the end of ch. 39, and concerning the security of the Israelites, does not agree with the times of Antiochus. For these followed after the liberation from captivity, whence Sanctius here invents a hyperbaton, as if those things which were said in ch. 38 and 39 concerning Gog were placed in a parenthesis, which is indeed vain: for it is a mere fiction. Grotius takes it concerning those oppressed by Antiochus being restored to the possession of the city and temple. But these do not correspond to the magnitude of the promises: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Now I will bring back the captivity of Jacob and will have mercy on all the house of Israel, and will take up zeal for my holy name. The Lord wishes to have mercy on all the house of Israel, and to bring them back, as he adds afterwards, from the peoples: and to gather them from the lands of their enemies, and to be sanctified in them in the eyes of many nations. Because they will say, that I (says the Lord) am the Lord their God, in that I have trans-

ferred them indeed into the nations and yet have gathered them (again) upon their own land, and have not left any one of them there. What have these to do with the times of Antiochus, and the constitution of the temple? But it is manifest that the Holy Spirit, according to the solemn custom in prophecies, exhibits new things under the phrases of the Old Testament, which are to be exhibited under the times of the New Testament; that he transfers those things which happen under the Israelitic Church to the Christian Church, the type to the antitype, and refers the reduction from the Babylonian captivity to the spiritual liberation and conversion. Such a restitution indeed this Holy Spirit predicted here, in which not even one exile remains, ch. 39:28. Of which it is certain that there has been none in this age, nor will there be any. Blessed Osiander wishes to look to the liberation of Christians from the Anti-Christian tyranny, which was harsher than the Babylonian. For since, having been liberated from it, they live too securely and loosen the reins to the flesh more freely than they ought, heavy punishments cannot but follow, which are to be inflicted by Gog and Magog. But because they will finally know and acknowledge, says the Lord, that I am the Lord their God, in whom alone they can find help: who indeed delivered them into captivity, but yet again liberated them, therefore in those final straits, in the incursion of Gog, they will flee to me with their prayers, and will be saved. And after this I WILL NOT HIDE MY FACE ANY MORE FROM THEM; this will be the final persecution which will befall them from Gog: In the future I will spare them: BECAUSE I HAVE POURED OUT MY SPIRIT UPON ALL THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL, SAYS THE LORD GOD. That is, because Christians (in reality, not in name only) illuminated by the Holy Spirit will order their life according to the prescription of my word. But when the final persecution under Gog has been overcome, the pious will indeed persevere in the true faith, even if they are very few in number: but the rest will rush into the utmost carnal security, and in it will be suddenly overwhelmed by the coming of Christ, but the pious, changed in the twinkling of an eye, will be caught up to meet Christ in the clouds, and will always be with the Lord 1 Thess. 4. Thus Osiander: who nevertheless interprets the same of Gog regarding the bodily slaughter of the Turks, which they are to suffer from Christians, whereas the literal sense (τὸ ῥητὸν) of it is very emphatic in ch. 38, 21. c. 39, 4. 5. 6. seqq.

Whence a new (sixteenth) argument, that the slaughter of Antiochus cannot be understood: because it treats of the final slaughter of the enemies of the Church, and GOD protests, not with respect to some at least who have seriously repented (as Grotius wishes), but with respect to the whole Church and his entire people: I WILL NOT HIDE MY FACE ANY MORE FROM THEM.

Nor can these things be accepted regarding external peace, which although it shone upon the Jews under Simon 1 Macc. 14, nevertheless barely lasted five years, with Antiochus ravaging Judea anew through Cendebaeus, and after the death of Simon, Antiochus Soter subduing the whole land. Here, however, two other corruptions are to be noted in passing (ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ). The former, that he deduces repentance for the abandoned law v. 26 from the passage Dan. 12, 2, where the discourse is about eternal disgrace, having no connection at all with repentance. The latter, that to pour out the Spirit upon all the house of Israel signifies to pursue with love; which gloss, hitherto unheard of, Grotius does not prove (for the passages 1 Sam. XVIII. 1, Ex. 35, 20, Is. 58, 20 do not pertain to the matter at all). But that this phrase denotes spiritual gifts

That the Holy Spirit is communicated abundantly and copiously, both the passage adduced by Grotius, Isaiah 32:16, and other parallels in Joel 2, Zechariah 12, and Isaiah 44:5, teach. But this by the way: we return to the main subject.

To these arguments already adduced, let there also be added, most recently, the Apocalyptic repetition: since this prediction is not alleged by mere allusion in Revelation 20, but it is indicated by the Holy Spirit that the same is now to be fulfilled toward the end of the age. Whence it cannot be considered to have been fulfilled in the Seleucids. Not to mention that the authors of this opinion do not agree about it. Some holding Antiochus to be Gog, while others establish Gog as Halyattes, the father of Croesus, who ruled over the Albanians and Cappadocians, which is the opinion of Junius in his Commentary: for he calls Meshech Cappadocia, and Tubal Albania. And so much for that opinion which Grotius chose: that Antiochus is understood; ours, that the discourse is about the Turk, was proved primarily from our own by the blessed Dr. Gesner, Disputation 1 on the Turk, which is contained in the decade of disputations. (1) By name, since it is evident from the Genealogy of the Turkish Sultans that they trace their lineage from Japheth, so that Gokelp descends from Oguz, who was also called Gog Elp and Gog Chan, and many princes who were known by the appellation Gog and Og or Ogoza (as by this appellation of Gog the Holy Spirit wished to show the Turkish nation), and thence the origin of the Osmanlis comes. This, therefore, according to the blessed Gesner, is what the Holy Spirit says through Ezekiel about the Gogazian family, that it is נשיא ראש, an elevated and sublime head, or Prince; with Meshech and Tubal, since this family, having oppressed all other families in the Mahometan kingdom, raised its own head and obtained the principality. (2) From habit and attire: That they are said to be well adorned and equipped, all most skilled in equestrian matters, using shields, bows, and scimitars: since no nation under the sun hostile to Christians is so equipped in every military matter, and wears arms of such form and kind, except the Mahometan rabble. (3) That Gog and Magog is called Prince in Meshech and Tubal. But Meshech is a nation of Scythians, which the ancients called Moschians, as testified by Strabo, book 12 of Geography, and Xenophon, book 5 of the Education of Cyrus; we do not call them Muscovites. But Tubal designates the Tartars, who are themselves also Scythians, and Josephus testifies that the Magogians are called Scythians; and that the Turks are not the least of the Scythians is evident from Mela, book 1, last chapter, Pliny, book 6, chapter 7, and Ptolemy: who, together with the Armenians and Russians (likewise Scythians), around the year of Christ 1202, poured into Asia with an incredible army, subdued the power of the Saracens, suppressed the Mahometan stock, and gave origin to the Ogugian or Oguian family, which is that of the Ottomans, as testified by Leunclavius, book 11 of the History of the Mussulmans, Lonicerus, Volume 1 of the Turkish Annals, and others. (4) Gog and Magog leads in his army Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans, or Africans, and indeed now the Turkish tyranny has not only flowed together from those nations: but there is no King or Prince today more hostile to the Christian name, to whose dominion those peoples are subject, or who can conscript an army from them, except the Mahometan Sultan, who has a prefect in the Ethiopian city of Modin with ten thousand horsemen perpetually ready for battle, and since he depopulates the Persians with perpetual incursions, he also has many Persians in his army. (5) That the Mahometans obtained the principality of Arabia (to which Dedan is near), extended the borders of their tyranny very far through Asia, and the Northern peoples, Cimbri, Scythians, Moschi, Tartars, who formerly came under the appellation of Turks, or Turkorum or Zurkorum, that is, Nomads, and were satisfied by the sons of Japheth, Gomer, Magog, Tubal, Mosoch, and the grandson Thogarma, especially the Idumeans (whose city was Dedan) joined themselves to them, as Galatinus testifies, book 4, chapter 28, and Methodius.

(6) That the little horn rising from the midst of the ten horns in Daniel 7, casting down three primary horns by its speed and strength, and equipped with human eyes and a blasphemous mouth, designates the Turkish tyranny, with which place of Daniel the present prophecy agrees to a hair, whether you consider the origin, or the time, or the power, ferocity, or blasphemy: since that little horn must have arisen toward the end of the fourth Monarchy, immediately before the last judgment: and Ezekiel introduced Gog as the final enemy of the Church.

(7) That John, in the interpretation of this prophecy in chapter 20 of Revelation, hands down most evident signs from which the Turk can be recognized: namely, that this enemy is to come after the detection of the whoredom of the Babylonian harlot, shortly before the consummation of the age, that the devil is to gather the nations for the destruction of the Church from all four parts, and is to invade the Church, or the camps of God: All of which the blessed Gesner judges to apply to the Turkish tyrant in such a way that they apply to no other.

But as for the nation which the Gogucian cohort is to invade, he shows in Disputation 3 on the Turk, chapter 2, that this slaughter is to be feared by no people more than the Germans, by four arguments which he judges to be most evident: (1) That it is said that in the last times the people to be invaded is one that has been rescued from the sword, which, whether it be understood of the swords of the Mussulmans and the slaughters of the Tartars from whom they trace their origin, or understood of the cruelty of the Roman Anti-Christ, applies most to the Germans, as testified by the slaughter at Liegnitz in the year 1241 by the Tartars, from the slaughter often inflicted by the Turks in Transylvania, Hungary, and Austria, and also the truculence of the Roman Anti-Christ, from which, if the blessed Gesner had reached our times by living, he would have pronounced more clearly how the people of God were rescued, and how that people was rescued from the sword. (2) That that nation is gathered from many peoples. For in Germany in this last century the truth of the Gospel first shone forth from Papal darkness, and very many peoples have been gathered to our orthodox confession, and associated by faith and profession. (3) That Germany is truly that illustrious mount of Zion, to which peoples have flowed together, and that the Germans acknowledge Germany as the Metropolis of the Churches of this last century, from whence colonies have been led forth into the remaining nations, and as it were daughters have been propagated. This city, therefore, is beloved of God, which St. John in Apoc. 20 predicted would be surrounded by a siege by Gog. (4) That Daniel handed down that concerning the Mahometan little horn, he would turn all his counsels toward the destruction of the fourth Monarchy, the leadership of which has come to the Germans, and experience testifies that nothing else is sought by him than the ruin of the German empire. To this point, the blessed Gesner also refers that ancient, as he speaks, prophecy of many outstanding men, who have always feared that the Turk, just as he obtained the strength of his army from the Northern regions, from Tartary and Muscovy, and poured through Poland and Sarmatia into Thrace, Macedonia, Greece, and Hungary, so too would invade our lands from the same places by the just judgment of God. All of which our Gesner, of blessed memory, has executed at greater length.

But as to what Bellarmin objects, that Gog will come on the last day and will not last long, whereas the kingdom of the Saracens has already lasted for almost a thousand years, B. Cluverus answers this by saying that the whole time of the New Testament is called the last time by the Prophets, and that here it is not properly the kingdom of the Saracens, that is, Seba, Dedan, and Agar, that is understood; but the Scythian [kingdom], whose princes are Gog and Magog, and of which the Saracen Arabs eventually become a part. Because the Saracens did not found any one universal Empire, but scattered, they infested now these provinces, now those, and were often punished with the most severe slaughter by the Christians, and were even forced to pay tribute to the Emperors: and the supreme power of the world remained with the Christians, until the prince of the world was released from his prison, Apoc. 20. and the Ottoman or Turkish empire broke out, and thus gathered the remaining infidel nations once again for war against the Church: whence Augustine warns in book 20 of the City of God, chapter 11, that these nations are not to be interpreted as referring only to some Barbarians, since the whole world is signified, but that the last and universal persecution of the holy city is described here, by the whole and universal city of the devil. For nations placed in certain corners of the earth cannot surround the whole Church, but those which are in all the corners of the world, nations [surround] the whole city of God placed in those same four parts. Therefore, as Cluverus notes, Ezekiel says that the sword is to be summoned against Gog in all the mountains of Israel. For all the mountains of Israel are all those places where the Israelites, that is, the Christians, have placed their garrisons and hold their assemblies. And so much for those prophecies, sufficiently obscure, but made more confused by the variety of interpretations, and especially against the Grotian τὴν ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν [private interpretation]. Which we shall now append in its entirety. Vers. 2. SET THY FACE AGAINST GOG] Lest the Jews, who had understood that that long happiness after their return was promised to them, should wonder if any trouble happened afterwards, God wished to warn them that times would not be lacking in which the faith of the good would be tested: which was never done more than under Antiochus the Illustrious, about whom Daniel also predicted so much, so that pious minds might be armed by the prediction itself. God therefore wishes through Ezekiel that this also be predicted, that if any kings should harass the Jewish people on account of their religion, it would not go unpunished for them. He designates, however, Antiochus from the peoples whom he possessed. Therefore the best version is 'to Gog and Magog, the prince of the land'. Polychronius on this passage: Ἐπάγ' γὲν ἄρχοντα Ῥὼς κὶ Θοβὲλ, ἵνα εἴπῃ ἰδὲ ἐκ διαφόρων συλλεγόντας ἐθνῶν, ὥσε κὶ πρὸς ἑνα ὡς οἶμαι Ἀντίοχον ὁ διαλέγεται, ἀλλὰ πρὸς ἀυτὸ τὸ σύστημα. Before the times of Ezekiel, Gyges had possessed Lydia and the neighboring places of Asia, from whom the Gygaean lake has its name, whence in antiquity the whole region was named. Homer is older than Ezekiel: Ὑιὲ Πα- λαιμένεος ῷ Γυγαίη τέκε λίμνη. The Hebrew Holem is usually put for υ, as can be seen in the name of Cyrus. Lydia with the neighboring places was in the part of the Lagidae, from whose family was Antiochus. See Appian in the Syriaca, where among those things which were possessed by Antiochus the Great, he places Sardis, Pergamum, Phrygia, Aeolia, and Ionia of Asia. But it is named Gygaea in the first place, because of the immense riches which had made that region most famous. Archilochus: Οὐ μοι τὰ Γύγεω τῶ πολυχρύσε μέλει. Anacreon: Οὐ μοι μέλει Γύγαο Τῶ Σαρδίων ἄνακτος. Alpheus of Mitylene: Οὐκ ἔθελον πολύχρυσον οἷα Γύγης. And the proverb among the Greeks: Γύγεω τάλαντα. See also Herodotus in the first book, and Pausanias in the Laconica. THE LAND OF MAGOG] Syria, in which Hieropolis is, called Magog. Plin. 6, 23. Everyone knows that Syria belonged to Antiochus and his ancestors. See Livy, Polybius, Appian. PRINCE OF THE HEAD OF MESHECH] You would translate it better, as we began to say, 'Gog and the prince of the land of Magog, the head of Mazaca': That is, of Cappadocia. The Greeks thought ראש was a proper name, and translated it Ῥως, which later Greeks ineptly dragged to Russia.

Vers. of the same.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVIII. Adversus persequutiones Ecclesiæ gravissimas à Gogo, qui terrorem maximum incutiet, solatium, quod Dominus super eum gla- dium advocaturus, & variis modis ipsum puniturus sit.

Vers. 1. PONE FACIEM TVAM CONTRA GOG] De- signat Antiochum ex populis, quos possidebat. Itaque versio optima est ad Gog & Magog terræ principem.

QUod hæc duo capita refert Grotius ad Mac- cabæorum tempora ex præconcepta opinio- ne procedit; quod nempe præcedens vaticinium de Zorobabele agat, & de conservatione politiæ Ju- daicæ per diuturnum tempus, quasi voluerit Deus monere Judæos, ne meram felicitatem sibi inde promitterent, non defuturas calamitates. Lubri- cum, imo nullum est illud fundamentum. Præce- dens enim vaticinium non de Zorobabele, sed de Messia egit. Non diffitemur autem hanc de Gog & Magog Prophetiam valde obscuram, & variis autorum expositionibus obnoxiam esse, quarum plerasque recenset Bellarminus lib. III. de Rom. Pont. cap. 17. E quibus primo inepti sunt, qui prælia Diaboli & angelorum ejus cum bonis angelis in cælo notari apud Hieronymum putarunt, quum Prophetia de futuris proponatur; & prælia non inter angelos, sed inter homines gerenda exhi- beantur. A quibus non multum abeunt, qui apud Maldonatum hæc referunt ad prælia Diaboli, olim in cælis futura contra electos & glorificatos, & per diversas gentes diversos ordines Diabolorum intelli- gunt; quas nænias suis autoribus relinquimus.

Neque secundo convenit S. Augustini inter- pretatio, qui per Gogum intelligit Diabolum, per Magog autem Anti-Christi exercitum: quia Gog est Princeps aliquis terrenus Dux exercitus, morti obnoxius.

Tertio Judæorum sententia, quod Messias ceu Rex terrenus, cujus adventum adhuc expectant, bellum corporale contra Gog & Magog gesturus, & hanc ipsorum insignem cladem, quæ operose ab Ezechiele describitur, effecturus sit, ex ipso textu facile reprobatur; quia nullo prorsus verbo Messia hic mentio facta est per integra duo capita, quæ de prælio Gogitico agunt, neq; Messias aliquis terre- nus, qualem Judæi fingunt, sed Jehovah in acie constituitur contra Gogum c. 38, 21. c. 39, 2. 3. 4. 22. Quum sic ergo hostis hujus gravissimi populi Do- mini debellator, quem introducit Propheta, Jeho- vah sit, Messiam oportet Jehovam esse, agnoscant, si ipsum eidem hic opponi velint Judæi. Nullus e- nim alius exertis verbis eidem opponitur à Pro- pheta, nisi Jehovah. Taceo ea quæ de gemino Mes- sia hic commenti sunt Judæi, altero filio Josephi, cui nomen Nehemias filius Husiel, altero Davidis filio, quorum ille in hoc prælio Gogitico occidendus sit: iste succedens ei, regnum sit occupaturus: De quibus legere est in Targum in Cant. 4. apud A- benezra in Zach. 9, 1. & alios passim. Auctor As- kath Rochel sub signo nono, somnia sua de hisce ita expandit; Clanget Michael clangorem magnum, quo sepulchra mortuorum aperientur Hierosolymis, e- osq; Deus Bened. vitæ restituet. Messias enim Ben Da- vid, & cum ipso Elias Propheta è mortuis suscitabunt Messiam Ben Joseph, qui sub portis Hierosolymæ asser- vabatur. Deinde mittent Messiam Ben David ad col- ligendas Judæorum reliquias in omnibus terris disper- sas. Et confestim omnes gentium Reges totius orbis Israelitas humeris suis impositos ad Deum deducent, &c. Ejusdem & hæc sunt: Dicunt autem Rabbi- nib. m. prius venturum, Messiam Ben Joseph ad col- ligendas captivitates, & tum fore bella Gog & Ma- gog, prout exponunt cap. Roch. exaltatus super omnia in caput (ex 1. Paral. 29, 11.) Exaltatus in ca- put, hæc sunt bella Gog & Magog, juxta illud Ezech. 38, 3. Ecce me contra te: Et Gog & Magog, Princeps primarie Meschechi & Thubalis. Sic capit. Ha- chalil de isto tempore exponunt Scripturam, quæ ex- tat Zach. 12, 11. Planget unaquæq; familia seorsim &c. propter mortem scilicet Messiæ Ben Joseph, qui occidetur. Et cap. 1. eod. Megilla, ad eundem re- fertur id quod dicitur vers. 11. Die illo magnus erit plan- ctus Hierosolymis &c. Portenta alia de hisce ita proponit R. Manasse Ben Israel lib. Spes Israelis p. 78. Tempore illo X. tribus venient Hierosolyma, sub ductu principis, quem Rabbini nonnulli in Talmud, & Paraphrasi Chaldæa aliquot in locis vocant Messiam filium Joseph; Et alibi Messiam filium Ephraim, qui cæsus in ultimo bello Gog & Magog, ostendet se esse (forte legendum non esse) Messiam filium Davidis, qui erit, ut dicunt Oseas & Ezechiel, princeps æter- nus omnium 12. Tribuum. Messiæ istius filii E- phraimi mentionem faciunt multis in locis sapien- tes, maxime vero in Thalmud Babylonico in tractatu Suca c. 5. ubi moriturum eum ajunt in ultimo bello Gog & Magog, & ita explicant c. 13. Prophetæ Zachariæ: Et aspicient ad me, quem confixerunt, plangentq; super eo, ut solet super unigenito filio. Addunt etiam, quod quatuor Duces, de quibus Propheta idem loquitur c. 11. sunt Messias filius Davidis, Messias fi- lius Josephi, Propheta Elias, & summus sacerdos, quæ quatuor istæ dignitates sunt, quæ in isto seculo bea- to ostendent potentiam suam. Advertite autem, quod aliquando vocent Messiam filium Ephraimi, aliquan- do Josephi: Prodibit enim ex tribu Ephraimi, & erit Dux omnium decem tribuum, nomen Ephraimo dan- tium, propterea quod primus eorum Rex Ierobeam ex ista tribu fuit. Non sine ratione vocant ipsum filium Josephi; ipse enim erat verus typus domui Israelis pro- pter incarcerationem suam, ac subsequentem felicita- tem. Adde, quod tamdiu fratres suos latuerit, ut plane iis ignoraretur: prorsus ut hodie decem tribus, quæ, ut- ut captivitas se dicant, postmodum tamen ad summum felicitatis fastigium ascendent eodem, ac Joseph, mo- do. Iste Messias Josephi morietur in prœlio Gog & Ma- gog, & postea resurget, ut fungatur dignitate ista, non sceptro quidem Regis, sed munere tantum vice regis, ut Josephus in Ægypto, eo quod imperium domus Israe- lis, quod cecidit sub regno Oseæ filii Ela, non resurget, ut ait Propheta Amos c. 5. v. 2. non restaurabitur igi- tur regnum decem tribuum, ut monet Ezech. c. 37. sub imperio Messiæ filii Davidis, qui erit æternus, & per mortem Messiæ, filii Josephi, agnoscent X. tribus Deum nolle, ut plures habeant, præter unum, principes; &c. Idem Menasse lib. 3. de resur. c. 5. hæc tradit; O- mnes Rabini in eo consentiunt, Israelitas post reditum in patriam suam, qui redemptionis tempore futurus est, non plane & perfecte omni tranquillitate, & pace fruituros, nisi demum post confectum postremum, ac ultimum bellum Gog & Magog. Futurum enim est, ut postquam Israelitæ in Palæstinam redierint, gens illa Gog & Magog ad invadendum ac occupan- dam terram illam, & quidem cum ingenti hominum multitudine, infinitisq; militum copiis, ea spe, animo- que, ut regnum atq; imperium illud sibi vindicet, non aliter quam Gothi olim Vandalig; vili turba comita- ti, opulentissima regna subjecerunt sibi, & de illis tri- umpharunt. Et quanquam forte persuasum habi- turi sint, non nisi singulari providentia divina Mo- narchiam istam Iudaicam erectam esse, forte tamen cogitabunt, eam ad tempus tantum aliquod duratu- ram esse; ac proinde eam non minus tum a se everti, ac subjugari posse, quam eversa, aut subjugata olim fuit à Nabuchodonosor & Tito Vespasiano. Hæ spe, ac fiducia armata manu invadent gentes illæ terram sanctam, eamque, expulsis iterum Israelitis, in potestatem suam conabuntur redigere. Quod conatur probare imprimis ex hoc vaticinio. Hoc autem prælium, ait Manasse, in fine mundi committetur nam postremo ac ultimo ejus die concutietur tota terra, & in partes dissoluta dissipabitur inundationibus, terræ motibus, & id genus aliis ruinis. Ac tum destruentur universa, Gog cum omnibus gentibus delebitur, & ex eorum clade, tot cadaveribus terra complebitur, ut septem mensibus opus futurum sit, ad cadavera sepelienda, & expiandam terram.

Sed commenta ἀσύσατα, anilibus fabulis ineptiora, recitasse est solidissime refutasse. Et videmus hic palam, ex mera desperatione, Manassem adventum Messiæ in finem mundi rejicere. Quo pacto illis Messias terrenus, in quem per tot secula sperarunt, nulli usui erit, neque ea, quæ de ipsius prælio hic prædicta somniant, ullatenus sibi constare poterunt. Si templi tertii, quod somniant Judæi, extructio cum adventu Messiæ conjungenda, quomodo hic ad finem mundi rejici, & cum illo concurrere potest, nisi forte post resurrectionem mortuorum demum & extremum judicium templum materiale extruendum dicere velint. Quod dicit quidem Manasse lib. 3. de Resurrect. c. 8. sed quam ineptum id sit, atque absonum, nemo non intelligit.

Verum, ut fabulæ illius de congressu gemini Messiæ cum Gogo textura, & origo plenius constet, subjungere ex auctore As kath Rochel ab Hulsio edito, nonnulla placet. Ita autem sub signo Messiæ septimo pag. 51. habetur: Deus mirabilium patrator prodigium ostendet in mundo: dicunt Romæ lapidem marmoreum esse puellæ formosissimæ formam referentem, qui non manu sit effectus, sed virtute divina creatus sit, ad hunc lapidem sceleratissimi ex mundi nationibus convenient, eumq́; calefacientes concumbent cum illo, Deus autem guttas seminis eorum in medio lapidis conservabit, creabitq́; creaturam in illo, ac infantis speciem formabit, tandemq́; lapide dirupto formam hominis educet, cui nomen erit Armillus, qui adversarius erit, & gentes illum vocabunt Antichristum. Longitudo ejus erit duodecim cubitorum, & inter utrumq́; oculum ejus spiramæ spatium erit; oculis profundis & rutilantibus, capillus capitis ejus erit sicut color auri, plantæ pedum ejus erunt virides, duosque habebit vertices. Hic ad impios accedet, & ipsis dicet; Messias ego sum, ego sum Deus vester, qui statim in ipsum credent, & regem sic constituent, associabuntur ipsi omnes posteri Esau.
