Reg. 25, 8. Jer. 52, 29. connectit. Daniel ergo, (& quidem solus) adventum Nebucadnezaris conjicit in tertium Jojakimi annum. Posterior Regum cum Jeremia an- num primum Nebucadnezaris inchoant à Ierosoly- mæ expugnatione facta anno quarto Jojakimi bonam partem elapso, ita ut primus Nebucadnezaris cum quarto & quinto Jojakimi concatenandus sit, & ita consequenter. Hæc qui non attendit, censente B. Behmio, in varias se præcipitem dabit difficultates. Monstravit tamen Usserius in Chronol. S. p. 30. quo- modo difficultates illæ expediri possint. Et po- sterioribus iisque sapientioribus meditationibus B. D. Behmius in Disp. de termino à quo, & ad quem LXX. annorum captivit. Babyl. Ann. 1633. Regimonti habita th. 17. agnovit primum adventus Nebucadnezaris in Judæam annum esse Jojakimi ter- tium inchoatum, quartum ineuntem.

Alium calculum init Lyra, Tostatus & Gef- nerus, ut & B. Meisnerus in Schol. Babyl. part. 1. §. 12. ut annus tertius intelligatur, à quo tributa cœpit pendere. Contraria ratione Maldonatus ad h. l. cum R. Saadia, annum tertium Jojakim indigitari vult, ex quo adversus Regem Babylonis rebellio- nem fecit, nec sub tributo, sed liber regnavit. Interpretationem putat se ex quatuor perspicuis scripturæ locis inter se collatis docere posse; sed hæc illic (apud Maldonatum) legantur. Juxta illos intelligitur annus undecimus vel ultimus Joja- kimi. Verum à pensione tributi, vel etiam rebel- lione & defectione à Rege Babylonis annos numerari, cum nulla sive istius, sive hujus mentio præcessit, inusitatum planè est; adhæc nimis durum vide- tur; annum tertium REGNI dici, & intelligi an- num regni undecimum. Ideoque præferenda omni- no prima conciliatio: secundum quam omnia pla- na esse, agnoscit B. Meisnerus, ne annum tertium cogamur aliunde supputare, quam ab initio re- gnandi, ut ipsa litera requirit. Quod vero eidem obstare putat, quod Daniel hic loquatur de illa Nebucadnezaris expeditione, qua se & alios Prin- cipum filios abduxit captivos (quam terminum respici facile agnoscimus) id obstare nobis haud videtur: non enim concedimus Jer. 52, 28. ab- ductionem illam designari, quod hic precario as- sumitur. Ibi enim de alia Nebucadnezaris expe- ditione agitur. Vide quæ ad Jer. 52, 28. diximus.

## 1:2
Vers. 2.

THE LORD DELIVERED INTO HIS HAND JEHOIAKIM KING OF JUDAH, AND PART OF THE VESSELS OF THE HOUSE OF GOD] It agrees with 2 Chron. 36:6, 7.

AND HE CARRIED THEM INTO THE LAND OF SHINAR] Which is also in the Greek Σενναὰρ, and in Pliny and Ptolemy Singara, as we said in the Annotations to the first book on the Christian Religion.

Babylon, as is evident from Gen. 10:10, ch. 11:2, 9, the Septuagint Interpreters at Is. 11:11, Zech. 5:11, the Targumim likewise, and Hestiaeus of Miletus in Josephus, book 1, ch. 5.

INTO THE HOUSE OF HIS GOD] Of his principal god, that is, Bel. See the passage of Hecataeus in the first book of Josephus against Apion, and Jer. 51:44. As also Isa. 46, 1. Whom Vossius, lib. 1. Idol. c. 16. and Selden, l. 2. de Diis Syr. c. 1. teaches to have been Mars; although here c. 6. p. 334. he also teaches that Bel was called the Sun by the Assyrians and Chaldeans: which is more likely: because it denotes the supreme Lord by contraction from בעל: Concerning the magnificence of this temple, and its treasures, see Diodorus Siculus, l. 2.

But why were these gifts from the spoils consecrated only to Bel, and not also to the idol Nebo, Isa. 46, 1, from whom Nebuchadnezzar had his name, nor to the idol Merodach, Jer. 50, 2, from whom he wished his son to be named?

Latin:

Vers. 2.

TRADIDIT DOMINUS IN MANU EJUS JOACIM REGEM JUDÆ, ET PARTEM VASO- RUM DOMUS DEI] Convenit cum 2. Paral. 36, 6. 7.

ET ASPORTAVIT EA IN TERRAM SENNA- AR] Quæ etiam in Græco Σενναὰρ, Plinio & Ptolemæo Sin- gara, ut diximus Annotatis ad primum librum de Religio- ne Christiana.

Babylonem, ut è Gen. 10, 10. c. 11, 2. 9. Septua- ginta Interpp. ad Ef. 11, 11. Zach. 5, 11. Targumim i- tem, & Histiæo Milesio apud Joseph. l. 1. c. 5. constat.

IN DOMUM DEI SUI ] Præcipui dei, id est, Beli. Vide Hecatæi locum priore Josephi libro contra Appionem, & Jer. 51, 44. Ut & Esa. 46, 1. Quem Martem fuisse Vos- sius lib. 1. Idol. c. 16. & Selden. l. 2. de Diis Syr. c. 1. docet; licet hic c. 6. p. 334. etiam Solem Assyriis & Chaldæis Belum dictum doceat: quod verisimilius est: quia Dominum supremum per contractionem è בעל notat: De templi hujus magnificentia, & thesauris vid. Diodor. Sicul. l. 2.

Cur vero Belo tantum consecrata ex manu- biishisce munera, non etiam idolo Nebo Es. 46, 1. unde nomen erat Nebucadnezari, nec idolo Me- rodach Jer. 50, 2. à quo denominari voluit filium suum?

## 1:3
Verse 3.

MASTER OF THE EUNUCHS] The kings of the East used the services of such men in their houses to preserve the modesty of their women.

The Hebrew word סריס denotes not only a castrated person, but also a more confidential minister, as R. Jeschua, Lyranus, Calvin, Junius, Maldonatus, and others have observed. Compare Gen. 37, 36. c. 39, 1. c. 40, 2, 7. 1 Sam. 8, 15. 1 Kings 22, 9. 2 Chron. 18, 8. 2 Kings 25, 14. Jer. 52, 25. Nor is it likely that those סריסים of David, 1 Chron. 28, 1, were castrated; for that is ἄνομον, Deut. 23, 1, not to mention that some make not that meaning of a castrated person, Isa. 46, 3, but this meaning of a chief minister, the primary and proper one for both this word סריס and the Greek εὐνῦχος, which they derive from εὖ νῶς and ἔχειν, because he is of proven virtue: which Greek word others prefer to derive from εὔνη, a bed, and ἔχειν, to guard. Wrongly, therefore, does Cornelius conclude from this word that Daniel was castrated: who is not even called by that name, but is only said to have been committed to the master of the סריסים. Junius translates it prefect of the praetorium. Luther, with the Belgian, translates it: Chief of the chamberlains.

AND OF THE ROYAL SEED] As Isaiah had predicted, 39, 7.

AND OF THE TYRANTS] Symmachus translates it Parthians, not aptly: the same interpreter translates it 'the noble' here, Esther 1, 3, and 'tyrants', as here, Esth. 6, 9. In which places of Esther the Chaldean interpreter has פַּרתְּכַיָא. Is this from the Greek word πρώτων?

Aben Ezra takes it for a foreign word, and interprets it סגנים, primates. R. Solomon Jarchi on Esther calls it Persian. Hottinger likewise, l. 1. Smegm. p. 77, explaining it as 'Magnificent' (as Kimchi does 'illustrious' or 'magnates'). Drusius notes that it is a title of dignity among the Persians and Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

PRÆPOSITO EUNUCHORUM] Talium opera in domo sua utebantur reges Orientis ad servandam mu- lierum pudicitiam.

Vox Ebræa סריס non tantum castratum no- tat, sed etiam secretiorem ministrum, ut R. Jeschua, Lyranus, Calvinus, Junius, Maldonatus, aliique ob- servarunt. Cons. Gen. 37, 36. c. 39, 1. c. 40, 2, 7. 1. Sam. 8, 15. 1. Reg. 22, 9. 2. Par. 18, 8. 2. Reg. 25, 14. Jer. 52, 25. Neque verisimile est סריסים illos Da- vidis 1. Par. 28, 1. castratos fuisse; id enim ἄνομον, Deut. 23, 1. ut taceam, quod nonnulli non illam ca- strati Es. 46, 3. sed hanc præcipui ministri significa- tionem & voci huic סריס & Græcæ εὐνῦχος, quam ab εὖ νῶς & ἔχειν deducunt, quod sit spectatæ virtutis, faciant primariam, & propriam: quam vero Græcam vocem alii malunt ab εὔνη cubile & ἔ- χειν custodire derivare. Perperam ergo ex hac voce Cornelius colligit Danielem castratum fuisse: qui ne quidem ita vocatur, sed tantum præposito סריסים commissus dicitur. Junius reddit præfe- ctum prætorii. Luther. cum Belg. Obersten der Cämmerer.

ET DE SEMINE REGIO] Ut prædixerat Esaias 39, 7.

ET TYRANNORUM] פרתמים Parthos vertit Symmachus, non apposite: inclytos vertit hic idem inter- pres Estheræ 1, 3. tyrannos, ut hic, Esth. 6, 9. In qui- bus Estheræ locis Chaldæus interpres habet פַּרתְּכַיָא. An hoc ex Græca voce πρώτων;

Abenesra habet pro voce peregrina, & inter- pretatur סגנים primates. Persicam dicit R. Salom. Jarchi ad Esth. Hottingerus item l. 1. Smegm. p. 77. exponens Magnificus (uti Kimchius illustres vel magnates.) Drusius nomen dignitatis apud Persas & Chaldæos esse notat.

## 1:4
Vers. 4. CHILDREN] νεανίσκες (neaniskes) in Greek, that is, youths, which fits well with what follows.

IN WHOM THERE SHOULD BE NO BLEMISH] מוּם signifies every defect, such as a defect of a limb, or something dislocated or distorted. See Levit. 21, 6. The Greek interpreters are accustomed to translate it μῶμον: for this Greek word also comes from that Oriental one.

HANDSOME IN APPEARANCE] For a beautiful face is a silent recommendation, and from it one is also accustomed to judge of character.

Which GOD so directed that through these youths in the court, sincere religion and the salvation of the Jews might eventually be promoted. See ch. 2, 47; ch. 3, 28, 29; ch. 4, 14; ch. 6, 27.

AND LEARNED IN ALL WISDOM, CAUTIOUS IN KNOWLEDGE, AND TAUGHT IN DISCIPLINE] Namely, in those things which they could have learned in Judea. By wisdom, it seems, the law of Moses should be understood: by prudence (for so the Hebrews translate דעת) those admonitions concerning morals, family affairs, and civil matters, such as are many in Solomon: but by discipline, that is, מדע, the arts of measuring, numbering, and the knowledge of history.

The name of wisdom חכמה is more correctly understood as the knowledge of divine and sublime things, or Theology as a whole, than as the law of Moses alone; דעת of knowledge as the acquaintance with Theoretical Philosophy, מדע of discipline as the acquaintance with Practical Philosophy: just as the LXX translated συνιέντας ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ, καὶ γινώσκοντας γνῶσιν, καὶ διανοουμένους φρόνησιν, understanding wisdom, knowing knowledge, perceiving prudence: Abenezra understands by the first, erudition; by the second, the quickness of the mind to perceive things; by the third, the ability to express things perceived by the mind.

AND WHO COULD STAND] In the Hebrew, those who have the strength to stand: ἰσχὺς in Greek: for certainly a firm constitution of body is also required for those long periods of standing in the court.

Not concerning the strength of the body, or a firm constitution for long periods of standing in the court, but concerning the ἱκανότητι (fitness) worthy of royal service and presence; who might be of a noble spirit, or of such virtues and qualities that they could stand before the King (with boldness), since they were not unworthy of the royal appearance. Concerning the body, it had already been spoken of before. Compare verse 19.

THAT HE MIGHT TEACH THEM THE LETTERS] Of letters, thus Saadia and Abenesdra.

AND THE LANGUAGE OF THE CHALDEANS] Which did not differ a little from the Hebrew. See 2 Kings 18, 26; Jeremiah 5, 15. This, however, pertained to the fact that they might be able to explain to the king those things which they themselves had learned at home, and to learn the Chaldean arts, Astrology, Architecture, and military affairs.

What kind of disciplines and arts seem to be included or implied here by the word ספר, because the books of the Chaldeans contained such things. However, that Chaldean dialect did not differ so much from the Hebrew language then, as it did later in the time of Jonathan ben Uzziel, who is believed to be contemporary with the last Prophets, let alone as the Jerusalem dialect, which occurs in the Targum Hierosolymitanum, mixed from the Ammonite, Moabite, Persian, and Greek languages, or even as that in which the books of the Kethuvim are paraphrastically explained. Some also prove from this that the letters of the Chaldeans were different (which diversity is championed by Jerome, Genebrard, Montanus, Drusius, Scaliger, Waferus, Postell, Whitaker, and others), but rashly, because by the word ספר, books are denoted, not the letters of the Chaldeans.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PUEROS] νεανίσκες Græci, id est, juvenes, quod bene convenit cum sequentibus.

IN QUIBUS NULLA ESSET MACULA] מוּם omne vitium significat, ut membri defectum, aut luxa- tum, distortumvę aliquid. Vide Levit. 21, 6. Solent Græ- ci interpretes vertere μῶμον: nam & hæc Græca vox ex il- la est Orientali.

DECOROS FORMA] Nam Formosa facies muta commendatio, Et solet inde etiam de ingenio judicari.

Quod ita direxit DEUS ut per hos juvenes in aula sinceræ religioni & Judæorum saluti ali- quando velificaretur. Vid. c. 2, 47. c. 3, 28. 29. c. 4, 14. c. 6, 27.

ET ERUDITOS OMNI SAPIENTIA, CAUTOS SCIENTIA, ET DOCTOS DISCIPLINA] Nempe iis quæ in Judæa disci potuerant. Per sapientiam videtur intel- ligenda lex Mosis: per prudentiam (ita enim Hebræi ver- tunt דעת) monita illa de moribus, re familiari, ac ci- vili, qualia multa apud Salomonem: per disciplinam ve- ro, id est, מדע, artes metiendi, numerandi, & historiæ cognitio.

Sapientiæ nomen חכמה rectius de cognitione rerum divinarum & sublimium, vel Theologia uni- versa, quam de sola Mosis lege intelligitur; דעת scientiæ de notitia Philosophiæ Theoreticæ, מדע di- sciplinæ de notitia Philosophiæ practicæ: uti LXX. verterunt συνιέντας ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ, καὶ γινώσκοντας γνῶσιν, καὶ διανοουμένους φρόνησιν, intelligentes sapien- tiam, scientes scientiam, cognoscentes prudentiam: Abenezra per primum eruditionem, per alterum ingenii ad res percipiendas celeritatem, per tertium facultatem res animo perceptas eloquendi intelligit.

ET QUI POSSENT STARE] In Hebræo, qui- bus robur ad standum: ἰσχὺς Græce: nam certe etiam firma corporis constitutio requiritur ad longas illas in aula sta- tiones.

Non de robore corporis, aut de firma consti- tutione ad longas in aula stationes, sed de ἱκανότη- τι digna regio ministerio ac conspectu; qui animo es- sent excelso, vel iis virtutibus & qualitatibus, ut coram Rege consistere (μετὰ παῤῥησίας) possent, cum aspectu regio non indigni essent. De cor- pore jam ante dictum erat. Conf. vers. 19.

UT DOCERET EOS LITERAS] Literarum, ita Saadia & Abenesdra.

ET LINGUAM CHALDÆORUM] Quæ ab He- bræa non parum differebat. Vide 2. Reg. 18, 26. Jerem. 5,15. Hoc autem eo pertinebat, ut ea quæ ipsi domi didi- cerant, regi possent exponere, & addiscere artes Chal- daicas, Astrologiam, Architecturam, ac rem militarem.

Quales disciplinæ & artes voce ספר hic com- prehendi vel insinuari videntur, quia libri Chal- dæorum talia complectebantur. Non autem adeo differebat tum Chaldaica Dialectus illa ab Ebræa lingua, uti postea tempore Jonathani Uzielis F. qui postremis Prophetis coætaneus creditur, ne- dum uti Hierosolymitana, quæ ex Ammonitica, Moabitica, Persica & Græca linguis mixta in Targ. Hierosolym. occurrit, aut etiam uti illa, qua libri כתוכים paraphrastice expositi sunt. Literas e- tiam hinc Chaldæorum diversas nonnulli probant (quam diversitatem propugnant Hieronym. Gene- brard. Montan. Drus. Scalig. Waferus, Postell. Wita- ker. alii) sed temere, quia voce ספר non literæ sed libri notantur Chaldæorum.

## 1:5
Vers. 5. THE KING APPOINTED FOR THEM A DAILY PORTION] A ration.

CONCERNING HIS FOOD AND THE WINE FROM WHICH HE HIMSELF DRANK] Namely, so that from the best foods something might be added to both his appearance and his character.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CONSTITUIT EIS REX ANNONAM] Dimensum.

DE CIBIS SUIS ET DE VINO UNDE BIBE- BAT IPSE] Nempe ut ex alimentis optimis & formæ & ingenio aliquid accederet.

## 1:6
DANIEL, ANANIAS, MISAEL, AZARIAS] In all of which names the name of God is present, with the addition of words signifying judgment, grace, contact, and help.

Latin:

DANIEL, ANANIAS, MISAEL, AZARIAS] In quibus nominibus omnibus inest Dei nomen, additis voci- bus judicium, gratiam, contactum & auxiliū significantibus.

## 1:7
Verse 7. AND THE CHIEF OF THE EUNUCHS GAVE THEM NAMES] Namely, taken from Chaldean gods, as Jacchiades notes here.

BALTASSAR] It is written here בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר, below verse 10, 1, בֵּלְטְאשַׁאצַּר, differing by one letter from the king's name; below 5, 1 and 7, 1; it signifies, however, as it is written here בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר, Bel preserves treasures.

ANANIÆ SIDRACH] Let a soft Sad be supplied, Sad being the name of a harmful demon. The Rabbis use it in the singular. The Chaldean and Talmudic interpreters use the plural שֵׁידִין. This name is therefore apotropaic.

Some prefer to refer it to שֶׁמֶשׁ, the Chaldean name for the Sun.

MISACH] With a part of the Hebrew name retained, שָׁךְ is placed instead of אֵל, which is a goddess of the Babylonians, whence comes sacchaea. More fully in Jeremiah, שֵׁשַׁךְ, Jer. 25, 26 and 51, 41, where see the remarks made.

Junius, Polanus, and the Belgians believe Venus is indicated. Others, the earth, which was also worshipped as a goddess.

AND AZARIÆ ABDENAGO] Servant of Lucifer. נְגוֹ in Chaldean, which is נֹגַהּ in the Chaldean of Esther 10, 3, נגהא in the Chaldean version of Isaiah 14, 11. עֶבֶד־נְגוֹ is said in the same form as עֶבֶד־עֶלְיוֹנִים, Abdolonymus in Curtius, book 4.

Others understand Fire, which was held as a GOD. Thus those four names were imposed from the gods of the Chaldeans and in their honor, namely those of Mars, the Sun, the Earth, and Fire, or Venus, or Lucifer.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET IMPOSUIT EIS PRÆPOSITUS EU- NUCHORUM NOMINA] Nempe de diis sumpta Chal- daicis, ut hic notat Jacchiades.

BALTASSAR] Scribitur hic בלְטְשׁאַצַּר, infra ve. 10, 1. בְּלְטְאשַׁצַּר una litera differens a regis nomine; infra 5, 1. & 7, 11. significat autem ita ut hic scribitur בּרְטשׁאצר, Belus servat opes.

ANANIÆ SIDRACH] Sad lenis supple sit, Sad no- men dæmonis nocentis. Usurpant Rabbini in singulari. Interpretes Chaldæi & Talmudici in plurali שֵׁידִין. Est ergo hoc nomen ἀποτρόπαιον.

Nonnulli malunt referre ad שֶׁמֶשׁ Solis nomen Chaldaicum.

MISACH] Retenta parte nominis Hebraici, pro אֵל positum שָׁךְ, quæ dea Babyloniorum, unde σακχαῖα. Jere- miæ plenius שֵׁשַׁךְ Jer. 25, 26. & 51, 41. ubi dicta vide.

Venerem notari Junius, Polanus & Belgæ cen- sent. Alii terram, quæ etiam pro dea culta fuerit.

ET AZARIÆ ABDENAGO] Servus luciferi. נְגוֹ Chaldæis, quod נֹגַהּ in Chaldaico Estheræ 10, 3. נגהא in versione Chaldaica Esaiæ 14, 11. עֶבֶד־נְגוֹ pari forma di- citur qua עֶבֶד־עֶלְיוֹנִים Abdolonymus apud Curt. lib. 4.

Alii Ignem intelligunt, qui pro DEO habi- tus. Ita quatuor ista nomina a Diis Chaldæorum, & in honorem eorum imposita, utpote Martis, So- lis, Terræ, & ignis, vel Veneris, seu Luciferi.

## 1:8
Verse 8. LEST HE BE DEFILED BY THE KING'S TABLE, NOR BY THE WINE OF HIS DRINK] Instead of 'by the king's table,' you will more correctly say 'by his bread.' For פַּתבַּג is nothing other than ποτίβαζις, a type of bread in the East, as Athenaeus teaches us in book 2 from the 3rd book of Dino's Persica. The reason, however, why Daniel abstained from the royal bread and wine is none other than that it was the custom of those nations to cast a portion of the bread and wine onto the altar, or if an altar were not present, into the hearth, in place of an altar, and in that way to consecrate to their gods all that which they were eating. But just as that was holiness in their foolish opinion, so to the Hebrews, who were better instructed, and because such things were dedicated to certain false deities, it was pollution. Thus Jacchiades and Theodoret. Whence the prohibition concerning table fellowship with the Gentiles, Acts 10:18, Job 4:9, Gal. 2:12. Add also the danger of foods forbidden by divine law, Ex. 22:31. For by the mention of bread, food is understood synecdochically. Vers. 9. BUT GOD GAVE DANIEL THANKS AND MERCY IN THE SIGHT OF THE PRINCE OF THE EUNUCHS] According to the prayers of Solomon, 1 Kings 8:50. Vers. 10. IF HE SEES YOUR FACES MORE LEAN] Sadder, σκυθρωποτέρους, such as the faces of those who have eaten sparingly are wont to be. See Matt. 6:16. The word זעף signifies this in both Hebrew and Chaldean. Vers. same. YOUR CONTEMPORARIES. LXX. τὰ συνήλικα ὑμῶν, as Schindler teaches that גיל from an Arabism denotes an age or generation. Calvin. Vatabl. who are like you; Forster renders, your planets (under whom you were born at the same time); Piscator, Tretnell, Polan, the Belgians, to be educated with you in the same revolution of time. Marc. Marin, Avenar, and Schvaning explain it as, who are (now) of the same cheerfulness as you. Vers. 11. TO MALASAR] Theodotion reads ה instead of ר, for his version has ἀμελσάδ; other codices have Μελσὰδ. It is doubted whether it is the name of a man or an office under that first inspector of the eunuchs. I would rather believe it to be the name of a man, as Asphenez above: so that the ה here is part of the name: Jacchiades also accepts it thus. Others, along with the Vulgate, Luther, Calvin, and the Belgians, take it for a proper name of a person, but they judge the He to be emphatic, which is sometimes prefixed even to proper names, Jos. 1:12, Ps. 133:20. Vers. 12. TEST US, I BESEECH THEE, THY SERVANTS] That is, make a trial of us: Theodotion πείρασον. Symmachus δοκίμασον. DENTUR NOBIS LEGUMINA] מן־הזרעים ἀπὸ τ̃ σπερμάτων. Thus are called herbs and legumes, which are prepared at a cheap price, and are hardly worthy to be brought to a royal table. That saying is indeed true: Παχεῖα γαστὴρ λεπτὸν ὀ τίκτει νόον. But here, where it is also a matter of form, the work of God appears. From Ex. 61:11, some gather that fruits of trees were also used: and they explain it not inappropriately as referring to all kinds of things growing from the earth, whether wild or cultivated. See Dn. D. Geier, h. l. Vers. 15. THEIR FACES WERE BETTER AND FATTER] ἰδέᾳ αὐτῶν ἀγαθαὶ καὶ ἰσχυραὶ ταῖς σαρξὶν, that is, they were both of a vivid color and succulent. It is evident from Gen. 41:2, 2 Sam. 23:21, Is. 53:2 that the word מראה refers to the external appearance of the whole body rather than to the face alone. Vers. 16. HE TOOK AWAY THE FOOD, AND THE WINE OF THEIR DRINK] He refrained from giving them the royal bread or wine, complying with their requests. Vers. 17. BUT TO THESE BOYS GOD GAVE KNOWLEDGE AND DISCIPLINE] Knowledge and understanding, that is, not only cognition, but also sagacity for discovering one thing from another. IN EVERY BOOK] Literature: as above 4. The Greek text has ἐν πάσῃ γραμματικῇ, which Jerome here teaches us is from Symmachus. Thus we often see versions mixed. AND WISDOM] In the knowledge of natural things, which is the chief wisdom among the Chaldeans. BUT TO DANIEL] In addition, of course. UNDERSTANDING OF ALL VISIONS AND DREAMS] That is, of interpreting θεόλατα visions and dreams, which signify future things not openly, but through images. See what was said at Num. 12:8; this is the gift of ἑρμηνείας, 1 Cor. 12:10, 14:26. Rightly are θεοπέμπτα dreams understood here, and not those which occur daily to sleepers during rest, about which oneirocritics busy themselves and rave. Why then does Grotius so often insert his Achmet here, and the ravings of the Oneirocritics, which have nothing in common with these divine dreams and the interpretations of dreams?

Latin:

Vers. 8. NE POLLUERETUR DE MENSA REGIS, NEQUE DE VINO POTUS EJUS] Pro de mensa regis, rectius dices de pane ejus. Est enim פַּתבַּג, non aliud quam ποτίβαζις, panis genus in Oriente, ut ex Dinonis 3. Persicorum nos docet Athenæus lib. 2. Causa vero cur Da- niel pane vinoq; regio abstinuerit, non alia est, quam quod moris erat illis gentibus partem de pane & de vino injicere in aram, aut si ara non adeffet, in focum, vice aræ, atque eo modo diis suis consecrare totum illud quod erant com- melliuri. Id vero sicut stulta illorum opinione erat sancti- tas, ita Hebræis melius institutis, & certis talia dedicata es- se falsis numinibus, erat pollutio. Sic Jacchiades & Theo- doretus. Unde interdictum de communione mensæ cum gentilibus Act. 10,18. Job. 4, 9. Gal. 2,12. Adde & periculum immistorum ciborum vetitorum le- ge divina Ex. 22, 31. Nam mentione panis synecdo- chice intelligitur cibus. Vers. 9. DEDIT AUTEM DEUS DANIELI GRA- TIAM ET MISERICORDIAM IN CONSPECTU PRINCIPIS EUNUCHORUM] Secundum preces Solo- monis. 1. Reg. 8,50. Vers. 10. SI VIDERIT VULTUS VESTROS MA- CILENTIORES] Tristiores, σκυθρωποτέρους, quales solent esse facies eorum qui modice pasti sunt. Vid. Matth. 6, 16. Id & in Hebræo & in Chaldæo sonat vox זעף. Vers. eod. COÆVIS VESTRIS. LXX. τὰ συνήλικα ὑμῶν, uti Schindlerus גיל ex Arabismo docet ævum generationem notare. Calvin. Vatabl. qui sunt similes vobis; Forsterus red- dit, planetæ vestri (sub quo simul estis nati;) Pi- scat. Tretnell. Polan. Belgici, eadem vobiscum tem- poris revolutione educandi. Marc. Marin. Avenar. & Schvaning. exponunt, qui sunt (jam) ejusdem vobiscum hilaritatis. Vers. 11. AD MALASAR] Theodotion legit ה pro ר ejus enim versio habet ἀμελσάδ alii codices habent Μελσὰδ. Dubitatur nomen sit hominis, an muneris, sub primo illo eunuchorum inspectore. Ego potius hominis nomen esse credam, ut supra Asphenez: ita ut ה hic sit pars nominis: ita accipit & Jacchiades. Pro nomine proprio personæ habent cum Vulg. Luthero, Calvino & Belgis etiam alii, sed He Emphaticum esse censent, quod etiam nominibus propriis quandoq; præmittitur Jos. 1, 12. Ps. 133,20. Vers. 12. TENTA NOS OBSECRO SERVOS TUOS] Id est, periculum fac de nobis: Theodotio πείρα- σον. Symmachus δοκίμασον. DENTUR NOBIS LEGUMINA] מן־הזרעים ἀπὸ τ̃ σπερμάτων. Sic vocantur herbæ & legumina, quæ vili pretio parantur, & vix digna sunt quæ ferantur ad mensam regiam. Est quidem verum illud: Παχεῖα γαστὴρ λεπτὸν ὀ τίκτει νόον. Sed hic, ubi & de forma agitur, Dei opus apparet. Ex Ef. 61,11. nonnulli fructus etiam arborum adhibitos colligunt: & de omnis generis terra na- scentibus aut sativis explicant non inconmode. Vide Dn. D. Geier, h. l. Vers. 15. VULTUS EORUM MELIORES ET COR- PULENTIORES] ἰδέᾳ αὐτῶν ἀγαθαὶ καὶ ἰσχυραὶ ταῖς σαρξὶν, id est, & colore erant vivido & succosi. Ad externum universi corporis aspectum po- tius, quam ad faciem tantum vocem מראה specta- re è Gen. 41, 2. 2. Sam. 23, 21. Es. 53, 2. patet. Vers. 16. TOLLEBAT CIBARIA, ET VINUM PO- TUS EORUM] Abstinebat illis dare de pane aut vino re- gio, ipsorum precibus morem gerens. Vers. 17. PUERIS AUTEM HIS DEDIT DEUS SCIENTIAM ET DISCIPLINAM] Scientiam & intel- lectum, id est, non cognitionem tantum, sed & sagacita- tem ad alia ex aliis reperienda. IN OMNI LIBRO] Literatura: ut supra 4. ἐν πά- σῃ γραμματικῇ habet textus Græcus, quod esse ex Symma- cho docet nos hic Hieronymus. Ita sæpe misceri versio- nes videmus. ET SAPIENTIA] In cognitione rerum naturalium, quæ præcipua sapientia apud Chaldæos. DANIELI VERO] Insuper scilicet. INTELLIGENTIAM OMNIUM VISIONUM ET SOMNIORUM] Id est, interpretandi visa & somnia θεόλα- τα, quæ non aperte, sed per imagines futura significant. Vide quæ dicta Num. 12,8. hoc est donum ἑρμηνείας. 1. Cor. 12, 10. 14, 26. Recte somnia θεοπέμπτα hic intelliguntur, non vero quæ per quietem dormientibus quoti- die occurrunt, circa quæ onirocritæ versantur & delirant. Cur ergo Grotius suum Achmetem hic tam sæpe ingerit, & Onirocritarum deliramenta, quibus nihil commercii cum divinis hisce somniis & somniorum interpretationibus?

## 1:19
Vers. 19. AND THEY STOOD IN THE SIGHT OF THE KING] As daily ministers.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET STETERUNT IN CONSPECTU RE- GIS] Tanquam quotidiani ministri.

## 1:20
Vers. 20. EVERY WORD OF WISDOM AND UNDERSTANDING] In the Hebrew it is construct, חכמת בינה, wisdom of understanding, that is, of those parts of philosophy which require a most perceptive intellect.

ABOVE ALL THE SOOTHSAYERS] For החרטמים, the Greek version has τὲς ἐπαοιδὲς; and elsewhere, Exod. 7:11, 8:7, 18, it is φαρμακές. They were natural scientists, but who often also used the work of demons.

AND MAGICIANS] ואשפים, which is read here, I would believe to be a Greek word: for before the times of Nebuchadnezzar, the fame of Thales and others who were called σοφοὶ was celebrated; and Thales was from Asiatic Ionia. It is characteristic of the Syrians to prefix N to words.

Lempereur h. l. derives σοφὸς from אשפים, and seeks that word from an Arabism, which was also done by Hottinger, Thes. Philol. p. 57.

Latin:

Vers. 20. OMNE VERBUM SAPIENTIÆ ET IN- TELLECTUS] In Hebræo est constructive חכמת בינה, sapientiæ intellectus, id est, earum partium Philosophiæ, quæ maxime perspicacem intellectum requirunt.

SUPER CUNCTOS ARIOLOS] Pro החרטמים, τὲς ἐπαοιδὲς Græca habet versio; nec aliter Exod. 7, 11. 22.8, 7. 18. alibi φαρμακές. Erant Physici, sed qui sæ- pe etiam dæmonum uterentur opera.

ET MAGOS] ואשפיםquod hic legitur, credide- rim vocem esse Græcam : nam ante Nabuchodonosori tem- pora, celebris erat Thaletis & aliorum qui σοφοὶ dicti sunt fama; erat autem Thales ex Jonia Asiatica. Syrorum est N vocibus præponere.

Contra σοφὸς ab אשפים Lempereur h. l. de- ducit, vocemque illam ex Arabismo petit, quod e- tiam factum ab Hottingero Thes. Philol. p. 57.

## 1:21
Vers. 21. BUT DANIEL WAS] That is, he lived in Babylon: for it is said by the Hebrews that he went to Judea afterwards.

TO THE FIRST YEAR OF CYRUS THE KING] Even to the end of the seventy years, which Jeremiah had said were appointed for the exile.

Jerome: Daniel, he says, was powerful in Chaldea until the first year of Cyrus, who destroyed the empire of the Chaldeans. But afterwards he was transferred from Darius to the Medes. Nor is it added without cause, 'until the first year of Cyrus': because it is not obscurely signified that Daniel saw that time which had been predicted by Isaiah, who intimated that the Jews were to be liberated from Babylon by Cyrus.

Latin:

Vers. 21. FUIT AUTEM DANIEL] Id est, vixit Ba- bylone: nam postea in Judæam ivisse ab Hebræis dicitur.

AD ANNUM PRIMUM CYRI REGIS ] Ad fi- nem usque septuaginta annorum, quos præstitutos exsilio dixerat Jeremias.

Hieronymus: Daniel, inquit, usq́; ad primum annum Cyri, qui Chaldæorum destruxit imperium, potens fuit in Chaldæa. Postea vero à Dario ad Me- dos translatus est. Nec absque causa additur, us- que ad annum primum Cyri : quia non obscure si- gnificatur ita, Danielem id tempus vidisse, quod ab Esaia prædictum erat, qui Judæos per Cyrume Babylone liberandos intimavit.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

Nebuchadnezzar had a dream, which, when the Chaldean wise men could not interpret, and were therefore ordered to be killed, was revealed to Daniel as he prayed, who disclosed it to the King concerning a certain great statue, with an added exposition concerning the four kingdoms, and he was affected with honors and gifts by the King, who confessed the God of Daniel.

Ver. 1.

IN THE SECOND YEAR OF THE REIGN OF NEBUCHADNEZZAR] Understand the reign established in the parts around Judea, Syria, Ammonitis, Moabitis, and a great part of Egypt. Thus Josephus here. But Jerome notes here that this interpretation also pleased other Hebrews.

Most people, Tremellius, Torniellus, Salianus, Pererius, Petavius, Sanctius, Maldonatus, Oecolampadius along with Aben Ezra, and among our own, Schvaningius, explain the second year not of the reign, but of the Monarchy of Nebuchadnezzar, following Josephus and Jerome: But in this way, this dream would have been sent seven years after the conquest of Jerusalem. Yet how could Daniel's wisdom have been unknown then, which was already publicly celebrated five years before the destruction in Ezekiel 14, and predicted in the very year of the destruction in Ezekiel 28:3? This cause moved the blessed Gesner to count this second year from the completion and end of that three-year period which Daniel spent in the school of the Chaldeans. Polanus, Tremellius, Glassius (Phil. S. 1. 4. p. 633), and others, whom Schvaningius acknowledges perhaps do not stray much from the truth, also agree with him. The Zakephkaton accent above the letter ת in the word שתים confirms this sense, signifying that those words 'IN THE SECOND YEAR' are not to be connected with the following 'OF THE REIGN' of Nebuchadnezzar. Moreover, it is added that this happened in the reign of Nebuchadnezzar on account of the conclusion of the preceding chapter, where mention of Cyrus was made, whence this is the continuity: Daniel indeed was occupied in the Babylonian court until the first year of Cyrus, but two years after he had come from the school into the court, while Nebuchadnezzar was still reigning, the King saw the dream.

Vers. same. NEBUCHADNEZZAR SAW A DREAM] In the Hebrew: Dreams; namely, on account of the many things which were contained in one dream.

AND HIS SPIRIT WAS TERRIFIED] Tossed by turns, his thought carrying itself now hither, now thither. Compare Gen. 6.

Compare Gen. 41, 8. Ps. 77, 5.

AND HIS DREAM FLED FROM HIM] Because his dream had fled from him. He did not remember it exactly, but certain outlines had remained in his mind, through which the matter could return to memory.

B. Luther, along with the LXX, Pagninus, and the Dutch, more correctly express the sense: which is in the Hebrew, And sleep fled from him. Compare Esth. 6, 1. Gen. 31, 40.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Somnium habuit Nebucadnezar, quod cum conjectare non valerent Sapientes Chal- dæi, adeoque interfici juberentur, Danie- li oranti revelatum est, qui id Regi aperuit de statua quadam magna, addita exposi- tione de quatuor regnis, & à Rege Deum Danielis confitente, honoribus & muneri- bus affectus est.

Vers. 1.

IN ANNO SECUNDO REGNI NABUCHO- DONOSAR] Regni intellige constituti in partibus circum Judæam, Syriæ, Ammonitide, Moabitide, & Ægypti magna parte. Ita hic Josephus. Sed & aliis Hebræis hanc pla- cuisse interpretationem, notat hic Hieronymus.

DE anno secundo non regni, sed Monarchiæ Na- buchodonosaris è Josepho & Hieronymo ple- rique, Tremellius, Torniellus, Salianus, Pererius, Pe- tavius, Sanctius, Maldonatus, Oecolampadius cum Aben Esra, & è nostris Schvaningius explicant: Sed ita septennio post expugnationem Hierosoly- mæ hoc somnium immissum fuisset. Quomodo vero ignota tum esse potuisset Danielis sapientia, quæ quinquennio ante excidium publice jam de- cantata fuit Ezech. 14. & ipso excidii anno prædi- cata Ezech. 28,3. Quæ causa Beatum Gesnerum movit, ut numerarit annum hunc secundum à complemento, & fine illius triennii, quod Daniel in Schola Chaldæorum consumsit. Cum quo etiam faciunt Polanus, Tremellius, Glassius Phil. S. 1. 4. p. 633. aliique, quos non multum fortassis à vero aberrare agnoscit Schvaningius. Quem sensum firmat accentus Zakephkaton supra literam ת in voce שתים significans, verba illa ANNO SECUN- DO non connectenda esse cum sequentibus REGNI Nebucadnezaris. Additur autem in regno Nebucad- nezaris hoc factum esse, ob conclusionem præcedentis capitis, ubi mentio Cyri facta, unde hæc est συνέ- χεια: Daniel quidem in aula Babylonica versatus est, usq; ad annum primum Cyri, biennio autem post- quam è Schola in aulam venisset, regnante adhuc Ne- bucadnezare, vidit Rex somnium.

Vers. eod. VIDIT NABUCHODONOSOR SOMNIUM] In Hebræo: Somnia; nempe ob res multas quæ uno somnio continebantur.

ET CONTERRITUS EST SPIRITUS EJUS] Vicibus jactatus, modo huc, modo illuc ferente se ejus cogitatione. Confer. Gen. 6.

Confer. Gen. 41, 8. Psal. 77, 5.

ET SOMNIUM EJUS FUGIT AB EO] Quia somnium ejus fugerat ab eo. Exacte non meminerat, sed manserant in animo velut lineamenta quædam, per quæ redire res in memoriam posset.

Rectius B. Lutherus cum LXX. Pagnin. & Batav. sensum exprimunt: qui in Ebræo est, Et fugit somnus ab eo. Conf. Esth. 6, 1. Gen. 31, 40.

## 2:2
Vers. 2.

AND THE SORCERERS] מכשפים Jerome interprets as necromancers, as does also Jacchiades. The same word is in the feminine in Exod. 20, 16.

Jugglers are usually understood by this word. See Ex. 7, 11. Deut. 18, 10. Luther rightly rendered it here as Zauberer [sorcerers], but he explained the following word כשדים [Chaldeans] in a special sense for Astrologers, who were famous in Chaldea, Genethliacs, dream-interpreters, and the like, who are gathered to have been the chief among the soothsayers from v. 4, where they answer in place of all.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET MALEFICI] מכשפים Hieronymus interpretatur τὺς νεκρομάντεις, ut & Jacchiades. Est eadem vox in feminino Exod. 20, 16.

Præstigiatores intelligi solent hac voce. Vid. Ex. 7, 11. Deut. 18, 10. Luth. recte Zauberer hic reddidit, vocem vero sequentem כשדים Chaldæor. sensu speciali pro Astrologis, qui in Chaldæa celebres erant, Genethlicis, Onirocriticis, & similibus exposuit, quos præcipuos fuisse inter ariolos è v. 4. qui omnium loco respondent, colligitur.

## 2:4
Vers. 4. AND THE CHALDEANS ANSWERED THE KING IN SYRIAC] That is, in Chaldean. For Chaldea is also a part of the Arameans. From here until chapter 8, all things are written in Chaldean, because they concern the Chaldeans most; but from there on again in Hebrew, because the things which are said there concern the Hebrews most. When the Chaldeans are mentioned here, understand at the same time those others named above.

Compare c. 1. 4. 2 Kings 18, 26. Isa. 36, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 4. RESPONDERUNTQUE CHALDÆI REGI STRIACE] Id est, Chaldaice. Nam & Chaldæa pars Aramæorum. Abhinc usque ad caput 8. omnia scripta sunt Chaldaice, quod Chaldæos maxime tangant: inde vero rursum Hebraice, quod quæ ibi dicuntur, maxime Hebræos respiciant. Cum hic Chaldæi dicuntur, simul intellige cæteros illos supra nominatos.

Conf. c. 1. 4. 2. Reg. 18, 26. Esa. 36, 11.

## 2:5
Vers. 5. YOU SHALL PERISH, AND YOUR HOUSES SHALL BE MADE A DUNGHILL] In the Chaldean: You shall be torn limb from limb, and your house shall be turned into a latrine. To be torn limb from limb is a severe punishment, but not unusual in the East. See 1 Sam. 15. Orpheus was subjected to this punishment by the women of Thrace, Bessus by Alexander the Great. Also, to turn a house into a latrine was a certain condemnation of memory in the East. 2 Kings 10, 27. Ezra 6, 11, according to the Chaldean interpreter. You have both also below 3, 29. The king, being angry, wanted it to appear that they were impostors, who, although they claimed that the most hidden things were known to them, yet did not show it in this fact.

Vers. same. O KING, LIVE FOREVER.

Such formulas for greeting Magnates were customary both among the gentiles c. 3, 9. c. 5, 10. c. 6, 6. and among the Jews 1 Sam. 10, 25. 1 Kings 1, 25. 31. 34. 39. 2 Chron. 23, 11., but the former prayed for long life, whereas the latter prayed for eternal life.

Verse 5.

AND YOUR HOUSES SHALL BE MADE PUBLIC.

Sanctius: They shall be assigned to the royal treasury and public uses, but נולי denotes a dunghill, therefore it should have been rendered: let them be carried (to) a dunghill: houses which were hitherto a workshop of the liberal arts, are to be leveled to the ground and marked with the stigma of ignominy. See similar passages Deut. 29, 23. Jud. 9, 45. Ezra 6, 12. Prov. 15, 25.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PERIBITIS VOS, ET DOMUS VESTRÆ PUBLICABUNTUR] In Chaldæo: Membratim laniabimini, & domus vestra in latrinas mutabitur. Membratim laniari, grave supplicium, at non inusitatum Orienti. Vide 1. Sam. 15. Hac pœna affectus Orpheus à Thraciæ fœminis, Bessus ab Alexandro Magno. Domus quoque in latrinas vertere, erat quædam in Oriente memoriæ damnatio. 2. Reg. 10, 27. Esdræ. 6, 11. secundum Chaldæum interpretem. Utramque habes & infra 3, 29. Rex iracundus, volebat videri, eos esse impostores, qui cum abditissima quæque sibi nota dicerent, id tamen non oftenderent in hoc facto.

Vers. eod. REX IN SEMPITERNUM VIVE.

Tales salutandi Magnates formulæ & apud gentiles c. 3, 9. c. 5, 10. c. 6, 6. & apud Judæos 1. Sam. 10, 25. 1. Reg. 1, 25. 31. 34. 39. 2. Par. 23, 11. usitatæ fuere, sed illi longævam vitam precabantur, hi vero æternam.

Vers. 5.

ET DOMUS VESTRÆ PUBLICABUNTUR.

Sanctius: Regio fisco & publicis commodis adscribentur, sed נולי sterquilinium notat, ideo reddendum erat (in) sterquilinium portentur: ædes quæ officina liberalium artium hactenus, solo æquandæ, & ignominiæ nota afficiendæ. Vid. similia Deut. 29, 23. Jud. 9, 45. Esdr. 6, 12. Prov. 15, 25.

## 2:6
Verse 6.

AND GIFTS] נבזבה It is an annual disbursement, as appears by comparing the passages of the Paraphrasts Deut. 33, 24. and Jer. 40, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET DONA] נבזבה Est annua erogatio, ut apparet collatis locis Paraphrastarum Deut. 33, 24. & Jer. 40, 5.

## 2:8
Verse 8.

SURELY I KNOW THAT YE WOULD GAIN THE TIME] You are seeking delays: for before those things happen which you would say in interpreting the dream, much time will intervene, which might free you from punishment. The following words demand this sense. The Greek version here is καιρὸν ὑμεῖς ἐξαγοράζετε: which expression is also found in Paul, Eph. 5, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

CERTE NOVI QUOD TEMPUS REDIMITIS] Moras quæritis: nam antequam eveniant, quæ vos in somnio interpretando diceretis, multum intercedet temporis, quod vos à pœna liberet. Hunc sensum postulant sequentia. Græca hic versio καιρὸν ὑμεῖς ἐξαγοράζετε: quæ locutio & apud Paulum Ephes. 5, 16.

## 2:10
Verse 10.

THERE IS NO MAN UPON THE EARTH, THAT CAN SHEW THE KING'S MATTER] They themselves acknowledge that their previous promises were vain.

NOR ANY LORD, THAT IS GREAT AND POWERFUL] There are three degrees in the Chaldean: King: מלך, that is, prince: שליט, that is, ruler of a city, and of a city-region.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

NON EST HOMO SUPER TERRAM, QUI SERMONEM TUUM, REX, POSSIT IMPLERE] Agnoscunt ipsi vanas esse suas antehac pollicitationes.

NEQUE REGUM QUISQUAM MAGNUS ET POTENS] Sunt in Chaldaico tres gradus: Rex: מלך, id est princeps: שליט, id est, rector urbis, & regionis urbicæ.

## 2:11
Verse 11.

EXCEPTING THE GODS, WHOSE CONVERSATION IS NOT WITH MEN] As if they were saying, the knowledge of those demons, or aerial gods, who have commerce with men, does not reach that far. This matter is reserved for the greater gods.

Simplicius understands this predicate universally of the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh, as Piscator renders כאן woda: for whence will it be taught that such demons were believed by the Chaldeans, from whose benevolent conversation with men secrets could be known, to be different from the greater gods?

Latin:

Vers. 11.

EXCEPTIS DIIS, QUORUM NON EST CUM HOMINIBUS CONVERSATIO] Quasi dicant, illorum dæmonum, sive deorum aërëorum, qui cum hominibus commercium habent, notitia eo usque non pertingit. Hæc res diis majoribus reservata est.

Simplicius universaliter de diis hoc prædi- catum intelligitur, quorum habitatio cum carne non est, ut כאן woda reddit Piscator: nam creditos fuisse tales Dæmones Chaldæis, e quorum conver- satione benevola cum hominibus arcana sciri pos- sint, à Diis majoribus diversos undenam docebi- tur?

## 2:13
Verse 13.

AND THE SENTENCE WENT FORTH] The king's decree having been published. Thus ἐξῆλθε δόγμα in Luke 2:1.

THE WISE MEN WERE BEING KILLED] They had begun to be killed.

AND DANIEL AND HIS COMPANIONS WERE SOUGHT, THAT THEY MIGHT PERISH] Most unjustly, that they might come into a share of the punishment, who had not come into a share of the rewards, having been despised by the others on account of their youth.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET EGRESSA SENTENTIA] Publicato regis de- creto. Sic ἐξῆλθε δόγμα Luc. 2, 2.

SAPIENTES INTERFICIEBANTUR] Cœperant interfici.

QUÆREBANTURQUE DANIEL ET SOCII EJUS, UT PERIRENT] Iniquissime, ut in pœnæ partem venirent, qui in præmiorum partem non venissent, con- temti à cæteris ob juventutem.

## 2:14
Verse 14.

HE INQUIRED CONCERNING THE LAW AND THE SENTENCE] In the Chaldean: he brought back counsel, and the cause of his counsel, to be sure. Theodotion: ἀπεκρίθη βελὴν καὶ γνώμην.

It is more correctly translated: Then Daniel rendered void the counsel and the sentence to Arioch, the captain of the king's soldiers. The word התיר is to be explained by a comparison of the Hebrew and Chaldean text of Esther 8 as to render void, to cause to return, or to cause a sentence to be revoked, so that the sum of what is to be said here may be held. For the manner in which Daniel made this counsel void or rendered it void is explained in what follows.

FROM ARIOCH THE CAPTAIN] More correctly the Greeks: τῷ Ἀριώχ, to Arioch.

CAPTAIN OF THE MILITIA] In the Chaldean: the president of the king's executioners, that is, the prefect over capital matters. טבח for the Syrians and Arabs is to slaughter: whence the name is derived, sometimes taken from cooks, sometimes from guards or executioners: which meanings, however, the Arabs distinguish with little points, as noted by Aben Ezra.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

REQUISIVIT DE LEGE ATQUE SENTEN- TIA] In Chaldæo: retulit consilium, & causam scilicet con- silii sui. Theodotio: ἀπεκρίθη βελὴν καὶ γνώμην.

Rectius vertitur: Tunc Daniel irritum reddi- dit consilium & sententiam Ariocho præfecto militum Regis. Vox התיר è collatione textus Ebræi & Chaldaici Esth. 8. per irritum reddere, redire facere vel ut revocetur sententia efficere explicanda, ut summa hic dicendorum habeatur. Exponitur enim in sequentibus modus, quo irritarit hoc consilium Daniel vel irritum reddiderit.

AB ARIOCH PRINCIPE] Rectius Græci: τῷ Ἀ- ριώχ, ad Ariochum.

PRINCIPE MILITIÆ] In Chaldaico: præsidem carnificum regis, id est, præfectum rebus capitalibus. טבח Syris & Arabibus est mactare: unde deducitur nomen mo- do de coquis, modo de satellitibus, aut carnificibus sum- ptum: quas tamen significationes Arabes punctulis di- stinguunt, ut Abenesdræ notatum.

## 2:15
Verse 15.

SUCH A CRUEL SENTENCE] So hasty: for חצף also signifies this in Chaldean, and it is more credible that Daniel said this, on account of the things which follow.

WHEN THEREFORE HE HAD INDICATED THE MATTER TO DANIEL] Had signified to him with how much anger the King had been inflamed.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

TAM CRUDELIS SENTENTIA] Tam festina: nam חצף etiam hoc in Chaldaico fignificat, idque credi- bilius dixisse Danielem, ob ea quæ sequuntur.

CUM ERGO REM INDICASSET ARIOCH DANIELI] Significasset ei, quanta ira Rex accensus esset.

## 2:16
Ver. 16.

TO INDICATE THE SOLUTION TO THE KING] What the Dream was, and what it tended toward.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

AD SOLUTIONEM INDICANDAM REGI] Quod esset Somnium, & quo tenderet.

## 2:18
Ver. 18.

THAT THEY MIGHT SEEK MERCY FROM THE FACE OF GOD] That in a common danger they might also implore the counsel of God with a common prayer.

CONCERNING THIS MYSTERY] Concerning this secret. For it is רז for the Chaldeans, and μυσήριον for the Greeks (which word Theodotion uses here) everything that is unknown: τὸ ἀγνοούμενον, as Chrysostom interprets it.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

UT QUÆRERENT MISERICORDIAM A FA- CIE DEI] Ut in communi periculo communi etiam pre- ce Dei consilium implorarent.

SUPER SACRAMENTO ISTO] Super arcano isto. Est enim רז Chaldæis, & μυσήριον Græcis (qua voce hic utitur Theodotion) omne id quod ignoratur: τὸ ἀγνοού- μενον, ut interpretatur Chrysostomus.

## 2:20
Ver. 20.

HE SPOKE AND SAID] A similar manner of speaking in Deut. 16, 5.

WISDOM AND STRENGTH ARE HIS] Wisdom in knowing hidden things: supreme power over Kings and kingdoms, about which this dream was concerned. The following things confirm this explanation.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

LOCUTUS AIT] Simile loquendi genus Deut. 16, 5.

SAPIENTIA ET FORTITUDO EJUS SUNT] Sapientia in cognoscendis rebus absconditis: potentia summa in Reges & regna, de quibus agebat hoc somnium. Hanc explicationem firmant sequentia.

## 2:21
Ver. 21. AND HE CHANGES TIMES AND AGES] Virgil: Times are changed, and we are changed in them.

HE GIVES WISDOM TO THE WISE] He has many things which He may teach even the wisest.

AND KNOWLEDGE TO THOSE WHO UNDERSTAND DISCIPLINE] In the Chaldean: And knowledge to those who know understanding: that is, he gives the knowledge of many arts to those who know how much it is worth to understand, and therefore turn themselves to God.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET IPSE MUTAT TEMPORA ET Æ- TATES] Virgilius: Tempora mutantur, & nos mutamur in illis.

DAT SAPIENTIAM SAPIENTIBUS] Etiam sa- pientissimos multa habet, quæ doceat.

ET SCIENTIAM INTELLIGENTIBUS DISCI- PLINAM] In Chaldæo: Et scientiam scientibus intelligentiæ: id est, dat multarum artium cognitionem iis qui sciunt, quanti sit intelligere, ac propterea ad Deum se vertunt.

## 2:22
V. 22. AND HE KNOWS WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IN DARKNESS, AND LIGHT IS WITH HIM] Although he himself is in the highest light. 1 Tim. 6, 16. yet he sees all things which are wrapped in darkness. 1 Cor. 4, 5.

Latin:

V. 22. ET NOVIT IN TENEBRIS CONSTITUTA, ET LUX CUM EO EST] Quanquam ipse in luce sum- ma est. 1. Tim. 6, 16. tamen cuncta, quæ tenebris involuta sunt, videt 1. Cor. 4, 5.

## 2:23
Vers. 23. AND YOU HAVE GIVEN STRENGTH TO ME] The ability to rescue both myself and others from most grave danger.

THE WORD OF THE KING] That matter which the King seeks.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET FORTITUDINEM DEDISTI MIHI] Facultatem & me & alios eripiendi periculo gravissimo.

SERMONEM REGIS] Rem illam, quam Rex quærit.

## 2:27
Vers. 27. AND SOOTHSAYERS] גזרין Theodotion retained this Chaldean word, γαζαρηνῶν, as the Greeks often do in obscure matters. גזר for the Chaldeans, as also for the Arabs, among other things means to cut up. There were, however, also those among the Chaldeans who used entrails for prophecies. Ezek. 21, 21. Symmachus had translated it θυτάς: for so it seems it should be read in Jerome instead of

δούς. Jerome says the same are called by the Greeks ὑπατικούς. Perhaps others more correctly derive it from שׁוד, which is to decree, taking them here as guardians of decrees, who below with the addition of אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּא?

The interpreters, but also a comparison of Gen. 25. 33. and the representation of the human image, teach this; for what would that be, if the image is believed to be destitute of a belly, and how would the viscera be joined with the head, chest, and arms rather than the belly containing the viscera; add that the word added and its sides or thighs cohere more correctly to the belly than to the intestines: and that D. D. Svaningius, preferring the sense of viscera, acknowledges that just as the belly provides a receptacle for the viscera, such as the liver, spleen, intestines, kidneys, etc., and is placed immediately beneath the chest, so also the little word of the belly can be used not inconveniently, both to indicate the just sequence of this empire and to express its vastness united in Alexander.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET ARUSPICES] גזרין Chaldaicam hanc vocem retinuit Theodotio, γαζαρηνῶν, ut sæpe faciunt Græ- ci in obscuris. גזר Chaldæis, ut & Arabibus, inter alia est pro- secare. Erant autem apud Chaldæos etiam, qui extis ad vaticinia uterentur. Ezech. 21, 21. Symmachus θυτάς ver- terat: ita enim apud Hieronymum legendum videtur pro

δούς. Eosdem ait Hieronymus Græcis vocari ὑπατικούς. Alti forte rectius à שׁוד, quod est decernere acci- piunt hic decretorum custodes, qui infra cum additamen- to אֲדַרְגָּזְרַיָּא?

Interpp. sed etiam collatio Gen. 25. 33. & imaginis humanæ repræsentatio docet; quæ enim illa foret, si imago ventre destituta credatur, & quomodo cum capite, pectore, & brachiis jungerentur po- stius viscera, quam venter viscera continens; adde quod vox addita & latera ejus vel femora rectius cohæreant ventri, quam intestinis: quodque D. D. Svaningius viscerum sensum præferens agno- scat, quod prout venter visceribus, ut epati, lieni, intestinis, renibus &c. receptaculum præbet, & pe- ctori proxime substernitur, ita quoq; vocula ventris tum ad hujus imperii justam seriem indigitandam tum ad ejusdem in Alexandro unitam vastitatem ex- primendam haud incommode adhiberi possit.

## 2:28
Vers. 28. AND GOD IN HEAVEN REVEALING MYSTERIES] See the modesty of the prophet, attributing glory to God. See also below 30.

IN THE LATTER DAYS] This expression has led many who are ignorant of it into perverse interpretations of the following, since it signifies nothing other than hereafter. See Gen. 49, 1. Deut. 4, 30. Prov. 31, 25. Is. 2, 2. 41, 22. 46, 10. Jer. 23, 20. Ezek. 38, 8. 16. for אַחֲרִין is not necessarily the last, but everything that is later.

VISIONS OF THY HEAD] The Hebrews assign affections to the heart, the imaginative power to the head.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ET DEUS IN COELO REVELANS MYSTERIA] Vide modestiam vatis, gloriam Deo tribuen- tis. Vide & infra 30.

IN NOVISSIMIS TEMPORIBUS] Hæc locutio multos ejus ignaros ad pravas sequentium interpretationes egit, cum nihil aliud significet, quam posthac. Vide Gen. 49, 1. Deut. 4, 30. Prov. 31, 25. Es. 2, 2. 41, 22. 46, 10. Jerem. 23, 20. Ezech. 38,8. 16. nam אַחֲרִין non utique postremum est, sed omne quod est posterius.

VISIONES CAPITIS TUI] Hebræi affectus dant cordi, vim imaginatricem capiti.

## 2:29
Vers. 29. THOU BEGANNEST TO THINK UPON THY BED] Before sleep.

Latin:

Vers. 29. COGITARE COEPISTI IN STRATU TUO] Ante somnum.

## 2:30
Vers. 30. BUT THAT THE INTERPRETATION MIGHT BE MADE KNOWN TO THE KING] But that there might be those who would make the interpretation known to the king. An enallage of number, which is often used for the sake of modesty, as, --- and we bore some name and glory. We have imposed it upon the people, and we seemed to be orators. Thus also below 36 we shall say, that is, I shall say.

It is not the custom of the Hebrew language, as it is most simple, to speak thus for the sake of authority or modesty; and Daniel includes at the same time his companions, who had obtained the interpretation of the dream from God: indeed God Himself, who revealed the dream, vers. 29. 45. 47. and was speaking through Daniel.

Latin:

Vers. 30. SED UT INTERPRETATIO REGI MANIFE- STA FIERET] Sed ut essent qui interpretationem regi notam facerent. Enallage numeri, quæ sæpe modestiæ causa adhibetur, ut, --- & nos aliquod nomenque decusque Gessimus. Imposuimus populo, & oratores visi sumus. Sic & infra 36. dicemus, id est, dicam.

Non est linguæ Ebrææ ceu simplicissimæ hic mos, autoritatis, seu modestiæ causa ita loqui; & includit Daniel simul socios suos, qui interpre- tationem somnii à Deo impetrarant: imo Deum ipsum, qui somnium revelavit, vers. 29. 45. 47. & per Danielem loquebatur.

## 2:31
Vers. 31. BEHOLD AS IT WERE ONE GREAT STATUE] Future empires are shown to Nebuchadnezzar under a human, august, great, and splendid appearance, because he valued empires highly, and held them almost as his own Gods, who were accustomed to be worshipped through statues. But to Daniel below, the same appear under the image of wild beasts: for the Prophet knew that all those empires were idolatrous, and therefore instruments of the devil, through which, however, as also through the devils themselves, God executes his decrees.

Neither reason is sufficiently convenient. For if the empires were represented in a statue because the King held them almost as Gods, his idolatry would have been confirmed in that way. And that the Empires are instruments of Idolatry and the devil, that happens by accident. Wherefore they seem to be human statues both because of the analogy which they have with the parts of the human body, and because of their august gravity and dignity, because human Emperors bear the image of God. Emperors perform the role of God their head on earth, and ought to imitate him in their rule with virtues, just as man was created in the image of God, and the virtues of the creator shone forth in him: but they seem to be adumbrated by living creatures in a new vision, both because they correspond to those living creatures by some similarity, and because the princes themselves are delighted by images of living creatures on their insignia.

ITS APPEARANCE WAS TERRIBLE] Because most kings care more to be feared than to be loved. Let them hate, they say, provided they fear.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ECCE QUASI STATUA UNA GRANDIS] Na- buchodonosoro futura imperia ostenduntur sub facie hu- mana, augusta, grandi, splendida, quia ille imperia magni faciebat, & habebat quasi pro Diis suis, qui per statuas coli solebant. At Danieli infra eadem apparent sub ferarum imagine: noverat enim Propheta esse omnia ista imperia idololatriz, ac proinde diaboli instrumenta, per quæ ta- men, ut & per ipsos diabolos, Deus sua decreta exseque- tur.

Neutra ratio satis commoda est. Nam si ideo in statua repræsentata imperia, quod Rex ea quasi pro Diis haberet, idolatria ipsius confir- mata ita fuisset. Et quod Imperia Idololatriæ & diaboli instrumenta sint, id ex accidente fit. Qua- propter statuæ humanæ videntur tum ob analo- giam, quam cum partibus humani corporis ha- bent, tum ob augustam gravitatem, & dignita- tem, quod imaginem Dei humani Imperatores re- ferant. Imperatores Dei capitis sui vicem in ter- ris gerunt, eumque virtutibus imitari in regimine debent, quemadmodum homo conditus ad imagi- nem Dei fuit, virtutesque creatoris in ipso elu- xerunt: per animantia autem adumbrata illa vi- dentur nova visione, tum quod similitudine aliqua istis animantibus respondeant, tum quod dele- ctentur ipsimet principes imaginibus animantium in insignibus suis.

INTUITUS EJUS ERAT TERRIBILIS] Quia reges plerique timeri quam amari magis curant. Oderint, ajunt, dum metuant.

## 2:32
Vers. 32. THE HEAD OF THIS STATUE] The higher the part of the statue, the earlier the times it signifies; the lower, the later.

Interpreters, both Jews and Christians, easily agree on this, that by this stone Christ our King, or the kingdom of Christ, is designated, even if the Jews draw it to their Utopian and fictitious Messiah, whom they expect. And it is very well known that Christ is compared to a stone, from Ps. 118, Is. 8, and ch. 28. Most Christian interpreters wish Christ to be called cut from the mountain without hands, because he was born without male agency; see Justin, dial. with Trypho; Irenaeus, lib. 3, cap. 28; Cyprian, l. 3, adv. Jud.; Epiphanius, Serm. de laud. virg.; Jerome, Epist. to Eustoch. de custod. Virg. c. 22; Augustine, Tr. 9 in John; Theodoret in h. l., although he notes here that the cutting of a stone is accustomed to be called an origin above nature. For a rock is not naturally accustomed to produce or generate anything from itself, nor is it able. To this pertains what is held in Is. 52: Look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the hole of the pit from which you were cut, because Isaac and the Hebrews were procreated from the barren Sarah above nature, just as if they had been cut from a rock.

OF FINEST GOLD] That is, with the greatest glory. below 37.

ARMS OF SILVER] With less glory. below 39.

BELLY AND THIGHS OF BRASS] With an invincible spirit. Such is that: He had strength and triple bronze around his chest. And a bronze forehead, Isa. 48, 4, that is, firm, immovable.

Although the word מְעוֹהִי may denote the intestines, it is used by synecdoche for the belly which contains them, not only by the consensus

But it is said to be cut from the mountain, either because it is from the people and the Jewish Church, which stood out among the nations like a mountain, as Augustine explains in Tractate 9 on John and Tractate 1 on 1 John, Epistle 1; or because it is from the Virgin Mary, who was like a mountain on account of the sublimity of her thanks and virtues, as Jerome and Theodoret declare. The former sense, however, is more convenient. For just as kingdoms and nations are expressed here by the name of mountains, so Christ, that precious stone, was cut from the Israelite nation and the Royal lineage, because he was born of the Fathers according to the flesh. But that it is cut without hands denotes a mode of birth that is entirely ἐξαίρετον (exceptional) and peculiar, because he was born without the work or virtue of a man, by the power of the Holy Spirit alone. Compare Blessed Gesner on this passage. Blessed Lyserus is otherwise, page 163. By the mountain here we understand nothing other than heaven. Just as David speaks: I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from whence help comes to me. My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. For Christ descended from heaven, whence the Prophet said: His going forth is from the beginning, and from the days of eternity: And the Baptist says of Christ: He who comes from above is above all. He who is of the earth, is of the earth, and speaks of the earth. But he who comes from heaven is above all. But it was cut without hands, that is, without any merit of men, by the mere grace of God. Osiander explains it concerning the most recent coming of Christ: The stone cut without hands signifies Christ, who is the rock suddenly to come upon the world on the last day: no otherwise than if some great rock, torn from a mountain, rushing headlong by its own mass, should overthrow and crush everything in its path with a very great crash. And this stone, Christ, even today, but invisibly, fills the whole world, and governs all things present: for he ascended above all heavens, that he might fill all things, Eph. 4. And after this life he will be visibly present to all the elect for all eternity. This tearing away of the stone from the mountain, done without hands, could also be understood of the rise of the kingdom of Christ, which went forth from Mount Zion, and was cut from there without human hands, and although King Christ was held as a rejected and reprobated stone, yet that stone grew into a mountain of huge size, into a most ample kingdom, so as to fill the whole earth, Ps. 2, Ps. 72, Isa. 2, Mic. 4, Col. 1, so that it might crush all the remaining kingdoms and subject them to itself; because he reigns through all empires, and at length is about to abolish all kingdoms by his glorious coming, when Christ is to reign with the elect in the kingdom of glory for ages of ages.

Furthermore, it is certain, unless the words are greatly twisted, that these ἀξιώματα (dignities) do not fit the Roman Empire, that it struck the four-metal statue and crushed the iron, brass, silver, and gold alike, and reduced them as if into chaff from the summer threshing floor, which the wind carried away, so that no place was found for them: and that after the statue was struck, it became a great mountain, filling the whole earth and standing forever. To say nothing of the fact that there is no reason why the Roman Empire should have borne the type of the Gospel, if it is the stone cut from the mountain without hands, as the mystical sense ought to agree with the primary and literal sense. Interpreters, as well as historians and politicians, certainly agree in this opinion; that by that four-metal statue the four Monarchies are shadowed forth, for which reason the Roman Empire, which is of the fourth Monarchy, cannot be signified by the cut stone. Finally, we add the confession of Grotius himself from book 5 of De Veritate Religionis Christianae. §. 14. where he acknowledges, and proves also from the Jews, that by that Stone Christ is to be understood; dealing with the signs of the time of the Messiah; With this sign of time (namely, the seventy weeks) agrees another, concerning the empire being given divinely over all nations, after the posterity of Seleucus and Lagus had ceased to reign, the latter of which ended in Cleopatra, not long before Jesus was born. In the Annotations to these words of his, Grotius has these things: R. Levi Ben Gerson handed down that that stone, by whose striking that image having the figure of empires was to be crushed, is the Messiah: and R. Solomon, R. Abenesdra, and R. Saadia teach that that kingdom which is to take over the other kingdoms is the kingdom of the Messiah.

Latin:

Vers. 32. HUJUS STATUÆ CAPUT] Pars statuæ quo superior, eo priora; quo inferior, eo feriora tempora significat.

Consentieunt autem in eo interpretes facile cum Judæi, tum Christiani, quod per lapidem istum designetur Christus Rex noster, vel regnum Christi, etsi Judæi id ad Messiam suum Utopicum & fi- ctitium, quem expectant, trahant. Et Chri- stum lapidi comparari notissimum est, è Psal. 118. Es. 8. & 28. capp. Abscissum autem sine manibus de monte Christum dici plerique interpretes Chri- stiani volunt, quod sine virili opera prognatus; vid. Justinus dial. cum Tryph. Irenæus lib. 3. cap. 28. Cyprianus l. 3. adv. Jud. Epiphanius Serm. de laud. virg. Hieronymus Epist. ad Eustoch. de custod. Virg. c. 22. Augustin. Tr. 9. in Joh. Theodoretus in h. l. etsi hic notet, quod ortus supra naturam soleat lapidis excisio nominari. Petra enim ex se naturaliter aliquid producere aut generare non solet, nec valet. Quo facit, quod Es. 52. habetur; Attendite ad petram unde excisi, & ad cavernam laci, de qua præcisi estis, quia Isaac & Ebræi ex sterili Sara procreati sunt su- pra naturam, perinde ac si de petra præcisi essent.

EX AURO OPTIMO] Id est, maxima cum gloria. infra 37.

BRACHIA DE ARGENTO] Minore cum glo- ria. infra 39.

VENTER ET FEMORA EX ÆRE] Animo in- victo. Tale illud: Illi robur & as triplex Circa pectus erat. Et frens ænea Esa. 48, 4. id est, firma, immobilis.

Vocem מְעוֹהִי etsi intestina notet, Synecdoch. pro continenti ventre poni non tantum consensus

De monte autem abscissus dicitur, sive quia de po- pulo & Ecclesia Judaica, quæ inter gentes quasi mons eminebat,uti explicat August. tr.9. in Johan- nem & tr. 1. in 1. Joh. Epist. 1. sive quia de Maria virgine,quæ quasi mons erat ob gratiarum & virtu- tum sublimitatem,ut Hieronymus & Theodor.de- clarant. Prior tamen sensus convenientior est. Nam uti montium nomine regna hîc exprimun- tur,& gentes, ita Christus lapis ille pretiosus excisus est è gente Israelitica,& stirpe Regia,quia natus est ex Patribus secundum carnem.Quòd autem sine ma- nibus abscinditur,modum nativitatis prorsus ἐξαί- ρετον & peculiarem notat, quod natus sit sine viri opera aut virtute,sola Spiritus Sancti δυνάμει. Con- fer. B. Gesnerus in h. l. Aliter B. Lyserus pag. 163. Per montem hic nihil aliud intelligimus, quam cœ- lum. Sicut David loquitur: Levavi oculos meos in montes, de quibus mihi auxilium venit. Auxi- lium meum à Domino, qui fecit cœlum & terram. Christus enim de cœlo descendit, unde Propheta dixit: Egressus ejus ab initio, & à diebus æternitatis: Et Baptista de Christo dicit: qui desursum venit, super omnes est. Qui est de terra,de terra est,& de ter- ra loquitur.Qui autem de cœlo venit,super omnes est. Abscissus autem est sine manibus, hoc est, absq; omni hominum merito,ex mera Dei gratia. Osiander explicat de adventu Christi novissimo: Sine mani- bus lapis abscissus significat Christum, qui est petra su- bito superventurum mundo in novissimo die: non ali- ter, quam si petra aliqua grandis à monte avulsa per præceps mole sua ruens, maximo cum fragore obvia quæq; prosternat atq; conterat.Et hic lapis Chri- stus etiam hodie, sed invisibiliter tamen totum mun- dum implet, omnia præsens gubernat: ascendit enim super omnes cœlos, ut omnia impleat, Ephes. 4. Et post hanc vitam visibiliter omnibus aderit electis in omnem æternitatem. Posset etiam hæc lapidis avulsio à monte sine manibus facta de ortu regni Christi intelligi, quod è monte Zion prodiit, ac sine manibus humanis excisum inde fuit,ac quamvis ceu lapis abjectus & reprobatus Rex Christus habere- tur, evasit tamen lapis ille in montem ingentis ma- gnitudinis, in regnum ampliffimum, ut univer- sam terram impleret Psal.2. Psal. 72. Esa. 2. Mich. 4. Col. 1. ut reliqua regna omnia comminueret, si- bique subjiceret; quia regnat per universa impe- ria, ac tandem aboliturus est omnia regna adventu suo glorioso, cum electis in regno gloriæ Christus regnaturus in seculorum secula.

Porro certum est,nisi verba valde torquean- tur,non convenire ImperioRomano hæc ἀξιώμα- τα,quod statuam sesραμέταλλον percusserit univer- sam,& contriverit pariter ferrum,æs, argentum & aurum, ac redegerit quasi in paleas de area æstiva, quæ vento abrepta,ut nullus eis locus inventus sit: quodque percussa statua factus sit mons magnus, universam terram implens, & in æternum consi- stens. Ut taceam nulla ratione Imperium Roma- num typum Evangelii gessisse,si id sit lapis de monte sine manibus abscissus,uti congruere oportet sen- sum mysticum sensui primario, & literali. Conve- niunt utique interpretes,ut & Historici, & Politici in hac sententia; quod per statuam illam τετραμέ- ταλλον quatuor Monarchiæ adumbratæ sint, qua- propter per lapidem excisum Romanum Imperium, quod est quartæ Monarchiæ, significari nequit. Addimus deniq; confessionem ipsiusmet Grotii è l. 5. de Verit. Rel. Christ. §. 14. ubi agnoscit, & è Judæis quoque probat, per Lapidem illum Chri- stum intelligendum esse; agens de notis temporis Messiæ; Cum hac nota temporis (LXX. sc. septima- narum) congruit altera,de imperio in omnes nationes dando divinitus, postquam Seleuci & Lagi posteritas regnare desiisset, quarum posterior in Cleopatra de- fiit, non multo antequam Jesu nasceretur. In An- notatis ad hæc verba sua Grotius hæc habet: La- pidem illum, cujus percussu imago illa imperio- rum figuram habens comminuenda esset, Messiam esse tradidit R. Levi Ben Gerson: & regnum il- lud cætera regna assumpturum, esse regnum Mes- siæ docent R. Salomo, R. Abenesdra, & R. Saa- dia.

## 2:33
Vers. 33. BUT THE LEGS OF IRON] Any violence breaking what is in its way. Below 40.

WHAT SHOULD COME TO PASS HEREAFTER] Concerning the Chaldeans and other nations of thy empire, among whom are also Syria and a great part of Egypt.

BUT PART OF CLAY] Fragile power. Below 42.

Latin:

Vers. 33. TIBIÆ AUTEM FERREÆ] Violentia quævis obvia frangens. Infra 40.

QUID ESSET FUTURUM POSTHAC] De Chaldæis & aliis gentibus imperii tui, in quibus sunt & Sy- ria, & Ægypti magna pars.

QUÆDAM AUTEM FICTILIS] Potentia fragilis. Infra 42.

## 2:34
Vers. 34. UNTIL A STONE WAS CUT OUT FROM THE MOUNTAIN WITHOUT HANDS] The army of the people, which was of its own will, and obeyed no King; the origin of which people is from a mountain, namely the Palatine. See Virgil book 8 of the Aeneid, Livy book 1. The same stone, and the son of man. Moreover, the Roman empire in this matter bore no obscure type of the Gospel, which, having arisen from heaven from small beginnings, grew to an immense size.

This gloss is new, and hitherto, I believe, unheard of: that by the stone cut from the mountain without hands the Roman Empire is signified, as an army of the people which was of its own volition, and that that Roman Empire bore the type of the Gospel. Grotius invented this according to his own genius.

Furthermore, the interpretation of the θεόπνευστος [God-breathed] St. Daniel does not agree. For he interpreted that stone in a far different way, namely, concerning the eternal kingdom of Christ: and not concerning the Roman Empire, as we shall note at verse 44. Nor does this gloss fit the description of the stone, for the stone is said to be cut from the mountain without hands; where what Grotius has here is too jejune; that the Roman Empire has its origin from the Palatine mount, and was of its own volition, an army of the people obeying no King. Which, moreover, everyone sees to be ἀσύγκλωσα [incoherent]. And how in the days of the other empires was that stone cut, or the Roman Empire raised up? How did it crush all the rest? How did it become such a great mountain that it filled the whole earth? How is it a kingdom, that is, one which will not be dissipated for eternity? Finally, it is beyond controversy among almost all interpreters that the Roman Empire is the fourth Kingdom, which is like iron, in this vision, v. 40. Therefore, the stone cut from the mountain cannot be the Roman Empire itself.

Latin:

Vers. 34. DONEC ABSCISSUS EST LAPIS DE MONTE SINE MANIBUS] Exercitus populi, qui suæ esset spontis, nullique Regi pareret; cujus populi origo à monte, nempe Palatino. Vide Virgilium libro 8. Æneidos, Livium libro 1. idem lapis, & filius hominis. Gessit autem in hac re im- perium Romanum non obscurum typum Evangelii, quod ortum de cœlo ab exiguis initiis, in immensum crevit.

Glossa hæc nova est, atque hactenus, credo, inaudita: per lapidem de monte abscissum sine mani- bus imperium Romanum, ceu exercitum populi, qui suæ spontis esset, notari, illudque Romanum imperium typum Evangelii gessisse. Hæc pro in- genio suo confinxit Grotius.

Porro non congruit interpretatio θεόπνευστος S. Danielis. Nam ille lapidem istum longe aliter in- terpretatus est, de regno nempe æterno Christi: non autem de Imperio Romano, ut ad versum 44. nota- bimus. Neque descriptioni lapidis convenit hæc glossa, nam sine manibus abscissus lapis dicitur de monte; ubi nimis jejunum est, quod hic habet Grotius; quod Romanum imperium originem a monte Palatino habeat, suaque spontis fuerit, nulli Regi parens exercitus populi. Quæ insuper ἀσύγ- κλωσα esse nemo non videt. Et quomodo in die- bus imperiorum cæterorum lapis ille abscissus, aut excitatum Romanum Imperium? Quomodo id reliqua omnia comminuit? quomodo mons tan- tus factum est, ut universam terram impleret? quo- modo regnum, id est, quod in æternum non dissi- pabitur? Denique penes omnes fere interpretes extra controverfiam est, Romanum imperium quartum Regnum, quod veluti ferrum, in hac vi- sione esse, v. 40. Non ergo lapis de monte abscif- sus ipsum imperium Romanum esse potest.

## 2:35
Vers. 35.

AS IF INTO CHAFF OF THE SUMMER THRESHING FLOOR, WHICH ARE TAKEN BY THE WIND] In the Chaldean: like chaff from the summer threshing floor, which the wind takes. IT BECAME A GREAT MOUNTAIN, AND FILLED THE WHOLE EARTH] A most wide empire is signified. Below 44.

Indeed, not only a most wide empire, but such a one is signified, as the letter of the text, from which one must not depart, has, that it extends through the whole earth: For that stone is said to have become a great mountain, AND TO HAVE FILLED THE WHOLE EARTH. Which has been fulfilled by nothing other than the kingdom of Christ: who rules from sea to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the ends of the earth, Psalm 72, 8. To whom the Father gave the nations as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth as a possession: Ps. 2, 7. Compare Rom. 10, 19. Col. 1, 23.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

QUASI IN FAVILLAM ÆSTIVÆ AREÆ, QUÆ RAPTA SUNT VENTO] In Chaldæo: sicut palea de area æstiva, quas rapit ventus. FACTUS EST MONS MAGNUS, ET IMPLE- VIT UNIVERSAM TERRAM] Latissimum Imperium significatur. Infra 44.

Imo non tantum latissimum imperium, sed ta- le significatur, ut litera textus, à qua discedendum non est, habet, quod per totam terram extenditur: Dicitur enim lapis ille factus in montem magnum, ET IMPLEVISSE UNIVERSAM TERRAM. Quod de nullo alio, quam Christi regno imple- tum est: qui dominatur à mari ad mare, & à flu- mine usq; ad terminos orbis terrarum Psalm. 72, 8. Cui pater dedit gentes hæreditatem, & possessio- nem terminos terræ: Psal. 2,7. Confer. Rom. 10, 19. Col. 1, 23.

## 2:37
Vers. 37.

THE GOD OF HEAVEN GAVE THEE THE KINGDOM, AND STRENGTH, AND EMPIRE, AND GLORY] The greatest splendor, so that the affairs of Nebuchadnezzar are said to have been greater than the affairs of that ancient Hercules, that is, Melcart. See the passages of Berosus and Megasthenes and Strabo in our Annotations to the books on the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

DEUS CŒLI REGNUM, ET FORTITUDI- NEM, ET IMPERIUM, ET GLORIAM DEDIT TIBI] Splendorem maximum, ita ut res Nabuchodonosori dican- tur rebus Herculis illius antiqui, id est, Melcarti, fuisse ma- jores. Vide Berosi & Megasthenis & Strabonis loca in Annotatis nostris ad libros de Veritate Religionis Christia- næ.

## 2:38
Vers. 38.

AND ALL THINGS IN WHICH THE SONS OF MEN DWELL] Many cultivated places. AND THE BEASTS OF THE FIELD] The desert places of Arabia and Africa. THE BIRDS ALSO] The impassable rocks, where only the birds keep themselves. AND HATH SET ALL UNDER THY DOMINION] A huge tract even to the pillars of Hercules. See the passage of Strabo. Nor should that seem so very wonderful, since the Saracen kings later advanced even that far. THOU ART THEREFORE THE GOLDEN HEAD] Thou, and thy successors, are those who are signified by the golden head.

Not only is Nebuchadnezzar considered here with his successors, but also with his predecessors, because the first universal Monarchy, over which he himself presided, is represented by the golden head, just as the other Monarchies are represented by the remaining parts of the statue. For Daniel does not designate Kings, but kingdoms. Therefore he expressly names the second and third and fourth kingdom; for which reason the first kingdom, without doubt, was also indicated here, and not only the King Nebuchadnezzar himself: because God wishes to teach how He transfers kingdoms from nation to nation, as the supreme Monarch, and true King of kings, and Lord of Lords. Therefore Grotius himself interprets that 'LESS THAN THEE' in verse 39 thus: less than thy kingdom. But why the Babylonian kingdom is compared to gold, in comparison with others, which in Jer. 51:7 is also called a golden cup, Daniel explains that: Thou art King of Kings, and the God of Heaven hath given thee the kingdom, and strength, and empire, and glory. Thou art therefore the golden head. And chap. 4:19. Thou O King art magnified, and thy greatness hath reached even unto the heavens, and thy power to the ends of the whole earth. Isaiah 47:5 calls Babylon the Lady of kingdoms; chap. 14:19, glorious among kingdoms and renowned. Jeremiah calls it the land of Lords, chap. 50:21. It is therefore called the golden head guilty, because the head indeed in this statue of the Empires of the world, that is, the first and most ancient Empire, was golden, not so much on account of opulence and splendor, as on account of happiness, glory, and excellence, because it was most happy, most glorious, most famous, and most extensive. Just as Jeremiah subjected all the nations then famous to Nebuchadnezzar, ch. 27, 7, and also called him the hammer of the whole earth, ch. 50, 23. And Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Daniel speak gloriously throughout about his dominion over the Jews and all nations. Tertullian, in his book against the Jews, says he reigned from India even to Ethiopia. Let those things also be seen which Josephus, in book 1 against Apion, and Eusebius, in book 10 of the Preparation for the Gospel, the last chapter, have produced from profane writers, Berosus, Manetho, Megasthenes, Philostratus, Abydenus, and others, concerning the glory of this Empire. whence Grotius observes, at verse 39, that the kingdom of the Persians and Medes was inferior to the Babylonian Empire, because Cyrus and his successors did not hold Africa. Blessed Gesner notes that the first Monarchy is called similar to good gold, not on account of the piety and virtue of the Emperors, but 1. on account of the divine bodily benefits most richly bestowed upon this Monarchy. 2. On account of the simplicity, candor, and integrity of the men at that time, which was greater than in later centuries, and finally because it was more tolerable to the people of God than the others.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

ET OMNIA IN QUIBUS HABITANT FILII HOMINUM] Loca culta plurima. ET BESTIÆ AGRI] Deserta loca Arabiæ & A- fricæ. VOLUCRES QUOQUE] Rupes invias, ubi solæ volucres se tenent. ET SUB DITIONE TUA UNIVERSA CON- STITUIT] Ingentem tractum ad Herculis usque co- lumnas. Vide Strabonis locum. Neque id mirum adeo videri debet, cum eo usque postea reges Sarraceni pro- cesserint. TU ES ERGO CAPUT AUREUM] Tu, & successores tui ii estis, qui per caput aureum significamini.

Non tantum consideratur hic Nabuchodono- sor cum successoribus, sed etiam cum præcessoribus suis, quia prima Monarchia universa, cui ipse præ- erat, aureo capite figurata est, quemadmodum cæteræ Monarchiæ figurantur reliquis statuæ par- tibus. Non enim Daniel Reges, sed regna desi- gnat. Ideo expresse nominat regnum alterum & tertium & quartum; quapropter etiam pri- mum regnum, sine dubio, hic indigitatum fuit, non autem solum Rex ipse Nabuchodonosor: quia docere vult Deus, quomodo regna trans- ferat de gente in gentem, ceu supremus Mo- narcha, & verus Rex regum, ac Dominus Do- minantium. Ideo Grotius ipse illud MINUS TE vers. 39. sic interpretatur, minus regno tuo. Cur autem regnum Babylonicum auro compare- tur, in συγκρίσει cum aliis, quod Jer. 51, 7. etiam calix aureus dicitur, id explicat Daniel: Tu Rex Regum es, & Deus Cæli regnum, & fortitudinem, & imperium, & gloriam dedit tibi.
