Tu es ergo caput aureum. Et cap. 4, 19. Tu Rex magnificatus es, & magnitudo tua pervenit usq; ad cælos, & potestas tua ad terminos universæ terræ. Esaias 47, 5. Babylonem appellat Dominam regnorum; cap. 14, 19. gloriosam in regnis & inclytam. Jeremias vocat eam terram Dominantium cap. 50, 21. Dicitur itaq; caput au- reum, quia caput quidem in hac Imperiorum mundi statua, hoc est, primum & antiquissimum Imperium fuit, aureum vero non tam ob opulentiam & splendorem, quam ob felicitatem, gloriam & præ- stantiam, quia felicissimum, gloriosissimum, famosissi- mum & amplissimum fuit. Quemadmodum Jere- mias omnes gentes tunc celebres Nabuchodono- sori subjecit cap. 27, 7. eumque etiam Malleum uni- versæ terræ nuncupavit cap. 50, 23. Et de ejus in Judæos, gentesque universas dominatu Jeremias, Ezechiel, Daniel passim gloriose loquuntur. Ter- tullianus l. contra Jud. regnasse eum dicit ab India usq; ad Æthiopiam. Videantur etiam quæ de glo- ria hujus Imperii è prophanis Scriptoribus, Bero- so, Manethone, Megasthene, Philostrato, Abydeno & aliis produxere Josephus lib. 1. contr. Appion. Eu- sebius lib. 10. præp. Evang. cap. ult. unde Grotius Babylonico Imperio minus regnum Persarum & Me- dorum fuisse, observat ad v. 39. quod Cyrus & succes- sores ejus Africam non tenuerint. B. Gesnerus auro bono similem dici primam Monarchiam notat, non ob Imperatorum pietatem & virtutem, sed 1. ob be- neficia divina corporalia locupletissime in hanc Mo- narchiam collata. 2. Ob hominum eo tempore simplicitatem, candorem & integritatem, quæ ma- jor fuit, quam posterioribus seculis, & denique quod populo Dei fuit tolerabilior, quam cætera.

## 2:39
Verse 39. ANOTHER KINGDOM SHALL ARISE] Coalesced from the Medes and Persians, which are the two arms. Cyrus himself was a Medo-Persian, a Mede by his mother, a Persian by his father, whence he was called ἡμίονος (mule). These two arms are named in Isaiah 21, 2.

INFERIOR TO THEE] Inferior to thy kingdom: because Cyrus and his successors did not hold Africa.

The Chaldean text does not have INFERIOR TO THEE: as indeed the Vulgate and Vatablus explained it with the LXX, but 'lower than thee,' just as the word אֲרַע in Genesis 1, 6 and chapter 6, 16 is used in the Targum; nor does it make mention of silver; but 'lower' is to be understood not so much in respect of place as of status and condition, if it is estimated by the inconveniences of continuous wars, the tragic death of the Persian Emperors, the ruin contracted in the adverse battles of Xerxes, Darius, and others, shorter duration, and other difficulties, by which this empire was more unhappy than the former, as even Dr. Svaningius admits.

AND ANOTHER THIRD KINGDOM OF BRASS] Which is called below the kingdom of אֲרַע, that is, of the Greeks, namely of Alexander, who, supported by the forces of all Greece, subdued the Persians and Medes.

While it is called 'another,' the distinction of this from the former is sufficiently designated: therefore the added word 'brazen' does not denote only a discrepancy, as Dr. Svaningius thinks, but also imports some reason for diversity, whatever that may be: for when compared with the golden head, that is, the empire of Nebuchadnezzar, and the silver breast of the Persian empire, the Kingdom of the Greeks, in its greatest part, whence the denomination is deservedly made, can be considered brazen on account of its inferior condition, from which, after the death of Alexander, it was miserably torn apart.

WHICH SHALL BEAR RULE OVER ALL THE EARTH] Namely, over that which the Medo-Persians had held, and partly even beyond.

This will be more correctly understood partially and relatively, as they say, that is, by reason of the empire of Alexander the Great, so that this empire is to be considered brazen, and indeed viler as far as his successors are concerned: yet it is the greatest and very remarkable as far as the beginnings and the rule of the first Monarch in this kingdom are concerned: concerning which 1 Maccabees 1, 3: he passed even to the ends of the earth: and in his sight all the earth was silent. See also Justin, book 12; Pliny, Natural History, book 6, chapter 16, and book 4, chapter 10. For they note that the principal part of Europe, all Syria, and Egypt, the whole of Asia, and finally India as far as the Ganges and the Ocean, obeyed him.

Latin:

Vers. 39. CONSURGET REGNUM ALIUD ] Ex Medis & Persis coalitum, quæ duo brachia. Cyrus ipse Medopersa, Medus è matre, Persa à Patre, unde dictus ἡ- μίονος. Duo hæc brachia nominantur Es. 21, 2.

MINUS TE] Minus regno tuo: quia Cyrus & suc- cessores ejus Africam non tenuerunt.

Chald. textus non habet MINUS TE: uti quidem cum LXX. Vulgatus & Vatablus exposuê- re, sed inferius te, quemadmodum vox אֲרַעא Gen. 1, 6. c. 6, 16. in Targum usurpatur; neque argenti mentionem facit; inferius autem intelligendum non tam loci respectu quam status & conditionis, si æ- stimetur eadem è bellorum continuorum incommo- dis, tragica Imperatorum Persicorum morte, contracta Xerxis, Darii & aliorum adversis præliis labe, brevio- ri duratione, aliisq́; difficultatibus, quibus hoc impe- rium priori infelicius fuit, fatente etiam Dn. D. Sva- ningio.

ET REGNUM TERTIUM ALIUD ÆREUM] Quod infra dicitur regnum אֲרַע, id est Græcorum, Alexan- dri scilicet, qui viribus Græciæ totius subnixus, Persas ac Medos subegit.

Dum aliud dicitur, distinctio hujus à priori satis designata est: non ergo vox addita æreum solum discrepantiam notat, ut Dn. Svaningius putat, sed rationem etiam aliquam diversitatis, quæcunque tandem illa sit, importat: Comparatum enim cum aureo capite, hoc est, imperio Nebucadnezaris, & argenteo pectore Persici imperii, Græcorum Regnum maxima sui parte, unde merito denominatio fit; æreum ob conditionem sequiorem, ex quo post mortem Alexandri misere dilaceratum est, censeri potest.

QUOD IMPERABIT UNIVERSÆ TERRÆ] Nempe ei quam Medopersæ tenuerant, partim etiam ultra.

Rectius intelligetur hoc μερικῶς & respecti- ve, ut loquuntur, hoc est, ratione imperii Alexandri M. ut ita æreum, & vilius quidem hoc imperium qua successores habendum sit: maximum tamen & val- de insigne qua primordia & imperium primi in hoc regno Monarchæ: de quo 1. Macc. 1, 3. pertransiit usq́; in fines terræ: & in ejus conspectu siluit omnis terra. Vid. & Justin. l. 12. Plin. lib. 6. Hist. Nat. c. 16. l. 4. c. 10. Huic enim præcipuam partem Eu- ropæ, omnem Syriam, & Ægyptum, univer- sam, Asiam, denique Indiam ad Gangen usque & Oceanum paruisse notant.

## 2:40
Verse 40. AND THE FOURTH KINGDOM SHALL BE AS IRON] The kingdom of the Seleucids and the Lagids is called one: but yet divided, as follows: one, because both houses are from Macedonia, and the borders are uncertain, and often disturbed by wars.

IT SHALL BREAK IN PIECES AND BRUISE ALL THESE] It will treat the subjects harshly, but especially the Jews.

The sacred text does not allow this explanation concerning the Kingdom of the Seleucids and the Lagids. For just as the other three kingdoms exhibited a Monarchy, the Babylonian, the Persian, and the Greek, as Grotius does not deny, so Daniel openly indicates that the fourth Monarchy is designated here when he says: And the FOURTH Kingdom shall be as iron. How could it be signified more clearly that this is the fourth Monarchy? Nor indeed is the iron empire said to break in pieces and bruise the subjects, as Grotius perverts it, but ALL THINGS. It is one thing to treat subjects harshly, another to break in pieces and bruise other empires: which are as different as heaven and earth. Moreover, that the Roman Empire, not that of the Seleucids, is noted is taught (1.) by the consequence; because no other kingdom succeeded the Greek Monarchy, which is called the third kingdom, that brought all things under its power, except the Roman. For the Romans subdued them with arms, as Blessed Polycarp Lyserus has in his Babylonian Colossus, page 151. nations however powerful, and all kingdoms although most mighty: They subjected to themselves towards the South the Carthaginians, then powerful in Empire, with Africa. Towards the North the Germans and Gauls, most warlike nations: Towards the West the Spaniards, famous for strength and wit: Yea, they even subjected those more remote. Macedonia around the times of the Maccabees, with King Perseus captured by Paulus Aemilius, Syria and Asia by Lucullus and Pompey, with Mithridates and Tigranes overcome, Egypt by Augustus, with Cleopatra overcome, who was the last of the family of the Lagidae. Not counting here the Jews, Cappadocians, Armenians, Iberians, Albanians, Scythians, the Islands, and the Britons separated from the whole world. So that the Roman power, as if iron, truly crushed all things and subjected them to itself, and thus was the greatest. Perhaps the ancients looked to this vision, because they assigned an iron crown to this Monarchy, which is kept at Aachen, and is placed upon the Caesar first, when he is crowned. (2.) These γνωρίσματα [marks] fit no other Empire, and those things which are held here concerning the iron feet mixed with clay, except the Roman, of which Halvicus in his Synopsis of Universal History, page 54, has this: It is compared to iron shins, for as iron crushes all things, so the Roman power, having tamed and worn down all things, rules through all the regions of the earth, which indeed are not inaccessible, but are inhabited by men, not only within the pillars of Hercules, but even the Ocean, wherever it is navigable, and the first and and alone in all the memory of men has placed the rising and setting sun as the boundaries of its empire, having dared to take upon itself the empire of the world, it constantly maintains dominion in all lands, nor is there any nation, so to speak, which does not acknowledge it as Mistress of all, or refuse its empire, as Dionysius of Halicarnassus says, book 1. Then, just as iron is the hardest; so this empire has lasted a very long time, and will last until the consummation of the world. Dan. 7. v. 9. 29. &c. cap. 2, 45. It is compared to feet partly of iron, partly of earthenware, because the Empire was to be divided, as the Prophet himself interprets, Dan. 2, 41. The toes of the feet are partly iron, partly earthenware, because the power of the empire would be now greater, now lesser, as the same explains in verse 42. (3.) Since Daniel testifies that in the time of those kings the Messiah would come, who was born under the Roman Monarchy, this empire cannot be explained otherwise than as the Roman Monarchy. (4.) Since the end of the fourth kingdom brings the summation of all kingdoms, necessarily the Roman empire, but not the kingdom of the Seleucids and Lagids is to be understood. (5.) That kingdom is understood in this place by the fourth, which is shadowed forth under the fourth beast. But we shall prove at chapter 7, 10, etc., that the successors of Alexander are not shadowed forth by it. (6.) Doctors with great consensus, both ancient and modern, understand by that iron kingdom the Roman Empire, indeed even Midrash Ps. 18 and Jacchiades. Therefore Jerome: The fourth kingdom clearly pertains to the Romans. It is iron, which crushes and tames all things: but its feet and toes are partly of iron and partly of clay, which is most manifestly proven at this time. For just as in the beginning nothing was stronger and harder than the Roman empire: so in the end of things nothing is weaker, indeed we are in need of the help of other barbarian nations both in civil wars and against diverse nations. Theodoret, he says, speaks of the Roman Kingdom, which was most robust, and, if I may say so, overcame all nations, and exacted tribute and tax from all. For he added, 'it will crush,' in order to signify this, and 'it will tame,' to indicate obedience, and order, and the legitimate administration of the republic. And Theodoret refutes the opinion of those who referred these things concerning the feet and the toes of the feet composed of iron and clay to the Ptolemies, and the Seleucids, and the Antiochi, and the Demetrii, from the sequence of the kingdoms: But it was necessary for them to notice first that he said the head was Nebuchadnezzar, that is, the kingdom of the Babylonians or Assyrians, which at the same time was taken over by the kingdom of the Persians and Medes; for Cyrus was born of both peoples, and ruling over these and those, he dominated the Persians after the kingdom of the Babylonians was overturned; but the kingdom of the Persians, which was the second, Alexander the Macedonian demolishes, whom blessed Daniel also said dominated the whole earth. He called this the third kingdom, to which no other succeeded except the Roman. It was necessary, therefore, for them first to understand and perceive from the number and the matters declared besides, that the third was the kingdom of the Macedonians, that is, brass, but the fourth that of the Romans, that is, iron. But if those things seemed altogether more obscure to them, yet certainly every prediction ought to have been discerned by them from the event. For as soon as he showed the weak and clay-like end of the iron Kingdom, he immediately added, and in the days of their Kings, that is, of the clay and iron, who embraced commerce and mutual kinship, yet were not concordant even because of the kinship: The God of heaven will raise up a Kingdom, which will not be corrupted for ages, and its kingdom will not be left to another people, it will crush and winnow all kingdoms, and it itself will stand forever, just as you saw, because a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and it crushed the clay, and the iron, the brass, the silver, the gold. But in the days of those kingdoms the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom, which will not be dissipated forever, and its kingdom will not be handed over to another people, but it will crush and consume all kingdoms, and it itself will stand forever. These things openly show the end of present things, but the kingdom of the heavens lacking an end. For when the iron kingdom shall have been weakly affected, and mixed with clay, then the stone cut without hands will appear, and will crush the clay, the iron, and the brass, the silver and the gold, and will reduce them utterly to nothing: and it will provide an everlasting kingdom, devoid of succession and end, to those who shall be worthy of it: for it says, it will not be corrupted forever, and will not be left to another people, and it will crush, and tame all kingdoms, and it itself will stand forever. But if anyone should object, and not wish these things to be so, let him show from human affairs what is eternal, and what kingdom of men is to be without an end. For it is foolish, and altogether insane to expect the end of the present age, and to assert that some kingdom in the present life will be without an end. But if to some it also seems that by these words that kingdom is signified which God is about to bestow upon the worthy, then he did not call the Macedonian kingdom iron, for neither was an end imposed upon the present life while it was flourishing. But the Roman, with the Macedonian overturned, holds the helm of the world. Calvin himself notes this consensus on Dan. 2. This matter, he says, IS BEYOND CONTROVERSY, whoever are endowed with sound judgment and also candidly desire to expound the mind of the Prophet, understand it of the four Monarchies. And afterwards: Meanwhile it is true what I said, namely that interpreters, who possess even mediocre judgment and candor, ALL to one expound this place concerning the Babylonian, Persian, Greek, and Roman Monarchy. And Daniel himself will show sufficiently in his own words afterwards.

Latin:

Vers. 40. ET REGNUM QUARTUM ERIT VEL- UT FERREUM] Seleucidarum, & Lagidarum unum dicitur regnum: Sed divisum tamen, ut sequitur: unum, quia utraque domus è Macedonia, & fines incerti, bellis- que sæpe turbati.

COMMINUET ET CONTERET OMNIA HÆC] Dure tractabit subditos, maxime vero Judæos.

Explicationem hanc de Regno Seleucidarum & Lagidarum non patitur textus sacer. Nam uti reliqua tria regna Monarchiam exhibebant, Baby- lonicam, Persicam & Græcam, non dissitente Grotio, ita quartam Monarchiam hic designari aperte indi- cat Daniel, cum ait: Et Regnum QUARTUM erit velut ferreum. Quomodo clarius significari po- terat, quod hæc quarta sit Monarchia? Neque vero ferreum imperium comminuere, & conterere dicitur subditos, ut pervertit Grotius, sed OMNIA. Aliud est dure tractare subditos, aliud comminuere & conterere imperia alia: quæ toto cœlo diversa sunt. Imperium autem Romanum, non Seleuci- darum, notari docet (1.) consequutio; quia Græco- rum Monarchiæ, quæ regnum tertium dicitur, nullum aliud regnum successit, quod universa in potestatem suam redegerit, quam Romanum. Nam Romani armis subegêre, ut habet B. Polycarpus Ly- serus in Coloss. Babylonico pag. 151. gentes utcunque prævalidas, & omnia regna licet potentissimo: Subje- cerunt sibi versus Meridiem Carthaginenses, tunc Imperio potentes, cum Aphrica. Versus Septentrio- nem Germanos & Gallos bellicosissimas gentes: Ver- sus occasum Hispanos, robore & argutiis claros: Imo etiam remotiores subjugarunt. Macedoniam circa tempora Maccabæorum, capto Rege Perse, per Pau- lum Æmilium, Syriam & Asiam per Lucullum & Pompejum, superato Mithridate & Tigrane, Ægy- ptum per Augustum, superata Cleopatra, quæ postre- ma fuit ex Lagidarum familia. Non numeratis hic Judæis, Cappadocibus, Armenis, Iberis, Albanis, Scy- tis, Insulis & toto terrarum orbe disjunctis Britannis. Ut ita potentia Romana, ceu ferrea, vere omnia com- minuerit, & sibi subjecerit, sicq́; maxima fuerit. Fortassis veteres ad hanc visionem respexerunt, quod huic Monarchiæ ferream coronam assigna- runt, quæ Aquisgrani asservatur, & Cæsari pri- mo imponitur, quando coronatur. (2.) Nulli alii Imperio hæc γνωρίσματα conveniunt, & quæ de ferreis pedibus luto commixtis hic habentur, nisi Ro- mano, de quo Halvicus in Synopsi Historiæ univer- sal. pag. 54. ita habet: Comparatur tibiis ferreis, ut enim ferrum omnia comminuit, ita Romana potentia, domitis & attritis omnibus, imperat per cunctas ter- ræ plagas, quæ quidem inaccessæ non sunt, sed ab homi- nibus habitantur, non solum intra columnas Herculis, verum etiam Oceano, quacunq́; est navigabilis, primaǵ; & sola in omni hominum memoria ortum & occasum terminos imperii sui posuit, ausa orbis imperium sibi sumere, dominium omnibus in terris constanter obti- net, nec est ulla gens, ut sic dicam, quæ non agno- scat universorum Dominam, aut detrectet ejus im- perium, sicut inquit Dionysius Halicarnass. lib. 1. Deinde sicut ferrum est durissimum; ita hoc im- perium diutissime duravit, & durabit ad con- summationem mundi. Dan. 7. v. 9. 29. &c. cap. 2, 45. Pedibus comparatur ex parte ferreis, ex parte fictilibus, quod divisum sit futurum Imperium, In- terprete ipso Propheta Dan. 2, 41. Digiti pedum partim ferrei sunt, partim fictiles, quod modo major, modo minor potentia imperii futura, ut idem exponit vers. 42. (3.) Quum testetur Da- niel, tempore regum istorum Messiam venturum, qui sub Romana Monarchia natus est, non potest hoc imperium aliter, quam de Romana Monarchia explicari. (4.) Quum quarti regni finis adferat con- summationem omnium regnorum, necessario Ro- manum imperium, non vero Seleucidarum & La- gidarum regnum intelligendum. (5.) Illud Re- gnum per quartum intelligitur hoc loco, quod sub quarta bestia adumbratum est. Successores autem Alexandri non adumbrari per eam ad caput 7, 10. seqq. evincemus. (6.) Doctores magno consensu tum veteres, tum recentiores per ferreum illud regnum, Imperium Romanum intelligunt, imo etiam Midrasch. Ps. 18. & Jacchiades. Ideo Hiero- nymus: Regnum quartum perspicue pertinet ad Ro- manos. Ferrum est, quod comminuit & domat omnia: sed pedes ejus & digiti ex parte ferrei & ex parte sunt fictiles, quod hoc tempore manifestissime comprobatur. Sicut enim in principio nihil Romano imperio fortius & durius fuit: ita in fine rerum nihil imbecillius, quin & in bellis civilibus, & adversum diversas nationes aliarum gentium barbararum indi- gemus auxilio. Theodoretus, de Romano, inquit, Re- gno loquitur, quod robustissimum fuit, omnesq; natio- nes, ut ita dixerim, superavit, & ab omnibus tribu- tum & vectigal exegit. Illud enim comminuet, idcir- co adscripsit, ut hoc significaret, & illud domabit, ut indicaret obedientiam, & ordinem, ac legitimam rei- publicæ administrationem. Et refutat Theodore- tus illorum opinionem, qui hæc de pedibus, ac pedum digitis ex ferro & testa compositis ad Ptolemæos, & Se- leucorum, & Antiochos, & Demetrios retulerunt, ex consequentia regnorum: Oportebat autem ipsos a- nimadvertere primum ipsum dixisse caput esse aureum Nabuchodonosar, hoc est, Babyloniorum seu Assy- riorum Regnum, quod eodem tempore à Persarum & Medorum regno exceptum est; Cyrus enim ab u- traq; gente oriundus erat, & his atq; illis imperans Babyloniorum everso regno Persis dominatus est; re- gnum vero Persarum, quod secundum fuit, Alexan- der Macedo demolitur, quem etiam beatus Daniel dominatum esse dixit universæ terræ. Hoc regnum tertium vocavit, cui nullum aliud præterquam Roma- num successit. Oportebat itaq; ipsos primum ex nu- mero, & rebus præterea declaratis intelligere atque percipere, tertium esse Macedonum regnum, hoc est, æs, quartum vero Romanorum, hoc est, ferrum. Quod si omnino ipsis illa esse obscuriora visa sunt, at certe ab eventu oportebat omnem ab ipsis prædictionem discer- ni. Nam simul atq; ostendit ferrei Regni imbecil- lem & fictilem finem, statim subjecit, & in diebus Regum eorum, hoc est, fictilis & ferrei, qui com- mercium, mutuamq; cognationem complexi, ne propter cognationem quidem concordes fuere: Suscitabit Deus cœli Regnum, quod in secula non corrum- petur, & regnum ejus populo alteri non relinque- tur, comminuet & ventilabit omnia regna, & i- psum stabit in æternum, quemadmodum vidisti, quia excisus est de monte lapis sine manibus, & comminuit testam, & ferrum, æs, argentum, aurum. In diebus autem regnorum illorum suscitabit Deus cœli regnum, quod in æternum non dissipabitur, & regnum ejus alteri populo non tradetur, commi- nuet autem & consumet universa regna, & ipsum stabit in æternum. Hæc aperte ostendunt præsen- tium quidem rerum finem, regnum vero cœlorum fine carens. Cum enim ferreum regnum imbecilliter af- fectum fuerit, ac testæ commistum, tunc apparebit la- pis sine manibus excisus, & comminuet testam, fer- rum, & æs, argentum ac aurum, & ad nihilum ea prorsus rediget: regnumq; sempiternum successionis ac finis expers iis, qui digni eo fuerint, præbebit: in æ- ternum enim, inquit, non corrumpetur, & populo alteri non relinquetur, & comminuet, & domabit omnia regna, & ipsum stabit in æternum. Quod si quis repugnet, atq; hæc ita se habere nolit, ostendat il- le ex humanis rebus, quidnam sit æternum, & quodnam hominum regnum sit fine cariturum. Stultum enim est, atq́; admodum demens seculi præsentis expectare finem, & regnum aliquod in præsenti vitæ finis expers futurum asserere. Si vero aliquibus quoq́; videtur per hæc verba regnum illud significari, quod dignis impertiturus Deus est, non igitur Macedonicum re- gnum appellavit ferrum, neq́; enim illo vigente præ- senti vitæ impositus est finis. Sed Romanum, everso Macedonico, orbis terrarum clavos tenet. Calvinus ipse notat hunc consensum ad Dan. 2. Hoc ὄργυμα, inquit, EXTRA CONTROVERSIAM quicunque præditi sunt sano judicio & candide etiam cupiunt mentem Prophetæ exponere, intelligunt de quatuor Monarchiis. Et postea: Interea verum est quod dixi, nempe interpretes, qui & mediocri judicio pollent & candore, OMNES ad unum hunc locum exponere de Monarchia Babylonica, Persica, Græca & Romana. Et Daniel ipse postea suis verbis satis ostendet.

## 2:41
Ver. 41. OF THE PLANTING OF IRON] There will be an origin for them from strong kings.

Latin:

Vers. 41. DE PLANTARIO FERRI] Ortus illis erit ex validis regibus.

## 2:42
Ver. 42. THE KINGDOM WILL BE PARTLY SOLID AND PARTLY BROKEN] Now this part, now that will prevail. These things will be explained more fully below in chapter 11.

Latin:

Vers. 42. EX PARTE REGNUM ERIT SOLIDUM ET EX PARTE CONTRITUM] Modo hæc pars, mo- do illa prævalebit. Hæc fusius explicabuntur infra cap. II.

## 2:43
Ver. 43. THEY WILL INDEED BE MIXED WITH HUMAN SEED] That is, they will be glued together through marriages. Antiochus, called God by his own, took as wives Laodice and Berenice, the daughters of Ptolemy Philadelphus. Livy is the witness. And Magas, the father of Philadelphus, took Apame, the daughter of Antiochus, who had been the son of Seleucus: which Pausanias teaches us in the Attica: and Antiochus the Great gave his daughter Cleopatra in marriage to Ptolemy Epiphanes, as we shall say below. Polychronius explained all these things very well.

BUT THEY WILL NOT ADHERE TO THEMSELVES] Namely because, as Tacitus says, the desire for ruling is more burning than all passions. Plutarch to Demetrius: 'Thus for all the successors of Alexander, the continuous war made the connections of affairs and of ways concerning one thing more conspicuous and inflamed them more.'

JUST AS IRON CANNOT BE MIXED WITH CLAY] For those things are incompatible.

Although some analogy may somehow be found, by which these things are drawn back to the Seleucids and Lagids, it is not however permitted to conclude anything certain immediately from any similarity of some people, but it is necessary that all the προσκείμενα [additions/adjuncts] correspond exactly. Which can be said of no empire except the Roman. For because it is the fourth in order among the Empires which God deems worthy of the title of Monarchies; since after the Assyrians, Persians, and Greeks, no Monarchs can be named so called in the Biblical style, except the Roman Emperors, and under that empire the stone was cut from the mountain, filling the whole earth, and not indeed under the kingdom of the Seleucids. The Roman empire like iron crushed all kingdoms, because this was the last empire, subduing all things, and no force can resist it, so that it might be tamed and crushed. Its two legs are the empire of the east and the west: but the later Emperors in this Monarchy were far weaker, because part of the feet was iron, part earthenware, and the iron was mixed with earthenware from clay, since some of the later Emperors were more truly of clay and earthenware than of iron, although they retained something of the iron root, under whom the Roman empire was greatly attenuated. Concerning which Helvicus loc. cit. The toes of the feet are partly iron, partly earthen, which means the power of the empire would be sometimes greater, sometimes lesser, as the same explains in verse 42. Both of which can be seen exactly both in the division of the Empire into east and west, and in the defection of very many kingdoms, and the irruptions of the Barbarians, in the times of Theodosius and those following, when the Vandals, Huns, Alans, Goths, Franks, Suebi, Lombards, Saracens, etc., miserably tore the Empire apart, although more often repressed, and some even thoroughly destroyed, until Charlemagne, after the West had been abandoned by the Constantinopolitan Emperors, reunited a great part of it and raised up the Dynasty of the Germans, whom many very brave Heroes followed later in the Empire, and many weak ones too, who power; and thus no force, nor confederations, nor friendships contracted through marriages could accomplish anything, just as Daniel predicted in verse 43.

It is, however, especially to be noted that, although it had to be reduced to such infirmity, the Plant of iron was nevertheless to remain, and so much strength was always to survive that no one would be able to uproot it or destroy it completely before the last day, which we clearly perceive even this very day. For the ἀξίωμα and majesty of the Holy Roman Empire, which resides with the Germans, remains even now and will endure until the end of the world, above all other kingdoms: whence we rightly call our Emperor August and invincible.

Furthermore, what is held in verse 43 concerning the human Seed, or the conglutination through nuptials, was not fulfilled so much in the Antiochians as in the Roman Emperors. Which I am pleased to explain likewise in the words of our blessed Helvicius: I will not, however, bring forward what others adduce concerning Gnaeus Pompey and Julius Caesar his son-in-law, lest it be objected that Daniel is speaking of the Empire already decaying. But I will begin from that very time when the Roman Empire began to be enormously shaken. Therefore, in the family of Theodosius the Great, in whose times diverse barbarian hordes broke in in swarms, five or six examples occur of attempted consolidation and strengthening of the Empire through marriages. For (1.) Theodosius the Great, sent against the Goths by the Emperor Gratian and later made a partner in the Empire in the East, marries Gallia, the sister of Gratian. (2.) Gratian himself, having been previously admitted into the partnership of the Empire, had married the daughter of the Emperor Constantius. Marcellinus, book 29. (3.) Placidia, daughter of Theodosius the Great, granddaughter of Gratian through his sister, and sister of the Emperor Honorius, is given in marriage by her brother the Emperor to the General Constantius, and he himself is declared Caesar or successor in the Empire of the West, Prosper in his Chronicle, Sigebert, Jordanes. (4) From this marriage was born Valentinian III, Emperor of the West, who marries Eudoxia, the daughter of Theodosius II, his cousin, under the name of the Emperor in the East. Tripartite History, book 12, chapter 1, 13. (5.) From this marriage was born Eudoxia, who is given in marriage to Huneric by Genseric, King of the Vandals, the father of Huneric. (6.) For Eudoxia, the mother, after Valentinian III was killed, was forced to marry Maximus, the author of the slaughter. To be freed from this marriage, she summons Genseric, King of the Vandals, from Africa. He, therefore, having entered Italy and put Maximus to flight, carries off the Empress together with her two daughters, and later sends them back, having retained one, Eudoxia, whom he gave as a wife to his son. Marcellinus, Nicephorus. (7.) The other sister, Placidia, married Olybrius, Emperor of the West, who was sent into the West by Leo I and established as Emperor. (8.) Leo the Thracian, Emperor of the East, sends Anthemius to be Emperor of the West. His son, Fl. Martianus, takes as his wife Leontia, the daughter of the Emperor Leo. (9.) In the family of Theodoric of Verona, some examples exist. Now Theodoric of Verona was King of the Goths, who, after peace was made with the Emperor Zeno, by whom he was called Master of the Soldiers and Consul, and later the Western Empire was committed to him, strove to stabilize his kingdom with many marriages and affinities. For (the words are of Jordanes) having sent an embassy to Clovis, King

of the Franks, he seeks his daughter Audefleda for himself in marriage. Which he granted gratefully and willingly, believing that his sons Hildebert, Cheldebert, and Theldebert would be allied with the race of the Goths through this society, once a treaty was entered into. But that union did not contribute much to the concord of peace, because they often fought bitterly among themselves on account of the lands of the Gauls (so speaks Jordanes) and the Goth never yielded to the Franks while Theodoric lived. Therefore, before he had offspring from Audefleda, he had daughters whom he had begotten from a concubine while still in Moesia, one named Theudicodo and another Ostrogotho. These, as soon as he came into Italy, he joined in marriage to neighboring kings, one to Alaric of the Visigoths, and the other to Sigismund of the Burgundians. From Alaric, therefore, was born Amalaric. Whom his grandfather, while he cherishes and protects him in his boyhood years, now orphaned of both parents, finds Eutharic, son of Witericus, grandson of Beremund and Torismund, descending from the stock of the Amali, living in Spain, a man of youthful age, excelling in prudence, virtue, and bodily integrity. He makes him come to him and joins to him his daughter Amalafuentha in marriage. And so that he might fully expand his progeny, he sends Amalafreda, his own sister, the mother of Theodatus, who was later King, to Trasamund, King of the Vandals in Africa, as his wife, and he associates his granddaughter, her daughter Amalaberga, with Hermanfred, King of the Thuringians. Thus far the words of Jordanes. And after a few words he says: Nor was there a nation in the western part that did not serve Theodoric while he lived, either by friendship or by subjection. Behold five marriages with which Theodoric labored to fortify the Empire of the West, although in vain, as Jordanes teaches in the same place. See Paul the Deacon. & Otho of Freising, who describes his plan. (14.) The plan of Emperor Charlemagne may also be brought in here, when he attempted a union of both Empires again through the marriage of the Empress Irene, which he sought, since Irene had previously sent envoys to Charlemagne to ask for his daughter as a wife for her son. And Irene indeed consented to the marriage, and the marriage was ratified by both, but it was hindered by the nobles of the Greek Empire. Theophanes, Life of Eginhard. (15.) Otto II, German Emperor, married Theophania, daughter of the younger Roman Emperor of Constantinople, in the year 967. Others say she was the daughter of Emperor Nicephorus; understand stepdaughter. Sigebert, Regino, appendix to Witichind, Cuspinian on Otto 1 & 2, Luitprand. (16.) Philip Caesar, son of Frederick Barbarossa, married Irene, daughter of Isaac Angelus, Emperor of Constantinople. The daughter of Philip later married Otto IV for the sake of reconciliation. Nauclerus, Reusner in Genealogy. (17.) The marriages of Michael Palaeologus, John Vatatzes, and Irene, daughter of Andronicus the Elder, may also be brought in here. Nor do I doubt that more can be noted and observed by diligent readers of histories. These occurred to us at present.

Latin:

Vers. 43. COMMISCEBUNTUR QUIDEM HUMANO SEMINE] Id est, per nuptias conglutinabun- tur. Antiochus, Deùs à suis dictus Laodicen & Berni- cen uxores duxit Ptolemæi Philadelphi filias. Testis Li- vius. Et Magas Philadelphi pater Apamen duxit filiam An- tiochi, qui Seleuci fuerat filius: quod nos docet Pausa- nias in Atticis: & Antiochus Magnus Cleopatram filiam suam collocavit in matrimonium Ptolemæo Epiphani, ut in- fra dicemus. Omnia hæc optime explicavit Polychronius.

SED NON ADHÆREBUNT SIBI] Nempe quia, ut ait Tacitus, dominandi cupido cunctis affectibus flagran- tior est. Plutarchus Demetrio: ὅτως ἦν πᾶσι τοῖς Ἀλεξάν- δρε διαδόχοις ὄντα συνεχῆ πόλεμον αἱ  πραγμάτων, καὶ  τρόπων συνάφειαι περὶ ἑνὸς ἐποίεν ἐπιφανέστερον καὶ μᾶλλον ἐξέκαιον.

SICUTI FERRUM MISCERI NON POTEST TESTÆ] Sunt enim ista ἀσύγκλωσα.

Etsi aliqua analogia utcunq; inveniri possit, qua hæc retro ad Seleucidas & Lagidas trahantur, non tamen è quacunq; nonnullorum similitudine statim concludere certi quid licet, sed necessum est, ut omnia προσκείμενα ex asse congruant. Quod de nullo nisi Romano imperio dici potest. Quia e- nim quartum est in ordine Imperium ex iis, quæ Deus Monarchiarum titulo dignatur; quum post Assyrios, Persas, Græcos, nulli nominari possint Mo- narchæ stylo Biblico ita dicti, nisi Romani Impe- ratores, & sub illo imperio abscissus est lapis de monte, terram universam implens, non vero sub Seleucidarum regno. Romanum imperium velut ferrum comminuit omnia regna, quia hoc postre- mum fuit imperium, omnia subigens, eiq; nulla vis resistere potest, ita ut dometur, & comminuatur. Hujus crura duo sunt imperium orientis ac occiden- tis: sed pofsteriores in hac Monarchia Imperatores longe infirmiores, quia pars pedum ferrea, pars te- stæa & ferrum mistum testæ ex luto, siquidem non- nulli sequiorum Imperatorum verius lutei & te- stacei, quam ferrei fuere, etsi aliquid de radice fer- rea retinuerunt, sub quibus Romanum imperium valde fuit attenuatum. De quo Helvicus loc. cit. Digiti pedum partim ferrei sunt, partim fictiles, quod modo major, modo minor potentia imperii fu- tura, ut idem exponit vers. 42. Quod utrumq; tum in divisione Imperii in orientem & occidentem, tum in defectione regnorum plurimorum, & Barba- rorum irruptionibus, ad amussim videre est, tempo- ribus Theodosii & sequentibus, quando Vandali, Hunni, Alani, Gotti, Franci, Svevi, Longobardi, Saraceni &c. Imperium misere dilacerarunt, licet sæpius repressi, nonnulli etiam penitus deleti fuerint, usq́; dum occidentem ab Imperatoribus Constantinopo- litanis desertum Carolus Magnus magnam partem iterum conjunxit, & Germanorum Dynastiam excita- vit, quem in Imperio postea multi fortissimi Heroes secuti sunt, multi etiam imbecilles, qui tamen nun- quam ad pristinum florem & potentiam Imperium distractum potuerunt reducere, adeoǵ; nulla vis, ne- que confæderationes aut per conjugia contractæ ami- citiæ quicquam proficere potuerunt, quemadmodum Daniel prædixit v. 43.

Apprime tamen notandum, quamvis ad tan- tum infirmitatem redigendum fuerit, Plantarium tamen ferri permansurum, & tantum roboris su- perfuturum semper, ut nemo illud ante novissi- mum diem extirpaturus, aut penitus destructurus sit, quod & hodierno die manifeste perspicimus. Manet enim adhuc, & durabit ad finem mundi ἀ- ξίωμα & majestas sacri Romani Imperii, quod pe- nes Germanos est, præ cæteris regnis omnibus: Unde merito Imperatorem nostrum Augustum, & invictissimum appellamus.

Porro quod de Semine humano v. 43. habetur, seu conglutinatione per nuptias, id non tam in Antio- chis impletum, quam in Romanis Imperatoribus. Quod itidem B.Helvici nostri verbis exponere lu- bet: Non autem adducam, quod alii afferunt de Cneo Pompejo, & Julio Cæsare ejus genero, ne ex- cipiatur, Danielem loqui de Imperio jam labescen- te. Sed ab ipso eo tempore incipiam, quo enormi- ter labefactari Imperium Romanum cœpit. Igi- tur in Theodosii Magni familia, cujus temporibus catervatim barbarica diversa agmina irruperunt, quinque vel sex exempla occurrunt tentatæ con- solidationis & corroborationis Imperii per conju- gia. Nam (1.) Theodosius Magnus contra Gothos à Gratiano Imperatore missus, & postea consors Im- perii factus in Oriente ducit Galliam Gratiani so- rorem. (2.) Ipse Gratianus antea in Imperii socie- tatem adscitus duxerat Constantii Imperatoris fi- liam. Marcel. lib. 29. (3.) Placidia filia Theodosii Magni, Gratiani neptis è sorore, soror Honorii Im- peratoris, à fratre Imperatore nuptum datur Con- stantio Duci, & ipse Cæsar seu successor in Imperio occidentis declaratur, Prosp. in Chron. Sigeb. Jord. (4) Ex hoc conjugio natus Valentinus 3. Impera- tor Occidentis, ducit filiam Theodosii secundi con- sobrini sub Imperatoris in Oriente nomine Eudo- xiam. Tripart. lib. 12. cap. 1, 13. (5.) Ex hoc con- jugio nata Eudoxia, nuptum datur Hunerico à Gen- serico Vandalorum Rege, Hunerici patre. (6.) Eu- doxia enim mater Valentiniano 3. occiso, coacta fuit nubere Maximo cædis autori. Quo conjugio ut liberaretur, evocat Genserirum Vandalorum Regem ex Africa. Ille igitur in Italiam ingressus, fugato Maximo, Imperatricem una cum duabus fi- liis abducit, & postea remittit, retenta altera, Eu- doxia, quam filio uxorem dedit. Marcell. Niceph. (7.) Altera soror Placidia nupsit Olybrio Imperato- ri Occidentis, qui à Leone primo in Occidentem missus & Imperator constitutus fuit. (8.) Leo Thrax Imperator Orientis mittit Anthemium, ut sit Im- perator Occidentis. Ejus Filius Fl. Martianus ducit in uxorem Leontiam Imperatoris Leonis fi- liam. (9.) In familia Theodorici Veronensis ali- quot exempla extant. Fuit autem Theodoricus Veronensis Rex Gothorum, qui pace facta cum Zenone Imperatore, à quo Dux militiæ & consul appellatus fuit, & postea Occidentale Imperium ei commissum fuit, multis connubiis & affinitatibus regnum suum stabilire nisus fuit. Nam (verba sunt Jornandis) missa legatione ad Clidovæum Regem

Francorum, filiam ejus Audefledam sibi in matrimo- nium petit. Quam ille grate libenterque concessit, suos filios Hildebertum & Cheldebertum & Theldeber- tum credens hac societate cum gente Gothorum, inito fœdere, sociari. Sed non adeo pacis ad concordiam profuit illa conjunctio, quia sæpenumero propter Gal- lorum terras graviter inter se decertati sunt (sic lo- quitur Jornandes) & nunquam Gothus Francis ces- sit, dum Theodoricus viveret. Antequam ergo de Audefleda sobolem haberet, naturales ex concubina quas genuisset adhuc in Mœsia, filias habuit, unam nomine Theudicodo & aliam Ostrogotho. Quas mox ut in Italiam venit, regibus vicinis in conjugio copula- vit, unam Alarico, Vestgothorum, & aliam Sigis- mundo Burgundionum. De Alarico ergo natus est Amalaricus. Quem avus in puerilibus annis, utroque parente orbatum dum fovet atque tuetur, competit, Eutharicum Witerici F. Beremundi & Torismundi nepotem, Amalorum de stirpe descendentem in Hispa- nia degere, juvenili ætate, prudentia & virtute, cor- porisque integritate pollentem. Ad se eum facit venire, eique Amalafuentham filiam suam in matrimonium jungit. Et ut ad plenum progeniem suam dilataret, Amalafredam Germanam suam matrem Theodati, qui postea Rex fuit, Africæ Regi Vandalorumque con- jugem dirigit Trasemundo, filiamque ejus neptem suam Amalabergam Thuringorum Regi consociat Her- neenfredo. Hactenus verba Jornandis. Et post pauca inquit; Nec fuit in parte occidua gens, quæ Theodorico dum viveret, aut amicitia aut subjectione non deserviret. En quinque connubia, quibus Im- perium Occidentis munire Theodoricus labora- vit, quamvis frustra, ut eodem loco Jornandes do- cet. Vide Paul. Diac. & Oth. Frising. qui ejus con- silium describit. (14.) Potest & huc afferri Caroli Magni Imperatoris consilium, quando per nuptias Irenes Imperatricis in Oriente, quas ambivit, conjunctionem utriusque Imperii rursum molitus est, cum prius Irene legatos ad Carolum misisset, petitum filio suo filiam ipsius in uxorem. Ac Ire- ne quidem consensit in nuptias, fuitque matrimo- nium utrumque ratum, sed à proceribus Græci Im- perii impeditum. Theophan. Vita Eginhard. (15.) Otto secundus Imperator Germanus duxit Theophaniam, filiam Romani junioris Imperatoris Constantinopolitani, anno 967. Alii dicunt filiam Nicephori Imperatoris, intellige privignam. Si- geb. Regin. app. Witich. Culpinian. in Otton. 1. & 2. Luitpr. (16.) Philippus Cæsar Friderici Barbarossæ F. duxit Irenen Isaaci Angeli Imperatoris Con- stantinopolitani filiam. Filia Philippi postea nu- psit Ottoni 4. reconciliationis ergo. Naucler. Reus. in Genealog. (17.) Possunt & huc adferri Michaelis Paleologi, Johannis Bataris, Irenes An- dronici Senioris filiæ, connubia. Nec dubito à dili- gentibus Historiarum lectoribus plura annotari & observari posse. Nobis hæc in præsenti succurre- bant.

## 2:44
Verse 44. BUT IN THE DAYS OF THOSE KINGDOMS] While the kingdoms of Syria and Egypt were still standing. THE GOD OF HEAVEN WILL RAISE UP] Whose it is to raise up, preserve, and destroy empires, as above 37 and below 4, 20. A KINGDOM WHICH SHALL NOT BE DESTROYED FOR EVER, AND ITS KINGDOM SHALL NOT BE DELIVERED TO ANOTHER PEOPLE: AND IT SHALL STAND FOR EVER] The Roman Empire, which will remain perpetually, which will be the seat of the Church. The Church is in the Roman Empire, says Optatus, namely for the greatest part.

Latin:

Vers. 44. IN DIEBUS AUTEM REGNORUM IL- LORUM] Stantibus adhuc Syriæ & Ægypti regnis. SUSCITABIT DEUS COELIJ Cujus est excitare, servare, ac diruere imperia, ut supra 37. & infra 4, 20. REGNUM QUOD IN ÆTERNUM NON DIS- SIPABITUR, ET REGNUM EJUS ALTERI POPU- LO NON TRADETUR: ET IPSUM STABIT IN ÆTERNUM] Imperium Romanum perpetuo mansurum, quod sedes erit Ecclesiæ. Ecclesia in imperio Romano, ait Optatus, nempe maxima ex parte.

## 2:45
Verse 45. AND BROKE IN PIECES THE CLAY AND THE IRON] The Romans subjected Syria and Egypt to themselves. AND THE BRASS] Also Macedonia and Greece. AND THE SILVER] Also the kingdoms of Attalus, and of Nicomedes, and of Mithridates, which had belonged to Cyrus. AND THE GOLD] Armenia, Cappadocia, the Iberians, the Colchians, the Albanians, Tyre, Judea, possessed by Nebuchadnezzar.

A more sublime sense, that Christ will put an end to all earthly empires. 1 Cor. 15, 24.

The subject here is the stone cut out without hands, which we have taught, at verse 33, denotes not the Roman Empire, but the Kingdom of Christ, or Christ the King. And the ψευδερμηνεία (false interpretation) of Grotius is manifest here, since one must twist the text if a place is to be left for his gloss. For those words: IN THE DAYS OF THOSE KINGDOMS, speak manifestly of those four kingdoms, of which mention was made, and not of the kingdoms of Syria and Egypt, which, since Grotius wishes them to be indicated by the name of the fourth Kingdom, should not have been called 'in the days of the kingdoms,' but 'OF THAT KINGDOM,' namely the fourth; for Grotius wishes one kingdom of the Seleucids and Lagids to be indicated: although it has been shown that he is mistaken in this. Furthermore, lest anyone doubt that the days of those four kingdoms are meant, of which the Prophet had spoken, it is subjoined in verse 45. That the clay and iron, and likewise the bronze, as well as the silver and the gold in the statue, would be crushed, i.e., that all those four kingdoms would be crushed by the kingdom which God will raise up in the days of those Empires. This kingdom, therefore, cannot be the Roman Empire. Furthermore, since the discourse is about a Kingdom that will not be dissipated FOR EVER, WHICH SHALL STAND FOR EVER, the Roman Empire cannot by any means be understood. For this will not last for ever, but will have an end. Most openly, therefore, the kingdom of Christ is designated by this predicate, of which there shall be no end, Luke 1. Again, therefore, Grotius had need of a ψευδερμηνεία (false interpretation), or rather an open distortion, while he argues that by gold and silver, and bronze and iron, one should not understand those Monarchies and kingdoms, as Daniel had explained them—the Assyrian, Persian, Greek (for Grotius acknowledged that these three were predicted above, although he did not understand the fourth as the Roman Empire, and brought forward another interpretation)—but some part of the kingdoms. But the Prophet teaches that the whole kingdoms would be crushed. Just as he had taught that by gold the whole Monarchy of the Assyrians, by silver the whole Monarchy of the Medes and Persians, and by bronze the whole Monarchy of the Greeks was to be understood; whence an invincible argument: the discourse here is, according to the letter or the literal sense of the Prophet, about that kingdom raised up by the God of heaven in the days of the kingdoms of the world enumerated by Daniel, which crushes all those kingdoms shadowed forth by the gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay. But it is not the Roman Empire, but the Kingdom of Christ, that was raised up by God in the days of the kingdoms of the world; it is not the Roman Empire, but the Kingdom of Christ, that crushes all those kingdoms. For the Kingdom of Christ was raised up and preserved in the days of those four Monarchies: (for it did not begin only under the last one, even though Christ was born under it, as far as his temporal birth is concerned) and it crushes all those Empires, inasmuch as those three have already ceased to be, but the fourth will be destroyed at the consummation of the age. But the Kingdom of Christ will remain for ever. Then, indeed, the Kingdom of Christ also crushes worldly empires when Christ subjects them to his power and places them as a footstool for his feet, so that they may obey his command, or at least be encompassed by his power and iron rod, according to the Psalmist, Psalm 2, and Revelation 19, until they are utterly crushed. Therefore, there is no need for us to laboriously inquire here whether these things are to be referred to the first or to the second coming of Christ, since it looks to the kingdom of Christ which began from the beginning, in the first-created, and will endure until the consummation of the age (I speak of the kingdom of grace). It is not, therefore, only in a mystical and more sublime sense that it is noted that Christ will put an end to all earthly empires, but in a proper and literal sense. Of this, Isaiah 60:12: 'The nation and Kingdom that will not serve you shall perish, and the nations shall be wasted in solitude.' Of this, also, Christ himself, Matthew 22:44: 'Whoever shall fall upon this stone shall be broken, but upon whomsoever it shall fall, it shall crush him.' By which words he seems to look back to this place of ours, concerning the stone that would crush all kingdoms.

Latin:

Vers. 45. ET COMMINUIT TESTAM ET FER- RUM] Syriam & Ægyptum Romani sibi subjecere. ET ÆS] Etiam Macedoniam & Græciam. ET ARGENTUM] Etiam Attali, & Nicomedis, & Mithridatis regna, quæ Cyri fuerant. ET AURUM] Armeniam, Cappadociam, Iberas, Col- chos, Albanos, Tyrum, Judæam, possessa Nabuchodonosori.

Sensus sublimior, Christum finem impositurum omnibus imperiis terrestribus. 1. Cor. 15, 24.

Agitur hic de lapide sine manibus exciso, quem vero non Romanum Imperium, sed Regnum Chri- sti, vel Christum Regem notare ad vers. 33. docui- mus. Et manifesta hic est ψευδερμηνεία Grotii, quum torquere oporteat textum, si illi glossæ locus relinquendus. Nam verba illa: IN DIEBUS RE- GNORUM ILLORUM, manifeste de regnis illis quatuor loquuntur, quorum facta mentio, non ve- ro de Syriæ & Ægypti regnis, quæ quum nomine quarti Regni indicata esse velit Grotius, non di- cendum fuisset, in diebus regnorum, sed REGNI ILLIUS, quarti scilicet; Nam Seleucidarum & La- gidarum unum regnum indigitari, vult Grotius: quamvis in eo falli eundem ostensum sit. Adhæc ne quis ambigat, dies regnorum illo- rum quatuor intelligi, de quibus egerat Propheta, subjungitur vers. 45. Comminutum iri testam & fer- rum, itemque æs, nec non argentum, ut & aurum in statua, h. e. omnia illa quatuor regna contritum iri à regno, quod Deus in istorum Imperiorum die- bus excitabit. Hoc ergo regnum Imperium Ro- manum esse non potest. Porro quum de Regno non dissipando IN Æ- TERNUM, QUOD IN ÆTERNUM CON- STET, sermo sit, non potest utique Romanum Imperium intelligi. Hoc enim in æternum non durabit, sed finem habiturum est. Apertissime ita- que hoc prædicato designatur regnum Christi, cu- jus nullus finis erit, Luc. 1. Iterum ergo ψευδερμη- νεία opus habuit Grotius, vel potius aperta detor- sione, dum per aurum & argentum, & æs & ferrum, non Monarchias illas, & regna, quemadmodum ea explicaverat Daniel, Assyriacum, Persicum, Græcum (hæc tria enim supra prædicta esse agnovit Grotius, quamvis quartum non de Imperio Ro- mano intellexerit, & aliam interpretationem attu- lerit) intelligenda esse, sed partem aliquam regno- rum. At Propheta tota regna comminutum iri, docet. Quemadmodum per aurum totam Mo- narchiam Assyriorum, per argentum totam Medo- rum, & Persarum, per æs totam Græcorum Monar- chiam intelligendam esse docuerat; unde argu- mentum invictum; De illo regno suscitato à Deo cœli in diebus regnorum mundi à Daniele recen- sitorum hic sermo est, secundum literam, vel sen- sum literalem Prophetæ, quod omnia illa regna, per aurum, argentum, æs, & ferrum & testam adumbra- ta, comminuit. At non Romanum Imperium, sed Regnum Christi, suscitatum à Deo in diebus regno- rum mundi; non Romanum Imperium, sed Re- gnum Christi omnia illa regna comminuit. Nam Regnum Christi in diebus illis quatuor Monar- chiarum suscitatum, & conservatum est: (non enim cœpit demum sub novissima, etsi sub eadem Christus ortus sit, quoad temporalem nativitatem) & comminuit omnia ista Imperia, siquidem tria ista jamdum esse desierunt, quartum vero sub consum- mationem seculi destruetur. Regnum autem Christi æternum manebit. Tum vero comminuit etiam mundana imperia regnum Christi, quando Christus ea potestati suæ subjicit, & in scabellum pedum suorum ponit, ut suo pareant imperio, vel saltem complescantur potestate ipsius & virga fer- rea, secundum Hieropsaltem Psal. 2. & Apoc. 19. donec penitus conterantur. Proinde opus non est, ut operose quæramus hic, an ad primum, an vero ad secundum adventum Christi hæc referenda quum ad regnum Christi quod cepit inde à primor dio, in Protoplastis, usque ad consummationem se- culi duraturum (de regno gratiæ loquor) respicia- tur. Non ergo tantum sensu mystico & sublimiori notatur, Christum finem impositurum omnibus imperiis terrestribus, sed sensu proprio & literali. De eo Esaias 60, 12. Gens & Regnum, quod non ser- vierit tibi, peribit, & gentes solitudine vastabuntur. De eo etiam Christus ipse Matth. 22, 44. Qui cecide- rit super lapidem istum, confringetur, super quem vero ipse ceciderit conteretur. Quibus verbis hunc nostrum locum respicere videtur, de lapide con- trituro regna omnia.

## 2:46
Vers. 46.

HE FELL UPON HIS FACE] προσκυνεῖν (to worship), προσπίπτειν (to fall before), ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον (he fell upon his face), which we said have the same meaning in our fuller explanation of the Decalogue. AND WORSHIPPED DANIEL] He venerated him, as Livy speaks, in the same way as the captain of the guard venerated Elijah, 2 Kings 1:13; for those signs of honor were used even among men: nor was so great a Prophet unworthy of that honor. Tremellius is more correct, that he worshipped Daniel: because only an attempt is noted. See what is said at v. 47. AND COMMANDED THAT THEY SHOULD SACRIFICE GIFTS AND INCENSE TO HIM] In the Hebrew: He commanded that there be offered to him מנחה (that is, a meal offering of fine flour) and odors. He did indeed command it, but Daniel did not allow it: for the custom of the nations consecrated those honors to God, or to those who are held as gods. Thus here Jachiades and other Hebrews. Some wish that Nebuchadnezzar did not command this honor to be shown to Daniel, but to God in Daniel, because in the following verse he confesses God; but although the former words can be rendered thus, 'and he worshipped before Daniel,' yet these things concerning the sacrifices seem, even to those who render the former words thus, to be referred to Daniel himself: that, namely, he wished gifts and incense to be offered to him. We entirely approve the opinion of the blessed Luther and Dr. Geier, that the King did not worship Daniel, but worshipped before Daniel, because the prefix ל is taken in that way in Ps. 49:5, c. 39:17, Prov. 4:3, nor do we see any reason why the rest should not also be rendered in such a way that they should sacrifice BEFORE him.

Latin:

Vers. 46.

CECIDIT SUPER FACIEM SUAM] προσκυνεῖν προσπίπτειν, ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον, quæ idem valere dixi- mus, in ampliori explicatione Decalogi. ET DANIELEM ADORAVIT] Veneratus est, quomodo loquitur Livius, pari modo quo Eliam aulæ ma- gister 2.Reg. 1, 13. signa enim illa honoris etiam inter homi- nes usurpabantur:nec indignus eo honore tantus Propheta. Rectius Tremellius, ut Danielem adoraret: Quia conatus tantum notatur. Vid. quæ ad v. 47. ET HOSTIAS ET INCENSUM PRÆCEPIT, UT SACRIFICARENT EI] In Hebræo: Iussit ei offerri מנחה, (id est, libum è simila) & odores. Jussit quidem, sed non sivit id Daniel: eos enim honores Deo, aut iis qui pro diis habentur mos gentium sacravit. Ita hic Jacchia- des & Hebræorum alii. Nonnulli hunc honorem non Danieli sed in Daniele Deo exhiberi jussisse Nebucadn. volunt, quia vers. sequente Deum confitetur; sed quamvis verba priora ita reddi possint, & adoravit coram Daniele, hæc tamen de sacrificiis videntur etiam il- lis, qui priora sic reddunt, ad ipsum Danielem re- ferenda: quod nempe ei voluerit offerri dona & suffimenta. Nobis omnino placet B. Lutheri, & Dn. D. Geieri sententia, adorasse Regem non Da- nielem, sed coram Daniele, quia ita præfixum ל sumitur Ps. 49, 5. c. 39, 17. Prov. 4, 3. neque causam ullam videmus, cur non reliqua etiam ita reddan- tur, ut sacrificarent CORAM eo.

## 2:47
Vers. 47. THE KING THEREFORE SPEAKING] Instructed, namely, by Daniel that the honor of this revelation is owed to God.

This confession of the King confirms that the honor of adoration was shown not to Daniel, but to the true God before Daniel, and that sacrifices were to be offered to the same before Daniel. And although it is said that adoration and sacrifices were shown to Daniel himself, yet only the attempt of the King is noted, not the act itself or the admission of that honor, as the words of acts are sometimes to be explained as an attempt: Gen. 37:21, Ez. 24:13, Amos 9:3. Cf. Suaning. in h. l. HE IS THE GOD OF GODS] Greater than other gods. AND THE LORD OF KINGS] Lord here in Chaldean is מרא: whence in Etruria the kings were called Murani, as Servius teaches in Aeneid 12. Hence also Maranatha, and the Syrian Maranita, because they call Christ מראן our Lord. And Marnas, the idol of Gaza, according to Jerome, who [cites] Euripides in the Bacchae, and Nonnus in the Dionysiaca, [calling him] Μάρων.

Latin:

Vers. 47. LOQUENS ERGO REX] Institutus sci- licet à Daniele Deo honorem hujus revelationis deberi.

Hæc confessio Regis confirmat, non Danie- li, sed coram Daniele Deo vero honorem adora- tionis exhibitum, eidemq; coram Daniele sacrificia offerenda fuisse. Et licet Danieli ipsi adoratio, & sacrificia dicantur exhibita, tamen conatus tan- tum Regis non actus ipse aut admissio illius hono- ris notabitur, uti verba actuum de conatu quandoq; explicanda: Gen. 37, 21. Ez. 24, 13. Amos. 9, 3. Conf. Suaning. in h. l. DEUS DEORUM EST] Major diis cæteris. ET DOMINUS REGUM] Dominus hic in Chal- daico est מרא: unde in Ethruria reges Murani, docente id Servio 12. Æneid. Hinc & Maranatha, & Syri Maranita, quod Christum vocent מראן Dominum nostrum. Et Marnas idolum Gazæ, teste Hieronymo, qui Euripidi in Bacchis, & Nonno in Dionyfiacis Μάρων.

## 2:48
Vers. 48. HE APPOINTED HIM RULER OVER ALL THE PROVINCES OF BABYLON] In the Chaldean: over every province of Babylon: for there were many provinces in that empire. The Chaldean word is מדינתא, which the Arabs also use; whence also in many places in Spain the name Medina.

AND PREFECT OF THE MAGISTRATES] Chief prefect: because without doubt the first prefecture was the Babylonian one.

OVER ALL THE WISE MEN OF BABYLON] The 'and' is missing: he made him also the prince of his council. Vers. 49. AND HE APPOINTED OVER THE WORKS OF THE PROVINCE OF BABYLON SIDRACH, MISACH, AND ABDENAGO] That is, he substituted them for himself, the king willing it.

Latin:

Vers. 48. CONSTITUIT EUM PRINCIPEM SU- PER OMNES PROVINCIAS BABYLONIS] In Chal- dæo: supra omnem provinciam Babylonis: erant enim in il- lo imperio multæ provinciæ. Chaldaica vox est מדינתא, quam & Arabes usurpant; unde & multis locis in Hispania nomen Medinæ.

ET PRÆFECTUM MAGISTRATUUM] Primum præfectum: quia haud dubie prima præfectura erat Baby- lonica.

SUPER CUNCTOS SAPIENTES BABYLONIS] Deest &: fecit eum etiam principem consilii sui. Vers. 49. ET CONSTITUIT SUPER OPERA PRO- VINCIÆ BABYLONIS SIDRACH, MISACH, ET ABDENAGO] Id est, eos sibi substituit rege volente.

## 2:49
BUT DANIEL HIMSELF WAS AT THE KING'S GATES] In the Chaldean: In the gate of the king: that is, in the court, just as the Turks also speak now. Because he held a principal place in the royal council, for that reason he did not depart from the king, but used the help of friends to carry out the affairs of his prefecture. Therefore, not only judicial power is noted, as Vatablus wishes, which was exercised in the gates of cities, not of courts.

Latin:

IPSE AUTEM DANIEL ERAT IN FORIBUS REGIS] In Chaldaico: In porta regis: id est, in aula, quo- modo & Turcæ nunc loquuntur. Quia principem locum tenebat in consilio regio, ob id à rege non discedebat, sed ad res præfecturæ suæ peragendas amicorum utebatur opera. Non ergo judiciaria tantum potestas nota- tur, ut Vatabl. vult, quæ in portis civitatum, non aularum exercebatur.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refusing to adore the statue erected by Nebuchadnezzar, are bound and cast into a furnace of burning fire, but remain unharmed as an Angel restrains the flame; upon seeing this, the King sets them free, declares their God, forbids Him to be blasphemed by a severe edict, and grants those three great power.

Vers. 1. HE MADE A STATUE] Of the King, as is credible, Nabonassar; for it was the custom of kings to bestow divine honors upon their parents, for which use statues served.

Others say he made a statue of his own image out of ambition, as Jerome on Habakkuk 1 and in this place, as well as Chrysostom, Maldonado, Pinto, and Oecolampadius: others say it was in memory of the image seen in a dream, and in honor of the Monarchies of the world, but made of gold alone: either to overthrow the prophecy of the dream, or to display the eminence of his own glory, which would glitter like gold above all other empires. But since Nebuchadnezzar had already acknowledged and preached the true God, B. Luther more correctly thinks that the King wished to worship the same God with this golden statue, in an idolatrous manner, just as they did with the μοσχολατρεᾳ in the desert and the kingdom of Israel: to which εἰδωλολατρείαν the companions of Daniel refused to be driven.

GOLDEN] Pliny 33, 4. The first statue of all made of solid gold, and before any was made of bronze in that manner, which they call Holosphyron, is said to have been placed in the temple of Anaitis.

AND HE SET IT UP IN THE PLAIN OF DURA OF THE PROVINCE OF BABYLON] Theodotion has Δεεῖρα, or Δεηρᾶ, for the codices vary: whence it is believed by many that the πεδίον Δεηρᾶ is designated, which Ptolemy places in Susiana. But the province of Susiana is one thing, and that of Babylon another, and there is no precedent for taking מדינה for the whole empire: wherefore I think it more correct to take this name for that which is Δόραβα in Ptolemy in his description of Babylonia, and it is the more probable because Symmachus had placed Doraüm here, as Jerome teaches us.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Statuam à Nebucadnezare erectam adorare renuentes Sidrach, Misach & Abednego li- gati in fornacem ignis ardentis immissi il- lasi manent Angelo flammam cohibente, quo à Rege viso liberantur, & Rex Deum prædicat, eumq; blasphemari severo edi- cto vetat, tribus vero illis magnam pote- statem tribuit.

Vers. 1. FECIT STATUAM] Regis, ut credibile est, Nabo- donassari; mos enim erat regum parentes suos donare di- vinis honoribus, cui usui inserviebant statuæ.

ALii statuam suæ imaginis ex ambitione fecisse ajunt, cum Hieron. ad Hab. 1. & h. l. nec non Chrysost. Maldonato, Pinto, Oecolampadio: alii in memoriam imaginis in somnio visæ, & honorem Monarchiarum mundi, sed ex solo auro: sive ad convellendam somnii Prophetiam, seu ad ostentan- dam gloriæ suæ, auri instar coruscatura per o- mnia reliqua imperia eminentiam. Sed quum agno- verit jam Nebucadnezar & prædicarit verum De- um, rectius B. Lutherus, eundem hac aurea statua Regem colere voluisse, more idololatrico, uti μοσχο- λατρεᾳ in deserto & regno Israëlis fecêre: ad quam εἰδωλολατρείαν adigi socii Danielis noluerint.

AUREAM] Plinius 33, 4. Aurea statua prima omnium nulla inanitate, & antequam ex ære aliqua illo modo fieret, quam vocant Holosphyron, in templo Anaitidis posita dicitur.

ET STATUIT EAM IN CAMPO DURA PRO- VINCIÆ BABYLONIS] Theodotion habet Δεεῖρα, aut Δεηρᾶ, variant enim codices: unde multis creditur desi- gnari πεδίον Δεηρᾶ, quod in Susiana ponit Ptolemæus. At a- lia provincia est Susianes, alia Babyloniæ, & מדינה pro to- to imperio sumere exemplo caret: quare rectius arbitror accipere hoc nomen pro eo quod est Δόραβα Ptolemæo in Babyloniæ descriptione, eoque id probabilius quod Do- raüm hic posuerat Symmachus, ut nos docet Hieronymus.

## 3:2
Vers. 2. SATRAPS] אחשדרפניא in the singular Theopompus called ἐξατράπην, as we noted on Matthew 18:10. Others say Σατράπην, which Herodotus and most Greeks think is a Persian word. I would rather think that this word (as well as those that follow, which bear no Chaldean mark) came first from the Assyrians to the Chaldeans, and then to the Persians. You have that name in the Persian court, and not only among the Greeks, but also in Esther 9:3. Theodotion [translates it] ὑπάτους: Jacchiades interprets it as Bassas, taking the word from the Turkish empire, just as he compares the following names to Turkish ones.

MAGISTRATES] סגניא. It is the same name as above in 2:48, whom we said there were the prefects of the provinces. Theodotion [calls them] σφελίωνas, Jacchiades calls them Beglerbeys.

AND JUDGES] פחוותא are for Theodotion τοπάρχαι, as also in 2 Kings 18:24, Isaiah 36:9. For the Jacchiades, Agas. It appears they were lesser prefects under those greater ones. Ezra 2:7, 9; 5:3, 14; ch. 6:6, 13; ch. 8:35; below 6:7.

DUKES] אדרגזריא, that is, scribes, keepers of the decrees. See what is above in 2:27. These are the ἡγέμενοι in Greek.

AND TYRANTS] גדבריא are dispensers of money, as appears from the Chaldean version of Ecclesiastes 2:7. The same office is called גזבר in Ezra 1:8, and in the Chaldean end of Esther, and in the title of the Talmud concerning Shekels: indeed, ז and ד are easily interchanged among themselves: perhaps it is the Greek word γαζόφοροι. Theodotion said τὲς ἐπὶ ἐξεσιῶν. Jacchiades, in the Turkish manner, [calls them] Defterdars.

AND PREFECTS] דתבריא are Jurisconsults, to whom Jacchiades compares the Alphakis of the Turks. To these the Chaldean text here adds תפתיא, whom Saadia interprets as janitors, and Jacchiades as Doctors of the law.

AND ALL THE PRINCES OF THE PROVINCES] שלטני are those who preside not over prefectures or provinces, but over individual cities and suburban regions. See above 2, 10. The word מדינתא signifies a region, and is sometimes broader, sometimes more restricted. Jacchiades compares the Zangiahi to these.

Concerning all these names of dignities or offices, see especially our Lord Dr. Geier in his Commentary on this passage. Compare also Svaningius on this passage.

AT THE DEDICATION OF THE STATUE] He used a very proper word, for which Theodotion has τὰ ἐγκαίνια here. See what was said at John 10:22.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SATRAPAS] אחשדרפניא in singulari ἐξατράπην dixit Theopompus, ut notavimus ad Matth. 18, 10. Alii Σατράπην, quam Persicam esse vocem putat He- rodotus, & plerique Græci. Ego potius ab Assyriis eam vocem (ut & eas quæ sequuntur nihil Chaldaicum præ se ferentes) putem venisse primum ad Chaldæos, deinde ad Persas. In Persica aula id nomen habes, nec apud Græcos tantum, sed & Estheræ 9, 3. Theodotion ὑπάτους: Bas- sas interpretatur Jacchiades, sumta voce ex imperio Turci- co, sicut & sequentibus nominibus comparat Turcica.

MAGISTRATUS] סגניא. Est idem nomen quod supra 2. v. 48. quos præfectos esse provinciarum ibi diximus. σφελίωνas Theodotion, Beglerbeios dicit Jacchiades.

ET JUDICES] פחוותא sunt Theodotioni το- πάρχαι, ut & 2. Regum 18, 24. Es. 36, 9. Jacchiadæ Agæ. Apparet fuisse præfectos minores sub illis majoribus. Esdræ 2, 7. 9. 5, 3. 14. c. 6, 6. 13. c. 8, 35. infra 6, 7.

DUCES] אדרגזריא, id est, scribas decretorum custodes. Vide quæ supra 2, 27. Hi sunt ἡγέμενοι in Græco.

ET TYRANNOS] גדבריא sunt pecuniarum dispensatores, ut apparet ex Chaldaica versione Eccles. 2, 7. Idem munus dicitur גזבר Esdr. 1, 8. & in Chaldaico fi- ne Estheris, & in titulo Thalmudis de Siclis: nimirum fa- cile inter se mutantur ז & ד: forte Græca vox est γαζόφο- ροι. Theodotion dixit τὲς ἐπὶ ἐξεσιῶν. Jacchiades Tur- cico more Dephtardaros.

ET PRÆFECTOS] דתבריא sunt Juriscon- sulti, quibus Jacchiades confert Alphakios Turcarum. His addit textus hic Chaldaicus תפתיא, quos janitores inter- pretatur Saadia, Jacchiades Doctores legum.

OMNESQUE PRINCIPES REGIONUM] שלטני sunt qui non præfecturis aut provinciis, sed urbi- bus & regionibus suburbicariis singulis præsunt. Vide supra 2, 10. Vox מדינתא regionem significat, estq; modo amplior, modo restrictior. His Zangiahos comparat Jacchiades.

De omnibus istis dignitatum, vel officiorum nominibus vid. imprimis Dn. D. Geierus Noster in Comment. ad h. l. Conf. & Svaningius in h. l.

AD DEDICATIONEM STATUÆ] Voce usus est valdè propria, pro qua τὰ ἐγκαίνια hic habet Theodo- tion. Vide quæ dicta Joh. 10, 22.

## 3:3
BUT THEY STOOD IN THE SIGHT OF THE STATUE] In a place from where the statue could be seen.

Latin:

STABANT AUTEM IN CONSPECTU STA- TUÆ] In loco unde conspici statua poterat.

## 3:4
Ver. 4.

PEOPLES, TRIBES, AND TONGUES] Nations, peoples, and languages.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

POPULIS, TRIBULIS, ET LINGUIS] Gen- tibus, nationibus, & linguis.

## 3:5
Ver. 5.

THE SOUND OF THE TRUMPET] In the Chaldean: Horn, that is, a trumpet.

AND THE PIPE] משרוקיתא from שרק, which in Chaldean and Hebrew is the same both in sound and in thing as the Greek συρίζω, or συρίσδω.

AND THE HARP] קיתרוס, without doubt the Greek word κιθάρα. Already before Daniel, great colonies of both Aeolians and Ionians had been led into Asia, and had scattered Greek words in those places.

SACKBUT] This word is of the Orient; for the Sambuca is an invention of the Syrians, according to Athenaeus, Book 4. סבכא, or שבכא, with the Dagesh resolved into נ according to the custom of the Syrians, is סנבכא: and the Greeks change the N before β into μ. It is an instrument of Syrian women, as Porphyry and Suidas teach us. Athenaeus adds that it was a four-stringed instrument of high pitch.

AND THE PSALTERY] This word also, פסנתרין, or, as it is written elsewhere, פסנטרין, is clearly Greek, with the λ changed into נ. Both Jerome and Augustine teach us that the psaltery was an instrument not unlike the cithara, except that the place from which they receive the sound, which is called the hollow, the cithara has in the lower part, the psaltery in the upper part; and the psaltery is struck from above, but the cithara from below. Chrysostom: ψαλτήριον τῶν ἐντατῶν μὲν ἦν, πλὴν ὄρθιον κᾀ ἄνωθεν εἶχε τῶν φθόγγων τὰς ἀφορμάς.

ET SYMPHONIÆ] This word also סומפוניה, or as below סמפוניא, is purely Greek, συμφωνία. Moreover, a Symphonia is an oblique flute, πλαγίαυλος, according to the interpretation of Servius on the 11th book of the Aeneid. But Isidore says: They commonly call a Symphonia a hollow piece of wood with skin stretched over both sides, which musicians strike with small rods from here and there; and from the harmony of the deep and the high, a most pleasing song is made in it. Where you also have the reason for this name.

CADENTES ADORATE STATUAM] In Chaldean: Fall down. It corresponds to the Hebrew תשת, as in Genesis 37, verses 9, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

SONITUM TUBÆ] In Chaldæo: Cornu, id est, buccinæ.

ET FISTULÆ] משרוקיתא à שרק, quod in Chaldæo & Hebræo idem est & fono & re cum Græco συρίζω, vel συρίσδω.

ET CITHARÆ] קיתרוס, Græca haud dubie vox κιθάρα. Jam ante Danielem magnæ & Æolum & Jonum coloniæ in Asiam deductæ, Græcas voces illis in locis sparserant.

SAMBUCÆ] Hæc vox est Orientis; nam Sambuca Syrorum repertum, teste Athenæo, Libro 4. סבכא, vel שבכא, Dagesch Syrorum more in נ resoluto, est סנבכא: N vero ante β Græci in μ mutant. Est in- strumentum mulierum Syrarum, ut nos docent Porphyrio & Suidas. Addit Athenæus τετράχορδον fuisse acuti soni.

ET PSALTERII] Etiam hæc vox פסנתרין, vel, ut alibi scribitur, פסנטרין Græca plane est, λ mutato in נ. Docent nos & Hieronymus, & Augustinus psalterium fuisse Instrumentum citharæ non absimile, nisi quod illum locum, unde sonum accipiunt, quod cavamen dicitur, ci- thara in parte inferiore, psalterium in parte superiore ha- bet; percutiturque psalterium quidem sursum, cithara vero deorsum. Chrysostomus: ψαλτήριον τῶν ἐντατῶν μὲν ἦν, πλὴν ὄρθιον κᾀ ἄνωθεν εἶχε τῶν φθόγγων τὰς ἀφορμάς.

ET SYMPHONIÆ] Etiam hæc vox סומפוניה, vel ut infra סמפוניא, mere Græca, συμφωνία. Est autem Symphonia tibia obliqua, πλαγίαυλος, interprete Servio ad 11. Æneidos. At Isidorus: Symphoniam vulgo appellant lignum cavum ex utraq́; parte pelle extensa, quod virgulis hinc & inde Musici feriunt; fitq́; in ea ex concordia gravis, & acuti gratissimus cantus. Ubi & causam habes hujus nominis.

CADENTES ADORATE STATUAM] In Chal- dæo: Procumbite. Respondet Hebræo תשת, ut Genes. 37. vers. 9. 10.

## 3:6
Vers. 6.

MITTETUR IN FORNACEM IGNIS ARDENTIS] A punishment not infrequent among the Chaldeans. See Jeremiah 29, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

MITTETUR IN FORNACEM IGNIS AR- DENTIS] Pœna non infrequens apud Chaldæos. Vide Jerem. 29, 22.

## 3:7
Vers. 7.

OMNES POPULI, TRIBUS, ET LINGUÆ] Some from all the peoples of the Babylonian empire.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

OMNES POPULI, TRIBUS, ET LINGUÆ] A- liqui ex omnibus imperii Babylonici populis.

## 3:8
Vers. 8.

VIRI CHALDÆI ACCUSAVERUNT JUDÆOS] Envying the Jews, and either the instigators of this edict to oppress them, or diligent hunters of an occasion that had arisen.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

VIRI CHALDÆI ACCUSAVERUNT JU- DÆOS] Invidentes Judæis, & ad eos opprimendos, aut suasores hujus edicti; aut natæ occasionis seduli aucupes.

## 3:12
Vers. 12.

VIRI ISTI CONTEMSERUNT, REX, DECRETUM TUUM] In Chaldean: They have not placed, O King, a reason: that is, they have had no regard for you.

DEOS TUOS NON COLUNT] They worship none of the gods whom Babylon worships, not even this parent of yours.

ET STATUAM AUREAM QUAM EREXISTI, NON ADORANT] They show this, because they refuse to fall down before the statue, which is a sign of one invoking that god of yours.

These things can be taken as an ἐξήγησις of the preceding; or let Vav be explained causally: They do not worship your gods, because they do not adore the statue which you have erected. Concerning the golden calf, Exod. 32. v. 4. These are your gods, O Israel. Compare what was said at v. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

VIRI ISTI CONTEMSERUNT, REX, DE- CRETUM TUUM] In Chaldæo: Non posuerunt, ô Rex, rationem: id est, rationem tui non habuerunt.

DEOS TUOS NON COLUNT] Nullum deo- rum, quos colit Babylon, ne hunc quidem parentem tuum.

ET STATUAM AUREAM QUAM EREXISTI, NON ADORANT] Ostendunt hoc, quod procumbere coram statua nolunt, quod signum est Deum illum tuum invocantis.

Possunt hæc tanquam ἐξήγησις præceden- tium accipi; vel explicetur Vav causaliter: Deos tuos non colunt, quia statuam quam erexisti non ado- rant. De vitulo aureo Exod. 32. v. 4. Hi sunt Dii tui Israel. Conf. quæ ad v. 1. dicta.

## 3:13
Vers. 13.

IN FURY AND WRATH] Powerless of mind from long-standing happiness.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

IN FURORE ET IRA] Præ longa felicitate ani- mi impotens.

## 3:14
Vers. 14.

VERE NE] Thus both Theodotion, and Abenesdra, and Saadia interpret that הצדא: perhaps better, whether deliberately? so that צדא may be for the Hebrew צדיה. Others think it is of one wondering, as if he were saying, what is this portent?

Latin:

Vers. 14.

VERE NE] Sic illud הצדא interpretantur, & Theo- dotio & Abenesdra, & Saadia: melius forte, an consulto? ut צדא sit pro Hebræo צדיה Alii admirantis esse putant, quasi diceret, quid hoc portenti?

## 3:15
Vers. 15.

NOW THEREFORE IF YOU ARE READY] Are you ready?

AND WHO IS THE GOD, WHO SHALL DELIVER YOU OUT OF MY HAND?] As if he were saying: That God of yours, in whom you trust in vain, will not be able to perform that. Compare the words of the Assyrian, 2 Kings 18:30, 33, 34, 35. Nebuchadnezzar was of a temperament, like Saul, variable and changeable for good and evil.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

NUNC ERGO SI ESTIS PARATI] An estis parati?

ET QUIS EST DEUS, QUI ERIPIAT VOS DE MANU MEA?] Quasi diceret: Vester ille Deus, cui frustra confiditis, id præstare non poterit. Confer verba Assyrii 2. Regum 18,30. 33. 34. 35. Erat Nabu- chodonosor ingenio, quasi Saul, vario ac mutabili in bo- num malumque.

## 3:16
Vers. 16.

Verse 16.

WE ARE NOT REQUIRED TO ANSWER YOU CONCERNING THIS MATTER] In the Chaldean: We are not anxious in this matter to answer you. Thus Cyprian to the Proconsul: In a matter so just there is no consultation. Through these examples of constancy, men were gradually prepared for Evangelical obedience.

Not only is there a preparation here for Evangelical obedience, but a notable example of the same. Because the most holy martyrs demonstrated the constancy of their faith in such a way as has been done by any under the New Testament. However, this error of Grotius concerning faith under the New Testament, already noted more often, recurs here.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Vers. 16.

NON OPORTET NOS DE HAC RE RESPON- DERE TIBI] In Chaldæo: Non solliciti sumus in hac re ad respondendum tibi. Sic Cyprianus ad Proconsulem: In re tam justâ nulla consultatio est. Per hæc constantiæ ex- empla homines paulatim adEvangelicam obedientiam pa- rabantur.

Non hîc præparatio tantum ad Evangelicam o- bedientiam, sed exemplum ejusdem insigne.Quia fidei suæ constantiam martyres sanctissimi sic de- monstrarunt,quemadmodum ab ullis sub N. T. fa- ctum. Recurrit autem hic error Grotii de fide sub N. T. sæpius jam notatus.

## 3:17
Verse 17.

BEHOLD, FOR OUR GOD, WHOM WE WORSHIP, IS ABLE TO DELIVER US FROM THE FURNACE OF BURNING FIRE, AND TO FREE US FROM YOUR HANDS, O KING. BUT IF HE WILL NOT, BE IT KNOWN TO YOU, O KING, THAT WE DO NOT WORSHIP YOUR GODS] Better: Whether our God, who is powerful to rescue us from the ignited furnace, delivers us from your hand, or not, have this for certain, O King, that we will not be worshippers of your gods. Often 'Si' is 'or' or 'whether'. They were looking here at the first commandment of the Decalogue.

Latin:

Vers. 17

ECCE ENIM DEUS NOSTER, QUEM CO- LIMUS, POTEST ERIPERE NOS DE CAMINO I- GNIS ARDENTIS, ET DE MANIBUS TUIS, O REX, LIBERARE. QUOD SI NOLUERIT, NOTUM TIBI SIT, O REX, QUIA DEOS TUOS NON CO- LIMUS] Melius: Sive Deus noster, qui potens est ad nos de fornace ignita eruendos, è manu tua nos liberet, sive non, illud, Rex, pro certo habe,nos cultores Deorum tuorum non futuros. Sæpe est Si aut sive. Spectabant hîc primum præce- ptum Decalogi.

## 3:18
Verse 18.

AND THE GOLDEN STATUE WHICH YOU HAVE ERECTED, WE DO NOT ADORE] We will not exhibit any honorific gesture before the statue, the second commandment of the Decalogue standing in the way.

We taught in its proper place that these things likewise look to the first commandment. And they speak of the same matter: namely, of that worship which the King had now publicly demanded: but that worship concerned the statue erected, and not truly the adoration of the other gods of the King.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

ET STATUAM AUREAM QUAM EREXISTI, NON ADORAMUS] Non exhibebimus ullum gestum honorificum coram statua, obstante præcepto Decalogi secundo.

Ad primum hæc itidem præceptum spectare, suo loco docuimus. Et de eadem re loquuntur: ni- mirum de cultu illo, quem publice jam demandâ- rat Rex: Is autem cultus concernebat statuam e- rectam, non vero adorationem aliorum Deorum Regis.

## 3:19
Verse 19. AND THE ASPECT OF HIS FACE WAS CHANGED] He flared up.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET ASPECTUS FACIEI ILLIUS IMMU- TATUS EST] Excanduit.

## 3:20
Verse 20. TO THE STRONGEST MEN OF HIS ARMY] That is, of the praetorian cohorts.

Latin:

Vers. 20. VIRIS FORTISSIMIS DE EXERCITU SUO] Id est, de prætorianis cohortibus.

## 3:21
WITH THEIR TROUSERS] In the Chaldean: Saraballis. Now Saraballae, which are corruptly Sarabara, or Saraba, were not leggings, as Jerome thinks, but mantles, as Jacchiades and Abenesdra explain here. That appears from the Talmudic titles concerning the Sanhedrin, and concerning the seven weeks. The word סרבל for the Chaldeans and Arabs is to cover.

AND TURBANS] פטיש seems to be the same in sound, and in reality, as τίαρας to the Greeks, which does not differ much from tiara. But Aben-Ezra and Jacchiades wish for undergarments to be understood here.

AND WITH SHOES [כרבלתא, is the crest of a cock, and from its likeness, everything that is placed upon the head. Thus Saadia, David Kimchi, and Jacchiades. Otherwise, כרבל for the Hebrews is to clothe, as appears in 1 Chronicles 15:27.
