AND WITH GARMENTS] Inner ones, which are under the mantle. Thus Jacchiades here. לבוש, as it is to clothe for the Hebrews, so it is also for the Chaldeans, as is evident below 5:7.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CUM BRACCIS SUIS] In Chaldæo: Sara- ballis. Erant autem Saraballæ,quæ corrupte Sarabara, aut Saraba,non tibialia,ut Hieronymus existimat, sed mantel- la,ut hic explicat Jacchiades & Abenesdra. Apparet id ti- tulis Talmudicis de Synedrio, & de Sept manis. Ver- bum סרבל Chaldæis & Arabibus est obtegere.

ET TIARIS] פטיש videtur esse idem sono, ac re, quod τίαρας Græcis, quod non longe abit à tiara. At Aben-Esdras & Jacchiades hic intelligi volunt subligaria.

ET CALCEAMENTIS[ כרבלתא, est crista gal- li, & ab ejus similitudine omne id,quod capiti imponitur. Ita Saadia, David Kimchi & Jacchiades. Alioqui כרבל Hebræis est amicire, ut apparet 1. Paralipomen. 15, 27.

ET VESTIBUS] Interioribus, quæ sub mantello. Ita hic Jacchiades. לבוש,ut Hebræis est induere, ita & Chaldæis, ut patet infra 5,7.

## 3:22
FOR THE KING'S COMMAND URGED] It brooked no delay.

Verse 22. THE FLAME OF FIRE KILLED] A spark leaping out from the furnace. That was the reason why Nebuchadnezzar approached the furnace with the intention of knowing the whole matter. The hymn of the three youths is not in the Hebrew; it is a poem made by some Hebrew of later times, as if fitting for the event.

I do not read those things in the Hebrew, Jerome also observes at this place, and in the Proem. Therefore, as Apocryphal, they are deservedly rejected.

Latin:

NAM JUSSIO REGIS URGEBAT] Moram non ferebat.

Vers. 22. INTERFECIT FLAMMA IGNIS] Scintil- la exsiliens è fornace. Ea causa fuit, cur Nabuchodono- sor rem omnem cognoscendi animo ad fornacem accede- ret. Hymnus trium juvenum non est in Hebræo, Est poe- ma factum à posteriorum temporum Hebræo aliquo,quasi rei conveniens.

Non legi illa in Ebræo, observat etiam Hiero- nymus ad hunc locum,& in Proœm. Ideo tanquam Apocrypha merito reprobantur.

## 3:24
Verse 91. BOUND] Well bound, as above in verse 23.

Latin:

Vers. 91. COMPEDITOS] Bene ligatos, utsupra v.23.

## 3:25
Verse 92. THE APPEARANCE OF THE FOURTH IS LIKE THE SON OF GOD] Angelic: how the LXX translated here, ὁμοία ἀγγέλῳ θεῦ. See Job 1:6. Thus the Hebrew interpreters.

Others understand by the Son of God the Son begotten by the Father, whom the blessed Polycarp Lyserus judges to act more correctly in the Babylonian furnace, p. 101 and p. 204, about whom Rupertus thinks in this place that the King had heard something from Daniel. The blessed Lyserus says that God so governs the mouth and tongue of great princes that they often speak the truth unknowingly. And thus Tertullian, lib. 4 against Marcion 40, Justin, Hilary, Augustine, and others explain it. There is no reason why one should depart from the proper meaning of the Son of God.

Latin:

Vers. 92. SPECIES QUARTI SIMILIS FILIO DEI] Angelica: quomodo LXX. hic verterunt,ὁμοία ἀγγέλῳ θεῦ. Vide Jobum 1,6. Sic Hebræi interpretes.

Alii per Filium Dei intelligunt Filium unigenitum à Patre, quos rectius facere judicat B. Polycarpus Lyserus in fornace Babylon. p.101. & p. 204. de quo Regem à Daniele aliquid inaudisse Rupertus in h. loc. putat. Deum os & linguam magnorum prin- cipum ita gubernare, ut sæpe inscii verum dicant, ait B. Lyserus. Atque ita exponunt Tertull. lib. 4. contra Marc. 40. Justinus, Hilarius, August. & a- lii. Nulla est causa,cur à propria Filii Dei signifi- catione discedendum sit.

SERVANTS OF THE MOST HIGH GOD] Worshippers of that God whom Nebuchadnezzar had also admired before in 2:47: אלהא עליא the most high God, as there אלה אלהין God of gods.

TUNG ACCESSIT NABUCHODONOSOR AD OSTIUM FORNACIS] Propius nempe quam ante, ut & alloqui illos posset.

SERVI DEI EXCELSI] Cultores illius Dei, quem antea quoque admiratus fuerat Nabuchodonosor 2, 47: אלהא עליא Deus summus, ut illic אלה אלהין Deus deorum.

## 3:27
Verse 94.

AND MAGISTRATES] Prefects of the provinces, as above 2,48. 3,2.

AND JUDGES] Lesser prefects: as above v. 2.

AND MIGHTY ONES [הדברין], is read also below 4, 32. & 6, 7. It seems to be the same as מדברא in Chaldean: Proverbs 11,14. & מדברנא in the Talmud under the title of Contracts. It is a common name for magistrates, by which are signified those who are mentioned by several names above in v.3.

THEY CONTEMPLATED THOSE MEN] Namely with admiration.

AND THE HAIR OF THEIR HEAD WAS NOT SINGED] That is, not even the least bit of their body. See Luke 12,7. & 21,18.

AND THEIR SARABALLA HAD NOT BEEN CHANGED] Not even their garments.

AND THE SMELL OF FIRE HAD NOT PASSED THROUGH THEM] They smelled of nothing of smoke.

Latin:

Vers. 94.

ET MAGISTRATUS] Præfecti provinciarum, ut supra 2,48. 3,2.

ET JUDICES] Præfecti minores: ut supra v. 2.

ET POTENTES[ הדברין, legitur & infra 4, 32. & 6, 7. Videtur idem esse, quod מדברא in Chaldæo: Proverb. 11,14. & מדברנא in Thalmudetitulo de Con- tractibus. Est nomen commune magistratibus, quo si- gnificantur illi, qui pluribus nominibus supra v.3.

CONTEMPLABANTUR VIROS ILLOS] Nem- pe cum admiratione.

ET CAPILLUS CAPITIS EORUM NON ES- SET ADUSTUS] Id est, ne minimum quidem de cor- pore. Vid. Luc. 12,7. & 21,18.

ET SARABALLA EORUM NON FUISSENT IMMUTATA] Ne eorum quidem vestimenta.

ET ODOR IGNIS NON TRANSISSET PER EOS] Nihil de fumo olebant.

## 3:28
Verse 95. AND NABUCHODONOSOR BREAKING FORTH SAID] In the Hebrew: Nabuchodonosor spoke, and said: as above 2,16. & 47.

WHO BELIEVED IN HIM] Who trusted in him. A certain degree toward Evangelical trust.

The Grotian commentary concerning faith and the faithful of the Old Testament recurs here, as if only a certain degree toward Evangelical trust had a place there, and not truly Evangelical trust. But faith is one, and the object of saving faith is one under the Old and New Testaments, nor was there only a preparation or degree toward that trust which has a place under the New Testament, but we believe that we shall be saved through the same grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, just as they were saved, Acts 15,10. And was there not true trust in Abraham, the Father of believers, who is set before us as an Example, so that we might insist upon his footsteps, Romans 4? Was it not in David, whose spirit of faith we ought to have, 2 Corinthians 4? Was it not in Job, and in other faithful ones of the Old Testament, who certainly were justified in no other way than through faith in the Messiah?

Verse the same.

AND THEY CHANGED THE KING'S WORD] To change, as also to break the law, is said of one who acts against the law. Matthew 5,17. 7,23. 10,35. Now at last he judges it fair that the law of God be preferred to his own; according to that: Οὐ γάρ τί μοι Ζεὺς ἦν ὁ κηρύξας τόδε.

AND THEY DELIVERED THEIR BODIES] They exposed them to death.

THAT THEY MIGHT NOT SERVE] That is, that they might offer sacrifice: for that is what עבד means.

AND THAT THEY MIGHT NOT WORSHIP] That they might show honor by a gesture of the body before the image.

ANY GOD] Any God.

EXCEPT THEIR GOD] The Maker of heaven and earth.

Latin:

Vers. 95. ET ERUMPENS NABUCHODONOSOR AIT] In Hebræo: Locutus est Nabuchodonosor, & ait: ut supra 2,16. & 47.

QUI CREDIDERUNT IN EUM] Qui confisi ei sunt. Gradus quidam ad Evangelicam fiduciam.

Commentum de fide, & fidelibus Vet. Testam. Grotianum hic recurrit, quasi ibi tantum gradus quîdam locum habuerit ad Evangelicam fidu- ciam, non vero Evangelica fiducia. At una est fi- des,unumq; fidei salvificæ objectum sub Veteri & Novo Testamento,neque ibi præparatio aut gra- dus solum fuit ad fiduciam illam, quæ sub Novo Testamento locum habet,sed credimus per eandem gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi salvatum nos iri, quemadmodum & illi salvati sunt,Act. 15,10. Et an- non fiducia vera in Abrahamo Patre credentium fuit,qui nobis in Exemplum sistitur, ut vestigiis e- jus insistamus Rom. 4. annon in Davide, cujus fidei Spiritum nos habere debemus,2. Corinth. 4. annon in Jobo, & in aliis fidelibus Veteris Testamenti,qui utique non aliter,quam per fidem in Messiam ju- stificati sunt.

Vers. eod.

ET VERBUM REGIS IMMUTAVERUNT] Mu- tare, ut & solvere legem dicitur, qui contra legem facit. Matth. 5,17. 7,23. 10,35. Jam tandem æquum judicat Dei legem suæ anteferri; juxta illud: Οὐ γάρ τί μοι Ζεὺς ἦν ὁ κηρύξας τόδε.

ET TRADIDERUNT CORPORA SUA] Expo- fuerunt morti.

NE SERVIRENT] Id est, sacrificium facerent: id enim est עבד.

ET NE ADORARENT] Corporis gestu honorem exhiberent apud imaginem.

OMNEM DEUM] Ullum Deum.

EXCEPTO DEO SUO] Opifice cœli & terræ.

## 3:29
Vers. 96.

WHOSOEVER SHALL HAVE SPOKEN BLASPHEMY] In the Chaldean: He who shall have spoken error, that is, he who shall have sinned by speaking. He did not yet dare to depose the gods of his empire. Meanwhile, which is no small thing, he forbids cursing the God of the Hebrews, whom he had recognized as so powerful.

Nay, what else was this than the deposition of the Gentile gods, whom he had previously worshipped, when he brings forward the glory of one God, and with a resounding voice professes, and by royal edict sanctions and decrees, that there is no other God who can save in such a way as the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and furthermore promulgates a decree throughout the whole Empire, that every people, tribe, and tongue, whatsoever shall have spoken blasphemy against this God, shall perish, and his house shall be laid waste. And when he celebrates God as the deliverer of those who believe in Him; Blessed be their God, namely, of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent His angel, and delivered His servants who believed in Him.

Does he not testify that trust is to be placed in him alone, as one who alone can save those who believe in him? Does he perhaps not yet dismiss his gods, by another new edict, which is subjoined, in which he publicly proclaims the true God: The most high God has wrought signs and wonders with me. It has pleased me therefore to proclaim his signs, because they are great, and his wonders, because they are mighty, and his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his power is from generation to generation. What is more evident than that, having been led by a miracle to the true recognition and celebration of the true God, Nebuchadnezzar wished his subjects to be led to the same? With which, as the worship of idols cannot consist, so by this same reasoning it is manifest that the false gods were dismissed by Nebuchadnezzar. He was therefore made a most august herald of the true God, by the admirable economy of God. Meanwhile, if it be asked whether this doxology and confession of the King is prior (for the other pertains to the following chapter, and was made after the King, deprived of the use of reason and cast down to the beasts, returned to himself by divine mercy and was truly converted to God) sincere, true, and full, such as the salvific faith of a true Christian and the confession of the same ought to be, B. Lyferus answers: I cannot affirm it to be perfect and sincere. It is, however, the beginning of a faith to be more perfected through fuller instruction. For true faith ought to have not only knowledge and assent, but also trust and application. Regarding the first two, we discern in the King some knowledge and assent of the true God of Israel: but concerning trust we cannot yet pronounce anything, much less concerning application. Because he only names God the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego: whereas true faith ought to acknowledge and worship the true God as its own God.

But concerning the later doxology in chapter 4, 34, it must be acknowledged entirely that it proceeded from true faith, after Nebuchadnezzar, having been converted to God by a temporal punishment by far the most severe, whom also many think to have died shortly after, and thus to have become an heir of eternal life: Dorotheus in the Synopsis, Epiphanius, Theodoret, Augustine, Epistle 112, etc.

Vers. eod.

FOR THERE IS NO OTHER GOD WHO CAN SAVE IN THIS WAY] Bel could not save his worshippers placed outside the furnace from the fire. But the God of the Hebrews kept his own safe in the midst of the fire.

LET HIM PERISH] Let him be torn limb from limb.

AND HIS HOUSE BE MADE A DUNGHILL] Let it be turned into latrines. The same punishment, and the same words, which are above 2, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 96.

QUÆCUMQUE LOQUUTA FUERIT BLAS- PHEMIAM] In Chaldæo: Qui dixerit errorem, id est, qui loquendo peccaverit. Nondum ausus deos imperii sui exauctorare. Interim, quod non parum est, vetat maledici Hebræorum Deo, quem tam potentem cognoverat.

Imo quid hoc aliud erat,quam exauctoratio Deo- rum gentilium, quos antea coluerat, cum unius Dei gloriam adferit, & sonora voce profitetur, quod regio edicto sancit & decernit,non esse alium Deum,qui possit ita salvare, ut Deus Sidrach, Mi- sach & Abednego, adeoq; decretum per totum Im- perium promulgat,ut omnis populus, tribus,& lin- gua, quæcunque locuta fuerit blasphemiam contra hunc Deum, dispereat, & domus ejus vastetur. Et quum celebret Deum ceu liberatorem eorum,qui credunt in ipsum; Benedictus Deus eorum,Sidrach, videlicet,Misach, & Abednego, qui misit angelum suum, & eruit servos suos, qui crediderunt in eum.

Annon in eum solum fiduciam collocandam esse testatur, utpote qui solus eos, qui credunt in se, servare potest? Num forte nondum exauctoravit Deos suos, altero edicto novo, quod subjungitur, quo verum Deum publice deprædicat: signa & mi- rabilia fecit apud me Deus excelsus. Placuit ergo mi- hi prædicare signa ejus, quia magna sunt, & mirabilia ejus, quia fortia, & regnum ejus regnum sempiter- num, & potestas ejus in generationem & generatio- nem. Quid evidentius est, quam quod per mira- culum ad veram veri Dei agnitionem & celebra- tionem perductus, subditos ad eandem perductos voluerit Nabuchodonosar? Cum qua uti consiste- re nequit cultus Idolorum, ita eadem hac ratione falsos Deos exauctoratos à Nebucadnezare fuisse, manifestum est. Fuit ergo ita augustissimus præ- co veri Dei, admiranda Dei οἰκονομίᾳ factus. Inte- rim si quæratur, an ista δοξολογία & confessio Re- gis prior (nam altera ad Caput sequens pertinet, & facta est, postquam Rex rationis usu privatus ac ad feras abjectus, divina misericordia ad se rediit, & ve- re conversus ad Deum est) sincera sit, vera & plena, qualis veri Christiani salvifica fides, & ejusdem confessio esse debet, respondet B. Lyferus: Per- fectam & synceram eam affirmare non possum. Est ta- men initium fidei per institutionem uberiorem magis perficiendæ. Vera enim fides non debet habere tantum notitiam & assensum, verum etiam fiduciam & ap- plicationem. Quoad priora duo deprehendimus in Rege aliqualem veri Dei Israëlis notitiam & assen- sum: de fiducia autem nihil dum pronunciare possu- mus, multo minus de appellatione. Quia Deum tantum nominat Deum Sadrach, Mesach & Abed- nego: Cum vera fides verum Deum suum Deum a- gnoscere, & colere debeat.

De posteriori vero δοξολογίᾳ cap. 4, 34. a- gnoscendum omnino est, quod ex vera fide profe- cta sit, postquam Nabuchodonosar pœna tempora- li longe gravissima ad Deum conversus, quem et- iam paulo post obiisse, adeoque vitæ æternæ hæ- redem factum esse censent plerique: Dorotheus in Synopsi, Epiphan. Theodoret. August. Epist. 112. &c.

Vers. eod.

NEQUE ENIM EST ALIUS DEUS, QUI POS- SIT ITA SALVARE] Belus suos cultores extra forna- cem positos ab igne servare non potuit. Deus autem He- bræorum suos in medio igne incolumes præstitit.

DISPEREAT] Membratim lanietur.

ET DOMUS EJUS VASTETUR] In latrinas ver- tatur. Eadem pœna, & eadem verba, quæ supra 2, 5.

Verse 1.

I WAS AT REST IN MINE HOUSE] The nations having been conquered.

Vers. 1.

## 4:1
Vers. 98.

NEBUCHADNEZZAR THE KING] They do better who connect these three verses with the following ones, which are in the fourth chapter. For this is the preface to the following Edict. When Daniel had finished the history of the three youths, he subjoins another truly wonderful history, not in his own words, but in the words of the published edict itself, so that no one might doubt the faith.

PEACE BE MULTIPLIED UNTO YOU] That is, may all things most prosperous happen to you.

Latin:

Vers. 98.

NABUCHODONOSOR REX] Rectius faciunt, qui hæc tria commata connectunt cum sequentibus, quæ sunt in capite quarto. Est enim hoc Edicti sequentis præfatio. Daniel cum Historiam trium juvenum absol- visset, aliam Historiam sane mirabilem subjicit, non suis, sed ipsius edicti publicati verbis, ut de fide nemo dubita- ret.

PAX VOBIS MULTIPLICETUR] Id est, omnia vobis prosperrima contingant.

## 4:2
Verse 99.

SIGNS AND WONDERS HE HATH WROUGHT TOWARD ME] Toward me. Namely, by pre-signifying future things so incredible.

THE MOST HIGH GOD] The highest God, as above 3, 93. Thus he calls the God whom Daniel and the Hebrews worshipped.

Latin:

Vers. 99.

DEUS EXCELSUS] Summus Deus, ut supra 3, 93. ita appellat Deum, quem colebat Daniel, & Hebræi.

## 4:3
Verse 100.

HIS KINGDOM IS AN EVERLASTING KINGDOM] Namely, having experienced it, he had learned that: Over their own flocks are kings to be feared, but over the kings themselves is the rule of Jove.

Nebuchadnezzar, by a public proclamation, makes known the dream about the tall tree being cut down, which was explained to him by Daniel alone, that having been driven from his kingdom he would live with the beasts for seven years, and the counsel given: the fulfillment of which is reported concerning the King, because of his pride, after a voice was first heard from heaven, being cast out from men to the wild beasts; but after the seven years had passed, being restored again; whence he glorifies God and proclaims His judgments.

Latin:

Vers. 100.

REGNUM EJUS REGNUM SEMPITERNUM] Nempe expertus illud didicerat: Regum timendorum in proprios greges, Reges in ipsos imperium est Iovis.

Nebucadnezar programmate publico so- mnium de arbore excelsa præcisa, à solo Daniele sibi expositum, quod regno pulsus per septem annos cum bestiis victurus sit, & consilium datum intimat: cujus com- plementum refertur de Rege ob superbiam, voce prius de cælo audita, ab hominibus ad feras ejecto; sed exacto septennio iterum restituto; unde Deum glorificat, & ju- dicia ejus prædicat.

THE VISIONS OF MY HEAD TROUBLED ME] Such as that: 'Anna, my sister, what dreams are these that terrify me in my suspense?' And in Octavia: 'Confused by the sad fear of the approaching night, and by visions, nurse, I am carried away with a troubled mind.'

Vers. 2.

Verse 4.

Vers. 4.

## 4:8
Verse 5.

UNTIL A COLLEAGUE ENTERED] It is usually translated from the Chaldean as 'until at last he entered.' But there is no doubt that אחרין signifies another of the same order, that is, a colleague. For thus Theodotion, Aquila, and Symmachus translated it, according to Jerome, although that word is now absent from the Greek.

BUT in the authentic text it is ועד אחרין, and Buxtorf in his Talmudic Lexicon teaches that it should be translated as 'at the last' or 'finally.' Therefore, the question of how the King called Daniel his colleague has no place: although if it is translated as 'colleague' at all, it should not immediately be understood as a colleague of the King, since it can be referred to the soothsayers and magicians, whose colleague the King called him when, as in v. 6, he calls him the Prince of the soothsayers.

Same verse.

ACCORDING TO THE NAME OF MY GOD] Bel. See what was said at 1, 7.

WHO HAS THE SPIRIT OF THE HOLY GODS] He speaks as an idolater. Theodotion, however, translates πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἁγιου, for which ἁγίων is now wrongly written.

It is not right, we say, for Nebuchadnezzar to speak here in such a holy document and edict as an idolater. He is entirely occupied with celebrating and propagating the glory of the true God, as both the beginning of this edict, proposed at the end of the preceding first chapter in the Vulgate, and the conclusion of the same abundantly testify. Therefore, by the phrase of Scripture, the mystery of the plurality of the divine persons is indicated, about which the King was undoubtedly instructed by Daniel. For the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of Elohim, of God the Father, and of God the Son.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

DONEC COLLEGA INGRESSUS EST] Ex Chaldaico verti solet, donec tandem ingressus est. At אחרין non est dubium, quin alium ejusdem ordinis, id est, Colle- gam significaverit. Nam ita verterunt Theodotion, A- quila, Symmachus, teste Hieronymo, quanquam nunc in Græco ea vox abest.

AT in textu authentico est ועד אחרין, & ad postremum, vel tandem, in Buxtorff. in Lex. Talmud. vertendum esse docet. Non ergo lo- cum habet quæstio, quomodo Rex Danielem col- legam suum dixerit: Quamvis si omnino vertatur per collegam, non statim collega Regis intelligen- dus sit, quum referri possit ad Ariolos & Magos, quorum collegam cum dixerit Rex, ut v. 6. eum Principem ariolorum vocat.

Vers. eod.

SECUNDUM NOMEN DEI MEI] Beli. Vide quæ dicta 1,7.

QUI HABET SPIRITUM DEORUM SAN- CTORUM] Loquitur ut idololatra. Theodotion tamen vertit πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἁγιου, pro quo ἁγίων nunc male scribi- tur.

Non fas est, dicamus, loqui hic Nabuchodo- nosarem in tam sancto diplomate & edicto, ut Ido- lolatram. Qui totus in eo est, ut veri Dei gloriam celebret, atque propaget, ut tum initium edicti hujus, sub finem capitis primi præcedentis, in Vul- gata propositum, tum conclusio ejusdem abunde te- statur. Quapropter Scripturæ phrasi indigitatur mysterium pluralitatis personarum divinarum, de quo edoctus sine dubio Rex à Daniele fuit. Est enim Spiritus Sanctus, Spiritus Elohim, Dei Pa- tris, & Dei Filii.

Ἡ δὲ ὄψις ἦν ἥδε. Ἐδόκεε ὁ Ξέρ ξης ἐστεφανῶσθαι ἐλαίης θαλλῷ. Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς ἐλαίης τοὺς κλάδους γῆν πᾶσαν ἐπισχεῖν.

## 4:13
Verse 10. AND BEHOLD, A WATCHER AND A HOLY ONE CAME DOWN FROM HEAVEN] Here also AND is placed for THAT IS. The Chaldean word עיר, as Theodotion writes, the LXX translate as 'angel'. The others [translate it] with the same meaning, but closer to the word ἐγρήγορον [watcher], which word has the same meaning in the book bearing the name of Enoch, a part of which Scaliger inserted into his notes on Eusebius. (There is, moreover, mention of that book also in the Hebrew Book of Zohar, and in the second book of the Paedagogus of Clement.) Jerome thinks that Iris, the messenger of the gods, derives her name from this.

Grotius seems not to regard the book of Enoch, which is still sold under his name, as apocryphal: but not a few have sufficiently proven it to be spurious and counterfeit. Josephus Scaliger also made mention of the title of the book of Enoch, περὶ τῶν ἐγρηγόρων [concerning the watchers]. That the book is a fabrication, invented by the Jews, he teaches in his notes on Eusebius, page 244. See concerning the same, Christ. Schottanus in Tohu on Genesis 6, and from our own [authors], B. Walth. Offic. Bibl. page 1176 et seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET ECCE, VIGIL ET SANCTUS DE COELO DESCENDIT] Etiam hic ET positum pro ID EST. Vox Chaldæa עיר, ut scribit Theodotion, LXX. ἄγγελον vertunt. Cæteri sensu eodem, sed propius ad vo- cem ἐγρήγορον, quæ vox eodem significatu est in libro Eno- chi nomen præferente, cujus partem Scaliger notis ad Eu- sebium inseruit. (Est autem ejus libri mentio & in Hebræo Libro Zoar, & in Pædagogo Secundo Clementis.) Hiero- nymus hinc nomen habere putat Irin deorum nuntiam.

Videtur Grotius librum Enochi, qui adhuc sub ejus nomine venditatur, non habere pro Apo- crypho: sed nothum eum, atque spurium esse satis probarunt non pauci. Josephus Scaliger men- tionem etiam fecit tituli libri Enochi περὶ τῶν ἐ- γεηγόρων de vigilibus. Librum autem illum com- mentitium à Judæis esse confictum docet in not. ad Euseb. pag. 244. Vide de eodem Christ. Schotta- nus in Tohu ad Genes. 6. & è nostris B. Walth. Of- fic. Bibl. pag. 1176. seqq.

## 4:14
Verse 11. CUT DOWN THE TREE] The cutting down of a tree signifies exile. Achmetes, chapter 151.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SUCCIDITE ARBOREM] Arboris excisio exsilium significat. Achmetes cap. 151.

## 4:15
Verse 12. LEAVE THE SHOOT OF ITS ROOTS IN THE EARTH] May the kingdom remain for him.

LET IT BE BOUND WITH A BAND OF IRON AND BRONZE] May the kingdom be firm and unshaken, like things that are held by bronze and iron.

WITH THE HERBS THAT ARE OUTSIDE] With wild herbs, supply 'let him graze'. Here the thing signified is mixed with the sign, as often. See below 22.

Latin:

Vers. 12. GERMEN RADICUM EJUS IN TER- RA SINITE] Regnum ipsi maneat.

ALLIGETUR VINCULO FERREO ET Æ- NEO] Sit regnum firmum & inconcussum, ut quæ ære & ferro tenentur.

IN HERBIS, QUÆ FORIS SUNT] Herbis a- grestibus, supple pascatur. Hic miscetur res significata cum signo, ut sæpe. Vide infra 22.

## 4:16
Vers. 13. HIS HEART SHALL BE CHANGED FROM A HUMAN ONE] Let it become brutish.

AND SEVEN TIMES SHALL BE CHANGED OVER HIM] Let them pass. Times, that is, years, as always in this Prophet. It is a Chaldean manner of speaking.

Latin:

Vers. 13. COR EJUS AB HUMANO IMMUTE- TUR] Brutescat.

ET SEPTEM TEMPORA MUTENTUR SU- PER EUM] Transeant. Tempora, id est, anni, ut semper in hac Propheta. Est loquendi genus Chaldaicum.

## 4:17
Vers. 14. BY THE SENTENCE OF THE WATCHERS IT IS DECREED] That is, the greater Angels have resolved this. For God is depicted as if He were a King acting by the counsel of a Senate. Compare what is below in v. 21.

AND THE WORD OF THE HOLY ONES, AND THE PETITION] In the Chaldean: and in the word of the Holy Ones a petition. That is, the lesser Angels have long since been requesting this, as a most equitable matter. There follows in the Chaldean עד־דברת, until it is brought, that is, until the thing itself comes to pass.

The interpretation is merely arbitrary. By the sentence of the watchers it is decreed, i.e., the greater angels have resolved this. And it is truly a fiction of Grotius, not of the Prophet: that God acts as if by a decree of the senate; for nowhere does that figment have any trace in Scripture. Indeed, Scripture denies that God calls angels into counsel, Is. 40, Rom. 11. Wherefore others judge that the counsel of the Most Holy Trinity is more correctly indicated here. For since the name of guardian is attributed to God in Psalm 121:3, it will by no means be inconvenient for this plural עירימ (watchers) to denote several divine persons. Furthermore, because to watch over the Monarchies and empires of the world, to establish and decree concerning them, to pass sentence upon the highest heads and Monarchs, and to execute judgment, is proper to God the King of all Kings, it cannot be through these עירימ and their council, by whose sentence the most grave judgment was decreed against Nebuchadnezzar, be understood as anything other than the council of the Most Holy Trinity. Furthermore, since God does not institute consultation concerning His government, nor does He wish to institute it with angels, as witnessed by Is.

chapter 40, and thus angels cannot be understood here, it must be confessed that the consultation was instituted among those who are read in Gen. 1:26 concerning the creation of man, Gen. 11 concerning the judgment against the Babylonians, and chapter 19 concerning the judgment against the Pentapolitans, to have consulted and made a decree. Which we have shown in the annotations to those places are to be understood concerning the persons of the Most Holy Trinity. Worldly Kings and Princes are indeed accustomed to deliberate with counselors, but that is a mark of imperfection, because they have need to hear the opinion of others, partly due to a lack of wisdom, partly due to a less secure or free power of acting; but God needs no one's counsel, and enjoys the most free power as ἀυτεξέσι@, and therefore that consultation with others, which Grotius attributes to God after the manner of the Jews, detracts not a little from the divine wisdom, and from the most free and entirely independent will, as also from the supreme majesty of GOD, who does not wish to give His glory to another, Is. 42:8.

Nor are the angels for God as counselors, but for the ministry and execution of commands, Ps. 103:20, Dan. 7:10, Ps. 91:11, Heb. 1:14. If the passage 1 Kings 22 is objected, no consultation is instituted there either, but rather the Majesty of God is shadowed forth by some vision, how He Himself as a just Judge and Lord of all things directs everything, without whose nod, permission, and direction, not even Satan dares to undertake anything. Theodoret says it is a fiction of person and prosopopoeia, which teaches divine permission: and Polychronius, Eusebius, Hugo, Vatablus, and others place a mere vision there, just as the text also openly calls it 1 Kings 22:18. And it is sufficiently clear that a right or left hand cannot truly be assigned to God. Wherefore, since no example can be shown of God's consultation with angels, much less a common decree, and it furthermore conflicts with the divine oracle of Is. 40:18, and with divine majesty and eminence, we conclude that the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is hinted at here. Inasmuch as later in verse 21 it is manifestly said that this is the decree of the MOST HIGH, and in v. 23 similarly the same mystery is insinuated by the plural number; from which you may know that they are שליטין DOMINIONS of heaven, which one may also observe in Dan. 7:18, 22, 25, 26, where the elect are called the holy ones of the עליונין Most Highs, i.e., of the exalted divine persons, who are that one most high and exalted God.

Which opinion I see also approved by the blessed Lucas Osiander in his paraphrase: In the sentence of the watchers this is decreed, and the word of the holy ones is this, and this is their petition or will: as if you were to say: They (after the opinions were asked) made this senate decree: that is; The Holy Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit) made this decree concerning the Babylonian King. For such a phrase exists in Josh. 24: You will not be able to serve the Lord; for He is a holy God. Moreover, the three persons of the Divinity are called watchers: because the Holy Trinity watches for the salvation of the elect. For it is written: Behold, He shall not slumber who guards Israel: Ps. 121. Which also the blessed Lord Dr. Andreas Osiander made his own regarding the words, in the sentence of the watchers in this place, noting thus: But the persons of the Most Holy Trinity are so called, because they keep watch for the salvation of the elect: Hence Daniel v. 21 says: That this is the sentence of the most high. Which our Lord Dr. Haberkorn also took up and proved at length in Syntagm. 1. Dispp. Theol. disp. 1. p. 98. with these arguments in particular: (1) Because to govern human affairs, among which Monarchies are eminent, from heaven, and to establish either rewards or punishments for them, is a work of supreme and divine providence, which in all of Holy Scripture belongs to God alone, Dan. 2:21, Ezek. 21:27, chapter 31:11, etc. But far be it that that which is declared to be proper to God alone, to angels should be attributed in any equal or inferior manner. (2) Because it is said in the text v. 14. Therefore that the holy watchers have so decreed, that Nebuchadnezzar for a time be deposed from his throne, so that the living may thence know, that the Most High is Ruler, having power in the kingdom of man, and giveth it to whomsoever He will were angels, then that very thing would not follow immediately, and thus firmly from it, but this, that angels have power over earthly kingdoms. (3.) The decree and sentence, which in v. 14 is attributed to these watchers, is afterwards in v. 20 most expressly said to be the decree and sentence of the Most High, and Nebuchadnezzar repenting ascribed this fate of his not to the angels, but to God, and praised Him v. 31. seqq. (4) That it is not unusual for Daniel to speak of God in the plural number cap. 4, 5. c. 7, 18. 22. 25. 26. (5) That the Holy Scripture everywhere assigns to our God the highest care, custody, and vigilance over human affairs, Pf. 127, 2. Psal. 80, 2. Pf. 121, 4. Psal. 44, 24. Zach. 4, 10. cap. 9, 1. Ier. 31, 26. (6) To this point refers that Talmudic saying: The Holy God blessed be He does not do any thing, unless He has consulted with His family, or as others say, with the house of His judgment. Compare Buxt. in Lexic. Chaldaico Thalmudico under the word פמל col. 1753. Which Galatinus applies to the very persons of the Most Holy Trinity, and derives that explanation from the Rabbis, lib. 2. de Arcan. Cathol. veritat. cap. 9. near the end, page 73. 34. Add also to these: that some understand by the watcher descending from heaven, verse 10, the Son of God. Nor is this explanation disapproved of by B. Lysero in Cedro Babylonica page 67. Others understand by the holy watcher the Son of God Himself. For when he cries out that this was decreed concerning the king in the council of the watchers: But let no one be admitted to that most sacred council of the heavens, except the three persons of the Most Holy Trinity: Therefore they gather from thence, that the second person of this council, who is ὁ λόγος, the eternal counselor of the eternal Father, announced this decree to the King. This opinion also agrees with Holy Scripture, for the Lord is called the watcher or keeper of Israel (Der Wächter Israels). For thus David sings in the Psalm: Behold, he shall not slumber nor sleep, that keepeth Israel. The Lord is thy protection upon thy right hand. Nor indeed is there any reason that we should admit that an opposition is instituted here between lesser and greater angels, as if the former had conspired in this decree concerning Nebuchadnezzar: But the latter demanded it as a most equitable matter, which is a Judaic-Grotian fiction: If indeed the words κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν are rightly understood, so that the decree of the watchers, and the word, and the PETITION, OR WILL OF THE HOLY ONES are held to be ἰσοδυναμῦντα; just as Osiander, the Father, has interpreted: which ἰσοδυναμίαν I see Lud. de Dieu also does not disapprove of here, because פִתְגָמָא & שְׁאֵלְתָא is the same as the preceding פִּתְגָּמַיְ & שְׁ- and both are the same as the דָּבָר of the Hebrews. Certainly among the Arabs מִשְׁאֵלָה, a petition, the plural of which is מִשְׁאֵיל, is used for הַדְּבָרִים as in Gen. 15, 1. c. 24, 66. In this manner שְׁאֵלְתָא will be business, a thing.

Vers. eod. UNTIL THE LIVING MAY KNOW, THAT THE MOST HIGH RULETH IN THE KINGDOM OF MEN] That they may know. See below 22.

AND WHATEVER HE SHALL WISH, HE SHALL GIVE IT] The Essenes: ὅ δίχα Θεῦ περιγίνεται τό ἄρχειν. Homer: τιμὴ δ' ἐκ Διός ἐςι. That powers are given by fate is in Sextus Aurelius. Add Augustine, book 5, de Civit. Dei, c. 2.

AND HE SHALL SET THE LOWEST OF MEN OVER IT] As in Judea, David. See 1 Sam. 2, v. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN SENTENTIA VIGILUM DECRETUM EST] Id est, majores Angeli hoc consceiverunt. Fingitur enim Deus tanquam Rex agere ex Senatus consilio. Con- fer, quod infra v. 21.

ET SERMO SANCTORUM, ET PETITIO] In Chaldæo: & in sermone Sanctorum petitio. Id est, mi- nores Angeli jampridem id postulant, ut rem æquissimam. Sequitur in Chaldæo עד־דברת, donec adducatur, id est, donec res ipsa eveniat.

Mere arbitraria est interpretatio. In sententia vigilum decretum est, i. e. majores angeli hoc consci- verunt. Et vere fingitur à Grotio, non à Prophe- ta: Deum agere velut ex senatus consulto; nuspiam enim id figmentum ullum in Scriptura habet vesti- gium. Imo negat Scriptura, Deum in consilium vo- care angelos, Es. 40. Rom. 11. Quapropter rectius hic consilium S. S. Trinitatis indigitari, censent alii. Quum enim nomen custodis Deo tribuatur Psal. 121, 3. plurale hoc עירימ vigilum plures personas divinas denotare, nequaquam inconveniens erit. Porro quia vigilare pro Monarchiis & imperiis mundi, statuere atq́; decernere de iisdem, de summis capitibus & Monarchis sententiam ferre, & judicium exequi, Dei Regis Regum omnium proprium est, non po- test per hosce עירימ eorumq; concilium, quorum sententia decretum est adversus Nebucadnezarem judicium longe gravissimum, aliter quam conci- lium Sacro-Sanctæ Trinitatis intelligi. Adhæc cum Deus consultationem de regimine suo non in- stituat, neque instituere velit cum angelis, teste Es.

cap. 40. adeoque angeli hic intelligi nequeant, in- ter illos consultationem institutam, & sententiam ab illis decretam esse fatendum est, qui Genes. 1, 26. de condendo homine, Gen. 11. de judicio adver- sus Babylonios, cap. 19. de judicio adversus Penta- politanos consultâsse ac decretum fecisse leguntur. Quæ de personis S.S.Trinitatis intelligenda esse, in annotatis ad ista loca ostendimus. Reges sane atque Principes mundani deliberare solent cum consilia- riis, sed id imperfectionis est, quod aliorum sen- tentiam audire opus habeant, partim ob defectum sapientiæ, partim ob minus tutam aut liberam agen- di potestatem; at Deus nullius consilio eget, & li- berrima potestate gaudet ceu ἀυτεξέσι@, ideo- que illa cum aliis consultatio, quam more Judæo- rum Deo tribuit Grotius, non parum derogat di- vinæ sapientiæ, ac liberrimæ, & prorsus indepen- denti voluntati, ut & majestati supremæ DEI, qui gloriam suam alteri dare non vult, Es. 42, 8.

Neque angeli Deo sunt à consiliis, sed à mi- nisterio & exequutione mandatorum Ps. 103, 20. Dan. 7, 10. Psal. 91, 11. Ebr. 1, 14. Si locus 1. Reg. 22. obji- ciatur, nec consultatio ibi instituitur, sed adumbra- tur potius Dei Majestas, visione aliqua, quomodo ipse ceu justus Judex & Dominus rerum omnium omnia dirigat, sine cujus nutu, permissione ac di- rectione, ne Satanas quidem aliquid suscipere ausit. Theodoretus fictionem personæ & prosopo- pœiam esse dicit, quæ divinam permissionem do- ceat: & visionem meram ibi ponunt Polychronius, Eusebius, Hugo, Vatablus, alii, quemadmodum tex- tus etiam aperte vocat 1. Reg. 22, 18. Neque Deo dextram aut sinistram vere assignari posse, satis con- stat. Quapropter cum nullo exemplo doceri possit consultatio Dei cum angelis, nedum commune decretum, & repugnet insuper divino oraculo Esa. 40, 18. ac divinæ majestati & eminentiæ, concludimus, innui hic mysterium S. S. Trinitatis. Siquidem postmodum vers. 21. manifeste dicatur hoc esse decretum ALTISSIMI, & v. 23. similiter plurali numero idem mysterjum insinuetur; ex quo co- gnoveris, quod sint שליטין DOMINATIONES cœ- li, quod observare etiam licet Dan. 7, 18. 22. 25. 26. ubi electi dicuntur sancti עליונין Altissimorum h. e. Excelsarum divinarum personarum, quæ sunt u- nus ille altissimus & excelsus Deus.

Quam sententiam video etiam probatam B. Lucæ Osiandro in paraphrasi: In sententia vigilum hoc decretum est, & sermo sanctorum hic est, & hæc eo- rum est petitio seu voluntas: quasi dicas: Hoc (post rogatas sententias) fecerunt senatus consultum: id est; Sancta Trinitas (Pater, Filius & Spiritus San- ctus) hoc decretum super Rege Babylonio fecit. Talis enim phrasis extat Jos. 24. Non poteritis servire Domino; Dii enim sancti est ipse. Vocantur autem tres Divinitatis personæ vigiles: quia Sancta Trini- tas vigilat pro salute electorum. Scriptum est enim: Ecce non dormitabit, qui custodit Israël: Psal. 121. Quam etiam suam fecit B. Dn. D. Andr. Osiander ad verba, in sententia vigilum h. l. ita notans: Sic autem vocantur Sacrosanctæ Trinitatis personæ, quia pro salute electorum excubias agunt: Inde Daniel v. 21. dicit: Hanc esse sententiam altissimi. Quam assumpsit quoq;, ac prolixe probavit Dn. D. Haber- korn. noster Syntagm. 1. Dispp. Theol. disp. 1. p. 98. hisce imprimis argumentis: (1) Quia res humanas, inter quas eminent Monarchiæ, cœlitus guberna- re, iisque vel præmia vel supplicia constituere est opus summæ ac divinæ providentiæ, in tota sacra Scriptura soli Deo competentis Dan. 2, 21. Ezech. 21, 27. cap. 31, 11. &c. absit autem, ut il- lud, quod soli Deo proprium prædicatur, angelis ullo sive æquali sive inferiori modo tribuatur. (2) Quia in textu dicitur v. 14. Propterea vigiles san- ctos ita decrevisse, ut Nebucadnezar ad tempus à so- lio suo deponatur, quo viventes exinde cogno- scant, quod Altissimus sit Dominator, potestatem ha- bens in regno hominis, illudq́; det, cui voluerit & hu- milem ex hominibus super illud constituat. At si an- geli essent illi vigiles decernentes, tum illud ipsum non immediate, & adeo firmiter ex eo sequeretur, sed hoc, quod angeli habeant in regna terrestria potestatem. (3.) Decretum & sententia, quæ v. 14. hisce vigilibus tribuitur, postea v. 20. exertissime decretum & sententia Altissimi esse dicitur, Et Ne- bucadnezar resipiscens fatum hoc suum non ange- lis, sed Deo acceptum tulit, & illum laudavit v. 31. seqq. (4) Quod non insolens sit Danieli de Deo in plurali numero loqui cap. 4, 5. c. 7, 18. 22. 25. 26. (5) Quod sacra Scriptura passim Deo nostro sum- mam rerum humanarum curam, custodiam, & vi- giliam assignet Pf. 127, 2. Psal. 80, 2. Pf. 121, 4. Psal. 44, 24. Zach. 4, 10. cap. 9, 1. Ier. 31, 26. (6) Refert huc Thalmudicum illud dictum: Deus Sanctus be- nedictus non facit rem aliquam, nisi consultaverit cum familia, seu ut alii, cum domo judicii sui. Con- fer Buxt. in Lexic. Chaldaico Thalmudico in voce פמל col. 1753. Quod Galatinus ipsis Sacrosanctis Trinitatis personis applicat, & ex Rabbinis ex- plicationem illam derivat lib. 2. de Arcan. Ca- thol. veritat. cap. 9. circa finem pag. 73. 34. Ad- de etiam his: quod nonnulli per vigilem de cælo descendentem vers. 10. Filium Dei intelligant. Ne- que improbatur hæc explicatio B. Lysero in Ce- dro Babylonica pag. 67. Alii per sanctum vigi- lem ipsum Dei filium intelligunt. Cum enim is cla- marit, in consilio vigilum istud de rege decretum esse: Nemo autem ad sacratissimum illud cælorum consi- lium adhibeatur, præterquam tres personæ Sacrosan- ctæ Trinitatis: Ideo inde colligunt, secundam hujus consilii personam, quæ est ὁ λόγος æternus æterni pa- tris consiliarius, hoc decretum Regi denunciasse. Con- venit quoq́; hæc sententia cum Scriptura Sacra, Do- minus enim vigil vel custos Israëlis (Der Wächter Israels) dicitur. Sic enim David in Psalmo canit: Ecce, non dormitabit, nec dormiet, qui custodit Israël. Dominus protectio tua super manum dex- teram tuam. Neq; vero est, quod admittamus, op- positionem hic institui, inter angelos minores & majores, quasi illi consciverint hoc decretum de Nebucadnezare: Hi vero postularent id, ut rem æ- quissimam, quod commentum est Judaico-Grotia- num: Siquidem verba κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν recte ac- cipiantur, ut decretum vigilum, & sermo, & PETI- TIO, VEL VOLUNTAS SANCTORUM ἰσο- δυναμῦντα habeantur; Quemadmodum inter- pretatus est Osiander, Pater: Quam ἰσοδυναμίαν video etiam Lud. de Dieu hic non improbare, quod פִתְגָמָא & שְׁאֵלְתָא idem sit quod præcedens פִּתְגָּמַיְ & שְׁ- trumq́; idem quod Hebræorum דָּבָר. Certe apud A- rabes מִשְׁאֵלָה petitio, cujus plurale est מִשְׁאֵיל u- surpatur pro הַדְּבָרִים ut Gen. 15, 1. c. 24, 66. Ad hunc modum שְׁאֵלְתָא erit negotium, res.

Vers. eod. DONEC COGNOSCANT VIVENTES, QUONIAM DOMINATUR EXCELSUS IN REGNO HOMINUM] Ut cognoscant. Vide infra 22.

ET CIRCUMQUE VOLUERIT, DABIT IL- LUD] Esseni: 8' δίχα Θεῦ περιγίνεται τό ἄρχειν. Homerus τιμὴ δ' ἐκ Διός ἐςι. Potestates fato dari est in Sexto Aure- lio. Adde Augustinum libro 5. de Civit. Dei c. 2.

ET HUMILLIMUM HOMINUM CONSTITUET SUPER EUM] Ut in Judæa Davidem. Vide 1. Sam. 2. v. 8.

## 4:18
Ver. 15. NARRA FESTINUS] In the Chaldee there is not festinus: for that whole כָּל קְבֵל דִּי is nothing else than because.

Latin:

Vers. 15. NARRA FESTINUS] In Chaldæo non est fe- stinus: nam totum illud כָּל קְבֵל דִּי nihil aliud est quam quia.

## 4:19
TACITUS COGITARE] To be struck dumb, by reason of the magnitude and dreadfulness of the things which he saw. In the Greek, ἀπηνεώθη, that is, ἐξεπλάγη, says Polychronius.

QUASI UNA HORA] In the Chaldean, בשעת חדא, that is, a short time. For שעה signifies to the Chaldeans any part of time whatsoever.

LET NOT THE DREAM AND ITS INTERPRETATION TROUBLE THEE] That is, whatever it may be that thou understandest, speak it out freely.

MAY THE DREAM BE TO THOSE WHO HATE THEE, AND THE INTERPRETATION THEREOF TO THINE ENEMIES] May that which the dream portends happen to the enemies. A frequent manner of speaking to those who are averse, may it happen to the enemies. Such also is that of Horace: Hostium uxores pueriq; cæcos Sentiant motus orientis hædi. In Octavia: Ut expientur noctis & somni minæ, Terrorq; in hostes redeat attonitus meos.

Latin:

TACITUS COGITARE] Obstupescere, præ re- rum quas videbat magnitudine ac diritate. In Græco, ἀπηνεώθη, id est, ἐξεπλάγη, ait Polychronius.

QUASI UNA HORA] In Chaldæo, בשעת חדא, id est, modico tempore. Nam שעה Chaldæis qualemcun- que partem temporis significat.

SOMNIUM ET INTERPRETATIO EJUS NON CONTURBENT TE] Id est, qualecunque sit quod intel- ligis, id libere eloquere.

SOMNIUM HIS QUI TE ODERUNT, ET INTERPRETATIO EJUS HOSTIBUS TUIS SIT] Hostibus eveniat quod portendit somnium. Frequens a- versantibus loquendi genus, hostibus eveniat. Tale & il- lud Horatii: Hostium uxores pueriq; cæcos Sentiant motus orientis hædi. In Octavia: Ut expientur noctis & somni minæ, Terrorq; in hostes redeat attonitus meos.

## 4:22
Vers. 19. THOU ART KING] Thou art he, whom that tree signifies.

THY GREATNESS IS GROWN AND THY DOMINION UNTO THE HEAVEN] To the highest ridges of the mountains.

AND THY DOMINION UNTO THE ENDS OF THE WHOLE EARTH] To the Caspian Sea, to the Euxine Pontus, to the Atlantic Ocean.

Josephus, book 1 against Apion, reports that Megasthenes wrote in the 4th book of the Jewish history that Nebuchadnezzar surpassed Hercules in fortitude and the magnitude of his achievements, and that he subjugated the greatest part of Africa and Spain. And Strabo, at the beginning of book 15, recites from the same Megasthenes that Nebuchadnezzar came even to the pillars of Hercules. Eusebius, in book 9 of the Preparation, noted things consistent with these from Abydenus: that Nebuchadnezzar led an army into Libya and Iberia, and when he had subdued those peoples, he led colonies from there into Pontus.

Latin:

Vers. 19. TU ES REX] Tu is es, quem arbor ista significat.

MAGNITUDO TUA CREVIT ET POTESTAS USQUE AD COELUM] Ad summa montium juga.

ET POTESTAS TUA IN TERMINOS UNI- VERSÆ TERRÆ] Ad mare Caspium, ad Pontum Euxi- num, ad Oceanum Atlanticum.

Josephus lib. 1. contra Appionem refert, Mega- sthenem in 4. Judaicorum scripsisse, quod Nebu- cadnezar Herculem fortitudine, & rerum gestarum magnitudine præcesserit, & quod maximam Africæ partem, Hispaniamq; subjugaverit. Et Strabo initio libri 15. ex eodem Megasthene recitat, Nabuchodo- nosarum usq; ad columnas Herculis venisse. Quibus ex Abydeno consentanea annotavit Eusebius lib. 9. præpar. Quod Nabuchodonosar in Lybiam & Ibe- riam exercitum duxerit, cumq; illos populos subegis- set, colonias inde in Pontum deduxerit.

## 4:24
Vers. 21.

WHICH IS COME UPON MY LORD THE KING] He tempers the sadness of the matters with the gentleness of his words as much as he can.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

QUÆ PERVENIT SUPER DOMINUM MEUM REGEM] Tristitiam rerum lenitate verborum quantum potest temperat.

## 4:25
Vers. 22. THEY SHALL DRIVE THEE FROM MEN] That is, you shall be driven out. Thus, soon where you are 'drenched' in Latin, it is in the Chaldean 'they shall moisten,' in certain Greek texts βαφήσεται. This is that very thing which Megasthenes said concerning Nebuchadnezzar: πα- ραχρῆμ' ἀφάνιϛο.

THY DWELLING SHALL BE WITH THE BEASTS AND WILD ANIMALS] It happens even to others from black bile that they wish to live with wild beasts.

THOU SHALT EAT GRASS AS AN OX] Herb. For that is עשבא.

AND THOU SHALT BE DRENCHED WITH THE DEW OF HEAVEN] Naked, without home or shelter.

Latin:

Vers. 22. EJICIENT TE AB HOMINIBUS] Id est, ejicieris. Sic mox ubi Latinus infunderis, in Chaldæo est, tingent, in Græcis quibusdam βαφήσεται. Hoc est illud ipsum, quod de Nabuchodonosoro dixit Megasthenes: πα- ραχρῆμ' ἀφάνιϛο.

CUM BESTIIS FERISQUE ERIT HABITATIO TUA] Etiam aliis ex atra bile id contigit, ut cum feris vellent vivere.

FOENUM UT BOS COMEDES] Herbam. Id enim עשבא.

ET RORE COELI INFUNDERIS] Nudus sine lare ac tecto.

## 4:26
Vers. 23. THY KINGDOM SHALL BE SURE UNTO THEE] Another king shall not be chosen while you are alive, and you shall recover the royal power.

Latin:

Vers. 23. REGNUM TUUM TIBI MANEBIT] Non eligetur rex alius te vivente, & regiam potestatem recupe- rabis.

## 4:27
Vers. 24. BREAK OFF THY SINS BY ALMS] The Chaldean פרק corresponds to the Hebrew פדה, which Jacchiades placed here in his interpretation. It appears in 2 Sam. 4:9, Is. 35:9, Num. 3:49, ch. 18:15, and often elsewhere. Wherefore Theodotion translates it most excellently λύτρωσαι. Nor should it offend anyone that what properly belongs to repentance is attributed to works of penance, in which alms excel: for such is a very frequent metonymy or synecdoche, about which we spoke at Luke 11:41. Chrysostom, in his second letter to Theodore, for λύτρωσαι, cites καθαροῖ, in the same sense. Jerome objects here: if he foretold the sentence of GOD, how does he exhort to alms and mercies to the poor, so that the sentence of GOD might be changed? But he answers with the example of Hezekiah and the Ninevites, and that saying of Jer. 18, and adds: for God is not angry at men, but at vices, which when they are not in a man, He by no means punishes what has been changed.

He strives to defend the Vulgate, because the Chaldean פרק corresponds to the Hebrew פורק, and is best rendered by λύτρωσαι by Theodotion, and by redime by the Vulgate. But although that word is sometimes used in this way; it nevertheless also signifies to break, to break off, to tear away, to abstract, to lay down, and this is perhaps its primary signification, whence it is taken metaphorically for to snatch away, to save: as Buxtorf observed in his Chaldean lexicon. See Rabbinic commentaries. See Exod. 32, 2. c. 28, 28. Num. 1, 51. c. 4, 5. Gen. 27, 40. And that primary meaning is more correct, because sins are not redeemed by alms, but there is a single ἀπολύτρωσις (redemption) of sins made by Christ, Heb. 9, 15, who gave his soul as a λύτρον (ransom) for us, Matt. 20, 18, Mark 10, 45; whence those are injurious to this most perfect ἀπολύτρωσις of Christ who claim the redemption of sins by their own works or alms. Therefore, the meaning of Daniel is, as the blessed Gesner explained, that the King should cease to sin by idolatry, by unjust plundering of subjects, etc., and finally break off the web of various iniquities, and amend his life. Nor indeed is there any mention of alms in the Chaldean, as the Vulgate rendered it, 'redeem your sins by alms,' but the sources are thus: 'Break off your sins by righteousness': which can be understood of the righteousness of faith, for thus we are absolved from sins, as the blessed Gesner observed; and injustice, or when we have attained righteousness, we finally break off sins: and iniquities by mercy or compassion for the poor, namely, the iniquities which were committed by the oppression of the poor, by the plundering of subjects, to whom mercy is subsequently to be shown, or if by righteousness one must also understand inherent righteousness, it exhibits a description of repentance, made a posteriori, whence Osiander paraphrases thus: 'You, O King, have done many things unjustly, proudly, greedily, cruelly in your empire. Therefore, perform true repentance, live justly and innocently hereafter: for injustice exercise justice and equity toward all: for pride embrace humility and kindness: for greed show liberality and beneficence toward miserable men: for cruelty show humanity and clemency to your neighbor.' Then the Lord, when He has seen in you the true fruits of repentance, will repent of the evil which He had thought to do to you, Jer. 18. And for His immense long-suffering and goodness, He will either avert the deserved punishments entirely, or at least will mitigate them greatly. Compare concerning the tyranny of Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 5, 19, 20. The Vulgate wrongly rendered the word צדקת as alms: which meaning it has nowhere in the Holy Scripture, which the Papists more ineptly distort toward satisfactory alms, which are utterly repugnant to the single λύτρῳ (ransom) of Christ.

Same verse.

FORSITAN IGNOSCET DEUS DELICTIS TUIS (PERHAPS GOD WILL FORGIVE YOUR OFFENSES)] הן is put for the Hebrew אולי, and it is rightly translated here by 'perhaps'. Theodotion: ἴσως ἔσαι μακρόθυμος (perhaps He will be long-suffering): And thus Chrysostom cites it. Daniel was not certain about the pardon, but neither did he despair entirely, just as Peter also conducted himself in the matter of Simon Magus, Acts 8, 22.

Although that interpretation of הן as FORSITAN (PERHAPS) can be admitted, by which the relaxation of that most grievous temporal calamity [is meant]; for concerning this we cannot be entirely ἀμετάπτωτοι (unwavering), even if the remission of sins is certain to us, since God, having remitted sins, does not immediately remove the calamities of the faithful, and therefore he could have been entirely certain that the evil which God had threatened would be removed; yet it seems that Grotius here again wished to gratify the Papists with this gloss, who contend from this passage that one must doubt the grace of God. But that dogma can in no way be carved out of this text. For Daniel does not command one to doubt grace and the remission of sins, which is repugnant to the nature of true faith; for this is παρῥησία (boldness), πληροφορία (full assurance), πεποίθησις (confidence), and ὑπόστασις (substance), Rom. 6, 2, Eph. 3, Heb. 10, 8, c. 11, 1. Nor does he make any mention here of the remission of sins, or of eternal salvation, since only a temporal benefit is being dealt with here, namely, the condonation of the denounced punishment: and the sources of Chaldean truth flow thus: 'Behold, there will be a prolongation of your safety.' For the little word הן properly and ordinarily denotes 'Behold,' and so far is it from introducing doubt that it rather refers to a certain confidence and a hope that is not in the least doubtful: as if demonstrating the present grace of God: 'Behold, there will be a prolongation of your safety.' Therefore, the Vulgate Version should have been corrected here, not defended, as the blessed Gesner rightly observed. And in the Bibles of Pagninus an amendment was made, in this way: 'Behold, there will be a prolongation of your peace'; Finally, if you should prefer to translate the word הן with Junius and Pererius as 'Perhaps,' still שליוא cannot be rendered as 'offense' (IT WILL BE A HEALING, OR CURE FOR YOUR OFFENSES). For that is called שלותא and שלו, Dan. 3, 29, and 6, 5. but it ought to be explained by tranquility, prosperity, and safety. Whence Ludov. de Dieu also approved here the interpretation of Junius: 'if perhaps there will be a prolongation of your tranquility.' But these things have nothing to do with doubt concerning the remission and pardon of sins.

Latin:

Vers. 24. PECCATA TUA ELEEMOSYNIS REDI- ME] פרק Chaldæum respondet Hebræo פדה, quod hic in interpretatione posuit Jacchiades. Apparet id 2.Sam. 4, 9. Es. 35, 9. Num. 3, 49. c. 18, 15. & alibi sæpe. Quare optime vertit Theodotion λύτρωσαι. Neque offendere quenquam debet, quod operibus pœnitentiæ, in quibus excellunt ἐλεημοσύναι, tribuatur id, quod pœnitentiæ pro- prie convenit: Est enim talis Μετωνυμία aut συνεκδοχὴ per- frequens, de qua diximus ad Luc. 11, 41. Chrysostomus se- cunda ad Theodorum, pro λύτρωσαι, citat καθαροῖ, sensu eodem. Objicit hic Hieronymus: si prædixit sententiam DEI, quomodo hortatur ad Eleemosynas & misericordias pauperum, ut DEI sententia commutetur? Reponit autem Exemplum Ezechiæ, & Ninivitarum, & dictum illud Jer. 18. additque: neque enim Deus hominibus, sed vitiis ira- scitur, quæ cum in homine non fuerint, nequaquam pu- nit, quod mutatum est.

Vulgatam tueri satagit, quod פרק Chaldaicum respondeat Ebræo פורק, & per λύτρωσαι optime reddatur à Theodotione, à vulgata redime. At quan- quam ita quandoque usurpetur illud verbum; si- gnificat tamen etiam rumpere, abrumpere, avellere. abstrahere, deponere, atque hæc forte est primaria si- gnificatio ejus, unde tralatitie pro eripere, servare sumitur: uti observavit Buxtorfius in lex. Chal- daic. Rabb. vid. Exod. 32, 2. c. 28, 28. Num. 1, 51. c. 4, 5. Gen. 27, 40. & rectius convenit primaria illa significatio, quia peccata non redimuntur Eleemo- synis, sed unica est peccatorum ἀπολύτρωσις à Christo facta, Ebr. 9, 15. qui animam suam dedit λύ- τρον pro nobis Matth. 20, 18. Marc. 10, 45. unde in- jurii sunt in hanc perfectissimam ἀπολύτρωσιν Christi, qui suis operibus, aut Eleemosynis redem- ptionem peccatorum vendicant. Sententia ergo Danielis est, quam B. Gesnerus exposuit, ut Rex desinat peccare idololatria, injustis expilationibus sub- ditorum &c. & telam variarum iniquitatum tandem abrumpat, vitamq́; emendet. Neque vero in Chaldeo Eleemosynarum mentio sit, uti Vulgata reddidit, re- dime peccata tua Eleemosynis, sed ita habent fontes: In justitia abrumpe peccata tua: quod de justitia fi- dei intelligi potest, sic enim absolvumur à peccatis, ut observavit B. Gesnerus; & injustitia, vel cum justitiam adepti sumus, abrumpimus demum pec- cata: & iniquitates in misericordia vel commiseratio- ne pauperum, iniquitates nempe, quæ commissæ sunt oppressióne pauperum, expilationibus subditorum, quibus deinceps exhibenda misericordia, aut si per justitiam etiam intelligenda inhærens justitia, pœni- tentiæ descriptionem exhibet, à posteriori factam, unde ita παραφραζει Osiander: Tu Rex multa injuste, superbe, avare, crudeliter fecisti in tuo im- perio. Quare pœnitentiam veram age, justo & inno- center posthac vive: pro injustitia exerce justitiam & æquitatem erga omnes: pro superbia humilitatem & comitatem amplectere: pro avaritia liberalitatem & beneficentiam erga homines miseros: pro crudelitate humanitatem & clementiam proximo tuo exhibe. Tum Dominum, ubi veros pœnitentiæ fructus in te conspexerit, pœnitebit mali, quod tibi facere cogita- verat, Jer. 18. & pro immensa sua longanimitate & bonitate pœnas meritas aut omnino avertet, aut certe plurimum mitigabit. Confer de Tyrannide Ne- bucadn. Dan. 5, 19. 20. Vulg. vocem צדקת perpe- ram Eleemosynas reddidit: quem sensum nuspiam habet in Scriptura Sacra quod ineptius Papistæ ad Eleemosynas satisfactorias detorquent, quæ unico Christi λύτρῳ prorsus repugnant.

Vers. eod.

FORSITAN IGNOSCET DEUS DELICTIS TUIS] הן pro אולי Hebræo ponitur, & recte hic ver- titur per forsitan. Theodotion: ἴσως ἔσαι μακρόθυμος: Et sic citat Chrysostomus. Non erat certus Daniel de venia, sed nec desperabat omnino, quomodo & Petrus se gessit in negotio Simonis Magi, Act. 8, 22.

Quamvis admitti possit illa interpretatio הן FORSITAN, qua relaxationem calamitatis istius gravissimæ temporalis; de hac enim non possumus omnino esse ἀμετάπτωτοι, etsi remissio peccato- rum nobis certa sit, siquidem Deus remissis pecca- tis non tollit statim calamitates fidelium, ideoque certus omnino esse potuerit, id mali, quod com- minatus erat Deus, sublatum iri; Videtur tamen hic iterum Grotius Papistis hanc glossam gratifica- ri voluisse, qui de gratia Dei dubitandum esse, ex hoc loco contendunt. Quod vero dogma nulla- tenus ex hoc textu exsculpi potest. Non enim ju- bet Daniel dubitare de gratia & remissione pecca- torum, quod repugnat veræ fidei naturæ; hæc e- nim παρῥησία, πληροφορία, πεποίθησις & ὑπό- στασις est Rom. 6, 2. Eph. 3. Ebr. 10, 8. c. 11, 1. Neque ullam mentionem hic facit remissionis peccato- rum, aut salutis æternæ, siquidem tantum de tem- porali beneficio hic agitur, pœnæ nempe denun- ciatæ condonatione: & fontes veritatis Chaldaicæ ita fluunt; Ecce erit prolongatio incolumitatis tuæ. Vocula enim הן proprie & ordinarie notat Ecce, adeoque tantum abest, ut dubitationem inferat, ut potius certam fiduciam ac spem minime dubiam referat: quasi præsentem Dei gratiam demonstrans: Ecce erit prolongatio incolumitatis tuæ. Corrigenda ergo hic, non defendenda erat vulgata Versio, ut recte observavit B. Gesnerus. Et in Bibliis Pagnini emendatio facta est, hoc modo: Ecce erit prolonga- tio paci tuæ; Denique si maxime vocem הן cum Ju- nio & Pererio malis vertere, Forte, non tamen שליוא reddi potest delictum (ERIT MEDELA, VEL CURATIO DELICTIS TUIS) Nam id dicitur שלותא & שלו Dan. 3, 29. & 6, 5. sed expo- ni debet per tranquillitatem, prosperitatem, & inco- lumitatem. Unde Ludov. de Dieu etiam proba- vit hic Junii interpretationem: si forte erit proro- gatio tranquillitati tuæ. Hæc vero nihil ad dubita- tionem de remissione & venia peccatorum.

## 4:29
Verse 26.

POST FINEM MENSIUM DUODECIM (AFTER THE END OF TWELVE MONTHS)] The Hebrews, whom Jerome follows, think that Nebuchadnezzar, having followed the counsel of Daniel, attained by works of mercy that the punishment was suspended for twelve months: but then, his mind becoming arrogant again, no further delay was given to him, but the punishment was at hand. IN AULA BABYLONIS DEAMBULABAT (HE WAS WALKING IN THE PALACE OF BABYLON)] Abydenus: ἀναβὰς ἐπὶ τὰ βασιλήϊα (having ascended to the royal palace).

Latin:

Vers. 26.

POST FINEM MENSIUM DUODECIM] Cen- sent Hebræi, quos sequitur Hieronymus, Nabuchodo- nosorem, secutum consilium Danielis, per opera miseri- cordiæ id consecutum, ut pœna per duodecim menses suspenderetur: verum tunc iterum insolescente ipsius ani- mo, nihil ultra moræ ipsi datum, sed præsto fuisse pœnam. IN AULA BABYLONIS DEAMBULABAT] Abydenus: ἀναβὰς ἐπὶ τὰ βασιλήϊα.

## 4:30
Verse 27. RESPONDITQUE REX, ET AIT (AND THE KING ANSWERED AND SAID)] He spoke, and said. Πλεονασμὸς (pleonasm), such as several times above. For ענה is said not only of a response, but of any speech whatsoever.

NON EST HÆC BABYLON MAGNA, QUAM EGO ÆDIFICAVI? (IS NOT THIS GREAT BABYLON, WHICH I HAVE BUILT?)] To the old I added a new city; I surrounded each with triple walls, magnificent gates. See the passage of Berosus. IN ROBORE FORTITUDINIS MEÆ (BY THE MIGHT OF MY STRENGTH)] By the power of my riches. For that is חסן. ET IN GLORIA DECORIS MEI (AND FOR THE GLORY OF MY MAJESTY)] For the glory of my name.

A VOICE FALLS FROM HEAVEN] καταχθίση Θεῷ ὅτεῳ δὴ. Abydenus.

Latin:

Vers. 27. RESPONDITQUE REX, ET AIT] Lo- cutus est, & dixit. Πλεονασμὸς, qualis supra aliquoties. Nam ענה non de responsione utique, sed de quavis locutione dicitur.

NON EST HÆC BABYLON MAGNA, QUAM EGO ÆDIFICAVI?] Veteri addidi urbem novam; singulis terna circumjeci mœnia, portas magnificas. Vide Berosi locum. IN ROBORE FORTITUDINIS MEÆ] Vi opum mearum. Id enim חסן. ET IN GLORIA DECORIS MEI] Ad gloriam nominis mei.

VOX DE CŒLO RUIT] καταχθίση Θεῷ ὅτεῳ δὴ. Abydenus.

## 4:31
Vers. 28. AND WHILE THE WORD WAS YET IN THE KING'S MOUTH] παραχρῆμα, says Abydenus. THY KINGDOM SHALL DEPART FROM THEE] It shall go away from thee. Kingdom, that is, the function of the kingdom.

Latin:

Vers. 28. CUMQUE SERMO ADHUC ESSET IN ORE REGIS] παραχρῆμα, ait Abydenus. REGNUM TUUM TRANSIBIT A TE] Abibit abs te. Regnum, id est, regni functio.

## 4:33
Vers. 30. THE SAME HOUR] That is, at that very time. HIS HAIR GREW LIKE EAGLES' FEATHERS, AND HIS NAILS LIKE BIRDS'] The meaning is that his hair, beard, and nails had grown very long, because no one was present to trim them, nor did he himself think of trimming them, loving the likeness of wild beasts on account of black bile.

Thus he makes the punishment of Nebuchadnezzar nothing other than Melancholy, or a disease such as sometimes arises from black bile, whence he loved the likeness of wild beasts and wished to live with them on account of black bile. Although indeed one must by no means agree with those who say that he was either truly changed into a wild beast, or at least, with his rational soul left behind, passed into a beast as far as the form of his body is concerned, which the latter Augustine, Epist. 187, Dorotheus in Synops., and Epiphanius in the life of Daniel seem to have believed; as also Bodin, l. 2, c. 6, Dæmonol., and Corn. à Lap., whom Suaningius refutes here: Yet it was not merely a corruption of the Phantasy, as Grotius thinks with Pererius, much less mere illusions here, that he only appeared to others like a wild beast, or an external spectacle only, as if God had placed some figure of a wild beast around his body, under which he was believed by others to be a wild beast. Since the words of the text imply something more, and beyond the Phantasies and the corruption of the imagination, by which he seemed to himself to be changed into a wild beast, of one species or another, and thus also loved to live with wild beasts, and was deprived of the use of reason for a great part, and used almost only a bestial phantasy, since it is expressly said: LET A BEAST'S HEART BE GIVEN TO HIM, verse 13. Which cannot be taken parabolically, as Origen wished. For a true history is narrated here. Although it seems not to be denied that through some intervals he had that sole use of reason. Furthermore, the heart's complexion also was changed, and it was so brutalized that it was like that of a wild beast, as much as could happen short of the loss of human nature or transubstantiation. Furthermore, his habit also became more beastly than human, because he walked naked and was exposed to dew, rain, and other injuries of the air, wandering without hearth or home, and his hair grew so that it covered almost his entire body, and the very thick hairs resembled the feathers of birds. His nails were not trimmed and grew like the claws of birds. His skin was not soft, but hard and more like that of a beast than a human; his face, different from a human one, appeared to approach a beastly one; his gait was of a beastly form, because he did not walk erect, but curved and prone, crawling on hands and feet like a beast; therefore v. 33 says: my figure returned to me. Finally, he lived with beasts in the woods, like a beast, and enjoyed their food, herbs, and roots. B. Gesner also thinks that he himself, like a furious man possessed by Satan, was driven here and there through the lairs of wild beasts. Voetius, disp. select. p. 1. de Energ. p. 1056, thinks that an Energema was similarly mixed in. But he was guarded by God so that he would not be harmed by other beasts, to whom he also seemed a beast. Jacobus Capellus, Histor. Sac. & Exot. to the year of the World 3428, p. 241, has this to say about this punishment: The mode taken surpasses our mode. Let it be Lycanthropy, let it be Corybantism, let it be Melancholic fury, provided we know that the man was not actually changed into a beast, but that he took on an external figure, not an essential change of form, and that such a thing could not be performed by men of wicked superstition, or by Satan himself, as God performed here, to demonstrate His power and to confound the insolence of proud Princes. Moreover, nothing certain is known about the time of this punishment of the King: Josephus reports that this happened not long after the miracle of the three confessors. Salianus and Torniellus, with Pererius, refer it to the 36th year of Nebuchadnezzar, who, since he was finally restored after seven years, the restoration falls into the last year, which they make the 43rd: which others, however, think happened two years before his death. See the Notae Belgic. on this passage. Ussher, in Annal. Vet. Testamenti, refers his restoration to the last year of Nebuchadnezzar.

Latin:

Vers. 30. EADEM HORA] Id est, illo ipso tempore. CAPILLI EJUS IN SIMILITUDINEM AQUI- LARUM CRESCERENT, ET UNGUES EJUS QUA- SI AVIUM] Sensus est, plurimum excrevisse ei capil- los, barbam & ungues, quia nemo aderat, qui resecaret, nec ipse de iis refecandis cogitabat, amans ob atram bi- lem ferarum similitudinem.

Ita pœnam Nabuchodonosaris aliam non fa- cit, quam Melancholiam, vel morbum, qualis ex a- tra bile quandoque oritur, unde ferarum similitu- dinem amarit, & cum iis ob atram bilem vivere vo- luerit. Quanquam vero minime assentiendum illis, qui vel vere in feram mutatum, vel saltim relicta anima rationali, quoad formam corporis, in be- stiam transiisse ipsum dicunt, quod posterius Au- gustin. Epist. 187. Dorotheus in Synops. & Epiphan. in vita Danielis credidisse videntur; ut & Bodin. l. 2. c. 6. Dæmonol. & Corn. à Lap. quem hic refutat Suaningius: Non tamen mera tantum Phantasiæ corruptio fuit, uti cum Pererio Grotius existimat, ne- dum meræ hic præstigiæ, quod aliis tantum instar fe- ræ visus fuerit, aut externum solum spectaculum, qua- si Deus circa corpus ejus feræ aliquam figuram cir- cumposuerit, sub qua visus creditus aliis fuerit fe- ra. Siquidem aliquid amplius textus verba impor- tant, ac præter Phantasias ac imaginationis corru- ptionem, qua sibi in feram, unius puta aut alterius speciei mutatus videbatur, adeoque & cum feris vivere amabat, rationis usu magnam partem priva- tus fuerit, & phantasia fere tantum utebatur ferina, quum expresse dicatur: COR FERÆ DETUR EI, vers. 13. Quod non potest parabolice accipi, ut O- rigenes voluit. Nam hic vera historia narratur. Etsi per intervalla aliqua, eum solum usum rationis ha- buisse non negandum videtur. Adhæc cordis com- plexio etiam immutata, idque ita efferatum fuit, ut simile esset ferino, quantum citra naturae hu- manae amissionem, aut transsubstantiationem fieri potuit. Porro habitus etiam accedebat, ferinus ma- gis, quam humanus, quia nudus incedebat, rorique, imbri, & aliis aëris injuriis expositus, fine lare & tecto oberrabat, & capilliejus accreverunt, ut to- tum pene corpus contegerent, ac pili crassissimi avium plumas referrent. Ungues non resecaban- tur, & ad instar unguium avium excrefcebant. Cu- tis non erat mollis, sed dura & ferinae magis, quam humanae similis, facies ab humana diversa accede- re ad ferinam apparebat, incessus forma ferina e- rat, quia non erectus incedebat, sed curvus & pro- nus, manibus & pedibus reptabat instar bestiae, id- eo v. 33. dicit: figura mea reversa est ad me. Denique cum feris versabatur in sylvis, quasi fera, earumque victu fruebatur, herbis, & radicibus. B. Gefnerus pu- tat etiam ipsum instar furiosi & obfessi hominis à Sa- tana hinc inde per lustra ferarum agitatum fuisse. Similiter Energema admixtum fuisse, censet Voe- tius disp. select. p. 1. de Energ. p. 1056. Sed ne à fe- ris aliis laederetur, quibus fera quoque videbatur, à Deo custoditus est. Iacobus Capellus Histor. Sac. & Exot. ad annum Mund. 3428. p. 241. ita de hoc sup- plicio habet: Modus captus nostri modum superat. Sit sane Lycanthropismus, sit Corybantismus, sit furor Melancholicus, modo sciamus nec hominem reapse in feram mutatum, sed externam figuram, nec essentia- lem formae mutationem illum suscepisse, nec tale quic- quam à malefica superstitionis hominibus, aut ab ipso Satana praestari posse, quale hic patravit Deus, de- monstrandae potentiae sua & confundenda Principum superbientium insolentia. Ceterum de tempore hu- jus supplicii Regis nihil certi constat: Josephus non multo post miraculum trium confessorum haec evenisse refert. Salianus & Torniellus cum Pere- rio id referunt ad annum Nebucadnezaris 36. qui cum restitutus demum fuerit post septennium, in annum ultimum, quem faciunt 43. restitutio inci- det: quam tamen biennio ante obitum ejus acci- disse alii putant. Vid. Notae Belgic. ad h. l. In ulti- mum annum Nebucadnezaris refert Usserius in Annal. Vet. Testamenti ejus restitutionem.

## 4:34
Vers. 31. I LIFTED MY EYES TO HEAVEN] I prayed to the God of heaven. See concerning this expression Ezek. 18, 6. Add what is at Luke 16, 23. AND MY SENSE WAS RESTORED TO ME] Full use of the mind. AND I BLESSED THE MOST HIGH] I, a suppliant, gave thanks to that supreme God, the maker of heaven and earth, whom the Hebrews worship. FOR HIS POWER IS AN EVERLASTING POWER] Not temporary and mutable, like that of kings. HIS KINGDOM IS UNTO GENERATION AND GENERATION] The same sense as preceded, in other words. Vers. 32. AND ALL THE INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH ARE AS NOTHING BEFORE HIM] They are to be compared to nothing. THEY ARE REPUTED AS NOTHING] They are to be held for nothing. For the Hebrews and Chaldeans express such participles by the past, which also has the force of the present. FOR HE DOES ACCORDING TO HIS WILL] That is, whatever he wishes to effect, he effects, Jer. 23, 13. Ps. 115, 3. BOTH IN THE POWERS OF HEAVEN] Through those watchers ἐγρηγόρες. For ב here, as often, is 'by'. AND IN THE INHABITANTS OF THE EARTH] Through men also who are domestic. AND THERE IS NONE THAT CAN RESIST HIS HAND] His immense power. AND SAY TO HIM, WHY HAVE YOU DONE SO?] Who has the right to call Him to account, Rom. 9, 20. Vers. 33. AT THE SAME TIME MY SENSE RETURNED TO ME] That common sense, which is called the use of the mind. In the Chaldean, מַנְדְעִי; that is, the cognitive faculty: αἱ φρένες με, to Theodotion.

Latin:

Vers. 31. OCULOS MEOS AD COELUM LEVA- VI] Deum coe liprecatus sum. Vide de hac locutione E- zech. 18, 6. Adde quae ad Luc. 16, 23. ET SENSUS MEUS REDDITUS EST MIHI] Plenus mentis usus. ET ALTISSIMO BENEDIXI] Illi summo Deo coeli terraeque opifici, quem Hebraei colunt, supplex egi gratias. QUIA POTESTAS EJUS POTESTAS SEMPI- TERNA] Non temporaria ac mutabilis, ut regum. REGNUM EJUS IN GENERATIONEM ET GE- NERATIONEM] Idem sensus, qui praecessit, verbis aliis. Vers. 32. ET OMNES HABITATORES TERRAE JUXTA EUM] Scipsi comparentur. IN NIHILUM REPUTATI SUNT] Pro nihilo habendi sunt. Nam & participia talia per praeteritum, quod & praesentis vim habet, exprimunt Hebraei & Chaldaei. JUXTA VOLUNTATEM ENIM SUAM FA- CIT] Id est, quicquid efficere vult id efficit, Jer. 23, 13. Psal. 115, 3. TAM IN VIRTUTIBUS COELI] Per illos vi- giles ἐγρηγόρες. Nam ב hic, ut saepe, est per. QUAM IN HABITATORIBUS TERRAE] Per homines etiam domesticos. ET NON EST QUI RESISTAT MANUI EJUS] Potentiae ejus immensae. ET DICAT EI, QUARE FECISTI?] Qui jus habeat ipsum ad rationes vocandi, Rom, 9, 20. Vers. 33. IN IPSO TEMPORE SENSUS MEUS REVER- SUS EST AD ME] Sensus ille communis, qui dicitur, mentis usus. In Chaldaeo, מַנְדְעִי; id est, vix cogni- trix: αἱ φρένες με, Theodotioni.

## 4:36
AND I CAME TO THE HONOR OF MY KINGDOM AND MY GLORY] That is, to the function of the kingdom. Jerome well took הַדְרִי for הַדְרִית or הָדְרַת, a Chaldean verb of the first person by the usual apocope. Theodotion no less well ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν με ἰκραταιώθην. AND MY FIGURE RETURNED TO ME] So also in the Greeks, ἡ μορφή με ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ. Nor is זִיו taken otherwise below 5, 10. Jacchiades explains it as אֵיךְ פְּנֵי. For those whose mind is stirred by black bile are accustomed to show their disease even in their eyes and whole countenance. Pacuvius: But why did she seem to rave suddenly with burning eyes? Plautus, in Captivi: Do you see that your body is being stained with lurid spots? Thus bile agitates a man. This about black bile is now finished. Corn. hence sculpted a beastly figure: but neither below ch. 5, 10, nor elsewhere is the figure denoted by this word, which properly denotes splendor, such as that of the stars, Is. 14, 12. Job 31, 26. & then it is transferred to grace, beauty, dignity, Job 40, 5. 2 Sam. 22, 13. it is used of splendor above ch. 2, 31. AND MY NOBLES, [הַדָּבְרַי is a common noun for magistrates, as we said above 3, 94. AND MY MAGISTRATES] In the Chaldean רַבְרְבָנַי, great ones of the great. To Theodotion μεγιστᾶνες, as here, so 5, 1. 2. 9, 25. ch. 6, 17. these were the delegates of the orders, whom it is the custom to employ in such matters. SOUGHT ME] Touched by πολυπραγίας, and thence the following ἀνοχῆς. AND I WAS RESTORED IN MY KINGDOM] Something similar happened in France to Louis the Pious. AND GREATER MAGNIFICENCE WAS ADDED TO ME] μεγαλωσύνη: my authority among my people was greater than it was before, from this so great a benefit of God toward me. Vers. 34. THE KING OF HEAVEN] Him whom he called elsewhere the God of gods and the most high God. FOR ALL HIS WORKS ARE TRUE] That is, right: for so קשט is often taken among the Chaldeans, and אמת among the Hebrews. AND HIS WAYS ARE JUDGMENTS] All his actions are most just. AND THOSE WHO WALK IN PRIDE] Such as Nebuchadnezzar had been because of fortune flattering him for a long time. See his χαρακτηρισμὸν above 2, 5.12. 3, 6.19. 4, 7. HE IS ABLE TO HUMBLE] To depress. He shows this, of course, by an admirable example, ῥεῖα δ' ἀρίζηλον μινύθει. Chaeremon: Ὅλως τὸ κρεῖσσον ἐκ ἐᾷ μέγα φρονεῖν. Sophocles in Ajax: Τὰ γὰρ περισσὰ κἀνόνητα σώματα, Πίπτειν βαρεῖαις πρὸς Θεῶν δυς πραξίαις Ἔφαχ' ὁ μάντις, ὅςις ἀνθρώπυ φύσιν Βλαςὼν, ἔπειτα μὴ κατ' ἄνθρωπον φρονεῖ.

Latin:

ET AD HONOREM REGNI MEI DECOREM- QUE PERVENI] Id est, ad functionem regni. Bene הַדְרִי Hieronymus accepit pro הַדְרִית aut הָדְרַת Chaldaico verbo primae personae per apocopen usitatam. Theodotion non minus bene ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν με ἰκραταιώ- θην. ET FIGURA MEA REVERSA EST AD ME] Ita & Graecis, ἡ μορφή με ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ. Nec aliter su- mitur זִיו infra 5, 10. Jacchiades exponit אֵיךְ פְּנֵי So- lent enim quibus atra bile mens est percita, etiam oculis & vultu toto praeferre morbum. Pacuvius : Sed quid oculis rabere visa est derepente ardentibus? Plautus, captivis: Viden' tu illi maculari corpus tuum maculis luridis? Ita bilis agitat hominem. Hoc de atra bile jam profligatum. Corn. hinc figuram bestialem exsculpsit: sed neque infra cap. 5, 10. nec alibi figura hac voce notatur, quae proprie splendorem, qualis stellarum est, notat Ef. 14, 12. Iob. 31, 26. & deinde ad gratiam, decorem, di- gnitatem, transfertur Job. 40, 5. 2. Sam. 22, 13. de splendore adhibetur supra cap. 2, 31. ET OPTIMATES MEI, [הַדָּבְרַי est nomen commune magistratibus, ut diximus supra 3, 94. ET MAGISTRATUS MEI] In Chaldaico רַבְרְבָנַי magni magnorum. Theodotioni μεγιστᾶνες, ut hic, ita 5, 1. 2. 9, 25. c. 6, 17. fuere hi ordinum delegati, quos in talibus rebus adhibere mos est. REQUISIERUNT ME] Pertacti πολυπραγίας, & inde sequentis ἀνοχῆς. ET IN REGNO MEO RESTITUTUS SUM] Simile quid evenit in Francia Ludovico Pio. ET MAGNIFICENTIA AMPLIOR ADDITA EST MIHI] μεγαλωσύνη: major fuit mea quam ante apud meos auctoritas ex hoc tanto Dei in me beneficio. Vers. 34. REGEM COELI] Illum, quem alibi dixit Deum deorum & Deum summum. QUIA OMNIA EJUS OPERA VERA] Id est, recta: ita enim saepe קשט sumitur apud Chaldaeos, & אמת apud Hebraeos. ET VIAE EJUS JUDICIA] Omnes actiones ejus justissimae. ET GRADIENTES IN SUPERBIA] Qualis ob fortunam diu blandientem fuerat Nabuchodonosor. Vide ejus χαρακτηρισμὸν supra 2, 5.12. 3, 6.19. 4, 7. POTEST HUMILIARE] Deprimere. Ostendit id scilicet admirando specimine, ῥεῖα δ' ἀρίζηλον μινύθει. Chaeremon: Ὅλως τὸ κρεῖσσον ἐκ ἐᾷ μέγα φρονεῖν. Sophocles Ajace: Τὰ γὰρ περισσὰ κἀνόνητα σώματα, Πίπτειν βαρεῖαις πρὸς Θεῶν δυς πραξίαις Ἔφαχ' ὁ μάντις, ὅςις ἀνθρώπυ φύσιν Βλαςὼν, ἔπειτα μὴ κατ' ἄνθρωπον φρονεῖ.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

To King Balthasar celebrating a banquet and praising his idols, a hand writing on the wall was seen, because of which, being terrified, when the Magi were unable to provide an interpretation, at the Queen's warning he summons Daniel, who rebukes the King because, having neglected the example of the humiliation of Nebuchadnezzar, he had exalted himself against the Lord, and having abandoned Him, had worshipped his own idols, and he teaches that for this reason this hand was sent; whose writing he reads aloud and interprets concerning the reprobation of the King and the translation of the Kingdom to the Medes and Persians. Added is the remuneration of Daniel, the killing of King Balthasar, and the dissipation of the kingdom performed by Darius the Mede.

Vers. 1.

KING BALTHASAR] בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר, that is, Beltis is, whose wealth, that is, in the power of Bel are wealth and empires. The Greeks change ש into σ, as the Chaldeans themselves often do; therefore they write Βαλτάσαρ. Such names they assumed when raised to power, whereas in lesser fortune they were called by others.
