This Balthasar, however, who was killed in the city of Babylon itself by conspirators, cannot be anyone other than Laborosoarchodus, as he writes

Berosus, or Laborosoarchod, as Abydenus writes, both of whom record that he was killed by violence. He must have had a short reign, because Ptolemy omits his name. Daniel passed over the times of Evil-Merodach and Neriglissar, because nothing had happened during them pertaining to the confirming of the Jews in piety. Laborosoarchod was, however, the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar, but by a daughter, as we learn from Berosus and Abydenus. See Jer. 27, 6 and what is said there.

Many chronologists raise a very serious doubt against this opinion concerning Belshazzar and the Babylonian kings from Jer. 27, 7, because it seems to be said there that only Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his son's son—but not his daughter's son—would rule over the first monarchy, concerning which see also Gesner, disp. 6, Thes. 4, and Disp. 5, th. 15. The blessed Dr. Behm solves this in his Chronology, p. 225, as follows: (1) This passage of Jeremiah evidently does not prove that only three Babylonian kings are to be counted from Nebuchadnezzar to Cyrus, since no mention of Cyrus is made there. (2) Jeremiah wished to count the natural and hereditary kings born of royal blood. In this way, Jeremiah agrees perfectly with Berosus and Megasthenes. For although these do not count three, but five Babylonian kings from Nebuchadnezzar to Cyrus, two of them were not hereditary kings born of royal blood. For Neriglissar, the son-in-law of Nebuchadnezzar and kinsman of Evil-Merodach, occupied the kingdom after Evil-Merodach was killed (1) illegitimately through tyranny, (2) he administered the kingdom only in the name of a tutor, until Belshazzar, still a minor, should reach the years of puberty. Jeremiah also did not wish to count the last king of the Babylonians, Nabonidus, because he himself was not an hereditary king. For he was a Mede by seed and blood, as Daniel testifies, ch. 9, 1. Therefore, the same prophet writes in Belshazzar, King of Babylon, that the kingdom was absolute by reason of royal lineage; ch. 5, 26. And Megasthenes, in Eusebius, testifies that the Babylonians chose Nabonidus as king, οὐδὲν προσήκοντα, joined to the previous Babylonian kings by no blood, affinity, or proximity. (3) The phrase of Jeremiah (בֶּן־בְּנוֹ & son of a son) could also be easily reconciled with the history of Berosus and Megasthenes, provided that minds were eager for reconciliation. The word בֵּן is general and often includes both sexes among the Hebrews, just as the word 'children' does among the Latins. Thus, it is customary in Scripture to call grandchildren indiscriminately 'sons of sons,' whether from sons or daughters. Zedekiah is called בֵּן, or son of Jeconiah, 1 Chron. 3, 16, although he was the son of Jehoiakim, Zedekiah's brother, 2 Kings 24, 17. Zerubbabel is called the son of Shealtiel, Hag. 1, 1, Mal. 1, 12, and elsewhere, although he was the son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother, 1 Chron. 3, verse 19. Shealtiel is called the son of Jeconiah, 1 Chron. 3, 17, although he was the son of Neri from the posterity of Nathan, Luke 3, 27. Many such examples from the sacred texts could be produced if it were necessary. Since, therefore, Berosus and Megasthenes write that Laborosoarchod was the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar by a daughter, the son of Evil-Merodach's sister, no necessity compels us to accuse these fragments of falsehood and to take the word בֵּן most strictly for the son of a son (not a daughter), since the generic and indefinite acceptance of the word בֵּן in sacred texts is known even to a beginner in the holy language. This is the view of the blessed Dr. Behm. But there is no need for us to make a daughter out of a son, nor can any similar example be brought forward from the Scriptures. Jeremiah says only this: that the son of Nebuchadnezzar, Evil-Merodach, and the son of this son himself would reign until the end of the kingdom. Now, no other son of Evil-Merodach is found under whom the kingdom had its end than Nabonidus. Nor can it be established otherwise by the force of Jeremiah's oracle than that this Nabonidus is Belshazzar. For those two characteristics are certain and must concur in one person: to be the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar and the last Babylonian king. But the last king of Babylon was Belshazzar. Therefore, he is the same grandson of Nebuchadnezzar. According to foreign writers, the last Babylonian king was Nabonidus, from whom the transfer of the empire to the Medes and Persians took place. Therefore, the Belshazzar of Daniel is not Laborosoarchod, who was neither the son of a son of Nebuchadnezzar nor the last monarch of the Babylonians; but he is Nabonidus, whom the Scaligerians rashly confuse with Darius the Mede. For the latter was neither a grandson nor the last in the first monarchy, speaking precisely. Compare what is said at verse 31.

Verse of the same.

HE MADE A GREAT FEAST] Kings of the East were sometimes accustomed to do this, as appears from Herodotus, book 1, and Xenophon, book 7.

Some think a solemn feast was instituted in honor of Bel, which they confirm from Herodotus, book 1, and Xenophon, chapter 7, of the Cyropaedia; to which some also refer Ex. 21, 5, seqq. Junius and Polanus contend that the feast was celebrated in honor of the idol Shach, from Jer. 25, 26; but others prefer to note there by the word ששך not an idol, but either the last Chaldean king or the Chaldean empire itself. It is more likely that Belshazzar was celebrating his birthday, which some strive to prove from those very places in Herodotus and Xenophon. The day of that annual festival was not unknown to Cyrus from the custom of previous times; therefore, he thought the gamble of his entire fortune should be reserved for this night, which was especially dedicated to gluttony and drinking bouts; perhaps also, as it seemed to the blessed Svaningius, he was taught about the outcome at the time of the feast from Isa. 21, 5.

TO HIS THOUSAND LORDS] Who were indeed in the same hall, but sat separately from the king. Statius on the banquet of Domitian: 'Here Caesar ordered a thousand Romulean nobles and the trabeated ranks to sit at the tables at the same time.'

See the whole poem, so that you may grasp the image of this matter.

AND EACH ONE ACCORDING TO HIS AGE DRANK: HE COMMANDED THEREFORE NOW DRUNKEN] These depart far from the Chaldean. Theodotion follows the words and the sense well: καὶ κατέναντι τῶν χιλίων ὁ οἶνος, καὶ πίνων Βαλτάσαρ εἶπεν ἐν τῇ γεύσει τῶ οἶνω. The sense is: that a cup had been placed before each of the thousand guests, and a man who would pour wine for the one asking: thus according to the custom of the region. Then, while drinking, the wine pleased the king more and more.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Regi Balthafari convivium celebranti, & ido- la sua laudanti, manus scribens in pariete visa, ob quam perterrefactus Magis inter- pretationem reddere nescientibus Regina monitu Danielem accersit, qui reprehen- dit Regem, quod exemplo humiliationis Ne- bucadnezaris posthabito sese contra Domi- num extulerit, eog relicto idola sua colue- rit, atq, ideo hanc manum missam esse do- cet; cujus scripturam pralegit & interpre- tatur de Regis reprobatione, & Regni ad Medos, & Persas translatione. Additur re- muneratio Danielis, occisio Balthasaris Re- gis, & regni dissipatio à Dario Medo facta.

Vers. 1.

BALTHASAR REX] בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר, id est, Beltis est, cu- jus opes, Id est, in Beli potestate sunt opes & imperia. Graeci ש in σ mutant, ut & ipsi Chaldaei saepe; itaq; scribunt Βαλ- τάσαρ. Talia nomina assumebant ad imperium evecti, cum in minore fortuna aliis appellarentur. Hic autem Baltha- sar, qui in ipsa urbe Babylone à conjuratis interfectus est, non potest alius esse, quam Laborosoarchodus, ut scribit

Berosus, sive Laborossoaraschus, ut scribit Abydenus, qui ambo eum vi interfectum memorant. Breve oportet re- gaum habuerit, quia omittit ejus nomen Ptolemaeus. Da- niel Evilmeroduchi & Neriglassaris tempora transiit, quod per ea nihil contigisset ad Judaeos in pietate confirmandos pertinens. Fuit autem Laborosoarchodus Nabuchodo- nosoris nepos, sed ex filia, ut ex Beroso & Abydeno disci- mus. Vide Jerem. 27, 6. & ibi dicta.

Dubium adversus hanc de Balthasare, & Re- gibus Babyloniis sententiam gravissimum movent plerique Chronologi e Jer. 27, 7. quod ibi dictum videatur, solum Nebucadnezarem, & filium, ac fi- lium filii, non autem filiæ, Monarchiæ primæ præ- futurum, de quo etiam vide Gesneri disp. 6. Thes. 4. & Disp. 5. th. 15. Quod B. Dn. D. Behm. ita solvit in Chronolog. p. 225. (1.) Hunc Jeremiæ locum evidenter non probare tres tantum Babylonicos Reges a Nebucadnezare ad Cyrum numerandos, cum ibidem nulla Cyri fiat mentio. (2.) Jere- mias numerare voluit Reges naturales & hæredita- rios e regio sanguine progenitos. Hoc modo Jeremiæ cum Beroso & Megasthene optime conve- nit. Licet enim hi non tres, sed quinq; Babyloni- cos Reges numerent a Nebucadnezare ad Cyrum, duo tamen eorum non fuerunt Hæreditarii Reges, e Regio sanguine oriundi. Neriglissor enim Ne- bucadnezaris gener, Evilmerodachi affinis, Evil- merodacho interfecto Regnum occupavit (1.) ille- gitime per Tyrannidem, (2) Tutorio tantum nomi- ne regnum administravit, donec Balthasar adhuc minorennis ad pubertatis annos perveniret. Ulti- mum quoque Babyloniorum Regem Nabonnidum Jeremias numerare noluit, quia & ipse hæredita- rius Rex non fuit. Fuit enim semine & sanguine Medus, teste Daniele c. 9, 1. Ideo idem Propheta scribit in Balthasare Rege Babylonium, regnum ratione Regiæ prosapiæ absolutum; c. 5, 26. Et Megasthenes apud Eusebium testatur Babylonios Nabonnidum in Regem elegisse ουδεν προσηκοντα nul- lo sanguine nullave affinitate vel propinquitate prio- ribus Babylonicis Regibus junctum. (3.) Phrasis Jeremiæ (בֶּן־בְּנוֹ & filio filii) cum Berosi & Me- gasthenis historia facile quoque conciliaretur, mo- do forent mentes conciliationis avidæ. Vox בֵּן ge- neralis utrumq; sæpe sexum comprehendit apud Ebræos, ut apud Latinos vox liberi. Ita solenne est scripturæ filios filiorum appellare indifferetim nepotes tam ex filiis, quam filiabus. Zedekias nomi- natur בֵּן seu filius Jechoniæ 1. Chron. 3, 16. Cum ta- men fuerit filius Jehojakimi fratris Zedekiæ 2. Reg. 24, 17. Zerubabel nominatur filius Sealthielis Hag. 1, 1. Malach. 1, 12. & passim alibi, cum tamen Phadai, fratris Sealthielis filius fuerit, 1. Chron. 3. vers. 19. Schealthiel nominatur filius Iechoniæ 1. Chron. 3, 17. cum filius Neri fuerit ex posteritate Nathanis. Luc. 3, 27. Ejusmodi exempla ex sacris quam plurima produci possent, si necesse foret. Cum ergo Be- rosus cum Megasthene scribant Laborosoardochum fuisse nepotem Nebucadnezaris ex filia sororis Evil- merodachi filium, nulla nos cogit necessitas, hæc fragmenta falsitatis insimulare, vocemque בֵּן stri- ctissime pro filio filii (non filiæ) sumere, cum ge- nerica & indefinita vocis בֵּן in sacris acceptio, vel tyroni sanctæ linguæ nota sit. Hæc B. D. Behmius. Sed non opus est, ut ex filio faciamus filiam: neque simile exemplum e Scripturis proferri potest ul- lum: Id solum dicit Jeremias, filium Nebucadneza- ris, Evilmerodachum, & hujus filii ipsius filium regna- turum usq; ad finem regni. Filius autem Evilme- rodachi nullus alius reperitur, sub quo finem re- gnum habuerit, quam Nabonidus: Neq; aliter vi oraculi Jeremiæ statui potest, quam Nabonidum hunc esse Balthasarem. Duo enim illi characteres certi sunt, & in una persona concurrere debent: ne- potem esse Nebucadnezaris, & ultimum Regem Babylo- nium. At ultimus Babyloniæ Rex fuit Balthasar. I- dem ergo nepos Nebucadnezaris. Ultimus juxta exoticos scriptores Babyl. Rex fuit Nabonidus, à quo translatio facta imperii est in Medos & Persas. Balthasar ergo Danielis non est Laborosoardochus, qui nec filius filii Nebucadnezaris fuit, neque ulti- mus Babyloniorum Monarcha; sed Nabonidus: quem temere Scaligeriani cum Dario Medo confun- dunt. Hic enim nec nepos fuit, nec ultimus in pri- ma Monarchia, exquisite loquendo. Conf. quæ ad v. 31.

Verf. eod.

FECIT GRANDE CONVIVIUM] Solebant id interdum facere reges orientis, ut apparet ex Herodoto l. 1. & Xenophante lib. 7.

Nonnulli festum solemne in honorem Beli institutum existimant: quod ex Herodoto lib. 1. & Xenophonte cap. 7. de pædia Cyri confirmant: quo etiam quidam referunt Ex. 21. 5. seqq. Iunius & Po- lanus in honorem idoli Schacæ convivium celebra- tum è Jer. 25, 26. contendunt: sed ibi voce ששך non idolum sed vel Regem Chald. ultimum vel ipsum Chald. imperium notari alii malunt: Diem potius natalem celebrasse Belfazarum verisimile est: quod nonnulli ex ipsis illis locis Herodoti & Xenophontis probare satagunt. Non ignotus fuit Cyro dies an- nuæ illius festivitatis ex superiorum temporum consuetudine, ideo huic potissimum noctu helua- tionibus & compotationibus dicatæ universæ for- tunæ aleam reservandam duxit: forte etiam ex Es. 21, 5. de successu tempore convivii edoctus, u- ti B. Svaningio visum fuit.

OPTIMATIBUS SUIS MILLE] Qui eadem qui- dem in aula, sed seorsum à rege discumbebant. Statius de Domitiani epulo: Hic cum Romuleos proceres, trabeataq; Cæsar Agmina mille simul jussit discumbere mensis.

Vide carmen totum, ut hujus rei imaginem capias.

ET UNUSQUISQUE SECUNDUM SUAM BI- BEBAT ÆTATEM: PRÆCEPIT ERGO JAM TE- MULENTUS] Longe hæc abeunt à Chaldaico. Theodo- tion verba sensumq; bene sequitur: καὶ κατέναντι τῶν χιλίων ὁ οἶνος, καὶ πίνων Βαλτάσαρ εἶπεν ἐν τῇ γεύσει τῶ οἶνω. Sensus est; cuique mille convivarum antepositum fuisse poculum & hominem qui petenti vinum infunderet: ita poscente more regionis. Deinde inter potandum regi magis ma- gisque allubuisse vinum.

## 5:2
Verse 2.

THAT THE GOLDEN AND SILVER VESSELS SHOULD BE BROUGHT] For profane uses, whereas before they had retained some sanctity in the temple of Bel, as Jerome notes. What was then a sin, to profane sacred things, is now the sport of both princes and profane men. And we still ask why devastation occurs everywhere with such atrocious wars.

Jerome has it thus: What great folly, drinking from golden vessels, to praise gods of wood and stone. As long as the vessels were in the idols' temples of Babylon, the Lord was not angry: for they seemed to have consecrated the thing of God, according to a perverse opinion indeed, yet to divine worship. But after they contaminate divine things with human uses, punishment immediately follows the sacrilege. They praise their gods, insulting the God of the Jews, because, with those gods granting them victory, they were drinking from His vessels.

WHICH NABUCHODONOSOR HIS FATHER HAD CARRIED AWAY] That is, his grandfather, as Jacchiades rightly notes here. The Chaldeans and Hebrews often speak in this way, just as they call grandsons and great-grandsons sons.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

UT ADFERRENTUR VASA AUREA ET AR- GENTEA] In usus profanos, cum antehac in Beli tem- plo aliquam adhuc sanctimoniam retinuisseut, ut notat Hieronymus. Quod tunc piaculum fuit, sacra profana- re, nunc & principum, & profanorum lusus est. Et adhuc quærimus, cur bellis tam atrocibus vastitas passim fiat.

Hieronymus ita habet: Quanta stultitia, in aureis vasis bibentes, Deos ligneos laudabant, & la- pideos. Quamdiu vasa fuerunt in Idolia Babylonis, non est iratus Dominus: videbantur enim rem Dei, secundum pravam quidem opinionem, tamen divino cultui consecrasse. Postquam autem humanis usibus divina contaminant, statim pœna sequitur post sacri- legium. Laudant autem Deos suos, insultantes Deo Iudæorum, quod illis victoriam tribuentibus, bi- bebant in vasis ejus.

QUÆ ASPORTAVERAT NABUCHODONO- SOR PATER EJUS] Id est, avus, ut hic recte notat Jac- chiades. Sæpe ita loquuntur Chaldæi & Hebræi, quomodo & nepotes & pronepotes filios vocant.

## 5:4
Verse 4.

AND THEY PRAISED THEIR GODS OF GOLD AND SILVER, OF BRASS, OF IRON, AND OF WOOD AND OF STONE] Those gods are so called because they did not exist in reality, but only their images. Nevertheless, the king and the nobles sang thanks and praises to these gods, as if triumphing over the true God.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET LAUDABANT DEOS SUOS AUREOS ET ARGENTEOS, ÆREOS, FERREOS, LIGNEOS- QUE ET LAPIDEOS] Ita vocantur dii illi, quia ipsi revera non existebant, sed tantum eorum imagines. Ta- men his diis gratias laudesque canebat rex & proceres, de Deo vero quasi triumphantes.

## 5:5
Verse 5.

IN THE SAME HOUR] That is, at that very time.

Verse same. THERE APPEARED FINGERS AS IT WERE OF A MAN'S HAND] The Angel Gabriel moving those fingers. So Rabbi Solomon. WRITING AGAINST THE CANDLESTICK] Over against the lampstand, that is, the hanging one, which was nearest to the king; so that the writing might be seen more directly. ON THE SURFACE OF THE WALL] In the Chaldean, in the lime: that is, on the plaster, ἐπὶ τὸ κονίαμα, as Theodotion. AND THE KING SAW THE JOINTS OF THE HAND THAT WROTE] In the Chaldean; the palm. See 1 Kings 18:44. Understand, however, the back part of the palm. Verse 6. THEN THE KING'S COUNTENANCE WAS CHANGED] His face, as above 4:33. AND THE JOINTS OF HIS LOINS WERE LOOSED] That is, his urine flowed out. AND HIS KNEES SMOTE ONE AGAINST ANOTHER] From trembling. THAT THEY MIGHT BRING IN THE MAGICIANS] The wise men. Verse 7. AND THE ASTROLOGERS] Rather, the writers of decrees. See above 2:27. WHOSOEVER SHALL READ THIS WRITING] The Hebrews believe, although the words are Chaldean, that the writing was ancient Hebrew, that is, Canaanite, Phoenician, Samaritan. HE SHALL BE CLOTHED WITH PURPLE] Which only kings used, and a few to whom the king had granted it as a singular honor. AND SHALL HAVE A GOLDEN CHAIN ABOUT HIS NECK] This also is a great honor. See Gen. 41:42. He who dreams that he wears a chain will attain the greatest dignity, says Achmetes. AND SHALL BE THE THIRD IN MY KINGDOM] He shall obtain the third dignity: as below v. 16, 29. The first place is the king's, the second the king's son's, the third the first of the Satraps. Verse 10. NOW THE QUEEN] The king's grandmother, as Josephus rightly says. Nitocris, that is, a prudent woman. See our notes to the third of the Annotations on the truth of the Christian Religion. CAME INTO THE BANQUET HOUSE] For she had not been present at the banquet because of her widowhood. WHO HAS THE SPIRIT OF THE HOLY GODS IN HIM] She uses the very words which she had once learned from her husband Nebuchadnezzar. Chap. 4:5. Verse 11. IN THE DAYS OF THY FATHER] Grandfather, as above. AND IN THE DAYS OF THY FATHER KNOWLEDGE AND WISDOM WERE FOUND IN HIM] In the Chaldean: Light and intelligence and wisdom equal to the wisdom of the gods were found in him. Light, a lucid spirit, ἀγχίνοια; Intelligence, of natural things; wisdom, for conducting affairs. Verse 14. MORE ABUNDANT] Than in any of the wise men of the East. Ezek. 28:3. Verse 16. AND DISSOLVE DOUBTS] Knots, in the Chaldean. Thus Oedipus in Seneca: I have solved the knotted words of the fierce beast, and the tangled deceits, and the sad song. Verse 17. LET THY GIFTS BE TO THYSELF, AND GIVE THY REWARDS TO ANOTHER] What he here translates as gifts are properly honoraria, annual allowances, as stated above 2:6. It is also the mark of a wise man to know when things that are given should be accepted, and when not. See Gen. 14:23; 2 Kings 5:16, 26. There was no reason why Daniel should receive a reward for so sad a message. Verse 18. KINGDOM] An empire extending most widely. MAJESTY] Majesty among his subjects. GLORY] From victories. HONOR] From the city enlarged, walls built, temple, palace. Verse 19. ALL PEOPLE, TRIBES, AND LANGUAGES TREMBLED AND FEARED HIM] Even those who were not under his empire feared him. WHOM HE WOULD HE SLEW] חיה is indeed to slay for the Hebrews, but they seem to think more correctly who suppose here to be a mark of the participle, and that something is missing after מ, as often. For there is an opposition: Whom he would he killed, and whom he would he kept alive: that is, he preserved them alive, even those who deserved death. There was no one who dared to resist his will. Verse 20. BUT WHEN HIS HEART WAS LIFTED UP] Above 2:27. Verse 22. THOU HAST NOT HUMBLED THINE HEART] Before the true God.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

IN EADEM HORA] Id est, in eo ipso tempore.

Vers. eod. APPARUERUNT DIGITI QUASI MANUS HOMINIS] Movente eos digitos Angelo Gabriele. Ita Rabbinus Solomo. SCRIBENTES CONTRA CANDELABRUM] E regione lychnuchi, pensilis scilicet, qui proxime regem erat; quo rectius scriptio conspiceretur. IN SUPERFICIE PARIETIS] In Chaldæo, in calce: id est, in tectorio, ἐπὶ τὸ κονίαμα, ut Theodotion. ET REX ASPICIEBAT ARTICULOS MANUS SCRIBENTIS] In Chaldæo; palmam. Vid. 1. Reg. 18, 44. intellige autem partem palmæ aversam. Vers. 6. TUNC FACIES REGIS COMMUTATA EST] Vultus, ut supra 4, 33. ET COMPAGES RENUM EJUS SOLVEBAN- TUR] Id est, urina defluebat. ET GENUA EJUS AD SE INVICEM COLLI- DEBANTUR] Præ tremore. UT INTRODUCERENT MAGOS] Sophos. Vers. 7. ET ARUSPICES] Potius, decretorum scriptores. Vide supra 2, 27. QUICUMQUE LEGERIT SCRIPTURAM HANC] Credunt Hebræi, quamvis verba sint Chaldai- ca, scripturam fuisse Hebræam veterem, id est, Cananæam, Phoeniciam, Samaritanam. PURPURA VESTIETUR] Qua utebantur soli re- ges, & pauci, quibus id rex pro singulari honore concesse- rat. ET TORQUEM AUREAM HABEDIT IN COLLO] Magnus & hic honor. Vid. Gen. 41, 42. qui somniavit torquem se gerere, maximam dignitatem conse- quetur, ait Achmetes. ET TERTIUS IN REGNO MEO ERIT] Ter- tiam dignitatem obtinebit: ut infra v. 16.29. Primus locus regis, alter filii regis, tertius primi Satraparum. Vers. 10. REGINA AUTEM] Avia regis, ut recte Josephus. Nitocris scilicet, prudens femina. Vide nostra ad tertium Annotatorum de veritate Religionis Christianæ. DOMUM CONVIVII INGRESSA EST] Neque enim convivio interfuerat ob viduitatem. QUI SPIRITUM DEORUM SANCTORUM HABET IN SE] Usurpat ipsa verba, quæ ex marito quon- dam suo Nabuchodonosoro intellexerat. Cap. 4, 5. Vers. 11. IN DIEBUS PATRIS TUI] Avi, ut supra. ET IN DIEBUS PATRIS TUI SCIENTIA ET SAPIENTIA INVENTÆ SUNT IN EO] In Chaldæo: Lux & intelligentia & sapientia par deorum sapientiæ inventa est in eo. Lux, Spiritus lucidus, ἀγχίνοια; Intelligentia, rerum naturalium; sapientia, ad res agendas. Vers. 14. AMPLIORES] Quam in ullo sapientum Orientis. Ezech. 28, 3. Vers. 16. ET LIGATA DISSOLVERE] Nodos, in Chaldæo. Sic Oedipus apud Senecam: Nodosa fortis verba, & implexos dolos Ac triste carmen alitis solvi feræ. Vers. 17. MUNERA TUA SINT TIBI, ET DONA DO- MUS TUÆ ALTERI DA] Quæ hic dona vertit, pro- prie sunt honoraria, erogationes annuæ, ut dictum supra 2,6. Sapientis & hoc est, nosse quando acceptanda sint quæ dantur, quando non. Vide Gen. 14, 23. 2. Reg. 5,16.26. Non erat cur Daniel tam tristis nuntii præmium acciperet. Vers. 18. REGNUM] Imperium latissime patens. MAGNIFICENTIAM] Majestatem apud subditos. GLORIAM] Ex victoriis. HONOREM] Ex urbe aucta, structis mœnibus, templo, palatio. Vers. 19. UNIVERSI POPULI, TRIBUS, ET LIN- GUÆ TREMEBANT, ET METUEBANT EUM] Et- iam qui sub imperio ejus non erant, eum metuebant. QUOS VOLEBAT PERCUTIEBAT] חיה qui- dem Hebræis est percutere, sed rectius sentire videntur, qui hic putant esse participii notam, & deesse, post מ, ut sæ- pe. Est enim oppositio: Quos volebat interficiebat, & quos solebat vivificabat: id est, vivos conservabat, etiam mortem meritos. Nemo erat, qui voluntati ejus auderet obsistere. Vers. 20. QUANDO AUTEM ELEVATUM EST COR EJUS] Supra 2, 27. Vers. 22. NON HUMILIASTI COR TUUM] Sub Deo vero.

## 5:13
Ver. 13.

DANIEL OF THE CHILDREN OF THE CAPTIVITY OF JUDAH] As if he were saying: both a foreigner and captured in war, such as modesty most becomes,

Latin:

Vers. 13.

DANIEL DE FILIIS CAPTIVITATIS JUDÆ] Quasi diceret : & externus & bello captus, quales maxi- me decet modestia,

## 5:23
Verse 23. THE VESSELS OF HIS HOUSE] Carried away from the Jerusalem temple. THOU HAST DRUNK WINE IN THEM] As if in profane ones. Justinian took better care of himself, who, when he had obtained the vessels of the second Temple carried to Rome by Vespasian, and to Carthage by Genseric the plunderer of Rome, through Victory, did not turn them to his own uses, but sent them to the sacred basilica which was at Jerusalem, as Procopius narrates. AND THOU HAST PRAISED THE GODS OF SILVER, AND GOLD, AND BRASS, IRON, WOOD, AND STONE, WHICH SEE NOT, NOR HEAR, NOR KNOW] Those things which are nothing, except insofar as it pleases men. BUT THE GOD, IN WHOSE HAND THY BREATH IS, AND ALL THY WAYS] That God, who can not only prosper or overturn all thy acts, but even take away the vital spirit itself from thee, when He wills. HAST THOU NOT GLORIFIED] Αἰτότης. For Belshazzar had also despised Him. Verse 24. THEN WAS THE PART OF THE HAND SENT FROM HIM] The palm of the hand, as above v. 5. Verse 25. AND THIS IS THE WRITING THAT WAS WRITTEN] Inscribed. The same word below 6:10, 12. The Arabs also use it. MENE, TEKEL, PERES] It is in the Chaldean: Mene, mene, Tekel, Upharsin. Soon, however, for Upharsin there is Peres, that is, the singular for the plural, with the same meaning. In the Greek, in both places, φαρές. Verse 26. GOD HATH NUMBERED THY KINGDOM, AND FINISHED IT] That is, He has numbered it most perfectly, which the twice-repeated Mene signifies. He has defined the days of thy kingdom. Verse 27. THOU ART WEIGHED IN THE BALANCES, AND ART FOUND WANTING] The reason why thy kingdom will be so short is that thou hast been found wicked in the scales of divine equity, like adulterated coins. Verse 28. THY KINGDOM IS DIVIDED] That is, torn away from thy house. Broken, as Saadia and Jacchiades translate, that is, severed. Moreover, there is a double meaning in that Pharsin. For it signifies both severed, and the Persians themselves, who severed it. For the Persians are Phars or Pharas to the Chaldeans. The Pharusi of old, according to Pliny. There is no need for that double meaning. For concerning the Persians it follows immediately, which Daniel could have from revelation, not gather from the homonymy of the word. Verse same. AND GIVEN TO THE MEDES AND PERSIANS] It shall be given, under Cyrus. See Jer. 20:2, where the Persians are called עילם from Elymais, which is annexed to Persis, where it extends toward Media, according to the same Pliny 5:26. This was fulfilled seventeen years later. But these two peoples so coalesced into one nation that you may find the Medes called Persians everywhere among the Greeks, and those who favored the Persians called μηδίζοντας. Verse 29. THEN COMMANDED BELSHAZZAR, AND THEY CLOTHED DANIEL WITH PURPLE, AND PUT A CHAIN OF GOLD ABOUT HIS NECK, AND MADE A PROCLAMATION CONCERNING HIM, THAT HE SHOULD BE THE THIRD RULER IN HIS KINGDOM] He recovered the dignity which he had once held under Nebuchadnezzar. Thus King BALTHASAR felt thanks to a man, and not to GOD, as Jerome notes here. Verse 30. THAT SAME NIGHT WAS SLAIN] ὑπὸ ἅ φίλων ἀπετυμπανίσθη, says Berosus. Abydenus: τότε δὲ ἀποθανόντῶ βιαίῳ μόρῳ. Verse 31. AND DARIUS THE MEDE TOOK THE KINGDOM] He took up the kingdom. παρέλαβε τὴν βασιλείαν, that is, he obtained the kingdom, which is also below 9, 1. המלך, that is, he was constituted king, by the election of the people, and took for himself the name of Darius, whereas he was previously called Nabonnedus. For thus Berosus calls him; in Ptolemy he is written Nabonadius, in Abydenus Nabannidachus, in Herodotus Labynitus, with the n changed into l, which is also found in other names. This Nabonnedus indeed lived in Babylon, but he was a Mede by origin, below 9, 1. For he is the Mede who is said to have betrayed the citizens, that is, the Babylonians, in the oracles; not falsely. For at the arrival of Cyrus he fled to Borsippa, and there made a pact with Cyrus, that he might have the prefecture of Carmania. Darius, therefore, was the name of a famous and fortunate king of the Medes, whose name Nabonnedus, himself also sprung from the Medes, imposed upon himself for the sake of a good omen. Great faith ought to be held in Josephus regarding the affairs of Herod the Great, and thereafter. Likewise where he follows external authors, not where he follows the Jews, who dream up many things in their histories contrary to the truth.

Jerome provides the reason why Darius alone is said to have succeeded, and not Cyrus, since Babylon was conquered by both, and he also brings together here other prophecies concerning this conquest: That, however, when Cyrus, King of the Persians, and Darius, King of the Medes, were victorious, only Darius is written to have succeeded to the kingdom, is a matter of age, kinship, and the kingdom. For Darius was sixty-two years old, and we read that the kingdom of the Medes was greater than that of the Persians, and the uncle, who was prior by right of nature, ought to have been named successor to the kingdom. Whence also in the vision which is read in Isaiah against Babylon, after many things which it is long to set down, these future events are narrated: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not seek silver, nor desire gold, but shall kill the little ones with arrows, and shall not have pity on the wombs of the nursing. And Jeremiah says, Sanctify against her the nations of the King of Media, his leaders, and all his magistrates, and the whole land of his power: and in the following: Daughter of Babylon, as a threshing floor, the time of her threshing, yet a little while, and the time of her harvest will come. But that Babylon was captured at a banquet: My beloved is made a miracle to me: set the table, behold in the watchtower those eating and drinking, arise princes, take up the shield. Jerome therefore judges the history of the slain Balthasar to be the same as that by which Cyrus conquered Babylon, citing Josephus, who writes in the tenth book of Jewish Antiquities: Babylon being besieged by the Medes and Persians, namely Darius and Cyrus, Balthasar, King of Babylon, fell into such forgetfulness of himself that he entered upon a most celebrated banquet, and drank from the vessels of the temple, and while besieged, occupied himself with feasts. However, not only Jerome, but almost all chronologists today follow Josephus here. Yet not only Grotius, but other principal chronologists of this sort depart from this opinion. Especially indeed Scaliger, Calvisius, Dr. Behmius, and those who follow in their footsteps. Then because Darius the Mede did not occupy the kingdom after Balthasar was killed with an armed hand, but as is held in this passage קבל παρέλαβε, he received the kingdom, by which word is noted the acceptance of that which is handed from hand to hand, 1 Chron. 29, 26; Esth. 4, 4. Nowhere, however, does it mean to take by an armed hand: Then, because Dan. 9, 1. is said to have been made King by the word הָמְלַךְ, which designates him who is chosen as King by right of succession or by right of suffrage: Then because it is evident from Berosus and Megasthenes that, after Laborosoardochus was oppressed by treachery, the kingdom was handed over by common suffrage to Nabonnidus, or Labynetus the Babylonian-Mede; and that he was oppressed and slaughtered many years before Cyrus undertook that Babylonian expedition; then because Jeremiah c. 51, v. 31, testifies that the Babylonian King was not in Babylon at that time when Cyrus conquered Babylon, to which Berosus also agrees. Grotius, in book III of De veritate religionis Christianae, page 132, produced the words of Berosus, who was a writer of Chaldean affairs, a priest of Bel, and, according to Tatian, described Chaldean history in three books, from Eusebius, book IX, Praeparatio Evangelica, c. 4, Josephus, book X, Contra Apionem, c. 11, and the first book: His son Evilmerodachus received the kingdom. When he administered affairs unjustly and through evil lust, he was sought out by the treachery of Neriglissoorus, who had his sister in marriage, and perished after he had reigned for ten years. He being removed, his slayer Neriglissoorus, having become master of the kingdom, held power for four years. His son Laborosoarchodus, still a boy, held the kingdom for nine months: but because many signs of a depraved nature appeared in him, he was slaughtered by the treachery of his friends. When he was dead, the participants in that crime having gathered among themselves, by common consent they conferred the kingdom upon Nabonnidus, one of the Babylonians, who himself had also been in the same conspiracy. While he was reigning, those walls which were by the river on the side of Babylon were made better with brick and bitumen. But when the seventeenth year of his reign was passing, Cyrus came from Persia with a large army, and having subdued the rest of Asia, proceeded to Babylon. His arrival being known, Nabonnidus himself also met him with a great army, and having been defeated in the battle that took place, he fled with a few, and shut himself up in the city of the Borsippeni. Cyrus, however, having captured Babylon, decided to tear down its outer fortifications, because he saw the city was prone to new things, but the city itself was difficult to capture: thence he set out to Borsippa to besiege Nabonnidus. But he, not enduring the siege, surrendered himself. Cyrus, having received him kindly, ordered him to leave Babylonia to inhabit Carmania. And there Nabonnidus, the rest of his life having passed, met his day. Where also these things from Abydenus, the writer of the Assyrians, and Megasthenes, preserved for us by Eusebius in the cited place, are brought forward: After him his son Evilmaturuchus reigned. His slayer, who had been a relative to him, Neriglissares, left a son Labossorascus. This one having been extinguished by a violent death, the Babylonians make Nabonnidus king, who was joined by no blood to the dead King. Cyrus, when he had captured him in Babylon, placed him in charge of Carmania. This opinion may be seen more fully confirmed in Dr. D. Behm, Chronol. Manud. Decad. 1, observat. VIII, and Sethus Calvisius, Isag. Chron. c. 29. Furthermore, that this Darius was indeed a Mede by origin, but not King of the Medes, appears from Dan. 9, 1, because he was King of Babylon, elected to that kingdom by common suffrage, and after Astyages no one ruled over the Medes and Persians except Cyrus. Astyages, however, was never made King of Babylon. These things are according to the opinion of Scaliger. But when we weigh his arguments, they seem by no means of such weight that we should depart from Josephus, Jerome, and the common reckoning of chronologers for the sake of an illustrious man who is fond of innovation: Darius the Mede therefore received the kingdom of the Chaldeans handed over to him by Cyrus the Victor: nor is there need of votes or succession for one to be called a king: nor do we deny that the kingdom was handed over to Nabonidus, that is, Belshazzar, by common vote. But the fact that in Jer. 51:31 runners are ordered to announce to the King of Babylon that the city has been captured does not prove that he was absent from Babylon. For such was the magnitude of the city that when those who inhabited the outer parts of the city had already been captured, those who inhabited the middle of the city did not notice it; see Herodotus, book 1, chapter 191. What foreign writers report about Nabonidus dying in Carmania deservedly yields to the sacred writings, which report that Belshazzar, who is Nabonidus, was killed when Babylon was captured, Dan. 5:30; just as it is clear that those writers also erred in that they report Nabonidus was joined by no blood relationship with his predecessor: for that is contradicted by the divine oracle, Jer. 27:7. For after Evil-Merodach had been killed by his sister's husband Neriglissar, and the latter had reigned for 4 years, and his son Laborosoardochus had succeeded for nine months, the successor to him, who was killed, became the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar through his daughter, called Nabonidus by Berosus, Labynitus by Herodotus, Nabannidochus by Abydenus, and Belshazzar by Daniel, being the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar through his son Evil-Merodach. Darius, however, was entirely a King of the Medes, the son of Astyages, called Ahasuerus in Tob. 14:15, named Cyaxares, the brother of Cyrus's mother, as Xenophon has it in book 1 of the Cyropaedia, and therefore Darius is called in this passage the Mede, the son of Ahasuerus: who received the empire of the Chaldeans from Cyrus, and presided over it for two years, whose only daughter and heir Cyrus took in marriage, with the whole of Media as a dowry having been accepted as an inheritance. Therefore not undeservedly does our Lord Dr. Gejerus depart here from Calixtus in Appar. page 33, and Quistorp in Annot. Bibl., who, following Scaliger, say that Belshazzar was killed by friends invited to a banquet and that the kingdom was handed over by them to Darius the Mede, or Nabonidus, opposing to them the fact that in v. 28 it is held concerning the division of the kingdom between the Medes and Persians, along with other things which were observed by Graser in ultim. verb. p. 20: and responding to the scruple concerning the last Babylonian King being kept alive by Cyrus and left in Carmania, along with Pererius, that the authors who bring that forward confuse Astyages with Belshazzar, so that consequently greater faith should be held in Xenophon, and Daniel the eyewitness, than in other foreign authors.

Latin:

Vers. 23. VASA DOMUS EJUS] E templo Hiero- solymitano deportata. VINUM BIBISTI IN EIS] Tanquam in profa- nis. Melius cavit sibi Justinianus, qui vasa Templi secun- di a Vespasiano Romam portata, a Genserico Romæ ex- pilatoreCarthaginem, cum per Victoriam nactus esset, non in suos vertit usus, sed in sacram basilicam misit, quæ erat Hierosolymis, narrante Procopio. DEOS QUOQUE ARGENTEOS, ET AU- REOS, ET ÆREOS, FERREOS, LIGNEOS, ET LAPIDEOS, QUI NON VIDENT, NEQUE AU- DIUNT, NEQUE SENTIUNT LAVDASTI] Ea, quæ nihil sunt, nisi quantum hominibus lubet. PORRO DEUM, QVI HABET FLATVM TVVM IN MANV SVA, ET OMNES VIAS TVAS] Deum illum, qui non modo omnes actus tuos prosperare potest, aut evertere, verum etiam spiritum ipsum vitalem tibi auferre, ubi voluerit. NON GLORIFICASTI] Αἰτότης. Nam & con- tempserat eum Baltasar. Vers. 24. IDCIRCO AB EO MISSVS EST ARTI- CVLVS MANVS] Palma manus, ut supra v. 5. Vers. 25. HÆC AVTEM EST SCRIPTVRA, QVÆ DI- GESTA EST] Exarata est. Idem verbum infra 6, 10. 12. Usurpant eam & Arabes. MANE, TECEL, PHARES] Est in Chaldæo: Me- ne, mene, Thekel, Upharsin. Mox tamen pro Upharsin est Phares, id est, singulare pro plurali, sensu eodem. In Græ- co utrobique φαρές. Vers. 26. NVMERAVIT DEVS REGNVM TVVM, ET COMPLEVIT ILLVD] Id est, perfectissime nume- ravit, quod bis repetitum Mene significat. Dies regni tui definivit. Vers. 27. APPENSVS ES IN STATERA, ET IN- VENTVS ES MINVS HABENS] Causa cur tam breve futurum sit tibi regnum, est quod in lance divinæ æquita- tis repertus sis improbus, ut nummi adulterati. Vers. 28. DIVISVM EST REGNVM TVVM] Id est, a- vulsum a domo tua. Fractum, ut Saadia & Jacchiades ver- tunt, id est, abruptum. Est autem in illo Pharsin duplex significatio. Nam & abruptum significat, & ipsos Persas, qui abruperunt. Persæ enim Chaldæis Phars, vel Pharas. Pharusi olim, teste Plinio. Non opus est duplici illa significatione.DePer- sis enim mox sequitur, quod ex revelatione habe- re poterat èDaniel, non colligere vocis ὁμωνυμίᾳ. Vers. eod. ET DATVM EST MEDIS ET PERSIS] Dabi- tur, sub Cyro. Vide Jer. 20, 2. ubi Persæ dicuntur עילם ab Elymaide, quæ Persidi annexa, qua Mediam versus por- rigitur, teste eodem Plinio 5,26. Impletum hoc annis post septendecim. Adeo autem coaluerunt duo isti populi in gentem unam, ut passim apud Græcos reperias Medos pro Persis dici, & μηδίζοντας eos qui Persis studebant. Vers. 29. TVM JVBENTE REGE INDVTVS EST DA- NIEL PVRPVRA, ET CIRCVMDATA EST TOR- QVES AVREA COLLO EJVS, ET PRÆDICATVM EST DE EO, QVOD HABERET POTESTATEM TERTIVS IN REGNO SVO] Recuperavit dignitatem, quam olim sub Nabuchodonosoro habuerat. Ita Rex BALTASAR homini gratiam habuit, non & DEO, ut hic notat Hieronymus. Vers. 30. EADEM NOCTE INTERFECTVS EST] ὑπὸ ἅ φίλων ἀπετυμπανίσθη, ait Berosus. Abydenus: τότε δὲ ἀποθανόντῶ βιαίῳ μόρῳ. Vers. 31. ET DARIVS MEDVS SVCCESSIT IN REGNUM] Suscepit regnum. παρέλαβε τὴν βασιλείαν, id est, regnum adeptus est, quod & infra 9, 1. המלך, id est, rex fuit constitutus, electione populi, nomenque sibi sumsit Da- rii, cum Nabonnedus ante vocaretur. Ita enim eum ap- pellat Berosus, Ptolemæo scribitur Nabonadius, Abyde- no Nabannidachus, Herodoto Labynitus, n. mutato in l, quod & in aliis nominibus reperitur. Habitabat quidem is Nabonnedus Babylone, sed Medus fuit origine, infra 9,1. Namq; is est Medus, qui prodidisse cives, id est, Ba- bylonios dicitur in oraculis; non falso. Nam ad Cyriad- ventum fugit Borsippa, ibique cum Cyro pepigit, ut præ- fecturam haberet Carmaniam. Darius ergo nomen fuit regis Medorum clari ac felicis, cujus nomen sibi boni o- minis causa imposuit, ortus & ipse ex Medis Nabonnedus. Josepho magna fides haberi debet in rebus Herodis ma- gni, ac deinceps. Item ubi externos auctores, non ubi Ju- dæos, multa in historiis contra verum somniantes, se- quitur.

Cur Darius folum successisse dicatur, non Cyrus, quum ab utroque expugnata fuerit Babel, rationem reddit Hieronymus, qui hic etiam con- fert alias Prophetias de hac expugnatione: Quod autem vincente Cyro, Rege Persarum, & Dario Rege Medorum folus Darius successisse in regno scribitur, ordo ætatis ac propinquitatis & regni est. Darius e- nim sexaginta duorum annorum erat, & majus re- gnum Medorum, quam Persarum legimus, & avuncu- lus, qui prior erat jure naturæ successor regni debuit nominari. Unde & in visione, quæ contra Babylo- nem in Esaia legitur, post multa, quæ longum est po- nere, hæc futura narrantur: Ecce ego suscitabo su- per eos Medos, qui argentum non quærant, nec aurum velint, sed sagittis parvulos interficiant, & lactantibus uteris non misereantur. Et Hieremias sanctificate, inquit, contra eam gentes Regis Me- diæ, Duces ejus, & universos Magistratus ejus, cun- ctamque terram potestatis illius: & in consequen- tibus: Filia Babylon, quasi area, tempus trituræ e- jus, adhuc modicum, & veniet tempus messionis e- jus. Quod autem in convivio capta sit Babylon: Dilecta mea facta est mihi in miraculum: pone mensam, contemplare in specula comedentes & bibentes, surgite principes, arripite clypeum.Cen- set ergoHieronymus historiam interfectiBalthasa- ris eandem esse cum illa, qua CyrusBabylonem ex- pugnavit,adducens Josephum, qui in decimo anti- quitatis Judaicæ libro scribit: Obsessa Babylone a Medis & Persis, Dario videlicet & Cyro,in tantam venisse Balthasar Regem Babylonis oblivionem sui, ut celeberrimum iniret convivium, & ex vasis templi bibe- ret, & obsessus vacaret epulis. Josephum autem hic non tantumHieronymus, sed omnes fere hodie Chronologi sequuntur. Ab hac tamen senten- tia, non Grotius tantum, sed alii etiam præcipui commatis Chronologi discedunt. Imprimis vero Scaliger, Calvisius, D. Behmius, & qui eorum insi- stunt vestigiis. Tum quia Darius Medus non oc- cupavit post interfectum Balthasarem regnum ar- mata manu,sed ut loco hoc habetur קבל παρέλα- βε accepit regnum, quo verbo notatur acceptio ejus, quod de manu in manum traditur 1. Chron. 29, 26. Esth. 4. 4. Nuspiam vero id est, armata manu acci- pere: Tum,quia Dan. 9,1. dicitur Rex factus verbo הָמְלַךְ,quod eum,qui jure successionis,vel qui suf- fragiorum jure in Regem eligitur,designat: Tum quia ex Beroso, & Megasthene constat, Laborosoar- docho per insidias oppresso, communi suffragio, tradi- tum esse regnum Nabonnido, vel Labyneto Babylonio- Medo; illumque ante multos annos,priusquam Cy- rus expeditionem istam Babylonicam susciperet, oppressum & trucidatum esse; tum quia Jeremias c. 51. v. 31. testatur,BabylonicumRegem eo tempo- re, cum Cyrus Babylonem expugnaret, Babylone non fuisse,cui etiam Berosus consentit. Berosi ver- ba, qui rerum Chaldaicarum scriptor, Beli sacer- dos fuit, & teste Tatiano, tribus libris Historiam Chaldaicam descripsit, ex Eusebio lib.IX. præpar. Evang. c. 4. Josepho lib. X. orig. c. 11. & libro prio- re in Appion. produxit Grotius lib. III. de verit. Relig. Christ. pag. 132. Regnum accepit filius ejus Evilmcrodachus. Hic cum inique ac per malam libidi- nem res administraret, petitus insidiis Neriglosso- ori, qui sororem ejus in matrimonio habebat, interiit, postquam per annos regnaverat decem. Eo sublato regni compos factus interfector ejus Neriglossoorus imperium tenuit per annos quatuor. Hujus filius La- borosoarchodus puer adhuc regnum tenuit menses no- vem: sed quia pravæ in illo indolis multa signa appa- rerent, insidiis amicorum trucidatus est. Hoc mor- tuo, cum inter se coissent ejus facinoris participes, communi consensu regnum detulere ad Nabonnidum, ex Babyloniis unum, qui & ipse in eadem conjuratio- ne fuerat. Hoc regnante meliora facta sunt ea, quæ ad amnem erant ex latere & bitumine Babylonis mœ- nia. Cüm vero regni ejus annus ageretur deci- mus & septimus, venit ex Perside multo cum ex- ercitu Cyrus, reliquaque Asia subacta ad Babylonem perrexit. Adventu ejus cognito, Nabonnid us occurrit magno & ipse exercitu, prælioque facto victus, cum paucis fugit, conclusitque se in urbem Borsippenorum. Cyrus autem Babylone capta constituit exteriora e- jus munimenta diruere, quod civitatem videret ad res novas mobilem, urbem vero capi difficilem: inde in Borsippum proficiscitur ad obsidendum Nabonni- dum. Verum is obsidionis non tolerans se dedidit. Cy- rus benigne exceptum à Babylonia exire eum ad Car- maniam habitandam jussit. Atque ibi Nabonnidus transacto vitæ cætero diem suum obiit. Ubi etiam hæc ex Abydeno Assyriorum scriptore, & Megasthene, ab Eusebio loco citato nobis servata adducta sunt: Post hunc filius regnavit Evilmaturuchus. Hujus interfector, qui affinis ipsi fuerat Neriglissares filium reliquit Labossorascum. Hoc violenta morte exstin- cto, Babylonii Nabonnidum regum faciunt, cum Rege mortuo nullo junctum sanguine. Cyrus hunc, cum Babylone cepisset, Carmaniæ præfecit. Videa- tur hæc sententia uberius confirmata apud Dn. D. Behm. Chronol. Manud. Decad. 1. observat. VIII. & Sethus Calvisius Isag. Chron. c. 29. Cæterum Darium hunc Medum quidem fuisse origine, non autem Medorum Regem è Dan. 9, 1. apparet, quia fuit Rex Babyloniæ, communibus suffragiis in re- gnum illud electus, neque post Astyagem Medis & Persis ullus præfuit præter Cyrum. Astyages au- tem nunquam factus est Babyloniæ Rex. Hæc juxta Scaligeri sententiam. Sed cum argumenta ejus expendimus, tanti minime videntur, ut à Jo- sepho, Hieronymo, & communi calculo Chronologo- rum in gratiam novaturientis viri illustris disce- dendum sit: Accepit itaque Darius Medus regnum Chaldæorum sibi traditum à Cyro Victore: nec opus suffragiis, aut successione, ut quis regnare di- catur: neque negamus Nabonido, id est, Balthasari regnum communi suffragio traditum esse. Quod ve- ro Ier. 51, 3. cursores jubentur Regi Babyloniæ ca- ptam esse civitatem annunciare, non arguit eum Babylone abfuisse. Tanta enim erat urbis magnitu- do, ut cum capti jam essent, qui extremas urbis partes incolebant, ii, qui mediam habitabant ur- bem, id non animadverterent, vide Herodot. l. 1. c. 191. Quæ de Nabonido in Carmannia mortuo re- ferunt exotici, merito cedunt sacris, Balthasarem, qui Nabonidus est, capta Babylone interfectum tra- dentibus Dan. 5, 30. quemadmodum planum est istos in eo etiam errasse, quod Nabonidum nullo jun- ctum sanguine cum prædecessore suo tradunt: Id enim refragatur divino oraculo Ier. 27, 7. Nam vi- ejus, postquam Evilmerodachus à marito sororis suæ Neriglossoro interfecto hic 4. annis regnasset, ejus fi- lius Laborosoardochus successisset ad novem men- ses, huic Nebucadnezaris ex filia Nepoti peremto successor factus est Nebucadnezaris ex filio Evil- merodacho nepos, Beroso Nabonidus, Herodoto Labynitus, Abydeno Nabannidochus, Danieli Bal- thasar dictus. Darius autem omnino fuit Medorum Rex, Astyagis, Tob. 14, 17. Asveri dicti filius Cya- xares nuncupatus, matris Cyri frater, ut Xenophon habet c. 1. Instit. Cyri, atque ideo dicitur hoc loco Darius, Medus, Asveri filius: qui à Cyro Chaldæo- rum imperium accepit, eique per biennium præ- fuit, cujus filiam unicam & hæredem Cyrus in ma- trimonium duxit, dotis nomine universæ Mediæ hæreditate accepta. Ideo non immerito hic à Ca- lixto in Appar. pag. 33. & Quistorp. in Annot. Bibl. qui ex Scaligero ajunt Balthasarem ab amicis ad convivium vocatis interemtum ab iisque regnum Dario Medo, seu Nabonido traditum, discessit Dn. D. Gejerus noster opponens illis, quod v. 28. habe- tur de regni divisione inter Medos & Persas, cum aliis, quæ à Grasero in ultim. verb. p. 20. observa- ta: & ad scrupulum de ultimo Babylon. Rege per Cyrum in vivis conservato inque Carmania reli- cto, cum Pererio respondens, quod autores id af- ferentes confundant Astyagem cum Balthasare, ut proinde major habenda fides sit Xenophonti, & Danieli autoptæ, quam aliis extraneis.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

Daniel is appointed over the satraps of the kingdom by Darius, and having been accused because he had not observed the King's edict, because he did not cease prayers to the God of heaven, he was sent into the den of lions, but was brought out unharmed, his accusers having been thrown in and suddenly torn to pieces: whence the King commanded that his God be feared in all his provinces, and there was great authority for Daniel in the reign of Darius and Cyrus.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Daniel supra satrapas regni à Dario constitui- tur, & accusatus quod Regis edictum non servasset, quia preces ad Deum cœli non in- termittebat, missus est in lacum leonum, sed illæsus eductus, immissis ac subito dilania- tis ejus accusatoribus: unde Rex in omni- bus suis provinciis Deum ejus timendum præcepit, fuitque magna Danielis in Da- rii & Cyri regno autoritas.

## 6:1
IT PLEASED DARIUS, AND HE APPOINTED] That is, to appoint.

OVER THE KINGDOM ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY SATRAPS] Kings, as also the Roman emperors, are often accustomed to change the number of provinces at their own discretion.

Latin:

PLACUIT DARIO, ET CONSTITUIT] Id est, constitwere.

SUPER REGNUM SATRAPAS CENTUM VI- GINTI] Solent sæpe Reges, ut & Romani imperatores, pro suo arbitratu mutare numerum provinciarum.

## 6:2
Ver. 2.

AND OVER THEM THREE PRINCES] Such as were the praetorian prefects in the later Roman empire. In Chaldean these are called, both here and below, סרכין, that is, ἔξαρχοι. The same word is used of Joseph in Gen. 45, 41, in Jonathan's version.

OF WHOM DANIEL WAS] In the place of a prince, as the following shows.

AND THE KING MIGHT NOT SUFFER LOSS] From the Greek: ὅπως ὁ βασιλεὺς μὴ ἐνοχλῆται. But the Chaldean word signifies more; Lest the King might suffer damage: that is, lest the empire might receive any detriment through the deceit or fault of the governors.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET SUPER EOS PRINCIPES TRES] Quales fue- re in posteriore imperio Romano præfecti prætorio. In Chaldæo hi dicuntur, & hic & infra סרכין, id est, ἔξαρχοι. Est eadem vox de Josepho Gen. 45, 41. in Jonathanis ver- sione.

EX QUIBUS DANIEL ERAT] Loco principe, ut ostendunt sequentia.

ET REX NON SUSTINERET MOLESTIAM] Ex Græco: ὅπως ὁ βασιλεὺς μὴ ἐνοχλῆται. At Chaldæa vox magis significat; Ne Rex damnum pateretur: id est, ne quid detrimenti acciperet imperium per præsidum dolum aut culpam.

## 6:3
Ver. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

## 6:4
Ver. 4.

FURTHERMORE THE KING WAS THINKING OF APPOINTING HIM OVER THE WHOLE KINGDOM] So that those other praetorian prefects might also be subject to him, and he might be everything to the King, such as our own and previous centuries have seen many to be among Kings who were either little confident in their own ability, or fleeing from business.

WHENCE THE PRINCES AND SATRAPS SOUGHT AN OCCASION] For envy reigns in royal courts,

FROM THE SIDE OF THE KING] That is, they sought a charge of high treason, which Pliny in his Panegyric says is often the singular and unique charge of those who are free from crime. This is what the Romano-Greeks call ἔγκλημα βασιλείας.

AND COULD FIND NO CAUSE AND SUSPICION] Not even in appearance could anything be found. So great was his both faithfulness and reputation.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

PORRO REX COGITABAT CONSTITUERE EUM SUPER OMNE REGNUM] Ut etiam ei subef- sent alii illi prætorio præfecti, essetque Regi τὰ πάντα, qua- les multos esse, & nostra, & superiora sæcula viderunt apud Reges aut parum fidentes ingenio suo, aut fugientes nego- tiorum.

UNDE PRINCIPES ET SATRAPÆ QUÆRE- BANT OCCASIONEM] Livor enim in aulis regnat,

EX LATERE REGIS] Id est, quærebant crimen majestatis, quod sæpe esse singulare & unicum eorum, qui crimine vacarent, ait in Panegyrico Plinius. Hoc est quod Romano-Græci dicunt ἔγκλημα βασιλείας.

NULLAMQUE CAUSAM ET SUSPICIONEM INVENIRE POTUERUNT] Ne in speciem quidem re- periri quicquam poterat. Tanta erat ejus & fides & exi- stimatio.

## 6:5
Verse 5.

UNLESS PERCHANCE IN THE LAW OF GOD] A charge of violated religion must be sought where high treason is lacking. Jerome on this passage: A happy manner of life, in which enemies find no occasion, unless perchance in the lawful things of God.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NISI FORTE IN LEGE DEI] Quærendum est crimen læsæ religionis, ubi majestas deficit. Hieronymus ad hunc locum: Felix conversatio, in qua inimici nullam re- periunt occasionem, nisi forte in legitimis Dei.

## 6:6
Verse 6.

THEN THE PRINCES AND SATRAPS SURREPTITIOUSLY APPROACHED THE KING] I think it should have been written by the interpreter, subreferunt (they approached secretly). For that word is proper to this place. But the Chaldean word does not signify this so much as to make a gathering.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

TUNC PRINCIPES ET SATRAPÆ SURRIPUE- RUNT REGI] Scriptum puto fuisse ab interprete, subre- ferunt. Ea enim vox huic loco propria. At Chaldæa vox non tam hoc significat, quam concursum facere.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

THAT AN IMPERIAL DECREE MAY GO FORTH] In the Chaldean: A Royal Edict. Theodotion: στῆσαι στάσιν βασιλικὴν. In which he seems to have had regard for the term of the Roman Empire, which is a constitution.

AND AN EDICT] In the Chaldean: and to confirm an obligation. In Greek ἐνισχύσειν ὁρισμόν, that is, to make a law sacred, as the Romans used to say, perpetual, immutable, for which purpose a certain form was required. However, this custom did not exist among all nations.

THAT WHOSOEVER SHALL ASK ANY PETITION OF ANY GOD OR MAN FOR THIRTY DAYS, SAVE OF THEE, O KING] This counsel had a semblance, as if after that a greater majesty would be reconciled to the king, if he were already while alive equated to the gods. Horace concerning Augustus: To you present we bestow timely honors, and we place altars to be sworn by your name. Virgil: For he shall always be a god to me: a tender lamb from our sheepfolds shall often stain his altar. And in the Georgics: In the midst shall Caesar be for me, and shall hold the temple.

LET HIM BE CAST INTO THE DEN OF LIONS] גוב in Chaldean, Hebrew, and Arabic is any depressed and hollow place, such as a well, a cistern, a pit. Moreover, this hollow was so deep and steep that the lions could not climb out of it. To throw men to wild beasts is an ancient practice. Histories mixed with fables show this in the cases of Andromeda and of Diomedes of Thrace.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

UT DECRETUM IMPERATORIUM EXEAT] In Chaldæo: Edictum Regium. Theodotio: στῆσαι στάσιν βα- σιλικὴν. In quo videtur respexisse vocem Romani Impe- rii, quæ est constitutio.

ET EDICTUM] In Chaldæo: & confirmare obli- gationem. Græce ἐνισχύσειν ὁρισμόν, id est, facere legem sa- cratam, ut Romani loquebantur, perpetuam, immutabi- lem, quam ad rem certa forma requirebatur. Non erat autem is mos apud omnes gentes.

UT OMNIS QUI PETIERIT ALIQUAM PE- TITIONEM A QUOCUNQUE DEO ET HOMINE USQUE AD TRIGINTA DIES, NISI A TE, REX] Speciem habebat hoc confilium, quasi post id majestas re- gi conciliaretur amplior, si vivus jam Diis æquaretur. De Augusto Horatius : Præsenti tibi maturos largimur honores, Iurandúsque tuum per nomen ponimus aras. Virgilius : Namque erit ille mihi semper Deus : illius aram Sæpe tener nostris ab ovilibus imbuet agnus. Et in Georgicis : In medio mihi Cæsar erit, templumque tenebit.

MITTATUR IN LACUM LEONUM] גוב Chal- dæis, Hebræis, & Arabibus est omne depressum, & cavum, ut puteus, cisterna, fovea. Fuit autem cavum hoc tam profundum ac præceps, ut inde afcendere leones nequi- rent. Feris homines objicere vetus est. Ostendunt id fa- bulis mixtæ Historiæ de Andromede, de Diomede Thraciæ.

## 6:8
Ver. 8.

NOW THEREFORE O KING CONFIRM THE DECREE]

AND WRITE THE DECREE] And seal the writing: namely, not with your seal alone, but also with those of the nobles, to whom that right has been granted by the kingdom.

THAT THAT WHICH IS ESTABLISHED BE NOT CHANGED]

THAT IT MAY NOT BE LAWFUL FOR ANYONE TO TRANSGRESS AMONG THE MEDES AND PERSIANS] In the Chaldee: according to the custom of the Medes and Persians, (in making a law) which may not perish. The Babylonians did not have such a custom of making laws that were unchangeable even by the King, but the Medes and Persians had it from antiquity, and retained it for a long time, as we have shown at Esther 1:19, where the words are equal to these. From there, therefore, those flatterers seek an example, quite cunningly in the presence of a King sprung from the Medes. Iacchiades seems to have perceived this sense well.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NUNC ITAQUE REX CONFIRMA SENTEN- TIAM] Obligationem: ut modo 7.

ET SCRIBE DECRETUM] Et obsigna scripturam : nempe non tuo tantum sigillo, sed & procerum, quibus id jus à regno tributum est.

UT NON IMMUTETUR QUOD STATUTUM EST] In Chaldæo est tantum: ut non sit mutabile.

A MEDIS AC PERSIS NEC PRÆVARICARI CUIQUAM LICEAT] In Chaldæo : secundum morem Medorum & Persarum, (in facienda lege) quæ non pereat. Babylonii morem talem faciendi leges, ne à Rege quidem mutabiles non habebant, sed habebant eum antiquitus Medi, & Persæ, & diu retinuere, ut ostendimus ad Estherem 1, 19. ubi verba sunt his paria. Inde ergo adulatores isti exemplum petunt, satis callide apud Regem è Medis ortum. Videtur hunc sensum bene percepisse Iacchiades.

## 6:9
Ver. 9.

PORRO] Therefore. It is in the Chaldean, כל קבל דנה. PROPOSUIT EDICTUM ET STATUIT] In the Chaldean: He inscribed the writing and the obligation: That is, that sanction added, according to the said custom. רשם here, and in the following verse, is the same word as above 5, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

PORRO] Propterea. Est in Chaldæo, כל קבל דנה. PROPOSUIT EDICTUM ET STATUIT] In Chaldæo : Exaravit scripturam & obligationem : Id est, san- ctionem illam additam, juxta dictum morem. רשם hic, & in commate sequente est idem verbum quod supra 5, 24.

## 6:10
Ver. 10.

THAT IS THE SIGNED WRITING]

HE ENTERED HIS HOUSE, AND WITH THE WINDOWS OPEN IN HIS UPPER CHAMBER] ἐν τοῖς ὑπερῴοις, in the upper parts of the house. For that is עליה in Hebrew and עלית in Chaldean. He did everything as he was accustomed, as if the edict, being a Jew as the King himself knew, did not pertain to him.

CONTRA JERUSALEM] With face turned toward the temple, a custom which seems to have arisen from the words of Solomon 1 Kings 8:48.

AT THREE TIMES IN THE DAY] That is, the third, sixth, and ninth hours, a custom which Christians have also followed. We have spoken of this matter at Matt. 27:45. Jerome in his commentary on this passage: There are three times, moreover, at which knees are to be bent to God: Ecclesiastical tradition understands the third hour, the sixth, and the ninth. Finally, at the third hour the Holy Spirit descended upon the Apostles: At the sixth, Peter, wishing to eat, went up into the upper room to pray. At the ninth, Peter and John were going up to the temple.

HE WAS BENDING HIS KNEES] A custom of those praying in mourning and danger. See what is said at Matthew 6:5.

AND WAS WORSHIPPING] He was praying. For that is what מצלא means; whence the Massalian heretics [derive their name] from continuous prayers.

AND WAS CONFESSING BEFORE HIS GOD] That is, he was speaking praises to God; for that is what מודא means.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ID EST CONSIGNATAM LEGEM] Exaratam scripturam.

INGRESSUS EST DOMUM SUAM, ET FE- NESTRIS APERTIS IN COENACULO SUO] ἐν τοῖς ὑ- περῴοις, in locis domus supernis. Id enim עליה Hebræis & עלית Chaldæis. Fecit omnia ut c. at solitus, quasi edi- ctum ad se, utpote Judæum, ut Rex ipse norat, non perti- neret.

CONTRA JERUSALEM] Obversa ad templum facie, qui mos videtur natus ex verbis Salomonis 1. Reg. 8. v. 48.

TRIBUS TEMPORIBUS IN DIE] Id est, tertia, sexta & nona, quem morem secuti & Christiani. Diximus ea de re ad Matt. 27, 45. Hieronymus in commentario ad hunc locum : Tria autem sunt tempora, quibus Deo flectenda sunt ge- nua : tertiam horam, sextam & nonam Ecclesiastica traditio intelligit. Denique tertia hora descendit Spiritus Sanctus super Apostolos : Sexto volens Petrus comedere, ad orationem ascen- dit in cœnaculum. Nona Petrus & Iohannes pergebant ad tem- plum.

FLECTEBAT GENUA SUA] Qui mos orantium in luctu ac periculo. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 6, 5.

ET ADORABAT] Orabat. Id enim מצלא ; unde Hæretici Massaliani à continuis precibus.

CONFITEBATURQUE CORAM DEO SUO] Id est, Deo laudes dicebat; id enim est מודא.

## 6:11
Ver. 11.

INQUIRING MORE CURIOUSLY] In the Chaldean: running about, as above in verse 6.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

CURIOSIVS INQVIRENTES] In Chaldæo: con- cursantes, ut supra v. 6.

## 6:12
Ver. 12.

THE WORD IS TRUE] Firm, in the Chaldean: that is, what I have said will remain.

ACCORDING TO THE DECREE OF THE MEDES AND PERSIANS WHICH IS NOT PERMITTED TO BE VIOLATED] No less than those laws of the Persians and Medes, which are called immutable. Thus Iacchiades very well here.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

VERVS EST SERMO] Firmus, in Chaldæo : id est, manebit quod dixi.

JUXTA DECRETUM MEDORUM ATQUE PERSARUM QUOD PRÆVARICARI NON LICET] Non minus quam illas leges Persarum & Medorum, quæ dicuntur immutabiles. Ita hic Iacchiades optime.

## 6:14
Ver. 14.

HE WAS SADDENED] Pressed on one side by the necessity of the law, on the other by reverence for the man.

He set his heart, that he might deliver him] In the Chaldean: שׂם בּל: he set his care, for thus the Arabs use بلي. He labored that he might rescue him] Under some appearance of law.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

CONTRISTATUS EST] Pressus hinc legis neces- sitate, inde viri reverentia.

Posuit cor, ut liberaret eum] In Chaldæo; שׂם בּל: posuit curam, nam sic بلي Arabes usurpant. Laborabat ut erueret eum] Specie a- liqua juris.

## 6:15
Ver. 15.

Understanding the king] In the Chaldean: by a gathering made to the King. Know, O king, that it is the law of the Medes and Persians, that every decree which the king shall establish, it is not lawful to be changed] Translate: Know, O King, that such is the law among the Medes and Persians, that every obligation, if the King has established it, cannot be changed. The obligation here is, as above, the consent of the nobles chosen from the kingdom for that purpose, to which if the king's authority were added, that law according to the Persians and Medes (whose example they had followed in this matter) was then immutable.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Intelligentes regem] In Chaldæo: con- cursu ad Regem facto. Scito, rex, quia lex Medorum et Persarum est, ut omne decretum quod constituerit rex, non liceat immuta- ri] Verte: Scito, Rex, tale jus esse Medis ac Persis, ut omnis obligatio, si eam Rex constituerit, mutari nequeat. Obli- gatio hîc est, ut supra, consensus procerum à regno in id delectorum, cui si accederet regis autoritas, jam jus illud secundum Persas & Medos (quorum exemplum in hac re sequuti fuerant) erat immutabile.

## 6:16
Ver. 16.

Thy God whom thou servest continually] Even against human laws. Here he praises what he had forbidden, as above in Nebuchadnezzar 3, 95. He himself will deliver thee] May he deliver thee. It is a wish. The King had conceived this hope from the deliverance of the three youths.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Deus tuus quem colis semper] Etiam contra humanas leges. Hic laudat quod vetuerat, ut su- pra Nabuchodonosor 3, 95. Ipse liberabit te] Liberet te. Est optatum. Spem hanc conceperat Rex ex trium juvenum liberatione.

## 6:17
Ver. 17.

And a stone was brought, and placed upon the mouth of the den] All these things shadow forth the matters of Christ, as we said at Matt. 27, 60 and 66. The king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords] Namely, just as the decree itself had been signed. That nothing might be done against Daniel] Or rather, that what had been decreed concerning Daniel might not be changed. For so the Chaldean text is.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

Allatusque est lapis unus, et po- situs est super os laci] Hæc omnia res Christi obumbrant, ut diximus ad Matth. 27, 60. & 66. Obsignavit rex annulo suo, et an- nulo optimatum suorum] Nempe quomodo & decretum ipsum signatum fuerat. Ne quid fieret contra Danielem] Imo ne immutaretur quod decretum erat de Daniele. Sic e- nim textus Chaldaicus.

## 6:18
Ver. 18.

He slept fasting] As is wont to happen in heavy grief. And musical instruments were not brought before him] Musical songs were not brought to him. Thus Rabbi Saadia, whom Jacchiades follows. For they think דוון, with a transposed letter, is said for דוון. Moreover, sleep also departed from him] It fled from him: as is wont to happen to those who are very anxious or sorrowful.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

Dormivit incoenatus] Ut in gravi luctu fieri solet. Cibique non sunt allati coram eo] Cantus musici adducti ad eum non fuère. Ita Rabbi Saadia, quem sequitur Jacchiades. Putant enim דוון, litera trans- posita, dictum pro דוון. Insuper et somnus recessit ab eo] Fugit ab eo: ut valde anxiis aut mœstis solet evenire.

## 6:19
Ver. 19.

Then the king arising at the first light of dawn] In the Chaldean: Then the king rising in the morning as soon as it had grown light.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Tunc rex primo diluculo consur- gens] In Chaldæo: Tunc rex mane surgens simulatque il- luxerat.

## 6:20
Ver. 20.

Serve the living God] Not of imaginary Gods, such as we make daily. Thus God often wrings a confession of the true [God] from idolaters.

Darius was not destitute of the knowledge of the true God, nor were these things wrung from an idolater. For from v. 16 it appears (and Grotius acknowledges it) that he conceived hope concerning the God whom Daniel worshipped, that He would deliver Daniel, and he drew this from the deliverance of the three youths; and the edict which he promulgated in Dan. 3, v. 29, sufficiently testifies that he both worshipped the true God and wished Him to be worshipped without idolatry. Nor indeed does he only command that they should not speak evil of the true God, but that they should fear Him as the true, living, and eternal [God], whose kingdom is not destroyed, and whose power is even unto eternity, and as a Deliverer and Savior, who rescues and delivers whomsoever He wills, or rather those who trust in Him, and does signs and wonders, all of which are κριτήρια of the one true God. But if it be asked whether that knowledge was joined with saving faith, the reason for doubting is not slight. Inasmuch as he permitted Daniel to the lust of the wicked satraps, and faith cannot consist with sins against conscience. But the blessed Gesner answers: That the King indeed had true faith, as appears from his prayer full of confidence, yet he was hallucinating through human frailty and weakness of judgment: Then, having recognized his lapse, he performed penance and openly testified his grief for the admitted sin by fasting and serious contrition. And Grotius himself acknowledges at Dan. 7, 24, that the knowledge of the true God had been given to Nebuchadnezzar.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

Serve viventis Dei] Non imaginariorum Deorum, quales nos quotidie facimus. Sic ab idololatris veri confessionem sæpe Deus exprimit.

Darius non fuit destitutus veri Dei cogni- tione, neque hæc ab Idololatra expressa sunt. Nam ex v. 16. apparet (& agnoscit id Grotius) quod de Deo quem colebat Daniel, spem conceperit, ipsum li- beraturum Danielem eamq; hauserit ex trium juve- num liberatione; Et edictum quod promulgavit Dan. 3. v. 29. satis testatur ipsum verum Deum & coluisse, & coli voluisse citra Idololatriam. Neque vero tantum præcipit, ut non maledicant Deo vero, sed ut timeant eum ceu verum, viventem & æternum, cujus regnum non dissipatur, & potestas usŇ; in æternum est, & tanquam Liberatorem et Salvatorem, qui eruit ac liberat, quos- cunŇ; vult, vel potius eos, qui confidunt in eum, & facit signa, atque mirabilia, quæ omnia sunt κριτή- ρια unius veri Dei. Si vero quæratur, anne cum fide salvifica conjuncta fuerit illa notitia, ratio du- bitandi non levis est. Siquidem permiserit Da- nielem impiorum satraparum libidini, fides autem cum peccatis contra conscientiam consistere ne- queat. Sed respondet B. Gesnerus : Habuisse quidem Regem fidem veram, uti ex oratione fiducia plena appnreat, hallucinatum tamen esse humana fragilitate & judicii infirmitate: Deinde agnito lapsu suo pœnitentiam egit & dolorem suum de admisso pec- cato, jejunio & contritione seria palam testatus est. Et agnoscit Grotius ipse ad Dan. 7, 24. cognitionem veri Dei datam fuisse Nabuchodonosari

## 6:21
KING LIVE FOREVER] Live long. For so לעלמין is often taken among the Chaldeans, and similar words among the Hebrews.

Latin:

REX IN ÆTERNUM VIVE] Vivas diu. Ita e- nim לעלמין apud Chaldæos, & similes voces apud He- bræos sæpe sumuntur.

## 6:22
Verse 22.

MY GOD SENT HIS ANGEL] One of those watchers above 4, 14. AND SHUT THE MOUTHS OF THE LIONS, AND THEY HAVE NOT HURT ME] See 1 Macc. 2, 60; Heb. 11, 33. Something similar happened to Malchus, as Jerome narrates, and to the African Christians in the persecution of Huneric, as Victor testifies. BECAUSE BEFORE HIM JUSTICE WAS FOUND IN ME] Because I worshipped God, as is just and right. AND BEFORE THEE, O KING, I HAVE DONE NO WRONG] In no matter have I harmed your interests. I showed you all loyalty within the limits of sacred discipline.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

DEUS MEUS MISIT ANGELUM SUUM] u- num ex illis vigilibus supra 4, 14. ET CONCLUSIT ORA LEONUM, ET NON NOCUERUNT MIHI] Vid. 1. Macc. 2, 60. Hebr. 11, 33. Simile quid evenit Malcho, narrante Hieronymo, & A- fris Christianis in persecutione Hunerici, teste Victore. QUIA CORAM EO JUSTITIA INVENTA EST IN ME] Quia Deum colui, sicut justum & æquum est. ET CORAM TE, REX, DELICTUM NON FECI] Nulla in re tua læsi commoda. Exhibui tibi o- mnem idem intra limites sacræ disciplinæ.

## 6:23
Verse 23.

BECAUSE HE BELIEVED IN HIS GOD] He trusted in God, as Jachiades says. A huge reward of faith, and a certain preparation for the Gospel.

He calls the miraculous deliverance the reward of faith. It can certainly be called so; but since he calls confidence a certain preparation for the Gospel, according to his custom, how will it be taught that confidence is the reward of faith, which is its soul and form, or by what reason will it be proven that this confidence of Daniel was only a preparation for the Gospel? Inasmuch as confidence in God has the Gospel as its foundation, and is produced from the Gospel, and is born from the Word of the Gospel as from a seed. For faith is from the word heard, Rom. 10, 17. Indeed, unless the Ancients had had the Evangelical promises, they could not have placed their confidence in God. For the Word of the Gospel and faith or confidence are related. And how great this confidence of Daniel was, both the thing itself teaches, and the Apostle truly proclaims, when he says that through faith some wrought justice, obtained promises, and stopped the mouths of lions. Heb. 11, 33. Where there is no doubt that these things were said concerning Daniel. Is it only a preparation for the Gospel, that he is set forth as an example of Evangelical confidence, and celebrated with a distinguished eulogy?

Latin:

Vers. 23.

QUIA CREDIDIT DEO SUO] Confisus est Deo, quomodo hil Jacchiades. Ingens fidei præmium, & ad Ev- angelium quædam præparatio.

Fidei præmium liberationem dicit miraculo- sam. Nuncupari sane ita potest; sed quum præ- parationem quandam ad Evangelium, pro more suo vocet confidentiam, quomodo docebitur, confiden- tiam esse fidei præmium, quæ ejus anima est, & forma, aut qua ratione evincetur illud, quod hæc fiducia Danielis solum præparatio ad Evangelium fuerit? Siquidem fiducia in Deum Evangelium pro fundamento habet, & ex Evangelio procrea- tur, atque è Verbo Evangelii ceu semine nasci- tur. Fides enim est ex audito verbo Rom. 10, 17. Sane, nisi Veteres habuissent promissiones Evan- gelicas, fiduciam in Deum collocare non potuis- sent. Verbum enim Evangelii & fides vel fidu- cia relata sunt. Et quanta hæc fiducia Danielis fuerit, cum res ipsa docet, tum vero Apostolus de- prædicat, cum per fidem dicit nonnullos justitiam operatos, promissiones consequutos esse, & ora leoni- bus obturasse. Ebr. 11, 33. Ubi nullum est dubium, de Daniele hæc dicta esse. Num præparatio tantum ad Evangelium est, quod in exemplum fiduciæ Ev- angelicis sistitur, & insigni elogio celebratur?

## 6:24
Verse 24.

AND THEIR CHILDREN AND THEIR WIVES] As participants in the cruel counsel. AND THEY DID NOT REACH THE FLOOR OF THE PIT] To the bottom. UNTIL THE LIONS SEIZED THEM] When the lions seized them. So great was their hunger.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET FILII ET VXORES EORUM] Vt participes sævi consilii. ET NON PERVENERVNT AD PAVIMEN- TVM LACI] Ad fundum. DONEC ARRIPERENT EOS LEONES] Cum arripuêre eos leones. Tanta eorum erat fames.

## 6:25
Ver. 25.

THEN DARIUS THE KING WROTE TO ALL PEOPLES] As formerly Nebuchadnezzar 3, 96.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

TVNC DARIVS REX SCRIPSIT VNIVERSIS POPVLIS] Vt olim Nabuchodonosor 3, 96.

## 6:26
Ver. 26.

LET THEM TREMBLE AND FEAR THE GOD OF DANIEL] That is, let them not speak evil of Him, as above 3, 96. AND HIS KINGDOM SHALL NOT BE DESTROYED, AND HIS DOMINION SHALL BE EVEN UNTO ETERNITY] As above 3, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

TREMISCANT ET PAVESCANT DEVM DA- NIELIS] Id est, ne ei maledicant, ut supra 3, 96. ET REGNVM EJVS NON DISSIPABITVR, ET POTESTAS EJVS VSQVE IN ÆTERNUM] Vt supra 3, 11.

## 6:27
Ver. 27.

HE IS THE DELIVERER AND SAVIOR] He rescues and delivers, namely whomsoever He wills, as formerly the three youths, now Daniel. WORKING SIGNS AND WONDERS] Above 3, 100.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

IPSE LIBERATOR ATQVE SALVATOR] Ipse eruit ac liberat, nempe quoscunque vult, ut olim tres ju- venes, nunc Danielem. FACIENS SIGNA ET MIRABILIA] Supra 3, 100.

## 6:28
Ver. 28.

MOREOVER DANIEL PROSPERED EVEN UNTO THE REIGN OF DARIUS, AND THE REIGN OF CYRUS THE PERSIAN] In the Chaldean: But Daniel acted prosperously, both under the reign of Darius (that is, Nabonnedus), and under the reign of Cyrus. For it was Cyrus who took Babylon, and reigned there after Nabonnedus, even with the consent of Nabonnedus himself. Thus also Theodotion: κὶ Δανιὴλ κατήνθυνεν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ, Δαρείε κὶ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ Κύρε τῦ Πέρσε.

The Vulgate is correctly amended. For in the authentic text it is implied that he had more fortunate progress and flourished with greater authority after he was deemed worthy of such an illustrious liberation. Nor does that interpretation, 'he persevered until the reign of Darius,' fit. For the things which had preceded were done under the reign of Darius: and therefore the end of his life is not expressed here, but his happy success under those empires; that, however, is clear from the fact that he did not return to his homeland under these kings, but remained at court, without doubt so that he might watch over the welfare of his people there. And since he acted successfully, it must be a fable that it is said in chapter 14 (in the Vulgate) that he was cast into the lions' den a second time. But whether he lived after the times of Cyrus and subsequently returned to his homeland, nothing certain is held about that. If it be true, as Dorotheus has it, that he died in Chaldea and was buried alone with honor in the royal sepulcher, it is credible that he died while Cyrus was still alive; both because otherwise he would have acted prosperously himself under the successors of Cyrus until his own death, having been buried with such honor: and because after the vision had in the third year of Cyrus, it was said to him in ch. 12, 13: 'But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest,' as if he were already being dismissed from this world and ordered to rest in his dormitory. But Grotius is mistaken when he makes Nabonidus out to be Darius, since Darius was a Mede, but Nabonidus was a Chaldean, and the former defeated the latter together with Cyrus. Concerning which, previously.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

PORRO DANIEL PERSEVERAVIT VSQVE AD REGNVM DARII, REGNVMQVE CYRI PER- SÆ] In Chaldæo: Daniel autem prospere egit, tum sub Dario (id est, Nabonnedi) regno, tum sub regno Cyri. Cyrus enim fuit, qui Babylona cepit, ibique regnavit post Nabonne- dum, ipsius etiam Nabonnedi consensu. Sic & Theodotion: κὶ Δανιὴλ κατήνθυνεν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ, Δαρείε κὶ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ Κύρε τῦ Πέρσε.

Recte emendatur Vulgata. In textu enim authentico id innuitur, quod progressus habuerit fe- liciores & authoritate majori floruerit, postquam tam illustri liberatione dignus habitus fuit. Ne- que congruit illa interpretatio perseveravit usque ad regnum Darii. Nam quæ præcesserant, sub re- gno Darii gesta sunt: Ideoque non terminus vitæ e- jus hic exprimitur, sed felix successus sub istis impe- riis; id autem inde liquet, quod non reversus sit in Patriam sub his regibus, sed in aula manserit, fine dubio ut illic pro commodo populi sui vigila- ret. Et quum feliciter egerit, fabulam esse opor- tet, quod cap. 14. (in Vulgata) dicitur iterato in la- cum leonum conjectus. An autem post tempora Cyri vixerit, & deinceps in Patriam redierit, de eo nihil certi habetur. Si verum sit, quod habet Dorotheus, eum in Chaldæa mortuum, & in sepul- cro regio solum cum honore sepultum esse, credibile est, ipsum vivo adhuc Cyro obiisfe; tum quia alias sub successoribus Cyri etiam ipse prospere egisset, usque ad obitum suum, qui tanto honore sepultus fuit: tum quia post visionem tertio Cyri habitam dictum ei est c. 12, 13. Tu autem vade ad præfinitum, & requiesces, quasi jam dimitteretur ex hoc mun- do, & quiescere in dormitorio suo juberetur. Fallitur autem Grotius, dum è Dario Nabonidum facit, quum Darius Medus, Nabonidus vero Chal- dæus fuerit, & ille hunc devicerit una cum Cyro. De quo antea.

## 7:1 Argument
PART II. PROPHETIC. SECTION I. DANIEL'S VISIONS UNDER BELSHAZZAR. VISION I. CHAPTER VII.

Daniel saw four living creatures, and in the fourth he observed especially a little horn. He also saw one brought to the Ancient of days, the Son of man receiving glory and divine power and an everlasting kingdom: And he obtained an explanation of that vision concerning the four Monarchies, and the kingdom of Christ, and particularly concerning the fourth empire and the little horn prevailing against the saints until the judgment and the everlasting kingdom of the Most High.

Ver. 1.

IN THE FIRST YEAR OF BELSHAZZAR KING OF BABYLON] Thus far the History. Now follow the visions offered to Daniel divinely, which, because they happened at various times, he is forced to go backward and repeat the times which he had already passed over in the history, which also happens to other Prophets. For Belshazzar, which we had above, the more corrected Hebrew codices have Bel-esh-tzer, with the letter transposed and the meaning changed. For that signifies that Bel is of hostile fire, that is, to be burned by hostile flame, which Jeremiah had also predicted, ch. 51, 44. Thus the prophets used to twist names found in honor of idols with a slight inflection into the reproach of the same.
