Nevertheless, another word נָגַד is also attributed to this fiery river, which some render as to draw, others to be drawn, others otherwise: But from a comparison of the Targumim it is clear that this word, used by the Chaldeans and accepted regarding waters and rivers, denotes the distillation and effusion of the same: נטף which is had regarding the dripping clouds in Jud. 5, 4, is thus expressed by the Chaldean נגרו מטרא they dripped, they sent down rain. And Onkelos thus explains the word זָנַק Deut. 33, 22, implying an impetuous eruption of Dan: his land is irrigated by torrents, which flow down from Bashan, with the word וּנְגָדוּ likewise being used. So that in this illustrious vision, in which the government of the whole world is demonstrated to Daniel in the four beasts, and especially the kingdom of the Messiah of the New Testament to be established under the fourth beast and to endure even after the end of the world, besides the mystery of the Holy Trinity in the Ancient of Days and the Son of Man, and his exaltation, and this river of fire, not only is the third person of the Trinity, the Holy Spirit, taught, his divine essence, and personal property, and the emanation remaining in the throne on account of the essential περιχώρησιν, but also the effusion made in the New Testament, wonderful by reason of his gifts, is indicated. For what is promised to the believer in John 7:38: as the Scripture says, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly, is explained in the same place concerning the miraculous effusion of the Holy Spirit, which, as by reason of plenty and abundance, is compared to rain and rivers poured out in Is. 44, 3; 49, 10; Joel 2, 28. Zach. 14, 18, so by reason of excellence and power it is compared to fire. Whence also Baptism is called fire, Matt. 3, 11; Luke 3, 16. And who could doubt that a copious rain distilled from the river of fire upon the Apostles, when in this feast the gifts of the Holy Spirit were distributed copiously and most liberally among the Apostles in the figure of fiery tongues? A few drops of this river, only certain sparks of this fire, reached the men of the ancient age in the Old Testament, but the copious effusion, which corresponds to the word נגד, pertains to the more abundant grace of the New Testament, and was entirely fulfilled in the first Pentecost. These are the words of the blessed Lyserus, which it pleased me to add here, because no copies of the program are found, and they contribute not a little to the illustration of this remarkable vision. Compare what was said in Vol. III of the System, p. 840.

THOUSANDS OF THOUSANDS MINISTERED TO HIM, AND TEN HUNDRED THOUSANDS STOOD BEFORE HIM] Not those ten intelligences which Aristotle invents, but an immense number of ministering angels. THE JUDGMENT SAT] That is, those greater angels sat in lesser seats. בֵּית דִין for דִּינָא, that is, the council.

Whence is it certain that by the judgment the greater angels are understood? That had to be proven from the Scriptures. Angels without distinction all minister to God, as is had in the text: Thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten hundred thousands stood before him. That distinction of ministering and assisting angels smells of the Papists' lantern. But what is said, THE JUDGMENT SAT, is not for us to understand it as a Sanhedrin, since it can be taken as the Judge, that he sat for judgment. And even if it be said that assessors are included, we know at any rate that this dignity is attributed to the Saints, who are said to be about to judge the world, 1 Cor. 6, and that this was promised peculiarly to the Apostles: You also shall sit upon twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel, Matt. 19, v. 28; Luke 22, 36. Which is also read concerning the 24 Elders, Rev. 4, 4.

AND THE BOOKS WERE OPENED] The books are called the Scriptures of the whole lawsuit, the accusation, the defense, the testimonies, the instruments: Compare Rev. 20, 12.

Theodoret, Lyranus, Oecolampadius, and Sanctius understand the books of consciences. Calvin wishes the promulgation of the Gospel to be noted. Schvaningius, with Brochmand, the law of nature, the written law, and the Gospel of Christ. But the blessed Gesner's interpretation of the books of Scripture is to be preferred, because the judgment is to be instituted according to Scripture, John 12, 48. If for that reason they are not to be judged according to the Word, to whom the Word was not made known, then surely neither on account of unbelief toward Christ, because Christ was not made known to them either? But could they not, ought they not to have inquired for the Word?

Latin:

Vers. 10.

FLUVIUS IGNEUS, RAPIDUSQUE EGRE- DIEBATUR A FACIE EJUS] In Chaldæo: Flumen igneum manabat, ab ore ejus egrediens. Omnibus decretis ejus vis aderat perpetua.

Sic etiam B. Gefnerus sententiam Judicis innui vult, quæ vere erit ignea impiis. Rupertus Tutiefis vero per fluvium adumbrari vult Spiritum San- ctum, cujus sententia non inconveniens est: Nam uti Deus Pater per Antiquum dierum, Filius in specie filii hominis sistitur, ita in hac illustri θεοΦα- νείᾳ par erat etiam exhiberi Spiritum Sanctum, ter- tiam divinitatis Personam. Et quum Spiritus Sanctus sub fluvii similitudine ac specie alias in Scripturis exhibeatur Johan. 7. Apoc. 22. Idem- que igneam formam amet, eaque se visendum præ- beat Actor. 2. adhæc expressus hic habeatur Cha- racter personalis, in voce ἐκπορευόμενον, quæ in Græco textu occurrit, ac Spiritui Sancto appro- priatur Johan. 15, 26. Apoc. 21, 1. (In Chaldæo tex- tu occurrit verbum נפק, quo Syrus utitur Joh. 15, 26.) denique ἐκπορευόμενον dicatur AB ORE Antiqui Dierum, quod Spiritui oris Domini ἐκπο- ρευομένῳ παρὰ τ̃ πατρὸς proprium est, ideoque non immerito hæc de Spiritu Sancto exponuntur. Sicut Fluvius est ejusdem naturæ cum fonte, ita Spiritus Sanctus cum Patre. Facies sedentis est ve- lut ignis, fluvius à facie est etiam igneus. Vid. B. Gerhardum Cap. 178. Harmon. Evang. Plenius hanc ἐξήγησιν confirmavit B. Wilh. Lyserus, in Programmate pentecostali, A. MDCXXXIII. no- mine Rectoris hic, pro more Academiæ, publice proposito: Fluvius iste Danielis ignis est, & qui- dem non culinaris, cui Vitruvius prima hominum consortia accepta refert l. 2. c. 1. vel Elementaris, de quo adhuc inter Philosophos lis est, sed plane supercœlestis, & divinus, qui in ipso etiam se- dentis throno conspicuus, unde lucem inacces- sam inhabitare 1. Tim. 6,16. dicitur, ejusdem sum- mam sapientiam & scientiam, infinitam justitiam & immensam potentiam ostendit. Egreditur e- nim hic ignis fluvius à facie sedentis in throno, unde divina ejus origo, & natura conspicua. Flu- vius enim ignis hic מִן־קֳדָמוֹהִי ex facie, vel anterio- ri sedentis in throno antiqui dierum oritur, non ex posteriori, ut effectus ab ipso extra ipsam produ- ctus sequitur. De angelis statim subjicitur, quod steterint קָדָמוֹהִי coram eo: At de fluvio hoc quan- do S. S. loquitur, particulam מן adjungit, quæ flu- minibus addita ad originem, & fontem nos revo- care solet Ex. 17, 6. Jud. 15,19. Ita ergo fons flu- vii hujus in ipsa facie antiqui dierum est, in qua quia nihil est, quod non ipse Deus est, fluvius quoque hic ex eo emanans divinæ naturæ parti- ceps erit: fluvius enim ejusdem naturæ cum fon- te, ex quo promanat, est, juxta notum illud Bedæ lib. 1. in Morum. c. 1. Scimus fontem vivum stagnum tantam æqualitatem continere, ut si de quolibet eorum in aliud infundas, nullam dissimilitudinem in eis in- venias: dummodo nulla impuritas extrinsecus acce- dat. Quis ergo sciens hæc in terra visibili invisibilis creatoris Trinitatem & unitatem credere nequit? quis sciens fontis & rivi & stagni unam eandemque substantiam, id est, aquam, intelligere non potest illud, quod Dominus in Evangelio dicit: qui me videt, vi- det & Patrem. Etsi vero fluvius hic igneus ejus- dem cum facie sedentis in throno, ipsoque anti- quo dierum naturæ & essentiæ est; attamen per modum emanationis ab eodem distinguitur. Dici- tur enim fluvius hic ignis נָפֵק egrediens. נפק pro- prie per ἐκπόρευσιν redditur, unde LXX. senes ita Danielem h. l. explicarunt: ποταμὸς πυρὸς εἷλκεν ἐκπορευόμενος: Imo ipse S. Sanctus in commentario, quem supra Danielis hanc visionem in Apocalypsi per Johannem consignari fecit, idem verbum de fluvii hujus egressu adhibet c. 22, 1. ἔδειξέ μοι καθαρὸν ποταμὸν ὕδατος ζωῆς, ἐκπορευόμε- νον ἐκ τ̃ θρόνου τ̃ Θε̃, κ̀ τ̃ ἀρνίε. At ἐκπόρευ- σιν & processionem à Patre & Filio proprietatem Spiritus Sancti personalem esse ex Symbolo Atha- nasiano novimus & profitemur: Spiritus Sanctus non factus nec creatus, nec genitus sed à Patre & Filio procedens. Hujus fidei fundamentum in verbis Christi habemus Joh. 15,26. τὸ πνεῦμα τ̃ ἀληθείας ὃ παρὰ πατρὸς ἐκπορεύεται; quæ Syrus ita red- dit: רוּחָא דִשׁוּרָא הוּ דְמִנְלוּת אָבִי נָפֵק plane eandem vocem, quam hic Daniel habet, retinens. Ut ita hoc verbo interna & æterna Spiritus Sancti à Patre & filio emanatio nobis insinuetur, & ἄῤῥη- τον & ἀκατάληπτον alioqui mysterium in simili- tudine ignei fluminis ex ignea facie emanantis & in eadem tamen conspicue semper manentis, præter alio- rum fluminum naturam, quæ à fonte fluendo re- cedunt, nobis aliquo modo adumbretur. Attribuitur tamen etiam igneo huic fluvio & altera vox נָגַד quam aliqui trahere, alii protrabi, alii aliter reddunt : Sed ex collatione Targumim liquet, vocem hanc à Chaldæis usurpatam, ac de a- quis & fluminibus acceptam destillationem & ef- fusionem eorundem denotare : נטף quod de nubi- bus stillantibus Jud. 5, 4. habetur, à Chaldæo ita effertur נגרו מטרא stillaverunt, demiserunt plu- viam. Et vocem זָנַק Deut. 33,22. impetuosam eru- ptionem Dan insinuantem ita explicat Onkelos: terra ejus irrigatur à torrentibus, qui defluunt de Ba- san, voce וּנְגָדוּ itidem adhibita. Ut ita in hac præ- clara visione, in qua Danieli & totius orbis regi- men in quatuor bestiis, & cumprimis regnum Messlæ Novi Testamenti sub quarta bestia insti- tuendum & post finem etiam mundi duraturum demonstratur, præter mysterium S. S. Trinitatis in antiquo dierum filio hominis, ejusque exaltatione, & fluvio hoc ignis, de tertia Trinitatis persona Spiritu S. non tantummodo doceatur, ipsius divina essen- tia, & personalis proprietas, atque propter essen- tialem περιχώρησιν in throno immanens emanatio, sed etiam indicetur ratione donorum mirabilis in N. Test. facta effusio. Quod enim Joh. 7. 38. creditu- ro promittitur: sicut dicit Scriptura, flumina de ven- tre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ, id ibidem de Spiritus S. miraculosa effusione explicatur, quæ ut ratione co- piæ & abundantiæ, pluviæ & fluminibus effusis Es. 44, 3. 49,10. Joel. 2, 28. Zach. 14, 18. ita ratione præstan- tiæ & virtutis igni confertur. Unde & Baptismus ignis appellatur Matth. 3, 11. Luc. 3, 16. Et quis dubi- tare posset, copiosam pluviam de fluvio ignis hoc in Apostolos destillasse, cum in hoc festo in figura lin- guarum ignearum Spiritus S. dona copiose & lar- gissime inter Apostolos fuere distributa? Guttulæ aliquot hujus fluminis, scintillæ tantum quædam hujus ignis ad prisci ævi homines in Vet. Testam. pervenerunt, at copiosa effusio, quæ verbo נגד cor- respondeat, ad abundantiorem Nov. Test. gratiam pertinet, & in prima Pentecoste omnino impleta fuit. Hæc B. Lyserus, quæ addere hic placuit, quia programmatis nulla reperiuntur exemplaria, & non parum illa faciunt ad insignis hujus visionis illustrationem. Conf. quæ T. III. System. p. 840. dicta.

MILLIA MILLIUM MINISTRABANT EI, ET DECIES CENTENA MILLIA ASSISTEBANT EI] Non decem illæ, quas Aristoteles comminiscitur, intelli- gentiæ, sed immensus angelorum ministrantium numerus. JUDICIUM SEDIT] Id est, Angeli illi majores as- sederunt in sellis minoribus. בֵּית דִין pro דִּינָא, id est, τὸ συνέδριον.

Unde constat, per judicium angelos majores intelligi? Probandum id erat è Scripturis. Angeli citra discrimen ministrant omnes Deo, ut habetur in textu: Millia millium ministrabant ei, & decies centena millia assistebant ei. Distinctio illa angelo- rum ministrantium & assistentium Papistarum lu- cernam olet. Quod autem dicitur JUDICIUM SEDIT, non est, ut intelligamus de Synedrio, quum accipi possit de Judice, quod sederit ad judicium. Et si maxime assessores comprehendi dicantur, no- vimus utique quod Sanctis hoc ἀξίωμα tribuatur, qui dicuntur mundum judicaturi 1. Cor. 6. quod- que peculiariter hoc Apostolis promissum sit: Se- debitis & vos super sedes duodecim judicantes duode- cim tribus Israel Matth. 19. v. 28. Luc. 22, 36. Quod de 24. Senioribus etiam legitur Apoc. 4, 4.

ET LIBRI APERTI SUNT] Libri vocantur Scri- pturæ litis omnes, accusatio, defensio, testimonia, instru- menta: Confer. Apoc. 20, 12.

Conscientiarum libros intelligunt Theodor. Lyran. Oecolampad. Sanctius. Calvinus promulga- tionem Evangelii notari vult. Schvaningius cum Brochmando legem naturæ, legem scriptam, & Ev- angelium Christi. Sed præferenda B. Gesneri de libris Scripturæ interpretatio, quia judicium in- stituendum juxta Scripturam Joh. 12, 48. Si ob id non judicandi secundum Verbum, quibus Ver- bum non innotuit, utique nec ob ἀπισίαν erga Christum, quia nec Christus illis innotuit? Annon vero potuere, annon debuere inquirere Ver- bum?

## 7:11
Vers. 11.

I WAS LOOKING] I was watching attentively.

BECAUSE OF THE VOICE OF THE GREAT WORDS, WHICH THAT HORN WAS SPEAKING] Even against God himself. Below 25. I was eager to discern what outcome this matter would have.

AND I SAW THAT THE BEAST HAD BEEN SLAIN] In the Chaldean: I was watching until the beast was slain. I stood watching for so long, until I might discern the outcome of that Syrian and Egyptian Empire.

AND THE BODY HAD PERISHED, AND HAD BEEN DELIVERED TO BE BURNED WITH FIRE] That is, it was so destroyed that nothing of it appeared any more than of things which fire consumes. Pompey took Syria away from Antiochus Asiaticus, Augustus took Egypt from Cleopatra: thus the kingdoms ceased to be, and were made provinces of the Roman people.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ASPICIEBAM] Spectabam attentus.

PROPTER VOCEM SERMONUM GRAN- DIUM, QUOS CORNU ILLUD LOQUEBATUR] Etiam in Deum ipsum. Infra 25. Avebam cernere, quem exitum hæc res habitura esset.

ET VIDI QUONIAM INTERFECTA ESSET BESTIA] In Chaldæo: Spectabi donec interfecta est bestia. Tam diu substiti speculabundus, donec exitum cernerem Imperii illius Syriaci, & Ægyptiaci.

ET PERIISSET CORPUS, ET TRADITUM ESSET COMBURENDUM IGNI] Id est, ita deletum est, ut ejus non magis quicquam appareret, quam rerum quas ignis absumit. Pompejus Antiocho Asiatico Syriam ademit, Augustus Cleopatræ Ægyptum: ita regna desie- runt esse, factæque sunt provinciæ populi Romani.

## 7:12
THE POWER OF THE OTHER BEASTS ALSO HAD BEEN TAKEN AWAY] Macedonia was conquered by Paulus, the Greeks by Mummius and Flaminius, Mithridates, descended from Darius the son of Hystaspes, was broken by Sulla and Lucullus, and defeated by Pompey. Thus the kingdoms of Asia, Pergamum, Pontus, Cappadocia, and Bithynia were extinguished, which had once belonged to the Chaldeans, and then to the Persians.

AND THE TIMES OF LIFE HAD BEEN APPOINTED FOR THEM] Because a span of life had been appointed for them. Namely, by God. See a similar passage in Rev. 17:17.

UNTIL A TIME AND A TIME] In the Chaldean: Until a time, and indeed a preordained one. Beyond the limit fixed by God, it could not have subsisted.

Grotius understands this as a particular judgment to be exercised against Antiochus, and the end of this tyrant, and of the Syrian and Egyptian empire. But the ὑπόστασεις (hypostases) teach that the discourse is about the universal and final judgment, even though he has already received that infinite power, which is said to have been given to him, in his exaltation to the right hand of God, which confession will be most clearly manifested on the day of universal judgment, when the Son of Man is to come in the glory of God the Father. For the Son of Man is said to have come in the clouds of heaven, v. 13, which is a description of the final advent, Matt. 24:30, Luke 21:27. Thrones are said to be set for judgment, v. 9 and 19, and books are opened, v. 11, which are signs of the final judgment, Matt. 19:28, Luke 22:30, Rev. 20:12 and following. The saints are introduced as assessors in the judgment, v. 10, which it is established will happen at the final judgment, Luke 22:30, 1 Cor. 6:2. Finally, the saints are introduced to the plenary possession of the heavenly kingdom, v. 18 and 27. Which will not happen except on the last day, Matt. 25. Nor is the judgment established only against the little horn, or the fourth beast, but the power of the other beasts also has an end, v. 12, and only the power and empire of the saints remains eternal.

Latin:

ALIARUM QUOQUE BESTIARUM ABLATA ESSET POTESTAS] Macedonia à Paulo victa, Græci à Mummio, & Flaminio, Mithridates à Dario Histaspis fi- lio ortus, fractus à Sulla & Lucullo, à Pompejo devictus. Sic regna Asiæ Pergamenæ, Ponti, Cappadociæ, Bithyniæ extincta, quæ olim Chaldæorum, deinde Persarum fue- rant.

ET TEMPORA VITÆ CONSTITUTA ES- SENT EIS] Quia spatium vitæ ipsis constitutum fuerat. Nem- pe à Deo. Simile vide Apoc. 17, 17.

USQUE AD TEMPUS ET TEMPUS] In Chal- dæo: UsƊ ad tempus, & quidem præfinitum. Ultra ter- minum à Deo fixum non potuerat subsistere.

Grotius intelligit particulare judicium ex- ercendum adversus Antiochum, & exitum hujus tyranni, & imperii Syriaci & Ægyptiaci. At de universali & novissimo judicio sermonem esse ὑπό- saσεις docent, etsi potestatem illam infinitam, quæ ei data dicitur, acceperit jam in exaltatione ad dextram Dei, quæ confessio clarissime manife- stabitur in die pantocritico, cum in gloria Dei Pa- tris venturus est filius hominis. Filius enim ho- minis venisse dicitur in nubibus cœli v. 13. quæ est de- scriptio adventus novissimi Matth. 24, 30. Luc. 21, 27. Dicuntur Throni positi ad judicium vers. 9. & 19. & libri aperiuntur v. 11. quæ notæ sunt judicii ultimi Matth. 19, 28. Luc. 22, 3. Apoc. 20, 12. & seqq. Sancti ceu assessores in judicio introducuntur vers. 10. quod in novissimo judicio futurum esse con- stat Luc. 22, 3. 1. Cor. 6, 2. Denique intromittun- tur Sancti ad plenariam regni cœlestis possessio- nem vers. 18. & 27. Quod non fiet, nisi in novissi- mo die Matth. 25. Neque solum adversus cornu parvum, aut quartam bestiam judicium constitui- tur, sed aliarum etiam bestiarum potestas finem habet vers. 12. ac sola Sanctorum po- testas, & imperium æternum permanet.

## 7:13
Verse 13.

I WAS WATCHING THEREFORE] He now describes the manner by which that change happened. The same thing is signified as by the stone, by whose impact the feet of the statue were broken, 2, 34, 35.

AND BEHOLD WITH THE CLOUDS OF HEAVEN] That is, with the greatest speed and rapid motion in all directions, as in Jer. 4, 13.

AS THE SON OF MAN WAS COMING] The Roman people having no King within themselves, as is said in 1 Maccabees 8, 14. Sons of men are called private citizens, as in Psalm 82, 7. But that he was a private citizen here, insofar as that word is opposed to kings; as in Lucan: Let no one know this, except you who alone are privy to my vows, that I, though full of honors, and dictator, go to the Stygian shades, and Consul, a private citizen, by fortune, to die.

AND HE CAME EVEN TO THE ANCIENT OF DAYS, AND IN HIS PRESENCE THEY OFFERED HIM] That is, he was ordered to present himself before God, the judge of kings and kingdoms, as if to receive commands. Thus Cyrus is called the servant of God, because he carried out the decrees of God. Moreover, the Roman people is not obscurely an image of Christ, whose empire from the smallest beginnings reached the whole world, but in a divine manner. The author on the Governance of Princes felt the same.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ASPIEIEBAM ERGO] Jam modum describit, per quem contigit ista mutatio. Eadem res significatur, quæ per lapidem, cujus incussu fracti statuæ pedes, 2, 34, 35.

ET ECCE CUM NUBIBUS COELI] Id est, summa cum celeritate, ac motu rapido in partes omnes, ut Jer. 4, 13.

QUASI FILIUS HOMINIS VENIEBAT] Popu- lus Romanus nullum habens intra se Regem, ut dicitur 1. Maccab. 8, 14. Filii hominum dicuntur privati, ut Pf. 82, 7. Privatum autem hic fuisse, quatenus ea vox regibus oppo- nitur; ut apud Lucanum: Nefciat hoc quisquam, nisi tu quæ sola meorum Confcia votorum es, me quamvis plenus honorum, Et dictator eam Stygias, & Consul ad umbras Privatum, fortuna, mori.

ET USQUE AD ANTIQUUM DIERUM PER- VENIT, ET IN CONSPECTU EJUS OBTULE- RUNT EUM] Id est, jussus est se sistere coram Deo, re- gum & regnorum judice, velut ad accipienda mandata. Sic Cyrus servus Dei dicitur, quia Dei decreta exsequebatur. Est autem populus Romanus non obscure Christi imago, cujus imperium ab initiis minimis in totum orbem perve- nit, sed divino modo. Ita sensit & scripor de Regimine Prin- cipum.

## 7:14
Verse 14. AND HE GAVE HIM POWER, HONOR AND A KINGDOM] God gave him the greatest Empire.

AND ALL PEOPLES, TRIBES, AND TONGUES SHALL SERVE HIM] Compare Rev. 13, 7.

HIS POWER IS AN ETERNAL POWER, WHICH SHALL NOT BE TAKEN AWAY, AND HIS KINGDOM, WHICH SHALL NOT BE DESTROYED] Even now, the name and majesty of the Roman Empire remain, diminished in some places, but increased in other parts.

The detestable perversity of the illustrious opinion that the Roman people is to be understood by the son of man. Which gloss first betrays itself by its astonishing novelty. For that most learned man could find no one who had embraced it, except for some obscure writer on the Governance of Princes. But all ancient and recent Doctors agree that the Messiah is to be understood by the son of man. Furthermore, since Grotius acknowledges that the same thing is denoted by the son of man as by the stone torn away without hands, just as by that in chapter 2, we have shown that the Messiah is designated, it will be necessary to understand the same person here: Concerning whom Jerome says: The stone which in Nebuchadnezzar's dream is written as cut out without hands, and to have grown into a great mountain, and to have crushed the clay, iron, bronze, silver, and gold: is now introduced under the person of the son of man, so that the assumption of human flesh might be signified in the Son of God, according to that which we read in the Acts of the Apostles: Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven. Then indeed it is absurd and insolent for an entire people to be denoted by the term son of man; but that the Son of God is the son of man is not only most accepted in the phraseology of the New Testament, but it was also not unusual in the Old Testament, as is evident even from the Davidic expression in Psalm 8. Furthermore, the son of man is brought in the clouds to the Ancient of days, so that power to judge might be given to him, inasmuch as the Father gave all judgment to him, as is known from the parallel passage in John 5. Nor is he brought to receive commands as a servant of God, as Grotius thinks, but to be adorned and crowned with glory and honor. He is not established in a state of emptying, but of exaltation. Furthermore, not an earthly and worldly power, not a particular and local one, but an eternal and heavenly power, a universal and ecumenical power is given to the son of man, which remains forever, and so that all peoples, tribes, and tongues may serve him. Concerning which more fully in the Examination of Reformed Doctrine on the person of Christ, page 324. Which can be said of no earthly King. His power is an eternal power, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom, which shall not be destroyed. But this fits the Roman Empire not at all, nor any secular kingdom; for all those are crushed and have an end. To whom can this belong among men, says Jerome, let Porphyry answer: or who is this so powerful, who has broken and crushed the little horn, which he interprets as Antiochus? If he answers that the Princes of Antiochus were overcome by Judas Maccabeus, he must teach how he comes with the clouds of heaven as the son of man, and is offered to the Ancient of days, and power and kingdom are given to him, and all peoples, tribes, and tongues serve him: and his power is eternal, which is closed by no end. But that he appears AS the son of man, happens because he was not yet incarnate here, but was seen under the figure of the future incarnation, which used to be represented for a time by assuming a human appearance: just as it is also said of the figure of the leopard and the lion, as a leopard, as a lion, etc. But those glosses, that the son of man comes in the clouds of heaven, that is, with the greatest speed, and that by the son of man a private person is understood, and that he arrives at the ancient of days, that is, he is ordered to present himself, as if to receive commands, and that his power is eternal, that is, the name and majesty of the Roman empire remains in some way, are so cold, inept, and insipid that it is tiresome to dwell on refuting them. These arguments which we have brought forward also refute the trifles of Joh. Henr. Biesterfeld in refut. Crellii de uno Deo Patr. l. 1. sect. 1. c. 8. and of Henricus Meerbotius in sent. definitiva aphorism. 24. pag. 55, who invent that by the Son of man some earthly Prince or other (for they themselves do not know whom they ought to designate) is to be understood. That this prophecy treats of Christ, Grotius himself observed at Joh. 12, 34 and at Act. 10, 36. and he acknowledged that the calling of the Gentiles in the time of the New Testament is predicted here at Luc. 24, 47. In the Annotations indeed to l. 5. de Verit. Rel. Christ. §. 14. p. 177, he praised R. Levi Ben Gerson and Saadia, asserting that the son of man in Daniel is the Messiah: where he also has these words: Great teachers of the Jews, Salomon Jarchi, R. Josue cited by Abenesdra, and Saadias, agree that the Son of man in Daniel is the Messiah.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DEDIT EI POTESTATEM, HONO- REM ET REGNUM] Deus ei dedit Imperium maxi- mum.

ET OMNES POPULI, TRIBUS, ET LINGUÆ IPSI SERVIENT] Confer Apoc. 13, 7.

POTESTAS EJUS POTESTAS ÆTERNA, QUÆ NON AUFERETUR, ET REGNUM EJUS, QUOD NON CORRUMPETUR] Manet etiam nunc Imperii Romani, accisi alicubi, sed aucti in aliis partibus & no- men & majestas,

Detestanda σρεβλότης illustris sententiæ, per fi- lium hominis populum Romanum intelligendum es- se. Quæ glossa primum stupenda novitate sua se- se prodit. Neminem enim, qui eam amplexus fue- rit, nisi obscurum, nescio quem scriptorem, de Re- gimine principum invenire potuit vir πολυμαθέ- satος. Omnes autem veteres & recentiores Do- ctores Messiam per filium hominis intelligi consen- tiunt. Porro cum idem per filium hominis, quod per lapidem sine manu avulsum notari agnoscat Gro- tius, uti per istum cap. 2. Messiam designari osten- dimus, etiam hic eundem intelligere oportebit: De quo Hieronymus: Qui in somno Nabuchodono- sar lapis scribitur abscissus sine manibus, & cre- visse in montem magnum, & comminuisse testam, ferrum, æs, argentum, & aurum: nunc sub persona filii hominis introducitur, ut assumptio carnis huma- næ significetur in filio Dei, juxta illud, quod in Actis Apostolorum legimus: Viri Galilæi, quid statis aspi- cientes in cœlum? Hic Jesus, qui assumptus est à vobis in cœlum, sic veniet, quemadmodum vi- distis eum euntem in cœlum. Tum vero ineptum est, atque insolens, populum integrum voce filii ho- minis notari; Filium vero Dei esse filium hominis, non modo phrasi N. Test. receptissimum est, sed etiam in V. Testamento haud inusitatum fuit, ut vel è Davidica locutione Psal. 8. constat. Adhæc adducitur filius hominis in nubibus ad Antiquum dierum, ut ipsi detur potestas judicandi, utpote cui Pater omne judicium dedit, ut è loco paralle- lo Joh. 5. notum. Neque vero adducitur, ut man- data capessat ceu servus Dei, quemadmodum putat Grotius, sed ut gloria & honore mactetur ac coro- netur. Non in statu exinanitionis, sed exaltationis constitutus est. Ulterius non potestas terrena & mundana, non particularis & topica, sed potestas æ- terna & cœlestis, potestas universalis & œcumenica datur filio hominis, quæ in æternum permanet, & ut omnes populi, tribus, & linguæ ei serviant. Quo de fusius in Exam. doctrin. Reform. de persona Christi pag. 324. Quod de nullo Rege terreno dici potest. Potestas ejus potestas æterna, quæ non aufe- retur, & regnum ejus, quod non corrumpetur. Quod sed in Romanum Imperium minime quadrat, nec in ullum seculare regnum; omnia enim illa commi- nuuntur, ac finem habent. Hoc cui potest hominum convenire, inquit Hieronymus, respondeat Porphy- rius: aut quis iste tam potens sit, qui cornu parvu- lum, quem Antiochum interpretatur, fregerit atque contriverit? Si responderit, Antiochi Principes a Juda Maccabeo fuisse superatos, docere debet, quo- modo cum nubibus cæli veniat quasi filius hominis, & offeratur vetusto dierum, & detur ei potestas, & re- gnum, & omnes populi, tribus ac linguæ serviant illi: & potestas ejus æterna sit, quæ nullo fine claudatur. Quod autem videtur QUASI filius hominis, fit quia hic nondum incarnatus, sed sub figura in- carnationis futuræ, quæ repræsentari solebat ad tempus assumta humana specie, conspectus est: quemadmodum etiam de figura pardi & leonis di- citur, quasi pardus, quasi leo, &c. Illæ autem glof- sæ, quod in nubibus cæli veniat filius hominis, hoc est, cum summa celeritate, quodque per filium hominis privatus intelligatur, & quod usq; ad anti- quum dierum perveniat, id est, jussus sit se sistere, vel- ut ad mandata accipienda, & quod potestas ejus æ- terna sit, h. e. nomen & majestas imperii Romani aliqua ratione maneat, tam frigidæ, ineptæ, atque insulsæ sunt, ut iis refellendis immorari pigeat. Argumenta hæc, quæ adduximus, refellunt etiam Joh. Henr. Biesterfeld. in refut. Crellii de uno Deo Patr. l. 1. sect. 1. c. 8. & Henrici Meerbotii in sent. de- finitiva aphorism. 24. pag. 55. nænias, qui per Fi- lium hominis Principem terrenum, nescio quem (nam & illi nesciunt, quem designare debeant) intelligi comminiscuntur. De Christo hoc vatici- nium agere, observavit ipse Grotius ad Joh. 12, 34. & ad Act. 10, 36. & vocationem gentium tempore N. Testam. hic prædici agnovit ad Luc. 24, 47. In Annotatis vero ad l. 5. de Verit. Rel. Christ. §. 14. p. 177. laudavit R. Levi Ben Gerson, & Saadia, filium hominis apud Danielem esse Messiam asserentes: ubi etiam ista habet: Filium hominis apud Danie- lem esse Messiam consentiunt magni Judæorum Ma- gistri, Salomon Jarchi, R. Josue citatus ab Abenes- dra, & Saadias.

## 7:15
Vers. 15.

MY SPIRIT WAS HORRIFIED, I DANIEL WAS TERRIFIED IN THESE, AND THE VISIONS OF MY HEAD TROUBLED ME] Because of such great changes, which he conceived generally and confusedly in his mind, he soon understood more distinctly.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

HORRVIT SPIRITVS MEVS, EGO DANIEL TERRITVS SVM IN HIS, ET VISIONES CAPITIS MEI OBTVRBAVERVNT ME] Ob tantas mutationes, quas generaliter & confuse concipiebat animo, mox intel- lexit distinctius.

## 7:16
Vers. 16. I APPROACHED ONE OF THOSE STANDING BY] To one Angel, not from those sitting by, but from those standing by and ministering to God. See Zach. 3, 4, 7 and what was said by us at Matth. 18, 10.

AND I SOUGHT THE TRUTH] That is, clear understanding: τὴν ἀκρίβειαν, Theodotio.

HE TOLD ME THE INTERPRETATION OF THE WORDS] Of the things which I had seen in my rest.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ACCESSI AD VNVM DE ASSISTENTI- BVS] Ad Angelum unum, non ex adsidentibus, sed ex adstantibus, & ministrantibus Deo. Vid. Zach. 3, 4, 7. & quæ dicta a nobis ad Matth. 18, 10.

ET VERITATEM QVÆREBAM] Id est, claram intelligentiam: τὴν ἀκρίβειαν, Theodotio.

DIXIT MIHI INTERPRETATIONEM SERMO- NVM] Rerum, quas videram in quiete.

## 7:17
Vers. 17. THESE FOUR BEASTS ARE FOUR KINGDOMS] So also Theodotion τέσσαρες βασιλεῖαι. In the Chaldean it is מלכין Kings, that is, kinds of kings, or fourfold kings.

WHICH SHALL ARISE FROM THE EARTH] They will think and do nothing but what is earthly, being idolaters.

To arise from the earth denotes the origin of earthly empires, which arise on the earth, are conducted on the earth, and are earthly: and they are opposed to the eternal Empire, which is both the Lord's from heaven, and heavenly, and is conducted in a heavenly manner. However, the mind of the Monarchs is not expressed by this phrase, that they only savor of earthly things, much less that they are all Idolaters: which is an injury to many Monarchs who are most devoted to the worship of the true God under various Empires.

Latin:

Vers. 17. HÆ QVATVOR BESTIÆ QUATUOR SUNT REGNA] Sic & Theodotion τέσσαρες βασιλεῖαι. In Chaldæo est מלכין Reges, id est, regum genera, sive reges quadruplices.

QUÆ CONSURGENT DE TERRA] Nihil nisi terrenum cogitabunt, agentque, utpote idololatræ.

Consurgere de terra ortum notat imperiorum ter- renorum, quæ in terra exoriuntur, in terra gerun- tur, terrena sunt: & opponuntur æterno Imperio, quod & Domini de cælo, & cœleste est, ac cœlesti modo geritur. Non autem Monarcharum expri- mitur hac phrasi animus, quod terrena tantum sa- piant, nedum, quod omnes Idololatræ sint: quæ injuria est, in plures Monarchas, Dei veri cultui, sub diversis Imperiis addictissimos.

## 7:18
Vers. 18.

BUT THE SAINTS OF THE MOST HIGH SHALL RECEIVE THE KINGDOM] The greatest empire at length (that is, the Roman) will come to the worshippers of the one God. In this honor the Jews οἱ κατὰ σάρκα [according to the flesh] would have held the primary role, if they had received the humble Messiah: Now, since they themselves have rejected him, that honor has been transferred to the mystical Jews, i.e., to the Christians, who retain what was the chief part of Judaism, the worship of one God, being grafted in that manner into the Jewish tree: while this honor meanwhile remains with the Jews, that he to whom Christian kings themselves testify that they are servants, Jesus, was a Jew from among the Jews. But the saints are truly Christians, if they follow the precepts of Christ, which far surpass the holiness of all the Jews, even the best of them.

AND THEY SHALL OBTAIN THE KINGDOM EVEN UNTO THE AGES OF AGES] Christians will perpetually be possessors of great kingdoms, and if anything of the old Roman Empire shall fall away from them, it will be compensated by the addition of lands which never obeyed the Romans, such as Scanzia, Russia, Scotland, Ireland, Poland, Ethiopia.

Here the Judaism of Grotius reveals itself not obscurely, namely that worldly power and glory were promised to the Jews under a certain condition, if they had received the Messiah. Since they rejected him, he feigns that that glory has passed to the Christians. But where, I ask, is external worldly glory read to be promised in the Holy Scriptures if they received the Messiah? Where is it said that because the Messiah was not received by the Jews, that external glory was transferred to the Christians? These are feverish dreams. Furthermore, that kingdom which the saints of the Most High are said to be about to receive is not the Roman kingdom, nor any other worldly one, whether of Russia, or Scotland, or Ireland, or Poland, or whatever one might choose to invent, but it is a mystical Empire, which is openly distinguished here from worldly kingdoms, and is asserted to be eternal, v. 18 and 27. And therefore, concerning the kingdom which the faithful begin here in the kingdom of grace, but will one day consummate in the kingdom of glory, under Christ Jesus, the King of Kings and Lord of Lords, these things must necessarily be understood, and are explained by the common consensus of interpreters. Moreover, the faithful are called saints עֶלְיוֹנִין [Most Highs], i.e., of the Elohim, to denote the plurality of the divine persons. See Vol. 3 of the System of Theology, to which explanation Mr. Dr. Geier also agrees in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

SUSCIPIENT AUTEM REGNUM SANCTI DEI ALTISSIMI] Imperium tandem maximum (id est, Romanum) perveniet ad unius Dei cultores. In hoc honore primas habuissent partes Judæi οἱ κατὰ σάρκα, si Messiam humilem recepissent : Nunc cum ipsi eum repudiaverint, translatus est is honor ad Judæos mysticos, i. e. ad Christia- nos, qui quod præcipuum Judaismi erat, retinent, unius Dei cultum, eo modo in arborem Judaicam insiti : manente in- terim penes Judæos hoc honore, quod is, cui reges ipsi Christiani famulari se testantur, Jesus, Judæus fuit ex Judæis. Sancti autem revera Christiani, si Christi præcepta sequan- tur, multum vincentia omnem Judæorum, etiam optimo- rum, sanctitatem.

ET OBTINEBVNT REGNVM VSQVE IN SE- CVLA SECVLORVM] Christiani perpetuo compotes e- runt magnorum regnorum, & si quid de veteri Imperio Romano eis decedet, id compensabitur adjectione terra- rum, quæ Romanis nunquam paruêre, quales sunt Scanzia, Russia, Scotia, Hybernia, Polonia, Æthiopia.

Prodit hic sese non obscure Judaismus Gro- tii, quod nempe Judæis promissa fuerit mundana potestas, & gloria, sub certa conditione, si Messiam suscepissent. Quem cum rejecerint, eam gloriam ad Christianos transiisse fingit. Ast, ubi, obsecro, in sacris literis externa mundana gloria, si receperint Messiam, promissa legitur? ubi ob non susceptum Messiam à Judæis externa gloria illa ad Christianos translata dicitur? somnia ista sunt febrilia. Porro regnum illud, quod Sancti Dei altissimi suscepturi dicuntur, non est regnum Romanum, non aliud Mundanum, seu Russiæ, seu Scotiæ, seu Hyberniæ, seu Poloniæ, aut quodcunque fingere libeat, sed est Imperium Mysticum, quod aperte hic à regnis mun- danis distinguitur, & æternum esse asseritur v. 18. & 27. Ideoque de regno, quod hic inchoant fideles in regno gratiæ, olim autem consummaturi sunt in regno gloriæ, sub Rege Regum, & Domino Do- minantium Christo Jesu, hæc necessario accipien- da sunt, & communi Interpretum consensu expli- cantur. Cæterum dicuntur fideles sancti עֶלְיוֹנִין al- tissimorum sc. Elohim ad denotandam pluralitatem personarum divinarum. Vid. T. 3. Syst. Theol. cui explicationi annuit etiam Dn. D. Geierus in h. l.

## 7:19
Verse 19. AFTER THIS I WANTED DILIGENTLY TO LEARN] To learn more exactly.

OF THE FOURTH BEAST] Because that matter pertained most to the Jews, therefore it is explained more specially.

This is not the reason why the fourth beast is explained more specially, that the matter pertains most to the Jews, but because that beast is very terrible and many things to be wondered at and dreaded are said about it, and also because those things pertain most to Christians and the Church of Christ, and were revealed for the consolation of all the faithful.

WHICH WAS VERY DIFFERENT FROM ALL] See above v. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 19. POST HOC VOLVI DILIGENTER DI- SCERE] Exactius discere.

DE BESTIA QVARTA] Quia ea res maxime ad Judæos pertinebat, ideo specialius explicatur.

Non hæc causa est, cur bestia quarta expli- cetur specialius, quod ad Judæos maxime ea res pertineat, sed quia bestia illa valde terribilis & multa admiranda & tremenda de illa dicta, tum quia Christianos & Ecclesiam Christi ea maxime attineant, ac solatio omnium fidelium revelata sint.

QVÆ ERAT DISSIMILIS VALDE OMNIBVS] Vid. supra v. 7.

## 7:20
Verse 20. AND OF THAT HORN] That is, of that horn. For ו here, as elsewhere, is often explanatory.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET DE CORNV ILLO] Id est, de cornu illo. Nam ו hic ut alibi sæpe est ἐξηγητικὸν.

## 7:21
Verse 21. AND BEHOLD, THAT HORN WAS MAKING WAR AGAINST THE SAINTS] That is, the worshippers of one God, such as at that time among all peoples only the Jews were. Compare Rev. 11:7.

These things are not waged against the Jews, but against the Christians, who receive the kingdom, because they have their fulfillment under the fourth Monarchy and after the destruction of the Jews. The Grotian glosses proceed from a preconceived hypothesis, as if the discourse were about Antiochus, which we have previously refuted.

AND SHALL PREVAIL AGAINST THEM] Even after the city and temple are captured.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET ECCE, CORNV ILLVD FACIEBAT BELLVM ADVERSVS SANCTOS] Id est, unius Dei cultores, quales eo tempore inter omnes populos soli erant Judæi. Confer Apoc. 11, 7.

Hæc non adversus Judæos, sed Christianos, qui regnum suscipiunt, geruntur, quia sub quarta Monarchia, & post Judæorum excidium comple- mentum habent. Procedunt glossæ Grotianæ è præ- concepta hypothesi, quasi de Antiocho sermo sit, quam antea profligavimus.

ET PRÆVALEBIT EIS] Etiam urbe & templo capto.

## 7:22
UNTIL THE ANCIENT OF DAYS CAME] Well-cooked Judgments of God.

These things are most diverse. By the ancient of days, God the Father is understood, not indeed the well-cooked judgments of God. For He is described thus because of His eternity. Who will admit that the ancient of days is the same thing as well-cooked judgments? All the circumstances, which exhibit multivarious personal characters, require that a person be understood. But in a clear matter, there is no reason why we should linger, lest we seem to lend light to the sun. One must marvel at the glosses of Grotius, so not well-cooked.

Verse of the same. AND JUDGMENT WAS GIVEN TO THE SAINTS OF THE MOST HIGH] He will command his vengeance to the Jews. See Ezek. 38:18 and following, ch. 39. AND THE TIME CAME, AND THE SAINTS POSSESSED THE KINGDOM] And the time will come when the Saints will possess the kingdom: that is, with the soldiers of Antiochus ejected, they will govern themselves autonomously, self-judging, self-sufficient, and furthermore they will subdue Idumea, Samaria, and much of the Ammonitis and Moabitis. The books of the Maccabees and Josephus testify to this. Indeed, Isaiah 62 and 63, Jeremiah 31, and Ezekiel 36 had predicted it. In this, there was a figure of a much greater empire, which the Christians were to obtain. Concerning the Judgment, which is to be given to the Saints on the last day, 1 Cor. 6 is the discourse: because it treats of the universal and last Judgment, of the kingdom, which they will possess forever, and not indeed of any power whatsoever that the Maccabees were to obtain. And how will those things in v. 27 befit the Maccabees, AND ALL KINGS SHALL SERVE HIM, AND OBEY? That the glosses of Grotius are foreign, therefore, one would have to be blind not to see. But by what argument, I pray, will it be taught that the Jews in those wars of the Maccabees acted as a type of the Christians? Nor is it right to invent types at will, but one must show their traces in the sacred writings. Verse 23. WHICH SHALL BE GREATER THAN ALL KINGDOMS] In the Chaldean: it shall differ from all kingdoms: namely, because of greater cruelty and impiety. IT SHALL DEVOUR THE WHOLE EARTH] The earth, by way of excellence, is the land of Israel, the land promised to the fathers, the best land. Now the fourth beast is explained: since this interpretation of the angel does not suit the successors of Alexander, Grotius turns himself to the customary art of TWISTING the words of Scripture, that by the whole earth, the land of Israel, i.e., a small portion of the earth, ought to be understood. Although indeed the promised land was otherwise called the earth by way of excellence, yet not here, where the supreme empires of the world and Monarchies are compared among themselves, can such excellence belong to it; the power of the fourth beast, therefore, is described above the rest thus, IT SHALL DEVOUR THE WHOLE EARTH; but what would be its excellence above the rest, if it were understood to be going to overcome only the land of the Jews, when the most powerful Monarchs of the world have been adumbrated by the rest? And that kingdom is said to be greater than all kingdoms, which Grotius thinks happens because of greater cruelty and impiety. But the comparison teaches the magnitude of the power, or if it must be translated at all, it shall differ from all kingdoms, it will have been manifest that the successors of Alexander are not designated, because a kingdom entirely different from the former ones is indicated. Wherefore, by a consenting vote, almost everyone understands the Roman empire by the fourth beast, if you except those few who follow Porphyry the Apostate here, whom Grotius also chose as his leader. For the Roman Empire devoured the whole earth, because as iron crushes all things, so, as Helvicus says in his Universal History, page 54, the Roman power, having tamed and worn down all things, rules through all the regions of the earth, which indeed are not inaccessible, but are inhabited by men, not only within the pillars of Hercules, but also the Ocean, wherever it is navigable, and it was the first and only one in all human memory to place the rising and setting sun as the boundaries of its Empire, having dared to take the Empire of the world for itself, it constantly obtains dominion in all lands, nor is there any nation, so to speak, that does not acknowledge it as the Mistress of all, or refuse its empire, as Dionysius of Halicarnassus says, book 1. Furthermore, this fourth beast appeared terrible and very wonderful, to which no name is attributed, as to the others, because it was monstrous, having in one body many parts of different animals, just as in Apoc. 13:1, 2, the different parts of the preceding animals are observed, and a beast is seen like a Leopard, having a mouth

Of a lion, the feet of a bear. Because this fourth beast is as it were forged from the former ones, and surpasses all in ferocity and power, whose cruelty in the ten persecutions under the Heathen Emperors, and afterwards in the persecutions of the Anti-Christ, is sufficiently conspicuous and notorious. The Roman kingdom, says Jerome, he compared to no beast: unless perhaps to make the beast seem formidable, he kept silent the name, that whatever more ferocious things we might think of in beasts, we might understand this of the Romans. This which is here passed over in silence, the Hebrews think is spoken of in the Psalms: The Boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: and the singular wild beast hath devoured it. For which it has in the Hebrew: All the beasts of the field have torn it: while in the one Empire of the Romans we recognize all kingdoms at once, which were previously separated: But that which follows; Eating and crushing, and trampling the rest with its feet, signifies all nations, either killed by them, or subjugated to tribute and servitude. Some, with Osiander, refer those diverse forms of animals to the various forms of the Republic in this empire. For in the beginning it had Kings, upon whose expulsion an Aristocracy was established, so that the Republic might be ruled by the Senate and Consuls. Which form was afterwards changed again, so that the Decemvirs might hold power with supreme authority; meanwhile, the Tribunes of the people also mixed themselves into the government of the Republic, so that Democracy often struggled with Aristocracy. Finally, through Julius Caesar, the Monarchy of the Roman Emperors was established; lastly, the Roman Anti-Christ Pope occupied the seat of the Empire, and made the Roman Emperors as it were his vassals, and usurped the right of confirming the Roman Caesar. To this pertains the distribution of the Roman Empire into certain articles in Helvicus, page 59. The first from Julius to Constantine the Great in the year of the Christian era 308. Who first restored peace to the Church throughout the whole world, and transferred the seat of the Empire to Constantinople, after whose death also the first division of the Empire was made between his sons. The second from Constantine to Justinian in the year 527, under whom is the end of the Roman Consuls, and the promulgation of the Civil Law. In this article, a second division of the Empire was made between the sons of Theodosius, where not long after the western empire ceased in Augustulus in the year of Christ 476. And a little before, under Theodosius 1 and 2. Barbaric nations in great number began to tear apart and plunder the empire everywhere. The third from Justinian to Charlemagne and the final division of the Empire into East and West in the year of Christ 800, from which the fourth in the Western German Empire still endures. The Eastern of the Greeks ceased in the year 1453, with the capture of Constantinople by the Turks. The fourth Dynasty of the Germans may be subdivided into several particles or Dynasties. 1. It is of the Franks, and especially the Carolingians, up to Henry the Fowler in the year 920. 2. Of the Saxons from Henry the Fowler to Conrad the Second the Salian in the year 1024. 3. Again of the Franks from Conrad the Second the Salian to Conrad the Third in the year 1138. 4. From Conrad the Third of the Swabian Dynasty, up to Rudolph of Habsburg in the year 1273. More accurate Chronologists believe that the seven Electors were established in these times around the year 1250. 5. Of those who were established by the Electors, (for the most part Austrians) from Rudolph the first to Leopold I, the modern August Emperor, to whose empire may the Lord Jesus most graciously grant blessing for the glorification of His name, and for the preservation and propagation of the kingdom of grace!

Furthermore, this beast was MOST STRONG. For the power of the Romans was greatest. IT HAD GREAT IRON TEETH, EATING AND CRUSHING, whatever it might seize with its bite. AND THE REST WITH ITS FEET

TRAMPLING. For the Romans horribly raged with iron against other nations, and more human blood was shed through this Monarchy than through any other, but it also violently trampled and crushed the remaining kingdoms, just as Histories testify; for the Roman power first indeed brought Asia Minor under its control, with Antiochus the Great defeated, Livy book 37, Justin book 31. Then Macedonia, with Perseus defeated 156 years after the death of Alexander. Afterwards Syria, with Tigranes defeated by Pompey about 260 years after the death of Alexander, Livy, Plutarch, Justin. Furthermore Egypt, which Julius Caesar first occupied, with King Ptolemy Dionysius defeated, though the kingdom was granted to his sister Cleopatra. Octavius Augustus, however, with Antony and Cleopatra defeated, reduced it to a province, as Plutarch testifies, etc. It pertains to this, that in a not dissimilar way, as the fourth beast, the Roman Anti-Christ is described in the Johannine Apocalypse, as one who was to occupy the seat of the Roman Empire, and to claim for himself the axioms of the Empire, and to subject the Roman Emperors to himself: See Apoc. 13, 1. 2. chap. 17, 10. 18. Wherefore not without cause does the blessed Gesner institute a comparison here with the Apocalyptic passages, and from it demonstrates that this animal is not a type of the kingdom of the Seleucids in Asia, as Porphyry raved (and with him Grotius), but the Roman Monarchy, since Apoc. 17, 12 is explained thus: the seven heads are seven mountains, where the woman sits, the great Babylonian harlot riding upon this beast, the great city, which holds Empire over the Kings of the earth. For at that time, when Saint John was writing these things, truly no other city in the whole world held Dominion over the Kings of the earth than the Roman city, whence it is concluded by inevitable consequence that this beast, upon which the Babylonian harlot sits, is the Roman Empire; nor do they designate any other city than this by the description of the seven mountains, since it is certain that the Roman city before the Gothic and Vandalic devastations had encompassed seven mountains within its circuit.

Latin:

DONEC VENIT ANTIQVVS DIERVM] Be- ne cocta Dei Judicia.

Hæc maxime diversa sunt. Per antiquum dierum Deus Pater intelligitur, non vero judicia Dei bene cocta. Ille enim ob æternitatem ita describitur. Quis admittet antiquum dierum idem esse, quod bene co- cta Judicia? Personam intelligi debere omnes πε- ριστάσεις, quæ characteres personales multivarios exhibent, requirunt. Sed in re luculenta non est, quod immoremur, ne soli lucem fœnerari videa- mur. Mirari oportet glossas Grotii, tam non bene coctas.

Verf. eod. ET JVDICIVM DEDIT SANCTIS EXCELSI] Vindictam suam mandabit Judæis. Vide Ezech. 38,18. & sequentibus, c. 39. ET TEMPVS ADVENIT, ET REGNVM OB- TINERVNT SANCTI] Et tempus veniet, cum Sancti obtinebunt regnum: id est, ejectis Antiochi militibus ipsi semet gubernabunt αὐτόνομοι, ἀυτόδικοι, ἀυτοτελεῖς, ac præterea subigent Idumæam, Samariam, Ammonitidis & Moabitidis multa. Testantur hoc Maccabæorum libri & Josephus. Præ- dixerant vero Es. 62. & 63. Jer. 31. Ezech. 36. In hoc fi- gura fuit imperii multo majoris, quod obtenturi erant Christiani. De Judicio, quod dandum est Sanctis in no- visfimo die, 1. Cor. 6. sermo est: quia agitur de Judi- cio universali & novissimo, de regno, quod in æter- num possidebunt, non vero de qualicunque pote- state, quam Maccabæi obtenturi sint. Et quomodo Maccabæis convenient illa v. 27. ET OMNES RE- GES SERVIENT EI, ET OBEDIENT? A- lienas ergo Grotii glossas esse cæcus sit, qui non vi- deat. Gessisse vero Judæos in istis bellis Maccabæo- rum typum Christianorum, quo sodes, argumento docebitur? Neq; fas est pro lubitu fingere typos, sed monstrare eorum oportet in sacris vestigia. Vers. 23. QVOD MAJVS ERIT OMNIBVS RE- GNIS] In Chaldaico: differet ab omnibus regnis: nempe ob majorem sævitiam & impietatem. DEVORABIT VNIVERSAM TERRAM] Terra κατ' ἐξοχήν, est terra Israël, terra promissa patribus, terra optima. Explicatur jam quarta bestia: quæ ἐξήγησις angeli quum non conveniat Alexandri successoribus, ad consuetam artem TORQVENDI verba Scri- pturæ, se convertit Grotius, per universam terram, terram Israëlis, h. e. exiguam portionem terræ intel- ligi debere. Quamvis vero âlias terra promissa κατ' ἐξοχὴν terra diceretur, non tamen hic, ubi summa imperia mundi, & Monarchiæ inter se comparan- tur, talis ἐξοχὴ ei competere potest; Quartæ ergo bestiæ potentia præ reliquis ita describitur, DE- VORABIT VNIVERSAM TERRAM; quæ vero ejus esset præ reliquis ἐξοχὴ, si solum Judæo- rum terram superatura intelligeretur, quum per reliquas potentissimi orbis Monarchæ adumbrati sint? Et dicitur regnum illud majus omnibus regnis, quod ob majorem sævitiam & impietatem fieri pu- tat Grotius. Sed comparatio docet magnitudi- nem potentiæ, aut si omnino vertendum, differet ab omnibus regnis, manifestum fuerit, non designa- ri successores Alexandri, quia regnum prorsus di- versum à prioribus indigitatur. Quapropter con- sentienti suffragio pleriq; omnes per quartam be- stiam Romanum imperium intelligunt, si paucos illos excipias, qui Porphyrium Apostatam hic sequuntur, quem etiam ducem elegit Grotius. Nam Romanum Imperium devoravit universam terram, quia ut fer- rum omnia comminuit, ita, Helvico dicente Hist. univers. pag. 54. Romana potentia domitis & attritis omnibus, imperat per cunctas terræ plagas, quæ qui- dem inaccessæ non sunt, sed ab hominibus habitantur, non solum intra columnas Herculis, verum etiam O- ceano, quacunq; est navigabilis, primaq; & sola omni hominum memoria ortum & occasum terminos Im- perii sui posuit, ausa orbis Imperium sibi sumere, do- minium omnibus in terris constanter obtinet, nec est ulla gens, ut sic dicam, quæ non agnoscat universorum Dominam, aut detrectet ejus imperium, sicut inquit Dionys. Halicarn. lib. 1. Porro hæc bestia quarta terribilis, atq; mirabilis admodum visa est, cui nul- lum tribuitur nomen, ut cæteris, quod monstrosa fuerit, in uno corpore plures habens diversorum animalium partes, quemadmodum Apoc. 13, 1. 2. observantur præcedentium animalium partes di- versæ, & conspicitur bestia similis Pardo, habens os

Leonis, pedes Ursi. Quia conflata veluti est hæc be- stia quarta è prioribus, & ferocia, potentiâq́; omnes superat, cujus crudelitas in decem persecutionibus sub Ethnicis Imperatoribus, ac postmodum in perse- cutionibus Anti-Christi satis conspicua & notoria est. Romanum regnum, inquit Hieronymus, nulli bestiæ comparavit: nisi forte ut formidolosam faceret bestiam, vocabulum tacuit, quicquid ferocius cogita- verimus in bestiis, hoc Romanos intelligamus. Hoc quod hic tacitum est, Hebræi in Psalmis dictum putant: Devastavit eam Aper de sylva: & singularis fe- rus depastus est eam. Pro quo in Hebræo habet: Omnes bestiæ agri laceraverunt eam: dum in uno Imperio Romanorum omnia simul regna cogno- scimus, quæ prius fuerunt separata: Illud autem quod sequitur; Comedens atq́; comminuens, & re- liqua pedibus suis conculcans, significat omnes na- tiones, vel interfectas ab eis, vel tributo & servituti subjugatas. Diversas illas animalium formas non- nulli cum Osiandro ad formas Reip. varias in hoc imperio referunt. Initio enim habuit Reges, qui- bus ejectis constituta fuit Aristocratia, ut Resp. per Senatum & Consules regeretur. Quæ forma postea iterum immutata est, ut Decemviri cum summa potestate imperium tenerent, interea etiam admi- scuerunt sese gubernationi Reipublicæ Tribuni plebis, ita ut Democratia cum Aristocratia sæpe lu- ctaretur. Tandem per Julium Cæsarem constituta fuit Monarchia Imperatorum Romanorum, ultimo Papa Anti-Christus Romanus sedem Imperii oc- cupavit, & Romanos Imperatores quasi Vasallos suos fecit, atq; jus confirmandi Cæsaris Romani u- surpavit. Quo facit distributio Imperii Romani in certos articulos apud Helvicum pag. 59. Primus à Julio ad Constantinum M. Anno æræ Christianæ 308. Qui primus pacem Ecclesiæ per totum orbem re- stituit, & sedem Imperii Constantinopolin transtu- lit, post cujus obitum etiam prima divisio Imperii facta inter ejus filios. Secundus à Constantino ad Justinianum anno 527. sub quo finis est Consulum Romanorum, & promulgatio Juris Civilis. In hoc articulo facta divisio Imperii inter Theodosii filios altera, ubi non multo post occidentale impe- rium in Augustulo desiit anno Christi 476. Et pau- lo ante, sub Theodosio 1. & 2. Barbaricæ gentes ma- gno numero passim imperium cœperunt dilacera- re, ac diripere. Tertius à Justiniano ad Carol. M. & divisionem ultimam Imperii in Orientem & Occi- dentem anno Christi 800. à quo quartus in Germano- rum Imperio Occidentali etiamnum perdurat. Orien- tale Græcorum anno 1453. desiit, capta Constantino- poli à Turcis. Quartam Dynastiam Germanorum li- cet in plures particulas seu Dynastias subdividere. 1. Est Francorum, & præcipue Karolidarum, usq́; ad Heinricum Aucupem anno 920. 2. Saxonum ab Hein- rico AucuPe, ad Conradum Secundum Salicum anno 1024. 3. Rursus Francorum à Conrado Salico Secun- do ad Conradum Tertium anno 1138. 4. A Conrado Tertio Svevorum Dynasta, usq́; ad Rodolphum Hab- spurgicum anno 1273. His temporibus septem Electores constitutos circa annum 1250. sentiunt accuratiores Chronologi. 5. Eorum, qui ab Electoribus constitu- ti sunt, (Austriacorum ut plurimum) à Rudolpho primo ad Leopoldum I. Modernum Imperatorem Augustum, cujus imperio Dominus Jesus ad nominis sui glorifi- cationem, & regni gratiæ conservationem, ac propa- gationem gratiosissime benedicat!

Ulterius FORTISSIMA fuit hæc bestia. Ma- xima enim fuit Romanorum potentia. DENTES FERREOS HABEBAT MAGNOS, COME- DENS AC COMMINUENS, quæcunq; mor- su apprehenderet. ET RELIQUA PEDIBUS

SUIS CONCULCANS. Romani enim ferro horribiliter grassati sunt in alias gentes, & plus san- guinis humani per hanc Monarchiam, quàm per ullam aliam fusum est, sed & reliqua regna violen- ter conculcavit & attrivit, quemadmodum Histo- riæ testantur; Romana enim potentia primum qui- dem Asiam minorem sub potestatem suam rede- git, victo Antiocho Magno, Liv. l. 37. Just. l. 31. Dein- de Macedoniam, victo Perseo annis 156. à morte Alexandri. Postea Syriam, victo Tigrane à Pompe- jo annis 260. circiter à morte Alexand. Liv. Plut. Just. Ulteriùs Ægyptum, quam primus occupavit Julius Cæsar, victo Rege Ptolemæo, Dionysio, concesso tamen regno Cleopatræ sorori ejus. O- ctavius autem Augustus, victo Antonio, & Cleo- patra redegit in provinciam, Plutarcho teste &c. Facit huc, quod non absimili modo, ut bestia quar- ta, describatur Romanus Anti-Christus in Apo- calypsi Johannea, utpote qui sedem Imperii Roma- ni occupaturus erat, & axiomata Imperii sibi ven- dicaturus, & Imperatores Romanos sibi subjectu- rus: Vid. Apoc. 13, 1. 2. cap. 17, 10. 18. Quapropter non immerito collationem instituit hic B. Gesne- rus cum locis Apocalypticis, & ex ea demonstrat, quod hoc animal non sit typus regni Seleucidarum in Asia, ut Porphyrius insanivit, (& cum eo Gro- tius) sed Monarchia Romana, siquidem Apoc. 17, 12. ita explicatur: septem capita sunt septem montes, ubi mulier sedet, magna meretrix Babylonica bestiæ huic inequitans, civitas magna, quæ tenet Imperium in Reges terræ. Eo enim tempore, quo sanctus Jo- hannes ista scribebat, nulla profecto civitas alia in toto terrarum orbe Dominium obtinebat in Re- ges terræ, quam urbs Romana, unde inëvitabili consequentia concluditur, Istam bestiam, cui me- retrix Babylonica insidet, esse Romanum Imperium; nec aliam urbem, quam hanc designant œsteg- œse de septem montibus, siquidem constat Roma- nam urbem ante Gothicas & Vandalicas devasta- tiones septem montes suo ambitu comprehendisse.

## 7:24
Verse 24. FURTHERMORE THE TEN HORNS OF HIS KINGDOM SHALL BE TEN KINGS] Now of Syria, now of Egypt, who will vex Judea.

AND ANOTHER SHALL RISE AFTER THEM, AND HE SHALL BE MORE POWERFUL THAN THE FORMER] Not so in the Chaldean: but, he shall be different from the former: for he will accomplish many things not by force, but by cunning. Which the eyes of a man signify, above 8. See also below 8, 23. 11, 21. 25.

AND HE SHALL HUMBLE THREE KINGS] Ptolemy Philometor, Seleucus his elder brother, and his son Demetrius, as was said above 8.

Latin:

Vers. 24. PORRO CORNUA DECEM EJUS REGNI DE- CEM REGES ERUNT] Modo Syriæ, modo Ægypti, qui Judæam vexabunt.

ET ALIUS CONSURGET POST EOS, ET IPSE POTENTIOR ERIT PRIORIBUS] Non ita in Chaldæo: sed, diversus erit à prioribus: multa enim peraget non vi, sed astu. Quod significant oculi hominis, supra 8. Vide & infra 8, 23. 11, 21. 25.

ET TRES REGES HUMILIABIT] Ptolemæum Philometorem, Seleucum fratrem suum majorem, & fi- lium ejus Demetrium, ut dictum supra 8.

## 7:25
Ver. 25. AND HE SHALL SPEAK WORDS AGAINST THE MOST HIGH] He will despise the true God, below 11, 36. to imitate the Lord, the ministers ὑπεράγων ἐβλασφήμει, and they uttered unlawful words, 2 Macc. 10, 34. & 12, 14.

AND HE SHALL THINK THAT HE CAN CHANGE TIMES] He will hope that he can abolish forever the Sabbaths, Passovers, Pentecosts, Feast of Tabernacles, days of atonement, new moons. This is what is said in 1 Macc. 1, 47, and to profane the sabbaths and feasts.

AND LAWS] And the law, in the Chaldean: i.e. circumcision, the reading of the law, and other rites: to take away the lawful ordinances, 1 Macc. 3, 29. who followed him, departed from the holy covenant. v. 1, 14, 15, 16, 17, 45, and following. See Josephus 12, 7.

AND THEY SHALL BE DELIVERED INTO HIS HAND] The law and the observances of days shall lie trampled under his power, God permitting it,

FOR A TIME AND TIMES, AND HALF A TIME] What we have here in Chaldean, we have in Hebrew below 12, 7. Times, χρόνοι, by way of excellence years, as above 4, 29, and often among the Greeks. Josephus in the Jewish War, book 1, chapter 1, dealing with Antiochus: he plundered the temple and stopped the daily continual sacrifices for three years and six months. It was a little more, that is, one thousand two hundred and ninety days, as we shall have below 12, 11. Josephus said one thousand two hundred and ninety-six, 9, 12. three years and a half and a little something more, says Chrysostom: but that which grows over is held in addition. to round off the number. The Apocalypse, in the history corresponding to this type, said one thousand two hundred and sixty days, 11, 6. and elsewhere 42 months, c. 11, 2. and 13, 5. The Praetor does not care about a trifle, nor does the Prophet. However, this time is reckoned from the capture of the city and the interdiction of the rites; for from the time the idol had been placed, there were only three years. Thus Josephus, and 2 Macc. 10, 5. Likewise 1 Macc. 1, 62, compared with the passage of the same book 4, 52. Whence it appears that in the said passage 2 Macc. 10, verse 3, for διετῆ one should read τριετῆ.

Grotius seizes upon these for Antiochus. But rashly, as has been demonstrated thus far. Now he is also less fair to the Prophet's calculation, as if the Prophet does not care about a trifle. Just as that is commonly said of the Praetor. But our Prophet is entirely accurate in designating time. When he deals with the profanation of Antiochus in ch. 8, 18, he counts two thousand three hundred days, which make up six years, during which Grotius himself acknowledged in the same place that the Priesthood was profaned. Which, however, he will not be able to extract from this present designation of time, and times, and half a time. For even if we understand by time a year, by times two years, and by half a time a half-year, only three and a half years result. Nor does the passage c. 12, 11 contribute to this. For neither is a three-and-a-half-year period designated there, but 1290 days are expressed, and it does not appear that common days are to be understood there. For that periphrasis is not added, by which the Prophet designated the space of days and nights in c. 8, 14, defining the days in this way, 'until evening and morning'; in vain, therefore, are these compared as parallels.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET SERMONES CONTRA EXCELSVM LOQVETUR] Spernet Deum verum infra 11, 36. imitari Dominum ministri ὑπεράγων ἐβλασφήμει, κ̓ λόγυς ἀθεμί- τυς προΐεντο 2. Macc. 10, 34. & 12, 14.

ET PUTABIT QUOD POSSIT MUTARE TEMPORA] Sperabit se in perpetuum abolere posse Sab- bata, Paschata, Pentecostas, skenopegias dies propitiatio- nis, novilunia. Hoc est, quod dicitur 1. Macc. 1, 47, κ̓ βε- βηλῶσαι σάββατα κ̓ ἑορτάς.

ET LEGES] Et legem, in Chaldæo: i. e. circumci- sionem, lectionem legis, ritusq; alios: τᾶ ἄραι τὰ νόμιμα, 1. Macc. 3, 29. qui eum sectati sunt, ἀπέσησαν ἀπὸ δια- θήκης ἁγίας. v. 1. 14. 15. 16. 17. 45. & sequentibus, Vide Jose- phum 12, 7.

ET TRADENTUR IN MANU EJUS] Lex & dierum observationes proculcatæ jacebunt sub ipsius po- testate, Deo id sinente,

AD TEMPUS ET TEMPORA, ET DIMIDIUM TEMPORIS] Quod hic habemus Chaldaice, idem habe- mus Hebraice infra 12, 7. Tempora, χρόνοι, per excellentiam anni, ut supra 4, 29. & apud Græcos sæpe. Josephus de Bel- lo Judaico l. 1. cap. 1. de Antiocho agens: ᾗ ναὸν ἐσύλησε κ̓ τὸ ἐνδελεχισμὸν τῶν καθʼ ἡμέραν ἐναγιασμῶν ἔπαυσεν ἐπʼ ἔτη τρία κ̓ μῆνας ἕξ. Paulo plus fuit, id est, dies mille ducenti no- naginta, ut habebimus infra 12, 11. mille ducentos nonagin- ta sex dixit Josephus 9, 12. ἔτη τρία κ̓ ἥμισυ κ̓ μικρόν τι πρός, ait Chrysostomus: sed illud supercrescens insuper habetur ad rotundandum numerum. Apocalypfis in historia huic typo respondente dixit dies mille ducentos & sexaginta, 11, 6. & alibi menses 42. c. 11, 2. & 13, 5. Modicum nec Prætor curat, nec Propheta. Putatur autem hoc tempus ab ur- be capta, & interdictis ritibus; nam ex quo Idolum fuerat collocatum, erant tres tantum anni. Ita Josephus, & 2. Macc. 10, 5. Item 1. Macc. 1, 62. collato loco ejusdem libri 4, 52. Unde apparet dicto loco 2. Macc. 10. comma- te 3. pro διετῆ legendum τριετῆ.

Arripit hæc Grotius ad Antiochum. Sed te- mere, uti hactenus demonstratum. Nunc in calcu- lum etiam Prophetæ minus æquus est, ac si Prophe- ta modicum non curet. Quemadmodum id vulgo de Prætore dicitur. At Propheta noster accuratus omnino est in designando tempore. Cum de An- tiochi prophanatione agit cap. 8, 18. numerat dies bis mille, trecentos, qui annos sex efficiunt, quibus Sacerdotium prophanatum esse, ibidem Grotius ipse agnovit. Quos vero ex hac præsenti temporis & temporum, & dimidii temporis designatione exscul- pere non poterit. Nam etiamsi per tempus annum, per tempora biennium, per dimidium temporis semestre intelligamus, prodeunt tantum tres cum dimidio anni. Neque facit huc locus c. 12, 11. Nam nec ibi triennium cum dimidio designatur, sed dies 1290. exprimuntur, & communes dies intelligen- dos ibi esse, haud apparet. Neque enim additur περίφρασις illa, qua spatium νυχθημέρων desi- gnavit Propheta c. 8, 14. Dies hoc modo definiens, usq; ad vesperam & mane; frustra ergo hæc confe- runtur, ceu παράλληλα.

Judai- smi enim substantia est ἡ μονοθεία; Cætera accessoria. Vide quæ supra dicta ad v. 18. CUJUS REGNUM REGNUM SEMPITERNUM EST] Nam & nunc durat. Vide supra 4, 33. 5, 6. 10. VERBUM AUTEM IN CORDE MEO CON- SERVAVI] Nempe ut ea accurate perscriberem, & re- linquerem posteris ingens documentum divinæ providen- tiæ, præscientiæque.

## 8:1 Argument
VISION II. CHAPTER VIII.

The vision of Daniel of two horns and one he-goat with a great horn, which overcame the ram, as well as of four horns, from which a little horn grew up, devastating the Sanctuary, the time of which is defined: And the exposition made by Gabriel, that the ram designates the Kings of the Medes and Persians, but the he-goat the Greeks: and the great horn the first of their Kings, upon whose breaking four kingdoms were to arise: but the little horn the impudent, fraudulent, and proud Tyrant, who shall be crushed without hand.

HENCE the Hebrew discourse begins again, because the things that follow pertain directly to the Hebrews, whereas those that preceded were sufficient to instruct the Chaldeans. And so, with the affairs of the Chaldeans now passed, he deals only with the empires and affairs that were to exist after the ruin of the Chaldean empire. Moreover, God shows the same things to Daniel quite often. First, so that those things might stick more firmly in his mind, for which reason teachers also often repeat among their students those things which they judge to be of the greatest use: then, because he learns those things little by little, as it were more distinctly, with their circumstances. Which it appears God also did in other Prophets.

THE same things are not presented here as in the preceding chapter. For those pertained to the whole world and concerned all four Monarchies, up to the final Judgment. But the things that follow in this chapter concern primarily the Jewish people: What their lot would be before the Roman empire and the coming of the Messiah, under the third Monarchy, so that they might not despair in such great calamities concerning the promises made about the Messiah, as the blessed Luther rightly observed in the preface to this Prophet.

Vers. 1.

IN THE THIRD YEAR OF THE REIGN OF BELSHAZZAR] Of Laborosoardoch, as we said above.

Indeed to Nabonidus, as we previously warned, inasmuch as he was the last King in this Monarchy.

Verse of the same.

A VISION APPEARED TO ME] Not now according to rest; but ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ (in a vision), which is considered a more perfect degree of revelation.

Whether the images were presented to the senses, or indeed only to the mind, can there be any doubt? Concerning which see Mr. Dr. Geier.

AFTER THAT WHICH I HAD SEEN IN THE BEGINNING] Namely, of the reign of the same king; above 7, 1.

Latin:

VISIO II. CAPUT VIII.

Visio Danielis duorum cornuum & hirci u- nius cum magno cornu, qui devicit arietem, nec non quatuor cornuum, è quibus cornu parvum enatum devastans Sanstuarium, cujus tempus definitur: Et expositio a Gabriele facta, quod aries Reges Me- dorum & Persarum designet, hircus au- tem Græcorum: & magnum cornu pri- mum eorum Regem, quo fracto exoritura quatuor sint regna: parvum autem cor- nu Tyrannum :impudentem, fraudulentum & superbum, qui sine manu conteretur.

HINC rursus incipit sermo Hebræus, quia quæ se- quuntur, ad Hebræos directè pertinent, cum ea, quæ præ- cesserunt, sufficerent ad Chaldæos instruendos. Itaque præteritis jam rebus Chaldæorum, tantum de imperiis & rebus agit post ruinam Chaldaici imperii exstituris, Sæpius autem res easdem Deus ostendit Danieli. Primum quo eæ res hærerent animo firmius, quam ob causam & magi- stri apud discipulos ea sæpe repetunt, quæ maximi usus esse existimant: deinde quod paulatim res eas cognoscit, velut distinctius, cum suis circumstantiis. Quod Deum & in aliis Prophetis fuisse apparet.

NON hic res eædem exhibentur, quæ præce- denti capite. Nam illa pertinebant ad to- tum orbem, & omnes quatuor Monarchias concer- nebant, usque ad novissimum Judicium. Quæ autem sequuntur hoc capite, concernunt cumpri- mis populum Judaicum: Quæ sors eorum futura ante Romanum imperium, & adventum Messiæ, sub tertia Monarchia, ne desperarent scilicet in tantis calamitatibus de promissionibus de Messia factis, ut rectè observavit B. Lutherus in præfatio- ne hujus Prophetæ.

Vers. 1.

ANNO TERTIO REGNI BALTASSAR] Labo- rosoardochi, ut supra diximus.

Imo Nabonidi, quemadmodum antea mo- nuimus, utpote ultimi in hac Monarchia Regis.

Vers. eod.

VISIO APPARUIT MIHI] Non jam secundum quietem; sed ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ, qui gradus revelationis habetur perfectior.

An sensibus objectæ fuerint species, an ve- ro menti solum, dubium esse nequeat? de quo vid. Dn. D. Geierus.

POST ID, QUOD VIDERAM IN PRINCI- PIO] Nempe regni ejusdem regis; supra 7, 1.

## 8:2
Verse 2.

WHEN I WAS IN THE CITADEL OF SUSA] For it seems that Daniel, before that highest honor which he attained at the end of Laborosoarchod, had held some office in Susiana: and had returned there after the death of King Laborosoarchod: for he is believed to be buried in Susa. Concerning which matter see the narrative of Benjamin of Tudela. Josephus, however, says that a Baris (that is indeed a tower, as Jerome interprets at the eighth chapter of Hosea) was built by him in the city of Ecbatana in Media, the structure of which was seen as recent in his own age; and that a Jew of the priestly line was in charge of it in honor of Daniel, and that the kings of the Medes and Persians, and later the Parthians, were buried in that place. Jerome, however, places that same tower at this location, not in Ecbatana, but in Susa, perhaps by a lapse of memory.

These things concerning the burial of Daniel are uncertain. And that Daniel was not in Susa in real presence when he had this vision is beyond doubt. Aben Ezra, Theodoret, Vatablus, Calvin, Polanus, the Belgians, Cornelius à Lapide, Sanctius, Fernandus, and others hold that Daniel was there only in imaginary presence, just as Ezekiel is said to have been in Jerusalem, chapter 12, 3, and chapter 40, 2. In which manner also Mr. Svaningius says that, while he remained in body in Chaldea, he seemed to himself in dreams to have been in Susa: And Sanctius notes that this was done because Susa was, as it were, a certain symbol and compendium of Persia and the whole empire, and there it could most conveniently be fought over by the Greeks and Persians for the supremacy of the empire with arms, inasmuch as it was an invincible citadel and the bulwark of the whole kingdom. Whence Alexander celebrated great triumphs when this city was captured, as Curtius testifies in book 5. Josephus, however, in book 10, chapter 14, reports that Daniel was indeed at that time in the metropolis of Persia. But the former opinion is more like the truth; especially because in verse 27 it is said that Daniel, having seen this vision, fell into ill health, and from the time he had recovered, he immediately returned to the King's business: which he certainly conducted in the Chaldean court, not in Susa. Nor

The Vulgate rendered the words of the Hebrew text well enough: I saw in my vision, when I was in the castle of Susa: whereas the Hebrew words are thus: I saw however in a vision, and it came to pass, as I was seeing, that I was in the royal Susa: which relate more to an imaginary presence. The word בירה, because it is used of the temple in 1 Chron. 29, 1. 19. Nehem. 2, 8. chap. 7, 2. built magnificently in honor of God, is more correctly taken here as the royal residence and magnificent palace of the Persian Emperors, than as a castle or fortress: for the Temple was certainly not a castle.

Verse of the same.

WHICH IS IN THE REGION OF ELAM] Susiana, although it was a satrapy by itself (as others show, and Curtius book 5), is nevertheless usually reckoned to Persia. The Hebrews call Persia עילם, as in Is. 21, 2. and elsewhere. For which reason Benjamin of Tudela also places Susa in the land of Elam. Pliny 5, 27. Below the Eulæus, Elymais is on the coast joined to Persia. Josephus 1, 7 calls the Ἐλυμαίους the leaders of the Persians. UPON THE GATE OF ULAI] Certain Greeks retained Οὐβὰλ, and Chrysostom cites it thus in his 2nd against the Jews. Symmachus translates it as a stream, from the Hebrew יבל Is. 30, 25. and 44, 4. But to the Chaldeans אובלא is a gate, as appears in Jonathan on Deut. 28, 52. and more than once in the Talmudic writings. Daniel, however, although speaking in Hebrew, keeps the names of places used by the Chaldeans. Gates are accustomed to take their name from rivers. Ulai is the Eulæus to Strabo, Pliny, and Ptolemy. Concerning it, Pliny 6, 27. The river Eulæus separates Susiana from Elymais, having risen in the Medes, and having been hidden in tunnels for a middle space and having emerged again through Mesobatene, it flows around the citadel of Susa. Its water was believed to be of such healthfulness that the kings of the Persians would drink no other, and would have it brought to them in distant places. Josephus says this vision happened to Daniel in a field, namely outside the river gate.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CUM ESSEM IN SUSIS CASTRO] Videtur e- nim Daniel ante summum illum honorem, quem conse- cutus fuit fine Laborosoardochi, munus aliquod habuisse in Susiane: atque eo rediisse post regis Laborosoardochi mortem: creditur enim Susis sepultus. Qua de re vide nar- rationem Benjamini Tudelensis. Josephus autem in Ecba- tanis Mediæ urbe structam ab eo ait Barin, (id vero est tur- rim, ut ad octavum Oseæ interpretatur Hieronymus) cu- jus structura ad suam ætatem recens visa fuerit; eique in Danielis honorem præfuisse Judæum è Sacerdotum gene- re, eoque in loco sepultos Medorum ac Persarum, & post Parthorum reges. Hieronymus vero ad hunc locum tur- rim eandem ponit, non Ecbatanis, sed Susis, errore forte memoriæ.

Incerta hæc sunt de sepultura Danielis. Neque in Susan fuisse reali præsentia Danielem, cum hoc visum haberet, extra dubium est. Imaginaria tan- tum præsentia fuisse illic Danielem Aben-Esdra, Theodoret. Vatablus, Calvinus, Polanus, Belgæ, Cor- nelius à Lapide, Sanctius, Fernandus, & alii volunt, uti Ezechiel Hierosolymis fuisse dicitur cap. 12, 3. cap. 40, 2. quo pacto etiam Dn. Svaningius ait, quod corpore Chaldææ commoratus in somniis visus sibi sit Susis fuisse: Idq; ideo factum notat Sanctius, quod Susan Persidos & totius imperii veluti Symbo- lum quoddam atq; compendium fuerit, ibiq; commo- dissime à Græcis & Persis, de summa imperii armis decertari potuerit, utpote ubi arx invicta, & to- tius regni propugnaculum erat. Unde triumphos magnos egit Alexander, cum urbs hæc capta esset, teste Curtio lib. 5. Josephus tamen lib. 10. cap. 14. revera tum in Metropoli Persidis Danielem fuisse refert. Sed prior sententia vero est similior; im- primis quia v. 27. Daniel conspecta hac visione in adversam incidisse valetudinem, & ex quo conva- luisset statim ad negotia Regis rediisse dicitur: quæ utique in Chaldaica aula gessit, non in Susan. Neq;

commode satis vulgata reddidit verba textus E- bræi: Vidi in visione mea, cum essem in Susan Ca- stro: quum ita sese Ebræa habeant: Vidi autem in visione, & factum est, vidente me, ut essem in Susan Regia: quæ magis respiciunt imaginariam præsen- tiam. Vox בירה, quia de templo adhibetur 1. Par. 29, 1. 19. Nehem. 2, 8. cap. 7, 2. in honorem Dei magnifice exstructo, rectius hic de regia & pala- tio magnifico Imperatorum Persicorum accipitur, quam de castro, vel propugnaculo: Templum enim castrum certe non fuit.

Vers. eod.
