QUOD EST IN ELAM REGIONE] Susiane, quanquam satrapia per se fuit, (ut ostendunt & alii, & Curtius lib. 5.) Persidi tamen accenseri solet. Persidem autem עילם Hebræi vocant, ut Es. 21, 2. & alibi. Qua de causa etiam Benjamin Tudilensis Susa ponit in terra E- lam. Plinius 5, 27. Infra Eulæum Elymais est in ora juncta Persidi. Josephus 1, 7. Ἐλυμαίους vocat Περσῶν ἀρχηγέτας. SUPER PORTAM ULAI] Græci quidam Οὐβὰλ retinuêre, & sic citat Chrysostomus 2. adversus Judæos. Symmachus rivum vertit, ex Hebræo יבל Es. 30, 25. & 44, 4. At Chaldæis אובלא est porta, ut apparet in Jonathane Deuter. 28, 52. & in Thalmudicis non semel. Daniel au- tem, quanquam Hebraice loquens, nomina locorum servat Chaldæis usitata. Solent portæ à fluminibus nomen ac- cipere. Ulai est Straboni, Plinio, & Ptolemæo Eulæus. De eo Plinius 6, 27. Susianem ab Elymaide disterminat amnis Eu- læus ortus in Medis, medioq; spatio cuniculis conditus ac rur- sus exortus per Mesobatenen, lapsus circuit arcem Susarum. Aquæ ejus tanta credita salubritas, ut non aliam reges Per- sarum biberent, & eam ad longinqua loca apportari sibi facerent. Josephus hoc visum Danieli ait obtigisse in cam- po, nempe extra portam flumentanam.

## 8:3
Verse 3.

AND BEHOLD, ONE RAM STOOD BEFORE THE MARSH] Before the gate. For here too is אובל, which Jerome also noted. The ram according to the Persians signifies riches, as Achmet testifies 242, 2, namely because of the wool. It is the same thing as the bear before: the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, as is explained below. HAVING EXALTED HORNS] In the Hebrew, which we use, it is the dual form. But Josephus reads it in the plural: for he says κέρατα ὑπεκφυκότα πολλά: and that is more correct. For there were many Kings, who are indicated here by the horns. The Hebrew text is wrongly corrected from Josephus, and Canonical Scripture from a human book. Nor is the dual number used without cause, because by those two horns of the Ram the two kingdoms of the Medes and Persians are signified; and not indeed the Kings succeeding one another in the second Monarchy. In which most Interpreters agree; namely that because of the double kingdom, Median and Persian, the ram is two-horned. It is thus explained by the angel himself in verse 26, where the two horns of the ram are expressed again (although even there Grotius dared, which was a rashness of man, to argue that the text was spurious, and to amend it) and are explained as the Kings of the Medes and Persians. Which sense the following words further confirm.

Verse of the same.

AND ONE HIGHER THAN THE OTHER, AND GROWING UP] Translate: The first was higher than the second, and the one that was being raised up was higher (than that). For Cyrus had gained the greatest wealth for himself, more than his successors. Cyrus (says Pliny) had found 34,000 pounds of gold from conquered Asia; besides golden vessels, and wrought gold, and in it leaves and a plane tree, and a vine. By which victory he brought back 15,000 talents of silver, and the crater of Semiramis, the weight of which amounted to 15 talents. Varro reports that an Egyptian talent amounts to 80 pounds. The last of the Persian kings was Darius Codomannus. He, besides what was in other cities, had 120,000 talents in Persepolis alone: 6,000 in Pasargadae, as Curtius testifies. But Strabo book 15 says that 40, or as others wish, 50,000 talents were found in Persepolis and Susa: It is reported by others that 80,000 talents had been collected in Ecbatana from various places of the Persian empire. 8,000 plundered by those who killed Darius. Truly, amazing wealth.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET ECCE, ARIES UNUS STABAT ANTE PALUDEM] Ante portam. Est enim & hic אובל quod & Hieronymus notavit. Aries secundum Persas divitias significat, teste Achmete 242, 2. nempe ob lanam. Idem argo quod ante ursus: regnum Medorum & Persarum, ut infra explicatur. HABENS CORNUA EXCELSA] In Hebræo, quo nos utimur, est forma dualis. At Josephus pluraliter legit: ait enim κέρατα ὑπεκφυκότα πολλά: & id rectius. Multi enim Reges fuere, qui hic per cornua indicantur. Perperam corrigitur Ebræus textus è Jose- pho, Scriptura Canonica è libro humano. Nec sine causa dualis numerus adhibitus est, quia per duo illa Arietis cornua regna duo Medorum & Per- sarum significantur; non vero Reges in secunda Monarchia sibi succedentes. In quo plerique Interpretes conveniunt; quod nempe ob gemi- num regnum Medicum, & Persicum, aries bicor- nis sit. Ita exponitur ab ipso angelo vers. 26. ubi duo cornua arietis iterum expressa sunt (etsi & ibi ausit Grotius, quæ hominis fuit temeritas, textum νοθείας arguere, atque emendare) & explicata sunt de Regibus Medorum atque Persarum. Quem sen- sum porro confirmant etiam verba sequentia.

Vers. eod.

ET UNUM EXCELSIUS ALTERO, ATQUE SUCCRESCENS] Verte: Primum celsius erat secundo, & excelsus (illo) id quod attollebatur. Nam primum Cyrus ma- ximas sibi opes pepererat, plus quam succeffores. Cyrus de victa Asia (ait Plinius) pondo 34. millia invenerat; præter vasa aurea, aurumque factum, & in eo folia ac platanum, vitem- que. Qua victoria argenti IↃ. millia talentorum reportavit, & craterem Semiramidis, cujus pondus 15. talentorum collige- bat. Talentum autem Ægyptium pondo 80. patere Varro tra- dit. Postremus regum Persarum fuit Darius Codomannus. Is præter quod in aliis urbibus fuit, in sola Persepoli ha- buit 120. millia talentorum: Persagadis sex millia, Cur- tio teste. At Strabo lib. 15. Persepoli & Susis reperta ait 40. aut ut alii volunt, 50. millia talentorum: Ab aliis tra- di Ecbatanis fuisse comportata ex variis imperii Persici lo- cis 80. millia talentorum. 8. millia direpta ab iis, qui Darium occiderunt. Opes sane mirandas.

## 8:4
Verse 4.

I SAW THE RAM PUSHING WITH ITS HORNS TOWARD THE WEST] For the Persians under Darius the son of Hystaspes and Xerxes brought war upon Greece,

AND TOWARD THE NORTH ] Darius the same waged war against the Scythians. Herodotus, Justin, and others make mention of it.

AND TOWARD THE SOUTH ] Cambyses invaded Egypt and Ethiopia.

AND ALL THE BEASTS COULD NOT RESIST HIM: NEITHER BE DELIVERED OUT OF HIS HAND: BUT HE DID ACCORDING TO HIS WILL, AND BECAME GREAT ] Namely, Babylon having been captured by the Persians with all its empire, Lydia, Ionia, Asia Minor, Egypt.

Mr. Dr. Geier: By the west, therefore, in this place we understand the islands of the Mediterranean Sea, since most of them obeyed the Persians, as can be seen from the war of Xerxes against the Greeks, of which Theodoret also makes mention; to these very ones we also add Syria, Cappadocia, and Asia Minor. Toward the south, the Persians attacked Egypt, Arabia, India, Ethiopia, and Libya; and finally toward the north, Scythia, the Pontic nations, Lydia, Armenia, the Iberians, Albanians, Colchians, Caspians, etc. The lords of all these provinces were driven out from their stalls and pastures by this ram, so that there was no one who did not submit himself to this spirited invader. Compare Esther 1:1 concerning the hundred and twenty-seven provinces, likewise Daniel 7:5 concerning the three ribs in the mouth of the bear, which some have understood as the three regions of the world.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

VIDI ARIETEM CORNIBUS VENTILAN- TEM CONTRA OCCIDENTEM] Nam Persæ sub Da- rio Hystaspis filio & Xerxe bellum Græciæ intulerunt,

ET CONTRA AQUILONEM ] Darius idem Scythis bellum intulit. Meminere Herodotus, Justinus, & alii.

ET CONTRA MERIDIEM ] Cambyses Ægy- ptum & Æthiopiam invasit.

ET OMNES BESTIÆ NON POTUERUNT RESISTERE EI: NEQUE LIBERARI DE MANU EJUS: FECITQUE SECUNDUM VOLUNTATEM SUAM, ET MANIFICATUS EST ] Nempe capta à Persis Babylon cum omni suo imperio, Lydia, Jonia, A- sia minor, Ægyptus.

Dn. D. Geierus: Per occidentem igitur h. l. intelligimus insulas maris mediterranei,quippe quæ pleræque paruerunt Persis, ut videre est ex Bello Xerxis contra Græcos, cujus meminit etiam Theo- doretus; his ipsis addimus etiam Syriam, Cappa- dociam & Asiam minorem. Meridiem versus Per- sæ oppugnarunt Ægyptum, Arabiam, Indiam, Æthio- piam, & Lybiam; & denique versus Septentrio- nem, Scythiam, gentes Ponticas, Lydiam, Armeniam, Iberos, Albanos, Colchos, Casbios, &c. Omnium harum provinciarum Domini ab hoc ariete è suis vel- ut stabulationibus ac pabulis ejecti sunt, adeo ut nemo non huic se submittere invasori animoso. Confer Esth. 1, 1. de centum viginti & septem provinciis,item Dan. 7, 5. de tribus costis in ore ursi, quas de tribus mundi plagis nonnulli intellexerunt.

## 8:5
Verse 5.

AND I WAS UNDERSTANDING] While I consider these things: and namely marvel at the opulence.

HE-GOAT OF THE GOATS] A he-goat of the goat kind. A he-goat signifies rapacious men in Achmet 242. This he-goat signifies all the Greeks, of whom the Macedonian is a portion. Therefore, this he-goat corresponds both to the belly and the legs of the statue. Likewise to the leopard and the fourth beast.

Grotius says these things τῇ ὑποθέσει δουλεύων [serving his hypothesis]. We deny, however, that the he-goat corresponds to the belly and legs of the statue, and likewise to the leopard and the fourth beast. It corresponds only to the belly, and to the leopard; but we have previously shown that the legs of the statue and the fourth beast pertain to signifying the fourth Monarchy. Grotius followed Porphyry in this, of whom Jerome writes on chapter 7: Porphyry places the two later beasts of the Macedonians and Romans into one kingdom of the Macedonians, and divides it: wishing the leopard to be understood as Alexander himself: but the beast dissimilar to the other four beasts as the successors of Alexander, and then he counts ten kings up to Antiochus Epiphanes by surname, who were most cruel: and he does not place these kings as of one kingdom; for example, of Macedonia, Syria, Asia, and Egypt, but he makes one order of kings out of diverse kingdoms.

Verse the same.

HE WAS COMING FROM THE WEST] With respect to Persia.

UPON THE FACE OF THE WHOLE EARTH] Namely, of Asia.

AND HE WAS NOT TOUCHING THE EARTH] It indicates the swiftness of flight. See above concerning the others 7:6.

HE HAD A NOTABLE HORN BETWEEN HIS EYES] A king no less ingenious than brave, Alexander the Great, who was not only king of Macedonia, which is a good part of Greece, but was also chosen by all of Greece (except the Lacedaemonians) as commander for the war against the Persians. See Justin book 11, Plutarch in his Alexander, and others. Add what is below in verse 21.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET EGO INTELLIGEBAM] Dum ego hæc consi- dero: & opulentiam scilicet miror.

HIRCUS CAPRARUM] Hircus de caprugno ge- nere. Hircus rapaces significat Achmeti 242. Hircus hic omnes Græcos significat, quorum portio Macedonis. Re- spondet ergo hircus hic & ventri & cruribus statuæ. Item pardo & feræ quartæ.

Hæc Grotius τῇ ὑποθέσει δουλεύων. Nega- mus autem hircum & ventri, & cruribus statuæ,item Pardo & Feræ quartæ respondere. Ventri solum respondet, & Pardo; at crura statuæ, & feram quar- tam pertinere ad quartam Monarchiam significan- dam, antea ostendimus. Porphyrium in eo sequu- tus est Grotius,de quo Hieronymus ad c. 7. Por- phyrius duas posteriores bestias Macedonum & Ro- manorum, in uno Macedonum regno ponit, & divi- dit: Pardum volens intelligi ipsum Alexandrum: be- stiam autem dissimilem cæteris bestiis quatuor Ale- xandri successores, & deinde usq; ad Antiochum E- piphanem cognomento decem Reges numerat, qui fue- runt sævissimi: ipsosq; Reges non unius ponit Regni; verbi gratia, Macedoniæ, Syriæ, Asiæ, & Æ- gypti, sed de diversis regnis unum efficit Regum or- dinem.

Vers. eod.

VENIEBAT AB OCCIDENTE] Respectu Persi- dis.

SUPER FACIEM TOTIUS TERRÆ] Nempe A- siæ.

ET NON TANGEBAT TERRAM] Volatus ce- leritatem indicat. Vide supra de aliis 7, 6.

HABEBAT CORNU INSIGNE INTER OCU- LOS SUOS] Regem non minus ingeniosum, quam for- tem, Alexandrum magnum, qui non tantum Macedo- niæ, quæ bona pars Græciæ, rex erat, sed & ab omni Græ- cia (exceptis Lacedæmoniis) belli in Persas lectus impera- tor. Vide Justinum lib. 11. Plutarchum Alexandro & alios. Adde quod infra 21.

## 8:6
Verse 6.

HE RAN AT HIM IN THE FURY OF HIS POWER] This signified the expeditions of the Greeks into Asia: for it concerns the whole goat, not just one of its horns.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

CUCURRIT AD EUM IN IMPETU FORTI- TUDINIS SUÆ] Expeditiones Græcorum in Asiam id si- gnificavit: de toto enim hirco, non de uno tantum e- jus cornu agitur.

## 8:7
Verse 7.

AND BROKE HIS TWO HORNS] First Artaxerxes Mnemon, by sending auxiliaries to his brother Cyrus, among whom was Xenophon: then Darius Codomannus. Horns here are everywhere kings.

AND THE RAM COULD NOT RESIST HIM] The Persian Empire could not resist the Greeks at the Granicus, at Issus, and elsewhere.

Verse of the same.

AND WHEN HE HAD CAST HIM TO THE GROUND] He had clearly defeated him from Arbela. HE TRAMPLED HIM, AND THERE WAS NONE THAT COULD DELIVER THE RAM OUT OF HIS HAND] The whole empire of the Medes and Persians passed to the Greeks.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET COMMINUIT DUO CORNUA EJUS] Prius Artaxerxem Mnemonem, missis ad Cyrum ejus fra- trem auxiliis, in quibus fuit Xenophon: deinde Darium Codomannum, Cornua ubique hic sunt reges.

ET NON POTERAT ARIES RESISTERE EI] Imperium Persicum resistere Græcis non potuit ad Granic- cum, ad Issum, & alibi.

Vers. eod.

CUMQUE EUM MISISSET IN TERRAM] Plane debellasset ab Arbela. CONCULCAVIT, ET NEMO QUIBAT LI- BERARE ARIETEM DE MANU EJUS] Totum im- perium Medorum Persarumque ad Græcos pervenit.

## 8:8
Verse 8.

AND THE HE-GOAT BECAME VERY GREAT] With the addition to that empire of the Hyrcanians, the Paropamisadae, and a part of the Indians. THE GREAT HORN WAS BROKEN] The great Alexander died. AND THERE CAME UP FOUR HORNS UNDER IT TOWARD THE FOUR WINDS OF HEAVEN] Here too he understands those first four leaders, who under the name of the sons and brothers of Alexander, drew the sum of affairs to themselves: Whence afterwards arose kingdoms, both others, and especially those of Syria and Egypt. Those leaders pertain to the brass, these Kings to the iron and clay: Those are the horns of the Leopard: These the fourth beast. The prior error recurs. For the kingdom of Syria and Egypt does not pertain to the iron and clay, or to the fourth beast, but to the brass and to the third beast, or the four-headed and four-winged Leopard, and to the four-horned He-goat. Those four horns of the He-goat, and the four heads of the leopard, do not denote the first four Leaders of Alexander, but the four principal kingdoms; which after the death of Alexander were born from his Empire, such as the Syrian, Egyptian, Macedonian, and Asian, as Daniel himself interprets in chapter 8, 27. Compare Polybius, book 5. Curtius and Justin indeed list more satrapies, according to the number of the leaders, but it is certain that those four were the principal ones, just as Josephus also enumerates only the dynasts of Syria, Egypt, Macedonia, Asia, and the Hellespont as the more powerful, to whom the others joined themselves as they rushed into mutual wars, and thus were gradually consumed. Let us also hear Jerome, who says: The great horn is the first King Alexander himself, who having died in Babylon in the thirty-second year of his age, four of his leaders rose up in his place, who divided the Empire among themselves. For Ptolemy, son of Lagus, held Egypt. Philip, who was also Audaus, brother of Alexander, held the Macedonians; Seleucus Nicanor held Syria and Babylon and all the kingdoms of the east: Antigonus reigned over Asia.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

HIRCUS AUTEM CAPRARUM MAGNUS FACTUS EST NIMIS] Adjectis ad imperium illud Hyr- canis, Paropomisadis, Indorum parte. FRACTUM EST CORNU MAGNUM] Mortuus est magnus Alexander. ET ORTA SUNT QUATUOR CORNUA SUBTER ILLUD IN QUATUOR VENTOS COELI] Etiam hic primos illos quatuor duces intelligit, qui sub no- mine filiorum & fratrum Alexandri, rerum summam ad se traxêre: Unde postea orta sunt regna, tum alia, tum præcipue Syriæ & Ægypti. Illi duces ad æs, hi Reges ad ferrum ac testam pertinent: Illi sunt cornua Pardi: Hi bestia quarta. Recurrit prior error. Regnum enim Syriæ & Ægypti non ad ferrum & testam, aut ad bestiam quartam pertinet, sed ad æs & ad tertiam bestiam, vel Pardum quadricipitem, & τετεράπτερον, & ad Hircum quadricornem. Cornua illa quatuor Hirci, & capita quatuor bardi, non primos quatuor Du- ces Alexandri, sed quatuor regna principalia notant; Quæ post obitum Alexandri enata sunt ex ejus Imperio, utpote Syriacum, Ægyptiacum, Mace- donicum, Asiaticum, interprete ipso Daniele cap. 8, 27. Confer Polyb. lib. 5. Recensent quidem Cur- tius & Justinus plures satrapias, pro ducum scilicet numero, at certum est quatuor illas præcipuas fuis- se, sicut & Josephus tantum Syriæ, Ægypti, Macedo- niæ, Asiæ, Hellesponti Dynastas tanquam potiores e- numerat, quibus in mutua bella ruentibus cæteri se adjunxerunt, atque ita paulatim absumpti fuerunt. Audiamus & Hieronymus, qui, cornu, inquit, grande, ipse est Rex primus Alexander, quo tricesimo secundo ætatis suæ anno mortuo in Babylone, surrexerunt pro eo quatuor duces ejus, qui sibi Imperium diviserunt. Ægyptum enim Ptolemæus Lagi filius tenuit. Ma- cedonas Philippus, qui & Audaus frater Alexandri, Syriam & Babylonem & omnia regna orientis Seleu- cus Nicanor: Asiæ regnavit Antigonus.

## 8:9
Verse 9.

AND OUT OF ONE OF THEM] Of Antiochus the Great. CAME FORTH A LITTLE HORN] Antiochus, at first of modest fortune, a private citizen, and a hostage at Rome: called Epiphanes after the fact. AND IT BECAME GREAT TOWARD THE SOUTH] Against Egypt: for he attacked Ptolemy Philometor. AND TOWARD THE EAST] For he also conquered Armenia. AND TOWARD THE GLORIOUS LAND] In the Hebrew: צבי. It is so called in 2 Sam. 1, 19 and Ezek. 20, 6, 15, namely because it was the most pleasant of lands, Ps. 48, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

DE UNO AUTEM EX EIS] De Antiocho Ma- gno. EGRESSUM EST CORNU UNUM MODI- CUM] Antiochus modicæ primum fortunæ, privatus, & Romæ obses: ex post facto dictus Epiphanes. ET FACTUM EST GRANDE CONTRA ME- RIDJEM] Contra Ægyptum: oppugnavit enim Ptole- mæum Philometora. ET CONTRA ORIENTEM] Nam & Armeniam devicit. ET CONTRA FORTITUDINEM] In Hebræo: צבי. Sic vocatur Judæo 2. Sam. 1, 19. & Ezech. 20, 6. 15. nempe quod amœnissima esset terrarum, Ps. 48, 3.

## 8:10
Verse 10.

AND IT MAGNIFIED ITSELF EVEN TO THE HOST OF HEAVEN] Against the host of heaven. Thus are called the Levites, who kept watch in the temple, serving in their own way the King of heaven. Thus the word צבא is used in Numbers 8, 24, 25. AND CAST DOWN SOME OF THE HOST] Of that host, he cast down some, that is, he led them away from the observance of the law. This is evident in 1 Macc. 4, 42 and 2 Macc. 4, 14. AND OF THE STARS] Of those who were famous by name for their learning. See what was said on Matt. 24, 29. See also below 12, 3. AND TRAMPLED UPON THEM] He profaned them with pagan rites.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET MAGNIFICATUS EST USQUE AD FOR- TITUDINEM COELI] Adversas exercitum cœli. Sic dicun- tur Levitæ, qui in templo excubias agebant, militantes suo modo regi cœlorum. Sic vox צבא usurpatur Numer. 8, 24. 25. ET DEJECIT DE FORTITUDINE] De illo ex- ercitu, quosdam dejecit, id est, abduxit à legis observatio- ne. Patet id 1. Macc. 4, 42. 2. Macc. 4, 14. ET DE STELLIS] De iis, qui eruditionis nomine erant celebres. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 24, 29. Vide & infra 1 2, 3. ET CONCULCAVIT EOS] Profanavit ritibus paganicis.

## 8:11
Verse 11.

AND IT MAGNIFIED ITSELF EVEN TO THE PRINCE OF THE HOST] It exalted itself even against the prince of his host: namely Onias, the high priest, whom he first stripped of his dignity: and he sold the high priesthood for a price, 2 Macc. 4. Jerome, whom most others follow, more correctly understands God by the Prince of the host. The entire passage is worthy of being read here: AND AFTER THEIR KINGDOM Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Seleucus, who was also called Philopator, shall arise. Who, when he had been a hostage at Rome and had seized the Empire by deceit without the knowledge of the Senate, fought against Ptolemy Philometor, that is, against the south and against the Egyptians. And again, fighting towards the East against those who were stirring up new things in Persia, and finally against the Jews: having captured Judea, he entered Jerusalem: and in the temple of God he set up an image of Jupiter Olympius: and he raised his magnificence even to the strength of heaven, that is, the children of Israel, who were guarded by the help of angels: So that he subjected many of the Saints to Idolatry, and trampled them under his feet like the stars of heaven. And so it came to pass that he held both the south and the east, that is, Egypt and Persia, under his empire. And what he says: he was magnified even to the Prince of the strength: this signifies that he was raised up against God, and persecuted His saints, and took away the ἐνδελεχισμὸν, that is, the daily sacrifice, which was offered in the morning and in the evening, and polluted and cast down the place of His sanctification. And this not by his own power, but because of the sins of the people. And so it came to pass that truth was cast down to the ground: And with the worship of Idols flourishing, the religion of God rested.

Verse of the same.

AND HE TOOK AWAY THE DAILY SACRIFICE FROM HIM] He forbade Onias to perform the sacred rites. AND HE CAST DOWN THE PLACE OF HIS SANCTIFICATION] The place of His holiness: that is, he cast down the high Priesthood, that is, he exposed it to contempt, giving it against the law to wicked men, first to Jason, then to Menelaus.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET USQUE AD PRINCIPEM FORTITUDI- NIS MAGNIFICATUM EST] Extulit se etiam contra ex- ercitus ejus principem: Oniam scilicet, sacerdotem maxi- mum, quem primum dignitate exuit: Sacerdotium autem summum pretio vendidit 2. Macc. 4. Per Principem fortitudinis rectius intelligi Deum Hieronymus, quem plerique alii sequun- tur. Locus integer dignus est, qui hic legatur : ET POST REGNUM EORUM consurget Antio- chus Ἐπιφανὴς filius Seleuci, qui & Philopator ap- pellatus est. Qui cum obses fuisset Romæ & nesciente Senatu, per dolum cepisset Imperium, contra Ptole- mæum Philometora dimicavit, hoc est, contra meri- diem & contra Ægyptios. Rursumque ad Orientem contra eos, qui res novas in Perside moliebantur, ad extremum contra Judæos dimicans : capta Judæa in- gressus est Hierosolymam : & in templo Dei simula- crum Jovis Olympii statuit : & usque ad fortitudi- nem cœli, id est, filios Israël, qui angelorum valla- bantur auxilio, erexit magnificentiam suam: Ita ut de Sanctis plurimos Idololatriæ subjiceret, & velut stellas cœli conculcaret pedibus suis. Atque ita factum est, ut & meridiem & orientem, id est, Ægyptum & Persidem suo teneret imperio. Quodque ait : usque ad Principem fortitudinis magnificatus est : hoc signi- ficat, quod erectus sit contra Deum, & sanctos illius persecutus sit, & tulerit ἐνδελεχισμὸν, id est, juge sacri- ficium, quod mane offerebatur & vespere, & polluerit atque dejecerit locum sanctificationis ejus. Et hoc non sua virtute, sed propter peccata populi. Atque ita factum est, ut veritas prosterneretur in terram : Et cultu Idolorum florente, Dei religio conquiesceret.

Vers. eod.

ET AB EO TULIT JUGE SACRIFICIUM] Vetuit Oniam sacra peragere. ET DEJECIT LOCUM SANCTIFICATIONIS EJUS] Locum sanctitatis ejus : id est, summum Sacerdo- tium dejecit, id est, contemtui exposuit, dans illud contra legem hominibus improbis, Jasoni primum, deinde Me- nelao.

## 8:12
Verse 12.

BUT STRENGTH WAS GIVEN TO HIM AGAINST THE DAILY SACRIFICE BECAUSE OF SINS] Better thus: And an army (that is, the garrison of Antiochus) shall be given (shall be imposed upon the city) against the daily (sacrifice) through wickedness. Through the highest contempt of God, Antiochus will impose soldiers upon the city, so that they may inhibit the daily sacrifice, 1 Macc. 1:47. Josephus 12:7. For he forbade them to offer the daily sacrifices which they offered to God according to the law. AND TRUTH SHALL BE CAST DOWN TO THE GROUND] Truth here is the book of the law, as in Malachi 2:6, it shall be trampled everywhere. Josephus: And if any sacred book or law were found, it was destroyed. The writer of 1 Macc. 1:59 says the books of the law were torn and burned. AND HE SHALL ACT, AND SHALL PROSPER] Whatever he does, it will succeed for him: for a time, that is.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ROBUR AUTEM DATUM EST EI CONTRA JUGE SACRIFICIUM PROPTER PECCATA] Melius sic : Et exercitus (id est, præsidium Antiochi) dabitur (im- ponetur urbi) contra juge (sacrificium) per scelus. Per sum- mum Dei contemtum milites urbi imponet Antiochus, ut juge sacrificium inhibeant, 1. Macc. 1, 47. Josephus 12, 7. καὶ γὰρ τὰς καθημερινὰς θυσίας ἃς προσέφερον τῷ Θεῷ κατὰ τὸ νόμον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτὰς προσφέρειν. ET PROSTERNETUR VERITAS IN TERRA] Veritas hic est liber legis, ut Malach. 2, 6. is passim pro- culcabitur. Josephus : ἠφανίζετο δὲ εἴπη βίβλος εὑρεθείη ἱε- ρὰ καὶ νόμος. Libros legis conscissos ustosque dicit scri- ptor 1. Macc. 1, 59. ET FACIET, ET PROSPERABITUR ] Quic- quid agit, ei succedet : ad tempus scilicet.

## 8:13
Verse 13.

AND I HEARD ONE OF THE SAINTS] Of the Angels. The angel of Daniel, the Hebrews say. TO ANOTHER I KNOW NOT WHOM] Τινί ποτε, Symmachus, LXX, Aquila, Theodotion, Clement of the Constitutions 7:36. They retained the Hebrew Φελμωνὶ or Φελμωνί. It is thought to be composed of two names, פלני & אלמוני, which you have in Ruth 4:1 and 2 Kings 6:8; however, it seems to signify not just anyone, but someone eminent. And this Angel must have excelled the others, since he teaches the others.

The opinion of others seems better to B. Gesner in Thes. 80, who wish the name Palmoni to be composed of Pele, which signifies wonderful, and Meneh, which is to count, so that Palmoni is the same as the wonderful divider of times, who in his inscrutable wisdom has the origins and periods of kingdoms in his count. Tremellius renders it, he who has hidden things in his count. And this explanation fits the present place, since this Palmoni enumerates to the inquiring Angel the duration of the tyrannical persecution that would occur under Antiochus. And since the Son of GOD is also called Pele, Wonderful, in Isaiah 9, it is consistent that the same One is predicting future things to the Angel in this place, especially since it belongs to God alone to foreknow and announce the future changes of empires and times, Isaiah 46:10, Matthew 24:36.

Constant. L'Empereur derives it from פלא and מנה, because in Piel it is the same as to appoint, so that it may be noted that he was appointed by God the Father over the Church. It is also interpreted as the Son of God by the ancients Theodoret and Isidore, and among the more recent ones not only by the Weimar Paraphrasts Mr. Dr. Geier and B. Svaningius, but also by the Reformed Junius and the Dutch interpreters, although they do not agree on the meaning of the word, which Svaningius wishes to be formed as it seemed to Grotius, citing it in the opinion of R. Abenezra, R. Saadia, Pagninus, Vatablus, Mercerus, Marc. Marinus, Schindler, Piscator, the Dutch, and explaining it as Anonymous. Whose interpretation in this part pleases here, because he makes the holy one speaking the same as he who is immediately called that anonymous speaker. With the demonstrative He confirming that explanation: For in this way he renders it: And I heard a certain holy one speaking, and he said to another holy one, that anonymous speaker; so that three are not introduced here, but only two persons, a certain holy one speaking, who is also Palmoni (whatever the etymon of that word may be) with the demonstrative ה, and is called THAT speaker, namely the Son of God, and others, or as I would prefer, SOME ONE holy one, namely from the order of holy created angels.

Verse of the same. UNTIL WHEN THE VISION] For how much time those evils will last, which that little horn will bring upon the people of God, shown to Daniel from verse 9.

AND THE DAILY SACRIFICE] Interrupted, of course, which was a great part of those evils.

AND THE SIN OF DESOLATION WHICH HAS BEEN DONE: AND THE SANCTUARY, AND THE STRENGTH SHALL BE TRAMPLED] Translate thus: and that wickedness of desolation (that is, the oppression of the city by the garrisons of Antiochus) which he explained, and the sanctuary, (the Temple) and the army (of God, that is, the Levites) to trampling, through which both the Temple was profaned, and many of the Levites were corrupted.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET AUDIVI UNUM DE SANCTIS] De Ange- lis. Angelum Danielis, ajunt Hebræi. ALTERI NESCIO CUI] Τινί ποτε, Symmachus, LXX. Aquila, Theodotio, Clemens constitutionum 7, 36. retinuêre Hebræum Φελμωνὶ vel Φελμωνί. Compositum id putatur, ex duobus nominibus פלני & אלמוני, quæ habes Ruth. 4, 1. & Reg. 6, 8. videtur autem significari, non qui- vis, sed eximius aliquis. Et hic Angelus necesse est præsti- terit cæteris, cum alios doceat.

Melior B. Gesnero videtur Thes. 80. aliorum sententia, qui nomen Palmoni compositum esse volunt ex Pele, quod mirabilem significat, & Me- neh quod numerare est, ut Palmoni idem sit, quod mirabilis temporum partitor, qui inscrutabili sua sapientia ortus, & periodos regnorum in numera- to habet. Tremellius reddit, illum qui occulta in numerato habet. Atque hæc explicatio præsenti loco convenit, quandoquidem iste Palmoni Ange- lo sciscitanti durationem tyrannicæ persecutionis, sub Antiocho futuræ, eandem enumerat. Et cum Filius DEI Es. 9. quoque vocetur Pele, Mirabilis, consentaneum est, eundem hoc loco futura Ange- lo prædicere, præsertim cum solius Dei sit, futu- ras imperiorum, temporumque mutationes præ- scire, & prænunciare Es. 46, 10. Matth. 24, 36.

Constant. L'Empereur à פלא & מנה deducit, quod in Piel idem sit ac præficere, ut notetur eum à Deo Patre Ecclesiæ præfectum esse. De filio Dei etiam interpretatur è veteribus Theodor. & Isidorus, è re- centioribus non solum Vinarienses Paraphrastæ Dn. D. Geierus, B. Svaningius, sed etiam è Refor- matis Junius & Belgici interpretes, etsi de vocis si- gnificatu non conveniant, quam ita conflatam, ut Grotio visum, vult Svaningius, allegans eam in sen- tentiam R. Abenezra, R. Saadiam, Pagninum, Va- tablum, Mercerum, Marc. Marinum, Schindle- rum, Piscatorem, Belgas, & exponens Ἀνώνυμον. Cujus ea in parte hic placet interpretatio, quod sanctum loquentem eundem faciat, qui statim voca- tur anonymus ille loquens. He demonstrativo illam explicationem confirmante: Hoc enim modo red- dit: Et audivi quendam sanctum loquentem, & dixit a- lis sancto anonymo illi loquenti; ut ita non tres hic in- troducantur, sed duæ tantum personæ, Sanctus qui- dam loquens, qui & Palmoni (quæcunq; tandem vo- cis illius sit etymon) cum ה demonstrativo, & המנכו ILLE loquens dicitur, Filius nempe Dei, & alias, vel quod malim UNUS aliquis sanctus, nem- pe ex angelorum creatorum sanctorum ordine.

Vers. eod. USQUE QUO VISIO] In quantum tem- pus durabunt mala ista, quæ inferet populo Dei cornu il- lud exiguum, ostensa Danieli à commate 9.

ET JUGE SACRIFICIUM] Interruptum scilicet, quæ pars magna erat istorum malorum.

ET PECCATUM DESOLATIONIS QUÆ FA- CTA EST: ET SANCTUARIUM, ET FORTITUDO CONCULCABITUR] Sic verte: & scelus illud vastatio- nis (id est, oppressio urbis per præsidia Antiochi) quod exposuit, & sanctuarium, (Templum) & exercitum (Dei scilicet, id est, Levitas) conculcationi, Per quod & Tem- plum profanatum est, & multi Levitarum corrupti.

## 8:14
Verse 14. AND HE SAID TO HIM, UNTIL THE EVENING THE MORNING] That is, until the nycthemera. For the Hebrews, since they have hardly any compound words, are forced to use a circumlocution. See Gen. 1, v. 5 and the following, and what was said on Matt. 12, 40.

TWO THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED DAYS] Two thousand and three hundred. This time, of about six years, begins from the first arrival of Antiochus in Judea, when the priesthood was profaned, and it includes his second arrival, the forbidden rites, then the placement of the idol in the temple, and the whole time of the interrupted daily Sacrifice.

AND THE SANCTUARY SHALL BE CLEANSED] That is, that space of time having elapsed, from the first arrival of Antiochus, the temple will be purified, an enkainismos will take place, about which see 1 Macc. 4, Josephus 12, 10, and what we said on John 10, 22. Note that צדק is often used for to cleanse.

Regarding this time, B. Gesnerus has it thus: 2300 days make six years, three months and twenty days, which space exactly agrees with the history of Antiochus. For he, having been driven from Egypt by C. Popilius, first came to Jerusalem in the year 143 of the Greek Empire, as it is written in 1 Macc. 1, 21, and he plundered the temple and abrogated divine worship and the Biblical books, in the same place v. 51. But he died in Babylon in the year 149 of the Greek Monarchy, as is noted in 1 Macc. 6, 16, which year falls in the year 3840 from the creation of the world. And it is 161 before the birth of Christ. Thus, in this six-year period, the Jews were freed from the cruelty of the most monstrous enemy.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET DIXIT EI, USQUE AD VESPE- RAM EO MANE] Id est, usque ad νυχθήμερα. Nam Hebræi, cum compositas voces vix ullas habeant, cogun- tur uti circumlocutione. Vide Gen. 1. v. 5. & sequenti- bus, & quæ dicta ad Matth. 12, 40.

DIES DUO MILLE TRECENTI] Bis mille & trecenti. Hoc tempus, sex circiter annorum, incipit à priori adventu Antiochi in Judæam, cum sacerdotium pro- fanatum est, comprehenditque secundum ejus adventum, interdictos ritus, deinde idoli collocationem in templo, & totum tempus interrupti jugis Sacrificii.

ET MUNDABITUR SANCTUARIUM] Id est, illo spatio temporis exacto, à primo Antiochi adventu, repurgabitur templum, fiet ἐγκαινισμός, de quo vide 1. Macc. 4. Joseph. 12, 10. & quæ diximus Joh. 10, 22. Nota צדק sæpe poni pro mundare.

De hoc tempore ita habet B. Gesnerus: Dies 2300. efficiunt annos sex, tres menses & viginti dies, quod spatium exactè cum historia Antiochi convenit. Ille enim per C. Popilium ex Ægypto pulsus Hieroso- lymam primum venit anno Imperii Græcorum 143. ut scriptum est 1. Macc. 1, 21. templumque spoliavit & divinum cultum librosq́, Biblicos abrogavit, ibidem v. 51. Mortuus autem est Babyloni Ann. 149. Mo- narchiæ Græcorum, ut annotatum extat 1. Macc. 6, 16. qui annus incidit in annum à mundo condito 3840. Estque ante Christum natum 161. Hoc i- taque sexennali tempore ab immanissimi hostis crudelitate Judæi liberati sunt.

## 8:15
Verse 15. WHEN I SAW] I had seen.

AND I SOUGHT UNDERSTANDING] A fuller explanation.

AS THE APPEARANCE OF A MAN] For angels are accustomed to appear in the form of men, because among those things which are visible to us, there is nothing that approaches closer to them. The Hebrews believe that this Angel was Michael, the Prince of the Angels: and certainly it is credible, since he also commands Gabriel, the messenger of the greatest matters.

All these things are Rabbinico-Papistical concerning Michael the Prince of the angels, commanding Gabriel, the Leader or President of the Hebrew people: of which Scripture knows nothing. However, our people conclude from a comparison of several passages that Michael the Prince of the host of the Lord is the Son of God: see especially Rev. 12. And indeed, it has seemed to some that this man, who appeared here, is the same one who is described at length as having been seen again by the Prophet in Dan. 10:5; that he was indeed Christ is by no means obscure from a comparison of Rev. 1:13 seqq. To this also contribute those things observed at v. 13 from Gesner. Finally, there is added to these the fact that the angel Gabriel reveres this man and renders obedience to him, nay, even learns future things from him: if indeed he is, according to Grotius, that same one whose voice is said to have been heard between the Ulai v. 16, who is also called by the name אדש and was seen as the form of a man. Which again the blessed Gesner rightly observed in Thes. p. 101. & 102. Let the incomparable difference between Christ and the holy angels be noted here. For the angel adores the Son of God, who is called Palmoni, and from him, as the substantial wisdom of the eternal Father (Prov. 8), who is also called the Counselor of God and wonderful (Isa. 9), he inquires about the oracle concerning the persecution that was to spread against the Jewish people. Hence Ps. 97 is written: Let all his angels adore him, and Heb. 1:4: Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they. But that the Prophet says there was as it were the image of a man, that is WITHOUT DOUBT for the reason that the Son of God was not yet incarnate, but appeared to the holy Fathers and Prophets in the form of a human body, which for his wonderful wisdom he adapted to himself for a time; whence he adds concerning the same in th. 205 that there is NO DOUBT at all that this man IS NONE OTHER than the Son of God, who in the preceding was called Palmoni. And thus also Theodoret and Isidore, as well as Osiander and the Vinarie Paraphrasts, nay even Calvin himself, understood the Son of God through this man. Although indeed Dr. Svapingius prefers here with the Hebrews to understand Gabriel, seen in human form, to whom afterwards a command is given to explain the vision, he does not, however, make that man whose voice was heard any created angel, but the Son of God himself: and it seems that at verse 16 the voice of that same one was heard, who unexpectedly at v. 15 was seen by Daniel in the form of a man, whom he indicates to have spoken with a human voice, that is, which could be perceived and understood by men: so that consequently the address was made to him who at v. 13 is called by the general name HOLY, but here is expressed by his own name, GABRIEL, to whom it is commanded, explain the vision. Thus the same ones are introduced conversing in this place v. 15, 16, specifically designated, who had been introduced at v. 13 by more general names, because indeed that holy one was Gabriel; but that Palmoni, commanding Gabriel, was seen in the form of a man, and thus the Son of God was at some time to assume human form or nature.

Latin:

Vers. 15. CUM VIDEREM] Vidissem.

ET QUÆREREM INTELLIGENTIAM] Expli- cationem pleniorem.

QUASI SPECIES VIRI] Angeli enim hominum specie solent apparere, quia inter ea, quæ nobis conspicua sunt, nihil est, quod ad illos propius accedat. Hunc An- gelum fuisse Michaelem Principem Angelorum, credunt Hebræi: & certe credibile id est, quando & Gabrieli rerum semper maximarum nuntio imperat.

Omnia ista sunt Rabinico-Papistica de Mi- chaele Principe angelorum, imperante Gabrieli, Duce vel Præside populi Ebraici: De quibus scri- ptura nihil novit. Michaëlem autem Principem esse exercitus Domini esse Filium DEI ex collatione locorum nonnullorum Nostrates colligunt: vide imprimis Apoc. 12. Et virum sane istum, qui hic apparuit, eundem esse, qui Dan. 10, 5. Prophetæ iterum visus prolixe describitur, nonnullis visum; quem vero fuisse Christum, e collatione Apoc. 1, 13. seqq. minime obscurum est. Quo faciunt etiam, quæ ad v. 13. observata e Gesnero. Denique ac- cedit his, quod angelus Gabriel hunc virum ve- neretur, eique obsequium præstet, imo ab eo di- scat res futuras: Siquidem is secundum Grotium idem ille sit, cujus vox inter Ulai v. 16. audita di- citur, qui & nomine אדש vocetur & conspectus fuerit tanquam forma viri. Quod iterum B. Ges- nerus recte observavit Thes. p. 101. & 102. Notetur hic incomparabile discrimen inter Christum, & san- ctos angelos. Nam angelus Filium DEI, qui Palmoni dicitur, adorat, & ex illo, tanquam substantiali sa- pientia æterni Patris Prov. 8. qui etiam Consiliarius Dei, & admirabilis vocatur Esa. 9. oraculum de per- secutione in Judaicum populum grassatura sciscitatur. Hinc Pf. 97. scriptum est: Adorent eum omnes Ange- li, & Ebr. 1, 4. Tanto melior factus est angelis, quan- to præstantius præ illis nomen hæreditario jure acce- pit. Quod autem Propheta ait fuisse tanquam ima- ginem viri, id PROCUL DUBIO eam fit ob causam, quod Filius Dei tunc nondum fuit incarnatus, appa- ruit autem S. Patribus, & Prophetis in humani cor- poris forma, quam pro admirabili sua sapientia sibi ipsi ad tempus adaptavit; unde de eodem addit th. 205. virum istum NON ESSE ALIUM quam Fi- lium Dei, qui in præcedentibus fuit appellatus Pal- moni, NULLUM omnino dubium est. Atque ita per virum istum Filium Dei intellexere etiam Theodoretus & Isidorus, ut & Osiander, ac Paraphr. Vinarienses, imo etiam Calvinus ipse. Quanquam vero Dn. D. Svapingius cum Ebræis hic malit Ga- brielem intelligere, forma humana visum, cui post- modum mandatum datur, ut visionem explicet, vi- rum tamen illum, cujus vox audita est, non ange- lum aliquem creatum facit, sed ipsummet Filium Dei: & videtur vers. 16. ejusdem illius vox audita, qui ἀπροσδοκήτως v. 15. in forma viri Danieli vi- sus est, quem humana voce loquutum fuisse, indi- cat, hoc est, quæ ab hominibus percipi & intelligi potuerit: ut proinde alloquium factum sit ad e- um, qui v. 13. generali voce SANCTUS nuncupa- tur, hic vero nomine suo exprimitur, GABRIEL, cui mandatur, expone visionem. Ita iidem collo- quentes introducuntur hoc loco v. 15. 16. speciatim designati, qui v. 13. generalioribus nominibus intro- ducti erant, quod nempe sanctus ille fuerit Gabriel; Palmoni vero ille Gabrieli impèrans in forma viri conspectus sit, adeoque Filius Dei fuerit aliquan- do humanam assumturus formam, vel naturam.

## 8:16
Vers. 16.

I HEARD A MAN'S VOICE BETWEEN THE ULAI] Between me and the river Eulaeus. GABRIEL MAKE THIS VISION UNDERSTAND] Just as some prince of a royal council gives commands to legates. Make understand: that is, explain more openly, if there is anything that he does not fully perceive.

Thus, therefore, the man who commands Gabriel to explain the vision to Daniel has authority and power over Gabriel: the circumstances teach that this man is the Son of God himself, who also appeared in the form of a man in chapter 10, v. 5. But because he commands Gabriel as a minister, it is to be held as a mere fiction that Mr. Christian Ravius in his new Chronology repeatedly asserts that Gabriel is the Holy Spirit: which, although I refuted in the solid discussion of the infallible new Ravian Chronology, the author nevertheless in letters sent to me on the 21st of September in the year 1670 still did not hesitate to defend, as if it were consistent with the Scripture of the Old and New Testament. But where it is taught, either in the Old or in the New Testament, that the Holy Spirit is Gabriel, neither can I find, nor has any theologian, whether ancient or modern, found to this very day. Moreover, it is certain that this is repugnant to the Holy Scriptures; nor has it been doubted by anyone that Gabriel is a created angel: because he is always introduced as a minister, as here, and ch. 9, 21, and also Luke 1, 19, where Gabriel speaks thus: 'I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and was sent to speak to you,' which refer to an angel standing before God and ministering to Him, and sent by God, but which in no way befit the Holy Spirit: in which manner also the angel Gabriel is introduced as a minister sent from heaven by God to the virgin Mary, v. 26, and he speaks of the Holy Spirit as a divine person, v. 35. 'The Holy Spirit,' he says, 'will come upon you,' not indeed, 'I will come upon you.' And who would admit one saying that the angel Gabriel came upon Mary, and that by that union she was rendered fruitful? But enough of this absurd invention.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

AUDIVI VOCEM VIRI INTER ULAI] Inter me & flumen Eulæum. GABRIEL FAC INTELLIGERE ISTAM VI- SIONEM] Sicut princeps aliquis consilii Regii dat legatis mandata. Fac intelligere: id est, explica apertius, si quid sit quod non pervideat.

Ita ergo vir, qui mandat Gabrieli, ut visionem Danieli explicet, auctoritatem, ac potestatem, in Gabrielem habet: quem virum ipsummet Filium Dei esse, circumstantiæ docent: qui etiam cap. 10. v. 5. in forma viri apparuit. Quia vero Gabrieli ceu ministro præcipit, pro mero commento haben- dum, quod Dn. Christianus Ravius in nova Chro- nolog. sua Gabrielem esse Spiritum S. dictitat: quod etsi in solida discussione infallibil. novæ Chro- nol. Ravianæ confutarim, autor tamen adhuc in li- teris ad me datis d. 21. Sept. Ann. 1670. tueri non dubitavit, ceu consentaneum Scripturæ Vet. & Nov. Testamenti. At ubi vel in Vet. vel in N. T. tradi- tum sit Spiritum S. esse Gabrielem, nec ego inve- nire possum, nec quisquam seu veterum, seu re- centiorum Theologorum invenit in hunc usque diem. Repugnare autem illud S. literis certum est; neq; dubitatum à quoquam Gabrielem esse ange- lum creatum: quia semper ut minister introduci- tur, utpote hic, & c. 9, 21. nec non Luc. 1, 19. ubi ita infit Gabriel, Ego sum Gabriel, ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σε, quæ Ange- lum coram Deo stantem eig; ministrantem, & à Deo missum referunt, Spiritui autem Sancto nullatenus conveniunt: quo pacto etiam Angelus Gabriel ut minister à Deo cœlitus missus ad Mariam virgi- nem introducitur v. 26. & de Spiritu S. ceu divina persona loquitur v. 35. Spiritui S. inquit superve- niet in te, non vero, Ego superveniam in te; Et quis ad- mittet dicentem, Gabrielem angelum supervenisse in Mariam, eaque ἐπιπλοκῇ eandem fœcundam redditam. Sed satis de inepto isto εὐρήματι.

## 8:17
Vers. 17. HE STOOD NEAR WHERE I WAS STANDING] So that he might be heard better from close by. I FELL TREMBLING UPON MY FACE] Terrified by such great brightness. See what is said at Matt. 17, 6. UNDERSTAND, SON OF MAN] Thus angels call men, so that they may remember they are flesh and blood, and not be puffed up beyond measure by heavenly visions. So Ezek. 2, 2. 3. 6. 8, ch. 3, 1, and elsewhere. FOR AT THE TIME OF THE END THE VISION SHALL BE FULFILLED] To the time (is deferred) the implementation of this vision. Josephus on this prophecy: 'He wrote down many years beforehand the things that were to happen.' It will be fulfilled after almost four hundred years. To this pertains also what is below, 26. Vers. 18. AND AS HE WAS SPEAKING TO ME, I FELL PRONE TO THE EARTH] As before I was terrified by the sight, so now by the hearing of his voice. AND HE TOUCHED ME, AND SET ME IN MY PLACE] By his touch alone he restored my strength. Vers. 19. WHAT SHALL BE IN THE LAST END OF THE INDIGNATION] What is to happen even to the end of the divine wrath: that is, even to the dedication. FOR THE VISION HAS ITS ENDED TIME] Certainly (for) at the appointed time that end will arrive, namely, of the divine wrath. Vers. 20. THE RAM WHICH YOU SAW HAVING HORNS] That horned ram. Even here in the Hebrew it is dual, as above: but it is better, as we said before, that we read it in the plural. All the consonants are the same, whichever way you read it. The vowels have long varied. We have corrected this itch for correcting the Hebrew Truth at verse 3. IS THE KING OF THE MEDES AND PERSIANS] In the Hebrew it is better: The kings are of Media and Persia: that is, the kingdom, as above 7, 16, in the Latin. Vers. 21. FURTHERMORE THE HE-GOAT OF THE GOATS] In the Hebrew: That shaggy he-goat: that is, the intrepid one. See Gen. 25, v. 25. IS THE KING OF THE GREEKS] Here also king is put for kingdom: by a Hebrew idiom which mixes such things. Thus above 7, 16, in the Hebrew. The following things show this. HE IS THE FIRST KING] The first King of the Greeks in Asia, and all these prophecies, written by Daniel in the Hebrew language, which are all directed to Judea, look to nothing else. If one wants an expressed reason in these words for why all these prophecies look to the Jews, because they are written in the Hebrew idiom, that reason is nothing. For many things are written in the Hebrew idiom which do not look to the Hebrews, but to other peoples. But it is also false that all the prophecies set forth by Daniel in the Hebrew language pertain to the Jews. The contrary will be evident from Dan. 11 and 12.

Latin:

Vers. 17. STETIT JUXTA UBI EGO STABAM] Ut de proximo melius exaudiretur. PAVENS CORRUI IN FACIEM MEAM] Tan- to fulgore exterritus. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 17, 6. INTELLIGE FILI HOMINIS] Ita Angeli appel- lant homines, ut se meminerint esse carnem & sanguinem, neque cœlestibus visis supra modum efferantur. Sic E- zech. 2, 2. 3. 6. 8. c. 3, 1. & alibi. QUONIAM IN TEMPORE FINIS COMPLE- BITUR VISIO] Ad tempus (differtur) implementum hujus visi. Josephus de hoc vaticinio, πολλοῖς ἔτεσιν ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέ- γραψε τὰ γενησόμενα. Implebitur annis ferme post qua- dringentis. Huc pertinet & quod infra est 26. Vers. 18. CUMQUE LOQUERETUR AD ME, COLLAPSUS SUM PRONUS IN TERRAM] Ut ante conspectu, ita nunc vocis auditu territus. ET TETIGIT ME, ET STATUIT ME IN GRADU MEO] Solo tactu vires mihi restituit. Vers. 19. QUÆ FUTURA SUNT IN NOVISSIMO MALEDICTIONIS] Quæ eventura sunt ad finem usq; iræ divinæ: id est, usque ad ἐγκαινισμὸν. QUONIAM HABET TEMPUS FINEM SUUM] Certe (enim) ad condictum tempus aderit ille finis, nempe iræ divinæ. Vers. 20. ARIES QUEM VIDISTI HABERE COR- NUA] Aries ille cornifer. Etiam hic in Hebræo est dua- le, ut supra: sed melius ut ante diximus, videtur esse ut legamus pluraliter. Consonantes omnes sunt eædem, u- trovis modo legas. Vocales pridem variant. Hunc pruritum corrigendi Ebraicam Verita- tem castigavimus ad vers. 3. REX MEDORUM EST ATQUE PERSARUM] In Hebræo melius: Reges sunt Mediæ & Persidis: id est, re- gnum, ut supra 7, 16. in Latino. Vers. 21. PORRO HIRCUS CAPRARUM] In He- bræo: Hirsutus ille hircus: id est, intrepidus. Vide Ge- nes. 25. v. 25. REX GRÆCORUM EST] Hic quoq; rex pro re- gno ponitur: Hebraica locutione quæ talia permiscet. Ita supra 7, 16. in Hebræo. Ostendunt id sequentia. IPSE EST REX PRIMUS] Primus Græcorum Rex in Asia, neque alio spectant omnia hæc vaticinia, He- bræo sermone à Daniele scripta, quæ ad Judæam dirigun- tur omnia. Si rationem expressam his verbis velit, cur ad Judæos omnia spectent hæc vaticinia, quia E- bræo Idiomate scripta sunt, ratio illa nulla est. Multa enim Ebræo Idiomate scripta sunt, quæ non ad Ebræos, sed ad alios populos spectant. Sed & falsum est, omnia Ebraico sermone à Daniele ex- posita vaticinia ad Judæos pertinere. Contra- rium è Dan. 11. & 12. capp. constabit.

## 8:22
Vers. 22. FOUR KINGS] In the Hebrew, kingdoms: that is, the powers of leaders. For often the word מלך is taken thus among the Hebrews, as Deut. 33, 5, Jud. 18, 31, ch. 21, 24, 2 Kings 3, 9, and elsewhere. That not only leaders, or the powers of leaders, but as the Hebrew word sounds, kingdoms are indicated, can be evident from those things which we observed at verse 8.

FROM HIS NATION THEY SHALL ARISE] From the Greeks, under whose name the Macedonians also were included from every age, especially.

BUT NOT IN HIS STRENGTH] Not with equal majesty. For he was a king, these were leaders: two of whom assumed the royal name in a smaller empire almost 12 years later.

Latin:

Vers. 22. QUATUOR REGES] In Hebræo, regna: id est, Ducum potentiæ. Nam sæpe vox מלך sic sumitur a- pud Hebræos, ut Deut. 33, 5. Jud. 18, 31. cap. 21, 24. 2 Reg. 3, 9. & alibi. Non tantum Duces, aut Ducum potentias, sed ut verbum Ebræum sonat, regna indigitari, ex iis quæ ad vers. 8. observavimus, patere po- test.

DE GENTE EJUS CONSURGENT] Ex Græ- cis, sub quorum nomine & Macedones vel in primis com- prehensi ab omni ævo.

SED NON IN FORTITUDINE EJUS] Non pari cum majestate. Ille enim rex, hi duces: quorum duo regium nomen, in minore imperio annis ferme post 12. assumsere.

## 8:23
Vers. 23. AND AFTER THEIR KINGDOM] In the Hebrew: And in the progress of their power: when now Seleucus and his posterity for 120 years, or more, had increased their wealth, having also taken the diadem.

WHEN INIQUITIES HAVE INCREASED] The reason why God permitted such great evils is indicated here. You have the exposition in 1 Macc. 1, 12, 2 Macc. 4, Joseph. 12, 6.

A KING SHALL ARISE, IMPUDENT OF FACE] With a hardened countenance: that is, impudent. Deut. 28, Prov. 7, 13, Eccles. 8, 1. Antiochus had no care for piety, none for a true or false God, none for honesty: he measured everything by his own advantage.

AND UNDERSTANDING PROPOSITIONS] Understanding of subtleties. He knew by what means many of the Jews, light and wicked men, could be led away from religion. Such was Julian afterwards, he knew the depths of Satan, as it is in Ap. 2, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET POST REGNUM EORUM] In Hebræo: Et in progressu potentiæ eorum: cum jam Seleu- cus ejusque posteritas per 120. annos, aut amplius, suas opes auxerit, sumpto & diademate.

CUM CREVERINT INIQUITATES] Causa cur Deus tanta mala permiserit hic indicatur. Expositionem habes 1. Macc. 1, 12, 2. Macc. 4. Joseph. 12, 6.

CONSURGET REX IMPUDENS FACIE] Ob- firmato vultu: id autem est, impudens. Deut. 28. Prov. 7, 13. Eccles. 8, 1. Antiocho nulla pietatis, nulla Dei veri aut ficti, nulla honesti cura: cuncta suo ex usu metiebatur.

ET INTELLIGENS PROPOSITIONES] Versu- tiarum intelligens. Sciebat quibus modis Judæorum multi, homines leves & improbi, à religione abduci possent. Talis fuit postea Julianus, ἔγνω τὰ βάθη τῦ Σατανᾶ, ut est Ap. 2, 24.

## 8:24
Verse 24. AND HIS STRENGTH SHALL BE STRENGTHENED] His powers will increase, namely in Judea. For all these things are said for the sake of Judea.

BUT NOT IN HIS OWN STRENGTH] The cause of such great increase will not be so much from him as from the factions of the Jews. See Josephus at the cited place 12, 6.

AND BEYOND WHAT CAN BE BELIEVED HE SHALL LAY WASTE EVERYTHING] He will inflict a wondrous devastation upon Judea.

AND HE SHALL PROSPER AND DO] Whatever he does will succeed for him. As above 12.

AND HE SHALL DESTROY THE MIGHTY] That is, the nobles.

AND THE PEOPLE OF THE SAINTS] Many of the common people who truly revere God. 1 Macc. 1, 52. 60. 61. Joseph. 12, 7. 'But the most approved and noble-souled, did not care for him. And for this reason, being tortured every day and enduring bitter torments, they died.'

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET ROBORABITUR FORTITUDO E- JUS] Vires ejus increscent, nempe in Judæa. Nam Judææ causa omnia hæc dicuntur.

SED NON IN VIRIBUS SUIS] Non tam ex ipso causa erit tanti incrementi, quam ex factionibus Judæo- rum, Vide Josephum dicto loco 12, 6.

ET SUPRA QUAM CREDI POTEST UNI- VERSA VASTABIT] Miram vastitatem inferet Judææ.

ET PROSPERABITUR ET FACIET] Quic- quid aget ei succedet. Vt supra 12.

ET INTERFICIET ROBUSTOS] Id est, proceres.

ET POPULUM SANCTORUM] Multos de ple- be Dei veri reverentes. 1. Macc. 1, 52. 60. 61. Joseph. 12, 7. οἱ δὲ δοκιμώτατοι κὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἐυγενεῖς, ἐκ ἐφρόντισαν ἀυτῦ. κὶ διὰ τῦτο κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν ἀικιζόμενοι κὶ πικρὰς βασάνες ὑποφέροντες, ἀπέθνησκον.

## 8:25
Verse 25. AND DECEIT SHALL BE DIRECTED IN HIS HAND] His craftiness will have success.

AND HE SHALL MAGNIFY HIS HEART] Elated by successes, he will always dare more.

AND IN THE ABUNDANCE OF ALL THINGS] In the Hebrew: And in peace he shall destroy many: with no war, with no injuries against him preceding, he will miserably destroy more day by day. See the history of the mother and the children in Josephus and others.

AND HE SHALL RISE UP AGAINST THE PRINCE OF PRINCES] In the Hebrew: He shall stand against the prince of princes. שרים are called all the princes of the priestly families, as in Ezra 8, 24. 28. ch. 10, 5. The chief of these is the High Priest. Antiochus will subject him to himself. He will remove him at his pleasure, having despised the divine law.

Others more correctly understand God by the Prince of Princes, whom Scripture otherwise calls King of Kings, Lord of Lords, 1 Tim. 6, because He has sovereignty over all the princes of the world, not only by right of creation, but He also distributes the kingdoms of the world by His own authority and at His pleasure, Dan. 2; finally, He can without any trouble defeat and extirpate all tyrants. For when it has been explained what kind of person Epiphanes will show himself to be toward men, it is now indicated what he will be toward God. Whose worship and all sacred things he attempted to abolish.

AND HE SHALL BE BROKEN WITHOUT HAND] By a disease divinely sent. Joseph. 12, 13. 1 Macc. 2, 8. 2 Macc. 9, 5.

Not 1 Macc. 2, 8, but 1 Macc. 6, 16, concerning the death of Antiochus is held, most especially however 2 Macc. 9.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET DIRIGETUR DOLUS IN MANU E- JUS] Astus ejus successum habebunt.

ET COR SUUM MAGNIFICABIT] Successibus elatus plura semper audebit.

ET IN COPIA RERUM OMNIUM] In Hebræo: Et in pace multos perdet: nullo bello, nullis in ipsum inju- riis præcedentibus plures in dies perdet misere. Vide hi- storiam matris & puerorum apud Josephum & alios.

ET CONTRA PRINCIPEM PRINCIPUM CONSURGET] In Hebræo: Stabit super principem princi- pum. שרים dicuntur omnes principes familiarum Sa- cerdotalium, ut Esdr. 8, 24. 28. c. 10, 5. Horum Prin- ceps summus Sacerdos. Hunc sibi subjiciet Antiochus. Di- movebit pro libitu, spreta divina lege.

Rectius alii Deum per principem Principum, quem alias Regem Regum, Dominum Dominorum Scriptura vocat 1. Tim. 6. intelligunt, quia princi- patum habet super omnes principes mundi, non modo creationis jure, sed distribuit etiam regna mundi ἀυτεξεσίως & pro lubitu Dan. 2. denique absque omni negotio universos tyrannos debella- re & extirpare potest. Quum enim expositum fue- rit, qualem se Epiphanes erga homines exhibiturus sit, indicatur nunc, qualis futurus sit in Deum. Cu- jus cultum & sacra omnia abolere conatus est.

ET SINE MANU CONTERETUR] Morbo di- vinitus immisso. Joseph. 12, 13. 1. Macc. 2, 8. 2. Macc. 9, 5.

Non 1. Macc. 2, 8. sed 1. Macc. 6, 16. de mor- te Antiochi habetur, maxime tamen 2. Macc. 9.

## 8:26
Verse 26. AND THE VISION OF THE EVENING AND THE MORNING, WHICH WAS TOLD] That is, an explanation of the vision setting forth the number of days 2300 beyond 14. It is a metonymy.

IT IS TRUE] That is, it has nothing obscure, provided the beginning is taken from where it ought to be, that is, from the things said in verse 9. But here, it is clear, open, as above 2, 45.

BUT YOU THEREFORE SEAL THE VISION] That is, so enclose this vision written down exactly, that the archetype itself may be able to be preserved until the event, and then be compared with the event. Thus Isa. 18, 6. Jer. 32, 14. 35, 32.

FOR IT IS FOR MANY DAYS] Between the vision and the event more than three hundred years will intervene.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET VISIO VESPERE ET MANE, QUÆ DICTA EST] Id est, explicatio visi exponens numerum dierum cIɔ cIɔ CCC supra 14. Est μετωνυμία.

VERA EST] Id est, nihil habet obscuri, modo ini- tium sumatur unde debet, id est, ex dictis commate 9. Verum hic, est clarum, apertum, ut supra 2, 45.

TV ERGO VISIONE SIGNA] Id est, visum hoc exacte perscriptum ita include, ut archetypum ipsum ser- vari possit usque ad eventum, & tunc cum eventu confer- ri. Sic Esa. 18, 6. Ier. 32, 14. 35, 32.

QUIA POST MULTOS DIES ERIT] Inter vi- sum & eventum anni intercedent plus trecenti.

## 8:27
Verse 27. AND I DANIEL LANGUISHED AND WAS SICK FOR SOME DAYS] Sorrowful on account of that profanation of the Priesthood and the Temple.

AND WHEN I HAD RISEN] As soon as my health allowed me to rise.

AND I WAS ASTONISHED AT THE VISION, AND THERE WAS NONE THAT COULD INTERPRET IT] You will translate it best: Although I was stunned by this vision, there was nevertheless no one who knew it. In Greek ἐκ ἧν ὁ συνιών: that is, I was concealing my grief as diligently as I could.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET EGO DANIEL LANGVI ET ÆGRO- TAVI PER DIES ALIQUOT] Mœstus ob illam pro- fanationem Sacerdotii & Templi.

CUMQUE SURREXISSEM] Simulatque per va- letudinem surgere mihi licuit.

ET STUPEBAM AD VISIONEM, ET NON ERAT QUI INTERPRETARETUR] Optime vertes: Quanquam obstupescebam ob hoc visum, nemo tamen erat qui id sciret. Graece ἐκ ἧν ὁ συνιών: id est, quam poteram dili- gentissime dissimulabam dolorem meum.

## 9:1 Argument
SECTION II. VISION UNDER DARIUS. CHAPTER IX.

The prophet, observing the 70 years defined by Jeremiah for the captivity, fasts, and by publishing a confession of sins, prays against the divine wrath, and prays that God may deign to look upon the sanctuary for the Lord's sake, and receives from Gabriel the oracle concerning the LXX Weeks, in which the city itself is to be rebuilt, and Christ is to be cut off to expiate sins, with the typical sacrifices to cease, and the covenant of grace to be confirmed for many in the last week, although the sanctuary is to be destroyed again with the city, and that into perpetual desolation.

Ver. 1.

IN THE FIRST YEAR OF DARIUS] That is, of Nabonnedus, as said above. Porphyry, in order to persuade the ignorant that Daniel lived later, wickedly claims this Darius to be the one by whom the Temple was restored.

Scaliger with his followers, Capellus, Rainoldus, Petavius, and others do indeed make Darius the Mede to be Nabonidus: but against all antiquity, and indeed against Scripture, from which it is certain that Nabonidus was the last monarch of the Chaldeans, Belshazzar; and that this man, his successor, Darius the Mede Ahasuerus, is Cyaxares the son of Astyages, is certain from Xenophon's Cyropaedia, Josephus, Jerome, and other ancients, whom Behmius acknowledges the greater part of chronologers follow, Dec. Chron. Observ. 9. p. 231. See Sect. 6. Quest. 23. in our Biblical Chronology.

SON OF AHASUERUS] That name was common to many in Media.

OF THE SEED OF THE MEDES] The Mede, called by origin in the oracle, and above 5, 31.

Latin:

SECTIO II. VISIO SUB DARIO. CAPUT IX.

Propheta 70. annos à Ieremia captivitati de- finitos observans jejunat, editaǵ confessio- ne peccatorum iram divinam deprecatur, & orat, ut sanctuarium respicere dignetur Deus propter Dominum, atǵ à Gabriele o- raculum de LXX. Septimanis accipit, qui- bus ipsa etiam civitas reaedificanda, & ex- scindendus Christus ad expianda peccata, cessaturis sacrificiis typicis, & confirman- dum multis pactum gratiae, ultima septi- mana, quanquam destruendum iterum cum urbe sit sanctuarium, idǵ in deso- lationem perpetuam.

Vers. 1.

IN ANNO PRIMO DARII] Id est, Nabonnedi, ut supra dictum. Improbe Porphyrius, ut Danielem se- rius vixisse imperitis persuadeat, hanc Darium eum vult esse ab quo Templum est restitutum.

Darium Medum faciunt quidem Scaliger cum Asseclis, Capellus, Rainoldus, Petavius & alii Nabonidum: sed invita tota antiquitate, imo & Scriptura, è qua constat Nabonidum ultimum Chaldaeorum Monarcham Baltasarem esse: hunc autem ejus successorem, Darium Medum Asverum Cyaxarem esse Astyagis filium, è Xenophontis pae- dia, Josepho, Hieronymo & aliis veteribus certum est, quos majorem Chronologorum partem sequi agnoscit Behmius, Dec. Chron. Observ. 9. p. 231. Vid. Sect. 6. Quaest. 23. in Chron. nostr. Biblic.

FILII ASSVERI] Nomen illud multis commune fuit in Media.

DE SEMINE MEDORUM] ὁ Μήδης, ex ortu di- ctus in oraculo, & supra 5, 31.

## 9:2
Ver. 2. IN ONE YEAR] That is, the first, in the Hebrew manner.

I DANIEL UNDERSTOOD BY BOOKS] Jeremiah 25, 11. 12. ch. 29, 10. For there were then in hand copies of the Prophetic books, as also of the Pentateuch, as is evident below 11.

OF DESOLATION] Wasteness: חרבות, is the very word which Jeremiah had used in this matter 7, 3. 22, 5. 25, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ANNO UNO] Id est, primo, more Hebraeo.

EGO DANIEL INTELLEXI IN LIBRIS] Je- remiae 25, 11. 12. c. 29, 10. Erant enim tunc in manibus exempla librorum Propheticorum, ut & Pentateuchi, ut patet infra 11.

DESOLATIONIS] Vastitas: חרבות, est ipsa vox, qua Jeremias in hac re usus fuerat 7, 3. 22, 5. 25, 18.

## 9:3
Ver. 3. AND I SET MY FACE UNTO THE LORD MY GOD, TO SEEK AND TO PRAY] Unto the Lord, that is, towards the temple. As above 6, 10. The return was indeed promised after 70 years. But on this condition, if the exiled Jews would turn themselves to God. Wherefore Daniel does what is his part, and is the author of others doing the same.

It does not appear from the Prophetic passages Jer. 25, 11. 12. ch. 29, 10. that the promise of liberation from the Babylonian captivity was hypothetical, made under that condition, if the exiles should turn themselves to God. Because simply in Jer. ch. 25, he threatens that the people shall serve the King of Babylon for 70 years: simply he promises in ch. 29, 10. that the Lord will visit the people, when the 70 years of captivity are finished. But we do not deny that those things which are subsequently added in v. 14. of ch. 29. of Jeremiah concerning the universal gathering from all peoples have that condition annexed: which promise seems to be distinguished from the very release from the Babylonian captivity on account of the promises.

IN FASTING, SACKCLOTH, AND ASHES] As in grievous mourning, on account of the captivity lasting so long.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET POSUI FACIEM MEAM AD DOMI- NUM DEUM MEUM, ROGARE ET DEPRECARI] Ad Dominum, id est, versus templum. Ut supra 6, 10. Promissus quidem erat reditus post annos 70. Sed ita, si se exules Judaei ad Deum converterent. Quare Daniel quod suarum est partium facit, & idemfaciendi aliis autor est.

Non apparet ex locis Propheticis Jer. 25, 11. 12. c. 29, 10. promissionem liberationis captivitate Ba- bylonica hypotheticam fuisse, factam sub illa con- ditione, si ad Deum se exules converterint. Quia simpliciter Jer. c. 25. minatur, 70. annos populum serviturum Regi Babylonico: simpliciter pro- mittit c. 29, 10. Dominum visitaturum populum, finitis 70. captivitatis annis. Quae vero deinde v. 14. cap. 29. Jeremiae subjunguntur de collectio- ne universali ex omnibus populis, eam annexam habere conditionem, non diffitemur: quae pro- missio distinguenda videtur ab ipsa solutione capti- vitatis Babylonicae propter promissa.

IN JEJUNIIS, SACCO, ET CINERE] Ut in gravi luctu, ob durantem tamdiu captivitatem.

## 9:4
Ver. 4.

AND I HAVE CONFESSED] Praises and I have said follow. For that is ידה. This prayer agrees much with that which is in Nehemiah 9, Jerome in this place: Therefore what God promises is not immediately to be, but He fulfills His promises upon those who keep His commandments.

GREAT AND TERRIBLE] Against the contumacious.

KEEPING THE COVENANT] Fulfilling the promises.

AND MERCY] Supply, showing also above the promises.

TO THEM THAT LOVE THEE] To the truly pious.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET CONFESSUS SUM] Laudes ei dixique se- quuntur. Id enim est ידה. Multum convenit haec oratio cum ea quae est Nehemiae 9, Hieronymus hoc loco: Non ergo quod pollicetur Deus statim futurum est, sed in eos sua promissa implet, qui custodiunt mandata illius.

MAGNE ET TERRIBILIS] Adversus contuma- ces.

CVSTODIENS PACTUM] Promissa implens.

ET MISERICORDIAM] Supple, ostendens et- iam supra promissa.

DILIGENTIBUS TE] Vere piis.

## 9:5
Ver. 5.

WE HAVE SINNED, WE HAVE COMMITTED INIQUITY, WE HAVE DONE WICKEDLY AND HAVE REBELLED, AND HAVE DEPARTED FROM THY COMMANDMENTS AND THY JUDGMENTS] Jerome here: he enumerates the sins of the people (because he is one of the people) from his own person, which we also read that the Apostle did in the Epistle to the Romans. Namely in the seventh chapter.

We have proven in Theolog. Apost. Rom. on ch. 7. against the Pelagians and Socinians, whom Grotius seems here to favor, that the Apostle in Rom. 7. speaks not from the person of others, but his own. Nor is Daniel to be excluded in this place from the number of sinners. He acknowledges sins, and confesses with true repentance; and that not only for the people, and from the person of the people, but also from his own person: Not at all excluding himself from the number of transgressors, which would not be of humility, but including himself, as is manifest from v. 10. Rightly therefore does the blessed Gesner note here in th. XCVII. Although Daniel was a most holy man, so much so that God counts him among the most righteous Noah and Job: Nevertheless, he includes himself in the promiscuous heap of sinners, while he says that he confessed not only the sins of his people, but also his own sins to God. Let the Papists therefore be ashamed, who do not blush to boast so much of the integrity of the obedience of reborn men, that in sess. 5. of the Council of Trent They have decreed anathema against those who think that concupiscence in the reborn is properly called sin by Paul in Rom. 7. But Augustine, in book 3 against the letter of Petilian, chapter [10], most powerfully opposes this impious dogma of the Pelagians with the present passage of Daniel, whose words are these: 'The most righteous man, one of the three memorable ones, prays and says: When I was praying and confessing my sins, etc. And you say that you are without sin.' Thus he.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PECCAVIMUS, INIQVITATEM FECIMUS, IMPIE EGIMUS ET RECESSIMUS, ET DECLINA- VIMUS A MANDATIS TUIS ET JUDICIIS] Hie- ronymus hic: peccata populi (quia unus e populo est) enume- rat ex persona sua, quod & Apostolum in Epistola ad Romanos fuisse legimus. Nempe capite septimo.

Apostolum Rom. 7. non ex persona aliorum, sed propria loqui adversus Pelagianos & Socinia- nos in Theolog. Apost. Rom. ad c. 7. evicimus, quibus hic velificari videtur Grotius. Neque hoc loco excludendus est Daniel e numero pecca- torum. Agnoscit peccata, & confitetur vera pœ- nitentia; neque id modo pro populo, & ex persona populi, sed etiam ex propria persona: Se minime excludens e transgressorum numero, quod non humilitatis esset, sed includens, ut e v. 10. manife- stum est. Recte ergo hic B. Gesnerus notat th. XCVII. Licet Daniel vir esset Sanctissimus, adeo ut Deus ipsum justissimo Noa & Jobo annumeret: Ni- hilominus tamen in promiscuo peccatorum cumulo se complectitur, dum ait, se non modo populi sui, sed et- iam sua peccata Deo confessum esse. Pudeat ergo Pontificios, qui de integritate obedientiæ hominum renatorum adeo gloriari non erubescunt, ut sess. 5. Concil. Trid. Anathema in illos decreverint, qui concupiscentiam in renatos a Paulo ad Rom. 7. pec- catum proprie appellatum esse sentiant. Huic au- tem impio Pelagianorum dogmati August. lib. 3. contra lit. Petil. cap. præsentem Danielis locum validissime opponit, cujus hæc sunt verba: Vir ju- stissimus unus ex tribus memorabilibus orat & dicit: Cum orarem & confiterer peccata mea &c. Et tu te dicis esse sine peccato: Sic ille.

## 9:7
Verse 7.

TO THEE O LORD RIGHTEOUSNESS] That is, praise of righteousness is owed. Thus below, mercy, that is, praise of mercy.

BUT TO US CONFUSION OF FACE, AS IT IS THIS DAY] This ignominy, which we suffer, was owed to us.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

TIBI DOMINE JUSTITIA] Id est, laus Justitiæ debetur. Sic infra misericordia, id est, laus misericordiæ.

NOBIS AUTEM CONFUSIO FACIEI, QUA- LIS EST HODIE] Nobis debebatur hæc ignominia, quam patimur.

## 9:9
Verse 9.

BECAUSE WE HAVE REBELLED AGAINST HIM] He meets a tacit objection: How is He merciful, who delivered the people to such great evils? The answer is: this was extorted from Him by the excessive contumacy of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

QUIA REBELLES FUIMUS IN EUM] Occur- rit tacitæ objectioni: Quomodo misericors, qui tantis malis populum tradidit? responfio est: extortum hoc ipsi per ni- miam populi contumaciam.

## 9:11
Verse 11.

ALL ISRAEL] Very many. As in Psalm 14:3, Rom. 3:12.

In the places which are compared here, it is a matter of all universally, not only of very many, which we proved in their Vindications on Psalm 14:3 and Rom. 3:12. Nor is it otherwise in this place. For however much all the Israelites were not liable to equal guilt, yet no one of them was entirely devoid of guilt. All the saints are bound to seek the remission of sins. Psalm 32.

AND THE CURSE HAS DRIPPED UPON US] The execration of the law has been poured out upon us; that is, it has fallen upon us copiously. See Nahum 1:6, Jer. 7:17, where in the Greek it is χέεται, here ἐπῆλθεν.

WHICH IS WRITTEN IN THE BOOK OF MOSES] Levit. 26, Deut. 28.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

OMNIS ISRAEL] Plurimi. Sicut Psalm. 14, 3. Rom. 3, 12.

In locis, quæ hic conferuntur, de omnibus universim, non de plurimis solum agitur, quod in Vindiciis eorum ad Psalm. 14, 3. Rom. 3, 12. evi- cimus. Nec aliter hoc loco. Nam utut parili culpæ obnoxii non fuerint omnes Israelitæ, nemo tamen eorum culpæ prorsus expers fuit. Omnes Sancti tenentur petere remissionem peccatorum. Psal. 32.

ET STILLAVIT SUPER NOS MALEDICTIO] Effusa est super nos exsecratio legis; id est, copiose in nos cecidit. Vide Nahum 1, 6. Jer. 7, 17. ubi in Græco χέεται, hic ἐπῆλθεν.

QUÆ SCRIPTA EST IN LIBRO MOTSI] Levit. 26. Deut. 28.

## 9:12
Verse 12.

AND HE ESTABLISHED THE WORDS

WHO JUDGED US] Who ruled us. שפט means to rule.

THAT HE MIGHT BRING UPON US A GREAT EVIL, SUCH AS NEVER WAS UNDER ALL THE HEAVEN, ACCORDING TO WHAT WAS DONE IN JERUSALEM] As it happened in Jerusalem.

Destructions had occurred elsewhere too, but nowhere more cruelly than at Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET STATUIT SERMONES] Ratos fecit.

QUI JUDICAVERUNT NOS] Qui rexerunt nos. שפט est regere.

UT SUPERINDUCERET IN NOS MAGNUM MALUM, QUALE NUNQUAM FUIT SUB O- MNI COELO, SECUNDUM QVOD FACTVM EST IN JERVSALEM] Quomodo evenit Hierosolymis.

Excidia & alibi evenerant, sed nusquam atrocius quam Hierosolymis.

## 9:14
Verse 14.

AND THE LORD WATCHED OVER THE MALICE, AND BROUGHT IT UPON US] And the Lord was diligent in bringing this evil upon us.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET VIGILAVIT DOMINUS SUPER MALI- TIAM, ET ADDUXIT EAM SUPER NOS] Et sedulus fuit Dominus in malo hoc in nos adducendo.

## 9:15
AND YOU HAVE MADE YOURSELF A NAME ACCORDING TO THIS DAY] Such as it is today.

Verse 15. WE HAVE COMMITTED INIQUITY O LORD AGAINST ALL YOUR JUSTICE] Against your whole law, which is justice here, as truth is above in 8, 12.

Latin:

ET FECISTI TIBI NOMEN SECUNDUM DIEM HANC] Quale est hodie.

Vers. 15. INIQUITATEM FECIMUS DOMINE IN OMNEM JUSTITIAM TUAM] Adversus totam legem tuam, quæ hic justitia, ut supra veritas 8, 12.

## 9:16
Verse 16. THEY ARE A REPROACH TO ALL] Behold, say those victors, the people who proclaim themselves the peculiar people of God.

Latin:

Vers. 16. IN OPPROBRIUM SUNT OMNIBUS] En, ajunt victores isti, populum qui se populum Dei pe- culiarem prædicat.

## 9:17
Verse 17. SHOW YOUR FACE UPON YOUR SANCTUARY] Look kindly upon that ground where the temple stood.

FOR YOUR OWN SAKE] Do this so that you may show your truth. In the Hebrew it is for the Lord's sake. But the Greek and Latin have expressed the sense well. For it is the custom of the Hebrews to place nouns in place of pronouns, as Gen. 1:27, 1 Sam. 3:21, 2 Thess. 1:7-8, 2 Tim. 1:18.

Although in certain places that custom prevails, that nouns are placed in place of pronouns, it is not always done so. And since it is the duty of an interpreter to render word for word, as far as it can be done, Blessed Luther rendered it more correctly: For the Lord's sake. Furthermore, it is better to adhere to the tenor of the letters and to examine the cause of it. For there is no word in Scripture that is idle. The cause of this locution is by no means doubtful if we consult Scripture. For the hearing of prayers by the Lord is done for the sake of the Lord Messiah, in whom all promises are Yes and Amen, 2 Corinthians 1. In whose name it is necessary to pray, if prayers are not to be void, John 16. If Blessed Gesner is to be heard here, Daniel specifically seeks to be heard in these prayers for the Lord's sake, so that indeed for the sake of the Messiah and the fulfillment of the promises concerning the Messiah, the Lord may grant the prayers, so that they may attain their end: Whence he also observes an emphasis in the phrase, shine your face upon your Sanctuary for the Lord's sake, i.e., Bring it about, my God, that having been returned to our homeland, we may at last attain that blessed hope, that we may behold the Messiah face to face, and that the types of the legal shadows may be illuminated by the presence of Christ himself, as if by a light. Blessed Franzius in Schol. Sacrif. disp. 10, thes. 4. The sum of the petition is entirely this: You, O God, chose our nation and made a covenant with it, that you would give it a vast posterity, and a singular land, and in that land produce from our nation the Messiah, Lord and Savior. Meanwhile, we have sinned: and you have cast us out. But you were at the same time mindful of your covenant, and you promised us the restoration of the polity and a return from this Babylonian captivity, and at the same time the production of the Messiah the Savior. Since therefore the time destined by you for servitude has elapsed, I vehemently pray to you, deliver us from Babylon, restore Judea to us, and now at last send the Lord Messiah into Judea. Whoever has considered the whole chapter of Daniel, indeed the whole history of this chosen people in the line of Christ, and the promise of a certain land, attributed for the same end, will confess this to be the true scope of Daniel's petition. Add that it is the custom of the Holy Scriptures in similar places to express in this way the plurality of the divine Persons, when something is asked of the Lord for the Lord's sake, or the Lord is said to have done something by the Lord, or by a similar reason mention is made of the Lord and the Lord, just as we have otherwise expressly shown against the Jews and Socinians. Distinctly, therefore, the Lord is shown here, God the Father, who hears prayers and illuminates his face upon Jerusalem, and the Lord for whose sake he hears, the Son of God, the mediator and sole intercessor, for whose sake the Lord illuminates his face. Nor is the mystery in the triple repetition of the word Lord in verse 19 observed rashly: O Lord hear, O Lord forgive,

Lord, attend: by which some believe the Holy Trinity of divine Persons is indicated; to which is subjoined; incline your ear, my God, so that it may be shown that those three persons are one God, just as the Seraphim also in their hymn in Isa. 6, by the threefold repetition of the word HOLY, celebrate the H. H. Trinity, but designate the unity of the divine essence with the word Jehovah Zebaoth.

Latin:

Vers. 17. OSTENDE FACIEM TUAM SUPER SANCTUARIUM TUUM] Benignus aspice solum il- lud, ubi stetit templum.

PROPTER TEMETIPSUM] Fac hoc ut veritatem tuam ostendas. In Hebræo est propter Dominum. Sed bene sensum expreffere Græcus & Latinus. Mos enim Hebræo- rum nomina ponere vice pronominum, ut Gen. 1, 27. 1. Sam. 3, 21. 2. Thess. 1, 7.8. 2. Tim. 1, 18.

Etsi in quibusdam locis mos obtineat ille, ut nomina ponantur vice pronominum, non tamen semper id fit. Et cum interpretis sit reddere ver- bum verbo, quoad ejus fieri potest, rectius utique B. Lutherus reddidit: Umbb desz HErren willen. Porro præstat tenori literarum inhærere, ejusque caufam scrutari. Non enim otiosum est ullum in scriptura verbum. Causa vero hujus locutionis minime dubia est, si Scripturam consulamus. Nam exauditio precum à Domino fit propter Dominum Messiam, in quo omnes promissiones sunt na & Amen 2. Corinth. 1. In cujus nomine precari oportet, si preces non debeant esse irritæ Joh. 16. Si B. Gef- nerus hic audiendus, peculiariter Daniel in hisce precibus exaudiri petit propter Dominum, ut nempe propter Messiam & complementum promissionum de Messia precibus annuat Dominus, quo illa finem suum sortiantur: Unde Emphasin etiam observat in phrasi, illumina faciem tuam super Sanctuarium Tuum propter Dominum, q. d. Effice mi Deus, ut in Patriam redditi tandem aliquando beata illa spe po- tiamur, ut Messiam coram intueamur, & typi um- brarum legalium præsentia ipsius Christi, tanquam lumine illustrentur. B. Franzius in Schol. Sacrif. disp. 10. thes. 4. Summa petitionis ex asse est ista: Tu Deus elegisti gentem nostram & fecisti pactum cum ea, quod velis ei dare ingentem posteritatem, & singularem terram, atque in ea terra ex nostra gente producere Messiam, Dominum & salvatorem.
