Quanquam Prophetæ Vet. Test. quos S. A- thanasius de incarnat. verbi non populi Judaici, sed orbis universi Magistros, Scholamq́; sacram publi- cam merito nuncupat, Dn. JESUM Nostrum e- minus solummodo viderint ceu eum, qui VEN- TURUS ERAT, EJUS tamen adventum, in- carnationem, prædicationem, Passionem, Resurre- ctionem, Ascensionem in cœlum, Redemtionem, & id genus alia beneficia non raro ita exhibent, ac si Filium DEI ἐνσώματον, καὶ ἔνσαρκον cominus in- tuiti, quæ salutis nostræ causa egit, aut passus est, o- culis suis usurpaffent, & quæ è sinu Patris protulit, ex ore ipsius sanctissimo hausiffent. Neque dubium est, Prophetas talia, Spiritu Christi, qui in ipsis erat, iisdem ostendere, mentis oculis vidisse, qui VI- DENTES etiam dicti sunt, quod futura tanquam præsentia conspicerent, interprete S. Basilio præf. in Ef. Filiumque Dei eadem sibi explicantem coram audivisse, quemadmodum imprimis oracula Pro- phetica de Messia AUDITUS nomine appellan- tur, Esa. 53, 1. Rom. 10, 16. quod Prophetæ audito- res Dei fuerint in excipiendis oraculis, ut ea vicis- sim suos auditores docerent. Ideo Obadias c. 1, 2. auditum, inquit, audivimus à Domino, vel audivi- mus palam loquentem Dominum, & Habac. cap. 3, 1. Domine, audivi auditionem tuam, & timui. Quan- quam S. Basilio in Esa. c. 11. visum fuerit, Prophetis neq́; visionem oculis propositam fuisse spectandam, ne- que cognitionem auribus audiendam, sed illustrem af- fulgentiam à Spiritu S. profluentem cordibus sese in- sinuasse aut præsentia exhibendo, aut futura prœnun- ciando; splendoremq́; lucis, ut in c. 7. Esa. loquitur, mentem præoccupasse, subservientem ad illustratio- nem. Non dubitavit tamen Theodoretes in initio Nahum asserere, sanctissimi Spiritus benignitatem Prophetis quibusdam per sonitum, quæ volebat, infu- disse, ut illi se quendam arbitrarentur loquentem au- dire, sicuti pariter visiones quædam oculis objectæ sunt, ut easdem coram intuerentur. Præcipuum autem visionis & auditus Prophetarum objectum fuit Christus Θεάνθρωπος, qua personam & of- ficium, cujus diem cum Patriarcha Abrahamo o- mnes videre desiderarunt Johan. 8, 56. Luc. 10, 23. 1. Petr. 1, 11. quicquid Juliano Apostatæ veteri, No- voq́; hic secus videatur. Præclare Theodoretus de curandis Græcor. affectionib. Sicut in regiam viam reliqui calles à pagis, agrisque conveniunt, ita Prophetæ hunc (CHRISTUM) viam esse credenti- bus ostenderint, per quem unice aditus patet ad vi- tam. Omnes Prophetæ ante faciem Christi trans- missi sunt, & Angeli vocati, ait S. Chrysost. in cap. 2. Matth. hom. XXVII. Omnes Prophetias ea præ- nunciare, quæ propter æternam vitam fidelium, in Christo & impleta credimus & impleri cernimus, & implenda confidimus, docet S. Augustinus l. VII. de Civ. Dei cap. XXXII. nec dubitat asserere, omnia, quæ in Prophetarum libris continentur, vel de Chri- sto, vel propter Christum dicta esse l. XII. contra Faust. cap. VII. Causam reddit in Psalm CXLII. Ipse Chri- stus, inquit, se in Prophetis prædicabat, quoniam ipse est Verbum Dei, nec illi tale aliquid dicebant, nisi ple- ni Verbo DEI. Annuntiabant ergo Christum pleni Christo, & illi eum venturum præcedebant, quos præ- cedentes non deserebat. Clemens Alexandrinus ad- ducit eam in sententiam S. Petri quoddam testi- moniũ per πατροπαράδοσιν acceptũ commemo- ratu sane dignissimum l. VI. Stromatum p. m. 314. Unde etiam Petrus in prædicatione loquens de Apo- stolis dicit : Nos autem cum evolvissemus libros, quos habuimus Prophetarum, qui partim quidem per parabolas, partim autem per ænigmata, partim vero expressa sua authoritate & ipsis verbis Christum Je- sum nominant, invenimus ejus adventum, & mor- tem, & crucem, & reliqua omnia supplicia, quibus eum affecerunt Judæi, & resurrectionem, & in cælos assumtionem, priusquam conderentur Hierosolyma, sicut scriptum est. Hæc omnia, quæ oportebat ipsum pati, & post ipsum ea, quæ erunt. Hæc ergo cum agnovissemus, Deo credimus per ea, quæ de ipso scri- pta sunt. E qua etiam prædicatione Petrina illud apophthegma Coryphæi Apostolorum paulo post observavit Clemens, οὐδὲν ἄτερ γραφῆς. Quæ tradi- tio prorsus consonat illis, quæ 1. Ep. 1. vers. 10. 11. de Prophetis scripta reliquit S. Apostolus. Quomodo autem Christum prænunciarint Sancti Dei viri, di- stincte ac per partes explicavit Augustinus l. 18. de C. D. c. 28. & seqq. ipsoq; longe prior S. Irenæus e- leganti compatatione docuit l. 4. cap. 66. Cum enim & ipsi (Prophetæ) membra essent Christi, unus- quisq; eorum, secundum quod erat membrum, secun- dum hoc & prophetiam manifestabat, omnes & mul- ti unum præformantes, & ea, quæ sunt unius annunci- antes. Quomodo enim per nostra membra operatio quidem universi corporis ostenditur, figura autem to- tius hominis per unum membrum non ostenditur, sed per omnia; sic & Prophetæ omnes quidem unum præ- figurabant, unusquisq; autem eorum secundum quod erat membrum, secundum hoc & dispositionem adim- plebat, & eam quæ secundum illud membrum erat o- perationem Christi prophetabat. Quæ exemplis variis prolixe illustrat. Quod autem in genere de Prophetis diximus, id in primo eorum, quorum scripta Canoni cum lege Mosis & Psalmis Davidis consecrata sunt, HOSEA, (hunc enim Athanas. in Synopsi, & August. loc. cit. primum inter ipsos faciunt) speciatim deprehendere licet : qui cum ESAIA συγχρόνῳ, non tam Jesu Servatoris nomen, quam ipsum Jesum in corde, labiis & calamo gessit, adeo ut quod S. Athanasius de parte maxima Esaiæ dixit, etiam censeri possit de non minima Prophe- tias HOSEÆ parte: quod nempe Evangelium po- tius sit de adventu Verbi DEI in carnem, quam Pro- phetia, si claritatem oraculorum respicias, utut eo efferantur modo, quo sua efferre consueverunt, qui ab officio PRÆFANDI, secundum Tertullianum, nuncupati sunt. Quid enim aliud, quam Chri- stum sonat mox ab initio, ex persona Dei Patris promittens : & miserebor Domus Juda, & SAL- VABO eos IN JEHOVAH DOMINO DEO suo, c. 1, 7. ubi sane Chaldæus interpres Messiam agno- vit reddens, Salvabo eos in VERBO Domini DEI ipsorum, quem Christiani, Judæis hic deteriores, a- gnoscere nolunt. Quam præclare summum illud Messiæ beneficium de vocatione nostra ad re- gnum gratiæ sistit illustre vaticinium c. 2, 10. & erit numerus filiorum Israel quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est, & non numerabitur, & erit in loco, ubi dicetur eis, non populus meus vos, dicetur eis: Filii DEI viventis. Quam jucunda, quam suavis ac mellita est illa CHRISTI Spon- si nostri pollicitatio! & desponsabo te mihi in æter- num: desponsabo te mihi in justitia & judicio, & in gratia, & in miserationibus, in fide desponsabo te mi- hi, & cognosces Dominum. c. 2, 19. Profecto explica- ri verbis non possunt abundantes hæ gratiæ divinæ, ait Megalander Lutherus, præclare gemmas maritalis annuli, quem Christus Sponsæ suæ Ecclesiæ donat, & aurum fidei, ex quo annulus hic factus est, quod- que pretiosas has gemmas complectitur, explicans, cum hoc epiphonemate: Sic Prophetæ eleganter & erudite commendarunt auditoribus suis & posteris eo- tum doctrinam: Legi autem & operibus nostris sim- pliciter gloriam justificationis in totum ademerunt. Porro quam plena sit consolationis illa de muliere a- dultera & Deo amata concio cap. 3. & quomodo ea proprie ad descriptionem regni Christi pertineat, optime præ aliis idem Heros noster docuit: Quid, inquit, potuit fingi suavius? qua alia similitudine DEI misericordia æque potuit commendari? Suavis- simum est, quod ipse Christus dicit de ovicula perdita, sed hæc culpæ significatio tam illustris abyssos miseri- cordiæ divinæ clarius ostendit. Quam solide vero ac potenter convincuntur cap. 3, 5. Judæi, & omnes qui agnoscere Christum renuunt verum cum Patre Deum? Audiamus iterum B. Lutherum pag. 508. Respondeant hic Judæi, cur is cultus, qui Deo tribui- tur, etiam tribuitur Regi David? Num igitur cole- mus plures Deos? aut Deus dabit gloriam suam alte- ri? Non solum enim dicit, Deum quærent, sed pro- mittit futurum, ut etiam quærant Regem suum Da- vid. CLARUM igitur hoc testimonium est, eodem studio & affectu Regem David quærendum, quo ve- rus Deus quæritur. Hoc autem si absurdum & impiis videbitur (Deus enim Deus unus est) coget Judæos necessitas, ut definiant, Deum(Jehovah) & hunc Re- gem David esse unum & eundem Deum. Siquidem eodem sunt cultu colendi. Resurrectionem autem nostram miro verborum compendio ita exhibuit Propheta c. 6. ut Christi resuscitationem, cujus illa fructus est, simul insinuarit. Quo de egregie B. Lu- therus; Propheta recte mutat personas. Dicendum enim erat, Christus vivificabitur post biduum, & tertia die resurget. At Propheta inquit, nos vivi- ficandos post biduum & tertia die, quo Christus re- surrexit, resurrecturos. Idq́; ideo; quia enim peccato demersi in mortem, perpetuo eramus in morte mansuri, Filius Dei nostra peccata in se transtulit, & pro eis sa- tisfecit in cruce, ac postea resurgens, mortem, quam pro nobis obierat, vicit. Itaq́; nos tum resurgere & vi- vere cœpimus, cum Christus resurgeret. Per eum enim nostra mors devicta, & vita, quam amiseramus reddita est. Luctam quoq; Jacobi, & antagonistam ejus tam luculenter describit c. 12. Propheta, ut mi- rum sit, quenquam reperiri, qui Christum in ea in- venire nequeat. De Judæis forte id non mirum, qui oculos habent, & non vident, id vero dolendum, quod hic tantopere cæcuciant Christiani. Non gra- vabor iterum adducere B. Luth. quem in hac causa nullo suo merito nobis opponunt adversarii: Judæi, inquit, suo more nugantur, & Elohim etiam expo- nunt Angelum. Sed veritas nos aliud docet; scimus enim Christum propter ministerium, quod in Ecclesia & in carne habiturus erat, dici Angelum Gen. 48. Es. 63. Mal. 3. Itaq; CLARUM est Angelum hunc, qui & Elohim dicitur, fuisse Filium Dei, & Jacob, qui in ea lucta vicit, vocatur Israel, quod Deum vicerit. Et paulo post: Hic iterum memineris mysterii Trini- tatis; Deum & Angelum vocat, ac post addit, in Be- thel invenit eum & ibi locutus est nobis. Quis? Ni- mirum qui erat Deus & Angelus(Maleach Elohim) ut autem prorsus nihil dubites, quis ille DEUS & Angelus sit, addit DOMINUS DEUS exercituum, DOMINUS memoriale, seu nomen ejus: Hic augustum Dei nomen (Jehovah) tribuitur Domino nostro Jesu Christo, quod ipse si- bi sumit, cum dicit, Philippe, qui videt me, videt Pa- trem meum. Hanc lucem cæci Judæi non digni sunt, ut videant. Itaq; cum legunt hæc, quid legant nesci- unt, & impossibile est, ut ex hoc loco possint se evol- vere, aut eum recte explicare. Si autem verum est, quod Prophetæ ex Sp. Sancto locuti sunt, quod potest Trinitatis clarius testimonium ostendi? Sed ut alia plurima in hoc Propheta occurrentia vere Evan- gelica nunc silentio involvamus, emicat profecto tanquam sydus splendidissimum promissio illustris c. 13, 14. De manu inferni redimam eos, à morte vin- dicabo eos. Ero pestis tua mors, ero exitium tuum in- ferne. De qua eximie insignis Prophetarum inter- pres, S. Hieronymus: liberavit omnes Dominus, & re- demit in Passione crucis & effusione sanguinis sui: quando anima ejus descendit in infernum, & caro e- jus non vidit corruptionem, & ad ipsam mortem, atq; infernum locutus est: Ero mors tua mors, idcirco e- nim mortuus sum, ut tu mea morte moriaris. Ero mor- sus tuus, inferne, qui omnes tuis faucibus devo- rabas. Cui magno consensu suffragantur alii Docto- res, & è Judæis quoq; ipsis R. Moses Hadarschan a- pud Galatinum l. 8. c. 21. Sed optimum interpre- tem, omniq; exceptione majorem hic imprimis ha- bemus S. Apostolum 1. Cor. 15. qui quomodo simul praxin saluberrimam hujus vaticinii ostenderit, ju- vat potius B. Lutheri, quam meis exponere verbis: Paulus, inquit, pro excellenti sua cognitione, pulcher- rimas & plenissimas consolationum consequentias ex hoc Prophetiæ loco nectit; Si, inquit, mors amisit acu- leum seu potentiam suam, sequitur etiam peccatum per Christum expiatum, & nos ab eo liberatos esse. Ubi enim peccatum est, ibi mortem existere necesse est. Si- cut contra ubi peccatum non est, ibi vita & justitia adsit necesse est. Sed sic peccatum per hanc victoriam sublatum est, peccati quoque virtus, hoc est, lex simul sublata est, ne damnare vel accusare nos possit. Hæc, inquit, est præclara illa victoria, quam habemus per Christum, & merito pro eo gratias agimus Deo nostro, qui eam nobis dedit, ut nos ea fruamur.

ET NON SALVABO EOS IN ARCU, ET IN GLADIO, ET IN BELLO, ET IN EQVIS, ET IN EQVITIBVS) Efficiam, ut neque Syri, neque reliqui de- cem tribuum nocere illis quicquam valeant: objecto eis metu ab Assyrio, II. Regum XVI. Esaiæ VII, 1.

Si hæc historia de Rezin & Peka respicitur, quo- modo hanc liberationem dedit Dominus pietati Regis Ezechiæ? Quamvis enim non negemus illam liberatio- nem huc etiam pertinere; verba tamen non in arcu, nec in gladio &c. videntur imprimis referre illam salutem, quæ Judæis sub Ezechia contigit prorsus mi- raculosa vereq; divina, percusso exercitu Sennacheribi manu Angeli 2. Reg. 19. Esa. 38. de qua etiam hoc vaticinium exposuit Hieronym. in h. l.

## 1:8
Vers. 8.

AND SHE WEANED HER WHO WAS WITHOUT MERCY, AND SHE CONCEIVED, AND BORE A SON) That is, after she had weaned the little daughter, she conceived a son, for women scarcely conceive while they are nursing.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET ABLACTAVIT EAM QVÆ ERAT ABSQVE MISERICORDIA, ET CONCEPIT, ET PEPERIT FILIUM) Id est, postquam filiolam à lacte depulisset, con- cepit filium, vix enim concipiunt feminæ dum lactant.

## 1:9
Vers. 9. CALL HIS NAME: NOT MY PEOPLE: FOR YOU ARE NOT MY PEOPLE, AND I AM NOT YOURS) This was fulfilled when those who were left of the ten tribes were driven away by Shalmaneser, to be henceforth not the people of GOD, but servants of the Assyrians.

Latin:

Vers. 9. VOCA NOMEN EJUS: NON POPULUS MEUS: QUIA VOS NON POPULUS MEUS, ET EGO NON VESTER) Id impletum, cum qui de decem tribubus erant reliqui, abacti sunt per Salmanasarem, futuri posthac non DEI populus, sed Assyriorum servi.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. AND THE NUMBER OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SHALL BE AS THE SAND OF THE SEA, WHICH IS WITHOUT MEASURE, AND SHALL NOT BE NUMBERED: AND IT SHALL BE IN THE PLACE, WHERE IT SHALL BE SAID TO THEM: YOU ARE NOT MY PEOPLE: IT SHALL BE SAID TO THEM, YE ARE THE SONS OF THE LIVING GOD) After the number of the children of Israel (shall have become in exile like the sand of the sea, such that it can be comprehended by neither number nor measure, then for that which they were called not my people, they shall be called the sons of the living God. The ו placed twice among the Hebrews often connects tenses, so that it is best rendered in Latin by 'after'. That במקום is equivalent to 'for that which': and thus many peoples even now speak: they shall be called the sons of the living God, namely those who shall have returned to God and the law, and shall have had faith in the Prophets; such, however, were some from the ten tribes, who returned home with the Jews under Cyrus. See Ezra II.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET ERIT NUMERUS FILIORVM ISRA- EL QVASI ARENA MARIS, QVÆ SINE MENSU- RA EST, ET NON NUMERABITUR: ET ERIT IN LOCO, UBI DICETUR EIS: NON POPULUS MEUS VOS: DICETUR EIS FILII DEI VIVENTIS) Postquam numerus filiorum Israel (in exilio factus fuerit velut arena maris, talis ut neq; numero neq; mensura comprehendi que- at, tunc pro eo quod dicti fuere non populus meus, dicentur filii Dei viventis. ו bis positum apud Hebræos sæpe tempora connectit, ita ut Latine per postquam reddatur optime. Illud במקום valet pro eo quod: & sic multi populi etiam nunc loquuntur: dicentur filii Dei viventis, nempe illi, qui ad De- um & legem reversi fuerint, Prophetisq; habuerint fidem, tales autem fuere nonnulli ex decem tribubus, qui cum Ju- dæis domum rediere sub Cyro. Vide Esdram II.

## 1:11
Vers. 11. AND THE CHILDREN OF JUDA AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SHALL BE GATHERED TOGETHER) Synecdoche, that is, some from Israel.

AND THEY SHALL APPOINT FOR THEMSELVES ONE HEAD) Zerubbabel, a type of Christ. See Jerem. 30, 20, 21, 22, 33, 22, and following, Ezech. 16, 61, 34, 22, 37, 16, and following.

AND THEY SHALL GO UP FROM THE LAND) They shall go from Galilee and other places to the Temple. See Luke 11, 44.

FOR GREAT IS THE DAY OF JEZREEL) That is, for the seed of God, for those whom he had just called the sons of the living God: for that is what יזרעאל signifies. There is, however, an allusion to a certain noble city among the ten tribes. The great day, the time of return, of the restored temple and city.

Thus, an illustrious prophecy concerning Christ is twisted to refer solely to the return from the Babylonian captivity. Many things, however, refute this Jewish gloss. And first, indeed, the conversion of the Israelites occurred in such abundance that it could not be counted at all. Grotius refers this to the multiplication and abundance of the Israelites in exile. But in this verse 10, no mention is made of exile: and the words of the promise, in which the very nucleus of the promised grace is contained, are very poorly perverted into a circumstance of time, as if they contained no promise, but only described a circumstance of time, namely, that this happened when the number of the children of Israel had grown to a huge magnitude, whereas it is too evident from these words: And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which is without measure, and cannot be numbered, that a promise of a huge abundance of those to be converted is being presented, not a circumstance of time being described. And such a gloss has been unheard of until now, as if a time were being expressed, and the particle Vav here ought to be rendered as 'after,' which renders itself suspect by its very novelty. All paraphrases refer these things to the promise itself, not to the time. Nor is there talk of bodily multiplication, but of spiritual: Because as God had threatened in the preceding verses, not so much bodily as spiritual destruction, concerning his name, 'not my people': because 'you are not my people, and I will not be yours,' which primarily bring about the deprivation of spiritual grace, so now he promises that the grace of the promise made to Abraham, Gen. 17:7, c. 22:17, will not, however, cease entirely. Furthermore, since God had threatened the Israelites according to the flesh with final rejection in v. 6 and 9, and it is evident from history that the ten tribes of Israel were not returned, nor was their kingdom restored, these things cannot be accepted concerning the bodily multiplication of the Israelites according to the flesh, but must be understood concerning the multiplication of the faithful and the Israelites according to the spirit: Namely, the Prophet answers, as Rivetus rightly says in this place, page 26, to the thought of those who might have supposed that God would not stand by the promises made to Abraham to propagate his offspring without measure and number, if he rejected the greatest part of Abraham's offspring from himself and counted them among the Gentiles, and cast them out from the communion of his people. For on this occasion, he preaches about the preservation, amplitude, and dignity of the new Church under the kingdom of Christ, in order to comfort the pious and fortify them against temptation. He answers, therefore, that the promise of the covenant will remain firm forever, because notwithstanding the punishments and rejection of the impious, God will stand by his promises, he will save and accumulate the remnant: that both are true, that the degenerate sons of Abraham, such as those were, are to be utterly cast off, and yet the number of the children of Israel according to the promise will be immense, just as the sand of the sea. Furthermore, it does not appear how the fulfillment corresponds to the prophecy, according to the gloss of Grotius. For why is this innumerable multitude of the children of Israel commemorated here, if only those who returned home under Cyrus are understood, whose abundance from the ten tribes was certainly not so great?

Moreover, there are those who, with Augustine, posit a hyperbole in this phrase: but there is no need; for this comparison is of similar things, not equal things: that the multitude of the children of Israel cannot be counted in the same way that the sands of the sea cannot be counted, not that there will be as many of them as there are sands of the sea. For the Holy Spirit is accustomed to use these three things in a proverbial expression concerning a great, and as far as we are concerned, innumerable multitude: The dust of the earth Gen. 13:16, Num. 23:10, the sand of the sea Gen. 32:13, Psalm 78:27, Jerem. 25:8, and the stars of heaven Gen. 22:17, Deut. 1:10. Finally, even if the little word בִמְקוֹם is rendered by Kimchi, Tremellius, and Junius also in such a way that it signifies only the turn or change of the condition of the people, and not the place in which he was to experience these things, in no place of Scripture, however, in which this noun is used, whether in the absolute state or in the construct, is it taken for 'THAT WHICH,' but it is the same as 'in the place' Lev. 4:24. Jerem. 22:22, etc., nor is it explained otherwise by the Apostle Rom. 9:26 than concerning the place ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, who furthermore, for the sake of evidence, adds ἐκεῖ 'there,' so that every doubt may be removed that the words are to be understood concerning the place. And therefore it is manifest that these things cannot be drawn to the return from the places of exile. For thus, according to Grotius's mind, it was not in the same place where it was said to them 'not my people' that it was said to the same ones 'sons of the living God'; but rather the former was said in exile, the latter in the return to the land of Canaan, according to Grotius. But if you follow our opinion, and understand it concerning the conversion and the spiritual Israel, there is no doubt that even in those places where the Israelites had once been rejected among the Gentiles, many were converted to Christ by the preaching of the Gospel in the time of the N.T., both from the Israelites according to the flesh and from the Gentiles, who belong to the Israelites according to the spirit. It can also be said that the land of Canaan is designated, where the Israelites lived, in which the threat of rejection was often proposed, in which also the Church was gathered at the beginning of the N.T., which is the explanation of B. Meisner. But Rivetus does not poorly deduce the universality of the Church from this, page 28. Not only in Judea, but wherever it was said to men, 'you are not my people,' that is, everywhere in the world where foreign nations previously lived, the Church of Christ will dwell, according to that of Malachi 1:11, 'From the rising of the sun to its setting, my name shall be great among the nations, and in every place incense shall be offered to my name.' Whence Christ, John 4:21, 'The hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem,' etc. The universality of the Church by reason of places, by which it is simultaneously shown that there is no need for those who are reckoned among the people of God to return to that land to which God for a time bound His worship: because in that restoration of the Church, He is going to consecrate all the places of the earth to Himself through the doctrine of the Gospel: although therefore the Israelites are not to return, nevertheless in that place where, mixed with the nations, they lost the name of the people of God, in that same place it will be restored to them.

Then the title by which they are said to be called Israelites, the sons of the living God, undoubtedly pertains to the spiritual grace of regeneration and conversion; and therefore the interpretation of Grotius concerning a return to sacred rites is too meager and diluted; which were by no means entirely interrupted in exile, even if public and solemn worship did not have a place there.

Thirdly, the conjunction of the Israelites and the Jews. And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel shall be gathered together alike: where, by synecdoche, he vainly restricts these things to those few from Israel who returned with the Jews. For those Israelites are not distinguished from the Jews; but they are counted with the two tribes, when Scripture says that two tribes were captured by Nebuchadnezzar and granted liberty by Cyrus. Nor were those who from the Israelites adhered to the Jews under Zerubbabel of such a number that they could in any way be compared to the sand of the sea. Furthermore, neither was that the measure of the Church of the sons of Israel, such that it could be said of the same that it was without measure or concluded by no boundaries.

Fourthly, by that one head which the Jews and Israelites are said to be about to appoint for themselves, Zerubbabel, a type of Christ, is not understood, but Christ Himself: because under Zerubbabel there was not such an innumerable multitude of the children of Israel. And since Grotius admits that those parallel passages to ours, Jer. 23, Exod. 34, and 37, which we have shown in our annotations to treat of Christ ῥητῶς (expressly), it is necessary to understand the present passage also as referring to Christ according to the letter; who is that one head of the Church, Col. 1:18, Eph. 1:22, and King in Sion: Ps. 2:7. Which is especially confirmed also by chapter 3 and the comparison with this Prophet. To which, finally, it corresponds that he is placed as head by the Israelites or the Church, because he is indeed placed as head by God, by reason of ordination and inauguration; but by the Church, in respect of recognition, acceptance, and celebration. The sense of the passage is therefore conveniently rendered here by B. Meisner: I shall indeed cast away the whole of Israel, yet I will save the remnant, and I will raise up true Israelites, children of promise and faith, whose abundance will be innumerable, and that will happen at the beginning of the New Testament, when the Church will be gathered from the Gentiles and the Jews, and all will coalesce into one people and one fold under one King and shepherd.

Fifthly, the ascent from the land is not an ascent to the Jerusalem temple, which very few Israelites saw, but the worship of the New Testament is described by a phrase of the Old Testament, according to a manner accepted by the Prophets: according to which to ascend to Jerusalem is to worship God, because they used to ascend formerly for the sake of worship. See Is. 2:3, Mic. 4:2. In which manner Hosea himself explains it in 3:5: They shall seek the Lord their God. They shall ascend, therefore, not from the land of migration, as the Chaldean says, but from the land of their habitation, whatever that may be, whether of the Gentiles or of the Jews; so that the unanimous worship of the Church may be designated, as if they were gathering in one place, although they are joined not in body, but in spirit: and as Jerome explains, from infidelity to faith, or as Rupert of Deutz explains, they ascend from earthly affections to heavenly ones, and strive with pious desire toward the heavenly Jerusalem.

Sixthly, the great day of Jezreel or the Seed of God, as Grotius explains, is not so much the time of the return, or of the resurrected temple and city, which are separated from each other by a full hundred years, as it is the time of the New Testament: which is accustomed to be described as the day of salvation, the acceptable time, the time of grace, a great and venerable day, and which is truly a great day for the whole seed of God, for all believers, from all languages, nations, and peoples, on which God sows the Church for Himself in the whole earth, Hos. 2:23.

Seventhly, if it were a matter of the return from captivity under Zerubbabel, since that is promised not so much to the Israelites as to the Jews, the Prophet would prophesy rather of the number of these than of the number of the children of Israel. For Hosea still promised the Jews some harvest, and a solution of captivity, not of Israelitism, ch. 6:11.

Eighthly, the explanation of the New Testament is clear, who those Israelites are to whom it is said, sons of the living God, who place one head for themselves, and what that great multitude is; namely, that Israel is to be understood as being gathered from the Jews and Gentiles, whose number is like the sand of the sea, according to the promise made to Abraham, Gen. 13:16, concerning which see especially Rom. 4:16, 17, Gal. 3:7, Rom. 9:6 ff., Gal. 6:16.

Ninthly, the interpretation and Apostolic demonstration is especially to be observed, by which he directly proves the calling of the Gentiles from this passage, Rom. 10:26. Which is so clear that Rivetus was forced here to desert his own party, who said that the passage was brought in by the Apostle only by a certain accommodation: But with all respect to those who think so, I cannot be brought to believe that Paul, when he was dealing with the Jews about a matter of the greatest moment, and one controversial and odious among them, directly and in such express words cited Hosea for his own opinion, for the calling of the Gentiles, in that place in which the Holy Spirit had not intended to deal with the calling of the Gentiles even by a single word, and had sought only a similarity, not a direct proof. Nay rather, Augustine, in his book to Simplicianus and in his book of the Exposition of the propositions of the Epistle to the Romans, proves by the most manifest reason that this testimony was brought forward directly by Paul for the Gentiles. Indeed, because when Paul had said two things in these words, that God had called us, not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles, while he resumes these two members, and according to the custom of the Hebrews, confirms first what he placed last, he brings forward this testimony of Hosea, to prove that they had been called from the Gentiles. But he proves the other regarding the Jews from Isaiah 10:27. But Isaiah cries out over Israel, if the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, the remnant shall be saved. I do not see why he would have brought forward this proof for Israel, as it is direct, as an indirect one for the Gentiles, when others were available from elsewhere, unless this one had been proper. Then he sufficiently shows, while he promises that salvation only to the remnant of Israel, not to the people numerous according to the flesh, that the prophecy of Hosea concerning the multiplication of the children of God above the sand of the sea does not pertain to carnal Israel. If, I say, this promise did not pertain to the Gentiles to be converted to the faith of Christ, that promise concerning the true children of God would not have been fulfilled in such a great number; which had its true completion when believers from the Gentiles came from the East and the West, who would recline in the bosom of Abraham, the common father of believers, and having become participants of the same adoption, by faith in Christ, constituted one and the same Church of God with the children of Israel, according to the promise. This is Rivetus, p. 26. A doubt could be raised here: whether the name of the Israelites has a double meaning here, and denotes both the Israelites according to the flesh, and the Israelites according to the Spirit. But it must be answered: that it is not a double meaning of the same word, but that it is considered for one Church of the Israelites, both the holy remnant which survives from Israel, and the Gentiles to be gathered and associated to the Israelites: for the Gentiles did not constitute a peculiar Church, nor were the Israelites gathered to the Gentiles, but the Gentiles were gathered to the Israelites; and therefore the Israelites are viewed in these places not separately, but collectively together with the Gentiles to be gathered to them, the denomination being made from those who were the first to be elected to the people of God, to whose holy, albeit small, seed which remained, the Gentiles were gathered, and with whom they constituted one Church. To which we finally add the confession of Grotius himself, who in his annotations on Luke 24:47 explains this prophecy concerning the calling of the Gentiles.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET CONGREGABUNTUR FILII JUDA ET FILII ISRAEL PARITER) Συνεκδοχὴ, id est, aliqui ex Israele.

ET PONENT SIBIMET CAPVT UNUM) Zoro- babelem typum Christi. Vide Jerem. 30, 20, 21. 22. 33, 22. & sequentibus, Ezech. 16, 61. 34, 22. 37, 16. & sequentibus.

ET ASCENDENT DE TERRA) Ibunt ex Gali- læa & aliis locis ad Templum. Vide Luc. 11. 44.

QVIA MAGNVS DIES JEZRAEL) Id est, semini Dei, illis, quos modò dixerat filios Dei viventis : id enim si- gnificat יזרעאל. Allusio autem est ad nobilem quandam in decem tribubus urbem. Magnus dies, tempus reditus, resuscitati templi & urbis.

Ita detorquetur illustre de Christo vaticinium ad solam reductionem è captivitate Babylonica. Huic autem glossæ Judaicæ multa refragantur. Et pri- mo quidem conversio Israëlitarum tanta copia facta quæ numerari prorsus nequeat. Refert hæc Gro- tius ad multiplicationem & copiam Israëlitarum in exilio. Sed de exilio nulla est in hoc versu 10. facta mentio:& pessime verba promissionis, quibus ipse nucleus continetur promissæ gratiæ, pervertuntur in περίστασιν temporis, ac si nihil promissionis con- tineant, solum temporis circumstantiam describant, quod nempe tum id factum sit, quando numerus filiorum Israël in ingentem magnitudinem excre- verit, quum ex adverso nimis apertū sit hisce ver- bis : Et erit numerus filiorum Israël quasi arena maris, quæ fine mensura est, & numerari non potest, exhi- beri promissionem de ingenti convertendarum co- pia, non describi temporis circumstantiam. Et in- audita fuit hactenus talis glossa, quasi tempus ex- primatur, & particula Vav hic per postquam reddi debeat, quæ ipsa sui novitate se reddit suspectam. Omnes paraphrases hæc ad ipsam promissionem, non ad tempus referunt. Neque de multiplica- tione corporali sermo est, sed de spirituali : Quia ut antecedentibus Deus minatus erat, non tam cor- porale, quam spirituale exitium, circa nomen ejus, non populus meus : quia vos non populus meus, & ego non ero vester, quæ privationem spiritualis gra- tiæ imprimis inferunt, ita nunc pollicetur, non ta- men desituram omnino gratiam promissionis A- brahæ factæ Gen. 17, 7. c. 22, 17. Deinde quum Deus Israëlitis secundum carnem finalem abjectionem mi- natus fuerit v. 6. & 9. & ex historia constet, decem tribus Israël reductas non esse, nec instauratum es- se regnum eorum, non possunt hæc de corporali multiplicatione Israëlitarum secundum carnem accipi, sed de multiplicatione fidelium & Israëlitarū, secundum spiritum, intelligenda sunt : Nimirum respondet Propheta, ut recte Rivetus in h. l. pag. 26. cogitationi eorum, qui potuissent existimare, Deum non stare promissis Abrahæ factis propaganda ipsius sobole, absq; mensura & numero, si maximam partem sobolis Abrahæ, à se rejectam Gentibus annumeret, & à populi sui communione rejiciat. Hac enim oc- casione, de conservatione, amplitudine, & dignitate novæ Ecclesiæ, sub regno Christi, concionatur, ut pios soletur, & adversus tentationem eos muniat. Respon- det igitur, semper firmam mansuram promissio- nem fœderis, quia impiorum pœnis & rejectione non obstantibus, stabit Deus promissis, servabit & cumulabit reliquias : utrumque verum esse, & de- generes Abrahæ filios, quales illi erant, penitus ab- dicandos, & tamen numerum filiorum Israël secun- dum promissionem immensum fore, sicut est arena maris. Porro non apparet, quomodo comple- mentum respondeat vaticinio, secundum glossam Grotii. Nam cur innumerabilis hic commemo- rata multitudo filiorum Israël, si tantum intelligun- tur illi, qui domum rediere sub Cyro, quorum copia de decem tribubus non utique tanta fuit?

Cæterum sunt, qui cum Augustino hyperbo- len ponunt in hac phrasi : sed non opus est; nam comparatio hæc similium est, non æqualium : quod similiter numerari nequeat multitudo filiorum Is- raël, uti arena maris numerari non possunt, non quod tot futuri illi sint, quot maris sunt arenæ. Tria enim hæc proverbiali locutione adhibere solet Sp. Sanct. de magna, & quoad nos, innumerabili multitudine: Pulverem terræ Gen. 13, 16. Num. 23, 10. arenam maris Gen. 32, 13. Psalm. 78, 27. Jerem. 25, 8. & stellas cæli Gen. 22, 17. Deut. 1, 10. Denique etsi vocula בִמְקוֹם à Kimchio, Tremellio & Junio etiam reddatur ita, ut significet tantum vicem aut commutationem conditionis populi, non autem locum, in quo experturus hæc erat, in nullo tamen Scripturæ loco, in quo hoc nomen si- ve in statu absoluto, sive in constructo adhibetur, accipitur pro EO QUOD, sed idem est, quod in loco Lev. 4, 24. Jerem. 22, 22. &c. nec aliter ab Apo- stolo explicatur Rom. 9, 26. quã de loco ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, qui præterea evidentiæ causa addit ἐκεῖ illic, ut o- mne tollatur dubium, de loco verba intelligenda es- se. Ideoque manifestum est, non posse hæc ad redu- ctionem è locis exilii trahi. Sic enim non in eodem loco, in quo ipsi dictum non populus meus, dictum est iisdem filii Dei viventis, juxta Grotii mentem; sed potius illud in exilio, hoc in reditu in terram Canaan ipsis dictum est, secundum Grotium. At si nostram sequaris sententiam, ac de conversione & Israëlë spirituali intelligas, dubium nullum est, etiam in illis locis, ubi reprobati quondam erant in- ter gentes Israëlïtæ, præconio Evangelii multos conversos ad Christum esse tempore N. T. tum ex Israëlitis secundum carnem, tum è gentilibus, qui pertinent ad Israëlitas secundum spiritum. Dici etiam potest terram Canaan designari, ubi habita- bant Israëlïtæ, in qua abjectionis comminatio sæpe proposita est, in qua etiam Ecclesia sub initium N. T. collecta, quæ B. Meisneri est explicatio. Sed Rivetus non male hinc universalitatem Ecclesiæ colligit pag. 28. Non solum in Judæa, sed ubicunq; di- cebatur hominibus, non populus estis vos, id est, ubiq; terrarum, ubi prius habitabant gentes alienæ, habi- tabit Ecclesia Christi, juxta illud Malach. 1. v. 11 Ab ortu solis ad occasum ejus, magnum erit no- men meum in gentibus, & in omni loco suffimen- tum afferetur nomini meo. Unde Christus Joh. 4, 21. Venit hora, quando nec in monte hoc, neque Hierosolymis adorabitis Patrem &c. Universali- tas Ecclesiæ ratione locorum, qua simul ostenditur non opus esse, ut populo Dei accenseantur, redire in illam terram, cui ad tempus Deus cultum suum alligavit: quia in illa Ecclesiæ restauratione, sibi omnia terra- rum loca consecraturus est per Evangelii doctrinam: etsi ergo non sint redituri Israëlïtæ, tamen in loco illo, ubi gentibus admixti nomen populi Dei amiserunt, ibidem ipsis restituetur.

Deinde titulus, quo nuncupandi dicuntur Israë- lïtæ filii Dei viventis, ad gratiam spiritualem rege- nerationis & conversionis indubie spectat; ideoque nimis jejunia atque diluta est interpretatio Grotii de reditu ad sacra; quæ intermissa minime fuere penitus in exilio, etsi publicus & solemnis cultus ibi locum non habuerit.

Tertio Israëlitarum & Judæorum conjunctio. Et congregabuntur filii Juda & filii Israël pariter: ubi per συνεκδοχὴν frustra ad paucos illos ex Israëlë hæc restringit, qui cum Judæis redierunt. Nam Israëlïtæ illi non distinguuntur à Judæis; sed cum duabus tribubus numerantur, cum Scriptura dicit duas tribus captas esse à Nebucadnezare, & liber- tate donatas à Cyro. Neque tanto fuere illi nu- mero, qui ex Israëlitis adhæsere Judæis sub Zoro- babele, ut cum arena maris comparari ullatenus potuerint. Porro nec ea mensura Ecclesiæ filio- rum Israël fuit, ut dici de eadem potuerit, quod sine mensura aut nullis finibus conclusa fuerit.

Quarto per unum illud caput, quod sibi posituri Judæi & Israëlïtæ dicuntur, non Zorobabel intelli- gitur, Christi typus, sed Christus ipse: quia sub Zo- robabele tam innumerabilis multitudo filiorum Israël non fuit. Et quum fateatur Grotius loca illa parallela nostro esse, Jer. 23. Exod. 34. & 37. quæ de Christo ῥητῶς agere ostendimus, in annotatis no- stris, præsentem etiam locum de Christo secundum literam intelligere oportet; qui est unicum illud caput Ecclesiæ Col. 1, 18. Ephes. 1, 22. & Rex in Sion: Psal. 2, 7. Quod imprimis etiam confirmat cap. 3. & cum hoc Propheta collatio. Cui deniq; conve- nit, quod ab Israëlitis vel Ecclesia caput positus sit, quia ponitur quidem à Deo caput, ratione ordina- tionis, & inaugurationis: ab Ecclesia vero respectu agnitionis, acceptationis & celebrationis. Sensus er- go loci commode hic redditur à B. Meisnero: Ab- jecturus quidem sum totum Israël em, servabo tamen reliquias, & excitabo veros Israëlitas, promissionis & fidei filios, quorum copia erit innumerabilis, fietq; il- lud in principio Novi Testamenti, quum ex gentibus & Judæis colligetur Ecclesia, omnesque sub uno Rege & pastore in unum populum & ovile coalescent.

Quinto ascensus de terra non est ascensus ad tem- plum Hierosolymitanum, quod Israelitarum pau- cissimi viderunt, sed phrasi Veteris Testamenti de- scribitur cultus N. Test. more Prophetis recepto: juxta quem ascendere Hierosolymam est colere Deum, quia cultus causa ascendebant olim. Vid. Es. 2, 3. Mich. 4, 2. Quo pacto explicat ipse Hoseas 3, 5. Quærent Dominum Deum suum. Ascendent ergo nõ de terra migrationis, ut Chaldæus, sed de terra ha- bitationis suæ, quæcunque illa sit sive gentium, sive Judæorum; ut designetur unanimis cultus Eccle- siæ, ac si in uno loco convenirent, quamvis non corpore, sed animo conjungantur: & ut Hierony- mus, ab infidelitate ad fidem, vel ut Rupertus Tui- tiens. explicat ab affectibus terrenis ad cælestes as- cendant, & pio desiderio ad cœlestem Hierosoly- mam contendant.

Sexto magnus dies Jesraël vel Semini Dei, uti ex- plicat Grotius, non tam est tempus reditus, aut re- suscitati templi & urbis, quæ integris centum annis à se invicem distant: quam tempus Novi Testa- menti: quod tanquam dies salutis, tempus acceptum, tempus gratiæ, magnus & verendus dies describi so- let, quodque universo semini Dei, omnibus fidelibus, ex omnibus linguis, nationibus & populis, vere est magnus dies, quo seminat Deus sibi Ecclesiam in terra universa Hos. II, 23.

Septimo si de reditu è captivitate sub Zoroba- bele ageretur, quum is non tam Israëlitis, quam Judæis promissus sit, de horum potius numero Propheta vaticinaretur, quam de numero filiorum Israël. Nam Judæis messem adhuc promisit ali- quam Hoseas, & captivitatis solutionem, non Isra- elitatis cap. 6, 11.

Octavo clara est Novi Testamenti explicatio, qui- nam Israëlitæ illi sint, quibus dicitur, filii Dei vi- ventis, qui sibi caput unum ponunt, & quænam illa tanta multitudo sit; quod nempe intelligatur Is- rael, ex Judæis & gentibus colligendus, cujus nu- merus sit instar arenæ maris, ex promissione Abra- hæ facta Genes. 13, 16. de quo vid. imprimis Rom. 4, 16. 17. Gal. 3, 7. Rom. 9, 6. seqq. Gal. 6, 16.

Nono observanda potissimum est interpretatio & demonstratio Apostolica, qua ex hoc loco directe probat vocationem gentium Rom. 10, 26. Quæ adeo luculenta est, ut Rivetus hic suos gregales pro- prios deserere coactus fuerit, qui locum tantum per accommodationem quandam ab Apostolo ad- ductum esse dixere: At salva eorum pace, qui sic sen- tiunt, non possum adduci, ut credam, Paulum cum apud Judæos ageret de re maximi momenti, & apud eos controversa & odiosa, directe & verbis adeo ex- pressis, Oseam citasse in suam sententiam, pro Gen- tium vocatione, in eo loco, in quo Spiritus Sanctus ne verbo quidem unico de vocatione gentium intendis- set agere, & similitudinem tantum quæsivisse, non di- rectam probationem. Quinimo testimonium hoc di- recte fuisse à Paulo allatum pro Gentibus, ratione ma- nifestissima evincit August. lib. ad Simplic. & libr. Expositionis propositionum Epistolæ ad Rom. Nempe quod cum Paulus his verbis duo dixisset, Deum vo- casse nos, non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex genti- bus, dum hæc duo membra resumit, & pro more E- bræorum, quod ultimum posuit, primum confirmat, adducit hoc testimonium Hoseæ, ut probet, vocatos fuisse ex gentibus. Alterum autem de Judæis probat ex Es. 10, 27. Esaias autem clamat super Israël, si fuerit numerus filiorum Israël, ut arena maris, reli- quiæ salvæ erunt. Quæ probatio pro Israëlæ, ut directa est, non video, cur indirectam pro gentibus attulerit, cum aliæ aliunde suppeterent, nisi hæc propria fuisset. Deinde satis ostendit, dum salutem illam pollicetur tantum reliquiis Israëlis, non populo secundum car- nem numeroso, prophetiam Hoseæ de multiplicatione filiorum Dei supra arenam maris, ad Israëlēm carna- lem non pertinere. Si, inquam, hæc promissio ad gentes ad Christi fidem convertendas non pertineret, promis- sio illa de veris Dei filiis, in tanto numero non fuisset impleta; quæ verum suum habuit complementum, quando ab Oriente & Occidente accesserunt fideles ex gentibus, qui recumberent in sinu Abrahæ, communis fidelium patris, atque ejusdem adoptionis, fide in Chri- stum, participes facti, unam & eandem Dei Ecclesiam cum filiis Israelis, ex promissione, constituerunt. Hæc Rivetus p. 26. Dubium hic moveri posset: anne ita Israelitarum nomen geminam significationem hic habeat, notetque tum Israelitas secundum carnem, tum Israelitas secundum Spiritum. Sed responden- dum est; Non geminam significationem ejusdem vocis esse, sed pro una Israëlitarum Ecclesia censeri, cum quæ ex Israele supersunt, sanctas reliquias, tum gentes ad Israelitas congregandas & associandas: Non enim gentes peculiarem constituebant Eccle- siam, nec ad gentes Israelitæ, sed ad Israelitas gentes aggregabantur; Ideoq; Israelitæ in hisce locis spe- ctantur non seorsim, sed complexim una cum gen- tibus ad ipsos aggregandis, facta denominatione ab iis, qui primi fuere ad populum Dei electi, ad quo- rum sanctum etsi exiguum semen, quod supererat, gentes aggregabantur, & cum quibus unam consti- tuebant Ecclesiam. Quibus tandem addimus ipsius- met Grotii confessionem, qui annot. ad Luc. 24, 47. hoc vaticinium de vocatione gentium explicat.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

There is further explained both the promise, that the Israelites in the time of the New Testament are to be the people of the Lord, and the reprobation of the Jewish Synagogue, on account of whoredom or idolatry, whose blessing is to be taken away, nakedness to be uncovered, feasts to be ended, land to be devastated: but so that hope may remain for the remnant on the cross; whom the Son of God is about to betroth to himself, and will fill with every kind of blessing together with the Gentiles to be gathered to this remaining seed.

The Lord calls away from idols, let conversion be made.

Verse 1. SAY TO YOUR BRETHREN, MY PEOPLE: AND TO YOUR SISTER, HAVING OBTAINED MERCY) This clause is to be attached to the previous chapter. The sense is: You who are from the ten tribes, say then to the Princes of Judah and Benjamin, and to all the people of the two tribes, with those long-standing hatreds cast aside: you are our kinsmen, having obtained great mercy from God, of which we also are participants; for Judah and Benjamin were those tribes to which God principally conferred this benefit: the others in the place of an accession.

The sacred text is rashly corrected: according to which a new chapter is begun here. And according to some, indeed, a command is given to warn the brothers and sisters, or fellow countrymen, descending from the same stock of Abraham. Who therefore in the vocative case receive those [words], O Ammi, O Ruchama, i.e., you pious ones among the people, who still are Ammi and Ruchama, the people of God, having obtained mercy, say to your brothers and sisters, that if they wish to avoid that horrible change, by which instead of Ammi they will be called Lo-Ammi, etc., they should repent in time, as Rivetus explains. But our opinion is that the promise is confirmed to the spiritual brothers and sisters, but with an ἀντιθέσει (antithesis) of judgment against the mother, the Jewish Church. For in order that the Prophet might descend to this judgment, he took the occasion from the promise made concerning the spiritual Israel, which, having been repeated through a brief ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν (recapitulation) as it were, was confirmed: say to your brothers, my people, and to your sister, having obtained mercy; so that the faithful may mutually congratulate one another, as brothers and sisters, the divine judgment is subjoined against the Jewish Church, which is like a mother, since from her, as daughters, the other Churches had proceeded, to whom a bill of divorce is given and denounced on account of spiritual fornication. For it does not seem appropriate that these words Ammi and Ruchama should be taken in the vocative case, since rather that which is to be said to the brothers and sisters is contained in them, namely that they are a people, and that they have obtained mercy. Therefore, they are not the same who are called brothers and sisters with the mother herself. However, a certain ἐναντιοφανεία (apparent contradiction) occurs here: because at the end of the preceding chapter, conversion and gathering to Christ are promised to the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel: but here, divorce and reprobation are indicated to the Israelites: but there, Israelites are understood according to the promise and the spirit, here, Israelites according to the flesh. There, those faithful ones especially, who in the time of the New Testament, whether from the Jews or from the Gentiles, were to be converted, are designated: but here, the matter concerns the Israelite people, given to idolatry before the coming of Christ, to whom therefore the judgment and reprobation of God is denounced, v. 2, as Jerome rightly observes. The distinction of the text, which Grotius urges along with some Hebrews, relies primarily on a ψευδερμηνείᾳ (false interpretation), as if in the preceding [verses] it were a matter of the return from captivity, and here the conjunction of the two tribes with the others were designated. But since that has been refuted before, and the former [verses] treat of conversion to Christ, there is no place for this Grotian gloss.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Explicatur ulterius cum promissio, quod Israë- litæ tempore N. T. futuri sint populus Domi- ni, tum reprobatio Iudaicæ Synagogæ, ob scor- tationem vel idololatriam, cujus benedictio auferenda, nuditas detegenda, festa finien- da, terra devastauda: sed ut reliquiis in cru- ce spes supersit; quas sibi Filius Dei desponsa- turus, & omnigena benedictione repleturq una cum gentibus huic semini reliquo ag- gregandis.

Avocat idolis Dominus, conversio fiat.

Vers. 1. DICITE FRATRIBUS VESTRIS, POPU- LUS MEUS: ET SORORI VESTRÆ, MISERICOR- DIAM CONSECUTA) Hoc comma annectendum su- periori capiti. Sensus est: Vos qui estis ex decem tribubus, dicite tunc Principibus Judæ & Benjaminis, omnique plebi duarum tribuum, abjectis odiis illis diuturnis: vos estis con- sanguinei nostri, magnam à Deo misericordiam consecuti, cujus & nos sumus participes; nam Judas & Benjamin eæ e- rant tribus, quibus Deus principaliter hoc beneficium con- tulit: alii accessionis loco.

TEmere corrigitur sacer textus : juxta quem hic inchoatur novum caput. Et juxta non- nullos quidem mandatum datur monendi fratres & sorores, seu conterranos, ex eadem stirpe A- brahæ descendentes. Qui proinde in casu vo- candi illa accipiunt, ô Ammi, ô Ruchama h. m. vos pii in populo, qui adhuc estis Ammi & Ruchama, po- pulus Dei, misericordiam consecutus, dicite fra- tribus, & sororibus vestris, ut si velint cavere hor- rendam illam mutationem, qua pro Ammi dicentur Lo-Ammi &c. mature resipiscant, ut exponit Ri- vetus. Nostra vero sententia promissio confir- matur fratribus & sororibus spiritualibus, sed cum ἀντιθέσει judicii adversus matrem, Judaicam Ec- clesiam. Nam ut ad hoc judicium descenderet Propheta, occasionem sumsit à promissione de Israë- le spirituali facta, qua repetita per brevem quasi ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν confirmata : dicite fratribus ve- stris populus meus, & sorori vestræ misericordiam consecuta; ut mutuo sibi gratulentur fideles, ceu fratres & sorores, subjungitur judicium divinum adversus Ecclesiam Judaicam, quæ matris instar est, cum ab illa, ceu filiæ prodierant cæteræ Ec- clesiæ, cui repudium datur, & denunciatur ob fornicationem spiritualem. Neque enim vide- tur convenire, ut hæ voces Amma & Ruchama casu vocandi accipiantur, quum potius illis con- tineatur id, quod dicendum fratribus & sorori- bus, quod nempe sint populus, quodque sint mi- sericordiam consecuti. Non ergo iidem sunt, qui fratres & sorores vocantur cum matre ipsa. Oc- currit autem hic quædam ἐναντιοφανεία : quia filiis Juda & filiis Israël promittitur sub finem ca- pitis præcedentis conversio, & ad Christum aggre- gatio : hic vero Israëlitis indicatur repudium & reprobatio : sed ibi Israëlita secundum promissio- nem & spiritum intelliguntur, hic Israëlita secun- dum carnem. Ibi fideles imprimis illi, qui tem- pore N. Testamenti, sive è Judæis, sive è Gentibus convertendi erant, designantur : hic vero res est de populo Israëlítico, ante adventum Christi ido- lolatriæ dedito, cui proinde judicium & reproba- tio Dei denunciatur v. 2. ut recte Hieronymus observat. Distinctio textus, quam cum Ebræis nonnullis urget Grotius, ψευδερμηνείᾳ potissimum nititur, quasi in præcedentibus de reditu è captivitate a- gatur, atque hic conjunctio duarum tribuum cum cæteris designetur. Sed quum illud an- te profligatum sit, ac priora de conversione ad Christum agant, non est huic glossæ Grotianæ locus.

## 2:2
Ver. 2.

PLEAD WITH YOUR MOTHER, PLEAD) A new discourse. ריב (rib) is to litigate: individuals who wish well for themselves are commanded to accuse openly the evil deeds of the whole nation, namely of the ten tribes, so that they may escape common punishments.

LET HER PUT AWAY HER WHOREDOMS OUT OF HER SIGHT) That is, let her remove them far from herself, like those things which are cast out of view. Say: let her do this, if she wishes to be reconciled to me.

AND HER ADULTERIES FROM BETWEEN HER BREASTS) See what we have said on Ezek. 23:21.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

JUDICATE MATREM VESTRAM, JUDICA- TE) Nova oratio. ריב est litigare : jubentur singuli, qui sibi bene esse cupiunt, accusare palam mala facta gentis to- tius, nempe decem tribuum, ut communes pœnas evadant.

AVFERAT FORNICATIONES SUAS A FA- CIE SUA) Id est, longe à se amoveat, ut ea, quæ extra conspectum projiciuntur. Dic : hoc faciat, si mihi vult re- conciliari.

ET ADULTERIA SVA DE MEDIO UBERUM SUORUM) Vide, quæ diximus ad Ezech. 23, 21.

## 2:3
Ver. 3.

LEST PERCHANCE I STRIP HER NAKED) Compare Ezek. 16, 39. 23, 26.

AND I WILL SET HER ACCORDING TO THE DAY OF HER BIRTH) As she was when she was born, without clothing and adornment. Compare Ezek. 16, 4.

AND I WILL MAKE HER AS A WILDERNESS) Here he explains in plain words that which he had said in the wrapping of a figure.

AS A LAND WITHOUT A WAY) In Hebrew: As a parched land. See Is. 41, 18.

AND I WILL SLAY HER) I will destroy her. WITH THIRST) ἀνομβρίᾳ, with squalor; that is, all things which are wont to be desired will be lacking to her.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

NE FORTE EXSPOLIEM EAM NUDAM) Confer Ezech. 16, 39. 23, 26.

ET STATUAM EAM SECUNDUM DIEM NATIVITATIS SUÆ) Qualis erat cum nata est, sine ve- stitu & ornatu. Confer Ezech. 16, 4.

ET PONAM EAM QVASI SOLITUDINEM) Hic nudis verbis explicat id quod in figuræ involucro dixerat.

VELUT TERRAM INVIAM) In Hebræo : Velut terram arentem. Vide Es. 41, 18.

ET INTERFICIAM EAM) Perdam eam. SITI) ἀνομβρίᾳ, squallore; id est, omnia, quæ optari solent ei deerunt.

## 2:4
Verse 4.

FOR THEY ARE CHILDREN OF WHOREDOMS) Bastards, as above 1, 2, of uncertain father. That rightly applies to those who worshipped a multitude of gods.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QUONIAM FILII FORNICATIONUM SVNT) Spurii, ut supra 1, 2. incerti patris. Recte id convenit iis, qui deorum multitudinem colebant.

## 2:5
Verse 5.

SHE IS CONFOUNDED THAT CONCEIVED THEM) In Greek: καλήσχυνεν, namely herself. Purer Greeks would say ἐνυβρίσθη. SHE SAID: I WILL GO AFTER MY LOVERS) It pleases me to follow the examples of the Assyrians, Syrians, Egyptians. MY WOOL) The Chaldean interprets it as silk. Greeks and Latins long believed that silk was combed from the down of trees. MY FLAX) Fine linen, the Chaldean: which is a most excellent kind of flax.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

CONFUSA EST, QUÆ CONCEPIT EOS) In Græco: καλήσχυνεν, nempe ἑαυτήν. Græci puriores dicerent ἐνυβρίσθη. DIXIT: VADAM POST AMATORES MEOS) Lubet mihi exempla sequi Assyriorum, Syrorum, Ægy- ptiorum. LANAM MEAM) Serica interpretatur Chaldæus. Ex lanugine arborum depecti sericum etiam Græci & Lati- ni diu crediderunt. LINUM MEUM) Byssinum, Chaldæus: quod lini genus præstantissimum.

## 2:6
Verse 6.

I WILL HEDGE UP THY WAY WITH THORNS, AND I WILL HEDGE HER WITH A WALL) Being led away in the chains of the Assyrians, you will be confined to a place from which it will not be permitted for you to depart. Others explain the thorny hedge as internal disturbances, by which they were hindered so that they could not safely go down into Dan and Bethel, into Egypt and Assyria, and the wall as stronger barriers, namely external wars and sieges: but we prefer the explanation handed down by Grotius. For these things happen to a people already rejected.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

SEPIAM VIAM TUAM SPINIS, ET SEPIAM EAM MACERIA) Abducti in Assyriorum vinculis, loco adstringemini unde exire vobis non liceat. Alii exponunt sepem spinosam de intestinis mo- tibus, quibus impediti sunt, ne tuto descenderent in Dan & Bethel, in Ægyptum & Assyriam, mace- riam vero de fortioribus repagulis, bellis nempe ex- ternis & obsidionibus: sed magis probamus ex- plicationem à Grotio traditam. Nam hæc eve- niunt populo jam reprobato.

## 2:7
Verse 7.

AND SHE SHALL FOLLOW HER LOVERS) She will wish to follow. AND SHE SHALL NOT OVERTAKE THEM) No one will care for her. SHE SHALL SAY: I WILL GO AND RETURN TO MY FORMER HUSBAND) For a similar plan see Luke 15, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET SEQUETUR AMATORES SUOS) Volet sequi. ET NON APPREHENDET EOS) Nemo eam curabit. DICET: VADAM ET REVERTAR AD VI- RUM MEUM PRIOREM) Simile consilium vide Luc. 15, 18.

## 2:8
Verse 8.

AND SHE KNEW NOT) She had not thought. Thus ידע is often used by the Hebrews. See Acts 23, 5. I GAVE HER CORN, AND WINE, AND OIL, AND MULTIPLIED HER SILVER, AND GOLD, WHICH THEY MADE FOR BAAL) Which they made to be Baal's. A similar complaint in Ezek. 16, 17. 18. 19. 23, 41.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET HÆC NESCIVIT) Non cogitaverat. Ita ידע sæpe sumitur Hebræis. Vide Act. 23, 5. EGO DEDI EI FRUMENTVM, ET VINUM, ET OLEUM, ET ARGENTUM MULTIPLICAVI EI, ET AURUM, QUÆ FECERUNT BAAL) Baalis esse fecerunt. Similis querela Ezech. 16, 17. 18. 19. 23, 41.

## 2:9
Verse 9.

THEREFORE I WILL RETURN) I will change my plan. I will deal with her far otherwise. I WILL TAKE AWAY MY CORN) I will take it from them, like a husband who casts out an unchaste wife. AND I WILL DELIVER MY WOOL) I will snatch it away, from their uses, that is. WHICH COVERED HER SHAME) The parts which modesty forbids to be seen.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

IDCIRCO CONVERTAR) Mutabo consilium. Longe aliter cum ea agam. SUMAM FRUMENTUM MEUM) Tollam ab ipsis, ut maritus, qui uxorem impudicam ejicit. ET LIBERABO LANAM MEAM) Eripiam, illo- rum usibus scilicet. QUÆ OPERIEBANT IGNOMINIAM EJUS) Partes quas videri honestas vetat.

## 2:10
Verse 10.

AND NOW I WILL DISCOVER HER FOLLY) Her lusts, which the Greeks also call ἀφροσύνας. Thus this word is used in Genesis 34, 7. Explain it from those things which we have said at Jeremiah 13, 26. 27. AND NO MAN SHALL DELIVER HER OUT OF MY HAND) No one shall deliver her.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET NVNC REVELABO STULTITIAM EJUS) Libidines ejus, quas Græci etiam ἀφροσύνας vocant. Ita vox hæc sumitur Genes. 34, 7. expone ex iis, quæ diximus ad Jerem. 13, 26. 27. ET VIR NON ERUET EAM DE MANU MEA) Nemo eruet.

## 2:11
Verse 11.

AND I WILL CAUSE ALL HER MIRTH TO CEASE, HER FEAST DAYS, HER SABBATHS, AND ALL HER SOLEMN FEASTS) No rest from labors will be given to them. Compare Jeremiah 7, 14. 16, 9. 25, 10. Not only is the denial of rest indicated, but the abolition of the polity, and especially of the Church, whose common feasts these two were, the Sabbath and the New Moon, with the cessation of which the anniversaries, the feast of the Passover, of Pentecost, and of Tabernacles, were much more bound to cease. Some say this was fulfilled in the Babylonian captivity. But the discourse here is not about the Jews, but about the Israelites, and therefore these things pertain to the Assyrian servitude. For Israel is openly named in verse 22, which city was in Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET CESSARE FACIAM OMNE GAUDIUM EJUS, SOLEMNITATEM EJUS, SABBATUM EJUS, ET OMNIA FESTA TEMPORA EJUS) Nullum illis otium dabitur à laboribus. Confer Jerem. 7, 14. 16, 9. 25, 10. Non tantum otii negatio, sed politiæ, & imprimis Ecclesiæ abolitio indicatur, cujus festa communia erant hæc duo, Sabbatum & Neomenia, quibus cessantibus multo magis anniversaria, festum Paschatos, Pentecostes, tabernaculorum cessare o- portebat. Impletum id nonnulli dicunt in capti- vitate Babylonica. Sed hic non de Judæis sermo est, sed de Israëlitis, ideoque hæc ad servitutem Assyriacam pertinent. Nam aperte nominatur Israël v. 22. quæ civitas in Israël erat.

## 2:12
Verse 12.

AND I WILL PLACE IT IN THE FOREST) לְיַעַר : but the LXX, as Jerome notes, read לְעֵד, εἰς μαρτύριον (for a testimony). You see how old the variation in writing is. The reading which we use is better, as the following words indicate.

AND THE BEAST OF THE FIELD SHALL EAT IT) With the people led away elsewhere, the land being empty.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET PONAM EAM IN SALTUM) לְיַעַר : at LXX. ut Hieronymus notat, legerunt לְעֵד, εἰς μαρτύριον. Vides quam vetus sit scribendi varietas. Lectio, qua nos utimur melior est, ut indicant sequentia.

ET COMEDET EAM BESTIA AGRI) Abdu- ctis alio hominibus, vacante terra.

## 2:13
Verse 13.

AND I WILL VISIT UPON HER THE DAYS OF THE BAALS) metonymy. Time for actions: I will punish those things which they did when they worshipped those Baals.

AND SHE ADORNED HERSELF WITH HER EARRING, AND HER NECKLACE, AND WENT AFTER HER LOVERS) He mixes the parable and the application, as writers often do with the figure and the thing figured. See what was said at Matthew 23:25. Adulteresses are accustomed to adorn themselves so that they may please their adulterers.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET VISITABO SUPER EAM DIES BAALIM) μετωνυμία. Tempus pro actionibus: puniam ea, quæ fe- cerunt, cum Belos illos colerent.

ET ORNABATUR IN AURE SUA, ET MO- NILI SUO, ET IBAT POST AMATORES SUOS) Miscet παραβολὴν & ἀπόδοσιν, ut sæpe scriptores figuram & rem figuræ. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 23, 25. adulteræ ornare se solent, ut adulteris placeant.

## 2:14
Verse 14.

THEREFORE BEHOLD I WILL ALLURE HER) All these things are said with ambiguous words mockingly. The words are taken from lovers: the reality is far different. Adulterers are accustomed to deceive women with flattering words. God will egregiously deceive those of the ten tribes.

AND I WILL LEAD HER INTO THE WILDERNESS) Adulterers are accustomed to lead women away into solitary and pathless places. Thus God will lead them away into the vast places of Assyria.

AND I WILL SPEAK TO HER HEART) This also is ambiguous. For to speak to the heart is said both of one who flatters, and of one who treats badly someone who is ill-disposed toward him.

These things are wrongly taken in a bad sense. Nor are they so ambiguous that they do not reveal the meaning intended by God: indeed, since the enticing, the leading away, and the speaking to the heart is God's, which is as different as heaven from earth from the gestures and acts of lovers and adulterers, and has an excellent end, therefore it is not without reason that the interpreters establish here the beginning of the Evangelical promise, which is subjoined to the legal sermon, by which the impious were terrified, so that the timid might be raised up. For this part, as the blessed Meisner has not inappropriately delivered its οἰκονομία, is nothing other than a notable prophecy concerning the gathering of the Church in the New Testament and its various spiritual benefits, completed in three members: in the first of which are described the means of conversion, which are the preaching of the Gospel, the chastisement of the cross v. 14, and the promise of gifts v. 15. In the second, the obedience of the Church is noted, which is expressed through joy and confession v. 15, through return and religious reformation v. 16, through constancy and the continuation of repentance v. 17. In the third, the benefits of God which He promises to the converted and the faithful are recounted, of which there are five, namely the donation of peace and concord, joined with security from dangers, v. 18, mystical betrothal, v. 19, 20, the hearing of prayers, v. 21, the bestowing of bodily goods, v. 22, preservation proceeding from mere mercy, v. 23, 24. The first medium, therefore, is the gentle persuasion of God מְפַתָּהּ, which is to persuade, and sometimes to seduce by persuading; the Vulgate rendered it 'to entice', the LXX 'I will lead her astray'. Tremellius: 'I am about to entice'. Blessed Luther: 'I will allure her'. For it is not taken in a bad sense, but rather the gentle address of God is hinted at, by which He intends to lead the erring Church little by little away from the pathless places as if doing something else, not unlike how a seducer leads a traveler away with various enticements. Therefore the Chaldean rendered it thus: 'I will subject her to the law and I will work miracles for her.' The particle לָכֵן therefore is not causal here, but of order: as if to say, after I have long afflicted them with various punishments and chastised them sufficiently, then I will persuade them with gentle words.

The second medium, the chastisement of the cross, is as follows: AND I WILL LEAD HER INTO THE WILDERNESS (which, however, others understand as separation from the impious) to which is joined a gentle consolation: AND I WILL SPEAK TO HER HEART. Grotius could not show where this is taken in a bad sense. Regarding consolation, it occurs everywhere, which is instilled into the heart through gentle and consolatory words; see Gen. 34:3, ch. 50:21, Jud. 19:3, Ruth 2:13, Is. 40:2. In what manner that in Job 11:19, 'that they might console them', the Syriac translated as 'that they might speak with their heart'.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

PROPTER HOC ECCE EGO LACTABO EAM) Omnia hæc verbis ambiguis dicta sunt χλευαστικῶς. Verba sumpta ab amatoribus: res longe aliæ. Mœchi solent fœminas blandis verbis decipere. Deus illos de decem tribubus egregie decipiet.

ET DUCAM EAM IN SOLITUDINEM) Mœ- chi solent fœminas abducere in loca sola & invia. Sic Deus illos abducet in loca vasta Assyriæ.

ET LOQVAR AD COR EJUS) Hoc quoque ambiguum. Nam loqui ad cor dicitur, & qui blanditur, & qui male in se animatum male tractat.

Perperam hæc in malam partem accipiuntur. Neque ita ambigua sunt, ut non prodant sensum à Deo intentum: imo quum lactatio, deductio, & allo- cutio ad cor facta, Dei sit, quæ toto cœlo ab amato- rum mœchorum gestibus & actibus diversa est, & o- ptimo fine sit, ideo non immerito hic statuitur ab Interpp. initium promissionis Evangelicæ, quæ con- cioni legali, qua terrebantur impii, subjungitur, ut erigantur timidi. Hæc enim pars, uti non incom- mode B. Meisnerus ejusdem οἰκονομίαν tradidit, ni- hil aliud est, quam insigne vaticinium de collectione Ecclesiæ in N. Test. variisq; beneficiis spiritualibus, tribus membris absolutum: in quorum primo de- scribuntur media conversionis, quæ sunt prædicatio Evangelii, crucis castigatio v. 14. & donorum promis- sio vers. 15. In secundo notatur obsequium Ecclesiæ, quod exprimitur per gaudium & confessionem v. 15. per reditum & religiosam reformationem v. 16. per constantiam & pœnitentiæ continuationem v. 17. In tertio recensentur beneficia Dei quæ conversis & fidelibus promittit, quorum quinque sunt, nempe pacis & concordiæ donatio, cum securitate à pericu- lis conjuncta, v. 18. desponsatio mystica, v. 19. 20. pre- cum exauditio, v. 21. bonorum corporalium elargitio, v. 22. conservatio ex mera misericordia proficiens, v. 23. 24. primum ergo medium est blanda Dei persuasio מְפַתָּהּ, quod est persuadere, & interdum persuadendo seducere; vulgatus reddidit lactare, LXX. πλανῶ αὐτὴν. Tremellius pellecturus sum: B. Lutherus, ich wil sie locken. Non enim in ma- lam partem accipitur, sed innuitur potius blandum Dei alloquium, quo Ecclesiam errantem velut a- liud agens ab inviis paulatim abducere cogitat, non secus ac seductor variis illecebris abducit via- torem. Ideo Chald. sic reddidit: subjiciam eam legi & operabor illi miracula. Particula ergo לָכֵן propterea hic non causalis est, sed ordinis: q. d. postquam eos variis pœnis diu afflixero, & satis ca- stigabero, tum blandis verbis persuadebo.

Alterum medium crucis castigatio ita habet: ET DUCAM EAM IN SOLITUDINEM (quod tamen alii de separatione ab impiis intelligunt) cui conjuncta est blanda consolatio: ET LOQUAR AD COR EIUS. Hoc enim ubi in malam partem accipiatur, osten- dere Grotius non potuit. De consolatione vero passim occurrit, quæ cordi instillatur per verba blanda & consolatoria; vid. Gen. 34, 3. c. 50, 21. Jud. 19, 3. Ruth. 2, 13. Ef. 40, 2. Quo pacto illud Job. 11, 19. ut consolarentur eas, Syrus transtulit, ut lo- querentur cum corde earum.

## 2:15
Vers. 15.

AND I WILL GIVE HER HER VINEYARDS FROM THE SAME PLACE) They read כרמיה with a holem after the כ. This is also ambiguous here. Adulterers are called vinedressers, just as the female part is a vineyard, as in Cant. 8:12. But the Assyrians will be wondrous vinedressers, who will draw blood from many of the Israelite people.

AND THE VALLEY OF ACHOR) A valley in love affairs is the same as a vineyard: but God threatens her with a fatal and mournful valley, such as that one where Achan perished with many others, which is called the Valley of Achor from the disturbance, Joshua 7:24, 25, 26.

TO OPEN HOPE) The LXX 'to open understanding for them', not badly, so that תקוה may be the drawing of lines, to which children are instructed. See Is. 18:2, 28:10. These evils will be the beginning of their instruction.

AND SHE SHALL SING THERE) An alternating song, for that is what ענה especially means: Understand, however, a song of weeping and prayers. The LXX, not badly as to the sense, 'she shall be humbled', and Symmachus 'she shall be afflicted'.

ACCORDING TO THE DAYS OF HER YOUTH) When she was oppressed by Egyptian servitude, as she is now by Assyrian.

AND ACCORDING TO THE DAYS OF HER ASCENT FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT) That is, before she went out. Synecdoche.

There is no ambiguity in the text. The word כרמיה denotes her vineyards; her vinedressers would be called כורמיה. But how will it be taught that adulterers are pointed out as vinedressers, and that the Assyrians are noted here? The allegation of the passage from the mystical canticle is inept and impious. For in Cant. 8:12, by the vineyard is understood not a woman's part, but the Church. It is manifest, however, that the Evangelical promise is continued here, and just as the means of the people's conversion were insinuated before—the preaching of the Gospel and the chastisement of the cross—so here the divine promise of gifts is set forth, namely the granting of vineyards: by which the planting of the Church, as a spiritual vineyard, is designated, or even a temporal blessing, as that by which men are also enticed to conversion; and the instillation of good hope: I will give the valley of Achor for a door of hope, as it is held in the source. For just as the Israelites obtained good hope of obtaining the land of Canaan when they entered the valley of Achor, so the Lord promises that He will instill good hope in the people. Therefore, these things are not to be understood as concerning evils, nor as concerning a deadly and mournful valley. If, however, with the blessed Gefn., one understands the sending of evils, as in the valley of Achor, because of Achan having been punished, there was cause for weeping for the Israelites, Josh. 7:25 [8:25], God can be said to give the valley of Achor for a door of hope when He mitigates afflictions and converts them to the salvation of the pious, and changes the perturbations of the Church into good, Rom. 5:3, 4; 8:28. For that not sad, but joyful things are delivered here, the canticle also confirms: which they are said to sing according to the days of her youth, according to the days, namely, of her ascent from the land, which Grotius wrongly twists against the open letter of the text by synecdoche, as if it did not denote the days of the ascent, but the time of pressure before the exit from Egypt. Therefore, the joy of spiritual liberation wrought through Christ is compared here with the joy of Israel's liberation from Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET DABO EI VINITORES EJUS EX EODEM LOCO) Legerunt כרמיה per holem post כ. Est hic quoque ambiguum. Adulteri dicuntur vinitores, sicut & pars muliebris vinea, ut Cant. 8, 12. Assyrii au- tem miri vinitores erunt, qui multis de Israëlítico populo sanguinem educent.

ET VALLEM ACHOR) Vallis in amoribus idem quod vinea: at Deus ei minatur vallem funestam, ac luctuo- sam, qualis illa, ubi Achan cum multis aliis interiit, quæ à perturbatione dicta vallis Achor, Josuæ 7, 24, 25, 26.

AD APERIENDAM SPEM) LXX. διανοῖξαι σύν- εσιν αὐτοῖς, non male, ut sit תקוה linearum ductio, ad quam instituuntur pueri. Vide Ef. 18, 2. 28, 10. Hæc ma- la initium erunt institutionis ipsorum.

ET CANET IBI) Carmen ἀμοιβᾶιον, id enim præ- cipue ענה: Intellige autem carmen fletus & precum. LXX. ad sensum non male ταπεινωθήσεται, & Symmachus κακωθήσεται.

JUXTA DIES JUVENTUTIS SUÆ) Cum ser- vitute premeretur Ægyptiaca, ut nunc Assyriaca.

ET JUXTA DIES ASCENSIONIS SUÆ DE TERRA ÆGTPTI) Id est, priusquam exiret. Συνεκδοχή.

Nulla in textu ambiguitas. Vox כרמיה notat vi- neas ejus; vinitores ejus dicerentur כורמיה. Adul- teros vero indigitari vinitores, & Assyrios hic nota- ri unde docebitur? Inepta & impia est loci è canti- co mystico allegatio. Nam Cant. 8, 12. per vineam nõ pars muliebris, sed Ecclesia intelligitur. Manife- stum autem est, hic promissionem Evangelicam con- tinuari, atque uti media conversionis populi antea insinuata sunt, Evangelii prædicatio, & crucis casti- gatio, ita hic exponi donorum pollicitationem divi- nam, utpote vinearum concessionem: per quas plan- tatio Ecclesiæ, ceu spiritualis vineæ designatur, vel etiam benedictio temporalis, utpote qua etiam ad conversionem homines alliciuntur; & bonæ spei in- stillationem: Dabo vallem Achor in ostium spei, ut in fonte habetur. Quemadmodum enim bonam spem consequebantur Israëlítæ terram Canaan conse- quendi, quum ingrederentur vallem Achor: ita etiam bonam spem instillaturum se populo pro- mittit Dominus. Non ergo hæc de malis, non de valle funesta ac luctuosa intelligenda. Si tamen cum B. Gefn. quis malorum immissionem intelligat, ut in valle Achor ob Achan supplicio affectum ploran- dum Israëlitis erat Jos. 8, 25. Deus dare vallem Achor in ostium spei dici potest, cum afflictiones mitigat, & in piorum salutem convertit, & perturbationes Eccle- siæ in bonum mutat, Rom. 5, 3. 4. 8, 28. Nam quod non tristia, sed læta hic tradantur, canticum etiam con- firmat: quod juxta dies juventutis suæ dicuntur can- taturi, juxta dies sc. ascensionis suæ de terra, quod perperam contra apertam textus literam detor- quet Grotius per συνεκδοχὴν, ac si non dies ascen- sionis, sed tempus pressuræ ante exitum ex Ægypto no- taretur. Confertur ergo hic gaudium liberationis spiritualis per Christum factæ, cum gaudio libera- tionis Israëlis ex Ægypto.

## 2:16
Ver. 16.

AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY) In those straits. THOU SHALT CALL ME MY HUSBAND) אישי. AND SHALT CALL ME NO MORE BAALI) Although בעל in common usage signifies a husband, she will not dare to use that word because of the horror of that name, which is imposed upon an idol.

There is nothing here about straits. The day of the kingdom of Christ and the purification of religion and the true invocation of God is noted: Whence Jerome rightly says: Since in both languages (Hebrew and Syriac) my husband or my spouse is called Ischi and Baali, I so hate the names of idols that even what can be well said, because of ambiguity and the similarity of the word, I would by no means wish to be said: but that I be called Ischi rather than Baali, so that while one thing is spoken, one might not be reminded of the other, and while naming the husband, think of the idol. It is added afterwards in verse 17, as a sign of true conversion, the total abrogation of idols in true worship: I will take away the names of Baalim, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET ERIT IN DIE ILLA) In illis angustiis. VOCABIT ME VIR MEUS) אישי. ET NON VOCABIT ME ULTRA BAALI) Quanquam בעל in usu communi maritum significat, ea voce uti non audebit horrore ejus nominis, quod idolo est impositum.

Nihil hic de angustiis. Dies notatur regni Christi & religionis repurgatio, veríq́ Dei invocatio: Unde recte Hieronymus: Quum utroq́ sermone (Ebrai- co & Syriaco) Ischi & Baali appelletur vir meus, si- ve maritus meus, tantum odi idolorum nomina, ut etiam quod bene dici potest, propter ambiguitatem & verbi similitudinem, nequaquam velim dici: sed ap- pellari me Ischi magis quam Baali, ne dum aliud lo- quitur, alterius recordetur, & virum nominans idolum cogitet. Additur postea vers. 17. ceu veræ conversionis fignum, omnimoda idolorum abroga- tio, & in vero cultu perseverantia: Auferam nomi- na Baalim &c.

## 2:18
Verse 18. AND I WILL STRIKE A COVENANT WITH THEM IN THAT DAY) Better: I will strike for them: that is, for their own good, as the Chaldean interprets here. I will make a covenant, that is, I will give commands to the wild beasts, the birds, the serpents, that they may not harm them: that is, I will make it effective that the Idumeans, Ammonites, Moabites may not harm them. Compare Isaiah 11. AND THE BOW AND THE SWORD AND THE WAR I WILL BREAK FROM THE EARTH) I will ensure that there are no civil wars, such as there once were.

The divine benefits to be exhibited to the converted are now recounted, as we said at verse 14, the first of which is the gift of peace and concord, expressed by the striking of a covenant with the beasts, the breaking of instruments of war, and the granting of quiet habitation. That covenant, therefore, with the beasts pertains to tyrants and any enemies of the Church, not precisely to the Idumeans, Ammonites, and Moabites. For by that phrase, the hostilities of the enemies of the Church are noted from the snares of wild beasts. Cf. Is. 11, 6.7. Joh. 5, 23. Some, more subtly, understand by the beasts of the field, tyrants; by the birds of the air, the wise and proud of this world; by the reptiles, the promiscuous and deceitful rabble, which is the explanation of the blessed Gesner.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET PERCUTIAM CUM EIS FOEDUS IN DIE ILLA) Melius: percutiam eis: id est, ipsorum bono, ut hic interpretatur Chaldæus. Faciam fœdus, id est, præcepta dabo feris, avibus, serpentibus, ne ipsis no- ceant: id est, efficaciam ne ipsis noceant Idumæi, Ammo- nitæ, Moabitæ. Confer Efaiam 11. ET ARCUM ET GLADIUM ET BELLUM CONTERAM DE TERRA) Faciam ne ulla sint bella civilia, qualia olim fuere.

Recensentur jam beneficia divina conversis ex- hibenda, ut ad v.14. diximus, quorum primum est, pacis & concordiæ donatio, expressa percussione fœde- ris cum bestiis, contritione instrumentorum bellico- rum, & quietæ habitationis concessione. Illud ergo fœdus cum bestiis ad tyrannos & quosvis hostes Ecclesiæ pertinet, non præcise ad Idumæos, Ammo- nitas, Moabitas. Phrafi enim ista à ferarum insidiis inimicitiæ hostium Ecclesiæ notantur.
