Argumenta vero, quæ Ca- lixtus eam in rem ex textu nostro depromit, aliud nihil probant, quam quod hic de statu Judæorum sub Babylonica captivitate sermo non sit, quod προθύμως admittimus: quanquam vero è nostris nonnulli, Brentius in Commentar. h. l. Flacius in glossa, D. Ægid. Hunnius, D. Georg. Mylius, Winckelm. Balth. Mentzerus in Analys. Rom. 11. Tom. 1. Disp. Giess. §. 60. D. Gesnerus & Baldui- nus in Rom. 11. D. Meisnerus Comment. in Hos. 3. Haffenreffer, in Templ. Ezech. p. 313. οι νῦν ἐν ἁγίοις, è loco imprimis Apostolico Rom. 11, 25. 26. 27. sub finem mundi aliquam insignem Judæorum con- versionem futuram existiment, alii tamen pleriq;, ob causas non leves, haud annuunt, B. Lutherus ipse Tom. 8. Jen. Germ. fol. 110. Phil. Melanchthon, Osiander, D. Daniel Cramerus de Regno Christi part. 2. c. 4. q. 6. B. Hoë commentar. in Apocalyps. Tom. 2. pag. 605. B. Pappus in comment. in Hos. 3. D. Brochmand, in System. quæst. 13. de extr. Judic. D. Joh. Cluverus in Rom. 11. Paraphrast. Vinarien- se in Rom. 11. B. Jac. Wellerus in comment. Rom. 11. B. Dn. D. Hülsemannus, B. Dn. D. Georg. Grossshain in Diatribe de Catholica Judæorum conversione, &c. B. Wigandus comment. in h. l. ita habet: NO- VISSIMO DIERUM significat tempus exhibitio- nis Christi. Docet enim ista tam cito non futura esse, sed præfinitum tempus observaturum esse Deum. Quamvis & hæc phrasis respicit ea, quæ promissa sunt, nempe, quod absq; Rege & Sacerdote futuri es- sent. Nam utraque labefactata sunt, quando Christus apparuit. B. Winckelmannus ad h. l. IN NOVISSI- MO DIERUM, i. e. post adventum Messiæ. Totum illud tempus ab adventu Messiæ novissimum tempus, finis seculi, postrema hora dicitur. Pertinent igitur hæc ad consolationem piorum in decem tribubus, quamvis pauci illi fuerint. B. Dn. D. Pappus de hoc vaticinio & aliis similibus ita differit comm. in h. l. Principio negamus, quando apud Prophetas est, ali- quid fore in novissimo dierum, id ad postremum CHRISTI adventum sive reditum ejus ad universa- le judicium referendum esse. Et perspicue ostendi posse contendimus, omnes eos lacos, qui novissimi dierum apud Prophetas meminerunt, de primo Christi adven- tu accipiendos, & in eo impletos esse. Nisi igitur ne- cessaria causa adferatur, cur hoc loco aliam interpre- tationem sequamur: hanc etiam Prophetiam affer- vabimus, de fine mundi, & temporibus finem mundi præcessuris apud Prophetas quoq; aliqua esse: Sed hoc inficiamur, illas prædictiones nota postremorum tem- porum insigniri: propterea, quod totum illud tempus, quod est à nativitate Domini & exhibitione Messiæ ad finem usq; mundi, novissimum tempus est Pro- phetis. Impletam ergo dicimus esse hanc Prophetiam, initio statim Novi Testamenti; cum multa millia

Iudæorum ad Christum converterentur, ut docet omnis Actorum Apostolicorum historia, & vigesi- mum primum præcipue caput: ubi non modo Pau- lus narrat, quanta Deus fecerit in gentibus per mini- sterium ipsius: Sed Iacobus quoq́; & cæteri Presby- teri Hierosolymitani Paulum admonent, quod millia ex Iudæis crediderint. Et paucis interjectis, sic per- git: Quod autem ad illam quæstionem attinet, de universali Judæorum, qui superfuturi sunt, conver- sione ante novissimum diem, ejusdem farinæ com- mentum esse arbitror; cujus est illud de Anti-Chri- sto, orituro ex stirpe & tribu Dan, & regnaturo annis tribus & dimidio. Non quidem nostrum est, ut pœ- nitentiam negemus cuiquam hominum, sive Iudæo- rum, sive gentilium, sed neq́; nostrum est de universali alicujus gentis conversione comminisci, quod sacræ non prædixerint Literæ. Nam locus ille ad Romanos, si penitius introspiciatur, non modo non confirmat hanc opinionem, pro qua adducitur, sed plane etiam evertit, Rom. 11, 25. In hoc enim & magnum illud mysterium situm est, quod & in aliis Epostolis prædi- cat Paulus: Quod omnis Israel salvandus, constet ex reliquiis Judæorum & plenitudine gentium: neq́; affirmat Paulus, postquam plenitudo gentium introierit, alios adhuc de carnali Israele illuminan- dos esse; sed statim post plenitudinem gentium omnem Israelem salvum fore annunciat: hoc est, juxta 9. & hujus quoq́; 11. cap. doctrinam, spiritua- lem Israelem considerandum esse, ejusque ex Ju- dæis & gentibus collectionem. Eodem facit, quod in ipsa Prophetæ nostri prædictione, non modo rever- sio filiorum Israel prædicitur, sed duratio quoque Ec- clesiæ illius, quæ duratio de fine mundi non potest ac- cipi. Hæc Dn. D. Pappus.

E qua sententiarum recensione manifestum est, non habuisse causam D. Calixtum arguendi B. Hülsemannum nostrum, quod in hac quæstione de conversione Judæorum à Præceptoribus suis B. Rungio, & B. Huttero divortium fecerit, cui o̔ μα- καρίτης noster im Calixtinische Gewissens-Wurm ita respondit cap. 8. p. 1173. Wenn Calixtus etli- cher, und zwar einer ansehnlichen Anzahl Jüden noch künfftige Bekehrung, als vermuthlich angege- ben hätte, wie Dd. Rungius und Hutterus thun, wäre er deßwegen nicht zu tadeln, allein, daß ers (1.) als ein Göttlich und unzweiffelich Zeichen, wel- ches vor annahenden jüngsten Tag hergehen, und geglaubet werden solle, (2.) Die Bekehrung der Jüden ingesaimbt dergestalt extendiret, daß wie man jetzt sagt von Deutschland: Ganz Deutsch- land hat den Christlichen Glauben ange- nommen, also auch von dem gantzen Jüdischen Volcke noch vor dem jüngsten Tage sagen solle: Gantz Israel ist selig worden (wie er es denn nochmahlen extendiret) das tadelt D. Hülse- mann, als dem Worte Gottes, und allen Recht- gläubigen Lehrern, auch D. Rungio und Huttero ungemäß. Quo etiam B. Dn. D. Wellerus abit, in Commentar. ad Rom. XI. p. 644. Indicat Apostolus, quod perpetuo aliqui ex Iudæis sint convertendi, & quod totus Israel, h.e. filius promissionis una cum genti- bus aliquando hæreditatem accepturus sit. Sic diversis temporibus Iudæos magno numero baptizatos, & in Ecclesiæ collegium adscriptos esse, testatur Osiander cent. 5. lib. 1. cap. 24. cent. 6. lib. 4. cap. 4. & 5. pag. 244. 245. cent. 7. lib. 2. cap. 7. p. 95. Non negamus, (quod tamen ex h. l. ἀποδεικτικως evinci non potest, sed soli Deo cognitum est) fieri adhuc posse, ex singula- ri Dei misericordia, ut insignis aliquis Iudæorum numerus ad Messiæ regnum, ante gloriosum ejus redi- tum, accedat, quod ut certo fiat, ὁλοκαρδίως preca- mur. Prævenerat in hac moderatione B. Gerhar- dus in LL. CC. T. IX. p. 111. Qualis & quanta præ- cise futura sit Judæorum conversio, ante oraculi hujus complementum apodictice sciri nequit. Quæ longe tutior, quam temeritas Balthasaris Willii com- ment. in Zach. c. 14, 5. p. 515. definientis Judæorum conversionem certo certius sub Philadelphensi perio- do, (mira de periodis sibi fingit è detorsione Apo- calypseos cap. 2. & 3. somnia) non longe post hæc tempora (nostra) eventuram. Sed hæc ex occasio- ne loci nostri Prophetici; plenius, si Deo visum fuerit, de his ad Rom. 11, 25. dispiciemus; ubi Grotius novam Apostolici oraculi ἐξήγησιν non minus à propria l. 2. de Verit. Relig. Christ. sect. VIII. tradita, quam ab aliorum interpretationibus plane diversam proposuit.

Si autem quæras, quis ergo tandem Prophe- tici vaticinii sensus sit, de Israelitarum ad Dominum conversione; simplicissima videtur B. Lutheri nostri explicatio in Comm. ad h.l. (à qua non alienæ sunt ἐξηγήσεις Wigandi, Winckelmanni, Pappi, nec pa- raphrases Osiandrina, aut Vinariensium) Populus Israel inter gentes mansit disseminatus, donec per Apo- stolos Evangelium in gentes vulgatum esset, demum cœpit converti, & quærere Dominum Deum suum, & David Regem suum. Et in glossa marginali: Israel ist nach der Gefängnüß nicht wieder zum König komen, biß der rechte David Christus kam, aller Welt König. Voëtius certe, etsi operosus sit in adserenda generali conversione Judæorum, negat ipse loco cit. p. 133. decem tribus eadem converten- das, si de tribubus sub specie & forma illius gentis, cum Ecclesiastice, tum politice consideratis sermo sit: & observat, homines istarum tribuum in tres classes distribui posse. 1. Eorum, qui per bella jam in- de à Jeroboamo usq́; ad captivitatem Assyriam, alias sedes quæsiverunt, partim apud vicinas nationes, par- tim in Judæa (quorum illi aut Judaicis Synagogis in terris Gentilium erectis se adjunxerant, & sic Ecclesiæ ac populo Judaico incorporati sunt; aut cum Gentibus permixti sunt, cum iis coaluerunt, atque in illos degenerarunt: isti in terra Judæo- rum cum corpore Ecclesiæ & populi Judaici coa- luerunt, non tantum ante captivitatem Babyloni- cam, 1. Reg. 11, 20. 21. 23. 2. Paral. 2. v. 13. 14. & 15. v. 9. & 30. v. 11. Luc. 2. Philipp. 3, 5. coll. cum Rom. 9. 2. sed etiam post reditum ex captivitate, Ezra 1, 5. & 4, 1. 2. Eorum, qui per captivitatem Assyriam & præcedentes eam invasiones in terras gentium transportati sint, 2. Reg. 17. Quos omnes dicen- dum est, partim in Gentiles degenerasse; partim Judaicis Synagogis & διασποραῖς illic se adjunxisse (Jacobi 1. vers. 1.) ac cum illis coaluisse; partim in terram Judæorum rediisse, cum redirent Judæi ex Babylone, & vicinis gentibus Ammonitis, Moabitis, &c. partim in terram decem tri- buum rediisse, ac cum Cuthæis seu Samaritis coaluisse. 3. Eorum, qui tempore deportationis As- syriæ in terra decem tribuum relicti sunt, & cum co- loniis Gentilium eo deductis coaluerunt, aut sal- tem permixti fuerunt, 2. Reg. 17. Ex qua distri- butione constat, posteros istorum Israelitarum, si qui convertuntur, aut convertendi sunt, non converti conversione generali (qualis est Judæo- rum) nec ut Judæos aut Israelitas, seorsim natio- nem quam constituentes; sed partim ut hos at- que illos Gentiles, cum quibus coaluerunt, aut in quos degenerarunt, partim ut Judæos, par- tim ut Samaritas. Ad hos ergo cum revertendi sint Israelitæ, dubium nullum est, Gentibus, Ju- dæis & Samaritis tempore Nov. Testamenti con- versis plurimos ex Israelitis (vel decem tribubus) Qui diu sederant sine Rege, ad Regem David Mes- siam conversos esse.

mini sano in mentem venire potuisse, oppido miramur. Memores illi esse debuissent, quod alibi, sed non in loco Hos. 4, 2. Calvinus, Ma- gister ipsorum communis monuit; Semper hoc spectandum est nobis, ne volitemus in aere. Placent argutæ speculationes primo intuitu, sed postea evanescunt.

## 4:1 Argument
SERMON III. and that a legal one. CHAPTER IV. EPANORTHOTIC. A rebuke of the Israelites because, destitute of charity toward their neighbor and true religion, they are polluted by various crimes, with a threat of miserable destruction, especially because they do not bear divine rebuke, but listen to false prophets, being about to be overthrown with them, especially on account of drunkenness and idolatry, and a warning to the Jews, that they should not serve idols and the true God through an impious syncretism, but with a view to the reprobation and dissipation of the Israelites, they should have no communion with them. He threatens the plagues of vengeance for the sins of the people.

Latin:

CONCIO III. eaque legalis. CAPUT IV. EPANORTHOTICUM. Increpatio Israëliturum quod charitate erga proximum & vera religione destituti va- riis criminibus polluantur, cum commina- tione miserabilis excidii, imprimis quia non ferunt divinam increpationem, sed Pseudo - Prophetas audiunt, cum iisdem evertendi maxime ob ebrietatem & idolo- latriam, ac præmonitione Judæorum, ne im- pio Syncretismo idolis & vero Deo serviant, sed intuitu reprobationis & dissipationis Israëlitarum nullam cum illis commu- nionem habeant. Delictis populi plagas vindicta minatur.

## 4:1
Ver. 1. THE LORD HATH A CONTROVERSY WITH THE INHABITANTS OF THE LAND) A lawsuit.

Latin:

Vers. 1. JUDICIUM DOMINO CVM HABITATORI- BUS TERRÆ) Lis.

## 4:1
THERE IS NO KNOWLEDGE OF GOD IN THE LAND) Piety, as the Chaldean interprets it here: for the Hebrews often call virtues sciences,

Latin:

NON EST SCIENTIA DEI IN TERRA) Pietas, ut hic interpretatur Chaldæus: sæpe enim Hebræi virtu- tes scientias vocant,

## 4:2
Vers. 2. CURSING) In Hebrew: by swearing falsely.

AND LYING) In Hebrew: by denying, namely a deposit.

Latin:

Vers. 2. MALEDICTUM) In Hebræo: pejerando..

ET MENDACIUM) In Hebræo: abnegando, nem- pe depositum.

## 4:2
AND BLOOD HAS TOUCHED BLOOD) That is: Slaughter shall follow slaughter. This is, Shallum shall kill Zechariah, Menahem shall kill Shallum. 2 Kings 15.

Latin:

ET SANGVIS SANGVINEM TETIGIT) Id est: Cædes cædem sequetur, Hoc est Zachariam Sellumus, Sel- lumum Manahemus occidet. 2. Regum 15.

## 4:3
Ver. 3. FOR THIS THE LAND SHALL MOURN) A good part of the land of the ten tribes shall be desolate without inhabitants, and that by Tiglath-Pileser: the remaining part by Shalmaneser.

AND EVERY ONE THAT DWELLETH THEREIN SHALL LANGUISH) If any one shall have remained there, he shall languish as food supplies fail.

WITH THE BEAST OF THE FIELD AND WITH THE FOWL OF HEAVEN) Even the cattle and birds shall languish, not only with the crops, but also with the herbs all eaten, or corrupted by the army and the horses of the enemies. Jerome notes here that the same thing happened in his time through Illyricum, Thrace, Macedonia, the Pannonias, and all that extends to the Julian Alps.

YEA, THE FISHES OF THE SEA ALSO SHALL BE GATHERED) The fish of the lakes shall be cast out to the banks, the waters being corrupted by blood.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PROPTER HOC LUGEBIT TERRA) Bona pars terræ decem tribuum erit vasta sine colonis, idque per Teg- lathphalasarum: reliqua pars per Salmanasarum.

ET INFIRMABITUR OMNIS QUI HABI- TAT IN EA) Siquis ibi restiterit, languebit deficienti- bus alimentis.

IN BESTIA AGRI ET IN VOLUCRE CŒ- LI) Etiam pecudes & aves languebunt, non frugibus tan- tum, sed & herbis omnis comefis, aut corruptis ab exerci- tu & equis hostium. Idem suo tempore evenisse per Illy- ricum, Thraciam, Macedoniam, Pannonias, omnemque ad Alpes Julias tenditur, notat hic Hieronymus.

SED ET PISCES MARIS CONGREGABUN- TUR) Lacuum pisces ad ripas ejicientur, aquis sanguine corruptis.

## 4:4
Ver. 4. YET LET NO MAN JUDGE) Let no one litigate against them,

Latin:

Vers. 4. VERUNTAMEN UNUSQUISQVE NE JUDI- CET) Nemo adversum eos litiget,

## 4:4
AND LET NO MAN REPROVE) Let no one rebuke: namely, another.

FOR THY PEOPLE) Of the ten tribes; for he addresses now all, now individuals.

FOR THERE IS NO TRUTH) Good faith. The Hebrews gather from this that even to idolaters something good happens from God, if they keep the laws of humanity.

Latin:

ET NON ARGUATUR VIR) Nemo increpet: nempe alterum.

POPULUS ENIM TUUS) Decem tribuum; nam modo cunctos, modo singulos alloquitur.

NON EST ENIM VERITAS) Bona fides. Col- ligunt hinc Hebræi etiam idolatolatris aliquid boni à Deo contingere, si jura humanitatis servent.

## 4:4
AS THOSE WHO CONTRADICT THE PRIEST) They are like those who contumaciously oppose public decrees, for which crime the penalty of death is established in Deut. 17, 12. see the things said at that place.

Latin:

SICUT HI QVI CONTRADICUNT SACER- DOTI) Similes sunt his qui publica decreta contumaciter oppugnant, cui crimini capitis pœna constituta est Deut. 17, 12. ad quem locum dicta vide.

## 4:5
Vers. 5. AND YOU SHALL FALL TODAY) That is, shortly.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET CORRUES HODIE) Id est, brevi.

## 4:5
AND THE PROPHET ALSO SHALL FALL WITH YOU) A false prophet, as the Chaldean has it here.

AND MURDER) In Hebrew: And by killing,

AND ADULTERY) And by committing adultery.

BY NIGHT) This is connected with the preceding in Hebrew: but interpret it with the Chaldean: as if by night: that is, unexpectedly.

THEY HAVE OVERFLOWED) They break, namely the laws.

Latin:

ET CORRUET ETIAM PROPHETA TECUM) Pseudo-Propheta, ut hic habet Chaldæus.

ET HOMICIDIUM) In Hebræo: Et occidendo,

ET ADULTERIUM) Et mœchando.

NOCTE) Hoc cum præcedentibus connectitur in Hebræo: interpretare autem cum Chaldæo: quasi nocte: hoc est improviso.

INVNDAVERUNT) Frangunt, nempe leges.

## 4:5
I HAVE MADE YOUR MOTHER SILENT) I will cut off your mother: that is, the nation: thus דמה is taken & below 10, 15. it also signifies to liken; which the LXX followed here. The Latin, however, derived it from דום to be silent: but the exposition which I have stated is the best.

Latin:

TACERE FECI MATREM TVAM) Exscindam matrem tuam: id est, gentem: sic דמה sumitur & infra 10, 15. significat & assimilare; quod hic secuti & LXX. Latinus autem derivavit à דום tacere: sed expositio quam dixi est optima.

## 4:6
Verse 6. MY PEOPLE HAVE BEEN SILENT) Here too the truth will be most correctly cut out: for it is the same word.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE NOT HAD KNOWLEDGE) That is, piety, as above in 1.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE REJECTED KNOWLEDGE) Here God addresses the individual priests, not those established according to the laws, as appears in 1 Kings 12:31, but nevertheless those claiming this name for themselves, and therefore obligated to teach the people, just as one who has acted as a guardian is obligated to guardianship. D. [Digest] concerning him who acts as a guardian.

I WILL REJECT YOU, THAT YOU MAY NOT SERVE ME AS PRIEST) I will strip that person from you.

AND YOU HAVE FORGOTTEN THE LAW OF YOUR GOD) In the Hebrew: And (because) you have forgotten the law of your God: for he continues to address any priest whatsoever.

Thus the Hebrews explain it. But since the Prophet has already refuted homicide before, some interpret this as the incessant mixing of blood, others generally as various crimes, because blood in general is accustomed to denote crime, Psalm 51:16, as the Chaldean [Targum] says, sins are added to sins, and B. Luther: One blood-guilt comes after another. Gregory, Homily 2 on Ezekiel: Blood touches blood when sin is added to sin, so that the soul is stained with blood by the addition of iniquities before the eyes of God. The commentary of Joh. Cocceius on this chapter is wonderful, p. 38. This is a prophetic pericope explaining the corruptions and castigations of the external Christian Church after the liberation from the persecution of the Gentiles, up to the restraint of the Anti-Christ: The thing itself, if I am not mistaken, and the fullness of meaning in the sentences, and the order of the event, and the parallels of the prophecy will be the seal of our application. Which, if it is not received as a designation of the history itself, certainly cannot be called a reason why anyone should deny that the τύπον [type] of the ancient time has been renewed in this later time: But has anyone ever, even in a fever, dreamed that these things pertain to those times which followed the liberation from the persecution of the Gentiles, up to the restraint of the Anti-Christ: but that kind of commentary seems new, strange, and almost cabalistic to certain modern Calvinists, primarily those originating from the Bremen School. Besides this Cocceius, there is a clear example in Lud.

I WILL FORGET YOUR CHILDREN ALSO) They will be orphans and needy.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CONTICUIT POPVLUS MEUS) Etiam hic re- ctissime veritas exscindetur: est enim verbum idem.

EO QVOD NON HABUERIT SCIENTIAM) Id est, pietatem, ut supra 1.

QVIA TU SCIENTIAM REPULISTI) Hic Deus Sacerdotes singulos alloquitur, non qui em secun- dum leges constitutos, ut apparet 1. Reg. 12, 31. sed tamen nomen hoc sibi vindicantes, & propterea obligatos ad do- cendum populum, sicut tutelæ obligatur qui pro tutore se gessit. D. de eo qui pro tutore.

REPELLAM TE, NE SACERDOTIO FUNGA- RIS MIHI) Illam personam tibi detraham.

ET OBLITA ES LEGIS DEI TUI) In Hebræo: Et (quia) oblitus es legis Dei tui: pergit enim Sacerdotem quemlibet alloqui.

Sic Ebræi exponunt. Sed quum homicidium jam antea redarguerit Propheta, alii hoc de in- cessa sanguinis mixtione, alii generaliter de sceleri- bus variis interpretantur, quia sanguis in genere scelus notare solet Psal. 51, 16. ut Chaldæus, pecca- ta peccatis aggregantur, & B. Lutherus: Es kommt eine Blutschuld nach der andern. Gregorius Hom. 2. in Ezech. Sanguis sanguinem tangit, quando pec- catum peccato additur, ut ante Dei oculos adjunctis iniquitatibus anima cruentetur. Mirabilis in hoc capite est Commentarius Joh. Cocceji p. 38. Est hæc pericopa Prophetica 3. explicans corruptiones & castigationes Ecclesiæ Christianæ externa post li- berationem à persecutione gentilium, usque ad coer- citionem Anti-Christi: Res ipsa: ni fallor, & pleni- tudo significationis in sententiis, & ordo rei gestæ, & parallelia prophetiæ erit signaculum nostræ applica- tionis. Quæ, si non recipiatur, ut designatio ipsius hi- storiæ, causa certe dici non potest, quare quis neget, τύπον vetusti temporis posteriore hoc tempore esse re- novatum: Ecquis vero unquam vel per febrim somniavit, hæc ad illa tempora, quæ liberationem à persecutione gentilium sequuta sunt, usque ad coercitionem Anti-Christi pertinere: sed id ge- nus commentaria nova, mira, & pene cabalisti- ca Neotericis quibusdam Calvinianis, imprimis è ScholaBremensi oriundis, propria videntur. Ex- emplo, præter hunc Coccejum, luculento sunt Lud.

OBLIVISCAR FILIORUM TUORUM ET EGO) Erunt pupilli & egentes.

## 4:7
Verse 7. ACCORDING TO THE MULTITUDE OF THEM SO THEY HAVE SINNED AGAINST ME) That is: the more numerous they became, the more gravely they offended me.

I WILL CHANGE THEIR GLORY INTO SHAME) Instead of the honor of the priesthood, I will overwhelm them with disgrace. The Rabbis say that formerly it was כבודי, that is, my glory, namely, I will afflict the land of Israel with disgrace, but this was changed by the Sages, because, forsooth, in later times כבוד began to be used only in the sense of divine power and majesty. Some say that a change happened for a similar reason in Psalm 106:20 and Jeremiah 2:11.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SECUNDUM MULTITUDINEM EORVM SIC PECCAVERUNT MIHI) Id est: quo facti sunt plures, eo gravius me offenderunt.

GLORIAM EORUM IN IGNOMINIAM COM- MUTABO) Pro honore Sacerdotii dedecore eos ob- ruam. Ajunt Rabbini olim fuisse כבודי, id est, gloriam meam, nempe terram Israelis, dedecore afficiam, sed muta- tum hoc à Sapientibus, quia scilicet temporibus ferioribus כבוד usurparı cœpit in solo sensu potentiæ majestatisq; divinæ. Quidam mutatione pari de causa ajunt evenisse Psal. 106, 20. & Jeremiæ 2, 11.

## 4:8
Verse 8. THEY WILL EAT THE SINS OF MY PEOPLE) They will eat

Crocius and Balt. Willius, the former of whom may be seen in the preface to his Syntagma Theologicum, the latter in his Commentary on Zechariah, who also wishes to compare Isaiah and Zechariah with the Johannine Apocalypse in such a way that a continuous history of the New Testament, woven together in the same order, may be elicited from them. These portentous interpretations are displeasing. Therefore, they do not seriously rebuke sins, so that they may receive more victims by which they may be fed.

AND TO THEIR INIQUITY THEY SHALL LIFT UP THEIR SOULS) They lift up their soul: that is, they greatly look for, and expect, that the people may sin as much as possible: this phrase is to be explained in this way from Deuteronomy 24:15.

Latin:

Vers. 8. PECCATA POPULI MEI COMEDENT) Come-

Crocius & Balt. Willius, quorum ille in præfaz. Syn- tag. Theologici, hic in Commentario in Zacha- riam videatur, qui & Esaiam & Zachariam cum Apocalypsi Johannea ita conferre vult, ut inde con- tinua historia Nov. Testamenti eodem ordine per- texta eruatur. Quæ portentosa ἐξηγήματα ho- dunt. Ideo non reprehendunt serio peccata, ut plures ac- cipiant victimas quibus pascantur.

ET AD INIQVITATEM EORVM SUBLE- VABUNT ANIMOS EORVM) Attollunt animam suam: id est, maxime spectant, & exspectant, ut quampluri- mum peccet populus: ita explicanda hæc locutio ex Deuteron. 24, 15.

## 4:9
Verse 9.

AND IT SHALL BE LIKE PEOPLE, LIKE PRIEST) In the same way they will be treated by me: μηδὲ πυρφόρος σωθήσεται.

AND I WILL VISIT UPON HIM HIS WAYS AND HIS THOUGHTS I WILL RENDER TO HIM) Punishments will correspond to sins.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET ERIT SICUT POPVLVS, SIC SA- CERDOS) Pari modo à me tractabuntur : μηδὲ πυρφό- ρος σωθήσεται.

ET VISITABO SVPER EUM VIAS EJUS ET COGITATIONES EJUS REDDAM EI) Pœnæ re- spondebunt peccatis.

## 4:10
AND THEY SHALL EAT AND NOT BE SATISFIED) They will use poorly nourishing foods. The cause follows.

THEY HAVE COMMITTED WHOREDOM, AND HAVE NOT CEASED) They have whored and have not brought forth. That is, they practiced Venus upon males, from which no birth could follow; see below 14. פרץ which properly is to break, is taken among the Hebrews for to bring forth: Gen. 28, 14. and elsewhere.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE FORSAKEN THE LORD IN NOT KEEPING) In not observing the law.

Latin:

ET COMEDENT ET NON SATURABUN- TUR) Male alentibus utentur cibis. Causa sequitur.

FORNICATI SUNT, ET NON CESSAVE- RUNT) Scortati sunt & non pepererunt. Id est, Venerem in mares exercuere, unde partus nullus sequi posset; vide in- fra 14. פרץ quod proprie est rumpere, sumitur apud He- bræos pro parere: Gen. 28, 14. & alibi.

QUONIAM DOMINVM DERELIQVE- RUNT IN NON CUSTODIENDO) Non servan- do legem.

## 4:11
WHOREDOM AND WINE AND DRUNKENNESS TAKE AWAY THE HEART) Whoredom, and wine, and new wine have taken away (from them) the heart: that is, Wisdom.

Latin:

FORNICATIO ET VINVM ET EBRIETAS AVFERVNT COR) Scortatio, & vinum, & mustum abstu- lerunt (ipsis) cor : id est, Sapientiam.

## 4:12
Verse 12.

MY PEOPLE HAVE ASKED AT THEIR WOOD) A Hebrew idiom, for they consulted the wood.

AND THEIR STAFF HATH DECLARED UNTO THEM) They took lots from little rods, using ῥαβδομαντείᾳ after the example of the Chaldeans, concerning which see at Ezech. 21, 21. The LXX have well attained this sense here: ἐν συμβόλοις ἀυτῶν ἐπηρώτων, κὴ ἐν ῥάβδοις ἀυτῶν ἀνήγγειλον ἀυτῷ.

FOR THE SPIRIT OF WHOREDOMS HATH DECEIVED THEM) Here whoredom is idolatry, by the examples of which they were deceived.

AND HAVE COMMITTED WHOREDOM FROM THEIR GOD) So that they might whore against God.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

POPVLVS MEVS IN LIGNO SVO IN- TERROGAVIT) Locutio Hebraica, pro lignum consuluit.

ET BACULUS EJUS ANNUNCIAVIT EI) Sortes captaverunt ex virgulis, usi ῥαβδομαντείᾳ ad exem- plum Chaldæorum, de quo vide ad Ezech. 21, 21. Hunc sensum bene assecuti hic sunt LXX. ἐν συμβόλοις ἀυτῶν ἐπη- ρώτων, κὴ ἐν ῥάβδοις ἀυτῶν ἀνήγγειλον ἀυτῷ.

SPIRITVS ENIM FORNICATIONUM DECE- PIT EOS) Hic fornicatio est idololatria, cujus exemplis decepti sunt.

FT FORNICATI SUNT A DEO SVO) Ut scor- tarentur contra Deum.

## 4:13
UPON THE TOPS OF THE MOUNTAINS) On the summits of the mountains, against the law.

THEY SACRIFICED) They slaughtered victims.

AND UPON THE HILLS THEY BURNED INCENSE) They burned.

AND THE TEREBINTH) Others translate it as oak, others as elm, others as linden. See Gen. 35, 4.

BECAUSE THE SHADOW THEREOF WAS GOOD) ἔυσκιον ὕψος, the Greek poets would say.

THEREFORE YOUR DAUGHTERS SHALL COMMIT WHOREDOM AND YOUR SPOUSES SHALL BE ADULTERESSES) Here also the punishment corresponds to the sin: and great corruptions of morals usually follow idolatry, that is, the contempt of God.

Latin:

SVPER CAPITA MONTIUM) In montium ver- ticibus, contra legem.

SACRIFICABANT) Mactarunt victimas.

ET SUPER COLLES ACCENDEBANT THT- MIAMA) Adoleverunt.

ET TEREBINTHVM) Alii vertunt quercum, alii ulmum, alii tiliam. Vide Gen. 35, 4.

QVIA BONA ERAT UMBRA EJUS) ἔυσκιον ὕψος, dicerent Poetæ Græci.

IDEO FORNICABUNTUR FILIÆ VESTRÆ ET SPONSÆ VESTRÆ ADULTERÆ ERUNT) Hic quoque peccato pœna respondet : & solent plerum- que idololatolatriam, id est, Dei comtemtum, magnæ sequi morum corruptelæ.

## 4:14
Verse 14.

I WILL NOT PUNISH YOUR DAUGHTERS WHEN THEY SHALL COMMIT WHOREDOM, NOR YOUR SPOUSES WHEN THEY SHALL COMMIT ADULTERY) I will overlook these things, because you fathers and husbands gave the cause.

FOR THEY THEMSELVES WITH HARLOTS) In the Hebrew: They separate themselves with harlots: that is, they go into the groves. 1 Kings 15, verse 13.

AND WITH THE EFFEMINATE THEY SACRIFICED) He explained קדשוח, as if it were קדשים: in which way also Aquila here translates ἐνηλλαγμένας, namely those who changed the natural use into that which is against nature. But the word which is read here is feminine: and, as the Hebrews note, it signifies a female priest who prostituted herself in honor of the idol Beelphegor.

AND THE PEOPLE THAT DOTH NOT UNDERSTAND SHALL BE BEATEN) The people not understanding: that is, not caring for God, shall fall.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

NON VISITABO SVPER FILIAS VESTRAS CUM FVERINT FORNICATÆ, ET SVPER SPONSAS VESTRAS CVM ADVLTERAVERUNT) Dissimulabo ista, quia vos Patres & mariti causam dedistis.

QUONIAM IPSI CUM MERETRI- CIBVS CONVERSABANTVR) In He- bræo: Cum scortis separant se: id est, in lucos eunt. 1, Reg. 15. vers. 13.

ET CVM EFFEMINATIS SACRIFICABANT) Explicavit קדשוח, quasi esset קדשים : quo- modo & Aquila hic vertit ἐνηλλαγμένας, eos scilicet, qui με- τήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν. Sed vox quæ hic legitur feminina est: &, ut Hebræi notant, signi- ficat sacerdotem feminam quæ se vulgabat in honorem ido- li Beelphegor.

ET POPVLVS NON INTELLIGENS VAPV- LABIT) Populus non intelligens : id est, Deum non cu- rans, corruet.

## 4:15
Verse 15.

IF YOU PLAY THE WHORE, O ISRAEL) If it pleases you to follow idols.

LET NOT JUDAH AT LEAST OFFEND) Let the two tribes beware for themselves, lest they follow such examples.

AND DO NOT ENTER INTO GILGAL) This speech turns to the men of the two tribes. Gilgal was a place on the very borders of the ten tribes: where idols were worshipped. Below 9, 15.

AND DO NOT GO UP TO BETHAVEN) The LXX [translate] τὸν οἶκον ὣν in the latter part, recently from the Hebrew: which other interpreters, translating into Greek, have called, Theodotion, οἶκον τῆς ἀδικίας [house of injustice], Aquila & Symmachus οἶκον ἀνωφελῆ [useless house]. The Chaldean well translates the sense as Bethel both here and below 15; for that is the ancient name of the place: but the pious, in execration of the idolatry which was practiced there from the times of Jeroboam, called it Beth-on, or Beth-aven, that is, the house of vanity: for idols are vanity: and therefore this interpreter below 6, 8 translates און as idol, not badly as to the sense. He also joined Gilgal & Bethel, as the principal places of idolatry, in Amos 5, verse 5, and says that בֵּית־אֵל will be לְאָוֶן into nothing, with an allusion made to that other name בֵּית־אָוֶן. NOR SHALL YOU SWEAR, THE LORD LIVES) Namely, in that temple of Bethel or Beth-aven: for they called those calves יהוה, because they thought that He was rightly worshipped in such an image, for reasons stated elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

SI FORNICARIS TV ISRAEL) Si tibi libet se- qui idola.

NON DELINQVAT SALTEM JUDA) Ca- veant sibi duæ tribus, ne talia exempla sequantur.

ET NOLITE INGREDI IN GALGALA) Hic sermo se convertit ad homines duarum tribuum. Galgala locus erat in ipsis finibus decem tribuum : ubi idola cole- bantur. Infra 9, 15.

ET NE ASCENDERITIS IN BETHAVEN) LXX. τὸν οἶκον ὣν posteriore parte ex Hebræo recenta : quam alii Interpretes Græce vertentes dixere, Theodotion, οἶκον τῆς ἀδικίας, Aquila & Symmachus οἶκον ἀνωφελῆ. Chaldæus ad sensum bene vertit Bethel tam hic quam infra 15. id enim antiquum loco nomen : sed pii in execrationem idolatriæ, quæ ibi exercita à Jeroboami temporibus, dixere Beth-on, vel Beth-aven, id est, domum vanitatis : idola enim vanitas : ideoqs hic interpres infra 6, 8. און vertit idolum, non male ad sensum. Gilgala & Bethel, ut præcipua idolo- latriæ loca, conjunxit etiam Amos 5. vers. 5. & dicit בֵּית־אֵל futurum לְאָוֶן in nihilum, allusione facta ad il- lud nomen alterum בֵּית־אָוֶן. NEQVE JURAVERITIS VIVIT DOMINUS) Nempe in illo templo Bethelis sive Beth-aven: nam illi vi- tulos istos vocabant יהוה, quod putarent eum in tali ima- gine recte coli, ob causas dictas alibi.

## 4:16
Verse 16.

FOR AS A LASCIVIOUS COW ISRAEL HAS DECLINED) The Prophet alludes to those images. They wanted to make God such a one. But they themselves are such. In the Greek here [it is] ὡς δάμαλις παροιστρῶσα [as a heifer stung by a gadfly]: and those calves erected by Jeroboam are likewise called δαμάλεις [heifers] in the Greek 1 Kings 12, verse 28 and following. Heifers are accustomed to stray from the Shepherd. NOW THE LORD WILL FEED THEM AS A LAMB IN A LARGE PLACE) And this is a χλευασμὸς [mockery] from an ambiguity. Lambs love to graze in a large place. God will scatter Israel throughout the whole kingdom of the Assyrians.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

QUONIAM SICUT VACCA LASCIVIENS DECLINAVIT ISRAEL) Alludit Propheta ad illas imagines. Deum voluerunt facere talem. At ipsi tales sunt. In Græco hic ὡς δάμαλις παροιστρῶσα: & illi vituli ab Jeroboamo erecti, dicuntur itidem δαμάλεις in Græco 1. Reg. 12. vers. 28. & sequentibus. Juvencæ solent aber- rare a Pastore. NUNC PASCET EOS DOMINUS QUASI AGNUM IN LATITUDINE) Et hic est χλευασμὸς ex ambiguo. Late pascere amant agni. Deus Israelem disperget per totum Assyriorum regnum.

## 4:17
Verse 17.

EPHRAIM IS A PARTAKER OF IDOLS) He continues to address those of the two tribes. Ephraim is addicted to idols. Thus the ten tribes are called, because the princes had been from that tribe. The sense is: they are incurable from this disease. LET HIM ALONE) Leave him be, O Judah.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

PARTICEPS IDOLORUM EPHRAIM) Per- git illos de duabus tribubus alloqui. Addictus est idolis Ephraim. Sic vocantur decem tribus, quod principes ex ea tribu fuissent. Sensus est: sunt illi insanabiles ab isto morbo. DIMITTE EUM) Missum eum fac, ô Juda.

## 4:18
Verse 18.

THEIR FEAST IS SEPARATED) Their drink has become sour: that is, it is unworthy to be drunk, which has been offered to gods. The Chaldean takes סָר for a prince, & this interpreter wishes it to be: The princes sought a feast. But the LXX [take] סָר as elders, [or] it is 'approached': סֹבְאִים are the drunkards, that is, the idolaters, for whom they themselves placed the name of a people no less impious: for they translate ἠρέλισε Χαναναίους, he loved the Canaanites: but Jerome reads ἠρέθισε, that is, he provoked. THEY HAVE COMMITTED WHOREDOM) Because they are idolaters. THEY HAVE LOVED TO BRING IGNOMINY, ITS PROTECTORS) They loved to say to their nobles: bring ignominy. They were saying, bring idols: but the Prophet says not what they themselves were saying, but what the reality was: such as we have noted elsewhere. מָגִנֶּיהָ, the Chaldean also translates as nobles.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

SEPARATUM EST CONVIVIUM EORUM) Acidus factus est potus eorum: id est, indignus est, qui biba- tur, qui diis libatus est. Chaldæus סָר sumit pro principe, & interpres hic vult esse: Principes quæsiveruut convivi- um. LXX. vero senibus סָר est acceffit: סֹבְאִים sunt Sabæi, id est, idololatræ, pro quibus ipsi posuere populi non minus impii nomen: vertunt enim ἠρέλισε Χαναναίους, amavit Chananæos: sed Hieronymus legit ἠρέθισε, id est, provocavit. FORNICATIONE FORNICATI SUNT) Quia sunt idololatræ. DILEXERUNT AFFERRE IGNOMINIAM PROTECTORES EJUS) Amarunt dicere proceres eo- rum: afferte ignominiam. Illi dicebant, afferte idola: sed Propheta dicit non quod ipsi dicebant, sed quod res erat: qualia & alibi notavimus. מָגִנֶּיהָ, proceres vertit & Chaldæus,

## 4:19
Verse 19.

THE WIND HAS BOUND HIM IN ITS WINGS) The spirit, that is, the wind, will carry him away as if bound in its wings: that is, he will be carried away most swiftly into a far-distant region. Both Greek and Latin poets attribute wings to the winds. AND THEY SHALL BE CONFOUNDED BECAUSE OF THEIR SACRIFICES) So that they may be confounded. That is, so that they may see that those sacrifices made to idols have profited them nothing.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

LIGAVIT EUM SPIRITUS IN ALIS SUIS) Spiritus, id est, ventus eum, velut alis suis ligatum auferet: id est, celerrime auferetur in regionem longe diffitam. Ven- tis alas tribuunt & Græci & Latini Poëtæ. ET CONFUNDENTUR A SACRIFICIIS SUIS) Ut confundantur. Id est, ut videant sacrificia illa idolis facta nihil sibi profuisse.

## 5:1 Argument
SERMON IV. PENITENTIAL. CHAPTER V. Comminatory.

Here is contained a threat against all Israelite estates, because on account of continuous idolatry they are finally to be punished, and will seek the Lord in vain: inasmuch as they are mere hypocrites, and perfidious despisers of the Lord, therefore they are shortly to be devastated by enemies already imminent, not without damage also to the Jewish people. The idolatrous priest will bear the punishment with the leader.

Vers. 1.

HEAR THIS O PRIESTS) You who call yourselves priests, and are held as such: as above 4. vers. 6. HOUSE OF ISRAEL) Of the ten tribes. AND HOUSE OF THE KING) Of Menahem. JUDGMENT IS FOR YOU) Punishment hangs over you, which is indicated metonymically by the name of judgment. A SNARE HAS BEEN MADE FOR MIZPAH) In the Greek also τῇ σκοπιᾷ. But it is a proper name in Mizpah. Mizpah and Tabor are wooded mountains where much bird-catching was practiced; Thus by the bad example of the Israelites, many Jews also were seduced. Below 3,

UPON THABOR) Ιταβύριον, according to the Greeks and Josephus. Verse 2.

Latin:

CONCIO IV. POENITENTIALIS. CAPUT V. Comminatorium.

Habetur hic comminatio adversus omnes sta- tus Israëliticos, quod ob idololatriam con- tinuam tandem puniendi, nequicquam quæsituri Dominum sint: utpote hypocri- tæ meri, & perfidi Dominum contemnen- tes, ideo brevi ab hostibus jam imminen- tibus, non sine damno etiam populi Ju- daici, devastandi. Cum Duce supplicium feret idolatra sacerdos.

Vers. 1.

AUDITE HOC SACERDOTES) Qui sa- cerdotes vos dicitis, & pro talibus habemini: ut supra 4. vers. 6. DOMUS ISRAEL) Decem tribuum. ET DOMUS REGIS) Manahemi. VOBIS JUDICIUM EST) Vobis pœna imminet, quæ μετωνυμικῶς judicii nomine indicatur. LAQVEUS FACTUS EST SPECULATIONI) In Græco quoque τῇ σκοπιᾷ. Sed est nomen proprium in Mispa. Mispa & Thabor nemorosi montes ubi multa aucupia exercebantur; Sic malo exemplo IsraëBackgroundlitarium, etiam Judæi multi seducebantur. Infra 3,

SVPER THABOR) Ιταβύριον, Græcis & Jo- sepho. Vers. 2.

## 5:2
AND YOU HAVE DECLINED VICTIMS INTO THE DEPTH) In the Hebrew: inclining victims to cast them into the depth. It was the custom of idolaters to cast slaughtered victims into a cave in which there was fire. See Euripides, Iphigenia in Tauris. The transition from the second person to the third is frequent among the Hebrews.

AND I AM THE INSTRUCTOR OF THEM ALL) Since I instructed them daily, namely through Ahijah, Elijah, Elisha, and other Prophets. Verse 3.

Latin:

ET VICTIMAS DECLINASTIS IN PROFUN- DUM) In Hebræo: victimas inclinantes in profundum deje- cere. Mos idololatrarum victimas jugulatas dejicere in specum, in quo erat ignis. Vide Euripidem Iphigenia in Tauris. Transitus de persona secunda in tertiam fre- quens Hebræis.

ET EGO ERUDITOR OMNIUM EORVM) Cum ego quotidie eos instituerem, nempe per Achiam, Eliam, Elisæum, & Prophetas alios. Vers. 3.

## 5:3
I KNOW EPHRAIM) I know them. Ephraim is the principal part of the ten tribes.

AND ISRAEL IS NOT HIDDEN FROM ME) The other nine tribes.

EPHRAIM HAS COMMITTED FORNICATION) In the Hebrew: you commit fornication. You persist in idolatry. Verse 4.

Latin:

EGO SCIO EPHRAIM) Novi eos. Ephraim pars præcipua decem tribuum.

ET ISRAEL NON EST ABSCONDITVS A ME) Novem tribus aliæ.

FORNICATVS EST EPHRAIM) In Hebræo: fornicaris. Pergis in idololatria. Vers. 4.

## 5:4
BECAUSE THE SPIRIT OF FORNICATIONS IS IN THE MIDST OF THEM) Like the spirit of perversities in Isaiah 19, verse 14; they are clearly driven by the gadfly of idolatry.

AND THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN THE LORD) They are so disposed that they do not know the Lord. Verse 5.

Latin:

QVIA SPIRITUS FORNICATIONVM IN MEDIO EORVM) Qui Spiritus perversita- tum Esaïæ 19. vers. 14. idololatriæ œstro plane sunt perciti.

ET DOMINUM NON COGNOVERUNT) Eo sis, ne Dominum cognoscant. Vers. 5.

## 5:5
AND THE ARROGANCE OF ISRAEL SHALL ANSWER IN HIS FACE) The contumacy of Israel shall bear witness against him. For that is often ענה. EPHRAIM SHALL FALL) That is, the Ephraimites.

IN THEIR INIQUITY) As a punishment owed to them.

JUDAH ALSO SHALL FALL WITH THEM) The two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, having followed the examples of the ten tribes, shall fall under the Egyptians and Chaldeans. Verse 6.

Latin:

ET RESPONDEBIT ARROGANTIA ISRAEL IN FACIE EJUS) Contumacia Israe- lis contra ipsum testimonium feret. Id enim sæpe est ענה. EPHRAIM RUENT) Id est, Ephraimitæ.

IN INIQVITATE SUA) In pœnam sibi de- bitam.

RUET ETIAM JUDA CVM EIS) Duæ tribus Judæ & Benjaminis exempla decem tribuum secutæ, cor- ruent sub Ægyptiis & Chaldæis. Vers. 6.

## 5:6
WITH THEIR FLOCKS AND HERDS THEY SHALL GO TO SEEK THE LORD, AND SHALL NOT FIND HIM) They shall seek the peace of God through victims in vain.

HE IS TAKEN AWAY FROM THEM) He withdrew himself far from them. Verse 7.

Latin:

IN GREGIBUS SUIS ET ARMENTIS VADENT AD QVÆRENDUM DOMINVM, ET NON INVENIENT) Pacem Dei per victimas frustra exposcent.

ABLATUS EST AB IIS) Subduxit se longe ab eis. Vers. 7.

## 5:7
BECAUSE THEY HAVE BEGOTTEN STRANGE CHILDREN) From the women of those nations with whom they had no right of marriage.

NOW SHALL A MONTH DEVOUR THEM.) A monthly payment, which the King imposed upon his people, to repair the damage he had done by giving great sums of money to Phul, King of Assyria, 2 Kings 15, verses 19, 20. See also below 8, verse 10. The Greeks did not read חדש, but חסל, as Jerome notes here.

Other expositions of what 'month' denotes here were exhibited especially by the blessed Meisner, p. 529. By 'month' four things can be understood: (1) The New Moon, or the idolatrous feast of the new moon, in which sense 'month' is taken in 1 Sam. 20, v. 5; 2 Kings 4, v. 23; Is. 66, v. 23. This feast is said to devour the Israelites because it was going to result in destruction; they were about to perish on account of it along with their parts, that is, with all their sacrifices. Luther: 'Therefore the new moon shall also devour them with their inheritance.' (2) A certain month in particular, in which a slaughter was to happen in Israel. Lyra thinks the month of July is noted, in which Samaria was captured. The Rabbis explain it as the month of Ab, which corresponds to our August, and was most calamitous to the Jews because of the burning of the first temple, 2 Kings 25, v. 9, and the final destruction of Jerusalem, which took place on the 10th of August. Hence, on the ninth day of the same month, the Jews observe a fast most strictly, walk with bare feet, sit on the ground, and read through the Lamentations of Jeremiah with great wailing and howling, as Gesner notes on page 213. (3) A monthly space in general, so that it may be implied that the punishment is not to come after many years, but shortly, and as it were within a month; therefore some explain it as the miserable slaughter made by the army of Pekah, where one hundred and twenty thousand Jews were slain, 2 Chron. 28, verse 6. Finally (4) a continuation of the slaughter, so that 'month' is put for any one month. Thus Jonathan understood it: 'Now I will bring upon them peoples in every month,' which history testifies also happened, 2 Kings 15. For first came Phul Asser, who fined King Menahem with a huge sum of money, verses 19, 20. After him, Tiglath-Pileser, under King Pekah, led away a good part of the people into Assyria, verse 29. Finally, Shalmaneser first made King Hoshea a tributary, 2 Kings 17, v. 3. Then he overturned the whole Kingdom and carried away the remnants of the people, v. 6. I add a fifth exposition: 'a month shall devour,' namely, one. Let all things be consumed in a short time, namely, the space of one month. Thus Zech. 2, v. 8: 'I will cut off three shepherds in one month.' These are the words of the blessed Meisner. But that explanation of Grotius does not seem inconsistent, that by 'month' is understood a monthly payment. I have decided to present these together and commit them to the judgment of the reader.

WITH THEIR PARTS) With their possessions. Both they and their land shall be pressed by heavy tributes. Verse 8.

Latin:

QVIA FILIOS ALIENOS GENVERUNT) Ex feminis earum gentium, quibuscum jus connubii ipsis non erat.

NUNC DEVORABIT EOS MENSIS.) Menstrua pensio, quam Rex populo suo injunxit, ut sarciat damnum quod fecit, magnas pecunias dando Phuli Regi Assyriæ, 2. Reg. 15. vers. 19. 20. Vide & infra 8. vers. 10. Græci non חדש legerunt, sed חסל, ut hic no- tat Hieronymus.

ALias expositiones, quid mensis hic notet, exhi- buit imprimis B. Meisnerus p 529. Per mensem quatuor possunt intelligi, (1) Novilunium, vel fe- stum novilunii idololatricum, quo sensu mensis su- mitur 1. Sam. 20. v. 5. 2. Reg. 4. v. 23. Es. 66. v. 23. Hoc festum dicitur Israelitas devorare, quia cessu- rum erat in interitum, perituri ob id erant una cum partibus, id est, cum omnibus sacrificiis suis. Luthe- rus: Darumb wird sie auch der Neumond fressen mit ihrem Erbtheil. (2) Certus mensis in specie, quo clades in Israel debebat contingere. Lyra putat no- tari mensem Julium, quo capta fuerit Samaria. Rabbini exponunt de mense Ab, qui respondet no- stro Augusto, & Judæis maxime fuit calamitosus ob primi templi exustionem 2. Reg. 25. v. 9. & ulti- mam Hierosolymæ destructionem die 10. Augusti factam. Hinc nono ejusdem mensis die Judæi stri- ctissime servant jejunium, incedunt nudis pedibus, sedent humi, & threnos Jeremiæ magno cum boa- tu & ululatu perlegunt, notante Gesnero pag. 213. (3.) Menstruum spatium in genere, ut innuatur, pœ- nam non post multos annos, sed brevi, & velut intra mensem imminere, ideoque nonnulli exponunt de miseranda clade, per exercitum Pekæ facta, ubi cen- tum viginti millia Judæorum cæsa sunt, 2. Paral. 28. vers. 6. Tandem (4) continuatio cladis, ut men- sis ponatur pro unoquolibet mense. Sic Jonathan in- tellexit: Nunc adducam in eos populos unoquo- que mense, quod etiam factum esse testatur hi- storia 2. Reg. 15. Nam primum venit Phul Asser, qui Regem Menahem ingenti pecunia mulctavit vers. 19. 20. Post Tiglat Pelasser sub Rege Peka bonam populi partem abduxit in Assyriam vers. 29. De- mum Salmanasser Regem Osee primum fecit tri- butarium, 2. Reg. 17. v. 3. Deinde totum Regnum evertit, & reliquias populi transtulit, v. 6. Addo expositionem quintam : devorabit mensis, scilicet unus. Omnia absumantur brevi tempore, videlicet spatio unius mensis. Sic Zach. 2. v. 8. Exscindam tres pastores mense uno. Hæc B. Meisnerus. Sed nec inconcinna videtur illa Grotii explicatio, quod per mensem intelligatur menstrua pensio. Conjun- ctim illas sistere, atque arbitrio lectoris commit- tere placuit.

CUM PARTIBVS SUIS) Cum possessionibus ipso- rum. Etipsi, & terra eorum prementur gravibus tributis. Vers. 8.

## 5:8
BLOW THE CORNET IN GIBEAH, THE TRUMPET IN RAMAH) A cornet made of horn, a trumpet made of brass or silver. It signifies that enemies are about to come upon both kingdoms: for the arrival of enemies was signified by cornets and trumpets. Gibeah and Ramah are of the portion of Benjamin, about seven miles from Jerusalem, as Jerome notes here. See 1 Kings 15, 17, 22.

HOWL IN BETH-AVEN) In Bethel, as above 4, 15.

AFTER THEE, O BENJAMIN) Which city is very near to you, O Benjamin. For where the tribe of Benjamin ends, not far away in the tribe of Ephraim, Bethel was founded, as Jerome says here.

Latin:

CLANGITE BUCCINA IN GABBA, TUBA IN RAMA) Buccina ex cornu, tuba ex ære, vel argento. Significat hostes superventuros utrique regno: nam hostium adventus per buccinas & tubas significabatur. Gabba & Rama sunt de portione Benjaminis, septimo fer- me ab Hierosolymis lapide, ut hic notat Hieronymus. Vi- de 1. Reg. 15, 17. 22.

ULULATE IN BETHAVEN) In Bethel, ut su. pra 4, 15.

POST TERGVM TVVM BENJAMIN) Quæ urbs valde tibi propinqua est, o Benjamin. Ubi enim tri- bus finitur Benjamin, haud procul in tribu Ephraim con- dita est Bethel, ut hic ait Hieronymus.

## 5:9
Verse 9.

EPHRAIM SHALL BE IN DESOLATION) It shall become waste.

IN THE DAY OF REBUKE) When God shall send Shalmaneser against him.

IN THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL I HAVE SHOWN FAITHFULNESS) When I shall show constancy against the tribes of Israel, namely my own in fulfilling those things which the Prophets foretold.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

EPHRAIM IN DESOLATIONE ERIT) Vasta fiet.

IN DIE CORREPTIONIS) Cum Deus ipsi im. mittet Salmanasarum.

IN TRIBUBUS ISRAEL OSTENDI FIDEM) Cum adversus tribus Israel ostendam constantiam, meam scili- cet in iis implendis quæ Prophetæ prædixerunt.

## 5:10
THE PRINCES OF JUDAH HAVE BECOME AS THOSE REMOVING THE BOUNDARY) He often passes from this kingdom to that, so that he may show the sins of both, and announce their punishments. To move boundaries established by men is a grave crime, Deut. 19, verse 14; how much more, then, to move the boundaries established by God, that is, the law, which the princes of Judah did: as Ahaz, 2 Kings 16, 10; 2 Chronicles 28, 3.

I WILL POUR OUT MY WRATH UPON THEM AS WATER) That is, with great force.

Latin:

FACTI SUNT PRINCIPES JUDA QVASI ASSUMENTES TERMINVM) Transit sæpe ab hoc regno in illud, ut utriusque peccata ostendat, & pœnas prænunciet, Terminos ab hominibus constitu- tos movere crimen grave, Deuter. 19. vers. 14. quan- tum ergo, constitutos a Deo terminos, id est, legem,quod fecere principes Judæ : ut Achazus, 2. Reg. 16, 10. 2. Paralip. 28, 3.

SUPER EOS EFFUNDAM QVASI AQVAM IRAM MEAM) Id est, magno impetu.

## 5:11
Verse 11.

EPHRAIM IS SUFFERING CALUMNY: BROKEN BY JUDGMENT) Ephraim is oppressed, and broken by judgment. The people in the ten tribes are oppressed both by the force of the more powerful and by unjust judgments.

BECAUSE HE BEGAN TO GO AFTER FILTH) Because the judges gave themselves over to filth, that is, to foul avarice. Thus the Chaldean here. And so the Interpreters took צו, by apocope for צואה, which in the Chaldean signifies filth.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

CALUMNIAM PATIENS EST EPHRAIM: FRACTVS JUDICIO) Opprimitur Ephraim, & judicio frangitur. Tum vi potentiorum tum iniquis judiciis op- primitur populus in decem tribubus.

QVONIAM COEPIT IRE POST SOR- DES) Quia judices se dederunt sordibus, id est, fœ- dæ avaritiæ. Ita hic Chaldæus. Itaque sumfere Inter- pretes צו, per ἀποκοπὴν pro צואה, quod Chaldæus sordes significat.

## 5:12
Verse 12.

AND I AM AS A MOTH TO EPHRAIM AND AS ROTTENNESS TO THE HOUSE OF JUDAH) A moth consumes a garment, rottenness the flesh itself. The superiority of the two tribes over the other ten is signified, on account of the house of David and the Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET EGO QVASI TINEA EPHRAIM ET QUASI PUTREDO DOMUS JUDÆ) Tinea vestem consumit, putredo carnem ipsam. Significatur præstan- tia duarum tribuum præ decem aliis, propter domum Da- vidis & Templum.

## 5:13
Verse 13.

AND EPHRAIM SAW HIS LANGUOR) His wound: for the word מחלים is also taken in this sense in 1 Kings 22, 34, and following.

AND JUDAH HIS BINDING) His wound. It is called מזור, because it is accustomed to be bound. Therefore Aquila translates it ἐπίδεσιν: but the LXX ὀδύνην. Both peoples saw in what great evils they were involved.

AND EPHRAIM WENT TO ASSYRIA) Menahem will send gifts to Pul 2 Kings 15:20.

AND SENT TO THE AVENGER KING) He will send, supply, Judah, to King Tiglath-Pileser so that he may be a helper to him: or avenger: for that is what ירב means, as Jerome rightly thinks from Judges 6:32. You will see this fulfilled in 2 Kings 16:6, 2 Chronicles 28:16.

The Greeks thought the name Ἰαρεὶβ was a proper name, for which already in Jerome's time it was wrongly written Ἰαρεὶμ, due to the similar ductus of the letters β & μ, which those who are versed in manuscripts know.

Some take the word Jareb as a proper name along with the Greeks, and some make it the name of a city in which the King had his seat, others the name of the King, which designates either some certain King so called, or indefinitely the Assyrian King, since those Kings were called Jareb, as avengers of the city and scourges of God, Is. 10, 5. We do not disapprove of Grotius's explanation, with which the Chaldean also agrees: They sent to the King, that he might come to avenge them. On ch. 10, 6. Grotius has it thus: A gift to the avenging King: It is here again in the Hebrew יריב as above 5, 13. that is, to a helper, a protector. They called the lesser Kings by this name, and others the greater, to whose faith and protection they had given themselves. See 2 Kings 17, 3.

AND HE HIMSELF) The Assyrian. HE WILL NOT BE ABLE TO HEAL YOU, NOR IS HE ABLE TO LOOSE THE BOND FROM YOU) And he will not cure your wound. He will not be able to keep the two tribes unharmed, either from Phaceas the son of Romelia, 2 Chron. 28. verse 6. or from the Egyptians, 2 Kings 23. verse 29. But as for the ten tribes, it is so far from the case that the Assyrian wishes to rescue them from evils, that he will inflict upon them things much greater than before: namely, in the time of Salmanasar.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET VIDIT EPHRAIM LANGUOREM SVVM) Vulnus suum: nam & verbum מחלים hoc sensu sumitur 1. Regum 22, 34. & sequentibus.

ET JUDA VINCULUM SVVM) Plagam suam. Ea dicitur מזור, quod obligari soleat. Ideo Aquila ἐπίδε- σιν vertit: at LXX. ὀδύνην. Viderunt populus uterque quantis in malis versarentur.

ET ABIIT EPHRAIM AD ASSVR) Manahem dona mittet Phuli 2. Reg. 15, 20.

ET MISIT AD REGEM ULTOREM) Mittet, supple, Juda, ad Regem Teglathphalasarum ut ipsi sit adjutor: sive ultor : id enim est ירב, ut recte putat Hieronymus ex Jud.6,32.Videbis impletū hoc 2. Reg. 16,6. 2. Paral. 28,16.

Græci Ἰαρεὶβ nomen putarunt proprium, pro quo jam Hie- ronymi tempore male Ἰαρεὶμ scribebatur, vicino ductu lite- rarum β & μ, quod norunt, qui in manuscriptis versati sunt.

Nonnulli pro nomine proprio vocem Jareb cum Græcis habent, idq; alii urbis, in qua Rex se- dem habuerit, alii Regis nomen faciunt, quod vel certum aliquem Regem ita appellatum, vel indefi- nite Regem Assyrium, quum Reges illi dicti fuerint Jareb, ceu vindices urbis & flagella Dei Es. 10, 5. de- lignet. Non improbamus Grotii explicationem, cui consonat etiam Chaldæus : Miserunt ad Re- gem, ut adventaret ultum eos. Ad c. 10, 6. ita habet Grotius : Munus Regi ultori : Est hic iterum in Hebræo יריב ut supra 5, 13. id est, adjutori, protecto- ri. Appellabant hoc nomine Reges minores, alios majores, quorum se in fidem clientelamq́; dederant. Vide 2. Reg. 17, 3.

ET IPSE) Assyrius. NON POTERIT SANARE VOS, NEC SOL- VERE POTEST A VOBIS VINCULUM) Et non curabit plagam vestram. Duas tribus non poterit in- demnes præstare, aut à Phacea Romeliæ filio, 2. Paral. 28. vers. 6. aut ab Ægyptiis, 2. Regum 23. vers. 29. Decem autem tribus tantum abest ut a malis eripere velit Assy- rius, multo quam ante majora illis inferet : nempe Salma- nasari tempore.

## 5:14
Ver. 14. FOR I AM AS A LIONESS TO EPHRAIM) As a panther to Ephraim: for Jerome noted here that שחל is a panther, and we did so on Job 10. verse 16. It will be of no use to seek the favor of men, when I (says God) wish to consume the ten tribes as swiftly as a panther comes, but the two tribes as savagely as a lion is wont.

I WILL TAKE AND GO) A similitude drawn from wild beasts: which return to their dens with their prey: which the following words also express.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QUONIAM EGO QUASI LEÆNA EPHRAIM) Quasi panthera Ephraim : nam שחל pan- theram esse & hic Hieronymus notavit, & nos ad Jobum 10. vers. 16. Nihil proderit hominum favorem quærere, cum ego (inquit Deus) velim absumere decem tribus tam velociter, quam venit panthera, duas autem tribus tam sæ- ve quam solet leo.

CAPIAM ET VADAM) Similitudine à feris du- cta : quæ cum præda in lustra redeunt : quod & sequen- tia exprimunt.

## 5:15
UNTIL YOU FAIL) Until they acknowledge themselves guilty. Thus the word אשם is used in Levit. 4, 13.

AND SEEK MY FACES) In the Hebrew: they shall seek. My face, that is, my favor.

Latin:

DONEC DEFICIATIS) Donec se reos peragant. Ita vox אשם usurpatur Levit. 4, 13.

ET QUÆRATIS FACIES MEAS) In Hebræo: quærant. Facies mea, id est, favorem meum.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. An exhortation to serious conversion.

Because of the injustice of the nobles, a just divine plague, and because of the abandonment of God, the leonine wrath and ferocity of God are denounced to Ephraim, as also to Judah, with the turning away of the face of grace, until, having acknowledged their guilt, they are converted to God who heals us after wounds and plagues and raises us up with Christ resurrected on the third day for our sake, and more fully recognize the Lord breaking forth like the dawn in the time of the New Testament through faith and enjoy his grace: to that end, they are still perpetually to be grieved and mortified by the Prophets, so that they may be free for true charity and the knowledge of God, and not indeed for sacrifices offered without faith, nor continue to violate the divine covenant, like Adam, with Gilead through idols and innocent blood: promises to the Jewish people of still some joyful harvest in the liberation from the Babylonian captivity.

He strikes so that he may heal those desiring help, as once Jesus did. V. 1. IN THEIR TRIBULATION THEY SHALL RISE EARLY TO ME) They shall awake. For these things cohere plainly with those which precede, and it is one discourse. They shall awake as if from the sleep of sins, when they shall be in exile.

COME AND LET US RETURN TO THE LORD) Just as those words which we have just now had are wrongly torn from the previous ones in the Greek and Latin, so are these in the Hebrew: for the sense hangs, and one must understand 'saying' before the word 'come'. The Chaldean added 'saying'.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. Exhortatio ad seriam conversionem.

Ob injustitiam procerum plaga justa divina, & ob derelictionem Dei leonina ira Dei fero- cia denunciantur Ephraimo, ut & Judæ, cum aversione faciei gratiæ, donec agnita culpa ad Deum nos post vulnera & plagas sanantem & cum Christo tertia die nostri causa resuscitato erigentem conversi Domi- num instar auroræ prorumpentem Nov. Test. tempore plenius per fidem agnoscant & gratia ejus fruantur : Eo fine perpetuo adhuc per Prophetas dolandi & mortifi- candi, ut veræ charitati & cognitioni Dei vacent, non vero sacrificiis sine fide offeren- dis, neq́; fœdus divinum, instar Adami, cum Galead per idola, & sanguinem innoxium violare pergant : promissa populo Judaico adhuc messe aliqua læta in liberatione è captivitate Babylonica.

Percutit ut cupidos opis olim sanet Jesus. V. 1. IN TRIBULATIONE SVA MANE CONSVR- GANT AD ME) Evigilent. Cohærent enim hæc plane cum iis, quæ præcedunt, & unus est sermo. Evigilent velut è somno peccatorum, ubi in exsilio erunt.

VENITE ET REVERTAMVR AD DOMI- NUM) Sicut illa verba, quæ jamjam habuimus, male di- vulsa sunt à prioribus in Græco & Latino, ita hæc in He- bræo : pendet enim sensus, & subaudiendum est dicentes, ante verbum venite. Chaldæus dicent addidit.

## 6:2
V. 2. HE HAS TAKEN) He has torn apart, namely the Israelite body. AND HE WILL HEAL US) He will restore to their homeland those who have amended themselves. But those were many more from the two tribes than from the ten, but yet some also from these, ἡ ἐκλογή.

HE WILL STRIKE) Nay, he has struck: for those who are to be in exile are introduced speaking.

Latin:

V. 2. IPSE CEPIT) Discerpsit, corpus nempe Israeliticum. ET SANABIT NOS) Restituet in patriam eos qui se emendaverint. Ii autem multo plures fuere de duabus tri- bubus quam de decem, sed tamen & ex his aliqui, ἡ ἐκλογή.

PERCUTIET) Imo percussit: introducuntur enim loquentes ii qui in exsilio futuri sunt.

## 6:3
AND HE WILL HEAL US: HE WILL REVIVE US AFTER TWO DAYS: ON THE THIRD DAY HE WILL RAISE US UP, AND WE SHALL LIVE IN HIS SIGHT) That we may live. The sense first obvious is: after the Hebrews have amended themselves, it will come to pass that God will shortly restore them from such great miseries, which are wont to be compared to death. But without doubt, by the will of God, these words were directed in such a way, as were many others of the Prophets, that they might most openly prefigure to us the time within which both Christ was to receive life, and his Church was to receive hope. From this passage, the Jews imagine that the final and universal judgment will be completed within three days.

WE SHALL KNOW AND WE SHALL FOLLOW, THAT WE MAY KNOW THE LORD: AS THE DAWN HIS GOING FORTH IS PREPARED) You may translate it thus most excellently, by supplying what is often wont to be omitted in the Hebrew: If we know the Lord, and by knowing him we follow him, his help will be as prompt for us as the dawn is.

AND HE WILL COME AS THE EARLY RAIN TO US, AND THE LATTER RAIN TO THE EARTH) The early rain is called that which is at the time of sowing, the latter that which is at the time of the ripe harvest, as we said in Deut. 11, 14. The sense is: at every time all prosperous things will come to them from God.

Latin:

ET CVRABIT NOS: VIVIFICABIT NOS POST DVOS DIES: IN TERTIA DIE SUSCITA- BIT NOS, ET VIVEMUS IN CONSPECTU EJUS) Ut vivamus. Sensus primum obvius est: postquam se emen- daverint Hebræi, futurum, ut brevi eos Deus ex tantis mi- seriis, quæ morti comparari solent, restituat. Sed haud du- bie Dei nutu ita directa sunt hæc verba, quomodo & multa alia Prophetarum, ut apertissime nobis præfigurarent tem- pus, intra quod & Christus viram, & Ecclesia ejus spem e- rat receptura. Judæi ex hoc loco sibi fingunt intra triduum absolutum iri postremum & universale judicium.

SCIEMUS SEQVEMURQUE, VT COGNO- SCAMUS DOMINUM: QUASI DILVCVLVM PRÆ- PARATUS EST EGRESSUS EJUS) Optime sic vertas, supplendo quæ in Hebræo sæpe omitti solent: Si cogno- scamus Dominum, & cognoscendo eum sectemur, tam promptum nobis erit ejus auxilium, quam est aurora.

ET VENIET QVASI IMBER NOBIS TEM- PORANEVS, ET SEROTINVS TERRÆ) Imber tem- poraneus dicitur, qui est sementis tempore, serotinus, qui adulta segere, ut diximus Deut. 11, 14. Sensus est: omni tempore omnia ipsis à Deo prospera ventura.

## 6:4
Vers. 4. WHAT SHALL I DO TO THEE EPHRAIM? WHAT SHALL I DO TO THEE JUDA?) That is, what good could I do for you, while you are such as you are?

YOUR MERCY) חסד, is indeed wont to be translated as έλεος and ἐλεημοσύνη, both among the Greek Interpreters of the Old Testament and among the writers of the New; but in truth, the meaning of the word includes this part indeed, but it lies wider and extends itself to all duties of piety and probity: whence חסידים are called Ἀσιδαῖοι in the Maccabees, who solicitously fulfilled all parts of their duties, whence it happened afterwards, with the ו struck out, the name ἱσσιαίων or ἐσσηνῶν, and it is believed that there is somewhat more in it than in the word צדיק.

AS THE MORNING CLOUD, AND AS THE DEW PASSING AWAY IN THE MORNING) Your probity failed shortly, just as the dew, or the cloud risen in the morning, perish upon the arrival of the sun.

Grotius rightly abandons the commentaries of the Jews here, whom I wish he had not followed in most other things! Jerome, however, reports the figment of the Jews differently (unless perhaps it is another one or belongs to others: for neither Grotius nor Jerome expressed any by name), namely, that by the second day they understand the time of the Messiah, by the third the time of judgment, in which they dream they will be freed from all evils and will enjoy various delights for a thousand years. Which is an insipid fantasy of the Chiliasts. And here Jerome urges the Jews: Let them answer us, what the first day is: that is: the first coming of the Savior: And when they cannot answer, let us infer that the first day is, according to what they themselves wish, the coming of the Savior in humility: the second in glory: the third in the habit of a judge. But those who accept the second and third: testify that they have lost the first: because the second and third cannot be called such without the first. Others understand by the first day the time of liberation from the Babylonian captivity, by the third the liberation from the present crisis, to which they are subject to this day, but here it is not a matter of the vivification done on the first and second day, and which is to be hoped for on the third day. He will revive us, says the Prophet, after two days: on the third day he will raise us up. And the expectation of a Messiah who will free them from the modern dispersion is most vain. The Messiah will come, but to judge those who, when he came, did not wish to receive him. The interpretation of others concerning the three temples, the first built by Solomon, destroyed by the Assyrians, the second erected after the captivity, conquered by the Romans, the third to be restored by the Messiah, which is also R. Solomon's, is both more inept and more alien here than to need refutation; which, however, Abarbenel interpolated in this way: after two vengeances, which passed over us, after two temples, which were destroyed, and on the third day, i.e., under the future temple, he will raise us up, and we shall live before him, so that we shall neither fall hereafter, nor be led away captive, which is intellectual death: but at that time he will make us stand, and we shall persevere in that state all the days of the earth, and we shall live before him, i.e., we shall persevere in his worship, and we shall not die, and the land shall not be desolate. And then, in the time of that salvation, we shall know, we shall pursue to know the Lord, etc. According to his own sense, the first day would be the state of the first temple, the second the state of the second temple, the third the erection of the third: concerning which see Cocceius in this place, p. 61. Moreover, there have not been wanting those among the Rabbis to whom Grotius himself ought to have lent an ear here: who also explained the present passage concerning the resurrection of the Messiah and our own, concerning whom see Galatinus, book 3, De arcanis catholicae veritatis, ch. 12; book 8, ch. 22; book 12, ch. 3.

Although indeed Grotius could not deny that the words of the Prophet MOST CLEARLY prefigure the time within which Christ was to receive life, and His Church hope, yet he makes the literal sense far different, namely this: that God would shortly restore the Hebrews from such great miseries, which are wont to be compared to death: whence that sense concerning Christ and the Church must be mystical, or eminent, as he likes to speak elsewhere. Thus, forsooth, Scripture is to be attenuated, so that we may obtain what it eminently denotes, as Cocceius complained in a similar case regarding Grotius. But he who here treated this distinguished passage in no other way, so that according to a preconceived new and wonderful economy of the Prophet, he might be carried away to a much more inept sense, which no one before Cocceius ever dreamed of in the Prophet, nor would anyone rashly admit after him. Cocceius indeed confesses that it cannot be that there is no respect in this place to the resurrection of Christ, and yet he explains these things according to the literal sense concerning the Christian Church cut down and lacerated by the Assyrians, i.e., the Saracens and Turks, and struck by the hand of the Anti-Christ (the Roman), in this manner: He will vivify us, and will raise us up, that we may live before him, i.e., It is certain that God will not be wanting to our efforts, and even if it should seem for some time that success is lacking to our efforts, yet the seed which is in us will not die, and the seed which shall be recounted to him for an age shall not perish, for it was said in ch. 2, 21: I will betroth thee unto me for an age. Therefore, if we should even seem to fall and be delivered into the hand of our enemies, nevertheless we shall at some time rise in our posterity, and the Church will live before him. Thus is signified the consolation which the Martyrs had, who resisted the Anti-Christ, in their sufferings, because they were certain that in the end the fruit of their sufferings would respond to their labor for the Church, in amendment and peace and amplification. Who has ever been able to scent these things in the prophetic text or attain them by divination, whether that there is any trace here of the Saracens and Turks, or of the Roman Anti-Christ! And how will these things look toward the resuscitation of Christ, if they do not treat of the resurrection from death, let alone the resurrection of Christ himself, but only teach that the faithful will rise in their posterity? You say: the brevity of the time, in which they will rise again and fall no more, expresses by analogy the time in which Christ lay in the sepulcher; but what Oedipus will find that analogy, unless he has perhaps been accustomed to the analogy of the Sacramentarians? Let us hear, however, Cocceius explaining the mysteries of that analogy: It has that force, i.e., Christ our head did not rise from the dead to the end that he should suffer his own to succumb, and deliver the kingdom to his enemies. Moreover, it is also signified that in the meantime the testimony of the truth ought to shine forth twice or thrice against the Anti-Christ; he will vivify us from two days, or after two days, i.e., The Church and the kingdom of Christ will last longer than to be finished by one or two flashes. He will raise us up on the third day. The simple mind of the prophecy is that this and similar prophecies will be for the consolation of the faithful for patience in the struggle with the Antichrist, so that even if they see themselves pressed, and their predecessors to have fallen, nevertheless they may not despair, or cast away the confession of hope. Huss is said to have predicted in his last agony concerning the battle and reformation that would arise after a century. Certainly the pious could also conceive that hope from the Apocalypse, where it is shown that the Saints would be overcome for a time and times and half a time. By which measure of time not only is the interval from the rise of the Beast to the separation of the Church from it determined, but also the turns of the contradictions are shown, and the continuous succession not to be broken off of the fourth turn, or the beginning of victory in the fourth time. Hosea says on the third day, understanding the third day of resuscitation, or the resuscitation to be repeated a third time, i.e., that they would struggle with the Kingdom of the Antichrist after the first fall, he will raise them up three times, and then we shall live before him, as our King and only teacher, and we shall rejoice in him. These three turns of the excitation of the oppressed Church, concerning which oppression is Isaiah 57, 1, are proven in the Waldensians, the disciples of Wycliffe and Huss, and the latest Reformers, Luther, Melanchthon, Calvin, and their colleagues. And after some many things: In the Christian Church delivered into the hand of the Anti-Christ we recognize those three days after the first time; and now on the third day, with the two witnesses killed by the Beast, we have seen the Church herself to have revived, and although constrained, yet we have found that she could not yet be suppressed, and we are certain that with the evening threatening, the light will rise on the day, and the harvest being finished, the losses are to be repaired. But enough of the Cocceian trifles: to have recited which is to have refuted them most solidly, for in these inventions there is nothing sound.

Cocceius's teacher, John Calvin, conceded to no one that the resuscitation of Christ was looked at here by the Prophet: nay, he held that sense as too subtle and evanescent, and judged those to be flying in the air who understand it so. This passage is wont to be explained concerning Christ, that after three days and on the third day he will raise up his Church, because we know that Christ did not rise for himself privately, but for his members: for he is the firstfruits of those who rise. This sense therefore seems not to square badly, that the Prophet here raises the faithful into the hope of salvation, because God will raise his firstborn son, whose resurrection will be common, and the life of the whole Church. But that sense seems to me TOO SUBTLE. And this must always be looked to by us, that we do not fly in the air. Subtle speculations please at first glance, but afterwards they vanish. Therefore, whoever wishes to make progress in the Scriptures, let him always hold to this rule, that whatever he gathers, whether in the Prophets or in the Apostles, should be solid. Others, his disciples, followed Calvin, and explained the prophecy concerning the liberation from captivity and the restoration of the Church after two days, that is, in a short time, in almost the same manner as Grotius: such as Gualterus, Mollerus, Tremellius, Polanus, Drusius, and others, except that most stop at the liberation from bodily miseries in a prominent sense, setting aside the Grotian view. Paræus, however, as a defender of Calvin against B. Ægidius Hunnius, who accused Calvin of ἰsdaΐζειν even here, taught that this prophecy could be explained concerning Christ in two ways, lest, forsooth, he should seem to have departed entirely from the sense of the ancients: (1.) by reason of the type, because the liberation from captivity was a type of the liberation to come through Christ's resurrection. Therefore, the prophecy must be understood both of the type literally and primarily, and of the antitype mystically and secondarily. (2.) By the necessary connection of an effect with its cause. For no redemption of the Church, whether it be temporal or eternal, happens except through Christ, and therefore he opines that this oracle is necessarily referred to Christ in this sense also, as to its cause. But as to the latter method, no prudent person admits that this is to explain Scripture. For it is one thing to declare by whose merit the resurrection on the third day would happen to the Israelites, concerning which merit of his there is nothing in that text but it is another thing to explain the text, as to whom the Holy Spirit predicts will be raised and who that third day is, on which he is to be raised. For we cannot be considered to be expounding the text of Scripture when we explain and adduce something demonstrated from elsewhere in the Scriptures, but [we are] when we teach that something is contained in that text of Scripture which is at hand, whether explicitly (ῥητῶς) or conceptually (διανοητικῶς), even if to elicit that from the text there is need of other passages, but parallel ones, not entirely foreign (ἀλλοτρίοις) or heterogeneous. But as regards the former exposition, which Pareus calls for, which concurs with the Grotius one: it is by no means to be admitted that a double, and such a disparate, sense should be attributed to one and the same oracle, which neither the perspicuity of Scripture, nor the most simple, and least ambiguous or intricate, method of teaching of the Holy Spirit admits. For in that way the subject of vivification is doubled, so that one object is in the literal sense, namely the Israelites, another in the mystical sense, namely Christ; thus the predicate, even if it is one and the same, is also taken in a double sense, namely vivification and raising up, so that it denotes both a true raising and vivification from death properly, and metaphorically a restoration from miseries similar to death. But that the same word should be used both properly and figuratively in the same place, when it occurs only once, is absurd (ἄτοπον), and alien to the custom of Scripture. Similarly, the third day also will have to be understood in a far different way in the eminent sense. For there it will figuratively denote a short time: here, however, properly, as it sounds, it will signify the third day after the two days have elapsed: which sense one would rather call the first and obvious one, because it adheres to the propriety of the letter. Therefore, since a double sense of that kind can by no means stand together, it remains that only one or the other sense be retained here.

What, therefore, shall we establish as the genuine and native sense of this prophecy, other than that which both the Ecclesiastical Doctors and some of the Rabbis of the Jews held to be native in the words of the Prophet, and which neither Grotius, nor Pareus, or Cocceius, and some other more recent Calvinists dared to exclude here? Which, however, they do not always propose in the same way. Our blessed Meisner, differing on true and literal interpretation in his Commentary, explains it thus on p. 597. This is nothing other than that the prophecy speaks of the resurrection both of Christ, as the head, and of us as members. For it is confessed that this discourse is not about liberation from temporal captivity, but rather about a certain act of the Messiah and a benefit of the New Testament. That act is the resurrection of Christ, the benefit is our raising up. For as regards Christ, he had his own peculiar three days. We call the first the day of passion and death: the second of burial and rest: the third of glorious resurrection, on which he came forth from the sepulcher according to Scripture 1 Cor. 15, 4. But no Scripture concerning the third day besides this one of Hosea is found in the whole Old Testament, as Dorotheus observes. As for us, we rise again in two ways (1.) In soul, when we are regenerated, and begin to walk in newness of life, of which it is said in Rom. 6, 8: If we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him. And more clearly in Eph. 2, 4. 5. GOD, when we were dead in sins, made us alive together in Christ, and raised us up together, which words coincide entirely with the prophecy of Hosea. (2) In body, which again happens in two ways: 1. in hope and by reason of right, in which manner we were vivified with Christ on the third day, 1. Cor. 15, 22. because then we received the right of our resurrection: 2. in reality and by reason of the fact itself, when on the last day we shall recover life in reality. This raising up also happens after two days. For to every Christian there are also three days. The first is of the cross, as long as we live on this earth. The second is of rest, when we lie in the sepulcher. The third is of resurrection, when, glorified, we shall come forth to a new life. Although these things are pious and pleasant, and can have their use when duly applied in homiletics, yet if we urge the text more strictly, as to what two days and what third day is understood by the Prophet, that three-day period of Christians of the cross, rest, and resurrection will certainly not apply here, but only that of Christ: And therefore the blessed Meisner himself, when he later disputes competitively (ἀγωνιστικῶς) and exquisitely about the sense in the same commentary, whether Hosea prophesies about the resurrection of Christ to be on the third day, renders this, and no other, sense, and asserts that it is the literal one on page 616. We truly will rise again on the third day, but not in our own person, but in Christ. As to what Pareus desires to be observed regarding the genuine formation of the state on p. 123 on Hosea, he deals craftily with us, and attributes to us such an absurd interpretation, that a double figure must be used, namely Enallage of the plural number for the singular, and Synecdoche of the whole for the part, as if the Prophet had said: On the third day he will raise us up through Christ, and us with him. As if we were so stupid that we would change the plural into the singular, when rather we retain the plural and say without figure or trope: We truly will rise again on the third day, but not in our own person, but in Christ. These are the words of the blessed Meisner. Which sense the blessed Gesner had also handed down, that namely the present passage cannot be accepted concerning at least an external and bodily liberation, but that it must necessarily be explained concerning the redemption to be performed through Christ from the dead on the third day. And before these our Doctors, especially Megalander in his Commentary on this passage.
