Jac. 5, 7.) quarum illa statim facta semente di- missa efficit, ut semen radices agat in terra, hæc vero tunc decidit, cum seges in spicas & culmos succrescit, ut fructus ad maturitatem perveniat, quia Christus suo Evangelio ubique prædicato ari- da & sitientia corda refocillavit, mortua vivifica- vit, & in bonis operibus remissa crescere fecit, at- que ad messem cœlestem matura reddidit, uti B. Meisnerus ipse exposuit.

Non ergo generali tantum sensu accipienda promissio, cum Grotio, quod cum tempore piis pro- spera eventura sint, neque cum Calvinianis ad ca- ptivos restringenda sub Babylonica potestate, quod Deus illis se propitium exhibere velit, uti Rivetus le- vi argumento contendit, quod egressus Dei oppona- tur discessus, quo reversus erat in suum locum; nam etsi hæc oppositio hic locum haberet, annon illu- strius ea sibi constat, cum derelictioni Israëlitarum opponitur illa gratiosa visitatio, quæ sub Nov. T. accidit. Cui uti insigne hoc elogium gemina figu- ra auroræ & pluviæ tempestivæ adumbratum aptius convenit, ita referunt communiter interpp. cum glossa ordinaria & interlineari, nec non Lyrano, hæc ad tempus N. Test. Supra, inquit B. Gesne- rus, Dominus sese abscondit, & propter populi pec- cata in locum suum abiit, hoc est, opem suam & au- xilium, conciones etiam consolatorias Evangelii ob- stinatis aliquandiu subtraxit, adeo ut populus Israë- liticus à Deo prorsus desertus, & Messiæ adventus plane negatus videretur. Nunc autem pœnitentes cum gaudio exclamant: Dominum Messiam de la- tibulo suo iterum prodire & adventare. Quamvis enim introduci videantur hæc loqui illi, qui hæc tem- pora assecuturi non erant, tamen ab eis, qui sunt unus populus & eadem spe seipsos sustentant, & in spiritu hæc prædicuntur.

Decimum argumentum depromimus ex gra- tuita peccatorum propter Christum condonatione.

Quod beneficium prædicationi Evangelii con- junctum subjicit Propheta: QUID FACIAM TIBI EPHRAIM? QUID FACIAM TIBI JUDA? MISERICORDIA VESTRA QVA- SI NUBES MATUTINA, ET QUASI ROS MANE PERTRANSIENS. Grotius in partem malam accipit, id est, quid boni vobis possem facere, dum tales estis? Misericordia, id est probitas vestra brevi deficit, quomodo ros aut nubes mane exorta sole adventante dissipantur: & de voce MISERICOR- DIA, hæc annotat: חסד ἔλεος quidem & ἐλεημοσύνη verti solet, tum apud Græcos interpretes V. Testamenti, tum apud Scriptores Novi: sed revera significatio vocis hanc quidem partem complectitur, sed latius patet, extenditque se ad omnia pietatis & probitatis officia: unde חסידים ἀσιδαῖοι in Maccabæicis dicuntur, qui omnes officiorum partes sollicite explebant, unde factum postea extrito ח nomen ἐσσαίων, vel ἐσσηνῶν. Et aliquanto plus in eo esse creditur, quam in voce צדק. Sed quidquid sit de illa Hassi-dæorum, & ἐσσαίων nomenclatura, non debebant certe corrigi, aut censura notari, cum interpretibus Græcis V. Test. ipsi etiam Scriptores Novi, qui ἀπὸ πνεύματος ἁγία φερόμενοι scripsere. Neque hic misericordia vestra sensu active, sed passivo accipi-enda, misericordia vobis exhibenda: quia in promissionibus beneficiorum, quibus pœnitentes erigen-di; occupatur Propheta, non in reprehensione vitiorum: Et collatio similitudinis de nube matutina, & rore mane pertranseunte, cum priore de aurora & pluvia matutina vel tempestiva, satis docet persistere Prophetam in genere paracletico, non vero ad Epanorthoticum genus hæc trahenda esse. Quapropter misericordia vestra passive intelligenda de gratuita peccatorum condonatione. Sicut enim squalorem æstivarum noctium pluvia matutina temperat; & ros flaccentes herbas & segetes reficit: ita quoque perterritas conscientias hominum, & actu iræ divinæ adustos, nulla res alia, quam immensa Dei misericordia recreat & vivificat. Ideo quod in αὐτογράφῳ laudato B. Lutherus reddiderat: Was soll ich dir doch thun Ephraim, correxit manu sua ἐμφατικωτέρως in partem bonam interpretatus, hoc modo: Wie will ich dir so wohl thun Ephraim? Et quod reddiderat prius: Denn die Güte so euch gebühret, ist wie eine Morgen-Wolcke, und wie ein Thau, der früh morgens dahin fähret: Id postea per φροντίδας δευτέρας ita emendavit: Denn die Gnade so ich euch erzeigen will, wird seyn wie eine Morgen-Wolcke, und wie ein Thau, der früh morgens fället: de quo audiendus ipse est è commentario p. 520. Dixit Propheta de tempore Novi Testamenti, quod prædicabitur liberatio à morte Christi resurrectionem, & æterna vita, ac tum vere agnituros homines Deum. Non enim timebunt eum, sicut coguntur timere, quibus recte notus non est, sed acquiescent in ejus misericordia. Etsi autem Synagoga & gentes huic doctrinæ se opponent, tamen futurum esse dicit, ut sicut aurora cohiberi non possit, sed magis ac magis illustret mundum, non sine ingenti fructu, ita neque verbi cursus & fructus impediri poterit. Hæc hactenus de Christi regno Propheta dixit. Nunc addit amplificationem horum beneficiorum: Quid tibi faciam ô Ephraim? Quid tibi faciam ô Juda? quasi collaturus ea cum beneficiis veteri populo exhibitis. Magnum fuit liberari ex Ægypti servitute, ornari præclaris victoriis contra gentes, possidere terram promissam Patribus, sed hæc omnia temporalia fuerunt, & tantum præsentes adjuti sunt. Novum autem Testamentum affert ad nos opes spirituales & æternas, nempe reconciliationem cum Deo, remissionem peccatorum, Spiritum Sanctum, & vitam æternam. Ideo Propheta addit: Vestra gratia erit sicut matutina nubes. Hic interpretes non solum ambiguitas, sed etiam similitudinis ratio fefellit. Nam recentiores fere omnes accipiunt beneficentiam seu pietatem active, qua aliis benefaciebant Judæi, ac putant eam comparari rori, quod subito ab ea deflexerint ad impietatem & peccata. Hieronymus passive accipit, sed similitudinis rationem eandem putat esse, quod beneficentia, qua eos Dominus adjuverit, cito sit defitura.

situra. Abducendos enim in captivitatem ab Assy- riis & Babyloniis, &c. Sed neutram sententiam pro- bo. Verum quidem est, quod pietas seu beneficentia accipiatur passive, qua Deus est usurus erga hunc populum. Sed similitudine roris non utitur Pro- pheta, ideo quod cito evanescit, sed eo potius respicit, quod per rorem recreatur terra. Nam in magnis æ- stibus etiam noctes usque ad languorem homi- num calent. Sed cum jam aurora proditura est, ex- citantur aurulæ frigidiusculæ, & roridæ nubes de- stillantes restringunt calorem, & refrigerant ter- ram. Sicut igitur calentia & sitibunda corpora, cum frigidam bibunt, recreantur, & amissam alacrita- tem resumunt: Ita quoque terra recreatur, & quasi vires resumunt, ac eriguntur languentes herbæ, cum matutinum rorem bibunt. Sed quis iste æstus est in hominibus? Aliud nihil, quam sensus peccati, iræ Dei, & æternarum pœnarum. Hæc enim cum occupant animum, tantum non præcludunt Spiri- tum sicut egregie describitur hæc ipsa tentatio in Ps. 38. Domine ne in furore tuo arguas me, neque in ira tua corripias me. Quoniam sagittæ tuæ infixæ sunt mihi, & manus tua gravis est super me. Non est sa- nitas in carne mea propter iram tuam, nec est pax ossibus meis propter peccatum meum. Quoniam peccata mea supergressa sunt caput meum, & sicut onus grave gravata sunt super me. Curvus & de- pressus nimium, & tristis tota die incedo. Quo- niam lumbi mei ariditate pleni sunt, & non est sani- tas in carne mea, collisus & contritus sum vehe- menter, ejulo præ anxietate cordis mei. Domine coram te est omne desiderium meum, & gemitus à te non est absconditus. Cor meum tremit, dereli- querunt me vires meæ, & lumen oculorum meo- rum non est apud me. In his doloribus & periculis languentes, & tantum non mortuos animos nihil eri- git, quam doctrina Evangelii, quæ docet : Christum nostra peccata in se transtulisse, pro iis satisfecisse, & nobis morte suo patefecisse aditum ad vitam. Hæc cum audiunt animi, concipiunt spem veniæ, & sicut pene emortui flores redeunt ad pristinam alacri- tatem & nitorem.

Undecimum argumentum petere licet ab in- certitudine aliarum expositionum. Nam qui rece- dunt à proprietate literæ in temporis designatio- ne, post biduum & tertio die, quæ certum sensum gignit, nihil certi habent, in quo pedem figant. A- liis post biduum est idem, quod BREVI, cum Gro- tio, in quem sensum Rivetus similia loca conquire- re voluit, sed nulla invenit, nisi parum similia, & heterogenea: uti è Commentario ejus liquet. Alii plane contrario sensu accipiunt pro longo tempore, quasi Deus diceret: Sic cogitate & statuite apud vos, & vicissim alii aliis persuadete, etsi non statim primo quoque tempore Deus curet vulnera vestra, sed sinat mortuos jacere ad biduum, hoc est, tempus, ut sitis putribus cadaveribus similes, non tamen de re- demptione vestra dubitandum esse, quia jam dudum mortuis potest momento vitam restituere. Huc refe- runt, quod de Lazaro dicitur Joh. 11,39. Domine jam olet, quia quatriduanus est, ut observavit Rivetus p. 209. Sed dum priorem sensum assumit, nec sibi nec aliis satisfacit. Nam modo tertium diem de tempore liberationis è captivitate & miseriis, modo de tem- pore N. Testamenti intelligit, atque ita exponit: Post paucos dies, misso filio suo in carne humana, nos spirituali vita donabit, atque ita suscitabit nos. Sed quomodo biduum & breve tempus, & simul ali- quod seculorum effluxum notabit, & quomodo post paucos dies eventurum dici potest, quod evenit post decursum octingentorum circiter annorum?

terpretum Christianorum, qui etsi in modo expli- candi non conveniant omnes, facile tamen in sum- ma rei consentiunt, quod de tertio die resurrectionis Christi hoc vaticinium loquatur. Quod non dissi- mulare potuit Rivetus: Certum est, multos ex Pa- tribus hunc locum explicare de resurrectione Chri- sti, facta tertio die, quorum nonnulli id directe conten- dunt. Alii tamen volunt promitti hominum resurre- ctionem in Christi resurrectione, quasi in causa & principe suscitandorum, inter quos Cyrill. Ierosol. Ca- tech. 14. Greg. Nyss. lib. de cognit. Dei cap. de Christi resurr. & Ruffin. in symbolum num. 17. putant hac verba: vivificabit nos per duos dies, in tertia susci- tabit nos, & vivemus in conspectu ejus, in persona eorum dici, qui una cum Christo surrexerunt, & ve- nerunt in sanctam civitatem & apparuerunt mul- tis, Matth. 27. v. 53. Alii intelligunt de omnibus suscitandis, qui in Christo capite tertia die suscitati fuerunt, quia sua resurrectione spem nobis nostræ in- generavit. HæcRivetus.Theodoretus commodissime exposuit: Per hæc, inquit, designat, post tres dies factam Servatoris resurrectionem, quæ publicam resurrectionem conciliavit, omnibusque nobis spem immortalitatis dedit ingeneratam ex Dei agnitione. Neque omnino abnuit è Calvinianis Zanchius in Comment. ad h.l. Quia Israeliticæ & Judæi electi, qui erant vivificandi, hoc erant habituri à Christo capite resurgente propter nostram justificationem, ergo PRINCIPALITER de Christo intelligere necesse est. Atque hæc in præsenti de hoc vaticinio.

## 6:5
Verse 5. FOR THIS I HAVE HEWN BY THE PROPHETS.) I have cut them down by the Prophets: That is, I have denounced great plagues to them: for Prophets, and God through the Prophets, are said to do those things which are predicted. Jer. 1:10.

I HAVE SLAIN THEM BY THE WORDS OF MY MOUTH) That is: I have predicted to them that slaughters would come to pass.

AND THY JUDGMENTS) The punishments which will come upon you.

AS LIGHT THEY SHALL GO FORTH) They shall appear to be most just: nothing shall happen, concerning which you have not been forewarned, and indeed quite often.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PROPTER HOC DOLAVI IN PROPHE- TIS.) Cecidi eos per Prophetas: Id est, magnas plagas ipsis denunciavi: nam Prophetæ, & Deus per Prophetas dicun- tur ea facere, quæ prædicuntur. Jer. 1, 10.

OCCIDI EOS IN VERBIS ORIS MEI) Id est: Occidiones ipsis prædixi eventuras.

ET JUDICIA TVA) Pœnæ quæ in te venient.

QVASI LUX EGREDIENTUR) Apparebunt esse justissima: nihil eveniet, de quo non præmoniti sitis, & quidem sæpius.

## 6:6
Vers. 6. FOR I DESIRED MERCY, AND NOT SACRIFICE) This was said comparatively, as we explained at the passage of Matthew 9, 13, where Christ uses this passage of the Prophet. You think you do much because you offer me ὁλοκαυτώματα [whole burnt offerings] or even expiatory victims. And yet those things, which are common to good and bad men, are of the least account with me: those things which are always and everywhere honorable greatly prevail.

THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOD) That is, piety, as I said above. The same words are often accustomed to be taken now more loosely, now more strictly, which the opposition of the other member often shows. Therefore in this place דעת אלהים signifies the true and internal worship of God. חסד [signifies] all things which are either owed to another man, or are performed with praise.

These things can also be referred to the preceding: so that they may indicate the means and manner by which God prepares us for the enjoyment of His mercy. That is to say: If they were doing true repentance, they would obtain mercy. I have hewn them by the Prophets. For we are compared either to rough stones, or to unpolished wood, which is rendered suitable for use by axes and adzes. The Law, however, is like an adze, which cut down the Israelites through the Prophets, which in 2 Cor. 3, 6 is called the letter that kills and the ministry of death, because it denounces death to transgressors. Therefore those things explain each other. I have hewn in the Prophets, and I have killed them by the words of my mouth. The end, however, of that hewing was that their judgments might go forth as light, or be as light going forth. By judgments is noted both imputed justice and inherent [justice], or that which is begun, according to the interpretation of B. Meisner, and according to others, the justice of Christ and the liberation of the Church. Concerning that adze of the law (these are the words of B. Gesner) the Lord says here: By the lightning of the curse, which is expressed in the law, and by the threatening of temporal and eternal punishments, I terrified and spiritually killed them: Which when it is so, then the judgment, that is, the justice of the faithful, which is in Christ the Redeemer our, 1 Cor. 1:30, Jer. 23:6, shines forth as the most splendid light before God and in the conscience of believers: and at the same time the true liberation, defense, and propagation of the Church shines forth before the whole world. That Grotius understands these things as punishments is less fitting. For thus it would have to be said, 'my judgments,' as the Chaldean interprets. 'Truly my judgment as light will go forth.' In Hebrew it is 'THY judgments,' and the words do not cohere sufficiently when they are understood as punishments, because the preceding things, with which these cohere, concern promises of grace: and the Prophet remains in the simile which he used concerning the going forth of the dawn, v. 2, here concerning the going forth of light, v. 5. he acts, with whom the going forth in the Gospel is prepared as the dawn; to them, if they are properly hewn by the Prophets, they receive by true faith the mercy by which God, like a morning cloud and dew pervading in the morning, drenches hearts terrified by the curse of the law and parched by the heat of wrath; the judgments, i.e., the righteousness of Christ, and his liberation, perfection, and defense will be as light going forth. Others explain 'judgments going forth as light' as the manifestation of a just cause: and as the happy success of affairs, as Vatablus, 'your affairs will turn out happily for you,' and especially Osiander, who conveniently shows here the συνέχειαν (continuity) of the preceding and following: He says, the Prophet passes again from the time of the New Testament to his own age: and recounts that great benefit of God, namely, that through the ministers of the word he argues errors and sins, and teaches the true way of worshipping God. 'For this reason he hewed them (says the Lord) by the Prophets:' I gave Prophets, who as a hewing-tool would correct and reform their errors and vices: and I killed them by the words of my mouth: through the preachings of the law I stirred up true contrition in the hearts of the elect. But if you, O Israelite nation, are willing to obey me and follow my word, your affairs will be in a good state: and your judgments will go forth as light: then your just cause against the impious nations will be manifest and will prevail: for I (by your happy successes) will show the nations that you are a care to me, and that I do not neglect your injuries. I will show, however (says the Lord), to you the true way of worshipping God, far distant from the hypocritical one. For they are occupied with external ceremonies, meanwhile they neglect the true knowledge of God and charity toward their neighbor. I, however, require these two as the marrow of the first and second table, especially: not so very solicitous about sacrifices, whether they are provided and offered in great number or price, or small. 'Because I desired mercy:' I require true and sincere charity toward one's neighbor, 'and not sacrifice:' and the knowledge of God (that is, true faith in God and the Messiah) I require more than burnt offerings. I did not command sacrifices to be offered to this end, as if all piety consisted in that thing: or that sins were truly expiated by those sacrifices (without Christ). But I wanted sacred rites to be performed for this reason, that by the sacrifices you might be reminded of the Messiah (who would one day die for our sins) and place all your trust in him. And whoever (out of faith in the Messiah) has benefited his neighbor from the heart (whatever benefit he may have conferred upon him), he does a thing far more pleasing to me than if he offered Hecatombs to me daily. Grotius also approves of this gnome, 'I desire mercy, etc.': The same words are often accustomed to be taken now more loosely, now more strictly, which the opposition of the other member often shows. Therefore in this place דעת אלהים (knowledge of God) signifies true and internal worship of God, חסד (mercy) all things which are either owed to another man or are performed with praise.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QVIA MISERICORDIAM VOLUI, ET NON SACRIFICIUM) Dictum est hoc comparate, ut explicavimus ad Matthæi locum 9, 13. ubi Christus hoc Prophetæ loco utitur. Putatis multum vos facere quod ὁλοκαυτώματα mihi offertis aut etiam piaculares victimas. Atqui ista quæ bonis & malis hominibus sunt communia, in minimo censu sunt apud me: multum præpollent ea quæ semper & ubique honesta sunt.

SCIENTIAM DEI) Id est, pietatem, ut supra dixi- mus. Solent sæpe voces eædem modo laxius sumi modo strictius, quod sæpe ostendit membri alterius oppositio. Er- go hoc loco דעת אלהים verum & internum Dei cul- tum significat. חסד omnia quæ homini alteri aut deben- tur, aut cum laude præstantur.

Possunt hæc etiam ad superiora referri: ut me- dium ac modum indicent, quo Deus nos præparat ad misericordiæ suæ fruitionem. q.d. Si veram age- rent pœnitentiam, misericordiam consequerentur. Dolavi eos per Prophetas. Nos enim comparamur vel rudibus saxis, vel impolito ligno, quod asciis & dolabris ad usum redditur idoneum. Lex autem dola- bræ instar est, quæ cecidit Israelitas per Prophetas, quæ 2. Cor. 3,6. litera occidens & mysterium mortis di- citur, quia prævaricatoribus mortem denunciat. Ex- plicant ergo illa sese mutuo. Dolavi in Prophetis, & occidi eos in verbis oris mei. Finis autem illius do- lationis fuit, ut judicia illorum quasi lux egrederen- tur, vel essent quasi lux egrediens. Per judicia notatur tum justitia imputata, tum inhærens, vel inchoata, interprete B. Meisnero, juxta alios justitia Christi & Ecclesiæ liberatio. De ista legis dolabra (verba sunt B. Gesneri) ait hic Dominus: Fulmine maledictio- nis, quæ in lege expressa est, & comminatione tem- poralium æternarumque pœnarum terrui, ac spi- ritualiter occidi eos: Quod cum sit, tum judicium, id est, justitia fidelium, quæ est in Christo Redem- ptore nostro, 1. Cor. 1, 30. Jerem. 23, 6. tanquam splendidissima lux coram Deo, & in conscientia credentium refulget: simulque etiam vera Ecclesiæ liberatio, defensio & propagatio coram universo mundo illucescit. Quid Grotius hæc de pœnis in- telligit, minus convenit. Nam ita dicendum foret, judicia mea, uti Chaldæus interpretatur. Profecto judicium meum q. lux egredietur. In Ebræo est Judi- cia TUA, neque cohærent satis verba, cum de pœnis intelliguntur, quia præcedentia, cum quibus hæc cohærent, promissiones gratiæ concernunt : & per- manet Propheta in similitudine, qua usus est de di- luculi egressu, v. 2. hic de egressu lucis v. 5. agit, penes quos egressus in Evangelio quasi diluculum præpara- tur, illis, si probe dolati per Prophetas, misericordiam, qua Deus instar nubis matutinæ, & roris mane per- vadentis, corda legis maledictione territa, & æstu iræ arida perfundit, vera fide suscipiunt, judicia, h. e. ju- stitia Christi, ejusdemque liberatio, perfectio, ac defensio erit quasi lux egrediens. Alii judicia egre- dientia instar lucis, de justæ causæ manifestatione ex- ponunt: & de felici rerum successu, uti Vatablus, res tuæ feliciter tibi cedent, & imprimis Osiander, qui συνέχειαν etiam antecedentium & consequentium hic commode monstrat: Transit, inquit, Propheta rursus à tempore Novi Testamenti ad suum seculum: & recenset ingens illud beneficium Dei, quod videli- cet per ministros verbi errores & peccata arguat, & verum colendi Deum modum doceat. Propter hoc dolavit eos (inquit Dominus) in Prophetis: Dedi Prophetas, qui tanquam dolabra eorum errores & vi- tia corrigerent & reformarent: & occidi eos in ver- bis oris mei: per conciones legis in electorum cordibus veram contritionem excitavi. Quod si tu o gens Israe- litica, mihi parere & verbo meo obsequi volueris, bo- no loco res tuæ erunt: & judicia tua quasi lux egre- dientur: tum justa tua causa adversus impias gentes manifesta erit & obtinebit: ego enim (felicibus tuis successibus) monstrabo gentibus, te mihi curæ esse, & me injurias tuas non negligere. Ostendam autem (in- quit Dominus) tibi verum Dei colendi modum, ab hypocritico plurimum distantem. Illi enim circa ex- ternas ceremonias occupantur, interim veram Dei a- gnitionem, & charitatem erga proximum negligunt. Ego vero hæc duo tanquam medullam primæ & se- cundæ tabulæ, imprimis requiro: de sacrificiis non us- que adeo sollicitus, sive ea magno numero aut pretio, sive parvo comparentur, & offerantur. Quia mise- ricordiam volui: veram & sinceram charitatem er- ga proximum requiro, & non sacrificium: & scien- tiam Dei (id est, veram in Deum & Messiam fi- dem) plus requiro quam holocausta. Non in hunc finem sacrificia offerri præcepi, quasi in ea re tota pietas esset: aut istis sacrificiis peccata revera (absque Chri- sto) expiarentur. Sed ideo sacra fieri volui, ut sacrifi- ciis de Messia (aliquando morituro pro peccatis no- stris) commonefieretis, & omnem in ipsum fiduciam collocaretis. Et qui (ex fide in Messiam) proximo suo ex animo benefecerit (qualecunque in eum beneficium contulerit) is mihi rem longe gratiorem facit, quam si quotidie mihi Hecatombas offerat. Istam hujus gno- mæ, Misericordiam volo, &c. probat etiam Gro- tius: Solent sæpe voces eædem modo laxius sumi, modo strictius, quod sæpe ostendit membri alterius oppositio. Ergo hoc loco דעת אלהים verum & internum Dei cultum significat, חסד omnia quæ homini alteri aut debentur, aut cum laude præstantur.

## 6:7
Vers. 7.

BUT THEY ARE ADAM [LIKE MEN] THEY HAVE TRANSGRESSED THE COVENANT) The Greeks for עברו read עבר as a participle. They are like a covenant-breaking man: The Chaldean by אדם (Adam) understands those giants who were born from בנות האדם (the daughters of men), Gen. 6:4. They like the ancient generations have transgressed my covenant. Others

take כְּאָדָם (like Adam/man) commonly, and express it: Thus they have transgressed my covenant as if it were the covenant of a man. This Latin interpretation does not displease me, so that the sense here may be: As Adam, because he violated my covenant, was expelled from Eden, so also it is just that these be expelled from their land.

THERE THEY HAVE TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME) 'There' is as if pointing with a finger. 'There,' in that best land which I had given to them, as the Chaldean explains here. Add, so that you may connect it with the preceding, in that land which is compared to Eden, Gen. 13:10, Isaiah 51:3, as also the places near to it. Ezek. 28:13.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

IPSI AUTEM SUNT ADAM TRANSGRESSI SUNT PACTUM) Græci pro עברו legunt עבר partici- pialiter. Similes sunt homini fœdifrago: Chaldæus per אדם, intelligit illos gigantes, qui nati ex בנות האדם, Genes. 6, 4. Ipsi sicut generationes priscæ transgressi sunt pactum meū. Alii

כְּאָדָם sumunt communiter, & exprimunt: Ita transgressi sunt pactum meum quasi pactum esset hominis. Mihi Latina haec in- terpretatio non displicet, ut sensus hic sit: Sicut Adam, quia pactum meum violavit, expulsus est ex Hedene, ita & hos aequum est ex sua terra expelli.

IBI PRAEVARICATI SUNT IN ME) Ibi est velut digito monstrantis. Ibi, in terra illa optima, quam ego eis dederam, ut hic exponit Chaldaeus. Adde, ut connectas cum superioribus, in illa terra quae Hedeni com- paratur, Gen. 13, 10. Esaiae 51, 3. ut & loca ei proxi- ma. Ezech. 28, 13.

## 6:8
Vers. 8.

GILEAD IS A CITY OF THOSE WORKING IDOLATRY) אָוֶן (Aven), indeed, sometimes signifies an idol: but also injustice, as the Chaldean takes it here, and the Greeks in many places translate it as ἀδικίαν (injustice) and ἀνομίαν (lawlessness).

SUPPLANTED WITH BLOOD) That is, they have the traces of slaughter impressed on every soil: for there are very many murderers there. And therefore there are more cities of refuge beyond the Jordan for the space of the land than on this side of the Jordan. Num. 35:13, Deut. 4:41, 42, 43, Jer. 20:8.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

GALAAD CIVITAS OPERANTIUM IDO- LUM) אָוֶן ,idolum quidem interdum significat: sed & in- justitiam, quomodo hic accipit Chaldaeus, & Graeci multis in locis, vertunt ἀδικίαν & ἀνομίαν.

SUPPLANTATA SANGUINE) Id est, in omni so- lo impressa habent caedis vestigia: plurimi enim ibi homici- dae. Ideoque trans Jordanem plura pro terrae spatio asyla quam cis Jordanem. Num. 35, 13. Deut. 4, 41. 42. 43. Jerem. 20, 8.

## 6:9
Verse 9.

AND AS THE THROATS OF MEN WHO ARE ROBBERS, A PARTAKER OF THE PRIESTS KILLING IN THE WAY TOWARD THE NATIONS OF SICHEM) The transposition makes the passage more obscure, which being resolved, the sense will be this: Just as robbers lie in wait for someone on the road that leads to Shechem, in order to kill him, so is the gathering of the priests. Thus all the priests consent to evil, like a band of robbers. Similar is that of Ovid: You would think they had sworn to commit a crime.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE WROUGHT WICKEDNESS) Because they devote themselves to wickedness: they do nothing else.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET QUASI FAUCES VIRORUM LATRONUM PARTICEPS SACERDOTUM IN VIA INTERFI- CIENTIUM PER GENTES DE SICHEM) Transpo- sitio locum facit obscuriorem, qua enodata hic erit sensus: Sicut expectant aliquem latrones in via qua fert Sicima, ut eum interficiant, ita se habet coitio Sacerdotum. Ita omnes sa- cerdotes in malum consentiunt, ut manipulus latronum. Simile illud Ovidii: In facinus jurasse putes.

QUIA SCELUS OPERATI SUNT) Quia sceleri dant operam: nihil agunt aliud.

## 6:10
Verse 10.

IN THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL) In the ten tribes.

BEHOLD A HORRIBLE THING) An astonishing matter. As in Jeremiah 5:30, 18:13, 23:14. For it is written with the שׁ having the point on the right, but it seems to come from שָׁעַר, which signifies to fear, and has the point on the left. These distinctions in the letters were not added in ancient times.

THERE ARE THE WHOREDOMS OF EPHRAIM, ISRAEL IS DEFILED) Better: By the whoredom of Ephraim (that is, of Jeroboam, who was of that tribe) Israel is defiled. That is, the ten tribes: for Jeroboam first gave the example of the worship of the calves, which flowed into so many thousands of men with surprising suddenness.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

IN DOMO ISRAEL) In decem tribubus.

VIDE HORRENDUM) Rem stupendam. Ut Je- rem. 5, 30. 18, 13. 23, 14. scribitur enim שׁ dextrum ha- bente punctum, sed videtur venire à שָׁעַר, quod timere significat, & sinistrum punctum habet. Ista discrimina in literis olim non addebantur.

IBI FORNICATIONES EPHRAIM, CONTA- MINATUS EST ISRAEL) Melius: Fornicatione Ephraim (id est, Jeroboami, qui ex ea erat tribu) contaminatus est Israel. Id est, decem tribus: nam Jeroboam primus ex- emplum dedit cultus vitulorum, qui mirum quam subito in tot hominum millia fluxerit.

## 6:11
ALSO, O JUDA, SET A HARVEST FOR THEE, WHEN I SHALL HAVE RETURNED THE CAPTIVITY OF MY PEOPLE) This is rather obscure. I think it is rightly translated: But also, O Judah, He will set distresses for you (that is, distresses will be set for you, an active verb without a person for a passive) after I have returned to make my people captive. That is, after I have again caused the Israelites to be led away captive. The first abduction was done by Tiglath-Pileser: the second by Shalmaneser. After this came Sennacherib, who devastated Judea and closely besieged Jerusalem. Interpreters here translate קָצִיר as harvest or planting: but in the Chaldean, קְצִירָא is a disease or distress, and the Yod is often accustomed to be dropped.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SED ET JUDA PONE MESSEM TIBI, CUM CONVERTERO CAPTIVITATEM POPULI MEI) Est hoc obscurius. Recte verti puto: Sed & o Juda ponet angustias tibi (id est, ponentur tibi angustiae, activum sine persona pro passivo) postquam ego rediero ad captivum faciendum populum meum. Id est, postquam iterum fece- ro captivos adduci Israelitas. Prior abductio per Teglath- phalasarum facta: altera per Salmanasarum. Post hanc venit Sennacheribus, qui vastavit Judaeam, & Hierosolyma arcte obsedit. קָצִיר messem, aut plantarium hic vertunt Interpretes: sed Chaldaeus קְצִירָא est morbus, vel angu- stiae, & solet Jod saepe abjici.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. An accusation of hypocrisy and impenitence.

The Lord complains that He labored in vain to heal Israel, even when harsher remedies were applied through enemies, while false prophets rendered him secure, so that the nobles together with the common people might persevere in hypocritical devotion and idolatrous worship, not feeling divine punishments and turning themselves to foreign aids, though in vain, to be entirely enclosed and destroyed by the Assyrian net, on account of apostasy, idolatry, hypocrisy, disobedience, and refusal of divine instruction and true conversion. The degenerate Hebrew, with the Lord acting as physician, will perish.

Verse 1.

WHEN I WOULD HAVE HEALED ISRAEL) When I had healed Israel. That is, when I had overthrown the whole house of Ahab on account of idolatry.

THE INIQUITY OF EPHRAIM WAS REVEALED) A new guilt manifested itself, Jehu leaving the calves for the people 2 Kings 10, 31.

AND THE MALICE OF SAMARIA) ἐπεξήγησις.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE WROUGHT A LIE, AND A THIEF HAS ENTERED SPOILING, A ROBBER OUTSIDE) The copula here is redundant in the Hebrew manner. For the sense is: because they made images for themselves (which are called a lie by the Hebrews), therefore they became prey at home to judges, outside to enemies, namely under Hazael. Above 5, 11. & 2 Kings 10, 32.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. Accusatio hypocriseos, & impoe- nitentiae.

Queritur Dominus, quod frustra ipse sanare Israelem, etiam adhibitis per hostes gravio- ribus remediis laborarit, falsis Prophetis illum securum reddentibus, ut in hypocriti- ce devotione & cultu idololatrico proceres cum vulgo perseverent, poenas divinas non sentientes & ad auxilia extera etsi frustra se convertentes reti Assyriaco omnino con- cludendi, & destruendi, ob apostasiam, ido- lolatriam, hypocrisin, inobedientiam & recusationem informationis divinae, ve- raque conversionis. Degenerans, Domino medicante, peribit Hebraeus.

Vers. 1.

CUM SANARE VELLEM ISRAEL) Cum sanas- sem Israelem. Id est, cum totam domum Achabi ob ido- lolatriam evertissem.

REVELATA EST INIQUITAS EPHRAIM) No- va culpa se aperuit, Jehu vitulos populo relinquente 2. Reg. 10, 31.

ET MALITIA SAMARIAE) ἐπεξήγησις.

QVIA OPERATI SVNT MENDACIUM, ET FVR INGRESSVS EST SPOLIANS, LATRNCVLVS FORIS) Copula hic Hebræo more abundat. Sensus enim est: quia fecerunt sibi imagines, (quæ mendacium dicuntur Hebræis) ideo præda facti sunt domi Judicibus, foris hostibus, sub Hazaële scilicet. Supra 5, 11. & 2. Reg. 10, 32.

## 7:2
Ver. 2. AND LEST THEY SAY IN THEIR HEARTS, I HAVE REMEMBERED ALL THEIR MALICE) Better: Neither do they say in their hearts (that is, they do not think) that I remember their crimes.

NOW THEIR OWN INVENTIONS HAVE SURROUNDED THEM) They surround, that is, they will shortly surround; their own devices will fall back upon themselves.

THEY HAVE BEEN MADE BEFORE MY FACE) The word 'which' is missing: the sense is: which appear most plainly.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET NE FORTE DICANT IN CORDIBVS SVIS, OMNEM MALITIAM EORVM ME RECORDATVM) Melius: Neque dicunt in cordibus suis (id est, non cogitant) me meminisse ipsorum crimina.

NVNC CIRCVMDEDERVNT EOS ADINVENTIONES SVÆ) Circumdant, id est, brevi circumdabunt: commenta ipsorum in ipsos recident.

CORAM FACIE MEA FACTÆ SVNT) Deest quæ: sensus: quæ planissime apparent.

## 7:3
Ver. 3. IN THEIR MALICE THEY HAVE MADE THE KING GLAD) Jehu, they gave him false hopes.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IN MALITIA SVA LÆTIFICAVERUNT REGEM) Jehum, falsas ei spes dedere.

## 7:4
Ver. 4. ALL ADULTERERS) They have become idolaters.

AS AN OVEN HEATED BY THE BAKER: THE CITY RESTED A LITTLE FROM THE MIXING OF THE LEAVEN, UNTIL THE WHOLE WAS LEAVENED) They are like an oven heated by a baker, who ceases to watch after he has deposited the dough, until it ferments. While the baker sleeps, a flame arising from the poorly guarded oven consumes the house. Thus this nation is inflamed with the zeal of idolatry, with Jehu conniving.

More convenient here is the metaphrasis and paraphrase of our Osiander: As an oven heated by a baker (they seem to burn with love of religion while they perform sacred rites), but he (the baker) rests from watching after he has kneaded the dough, until it is leavened: but in the morning he heats the oven: so they indulge in lusts or other shameful acts by night, and on the following day they sacrifice with great ardor. The commentary of the blessed Gesner also agrees with this. See other interpretations in B. Meisner.

Latin:

Vers. 4. OMNES ADVLTERANTES) Facti sunt idololatræ.

QVASI CLIBANVS SVCCENSVS A COQVENTE: QVIEVIT PAVLVLVM CIVITAS A COMMISSIONE FERMENTI, DONEC FERMENTARETVR TOTVM) Similes furno succenso à pistore, qui desint vigilare, postquam deposuit massam, donec ea fermentescat. Dormiente pistore, ex furno male custodito flamma exoriens domum consumit. Ita ista gens incensa est studio idololatriæ, Jehu connivente.

Commodior hic metaphrasis & paraphrasis Osiandri nostri: Quasi clibanus succensus à pistore (videntur ardere religionis amore, dum sacra peragunt) quiescit autem ab evigilando (pistor) postquam massam subegit, donec fermentetur: mane autem clibanum succendit: ita illi noctu libidinibus aut aliis flagitiis indulgent, posteriore die magno ardore sacrificant. Cui etiam consonat B. Gesneri commentarius. Alias interpretationes vide apud B. Meisnerum.

## 7:5
Ver. 5.

THE DAY OF OUR KING: THE PRINCES BEGAN TO RAGE WITH WINE) The day of our king, that is, in the time of the reign of Jehu, who was a king anointed by God, the princes began to act like madmen, as if drunk, concerning the calves. In the Hebrew it is, from a bottle of wine: that is, with much wine, not with sipping cups.

HE STRETCHED OUT HIS HAND WITH THE SCORNERS) לצים, or as it is written elsewhere לצצים, are profane men. For 'he stretched out his hand,' you would rightly translate, 'he drew out his hand': that is, he refrained from punishing them as he ought.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

DIES REGIS NOSTRI: COEPERUNT PRINCIPES FURERE A VINO) Die regis nostri, id est, tempore regni Jehu, qui erat rex à Deo unctus, cœperunt principes velut ebrii insanire circa vitulos. In Hebræo est, ab utre vini: id est, multo vino, non rorantibus poculis.

EXTENDIT MANVM SVAM CVM ILLVSORIBVS) לצים, aut ut scribitur alibi לצצים, sunt homines profani. Pro extendit manum suam, recte verteris, protraxit manum suam: id est, abstinuit eos punire ut debuit.

## 7:6
Ver. 6.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE APPLIED AS AN OVEN THEIR HEART) Those princes were clearly burning with a zeal for illicit worship.

WHEN HE LAY IN WAIT FOR THEM) Better: While the princes themselves were laying snares, namely for the king, with the worst counsels.

ALL THE NIGHT HE SLEPT) For a long time the king dissembled their faults.

BAKING THEM IN THE MORNING THEY THEMSELVES WERE KINDLED AS A FLAMING FIRE) While they were being baked, in the morning he himself was also kindled like a flaming fire. While they proceed in their crimes, gradually he himself was also carried away into the same zeal.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

QVIA APPLICVERVNT QUASI CLIBANVM COR SVVM) Illi principes plane flagrabant studio cultus illiciti.

CUM INSIDIARETUR EIS) Melius: Dum ipsi principes insidias struunt, regi scilicet, pessimis consiliis.

TOTA NOCTE DORMIVIT) Diu rex dissimulavit illorum culpas.

COQVENS EOS MANE IPSIS SUCCENSUS QVASI IGNIS FLAMMÆ) Dum illi coquuntur, mane & ipse succensus est velut flammeus ignis. Dum illi in facinoribus suis pergunt, sensim & ipse in idem studium abreptus est.

## 7:7
Vers. 7.

ALL ARE HEATED AS AN OVEN) Like a furnace. The whole populace of the princes followed the example.

AND THEY HAVE DEVORED THEIR JUDGES) They will devour, that is, they will kill their nobles, as at Thapsa. 2 Kings 15, 16.

ALL THEIR KINGS HAVE FALLEN) They will fall: namely by the snares of the common people, Zacharias, Shallum, Pekahiah. The nobles sinned, the kings sinned: and both these and those will bear their punishments.

THERE IS NONE THAT CRIETH AMONG THEM UNTO ME) Among them: that is, among the people. Although my presence is so apparent with such great signs, there is no one who thinks about appeasing me.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

OMNES CALEFACTI SVNT QVASI CLIBANVS) Ut furnus. Tota plebs principum secuta exemplum.

ET DEVORAVERUNT JUDICES SVOS) Devorabunt, id est, occident proceres suos, ut Thapsæ. 2. Reg. 15, 16.

OMNES REGES EORVM CECIDERVNT) Cadent: nempe insidiis popularium, Zacharias, Sellumus, Phadias. Peccarunt proceres, peccarunt reges: & hi & illi suas pœnas ferent.

NON EST QUI CLAMAT IN EIS AD ME) In eis: id est, in populo. Cum tantis indiciis ita mea appareat, nemo est qui de me placando cogitet.

## 7:8
Vers. 8.

EPHRAIM AMONG THE PEOPLES HE HIMSELF WAS MIXED) He will be mixed: that is, he will be scattered among foreign nations.

EPHRAIM IS BECOME) He will become.

ASH-CAKE, WHICH IS NOT RESERVED) In Hebrew: Which is not turned: that is, which is eaten before it is turned, as the Chaldean explains here. The swiftness of the enemies is signified. The following things confirm this.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

EPHRAIM IN POPVLIS IPSE COMMISCEBATUR) Commiscebitur: id est, inter gentes extraneas spargetur.

EPHRAIM FACTUS EST) Fiet.

SUBCINERICIUS PANIS, QVI NON RESERVATVR) In Hebræo: Qui non versatur: id est, qui comeditur priusquam versetur, ut hic explicat Chaldæus, Significatur hostium celeritas, Firmant hoc sequentia,

## 7:9
Vers. 9.

STRANGERS HAVE EATEN HIS STRENGTH) Riches: for כח often signifies that.

AND HE HIMSELF KNEW NOT) He does not understand the cause.

AND GRAY HAIRS ARE SPRINKLED UPON HIM) That is, he has come near to destruction, like those who grow very gray.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

COMEDERVNT ALIENI ROBUR EJUS) Divitias: כח enim sæpe id significat.

ET IPSE NESCIVIT) Causam non intelligit.

ET CANI EFFUSI SUNT IT EO) Id est, prope ad interitum venit, ut ii qui multum canescunt.

## 7:10
Vers. 10.

AND THE PRIDE OF ISRAEL SHALL BE HUMBLED TO HIS FACE) His pride shall testify against him. As above 5, 5.

AND THEY HAVE NOT SOUGHT HIM IN ALL THESE) When such great dangers were so often denounced to them.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET HVMILIABITVR SVPERBIA ISRAEL IN FACIE EJUS) Testificabitur contra eum fastus suum. Ut supra 5, 5.

ET NON QUÆSIVERVNT EUM IN OMNIBUS HIS) Cum tanta pericula ipsis tam sæpe denunciarentur.

## 7:11
Vers. 11.

AS A SILLY DOVE WITHOUT HEART) Foolish and senseless.

THEY CALLED UPON EGYPT) They call upon. 2 Kings 17, 4.

THEY WENT TO THE ASSYRIANS) They seek now these, now those friendships, not caring for the friendship of God. 2 Kings 15, 19. above 5, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

QUASI COLUMBA SEDUCTA NON HABENS COR) Stolida ac vecors.

ÆGYPTVM INVOCABANT) Invocant. 2. Reg. 17, 4.

AD ASSYRIOS ABIERVNT) Quærunt nunc has, nunc illas amicitias, Dei amicitiam non curantes. 2. Reg. 15, 19. supra 5, 13.

## 7:12
Verse 12.

AND WHEN THEY SHALL HAVE GONE) When they shall have departed: that is, when they shall have done whatever they wished; for thus הלך and πορεύεσθαι are accustomed to be taken.

I WILL SPREAD MY NET OVER THEM) I will execute my decrees.

I WILL BRING THEM DOWN AS A BIRD OF THE HEAVEN) From those mountains of Samaria.

I WILL CHASTISE THEM) I will afflict them with punishments: for that is what יסר means, nor did the Greeks or the Chaldean take it otherwise.

ACCORDING TO THE HEARING OF THEIR CONGREGATION) That is, just as I have often testified to them through the Prophets. 2 Kings 17, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET CUM PROFECTI FUERINT) Cum abierint: id est, ubi fecerint quicquid voluerint; sic enim הלך & πορεύεσθαι sumi solent.

EXPANDAM SVPER EOS RETE MEUM) Decreta mea exsequar.

QUASI VOLUCREM COELI DETRAHAM EOS) De montibus illis Samariæ.

CÆDAM EOS) Pœnis eos afficiam: id enim יסר, nec aliter sumfere Græci, aut Chaldæus.

SECUNDUM AUDITIONEM COETVS EORVM) Id est, prout sæpe eos contestatus sum per Prophetas. 2. Reg. 17, 13.

## 7:13
Verse 13.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME, AND I REDEEMED THEM) For, against me who redeemed them: I freed them from the Egyptians, Canaanites, Midianites, Philistines, Ammonites, Amalekites, Syrians.

AND THEY SPOKE LIES AGAINST ME) Likening me to calves.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

QUIA PRÆVARICATI SVNT IN ME, ET EGO REDEMI EOS) Pro, in me qui redemi eos: liberavi eos ab Ægyptiis, Chananæis, Madianitis, Philistinis, Ammonitis, Amalecitis, Syris.

ET IPSI LOCVTISVNT CONTRA ME MENDACIA) Assimilantes me vitulis.

## 7:14
Verse 14.

AND THEY DID NOT CRY TO ME IN THEIR HEART, BUT HOWLED IN THEIR BEDS) When they were howling. In their evil circumstances they did not pour out prayers to me.

THEY RUMINATED OVER WHEAT AND WINE, THEY DEPARTED FROM ME) When they were ruminating: that is, when they were gorging themselves like cattle with bread and wine, in their good circumstances they went far from me. Thus that saying truly fits them: ἠυλήσαμεν ὑμῖν, κὶ ἐκ ὠρχήσασθε. ἐθρηνήσαμεν ὑμῖν, κὶ ἐκ ἐκόψασθε. Matt. 11, 17.

Those foreign and overly arbitrary [interpretations] concerning the calves. They denote rather lies, calumnies, and blasphemies, by which true religion is torn apart; moreover, they are said to howl in their beds, because in idolatrous temples, in which they pollute themselves with spiritual fornication as if in a bed, they chant impious dirges; and they celebrate not for the glory of God, but for the sake of their own belly: therefore they are said to ruminate over wheat and wine.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET NON CLAMAVERUNT AD ME IN CORDE SVO, SED ULVLABANT IN CVBILIBVS SVIS) Cum ulularent. In rebus suis malis ad me preces non fuderunt.

SVPER TRITICUM ET VINUM RVMINABANT, RECESSERVNT AD ME) Cum ruminarent: id est, cum pecudum more se ingurgitarent pane & vino, in rebus suis bonis longe à me abiere. Ita vere illis convenit illud: ἠυλήσαμεν ὑμῖν, κὶ ἐκ ὠρχήσασθε. ἐθρηνήσαμεν ὑμῖν, κὶ ἐκ ἐκόψασθε. Matth. 11, 17.

Aliena illa & nimis arbitraria de vitulis. Mendacia potius, calumnias & blasphemias, quibus vera religio proscinditur, notant; ululare autem in cubilibus suis dicuntur, quod in templis idololatricis, in quibus sese spirituali fornicatione, tanquam in cubili polluunt, impias nænias decantent; nec gloriæ Dei, sed ventris sui causa celebrent: ideo ruminari dicuntur super triticum & vinum.

## 7:15
AND I INSTRUCTED THEM, AND STRENGTHENED THEIR ARMS, AND AGAINST ME THEY DEVISED MALICE) The same sense as in the preceding: whether I punished them, or added strength to them, they always dishonored me through images.

Latin:

ET EGO ERVDIVI EOS, ET CONFORTAVI BRACHIA EORVM, ET IN ME COGITAVERUNT MALITIAM) Idem sensus, qui in superioribus: sive eos punirem, sive vires ipsis adderem, semper me dehonestarunt per imagines.

## 7:16
Vers. 16. THEY RETURNED THAT THEY MIGHT BE WITHOUT A YOKE) That is, they wished again to be without a yoke. By yoke, the law is to be understood. Both the Chaldean and the Latin took על for עול: and perhaps where there is now a kametz, in other books there was a holem.

THEY BECAME LIKE A DECEITFUL BOW) Which threatens one thing, but strikes another. Psalm 78:57. In the Greek epigram: ἀπόσκοποι οἱ δ' ἐγίνοντο.

THEIR PRINCES SHALL FALL BY THE SWORD) Above v. 7.

FROM THE FURY OF THEIR TONGUE) The beginnings of such conspiracies are from virulent speeches and pamphlets, which Tacitus rightly calls the provocations of the mob. The subject matter of these complaints, however, was sought mostly from taxes.

THIS MOCKERY OF THEIRS IN THE LAND OF EGYPT) Because of those frequent changes, they will be a laughingstock to the Egyptians, whom Virgil also teaches us in the fourth Georgic were very observant of Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 16. REVERSI SVNT UT ESSENT ABSQVE JVGO) Id est, denuo voluerunt esse absque jugo. Per jugum intelligenda lex. Tam Chaldæus quam Latinus על sumfere pro עול: & forte ubi nunc est kametz, in libris aliis fuit holem.

FACTI SVNT QVASI ARCVS DOLOSVS) Qui aliud minatur, aliud ferit. Psalm. 78, 57. in Epigrammate Græco: ἀπόσκοποι οἱ δ' ἐγίνοντο.

CADENT IN GLADIO PRINCIPES EORVM) Supra v. 7.

A FVRORE LINGVÆ SVÆ) Initia talium conjurationum sunt à virulentis sermonibus, & libellis, quos tentamenta vulgi recte vocat Tacitus. Harum autem querelarum materia maxime ex tributis petebatur.

ISTA SVBSANNATIO EORVM IN TERRA ÆGTPTI) Propter crebras illas mutationes ludibrio erunt Ægyptiis, quos valde fuisse Regum observantes etiam Virgilius nos decet Georgicon quarto.

## 8:1 Argument
SERMON V. A TRUMPET CONCERNING THE IMMINENT JUDGMENT OF GOD, ON ACCOUNT OF THE VIOLATION OF THE DIVINE COVENANT. CHAPTER VIII. A threatening trumpet. The Prophet is commanded to sound the trumpet to the Israelites concerning the coming of the Assyrian, to avenge the divine covenant, because they have chosen kings without God, have formed for themselves idols, primarily the calf in Samaria, have entered into a covenant with the Assyrians, are erecting many altars, hold the law of God in contempt, and offer sacrifices without faith: a threat is also added against the Jews, who trust in their fortifications. On account of the worship of the calf, a heavy punishment from Assur is imminent.

Vers. 1.

IN THY THROAT LET THERE BE A TRUMPET) God addresses the prophet Hosea, and wishes him to proclaim with a very loud voice both the sins of the people and the evils that are to come. A similar locution is in Isaiah 58:1. חיך properly means the palate, but it is taken synecdochically for the whole mouth. The LXX in their codices less correctly had אל-חיך כנשר as εἰς κόλπον αὐτῶν ὡς γῆ.

AS AN EAGLE OVER THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) Which may be heard as widely as an eagle flying over the temple, and croaking from on high. Compare Rev. 8:13.

FOR THAT THEY HAVE TRANSGRESSED MY COVENANT) That they have transgressed my covenant. For this is the very thing which GOD wishes to be proclaimed.

Latin:

CONCIO V. TUBA DE IMMINENTI DEI JUDICIO, OB FOEDERIS DIVINI VIOLATIONEM. CAPUT VIII. Tuba comminatoria. Jubetur Prophet a Israelitis ebuccinare Assyrii, ad vindicandum fœdus divinum, adven- tum, quod Reges absque Deo elegerint, ido- la, imprimis vitulum in Samaria sibi for- marint, cum Assyriis fœdus inierint, alta- ria multa erigant, legem Dei contemtui habeant, sacrificia sine fide offerant : ad- dita etiam contra Judæos, in munitionibus confidentes, comminatione. Ob vituli cultum gravis instat ab Assure pœna.

Vers. 1.

IN GUTTURE TVO SIT TVBA) Prophetam Oseam Deus alloquitur, vultque eum editissima voce pro- clamare & peccata populi & mala eventura. Similis locu- tio Esaia 58, 1. חיך proprie palatum, sed sumitur συνεκδο- χικῶς pro ore toto. LXX. in suis codicibus minus recte habuerunt אל-חיך כנשר cis xόλπον αυτών ως γῆ.

QUASI AQUILA SVPER DOMVM DOMINI) Quæ tam late audiatur, quam aquila templum supervoli- tans, & e sublimi crocitans. Confer. Apoc. 8, 13.

PRO EO QVOD TRANSGRESSI SUNT FE- DUS MEUM) Transgressos hos esse fœdus meum. Hoc enim ipsum est quod proclamari vult DEUS.

## 8:2
Vers. 2.

THEY SHALL CALL UPON ME) The time will come when they are about to call upon me,

MY GOD) They shall say individually, My God. Thus Cornelius Severus: ---and poured out upon the grass, This is my day, they said.

They said, says Seneca, not all at once, but each one individually.

WE HAVE KNOWN THEE ISRAEL) We Israelites have known thee to be the true God. Similar to Matt. 7:22.

ISRAEL HAS CAST OFF THE GOOD) Understand, God will answer, Israel flees from the good. The good, that is, the benefactor.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ME INVOCABUNT) Tempus veniet cum me in- vocaturi sunt,

DEUS MEUS) Singuli dicent, Deus meus. Sic Cornelius Severus: ---fusique per herbam Hic meus est dixere dies.

Dixerunt, ait Seneca, non omnes simul, sed singuli cœnus.

COGNOVIMUS TE ISRAEL) Non Israelitæ te DEum verum esse cognovimus. Simile Matth. 7, 22.

PROJECIT ISRAEL BONUM) Subintellige, respon- debit Deus, Fugit Israel a bono. Bonum, id est, ευεργέτην.

## 8:3
THE ENEMY SHALL PURSUE HIM) Namely, in such a way that he cannot flee.

Latin:

INIMICUS PERSEQVETVR EVM) Nempe ita, ut fugere nequeat.

## 8:4
Verse 4.

THEY REIGNED, AND NOT FROM ME) They make kings. For it is Hiphil, that is to say, often: for Jeroboam and Jehu and their descendants reigned by GOD's command: not likewise those who were in the time between them, as neither those who were after the descendants of Jehu.

THEY HAVE BECOME PRINCES) They appoint princes. For it is the same form of the verb. The judges of the two tribes had their origin from GOD, the judges of the ten tribes from the kings.

AND I HAVE NOT KNOWN) That is, I have not approved of them.

THEIR SILVER AND THEIR GOLD THEY HAVE MADE FOR THEMSELVES IDOLS) עצב properly signifies sorrow. The Hebrews called idols by these and other fatal or vile words: as 1 Kings 31:9 and often elsewhere.

THAT THEY MIGHT PERISH) In the Hebrew: Therefore he shall be cut off, supply the people.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

IPSI REGNAVERVNT, ET NON EX ME) Reges faciunt. Est enim Hiphil, sæpe scilicet: nam Jero- boamus & Jehu eorumque posteri DEI jussu regnarunt: non item illi qui medio inter eos tempore fuere, ut nec illi qui post Jehu posteros.

PRINCIPES EXSTITERVNT) Principes consti- tuunt. Est enim forma eadem verbi. Judices duarum tri- buum originem habebant a DEO, judices decem tribuum a regibus.

ET NON COGNOVI) Id est, non approbavi eos.

ARGENTVM SUUM ET AURUM SVVM FE- CERUNT SIBI IDOLA) עצב proprie dolorem signi- ficat. Hebræi & his & aliis funestis aut vilibus vocabulis appellavere idola: ut 1. Reg. 31, 9. & alibi sæpe.

UT INTERIRENT) In Hebræo: Ideo exscindetur, supple populus.

## 8:5
Verse 5.

THY CALF IS CAST OFF, O SAMARIA) Thy calf shall desert thee, O Samaria. That is, it will profit thee nothing in dangers.

MY FURY IS KINDLED AGAINST THEM) The worshippers of the calves.

HOW LONG WILL THEY NOT BE ABLE TO BE CLEANSED?) In the Hebrew: How long will they not be able to [attain] innocence? that is, to be loved.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PROJECTVS EST VITULUS TUUS SAMA- RIA) Deseret te vitulus tuus, o Samaria. Id est, nihil in pe- riculis tibi proderit.

IRATUS EST FVROR MEVS IN EOS) Vitu- lorum cultores.

USQUE NON POTERVNT EMUNDARI?) In Hebræo: Usquequo non poterunt innocentiam ? amari scilicet.

## 8:6
Verse 6. FOR FROM ISRAEL IT ALSO IS) Not of the Ammonites, or of the Moabites, but this is the invention of Israel himself.

THE WORKMAN MADE IT) Molten.

AND THERE IS NO GOD) There is no divine power in it.

FOR THE CALF OF SAMARIA SHALL BE AS SPIDER WEBS) For it will be reduced into the smallest parts. By that argument it will sufficiently appear to all that there is nothing divine in it. שבב is the smallest thing in any matter, such as a spark, fragments, segments: Jerome called them atoms in his Commentary. This was done by the Assyrians. The Greeks thought ש to have the same value as ס. And so some translated it as wandering, others as unstable, others as roving.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QVIA EX ISRAEL ET IPSE EST) Non Ammonitarum, aut Moabitarum, sed ipsius Israelis hoc est commentum.

ARTIFEX FECIT ILLUM) Fufos.

ET NON EST DEUS) Nulla in eo est vis divina.

QUONIAM IN ARANEARUM TELAS ERIT VITVLVS SAMARIÆ) Nam in minutissimas partes re- digetur. Eo argumento satis apparebit omnibus, nihil in eo esse divini. שבב est minimum quidque in re quavis, ut scintilla, fragmenta, segmenta: atomos dixit in Com- mentario Hieronymus. Factum hoc per Assyrios. Græci ש putarunt idem valere quod ס. Itaque verterunt alii πλανῶν, alii ἀκατάσατον, alii ῥεμβεύων.

## 8:7
Ver. 7. FOR THEY SHALL SOW THE WIND, AND

THEY SHALL REAP THE WHIRLWIND) A proverbial expression, signifying that the reward of empty works will be calamitous. Similar to Job 4:8, Prov. 22:8. For wind, the LXX here have wind-blasted, in which way seeds are said to be, which are empty, that is, have no marrow, as Jerome notes here. The same LXX placed destruction for whirlwind: but the sense expressed in the Latin is simpler. The Chaldean says that those things which were sown while the wind was blowing will be cast down by a whirlwind.

THE STANDING STALK IS NOT IN IT, THE BUD SHALL NOT MAKE FLOUR) Distinguish it thus: The standing stalk, there is no bud in it, nor shall it produce flour. The sense is plain: that the stalk will indeed rise, but without a bud; and consequently there will be no yield of grain from it.

WHICH IF IT SHALL HAVE MADE) If the stalk shall have produced any fruit.

STRANGERS SHALL EAT IT) Foreigners. The natives will say: Behold those for whom we have sown the fields.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QUIA VENTUM SEMINABUNT, ET

TURBINEM METENT) Proverbiale, significans ina- nium operum calamitosam fore mercedem. Simile Job. 4, 8. Prov. 22, 8. pro vento LXX. hic habent ἀνεμόφθορα, quomodo dici semina, quæ ἰτερευμένη, id est, medullam non habent, notat hic Hieronymus. Iidem LXX. pro turbine posuerunt κατατροφὴν : sed sensus in Latino expressus sim- plicior est. Chaldæus, quæ vento flante seminata sunt, a turbine ait dejectum iri.

CULMUS STANS NON EST IN EO,GERMEN NON FACIET FARINAM) Distingue sic: Culmus stans, non est in eo germen, neque proferet farinam. Sensus est pla- nus: culmum quidem surrecturum, sed sine germine; ac proinde nullum inde futurum frumenti proventum.

QUOD ETSI FECERIT) Si quid frugis protulerit culmus.

ALIENI COMEDENT EAM) Extranei. Dicent indigenæ: En queis consevimus agros.

## 8:8
Ver. 8. ISRAEL IS DEVOURED)

NOW) Within a short time.

HE IS BECOME AMONG THE NATIONS) He shall become.

AS AN UNCLEAN VESSEL) Displeasing, in the Hebrew: as a chamber pot, or urinal, which we use, but with contempt.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DEVORATVS EST ISRAEL) Absorbebitur Israel.

NUNC) Intra breve tempus.

FACTVS EST IN NATIONIBUS) Fiet.

QVASI VAS IMMUNDUM) Displicens, in He- bræo: ut lasanum, aut matula, quibus utimur, sed cum contemtu.

## 8:9
Ver. 9.

FOR THEY HAVE GONE UP TO ASSYRIA, A SOLITARY WILD ASS FOR HIMSELF) They shall go up to the Assyrian, a solitary wild ass for himself: That which we read in 2 Kings 15:21 and 17:3 is predicted again. The Assyrian is called a wild ass feeding by himself, because he managed only his own affairs and did not care for other nations. The LXX here, for פרא, which signifies a wild ass, read פרה, which is ἀνιδάζει.

EPHRAIM HAVE GIVEN GIFTS TO LOVERS) Namely, for the sake of conciliation, so that they might obtain peace and a treaty from the Assyrian. See the aforementioned place in 2 Kings, and add Ezekiel 16:33.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

QUIA IPSI ASCENDERVNT AD ASSVR, O- NAGER SOLITARIUS SIBI) Ascendent ad Assyrium, onagrum solitarium sibi: Prædicitur rursus id, quod legi- mus 2. Reg. 15, 21. & 17, 3. Assyrius dicitur onager sibi pascens, quod sui solius negotia gereret, alias gentes non curaret. LXX. hic pro פרא, quod onagrum significat, le- gerunt פרה, quod est ἀνιδάζει.

EPHRAIM MUNERA DEDERUNT AMATO- RIBUS) Nempe conciliandis, ut pacem & fedus ab Assy- rio impetrarent. Vide dictum locum 2. Reg. & adde Ezech. 16, 33.

## 8:10
Verse 10.

BUT EVEN THOUGH THEY HAVE HIRED NATIONS WITH A PRICE) Even though they have hired nations with a price. Namely, being not at all solicitous about joining God to themselves.

NOW I WILL GATHER THEM) I will bring those very Assyrians against the Israelites.

AND THEY SHALL REST A LITTLE WHILE FROM THE BURDEN OF KINGS AND PRINCES) This is a mockery. They complained vehemently about those burdens which the kings of Israel and the prefects of the kings imposed upon them: and therefore they killed the kings and prefects, ch. 5:7, 7:16. I will bring it about that they shall pay nothing to those kings or prefects, namely, when they live in a servile condition in the lands of the Assyrians. Moreover, that word, 'a little while,' is said in derision, for the condition which is predicted here was to last a long time. This interpreter rightly derives חלו from יחל, which is to wait, to rest, not from חלל, as others do. Verse 11.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

SED ET CUM MERCEDE CONDUXERINT NATIONES) Quimercede conduxerunt nationes. De Deo scilicet sibi adjungendo nihil solliciti.

NUNC CONGREGABO EOS) Illos ipsos Assy- rios contra Israelitas adducam.

ET QVIESCENT PAULISTER AB ONERE REGUM ET PRINCIPUM) Est χλευασμός. Conquesti vehementer sunt de iis oneribus, quæ reges Israelis, re- gumque præfecti ipsis imponebant: ideoque reges & præ- tectos occiderunt c. 5, 7. 7, 16. Efficiam ego; ne quic- quam pendant regibus illis, aut præfectis, nimirum cum ser- vili conditione in Assyriorum terris vivent. Est autem & il- lud, paulisper, dictu per irrifum, diu enim duratura erat, quæ hic prædicitur conditio. Interpres hic recte חלו derivat a יחל, quod est expectare, quiescere, non a חלל, ut alii. Vers. 11.

## 8:11
BECAUSE EPHRAIM HAS MULTIPLIED ALTARS TO SIN, ALTARS HAVE BEEN MADE FOR HIM FOR AN OFFENSE) In the Hebrew, לחטא is used twice, but with a different sense: because they made many altars for themselves, in which they might sin against God, therefore the altars, namely of the Assyrians, will be a punishment to them, when they are forced to carry wood, water, and victims there.

Latin:

QUIA MULTIPLICAVIT EPHRAIM ALTARIA AD PECCANDUM, FACTÆ SUNT EI ARÆ IN DELICTVM) In Hebræo bis est לחטא, sed sensu diverso: quia multa sibi altaria fecerunt, in quibus contra Deum peccarent, ideo altaria, Assyriorum scilicet, ipsis in pœnam erunt, cum ligna, aquam, victimas eo ferre cogentur.

## 8:12
Verse 12.

I WILL WRITE FOR HIM MY MULTIPLE LAWS) I had written for them my multiple laws: through Moses.

The Vulgate version had to be corrected: for חורתי ברי are not my multiple laws, but the great things of my law. However, the first member is not badly read according to the keri ברי by Lud. de Dieu by way of an interrogation: Shall I write for him the great things of my law? They are reckoned as something foreign. He also says that the reading רבו rightly squares: When I write for him my excellence, namely my law, they are reckoned as something foreign.

WHICH HAVE BEEN RECKONED AS ALIEN) The Israelites held them as a thing pertaining in no way to themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SCRIBAM EI MULTIPLICES LEGES MEAS) Scripseram eis multiplices leges meas : per Mosen.

Emendanda erat vulgata versio:nam חורתי ברי non sunt multiplices leges meæ, sed magnalia legis mea. Non male autem primum membrum juxta το keri ברי Lud. de Dieu legit per interrogationis modum: Scribo ei magnalia legis mea? tanquam pe- regrinum quid reputantur. τε Letif רבו etiam re- cte quadrare ait : Quum fcribo ei præftantiam tuam,nempe legem meam, tanquam extraneum quid reputantur.

QVÆ VELUT ALIENÆ COMPUTATÆ SVNT) Habuerunt eas Israelitæ, tanquam rem ad se nihil pertinentem.

## 8:13
Verse 13. THEY SHALL OFFER SACRIFICES, THEY SHALL SACRIFICE FLESH, AND EAT, AND THE LORD WILL NOT ACCEPT THEM) As regards the flesh of the sacrifices which they offer to me, let them slaughter them and eat them, as much as they want: but God will not hold them acceptable, because they are given with an unamended mind.

(NOW HE WILL REMEMBER THEIR INIQUITY, AND WILL VISIT THEIR SINS: THEY SHALL RETURN TO EGYPT) In short, He will call their misdeeds to mind, and will punish their crimes, when they themselves set their heart upon Egypt: namely, against the faith given to the Assyrian, see this fulfilled 2 Kings 17, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 13. HOSTIAS OFFERENT, IMMOLABUNT CARNES, ET COMEDENT, ET DOMINVS NON SVSCIPIET EAS) Hostiarum quas mihi offerunt carnes, quod attinet, mačtento eas & comedunto, quantum volent: Deus autem eas gratas non habebit, quia dantur animo non emendato.

NUNC RECORDABITUR INIQVITATIS EO- RUM, ET VISITABIT PECCATA EORVM IPSI IN ÆGYPTUM CONVERTENTUR) Brevi in memoriam revocabit eorum facinora, & crimina eorum puniet, cum ipsi animum ad Ægyptum adjiciant: nempe contra fidem Assyrio datam, Impletum hoc vide 2. Reg. 17, 4.

## 8:14
Verf. 14. AND ISRAEL HAS FORGOTTEN HIS MAKER) And for 'nam'. AND BUILT TEMPLES) In very many places. AND JUDAH MULTIPLIED FORTIFIED CITIES) The two tribes, seeing the incursions of the Assyrians under Phul, Tiglath-Pileser, and Shalmaneser into the land of the ten tribes, diligently fortified their cities, secure in obtaining God's peace. Isaiah 22, 8. I WILL SEND FIRE INTO HIS CITIES) Namely, Judah's, as the construction indicates. This was done when Sennacherib burned all the cities outside Jerusalem. AND IT SHALL DEVOUR HIS PALACES) And for 'cum'. When (the Assyrian fire) shall have devoured his palaces: namely, of the nation of the ten tribes.

Latin:

Verf. 14. ET OBLITUS EST ISRAEL FACTO- RIS SUI) Et pro nam. ET ÆDIFICAVIT DELUBRA)] Plurimis in locis. ET JUDAS MULTIPLICAVIT URBES MUNI- TAS) Duæ tribus, videntes incurfus Afsyriorum sub Phule, Theglathphalasaro, & Salmanasaro in terram de- cem tribuum, urbes suas diligenter muniverunt, de Dei pace obtinenda securi. Esaiæ 22, 8. MITTAM IGNEM IN CIVITATES EJUS) Nempe Judæ, ut constructio indicat. Hoc factum cum Sennacheribus omnes urbes extra Hierosolyma combussit. ET DEVORABIT ÆDES ILLIUS) Et pro cum. Cum devoraverit (ignis Assyrius) ædes illius: nempe gentis decem tribuum.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX. The trumpet blunting the boastings of Israel.

The people's boasting of blessing through the worship of idols, the subtraction of blessing, the ejection into Egypt and Assyria, where there is no place for sacrifices or feasts. The vain prophecies of false prophets are to be recognized, whose doctrine is a snare to idolatry, as once the daughters of the Moabites were to the worship of Baal-Peor: Therefore the glory of Ephraim is to perish, the sons to be killed, the families to be punished with sterility, the whole people for idolatry in Gilgal to be eliminated from the house of the Lord, to be trampled by enemies, to be rejected by GOD. A sick, sterile famine will befall the worshippers of the altar.

Verf. 1.

DO NOT REJOICE, O ISRAEL, DO NOT EXULT LIKE THE PEOPLES) Do not please yourself in prosperous things, as other nations do. BECAUSE YOU HAVE PLAYED THE HARLOT FROM YOUR GOD) Punishment hangs over you because of idolatry. YOU HAVE LOVED A REWARD) You hoped that you would have a reward for its worship. Properly אתנה, or אתנן is said of the reward of a harlot, which fits this place very well. UPON ALL CORNFLOORS) ἐπιτηδὲς, for that which we would call prosperity throughout all the grain floors: namely, the reward of your worship, as preceded. Compare above 2, 12.

Latin:

CAPUT IX. Tuba gloriationes Ifrael. retundens.

Populi gloriatio de benedictione penes cultum idolorum, subtractione benedictionis, eje- ctione in Ægyptum & Assyriam, ubi nul- lus sacrificiis, aut festis locus. Falsorum Prophetarum vaticinia vana agnoscenda, quorum doctrina laqueus ad idolola- triam est, ut olim Moabitarum filiæ ad cultum Baal-Peor: Ideo gloria Ephraim peritura, filii occidendi, familiæ sterilitate puniendæ, populus totus ob idololatriam in Gilgal è domo Domini eliminandus, ab ho- stibus conculcandus, à DEO reprobandus. Accidet ægra fames sterilis cultoribus aræ.

Verf. 1.

NOLI LÆTARI ISRAEL, NOLI EXSULTARE SICUT POPULI) Noli tibi placere in rebus prosperis, ut aliæ gentes faciunt. QUIA FORNICATUS ES A DEO TUO) Pœ- na tibi imminet ob idololatriam. DILEXISTI MERCEDEM) Sperasti te mercedem, habitūrum ejus cultus. Proprie אתנה, five אתנן de mer- cede meretricis dicitur, quod huic loco optime convenit. SUPER OMNES AREAS TRITICI) ἐπιτηδὲς, pro eo quod diceremus prosperitatem per omnes areas fru- mentarias: mercedem scilicet cultus tui, ut præcessit. Con- fer supra 2, 12.

## 9:2
Verf. 2.

THE FLOOR AND THE WINEPRESS SHALL NOT FEED THEM) Its citizens. You dedicated your fields and vineyards to false gods. You acted ἀδικα. God will show that these are in no one's power but His own, and how that hope in false gods was false. See above 2, 9. and 8, 7. this sterility seems to have preceded the arrival of Tiglath-Pileser a little. AND THE WINE SHALL DECEIVE THEM) In a similar expression Horace: The crop deceived the hope.

Latin:

Verf. 2.

AREA ET TORCULAR NON PASCET EOT) Cives suos. Dedicasti arva & vineta tua diis falsis. Egisti ἀδικα. Deus ostendet, hæc in non alterius, quam in sua esse potestate, & quam spes ista in diis falsis falsa fuerit. Vide supra 2, 9. & 8, 7. hæc sterilitas videtur paulum præcessisse adventum Teglathphalasari. ET VINUM MENTIETUR EIS) Simili locutio- ne Horatius: Spem mentita seges.

## 9:3
Verf. 3.

THEY SHALL NOT DWELL IN THE LORD'S LAND) And deservedly, since they said it was the land of idols. EPHRAIM HAS RETURNED TO EGYPT) He shall return whence I led them out: Namely, because many of the ten tribes at the first arrival of Shalmaneser retreated into Egypt. See the similar passage in Isaiah 11, 11. AND IN ASSYRIA) Among the Assyrians, under whom they will live as slaves. HE SHALL EAT THE POLLUTED) He shall eat. Foods forbidden by my law, which he ate in my land, he will eat there by command, and to his weariness.

Latin:

Verf. 3.

NON HABITABUNT IN TERRA DOMINI) Et merito, quam illi idolorum terram esse dixerunt. REVERSUS EST EPHRAIM IN ÆGYPTUM) Revertetur unde ego eos eduxi: Nempe quia multi de de- cem tribubus ad primum adventum Salmanasari in Ægy- ptum se recepere. Vide simile Esaiæ 11, 11. ET IN ASSTRIIS) Inter Assyrios, sub quibus ser- vi vivent. POLLUTUM COMEDIT) Comedet. Cibos lege mea vetitos, quos in mea terra comedit, ibi comedet ex im- perio, & ad tædium.

## 9:4
Verf. 4.

THEY SHALL NOT POUR OUT WINE TO THE LORD) They had omitted this, when they could: the time will come that they may wish to pour out to GOD, and cannot. AND THEIR SACRIFICES SHALL NOT PLEASE HIM) Thus it must be distinguished with the Chaldean, if they wish to offer victims, they will not be pleasing to God, because they are against the law in a profane soil. AS THE BREAD OF MOURNERS) Like νεκρόδειπνα, or περίδειπνα, from which nothing is accustomed to be brought into the Temple. Concerning such feasts see Proverbs 31, 6. and Jeremiah 16, 7. ALL WHO EAT IT SHALL BE POLLUTED) Who shall eat of it: namely, the sacrifice, they shall be impure, because in such a place sacrifices are repugnant to the law.

FOR THEIR BREAD IS FOR THEIR SOULS) Their food will be for themselves: it will be able to serve only their own uses, as if he were saying: ὀνησις. לחם to the Hebrews is everything that is eaten. IT SHALL NOT ENTER INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) They will be able to send nothing of it to the Temple, which they omitted before when they could do so. The Temple will be too far away from them: afterwards it will also be taken away. WHAT WILL YOU DO ON THE SOLEMN DAY, ON THE DAY OF THE FEAST OF THE LORD?) מועד, which is translated here as the solemn day, is said especially of the Passover, and those days on which the law had commanded to assemble into the Temple from all the land. Exodus 13, 10. 23, 15. 34, 18. Leviticus 23, 4. But חג, which he translated here as the day of the feast, extends more widely, as appears in Judges 21, 19. and Ezekiel 46, 11. where the Latin interpreter understood the new moons, which he calls markets. What will you do then, says the Prophet, when those three solemn days come, or other feast days? You will want to rest: but your masters will not permit that to you. They will press you with works. See above 2, 11.

Latin:

Verf. 4.

NON LIBABUNT DOMINO VINUM) Omise- rant id, cum possent: tempus veniet ut libare DEO velint, & non possint. ET NON PLACEBUNT EI SACRIFICIA EO- RUM) Sic distinguendum cum Chaldæo, si victimas of- ferre velint, non erunt Deo gratæ, quia contra legem in so- lo profano. QUASI PANIS LUGENTIUM) Tanquam νεκρό- δειπνα, sive περίδειπνα, de quibus nihil solet inferri in Tem- plum. De talibus epulis vide Proverb. 31, 6. & Jerem. 16, 7. OMNES QUI COMEDENT EUM CONTA- MINABUNTUR) Qui comedent de eo: nempe sacrificio, impuri erunt, quia in tali loco sacrificia legi repugnant.

QUIA PANIS EORUM ANIMÆ IPSORUM) Cibus eorum ipsis erit: ipsorum tantum usibus servire pote- rit, quasi dicat: ὀνησις. לחם Hebræis est omne quod editur. NON INTRABIT IN DOMUM DOMINI) Ni- hil ejus mittere ad Templum poterunt, quod antehac cum facere possent, omiserunt. Nimis longe ab ipsis aberit Tem- plum: postea & auferetur. QUID FACIETIS IN DIE SOLENNI, IN DIE FESTIVITATIS DOMINI?) מועד, quod hic vertitur dies solennis, eximie dicitur de Paschate, & illis diebus quibus ex omni terra in Templum conveniri lex præceperat. Exod. 13, 10. 23, 15.34, 18. Levit. 23, 4. חג vero quod hic transtulit, diem festivitalis, latius patet, ut apparet Jud. 21, 19. & Ezech. 46, 11. ubi interlunia in- tellexit Latinus interpres, quas nundinas appellat. Quid facietis tunc, ait Propheta, cum venient tres illi dies solen- nes, aut alii dies festi? voletis otiari: sed domini vobis id non permittent: urgebunt vos operibus. Vide supra 2, 11.

## 9:6
Verse 6.

FOR BEHOLD THEY HAVE GONE FORTH FROM DEVASTATION) Behold, some are departing from the devastated land. Let there be some who escape the hands of the Assyrians, as we noted above that it happened in 3. EGYPT SHALL GATHER THEM) It will compose them. It will perform the funeral rites for them, and they shall not return to their homeland. MEMPHIS SHALL BURY THEM) An explanation of the preceding. See Isaiah 29, 13. THE NETTLE SHALL INHERIT THEIR DESIRABLE SILVER) In the Hebrew: The desire of their silver the nettle shall possess. That is, houses bought at a great price. A THISTLE IN THEIR TABERNACLES) In their palaces. What this interpreter translates as thistles, the Greeks translate as thorns: the Chaldean as cats: nevertheless, you may find קמוש for thorns also in the Chaldean interpreters elsewhere.

Latin:

Verf. 6.

ECCE ENIM PROFECTI SUNT A VASTITA- TE) Ecce abeunt quidam è terra vastata. Sint quidam qui Assyriorum manus effugiant, ut evenisse & supra nota- vimus 3. ÆGYPTUS CONGREGABIT EOS) Componet illos. Pollincturam illis faciet, nec redibunt in patriam. MEMPHIS SEPELIET EOS) ἐπεξήγησις præce- dentis. Vide Esaiam 29, 13. DESIDERABILE ARGENTUM EORUM URTICA HEREDITABIT) In Hebræo: Desiderium ar- genti eorum possidebit urtica. Id est, domos magno pretio comparatas. LAPPA IN TABERNACULIS EORUM) In præ- toriis. Quod hic interpres lappas, spinas vertunt Græci: Chaldæus feles: tamen קמוש pro spinis etiam in Chaldæis interpretibus alibi reperias.

## 9:7
Verse 7.

THE DAYS OF VISITATION HAVE COME, THE DAYS OF RETRIBUTION HAVE COME) They will come. KNOW O ISRAEL) Israel shall know: namely, that I have spoken the truth, as the Chaldean supplies here. THE FOOLISH PROPHET) Better in a new sense in the nominative, the mad Prophet: that is, the possessed one, such as those were, whom not God, but a demon agitated. THE SPIRITUAL MAN, FOR THE MULTITUDE OF THINE INIQUITY AND THE MULTITUDE OF MADNESS) The man is a Spirit, that is, breathing to increase your iniquity, and to the force of hatred. All their words are nothing other than to kindle your faults and hatred against the good.

Latin:

Verf. 7.

VENERUNT DIES VISITATIONIS, VENE- RUNT DIES RETRIBUTIONIS) Venient. SCITOTE ISRAEL) Scient Israel: me scilicet ve- rum dixisse, ut hic supplet Chaldæus. STULTUM PROPHETAM) Melius novo sensu in nominativo, furiosus Propheta: id est, arreptitius, quales e- rant, quos non Deus, sed dæmon agitabat. VIRUM SPIRITUALEM, PROPTER MULTI- TUDINEM INIQUITATIS TUÆ ET MULTITU- DINEM AMENTIÆ) Vir est Spiritus, id est, spirans ad augendam iniquitatem tuam, & ad vim odii. Omnia illo- rum verba nihil aliud, quam culpas vestras, odiumque in bonos accendunt.

## 9:8
Verse 8.

THE WATCHMAN OF EPHRAIM WITH MY GOD: THE PROPHET HAS BECOME A SNARE OF RUIN, OVER ALL HIS WAYS, MADNESS IN THE HOUSE OF HIS GOD) All the expositions of this passage are difficult: a more easy one offers itself if you read צפה, not with the Hiric subscript, but with a Patach, so that it signifies the people, and the sense may be: The watchman of Ephraim, who was the people of God, that is, the Prophet, (who indeed calls himself such) has become a snare for ruin in all his ways, in hatred against the house of his God: that is, the Jerusalem Temple. Those false prophets were setting traps along all the ways for good men wishing to go to the Temple. Compare above 6, 9.

THERE is no reason why we should change the points of the text, for that is not situated within our discretion. Nor does it appear how the Grotian interpretation is easier than if you understand it with B. Luther, Osiander, Gesner, Meisner, and others in a comparative sense, that the ancient Prophets were indeed watchmen, such as God requires, Ezek. 3, 17, divinely excited and speaking from God, but that those who now sell themselves as Prophets are impostors, or if absolutely with others in this way: they called themselves watchmen of Ephraim, who are and speak with my GOD, but the Prophet is a snare of a fowler; or: he who ought to be the watchman of Ephraim with my God, and the Prophet, he is a snare, etc. or as Lodovicus de Dieu: Watchman, thus צופה, let it not be a noun but a verb: Ephraim with my God (he seems to want to adhere to God, but he only acts as a watchman with Him) the Prophet

He is the fowler's snare in all his ways. We see no reason why that sense, either compared or absolved from the debt, which is the fowler's snare, should not be admitted, since he ought to be a watcher with God: nay, this is easier and more obvious than the Grotian one. Verf. 9. THEY HAVE DEEPLY CORRUPTED THEMSELVES) Most imprudently they have corrupted themselves. Wickedness does not swim on the surface for them, but resides in the deepest heart.

Latin:

Verf. 8.

SPECULATOR EPHRAIM CUM DEO MEO: PROPHETA LAQUEUS RUINÆ FACTUS EST, SU- PER OMNES VIAS EJUS, INSANIA IN DOMO DEI EJUS) Duræ sunt omnes hujus loci expositiones: facilior se offert, si צפה legas, non subscripto Hiric, sed Patach, ut populum significet, sensusque sit: Speculator E- phraim, qui populus Dei fuit, id est, Propheta, (qui nempe talem se dicit) laqueus ad ruinam factus est in omnibus viis ejus, odio adversus domum Dei ejus: id est, Templum Hie- rosolymitanum. Pseudoprophetæ isti insidias tendebant per omnes vias viris bonis ire volentibus ad Templum. Confer supra 6, 9.

NON est quod mutemus textus puncta, neque enim id in nostro arbitrio situm est. Nec apparet, quomodo facilior sit Grotiana interpre- tatio, quam si cum B. Luthero, Osiandro, Gesnero, Meisnero, & aliis intelligas sensu comparato, Veteres quidem Prophetas fpeculatores fuisse, quales Deus requirit, Ezech. 3, 17. divinitus excitatos, & ex Deo loquutos, sed istos, qui nunc pro Prophetis se venditant, impostores esse, vel si absolute cum aliis hoc modo: vocarunt se speculatores Ephraim, qui cum DEO meo sint & loquantur, Prophetas, la- queus autem sunt aucupis; vel: qui debet esse spe- culator Ephraim cum Deo meo, & Propheta, is est laqueus, &c. vel ut Lodovicus de Dieu: Specula- tor fic צופה non nomen sit sed verbum: Ephraimus apud Deum meum (videtur velle adhærere Deo, sed speculatorem tantum agit apud eum) Propheta

Laqueus aucupis est in omnibus viis eius. Nihil videmus causae, cur non vel comparatus ille sensus, vel ab solutus de debito, quo, qui laqueus aucupis est, speculator cum Deo esse debeat, admittendus sit: imo hic facilior magisque obvius est, quam Grotianus. Verf. 9. PROFUNDE PECCAVERUNT) Imprudentissime se corruperunt. Non in superficie natat illis improbitas, sed in imo corde refidet.

## 9:9
AS IN THE DAYS OF GIBEAH) The history is in Jud. 19, 16, 22, & following. Verf. 10. I FOUND ISRAEL LIKE GRAPES IN THE DESERT) If grapes should happen to someone wandering through the desert of Arabia, he rejoices greatly in them: so also God was glad when He saw the good actions of the Israelite people in the desert. AS THE FIRST RIPE FRUIT OF THE FIG TREE AT ITS TOP, I SAW THEIR FATHERS) I saw in its beginning (the people now liberated) your fathers (namely those who had gone out from Egypt) like early figs.

Premature figs are loved, but they perish easily. Pliny 17, 27. BUT THEY THEMSELVES ENTERED UNTO BAAL-PEOR) Into the temple of the idol of the Moabites. Num. 25, 3. AND THEY WERE ALIENATED UNTO CONFUSION) ἀπηλλοτριώθησαν εἰς αἰσχύνην, that is, they were initiated into shameful rites: for such are almost the mysteries of Baal-peor, as those among the Egyptians of Osiris, among the Greeks of Father Liber, and Ceres.

Latin:

SICUT IN DIEBUS GABAA) Historia est Jud. 19, 16. 22. & sequentibus. Verf. 10. QUASI UVAS IN DESERTO INVENI ISRAEL) Si cui per desertam Arabiam peregrinam uvae obveniant, valde eis laetatur: sic & Deus laetus est, cum vidit populi Israelitici in deserto actiones bonas. QUASI PRIMA POMA FICULNEAE IN CACUMINE EJUS, VIDI PATRES EORUM) Vidi in principio ejus (populi jam liberati) patres vestros (nempe eos qui ex Aegypto exierant) quasificus praecoces.

Ficus praematurae amantur, sed facile pereunt. Plinius 17, 27. IPSI AUTEM INTRAVERUNT AD BEEL PHEGOR) In templum idoli Moabitarum. Num. 25, 3. ET ABALIENATI SUNT IN CONFUSIONE) ἀπηλλοτριώθησαν εἰς αἰσχύνην, id est, initiati sunt sacris pudendis: nam talia ferme μυστήρια τῶ Beelphegor, qualia apud Aegyptios Osiridis, apud Graecos Liberi patris, & Cereris.

## 9:10
AND THEY BECAME ABOMINABLE, AS THOSE THINGS WHICH THEY LOVED) Idols are called by the Hebrews shiqquwtsim, and that Hebrew word is accustomed to be translated 'idol', sometimes 'abomination', sometimes 'pollution', and for the most part idolaters also learn foul customs, especially when the mysteries themselves lead to it.

See at Rom. 1. Verf. 11. EPHRAIM AS A BIRD, THEIR GLORY HAS FLOWN AWAY) These things are coherent, and it is a Hebrew idiom, for Ephraim's glory shall fly away like a bird. He understands glory here as fertility, of which they boasted. FROM THE BIRTH) That is, infants recently born from the mother shall die. AND FROM THE WOMB) Women shall miscarry. AND FROM CONCEPTION) Conceptions shall be unfruitful.

Latin:

ET FACTI SUNT ABOMINABILES, SICUT EA QUAE DILEXERUNT) Idola Hebraeis dicuntur שקוצים, & folet vox illa Hebraea verti ἄδωλον, modo δίλυγμα, modo μίασμα, & plerumque idololatrae etiam mores foedos addiscunt, praesertim cum eo ducant ipsa mysteria.
