Ea vero, quæ à versu secundo ad octavum sequuntur, ostenderunt, quam indignum se præbuerit gratuitæ Dei dilectio- ne, adeoque ex adverso testantur, quam constans fuerit Deus in sua misericordia, qui toties irritatus nondum populi illis curam deposuerit, & post tot remedia tentata, ab illis vero neglecta & rejecta, ultimum illud & maxime salutare de Christo doctore illis donando, statuerit tandem suo tempore præ- parare & applicare. Est ergo occupatio quædam, ut recte Rivetus, & concessio, qua dum benignitatis suæ testimonia, cum ingratissimis Israelitarum ma- leficiis confert, concedit quidem illos indignos es- se, quibuscum deinceps adeo clementer agat: vel- le se nihilominus plenitudinem gratiæ & veritatis exhibere in Christo, suo tempore manifestando. Similiter. B. Tarnovius: Hunc versum primum pu- to prolepticam esse propositionem omnium eorum, quæ deinceps exponuntur. Ea autem sunt duum generum præcipue, nempe quæ populo Israel ingrato præsti- ta beneficia & ab ipso admissa flagitia, & quæ per Christum ei obtingat gratia. Flagitia his verbis no- tat, quamvis Israel sit puer est excutiens sæpius jugum paternum, beneficia istis vocibus, tamen diligo eum, designat, & fundamentum hujus dilectionis ac con- niventiæ atque remissionis peccatorum subjicit hoc commate, ideo ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum unigenitum, in Judæam, ut ibi recte docendo, pie vivendo, ac dura morte pereundo, pro peccatis hu- mani generis sufficienter, & pro fideli Israele effi- caciter satisfaciat (Lutherano sensu illam distin- ctionem adhibeo, non Calviniano) & salutem pa- riat, ut ita ejus intercessione ergo Deus pater, cujus est filius, motus non omnia stricto jure cum homi- nibus agam, sed quos ob sua peccata poteram per- dere, ut Sodomam & Gomorrham, eos in Chri- stum credentes amem & filiorum loco habeam.

Nono idem Tarnovius ex occasione dicendi hanc explicationem ita firmat: Ultima fuerant ista (quæ propterea etiam in multis libris huic capiti adduntur, vide vulgatam versionem & Commen- tatores Pontificios, aliosque qui eam sequuntur) subito de improviso excisus est omnino Rex Israe- lis. Hinc jam statim oritur (1) hæc quæstio, cur ita severe Deus punit Israelem? Respondet uno verbo Propheta, quia Israel puer inobediens est. (2) Ergone cum Regem tollit Deus, plane suum po- pulum abjicit? non ita, regnum adimit, non dene- gat prorsus suum amorem, quia dicit, tamen diligo eum. (3) Nullumne igitur regem dabis? utique Christum filium meum, cujus regnum est æternum licet non de hoc mundo, ille est, in quo solo εὐδόκη- σα, & Israelem diligo, ne plane perdam. Hæc B. Tarnovius pag. 360.

Decimo accedit his autoritas Doctorum & In- terpp. qui etsi in modo explicandi non omnes con- veniant, in eo tamen consentiunt unanimes, secun- dum literam hic de Christo sermonem esse, non pauci etiam nostræ interpretationi, quantum ad summam rei, suffragantur. Eusebium laudavimus antea e lib. 9. Demonstr. p. m. 426. nec non Isido- rum Clarium in not. ad Matth. 2. cum quibus Ly- ranus & Dionysius itidem secundum literam, hunc locum de Christo intelligunt, ut & Andr. Osiandr. in Harmon. ac Francisc. Junium in Parallelis, eun- dem & Tremellium in notis, Piscatorem ad Matth. 2. Ioh. Tarnovium in Commentar. Andr. Rivetum in Comment. Johannem Coccejum in Comment. ad h. l. Fridericus Spanhemius dicit eam esse plero- rumque interpretum & magnos habere autores: à quibus se invitum dissentire profitetur, intercede- re tamen quædam, quo minus huic sententiæ sub- scribendum censeat. Illa vero tanti minime sunt, ut nos ab hac tam solide fundata sententia dimove- ant, ideoque operæ pretium erit dispicere.

Pri- mum est: quod כִּי illud non videatur αἰτιολογικὸν esse, sed σημαντικὸν tantum temporis, reddendum, quum vel quando Israel erat puer, hoc est, in te- nero statu dilexi eum, sed unde probabitur, quod hæc particula ita hic reddenda sit? Nullo argumen- to id docet, nude tantum, & dubitanter dicit Span- hemius VIDETUR, ac ne loca quidem ad- fert, in quibus particula כִּי sit designativa temporis. Quod autem αἰτιολογικὴ sit, indubium est ex usitata acceptione: Quod etiam adversativo sensu usurpetur, loca passim obvia docent; neque hic quicquam huic interpretationi obstat, sed apprime conveniunt omnia.

Alterum est, quod evidens ex inspectione textus sit, idem suppositum sensu literali vocari & נער & בן puerum & filium, nec id negari possit, quin vis aperta fiat verbis Prophetæ: Id vero nec Riveto nec aliis oculatissimis viris evidens fuit, neque quomodo vis verbis Prophetæ fiat, docuit Spanhemius. Petit er- go pro more, sibi solemni τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ. Dixerim po- tius evidens esse, non de eodem subjecto nomen utrumque hic efferri, & vim verbis Prophetæ fieri, si ad idem subjectum trahatur; certe & à proprieta- te vocis propheticæ receditur, & Apostolo palam contradicitur, si posterius comma de alio, quam Christo accipiatur. Et opponimus hic Spanhemio Coccejum: Filium Dei in emphasin & ἐν δυνάμει (h. e. in omni valore significandi, ut notet potentiam τοῦ ἰδίου, non vero infirmitatem υἱοῦ Θεοῦ) de Filio Dei unigenito accipimus, ut Psal. 2, 1. 12. Es. 9, 5. Ezech. 21, 15. Prov. 30, 4. Causa sic intelligendi est, quia di- citur in ἀντιδιαστολῇ Israelis. Et verba in proprieta- te debent explicari, nisi id evidens ratio impediat. Et illa expositio est conformis promissionibus, & prophe- tiis, & imprimis illi, quæ est Hos. 1, 7. Salvabo ipsos in Jehovah Deo ipsorum & cap. 2, 1. Vocabuntur filii Dei vivi. Habet etiam hæc expositio auctorem Spiritum S. Matth. 2, 15. & historia subsequentium ei adstipulatur. LXX. ἐξ Αἰγύπτου μετεκάλεσα τὰ τέκνα αὐτοῦ. Ergo legendum censuerunt לבניו quasi י in fine periisset. Nempe inconveniens putarunt de Israe- le per antonomasiam accipere, filium meum. Ob- servetur hic Matthæum versionem LXX. interpretum emendasse. Hæc Coccejus.

Tertium est, quod nimis abrupta & concisa ita foret Messiæ commemoratio, si solus Messias verbis illis postremis intelligendus dicatur, qualis vix alibi repe- rietur. Finit Propheta per comminationem caput ante- cedens, subjicit commemorationem beneficii in vulgus noti, & quod solenne apud Prophetas: & statim ver- su immediate sequenti redit ad exprobrandam po- pulo ingratitudinem, quæso qui cum antecedentibus & consequentibus his cohærere potest sola mentio evocationis Messiæ ex Ægypto? Omnia vero optime inter se connectentur, si sensum literalem de populo Israelitico, & beneficio illi exhibito simul admittamus. Ita Spanhemius. Sed quid novi in Scriptura Vet. Testamenti concisa Messiæ commemoratio? Abrup- tam autem nimis illam esse non concedimus. Nam & ratio redditur, cur ex Ægypto Israelis bono filium vocaverit, & dubium κατ' ἀνθυποφορὰν remove- tur à malitia Israelis. Coccejus plura adhuc cumu- lat in commentario suo. Recapitulat, inquit, Pro- pheta omnem gubernationem Israelis, & ostendit I. statum ejus primum in pueritia, h. e. statum pæda- gogiæ & servitutis elementorum mundi. Nam hæc est pueritia Israelis, Gal. 3, 24. 4, 1. 2. 3. Hic status est Israelis ab eductione ex Ægypto usque ad Regnum Dei sive Christi, sub fœdere primo. Jer. 31, 32. II. Missio- nem Filii DEI ad eum in eo statu, ut fieret minor etiam illis, qui vocantur dii, servus dominantium, servus circumcisionis sub lege Psal. 8, 6. Es. 49, 7. Es. 53, 11. Rom. 15, 8. Gal. 4, 4. III. Filii per fugam in Ægy- ptum subducti revocatione ad populum. Vide Matth. 2, 13. 14. 15. De hac fuga & consequente cæde puero- rum in Bethlehem, & reditu ex fuga loquitur & Je- rem. 31, 15. 16. Vox in Ramah audita est, ejulatus, ploratus amarissimi: Rachel (matres Bethlemiticæ) flet super filiis suis, renuit consolationem admittere su- per filiis suis occisis; quia ille non est, Ille δεικτικῶς, vel ex versu superiore illud, טוּב bonum meum. Major causa flendi, quod Christus, bonum Domini, non appareret, quam quod filii occisi essent. Alioqui si is apparuisset, pro solatio id futurum fuisset. Sic di- xit Jehovah: Arce vocem tuam à ploratu & oculos tuos à lacryma. Nam est merces in opere precium tuum, & revertetur filius meus, salus mea, cum ma- tre & Josepho, ex terra inimici: & est exspectatio in extremum tui, & revertentur filii ad terminum suum: etiam Israel per Evangelium revocabitur. Hæc fuga est specimen passionum Christi. Reductionis hujus causam facit Amorem suum. Amoris enim Dei est, quod filium suum dedit imo tradidit pro nobis victimam. Joh. 3, 16. Rursum hic monemus, & vocem amoris in emphasi accipi longe melius de donatione filii ad salutem, quam de quibus vis bene- ficiis, quæ Israeli ante id tempus præstita sunt, quæ ipsi non proserunt, quo minus in sua νηπιότητι relinque- retur, exsors υἱοθεσίας illius, quæ datur per Christum. IV. Vocationem Israelitarum factam per Christum, Mich. 6, 9. Jerem. 23, 6. 33, 16. Ps. 2, 7. & Aposto- los Psal. 8, 3. 68, 12. Confer Hos. 11, 4. Contendite cum matre vestra &c. V. Inobedientiam, & quidem cum contumacia: Sic abiverunt à facie illorum. Sic in apodosi ponitur, ut in protasi particula assi- mulationis sit subintelligenda, q. d. Quo magis & ardentius eos vocarunt, eo majori dedignatione abie- runt à facie ipsorum, vocantium, ne eos audirent. Si- milis ellipsis Es. 55, 9. Psal. 48, 6. Hæc ille, qui alia etiam ibi ad Novi Testamenti tempora pertinere vult, in quo etsi ei non suffragemur, sed ea, quæ de ingratitudine populi queritur Propheta, ad popu- lum istius temporis pertinere admittamus, nihil tamen obstat, quo minus beneficium huic populo exhibendum tempore Novi Testamenti hic exhi- beatur: quia idem est populus, quemadmodum etiam idem populus erat, qui ex Ægypto eductus fuit, & qui Hoseæ tempore & deinceps vixit, imo etiam ille, cujus fata post aliquot tempora designa- vit. Porro annon præstat, dicamus Prophetam sub- jicere commemorationem beneficii singularis, quam beneficii in vulgus noti, & ita redire ad ex- probrandam ingratitudinem populo! Nam quan- to eminentiusest beneficium, tanto gravius est in- gratitudinis vitium! Sed quis quæso mortalium (ait Spanhemius) ex Israelitis evocationem illam Mes- siæ ex Ægypto animo præcipere poterat, quem crede- bant omnes vocandum non ex Ægypto, sed ex Israele, vel potius ex Juda. Resp. Non mirum, quod non credidisse Israelitas, quæ de Messia prædicta, statuit Spanhemius, quum ore quidem Prophetis sensum prædictionum perspectum fuisse asserat. pag. 486. Cæterum omnino intelligere poterant evocatio- nem Christi ex Ægypto; nam verbis luculentis ea prædicta hic est; Evocavi (evocabo more Pro- phetis solemni) Filium meum ex Ægypto: quæ ita ut sonant, accepta alium sensum non pariunt, quam Christum ex Ægypto evocatum iri, cum qua præ- dictione nequaquam pugnat suscitatio Messiæ ex Juda. Aliud enim est ejus nativitas, vel suscitatio, quæ ex Juda facta, aliud ex Ægypto revocatio: quæ sibi opponenda non sunt.

Quarto ita disserit: Sic longe majori probabili- tatis specie ad solum Messiam referri possent verba postrema versus primi, si à Spiritu S. dictum fuisset, quia Israel puer est, dilexi eum, & ei dedi vel misi, vel destinavi filium meum, vel missurus ei sum ser- vatorem, vel tale quid. Verum resp. Eadem proba- bilitatis specie, imo eadem certitudine ad solum Messiam illa verba pertinent, cum dicitur, ideo evo- cavi filium meum ex Ægypto, imo hoc convenien- tius hic loci erat: quia beneficium proprium Ifraeli- tarum, uti supra dictum. Nec est, quod dicat prævi- deri evocationem ejus à Judæis non potuisse, non magis quam ejus causam, & alieniorem fidei ejus mentio- nem, quia non statim ab adventu ex Ægypto accinxit se Messias ad Israelis pueri gubernationem: Nam ut prævideretur aliunde, opus non erat: Siquidem ex hoc vaticinio cognosci potuerit, eoque interprete S. S. prædicta fuerit illa evocatio, etsi fuga, & fugæ causa non indicata. Nec aliena est ideo mentio re- vocationis Messiæ in terram Israelis, quod non sta- tim Israëlem gubernarit. Nam & id amori erga Israelem accepto ferendum, quod voluerit inter ipsos educari, neque dubium est, quod puerulus πληρούμενος σοφίας, cum quo erat χάρις Θεoῦ, Luc. 2, 40. fidelibus fuerit gaudio, & voluptati at- que exemplo insigni: qui duodecennalis ipsos etiam magnos doctores publice informavit.

Quod (5) Israel sæpe vocetur puer, filius Dei, primogenitus Dei Ef. 4, 22. Ier. 31, 9. nihil ad rem fa- cit: nam illa filii Dei & primogeniti appellatio est impropria & tralatitia. Et manifestum ibi est de Israele sermonem esse. Hic vero de eodem in alte- ro colo agi, nullo documento constat, imo non de Israele, sed Christo id loqui S. S. interprete novi- mus, cui absit, ut contradicamus. Neque fas est pro arbitrio relicto propriæ vocis בני significatu ad improprium descendere.

Quod (6) de insolubili nodo, qui Judæis obji- ciatur, de ortu Messiæ, qui non ex tribu Judæ vel Beth- lehem egressus sit, obvertitur, quia vocandus intelli- gitur ex Ægypto, id nauci est: Nam nulla est pugna inter ortum è Bethlehem, vel è tribu Juda, & vocatio- nem ex Ægypto, imo utrumque credi debebat, quia utrumque revelatum erat. Et cum ipse Spanhemius sensu mystico vocationem Christi hic exhiberi sta- tuat, utique si ille cognitus fuit Prophetæ, aliisque fidelibus, credere non minus vocationem ex Ægy- pto, quam ortum è Juda debuere. Et quis obsecro, hic nodus, non dicam insolubilis Judæis, sed alicujus solum perplexitatis? An non in proclivi erat cogi- tare, eum qui certo nasciturus è Bethlehem, quia vocandus aliquando erat ex Ægypto, in Ægyptum transiturum, ut inde vocetur nutu divino?

Atq; hæc sunt, quæ ἀνασκευαστικῶς adversus no- stram explicationem allata sunt à Spanhemio, quæ dissimulanda vel transmittenda non videbantur, si- quidem eximium etiam quendam Theologum in eam partem pertraxerint, ut quid illis roboris insit, constaret. Jam ut κατασκευαστικῶς suam de duplici hujus oraculi sensu sententiam adstruat, primora- tionem à verbis & nexu Prophetæ petit, quæ claris- sime doceant, eum depopulo Iudaico, & beneficio in illorum eductione ex Ægypto loqui. Concedimus lo- qui de populo Isralitico, & de beneficio divino: sed longe eminentiori, nimirum destinationis ad eundem Filii unigeniti. Alteram à Scopo V. Testam. & consuetudine S. Scripturarum desumit, quod a- pud illos Messiæ persona, tempora, officium, benefi- cia, actiones, passiones & id genus alia frequentis- simis typis expressa reperiantur: sed hæc procedit à non distributo ad distributum, vitiosa consequen- tia. Non enim si nonnunquam typi in Scripturis oc- currunt, consequens est hic etiam typum haberi; non minus frequens est penes Scriptores sacros V. T. illa expressis oraculis exhiberi; unde fortius argumentum stringet hoc modo: Quum omnia, quæ Christus egit & passus est, etiam minutiora, & beneficia ejus omnia in V. T. prædicta fuerint oraculis propheticis, mirum si hic tam insigne opus prædictum non fuerit? Et quum interprete Spiri- tu S. habeamus id etiam prædictum olim fuisse ab Hosea, nefas fuerit vaticinium illud, quo id prædi- xit S. S. hoc sensu exuere, eiq; alium sensum tribue- re, ac ad nudam typi rationem se recipere, imprimis eo loco, ubi nemo unquam typum cogitare potuit. Ecquis enim mortalium ex Israelitis, ut hic argu- mento & verbis Spanhemii utamur, evocationem illam Messiæ (typice adumbratam in eductionem ex Ægypto) animo præcipere poterat? Et quid o- pus erat verba illa Hoseæ allegasse, si nihil aliud in- dicari debuit, quam vocationem ex Ægypto per edu- Etionem populi figuratam? Ita profecto aliter loquu- tus fuisset Evangelista, & cum Christo potius si- gnum Jonæ proponente signum datum fuisse Israe- litis futuræ evocationis Christi in sui eductione ad- seruisset, vel certe aliunde constare oporteret, de illa figura.

Tertiam rationem in analogia & convenientia multiplici quærit Spanhemius, sed in illis 14. com- parationis membris ne unum invenire potuit, quod typi vel figuræ, qualis hic requirebatur, rationem doceret. Nam aliud longe est comparationis quæ- dam ac similitudinis membra intercedere, quæ in multis historiis interveniunt, si cum aliis factis componantur, aliud rem sub N. T. gestam typum ex intentione Spir. S. gessisse rei sub N. T. gerendæ : ita ut dum hæc evenit, dictum de illa agens adimpletum recte dici possit. Quod à Tarnovio jam didicisse po- terat Spanhemius, cum Riberæ aliqua membra comparationis investiganti in Commentario suo respondit: Licet sint quædam, in quibus comparatio quædam potuit institui, tamen quis inde probabit, ea fuisse adumbrata, & prædicta apud Prophetam, & propterea ita impleta. Filium Dei (1) tum populum Israelis, tum Christum dici certum, sed num in eo populus Israelis typus fuit υἱότητος Christi? Ecquis hoc dixerit? (2) Israel fugit in Ægyptum, idem con tigit circa Christum. Sed ubi profectio Israelis in Ægyptum typus profectionis Christi in Ægyptum constituitur? (3) Israel coactus fame fugit, Christus coactus gladio: Comparatio hic aliqua, sed num ilico figuram & typum dicemus? (4) Illic extraor- dinaria Dei se prudentia exercuit, similiter etiam hic; quis vero admittet in eo typum exhibitum conservandi Christi? (5) ut Israel, ita & Christus tutum receptum habuere in Ægypto, sed an tutus re- ceptus Israelis fuerit tuti receptus Christi typus, disquiritur. (6) ut per illam migrationem Israelis Deus Ægypto innotuit, sic etiam Josephi & Mariæ præconio nomen Christi in Ægypto innotuisse du- bitari non debet. Esto: Comparatio hæc aliqua e- rit, non actutum typus. (7) Servitus Israelis in Æ- gypto typus fuit servitutis populi Dei, quam sæpe subire cogitur in hoc mundo: Sic & fuga Christi instar quoddam est nostri exilii. At ea ratione non servitus Israelis in Ægypto, Christi in Ægypto a- gentis, qui ibi serviisse non legitur, typus constitui- tur, sed utriusque, Israelis nempe, & Christi mora in Ægypto alterius nempe populi Dei & Ecclesiæ fi- gura fuerit. (8) Ut Israel in Ægypto nutritium & propinquum habuit ex sua gente, sic etiam Christus Josephum & Mariam. At hic dissimilitudo verius quam similitudo. Illius enim causa Christus in Æ- gyptum fugere necessum non habuit, ut illic nutri- tium & propinquum inveniret, quemadmodum eo nomine Israelitæ descenderunt. Mirum, quod non etiam typum in Josepho constituit Spanhemius, qui adeo felix in typis inveniendis fuit. Nam age- bat Israel cum Josepho in Ægypto: habebat etiam Christus ibi suum Josephum. (9) ut Israel speciali Dei ductu ex Ægypto evocatus, sic etiam Christus. (10) Ut Israel substitit illic donec educeretur à Deo, fic etiam Christus. In eo vero imprimis typi ratio- nem monstrare debuit, quod nempe eductio illa populi ex Ægypto figuravit evocationem Messiæ. Quod hactenus nemini Judæorum in mentem ve- nit, etsi illi, fatente Spanhemio sub dictorum & ge- storum externorum cortice sæpissime Messiam desi- gnari contendant. Quid? quod Christus ipse edu- xerit Israëlitas, & autor eductionis eorum fuerit, nec in Israëlitis, sed in Mose quærenda figura sit in liberatore populi, si de figura res sit. (11) ut Israël eductus per angelum alloquentem Mosem, sic etiam Christus angeli monitu. Hic iterum dissimilitudo elucescit seu contrarium. Nam Angelus Mosen educens, non typus angeli creati fuit, sed ipse Fi- lius Dei. (12) ut populus post egressum ex Ægypto in- troductus in terram sanctam, quam ante incoluerat, Sic & Christus. Mera hic comparatio. (13) Ut Israël sic & Christus eductus, Rege infanticida sublato. Ille Pharaone, hic Herode sublato. Hic iterum mera & fatis coacta comparatio. (14) ut illic amor Dei er- ga Israëlem, ita hic erga Christum comprobatus fuit. Ecquis vero dicet, Israelem Deo dilectum typum fuisse Christi, Deo dilecti, amorem Dei adversus Israëlem, typum amoris Dei adversus Christum? Id vero est κρινόμενον, pro quo probando in tanta prolixitate ne γρὺ vel μὺ quidem deprehendo apud Spanhemium.

Sed recipit is se porro (4) ad loca, quæ vocat, parallela de gemino complemento, de osse non commi- nuendo agni paschalis Joh. 19, 36. & in illo oraculo 2. Sam. 7, 14. Ebr. 1, 5. item illis, quæ de Isaaco, Ismaë- le, Sara, Agar typice dicta, mystice ad N. Testamenti mysteria referuntur. Ea vero loca nil minus sunt, quam parallela nostro oraculo, nec geminum sen- sum ejusdem sententiæ probant, quem probare de- bebant. Nam agnum paschalem typum Christi fuis- se aliunde constabat, unde etiam illa περίστασις de non comminuendo osse ei de facili applicari poterat: Et Israëliticum populum typum Christi fuisse, un- de, obsecro, constat? Et quis Judæorum Israëlitas typum Messiæ constituit? Oraculum 2. Sam. 7. per- verse omnino abripitur ad Salomonem, quantum ad sensum literalem: quum ne ulli quidem angelorum talia dicta sint, teste Apostolo Ebr. 1, 5. de uno Chri- sto loquitur: ut istic adversus Grotium ostendi- mus. Isaacus typus Christi à Spiritu Sancto in ma- ctatione constituitur Ebr. 11. Sed num ideo totus populus Israëliticus typus est Christi? Quæ ab Isaa- co & Israële, Sara & Agar sumuntur figuræ, in Scri- pturis fundamentum habent, nec tamen geminum ejusdem sententiæ docent sensum. Hic vero fun- damentum typi desideramus, & de gemino ejus- dem oraculi sensu disquirimus.

Ad sagittas itaque Jonathanis earumque jactum 1. Sam. 20, provocat Spanheimus, ut ostendat aliqua ratione, diversa iisdem sive verbis sive rebus designa- ri posse. Sed hæc toto cœlo diversa sunt: unius ver- bi & dicti geminum esse sensum ex intentione Spiritus Sancti & rem unam alterius esse figuram & signum. Ibi de significatione verborum res est, hic de rei à- licujus designatione vel adumbratione. Symbolo quodam aliud atq; aliud designari novum non est, maxime si ex conventione assumantur Symbola, eo- rumque declaratio fiat. Sed iisdem verbis in eodem oraculo tam disparatos subesse sensus, hoc vero ἀποτόμως negamus. Dum vero Spanhemius occu- rit, nec novum esse, nec absurdum, vocem eandem su- mi & collective & individualiter, exemplo primæ promissionis, in eo perquam absurde principium pe- tit, nam contritio capitis serpentini non nisi semini mulieris μοναδικῶς intellecto h. e. Messiæ tribuitur: per semen autem mulieris illud simul etiam Eccle- fiam ibi notari, novum est, & æque absonum, ac cum Mariam etiam illo notari ajunt Papistæ. Nam mortalium genus per hoc semen mulieris, per con- tritionem serpentis liberandum est, non vero ipsum illud semen mulieris esse potest. Porro, ni- hil obstare dicit, idem verbum aliter sumi historice, aliter prophetice, aliter de actu præterito, aliter de fu- turo. Sed omnino obstat, idem verbum eodem loco tam disparatas obtinere significationes, nec ullo id exemplo è Scripturis docebitur. Id autem perquam absonum iterum est, quod huc trahitur de Spiritu Sancto, cui futura etiam præsentia sunt, nam sim- pliciter etiam præterita eidem præsentia sunt, Num ergo Spiritum S. cum de futuro loquitur, si- mul etiam de præsenti, ac de præterito loqui, inde colligendum? Ἄτοπον ἀτοπώτατον! unde nihil nisi mera incertitudo, & confusio in Scripturis orietur. Dicit, plures quidem sensus ejusdem generis, nempe literales, eidem loco convenire, absurdum esse, non item, si de diversi generis sensibus res sit, v. g. literali & mystico (quod ἀναντιῤῥήτως se probaturum confidit tum ratione, tum exemplis, sed nos utrumq; pro ab- surdo habemus, & rationes ab ipso adductæ adver- sus utrumque militant, h. e. tam docent, non posse diversos sensus esse ejusdem oraculi diversi gene- ris, quam ejusdem generis, utpote quod Scripturæ sententia aliqua unam tantum formam habeat: Er- go & unum tantum sensum; item quod non enuncia- tio sed enunciationes dentur, ubi non unum, sed plura enunciantur, quum unum & verum inter se conver- tantur: item quod sic Scriptura reddatur ἀμφιδέ- ξιος, ἀμφίλοξος, æquivoca, obscura, incerta; Qua- rum vim nequicquám elidere satagit, quasi maneat unitas formæ Scripturæ, etsi duplex sensus literalis & mysticus statuatur in eodem dicto, eo, quod sensus mysticus non tam verbis significetur quam rebus, quodque harmonia detur & σχέσις sensus literalis ad mysticum, typi ad antitypum, & ex utroque demum sensus integer & completus exurgat. Unde oracula illa composita vocant: quodque duplex enunciatio in talibus reperiatur implicite, etsi una tantum sit explicite, nec Scriptura S. ideo ambigua & incerta sit cum à Spir. S. indicatur ille sensus. Nam quomodo unitas formæ manet, si tam disparatæ significatio- nes, imo contrariæ sæpe uni verbo tribuuntur in eodem loco, significatio præteriti & futuri, signifi- catio propria & metaphorica, significatio indivi- dui, & totius multitudinis &c. Quod non tam ver- bis significatur quam rebus, id nemo sensum verbo- rum dixerit. Nam sensus est demum, quem ver- ba reddunt, & significant. Aliud est ergo, quærere verborum significationem, aliud vero quod res aliqua per verba significata adumbravit. Ita in serpente æneo erecto verba in historia Mosis unam tantum habent significationem, sed historia illa erecti ser- pentis ænei historice à Mose tradita Deus aliquid aliud intendebat significare, & adumbrare. Non ergo confundere debebat Spanhemius verba, & res ipsas. Neque vero harmonia illa in verbis aut enunciationibus deprehenditur in ordine ad di- versa, disparata, & contraria significata, sed in rebus per verba indicatis. Si vero per verba eadem ex intentione autoris principalis Spiritus Sancti, & significata eductio Israëlitarum ex Ægypto, & simul indicata revocatio Christi ex Ægypto, quomodo manebit unitas formæ Scripturæ, quomodo unitas enunciationis, quomodo non erit oratio S. S. am- bigua ex ipsa intentione Spiritus Sancti atque obscura, de qua ipse Spanhemius ambigit, utrum etiam Propheta ipse illum sensum perceperit? certo id asseri & probari non posse, agnoscit pag. 513. Qui autem magis ambigua est oratio dicentis, quam quæ ex parte primarii loquentis geminum sensum, alterum apertum, alterum involutum & ob- scurum habet, quem nec ipse proferens vel referens minister intelligit, in illum unice mentem refle- ctens. Unde necessum habet Spanhemius oracula COMPOSITA comminisci, vel à Pareo suo pete- re, ex una enunciatione geminam fingere, ex uno sub- jecto geminum, ita ut aliud diversum plane supponat, ac prædicatum etiam diversimode interpretetur, et- si non sit, nisi unicum in textu sacro: quod non est explicare Scripturam, sed pervertere: perinde uti solent Sacramentarii in una voce edite sensum, & proprium & metaphoricum fingere, ne unum tan- tum sit manducationis objectum, nec una mandu- catio, sed gemina eadem voce in S. Eucharistia præ- cepta. Quam nos omnes, quotquot τῷ ῥητῷ inhæ- remus, pro insigni depravatione verborum Testa- menti illius habemus.

Quamnam vero rationem, quænam exempla pro- fert hujus æquivocationis, quæ adeo ἀναντίῥῥητα sunt? Negari nequit (ita habet αὐτολεξεὶ) illum esse sensum Scripturæ, quem Spiritus S. ejus author pro- ponit, quem Scriptores θεόπνευσοι, & eo ipso αὐτόπι- σοι declarant. Atqui præter sensum literalem mysti- cus à Spiritu S. & amanuēsibus ejus frequentissime proponitur in N. Testam. Hoc argumentum ejus est: in quo majori concessà minor probanda est. Quam vero, non ut receperat tum ratione tum ex- emplis, sed solum exemplis probat, de non comminu- endis ossibus agni paschalis, & è verbis: Ero ei in pa- trem, & Uxoribus Abrahæ, ad quæ vero jam respon- sum est. Addit typos Melchisedeci, anei serpentis, Jonæ &c. sed peccat ignoratione Elenchi. Non enim probandum typos dari in V. T. sed præter sen- sum literalem uni eidemque oraculo etiam subesse sensum mysticum, ἰδέ ῤόδον, ἰδὲ πόδομα, in quo ve- ro probando plane defecit Spanhemius, adeoque magno conatu vere nihil egit. Cætera, in quibus adhuc verbosus est, distinctiunculis, & pro more suo, luxuriat Spanhemius, non merentur hanc ope- ram, ut retexantur, & ex his dijudicari affatim pos- sunt. Quæ vero hic ἀλλότρια videri non debent, siquidem & Grotius ipse eandem sententiam de du- plici sensu Scripturæ hic & in aliis plurimis Scriptu- ræ locis iisdem telis cum Spanhemio pugnet.

Atque hæc de isto oraculo: quod Spiritus San- ctus ipse in Novo Testamento de Christo inter- pretatus est, unde sensus ille nobis sancte custodien- dis. Quæ etiam causa fuit, cur non versionem LXX. Interpp. quod alias plerumque consuevit, addu- xerit, quod nempe illa perperam in plurali reddi- derit, sensumque genuinum assecuta non sit κατε- κάλεσά μιν τὰ τέκνα αὐτῦ, sed juxta Ebraicam ve- ritatem, quam etiam Aquila expressit, ἐκάλησα τὸν υἰόν με, ut constaret de Filio Dei Prophetam lo- quutum esse. De quo D. Lutherus in h. l. Hoc ma- gis observandum est, cum fere semper Apostoli trans- lationem Septuaginta sequantur, quod Matthæus hoc in loco Ebræorum Biblia sequi voluit. Nam Septua- ginta non singularem sed pluralem numerum habent: Ex Ægypto vocavi filios ejus. Hunc errorem cor- rigit Evangelista & pro autoritate sua ostendere hoc testimonio vult, hunc Jesum ex Maria natum, & ex Ægypto per angelum vocatum, esse verum DEI æterni filium, ab æterno genitum. Ideo verius in eum competere hoc testimonium Prophetæ, quam in veterem populum, qui non natura, sed adoptione erat filius. Hæc simplex & genuina sententia est. Hæc B. Lutherus. Nec omnino ignotus fuit Judæis hic sen- sus, etsi suis involucris, uti solent, obtexerint. Nam verba illa Psal. 80, 9. Vitem de Ægypto transferes de Messia interpretantur in libro Bereschith in sect.

Harvel. Makom. At de eodem verba illa Psalmi agere, de quo hic Hoseas cap. 11, 1. agit, profitentur in Schemoth Rabba sect. 43. unde colligere licet, etiam verba Hoseæ ipsos de Messia accepisse. Con- fer. Pugio fidei Raimund. Martini p. 125. 432.

## 11:2
Verse 2.

THEY CALLED THEM) Namely Moses and the other Prophets to piety. SO) That is, all the more. THEY WENT AWAY FROM THEIR FACE) They turned their backs to the Prophets, Jer. 2:27. THEY SACRIFICED TO BAALIM) As to Beelphegor, Num. 25:3. AND SACRIFICED TO IDOLS) They burned incense. To idols, that is, before idols, as to the calf, Ex. 32:4.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

VOCAVERUNT EOS) Nempe Moses & Prophe- tæ alii ad pietatem. SIC) Id est, tanto magis. ABIERUNT A FACIE EORUM) Terga obver- terunt Prophetis Jer. 2, 27. BAALIM IMMOLABANT) Ut Beelphegori, Num. 25, 3. ET SIMULACRIS SACRIFICABANT) Adolebant. Simulacris, id est, coram simulacris, ut vitulo, Ex. 32, 4.

## 11:3
Verse 3.

AND I AS A NURTURER OF EPHRAIM) In the Hebrew: I made Ephraim walk: that is, just as children are taught to walk, so I formed them from the beginning, and led them. I CARRIED THEM IN MY ARMS) In the Hebrew: He carried them upon His arms: namely, Moses was as it were their bearer; what is here attributed to Moses, that is elsewhere attributed to God, as Deut. 1:31, 32:11. AND THEY KNEW NOT THAT I CARED FOR THEM) They did not sufficiently understand that this was done by me so studiously for this reason, that I might lead them away from idols. I WILL DRAW THEM WITH CORDS OF ADAM, WITH BANDS OF LOVE) All the Greeks here take 'baadam' not as a proper name, but as a common one. The cords of a man, or human ones, are benefits, by which men are most accustomed to be drawn. I WILL BE TO THEM) I was to them. AS ONE EXALTING THE YOKE OVER THEIR JAWS) As one who removes the yoke from the neck over the jaws. 'Darem' is not rarely translated as to lift up, to take away, to exalt, to remove. This is a new comparison taken from a farmer, by which he designates the liberation from Egypt. AND I INCLINED TO HIM THAT HE MIGHT EAT) I brought food to them: namely manna and birds. 'Darem' among other things signifies to bring upon, to set before, and is so translated. The commemoration of benefits shows the gravity of the guilt.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET EGO QUASI NUTRITIUS EPHRAIM) In Hæbræo: Ire feci Ephraimtum: id est, sicut pueri docentur ire, sic ego illos ab initio formavi, duxique. PORTABAM EOS IN BRACHIIS MEIS) In Hebræo: Portavit eos super brachiis suis:: nempe Moses fuit illorum quasi gerulus; quod hic Mosi tribuitur, id alibi Deo, ut Deut. 1, 31. 32, 11. ET NESCIERUNT QUOD CURAREM EOS) Non satis intellexerunt hoc ideo tam studiose a me fieri, ut eos ab idolis abducerem. IN FUNICULIS ADAM TRAHAM EOS, IN VINCULIS CARITATIS) Græci omnes באדם hic non ut nomen proprium, sed ut commune accipiunt. Funes ho- minis, sive humani, sunt beneficia, quibus maxime solent attrahi homines. ERO EIS) Fui eis. QUASI EXALTANS JUGUM SUPER MA- XILLAS EORUM) Ut qui jugum a collo trans maxillas amovet. דרים non raro vertitur pro αἴρειν, ἀπαίρειν, ἐξαί- ρειν, ἀφαιρεῖν. Hæc nova est comparatio ab agricola sumta, qua liberationem ab Ægypto designat. ET DECLINAVI AD EUM UT VESCERE- TUR) Admovi eis vescenda: manna scilicet & aves. דרים inter alia significat ἐπάγειν, παραβάλλειν, & sic vertitur. Beneficiorum commemoratio culpæ gravitatem ostendit.

## 11:5
Verse 5.

HE SHALL NOT RETURN INTO THE LAND OF EGYPT) He shall no longer run back to Egypt for the sake of help, as he did heretofore. The same manner of speaking on the same matter above 8, 13. See also 7, 11. 2 Kings 7, 4. AND ASSUR HIMSELF SHALL BE HIS KING) But the Assyrian shall be his king. He shall live under the dominion of the Assyrians. BECAUSE THEY REFUSED TO RETURN) For so long a time, that is to say.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

NON REVERTETUR IN TERRAM ÆGYPTI) Iam non ultra recurret ad Ægyptum opis causa, ut antehac fecit. Idem loquendi genus in eadem re supra 8, 13. Vide & 7, 11. 2. Reg. 7, 4. ET ASSUR IPSE REX EJUS) Sed Assyrius erit rex ejus. Vivet in Assyriorum ditione. QUONIAM NOLUERUNT CONVERTI) Tan- to scilicet tempore.

## 11:6
Verse 6.

THE SWORD HAS BEGUN IN HIS CITIES) When the sword remained in their cities: when he is still engaged in civil wars. AND SHALL CONSUME HIS CHOSEN ONES) And shall consume his strong ones. Thus the Chaldean. In Chaldean, בדי is a bar. By that name, those who sustain the Republic with arms are rightly designated. The Greeks read בירי. AND SHALL EAT THEIR HEADS) And shall eat those who are of their councils, the chief of the nobles. Thus the Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

CŒPIT GLADIUS IN CIVITATIBUS EJUS) Cum maneret gladius in urbibus eorum: cum adhuc in bellis civilibus versatur. ET CONSUMET ELECTOS EJUS) Et consu- meret fortes ejus. Sic Chaldæus. בדי Chaldaice est vectis. Eo nomine recte veniunt, qui armis Remp. sustentant. Græci legerunt בירי. ET COMEDET CAPITA EORUM) Et comede- ret eos, qui sunt a consiliis eorum, procerum præcipuos. Sic Chaldæus.

## 11:7
Verse 7.

AND MY PEOPLE HUNG TOWARD MY RETURN) Yet the people hesitated concerning my conversion. That is, they could not resolve within themselves that they must return to me. BUT A YOKE SHALL BE IMPOSED UPON THEM TOGETHER) He took על for a yoke, as the Chaldean also seems to have taken it. But the sense seems best: toward the high one (that is, God) they urged him (Israel, of whom the discourse is) together (all the prophets). WHICH SHALL NOT BE TAKEN AWAY) No one lifted up his head, so as to listen with pricked-up ears.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET POPULUS MEUS PENDEBAT AD RE- DITUM MEUM) Tamen populus hæsitabat circa conversio- nem meam. Id est, non poterat penes se constituere ad me esse redeundum. JUGUM AUTEM IMPONETUR EIS SIMUL) Sumfit על pro jugo, ut & Chaldæus sumfisse videtur. Sed sensus videtur optimus: ad excelsum (id est, Deum) fovabant eum (Israëlem de quo sermo) simul (Prophetæ omnes). QUOD NON AUFERETUR) Non extulit quis- quam caput suum, ut arrectis auribus auscultaret.

## 11:8
Verse 8.

HOW SHALL I GIVE THEE UP, EPHRAIM?) How shall I treat thee for these merits? I WILL DELIVER THEE, ISRAEL) I will hand thee over, namely to destruction. Symmachus here [translates] ἐκδώσωσε, for מגן, which the Greeks translate variously here, is to deliver, as Gen. 14, 19, where the Greeks [used] παρέδωκε, Prov. 4, 8. AS ADMAH I WILL MAKE THEE, AS ZEBOIM) As Zeboim: which cities were utterly destroyed with Sodom: but he preferred to name these, from which no one survived. God shows what he could determine concerning them for the merits of the Israelites. MY HEART IS TURNED WITHIN ME) I do not wish to fulfill those threats.

MY REPENTANCE IS EQUALLY DISTURBED) In the Hebrew: My repentances are moved together. That is, the bowels are moved to repentance. An anthropopathy sufficiently frequent.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

QUOMODO DABO TE EPHRAIM?) Quo- modo te tractabo pro istis meritis? PROTEGAM TE ISRAEL) Tradem te, nempe exitio. Symmachus hic ἐκδώσωσε, nam מגן, quod varie hic vertunt Græci, est tradere, ut Gen. 14, 19. ubi Græci παρέδωκε Prov. 4, 8. SICUT ADAMA PONAM TE, UT SEBOIM) Sicut Seboim: quæ urbes cum Sodomis funditus excisæ: sed maluit has nominare, ex quibus nemo superstes fuit. Osten- dit Deus, quid pro meritis Israëlitarum statuere de eis possit. CONVERSUM EST IN ME COR MEUM) Nolo illas minas implere.

PARITER CONTURBATA EST POENITUDO MEA) In Hebræo: Simul commotæ sunt pœnitentiæ meæ. Id est, viscera commota sunt ad pœnitentiam. Ἀνθρωποπάθεια satis frequens.

## 11:9
I WILL NOT EXECUTE THE FURY OF MY WRATH) I will not act by the highest law.

I WILL NOT RETURN TO DESTROY E- PHRAIM) I will not be brought to the point of destroying Ephraim by slaughter. The Greeks: 8̓ μὴ ἐγκαταλίπω τε̄ ἐξαλειφθη̄ναι τὸν Ἐφραίμ.

FOR I AM GOD AND NOT MAN) That is, much more merciful than men. Exod. 34, 6.

IN THE MIDST OF THEE IS THE HOLY ONE) That is, the sanctified one. I have been honored with fitting worship by your ancestors.

AND I WILL NOT ENTER THE CITY) Therefore I will not suffer that any city of yours be taken by force, but I will cause a surrender to be made, and thus men shall be saved in life.

Latin:

Vers. 9. NON FACIAM FUROREM IRÆ MEÆ) Non agam summo jure.

NON CONVERTAR UT DISPERDAM E- PHRAIM) Non eo adducar, ut Ephraimum internecione de- leam. Græci: 8̓ μὴ ἐγκαταλίπω τε̄ ἐξαλειφθη̄ναι τὸν Ἐφραίμ.

QUONIAM DEUS EGO ET NON HOMO) Id est, multo hominibus clementior. Exod. 34, 6.

IN MEDIO TUI SANCTUS) Id est, sanctificatus. Cultu conveniente honoratus à majoribus vestris fui.

ET NON INGREDiAR CIVITATEM) Pro- pterea non patiar ut urbs ulla vestrarum vi capiatur, sed efficiam ut deditio fiat, ac sic homines serventur in vita.

## 11:10
Verse 10.

THEY SHALL WALK AFTER THE LORD AS A LION HE SHALL ROAR) They shall walk, that is, when I have shown my wrath, namely through deportation, even then they may obey me.

FOR HE SHALL ROAR) When he shall roar. He repeats what he had said.

AND THE CHILDREN OF THE SEA SHALL FEAR) That is, let them fear me, who upon the arrival of Shalmaneser betook themselves to the shore of the Red Sea. Compare Is. 11, 11 and what is said there.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

POST DOMINUM AMBULABUNT QUASI LEO RUGIET) Ambulabunt, id est, ubi iram meam osten- dero, nempe per deportationem, vel tunc mihi pareant.

QUIA RUGIET IPSE) Cum rugiet ipse. Repetit quod dixerat.

ET FORMIDABUNT FILII MARIS) Id est, timeant me, qui se adventante Salmanaffere ad oram ma- ris Rubri receperint. Confer Ef. 11, 11. & ibi dicta.

## 11:11
AND THEY SHALL FLY AWAY AS A BIRD OUT OF EGYPT) Let them be afraid like an Egyptian bird, that is, a stork. He says this on account of those Israelites who, at the arrival of Shalmaneser, betook themselves into Egypt. Above 9, 3.

AND AS A DOVE OUT OF THE LAND OF THE ASSYRIANS) As an Assyrian dove. Assyria is full of doves. He says this on account of those who were led away into the regions of the Assyrians.

AND I WILL SETTLE THEM IN THEIR HOUSES) He persists in the simile: for both the stork returns to its nest, and the dove to the dovecote. This was fulfilled in not many of the Israelites, who, having turned to God, returned with the tribe of Judah: and it would have been fulfilled in more, if more had returned to a good mind. As is said elsewhere. See above I, 11.

Grotius again perverts a notable Evangelical promise. For this is not to be understood, with the more recent Rabbis, as concerning the reduction of the Israelites, but, with the better part of interpreters, as concerning the conversion to the Lord and spiritual restoration through the Messiah, whom God was about to recall from Egypt, so that He might gather the dispersed sheep of Israel. Which is taught by 1. the subject: For it does not speak of the Jews, who were restored after an exile of some years; but of Ephraim, or the Israelites of the ten tribes, who were never restored. And therefore it does not appear how it can be taken literally concerning their restitution. For what some say, that the power of returning was also promiscuously granted to them by Cyrus, and that the Israelites living there were spared when the Egyptians were defeated by Cambyses, are only conjectures, and do not respond to or satisfy this illustrious prophecy. Grotius himself admits that not many of the Israelites, converted to God, returned then with the tribe of Judah, in whom he thinks it was fulfilled. But he sees that the Prophetic oracle is not exhausted by such a small number. Rivetus rightly says: Its fulfillment cannot be referred to some small number of Israelites who perhaps were mixed with the Jews, whose band was so small that they were held for nothing, when in the census of the people made by the leaders, Ezra and Nehemiah, no mention is made of them, which certainly would not have been omitted if the completion of such a great prophecy had been situated in that very thing. Grotius saw this well, therefore he feigns that it would have been fulfilled in more, if more had returned to a good mind. But in truth, this is not a hypothetical promise, but a simple one, and not only a promise, but also a prediction, in which the Holy Spirit could certainly not be mistaken. B. Gesnerus does not refer these things to the Israelites, but to the nations. It is to be noted, who are to be called? Two kinds of men are named: One are the Jews, and the remnants of the Israelite kingdom, as those of whom it has been spoken so far. The others are the sons of the sea, that is, those dwelling then in the islands of the Mediterranean Sea, and beyond it in Europe, Greece, Spain, Germany, etc. But mention is made here specifically of the Egyptians and Assyrians, because those two kingdoms were always more devoted to superstition and idolatry than all other nations. But if these peoples were admitted into the kingdom of Christ, when they did penance, then there will be no cause for despair for the others. (2) The predicate: They shall fly, as birds from Egypt, and as a dove from the land of the Assyrians. Noted is not only the return to the nest and the dovecote, but also the highest alacrity and promptness, because they are to depart from there in haste, just as those birds tend with most swift flight from one place to another, Psalm 55:7, Eph. 60:8. And thus is expressed the energy of the Holy Spirit, whose grace, as the Church sings, knows no slow efforts. For He instills that mind into the faithful, so that they may flee the pollutions of the Gentiles, and strive toward holiness with great alacrity.

3. The term from which is indeed expressed Egypt and the land of the Assyrians, because clearly the greatest part of the Israelites was dispersed there, but since the prediction concerns the Israelites generally, their return is understood not only from those places, but from all the corners of the world, wherever they had betaken themselves; it was certainly not fulfilled in their temporal reduction; but it pertains to the remnants of Israel according to election, to be gathered and converted in their own time from all parts of the world: THE SONS OF THE SEA SHALL FEAR, with fear and trembling they shall hasten from the ends of the earth. For the sea was the western boundary of the holy land, and that land is washed on all sides by the sea.

4. The term to which. I will settle them in their houses. This promise was not fulfilled in the 10 tribes as far as their material houses or fields are concerned. And therefore it must necessarily be understood spiritually concerning the conversion to the Church. For it is, as we have said, not a hypothetical promise, as Grotius feigns, but simple and absolute. If therefore it must be taken historically, the Israelites never even in part occupied their houses, nor were their cities restored to the ten tribes, proper to them and once assigned by divine inheritance, or fields previously occupied by the peoples sent there by the Assyrians, and therefore they could not return to their nest and to their own dovecote like storks and doves. Therefore, Rivetus not undeservedly observes that those who among Christians refer these things to a real restitution of the Israelites in their own land, which never happened, weary themselves in vain.

5. Collation v. 9. AND I WILL NOT ENTER INTO THE CITY. Grotius rashly takes these words in a good sense: Therefore I will not suffer any city of yours to be taken by force, but I will bring it about that a surrender is made, and thus men may be saved in life. The words report nothing of the sort. Which our blessed Pappus rightly explains from the context: The other part of the Chapter proposes to us a most sweet dialogue of Divine Justice and Mercy consulting about the people of Israel, and indeed the Justice of God pronounces them unworthy of His protection, having surely deserved the same punishments as Admah and Zeboim, which perished together with Sodom and Gomorrah by fire sent down from heaven. But the Mercy of God brings forward two reasons why this just wrath should be mitigated. For God is moved to mercy, and to mitigating punishments, partly out of respect for our weakness, which can in no way endure the severity of divine justice; but partly out of His own clement Will, by which He does not wish the whole human race to have been created in vain; but He wishes to gather to Himself from it a Church, into which He may pour out the riches of His Grace, and to which He may communicate His goods for all eternity. Thus each of these causes testifies that we are received freely by

[To the] Son of God, without our merits. Moreover, he adds, 'and I will not enter into the city': by which clause he distinguishes the promises made to the Israelite kingdom from those which were made to the Judean kingdom. For the former has only spiritual promises; the latter, in addition, also has bodily ones concerning the return to the fatherland and the restoration of the external polity. That this is the meaning of this passage, the following also confirms. B. Gesner says: 'For the preservation of the earthly city of Samaria, which the Lord denied to those repenting, he now promises the building of the city of God and of the Church of the New Testament, which is accomplished by the calling of the Jews and Gentiles through the trumpet of the Gospel.' Rightly, therefore, B. Luther, f. 537. It seems to me most simple and most consistent with the Prophet's meaning that you should understand God as wishing to have mercy on the kingdom of Israel, scattered among the nations, in such a way, however, that the Israelites do not return to the Mosaic polity and Church, which remained in the kingdom of Judah until the time of the Gospel. B. Meisner noted a similar gloss of Grotius, concerning which and his judgment we submit: 'For some think that God here looks to the custom of mild victors, who, when a surrender of some city has been made, since they wish to spare the conquered and not commit the property of the citizens to military plunder, do not enter the city with an army.' Thus also it is hinted that God wishes to spare the Israelites, so that they are not utterly destroyed. This exegesis could be admitted regarding the spiritual grace, which God did not entirely withdraw; but it can by no means be approved regarding temporal grace, because the cities of the Israelites were entirely plundered by enemies. And because the text speaks of cities properly so called, it certainly cannot be understood as referring to the temporal preservation of cities, since the outcome has taught otherwise. Hence also falls that exposition of Drusius, by which he rendered it thus: 'I will not come against the city,' namely in a hostile manner: 'I will no longer besiege your cities in a hostile way.'

(6.) The force of the phrase: 'they shall walk after the Lord,' confirms our opinion: for this implies conversion: since it is indicated that they will no longer walk after the Baalim, but after the Lord their King, the Messiah, just as it was predicted in chapter III. 5 that they would walk. Before, they had departed from God, ch. VII. 3, and had said, 'I will go after my lovers,' ch. II. But now they will walk after Jehovah with true faith, and with the obedience of faith they will follow that Lord of theirs, called out of Egypt, ch. 11, 1, as their Leader and Guide. Isa. 52, 12. Zech. 3, 5. Mic. 2, 12. Beautifully on this phrase, Luther, f. 538: 'This at last will be the fruit that will follow the word of the Gospel and sanctification. Because, whereas hitherto they have walked according to the desires of their hearts, whereas they have established their own sacred rites, ceremonies, and other things to be righteousness before God, they will cast all these away at once, and will rely only on the righteousness and merits of the Son of God, whom they will hear in the Gospel delivered for their sins.' For this sentence has a remarkable exclusion of all works and cults which are not the Lord. How great is the variety of cults and works in the papacy? And yet, not a monk dared to call his vow, not a priest his Mass, not a hypocrite his fasts, not the rich their alms, 'the Lord.' Therefore, what he says, 'they shall walk after the Lord,' is the same as if he said: 'They will cast away all trust in human works and will rely and trust only in the grace and goodness of God.' For he who believes the Son of God was made a victim for his sins, he will rely on no work of his own. He sees that our works cannot be equal to the death of the Son of God. Therefore, by that one [merit] he will raise himself up; by that one he will establish that God is reconciled to him, and that the remission of sins and eternal life have been obtained. This truly is to walk after the Lord. And there follows this faith a zeal for obedience towards

the Law. For, liberated from sins, they desire to retain this innocence. Although, therefore, they slip through infirmity, yet they raise themselves up again by this trust, and afterwards they will walk more cautiously.

(7.) The means of conversion is also to be noted. The roaring of God, compared to the roaring of a lion inviting others to prey, by which the preaching of the divine word is designated. For this is called the roaring of a lion, Joel 3, v. 17, Amos 1, 2, ch. 3, 8, cf. Heb. 12, 25. And as a lion calls the animals of its own kind, and especially its cubs, to the prey, see Plutarch, 'On the Nature of Animals,' so the Messiah, with the clear voice of proclamation, will summon his own to the perception of the prey and the goods provided by himself; as a lion, calling his own, terrifies others and puts them to flight, so also the roaring of Christ will terrify and put to flight enemies, devils, and other foes of the Church. Rightly here, the Blessed Pappus of ours: 'The preaching of the Gospel made through the Apostles is compared with the roaring of a lion: because the roaring of a lion terrifies most, and is heard from a very great distance; so also the Holy Spirit, by the voice of the Gospel, convicts the world of sin, of righteousness, of judgment, and spreads this very voice most widely through the whole world.' The Lord promises this roaring of a lion; which both the Israelites dispersed in exile and the very nations themselves, among whom the Israelites were to dwell, are also to acknowledge and walk after him. For always with the prediction concerning the acknowledgment of the Messiah is joined the calling of the Gentiles.

(8.) A parallel passage is added: Which Grotius wishes to be compared here from Hos. 1:11. For since it was demonstrated above that in that passage it is not a matter of a bodily return, but of the conversion of the Israelites to the Lord, the same sense is solidly confirmed by the collation of the same with our present passage. Similarly, the passage Isa. 60:3 et seqq. may be compared. Whence not a little light will again accrue to ours. (9.) Finally, the consensus of the Interpreters is added. Of our own, all here easily agree that an Evangelical promise is being exhibited. The blessed Luther, Brentius, Osiander, Gesnerus, Pappus, Meisnerus, Tarnovius, the Weimar Paraphrase, as well as most of the Reformed, although they do not all proceed in the same way in their explanation. This is Osiander's paraphrase: Christ, by his Spirit through the Ministry of the word (which embraces Law and Gospel), convicts the World of sin and impiety, because it seeks salvation either in the worship of idols or in a hypocritical holiness of life. Then indeed the hearers, as if by a sudden crash or the roar of a lion, will be terrified, those dwelling to the West and the East: (not only Jews, but also the Gentiles.) But I will not allow them to wander uncertain in Religion, but in those places where they dwell, I will gather Churches, in which they themselves, like a bird in a nest, may be preserved for eternal salvation. Most of the others interpret it in that way, as we do. Among the Papists also, the principal ones stand on our side. Cornelius à Lapide, although according to his custom he collects diverse senses, nevertheless approves ours most: Christ being incarnate and preaching, and roaring as if a lion, then both through himself and through the Apostles, many Israelites were converted to him as much from Samaria and Judea as from Egypt, Assyria, and every region of the world, and flew like a dove, whom he himself placed in his houses, that is, in particular Churches, where they piously and holily serve and will serve God. Which is also the interpretation of Jerome from the Ancients, that these things are to be understood of Christ, indeed even of the ancient Hebrews, as the same author testifies in this place. The Hebrews refer these things to the coming of Christ: whom they hope is to come: We convince them that it has already passed: because both from Egypt and from the Assyrians, that is, both from the East and from the West, and from the North, and from the South, they have come: and daily they come, who may recline with Abraham,

Isaac, and Jacob. We may call them sons of the sea, or of the waters, who have been caught by the net of the Lord and drawn out from the sea of this world. And when they have been captured from death to life, they will be placed in their houses, which the Gospel calls barns, in which the grain, chosen and separated from the chaff, is stored. It is said to be the nature of lions that when they growl and roar, all living creatures tremble and cannot move from the spot where they stand: such is the dread, such is the terror. Therefore, when the Lord also roars and thunders like a lion and gives forth His voice, all birds and all winged creatures will shudder and will go to their nests, that is, to their houses, in which the Lord will dwell with them. Let us say it another way: When the true lion roars, the false lion, who according to the Apostle Peter is our adversary, will immediately fall silent; and every perverse dogma will be unable to open its mouth, and those who had previously been captured by him, released by the roar of the lion and by the terrible threat, will follow the Lord their God. Then the sons of the sea or of the waters, who had been begotten in the bitterness and false waters of the heretics, will fear; and having taken up wings, they will fly like birds out of Egypt, and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians, and they will say: Who will give me wings like a dove, and I will fly, and find rest? So that those who had labored among the heretics may find rest in the Church, and dwell in their houses, from which they had been seduced by error. Thus Jerome. The Chaldean also has a note here regarding the Messiah: Then I will bring them back in peace to their houses, and my word will be present for their protection, says the Lord. The WORD of the Lord is accustomed to designate the λόγον ὑποστατικὸν.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET AVOLABUNT QUASI AVIS EX Æ- GYPTO) Paveant quasi avis Ægyptia, id est, ciconia. Hoc dicit propter eos Israelitas, qui ad Salmanasaris adventum se in Ægyptum receperunt. Supra 9, 3.

ET QUASI COLUMBA DE TERRA ASSY- RIORUM) Quasi columba Assyriaca. Assyria plena colum- bis. Hoc dicit propter eos, qui in regiones Assyriorum ab- ducti sunt.

ET COLLOCABO EOS IN DOMIBUS SUIS) Perstat in similitudine:nam & ciconia ad nidum suum redit, & columba ad columbarium. Impletum hoc in Israelita- rum non multis, qui ad Deum conversi cum Judæ tribu re- diere: implendumque fuisset in pluribus, si plures se ad bo- nam mentem retulissent. Ut dictum alibi. Vide supra I, 11.

Pervertit iterum Grotius insignem promissio- nem Evangelicam. Non enim de reductione Israëli- tarum hæc cum Rabbinis recentioribus accipien- da, sed cum meliori interpretum parte de conversio- ne ad Dominum & restauratione spirituali per Mes- siam, quem Deus ex Ægypto revocaturus erat, ut oves Israëlis dispersas colligeret. Quod docet 1. subjectum: Non enim de Judæis loquitur, qui re- stituti fuere post aliquot annorum exilium; Sed de Ephraimo, vel Israelitis decem tribuum, quæ resti- tutæ nunquam sunt. Ideoque non apparet, quomo- do ad literam de illorum restitutione hic agi possit. Nam quod nonnulli dicunt, & per Cyrnm illis pro- miscue quoque factam redeundi potestatem & debella- tis à Cambyse Aegyptiis parcitum fuisse Israelitis ibi agentibus, conjecturæ tantum sunt, nec huic pro- phetiæ illustri respondent, aut satisfaciunt. Fate- tur ipse Grotius, Israelitarum non multos ad Deum conversos tum Judæ tribu rediisse, in quibus id im- pletum putat. Sed paucitate tanta videt non exhau- riri oraculum Propheticum. Recte Rivetus: Non potest ejus impletio referri ad exiguum aliquem nu- merum Israelitarum, qui forte cum Iudæis mixti fue- runt, quorum adeo fuit exigua manus, ut pro nihilo habiti fuerint, quando in recensione populi a ductori- bus, Esdra & Nehemia facta, nulla eorum mentio habetur, quæ certe non fuisset omissa, si quidem com- plementum tantæ Prophetiæ in ipsa situm fuisset. Vidit id probe Grotius, ideo fingit, implendum id fuisse in pluribus, si plures se ad bonam mentem retulissent. Verum enimvero hic non promissio habetur hypo- thetica, sed simplex, neque promissio tantum, sed etiam prædictio, in qua utique falli Spiritus Sanctus non potuit. B. Gesnerus non ad Israelitas hæc re- fert, sed ad gentes. Notandum, qui sint vocandi? Duo autem hominum genera nominantur: Unum sunt Judæi, & reliquiæ regni Israelitici, utpote de quibus hactenus est dictum. Alterum sunt filii maris, id est, habitantes tum in Insulis maris mediterranei, tum ultra illud in Europa, Græcia, Hispania, Germania &c. Sigillatim autem hic mentio fit Ægyptiorum & Assyriorum, quia duo ista regna præ omnibus aliis gentibus superstitioni & idololatriæ semper fuerunt dedita. Si vero hi populi in regnum Christi sunt ad- missi, cum pœnitentiam agerent, utique cæteris non erit desperandum. (2) Prædicatum: Avolabunt, quasi aves ex Ægypto, & quasi columba de terra Assy- riorum. Notatur non tantum reditus ad nidum & columbarium, sed etiam summa alacritas & prom- ptitudo, quod festini inde sint discessuri, uti aves illæ volatu pernicipssimo ab uno loco in alium ten- dunt, Psal. 55, 7. Ef. 60, 8. Adeoque exprimitur ita ἐνέργεια Spiritus S. cujus gratia, uti Ecclesia canit, nescit tarda molimina. Nam illa fidelibus illam indit mentem, ut pollutiones gentilium fugiant, & ad sanctitatem magna alacritate contendant.

3. Terminus à quo exprimitur quidem Ægyptus & terra Assyriorum, quia scilicet maxima pars Israe- litarum illuc dispersa erat, sed quum prædictio Israelitas communiter concernat, non ex illis tan- tum locis, sed ex omnibus mundi angulis, quocunque se receperant, eorundem reditus intelligitur, uti- que non in temporali ipsorum reductione impleta est; Sed ad reliquias Israëlis secundum electionem per- tinet, ex omnibus mundi partibus suo tempore col- ligendas & convertendas: FORMIDABUNT FILII MARIS cum timore ac tremore accurrent à finibus orbis terrarum. Erat enim mare terminus occidentalis terræ sanctæ, & ista terra undiquaque mari alluitur.

4. Terminus ad quem. Collocabo eos in domibus suis. Promissio hæc non impleta in 10. tribubus quantum ad materiales ipsorum domus vel agros. Ideoque spiritualiter intelligenda ἐξ ἀνάγκης est de conversione ad Ecclesiam. Est enim, uti diximus, non hypothetica promissio, quemadmodum fingit Grotius, sed simplex & absoluta. Si ergo historice accipi debeat, nunquam Israëlitæ vel ex parte do- mos suas occuparunt, neque enim tribubus decem restitutæ fuerunt urbes suæ, ipsis propriæ, & olim assignatæ divina κληροδοσία, aut agri antea à populis per Assyrios eo missos occupati, ideoque ad nidum suum, & ad columbarium proprium redire non po- tuere instar ciconiarum & columbarum. Frustra itaque se fatigare non immerito observat Rivetus, qui inter Christianos hæc referunt ad realem restitu- tionem Israelitarum in terra sua, quæ nunquam accidit.

5. Collatio v. 9. ET NON INGREDIAR IN CIVITATEM. Temere hæc Grotius in bo- nam partem accipit: Propterea non patiar, ut urbs ulla vestrarum vi capiatur, sed efficiam, ut deditio fiat, ac sic homines serventur in vita. Nihil tale verba referunt. Quæ ex contextu recte B. Pappus noster explicat: Altera pars Capitis proponit nobis dulcis- simam sermocinationem Iustitiæ & Misericordiæ di- vinæ consultantium de Populo Israëlitico, & Iustitia quidem Dei pronunciat indignos eos esse protectione sua, promeritos quippe easdem pœnas, atque Adama & Zeboim, quæ una cum Sodoma & Gomorrha igni cæ- litus demisso perierunt. Misericordia autem Dei duas rationes adfert, quare justa hæc ira lenienda sit. Mo- vetur enim Deus ad misericordiam, & ad mitigan- das pœnas, partim respectu imbecillitatis nostræ, quæ severitatem justitiæ divinæ nullo modo perferre potest; partim autem clementi sua Voluntate, qua non vult universum genus humanum frustra con- ditum esse; sed vult ex eo sibi colligere Ecclesiam, in quam divitias Gratiæ suæ effundat, & cui bo- na sua in tota æternitate communicet. Sic utra- que causarum harum testatur, nos gratis recipi à

Filio Dei, sine nostris meritis. Addit autem, & non in- grediar in civitatem: qua particula distinguit pro- missiones regno Israelitico factas, ab iis quæ factæ fuerunt regno Judaico. Illud enim spirituales tan- tum promissiones habet: hoc præterea corporales quoque de reditu in patriam & Restitutione poli- tiæ externæ. Esse autem hanc istius loci senten- tiam, sequentia etiam confirmant. B. Gesnerus: Pro terrenæ, inquit, urbis Samariæ conservatione, quam resipiscentibus negavit Dominus, jam pollice- tur civitatis Dei & Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti ædifi- cationem, quæ vocatione Judæorum & gentium per Evangelii tubam conficitur. Recte itaque B. Lu- therus f. 537. Mihi videtur simplicissimum & sen- tentiæ Prophetæ convenientissimum, ut intelligas De- um sic velle misereri regni Israelis disseminati inter gentes, ut tamen non redeant Israelitæ ad politiam & Ecclesiam Mosaicam, quæ usque ad Evangelii tempus in regno Juda mansit. Grotianæ glossæ similem notavit B. Meisnerus, de qua ejusque judicium sub- jicimus: Putant enim nonnulli, Deum hic ad mo- rem lenium victorum respicere, qui urbis alicujus deditione facta, quum volunt victis parcere, nec militari direptioni res civium committere, non in- grediuntur urbem cum exercitu. Ita quoque in- nui Deum velle Israelitis parcere, ne prorsus de- struantur. Hæc ἐξήγησις admitti posset, quoad gra- tiam spiritualem, quam Deus non subtraxit peni- tus; minime autem probari potest, quoad gratiam temporalem, quia urbes Israelitarum sunt omnino direptæ ab hostibus. Et quia textus loquitur de ur- bibus proprie dictis, utique de temporali urbium conservatione, quum eventus aliud docuerit, intel- ligi nequit. Hinc cadit & illa Drusii expositio, qua ita reddidit: Non veniam contra urbem, nem- pe hostili modo: non amplius obsidebo urbes vestras hostiliter.

(6.) Vis phraseos: post Dominum ambulabunt, sententiam nostram confirmat: Hæc enim impor- tat conversionem: quum indicetur non amplius post Baalim, sed post Dominum Regem suum Messiam, quemadmodum cap. III. 5. prædictum, ambulatu- ros. Antea recesserant à Deo cap. VII. 3. & dixe- rant, Vadam post amatores meos c. II. Nunc vero am- bulabunt post Jehovam vera fide, fideique obedien- tia sequentur Dominum illum suum ex Ægypto voca- tum c. 11, 1. ceu Ducem ac Ductorem suum. Esa. 52, 12. Zach. 3, 5. Mich. 2, 12. Pulchre de hac phrasi Luther. f. 538. Hic demum erit fructus, qui sequetur verbum Evangelii & sanctificationem. Quod cum hactenus ambulaverint secundum desideria cordium suorum, cum statuerint sua sacra, ritus & alia esse justitiam coram Deo, hæc omnia simul abjicient, & nitentur tantum justitia & meritis filii Dei, quem in Evangelio audient traditum pro peccatis ipsorum. Habet e- nim sententia hæc insignem exclusivam omnium ope- rum & cultuum, qui non sunt Dominus. Quanta in papatu cultuum & operum est varietas? & tamen non Monachus votum suum, non sacrificulus Missam suam, non hypocrita jejunia sua, non divites eleemosy- nas suas audebant appellare, quod sint Dominus. Quod igitur dicit, ambulabunt post Dominum, idem est, ac si dicat: Abjicient omnem fiduciam o- perum humanorum & sola Dei gratia ac bonitate nitentur & fident. Nam qui credit Filium Dei fa- ctum victimam pro peccatis suis, hic nullo suo ope- re nitetur. Videt enim nostra opera non posse æquari morti Filii Dei. Itaque ea una se eriget, per eam unam statuet sibi reconciliatum Deum, impetratam remissionem peccatorum & vitam æ- ternam. Hoc vere est post Dominum ambulare. Ac sequitur hanc fidem studium obedientiæ erga

Legem. Liberati enim à peccatis, cupiunt inno- centiam hanc retinere. Etsi igitur labuntur per infirmitatem, tamen se iterum erigunt hac fiducia, & postea ambulabunt cautius.

(7.) Notandum etiam Medium conversionis. Rugitus Dei leonis rugitui alios ad prædam invitan- tis comparatus, quo prædicatio verbi divini desi- gnatur. Hæc enim rugitus leonis dicitur Joel. 3. v. 17. Amos. 1, 2. cap. 3, 8. conf. Ebr. 12, 25. Et ut leo sui generis animalia, & præcipue catulos vocat ad prædam, vid. Plutarch. de natur. animal. Sic Messias clara voce præconii ad perceptionem prædæ, ac bonorum à se partorum convocabit suos; ut leo suos vocans alios terret, & in fugam conjicit, sic etiam Christi rugitus inimicos, diabolos, & alios Ecclesiæ hostes perterrefaciet & fugabit. Recte hic Beat. Pappus noster: Prædicatio Evangelii facta per Apostolos comparatur cum Rugitu Leonis: quia Leonis rugitus maxime terret, & ex maxima di- stantia auditur; Ita & Spiritus Sanctus voce Evan- gelii arguit mundum de peccato, de Iustitia, de Iudicio, & latissime hanc ipsam vocem spargit per universum terrarum orbem. Hunc Rugitum Leo- nis promittit Dominus; quod etiam agnituri sint, & post eum ambulaturi, tum Israëlitæ in exilio di- sperfi, tum ipsæ quoque gentes, inter quas habi- taturi erant Israëlitæ. Semper enim cum prædi- ctione de Agnitione Messiæ conjungitur Vocatio Gentium.

Accedit (8.) locus parallelus: Quem hic con- ferri vult Grotius ex Hos. 1, 11. Quum enim in illo non de reditu corporali, sed conversione Israëllitarum ad Dominum agi supra demonstratum sit, ex ejus- dem cum nostro præsente loco collatione idem sensus solide firmatur. Similiter conferri poterit locus Esa. 60, 3. seqq. Unde non parum lucis nostro iterum accedet. (9.) Accedit denique consensus Interpp. E nostris hic omnes facile conveniunt, promissionem exhiberi Evangelicam. Beat. Luth. Brentius, Osiander, Gesnerus, Pappus, Meisnerus, Tarnovius, Paraphr. Vinariens. ut & Reformati plerique omnes, quamvis non eadem ratione o- mnes in explicatione procedant. Osiandr. hæc est paraphrasis: Christus spiritu suo per Ministerium verbi (quod Legem & Evangelium complectitur) arguit Mundum peccati & impietatis, quod salutem vel in cultu idolorum vel in hypocritica vitæ sancti- monia quæret. Tum vero auditores tanquam aves subito fragore aut leonis rugitu consternabuntur ad Occidentem & Orientem habitantes: (non modo Iu- dæi, sed etiam gentes.) Ego autem non sinam eos incer- tos in Religione vagari, sed iis locis, ubi habitant, colli- gam Ecclesias, in quibus ipsi, tanquam avis in nido, ad perpetuam salutem conserventur. Cæteri plerique, illa, uti nos, ratione interpretantur. E Pontificiis etiam præcipui à nostra stant parte. Corn. à Lapide, etsi pro more diversos sensus colligat, maxime ta- men nostrum probat: Christo incarnato & prædi- cante, ac rugiente quasi leone, tum per se, tum per A- postolos, multi Israëlitæ tam ex Samaria & Judæa, quam ex Ægypto, Assyria, omnique mundi plaga ad eum conversi sunt, & quasi columba advolarunt, quos ipse collocavit in domibus suis, puta in particularibus Ecclesiis, ubi pie sancteque Deo serviunt & servient. Quæ etiam è Veteribus Hieronymi est interpreta- tio, hæc de Christo intelligenda esse, imo etiam E- bræorum veterum, teste eodem in h. l. Hæc Hebræi ad adventum Christi referunt: quem sperant esse venturum: Nos jam transacta convincimus: quia & de Ægypto, & de Assyriis, hoc est, & ab Oriente & ab Occidente, & ab Aquilone, & à Meridie venerunt: & quotidie veniunt, qui discumbant cum Abraham,

Ifaac, & Jacob. Filios autem maris, sive aquarum eos possumus appellare, qui sagena Domini compre- hensi sunt, & abstracti de mari hujus seculi. Cumque capti fuerint de morte ad vitam, collocabuntur in do- mibus suis, quæ horrea vocat Evangelium, in quibus electa & à paleis separata frumenta conduntur. Na- tura leonum esse dicitur: ut cum infremuerint & ru- gierint, omnia animantia contremiscant, & fixo gra- du se movere non possint: tantus pavor est, tanta for- mido. Itaque & dominus cum instar leonis rugierit & intonuerit ac dederit vocem suam, cunctæ aves, & universa volatilia perhorrescent: & ibunt ad nidos, id est, ad domos suas, in quibus Dominus habitabit cum eis. Dicamus & aliter: Cum verus leo infre- muerit, falsus leo, qui est juxta Apostolum Petrum adversarius noster, ilico conticescet: & omne dogma perversum, os suum aperire non poterit, quique ante ab eo capti fuerant, rugitu leonis soluti, & commina- tione terribili sequentur Dominum Deum suum. Tunc timebunt filii maris sive aquarum, qui in ama- ritudine & falsis hæreticorum aquis fuerant procrea- ti: & assumtis pennis volabunt quasi aves ex Ægypto, & quasi columba de terra Assyriorum, & dicent: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ, & volabo, & requiescam? Ut qui apud Hæreticos laboraverant, requiescant in Ecclesia, & habitent in domibus suis, de quibus fuerant errore seducti. Hæc Hieronymus. Notam etiam Messiæ hic habet Chaldæus: Tunc reducam eos in pace ad domos suas, & verbum meum aderit in patrocinium eorum dicit Dominus. VER- BUM Domini λόγον ὑποστατικὸν designare solet.

## 11:12
Verse 12. EPHRAIM HAS SURROUNDED ME IN NEGATION) The Hebrews better refer this to the following chapter. You should translate it correctly: Ephraim has surrounded me with a lie. He promised excellent things: he performed nothing.

AND IN DECEIT THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL, BUT JUDAH DESCENDS AS A WITNESS WITH GOD, AND WITH THE HOLY ONES IS FAITHFUL) When Judah was still strong with God (in the worship of God) and acted faithfully with the Holy Ones (that is, the Prophets). A description of the times of Hezekiah, who restored the worship of God in Judah, having faith in Isaiah and other Prophets; at which time the morals of the ten tribes were most corrupt, with King Hosea trying in vain to correct them somewhat.

The punctuation of the Vulgate is rightly criticized: and therefore this section is to be referred to the final sermon, which begins here.

Latin:

Vers. 12. CIRCVMDEDIT ME IN NEGATIONE EPHRAIM) Melius Hebræi hoc ad caput sequens referunt. Vertas recte: Circumbenit me mendacio Ephraim. Egregia promisit: nihil præstitit.

ET IN DOLO DOMUS ISRAEL, JVDAS AV- TEM TESTIS DESCENDIT CVM DEO, ET CVM SANCTIS FIDELIS) Cum Iudas adhuc fortis esset cum Deo, (in Dei cultu) & fideliter cum Sanctis (id est, Prophetis) ageret. Descriptio temporum Ezechiæ, qui in Juda cultum Dei re- stituit, Esaia aliisque Prophetis fidem habens; quo tempore corruptissimi erant decem tribuum mores Osea rege fru- stra eos nonnihil corrigere conante.

Recte distinctio Vulgati redarguitur: ideoque hoc tmema ad concionem postremam, quæ hic in- cipit, referenda est.

## 12:1 Argument
SERMON VII. THE LATTER EVANGELICAL. CHAPTER XII. Exhorting to repentance.

Having premised a complaint about the idolatrous worship of GOD, while Judah still faithfully adhered to its GOD, the Israelites are warned to perform repentance without hypocrisy, by the proposed example of their common parent Jacob and the benefit of divine preservation and the concession of the Prophets, so that they may no longer, having disregarded those things which God showed to Jacob and to the people themselves, serve idols and perish.

Let not that which man has made be done, but that which the Lord has said.

Verse 1. EPHRAIM FEEDS ON WIND) He gapes at the wind: he follows empty things.

AND FOLLOWS THE HEAT) The East wind, which in those regions not only does no good, but also does the greatest harm.

ALL DAY HE MULTIPLIES A LIE AND DEVASTATION) A lie, the fault of Israel. Devastation, the punishment. He will now show the lie by an example.

AND HAS MADE A COVENANT WITH THE ASSYRIANS) At which time, having entered into a covenant with the Assyrians, he was held,

AND OIL WAS CARRIED INTO EGYPT) At the same time he sends oil, which is most excellent in the land of Israel, and other gifts into Egypt, so that by the help of Egypt he might revolt from the Assyrian, 2 Kings 17, 4.

Latin:

CONCIO VII. EVANGELICA POSTERIOR. CAPUT XII. Ad pœnitentiam excitans.

Premissa querela de idolatrico DEI cultu, Iu- da adhuc fideliter DEO suo adhærente, mo- nentur Israelitæ ad pœnitentiam sine fuco a- gendam proposito exemplo communis paren- tis Iacobi ac beneficio divinæ conservationis & concessionis Prophetarum, ne amplius in- super habitis iis, quæ Deus Iacobo, ipsique po- pulo exhibuit, idolis servant, & pereant.

Non quod homo fecit, Dominus quod dixit, agatur.

Vers. 1. EPHRAIM PASCIT VENTVM) Hiat ad ven tum: inania sequitur.

ET SEQVITVR ÆSTVM) Eurum, qui in illi regionibus non modo non prodest, sed & plurimum no cit.

TOTA DIE MENDACIVM ET VASTITA TEM MVLTIPLICAT) Mendacium, cupla Israelis. Va stitas, pœna. Mendacium jam exemplo ostendet.

ET FOEDVS CVM ASSYRIIS INIIT) Qu tempore, fœdere cum Assyriis inito tenebatur,

ET OLEVM IN ÆGYPTVM FEREBAT) Eo- dem tempore oleum, quod in terra Israelis præstantissi- mum, & munera alia mittit in Ægyptum, ut ope Ægypti ab Affyrio deficiat 2. Reg. 17, 4.

## 12:2
THEREFORE THE JUDGMENT OF THE LORD WITH JUDAH) There is also a dispute for the Lord with Judah. I have, says God, that which I may complain of concerning Judah; for although Hezekiah removed idolatry publicly, many vices nevertheless remain in the people. See Isaiah 22.

AND I WILL VISIT UPON JACOB) But the ten tribes, which are the greater part of the descendants of Jacob, I will punish more severely.

ACCORDING TO HIS WAYS, AND ACCORDING TO HIS INVENTIONS HE WILL RENDER TO HIM) He will be treated according to his ungrateful spirit toward God.

Latin:

JVDICIVM ERGO DOMINI CVM JVDA) Etiam lis Domino cum Iuda. Habeo, inquit Deus & quod de Juda querar; nam quanquam idololatriam publicitus sustulit Ezechias, multa tamen vitia in populo manent. Vide Esaiam 22.

ET VISITABO SVPER JACOB) Sed decem tri- bus, quæ pars major posterum Jacobi, gravius puniam.

JVXTA VIAS EJVS, ET JVXTA ADINVEN- TIONES EJVS REDDET EI) Tractabitur pro ingrato suo in Deum animo.

## 12:3
Ver. 3. IN THE WOMB HE SUPPLANTED HIS BROTHER) Namely by divine power, not by his own natural ability, being as yet devoid of reason: and even then he received an omen of greater fraternal happiness.

AND IN HIS STRENGTH HE WAS DIRECTED WITH THE ANGEL) He prevailed over the Angel.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IN VTERO SVPPLANTAVIT FRATREM SVVM) Nempe divina virtute, non suopte ingenio, ratio- nis adhuc exsors: ac jam tum omen accepit, felicitatis fra- terna majoris.

ET IN FORTITVDINE SVA DIRECTVS EST CVM ANGELO) Prævaluit Angelo.

## 12:4
Ver. 4. AND HE PREVAILED OVER THE ANGEL) In the Hebrew the same words are repeated, so that it may be shown that the matter is great, Gen. 32, 28.

AND HE WAS STRENGTHENED) Because he had been invigorated by God, namely by the Lord of the angels.

HE WEPT AND BESOUGHT HIM) What he did to the Angel, do you perform to God.

IN BETHEL HE FOUND HIM) The same Angel. In Bethel, said emphatically, that is, where you worship calves against the law of God. The history is Gen. 35, 8. 9.

AND THERE HE SPOKE WITH YOU) So also the Chaldean reads, who attributes these words and the preceding ones to the Israelites, as if they were defending themselves because they had placed the place of their worship at Bethel: but by changing one point, Capellus, a most learned man, made an excellent sense: with him, namely with Jacob. The Greeks [read] πρὸς ἀυτὸς.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET INVALVIT AD ANGELVM) In He- bræo eadem verba repetuntur, ut ostendatur res esse ma- gna, Gen. 32, 28.

ET CONFORTATVS EST) Quia roboratus erat à Deo, nempe angelorum Domino.

FLEVIT ET ROGAVIT EVM) Quod ille An- gelo, hoc Deo vos præstate.

IN BETHEL INVENIT EVM) Eundem Ange- lum. In Bethel, ἐμφατικῶς dictum, id est, ubi vos contra Dei legem vitulos colitis. Historia est Gen. 35, 8. 9.

ET IBI LOCVTVS EST VOBISCVM) Ita & Chaldæus legit, qui hæc verba & præcedentia tribuit Israe- litis, quasi se defendentibus, quod locum cultus sui Bethe- lem posuissent: at uno puncto mutato Capellus vir erudi- tissimus sensum optimum fecit: cum eo, cum Jacobo nem- pe. Græci πρὸς ἀυτὸς.

## 12:5
Ver. 5.

AND THE LORD GOD OF HOSTS, THE LORD IS HIS MEMORIAL) That is, his name, by which he is recognized, That God, who revealed himself to Jacob through an angel, is by far the most powerful, therefore do not distrust his power: there are no evils so great, from which he cannot deliver you.

One must note here first that στρεβλότης [distortion] by which he draws to a created angel those things which must be understood of the Son of God, the uncreated angel. For that he was the antagonist and wrestler of Jacob, various things not only in the Mosaic History Gen. 32, but also in this Prophetic text prove. First, the name אלהים, which is attributed to this angel. For no single created angel is anywhere designated by the name Elohim. But that name either denotes the persons of the Deity πληθηντικῶς [in the plural], or is attributed to one person of the H. H. Trinity, because one divine person is not without another, on account of the essential περιχώρησιν [indwelling] which exists between them and their ὁμουσίαν [consubstantiality]. And therefore the angel, who is called Elohim, is none other than the uncreated angel, the Son of God. For what the Vulgate rendered in v. 3, AND IN HIS STRENGTH HE WAS DIRECTED WITH THE ANGEL, and Grotius interpreted as: He prevailed over the Angel, that in Hebrew is, he prevailed over את אלהים God himself. Grotius acknowledges that the same words are repeated in the Hebrew to show the magnitude of the matter in v. 3 and 4. But he who in the latter place is called מלאך [angel] is in the former called אלהים [Elohim], whence the argument: He with whom Jacob fought and whom he prevailed over there, is Elohim, the true God. The Angel of the Lord is he with whom Jacob fought and whom he prevailed over there. Therefore that Angel of the Lord is Elohim, the true God, and thus he is not a created angel, but uncreated. Furthermore, the narration of the angel confirms the same: He wept and besought him; he whom the Patriarch Jacob besought with weeping, and from whom he sought a blessing, is certainly not some created angel. For from such a one a blessing ought not to be sought. And penitential tears of this kind are not to be offered to angels, but to God alone.
