DE MANU MORTIS LI- BERO EOS, Liberarem, si pœnitentiam age- rent. DE MORTE REDIMAM EOS, re- dimerem, id est, eriperem eos ab exitio. ERO MORS TUA, O MORS. Essem pestis tibi ô mors, id est, omnia mortifera extinguerem, ut in Sen- nacheribi exercitu factum est postea. MORSUS TUUS ERO INFERNE. Excidium tibi ô se- pulchrum. Sepulchrum hic intellige fossam, in quam toti populi conjiciuntur, ut fit in publicis cladibus. Hæc ille, artifex pervertendi oracula Prophe- tica, sine compare. Sed ad literam hæc de CHRISTO agere, qui sua passione & resur- rectione nos ab inferno & morte liberavit, omnes- que plenariæ liberationis hujus participes redditu- rus est, in resuscitatione ad vitam æternam, non so- lum Patres & Doctores Ecclesiæ magno consensu docuere: Eusebius lib. IV. demonstr. Evangel. c. XII. S. Hieronymus in h. l. & in Epitaph. Nepot. S. Augustinus serm. 137. de temp. Gregorius M. ho- mil. 22. in Evang. alique, sed in confesso etiam id fuit penes Ebræos antiquiores, de liberatione per Messiam futura hæc accipienda esse: unde R. Moses Hadarschan, teste Galatino lib. 8. de arcanis Catho- lic. Verit c. 21. mysteria fidei more Rabbinico in- volvens: Ibat mecum Messias filius David, quousque perveni, ad portas gehennæ, cumque viderent captivi, qui in gehenna erant, lumen Messiæ, gavisi sunt eum recipere dicentes; Hic educet me de his tenebris, sicut dictum est Ose 13. de manu inferi redimam eos, de morte liberabo eos. Quæ è R. Mose in Bereschith Rebba ad Gen. 24, 67. collatione loci Esa. 35, 10. instituta: Et redemti Domini redibunt, & fugient dolor & gemitus, adducta: ubi fabulatus Moses est, Kippod Angelum mortis mensurasse infernum, ejusque profundum iter esse 300. annorum, longitudinem ve- ro & latitudinem 500. annorum, uti legere est in

Pugione Fidei Raimundi Martini part. 3. dist. 2. c. 8. §. 4. Nec pariter assensum apud suos invenit Jesui- ta Christus, uti apud Grotium. De CHRISTO enim haec intelligenda esse, quoad literam, cum lau- datis Patribus, & Haymone, Hugone, Ruperto, Ly- rano, Vatablo, & Aria Montano, Ribera, Meno- chius, Tirinus, Cornel. à Lapide, Jesuitae agnoscunt, de quo etiam vaticinium, sed sensu allegorico, Theo- doretus explicat. Non ineleganter Cornelius: Est prosopopoeia: mors enim & infernus hic quasi duae per- sonae & duo Reges inducuntur late dominantes, quos Regno & vita spoliavit CHRISTUS è morte, & inferno resurgens, ac de utroque triumphavit: mortem qui- dem, quia post resurrectionem mors nulla erit: infer- num vero, quia post eandem nullum amplius poterit capere & devorare. Celebrant veteres robur, vi- ctorias, & triumphos Achillis, Herculis, Alexan- dri, Julii Caesaris, & similium, quibus nemo in hac vita resistere valuit: Sed hi omnes à morte victi sunt & ad inferos descenderunt. Solus Christus do- mitor est mortis & inferni. Unde ait ipse Apoc. 1, 18. Ego habeo claves mortis & inferni. Et habemus interpretem omni exceptione majorem, S. Apo- stolum, qui haec de CHRISTO praedicta & plenarie in universali resurrectione implenda esse, sonora voce testatur 1. Cor. 15, 54. Cum autem mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, tunc fiet sermo, qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoriam. Ubi est mors vi- ctoria tua? ubi est mors stimulus tuus? Stimulus au- tem mortis peccatum est: virtus vero peccati lex. DEO autem gratias, qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Quid ergo cla- rius, aut certius, quam de CHRISTO haec praedi- cta esse, nisi quis palam Apostolo obstrepere velit? Hoc itaque ἐπινίκιον est CHRISTI triumphantis de morte & inferno, imo de peccato, & lege: Hoc Epitaphium est congruum morti & inferno: uti Gre- gor. Nazianz. eleganter orat. 42. loquitur: ubi est mors stimulus tuus? ubi tua inferne victoria? Crux te prostravit, vitae autor tibi necem attulit. Ex- animis es, immobilis, iners. Insultare nunc cum Hieronymo in Epitaph. Nepot. ad Heliod. morti laeto animo possumus, cum nos aggreditur: Qui per Osee quondam tibi rigidus minabatur, Ero mors tua ô mors, ero morsus tuus, inferne, illius morte tu mortua es, illius morte nos vivimus: devorasti, & devorata es, dumque assumpti corporis CHRISTI solicituris illece- bra, & aridis faucibus praedam putas, interiora tua adunco dente confossa sunt. Gratias tibi CHRISTE Salvator, tua agimus creatura, quod tam potentem adversarium nostrum dum occideres, occidisti. Hoc pacto Bernhardi frater Gerhardus, laetissimo pecto- re excipiebat mortem; cum stupore adsidentium eidem insultans: de quo praeclare Bernhardus serm. 26. in Cant. Accitus, inquit, sum ego ad id mi- raculi, videre exultantem in morte hominem, & in- sultantem morti: ubi est mors victoria tua? ubi est mors stimulus tuus? jam non est stimulus, sed jubilus, jam cantando moritur homo & moriendo cantat. Usurparis ad laetitiam mater moeroris, usurparis ad gloriam gloriae inimica, usurparis ad introitum regni porta inferi, & fovea perditionis ad inventionem salutis, idque ab homine peccatore: juste nimirum, quia tu inique in hominem inno- centem & justum potestatem temeraria usurpasti, mortua es ô mors & perforata hamo, quem incauta glutijsti, cujus illa vox est in Propheta: o mors ero mors tua, morsus tuus ero inferne. Illo, inquam, ha- mo perforata, transeuntibus per medium tui fideli- bus, latum laetumque exitum pandis ad vitam. Quapropter ad hunc victorem, Redemptorem nostrum, cum Abbate devotissimo serm. de pass. Domini nos convertamus: Quid Domine JESU, fortissime Zelotes, quid gratiarum retribuam, ut di- gne retribuam ego homo pulvis & vile figmentum. Quid enim pro mea salute facere debuisti, & non fe- cisti? Ab imo pedis usque ad summum verticis te totum in aquas passionum demersisti, ut me totum extraheres de illis, & intraverunt usque ad animam tuam. Nam animam tuam in mortem perdidisti, ut meam perdi- tam mihi redderes. Et ecce me duplici debito obliga- sti. Nam & pro eo quod dedisti tuam, debitor tibi sum: & pro mea quidem anima bis a te mihi data semel in creatione, & semel in redemtione, quid magis juste ti- bi reddam, quam ipsam, non habeo. Pro tua autem pretiosa anima ita contribulata quid ab homine di- gne rependi possit, non invenio. Nam etsi cælum & terram, & omnem ornatum eorum pro ea possem re- pendere, certe nec sic usque ad mensuram debiti ullate- nus attingere possem. Ut autem ipsum quod & de- beo & possibile mihi est, retribuam: tui Domine mu- neris est. Diligendus es mi Domine toto corde, tota anima, tota virtute. Et tua mihi sequenda vestigia, qui pro me mori dignatus es. Et quomodo fiet istud in me nisi per te? Adhæreat anima mea post te, quia tota virtus ejus pendet ex te. O quam bonus, quam suavis es, Domine JESU, redemptor perditorum, sal- vator redemtorum, spes exulum, fortitudo laboran- tium, anxietati spiritus latitudo, animæ lacrymosæ & post te currentis in sudore & solatium & suave refrige- rium: corona triumphantium, unica merces & læti- tia omnium supernorum civium, uberrimus fons o- mnium gratiarum, inclyta proles summi DEI, & DEUS summus, benedicant te omnia quæ in cælo sunt sursum, & quæ in terra deorsum. Magnus tu & magnum nomen tuum. Hoc ergo agamus, & CHRISTO nos totus consecremus, qui totum se impendit pro nobis. Mortuus ipse est pro nobis, ut non nobis, sed ipsi vivamus. Peccata pertulit in corpore suo super lignum, ut mortui peccatis vivamus justitiæ. Resurrexit a mortuis, ut nos re- surgamus a vitiis. Resuscitati in anima, monet S. August. per fidem cum justitia vivamus, ut etiam corpore ad æternam lætitiam resurgamus. Disce- damus ab operibus malis, quæ mortificant animam, & dum vivit corpus, ut in æternis bonis & anima no- stra consequatur esse, & corpus. Ille cum CHRI- STO vivit, ille regnat cum CHRISTO, qui resur- gentis CHRISTI innocentiam sequitur, imitatur vi- tam, juxta Chrysologum serm. CXIII. Hoc ut fiat, conventus Paschales seduli adeamus, Angelos Do- mini, præcones Resurrectionis, devoti audiamus, munera etiam ad aram grati illis deponamus, qui munera spiritualia, & cœlestia nobis dispensant. Impleat nos omnes triumphi Paschalis gaudiis & fructibus, hostesque nostros convertat, aut sub pe- des nostros conterat Triumphator noster gloriosus P. P. profesto Paschatos Anno clɔ Iɔc LXIII.

ADDUCET URENTEM VENTUM) Orienta- lem, qui pestifer illis in locis. Simul ostenditur situs As- syriæ.

DOMINI) Deo immittente.

DE DESERTO ASCENDENTEM) Per Syriæ par- tem desertam 1. Reg. 19, 15. Nam hac iter Assyriis in Sama- ridem.

ET SICCABIT VENAS EJUS, ET DESOLA- BIT FONTEM EJUS.) Ventus enim ab Oriente erat adu rens: unde καύσων Græcis dicitur, ac proinde & exsiccans Ezech. 17, 10. 19, 12. Quid autem per hanc ἀλληγορίαν significetur, explicant sequentia.

ET IPSE) Assyrius, qui per ventum illum intelli- gendus.

DIRIPIET THESAURUM OMNIS VASIS DE SIDERABILIS) Rerum pretiosarum. Ita hæ voces sumun- tur 2. Par. 32, 27. 36, 10. Dan. 11, 8. Nah. 2, 9.

Hæc interpretatio, uti dixi, admitti potest, mo- do priora non habeantur pro communicatione, sed juncta dicatur promissioni comminatio, quod pe- nes Prophetas perfrequens. Non desunt tamen, qui allegorice de gratia Novi Testamenti expli- cent, ut notetur per adductionem venti effusio Spiritus Sancti, per siccationem fontis obstru- ctio venæ peccatorum, per direptionem vasorum desiderabilium, ab Ephraim vel Ecclesia faciendam, victoria Ecclesiæ ab hostibus reportanda, quæ vid. apud Meisnerum. Sic etiam B. Tarnovius hæc per promissionem Ephraimo factam exposuit hoc modo; Quia hoc, (quod cum ita sit) inter fratres faciet fructificare,, & fœcundum reddet ipse redem- ptor Ephraimium suum seu Israelem spiritualem; re- liquis suis fratribus Christus multos alios Evange- lii præconio adjunget denuo, vide Ps. 22. & 23. Joh. 20, 17. Heb. 2, 10. 11. 12. qui fructum ferant multipli- cem in Ecclesia Joh. 15, 2. 8. 16. Veniet Eurus, ven- tus Jehovoæ (maximus) hostis crudelis & impetuo- sus Assyrius è deserto oriens, & exarescet scaturigo e- jus (afflicti populi) tamen ille Ephraim non modo evadei victor per Christum, sed etiam diripiet the- saurum omnium desiderabilium. Ita Tarnovius.

Nono confirmat imprimis hanc interpretatio- nem S. Apostolus 1. Corint. 15, 54. seqq. cum ex hoc oraculo probat nos incorruptibiles & immorta- les resurrecturos ad æternam vitam. Cum au- tem mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, tunc fiet sermo, qui scriptus est, absorpta est mors in victoria (εἰς νῖκος in victoriam,) ubi est, mors, victoria tua? ubi est, inferne, stimulus tuus? In Græco est πῦ σγ, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον, πῦ σγ, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος, ubi est, mors, stimulus tuus? Ubi est, inferne, victoria tua? Addit Apostolus explicationem, quis sit stimulus mortis? v. 56. τὸ δὲ κέντρον ῾ῤ θανάτε ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος. Stimulus autem mortis peccatum est, virtus vero peccati lex: Et gra- tiarum actionem v. 57. Deo autem gratia, qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum Jesum Chri- stum. Unde luce meridiana clarius effulget, lo- cum Propheticum ab Apostolo non de liberatione Judæorum è captivitate Babylonica, nec de reductio- ne Israelitarum è dissipatione Assyriaca intellectum fuisse, sed de liberatione nostri, per Dominum no- strum Jesum Christum facta, neque liberationem ab exitio corporali, aut à periculo ad sepulcrum ducen- te, juxta interpretationem Apostolicam, à Prophe- ta designatam esse, sed liberationem à morte, & stimu- lo mortis, peccato, ac maledictione legis, quæ virtus est peccati, nec non ab inferno, seu æterna condem- natione, abolitionem mortis, peccati, maledictio- nis legis, inferni, vel potestatis infernalis, quæ ma- nus inferni dicta Prophetæ, & victoriam adversus hostes illos spirituales, per Christum Dominum no- strum concessam, qui nos ab iisdem liberavit per mortem & resurrectionem suam ratione meriti, & quantum ad victoriæ acquisitionem, sed in novissimo die plene liberaturus est ratione efficaciæ ad victoriæ istius plenariam fruitionem, ubi mortem prorsus ab- sorptam esse in victoriam, lætabuntur electi, & hoc epinicio insultabunt morti & inferno: Ubi, mors, tuus est stimulus? ubi, inferne, tua est victoria? Nam tum non solum immunes erunt electi in æternum à manu, vel potestate inferni, sed destruetur etiam hostis novissimus, mors, quam ita vocat Apostolus vers. 26. quia à morte resuscitabimur, nec mor- tali corpore, sed immortali prodituri sumus, & mortale hoc induet immortalitatem, nec infernus, condemnatio, maledictio, vel lex maledicens, aut peccatum, mortis stimulus, ullam in nos habitura funt potestatem, sed vitam, salutem & gloriam æ- ternam consequemur per Christum Dominum no- strum, ejusque victoria ita plenarie fruemur in o- mnem æternitatem. Quod ergo ipse Spiritus San- ctos interpretatur de mortis abolitione, & immor- talitate gloriosa per Christum, ejusque mortem & resurrectionem nobis acquisita, & in resurrectione beata in nobis perficienda, id certe non loquitur de sola Ephraimi ab exitio sui temporis corporali sibi impendente, liberatione. Atqui ita interpre- tatur Spiritus Sanctus sententiam emphaticam: A morte redimam: Ero pestis tua, ô mors. Ergo hæc sententia non loquitur de sola Ephraimi ab exitio corporali impendente liberatione. Quod A- postolus de inferni & condemnationis æternæ de- structione, & vitæ ac salutis æternæ conciliatione interpretatur, facta per Christum Dominum no- strum, id utique non agit de Israëliturum à periculis ad sepulcrum ducentibus liberatione. Ac fic inter- pretatur Apostolus verba Prophetæ nostri: De manu inferni liberabo eos: ero exitium tuum, ô in- ferne. Ergo non agunt illa de Israëlitarum à peri- culis ad sepulcrum deducentibus liberatione.

Jam si conferatur alterum dictum, quod ceu παράλληλον conjunxit Apostolus Ef. 25, 8. Præci- pitabit mortem in æternum: iterum manifestum est, hæc de vi & efficacia mortis & resurrectionis Chri- sti accipienda esse, utpote per quam absorpta mors est in victoriam, per quam deletum est, quod contra nos erat, chirographum decreti, & de medio subla- tum, crucique affixum, & exspoliati principatus & po- testates, quas traduxit confidenter, palam triumphans illos in semetipso, teste eodem Apostolo Col. 2, 14. Non ergo dubium, illum redemptorem, qui hic lo- quitur, de manu inferni liberabo eos, de morte redi- mam eos, Christum esse Dominum nostrum, in quo nobis data est victoria: Eundemque esse Dominum illum, qui promittit: Ero, ô mors, pestis tua: Ero, ô inferne, exitium tuum. Neque porro dubium, eum victoriam quoad meritum obtentam nobis esse morte & resurrectione Christi, cum traditus est propter peccata nostra, & propter justitiam nostram refuscitatus; quod ad plenum autem illius victoriæ effectum & fructum, obtentum iri in gloriosa à mortis resuscitatione, ac vitæ æternæ concessio- ne. Cum enim mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος, tunc fiet (quoad plenum complementum) sermo ille, qui scri- ptus est, tum apud Esaiam cap. 25, 8. tum penes Hoseam cap. 13, 14. Quæ interpretatio, uti omni exceptione superior est, ita nullatenus eam cum Grotiana aut Calvini glossa consistere posse, in solis disco, quod ajunt, positum esse arbitramur.

Ineptus autem est Calvinus, cum Apostolum dicit nec allegare verba Hoseæ, nec etiam alludere, sed tan- tum tritum apud Judæos proverbium: Quod Jehovah sit Dominus & victor mortis: ad suum institutum de resuscitatione mortuorum, per Christum facienda accommodare. Non enim loquitur Paulus de pro- verbio aliquo Judaico, sed de λόγῳ γεγραμμένῳ vel sermone scripto, nec sola hic est accommoda- tio, sed tunc impletum iri sermonem illum scriptum, ait. Unde Pareus ipse: allegationem esse non nega- verim. Quapropter concludimus cum Hierony- mo: Quod Apostolus in resurrectionem interpre- "tatus est Domini, nos aliter interpretari nec pos- "sumus, nec audemus.

Neque scrupulus ille de verborum varietate quemquam movere potest, qui novit Apostolos non semper presse verba ipsa textus sequutos, sed sæpissime Græcas versiones receptas, cum sensus idem prodit, retinuisse, nonnunquam etiam ad ex- primendam sententiam textus originalis paululum mutasse, quod hic etiam factum. Nam LXX. sic ha- bent: πῦ ἡ δίκη σε, θάνατε, πῦ τὸ κέντρον σε, ἅδη. Apostolus vero τὸ κέντρον apponit morti, quia ei concinnius quadrat, & inferno manus tributa erat à Propheta: de manu inferni liberabo eos. Inferno ita- que τὸ νῖκος concinnius tribuitur, quod potestas in- ferni prævalere nobis non valeat, sed devicta per Christum sit. Etsi autem exemplaria quædam Græ- ca LXX. Interpp. legant δίκη caula, alia tamen νῖκος, nonnulla, uti Apostolus, νῖκος habent. Nec vero opus esse existimamus, ut verba singula LXX. in- terpp.è verbis Ebræis indagemus, in quo frustra alii desudant, quasi legerint illi איה, quod אהי nunc est, & vocem קטב κέντρον reddiderint, eo quod apud Ebræos quicquid perfodiendo & pertundendo repen- te penetrat, impetu vehementissimo, ut cuspis acuta solet, nomine illo (ab exscindendo) deducto expri- matur, (quemadmodum Rivetus, cum aliis quibus- dam vult, sed citra exemplum Scripturæ) ac deniq; per דבריך pestes tuæ à דבר verbum deduxerint, uti Aquila & Quinta editio reddidere, ubi sunt sermo- nes tui? vocemque illam per δίκην causam exposue- rint. Drusius novum adhuc εὕρημα habet in parall. p. 116. cur Paulus דבריך verterit per κέντρον, quod nempe legerit דרבנך quum דרבן notet stimulum, vel aculeum baculo infixum ad pungendum bestiam. Sed quis finis erit mutationum textus, si conjecturis ita indulgere fas sit? Longe simplicius est, si sensum expressisse, non verbum verbo reddidisse dicantur LXX. Interpp. eosque sequutum Apostolum, sed ita ut adhuc concinnior prodiret sententia, & verus Prophetæ sensus autoritate Apostolica magis illu- straretur. Nam quod categorice Propheta, id Apo- stolus per figuram interrogationis proposuit. In illo antecedens occurrit, ipsa mortis nempe aboli- tio, hic consequens expressit, ἐπινίκιον seu carmen triumphale, quo post abolitionem mortis trium- phabunt de morte & inferno. Ita ergo insultant morti, & adversus eam gloriantur electi: Evax! Christus nos liberavit à morte & mortis stimulo. Evax! Christus fuit pestes tuæ, ô mors, ubi ergo nunc, ô mors, stimulus tuus? Tu confixisti nos aculeo tuo peccati, instar bestiæ venenatæ, quæ aculeum infigendo letife- rum virus infundit. Sed ubi nunc tuus ille aculeus, siquidem Christus pestis tua facta sit? Infigere illi sti- mulum tuum conata es, sed eo ipso perdidisti eum, il- loque amisso, ipsa periisti. Nam scorpiis, vespis, api- bus, aculeo perdito, est moriendum. Tu inique in hominem justum & innocentem potestatem temera- rie usurpasti. Mortua es, ô mors, & perforata hamo, quem incauta glutisti, uti Bernhardus habet Serm. 26. in Cantic. Illius morte tu mortua es, illius morte nos vivimus. Devorasti, & devorata es, dumque as- sumti corporis Christi solicitans illecebra, & avidis faucibus prædam putas, interiora tua, adunco dente (unco alii) confossa sunt. Gratias tibi, Christe Sal- vator, tua agimus creatura: quod tam potentem ad- versarium nostrum, dum occideret, occidisti, uti san- ctus Hieronymus eleganter in Epitaph. Nepot. ad Heliodor. Ita insultant inferno, & gloriantur ad- versus illum electi: Evax! Christus liberavit nos à manu inferni. Evax! Christus fuit tibi excisio, ô inferne, ubi ergo nunc, ô inferne, victoria tua? Tu sub potestatem tuam nos redegeras & de nobis trium- phabas. Sed ubi nunc tua potestas? ubi nunc tua vi- ctoria? Sub potestatem tuam redigere etiam Chri- stum conatus es: sed ille te devicit, exspoliavit, & de- struxit, nosque è manu tua potenter liberavit. Unde manifestissimum est, suavem in sensu esse consen- sum dicti Prophetici, & ἐπινικίε Apostolici, atque elegantissime illa sese mutuo explicare. Est sane pulcra prosopopœia, inquit B. Lutherus noster loco citato p. 558. qua mors & infernus finguntur hostes humanæ naturæ, terribiles armis suis, aculeo (Deber Keteb) victores, triumphatores, insultatores in æter- num sua victoria, id est, peccato & morbo naturæ, quos Filius Dei per seipsum pro nobis, ut David Go- liath, prostravit, & sustulit in sempiternum, & in victoriam.

Decimo ab autoritate Interpp. Nemo facile in- venitur, qui hoc tam illustre dictum adeo exiliter habuerit, atque Grotius. De Christo vero id accepe- runt Patres orthodoxi magno consensu. Irenæus lib. 5. adv. hæref. c. 13. Tunc juste dicentur hæc: ubi est, mors, aculeus tuus? ubi est mors, victoria tua, quando mortalis hæc & corruptibilis caro, circa quam & mors est, quæ & quodam dominio mortis pressa est, in vitam conscendens induerit incorruptelam, & im- mortalitatem: Tunc enim vere erit victa mors, quan- do ea, quæ continetur ab eo, caro exiverit de dominio ejus. Tertull. l. 5. advers. Marc. c. 10. vocat hoc Pro- phetæ verbum insultatorium de morte, & triumpha- torium. Athanas. de incarn. Verbi T. I. p. m. 80. Ita mortem jam debellatam, & per Salvatorem nostrum Jesum Christum in cruce triumphatam, manibus ejus pedibusque obligatis omnes, qui eam in Christo trans- eunt, pedibus proterunt, martyresque Christo se præben- tes, sannis, ludibriis, convitiis exagitant, objectantes & quæ superius scripta sunt per Apostolum Paulum: Absorpta est mors in victoria: ubi, mors, victoria tua? ubi, orce, stimulus tuus? Stimulus autem mor- tis peccatum est, virtus vero peccati lex. Ergone il- lud exiguum est momentum de imbecillitate mortis? aut parva est demonstratio victoriæ Jesu Christi de morte illius reportatæ? Euseb. Demonstr. Evangel. l. 4. c. 12. p. 166. Ipse vero universi Salvator, ac Do- minus noster, qui Christus est Dei, victoriaque repor- tator dicitur, in Propheticis vaticiniis mortem ob- jurgans inducitur, & animas solvens, quæ illic vin- ctæ detinebantur, ubi victoriæ hymnum pronunciat, ipsa hæc plane dicens: De manu inferni eripiam eos, & a morte liberabo eorum animas: ubi, tua mors, victoria? ubi tuus, mors, stimulus? Cyrillus Ale- xandr. Commentar. in hunc locum sic enarrat hunc textum Tom. 3. Oper. pag. 187. Redemit nos (Christus) de manu inferni, hoc est, de tyran- nide mortis. Et modus redemptionis, Christi mors intelligitur. Libens enim necem pro nobis in ligno per- tulit, & principatus ac potestates, affixo illi contra nos chirographo, triumphavit. Tunc enim, tunc etiam omnis iniquitas oppilavit os suum, & mortis imperi- um, peccato sublato, destructum est. Ipsum enim est mortis victoria, & stimulus inferni. Si enim & sapi- ens Paulus nobis est interpretatus. Ait namque: (sti- mulus mortis peccatum est: virtus autem peccati lex) Quapropter omnium peccato deleto, & nos jure dixerimus: (Ubi est victoria tua, mors? ubi stimu- lus tuus, inferne? Deus enim, qui justificat, quis est, qui condemnet? Christus Jesus, qui mortuus est pro nobis.) Imo qui dedit semetipsum redemptionem pro omnibus, unus dignior omnibus, per quem & in quo divites facti sumus, ut ad incorruptionem redea- mus. Hieronymus in hunc locum: Liberavit omnes Dominus, & redemit in passione crucis, & effusione sanguinis sui: quando anima ejus descendit in infer- num, & caro ejus non vidit corruptionem, & ad ipsam mortem atque infernum locutus est: Ero mors tua, ô mors. Idcirco enim mortuus sum, ut tu mea morte moriaris. Ero morsus tuus, inferne, qui omnes tuis faucibus devorabas. Eundem etiam produximus antea ex Epitaph. Nepot. ad Heliodorum. Quibus adde Augustin. serm. 137. de tempore: Gregorium M. Homil. 22. in Evangelia. Bernardum Serm. 26.

in Cant. Rupert. 6. in Johannem. Petr. Damian. libr. 2. Epist. 18. Haymon. Hugon. Lyran. &c. qui omnes de Christo ad literam intelligunt. Quid quod cum Calviniāni, tum Judæi itidem sensum li- teralem ad Christum pertinere agnoscant: impri- mis Beza in Annot. super N. Testamentum, Junius parallel. l. 2. par. 43. Polanus in Comment. p. 278. Tremellius cum Junio in notis ad hunc locum. Pa- ræus ipse, hyperaspistes Calvini, in Hoseam p. 561. concedit, quod hæc verba sint Christi SALVA- TORIS, & ab Apostolo allegentur, ac principali- ter de Christo, ejusque redemptione spirituali agant, etsi geminum sensum fingat, unum in typo, redem- tione Israëlitarum ex sepulcro captivitatis, alterum perfectiorem in antitypo, Ecclesiæ æterna redem- tione & vindicatione à morte per Christum. De an- titypo, inquit, perfectius intelligendum esse, cogit bene- ficiorum genus hic promissum, minime externum tan- tum, aut metaphoricum, sed æternum & proprium: co- git etiam autoritas Spiritus Sancti in N. T. sic inter- pretantis oraculum. Sed quum sensus ille typicus nullum hic locum habeat, neque διπλότης sensus in eodem loco admittenda sit, superest, ut unice de Christo interpretandum sit oraculum Propheticum. Quod proinde Rivedus agnovit in hoe loco p. 410. Id in Christo fuit impletum, quando morte sua mor- tem devicit, & in sepulchro de potestate ejus trium- phavit: cujus suæ victoriæ efficacia, mortui cum eo & sepulti in novam vitam resurgunt; & in spe cer- tissima vivunt futuræ suæ resurrectionis ad vitam æ- ternam, per eum, qui mortuus est, & resurrexit à mortuis. Est ergo simplex & absoluta promissio ad electos pertinens, de futura salute & redemptione per Christum facienda,ita tamen, ut in liberatione à mor- te & sepulchro synecdochen esse intelligamus, pro libe- ratione ab omnibus electorum inimicis, quorum qui postremo destruitur, est mors, ut ait Paulus, cujus ideo & sepulcri expresse meminit. Hunc sensum con- stat optime facere ad probandam corporum resur- rectionem, ut voluit Paulus, quæ pars est redem- ptionis per Christum, & aptissime subjectam fuisse hanc promissionem gravibus comminationibus, in gratiam piarum reliquiarum, post denunciatum Israëlis exitium, ad eas erigendas & consolatione afficiendas, hac fide nempe electos aliquando à morte servatum iri, etsi totum corpus in communi sit periturum. Acquiescimus ergo sententiæ illo- rum, qui hæc verba esse Christi, morti & sepulcro insultantis censent, quod etsi ex verbis Prophetæ non plane manifestum esse, post Evangelii lucem in du- bium revocari non debet. Non ait simpliciter, libera- bo, sed utitur verbo,quod significat, pretio seu λύτρῳ redemptionis dato, liberare, Ephdem, unde pidion, apud Ebræos sumitur pro pretio, quo quis redimi- tur. Præterea altero verbo Gaal, quod significat jure affinitatis redimere, unde Goël affinis, ad quem pertinebat jus redimendi. Quæ verba satis innuunt Christum loqui, qui pretio dato, & affinitatis initæ nobiscum jure suos redemit à peccato & morte. Esse autem pestem mortis & exitium sepulcri est mor- tem & sepulcrum destruere, ut 1. Cor. 15, 26. exponit Paulus: Novissimus autem hostis aboletur mors. Mors autem non destruitur, nisi per vitam, & mor- tis destructio nil est, quam vitæ restitutio, quemad- modum ibidem docet Paulus. Hæc Rivetus. Coc- cejus, nescio quæ Apocalyptica hic sibi videre vi- sus est, vel potius ollas & cucurbitas lippiit: Mor- tem, inquit, hic vocat Metonymice Pseudo-Prophe- tam auctorem mortis secundæ, ut Apoc. 6, 8. Indigitat enim Bahalem, in quo reus factus erat Juda, & mor- tuus fuerat, Hos. 13, 1. Infernum similiter vocat Re- ges mœchantes cum bestia, & ei potestatem suam dan- tes, Apocal. 17, 13. 17. qui etiam per nomen Inferni notantur Apocal. 6, 8. quia ut inferiores partes terræ (quæ proprie שׁאול infernus, ᾴδης dicuntur) sunt car- cer cadaverum & locus corruptionis, & impedimen- tum vitæ: ita hi reges suis edictis & tyrannide effici- unt, quantumpote, ut homines in morte secunda, odio veritatis, quæ demonstratur in Scriptura, & errori- bus suis perseverent. Modus redimendi eos à manu Mortis & Inferni est ille, quod Deus totam illam gen- tem, malis consiliis utentem, tradidit in manum popu- lorum Barbarorum, Sarracenorum & Turcarum, sub quibus possent, si vellent, utut in angustia, Deum secundum conscientiam suam & doctrinam Scripturæ colere. Redimam ipsos virtute pretii à me per- soluti, & per potentiam magnam & manum vali- dam eos eripiam è manu Mortis & Inferni, ut libe- ri sint ad serviendum mihi. Vindicabo, ut meos, ut redemptos, ut fratres, ne extendatur in ipsos sce- ptrum injustitiæ. Propheta porro verbis Dei subsan- nat Mortem & Infernum, & triumphat de Pestibus & Virulentia utriusque. קטב venenum indomitum & vincens. Apostolus vertit νĩκē 1. Cor. 15, 55. LXX. δίκη, alii νίκη. Symm. ἔσομαι ἡ πληγή σε. Hæc directè & immediate spectant Antichristum, & tyrannos ei sup- parasitantes, quos Spiritus Sanctus irridet, ut frustra- tos spe sua: quum Deus comparaverit potentiam, per quam, licet in afflictione, eripiat magnam partem po- puli ex ipsorum potestate & jugo. S. Paulus 1. Cor. 15, 55. 56. hinc efficit Triumphum Ecclesiæ de morte etiam corporis: & vere, quia nisi mors à Christo pe- nitus victa esset, non ita Propheta huic instrumento Diaboli ad mortem secundam inferendam compara- to insultaret. Hæc Coccejus: è quibus postrema solum, quæ Apostoli sensum referunt, vera sunt, cæ- tera somnia hominis plusquam febrilia resipiunt. E Judæis R. Moses Hadarschan (è R. Josua Ben Le- vi) in Comment. Gen. 24, 6. 7. in Bereschit Rabba, hæc adducit: Ivi cum Kippod Angelo mortis, & ivit mecum Messias filius David usque quo perveni ad por- tas gehennæ: cum autem viderunt captivi, qui sunt in gehenna, lumen, sive lucem Messiæ: fuerunt gau- dentes ad recipiendum eum, dicentes: iste educet nos de hac obscuritate, sicut dictum est Hos. 13, 14. De manu inferni redimam eos. Vide Pug. Fid. Raim. Martini part. 3. Dist. 3. c. 17. p. 680.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. Promised grace and blessing to the penitent.

A Prophetic call to repentance, a formula of supplication, and of the renunciation of trust in men, and idols prescribed: With the sweetest promises of healing, of love, of the dew of grace, that they may flourish, put forth leaves, and give off a sweet scent: that they may be sustained under the shadow of the Lord, and have the reputation of generous wine. Finally, the prudent and the just are proclaimed, in place of a conclusion, who observe these things, whereas on the contrary it is necessary for the prevaricators to fall.

Seek God as a suppliant, conversion will grow green with dew.

Vers. 1.

LET SAMARIA PERISH) The Chaldean perhaps more correctly: Samaria is guilty, namely of grave sins.

BECAUSE SHE HAS PROVOKED TO BITTERNESS HER GOD) As if from מרר: others better from מרה, because she rebelled against the word of God, the Chaldean. LXX. because she has risen against her God.

LET THEM PERISH BY THE SWORD) They shall perish by the sword: a part of them, namely. LXX. he shall fall by the sword. And the Chaldean no differently.

LET THEIR LITTLE ONES BE DASHED) They shall be dashed against the ground or rocks, as happens in a cruel victory, Psalm 137, 8. Homer in such a matter: infant children dashed to the ground in dire conflict.

AND THEIR PREGNANT WOMEN SHALL BE RIPPED OPEN) Her pregnant women shall be ripped open. Histories teach us that this is also sometimes done by victors.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Pœnitentibus promissa gratia & benedictio.

Κέλευσμα Propheticum ad pœnitentiam, for- mula deprecationis, & renunciationis fidu- ciæ in hominibus, & idolis præscripta: Cum dulcissimis promissionibus sanationis, amo- ris, roris gratiæ, ut floreant, frondeant, odo- rem suavem reddant: sub umbra Domini su- stententur, & famam vini generosi habe- ant. Prudentes deniq; ac justi prædicantur, conclusionis loco, qui hæc observant, quum contra prævaricatores ruere oporteat.

Quære Deum supplex, conversio rore virescet.

Vers. 1.

PEREAT SAMARIA) Chaldæus forte rectius: Rea est Samaria, gravium scilicet peccatorum.

QVONIAM AD AMARITVDINEM CONCI- TAVIT DEVM SVVM) Quasi à מרר: melius alii à מרה, quia rebellavit in verbum Dei, Chaldæus. LXX. ὅτι ἀνέστη πρὸς ὸ θεὸν ἀυτῆς.

IN GLADIO PEREANT) In gladio peribunt: pars scilicet eorum. LXX. ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ πεσεῖται αὐτόν. Nec aliter Chaldæus.

PARVVLI EORVM ELIDANTVR) Allidentur folo aut saxis, ut fit in crudeli victoria, Psal. 137, 8. Ho- merus in re tali: νήπια τέκνα Βαλλόμενα ποτὶ γαίῃ ἐν αἰνῇ δηϊοτῆτι.

ET FOETÆ EJVS DISCINDANTVR) Præ- gnantes ejus discindentur. Hoc etiam interdum à victoribus fieri docent nos historiæ.

## 14:1
Verse 2.

RETURN O ISRAEL TO THE LORD THY GOD) Either now after so many evils, in exile. He speaks as if in the present matter, as do other Prophets.

FOR THOU HAST FALLEN BY THINE INIQUITY) For thou seest into how great evils thou hast fallen, through idolatry and other crimes.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CONVERTERE ISRAEL AD DOMINVM DEVM TVVM) Vel nunc post tanta mala, in exilio. Lo- quitur velut in re præsenti, ut & alii Prophetæ.

QVONIAM CORRVISTI IN INIQVITATE TVA) Vides enim in quanta mala incideris, per idolo- latriam & alia crimina.

## 14:2
Verse 3. TAKE WITH YOU WORDS) Bring with you (to God) words, namely ἐξομολογήσεως (of confession), as the Chaldean rightly assumes here.

AND RETURN TO THE LORD) Amend your life.

AND SAY UNTO HIM: TAKE AWAY ALL INIQUITY) That is, these punishments which we feel.

TAKE AWAY THE GOOD) Accept that good which we now do, just as if we had not sinned.

AND WE WILL RENDER THE CALVES OF OUR LIPS) So the Chaldean also reads, not with another vowel point, like the LXX, who said καρπὸν χειλέων (fruit of the lips). It is a very emphatic expression. We cannot in this exile offer thee oxen for a sacred thanksgiving, but instead of oxen we will offer pious words humbly giving thanks.

Latin:

Vers. 3. TOLLITE VOBISCVM VERBA) Afferte vobiscum (ad Deum) verba, nempe ἐξομολογήσεως, ut recte hic sumit Chaldæus.

ET CONVERTIMINI AD DOMINVM) Emen- date vitam.

ET DICITE EI: OMNEM AVFER INIQVI- TATEM) Id est, pœnas has, quas sentimus.

ACCIPE BONVM) Acceptum habe id bonum, quod nunc facimus, plane quasi non peccassemus.

ET REDDEMVS VITVLOS LABIORVM NO- STRORVM) Sic legit & Chaldæus, non cum alio puncto, ut LXX, qui καρπὸν χειλέων dixere. Est locutio μάλα ἐμφατι- κή. Non possumus in hoc exsilio tibi offerre boves in sacrum εὐχαριστικόν, sed pro bobus offeremus pia verba gratias sup- pliciter agentia.

## 14:3
Verse 4. ASSHUR SHALL NOT SAVE US) We shall no longer call the Assyrian our savior, as formerly. 2 Kings 15, 17.

WE WILL NOT RIDE UPON HORSES) We will not implore the help of Egypt, as formerly 2 Kings 17, 4. Egypt is described by its cavalry, in which it was most powerful, Deut. 17, 16. so also Is. 30, 16.

NEITHER WILL WE SAY ANY MORE: OUR GODS ARE THE WORKS OF OUR HANDS) I think the interpreter wrote to the work: for so it is in the Hebrew and Chaldean: the Greeks also have, τοῖς ἔργοις (to the works). We will no longer give the name of God to images.

FOR IN THEE THE FATHERLESS FINDETH MERCY) In the Hebrew: For with thee it is to have mercy on the fatherless. They call those fatherless who neither have strength by themselves, nor have a father who may protect them. Such had the Hebrews formerly been in Egypt, when God had mercy on them. In a like state they expect the same from his goodness.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ASSVR NON SALVABIT NOS) Non am- plius dicemus Assyrium servatorem nostrum, ut olim. 2. Reg. 15, 17.

SVPER EQVVM NON ADSCENDEMVS) Non implorabimus auxilia Ægypti, ut olim 2. Reg. 17, 4. descri- bitur autem Ægyptus ex equitatu, quo maxime pollebat, Deut. 17, 16. sic & Es. 30, 16.

NEC DICEMVS VLTRA: DII NOSTRI OPE- RA MANVVM NOSTRARVM) Puto scripsisse inter- pretem operi: ita enim est in Hebræo & Chaldæo: Græci quoque habent, τοῖς ἔργοις. Non ultra imaginibus dabimus Dei nomen.

QVIA EJVS, QVI IN TE EST MISEREBE- RIS PVPILLI) In Hebræo: Quia penes te est misereri pupil- lorum. Pupillos vocant eos, qui neque per se vires habent, neque patrem habent, qui eos tueatur. Tales olim in Ægypto fuerant Hebræi, cum Deus eorum misertus. Pari in statu eadem ab ipsius bonitate exspectant.

## 14:4
Verse 5.

I WILL HEAL THEIR CONTRITIONS) I will heal their conversions: that is, them converted: if they shall have so turned themselves to straight paths, when they shall have entreated me, I will heal them, that is, I will bring them back from exile.

I WILL LOVE THEM FREELY) In the Hebrew: I will love them liberally: that is, mercifully. Liberality and mercy have much in common, as do debts and sins, therefore the terms pass from one to the other.

FOR MY FURY IS TURNED AWAY FROM THEM) For my fury is turned away from him, supply the people ממנו: but the Eastern Codices had ממני from me: the anger has departed from me.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

SANABO CONTRITIONES EORVM) Sanabo conversiones eorum: id est, ipsos conversos: si ita se conver- terint ad vias rectas, ubi me deprecati fuerint, sanabo eos, id est, reducam eos ab exilio.

DILIGAM EOS SPONTANEE) In Hebræo: Di- ligam eos liberaliter: id est, clementer. Multum simile habent liberalitas & clementia, ut debita & peccata, Ideo ex vicino transeunt vocabula.

QVIA AVERSVS EST FVROR MEVS AB EIS) Quia aversus est furor meus ab eo, supple populo ממנו: at Orientis Codices habuerunt ממני à me: abiit à me ira.

## 14:5
Verse 6.

I WILL BE AS THE DEW TO ISRAEL) I think the interpreter wrote, I will be as the dew to Israel: for the Hebrew text has it so, and the Chaldean no otherwise. The LXX also, ἔσομαι ὡς δρόσος τῷ Ἰσραήλ, I will cause that all things may flourish for them; as fields bedewed, Gen. 27, 39. Is. 26, 19. Mic. 5, 7.

IT SHALL BUD, AS THE LILY) It shall rise up, as the lily: for פרח is translated by ἀνατίλλειν. Also by ἐξανθεῖν, Ezek. 7, 10.

AND HIS ROOT SHALL BREAK FORTH, AS OF LIBANUS) It shall cast roots, as (the trees of) Libanus. βαλεῖ τὰς ῥίζας, that is, he shall be placed in a firm place.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ERO QVASI ROS ISRAEL) Puto scripsisse in- terpretem, Ero quasi ros Israeli: nam sic habet textus He- bræus, nec aliter Chaldæus. LXX. quoque, ἔσομαι ὡς δρόσος τῷ Ἰσραήλ, Faciam, ut omnia eis floreant; ut agri irrorati, Gen. 27, 39. Es. 26, 19. Mich. 5, 7.

GERMINABIT, SICVT LILIVM) Assurget, sicut lilium: nam פרח per ἀνατίλλειν vertitur. Etiam per ἐξαν- θεῖν, Ezech. 7, 10.

ET ERVMPET RADIX EJVS, VT LIBANI) Iaciet radices, ut (arbores) Libani. βαλεῖ τὰς ῥίζας, id est, erit in firmo loco positus.

## 14:6
Verse 7. HIS BRANCHES SHALL GO) That is, they shall spread themselves wide. By branches he understands offspring.

AND HIS GLORY SHALL BE AS THE OLIVE TREE) Which abounds both in leaves and in fruits, Ps. 52, 10. זית signifies an olive. Ammianus 22. Having declared from thence we came to the place Zaita, which is interpreted as the olive tree. It is called thus both as fruit and oil by the Arabs: nor did the Chaldean understand it otherwise here: for he translates: Their splendor, as the splendor of a lamp in the Temple.

AND HIS SMELL, AS OF LIBANUS) You would translate more correctly: as of incense: for לבנון signifies both, as Jerome noted here, and the mention of the mountain has already preceded, and incense better suits the smell: and thus the Chaldean understood it. The sense is: he shall be gracious among all. Thus, on the contrary, those who are in hatred are said to stink. Gen. 34, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 7. IBVNT RAMI EJVS) Id est, late se spar- gent. Per ramos progeniem intelligit.

ET ERIT QVASI OLIVA GLORIA EJVS) Quæ & frondibus abundat, & fructibus, Ps. 52, 10. זית olivam significat. Ammianus 22. Professi exinde Zaitam venimus lo- cum, qui olea arbor interpretatur. Vocatur sic & fructus & oleum Arabibus: nec aliter hic cepit Chaldæus: vertit enim: Splendor eorum, velut splendor lychni in Templo.

ET ODOR EJVS, VT LIBANI) Rectius vertas: ut thuris: nam לבנון uttumque significat, ut hic notavit Hieronymus, & montis mentio jam præcessit, & odori me- lius congruit thus: & sic accepit Chaldæus. Sensus est: gra- tiosus erit apud omnes. Sic contra fœtere dicuntur, qui in odio sunt. Gen. 34, 30.

## 14:7
Verse 8.

THEY SHALL RETURN WHO SIT IN HIS SHADOW) Many foreigners, such as the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites, will live under their protection and will be converted to the true God.

THEY SHALL LIVE BY THE WHEAT) They will revive themselves like wheat. Wheat buried in the ground sprouts: so they will lift themselves up out of calamities. The Rabbis refer these and the following things to the time between the two resurrections. Kimchi, connecting these to the following, says that at that time grain will be sown only once, for all time, just as vines are.

THEY SHALL BLOSSOM AS THE VINE) The women will be fruitful, Ps. 128:3.

HIS MEMORIAL, LIKE THE WINE OF LEBANON) Their name will be sweet to all. Or, it will sound like the blast of a trumpet when new wine is poured out in the Temple. Thus the Chaldean here. Pliny places the Berytian and Tyrian among the noble wines, because they were imported from there. Near Lebanon was a city called Ampelœssa by the Greeks because of the excellence of its wine. Plin. 5, 17.

Grotius understands nothing but earthly and bodily things: the return from exile, the stability of the place in v. 6, the progeny spreading itself far and wide in v. 7, the fruitfulness of women, and the sweetness of the name in verse 8. He is undoubtedly seduced by the Jews, concerning whom the Blessed Luther says here on fol. 552: What the Prophet had said earlier simply and without figure, he here says figuratively, and proposes as if in a picture a description of the Church, believing in Christ, what it is like before God, and with what gifts it is adorned. The Jews also acknowledge that these things are said about the time of the Messiah. Therefore, when they hear the likenesses of bodily things proposed, they expect the comforts of this life from the Messiah, and they think that when he comes, he will adorn his people with bodily blessing, so that just as a rose blooms, or a tree that has taken deep roots and spread its branches, it is not only pleasant to look at, but also firm against the force of winds and storms: so the Jews will be an object of admiration to all nations throughout the whole world, and they alone will rule everywhere. They do not even dream of the remission of sins, the gift of the Holy Spirit, and eternal life. This blindness arises from the fact that, first, as Christ objects to them in Matthew 22, they do not know whose son the Messiah is. For they think he is only the son of David, and therefore, as if from a man, they expect nothing but human and temporal things. Furthermore, they do not see that this nature is so vitiated by sin that it cannot of itself evolve out of the wrath and judgment of God. For if they were to establish this, they would look around for outside help, which now in that blindness of theirs, when it is offered by the Son of God, they so securely neglect. They forget, therefore, that sentiment which the Prophet proposed a little earlier, when he compares the Church to an orphan, which is both pressed in the world in various ways and has no strength against those most grievous enemies, Satan, sin, and death. Because the Jews do not see this, it is no wonder if they are intent only on temporal comforts and do not even see the shadow of these promises. We have been more rightly instructed; we know that man through sin fell into the wrath of God and eternal death, but that God, having pity on us, sent his Son, who would not, as the Kings of the world are wont to do, take care of bodies and possessions, but would bring to us the remission of sins, and reconcile us with the Father, and deliver us from eternal death and all the tyranny of Satan, just as the Prophet said a little earlier, that God would heal the aversion of those who are converted, and would love them, and would turn his wrath away from them. These are those good things in which the Church rejoices and gives thanks to God; but the blind Jews do not see them at all, and therefore they are most ungrateful toward God. And indeed, the better part of the Interpreters unanimously establishes that these promises are spiritual. Although we would not wish the promises of bodily benefits to be excluded, since the abundance of them is promised to the faithful under these images; yet they are primarily intended to foreshadow spiritual things. Because as the penitent had asked for divine benefits before, and had promised their own duties, so God now promises that he will liberally grant the benefits and will hold those duties as pleasing. They had asked for both negative grace, or the removal of sins, 'take away all iniquity': and positive grace: 'receive or show good' (cf. the reason for the phrase in Ps. 68:19, Eph. 4:8), by which name they sought primarily whatever pertains to spiritual happiness. And therefore, the divine promises respond to these petitions of the penitent. (2) Because God promises the healing of rebellion. Grotius renders this wrongly and too dryly: 'I will heal their conversion,' that is, the converted themselves. 'I will heal,' that is, I will bring back. For where is 'bringing back' called 'healing'? And why should one not adhere to the letter? 'I will heal their rebellion or aversion.' For that is what משובתם denotes, which is a healing not of the body, but of the soul, and it responds to the first petition, 'take away iniquity.' Compare 2 Chron. 30:20, Is. 6:10, Ps. 103:3. The Jews themselves acknowledge that it is a matter of the healing of defection: which God is said to heal, because what a disease is in the body, rebellion is in the soul, as Aben-Ezra holds. In the book Yoma, distinction Yom ha-Kippurim, these things are read: It is a tradition that R. Meier said: Great is repentance: for on account of one person who performs repentance, they will absolve the whole world, as it is said in Hos. 14:5, 'I will heal their aversion.' (3) He promises gratuitous love: I will love them spontaneously, which is the special love of the faithful, because it is promised to the penitent, and it embraces the good which God exhibits to the faithful, and which they were praying for, and that primarily spiritual, Eph. 1:6. (4) He promises, moreover, the turning away of wrath. My fury is turned away from them. The past tense is used for the future, on account of certainty: he turns away wrath, however, so that he may turn his grace toward them, primarily in exhibiting spiritual benefits.

Here Grotius again invents a different reading, which Capellus himself did not observe, even though he wished to be seen to seek out different readings more than others. The Codices of the East, he says, had ממני from me; my wrath has departed from me. But what solid evidence is there of a different reading?

(5) He promises his grace with an elegant similitude: I will be as the dew to Israel. Which certainly cannot be restricted to bodily benefits alone, and is not even restricted by the Jews themselves, who make the Messiah the one speaking these things, as Raimundus Martini observed from them in Pugio Fidei, page 526. Jonathan renders it: My word shall be as the dew to Israel. Just as dew moistens, cools, nourishes, invigorates, and promotes parched meadows, gardens, and dry crops, and provides material for honey, manna, and pearls, as attested by Pliny, book 5, chapter 16, and book 9, chapter 35. So God recreates, sustains, nourishes, and leads to maturity the hearts of men, which wither and languish from the squalor of sin and the heat of wrath and punishments, and at the same time generates in us honey and pearls, that is, true faith, charity, hope, and patience.

(6) The similitudes by which he adumbrates various goods are too illustrious to be restricted to the bodily goods of Israel alone. Israel is compared indeed (1) to a rose, or a flowering lily: He shall blossom as the lily, by which similitude the Church is depicted in Cant. 2:2, inasmuch as it is truly a flowering rose by reason of color, odor, fecundity, and utility, because it recreates the fallen and strengthens the languishing. But if one prefers with R. David Kimchi to render by lily what is called שושן from the number of six leaves, and which grows in valleys, likewise the great decor, good odor, true humility, and wondrous beauty of the Church are conveniently signified. See Matt. 6:28, 29. (2) to trees deeply rooted: AND HE SHALL CAST, he shall fix or SHALL PROPAGATE his roots, like Lebanon. Luther: His roots shall strike out, like Lebanon. The Church is truly πολυκαρπος [fruitful], Col. 1, 6. Luke 8, 8. 15. (3.) With branches spread here and there. Which Grotius, with Danaeus, snatches away to the multiplication of offspring, but this often happens to the impious. Blessed Meisner wishes to be noted by that simile the double increments of the Church: by reason of quantity, because it is ample like spreading branches, Ps. 72, 8. 80, 10; and by reason of quality, or regarding the gifts of the Holy Spirit, in respect of which it presently progresses.

2 Cor. 4, 16. (4) Like the ever-green olive. And his beauty shall be as the beauty of the olive, which is celebrated as fruit-bearing, peaceful, beautiful, fragrant, and decorous, perpetually flourishing. Cf. Lev. 23, 40. Sir. 50, 14. By which picture likewise the just are shadowed forth, Ps. 1, 3 and 52, 9. (5) Like the odoriferous trees of Lebanon. His odor shall be as Lebanon, in which are many cedars, most fragrant, and frankincense breathing forth a sweet odor. Thus is figured primarily the odor of true doctrine, 2 Cor. 2, 14, and the odor of unfeigned holiness, Rom. 1, 8. Phil. 4, 18. (6) Sitting in the shadow, which is provided by the leafy tree. They shall return to dwell in his shadow. Blessed Luther: They shall again sit under his shadow. Grotius refers these to others, not to Israel, i.e., THEY SHALL BE CONVERTED SITTING IN HIS SHADOW: Many foreigners, such as Ammonites, Moabites, Idumeans, will live under their protection and will be converted to the true God. THEY SHALL LIVE BY WHEAT. They shall quicken themselves, as wheat. Wheat buried in the ground springs up: so they shall raise themselves up from calamities. He adds the dreams of the Rabbis: The Rabbis refer these and the following to the time between the two resurrections. Kimchi, connecting these to the following, says that at that time grain will be sown only once, for all time, just as vines. We dismiss those Jewish commentaries. But as for that conversion, it seems rather to be thrust into the text than deduced from the text. For nothing is held therein about Ammonites, Moabites, or Idumeans. The gloss itself is also forced; They shall live by wheat, that is, they shall quicken themselves, as wheat. If one does not wish to refer the pronoun HIS to the MESSIAH with the Chaldean, under whose shadow, as of a tree and tree of life, we are safe from the heat of divine wrath and are sweetly refreshed, one can refer it to the preceding noun, so that this colon may be rendered: They shall be refreshed (as those) sitting under the shadow of Lebanon: because the word ישוב sometimes denotes to be refreshed, Ps. 19, 8. Lam. 1, 19. Or with Schindler, Piscator, Moller, Tarnovius: they shall return to themselves, (they shall refresh themselves) sitting in his shadow, namely God's, from verse 1 and 2. (7) Eating wheat. They shall revive with wheat. For although the verb יחיו is in Piel, it can nevertheless be rendered here intransitively, they shall revive, or they shall be refreshed with wheat, the Word of God, the spiritual food of the soul, which is compared to wheat by reason of purity, nutrition, exhilaration, and recreation. (8) To the flourishing vine: It shall germinate like a vine, as the Vulgate and LXX have: or they shall flourish like vines, as it is in the Hebrew. In Lebanon near Antioch, almost as far as Sidon, most choice vines flourished, beautiful in appearance, pleasant in odor, most green with tendrils, and most fertile with flowers and grapes. Such vines are all the pious and faithful. See John 15, 1. And at Antioch the name of Christians first began, by which the faithful were distinguished under the New Testament, who were formerly called Israelites under the Old. Grotius snatches it away to the fecundity of women. But that is common to both the pious and the impious. Here, however, the benefits proper to the faithful are recounted. (9) Most generous wine of Lebanon. His memory (that is, of each of them) as the wine of Lebanon, or Lebanon, that is, as Ps. 112, 6 speaks: the just shall be in everlasting remembrance. Compare Sir. 49, 1. Those things about the sound and clangor of the trumpet, when new wine is poured out, are too forced. Nor does the metaphrase of Piscator, Pareus, and others fit, his odor as the wine of Lebanon: for זכר properly denotes memory, not odor, and it would thus be a tautology, because it was already spoken of the odor in verse 6. Therefore the LXX Interpreters, the Vulgate, and Blessed Luther interpret it as memory. How the celebrity of the Church is compared to the wine of Lebanon, which, as Asaph the physician testifies in Drusius on this passage, page 199, was most noble, because of the generosity of its color, the fragrance of its odor, the sweetness of its taste, the excellence of its effect, and its long duration, Blessed Meisner teaches here. Thus, therefore, by nine most pleasant metaphors, the highest dignity of the Church of Christ and its most excellent state is promised and depicted, such as it is not before the world, but before God, not in the flesh, but in the spirit, not according to the external schema on earth, but according to internal glory, consisting in spiritual gifts, all of which are to be opposed to calamities and worldly contempt in place of solace. For the Church is 1. fruitful like a rose. 2. firm, as a rooted tree. 3. ample, like branches. 4. beautiful, as an olive. 5. celebrated, as the cedars of Lebanon. 6. safe, as one sitting in the shadow. 7. alive and vigorous, as one satisfied with wheat. 8. flourishing, as a vine. 9. generous, as the wine of Lebanon. These are from Blessed Meisner. Which Blessed Luther magnificently executes according to his eloquence. The interpreters easily agree on this, that spiritual goods primarily promised to the Church and the faithful are shadowed forth here. Let Grotius therefore retain carnal things with his Jews. To which is added (7) and finally, that those promises were not fulfilled in the Israelites: for they were never led back into their homeland; but they are fulfilled in the faithful, who never cease to perceive their power. Although, therefore, it can be admitted that Israel, or the Ephraimites, is particularly addressed here, and excited to repentance, so that, with the kingdom of Samaria perishing, which the Lord had threatened, some remnants might be saved: yet let us think that we are all excited in their person, because the promises are made to all who will truly be converted to the Lord, and they pertain primarily to the times of the New Testament, and in them they have been more fully fulfilled: just as the Apostle applies certain things from verse 2 to his own time, Heb. 13, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

CONVERTENTVR SEDENTES IN VMBRA EJVS ) Multi extranei , ut Ammonitæ, Moabitæ, Idu- mæi , sub eorum præsidio vivent, & ad Deum verum con- vertentur.

VIVENT TRITICO ) Vivificabunt se ut triticum. Triticum humo obrutum enascitur : ita ipsi ex calamitati- bus se attollent. Rabbini hæc & sequentia ad tempus in- ter duas resurrectiones referunt. Kimchi, hæc sequentibus annectens, ait, eo tempore frumentum semel tantum satum iri, pro omni tempore, quomodo vites.

GERMINABVNT QVASI VINEA ) Fœminæ erunt fœcundæ, Pf. 128, 3.

MEMORIALE EJVS, SICVT VINVM LIBANI) Nomen eorum suave erit omnibus. Aut, ita sonabit, ut clangor tubæ, cum in Templo libatur vinum novum. Ita hic Chaldæus. Inter nobilia vina Berytium & Tyrium ponit Plinius, quod inde advectarentur. Ad Libanum erat urbs Græcis Ampelœssa dicta ob vini præstantiam. Plin. 5,17.

NIl sapit Grotius, nisi terrena & corporalia, re- ductionem ab exilio, loci stabilitatem v. 6. pro- geniem se late spargentem v. 7. fœminarum fœcundi- tatem, & nominis suavitatem vers. 8. Seductus fine dubio à Judæis, de quibus Beatus Lutherus hic fol. 552. Quod Propheta prius simpliciter & sine figura dixerat, hic figurate dicet, & tanquam in pictura pro- ponit descriptionem Ecclesiæ, credentis in Christum, qualis sit coram Deo, & quibus donis ornata. Agno- scunt Judæi quoque hæc dici de tempore Messiæ. Itaque cum audiunt proponi similitudines corporalium re- rum, expectant à Messia hujus vitæ commoda, & pu- tant, cum veniet, corporali benedictione or naturum populum suum, ut sicut rosa floret, sicut arbor, quæ al- te radices egit, & diffudit ramos, non solum aspectu jucunda, sed etiam contra ventorum & tempestatis vim firma est: Ita Judæos in toto orbe terrarum ad- mirationi futuros omnibus gentibus, & solos domina- turos ubique. De peccatorum remissione, de Spiritus Sancti dono, & vita æterna ne somniant quidem. Hæc cæcitas inde nascitur, quod primum, sicut Christus Matth. 22. eis objicit, nesciunt, cujus filius Messias sit. Putant enim, eum tantum Davidis filium, itaque tanquam ab homine nihil nisi humana & temporalia expectant. Deinde non vident naturam hanc peccato sic vitiatam, ut non possit ipsa ex ira & judicio Dei se evolvere. Hoc enim si statuerent, circumspicerent de alieno auxilio, quod nunc in ista cæcitate, cum offer- tur à Filio Dei, tam secure negligunt. Obliviscuntur igitur ejus sententiæ, quam paulo ante Propheta pro- posuit, cum comparat Ecclesiam pupillo, quod & pre- mitur in mundo varie, & nihil habet virium contra gravissimos illos hostes, Satanam, peccatum & mor- tem. Hoc quia non vident Judæi, nihil mirum est, si tantum in temporalia commoda sunt intenti, & ne quidem umbram harum promissionum vident. Nos rectius eruditi sumus, scimus hominem per peccatum incidisse in iram Dei & æternam mortem, Deum au- tem, misertum nostri, misisse Filium, qui non, ut solent Reges mundi, corporum & facultatum curam gere- ret, sed afferret ad nos remissionem peccatorum, & reconciliaret nos cum Patre, ac ab æterna morte & omni Satanæ tyrannide nos liberaret, sicut Propheta paulo ante dixit, Deum sanaturum aversionem eo- rum, qui convertuntur, & dilecturum eos, & aver- surum ab eis iram suam. Hæc illa bona sunt, quibus Ecclesia gaudet, & Deo agit gratias; Cæci autem Ju- dæi ea prorsus non vident, & ideo in Deum sunt in- gratissimi. Et sane promissiones istas spirituales esse, melior pars Interpretum ὁμοθυμαδὸν statuit. Quanquam non exclusas promissiones corpora- lium beneficiorum cupiamus, cum sub istis ima- ginibus earum ubertas fidelibus promissa sit; præ- cipue tamen adumbrata iisdem sunt spiritualia. Quia ut petierant antea pœnitentes beneficia divi- na, ac promiserant sua officia, ita Deus nunc pro- mittit se beneficia liberaliter concessurum, & offi- cia ista grata habiturum. Petierant autem tum gra- tiam privativam, vel peccatorum remotionem, omnem iniquitatem aufer: tum gratiam positivam: accipe vel exhibe bonum, (conf. ratione phraseos Psal. 68, 19. Eph. 4, 8.) quo nomine imprimis, quic- quid ad spiritualem felicitatem pertinet, ambie- runt. Ideoq; his petitionibus pœnitentium respon- dent promissiones divinæ. (2) Quia pollicetur Deus fanationem rebellionis. Perperam hoc reddit Grotius, & jejune nimis: Sanabo conversionem eo- rum, id est, ipsos conversos. Sanabo, id est, reducam. Ubi enim reductio sanatio dicitur? Et cur non in- hærendum literæ? Sanabo rebellionem, vel aversio- nem eorum. ID notat enim משובתם, Quæ est sana- tio non corporis, sed animæ, & respondet primæ petitioni, aufer iniquitatem. Confer 2. Par. 30, 20. Es. 6, 10. Ps. 103, 3. Agnoscunt ipsimet Judæi, de sa- natione defectionis agi: quam sanare dicitur Deus, quia quod morbus est in corpore, rebellio est in a- nima, uti Aben-Ezra habet. In libro Jomma, di- stinct. Jom hakippurim hæc leguntur: Traditio est, quod R. Meier dixit: Magna est pœnitentia: propter unicum namque, qui agit pœnitentiam, absolvent uni- versum mundum, sicut dictum est Os. 14, 5. Sanabo aversionem eorum. (3) Pollicetur gratuitam dile- ctionem: diligam eos spontanee, quæ est dilectio spe- cialis fidelium, quia promittitur pœnitentibus, & complectitur bonum, quod exhibet Deus fidelibus, quodque illi precabantur, idque imprimis spiri- tuale Ephes. 1, 6. (4) Pollicetur insuper iræ aversio- nem. Aversus est furor meus ab eis. Præteritum ad- hibetur pro futuro, ob certitudinem: avertit autem iram, ut gratiam suam advertat, imprimis in exhi- bendis beneficiis spiritualibus.

Fingit hic iterum Grotius diversam lectionem, quam Capellus ipse non observavit, etsi diversas le- ctiones præ aliis videri voluerit conquirere. Orien- tis Codices, inquit, habuerunt ממני à me; abiit à me ira. Sed quodnam solidum documentum diversæ lectionis?

(5) Promittit gratiam suam eleganti similitudi- ne: Ego ero quasi ros Israëli. Quæ certe ad sola cor- poralia beneficia restringi nequit, ac ne ab ipsis qui- dem Judæis restringitur, qui hæc loquentem faci- unt Messiam, ut observavit ex iisdem Raimundus Martini Pug. fidei pag. 526. Jonathan reddit: Erit verbum meum, sicut ros Israëli. Quemadmodum ros prata arentia, hortos, ac segetes siccas hume- ctat, refrigerat, nutrit, vegetat, promovet, mate- riam præbet melli, mannæ & margaritis, teste Pli- nio lib. 5. cap. 16. lib. 9. cap. 35. Sic Deus corda ho- minum, quæ squalore peccati, & æstu iræ, pœna- rumque flaccescunt & languent, gratia sua recreat, substentat, nutrit, ad maturitatem perducit, simulq; generat in nobis mel & margaritas, id est, veram fidem, charitatem, spem & patientiam.

(6) Similia, quibus varia bona adumbrat, illu- striora sunt, quam ut restringi ea possint ad corpo- ralia solum Israëlis bona. Comparatur vero Israël (1) rosæ, vel lilio florenti: Germinabit, ut lilium, qua similitudine Ecclesia depingitur Cant. 2, 2. utpote quæ vere rosa florens est ratione coloris, odoris, fœ- cunditatis & utilitatis, quia recreat lapsos, & con- fortat languentes. Si autem malis cum R. David. Kimchi per lilium reddere, quod à numero sex fo- liorum שושן vocatur, & in vallibus crescit, iti- dem Ecclesiæ magnus decor, bonus odor, vera hu- militas, & mira venustas commode significatur. Vide Matth. 6, 28. 29. (2) arboribus profunde ra- dicatis: ET JACIET, figet vel PROPAGABIT radices suas, tanquam Libanus. Lutherus: Seine Wurtzeln sollen ausschlagen, wie Libanon. Ecclesia vere est πολυκαρπος, Col. 1, 6. Luc. 8, 8. 15. (3.) Ra- mis hac illac dilatis. Quod Grotius cum Danao ad prolis multiplicationem abripit, sed hæc sæpe impiis obtingit. B. Meisnerus similitudine illa notari vult duplicia Ecclesiæ incrementa, ratione quantitatis, quod sit ampla instar ramorum excurrentium Psal. 72, 8. 80, 10. & ratione qualitatis, vel quoad dona Spiritus Sancti, quorum respectu subinde proficit

2. Cor. 4, 16. (4) Olea semper virenti. Eritque decus ejus, ut decus olivæ, quæ ceu frugifera, pacifica, pul- cra, odora, decora, perpetuo florida celebratur. Conf. Lev. 23, 40. Syr. 50, 14. Qua pictura itidem justi adumbrantur Psal. 1, 3. & 52, 9. (5) Odoriferis Libani arboribus. Erit odor ejus, ut Libani, in quo multæ Cedri maxime odoratæ, & thura odorem suavem spirantia. Figuratur ita imprimis odor veræ doctrinæ 2. Cor. 2, 14. & odor sanctitatis infucatæ Rom. 1, 8. Phil. 4, 18. (6) Sedentibus in umbra, quæ ab arbore frondosa præbetur. Revertentur habita- turi in umbra ejus. B. Luherus: Sie sollen wieder unter seinem Schatten sitzen. Grotius hæc ad alios refert, non ad Israëlem, h. m. CONVERTEN- TUR SEDENTES IN UMBRA EJUS: Multi extranei, ut Ammonitæ, Moabitæ, Idumæi sub eorum præsidio vivent, & ad Deum verum conver- tentur. VIVENT TRITICO. Vivificabunt se, ut triticum. Triticum humo obrutum enascitur: ita ipsi ex calamitatibus se attollent. Addit Rabbino- rum somnia: Rabbini hæc, & sequentia ad tem- pus inter duas resurrectiones referuntur. Kimchi, hæc sequentibus annectens, ait, eo tempore frumentum semel tantum satum iri, pro omni tempore, quomo- do vites. Mittimus commenta illa Judaica. Illam autem conversionem quod attinet, ingeri potius videtur in textum, quam è textu deduci. Nihil e- nim de Ammonitis, Moabitis, Idumæis inibi ha- betur. Contorta est etiam ipsa glossa; Vivent triti- co, id est, vivificabunt se, ut triticum. Si pronomen EJUS quis ad MESSIAM referre cum Chaldæo nolit, sub cujus umbra, ceu ligni & arboris vitæ, tu- ti sumus ab æstu iræ divinæ, & suaviter reficimur, ad præcedens nomen referre potest, ut ita redda- tur hoc colon: Reficientur (velut) sedentes sub um- bra Libani: quia verbum ישוב notat quandoque re- creari Psal. 19, 8. Thren. 1, 19. Vel cum Schindlero, Piscatore, Mollero, Tarnovio: redibunt ad se, (re- creabunt se) sedentes in umbra ejus, Dei scilicet, ex versu 1. & 2. (7) Comedentibus triticum. Revivi- scent tritico. Etsi enim verbum יחיו in Piel sit, potest tamen hic intransitive reddi, revivifcent, vel refi- cientur tritico, Verbo Dei, pabulo animæ spirituali, quod tritico ratione puritatis, nutritionis, exhila- rationis, & recreationis confertur. (8) Viti efflore- scenti: Germinabit quasi vinea, uti Vulg. & LXX. habent: vel florebunt quasi vites, ut in Ebræo est. In Libano juxta Antiochiam fere usque ad Sidonem electissimæ vites effloruerunt, aspectu pulcræ, odo- re gratæ, pampinis viridissimæ, floribus & uvis fer- tilissimæ. Tales vites sunt omnes pii & fideles. Vi- de Johan. 15, 1. Et Antiochia cœpit primo nomen Christianorum, quo fideles insigniti sunt sub No- vo Testamento, qui olim sub Veteri Israëlitæ vo- cabantur. Grotius ad fœminarum fœcunditatem abripit. Sed ea communis & piis & impiis. Hic ve- ro beneficia fidelium propria recensentur. (9) Ge- nerosissimo vino Libani. Memoria ejus (id est, cujus- que eorum) ut vinum Libani, seu Libanum, hoc est, ut Psal. 112, 6. loquitur: in memoria perpetua erit justus. Confer Syr. 49, 1. Illa de sono & clango- re tubæ, cum libatur vinum novum, nimis contorta sunt. Neque convenit Piscatoris, Parei, & aliorum metaphrasis, odor ejus, ut vinum Libani: Nain זכר proprie notat memoriam, non odorem, & tavto- logia ita foret, quia de odore jam vers. 6. dictum. Ideo LXX. Interpretes, Vulgatus, & Beatus Lu- therus de memoria interpretantur. Quomodo Ecclesiæ celebritas vino Libani, quod teste Asa- pho medico apud Drusium in h. l. pag. 199. nobilis- simum fuit, comparetur ob generositatem coloris, odo- ris fragrantiam, saporis suavitatem, effectus præstan- tiam, & diuturnam durationem, docet hic B. Meis- nerus. Ita ergo novem metaphoris jucundissimis promissa & depicta est summa Ecclesiæ Christi di- gnitas, & status præstantissimus, qualis nempe est non coram mundo, sed coram Deo, non in carne, sed in spiritu, non juxta externum schema in terris, sed juxta internam gloriam, consistentem in donis spiritualibus, quæ omnia calamitatibus & contem- tui mundano solatii loco opponenda sunt. Est e- nim Ecclesia 1. fœcunda instar rosæ. 2. firma, ut radicata arbor. 3. ampla, instar ramorum. 4. for- mosa, ut olea. 5. celebris, ut cedri Libani. 6. tuta, ut sedens in umbra. 7. viva, & vegeta, ut saturatus tritico. 8. florida, ut vitis. 9. generosa, ut vinum Libani. Hæc Beat. Meisnerus. Quæ magnifice pro facundia sua exequitur Beat. Lutherus. Ex consen- tiunt facile in eo Interpp. hic spiritualia imprimis bona, Ecclesiæ & fidelibus promissa, adumbrari. Retineat ergo Grotius cum Judæis suis carnalia. Quibus accedit (7) & postremo, quod comple- tæ non fuerint promissiones illæ in Israëlitis: nam isti nunquam reducti sunt in patriam; sed com- plentur in fidelibus, qui earum vim nunquam non percipiunt. Etsi ergo admitti possit, peculiariter hic compellari Israëlem, vel Ephraimitas, & ad pœ- nitentiam excitari, ut, pereunte Samaria regno, quod comminatus erat Dominus, reliquiæ non- nullæ salventur: in eorum tamen persona excitari nos omnes cogitemus, quia promissiones omni- bus fiunt, qui vere ad Dominum convertentur, & imprimus ad Novi Testamenti tempora pertinent, inque iisdem plenius adimpletæ sunt: quomodo Apostolus quædam ex vers. 2. suo tempori appli- cat Ebr. 13, 15.

## 14:8
Verse 9. EPHRAIM, WHAT HAVE I TO DO ANY MORE WITH IDOLS?)

In the Hebrew: to idols, supply, does he run? Since things are so, why do the Ephraimites still worship idols? Why do they not depart from them?

I WILL HEAR) Idols do not hear, much less do they answer.

AND I WILL DIRECT HIM, LIKE A GREEN FIR TREE)

EX ME ERUCTUS TUUS INVENTUS EST) With me there has always been a reward for your work.

It is more correct to understand the word 'will say' with Ephraim, than the ellipsis the Chaldean supplied, as also Drusius, Piscator, Paræus, Tarnovius: what is there for me further regarding idols, or with idols? But I (your God) have answered, or I will surely hear you (the past tense for the future). I will look upon him (I will observe him with intent eyes, which the Hebrew שור implies. The Chaldean: I will have mercy on him in my word.) I, like a green fir tree, (will be to him) which blooms perpetually, and provides a most grateful …shade to the traveler in the heat. And your fruit is found, or will be found. God promises not only the shade of protection, but also fruit and abundant blessing. Let our interpreters, the blessed Meisner and Tarnovius, be compared. The blessed Gefner attributes all these words only to God in this way: O Ephraim, what do you boast of your idols to me any longer? From me you have benefits of every kind, the sum of which is contained in these three: in the fatherly and free hearing of prayers in calamities, in protection and governance, in fruitfulness. Vers. 10. WHO IS WISE AND UNDERSTANDS THESE THINGS? THE INTELLIGENT ONE SHALL KNOW THEM?) He shows that there will be few in the ten tribes who will consider these things as they ought. He said the same thing twice in the Hebrew manner. FOR THE WAYS OF THE LORD ARE RIGHT) The counsels and decrees of God are meanwhile most equitable. AND THE JUST SHALL WALK IN THEM) Through them the just shall proceed with an unoffending foot. BUT THE TRANSGRESSORS SHALL FALL IN THEM) They will fall into all the evils already mentioned before from these same decrees. This final epiphonema regards not only the ten tribes, but all in general: since these promises were made to all the faithful and those performing true repentance, and this is held here not so much as a comminatory decree or a complaint of the Prophet, but rather as a singular wish of the Prophet, who desires that all might understand these things with reason, as Rivetus and Tarnovius rightly say on this passage: Who is wise, let him understand these things; who is intelligent, let him acknowledge these things. A similar exhortation may be seen in James 3:15. Conf. Deut. 32:29. The Prophet adds, however, a triple argument: the first from the adjunct of this Prophetic doctrine, because the ways of the Lord are right, i.e., most equitable, most just, indeed the rules of all equity, justice, and rectitude. The second from example: And the just shall walk in them. Conf. Col. 1:6, Isa. 33:15. The third from the contrary effect by accident in the impious and wicked. But the defectors or transgressors shall fall in them. If, however, it pleases you to say that only a single reason is properly brought forward, from the certainty of the ways of the Lord, you would most rightly say that the final sentence is added in place of a conclusion, like an epiphonema, or aphorism, and a final Maxim, leaving behind a singular stimulus. For those who are justified through faith delight to walk in the ways of the Lord: they shall walk confidently, prosperously, and happily. (Conf. Jud. 5:3, Mal. 4:2) and thus they shall attain the end of faith, the salvation of the soul. Conf. Syr. 39:30. But transgressors stumble in them, and fall, and perish eternally. Whence Rabbi Solomon Jarchi explains the particle ב with the Chaldean, they shall fall because of them, they shall be delivered to Gehenna, for the reason that they did not walk in them. Thus, therefore, this is not an imprecation, as Junius and Tremellius wish, whom Piscator himself refutes, nor a simple prophecy, but an indicative or denunciatory epiphonema, and furthermore a votive and precatory one, and finally a parenetic and exhortatory one. We conclude with a similar epiphonema and Davidic wish from Psalm 125:4. Do good, O Lord, to the good, and to the upright in heart. But those who decline into their perversities the Lord shall drive away with those who devote effort to iniquity: PEACE BE UPON ISRAEL, Amen!

Latin:

Vers. 9. EPHRAIM, QUID MIHI ULTRA IDOLA?)

In Hebræo: ad idola, supple, currit? cum res ita se ha- beant, cur adhuc Ephraimitæ idola colunt? cur non ab eis discedunt?

EGO EXAUDIAM) Idola non audiunt, nedum ut exaudiant.

ET DIRIGAM EGO EUM, UT ABIETEM VIRENTEM)

EX ME ERUCTUS TUUS INVENTUS EST) Apud me semper fuit operæ tuæ pretium.

Rectius ad Ephraim subintelligitur verbum di- cet, quam ellipsin Chaldæus supplevit, ut & Drusius, Piscator, Paræus, Tarnovius: quid mihi ultra ad idola, vel cum idolis? Ego autem (Deus tuus) respon- di, vel exaudiam Te (præteritum pro futuro) cer- tissime. Ego respiciam eum (intentis oculis obser- vabo eum, quod Ebræum שור importat. Chal- dæus: Ego miserebor ipsius in verbo meo.) Ego, ut abies virens, (ero ipsi) quæ perpetuo floret, præ- statque viatori in æstu gratissimam umbram. Et fru- ctus tuus inventus est, vel invenietur. Non solum protectionis umbram, sed etiam fructum & bene- dictionem largam promittit Deus. Conferantur Interpp. nostri Beatus Meisnerus, & Tarnovius. B. Gefnerus solum hæc verba omnia Deo tribuit hoc modo: O Ephraim, quid mihi jam amplius ja- Etitas idola tua? Ame habes omnis generis beneficia, quorum summa in istis tribus continetur, in paterna & gratuita precum exauditione in calamitatib9, in protectione & gubernatione, in fructificatione. Vers. 10. QUIS SAPIENS ET INTELLIGIT ISTA? INTELLIGENS ET SCIET HÆC?) Ostendit paucos fore in decem tribubus, qui ista, ita ut oportet, sint consideraturi. Bis idem dixit more Hebræo. QUIA RECTÆ VIÆ DOMINI) Consilia Dei & decreta interim æquissima sunt. ET JUSTI AMBULABUNT IN EIS) Per ea justi procedent inoffenso pede. PRÆVARICATORES VERO CORRUENT IN EIS) In omnia jam ante dicta mala incident ex iisdem decretis. Epiphonema hoc finale non solum decem tribus, sed in genere omnes respicit: siquidem omnibus fidelibus, & veram pœnitentiam agentibus promissiones hæ factæ sint, nec tam decretum comminatorium, aut querela Prophetæ hic habetur, quam votum potius singulare Prophetæ, qui optat, ut omnes hæc intelligant cum ratione, ut recte Rivetus & Tarnovius in hunc locum: Quis est sapiens, is intelligat ista, quis est intelligens, is agnoscat ista. Similis parænesis videatur Jac. 3,15. Conf. Deut.32,29. Addit autem Propheta argumentum triplex, primum ab adjuncto hujus doctrinæ Propheticæ, quia rectæ viæ Domini, h. e. æquissimæ, justissimæ, imo omnis æquitatis, justitiæ & rectitudinis regulæ. Alterum ab exemplo: Et justi ambulabunt in eis. Conf. Col. 1, 6. Es. 33, 15. Tertium ab effectu contrario per accidens in impiis & sceleratis. Defectores autem vel prævaricatores corruent in eis. Si vero placeat, unicam proprie tantum rationem adferri, à certitudine viarum Domini, postremam sententiam, conclusionis loco, instar Epiphonematis, vel aphorismi, & Maximæ finalis, singularem stimulum relinquentis, subjici rectissime dixeris. Qui enim per fidem justificati sunt, delectantur ambulare in viis Domini: ambulabunt confidenter, prospere ac feliciter. (Conf. Jud. 5, 3. Mal. 4, 2.) adeoque finem fidei consequentur, animæ salutem. Conf. Syr. 39, 30. Prævaricatores autem impingunt in eis, atque corruunt, & æternum pereunt. Unde Rabbi Salomo Jarchi particulam צ per Chaldæo explicat, corruent propter eas, tradentur gehennæ, eo quod non ambulaverunt in illis. Sic ergo non imprecatio hæc est, ut Junius vult & Tremellius, quos Piscator ipse refellit, neque simplex vaticinium, sed Epiphonema indicativum, seu denunciatorium, adhæc votivum & precatorium, denique paræneticum, & adhortatorium. Concludimus simili Epiphonemate ac voto Davidico è Psal. 125, 4. Benefac, Domine, bonis, & rectis corde. Declinantes autem in perversitates suas abiget Dominus cum iis, qui operant dant iniquitati: PAX SIT SUPER ISRAEL, Amen!

# Joel

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
I. N. J. ANNOTATIONS ON JOEL.

Latin:

I. N. J. ANNOTATA AD JOELEM.

## 1:1 Introduction: Preface
PREFACE.

Jerome, who in his Version follows the Hebrew codex, notes that these Prophets are arranged differently in the Greek codices, namely in this manner: Hosea, Amos, Micah, Joel, Obadiah, Jonah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. The same Jerome, however, feels that because the book of Joel does not have a pre-noted time, and is subjoined to Hosea, they were contemporaries, which the matters contained in Joel also prove. But just as the words of Hosea pertain especially to the ten tribes, so those of Joel pertain most of all to the two remaining ones.

Danaus establishes, in his commentary on chapter 1, that the Prophet Joel prophesied under Josiah, a little before that most grievous famine, which had also been foretold by Jeremiah in chapter 14, had occurred in Judea, to which he was prophesying, and was raging there. But Joel is rightly said to have preached to the two tribes, because he does not mention the ten tribes, which had already been carried away at that time; but he makes mention of the House of God (ch. 1:9, 14, 16) and of Zion (ch. 2:1, 15, 23, 32; ch. 3:16, 17, 21), which was in Jerusalem in the tribe of Benjamin, and in ch. 3:1, 6, God promises that He will bring back the multitude of Judah and Jerusalem.

Whence Joel has his name seems ambiguous, which according to the interpretation of Jerome is 'the beginner', but to the blessed Tarnovius it is conjectured to be the same as 'desire' from the unused root יָאַל, which in Hiphil signifies 'he willed, he desired'. He was the son of Pethuel, who is not Samuel, as some Hebrews believe, for the sons of the latter were judges (1 Sam. 8:1) and wicked (v. 3 and 5), nor does the timing agree; but [the son] of some other, whom they say was of the tribe of Reuben, and they say Joel was born in the field of Bethoron and died and was buried there, according to Dorotheus in his Synopsis and Isidore in his 'On the Birth and Death of the Fathers', which we leave in their place. There is no certainty regarding the Grotius synchronism of Joel and Hosea. Some indeed refer the famine noted by Joel to the 14th year of Hezekiah, before war was brought upon the Jews by Sennacherib, along with Osiander, but Funccius, Montanus, Genebrardus, and Castrio, as well as Drusius with the author of Seder Olam, prefer that Joel prophesied in the times of Manasseh. But to the blessed Tarnovius, the opinion of those who wish these things to have happened under Josiah seems most probable, since a great famine occupied the land in his time, which is described in the same way in Jer. 14:1, 2. Conf. 2 Kings 23:6. So also Lambertus

The occasion of the prophecy was the sending of insects, destroying grasses, flowers, and fruits, so that he might warn the people to serious repentance by the sense of present evil and the fear of future evil to be brought in by the Chaldeans, with notable consolations proposed to those repenting, partly temporal, which were to befall the men of that age, and partly perpetual, to be fulfilled in Christ, especially in the New Testament: in which, therefore, the sum and argument of this prophecy consists. There are two parts, according to the two sermons of the prophet. The former is completed in chapter 1: the latter in the two remaining chapters. In the first, he dwells upon, and furthermore threatens, powerful and fierce armies that will lay waste the vineyards and fig trees; and he exhorts the priests and the people to repentance on account of the famine that will grievously afflict men, cattle, and wild beasts. In the latter, chapter 2, he partly threatens the warlike calamity to be brought on by the Chaldeans, and partly promises grace to the penitent, both corporal, by which there will be a satiety of crops and liberation from enemies; and spiritual, Christ himself, the Teacher of Righteousness, and the Holy Spirit to be poured out upon all flesh.
