Nor does the Chaldean paraphrase deny it: O sons of Zion, exult and rejoice in the WORD of the Lord your God, because (the Lord your God) has given you your Teacher for righteousness, which can be taken in such a way that the WORD of the Lord, in whom the sons of Zion ought to rejoice, is the Teacher of righteousness himself, whom the Lord has given, so that these things explain each other mutually, joy in the word of the Lord, and joy in the fact that a Teacher has been given for righteousness. We treated of this Teacher recently in the doctoral program of Mr. Dr. CHRISTIAN WEBER, supreme court preacher of Württemberg-Oels, publicly proposed on the Sunday of Misericordias Domini in the year 1671; which treatment we repeat here for the sake of illustration.

Exult, O sons of Zion, and rejoice in the Lord your GOD, because He has given you a Teacher of righteousness. The Son of GOD invites the sons of Zion, that is, all believers, to joy and gladness, namely that they should exult and rejoice in the Lord their GOD, because JEHOVAH

May GOD the Father be their GOD, and may He will to be so forever, and since He is about to give them the Teacher of righteousness, who will teach righteousness, bringing true joy, not only by word, but will perform it by the very deed. The Lord used this κέλευσμα [summons] for the Prophet Joel, who was to be Joel, that is, ἔρασμιος [lovely] & the desire of the people, ch. 2, 23. That the Son of GOD speaks these things is not obscure from the entire discourse; because the Lord speaks about the Lord, the Son of GOD about the Father: & He commands to rejoice in the Lord GOD, in the Father, who was about to give the Teacher of righteousness and to send the rain, & the shower v. 23. and He performed wonders among the people v. 26. and furthermore promised v. 27. that He would be in the midst of Israel, which phrase is of the future ἐνσάρκωσις [incarnation], & σκήνωσις [tabernacling] among the people, of whom He also promises that He will be their GOD, so that the people believing in Him may not be put to shame forever. Therefore, it is explained concerning the Economy of the incarnation by Cyrill. Alex. & B. Luther. Therefore, not the least matter and cause of exultation & joy in the Lord is that He gives the Teacher of righteousness. There are indeed not wanting those who prefer to render it 'the rain of righteousness' with Calvin, Junius & Tremellius, and Piscatus; but especially Joh. Drusius; but as those Innovators depart from the Chaldean, the Greeks, the Latin Vulgate, B. Luther, & most Interpreters, so Joh. Coccejus rightly refuted them in the same School, and the plain and simple meaning concerning the TEACHER OF RIGHTEOUSNESS is altogether to be preferred to those tangled and twisted glosses. But who is that Teacher of righteousness, whom GOD the Father promised here that He would give, for whom He provokes all the faithful to exultation & joy? Certainly not Hezekiah, as some Jews trifle, whom Ruffinus also applauds, for the reason that the most pious King stirred up the people to piety & the worship of the true GOD: nor Josiah, which pleased others, who overturned the altars of idols: because neither of these is anywhere adorned with the title of Teacher in the sacred scriptures, and it is likely that Hezekiah was after Joel. Nor is this to be understood of Isaiah himself, as Grotius contends, who is vehemently mistaken when he asserts that the Prophet prophesied about the slaughter of Sennacherib, if indeed that had already happened before Joel, and the Prophet had dealt in the preceding parts not about Sennacherib, but about the army of the Chaldeans. Nor indeed is this Prophecy to be understood of the later Prophets, who flourished after the Babylonian captivity was completed, as Lyranus believed with certain more recent Rabbis, with the approval of Hugo and Dionysius, as for instance Haggai, Zechariah, & Malachi. For there were never lacking Teachers for the people of the Lord, not even in the Babylonian captivity itself; in which they had Jeremiah in their midst, not to speak of Ezekiel or Daniel. Who then is that Teacher of righteousness promised here with such great jubilation? Indeed, these things seem to some to sound indefinitely about any teachers, of whom GOD never deprived the Church; nor do the Weimar Paraphrasts deny this. But there is no doubt for us that Christ is definitely looked to here, of whom not only some of the Ancients, Haymo of Halberstadt, accept this oracle. Remigius of Auxerre, Rupert of Deutz, but also from our own B. Luther, B. Wigandus, B. Winckelmann, B. Pappus, B. Himmelius, from the Pontificals Albert the Great, Montanus, Vatablus, Ribera, Christopher à Castro, Cornelius à Lapide, and even from the Calvinists Coccejus, the Belgian Paraphrasts, the Authors of the annotations to the Bible of Paulus Tossanus, recently augmented with new additions, and also from the Jews themselves Abarbanel, and what is worth all of them, the Chaldean Paraphrase. For when the Lord excites and provokes all the faithful to joy, not for some common benefit, but for that which is the fountain & spring of all joy, and by which alone the faithful of the Old Testament could be refreshed; desiring it with great desire, in which alone the faithful of the New Testament place joy & gladness, namely the MESSIAH promised to the Ancients, given to us, it must be believed that this is done; if indeed nothing is more solemn for the Prophets than to excite the faithful to joy by that reason, namely the promised gift of the Messiah, or the Economy of His advent. To which St. Cyril also refers the preceding, v. 21. 22. Fear not, O land, exult & be glad, for the Lord has magnified to do: Θάρσει γῆ χαῖρε, καὶ εὐφραίνου have the LXX Interpreters. whence Cyril: It is the custom of the Holy Prophets to direct their words from particular goods, and those conferred upon a few, to the universality and the genus itself, as are those things which we have obtained through Christ. Therefore, our discourse proceeds again to these. For when was it given to the earth to be confident? Again, when did the Lord magnify τὸ ποιῆσαι [to do], unless when the Word, which was GOD, put on human nature, so that flooding the earth with heavenly goods, He might be found by those believing in Him as a river of peace, as a torrent of pleasure, as the early and latter rain, and the bestower of all fertility. Furthermore, the Lord testifies that He is not speaking indefinitely about teachers, when He prophesies that GOD will give not teachers, but μοναδικῶς [singularly] & with the emphatic or demonstrative He, THAT TEACHER, who indeed was particularly promised to Moses, that He alone is to be heard, Deut. 18, 15. & is described by Elihu, that it is His task to hand down to man the righteousness of GOD, Job 33, 23. Through David He received that He would preach the name of the Lord, Ps. 22, 23. & would announce Righteousness in the great Congregation, Ps. 40, 10. through Solomon He calls us all into the School of His instruction, Prov. 8 & 9. through Isaiah He testifies that the Lord had given Him a learned tongue, Is. 50, 4. & that He is the Teacher of righteousness, ch. 63, 1. the Teacher & Evangelist of the Gentiles, ch. 55, 4. who finally professed of Himself in the days of His flesh, Matt. 23, 8. One is your Master. That Teacher of teachers; the Teacher of the Prophets, because the Spirit of Christ was in them, 1 Pet. 1, 11. by whom they were moved, 2 Pet. 1, 21. the Teacher of the Apostles, because He promised and gave them His Spirit, John 16, 7. ch. 20, 22. the Teacher of all, because we receive the anointing from Him, & His anointing teaches us about all things, 1 John 2, 27.

This Doctor is therefore here called so ἐξαιρέτως & κατ᾿ ἀντονομασίαν, as being a truly divine doctor, because he is in the Bosom of the Father, and ὁμοόσιος to Him, John 1:14, ch. 10:30. The most excellent Doctor, because he is the very Wisdom of GOD & the eternal λόγος of GOD, Prov. 8:1, seqq., John 1:1. The most universal Doctor, because no one knows the Father, except the Son and he to whom he wishes to reveal him, Matt. 11:27. The most wholesome Doctor, because he has the words of eternal life, John 6:68. The most efficacious Doctor, because the words which he speaks are Spirit & life, John 6:63. The only Doctor on earth to be heard, Matt. 17:5. The perpetual & eternal Doctor in the heavens, continually illuminating the Elect with his light, Rev. 21:23, and informing the Angels themselves by the sight of his face, 1 Pet. 1:12, whom alone the Angels and the Elect in heaven worship and proclaim as worthy to open the sealed book, Rev. 5:9, seqq. Although this Doctor was indeed given and sent by the Father from the very first cradles of the world as the λόγος & Word of GOD the Father, whom the Fathers wish to be the interpreter of the will of God, a κήρυκα ἐξαγγελτικὸν, as also the LXX Interpreters call him εὐαγγελιστὴν κ᾿ ἑρμηνέα τῶν μεγάλων βελημάτων τᾶ θεᾶ, an ἄγγελον μεγάλης βελῆς: already long ago proposed to the people to be heard by God, Ex. 23:21, Observe him, & hear his voice; who instructed Adam in Paradise, Gen. 3:15, Abraham in the oak grove of Mamre, Gen. 18, Moses in the burning bush, & on Mount Sinai, Ex. 3 & 19.

Act. 7, 30. 35. 38. He spoke to David, as his latest words testify, 2 Sam. 23, 2. He sent Isaiah, when he saw his glory Eph. 6, 3. seqq. John 12, 41. Yet it is promised by Joel that the same one will be solemnly sent, and will dwell in the midst of the people; which things pertain to the Economy of the flesh: just as the Pharisees professed him to be Rabbi, Teacher, and Master, who came from GOD John 3, 2. Matt. 22, 16. and the whole people acclaimed him Luke 7, 16. Truly that great Prophet has risen among us: and again John 6, 14. This is truly that Prophet who was to come into the world.

Finally, it is a question here not of an ordinary or common Teacher, but one given לצדקה for righteousness: which fits no one except CHRIST, who alone is our righteousness Jer. 23, 6. c. 33, 15. made for us by GOD Wisdom and righteousness 1 Cor. 1, 30. in whom alone we are made the righteousness of GOD 2 Cor. 5, 21. That Teacher was therefore given for righteousness to be acquired for us by his obedience, both active and passive Isa. 53, 11. Rom. 5, 18. 19. c. 8, 3. to teach us the righteousness acquired, Isa. 63, 3. and to announce it to us, Ps. 40, 10. to apply to us the righteousness both acquired and announced, through the Word and Sacraments, and to constitute us righteous before GOD through the same Rom. 4, 28. c. 5, 19. O Teacher truly μονότροπον and singular! O Teacher entirely ἀνεκφραστον, and admirable! For he has a name which no one knows except himself, and his name is called the Word of GOD Rev. 19, 12. 13. But we have said more about this Teacher in the Annotations to this prophecy, which anyone who wishes may consult.

Moreover, this Teacher had to be given in such a way, and was given in such a way, that he would have the authority to give other Teachers also: because he wished not only to teach himself directly and in his own person, but also to appoint others who might perform an embassy for him 2 Cor. 5, 20. his ministers, and stewards of the mysteries of GOD 1 Cor. 4, 1. both Apostles and their successors: to whom he says: as the Father has sent me, even so I send you John 20, 21. indeed all, as many Teachers as have existed from the world, were sent by the Hypostatic wisdom of GOD, this Teacher of righteousness Luke 11, 49. nor were they ever sent by the merit of any other than this Teacher given to us for righteousness, nor did they announce the remission of sins and righteousness except in his name. Acts 10, 43. c. 4, 12. For for this reason it was necessary for him both to descend from the heavens and to ascend into heaven, that he might acquire this benefit for us, who were eternally excluded from the light of information and eternally damned to outer darkness, and that he might receive gifts for men, and give and confer the same to men, and thus also be able to send from heaven those who would instruct us in righteousness: Ps. 68, 19. Eph. 4, 8. 9. 10. 11. Dan. 12, 3. from whom, therefore, Teachers and Pastors have always been sent, and will be sent until the end of the age, for the perfecting of the Saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the Body of Christ Eph. 4, 17. that is, of the universal Church, which began in Paradise, and will not have an end on this earth until the world itself ends.

Verse same. AND HE WILL CAUSE TO DESCEND FOR YOU THE EARLY AND THE LATTER RAIN) He will give convenient weather at the time of sowing and harvest. Deut. 11, 14. Prov. 16, 16. Jer. 5, 24. Hos. 6, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 23. DEDIT VOBIS DOCTOREM JUSTI- TIÆ) Esaiam.

Perperam de Esaia hoc explicatur. Nam Joel Esaia posterior fuit, nec de Sennacheribo vatici- natus hactenus est, sed de Chaldæorum exercitu, qui Hierosolyma destruxit. Ideoque rejicitur etiam Judæorum nonnullorum, & Ruffini interpretatio, qui hunc Doctorem Ezechiam faciunt, qui popu- lum excitavit ad pietatem, & cultum Dei 2. Par. 30. nec non aliorum, qui Josiam Regem intelligunt, qui aras idolorum evertit. Recentiores nonnulli Rabbini, ut & Lyranus, Hugo, & Dionysius, aliique de Prophetis Judæorum post captivitatem Babyloni- cam, Zacharia, Aggæo, & Malachia interpretantur, redduntque communiter Doctores justitiæ, quibus favere videtur B. Lutheri translatio in plurali nu- mero hæc reddens: Der Euch Lehrer zu Gerech- tigkeit giebet: & glossa marginalis: Er wil sagen/ bisz dasz Christus kompt/sol bey euch bleiben Pre- digt und Futter/Geistliches und Weltliches Re- giment/ das ist/ die Lehrer der Gerechtigkeit/ und Früchte des Landes / wie es am ersten/ und vor- mahls geschehen. De Christo tamen μοναδικῶς in- telligit idem B. Lutherus noster in Commentar. ad h. l. quam sententiam B. Wigandus, B. Gefnerus, B. Winckelmannus, & alii amplectuntur. Ei favere vi- detur 1. quod hic filii Zion ad gaudium in Domino Deo suo excitentur: quod à Prophetis fieri eadem ratio- ne solet, cum de Christo vaticinatur Es. 61. Zach. 2. c. 9. Ubi negligenda non est pulchra B. Lutheri obser- vatio: usitatum est, inquit Vir Dei, Zionis appellatio- ne venire Ecclesiam Novi Testamenti: Idque hac ra- tione. In Zione monte Hierosolymorum fuit Regia arx, extructa à Davide, sicut docet historia 2. Sam. 5. Quia autem Christus Davidi promissus est, vocatur Christus quoque Rex Zionis, tanquam filius & hæres Davidis. Hinc mons Zion vocatur sanctus mons Ps. 2. Quod sanctum semen ibi regnaturum sit, sicut Ps. 110. dicit, ex Zione emissurum hunc Regem sceptrum suum. Hac igitur ratione filii Zion vocantur Ecclesia à suo rege, qui in Zione habitaturus, & novum inde regnum auspicaturus erat, per Evangelii prædicatio- nem: à monte Moria denominationem Ecclesia non habet. Etsi enim is mons dicatus erat cultui Dei, & i- deo quoque sanctus appellatur à Prophetis, tamen, quia exhibito Christo abrogandi cultus hi erant, tanquam umbra & figura, à Zione potius Ecclesiæ nomen habet.

2. Quod Propheta μοναδικῶς loquatur de Doctore uno, & quidem cum He Hajediab, & præmisso quoq; articulo הַ qui vim habet ostendere aliquid sin- gulare & peculiare, ut designetur certus olim pro- missus & fidelibus probe notus ac vehementer de- sideratus ILLE DOCTOR, quem κατ' ἀντονομα- σίαν ita vocat S.S. Propheta ille per Mofem promissus Deut. 18, 19. Doctor & Evangelista gentium Es. 55, 4. unicus ille Magister & Rabbi Matth. 23, 8. (3) Quod notet ipsum proprio suo nomine Doctorem justitiæ, quod Christus sibi jure vindicat Es. 63, 1. Ego sum Doctor justitiæ. De quo eleganter B. Lu- therus, instituta comparatione Christi & Mosis: Dicit Propheta, non solum daturum Deum Docto- rem seu magistrum, sed addit, ad justitiam, hoc est, qui verbo & doctrina sua, quam afferet, homines à pec- catis liberabit, & justos faciet. Talem Doctorem Mo- sen fuisse nemo dicet. Docet Moses præclare de volun- tate Dei, quid à nobis exigat Deus, quid faciendum nobis sit, si velimus Dei voluntatem facere. In hoc ar- gumento Moses non habet similem. Sed quid respondet Johannes Baptista? Hoc scilicet: Lex per Mosen data est, hoc est, Moses tantum est Legislator, hoc tan- tum agit, ut ostendat, quid nobis faciendum sit. Sed interim corda per peccatum depravata, abhorrent hanc Dei voluntatem, & malunt sequi suas cupi- ditates. Ac si qui gubernant hos vitiosos motus ali- quo modo, fit hoc tantum metu pœnæ, non vero o- bediendi studio, aut amore Dei, cor interim depen- det totum in aliam partem. Quia autem lex Dei re- quirit cor purum, nos autem ne quidem manus, lin- guam & alia membra regere possumus, quin sæpe contra legem Dei delinquamus, hinc fit, ut, sicut Paulus loquitur, Moses sit minister mortis, & lex augeat peccatum, & occidat. Si enim lex non esset, non esset peccatum. Nunc cum lex posita sit, nos autem convincat cor nostrum de violata lege, quid aliud restat, quam ut animi turbentur, ut peccatum fiat excellenter peccatum, & lex nos morti objici- at? Sicut enim Syngrapha te convincit debiti, ut id negare non possis, ita Lex vere est chirographum contra nos, quo animi convincuntur peccati, & consequenter subjiciuntur pœnis Lege constitutis. De tali Doctore gloriantur Judæi, cum de Lege & Mose gloriantur, qui ceu lictor & carnifex arripit furem & strangulat laqueo. Et tamen verum hoc est, Legis doctrinam necessariam, sanctam, perfe- ctam esse. Omne autem vitium in nobis est. Per peccatum enim corrupta voluntate & intellectu, neque videre possumus recta, neque si ostendantur, perficere. Alia igitur doctrina, alio Doctore opus est, qui primum hoc cordium vitium sanet. Deinde etiam vires suppeditet præstandi ea, quæ lege jubemur face- re. Talis Doctor, cum Christus sit, tribuit ei Joel excel- lens & sublime hoc nomen, quod sit Doctor justitiæ, & non, sicut Moses, Doctor peccati. Quia enim ostendit, quid faciamus, nos autem id facere non possumus, ni- hil aliud, quam peccatores ex nobis facit, & gravat conscientias nostras, perturbat animos, & implet eos metu, imo etiam odio judicii Dei. Malet enim natura Deum non esse, quam se æternis suppliciis subjici. Huic impietati non solum lex non medetur, sed etiam ac- cendit eam, & auget, non ut dixi, suo vitio, est enim cœlestis pluvia. Sed nostro, qui ceu petra rigata largis imbribus, tamen perpetuo manemus steriles. Christus igitur, Rex Zionis sancti montis, est justitiæ Doctor. Mutat enim corda per Spiritum S. & quod vitiosum in nobis est, hoc condonat, sicut Baptista egregie dicit, Lex per Mosen data est: Gratia autem & veritas per Je- sum Christum facta. Gratia est remissio peccato- rum, quæ credentibus in Christum donatur. Veritas autem est donum Spiritus S. qui mutat corda & in- citat ad veram obedientiam contra peccatum, ac excludit omnem hypocrisin. Talem Doctorem hic promittit Propheta Ecclesiæ, & jubet eam ideo gaudere in Domino. Sic Esaias: Servus meus justus notitia sui justificabit multos, hoc est, Filius Dei pa- tefaciet se per Evangelium, & sic multi justificabuntur. Hæc B. Lutherus.

Addunt (4) nonnulli, quod per pluviam pri- mam & serotinam pluvia spiritualis designetur: quod nempe, uti Gesnerus explicat p. 107. Christus Ecclesiam N. Test. cœlesti rore verbi sui & sacra- mentorum, benigne recreaturus & irrigaturus sit, statim ab initio factæ sationis, & deinde quoq; cum in maturam segetem adoleverit, & messis ultimi ju- dicii appropinquaverit, de qua infra c. 3, 13. Et certe fœcundissimus imber fuit, cum Christus Apostolos in totum orbem terrarum misit; & doctor ille no- ster, cum ad cœlos adscendisset, & ad dextram æterni Patris consedisset, dedit Ecclesiæ pastores, docto- res, Evangelistas &c. Eph. 4, 11. Ps. 68, 19. Hic fuit imber ille matutinus. Non minus autem insignis & fertilis pluvia, postremis hisce temporibus, per lu- cem renascentis Evangelii, animis & cordibus ho- minum, Papisticarum superstitionum tenebris pe- ne enectis contigit. Et hic est vespertinus ille imber, de quo hic Propheta loquitur. Ita Gesnerus. Quo e- tiam illa, quæ subjunguntur v. 14. & implebuntur areæ frumento, & redundabunt torcularia vino & oleo, de spirituali proventu interpretatur p. 108. Cum de corporali benedictione agrorum, vinea- rum, & hortorum, supra copiose actum sit: hic spiri- tualia procul dubio intelliguntur bona, quæ sunt propria regni Christi, quod non consistit in cibo & potu, sed in justitia, pace & gaudio in Spiritu S. Rom. 14, 17. Cibus autem & potus spiritualis est Chri- stus cum omnibus suis beneficiis in Evangelio & Sa- cramentis nobis propositus. Joh. 4, 14. & c. 6, 48. Matt. 22, 2. Es. 25, 6. Reliqua autem de compensatio- ne annorum, quos comedit locusta, bruchus &c. de corporalibus bonis interpretatur Gesnerus, quod Dominus polliceatur, se hæc spiritualibus adjectu- rum. Sed ea B. Lutherus etiam de spiritualibus be- neficiis interpretatus est, instituta itidem ἀντιθέσει Mosis & Christi: Significat, inquit, Propheta felicem Evangelii successum, & pulchros fructus, qui hanc do- ctrinam justitiæ subsequentur, non tantum in illo bre- vi angulo, in quo Judæi habitabant, sed per omnem ter- rarum orbem. Hæc sunt horrea plena & torcularia re- dundantia musto & oleo. Reddam, seu compensabo vobis annos, quos voraverunt locustæ, & come- dentes comedetis, hoc est, cupide & cum singulari voluptate comedetis, sicut famelici solent. Respicit autem hic quoque ad Legem, ea recte comparatur cibo, qui movet nauseam. Non quod lex mala sit. Est enim ros divinitus demissus, ut Moses appellat, hoc est, cœlestis doctrina. Nos autem tum palatum, tum stomachum vitiosum habemus, qualis esse so- let ægrotantium, ideo salubrem cibum fastidimus. Sicut enim Paulus dicit Rom. 8. Sensus carnis est ini- micitia adversus Deum, Legi enim Dei non subditur, non enim potest. Qui autem secundum carnem vivunt, Deo placere non possunt. Hic est morbus noster, qui palatum & stomachum vitiat, ut cœlestis cibus a nobis fastidiatur. Quæ enim Deo placent, nobis di- splicent. Contra quæ nobis placent, Deo displicent. Quia autem lex pœnas minatur transgressoribus, ideo abhorremus ab ea, & odimus eam. Sed Evan- gelium est ille cœlestis cibus, de quo hic Propheta concionatur, quod cupide & cum voluptate sum- ma simus eum comesturi. Non enim, ut lex, docet, quid a nobis exigat Deus, non intentat pœnas, sed proponit Deum, ut supra Propheta dixit, cle- mentem, misericordem, tardum ad iram, benefi- cum, & pœnitentem super malo. Ostendit Filium Dei ideo in hanc nostram carnem venisse, ut opera Diaboli destrueret, hoc est, ut aboleret peccatum, vinceret mortem, patefaceret vitam, & tyranni- dem Satanæ everteret. Hic est gratus menti cibus & suavis, quem territi animi conspectu peccatorum suorum, & metu iræ ac judicii Dei, ceu fameli- cus stomachus, avide arripiunt. Hoc primum est beneficium hujus Doctoris, quod affert ad nos ci- bum, quem comedentes comedimus, hoc est, cu- pide & cum singulari voluptate. Alterum est, quod non solum dicit; Comedetis cupide : Sed addit etiam: & exfaturabimini. Respicit autem hic quoque oblique ad Legem. Etsi enim habet cultus suos, etsi ostendit quid faciendum sit, tamen sicut cibus, qui famem non sedat, sed accendit magis & irritat stomachum; Ita lex relinquit animos anxios, & dubios de salute, non possunt mentes in his acquie- scere. Atque hoc vitium in genere est omnium studiorum & operum, quæ suscipiuntur ad placan- dam iram Dei. Relinquunt enim magis dubios & anxios animos, quam acceperunt. Contra Evange- lium, quod hic justitiæ Doctor, ex sinu Patris, ad nos affert, est solidus cibus, qui implet & exatiat stomachum, ac famem tollit. Animi enim, intuen- tes Filium Dei, factum victimam pro nobis, in hoc sacrificio acquiescunt, implentur gaudio, & cer- tam etiam in ipsa morte consolationem habent. Sequitur in Propheta, Et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri. Hic fructus saturitatem hanc cœlestis cibi semper sequitur. Vides autem hic quoque cla- rum discrimen Legis & Evangelii. Lex operatur i- ram. Commoventur enim animi contra Deum, ju- dicant injustum & crudelem esse, quod hanc infir- mam naturam oneravit ingenti hac mole legis, quam sustinere impossibile est. Contra Evange- lium, quia concionatur de misericordia, & æternis beneficiis Dei Patris, qui filium suum dedit pro pec- catis nostris, & Spiritus Sancti, qui accendit in ani- mis fiduciam erga Deum per Christum. Ideo animi intuentes in has divitias misericordiæ & bonitatis Dei, erumpunt in laudem Dei, prædicant bonita- tem ejus, laudant & ornant eum, ac etiam vitam potius abjiciunt quam confessionem. Laudabitis, inquit, nomen Domini Dei vestri, quia mirabilia vobiscum. Hæc enim mirabilia non sunt benedi- ctio corporalis, & annonæ ubertas, sed quod no- bis miseris peccatoribus, qui sumus natura filii iræ, datur justitiæ Doctor, Filius Dei, qui famelicos nos, positos sub Lege & ira Dei, pascit verbo suo, & hoc modo ex peccatoribus justos, ex iræ filiis Deo gra- tos, ex damnatis salvos, ex mortalibus immortales facit. Hæc vere sunt mirabilia, quæ nemo unquam fecit, nisi Doctor hic justitiæ, Filius Dei. Hæc B. Lutherus : Quem sequutus est B. Winckelmann. Comm. in Minor. Prophet. pag. 210. ET IMPLE- BUNTUR) immoratur Propheta allegoriæ. Sicut autem abundantiam beneficiorum spiritualium & consolationum Evangelicarum confert cum plu- via & fœcunditate, & copia rerum externarum. Ita comparat τὸ ἀνωφελὲς ϰαὶ ἀσθενὲς legis, non valentis hominem corruptum ad perfectionem adducere, Heb. 7. cum sterilitate, penuria & defectu. Atqui Evangelium seu doctrina justitiæ præstat hoc, quod legi est impossibile. ET COMEDETIS VE- SCENTES) id est, cupide comedetis. Homines e- nim agnoscentes ex Lege peccatum & iram Dei, re- cte conferuntur cum famelicis, avide cibum Evan- gelicum comedentibus : quæ sunt, ut LXX. habent τὰ βρώματα εἰς δικαιοσύνην. Illis enim Christus pa- nis vitæ dulcescit. SATURABIMINI) id est, in Deo misericorde, & propter Messiam propitio, acquiescetis, tanquam omni bono saturati : ET LAUDABITIS NOMEN DEI VESTRI) Opulentia & satietas bonorum externorum ut plurimum gignit securi- tatem & rebellionem : sicut Dominus conqueritur Deut. 32. Incrassatus est, recalcitravit, incrassatus o- pertus est. Dereliquit Deum factorem suum. Sed satietas spiritualis parit δοξολογίαν. QUI FECIT MIRABILIA) Vere enim missio filii Dei in hunc mundum, redemptio generis humani, missio Spiri- tus Sancti sunt opera mirabilia.

5. Urget B. Lutherus imprimis etiam hoc, quod hic promittatur non futurum post hac, in æter- num ut confundatur populus. Hoc autem quomodo, inquit, potest dici de populo legis, qui etsi restitutus sit ab exilio suis sedibus, tamen subinde à Syriis, Ægy- ptiis, tandem Romanis quoque varie vexatus, & tan- tum non oppressus est. Et postea f. 668. Quod de non confundendo in sempiternum addit, dixi argu- mentum esse certum, quod hæc non de reductione in terram Canaan ex Babel, sed de tempore Evan- gelii intelligenda sint, præsertim cum scriptura hac ipsa phrasi in aliis quoq; locis soleat uti, ubi non de corporalibus beneficiis, sed de remissione pecca- torum agit. Psal. 25. dicit: Omnes qui te expectabant, non confundentur, & Psal. 31. In te spero Domine, non confundar in æternum. Habet autem hæc quoque particula insignem antithesin Evangelii & Legis. Justificati fide, inquit Paulus, pacem habemus apud Deum, per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, per quem etiam aditum habemus fide ad gratiam hanc, in qua stamus. Et Ephes. 3. Per Christum habemus li- bertatem & aditum cum fiducia, quæ est per fidem. Et Ebr. 4. Accedamus igitur cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut accipiamus misericordiam & gratiam in- veniamus, ut oportunum nobis contingat auxilium. Quia enim Evangelium ostendit Christum, Dei fili- um, ex voluntate Patris factum victimam, & satis- fecisse pro peccatis. Ideo animi non dubitant de Dei benevolentia, non pavent, non refugiunt à Deo, spem omnem in Dei misericordia habent po- sitam. Sed quid Lex faciet? Ostendit quidem Dei voluntas quæ sit, quod attinet ad nostra opera, & quid Deus à nobis exigat, sed quia facultatem fa- ciendi non præstat, nihil aliud sequitur legem, quam confusio. Similiter Winckelmannus: ET NON CONFUNDETUR POPULUS. Lex o- stendens peccati turpitudinem & iram Dei, opera- tur confusionem, quia peccatores necesse est con- fundi coram Deo: sed Evangelium aufert confusio- nem, & restituit nobis amissam gloriam. Qui enim credit in Christum, non confundetur, Rom. 10.

6. In postremo commate hujus capitis Chri- stum loquentem introduci vult B. Lutherus, qui se verum hominem, & verum Deum esse doceat. Et scietis, quoniam in medio Israel ego, & ego Dominus Deus vester, & non alius. Non enim satis est scire, quod in medio Israel sit, hoc est, quod sit verus homo iste Doctor, sed addendum hoc quoque est, scietis, quod ego Dominus Deus vester & non alius. Quia i- gitur Filius Dei inducit carnem nostram & habita- vit in medio Israel, recte igitur populus meus non confundetur in æternum: Ideo enim venit, ut dis- solveret opera diaboli, ut liberati à lege, peccato, morte, & Satana, essemus in gloria æterna per i- psius mortem & gratiam. Sic etiam Cyrillus Ale- xandr. in Comment. p. 226. Manifesto modum æco- nomiæ incarnationis, & sese exinaniturum, & cum terricolis habitaturum promittit, nostri similem, id est, hominem factum. Tunc enim in medio Israel fuit, & nos ignominiam effugimus, & è confusione exem- pti sumus, morte nimirum prostrata, peccato interfe- cto, & cognitione veritatis introducta.

Hæc non inconcinna sunt, nec à more lo- quendi Prophetico, cum de beneficiis Novi Test. agunt, aliena, sed cum illa compensatio annorum sic- citatis respiciat ea, quæ capite præcedente de sicci- tate à locustis, brucho &c. illata, dixerat Propheta, du- bium nullum est, beneficia corporalia illis insinua- ri, quod priorem inopiam agrorum vinearumque benigne compensaturus sit Dominus, quod hic a- gnoscit B. Gefnerus. Porro manifestum satis videtur illam pluviam matutinam, quæ Græcis πρώϊμος ὑετός, tunc decidit, quando facta est satio, ut semen in a- grum conjectum radices agere queat, & pluviam serotinam, quæ ὄψιμος ὑετὸς tunc decidens, cum se- ges in culmos & spicas succrevit, ut grana turge- scant, pluvias apud Judæos usitatas designare Deut. 11, 14. Ier. 5, 24. Zach. 10, 1. Iac. 5, 7. quum nullum in textu allegoriæ extet vestigium, etsi alias non i- gnotum sit, doctrinam pluviæ comparari Es. 50, 10. 11. (Conf. Job. 29, 22. Es. 21, 1.2. Am. 6, 26. Mich. 2, 6. c. 5, 2.) & pluviam matutinam & serotinam allego- rice adhiberi Os. 6, 3. c. 10, 12. Siquidem illa omnia ita cohæreant, atque mutuo se explicent, quæ de pluvia matutina & serotina, de implendis horreis & torcularibus, & de compensatione annorum sterilium promittuntur, ut discerpi, ac tam disparato sensu accipi non possint, quasi alia de spirituali, alia de corporali loquantur benedictione. Neque alia ple- risque videtur persona, quæ promittit Doctorem ad justitiam, ab ea, quæ hic sui præsentiam in Israel pol- licetur. Et simplicior apparet glossa marginalis B. Luther. cui etiam ceu magis τῷ ῥητῷ convenienti inhæremus cum B. Osiandro, B. Pappo, & Vinarien- sibus, quod cum Doctore justitiæ simul bona corporalia promittantur, quemadmodum ab Esaia etiam fa- ctum c. 30. Dabit tibi Dominus panem tribulationis, & aquam afflictionis, nec avolabit amplius abs te Do- ctor tuus, sed oculi tui videbunt Doctorem tuum. Et à Christo quærentibus regnum Dei & JUSTI- TIAM ejus promissio sit corporalium beneficio- rum: Cætera adjicientur vobis. Matth. 6.

Per Doctorem autem illum justitiæ non incom- modè Christus μοναδικῶς intelligi potest, cujus ad- ventum excipit missio Spiritus S. hic juxta Petri- nam interpretationem à Joele promissa; nisi forte hæc quis ipsummet Messiam loqui malit, quum Do- minus de Domino loquatur v. 26. Sic enim Messias ipse promittit, quod in medio Israel esse velit per ad- ventum in carnem, quodq; populus ipsius, hoc est, qui in ipsum crediderint, in æternum confundendi non sint, siquidem alio, longeque propiore modo tum in medio Israel habitarit, quam antea in domo sua habitans Joh. 1, 14. & in eo summa consistat Ev- angelii, qui crediderit in eum, non confundetur Rom. 10, 11. 1. Petr. 2, 6. quam Joel ita postmodum effert hoc secundo cap. vers. 23. qui nomen Domini invocaverit, salvus erit. Quod etsi post captivita- tem Babylonicam etiam Doctores justitiæ tradide- rint, experimento tamen ipso, & clariori notitia tum demum discere, & cognoscere datum est, cum in medio Israel habitavit, & cum effudit spiritum suum super omnem carnem. Quæ interpretatio concioni Petrinæ Act. 2. videri possint congrua, si- quidem is, qui effudit Spiritum S. sit Christus v. 33. à quo hic promissa effusio Spiritus Sancti.

Ioh. Drusius, qui hic singularis esse voluit, etsi eandem ante ipsum orbitam triverit Iohannes Cal- vinus, & alii, à B. Gesnero & Cornelio à Lapide jam notari, הַמּוֹרֶה interpretatus est pluviam: quam ex- plicationem arripuit quoque Iunius & Tremellius, nec non Piscator in translatione sua, ut & D. Ioh. Tarnovius in Commentar. Drusiana ita habent p. 458. Comment. in Proph. Minor. DOCTOREM AD JUSTITIAM. Sic Chaldæus, Græci, Latini, vulgata, & consentiunt interpretes, ut putent Chri- stum significari, de quo Hos. 10, 12. donec veniat & doceat vos justitiam; potest ita esse: tamen confide- ranti mihi seriem concionis, non displicet pluvia ad justitiam, ut nec in Hoseæ loco citato, si quis scholiastæ secutus ita vertat, donec veniat & pluvia justitiæ vo- bis. Sensus autem hic est, dedit vobis pluviam justi- tiæ, id est, largam, copiosam, ut sol justitiæ Mal. 4, 2 qui benigne tum lucet, cum calefacit: vel dedit a justitiam, hoc est, largitur: cui simile: seminate ad justitiam, inibi apud Hoseam. Quidam reddunt, se- cundum justitiam, per justitiam autem intelligunt jus & æquum: ac si diceret: dedit vobis tantum plu- viæ, quantum satis est, & æquitas postulat. Refutavit autem Drusium (adeoque Calvinum etiam suum, Piscatorem & Junium) Ioh. Coccejus, cujus rationes subjicimus: Per מורה debet intelligi Doctor. 1. quia sic commodè intelligi potest. 2. quia à pluvia, quæ מרה vocatur, distinguitur. 3. quia est ad justitiam. Sed pluvia non est propter justitiam, neque ad justitiam. 4. quia est ratio gaudendi in Domino ut Deo suo, scil. solo. Hæc Coccejus, qui porro ita probat Chri- stum solum intelligi, non vero alium quendam Do- ctorem, aut Legislatores collective intelligendos esse: Doctor vero ille ὁ διδάσκαλος, non tantum justi- tiæ Doctor, sed & datus ad justitiam. Idque Christus 1. quia ipsi hic titulus Doctor & justitiæ soli convenit; quippe qui cum docet se imitari, & sibi credere docet id, quo justi simus, & fructus justitiæ ferimus, 2. quia promissus est. Verbum autem dedit, & articulus ad promissionem & spem filiorumSionis respiciunt. 3. quia datus est ad justitiam, h. e. ut purgationem peccati faceret in sanguine suo, & accusationem Legis, & consequenter servitutem Legis ceremonialis tol- leret. Justitia enim reatui & accusationi opponitur, quando de peccatore sermo est. Non intelliguntur col- lective המחוקקים legislatores sive seniores ur- gentes legem, 1. quia potius hoc ipso vocabulo מחוקקים fuisset usus, ex Gen. 49, 10. 2. quia sine ar- ticulo fuisset locutus. Articulus enim certum indicat, & illum quidem eximium & omnibus aliis eodem nomine indigitatis oppositum. Sic הנביא ὁ προφή- της. 3. quia legislatores non docuerunt justitiam, sed accusationem; & propter eos nomen Dei blasphe- mabatur Es. 52, 5. 4. quia illa non sunt dati ad justiti- am, qui ipsi indigni fuerunt vestiri justitia & salute. Pf. 132. Non Propheta quivis alius, quia hi omnes non fuerunt lux & justitia populi, sed testati sunt de ea. Hic autem agitur de Magistro dato ad justitiam. Conf. Jer. 23, 5.6. 33, 15. 16. Es. 53, 11. in agnitione sui justificabit justus servus meus multos. Heb. 2, 4. Iu- stus in fide ejus vivet. Hæc iterum Coccejus rationes easdem adducens, quas B. Lutherus, & B. Gesnerus exequuti sunt, è quibus priores tres, cum quinta su- pra proposita facile assensum nostrum impetrant, ut de Messia hoc vaticinium intelligamus, quod non tantum plerique Interpp. ita interpretati sunt, Remigius, Rupertus, Haymo, Lutherus, Wigandus, Winckelmannus, Albertus, Arias, Vatablus, Riebe- ra, à Castro, à Lapide, Coccejus; Paraphrastæ Belgi- ci &c. sed etiam è Judæis nonnulli, & inter hos Christi & Christianorum hostis infestus Abarbanel. Neque abnuit Chaldaica paraphrasis: ô filii Sion ex- ultate, & lætamini in VERBO Domini Dei vestri, quo- niam (Dominus Deus vester) dedit vobis Doctorem vestrum in justitiam, quæ ita accipi potest, quod VERBUM Domini, in quo lætari filii Sion debent, sit ipse Doctor justitiæ, quem dedit Dominus, ut hæc sese mutuo explicent, lætitia in verbo Domini, & lætitia in eo, quod datus sit Doctor ad justitiam. De hoc Doctore egimus nuper in programmate Do- ctorali Dn. D. CHRISTIANI WEBERI concio- natoris aulici supremi Würtenbergico - Olsnensis Dominica Misericordias Domini Anno 1671. publice proposito; quam tractationem illustrationis causa hic repetimus.

Exultate filii Sion, & lætamini in Domino DEO vestro, quia dedit vobis Doctorem justitiæ. Ad gaudium & lætitiam invitat filios Sion, hoc est, cre- dentes universos Filius DEI, ut nempe exultent, & lætentur in Domino DEO suo, quod JEHOVA

DEUS Pater ipsorum DEUS sit, atque esse velit in æternum, quodque idem daturus ipsis sit Docto- rem justitiæ, qui justitiam, gaudium verum adfe- rentem, non verbo tantum docebit, sed opere ipso præstabit. Ad κέλευσμα hoc usus est Dominus Joele Propheta, qui Joel, hoc est, ἔρασμιος & desi- derium populi esse debebat cap 2, 23. Filium au- tem DEI hæc loqui non obscurum est ex oratione universa; quia loquitur Dominus de Domino, Filius DEI de Patre: & jubet lætari in Domino DEO, in Patre, qui daturus Doctorem justitiæ & immissurus erat imbrem, & pluviam v. 23. fecitque in populo mirabilia v. 26. ac præterea recepit v. 27. se in medio Israel futurum, quæ phrasis est futuræ ἐνσαρκώσεως, & σκηνώσεως in populo, cujus etiam se DEUM fore promittit, ne pude fiat populus in se credens in æter- num. Ideo de Oeconomia incarnationis explica- tur à Cyrill. Alex. & B. Luthero. Exultationis er- go, & lætitiæ in Domino non postrema materia, & causa est, quod donet Doctorem justitiæ. Non de- sunt quidem, qui reddere malint pluviam justitiæ cum Calvino, Junio & Tremellio, ac Piscatore; impri- mis vero Job. Drusius; sed uti Novatores illi à Chal- dæo, Græcis, Latina vulgata, B. Luthero, & Interpp. plerisque recedunt, ita merito in eadem Schola illos confutavit Joh. Coccejus, & tricosæ isti, ac contortæ glossæ sententia plana, & simplex de DOCTORE JUSTITIÆ omnino præferenda est. Quis autem Doctor ille justitiæ est, quem DEUS Pater se datu- rum hic promisit, ob quem fideles universos ad ex- ultationem & gaudium provocat? Non utique Eze- chias, ut Judæi nonnulli nugantur, quibus applaudit etiam Ruffinus, eo quod excitavit Rex pientissimus populum ad pietatem, & cultum veri DEI: neque Josias, quod aliis placuit, qui aras idolorum ever- tit: quia neuter istorum Doctoris titulo uspiam in sacris literis ornatur, & Hiskia posteriorum Joëlem fuisse verisimile est. Nec de Esaia ipso hoc acci- piendum, ut contendit Grotius, qui vehementer fallitur, cum de clade Sennacheribi vaticinatum Pro- phetam esse asserit, siquidem illa jam contigerit ante Joelem, neque de Sennacheribo, sed de Chaldæo- rum exercitu in superioribus egerit Propheta. Nec vero de posterioribus Prophetis, qui scil. exacta Baby- lonica captivitate floruere, hæc Prophetia intelli- genda, quemadmodum cum recentioribus quibus- dam Rabbinis Lyranus credidit, annuente Hugone & Dionysio ut puta de Haggæo, Zacharia, & Malachia. Nam nunquam defuerunt populo Domini Docto- res, ne in ipsa quidem captivitate Babylonica; in qua in medio sui habuere Jeremiam, ne de Ezechie- le dicamus aut Daniele. Ecquis ergo Doctor ille justitiæ hic tanto cum jubilo promissus? Equidem de Doctoribus quibusvis indefinite hæc nonnullis sonare videntur, quibus DEUS nunquam desti- tuit Ecclesiam; neque abnuunt Vinarienses Para- phrastæ. Sed dubium nobis nullum est Christum de- finite hic respici, de quo hoc oraculum accipiunt non tantum Veteres nonnulli Haymo Halberstat. Remigius Antisiodorensis, Rupertus Tuitiensis, sed etiam è Nostris B. Lutherus, B. Wigandus, B. Win- ckelmannus, B. Pappus, B. Himmelius è Pontificiis Albertus M. Montanus, Vatablus, Riebera, Christo- phorus à Castro, Cornelius à Lapide, imo & è Calvi- nianis Coccejus, Paraphrastæ Belgici, Autores anno- tatorum ad Biblia Pauli Tossani Novis accessionibus nuper auctorum, nec non è Judæis ipsis Abarbenel, ac quæ instar omnium est, Paraphrasis Chaldaica. Quum enim fideles universos excitet, atque pro- vocet Dominus ad lætitiam, non ob vulgare ali- quod beneficium, sed ob istud, quod fons & scatu- rigo est omnis gaudii, & quo solo recreari poterant fideles Veteris Testamenti; cum magno desiderio id desiderantes, in quo solo gaudium & lætitiam collocant fideles Novi Testamenti, MESSIAM nempe Veteribus promissum, nobis datum, id fieri credendum est; siquidem nihil so- lemnius Prophetis sit, quam ea ratione ad gau- dium fideles excitare, promissa scilicet Messiæ donatione, vel Oeconomia adventus ejus. Quo refert etiam antecedentia S. Cyrillus, vers. 21. 22. Noli timere, terra, exulta & lætare, quoniam ma- gnificavit Dominus ut faceret: Θάρσει γῆ χαῖρε, καὶ εὐφραίνε habent LXX. Interpp. unde Cyrillus: Mos est S. Prophetis à bonis particularibus, & in paucos collatis ad universitatem, & genus ipsum verba diri- gere, ut sunt ea, quæ per Christum consecuti sumus. Horfum igitur denuo procedit nobis oratio. Quando enim datum est terræ, ut confideret? Rursum, quan- do magnificavit Dominus τὸ ποιῆσαι FACERE, nisi quando Verbum, quod erat DEUS, humanam naturam induit, ut bonis supernis terram inundans inveniretur in se credentibus ut fluvius pacis, ut tor- rens voluptatis, ut temporaneus & serotinus imber, & totius ubertatis largitor. Porro non indefinite de Doctoribus se loqui Dominus testatur, cum datu- rum DEUM non Doctores, sed μοναδικῶς & cum He emphatico, vel demonstrativo DOCTO- REM ILLUM, vaticinatur, qui nempe peculiari- ter promissus erat Mosi, quod unus ille audiendus sit, Deut. 18, 15. & describitur ab Elihu, quod ejus sit homini tradere rectitudinem DEI Job. 33, 23. Per Davidem recepit, se nomen Domini prædicaturum Psal. 22, 23. & Justitiam annunciaturum in magna Communione Psal. 40, 10. per Salomonem nos o- mnes in Scholam informationis suæ vocat Prov. 8. & 9. per Esaiam testatur Dominum sibi linguam e- ruditam dedisse, Es. 55, 4. seque esse Doctorem justi- tiæ cap. 63, 1. Doctorem, & Evangelistam gentium cap. 55, 4. qui denique de se professus ipse est in die- bus carnis suæ Matth. 23, 8. Unus est Magister Ve- ster. Doctor ille doctorum; Doctor Prophetarum, quia Spiritus Christi in eis fuit 1. Petr. 1, 11. per quem agitati ipsi sunt. 2. Petr. 1, 21. Doctor Apostolorum, quia promisit & dedit ipsis Spiritum suum Joh. 16, 7. c. 20, 22. Doctor omnium, quia unctionem accipi- mus ab eo, & unctio ejus docet nos de omnibus, 1. Joh. 2, 27.

Est itaque hic Doctor ἐξαιρέτως & κατ᾿ ἀντο- νομασίαν ita dictus utpote doctor vere divinus, quia in Sinu Patris, eique ὁμοόσιος est Joh. 1, 14. c. 10, 30. Doctor excellentissimus, quia ipsa Sapientia DEI & λόγος DEI æternus Prov. 8, 1. seqq. Job. 1, 1. Doctor universalissimus, quia nemo novit Patrem, nisi Filius & cui ille vult manifestare Matth. 11, 27. Doctor sa- luberrimus, quia verba habet vitæ æternæ Joh. 6, 68. Doctor efficacissimus, quia verba, quæ loquitur, Spi- ritus & vita sunt Joh. 6, 63. Doctor interris unicus solus audiendus Matt. 17, 1. Doctor in cælis perpetu- us & æternus jugitur Electos luce sua illuminans Ap. 21, 29. Angelosque ipsos faciei suæ conspectu infor- mans, 1. Petr. 1, 12. quem solum Angeli, & Electi in cœlis ceu dignum aperire librum obsignatum vene- rantur, & deprædicant. Ap. 5, 9. seqq. Quanquam ve- ro datus hic Doctor, missusque à Patre sit à primis statim mundi cunabulis utpote λόγος & Verbum DEI Patris, quem Patres interpretem voluntatis Dei κήρυκα ἐξαγγελτικὸν, ut & εὐαγγελιστὴν κ᾿ ἑρμηνέα τῶν μεγάλων βελημάτων τᾶ θεᾶ, LXX. Interpp. ἄγ- γελον μεγάλης βελῆς vocant: à Deo audiendus jam olim populo propositus, Ex. 23, 21. Observa eum, & audi vocem ejus; qui Adamum in Paradiso, Gen. 3, 15. Abrahamum in querceto Mamre Gen. 18. Mosen in rubo ardente, & monte Sinai instruxit, Ex. 3. & 19.

Act. 7, 30. 35. 38. locutus est Davidi, testibus verbis ejus novissimis, 2. Sam. 23, 2. misit Esaiam, cum vi- dit gloriam ejus Ef. 6, 3. seqq. Ioh. 12, 41. Promittitur tamen à Joële, eundem solenniter missum iri, ha- bitaturum in medio populi; quæ ad Oeconomiam carnis pertinent: uti Pharisæi ipsum Rabbi, Do- ctorem, & Magistrum, qui à DEO venit, professi sunt Ioh. 3, 2. Matth. 22, 16. & universus populus ac- clamavit eidem Luc. 7, 16. Vere inter nos surrexit magnus ille Propheta: atque iterum Ioh. 6, 14. Hic vere est Propheta ille, qui venturus erat in mundum.

Denique de Doctore hic agitur non vulgari, aut communi, sed dato לצדקה ad justitiam: quod ne- mini convenit, nisi CHRISTO, qui solus est ju- stitia nostra Ier. 23, 6. c. 33, 15. factus nobis à DEO Sapientia & justitia 1. Cor. 1, 30. in quo solo reddi- mur justitia DEI 2. Cor. 5, 21. Datus ergo Doctor il- le ad justitiam nobis obedientia sua tum activa tum passiva acquirendam Ef. 53, 11. Rom. 5, 18. 19. c. 8, 3. ad acquisitam nos docendam, Ef. 63, 3. nobisque annun- ciandam, Ps. 40, 10. ad justitiam & acquisitam, & an- nunciatam nobis, per Verbum, & Sacramenta ap- plicandam, nosque per eandem justos coram DEO constituendos Rom. 4, 28. c. 5, 19. ô Doctorem vere μονότροπον & singularem! ô Doctorem prorsus ἀνεκφραστον, & admirabilem! Habet enim nomen, quod nemo novit nisi ipse, & vocatur nomen ejus Ver- bum DEI Ap. 19, 12. 13. Sed de hoc Doctore plura diximus in Annotatis ad hoc vaticinium, quæ cui libuerit, adire poterit.

Cæterum ita dandus erat hic Doctor, & ita da- tus est, ut ἐξουσίαν haberet alios quoque dandiDo- ctores: quia non solum ipse ἀμέσως, & αὐτοπρο- σώπως docere voluit, sed etiam alios constituere, qui pro ipso legatione fungantur 2. Cor. 5, 20. mi- nistros suos, & dispensatores mysteriorum DEI 1. Cor. 4, 1. tum Apostolos, tum Successores eorum: quibus dicit: sicut misit me Pater, & ego mitto vos Ioh. 20, 21. imo omnes, quotquot ab orbe extitere Doctores missi sunt ab Hypostatica DEI sapientia, Hoc Do- ctore justitiæ Luc. 11, 49. nec alterius merito, nisi Doctoris hujus nobis in justitiam dati missi unquam sunt, nec nisi in nomine ejus remissionem peccato- rum, & justitiam annunciarunt. Ap. 10, 43. c. 4, 12. Nam ideo & è cælis descendere ipsum oportuit, & ascendere in cælum, ut hoc beneficium nobis ab in- formationis luce æternum exclusis, ad tenebras ex- teriores æternum damnatis acquireret, & dona ac- ciperet pro hominibus, eademque dare & conferre hominibus, adeoque etiam mittere posset de cœlo eos, qui nos erudirent ad justitiam: Ps. 68, 19. Eph. 4, 8. 9. 10. 11. Dan. 12, 3. à quo proinde semper missi sunt, & mittentur usque ad finem seculi Doctores, & Pastores ad consummationem Sanctorum, in opus ministerii, in ædificationem Corporis Christi Eph. 4, 17. hoc est, Ecclesiæ universæ, quæ in Paradiso ce- pit, nec nisi cum mundo ipso finem in his terris ha- bitura est.

Vers. eod. ET DESCENDERE FACIET AD VOS IMBREM MATVTINVM ET SEROTINVM) Semen- tis & messis tempore commodas dabit tempestates. Deut. 11, 14. Prov. 16, 16. Jerem. 5, 24. Os. 6, 3.

Verse 24. THE WINEPRESSES WITH WINE AND OIL) The Hebrew word fits oil presses no less than winepresses.

## 2:25
Verse 25. AND I WILL RESTORE TO YOU THE YEARS) I will compensate for those bad years with good years,

WHICH THE LOCUST, THE CANKERWORM, AND THE RUST, AND THE CATERPILLAR HAVE EATEN) The locust and the caterpillar. We said above that by these four devouring animals are denoted Phul, Tiglath-pileser, and Shalmaneser, and Sennacherib.

MY GREAT STRENGTH, WHICH I SENT AMONG YOU) My great army. Thus he explains what he had said obscurely, My [army], that is, which I used, as above 2, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET REDDAM VOBIS ANNOS) Compen- sabo bonis annis illos annos malos,

QVOS COMEDIT LOCVSTA, BRVCHUS, ET RVBIGO, ET ERVCA) Attelabus & eruca. His quatuor animalibus æstantibus denotari Phulem, Teglath- phalasarum, & Salmanasarem, & Sennacheribum, diximus supra.

FORTITVDO MEA MAGNA, QVAM MISI IN VOS) Exercitus meus magnus. Ita explicat, quod obscure dixerat Meus, id est, quibus ego usus sum, ut su- pra 2, 11.

## 2:26
Verse 26. YOU SHALL EAT, EATING) You shall eat by eating, that is, as much as you like.

AND YOU SHALL PRAISE THE NAME OF THE LORD YOUR GOD) By giving thanks.

AND MY PEOPLE SHALL NOT BE PUT TO SHAME FOREVER (עולם, that is, for a long time, as long as Hezekiah shall live. עולם to the Hebrews is often the life of one man.

A gloss too meager, nor confirmed by any similar example, that עולם is the life of one man. And who could ever have attained this by dreaming, that these things must be restricted to the life of Hezekiah? Finally, it has been shown before that the times of Hezekiah are not being referred to; therefore, there is no reason why we should depart from the more famous meaning of the word עולם, but rather that we should explain the present passage from similar divine promises, Is. 28:16, 1 Pet. 2:6, Rom. 10:10, as also from the axiom of Joel v. 32, subjoined: Whoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Thus we shall have here a notable Evangelical promise made to the people of the Lord, that is, to true believers: He is not put to shame forever, who, having been freed from eternal ignominy, is crowned with eternal glory. It is a litotes, or tapinosis. He shall not be put to shame by ignominy, that is, he shall be affected by glory. A negative verb placed for the contrary affirmative with emphasis, Ps. 84:12, Prov. 12:2, Is. 42:3, Rom. 1:16. Heb. 11:16.

Latin:

Vers. 26. COMEDETIS VESCENTES) Comedetis co- medendo, id est, quantum libet.

ET LAVDABITIS NOMEN DOMINI DEI VE- STRI) Gratias agendo.

ET NON CONFVNDETVR POPVLVS MEVS IN SEMPITERNVM( עולם, id est per longum tem- pus, quamdiu vivet Ezechias. עולם Hebræis sæpe unius hominis vita.

Glossa nimis jejuna, nec ullo exemplo simili comprobata, quod עולם sit unius hominis vita. Et quis unquam somniando hoc assequi potuit, hæc ad vitam Ezechia restringenda esse? Denique non respici tempora Ezechia, antea ostensum est; non ergo est, quod discedamus à famosiori significatio- ne vocis עולם, quin è similibus potius promissioni- bus divinis præsentem explicemus, Ef. 28, 16. 1. Petr. 2, 6. Rom. 10, 10. ut & è Joëlis axiomate v. 32. sub- juncto: Quisquis invocaverit nomen Domini, sal- vus erit. Ita habebimus hic insignem promissionem Evangelicam populo Domini, h. e. vere credenti- bus factam: Non confunditur in æternum, qui ab æ- terna ignominia liberatus, æterna gloria corona- tur. Est litote, vel tapinosis. Non confundetur ignomi- nia, id est, afficietur gloria. Verbum negans pro con- trario affirmante cum emphasi positum Ps. 84, 12. Prov. 12, 2. Ef. 42, 3. Rom. 1, 16. Ebr. 11, 16.

## 2:29
Ver. 29. AND UPON MY SERVANTS AND HANDMAIDS IN THOSE DAYS I WILL POUR OUT MY SPIRIT) In the Hebrew, 'my' is not there: and the sense is: I will impart even to those who will seem the most vile, if not prophecy and dreams, certainly some extraordinary and heavenly motions. The Hebrews are accustomed to use the Holy Spirit for a gift below prophecy: but that distinction is not perpetual in the books of the Old or New Testament. All these things were fulfilled much more excellently than then in the Christian Church, to which Peter most aptly adapts these things in Acts 2.

Latin:

Vers. 29. SEDET SVPER SERVOS MEOS, ET AN- CILLAS IN DIEBVS ILLIS EFFVNDAM SPIRITVM MEVM) In Hebræo non est meos: & sensus est: etiam iis, qui vilissimi videbuntur, impartiar, si non Prophetiam & somnia, certe motus quosdam extraordinarios atque cœle- stes, Hebræi Spiritum S. solent usurpare de dono infra Pro- phetiam: sed id discrimen neque in Veteris, neque in N. T. libris perpetuum est. Hæc omnia multo quam tunc excel- lentius impleta in Ecclesia Christiana, ad quam hæc optime aptat Petrus Act. 2.

## 2:30
V. 30. AND I WILL SHOW WONDERS IN HEAVEN AND IN EARTH, BLOOD AND FIRE AND PILLARS OF SMOKE) Comets, burning swords, and other figures of that kind are accustomed to precede great upheavals of things. But this treats of the coming of Nebuchadnezzar, who inundated Judea with blood, and having burned cities, towns, and villages, filled everything with fire and smoke. Is. 32:13, Lam. 2:5, and elsewhere passim.

Latin:

V. 30. ET DABO PRODIGIA IN COELO ET IN TERRA, SANGVINEM ET IGNEM, ET VAPOREM FVMI) Solent magnas rerum conversiones præcedere co- metæ, gladii ardentes, aliaque figura ejusmodi. Agitur autem hic de adventu Nabuchodonosori, qui Judæam sanguine inundavit, incensis autem urbibus, vicis, & villis, cuncta implevit igne & fumo. Ef. 32, 13. Thr. 2, 5. & passim alibi.

## 2:31
Ver. 31. THE SUN SHALL BE TURNED INTO DARKNESS) Namely, because of that smoke rising from everywhere. See above 2:10, and what is said there.

AND THE MOON INTO BLOOD) The moon will appear blood-colored, because of much blood drawn up from the ground into the air, for which reason it has also often been seen to rain blood.

BEFORE THE GREAT AND TERRIBLE DAY OF THE LORD SHALL COME) The destruction of the Temple and the city by the Chaldeans. But equal or greater things preceded the destruction wrought by the Romans, concerning which Christ and the Apostles spoke.

Latin:

ET LVNA IN SANGVINEM) Luna sanguinolen- ta apparebit, propter multum sanguinem ex solo in aerem attractum, qua de causa & sæpe sanguis pluisse visus.

ANTEQVAM VENIET DIES DOMINI MAGNVS ET HORRIBILIS) Excidium Templi, & urbis per Chal- dæos. Paria vero aut majora præcesserunt excidium per Romanos factum, de quo Christus & Apostoli.

## 2:32
Ver. 32. AND IT SHALL BE: WHOSOEVER SHALL CALL UPON THE NAME OF THE LORD, SHALL BE SAVED) That is, he shall preserve his life: which is denoted by an excellent figure in Ezekiel 9.

FOR IN MOUNT SION, AND IN JERUSALEM THERE SHALL BE SALVATION) That is, some shall survive the destruction, and shall be carried away as captives, as what follows in 3, 1 shows; for those words cohere with these.

AND IN THE REMNANT WHOM THE LORD SHALL CALL) Namely, in those remnants whom God shall have destined for that purpose. Thus the Chaldean. 7 is often ἐξηγητικόν. קרא for to destine. Jerem. 32, 23.

This illustrious prophecy is not only applied by Peter to the time of the New Testament, but is explained concerning the same, according to its proper sense, in Acts 2. But it is very poorly twisted by Grotius, while he draws it to Isaiah and his συγχρόνως, whereas it treats expressly of the Christian Church. And here too Grotius has imitated the blinded Jews, and

Ruffinus. For they refer these things to the times of Hezekiah and his messengers, whom he himself sent through Judea, that he might recall them to the ancestral faith. Whence Ruffinus, just like Grotius, says that Peter only accommodated these things to his own time. And that there were others who thought that the outpouring of the Spirit of piety upon the people should be understood of the time following the resolution of the Babylonian captivity. But many things clearly teach that this prophecy does not speak of the time of Hezekiah, or after the captivity was resolved, but of the time of the New Testament. First, the prophetic description of the time itself: AND IT SHALL BE AFTER THIS. That is, after the Lord has had mercy on His people after the slaughter and servitude of Babylon, has liberated it from its enemies, and has overturned the enemies themselves, and has prepared for the sons of Zion the most desired joy from the Lord, and has given them that Teacher of righteousness, with various bodily blessings. After these times, I say, He will pour out His Spirit. The LXX interpreters rendered it ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις [in the last days], whose version St. Peter confirms in Acts 2:17. By which name is designated the final time, both with respect to the Synagogue and the Jewish Polity, which were threatened with extremes, and with respect to the final grace, which was exhibited through the incarnation of the Son of God and the proclamation of the Gospel in the whole world: just as that whole time after the Messiah was exhibited is accustomed to be called the final time, because no other revelation is to be expected than that by which God spoke in His Son in the last of the days, Heb. 1:2. See Is. 4:2, Mal. 4:1, 1 Cor. 10:11. And thus also R. D. Kimchi explained the circumstance of time in this place, באחרית הימים [in the last of the days]: by which phrase they express the time of the Messiah. For the Rabbis observe: wherever that phrase occurs, there the days of the Messiah are hinted at.

Secondly, the designation of the outpouring. For by that word is not promised the usual distribution of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, such as happened either to all the faithful and holy, or even to the Prophets in the Old Testament, but a clearly most generous outpouring, by which He wills to open all the treasures of that heavenly rain, and to confer the charisms of the Holy Spirit most abundantly upon the Apostles. Which is also indicated through Isaiah 44:3, I will pour waters upon the thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground, I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thy offspring. Which force and emphasis Calvin recognized in our oracle, who for the most part is accustomed to weaken other prophecies of the Old Testament dealing with Christ in the Jewish manner. There is no doubt, he says, but that the Prophet here promises something greater than the Fathers had experienced under the law. We know that the grace of the Holy Spirit flourished even in the ancient people: but the Prophet here does not promise what the faithful had previously experienced, but something greater, as I have touched upon. And this can be gathered from the word to pour, which he uses. For שפך does not signify only to drip, but to pour in full abundance. But God did not pour out the Holy Spirit so abundantly or generously under the law, as He did after Christ was manifested. Since, therefore, a more abundant grace of the Spirit came to the Church after the advent of Christ, for that reason the Prophet here uses an unusual word, namely, that God will pour out His Spirit.

Thirdly, the description of the object into which the Spirit is to be poured: UPON ALL FLESH, which certainly cannot be so restricted as Grotius has attempted. For is this what it is, for the Spirit to be poured upon all flesh, when the gifts of the Spirit were granted to some others besides Isaiah? And were the gifts of the Spirit given only in the time of Hezekiah to others than the distinguished men of God and prophets? Or what did the times of Isaiah have that was proper and peculiar in that matter? By ALL FLESH are understood all men, Gen. 6:12, Lev. 13:18, Ps. 145:21, Is. 40:6, Rom.

3:20, so that the promise may be universal, from which no one is to be excluded, since God wills that all may become participants of the gift of the Holy Spirit, that all who do not resist God may be taught by God, John 6:46. Behold clearly, says St. Cyril, He promises that He will give the grace of the Holy Spirit, that is, a most generous donation, not as if He were to choose for Himself one or another of the Prophets, if the situation so requires: but absolutely upon all who will deserve to receive it. The difference between the Old and New Testament is indicated primarily in this way, because under the former the Spirit was not poured out upon all flesh, but especially in Judea upon the people of the Lord: now, however, it is predicted that the Holy Spirit will be poured out not in a narrow corner of the world, but through the whole world. Therefore, those 120 who were gathered in the upper room in Jerusalem are not to be understood alone by all flesh, Acts 2, with Chrysostom, hom. 2 in Acts, nor the Jews alone, as Rupert and Christoph. à Castro, who also praises Jerome and Theodoret for that opinion, because this promise was made to the Jews, and fulfilled to them by the debt of truth and faithfulness, and to the Gentiles only out of mercy, Rom. 15:8. But he confuses the promise concerning sending Christ to the Jews in the days of His flesh, of whom He was a minister and Prophet, and concerning the Holy Spirit, who was to be sent not to the Jews only, but to all after the assumption of Christ as a common Teacher, since all were to be called to the Gospel. Whence Tertullian, Jerome, Theodoret, Rupert, Albert, Lyranus, Montanus, as noted by Christoph. à Castro, say that the outpouring of the Holy Spirit was promised here both to the Jews and to the Gentiles. Which opinion agrees with the universal assertion, UPON ALL FLESH, and with the nature of the spiritual promises looking toward the times of the New Testament. Although, therefore, the prophecy began to be fulfilled in an illustrious manner in the visible outpouring of the Holy Spirit at the Feast of Pentecost, it does not, however, pertain only to that solemn act, but concerns the entire state of the final times, or the New Testament, in the manner of other universal promises.

Fourth, the distribution of the object is to be observed: Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. Your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. But also upon the menservants and maidservants in those days I will pour out my spirit. Here again is a character of the time of the N. T. For in the Old Testament, old men and young men, sons and daughters, menservants and maidservants did not receive the spirit so indiscriminately. What is brought forward concerning the sons of Isaiah from ch. 8, 18, is irrelevant, because these things looked toward later times, nor are the sons of Isaiah indicated there, but the spiritual children of the Messiah, namely the faithful, whom the Lord gave to him, as we have from the Apostolic interpretation in Heb. 2. How, however, under the N. T. are those gifts of prophecy, visions, and dreams common to all? The Prophet does not mean that all will possess those peculiar gifts which will be the property of Prophets and Teachers, but that those gifts will be communicated to more people, without distinction of age, sex, and condition, than under the Old Testament, where they were restricted to fewer. But those things which are common to all the faithful, the knowledge of God, faith, etc., are to be distributed far more broadly and copiously throughout the whole world, to be conferred without distinction upon all who are to hear the word, which was to be preached in the whole world. Tarnovius rightly says here: The O. T. differs from the New, in that in the former these gifts as it were only trickled, but in the latter they flow out in great abundance, and are poured out πλουσίως Tit. 3, 6. In the former there was only as it were a drop of them in the Prophets, in the latter there is an outpouring upon all flesh: In the former only in a hidden way, in the latter by manifest revelation. For in the New Testament the distinction of persons has been removed: there is no

Jew, or Greek, neither bond, nor free, neither male, nor female Gal. 3, 28.

Fifth, the specification of the modes of revelation. There were in the O.T. three modes in particular: prophecy, dream, vision. Num. 12, 6. Job 33, 25. Hos. 9, 7. but those happened to few: But now both prophecy, and vision, and dream are promised indiscriminately by God: not that the revelations which were made immediately to the Patriarchs and Prophets are to be granted to all, for these do not pertain to the last times, after God has spoken most recently to the Jews in his Son, and the canon of St. John has been completed, so that it admits neither addition nor any diminution Ap. 22, 18. 19. but that such things, which were once revealed to certain select persons through those extraordinary modes of revelation, prophecies, visions, and dreams, are to be openly manifested to all through ordinary revelation: so that sons and daughters, old men and young men, servants and handmaids may now have divine knowledge, which was once scarcely granted to Patriarchs, Prophets, and men of God. For Scripture uses phrases of the Old Testament to signify the goods of the New Testament, as we see happening from time to time in Prophetic predictions. And therefore nothing here do the Anabaptistic and fanatical spirit, nothing do the new prophets, Theosophists, Quakers, and men of similar bran find as support for the immediate revelations which they boast of: For extraordinary and immediate revelations are not promised here, even if the words prophecy, dream, vision seem to refer to immediate revelations made in the past. Therefore the Lord himself interprets what he wishes to be understood by prophecies, dreams, and visions, when he adds: I will pour out my spirit upon servants and handmaids. Namely, that all are to receive the spirit, who teaches us about all things 1 John 2, and through the spirit are to know those things which, in the past, men of God scarcely knew through prophecies, dreams, and visions. Which exegesis the blessed Luther rightly observed here against the Papists and Anabaptists who abuse this oracle for their own revelations. But the Prophet himself, he says, explains himself sufficiently when he mentions the spirit of the Lord being poured out upon servants and handmaids. For he does not signify new revelations through dreams and visions, but simply the gift itself of the Holy Spirit, who purifies hearts by faith and governs minds. This gift is truly of this time in the New Testament. For although even in later times the gift of prophecy, or of predictions, is not lacking, yet it must be placed far below this gift, of which the Prophet makes mention here. For true knowledge of the Son of God brings knowledge of the Father, brings remission of sins, brings governance, so that we do not yield to temptation, nor does sin rule over us, it brings in sum eternal life itself. Since the gift of prophecy concerning future events can also exist among the wicked, such as Balaam, and that Prophet of Judah, who predicts to King Jeroboam concerning Josiah and was afterwards torn by lions. Indeed, Satan himself, from the instruction of causes which he sees, often predicts future things. But this gift, which is promised here, is of such a kind that it certainly brings eternal life. Therefore it is so magnificently commended. For what are all other gifts compared to this, that the Spirit of God himself, the eternal God, descends into our minds, nay into our bodies, and dwells in us, rules and governs us? As Paul clearly says 1 Cor. 6. Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Spirit of God, who is in you? Therefore, as far as the present passage of the Prophet is concerned, prophecy, vision, dreams are one and the same, namely the knowledge of God through Christ, which the Holy Spirit makes shine through the word of the Gospel. Thus the blessed Luther. If, however, anyone wishes to understand the gift of prophecy as the gift of understanding and interpreting the scriptures, and dreams and visions as the new spiritual knowledge of God, by which we acknowledge God the Father in the Son the mediator, of which Christ speaks in John 14, 'He who sees me, sees the Father,' with Dr. Winckelman, we will not object. Although we judge the exegesis already given to be simpler and to be preferred. For the Prophet is not occupied with distinguishing those modes of revelation, since he makes them all common to all, but he only amplifies the abundance of knowledge under the New Testament through the large and copious communication of the Holy Spirit, which was to be so great that all could seem like prophets seeing and having dreams. For not even those in whom Peter testified that this prophecy was fulfilled in Acts 2 had prophecy, or dreams, or visions, yet they were filled with the Holy Spirit so that they could utter the mighty works of God in various languages, being carried by the Holy Spirit, just as the Holy Spirit gave them to speak.

Sixth, the commemoration of prodigies. For the Prophet did not keep silent about what things were to happen throughout the whole world under those times of the New Testament, when indeed this prophecy will begin to be fulfilled, and the outpouring of the Spirit will take place upon the Jews, but so that the same Spirit might further be poured out upon the Gentiles, but he indicated them openly and in express words, so that, namely, the time might be designated by a more certain character, and the fulfillment might one day become more evident: And I will show wonders in heaven, and in the earth blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come. Those prodigies cohere with the oracle concerning the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and therefore it is not to be laboriously sought to what times they ought to be referred: although Interpreters, by the variety of their explanations, as is wont to happen, have rendered the text, which is in itself sufficiently clear, obscure. For most have accepted these as concerning the signs and prodigies of the final judgment, such as Tertullian in his book on the resurrection of the flesh, chapter 22, and book 4 against Marcion, chapter 39; Origen in tract 30 on Matthew; Theodoret on this passage; Chrysostom on chapter 2 of Acts; Bede on chapter 13 of Mark; Oecumenius on Acts 2; Thomas on Matthew 24; Lyranus, Rupert, Montanus, Vatablus, whom Christoph à Castro brings forward for that opinion on this passage. Others interpret them as concerning the destruction of Jerusalem carried out by the Romans, which opinion they prove with a twofold argument: both because that destruction happened after the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and because the faithful of the Lord escaped according to this prediction, and were saved at that time. Grotius, at verse 31, acknowledges that equal or greater prodigies preceded the destruction carried out by the Romans. This opinion is attributed by Christoph à Castro to Chrysostom, Munster, and Isidore Clarius. Others explain it as concerning the destruction carried out by Nebuchadnezzar, which opinion Grotius made his own. Others understand it as concerning the siege of Jerusalem carried out by Sennacherib, that at that time such prodigies truly existed, or that by allegory the calamity which the Jews sustained was designated here. Nor do few interpret the day of the Lord as the day of Christ's passion. By which diverse interpretations the passage is only rendered doubtful, but is not explained according to the continuity of the context. Nor did Grotius state the reason why he prefers that one here concerning the arrival of Nebuchadnezzar, and since he has accepted the rest up to this point as concerning Sennacherib, it is strange that he did not similarly refer these to those times. Without doubt, however, the opinion of those who understand it as concerning the day of the arrival and passion of the Lord is more consistent with the propriety of the words and the coherence of the text. For (1) it is a discourse about that day of the Lord which is connected with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and brought it about. (2) which is conspicuous for great prodigies in heaven and on earth. (3) which is truly great and to be revered. (4) it is the day of the Lord by antonomasia. (5) which is the preparer and conciliator of our salvation, by which he brought forth and acquired for us

the Lord, so that whoever calls upon the name of the Lord may obtain eternal salvation, (6) which was followed by Salvation on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, as also in the remnant whom the Lord called. This is no other day of the Lord than the day of the advent, birth, passion, resurrection, and ascension of the Lord, or that entire time of the saving ὀικονομία, by which salvation was procured for us. For that time brought (1) the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, inasmuch as it followed the ascension of the Lord into heaven, and even now is continued by the power of the divine promise, having been done then indeed to the Apostles in a more illustrious and conspicuous manner, and visibly, but afterwards also to the firstfruits of the Gentiles in the house of Cornelius, Acts 10, and thus it happened not only to the Jews, but also to the Gentiles, at the beginnings of the Church of the New Testament through the extraordinary and illustrious gifts of the Holy Spirit. But it still happens in an invisible manner, when the Holy Spirit is poured out upon us abundantly after the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared, Tit. 3, 4.6. (2) That day was conspicuous and illustrious through various prodigies, which happened at the time of the Lord's advent, and no less at the time of the passion and resurrection in heaven and on earth: Concerning which it is helpful to hear our very blessed Luther: I judge entirely that these signs, which Joel alleges, are the same as those which are commemorated by the Evangelists as having happened during the passion of the Savior. The eclipse of the sun on the very day of the full moon was portentous, which so enveloped everything in darkness, as if a widely spread smoke were hindering the eyes, so that things placed nearby could not be seen. And the Prophet himself explains himself in this manner, when he adds about the sun being darkened, and the moon taking on the appearance of blood. But, you will say, the Evangelists did not mention the moon, and it was during the day under the earth, so that it could not be seen. I answer: It was seen at night, and what is the wonder if sad marks appeared in it also, just as in the sun? For one must believe the Prophet asserting this, even if the Evangelists mentioned nothing about the Moon. They did, however, mention the earthquake and the opening of the graves, which Joel points out when he speaks of the portents on earth. St. Cyril of Alexandria preceded Megalandrus, p. 230. The very nature of the elements, designated by the Jews impiously against Christ, also took it indignantly, and the creature, beholding the creator treated so contumeliously, mourned in a certain way, and the divine temple (as if grieving and sad along with them) was torn apart. For it is written (And the veil of the temple was rent from the top even to the bottom) and the sun, its splendor repressed, refused to shine any longer for mortals. For it brought darkness upon things from the sixth hour until the ninth. The rocks were likewise rent. Perhaps also something unusual happened around the orb of the moon, so that it seemed turned into blood. Such a thing, therefore, the holy Evangelists omitted. But from the Prophecy it may be sufficiently credible that, by the nod of the creator, signs were made not only in the sun: but that almost the entire nature of things put on a deformity and a certain unaccustomed countenance: Nor are these prodigies designated precisely as if they were to precede the day of the Lord, but the Prophet teaches that there will be prodigies, at the faces of the advent of the day of the Lord, whence these can also be referred most excellently to the concomitant portents and prodigies which happened on the day of the birth, passion, resurrection, and the very outpourings of the Holy Spirit. (3)

That day is truly great, truly tremendous and to be revered. A great day, because the greatest works were performed on it, the human race repaired, the head of the ancient serpent crushed, the sin of the whole world expiated, heaven unlocked for mortals, the greatest mysteries exhibited in it, God made visible in the flesh: the Son of God, Lord of the law, was made subject to the law, the Lord of glory crucified, the author of life killed, death swallowed up death, repaired life, the dead one triumphed over death, and restored immortality, the one cursed before God brought forth a blessing for the world, subject to the pains of hell he ascended gloriously into heaven, which truly miraculous works, and truly sublime mysteries, what things more eminent or greater can even be thought of? A tremendous and to-be-revered day, whether we look at the enemy of the human race, the Devil, and his infernal troop, to whom it was truly horrible, inasmuch as on it the head of the serpent was crushed, the works of the Devil destroyed, the infernal powers despoiled: or the human race itself, to whom it proved truly venerable, as the Church sings: Hail, festive day, to the whole world VENERABLE. For the Hebrew word הַנּוֹרָא can be rendered not only as that horrible one, but also as that to-be-revered, or venerable one: just as the verb יָרֵא, he feared, he was afraid, is used not only of servile fear, but also of reverence and filial fear, whence they derive the Greek ἱερὸς, sacred, religious, to be feared, and to be venerated, and the German Ehr/Ehren. Compare Ex. 3, 6. Deut. 6, 32. Jos. 4, v. last. Ps. 34, 10. as also Ps. 130, 4. The LXX translate in this place ἐπιφανὴς, illustrious, which translation St. Peter also approved. But what time is more illustrious than the time of the New Testament, the saving grace of God appeared. And lest anyone doubt whether these appellations fit the day of the former advent, let him compare Mal. 4, 5, where there can be no doubt that the discourse is about the first advent of the Messiah. For the same names are held there, the same manner of speaking, which is in this place: לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם יְהוָה הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא, before the coming of the day of the Lord, that great and that to-be-revered, or venerable day. (4) That day of the advent of the Lord, and of his passion or redemption to be performed in the flesh, is called in the Scriptures by antonomasia the day of the Lord, Ps. 118, 24. Mal. 4, 5. John 8, 59. and is celebrated above other days in the scriptures, Is. 61, 2. ch. 63, 4. Zech. 3, 9. in whose memory the day of the sun is called the Lord's day because of the resurrection of Christ, Rev. 1, 10, by which our redemption was consummated. Rom. 4, 24. That day is called the day of the Lord, that is, of Christ, on which our Lord is called by a special reason. For here the Lord God the Father speaks of the day of the Lord, the Son of God, the Messiah and our Lord. (5) On that day eternal righteousness and salvation were acquired and procured for us, which all enjoy who believe in Christ, and in true faith call upon the name of the Lord, as the Apostle interprets in Rom. 10, 13. From the comparison of which passage it is permitted to conclude thus: It is a question here of the day of that Lord whom all who wish to be saved are bound to call upon in true faith as their Lord: But that Lord, whom they are bound to call upon in this way, according to the interpretation of the Apostle, is Christ. For if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, you will be saved, says the Apostle in Rom. 10, and he confirms it from this oracle of ours, v. 13: for everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved. And it is a question here of the day of Christ, which is called the day of the Lord. Therefore these things are not to be understood of the day of the devastation of the Chaldeans or the Romans, but of the day of Christ. But what other Day of Christ shall we understand rather than that over which Abraham himself exulted, that he might see that day, John 8, 56. The Apostle joins and interchanges these things among themselves, to confess Jesus as Lord, and to believe that God raised him from the dead, and to this faith and confession he vindicates eternal salvation from this oracle.
