Therefore this discourse is about the day of the first advent of the Lord, on which he was delivered up for our sins, and raised for our justification, and was constituted Lord of all, rich over all who call upon him: whence is refuted at the same time that jejune gloss of Grotius, everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved, that is, he will save his life. For that which, according to the infallible interpretation of the Apostle, is to be understood concerning the manner of obtaining eternal salvation through faith in Christ, is wrongly explained as the preservation of temporal life in the destruction of the Chaldeans. (6) That day of the first coming of the Lord was followed by the preaching of the Gospel and salvation on Mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, (i.e., of the Jews) Luke 24:47. And also in the remainder, whom the Lord called, i.e., of the Gentiles, when the Apostles were sent out into the world to preach the Gospel, they made the beginning in Jerusalem. For these things were done on the day of the first coming, with which Scripture is accustomed to connect the going forth of the law from Mount Zion and the calling of the Gentiles, not with the day of the second coming. Isa. 2:2. Mic. 4:1. Isa. 60:1. seqq. etc. Grotius's gloss here is again jejune: 'on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be salvation,' that is, some shall survive the destruction, and be carried away as captives. For there is nothing here about captivity, nothing about destruction, or preservation in destruction, nor does that salvation concern temporal, but eternal salvation, as is indubitably certain from the Apostolic interpretation. And who are those remainder, whom the Lord called? The same cannot be understood as those who are to be saved on Mount Zion. For they are openly distinguished from them. For 'ו' properly has the force not of explaining, but of coupling: it ought not, therefore, to be taken 'exegetically' at will, its genuine meaning being dismissed. Nor is the discourse about the destination of certain Jews to captivity, but about the calling of others, who are distinguished from the Jews on Mount Zion and Jerusalem, i.e., the Gentiles, whom the Lord is said to be about to call. Concerning which the Blessed Luther, f. 675: 'It is clear that these, whom he calls (Scharidim) the remnant, are distinguished from the Zionites, or Jews, even by the very calling. For the promise concerning the seed was made to the Jews.' But just as in the parable of the Gospel, after the Jews refuse to come to the wedding and the Supper, the servant is sent with a new command to those who lived outside the city in the crossroads. Thus the Prophet says here that it will come to pass that the Lord will call others also outside the Church, so that they may be gathered to the Church, and they themselves also be saved. Thus, without doubt, this particle pertains to the Gentiles.

To these reasons, which solidly confirm our opinion, is added the authority of the Interpreters who have expounded the text concerning the day of the Lord's passion: for example, Cyril, whom we cited earlier, Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Albert, Hugo, Dionysius, who explain all these things concerning the time of Christ's passion. Cornelius à Lapide says this opinion is probable, and expounds it thus: 'Some Catholics think these prodigies happened 1. at Christ's birth, when the star appeared to the Magi, and the angels sang: Glory to God in the highest. 2. At Christ's resurrection, when the flashing angels struck down the soldiers guarding Christ's sepulcher, and comforted Magdalene and her companions. 3. At Christ's passion, when the sun was obscured by a universal eclipse over the whole world, the earth trembled, the rocks were split, the monuments opened, etc.' Jerome understands the blood from the blood of Christ poured out, the fire from the fire of the Holy Spirit. Of our own, we heard the Blessed Luther above, whom the Blessed Winckler followed. We insist on the circumstance of time, which the Prophet notes, and we understand those signs which are described in Matt. 27, when about the death of Christ darkness was made over the whole earth. And although the Evangelists do not make mention of the moon: yet the Prophet Joel is a witness to us greater than any exception, so that there is no doubt that bloody spots were also seen on the moon itself. So also the earth was moved, the rocks were split, the monuments opened: where likewise there is no doubt that fire and vapor of smoke erupted at the same time. BEFORE, says the Prophet, THE GREAT DAY SHALL COME.) There was no day greater than the day of the passion, death, and resurrection of Christ, the pouring out of the Holy Spirit upon the Apostles, and the propagation of the Gospel of Christ against the furies of the Devils and the World into the whole world, the abrogation of the Mosaic priesthood and Polity, and the conquest of the idolatry of the Gentiles. History is utterly ignorant of the portents which Grotius says preceded the arrival of Nebuchadnezzar in heaven and on earth. But if the blood with which Judea was inundated, and the fire and smoke from burned cities, be designated here, as Grotius wishes, would it not more correctly fit the blood poured out at the time of the destruction made by the Romans, and the most recent burning of the city and temple, which were connected with that great day of the coming of the Lord, just as the Jews in the very passion of Christ vowed such things upon themselves: His blood be upon us, and our children. Finally, the sun turned into darkness because of the smoke rising everywhere from the conflagrations, the Moon into blood because of much blood drawn from the ground into the air, can neither be counted among prodigies in heaven, nor does it fit the destruction of the Chaldeans at all, in which history does not teach that so much Jewish blood was shed: indeed, sound Rules of Hermeneutics demand that in such prodigies the literal sense be deservedly retained.

Seventh, the Apostolic explanation is to be noted. For we have it from the indubitable interpretation of St. Peter that that pouring out of the Holy Spirit was then fulfilled in an illustrious manner, or began to be fulfilled, when the Holy Spirit came on the feast of Pentecost in the form of fiery tongues upon the Apostles and other saints gathered at Jerusalem, who not only adapts this prophecy of Joel, but testifies that this prophecy treats of that pouring out, and at the same time teaches that the sentence: 'Everyone who shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved,' is to be understood concerning eternal salvation, Acts 2:16 seqq. This is what was said by the Prophet Joel: And it shall be in the last days (says the Lord) I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams: And indeed upon my servants and upon my handmaids in those days I will pour out of my spirit, and they shall prophesy: and I will give wonders in heaven above, and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And it shall be that everyone who shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. And v. 32. This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses. Exalted therefore by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, HE HAS POURED OUT this, which you now see and hear. What clearer explanation could be given? And shall we still deny, or at least remain in doubt, that Joel prophesied here concerning these times? To what purpose is it that Christ predicted this outpouring of the Holy Spirit with the same metaphor in John 7:38-39? 'He who believes in me, as the scripture says, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.' For he said this concerning the Spirit, which those who believed in him were about to receive. The Holy Spirit was not yet given (namely, according to the illustrious prophecy of Joel) because Jesus was not yet glorified. The promises of Christ concerning the baptism of the Holy Spirit also contribute to this, which likewise imply a large outpouring of the Holy Spirit, Matthew 3:11, Acts 1:5, and the large outpouring of the Holy Spirit which is brought about through Jesus Christ our Savior. Add finally that not only the orthodox Fathers, Justin with Trypho, Hilary book 8 on the Trinity, Cyril of Alexandria on this passage, Theodoret, Oecumenius on this passage, but even the Jews themselves refer these things to the times of the Messiah, as R. Saadia Gaon in Sepher Hacmunoth. chapter 8, concerning the final redeemer: 'Then prophecy shall reside in the midst of our people, so that our sons and our servants shall prophesy, according to that which is in Joel chapter 2:28, and it shall be in the last days, I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.' It is pleasing to note here toward the end of the chapter (according to the common division, not that of the original sources) the errors of the Grotius interpretation, which Cocceius noted at the conclusion in his Commentary on Joel, p. 175. The Jews, who refer this prophecy to the days of the Messiah, act more wisely than H. Grotius, who wishes it to have been entirely fulfilled before Christ. The faults of which interpretation are many. 1. To remove the prophecy concerning Christ, and the giving of the Holy Spirit, and the state of the Church under the New Testament, and to that end to enervate and empty the Scripture. 2. To make suspect the citation of this Prophecy, which is in the New Testament, whether it be from the Holy Spirit and His intention. 3. To contradict openly the fulfillments which explain the Prophecies, and which it is impossible that the Holy Spirit did not designate (Since it cannot be that Scripture is fulfilled contrary to the mind of the Holy Spirit). You will say: But nevertheless Grotius teaches that some things were more truly fulfilled in the New Testament. Resp. He leaves nothing of the New Testament except a parody. But he posits a different primary fulfillment: and he removes the analysis and demonstration according to the times. 4. To make the Scripture itself of uncertain exposition. For if it is permitted to say anything about anything, what will be the difference between Scripture and the leaves of the Sibyl? 5. To twist Scripture rashly. He makes Joel prophesying about Isaiah. And whence does he know that Joel was before Isaiah? That he is the teacher of righteousness? But this teacher was given for righteousness. And Isaiah was no more a teacher of righteousness than Moses and any Prophet. He interprets the outpouring of the Holy Spirit concerning the sons of Isaiah and Huldah. He interprets the day of the Lord concerning the Babylonian and Roman captivity at the same time, which cannot be done unless he understands universally by the day of the Lord the abolition of those things that pass away for the establishing of the eternal kingdom of liberty. Which being granted, all other things must be explained in the same emphasis. Such are the rest, in which there is nothing but the movements of a blind gladiator. Prophecies ought not to be snatched at for just anything. They are histories of future things. And the signs of the times are to be noted in them. And the emphasis is to be retained. Especially those things which are proper to Christ and the Church of the New Testament; and spiritual benefits are not to be extenuated. The Antichrist, the enemy of the kingdom of Christ, ought not to be hidden. Which Grotius seems to have sought most of all. That boasting ought not to be snatched from the Church, by which it can demonstrate itself to be absolute in the word of God, and its enemies described therein for judgment: and that boldness, by which, following the example of God Himself, Isa. 41, 21. 22. 23., it can provoke the enemies of the truth to indicate either past or future things, which will be difficult if we dream of the Babylonian captivity or Antiochus everywhere in the Scriptures. Thus Cocceius. But it is also to be observed that Grotius himself, before he allowed his eyes to be snatched away by more recent Jews, in his annotations on the Gospel, explained that passage of Joel: 'Whoever shall call upon the name of God shall escape,' concerning the calling and conversion of the Gentiles under the New Testament, at Luke 24, 47.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ET ERIT: OMNIS QVI INVOCAVERIT NOMEN DOMINI, SALVVS ERIT) Id est, vitam suam servabit: quod egregia figura denotat Ezechiel 9.

QVIA IN MONTE SION, ET IN JERVSA- LEM ERIT SALVATIO) Id est, quidam excidio erunt superstites, & captivi avehentur, ut ostendunt quæ sequun- tur 3, 1. ea enim verba cum his cohærent.

ET IN RESIDVIS QVOS DOMINVS VOCA- VERIT) Nempe in illis residuis, quos Deus ad id destina- verit. Ita Chaldæus. 7 sæpe est ἐξηγητικόν. קרא pro desti- nare. Jerem. 32, 23.

Illustre hoc vaticinium non aptatur tantum à Petro tempori N. T. sed de eodem explicatur, le- cundum proprium sensum Act. 2. pessime vero tor- quetur à Grotio, dum id trahit ad Esaiam, ejusque συγχρόνως, quod διαρρήδην agit deEcclesia Christia- na. Imitatus & hic Grotius est excæcatos Iudæos, &

Ruffinum. Illi enim ad Ezechiæ tempora, ejusque nuncios hæc referunt, quos ipse per Judæam misit, ut eos ad avitam fidem revocaret. Unde Ruffinus æque, uti Grotius, Petrum hæc tantum accommodasse suo tempori, ait. Et fuisse alios, qui putarint effusum Spiritum pietatis in populum intelligant de tempore solutionem captivitatis Babylonicæ sequuto. Sed lo- qui hoc vaticinium non de tempore Ezechiæ, aut post solutam captivitatem, sed de tempore N. Te- stamenti, multa luculenter docent. Primo ipsa tem- poris prophetica descriptio : ET ERIT POSTHÆC. Postquam scil. Dominus populi sui post cladem & servitutem Babylonicam misertus fuerit, ab hosti- bus ipsum liberavit, hostesque ipsos everterit, ac filiis Sionis gaudium desideratissimum à Domino pararit, iisque Doctorem illum justitiæ, cum varia benedictione corporali dederit. Post hæc, inquam, tempora effundet spiritum suum. LXX. interpp. reddidere ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, quarum versio- nem comprobat S. Petrus Act. 2, 17. Quo nomine designatur tempus novissimum tum respectu Syna- gogæ & Politiæ Judaicæ, cui extrema imminebant, tum respectu gratiæ novissimæ, quæ per ἐνσάρκωσιν Filii Dei & præconium Evangelii in orbe universo exhibita: quemadmodum totum illud tempus post exhibitum Messiam appellari solet novissimum, quod nulla alia revelatio expectanda sit, quam qua ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν loquutus est Deus in Filio suo Ebr. 1, 2. Vid. Es. 4, 2. Mal. 4, 1. 1. Cor. 10, 11. Atque ita etiam circumstantiam temporis exposuit R. D. Kimchi in h. l. באחרית הימים in novissimo dierum: qua phrasi tempus Messiæ exprimunt. Ob- servant enim Rabbini: ubicunque ea phrasis oc- currit, ibi innui dies Messiæ.

Secundo effusionis designatio. Voce enim illa non promittitur usitata donorum S. S. distributio, qualis contigit vel fidelibus & sanctis omnibus, vel etiam Prophetis in V. T. sed largissima plane effu- sio, qua thesauros omnes cœlestis illius imbris a- perire, & in Apostolos charismata S. S. uberrime conferre velit. Quod etiam per Esaiam 44, 3. indi- catum, effundam aquas super sitientem, & fluenta su- per aridam, effundam spiritum meum super semen tuum, & benedictionem meam super stirpem tuam. Quam vim & emphasin in nostro oraculo agnovit Calvinus, qui plerumque alias consvevit vaticinia Vet. Test. de Christo agentia more Judaico ener- vare. Non dubium est, inquit, quin Propheta hîc ali- quid majus promittat, quam senserant Patres sub le- ge. Scimus viguisse gratiam Spiritus Sancti, etiam in veteri populo: sed Propheta hîc non promittit, quod prius experti erant fideles, sed aliquid majus, quem- admodum attigi. Et hoc colligi potest ex verbo Fun- dendi, quo utitur. Nam שפך non significat tantum stillare, sed plena copia fundere. Deus autem non tam abunde neque largiter Spiritum Sanctum sub lege effudit, sicuti post Christum manifestatum. Quo- niam ergo uberior gratia spiritus contigit Ecclesiæ post Christi adventum: ideo Propheta hîc utitur verbo insolito, quod scilicet Deus spiritum suum effundet.

Tertio objecti, in quod effundendus spiritus, descriptio: SUPER OMNEM CARNEM, quod certe ita coarctari non potest, uti Grotius conatus est. Num enim hoc est, effundi spiritum super o- mnem carnem, cum dona spiritus nonnullis aliis præter Esaiam concessa? Et num Ezechiæ solum tempore aliis quam insignibus Dei viris & prophe- tis dona spiritus data? Aut quid ea in re proprium ac peculiare habuerunt Esaiæ tempora? Per O- MNEM CARNEM intelliguntur omnes homines Gen. 6, 12. Lev. 13, 18. Psal. 145, 21. Es. 40, 6. Rom.

3. 20. ut promissio sit universalis, à qua nemo ex- cludendus sit, quum Deus velit, ut omnes doni Spiritus Sancti participes fiant, omnes qui non re- pugnant Deo, docti fiant à Deo Joh. 6, 46. En per- spicue, inquit S. Cyrillus, sancti Spiritus gratiam se donaturum promittit, id est, donationem largissimam, non ut sibi Prophetas unum aut alterum, si ita ferat res, deligat: sed absolute in omnes, qui accipere me- rebuntur. Indicatur imprimis ita differentia Vete- ris & Novi Testamenti, quia sub illo non effunde- batur Spiritus super omnem carnem, sed præcipue in Judæa super populum Domini: jam vero non in angusto orbis angulo, sed per totum orbem effu- fum iri S. S. prædicitur. Non ergo tantum intelligen- di sunt per omnem carnem CXX. illi, qui Hiero- solymis congregati in cœnaculo erant Act. 2. cum Chrysost. hom. 2. in Act, non Judæi soli, ut Ruper- tus, & Christoph. à Castro, qui Hieronymum & Theodoretum etiam in eam sententiam laudat, quod Judæis hæc promissio facta, illisque ex debito veritatis & fidelitatis impleta, gentibus solum ex misericordia Rom. 15, 8. qui vero confundit pro- missionem de Christo in diebus carnis suæ Judæis mittendo, quorum fuit minister & Propheta: & de Spiritu Sanct. qui non Judæis solum, sed omnibus mittendus post assumtionem Christi ceu commu- nis Doctor, siquidem omnes ad Evangelium vo- candi fuerint. Unde Tertulian. Hieronym. Theodore- tus, Rupertus, Albertus, Lyranus, Montanus, notan- te Christoph. à Castro, tum Judæis, tum gentibus ef- fusionem S. S. promissam hic dicunt. Quæ sententia universali assertioni, super OMNEM CARNEM & promissionum spiritualium, tempora N. Test. re- spicientium indoli convenit. Quanquam ergo in Festo Pentecostes in visibili effusione S. S. vatici- nium adimpleri illustri ratione cœperit, non tamen ad illum actum solemnem tantum pertinet, sed universum statum novissimorum temporum, vel N. Test. concernit, more aliarum promissionum universalium.

Quarto observanda objecti distributio: Propheta- bunt filii vestri, & filiæ vestræ. Senes somnia somnia- bunt, & juvenes vestri visiones videbunt. Sed & super servos & ancillas in diebus illis effundam spiritum meum. Est hic iterum character temporis N. T. Nam in Veteri Testamento non ita promiscue se- nes & juvenes, filii & filiæ, servi & ancillæ spiritum accipiebant. Quod de filiis Esaiæ è c. 8, 28. adfertur, alienum est, quia hæc respiciebant tempora poste- riora, neque etiam ibi Esaiæ filii, sed Messiæ indigi- tantur liberi spirituales, fideles nempe, quos ipsi dedit Dominus, ut habemus ex interpretatione Apostolica Ebr. 2. Quomodo autem sub N. T. omni- bus communia sunt illa prophetiæ, visionum, somnio- rum dona? Non id vult Propheta, omnes illa pecu- liaria dona, quæ Prophetarum & Doctorum erunt, propria habituros, sed pluribus illa communica- tum iri, sine discrimine ætatum, sexus & conditio- nis, quam sub Vet. Test. ubi ad pauciores restricta erant. Quæ vero fidelibus omnibus communia sunt, agnitio Dei, fides &c. longe largius & copiosius per totum orbem distribuenda, omnibus verbum audituris, quod in universo mundo prædicandum erat, sine discrimine conferenda. Recte hic Tarno- vius: Differt V. T. à Novo, quod in illo tantum hæc do- na q. stillabant, in hoc autem magna copia effluant, & πλουσίως effundantur Tit. 3, 6. In illo eorum quasi gut- ta tantum erat in Prophetis, in hoc fit effusio super o- mnem carnem: In illo tantum occulto modo, in hoc manifesta revelatione. In Novo enim Testamento sublatum est personarum discrimen: ibi nullus est

Judæus, aut Græcus, neque servus, neque liber, neque mas, neque fœmina Gal. 3, 28.

Quinto modorum revelationis specificatio. Gele- bres erant in V. T. tres imprimis modi, prophetia, somnium, visio. Num. 12, 6. Job. 33, 25. Os. 9, 7. sed illi paucis obtingebant: Jam vero & prophetia, & visio & somnium promiscue à Deo promittuntur: non quod immediate revelationes quæ Patriarchis & Prophetis factæ sunt, omnibus concedendæ sint, hæ enim non pertinent ad tempora novissima, postquam Deus novissime loquutus est Judæis in Filio suo, & consummato canone S. Johannis, ut nec additionem, nec diminutionem ullam admittat Ap. 22, 18. 19. sed quod talia, quæ olim selectis qui- busdam personis patefacta sunt, per extraordina- rios illos revelationis modos, prophetias, visiones & somnia, per ordinariam revelationem omnibus pa- lam manifestanda sint: ut filii & filiæ, senes & juve- nes, servi & ancillæ jam divinitus habeant cognitio- nem, quæ vix Patriarchis, Prophetis, & viris Dei o- lim concessa. Utitur enim scriptura phrasibus Ve- teris Testamenti ad significanda bona Novi Testa- menti, ut in vaticiniis Propheticis subinde fieri vi- demus. Ideoque nihil hic spiritus Anabaptistici & fanatici, nihil Prophetæ novelli, Theosophi, Quac- queri, & similis furfuris homines pro immediatis revelationibus, quas jactant, præsidii inveniunt: Non enim extraordinaria & immediatæ revelationes hic promittuntur, etsi voces Prophetiæ, somnii, visio- nis olim factas immediatas revelationes referre vi- deantur. Ideo interpretatur ipse Dominus, quid per Prophetias, somnia & visiones intellectum ve- lit, cum addit: super servos & ancillas effundam spi- ritum meum. Quod nempe spiritum, qui nos docet de omnibus 1. Joh. 2. omnes accepturi sint, & per spiritum ea cognituri, quæ olim per Prophetias, somnia & visiones, viri Dei vix cognoscebant. Quam ἐπηξήγησιν recte B. Lutherus, hic adversus Papistas & Anabaptistas hoc oraculo pro revela- tionibus suis abutentes, observavit. Sed Propheta ipse, inquit, satis se explicat, cum de servis & ancillis commemorat spiritum Domini in eos effundendum. Non enim novas revelationes per somnia & visiones, sed simpliciter ipsum donum spiritus sancti purifican- tis fide corda & gubernantis animos significat. Hoc donum vere hujus temporis in Nov. Test. est. Etsi e- nim etiam posterioribus temporibus non desunt Pro- phetiæ, seu vaticiniorum donum, tamen id longe infra hoc donum collocandum est, de quo Propheta hic com- memorat. Vera enim cognitio Filii Dei affert cognitio- nem Patris, affert remissionem peccatorum, affert gubernationem, ne cedamus tentationi, neve domine- tur nobis peccatum, affert in summa ipsam vitam æ- ternam. Cum Prophetiæ donum de futuris eventibus etiam possit esse apud malos, sicut Bileam, & ille Juda Propheta, qui Regi Jeroboam prædicit de Josia & po- stea lacerabatur à leonibus. Quin ipse Satan ex in- structione causarum, quas videt, sæpe prædicit futura. Hoc autem donum, quod hic promittitur, ejusmodi est, ut certo afferat æternam vitam. Ideo tam magni- fice commendatur. Quid enim alia dona omnia ad hoc sunt, quod ipse Dei spiritus, æternus Deus de- scendit in nostros animos, imo in corpora nostra, inque nobis habitat, nos regit & gubernat? Sicut Paulus clare dicit 1. Cor. 6. Nescitis, quod corpora vestra sunt templa spiritus Dei, qui est in vobis? Quod igitur ad præsentem Prophetæ locum attinet, u- num sunt Prophetia, visio, somnia, nempe cogni- tio Dei per Christum, quam Spiritus Sanctus per verbum Evangelii lucere facit. Hæc B. Lutherus. Si quis autem donum Prophetiæ de dono intelligendi & interpretandi scripturas, somnia & visiones de no- vis titia Dei spirituali, qua Deum Patrem in Filio me- diatore agnoscimus, de qua Christus Joh. 14. Qui videt me, videt Patrem, cum D. Winckelm. intel- ligere velit, non refragabimur. Quamvis ἐξήγησιν jam datam ceu simpliciorem, præferendam censea- mus. Non enim in distinguendis istis modis revela- tionem occupatur Propheta, quum omnes omnibus communes faciat, sed amplificat solum ubertatem cognitionis sub Nov. Test. per largam & copiosam S. S. communicationem, quæ tanta futura, ut omnes similes Prophetis videntibus, & somnia habenti- bus videri queant. Nam nec illi quidem, in quibus hoc vaticinium impletum Petrus Act. 2. testatus est, habebant Prophetiam, aut somnia, aut visiones, replebantur tamen S. S. ut variis linguis τὰ μεγα- λεῖα τοῦ θεοῦ efferre potuerint ὑπὸ τοῦ πνέυματος ἁγίου φερόμενοι, prouti S. S. ipsis dedit eloqui.

Sexto prodigiorum commemoratio. Quæ enim sub illa Nov. Test. tempora, cum nempe incipiet compleri hoc vaticinium, & effusio spiritus super Judæos fiet, sed ut porro idem spiritus effundatur super gentes, per orbem universum eventura sint, non subticuit Propheta, sed palam & disertis ver- bis indicavit, ut sc. certiori charactere designa- retur tempus, & complementum olim evidentius fieret: Et dabo prodigia in cælo, & in terra sangui- nem & ignem, & vaporem fumi. Sol convertetur in te- nebras & Luna in sanguinem, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus & horribilis. Cohærent illa prodigia cum oraculo de effusione S. Sanct. ideoque non quæ- rendum operose est, ad quænam tempora referri debeant: quamvis Interpp. varietate explicatio- num suarum, ut fieri solet, textum per se satis lucu- lentum, obscurum reddiderint. Plerique enim de signis, & prodigiis extremi judicii hæc acceperunt, utpote Tertulianus l. de resurr. carn. cap. 22. & libr. 4. contr. Marcion. c. 39. Origenes tract. 30. in Matth. Theodoretus in h. l. Chrysostom. in cap. 2. Actor. Beda in cap. 13. Marc. Oecumen. in Actor. 2. Thom. in Matth. 24. Lyranus, Rupertus, Montanus, Vatablus, quos in eam sententiam adducit Christoph. à Castro in h. l. Alii de excidio Hierosolymitano per Romanos facto interpretantur, quam sententiam probant ge- mino argumento: tum quia excidium istud factum est post effusionem Spiritus Sancti, tum quia fideles Domini evaserunt juxta hanc prædictionem, & salvati tum sunt. Paria aut majora prodigia præces- sisse excidium per Romanos factum agnoscit Gro- tius, ad v. 31. Hæc sententia tribuitur à Christoph. à Castro Chrysostomo, Munstero, Isidoro Clario. Alii de excidio per Nebucadnezarem facto explicant, quam sententiam suam fecit Grotius. Alii de obsidio- ne Hierosolymæ per Sennacheribum facta intelligunt, quod tum ejusmodi prodigia vere extiterint, aut per allegoriam calamitas, quam sustinuere Judæi, hic designata fuerit. Nec pauci diem Domini de die passionis Christi interpretantur. Quibus diversis in- terpretationibus dubius solum redditur locus, non vero juxta συνέχειαν contextus explicatur. Neque causam Grotius dixit, cur illam de Nebucadnezaris adventu hic præferat, & quum cætera hucusque de Sennacheribo acceperit, mirum quod non simili- ter hæc ad ista tempora retulerit. Sine dubio au- tem verborum proprietati, & cohærentiæ textus magis consentanea est eorum sententia, qui de die adventus & passionis Domini intelligunt. Nam (1) de illa die Domini sermo est, quæ cum effusione Spi- ritus Sancti connexa, eamque attulit. (2) quæ pro- digiis magnis in cælo & in terra conspicua. (3) quæ vere magna & verenda. (4) κατ' ἀντονομασίαν dies Domini est. (5) quæ salutis nostræ pararia & conciliatrix est, qua peperit, & acquisivit nobis

Dominus, ut quicunque invocat nomen Domini, sa- lutem consequatur æternam, (6) quam sequuta est Salvatio in monte Sion & in Jerufalem, ut & in resi- duis, quos advocavit Dominus. Hæc nulla alia dies Domini est, quam dies adventus, nativitatis, passio- nis, resurrectionis, & adscensionis Domini, vel tempus illud universum ὀικονομίας salutiferæ, qua nobis salus parta est. Nam istud tempus attulit (1) effusionem Spiritus S. utpote quæ sequuta est ascen- sionem Domini in cœlum, atque etiamnum vigore promissionis divinæ continuatur, facta quidem tum Apostolis illustriori & conspicua ratione, & visibiliter, at postmodum etiam primitiis gentium in ædibus Cornelii, Act. 10. adeoque non Judæis solum, sed & gentibus, sub primordia Ecclesiæ N. T. per dona Spiritus S. extraordinaria atque illu- stria contigit. Sed adhuc sit invisibili ratione, cum πλεσίως effunditur in nos Spiritus Sanct. postquam ἐπεφάνη ἡ χρησότης κὲ Φιλανθρωπία τῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεῦ Tit. 3, 4.6. (2) Dies illa conspicua & illu- stris fuit per varia prodigia, quæ tempore adventus Dominici, nec minus tempore passionis & resur- rectionis in cœlo & in terra accidere: De quibus juvat audire πάνυ B. Lutherum nostrum: Omnino judico, hæc signa, quæ allegat Joel, esse eadem, quæ ab Evangelistis commemorantur facta sub passionem Sal- vatoris. Portentosa fuit ecclipfis solis in ipso plenilunii die, quæ ita involvit caligine omnia, ac si late diffu- sus fumus impediret oculos, ne in vicino posita possent conspici. Ac ipse Propheta ad hunc modum se explicat, cum addit de sole obtenebrato, & luna referente san- guinis speciem. At, inquies, Evangelistæ lunæ non meminerunt, & fuit ea interdiu sub terra, ne posset conspici. Respondeo: Noctu conspecta est integra, & quid mirum, si in ea quoque apparuerunt tristes notæ, sicut in sole. Nam Prophetæ hoc asserenti credendum est, etsi Evangelistæ nihil de Luna me- minerunt. Meminerunt autem terræ motus & aper- tionis sepulcrorum, quæ Joel ostendit, cum de por- tentis in terra loquitur. Præivit Megalandro S. Cy- rillus Alexandr. p. 230. A Judæis impie in Christum designata ipsa quoque elementorum natura indigne tulit, & creatura tam contumeliose habitum intuens creatorem, quodammodo luxit, ac divinum templum (ut æque cum illis dolens, ac mæstum) diruptum est. Scriptum quippe extat (Et velum templi scissum est a summo usque deorsum) & sol represso splen- dore suo mortalibus amplius lucere noluit. Tenebras enim rebus ab hora sexta usque ad nonam induxit. Scissæ sunt item petræ. Fortassis etiam & circa lunæ orbem inusitatum quiddam accidit, ut conversa in sanguinem videretur. Tale quiddam igitur sacri E- vangelistæ omiserunt. Verum ex Prophetia satis sit credibile, nutu conditoris non modo in sole signa facta: sed quasi universam rerum naturam deformi- tatem & vultum quendam inconsuetum induisse: Ne- que vero prodigia hæc ceu præcessura diem Domi- ni præcise designantur, sed prodigia futura docet Propheta, ad facies adventus diei Domini, unde etiam ad concomitantia portenta & prodigia, quæ in die nativitatis, passionis, resurrectionis, ipsiusque effusio- nes S. S. acciderint, hæc referri optime possunt. (3)

Dies illa vere magna, vere tremenda & verenda est. Magna dies, quia maxima in ea patrata opera, ge- nus humanum reparatum, caput serpentis antiqui conculcatum, peccatum universi orbis expiatum, cœlum mortalibus reseratum, maxima mysteria in eadem exhibita, Deus conspicuus factus in carne: Filius Dei Dominus legis subjectus est legi, Domi- nus gloriæ crucifixus, autor vitæ interfectus, mors mortem absorpsit, vitam reparavit, mortuus de morte triumphavit, & immortalitatem restituit, maledictus coram Deo benedictionem orbi pepe rit, inferni doloribus obnoxius gloriose in cœlum ascendit, quibus operibus vere miraculosis, & my- steriis vere sublimibus, quænam eminentiora aut majora vel cogitari possunt? Tremenda dies & ve- renda, sive hostem generis humani Diabolum, & catervam ejus infernalem spectemus, cui vere hor- ribilis fuit, siquidem in ea caput serpentis contri- tum, opera Diaboli destructa, potestates inferna- les exspoliatæ sint: sive ipsum genus humanum, cui vere venerabilis extitit, uti Ecclesia canit: Salva fe- sta dies toto VENERABILIS orbi. Vox enim Ebræa הַנּוֹרָא non tantum reddi potest illa horribilis, sed etiam illa reverenda, vel venerabilis: uti verbum יָרֵא timuit, veritus est, non modo de timore servili, sed etiam de reverentia ac timore filiali adhibetur, unde Græcum ἱερὸς sacer, religiosus, timendus, & ve- nerandus, & Germanicum Ehr/ Ehren deducunt. Conf. Ex. 3, 6. Deut. 6, 32. Jos. 4, v. ult. Ps. 34, 10. ut & Ps. 130, 4. LXX. vertunt hoc loco ἐπιφανὴς illustris, quam translationem etiam S. Petrus approbavit. Quodnam autem illustrius tempus est, quam tem- pus N. T. ἐπιφάνη ἡ χάρις τῶ̃ θεῶ̃ ἡ σωτήριος. Et ne ambigat quispiam, anne diei adventus prioris conveniant hæ appellationes, conferat Mal. 4, 5. ubi de adventu primo Messiæ sermonem esse, du- bitari nequit. Eadem enim ibi nomina haben- tur, eadem loquendi ratio, quæ hoc in loco: לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם יְהוָה הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא ad facies venire vel adventus dies Domini magnæ illius, & illius reve- rendæ, vel venerabilis diei. (4) Dies illa adventus Do- mini, & passionis ejus vel redemptionis in carne exequendæ in Scripturis κατ' ἀντονομασίαν dici- tur dies Domini Ps. 118, 24. Mal. 4, 5. Joh. 8, 59. & præ aliis diebus celebratur in scripturis Es. 61, 2. c. 63, 4. Zach. 3, 9. in cujus memoriam dies solis ob resurre- ctionem Christi vocatur dies Domini, Ap. 1, 10. qua nostra redemptio consummata est. Rom. 4, 24. Vo- catur ille dies dies Domini, h. e. Christi, qua Dominus noster peculiari ratione appellatur. Nam loquitur hic Dominus Deus Pater de die Domini, Filii Dei, Messiæ & Domini nostri. (5) in illa die acquisita & parta nobis est æterna justitia & salus, qua fruuntur omnes, qui credunt in Christum, & in fide vera in- vocant nomen Domini, ut interpretatur Apostolus ad Rom. 10, 13. Ex cujus loci collatione ita conclu- dere licet: De illius Domini die hic agitur, quem in- vocare vera fide, ceu Dominum suum, tenentur, quicunq; salvari volunt: At Dominus ille, quem ita invocare tenentur, interprete Apostolo, est Chri- stus. Si enim confessus ore fueris Dominum Jesum, salvus eris, ait Apostolus Rom. 10. & confirmat id ex hoc oraculo nostro v. 13. omnis enim, qui invoca- verit nomen Domini, salvus erit. Et agitur hic de die Christi, qui vocatur dies Domini. Non ergo de die vastationis Chaldæorum, aut Romanorum hæc ac- cipienda, sed de die Christi. Quem autem alium Diem Christi intelligemus potius, quam de qua i- pse Abraham exultavit, ut videret diem illum Ioh. 8, 56. Conjungit & commutat hæc inter se Apostolus, confiteri Jesum Dominum, & credere, quod Deus ipsum è morte excitavit, & huic fidei, & confessioni ex hoc oraculo vindicat salutem æternam. De die ergo ad- ventus primi Domini hic sermo est, quo traditus est propter nostra peccata, & resuscitatus propter justiti- am nostram, ac Dominus constitutus est omnium, dives super omnes invocantes ipsum: unde refellitur simul jejuna ista Grotii glossa, omnis qui invocaverit no- men Domini, salvus erit, id est, vitam suam servabit. Nam quod juxta infallibilem Apostoli interpreta- tionem de ratione consequendi æternam salutem per fidem in Christum intelligendum est, id per- peram de conservatione temporalis vitæ in exci- dio Chaldæorum, explicatur. (6) Diem illam ad- ventus primi Domini sequuta est prædicatio Evan- gelii & salvatio in monte Sion, & in Jerusalem, (h.e. Judæorum) Luc. 24, 47. nec non in residuis, quos ad- vocavit Dominus, h. e. gentium, cum emissi Apostoli in orbem terrarum ad prædicandum Evangelium, initium fecere in Jerusalem. Hæc enim facta sunt die adventus primi, cum qua Scriptura exitum le- gis e monte Sion, & vocationem gentium conne- ctere solet, non cum die adventus secundi. Es. 2, 2. Mich. 4, 1. Es. 60, 1. seqq. &c. Jejuna hic iterum est glossa Grotii, in monte Sion, & in Jerusalem erit sal- vatio, id est, quidam excidio erunt superstites, & captivi avehentur. Nihil enim hic de captivitate, nihil de excidio, aut conservatione in excidio, nec salvatio illa temporariam, sed æternam concernit sa- lutem, ut ex interpretatione Apostolica indubitato constat. Et quinam sunt illi residui, quos vocavit Do- minus? Non possunt intelligi iidem, qui in monte Sion salvandi sunt. Nam aperte ab illis distinguun- tur. Nam ו propriè habet vim non explicandi, sed copulandi: non ergo pro arbitrio, missa ejus ger- mana significatione, ἐξηγητικῶς accipi debet. Nec de destinatione Judæorum quorundam ad captivita- tem, sed de vocatione aliorum, qui à Judæis in monte Sion, & Jerusalem distinguuntur, h. e. gentium, ser- mo est, quos advocaturus dicitur Dominus. De quo B. Lutherus f. 675. Clarum est hos, quos vocat (Scharidim) reliquias, discerni à Zionitis, seu Judæis ettam ipsa vocatione. Nam Judæis promissio de semine facta est. Sicut autem in parabola Evangelii, post- quam Judæi venire ad nuptias, & ad Cænam recu- sant, servus mittitur novo mandato ad illos, qui extra civitatem in compitis habitabant. Ita hic dicit Pro- pheta futurum, ut Dominus alios quoque vocet extra Ecclesiam, ut colligantur ad Ecclesiam, & ipsi quoque salventur. Ita sine dubio hæc particula ad gentes pertinet.

Hisce rationibus sententiam nostram solide fir- mantibus accedit autoritas Interpp. qui de die passio- nis Domini textum exposuere: puta Cyrilli, quem antea adduximus, Hieronymi, Remigii, Haymonis, Al- berti, Hugonis, Dionysii, qui hæc omnia de tempore passionis Christi explicant. Cornelius à Lapide hanc sententiam probabilem esse dicit, eamque ita expo- nit: Catholici nonnulli putant hæc prodigia conti- gisse 1. in Christi nativitate, cum stella apparuit Ma- gis, & angeli cecinerunt: Gloria in excelsis Deo. 2. In Christi resurrectione, cum angeli fulgurantes perculerunt milites custodes sepulcri Christi, ac consolati sunt Magdalenam, ejusque comites. 3. In passione Christi, cum sol universali ecclipsi toto or- be obscuratus est, terra contremuit, lapides scissi sunt, monumenta aperta &c. Hieronymus sanguinem de effuso sanguine Christi, ignem de igne S. S. intel- ligit. E nostris B. Luth. superius audivimus, quem sequutus est B. Winck. Nos insistimus circumstan- tiæ temporis, quam Propheta notat, & intelligimus illa signa, quæ Matt. 27. descripta sunt, quando circa mortem Christi tenebræ factæ sunt super universam terram. Et quamvis lunæ mentionem non faciant Evangelistæ: tamen nobis omni exceptione major testis est Propheta Joel, ut dubium non sit, in ipsa lu- na etiam conspectas fuisse maculas sanguineas. Ita et- iam terra mota est, petræ scissæ sunt, monumenta aper- ta: ubi similiter dubium non est, ignem & vaporem fumi simul erupisse. ANTEQUAM, inquit Prophe- ta, VENIET DIES MAGNA.) Nulla major dies fuit die passionis, mortis & resurrectionis Christi effusionis S. S. super Apostolos, & Evangelii Chri sti, contra furores Diabolorum & Mundi, in or bem universum propagationis, abrogationis sa cerdotii & Politiæ Mosaicæ, expugnationis idolo latriæ gentium. Portenta, quæ Grotius antecessiss adventum Nebucadnezaris dicit in cœlo & in terra, ignorat prorsus Historia. Sanguis vero, quo inundata est Judæa, ignis & fumus ex incensis urbibus, si hic desi- gnetur, ut vult Grotius, annon rectius sanguini effu- so tempore excidii, per Romanos facti, & exustio- ni urbis & templi novissimæ conveniet, qua conne- xa fuere cum die illa magna adventus Domini, quemadmodum Judæi in ipsa passione Christi sibi talia voverunt: Sanguis ejus sit super nos, & filios no- stros. Denique solem conversum in tenebras propter fumum, undique ex incendiis surgentem, Lunam in san- guinem propter multum sanguinem, ex solo in aerem attractum, neque prodigiis in cœlo accenseri pot- est, neque Chaldæorum excidio omnino convenit, in quo tantum Judæorum sanguinem effusum esse, Historia non docet: imo in talibus prodigiis τὸ ῥητὸν merito retineri, sanæ Hermineutices Regu- læ postulant.

Septimo notanda Apostolica explicatio. Nam effu- sionem illam S. S. tunc illustri ratione impletam es- se, vel impleri cœpisse, cum S. S. in festo Penteco- stes in forma linguarum ignearum super Aposto- los, & alios sanctos Hierosolymis congregatos ve- nit, ex indubitata S. Petri interpretatione habemus, qui non aptat tantum hoc Joelis vaticinium, sed de illa effusione hoc vaticinium agere testatur, simul- que illam sententiam: Omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit, de salute æterna intelligendam esse docet Act. 2, 16. seqq. Hoc est, quod dictum est per Prophetam Joel: Et erit in novissimis diebus (dicit Do- minus) effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem: & prophetabunt filii vestri, & filiæ vestræ, & juvenes vestri visiones videbunt, & seniores vestri somnia som- niabunt: Et quidem super servos meos, & super ancil- las meas in diebus illis effundam de spiritu meo, & pro- phetabunt: & dabo prodigia in cœlo sursum, & signa in terra deorsum, sanguinem & ignem & vaporem fu- mi. Sol convertetur in tenebras, & Luna in sanguinem, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus & manifestus. Et erit omnis, quicunque invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit. Et v. 32. Hunc Jesum resuscitavit Deus, cu- jus nos omnes testes sumus. Dextra igitur Dei ex- altatus, & promissione S. S. à Patre accepta EFFU- DIT hoc, quod nunc videtis & auditis. Quæ luculen- tior explicatio dari poterat? Et adhuc negabimus, aut saltim dubii hærebimus, Joelem de istis tempo- ribus hic vaticinatum esse? Quo pertinet, quod Christus eadem metaphora prædixerit hanc effu- sionem S. S. Joh. 7, 38. 39. Qui credit in me, sicut scri- ptura dicit, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Hoc enim dixit de spiritu, quem accepturi erant cre- dentes in eum. Nondum erat S.S. datus (scil. juxta il- lustre Joelis vaticinium) quia Jesus nondum erat glo- rificatus. Faciunt etiam huc promissiones Christi de βαπτισμῷ S. S. quæ effusione largam S. S. iti- dem important Matth. 3, 11. Act. 1, 5. & larga effusio S. S. quæ fit per Jesum Christum Salvatorem no- strum. Adde postremo, quod non tantum Patres orthodoxi Justin. cum Tryphon. Hilar. l. 8. de Trin. Cyrill. Alex. in h. l. Theodor. Oecumen. h. l. sed etiam ipsimet Judæi hæc ad tempora Messiæ referant, ut R. Saadia Gaon in Sepher Hacmunoth. c. 8. de ulti- mo redemptore: Tunc residebit Prophetia in medio populi nostri, ita ut filii nostri & servi nostri prophetent, juxta illud Joel c. 2, 28. & erit in novissimis, effun- dam spiritum meum super omnem carnem. Nota- re hic sub finem capitis (juxta distinctionem vulga- tam, non fontium) placet ἁμαρτήματα Grotia- næ interpretationis, quæ notavit Coccejus sub co- lophonem in Comment. Joelis p. 175. Judæi, qui hanc Prophetiam referunt ad dies Messiæ, sapi- entius agunt H. Grotio; qui totam ante Chri- stum vult impletam. Cujus interpretationis vitia multa sunt. 1. Tollere vaticinium de Christo, & da- tione Spiritus sancti, & de statu Ecclesiae sub N. T. at- que eo fine scripturam enervare & exinanire. 2. Su- spectam facere citationem hujus Prophetiae, quae est in Nov. Test. an ea sit à Spiritu S. & ejus intentione. 3. Aperte implementis, quae Prophetias explicant, & quae non designasse Sp. S. impossibile est, (Quum fieri non possit, ut praeter mentem Spiritus S. scri- ptura impleatur) contradicere. Dices: Atqui ni- hilominus Grotius quaedam docet verius in N. T. impleta esse. Resp. Nihil relinquit. N. T. nisi παρω- διαν. Primum vero implementum aliud ponit: & tollit analysin & apodixin secundum tempora. 4. Ipsam scripturam facere incertae expositionis. Si enim quidvis de quovis licet dicere, quid intererit inter scripturam & folia Sibyllae? 5. Torquere scri- pturam temere. Facit Joelem vaticinantem de Esaia. Et unde scit, Joelem fuisse ante Esaiam? Doctorem justitiae illum esse? Atqui hic doctor ad justitiam datus. Et Esaias non fuit magis do- ctor justitiae, quam Moses & quivis Propheta. Ef- fusionem Spiritus S. interpretatur de filiis Esaiae & Hulda. Diem Domini interpretatur de captivita- te Babylonica & Romana simul, quod fieri non potest, nisi universim per diem Domini intelligat abolitionem transeuntium ad stabiliendum re- gnum libertatis aeternum. Quo dato alia omnia in eadem emphası explicanda erunt. Talia sunt reli- qua, in quibus nil nisi motus Andabatae. Prophe- tiae non debent rapi ad quaevis. Sunt historiae re- rum futurarum. Et signa temporum in illis anim- advertenda sunt. Et emphasis retinenda. Impri- mis quae Christo, & Ecclesiae N. T. sunt propria; & spiritualia beneficia non sunt extenuanda. Anti- Christus hostis regni Christi non debet occultari. Quod vel maxime Grotius videtur quaesivisse. Non debet Ecclesiae eripi illa gloriatio, qua se in verbo Dei absolutam, & hostes suos ibidem ad judicium descriptos demonstrare potest: & ea parrhesia, qua juxta Dei ipsius exemplum, Esa. 41, 21. 22. 23. hostes veritatis ad indicandum vel praeterita vel fu- tura potest provocare, quod difficile erit, si in scri- pturis ubique captivitatem Babylonicam vel An- tiochum somniemus. Haec Coccejus. Sed & obser- vandum, quod Grotius ipse antequam sibi oculos eripi à Judaeis passus est recentioribus, in annot. ad Evangel. locum illum Joelis: Quisquis invocabit nomen Dei evadet, de vocatione & conversione gentium sub N. T. exposuerit ad Luc. 24, 47.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. It exhibits the promises of the destruction of enemies and the happiness of the faithful.

Under the conversion of the captivity of Judah, he predicts the gathering of all hostile nations for judgment and the retaliation of those things which they exhibited to the inheritance of the Lord in the dissipation of the people, the occupation of the land of the Lord, and the selling of the people, until at last the sickles are sent in at the time of harvest, so that the winepress may overflow on the day of the coming of the Lord for the final judgment. Before which, however, the voice of the Lord will resound from Zion through the world, in whose kingdom joy and an abundance of all good things is promised to the faithful, but destruction is announced to the unfaithful.

Judgment will come to the nations of the whole world. Vers. 1.

FOR BEHOLD IN THOSE DAYS AND IN THAT TIME) Truly behold. For כי is often 'but'. These things cohere, as I said, with the preceding. He kept silent by euphemism that it would come to pass that those remnants would be carried away: but he shows it sufficiently now, when he says they will return. WHEN I SHALL CONVERT THE CAPTIVITY OF JUDAH AND JERUSALEM.) I shall have made the captives return. The same expression is in Ps. 85, 1. Ps. 126, 1. Jerem. 33, 26. ch. 39, 14. ch. 48, 46. Ezech. 29, 14. ch. 39, 15. and often elsewhere.

Latin:

CAPUT III. Promissiones excidii hostium & felici- tatis fidelium exhibet.

Sub conversionem captivitatis Judae congrega- tionem omnium gentium hostilium ad judi- cium & retaliationem eorum, quae heredita- ti Domini exhibuerunt in populi dissipa- tione, terrae Domini occupatione & populi venditione praedicit, donec tandem falces mittantur tempore messis, ut exundet torcu- lar in die adventus Domini ad judicium no- vissimum. Ante quod vero vox Domini è Zio- ne per orbem resonabit, in cujus regno fide- libus laetitia & bonorum omnium affluentia promittitur, infidelibus vero exitium indi- citur.

Judicium veniet totius gentibus orbis. Vers. 1.

QVIA ECCE IN DIEBUS ILLIS ET IN TEM- PORE ILLO) Verum ecce. Nam כי saepe est sed. Cohaerent haec, ut dixi, cum superioribus. Reticuit κατ’ ἐυφημισμὸν fore ut illi residui aveherentur: satis autem ostendit nunc, cum redituros dicit. CVM CONVERTERO CAPTIVITATEM JV- DA ET JERUSALEM.) Fecero reverti captivos. Locutio eadem Ps. 85, 1. Ps. 126, 1. Jerem. 33, 26. cap. 39, 14. c. 48, 46. Ezech. 29, 14. c. 39, 15. & alibi sæpe.

## 3:2
Vers. 2.

I WILL GATHER ALL NATIONS.) Those, namely, who treated my people badly, not because of the sins for which I permitted it, but out of hatred for me and the religion handed down by me. AND I WILL BRING THEM DOWN INTO THE VALLEY OF JOSHAPHAT.) So also the LXX, into the valley of Josaphat. But Theodotion, into the land of judgment. Nor in any other sense the Chaldean, into the valley of the division of judgment: that is, where punishments will be distributed to each according to their merits. יהושפט signifies divine judgment; משפטי יה, as Solomon Jarchi explains. Moreover, divine judgments are accustomed to be depicted in the likeness of human ones. In human judgments, judges sit in a high place; the accused stand in a lower place, which is called a valley because of the similarity. AND I WILL PLEAD WITH THEM.) I will demand the causes why they did this. WHOM THEY DISPERSED AMONG THE NATIONS AND DIVIDED MY LAND.) Not only the Assyrians and Chaldeans, but also certain neighboring peoples, relying on their help. Jer. 49, 1. Vers. 3. AND THEY CAST LOTS UPON MY PEOPLE.) As was the custom to be done concerning captives. Hence that in Virgil: 'I will take by lot.' See what we said in the third book on the Law of War and Peace, ch. 6, §. 14. AND THEY PUT A BOY IN A BROTHEL.) In the Hebrew: they gave sons for a harlot. For so that word זנה is to be interpreted, the following member indicates. The meaning is: they gave Jewish boys to harlots in place of money: as Phaedria gave the Eunuch to Thais. AND THEY SOLD A GIRL FOR WINE THAT THEY MIGHT DRINK.) For a very cheap price. Vers. 4. BUT WHAT TO ME AND TO YOU, TYRE AND SIDON AND ALL THE COAST OF THE PHILISTINES?) In the Hebrew: What are you to me? that is, why are you troublesome to me? See what I wrote at Matth. 8, 29. WILL YOU RENDER REVENGE TO ME? AND IF YOU REVENGE YOURSELVES AGAINST ME.) Here an interrogation should be placed, and 'if' for 'whether', as often with this interpreter. But the meaning seems to be: Do you repay this turn to me, and do you render this to me? namely for so many benefits conferred upon you. I WILL QUICKLY, SPEEDILY RETURN THE RECOMPENSE UPON YOUR OWN HEAD.) I indeed, since, without any injury received, you have treated my people so badly, I will return the favor to you, and indeed shortly. See Isa. 23. Ezek. 25. 26. 27. 28. Vers. 5. FOR YOU HAVE TAKEN MY SILVER AND MY GOLD, AND HAVE BROUGHT MY DESIRABLE AND MOST BEAUTIFUL THINGS INTO YOUR TEMPLES) מחמדי are precious things, as we said at Hosea 13, 15. Thus God calls here not those things which belonged to the temple and were carried off to Babylon, but those which belonged to his people, and were sold by the Chaldeans to neighbors when the city was captured. Thus also he just now said that the injury done to his people was done to himself. Vers. 6. YOU HAVE SOLD TO THE SONS OF THE GREEKS.) With whom there was great commerce with the Phoenicians from every age. Ezek. 27, 13. THAT YOU MIGHT REMOVE THEM FAR FROM THEIR BORDERS.) Ἐπ᾿ ἐξαγωγῆς: so that there would be less opportunity to redeem them. Vers. 7. I WILL RAISE THEM UP FROM THE PLACE WHERE YOU HAVE SOLD THEM.) Through Alexander and his successors, who, in favor of the Jewish nation, restored many Jews serving in Greece to liberty. Demetrius in Josephus 13, 5. Καὶ Ἰεδαίων δὲ τὰς αἰχμαλωτισθέντας κὶ δελεύοντας ἐν τῇ ἡμετέρᾳ ἀφίημι ἐλευθέρες. We have brought similar histories in the third book on the Law of War and Peace 9, 2, in the text and annotations. AND I WILL TURN YOUR RETRIBUTION UPON YOUR OWN HEAD.) I will inflict punishments upon you, which the following verses explain. Vers. 8. AND I WILL SELL YOUR SONS AND YOUR DAUGHTERS INTO THE HANDS OF THE SONS OF JUDA) Namely, when Gaza, Sidon, and Tyre were captured by Alexander. AND THEY SHALL SELL THEM TO THE SABEANS.) To the Arabians. Gen. 10, 7.

Interpreters vary greatly in the explanation of this chapter. Some Hebrews understand it concerning the victory of Josaphat reported over the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites 2 Chron. 20: but that without doubt [was] the times (Uuu) 4 of Joel

Joel’s preceded, nor is the matter here about the Ammonites and Moabites, but about the Tyrians, Sidonians, and Egyptians. (2.) Others interpret it as concerning the destruction of the Assyrians in the valley of Jehoshaphat, when Sennacherib was besieging Jerusalem, which is also the ἔκθεσις of Mariana. But neither does that explanation fit the time, and it is too manifest that the discourse here is about other enemies. Therefore Grotius himself did not refer these things to the army of Sennacherib, although he did not hesitate to refer the preceding things to it.

(3.) Others among the Hebrews, as Jerome reports, wish to refer these things partly to the times of Vespasian and Titus, and partly to the final times, in which they await a bodily restoration through the Messiah, whom they blindly expect. But in those times, it was not captivity that befell the Jews, but the destruction of their entire nation, which is not to be exchanged for better things, but is to endure until the consummation of the age, as Daniel testifies in chapter 9:26. (4.) Some refer them to the times of the persecutions under the New Testament, and of these, some wish to see here a reference to the persecutions of the Roman Emperors, Nero, Decius, Diocletian, etc., while others wish to see a reference to the persecutions of both Antichrists. (5.) There have not been wanting those who have interpreted them as referring to the times after the release from the Babylonian captivity, which opinion Grotius made his own. Although these men, which is to be well noted, do not, as Grotius does, [refer] the prodigies mentioned above to the outpouring of the Spirit. S. refer them to that very time, so that they may not thus enervate the force of the former prophecy, but rather retain it entire. Thus Cyril acknowledged that the outpouring of the Holy Spirit took place upon the risen Christ, and when the empire of death was destroyed on the days of holy Pentecost, yet he wishes these things to have happened when at last, by the permission of Cyrus, the Israelites returned into Judea, with a battle fought in the valley of Jehoshaphat, not many stadia from Jerusalem, against Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, and the Ammonites, which he confirms from tradition. And he judges that among the leaders of the enemies of the Jews at that time were the Damascenes, the Tyrians, and those who were called Philistines. So also Theodoret, although he plainly confesses that what was promised here concerning the outpouring of the Holy Spirit was completed on the day of Pentecost, yet he judges that the gathering of the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat took place not in the time of spiritual graces, but immediately after the return from Babylon. And therefore those words: Behold, I in those days, and in that time, do not refer to the preceding matters, or to those times of which mention was made before, but to the following: WHEN I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will gather all nations. If Grotius had delivered this sense, and had left the prophecy concerning the outpouring of the Holy Spirit intact according to the Apostolic interpretation, he would not have us so opposed in the explanation of the beginning of this chapter, regarding those things which are to be done after the liberation from the Babylonian captivity. Which could have been consistent with itself, even if the preceding parts treat of the times of the N. T., so that this may be the συνέχεια: There shall be in its time salvation for the Jews on mount Sion: Because the Jews shall neither be left in captivity (concerning which other Prophets had already prophesied) nor shall they be utterly oppressed by the opposing nations, nay, it shall be in that time, when I shall bring again all nations, and will plead with them for my people. It signifies the cause, says B. Wigandus, why God wills to lead the Jews back from captivity, namely that the promises concerning the Messiah may be fulfilled and perfected. He says that the enemies must be destroyed, but the Jewish Church must be preserved: and I WILL GATHER, the people having been liberated and restored. He teaches that God is about to take vengeance upon the enemies. Thus all things which are handed down in the paraphrase, and are observed by Grotius from the history of those times, will be able to be admitted. It could, however,

(6.) Perhaps not inappropriately, I have determined that an allusion is made only to those things which were then done, and that the matters of the New Testament are explained through ancient phrases and histories, on account of the analogy, which has seemed so to some: who wish these things to be understood also concerning the times of the New Testament, moved especially by the argument that it is said, IN THOSE DAYS, AND AT THAT TIME. Which, however, does not seem apodictic, since those things need not be referred to the preceding times of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit or of the wonders and portents of the day of the Lord, but can be referred to the following times, WHEN I shall turn back the captivity, in the way we have stated. Cornelius a Lapide wishes it to be alluded here to the slaughter of Sennacherib, and that it is touched upon allusively. Others think that an allusion is made to the times after the Babylonian captivity, or even to the expedition of the Moabites, Ammonites, and the children of Mount Seir, which took place in the time of Jehoshaphat. Thus the Belgian paraphrasts conclude from the initial words at that time, that this prophecy also pertains to the state of the N. T. described according to phrases drawn from the state of the V. T. And therefore, when they have translated the captivity of Judah, they understand it concerning the liberation through the Messiah, with the liberation from the Babylonian captivity being foreshadowed. Similarly, they wish for all the enemies of the Church to be understood by the Tyrians, Sidonians, & Philistines, and they think that the things which are held concerning gold & silver in v. 5 are expressed according to the style of the V. T. Similarly, B. Tarnovius explains these things regarding the future spiritual restoration of the captives by the Apostles and their successors to the Kingdom of Christ, who, just as He previously liberated His Church, will subsequently defend it against powerful enemies: and he observes the custom of the Prophets, that they often allude to bodily things and principal places even in spiritual matters, and thus he maintains that in this passage also, through those things which Israel once suffered according to the flesh, those things which the true Israel of God always suffers are metaphorically indicated. Junius and Tremellius in their notes to this passage set forth an exposition of the judgments of God against the adversaries on behalf of the Church: I will station all the adversaries as Judge before me, and before the assembly of the Church, in the sight of my whole Church: just as the valley of Jehoshaphat was situated near Jerusalem in the sight of the city. And regarding those things about Tyre and Sidon: it is a protestation, they say, by which the Prophet touches upon certain neighboring nations by name, and confirms the general judgment that is to be in that day by the prediction of particular judgments, which were soon to come upon those nations. For Isaiah, in chapters 15 and 25, prophesied these same judgments more copiously at about the same time. To which also the notes of Piscator tend.

(7.) Lambertus Danaeus makes a general promise for all times: When he shall bring back the captivity of Judah, that is, when he shall gather his dispersed Church. For this promise is general, and embraces the entire time during which the Church will be or exist in this world. For although God sometimes gathered his Church more illustriously from miserable dissipation, as after the Babylonian captivity under the Maccabees: but especially through the preaching of the Gospel after the coming of Christ: and finally in these last times, having been restored and reinstated for us by his great mercy, by the light of the Gospel, he gathers it: it is nevertheless most true that God is always present to his Church, and preserves it and breaks the force of its enemies, so that they do not utterly destroy it. Therefore, as often as God wills to restore it, then also those most certain judgments of God against the enemies of the Church, which are now denounced, appear, and are exercised by him. But here a special regard is had to the calamity predicted in chapter 2, and the restoration from the Babylonian captivity. For Danaeus acknowledges that the Prophet prophesied there concerning the Chaldeans, just as also the famine, which the Prophet predicted in chapter 1, according to it itself is not to be understood indefinitely, but to be referred to those times in which he prophesied.

(8.) The Weimar Paraphrasts refer this to the liberation from the Antichristian Babylonian captivity, and also to the divine judgments against the enemies of the Church of the New Testament, even though an allusion is made to the liberation of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity and the enemies of the Jews under the Old Testament. Such also is the interpretation of our blessed Gesner, that this concerns the wonderful preservation and protection of the Church against enemies, and especially against both Antichrists in the most turbulent times of the last age, comparing the predictions of Ezekiel concerning the army of Gog and Magog in chapters 32 and 39, and concerning the revelation of the Roman Antichrist and his slaughter by the sword of the word in Daniel 12 and Revelation 17. Which may be read in his Commentary. Similar things are found in Cocceius: But he further attempts to extract very special things from the prophetic text, which no one besides himself easily detects or is going to detect in it, even with his own spectacles applied.

(9.) There is also a singular explanation which blessed Luther provides in his Commentary, who understands the judgment against the nations not as a judgment of wrath, by which sins are condemned, but of grace, by which sins are remitted; concerning a judgment not of the law, but of the Gospel. (10.) No less singular is the ἔκθεσις of blessed Winckelmann, who adapts this chapter to the passion and death of Christ, who was judged in the valley of Jehoshaphat in place of all nations, in which point blessed D. Cramer nevertheless agrees with him in his Summary, and opines that the nations were sold to the Sabeans, when in truth all other nations came into the communion of faith with them, in which he followed blessed Luther in part.

(11.) The common gloss of the Papists is that it concerns the final judgment to be carried out in the valley of Jehoshaphat, because of which they say that all nations are to be set before Christ, who will be sitting in the air above the Mount of Olives, in that valley: see Cornelius à Lapide and Christoph à Castro on this passage, who brings in Remigius, Lyranus, Dionysius, Vatablus, and indeed Albert and Thomas on Matthew chapter 24 and in 4 Sentences distinction 48, along with all the Scholastics. See also Gregor de Valentia, Volume 12, Commentary on Thomas, page 2320; Joseph à Costa, book 4, on the final times, chapter 13; Ribera, Commentary on this passage; Maldonatus on Matthew 25, etc. But they drew this comment from Rabbinic trifles: Almost all the Rabbis, as Galatinus has it in book 8 on the arcana of the Catholic truth, chapter 15, not at all disagreeing, say that the nations which now suppress and afflict the Jewish people in this captivity are likewise to be punished by God for this in judgment, to prove which they bring forward that passage of Joel: I will gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat. It is certain, therefore, that the Papists Judaize, as has been observed among them in many other things. Cyril of Alexandria calls them the putrid and old-wives' fables of the Jews, which Jerome also noted at verse 12. To which, however, Calixtus deigned to defer so much in his work on the supreme judgment, page 106, as to assert that it does not lack probability that the Lord will appear in the supreme region of the air looking down toward Palestine and the city of Jerusalem itself when He institutes the judgment. But what probability is there here? The place of the final judgment, just like the time, is hidden in the treasures of divine wisdom. It cannot, says Bede, book 5 on Luke chapter 17, have its time or place of coming observed by mortals, which will arrive like lightning, flashing and sudden to all. Nor will all men who ever were, are, and will be, be able to be set in the valley of Jehoshaphat, which what man of sound mind would believe to be sufficient to hold countless myriads? And most think that this name is not proper here, but appellative, with Jerome leading the way on this passage: everyone who is judged is placed in a valley, which is called Jehoshaphat, that is, the judgment of the Lord; so Haymo, Albert, Abulensis, citing Christoph à Castro, who brought forward these reasons of theirs, both because it is named later the valley of decision (which word חרוץ, since it signifies not only slaughter and cutting, but also a decided and determined judgment, the LXX and Theodotion rendered as 'of justice and of judgment,' as Jerome also notes) and because this name has been imposed on different valleys, as a name common to places in which God exerts His judgment; since the valley of Jehoshaphat is near the city of Jerusalem, at the roots of the Mount of Olives, but the valley of the victory of Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20) is much further distant from the city of Jerusalem; whence the Chaldean Jonathan rendered it, 'into the valley of the distribution of judgment.' Solomon Jarchi: 'I will descend with them into the depth of judgment,' יחושפט being the same as משפטי יי, the judgments of the Lord. Arias Montanus notes that the name is not defined by the place, but the place by the name and interpretation, namely, that wherever in the world it may be, it was chosen by God in which He might exercise judgment against the impious and the enemies of His people. We do not deny, however, if someone says that there is an allusion to the valley of Jehoshaphat, with Rupert of Deutz. Rupert himself rejects the Jewish trifles of the Papists in the Glossa Ordinaria, and from the same, Lombard, book 4 of the Sentences, distinction 48: 'Some understand this childishly, that the Lord is to descend for judgment into the valley which is on the side of the Mount of Olives. Which is frivolous.' (11.) Some of our own, and especially blessed Gerhard, adapt this prophecy to the second coming of Christ, by which He is to judge the world, which place, with respect to heaven, may be mystically called the valley of Jehoshaphat: because as once a particular judgment was instituted in the valley of Jehoshaphat against the enemies of the people of God, so on the last day a universal judgment is to be instituted against all the enemies of the Church, Treatise on the Final Judgment, § 75 and § 13. But this opinion rests upon a twofold hypothesis: both that the prodigies mentioned quite often are signs of the final judgment, and the great and fearful day is the day of the Almighty, and that in this third chapter the same time is designated which was indicated in the preceding one.

With all opinions weighed by us, and the circumstances of the Prophetic text diligently compared, there seems to be no reason why we should not refer these things to the times that followed the Babylonian captivity, with Theodoret and Cyril of Alexandria, and here grant place to the Grotian explanation, but under that necessary caution which we said before must be observed, so that both the preceding things may look to the times of the New Testament, and the things which are predicted here concerning the judging of enemies may tend to this, that the people of the Lord may be preserved until the time of the mission of Christ and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the faithful may enjoy spiritual prosperity, of which it is treated here toward the end of the chapter, in the kingdom of Christ: or, since all those things can scarcely be deduced from sacred or profane history, and those which are deduced are for the most part too slight to correspond to these magnificent promises, let us say with others that there is at least an allusion to the release from the Babylonian captivity and the times that followed, in such a way that after the manner of the Prophets the histories and phrases of the Old Testament are applied to those things which are to be under the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CONGREGABO OMNES GENTES.) Eas scilicet, quæ populum meum male tractarunt, non ob peccata, pro- pter quæ ego id permisi, sed odio mei, ac religionis à me traditæ. ET DEDVCAM EAS IN VALLEM JOSA- PHAT.) Sic & LXX. εἰς τὴν κοιλάδα Ἰωσαφάτ. At Theodotio, εἰς τὴν χώραν τῆς κρίσεως. Nec alio sensu Chaldæus, in vallem divisionis judicii: id est, ubi cuique pro meritis pœnæ distri- buentur. יהושפט significat judicium divinum; משפטי יה, ut exponit Salomon Jarchi. Solent autem judicia di- vina ad instar humanorum depingi. In humanis judiciis sedent in loco sublimi judices; rei stant in loco inferiori, qui vallis ob similitudinem dicitur. ET DISCEPTABO CVM EIS.) Causas exigam, cur id fecerint. QVOS DISPERSERUN IN NATIONIBUS ET TERRAM MEAM DIVISERUNT.) Non Assyrii tan- tum & Chaldæi, sed & viciniores quidam populi, illorum fre- ti auxilio. Jer. 49, 1. Vers. 3. ET SUPER POPULUM MEUM MISE- RUNT SORTEM.) Ut de captivis fieri mos erat. Inde illud apud Virg. Excipiam sorti. Vide quæ diximus libro tertio de jure Belli ac Pacis c. 6. §. 14. ET POSUERUNT PUERUM IN PROSTIBU- LO.) In Hebræo: dederunt filios pro meretrice. Ita enim il- lud זנה interpretandum indicat membrum sequens. Sensus est: pueros Judæos donarunt meretricibus vice pecuniæ: ut Phædria Eunuchum Thaidi. ET PUELLAM VENDIDERUNT PRO VINO UT BIBERENT.) Vilissimo pretio. Vers. 4. VERUM QVID MIHI ET VOBIS, TYRUS ET SIDON ET OMNIS TERMINUS PALÆSTI- NORUM?) In Hebræo: Quid vos mihi? id est, cur mihi molesti estis? Vide quæ ad Matth. 8, 29. NUMQVID ULTIONEM VOS REDDETIS MIHI? ET SI ULCISCIMINI VOS CONTRA ME.) Hic ponenda interrogatio, & si pro an, ut sæpe apud hunc interpretem. Sed sensus videtur esse: An hanc vos vicem mihi rependitis, & hoc mihi redditis? nempe pro tot in vos collatis beneficiis. CITO, VELOCITER REDDAM VICISSITUDI- NEM VOBIS SUPER CAPUT VESTRUM.) Ego vero, cum, sine ulla accepta injuria, tam male tractaveritis po- pulum meum, vobis vicem reponam, & quidem brevi. Vide Jes. 23. Ezech. 25. 26. 27. 28. Vers. 5. ARGENTUM ENIM MEUM ET AURUM TULISTIS, ET DESIDERABILIA MEA ET PUL- CHERRIMA INTULISTIS IN DELUBRA VESTRA) מחמדי funt res pretiosæ, ut diximus Osee 13, 15. Ita hic appellat Deus non quæ templi erant, & Babylonem avecta sunt, sed ea quæ erant populi sui, & à Chaldæis, capta urbe, vicinis vendita sunt. Sic & modo sibi dixit factam inju- riam, quæ populo suo facta erat. Vers. 6. VENDIDISTIS FILIIS GRÆCORUM.) Quibus magnum ab omni ævo cum Phœnicibus commer- cium. Ezech. 27, 13. UT LONGE FACERETIS EOS DE FINIBUS SUIS.) Ἐπ᾿ ἐξαγωγῆς: quo minor esset facultas eos redi- mendi. Vers. 7. SUSCITABO EOS DE LOCO IN QVO VENDIDISTIS EOS.) Per Alexandrum, ejusque successo- res, qui in gratiam Judaicæ gentis, multos Judæos in Græcia servientes libertati reddiderunt. Demetrius apud Josephum 13, 5. Καὶ Ἰεδαίων δὲ τὰς αἰχμαλωτισθέντας κὶ δελεύοντας ἐν τῇ ἡμετέρᾳ ἀφίημι ἐλευθέρες. Similes Historias attulimus li- bro tertio de jure Belli ac Pacis 9, 2. in textu, & annotatis. ET CONVERTAM RETRIBUTIONEM VE- STRAM IN CAPUT VESTRUM.) Pœnas vobis repo- nam, quod explicant sequentia. Vers. 8. ET VENDAM FILIOS VESTROS, ET FILIAS VESTRAS IN MANIBUS FILIORUM JUDA) Nempe cum Gaza, Sidon, & Tyrus captæ ad Alexandro. ET VENUNDABUNT EOS SABÆIS.) Arabi- bus. Gen. 10, 7.

VAriant admodum Interpp. in explicatione hujusce capitis. Ebræi nonnulli de victoria Jo- sophati ab Ammonitis, Moabitis & Edomæis reportata 2. Par. 20. intelligunt: sed illa sine dubio tempora (Uuu) 4 Joelis

Joelis præcessit, neque hic de Ammonitis & Moabi- tis, sed de Tyriis, Sydoniis & Ægyptiis res est. (2.) A- lii de Assyriorum concisione in valle Josaphat, cum Sennacherib obsideret Hierosolyma, facta inter- pretantur, quæ etiam Marianæ est ἔκθεσις. Sed nec illa explicatio tempori congruit, & de aliis hosti- bus hic sermonem esse, nimis manifestum est. Ideo Grotius ipse ad Sennacheribi exercitum hæc non retulit, etsi superiora eo referre non dubitavit.

(3.) Alii ex Ebræis, perhibente Hieronymo, partim ad tempora Vespasiani & Titi ea pertinere volunt, partim ad novissima tempora, quibus corporalem restaurationem præstolantur per Messiam, quem cæci expectant. At illis temporibus non captivitas Judæis accidit, sed excidium universæ gentis ipso- rum, quod non commutandum cum melioribus, sed ad consummationem seculi duraturum est, Da- nieli teste c. 9. 26. (4.) Nonnulli ad tempora perse- quutionum sub N. T. referunt, & ex his alii ad Impe- ratorum Romanorum, Neronis, Decii, Diocletiani, &c. alii ad Antichristi utriusque persequutiones hic respici volunt. (5.) Non defuerunt qui de tempo- ribus post solutionem captivitatis Babylonicæ inter- pretati sunt, quam sententiam suam fecit Grotius. Quanquam isti, quod probe notandum, non uti Grotius, prodigia superius commemorata, ad effu- sionem Sp. S. ad illud ipsum tempus referant, ne- que vim prophetiæ superioris ita enervent, sed eandem integram retineant. Ita Cyrillus, effusio- nem Sp. S. factam esse Christo redivivo, & destru- cto mortis imperio in diebus sanctæ Pentecostes agnovit, hæc autem contigisse vult, quando Cyro tandem dimittente in Judæam Israelitæ redierunt, prælio in valle Josaphat non multis ab Hierosoly- ma stadiis, adversus Sanaballat, Tobiam, Arabes, & Ammonitas confecto, quod è traditione confir- mat. Et antefignanos inter hostes Judæorum tum fuisse arbitratur Damascenos, Tyrios, & qui appella- bantur Philistæi. Sic & Theodoreius, quamvis pla- ne in die Pentecostes completum fuisse fateatur, quod hic de effusione Sp. S. promissum, non tamen in tempore spiritualium gratiarum, sed statim post à Babylone reditum congregationem gentium in valle Josaphat factam judicat. Ideoque verba illa: Ecce ego in diebus illis, & in tempore illo, non ad præ- cedentia referunt, vel ad ea tempora, quorum an- tea mentio facta, sed ad sequentia: QUANDO con- vertero captivitatem Juda & Jerusalem, congregabo omnes gentes. Quem sensum si tradidisset Grotius, & salvam reliquisset Prophetiam de effusione Sp. S. juxta interpretationem Apostolicam, nos adeo repugnantes non haberet, in explicatione initii hujus capitis, de iis quæ gerenda sint post libera- tionem è captivitate Babylonica. Quæ sibi consta- re poterat, etsi præcedentia de temporibus N. T. agunt, ut hæc sit συνέχεια: Erit suo tempore salvatio Judæorum in monte Sion: Quia nec in captivitate relinquentur Judæi (de quâ alii Prophetæ jam vati- cinati erant) nec à gentibus adversariis opprimen- tur penitus, imo erit in tempore illo, quando convertero omnes gentes, & disceptabo cum eis super populo meo. Significat causam, inquit B. Wigandus, cur Deus velit Judæos ex captivitate reducere, nimirum ut pro- missiones impleantur, & perficiantur de Messia. Hostes, ait, delendos esse, Ecclesiam vero Judaicam conser- vandam: & CONGREGABO, liberato & resti- tuto populo. Docet vindictam Deum esse de hosti- bus sumturum. Sic omnia admitti poterunt, quæ in paraphrasi traduntur, & ex historia istorum temporum observantur à Grotio. Posset tamen

(6.) forte & non inconvenienter statui allusionem solum ad illa fieri, quæ tum gesta sunt, & explicari res novi Testamenti per phrases & historias antiquas, ob analogiam, quod nonnullis visum fuit: qui haec etiam volunt de temporibus Novi Testamenti in- telligi, eo imprimis argumento moti, quod dicatur, IN DIEBUS ILLIS, ET IN TEMPORE ILLO. Quod tamen non videtur apodicticum, quum illa non necessum sit referri ad superiora ef- fusionis Spiritus S. vel prodigiorum & portento- rum diei Domini tempora, sed ad sequentia, QUANDO convertero captivitatem, eo quo dixi- mus modo referri possint. Cornelius a Lapide ad stragem Sennacheribi hic alludi, eamque allusive perstringi vult. Alii ad tempora post captivitatem Ba- bylonicam alludi putant, vel etiam ad expeditionem Moabitarum, Ammonitarum, & filiorum montis Seir, tempore Josaphati factam. Sic Paraphrastae Belgici e verbis initialibus in tempore illo concludunt, hanc prophetiam etiam pertinere ad statum N. T. se- cundum phrases a statu V. T. depromptas descri- ptum. Ideoque illa cum convertero captivitatem Juda de liberatione e per Messiam intelligunt, adumbra- ta liberatione e Babylonica captivitate. Similiter per Tyrios, Sidonios & Philistaeos hostes omnes Eccle- siae intelligi volunt, & quae de auro & argento v. 5. habentur, secundum stylum V. T. efferri putant. Similiter fere B. Tarnovius de spirituali per Apo- stolos eorumque successores futura captivitatis re- ductione ad Regnum Christi haec explicat, qui ut antea Ecclesiam suam liberavit, deinceps eam con- tra hostes potentes defensurus sit: & observat Pro- phetarum morem, quod saepe in spiritualibus et- iam ad res corporeas, & loca praecipua alludant, adeoque vult etiam hoc loco per ea, quae Israel quon- dam secundum carnem passus est, metaphorice indica- ta esse, quae verus Israel Dei semper patitur. Junius & Tremellius in notis ad h. l. enarrationem hic ponunt judiciorum Dei contra adversarios pro Ecclesia: Si- stam velut Judex omnes adversarios coram me, & coram coetu Ecclesiae, in conspectum totius Ec- clesiae meae: quemadmodum vallis Josaphati sita erat proxime Hierusalem in conspectu urbis. Et ad illa de Tyro & Sidone: contestatio, ajunt, qua Propheta gentes aliquot propinquas nominatim per- stringit, & judicium generale in die illo futurum confirmat praedictione judiciorum singularium, quae propediem erant gentibus illis superventura. Nam haec eadem judicia sub idem tempus copiosius prophetavit Esaias c. 15. & 25. Quo etiam abeunt notae Piscatoris.

(7.) Lambertus Danaeus promissionem ge- neralem facit omnium temporum: Quum reducet captivitatem Jehudah, id est, quum suam Ecclesiam dispersam colliget. Haec enim promissio generalis est, & complectitur universum tempus quo erit seu existet in hoc mundo Ecclesia. Quanquam enim Deus non- nunquam illustrius Ecclesiam suam ex misera dissi- patione collegit, uti post captivitatem Babylonicam sub Machabaeis: praecipue vero per Evangelii prae- dicationem post Christi adventum: denique postre- mis hisce temporibus instaurata restitutaque nobis ma- gna ipsius misericordia, Evangelii luce, eam colligit: verissimum est tamen Deum semper Ecclesiae suae ades- se, & eam servare vimque hostium illius infringere, ne eam prorsus perdant. Ergo quotiescunque eam re- stituere Deus vult, tunc quoque certissima illa Dei in hostes Ecclesiae judicia, quae nunc denunciantur, ap- parent, atque ab eo exercentur. Sed hic specialis respectus habetur ad calamitatem cap. 2. praedi- ctam, & reductionem e captivitate Babylonica. De Chaldaeis enim illic vaticinatum esse Prophe- tam agnoscit Danaeus, quemadmodum & fa- mes, quam Propheta cap. 1. praedixit, secundum- ipsum non indefinite intelligenda, sed ad illa tempo- ra referenda, quibus vaticinatus est.

(8.) Ad liberationem ex captivitate Babyloni- ca Antichristiana referunt Paraphrasta Vinarienses, nec non judicia divina adversus hostes Ecclesiæ Nov. Test. utut allusio fiat ad liberationem Judæo- rum è captivitate Babylonica, & hostes Judæorum sub V. T. Qualis etiam est interpretatio B. Gefneri nostri, quod hic agatur de mirabili conservatione & protectione Ecclesiæ adversus hostes, & impri- mis contra utrumque Antichristum futura turbu- lentissimis postremæ ætatis temporibus, conferen- tis prædictiones Ezechielis de exercitu Gogi & Ma- gogi c. 32. & 39. & de Antichristi Romani revelatio- ne, ac per gladium verbi jugulatione Dan. 12. Apoc. 17. Quæ in Commentario ejus legantur. Similia penes Coccejum habentur: Sed hic præte- rea valde specialia ex textu prophetico exsculpe- re conatur, quæ nemo præter ipsum in eodem faci- le deprehendit, aut deprehensurus est, etiam ipsius- met adhibitis conspiciliis.

(9.) Singularis quoque explicatio est, quam tradit B.
