Lutherus in Commentar. qui judicium adversus gentes non de iræ judicio, quo damnantur peccata, sed gratiæ, quo remittuntur peccata, intel- ligit, de judicio non legis, sed Evangelii. (10.) Nec minus singularis est B. Winckelmanni ἔκθεσις ad passionem & mortem Christi hoc caput accommo- dantis, qui loco omnium gentium in valle Josaphat ju- dicatus sit, in quo ei tamen annuit B. D. Cramerus in Summario, & gentes Sabæis venundatas opinan- tis, quando cum eis revera omnes aliæ gentes in communionem fidei venerunt, in quibus ex parte Beat. Lutherum sequutus est.

(11.) Pontificiorum communis glossa est, de judi- cio novissimo in valle Josaphat peragendo, ob quod omnes gentes Christo in aere super montem olive- ti considenti sistendas in illa valle dicunt: vid. Cor- nel. à Lapid. & Christoph. à Castro in h. l. qui in eam sententiam adducit Remigium, Lyranum, Diony- sium, Vatablum, quin & Albertum ac Thomam in c. 24. Matth. & in 4. d. 48. cum omnibus Scholasti- cis. Vid. etiam Gregor. de Valentia Tom. 12. Com- ment. in Thom. pag. 2320. Josephus à Costa l. 4. de tempor. noviss. cap. 13. Riebera Comment. in h. l. Maldonat. in Matth. 25. &c. Sed hoc commentum hauserunt è nugis Rabbinicis: Omnes fere Rabbini, ut habet Galatinus l. 8. de arcan. Cath. verit. c. 15. minime discrepantes dicunt, quod gentes, quæ jam Ju- daicum populum in hac captivitate supprimunt & af- fligunt, similiter sint propter hoc à Deo in judicio puni- endæ, ad quod probandum illud Joelis adducunt: con- gregabo omnes gentes, & ducam illas in vallem Jo- saphat. Certum ergo est Judaizare Papistas, uti in multis aliis id penes ipsos observatum est. Cyrillus Alex. vocat putidas & aniles fabulas Judæorum, quas notavit etiam Hieronym. ad v. 12. Quibus tn. tantum deferre dignatus est Calixtus in de supr. Judicio p. 106. ut assereret, non carere probabilitate, Domi- num in suprema aeris regione deorsum Palestinam & ipsam urbem Jerosolymam versus spectante compari- turum, cum instituet judicium. Sed quæ hic proba- bilitas? Locus judicii novissimi, æque ut tempus, in thesauris sapientiæ divinæ absconditus est. Non potest, inquit Bedal. 5. in Luc. cap. 17. ejus venturi tempus aut locus à mortalibus observari, qui fulguris instar omnibus coruscus & repentinus adveniet. Ne- que omnes, qui unquam fuerunt, sunt, & erunt homines, in valle Josaphat sisti poterunt, quam innumeris myriadibus capiendis sufficicere ecquis sanæ mentis homo credat. Et nomen illud non pro- prium hic esse, sed appellativum plerique censent, præeunte Hieronym. in h. l. omnis, qui judicatur in valle positus est, quæ appellatur Josaphat, hoc est, Domini judicium, ita Haymo, Albertus, Abulensis, ci- tante Christ. à Castro, qui has eorum rationes ad- duxit, tum quia nominatur postea vallis concisionis (quam vocem חרוץ quum non tantum cædem & concisionem, sed etiam decisum & determinatum judicium significet, LXX. & Theodotio reddidere τῆς δίκης και τῆς κρίσεως, causæ & judicii, notante etiam Hieronymo) tum quia nomen hæc diversis vallibus impositum est, ceu nomen commune locis, in quibus Deus exerit judicium suum; Siquidem vallis Josaphat juxta urbem sit Jerusalem, ad radices montis oliveti, multo longius autem distet vallis vi- ctoriæ Josaphat 2. Par. 20. ab urbe Hierosolyma; unde Chaldæus Jonathan reddidit, in vallem distri- butionis judicii. Salomon Jarchi, descendam cum eis in profundum judicii, יחושפט idem quod משפטי יי judicia Domini. Arias Montanus notat, nomen non ex loco, sed locum ex nomine & interpretatio- ne definiri, scilicet, quod ubicunque terrarum sit, à Deo delectus fuerit, in quo judicium adversus im- pios & populi sui hostes exerceat. Non abnuimus tamen, si quis alludi ad vallem Josaphat dixerit, cum Ruberto Tuitensi. Nugas Judaicas Papistarum re- jicit ipse Rupertus in glossa ordinar. & ex eodem Lombard. l. 4. sent. dist. 48. Hoc quidam pueriliter intelligunt, quod in valle, quæ est in latere montis oli- veti descensurus sit Dominus ad judicium. Quod fri- volum est. (11.) Nonnulli è nostris, & imprimis B. Gerhardus ad secundum Christi adventum hoc vati- cinium accommodant, quo orbem terrarum judi- caturus est, qui locus respectu cœli vallis Josaphat mystice vocetur: quia ut olim particulare judicium in valle Josaphat adversus hostes populi Dei insti- tutum, ita in novissimo die universale judicium in- stituendum sit adversus omnes Ecclesiæ hostes tr. de Jud. extrem. §. 75. & §. 13. Sed hæc sententia ge- mina nititur hypothesi, tum quod prodigia sæpius commemorata signa sint novissimi judicii, & dies magnus ac verendus dies παντοκριτικός sit, tum quod hoc capite tertio idem tempus designetur, quod præcedenti indicatum fuit.

Nobis expensis omnibus sententiis, textusque Prophetici circumstantiis sedulo collatis nihil cau- sæ videtur, cur non referamus hæc ad tempora ca- ptivitatem Babylonicam sequuta, cum Theodoreto & Cyrillo Alexandr. locumque Grotianæ explicationi hic concedamus, sed sub illa necessaria cautela, quam antea observandam diximus, ut & anteceden- tia ad tempora N. T. spectent, & quæ hic de hosti- bus judicandis prædicuntur, eo tendant, ut populus Domini usque ad tempus missionis Christi & effu- sionis S.S. solemnis conservetur, ac fideles spiritua- li prosperitate, de qua hic sub finem capitis agitur, in regno Christi fruantur: aut, quam vix omnia il- la è sacra vel prophana historia deduci possint, & quæ deducuntur, pleraque tenuiora sint, quum ut hisce magnificis promissis respondeant, saltem al- ludi ad captivitatis Babylonicæ solutionem, & tempo- ra postsequuta cum aliis, dicamus, ita ut more Pro- phetarum historiæ & phrases V. T. adhibeantur ad ea, quæ futura sunt sub N. T.

## 3:9
Verse 9. PROCLAIM THIS AMONG THE NATIONS) That they may note what is to be. SANCTIFY WAR) Prepare. A simile from sacrifices, which require much preparation, Jerem. 6:4, chap. 51:28. AROUSE THE MIGHTY.) As if he were to say: all things will be in vain. LET THEM ASCEND.) Into battle.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CLAMATE HOC IN GENTIBUS) Ut no- tint, quid futurum sit. SANCTIFICATE BELLUM) Præparate. Similitu- do à sacrificiis, quæ multæ egent præparationis Jerem. 6, 4. cap. 51, 28. SUSCITATE ROBUSTOS.) Quasi dicat: frustra erunt omnia. ASCENDANT.) In prælium.

## 3:10
Verse 10. BEAT YOUR PLOWSHARES INTO SWORDS) Virgil, Georgics 1. And curved sickles are forged into a rigid sword.

LET THE WEAK SAY: FOR I AM STRONG) Let even the weak increase the number, as if they could do something.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CONCIDITE ARATRA VESTRA IN GLADIOS) Virgilius Georg. 1. Et curvæ rigidum falces conflantur in ensem.

INFIRMVS DICAT: QVIA FORTIS EGO SVM) Etiam infirmi numerum augeant, quasi aliquid possent.

## 3:11
Verse 11.

ALL NATIONS FROM ROUND ABOUT) All the strength of Asia.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

OMNES GENTES DE CIRCVITV) Omnis vis Asiæ.

## 3:12
Verse 12.

LET THE NATIONS ASCEND INTO THE VALLEY OF JOSHAPHAT.) Of divine judgment, as we said above. Let them ascend, namely, as those who are held in subterranean prisons.

In what way such a paraphrase can be admitted, we have said. Others do not wish these things to be said to the enemies by irony: but to their antagonists, so that they may be animated by this κελεύσματι [exhortation]. Thus the annotations of D. Wigand hold, which it pleases me to append here: CRY OUT: The Prophet sounds the trumpet, that is, it is a grave exhortation: so that the Church may know that this prophecy will not be empty, and so that terror may be struck into the enemies, SANCTIFY THE WAR. He institutes a holy war, because a holy God commands it. Then also because of the holy cause and holy effects: because God wishes to preserve His Church. But it is preserved because of the Messiah, so that the Messiah may be exhibited in it, and may perfect the redemption of the whole human race. Above he said, sanctify the fast, sanctify the Church. AKATRA. Hypotyposis: how arms are to be prepared, and the army is to be equipped with spears. ARATRA. Plowshares. LIGONES. Sickles. INFIRM. Let no one say that he is weak, for strength will be from the Lord. For otherwise the Jews seemed to be much too feeble to conquer such great nations in war. BREAK FORTH. Gather together, join the armies. THERE TO FALL. Victory over the enemies. LET THEM ARISE. He repeats the threat again. THAT I MAY JUDGE; I will punish, and it signifies a just punishment, I will not do them an injury.

Concerning the spiritual slaughter of enemies, which is done by the sword of the word, others interpret, such as B. Winckelmann. Cocceius wishes the preaching of the word done through Wycliffe, Huss, and others to be designated as having followed. But the earlier interpretations are simpler: this Cocceian one savors of a mere ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν [private interpretation].

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ASCENDANT GENTES IN VALLEM JOSA- PHAT.) Iudicii divini, ut supra diximus. Ascendant, nem- pe, ut qui in subterraneis carceribus tenentur.

Quo pacto ejusmodi paraphrasis admitti pos- sit, diximus. Alii hæc non ad hostes per ironiam dicta volunt: sed ad eorum antagonistas, ut hoc κελεύσματι animentur. Ita habent D. Wigandi annotationes, quas hic subjungere placet: CLA- MATE: Classicum Propheta canit, id est, est exhor- tatio gravis: ut Ecclesia sciat, hanc prophetiam non fore inanem, & ut hostibus incutiatur terror, SAN- CTIFICATE BELLUM. Sanctum bellum insti- tuit, quia sanctus Deus præcipit. Deinde etiam pro- pter sanctam causam & sanctos effectus: quia Deus vult Ecclesiam suam conservare. Ea vero conserva- tur propter Messiam, ut in ea Messias exhibeatur, & redemptionem totius generis humani perficiat. Su- pra dixit, sanctificate jejunium, sanctificate Eccle- siam. AKATRA. Hypotyposis: quomodo arma com- paranda, & exercitus instruendus sit lanceis. ARA- TRA. Vomeres. LIGONES. Falces. INFIRMUS. Nemo se dicat esse infirmum, nam robur erit à Domi- no. Nam alias videbantur Judæi multo esse imbel- liores, quam ut tantas gentes bello vincerent. ERUMPITE. Conglobamini, jungite exercitus. IBI OCCUMBERE. Victoria de hostibus. CONSURGANT. Iterum repetit comminatio- nem. UT JUDICEM; Puniam, & significat pœ- nam justam, non faciam eis injuriam.

De spirituali hostium occisione, quæ fit gladio verbi, alii interpretantur, uti B. Winckelmannus. Prædicationem verbi factam per Wiclefum, Hus- sum, & alios consequutos designari vult Coccejus. Sed simpliciores sunt priores interpretationes: hæc Coccejana meram ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sapit.

## 3:13
Verse 13. PUT IN THE SICKLES, FOR THE HARVEST IS RIPE.) Here God addresses the Macedonians, as the ministers of His judgments. Thus elsewhere God is introduced, giving commands to the Chaldeans and Medes. Just as a field is mowed with a sickle, so the nations with a sword: it seems that the battle at Arbela is especially looked to. THE WINEPRESS IS FULL.) Namely with grapes. Thus the fields are full of soldiers from all Asia. THE WINEPRESSES OVERFLOW) They shall overflow, that is, much blood is poured out, which is accustomed to be compared with wine. Isaiah 63, 3. FOR THEIR MALICE IS MULTIPLIED.) Thus those nations have deserved. PEOPLES PEOPLES IN THE VALLEY OF DECISION.) To the valley of decision, supply, go: to the plain at Gaugamela. THE DAY OF THE LORD IS NEAR.) Divine vengeance.

Latin:

Vers. 13. MITTITE FALCES, QVONIAM MATV- RAVIT MESSIS.) Hic Deus Macedonas, tanquam judi- ciorum suorum ministros, alloquitur. Sic alibi Deus indu- citur, Chaldæis & Medis præcepta dans. Sicut falce ager demetitur, ita gentes gladio: videtur præcipue respici præ- lium ad Arbela. PLENVM EST TORCULAR.) Nempe uvis. Sic campi pleni militibus ex omni Asia. EXVBERANT TORCVLARIA) Exundent, id est, multus fundatur sanguis, qui cum vino comparari solet. Esaias 63, 3. QVIA MULTIPLICATA EST MALITIA EO- RVM.) Ita meruere illæ gentes. POPVLI POPVLI IN VALLE CONCISIONIS.) Ad vallem concisionis, supple, ite: in planitiem ad Gauga- mela. JVXTA EST DIES DOMINI.) Ultio divina.

## 3:15
Verse 15. THE SUN AND THE MOON HAVE BEEN DARKENED AND THE STARS HAVE WITHDRAWN THEIR SPLENDOR.) With Persepolis smoking. See what is above 2, 10. 31.

Most people think that these things will be fulfilled at the time of the final judgment, because such things are repeated about the same time in almost the same words in Rev. 14, 15. And another Angel went out from the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat upon the cloud: Put in your sickle, and reap, because the hour has come to reap, because the harvest of the earth is ripe: and he who sat upon the cloud put in his sickle into the earth, and the earth was reaped. Where also the full and overflowing winepress is looked to in verse 9. 20. But it can be said that in the Apocalypse the universal judgment is described by the words which the Prophet used in a particular judgment against some enemies of the Church. Because there the discourse is about the hour of reaping the whole earth, here it seems to be concerned only with some nations or certain enemies of the Church. If, however, these things which are said in this place about the putting in of the sickles refer entirely to the final judgment, there will be no need to restrict the preceding things to both Antichrists, or only to those times which are about to immediately precede the supreme judgment. For could not the Prophet have joined to a particular judgment against the enemies of the Church—which is either always being carried out by God, the avenger of the Church, while He rules in the midst of His enemies, and will be carried out until the consummation of the age, or which He was once about to exercise against the enemies of the Jews—the universal and supreme judgment, which will be instituted when the harvest of the whole earth has ripened? But Grotius too rashly restricts that darkening of the Sun, Moon, and Stars to the smoke of Persepolis alone. This manner of speaking seems to have been used here allegorically for the designation of the greatest miseries, as Winckelmann noted. Wigandus has this to say about it: Exaggeration: The slaughter will be so great, the destruction of the enemies so great, that even the stars will be about to abhor it. Others understand these things as referring to the prodigies which precede and denounce horrendous slaughters. If, however, the final judgment is referred to for the reason stated, these things could conveniently be referred to the prodigies about to precede the extreme judgment. Before which, indeed, the voice of the Lord will resound from Zion through the world, which was fulfilled in the time of the Apostles: Matt. 28, 19. Rom. 10, 18. Col. 1, v. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SOL ET LVNA OBTENEBRATI SVNT ET STELLÆ RETRAXERVNT SPLENDOREM SVVM.) Fumante Persepoli. Vide quæ supra 2, 10. 31.

Extremi judicii tempore hæc impletum iri, ple- rique censent, quod circa idem talia repetantur iisdem fere verbis Ap. 14, 15. Et alius Angelus exi- vit è templo, clamans voce magna, ad sedentem super nubem: Mitte falcem tuam, & mete, quia venit ho- ra, ut metatur, quoniam aruit messis terræ: & misit qui sedebat super nubem falcem suam in terram, & demessa est terra. Ubi & ad plenum & exuberans torcular respicitur vers. 9. 20. Sed dici potest in Apocalypsi verbis iis universale judicium describi quibus usus Propheta in particulari adversus hostes nonnullos Ecclesiæ judicio. Quia illic de hora me- tendi universam terram sermo est, hic de nonnul- lis gentibus vel hostibus Ecclesiæ quibusdam so- lum agi videtur. Si tamen hæc omnino respiciant judicium novissimum, quæ de falcibus mittendis hoc loco dicuntur, non opus erit restringere ante- cedentia ad Antichristum utrumque, vel ad tem- pora solum illa, quæ proxime antegressura sunt su- premum judicium. Annon enim potuit à Propheta particulari adversus hostes Ecclesiæ judicio, quod vel semper à Deo Ecclesiæ vindice peragitur, dum in medio inimicorum dominatur, & peragetur usq; ad consummationem seculi, vel quod olim adver- sus Judæorum hostes exerciturus erat, conjungi universale ac supremum judicium, quod institue- tur, cum messis naturuerit totius terræ? Illam au- tem Solis, Lunæ & Stellarum obtenebrationem ad so- lum Persepoleos fumum nimis temere restringit Grotius. Videtur hæc loquendi ratio allegorica hic esse adhibita ad maximarum miseriarum desi- gnationem, ut Winckelmannus annotavit. Wディガン- dus ita de ea habet: Exaggeratio: Tanta erit cla- des, tanta strages hostium, ut & astra sint eam abhor- ritura. Alii de prodigiis hæc intelligunt, quæ clades horrendas præcedunt, & denunciant. Si tamen dicta ratione judicium novissimum respiciatur, hæc ad prodigia judicium extremum antecessura commo- de referri poterunt. Ante quod vero vox Domini è Zion per orbem resonabit, quod Apostolorum tempore impletum est: Matth. 28, 19. Rom. 10, 18. Col. 1, v. 6.

## 3:16
Vers. 16.

AND THE LORD WILL ROAR FROM ZION, AND FROM JERUSALEM HE WILL GIVE HIS VOICE, AND THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH WILL BE MOVED, AND THE LORD IS THE HOPE OF HIS PEOPLE, AND THE STRENGTH OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.) I judge that these things should be referred to the victories of the Jews over the leaders of Antiochus. This huge benefit of God is predicted, and Isaiah 63, 7. Ezekiel 38, 18 calls it the indignation of God, and a great commotion upon the earth: who also says that He rained fire and sulfur upon the soldiers of Antiochus. The heaven was moved, that is, the Angels Dan. 12. Isa. 63, 8.

But these things, and those which follow further, deserve censure. For it is not necessary, indeed no probable reason persuades, that these should be referred to the victories of the Jews over the leaders of Antiochus. And it is false that they were predicted either by Isaiah ch. 63, 7 or by Ezekiel ch. 38, 18. Our annotations have proven that far different things are handed down there. We do not wish to do what has already been done. Nor do we judge it necessary to refute the Grotian gloss at length. For if anyone should say that it coheres not badly with the former things, it is known that the laws of good hermeneutics warn that not just any connection, but primarily the connection and evidence of the words of the text themselves must be observed, lest the force and energy of the words in the text itself, which is the matter at hand, be distorted on account of a preconceived coherence of the context. And it is too manifest that the promises which the Prophet adds here are too extensive to be restricted to the state of the Jews under those times. For the rest, these will cohere properly with the preceding (however those may be understood regarding the deletion of the enemies of Judea) even if this last part of the prophecy is referred to spiritual benefits under the New Testament. For God did not only promise the Jews after the return from Babylon the deletion of enemies and the preservation of the Church until the times of the Messiah, but primarily He also promised grace under the Messiah and the times of the New Testament, which the faithful longed for most of all. For their whole hope was fixed on the Messiah, who was the expectation and consolation of the true Israel even under the Old Testament. What is more, the promises made here by Joel have seemed so august and distinguished to many that they have judged that their fulfillment should not even be sought in the kingdom of grace under the New Testament, but have referred them to the kingdom of glory and the other age of celestial blessedness.

Therefore, as to the roaring of the Lord from Zion, in two ways it is explained by others primarily. First, concerning the power of the preaching of the word, which had to go forth from Zion. In what manner Mr. Wigandus here establishes the prophecy concerning the public ministry to be preserved in Jerusalem at the time of the Messiah: And THE LORD; he teaches concerning Jehovah himself, that he was about to propose his voice there. For that is the end for which the Jewish polity was preserved. That roaring is referred to the terrifying law, but the voice to the Gospel: THE HEAVENS AND EARTH SHALL BE MOVED. Miracles and wonders, which were done in the times of Christ. AND THE LORD HOPE. The fruit of the word preached through the Messiah. Hope in the Lord, that is, trust in Christ. STRENGTH. Another effect of the word is solid and firm consolation, strength in all temptations, etc. Thus Wigandus. And not dissimilarly the Weimar Paraphrasts: The Lord will, before the day of judgment, cause his Gospel to resound powerfully from Zion and Jerusalem into all the world, and announce the coming day of judgment to all men, that they may do penance. Matt. 24:14, Acts 17:31. Luther had preceded this in his Commentary on Joel. In the first place, this roaring is placed, which is a symbol of the doctrine of repentance. For the voice of a lion is the most formidable among all living creatures, nor does it utter it unless moved by anger. Therefore, Scripture attributes roaring to a hungry lion that has obtained its prey. In this manner, the Gospel convicts the world of sin, not only so that the world may learn that it has sin—which, unless it were admonished by the word, would be secure about its sins—but it also teaches that there is no protection in us against sin. Nay, that sins are increased if anyone tries in any way to make satisfaction for them. This doctrine, impressed upon the mind, casts man down. For it not only takes away all defenses, but also proposes the inevitable judgment of eternal death. After the roaring from Zion, however, he also gives a voice from Jerusalem, that is, he speaks more gently, and no longer terrifies, but consoles souls. He proposes the most merciful mind of his Father, commands his cross to be looked upon, urges that by trust in his death we hope for the remission of sins, and by trust in his resurrection we hope for eternal righteousness and life. Therefore, at this voice sounding from Zion, heaven and earth are moved. Heaven is opened, nor does it remain closed any longer. The Father himself commends the Son to us from heaven, and not only do angels descend, mingling in conversation with men, but the Spirit of God himself descends, that he may dwell in our bodies. These things were unusual before this voice sounding from Jerusalem. The earth also puts on a completely new face. Those who were secure begin to fear God; they lay aside not only the pursuits of the flesh, but also reject the forms of worship used until now. For they see that God does not wish to be worshipped according to our own judgment, but according to the prescription of his word. This they embrace with reverence, and through faith in the word they receive the remission of sins and the Holy Spirit; through him they call upon God in all dangers, and confess his name, fearing nothing of the threats and fury of the world. Is this not a remarkable commotion, that suddenly at this voice (as the Prophet says) all things are made new! Compare what we said regarding Amos 1:2.

Then others interpret it concerning the power of the voice of Christ on the last day, especially the Papists, who say that this voice from Zion is to be heard for the reason that the Lord is to have his throne in the air above Jerusalem. See Christ. à Castro and Cornel. à Lapide. Others, however, with Montanus, say that the roaring will not be from Zion, but on account of Zion, and they do not admit that circumstance of place. They say that heaven and earth will be moved because the heavens will perish with a great noise; but the earth, and the works that are in it, will be burned up, 2 Pet. 3:10. See B. Gesnerus. But the former explanation is more common, because it was not a judicial voice condemning the unfaithful on the day of the Almighty that was to go forth from Mount Zion, but the doctrine of Christ, like the roaring of a Lion, the voice of the Lord, because that Lion of the tribe of Judah is Jehovah the Lord, according to similar prophecies in Isa. 2:2, Mic. 4:2, and the history of the Gospel in Luke 24:47.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET DOMINVS DE SION RVGIET, ET DE JERUSALEM DABIT VOCEM SUAM, ET MOVE- BUNTUR COELI ET TERRA, ET DOMINUS SPES POPULI SUI, ET FORTITUDO FILIORUM ISRAEL.) Hæc referenda censeo ad victorias Judæorum de Antiochi Ducibus. Hoc ingens Dei beneficium prædicitur & Esa. 63, 7. indignatione Dei id vocat Ezechiel 38, 18. & com- motionem magnam super terram : qui & ignem & sulphur super Antiochi milites pluisse dicit. Commotum cœlum, id est, Angeli Dan. 12. Esa. 63, 8.

Hæc vero, & quæ porro sequuntur, censuram merentur. Non enim necessum est, imo nulla vel probabilis ratio suadet, ut hæc ad victorias Judæo- rum de Antiochi Ducibus referantur. Et falsum est eas vel ab Esaia. c. 63, 7. vel ab Ezech. c. 38, 18. præ- dictas. Longe alia illic tradita, vindices nostræ an- notationes evicerunt. Nolumus actum agere. Ne- que opus judicamus prolixe Grotianam glossam refellere. Nam si quis prioribus eandem non male cohærere dixerit, notum est, leges bonæ ἑρμηνείας non qualemcunque συνέχειαν, sed imprimis ipso- rum verborum textus συνάφειαν & evidentiam observandam esse, commonefacere, ne ob præ- conceptam contextus cohærentiam verborum vis & ἐνέργεια in textu ipso, de quo res est, interverta- tur. Et ampliora esse promissa, quæ hic subjungit Propheta, quam ut eadem ad Judæorum statum sub ista tempora restringenda sint, manifestum ni- mis est. De cætero probe cohærebunt hæc superio- ribus (utut illa de hostium Judææ deletione intelli- gantur) etsi postrema hæc Prophetiæ pars ad bene- ficia spiritualia sub Novo Testamento referatur. Non enim tantum promisit Deus Judæis post reditum è Babylone, hostium deletionem, & Ecclesiæ conser- vationem usque ad tempora Messiæ, sed imprimis pollicitus etiam gratiam est sub Messia, & tempori- bus N. Test. quam fideles vel maxime anhelabant. Tota enim eorum spes defixa erat in Messiam, qui expectatio & consolatio veri Israelis etiam sub V. Test. fuit. Quid quod tam augustæ & insignes pro- missiones à Joele hic factæ plerisque visæ sint, ut ne quidem in regno gratiæ sub N. T. earum comple- mentum quærendum judicarint, sed ad regnum gloriæ, & alterum beatitudinis cœlestis seculum easdem retulerint.

Quod itaque ad Domini rugitum de Sione, bifa- riam potissimum ab aliis explicatur. Primo de vi prædicationis verbi, quod è Sion exire debuit. Quo pacto Dn. Wigandus hic vaticinium constituit de ministerio publico conservando Hierosolymis tempore Messiæ: Et DOMINUS; de ipso Je- hova docet, quod is ibi vocem suam propositurus esset. Nam iste est finis, quare politia Iudaica sit conserva- ta. Rugitus ille ad legem territantem, vox vero ad Evangelium refertur: MOVEBUNTUR CŒ- LI ET TERRA. Miracula & prodigia, quæ facta sunt temporibus Christi. ET DOMINUS SPES. Fructus prædicati verbi per Messiam. Spes in Domi- no, hoc est, fiducia in Christum. FORTITUDO. Alius effectus verbi solida & firma consolatio, robur in omnibus tentationibus &c. Ita Wigandus. Nec absimiliter Paraphrastæ Vinarienses: Der HErr wird vor dem Tag des Gerichts von Zion und Je- rusalem auß sein Evangelium in aller Welt kräff- tiglich erschallen lassen/und den vorstehenden Ge- richts-Tag allen Menschen ankündigen / daß sie Busse thun. Matth. 24, 14. Act. 17, 31. Præiverat Lu- therus Comment. in Joel. Primo loco rugitus hic poni- tur, qui doctrinæ de pœnitentia symbolum est. Est enim vox leonis inter omnia animantia maxime formidabi- lis, nec edit eam nisi commotus ira. Ideo scriptura fa- melico leoni, & prædam adepto rugitum attribuit. Ad hunc modum Evangelium arguit mundum de peccato, non solum ut mundus discat se habere peccatum, qui nisi verbo admoneretur securus de peccatis esse, sed et- iam docet, in nobis nullum esse præsidium contra pecca- tum. Quin augeri peccata, si quis ulla ratione pro iis conetur satisfacere. Hæc doctrina impressa animis de- jicit hominem. Non solum enim præsidia omnia adi- mit, sed etiam inevitabile æternæ mortis judicium proponit. Post rugitum autem ex Zion, etiam vocem dat ex Hierusalem, hoc est, loquitur blandius, nec amplius terret, sed consolatur animos. Proponit Pa- tris sui clementissimum animum, jubet respici crucem suam, hortatur, ut fiducia suæ mortis speremus remissi- onem peccatorum, & fiducia resurrectionis speremus æternam justitiam & vitam. Ad hanc igitur vocem de Zion sonantem, commovetur cælum & terra. Cæ- lum aperitur, nec manet amplius clausum. Pater ipse de cælo nobis commendat filium, & descendunt non solum Angeli miscentes colloquia cum hominibus, sed ipse Dei spiritus, ut habitet in corporibus nostris. Hæc inusitata fuerunt ante hanc vocem de Hierusa- lem sonantem. Terra quoque novam prorsus induit fa- ciem. Qui securi erant, incipiunt timere Deum, depo- nunt non solum studia carnis, sed etiam cultus usitatos hactenus abjiciunt. Vident enim Deum non velle coli ad nostrum arbitrium, sed ad verbi sui præscriptum. Hoc cum reverentia amplectuntur, & per fidem in verbum accipiunt remissionem peccatorum, & Spiri- tum sanctum, per eum invocant Deum in omnibus periculis, & confitentur nomen ejus, nihil veriti mun- di minas & furorem. Hæc annon insignis commotio est, quod subito ad hanc vocem (ut Propheta ait) no- va fiunt omnia! Conf. quæ ad Amos 1, 2. diximus.

Deinde alii de vi vocis Christi in novissimo die interpretantur, imprimis Pontificii, qui ideo hanc vocem de Sion exaudiendam dicunt, quod super Ie- rusalem in aere thronum suum habiturus sit Domi- nus. Vid. Christ. à Castro & Cornel. à Lapid. Alii tamen cum Montan. non de Zion, sed ob Zion rugi- tum illum futurum dicunt, nec περίστασιν illam loci admittunt. Cœlum autem terramque commotum iri ajunt, quia cœli magno impetu interibunt: terra autem, & quæ in ea sunt opera, comburentur 2. Pet. 3, 10. Vid. B. Gesnerus. Sed prior explicatio com- munior est, quia è monte Zion non vox condemna- toria infidelium judicialis in die παντοκριτικῷ au- diri, sed doctrina Christi, ceu rugitus Leonis, vox Do- mini, quia Leo ille de stirpe Juda est Jehovah Domi- nus, prodire debuit, juxta vaticinia similia Esa. 2, 2. Mich. 4, 2. & historiam Evangelii Luc. 24, 47.

## 3:17
Ver. 17. AND YOU SHALL KNOW THAT I AM THE LORD YOUR GOD) By experience you shall feel this. AND JERUSALEM SHALL BE HOLY, AND STRANGERS SHALL PASS THROUGH NO MORE.) With a hostile army. A similar manner of speaking to Isaiah 52:1.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET SCIETIS QVIA EGO DOMINVS DEVS VESTER ) Experimento hoc sentietis. ET ERIT JERVSALEM SANCTA, ET ALIE- NI NON TRANSIBUNT AMPLIVS.) Hostili exercitu. Simile loquendi genus Esaiae 52, 1.

## 3:18
Ver. 18. THE MOUNTAINS SHALL DRIP SWEETNESS,) They shall sweat dewy honey. AND THE HILLS SHALL FLOW WITH MILK,) Because of the abundance and succulence of the cattle, AND WATERS SHALL GO THROUGH ALL THE RIVERS OF JUDAH.) The people, free from the enemy and in great leisure, will clear out the silted-up ditches and make new aqueducts, works of deep peace. See Ezek. 47. AND A FOUNTAIN SHALL GO FORTH FROM THE HOUSE OF THE LORD, AND SHALL WATER THE TORRENT OF THORNS.) It shall water the valley of Shittim. Thus the Chaldean, and Jerome adds that the place not far from the Dead Sea is so called: whence it appears that the same aqueduct is described here which Ezekiel leads from the Temple to the Dead Sea and beyond, 47:1 to 12.

Grotius, in this most remarkable promise, understands things as merely carnal, in the Jewish manner. But Christian interpreters acknowledge with great consensus that truly spiritual goods are promised here. For to those for whom that Lord, who gave his voice from Jerusalem, is hope and strength, these benefits follow therefrom: 1. The manifestation of grace: YOU SHALL KNOW that I am Jehovah your God. (2.) Gracious presence and indwelling: That I may dwell in Zion, the mountain of my holiness, that is, in the Church, Ps. 2:6, Zech. 3:14, ch. 6:15. (3.) Sanctification: And the city of Jerusalem shall be holiness, that is, most holy, clothed by the imputation of the righteousness of the Lord her Spouse, adorned with the garment of salvation, purified by his blood, sanctified by the word and Sacraments, Isa. 61:10, 1 John 1:7, Eph. 5:25, Tit. 2:14. (4.) defense: because foreign enemies will not pass through it anymore, that is, they will not harm it, Zech. 14:11, Isa. 26:1, Ps. 146:1, or also separation from the impious and infidels, who although they may be mixed with the external assembly, yet do not belong to the internal communion of the Church: the rest contain the figurative and allegorical amplification of which promises: the mountains themselves, which otherwise are and are considered sterile, will drip must, new wine, generous, which the more robust in the Church use Deut. 32:13. The hills will flow with milk, and will abundantly provide food and drink, by which the little ones may be nourished 2 Cor. 4:2, 1 Pet. 2:2. All the channels of Judah will flow with the waters of doctrine Isa. 44:3. A fountain will go forth from the house of Jehovah, that sacred washing of baptism Tit. 3:5, which is the fountain opened to the house of David, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem Zech. 13:1, which will irrigate the valley of the most choice cedars, of trees planted in the paradise of Jehovah Psalm 92:13, as Tarnovius rightly paraphrases, with which also the annotations of Wigand and Winckelmann agree. Others explain it concerning heavenly happiness, and recount these goods of the same: (1.) The presence of the Lord in the triumphant Church. (2.) The absence of the Devil and of evils. (3.) The affluence of all good things, which is described by phrases and images of things pleasant in this life, such as must or wine, butter, milk, honey, pleasant and limpid rivers. (4.) The abundance of living water. See Gesner on this passage. Osiander: Must signifies joy: milk the sufficiency and pleasure of all things: waters irrigating all things perpetual consolation, and liberation from all temptations (even those drying up the bones); whence also the elect will flourish perpetually in the kingdom of God. And that eternal solace emanates from Christ, who is the Temple of the most holy Trinity. Similarly, the Weimar Paraphrasts explain these. Which sense Cornelius a Lapide strives to confirm at length, and im- mediately the Papists urge this, because they think that the judgment concerning the final judgment to be instituted in the valley of Jehoshaphat was dealt with in this chapter. There is no doubt that these things will be fully consummated in heavenly happiness, which we enjoy less fully in the kingdom of grace. But the goods of the kingdom of grace, which befall the faithful in these lands, are not to be excluded here, even though we are to attain the same in heavenly glory in a more perfect manner (the ὀι̉κονομίᾳ, proper to the kingdom of grace, having been set aside, which we shall one day lack). (Conf. what is at Am. 9. v. 13.) Which the Belgian Paraphrasts acknowledged. Jerome, Remigius, Hugo, Isidore, Arias Montanus, and also Gregory Nazianzen, Theodoret, and Nicetas explain this concerning the militant Church, while they understand the fountain of Baptism flowing from the Church. Blessed Luther does so as well. But other similar testimonies of the Prophets show that something peculiar is designated here. In the Prophet Zechariah, chapter 13, there exists a prophecy concerning a fountain, which shall be opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem to wash away sin and uncleanness, that is, concerning such a fountain, in which those washing shall wash away sin and all uncleanness. Thus Isaiah says in chapter 12: You shall draw waters with joy from the fountains of salvation. He does not name any one fountain, as Joel does in this place, who, although he speaks of one fountain, yet says it will flow out as far as Sittim beyond the temple, so that the waters of one fountain are diverted into a far-off region. As therefore there is no doubt that Zechariah and Isaiah speak of holy Baptism: so what prevents us from applying Joel to Baptism, since he speaks expressly of a fountain in the house of the Lord? It is not called a fountain where there is no water. But in this fountain there is not simple water, but the water of the Lord. For it springs from the house of the Lord. But just as the use of simple or natural water is manifold—it is drunk, it irrigates, and it makes arid places fruitful, and it is also most apt for washing away filth—so holy Baptism gives drink to the soul inflamed with the thirst of grace. For it is the fountain of salvation, which those who drink, that is, those who believe the promise added to it, never thirst. As Christ says: He who shall have believed, and shall have been baptized, shall be saved. Accord this, refreshed by the heavenly drink of the house of the Lord, they are no longer arid and sterile, but as the Psalm says, they are like a tree planted by the rivers of waters, which brings forth its fruit in its season. For it is not hindered, nor is it harmed by the heat of the Sun. But the chief fruit is that of which Zechariah speaks, that sins and uncleanness are washed away by this water. Eternal life follows this fruit.

Latin:

Vers. 18. STILLABVNT MONTES DVLCEDI- NEM,) Sudabunt roscida mella. ET COLLES FLVENT LAGTE,) Prae pecoris abundantia & succulentia, ET PER OMNES RIVOS JVDAE IBVNT AQVAE.) Populus ab hoste liber, & in magno otio fossas oblimatas deterget: & novos faciet aquaeductus, altae pacis opera. Vide Ezech. 47. ET FONS DE DOMO DOMINI EGREDIE- TVR, ET IRRIGABIT TORRENTEM SPINARVM.) Irrigabit vallem Sittim. Sic Chaldaeus, & addit Hieronymus fic appellari locum non longe a mari mortuo: unde apparet describi hic aquaeductum eundem, quem Ezechiel e Tem- plo deducit ad mare mortuum & ultra, 47. ab initio ad 12.

Mere carnalia tantum more Judaico sapit Gro- tius in hac tam insigni promissione. At vere spiri- tualia bona hic promissa esse Christiani Interpp. magno consensu agnoscunt. Quibus enim Do- minus ille, qui dedit vocem suam de Jerusalem, spes & fortitudo est, haec inde consequuntur be- neficia, 1. Gratiae manifestationem: SCIETIS me Je- hovam Deum vestrum esse. (2.) Gratiosam praesen- tiam & inhabitationem: Quod habitem Sione, mon- te sanctitatis meae, id est, in Ecclesia Ps. 2, 6. Zach. 3, 14. c. 6, 15. (3.) sanctificationem: Eritque urbs Jerso- lymorump sanctitas, id est, sanctissima per imputatio- nem justitiae Domini Sponsi sui vestita, indumento salutis ornata, per sanguinem ejus purificata, per verbum & Sacramenta sanctificata Ef. 61, 10. 1. Joh. 1, 7. Eph. 5, 25. Tit. 2, 14. (4.) defensionem: quia ex- tranei hostes non transibunt per eam amplius, id est, non nocebunt ei, Zach. 14, 11. Esa. 26, 1. Ps. 146, 1. vel etiam segregationem ab impiis & infidelibus, qui etsi externo coetui admixti sint, ad internam tamen Ecclesiae communionem non pertinent: quarum promissionum figuratam & allegoricam amplifica- tionem caetera continent: stillabunt montes ipsi, qui alias sunt & habentur steriles, mustum, vinum no- vum, generosum, quo robustiores in Ecclesia utun- tur Deut. 32, 13. Colles diffluent lacte, cibumque ac po- tum abunde praebebunt, quo alantur parvuli 2. Cor. 4, 2. 1. Petr. 2, 2. Omnes alvei Iudae diffluent aquis doctrinae Ef. 44, 3. Fons e domo Jehovae prodi- bit, sacrum illud baptismi lavacrum Tit. 3, 5. quod est fons apertus Domi Davidis, & habitatoribus Jerusalem Zach. 13, 1. qui irrigabit vallem Cedrorum lectissimarum, arborum plantatarum in paradiso Ie- hovae Psalm. 92, 13. ut recte παραφράζει Tarnovius, quibus congruunt etiam annotationes Wigandi, & Winckelmanni. Alii de felicitate caelesti explicant, & haec ejusdem bona recensent (1.) Domini in Ec- clesia triumphante praesentiam. (2.) Diaboli & malorum absentiam, (3.) omnium bonorum afflu- entiam, quae describatur phrasibus & imaginibus in hac vita gratorum, ut sunt mustum seu vinum, bu- tyrum, lac, mel, amoeni & limpidi fluvii. (4.) Aquae vivae abundantiam. Vid. Gesnerus in h. l. Osian- der: Mustum significat laetitiam: lac omnium re- rum sufficientiam & voluptatem: aquae irrigantes omnia perpetuam consolationem, & ab omnibus ten- tationibus (exsiccantibus etiam ossa) liberatio- nem; unde & electi perpetuo in Dei regno virebunt. Et illud solatium aeternum emanat a Christo, qui est, Templum sacratissimae Trinitatis. Similiter haec explicant Paraphrastae Vinarienses. Quem sensum prolixe confirmare nititur Cornel. a Lapide, & im- primiṡ ideo urgent Pontificii, quod fentiant de no- visfimo judicio in valle Iofaphat instituendo, hoc ca- pite actum esfe. In cœlesti felicitate hæc plene con- fummatum iri, quibus in regno gratiæ minus ple- ne fruimur, nullum dubium est. Sed non excluden- da hîc sunt bona regni gratiæ, quæ in his terris fideli- bus obtingunt, tametsi perfectiori ratione (seque- strata ὀι̉κονομίᾳ, regno gratiæ propria, olim destitu- ra) eadem in gloria cœlesti consequuturi fumus. (Conf. quæ ad Am. 9. v. 13.) Quod agnovere Pa- raphrastæ Belgici. De Ecclesia militante exponunt Hieronymus, Remigius, Hugo, Isiddrus, Arias Mon- tanus, etiam Gregor. Nazianz. Theodor. & Nicetas, dum fontem Baptismatos ex Ecclesia manantis in- telligunt. Sic autem B. Luth. Sed alia Prophetarum similia testimonia oftendunt, peculiare aliquid hic de- signari. Apud Zachariam Prophetam cap. 13. ex- tat vaticinium de fonte, qui aperietur domui David & habitatoribus Jerusalem ad peccatum & inmun- ditiem abluendam, hoc est, de tali fonte, in quo la- vantes abluent peccatum, & immunditiem omnem. Sic Esaias cap. 12. inquit : Haurietis aquas cum gaudio de fontibus salutis. Non nominat unum ali- quem fontem, sicut Ioel hoc in loco, qui etsi de uno fonte loquitur, tamen dicit extra templum in Sittim usque emanaturum, ita ut unius fontis aquæ in longin- quam regionem deriventur. Sicut igitur Zacha- riam & Esaiam de sancto Baptismo loqui dubium non est: Ita Ioelem quoque quid prohibet, ad Baptis- mum accommodare, cum diferte de fonte in Domini domo loquatur? Fons non dicitur, ubi nulla est aqua. In hoc autem fonte non simplex aqua est, sed aqua Do- mini. Nam ex Domini domo scaturit. Sicut autem aquæ simplicis seu naturalis multiplex est usus, bibi- tur, rigat, & fœcundat arida loca, sordibus quoque ab- luendis aptissima est. Ita facer Baptismus animam accensam siti gratiæ potat. Est enim fons salutis, quem qui bibunt, hoc est, qui promissioni additæ cre- dunt, nunquam sitiunt. Sicut Christus dicit : Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit. Accor- da hoc cœlesti potu domus Domini refecta, non am- plius sunt arida & sterilia, sed ut Psalmus ait, sunt si- milia arbori plantatæ ad rivos aquarum, quæ fert fructum suum suo tempore. Non enim impeditur, nec læditur ardoribus Solis. Præcipuus autem fru- ctus est, de quo Zacharias dicit, quód peccata & im- mundities hac aqua abluuntur. Hunc fructum se- quitur vita æterna.

## 3:19
Ver. 19. EGYPT SHALL BE FOR A DESOLATION,) Antiochus plundering it. Dan. 11, 40. 42. 43.

AND IDUMEA FOR A DESERT OF DESTRUCTION.) The Maccabees laying it waste. Josephus 12, 11. 12. Compare Isaiah 63.

FOR THAT THEY HAVE DEALT UNJUSTLY AGAINST THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH AND HAVE SHED INNOCENT BLOOD IN THEIR LAND.) For Judea was vexed now by the kings of Syria and Asia, now by the kings of Egypt: which the ten horns in Daniel signify. But the Idumeans for the most part joined themselves to the oppressors of the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ÆGYPTUS IN DESOLATIONEM ERIT,) Diripiente eam Antiocho. Dan. 11, 40. 42. 43.

ET IDUMÆA IN DESERTUM PERDITIO- NIS.) Vastantibus eam Maccabæis. Josephus 12, 11. 12. Confer Esaiam 63.

PRO EO QUOD INIQUE EGERINT IN FI- LIOS JUDA ET EFFUDERINT SANGUINEM IN- NOCENTEM IN TERRA SUA.) Nam Judæa, modo à Syriæ Asiæque, modo ab Ægypti regibus fuit vexata: quod significant decem cornua apud Danielem. Idumæi autem plerumque Judæorum oppressoribus se aggregabant.

## 3:20
Ver. 20. AND JUDAH SHALL BE INHABITED FOR EVER.) It shall be in peace for a long time.

AND JERUSALEM UNTO GENERATION AND GENERATION.) For some ages of men.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET JUDÆA IN ÆTERNUM HABITA- BITUR.) Per longum tempus in pace erit.

ET JERUSALEM IN GENERATIONEM ET GENERATIONEM.) Per aliquot hominum ætates.

## 3:21
Ver. 21. AND I WILL CLEANSE THEIR BLOOD, WHICH THEY HAVE NOT CLEANSED.) ונקיתי in this place is to avenge, the Greeks ἐκζητήσω, nor does the Chaldean and Syrian say otherwise. It is also translated ἐκδικεῖν in Zech. 5, 3. The sense is, which the Chaldean beautifully expressed: If there shall still be any blood of the Jews shed, which I have not yet avenged, I will avenge even this: As against the Ammonites and Moabites. See Josephus in the cited place.

AND THE LORD SHALL DWELL IN SION.) The worship of God shall remain in Jerusalem.

These things do not pertain to the times of Antiochus or the Maccabees, nor to Egypt and Idumea as the enemies of the Jews, but under the name of Egypt and Idumea the enemies of the Church are designated. Nor do those ten horns of Daniel refer to the Kings of Syria and Egypt, concerning which we have spoken in the commentary on Daniel. Where any spiritual goods are promised to the Church in v. 17, 18, so now punishments are denounced against the enemies of the Church: and since those things look specifically to the times of the New Testament, where the Lord roared from Sion, and the heavens and the earth were moved, and the Lord was present as the hope of his people, and was known by them more fully: So on the contrary the Egyptians, i.e., the adverse enemies of the Church, shall perish with the Idumeans, i.e., the false brethren, for that they have dealt unjustly against the children of Judah, and have shed innocent blood in their land, because both afflicted the Church. We do not deny that there is an allusion to ancient histories, but the times of the New Testament are looked to, and their fate by the phrases and histories of the Old. The testimony is adumbrated. Compare Isaiah 19, Jeremiah 46, as also Isaiah 21:11, Jeremiah 49:7. St. Cyril also approved this sense, although he indicated that regard should be had for ancient history: As far as the historical sense is concerned, Egypt was punished when Cambyses, son of Cyrus, subdued the kingdom. And Idumea was reduced to a wilderness, which the thing itself speaks. Furthermore, the prophetic words seem to cover a hidden covenant, which the only-begotten, having become man, fulfilled. For divine scripture is always accustomed to make the hosts of demons and the attackers of the saints similar to great idolaters and those vehemently inclined toward them. Therefore, it prophesies that all enemies will perish, compared to the Egyptians and Idumeans. For the promise of Christ concerning the Church is firm (The gates of hell shall not prevail against it). Moreover, it clearly hands down that punishments will be exacted for sins committed against men, and against malignant powers, and as many as have dared things equal to them, either leading away to certain errors of the Greeks, or precipitating into a reprobate mind while they teach to pursue perverse things: therefore saying that those who attacked Sion will be destroyed, because they shed innocent blood and intolerably vexed the sons of Judah, that is, the saints, the sons of confession. For Judah is rendered as confession: Blessed Luther in this place, folio 683. He signifies by Judah a man who acknowledges, confesses, and praises God, on account of His mercy exhibited to the human race. For all the rest, who do not admire and proclaim this benefit, blaspheme God. Since the Synagogue, which killed Christ and the Apostles and condemned the Gospel as a most harmful plague, is also in this number of blasphemers, it does not deserve this name, to be called Judah. Concerning the eternal punishment of the enemies of the Church, Cornelius à Lapide, and from our own, Blessed Gesner, Osiander, and the Weimar Paraphrasts interpret it; we do not deny that that perdition is to be extended to this, yet we judge that temporal punishments, especially spiritual ones, are not to be excluded. Let there be an opposition of the happiness of the faithful, which is begun in the kingdom of grace and will be consummated in the kingdom of glory, and the unhappiness and destruction of the unfaithful, who are here in desolation and in the desert of perdition, since they are deprived of the grace of God by their own fault, and will be forever in desolation and the desert of perdition, excluded from heavenly glory, and thrust down to the perdition of hell. Whence it is added, Judah will remain forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation, which certainly cannot be understood of the earthly Jerusalem and Judah according to the flesh: as Grotius opines with the Jews and Judaizing Chiliasts, who accept these in a carnal sense concerning happiness in these lands; but of the Church of Christ adumbrated by Judah and Jerusalem: and it is a violent gloss to restrict the words 'forever,' 'from generation to generation' to a few ages of men, since they exhibit a periphrasis of eternity, nor can the ages or centuries be shown in which 'yashab' (sat) and remained quiet Jerusalem with Judah, since it was perpetually infested by enemies. Concerning the protection of the Church in these lands, which is to be preserved even against the very gates of hell until the end of the age, and regarding its glorious habitation for all eternity, others interpret this more correctly. Thus also Cyril: Therefore he says that the adversaries of Zion will go into destruction, and that Judea will be inhabited not that one devastated and burned (since the Lord and God, as truth itself, cannot speak falsely) but that which is comprehended by the mind, the heavenly Jerusalem, the supernal and divine Zion, the glorious and illustrious city, whose builder and maker and architect is God himself, into which may we also, through Christ, arrive. Thus also Theodoret himself: But let us understand that statement: 'it will be inhabited forever,' in the manner which we explained above; for it is not right that God should make promises of good things to the unworthy and keep them, since He is just and abhors iniquity. Therefore, the Jews brought upon themselves a dispersion among the nations when they acted insanely against their benefactor, but we, having been called in their place into the order of the Bride, shall diligently love the bridegroom who has pursued us with such love and heaped us with such gifts, lest we fall away from the eternal promises.

The word נקָה, although the Greeks, the Chaldean, and the Syrian, as well as the Arab, explain it as vengeance—which sense Cornelius à Lapide pursues more fully—should not, however, be snatched away to mean the vengeance of the blood of the Jews against the Ammonites and Moabites, concerning whom no word is held here. Others explain it as the vengeance of the blood of the faithful against the enemies of the Church, which the souls of the Saints demand in Apoc. 6:10, along with Remigius and Hugo. This seems to look back to the preceding matters concerning the Egyptians and Idumeans, who shed innocent blood. Gesner, who interprets these things specifically regarding the Western and Eastern Antichrist as the primary enemies of the Church, has diligently expounded this phrase. The cause of such horrible punishment for the enemies of the Church is added: because they shed innocent blood in their land. By this mark, the Turkish thief and the Roman Pope are especially indicated. For the former has shed the blood of Christians for many centuries now, like water (Ps. 79:3). But concerning the latter, the Holy Spirit says in Apoc. 17:6 that the harlot is drunk with the blood of the saints and the martyrs of Jesus. And just as the blood of Abel cries out to God (Gen. 4:16; Heb. 11:4), so also the souls of those killed for the word of God cry out with a loud voice: 'How long, O Lord, holy and true, do you not judge and avenge our blood from those who dwell on the earth?' (Apoc. 6:10). The Lord, however, answers here through Joel: 'I will not leave it unavenged, but avenging I will avenge their blood.' Jerome renders it: 'I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed.' And the Seventy, quite contradictorily: 'And I will avenge their blood, and I will not cleanse.' But this reduplication of the verb is customary, which denotes swift and severe vengeance. For the word נקָה in Kal signifies to be pure and clean, but in Piel to absolve and pronounce pure from guilt, and often to leave unpunished, to exempt from penalty, not to avenge, and not to punish. Here the preceding and subsequent context argue that the Lord is speaking of vengeance. For He says that He will punish the Egyptians and Idumeans for the innocent blood shed, which they shed in their land. On the other hand, He promises to the house of Judah, that is, to the Church of the faithful, by leaving their blood unavenged—I will not leave it unavenged. A similar expression is Ex. 34:7, וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה, 'By purifying He will not purify.' By vacating He will not allow to be vacant of punishment, or He will not allow the wicked to go unavenged; He speaks of the justice of God. And Jer. 30:11, וְנַקֵּה לֹא אֲנַקֶּךּ, 'And by holding innocent I will not hold you innocent.' The Vulgate version expressed the meaning, not the words: 'I will chastise you in judgment, lest you seem innocent to yourself.' Others, however, retain Jerome's or the Vulgate version and explain it thus: 'Where (namely, in Jerusalem) I will cleanse them, whose blood I had not cleansed before,' that is, the nations co-opted into the Church and Mount Zion, who were previously orphans, I will sanctify; and those who were previously dead in their offenses and sins, without Christ, and alien to the Commonwealth of Israel, I will vivify and make citizens of the Church (Eph. 2:1; supra c. 2:31). Indeed, even the Jews, whom the law could not cleanse, faith conceived from the preaching of the Gospel will cleanse (Acts 15:9, 10). Thus B. Tarnovius. B. Wigandus understands it of the faithful, concerning whom the preceding had dealt under the name of Judah, so that the cause of perpetual happiness may be rendered: 'because I will cleanse the blood,' i.e., the guilt (1 John 1:7), which Haymo draws toward purgatory, as if to say that sins not cleansed here will be cleansed there. But that is not approved by Christophorus à Castro, nor by Corn. à Lapide, who wishes here to look clearly at the blood, concerning which it was said a little before: 'they shed innocent blood'; nor is there a need here to admit Purgatory, even if it is taken regarding cleansing from impiety. Osiander explains it thus: 'I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed,' i.e., Christians will be most clean from all impurity with which they had once labored. For in the other life, sin will not only be forgiven but also clearly abolished. But we have no cause to depart from the metaphrase of B. Luther, which is simpler and agrees more with the text, and has been sufficiently confirmed by B. Gesner and approved by the authority of most interpreters. 'The Lord,' says B. Luther, 'consoles the Church in this place and says that innocent blood is shed. For the Church is not guilty of these crimes, but by the divine voice it is commanded to despise these unjust judgments of the world and to establish that it is afflicted by the world without merit.' This is certainly no small consolation. Therefore Satan tries to remove it from our eyes and our mind. For in such calamities the first thing is that souls, looking upon their own uncleanness, are convicted and judge that the punishment comes from merit, but the Lord declares that the innocent are afflicted. For although they are sinners, yet their sins have been forgiven them through Christ, and their enemies by no means do this, that they punish them on account of their sins; they hate the doctrine, the confession, the faith. These alone they pursue with Satanic hatred, and strive to extinguish. Therefore they are innocent on a double account: both on account of faith in Christ, which takes away sins, and on account of the unjust judgments of their enemies, who declare the highest gifts of the Holy Spirit to be blasphemy. These are the words of Luther and Christoph. à Castro says, 'The best sense of all is the former one of Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Albert, and Hugo, and then I will avenge and vindicate the innocent blood of my elect, which their enemies had shed; and I had not yet taken vengeance, as they were requesting, Apoc. 6.' Nor does Jerome reject that sense: 'And the Lord will cleanse the blood of all sinners, which he had not cleansed before: that he may cleanse in the Gospel those whom he had left unclean while sinning under the Law.' For he concluded all under sin, that he might have mercy on all, or that he might avenge the blood of his servants: which they shed in martyrdom for the confession of his name. The final words: AND THE LORD WILL DWELL IN SION, are understood again as referring to the triumphant Church by B. Gesner, Osiander, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and the Belgian ones, as also by Christoph. à Castro, citing to the same effect also Remigius, Rupert, Albert, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, and Vatablus, because they expound it concerning the Church of the triumphant, who, with their enemies destroyed, enjoy perpetual peace in the heavenly Jerusalem.

But just as in spiritual promises the benefits which are exhibited to the faithful in the kingdom of grace, the full enjoyment of which is expected in heaven in the kingdom of glory, can by no means be excluded, so also this dwelling of the Lord in Zion embraces a presence that is both gracious and glorious, because He wills to be present graciously with Zion and His faithful ones in these lands, and to fill them with His glory in heaven. For Zion is one, the Church militant and triumphant, which in this and the future age is gladdened by the presence and perennial cohabitation of its head, Christ Jesus. Since here the Lord (God the Father) speaks of the Lord, and is distinguished from the same, 'I will cleanse,' says the Lord God the Father, 'their blood,' and He adds: 'AND THE LORD, will dwell in Zion,' the Lord dwelling in Zion is to be understood as God the Son, who is the head of the Church, and is called the Lord of the same by a special reason. Thus the blessed Tarnovius. And this I, God the Father, am about to do, and Jehovah my Son dwelling in Zion, the king established by me in the same place Ps. 2, 2. 6. & 87, 1. who remains in the pious and the pious in Him, and in whom the Father purges them, that they may bear much fruit, John 15, 1. 2. and this is the cause of the cleansing or sanctification of the Church, because Christ, nay the whole Trinity, dwells in it graciously John 14, 23. Whence some translate the Hebrew words ויהוה שכן בצין in this way: Because Jehovah is dwelling, to wit, or dwells in Zion. Jerome also subscribed to this interpretation, which looks to the militant Church: And the Lord will dwell in Zion.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET MUNDABO SANGUINEM EORUM, QUEM NON MUNDAVERUNT.) ונקיתי hoc loco est ulcisci, Græci ἐκζητήσω, nec aliter Chaldæus & Syrus. Verti- tur & ἐκδικεῖν Zach. 5, 3. Sensus est, quem pulchre expressit Chaldæus: Si quis adhuc erit Judæorum sanguis effusus, quem ultus nondum fuero, etiam hunc ulciscar: Ut in Ammonitas & Moabitas. Vide Josephum dicto loco.

ET DOMINUS COMMORABITUR IN SION.) Cultus Dei manebit Hierosolymis.

Non pertinent hæc ad Antiochi, aut Macca- bæorum tempora, nec ad Ægyptum & Idumæam ho- stes Judæorum, sed sub nomine Ægypti & Idumæe hostes Ecclesiæ designantur. Neque cornua illa de- cem Danielis, Syriæ & Ægypti Reges referunt, de quo ad Danielem diximus. Ubi bona quævis spiri- tualia promissa Ecclesiæ sunt v. 17. 18. ita nunc sup- plicia denunciantur hostibus Ecclesiæ: & quum illa respiciant speciatim tempora N. Test. ubi Domi- nus de Sion rugiit, & commoti sunt cœli, & terra, adfuitque Dominus spes populi sui, & cognitus ab illis plenius est: Sic ex adverso Ægyptii, h. e. adversi hostes Ecclesiæ peribunt cum Idumæis, h. e. falsis fratribus, pro eo, quod inique egerint in filios Juda, & sanguinem innocentem effuderint in terra sua, quod Ecclesiam utrique afflixerint. Alludi ad veteres hi- storias, non abnuimus, sed tempora respiciuntur N. Test. eorumque fors phrasibus & historiis Vet. Test. adumbratur. Conf. Esa. 19. Jer. 46. ut & Esa. 21, 11. Jer. 49, 7. Quem sensum probavit etiam S. Cyrillus, etsi respectum haberi ad historiam vete- rem indicarit: Quod ad sensum historicum attinet, punita est Ægyptus, quando Cambyses Cyri filius re- gnum subegit. Et Idumæa redacta est in solitudinem, quod res ipsa loquitur. Cæterum videntur Propheti- ca verba pactum occultum tegere, quod unigenitus homo factus implevit. Semper enim divina scriptu- ra magnis idololatris, & eo vehementer propensis, ca- tervas dæmonum, & sanctorum oppugnatores, similes facere consuevit. Omnes igitur inimicos perituros vaticinatur, Ægyptiis & Idumæis comparatos. Fir- ma est enim Christi promissio de Ecclesia (Portæ in- feri non prævalebunt adversus eam.) Omnino au- tem pœnas sumptum iri admissorum in homines, & malignas potestates, & quotquot illis paria ausi sunt, aut ad Græcorum errores quosdam abducentes, aut in reprobum sensum præcipitantes, dum perversa conse- ctari docent, manifeste tradit: propterea disperdi- tum iri dicens, qui Sion oppugnarunt, quia sanguinem innocentem effuderint, & intolerabiliter filios Juda vexaverint, hoc est, sanctos, filios confessionis. Red- ditur enim Judæ confessio: B. Lutherus in h. l. f. 683. Significat Juda hominem qui agnoscit, confitetur, & laudat Deum, propter misericordiam suam humano generi exhibitam. Reliqui enim omnes, qui hoc bene- ficium non admirantur & prædicant, Deum blasphe- mant. In hoc blasphemantium numero cum Syna- goga quoque sit, quæ Christum & Apostolos occi- dit, & Evangelium, ut nocentissimam pestem da- mnavit, non meretur nomen hoc, ut Juda vocetur. De æterna pœna hostium Ecclesiæ Cornel. à Lapide, & è nostris B. Gesnerus, Osiander, ac Paraphrastæ Vi- narienses interpretantur, ad quam illam perditio- nem extendendam esse, non abnuimus, pœnas ta- men temporales, imprimis spirituales haud exclu- dendas censemus. Oppositio sit, felicitatis fidelium, quæ in regno gratiæ inchoatur, in regno gloriæ con- summabitur, & infelicitatis ac interitus infidelium, qui hic in desolationem & in desertum perditionis sunt, cum gratia Dei privantur culpa sua, & in æter- num erunt in desolationem, & desertum perditio- nis, exclusi à cœlesti gloria, & detrusi ad perditio- nem inferni. Unde additur, Juda in seculum perma- nebit, & Hierosolyma in generationem & generatio- nem, quæ certe intelligi nequeunt de terrena Hie- rosolyma, & Juda secundum carnem: quemad- modum cum Judæis & Judaizantibus Chiliastis, qui hæc sensu carnali de felicitate in his terris ac- cipiunt, Grotius opinatur; Sed de Ecclesia Christi per Juda & Jerusalem adumbrata: & violenta glossa est, verba in seculum, in generationem & generatio- nem, ad aliquot ætates hominum restringere, quum περίφρασιν æternitatis exhibeant, neque mon- strari possunt ætates aut secula, quibus ישב sedit ac permansit quieta Jerusalem cum Juda, cum perpe- tuo ab hostibus infestata fuerit. De protectione ergo Ecclesiæ in his terris, adversus ipsas etiam in- ferorum portas conservandæ, usque ad consum- mationem seculi, ejusdemque in omnem æternita- tem gloriosa habitatione, hæc rectius alii interpre- tantur. Sic etiam Cyrillus: Itaque abituros in exitium Sionis adversarios dicit, & Judæam habitatum iri in sempiternum, & Hierusalem in generationes genera- tionum: non illam vastatam & exustam (siquidem Dominus ac Deus, ut ipsa veritas, falsum dicere non potest) sed eam, quæ mente comprehenditur potius, cœlestem Hierusalem, supernam, & divinam Sion, gloriosam & præclaram civitatem, cujus artifex & fabricator, & architectus ipse Deus, in quam & nos utinam per Christum perveniamus. Sic & Theodo- retus ipse: At vero istud: in æternum habitabitur: intelligamus ea ratione, quam supra explicavimus, neque enim indignis bonorum promissa facere, ac ser- vare Deum, æquum est, cum sit justus & abhorrens ab iniquitate. Itaque Judæi sibi in gentes dispersionem conciliaverunt, cum in benefactorem insanierunt, nos autem loco illorum in Sponsæ ordinem vocati, sponsum, qui nos tanto amore prosequutus est, tantis- que donis cumulavit, assidue diligemus, ne ex æternis promissionibus excidamus.

Verbum נקָה, etsi Græci ἐκζητήσω, Chaldæus & Syrus, ut & Arabs de ultione explicent, quem sen- sum fusius exequitur Cornelius à Lapide, non tamen abripi ad ultionem sanguinis Judæorum adversus Ammonitas & Moabitas, de quibus hic nullum ha- betur verbum, debet. De ultione sanguinis fidelium adversus hostes Ecclesiæ alii explicant, quam animæ Sanctorum poscunt Apoc. 6, 10. cum Remigio, & Hugone. Quod respicere videtur ad præcedentia de Ægyptiis & Idumæis, qui sanguinem innocentem ef- fuderunt. Quam phrasin diligenter exposuit & Gesnerus, qui hæc specialiter de Antichristo occiden- tali, & orientali, ceu primariis Ecclesiæ hostibus interpretatur. Causa tam horrendi supplicii ho- stium Ecclesiæ adjicitur, quod effuderint sanguinem innocentem in terra sua. Qua nota imprimis Turci- cus latro, & Romanus Papa indigitantur. Nam ille sanguinem Christianorum à multis jam seculis effu- dit, ut aquam Ps. 79, 3. De hoc autem dicit Spiritus S. Apoc. 17, 6. quod meretrix ebria sit sanguine sancto- rum, & martyrum Jesu. Sicut autem sanguis Abelis clamat ad Deum Gen. 4, 16. Ebr. 11, 4. Ita etiam a- nimæ istorum interfectorum propter verbum Dei cla- mant voce magna: Usque quo Domine, sancte & vere non judicas, & non vindicas sanguinem no- strum de iis, qui habitant in terra? Apoc. 6, 10. Do- minus autem hic per Joelem respondet: Ego non in- ultum relinquam, sed vindicans vindicabo sangui- nem eorum. Hieronymus reddit: Mundabo san- guinem eorum, quem non mundaveram: Et septua- ginta plane contradictorie: Et ulciscaf sanguinem eorum, & non mundabo. Sed usitata est hujus verbi ἀναδιπλωσις, quæ denotat celerem & severam vin- dictam. Nam verbum נקָה in Kal significat purum esse, & mundum, sed in Piel absolvere, & purum pro- nunciare à culpa, & sæpe impunitum relinquere, pœnæ eximere, non vindicare, & non punire. Hic præcedentia & subsequentia arguunt, Dominum de vindicta loqui. Ait enim se Ægyptios & Idumæos puniturum ob effusum innocentem sanguinem, quem in terra effuderunt. Ex adverso autem pro- mittit domui Juda, hoc est, Ecclesiæ fidelium, inul- tum relinquendo sanguinem eorum non inultum re- linquam. Similis locutio est Ex. 34, 7. וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה Purificando non purificabit. Vacando non sinet va- care pœna, seu non sinet inultum impium, loquitur de justitia Dei: Et Jer. 30, 11. וְנַקֵּה לֹא אֲנַקֶּךּ Et inno- centem habendo non innocentem habebo te. Vulgata versio sententiam non verba expressit: Castigabo te in judicio, ne tibi videaris innoxius. Alii tamen Hie- ronymi vel vulgatam versionem retinent, eamq; ita explicant: Ubi, (sc. in Hierusalem) mundabo eos, quo- rum sanguinem antea non mundabam, gentes videl. in Ecclesiam & montem Sion cooptatas, quæ prius erantorphanæ, sanctificabo, & quæ antea erant mortuæ in offensis ac peccatis suis, absque Christo, & alienæ à Rep. Israelis, vivificabo, & cives Eccle- siæ faciam Eph. 2, 1. supr. c. 2, 31. imo & Judæos, quos lex mundare non poterat, mundabit fides ex Evangelii prædicatione concepta Act. 15, 9. 10. Ita B. Tarnovius. De fidelibus B. Wigandus intel- ligit, de quibus antecedentia egerant, sub Judæ no- mine, ut causa perpetuæ felicitatis reddatur, quia mundabo sanguinem, i. e. reatum, 1. Joh. 1, 7. quod Haymo ad purgatorium trahit, q. d. peccata hic non emundata, ibi emundatum iri. Sed id non probatur Christophoro à Castro, nec Corn. à Lap. qui hic pla- ne respici vult ad sanguinem, de quo paulo anteat: effuderunt sanguinem innocentem: neque opus est hic Purgatorium admittere, etsi de purgatione ab impietate accipiatur. Osiander ita explicat: Mundabo sanguinem eorum, quem non mundave- ram, i. e. Christiani ab omni impuritate, qua ali- quando laboraverant, mundissimi erunt. In al- tera enim vita peccatum non tantum erit remis- sum, sed etiam plane abolitum. Sed non habe- mus causam discedendi à metaphrasi B. Lutheri, quæ simplicior est, & textui magis congruit, & à B. Gesnero satis confirmata, & autoritate plerorumq; interpretum comprobata est: Consolatur, inquit B. Lutherus, Dominus hoc in loco Ecclesiam, & dicit, sanguinem innocentem fundi. Non enim istorum criminum rea est Ecclesia, sed divina voce jubetur hæc iniqua mundi judicia contemnere, & statuere, quod præter meritum à mundo affligatur. Hæc sane non est exigua consolatio. Itaque Satan conatur eam re- movere ex oculis, atque animo. Hoc enim in talibus ca- lamitatibus primum est, ut animi suam immunditiem intuentes arguantur, & ex merito venire pœnam judicent, sed Dominus pronunciat innocentes affligi. Etsi enim peccatores sunt, tamen & condonata sunt eis peccata per Christum, & hostes ipsorum neuti- quam hoc agunt, ut propter peccata eos puniant; Do- ctrinam, confessionem, fidem oderunt. Hæc sola Satani- co odio persequuntur, & extinguere student. Duplici igitur nomine sunt innocentes, & propter fidem in Christum, quæ tollit peccata, & propter hostium iniqua judicia, qui summa dona Spiritus S. blasphe- miam esse pronunciant. Hæc Luth. Christoph. à Ca- stro, Omnium, inquit, optimus sensus est prior Hie- ronymi, Theodoreti, Remigii, Alberti, & Hugonis, & tunc ego ulciscar, ac vindicabo sanguinem inno- centem electorum meorum, quem effuderant ho- stes eorum; & ego nondum ultus fueram, ut ipsi postulabant Apoc. 6. Nec reprobat Hieronymus il- lum sensum: Et mundabit Dominus sanguinem o- mnium peccatorum, quem prius non mundaverat: ut mundet in Evangelio, quos in lege peccantes im- mundos reliquerat. Ideo enim conclusit omnia sub peccato, ut omnibus misereretur, sive ulcisceretur ser- vorum suorum sanguinem: quem in martyrio pro no- minis ejus confessione fuderunt. Postrema verba: ET DOMINUS COMMORABITUR IN SION, iterum de Ecclesia triumphante intelligunt B. Gesne- rus, Osiander, Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, & Belgici, ut & Christoph. à Castro, allegans in eandem senten- tiam & Remigium, Rupertum, Albertum, Hugonem, Lyranum, Dionysium, & Vatablum, quod de Eccle- sia triumphantium exponant, qui deletis hostibus perpetua pace in cœlesti Hierusalem perfruuntur.

Sed uti in spiritualibus promissis excludi minime possunt beneficia, quæ in regno gratiæ fidelibus ex- hibentur, quorum plenaria fruitio in cœlis in re- gno gloriæ expectatur, ita etiam hæc commoratio Domini in Sione præsentiam gratiosam pariter & gloriosam complectitur, quod Sioni & fidelibus suis, tum in his terris gratiose adesse, tum in cœlis glo- ria sua illos implere velit. Est enim una Sion, Ec- clesia militans & triumphans, quæ in hoc & futuro seculo capitis sui Christi Jesu præsentia & cohabi- tatione perenni exhilaratur. Quum hic Dominus (Deus Pater) de Domino loquatur, & ab eodem di- stinguatur, MUNDABO ego, inquit Dominus Deus Pater, sanguinem eorum, & addit: ET DO- MINUS, commorabitur in Sion, intelligendus per Dominum in Sione commorantem est Deus Filius, qui Ecclesiæ caput est, & Dominus ejusdem peculiari ratione vocatur. Ita B. Tarnovius. Et hoc facturus sum ego Deus Pater, & Jehova Filius meus habitans Sione, rex à me ibidem constitutus Pf. 2, 2. 6.& 87, 1. qui manet in piis & pii in illo, & in quo Pater eos pur- gat, ut ferant multum fructum, Joh. 15, 1. 2. & hæc est causa mundationis seu sanctificationis Ecclesiæ, quia Christus, imo tota Trinitas eam gratiose inha- bitat Joh. 14, 23. Unde nonnulli verba Ebr. ויהוה שכן בצין hoc modo vertunt; Quia Jehova habitans scil. est, vel habitat Sione. Huic interpretationi ad Ecclesiam militantem spectanti etiam Hierony- mus subscripsit: Et Dominus commorabitur in Sion

# Amos

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
IN THE YEAR TO THE PRESS

Amos has his name from a burden, which is called עומס, or from עמס, he burdened, which name fits him well, because he was laden with heavy threats, and imposed a burden upon the people, or those things which were to be very burdensome to them, whose words the land could not sustain, as Amaziah judged Amos 7, 10. That he was a different person from Amoz, the parent of Isaiah, even the writing itself teaches, with whom some of the ancients wrongly confused him, because of the similar writing of the Greek and Latin texts, Αμως, Amos. He is said to have been among the herdsmen and shepherds c. 1, 1. c. 7, 14. from the small town of Tekoa, in Jerome's time a little village, and not very cultivated on account of its sterility 2 Chron. 20, 21. 1 Macc. 9, 33. He lived, however, in the time of Uzziah, King of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam II, King of Israel, as he himself indicates at the beginning, whence among the Prophets the first place is granted to Jonah, who lived in the time of Amaziah 2 Kings 14, 23. 25. The blessed Tarnovius assigns the second place to Amos along with most others, making Hosea later than both, and he establishes the occasion of the prophecy of Amos as the happiness of the kingdom of Israel under Jeroboam, and the security of the people arising thence, which God went to shake off by the most grave threats of Amos; since he preached specifically to the kingdom of Israel, or the ten tribes, c. 1, 1. 3. 1. 4, 1. 5, 1. 7, 10. and delivered a few things concerning the kingdom of Judah ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ (as if in passing) c. 2, 4. 6. and proposed those things which he predicts concerning the nations at the beginning for the sake of the Israelites, so that from thence they might take a taste of the divine vengeance imminent upon them. His prophecy is therefore completed by threats both concerning the neighboring nations, and concerning that of which (Psalm 68) it is written: 'Its foundations are in the holy mountains, the Lord loves the gates of Zion above all the tabernacles of Jacob.' Arias-Montanus also subscribes to Jerome, as does our blessed Luther, with whose words and most pious prayers we seal this Prophet: May the Lord God, blessed for evermore, hear them: 'Egypt, which afflicts the children of Israel, and Edom, which sheds innocent blood, shall be a desolate wilderness; but Judah, that is, those who retain the confession of the Gospel, shall be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. For the Lord dwells in Zion,' that is, in the Church, which although He allows to be afflicted, He will not, however, allow to be overturned or utterly laid waste. With this excellent and most sweet promise Joel closes his discourses. Let us therefore join our vows and prayers in these miserable times. O eternal Father of our Lord and deliverer Jesus Christ, we feel what the fortune of Thy Church is in this life, and how it is variously exercised by Satan and the world. We beseech you, therefore, through this your only-begotten Son, that first you may strengthen our souls with your Holy Spirit, lest we succumb to so many dangers: Then that you may not only hinder the attempts of our enemies, but by your faithful and wondrous aid declare to the whole world that your Church is your care, and that you may rule, protect, and save it: who live and reign eternal God, God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.

Latin:

IN ANNO AD AM PRÆLO

NOmem habet Amos ab onere, quod עומס dicitur, vel ab עמס oneravit, quod nomen ipsi pro- be convenit, quia onustus gra- vibus comminationibus fuit, & onus populo indixit, vel ea, quæ valde ipsi onerosa futura, cujus verba sustinere terra non potuit, censente Amazia Amos 7, 10. Alium fuisse ab אמוץ parente Esaiæ, vel ipsa scriptio docet, cum quo perperam, ob similem scriptionem Græci & Latini textus, Αμως, Amos, eundem nonnulli vete- rum confunderunt. Inter pecuarios fuisse dicitur & armentarios c. 1, 1. c. 7, 14. ex Thekoa oppido exiguo, Hieronymi tempore viculo, eoque non admodum culto ob sterilitatem 2. Chron. 20, 21. 1. Macc. 9, 33. vi- vit autem tempore Usiæ Regis Judæ, & in diebus Je- roboami II. Regis Israelis, ut ipse indicat sub initium, unde inter Prophetas Jonæ primo concesso loco, qui tempore Amaziæ vixit 2. Reg. 14, 23.25. Amoso se- cundum assignat locum B. Tarnovius cum plerisque aliis, utroque posteriorem faciens Hoseam, & occasi- onem Prophetiæ Amosi constituit regni Israelis sub Jeroboamo felicitatem, & inde ortam populi secu- ritatem, quam excussum iverit Deus gravissimis A- mosi comminationibus; siquidem specialiter regno Israelis, vel decem tribubus prædicavit, c. 1, 1. 3. 1. 4, 1. 5, 1. 7, 10. & pauca de regno Judæ ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ tradiderit c. 2, 4. 6. atque ea, quæ de gentibus sub initium prædicit, Israelitarum causa proposuerit, ut inde sibi imminentis futuræ divinæ vindictæ gustum capiant. Absolvitur ergo Prophetia ejus comminationibus tum de vicinis gentibus, tum de de qua (Psal. 68.) scriptum est : Fundamenta ejus in montibus sanctis, diligit Dominus portas Sion su- per omnia tabernacula Jacob. Subscribit etiam Hieronymo Arias-Montanus, nec non B. Lutherus noster, cujus verbis, & pientissimis precibus obsi- gnamus hunc Prophetam, Exaudiat eas Dominus Deus benedictus in secula : Ægyptus, quæ affligit filios Israel, & Edom, qui effundit innocentem sangui- nem, erunt in vastam solitudinem ; Sed Juda, h. e. qui retinent confessionem Evangelii, habitabitur in æter- num, & Hierusalem in generationem & generatio- nem. Quoniam Dominus habitat in Zion, h. e. in Ec- clesia, quam etsi affligi sinit, non tamen sinet everti, aut vastari penitus. Hac eximia & suavissima promissio- ne claudit Joel suas conciones. Conjungamus igitur vota & preces his miseris temporibus. O æterne Pa- ter Domini & liberatoris nostri Jesu Christi, senti- mus, quæ tuæ Ecclesiæ in hac vita sit fortuna, & quam exerceatur varie à Satana & mundo. Rogamus igi- tur te, per hunc unigenitum Filium tuum, ut primum Spiritu tuo Sancto nostros confirmes animos, ne tot pe- riculis succumbamus : Deinde ut hostium conatus non solum impedias, sed fido & mirando auxilio tuo toti mundo declares, Ecclesiam tuam tibi esse curæ, eamque regas, tuearis, & salves : qui vivis & regnas æternus Deus, Deus Pater, Deus Filius, Deus Spi- ritus Sanctus, in secula seculorum. Amen.

## 1:1 Introduction: N. J. Otata Mosum
N. J. OTATA MOSUM.

QVIVM.

To the Israelites, whom he sharply rebukes for various crimes, predicting to them, unless they repent, both other punishments and the overthrow of both kingdoms and the withdrawal of the divine word, yet with Evangelical promises added at the end for the faithful and penitent concerning the erection of Israel in the New Testament. It can, however, be distributed into sermons, both plain and clothed in types and visions. Four plain ones are established. The first of these is common, pertaining also to others; the remaining three are proper to the Israelites. The first is completed in Chapters 1 and 2, concerning the judgments that would befall both foreign enemies and those living in the kingdom of Judah and Israel: most of the former, except indeed the judgments concerning the Moabites delivered in chapter 1, but the latter were proposed in chapter 2 after the judgments to be exercised against the Moabites.
