The sermons proper to the Israelites are partly minatory, which are directed both to all in general, such as the second in chapter 3, and to the fat cows or nobles of the kingdom specifically, such as the third sermon in chapter 4, in which, because of neglected divine benefits, the Prophet threatened them with most grave divine judgments; partly penitential, such as the fourth sermon in chapters 5 and 6, where life is promised if they should repent, but since Amos foresees their impenitence, he intimates the abduction of the people, chapter 5 (though an Evangelical promise is inserted in verse 24) and confirms it with other examples and the oath of God, and for the secure he outlines their destruction more fully, though a succinct Evangelical promise is inserted.

The sermons outlined by types or visions are presented in chapters 7, 8, and 9, and contain both legal threats and Evangelical promises, and in the chapter In the seventh, indeed, three visions are handed down, in two of which the Prophet still intercedes for the people, but because of the third, the desolation of the high places and temples and the destruction of the house of Jeroboam having been predicted, Amos is accused of sedition by Amaziah, but he defends himself and pronounces the exile of Amaziah and the destruction of his family. In the eighth chapter, by a new vision, he intimates the end of the Israelite people and a famine of the divine word. Finally, in the ninth, by a final vision, he describes the gravity of the hand of God, which no one can escape, and the power of the divine face directed toward destruction: at the same time, however, he sprinkles in a promise concerning the house of Jacob not being utterly destroyed, v. 8. Concluding at last his prophecy in the same chapter from v. 11 to the end with an Evangelical promise concerning the raising up of the tabernacle of David and the bringing in of the Edomites and the nations.

IN THE DAYS OF UZZIAH KING OF JUDAH) Who is written as Azariah in the books of Kings.

AND IN THE DAYS OF JEROBOAM, SON OF JOASH KING OF ISRAEL.) Of that Jeroboam in whose time Hosea also prophesied: and whose history is in 2 Kings 15:8.

TWO YEARS BEFORE THE EARTHQUAKE) Both Hebrew writers and Jerome three times—that is, in this place, at Isaiah 6, and at Zechariah 4—say that this earthquake happened at that very time when King Uzziah, because of attempted priestly duties, was struck with leprosy. The authority of Josephus is added, Antiquities 9, 11. 'A great earthquake shook the earth. And the temple being split, a bright ray of the sun shone forth and fell upon the face of the king, so that leprosy immediately overspread him; and before the city, at the place called Eroge, half of the mountain on the west was broken off, and having rolled four stadia, it stood against the eastern mountain, so that the paths and the royal gardens were blocked.'

Not only Josephus and Jerome, but the Prophet Zechariah also, chapter 14:5, makes mention of an earthquake which occurred in the time of King Uzziah. Scripture, however, defines nothing about the exact moment of time; because the matter was then known to the common people, and that earthquake was obscure to no one on account of its magnitude. While most, indeed, both Hebrews and Christians, refer it to that time when Uzziah was struck with elephantiasis (2 Kings 15:5, 2 Chron. 26:20), some draw it to the tumults and warlike movements that followed the death of Jeroboam (2 Kings 15:8, 13); some opine that it should be referred to the year of Uzziah's death from a comparison with Isaiah 6:4. It seemed to B. Gerhard that this earthquake lasted at least two years, at intervals, otherwise the Prophet would have been said: Two years before the earthquake.

PART I. Presenting four discourses, bare and almost only legal. DISCOURSE I. General. CONCERNING THE JUDGMENTS OF GOD CHAPTER I. The judgments of GOD against foreigners.

The condition of the Prophet Amos, his vision, and the circumstance of time having been premised, he intimates the roaring of the voice of the Lord; and indicates judgments against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, and Edom.

Amos sings of the vengeance of Israel against its enemies.

Ver. 1.

THE WORDS OF AMOS) This inscription, and that of other prophecies, was made not by the Prophets, but by the Great Senate, which collected the writings of the Prophets and noted the times. The mention of the earthquake shows this. The name is עמוס, entirely different from אמוץ, which is the name of the father of Isaiah, although it is written in the same way in Latin.

Ver. 2.

THE LORD WILL ROAR FROM ZION, AND FROM JERUSALEM WILL GIVE HIS VOICE) The same expression as in Joel 3:16. So also Jeremiah 25:30. The wrath of God is signified by these words.

And if it may be admitted that the wrath of God is signified by this locution, there is nevertheless no doubt that the word of the Lord, by which wrath is denounced and men are invited to repentance, being stirred by the impending judgments of God, is designated by that roaring of the Lord; both because that roaring is heard from Sion and from Jerusalem, which agrees with the Word of the Lord from Sion, where the Lord had His fire and His hearth, not so much with the wrath of the Lord, which is said to be manifested rather from heaven, Rom. 1:16, and because that roaring is declared by the voice of the Lord, or is joined with the same. Therefore, not only is wrath noted, but the denunciation of the judgments of God through the WORD of the Lord, which is a horrible roaring to the impious, but to the faithful and penitent, the voice of the Lord is not unpleasant. For the Lord does not roar in order to terrify only, much less to devour, which roaring is attributed to the infernal lion, 1. Petr. 5:8, but in order to stir up repentance, and that He may be able to show grace instead of punishment, since He does not desire the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live, Ezech. 18 and 33. Therefore, the roaring of the Lord from Sion is used here, and in Jerem. 25:30, not only for the denunciation of judgments and terrible punishments, but also for the preaching of repentance, which ought to have been done in the name of the Lord Jesus throughout the circle of the earth; the same speech and phrase is read to be used in Joel 3:16, as we have said regarding that passage, which diversity of application is detected from the underlying subject matter. For it is not necessary that the same phrase be used for the same argument, but one must look to the context of the text along with the phrase, especially. Although indeed He here denounces the judgments of the Lord to the Syrians, Moabites, and other foreign peoples, yet because He is said to have seen these things CONCERNING ISRAEL, or the ten tribes, it looks primarily to this, that Israel

Whence he has this opinion concerning the ἐπιγραφή of this Prophet and others, or by what argument he was moved to embrace the same, Grotius does not indicate. From the mention of the earthquake, such a thing cannot be gathered. For what prevents one from saying that its commemoration was made by the Prophet himself? That opinion, therefore, as new, merely arbitrary, resting on no foundation, and not sufficiently equal to the αὐθεντία of the Prophetic text, or certainly rendering the same doubtful regarding such inscriptions, is deservedly reprobated. No one, so far as I know, has doubted that they proceeded from the Prophets themselves; no one has held them to be rags added from elsewhere. And they cohere with the text, as parts of the text without any indication or mark of a προσθέσεως. Whether that great Senate added them θεοπνεύστως, which he believed it to have added, Grotius would hardly have said: indeed, he would have denied, without doubt, that those additions were θεόπνευστα. How therefore can the θεοπνευστία and the αὐθεντία ἀνυπεύθυνος of these parts of Scripture thus stand?

Vers. eod.

IN THE HERDSMEN) See below 7:14. Such is that of Hesiod concerning himself: Αρνας ποίμαινονθ' Ελικῶνος ὑπὸ ζαθέοιο. For נקדים, the LXX read נקרים: and translated ἐν νακκαρείμ, for which ἐν ἀκκαρείμ is written in certain books.

OF THECUE) Which tract, six miles distant from Bethlehem, is continuous with the great desert which crosses Arabia, as Jerome notes here.

may terrify, and call back to repentance, by the example of the judgments of the Lord upon foreigners, before he denounces their own punishments, i.e., If the Lord does not spare the nations destitute of the light of the divine Word, and ignorant of his will, much less will he spare his own people who despise the word. Luke 12:47. James 4:17. For those nations were neighbors to the Jews, to whom that thought should have occurred: And your own matter is at stake, when the neighboring wall burns. And: Happy is he whom the dangers of others make cautious. Situated to the North with respect to Judea was Syria, whose metropolis is Damascus; to the South and West were the neighboring Philistines, whose four Satrapies, Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, and Ekron, are noted here. The fifth, Gath, is omitted, perhaps because it was still under the dominion of the Kings of Judah, from the time David captured it 2 Sam. 18:1. 1 Chron. 19:1. Between the West and the North, the Tyrians were neighbors: to the South, the Idumeans were conterminous: to the East in the Northern part were the Ammonites, in the Southern part the Moabites.

Verse same. AND THE BEAUTIFUL PLACES OF THE SHEPHERDS SHALL MOURN) Pastures. Joel 2:22.

AND THE TOP OF CARMEL IS DRIED UP) כרמל is generally said of planted places. Specifically, two places are so called: one by the sea where Elijah lived, another in which Nabal dwelt: and Jerome thinks this one is to be understood here, because it was closer to the desert, and for that reason better known to the shepherds. Often drought gives cause for the earth to be moved, as noted by Aristotle. The same cause for sterility in fields. Pliny says the city of Rome never trembled without it being a harbinger of some future event.

Verse 3. FOR THREE TRANSGRESSIONS OF DAMASCUS, AND FOR FOUR I WILL NOT TURN AWAY THE PUNISHMENT THEREOF) I will not revoke this: namely, what I have decreed. The Chaldean expressed the meaning: I will not spare them: because they act wickedly so often, I will execute my threats.

BECAUSE THEY HAVE THRESHED GILEAD WITH IRON SLEDGES) Under King Hazael, who invaded the land of Gilead 2 Kings 10:33, such a cruel victor, that he even cut up infants, 2 Kings 8:12. For iron sledges, Theodotion said, iron wheels. LXX. ἐν πρίοσι σιδηροῖς. Jerome explains this, saying it was a type of sledge, which was rolled on iron and toothed wheels underneath, so that by shaking out the grain it would crush the stubble on the threshing floor, and break up the straw into fodder for beasts of burden because of the scarcity of hay.

Verse 4. AND I WILL SEND A FIRE INTO THE HOUSE OF HAZAEL) Into the palaces built by Hazael. Similar to Is. 49:27.

AND IT SHALL DEVOUR THE HOUSES OF BENHADAD) Of him who succeeded Hazael his father 2 Kings 13:3. The Greeks read ד for ך in this name, as we have noted elsewhere, and Jerome here.

Verse 5. AND I WILL BREAK THE BAR OF DAMASCUS) that is, the gates which were accustomed to be closed with bars.

AND I WILL CUT OFF THE INHABITANT FROM THE PLAIN OF AVEN) בקעת און was that place called by the Hebrews: but by the Syrians בקעת שמש, which is Heliopolis to the Greeks. See Ptolemy on Syria.

AND HIM THAT HOLDETH THE SCEPTER FROM THE HOUSE OF EDEN) From the house of Eden, which is Paradise to the same Ptolemy.

AND THE PEOPLE OF SYRIA SHALL GO INTO CAPTIVITY UNTO KIR) We said at 2 Kings 16 that Kir is not Cyrene, but a part of Albania situated by the river Cyrus, from which place we learn that what is said here about Damascus being devastated, and about the deportation of the Syrian Damascenes, was fulfilled by Tiglath-pileser.

Ver. 6. FOR THREE TRANSGRESSIONS OF GAZA) He passes from the Syrian Damascenes to the Palestinians.

BECAUSE THEY CARRIED AWAY A PERFECT CAPTIVITY, TO SHUT THEM UP IN EDOM) A peaceful captivity, that they might deliver them to the Edomite. When Sennacherib invaded Judea, many at his first arrival betook themselves to neighboring regions, as appeared in Isaiah 16:4. The Philistines did not protect these Jews, who had harmed them in nothing, as suppliants, but sold them to the Edomites as if they were captives of war.

Ver. 7. AND I WILL SEND A FIRE ON THE WALL OF GAZA) These things, which are predicted concerning the cities of the Philistines, were fulfilled by Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:8. The same is predicted by Isaiah 15.

Ver. 8. THE REMNANT OF THE PHILISTINES SHALL PERISH) By the Assyrians. Is. 20.

Ver. 9. BECAUSE THEY HAVE SHUT UP A PERFECT CAPTIVITY) They held as captives those with whom they had peace, as above.

AND HAVE NOT REMEMBERED THE BROTHERLY COVENANT) Of Solomon and Hiram: for those allied among themselves were called brothers, 1 Kings 9:13.

Ver. 10. AND I WILL SEND A FIRE ON THE WALL OF TYRE) Many parts of the city were burned by the fiery darts of the Chaldeans, Jer. 25:12. Ezek. 26, ch. 27, & 28, where see the remarks.

Ver. 11. BECAUSE HE DID PURSUE HIS BROTHER WITH THE SWORD) The descendants of Jacob, who was the brother of Esau. Hence also descendants are called brothers, Deuteronomy 23:7. This was done at that time when the Syrians besieged Jerusalem, 2 Kings 16:5.

AND DID CAST OFF HIS PITY) that is, he extinguished all pity toward the Jews.

AND HIS ANGER DID TEAR PERPETUALLY, AND HE KEPT HIS WRATH FOR EVER) Persistent in hatred, like Esau, Gen. 27:41.

Ver. 12. I WILL SEND A FIRE UPON TEMAN, WHICH SHALL DEVOUR THE PALACES OF BOZRAH) By Sennacherib. Teman and Bozrah are noble cities of Edom. Gen. 25:15. Jer. 25:23. Is. 63.

Ver. 13. BECAUSE THEY HAVE RIPPED UP THE WOMEN WITH CHILD OF GILEAD) It is the same as what is said in Jeremiah 49, where see the remarks.

Vers. 14. ON THE WALL OF RABBAH) Which is Rabbath-Ammon in Polybius. See Jer. 49, 2. Ezek. 25, 5.

Vers. 15. AND MELCHOM SHALL GO INTO CAPTIVITY) Their idol is called Moloch. This is here, and in Jerem. 49, 1, called their Meloch, as below 'your Moloch'. 5, 26. With the cities captured, the gods also shall be captured. Jer. 49, 3.

AND HIS PRINCES TOGETHER) The priests, thus the LXX.

It is not about the idol Moloch, but the discourse is about the King of the Ammonites. Grotius confuses different words with the Vulgate Interpreter. For in the Hebrew text it is not מלכם as in 1 Kings 11, 5, just as the Vulgate rendered it Melchom, as if it were about an idol, but מלכם which is THEIR King, which also occurs in Jer. 49, 3. And therefore there is no doubt that it is about the King here, who is to go away in deportation together with his Princes, nor is there any reason why we should understand here the priests of the idol, since the Hebrew word שרים nowhere denotes priests, but Princes.

Latin:

N. J. OTATA MOSUM.

QVIVM.

Israelitis, quos ob varia crimina acriter reprehen- dit, iisdem nisi resipuerint tum alias pœnas, tum e- versionem regni utriusque ac verbi divini subtra- ctionem prædicens, adjectis tamen sub finem ob fi- deles ac pœnitentes promissionibus Evangelicis de Israelis in N. T. erectione. Distribui autem potest in conciones tum nudas, tum typis & visionibus vesti- tas. Nudæ quatuor constituuntur. Earum prima est communis, ad alios etiam pertinens, reliquæ tres Is- raelitarum propriæ sunt. Prima Cap. 1. & 2. absol- vitur de judiciis, tum hostibus exteris, tum degentibus in regno Judæ & Israelis obventuris : priora plera- que exceptis nempe judiciis de Moabitis cap. 1. tra- dita, posteriora vero cap. 2. post judicia adversus Moabitas exercenda proposita sunt.

Israelitarum propriæ conciones sunt partim com- minatoriæ, quæ diriguntur tum ad universos genera- tim, utpote secunda cap. 3. tum ad pingues vaccas vel proceres regni speciatim, utpote tertia concio c. 4. in quibus ob posthabita beneficia divina Prophe- ta iis minatus est gravissima divina judicia ; partim pœnitentiales, qualis est quarta concio c. 5. & 6. ubi vita promittitur, si pœnitentiam egerint, sed cum prævideat Amos eorum impœnitentiam, abductio- nem populo intimat, c. 5. (inserta tamen v. 24. pro- missione Evangelica) eamque exemplis aliis ac jura- mento Dei confirmat, & ob securos exitium eorum plenius adumbrat, inserta tamen succincta pro- missione Evangelica.

Conciones typis vel visionibus adumbratæ exhi- bentur c. 7. c. 8. & 9. & continent tum legales com- minationes, tum Evangelicas promissiones, & capite septimo quidem visiones tres traduntur, in quarum duarum Propheta pro populo adhuc intercedit, ob tertiam vero excelsorum & templorum desolatio- ne ac domus Jeroboami clade prædicta Amos sedi- tionis ab Amasia arguitur, sed se defendit, & Amasiæ exilium, ejusque familiæ exitium indicit. Octavo vero capite nova visione finem populi Israëlitici & famem verbi divini intimat. Nono denique visione finali manus Dei gravitatem, quam nemo effugere queat, & faciei divinæ ad eversionem directæ vim describit: Simul autem promissionem de non penitus exscindenda domo Jacobi v. 8. inspergit. Conclu- dens tandem Prophetiam suam cap. eodem à v. 11. usque ad finem promissione Evangelica, de erigen- do tabernaculo Davidis, & adducendis Edomitis, & gentibus.

IN DIEBVS OSIÆ REGIS JVDÆ) Qui Aza- rias scribitur in Regum libris.

ET IN DIEBVS JEROBOAM, FILII JOAS REGIS ISRAEL.) Illius Jeroboami, cujus tempore & Osees vaticinatus fuit: & cujus historia 2. Reg. 15, 8.

ANTE DVOS ANNOS TERRÆ MOTVS) Eum terræ motum & Hebræi scriptores, & ter Hieronymus, id est, hoc loco, ad 6. Esaia, & ad 4. Zachariæ, ait evenisse, eo ipso tempore, quo rex Osias, ob attentata munera sacerdota- lia, lepra percussus est. Accedit Josephi auctoritas Antiq. 9, 11. Μεταξὺ δὲ σεισμὸς ἐκλόνησε τὴν γῆν μέγας. κὴ διαστάν- τος τῶ ναῦ, φέγγος ἡλίκ λαμπρὸν ἐξέλαμψε, κὴ τῇ τῶ βασι- λέως ὄψει προσέπεσεν, ὡς τῷ μεν εὐθέως λέπραν ἐπιδραμεῖν πρὸ δὲ τῆς πόλεως, πρὸς τῇ καλουμένη ἐρωγῇ τὸ ὄρος, ἀποῤῥα- γῆναι τὸ ἥμισυ τὸ κατὰ τὴν δυσμὴν, κὴ κυλισθὲν τέσσαρας σταδίους ἐπὶ τὸ ἀνατολικὸν ὄρος στῆναι, ὡς τάς τε παρόδους ἐμφραγῆναι, κὴ τὰς παραδείσες βασιλικώς.

Non Josephus tantum, & Hieronymus, sed Prophe- ta etiam Zacharias cap. 14, 5. terræ motus mentio- nem facit, qui tempore Regis Osiæ icciderit. De articulo tamen temporis nihil Scriptura definit; quia res tum in vulgus nota, & motus ille terræ ob magnitudinem nemini obscurus fuit. Quem ple- rique sane cum Ebræi, tum Christiani ad illud tem- pus, quo Osias Elephantiasi percussus fuit 2. Reg. 15, 5. 2. Chron. 26, 20. referunt, nonnulli tamen ad tumultus & motus bellicos, qui mortem Jero- boami sequuti sunt, trahunt 2. Reg. 15, 8. 13. aliqui ad annum mortis Osiæ è collatione cap. 6. Es. 6, 4. referendum esse, opinantur. B. Gerhardo visum, terræ hunc motum duobus annis durasse saltem, per intervalla, alioquin dictum fuisse Prophetam: Duobus annis ante terræ motum.

PARS I. Exhibens quatuor conciones nudas, fere tantum legales. CONCIO I. Communis. DE JUDICIIS DEI CAUPT I. Judicia DEI adversus exteros.

Præmissa Prophetæ Amosi conditione, visione, temporisque circumstantia rugitum vocis Domini intimat; & judicia adversus Da- mascum, Gasam, Zor, Edom, indicat.

Amos vindictam canit Israelis in hostes.

Vers. 1.

VERBA AMOS) Inscriptio hæc, & aliarum Pro- phetiarum facta est non à Prophetis, sed à Senatu magno, qui Prophetarum scripta colligebat, & prænotabat tem- pora. Ostendit hoc mentio terræ motus. Nomen est עמוס plane diversum ab אמוץ,quod nomen Patri Esaiæ, quan- quam Latine pari modo scribatur.

Vers. 2.

DOMINVS DE SION RVGIET, ET DE JE- RVSALEM DABIT VOCEM SVAM) Locutio eadem quæ Joel 3, 16. Sic & Jerem. 25, 30. Ira Dei his verbis significatur.

Et si iram Dei significari hac loquutione admitti possit, verbum tamen Domini, quo ira denuncia- tur, & ad pœnitentiam invitantur homines, judi- ciis Dei impendentibus excitati, per rugitum il- lum Domini designari, dubitandum non est, tum quia de Sion & de Jerusalem rugitus ille auditur, quod Vebro Domini de Sione, ubi ignem & focum suum habuit Dominus, convenit, non adeo iræ Domini, quæ potius de cœlo manifestari dicitur, Rom. 1,16. tum quia rugitus ille per vocem Domi- ni declaratur, aut cum eadem conjungitur. Non ergo solum ira notatur, sed judiciorum Dei per VERBUM Domini denunciatio, quæ impiis hor- ribilis rugitus est, fidelibus vero ac pœnitentibus vox Domini non ingrata. Non enim rugit Domi- nus, ut terreat solum, nedum ut devoret, qui rugi- tus leoni infernali tribuitur, 1. Petr. 5, 8. sed ut ex- citet resipiscentiam, & gratiam loco supplicii ex- hibere possit, quum mortem peccatoris non velit, sed ut convertatur, & vivat Ezech. 18. & 33. Ideo rugitus Domini de Sion non tantum hic, & Jerem. 25, 30. denunciationi judiciorum, & pœnarum ter- ribili adhibetur, sed etiam de prædicatione pæniten- tiæ, quæ in nomine Domini Jesu fieri debebat, per terrarum orbem, sermo & phrasis eadem usurpa- ta legitur Joel 3, 16. ut ad istum locum diximus, quæ diversitas applicationis è materia substrata de- prehenditur. Non enim necessum est, eandem phrasin eidem argumento adhiberi, sed respi- cienda juxta cum phrasi imprimis etiam textus συνέχεια. Quanquam vero hic Syris, Moabitis, aliisque populis exteris judicia Domini denunciat, tamen quia hæc vidisse dicitur SUPER ISRAEL, seu decem tribus, id spectat imprimis, ut Israelem

UNde hanc de ἐπιγραφῇ Prophetæ hujus & aliarum opinionem habeat, vel quo argu- mento mutus, eandem amplexus sit, non indicat Grotius. E terræ motus mentione tale quid colligi non potest. Quid enim vetat ejus commemo- rationem ab ipso Propheta factam dicere? Sen- tentia ergo illa, ut nova, mere arbitraria, nullo fun- damento innixa, textus Prophetici αὐθεντίᾳ non satis æqua, vel certe dubium eundem, quoad istiusmodi inscriptiones reddens, merito repro- batur. Nemo, quod sciam, dubitavit easdem ab ipsis Prophetis profectas, nemo pro laciniis aliende affutis habuit. Et cohærent illæ textui, ceu partes textus sine ullo indicio aut characte- re προσθέσεως. Num Senatus ille magnus θεο- πνεύστως addiderit, quæ addidisse eum credidit, haud dixisset Grotius: imo θεόπνευστα illa addi- tamenta, sine dubio, negasset. Qui ergo ita con- stare queat harum Scripturæ partium θεοπνευ- σία & αὐθεντία ἀνυπεύθυνος?

Vers. eod.

IN PASTORIBUS) Vide infra 7, 14. Tale illud Hesiodi de se: Αρνας ποίμαινονθ' Ελικῶνος ὑπὸ ζαθέοιο Pro נקדים,LXX. legerunt נקרים: & verterunt ἐν νακ- καρείμ, pro quo ἐν ἀκκαρείμ, in quibusdam libris scri- ptum est.

DE THECUE) Qui tractus sex millibus à Be- thleemo abitus, continuus est cum maximo deserto, quod Arabiam transit, ut notat hic Hieronymus.

terreat, & ad pœnitentiam revocet, exemplo ju- diciorum Domini in exteros, priusquam illi pro- pria supplicia denunciet, q. d. Si Dominus non par- cit gentibus Verbi divini luce destitutis, & volun- tatis ejus ignaris, multo minus populo suo verbum contemnenti parcet. Luc. 12, 47. Jac. 4, 17. Finitimi enim erant illi populi Judæis, quibus cogitandum illud fuerat: Et tua res agitur, paries cum proximus ardet. Et: Felix quem faciunt aliena pericula cautum. Ad Septentrionem respectu Judææ sita erat Syria, cujus metropolis Damascus, inter Meridiem & Oc- cidentem finitimi erant Philistini, quorum Satrapiæ quatuor, Gaza, Asdod, Ascalon & Ekron hic notan- tur. Quinta Gad omissa, forsan quod adhuc in di- tione Regum Judæ fuerit, ex quo eam cepit David 2. Sam. 18, 1. 1. Paral. 19, 1. Inter Occidentem & Se- ptentrionem Tyrii vicini erant: Ad meridiem con- termini erant Idumæi: ad Orientem in parte Septen- trionali Ammonitæ, in parte Meridionali Moabitæ.

Vers. eod. ET LUXERUNT SPECIOSA PASTORUM) Pa- scua. Joel, 2, 22.

ET EXSICCATUS EST VERTEX CARMELI) כרמל generaliter dicuntur loci consiti. Speciatim duo lo- ca sic dicuntur: alter ad mare ubi vixit Elias, alter in quo ha- bitabat Nabal: & hunc hic intelligendum putat Hierony- mus, quia propior erat deserto, & pastoribus ob id notior. Sæpe siccitas causam dat cur moveatur terra, ut notatum Ari- stoteli. Eadem agris causa sterilitatis. Plinius ait nunquam urbem Romam tremuisse, ut non futuri eventus alicujus id prænuncium esset.

Vers. 3. SUPER TRIBUS SCELERIBUS DAMA- SCI, ET SUPER QVATUOR NON CONVERTAM EUM) Non revocabo hoc: nempe quod decrevi. Chaldæus sensum expressit: non parcam eis: quia toties inique agunt minas meas exequar.

EO QVOD TRITURAVERINT IN PLAU- STRIS FERREIS GALAAD) Hazaele Rege, qui terram Galaad invasit 2. Reg. 10, 33. tam crudelis victor, ut & in- fantes dissecaret, 2. Reg. 8, 12. Pro plaustris ferreis dixit Theodotion, rotis ferreis. LXX. ἐν πρίοσι σιδηροῖς. Explicat autem hoc Hieronymus, dicens plaustri fuisse genus, quod rotis subter ferreis atque dentatis volvebatur, ut excussis frumentis stipulam in aream contereret, & in cibos jumen- torum propter fœni sterilitatem paleas comminueret.

Vers. 4. ET MITTAM IGNEM IN DOMUM A- ZAEL) In palatia structa ab Azaele. Simile Es. 49, 27.

ET DEVORABIT DOMOS BENHADAD) Ejus, qui successit Hazaeli patri suo 2. Reg. 13, 3. Græci pro ך le- gerunt ד in hoc nomine, ut & nos alibi notavimus, & hic Hieronymus.

Vers. 5. ET CONTERAM VECTEM DAMASCI) id est, portas quæ vectibus claudi solebant.

ET DISPERDAM HABITATOREM DE CAM- PO IDOLI) בקעת און vocabatur is locus Hebræis: Syris vero בקעת שמש, quæ Ἡλιόπολις Græcis. Vide Ptolemæum in Syria.

ET TENENTEM SCEPTRUM DE DOMO VOLUPTATIS) De domo Heden, qui παράδεισος eidem Ptolemæo.

ET TRANSFERETUR POPULUS STRIÆ CY- RENEM) קיר esse non Cyrenen, sed partem Albaniæ ad- sitam Cyrrho amni diximus ad 2. Reg. 16. ex quo loco di- scimus, quæ hic de Damasco vastata, & de Syrorum Dama- scenorum deportatione dicuntur, impleta per Teglath- phalasarem.

Vers. 6. SUPER TRIBUS SCELERIBUS GAZÆ) A Syris Damascenis ad Palæstinos transit.

EO QVOD TRANSTULERINT CAPTIVI- TATEM PERFECTAM, UT CONCLUDERENT EAM IN IDUMÆA) Captivitatem pacificam, ut eos tra- derent Idumæo. Cum Sennacheribus Judæam invasit, multi ad primum ejus adventum in vicinas regiones se recepere, ut apparuit Esaiæ 16, 4. Philistini hos Judæos, qui nihil ipsis nocuerant, non ut supplices protexerunt, sed quasi bello captos vendiderunt Idumæis.

Vers. 7. ET MITTAM IGNEM IN MURUM GAZÆ) Hæc, quæ prædicuntur de urbibus Philistinorum, impleta sunt per Ezechiam 2. Reg. 18, 8. prædicitur idem ab Es. 15.

Vers. 8. PERIBUNT RELIQVI PHILISTINORUM) Per Assyrios. Es, 20.

Vers. 9. EO QVOD CONCLUSERINT CAPTI- VITATEM PERFECTAM) Pro captivis habuerunt, quibuscum pacem habebant, ut supra.

ET NON SINT RECORDATI FEDERIS FRA- TRUM) Salomonis & Hirami: nam federati inter se fra- tres vocabantur 1. Reg. 9, 13.

Vers. 10. ET MITTAM IGNEM IN MURUM TI- RI) Multae partes urbis incensae ignitis jaculis Chaldaeo- rum Jer. 25, 12. Ezech. 26. c. 27. & 28. ubi dicta vide.

Vers. 11. EO QVOD PERSECUTUS SIT IN GLA- DIO FRATREM SUUM) Jacobi posteros, qui frater Esavi. Hinc & posteri fratres dicuntur, Deuteron. 23, 7. Fa- ctum hoc eo tempore, cum Syri obsederunt Hioroso- lyma, 2. Reg. 16, 5.

ET VIOLAVERIT MISERICORDIA EJUS) id est, omnem misericordiam erga Judaeos exstinxerit.

ET TENUERIT ULTRA ODIUM SUUM, ET INDIGNATIONEM SUAM SERVAVERIT USQVE IN FINEM) Pertinax in odio, ut Esavus, Gen. 27, 23.

Vers. 12. MITTAM IGNEM IN THEMAN, ET DEVO- RABIT ÆDES BOSRAE) Per Sennacheribum. Theman & Bostra urbes nobiles Idumaeae. Gen. 25, 15. Jer. 25, 23. Es. 63.

Vers. 13. EO QVOD DISSECUERIT PRAEGNANTES IN GALAAD) Idem est, quod dicitur Jerem. 49. ubi dicta vide.

Vers. 14. IN MURO RABBA) Quae Rabbathamman Polybio. Vide Jer. 49, 2. Ezech. 25, 5.

Vers. 15. ET IBIT MELCHOM IN CAPTIVITA- TEM) Idolum ipsorum Moloch dictum. Id hic, & Jerem. 49, 1. dicitur Meloch ipsorum, ut infra Moloch vester. 5, 26. captis urbibus, capientur & Dii. Jer. 49, 3.

ET PRINCIPES EJUS SIMUL) Sacerdotes, Ita LXX.

Non de Moloch idolo, sed de Rege Ammonita- rum sermo est. Confundit Grotius cum vulgato Interprete diversas voces. In Ebraeo enim textu non habetur מלכם uti 1. Reg. 11, 5. quemadmodum Vulgatus reddidit Melchom, quasi de idolo ageretur, sed מלכם quod est Rex EORUM, quod etiam Jer. 49, 3. occurrit. Ideoque dubium non est de Rege hic agi, in deportatione cum Principibus suis si- mul abituro, nec causa ulla est, cur intelligamus hic Sacerdotes idoli, quum vox Ebraea שרים nuspiam sacerdotes notet, sed Principes.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. The judgments of God against the Moabites, Judah, and Israel.

To the Moabites, on account of the burning of the bones of the King of Edom, he predicts that fire will consume their palaces and destruction; to Judah, on account of the contempt of the law of the Lord, he likewise threatens a destructive fire; finally, to the Israelites, on account of injustice, incest, and gluttony, following the example of the Ammonite predecessors in that land, he prophesies a punishment which neither the swiftest nor the strongest will escape, especially because they offer wine to the Nazarites and forbid the prophets from prophesying.

He predicts double punishments for the sin of the Hebrews.

Vers. 1. FOR THREE TRANSGRESSIONS OF MOAB) It appears that these cohere with the preceding.

BECAUSE HE BURNED THE BONES OF THE KING OF EDOM EVEN TO ASHES) Why what is touched upon here should not be considered the same as that which we had in 2 Kings 3, 27, we said in that place. שיד, which is also סיד in Is. 33, 12, is lime rather than ash, and if we believe the Chaldean interpreter, the Moabites used the bones of the King of Edom for lime to plaster walls. It is credible that the Moabites, having been subdued by the Chaldeans and serving as soldiers for the Chaldeans, wished in this way to show their hatred against those who were still resisting the Chaldeans.

Thus also some Hebrews opine. But because the preposition ל often denotes the thing itself, not what is in place of the thing, Gen. 2, 7, Ezek. 37, 27, the opinion of those seems simpler who understand the bones of the King of the Edomites as burnt into LIME or ash, for ashes to lime are compared, on account of their thinness and whiteness.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Judicia Dei adversus Moabitas, Judam & Israelem.

Moabitis ob ossium Regis Idumaei combustionem ignem palatia consumturum & excidium praedicit: Judae ob legis Domini contemtum itidem ignem destructorium minatur: I- sraelitis denique ob injustitiam, incestus, gu- lam ad Ammonitarum antecessorum in illa terra exemplum poenam, quam nec velo- cissimi, nec fortissimi quique effugient, vati- cinatur, imprimis quod Nazaraeis vinum praebeant, & Prophetis vaticinia prohibeant.

Peccati poenas geminas praedicit Hebraeis.

Vers. 1. SUPER TRIBUS SCELERIBUS MOAB) Apparet haec cohaerere cum superioribus.

EO QVOD INCENDERIT OSSA REGIS IDU- MAEAE USQVE AD CINEREM) Cur quod hic tangitur, non idem censendum sit cum eo, quod habuimus 2. Reg. 3, 27. diximus illo loco. שיד, quod & סיד Es. 33, 12. est calx potius, quam cinis, & si Chaldaeo interpreti credimus, Moabitae ossibus Regis Idumaei usi sunt pro calce ad obli- nendos parietes. Credibile est Moabitas subactos a Chaldaeis, & Chaldaeis militantes, hoc modo odium suum voluisse o- stendere in eos, qui adhuc Chaldaeis resistebant.

SIc etiam opinantur Ebraei nonnulli. Sed quia praepositio ל saepe rem ipsam, non quod vice rei est, notat Gen. 2, 7. Ezech. 37, 27. simplicior vide- tur eorum sententia, qui ossa Regis Edomaeorum in CALCEM vel cinerem, nam cineres calci comparantur, ob exilitatem & albedinem, com- busta intelligunt.

Ver. 2. AND IT SHALL DEVOUR THE HOUSES OF KERIOTH) Cities of the Moabites, Jer. 48, 24.

Ver. 3. AND I WILL CUT OFF THE JUDGE FROM THE MIDST THEREOF) The Suffete and, as it were, the interrex.

Ver. 4. FOR THREE TRANSGRESSIONS OF JUDAH) That is, of the two tribes.

Vers. 4. SUPER TRIBUS SCELERIBUS JUDA) Id est, duarum tribuum.

Ver. 5. I WILL SEND A FIRE UPON JUDAH) [By] Nebuchadnezzar.

Vers. 5. MITTAM IGNEM IN JUDA Nabucho- donosori.

## 2:6
Ver. 6. FOR THREE TRANSGRESSIONS OF ISRAEL) Of the ten tribes.

BECAUSE HE SOLD THE RIGHTEOUS FOR SILVER) That is, corrupted by a price, he judged against him.

AND THE POOR FOR A PAIR OF SHOES) That is, for even the smallest price. So also below 8, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SUPER TRIBUS SCELERIBUS ISRAEL) Decem tribuum.

QVOD VENDIDERIT PRO ARGENTO JU- STUM) Id est, pretio corruptus contra eum judicaverit.

ET PAUPEREM PRO CALCEAMENTIS) Id est, pro minimo etiam pretio. Sic & infra 8, 6.

## 2:7
Ver. 7. WHO TREAD UPON THE DUST OF THE EARTH THE HEAD OF THE POOR) They afflict the poor to the ground.

The Hebrew, rendered variously by various people, B. Gerhard thinks can be explained most simply thus: who pant after the dust of the earth, which is and clings to the head of the needy, cast down by them into the earth, i.e., who do not have enough in casting them out, but furthermore pant after their head and life, so that they may take that away also. And yet here it does not seem that snares for slaughter are intended, but rather the unjust oppression of the poor in judgments and outside of them, so that the injustice noted in the preceding verse may be further depicted, and as the Greeks, the LXX, the Chaldean, the Vulgate, and Luther have correctly rendered the sense: They tread the head of the poor into the mire; since שׁאף, as B. Gerhard notes, means to pursue someone with panting and great zeal and effort, just as Saul insisted upon David, Psalm 56, 1. seqq. 57, 4. (see & Amos 8, 4.) [and] κτ̓ πόδα, the text can be rendered thus: They pant to pursue even into the dust of the earth; (which happens when one is trampled by feet, compare below chapter 5.) and thus they pant after the head of the needy. For the things that follow also still tend toward this injustice: they pervert the way, that is, the cause, of the humble, that is, of men of despised lot, they cut off their causes, so that they may not be legitimately recognized in judgment. For it follows.

AND TURN ASIDE THE WAY OF THE HUMBLE) That is, they pervert their affairs. Job 24, 3.

AND THE SON AND HIS FATHER SHALL GO UNTO THE MAID) Such a wickedness as is not heard of even among the nations (the Gentiles, that is) 1 Cor. 5.

THAT THEY MIGHT PROFANE MY HOLY NAME) He shows what followed from that. The profane nations used to say: behold the people of God, 2 Pet. 2, 3.

Concerning the various interpretation of the Hebrew phrase, and which may be the genuine one, see B. Tarnovius. The indefatigable effort of the wicked is noted, in oppressing the weak even before the judgment, while they pervert the way of the humble, that is, in the style of Scripture, their cause, business, judgment, Exod. 18, 20. John 17, 9. Job 24, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVI CONTERUNT SUPER PULVEREM TERRÆ CAPITA PAUPERUM) Pauperes affligunt solo.

Ebræa varie à variis reddita ita simpliciffime ex- poni posse censet B. Gerhardus: qui anhelant in pul- verem terræ, qui est & hæret in capite tenuium, à se in terram prostratorum, h. e. qui non sat habent eos ejicere, sed insuper ad caput & vitam eorum adspi- rant, ut eam quoque auferant. Atqui hic non vi- dentur insidiæ ad cædem, sed ad injustam pauperum in judiciis & extra ea oppressionem respici, ut injusti- tia versu præcedente notata ulterius depingatur, & qua sensum recte reddiderint Græci, LXX. Chald. Vulg. & Luther. Sie treten den Kopff der Armen in Koth; quum שׁאף notante B. Gerhardofit, cum an- helitu magnoque studio & conatu aliquem prosequi, uti Saul insistebat Davidi Psal. 56, 1. seqq. 57, 4. (vid. & Amos 8, 4.) κτ̓ πόδα ita reddi potest textus: An- helant ad persequendum usque in pulverem terræ; (quod fit, cum pedibus, quis proculcatur, confer infra cap. 5.) adeoque in caput tenuium anhelant. Nam & ea, quæ sequuntur, ad hanc injustitiam ad- huc tendunt: pervertunt viam, id est, causam, hu- milium, id est, hominum contemtæ sortis, interci- dunt causæ eorum, ne in judicio legitime agno- scantur. Sequitur enim.

ET VIAM HUMILIUM DECLINANT) Id est, res eorum pervertunt. Job. 24, 3.

ET FILIUS AC PATER EJUS ERUNT AD PUELLAM) Quale flagitium nec inter gentes (moratio- res scilicet) auditur 1. Corinth. 5.

UT VIOLARENT NOMEN SANCTUM) Osten- dit, quid inde sit consecutum. Dicebant gentes prophanæ: en populum Dei, 2. Pet. 2, 3.

De phraseos Ebrææ interpretatione varia, & quæ genuina sit vid. B. Tarnovius. Notatur eadem conatus improborum indefessus, in opprimendis et- iam coram judicio tenuibus, dum viam humilium, h. e. Scripturæ stylo, causam, negotium, judicium, Exod. 18, 20. Joh. 17, 9. pervertunt, Job. 24, 14.

## 2:8
Ver. 8. AND THEY LAID THEMSELVES DOWN UPON CLOTHES LAID TO PLEDGE BY EVERY ALTAR) On beds, the Chaldean. From those who did not worship idols together with them, they took pledges, and used them adorned in the temples. Thus Jerome here.

AND THEY DRANK THE WINE OF THE CONDEMNED IN THE HOUSE OF THEIR GOD) Wine procured from the goods of the condemned, because they did not worship idols with them. LXX. wine from extortions. Chaldean, wine of rapine.

B. Winckelmannus observes here three sins which had concurred: For first, idolatry is noted, because they sacrificed to their gods not in Jerusalem, but in Dan and Bethel, against the Lord's constitution. 2. The detention of the poor's pledge is argued against the law of the Lord, Deut. 24, 12. If he be a poor man, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge, but shalt in any case deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment, and bless thee. But they claimed for themselves the pledged garments, and reclined upon them at sacred feasts by every altar. 3. And they drank the wines of the fined, that is, they contributed to their sacred feasts fines extorted from men contrary to justice, which was a profanation of sacred things and an illusion of God. It was the custom to hold the solemn feasts of sacrifices in the Temple itself, Deut. 14, 23, 26. 1 Sam. 1, 3, 4. But especially also, a notable injustice is marked here by the Prophet, as we observed at v. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET SUPER VESTIMENTIS PIGNORATIS ACCUBUERUNT JUXTA OMNE ALTARE) In lectis, Chaldæus. Ab iis, qui non una cum ipsis idola colebant, sumebant pignora, eisque ornati utebantur in Templis. Ita hic Hieronymus.

ET VINUM DAMNATORUM BIBEBANT IN DOMO DEI SUI) Vinum comparatum ex bonis damna- torum, ob id quod idola cum ipsis non colerent. LXX. οἶνον ἐκ συκοφαντιῶν. Chaldæus, vinum rapinæ.

Observat hic tria peccata, quæ concurrerant, B. Winckelmannus: Notatur enim primum idolola- tria, quia non Hierofolymis, sed in Dan & Bethel sa- crificabant Diis suis, contra Domini constitutio- nem. 2. Arguitur detentio pignoris pauperum con- tra legem Domini Deut. 24, 12. Si pauper est, non pernoctabit apud te pignus, sed statim reddes ei in oc- casu Solis, ut dormiens in vestimento suo, benedicat tibi. Verum ipsi vestimenta oppignorata sibi vendi- cabant, & in epulis sacris juxta omne altare super illis accumbebant. 3. Et vina mulctatorum bibe- bant, id est, mulctas præter jus ab hominibus ex- tortas, in sacras suas epulas contribuebant, quæ a- rat sacrorum profanatio & illusio Dei. Moris erat in ipso Templo solemnia sacrificiorum convivia agitare, Deut. 14, 23. 26. 1. Sam. 1, 3. 4. Sed impri- mis etiam notata hîc à Propheta insignis injustitia, uti ad v. 7. observavimus.

## 2:9
Ver. 9.

YET DESTROYED I THE AMORITE BEFORE THEM) After the exodus from Egypt, as follows. God commemorates His benefits, so that the guilt of such ungrateful people may appear more grievous.

WHOSE HEIGHT WAS LIKE THE HEIGHT OF THE CEDARS) It abounds in the Hebrew manner; and it explains the case of only אשר, absolute. The Amorites were men of extraordinary stature.

AND HE WAS STRONG AS THE OAKS) They were the same, stronger than the other peoples around.

YET DESTROYED I HIS FRUIT FROM ABOVE, AND HIS ROOTS FROM BENEATH) An allegory taken from a tree, which is cast out from the foundations.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

EGO AUTEM EXTERMINAVI AMORRHÆ- UM A FACIE EORUM) Post exitum ex Ægypto, ut sequitur. Commemorat sua beneficia Deus, quo gravior appareat culpa tam ingratorum.

CUJUS ALTITUDO, CEDRORUM ALTITU- DO EJUS) Abundat ejus more Hebræo; & casum tantum explicat אשר, ἀπόλυτος. Amorrhæi homines erant eximiæ magnitudinis.

ET FORTIS IPSE QVASI QVERCUS) Erant iidem validiores cæteris circum populis.

ET CONTRIVI FRUCTUM EJUS DESUPER, ET RADICES EJUS SUBTER) Allegoria ab arbore sumpta, quæ funditus ejicitur.

## 2:11
Ver. 11. AND I RAISED UP OF YOUR SONS FOR PROPHETS) As the LXX. those in the time of Moses, such as Joshua, Samuel, then so many others.

AND OF YOUR YOUNG MEN NAZARITES) Which was a great honor to the people, Lam. 4, 7.

IS IT NOT SO O CHILDREN OF ISRAEL?) Such is that: Can you deny this also, O deceitful Crete?

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET SUSCITAVI DE FILIIS VESTRIS IN PROPHETAS) Ut LXX. illos Mosis tempore, ut Jo- suam, Samuelem, deinde tot alios.

ET DE JUVENIBUS VESTRIS NAZARÆOS) Quod magnum decus erat populo, Thren. 4, 7.

NUNQUID NON ITA EST FILII ISRAEL?) Tale illud: Nunquid & hoc fallax Creta negare potes?

## 2:12
Ver. 12.

AND YOU SHALL GIVE THE NAZARITES WINE TO DRINK) But you give the Nazarites wine to drink. Against the vow and the law. Num. 6, 2.

AND YOU SHALL COMMAND THE PROPHETS) You give orders. See an example below 7, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET PROPINABITIS NAZARÆIS VINUM) At vos datis Nazaræis vinum potandum. Contra votum & legem. Num. 6, 2.

ET PROPHETIS MANDABITIS) Præcipitis. Ex- emplum vide infra 7, 13.

## 2:13
Ver. 13. I WILL GROAN OVER YOU) I will press your place, so the Chaldean; namely, with enemies arriving from all sides.

AS A CART GROANS THAT IS LADEN WITH HAY) As it is pressed. The shepherd speaks things suitable to himself, and takes similes from rustic matters.

Latin:

Vers. 13. EGO STRIDEBO SUPER VOS) Pressurus sum locum vestrum, Ita Chaldæus; hostibus scilicet un- dique adventantibus.

SICUT STRIDET PLAUSTRUM ONUSTUM FOENO) Sicut premitur. Pastor sibi convenientia lo- quitur, & similitudines sumit à rebus rusticis.

## 2:14
Ver. 14. AND FLIGHT SHALL PERISH FROM THE SWIFT) Many shall be caught in the very flight.

THE STRONG SHALL NOT RETAIN HIS STRENGTH) He shall lose heart.
