## 3:1 Argument
SERMON II. PROPER TO THE ISRAELITES. CHAPTER III. A threatening against the Israelites in general.

Having set forth the divine benefits in the leading out from Egypt and the taking up of the people, as well as the foretelling of divine judgments, or the testimony of their enemies in Ashdod and Egypt, the Prophet teaches that the Israelites are convicted of injustice and wicked spoils, and therefore threatens them with siege, oppression, and the plundering of their house, and the destruction of their little ones and those who are weaker. When God wishes to punish, He first stirs up Prophets.

Verse 1.

ABOVE ALL THE KINDRED WHICH I BROUGHT OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT) He now addresses both the two and the ten tribes collectively.

Latin:

CONCIO II. ISRAELITIS PROPRIA. CAPUT III. Comminatorium adversus Israelitas generatim.

Propositis beneficiis divinis in eductione ex Ægypto & assumptione populi, nec non præ- nuntiatione judiciorum divinorum, vel ho- stium ipsorum in Asdod & Ægypto testimo- nio, convinci Israelitas de injustitia & spo- liis iniquis, docet Propheta, adeoque mina- tur iisdem obsessionem, depressionem & do- mum spoliationem eorumque parvulis iis- que infirmioribus ereptis consumtionem. Cum punire Deus vult, excitat ante Prophetas.

Vers. 1.

SUPER OMNEM COGNATIONEM, QUAM EDUXI DE TERRA ÆGYPTI) Communiter jam allo- quitur & duas & decem tribus.

## 3:2
Verse 2. YOU ONLY HAVE I KNOWN) I had acknowledged them as my own. Exod. 19, 5. Deut. 4, 20.

THEREFORE I WILL VISIT UPON YOU ALL YOUR INIQUITIES) He deserves a heavier punishment who adds an ungrateful spirit to his other crimes.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TANTUMMODO VOS COGNOVI) Pro meis agnoveram. Exod. 19, 5. Deut. 4, 20.

IDCIRCO VISITABO SVPER VOS OMNES INIQVITATES VESTRAS) Graviorem pœnam mere- tur, qui ad cætera facinora ingratum addit animum.

## 3:3
Verse 3. CAN TWO WALK TOGETHER, EXCEPT THEY BE AGREED?) They cannot be σύν τε δύ' ἐρχομένω, unless they are in harmony. Your ways do not agree with mine. Therefore our society cannot endure.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NUMQVID AMBULABUNT DUO PARI- TER, NISI CONVENERIT EIS) Non possunt esse σύν τε δύ' ἐρχομένω, nisi concordes sint. Vestri mores cum meis non congruunt. Ideo non potest durare nostra societas.

## 3:4
Verse 4. WILL A LION ROAR IN THE FOREST, WHEN HE HATH NO PREY?) Does prey not come to him by force? Thus my threats will not be in vain.

WILL THE LION'S WHELP GIVE?) A young lion.

UNLESS IT HAS APPREHENDED SOMETHING) So that it may not apprehend something.

Latin:

Vers. 4. NUNQVID RUGIET LEO IN SALTU, NISI HABUERIT PRÆDAM?) Vi non obveniat ei præda? sic minæ meæ non frustra erunt.

NVMQVID DABIT CATVLVS LEONIS?) Leo juvenis.

NISI ALIVD APPREHENDERIT) Ut non ali- quid apprehendat.

## 3:5
Ver. 5. WILL A BIRD FALL INTO A SNARE OF THE EARTH WITHOUT A FOWLER?) The snare is the Assyrian and Chaldean, the fowler is God.

SHALL THE SNARE BE TAKEN AWAY FROM THE EARTH BEFORE IT HAS CAUGHT SOMETHING?) Thus neither shall the enemies depart, unless the matters are finished.

Latin:

Vers. 5. NVMQVID CADET AVIS IN LAQVEUM TERRÆ ABSQVE AVCVPE) Laqueus Assyrii & Chal- dæi, auceps Deus.

NVMQVID AVFERETVR LAQVEVS DE TER- RA ANTEQVAM QVID CEPERIT) Sic nec hostes abscedent, nisi rebus confectis.

## 3:6
Ver. 6. SHALL A TRUMPET SOUND IN THE CITY, AND THE PEOPLE NOT BE AFRAID?) Shall a trumpet sound? Namely from the watchtower established for this. But I cry out, and for so long there is no one who is moved. These things will not pass away thus.

SHALL THERE BE EVIL IN A CITY, WHICH THE LORD HAS NOT DONE?) Shall there be? As if he were to say, by no means. ἐκ ἀθεεὶ ταῦθ’ ὑμῖν ἐπιγίνεται.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SI CLANGET TUBA IN CIVITATE, ET POPVLVS NON EXPAVESCET?) An clanget tuba? nempe de specula in hoc constituta. At ego clamo, & tam- diu nemo est, qui commoveatur. Hæc non sic abibunt.

SI ERIT MALUM IN CIVITATE, QVOD DOMINVS NON FECERIT) An erit? quasi dicat mini- me. ἐκ ἀθεεὶ ταῦθ’ ὑμῖν ἐπιγίνεται.

## 3:7
Ver. 7. FOR THE LORD GOD DOES NOT DO A WORD, UNLESS HE HAS REVEALED HIS SECRET TO HIS SERVANTS THE PROPHETS) But he who does not do, etc. that is, you cannot plead that you were not forewarned.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVIA NON FACIT DOMINVS DEVS VERBVM, NISI REVELAVERIT SECRETVM SVVM AD SERVOS SVOS PROPHETAS) At qui non facit, &c. id est, causari non potestis vos non præmonitos.

## 3:8
Ver. 8.

THE LORD GOD HAS SPOKEN) Where God speaks, that is, commands.

WHO SHALL NOT PROPHESY?) Who would dare to decline the command? 1 Cor. 9:16. For if the wrath of a lion is to be feared, how much more that of God?

Latin:

Vers. 8.

DOMINUS DEVS LOCVTVS EST) Ubi Deus loquitur, id est, imperat.

QVIS NON PROPHETABIT?) Quis audeat de- trectare imperium? 1. Cor. 9, 16. nam si leonis ira timen- da est, quanto magis Dei?

## 3:9
Ver. 9. MAKE IT HEARD IN THE HOUSES OF AZOTUS) You prophets, summon the Philistines, from whose hands I have so often snatched this people.

AND IN THE HOUSES OF THE LAND OF EGYPT) Summon also the Egyptians, from whose land I led them away, having vindicated them into liberty.

AND SEE THE MANY MADNESSES IN THE MIDST OF IT) See how they ascribe to idols what they owe to me.

AND SUFFERING CALUMNY IN ITS INNER CHAMBERS) The prophets themselves oppressed by force within Samaria itself. For this is what בְּקִרְבָּהּ means.

Latin:

Vers. 9. AVDITVM FACITE IN ÆDIBVS AZO- TI) Vos Prophetæ convocate Philistiños, quorum mani- bus toties hunc populum eripui.

ET IN ÆDIBVS TERRÆ ÆGYPTI) Convo- cate & Ægyptios, à quorum terra eos in libertatem vin- dicatos abduxi.

ET VIDETE INSANIAS MVLTAS IN ME- DIO EJVS) Videte quomodo quod mihi debent adscri- bant idolis.

ET CALVMNIAM PATIENTES IN PENE- TRALIBVS EJVS) Prophetas ipsos vi oppressos intra ipsam Samariam. Hoc enim est, בְּקִרְבָּהּ.

## 3:10
Verse 10.

AND THEY KNEW NOT HOW TO DO RIGHT) They did not care. For thus יָדַע is often taken.

TREASURING UP INIQUITY AND RAPINE) metonymy, that is, wealth acquired through force and injury.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET NESCIERVNT FACERE RECTVM) Non curarunt. Sic enim יָדַע sæpe sumitur.

THESAVRIZANTES INIQVITATEM ET RAPI- NAS) μετωνυμία, id est, opes per vim & injuriam partas.

## 3:11
Verse 11.

THE LAND SHALL BE TROUBLED AND CIRCLED, AND THY STRENGTH SHALL BE DRAWN FROM THEE) You may translate it conveniently: The enemy shall come around your land, and shall cast down your strength from you: the Assyrian [against] the land of Israel, the Chaldean [against] Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

TRIBVLABITVR ET CIRCViETVR TERRA, ET DETRAHETVR EX TE FORTITVDO TVA) Vertas commode: Hostis circum terram tuam veniet, & dejiciet abs te robur tuum: Assyrius terram Israelis, Chal- dæus Judæam.

## 3:12
Verse 12.

AS IF A SHEPHERD SHOULD SNATCH FROM THE MOUTH OF A LION TWO LEGS, OR THE EXTREMITY OF AN EAR) Just as it is impossible for anyone to dare to carve out prey from the mouth of a hungry lion.

SO SHALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL BE SNATCHED, WHO DWELL IN SAMARIA) It will be no more possible for the Israelites to escape hostile hands.

IN THE CORNER OF A BED AND ON THE COUCH OF DAMASCUS) Interpreters vary here, and refer the last word to the following clause, from which Jerome thinks the Hebrew was retained, and written ἀρὶς, but changed by scribes into ἱερεῖς: but it appears the Chaldean read not ערשׂ, but עֶשֶׂר, in a good sense: who (the people, that is) in the extremity of the rod (that is, in the breadth of their borders) and in Damascus strengthens himself: that is, thinks himself robust. The Israelites had relied both on the magnitude of their empire and the victory of the Damascenes allied to them. See 2 Kings 16:5. God shows that these things will be of no profit.

It is strange that he prefers to learn the true sense of the phrase of the Holy Spirit from the Chaldean rather than from the Hebrew text, which alone is authentic. Whatever he may have read, whose errors are frequent enough, it should not be of such value to us that we should therefore abandon the fountains of Hebrew truth. Nor does this translation, or explanation, of Grotius fit in any way. For the matter is not about the stubborn prevaricating Israelites, relying on the magnitude of their empire and the victory of the Damascenes allied to them, but about those whom the Lord deigned to snatch from the hostile hand: which promise was certainly not made to the wicked. Nor is it a threat, as if the Prophet were teaching that the power of the Israelites or their allies would be of no profit, but a promise of grace concerning the snatching of certain children of Israel. Nor does anything about Damascus seem to be found here in the Holy text. The proper name דמשק does not occur here, which is read in ch. 1, 3, but the appellative noun דמשק of four letters, as Kimchi observes in this place and in the Book of Roots, as well as Pagninus in the Greater Lexicon: whence Pagninus, and Arias Montanus, rendered it in the corner of a bed, or couch. Junius and Tremellius, and in the leg of a bedstead, to whom Piscator and the Belgian Paraphrasts accede, but these also understand it of those living delicately. B. Tarnovius more correctly [speaks] to the connection of the text: Thus the Israelites shall be snatched away, those most of all infirm and abandoned, just as the most contemptible parts are preserved from a little sheep; not the vigorous, and those fighting against the enemy, not the valiant and robust, but those who sit idle in Samaria in the side of a bed, nay, in the leg or corner of a bedstead, for whom there is no whole bed: by hiding, I say, a few shall escape, and those indeed who are already thought to have perished. He recounts other, but incongruous, expositions there. Coccejus also accepted it as an appellative noun: I do not doubt, with Aben-Ezra and Kimchi, that by דמשק he understands not indeed the same thing as פאה, but nevertheless something analogous, which Amos indicated by a word of his own century, now indeed dead, but nevertheless intelligible from the analogy of the place.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QVOMODO SI ERVAT PASTOR DE ORE LEONIS DVO CRVRA, AVT EXTREMVM AV- RICVLÆ) Sicut fieri non potest, ut quis audeat. Efuriente leone ex ore exsculpere prædam.

SIC ERVENTVR FILII ISRAEL, QVI HABI- TANT IN SAMARIA) Nihilo magis fiet, ut Israelitæ hostiles manus evadant.

IN PLAGA LECTVLI ET IN DAMASCI GRA- BATO) Variant hic Interpretes, & extremam vocem LXX. referunt ad sequens comma, à quibus retentum putat Hieronymus Hebræum, scriptumque ἀρὶς, sed à librariis mutatum in ἱερεῖς: at Chaldæum apparet legisse non ערשׂ, fed עֶשֶׂר, sensu bono: qui (populus scilicet) in extremitate virgæ (id est, in latitudine finium suorum) & in Damasco se roborat: id est robustum putat. Israelitæ freti erant & magnitudine imperii sui, & victoria Damascenorum sibi fœderatorum. Vide 2. Reg. 16,5. hæc nihil profutura often- dit Deus.

Mirum, quod à Chaldæo verum sensum Phraseos Spiritus S. discere malit potius, quam ab Ebræo tex- tu, qui solus authenticus est. Quicquid ille legerit, cuj9 παραπτώματα satis frequentia sunt, tanti no- bis esse non debet, ut ideo fontes Ebraicæ veritatis relinquamus. Neque congruit ullatenus ista Grotii seu translatio, seu explicatio. Non enim de Israeli- tis prævaricatoribus pervicacibus, magnitudine imperii, & victoria Damascenorum sibi fæderato- rum fretis res est, sed de illis, quos Dominus eruere dignabatur è manu hostili: quæ promissio certe non facta est improbis. Neque comminatio est, quasi in eo Propheta, ut nihil profuturam potentiam Israelitarum, aut fœderatorum doceat, sed pollicita- tio gratiæ de eruendis quibusdam filiis Israel. Nec de Damasco hic quicquam videtur in textu S. repe- riri. Non a. occurrit hic nomen proprium דמשק, quod c. 1, 3. legitur, sed appellativum דמשק nomen quatuor literarum, ut observat Kimchius h. l. & in libr. Radicum, nec non Pagninus in Lexic. Majori: unde reddidit Pagninus, & Arias Montanus, in angu- lo strati, vel grabati. Junius & Tremellius, & in crure spondæ, quibus accedunt Piscator & Paraphrasta Bel- gici, sed hi etiam de delicate viventibus intelligunt. Rectius B. Tarnovius ad textus συνέχειαν: Ita eri- pientur Israelitæ, omnium maxime infirmi & dere- licti, sicut conservata ex ovicula sunt partes omnium contemptissimæ, non eripientur strenui, & pugnantes contra hostem, non valentes ac robusti, sed qui desident Samariæ in latere lecti, imo in crure seu angulo spondæ, quibus non est lectus integer: latendo, inquam, evadent pauci, & illi quidem, qui jam periisse pu- tantur. Qui alias, sed incongruas expositiones ibi recenset. Coccejus etiam accepit, ut nomen appel- lativum: Non dubito, cum Aben-Esra & Kimchio, per דמשק non quidem idem, quod est פאה, sed tamen aliquid analogum intelligere, quod Amosus sui seculi vocabulo nunc quidem intermortuo, sed tamen ex a- nalogia loci intelligibili indicavit.

## 3:14
Verse 14.

IN THE DAY WHEN I SHALL BEGIN TO VISIT THE TRANSGRESSIONS OF ISRAEL UPON HIM) At which time I shall begin to punish the sins of Israel against himself. A small distinction must be placed here. I WILL VISIT ALSO UPON THE ALTARS OF BETHEL) I will not spare even the temples.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

IN DIE CUM VISITARE COEPERO PRÆVA- RICATJONES ISRAEL SUPER EUM VISITABO) Quo tempore punire cœpero peccata Israelis adversus ipsum. Hic ponenda distinctiuncula. VISITABO ET SUPER ALTARIA BETHEL) Ne templis quidem parcam.

## 3:15
Verse 15. THE WINTER HOUSE WITH THE SUMMER HOUSE) Kings and other powerful men had houses for different positions of the sky, some in which they would spend the summer, others in which they would spend the winter.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DOMUM HYEMALEM CUM DOMO ÆSTIVA) Reges & potentes alii ad diversos cœli positus habebant domos, alias in quibus æstatem, alias in quibus hyemen exigerent.

## 4:1 Argument
SERMON III. Likewise against the Israelites. CHAPTER IV. A comminatory [sermon] against the nobles in particular.

He threatens with casting out, and famine, and denied rain, drought and the palmerworm, likewise pestilence and the sword and overthrow, to the nobles oppressing the poor and indulging in drinking bouts, and trusting in vain in their idolatrous sacrifices, and he counsels them to meet their God with true conversion. Let the people learn to repent through various plagues.

Verse 1.

FAT KINE) The kine of Bashan, that is, as if from Bashanitis, where the kine are most fat, to which he compares opulent matrons. The following participles show this, and that אשת. 3. Whence it follows that כם is written twice in the following, for כן. That however אחריתכן is written according to the received expression. Thus also opulent men are compared to the heifers of Bashan. Psalm 22, 13.

WHICH SAY TO YOUR MASTERS) That is, husbands. Gen. 18, 12. Thus for the Attics the husband is ὁ κύριος.

Grotius is too headlong and rash in correcting the authentic sacred text. It should rather have been examined more accurately whom the Prophet is addressing. Jerome wishes these things to concern the Princes in Israel. But Grotius preferred to follow the Hebrews, and Vatablus, without an exquisite investigation of the matter, who wish the noble women of that nation to be noted. The sense is, as B. Tarnovius observes: You are indeed the leaders of the kingdom in the royal citadel of Samaria, but you only care for your own skin, while all parts of your duty are neglected in the meantime. And therefore, and in truth, you are to kine, which graze on the most fertile mount Bashan, so that they may be fattened, like: you are also deservedly to be called so. If he had adhered to the Hebrew text, no difficulty, nor any reason for amending the text, could have arisen. For the Prophet addresses the leaders of the kingdom, using now the masculine gender, now the feminine; this on account of the metaphor and likeness which he had taken from cows, the former having regard to the persons to whom he directed his speech. Moreover, the leaders of the kingdom are compared to fat cows because of their luxury (Isa. 5:11), because they devoured the marrow of the land; and their wantonness, which is wont to be the companion of luxury in fat cows; as also their softness and effeminate manners, whence they are compared not to oxen, but to cows: and also because of their disobedience, because well-fed cows are refractory; it may perhaps also be said that an allusion is made to the idolatry of those who were worshippers of the calves in Dan and Bethel (1 Kings 12:48). The herdsman Amos had to lead these cows back into the right way.

Latin:

CONCIO III. Itidem adversus Israelitas. CAPUT IV. Comminatorium adversus proceres in specie.

Proceribus pauperes opprimentibus & compo- tationibus indulgentibus, ac nequicquam sa- crificiis suis idololatricis confidentibus pro- jectionem, & famem, pluviaque negata, sic- citatem & erucam, pestem item & gladium atque eversionem minatur, ac ut Deo suo vera conversione occurrant, consulit. Par varias populus discat resipiscere plagas.

Vers. 1.

VACCÆ PINGUES) Vaccæ Basan, id est, quasi ex Basanitide, ubi pinguissimæ boves, quibus comparat ma- tronas opulentas. Ostendunt id participia sequentia, & il- lud אשת. 3. Unde sequitur bis in sequentibus כם scri- ptum, per כן. Illud autem אחריתכן secundum receptam locutionem scriptum. Sic & juvencis Basanis comparan- tur homines opulenti. Psal. 22, 13.

QVÆ DICITIS DOMINIS VESTRI) Id est, ma- ritis. Gen. 18, 12. Sic Atticis maritus ὁ κύρις.

NImis præceps & temerarius est Grotius in corrigendo textu sacro authentico. Dispi- ciendum potius erat accuratius, quosnam allo- quatur Propheta. Hieronymus Principes in Israel hæc concernere vult. Sed maluit Grotius Ebræos, & Vatablum sequi, sine exquisita rei indagine, qui mulieres nobiles ejus gentis notari volunt. Sensus est, observante B. Tarnovio: Vos regni primores estis quidem in arce regia Samariæ, sed tantum cu- ratis cuticulam, neglectis interim omnibus officii vestri partibus. Ideoque & revera vaccis, quæ in monte fertilissimo Basan pascuntur, ut pinguefiant, estis similes: merito etiam ita vocandi estis. Si Hebræo textui inhæsiffet, nulla difficultas, nec ratio textum emendandi suboriri potuisset. Nam alloquitur Propheta regni primores modo masculo utens ge- nere, modo fœminino, hoc ob metaphoram & simi- litudinem, quam à vaccis desumpserat, illo habita personarum ratione, adquas sermonem direxit. Comparantur autem primores regni vaccis pingui- bus ob luxuriam Esa. 5, 11. quia vorabant medullam terræ; & lasciviam, quæ luxuriæ in pinguibus vac- cis solet esse comes; ut & mollitiem, moresque effœ- minatos, unde non bobus, sed vaccis componun- tur: nec non ob inobedientiam, quia vaccæ bene pastæ refractariæ sunt; dici etiam forsan potest, al- lusionem fieri ad idololatriam eorum, qui vitulo- rum in Dan & Bethel cultores erant, 1. Reg. 12, 48. Has vaccas armentarius Amos in rectam viam re- ducere debebat.

## 4:2
Verse 2.

THEY SHALL TAKE YOU AWAY WITH HOOKS) They shall carry you away as if with hunting spears, just as wounded wild beasts are wont to be carried away. AND YOUR REMAINDERS) The rest of yours. IN BOILING POTS) As if with fishermen's hooks. סִירוֹת are thorns, and whatever is like thorns, such as fishermen's hooks. A similar expression is in 2 Kings 19:28.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

LEVABVNT VOS IN CONTIS) Auferent vos quasi venabulis, sicut vulneratæ feræ auferri solent. ET RELIQVIAS VESTRAS) Reliquos vestro- rum. IN OLLIS FERVENTIBVS) Quasi hamis Pi- scatorum. סִירוֹת spinæ, & quicquid spinis simile, ut hami piscatorum. Similis locutio 2. Reg. 19, 28.

## 4:3
Verse 3.

AND THROUGH THE BREACHES) Not through the gates, but through the ruins of the walls. YOU SHALL GO FORTH ONE AGAINST ANOTHER) One far from another: each one separately. AND YOU SHALL BE CAST INTO ARMON) Into Armenia. Thus the Hebrews take it. The old name is אֲרָרָט, the later name הַרְמֹן, that is, the Mountain of Minyas, whence also the Greek Ἀρμενία: elsewhere in Chaldean books it is written with ח, as Jer. 51:27, Mic. 7:12. That interpretation does not suit the Hebrew text: the Chaldean indeed renders it 'beyond the mountains of Armenia.' For he took the one word ההרמונה for two, as did Theodotion, rendering it 'into the mountain of Moria,' as if it were written הַהַר מוֹנָה; Symmachus explained it as Ἀρμενίαν. But the Hebrew word, if you cast away the local He, which the accent indicates, with the demonstrative He, הָרִמּוֹן denotes a palace, as Pagninus, Junius, Piscator, Tarnovius, Lud. de Dieu, Coccejus rightly [say], and the word וְהִשְׁלַכְתְּנָה is not 'you shall be cast,' but 'you shall cast,' concerning which see Buxtorf in Thesaurus, p. 174. The sense, therefore, overflows from the words themselves, and you shall cast [yourselves] into the palace itself. Therefore, Armenia has no place here, nor any other proper name, Rimnon, or Amamus. But it is rightly rendered by Pagninus, whom Dievius also praises, when he translates: And you shall cast yourselves into the palace. In Greek, he says, you would translate word for word, κὶ ἐπιβαλεῖτε πρὸς τὰς βασιλικὰς. Just as in Mark 14:72, concerning Peter rushing out of the high priest's hall, it is said, κὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιε: nor is ἐπιβάλλειν taken otherwise in 1 Macc. 4:2, 2 Macc. 12:9, 13, and 13:15, and 15:1; nor do I doubt that the Hellenists took this from the Hebrew הִשְׁלִיךְ, which is used here intransitively for ὁρμᾷν, to rush, which is to cast oneself with force toward some place. So he. The commentary of Tarnovius agrees, as does that of Coccejus: You shall cast yourselves, or your dear things and children: and Abarbenel, You shall cast yourselves into the citadel.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET PER APERTVRAS) Non per portas, sed per ruinas mœnium. EXIBITIS ALTERA CONTRA ALTERAM) Altera longe ab altera: seorsum singulæ. ET PROJICIEMINI ARMON) In Armeniam. Sic sumunt Hebræi. Vetus nomen est אֲרָרָט, posterius no- men הַרְמֹן, id est, Mons Minyadis, unde & Græcum Ἀρ- μενία: alibi in Chaldaicis libris per ח scribitur, ut Jerem. 51, 27, Mich. 7, 12. Non convenit ill interpretatio textui Ebræo: Chaldæus quidem reddit ultra montes Armeniæ. Ha- buit enim vocem unam ההרמונה pro duabus, ut & Theodotio, reddens in montem Moria, quasi sic i- ptum esse הַהַר מוֹנָה, Symmachus exposuit Ἀρμε- νίαν. Sed vox Ebræa, si He locale, quod accentus in- dicat, abjicias, cum He demonstrativo, הָרִמּוֹן notat palatium, ut recte Pagninus, Junius, Piscator, Tarno- vius, Lud. de Dieu, Coccejus, & verbum וְהִשְׁלַכְתְּנָה non est projiciemini, sed abjicietis, de quo vid. Bux- torff. in Thesaur. p. 174. Sensus ergo hic è verbis ipsis redundat, & projicietis in ipsum palatium. Non igitur Armenia hic locum habet, aut aliud nomen proprium, Rimnon, aut Amamus. Recte autem redditur à Pagnino, quem etiam Dievius laudat, cum vertit: Et conjicietis vos in palatium. Græce, in- quit, ad verbum vertas, κὶ ἐπιβαλεῖτε πρὸς τὰς βα- σιλικὰς. Sicut Marc. 14, 72. de Petro proripiente se ex aula Pontificis dicitur, κὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιε: neque aliter ἐπιβάλλειν accipitur 1. Macc. 4, 2. 2. Macc. 12. v. 9. 13. & 13, 15. & 15, 1. nec dubito, quin id Hellenistæ ex Hebræo הִשְׁלִיךְ desumpserint, quod intransitive hic usurpatur pro ὁρμᾷν, ruere, quod est, cum impetu conjicere se versus locum aliquem. Hæc ille. Con- sonat commentarius Tarnovii, nec non Cocceji: Projicietis vos, vel res caras, ac liberos: & Abarbene- lis, Conjicietis vos in arcem.

## 4:4
Verse 4.

COME TO BETHEL, AND DEAL IMPIOUSLY AT GILGAL.) If one must distinguish: act thus, when it pleases you so; the time will come when you will pay dearly for these things. Bethel and Gilgal, places famous for idolatrous rites, Hos. 4:15, 12:12. BRING IN THE MORNING YOUR VICTIMS) For they were nevertheless imitating the custom of the Jerusalem temple in that illicit worship. Exod. 29:38, Num. 28:4. EVERY THREE DAYS YOUR TITHES) יָמִים is sometimes placed in the plural idiomatically for שָׁנָה יָמִים, a year of days, that is, a full year. See Lev. 25:29. Thus you will rightly interpret it here, on the third year of days. The law is Deut. 14:28.

Others [say] on three days (annual festivals) about which Exod. 23:14, Lev. 23, Deut. 16, since they were not to appear empty-handed at those times. Coccejus wishes there to be a hyperbole: Tithe your produce every three days, comparing that to 1 Cor. 13:3, as if to say, Amos: If you tithe your produce every three days, until very little remains for you, and you lack faith in God, which works charity, it is nothing. Others wish this to be indicated: That only as much of the tithes or gifts is offered to the idol-priests every three days as is hardly offered to the priests of the true God in three years. Osiander, whom the Weimar theologians followed, translated it thus: Go to Gilgal to that place where idolatrous worship flourishes, and multiply transgression, fill up the measure of your impiety: and there on the first day, on which you came, rest: but on the next day offer your victims in the morning: not those which God commanded to be offered in Jerusalem, but those which you yourselves and your priests have impiously devised, and for three days: in Hebrew; on the third day (offer there) your tithes, by which you may preserve and promote that divine worship: so that every day you may have some splendid exercise of Religion. The word ימים indeed occurs for a year in Lev. 25:29, but שׁלשׁת ימים for שׁנים שלשׁ will not easily be found, and the tithes which are commanded for one year (which they call from Deut. 26:12) in Deut. 14:28, namely that every third year the tithes should be deposited at home to be given to the Levites, widows, and the poor, are foreign to this. For Amos is dealing with the bringing of tithes, which is done to a sacred place. Cf. Neh. 10:38, 2 Chron. 31:3. How then can the tithes of the third year, which were not brought, but were dispensed and distributed at home, be understood? Why is the proper sense of the word not retained, since it is the most convenient? You offer your tithes at those three annual festivals, which I had ordained for the sustenance of the Levites, not in Jerusalem, but in Gilgal, and thus you defraud my ministers of the very tithes destined for them. Num. 18:21, 24, Mal. 3:10.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

VENITE AD BETHEL, ET IMPIE AGITE AD GALGALAM.) Si distinguendum est: ita agite, quan- do ita vobis libet; veniet tempus cum magno ista luetis. Be- thel & Galgala, loca sacris idololatricis celebria, Osee 4, 15. 12, 12. AFFERTE MANE VICTIMAS) Nam morem templi Hierosolymitani in illo cultu illicito tamen imita- bantur. Exod. 29, 38. Num. 28, 4. TRIBVS DIEBVS DECIMAS VESTRAS( יָמִים pluraliter nonnunquam ponitur ἰδιωτικῶς, pro שָׁנָה יָמִים anno dierum, id est, pleno. Vide Lev. 25, 29. Ita hic recte interpretaberis, tertio anno dierum. Lex est Deut. 14. v. 28.

Alii tribus diebus (festis anniversariis) de quibus Exod. 23, 14. Lev. 23. Deut. 16. siquidem illis va- cui non debebant comparere. Coccejus vult hyperbolen esse: Decimate proventus vestros singulis triduis, conferens illud 1. Cor. 13, 3. q. d. Amos: Si in tridua singula decimaveritis proventus vestros, do- nec perparum vobis supersit, & fide in Deum careatis, quæ operatur caritatem, nihil est. Alii hoc indica- ri volunt: Singulis tribus diebus tantum decimarum, vel munerum offerri sacrificulis idolorum, quantum vix per triennium veri Dei sacerdotibus offertur. O- siander, quem Vinarienses sequuti sunt, ita reddidit: Ite ad Galgala in eum locum, ubi idololatricus cultus viget, & multiplicate prævaricationem, complete mensuram impietatis vestræ: & ibi primo quidem die, quo venistis, quiescite: postero vero die offerte ma- ne victimas vestras: non illas, quas Deus Jerosolymis offerri præcepit, sed eas, quas vos ipsi & vestri sacerdo- tes impie excogitastis, & tribus diebus: Hebraice; tertio die (offerte ibi) decimas vestras, quibus cultum illum divinum conservetis & promoveatis: ut sin- gulis diebus aliquod splendidum Religionis exerci- tium habeatis. Occurrit quidem vox ימים pro anno Lev. 25, 29. sed שׁלשׁת ימים pro שׁנים שלשׁ non facilè reperietur, & quæ uno anno decimæ (quem vo- cant è Deut. 26, 12.) Deut. 14, 28. præcipiuntur, ut nempe tertio quoque anno decimæ deponantur do- mi dandæ Levitis, viduabus, & pauperibus, hic alie- na sunt. Agit enim Amos de decimarum allatione, quæ fit ad locum sacrum. Conf. Neh. 10, 18. 2. Chro- nic. 31, 3. Quomodo ergo decimæ tertii anni, quæ non afferebantur, sed domi dispensabantur & di- stribuebantur, intelligi possunt? Cur non sensus vocis proprius retinetur, quum commodissimus sit? Vos istis tribus festis anniversariis offertis deci- mas vestras, quas ad Levitarum ordinaveram susten- tationem, non Hierosolymis, sed in Gilgal, adeoque fraudatis ministros meos decimis ipsis destinatis. Num. 18. v. 21. 24. Mal. 3, 10.

## 4:5
Verse 5.

AND SACRIFICE FROM LEAVENED BREAD תודה, the law of which you have in Leviticus 7:12, 13, where you will learn that in this sacrifice leaven is not rejected. The LXX wrongly read תורה. The Chaldean, however, interprets חמס as rapine. AND PROCLAIM VOLUNTARY OFFERINGS AND ANNOUNCE) Call an assembly, and there with the sound of trumpets make known your voluntary offerings. The Chaldean says with a song, meaning the same thing as is said in Matthew 7:2. Concerning נדבת, that is, a voluntary offering, see Exodus 35, Leviticus 32:18, 21. FOR SO YOU HAVE WILLED) For so it pleases you.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET SACRIFICATE DE FERMENTATO LAV- DEM) תודה, cujus legem habes Levit. 7, 12. 13. ubi di- sces in hoc sacro fermentum non respui. LXX. male lege- runt תורה. Chaldæus autem חמס interpretatur rapinam. ET VOCATE VOLVNTATIS OBLATIONES ET ANNVNCIATE) Vocate cœtum, & ibi tubarum sonitu notas facite voluntarias oblationes vestras. Cum cantico ait Chaldæus, idem significans, quod dicitur Matth. 7, 2. De נדבת id est, voluntaria oblatione, vide Exod. 35. Levit. 32, 18. 21. SIC ENIM VOLVISTIS) Sic enim vobis libet.

## 4:6
Verse 6.

WHENCE I ALSO GAVE TO YOU) I, whose you indeed forget. STUPOR OF TEETH) In the Hebrew: cleanness of teeth. Symmachus and Aquila: καθαρισμόν. It is a witticism, signifying a scarcity of meat: that famine is indicated, of which mention is made in 2 Kings 9.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

VNDE ET EGO DEDI VOBIS) Ego, cujus nempe vos obliviscimini. STVPOREM DENTIVM) In Hebræo: mundi- tiem dentium. Symmachus & Aquila καθαρισμόν. Est χαριεν- τισμὸς, carnium penuriam significans: indicatur fames illa, cujus mentio 2. Reg. 9.

## 4:7
Verse 7.

I WITHHELD RAIN FROM YOU) I sent a drought, narrated in 1 Kings 18. WHEN THREE MONTHS STILL REMAINED UNTIL THE HARVEST) Even then when three months remained until the harvest: that is, even in the season of the year from which rains are not accustomed to be absent, around the end of April. AND I RAINED UPON ONE CITY AND UPON ANOTHER CITY I DID NOT RAIN) That drought sent upon you was the more wonderful, because in the cities that were near yours, rain was not lacking. ONE PART WAS RAINED UPON) Of the land. AND THE PART UPON WHICH I DID NOT RAIN WITHERED) The part of the Israelite land near other regions was corrupted by aridity.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

PROHIBVI A VOBIS IMBREM) ἀνομβρίαν im- misi narratam 1. Reg. 18. CVM ADHVC TRES MENSES SVPERESSENT AD MESSEM) Tunc quoque cum tres menses superessent ad messem: id est, etiam anni tempestate, à qua abesse pluviæ non solent, circa finem Aprilis. ET PLVI SVPER VNAM AIVITATEM ET SVPER ALTERAM CIVITATEM NON PLVI) Eo mirabilior fuit ista ἀνομβρία vobis immissa, quod in urbibus quæ proximæ erant vestris, pluvia non deerat. PARS VNA COMPLVTA EST) Terræ. ET PARS SVPER QVAM NON PLVI ARV- IT) Pars terræ Israëliticæ vicina aliis regionibus, ariditate fuit corrupta.

## 4:8
Verse 8.

AND TWO AND THREE CITIES CAME) Men from the Israelite cities. TO ONE CITY) Of the Ammonites, for instance, or the Moabites.

AND THEY WERE NOT SATIATED) They could not be satiated because of the long thirst. Lucan: --- nor the burning plague. It yields still: but the needy disease now, with bowels full of the flood, demands waters for itself. Verse 9. I SMOTE YOU WITH A SCORCHING WIND) שדף, Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion translate it as wind-blasting in this place. So also the LXX. Deut. 28, 22. 2 Chron. 6, 28. It signifies corrupted air. AND WITH MILDEW) Which is ἴκτερος to the Greeks here and in 2 Chron. 6, 28. Jer. 30, 6. but ὤχρα in Deut. 28, 12. THE PALMERWORM ATE) A kind of worm devouring everything: from which Joel took his simile. Verse 10. I SENT AMONG YOU DEATH) Pestilence, which is called death by way of excellence. See what is said on Matt. 24, 7. IN THE WAY OF EGYPT) After the manner of Egypt, that is, after the manner of that plague which I once sent upon Egypt, Exod. 9. Grotius rightly rendered that כדרך as after the manner. So also Tremellius, Junius, the French version, Castalio, Edward, and Luvellæus. See a similar use of this word in Isa. 10, 24. 26. R. Solomon understood the pestilence as having been sent not to the Egyptians, but to the Israelites on the way out of Egypt, in the desert. R. David Kimchi understood it as the journey into Egypt at the time of the famine. Others understood it as some other journey into Egypt, such as Mercerus, Deodatus, and Drusius. Therefore, Capellus has no cause to amend the sacred text here, which Buxtorf corrected in Vindic. p. 974. Grotius did not wish to follow his Capellus here. This is the fourth punishment sent to the idolaters to correct and amend them. Namely, after the famine, because they had not provided for the temple of the Lord regarding sacrifice and tithes and had caused the Levites to go hungry, and thirst brought on by drought, because they themselves were waterless springs 2. Petr. 2, 17. and also the blight sent divinely because of crops consumed through luxury; now the Lord threatens the idolaters with a pestilence twin to the Egyptian, just as in the following words He threatened war and captivity: I killed your chosen ones or young men with the sword, even to the captivity of your horses, that is, I afflicted you with war and captivity. They were accustomed in olden times to hamstring captive horses, by cutting their feet from the hocks downward so that they could no longer be of use to the enemy, Josh. 11, 6. 1 Chron. 18, 4. I made the stench of your camps rise (the Greeks add: those censured by the Lord) even into your nostrils, cf. Isa. 34, 3. Joel 2, 20. Which was the fifth punishment. The sixth is found in v. 11. I overthrew you according to the overthrow of GOD, of Sodom and Gomorrah. Because they labored like Sodom, therefore they also reaped the same. Jer. 14, 13. Eph. 7, 9. Not that it is the same overthrow entirely, but that a similar punishment and a notable devastation befell them: by the species, a genus of extreme desolation is noted. Isa. 1, 9. ch. 13, 9. Thence the Prophet warns in v. 11. to prepare to meet thy God, O Israel: where the word הכון is rightly rendered passively by the Vulgate, to be prepared, namely, through the effective operation of the Holy Spirit; because this preparation is through the word, to which the grace of the Holy Spirit is present, and not indeed through the powers of free will; which the Papists therefore rashly seek here. I SMOTE WITH THE SWORD YOUR YOUNG MEN, EVEN TO THE CAPTIVITY OF YOUR HORSES, AND I MADE THE PUTREFACTION OF YOUR CAMPS RISE INTO YOUR NOSTRILS) See 2 Kings 5, 2. 13, 3. Verse 11. I OVERTHREW YOU AS GOD OVERTHREW SODOM AND GOMORRAH) In the Hebrew: I overthrew among you: that is, some parts of your region. See the already cited place 2 Kings, with 14, 26 added. AND YOU BECAME AS A BRAND FROM THE BURNING) The rest were barely saved from the hand of the Syrians. A proverbial expression, Zech. 3, 2. so also the Greeks say to be saved from a flame or from a fire. Verse 12. THEREFORE THUS WILL I DO TO THEE O ISRAEL) These things which I said above 2, 6. 13. 14. 15. 16. ch. 3, 11. 12. 15. here 3. 4. BUT AFTER I SHALL HAVE DONE THESE THINGS TO THEE, PREPARE TO MEET THY GOD O ISRAEL) Or then at least in captivity appease God. Verse 13. FOR BEHOLD HE THAT FORMS THE MOUNTAINS) He with whom you have business is the maker of things, both of those which are seen and of those which escape sight. AND ANNOUNCING TO MAN HIS SPEECH) In the Hebrew: His counsel, namely through the Prophets. Above 3, 7. The LXX read מה שחו as משיחו, his Christ. Grotius here invents a various reading with his Capellus. But that which the LXX interpreters translated into his Christ can come from elsewhere than from a diversity of reading, whether because they were deceived by similarity and ambiguity, as Jerome thinks, or because they willingly drew these things, like others, to Christ. It is a mere conjecture and a vain divination to establish various readings of the Hebrew Code from discrepancies of this kind, as Buxtorf rightly answered Capellus here, p. 686. Aquila, certainly, Symmachus, and Theodotion did not read otherwise than the Hebrew Codes now have. Which reading the sequence of the text confirms: for after the Lord had threatened various punishments, for the sake of confirmation He added arguments from the works of God, partly ordinary and then of infinite power v. 13. for behold I am forming the mountains, and creating the winds: Cf. Ps. 104, 28. Job 28, 9. then of divine grace in the announcement of His speech (as the Clementine has it). (B. Gerhardus renders what is שחו, what is his work? likewise what is his meditation? what is the divine meditation concerning the human race, comparing Ps. 147, 19. 20. Mic. 6, 8. Am. 3, 7.) partly extraordinary: Making the morning mist, in Hebrew the dawn of darkness, that is, most obscure, namely by the miraculous induction of darkness, and walking upon the high places of the earth, in which the idolaters exercised their worship Lev. 26. 30. Num. 33, 52. that is, trampling down and turning away the idolaters in a miraculous way also: Cf. Deut. 33. v. 29. MAKING THE MORNING MIST) Making the dawn and darkness, that is, giving prosperous things to the pious, adverse things to the wicked, as the Chaldean has it here. AND WALKING UPON THE HIGH PLACES OF THE EARTH) that is, crushing the proud.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET VENERVNT DVÆ ET TRES CIVITA- TES) Homines ex urbibus Israëliticis. AD VNAM CIVITATEM) Ammonitidis puta, aut Moabitidis.

ET NON SVNT SATIATÆ) Satiari nequivere ob longam sitim. Lucanus: --- nec fervida pestis. Cedit adhuc: sed morbus egens jam gurgite plenis Visceribus sibi poscit aquas. Vers. 9. PERCVSSI VOS IN VENTO VRENTE) שדף, ἀνεμοφθορίαν vertunt hoc loco Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotio. Sic & LXX. Deut. 28, 22. 2. Paralip. 6, 28. significat aërem corruptum. ET IN AVRVGINE) Quæ ἴκτερος Græcis hic & 2. Paralip. 6, 28. Jerem. 30, 6. at Deut. 28, 12. ὤχρα. COMEDIT ERVCA) Vermis genus omnia de- pascens: unde similitudinem sumsit Joël. Vers. 10. MISI IN VOS MORTEM) Pestilentiam, quæ mors κατ' ἐξοχήν dicitur. Vide quæ ad Matth. 24. 7. IN VIA ÆGTPTI) Ad modum Ægypti, Id est, ad modum ejus pestis, quam Ægypto olim immisi Exod. 9. Recte illud כדרך reddidit Grotius ad modum. Ita etiam Tremellius, Junius, versio Gallica, Castalio, Edvardus, Luvellæus. Vide similem hujus vocis u- sum Esa. 10, 24. 26. De peste immissa non Ægyptiis, sed Israëlitis in via ex Ægypto, in deserto, R. Salo- mo accepit. R. David Kimchi de itinere in Ægy- ptum tempore famis. Alii de alio quodam in Ægy- ptum itinere, uti Mercerus, Deodatus, Drusius. Non ergo Capellus causam habet emendandi hic textum sacrum, quem castigavit Buxtorff. in Vin- dic. p. 974. Noluit Capellum suum hic sequi Gro- tius. Pœna hæc quarta est idololatris immissa ad corrigendos & emendandos eosdem. Nimirum post famem, quia templo Domini de sacrificio & de- cimis non prospexerant & Levitas famescere fece- rant, & sitim per siccitatem illatam, quia ipsi erant fontes ἄνυδροι 2. Petr. 2, 17. nec non uredinem ob fruges per luxum absumtas, divinitus immissam, nunc minatur Dominus ob idololatriam Ægyptiacæ geminam pestilentiam, uti seqq. verbis bellum & ca- ptivitatem minatus est: occidi in gladio electos sive juvenes vestros, usque ad captivitatem equorum ve- strorum, id est, bello captivitate vos afflixi. Sole- bant olim captivos equos νευροκοπεῖν subnervare, se- cando à poplitibus deorsum pedes ne hostibus am- plius usui esse possint Jos. 11, 6. 1. Par. 18, 4. Feci ut ascen- deret fætor castrorum vestrorum (Græci addunt fuc censorum à Domino) etiam in nares vestras, conf. Esa. 34, 3. Joel. 2, 20. Quæ quinta pœna fuit. Sexta habetur v. 11. subverti vos secundum subversionem DEI, Sodomæ & Gomorræ. Quia ut Sodoma la- borarunt, ideo etiam pariter vindemiarunt. Jer. 14, 13. Ef. 7, 9. Non quod eadem omnino subver- sio, sed quod similis pœna, & insignis devastatio iis obtigerit: per speciem notatur genus extremæ vasti- tas. Esa. 1, 9. c. 13, 9. Inde monet Propheta v. 11. præ- parare in occursum Dei tui Israel: ubi verbum הכון recte passive redditur à vulgato, præparare sc. per efficacem Spir. S. operationem; quia hæc præpa- ratio per verbum sit, cui gratia Spirit. S. præsto est, non vero per vires liberi arbitrii; quas proinde te- mere hic quærunt Papistæ. PERCVSSI IN GLADIO JVVENES VE- STROS, VSQVE AD CAPTIVITATEM EQVO- RVM VESTRORVM, ET ASSCENDERE FECI PV- TREDINEM CASTRORVM VESTRORVM IN NA- RES VESTRAS) Vide 2. Reg. 5, 2. 13, 3. Vers. 11. SVBVERTI VOS SICVT SVBVERTIT DEVS SODOMAM ET GOMORRAM) In Hebræo: Subverti in vobis: id est, partes aliquas regionis vestræ. Vide dicto jam loco 2. Reg. addito 14, 26. ET FACTI ESTIS QVASİ TORRIS AB IN- CENDIO) Cæteri ægre servati à manu Syrorum. Prover- bialis locutio Zach. 3, 2. sic & Græci dicunt σῳζεσθαι ἐκ φλογὸς aut ἐκ πυρός. Vers. 12. QVAPROPTER HÆC FACIAM TIBI ISRAEL) Hæc quæ dixi supra 2, 6. 13. 14. 15. 16. c. 3, 11. 12. 15. hic 3. 4. POSTQVAM AVTEM HÆC FECERO TIBI, PRÆPARARE IN OCCVRSVM DEI TVI ISRAEL) Vel tunc saltem in captivitate Deum placa. Vers. 13. QVIA ECCE FORMANS MONTES) Is quicum tibi negotium est rerum est opifex, tum earum quæ conspiciuntur, tum earum quæ conspectum effugiunt. ET ANNUNCIANS HOMINI ELOQVIUM SUUM) In Hebræo: Consilium suum, nempe per Pro- phetas. Supra 3, 7. LXX. מה שחו legerunt משיחו, τὸν χριστὸν ἀυτᾶ. Variam lectionem hic fingit cum Capello suo Grotius. At quod LXX. Interpp. transtulerunt in Christum suum, aliunde esse potest, quam à le- ctionis diversitate, sive quod similitudine, & ambi- guitate decepti fuerint, ut Hieronymus existimat, seu quod libenter hæc, ut alia, ad Christum traxe- rint. Mera conjectura, & vana divinatio est ex hujusmodi discrepantiis varias lectiones Codicis Ebræi constituere, ut recte Capello hic respondit Buxtorf. p. 686. Aquila certe, Symmachus, Thedotio non aliter legerunt, quam nunc habent Cod.Ebræi. Quam lectionem confirmat συνέχεια textus: post- quam enim varias pœnas minatus erat Dominus, confirmationis causa addidit argumenta ab operi- bus Dei partim ordinariis tum potentiæ infinitæ v. 13. quia ecce ego formans montes, & creans ventos: Conf. Ps. 104, 28. Job. 28, 9. tum gratiæ divinæ in annuntiatione eloquii (ut Clementina habet) sui. (B. Gerhardus reddit quodnam שחו quod opus ejus? item quæ meditatio ejus? quæ divina de genere hu- mano meditatio, conferens Ps. 147, 19. 20. Mich. 6, 8. Am. 3, 7.) partim extraordinariis: Faciens ma- tutinam nebulam, in Ebr. auroram caliginem, id est, maxime obscuram, miraculosa scilicet tenebrarum inductione, & gradiens super excelsa terræ, in qui- bus idololatræ cultum suum exercebant Lev. 26. 30. Num. 33, 52. id est, idololatras conculcans & avertens modo etiam miraculoso: Conf. Deut. 33. v. 29. FACIENS MATUTINAM NEBULAM) Faciens auroram & tenebras, id est, res prosperas dans piis, adversas improbis, ut hic habet Chaldæus. ET GRADIENS SUPER EXCELSA TERRÆ) d est, conterens superbos.

## 5:1 Argument
SERMON IV. PENITENTIAL. CHAPTER V. CONCERNING SEEKING THE LORD.

The complaint instituted concerning the fall of Israel warns that they should not seek idols, so that they may live, lest they be consumed by the fire of divine wrath, and that those oppressing others may be destroyed by the Lord of all: And because they persecute the Prophets who rebuke them, and persevere in their injustice, he predicts their ejection: yet he invites them again to repentance by promised grace, but threatens woe in all the streets, fields, and vineyards, and mere darkness and destruction, with detestation of their sacred rites and sacrifices, and with a promised river of justice for the faithful, he intimates to the people, who have long deserved destruction on account of their ancient custom of idolatry, their abduction into Damascus.

The mournful complaint bids sins to fear ruin. Vers. 1. HEAR YE THIS WORD WHICH I TAKE UP AGAINST YOU, A LAMENTATION, O HOUSE OF ISRAEL) From the Hebrew you may well translate: Which I lift up over you, a lamentation for the house of Israel.

SHE IS FALLEN, AND SHALL NO MORE RISE) That is, she shall not rise again: namely, if she continues in this way. Vers. 3. THERE SHALL BE LEFT IN IT TEN) Alive. Vers. 4. FOR THUS SAITH THE LORD UNTO THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL, SEEK YE ME, AND YE SHALL LIVE) Yet thus he says: As if the decrees were not yet sealed, as the Hebrews say. Vers. 5. BUT SEEK NOT BETHEL, NOR ENTER INTO GILGAL) See above 4, 4.

AND YOU SHALL NOT CROSS OVER INTO BARSABEE) Do not cross over, namely into the borders of Judah, where Barsabee was, as Jerome notes here, and it would be proven from 1 Kings 19:3; however, the superstitious chose this place for their worship, because God had appeared there to Isaac. Gen. 26:24.

Latin:

CONCIO IV. POENITENTIALIS. CAPUT V. DE DOMINO QVÆRENDO.

Querela de casu Israelis instituta monet, Do- minum non idola quærant, ut vivant, ne igne iræ divinæ consumantur, & alios opprimen- tes à Domino universi destruantur: Et quia Prophetas corripientes insectantur, inque sua injustitia perseverant, ejectionem eo- rum predicit: iterum tamen ad pœniten- tiam promissa gratia invitat, væ autem in omnibus plateis, agris & vineis & meras te- nebras atque exitium minatur cum detesta- tione sacrorum & sacrificiorum, ac promis- so ob fideles justitiæ flumine, populo ob anti- quam idololatriæ consuetudinem pridem exitium merito abductionem in Damascum intimat.

Mæsta querela jubet peccata timere ruinam. Vers. 1. QVOD EGO LEVO SVPER VOS PLANCTVM DOMVS ISRAEL) Ex Hebræo bene vertas: Quod ego attollo super vos lugubre domui Israel.

CECIDIT, ET NON ADJICIET UT RESUR- GAT) Id est, non iterum surget: nempe si ita pergit. Vers. 3. RELINQVENTVR IN EA DECEM) Vivi. Vers. 4 QVIA HÆC DICIT DOMINVS DOMVI ISRAEL, QVÆRITE ME ET VIVETIS) Attamen hæc dicit: Quasi decretis nondum obsignatis, ut loquuntur Hebræi. Vers. 5. ET NOLITE QVÆRERE BETHEL, ET IN GALGALAM NOLITE INTRARE) Vide sup. 4, 4.

ET IN BARSABEE NON TRANSIBITIS) Ne transite, nempe in fines Judæ, ubi erat Barsabee, ut notat hic Hieronymus, & probaretur ex 1. Reg. 19, 3. hunc autem locum cultui suo superstitiosi delegerunt, quod ibi Deus Isaaco apparuerat. Gen. 26, 24.

## 5:5
GALGALA SHALL BE LED CAPTIVE) In the Hebrew there is an elegant παρονομασία, הגלגל גלה יגלה, for in those words 'gal' is repeated twice, as in the name Galgal.

AND BETHEL SHALL BE USELESS) In the Hebrew: there is also here an allusion to the name which the Jews gave to Bethel. That is, however, here בית און.

## 5:10
Verse 10. THEY HATED HIM WHO REPROVES IN THE GATE.) They hate him who is in the gate (that is, the judges) who gives upright counsel.

He wishes the judges to be reproved, because they hated him who gives upright counsel. Others think that those are reproved rather who hated the judge reproving in the gate, and could not bear justice with an even mind. Thus it will not be necessary to posit a certain ellipsis of the word אשר. The version of B. Luther has it thus, which Cocceius also approves. It can also be understood in this way: they hate him who reproves and rebukes their crimes openly and as it were in the very gate or house of judgment, as these were accustomed to be exercised in the gate in former times. Deut. 22:15. Zach. 8:16. Thus Tarnovius, and the Weimar Paraphrase. 'But they (the Israelites) are angry at him who punishes them in the gate (that is, publicly) for their wickedness and oppression of the poor.' Jerome, Theodoret, Lyra, Vatablus, Cornelius à Lapide understand it of the Prophet, because the Prophets also preached in the gates. Jer. 17:19. Neh. 8:2. Osiander indeed intimates that the vices of judges are noted, but he retains the Vulgate version: They hated him that rebuketh in the gate and him that speaketh perfectly (that is, those things which are pious and just) they abominate: they cannot bear that those things which are done wrongly in the court (where judgments are exercised and the Republic is deliberated upon) should be reproved by the Ministers of the Church. But also in the Senate they receive freer opinions with a most unjust spirit. If judges are to be reproved at all, which does not displease, since v. 15 the Prophet warns: Establish judgment in the gate, the words can be rendered without ellipsis thus: They hated in the gate him that rebuketh, so that the word IN THE GATE is referred to the former word hating (they hated in the gate) and not to the latter, him that rebuketh, as the Belgian Paraphrasts and Mr. Dr. Wigandus have it.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ODIO HABVERVNT CORRIPIENTEM IN PORTA.) Oderunt qui in porta sunt, (id est judices) recta monentem.

Judices reprehendi vult, quod recta monen- tem oderint. Alii censent, reprehendi potius il- los, qui judicem in porta corripientem odio habue- runt, nec justitiam æquo animo ferre potuerunt. Ita non erit, ut ellipsin quandam statuamus vocis אשר. Ita habet B. Lutheri versio, quam etiam Coc- cejus probat. Intelligi etiam hoc pacto potest: ode- runt corripientem, ac reprehendentem ipsorum scele- ra aperte & velut in ipsa porta seu domo judicii, ut- pote quæ olim in porta exerceri consuevere. Deut. 22, 15. Zach. 8, 16. Sic Tarnovius, & Paraph. Vinariens. Aber Sie (die Jsraeliter) sind dem gram/ der Sie im Thor (das ist öffentlich) wegen ihres Fre- vels und Unterdrückung der Armen straffet. De Propheta intelligunt Hier. Theod. Lyr. Vatabl. Corn. à Lapide, quod etiam Prophetæ in portis prædica- rint Jer. 17, 19. Neh. 8, 2. Osiander judicum quidem vitia notari innuit, sed retinet versionem vulgatam: Odio habuerunt corripientem in porta & loquentem perfecte (id est, ea quæ pia & justa sunt) abominan- tur: non possunt ferre, ut ea, quæ perperam fiunt in curia (ubi judicia exercentur, & de Republica deliberatur) à Ministris Ecclesiæ reprehendantur. Sed & in Senatu liberiores sententias iniquissimo animo accipiunt. Si omnino judices reprehendan- tur, quod non displicet, quum v. 15. moneat Pro- pheta: Constituite in porta judicium, sine ellipsi ita verba reddi poterunt: Odio habuerunt in porta cor- ripientem, ut vox IN PORTA, ad priorem vocem odio habentes referatur (odio in porta habuerunt) non ad posteriorem, corripientem, ut habent Pa- raphrastæ Belgici, & Dn. D. Wigandus.

Vers. 22. BUT IF YOU OFFER ME BURNT OFFERINGS) From the law of Levit. 1.

The Lord rejects gifts and burnt offerings, because they were not offered with faith, Bellarm. b. 2. on the efficacy of the Sacraments, ch. 14. from this passage he attempts to prove that the sacrifices and sacraments of the O.T. did not justify, which we easily concede concerning them, when faith did not accompany them. Because they did not have power from themselves or through themselves; but through another, namely through the merit of Christ who was to suffer, whom they typologically represented, to be apprehended by true faith, without which they were neither pleasing to God, nor efficacious Heb. 11, 6.

AND YOUR GIFTS) מנחות. Concerning which Levit. 2.
