## 5:24
Vers. 24. AND JUDGMENT SHALL BE REVEALED AS WATER, AND JUSTICE AS A STRONG TORRENT) But let justice (among you) flow like water, and kindness like a rapid torrent. The sense is: all rites are displeasing to me, until you have amended your life.

He refers that still to exhortation or correction, which has also been done by the Tigurines, Vatablus, Tarnovius, the Belgian Paraphrase, as also by Cocceius. Others wish the end of punishments to be designated, the revelation of the justice of God, like Wigandus, Osiander; or the denunciation of punishment, i.e., God, about to reveal himself, and to erupt with great force like a torrent, justice and severe judgment upon the Israelites, which they have hitherto earned by their crimes, as the Weimar Paraphrase and Cornelius à Lapide. Blessed Winckelman understands the passage Evangelically concerning that judgment, of which Christ speaks in John 16. The prince of this world has been judged, and concerning justice, which is, that he who believes in Christ, he is justified Acts 13. Which judgment began to be revealed in Samaria through Christ John 4. and thus a certain fountain began to be opened, whose rivulets then and afterwards, with the preaching of the Apostles added Acts 8. spread themselves far and wide. The weight of the words and the emphasis of the comparison correspond more correctly to Evangelical justice than to human justice. Compare Isa. 11, 9. and ch. 48, 18. or certainly they are referred to the vindicatory justice of God, agreeing with Theodoret and Cyril, rather than with Grotius to the pursuit of the justice of men. when for that is only such, that it can be compared to fields and a flowing torrent? Theodoret has it thus: A just judgment against you is established like a torrent, and most violent water, may it bring upon you punishments and torments, and you shall not be able to find an exit. These are the words of Cyril: but judgment shall roll like water, and justice proceeding from me, that is, against you a just sentence from now on shall be like a torrent, sweeping away with it, clearly, those things which have fallen in, and sparing no one. For torrents descend from the mountains with force. In the same way, if the divine sentence comes against certain people, it will be an impregnable water, and a torrent, which cannot be resisted, and nothing else. The Evangelical interpretation is nevertheless to be preferred, because the Prophets are accustomed, with similar threats, to intermix from time to time Evangelical promises for the sake of the faithful, and for a more effective exhortation toward salutary penetration: which is also the opinion of the Blessed Luther in his Commentary on this passage. After the threat, he here intermixed the kingdom of Christ, and it is a transition, as if to say: Why is it that you boast of your sacrifices, your offerings, and all those things? There will be a time sometime when all those external things will cease, and justice will be revealed most copiously. Therefore, he seems to me to be speaking entirely about the revealing of the Gospel through Christ. For to be revealed, to be preached, and to be manifested is that which at that time had not yet been done. Therefore, he here passes from a reprobate worship to a true worship, and one that pleases God. For thus are all the Prophets accustomed, when they are about to propose true justice through Christ, to condemn the works of all the faithful that are in appearance most holy. The same is in Psalm 40. Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but you have perfected ears for me, etc. When therefore he says, as water, he signifies the abundance of Grace, which is to be announced through the Gospel, just as there are similar things in Isaiah. AS A TORRENT, he signifies the power and efficacy of the word. For the word breaks through and runs forcefully, even where the fury of Satan and of adversaries is in the middle. Whether Princes want it or not, it breaks through like a torrent, which they cannot prohibit, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET REVELABITVR QVASI AQVA JV- DICIVM, ET JVSTITIA QVASI TORRENS FOR- TIS) Sed jus (apud te) ut aqua profluat, & benignitas ut torrens rapidus. Sensus est: omnes ritus mihi displicent, donec vitam emendaveritis.

Refert illa adhuc ad παραίνεσιν vel ἐπανόρθω- σιν, quod etiam à Tigur. Vatabl. Tarnovio, Paraph. Belgic. ut & Coccejo factum est. Alii finem designari volunt pœnarum, revelationem justitiæ Dei, ut Wi- gandus Osiander; vel denuntiationem pœnæ, q. d. Deus, à se proditurum, & magna vi erupturum in- star torrentis jus ac judicium severum in Israelitas, quod suis commeruere hactenus flagitiis, ut Paraph. Vinariens. & Cornel. à Lapide. Evangelice locum intelligit B.Winckelm. de judicio illo, de quo Chri- stus Joh. 16. Princeps mundi judicatus est, & de ju- stitia, quæ est, quod qui credit in Christum, is justifica- tus est Act. 13. Quod judicium revelari cœpit in Sa- maria per Christum Joh. 4. atque ita fons quidam aperiri cœpit, cujus rivuli se tum & postea, accedente brædicatione Apostolorum Act. 8. longe lateque se dif- fuderunt. Pondera verborum & emphasis simi- litudinis rectius justitiæ Evangelicæ congruunt, quam justitiæ humanæ. Conf Esa. 11, 9. & c. 48, 18. aut certe ad justitiam vindicatricem Dei referen- tur convenientis cum Theodoreto & Cyrillo, quam cum Grotio ad studium justitiæ hominum. Quando enim illud tantum est, ut agris & torrenti liquido conferri possit? Theodorethus ita habet: Constitutum contra vos judicium justum torrentis instar, & vio- lentissime aque, in vos pœnas & supplicia inferat, exi- tumque invenire non poteritis. Cyrilli hæc sunt: sed tanquam aqua volvetur judicium meum, & a me profecta justitia, hoc est, contra vos justa de cœtero sen- tentia quasi torrens erit contra vos, secum abstrahens videlicet quæ inciderint, & parcens nemini. De mon- tibus enim cum impetu descendunt torrentes. Eo- dem modo divina sententia si adversus quosdam venerit, aqua inexpugnabilis, & torrens, cui resisti non potest, erit, & aliud nihil. Præferenda tamen Interpretatio Evangelica, quia solent Prophetæ si- milibus comminationibus subinde promissiones Evangelicas ob fideles, & efficaciorem, ad saluta- rem penetrationem, exhortationem admiscere: quæ sententia etiam B. Lutheri est in Comment. ad h. l. Post comminationem hic immiscuit regnum Chri- sti, estque transitio, Q. d. Quid est, quod vestra sacri- ficia, vestras oblationes, & ista omnia jactatis? Erit aliquando tempus, cum ista omnia externa cessabunt, & revelabitur copiosissime justitia. Itaque omnino mihi loqui videtur de relevando Evangelio per Chri- stum. Revelari enim, prædicari & manifestari est, id quod tum factum nondum erat. Itaque hic tran- sit a cultu reprobo ad cultum verum, & qui Deo pla- ceat. Sic enim solent omnes Prophetæ, ut veram justi- tiam per Christum proposituri, damnent omnium fi- delium opera in speciem sanctissima. Idem est in Psal- mo 40. Sacrificium & oblationem noluisti, aures autem perfecisti mihi &c. Quando ergo ait, quasi aqua, significat abundantiam Gratiæ, quæ per Evan- gelium sit annuncianda, sicut & apud Esaiam simi- lia sunt. QVASI TORRENS, Potentiam & ef- ficaciam verbi significat. Fortiter enim perrum- pit & currit verbum, etiam ubi medius est furor Satanæ & adversariorum. Velint nolint Princi- pes, perrumpit ut torrens, quem non possunt pro- hibere, &c.

## 5:25
Vers. 25. DID YOU OFFER VICTIMS AND SACRIFICE TO ME IN THE DESERT FOR FORTY YEARS O HOUSE OF ISRAEL) Did you not? LXX. for forty years: that is, within that space of 40 years, did you not also at that time offer victims and manna? And yet those who were led out of Egypt perished on the journey, because of their evil ways.

Most others wish to answer the rhetorical question negatively, as in Joel 1, 2 and elsewhere frequently, namely that they did not offer sacrifices to God in the desert, both because immediately in the first year of their departure they made a golden calf: which Jerome, Rupert, Hugo, in this place, Chrysostom, and Bede on Acts 6 wish to be the answer: and because after the tabernacle was erected in the second year from the departure, and victims were offered in it, they afterwards offered either no, or rare, sacrifices to God in the desert, as Abarbenel, Cornel. a Lapide, and Coccejus note, that sacrifices ceased after the dwelling near Mount Sinai, just as circumcision and the passover also ceased, Jos. 5, 10. and because a great part of them, if not openly, yet secretly, preferred idolatrous rites to the legitimate worships instituted by God, and the sacred things of the Lord were contaminated by secret idolatry, as the Osiandrine paraphrase has it. Jerome; From that time, from which they transformed the gold into the head of a calf, saying: These are your gods O Israel, who led you out of the land of Egypt, all things which they did are shown to have been done not to God, but to idols. The Lord does not look at those things which are offered, but at the will of the one offering. But these things must be accepted with a qualification. Far be it that those things should be said of all.

Latin:

Vers. 25. NVMQVID HOSTIAS ET SACRIFICI- VM OBTVLISTIS MIHI IN DESERTO QVADRA- GINTA ANNIS DOMVS ISRAEL) Nonne? LXX. ἡ. quadraginta annis: id est, intra illud spatium annorum XL. nonne etiam eo tempore victimas & μαννὰν obtulistis? & tamen illi ex Ægypto educti n itinere perierunt, propter malos mores.

Plerique alii negative respondere volunt inter- rogationem Rhetoricam, ut Joël 1, 2. & alibi pas- sim, quod nempe Deo sacrificia non obtulerint in deserto, tum quia statim primo egressus anno vitu- lum aureum exerunt: quod Hieron. Rupertus, Hugo, in h. l. Chrysost. & Beda ad Act. 6. respici volunt: tum quod erecto secundo ab exitu anno tabernaculo, & oblatis in eo victimis, postea vel nullas, vel raras Deo in deserto obtulerint, uti Abarbenel, Cornel. a Lapide, Coccejus notant, cessasse sacrificia post ha- bitationem juxta montem Sinai, quemadmodum & circumcisio & pascha cessavit Jos. 5, 10. tum quod magna ipsorum pars, si non aperte, tamen occulte, idololatrica sacra legitimis a Deo institutis culti- bus prætulerit, & sacra Domini occulta idolatria contaminaris, ut habet paraphrasis Osiandrina. Hie- ronymus; Ex eo tempore, quo aurum in caput vituli transformarunt, dicentes: Isti sunt dii tui Israel, qui te deduxerunt de terra Ægypti, omnia quæ fecerunt, non Deo, sed idolis fecisse monstrantur. Dominus non ea, quæ offeruntur, sed voluntatem respicit offe- renti. Sed hæc κατά τι accipienda sunt. Absit, ut de omnibus illa dicantur.

## 5:26
Vers. 26. AND YOU CARRIED THE TABERNACLE OF YOUR MOLOCH) But now also the tabernacle, that is, the little shrine of your God Moloch, or Saturn, you carried, as the Chaldean here adds: you are so much worse than they; they murmured against me: you introduced other Gods. You carried in Greek is ἀνελάβετε. Eustathius on Iliad 1 says there were shrines carried by beasts, just as Philo Byblius also speaks. Servius on the 6th Aeneid: small images which were carried in litters: and moved by them they poured forth prophecies, which was done among the Egyptians and Carthaginians. The Israelites therefore in this either imitated the Tyrians, the progenitors of the Carthaginians, or the Egyptians, they translate סכות, a tent, here in the LXX, and the Chaldean no differently.

AND THE IMAGE OF YOUR IDOLS, THE STAR OF YOUR GOD WHICH YOU MADE FOR YOURSELVES) In the Hebrew: And Kiun your image of the star: your gods, which you made for yourselves. Where your gods is commonly referred to Moloch, and to Kiun. LXX. and the star of your god Remphan, the images which you made for yourselves. Luke follows this in Acts 7, 43. and the star of your god Remphan, the images which you made to worship them. The Chaldean: And Kiun your image, the star your idol, which you made for yourselves. Just as Moloch is an Ammonitic name, so כיון is Arabic, and Persian, which Abenesdra says is also written כיואן, and is for them Saturn. The same is called by the Syrians רמן 2 Kings 5, 18. surely because it was in the highest sphere, as Tacitus speaks. Just as כיון was pronounced, and כיואן Kivan, so רמן also רמון Remvan, which the Greeks, having lost the use of the digamma, wrote Ῥαμφᾶν or Ῥεμφάν, which is the true writing. But the gods Moloch and Kiun or Kivan are so called, because although they were referred to the same star, they nevertheless had other names, and appearance, and worship, like the Moon and Diana among the Greeks: indeed, more men were referred to the same star, among different peoples: and Moloch had the figure of a king: Kivan of a Star.

These verses have been a cross for interpreters, especially because of the translation of the LXX cited by Luke in Acts 7:43. Opinions vary on almost every individual word. Symmachus, Aquila, and the LXX take the word סכות as an appellative, rendering it σκηνὴν, whom the Evangelist Luke follows, as does the Vulgate, explaining it as tabernacle. Blessed Luther, along with many others, the Chaldean, Vatablus, etc., take it as the proper name of an idol, without doubt, because this word is entirely unique and is not found elsewhere in the Holy Code, and because the other word Kiun likewise denotes an idol. Therefore, he took the name מלככם as an appellative: You carried as your King; but since no such name of an idol is found anywhere, and yet the name מלכם occurs in 1 Kings 11:5, מלכם in Zephaniah 1:5, מלך in Leviticus 18:21, ch. 20:2, 4, 1 Kings 11:1, 2. Kings 23:11, concerning the idol of the Ammonites, to which the Israelites sacrificed in the desert, occurs, and is rendered by the LXX and St. Luke as τὴν σκηνὴν τῶν μολόχ, this interpretation is to be preferred without doubt. However, there is a much greater difficulty regarding the word Kiun, which Aquila, Symmachus, the Chaldean, and the Syrian retained in their translation. Grotius takes it for the same idol as Moloch, which is called כיון or כיואן by the Arabs and Persians, following Aben Ezra, and he thinks it is the same as that called רמן in 2 Kings 5:18 by the Syrian. But how can רמן be formed from רמון, which occurs in the books of Kings, so that from it finally ῥεμφὰν arises? Christoph. a Castro thinks the word ῥεμφὰν is Greek, but it is deservedly rejected by Cornel. à Lapide. Others say the word ῥεμφὰν was introduced thus: namely, that the LXX interpreters read ריואן instead of כיואן because the letter כ was erased at the bottom, and that this name was changed into Remphan by the insertion of μ. Which was more a suspicion than an opinion of Brentius, Mercerus, Forsterus, and Drusius. And although this Drusius is bold enough, he nevertheless deserves no approval. For who would admit that Kaph is transmuted into Resch, and that an error arising from the transformation of Kaph into Resch in this word should be established as approved by Luke? Therefore, Corn. à Lapide refutes it. This opinion is opposed by the fact that all Hebrew Codices have Kiun, not Rephan; conversely, all Greek and Latin Codices of Acts 7 consistently have Rephan, not Kevan or Kiun. It is therefore not likely that only the LXX read Rephan instead of Kevan in one Hebrew Codex, or that copyists transcribed Rephan for Kevan in the Septuagint, especially since the whole Church in the Vulgate edition of Acts 7 consistently reads Rephan, as if this were the true and genuine reading. It is added that in the Hebrew in Amos at this place it is not Kevan, but Kiun, as St. Jerome, Aquila, Symmachus, and others read everywhere: but Kiun is far from Rephan. The most learned Selden, in his Syntagma de Diis Syris, book 2, chapter 14, preferred to profess his own ignorance here rather than to accede to the audacity of Drusius. Some think that Remphan or Raphon, as it is found in 1 Maccabees 5:37, was a city, which was also called Chium, in which they served the heavenly host with the gravest idolatry. Ludovicus Capellus offers another conjecture, but one with which not even he himself, let alone others, was satisfied: concerning an Egyptian king named Remphan, worshipped by the Egyptians as a god: yet he does not dare to carve the name ῥεμφὰν out of that כיון, but rather considers it an appellative noun in his Spicilegium on Acts 7. Cornelius à Lapide has it thus: I say with Leo Castrius in his Apology, book 6, that Kiun and Kevan are the same as Rephan, for the reason that this idol, initially named and worshipped by the Israelites and Persians (as interpreters everywhere confess and the Rabbis hand down), was called in their language Kivan, or Kevan, which word, because the Hebrews did not understand it as a barbarian one, by a slight change of one letter, they called in their own language Rephan, that is, Giant: just as the Syrians call God the giant of the ages, because He himself, like a giant, encompasses and embraces all the spaces of the world as well as of time by His own immensity and eternity: or certainly Raphan, that is, Healer, as if to say, This is He who heals and saves us. Whence from the same Hebrew root the angel Raphael is called the Medicine or healing of God. Some codices read Rompha instead of Rephan, which in Hebrew is said רומפה, and is the same as height of the mouth: perhaps this idol had a large and high mouth, as most ancient idols have, which used to give oracles. For I have seen such in the Vatican, and such is that famous one which is visited near the Church of St. Mary in the Greek School, or in Cosmedin in Rome, and is commonly called Bocca de la verita, that is, the mouth or oracle of truth. Furthermore, although the common people of the Hebrews turned the barbarian name Rephan, and called it in Hebrew Rephan, Remphan, and Rompha, the more learned Hebrews nevertheless retained the original Kevan, which, by a slight change of letters or points or vowels, they called in the Hebrew tongue Kiun. For so Amos, Aquila, and Symmachus have it here. For Kiun is derived from the root כון which signifies to prepare, to fit, to be straight, to direct, to verify, to certify, to confirm, to perfect, to decree. Whence Kiun is the same as prepared, fitted, erected, perfect, giving true, certain, and firm oracles and decrees. Ludovicus de Dieu, at the suggestion of Claudius Salmasius, observes on Acts of the Apostles chapter 7 that the Egyptians call Saturn ῥηφὰν, and he exclaims on page 69: Now that opinion, received among almost all the learned, that ῥεφὰν in the LXX Interpreters is corrupted from the Hebrew כיון for which they read ריין, and thence ῥεφὰν, has fallen. The most learned and prudent interpreters are now to be praised because, when they were called to Egypt by Philadelphus, King of the Egyptians, for the sake of the Egyptians, to translate the Bible into the Greek language, they transmuted the Hebrew כיון, unknown to the Egyptians, into ῥεφὰν, which was most known to them. Athanasius Kircher in his Oedipus likewise observes that Remphan is Saturn in Coptic. Which opinion is far more probable than that of Grotius. Nor does De Dieu conceal the scruple, as to why the Israelites are said to have worshipped Saturn, concerning which he has this: But if it moves a scruple in anyone that God complains that the Israelites worshipped Saturn in the desert, when in the history of Moses mention is made only of a calf or an ox (for David calls it שׁוֹר in Ps. 106:20): I reply: that they referred the ox, the principal agent of plowing, to God, the author and president of agriculture: but that he was Saturn to the ancient Gentiles, for he is said to have been the one who taught Janus in Italy the way of living and the cultivation of fields, to whom for that discipline received he gave half of his kingdom: and for that reason, with his wife Rhea, he was held as a god, because he taught in Italy the planting, grafting, and education of all trees and the cultivation of all fruitful things. Therefore he interprets the words of the Prophet thus: And you carried the tabernacle of your Moloch, and Saturn your images, the star of your God, which you made for yourselves. Why did he say צלמיכם your images in the plural? Because סכות the tabernacle was not only a place and receptacle in which Moloch was carried enclosed or borne around, but it was the idol itself, being an image of the heaven in which the Sun or Moloch, that great king of the stars and president of sublunary things, is contained as if in a tabernacle: whence the Psalmist, Ps. 19:5, לשמש שם־אהל בהם set a tabernacle for the sun in them, the heavens. He reproaches them, therefore, because they carried around the tabernacle of Moloch Saturn for their images; but who is this Saturn? The star, he says, of your God, that is, which you hold and worship as God, just as we say the star of Saturn, which is Saturn himself. The star of Jupiter, which is Jupiter himself, the river Euphrates, which is the Euphrates itself. Finally, he reconciles Stephen with Amos thus: You carried Saturn, the star of your God, is the same as what Luke says, ἀνελάβετε τὸ ἄςρον ☿ θεᾶ ὑμῶν ῥεμφὰν, so that this proper name is in the accusative case, like τὸ ἄςρον, both because the Arabic termination suggests it, and because the construction in Greek is the same as in Hebrew, only the position of the words varies, and instead of the Arabic Kiun, the Egyptian ῥηφὰν is used by the LXX Interpreters and is usurped by Luke. Others, however, prefer to take the name Kiun as an appellative. It certainly differs from the name כיואן, and why should a Persian or Arabic name be attributed to an Egyptian idol by Amos? They derive it therefore from כון, he prepared, with Buxtorf and Marinus: thus they wish to denote a foundation, or a base skillfully made, upon which the images of idols were placed, so that they might be the better transferred from place to place, and set up in the temple. See Junius in the parallels, Beza on Acts 7, Ribera on this passage. Mariana renders it the apparatus of your idols. Others explain it as a cake with Avenarius, Pagninus, Vatablus, and R. David Kimchi. Theodotion translated it ἀμαύρωσιν, that is, obscurity; therefore that word was omitted, and the proper name of the idol ῥεμφὰν was added by Stephen, which did not exist in the Prophet, which some wish to be taken from the name of some place, namely Ῥεφὰν or Ῥεμφὰν, 1 Macc. 5:37, which is a town situated in the borders of the Ammonites, over which a tutelary god Rephan or Remphan presided. The arrangement of the words favors this opinion: You carried the TABERNACLE OF YOUR MOLOCH, AND BASAN OF YOUR OTHER IMAGES, the star also of your gods, which you made for yourselves. Thus the words of Luke agree, κ͵ ἀνελά- βετε τὴν σκηνὴν τᾶ μολὸχ ἡμῶν (which exactly reflect the Hebrew) κ͵ τὸ ἄςρον τᾶ θεᾶ ὑμῶν, the star of your God, τὰς τύπες, ὃς ἐποιήσατε, the figures which you made. He understands by the word Sicuth the litter in which the image of Moloch was carried, and Selden is prolix about it in book 1, chapter 6, page 199. If the word Kiun is rendered as apparatus, it will be said that from that apparatus of images Remphan is designated as the principal idol, so that with the apparatus of images expressed by Stephen, it is named only by the word star as the figure of their God, which Amos had not designated by name. What this star was, says Blessed Luther, cannot be gathered from Scripture; Stephen in the Acts calls it the star of the idol Remphan. Nor would there be opposed to this interpretation, by which that word is taken as an appellative noun, that Egyptian meaning of the word Remphan for Saturn. And therefore they shall be said to have carried the tabernacle of Moloch, and in it their Moloch and the apparatus of their images, and especially Remphan Saturn, the star of their God, or the star which they worshipped instead of their God, namely those images which they made for themselves for the sake of worship. If anyone should say that Moloch was also Saturn, Dievius objects: Nor is there any reason for it to trouble anyone that we have confused Saturn with Moloch above: for the Prophet and Luke distinguish these gods, and call the images by the plural number. For such was the propensity of the ancients to increase the number of gods, that the mere variation of a name or image sufficed to tear one and the same god or goddess into many. Isis, Lucina, Diana, Trivia, Hecate were various goddesses, when yet they were only different names of one Moon. Concerning which, he who wants more, let him see the third chapter of the Prolegomena of the illustrious Selden on the Syrian Gods. To Scaliger, book 1 on Manilius, Remphan is the same as רעם פעם Jupiter βροντὲυς or ζεὺς βροντιαῖος, the thunderer, or the Author of thunder. Ribera thinks it was also a Jupiter who had a star on his head. Others think it was Mars. Vossius, book 2 on idolatry, chapter 23, wants Remphan (as also Chiun) to be the Moon. Mercerus in his commentary explains it as Lucifer, or Venus. Which Cornelius à Lapide reports to have been the opinion of Jerome, Remigius, Albert the Great, Bede, and Lyranus, and proves it from the fact that the Syrians once worshipped this star as the Queen of heaven, as witnessed by St. Jerome in the life of St. Hilarion, and the Saracens still worship it, and that Giraldus, Syntagma 13, teaches from Aelian and others that Venus Urania, that is, the celestial one, who seems to be Lucifer, was worshipped by the Egyptians, Phoenicians, and Assyrians, and that Lucifer, called Kiun, is from כון to burn, to scorch, and there are many more such conjectures of his. Thus Sanchez here, and Acts 7, thinks Moloch is the sun, Remphan is Lucifer. Hence, he says, the star of Lucifer was placed on the forehead of Moloch, because Lucifer precedes the rising Sun, for the Sun is Moloch, that is, the King of the stars. If this opinion is admitted, that Moloch was the Sun and Remphan was Lucifer, the reason will become clear why Remphan is so described as the Star of your God, because the star Lucifer was believed to be Moloch or the Sun, the King of the stars. Giraldus, in his book of Syntagmata on Hercules, thinks Rephan is a name for Hercules, and signifies a giant from the Hebrew Repha, the father of giants, whence giants are called Rephaim, and that he was also called by the Gentiles by the Hebrew word Con or Kiun, i.e., the stayer or the erect and exalted one.

In this variety, the opinion of Ludov. de Dieu seems preferable, that Remphan is Saturn, just as we also observed in the Critica Sacra, page 27. But whom we shall perhaps more correctly distinguish here from Moloch, so that by this name the Sun was designated. For Selden, book 1, Syntagma, chapter 6, page 176, teaches that Moloch was the idol of the Ammonites, who was called βασιλεὺς θεῶν, King of the Gods, and in the most ancient theology of the Phoenicians was also named Adod, as Philo of Byblos testifies in Eusebius, and that he was worshipped by the Syrians; and he observes especially that the effigies of both Adod and Moloch are mentioned by ancient writers as almost the same, and fashioned to express one Sun, and that Scaliger in his Exercitationes noted that the Sun was called Adad in Persian. Therefore, it is not to be held as certain or indubitable what Grotius assumes, that Moloch and Rephan were referred to the same star. Nor is the new punctuation to be approved which he wishes to introduce, different from the Hebrew text; while he renders it thus: And Kiun your image of the star: your gods, which you made for yourselves. For in the Hebrew it is held thus, and Kiun of your images (in

(in the plural) the star of your God, or of your gods: אשר which pronoun seems to refer itself not to the Gods, but to all the preceding things: it is certainly referred to the images by the LXX and St. Stephen, τὲς τύπες ἑς ἐποιήσατε. These things concerning the words.

As for the matter itself, at what time these things were done, Grotius refers them to the present times of Amos, and therefore takes the particle ו not in a copulative sense, but in a disjunctive one. But now you have also carried the tabernacle, that is, the shrine of your God Moloch, that is, you will carry, in a prophetic sense, i.e., I will transfer you beyond Damascus into Assyria, and there the Assyrians will force you captives to carry Moloch on your shoulders; others admit that they look to past times, and refer them to the worship of the golden calf in the desert, with Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, and Rupert on this passage. and Oecumenius on Acts 7, but it is manifest from the sermon of Stephen that this worship, by which God permitted them to serve the host of heaven, is distinguished from the worship of the calf; and it is no less clear from this Prophetic passage, with the words of Stephen also compared, that the Prophet is not prophesying about the future, but is setting before the Israelites the sins to which they had already made themselves liable ever since their defection in the desert, for which he finally threatens them with abduction. Nor do the words of Stephen the Protomartyr easily admit that that idolatry should be restricted only to the times of Amos: since he reproaches the Israelites for their perpetual prevarication, apostasy, and idolatry from the exodus out of Egypt, as is especially clear from verse 51. Therefore, however much we may by no means exclude the times of Amos, we do not admit with Grotius that these things are restricted to those times alone. Nor is it necessary that we should refer them, as some do, only to the 40 years spent in the desert; for there are distinct heads of accusation, that they did not serve the ONE God even then, and from that they also not rarely progressed to such idolatries and impiety that they also carried or took up the tabernacle of Moloch. Which Lyranus says was done in the holy land, when Solomon served it, 1 Kings 11:5, others with Ribera in the desert, when they committed fornication with the daughters of Moab, and worshipped Baal-Peor, Num. 25:1, since Josephus, book 4, Antiquities, chapter 6, is the author that they then worshipped not one, but many gods, and the Ammonites were neighbors and kinsmen to the Moabites. Those things can be properly joined, and other moments of that idolatrous worship besides; which can be gathered to have flourished likewise in the time of Amos himself from Hosea especially, who was his contemporary, and described the manifold idolatry of Israel at length. For those whom the Prophet threatened with punishment did not call it guilt, and although that punishment fell upon the Israelites then present, or their children, they themselves are certainly not to be excluded from the guilt. Coccejus here, as for the most part elsewhere, is singular, and refers these things to the tabernacle, the ark, and the Cherubim, from which, however, Stephen openly distinguished them, as is evident from Acts 7:43-44: From of old it has been thought that the stars are either animals or bodies, as it were of genii, which they call intelligences, or at least their vehicles. Hence the worship of the stars. Since the Israelites were not averse to such opinions, and for the most part did not acknowledge God in Christ, but held the Cherubim as symbols of the angels above the ark, he not unjustly calls them by way of mockery images of the star of their gods themselves: or the ark a receptacle of images, on account of the resemblance. For since idolaters had something external similar to what God had instituted, what else could be said of the Israelites, with the idolatrous affection being added, than what was said of the idolaters? We think it is obscure to no one how alien these things are from the words of the Prophet and of St. Luke.

These things are correct: We add only Cocceius's observation: It should trouble no one here that Babylon is sometimes to the East. If you proceed according to the meridians, the meridian of the Holy Land is more easterly. Conversely, if you proceed according to the parallels, or the latitude of the world, Babylonia, as well as the Median regions and others, is carried much further to the North. And hence in the Prophecies, evil shall be opened from the north, i.e., from Babylon. From Amos it is clear that it concerns the X tribes. Stephen confirms the same, explaining τὸ ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ by ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος. Which explanation is not a substitution of one place for another, but of a more distinct place for an indefinite one. A more common and indefinite place. Beyond Damascus, indeed the whole region of the northern sky surpassing Damascus is understood indefinitely by the words of Amos. A more distinct one, beyond Babylon. Blessed Gerhard has this regarding the reconciliation of Stephen in Acts 7:42, 43, in this place. the Prophet says that it will come to pass that the Israelites will be deported beyond Damascus, the Evangelist, looking to the faith of sacred history and the truth of the event, explains that they were to be deported not only beyond Damascus, but also beyond Babylonia, since some of them were led away then into Persia, then into the region of the Caspians, far beyond Damascus. Compare the event in 2 Kings 17:6, chapter 18:11, Ezra 7:17. He proves the same regarding the word Remphan for the opinion of those who say it was substituted by Stephen for the word Kiiun: Others, he says, maintain that the word כִּיוּן was omitted by Stephen, and that the name of an idol was added which did not exist in the Prophet; which opinion is the best of all. To which we have long since added our vote in the Critico Sacro p. 524, praised by the blessed Joh. Ernst Gerhard in Comment. on Acts of the Apostles p. 264, where [he refers] to Drusius in Praeter., Vossius l. 2 de Idolol. c. 23, Buxtorf in Lexic., and Capellus in Spicil. p. 75. I will say he wrote that the LXX interpreters, deceived by the affinity of the letters Kaph and Resch, read רֵיפָן instead of כִּיוּן in Amos 5:23, and he accedes to our opinion, and establishes with us ὁμοψήφως that the star called ῥεφὰν by the Egyptians is Saturn; confirming this with the argument that the name רֵיפָן in 2 Kings 5:18 yielded to that star which is called Saturn, because רוּם denotes high to the Hebrews: and the star of Saturn is believed to be in the highest sphere. It is helpful here to add also the suffrage of Hottinger in primitiis Heidelberg. de idolograph. V. Test. p. 392, confirming that the word ῥεφαν is Egyptian and denotes Saturn, 1. by the authority of the Coptic N.T. version, which has ῥηφαν, 2. by the consensus of both the Coptic Commentaries on ch. 7 of Acts and the Arabic-Coptic Lexicon, which lists the seven planets in order, and among them ῥηφαν as Saturn. 3. Because כִּיוָן denoting Saturn in Hebrew, Arabic, and Persian, is the same as ῥεφαν. Cf. Bibl. Orient. p. 313. We add here, on the occasion of the idol Moloch, Rephan, and Kiiun, ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ from the same Hottinger's Idolograph. V.T. his judgment or rather conjecture regarding most false Deities: The Phoenician deity Baal in his judgment is the Sun: Moloch of the Ammonites and Egyptians is Mars: Rephan of these is Saturn; but Adramelech and Anamelech of the Assyrians are the same as Moloch, namely Mars. 2 Kings 17:31. Camosch of the Moabites is the same, Saturn, that is, Noah. Astharoth of the Sidonians is Venus or the Moon 1 Kings 11:5, 33. (Lucian in De Dea Syria and Herodian l. 5 on Heliogabalus wish Astarte to be the moon: but Philo Byblius and others [wish her to be] Venus:

Cornelius à Lapide on Judges 2:13 says that the gentiles initially worshipped the Sun and Moon: the Romans called them Jupiter and Juno, the Egyptians Osiris and Isis, the Syrians Baalim and Astaroth. Bonfrerius and Malvenda say Astharoth is Venus. Some wish this name to be the same as אֲשֵׁרוֹת of the groves, that is, the idols of the groves, Judges 3:7, as they explain by metonymy, although to others it seems rather that the deity or idol itself was Asarah, 2 Kings 21:7, ch. 23:6. But whether one should subscribe to these, so that the word Asara is always understood as the deity or Astartha of the Sidonians, and never as a grove, which Josephus says is implied, as Selden thinks, is rightly doubted) Gad of the Syrians is the Star of Jupiter, Menath to them is a constellation, Isa. 65:11. To these are added Baalzebub of the Philistines, worshipped in the image of a fly, 2 Kings 1:2, and Dagon or the magnificent fish, 1 Sam. 5:4. Baal-Peor of the Moabites, that is, Priapus: Num. 23, Job 22:17. Nergal of the Assyrians, who in his mind is fire. Nisroch of the same is considered to be a small boat, or the ship of Noah, 2 Kings 19:37. Asima of theirs, although the Hebrews and Kircher make it a goat, Hottinger professes that no more likely or certain opinion occurs to him, regarding which idol see 2 Kings 17:30. Apis of the Egyptians according to the LXX, Jer. 46:15, is an Ox. He says Thamuz of the same, Ezek. 8:15, is Baal Zephon, p. 402, Osiris, p. 383. Teraphim are images composed for a certain influx of the stars, as Talisman among the Arabs. Gods ἀλεξητήριοι, or averters, and fortune-tellers. Gen. 31:19. But regarding most of these, others [think] otherwise. See Selden in Syntagm., Kircher in Pantheo, Pococke in specim. Arab., etc., and what is [said] on Jer. 19:5.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET PORTASTIS TABERNACVLVM MOLOCH VESTRO) Nunc vero etiam tabernaculum, id est, ναῖσκον Molochi Dei vestri, sive Saturni, portastis, bini ut hic addit Chaldaeus: tanto pejores estis quam illi; illi mur- murarunt adversum me: vos alios Deos introduxistis. Por- tastis in Graeco est ἀνελάβετε. Eustathius ad Iliad. 1. ait fu- isse ναεὺς ζευγηφορεμένες, quomodo & Philo Byblius loqui- tur. Servius ad VI. Æneidos: ξόανα simulacra brevia quæ portabantur in lecticis: & ab ipsis mota infundebant vaticina- tionem, quod fiebat apud Ægyptios & Carthaginenses. Israeli- tæ ergo in hoc aut Tyrios imitati, Chartaginensium geni- tores, aut Ægyptios, סכות, σκηνὴν vertunt hic LXX. nec aliter Chaldæus.

ET IMAGINEM IDOLORUM VESTRORUM, SIDUS DEI VESTRI QVÆ FECISTIS VOBIS) In Hebræo: Et Kiun imaginem vestram stellæ: deos vestros, quos fecistis vobis. Ubi deos vestros communiter refertur ad Molo- chum, & ad Kiun. LXX. κὲ τὸ τὲ θεὲ ὑμῶν Ῥαμφᾶ, (alii libri habent ῥαιφάν) τὲς τύπες ἀυτῶν, ὃὓς ἐποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς. Hoc sequitur Lucas Act. 7, 43. κὴ τὸ ἄστρον τὲ θεοῦ ὑμῶν ῥεμφὰν, τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν ἀυτοῖς. Chaldæus: Et Kiun imaginem vestram, sidus idolum vestrum, quod fecistis vobis. Sicut Moloch est nomen Ammoniticum, ita כיון est Arabi- cum, & Persicum, quod & כיואן scribi ait Abenesdra, & esse eis Saturnum. Idem dictus Syris רמן 2 Reg. 5, 18. nimirum quod altissimo esset orbe, ut Tacitus loquitur. Sicut כיון pronunciabatur, & כיואן Kivan, ita רמן etiam רמון Rem- van, quod Græci, amisso digammæ usu, scripsere Ῥαμφᾶν aut Ῥεμφάν, quæ scriptura vera est. Dicuntur autem dii Mo- loch, & Kiun vel Kivan, quia quanquam ad idem sidus refe- rebantur, alia tamen habebant nomina, habitumque & cul- tum, ut Luna & Diana apud Græcos: quin & plures homines ad idem sidus relati, apud alias aliasque gentes: & Mo- loch regis habebat figuram: Kivan Stellæ.

Hi versus crucem fixerunt interpretibus, impri- mis ob translationem LXX. à Luca Act. 7, 43, ad- ductam. De singulis propemodum verbis senten- tiæ variant. Vocem סכות pro appellativa habent Symmachus, Aquila, & LXX. reddentes σκηνὴν, quos sequitur Lucas Evangelista, & Vulgatus, ex- ponens tabernaculum. Pro nomine idoli proprio B. Lutherus cum multis aliis, Chaldæo, Vatablo &c. sine dubio, quod hæc vox prorsus singularis est, nec alibi in S. Codice reperitur, quodque altera vox Kiun itidem idolum notet. Nomen ergo מלככם ac- cepit tanquam appellativum: Portastis sicut Regem ve- strum; sed quum nuspiam tale idoli nomen reperia- tur, nomen autem 1 מלכם. Reg. 11, 5. מלכם Soph. 1, 5. מלך Lev. 18, 21. c. 20, 2. 4. 1. Reg. 11, 1. 2. Reg. 23, 11. de idolo Ammonitarum, cui Israelitæ in deser- to litarunt, occurrat, & à LXX. ac S. Luca redda- tur τὴν σκηνὴν τῶν μολόχ, citra dubietatem præfe- renda hæc est interpretatio. De voce autem Kiun longe major est difficultas. Quam Aquila, Sym- machus, Chaldæus & Syrus retinuerunt in sua trans- latione. Grotius pro eodem idolo habet cum Mo- loch, quod Arabibus & Persis כיון vel כיואן dictum, Aben Esram sequutus, idemque Syrus רמן 2. Re- gum. 5, vers. 18. vocatum arbitratur. At quomo- do ex רמון quod in libris Regum occurrit, effor- mari potest רמן, ut inde tandem oriatur ῥεμφὰν? Christoph. a Castro vocem ῥεμφὰν Græcam esse ar- bitratur, sed merito rejicitur à Cornel. à Lapide. Alii vocem ῥεμφὰν sic invectam ajunt: legisse nempe LXX. Interpp. pro כיואן litera כ infer- ne eras à ריואן idque nomen inserto μ mutatum esse in Remphan. Quæ Brentii, Merceri, Forsteri, Drusii verius suspicio, quam sententia fuit. Et quamvis satis audax hic Drusius sit, nullum ta- men meretur calculum. Nam quis admittet ut Kaph in Resch transmutetur, & in hac voce er- ror è transformatione Kaph in Resch exortus à Luca approbatus statuatur? Ideo refellit id Corn. à Lapid. Obstat huic sententiæ, quod omnes Codices Hebræi habeant Kiun, non Rephan; adverso omnes Codices Græci & Latini Actor. 7. constanter habe- ant Rephan, non Kevan, aut Kiun. Non ergo est verisimile solos LXX. legisse in uno Codice Hebræo Re- phan pro Kevan, aut descriptores pro Kevan in Se- ptuag. descripsisse Rephan, præsertim cum tota Eccle- fia in vulgata editione Act. 7. constanter legat Rephan, quasi hac vera & genuina sit lectio. Accedit, quod in Hebræo apud Amos hoc loco non sit Kevan, sed Kiun, ut legit S. Hieronym. Aquila, Symmach. & alii passim : Kiun autem procul abest à Rephan. Do- ctissimus Seldenus syntagm. de Diis Syris l. 2. c. 14. ma- luit ignorantiam suam hic profiteri, quam audaciæ Drusianæ accedere. Nonnulli Remphan vel Ra- phon ut habetur 1 Macc. 5, 37. urbem fuisse putant, quæ etiam Chium appellata fuerit, in qua militiæ cœlesti servierint idololatria gravissima. Ludovicus Capellus aliam conjecturam profert, sed qua ne sibi quidem ipsi, nedum aliis satisfecit: de rege Ægyptii nomine Remphan ab Ægyptiis pro Deo culto: non audet tamen ex illo כיון nomen ῥεμφὰν exsculpere, quin illud potius pro appellativo ha- bet nomine in spicileg. ad Act. 7. Cornel. à Lapide sic habet : Dico ego cum Leone Castrio Apolog. l. 6. Kiun & Kevan idem esse quod Rephan, eo quod hoc idolon primitus nominatum & cultum ab Israelitis & Persis (ut passim interpretes confitentur & Rabbini tradunt) eorum lingua dictum sit Kivan, vel Kevan, quam vocem ut barbaram, cum non intelligerent He- bræi, levi unius literæ commutatione, sua lingua voca- runt illud Rephan, id est, Gigantem: quomodo Syri vocant Deum gigantem seculorum, quia ipse ut gi- gas omnia mundi æque ac temporum spatia, sua immen- sitate & æternitate ambit & complectitur: aut certe Raphan, id est, Sanatorem, q. d. Hic est qui nos sa- nat & salvat. Unde ab eadem Hebræa radice di- citur angelus Raphael Medicina vel sanatio Dei. Ali- qui Codices pro Rephan legunt Rompha, quod Heb. dicitur רומפה, idemque est, quod celsitudo oris : forte idolum hoc habebat magnum celsumque os, ut habent pleraque idola prisca, quæ dabant ora- cula. Talia n. vidi in Vaticano, ac tale est celebre illud, quod juxta Ecclesiam S. Mariæ in Schola Græ- ca, sive in Cosmedim Romæ visitur, & vulgo vocatur Bocca de la verita, id est, os vel oraculum veritatis. Porro licet vulgus Hebræorum nomen barbarum Re- phan verterit, vocaritque Hebraice Rephan, Rem- phan & Rompha, doctiores tamen Hebræi retinue- runt originale Kevan quod literas, & levi puncto- rum sive vocalium mutatione, Hebræa voce vocarunt illud Kiun. Ita enim hic habet Amos, Aquila, & Symmachus. Nam Kiun deducitur à Radice כון quod significat paravit, aptavit, rectus fuit, direxit, verificavit, certificavit, firmavit, perfecit, decre- vit. Unde Kiun idem est quod paratus, aptatus, e- rectus, perfectus, dans vera certa & firma oracula ac decreta. Ludovicus de Dieu, è Claudii Salmasii suggestione, observat ad Act. Apostolorum c. 7. Æ- gyptios Saturnum vocare ῥηφὰν, & exclamat p. 69. Jam cecidit recepta illa apud omnes fere eruditos sen- tentia ῥεφὰν apud LXX. Interpretes corruptum esse ex Hebræo כיון pro quo ריין legerint, inde ῥεφὰν. Lau- dandi jam doctissimi prudentissimique interpretes, quod cum in Ægypto, in Ægyptiorum gratiam à Phi- ladelpho Ægyptiorum Rege vocati, Biblia in Græcam linguam transferrent, ignotum Ægyptiis Hebræorum כיון in notissimum ipsis ῥεφὰν transmutarint. Atha- nasius Kircherus in Oedipo pariter Remphan Co- ptice Saturnum esse observat. Quæ sententia lon- ge probabilior est, quam Grotiana. Nec dissimu- lat Dievius scrupulum, qui Israelitæ Saturnum co- luisse dicantur, de quo ita habet: Quod si scrupu- lum cuipiam moveat, quod Saturnum in deserto colu- isse Israelitas queratur Deus, quum in historia Mo- sis solius vituli vel bovis (David enim שׁוֹר vocat Ps. 106, 20.) fiat mentio: Resp. bovem, arationis præci- puum actorem, retulisse Deum, agriculturæ autho- rem & præsidem: eum autem antiquis gentilibus fuisse Saturnum, is enim fuisse fertur, qui in Italia Ja- num vivendi rationem & agrorum cultum docuit, cui pro accepta ista disciplina dimidium regni sui de- derit: atque eo nomine cum conjuge sua Rhea pro Deo fuisse habitum, quod in Italia plantationes, & in- sitiones, & educationes omnium arborum, omni- umque fructiferarum rerum culturam docuerit. Verba ergo Prophetæ ita interpretatur: Et porta- stis tabernaculum Molochi vestri, & Saturnum ima- gines vestras, stellam Dei vestri, quæ fecistis vobis. Cur צלמיכם imagines vestras, dixit in plurali? quia סכות tabernaculum, non tantum locus erat & re- ceptaculum, in quo inclusus Moloch gestabatur, aut circumferebatur, sed & ipsummet idolum erat, quippe imago cœli, in quo Sol sive Moloch, ma- gnus ille astrorum rex, & rerum sublunarium præ- ses, tanquam in tabernaculo continetur: unde Psal- tes Ps.19,5. לשמש שם־אהל בהם soli posuit taber- naculum in illis, שמים cælis. Exprobrat ergo quod & tabernaculum Molochi Saturnum pro imaginibus circumferrent, quis autem iste Saturnus? Stella, in- quit, Dei vestri, id est, quam vos pro Deo habetis & co- litis, sicut stellam Saturni dicimus, quæ est ipse Satur- nus. Stellam Jovis, quæ est ipse Jupiter נהר פרת flu- vius Euphratis, qui est ipse Euphrates. Denique Ste- phanum cum Amos ita conciliat: Vos portastis Sa- turnum, stellam Dei vestri, idem esse quod Lucas ait, ἀνελάβετε τὸ ἄςρον ☿ θεᾶ ὑμῶν ῥεμφὰν, ut no- men hoc proprium accusativi sit casus, ceu τὸ ἄςρον, tum quod terminatio Arabica id innuat, tum quod eadem ita sit constructio in Græco, quæ in Ebræo, solum dictionum situs variet, ac pro Kiun Arabico Ægyptiacum ῥηφὰν à LXX. Interpp. adhibitum, à Luca usurpetur. Alii tamen malunt nomen Kiun pro appellativo accipere. Distat id certe à nomine כיואן, & cur ab Amos Persicum aut Arabicum nomen idolo Ægyptiaco tributum sit? Derivant ergo id à כון paravit cum Buxtorffio & Marino: sic fundamen- tum notare volunt, vel basin affabre factam, cui im- positæ imagines idolorum fuerint, ut tanto melius de loco in locum possint transferri, & in templo re- poni. Vid. Junius in parallelis, Beza ad Act.7. Riebe- ra ad h.l. Mariana reddit apparatum idolorum ve- strorum. Alii per placentam exponunt cum Avena- rio, Pagnino, Vatablo & R. Dav. Kimchio. Theodotion transtulit ἀμαύρωσιν, id est, obscuritatem, vocem er- go illam omissam, & nomen proprium idoli ῥεμ- φὰν adjectum à Stephano, quod apud Prophetam non extaret, quod nonnulli à nomine loci alicujus defumtum volunt, nempe Ῥεφὰν vel Ῥεμφὰν 1. Macc. 5, 37. quod oppidum in Ammonitarum fini- bus situm, cui Deus tutelaris præfuerit Rephan vel Remphan. Favet huic sententiæ positus vocum: Portastis TABERNACULUM MOLOCH VE- STRI, & BASAN aliarum IMAGINUM VE- STRARUM, sydus quoque Deorum vestrorum, quas fecistis vobis. Consonant ita Lucæ verba, κ͵ ἀνελά- βετε τὴν σκηνὴν τᾶ μολὸχ ἡμῶν (quæ exacte E- bræa referunt) κ͵ τὸ ἄςρον τᾶ θεᾶ ὑμῶν sydus Dei vestri, τὰς τύπες, ὃς ἐποιήσατε, figuras, quas feci- stis. Lecticam, in qua portata fuit Molochi imago, intelligit voce Sicuth, & prolixus de illa est Selde- nus l. 1. c. 6. p. 199. Si vox Kiun per apparatum red- datur, ex illo imaginum apparatu Remphan ceu præcipuum idolum designari dicetur, ut expres- so à Stephano apparatu imaginum per vocem stellæ solum τύπος Dei ipsorum nominetur, quem Amos nomine non designarat. Quæ fuerit hæc stella, inquit B. Lutherus, ex Scriptura colligi non potest, Stephanus in Actis appellat sidus idoli Rem- phan. Neque huic interpretationi, qua vox illa, ut appellativum nomen accipitur, adversa fue- rit illa Ægyptiaca vocis Remphan acceptio pro Sa- turno. Ideoque & Molochi tabernaculum, atque in illo Molochum suum & apparatum imaginum sua- rum, atque imprimis Remphan Saturnum, sidus Dei sui, vel sidus, quod pro Deo suo colebant, portasse dicentur, imagines nempe illas, quas sibi cultus causa fecerunt. Si quis Molochum etiam Saturnum fu- isse dicat, occurrit Dievius: Nec est, quod turbet quempiam, quod supra Saturnum cum Molocho con- fuderimus: Propheta autem & Lucas hos Deos di- stinguant, & plurali numero imagines vocent. Tan- ta enim fuit priscorum ad augendum Deorum nume- rum propensio, ut sola nominis imaginisve variatio ad unum,eundemque Deum, Deamve in plures discer- pendum sufficeret. Isis, Lucina, Diana, Trivia, He- cate, variæ erant Deæ, quum tamen unius Lunæ diversa solum essent nomina. De quo qui plura vult, videat de Diis Syris Prolegomen.caput tertium Cl. Seldeni. Scaligero libr. 1. ad Manil. Remphan idem est, quod רעם פעם Jupiter βροντὲυς vel ζεὺς βροντιαῖος tonitrualis, sive tonitruum Autor. Riebera censet etiam fuisse Jovem qui habuerit stellam in vertice. Alii Martem fuisse existimant. Vossius l. 2. de idol. c.23. Remphan (ut & Chium) Lunam es- se vult. Mercerus in commentario exponit de Lu- cifero, aut Venere. Quam Hieronymi, Remigii, Al- berti M. Bedæ, Lyrani sententiam fuisse refert Cor- nelius à Lapide, atque ex eo probat, quod hanc stel- lam quasi cæli Reginam coluerint olim Syri, teste S. Hieronymo in vita S. Hilarion, atque etiamnum colant Saraceni, quodque Giraldus Syntagm. 13. ex Æliano & aliis doceat, Venerem Uraniam, id est, cœlestem, quæ videatur esse Lucifer, cultam fuisse ab Ægyptiis, Phœnicibus & Assyriis, ac quod Luci- fer dictus Kiun sit à כון ardere, urere, & ejusmodi plures ejus sunt conjecturæ. Ita Sanchez hic, & Act. 7. censet Moloch esse solem, Rempham Lucife- rum. Hinc, Stella, ait, Luciferi posita erat in fron- te Moloch, quia Lucifer Solem orientem antecedit, Sol enim est Moloch, id est, Rex stellarum. Si hæc senten- tia admittatur, Moloch fuisse Solem, Remphan Luciferum, causa elucesces, cur Remphan ita de- scribatur Sydus Dei vestri, quod Lucifer stella cre- dita fuerit Molochi vel Solis Regis stellarum. Giraldus in Syntagm. libr. de Hercule, censet Rephan esse nomen Herculis, ac significare gigantem ab Ebr. Repha Patre gigantum, unde gigantes dicti sint Re- phaim, eundemque à gentilibus etiam Ebræa voce Con vel Kiun appellatum h. e. statorem vel erectum & excelsum.

In hac varietate Ludov. de Dieu præferenda videtur sententia, quod Remphan Saturnus sit, quemadmodum etiam in Critic. Sacr. observavi- mus pag. 27. Quem vero à Moloch fortassis re- ctius hic distinguemus, ut hoc nomine Sol designa- tus fuerit. Nam Molochum Ammonitarum fuisse idolum, qui βασιλεὺς θεῶν Rex Deorum dictus, in Phœnicum vetustissima Theologia Adod etiam nuncupatus fuerit, ex Sanchoniathone Philonem Bi- bliensem apud Eusebium testari, & à Syris cultum fuisse docet Seldenus l. 1. Synt. c. 6. p. 176. atque ob- servat imprimis, quod effigies utriusque & Adodi & Molochi easdem fere memorent Scriptores vetu- sti, & ad unum Solem exprimendum fictas, & quod Scaliger in Exercit. Solem Persice Adad vocatum esse, notarit. Non ergo pro certo aut indubitato ha- bendum, quod assumit Groti9, Moloch & Rephan ad idem sidus relatos fuisse. Nec probanda nova quam ab Ebræo textu diversam invehere vult, interpun- ctio; dum ita reddit: Et Kiun imaginem vestram stellæ: deos vestros, quos fecistis vobis. In Ebræo e- nim ita habetur, & Kiun imaginum vestrarum (in

(in plurali) stellam Dei vestri, vel deorum vestrorum: אשר quod pronomen videtur sese non ad Deos, sed ad superiora omnia referre: ad imagines certe refertur à LXX. & S. Stephano τὲς τύπες ἑς ἐποιήσατε. Hæc de vocibus.

Quod ad rem ipsam, quonam tempore ista gesta sint, refert ea Grotius ad præsentia Amosi tempo- ra, ideo particulam ו non sensu copulativo, sed dis- junctivo accipit. Nunc vero etiam tabernaculum, id est ναΐσκον Molochi Dei vestri portastis, id est, porta- bitis, sensu prophetico q. d. transferam vos trans Da- mascum in Assyriam, ibique Assyrii cogent vos captivos humeris portare Moloch; alii ad præterita tempora ea spectare admittunt, & ad cultum vituli aurei in de- serto referunt, cum Hieronymo, Theodoreto, Remi- gio, Ruperto in h. l. & Oecumenio ad Actor. 7. sed è concione Stephani manifestum est, distingui hunc cultum, quo permisit eos Deus servire militiæ cæli, à cultu vituli; nec minus etiam luculentum ex hoc loco Prophetico, collatis quoque Stephani verbis, non vaticinari Prophetam de futuris, sed sistere Israelitis delicta, quibus jam inde à defectione in deserto sese obnoxios fecerant, quibus tandem mi- nitatur abductionem. Neque facile admittunt verba Stephani Proto-Martyris, ut idololatria illa restringatur solum ad Amosi tempora: siquidem Israelitis perpetuam ipsorum prævaricationem, apostasiam, & idololatriam ab exitu ex Ægypto exprobrat, ut è vers. 51. imprimis liquet. Utut ergo minime excludamus Amosi tempora, ad ea tamen sola hæc restringi cum Grotio non admittimus. Neque vero necessum est, ut cum nonnullis ea so- lum referamus ad 40. annos in deserto transactos; nam sunt distincta accusationis capita, quod neque tum UNI Deo servierint, & ex eo etiam non raro progressi sint eo idololatrias & impietatis, ut Molochi quoque tabernaculum portaverint vel assumserint. Quod Lyranus factum dicit in terra sancta, cum ei- dem servivit Salomo 1. Reg. 11, 5. alii cum Ribera in deserto, cum fornicati sunt cum filiabus Moab, & Baal Phegor coluerunt Num. 25, 1. siquidem Jose- phus l. 4. Antiq. c. 6. autor sit, eos tunc non unum, sed multos Deos coluisse & Ammonitæ vicini ac cogna- ti fuerint Moabitis. Conjungi illa possunt probe, & alia insuper cultus istius idololatrici momenta; quem Amosi ipsius tempore itidem viguisse ex Osea imprimis, qui ei σύγχρονος fuit, & multipli- cem Israelis idololatriam prolixe descripsit, colli- gere est. Non enim vocabant illi culpa, quibus minabatur pœnam Propheta, & cum præsentibus Israelitis, aut liberis eorum pœna illa incubuerit, ipsi certe à culpa secludendi non sunt. Coccejus hic, ut plerumque alias, singularis est, & ad taber- naculum, arcam & Cherubinos hæc refert, à quibus vero aperte ea distinxit Stephanus, ut ex Act. 7. v. 43. 44. patet: Ab ævo putatum est, stellas vel esse a- nimalia, vel esse corpora, quasi geniorum, quas intel- ligentias nuncupant, aut saltem eorum q. vehicula. Hinc cultus siderum. Quum Israelitæ à talibus opi- nionibus non essent alieni, & Deum in Christo non a- gnoscerent plerumque Cherubinos autem ut symbola angelorum haberent supra arcam; non injuria illos vocat per irrisionem imagines astri deorum ipsorum: vel arcam locamentum imaginum, propter similitu- dinem. Nam quum idololatræ simile quid exter- num haberent, quale Deus instituerat, quid, acceden- te idololatrico affectu aliud dici poterat de Israelitis, quam quod de Idololatris? Quæ quam aliena sint à verbis Prophetæ, & S. Lucæ, nemini ob- scurum esse, arbitramur.

Hæc recte se habent: Addimus solum Coc- ceji observationem: Neminem hic debet turbare, quod Babylon aliquando ad Ortum est. Si progre- diaris secundum meridianos, meridiana terræ sanctæ est orientalior. Vicissim si progrediaris secundum parallelos, sive latitudinem mundi, Babylonia, ut & Regiones Mediæ, aliæque, ad Aquilonem est evectior longe. Et hinc in Prophetiis, à septentrione aperie- tur malum,h.e. à Babylone. Ex Amoso perspicuum est agi de X. tribubus.Idem confirmat Stephanus,expli- cans τὸ ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ per ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶ- νος. Quæ explicatio non est loci pro loco positio,sed loci distinctioris pro indefinito. Communior & indefini- tior locus. Ultra Damascum, quippe tota cæli A- quilonaris plaga superans Damascum verbis Amosi indefinite intelligitur. Distinctior, ultra Babylonem. B. Gerhardus ita de conciliatione Stephani Act. 7, 42. 43. habet in h. l. Quod in v. 27. dicit Propheta, fore ut Israëlitæ deportentur ultra Damascum, Evangelista, fidem historiæ sacræ & rei gestæ verita- tem spectans explicat, quod non tantum ultra Dama- scum, sed etiam ultra Babyloniam deportandi fuerint, quippe quorum nonnulli tum in Persiam, tum in re- gionem Caspiorum longe ultra Damascum sunt abdu- cti. Confer eventum 2. Reg. 17, 6. cap. 18, 11. Esræ 7. v. 17. Idem de voce Remphan eorum probat sen- tentiam, qui eam loco vocis Kiiun à Stephano sub- stitutam ajunt: Alii, inquit, statuunt vocem כִּיוּן à Stephano esse omissam, & omnem idoli proprium esse adjectum, quod apud Prophetam non extabat; quæ sententia est omnium optima. Cui jam olim calcu- lum adjecimus in Critico Sacro p. 524. laudato à B. Joh. Ernesto Gerhardo in Comment. ad Acta A- post. p. 264. ubi Drusio inPræter. Vossio l. 2. de Ido- lol. c.23. Buxtorffio in Lexic. acCapello in spici l. p.75. dicam scripsit, quod LXX. interpp. affinitate lite- rarum Kaph & Resch decepti רֵיפָן legerint pro כִּיוּן Am. 5, 23. nostræque accedit sententiæ, ac stellam Ægyptiis ῥεφὰν dictam Saturnum esse ὁμοψήφως nobiscum statuit; confirmans hoc eo argumento, quod stellæ illi, quæ Saturnus dicitur nomen רֵיפָן 2. Reg. 5, 18. ab altitudine cesserit, quia רוּם Ebræis altum notat: & Saturni stella in altissimo orbe esse creditur. Juvat hic subjungere etiam Hottingeri suffragium in primitiis Heidelberg.de idolograph.V. Test. p. 392. confirmantis ῥεφαν vocem Ægyptia- cam esse ac Saturnum denotare, 1. autoritate ver- sionis N.Test. Copticæ, quæ ῥηφαν habet, 2. consensu tum Commentariorum Copticorum, in c. 7. Act. tum Lexici Arabico-Coptici, quod septem planetas ordi- ne recenset, & inter eos ῥηφαν Saturnum. 3. Quod כִּיוָן notans Saturnum Hebraice, Arabice, Persice, idem sit cum ῥεφαν. Conf. Bibl. Orient. p. 313. Addimus hic occasione idoli Moloch Rephan, & Kiiun, ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ ex eadem Hotting. Reg. 17, 31. Moabitarum Camosch iidem Saturnus, id est, Noachus. Sidoniorum Astharoth Venus est vel Luna 1. Reg. 11, 5.33. (Astartem lunam esse volunt Lucian. de Dea Syria & Herodian. l. 5. de Heliogab. Venerem autem Philo Biblius & alii:

Cornel à Lapid. ad Jud. 2, 13. gentiles inquit primi- tus adorabant Solem & Lunam: Romani vocabant Jovem & Junonem, Ægyptii Osiridem & Isidem, Sy- ri Baalim & Astaroth. Bonfrerius & Malvenda Astharoth Venerem dicunt. Nonnulli nomen hoc idem esse volunt cum אֲשֵׁרוֹת lucis, id est, idolis lucorum Jud. 3, 7. uti per metonymiam explicant, quamvis aliis potius ipsum numen vel idolum Asarab fuisse videatur 2. Reg.21, 7. c. 23, 6. Quibus vero an subscribendum sit, ita ut temper voce Asara numen vel Astartha Sidoniorum, nunquam vero lucus,quem Josephus innui ait, intelligatur uti Seldenus putat, merito ambigitur) Syrorum Gad est Sidus Jovis, Menath ipsi est constellatio Esa. 65. v. 11. His accedit Philistæorum Paalzebub muscæ imagine cultus 2. Reg. 1, 2. & Dagon seu piscis ma- gnificus. 1. Sam. 5, 4. Moabitarum Baal-Peor, id est, Priapus: Num. 23. Job. 22, 17. Assyriorum Nergal qui ex ejus mente ignis. Eorundem Nisroch na- vicula, vel navis Noæ esse censetur 2. Reg.19. ult. Jer.46,5. Bos est. Eorundem Thamuz Ezech. 8, 15. esse Baal Zephon ait pag. 402. Osiridem pag. 383. Teraphim imagines sunt ad certum astrorum influxum compo- sitæ, ut apud Arabes Talisman. Dii ἀλεξητήριοι, vel aberrunci, & fatidici. Gen. 31, 19. De quibus vero plerisque alii aliter. Vid. Seldenus in Syntagm. Kir- cherus in Pantheo, Pockockius in specim. Arab. &c. & quæ ad Jer. 19, 5.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. He confirms and foreshadows the destruction of the people.

To those trusting in their own strength, he presents as an example the more powerful kingdoms of Calneh, Hamath, and Gath destroyed, and he assigns the first place in abduction to the security and pride of the princes and nobles, and denounces the destruction of palaces and the metropolis and the ruin of families by oath because of injustice and trust in their own strength.

Lest it swell with pride, Sion is warned by fleeting kingdoms.

He had no reason for preferring the Chaldean translation to the Vulgate, which he otherwise esteems with the Papists, as if the Jews were being censured because they imposed upon their children the Gentile names of neighboring peoples, with whom they had entered into commerce and treaties. Blessed Luther and Osiander followed the Vulgate, with which Cornelius a Lapide laboriously compares other translations, and renders this sense: that they imitated the pride of Gentile princes, especially in their gait. For as they desired to be eminent among the nations, so also in their proud gait they did not yield to them in the least. Not inconveniently, however, do others render it, 'he who is named head,' that is, the chief of his own peoples, so that the princes in the individual tribes are noted, to whom the whole [people] had need to assemble. house of Israel. See Tarnovius & Cocceius on this passage. Some refer these to the mountains of Zion and Samaria, along with the Geneva and Italian versions, which were famous among the chief nations to which the house of Israel, as a metropolis, was accustomed to resort. Blessed Gerhard very well understands by 'head of the nations' the Israelite people, inasmuch as God preferred them to other nations by a singular calling and revelation.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. Excidium populi confirmat & adumbrat.

Confidentibus in fortitudine sua in exemplum potentiora regnaCalne, Hemath & Gad de- structa sistit, & securitati ac superbiæ prin- cipum & procerum indicit τὸ πρωτεῖον in ab- ductione, ac jur ejurando palatiorum & me- tropoleos destructionem & familiarumin- teritum ob injustitiam & fiduciam in ro- bur suum denunciat.

Ne tumeat, Sion per regna caduca monetur.

Non habuit causam præferendi Chaldæam translationem vulgatæ, quam alioquin cum Papi- stis æstimat, quasi taxentur Judæi, quod filiis suis nomina gentilia vicinorum populorum imposue- rint, quibuscum commercia & fœdera inierant. Vulgatam sequutus est B.Lutherus & Osiander, cum qua alias translationes operose confert Cornelius a Lapide, ac sensum hunc reddit; quod genti- lium Principum fastum, præsertim in incessu imi- tarentur. Nam ut eminere inter gentes cupiebant, ita etiam in superbo incessu ipsis nequaquam cedebant. Non incommode tamen alii reddunt, qui nominatur caput, id est, præcipuus suarum gentium, ut notentur Principes in singulis tri- bubus, ad quos convenire necesse habebat tota domus Israel. Vid. Tarnov. & Coccejus in h. l. Non nulli ad montes Zion & Samariæ hæc referunt cum Genev. & Ital. versione, qui celebres inter præci- puas gentes, ad quas se domus Israel, ceu metropo- lis conferre solebat. B. Gerhardus optime per ca- put gentium intelligit populum Israeliticum, utpote quem Deus vocatione & patefactione singulari cæteris gentibus prætulit.

## 6:2
Verse 2.

PASS OVER TO CHALANE) We thought from the sound of the name that it was Callinifum, and we spoke about that matter in the first book on the truth of the Christian Religion. Jerome, at this place, wishes it to be Ctesiphon. Pass over, indeed, so that you may see that their lands are in no way superior to yours, if only you knew how to preserve your own affairs as you ought.

Cocceius refutes this: Grotius thinks Callinifum is a town on the Euphrates, to which that name remained until the times of Ammianus. Ammian. book 23. See Junius on Gen. 10, 10. But the most illustrious Bochart demonstrates that it is Καλλίνικον in Osroene. Jerome thought it was Seleucia or Ctesiphon. The Chaldean also brought this forth, and it was situated in Chalonitis, of which mention is made by Strabo, Pliny, Polybius, Dionysius, Priscian, as Bochart demonstrates. כלנה is mentioned in Gen. 10, 10; Amos 6, 2; Isa. 10, 9; Ezek. 27, v. 23. Some from the Greek version of Isa. 10, 9 called it καλάνης πύργον, thinking the Babylonian tower was being pointed out, which Bochart rightly refutes.

GO THENCE TO EMATH THE GREAT) Jerome, and others who followed him, think it is the city of Syria which was later called Antioch. We have said what seemed to be the case at 2 Kings 17, 24.

Cornelius à Lapide discusses at length whether Antioch is entirely being pointed out, and whether more than one Emath occurs in the Scriptures, or indeed only one, who can be seen here.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

TRANSITE IN CHALANE) Nos ex sono nominis Callinifum esse putavimus, diximusque ea de re libro primo de veritate Religionis Christianæ. Hieronymus ad hunc locum vult esse Ctesiphonta. Transite nempe, ut videatis, illorum terras vestris nihil præstare, si modo res vestras, ita ut oportet, servare noffetis.

Refutat hoc Coccejus: Grotius Callinifum esse putat oppidum ad Euphratem, cui id nomen manserit ad Ammiani tempora. Ammian. l. 23. Vide Junium ad Gen. 10, 10. sed Clariss. Bochartus demonstrat eam esse in Osroëna Καλλίνικον. Hieron. Seleuci- um, vel Ctesiphonta esse putavit. Hoc & Chaldæus extulit, & ea fuit sita in Chalonitide, cujus mentio- nem facit Strabo, Plinius, Polybius, Dionysius, Pri- scianus, demonstrante Bocharto. כלנה memora- tur Gen. 10, 10. Amos. 6, 2. Esa. 10, 9. Ezech. 27. v. 23. καλάνης πύργον dixerunt quidam ex Græca ver- sione Ef. 10, 9. putantes turrim Babylonicam indi- gitari, quod recte redarguit Bochartus.

ITE INDE IN EMATH MAGNAM) Hierony- mus, & alij eum secuti putant eam esse urbem Syriæ, quæ Antiochia post dicta est. Nos quid videretur diximus ad 2. Regum. 17, 24.

Antiochiam omnino indigitari, & an plures Emath in Scripturis occurrant, an vero unica tan- tum, Cornel. à Lapide prolixe differit, qui hic vide- ri potest.

## 6:3
Verse 3.

YOU WHO ARE SEPARATED UNTO THE EVIL DAY AND APPROACH THE THRONE OF INIQUITY) They will remove the evil day far from themselves. You, however, cause the throne of iniquity to approach. These lesser kingdoms will last longer than yours. For by your own deeds you voluntarily summon foreign masters upon yourselves.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

QVI SEPARATI ESTIS IN DIEM MALUM ET APPROPINQVATIS SOLIO INIQVITATIS) Illi longe à se removebunt diem malum. Vos autem facitis ut appropinquet folium iniquitatis. Diutius durabunt ista minora regna, quam vestra. Ultro enim factis vestris externos Dominos in vos accersitis.

## 6:4
Verse 4.

YOU WHO SLEEP ON IVORY BEDS) See L. Labeo, D. de supell. legata.

AND ARE WANTON ON YOUR COUCHES) You stretch yourselves out widely. Thus both the Chaldeans and the Arabs use this word.

YOU WHO EAT THE LAMB FROM THE FLOCK) That is, the choice one. Thus Veranius taught that those victims were called choice which were taken out from the flock. Macrobius mentions this in Saturnalia III. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QVI DORMITIS IN LECTIS EBURNEIS) Vide L. Labeo, D. de supell. legata.

ET LASCIVITIS IN STRATIS VESTRIS) Late extendimini. Sic & Chaldæi & Arabes hanc vocem usur- pant.

QVI COMEDITIS AGNUM DE GREGE) Id est, eximium. Sic hostias eximias dictas docebat Veranius eas, quæ eximebantur è grege. Meminit Macrobius III. Saturnal. 5.

## 6:5
Verse 5.

YOU WHO SING TO THE VOICE OF THE PSALTERY) You who chant to the sound of the nablium. פרט is properly for the Hebrews and Chaldeans what μινυρίζειν is for the Greeks. Ovid: Learn also to turn the genial nablia with a double palm: they suit sweet modes.

AS DAVID THEY THOUGHT THEY HAD INSTRUMENTS OF SONG) After the manner of David they devised for themselves musical instruments. Private individuals do this, which once had been the prerogative of kings. HAVE WE NOT TAKEN HORNS FOR OURSELVES BY OUR OWN STRENGTH? Have we not become victors over our neighbors through our own powers? See 2 Kings 14:25.

A NATION) The Assyrians.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QVI CANITIS AD VOCEM PSALTERII) Qui cantillatis ad sonum nablii. פרט proprie est Hebræis & Chaldæis quod Græcis μινυρίζειν. Ovidius: Disce etiam duplici genialia nablia palma Vertere: conveniunt dulcibus illa modis.

SICUT DAVID PUTAVERUNT SE HABERE VASA CANTICI) Ad instar David excogitarunt sibi instru- menta musica, Privati hoc faciunt, quod olim regum fuerat, NVMQVID NON IN FORTITVDINE NOS- TRA ASSVMSIMVS NOBIS CORNVA) Nonne per vi- res nostras facti sumus victores vicinorum ? Vide 2. Reg. 14, 25.

GENTEM) Assyrios.

## 6:6
Verse 6.

DRINKING WINE IN BOWLS) Namely, silver ones, which the Chaldean adds here. Bowls are more capacious cups: which very Greek word the Chaldean has placed here.

AND ANOINTED WITH THE BEST OINTMENT) For instance, with nard; for luxury, not for cleanliness or health.

AND THEY SUFFERED NOTHING OVER THE AFFLICTION OF JOSEPH) They are not moved by grief over the fracture, that is, the miseries, of Joseph: that is, the descendants of Joseph. They either oppress the needy themselves, or do not relieve those who are oppressed. Compare Ezek. 39, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

BIBENTES VINUM IN PHIALIS) Nempe ar- genteis, quod hic addit Chaldæus. Phialæ sunt pocula ca- paciora: quam ipsam vocem Græcam hic posuit Chal- dæus.

ET OPTIMO UNGUENTO DELIBUTI) Puta nardinis; ad luxum non ad munditiem aut sanitatem.

ET NIHIL PATIEBANTUR SUPER CONTRI- TIONE JOSEPH) Dolore non moventur super fractura, id est, miseriis, Josephi: id est posterum Josephi. Egenos aut ipsi opprimunt, aut oppressos non sublevant. Confer Ezech. 39, 4.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

THEY SHALL MIGRATE AT THE HEAD OF THE EXILES) Just as they were the first among the people, so they shall be the first among the captives.

AND THE FACTION OF THE LASCIVIOUS SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY) The banquets of those extending themselves far and wide shall cease. מרזח does not always signify a funeral banquet, but also a sumptuous one. This appears in Midrash Esther 1, 2. And thus Rabbi Solomon understands it, both in this place and in that of Jer. 16, 5. The books which the LXX used had it far otherwise, but less correctly.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

MIGRABUNT IN CAPITE TRANSMIGRAN- TIUM) Sicut primi fuerunt in populo, sic primi erunt in- ter captivos.

ET AUFERETUR FACTIO LASCIVIENTIUM) Cessabunt convivia late se extendentium. מרזח convivium non semper lugubre, sed & aliud sumptuosum significat. Apparet id in Midrasch Esther. 1, 2. & sic accipit Rabbi Sa- lomo, tum hoc loco, tum illo Jer. 16, 5. Longe aliter ha- buerunt libri, quibus usi LXX. sed minus recte.

## 6:8
Verse 8.

THE LORD GOD HAS SWORN BY HIS SOUL) By Himself. The Chaldean, by His word, as often.

I ABHOR THE PRIDE OF JACOB) Inhumanity is for the most part a companion of pride.

AND I HATE HIS HOUSES) Built from plunder.

AND I WILL DELIVER THE CITY) Samaria, concerning which above 1.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

JURAVIT DOMINUS DEUS IN ANIMA SUA) Per se. Chaldæus, in verbo suo, ut sæpe.

DETESTOR EGO SUPERBIAM JACOB) Su- perbiæ plerumque comes inhumanitas.

ET DOMOS EJUS ODI) Ex rapto structas.

ET TRADAM CIVITATEM) Samariam, de qua supra 1.

## 6:9
Vers. 9.

BUT IF TEN MEN SHALL REMAIN IN ONE HOUSE, AND THEY SHALL DIE) If after the land has been laid waste, they have fled into some remote villa, the pestilence will seize them there, so savage that it spares no one. Pestilence is accustomed to follow devastation, λιμὸν λοιμός. See Jerem. 24, 10. 44, 13. Ez. 6, 11. 12, 16. 14, 21. What I said concerning villas agrees well with the passage Ez. 33, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

QVOD SI RELIQVI FUERINT DECEM VIRI IN DOMO UNA, ET IPSI MORIENTUR) Si post va- statam terram, in aviam villam aliquam confugerint, ibi pestilentia eos comprehendet, tam sæva ut nemini parcat. Vastitatem sequi solet pestilentia, λιμὸν λοιμός. Vide Jerem. 24, 10. 44, 13. Ez. 6, 11. 12, 16. 14, 21. De villis quod dixi bene convenit cum loco Ez. 33, 27.

## 6:10
Vers. 10.

AND HIS KINSMAN SHALL TAKE HIM UP) To whom the care of the funeral pertains by custom.

AND SHALL BURN HIM) He shall not embalm, nor bury, for fear of contagion.

TO CARRY THE BONES OUT OF HIS HOUSE) To cleanse the house as soon as possible, with the body removed.

AND SHALL SAY TO HIM, WHO IS IN THE INNER PARTS OF THE HOUSE) In the courtyard of the villa, where gatekeepers are accustomed to be.

IS THERE YET ANY WITH THEE) Is anyone still living with you in this house?

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET TOLLET EUM PROPINQVUS SUUS) Ad quem cura funeris de moribus spectat.

ET COMBURET EUM) Non pollinciet, neque sepeliet, metu contagii.

UT EFFERAT OSSA DE DOMO SUA) Ut quamprimum domum repurget, ablato corpore.

ET DICET EI, QVI IN PENETRALIBUS DO- MUS EST) In corte villæ, ubi esse solent janitores.

NUMQVID ADHUC EST PENES TE) An quis adhuc tecum in domo hac vivit?

## 6:11
Vers. 11.

AND HE SHALL ANSWER: IT IS THE END) All have been consumed by the disease.

AND SHALL SAY TO HIM) This further.

BE SILENT AND DO NOT REMEMBER THE NAME OF THE LORD) Be silent, because it is not the time to commemorate the name of the Lord. Prayers would be in vain; for we too must die.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET RESPONDEBIT: FINIS EST) Omnes absum- pti morbo.

ET DICET EI) Hoc amplius.

TACE ET NON RECORDERIS NOMINIS DOMINI) Tace, quia non est tempus ad commemorandum nomen Domini. Frustra essent preces; nam & nobis mo- riendum est.

## 6:12
Vers. 12.

FOR BEHOLD THE LORD WILL COMMAND) The words of the Prophet. He uses the Assyrians just as a master uses those whom he commands.

AND HE WILL STRIKE) Through the Assyrians.

THE GREATER HOUSE WITH RUINS) The kingdom of the ten tribes, so that nothing remains. The time of Shalmaneser is being referred to.

AND THE LESSER HOUSE WITH BREACHES) He will afflict the kingdom of the two tribes not with destruction, but with heavy damage, namely through Sennacherib; this people will not perish. For Jerusalem will be safe, and those who have fled there. From these the nation will be restored.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QVIA ECCE DOMINUS MANDABIT) Verba Prophetæ. Assyriis ita utitur ac herus iis, quibus imperat.

ET PERCUTIET) Per Assyrios.

DOMUM MAJOREM RUINIS) Regnum decem tribuum, ita ut nihil supersit. Tempus Salmanassaris respicitur.

ET DOMINUM MINOREM SCISSIONIBUS) Non exitio, sed gravi damno, afficiet regnum duarum tribuum, nempe per Sennacheribum; non interibit hic populus. Salva enim erunt Hierosolyma, & qui eo confugerint. Ex his gens reparabitur.

## 6:13
Vers. 13.

CAN HORSES RUN UPON THE ROCKS.) Can horses run through steep places?

OR CAN ONE PLOW IN BUBALIS) In Hebrew: with oxen. Therefore, it must be repeated from the preceding, in steep places. Just as in such places horses and oxen are useless, so you are completely useless to God.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE TURNED JUDGMENT INTO BITTERNESS AND THE FRUIT OF JUSTICE INTO WORMWOOD) Force is carried out under the guise of law. For benefits, injuries are shown. See above v. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

NUMQVID CURRERE QVEUNT IN PETRIS EQVI.) An per abrupta cursare possunt equi?

AUT ARARI POTEST IN BUBALIS) In He- bræo: bubus. Quare repetendum ex præcedenti, in abruptis. Sicut in locis talibus inutiles sunt equi & boves, ita vos Deo plane estis inutiles.

QVONIAM CONVERTISTIS IN AMARITU- DINEM JUDICIUM ET ERUCTUM JUSTITIÆ IN ABSTNTHIUM) Juris specie vis peragitur. Pro beneficiis maleficia exhibentur. Vide supra v. 7.

## 6:14
Vers. 14.

YOU WHO REJOICE IN NOTHING) In your own strengths, which can be turned away in a light moment.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

QUI LÆTAMINI IN NIHILO) In viribus vestris, quæ levi momento averti possunt.

## 6:14
Ver. 15. AND HE SHALL AFFLICT YOU FROM THE ENTRANCE OF EMATH) This is the boundary of the land of Israel to the North. Num. 34:8. 2 Kings 14:35. Jerome said it was to the East, from which it is understood to have been situated midway between the North and the East. Jerome says this Emath was near the city of Epiphaneia, founded and named by Antiochus Epiphanes, and in his own time also called Emas, with the pronunciation of the letter ע softened, just as the Jews pronounce it even now.

Emath is not to be understood as near Epiphaneia, but next to Lebanon, which is placed as the boundary of the holy land for Emath in Deut. 11:24, which Marinus in his Lexicon calls Emath of Naphtali, because it was in the tribe of Naphtali. The maps of Adrichomius, Ortelius, and others show this: Compare Cornelius à Lapide on verse 2 of this chapter.

EVEN UNTO THE TORRENT OF THE DESERT) that is, even unto the stream of the Nile, which, coming from the Arabian desert, flows into the sea between Rhinocolura and Pelusium. Compare Num. 34:5, Joshua 15, and what Jerome has here.

It is not to be understood that the Nile is meant, but the torrent of the desert, Sichor, which separates the land of the Israelites from Egypt to the South and looks toward the west, Josh. 13:3, 1 Chron. 13:5, where it was a desert, Joel 1:20; Tarnovius proves this against Ribera. Since it is clear from the adjacent passages, the subject matter, and the opposite boundary itself, that the torrent meant here is the one that separates Judea from Egypt, which was conterminous to it toward the south and west: the Nile, however, by no means does this, since it rather divides Egypt itself.

PART II. Presents sermons clothed in types and visions, likewise legal, yet with an Evangelical promise subjoined.

SERMON I. THREE VISIONS AND THE PERSECUTION OF THE PROPHET ARISING THEREFROM.

CHAPTER VII. Against the people and Amaziah the Priest.

The prophet, having seen locusts devouring the grass, prays against the punishment, and again, having seen fire devouring the foundation, intercedes for the people and obtains grace; but having seen a plumb line that must be cast away, so that the sins of the people may no longer be plastered over, he predicts the demolition of the high places; he is accused of sedition by Amaziah and ordered to depart and no longer prophesy against Israel; whence he intimates to him the defilement of his wife, the destruction of his children, the seizure of his goods, and his death in an unclean land, and at the same time a second destruction for Israel.

The office of a prophet is considered a seditious thing.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET CONTERET VOS AB INTROITV EMATH) Is terminus terræ Israëliticæ ad Septentrionem. Num. 34, 8. 2. Reg. 14, 35. Hieronymus ad Orientem di- xit, unde intelligitur medio fuisse situ inter Septentrionem & Orientem. Hanc Emath Hieronymus fuisse dicit pro- pe Epiphaniam urbem ab Antiocho Epiphane conditam & dictam, & suo quoque tempore Emas vocatam emollita literæ יע pronuntiatione, quomodo nunc quoque Judæi eam efferunt,

Non intelligenda Emath prope Epiphaniam, sed juxta Libanum, qui pro Emath Deut. 11, 24. ter- minus terræ sanctæ ponitur, quam Marinus in Le- xico Emath Naphtbalim vocat, quia in tribu Naph- thalim fuit. Docent tabulæ Adrichomii, Ortelii, & aliorum: Conf. Cornel. à Lapid. ad v. 2. hujus capitis.

VSQVE AD TORRENTEM DESERTI) id est, usque ad rivum Nili, qui ex deserto Arabico veniens inter Rhinocoluram & Pelusium mare illabitur. Conf. Num. 34, 5. Josuæ XV. & quæ hìc habet Hieronymus.

Non intelligendum esse Nilum, sed torrentem deserti Sichorem notari, qui terram Israëlitarum ab Ægypto separat ad Austrum & respicit versus occidentem Jos. 13, 3. 1. Chron. 13, 5. ubi deser- tum erat Joel. 1, 20. adversus Rieberam probat Tar- novius. Quoniam ex locis adjunctis, subjecta ma- teria, & ipso opposito termino liquet, hìc intelligi illum torrentem, qui Judæam ab Ægypto, quæ erat ei versus meridiem, & occidentem contermina, se parat: Nilus autem hoc nequaquam facit, quippe qui Ægyptum potius ipsam dividat.

PARS II. Conciones typis & visionibus vestitas, itidem legales, subjuncta tamen pro- missione Evangelica sistit.

CONCIO I. VISIONES TRES ET INDE OR- TA PERSECUTIO PROPHETÆ.

CAPUT VII. Adversus populum & Amaziam Sacerdotem.
