Propheta visis locustis gramen depascenti- bus pœnam deprecatur ac rursus igne viso fundum devorante, pro populo intercedit, gratiamque impetrat; visa autem trulla cæmentaria abjicienda, ne amplius incru- stentur peccata populi, excelsorum demo- litionem prædicit, ab Amazia vero sedi- tionis arguitur, & discedere jubetur, nec amplius contra Israelem vaticinari; Vnde illi mulieris stuprationem, liberorum inte- ritum, bonorum ereptionem, & mortem in impuraterra, Israelique simul iterum exci- dium intimat.

Officium vatis res seditosa putatur.

## 7:1
Ver. 1. THE LORD SHOWED ME THESE THINGS) Also these things which follow. They agree, however, with Joel.

AND BEHOLD THE FORMER OF THE LOCUST) God was forming locusts, that is, an army, which you are to understand here as Pul.

IN THE BEGINNING OF THE SHOOTING FORTH OF THE LATTER RAIN) That is, in the spring itself. It signifies that at that time the state of Israel had begun to flourish again.

AFTER THE KING'S MOWING) After the fields had been mown by Ben-hadad, 2 Kings 13:3. After the disasters then received, the state of Israel had begun to flourish again, during the reign of Jeroboam son of Joash, as we see in 2 Kings 14:15. For גז in this place the LXX read גוז in their books. Aquila retained the Hebrew גזין: but scribes long ago corrupted it into γαζης.

Latin:

Vers. 1. HÆC OSTENDIT MIHI DOMINVS) Etiam hæc quæ sequuntur. Congruunt autem cum Joele.

ET ECCE FICTOR LOCVSTÆ ) Deus erat fingens locustas, id est, exercitum, quem hìc intelligē Phulis.

IN PRINCIPIO GERMINANTIUM SEROTI- NI IMBRIS) Id est, vere ipso. Significat eo tempore sta- tum Israelis revirescere cœpisse.

POST TONSIONEM REGIS) Postquam detonsi agri fuerant à Benadado 2. Reg. 13, 3. Post clades tunc ac- ceptas reftorescere status Israelis cœperat, regnante Jero- boamo filio Joasi, ut videmus 2. Reg. 14, 15. Pro גז hoc loco LXX. legerunt גוז in suis libris. Aquila Hebræum גזין retinuit : sed librarii pridem id corrupérunt in γαζης.

## 7:2
Ver. 2. WHEN HE HAD FINISHED EATING THE GRASS OF THE LAND) To enter the land in a hostile manner.

WHO SHALL RAISE UP JACOB, FOR HE IS SMALL) Who but you can save the people, so weak in comparison to the army of Pul? The Prophet speaks these things as if he were present at future events.

Latin:

Vers. 2. CUM CONSUMMASSET COMEDERE HERBAM TERRÆ) Ingredi terram hostiliter.

QVIS SUSCITABIT JACOB, QVIA PARVU- LUS EST) Quis nisi tu populum servare potest, tenuem adeo præ Phulis exercitu? hæc Propheta loquitur quasi fu- turis interesset.

## 7:3
Ver. 3. THE LORD RELENTED CONCERNING THIS) He brought it about that Pul, appeased by money, departed.

IT SHALL NOT BE) Devastation.

Latin:

Vers. 3. MISERTUS EST DOMINUS SUPER HOC) Effecit ut Phul pecunia placatus discederet.

NON ERIT) Devastatio,

## 7:4
AND BEHOLD HE WILL CALL FOR JUDGMENT BY FIRE) He will summon vengeance by fire. That is, by an enemy much more merciless than Pul had been: that was Tiglath-pileser. Such enemies are accustomed to be compared to fire.

AND IT DEVOURED THE GREAT DEEP) He carried away a great part of the Israelites. The deep, a great force of waters. The waters of the people.

AND IT ATE UP THE PORTION) The fields, namely. It ate, that is, it made desolate, it corrupted.

Latin:

ET ECCE VOCABIT JUDICIUM AD IGNEM) Vindictam advocabit per ignem. Id est, per hostem, multo inclementiorem, quam Phul fuerat: is fuit Teglathpha- lasar. Tales hostes igni comparari solent,

ET DEVORAVIT ABYSSUM MULTAM) Ma- gnam partem Israelitarum abduxit. Abyssus, magna vis aquarum. Aquæ populi.

ET COMEDIT SIMUL PARTEM) Agri nem- pe. Comedit, id est, vastam fecit, corrupit.

## 7:6
Ver. 6. BUT THIS ALSO SHALL NOT BE, SAITH THE LORD GOD) It will not be permitted to him to carry away all of Israel.

These things are correct, as regards the meaning of the vision, or the thing signified, what the Lord wished to show by the same, namely, after the disaster received from Ben-hadad, 2 Kings 13:3, where the kingdom of Israel had scarcely begun to flourish again, a new disaster would befall it through the army of Pul: which, however, the prayers of the pious would avert, so that a total devastation might not arise from it. With which the history of the Kings agrees. By the mowing of the King, therefore, that huge disaster brought upon Israel by Ben-hadad, King of Syria, is signified, who greatly afflicted Israel, so much so that in the time of Jehoahaz they did not exceed 50 horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, 2 Kings 13:7, which was truly a sharp mowing. But that he saw the grass mown by King Ben-hadad, and sprouting again through the latter rain, that happened under Jeroboam son of Joash, in the time of Amos, who restored the afflicted affairs of Israel in some part, 2 Kings 14. By the locusts, therefore, which he sees flying into the sprouting grass and devouring it, the army of Pul is adumbrated, which in the time of Menahem, King of Israel, invaded the kingdom. But it was obtained through the prayers of the faithful that, having received a thousand talents of silver, the hostile army left the land of Israel, 2 Kings 15:20. Wherefore, it is not with Lyranus, Clarius, Vatablus, and Montanus that famine and sterility, to be brought on by locusts, are signified, nor are the locusts to be drawn to Sennacherib and his hosts with Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, and Hugo: for these things which are signified did not happen to the kingdom of Judah, but to the kingdom of Israel: nor is it to be drawn to Shalmaneser, who devastated the ten tribes. For here is exhibited not a final devastation, but only a shearing with a state of regrowth.

But as regards the vision itself, by which such things were adumbrated, the Prophet in truth beheld locusts, at the beginning of spring, when all things germinate through the latter, or vernal, rain (as the morning rain is called by the Hebrews, which falls in the morning or at the time of sowing in October, so that the seeds may be moistened and take root in the earth), devouring the grass, seed, and herbage after they had sprouted again. B. Luther rightly: 'Da das Grummet auffgieng' [When the aftermath came up]. AFTER THE KING'S MOWINGS, after, that is, the first grass of the luxuriant grain in the royal field had been mown for the use and consumption of the beasts of burden, as most explain. The vision of fire is similar: because the Prophet truly saw fire: meanwhile, the thing signified in that vision of fire called to execute divine judgment is rightly explained by Tiglath-Pileser, who after Pul, like fire with immense heat, and ferocity invaded the Israelites, and an innumerable crowd of the people; namely, the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, situated in a lower place beyond the Jordan, as if in an abyss, and also a significant part of Israel on this side of the Jordan, the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and Zebulun, he led away into Assyria, 2 Kings 15:29. Who would have led away all the rest, had not God, moved by the prayers of the faithful, inhibited his ardor, as Christoph. à Castro, Cornel. à Lapide, and others have rightly observed. The explanations of others, whether concerning fire properly so called, sent into the land of Israel, or the heat of the sun drying up the abyss, or the Sea of Galilee, or a plague devouring a great part of the people, or even the slaughter and burning of Nebuchadnezzar in the land of Judea, are foreign, even if the latter, after Jerome and Remigius, Ribera and others have made their own. The slaughter signified here is that which is to be brought upon the kingdom of Israel, not the kingdom of Judah, and it is the same, namely, a military one.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SED ET ISTVD NON ERIT, DIXIT DOMINUS DEUS) Non permittetur ei, ut totum Israe- lem abducat.

Rectæ hæc se habent, quod ad visionis singnifi- cationem, vel rem significatam, quid eadem osten- dere voluerit Dominus, nempe post cladem à Ben- hadad acceptam 2. Reg. 13, 3. ubi vix reflorescere cœ- perit regnum Israelis, per exercitum Phulis novam illi futuram cladem: quam vero piorum preces a- versuræ sint, ne totalis vastatio inde oriatur. Qui- bus congruit Regum historia. Per tonsionem ita- que Regis ingens illa Israelis à Benhadad Syriæ Re- ge illata clades significatur, qui valde afflixit Israe- lem, adeo, ut tempore Joahas non superarint, nisi 50. equites, decem currus & decem millia peditum 2. Reg. 13, 7. quæ vere acris tonsio fuit. Quod au- tem vidit herbam à Rege Benhadat demossam, per imbrem serotinum repullulare, id sub Jeroboamo filio Joas factum, Amosi tempore, qui res Israelis af- flictas aliqua parte restituit 2. Reg. 14. Per locustas ergo, quas in herbam repullulantem involare, eamque depasci videt, adumbratus Phulis exercitus, qui tempore Menahem Regis Israelis regnum in- vasit. Sed fidelium precibus impetratum, quod acce- ptis mille talentis Argenti, terram Israelis reliquerit hostilis exercitus 2. Reg. 15, 20. Quapropter non cum Lyrano, Clario, Vatablo, Montano fames & sterilitas, per locustas inducenda, significata, neque ad Sennacheribum & agmina ejus locustæ trahendæ cum Hieronymo, Theodoreto, Remigio, & Hugone: nam hæc quæ significantur, non regno Judæ, sed regno Israelis acciderunt: nec ad Salmanassarem trahenda, qui decem tribus vastavit. Hic enim non vastatio finalis, sed tonsio solum cum reflo- rescente statu exhibetur.

Sed quod ad ipsam visionem attinet, qua talia ad- umbrata sunt, revera conspexit Propheta locustas, in principio veris, cum omnia germinant per im- brem serotinum, seu vernum (uti matutinus imber E- bræis dicitur, qui mane vel sementis tempore de- pluit in Octobri, ut semina rigentur, & in terra ra- dicentur) herbam, semen & gramina depascentes, postquam reflorescerent. B. Lutherus recte: Da das Grummet auffgieng. POST DETONSIO- NES REGIS, postquam sc. herba prima frumen- ti luxuriaris in agro regio, in usum & esum jumen- torum esset demessa, ut plerique explicant. Si- militer sese habet ignis visio: quia vere vidit Pro- pheta ignem: Interim recte explicatur res signifi- cata in illa visione de igne advocato ad exercen- dum judicium divinum, per Teglathphalasarum, qui post Phulem instar ignis ingenti ardore, & fe- rocia Isræelitas invasit, atque innumeram turbam populi; utpote tribus Ruben, Gad, & dimidiam tri- bum Manasse humiliore loco trans Jordanem, qua- si in abysso sitas, nec non insignem partem Israelis cis Jordanem, tribus Naphthalim, Aser & Zabulon in Assyriam abduxit 2. Reg. 15, 29. Qui reliquos omnes tum abduxisset, nisi precibus fidelium Deus flexus ardorem ejus inhibuisset, uti Christoph. à Castro, Cornel. à Lapide, & alii recte observarunt. Alio- rum explicationes, sive de igne proprie dicto, terræ Israelis immisso, sive de solis ardore abyssum, seu mare Galilææ exsiccante, sive de peste magnam populi par- tem devorante, vel etiam de clade & incendio Nebu- cadnezaris in terra Judææ, alienæ sunt, etsi hanc postremam, post Hieronymum & Remigium, Ribe- ra & alii suam fecerint. Significata hic clades re- gno Israelis inferenda, non regno Judæ, eademque bellica.

## 7:7
Verse 7. UPON A PLUMB WALL) In Hebrew: A wall of a trowel: that is, plastered with lime. This is the people of Israel, whose sins the Lord had long dissembled.

AND IN HIS HAND A MASON'S TROWEL) Which had often covered over the faults of that wall.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SUPER MURUM LITUM) In Hebræo: Murum trullæ: id est, calce oblitum. Is est populus Israel, cujus peccata diu Dominus dissimulaverat.

ET IN MANU EJUS TRULLA CÆMENTA- RII) Quæ sæpe muri illius vitia obduxerat.

## 7:8
Verse 8. BEHOLD I WILL SET A TROWEL IN THE MIDST OF MY PEOPLE ISRAEL) That is, I will cast it away.

I WILL NOT AGAIN PASS BY THEM) To plaster, that is, to excuse their sins.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ECCE EGO PONAM TRULLAM IN ME- DIO POPULI MEI ISRAEL) Id est, abjiciam.

NON ADJICIAM ULTRA SUPERINDUCERE EUM) Incrustare, id est, excusare peccata.

## 7:9
Verse 9. AND THE HIGH PLACES OF THE IDOL SHALL BE DEMOLISHED) All of them, so that nothing remains: by Shalmaneser.

AND THE SANCTUARIES OF ISRAEL SHALL BE LAID WASTE) Sanctuaries, shrines.

AND I WILL RISE UP AGAINST THE HOUSE OF JEROBOAM WITH THE SWORD) He calls the ten tribes the house of Jeroboam, in which, when the Prophet was saying these things, Jeroboam the son of Joash was reigning.

What is handed down here concerning the trowel regarding the Vulgate version, Grotius has from Cornelius à Lapide. The Hebrew אנך denotes a plumb line rather, although they say it signifies tin, and is then used by metonymy for a tin plumb line. Therefore, that level is indicated as being set in the midst of the people not to build them up, but to destroy them, Deut. 28:63, Am. 9:4, 8: Because when a plumb line is applied to a wall, many faults and defects are detected. The Israelite kingdom is therefore compared to a wall, skillfully built indeed, but very ruinous. For אנך the Chaldean puts דין, which Cocceius, with Drusius, noted corresponds to a plumb line, see Lam. 2:8, 1 Kings 21:13, observing that in Isa. 34:11, the placing of a plumb line signifies a judgment not only ordered, but also exact. By the SANCTUARIES of Israel, those things which in common opinion were such in Dan and Bethel are understood. HIGH PLACES are spoken of, not OF THE IDOL, as the Vulgate has, which Grotius neglected to amend here, but OF ISAAC, which the people had erected on the hills either out of a perverse emulation of Beersheba, or had built in memory of the sacrifice of Isaac. B. Winckelm. notes that in Hebrew it is not Iitzchak, which is the proper name of Isaac, derived from Zachak, that is, he laughed, but Iischchack from Schabak, meaning to laugh at, to despise, to hold in low esteem: so that by a deliberate permutation of a letter, he reproaches the people that they are mocked by those sacred rites: as if he were to say, the high places of mockery. Theodoret thinks they are called altars of laughter because the idolaters would indulge in banquets, merriment, laughter, songs, and games at them. Others say altars of laughter, that is, ridiculous, or worthy of laughter and to be derided, Jer. 10:15, ch. 51:18. BY THE HOUSE OF JEROBOAM is not understood his whole kingdom, nor the person of Jeroboam himself, but his son Zachariah, who was killed by Shallum, 2 Kings 15: v. 10. And therefore others have rightly rendered it, the sanctuaries of Israel shall be reduced to solitude, when I shall have first risen against the house of Jeroboam with the sword, which will be a sign of the remaining public slaughters.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET DEMOLIENTUR EXCELSA IDO- LI) Omnia, ut nihil restet: per Salmanasarem.

ET SANCTIFICATIONES ISRAEL DESOLA- BUNTUR) Sanctuaria, delubra.

ET CONSURGAM SUPER DOMUM JERO- BOAM IN GLADIO) Domum Jeroboami appellat de- cem tribus, in quibus cum Propheta hæc diceret, regnabat Jeroboam Joasi filius.

Quæ de trulla ad versionem Vulgatam hic tra- duntur, à Cornelio à Lapid. habet Grotius. Ebræ- um אנך perpendiculum potius notat, quanquam stannum id significare dicunt, & deinde per meto- nymiam adhiberi pro stanneo perpendiculo. Libel- lam ergo illam disponendam in medio populi non ad ædificandum eundem, sed ad destruendum Deut. 28, 63. Am. 9, 4. 8. indicatur: Quia applicato ad murum perpendiculo deprehenduntur multa vitia ac defectus. Regnum itaque Israeliticum cum mu- ro confertur affabre quidem exstructo, sed valde ruinoso. Chaldæus pro אנך ponit דין quod re- spondere perpendiculo cum Drusio notavit Cocce- jus, vid. Thren. 2, 8. 1. Reg. 21, 13. observans, quod Esa. 34, 11. positio perpendiculi significet judicium non tantum ordinatum, sed etiam exactum. Per SANCTUARIA Israelis ea, quæ opinione vulgo talia erant in Dan & Bethel intelliguntur. EXCEL- SA dicuntur, non IDOLI, ut vulgata habet, quam emendare hic neglexit Grotius, sed Isaaci, quæ po- pulus sive ex κακοζηλία Berfabæ in collibus ere- xerat, vel in memoriam immolationis Isaaci extru- xerat. B. Winckelm. notat, in Ebræo non esse Iitz- chak, quod est proprium nomen Isaaci, dictum à Zachak, id est, risit, sed Iischchack à Schabak ridendo, contempsit, floccifecit: ut data opera permutatione literæ, populo exprobret, se sacris istis irrideri: quadi dicat, excelsa irrisionis. Theodoretius putat aras risus dici, quod Idololatræ apud eas conviviis, hilaritati, risibus, cantibus & lusibus vacarent. Alii dicunt altaria risus, id est, ridicula, seu risu di- gna & deridenda Jerem. 10, 15. c. 51, 18. PER DO- MUM JEROBOAM non intelligitur totum ejus regnum, nec ipsa persona Jeroboami, sed filius ejus Zacharias, qui à Sallum occisus est, 2. Reg. 15. v. 10. Ideoque recte reddidere alii, sanctuaria Israe- lis in solitudinem redigentur, quum prius insurrexero contra domum Jeroboami gladio, quod erit signum reliquarum cladium publicarum.

## 7:10
Verse 10. THE PRIEST OF BETHEL) The successor of those whom Jeroboam the son of Nebat had instituted. AMOS HATH REBELLED AGAINST THEE) He is stirring up sedition. THE LAND IS NOT ABLE TO BEAR ALL HIS WORDS) Without grave disturbance, if he continues to speak in this way, the citizens will arm themselves against one another.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SACERDOS BETHEL) Successor eorum, quos Jeroboamus Nabati filius instituerat. REBELLAVIT CONTRA TE AMOS) Seditio- nem concitat. NON POTERIT TERRA SUSTINERE UNI- VERSOS SERMONES EJUS) Sine gravi motu, Si ita lo- qui pergit, civium alii in alios armabuntur.

## 7:11
Vers. 11. JEROBOAM SHALL DIE BY THE SWORD) The Prophet had not said this; but that the house of Jeroboam would die; that is, many of the people, of whom he was then king. AND ISRAEL CAPTIVE) Those who shall be survivors of the slaughter.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN GLADIO MORIETUR JEROBOAM) Non hoc dixerat Propheta; sed morituram domum Jeroboami; id est, multos ex populo, cujus ille tunc rex erat. ET ISRAEL CAPTIVUS) Qui de cæde erunt su- perstites.

## 7:12
Vers. 12. THOU THAT SEEST) You who call yourself a Prophet. FLEE INTO THE LAND OF JUDA) Since our calves displease you. See above 3, 14. AND EAT BREAD THERE, AND THOU SHALT PROPHESY THERE) There they will feed you well as a Prophet, since you are in agreement with their customs: --- Let Aeolus boast himself in that hall.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QUI VIDES) Tu qui te Prophetam dicis. FUGE IN TERRAM JUDA) Quando quidem vituli nostri tibi displicent. Vide supr. 3, 14. ET COMEDE IBI PANEM, ET PROPHETA- BIS IBI) Ibi te ut Prophetam bene pascent, puippe con- gruentem cum ipsorum moribus: - - - Ista se jactet in aula Æolus.

## 7:13
Vers. 13. PROPHESY NOT AGAIN ANY MORE AT BETHEL) Do not act as a seer in Bethel anymore. BECAUSE IT IS THE KING'S SANCTUARY) Sanctuary. The seat of worship. AND IT IS THE HOUSE OF THE KINGDOM) The seat also of the Empire, which you ought to have revered.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN BETHEL NON ADJICIES ULTRA UT PROPHETES) Noli ultra in Bethele vatem agere. QUIA SANCTIFICATIO REGIS EST) Sanctua- rium. Sedes cultus. ET DOMUS REGNI) Sedes etiam Imperii, quam revereri debueras.

## 7:14
Vers. 14. I AM NOT A PROPHET) I was not a Prophet; I did not profess myself to be such. AND I AM NOT A PROPHET'S SON) I was not a disciple of any of the Prophets: such as those who were, prepared themselves to receive the gift of Prophecy. BUT I AM A HERDSMAN) In Hebrew: I was, to be sure. PLUCKING SYCAMORES) That is, content with a little, so that you may not think I do anything for the sake of a feast. He understands by sycamores a wild kind of fig, which, unless it is plucked, is accustomed to be corrupted by gnats. Thus Jerome here.

Latin:

Vers. 14. NON SUM PROPHETA) Non eram Propheta; Non me talem profitebar. ET NON SUM FILIUS PROPHETÆ) Non e- ram discipulus alicujus Prophetarum: quales qui erant, pa- rabant se ad accipiendum donum Prophetiæ. SED ARMENTARIUS EGO SUM) In Ebræo: ego eram scilicet. VELLICANS STCOMOROS) Id est, pauxillo con- tentus, ne me dapis causa quicquam facere existimes. Sy- comoros intelligit agreste ficuum genus, quod nisi avella- tur, corrumpi à culicibus solet. Ita hic Hieronymus.

## 7:15
Vers. 15. AND THE LORD TOOK ME WHEN I FOLLOWED THE FLOCK) He took me, that He might give me commands.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET TULIT ME DOMINUS CUM SEQVERER GREGEM) Assumpsit me, ut mihi daret mandata.

## 7:16
Vers. 16. THOU SAYEST, THOU SHALT NOT PROPHESY AGAINST ISRAEL,) Do not prophesy. AND THOU SHALT NOT DROP THY WORD UPON THE HOUSE OF THE IDOL) To drop, for the Hebrews, is to act as a Prophet, Ezek. 21 v. 2. Mich. 2, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 16. TU DICIS, NON PROPHETABIS SUPER ISRAEL,) Ne vaticinare. ET NON STILLABIS SUPER DOMUM IDO- LI) Stillare, Hebræis est Prophetam agere, Ezech. 21 v. 2. Mich. 2, 11.

## 7:17
Vers. 17. THY WIFE SHALL PLAY THE HARLOT IN THE CITY) Symmachus is better, as Jerome judges, πορνευθήσεται, that is, she shall be defiled, by the enemies, to be sure. THY LAND SHALL BE MEASURED BY A LINE) As lands acquired by war are accustomed to be divided. Deut. 32, 9. AND THOU SHALT DIE IN A POLLUTED LAND) Not in the land of Israel, which God had dedicated to Himself. AND ISRAEL SHALL SURELY GO INTO CAPTIVITY OUT OF HIS LAND) Not some part of it, but all Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 17. UXOR TUA IN CIVITATE FORNICABITUR) Symmachus melius, ut judicat Hieronymus, πορνευθήσεται, id est, constuprabitur, ab hostibus scilicet. HVMVS TVA FVNICVLO METIETVR) Vt solent dividi terræ bello quæsitæ. Deut. 32, 9. ET TU IN TERRA POLLVTA MORIERIS) Non in terra Israelis, quam Deus sibi dicaverat. ET ISRAEL CAPTIVVS MIGRABIT DE TER- RA SVA) Non aliqua pars ejus, sed totus Israel.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

Amos, by the vision of a basket of summer fruit, prophesies the end of the Israelite people, and explains the change of songs into lamentation, on account of the oppression of the poor, injustice, contempt of the Sabbath, pride, and the bitterness of the imminent calamity, because the festivals are to be turned into mourning, and he predicts that young men with virgins are to be consumed by hunger and thirst for the divine word, and that the worshippers of idols shall fall without hope of resurrection.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Amos viso uncino pomorum finem populi Israelitici prophetat, ac canticorum in planctum commutationem, ob pauperum oppressionem,injustitiam,contemptum Sab- bathi, superbiam, acerbitatem imminentis calamitatis explicat, quod festivitates in luctum convertendæ, & præ fame & siti verbi divini juvenes cum virginibus con- ficiendos, cultoresque idolorum sine spe re- surrectionis casuros prædicit.

## 8:2
Verse 2.

THE END IS COME) An allusion in the word. For קץ is end, קיץ is summer.

I WILL NOT AGAIN PASS BY HIM) That is, I will not let him pass by unpunished.

Latin:

Verf. 2.

VENIT FINIS) Allusio in voce. Nam קץ finis, קיץ æstas.

NON ADJICIAM ULTRA UT PERTRANSE- AM EUM) Id est, impunitum transmittam.

## 8:3
Verse 3.

AND THE HINGES OF THE TEMPLE SHALL HOWL) The songs of the palace shall howl: That is, the joyful songs which were accustomed to resound in the palace shall be turned into howling.

IN EVERY PLACE SILENCE SHALL BE CAST) In every place (the enemy) shall cast silence: namely, by introducing solitude.

Latin:

Verf. 3.

ET STRIDEBUNT CARDINES TEMPLI IN DIE ILLA) Ejulabunt cantica platii: In est, in ejulatum ver- tentur læta cantica, quæ regiam personare solebant.

IN OMNI LOCO PROJICIETUR SILEN- TIUM) In omni loco injiciet (hostis) silentium: nempe indu- cta solitudine.

## 8:5
Verse 5.

SAYING, WHEN WILL THE MONTH PASS AWAY) The month shall come, חדש is properly ἕνη κ̓ νέα (the old and new moon), but by synecdoche it signifies a month: as in Genesis 29:14. And so it is translated in very many places, both in Greek and Latin, and no less so in the Chaldean. This month is understood as that of the harvest, when the grain is carried into the barns.

AND WE SHALL SELL WARES) Our crops.

AND THE SABBATH) That is, the sabbatical year, as the Chaldean takes it here, in which no produce came forth, the fields resting: and therefore, when it was finished, those who had not had enough money to provide for themselves before that year were forced by those who had storehouses to buy at a high price the things necessary for life.

Others wish to refer to the divine law concerning the new moon and the Sabbath, in which it was not permitted to devote effort to trade. See Exodus 20, chapter 24, chapter 31, 23. Leviticus 23:3, chapter 24, 2. Numbers 10, 1. 1 Samuel 20, 5. Nehemiah 10, 32, chapter 13, 15. Thus Jerome, Theodoret, Rufinus, Remigius, Lyranus, and most other interpreters, as if to say: you are so eager for profit that you are grieved that the feast of the new moon and the Sabbath is arriving, and you wish for them to pass quickly, so that once they are finished you may immediately return to your trade and profits, and sell grain at a high price according to your custom.

AND WE SHALL OPEN THE CORN) We shall release the grain that has been long withheld.

THAT WE MAY DIMINISH THE MEASURE) In Hebrew: Epha. They were making the measure of grain smaller than it ought to be.

AND INCREASE THE SHEKEL) Shekels were weighed. Gen. 23, 16. Isa. 55, 2. But they were making the other scale heavier. Thus they were profiting twice, both in the merchandise and in the money.

AND SUBVERT THE DECEITFUL BALANCES) And let us pervert the balances by deceit: so that it may be an ἔκθεσις of the letter כ.

Latin:

Verf. 5.

DICENTES, QVANDO TRANSIBIT MENSIS) Veniet mensis, חדש propriè est ἕνη κ̓ νέα, sed συνεκδοχικῶς mensem significat: ut Genes. 29, 14. & sic vertitur plu- rimis in locis tum Græce, tum Latine, nec minus apud Chaldæum. Mensis hic intelligitur τῆς συγκομιδῆς, cum frumentum in horrea portatur.

ET VENUNDABIMUS MERCES) Fruges no- stras.

ET SABBATVM) Id est, annus sabbaticus, ut hic sumit Chaldæus, quo nihil frugis prodibat, arvis quie- scentibus: ideoque eo exacto ii qui satis pecuniæ non habuerant, ut ante eum annum sibi prospicerent, coge- bantur ab iis, qui apothecas habebant, caro emere res ad vitam necessarias.

Alii respici volunt legem divinam, de novilu- nio, & Sabbato, in quibus non licebat mercimoniis operam dare. Vid. Exod. 20. c. 24. c. 31, 23. Lev. 23. 3. c. 24, 2. Num. 10, 1. 1. Sam. 20, 5. Neb. 10, 32. c. 13, 15. Sic Hieronymus, Theodoretus, Ruffinus, Remigius, Lyranus, plerique alii interpretes, q. d. ita inhiatis lu- cro, ut doleatis advenire festum neomeniæ, & Sabbati, ac optetis illa cito transire, ut illis transactis illico ad mercimonia & lucra vestra redeatis, ac de more ve- stro care vendatis frumentum.

ET APERIEMUS FRUMENTUM) Diu compres- sam annonam flagellabimus.

UT IMMINUAMUS MENSURAM) In Hebræo: Epha. Mensuram uridorum faciebant minorem quam esse debebat.

ET AUGEAMUS SICLUM) Ponderabantur sicli. Genes. 23, 16. Esa. 55, 2. illi autem lancem alteram fa- ciebant graviorem. Ita bis lucrabantur & in merce & in pecunia.

ET SUPPONAMUS STATERAS DOLOSAS) Et pervertamus stateras dolo: ut sit ἔκθεσις literæ כ.

## 8:6
Verse 6.

THAT WE MAY POSSESS THE NEEDY FOR SILVER) That we may acquire the needy through money: so that where they could not pay, they might give themselves to us into servitude, as was the custom of those nations.

AND THE POOR FOR A PAIR OF SHOES) Proverbial: that is, at a cheap price. Above 2, 6.

AND SELL THE REFUSE OF THE WHEAT) The sweepings of the wheat mixed with the wheat.

Latin:

Verf. 6.

UT POSSIDEAMUS IN ARGENTO EGENOS) Ut acquiramus per pecunias egenos: ideo ut ubi solvere non poterunt, dent se nobis in servitutem ut mos erat illarum gentium.

ET PAUPERES PRO CALCEAMENTIS) Prover- biale: id est, vili pretio. Supra 2, 6.

ET QVISQVILIAS FRUMENTI VENDAMUS) Purgamenta frumenti mixta frumento.

## 8:7
Verse 7.

THE LORD HATH SWORN BY THE PRIDE OF JACOB.) In Hebrew: by the loftiness of Jacob; that is, by those benefits by which He raised Jacob and his descendants on high.

God never swears by His benefits, cf. Heb. 6, 13. Therefore the Vulgate interpretation is to be preferred, He hath sworn against the pride of Jacob, that is, against the same. Which was the explanation of the LXX Interpreters, Theodoret, Jerome, Remigius, Hugo, Lyranus, and B. Luther. BY THE LOFTINESS OF JACOB, however, it will be permissible to understand Christ, who is the ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης of God the Father, and the glory of Jacob, and of all the faithful. And I see that B. Tarnovius has accepted it in this way: Note the Hebrew phrase, and indeed by the excellence of Jacob, in this place on account of the subject matter (since God swears only by Himself) by Himself or Christ, by whom Jacob, or all the Israelites, triumph and excel the other nations, as has been demonstrated above several times from c. 3, v. 2, and c. 9, 4.

following [verses] of the Epistle to the Romans it has been demonstrated, see Ps. 106, v. 20. Deut. 4, 7. 8.

IF I SHALL HAVE FORGOTTEN EVEN TO THE END ALL THEIR WORKS) Namely, lest you be considered as one who is. I have dissembled, but for a time.

Latin:

Verf. 7.

JURAVIT DOMINUS IN SUPERBIAM JA- COB.) In Hebræo: per celsitudinem Iacob; id est, per be- nefacta illa quibus Jacobum ejusque posteros in sublime extulit.

Nunquam jurat Deus per beneficia sua, conf. Ebr. 6, 13. Ideo præferenda vulgata interpretatio, juravit in superbia Jacob, id est, contra eandem. Quæ fuit LXX. Interpp. Theodoreti, Hieronymi, Remi- gii, Hugonis, Lyrani, B. Lutheri explicatio. PER CELSITUDINEM tamen JACOB intel- ligere licebit Christum, qui est ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης Dei Patris, & gloria Jacob, & omnium fidelium. Et video ita accepisse B. Tarnovium: Nota phrasin Ebræam, & quidem per excellen- tiam Jacobi, hoc loco propter subjectam mate- riam (siquidem Deus per se tantum jurat) per seipsum vel Christum, quo Jacob, seu Israeli- tæ omnes triumphant, atque excellunt reliquis gentibus, ut supra aliquoties ex c. 3. v. 2. & c. 9, 4.

seqq. Epist. Rom. demonstratum est, vid. Pf. 106. v. 20. Deut. 4, 7. 8.

SI OBLITVS FVERO VSQVE AD FINEM O- MNIA OPERA EORVM) Nempe ne, habearis qui sum. Diffimulavi, sed ad tempus.

## 8:8
Verse 8.

SHALL NOT THE EARTH TREMBLE FOR THIS?) Or, because of such things would the earth not tremble? that is, the public state.

AND EVERY INHABITANT OF IT SHALL MOURN.) Let him be in miseries.

AND IT SHALL RISE UP LIKE A RIVER ENTIRELY.) That is, however widely it may have spread itself, like a proud river.

AND IT SHALL BE CAST OUT, AND SHALL FLOW DOWN LIKE THE RIVER OF EGYPT.) It shall fail just like those trenches in Egypt, which sometimes have waters, sometimes lose them.

B. Tarnovius's Commentary has this more correctly: Every kind of calamity shall rise up, which often comes in the Scriptures by the name of waters, Psalm 18 v. 17 & 37 v. 6 & 69 v. 2, 16 & 124 v. 4, 5 & 144 v. 7, like a river into it entirely, so that there is an ellipsis in these words, or a hypallage frequently occurring in the sacred writings, by which it might be expelled and submerged (Hebrew נשקה for נשקעה, where the letter ע is suppressed by the Prophet on purpose, so that it might hint at an all-encompassing submersion, as Marinus thinks, Jerem. 51 v. 63, Apoc. 18 v. 21) and as if it were inundated, as the whole adjacent region is inundated annually by the river of Egypt, or the Nile, which κατ' ἐξοχὴν has this Hebrew name יאור and in this place is formed by aphaeresis of the פ into אור, see below chapter 9, 5. Gen. 41 v. 1, 2, 18. Exod. 1 v. 22 & 2 v. 3 & 3 v. 15. Isa. 19 v. 6 & 23 v. 3. But compare with the phrase Jerem. 46 v. 7, so that the sense of this place is: Just as the whole plain of Egypt. is oppressed by the waters of the flooding Nile, and is covered by the mud left behind: So my vengeance will oppress the secure Israelites, who now exult in light and a certain present happiness, but soon when darkness and calamities have overwhelmed them, they will mourn. Whence the magnitude of the evil is explained through the likeness of a thing which strikes the greatest terror. D. Winckelm. The universal punishment is like a flood overwhelming and taking men from the earth, just as the Nile, the river of Egypt, inundates the land annually. B. Luther in Comment. Just as the Nile floods monstrously: so I will bring a flood as it were upon this people, so that they may be dissipated among the nations, etc. Cocceius refers it to the final deletion of the King, and thinks that the emblem of the flooding Nile shadows it forth: and he snatches the following v. 9 to the darkness at the time of the passion of Christ, which was also done by Jerome.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NVMQVID SVPER ISTO NON COMMOVE- BITVR TERRA.) An propter talia non commoveretur terra? id est, status publicus.

ET LVGEBIT OMNIS HABITATOR EJVS.) In miseriis sit.

ET ADSCENDET QVASI FLVVIVS VNI- VERSVS.) Id est, quamvis late se diffuderit, ut superbus amnis.

ET EJICIETVR, ET DEFLVET QVASI RI- VVS AEGYPTI.) Ita deficiet sicut illae fossae in Aegypto, quae modo aquas habent, modo eas perdunt.

Rectius hic habet B. Tarnovii Commenta- rius: Adscendet omnis generis calamitas, quae a- quarum nomine saepe in Scripturis venit Pfalm. 18. v. 17. & 37. v. 6. & 69. v. 2. 16. & 124. v. 4. 5. & 144. v. 7. velut rivus in totam ipsam, ut sit in his verbis ellipsis, vel hypallage in sacris literis crebro occurrens, quo expelleretur & submer- geretur (Hebr. נשקה pro נשקעה, ubi litera ע studio a Propheta suppressa, ut omnimodam demersionem innuat, ut censet Marinus Jerem. 51. v. 63. Apoc. 18. v. 21.) ac velut inundaretur, ut rivo Aegypti, seu Nilo tota adjacens inunda- tur quotannis regio, qui κατ' ἐξοχὴν hoc no- men Ebræum יאור habet & h. l. per aphære- sin פ in אור conformatum vide infra cap. 9, 5. Gen. 41. v. 1. 2. 18. Exod. 1. v. 22. & 2. v. 3. & 3. v. 15. Esa. 19. v. 6. & 23. v. 3. Cum phrasi vero con- fer. Jerm. 46. v. 7. ut sit hujus loci sensus: Si- cut tota Aegypti planities. Nili inundantis aquis opprimitur, & luto relicto obducitur: Ita mea vindicta Israelitas securos opprimet, qui nunc in luce & felicitate quadam praesenti exultant, sed mox cum obruerint eos tenebrae & calamitates, lugebunt. Unde magnitudo mali per similitudinem rei, quae maximum incutit terrorem, explicatur. D. Win- ckelm. Universalis poena est quasi diluvium ob- ruens, ac tollens homines e terra, quemadmo- dum Nilus Aegypti fluvius quotannis inundat ter- ram. B. Lutherus in Comment. Sicut Nilus immaniter exundat: ita quasi diluvium super po- pulum hunc inducam, ut dissipentur in gentes &c. Ad deletionem Regis finalem refert Coccejus, eam- que emblema Nili exundantis adumbrare pu- tat: ac v. 9. sequentem ad tenebras tempore passionis Christi rapit, quod etiam ab Hieronymo factum.

## 8:9
Verse 9.

IN THAT DAY.) In that time. A Hebrew manner of speaking.

THE SUN SHALL SET AT NOON) It will please no one to lift their eyes to heaven because of the calamity.

AND I WILL MAKE THE EARTH GROW DARK IN THE DAY OF LIGHT.) In full light the earth will be as if beset by night: because nothing will appear there except it itself.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

IN DIE ILLA.) In tempore illo. More loquendi Hebraico.

OCCIDET SOL IN MERIDIE) Nemini libebit attollere ad coelum oculos prae calamitate.

ET TENEBRESCERE FACIAM TERRAM IN DIE LVMINIS.) In plena luce terra erit velut nocte ob- sita: quia nihil ibi apparebit praeter ipsam.

## 8:10
Ver. 10.

AND I WILL TURN YOUR FEAST DAYS INTO MOURNING.) Into dark days. See Hosea 2, ver. 11.

AND ALL YOUR SONGS INTO LAMENTATION.) Above 8, 3.

UPON ALL YOUR LOINS SACK- CLOTH.) Mourning attire.

AND UPON EVERY HEAD BALDNESS.) See Job 1, 20

AND I WILL PLACE IT) Supply the nation.

AS THE MOURNING OF AN ONLY SON) That is, as in mourning. The most grievous mourning is accustomed to be described thus: as Jer. 6, v. 26; Zach. 12, 10. Thus Catullus: When a bereaved mother weeps for her only child.

AND ITS LATTER END AS A BITTER DAY) The final part of that time will be by far the saddest: when not only will relatives be torn from relatives, but also children from parents, spouses from spouses. See the lamentation of that evil in the words of the Batavians in Tacitus, Hist. IV.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET CONVERTAM FESTIVITATES VESTRAS IN LVCTVM.) Dies festos in dies atros. Vide Osee 2. vers. 11.

ET OMNIA CANTICA VESTRA IN PLAN- CTVM.) Supra 8, 3.

SVPER OMNE DORSVM VESTRVM SAC- CVM.) Habitum lugubrem.

ET SVPER OMNE CAPVT CALVITIVM.) Vide Jobum. 1, 20

ET PONAM EAM) Supple gentem.

QVASI LVCTUM VNIGENITI) Id est, quasi in luctu, Solet sic describi luctus gravissimus: ut Jer. 6. v. 26. Zach. 12, 10. Sic Catullus: Orba cum flet unicum mater.

ET NOVISSIMA EJUS QVASI DIEM AMA- RUM) Pars postrema ejus temporis erit longe tristissima: cum non propinqui tantum a propinquis, sed & liberi a pa- rentibus, conjuges a conjugibus abstrahentur. Vide ejus mali deplorationem Batavorum verbis apud Tacit. Hi- stor. IV.

## 8:11
Ver. 11.

BEHOLD THE DAYS ARE COMING.) Namely, when Shalmaneser shall have arrived.

NOT A FAMINE OF BREAD, NOR A THIRST FOR WATER) Supply: only; in the Hebrew manner of speaking.

BUT OF HEARING THE WORD OF THE LORD.) Some prophecy, from which they might take counsel in straitened circumstances. A similar sense in Jer. 2, 9. Thus Maimonides in Guide for the Perplexed 2, 37, very well.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ECCE DIES VENIUNT.) Nempe cum Salmanasar advenerit.

NON FAMEM PANIS, NEQVE SITIM AQVÆ) Supple, tantum: loquendi genere Hebræo.

SED AUDIENDI VERBUM DOMINI.) Prophe- tiam aliquam, unde consilium capiant in rebus arctis. Simi- lis sensus Jer. 2, 9. Sic Maimonides Duce dubitantium 2, 37. optime.

## 8:12
Ver. 12.

AND THEY SHALL WANDER FROM SEA EVEN TO SEA.) From the Asphaltite [Dead Sea] to the Syrian Sea, as in Joel 2, v. 20; he draws a circle from the West to the East: thence again to the North, omitting the South, where Judea was.

SEEKING THE WORD OF THE LORD.) Explain as above in 11.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET COMMOVEBUNTUR A MARI USQVE AD MARE.) Ab Asphaltite ad mare Syriacum, ut Joel 2. v. 20. circinum ducit ab Occidente adOrientem: inde rursus ad Aquilonem, omisso Austro, ubi erat Judæa.

QVÆRENTES VERBUM DOMINI.) Explica ut supra 11.

## 8:13
Ver. 13.

FAIR VIRGINS AND YOUNG MEN SHALL FAINT FOR THIRST.) They will lose heart, destitute of all consolation.

The Prophet points out not only a desire to hear some prophecy, or to take counsel in tight circumstances, but a lack of the divine word, and a hunger and desire for the same. Because virgins and young men are said to fail and perish from thirst for the reason that they are destitute of all Evangelical consolation. For they were to be deprived of the true worship of God and the consolation of the divine word on account of their contempt for the word, in the Assyrian captivity. Jerome and others apply this to the miserable lot of the Jews, who after the final destruction were bereft of all consolation of the word. But the following verses concerning the oath in the sin of Samaria, by the god of Dan, and the way of Beersheba, teach that these things concern the kingdom of the ten tribes. Grotius seems to have followed Cornelius a Lapide, whose paraphrase is the same. If you listen to B. Gerhard, God seems most simply and literally to threaten the desolation of the region with these words, as above in ch. 5, v. 3, and to cut off the hope of posterity. Cf. Psalm 78, verse 63. Isa. 13, 12. Ch. 24, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

DEFICIENT VIRGINES PULCHRÆ ET ADO- LESCENTES IN SITI.) Animum despondebunt, destituti ab omni solatio.

Non tantum desiderium audiendi prophetiam ali- quam, vel consilium capiendi in arctis rebus, sed de- fectum verbi divini, ac famem & desiderium ejus- dem indigitat Propheta. Quia virgines & juvenes ideo deficere ac perire siti dicuntur, quod destitu- antur omni solatio Evangelico. Vero enim Dei cultu, & solatio divini verbi privandi erant ob ver- bi comtemtum, in Assyriaca captivitate. Hierony- mus & alii ad miseram sortem Judæorum, qui post excidium novissimum omni verbi solatio sunt or- bati, trahunt. Sed sequentia de juramento in delicto Samariæ, per Deum Dan, & viam Bersebeæ regnum decem tribuum hæc concernere docent. Sequutus videtur Grotius Cornel. a Lapide, cujus eadem est paraphrasis. Si B. Gerhardum audias, simplicissime & ad literam minari his verbis Deus videtur regionis desolationem, ceu supra c. 5. v. 3. & spem posteritatis præcidere. Conf. Psalm. 78. vers. 63. Esa. 13, 12. C. 24, 6.

## 8:14
Verse 14.

WHO SWEAR BY THE SIN OF SAMARIA) By the calf which is in Bethel, not far from Samaria.

AND SAY THY GOD LIVES, O DAN.) They swear: so surely as the God who is worshipped in Dan lives: there was another calf there.

AND THE WAY OF BEERSHEBA LIVES) May the worship which is in Beersheba live. To which place, situated within the borders of the two tribes, many Israelites used to run, in order to practice superstition there, where once God had appeared to their ancestors: as we said above 5, 5. The Hebrews call the worship of God, whether good or bad, a way: nor did the Chaldean take it otherwise.

THEY SHALL FALL AND SHALL NOT RISE AGAIN) No one will rescue them from destruction or captivity.

FINAL SERMON. A vision of the Lord, commanding that the threshold be struck, and promising the raising up of the tabernacle of David.

Amos, seeing the Lord standing upon the altar, who commands that the threshold be struck, and the lintels be shaken, and their avarice be visited, and their descendants perish by the sword, who will nowhere escape the hand of the Lord, nowhere hide themselves from the face of the Lord: which is directed toward their destruction, whose power in crushing the earth is described as that of the creator and Lord of all things, and is illustrated by the examples of other nations that have experienced it, yet with the addition of a promise that the whole posterity of Jacob will not be destroyed, even though Israel is to be scattered among the nations and those who are secure are to be killed by the sword. Whence is subjoined the Evangelical consolation concerning the raising up again and restoring of the collapsed tabernacle of David, that it may possess the Edomites and the nations: and the mountains shall drip with the sweetest must of Evangelical doctrine, and all the hills shall bring forth fruit, and the people of the Lord shall be planted and gladdened continually.

Who can be hidden from the Lord? Let conversion hope for pardon.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

QVI JURANT IN DELICTO SAMARIÆ) Per vitulum qui in Bethel, non longe a Samaria.

ET DICUNT VIVIT DEUS TUUS DAN.) Jurant: ita aut vivit Deus, qui in Dan colitur: ibi alter erat vitulus.

ET VIVIT VIA BERSABEE) Vivat cultus qui est in Bersabee. Ad quem locum, intra fines duarum tri- buum situm, cursitabant multi Israelitæ, ut superstitio- nem ibi exercerent, ubi quondam Deus majoribus ipso- rum apparuerat: ut diximus supra 5, 5. Hebræi Dei cul- tum sive bonum sive malum appellant viam: nec aliter sumsit Chaldæus.

CADENT ET NON RESURGENT ULTRA) Nemo eos ab interitu aut captivitate eripiet.

CONCIO ULTIMA. Visio Domini, cardinem percutiat, jubentis, & suscitationem ta- bernaculi David promit- tentis.

Amos Dominum videns super altare stantem, qui jubet, ut percutiatur cardo, & commo- veantur superliminaria, & avaritia eo- rum visitetur, & posteri gladio pereant, qui nusquam manum Domini effugient, nus- quam a facie Domini se abscondent: quæ ad perditionem eorum directa, cujus po- tentia in conterenda terra ceu conditoris & Domini rerum omnium describitur, & ab exemplis aliarum gentium quæ eam ex- pertæ sunt, illustratur, addita tamen pro- missione de non destruenda tota Iacobi posteritate, etsi inter gentes dispergendus sit Israel & gladio interficiendi securi. Unde subjungitur Evangelica consolatio de exci- tando iterum ac redintegrando collapso ta- bernaculo Davidis, ut possideat Idumæos & gentes: & montes stillent mulso dulcis- simo doctrinæ Evangelicæ, ac colles omnes fructus ferant, populusque Domini plante- tur & exhilaretur jugiter.

Quis Dominum lateat? veniam conversio speret.

## 9:1 Argument
Verse 1.

I SAW THE LORD STANDING UPON THE ALTAR) The glory of the Lord (that is, some light as an index of God) ascending from the Cherubim, and holding itself over the altar of burnt offerings, as if seeking many victims for itself, but human ones.

AND HE SAID) To the angel, as this Jerome. This vision pertains to the two tribes, as rightly noted by the Chaldean.

STRIKE THE LINTEL) The figure of the pomegranate, which was at the top of the Temple. By this is signified the slaughter of King Josiah, as the Chaldean explains.

AND LET THE LINTELS BE SHAKEN) The doorposts. This signifies the ruin of the whole nation.

FOR COVETOUSNESS IS AT THE HEAD OF ALL) You should more correctly take בצע as a verb, as the Greeks took it: he cut off the head of all, namely the enemy. He explains what he had said indirectly about Josiah: and the כ here is pleonastic, as often.

AND THE LAST OF THEM I WILL SLAY WITH THE SWORD) I will cause very many and very great slaughters to be brought upon the people, first by the Assyrians, then by the Chaldeans.

THERE SHALL BE NO FLIGHT FOR THEM) That is, escape, as the following indicates.

Latin:

Vers. 1.

VIDI DOMINUM STANTEM SUPER ALTA- RE) Gloriam Domini (id est, lucem aliquam Dei indi- cem) ascendentem a Cherubinis, & tenentem se super altare holocaustorum, quasi multas victimas sibi expeten- tem, sed humanas.

ET DIXIT) Angelo, ut hic Hieronymus. Visum hoc ad duas tribus pertinet, ut recte notatum a Chaldæo.

PERCUTE CARDINEM) Figuram mali punici, quæ in summo erat Templo. Significatur per hoc cædes Jo- siæ regis, ut explicat Chaldæus.

ET COMMOVEANTUR SUPERLIMINARIA) Postes. Id significat totius gentis ruinam.

AVARITIA ENIM IN CAPITE OMNIUM) Re- ctius בצע pro verbo accipias, ut Græci cepere: concidit ca- put omnium, hostis scilicet. Explicat quod de Josia per am- bages dixerat: & כ hic πλεονάζει, ut sæpe.

ET NOVISSIMUM EORUM GLADIO INTER- FICIAM) Faciam ut in plebem plurimæ ac maximæ strages edantur, primum per Assyrios, deinde per Chaldæos.

NON ERIT FUGA EIS) Id est, effugium, ut in- dicat sequentia.

## 9:2
Verse 2.

THOUGH THEY DESCEND EVEN TO HELL) Into the most hidden caves. Compare Ps. 139, 8.

THENCE SHALL MY HAND TAKE THEM) To destruction or captivity.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

SI DESCENDERINT USQVE AD INFERNUM) In abditissimos specus. Confer. Ps. 139, 8.

INDE MANUS MEA ABDUCES EOS) In exi- tium aut captivitatem.

## 9:3
Verse 3.

ON THE TOP OF CARMEL) Which overhangs the sea. We have spoken elsewhere.

IN THE DEPTH OF THE SEA) The Hebrew, in the bottom of the sea. The Chaldean understands the islands of the sea.

I WILL COMMAND THE SERPENT) Some sea monster, such as the Hebrews and Chaldeans call by the name of serpents and dragons. By such monsters, however, cruel kings are understood, as in Ps. 74:14.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

IN VERTICE CARMELI) Qui mari imminet. Di- ximus alibi.

IN PROFUNDO MARIS) Hebræus, in solo maris. Chaldæus insulas maris intelligit.

IBI MANDABO SERPENTI) Monstro alicui ma- rino, qualia Hebræi & Chaldæi serpentum & draconum ap- pellant nomine. Per talia autem monstra reges crudeles intelliguntur, ut Ps. 74, 14.

## 9:4
Verse 4.

AND IF THEY GO INTO CAPTIVITY BEFORE THEIR ENEMIES) Where they shall have been driven captive before their enemies.

I WILL COMMAND THE SWORD AND IT SHALL SLAY THEM) That it may slay. Even in the empire of the Chaldeans, many old men, the infirm, and children shall be slain, because it will not please them to feed men of no use.

I WILL SET MY EYES UPON THEM FOR EVIL) I will look upon them with a stern and hostile gaze.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET SI ABIERINT IN CAPTIVITATEM CO- RAM INIMICIS SUIS) Vbi ante hostes suos acti fuerint ca- ptivi.

IBI MANDABO GLADIO ET OCCIDET EOS) Ut occidat. Etiam in Chaldæorum imperio, multi senes, in- firmi, pueri occidentur, quod homines nullius operæ pa- scere non libebit.

PONAM OCULOS MEOS SUPER EOS IN MA- LUM) Torvum & hostile eos intuebor.

## 9:5
Verse 5.

AND THE LORD GOD OF HOSTS WHO TOUCHETH THE LAND) When the Lord God of hosts shall have touched the land, it shall melt away. That is, it shall be laid waste.

AND IT SHALL RISE UP LIKE A RIVER ) It is the same as what is above 8, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET DOMINUS DEUS EXERCITUUM QVI TAN- GIT TERRAM) Vbi Dominus Deus exercituum tetigerit terram, ipsa tabescet. Id est, desolabitur.

ET ADSCENDET SICUT RIVUS OMNIS ) Idem est, quod supra 8, 9.

## 9:6
Ver. 6. WHO BUILDS HIS ASCENT IN HEAVEN) He calls the royal throne an ascent, upon which one is accustomed to ascend by steps, 1 Kings 10, 18. 19.

AND HAS FOUNDED HIS BUNDLE UPON THE EARTH) Sheaves of crops.

WHO CALLS THE WATERS OF THE SEA AND POURS THEM OUT UPON THE FACE OF THE EARTH) Who calling the waters of the sea, pours them out upon the face of the earth: That is, he inundates the lands by his command.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QVI ÆDIFICAT IN COELO ASCEN- SIONEM SUAM) Ascensionem vocat solium regale, in quod ascendi solet per gradus, 1. Reg. 10, 18. 19.

ET FASCICULUM SUUM SUPER TERRAM FUNDAUIT) Manipulos frugum.

QVI VOCAT AQVAS MARIS ET EFFUN- DIT EAS SUPER FACIEM TERRÆ) Qui vocans aquas maris, effundit eas super faciem terræ: Id est, pro imperio terras inundat.

## 9:7
Ver. 7. ARE YOU NOT AS THE CHILDREN OF THE ETHIOPIANS UNTO ME, O CHILDREN OF ISRAEL) That is, I do not value you more than the Ethiopians, men who are barbarous and savage.

HAVE I NOT BROUGHT UP ISRAEL OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT, AND THE PHILISTINES FROM CAPHTOR, AND THE SYRIANS FROM KIR) Perhaps you trust in old benefits, but I have performed such things for other peoples as well. I led you out of Egypt, but I also led the Philistines out of Caphtor, (see Deut. 2, 23. and Jer. 47, 4.) and the Syrians from the region near Cyrrhus, to which Tiglath-Pileser drew them back, like old fugitives. Above 1, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 7. NUNQVID NON UT FILII ÆTHIO- PUM VOS MIHI ESTIS FILII ISRAEL) Id est, non pluris vos facio, quam Æthiopas, homines barbaros & feros.

NUNQVID NON ISRAEL ADSCENDERE FE- CI DE TERRA ÆGYPTI, ET PALÆSTINOS DE CAPPADOCIA, ET SYROS DE CYRENE) Fiditis forte veteribus beneficiis, sed talia etiam aliis populis præ- stiti. Vos eduxi ex Ægypto, sed & Palæstinos eduxi e Cap- padocia, (vide Deut.2, 23. & Jer. 47, 4.) & Syros e regione ad Cyrrhum, quo eos retraxit, velut veteres fugitivos, Te- glathphalasar. Supra 1, 5.

## 9:8
Ver. 8. BEHOLD THE EYES OF THE LORD GOD ARE UPON THE SINFUL KINGDOM, AND I WILL DESTROY IT FROM OFF THE FACE OF THE EARTH) That I may destroy. Whatever the kingdom may be, and from whatever ancestors it may come.

NEVERTHELESS I WILL NOT UTTERLY DESTROY THE HOUSE OF JACOB) I will not destroy by slaughter, as I have destroyed other peoples; I will destroy the kingdom, not the people.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ECCE OCULI DOMINI DEI SUPER RE- GNUM PECCANS, ET CONTERAM ILLUD A FA- CIE TERRÆ) Vt conteram. Qualecunque tandem sit re- gnum, & qualibuscunque e majoribus.

VERUMTAMEN CONTERENS NON CON- TERAM DOMUM JACOB) Non delebo internecione, ut delevi populos alios; regnum delebo, non populum.

## 9:9
Ver. 9. FOR LO, I WILL COMMAND, AND I WILL SHAKE THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL AMONG ALL NATIONS.) By my command I will move them here and there.

LIKE AS WHEAT IS SHAKEN IN A SIEVE) Wheat is not in the Hebrew: and what he calls a sieve is rather a winnowing fan, in which stones are separated from useless dust. The following verses show this.

AND THERE SHALL NOT FALL A SMALL STONE UPON THE EARTH) So also good men, although participants in the common evil, shall be saved from destruction.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ECCE ENIM MANDABO EGO, ET CON- CUTIAM IN OMNIBUS GENTIBUS DOMUM IS- RAEL.) Mandato meo commovebo huc illuc.

SICUT CONCUTITUR TRITICUM IN CRI- BRO) Triticum non est in Hebræo: & quod cribrum dicit, potius ventilabrum est, in quo lapides ab inutili pulvere se- gregantur. Ostendunt sequentia.

ET NON CADET LAPILLUS SUPER TER- RAM) Sic etiam viri boni, quanquam communis mali par- ticipes, ab exitio servabuntur.

## 9:10
Ver. 10. ALL THE SINNERS OF MY PEOPLE SHALL DIE BY THE SWORD) Wicked men, who refused to believe the Prophets: as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN GLADIO MORIENTUR OMNES PECCATORES POPULI MEI) Homines flagitiosi, qui Prophetis credere noluerunt: ut sequitur.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. IN THAT DAY) That is, afterwards, just as we have shown that τότε is used elsewhere.

I WILL RAISE UP THE TABERNACLE OF DAVID, WHICH FELL) The house of David, in Zerubbabel.

AND I WILL REBUILD THE BREACHES OF ITS WALLS) The Greeks: τὰ πεπτωκότα, that is, the ruins. For this noun is accustomed to be translated into Greek by πτῶμα and by κατάπτωμα.

AND I WILL RESTORE THOSE THINGS WHICH HAD FALLEN) τὰ κατεσκαμμένα, the demolished things.

AND I WILL REBUILD IT) That, supply the city of Jerusalem.

AS IN THE DAYS OF OLD) Such as it had once been.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN DIE ILLA) Id est, postea, quomodo & τότε sumi ostendimus alibi.

SUSCITABO TABERNACVLVM DAVID, QVOD CECIDIT) Domum Davidis, in Zorobabele.

ET REÆDIFICABO APERTVRAS MVRO- RVM EJVS) Græci: τὰ πεπτωκότα, id est, ruinas. Solet e- nim hoc nomen per πτῶμα, & per κατάπτωμα, Græce verti.

ET EA, QVÆ CORRVERANT INSTAVRA- BO) τὰ κατεσκαμμένα, diruta.

ET REÆDIFICABO ILLVD) Illam, supple ur- bem Hierosolyma.

SICVT IN DIEBVS ANTIQVIS) Qualis olim fuerat.

## 9:12
Vers. 12. THAT THEY MAY POSSESS THE REMNANT OF EDOM) Which was done in the time of Hyrcanus. Joseph. 13, 17.

AND ALL THE NATIONS, BECAUSE MY NAME HAS BEEN CALLED UPON THEM) All the nations upon whom the name of the Lord has been called. Among whom the worship of the true God once existed: such as the Ishmaelites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, of which the Maccabees subdued no small parts to themselves, Joseph. 12, 11. 12.

Grotius understands all these things in a carnal sense, concerning the house of David and the land of Judea being restored after the Babylonian captivity. But this is a notable perversion of the Evangelical prophecy concerning the restoration of the Church. For as far as (1) the subject is concerned, the matter here is not only about the house or family of David being repaired, or about Zerubbabel being raised up from the house of David, but about the tabernacle of David, which fell, which cannot be restricted to the family of David, unless it is understood concerning the kingdom of David which had clearly collapsed. Since that was not physically resurrected, it must be accepted concerning the spiritual restoration of the Church. Nor indeed is the discourse about the Jews alone, but as we warned before, also about the ten tribes. But how were the ten tribes restored after the captivity, if you understand it concerning a physical restoration? And therefore the Commentary of Tarnovius, p. 240, is not to be disapproved. Then (2) as far as the manner of the restoration is concerned, such a restoration is promised, which is to be such that the kingdom is to be recalled to a vigor and happiness not inferior to the former times, the vigor and happiness of the reign of David himself: I will restore the kingdom of David, AS IN THE DAYS OF OLD, so that indeed this new one may in no way yield to the former. That, however, was fulfilled neither in Zerubbabel, nor in any other, if you look at a physical restoration. And therefore Calvin himself, who is otherwise wont to willingly judaize, acknowledges that these things must be understood concerning the Kingdom of the Messiah.

Thirdly, the scope of all the Prophets, which is Christ, was not to be neglected by Amos. For to Him all bear witness, Acts 10:43, concerning whom Calvin's Commentary is correct: We know how often the Prophets, when they wish to give some hope to an afflicted people, propose the Messiah: because in Him were all the promises of God, Yes and Amen, as Paul says. And there was no other remedy for the dissipation than that God should gather the dispersed members under one head.

Fourthly, the time is considered, not of the captivity of the Jews, but of the destruction of the whole tabernacle of David, where almost everything has collapsed and seems to threaten total ruin. This was again observed by Calvin: The Prophet signifies not only that the throne of David will be overturned, but also that in an ignoble hut nothing will be intact, because it will dissolve into ruins, because all things will be subverted. Finally, he signifies that there will be sad ruins in the whole family of David. He speaks metaphorically of the tabernacle, as is sufficiently known: but yet the sense is clearer, that God will restore the royal dignity in the seat of David, just as before. The preceding verses confirm this sense, v. 9: 'nevertheless I will not destroy Jacob,' etc. For there is this sentiment there, according to the interpretation of B. Luther. The kingdom and priesthood being thus destroyed, I will gather and rebuild the tabernacle of David, which is miserably shaken and as it were collapsed, and there will come into it also from all nations those who are to believe, although they are not of the House of David. This passage, as I have said, is properly to be understood of the Kingdom of Christ. For by the tabernacle of David, understand the very people of David, the progeny of David, just as Isaiah in chapter 11 says to this effect: 'A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse,' that is, the kingdom of David, in which the Messiah was to reign. He calls it a root, however, because it was clearly despised, and had almost perished and ceased; at the coming of Christ, at least the lowest part remained, and it was like a dead trunk, which upon the coming of Christ was truly raised up, and the dead root flourished, and produced a most beautiful flower and fruit; all things were renewed and restored, all breaches were mended, and all things were made most beautiful. A wondrously elegant and beautiful prophecy, that he says from the most despised tribe of Judah, which had almost entirely ceased, he will build for himself an excellent Church of the elect, full of grace and the Holy Spirit. For he speaks of the abundance of the Spirit, in which also the whole kingdom of David was administered. For it had Princes full of the Holy Spirit, etc. These are the words of Luther, which serve to illustrate that remarkable restoration of the almost completely collapsed tabernacle of David. Add to these also the explanation of Cornel. à Lapide, whom Grotius has not infrequently followed.

Fifthly, some observe here an emphasis in the designation of THAT day or time. Concerning which B. Tarnovius says thus: Because in the O.T. they were ignorant of the point of time when He was to come in the flesh, and they inquired, 1 Pet. 1:11, they generally speak in a generic way of that day or time, Dan. 9:24, and of the time precisely appointed by God, Gal. 4:4, Joel 2:28 and 3:1. It is certain, therefore, that the Prophet looks to the time of the N.T., and not to the return from the Babylonian captivity, because he speaks to the Israelites, not to the Jews. But on that day of salvation and grace, 2 Cor. 6:1, Rom. 13:11, in Christ incarnate and having suffered finished John 19:30, when the shadows ceased as the body arrived Col. 2:17, Heb. 10:1, and the greater light of the Gospel shone forth, Rom. 16:20, 2 Tim. 1:9, 10, Heb. 8:6, how the law was an introduction to a better hope Heb. 7:19, I will raise up through the preaching of the Apostles the Church of Christ, which until now, both through the corruptions of false teachers Matt. 5:6, 23, and through the cruelty of tyrants, concerning which see the book of Maccabees passim, has greatly collapsed, and therefore does not seem to be a great and powerful building, but a hut that has fallen, and now threatens total ruin, see above ch. 5:2, I will restore its breaches, that is, the demolitions of each one of the particular churches, and I will rebuild it, so that it may be as glorious as it once was, on account of the Lord of glory present in the flesh, far more glorious than the former temple 1 Cor. 2:8, Hag. 2:8, 10. Thus he.

Sixth, what Grotius brings forward concerning the Idumeans and the nations subjugated by the Maccabees is too meager for such an august prophecy. The subject here is not a few certain people, but ALL nations: not those by whom the name of the Lord was once invoked, but those who are to be named after the name of the Lord, as is explained by James Acts 15:17. Which clearly indicate the calling of the Gentiles to the kingdom of Christ. Some render it thus: that they (the Israelites) may be heirs with the remnants of Edom, and all the nations which are called by my name, namely Christians from Christ Acts 11:16. But the matter comes to the same thing: for if you render it, that they may possess the remnants of Zion, what else is indicated than that the true Church, which will survive from the Israelites, is also going to admit and receive the Idumeans and all the nations?

Seventh, we have an undoubted interpreter, superior to all exception, St. James the Apostle, who, moved by the same Spirit, handed down to us the genuine meaning of Amos Acts 15:16, 17: that the Prophet is not dealing with Zerubbabel, or the people being freed from the Babylonian captivity, not with the Ammonites, Moabites, or Idumeans being subjected to the Maccabees, but with the conversion of the Gentiles to the Church: And the words of the Prophets agree with this, as it is written, After this I will return and will rebuild the tabernacle of David, which has fallen, and I will rebuild its ruins, and I will raise it up: that the rest of men may seek the Lord, and all the nations, upon whom my name is invoked, says the Lord, who does these things. What the Prophet therefore says, that they may possess the remnants of Idumea, has the same meaning as these words of James, that the rest of men may seek the Lord. For while others, even bitter enemies, such as the Edomites were with respect to the Jews, seek the Lord, by which phrase their conversion is expressed, they are brought into the possession and property of the true Church. Thus, therefore, the Israelite Church, which God had first chosen for Himself, when it was restored, received into its possession the rest of men, and all the nations; indeed, through them it was increased and restored.

To these arguments, finally, let the authority of both the Christian Church and also the sounder Jews be added, from whom Grotius here rashly made a divorce. For by a constant and almost unanimous opinion, Christian teachers have understood this oracle concerning the time of the New Testament: Jerome, Theodoret, Cyril of Alexandria, etc.

What of the fact that the Grotian gloss of this passage, and indeed even of other prophecies, was struck with an anathema in Theodore of Mopsuestia by Vigilius? About which Cornelius à Lapide could have warned Grotius, if indeed he had not willingly lent his ears to the Jesuits, and had not often plowed with their heifer. For when Theodore of Mopsuestia explained these words of Amos thus: In this place, he says, he predicts the return from Babylon, when they had Zerubbabel of the line of David as King; but James in the Acts of the Apostles transferred this passage to Christ, in whom the matter is brought to its true conclusion. This explanation of his was condemned under anathema by Pope Vigilius in the Roman Council, which is held in the Vatican Library, and from it P. Turrianus transcribed it on book 2 of the Constitutions. Apostolic, ch. 5, because he asserts that the passage, which is primarily and in the literal or historical sense explained in the Acts concerning Christ, is to be understood in the first and literal sense concerning Zerubbabel, and in the second and by way of translation concerning Christ: where, to omit other things, Theodore manifestly errs, since he makes Zerubbabel a king, who was only a leader of the people returning from Babylon. In a similar way, the same Theodore thought that all the oracles which were published literally concerning Christ historically pertained to David, Hezekiah, Zerubbabel, and the Jews; but were adapted to Christ by the Apostles and Evangelists only by way of accommodation and from the event of the matter. This is what Vigilius condemns under anathema, and before him the fifth general synod, which was the second of Constantinople, had condemned, as is evident from its fifth session, and from Leontius, who lived in the time of the Emperor Justinian and recounts the errors of Theodore. This is Cornelius. It is strange that Grotius, otherwise very devoted to the Roman Pontiff, cared nothing for the anathema of either the second general Council of Constantinople or the Roman Pontiff. But here, and in other oracles, the commentaries of the recent Jews prevailed with him, from which, however, the ancients were far removed. For in the Talmud itself these things were understood concerning the Messiah, as is held in Pugio Fidei, part 3, Dist. 3, ch. 16, p. 672, and ch. 10, p. 683, from the Book Sanhedrin, ch. Chelek.

Latin:

Vers. 12. VT POSSIDEANT RELIQVIAS IDU- MÆÆ) Quod factum Hyrcani tempore. Joseph. 13, 17.

ET OMNES NATIONES, EO QVOD INVO- CATVM SIT NOMEN MEVM SVPER EOS) Omnes nationes, super quas est invocatum nomen Domini. Penes quas olim fuit veri Dei cultus: quales sunt Ismaelitæ, Ammoni- tæ, Moabitæ, quarum non exiguas partes subjecere sibi Maccabæi, Joseph. 12, 11. 12.

Intelligit hæc Grotius omnia sensu carnali, de domo Davidis & terra Judææ redintegranda post captivitatem Babylonicam. Sed hæc insignis per- versio est vaticinii Evangelici de restauratione Eccle- siæ. Nam quod (1) ad subjectum attinet, non de do- mo vel familia Davidis refarcienda hic solum res est, aut de Zorobabele e Davidis domo excitando, sed de tabernaculo David, quod cecidit, quod ad fami- liam Davidis restringi non potest, quin de regno Davidis plane collapso intelligendum. Quod cum corporaliter resuscitatum non sit, de spirituali Ec- clesiæ instauratione id accipiendum. Nec vero de Judæis solis, sed uti monuimus antea, etiam de de- cem tribubus sermo est. At quomodo decem tribus restauratæ sunt post captivitatem, si de corporali restauratione intelligas? Ideoque non improban- dus Tarnovii Commentarius p. 240. Deinde (2) quod ad modum restaurationis attinet, talis ea pro- mittitur, quæ ad vigorem & felicitatem non infe- riorem priorum temporum, regiminis ipsius Da- vidis, vigore & felicitate revocandum sit regnum: restaurabo regnum Davidis, SICUT IN DIEBUS ANTIQUIS, ut nempe priori nequaquam cedat hoc novum. Id vero nec in Zorobabele, nec in ullo alio impletum fuit, si respicias corporalem restau- rationem. Ideoque agnoscit Calvinus ipse, qui lu- benter alias solet ἰυδαΐζειν, hæc de Regno Mesiæ intelligenda esse.

Tertio scopus Prophetarum omnium, qui Chri- stus est, non erat negligendus Amoso. Huic enim omnes testimonium perhibent Act. 10, 43. de quo re- cte se habet Calvini Commentarius: Scimus quo- ties Prophetæ volunt spei aliquid facere afflicto popu- lo, proponere Messiam: quia in ipso erant omnes pro- missiones Dei Etiam & Amen, ut dicit Paulus. Et non fuit aliud dissipationis remedium, quam ut Deus collegeret dispersa membra sub unum caput.

Quarto respicitur tempus non captivitatis Ju- dæorum, sed destructionis totius tabernaculi Davi- dis, ubi omnia pene collapsa sint, ac ruinam tota- lem minitari videantur. Quod iterum observatum Calvino: Significat Propheta non tantum solium Davidis eversum iri, sed etiam in tugurio ignobili ni- bil fore integrum, quia ruinis diffluet, quia omnia e- runt subversa. Denique significat fore tristes ruinas in tota familia Davidis. Loquitur metaphorice de ta- bernaculo, ut satis notum est: sed tamen clarius sen- sus est, quod Deus restituet dignitatem regiam in sede Davidis, sicuti prius. Quem sensum superiora fir- mant v. 9. veruntamen non delebo Jacob &c. Est enim ibi hæc sententia, interprete B. Luth. Destructo sic re- gno & sacerdotio, congregabo & rædificabo taberna- cultum David, quod misere labefactatum & quasi col- lapsum est, venientque in illud etiam ex omnibus genti- bus, qui credituri sunt, quanquam non sint de Domo David. Hic locus proprie, ut dixi, de Regno Chri- sti est intelligendus. Tabernaculum enim David intellige ipsum populum David, progeniem David, sicut Esaias cap. 11. in hanc sententiam inquit: Egre- dietur virga de radice Jesse, id est, regnum David, in quo regnare debuit Messias. Vocat autem radicem, quia plane contemptum erat, & fere interciderat ac desierat, Christo veniente, infima sex saltem su- pererat, & erat quasi emortuus truncus, quod Chri- sto vero veniente suscitatum est, & floruit Radix mortua, & produxit speciosissimum florem & fru- ctum, innovata sunt omnia & restaurata, rupturæ o- mnes sunt resartæ, omniaque facta sunt speciosissi- ma. Mirum in modum elegans & pulcra Prophetia, quod dicit ex contemptissima tribu Juda, quæ fere prorsus desierat, ædificabit sibi egregiam Ecclesiam electorum, plenam gratia & Spiritu Sancto. De pomda enim Spiritus loquitur, in qua etiam totum regnum Davidis est administratum. Habuit enim Principes Spiritu S. plenos &c. Hæc Lutherus, quæ faciunt ad illustrandum insignem illam restauratio- nem collapsi fere penitus tabernaculi Davidis. Ad- de his etiam Cornel. à Lapide, quem non raro se- quutus est Grotius, explicationem.

Quinto observant nonnulli hic emphasin in de- signatione diei ILLIUS seu temporis. De quo ita B. Tarnovius: Quia in V. T. temporis articulum, quo venturus erat ille in carnem, ignoràverunt, & inqui- siverunt 1. Petr. 1, 11. in genere plerumque loquuntur in die seu in tempore illo Dan. 9, 24. & à Deo præcise constituto Galat 4, 4. Joel 2, 28. & 3, 1. Ad tempus igitur N. T. Prophetam respicere certum est, & non ad reditum ex captivitate Babylonica, quia Israelitis, non Judæis loquitur. Die vero illo salutis ac gratiæ 2. Cor. 6, 1. Rom. 13, 11. in Christo incarnato ac passo consummata Joh. 19, 30. quando corpore adventante cessaverunt umbræ Col. 2, 17. Hebr. 10, 1. & major Evangelii lux affulsit, Rom. 16, 20. 2. Tim. 1, 9. 10. Hebr. 8, 6. quomodo lex fuit introductio ad spem meliorem Hebr. 7, 19. erigam per prædicationem Apostolorum Ecclesiam Christi, hactenus cum per corruptelas falsorum Doctorum Matth. 5, 6. 23. tum per crudelitatem tyrannorum, de qua lib. Macc. pas- sim, valde collapsam, & proinde non magnum ac po- tens ædificium, sed tugurium, quod cecidit, ac rui- nam totalem jamjam minari videtur, supra c. 5, 2. se- piam rupturas earum, uniuscujusque puta Ecclesia- rum particularium ac demolitiones ejus restituam, & reædificabo illud, ut sit tam gloriosum, quam fuit olim, ob Dominum gloriæ præsentem in carne, longe gloriosius templo priori 1. Corinth. 2, 8. Hag. 2, 8. 10. Hæc ille.

Sexto nimis exilia sunt pro tam augusto vaticinio, quæ Grotius de Idumæis & gentibus à Maccabæis subjugatis affert. Agitur hic non de paucis qui- busdam, sed de OMNIBUS gentibus: non de illis, à quibus olim nomen Domini invocatum est, sed quæ à nomine Domini denominandæ sunt, uti ex- ponitur à Jacobo Act. 15, 17. Quæ vocationem gen- tium ad regnum Christi palam indicant. Nonnulli ita reddunt: ut hæredes sint (Israëlitæ) cum reliquiis Edomi, & omnibus gentibus, quæ vocantur nomine meo, Christi videlicet Christiani Act. 11, 16. Sed res eodem recidit: nam si reddas, ut possideant reliquias Zion, quid aliud indigitatur, quam quod vero Ec- clesia, quæ superabit ex Israëlitis, etiam Idumæos & gentes omnes admissura ac receptura sit?

Septimo habemus indubitatum, omnique exce- ptione superiorem interpretem S. Jacobum Apo- stolum, qui eodem spiritu actus sensum Amosi ge- nuinum nobis tradidit Actor. 15, 16. 17. non agere Prophetam de Zorobabele, aut populo liberando è captivitate Babylonica, non de Ammonitis, Moa- bitis, Idumæis subjiciendis Maccabæis, sed de gen- tium conversione ad Ecclesiam: Et huic concordant verba Prophetarum, sicut scriptum, posthac revertar & reædificabo tabernaculum David, quod decidit, & diruta ejus reædificabo, & erigam illud: ut requirant cæteri hominum dominum, & omnes gentes, super quas invocatum est nomen meum, dicit Dominus, faciens hæc. Quod ergo Propheta dicit, ut possideant reliquias Idumææ, eundem sensum habet cum hisce Jacobi, ut requirant cæteri hominum Dominum. Dum enim alii, etiam hostes infensi, quales Edu- mæi respectu Judæorum fuerunt, Dominum requi- runt, qua phrasi conversio eorum exprimitur, in possessionem & peculium veræ Ecclesiæ redigun- tur. Sic itaque Ecclesia Israëlitica, quam primum Deus sibi elegerat, quum restaurata fuit, accepit in possessionem cæteros hominum, & omnes gentes, imo per illos aucta & restaurata fuit.

His argumentis accedat denique tum Christia- næ Ecclesiæ, tum saniorum etiam Judæorum auto- ritas, à quibus hic temere divortium fecit Grotius. Constanti enim & unanimi fere sententia Christia- ni Dd. hoc oraculum de tempore N. Testam. intel- lexerunt Hieron. Theodoret. Cyrillus Alex. &c.

Quid quod Grotiana glossa hujus loci, imo etiam aliorum vaticiniorum in Theodoro Mopsuesteno ana- themate percussa fuerit à Vigilio. Quo de Cor- nelius à Lapide commonefacere poterat Grotium, siquidem Jesuitis non illibenter aures præbuerit, eorumque vitula non raro arare fueverit. Cum enim hæc Amos verba Theodorus Mopsuestenus sic explicaret: Hoc loco, inquit, reditum è Babylone præ- dicit, quando Zorobabel ex stirpe David Regem ha- buerunt: Jacobus vero in Act. Apost. hunc locum ad Christum transtulit, in quo res est ad exitum ve- rum per ducta. Hanc ejus explicationem sub anathe- mate damnavit Vigilius Papa in Conc. Romano, quod habetur in Bibliotheca Vaticana, & ex ea transcripsit P. Turrianus super lib. 2. Const. Apost. c. 5. eo quod locum, qui primario & in sensu literali seu historico in Actis exponitur de Christo, asserat, in- telligendum esse in primo & literali sensu de Zoroba- bele, in secundo & per translationem de Christo: ubi, ut alia omittam, manifeste Theodorus errat, cum Zo- robabel facit regem, qui tantum Dux fuit populi, ex Babylone redeuntis. Pari modo idem Theodorus cen- sebat, oracula omnia, quæ ad literam de Christo edita sunt, historice ad Davidem, Ezechiam, Zorobabe- lem, & Judæos spectare; sed ex accommodatione, & ex rei eventu ab Apostolis & Evangelistis duntaxat adaptari Christo. Hoc est quod sub anathemate da- mnat Vigilius, & ante eum damnavat Synodus gene- ralis quinta, quæ fuit Constantinopolitana secunda, ut patet ex ejus Actione quinta, & ex Leontio, qui vixit tempore Justiniani Imper. & Theodori errores recenset. Hæc Cornelius. Mirum quod neque Con- stantinopolitanæ II. generalis Synodi, neque Ponti- ficis Romani anathema curarit quicquam Grotius, cætere Pontifici Romano valde addictus. Sed præ- valuere hic, & in aliis oraculis penes ipsum Judæo- rum recentiorum commenta, à quibus tamen alie- ni fuerunt veteres. Nam in ipso Thalmud hæc de Messia intellecta sunt, uti habetur in Pug. Fid. part. 3. Dist. 3. cap. 16. p. 672. & cap. 10. p. 683. è Libro Sanhedrim cap. Chelek.

## 9:13
Verse 13.

AND THE PLOWMAN SHALL OVERTAKE THE HARVEST) That is, he shall follow in his own order. After the harvest there will be plowing. AND THE TREADER OF GRAPES HIM THAT SOWETH SEED) After the vintage, sowing. AND THE MOUNTAINS SHALL DROP SWEETNESS) They shall drop with must. LXX: γλυκασμόν. AND ALL THE HILLS SHALL BE CULTIVATED) In the Hebrew: they shall flow, namely with milk as in Joel 3:18. These things are not to be understood in a carnal sense: for never have mountains or hills dropped in such a way, but concerning the kingdom of Christ; concerning which the Prophet prophesies: concerning the must and the sweetest milk of evangelical doctrine and joy. Some interpret the mountains as the Apostles and apostolic men, the hills as other preachers of the word. To others, the mountains of the Church are great men eminent in rank, the hills are men of lower status, i.e., all shall abound in doctrine and grace.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET COMPREHENDET ARATOR MESSEM) Id est, subsequetur suo ordine. Post messem erit aratio. ET CALCATOR UVÆ MITTENTEM SE- MEN) Post vindemiam satio. ET STILLABUNT MONTES DVLCEDINEM) Stillabunt musto. LXX. γλυκασμόν. ET OMNES COLLES CULTI ERVNT) In Hebræo: fluent, nempe lacte ut Joel 3, 18. Hæc non intelligenda carnali sensu: nunquam enim ita montes aut colles stillarunt, sed de regno Christi; de quo vaticinatur Propheta: de musto & lacte dulcissimo Evangelicæ doctrinæ & lætitiæ. Mon- tes nonnulli interpretantur de Apostolis, & Apo- stolicis viris, colles de aliis verbi præconibus. Aliis montes Ecclesiæ magni sunt homines gradu emi- nentes, colles sunt homines viliores, q. d. omnes doctrina & gratia affluent.

## 9:14
Vers. 14. AND I WILL TURN) Where I shall have caused to return. CAPTIVITY) That is, captives. THEY SHALL BUILD THE DESOLATE CITIES) Others also besides Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET CONVERTAM) Vbi reverti fecero. CAPTIVITATEM) Id est, captivos. ÆDIFICABUNT CIVITATES DESERTAS) A- lias etiam præter Hierosolyma.

## 9:15
Vers. 15. I WILL PLANT THEM UPON THEIR OWN LAND) I will place them in firm seats. Ezek. 15, 17. AND I WILL NOT PLUCK THEM UP ANY MORE OUT OF THEIR LAND) Namely, while they shall persist in piety.

He understands these things concerning the bodily restoration. Which opinion others do not entirely reject, but they do not admit that restriction of the benefits to the time of the restoration. For those benefits ought to have had a place primarily under the New Testament. Which also seems to have been the mind of Calvin. Although indeed an allusion is made to the bodily restoration of the Jews, and they could have been so easily confirmed concerning it, inasmuch as it is a continuous metaphor taken from those who return from captivity into their Fatherland, for these are accustomed to build cities, to plant vineyards and gardens: yet the Holy Spirit does not intend here to prophesy, namely in these words, concerning the bodily restoration of the Israelites, nor have the Israelites ever returned from the Assyrian captivity, concerning whom, however, it is certain that the Prophet is treating here. Whence these things are to be understood concerning the spiritual return of Israel, concerning the conversion of the Israelites according to the Spirit, and from the spiritual captivity by liberation. Cf. Ezek. 16, 55. Jer. 48, 47. ch. 49, 6. where it speaks similarly of the conversion of the captivity, and the mystical return of Samaria, Sodom, Moab, and Ammon. Thus Jerome in this place. So also do most other interpreters. We add only the words of blessed Luther, sealing this Prophet at the same time in the name of Jesus with his own doxology and prayer: He speaks of spiritual reduction and conversion. For he threatened above corporally that he would deliver all to captivity. By this reduction, therefore, all were reduced, as many as, upon Christ coming, believed the Gospel, and were translated through faith into that tabernacle of David which had fallen and was therefore despised, in which there is the highest security, peace, and joy of conscience, and in which those who exist produce rich fruits. Hence, strengthened by faith and the Holy Spirit given from heaven, they shall not be transferred forever. Moses always commanded to do, and it was not done. Therefore also the promises were promised to them in vain.

But here, because the Lord himself promises that he will act, that he will reduce, that he will plant, therefore it will be ratified. Magnificently is the divine mercy commended to us here, regarding us Gentiles, who are deserted and waste cities, nay (as in Luke 14) who are placed in the fields outside the city without law, without the worship of God, without good works, full of sins, worthy of eternal death, and are cultivated through the word of grace, that we may become vineyards and gardens, lovely and pleasant in the sight of God and the angels. Whence afterwards, as from fruitful plants, other gardens will be instructed and prepared, so that thus the glory and kingdom of God may be amplified and grow through us also.
