Let us therefore give thanks to God for this his inexhaustible benevolence and love toward us, and let us ask that we may truly be so cultivated that we may please God as pleasant gardens, and that men may enjoy our fruits, and through us be invited to piety, Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 15. PLANTABO EOS SUPER HUMUM SUAM) Firmis sedibus locabo. Ezech. 15, 17. ET NON EVELLAM EOS ULTRA DE TER- RA SUA) Nempe dum in pietate perstabunt.

De reductione corporali hæc intelligit. Quam sententiam alii non omnino reprobant, sed illam restrictionem beneficiorum ad tempus reductio- nis non admittunt. Nam beneficia ista imprimis locum habere debuere sub N. T. Quæ etiam mens Calvino videtur fuisse. Quamvis vero allusio fiat ad reductionem corporalem Judæorum, deque ea ita facile confirmari potuerint, siquidem continua me- taphora sit ab iis petita, qui è captivitate redeunt in Patriam, hi enim solent ædificare urbes, plantare vineas & hortos: non tamen id hic intendit Spiri- tus S. vaticinari nempe his verbis de Israëlitarum reductione corporali, nec unquam israëlitæ reversi sunt è captivitate Assyriaca, de quibus tamen hic Prophetam agere, certum est. Unde de spirituali Israëlis reditu ea intelligenda sunt, de Israëlitarum secundum Spiritum conversione, & è captivitate spi- rituali liberatione. Conf. Ezech. 16, 55. Jer. 48, 47. cap. 49, 6. ubi similiter de conversione captivitatis, & reditu mystico Samariæ, Sodomæ, Moab & Ammon. Ita Hieronymus in h. l. Sic etiam plerique alii interpp. Addimus solum B. Lutheri verba, ejusdem δοξολογίᾳ & precatione simul hunc Prophetam, in nomine Jesu, obsignantes: De spirituali reductione & conversione loquitur. Nam corporaliter minatus est supra, se omnes esse captivitati traditurum. Hæc igitur reductione reducti sunt omnes, quotquot, Christo veniente, Evangelio crediderunt, & in tabernaculum illud Davidis collapsum & ideo contemptum, sunt translati per fidem, in quo summa securitas, pax & gaudium conscientiæ est, in quo existentes uberes fructus faciunt. Hinc in sempiternum non transferentur fide firmati, & Spiritu S. cœlitus dato. Moses semper jussit facere, & non fiebat. Ideo quoque promissiones eis frustra promittebantur.

Hic vero, quia Dominus ipse promittit se facturum, se reducturum, se plantaturum, ideo ratum erit. Magnifice nobis hic commendatur misericordia divina, quoad nos gentes, quæ sumus civitates desertæ & vastæ, imo (sicut Luc. 14. est) quæ sumus in agris extra civitatem positæ sine lege, sine cultu Dei, sine bonis operibus, plenæ peccatis, dignæ morte æterna, & excolimur per verbum gratiæ, ut fiamus vineæ & horti amabiles, & amœni in conspectu Dei & angelorum. Unde postea tanquam ex plantis fœcundis alii horti instruentur & parantur, ut ita gloria & regnum Dei per nos quoque amplificetur & crescat. Agamus igitur Deo gratias pro hac inexhausta sua erga nos benevolentia & amore, & rogemus, ut vere sic excolamur, ut & Deo tanquam horti amœni placeamus, & fructibus nostris fruantur homines, perque nos ad pietatem invitentur, Amen.

# Obadiah

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
I. N. J. ANNOTATIONS ON OBADIAH.

Latin:

I. N. J. ANNOTATA AD ABDIAM.

## 1:1 Argument
CHAPTER THE ONLY ONE.

A prophecy concerning the destruction of the Idumeans, on account of their pride and trust in human power, and also on account of their ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν [rejoicing in the misfortune of others] and the injury inflicted upon Jacob; with the addition of comfort concerning God who will preserve his Church and will again gather the dispersed from Israel.

Edom is to be overturned, the Church of Christ is to be preserved.

At what time he wrote this is little known. Some of the Hebrews think this is that steward of the royal house who is named in 1 Kings 18. Jerome thinks him a contemporary of Hosea, Joel, Amos, and those who will follow. This opinion is proven by the order of these Prophets, which is the same in all Hebrew Codices. Jeremiah ch. 49 and Ezekiel ch. 25 took many things from this prophecy, because Idumea suffered, such as is predicted here, in the times of Sennacherib and again through Nebuchadnezzar. Therefore, in a similar matter, the words are used.

From the order of the arrangement of the Prophets, a synchronism or order of time is not solidly proven. Yet the opinion of the Hebrews concerning the steward of the Royal house is deservedly deserted: which Cyril, Theodoret, Vatablus, Ribera, Cornelius, Tirinus, Calvin, Drusius, Hottinger, and our own countrymen along with blessed Luther, and even Aben-Ezra among the Rabbis, reject. For it is certain that this Prophet lived around the Babylonian captivity, since he reproaches the Idumeans for their ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν [rejoicing in the misfortune of others] and injury during the deportation of the Jews, whence our countrymen along with blessed Luther make him a contemporary of Jeremiah and Ezekiel. Whence there is no place for the opinion of Josephus and Abarbenel, who wish that he was that prefect of the house of Ahab who was the husband of the widow of whom 2 Kings 4, 1 speaks: because it is repugnant to chronology. But that either Jeremiah or Ezekiel took their material from this prophecy is not likely; nay, the Prophet testifies that the same hearing was heard by others with him from the Lord. Nor is it to be admitted that Obadiah speaks of the times of Sennacherib, but since he predicts to the Edomites the same things as Jeremiah, and that in exactly the same words, it does not seem obscure that the same times are also regarded by him. Therefore, the opinion of blessed Luther, Tom. 3, Jena Latin, fol. 518, pleases me. To me indeed it seems entirely that he prophesied at the time of the Babylonian captivity, and took his prophecy from Jeremiah, especially from the 49th chapter, which certain places in this Prophet indicate. These are not obscure circumstances which argue that he was a contemporary of Jeremiah. These things, however, are to be understood in such a way that divine inspiration is not excluded. For not otherwise than through divine inspiration, and just as the Spirit dictated to them, did the sacred writers repeat those things which had been handed down by other divinely inspired writers: they did not draw them out from memory of their own accord. This is what is said about the same hearing being heard. That only Moses, the Prince of the Prophets, heard things from the Lord in the very same words and phrases, and that the other Prophets wrote down their visions in their own voices and words, is a fiction of Abarbenel, or rather of Maimonides. But it is an unwritten and copied thing: since God also dictates words to other Prophets, and they frequently inculcate that solemn 'thus said the Lord,' and all spoke just as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. The argument of the Prophet is this: He predicts destruction to the Idumeans, who will be greatly confounded in their pride and boasting, to be cut off on account of their iniquity against their brothers the Jews and their ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν [rejoicing in the misfortune of others]; by which name he still invites them to repentance, with the promise of salvation on Mount Zion, and the raising up of Saviors, and also the enlargement of the kingdom of the Lord. There are two parts: The former is legal, concerning the excision of the Idumeans, up to verse 17. The latter is Evangelical, concerning the salvation of the Messiah, to the end of the chapter.

PART I. LEGAL. CONCERNING THE EXTERMINATION OF THE IDUMEANS.

Verse 1.

THE VISION OF OBADIAH) That is, Prophecy. For this word is often used in a more general sense. WE HAVE HEARD A REPORT FROM THE LORD) A decree as it were pronounced by God. See the statement in Jeremiah, chapter 49, verse 14 and following.

The Prophet seems to join himself with other contemporary men of God, 'we have heard a report from the Lord.' They say that these words, along with those following in this verse, are spoken as if by way of a parenthesis, as are the former, 'Thus said the Lord God concerning Edom,' with verse 2, 'Behold, a small one' I have given you,' they connect. These can also be connected in this way: Thus said the Lord God to Edom, when we have heard a report from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, arise, and let us arise against her in battle. Behold, I have given you a little one, etc. Or also in this way: Thus said the Lord, but we have heard this report from the Lord The sense will be as follows: Let no one doubt that these things, which I am about to recite, were said by God. For we have also heard a clear manifestation, not one or two, but several Prophets, and now an ambassador has been sent to stir up the nations. That the Prophet joins himself with other men of God who foretold the same fates to the Idumeans, not only Jews like Aben-Ezra and Abarbenel, but also almost all Christians, establish: Remigius, Lyranus, Clarius, Montanus, Castrius, Cornelius, Saa, Ribera, Calvin, Mercerus, the Belgians, Vinariensis, Gesnerus, Winckelmann, etc. Jerome, however, at Micah 5:4, makes these words, 'we have heard a report,' the words of the Lord speaking, to indicate the mystery of the Trinity: 'We shall raise up, I and My Son and the Holy Spirit,' according to that which is written in Genesis: 'Let us make man in our image and likeness,' and in the beginning of Obadiah: 'Arise, and let us ascend against her in battle.' This also pleased Cocceius; he urges especially the comparison with the words of Jeremiah, because in both the preceding and following parts a prosopopoeia of God is made, or God is introduced speaking, and in the same way the words of Obadiah are also placed. And that there is no need for a parenthesis here, and the words flow better: And that such a locution also occurs in John 3:11, 'What we have seen and heard,' where the Son and the Holy Spirit, two witnesses, speak. What the Talmudists and some Rabbis hand down concerning Obadiah, that this Prophet was a courtier of Ahab, who had the same name 1 Kings 18:13, which opinion Lyranus and Chrysostom a Castro defend, rests on no more foundation than that opinion of Dorotheus, Epiphanius, and John of Jerusalem, or even of certain Hebrews, that he was the third of the captains of fifty of King Ahaziah, 2 Kings 1:14, or that which Cornelius alleges, that our Obadiah is that Prince who is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 17:7. With equal ease, therefore, such things are rejected as they are asserted.

AND HE SENT AN AMBASSADOR TO THE NATIONS) The angel who incites the Assyrians, as later the Chaldeans.

There is no need to explain these things as if they refer to an angel, as if God incites to wars through an angel. It is a hypotyposis, by which the embassy sent to the nations is expressed, namely, that the nations are going to stir each other up against the Idumeans, with ambassadors sent so that by common effort and joined hand they might check their insolence. But it is attributed to God because this would not happen without divine nod and direction, and thus would not lack success.

Latin:

CAPUT UNICUM.

Vaticinium de interitu Idumæorum, ob eorundem superbiam, ac fiduciam in humanam potentiam, nec non ob ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν & injuriam Jacobo illatam; adjuncto solatio de Deo Ecclesiam suam conservaturo, dispersosque ex Israele iterum congregaturo.

Evertendus Edom, servanda Ecclesia Christi.

QVotempore hic scripserit, parum constat. Hebræorum quidam hunc esse illum regiæ domus dispensatorem existimant, qui nominatur 1. Reg. 18. Hieronymus coævum Oseæ, Jœli, Amoso, & iis, qui sequentur. Quam sententiam probat horum Prophetarum ordo, qui est in Hebræis Codicibus omnibus. Multa è hoc vaticinio sumsere Jeremias c. 49. Ezechiel c. 25. quia Idumæa, qualia hic prædicuntur, Sennacheribi temporibus, passa est iterum per Nabuchodonosorem. Itaque in re pari usurpantur verba.

EX ordine collocationis Prophetarum haud solide probatur συγχρονισμὸς vel ordo temporis. Merito tamen Ebræorum opinio de dispensatore domus Regiæ deseritur: quam reprobant Cyrillus, Theodoret. Vatablus, Riebera, Cornelius, Tirinus, Calvinus, Drusius, Hottingerus, Nostrates cum B. Luthero, etiam è Rabbinis Aben-Esdra. Nam circa captivitatem Babylonicam hunc Prophetam vixisse, quum Idumæis ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν & injuriam in deportatione Judæorum exprobret, certum est, unde nostrates cum B. Luthero eum Jeremiæ & Ezechieli faciunt σύγχρονον. Unde nec Josephi & Abarbenel opinioni locus, qui præfectum illum domus Achabi maritum fuisse viduæ, de qua 2. Reg. 4, 1. volunt: quia Chronologiæ repugnat. Desumsisse autem ex hoc vaticinio vel Jeremiam vel Ezechielem sua, non est verosimile, imo eundem auditum secum alios audivisse Prophetas à Domino, Propheta testatur. Neque admittendum, quod de Sennacheribi temporibus Obadias loquatur, sed quum eadem, quæ Jeremias, prædicat Edomæis, idque verbis plane iisdem, haud obscurum videtur, eadem etiam ab ipso respici tempora. Placet ergo sententia B. Lutheri Tom. 3. Jen. Lat. f. 518. Mihi quidem omnino videtur prophetasse tempore captivitatis Babylonicæ, & sumpsisse suam Prophetiam ex Jeremia, maxime ex 49. capite, id quod indicant quidam loci in hoc Propheta. Hæ non obscuræ circumstantiæ sunt, quæ arguunt fuisse eum contemporaneum Jeremiæ. Hæc tamen ita intelligenda, ut non excludatur θεοπνευσία. Nam non aliter, quam per inspirationem divinam, ac prout Spiritus ipsis dictabat, sacri scriptores ea, quæ ab aliis θεοπνεύστοις scriptoribus tradita erant, repetebant: non ex memoria suapte sponte depromebant. Hoc est, quod dicitur de audito eodem auditu. Solum Mosen, Prophetarum Principem res à Domino audivisse totidem vocibus, & phrasibus, cæteros Prophetas visa sua ipsorummet vocibus & verbis conscripsisse, commentum est Abarbenelis, vel Maimonidis potius. Sed ἄγραφον, & ἀντίγραφον: quum aliis etiam Prophetis Deus verba præeat, illique solemne illud, sic dixit Dominus, frequenter inculcent, & omnes loquuti sint, prout agitati à S. S. fuere. Argumentum Prophetæ hoc est: Prædicit exitium Idumæis, qui in superbia & gloriatione sua valde confundentur, exscindendi propter iniquitatem in fratres Judæos & ἐπιχαιρεκακίαν; quo nomine adhuc ad pœnitentiam eosdem invitat, promissa in monte Sion salvatione, & excitatione Salvatorum, nec non regni Domini ampliatione. Partes duæ sunt: Prior legalis de Idumæorum excisione, usque ad v. 17. Posterior Evangelica, de Messiæ salvatione, ad finem capitis.

PARS I. LEGALIS. DE IDUMÆORUM EXCISIONE.

Vers. 1.

VISIO ABDIÆ) Id est, Prophetia. Ita enim sæpe generaliori significatu hæc vox ponitur. AVDITVM AVDIVIMVS A DOMINO) Decretum quasi pronunciatum à Deo. Vide dictum Jerem. caput commate 14. & sequent.

COnjungere se videtur Propheta cum aliis συγχρόνοις Dei viris, auditum audivimus à Domino. Quæ verba cum sequentibus in hoc commate quasi per παρένθεσιν dicta ajunt, ut priora, Sic dixit Dominus Deus ad Edom, cum vers. 2. Ecce parvulum dedi te, connectant. Possunt etiam haec ita conne- cti: Sic dixit Dominus Deus ad Edom, cum audi- tum audivimus a Domino, & legatus in gentes missus est, surge, & surgamus super eam in proelium. Ecce parvulum dedi te &c. Vel etiam hoc modo: Sic di- xit Dominus, nos vero auditum istum audivimus a Domino, cum legatus missus est. Sensus ita talis e- rit: Haec, quae recitaturus sum, Deum dixisse nemo dubitet. Nam & claram audivimus manifestatio- nem, non unus & alter, sed aliquot Prophetae, & jam legatus missus est, qui gentes concitet. Conjungere se Prophetam cum aliis viris Dei, qui eadem fata praedixere Idumaeis, non Judaei tantum Aben-Ezra, Abarbenel, sed etiam Christiani plerique omnes statuunt, Remigius, Lyranus, Clarius, Montanus, Castrius, Cornelius, Saa, Ribera, Calvinus, Merce- rus, Belgae, Vinariens. Gesnerus, Winckelmann. &c. Hieronymus tamen ad Mich. 5, 4. facit haec auditum audivimus, verba Domini loquentis, ad indican- dum mysterium Trinitatis: Suscitabimus autem e- go & Filius meus & Spiritus S. juxta illud, quod in Genesi scriptum est: Faciamus hominem ad ima- ginem & similitudinem nostram, & in Abdiae prin- cipio: Surgite, & adscendamus adversus eam in proelio. Quod placuit etiam Coccejo; urget impri- mis collationem cum verbis Jeremiae, quod & in antecedentibus & consequentibus fit prosopo- doeia Dei, vel Deus loquens introducatur, atque eodem modo etiam verba Abdiae ponantur. Et quod hic non opus sit parenthesi, meliusque verba fluant: Quodque talis loquutio etiam occurrat Joh. 3, 11. Quod vidimus & audivimus, ubi Filius & Spiritus Sanctus duo testes loquantur. Quae de Obadia Talmudici & Rabbini nonnulli tradunt, quod Propheta hic Aulicus Achabi fuerit, qui idem nomen habuit 1. Reg. 18, 13. quam sententiam tuetur Lyranus & Chrysost. a Castro, non magis fun- damento nititur, quam illa Dorothei, Epiphanii, & Joh. Hierosolym. imo etiam Ebraeorum quorundam sententia, quod fuerit tertius ex Pentecontarchis Regis Ochoziae 2. Reg. 1, 14. aut ea, quam allegat Cornelius, quod Obadias noster sit Princeps iste, cujus mentio fit 2. Par. 17, 7. Parili ergo facilitate talia rejiciuntur, qua asseruntur.

ET LEGATVM AD GENTES MISIT) Ange- lum incitatorem Assyriorum, ut postea Chaldaeorum.

Non opus est, ut haec de angelo explicemus, quasi Deus per angelum incitet ad bella. Est hypotyposis, qua exprimitur legatio ad gentes missa, quod nem- pe se invicem gentes excitaturae sint adversus Idu- maeos, missis legatis, ut communi opera, junctaque manu eorum insolentiam compefcant. Deo autem id tribuitur, quod non absq; nutu & directione divi- na id futurum, adeoq; successu haud cariturum sit.

## 1:2
Verse 2. I HAVE GIVEN YOU A LITTLE ONE AMONG THE NATIONS) I have made you weak.

Mercerus, Montanus, Cornelius and a Castro, as well as Gualtherus, Pareus, and the Belgian Interpreters, understand it in this way, with Theodoret and Remigius, that the Esauites, being obscure and ignoble, had no cause to exalt themselves so much; but rather the sum and proposition of the legal discourse seems to be contained here, and thus it is predicted that God wishes to render them the most abject of all, however much they may exalt themselves and believe themselves to be most invincible. To this also tends the interpretation of our blessed Tarnovius, as well as that of Lyranus, Rupertus, Ribera, Vatablus, Oecolampadius, Drusius, Junius, etc. For God threatens that He wishes to humble the proud and render them most contemptible.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PARVVLVM DEDI TE IN GENTIBUS) Infirmum te feci.

Id ita intelligunt cum Theodor. & Remigio Merce- rus, Montan. Cornel. & a Castro, ut & Gualth. Pa- freus, & Belgici Interpp. quod Esavitae, ut pote ob- scuri & ignobiles causam non habuerint, se adeo efferrendi, sed videtur potius summa, & propositio concionis legalis hic contineri, adeoque praedici, quod Deus ipsos reddere velit omnium abjectissi- mos, utcunque sese maxime efferant, & invictissi- mos credant. Quo etiam abit B. Tarnovii nostri in- terpretatio, ut & Lyrani, Ruperti, Riberae, Vatabli, Oecolampad. Drusii, Junii, &c. Minatur enim Deus, quod superbos humiliare velit; & maxime con- temtibiles reddere.

## 1:3
Verse 3. THE PRIDE OF YOUR HEART HAS EXALTED YOU) Your idol has deceived you. See what we said regarding Jeremiah; that idol was called Kose, denouncing destruction to enemies, which turned out the opposite.

In Jeremiah the same name זדון occurs, which denotes pride: but it is joined to the same תפלצתך, which some render 'your terror,' others 'your image.' Grotius there rendered it 'idol,' because מפלצת is taken in that way in 1 Kings 15:13, and he observed that 'terriculae' (scarecrows/terrors) are said in a similar sense in Lucilius: because פלץ means to terrify. But whatever may be the case with that word (which truly should not be rashly confused with the name of the idol Miphlezeth), זדון certainly in Jeremiah, and here, denotes pride, from זוד, to seethe, to swell: not an idol. For that word is nowhere the same as idol, and CORDIS TUI (OF YOUR HEART) is added. Therefore, the pride of their heart is indicated, even if it could be that they were confirmed in that pride by their idol. But the exposition of Avenarius is altogether more convenient: 'The fear of you (that you are a terror to others) has deceived you.' Thus those things explain each other: and the pride of your heart. For from that arose the pride, that they were a terror to others. That the discourse is about the pride of the heart, the proud and arrogant words or thoughts, which the Prophet introduces, testify sufficiently: 'Who say in your heart: who will bring me down to the ground?'

Verse same.

DWELLING IN THE CLEFTS OF THE ROCKS) Because you dwell in the caverns of the rocks: of Arabia Petraea, that is. EXALTING YOUR THRONE) By the height of your dwelling: in high and lofty places. WHO SAY IN YOUR HEART, WHO WILL BRING ME DOWN TO THE GROUND) From inaccessible places.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SVPERBIA CORDIS TVI EXTVLIT TE) Idolum tuum decepit te. Vide quae ad Jeremiam diximus, Id idolum vocabatur Kose, excidium hostibus denuncians, quod contra cecidit.

Apud Jeremiam idem nomen זדון occurrit, quod superbiam notat: Jungitur autem eidem תפלצתך, quod alii reddunt terror tuus, alii simulacrum tuum. Grotius ibi reddidit idolum, quia sic מפלצת sumi- tur 1. Reg. 15, 13. & observavit terriculas simili sensu apud Lucilium dici: quia פלץ est terrere. Sed quic- quid de illa voce sit (quæ vero temere non erat cum nomine idoli Miphlezeth confundenda) זדון certe penes Jeremiam, & hic superbiam notat, à זוד effer- buit, intumuit: non idolum. Nam vox illa nuspiam idem est quod idolum, & additur לבך CORDIS TUI. Superbia itaq: cordis ipsorum indigitatur, etsi fieri potuerit, ut in illa superbia per idolum suum confirmarentur. Commodior vero omnino Ave- narii expositio: Timor tui (quod aliis terrori sis) decepit te. Ita illa sese mutuo explicant: & superbia cordis tui. Nam inde orta est superbia, quod aliis terrori essent. De superbia cordis sermonem esse, voces vel cogitationes superbæ & arrogantes, quas introducit Propheta, affatim testantur: Qui dicis in corde tuo: quis detrahet me in ter am?

Vers. eod.

HABITANTEM IN SCISSVRIS PETRARVM) Eo quod habitas in cavernis rupium: Arabiæ Petrææ scilicet. EXALTANTEM SOLIVM TVVM) Altitudine habitationis tuæ: in locis celsis atque sublimibus. QVI DICIS IN CORDE TVO, QVIS DE- TRAHET ME IN TERRAM) Ex locis inaccessis.

## 1:4
Ver. 4. IF YOU SHALL BE EXALTED, AS THE EAGLE. Which makes its nest in the highest mountains, Job 39. 28. and is said to seek the sky, Prov. 23, 5. AND IF YOU SHALL PLACE YOUR NEST AMONG THE STARS. An impossible hypothesis, yet consistent with the pride of the Edomites, who were persuaded that they could be as secure as if they had their seats among the stars, and that they could no more be cast down than the stars could be dislodged from the sky. THENCE I WILL BRING YOU DOWN) By famine. See what is said regarding similar passages in Jeremiah. That the Prophet threatens not only famine, but utter ruin, is clear from a comparison with Jer. 49, 17. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SI EXALTATUS FUERIS, UT AQUILA. Quæ in altissimis montibus nidulatur, Job. 39. 28. & cælum petere dicitur Prov. 23, 5. ET SI INTER SIDERA POSUERIS NI- DUM TUUM. Hypothesis impossibilis, conformis tamen fastui Edomitarum, qui persuasi erant, tam se securos esse posse, ac si inter sydera sedes suas haberent, nec magis sese prosterni posse, quam sydera cælo deturbarı. INDE DETRAHAM TE) Fame. Vide quæ ad similia Jeremiæ. Non famem tantum, sed extremam ruinam mi- nari Prophetam, è collatione cum Jer. 49, 17. 18. liquet.

## 1:5
Ver. 5. WOULD THEY NOT HAVE STOLEN WHAT WAS SUFFICIENT FOR THEMSELVES) And would have been content with those things. Compare here also those things which are in Jer. 49, 9. and the following. There, in the Grotian notes, it is held thus: IF GRAPE-GATHERERS HAD COME UPON YOU, WOULD THEY NOT HAVE LEFT A GLEANING GRAPE? Would they not have left something to be gleaned? The following text demands this sense. Grape-gatherers leave something, and even thieves do too. But the Chaldeans will take away everything, down to the dust. These things are taken from Obadiah 5. However, there is no need for them to be explained hypothetically in the sense of questioning and affirmatively. Would they not have left something to be gleaned? when they can be explained categorically in a negative sense, as was done by the blessed Luther in Jeremiah, and here. Osiander's paraphrase from the Hebrew explains it conveniently: i.e., If thieves (the Chaldeans) come to you, if nocturnal robbers (that is, enemies who will attack you unexpectedly, make an assault upon you) how will you perish? will they not steal what is sufficient for themselves? if grape-gatherers (Chaldean soldiers) come to you, will they leave you clusters? How (excellently) will they search out (the treasures of) Esau? that is, of the Edomites, how (industriously) will they investigate his hidden things? (that is, the Babylonians, suddenly invading Idumea, like thieves and robbers, will carry off all precious things, and lead them away, even those things which are hidden and stored in almost inaccessible places. When that thievish and robber-like rabble comes upon you, how will they sweep your chests and boxes clean/ and will search out/ what lies hidden behind nine locks.) The Babylonians are called thieves and robbers, because they did not invade the remaining peoples for a sufficiently just cause, but driven by the lust for power and avarice, they undertook most wars. So also the Weimar Paraphrast and B. Winckelm. Others, however, understand it comparatively; that the plundering of robbers and thieves would be more tolerable than that of the Chaldeans, as Jerome does, as do Oecolampadius, Calvin, Gwalther, Mercerus, Junius, Pareus; Drusius; of our own, Gesnerus, Tarnovius, as also Ribera, Castrius, Cornelius, Tirinus, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 5. NONNE FVRATI ESSENT SVFFICIEN- TIA SIBI) Et iis contenti fuissent. Confer & hic illa, quæ apud Jer. 8. sequentibus. Ibi ad Jer. 49, 9. ita in Grotianis notis habetur: SI VINDEMIATORES VENISSENT SUPER TE, NON RELIQVISSENT RACEMUM. Nonne reliquissent aliquid ad racemandum? Hunc sen- sum exigit, quod sequitur. Vindemiatores aliquid relinquunt, imo & fures. At Chaldæi omnia auferent cum pulvisculo. Sumta hæc ex Abdia 5. Non opus autem est, ut hypothetice in sensu interrogandi & affirmative exponantur. Nonne reliquissent aliquid ad racemandum? quum categorice sensu negativo exponi possint, uti à B. Luthero in Jere- mia, & hic factum. Quem explicat commode paraphrasis Osiandri ex Ebræo: h. m. Si fures (Chaldæi) tibi venerint, si latrones nocturni, (id est, hostes, qui te de improviso adorientur, in te impetum fecerint) quomodo peribis? nonne suffi- cientia sibi furabuntur? si vindemiatores (Chaldæi milites) tibi venerint, an racemos tibi relinquent? Quam (egregie) scrutabuntur (thesauros) Esau? id est, Edumæorum, quam (industrie) inve- stigabunt abscondita ejus? (id est, Babylonii su- bito in Idumæam irruentes, tanquam fures & latrones, omnia pretiosa convafabunt, & ab- ducent, etiam ea, quæ in locis propemodum inaccessis abdita & reposita sunt. Wenn das die- bisch und räuberisch Gesindlein über Dich kommen wird/wie werden sie dir Kisten und Kasten so fein rein ausfegen/ und werden herfür suchen/was hinter neun Schlöffen verborgen liegt.) Vocantur autem Babylonii fures & latrones, quia non satis ju- sta de causa reliquos populos invadebant, sed libi- dine dominandi, & avaritia impulsi, pleraque bella suscipiebant. Sic etiam Paraphar. Vinariens. & B. Winckelm. Alii tamen comparative intelligunt; latronum & furum expilationem tolerabiliorem fo- re, quam Chaldaeorum, cum Hieronymo, utpote Oe- colamp. Calvin. Gvalther. Mercerus, Junius, Pareus; Drusius; e nostris Gesnerus, Tarnovius, ut & Ribera, Castrius, Cornelius, Tirinus &c.

## 1:7
Verse 7.

THEY HAVE SENT THEE EVEN TO THE BORDER) They will send thee forth to thy borders: namely, into foreign lands.

ALL THE MEN OF THY CONFEDERACY, THEY HAVE DECEIVED THEE) They will mock thee: the Assyrians, of course, whom you hoped were faithful to you, on account of a common hatred against the Jews.

THEY THAT EAT WITH THEE) The Chaldean also explains it thus. There is an ellipsis in the Hebrew. The full expression would be אנשי לחמך.

The word אנשי can be repeated from the preceding [words] by zeugma, as is often wont to happen. Calvin says they also call guests or intimates 'men of bread'. Others explain it without an ellipsis in this way: They have placed thy bread (namely, those men of thy peace) as a wound under thee, that is, those confederates and peaceful ones and friends of yours cause the meal which is common to them with you to be a stumbling block and a snare to you. For from that they take the opportunity of betraying you, since by learning your plans through this familiarity, they reveal them to the enemy. Thus R. Solomon. But Capellus is inept, who dares to carp at and correct the received reading of the Hebrews here, whom Buxtorf chastises in Vindic. p. 878.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

USQVE AD TERMINVM EMISERVNT TE) Apud fines tuos emittent te: nempe in terras exteras.

OMNES VIRI FOEDERIS TUI, ILLVSERVNT TIBI) Illudent tibi: Assyrii scilicet, quos tibi fidos spe- rabas, ob commune in Judaeos odium.

QVI COMEDVNT TECVM) Sic & Chaldaeus exponit. Est ἔλλειψις in Hebr. Plena esset locutio אנשי לחמך.

Potest vox אנשי ex praecedentibus ἀπὸ κοινῶ repeti, ut saepius fieri solet. Viros panis etiam vocant convivas, vel familiares, ait Calvinus. Alii sine elli- psi explicant hoc pacto: Panem tuum posuerunt (sc. viri illi pacis tuae) vulnus sub te, h. e. foederati & pa- cifici atque amici illi tui efficiunt, ut convictus, qui illis tecum est communis, tibi sit offendiculo & la- queo. Inde enim occasionem sumunt te prodendi, cum hac familiaritate consilia tua resciscentes, ea hosti aperiunt. Ita R. Salomo. Ineptus autem est Capellus, qui receptam Ebraeorum lectionem hic vellicare & corrigere audet, quem castigat Bux- torffius in Vindic. p. 878.

AND EVERY ONE OF THE MOUNT OF ESAU MAY BE CUT OFF) Because everyone from the mount of Esau shall perish. That is, in Seir.

## 1:10
Vers. 10.

FOR THE SLAUGHTER, AND FOR THE INIQUITY AGAINST THY BROTHER JACOB) Refer this to the time when the Syrians devastated Judea and besieged Jerusalem. 2 Kings 16:5. Compare Amos 1:11. The Idumeans did the same thing again to the Jews when Nebuchadnezzar captured the city: as Ezekiel 25:11 and Psalm 137:7 teach us, and they suffered the same things from Nebuchadnezzar himself.

Interpreters vary regarding the time of Obadiah. Similarly also regarding the time of the fulfillment of his prophecies. Grotius refers these, and those which were predicted by Jeremiah in chapter 49 and Ezekiel in chapter 25, to different times, and thinks that Jeremiah and Ezekiel took their material from this prophecy, because the Idumeans, such as are predicted here, suffered again in the times of Sennacherib through Nebuchadnezzar. But I do not see why those things which are handed down in exactly the same words by Jeremiah and Obadiah concerning Idumea should not be referred to the same times. Nor are the Edomites read to have exercised iniquity against the Jews at the time when the Syrians devastated Judea and besieged Jerusalem (2 Kings 16:5), or to have suffered the same things, either from the Assyrian or from Nebuchadnezzar. For there is nothing in the Scriptures concerning the slaughter inflicted upon them by the Assyrian. Therefore other interpreters generally refer those things which are predicted against the Idumeans to the Chaldeans, not to the Assyrians, to which view Aben-Ezra also assents, though refuted in vain by Abarbanel, whose mouth was stopped by Mr. Pfeiffer in his Philological-Anti-Rabbinical treatise on Obadiah against Don Isaac Abarbanel. The Edomites had been devastated and subdued long ago by David (1 Kings 11:15) and again by Amaziah, King of Judah (2 Kings 14:17). But when God saw that they were not being corrected by these scourges here, He intimated to them through Jeremiah and Obadiah a total destruction by the Chaldeans, until they were finally destroyed after the Persians, Greeks, and Maccabees by Titus Vespasian the Roman. These prophets certainly bring forward the same cause for the destruction: iniquity against the Jews, inasmuch as they killed or plundered those fleeing from enemies, and even assisted the Chaldeans with wealth and arms in the conquest of Jerusalem. Compare Psalm 137:7 and 3 Esdras 4:45. Whence Cornelius à Lapide conjectures that Obadiah prophesied during the times of Jeremiah, from the fact that his prophecy is exactly the same as the prophecy of Jeremiah against the Edomites. Obadiah may be seen to have looked to this when he speaks in the plural, WE HAVE HEARD A REPORT, joining himself with Jeremiah and Ezekiel, who had received the same report, as was observed before.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

PROPTER INTERFECTIONEM, ET PROPTER INIQVITATEM IN FRATREM TUUM JACOB) Hoc refer ad tempus, cum Syri Judaeam vastarunt, & Hie- rosolyma obsederunt. 2. Reg. 16, 5. Confer Amos 1, 11. Paria fecere iterum Idumaei in Judaeos, cum urbem cepit Nabuchodonosar: ut docet nos Ezech. 25, 11. & Ps. 137, 7. & paria passi sunt ab ipso Nabuchodonosoro.

De tempore Obadiae variant interpretes. Simi- liter etiam de tempore complementi vaticiniorum ejusdem. Grotius ad diversa tempora haec, & quae a Jeremia cap. 49. Ezech. c. 25. praedicta sunt, re- fert, atque Jeremiam ac Ezechielem sua ex hoc va- ticinio desumsisse putat, quia Idumaei, qualia hic praedicantur, Sennacheribi temporibus passi sint iterum per Nabuchodonosarem. Sed non video, cur, quae iisdem plane verbis a Jeremia & Obadia de Idumaea traduntur, non ad eadem tempora re- ferenda sint? Neque tum ubi Syri Judaeam vasta- runt, & Hierosolyma obsederunt 2. Reg. 16, 5. le- guntur Edomitae in Judaeos iniquitatem exercuis- se, aut paria etiam passi, ut ab Assyrio, ita a Nabu- chodonosoro. Nam de clade ab Assyrio ipsis illa- ta nihil in Scripturis habetur. Ideo alii Interpp. communiter fere ea, quae praedicuntur adversus Idumaeos, ad Chaldaeos referunt, non ad Assyrios, quibus etiam annuit Aben-Esra nequicquam ab Abarbenele confutatus, cui os oppilavit Dn. Pfeifferus in tract. Philologico-Anti-Rabbin. ad Obadiam adversus Don. Isaac Abarben. Vasta- tis ti erant Edomitæ olim, & subacti à Davide 1. Reg. 11, 15. atque iterum 2.Reg.14, 17. ab Amafia Rege Ju- da. Sed quum Deus eosdem hîc flagellis emendari non videret, per Jeremiam & Obadiam intimavit illis totale per Chaldæos excidium, donec post Per- sas, Græcos, Maccabæos à Tito Vespaf. Romano fina- liter exscinderentur. Caufam certe eandem hi Pro- phetæ proferunt excidii, iniquitatem adversus Ju- dæos, siquidem profugos ab hostibus occiderint vel spoliarint, quin etiam Chaldæos in expugnatione Hierosolymæ opibus armisque adjuverint. Confer Pf. 137, 7. & 3. Esdr. 4, 45. Unde Obadiam sub tem- pora Jeremiæ prophetasse conjectat Cornel. à Lap. ex eo, quod prophetia ejus eadem plane sit cum Prophetia Jeremiæ contra Edumæos. Quod respe- xisse videri potest Obadias, cum in plurali loquitur AUDITUM AUDIVIMUS, se cum Jeremia, & Ezechiele, qui eundem auditum acceperat, conjun- gens, uti antea observatum.

## 1:12
Vers. 12.

AND THOU SHALT NOT LOOK DOWN IN THE DAY OF THY BROTHER) Thou shouldst not have looked (with joy, to wit) upon those things which were happening in the day (of the evils) of thy brother. Thou shouldst not have looked, i.e., thou oughtest not to have looked: as: 'but you, Alban, should remain by your words.' Take the following verses in this way as well. Others make these words of dissuasion, and attribute them to God Himself, who even now out of His accustomed long-suffering warns the Idumeans not to continue to act in this way and to join themselves to the enemies of the people: to which view the LXX, Cyril, Tarnovius, and from the Reformed, Calvin, Junius, Drusius, and Cocceius subscribe. And thus the following verses are also to be understood. V. 12. do not look with malicious joy upon the day of his alienation or pilgrimage and exile, nor rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction, etc. IN THE DAY OF THEIR PERDITION) When many of them were perishing in the fields and in the smaller towns.

Sic sume & sequentia, Alii hæc dehortantis verba potius faciunt, Deo- que ipsi tribuunt, qui adhuc è solita μακροθυμίᾳ præmoneat Idumæos, ne ita pergant agere, seque hostibus populi adjungere: quo abeunt LXX, Cy- rillus, Tarnovius, & è. IN DIE PERDITIONIS EORVM) Cum pluri- mi eorum in agris, & in minoribus oppidis perirent.

## 1:16
Verse 16.

FOR AS YE HAVE DRUNK UPON MY HOLY MOUNTAIN) How ye have drunk (the heat of my wrath) because of my holy mountain. Because of Judea provoked by you. ALL NATIONS SHALL DRINK) The Philistines, Moabites, Damascenes, and others. See Is. ch. 14, ch. 15, & 16, & 17. AND THEY SHALL DRINK AND SHALL SWALLOW DOWN) By drinking they shall swallow down; that is, they shall drain the whole cup. AND THEY SHALL BE AS THOUGH THEY WERE NOT) As if they had never been. These things began to be fulfilled in the Idumeans through the Chaldeans, by whom they were subjugated, and never again became their own masters: yet they were fulfilled fully and successively. For they were defeated by Judas Maccabeus 1 Maccab. 5, 6, and so subdued by John Hyrcanus that they were compelled to receive Jewish rites, and were reckoned among the Jews, and began to coalesce with them into one people. See Joseph. Antiq. b. 13, ch. 17, 23, until they were overthrown with the Jews by the Romans. See Joseph. on the Jewish War, b. 6, ch. 40.

so that not even their name remained. For Jerome testifies that Idumea was called Gabalene in his time, and the Idumeans are nowhere to be found. Whence the absurdities of Abarbenel, that the Idumeans are the Romans, which Mr. Pfeiffer learnedly refuted, are laid bare of their own accord, which he scattered to the infamy of the Christian religion at the beginning of the previous century: For the Romans were not overthrown by the Jews: but conversely the Jews with the Edumeans by the Romans.

PART II. EVANGELICAL. CONCERNING THE LIBERATION TO BE PERFORMED BY THE MESSIAH. Verse 17.

Nam à Juda Maccabæo debellati 1. Maccab. 5, 6. à Joh. Hir- cano ita subacti sunt, ut ritus Judaicos recipere co- gerentur, & Judæis accenserentur, & cum iis in u- num populum coalescere inciperent. Vid. Joseph. Antiq. l. 13. c. 17, 23. donec cum Judæis everterentur à Romanis. Vid. Joseph. de bello Judaic. l. 6. c. 40.

ut ne nomen quidem eorum superaret. Nam Idu- mæam suo tempore Gabalenem dictam testatur Hie- ronymus, nec uspiam Idumæos reperire est. ## 1:17
AND ON MOUNT ZION THERE SHALL BE SALVATION) Jerusalem shall not be captured by Sennacherib, and there many even from the neighbors shall find safety. AND IT SHALL BE HOLY) The worship of God shall remain there. AND THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL POSSESS THOSE WHO POSSESSED THEMSELVES) The Philistines in the reign of Hezekiah 18, 8. Verse 18. AND THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL BE FIRE, AND THE HOUSE OF JOSEPH A FLAME, AND THE HOUSE OF ESAU STUBBLE: AND THEY SHALL BE KINDLED AGAINST THEM, AND SHALL DEVOUR THEM) Many of them. Reference is made to what the Maccabees did against the Idumeans. Josephus 12, 11. AND THERE SHALL BE NO SURVIVORS OF THE HOUSE OF ESAU) Namely, such as could harm the Jews. Verse 19. AND THEY SHALL INHERIT THOSE WHO ARE IN THE SOUTH) And they (the Jews) shall possess the south; that is, Teman. THE MOUNT OF ESAU) In the Hebrew: With the mount of Esau. These things were fulfilled most fully by Hyrcanus, as also the following. The same Josephus 13, 17. AND THOSE WHO ARE IN THE PLAINS OF THE PHILISTINES) And the plain with the (land of the) Philistines. AND THEY SHALL POSSESS THE REGION OF EPHRAIM, AND THE REGION OF SAMARIA) You have this history in the cited book of Josephus 13, 17. AND BENJAMIN) Joined with Judah. SHALL POSSESS GILEAD) Joseph 12, 12. 1 Macc. 5, 17. Verse 20. AND THE CAPTIVITY OF THIS HOST OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL) And those deported forces of the children of Israel: namely those who, few from Asher, Naphtali, and Zebulun, shall return with the Jews from the deportation. They shall possess, to be repeated from the former. ALL THE PLACES OF THE CANAANITES) In the Hebrew: whatever was of the Canaanites. EVEN TO SAREPTA) A city of the Sidonians 1 Kings 17, 10. Foolish Rabbis from this make France, from that which follows ספרד Spain, and dare to promise themselves the possession of those kingdoms by such a fanatical exposition.

Which explanation our blessed Luther also rejected in Lyranus: But that Lyranus brings forth I know not what trifles here, and wishes France to be understood, following the Rabbis, does not seem to me to fit at all. It is a violent and distorted gloss, which does not even have the appearance of truth. Similarly, the interpreters in our translation also err in the word Bosphorus. Jerome brings forward the testimony of his Jew, from whom he learned the Hebrew language, that Emperor Constantine transferred the Jews into the Bosphorus of Thrace, and that in that place they await that they will again establish a kingdom, and I know not what other fabrications: but the good man was deceived by a Jewish figment. We see entirely that the Prophet is speaking about those places which are in the land of Canaan, where the kingdom of Christ first began through the Gospel. Nor can the Vulgate help the Papist interpreters here. nay, they fight among themselves, Ribera, Cornelius, Mariana, Saa, whether the Thracian, or indeed the Cimmerian, or finally the Gaditanian Bosphorus is noted.

Latin:

ET POSSIDEBIT DOMVS JACOB EOS, QVI SE POSSEDERANT) Philisthæos rege Ezechia 18, 8. Vers. 18. ET ERIT DOMVS JACOB IGNIS, ET DOMVS JOSEPH FLAMMA, ET DOMVS ESAV STIPVLA: ET SVCCENDENTVR IN EOS, ET DEVORABVNT EOS) Multos ex iis. Respiciuntur, quæ Maccabæi egere contra Idumæos. Josephus 12, 11. ET NON ERVNT RELIQVIÆ DOMVS ESAV) Nempe tales, quæ nocere Judæis possint. Vers. 19. ET HÆREDITABVNT HI, QVI AD AV- STRVM SVNT) Et possidebunt (Judæi) meridiem; id est, Themanem. MONTEM ESAV) In Hebræo: Cum monte Esau. Impleta hæc plenissime per Hyrcanum, ut & sequentia. Idem Josephus 13, 17. ET QVI IN CAMPESTRIBVS PHILISTIIM) Et planitiem cum (terra) Philistinorum. ET POSSIDEBVNT REGIONEM EPHRAIM, ET REGIONEM SAMARIÆ) Hanc historiam habes dicto Josephi libro 13, 17. ET BENJAMIN) Conjunctus cum Juda. POSSIDEBIT GALAAD) Joseph 12, 12. 1. Macc. 5, 17. Vers. 20. ET TRANSMIGRATIO EXERCITVS HVJVS FILIORVM ISRAEL) Et deportatæ copiæ illæ filiorum Israel: nempe ii, qui pauci ex Asere, Nephtalimo & Zabulone cum Judæis redibunt a deportatione. Possidebunt, repetendum ex priori. OMNIA LOCA CHANANÆORVM) In Hebr. quicquid Chananæorum fuit. VSQVE AD SAREPTAM) Urbem Sidoniorum 1. Reg. 17, 10. Stulti Rabbini hinc Franciam, ex eo, quod se- quitur ספרד Hispaniam faciunt, audentque tam fanatica expositione eorum regnorum possessionem sibi spondere.

Quam explicationem in Lyrano etiam B. Lu- ther. noster reprobavit: Quod vero Lyranus nescio quas nugas hic profert, & vult intelligi Franciam, se- cutus Rabbinos, mihi omnino non videtur convenire. Violenta est & detorta glossa, quæ ne speciem quidem veri habet. Similiter errant etiam in nostra trans- latione Interpp. in vocabulo Bosphoro. Hiero- nymus producit testimonium sui Judæi, a quo lin- guam Ebræam didicit, quod in Bosphorum Thraciæ transtulerit Constantinus Imperator Judæos, atque in eo loco expectent rursum instituturos regnum, & ne- scio quæ alia commenta: sed fulsus est bonus vir Ju- daico figmento. Nos omnino videmus loqui Prophe- tam de illis locis, quæ sunt in terra Chanaan, ubi re- gnum Christi primum per Evangelium cœpit. Nec juvare hic possunt vulgatam Pontificii Interpp. imo dimicant ipsimet inter se, Riebera, Cornelius, Ma- riana, Saa, anne Thracius, num vero Cimmerius, an denique Gaditanus Bosphorus notetur.

## 1:20
Verse same. AND THE CAPTIVITY OF JERUSALEM) Those deported from Judea, when they shall have returned. WHICH IS IN THE BOSPHORUS SHALL POSSESS) They shall possess those things which are of Sepharad. For so the Hebrews, Symmachus, Aquila, Theodotion read: I think the LXX also read thus, and where we read ἕως Ἐφραθὰ, they wrote ἕως Σεφραδὰ.

Jerome says this word is a term in the language of the Assyrians. Nay, even of the Hebrews ספ-רד is the end of dominion. Blessed Luther has this to say about this word: In Hebrew it is Besepharad, which word is nowhere else found in the Bible. Therefore the Jews also invent anything, namely that it is Spain. But that does not fit at all, nor do I think any of the Jews knows what it is. And our interpreters, deceived by the allusion of the name, interpreted Bosphorus for Bispharad, which is to be understood as ridiculous. (Truly ridiculous, since the ב contributes nothing to the essence of the name. Cf. Mayer. Phil. S. p. 1. p. 196.) Therefore it is either a city or some region of Assyria, where the captive people were kept. Concerning the appellative acceptance of the word as if it consisted of סוף and רדה and denoted the end of dominion, although that also pleased Junius and blessed Tarnovius, rightly Mr. Pfeiffer observes: that such a composition is rather unusual: but more absurd is the conjecture of Cornelius that it is from סוף and ארץ: but for the opinion of Jerome, that the word denotes a term in the language of the Assyrians, he judges it more plausible to draw here the Chaldean ספר shore, port.

CITIES OF THE SOUTH) The city of the South. Because he had said a term, he shows which term he understands, namely that part of Arabia which lies to the south of Judea, where the kingdom of Sheba was, 1 Kings 10, 1, with the passage Matthew 12, 42 compared. See concerning this matter Josephus in the cited place 12, 12. 1 Macc. 5, 17. 25.

Latin:

Vers. eod. ET TRANSMIGRATIO JERVSALEM) Depor- tati ex Judæa, ubi redierint. QVÆ IN BOSPHORO EST POSSIDEBIT) Ea quæ sunt Sapharadis possidebunt. Ita enim legunt Hebræi, Symmachus, Aquila, Theodotion: puto sic legisse etiam LXX. & ubi legimus ἕως Ἐφραθὰ, scripsisse ἕως Σεφραδὰ.

Hieronymus hanc vocem Assyriorum lingua esse ait termi- num. Imo & Hebræorum ספ-רד est finis dominatus. B. Lutherus ita de hac voce habet: In Ebræo est Besepharad, quæ vox nuspiam alias habetur in Bi- bliis. Ideo Judæi etiam comminiscuntur quidvis, nempe esse Hispaniam. Sed id omnino non convenit, neque puto aliquem Judæorum scire, quid sit. Et nostri Interpp. falsi allusione nominis pro Bispharad inter- pretati sunt Bosphoro, id quod ridiculum est intelli- gendum. (Vere ridiculum, quum ב ad nominis es- sentiam nihil faciat. Conf. Mayer. Phil. S. p. 1. p. 196.) Ergo est vel civitas vel regio aliqua Assyriæ, ubi populus captivus est habitus. De appellativa vocis acceptione quasi ex סוף & רדה constaret finemque dominatus notaret, etsi ea quoque Junio & B. Tarno- vio placuerit, recte Dn. Pfeifferus observat: quod ta- lis compositio insolentior sit: absurdior autem Cor- nelii στοχασμὸς q. sit ex סוף & ארץ: pro Hierony- mi autem sententia, quod vox Assyriorum lingua terminum notet, plausibilius huc trahi censet Chal- daicum ספר littus, portus.

CIVITATES AVSTRI) Civitatem Austri. Quia ter- minum dixerat, ostendit quem terminum intelligat, nempe Arabiæ eam partem, quæ ad Austrum Judææ objacet, ubi regnum fuit Saba, 1. Reg. 10, 1. collato loco Matth. 12, 42. Vide de hac re Josephum dicto loco 12, 12. 1. Macc. 5, 17. 25.

## 1:21
Verse 21.

AND SAVIORS SHALL ASCEND ON MOUNT ZION TO JUDGE MOUNT ZION, TO JUDGE MOUNT ESAU) Saviors are to be understood, who saved themselves from captivity: whence in a like sense the LXX said ἀνασωζόμενοι, Aquila and Theodotion σεσωσμένοι: that is, those who were saved. But by those who were saved, understand their descendants, who, acting in Jerusalem, judged the Idumeans: Hyrcanus, namely, and his successors.

AND THE KINGDOM SHALL BE THE LORD'S) Not then any longer will the Jews obey foreign kings, but God, and there will be a theocracy, as of old.

Grotius understands all these things of the bodily salvation and happiness of the Jews, insisting in this upon the footsteps of the Rabbis, concerning whom Jerome [speaks] at this place; which things indeed not only Hugo Victorinus and Remigius, but also Cyril of Alexandria in a certain way followed, nay even those who accepted it according to the letter concerning the bodily subjugation of the Idumeans after the return from the Babylonian captivity, even though they left a spiritual liberation for the mystical sense, not only Papists, Ribera, Cornelius, Sa, Tirinus, Menochius, but also Reformed [scholars], Drusius, Pareus, not to speak of those who tear the text apart, explaining some things of bodily, others of spiritual liberation with Calvin, Junius, and Christoph. à Castro. But that they are to be accepted only of spiritual salvation and happiness, the remaining majority of Christian interpreters maintain by common calculation. In the first place, however, that application to the times of Sennacherib is false. For we have previously observed that this prophecy does not look to that. And it seems that Grotius either assumed or devised that hypothesis, that it treats of salvation shown to the people in the times of Sennacherib, solely to elude the explanation of Christian interpreters concerning spiritual salvation. Furthermore, that gloss is not sufficiently consistent with itself. For presently it makes a huge leap from the times of Sennacherib to the times of the Maccabees. Presently it passes to the kingdom of Hyrcanus, which is separated by a great interval from Sennacherib. Thirdly, the subject does not fit. For here the discourse is not of the tribe of Judah alone, but of the whole house of Jacob, and of the house of Joseph, v. 18. But there was no liberation of the Israelites from the Assyrian captivity. Whence Blessed Luther comments thus on the words: AND ON MOUNT ZION THERE SHALL BE SALVATION: This is the second part of this prophecy, in which, with the Jews led away into captivity, and the Idumeans, who had insulted the Jews, laid waste in turn, He promises another kingdom, which does not

And nothing else can be understood but the spiritual kingdom of Christ propagated through the Gospel into all nations. The Jewish people were divided into two kingdoms: into the kingdom of Israel, which, once devastated, was never again reparable, and into the kingdom of Judah, which was changed into the kingdom of Christ. This is what is supremely necessary to be understood by those who read the Prophets, in whose books there is frequent mention of these two kingdoms. Therefore, it is important to know that the Prophet speaks here of the spiritual kingdom of Christ. This is what the letter itself compels us to believe. For when he says: THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL POSSESS THOSE WHO HAD POSSESSED THEM: he indicates that the house of Jacob would recover the kingdom for itself, and would expand it, and would subject to itself those whose dominion it had previously endured. This is what that word in Hebrew, Jarasch, signifies, which our interpreter rendered as 'to possess,' but did not render the force of the Hebrew word. For it signifies properly that which the Germans call 'occupare' (to occupy). But because he joins the kingdom of Judah with the kingdom of Joseph or Israel, which nevertheless was never restored, and says that both would recover their former strength, those contradictions compel us to understand this passage as referring to the spiritual kingdom of Christ, namely that there would be Apostles from the Israelite people, and other disciples of Christ, who by the new preaching of the Gospel would subject the whole world to themselves, and thus would institute a new and eternal kingdom. And this is what he says, that on Mount Zion there would be an escape and a new salvation. That is, from Zion would go forth such a preaching which, if believed, would liberate from death, sin, and the underworld, and that this would come first from Zion, just as Isaiah also says in chapter 2: 'Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.' And Joel 2: 'In Jerusalem there shall be salvation.' And Psalm 110: 'The Lord shall send forth thy rod out of Zion,' etc. Thus Blessed Luther.

Fourthly, the former Theocracy was not restored to the Jews, as regards their earthly kingdom, nor was their former happiness restored. When therefore the Prophet says: AND THE KINGDOM SHALL BE THE LORD'S, it is manifest that it treats of the spiritual kingdom, which the Lord claims for Himself alone and immediately, of which Dan. 2:44, c. 7:14, Ps. 89:31 (2 Sam. 7:12), Ps. 2:6, Ps. 45:7, Ps. 72:8, Is. 9:9, Jer. 23:5, Zech. 9:9, Amos 9:11. Wherefore we have an evident prophecy concerning Christ, that He is to be the perpetual King of His Church, Luke 1:33, 71, Ezek. 14:9, Joel 3:17, to whom as head all things are to be subjected, Eph. 1:22.

Fifthly, when salvation is said to be on Mount Zion, it does not so much imply the preservation of holy worship as it is a description of those who will be in this new kingdom, namely that the SAINTS will be in it, so that it may be distinguished from worldly kingdoms, which do not confer true holiness, Is. 49, Jer. 23:6, 1 Cor. 1:30.

Sixthly, when Scripture treats of salvation on Mount Zion, it indicates spiritual salvation in the kingdom of the Messiah, whom God established as King on Mount Zion, Ps. 2:6, cf. Ps. 14:7, Is. 35:10, ch. 25:6 seqq., ch. 52:7, Nah. 1:15 (Rom. 10:25), Joel 3:7, Zech. 9:9. And thus is also designated the place in which the kingdom of the Messiah was to begin, Is. 2:3, Mic. 4:2. Add Matt. 15:26, Luke 24, Acts 2:29, ch. 13:16. Therefore Theodoret: 'He announces salvation arisen for all in Zion, and sanctification thence poured forth into the whole world through the cross of the Savior.'

Seventhly, the amplitude and expansion of the kingdom of the Messiah is presented here, which befits none but the time of the New Testament. The house of Jacob, that is, the Israelite kingdom, shall possess those by whom it had itself been possessed, namely the Chaldeans and other enemies. Which was never corporally completed. Again, when it is said: And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of

Esau stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them, and there shall be no remnants of the house of Esau, that is certainly wrongly snatched at regarding the deeds of the Maccabees against the Idumeans. For these were not of such magnitude that they could respond to this so ample a promise. Not just some consumption of the Esauites is designated, but a total overthrow of their power, so that no remnants of the house of Esau survive. And the subjection of the Edomites is promised to the Israelites, that by hereditary right they shall possess the South along with Mount Esau, just as they are also said to be about to possess the plain, and the land of the Philistines, and the region of Ephraim, and the region of Samaria, which κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν (according to the letter) were never fulfilled. For the land of Samaria was not restored to the Ephraimites: nor did they ever possess the whole land of Canaan, or all the places of the Canaanites, and whatever belonged to the Canaanites, after they were led away by Shalmaneser. For here the boundaries of the whole of Canaan are fixed as far as Sarepta of the Sidonians, which boundary is towards the North, 1 Kings 17:9. The Southern border is constituted by the cities of the South, according to Grotius. Judea, says Cornelius à Lapide, has Idumea to the South; to the West, Philistia; to the North, Samaria and Galilee; to the East, Gilead, Moab, and Ammon. Although, however, the Jews under the Maccabean leaders, and especially John Hyrcanus the High Priest, brought many cities of Syria and Idumea under their power, so much so that Hyrcanus, 130 years before the birth of Christ, compelled the Idumeans to circumcision, and to adopt the rest of the formula of living according to Jewish rites, unless they wished to be expelled from their country, from which time they also began to be counted among the Jews, as Josephus testifies, book 13, ch. 17, yet that dominion was unstable and often troubled, so much so that the Jews themselves confess that this notable prophecy concerning the kingdom over the Idumeans and other peoples has not yet been completed: and therefore it is to be believed that these things were fulfilled, and are still being fulfilled, spiritually in the kingdom of Christ. For here the Ephraimites, and Jews, Sidonians, Idumeans, Samaritans, and other nations are subjected to Christ, which prophecy concerning the calling of all nations is explained more fully elsewhere. Cf. Ps. 2:8, Ps. 72:8, Ps. 110:6. Isa. 49:6, ch. 54, ch. 60:13. The calling of the Idumeans was fulfilled by Christ himself, as is recorded in Mark 3:8, that a great multitude came to Christ from Galilee, Jerusalem, Idumea, and the regions beyond the Jordan. But afterwards, when the Apostles preached the Gospel in Samaria and the neighboring places, a notable Church was gathered in those lands. Whence Christoph. à Castro regarding that exposition which Grotius made his own: 'However, this (opinion) is opposed by the fact that from these passages (from the Books of Maccabees) it is only gathered that the Maccabees conquered and destroyed some cities, but did not possess the lands subject to these nations in peace; so that the Jews might have settled in them as in their own homes: for if it had happened so, it would properly be said that a kingdom had been acquired for the Lord from all these nations and regions: for the enemies remained for the most part in their own homes, although terrified by the mighty works of the Maccabees.' Lyra, however, Vatabl., Montanus, Rupert, and others, who understand these things concerning the expansion of the Gospel, explain it thus: The Apostles and apostolic men, having gone out from Judea towards all four corners of the world bordering on Judea, will convert all men to the end of the Gospel, as much the Idumeans to the South, as the Philistines to the West, and the Samaritans, and the Galileans to the North, and to the East Gilead, the Arabs, and those who inhabit that region. For in Acts 1:8, Christ said to his disciples, 'You shall be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth': and Acts 8:1, 'All were scattered' throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, apart from the Apostles: there is no doubt that the Apostles themselves also went into other neighboring regions a little later; thus the Apostles and disciples first subdued these other nations named by Obadiah: afterwards they brought the message of the Gospel into all parts of the world. And afterwards: The meaning will be: the faithful sons of Israel, the Apostles and disciples, who were dispersed through various parts of the world by fear of the persecutions of the infidel Jews, by the power of their Gospel, will occupy all the places in which the Canaanites formerly dwelt, having been cast out from there, as much of Illyricum as of Africa and Germany, even to the Gauls, to which came Maximinus, Lazarus with his sisters, Martial, and others. Or certainly the Apostles, and the faithful Jews, who will dwell in the places of the former Canaanites, will shed their Evangelical light upon every western part, even to the furthest limit of the Gauls; sent by Christ, when He said in Mark 16:15. Go into the whole world and preach the Gospel to every creature. And Isaiah 56:19. I will send from them, who shall have been saved, to the nations in the sea, into Africa and Lydia, and Greece, and Italy and to the islands afar off, and they shall announce my glory to the nations. Similarly, what is said concerning the transmigration or the exiles of Jerusalem, understanding Sepharad as Spain, was explained by a Castro concerning the Apostles in this manner: The Jews converted in Spain to the faith, who had migrated into it under Titus, or under Hadrian, or who went there to proclaim the faith, will possess, that is, will illuminate with the light of the Gospel, the cities of the South. Burgensis understands Africa. Lyra understands Spain itself, which James illuminated. Others better understand the southern region of Spain, which we call Baetica. Others think that the new world is signified, which is to the south of Spain, or established under the southern region: which in our age the Spaniards have subjected to their empire, and by the doctrine of the Gospel, having overthrown the worship of idols, have subjected to Christ. We will understand it more truly concerning the first preachers, James and his companions, who were Jews, who, dispersed into Spain, occupied it, as did also the Apostle Paul, especially the southern region. But above all, our Blessed Luther deserves to be heard here again: On those words: AND THE HOUSE OF JACOB SHALL BE FIRE: In this universal subjection of all nations, he says that the Idumeans also are to be subjected to this kingdom. All things are absurd and conflict with history if we understand a corporal subjection. For what is less fitting than that the house of Jacob should be fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, which itself was already as if reduced to ashes, and the house of Esau, that is, Idumea, should be stubble to be devoured by the flame? For the house of Joseph never returned after the Babylonian captivity, nor did the house of Judah ever possess the Idumeans. Finally, this is the most absurd of all, that when he had previously prophesied that all the Idumeans would perish and be reduced to nothing, he should here at last say that they are also to be devoured by fire. Therefore, these things compel us entirely to understand this concerning the Gospel spread by the Apostles and by other disciples from Israel into all nations, by which preaching they devoured and incorporated them into the kingdom of Christ spiritually, nor can they be snatched from His hand any longer, as Christ says in the Gospel. For when the Gospel is truly grasped, Satan does not easily prevail, which is what happened, as the Annals indicate. For that Petraean Arabia, in which the Idumeans were, was a notable place of holy men when the Gospel was revealed, which Isaiah also promises. THERE SHALL BE NO SURVIVORS. He will so subjugate the house of Esau to Himself that not even survivors shall remain, that is, there will be nothing that can prevail against this kingdom of Christ. For through the Gospel, Christians become masters of all creatures. These things [are] concerning the power and efficacy of the preached Gospel among the nations,

Jerome did not translate the Hebrew text of v. 19 badly in the Vulgate: And those who are to the South shall inherit the mountain (or mountainous regions) of Esau, and those who formerly dwelt in the plains will possess the Philistines (their neighbors); nay, they shall even possess the region of Ephraim, and the region of Samaria (that is, the kingdom which the Kings of Israel once held) they shall occupy, and the tribe of Benjamin shall possess (the region of) Gilead. Which translation Osiander therefore retained without amendment; but Grotius amended it without cause. For what is it to inherit the south with the mountain of Esau! The plain with the Philistines? And why is the particle את in the others here to be taken as a sign of the accusative concerning the field of Ephraim and Samaria, but concerning the mountain of Esau and the Philistines to be explained by the preposition 'with'? Therefore Drusius confirms the Vulgate: There are not wanting those who think it should be translated, they shall inherit the South, with the mountain of Esau. But these did not notice that it follows afterwards: And the exiles of Jerusalem, who are in Sepharad, shall inherit the cities of the South. The southern Jews, הנגב, the word sounds word for word South or midday. But it is a figure, which grammarians call a metonymy: those who use it place, for example, the land for the inhabitants of the land, and heaven for the inhabitants of heaven. In exactly the same way, the south is placed here for the inhabitants of the south. You will say: why then do you translate it, southern Jews? I answer, because he is not dealing here with the south simply, but κατὰ συνεκδοχὴν (by synecdoche) he calls the southern part of Judea the South, or that tract which looked toward the south and Idumea. The mountain of Esau (Idumea. Synecdoche). And the plains, השפלה, signifies the flat and low and level tract of Judea, whose inhabitants are designated here by the same name. There was also another tract, whose inhabitants were called mountaineers, because they dwelt in the mountains of Judea. For that part was mountainous. Thus I say that those inhabiting Judea, some southern, some in the plains, and others in the mountains, were called by the ancients Palestinians or Philistines from the place in which they dwelt, whose cities were Gath, Gaza, Ascalon, Acaron, Azotus. The Greeks designate these by the common name ἀλλοφύλους, i.e., aliens. This is Drusius. Lud. de Dieu also agrees: I entirely praise the ancient Interpreter, who took הנגב and השפלה in the nominative case, and translated, And they shall possess, who are to the south, the mount of Esau, and who are in the plains, the Philistines: so that the construction is the same as ובנימין את הגלעד. And Benjamin shall possess Gilead. Those who are to the south or meridian are seen to be the Judeans properly so called, to whom the tribe of Judah had fallen, the southern region of the land of Canaan, and bordering on the mountains of Esau or Seir to the south. From this is rightly distinguished השפלה, the plain, namely that part of the land of Canaan which, with respect to Judea, was flat and level. For the greatest part of Judea was mountainous, and therefore drier and more arid, and truly נגב, for that word properly denotes dry and arid land. B. Luther, as well as the Belgian Paraphrast, rendered the same sense, although they also observed another interpretation in their annotations, that of the Tigurines and Vatablus, which we would certainly judge to be preferred to the Grotian, if one must depart from the Vulgate: And they shall inherit the South, that is, the mountains, and the plains, that is, the Philistines. As for the letter of verse 20, the Vulgate is correct in the first member: And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel (shall possess) all the places (or WHICH ARE) of the Canaanites even unto Sarepta. Which Grotius did not disapprove. But the same reason for the construction exists in the second member: Therefore that is not conveniently rendered in the Vulgate, and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Bosphorus: or by others, which is in Sepharad. For the entire sense is held in this colon, and the analogy of the preceding member, and the accent in Hebrew teaches. Therefore, Grotius did not translate these badly: And the transmigration of Jerusalem, those which are of Sepharad shall possess, or those which are in the end of the dominion as Tremellius rendered it. For the interpreters vary greatly concerning that word. The Belgic paraphrase also agrees. But if the Atnach accent does not make a colon here, the version of B. Luther can be retained, which in this verse excels the Vulgate: and Osiander also rendered the Hebrew thus: And the captives of the army of the children of Israel, who are detained among the Canaanites as far as the town of Zarpath, and the Jerusalemite captives, who dwell in Sepharad (a city in Babylonia), shall possess the southern cities. The sense is: The Church of Christ will receive the greatest increases among the Gentiles. Calvin is correct here: God had promised to the posterity of Abraham the whole land from the Euphrates to the sea. Now the land was never possessed by the sons of Abraham. This was done through their sloth and ingratitude, as is sufficiently known: David extended the borders in his time: but yet he only rendered those tributary to himself, whom God had ordered to be killed. Thus that blessing was never fulfilled, because the people themselves placed an obstacle: Now the Prophet, when he speaks of the restoration of the Church, at the same time teaches that the people, who shall have returned from exile, will occupy all that region which had been promised to the Fathers: as if he were saying, now a full and solid inheritance will be yours. Now it is certain that this was never completed: we see that a small part of the land was possessed by the Jews. What then does this prophecy mean for itself? Certainly it is sufficiently evident that the Prophet is here prophesying about the kingdom of Christ: and we know that the Church was then truly restored: and that the Jews not only recovered their former state, from which they had fallen, but that the kingdom was increased. For what kind of splendor was there of both the Kingdom and the Temple under Christ? The Prophet understands this now, when he promises to the Jews the inheritance which they had lost: nay, God then dilated the borders of Judea, therefore he shows that they were not only to be restored to their former fortune, but that the kingdom was to be increased in splendor and opulence, when, namely, Christ had arrived. Thus Calvin. So also Gualterus, hom. 4, p. 123. The Jews after their return from Babylon never extended the borders of their kingdom so far, but the Apostles, according to the precept of Christ, began to preach in Zion or Jerusalem, and there, when persecution arose, as if with divided forces they occupied the whole of Judea, soon entering Samaria they brought this also to Christ. Thence they invaded the parts of Zidon, and such was the power of the Evangelical preaching that it could not be restrained even by the sea, etc. Among the Papists, Ribera in this place explains it concerning the proclamation of the Apostles in Judea, Samaria, Azotus in Palestine, in Joppa, Caesarea, Acts 8 and 10, and when they were dispersed as far as Phoenicia, in which was Sarepta, came ch. 11. Cornelius à Lapide also acknowledges that these things were more fully fulfilled in the Apostles under the New Testament. But because the Maccabees indeed subjected these places, but did not occupy them (for the Jews did not dwell in these places, but the Philistines, Samaritans, Idumeans), which nevertheless Obadiah signifies here will happen, saying: They shall inherit, and shall possess; hence it was more fully fulfilled mystically by the Apostles, who, having founded the Church in Judea, going out thence to the neighboring Samaritans, Idumeans, Philistines, and other peoples, subjected them all to themselves; thus Lyranus, Arias, Vatablus. and à Castro, who in his paraphrase says, The Apostles and Apostolic men will distribute among themselves the whole surrounding region, which they may subject to Christ by Evangelical war, and those who shall have gone to the south will traverse Idumea; those to the west, the whole land of the Philistines; those to the north, Galilee and Samaria; but those who to the East, will possess the Gileadites and Arabs for Christ: but by name Benjamin, that is, St. Paul, sprung from the tribe of Benjamin, will possess Gilead: because he himself converted Arabia, of which Gilead is a part: for as he himself says, Galatians 1:17, I went into Arabia, that I might preach there according to my calling and office, and make the Arabs Christians. But above others, our B. Luther has excellently executed these things on the words, AND THEY WHO ARE AT THE SOUTH SHALL POSSESS, & seq. Tom. 3. Jen. Lat. f. 521. There is a wonderful contradiction here, if you understand the letter and some external kingdom. First he says, they shall possess, then, they shall be possessed. Likewise, they shall possess the plains of the Philistines. Furthermore, which is the greatest thing, the kingdom of Israel was divided into twelve tribes, and it was diligently provided by the law of Moses that the tribes should not be mixed among themselves, which is to be seen in Moses. Since therefore he openly says here that the southerners, that is, those who are at the south, will possess the mount of Esau: Likewise that Benjamin will possess Gilead, contrary to how the land was divided by divine command by Moses and Joshua, etc., these things are to be understood in an entirely different way than the bare letter has. The meaning therefore is: The Christians, the Apostles, and other disciples, who are to be at the South, in Mount Zion namely, in which the Gospel will first be preached, they, I say, by their preaching will make fruit among the Idumeans. AND THE PLAINS. More correctly, the Lowlands, or the pleasant valleys between the mountains, Die Gründes, shall possess the Philistines, which thing was never done corporally after the Babylonian captivity. For even the whole kingdom could not overcome and subject the Philistines to itself. Therefore it is to be understood concerning spiritual subjection through the Gospel. EPHRAIM. This also is against the law. Therefore it was done through the Apostles, when they went into Samaria to announce the Gospel. You will therefore diligently note this text, as a clear and certain testimony that the law was to be abrogated when Christ came through the Gospel. For Benjamin was on this side of the Jordan. Gilead, however, was beyond the Jordan in the tribe of Gad. Therefore necessity compels us to refer everything to the preaching of the Gospel. AND THE TRANSMIGRATION OF THE ARMY. This, however, is far more absurd than the former, namely that those were to possess the whole land of the Canaanites, who nevertheless were led away into captivity, and never brought back. To which, if you look only at the letter, what can be said that is more absurd? The same is true of what follows concerning the transmigration of Jerusalem, that is, that the captives from Israel were to possess the cities of the South, i.e., those cities which are situated around Jerusalem and in Edom. Thus Luther.

Eighth. The coming of the saviors onto Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, so that the kingdom may be the Lord's, cannot be understood otherwise than of spiritual saviors. The Belgian paraphrasts explain it as referring to Christ, the most perfect Savior, because by the plural number the perfection of Christ's salvation is noted: comparing Ps. 40:10, Ps. 73:22, Prov. 1:20. But others more correctly explain it of the Apostles and heralds of the word, who are saviors διακονικῶς (ministerially), who are said to save through the word, not of themselves (for thus they are nothing at all, 1 Cor. 3:7), but as they are θεοῦ συνεργοὶ (God's fellow-workers), see 1 Cor. 9:22, 1 Thess. 2:13, 1 Tim. 4:16, Jude v. 23. Who judge the mount of Esau, or the Edomites, that is, by synecdoche any enemies of the Church, by the word and by writings, refuting the impiety of the world, John 16:8, and announcing the judgment to come, Acts 17:31, just as the Apostles also are to judge on the last day, Matt. 19:28, Luke 22:30. Others understand the word 'judging' not of punishment, but of governance, as Drusius does with Augustine, book 18 of The City of God, chapter 31. The mount of Esau is Idumea, by which is signified the Church of the Gentiles, which those saved from Mount Zion defended, so that the kingdom might be the Lord's. This was obscure before it happened, but who that is faithful does not acknowledge it once done? B. Luth. Motchiim

He calls leaders saviors, as it is in the book of Judges, where he sent them many saviors, that is, leaders who would lead them, and preside over them, and go before them, if at any time it were necessary to fight with enemies. Thus here the Apostles and other disciples are called saviors, namely, those who, by announcing the Gospel, that joyful message, delivered them from all enemies, from all the insults of Satan and the gates of hell, and who judged them in the Faith, ruled over them in justice and judgment, and thus prepared an eternal kingdom for the Lord. Similarly Cornelius à Lapide: He clearly signifies that the descendants of Esau will not perish, but will be judged, i.e., ruled by the Zionites and Jews, so that they may become Jews, and the kingdom of God. And afterwards to the words: And then the kingdom will be the Lord's: This was true in an incipient way in the Maccabees, fully in the militant Church of Christ, and will be most full in the triumphant Church. These things can be admitted so far, as the happiness of the Church promised after the return from captivity, and which began under the Maccabees, and was further continued in the time of the New Testament: provided one is careful not to establish a double sense of the same words, and that the same things are not understood both of the return and bodily happiness, in a literal sense, and of spiritual happiness at the same time, in a mystical sense.

Ninth, to be compared with this oracle are those things which occur elsewhere in the prophecies concerning the conversion of the Idumeans, such as Num. 24, 17. 18. A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a rod shall spring up from Israel, and shall strike the leaders of Moab, and shall lay waste all the children of Seth. And IDUMEA shall be his possession, the inheritance of SEIR shall yield to its enemies. Which prophecy agrees remarkably with ours, and is explained by the Rabbis themselves concerning the Messiah. Likewise Amos 9, 11. 12. In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild it, as in the days of old, THAT THEY MAY POSSESS THE REMNANT OF IDUMEA. That this deals with the conversion of the Gentiles is evident from Acts 15, 16. Likewise Is. 11, 14. And they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines by the sea, together they shall plunder the children of the East. IDUMEA and Moab shall be the command of their hands, and the children of Ammon shall be obedient. That these things deal with the time of the New Testament is certain from the whole context of chapter 11, and the Eucharistic song subjoined in chapter 12.

Tenth, there is added the authority of St. Peter, that ALL the Prophets bear witness concerning Christ, Acts 10, 43. Since Obadiah cannot be excluded from their number, his prophecy must be accepted in such a way that he himself is not the only one who is ἀσύμβολος (without a share) in this matter, especially since the very words of the Prophet refer not obscurely to the salvation and kingdom of Christ, and the conversion of the Gentiles. This not only have Christian interpreters generally acknowledged, but it is also evident from the suffrages of some Rabbis. In the tractate Schabbat, chapter 6, it is held thus: The Prophets did not prophesy except for the days of the Messiah. R. Moses Maimonides in his Hilkot in Schophetim, chapter 11, compared the prophecy of Balaam concerning the rod from Israel with this prophetic passage, in which he indeed mixes in his own comments, as if Balaam were speaking of two different things, yet he acknowledges that Obadiah is prophesying here about the times of the Messiah. In the distinction of Balaam it is said and prophesied concerning the first Messiah, who is David, and who saved Israel from the hand of those who oppressed them: and concerning the second Messiah, who is to be born from his sons, who is to save Israel from the hand of the sons of Esau: and there it says in Numbers 24, 17. I shall see him, but not now, this is David, I shall behold him, but not near, this is King Messiah.
