A star has risen out of Jacob, this is David, and a rod shall rise from Israel, this is King Messiah, and he shall break the leaders of Moab, this is David, of whom it is said 2 Kings 8, 2. And he struck Moab, and measured them with a line, and he overthrew all the children of Seth, this is King Messiah, of whom it is said Zech. 9, 10. And his dominion from sea even to sea, etc. And Edom shall be his possession, this is David, as it is said 2 Kings 8, 2. And all Edom became David's servants, etc. And the possession of Seir shall be for his enemies, this is the Messiah, as it is said in Obadiah v. 21. And saviors shall ascend onto Mount Zion, to judge Mount Seir. These are the words of Maimonides. From the Christian Doctors we have brought forward before St. Augustine, who explained these things concerning the time of the New Testament. With Augustine, however, agree Rupertus, Lyranus, Burgensis in his additions to this place, Mercerus, Gualtherus, Vatablus, Isidorus, Arias Montanus, the Belgians, and Albertus and Dionysius choose that sense as the better one, as reported by Christ. à Castro, who proves the same interpretation with two not-to-be-despised reasons. First: because it is evident from no history that this temporary happiness happened to the Jews from the return from Babylon until the coming of Christ. Whence Jerome: Whether this was done, let the Jew see. Therefore, the words of Obadiah cannot be explained concerning temporary happiness. That assumed proposition is proven: the Jews were never so superior that they took the Idumeans from the midst, since although they were worn down at times, just as the Jews themselves were, they were never destroyed. But Obadiah prophesies that the remnants of the Idumeans would not have remained: who nevertheless survived intact, when the Jews were overthrown by the Romans. Therefore, he speaks of another devastation, namely, a spiritual one. Furthermore, it is customary for the Prophets to end their prophecies of things to be done through Christ with a most joyful commemoration, by which they both console the afflicted, and the opinion of Peter is truly confirmed in his 1st Epistle c. 1, 10. Concerning which salvation the Prophets have inquired and searched, who prophesied of the grace to come in you. These are the words of Christoph. à Castro, who, as it appears, combines both opinions in this way: that of those who understand this oracle concerning the return of the Jews from Babylon, which he attributes to Jerome, Cyril, Theodoret, Remigius, Hugh of St. Victor, Albert, Haymo, and Dionysius, and that of those who explain it concerning the Evangelical business and the time of the New Testament with Augustine; [he says] that this prophecy began to be fulfilled after the return from Babylon, but the happiness of the Jews was completed and perfected then, when with Christ as leader the Apostles went forth from Mount Sion through all the regions of the world, and subdued the Jewish and impious nations, until the kingdom was made the Lord's. He even attempts to explain Jerome himself, along with Theodoret, Haymo, and Albert, as holding that same opinion: and he says that many others interpret it so, and among these Robert, whose words he praises: True salvation will be in Sion, which cannot be true unless it is eternal. It began to be fulfilled literally when they restored the second temple and city, into which the true Savior and Redeemer of Israel, Christ Jesus, was about to enter, Malach. 3, 2. For the Prophet foretells something deeper in this place, after the manner of all the Prophets, namely the true and eternal liberation in Christ. Thus, therefore, à Castro might seem to combine both opinions. But if his mind is weighed more correctly, he rather makes a certain compromise out of both. And therefore Christoph. à Castro does not properly mean à Castro, that under the same words both the historical and spiritual sense are contained (which he pronounces to be impossible), nor does he think this prophecy was completed as regards history, as regards all parts, so that the same might signify mystically the business of Christ, but he explains himself thus: that Obadiah cast his eyes upon all time after the return from Babylon, and looked upon the temporal and spiritual happiness of the Jews, and the victories won from visible and spiritual war, and in this he preferred the Jews, who had escaped to Mount Zion, to all other nations; and he claims that this full happiness of the Jews was foretold in the literal sense, under the words of the nations and places which he brings forward. And he notes that there are not a few words in Holy Scripture which promise goods so excellent that, unless spiritual things are added to temporal ones, that which is primarily signified by them is not fulfilled; wherefore that whole good, being so excellent, must be fulfilled by both temporal and spiritual things. Thus v. 19, AND ON MOUNT ZION THERE SHALL BE SALVATION, he thinks foretells the overthrow of evils, both bodily and spiritual, which began after 70 years on Mount Zion, and was perfected and completed through Christ, when He communicated salvation there to many, and chose and instituted the Apostles, who, as leaders, would sally forth from there and conquer the whole earth. The following words: AND THERE SHALL BE HOLINESS, he explains thus: There shall be a mount of holiness, as of old, i.e., a holy mount, and consecrated to God, on account of the temple and the worship performed in it after the captivity, and through the presence of Christ and the coming of the Holy Spirit upon that mount, from whence holiness began and was poured forth through the whole world, as Theodoret says. He is occupied in explaining v. 20 thus: More truly and clearly: the house of Jacob, having returned from the Babylonian captivity, will occupy its possessions, which the nations had assumed for themselves, and the properties of the nations themselves in part, under the Maccabees. And then at last the Apostles and disciples, the descendants of Jacob, having gone out from Mount Zion, of which it was written that the law shall go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, will subject to themselves and to Christ all the nations bordering on and situated far around Jerusalem, which had once dominated them, such as the Persians, Medes, Greeks, Romans, and the like. Such is the explanation of that Jesuit.

While we may concede the temporal happiness of the Jews, the benefits and victories which are promised here concern spiritual matters, and properly look to the times of the New Testament, for which the universal calling of the nations was reserved; wherefore, with St. Augustine, B. Gesner, B. Wigand, B. Pappus, B. Winckelmann, B. Tarnovius, the Weimar and Belgian Paraphrasts, likewise Drusius, and other interpreters previously praised, we judge that these things are to be understood solely concerning the kingdom of Christ under the New Testament and the calling of the nations, at which time salvation was made on Mount Zion, and the house of Jacob possessed those who had possessed them: we leave no room at all for Cocceius's glosses about some future conversion of the Synagogue, I know not what. But we think that those things were to be fulfilled at the beginning of the New Testament, and are even now being fulfilled in a certain way. Just as Castrius himself in his paraphrase has handed down this sense alone: But from all these calamities my people will escape on Mount Zion, because it will excel in holiness on account of the renewed worship and the coming of my Holy Spirit. Whence the sons of Israel, having gone forth like fire to stubble, will cut down the Idumeans, and convert them to their religion, and like fire will kindle and devour them, so that no one of them remains who is not subject to the true religion. For so the Lord has determined. And those Israelites, the Apostles, and Apostolic men will attribute to themselves all the surrounding region, which they may subject to Christ by an Evangelical war, and those who have gone out to the South will scour Idumea; those to the West, the whole land of the Philistines; those to the North, Galilee and Samaria; but those to the East will possess the Gileadites and Arabs for Christ. Moreover, whoever among the Israelite Apostles shall have migrated further, they will bathe all those places in their light, into which the Canaanites were dispersed, even as far as the Gauls, and those who shall have migrated from Jerusalem to Spain, surrounding the Herculean Bosphorus, will subject the whole Southern region to Christ. But then at last they will return as victors, as Saviors of the nations, to Mount Zion, from whence they had gone out, for the subjugating of Mount Esau in particular: and thus the Davidic kingdom will be restored to the Lord. So far the paraphrase of Castrius, in sum consonant with our explanation, which is this: that the land of all nations was to be occupied, or all nations were to be possessed in the time of the New Testament by the Jews, receiving the Messiah as King, which was fulfilled when the Apostles disseminated the doctrine of the Gospel through all nations and the whole world, and captured and subjected all nations to Christ under the obedience of faith. Thus therefore the Kingdom was made for the LORD, namely for the Messiah, who is Jehovah, GOD blessed above all forever, of whose kingdom there shall be no end, to whom be glory and honor for ever and ever. Amen!

But in truth, although these things may be more correct than those of Grotius, and it may be said that the Prophet, without prejudice to the unity of the sense, alluded to bodily victories, and at the same time embraced in his mind both temporal and spiritual happiness, and it is not inconvenient that he looked to every time after the return from Babylon regarding some predicates: I fear, however, that that exposition of Castrius can altogether consist with a single sense. For if the discourse is about the former possessions in the land of Judea to be occupied after the return, which the nations had claimed for themselves, how will the same phrases treat at the same time of the Apostles, who were to subject the nations to themselves through the word, without a double sense? For with the same words with which the Prophet prophesies about the Idumeans being truly conquered and subjugated by the Jews, he certainly does not treat of the impious and infidels being conquered by the disciples of Christ through the efficacy of the word and subjected to Christ. Wherefore, however much some allusion to the return and hap-

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ET ASCENDENT SALVATORES IN MON- TEM SION JVDICARE MONTEM SION, JVDI- CARE MONTEM ESAV) Salvatores intelligendi, qui semet servarint ex captivitate: unde pari sensu LXX. dixe- runt ἀνασωζόμενοι, Aquila & Theodotion σεσωσμένοι: id est, qui servati fuerint. Per illos autem qui servati fuerint, intelli- ge eorum posteros, qui Jerosolymis agentes jus Idumæis dixere: Hircanus scilicet, & successores ejus.

ET ERIT DOMINO REGNVM) Non tunc ul- tra Judæi externis regibus, sed Deo parebunt, & erit θεοκρα- τία, ut olim.

Omnia hæc Grotius de corporali salute, ac feli- citate Judæorum intelligit, insistens in eo Rabbino- rum vestigiis, de quibus Hieron. ad h. l. quæ vero non tantum Hugo Victorinus, & Remigius, sed etiam Cyrillus Alex. quodammodo sectatus, imo etiam illi, qui secundum literam de corporali Idumæo- rum subjugatione post reditum è captivitate Baby- lonica accepere, utut spiritualem liberationem sen- sui mystico reliquerint, non solum Papistæ, Ribera, Cornelius, Sa, Tirinus, Menochius, sed etiam Refor- mati, Drusius, Pareus, ne de illis dicamus, qui tex- tum discerpunt, nonnulla de corporali, alia de spiri- tuali liberatione explicantes cum Calvino, Junio, & Christoph. à Castro. Sed de spirituali tantum salute ac felicitate ea accipienda esse, communi calculo reliqui Christiani Interpp. plerique adstruunt. Pri- mum autem falsa est illa de Sennacheribi tempora applicatio. Non enim eo hanc spectare Propheti- am, antea observavimus. Et videtur Grotius illam hypothesin, quod de salute Sennacheribi tempori- bus populo exhibita agatur, solum ad eludendam Christianorum Interpp. explicationem de salute spirituali, vel assumsisse vel excogitasse. Porro non constat sibi satis illa glossa. Nam mox à Sennacheri- bi temporibus saltum ingentem facit ad Maccabæo- rum tempora. Mox ad Hyrcani regnum transit, quod magno intervallo à Sennacheribo distat. Tertio non congruit subjectum. Nam hic non de tribu Juda solum, sed de domo Jacob universa, & de domo Joseph sermo est v. 18. At Israëlitarum nulla fuit ex Assyriaca captivitate liberatio. Unde B. Lu- therus ad verba: ET IN MONTE SION ERIT SALVATIO, ita commentatur: Hæc altera pars est hujus Prophetiæ, in qua, abductis in captivita- tem Judæis, & vastatis rursum Idumæis, qui Judæis insultaverant, promittit aliud regnum, quod non

& potest aliud intelligi, nisi regnum spirituale Christi per Evangelium propagatum in omnes gentes. Divisus erat populus Judaicus in duo Regna, in regnum Israel, quod nunquam erat rursum reparabile semel devastatum, & in regnum Juda, quod mutatum est in regnum Christi. Id quod summopere necessarium est intelligi ab iis, qui Prophetas legunt, in quorum libris crebra sit horum duorum Regnorum mentio. Itaque scire refert, loqui hic Prophetam de spirituali regno Christi. Id quod ipsa litera cogit nos credere. Nam quum inquit. POSSIDEBIT DOMUS JACOB EOS, QVI SE POSSEDERANT: Indicat domum Jacob recuperaturam sibi Regnum, ac dilataturam, ac sibi subjecturam eos, quorum dominium antea est perpessa. Id quod significat verbum illud in Ebræo Jarasch, quod noster Interpres reddidit possidere, sed non reddidit vim Ebrææ vocis. Significat enim proprie id, quod Germani dicunt, occupare. Quia autem conjungit regnum Juda cum regno Joseph seu Israel, quod tamen nunquam restitutum est, & dicit utrumque recuperaturum pristinas vires, cogit nos pugnantia illa, ut de spirituali regno Christi hunc locum intelligamus, nempe futuros esse ex populo Israelitico Apostolos, & discipulos alios Christi, qui nova prædicatione Evangelii totum orbem sunt sibi subjecturi, sicque instituturi novum regnum & æternum. Atque hoc est, quod dicit, in monte Sion fore evasionem & salvationem novam. Hoc est, ex Sion exituram talem prædicationem, quæ credita liberaret à morte, peccato & inferis, hancque primum ex Sion venturam esse, sicut & Esaias ait cap. 2. De Sion exibit lex, & verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Et Joelis 2. in Jerusalem erit salvatio. Et Psal. 110. Ex Sion emittet Dominus sceptrum suum, &c. Hæc Beat. Lutherus.

Quarto penes Judæos non reddita fuit pristina Θεοκρατία, quod ad terrenum ipsorum regnum, nec restituta pristina felicitas. Quum ergo dicit Propheta: ET ERIT DOMINO REGNUM, manifestum est, de regno spirituali, quod sibi Dominus soli & immediate vendicat, agi, de quo Dan. 2, 44. c. 7, 14. Psal. 89, 31. (2. Sam. 7, 12.) Psal. 2, 6. Psal. 45, 7. Psal. 72, 8. Es. 9, 9. Jer. 23, 5. Zach. 9, 9. Amos 9, 11. Quapropter evidens habemus vaticinium de Christo, quod Ecclesiæ suæ Rex perpetuus futurus sit Luc. 1, 33. 71. Ezech. 14, 9. Joel 3, 17. cui tanquam capiti omnia sint subjicienda Ephes. 1, 22.

Quinto cum in monte Sion salvatio futura dicitur, non tam sancti cultus conservatio innuitur, quam descriptio futurorum in hoc novo regno, quod nempe SANCTI in eo futuri sint, ut à mundanis regnis distinguatur, quæ non conferunt veram sanctitatem Es. 49. Jer. 23, 6. 1. Cor. 1, 30.

Sexto cum de salvatione in monte Sion agit Scriptura, salutem spiritualem in regno Messiæ indicat, quem Deus in monte Sion Regem constituit Psal. 2, 6. conf. Psal. 14, 7. Es. 35, 10. cap. 25, 6. seqq. cap. 52, 7. Nah. 1, 15. (Rom. 10, 25.) Joel. 3, 7. Zach. 9, 9. Atque ita etiam designatur locus, in quo regnum Messiæ inchoari debuit Es. 2, 3. Mich. 4, 2. Adde Matth. 15, 26. Luc. 24, Act. 2, 29. cap. 13, 16. Ideo Theodoretus: Prænunciat salvationem omnibus exortam in Sion, & sanctificationem inde in omnem orbem terrarum profusam per crucem Salvatoris.

Septimo amplitudo & dilatatio Regni Messiæ ea hic exhibetur, quæ non nisi tempori N. T. convenit. Domus Jacob, id est, Regnum Israeliticum possidebit eos, à quibus ipsa possessa fuerat, puta Chaldæos, & alios hostes. Quod corporaliter nunquam completum fuit. Rursus cum dicitur: Et erit domus Jacob ignis & domus Joseph flamma, & domus

Esau stipula, & succendentur in eis, & devorabunt eos, & non erunt reliquiae domus Esau, id certe ad Maccabaeorum contra Idumaeos facta non nisi per- peram abripitur. Haec enim tanti non fuere, ut huic tam amplae promissioni respondeant. Non aliqua- lis tantum Esavitarum absumtio, sed totalis pote- statis eorum eversio designatur, ut nullae reliquiae domus Esavi superent. Et promittitur Israelitis subjectio Edomitarum, quod haereditario jure pos- seffuri sint Meridiem una cum monte Esau, sicuti etiam planitiem, & terram Philistinorum, & regionem Ephraim, & regionem Samariae possessuri dicuntur, quae κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν nunquam impleta sunt. Nam non restituta est Ephraimitis terra Samariae: nec posse- derunt ipsi unquam totam terram Canaan, vel omnia loca Cananaeorum, & quicquid Cananaeo- rum fuit, postquam abducti fuere à Salmanassare. Figuntur enim hic termini universae Cananaeae us- que ad Sareptam Sidoniorum, qui terminus est ver- sus Septentrionem 1. Reg. 17, 9. Limes Austrinus constituuntur civitates Austri, juxta Grotium. Ju- daea, inquit Cornelius à Lapide, ad Austrum habet Idu- meam: ad Occidentem Philisthaeam; ad Aquilonem Samariam, & Galilaeam, ad Orientem Galaad, Moab, & Ammon. Etsi autem Judaei Ducibus Maccabaeis, & imprimis Johanne Hircano Pontifice multas ur- bes Syriae & Idumaeae in suam potestatem redege- runt, adeo ut Hircanus Idumaeos annis 130. ante Christi nativitatem compulerit ad circumcisionem, & ut reliquam juxta Judaicos ritus vivendi formu- lam susciperent, nisi patria expelli vellent, ex quo etiam tempore inter Judaeos censeri ceperunt, teste Josepho l. 13. c. 17. instabilis tamen & saepe turbata fuit illa dominatio, adeo ut Judaei ipsi fateantur, hoc vaticinium insigne de regno super Idumaeos, & alios populos nondum esse completum: ideo- que spiritualiter in regno Christi haec impleta esse, atque etiamnum impleri, credendum est. Nam sub- jiciuntur hic Christo Ephraimitae, & Judaei, Sidonii, Idumaei, Samaritae, & aliae gentes, quod vaticinium de vocatione omnium gentium alibi fusius explicatur. Conf. Psal. 2, 8. Psal. 72, 8. Psal. 110, 6. Esa. 49, 6. c. 54. c. 60, 13. Vocatio Idumaeorum ab ipso Christo impleta est, sicut Marc. 3, 3. commemoratur, ma- gnam turbam è Galilaea, Hierosolymis, Idumaea & regionibus ultra Jordanem ad Christum venis- se. Postea vero cum Apostoli in Samaria & vici- nis locis Evangelium praedicarunt, insignis Eccle- sia iis in terris collecta fuit. Unde Christoph. à Ca- stro de illa expositione, quam Grotius suam fecit: Huic tamen (sententiae) obstat, quod ex his locis (è Libris Maccab.) tantum colligitur, Maccabaeos urbes aliquas debellasse, ac delevisse, non autem terras his gentibus subjectas cum pace possedisse; ita ut in eis Judaei tanquam in propriis sedibus consedissent: nam si ita occidisset, proprie diceretur, ex eis omnibus gen- tibus, & regionibus comparatum esse Domino re- gnum: manebant enim inimici magna ex parte in propriis sedibus, licet Macchabaeorum virtute con- territi. Lyra tamen, Vatabl. Montanus, Rupertus & caeteri, qui de dilatatione Evangelii haec intel- ligunt, ita explicant: Apostoli, virique Aposto- lici è Judaea egressi versus omnes quatuor mundi plagas Judaeae finitimas convertent omnes homi- nes ad finem Evangelicam, tam Idumaeos ad Au- strum, quam Philisthaeos ad Occidentem, & Sama- ritas, & Galilaeos ad Septentrionem, & ad Ortum Galaad, Arabes, & qui eam plagam incolunt. Nam Act. 1, 8. dixit Christus discipulis suis, Eritis mihi te- stes in Jerusalem, & in omni Judaea & Samaria, & usque ad ultimum terrae: & Act. 8, 1. Omnes dispersi- funt per regiones Judaeae & Samariae praeter Apostolos: haud dubium, quin in alias finitimas regiones abi- erint & ipsi Apostoli paulo post; ita has alias gentes ab Abdia nominatas primum debellarunt Apostoli, & discipuli: postea Evangelii nuncium in omnes orbis partes attulerunt. Et postea: Sensus erit: filii Israel fideles Apostoli, & discipuli, qui metu persequutionum infidelium Judaeorum dispersi sunt per varias orbis partes, vi sui Evangelii, oc- cupabunt omnia loca, in quibus morabantur Cha- nanaei olim inde ejecti, tam Illyrici, quam Afri- ci & Germaniae, usque ad Gallias, ad quam ve- nereMaximinus, Lazarus cum sororibus, Martia- lis, & alii. Vel certe Apostoli, & Judaei fideles, qui habitabunt in locis olim Chananaeorum, per- fundent sua Evangelica luce partem omnem oc- ciduam, usque ad ultimum terminum Galliarum; missi a Christo, cum dixit Marc. 16, 15. Euntes in mundum universum praedicate Evangelium omni cre- aturae. Et Esaiae 56, 19. Mittam ex eis, qui sal- vati fuerint, ad gentes in mari, in Africam & Ly- diam, & Greciam, & Italiam & ad insulas longe, & annunciabunt gloriam meam gentibus. Similiter quod de transmigratione vel exulibus Hierusalem dicitur, per Sepharad Hispaniam intelligens, expo- fuit de Apostolis a Castro h. m. Judaei conversi in Hispania ad fidem, qui in eam transmigraverant sub Tito, aut sub Adriano, vel qui illuc abierunt ad fidem denunciandam, possidebunt, id est, luce Evangelii il- lustrabunt civitates Austri. Africam intelligit Bur- gensis. Lyra ipsam Hispaniam, quam Jacobus illu- stravit. Alii melius Australem Hispaniae plagam, quam Boethicam dicimus. Alii putant novum or- bem significari, qui Hispaniae est Australis, aut sub Australi plaga constitutus: quem nostra aetate Hi- spani & suo imperio subjecerunt, & Evangelii do- ctrina idolorum cultu everso, Christo subdiderunt. Verius de primis praedicatoribus Jacobo & sociis, qui Judaei erant, intelligemus, qui dispersi in Hi- spaniam, eam occuparunt, ut etiam ApostolusPau- lus, praecipue plagamAustralem.Sed imprimis me- retur hic iterum audiri B. Lutherus noster: Ad illa verba: ET ERIT DOMUS JACOB IGNIS: In ista universali omnium gentium subjectione dicit, etiam Idumeos esse huic regno subjiciendos. Absurda omnia sunt & pugnant cum historia, si corporalem subjectionem intelligamus. Nam quid minus conve- nit, quam domum Jacob fore ignem, & domum Jo- seph flammam, quae ipsa jam quasi in cinerem redacta erat, & domum Esau, hoc est, Idumea, fore stipulam a flamma devorandam? Nam domus Joseph post captivitatem Babylonicam nunquam rediit, neque do- mus Iuda unquam possedit Idumeos. Postremo hoc omnium est absurdissimum, quod cum antea prophe- tarit, Idumaeos omnes perituros, & in nihilum redi- gendos, hic tandem dicat, igni etiam devorandos. Ita- que omnino cogunt nos ista, ut de divulgato per Apo- stolos, & per alios discipulos ex Israel Evangelio in o- mnes gentes intelligamus, qua praedicatione devora- runt & incorporarerunt eas regno Christi spiritua- liter, nec possunt amplius de manu ipsius rapi, ut ait Christus in Evangelio. Vere enim apprehenso Evan- gelio, non facile Satan praevalet, id quod factum est, ut indicant Annales. Nam Arabia illa Petraea, in qua fuerunt Idumaei, insignis locus fuit sanctorum ho- minum Evangelio revelato, id quod Esaias quoque pro- mittit. NON ERUNT RELIQVIAE. Adeo subjugabit sibi domum Esau, ut ne reliquiae quidem mansurae sint, h. e. nihil erit, quod contra hoc regnum Christi possit praevalere. Nam per Evangelium Chri- stiani Domini fiunt omnium creaturarum. Haec de vi & efficacia praedicati Evangelii inter gentes,

Hebræum textum v. 19. non male reddidit Hiero- nymus in Vulgata: Et hereditabunt hi, qui ad Au- strum sunt, montem (seu montana) Esau, & qui in campestribus olim habitabant Philistiim (vicinos possidebunt) quin etiam possidebunt regionem E- phraim, & regionem Samariæ (id est, regnum, quod olim Reges Israel tenuerunt) occupabunt, & tribus Benjamin possidebit (regionem) Galaad. Quam translationem proinde sine emendatione retinuit Osiander; citra causam vero emendavit Grotius. Quid enim est hæreditare meridiem cum monte E- sau! Planitiem cum Philistiim? Et cur particula את in cæteris hic de agro Ephraim & Samariæ, ut nota accusativi accipienda, de monte Esau vero & Philistæis per præpositionem cum explicanda? Ideo Drusius Vulgatam confirmat: Non desunt, qui ver- tendum putent, hæreditabunt Austrum, cum monte Esau. Sed hi non animadverterunt postea sequi: Et exules Jerosolymitani, qui in Sepharad, hæredita- bunt urbes Austri. Australes Judæi הנגב, verbum è verbo sonat Auster sive meridies. Sed est figura, quam Grammatici metonymiam vocant: ea qui u- tuntur, ponunt, exempli causa, terram pro habita- toribus terræ, & cœlum pro cœlicolis. Eodem pla- ne modo hic auster ponitur pro habitatoribus Austri. Dices: cur ergo reddis, australes Judæi? Respon- deo, quia hic agit non de austro simpliciter, sed κατὰ συνεκδοχὴν Austrum vocat partem Judææ australem, sive tractum illum, qui austrum & Idu- mæam respiciebat. Montem Esau (Idumæam. Synec- doche. Et campestres השפלה significat tractum Ju- dææ planum & humilem campestremque, cujus in- colæ eodem nomine hic insigniuntur. Erat & alius tractus, cujus incolæ montani dicebantur, eo quod habitarent in montanis Judææ. Nam pars ea mon- tosa erat. Sic dico Judæam incolentium alios au- strales, campestres alios, & alios montanos, à loco, in quibus commorabantur, veteres appełłabant Palæstinos) aut Philisthæos, quorum urbes Gath, Gaza, Ascalon, Acaron, Azotus. Hos Græci com- muni nomine ἀλλοφύλυς indigitant, i. e. alieni- genas. Hæc Drusius. Annuit etiam Lud. de Dieu: Omnino laudo veterem Interpretem, qui הנגב & השפלה accepit Nominativo casu, ac vertit, Et possi- debunt, qui ad austrum sunt, montem Esau, & qui in campestribus, Philisthæos: ut eadem sit constructio cum ובנימין את הגלעד. Et Benjamin possidebit Gilead. Qui ad austrum vel meridiem sunt, viden- tur esse Judæi proprie dicti, quibus Juda tribus cesse- rat, regio terræ Canaan meridionalis, & montibus Esau sive Seir ad meridiem contermina. Ab hac re- cte distinguitur השפלה planities, ea nempe terræ Chanaan pars, quæ respectu Judææ plana erat & cam- pestris. Erat enim Judææ maximam partem montosa, adeoque siccior & aridior, & vere נגב, ea etenim vox proprie siccam & aridam terram denotat. Eundem sensum reddidere etiam B. Lutherus, ut & Para- phrasta Belgici, quamvis aliam his quoque observa- rint in annotatis interpretationem, Tigurinorum & Vatabli, quam utique Grotianæ præferendam censeremus, si à Vulgata discedendum sit: Et hære- ditabunt Austrum, id est, montana, & campestria, id est, Philistiim. Quod ad literam versus 20. re- cte se habet Vulgata in membro primo: Et trans- migratio exercitus hujus filiorum Israel (posside- bit) omnia loca (vel QUÆ SUNT) Cananæo- rum usque ad Sareptam. Quod non improbavit Grotius. At eadem constructionis ratio est in se- cundo membro: Proinde illud non commode redditur in Vulgata, & transmigratio Jerusalem, quæ in Bosphoro est: vel ab aliis, quæ in Sepharad est. Nam integrum sensum in hoc colo haberi, & analogia præcedentis membri, & accentus in E- bræo docet. Ideo non male hæc transtulit Grotius : Et transmigratio Jerusalem, ea quæ sunt Sapheradis possidebunt, vel quæ sunt in fine dominatus uti Tre- mellius reddidit. Nam de illa voce valde variant In- terpp. Consonat etiam paraphrasis Belgica. Si vero accentus Atnach hic colon non faciat, B. Lutheri versio retineri poterit, quæ in hoc versu Vulgatæ præstat: atque ita Ebræa etiam reddidit Osiander : Et captivi de exercitu filiorum Israel, qui inter Cana- næos detinentur usque ad oppidum Zarpath, & captivi Hierosolymitani, qui in Sepharad (urbe in Babylo- nia) degunt, possidebunt civitates australes. Sensus est: Ecclesiam Christi maxima sumturam incremen- ta inter gentiles. Recte hic Calvinus: Promiserat Deus Abrahæ posteris totam terram ab Euphrate usque ad mare. Jam terra nunquam possessa fuit à filiis A- brahæ. Hoc factum est ignavia & ingratitudine eo- rum, sicuti satis notum est: David fines ampliavit suo tempore: sed tamen tantum sibi reddidit tributarios, quos Deus jusserat interfici. Ita nunquam fuit imple- ta illa benedictio, quia obstaculum posuit ipse populus: Nunc Propheta, quum de restitutione Ecclesiæ verba facit, simul docet populum, qui reversus fuerit ab exi- lio, accupaturum totam illam regionem, quæ promis- sa fuerat Patribus: quasi diceret, jam aderit vobis plena & solida hæreditas. Nunc certum est, hoc nun- quam fuisse completum: videmus exiguam terræ par- tem fuisse possessam à Judæis. Quid ergo sibi vult hoc vaticinium? Certe satis constat, Prophetam hic vati- cinari de Christi regno: & scimus tunc vere restitu- tam fuisse Ecclesiam : nec Judæos modo recuperasse priorem statum, à quo exciderant, sed regnum fuisse auctum. Qualis enim splendor fuit & Regni & Tem- pli sub Christo? hoc nunc intelligit Propheta, quum Judæis promittit hæreditatem, quam perdiderant: imzo dilatavit tunc Deus terminos Judææ, ideo ostendit non modo restituendos esse in priorem fortunam, sed augendum esse splendore, & opulentia regnum, quum scilicet advenerit Christus. Hæc Calvinus. Sic & Gualterus hom. 4. p. 123. Judæi post reditum è Ba- bylone nunquam sui regni terminos tam procul exten- derunt, Apostoli vero juxta Christo præceptum in Zio- ne sive Hierosolymis prædicare cœperunt, illic vero per- sequutione exorta quasi divisis copiis totam Judæam oc- cuparunt, mox Samariam ingressi hanc quoque Chri- sto adduxerunt. Inde Zidonis partes invaserunt, & tanta fuit prædicationis Evangelicæ vis, ut ne mari quidem cohiberi potuerit &c. E Pontificiis Rie- bera in h. l. explicat de præconio Apostolorum in Judæa, Samaria, Azoti in Palæstina, in Joppen, Cæ- sareæ, Act. 8. & 10. & quum dispersi usque ad Phœni- cem, in qua erat Sarepta, venerunt c. 11. Agnoscit etiam Cornel. à Lapide, plenius hæc impleta esse in Apostolis sub N. Testam. Verum quia Macchabæi hæc loca subjecerunt quidem, sed non occuparunt (nec enim in his locis habitarunt Judæi, sed Philisthæi, Sa- maritæ, Idumæi) quod tamen fore hic significat Abdi- as, dicens: Ethæreditabunt, & possidebunt; hinc plenius id impletum est mystice ab Apostolis, qui fun- data Ecclesia in Judæa, inde exeuntes ad vicinos Sa- maritas, Idumæos, Philisthæos aliosque populos, omnes illi subjecerunt; ita Lyran. Arias, Vatabl. & à Castro, qui in paraphrasi, Apostoli, inquit, virique Aposto- lici distribuent sibi omnem circum regionem, quam Evangelico bello Christo subjiciant, & qui ad meri- diem exierint, perlustrabunt Idumæam; qui ad occi- dentem, terram omnem Philisthæorum; qui ad se- ptentrionem, Galilæam & Samariam; at qui ad Or- tum, possidebunt Christo Galaaditas, & Arabes: no- minatim vero Benjamin, id est, S. Paulus ortus ex tribu Benjamin, possidebit Galaad: quia ipse con- vertit Arabiam, cujus pars est Galaad: nam ut ipse ait Galat. 1, 17. Abii in Arabiam, ut ibi ex vocatio- ne, & officio meo de more prædicarem, Arabesque face- rem Christianos. Sed præ aliis egregie hæc exequu- tus est B. Lutherus noster ad verba, ET POSSI- DEBUNT HI, QUI AD AUSTRUM SUNT & seq. Tom. 3. Jen. Lat. f. 521. Mira est hic con- tradictio, si literam & externum quoddam regnum intelligas. Primum dicit, possidebunt, deinde, pos- sidebuntur. Item campestria possidebunt Phili- sthiim. Præterea quod maximum est, regnum Israel in duodecim tribus erat divisum, & diligenter lege Mosi cautum erat, ne tribus inter se miscerentur, id quod est cernere in Mose. Cum igitur aperte hic dicit australes, hoc est, qui sunt ad austrum, possessu- ros esse montem Esau: Item Benjamin possessu- rum Gilead, contra quam mandato divino à Mose & Josua terra divisa erat &c. omnino aliter intelli- genda hæc sunt, quam nuda habet litera. Est ergo sen- tentia: Christiani, Apostoli, & alii discipuli, qui futuri sunt ad Austrum, in monte Sion scilicet, in quo primum prædicabitur Evangelium, ii, in- quam, sua prædicatione fructum facient in Idu- mæis. ET CAMPESTRIA. Rectius, Humi- lia, seu valles inter montes amœni, Die Gründes possidebunt Philisthæos, id quod nunquam corpo- raliter factum est post captivitatem Babylonicam. Nam etiam totum regnum non potuit superare & subjicere sibi Philisthæos. Igitur de spirituali sub- jectione per Evangelium intelligendum est. E- PHRAIM. Etiam hoc contra legem est. Igitur per Apostolos id factum est, quando iverunt in Sa- mariam annunciaturi Evangelium. Diligentur igi- tur notabis hunc textum, tanquam clarum testimo- nium & certum, quod lex Christo veniente per Evan- gelium erat abroganda. Nam Benjamin citra Jor- danem erat. Gilead vero ultra Jordanem in tribu Gad. Igitur necessitas cogit nos, ut omnia ad præ- dicationem Evangelii referamus. ET TRANS- MIGRATIO EXERCITUS. Hoc vero longe prioribus est absurdius, nempe eos possessuros es- se totam terram Chananæorum, qui tamen in ca- ptivitatem sunt abducti, neque unquam reducti. Quo, si literam tantum spectes, quid dici potest ab- surdius? Idem est, quod sequitur de transmigratio- ne Jerusalem, hoc est, captivos ex Israel possessu- ros esse civitates Austri, h. e. eas civitates, quæ circa Jerusalem & in Edom sitæ sunt. Hæc Lutherus.

Octavo. Adventus Servatorum in montem Sion ad judicandum montem Esau, ut Jehovæ sit regnum, aliter intelligi non potest, quam de servatoribus spi- ritualibus. Paraphrastæ Belgici explicant de Chri- sto perfectissimo Salvatore, quod plurali numero Sal- vationis Christi perfectio notetur: conferentes Psal. 40, 10. Psal. 73, 22. Prov. 1, 20. Sed rectius alii de A- postolis & præconibus verbi, qui Salvatores sunt δια- κονικῶς, qui per verbum salvare dicuntur non ex se (ita enim nihil quicquam sunt, 1. Cor. 3, 7.) sed qua sunt θεẽ συνεργοὶ, vid. 1. Cor. 9, 22. 1. Thess. 2, 13. 1. Tim. 4, 16. Jud. v. 23. Qui montem Esavi, vel Edu- mæos, hoc est, κτ' συνεκδοχὴν quosvis hostes Ecclesiæ judicant, verbo, & scriptis impietatem mundi re- darguendo Joh. 16, 8. & judicium venturum denun- ciando Act. 17, 31. quemadmodum & Apostoli in novissimo die judicaturi sunt Matth. 19, 28. Luc. 22, 30. Alii verbum judicandi non de pœna, sed de regimine intelligunt, uti Drusius cum Augu- stino l. 18. de Civ. Dei cap. 31. Mons Esau Idumæa est, per quam significata est Ecclesia gentium, quam defenderunt resalvati à monte Sion, ut esset Domino regnum. Hoc obscurum erat, antequam fieret, sed fa- ctum quis non fidelis agnoscat? B. Luth. Motchiim

Salvatores duces vocat, ut est in libro Judicum, ubi multos misit eis Salvatores, hoc est, duces, qui du- cerent eos, & præessent eis, ac præirent, si quando dimicandum esset cum inimicis. Ita hic Apostoli, & alii discipuli Salvatores vocantur, nempe, qui nuntiando Evangelium lætum illud nuncium, libe- raverunt eos ab omnibus hostibus, ab omnibus in- sultibus Satanæ & portarum infernarum, & qui ju- dicaverunt eos in Fide, dominati sunt eis in justitia & judicio, sicque præpararunt Domino regnum æ- ternum. Similiter Cornelius à Lapide : Plane signi- ficat, non perituros posteros Esau, sed judicandos, i. e. regendos à Sionidis & Judæis, ita ut fiant Judæi, & re- gnum Dei. Et postea ad verba: Et tunc erit Domi- no regnum : Hoc inchoate verum fuit in Maccabæis, plene in Ecclesia Christi militante, plenissimum erit in Ecclesia triumphante. Quæ hactenus admitti possunt, qua felicitas Ecclesiæ promissa post redi- tum à captivitate, ac sub Maccabæis cœpit, & porro tempore N. Testam, continuata fuit: modo caven- dum, ne eorundem verborum geminus sensus sta- tuatur, eademque & de reditu ac felicitate corpo- rali, sensu literali, & de spirituali simul, sensu my- stico, intelligantur.

Nono conferenda cum hoc oraculo sunt, quæ alibi in vaticiniis de Idumæorum conversione oc- currunt, utpote Num. 24, 17. 18. Orietur stella ex Ja- cob, & consurget virga de Israel, & percutiet duces Moab, vastabitque omnes filios Seth. Et erit IDU- MÆA possessio ejus, hæreditas SEIR cedet inimicis suis. Quod vaticinium nostro egregie consonat, & à Rabbinis ipsis de Messia explicatur. Item Amos 9, 11. 12. in die illa suscitabo tabernaculum David, quod cecidit, & reædificabo eum, sicut in diebus anti- quis, UT POSSIDEANT LELI QVIAS IDU- MÆÆ. Quod de conversione gentium agere ex Act. 15, 16. constat. Item Es. 11, 14. Et volabunt in humeros Philistiim per mare, simul prædabuntur filios Orientis. IDUMÆA & Moab præceptum manus eorum, & filii Ammon obedientes erunt. Quæ de tempore N. Testamenti agere è toto cap. 11. con- textu, & subjuncto cap. 12. carmine Evcharistico, certum est.

Decimo accedit autoritas S. Petri, quod O- MNES Prophetæ testimonium perhibeant de Chri- sto, Actor. 10, 43. E quorum numero cum excludi Obadias non possit, ita ejus Prophetia accipienda erit, ne ipse solus in hac causa ἀσύμβολος sit, maxi- me cum verba ipsa Prophetæ salutem ac regnum Christi, & conversionem gentium non obscure re- ferant. Quod non modo Christiani Interpp. ple- rinque agnovere sed etiam Rabbinorum nonnullo- rum suffragiis constat. In tr. Schabbat. cap. 6. ita habetur: Prophetæ vaticinati non sunt, nisi propter dies Messiæ. R. Moses Maimonides in Hilkot suis in Schophetim cap. 11. contulit vaticinium Bilea- mi de virga ex Israel cum hoc loco prophetico, in quo admiscet quidem sua commenta, quasi Bileam de duobus diversis loquatur, agnoscit tamen Abdi- am de Messiæ temporibus hic vaticinari. In distin- ctione Bileam dictum est, & prophetatum de primo Messia, qui est David, & salvavit Israel de manu tri- bulantium eos : & de secundo Messia, qui est nasci- turus de filiis ejus, qui salvaturus est Israel de manu filiorum Esau : & ibi dicit Numer. 24, 17. Videbo eum, sed non modo, iste est David, intuebor eum, sed non prope, iste est Rex Messias. Orta est stella ex Jacob, iste est David, & surget virga de Israel, iste est Rex Messias, & confringet Duces Moab, iste est David, de quo dicitur 2. Reg. 8, 2. Et percussit Moab, & mensuravit eos in fune, & subvertit o- mnes filios Seth, iste est Rex Messias, de quo dicitur Zach. 9, 10. Et Dominum ejus à mari usque ad mare, &c. Et erit Edom possessio ejus, iste est Da- vid, sicut dictum est 2. Reg. 8, 2. Et fuit totus E- dom servi Davidis &c. Et erit possessio Seir inimi- cis suis, iste est Messias, sicut dictum est in A- bdia v. 21. Et adscendent Salvatores in montem Sion, ad judicandum montem Seir. Hæc Maimo- nides. E Christianis Doctoribus adduximus an- tea S. Augustinum, qui hæc de tempore N. Testa- menti exposuit. Cum Augustino autem faciunt Rupertus, Lyranus, Burgens. in addit. ad h. l. Merce- rus, Gualtherus, Vatabl. Isidorus, Arias Montanus, Belgæ, illumque sensum ceu potiorem eligunt Al- bertus & Dionysius, referente Christ. à Castro, qui duabus rationibus non contemnendis eandem in- terpretationem probat. Primo: quia ex nulla hi- storia constat hanc temporarium felicitatem à re- ditu è Babylone usque ad adventam Christi Judæis contigisse. Unde Hieronymus: Hoc utrum factum sit, Judæus viderit. Ergo de temporaria felicitate non possunt Abdiæ verba explicari. Assumpta illa propositio probatur: nunquam tam superiores fuere Judæi, ut Idumæos de medio sustulerint, cum etsi aliquoties attriti, sicut & ipsi Judæi, nunquam tamen deleti. At Abdias prophetat, non remansu- ras reliquias Idumæorum: qui tamen integri super- fuerunt, Judæis per Romanos eversis. Ergo de a- lia vastatione, spirituali videlicet, loquitur. Deinde solenne est Prophetis suas vaticinationes rerum per Christum gerendarum lætissima terminare commemoratione, qua & consolentur afflictos, & Petri sententia vera comprobetur 1. sua Epistola c. 1, 10. De qua salute exquisierunt, atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetarunt. Hæc Christoph. à Castro, qui, ut apparet, utramque sententiam, & eorum, qui hoc oraculum de reditu Judæorum è Babylone intelligunt, quam Hierony- mo, Cyrillo, Theodoreto, Remigio, Hugoni de S. Victo- re, Alberto, Haymoni, & Dionysio tribuit, & illo- rum, qui de negotio Evangelico & tempore N. Te- stamenti cum Augustino explicant, hoc modo con- jungit; Prophetiam hanc cæptam impleri post redi- tum è Babylone, sed felicitatem Judæorum comple- tam & perfectam tunc, cum Christo duce Apostoli ex monte Sion per omnes mundi plagas excurrerunt, & gentes Judæas & impias subjugarunt, quoadusque fa- ctum est Domino regnum. In eam etiam sententiam ipsummet Hieronymum cum Theodoreto, & Hay- mone & Alberto explicare conatur: multosque a- lios ita interpretari, ait, & inter hos Robertum, cu- jus hæc verba laudat: Vera salus in Sion erit, quæ vera esse non potest, nisi sit æterna. Id ad literam com- pleri cæptum est, quando secundum templum & ur- bem instaurarunt, in quod introiturus verus Salva- tor, & Redemptor Israel Christus Jesus Malach. 3, 2. Propheta enim altius quiddam hoc loco, more omni- um Prophetarum, prænuntiat, nempe veram & æ- ternam liberationem in Christo. Sic ergo utrum- que sententiam conjungere videri possit à Castro. Sed si rectius mens ejus expendatur, temperamen- tum potius quoddam ex utraque facit. Ideoque non id vult proprie Christoph. à Castro, sub eis- dem verbis primo & sensum historicum & spiri- tualem contineri (quod impossibile esse pronuntiat) nec quoad historiam completam fuisse putat hanc Prophetiam, quoad omnes partes, ut eadem signi- ficaretur mystice Christi negotium, sed ita se- se explicat: Abdiam conjecisse oculos ad omne tem- pus post reditum è Babylone, & aspexisse felicita- tem temporalem & spiritualem Judæorum, victo- riasque partas ex bello spectabili & spirituali, atque in hoc prætulisse Judæos, qui evaserant in monte Sion, cæteris omnibus gentibus; atque hanc plenam Judæorum felicitatem prænunciasse in sensu literali, sub verbis gentium & locorum, quæ profert. Et notat, non pauca esse in Scriptura sacra verba, quæ bona promittunt adeo excellentia, ut nisi temporariis accedant spiritualia, non compleatur, quod primo sub illis significatur; quare universum illud bonum tam excellens ex temporali & spirituali debet compleri. Ita v. 19. ET IN MONTE SION ERIT SALVATIO, prænunciari putat eversionem malorum tam corporalium, quam spiritualium, quæ cæpit post 70. annos in monte Sion, & perfecta est atque completa per Christum, quando ibi salutem communicavit multis, & Apostolos elegit, ac instituit, qui uti duces inde excurrerent, & expugnarent terram universam. Verba sequentia: ET ERIT SANCTITAS, ita exponit: Erit mons sanctitatis, ut olim, i. e. mons sanctus, & sacratus Deo, propter templum, & cultum in eo præstitum post captivitatem, & per Christi præsentiam, & adventum Spiritus S. in illum montem, unde cæpi, & profusa est sanctitas per orbem universum, ut inquit Theodoretius. Ad v. 20. explicandum ita occupatur: Verius & clarius: domus Jacob reversa è captivitate Babylonica occupabit possessiones suas, quas gentes sibi assumpserant, & gentium ipsarum proprias ex parte, sub Maccabæis. Et tunc demum Apostoli & discipuli posteri Jacob, egressi è monte Sion, de quo scriptum erat, quod ex Sione exibit lex, & verbum Domini de Jerusalem, subjicient sibi & Christo gentes omnes finitimas, & longe positas circum Jerusalem, quæ illi fuerant dominatæ aliquando, quales fuerunt Persæ, Medi, Græci, Romani, ac similes. Sic se habet istius Jesuitæ explicatio.

licitatem temporalem Judæorum concedamus, beneficia tamen & victoriæ, quæ hic promittuntur, concernunt res spirituales, & proprie ad tempora N. T. spectant, quibus universalis gentium vocatio reservata erat, quapropter cum S. Augustino, B. Gesnero, B. Wigando, B. Pappo, B. Winckelmanno, B. Tarnovio, Paraphrastis Vinariensibus, & Belgicis, Drusio item, aliisque Interpp. prius laudatis hæc de regno Christi sub N. Test. & vocatione gentium unice intelligenda esse, censemus, quo tempore in monte Sion salvatio facta est, & domus Jacob possedit eos, qui se possederant: nullatenus vero Cocceji glossæ de nescio qua Synagogæ adhuc futura conversione locum relinquimus. Sed sub exordium N. T. ea implenda esse, atque etiamnum certa ratione impleri existimamus. Quemadmodum ipse Castrius in paraphrasi sua unice hunc sensum tradidit: Verum ex omnibus his calamitatibus evadet populus meus in monte Sion, quia præstabit sanctitate ob cultum renovatum, & Spiritus S. mei adventum. Unde egressi filii Israel ut ignis stipulæ excindent Idumæos, & ad suam religionem convertent, & veluti ignis succendent, ac devorabunt eos, ita ut nemo eorum supersit, non subjectus veræ religioni. Nam ita Dominus definivit. Atque illi quidem Israelitæ, Apostoli, virique Apostolici tribuent sibi omnem circum regionem, quam Evangelico bello Christo subjiciant, & qui ad Meridiem exierint, per lustrabunt Idumæam, qui ad occidentem, terram omnem Philisthæorum; qui ad septentrionem, Galilæam, & Samariam; at qui ad ortum, possidebunt Christo Galaaditas & Arabes. Quinimo quicunque ex Israelitis Apostolis longius transmigraverint, ea omnia loca sua luce perfundent, in quæ Chananæi dispersi sunt, usque ad Gallias, & qui ex Jerosolymis transmigraverint ad Hispaniam, Bosphorum Herculeum circumjacentem, subjicient Christo omnem plagam Australem. At tunc demum victores redibunt, uti Salvatores gentium, in montem Sion, unde exierant, ad subjugandum præcipue montem Esau: & sic regnum Davidicum instaurabitur Domino. Hactenus Castrii periphrasis, in rei summa nostræ explicationi consona, quæ hæc est, omnium gentium terram occupandam: vel omnes gentes possidendas esse tempore N. T. à Judæis, Messiam Regem suscipientibus, id quod impletum est, cum Apostoli Evangelii doctrinam per omnes gentes, & totum terrarum orbem disseminarunt, omnesque gentes Christo sub obsequium fidei captivarunt, & subjecerunt. Sic ergo DOMINO factum est Regnum, Messiæ nempe, qui Jehovah est DEUS super omnia benedictus in secula, cujus regni non erit finis, cui sit gloria & honor in sempiterna secula. Amen!

Verum enim vero, quamvis hæc se rectius habeant, quam Grotiana, salvaque unitate sensus allusisse Prophetæ dici possit ad victorias corporales, ac animo simul complexus esse temporalem & spiritualem felicitatem, neque id inconveniens sit, ad omne tempus post reditum è Babylone, quoad nonnulla prædicata, eum respexisse: vereor tamen, ut illa Castrii expositio cum unico sensu omnino consistere queat. Nam si de possessionibus pristinis in terra Judæa occupandis post reditum sermo sit, quas gentes sibi vendicarant, quomodo citra διπλότητα sensus iisdem phrasibus agetur simul de Apostolis, gentes sibi per verbum subjecturis? Quibus enim verbis de Idumæis vere expugnatis, & subjugatis à Judæis vaticinatur Propheta, iisdem illis utique non agit de impiis & infidelibus per discipulos Christi, efficacitate verbi expugnatis, Christoque subjectis. Quapropter utut allusionem aliquam ad reditum & fe-

# Jonah

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
I. N. J. ANNOTATIONS ON JONAH.

Latin:

I. N. J. ANNOTATA AD JONAM.

## 1:1 Introduction: Preface
PREFACE.

And Jerome places this man as contemporary with Hosea and Amos, according to the authority of the Hebrews, and the order suggests it: and the passage, which is 2 Kings 14:25. The King of Nineveh, of whom this book treats, could have been Pul, who later came with an army into the land of Israel: a man neither the best nor the worst.

bulon Josh. 19, which according to Jerome was situated between Sepharim and Tiberias near Eleutheropolis, or Diospolis. It is false, therefore, what the Hebrews have handed down, that Jonah was the son of the widow of Zarephath: for he was not a Gittite or a Philistine, but a Hebrew and a Zebulunite. Who that King of Nineveh was, is uncertain. Nor is there any proof that it was Pul. That he was not of a wicked party, his conversion teaches, which took place at the first proclamation of Jonah, and the public intimation of fasting and repentance.

Concerning the age of Jonah, 2 Kings 14:25 teaches more certainly than the order: namely, that he lived under Jeroboam II, King of Israel, and under Amaziah, King of Judah, and that he originated from Gath, which is Opher in the tribe of Zabulon moreover, Jonah first performed his Prophetic office among the Israelites, 2 Kings 14:25, concerning the restoration of the borders of Israel, and was afterwards sent to the Ninevites, whose present prophecy, besides the Jews Raschi, Kimchi, Aben-Ezra, and Abrabanel, has been illustrated by our own B. Luther, Vol. 4, Wittenberg Latin, Just. Jonas, Bugenhagen, Brentius, Theod. Snepfius, Wigandus, Pappus, Winckelman, Krackwitz, Himmelius, Tarnovius; among the Papists, Vatablus, Clarius, Montanus, Ribera, Sanctius, Cornelius, Mariana, Estius, Sa, Tirinus, Menochius, Gabriel a Costa; among the Reformed, Oecolampadius, Calvin, Gwalther, Piscator, Danaeus, Cocceius; to whom, among the Philologists, should be added Mercerus of Paris, Leusden the Dutchman, and our own Pfeiffer. The argument of this prophecy is: Jonah, sent to the Ninevites, first fled, but after being cast into the sea and swallowed by a whale, and miraculously preserved in its belly, he was cast alive onto the land after most ardent prayers; being sent again, he predicted destruction to the Ninevites, who, having performed penance, obtained mercy: Jonah grieving that the prediction was not fulfilled, but instructed by word and type concerning the grace shown to the Ninevites. There are two parts. I. The former calling of Jonah, which he refused, ch. 1 and 2. II. His latter calling, which he obeyed, ch. 3 and 4. There, both the punishment of the reluctant Jonah and the vivification of the supplicating Jonah are exhibited, ch. 2: Here, however, first the preservation of the repenting Ninevites is described, ch. 3, then the conviction of the rashly indignant Jonah, ch. 4.

Latin:

PRÆFATIO.

ET hunc Oseæ, & Amoso coævum ex Hebræorum auctoritate ponit Hieronymus, & ordo suadet: & locus, qui est 2. Reg. 14, 25. Rex Ninives, de quo agit hic liber, potuit esse Phul, qui postea cum exercitu venit in terram Israelis: homo nec optimus, nec pessimus.

bulon Jos. 19. quæ juxta Hieronymum sita fuit inter Sepharim & Tiberiadim juxta Eleutheropolim, seu Diospolim. Falsum ergo est, quod tradidere Ebræi, Jonam fuisse filium viduæ Sareptanæ: non enim Gethæus aut Philistæus fuit, sed Ebræus & Zabulonita. Quisnam ille Rex Ninives fuerit, incertum est. Neque Phulem fuisse ullo documento constat. Quod non fuerit πονηρᾶ κόμματος, conversio ejus docet, ad primum Jonæ præconium facta, & publica jejunii & pænitentiæ intimatio.

DE ætate Jonæ certius locus 2. Reg. 14, 25. docet quam ordo: vixisse nempe ipsum sub Jeroboamo II. Rege Israel, & sub Amasia Rege Juda, ortumque fuisse ex Geth, quæ est Opher in tribu Za- Cæterum officio Prophetico functus prius Jonas fuit apud Israelitas 2. Reg. 14, 25. de restituendis ter- minis Israelis, dehinc missus ad Ninivitas, cujus præsentem prophetiam præter Judæos Rasche, Kimchium, Aben-Esdr. Abraban. e nostris illustra- runt B. Lutherus T. 4. Witteb. Lat. Just. Jonas, Bu- genhagius, Brentius, Theod. Snepfius, Wigandus, Pappus, Winckelm. Krackwiz, Himmelius, Tarnov. e Pontificiis Vatabl. Clarius, Montanus, Ribera, Sanctius, Cornelius, Mariana, Estius, Sa, Tirinus, Menochius, Gabriel a Costa; e Reformatis Oeco- lampadius, Calvinus, Gvalterus, Piscator, Danæus, Coccejus, quibus e Philologis addendi Mercerus Parisiensis, Leusdenius Batavus, & Pfeifferus no- stras. Argumentum prophetiæ hujus est: Jonas ad Ninivitas missus fugit primum, sed postquam in mare præcipitatus a ceto absorptus in ventre ejus mirabiliter conservatus post ardentissimas preces vivus in terram projectus est, iterum missus prædi- xit Ninivitis exitium, qui acta pœnitentia miseri- cordiam consequuti sunt: Jona dolente, quod præ- dictio non impleretur, at verbo, & typo de gratia Ninivitis exhibita instructo. Partes duæ sunt. I. Prior Jonæ vocatio, quam renuit c. 1. & 2. II. Al- tera ejus vocatio, cui paruit c. 3. & 4. Ibi tum Jonæ reluctantis punitio est, tum Jonæ supplicantis vivifi- catio c. 2. exhibetur: Hic vero primum Ninivita- rum pœnitentium conservatio cap. 3. tum Jonæ teme- re indignantis convictio describitur cap. 4.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. THE FORMER CALLING OF JONAH. CHAPTER I.

Jonah, commanded to preach to the Ninevites, fled by sea, and because of the storm that arose on that account, he is cast into the sea.

Fleeing the commands of God, JONAH is devoured by a fish.

Ver. 1.

SON OF AMITTAI) There were also among the Greeks prophets called Amithaonidae, and the name Jonah can have the meaning of a man sprung from Greece.

Cocceius chastised this in someone (undoubtedly pointing to Grotius), who refers a certain JONAH to יון, as if it were Grecian, or sprung from Greece: and he notes that there were Amithaonid prophets among the Greeks. What are these, if not ravings? Where, having read and observed many things, as in dreams, everything is confused in our mind? Others more correctly recognize the Hebrew יונה, which denotes a dove: a name pleasing for its simplicity and pure love, and imposed upon the Bride of Christ herself, Cant. 3:14.

Latin:

PARS I. PRIOR JONÆ VOCATIO. CAPUT I.

Jonas Ninivitis prædicare jussus per mare fu- git, & ob tempestatem ideo exortam in ma- re præcipitatur.

Jussa Dei fugiens JONAS a pisce voratur.

Vers. 1.

FILIUM AMATHI) Etiam apud Græcos fuere va- tes Amithaonidæ, potestque Jonas nomen significationem habere hominis e Græcia orti.

CAstigavit Coccejus hoc in non nemine (Gro- tium sine dubio indigitans) JONAH quidam ad יון refert, quasi sit Græcanicus, vel ex Græcia ortus: & notat apud Græcos fuisse vates Amithaonidas. Quid hæc, nisi deliria? Quo multa legisse & obser- vasse, sicut in somniis, apud animum nostrum omnia confunduntur? Rectius alii יונה Ebræum agno- scunt, quod columbam notat: nomen ob simpli- citatem & amorem candidum gratum, ipsique Sponsæ Christi impositum Cant. 3, 14.

## 1:2
Ver. 2.

INTO NINEVEH) Which is Ninos according to Herodotus, Phocylides, Strabo, Lucan, Pliny.

From Nin, i.e., בני נוה, the habitation of Nin, as Drusius, Serarius, Cornelius; but not from נוה, he dwelt, as Pagninus, so called.

HER MALICE HAS ASCENDED BEFORE ME) It can no longer be tolerated. Luxury and rapine are accustomed to exceed all measure in ruling cities. Κρείσσων Νίνου τυφρανέσης, says Phocylides.

Understand the sins crying out to heaven. See Gen. 4, 10. c. 18, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

IN NINIVEN) Quæ Ninos Herodoto, Phocylidi, Straboni, Lucano, Plinio.

A Nino q. בני נוה habitatio Nini, ut Drusius, Serarius, Cornelius; non vero a נוה habitavit, ut Pagninus, ita dicta.

ASCENDIT MALITIA EJUS CORAM ME) Tolerari ultra non potest. Luxus & rapinæ solent in urbi- bus regnatricibus omnem modum excedere. Κρείσσων Νίνου τυφρανέσης, ait Phocylides.

Intellige peccata in cœlum clamantia. Vid. Gen. 4, 10. c. 18, 20.

## 1:3
Ver. 3.

THAT HE MIGHT FLEE TO THARSIS) Josephus takes it as Tarsus of Cilicia. But elsewhere the same Josephus, as also the Hebrews, and here Jerome, understand by Tharsis the Ocean sea, namely because the old city, a colony of the Phoenicians, not far from the Ocean, which was called Tartessus by the Greeks, and תרשיש by the Phoenicians themselves. How far Jonah arrived by sailing, I think is uncertain; yet I will not be silent that the Africans believe he was cast out at Mossa: (witness Joannes Leo Africanus) Josephus in the Euxine Sea.

Since it is undoubted that the Hebrew word is taken for the Ocean sea, as in Ps. 48, 8, as rendered here by the Blessed Luther with Osiander agreeing, and no inconvenience of this meaning appears in this place, nor is it necessary that a certain place of the continent be designated, for Jonah only hastened to the sea, so that wherever the ship might carry him, he would flee, only that he might not remain in his native land, the kingdom of Israel, we can easily acquiesce in that translation concerning the sea. Even though the LXX, the Syrian, the Arab, and the Danish version with the Vulgate do otherwise. For they cannot determine anything certain who wish for a determined place, whether into Africa, which Theodoret, Theophylact, and Arias, and as Abarbanel and Mariana wish, though in different ways; or into Spain, which Bochart and Bootius with Pineda, or indeed into Cilicia, which Lyranus, Castrius, Cornelius, the Blessed Tarnovius, and Drusius contend with Josephus. He had certainly defined no place in his mind, who had only decided to rush away from the face of the Lord, that is, from the land of Canaan, in which God had been accustomed to manifest Himself, wherever fortune might carry him. It is more fitting for a fugitive that he should not choose a certain place, says the Blessed Winckelmann. And how could he have determined a certain place for himself, if indeed it was uncertain in which port at Joppa the ships were about to set sail. Furthermore, why would the sailors have asked him, 'Whither goest thou,' when they were already being driven by storms and tempests at sea, if they had believed that he was contending with them to Tharsis? Jerome among the Ancients, Zwingli among the Reformed, Ribera among the Pontificians, nor the Chaldean interpreter, the Italian, or the French version do not deny our opinion. Nor does the local ה denote the final limit to which he was contending, but that Jonah betook himself to the sea, intending to betake himself further, whither perhaps the wind might have carried him, or the ship might have contended.

Ver. same.

FROM THE FACE OF THE LORD) That is, far from the land of Israel.

Thus some [understand it] as from the fellowship of the Church, Gen. 4, 16. Exod. 23, 15. Ps. 100, 2. Others, however, prefer to understand it of his office, because he refused it, just as to stand before God is to minister to Him, 1 Sam. 1, 12, such as the Jews, Lyranus, Vatablus, Brentius; He fled, however, not because he did not want to be held a false prophet if the Ninevites did penance, as it seemed to Theodoret, Theophylact, and Lyranus, because he was not certain of the outcome, but out of fear of danger, out of love for his country, because the Assyrians infested the Israelites. See Jerome and Mercerus.

AND HE DESCENDED INTO JOPPA) For he uses the harbor of the same, having descended to the sea. Strabo 16.

AND HE GAVE THE FARE TO THEM) Sailors are accustomed to receive the fare in advance from those unknown to them: L. ex conducto. §. item D. locati.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

UT FUGERET IN THARSIS) Josephus Thar- sum Ciliciæ accipit. Sed & alibi idem Josephus, ut & He- bræi, & hic Hieronymus, per Tharsis intelligit mare Ocea- num, nempe quod urbs vetus Phœnicum colonia, non longe ab Oceano, quæ Tarteslus Græcis, Phœnicibus ipsis תרשיש diceretur. Quousque navigando pervenerit Jonas, incer- tum puto; neque tacebo tamen Afros ad Mossam eum eje- ctum credi velle: (testis Joannes Leo Afer) Josephum in Ponto Euxino.

Cum indubium sit vocem Ebræam de mari O- ceano accipi, utpote Psal. 48, 8. uti reddita hic à B. Luthero Osiandro consentiente, neque appareat ullum inconveniens hujus significationis in hoc loco, aut necessum sit, certum locum continentis designari, nam properavit tantum Jona ad mare, ut quocunque navis ipsum vehat, fugeret, solum ne in patria terra, regno Israelis persisteret, acquiescere facile possumus illi translationi de mari. Etsi LXX. Syrus, Arabs, Danica versio cum vulg. faciant. Nec enim certi quid determinare possunt, qui locum determinatum volunt, num in Africam, quod Theo- dor. Theophylact. & Arias, & ut Abrabaneel & Maria- na licet diversimode volunt; an in Hispaniam, quod Bochartus & Bootius cum Pineda, an vero in Cili- ciam, quod Lyranus, Castrius, Cornelius, B. Tarno- vius & Drusius cum Josepho contendunt. Nullum utique locum in mente sibi definiverat, qui solum proripere se à facie Domini, hoc est, à terra Canaan, in qua Deus sese manifestare consueverat, decre- verat, quocunque sors ipsum ferret. Magis competit fugitivo, ut non eligeret locum certum, ait B. Winckel- mannus. Et quomodo certum sibi determinare potuisset locum, siquidem incertus fuerit, quonam in portu Joppensi soluturæ sint naves. Porro cur quæsivissent ex ipso nautæ, quo vadis, cum in mari jam procellis & tempestatibus agitarentur, si eun- dem in Tharsin secum contendere credidissent? Non abnuit nostræ sententiæ Hieronymus è Ve- teribus, Zwinglius è Reformatis, Ribera è Pontifi- ciis, nec Chaldæus interpres, Italica, Gallica versio. Nec vero ה locale terminum ultimum notat, quo contendebat, sed quod ad mare se contulerit Jo- nas, ulterius se collaturus, quorsum forte ventus tulerit, aut navis contenderit.

Vers. eod.

A FACIE DOMINI) Id est, longe à terra Is- raelis.

Ita nonnulli q. à consortio Ecclesiæ Gen. 4, 16. Exod. 23, 15. Psal. 100, 2. alii tamen malunt de offi- cio intelligere, quod id detrectarit, uti contra stare coram Deo est ei ministrare, 1. Sam. 1, 12. utpote Judæi, Lyranus, Vatablus, Brentius; Fugit autem, non quod noluerit falsus Propheta haberi, si pœni- tentiam agerent Ninivitæ, uti Theodoret. Theophyl. & Lyrano visum, quia de eventu certus non erat, sed ex metu periculi, ex amore in patriam, quia As- syrii infestarunt Israelitas. Vid. Hieronymus & Mercerus.

ET DESCENDIT IN JOPPEN) Nam ἐπινείῳ τῶν τῳ κέχρηται καταβάντες μέχρι θαλάσσης. Strabo 16.

ET DEDIT NAULUM EIS) Solent nautæ ab ignotis vecturam accipere promutuam: L. ex conducto. §. item D. locati.

## 1:4
Ver. 4.

BUT THE LORD SENT A GREAT WIND INTO THE SEA) In the Hebrew: He caused to rise.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

DOMINUS AUTEM MISIT VENTVM MA- GNUM IN MARE) In Hebræo: Surgere fecit.

## 1:5
Verse 5.

AND THE MEN CRIED OUT) In the Hebrew: A man. That is, each one: perhaps Jerome had written it thus. For the Greeks also have ἕκαστος.

TO HIS GOD) To their gods. Bel, for instance, Astarte, Melqart, Il.

It is a fable, which R. Solomon has, that there were 70 nations in the ship.

AND THEY THREW THE WARES THAT WERE IN THE SHIP INTO THE SEA) That is, they made a jettison. See the Title of the Digest on the Rhodian Law. By the name of wares the Hebrews understand any movable things.

SO THAT IT MIGHT BE LIGHTENED OF THEM) For the sake of lightening the ship, as Law 1 of the said title speaks.

DESCENDIT AD INTERIORA NAVIS) In Hebrew: to the sides of the ship: that is, to one of the sides. Mercer and Drusius understand the hold of the ship; but B. Tarnovius and the Dutch, with the Hebrews, prefer to understand one side or the other. ET DORMIEBAT SOPORE GRAVI) That is, κάρῳ, as the Greeks say. This torpor often accompanies grief. Most others, along with Jerome and Theodoret, think he was lulled to sleep by grief, but B. Bugenhagen attributes the sleep to security, because he believed himself to be out of danger, to which vigils combined with fatigue from the journey were added, which Schnepfius alleges. Vers. 6. GUBERNATOR) Master of the ship, Prince of the sailors, as the Chaldean has it here. DEUM TUUM) Your gods. Of your nation. Vers. 7. ET DIXIT VIR AD COLLEGAM SUUM) Each said to his companion. MITTAMUS SORTES) Which is usually done when there is no hope that all can be saved. ET SCIAMUS QUARE HOC MALUM SIT NOBIS) Horace: I will forbid him who has divulged the secret rites of Ceres to be under the same roof or to unmoor a fragile skiff with me. Often Jupiter, neglected, has joined the innocent with the guilty. Those who were sailing with Diagoras the Melian, when a huge storm arose, attributed the cause to him as an atheist. Vers. 8. QUOD EST OPUS TUUM) In what kind of life have you lived? HEBRÆUS EGO SUM) Born in the parts of Zabulon. Vers. 9. DEUM CŒLI EGO TIMEO) That is, I worship. QUI FECIT MARE ET ARIDAM) This mark distinguishes him best from the gods of the nations. Vers. 10. COGNOVERUNT ENIM VIRI QUOD A FACIE DOMINI FUGERET, QUIA INDICAVERAT EIS) It is a retroversion. Vers. 11. QUID FACIEMUS TIBI, ET CESSABIT MARE A NOBIS) From harassing us. MARE IBAT ET INTUMESCEBAT) It continued to swell. Vers. 12. ET DIXIT AD EOS: TOLLITE ME) If one man, in order to save many, rightly offers himself to death, which Phocion said to Demosthenes: he will do it much more justly who knows himself to be the cause of danger to others. Vers. 13. ET REMIGABANT VIRI UT REVERTERENTUR AD ARIDAM) Just as the Latins say to plow the sea, so the Hebrews say to dig: and here it signifies to row, by a very elegant metaphor, so that they might return to land; it is said so because all ships come from some land. QUIA MARE IBAT ET INTUMESCEBAT) The same words as above in verse 11. Vers. 14. ET CLAMAVERUNT AD DOMINUM) יהוה that is, to that God, the maker of the universe, whose worshipper Jonah had said he was. They had become more religious in danger: having sailed past Myle, you will be pious. NE PEREAMUS IN ANIMA VIRI ISTIUS) That is, because of the homicide which we have committed against him. As the Chaldean explains here, and the following verses show. QUIA TU DOMINE SICUT VOLUISTI FECISTI.) You who have stirred up this clearly extraordinary storm, who made the lot fall upon Jonah, who drove him to confess himself the source and cause of this evil. ET TIMUERUNT VIRI TIMORE MAGNO DOMINUM) Again יהוה. Piscator attributes this prayer to servile fear, Coccejus to carnal fear; but that those sailors truly feared and worshipped God with religious and sacred worship, the Prophet testifies expressly in verse 14. ET TIMUERUNT the men with GREAT FEAR the LORD יהוה, and they sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord, and made vows.

What are the proofs of true divine worship? Prayer suggests nothing else, because they cried out with a loud voice, no longer each to his own false gods, as before in v. 5. But to Jehovah, concerning whose majesty and will they had been instructed by Jonah: We beseech thee, O Jehovah, ah, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O Lord, hast done as it pleased thee. They acknowledge the αὐτοκρατορίαν and αὐτεξουσίαν of the Lord, that he could both destroy and save them in such a great tempest, and demand blood from them, or grant them grace. Grotius does not speak ill regarding those words: For thou, O Lord, hast done as it pleased thee: Thou who hast stirred up this plainly extraordinary tempest, who hast made the lot fall upon Jonah, so that he might confess himself the source and cause of this evil. Thou, Jehovah, hast directed this whole matter miraculously, so that it is certainly necessary that either this man alone, or we all together with him, must perish. They conclude from the storm, the lot, Jonah’s confession, and his counsel that this whole matter is the work of divine providence and will. Before, when they had heard Jonah speaking of the God of heaven who made the sea and the dry land, and of his own duty, and had understood that Nineveh, a very powerful and flourishing city, was to be overturned on account of its sins, and saw that Jonah himself was being so punished by his God, and that they themselves were being brought into such great danger along with him, they are said to have feared with a great fear, verse 10, because they were conscious of their own sins as well, and saw that most imminent destruction hung over them. Now, having grasped the Prophet’s counsel, when they perceive in reality that they can in no other way escape destruction, they betake themselves to God with fervent prayer, they pray that the danger in which they all stood on account of one might be averted, they beseech that the death of Jonah might not be imputed to them, and they praise God for His justice and power. Finally, when Jonah was cast into the sea, the waves of the sea were calmed, and the sea ceased from its surging and its heat, by which it seemed as if it were angry at him who had refused obedience to the Creator; they were confirmed by this miracle in the acknowledgment of the true God, and they worshipped Him, not with a hypocritical spirit, but in spirit and in truth, even vowing offerings to the Lord, because they would religiously worship this God as their own God. Most interpreters acknowledge that they were truly converted to the Lord: Lyranus, Vatablus, Arias Montanus, Cornelius à Lapide, as well as our own; and also from the ancients Theodoret, Cyril, and Jerome, who says, "Great is the faith of the passengers; they themselves are in peril, and they pray for the soul of another: for they know that the death of sin is greater than that of life." They do not fear simply, as we read in the beginning, but with a great fear, according to that which is said, with all their soul, with all their heart, and with all their mind. And they offered sacrifices, which certainly according to the letter they did not have in the midst of the waves: but because a contrite spirit is a sacrifice to God. And in another place it is said: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay thy vows to the most High. And again: We will render to thee the calves of our lips. Therefore they offer sacrifices in the sea: and others they promise spontaneously: making vows: that they would never depart from him whom they had begun to worship, for they feared with a great fear: Because from the tranquility of the sea and the flight of the tempest, they perceived the true words of the Prophet. Jonah, a fugitive in the sea, shipwrecked, dead, saves the tossing boat, saves the heathens previously tossed into diverse opinions by the error of the world.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET CLAMARUNT VIRI) In Hebræo: Vir. Id est, quisque: forte sic scripserat Hieronymus. Nam & Græci habent ἕκαστος.

AD DEUM SUUM) Ad Deos suos. Belum puta Astarten, Melcartum, Ilum.

Fabula est, quam habet R. Salomo, quod LXX. gentes in navi fuerint.

ET MISERUNT VASA, QVÆ ERANT IN NA- VI IN MARE) Id est, jactum fecerunt. Vide Titulum Di- gestorum ad legem Rhodiam. Vasorum nomine Hebræi res quasvis mobiles intelligunt.

UT ALLEVIARETUR AB ILLIS) Levandæ navis gratia, ut loquitur L. 1. dicti tit.

DESCENDIT AD INTERIORA NAVIS) In He- bræo: ad latera nabis : id est, ad laterum alterum. Mercer. & Drusius alveum navis intelligunt; sed B. Tarnovius & Belgæ cum Ebræis alterutrum latus intelligi malunt. ET DORMIEBAT SOPORE GRAVI) Id est, xάρω, ut loquuntur Græci. Is torpor sæpe mœrorem comitatur. Præ mœrore sopitum etiam alii plerique cum Hieronymo & Theodoreto putant, sed B. Bugenha- gius tribuit somnum securitati, quia jam se crede- bat extra periculum esse, cui vigiliæ cum fatigatio- ne ex itinere accessere, quas Schnepfius allegat. Vers. 6. GUBERNATOR) Magister navis, Princeps nauta- tum, ut Chaldæus hic. DEUM TUUM) Deos tuos. Tuæ gentis. Vers. 7. ET DIXIT VIR AD COLLEGAM SUUM) Dixit quisque socio suo. MITTAMUS SORTES) Quod fieri solet ubi spes non est omnes servari posse. ET SCIAMUS QUARE HOC MALUM SIT NOBIS) Horatius : Vetabo qui Cereris sacrum Vulgarit arcanæ sub isdem Sit trabibus, fragilemque mecum Solvat faselum. Sæpe Diespiter Neglectus, incesto addidit integrum. Qui cum Diagora Melio navigabant ingenti orta tempe- state, causam ad ipsum retulere tanquam α̋θεον. Vers. 8. QUOD EST OPUS TUUM) In quo vitæ genere vixisti ? HEBRÆUS EGO SUM) Natus in partibus Zabu- lonis. Vers. 9. DEUM CŒLI EGO TIMEO) Id est, colo. QUI FECIT MARE ET ARIDAM) Hæc nota eum à diis gentium optime discernit. Vers. 10. COGNOVERUNT ENIM VIRI QUOD A FACIE DOMINI FUGERET, QUIA INDICAVE- RAT EIS) Est retrogressio. Vers. 11. QUID FACIEMUS TIBI, ET CESSABIT MA- RE A NOBIS) Infestandis. MARE IBAT ET INTUMESCEBAT) Pergebat intumescere. Vers. 12. ET DIXIT AD EOS: TOLLITE ME) Si homo unus ut multos servet, recte morti se offert, quod De- mostheni dicebat Phocion: multo id faciet justius, qui se aliis periculi scit esse causam. Vers. 13. ET REMIGABANT VIRI UT REVERTEREN- TUR AD ARIDAM) Sicut Latini dicunt arare mare, ita Hebræi fodere: idque hic significat remigare, translatione perelegante, ut reverterentur ad terram, ideo dicitur, quia omnes naves à terra aliqua veniunt. QUIA MARE IBAT ET INTUMESCEBAT) Eadem verba quæ supra 11. Vers. 14. ET CLAMAVERUNT AD DOMINUM) יהוה id est, ad illum Deum opificem universi, cujus cultorem se Jonas dixerat. Facti erant in periculo religiosiores : ὐπὲρ Μιλέαν πλέυσας εὐσεβὴς ἔση. NE PEREAMUS IN ANIMA VIRI ISTIUS) Id est, propter homicidium quod in eo commisimus. Ut hic expli- cat Chaldæus, & ostendunt sequentia. QUIA TU DOMINE SICUT VOLUISTI FE- CISTI.) Qui tempestatem hanc plane extraordinariam su- scitasti, qui sortem fecisti cadere super Jonam, qui ipsum adegisti, ut se fontem & causam hujus mali fateretur. ET TIMUERUNT VIRI TIMORE MAGNO DOMINUM) Iterum יהוה. Piscator timori servili, Coccejus carnali tri- buit hanc orationem; sed vere timuisse & coluisse nautas illos Deum cultu religioso & sacro, testatur διαρ́ῤήδην Propheta v. 14. ET TIMUERUNT viri timore MAGNO DOMINUM יהוה, & im- molaverunt hostias Domino, & voverunt vota.

Quae sunt documenta veri cultus divini. Nec a- liud suadet precatio, quia inclamarunt voce alta, non amplius quisque suos Deos falsos, ut antea v. 5. Sed Jehovam de cujus majestate, & voluntate à Jo- na instructi erant: Obsecramus ô Jehovah, ah ne pereamus pro anima viri istius, & ne reponas nobis sanguinem innocentem: quia tu Domine, sicut voluisti, fecisti. Agnoscunt αὐτοκρατορίαν & αὐτεξουσίαν Domini, quod & perdere & servare ipsos in tanta tempestate, ac sanguinem ab ipsis poscere, aut gra- tiam iisdem concedere possit. Non male Grotius ad illa verba: Quia tu Domine sicut voluisti, fecisti: Qui tempestatem hanc plane extraordinariam su- scitasti, qui sortem fecisti cadere super Jonam, ut se fontem & causam hujus mali fateretur. Tu Jeho- vah totam hanc rem mirabiliter direxisti, ut certe necesse sit, vel hunc virum solum, vel nos simul cum ipso omnes perire. Concludunt ex tempesta- te, sorte, Jonae confessione, & consilio totum hoc esse opus divinae providentiae & voluntatis. Antea cum audivissent Jonam de Deo coelorum qui fecit mare & aridum, deque officio suo differentem, & intellexissent, Ninivem urbem admodum poten- tem & florentem, ob peccata subversum iri, & Jo- nam ipsum ita à Deo suo puniri, ac sese cum ipso in tantum discrimen adduci cernerent, dicuntur ti- muisse timore magno vers. 10. quoniam sibi quoque peccatorum conscii erant, praesentissimum immi- nere exitium videbant. Jam consilio Prophetae percepto, quum aliter exitium sese haud effugere posse, reapse deprehendant, ad Deum oratione ar- denti se recipiunt, precantur, ut periculum, in quo erant omnes propter unum, avertatur, deprecan- tur, ne mors Jonae sibi imputetur, laudantque De- um propter justitiam & potentiam. Denique cum Jona in mare praecipitato, fluctus maris sedarentur, & desisteret mare ab aestu, ac fervore suo, quo ve- luti irascebatur illi, qui creatoris obsequium detre- ctaverat, confirmati sunt hoc miraculo in agnitio- ne veri Dei, eamque coluerunt, non hypocritico ani- mo, sed in spiritu & veritate, vota etiam Domino vo- ventes, quod hunc Deum, ceu Deum suum religiose veneraturi sint. Vere ad Dominum conversos fuiffe, agnoscunt plerique Interpp. Lyranus, Va- tablus, Arias Montanus, Cornelius à Lapide, ut & nostrates; nec non è veteribus Theodoret. Cyrillus, & Hieronymus, qui, Grandis, inquit, vectorum fides, periclitantur ipsi, & pro alterius anima deprecantur: sciunt enim majorem esse mortem peccati, quam vitae. Non timent simpliciter, ut in principio legimus, sed timore magno, juxta illud quod dicitur, ex tota ani- ma, ex toto corde, & ex tota mente sua. Et im- molaverunt hostias, quas certe juxta literam in me- diis fluctibus non habebant: sed quia sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus est. Et in alio loco dicitur: Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, & redde altissimo vota tua. Et rursum: Reddemus tibi vitulos la- biorum nostrorum. Idcirco in mari immolant ho- stias: & alias sponte promittunt: vota facientes: se nunquam ab eo, quem colere coeperant, recessu- ros, timuerunt enim timore magno: Quia ex tran- quillitate maris & tempestatis fuga, vera Prophetae verba cernebant. Jonas in mari fugitivus naufra- gus, mortuus, salvat naviculam fluctuantem, salvat ethnicos in diversas prius sententias mundi errore ja- ctatos.

## 1:16
Verse of the same. AND THEY OFFERED SACRIFICES TO THE LORD, AND MADE VOWS) They promised victims, which they would offer to God in the Jerusalem temple; and they made vows, namely concerning works of mercy, as Kimchi thinks.

Regarding spiritual sacrifices, as we have seen, Jerome, and also Remigius and Albert, understand them; others, along with the Chaldean, such as Vatablus, Montanus, and B. Tarnovius, understand them as material ones offered in the ship; indeed, even when it was now permitted, having returned to the land and the holy city, they promised that they would show external worship in deed, and would sacrifice a sacrifice to the true God of Israel, to Jehovah himself, to whom they also vowed other vows, and not the least among them that this God would henceforth be their God. The Hebrew words imply not only a vowed or promised sacrifice, but the actual offering of sacrifices. Therefore, Christoph. à Castro, with Theophylact, Hugo, and Dionysius, maintains that they had arrived in port and had truly sacrificed victims to God. But since this worship of God, as appears from the words of the Prophet, was pleasing, it is not to be believed that those sacrifices were offered outside Jerusalem, and therefore the paraphrase of Osiander is pleasing, who renders it thus: They sacrificed victims to the Lord after they had arrived again on the continent to the holy land: For while they were still sailing, they had vowed vows, that by the offering of victims at Jerusalem they would show themselves grateful to the true God, the creator of heaven and earth, if they had arrived safely in port.

Latin:

Vers. eod. ET IMMOLAVERUNT HOSTIAS DOMINO, ET VOVERUNT VOTA) Promiserunt victimas, quas offerrent Deo in templo Hierosolymitano; & vota vove- runt, nempe de operibus misericordiae, ut sentit Kimchi.

De spiritualibus hostiis, ut vidimus, Hieronymus, nec non Remigius, Albertus, de materialibus in navi oblatis alii intelligunt cum Chaldæo, ut Vatablus, Montanus, B. Tarnovius, quin etiam quando jam licebat, in terram & urbem sanctam reversis, promiserunt se exhibituros cultum externum in opere, & sacrificaturos sacrificium vero Deo Israëlis ipsi Jehovæ, cui voverunt etiam alia vota, & inter ea non postremum hunc Deum dehinc fore Deum suum. Verba Ebræa non tantum votum vel promissum sacrificium, sed actualem oblationem sacrificiorum inferunt. Ideo Christoph. à Castro cum Theophyl. Hugone & Dionysio in portum eos appulisse, & hostias vero Deo immolasse vult. Sed quum hic cultus Deo, ut è verbis Prophetæ apparet, placuerit, extra Hierusalem sacrificia illa oblata fuisse, non credendum est, ideoque placet Osiandri paraphrasis, qui ita reddit: Immolaverunt hostias Domino, postquam iterum in continentem ad terram sanctam appulissent: Etenim cum adhuc navigarent, voverant vota, quod oblatione victimarum Jerosolymis Deo vero cœli terræque creatori gratos se exhibere vellent, si salvi in portum appulissent.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

Jonah, swallowed by a whale, remained in its belly for three days; by praying, he expressed the anxiety of his heart and his trust in the Lord, whom the whale vomited out alive onto the land.

Crying out to the Lord, he is cast forth from the throat of the underworld.

Ver. 1.

A GREAT FISH) A 'three-night dog,' as Lycophron says, who transferred the history received from the Hebrews to Hercules, to whom all great things were accustomed to be ascribed, as we said in the first book on the Truth of the Christian Religion.

Rondeletius (l. 13 de Pisc.), Ulysses Aldrovandus (l. 3 de Pisc. c. 32), Pineda (l. 4 de reb. Salom. c. 12), and Christoph. à Castro opine that it was called a Carcharias or dog by the Italians and a Lamia by Nicander. Cornel. à Lapide reports from Gellius that the Massilians caught a dog in which they had found an armored man.
