Concerning which, more has been said in the Antapologia against the Rintelenses published in the name of the Theological Faculty. Nor does B. Luther observe the word of uniting rashly. Therefore, he says, the Prophet uses the word of uniting, because the whole Kingdom of Israel was alien from the kingdom of Judah. These enmities, he says, will cease when the Gospel is divulged. For they will all be like sheep enclosed in one fold, which will feed together under the same shepherd. B. Hopfnerus also urges this argument. For that this congregation does not signify here a collection for destruction is proved from the abolition of the whole of Jacob and the remnants of Israel. For the Jews and the Israelites were not deported at the same time, but at different times: nor were only the remnants of the Israelites exiles, but all the Israelites were carried away. On the other hand, the congregation of the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel, who place one head over themselves by faith and confession, is said to be simultaneous, Hos. 1. 11, and the bringing into one fold through one shepherd is described, John X. Wherefore in this place also the congregation of Jacob and Israel is to be understood as simultaneous concerning the restoration of the Church. This very argument compelled even Cornelius à Lapide, so that although he said these things were best understood of the return of the Jews from Babylon, he finally yielded to our interpretation: Truly, because then only the Jews, not the Israelites, except for very few, were gathered again, and not all the Jews returned, but many remained in Babylon, and others wandered dispersed through various regions: furthermore, because Zerubbabel was not King, hence this liberation and congregation of Israel was only begun and imperfect. Wherefore we are compelled to say that these things must be referred plainly and fully to Christ. For although he alludes to Zerubbabel and the Jews of that age, and touches upon them as it were in passing, yet the mind and scope of the Prophet extends further, rises higher, and is carried to Christ, through whom this prophecy was perfectly fulfilled. For the Prophets are accustomed to terminate their oracles in Christ. Tarnovius himself confessed that the word שְׁאֵרִית is very often used concerning certain chosen remnants of the Jews, Am. V. 15, ch. IX. 12, Mich. V. 7, 8.

Fifthly, that ascent of the Happoretz or the breaker-through cannot be understood of a soldier, whether Assyrian or Chaldean. It is rather to be understood of a certain individual, who is designated by He Hajediah, and of such a breaker-through who ought to open a path so that those also to whom the path is opened may break through and enter through the gate. Which certainly does not fit an Assyrian or Chaldean soldier. The gloss of Grotius does violence to the text, while he imagines some passing through the gate, and others going out through it, the former being Assyrians and Chaldeans, the latter being citizens, which he introduces from mere ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει. The phrase itself and the mode of speaking argues that the discourse is about the same people, that they are to pass and enter through the gate, where the path will be opened for them by THAT BREAKER. And how can the Assyrian of Salmanasser and the Chaldean soldier of Nabuchodonosor be joined in the same act of breaking through? Such commentaries have hardly come into the mind of anyone except Grotius. Nor indeed can the breaker be understood with Calvin as the Assyrian and Babylonian King. For he himself did not ascend and break through by gathering before, but against them, and by scattering. On the contrary, however, the phrase (before them) denotes priority in breaking through, so that those before whom he breaks through may have followed the breaker: whence the argument: he is the breaker here, who has as followers in the breaking through those before whom he breaks through. But Christ, and not the Assyrian and Babylonian King, has as followers in the breaking through those before whom he breaks through, namely the faithful, whence in Col. 1 he is called ἀρχὴ the beginning and the firstborn of the dead, likewise πρόδρομος, and forerunner in the entry to heaven Heb. VI. 20. Therefore Christ and not the Assyrian or Babylonian is that breaker. We add what B. Höpfnerus has: In the Hebrew is הַפֹּרֵץ that breaker, and it is demonstrated δεικτικῶς as a certain individual, from פָּרַץ he broke through, destroyed: Christ the Redeemer who, by a plenary satisfaction rendered to God the Father for us, broke through and destroyed the force and obstacles and barriers of the Devil, of death, and of sin, which breaking through is followed by the ascension, by which, resurrected into life, he celebrated a triumph over Satan and his and our enemies and ascended into heaven to prepare a place for us, according to that in Eph. IV, he led captivity captive and penetrated the heavens closed to us Heb. IV. 14. In this breaking through and his ascension, however, he obtains the primacy, whence the Prophet says: The breaker shall ascend before them, i.e., he himself in this victory won over the devil and death did not profit himself but was made the cause and author of the liberation and vivification of all the pious, Col. 1, 18. Apoc. 1, 5. 1. Cor. XV. 10. Furthermore follows the efficacy of the death and life of Christ, and the communion of the same, as regards the faithful, which he expresses by the mention of both the breaking through, by which the pious, through the virtue and efficacy of Christ their head, strive to struggle out and even struggle out, from the power of all enemies and violently they seize the kingdom of heaven Luke 14:24. Then the passage and exit through the gate, which corresponds to the ascension, which he had previously attributed to the head. And therefore Christ is proposed as the head of the Church partly by merit and efficacy by which he is a breaker-through in the way we have said the communication of his efficacy, which he distributes to those united to the Church through the joints and ligaments of the Spirit and faith. For that efficacy of the death of Christ indeed consists in the abolition of sin and death, and likewise of the law insofar as it curses and is a bond against us, and the power of sin killing us; But the efficacy and power of the life of Christ communicated to us pertains to our placement in Christ the head in the heavens, as regards the spirit, and the resuscitation of us to eternal life and our placement in the heavens, as regards the whole man, which is therefore rightly expressed both by that breaking-through and by the passage and exit through the gate, i.e., the powerful forces of the devil and of all enemies, likewise the greatest dangers, and finally death itself. Sixth, lest they should doubt who is indicated by Happoretz, who is to ascend before the Israelites to open a path for them and make a passage, the Prophet adds, AND THEIR KING SHALL PASS BEFORE THEM, calling him their King, in which the Interpreters easily agree. But Grotius imagines that these things are to be understood not of that breaker-through, as the continuity of the words demands, but of the King of Israel at that time, Hosea, and of the King of the Jews, Zedekiah. Finally, what the Prophet has concerning the passage to the Israelites, so that a path may be opened for them, Grotius draws to the captivity of the King in the sight of the Israelites. Which is truly to tear apart and twist Scripture.

Seventh, the Prophet explains himself even more clearly when, to that prediction AND THEIR KING SHALL PASS BEFORE THEM, he adds this κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν (explanatory) which is customary and very solemn for the Prophets; AND THE LORD AT THEIR HEAD. That King therefore who is to pass before them, and that breaker-through, is Jehovah the Lord, who will be at their head, or who is to pass before them at the head or in the beginnings: or rather, that Jehovah is at the head, i.e., Lord, Prince, captain, as Deut. 28:13, he will set you as the head, Ps. 18:44, You have established me as the head of the nations; unless the name of head here is to be understood rather insofar as it is considered compacted with the body and its members through joints and ligaments, which the blessed Höpfnerus judges more significantly in this place: because thus Christ is called the head in the scriptures, and thus all four conditions of the head are included here, namely (1) vigor (merit), and efficacy. (2) Communication of efficacy. (3) eminence. (4) perfection. Seventh, those following the breaker-through and exiting through the gate cannot be understood as the Assyrian and Babylonian soldiers. For those are said to break through, before whom the breaker-through ascends. But Jacob and Israel to be gathered into one fold are those before whom the breaker-through ascends. Therefore, Jacob and Israel, and not the Assyrian and Babylonian soldiers, are said in this place to break through. Furthermore, the breakers-through are said to exit through the gate: but the enemies were not exiting, but entering the middle gate Jer. 39:3. Finally, the King of those who break through is said to go before. For Calvin himself and Piscator do not think this King passing through first is the King of the Chaldean enemies but the King of the Jews, Zedekiah. How then will those, whose forerunner King is not Assyrian or Babylonian, be the Assyrian or Babylonian enemies? I pass over the fact that the Jewish King did not pass through the gate, but through the walls.

Eighth, to be at the head or as the head denotes conjunction with someone and defense, but not his destruction. Now, however, the same one is at the head who is called here their King, who is to go before them. And it would follow that Jehovah had fled before everyone, and therefore it would have to be said that he was led into captivity, if this passage in which Jehovah is at the head were to be taken as flight. Which is to be noted against Calvin and Piscator, who take it in that way; from all of which it is now most evident that the prophecy is not to be understood of King Zedekiah, not of Zerubbabel, but of Christ the King, who is JEHOVAH, who is that Happoretz, whose BREAKING-THROUGH ASCENSION into heaven is predicted to open the way for us, of whom David also prophesied gloriously in Ps. 68, by whose merit and power we penetrate the gate of heaven. Whence the Osiandrian paraphrase is to be approved here entirely: The breaker-through shall ascend before them: (i.e. Christ through the passion and death of the cross and through hell will victoriously break through, and ascending to the heavens will sit at the right hand of the Father. For thus (says Christ) it behooved Christ to suffer and to enter into his glory Luke 24.) And they shall pass the gate and shall exit through it: Heb. they (themselves also) shall break through and shall walk through the gate (that is, the entrance into heaven will be open to them:) and their King shall go before them, and the Lord (Jehovah) at their beginning. (That is, the King Christ, who in this place (as also often elsewhere) is called Lord or Jehovah, will hold the primacy in all things: and will open to all who believe in him the entrance to heavenly and eternal glory. Indeed, in this life also, he will protect them, as Leader and Captain, so that they do not perish. Therefore, they too through afflictions, temptations, and death to eternal happiness

will break through.) Beautiful are the things which the blessed Luther has here. And this passage is wonderfully elegant and most full of consolation. For the first word of the dissipator contains the meaning of the Cross and obstacles, then also of certain liberation, as if to say: I give to my sheep eternal life, and I lead them to true pastures, but this costs much. For it is not a beaten or easy path, many things stand in the way, which try to delay the elect, namely Satan, death, sin, the Law, why many things? the whole old Adam stands in the way. I will cause, however, that, even if there are obstacles, they nevertheless do not delay you. I will send ahead the Breaker-through Christ, who will break through and remove every stumbling block, he will prepare the way for you with the power of Satan and death broken, so that the passage may be easy afterwards, helped by my spirit. I said the word of breaking through signifies the cross, because one must break through a thousand dangers of things. For which reason, when he establishes Christ as (Poretz) or the breaker-through, he shows him to be true man, and to struggle with dangers as a man. As those agonies in death and on the cross testify. But because he conquers in those dangers, and through that victory prepares for himself a people and a kingdom. Therefore he is called our King. But the same one is also called here (Jehovah), which name is attributed to GOD alone. Therefore, let students of sacred matters observe this testimony, by which the divinity of CHRIST is certainly affirmed. In the marginal notes, Megalander has it thus: Here he speaks of the kingdom of CHRIST, who is our hero, who has broken through before us, and makes the path through sin, death, devil, and all evil, follow him boldly! All our people follow the blessed Luther, if perhaps you except one, the blessed Tarnov, who, though a most learned interpreter in other respects, allowed himself to be led astray here and in certain other places by Junius; yet he does not defend his opinion stubbornly, but has testified that he is prepared to yield to arguments, and he valued the opinion of the blessed Luther and the orthodox so highly that he proposed the same in his own words not inelegantly, but left the decision to the reader. For he has it thus in his Commentary on this Prophet, p. 65: "Nevertheless, so that a judgment may be made all the better concerning individual points, it will be worth the effort to propose here also the common explanation of this passage, briefly collected from all the principal interpreters." He has it thus, however, because the Prophet now in verse 12 turns from the evil to the good, and from the bodily kingdom, which he says is to be forsaken and destroyed, to the spiritual, which he promises is to be restored, while by this saying the glorious resurrection of Christ is pronounced with its fruit, since that breaker, Christ, is breaking through by means of passion, death, hell, the grave, and the heavens, and thus obtaining that his own, together with him as leader, may break through, to which he encourages them thus: I will surely gather you, O Jacob, all of you, while I will punish the rest of the wicked, of whom I have spoken hitherto, a voice, you who imitate the faith of Jacob, I will gather all into my faith and protection, I will surely gather the remnants of Israel, John 11:52, and I will dispose him together with the nations, having been called, John 10:16. Eph. 2:12, 14, into one fold, which is the Church, and I will protect them as the sheep of Bozrah, their Shepherd, and I will call many, so that they may resound like a great flock in the midst of their fold because of the multitude of men, nor will they fear wolves or dogs, that is, devils and false prophets, that they might be deceived or devoured, since no one can snatch them from my hand, John 10:28, as long as they remain in me, and if there are any other obstacles, by which they are less able to proceed with unhindered foot to the heavenly fold, I will remove them happily, for this breaker, the God-man, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, Rev. 5:5, will ascend in their sight, following whom as their leader the pious will break through, passing through the gate, by which they go out and go in, in the way they are called violent ones, Matt. 11:12, and their King Christ will pass before them, and that begotten Jehovah God will be at their head, Eph. 1:22 and 4:15, Col. 1:18. Although, however, for certain reasons he prefers the interpretation of Junius, he nevertheless submitted those reasons to the judgment of candid fellow-theologians and those who test every point by the norm of Scripture. But those reasons are not of such moment that one must depart from the received opinion. As for what is sought from the preceding threats, Pareus himself cuts the nerve of it, and the blessed Tarnov confesses that often, on account of the pious remnants of the people, consolations are immediately subjected to threats, even if he denies that there is evidence of this thing in this place: but our arguments have shown that it is not lacking.

Although, however, he urges that the word פרץ does not fit Christ, and that the pious do not break through the gate of heaven by force, nor go out from it, nor is Jehovah said to be at their head (לראשם) but in their head (בראשם), yet all those things seem easily dissolvable. For פרץ signifies a breaker. But did not Christ break through and penetrate the heavens in his ascension? Heb. 4:14. Then, if one must attend to the force and violence applied, just as this word is used concerning the violent and powerful irruption of enemies, 2 Sam. 5:20, Christ certainly broke through by force the spiritual enemies, being about to ascend into heaven, which emphasis the blessed Luther observed above in his Commentary on this passage. For it is noted that Christ, Jehovah, would break through by means of passion, death, hell, the grave, and the heavens, and would obtain for the faithful that they themselves might break through by the power of his resurrection, with the Lord going before them, and they themselves following the footsteps of their forerunner and Leader through death and the grave even into eternal life, as the blessed Aegidius Hunnius rightly observed in the Anti-Pareus, page 270. Concerning the pious, the blessed Luther observed: "Moreover, this way seems most harsh to the flesh. Therefore Christ says in the Gospel concerning the kingdom of God, that it is taken by force, that is, the violent will seize it." Just as the Prophet says here (parezu), they themselves also will break through by the power of their Leader. For it is necessary for the flesh to be mortified, and to oppose itself to the whole world, and to Satan, who tries to hinder and delay us, so that we do not follow this Disperser. But Christ consoles us in these difficulties, saying: "Take heart, I have overcome the world," that is, I have broken through. You also, with me as leader, will break through to the kingdom of God, so that it may be open to you. Nor does the word of going out conflict. For the pious go out from this world through this gate, which Christ opened. Therefore, both the terminus a quo and the terminus ad quem are noted, the gate of heaven, which they penetrate and pass through, nay, break through, going out from this world, nay, even from the bonds and power of Satan, sin, death, and hell. Add that in the Hebrew text there is no mention of entering and going out, but of a passage through a gate, and an exit, where by the gate some understand, including the blessed Höpfner in his unpublished commentary, the power of the Devil, Matt. 16:18, as also the greatest dangers and the tenth wave of calamities, and also death itself temporal: because the greatest dangers are called the gates of death, Ps. 9:13, and concerning death itself, Ps. 107:18. Job 38:17, the gates of death are spoken of, so that the sense is that the pious will escape free from the bonds and prison of the Devil, from the dominion and service of sin, from the curse of the law, and finally will not be broken by any dangers, nor will they remain in death, but will return to life. The word יצא is 'he went out', but not 'he entered', as the Vulgate rendered it: according to which can be understood by the gate, the access to the Church (through the use of the Word and Sacraments) which in Ps. 118:19 is called the gate of righteousness and the gate of the Lord: as also the access to glory and eternal life, which in Matt. 7:14, Luke 13:24 is called the narrow gate, to enter which we are commanded to strive (ἀγωνίζεσθαι) and to break in with a certain force. Luther: 'Zum Thor aus und einziehen', that is, they will break through the gates of hell, and will enter through the gates of righteousness and eternal life. The pious are said to have the Messiah בראשם at the head or in the beginning, because he himself first penetrated the heavens, whom nevertheless they also have as head, because he is called their King, who is before them. Concerning which we again bring forward B. Höpfner: AND THEIR KING SHALL PASS BEFORE THEM, AND THE LORD AT THEIR HEAD. It is added how Christ is also head: by dominion or eminence. For just as in the human body the head is eminent, and is in a higher place than the other members subject to it: So Christ is above all things, that is, above all creatures, and thus also above the Church, and indeed he is constituted head over all things to the Church itself Eph. I. 21. i.e. he adjusts the government of the universe to the salvation of the Church, and is moved toward it with singular love above all other creatures and cares for and governs it in a special way. For although all creatures are subject to the feet of Christ Eph. I. 22. & he himself is also called the head of the Angels Col. II. 10. yet he is the head of all things only by reason of Creation and lordship: But believers are subject to the feet of Christ in such a way that they are at the same time also the feet, hands, and members of Christ. And in this respect Christ is called king, with this sanction of his office assigned, that he passes before their face, i.e. before them, namely, those united to him by faith:

which can be explained both concerning the first signs of victory, which Christ has already carried off from our enemies, John 16:33, and concerning the assertion of his own against enemies and the destruction of enemies. For to pass before someone is to go ahead, to precede, as in Exod. 17:5, Moses is ordered to pass before the people, i.e., to go ahead, and 1 Sam. 9:27, Tell the boy to pass before us, i.e., to precede. To go ahead here will therefore be either to hold the first place in dominion, or to lead out, to counsel, to assist, and to defend against enemies, as in Deut. 9:3, God is said to pass before the Israelites, i.e., to precede their enemies in order to put them to flight. Equivalent to this formula are those when he is said to precede the people in Deut. 1:33, ch. 4:37, and the angel of the Lord in Exod. 14:19, ch. 23:20, ch. 32:34. Finally, it is subjoined how Christ is also the head of the Church by perfection. JEHOVAH SHALL BE AT THEIR HEAD. For Christ is not only man, and ὁμούσιος with us, so that he can love us as his own flesh, Eph. 5:25, and sympathize with us, Heb. 4:15, but he is also JEHOVAH, who feels all our evils, sees all things that happen to us, hears us, speaks for us, and intercedes before GOD the Father. Here, therefore, Jehovah is given as head of the Church at the same time as he is man. But if, according to others, it pleases one to interpret the word בראשׁ as 'at the head,' then it will be an ἐξήγησις of the preceding member. But the name of head, insofar as it is considered through joints and connections with the body and its members as compacted, is more significant, and in this way includes all four conditions of a head: namely 1. Vigor and efficacy. 2. Communication of efficacy. 3. Eminence: and 4. perfection. To which Hosea ch. 1:11 also points a finger. The children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and shall appoint for themselves one head; as all these things have been excellently executed by B. Höpfnerus. Nor, finally, is it an obstacle that this prophecy is not cited in the N.T. For many other prophecies exist in the O.T. which are not cited in the N.T. διαῤῥήδην, which nevertheless sound undoubtedly of Christ. And it suffices that all things contained in this prophecy receive light from the N.T. and agree with it completely.

Which even doctors of no low rank in the very School of Calvin acknowledged, who therefore deserted their Calvin here. Thus Hier. Zanch. in Comment. on this passage is introduced, Jehovah, who promises that he will gather the people from all the lands of the nations in which the Israelites were dispersed. But this gathering of the ten tribes was not to be except through Christ: since by the power of his death, through the preaching of the Apostles, he gathered all the children of God who were dispersed, as John declared. These are the words of Jehovah: In gathering I will gather all of you, etc., their King shall pass before them, and Jehovah at their head. But this is Christ. For he promises that he will gather all Jacob, that is, all the elect. In that tumult, he promises victory through Christ. Therefore he says: The breaker shall ascend before them: This is Christ. For he is called the breaker, because by his power he broke the gates of the underworld: he overcame the Devil, and against his will led out his captives, and asserted them into liberty, and asserts them daily. Does not this title most fittingly suit Christ? At the end, he says, And Jehovah shall be at their head, that is, he shall be the head of the Church. But who is the head of the Church if not Christ? The Prophet certainly did not ignore this. Therefore he himself also knew Christ to be the true Jehovah. Thus Rudolphus Gualtherus:

First, he promises restoration in general, when he says: 'Gathering I will gather you, all Jacob; by the word of gathering he understands liberation and restoration, which he opposes to the dissipation or dispersion of the whole nation, which had been done by the Assyrians: so that

'he may show that it will not prevent them from being gathered at the appointed time under the Messiah. Where, however, we observe that the Prophet speaks of a spiritual congregation, which is of souls, when they are united by faith, so that they coalesce into one body in the spirit. For not all Israelites were gathered into some one region from that time, nor are we taught by any oracles of the prophets that this will ever happen. But that dispersion of the Israelite nation was a type of the human race, which we know had been most foully dissipated into various sects and pursuits of sin before Christ came into the world. 'But just as neither the Assyrian nor the Babylonian captivity prevented those whom God wished to return to their native seats from being liberated through Cyrus, so neither could that foul and miserable dispersion of all nations under the power of darkness prevent the son of God, Jesus Christ, from gathering all the children of God (as John says) into one. To this pertains what follows shortly after: I will place them together, as the sheep of Bozrah, as a flock in the midst of their fold. Behold, he speaks of one flock only, not many, and of one fold only, into which this whole flock ought to be gathered, and Christ agrees with the words of the Prophet, when in John 10 he says: There shall be one fold and one shepherd. He compares them to the sheep of Bozrah to show that this flock will be precious, and not common. For Bozrah was a region of Idumea, abounding in rich pastures, and therefore famous for the most delicate livestock. 'And indeed the Church cannot but be considered most delicate by God, which (as the Prophet says) he holds dearer than the apple of his eye, and which he willed to be redeemed by the blood of his son, Zech. 2, Acts 20. Furthermore, he teaches who those are that ought to be so gathered. And first indeed he names all Jacob, but soon adds an explanation: Gathering I will gather the remnants of Israel. There are those who think that by the name of Jacob the tribe of Judah is denoted, which is to return entirely from Babylon, together with some remnants of the Israelites who are to join themselves to it. Whose opinion I do not disapprove of, if we look at the bare history of the return from Babylon. Because, however, it is certain that the Prophet looks to something higher, and weaves a prophecy about the kingdom of Christ, I think that mention of the remnants is made so that he may restrict to the elect what he seemed to have promised to all in general. This agrees with the oracles of other Prophets, whom we know to do the same. Isaiah certainly says: If your people, O Israel, were as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved. Joel likewise: On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be salvation as the Lord says, and that in the remnant whom the Lord calls. And again Isaiah, intending to console Hezekiah when Sennacherib threatened the city, says among other things: For a remnant shall go out from Jerusalem, and those saved from Mount Zion. Thirdly, he describes the condition of the Church or the pious under Christ, where many things are said which serve for our consolation. First. They shall be in a tumult because of men. By which word he hints at the gathering, which is to be so great toward those remnants, the seed-plot of the Church, that it may bear the appearance of a public tumult. This began to be fulfilled in the time of the Apostles, when a wonderful change of the whole world took place, and everywhere the elect, having set aside either the ceremonies of the Jews or the superstitions of the Gentiles, betook themselves to the faith of Christ and the fellowship of his Church, and indeed with such fervor that they seemed to the impious to be in a tumult and to be stirring up something seditious. For it is relevant to this that we know it was more than once objected to the Apostles as a crime that they had disturbed the whole world. And today we see that wherever the light of the gospel is kindled, many embrace it with incredible zeal, and are so in a tumult that, having shaken off the darkness, they walk in it

can. This is that holy tumult, which in the meantime does not in the least disturb civil laws, however much this may seem to happen to the impious, who on this occasion cry out that the doctrine of the Gospel is the cause of sedition. Next, 'He shall ascend (he says) the breaker before them': he calls Christ the breaker or the one who breaks through, in order to express His invincible power, by which He both asserts His own and gathers His Church. For He is that most valiant hero who breaks into the house of the Devil, conquered and bound him while he resisted, and plundered his vessels, namely by asserting into liberty the men whom he was oppressing with his tyranny. That same one tore down the partition of the wall (to use the Apostle's words), which was keeping us from the kingdom of GOD. Furthermore, He destroyed the kingdom of the Devil and his works in their entirety, and propagated His own kingdom throughout the whole world, having removed and broken all the obstacles which the princes of the world, as well as the prelates of false doctrines and impostors, were throwing in the way. And it was necessary for us to be forewarned of this, so that we might not think this work was human, but that we might know that all these things were accomplished by divine power. He adds, however, to these: 'And they shall break through and pass the gate, and shall go out by it.' He speaks of the remnant of the Jews, among whom the Apostles easily held the primacy, and this passage is expounded concerning their Apostolic function. For although Christ is truly that breaker who destroyed the opposing power, yet, by His singular grace, He also deigned to use the ministry of men. And it is certain that the Apostles, with admirable alacrity and success, broke through all those things which were hindering the restoration of the kingdom of GOD. But what is said about them ought to be referred no less to all believers. Thus far also Gualtherus.

one Shepherd, and one fold. I will put together.) He united His people into one Church, because there is one faith, one Lord, one Baptism. Not, indeed, in place, so that it is necessary to go to Palestine, but in the concord of minds, and in equal dignity, which is in Christ. Moreover, those who were once wolves are to be converted into lambs, so that they may be able to dwell together with others. Here also Conr. Pelicanus is to be compared, who, although he thinks that the last verses can also be understood as the punishment of those who are unwilling to hear the Prophets, nevertheless indicated and handed down an opinion agreeing with ours in all respects; but also Pareus, the hyperaspistes of Calvin, retained such an interpretation in his Biblical notes, and in the defense of Calvin against B. Hunnius. I, he says, willingly accept the passage concerning Christ. Although he also wishes to defend another of Calvin's at the same time: but ineptly. Because there is such a great divorce between these two interpretations (as B. Hunnius warns) that if one stands, the other falls, since it is impossible for the same words to contain both the threats of punishments and the promises of spiritual benefits, and it is also impossible for God and the Babylonian to be understood at the same time by the word 'breaker,' or for Christ and King Zedekiah to be noted equally by the name of King.

But before Gualtherus and Zanchius, Oecolampadius, Calvin's teacher, explained it in a similar way: 'I will gather, I will gather.' In this one may see the kingdom of Christ, as often as the calling of the Church is predicted to us. Because, therefore, the whole of Jacob is to be recalled, this prophecy cannot look to those who went out from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem. When Cyrus sent them, then the ten tribes were left in captivity in Assyria; indeed, even then when they returned from Babylon, they were perpetually afflicted, and had almost no rest. Whence here is not promised a return from Babylon, but rather that liberty which was procured for us through Christ, and the gathering into one of the children of GOD who were dispersed. Where Christ had been exalted, He drew all things to Himself. I know that the Judaizers look to this, that toward the end of time the Jews are to be called to the faith and joined to the Church of GOD: to which I would not dare to accede. Let them see from Hosea not a few scriptures which manifestly indicate the Church gathered, and that those from the Jews who are worthy to be received have been received. Although I would not deny that some are also called to the faith daily, but they are called today as the other nations. (The remnant) Certainly he speaks of that Jacob who imitates the faith of Jacob, just as the true children of Abraham are those who follow the faith of Abraham, so are the true remnant of Israel. In the beginning he puts the whole of Jacob, finally he adds the remnant. A great part will perish because of their impiety. Peter in one sermon brought three thousand, then in another five thousand, and the others converted many thousands to the faith. Nevertheless, in the meantime, we can join to the remnant of Israel and Jacob those who come from the nations to the faith of Christ. For we have here manifestly, as in John X, how Christ is our shepherd, who is about to gather to Himself a flock from another fold, so that there may be

The Belgian Pampbrasta also abandon Calvin and embrace our explanation. Finally, Ioh. Coccejus (that I may supersede bringing in others) gravely refutes Junius and Grotius, because the latter preferred to follow the Jews: indeed, he observes that the ancient Jews also stand on our side. The breaking through of Zedekiah does not fit v. 13. For it is said that the breaker is about to ascend before the Israelites themselves. Therefore, neither the Assyrian nor the Babylonian can be understood. And immediately, when it is said 'their King,' whose King can be understood, if not the one before whom the breaker has ascended? Again, in whose principles will the Lord be, if not those whose King is said to pass through before them? And further: Truly, by this distortion, the Jews indeed attempt to obscure an illustrious prophecy concerning the coming of Christ and the time of His coming. In which matter they do not even have all their own people in agreement. For the Chaldean, the Ancients, (as Kimchi testifies) and R. Solomon understand it to be a promise: R. David is in doubt. It did not befit our people to follow those who corrupt the text, especially Grotius: after the Belgian edition, having abandoned Junius, gave a better explanation. Likewise: Junius follows partly the corruption of Aben Ezra, partly that of Joseph Kimchi, while he wishes it to be a communication in allusion to the promise of the Pseudo-Prophets. But the matter is evident, the convenient order of the Prophecies supporting the πα- ραλληλία [parallelism], and its own phrase by its emphasis, importing that which we have said. The Chaldean and the ancient Hebrews agree, and the beginning of this section agrees perfectly with its end. The Lord is awakened from his place and will descend, and will tread upon the high places of the earth. And he passes, their King goes on always more and more before them, nay, Jehovah is in their beginnings, indeed, so that he may break through, and tread upon the high places of the earth. Jerome, although, as he himself confesses, he struggled with great difficulties in the whole beginning of Micah: nevertheless he acknowledged no other King preceding the Church, except Christ. Furthermore, what kind of eruption that is, is explained at the beginning of chapter IV, as concerning the king in chapter IV. 14. and chapter V. 1. etc. Thus far Coccejus. We add the opinion of Jerome: They have entered, he says, because their King also entered the same gate, and opened the way for them, so that they might walk without any difficulty. For the Lord himself, both king and shepherd, is both the way and the gate, and he says: I am the gate, by me he who shall have entered, shall be saved: he shall enter in, and shall go out, and shall find pasture. Concerning which gate it is also prophesied elsewhere: This is the gate of the Lord, the righteous shall enter through it. And afterwards while: And they passed through the gate and went out through it: which passage and departure, however, cannot be attributed apart from Christ our King, who is King and Lord. For it is immediately connected: But the Lord shall be prince. Finally, that even some of the Hebrews themselves add their vote to this truth, these things confirm, namely that in Bereschith Rabba R. Moses Hadarschan on Gen. XL. it is read thus: The planting from below is Abraham: the planting from above is the Messiah, just as it is said in Mich. II. 13. He ascends breaking through the entrance before them, etc. And on that Gen. XLIV. 18. And Judah approached him. This is what is written in Cant. I. 4. We will exult and rejoice in thee, when we shall rejoice, when the feet of the divinity shall stand on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem to the East. Otherwise: we will rejoice, and we will exult in thee: When? when the captives shall ascend from hell, and the Deity at their head. As it is said in Mich. II. 13. And their King shall pass before them, and the Lord at their head. We treated of this oracle in the Paschal Program of the year 1671, publicly proposed in the name of the Magnificent Rector Dn. D. JOH. DEUTSCHMANN, Professor of Theology, which we only append here, so that the illustrious prophecy may be the more rightly vindicated. It reads thus verbatim:

Sing praises to our GOD, sing praises; Sing praises to our King, sing praises. For GOD is King of all the earth: Sing praises wisely, GOD shall reign over the nations. GOD sits upon His holy seat. Thus the Jessean prophet stirred us to Paschal joys, (Ps. XLVII, 7.) and to sing Psalms to our GOD, to our KING, to CHRIST JESUS, who is EMMANUEL, GOD WITH US, (Is. VII. 14.) OUR KING established upon Mount Zion. (Ps. II. 6.) That KING, who reigns over the nations, from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth (Ps. LXXII. 8.) to whom the nations are given as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth as a possession (Ps. II. 8.) That King over all the earth, of whom the Prophet, in that day the Lord shall be one, and His name shall be one (Zach. XIII. 9.) To Paschal joys, I say. For at Easter the risen Christ announced these joys, to be made known throughout the whole world. Thus it is written, and thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins be preached in his name to ALL NATIONS. Luke XXIV. 46. 47. At Easter Christ appointed the Apostles as heralds of this Oecumenical joy (John XX. 21.) As the Father has sent me, even so I send you. But whither did he send the Apostles? He explained that in Mark XVI. 15. Going into the WHOLE WORLD, preach the Gospel to EVERY CREATURE. Matt. XXVIII. 19. Going teach ALL NATIONS. At Easter Christ rose again, to distribute the good things which he brought forth, and the trophies which he acquired, throughout the whole world. For he was delivered for our offenses, and rose again for our justification (Rom. IV. 25.) Now therefore GOD ARISES and his enemies are scattered (Ps. LXVIII. 1.) Now Christ has scattered many, and Christ has distributed the strong as spoils, for the reason that he delivered his soul unto death, (Is. LIII. 12.) Which, although ascending into heaven, mounting the throne, and occupying his kingdom, he did in a more illustrious and ample manner, whence David applauds the one ascending, and provokes all peoples to jubilation: O clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with the voice of exultation. GOD ascends in jubilation: and the Lord with the voice of the trumpet. Sing praises to our God; sing praises:

In this Paschal festival, however, that distribution of spoils began, and the exultation over the conquered enemies. For Christ, the Victor of the Devil, of death, and of hell, HAS RISEN. The infernal regions render up the Victor, and the heavenly regions receive the triumphant one, as St. Augustine says in Sermon III. on the Resurrection. Now Christ has despoiled principalities and powers, he has made a show of them confidently, triumphing over them openly in himself (Coloss. II. 15.) Now he sings a joyful paean: And I have redeemed them from the hand of hell: I have delivered them from death: I have been thy plague, O death: I have been thy destruction, O hell (Hos. XIII. 14.) Now with dancing the Apostles sing in response: Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O hell, where is thy victory? (1 Cor. XV. 54. 55.) Now is fulfilled what, after the Shepherd was struck, the sheep dispersed in the bloody and cruel passion, according to the interpreter Zechariah, the Lord received (c. XIII. 7.) I will turn my hand to the little ones. And this is what the Prophet Micah foretold, who seems to have embraced all these things (c. II. 12. 13.) I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee: I will surely gather the remnant of Israel, I will put them together as the flock in the fold, as the sheep in the midst of the pens, they shall be in a tumult by reason of the multitude of men. For he shall ascend opening the way before them: they shall divide and pass through the gate and shall enter in by it: and their King shall pass before them, and the Lord at their head. Which is an illustrious Paschal prophecy, or sermon. For in the manner of the Prophets it is expressed in the past tense, what was to be only long after: not only for the sake of certainty, but especially so that the faithful of that time might be led into the present matter, and the benefits of Christ the Redeemer might always be held as recent, in which way the lamb was slain from the foundation of the world (Apoc. XIII. 8.) and according to the Apostle, (Heb. XIII. 8.) JESUS CHRIST yesterday, today, the same and for ever.

But here must be considered both the gathering of Jacob into one, promised in the time of the N.T., so that the fold of our Shepherd may be signally increased from various peoples: and the ascension of the breaking-through King and Lord. This is the cause of that. For unless that PERRUPTOR (BREAKER-THROUGH) had ascended, unless our King had passed before the Israelites, and the Lord had been at their head, no one could have passed through the gate, and entered in by it, much less could the whole of Jacob be gathered by gathering, or be established as a flock in the fold. The foundation of salvation, therefore, is situated in that title of BREAKER-THROUGH. Which at the same time exhibits a compendium of our faith concerning Christ. That Breaker-through is the God-man, GOD and Man. He broke through heaven in his DESCENT from heaven, and incarnation according to the prayers and sighs of the ancient faithful (Is. LXIII. 1.) O that thou wouldst REND the heavens, and come down? He broke through the closed womb at his birth: because he went forth from the womb without violation of the virgin mother through the closed gate, (Ezech. XLIV. 2.) What is the gate in the house of the Lord that is closed, (says S. Augustin. serm. XIX. de Natal. Dom.) if not that Mary will always be intact? And what is it that it will be closed forever, if not because Mary is a virgin before birth, a virgin in birth, a virgin after birth! He broke through all the force and fraud of the enemy; he broke through the pains and bars of death itself, because it was impossible for him to be held by death (Act. II. 24.) he broke through the Diabolical powers and the snares of hell (Ps. XVIII. 6. Heb. II. 14.) because he crushed the head of the infernal serpent (Gen. III. 15.) and as a stronger one coming upon him, he overcame Satan and took away all his armor in which he trusted, and distributed his spoils (Luc. XI. 22.) He broke through the sepulcher, because rising again he came forth through the sepulcher that was closed and fortified with a great stone; he broke through the closed door after the resurrection, when he penetrated to the disciples without the doors being opened, and with Justin saying (Quest. LXVII to the Orthodox) that by his own power he went out from the monument upon which a stone had been placed, and entered to the disciples with the door closed. He broke through heaven in his ascension: because, as the Apostle testifies, he penetrated the heavens (Heb. IV. 14.), having been made higher than the heavens (Heb. VII. 28.), he ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things (Ephes. IV. 10.) and by his ascension he opened heaven, which had been closed to us, he initiated for us a new and living way through the veil, that is, his flesh, that we might have confidence in the entrance of the saints in his blood (Heb. X. 19.) and he made known to us the ways of life, that he might fill [us] with joy with his countenance (Psal. XVI. 10.) That Breaker-through even now in the defense of his own breaks through all the counsels, all the machinations, all the attacks, all the violence, all the fraudulence of his enemies, who sitting at the right hand of the Lord places all his enemies as a footstool for his feet and rules in the midst of his enemies (Psal. CX. 1. 2.) That Breaker-through breaks through, in our conversion, and penetrates with the power of his word our stony hearts, that he may be able to enter them, and inhabit them, through faith (Ez. XXXVI. 26. Act. XVI. 14. Ap. III. 20. Eph. III. 17. Joh. XIV. 23.) That Breaker-through will break through on the last day our sepulchers, and will lead us out from our monuments with an omnipotent voice (Joh. V. 28.) having been made himself the firstborn of the dead (Apoc. I. 5.) therefore he exclaims: I am the first, and the last, and the living, and I was dead: and behold I am living for ever and ever, and I have the keys of death and of hell. (Apoc. I. 18.)

Some Papists, Lyranus, Cornelius a Lapide, and others, snatch these [words] to refer to the exit of Christ from limbo, who led out with him the souls of the Fathers, as a chosen flock, which had been detained in limbo as sheep in a fold. But Scripture is ignorant of this limbo of the Fathers; indeed, it testifies that they were in the hand of God, in the bosom of Abraham, in the bundle of the living, and in the heavenly Republic, in the people of God, to whom they were gathered through death. What of the fact that Cornelius himself explained the Prophetic oracle in a far different way: He alludes, he says, to the Babylonian captivity and prison, i.e. Zerubbabel will break through the Babylonian prison, and you following him will likewise break through the same, and from it you will joyfully appear in Zion: much more truly the antitype of Zerubbabel, that is, Christ, liberating you from the captivity and prison of the Devil, of infidelity, and of sin BY THE MERIT OF HIS CROSS, will break through the same, and you will likewise break through the same and will appear full of thanks in the spiritual Zion, that is, in the Church, which is the free, holy, and happy city of the living God. These are the words of the Jesuit: who even if he fabricates at the same time an anagogical sense about limbo, we know nevertheless that there is only one sense of Scripture. And Christopher a Castro of the same society acknowledges, indeed even Cornelius himself, that Jerome, Remigius, Rupert, Albert, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Clarius, Arias, Ribera, and others accept the present prophecy concerning the congregation of the Israelites into one Church with the Gentiles through baptism and grace, which will come to pass by the merit and efficacy of Christ THE BREAKER-THROUGH.

Therefore, the more recent Jews, or some Judaizers, Calvin, and Hugo Grotius (whose mouths have been stopped elsewhere), do not deserve to be heard at all when they explain these things concerning Zerubbabel. For who that breaker-through is, the Prophet has clearly explained, namely the KING of Jacob, which dignity Zerubbabel never obtained, indeed the LORD JEHOVAH, who is the head to Israel, i.e., his HEAD: namely the Messiah who, since he is Jehovah, and KING and HEAD of the Church in a peculiar way, as of his mystical body, and is said to be ὁμοούσιος to the same, there can be no doubt that he himself is designated. Which the chief among the Reformed and of Calvin's own disciples acknowledge, Oecolampadius, Gualtherus, Hier. Zanchius, Conrad Pelicanus, Pareus, Coccejus, the Belgian Interpreters of the Bible: and among the Jews the more ancient Rabbis, with the Chaldean Paraphrase leading the way, R. Moses Hadarschan, and R. Salomo, and others. We have therefore here the GLORIOUS BREAKER-THROUGH Christ, our King and Head, indeed Jehovah God blessed for ever above all: We have the VICTORIOUS ACT OF BREAKING-THROUGH, especially in the life-giving Resurrection, by which he broke through death, hell, and the sepulcher, indeed the whole Diabolical army, he broke down the barriers and prisons of sin, death, Satan, and hell, all the bolts and gates, he destroyed all contrary force, since the Hebrew word implies breaking, breaking-through, and destruction. We have the TRIUMPHANT AND MOST JOYFUL CONSEQUENCE OF THE BREAKING-THROUGH, namely the Ascension into heaven, by which the Hero of dual substance, having been resurrected into life, celebrated a triumph over the conquered enemies, and led captivity captive, occupying the heavenly kingdom, and ascending the throne of majesty. But we also have the ABUNDANT AND MOST WHOLESOME FRUIT OF THE BREAKING-THROUGH AND ASCENSION. Because he broke through not for himself, but for us, he ascended not for his own sake, but for ours, that he might gather all Jacob, i.e., not the Jews only, but the universal Church, since the Gentiles also are to be called, and belong to all Jacob; therefore he would gather the universal Church, but in particular (which is added for the sake of consolation) the remnant of Israel: for a seed was to be left, Isa. I. 9. And Jesus had to die not only for the nation, but that he might gather together in one the children of GOD who were scattered, Joh. XI. 52. He was sent to the sheep which were lost of the house of Israel, Matth. XV. 24. Thus our oracle agrees with the prophecy of Hosea, chap. II. 11. And the children of Judah shall be gathered together, and the children of Israel together, and they shall appoint themselves ONE HEAD: which does not agree with a bodily reduction of the Jews and Israelites, since the Israelites were not gathered with the children of Judah, but rather remained in the Assyrian captivity: or with a spiritual congregation, namely to the kingdom of Christ: concerning which Hos. III. 5. Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the LORD their GOD and David their King, i.e., the Messiah sprung from the lineage of David. Conf. Jerem. XXIII. 6. Ezech. XXXIV. 23. But they are to be gathered into one flock; into the fold of Christ, as a flock in the midst of the pens, by which security is indicated, that they, having been snatched from the jaws of wolves and infernal lions, are to be placed in safety, about to be tumultuous because of the multitude, which is to be such and so great, that it will have the appearance of a tumult in the world, since the world knows not how to endure the pursuits and actions of the faithful, which are approved by GOD. Just as it is evident concerning the Apostles, that they were accused of causing disturbances, as if they had turned the world itself upside down Acts XVII. 6. Concerning the gathering of the sheep, Christ himself has testified, John X. 16. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one Shepherd. Therefore in the ascension that BREAKER opens the way before them, so that they may enter both into the fold of the Church and into the heavenly fold. Therefore the faithful themselves also SHALL BREAK THROUGH, and shall walk through the gate: They shall break through from narrow things to august things, through many tribulations into the kingdom of God Acts XIV. 22. because through a thousand dangers of things as B. Luther has it, one must break through. And this is what is added; And their King shall go before them. Our breaker is our predecessor. I will send before, says the Lord, with B. Luther as interpreter, the breaker Christ, who will break through, and will take away every stumbling block, he will prepare for you the way, with the power of Satan and death broken, so that the passage may be easy afterwards, being helped by my spirit. AND JEHOVAH SHALL BE THEIR HEAD. Head not only by reason of ὁμοεσίας, (but how great is this, that Jehovah should be ὁμοεσιος to us, that that Shepherd should be of the same substance with the sheep!) But also by reason of vigor and power, by reason of communication of virtue and efficacy, by reason of superiority and eminence, by reason of perfection and excellence.

Therefore it is our duty to exult in this Breaker with true faith and due proclamation, especially in this festival, nay, in the whole time of our life: because he broke through for our good; To follow the same religiously, because he is our Shepherd and Predecessor, John X. 4. To serve him, as Lord, in Spirit and in truth. To venerate him as King with fear and trembling. Finally, to submit ourselves humbly to him as our head, and to commit ourselves entirely and devoutly. Christ broke the power of the enemies, and grants us also the powers of breaking through: let us therefore rejoice and sing, with Habakkuk ch. III. 19. The Lord God is my strength, and he will set my feet like hinds' feet and will lead me upon my high places, singing as a victor in the Psalms: Let us break through, helped by his virtue, the wild beasts of the flesh and the world, and let us break the chains and ropes of evil passions, by which we are still bound, nor let us again close to ourselves the heaven opened by the Breaker, by our wickednesses and sins. Let us be mindful of the sentence of Christ Matt. XI. 12. The kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force. If sins, if other difficulties seem to exclude us from the kingdom of heaven, let us break through these obstacles, and with true repentance and faith in Christ let us break into heaven, so that we may enjoy blessed tranquility in that heavenly fold. Christ is risen from the dead, exclaims Gregory the Theologian (Orat. XLII.) rise together: Christ is from the sepulcher, be loosed from the bonds of sin. The gates of hell are opened, and death is oppressed, and the old Adam is put off, and the new is perfected, if there is any new creature in Christ, be renewed. That this may be done, there is the greatest need for pious frequenting of temples, devout meditation on the word, and holy celebration and invocation of our BREAKER: nor will you cease to testify a grateful mind to the heralds of the word by depositing gifts at the altar. Now the God of peace who brought again from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep, fit us in every good thing, that we may do his will, doing in us that which is pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom is glory for ever and ever, Amen. Given on the eve of Easter in the Year of the Lord 1671.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ASCENDET ENIM PANDENS ITER ANTE EOS] Ascendet effractor coram eis, miles oppugnans urbes illas.

DIVIDENT ET TRANSIBUNT PORTAM, ET INGREDIUNTVR PER EAM] Perfringent Assyrii & Chaldæi mœnia, & transibunt per portam, per quam exire solebant urbani 2. Reg. XVII. 6. XXV. v. 4.

ET TRANSIBIT REX EORUM CORAM EIS] Inspectante populo trahetur captivus. 2. Reg. XVII. 6. XXV. 6.

ET DOMINVS IN CAPITE EORVM] Nempe Assyriorum & Chaldæorum. Deus illis omnia prospera- bit.

Depravationem illustris vaticinii Evangelici integram adscripsimus, in qua Grotius iterum Judæos sequutus est, imprimis Josephum Kimchium, relictis Christianis plerisque interpretibus. Hi enim vaticinium Propheticum de Christo intelligunt. Agnovit id Calvinus in h. l. Major pars interpp. huc inclinat, quod Deus hic promittat levationem aliquam Israelis, postquam duriter eos objurgaverat, & minatus etiam fuerat extrema. Referunt igitur hunc locum ad regnum Christi, q. Deus spem faciat restitutionis futuræ: sed discessit idem Calvinus etiam à majori Interpp. parte. Hunc ergo habuit prævium Grotius, ut & Tremellium ac Junium, Calvini discipulos. Sed nulla primum causa est deserendi plerorumque Interpretum consensum. Quod enim Calvinus urget, cætera quæ præcedunt esse meras ἐπιτιμήσεις, id proprius ejus hyperaspistes Dav. Pareus diluit. Non me impedir ratio, quod præcedentia omnia sint ἐπιτιμητικὰ. Neque enim est infrequens Prophetis ex abrupto comminationibus consolationes subjicere, & prædictiones futuræ vastitatis etiam de instauratione spirituali, & de regno Christi concionari. Exempla sunt Hos. III. & VI. & XIII. Joel. II. Am. V. & IX. Et convenit hæc consolatio probe illis quæ antecedunt: quia inter alia responderat Propheta, bonis bona esse verba Dei. Postquam ergo Impœnitentibus annunciavit fatum suum, accedit ad erigendos animos piorum, quibus testatur in mediis etiam cladibus publicis promissiones divinas præsertim spirituales impletum iri. De quo etiam B. Lutherus h. l. Hic prophetarum mos est, postquam impios secure peccantes castigarunt, ac prædixerunt futuram vastitatem, tandem etiam de regno Christi æterno concionantur, idque propter pios, non solum ut hoc modo eos consolentur, sed etiam ut spem augeant, ne metu corporalium incommodorum de regno CHRISTI desperent. Similiter B. Höpfnerus in Comment. ἀνεκδότῳ: ut impœnitentibus antea concionatus est Propheta, ita nunc ob piorum & pœnitentium, quibus verba DEI bona esse vers. 7. dixerat, consolationem promittit, quod licet terreno regno orbentur, nihilominus tamen spiritualis regni Messiæ cives sint futuri, idque confirmat ab insigni documento Ecclesiæ in N. T. ex Judæis & gentibus catervatim colligendæ. Congregando congregabo id est, omnino vel certo congregabo. Deinde verba congregatione congregabo Iacob totum te, consolationem utique, non comminationem fa- piunt, verba sunt suavia de congregatione Jacobi, non vero tristia. Quod agnoscit Coccejus. Calvini discipulus. Nunquam congregare reliquias extra benedictionis & gratiæ significationem ponitur Es. X. 20. 21. 22. Mich. IV. 6. c. V. 6. 7. Jes. XXIII. 3. De- ductio in exsilium vocatur, & projectio, non congrega- tio. TOTUM JACOB ET RELIQUIAS IS- RAELIS.

Videntur hæc secum pugnare. Si enim to- tus Jacob colligendus est non tantum reliquiæ colli- gentur! Distinguunt ergo reliqui inter vocatio- nem quæ totum Jacob spectet, & eventum, quod vocanti Deo obsequium præstent non omnes, sed reliquæ solum Israelis. Alii congregandum dicunt totum Iacob scilicet electum. Concinnior est eo- rum interpretatio, B. Höpfnero judice, qui propter gentium accessionem putant totum Iacob appellari, & qui secundum carnem sic dicuntur, & qui secundum promissionem seu Spiritum filii sunt Jacobi, quam- vis ex Ethnicis oriundi. Reliquias autem Israelis vo- cari posteros Israelitarum, qui ad Christum in N. T. sunt conversi, ut infra c. IV. 7. conf. Luc. I. 33. Vox אָסֹף quæ etiam c. IV. 6. occurrit, est colligere, & u- trobiq; per συνάγειν redditur, unde Christi ἐπι- συναγωγειν Matth. XXIII. 37. & vox συναγωγῆς pro Ecclesia Iac. II. 2. & ἐπισυναγωγῆς Ebr. X. 26 Verbum קָבֵץ est dispersos congregare, eosq; non sin- gulatim sed turmatim, ut numerus sere videatur intumescere seu turgescere, & ad augendum colle- ctionis hujus copiam adhibetur Piel q. d. frequen- ter colligam. Tertio simile ovilis congruit Ecclesiæ, quæ est ovile Domini. Et facere ovium similes, & qui- dem similes gregis in caula, non est compescere & concludere per obsidionem, vel deportare in ca- ptivitatem. Solum peregrinum desertum vocari solet, non caula, ut iterum Coccejus. Cæterum innuit Pro- pheta pari jure & dignitate futuros Iudæos & gentes in N. T. ubi Christus τὰ ἀμφότερα (ἔθνη) fecit u- num (ἕν i. e. unum populum) non quidem gen- tilem convertendo in Judaicum, ut volebant Ju- dæi tempore Pauli, neque Judaicum in gentilem, sed utrumque mutando in alium diversum, i. e. Christianum populum Eph. II. 14. adeoq; prædicit ἰσότιμον vocationem gentium ad Catholicam Ec- clesiam. בָּצְרָה proprie est metropolis Moabitarum (distincta à Bazra Edomitarum) à pascuis cele- brium, unde oves Bazra i. e. minime vulgares sed se- lectissimæ, delicatissimæ in oculis DEI, utpote Filii Dei sanguine redemptæ. Chald. & Lat. reddunt in ovili, quos sequitur Lutherus qui vertit in einem fe- sten Stall, cui translationi sequentia favent ceu ἐξήγησις priorum. Quamvis enim Bozra sit nomen proprium urbis, qui tamen urbs illa nomen habet à munitione, & celebris erat selectioribus ovibus, ideo appellative pro munitione proque septo, in quo oves coarctantur & muniuntur, sumi potest, ac subintelligi præpositio ב in LXX. ἐν θλίψει reddi- dere: quam versionem quia sequutus est Theodo- retus, mirum non est, quod de pœna totum hunc lo- cum acceperit: imperitiam autem suam prodit Ribera Jesuita, quod eam adhuc defendere cona- tur, unde enim sub præpositione ב Hateph-ka- metz? Vidit hæc Junius, hocque commento Aben- Ezræ, ut putat Tarnovius, quod suum hic etiam fe- cit Grotius, occurrere conatus est: Ludere Pro- phetam ex ambiguo in hoc versu, & ludificari Pseu- do-Prophetarum verba, qui promittebant magna & multa, quibus respondeat, recte dicit Deus congre- gabo Judam & Israelem, sed eo consilio, ut quam maximo numero abducantur in captivitatem, velut in alienam caulam. Verum μίμησις illa conficta est, neque phrasi scripturæ satis consentanea.

Non enim ita Pseudo-Prophetarum verba Pro- phetæ imitari consueverunt, ut phrasin Sp. S. plane negligant. At ubi terra peregrina vocatur caula, ubi vel conclusio in obsidione, vel deportatio in capti- vitatem congregatio in ovile? Quarto de toto Iacob & reliquiis Israel in unum congregandis sonat va- ticinium. At corporaliter in unum congregatæ nunquam sunt XII. tribus post abductionem in ca- ptivitatem; Per Iacobum enim decem tribus, per reliquias Israelis duas reliquas tribus intelligit Grotius. Jam quum illæ per Salmanaffarem, hæ per Nabuchodonosorem abductæ sint, quomodo in UNAM omnes CAULAM congregatæ? Quod adeo diserte hic Propheta exprimit, ut non tantum dicat, congregatione congregabo Iacob totum te, IN UNUM conducam reliquias Israel, sed addat decla- rationis gratia, pariter ponam illum, quasi gregem in ovili, ac denuo quasi pecus in medio caularum, ac po- stremo tumultuabuntur à multitudine hominum. Quam multitudinem detorquet Grotius ad ho- stes, sed contra textum: omnia enim illa loquun- tur congregationem universæ multitudinis Israe- lis, quam tantam Propheta futuram innuit, ut qua- si strepitum & sonitum effectura sit. Es werde doͤs nen und wimmeln von Leuten. Recte B. Luthe- rus hic: Ubi magna hominum frequentia est, ibi confusæ voces, tumultum quendam referunt. B. Höpf- nerus prius quidem non ad multitudinem, sed ad liberationis descriptionem refert. In posteriori tamen multitudinem depingi monet. QUASI PECUS IN MEDIO CAULARUM. Non indicatur, quod ita consertim congregandi sint, sed imprimis notatur hac similitudine liberatio ab exitio, quod ab inhiantibus lupis & leonibus infernalibus paratum est iis, qui Ecclesiæ non consociantur. De multitu- dine sequentia agunt. TUMULTUABUNTUR A MULTITUDINE HOMINUM. In Ebr. præ homine vel præ multitudine hominum. Non commotionem & convulsionem verbo tumultuan- di notat, sed maximam multitudinem & tantam quidem, quæ vel publici tumultus speciem apud impios præ se sit latura. Id quod impleri cœpit post ascensionem Domini, ut hinc sæpe Apostoli fuerint postulati turbarum, quibus orbem ter- rarum conturbaverint. Act. XVII. 19. Perti- net itaque hæc particula ad conversionem gentium, & ad ipsum ministerium verbi, quod ideo etiam tumultuantium vocibus comparatur, quia commo- vet mundum & mundus se ei opponit. Ut ita du- bium nullum sit de congregatione in unum cœ- tum sermonem esse. Quum ergo ejusmodi cor- poralis congregatio in unum cœtum nuspiam & nunquam facta sit, manifestum est, necessario hæc de spirituali congregatione intelligenda esse. Nec in obsidione cum X. tribubus duæ reliquæ in una civitate conclusæ fuere, neque post captivitatis Ba- bylonicæ solutionem revertentibus Judæis restitu- ti Israelitæ. Quod argumentum imprimis urget B. Lutherus. Si hunc locum cum prioribus conne- Etere, & de externa seu corporali restitutione po- puli intelligere velis, tota via aberraveris. Quan- do enim regnum Israel restitutum est, si autem non est restitutum, quid Propheta vult quod dicit resti- tuendum? Judæi quidem his promissionibus indu- cti, pertinaciter sperant liberationem corporalem, sed frustra. Non enim de corporali sed spirituali li- beratione loquitur Propheta, quæ fit per Evange- lium de Christo divulgatum in toto orbe terrarum. Ibi totus Jacob & reliquiæ Israel dispersæ sunt, qui per fidem Evangelium accipiunt, & credunt per Christum remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam. Hanc congregationem quia Judæi non intelligunt, fit, ut quando longius expectent & fpe- rent, tanto minus spei relinquatur. Sed inquies, Cur ista non clarius à Prophetis significata sunt? Respon- deo, Filius, qui in sinu Patris est, enarravit nobis. Fuerunt enim hæc involvenda, ut claritas Evangeli differret à claritate Legis, & eam vinceret. Chri- sti & Apostolorum conciones hæc mysteria omnia clarißime interpretantur. Hos cum Iudæi nolint a- gnoscere, merito in cæcitate ista horribili detinentur. Quod igitur ad verba Prophetæ attinet, diferte di- cit: Totum Jacob congregandum, & Israelis re- liquias colligendas. Sicut etiam promissio Abra- hæ universalis est: In te benedicentur omnes gen- tes. Hæc B. Lutherus, qui præclare etiam ibi- dem docet, quomodo hæ & similes promissiones universales veritatem suam obtineant. Hic in- cauti lectores iterum impingunt, & universales promissiones referunt ad eventum, qui maxime par- ticularis est. Neq; enim omnes credunt ideo, neq; salvantur omnes. Tenendum igitur discrimen est. Aliud enim est, benedicentur in te omnes gen- tes. Et aliud, omnes gentes promissionem hanc de benedictione accipient. Nam Evangelium offert quidem omnibus remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam per Christum, sed non omnes promissionem hanc Evangelii accipiunt. Ita in hoc loco dicit Propheta, universum te Jacob congregabo. Et tamen eventus docet, maximam partem populi Evangelio non credidisse, & ideo abjectam esse sicut Propheta idem ostendit, cum di- cit de reliquiis Israel. Cur igitur, inquies, senten- tiæ sic universales sunt? Ideo scilicet, ne quis se ab Evangelii promissione excludat. Christus enim non unius populi aut temporis thesaurus est: sed offertur per verbum omnibus, quod autem Christum non omnes accipiunt, ipsorum culpa fit: quod non cre- dunt, & indulgent incredulitati suæ. Interim ma- net sententia Dei & promissio universalis, quod Deus omnes homines vult salvos esse. Ad hunc modum Propheta quidem dicit, universum Jacob colligendum. Deus enim vult Christum esse com- munem thesaurum omnium, sicut dicit Christus: Ita dilexit Deus mundum, ut daret Filium suum, ut omnis qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Ecce colligendi studium, ut omnes colligat in unum ovile, ad unam gratiam per Chri- stum, sed huic voluntati Dei obsistunt increduli, cum verbo parere, & id accipere nolunt. Itaque tantum reliquiæ Israel colliguntur & salvantur. Quæ in gratiam Calvinianorum, novorum Prædestinatia- norum hic observanda duximus, nec non Rinte- lensium contrarium sensum Megalandro affingen- tium. De quo in Antapologia contra Rintelen- ses nomine Facultatis Theologicæ edita uberius dictum. Neque temere observat B. Lutherus verbum uniendi. Ideo, inquit, uniendi verbo uti- tur Propheta, quia Regnum Israel totum à regno Iu- da alienum erat. Hæ inimicitiæ, inquit, cessabunt, cum Evangelium divulgabitur. Erunt enim omnes sicut oves conclusæ in unum ovile, quæ simul pascen- tur sub eodem pastore. Urget etiam hoc argu- mentum B. Hopfnerus. Nam congregationem hanc non significari hic collectionem ad perden- dum probatur ex abolitione totius Iacob & reliquia- rum Israelis. Non enim Judæi, & Israelitæ simul fuerunt deportati, sed diversis temporibus: nec reli- quiæ tantum Israelis fuerunt extorres, sed omnes Is- raelitæ abducti sunt. Contra autem congregatio fi- liorum Juda & filiorum Israel sibi caput unum fide & confessione ponentium dicitur esse simultanea Of. 1. 11. & describitur adductio ne ad unum ovile per unum pastorem Joh. X. quare hoc in loco quoq; congregatio Iacob & Israelis simultanea de instaura- tione Ecclesiæ erit accipienda. Quod ipsum argu- mentum coëgit etiam Cornelium à Lapide, ut quam- vis hæc optime de reditu Judæorum è Babylone ac- cipi dixerit, manus tandem dederit nostræ inter- pretationi: Verum quia tunc soli Judæi, non Israe- litæ, nisi perpauci, rursum non omnes Judæi congre- gati sunt, nec redierunt, sed multi manserunt in Babylonè, & alii per varias regiones dispersi vagabun- tur: insuper quia Zorobabel non fuit Rex, hinc in- choata & imperfecta duntaxat fuit hæc Israelis libe- ratio & congregatio. Quocirca cogimur dicere, hæc plane & plene referenda esse ad Christum. Li- cet enim alludat ad Zorobabel & Judæos illius ævi, eosque obiter quasi perstringat, tamen mens & scopus Prophetæ ulterius porrigitur, altius assurgit, ac fertur in Christum, per quem hæc Prophetia perfecte imple- ta est. In Christum enim oracula sua terminare solent Prophetæ. Vocem שְׁאֵרִית sæpissime de electis qui- busdam reliquiis Judæorum usurpari fassus est ipse Tarnovius Am. V. 15. cap. IX. 12. Mich. V. 7. 8.

Quinto ascensus ille Happoretz vel perruptoris non potest de milite tum Assyrio, tum Chaldæo intel- ligi. De certo quodam individuo potius intelli- gendus est, qui per He Hajediah designatur, & de tali perruptore, qui iter pandere debeat ut & illi quibus panditur iter, perrumpant & ingrediantur per portam. Quod utique non convenit militi As- syrio aut Chaldaico. Glossa Grotii vim facit textui, dum alios, atque alios fingit transituros per por- tam, & egredientes per eam, illos Assyrios & Chaldæos, hos urbanos, quos è mera ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει ingerit. Ipsa phrasis & modus loquendi arguit de iisdem ser- monem esse, quod transituri & ingressuri sint per portam, ubi iter ipsis pandetur per ILLUM EF- FRACTOREM. Et quomodo in eodem perrum- pendi actu conjungi potest Assyrius Salmanasseris, & Chaldæus Nabuchodonosoris miles. Talia com- menta vix ulli præter Grotium in mentem vene- runt. Neque vero cum Calvino perruptor de Assyrio, & Babylonio Rege accipi potest. Ipse enim non ascendebat, & perrumpebat ante congregando, sed adversus eos, & dissipando. Contra autem phrasis (ante eos) notat priorem in perrumpendo, ut perru- ptorem sequuti sint illi, ante quos perruperit: un- de argumentum: ille hic est perruptor, qui habet sequentes in perruptione eos, ante quos perrum- pit. Sed Christus & non Assyrius & Babylonius Rex habet sequentes in perruptione eos, ante quos rumpit, nempe fideles, unde Col. 1. dicitur ἀρχὴ principium & primogenitus mortuorum, item πρόδρομος, & præcursor in aditu ad cœlum Ebr. VI. 20. E. Christus & non Assyrius aut Babylonius est per- ruptor ille. Addimus quæ habet B. Höpfnerus: In Ebræo est הַפֹּרֵץ perruptor ille, ac δεικτικῶς demon- stratur certum individuum, à פָּרַץ perrupit, destru- xit: Christus Redemtor qui plenaria satisfactione Deo Patri pro nobis præstita vim obicesque & cance- res Diaboli mortis & peccati perrupit ac destruxit, quam perruptionem sequitur ascensio, qua in vitam resuscitatus triumphum egit de Satana & hostibus suis & nostris atque in cœlum ascendit paraturus no- bis locum, juxta illud Eph. IV. captivam duxit ca- ptivitatem & cœlos nobis clausos penetravit Ebr. IV. 14. In hac autem perruptione & ascensione sua primatum obtinet, unde Propheta dicit: Ascendet perruptor ante eos, i. e. ipse in hac victoria de dia- bolo & morte reportata nobis non sibi profuit & fa- ctus est causa & autor liberationis & vivificationis o- mnium piorum, Col. 1, 18. Apoc. 1, 5. 1. Cor. XV. 10. Sequitur porro efficacia mortis & vitæ Christi, & communio ejusdem, quoad fideles, quam exprimit mentione tum perruptionis, qua pii per virtutem at- que efficaciam Christi capitis sui contendunt eluctari, atque eluctantur etiam, ex hostium omnium poten- tia & violenti rapiunt regnum cœlorum Luc. XIIII 24. tum transitus & egressus per portam, qui respon- det ascensioni, quam antea capiti tribuerat. Ideoque proponitur Christus ceu caput Ecclesiæ partim meri- to & efficacia qua perruptor est eo quo diximus mo- do; partim communicatione efficaciæ suæ, quam Ecclesiæ per commissuras & compages Spiritus & fidei adunitos distribuit. Consistit enim efficacia illa mortis quidem Christi in abolitione peccati & mortis, itemque legis quatenus maledicit & chiro- graphum est adversus nos, & vis peccati nos occiden- tis; Efficacia autem & vis vitæ Christi nobis com- municatæ pertinet ad nostri in Christo capite in cæle- stibus collocationem, quoad spiritum & resuscitatio- nem nostri ad vitam æternam atq; in cælestibus collo- cationem, quoad totum hominem, quæ proinde recte exprimitur tum per illam perruptionem tum per transitum & egressum per portam h. e. potentes diaboli viresque omnium hostium, maxima item discrimina, tandemque ipsam mortem. Sexto ne dubitarentus, quisnam Happoretz indigitetur an- te Israelitas ascensurus, ut illis iter pandat, & tran- situm patefaciat, subjicit Propheta, ET TRANSI- BIT REX EORUM CORAM EIS, vocans eun- dem Regem eorum, in quo facile consentiunt In- terpretes. At Grotius fingit, non de illo per- fractore, uti verborum συνέχεια postulat, sed de Rege tum Israelitico Hosea, tum Judæorum Ze- dekia hæc intelligenda esse. Denique quod Propheta de transitu ad Israelitas, ut iis iter pan- datur, habet, id Grotius ad Regis captivationem in conspectu Israelitarum trahit. Quod vere est dis- cerpere & torquere Scripturam.

Septimo adhuc dilucidius sese explicat Pro- pheta, cum illi prædictioni ET TRANSIBIT REX EORUM CORAM EIS, hanc κατ' ἐπε- ξήγησιν consuetam & valde solemnem Prophetis subjungit; ET DOMINUS IN CAPITE EO- RUM. Rex ergo ille coram eis transiturus, & perruptor ille est Jehovah Dominus, qui in capi- te eorum erit, vel qui ante ipsos transiturus in capite vel principiis : vel potius, quod Iehovah sit in capite, h. e. Dominus, Princeps, capitaneus, ut. Deut. XXVIII. 13. ponet te in caput, Psal. XIIX. 44. Constituisti me in caput gentium; nisi nomen capitis hic intelligendum potius sit, quatenus illud per commissuras & compages cum corpore, ac membris suis compactum consideratur, quod significantius h. l. censet B. Höpfnerus: quia ita Christus caput in scripturis dicitur, & sic omnes quatuor conditio- nes capitis hic includuntur, nempe (1) vigor(meri- tum), & efficacia. (2) Communicatio efficaciæ.(3)e- minentia.(4) perfectio.Septimo insequentes perru- ptorem, & egredientes per portam non possunt acci pi de militibus Assyriis & Babyloniis. Nam illi dicun- tur perrumpere, ante quos ascendit perruptor. Sed Jacob, & Israel congregandi in unum ovile sunt illi, ante quos ascendit perruptor. E. Jacob & Israel, & non milites Assyrii, & Babylonii dicuntur h. l. perrumpere. Adhæc perruptores dicuntur egredi per portam: hostes autem non egrediebantur, sed ingrediebantur medianam portam Jer. XXXIX. 3. Denique eorum, qui perrumpunt Rex dicitur præ- ire. Nam ipse Calvinus & Piscator Regem hunc prius transeuntem, non putant esse Regem ho- stium Chaldæorum sed Regem Judæorum Sede- chiam. Quomodo ergo illi, quorum Rex præcur- sor non est Assyrius vel Babylonius, erunt hostes Assyrii, vel Babylonii? Taceo quod Rex Iudaicus non transierit per portam, sed per muros.

Octavo esse in capite sive in caput notat con- junctionem cum aliquo & defensionem, non autem perditionem illius. Jam autem idem est in capi- te, qui hic Rex eorum dicitur, iturus ante eos. Et sequeretur Jehovam prius omnium fugisse, adeo- que dicendum esse, quod in captivitatem ductus sit, si transitus hic in quo Jehovah est in capite, esset de fuga accipiendus. Quod contra Calvinum & Piscatorem notandum, qui ita accipiunt; è qui- bus omnibus jam apertissimum est non de Rege Se- dekia, non de Zorobabele, sed de Christo Rege, qui est JEHOVAH vaticinium intelligendum esse, qui est Happoretz ille, cujus ASCENSUS PER- RUPTORIUS in cœlum viam nobis aperturus prædicitur de quo etiam gloriose vaticinatus est David Ps.LXIIX. cujus merito & virtute nos por- tam cœli penetramus. Unde probanda hic o- mnino Osiandrina paraphrasis: Ascendet perru- ptor ante eos: (i. e. Christus per passionem & mor- tem crucis atque per infernum victor perrumpet, atque ad cœlos ascendens sedebit ad dextram Pa- tris. Sic enim (inquit Christus) oportebat Chri- stum pati & ingredi in gloriam suam Luc. 24.) Et transibunt portam & egredientur per eam: Ebr.per- rumpent (ipsi quoque) & gradientur per portam (id est, patebit illis aditus in cœlum:) & ibit Rex eorum ante eos, & Dominus (Jehovah) in princi- pio eorum. (Id est, Rex Christus, qui hoc loco (sicut & alibi sæpe) Dominus seu Jehovah voca- ,,tur, in omnibus primatum tenebit: & patefa- ,,ciet omnibus in se credentibus aditum ad cœ- ,,lestem & æternam gloriam. Imo in hac etiam ,,vita, ipsos, tanquam Dux & Capitaneus, tuebi- ,,tur, ne pereant. Itaque & illi per afflictiones, ,,tentationes & mortem ad æternam felicitatem

,,perrumpent.) Pulchra sunt, quæ hic B. Lu- therus habet. Et hic locus mire elegans & plenissi- mus consolationis. Primum enim vocabulum dis- sipatoris continet significationem Crucis & obstacu- lorum, deinde etiam certæ liberationis q. d. Do ,,ovibus meis vitam æternam, & duco eas ad ,,vera pascua, sed hoc magno constat.
