Neque ,,enim trita aut expedita via est, multa obstant, ,,quæ electos morari conantur, nempe Satan, ,,mors, peccatum, Lex, quid multis? totus ,,vetus Adam obstat. Faxo autem, ut, etsi ob- ,,stacula sint, tamen vos non morentur. Præ- mittam Diruptorem Christum, qui perrumpet & ,,tollet omne offendiculum, is parabit vobis viam ,,fracta satanæ & mortis potentia, ut facilis po- ,,stea sit transitus adjutis spiritu meo. Dixi ,,verbum perrumpendi significare crucem, quod ,,per mille pericula rerum perrumpendum est. Quæ- ,,re cum constitvat Christum esse (Poretz) seu per- ,,ruptorem, ostendit eum esse verum hominem, ,,& luctari cum periculis tanquam hominem. Si- ,,cut testantur agoniæ illæ in morte & cruce. ,,Quia autem vincit in Periculis illis, & per eam ,,victoriam sibi parat populum & regnum. Ideo ,,dicitur Rex noster. Sed idem etiam hic ap- ,,pellatur (Jehovah) quod nomen soli DEO tri- ,,buitur. Itaque hoc testimonium observent ,,sacrarum rerum studiosi, quo CHRISTI ,,divinitas certo affirmatur. In notis mar- ginalib. ita habet Megalander: Hie redet er von dem Reich CHRISTI, der ist unser Held, der vor uns hindurch gebrochen hat, und die Bahn macht durch Sünd, Tod, Teuffel, und alles Vbel, dem frisch nach! B. Lutherum sequuntur nostrates omnes, si forte unum B. Tarnovium excipias, qui cætera do- ctissimus interpres à Junio se hic & in aliis quibus- dam ad alia abripi passus est, qui vero non præfra- cte suam sententiam tuetur, quin paratum se testa- tus est argumentis cedere, ac tanti fecit B. Lutheri & orthodoxorum sententiam, ut eandem suis ver- bis non ineleganter proposuerit: at lectori arbi- trium permiserit. Sic enim habet in Commentar. in hunc Prophetam p. 65. Veruntamen, ut tanto "melius possit de singulis fieri judicium, etiam "vulgatam hujus loci explicationem ex præcipuis "quibusque interpretibus breviter collectam hic "proponere erit operæ pretium. Sic autem ha- "bet, quod Propheta jam in versu 12. à malis ad bo- "nos se convertat, & à regno corporali, quod de- "stitutum & destructum iri ait, ad spirituale, quod "restitutum iri promittit, dum hoc dicto pronun- "ciatur gloriosa Christi resurrectio cum fructu "ejus, quoniam effractor ille Christus sit perrum- "pens per passionem, mortem, infernum, sepul- "chrum, & cælos, atque ita impetrans, ut sui si- "mul cum ipso duce perrumpant, ad quod eos ita "animet: Omnino recipiam, te Jacob totum, cum cæ- teros impios, de quibus hactenus, puniam vox, qui Ja- cobi fidem imitamini, omnes recipiam in meam fidem & clientelam, omnino congregabo reliquias Israelis Joh. XI. 52. & simul disponam eum cum gentibus vo- catus Joh. X. 19. Eph. II. 12. 14. in unum ovile, quod est Ecclesia, & tuebor eos, ut oves Botzrœ eorum Pastor, & multos advocabo, ut velut grex magnus in medio o- vilis sui perstrepant præ multitudine hominum, neq; à Lupis aut canibus, hoc est, Diabolis & Pseudo- Prophetis, timebunt, ne decipiantur aut deglutian- tur, cum nemo eas possit è manu mea rapere Iob. X. 28. quamdiu manent in me, & si quæ alia fuerint obsta- cula, quo minus in offenso pede possint ad cælestem caulam pergere, ea ego removebo feliciter, ascendet enim hic effractor θεανθρωπος Leo de tribu Iuda A- poc. V. 5. in conspectu eorum, quem ducem suum se- quentes pii perrumpent, transeuntes portam, quam egrediuntur & ingrediuntur, quomodo βιασται ap- pellantur Matth. XI. 12. transique Rex eorum Chri- stus ante ipsos, & Iehovah Deus ille genitus erit in ca- put eorum Eph. I. 22. & IV. 15. Col. I. 18. Quan- quam vero ob rationes nonnullas Junianam in- terpretationem præferat, illas tamen candido συν- θεολογούντων, atque ad Scripturæ normam singula exigentium subjecit judicio. Quæ vero ejus non fuut momenti, ut à recepta sententia discedendum sit. Quod à præcedentibus comminationibus petitur, ei nervum incidit ipse Pareus, & fatetur B. Tarnovius, sæpe propter pias populi reliquias, mi- nis subjici immediate consolationes, etsi neget hujus rei hoc loco indicium haberi: quod vero non deesse argumenta nostra docuere.

Quamvis vero urgeat vocem פרץ Christo non convenire, neque pios portam cælorum vi perrum- pere, nec ex ea egredi, neq; Iehovam dici לראשם sed בראשם in capite eorum, ea tamen omnia ἐυδιά- λυτα videntur. Nam פרץ perruptorem significat. Annon autem perrupit & penetravit cælos Christus in ascensione? Ebr. IV. 14. Tum si attendenda vis & violentia adhibita, quemadmo- dum de irruptione violenta & potenti inimicorum hoc verbum adhibetur 2. Sam. V. 20. perrupit utique Christus vi hostes spirituales, ascensurus in cælum, quam emphasin supra observavit B. Lutherus in Comment. ad h. l. Notatur enim Christum Iehovam perrupturum per passionem, mor- teim, infernum, sepulchrum & cælos, & impetratu- rum fidelibus, ut virtute resurrectionis suæ perrumpant & ipsi Domino præeunte illos, ipsis vero vestigia sui præcursoris atq́; Ducis per mortem & sepulcrum in vitam æternam usq́; sequentibus, uti recte B. Ægid. Hunnius in Anti-Pareo pag. 270. De piis observavit B. Lutherus: Cæterum hæc via car- ni asperrima videtur. Ideo Christus in Evangelio de regno Dei dicit, quod βιαζεται, id est, violenti ra- pient illud. Sicut Propheta hic dicit (parezu) per- rumpent ipsi quoque virtute Ducis sui. Oportet enim carnem mortificari, & se opponere toti mundo, & Satanæ, conanti nos impedire & morari, ne hunc Dissipatorem sequamur. Sed consolatur nos in his difficultatibus Christus, dicens: Confidite, ego vici mundum, hoc est, ego perrupi. Vos etiam me duce perrumpetis ad regnum Dei, ut illud vo- bis pateat. Neque repugnat verbum egrediendi. Nam egrediuntur pii ex hoc mundo per hanc portam, quam aperuit Christus. Notatur ergo tum terminus à quo, tum terminus ad quem, porta cœli, quam penetrant & transeunt, imo perrum- punt egredientes ex hoc mundo, imo etiam è vinculis & potestate Satanæ, peccati, mortis, & in- ferni. Adde, quod in textu Ebræo non fiat men- tio ingressus & egressus, sed transitus per portam, & egressus, ubi per portam intelligunt nonnulli, et- iam B. Höpfnerus in commentar. ἀνεκδότω poten- tiam Diaboli Matth. XVI. 17. ut &, maxima discri- mina, ac fluctus decumanos calamitatum, nec non ipsam mortem temporalem: quia discrimina maxi- ma vocantur portæ mortis Pf. IX. 15. deque ipsa morte Pf. CVII. 18. Iob. XXXIIX. 17. portæ mortis dicuntur, ut sensus sit, evasuros pios liberos à vincu- lis & carcere Diaboli, à dominio & servitio pecca- ti, à legis maledictione, deniq́; nullis periculis frangen- dos, nec in morte mansuros, sed ad vitam redituros. Verbum יצא est exivit, non vero ingressus est, ut vulg. reddidit: juxta quam intelligi potest per portam, aditus ad Ecclesiam (per verbi & Sacramen- torum usum) qui Pf. CXIIX. 19. dicitur porta justi- tiæ & porta Domini: nec non aditus ad gloriam & vitam æternam, qui Matth. VII. 14. Luc. XIII. 24. dicitur angusta porta, ad quam introgrediendam jubemur ἀγωνίζεσθαι contendere, & vi quadam ir- rumpere. Luther. Zum Thor aus und einziehen. id est, perrumpent portas inferorum, & ingredientur per portas justitiæ, ac vitæ æternæ. Habere autem Messiam dicuntur pii בראשם in capite vel princi- pio, quia ipse prior penetravit cœlos, quem tamen habent etiam pro capite, quia dicitur Rex eorum, qui ante ipsos est. Quo de iterum B. Höpfnerum producimus: ET TRANSIBIT REX EO- RUM CORAM EIS, ET DOMINUS IN CAPITE EORUM. Additur quomodo Chri- stus etiam caput: sit dominio sive eminentia. Quemadmodum enim in corpore humano caput emi- net, & loco est superiore, quam membra cætera illi subjecta: Ita Christus est supra omnia id est, supra omnes creaturas, atque ita etiam supra Ecclesiam & quidem constitutus est caput supra omnia ipsi Ecclesiæ Eph. I. 21. i. e. universorum gubernationem ad salutem Ecclesiæ attemperat, & præ aliis creatu- ris omnibus singulari amore fertur erga illam & speciali quadam ratione curat & gubernat. Nam licet omnes creaturæ pedibus Christi subjectæ Ephes. Eph. I. 22. & caput ipse etiam Angelorum dicatur Col. II. 10. tamen caput omnium est tantum ratione Creationis & domini: Credentes autem ita subsunt Christi pedibus, ut simul etiam sint pedes, manus ac membra Christi. Atq́; hoc respectu Christus dicitur rex, cum asignata hac muneris sanctione quod transeat ante faciem eorum, i. e. ante eos sc. sibi fide unitos:

quod exponi potest tum de primis insigniis victoriæ, quam Christus jam ante reportavit ab hostibus no- stris, Joh. XVI. 33. tum de assertione suorum adversus hostes & perditione hostium. Transire enim ante aliquem est præire, præcedere, uti Exod. XVII. 5. Moses jubetur transire ante populum i. e. præire, & 1. Sam. IX. 27. Dic puero ut transeat ante nos i. e. præcedat. Præire itaque hic erit vel primas tenere in dominio, vel educere, consu- lere, opitulari, & contra hostes defendere, uti Deut. IX. 3. Deus dicitur transire ante Israelitas, i. e. præ- cedere hostes ipsorum profugaturus. Huic formulæ æquipollent illæ, quando præcedere populum dicitur Deut. I. 33. c. IV. 37. & angelus Domini Exod. XIV. 19. c. XXIII. 20. c. XXXII. 34. Denique subjun- gitur quomodo Christus etiam caput Ecclesiæ sit per- fectione. JEHOVAH ERIT IN CAPUT EORUM. Non enim Christus tantum est homo, & nobis ὁμούσιος, ut possit nos tanquam carnem suam amare, Eph. V. 25. & nobis compati Ebr. IV. 15. sed etiam est JEHOVAH, qui omnia mala nostra sentit, omnia videt, quæ nobis eveniunt, au- dit nos, loquitur pro nobis & interpellat apud DEUM Patrem. Hic ergo Jehovah simul & homo est in ca- put Ecclesiæ datus. Quod si juxta alios verbum בראשׁ libeat interpretari in capite, tum erit ἐξήγησις præcedentis membri. Sed nomen capitis, quatenus illud per commissuras, & compages cum corpo- re, ac membris suis compactum consideratur, si gnificantius est, & hoc modo omnes quatuor condi- tiones capitis includit : nempe 1. Vigorem & effica- ciam. 2. Communicationem efficaciæ. 3 Emi- nentiam: & 4. perfectionem. Quo digitum quo- que intendit Oseas cap. 1, 11. Congregabuntur filii Iuda, & filii Israël simul, & ponent sibi caput u- num; uti hæc omnia præclare exequutus est. B. Höpfnerus. Nec denique obstat, quod hoc va- ticinium non sit allegatum in N. T. Nam multa alia extant vaticinia in V. T. quæ non citantur in N. T. διαῤῥήδην, quæ tamen indubio de Christo sonant. Et sufficit, quod omnia hoc vaticinio contenta lucem accipiant à N. T. eique ex asse consonent.

Quod agnovere etiam in ipsa Calvini Scho- la non infimi commatis Doctores, qui proinde Calvinum suum hic deserwere. Ita Hier. Zanch. in Comment. in h. l. introducitur Iehova, qui pro- mittit se collecturum populum ex omnibus gentium terris, in quibus erant dispersi Israelitæ. Hæc au- tem decem tribuum collectio non erat futura, nisi per Christum: quum vi suæ mortis, per prædicationem Apostolorum, collegit omnes Dei filios, qui erant dis- persi, ut Iohannes declaravit. Verba Iehovæ hæc sunt: Congregando congregabo te totum &c. per eam transibit Rex eorum ante eos, & Jehova in ca- pite eorum. Hic autem est Christus. Nam pro- mittit se collecturum totum Jacob id est, omnes ele- ctos. Isto in tumultu, promittit victoriam per Chri- stum. Ideo ait : Ascendet effractor ante ipsos : Hic est Christus. Dicitur enim effractor, quia sua poten- tia effregit portas inferorum: evicit Diabolum, & eo invito suos eduxit captivos, & in libertatem asseruit, & quotidie asserit. Annon hic titulus maxime convenit Christo? Ad extremum, ait, Et Jehova erit in caput eorum, hoc est, erit caput Ecclesiæ. Quis autem est caput Ecclesiæ nisi Christus? Non ignora- vit certe hoc Propheta. Novit igitur & ipse Christum esse verum Jehovam. Ita Rudolphus Gualtherus :

Primo restitutionem in genere pollicetur, cum ait: „Congregans congregabo te Jacob totum; con- „gregandi vocabulo liberationem & restitutionem „intelligit, qui hoc opponit dissipationi seu dispersio- „ni totius gentis, quæ per Assyrios facta fuerat: ut

„ostendat, eam non obstituram, quo minus consti- „tuto tempore sub Messia colligantur. Ubi tamen „observamus, de spirituali congregatione loqui Pro- „phetam, quæ animarum est, quando illi per fidem „uniuntur, ut in corpus unum in spiritu coalescant. „Nec enim ab illo tempore omnes Israelitæ in u- „nam aliquam regionem collecti sunt, neque illud „unquam futurum esse ullis prophetarum oraculis „edocemur. Fuit autem illa Israeliticæ gentis dis- „persio typus humani generis, quod priusquam „Christus in mundum veniret, in varias sectas & „peccati studia fœdissime dissipatum fuisse scimus. „Ut autem non obstitit captivitas vel Assyriaca vel „Babylonica, quo minus per Cyrum liberarentur, „quos Deus in patrias sedes redire voluit, ita nec „fœda illa & miserabilis omnium gentium sub po- „testate tenebrarum dispersio obstare potuit, quo „minus Dei filius Jesus Christus, omnes Dei filios „(ut Johannes ait) in unum colligeret. Huc facit, „quod paulo post sequitur: Simul ponam eos, tan- „quam oves Bozra sicut gregem in medio ovilis „sui. En unius modo gregis me, minit, non multorum, „& unius modo ovilis,in quod totum hunc gregem col- „ligi oporteat, & Prophetæ verbis Christus consentit, „quando Joh. X. ait: Fiet unum ovile & unus pa- „stor. Confert autem ovibus Bozra ut gregem hunc „pretiosum, & non vulgarem fore ostendat. Fuit „enim Bozra Idumææ regio, pascuis pinguibus ab- „undans, & proinde pecore delicatissimo celebris. „Et sane non potest non delicatissima Deo censeri „Ecclesia, quam (ut Propheta ait) oculi sui pupilla „chariorem habet, & filii sui sanguine redemptam „voluit Zach. II. Act. XX. Porro autem quosnam „ita congregari oporteat, docet. Et primo quidem „totum Jacobum nominat, mox vero expositionem „addit: Colligens colligam reliquias Israel. Sunt qui „Jacobi nomine tribum Juda denotari putent, quæ „tota ex Babylone reditura sit, una cum aliquot „Israelitarum reliquiis, qui se illi sint conjuncturi. „Quorum sententiam nec ego improbo, si nudam „reditus ex Babylone historiam spectemus. Quia ta- „men constat, Prophetam altius quid spectare, & „de regno Christi vaticinium contexere, ego reli- „quiarum mentionem ideo fieri arbitror, ut quod „in genere omnibus promisisse videbatur ad ele- „ctos restringat. Convenit hoc cum aliorum Pro- „phetarum oraculis, quos idem facere scimus. Isai- „as certe ait: Si fuerit ô Israel populus tuus ut are- „na maris, reliquiæ salvæ erunt. Joel item: In mon- „te Zion & in Jerusalem erit salvatio sicut dicit Do- „minus, idq; in reliquiis quas Dominus vocat. Et „rursum Isaias Ezechiam consolaturus, cum urbi im- „mineret Sennaherib, inter alia dicit. Quia prodibunt „reliquiæ de Jerusalem, & servati de monte Zion. „Tertio Ecclesiæ sive piorum sub Christo condi- „tionem describit, ubi multa dicuntur, quæ nostræ „consolationi serviunt. Primum. Tumultuabuntur „præ hominibus. Quo verbo concursum innuit, „qui ad reliquias illas Ecclesiæ seminarium, tantus „futurus sit, ut tumultus publici speciem præ se fe- „rat. Cœpit hoc impleri Apostolorum tempo- „re, quando mirifica facta fuit totius orbis muta- „tio, & ubique locorum electi, posthabitis vel „Judæorum ceremoniis, vel gentium supersti- „tionibus, ad Christi fidem, & Ecclesiæ ejus so- „cietatem concesserunt, & quidem tanto fervore, „ut impiis tumultuari, & aliquid seditiosi movere „viderentur. Facit enim huc, quod non semel A- „postolis hoc criminis loco objectum fuisse sci- „mus, quod orbem totum conturbaverint. Et „hodie videmus sicubi evangelii lux accenditur, „multos incredibili Zelo illam amplecti, adeoq; tu- „multuari, ut excussis tenebris in illa ambulare

„possint. Est hic sanctus ille tumultus, qui interim „Resp.& leges civiles minime turbat,utut hoc fieri „videatur impiis,qui ista occasione Evangelii do- „ctrinam seditionis causam esse clamant. Deinde, „Ascendet (inquit) effractor ante eos: Effractorem „vel perruptorem vocat Christum, ut illius in- „victam potentiam exprimat, qua & suos asse- „rit, & Ecclesiam suam congregat. Est enim for- „tissimus ille heros, qui in domum Diaboli irru- „pit,illum reluctantem vicit & strinxit,& illius va- „sa diripuit, in libertatem nimirum assertis homi- „nibus, quos ille sua tyrannide premebat. Idem „ille interstitium maceriæ (ut Apostoli verbis u- „tar) diruit, quæ nos à DEI regno arcebat. Ad- „hæc Diaboli regnum & illius opera in universum „destruxit, & regnum suum per orbem totum „propagavit, submotis & effractis obstaculis o- „mnibus, quæ mundi principes,simul & falsæ do- „ctrinæ antistites, & impostores objiciebant. Et „de hoc nos præmoneri oportuit, ne opus hoc „humanum fuisse putaremus, sed ut divina virtu- „te hæc omnia confecta sciremus. Addit tamen „his: Et effringent & transibunt portam, & egredien- „tur per ipsam. De reliquiis Iudæorum loquitur, in „quibus primatum facile tenuerunt Apostoli, de „quorum functione Apostolica locus iste exponi- „tur. Etsi enim Christus revera effractor ille sit, „qui adversariam potestatem destruxit, idem ta- „men pro singulari sua gratia, hominum quoque „ministerio uti dignatus est. Et constat Apostolos „admirabili alacritate & successu perrupisse omnia „ea,quæ regni DEI instaurationem impediebant. „At quod de illis dicitur, non minus ad omnes „credentes referri debet. Hactenus etiam Gual- „therus.

unus Pastor, & unum ovile. Simul ponam.) Ad-, „unavit populum suum in unam Ecclesiam, quia, „una fides,unus Dominus, unum Baptisma. Non,, loco quidem, ut necesse sit in Palestinam ire, sed,, concordia animorum, & pari dignitate, quæ est in Christo. Quin etiam qui olim lupi erant, hi con- vertendi sunt in agnos, ut simul possint cum a- liis inhabitare. Conferendus hic & Conr. Pelica- nus, qui etsi ultimos versus etiam posse de pœna nolentium audire Prophetas intelligi putet,tamen sententiam cum nostra per omnia consentientem indicavit, & tradidit, sed & Calvini hyperaspistes Pareus ejusmodi interpretationem retinuit in suis notis Biblicis, & in defensione Calvini contra B. Hunnium. Ego, inquit, de Christo locum libenter accipio. Quamvis etiam aliam Calvini simul tue- ri cupiat: sed inepte. Quia tantum est duarum istarum interpretationum divortium (monente B. Hunnio) ut stante una ruat altera, cum impossibile sit,iisdem plane verbis & comminationes pœnarum, & promissiones spiritualium beneficiorum comprehen- di,impossibile quoque sit, perruptoris voce simul Deum intelligi & Babylonium, vel regis nomine pariter no- tari Christum, & Regem Zedekiam.

Sed ante Gualtherum atque Zanchium, Oeco- lampadius Calvini præceptor simili exposuit mo- do: Congregando congregabo. In hoc licet videre „regnum Christi, quoties Ecclesiæ nobis vocatio „prædicitur. Quia igitur totus Jacob revocan- „dus est, prophetia ista non poterit spectare ad eos, „qui ex captivitate Babylonica egressi sunt ad Hie- „rusalem. Mittente illos Cyro, tunc decem „tribus relictæ sunt in captivitate in Assyria, imo „& tunc quando ex Babylonia redierunt, perpe- „tuo fuerunt adflicti, & sere nihil quietis habue- „runt. Unde hic non promittitur reditus è Ba- „bylone, sed potius libertas ista, quæ nobis per „Christum parta est, & filiorum DEI, qui dispersi „erant, in unum congregatio. Christus ubi ex- „altatus fuerat, traxit ad se omnia. Scio Iudæi- „zantes huc respicere, sub finem temporum Judæ- „os vocandos ad fidem, jungendosque Ecclesiæ „DEI: quibus non ausim accedere. Videant ex „Hosea non paucas scripturas, quæ manifeste in- „dicant Ecclesiam collectam, & qui ex Judæis re- „cipi digni receptos esse. Quamvis non inficias „iverim,etiam quotidie quosdam vocari ad fidem, „sed vocantur hodie ut cæteræ gentes. (Reliquias) „Utique de isto Jacob loquitur qui fidem Jacob „imitatur, sicut veri filii Abrahæ sunt, qui fi- „dem Abrahæ sequuntur, ita veræ reliquiæ Israel. „Principio totum Jacob ponit, tandem subdit re- „liquiæ. Peribit magna pars propter suam im- „pietatem. Petrus una concione tria millia addu- „xit, deinde altera quinque millia, & cæteri „multa millia ad fidem converterunt. Nihilo- „minus interim ad reliquias Israel & Jacob con- „jungere possumus eos, qui ex gentibus ad fi- „dem Christi accedunt. Nam manifeste hic ha. bemus, ut Ioannis X. quomodo Christus pastor no- ster sit, qui ex alio ovili collecturus sibi gregem, ut sit

Relinquunt etiam Calvinum Pampbrasta& Bel- gici, nostramque amplectuntur explicationem. Denique Iob. Coccejus (ut alios adducere superse- deam) graviter redarguit Iunium & Grotium, quod hic maluerint Judæos sequi: imo observat, antiquos Iudæos etiam à nostra parte stare. Non con- venit Zedekiæ eruptio v. 13. Nam dicitur ascensurus effractor ante ipsos Israelitas. Ergo nec Assyrius nec Babylonius intelligi potest. Et statim, quum dicitur Rex illorum,quorum Rex intelligi potest, ni- si ante quos ascenderit effractor? Rursus, in quorum principiis erit Dominus,nisi illorum, quorum Rex ante ipsos pertransire dicitur? Et porro: Profecto hac contorsione Judæi quidem illustrem prophetiam de adventu Christi & tempore adventus ejus obscura- re conantur. Qua in re ne omnes quidem suos con- sentientes habent. Nam Chaldæus, Antiqui, (te- ste Kimchio) & R. Solomo intelligunt esse promif- sionem: R. David dubitat. Illos corrumpentes tex- tum non decebat ut nostri sequeretur, imprimis Gro- tius: postquam Belgica editio, Iunio deferto, me- liorem explicationem dedit. Item: Iunius partim Abenefræ, partim Iosephi Kimchii corruptionem se- quitur, dum vult esse communicationem in allusione ad promissionem Pseudo-Prophetarum. Sed res e- videns est, ordo conveniens Prophetiarum πα- ραλληλία astipulans, & phrasis sua emphasi, id, quod diximus importans. Assentiuntur Chal- dæus & veteres Hebræi, & initium hujus periochæ cum ejus fine optime congruit. Dominus excitatus est de loco suo & descendet,& calcabit arces terræ. Et transit, pergit semper magis magisque Rex ipsorum ante ipsos, imo Jehova est in initiis ipso- rum,nimirum,ut perrumpat,& calcet arces terræ. Hieronymus,quanquam,ut ipse fatetur,cum magnis difficultatibus in toto initio Michææ luctatus: ta- men non alium Regem Ecclesiæ præcedentem agnovit, præterquam Christum. Porro qualis sit illa eruptio cap. IV. initio explicatur, ut de rege cap. IV. 14. & cap. V. 1. & c. Hactenus Coccejus. Hieronymi sententiam adjicimus: Ingressi sunt,inquit,quia & Rex eorum eandem ingressus est portam, & appe- ruit eis iter, ut absq; ulla difficultate graderentur. Ipse enim Dominus, & rex & pastor, & via est & porta, dicitque: Ego sum porta,per me qui fuerit ingressus, salvabitur: ingredietur,& egredietur,& pascua in- veniet. De qua porta & alibi prophetatur: Hæc est porta Domini, justi intrabunt per eam. Et postmo- dum: Et transierunt portam & egressi sunt per eam: qui tamen transitus & egressio absque Christo Rege nostro tribui non potest, qui Rex & Dominus est. Statim enim connectitur: Dominus autem prin- ceps erit. Denique ex ipsis Ebræis etiam non- nullos huic veritati calculum adjicere, hæc confir- mant, quod nempe in Bereschith Rabba R. Mo- ses Hadarschan super Gen. XL. ita legatur: Plan- tatio ab infra Abraham est: plantatio de supra est Messias, sicut dictum est Mich. II. 13. Ascendit irrumpens aditum ante eos &c. Et super illud Gen. XLIV. 18. Et appropinquavit ad illum Ju- da. Hoc est, quod scriptum est Cant. I. 4. Exsul- tabimus & lætabimur in te, quando nos gaude- bimus, quando stabunt pedes divinitatis in monte Olivarum, qui est coram Jerusalem ad Orientem. Aliter: lætabimur, & exultabimus in te: Quan- do? quando ascendent captivi ex inferno, & Dei- tas in capite eorum. Sicut dictum est Mich. II. 13. Et transibit Rex eorum ante eos, & Dominus à capite illorum. Egimus de hoc oraculo in Pro- grammate Paschali Anni 1671. nomine Rectoris Magnifici Dn. D. JOH. DEUTSCHMANNI, Profess. Theolog. publice proposito, quod hic solum subjungimus, ut illustre vaticinium eo re- ctius vindicetur. Sic autem habet αὐτολεξεὶ:

Psallite DEO nostro, psallite; Psallite Regi no- stro, Psallite. Quoniam Rex omnis terræ DEUS: Psallite sapienter, Regnabit DEUS super gentes. DEUS sedet super sedem Sanctam suam. Ita exci- tavit nos ad gaudia Paschalia Jessæus vates, (Psal. XLVII, 7.) & ad Psalmos DEO nostro, REGI no- stro, CHRISTO JESU decantandos, qui est IM- MANUEL, DEUS NOBISCUM, (Es. VII. 14.) REX NOSTER constitutus super montem Zion. (Ps. II. 6.) REX ille, qui super gentes regnat, à mari usq́; ad mare, & à flumine usq́; ad terminos orbis terrarum (Ps. LXXII. 8.) cui in hæreditatem da- tæ gentes, & in possessionem termini terræ (Ps. II. 8.) Rex ille super omnem terram, de quo Propheta, in die illa erit Dominus unus, & erit nomen ejus unum (Zach. XIII. 9.) Ad Paschalia, inquam, gaudia. Nam in Paschate annunciavit Apostolis Christus redivivus hæc gaudia, per orbem universum in- timanda. Sic scriptum est, & sic oportebat Christum pati, & resurgere à mortuis tertia die, & prædicari in nomine ejus pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum in OMNES GENTES. Luc. XXIV. 46. 47. In Paschate constituit Christus Apostolos præcones gaudii hujus Oecumenici (Joh. XX. 21.) Sicut misit me Pater, & ego mitto vos. Quorsum vero mi- sit Apostolos? Id exposuit Marc. XVI. 15. Eun- tes in MUNDUM UNIVERSUM, prædicate Ev- angelium OMNI CREATURÆ. Matth. XXIIX. 19. Euntes docete OMNES GENTES. In Paschate resurrexit Christus, post victoriam mortis bona, quæ peperit, & trophæa, quæ acqui- sivit, distributurus, per Orbem universum. Tradi- tus enim est propter delicta nostra, at resurrexit pro- pter justificationem nostram (Rom. IV. 25.) Jam ergo EXURGIT DEUS & dissipantur inimici (Ps. LXIIX. 1.) Jam dispersit Christo Dominus pluri- mos, & fortes distribuit Christus, ut spolia, eo quod tradidit in mortem animam suam, (Esa. LIII. 12.) Quod etsi ascendens in cœlum, conscendens thro- num, & occupans regnum suum illustriori, & am- pliori modo fecit, unde ascendenti applaudit Da- vid, & omnes populos ad jubilum provocat: Omnes gentes plaudite manibus; jubilate Deo in vo- ce exultationis. Ascendit DEUS in jubilo: & Do- minus in voce tubæ. Psallite Deo nostro; Psallite:

In hac tamen Paschali festivitate cepit illa spolio- rum distributio, & de hostibus devictis exultatio. Victor enim Diaboli, mortis, & inferni RESUR- REXIT Christus. Reddunt inferna Victorem, & superna suscipiunt triumphantem, dicente S. Augu- stino Serm. III. de Resurr. Jam expoliavit Chri- stus principatus, & potestates traduxit confidenter, palam triumphans illos in semetipso (Coloss. II. 15.) Jam pæana lætum canit: Et manu inferni redemi eos: è morte liberavi eos: Factus sum pestis tua, ô mors: Factus sum lues tua, ô inferne (Hos. XIII. 14.) Jam cum tripudio succinunt Apostoli: Absor- pta est mors in victoria. Ubi est mors stimulus tuus? Ubi est inferne victoria tua? (1. Cor. XV. 54. 55.) Jam impletum quod post percussum Pastorem, dis- persas oves in passione cruenta, & truculenta, in- terprete Zacharia, recepit Dominus (c. XIII. 7.) Convertam manum meam ad parvulos. Atque hoc est, quod prædixit Micheas Propheta, qui hæc omnia complexus videtur (c. II. 12. 13.) Congrega- tione congregabo Iacob totum te: in unum conducam reliquias Israel, pariter ponam illum quasi gregem in ovili, quasi pecus in medio caularum, tumultuabun- tur à multitudine hominum. Ascendet enim pan- dens iter ante eos: divident & transibunt portam & ingredientur per eam: & transibit Rex eorum coram eis, & Dominus in capite eorum. Quæ insignis est Paschalis seu Prophetia, seu concio. More enim Prophetarum effertur in præterito, quod longe post demum futurum erat: non ob certitudinem modo, sed imprimis ut in rem præsentem dedu- cerentur istius temporis fideles, & beneficia Chri- sti Redemtoris semper haberentur tanquam re- centia, quo pacto agnus occisus est ab origine mun- di (Apoc. XIII. 8.) & secundum Apostolum, (Ebr. XIII. 8.) JESUS CHRISTUS heri, hodie, idem & in secula.

Consideranda autem hic venit tum Iacobi in unum congregatio tempore N. T. promissa, ut insi- gniter è variis populis augeatur ovile Pastoris no- stri: tum perruptoris Regis ac Domini ascensio. Hæc illius causa est. Nisi enim פֹּרֵץ PERRU- PTOR ILLE ascendisset, nisi Rex noster coram Israelitis transiisset, & Dominus in capite eorum fuis- set, neque transire portam, & ingredi per eam po- tuisset quisquam, nedum congregando congregari totus Jacob, aut quasi grex in ovili constitui. Fun- damentum ergo salutis in titulo illo PERRU- PTORIS situm. Qui compendium simul exhi- bet fidei nostræ de Christo. Perruptor ille θεάν- θρωπος est DEUS & Homo. Perrupit cælum in DESCENSU de cælo, & incarnatione juxta preces & suspiria veterum fidelium (Es. LXIII. 1.) utinam DIRUMPERES cœlos, & descenderes? Perrupit per uterum clausum in nativitate: quia sine violatione matris virginis ex utero egressus est per clausam portam, (Ezech. XLIV. 2.) Quid est porta in domo Domini clausa, (inquit S. Augu- stin. serm. XIX. de Natal. Dom.) nisi quod Maria semper erit intacta? Et quid est quod clausa erit in æternum, nisi quia Maria virgo ante partum, virgo in partu, virgo post partum! Perrupit omnem ho- stium vim, & fraudem; perrupit mortis ipsius do- lores, & claustra, quia impossibile erat ipsum à morte teneri (Act. II. 24.) perrupit Diabolicas potestates, & laqueos inferni (Ps. XIIX. 6. Ebr. II. 14.) quia con- trivit caput serpentis infernalis (Gen. III. 15.) & ceu fortior superveniens Satanam devicit ac univer- sa ejus arma, in quibus confidebat, abstulit, & spo- lia ejus distribuit (Luc. XI. 22.) Perrupit sepul- crum, quia per sepulcrum occlusum & lapide ma- gno munitum resurgens prodiit; perrupit per ja- nuam clausam post resurrectionem, cum foribus non apertis ad discipulos penetravit, & Justino di- cente (quæst. LXVII. ad Orthod. suapte potentia e monumento cui lapis impositus fuit, egressus est, & ad discipulos ingressus janua clausa. Perrupit cœ- lum in ascensione: quia Apostolo teste, cælos pe- netravit (Ebr. IV. 14.) excelsior cælis factus (Ebr. VII. 28.) ascendit super omnes cælos, ut impleret o- mnia (Ephes. IV. 10.) & ascensu suo cœlum, quod clausum erat nobis, aperuit, initiavit nobis viam novam & viventem per velamen, id est, carnem suam, ut fiduciam habeamus in introitu sanctorum in san- guine ejus (Ebr. X. 19.) notasq; nobis fecit vias vitæ, ut adimpleret lætitia cum vultu suo (Psal. XVI. 10.) Perruptor ille etiamnum in defensione suorum perrumpit omnia consilia, omnes machinationes, omnes impetus, omnem violentiam, omnem frau- dulentiam inimicorum, qui sedens ad dexteram Do- mini inimicos omnes ponit scabellum pedum suorum & dominatur in medio inimicorum suorum (Psal. CX. 1. 2.) Perruptor ille perrumpit, in conversione no- stra, penetratque virtute verbi sui saxea corda nostra, ut intrare ea possit, & inhabitare in iis, per fidem (Ez. XXXVI. 26. Act. XVI. 14. Ap. III. 20. Eph. III. 17. Joh. XIV. 23.) Perruptor ille perrum- pet in novissimo die sepulchra nostra, nosque voce omnipotente e monumentis nostris educet (Joh. V. 28.) factus ipse primogenitus mortuorum (Apoc. I. 5.) ideo exclamat: Ego primus, & novissimus, & vivus, & fui mortuus: & ecce sum vivens in secula seculo- rum, & habeo claves mortis & inferni. (Apoc. I. 18.)

Pontificii nonnulli Lyranus, Cornelius a Lapide: & alii abripiunt hæc ad egressum Christi e limbo, qui secum animas Patrum eduxerit, quasi gregem sele- ctum, quæ in limbo quasi oves in caula detentæ fuerint. Sed hunc Patrum limbum ignorat Scriptura, imo eos in manu Dei, in sinu Abrahæ, in fasciculo vi- ventium, & Republica cœlesti, in populo Dei, ad quem collecti sunt per mortem, fuisse testatur. Quid quod longe aliter oraculum Propheticum exposuerit ipse Cornelius: Alludit, inquit, ad captivitatem, & carcerem Babylonicum, q. d. Zoro- babel perfringet carcerem Babylonicum, vosq; eum sequentes pariter eundem perrumpetis, & ex eo læti exhibitis in Sion: multo verius antitypus Zorobabel, id est, Christus e captivitate, & carcere Diaboli, infi- delitatis, & peccati vos liberans VI MERITOQUE CRUCIS SUÆ, eundem perfringet, vosque eun- dem pariter perfringetis & gratulabundi exhibitis in Sion spiritualem, id est, in Ecclesiam, quæ est civi- tas libera, sancta & felix Dei viventis. Hæc Jesuita: qui etsi anagogicum simul sensum de limbo confin- gat, Scripturæ tamen non nisi unicum esse sensum novimus. Et agnoscit Christophorus a Castro ejus- dem societatis, imo ipse etiam Cornelius, Hiero- nymum, Remigium, Rupertum, Albertum, Haymo- nem, Hugonem, Lyranum, Clarium, Ariam, Rie- beram, & alios vaticinium præsens accipere de congregatione Israelitarum in unam cum gentibus Ec- clesiam per baptismum & gratiam, Christi PERRU- PTORIS merito & efficacia futuram.

Non ergo ullatenus audiri merentur Judæi re- centiores, aut Iudaizantes nonnulli, Calvinus, & Hugo Grotius, (quibus os alias oppilatum est) de Zorobabele hæc explicantes. Nam quis perruptor ille sit, luculenter exposuit Propheta, nimirum REX Jacob, quam dignitatem nunquam obtinuit Zorobabel, imo DOMINUS JEHOVAH, qui in caput est Israeli, h. e. CAPUT ejus est: Messias nempe qui quum Jehovah sit, & REX atque CA- PUT Ecclesiæ peculiari ratione, ceu corporis sui mystici, eidemque ὁμοούσιος dicatur, nullum du- bium esse potest, ipsummet designari. Quod agnoscunt e Reformatis ipsiusque Calvini Disci- pulis præcipui, Oecolompadius, Gualtherus, Hier. Zanchius, Conrad Pelicanus, Pareus, Coccejus, In- terpp. Bibliorum Belgici: & e Judæis Rabbini anti- quiores, præeunte Paraphrasi Chaldaica, R. Mo- ses Hadarschan, & R. Salomo, aliique. Habemus itaque hic PERRUPTOREM GLORIOSUM Christum, Regem, & Caput no- strum, imo Iehovam Deum benedictum in secula su- per omnia: Habemus PERRUPTIONIS A- CTUM VICTORIOSUM, imprimis in Resur- rectione salutifera, qua per mortem, infernum, & sepulcrum, imo omnem exercitum Diabo- licum perrupit, obices & carceres peccati, mor- tis, Satanæ & inferni, seras, portasque omnes effregit, vim omnem contrariam destruxit, quum verbum Ebræum effractionem, perruptionem, & destructionem inferat. Habemus PERRUPTIO- NIS CONSEQUENS TRIUMPHALE, AC LÆTISSIMUM, Ascensionem nempe in cælum, qua in vitam resuscitatus Heros geminæ substan- tiæ triumphum egit de hostibus devictis, & ca- ptivam duxit captivitatem, regnum cœleste oc- cupans, & thronum majestatis conscendens. Sed & habemus PERRUPTIONIS ET A- SCENSIONIS FRUCTUM COPIOSUM ET SALUBERRIMUM. Quia perrupit non sibi, sed nobis, ascendit non sui, sed nostri causa, ut congregaret Jacob totum, h. e. non Judæos so- lum, sed universam Ecclesiam, siquidem gentes etiam vocandæ sint, & ad Jacobum totum perti- neant; universam ergo Ecclesiam sese congrega- turum, in specie autem (quod consolationis ergo additur) reliquias Israelis: semen enim relinquen- dum erat Esa. I. 9. Et mori debuit Iesus non tan- tum progente, sed ut filios DEI qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum, Joh. XI. 52. Missus erat ad oves, quæ pierunt domus Israel Matth. XV. 24. Ita concinit oraculum nostrum vaticinio Hoseæ, cap. II. 11. Et congregabuntur filii Juda, & filii Israel pariter, & ponent sibimet CAPUT U- NUM: quæ non conveniunt reductioni corpo- rali Judæorum, & Israelitarum, siquidem Israelitæ cum filiis Judæ non congregati sint, imo in Assyriaca captivitate remanserint: seu spirituali congregationi scilicet ad regnum Christi: de quo Hos. III. 5. Posthæc revertentur filii Israel, & quærent Dominum DEUM suum & David Regem suum, h. e. Messiam e Davidis stemma- te oriundum. Conf. Jerem. XXIII. 6. Ezech. XXXIV. 23. In unum autem gregem colligendi; in ovile Christi, quasi pecus in medio caularum, quo indicatur securitas, quod erepti e faucibus luporum, & leonum infernalium in tuto collocan- di sint, tumultuaturi præ multitudine, quæ talis & tanta futura, ut tumultus speciem habitura in mundo sit, siquidem fidelium studia & actiones, quæ DEO probantur, mundus ferre nesciat. Quemadmodum de Apostolis constat, quod tur- barum accusati sint, quasi ipsum terrarum orbem conturbaverunt Act. XVII. 19. De ovium vero con- gregatione testatus ipse Christus est, Ioh. X. 16. Et alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; & illas oportet me adducere, & vocem meam audient, & fiet unum ovile, & unus Pastor. Ideo in ascensione pandit iter PERRUPTOR ille, ante eas, ut tum in ovile Ecclesiæ, tum in cœleste ovile in- gredi possint. Ideo & ipsi fideles PERRUM- PENT, & gradientur per portam: Perrumpent per angusta ad augusta, per multas tribulationes in re- gnum Dei Act. XIV. 21. quia per mille rerum pericula ut B. Lutherus habet, perrumpendum est. Atque hoc est, quod additur; Et ibit Rex eorum ante eos. Perruptor noster antecessor noster est. Præmit- tam, inquit Dominus, B. Luthero interprete, diru- ptorem Christum, qui perrumpet, & tollet omne of- fendiculum, is parabit vobis viam fracta Satana, & mortis potentia, ut facilis postea sit transitus adjutis spiritu meo. ET JEHOVAH ERIT CAPUT EORUM. Caput non modo ratione ὁμοεσίας, (at quantum hoc, quod Jehovah nobis sit ὁμοεσιος, Pastor ille ejusdem sit cum ovibus substantiæ!) Sed etiam ratione vigoris & potentiæ, ratione com- municationis virtutis, & efficaciæ, ratione superiori- tatis, & eminentiæ, ratione perfectionis, & excellen- tiæ.

Nostrum ergo est in hoc Perruptore vera fide debitoque præconio exultare, in hac cumprimis festivitate, imo toto vitæ tempore: quia nostro bono perrupit; Eundem religiose sequi, quia Pastor & Antecessor noster est, Joh. X. 4. Ei, ceu Domino, servire in Spiritu & veritate. Eum ceu Regem venerari cum timore & tremore. Ei denique ceu capiti nos humiliter submittere, to- tosque devote committere. Perrupit Christus vim hostium, nobisque vires perrumpendi etiam donat: lætemur ergo & canamus, cum Habacuco c. III. 19. Deus Dominus fortitudo mea, & ponet pe- des meos, quasi cervorum & super excelsa mea dedu- cet me victor in Psalmis canentem: Effringamus, ejus adjuti virtute, feras carnis & mundi, ac di- rumpamus catenas, & funes malarum passionum, quibus adhuc constringimur, nec cœlum à Perru- ptore nobis adapertum sceleribus, & peccatis no- stris rursum occludamus. Memores simus sen- tentiæ Christi Matth. XI. 12. Regnum cælorum vim patitur, & violenti rapiunt illud. Si peccata, si a- liæ difficultates nos à regno cœlorum excludere videntur, perrumpamus hos obices, veraque pœ- nitentia, ac fide in Christum irrumpamus in cœ- lum, ut in ovili illo superno beata tranquillitate fruamur. Christus ex mortuis, acclamat Grego- rius Theologus (Orat. XLII.) simul surgite: Chri- stus ex sepulcro, peccati vinculis solvamini. Portæ inferni aperiuntur, & mors opprimitur, & vetus Adam deponitur, & novus perficitur, si qua nova in Christo creatura, renovamini. Hoc ut fiat, pia templorum frequentatione, devota verbi medi- tatione, sancta PERRUPTORIS nostri celebra- tione atque invocatione cum maxime opus est: neque intermittetis gratum præconibus verbi ani- mum depositis ad aram muneribus testari. Deus autem pacis qui eduxit de mortuis Pastorem magnum ovium, aptet nos in omni bono, ut faciamus ejus vo- luntatem, faciens in nobis, quod placeat coram se per Jesum Christum, cui est gloria in secula seculorum, Amen. P. P. profesto Paschatos Anno Domini cIɔ Iɔc LXXI.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. A THREATENING.

He intimates the rejection of princes and heads on account of iniquity and the tyrannical oppression of the poor, and the confusion of false Prophets, and on account of the vain persuasion of impunity of both, he indicates the devastation of Jerusalem and the temple.

He blames the avarice of the King, the Leader, and the Prophet.

Ver. 1. AND HE SAID: HEAR, O PRINCES OF JACOB ] That the justice of the punishments which God has threatened may appear the more, the Prophet shows that no order was exempt from grave crimes: nay, that those who ought to have led others to virtue, such as Judges and teachers, were the first in guilt. You have similar complaints in Ezekiel XXII, princes in Hebrew, heads, that is, senators of the whole nation.

Others more correctly observe that the former sermon was proposed under Ahaz, but this one in ch. III. IV. V. under King Hezekiah, and that it is different from that one, in which he both reproaches the Jews for their sins and threatens punishments, and promises liberation to the pious and penitent, and prophesies concerning the kingdom of Christ. Which opinion is confirmed from Jer. XXVI. 19. as also from this chapter III. Mich. V. 12. where the destruction of Jerusalem is announced, which although it was deferred on account of Hezekiah's repentance Jer. XXVI. 19. yet on account of the impenitence of his successors it finally followed.

AND LEADERS OF THE HOUSE OF ISRAEL] In Hebrew: קציני, that is, governors: the senators of the cities are understood below 9. Jerome translates it judges.

IS IT NOT FOR YOU TO KNOW JUDGMENT?] You yourselves condemn others: you ought therefore to know also what punishment awaits you, Rom. II. 1.

To know here is to be understood not theoretically, but practically, which they ought not only to have known: but also to have exercised judgment, i.e., justice, or laws, because this is incumbent upon the magistrate. 2 Chron. XIX. 6.

Latin:

CAPUT III. COMMINATORIUM.

Principum & capitum ob iniquitatem & tyranni- cam pauperum oppressionem rejectionem, Prophe- tarum falsorum confusionem, intimat, & ob u- trorumque vanam impunitatis persuasionem Hie- rosolymæ ac templi devastationem indicit.

Culpat avaritiam Regis, Ducis, atque Prophetæ.

Vers. 1. ET DIXIT: AUDITE PRINCIPES JA- COB ] Quo magis earum quas Deus minatus est pœna- tum justitia appareat, ostendit Propheta, nullum ordinem exsortem gravium criminum fuisse: imo eos qui aliis ad virtutem præire debuerant, ut Judices & doctores, primos fuisse in culpa. Pares querelas habes apud Ezechielem XXII, principes in Hebræo, capita, id est, senatores to- tius gentis.

REctius alii observant priorem concionem sub Achaz, hanc vero c. III. IV. V. sub Rege E- zechia propositam, & ab illa diversam esse, in qua tum peccata exprobrat Judæis, ac supplicia mi- natur, tum piis, & pœnitentibus liberationem pro- mittit, & de regno Christi vaticinatur. Quæ sen- tentia confirmatur è Jer. XXVI. 19. ut & è cap. hoc III. Mich. V. 12. ubi excidium Hierosolymæ renun- ciatur, quod etsi ob Ezechisæ pœnitentiam dilatum fuerit Jer. XXVI. 19. ob impœnitentiam tamen successorum tandem sequutum est.

ET DUCES DOMUS ISRAEL] In Hebræo : קציני, id est, gubernatores : intelliguntur urbium senato- res infra 9. Hieronymus judices vertit.

NUMQUID NON VESTRUM EST SCIRE JU- DICIUM ? ] Ipsi alios damnatis : debetis ergo scire, & quæ vos pœna manear, Rom. II. 1.

Scire hic intelligendum non theoreticum, sed practicum, quod non modo nosse : sed etiam exercere debuerint judicium h. e. jus, vel leges, quia hoc magistratui incumbit. 2. Chron. XIX. 6.

## 3:2
YOU WHO HATE GOOD ] And yet you hate virtue.

By good others understand both civil and external, such as is peace and tranquility, or the public security of life and fortunes, as also public honesty 1 Tim. II. 2. and also spiritual, which is piety or the exercise of religious worship.

YOU WHO VIOLENTLY TAKE AWAY THEIR SKINS FROM OFF THEM] From your fellow countrymen. The flock is not shorn, but flayed.

AND THEIR FLESH FROM OFF THEIR BONES] Both skin and flesh, and bones here signify possessions, according to the Chaldean interpreter.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUI ODIO HABETIS BONUM ] Atqui vos virtutem odio habetis.

Per bonum alii intelligunt tum civile & ex- ternum, quale est pax & tranquillitas, seu pu- blica vitæ & fortunarum securitas, ut & honestas publica 1. Tim. II. 2. tum spirituale, quod est pie- tas seu cultus religiosi exercitium.

QUI VIOLENTER TOLLITIS PELLES EO- RUM DESUPER EIS] Popularibus vestris. Non ton- detur pecus, sed deglubitur.

ET CARNEM EORUM DESUPER OSSIBUS EORUM] Et pellis & caro, & ossa hic facultates signifi- cant, interprete Chaldæo.

## 3:3
AND THEY HAVE BROKEN THEIR BONES AND CUT THEM] They have divided them among themselves.

AS IN A POT] As things are accustomed to be cut up which are thrown into a pot or cauldron.

Latin:

Vers. 3 ET OSSA EORUM CONFREGERUNT ET ET CONCIDERUNT] Inter se partiti sunt.

SICUT IN LEBETE] Sicut concidi solent quæ in lebetem, aut caldarium conjiciuntur.

## 3:4
THEN] When those times indicated above shall come.

HE WILL NOT HEAR THEM] The decrees will have been sealed.

HE WILL HIDE HIS FACE FROM THEM] He will withdraw his benevolence.

AS THEY HAVE WICKEDLY DEALT IN THEIR INVENTIONS] In the Hebrew: for the reason that they have done evil.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TUNC] Cum venient ista tempora superius indicata.

NON EXAUDIET EOS] Obsignata erunt de- creta.

ABSCONDET FACIEM AB EIS ] Benevolen- tiam subtrahet.

SICUT NEQUITER EGERUNT IN ADIN- VENTIONIBUS SUIS] In Hebræo : pro eo quod malefice- runt.

## 3:5
THUS SAITH THE LORD CONCERNING THE PROPHETS] Who call themselves such.

WHO BITE WITH THEIR TEETH, AND PREACH PEACE] While that which they may eat is given to them, they pronounce all things prosperous. The Chaldean follows this interpretation, and proves it by that which follows, the antithesis.

SANCTIFY WAR AGAINST HIM] They declare war upon him. Thus Joel 3:9.

Latin:

Vers. 5. HÆC DICIT DOMINUS SUPER PRO- PHETAS] Qui se tales dicunt.

QUI MORDENT DENTIBUS SUIS, ET PRÆ- DICANT PACEM] Dum illis detur quod edant, omnia prospera pronunciant. Hanc interpretationem sequitur Chaldæus, & probat eam, quod sequitur ἀντίθετον.

SANCTIFICANT SUPER EUM PRÆLIUM] Bellum ei indicunt. Sic Joel. III. 9.

## 3:6
Vers. 6. THEREFORE NIGHT SHALL BE UNTO YOU FOR A VISION] Instead of the good things which they predict to you, you shall have the greatest calamities, which are designated by the name of night and darkness among the Hebrews.

AND THE SUN SHALL GO DOWN OVER THE PROPHETS, AND THE DAY SHALL BE DARK OVER THEM] Dejected in spirit and countenance, they shall not dare to look upon the sky and the sun. The following words explain these things more clearly. Add Jer. 8:12.

Others understand these things concerning the night, concerning the Pseudo-Prophets, because that when they seemed to themselves to see the day and the light, that is, truth and prosperity, that vision shall be mere night and darkness and calamity: Or also that darkness and the darkening of the mind shall follow in place of visions. However, that distinction does not displease, that these things should be referred to the Israelites: because afterwards it follows concerning the Pseudo-Prophets: and the sun shall go down over the Prophets and the day shall be dark over them, the meaning of which Grotius did not correctly express: for it is not implied that, dejected in spirit and countenance, they shall not dare to look upon the sun, but that the light is to be turned into darkness for them, joy into sorrow, as is evident from a similar passage, Amos 8:9.

Latin:

Vers. 6. PROPTEREA NOX VOBIS PRO VISIO- NE ERIT] Pro bonis quæ illi vobis prædicunt, maximas calamitates habebitis, quæ noctis & tenebrarum nomine apud Hebræos designantur.

ET OCCUMBET SOL SUPER PROPHETAS, ET OBTENEBRABITUR SUPER EOS DIES] Animo vul- tuque dejecti non audebunt cœlum Solemque adspicere. Explicant hæc apertius sequentia. Adde Jer. VIII. 12.

Alii hæc de nocte, de Pseudo-Prophetis in- telligunt, quod illud quum visi sibi videre diem & lucem, id est, veritatem & prosperitatem, visio ista futura sit mera nox & caligo, & calamitas : Vel etiam quod caligo & obtenebratio mentis loco visionum sequutura sit. Non displicet tamen illa distinctio, ut hæc ad Israelitas referantur : quia postea de Pseudo-Prophetis sequitur : & occumbet sol super Prophetas & obtenebrabitur super eos dies, quorum vero sensum non recte expressit Grotius : nam non id innuitur, quod animo vultuque dejecti non au- suri sint solem aspicere, sed quod lux ipsis in tene- bras convertenda sit, gaudium in mœrorem, ut è loco simili constat Am. IIX. 9.

## 3:7
Verse 7. THEY SHALL COVER ALL THEIR FACES] They shall each cover their mustache, namely as lepers are accustomed to do. Leviticus 13:46. BECAUSE THERE IS NO ANSWER OF GOD] Namely that which they themselves had said.

Latin:

Vers. 7. OPERIENT OMNES VULTUS SUOS] Singuli mystacem suum obtegent, nempe ut solent leprosi. Levit. XIII. 46. QUIA NON EST RESPONSUM DEI] Nempe id quod ipsi dixerant.

## 3:8
Verse 8. BUT YET I] But I. He opposes himself to the false Prophets. I AM FILLED WITH STRENGTH BY THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD] I am full of divine power breathing into me, not with feasts, as they are. WITH JUDGMENT] Namely so that I may discern more serious faults from lighter ones, and denounce punishments according to the measure of each, as the following things show. AND WITH POWER] With constancy, so that I may not be moved from the command by anyone's reverence or fear.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VERUNTAMEN EGO] At ego. Opponit se fal- sis Prophetis. REPLETUS SUM FORTITUDINE SPIRITUS DOMINI] Vi divina afflante plenus sum, non dapibus, ut illi. JUDICIO] Nempe ut discernam culpas graviores à levioribus, & pro cujusque modo poenas denuntiem, ut ostendunt sequentia. ET VIRTUTE] Constantia, ne à mandato dimo- vear, cujusquam reverentia aut metu.

## 3:9
Verse 9. BECAUSE YOU ABOMINATE JUDGMENT]. Jerome wrote: You who abominate. For so it is in the Hebrew, Greek, and Chaldean. YOU WHO BUILD SION IN BLOOD] AND JERUSALEM IN INIQUITY] You who have built houses from wealth obtained by force and the condemnation of the innocent. Ezekiel 22:27.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QUIA ABOMINAMINI JUDICIUM]. Scripsit Hieronymus: Qui abominamini. Ita enim est in He- bræo, Græco, & Chaldæo. QUI ÆDIFICATIS SION IN SANGUINIBUS] ET JERUSALEM IN INIQUITATE] Qui domos ex- struxitis ex opibus vi ac innocentium damnatione partis. E- zech. XXII. 27.

## 3:11
Verse 11. HER PRINCES JUDGED FOR GIFTS] They were accustomed to judge for gifts. Ezekiel in the place cited. HER PRIESTS TAUGHT FOR HIRE] They taught for hire, pleasing to kings and the people: not what God had prescribed. AND HER PROPHETS DIVINED FOR MONEY] For money. Ezekiel 13:9. AND THEY LEANED UPON THE LORD] They rely: That is, they boast of his favor. SAYING: IS NOT THE LORD IN THE MIDST OF US] Does he not have his temple among us, and the most holy sanctuary, and the Ark, and the Cherubim? Compare Jeremiah 7.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PRINCIPES EJUS IN MUNERIBUS JUDICA- BANT] Pro donis judicare sunt soliti. Ezechiel loco dicto. SACERDOTES EJUS IN MERCEDE DOCE- BANT] Pro mercede docebant, placentia regibus ac po- pulo: non quæ Deus præscripserat. ET PROPHETÆ EJUS IN PECUNIA DIVI- NABANT] Pro pecunia. Ezech. XIII. 9. ET SUPER DOMINUM REQUIESCEBANT] Nituntur: Id est, de ejus favore se jactant. DICENTES: NUMQUID NON DOMINUS IN MEDIO NOSTRUM] Nonne apud nos templum suum habet, & adytum sanctissimum, & Arcam, & Cherubinos? Confer Jerem. VII.

## 3:12
Verse 12. BECAUSE OF THIS, BECAUSE OF YOU, SION SHALL BE PLOWED AS A FIELD] Indeed, because of you, Sion shall be plowed as a field. Because of your sins, judges, Priests, Prophets, an insolent army will imprint the hostile plow upon the walls. These very words of this Prophet are referred to, and indeed under his name, in Jeremiah 26:18. AND JERUSALEM SHALL BE AS A HEAP OF STONES] See above 1:6. The LXX, both in this place and in that of Jeremiah, as well as Psalm 79:1, translate עיים or עיי as a fruit-watcher's hut. AND THE MOUNTAIN OF THE HOUSE] The mountain of the temple, Moriah. INTO THE HIGH PLACES OF THE FOREST] It shall be such as mountains in forests are accustomed to be, overgrown with trees, wild beasts, shrubs, and thickets. He says that Sion, that is, that part in which the citadel is situated, is to be plowed like a mound, i.e., leveled to the ground, so that it can be plowed, i.e., according to the custom of the nations, by which victors condemned destroyed cities to eternal solitude by imprinting a plow upon them. Jerusalem or the city itself situated lower down is to be reduced to heaps of stones: the mountain of the House (Moriah) is to be in the high places of the forest, but turned into a high forest, eminent with the highest crags and slopes. However, it could seem doubtful from a comparison with Jeremiah 26:18 whether this prophecy of Micah was fulfilled. For the elders report there that Hezekiah, having performed penance, averted that evil. Truly, those elders indeed thought so. However, the sentence of GOD was not abolished, but suspended, and although Hezekiah averted it in his own days, he who prayed: let there only be peace in my days (Isaiah 39:8), the Jewish people did not escape its force, but that sentence was renewed through Jeremiah (ch. 25:11, ch. 26:9) and finally fulfilled in the 11th year of Zedekiah.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PROPTER HOC, CAUSA VESTRI, SION QUASI AGER ARABITUR] Imo propter vos Sion ut a- ger arabitur. Propter vestra peccata, judices, Sacerdotes, Prophetæ, imprimet muris hostile aratrum exercitus inso- lens. Referuntur hæc ipsa hujus Prophetæ verba, & qui- dem sub ejus nomine Jer. XXVI. 18. ET JERUSALEM QUASI ACERVUS LAPI- DUM ERIT] Vide supra I. 6. LXX. tum hoc loco, tum illo Jeremiæ, nec non Ps. LXXIX. 1. עיים, vel עיי ver- sunt ὀπωροφυλάκιον. ET MONS DOMUS] Mons templi, Moria. IN EXCELSA SILVARUM] Talis erit, quales esse montes in sylvis solent, arboribus, feris, fruticibusque & virgultis obsitus. Sionem, id est, eam partem, in qua arx sita, ut aggerem arandam, l. solo adæquandam dicit, ita ut arari possit, l. juxta consuetudinem gentium, qua victores dirutas urbes aratro impresso æternæ so- litudini addicebant. Hierosolymam seu civitatem ipsam inferius sitam redigendam in acervos lapi- dum: montem Domus (Moria) futurum in excelsa sylvarum, sed conversum in Sylvam excelsam altissimis rupibus, & clivis eminentem. Dubium autem videri posset è collatione Jerem. XXVI. 18. num hæc Prophetia Michææ completa fuerit. Nam referunt ibi seniores. Ezechiam acta poeni- tentia malum illud avertisse. Verum ita putabant quidem isti seniores. Cæterum non abolita fuit, sed suspensa DEI sententia, & quamvis Ezechias aver- terit eandem in diebus suis qui precatus est: sit tantum pax in diebus meis Es. XXXIX. 8. non tamen effugit ejusdem vim populus Judaicus, quin per Jeremiam renovata fuerit illa sententia c. XXV. 11. c. XXVI. 9. & anno XI. Sedeciæ tandem impleta.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. CONSOLATORY.

He promises the exaltation of the mountain of the Lord in the New Testament, the calling of the Gentiles, the slaughter of enemies, and the spiritual peace of the faithful under King Messiah, and promises liberation from Babylon.

Peace shall be in the kingdom of Christ, the preceding cross passes away. Verse 1. AND IT SHALL BE] The sense coheres with the previous ones: therefore we conclude that these things were taken from the older prophecy of Isaiah 2, not to signify the same thing, but a similar one, for Isaiah had said these things about the kingdom of Hezekiah, full of holiness, justice, and happiness. Micah, however, said the same things about the times after the return from Babylon, to which this chapter, and the one following it which coheres with it, pertain. IN THE LATTER DAYS] This signifies nothing other than afterwards, as we have said regarding the parallel place in Isaiah and elsewhere. THE MOUNTAIN OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD SHALL BE PREPARED ON THE TOP OF THE MOUNTAINS] That is, above other mountains. Temples at that time were generally on mountains: but the Jerusalem Temple, from the time it was restored, was much more illustrious than other temples. AND PEOPLES SHALL FLOW UNTO IT] Because of that huge benefit predicted by the Prophets and granted to the Jews by God, very many foreigners, especially from the Persians, who did not have images, and Greeks, who had drawn something from Socrates, then by their example others also, will come to worship the one God, the creator of the world, in the court of the Gentiles, as was the custom. Verse 2. AND HE WILL TEACH US OF HIS WAYS] Through the Prophets at first, then when they ceased, through Priests and Doctors. THE LAW SHALL GO FORTH FROM SION] The knowledge of the one God will be propagated from there in a wonderful way. Verse 3. AND HE SHALL JUDGE BETWEEN MANY PEOPLES] He will exercise judgments among many peoples. AND HE SHALL REBUKE STRONG NATIONS EVEN AFAR OFF] Through the Persian kings he will repress the Samaritans, Ammonites, Ashdodites, and indeed also the Arabs, who had wanted to hinder the construction of the temple and the city, Ezra 4:11, Nehemiah 4. AND THEY SHALL BEAT THEIR SWORDS INTO PLOWSHARES AND THEIR SPEARS INTO PRUNING HOOKS] The opposite of that which we had in Joel 3:10. The sense is: and the Persians and the peoples who will be under their empire, formerly most hostile to the Jews, such as the Assyrians, Babylonians, Syrians, Philistines, Ammonites, Moabites, Arabs, will cultivate deep peace with the Jews. Verse 4. AND A MAN SHALL SIT] That is, everyone, in a Hebrew idiom. UNDER HIS VINE, AND UNDER HIS FIG TREE] An idiom expressing great tranquility, 1 Kings 4:25. BECAUSE THE MOUTH OF THE LORD OF HOSTS HAS SPOKEN] That is, because God has so decreed. Verse 5. BECAUSE ALL PEOPLES WILL WALK EVERYONE IN THE NAME OF HIS GOD] They walk in the name of their gods. The sense is: it is no wonder that God has such singular care for us, for other nations invoke their gods to accomplish things. He speaks of the nations according to the far greater part of them, for the worshipers of the true deity among them were very few. IN THE NAME OF THE LORD] In Hebrew it is יהוה, by which name the true God is distinguished from imaginary ones. BUT WE WILL WALK] We walk, for in Hebrew, sometimes past tenses, sometimes future tenses are used for the present. FOR EVER AND BEYOND] We do that, and our descendants, so we trust, are going to do the same. עולם is the age of one man, in this place and often elsewhere.

The detestable στρεβλότης of the illustrious prophecy, Judaizing in this, that it understands it concerning corporal goods: namely, a material temple, and temporal happiness and security, although the Jews refer it to the times of the Messiah, being in this sounder than Grotius, provided they did not err concerning the Messiah, by not receiving the true one, and by expecting another, whom they themselves imagine. We have indeed vindicated it from the Grotian depravation at Isaiah II, yet here it must again be asserted in a few words. That it speaks of one and the same time, and of the same happiness, the words entirely the same, and the same signification of time prove, and the επιγραφή of both teaches that Micah was a contemporary of Isaiah. Who therefore will admit the Grotian figment, as if Micah speaks of far different times than Isaiah, and this one indeed of the reign of Hezekiah, but that one of the times after the return from Babylon, and both prophesy of temporal happiness. It is manifest that both Prophets looked to the times of the New Testament and spiritual happiness, by which the conversion of the nations to the Jewish Church, or the people of God and the kingdom of the Messiah. Since this has been proven from the prophecy of Isaiah, no further doubt can remain concerning the present oracle of Micah. The prophecy is repeated, however, by Micah in the same words, not through tautology, but so that the Jews might believe that he was moved by the same Spirit as Isaiah, and thus be more certain of the fulfillment of the remarkable promise. For repetition, according to Augustine, has the force of confirmation. And this sense is confirmed, and the Grotian gloss refuted, first by the consideration of the scope, which was to console the faithful, so that in public calamity they might have something by which to lift themselves up. Although it was a consolation that the captivity was to be ended by a certain number of years, yet there were few who lived until the exhibition of that promise. For the captivity lasted seventy years. But this was the solid consolation of all, to know for certain that the kingdom of Christ was to be revealed, through whom the remission of sins and eternal life were to come to those who believe, as the blessed Luther rightly says here, of whom Brentius also speaks on Isaiah 2. The prophets often and much discussed the devastation of the city of Jerusalem, which was done by Nebuchadnezzar. Zion, says Micah, shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a heap of stones, and the mountain of the Temple as the high places of the forest. What then, someone will say? If the metropolis of the Jews is to be devastated, will the nation itself surely perish? How then will it be true what the prophets said about the coming of the Messiah? They said he would reign in Zion, in the people of Israel, but how will he reign in Zion if Zion is plowed as a field? To these it is necessary to preach about the kingdom of Christ, so that the hearers may understand that although Jerusalem will be destroyed by the Babylonians, it is nevertheless necessary for it to be restored, so that the Messiah may receive his kingdom in it, and speak justice from that place to all nations. Next, the designation of time is to be observed; IN THE LATTER DAYS, which phrase Grotius rashly perverts, as if it denotes nothing other than AFTERWARDS. For one must not depart from the emphasis of the words at our own discretion, and since the latter time is introduced κατ' ἐξοχὴν (by way of excellence), the prophet is certainly to be understood concerning it. Calvin acknowledges this in this place. The prophet undoubtedly names the coming of Christ as the extremity of days, because then it was necessary for the Church of God to be erected anew. Finally, since Christ brought about the renewal of the city, his coming is deservedly called a new age, and therefore it is also now called the extremity of days, and this locution occurs frequently enough in Scripture: especially we know that the time of the preaching of the Gospel is called the last days and the extreme time, both by John and by the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews and also by Paul, which form of speaking they borrowed from the prophets. Something was also said about this matter in the second chapter of Joel. And Paul himself assigns the reason in chapter 10 of the first to the Corinthians. Because, he says, the ends of the ages have fallen upon us. Therefore, because Christ brought the fulfillment of things by his coming, the prophet rightly says that these will be the extreme days, when God will restore his Church by the hand of the Redeemer. Raimundus Martini in Pugio Fidei, part 12, notes that the He Hajediab designates the days of the Jews, so that their end is hinted at. But with no reason compelling the end, or the latter days, to be called in the aforementioned words of Isaiah and Micah the end, or the latter time of all men, that is, of the whole world, but rather of those to whom these prophets were speaking, namely the Jews, which is openly shown by this letter ה He, which is placed before this word ימים (days), when it is said הימים, that is, the days, as we commonly speak, which is therefore called הא הידעה, that is, the He of notification among them, because it notifies that the word to which it is prefixed is spoken not of an unknown thing, but of a known one. This is shown quite well where it is said by Moses in this way, Deut. 31:29: For I know that after my death you will corrupt yourselves with corruption, and will turn aside from the way which I have commanded you, and evil will befall you in the end of these days. Note that this evil, as the Jews themselves concede, then especially befell them, or happened, when in the end of their days, that is, when they still held the land, and having rejected the Lord Jesus Christ, they made two false Messiahs one after another, and for this reason they were all either taken captive or utterly destroyed by Titus and Vespasian, and then by Hadrian. Thirdly, the exaltation of the Temple of the Lord: The mountain of the Lord is said to be exalted not only above other temples, but a singular eminence is clearly indicated by that phrase: THE MOUNTAIN OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD SHALL BE PREPARED IN THE TOP or head OF THE MOUNTAINS, and it is added for the sake of emphasis: AND IT SHALL BE EXALTED ABOVE THE HILLS, and that exaltation is promised over all the kingdoms of the world, which are designated by mountains. Therefore, it is a matter of the eminence of the kingdom of Christ over the kingdoms of the world, not of the prerogative or excellence of the Jerusalem temple over the temples of the Gentiles. The kingdoms of the Gentiles are also called predatory mountains, Psalm 68:16. But the mountain of the Lord, the kingdom of the Messiah, is said to be about to surpass them in sublimity. Compare Daniel 2:34. Although the glory of the mountain of the house of the Lord was also great in the Old Testament, Psalm 68, yet that glory is meager compared to the glory of Zion in the New Testament: (1) by reason of Christ, in whom God was made visible; (2) regarding the more illustrious preaching of the grace of God; (3) regarding the multitude of miracles; (4) regarding the most abundant outpouring of the Holy Spirit; (5) regarding Christian liberty and immunity from Mosaic ceremonies; whence Haggai 2 says that the glory of the second house will be greater than the first, as the blessed Höpffner says here. Let us hear our blessed Luther: What he says therefore about the elevation and stability of the mountain is to be referred properly to the kingdom of Christ itself, not to the corporal place, which is devastated because of the sins of the people, and has been changed into the high places of the forest. The kingdom of Christ, or the Gospel itself, is so established that it can be oppressed or overturned by no forces, just as Christ says, The gates of hell shall not prevail. Not that it always shines with miracles, for which there was need at the beginning for a double reason. Because they were both promised in the Prophets, and a new doctrine had to be commended to men by God as if by this testimony, so that Christ might be recognized; but because it always conquers and triumphs against all its enemies. Therefore the Prophet used the word (Nachon), which signifies not only to prepare, but also to confirm and establish. So that just as the kingdom of Christ is above all kingdoms, so also it may remain, according to the sentence, But the word of the Lord remains forever. Nor does Calvin think otherwise: Now it is easy to see what that height was to be, namely because GOD wished to have that mountain like a royal seat: just as we know that under the Monarchy of the King of the Persians the whole Orient was subject to one tower of Persia: so also when the mountain of Zion was the seat of the highest Empire, where God wished to reign, and from where he also wished to subject the whole world to himself. This is the reason why the Prophet said it would be higher than all other mountains. Therefore in this one word his counsel is sufficiently clear.

Fourthly, this confluence of all nations and peoples to Mount Zion is explained too meagerly concerning certain Persians, who had no images, and Greeks, who had drawn something from Socrates, about to arrive at the court of the Gentiles, of which neither scripture nor hi- could allege history, as if it were abundantly sufficient if he only recounted his own inventions to us. But a far wider frequency of peoples is indicated by the Prophet, and the universal calling of the nations in the time of the N.T. is openly regarded. PEOPLES SHALL FLOW UNTO HIM in crowds like a river. Whence Justin, c. Tryphon, reads: 'and peoples shall place a river in it,' i.e., all nations shall run together to the Church, not with the steps of the body, but of the mind and spirit. It is a miracle if waters ascend from a valley and flow into a mountain: so it is a miracle that earthly nations ascend into the Church, whose doctrine and life is mountainous, arduous, and heavenly; indeed, the powerful and high grace of Christ effects this, as being sent down from heaven, as Cornel. à Lap. has it here. This observation of B. Luther is not to be despised: That which is added; And peoples shall flow unto him, in that is beautifully shown the diversity of this kingdom from other corporal kingdoms. For there, there is need of the bonds of laws and coercion, so that men may remain in their duty and disturb nothing: Therefore, there is also need of arms to retain empires and to defend the authority of Princes. But in the kingdom of Christ, there is no need of this care. It does not need arms with which to compel men; as soon as the word begins to sound in the ears and hearts of men, the men themselves of their own accord, or rather by their own will, as he says, run together compelled, and wish to cling to a part of this Kingdom, just as Christ says, 'The kingdom of God now suffers violence and the violent take it by force.' For what can be heard more joyfully than that through Christ the Father has been reconciled, sins forgiven, and eternal life given to us? Who would not wish to become a participant in such great riches? Therefore, as soon as this word is published, just as waters run down through precipices by a river, no one compelling them, but by their own force, so peoples flow together to this mountain, that is, to the Church, in which the treasures of the mercy of God are shown through the Gospel and distributed to believers. For the word (Naharu) embraces the likeness of a river running down with great force through sloping places. Just as also for that reason they call a river (Nahar) from its course or flowing down. But especially the Prophet wished to show the diversity of this Kingdom from the kingdom of the law or of Moses. For he is a violent Doctor, and can scarcely carve out some shadow of obedience with threats and many blows. For we see what the Law does when it most compels and urges; it makes either desperate men or presumptuous ones, that is, Hypocrites. But the Kingdom of Christ has, as Psalm 110 elegantly says, a willing people, who follow him further, like sheep their Shepherd. For benefits draw them, not threats or angry words. It is also noted by this likeness that the cause of the confluence is supernatural. For as the nature of waters and rivers is such that they do not rush except into a decline, but are derived and flow into a mountain contrary to nature by an external principle: so men cannot flow together to the mountain of Sion by the powers of nature, but this must be attributed to the supernatural grace of God.

AND MANY NATIONS SHALL HASTEN, AND SHALL SAY, COME LET US ASCEND TO THE MOUNTAIN OF THE LORD: AND TO THE HOUSE OF THE GOD OF JACOB. The word THEY SHALL GO, so continues Megalander, also signifies the highest will without anyone's coercion, just as also that they exhort one another and say: Come let us ascend. These show, however, that the kingdom of Christ is a kingdom of grace, which all who feel the burden of their sins desire and receive with the greatest pleasure and will. But it is especially worthy of observation that they say they will go to the mountain of the House of the Lord, and to the House of the GOD of Jacob. And they add the reason why they are to go, namely, that the Lord himself may teach them of his ways. Here, just as with one finger the Prophet shows the kingdom of Christ to be revealed in the last days; so also he wishes us to look back and see what kind of kingdom the Law was. I.e. Today from all corners of Judea all flow together at certain times to the mountain of the Lord, and to Jerusalem, so that they may perform sacred rites there, so that they may worship before the mercy seat, so that they may eat the passover there, etc. For the whole worship was destined to one Jerusalem and the place of the tabernacle. But in the last days, when Christ shall be revealed, there peoples and Nations shall run to the mountain of the Lord and the city of Jerusalem, but for far different reasons. For they shall not sacrifice, they shall not worship there, but there they shall hear, and allow themselves to be taught of the ways of the Lord, by the Lord himself. In this manner, the Prophet not only signifies the abolition of the rites of the law and of sacrifices, but also teaches of a new Word, of which men have no knowledge, not as of the law, but which is purely heavenly and hidden from the hearts of all men: for into whose heart did it ever descend that we are saved by the merit of Christ JESUS, who died for us? The Son who is in the bosom of the father, he has declared these things to us, of whom the Father commands from heaven: This is my beloved son: Hear him. The Law, besides the fact that it was implanted divinely into nature itself, just as Paul learnedly argues that there are thoughts in the hearts of the Gentiles also, by which evil deeds are either accused or good deeds defended, was also handed down before by Moses and shown to the Jews. Therefore, Christ in the New Testament brings a new kind of doctrine, by which we are taught concerning the remission of sins, and are gifted with the Holy Spirit, so that we may walk in the ways of the Lord, while we both believe the promises concerning Christ, and, helped by the Holy Spirit, resist sin, and are excited to perform obedience to God in all things. Calvin has followed Luther here again: Since there is express mention of many Nations, an antithesis underlies: because until that day God had been known in one people only. Since therefore God had chosen only the race of Abraham, a future change is noted here, while He will gather His Church from various nations, so that there will be no distinction between Gentiles and Jews. Now follows, they will say: Come and let us ascend to the mountain of Jehovah. By these words the Prophet shows not only that individuals will be obedient to God when they have been called, but also that they will all mutually exhort one another, and this zeal is deservedly required of the faithful, namely that they should animate and stimulate one another; for it will not suffice if each of us obeys God, but it is also necessary that this zeal be added, so that they may strive to win others over. This care is therefore now expressed in the words of the Prophet, when he says: Come let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord. He could have said that the peoples would come, and ended the discourse there: but here he wished to join two members, namely that they would come from everywhere, who had previously despised the God of Israel; then also that they would be exhorters to others: Come therefore that we may ascend.

Fifthly, when Jehovah Himself is established here as Teacher, HE WILL TEACH US of His ways AND WE WILL WALK IN HIS PATHS, it is indicated that He will instruct not through Prophets, much less through priests, but personally, and the peculiar privilege of the last days is noted, that they will have the Lord Himself as TEACHER, which the blessed Luther not undeservedly observed here, Brentius, Calvin, and other interpreters. Our Luther says that the Prophet teaches here concerning the Church of the New Testament, that it will have the Lord himself as its Teacher, who will teach it about his ways. Just as it is also said in the 2nd Psalm: I have set my king upon Zion my holy mountain. This king will announce the decree, saying, The Lord said to me, You are my son, etc. This is a clear statement, that the Kingdom of Christ is placed in teaching, just as the Prophets therefore call the Gospel itself a scepter, as in Psalm 9 and Psalm 14, the scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. For he speaks of the word, which is certain and firm and cannot deceive. Blessed Brentius notes here a triple commendation of the Gospel of Christ on Isaiah 2, p. 166. One is that the Messiah, who teaches the Gospel, is the Lord God himself. For they say: He will teach us, namely the Lord God. But it is treated here of the doctrine of the Messiah, which the Messiah taught first of all, and in whose name the Apostles taught afterwards. Wherefore the Prophet signifies in this place that the Messiah or Christ is the true Lord God, and whoever hears the Gospel of Christ, he hears truly divine Doctrine. The second is that the Gospel reveals the ways of the Lord God, that is, it explains to us the whole will of God, so that through the Gospel we may be able to know what affection God bears toward us men, and by what ways he wishes to save us. In the Gospel, however, we are taught that God, on account of Christ, favors all who believe in Christ, and that by this one way he wishes to save men, if they have believed in Christ. The third commendation is that the Gospel brings us the Spirit, so that we may walk in the paths of God, so that after we have believed in Christ, we may obey his calling, mortify the works of the flesh, and do the works of the Spirit, and finally enter, having overcome death, into eternal and heavenly life. These are the paths of God, in which one must walk.

Sixth, the promise is especially illustrious; The law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, which Grotius tries in vain to obscure with his own commentary, as if nothing else is noted than that the knowledge of one God would be propagated in wondrous ways after the return from the Babylonian captivity. For the Prophet looks back to that time when the Messiah was about to send forth the scepter of his kingdom from Zion, Ps. 110, just as Christ himself indicated that these prophecies were to receive their fulfillment when he ordered the remission of sins to be announced through the whole world, so that the beginning of that thing might be made in Zion and Jerusalem, Luke 24. Concerning which St. Cyril says: Immense and innumerable crowds of nations seeking the mountain of the Lord, that is, Jerusalem, and desiring to learn the way of the Lord and promising that they would go through it eagerly, explain the cause in this place, why they do not wish to be subject to the tax-paying punishments of the law any longer, and to run to Judaism. For before the coming of the Savior, while the laws and institutions of the nations still stood, some who served error approached, and having bidden farewell to the harms of idolatry, and having circumcised their flesh, they dedicated themselves to the customs and laws of the Jews. An innumerable multitude of such people was seen among them. Therefore Solomon, meditating on that august temple in Jerusalem, chose one hundred and fifty thousand stone-cutters and laborers and proselytes: for so we read in the Chronicles. Truly what was then being done was a type and a foreshadowing of the mystery: for they were about to construct a true and everywhere visible temple, namely the Church, for God, not more the Jews than those who were from the nations, carrying around the Jew who is in secret and having circumcision, not that which is in the flesh, but that which is in the spirit. Therefore, before this coming, they indeed betook themselves to the Jews from idolatry and lived by their laws. But when afterwards the mountain of the Lord was truly shown and demonstrated to be conspicuous, they burned with greater desire for it, rejoicing and saying: Because the law will go forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. Nor does blessed Luther rashly observe that another word is designated here than that which went forth from Sinai, and thus at the same time the abrogation of the law is hinted at, when a new doctrine is said to be about to go forth from Zion in the last of the days. But what does the added reason mean, Because the law will go forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem? This, namely, so that we may also know the proper cause why the Nations flow to the mountain of the Lord in such great numbers and we may learn to distinguish this word from the word of the law. For here he again transfers all the treasures of this kingdom into the word. He says, however, that there will be another word than that which went forth from Sinai through Moses, he says, The law will go forth from Zion, and the word from Jerusalem. Here, unless the Jews were struck with madness and blindness, does not the Prophet clearly show that this kingdom would not be corporal?
