Since after that magnificent preaching about the flowing together of the Nations he says nothing else than that the Lord will teach, and the word, he says, will go forth from Zion. But why does he promise a new Word, if that one given by Moses ought to be valid? The law is indeed valid and ought to be valid for teaching us about obedience toward God in this life; but concerning the possession of the future life it not only promises nothing (to the faithful) but even takes away the hope of it, while it convinces us that we have not satisfied the will of God. Hence arises that horrible danger of souls, that with the will of God known from the law, we feel nothing but our death and damnation. Therefore, souls are filled with desperation and anger against the judgment of God. It is therefore the supreme goodness of God that he teaches us otherwise about his will through the Gospel. In it is announced the remission of sins through Christ. For those terrified by the law receive this with the greatest pleasure, they proclaim God, they admire His goodness, they trust in His mercy, they call upon Him in the name of Christ, and joyfully they await the promise of future life, and they resist Satan and their own flesh. And they do all these things through the Teacher of this word, which shall go forth from Zion. For this word is so taught, that at the same time the Lord adds the Spirit. Thus B. Luther. Which, however, are not to be taken as if only the doctrine of the Gospel were indicated here, but that it is especially designated by it: For the whole heavenly doctrine is noted by the voice of the law as in Ps. XIX. and CXIX. Therefore it is explained by the word of the Lord, which comprehends the law and the Gospel: and judgment is said to be made through this law, which indeed announces the remission of sins to some, but to others condemnation. Nor does the parallel passage, in which the fulfillment of the prophecy is held, bring in another sense, Luke XXIV. 47. Calvin agrees with these again: We know, he says at this place, that the Jews came to the temple not only that they might worship, but also that they might be instructed in the Law of GOD. The Law therefore then resided in Zion; there was the sanctuary of heavenly wisdom. But what of our Prophet? The Law shall go forth from Zion, that is, it shall resound far and wide: the Lord will not only show in one corner how He wishes to be worshipped: but He will send forth His voice far even to the farthest ends of the earth. The Law therefore shall go forth from Zion: as it is said in Psalm 110. The LORD shall send the rod of Thy strength out of Zion. There the DOCTRINE OF CHRIST is metaphorically called a rod, or is compared to a Royal rod: because CHRIST does not otherwise rule among us, except through the doctrine of His Gospel.

There, however, David declares that that scepter is to be sent forth from God the Father, so that Christ may contain under himself all peoples who were previously alien. Thus, in this place, the Law will go forth from Zion. Cf. regarding this text Mr. Dr. Muller, Judaism, ch. XX, p. 67.

Seventh, the judgment of the Lord among many peoples and the correction of strong nations situated far away is explained specifically by the resolution regarding the repression of the Samaritans, Ammonites, Ashdodites, and Arabs, so that they would not hinder the repair of the temple and the city. For the preceding context proves that the discourse here is about the judgment of the Lord which is through the word, not by the external force of princes or monarchs. Nor is it only about the repression of peoples that is treated here, but about judgment or governance among peoples, because the Hebrew word is accustomed to be used for governance, Ex. 18:21, Jud. 3:3, and thus Christ is said to judge the earth, Ps. 96:8. Cf. Is. 42:1. Matt. 15:18, or if you prefer to render it, 'he shall act as judge among the peoples,' it must be understood from Job 16:49 [sic], ch. 16:8, that he ought to convince them of their sins and announce [it] so that they may repent, Acts 17:3, which is done by the Law, Rom. 2:12; causes and actions are directed to the will of God and the glory of the same: but by the Gospel we are instructed about the grace of God in Christ: wherefore both the Law and the Gospel pertain to his judgment: nor, finally, is the matter only about a few or neighboring peoples, but about MANY peoples, about strong nations SITUATED FAR AWAY; indeed, which those nations are, what kind of judgment [it is], and how they are to be reproved is manifest from the preceding, namely that those nations are understood which are to be brought to the mountain of the Lord, and that they are to be judged and reproved by the word. For by persuading [them] to abstain from errors, as Cyril does here, clearly showing that they are hastening to destruction unless they wish to live rightly and wipe away the stains of their old sins, he judges and reproves in a certain way, and not just one nation (but even to a distant land), that is, even to the ends of the earth: for the word of salvation is preached everywhere. To these he adds—these are the words of the Blessed Luther—the Prophet [gives] as it were an exposition of the preceding, so that he may clearly teach that this kingdom is not placed in external force or arms, but in the word, and that the nations pertain to it. It was not forbidden even in the Law for nations to gather at Jerusalem, like Naaman, the Queen of Sheba, and without doubt some neighboring kings, such as the King of Tyre and others. But the Prophet says here that it will come to pass that the King, who will teach his citizens in Jerusalem, will also teach great peoples and reprove strong nations situated far from Jerusalem. This is what is said in the last chapter of Luke: 'Repentance and remission of sins will be preached εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη to all nations,' yet in such a way that it begins from Jerusalem. Furthermore, when Scripture also says that the nations will come to the Kingdom of Christ, it not only casts aside Moses with his polity as a useless teacher for eternal life, but at the same time shows that the Kingdom of Christ is a kingdom of grace and the remission of sins. For what is it to be a Gentile, other than not to pertain to the people of God, to be without the law, to live in sins, in idolatry, in impiety? Therefore, since such [people] are called to the kingdom of Christ, is the kingdom of Christ not truly such a kingdom in which one is not judged according to works, but the gratuitous remission of sins through Christ is announced? As Paul says, the righteousness of God is revealed in the Gospel without the law, that is, in the kingdom of Christ those are held to be righteous who lack the righteousness of the Law, and who are sinners, if indeed they believe that their sins have been taken away through Christ. The Prophet uses significant words when he calls them many or great peoples—for it is the word (Rabbim)—and strong nations. For in this way he commends the power of the Word, than which no thing in the world is more despised. And yet, unless the nations and peoples, however great and strong, believe in this despised word, they will perish, according to the sentence: 'He who does not believe will be condemned.' By this danger, peoples and nations are moved, and they submit their necks to the Gospel, they suffer themselves to be judged, i.e., to have their sins shown and reproved, they acknowledge them, and believe in the remission through Christ. For the Prophet in this place uses the word for judging and reproving, just as Christ [does in] John 16. The Holy Spirit will reprove the world concerning sin, concerning judgment. This is: in the Gospel, men will be reproved so that they may acknowledge that unbelief is the greatest sin, and they will be taught to believe that the remission of sins is given through Christ, and to conclude that the tyranny of Satan has been broken, so that he cannot harm those who believe in Christ. These are the words of our Blessed Luther. Consonant with these are the things which Calvin has, which, since they also serve to explain the mind of the Prophet, we will not be reluctant to append here: Scripture speaks in two ways about the kingdom of God. For God governs the Devil and all the impious, but not by his word, nor by the sanctification of the Spirit; thus it happens that they obey God unwillingly and against their will: but the peculiar empire of God pertains to the Church alone, where, namely, God bends hearts to obedience both by his word and by his Spirit, so that they follow him spontaneously and willingly, having been taught within and without: within, by the instinct of the Spirit; without, by the preaching of the word. Therefore it is said in the same Psalm 110: 'Your people will then gather spontaneously.' Such a governance of God is described for us here by the Prophet. God, therefore, will judge not as he judges the whole world, but because he will subject the faithful to himself in a peculiar way, so that they desire nothing more than to surrender themselves entirely to him. Moreover, because men must be subdued before they offer such obedience to God, the Prophet expressly added: 'He will correct or reprove many peoples.' And this particle is to be diligently noted, because from this we gather that such pride is innate in us that none of us will be a suitable disciple of God unless he has been violently tamed. The doctrine, therefore, would grow cold by itself in such corruption of our nature, unless the Lord were to reprove us, that is, unless he were to prepare us first in a way that is, as it were, violent. Now therefore we hold the Prophet's counsel, why he joins correction to the command of God; for the word והוכיח signifies sometimes to expostulate, to argue, it signifies also to correct. Finally, here is noted the malice and perversity of our flesh, because even the very best never offer themselves to GOD unless first subdued: and in what manner? namely by the violent correction of God. These therefore are the beginnings of the kingdom of Christ. Now as to what he says, robust peoples, he extols and illustrates this same kingdom, of which he discourses, with this eloquence also. And from this also is gathered the power of doctrine, that robust men will offer themselves to be ruled by God without any resistance, when they have been so corrected. Correction is likewise necessary, but God does not use any external force, nor an armed hand when he wishes to subject the Church to himself, and yet he gathers robust nations. From this therefore the efficacy of doctrine is perceived, for where there is strength, there also is confidence and pride, and then also rebellion. Since therefore the word without other aids so corrects contumacy in men, we see in what an incredible way God works, when he gathers his Church. Furthermore, there is no doubt at all that these things ought to be referred to the person of CHRIST. And afterwards: the particle is to be noted, which is interjected עד רחוק, as much the duration of time as the distance of places can be noted by this word. Jonathan refers it to a long time.

That is to say, that God will argue with the peoples even unto the age, but I do not doubt that the Prophet here wished to include regions far distant, as if he were saying that God would then be King not of one people only, nor of Judea alone, but that His kingdom would be propagated even to the furthest ends of the earth; He will therefore argue with the peoples even unto the far distance. These are the words of Calvin, who is otherwise wont to willingly pervert prophecies concerning Christ.

Eighth, the universal peace and tranquility which Micah promises cannot be understood as temporal peace: for there was never a time when peace and concord flourished among all peoples, as it is predicted here: And they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks, nation shall not take up the sword against nation, and they shall not learn to wage war anymore. Which Grotius accepted as referring to all peoples, a deep peace with the Jews cultivating under the Persian empire; but history contradicts this. For the Jewish nation never had such great peace, and Grotius himself recently listed the Samaritans, Ammonites, Ashdodites, and Arabs, who were opposed to the people of God and were very hostile; even in the imperial court itself, and throughout the Persian empire, most destructive plots were constructed against the same by Haman and other enemies, concerning whom is the history of Ezra, Nehemiah, and Esther. Therefore, it is not to be thought that the Prophet is speaking in this place of public peace in these lands, because just as there was war before Christ was born, so there was war even when He was born, and there will be war among the nations until the last time of this age. But he is speaking of the kingdom of Christ itself and of the manner in which this kingdom will be dilated in the world. He is not speaking of worldly kingdoms, which are wont to be occupied, contained, and extended by war: But he is speaking of the kingdom of Christ. For this kingdom will not be occupied, nor will it be extended by cannons, as worldly kingdoms are: but it will be extended peacefully and tranquilly. They shall beat (he says) their swords into plowshares, etc. that is, those who in the name of Christ are about to receive the kingdom of the world, and are about to subject the nations and peoples to Christ, will not bring arms against the nations so as to force them with a violent hand to acknowledge Christ: nor will they arm their subjects so that they may defend the kingdom of Christ with swords, but they will run through the world unarmed: they will not incite those who acknowledge the name of Christ through faith to help themselves with arms to subject the remaining nations to the empire of Christ, but they will command each one to serve his own calling, and as much as is in them, to study public peace and tranquility; they will not institute schools in which recruits are exercised for worldly warfare: as the Princes and Kings of this earth are wont to do. But they will institute schools in which the hearers may learn spiritual warfare against sins, death, and hell, as Mr. Brentius has it on Isaiah II. And not only is the manner of propagating the kingdom of Christ looked to, but also the peaceful state in the kingdom of Christ. Concerning which Blessed Luther says: The Prophet here speaks of such peace, by which hearts are freed from the fear of the body and the judgment of God, through the Gospel concerning the Son of God delivered for our sins. But because through the Gospel all are made equal (for just as God concluded all under sin, so He also wishes to have mercy on all), there follows from this equalization also external peace among the members of the Church, nor does that most bitter hatred remain any longer, which was between the Jews and the nations, while the wall of the law still stood. For why should either a Jew prefer himself to a Gentile, or a Gentile to a Jew, when Jesus Christ the Son of God is the equal and common possession of all? Since we are all baptized into the death of Christ, and live in the hope of eternal life to be obtained through Christ? It happens, therefore, that those who before the Gospel was known used that hatred as if they were sharp swords and poisoned darts, these now live in concord among themselves, and use that holy concord as if they were plowshares and sickles to cut and reap those noble fruits of faith, by instructing others also in righteousness, and by inviting them through piety and blameless morals to know and obtain the benefits which the Gospel shows us have been exhibited through the Son of God. Therefore the Prophet adds, nation shall not lift up the sword against nation, nor shall there be any longer a study of war, that is, there shall be the greatest union of souls among themselves, after men in this way acknowledge Christ, and through the remission of sins hearts are pacified. They will no longer study war, that is, not only will they not harm others, but they will use every kind of duty among themselves, they will help their brothers in deed and work, and especially they will perform those excellent things, such as teaching the rude, admonishing the incautious, chastising the slothful, consoling the fearful, exhorting those in danger, and confirming the infirm, etc. For these duties ought to be perpetual in the Church. Therefore, the Anabaptists have no support here; if anyone is so unskilled in sacred matters that he adapts these to mean that it is not permitted for a Christian either to bear arms or to use them legitimately, he most ineptly perverts the meaning of the Prophet. For he transfers the meaning from the spiritual kingdom of Christ to the corporal kingdom. And that against manifest scripture, which imposes upon the Magistrate the necessity of defending subjects from unjust force and of keeping the peace. Just as Abraham defended Lot with arms, and the histories of kings show that pious Kings not only waged the greatest wars, but that God also made their counsels successful. And there is a manifest sentence in the Sermon of John on repentance, where he commands soldiers to be content with their wages. For he approves the legitimate use of arms, whether granted or commanded by the Magistrate, nor does he command them to cast away their arms. The true meaning of this passage, therefore, is that the Prophet speaks figuratively of the fruit which follows the Gospel when it is spread among the Nations. Concerning which Brentius also warned: It is not, however, to be thought that when it is said they shall beat their swords into plowshares, the Apostles, whose duty it was to subject peoples to the kingdom of Christ, ordered the legitimate magistrate to lay down [his office] and not to train subjects for battle: but that they themselves, for the sake of receiving the kingdom in the name of Christ, did not use corporal arms, nor did they exhort their subjects, that is, those believing in their Gospel, to take up arms in the name of Christ: meanwhile, however, they ordered everyone, after he had believed in Christ, to serve his legitimate calling diligently and in faith. Therefore, if any Prince or Centurion has become a hearer of the Gospel of Christ, and has given his name to Christ, he was indeed just, as far as Christianity is concerned, to convert his sword into plowshares, that is, to devote effort to public peace and tranquility: but as far as his office is concerned, he was just to change plowshares into swords, that is, to protect his subjects and defend them from enemies and robbers. For this is the calling of the Magistrate. If any craftsman or farmer has acknowledged Christ through faith, he too was just to beat his sword into a plowshare, and to follow his calling in tranquility, as far as Christianity is concerned: but as far as the duty of a citizen is concerned, who is subject to worldly empire in corporal matters, he was just to carry a sword, if the Magistrate has commanded it. For the doctrine of the Gospel, by which the kingdom of Christ is received and expanded on earth, does not change or invert, as far as it itself is concerned, the external state of worldly empires, and of those things which pertain to their legitimate preservation, but it sets forth the spiritual majesty of Christ, by which the remission of sins, righteousness before GOD, and eternal life are offered to us, meanwhile commanding everyone to perform from faith those duties to which he has been called in these worldly kingdoms.

Ninth, that security is promised here by the Prophet in that high peace which excludes all terror and fear entirely, such as is never to be expected in any earthly kingdom. For what kingdom has been so tranquil, or will be, that there is no place for the fear or terror of any enemy, as is promised here; AND EVERYONE SHALL SIT under his vine, and under his fig tree, AND THERE SHALL BE NONE TO MAKE THEM AFRAID. Therefore, it is necessary that these things be understood spiritually. These things also signify, says our blessed Luther, the supreme tranquility which those souls will enjoy who acquiesce in that preaching of the Gospel. And yet the Prophet seems to have wished by singular design first to use not just the appearance of trees, but then such trees as are both most fruitful and are cultivated for their fruit alone, not for their shade or appearance. For there are various functions and various offices in the Church, and there is no Christian who is not in his own kind like a fruitful vine or fig tree. The offices are diverse, to teach the Churches and to administer the sword, just as the species are diverse, the vine and the fig tree. And yet both have their most beautiful fruits. But βεβαιώσεως is added therefore: FOR THE MOUTH OF THE LORD OF HOSTS HAS SPOKEN IT, as a confirmation of such a magnificent promise of Christ, which, as blessed Luther warns, was necessary because of that huge scandal of the desolation and captivity of the kingdom of Judah: For it seemed that not only was destruction imminent for the whole people and religion, but also that the promise concerning the kingdom of Christ was being called into doubt. The Prophet therefore consoles the pious, that in that public calamity they may be of great heart, and console themselves with the certain hope of the future kingdom of Christ, in which all who believe in Jesus Christ are to obtain both the remission of sins and eternal life, that is, supreme peace and security. For the mouth of the Lord of Hosts has spoken these things.

Tenth, the Prophet signifies that there is a discourse about the Church being perpetually preserved when he says, but we will walk in the name of the Lord FOR EVER AND PERPETUALLY. The Vulgate rendered it wrongly and inappropriately FOR EVER AND BEYOND. For what is this beyond eternity? But Grotius perverts the very sense while he refers this to the age of one man: for where the word לעולם is joined with ועד, it will not be a long time, nor will the age of a man be a century, but an interminable eternity is designated. And what sort of solace for the Church would that be, that it would be preserved until the age of one man and beyond? Was not perpetual preservation promised to it until the consummation of the age, nay, into all eternity? For just as we walk here by faith, so faith is one day to be followed by the blessed vision 2. Cor. V. But what is said here, all peoples will walk, each in the name of his God, that does not seem to agree with the preceding, that all are to flow to Mount Zion. Grotius renders these in the present: They walk in the name of their gods, and adds: The sense is: it is no wonder that God has such singular care for us: for the other nations invoke their own gods to conduct their affairs. He speaks of the nations according to the far greater part of them, for the worshippers of the true deity among them were very few. But even if it be rendered in the future, and the last times are looked to, these things can easily be reconciled with the preceding, as blessed Luther taught. For however the universal calling of all nations and the conversion of many peoples to the true God may be promised, idolatry and false worship will not cease in the world: But how does that which he said above, that nations and many peoples would come, agree with that which he now adds, that individual peoples would walk in the name of their own God? The Prophet looks to the malice of Satan and the world. For just as when Christ was the herald of this kingdom, the impious Jews, Pharisees, Priests, and Kings were incited by Satan against Christ and the Apostles, so it always happens in the world. Never has this word of the kingdom of Christ been preached without others opposing themselves, without others following other Gods and another religion. Just as Christ also shows when he says: The poor have the Gospel preached to them. Likewise, if they have kept my word, they will keep yours also. This particle therefore pertains to teaching the Church and warning it beforehand about the scandal. That wherever this kingdom is in the world, there also will be those who do not wish to follow this God, and who boast of other Gods, of another religion, and of other forms of worship. Indeed, that there will always be those who will condemn the true Church, as if it did not have God. For thus individual nations walk in the name of their God, so that following different things they judge others to be impious.

Eleventh, that congregation of the limping Israelite people, over whom the Lord is to reign forever, cannot be understood otherwise than as the congregation to the Church of Christ, made under the New Testament. For the Israelites were never again gathered to the Jewish people, and united with them, just as Micah predicted here. Blessed Luther is excellent here: it is customary among the Prophets to call a Nation or people by the name of a woman. This limping and cast-off woman is therefore the House of Israel, which the Prophet above in chapter 2 says is to be cast off and scattered among the nations, so that it no longer has a part in the lot of the Lord, that is, that while that Republic and Mosaic worship stood, it was not to return to its own land. He calls (Hazoleah) the limping one, whether on account of sterility, because those whose thigh bone is displaced are little suited for childbirth, or because the house of Israel (as Elijah also speaks) after it tore itself away from the kingdom of Judah, lived in perpetual idolatry, and did not walk rightly in the worship of God divinely instituted. And this appellation shows the cause of the calamity, that on account of idolatry the kingdom of Israel was laid waste. Therefore this consolation was necessary. Because even if the hope of returning to the people of the Jews was cut off, nevertheless they hear that they are not for that reason to be excluded from the kingdom of Christ. The Prophet therefore wishes that they should not only look upon the present devastation, which the Assyrian was about to bring, so that gathered to the Church they might enjoy the promised seed and eternal goods through the seed of the Church of the faithful part. These things are so great that it was easy for the good to bear the inconveniences of the present captivity and devastation. For who, in the certain hope of eternal goods, would not easily suffer temporal things to be taken away from him? But this was only the consolation of the faithful. The greater part, however, were the impious, who both neglected the promises of spiritual liberation and, out of a desire for corporal advantages, not unwillingly joined themselves to the nations, and thus perished in impiety. Furthermore, this passage clearly explains the more obscure sentences of other Prophets concerning the restitution of the ten tribes of Israel. For because He states clearly that they must be restored after the kingdom of Christ has begun in Jerusalem and the nations have embraced the Gospel; without doubt, such a restoration will be of the same nature as this kingdom, namely, not a corporal one, such as the Jews still dream of, but a spiritual one. That the Gospel having been preached among the nations, they themselves will also believe and will be made partakers of the benefits of Christ through faith in Christ. And according to this opinion, those things which follow must also be understood: And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast off a strong nation. And the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion, from henceforth even for ever. He does not mean by this that they will attain power and wealth. For just as the King of this Kingdom was poor and calamitous in this life, so also will all those who believe in him be poor and calamitous in this life. In vain, therefore, do the Jews expect a corporal dominion. All the glory of this King and his subjects will consist in the fact that they will live forever with their King. For this is the first notable testimony in this place that the head of this Kingdom, Christ, is the true God, for it attributes to him the name of the true God (Jehovah). Furthermore, it is also a clear testimony concerning the resurrection of the dead and another life after this life. For if the Lord reigned over them, not only in this life but also forever, it is surely necessary that they live forever. For God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. And why would a kingdom be preached here so magnificently over the dead, who are nothing? If it is a kingdom, it is a kingdom of the living. Therefore, just as it is necessary for all men to die once, so the power of this kingdom is such that in it the dead live again and do not die, just as these things are said more clearly in the New Testament: He who believes in me, even if he has died, shall live. Likewise: That everyone who believes in the Son of God should not perish, but have eternal life. He proposes this consolation to the forsaken and rejected house of Israel, so that they may lift themselves up with the hope of these eternal goods and overcome the corporal inconveniences which they have earned by their sins. Theodoret interprets these things thus: He calls those souls who serve piety 'contrite and cast off,' for whose sake the only-begotten Word of God, by the assumption of human flesh, was seen on earth and walked with men, and he himself is a witness of these things, speaking words to the Jews: 'They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick.' And, 'I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.' Therefore, gathering the publican, and the harlot, and the thief, and those of that kind, and changing their morals for the better, he established the Holy Church, commanding them from this time forth even for ever. For the rest, Grotius does not explain the words themselves badly, but since he corrupted the sense in the preceding parts, he perverts the entire meaning of the Prophet. Thus he holds concerning verse 6 and 7.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. CONSOLATORIUM.

Montis Domini exaltationem in N. T. gentium voca- tionem, hostium cladem & fidelium pacem spiritua- lem sub Rege Messia promittit, & liberationem è Babylone pollicetur.

Pax erit in Christi regno, crux prævia transit. Vers. 1. ET ERIT] Cohæret sensus cum prioribus: ideo que colligimus sumta hæc ex antiquiore Prophetia Esaiæ II, non ad significandum rem eandem, sed parem, nam Esaias hæc dixerat de regno Ezechiæ pleno sanctitatis, ju- stitiæ, ac felicitatis. Michæas vero eadem dixit de tem- poribus post reditum ex Babylone, quo hoc caput, & quod ei cohæret sequens, pertinent. IN NOVISSIMO DIERUM] Nihil aliud hoc si- gnificat quam postea, ut ad comparem Esaiæ locum, & ali- bi diximus. ERIT MONS DOMUS DOMINI PRÆPARA- TUS IN VERTICE MONTIUM] Id est, supra mon- tes alios. Templa eo tempore ferme erant in montibus: Templum autem Hierosolymitanum ex quo instauratum est, multo fuit illustrius templis aliis. ET FLUENT AD EUM POPULI] Propter in- gens illud beneficium prædictum a Prophetis, & a Deo Judæis præstitum, plurimi alienigenæ, maxime e Persis, qui imagines non habebant, & Græci, qui de Socrate aliquid hauferant, deinde eorum exemplo & alii venient Deum u- num mundi opificem veneraturi in atrio gentium, ut erat mos. Vers. 2. ET DOCEBIT NOS DE VIIS SUIS] Per Prophetas primum, deinde iis cessantibus, per Sacerdo- tes & Doctores. DE SION EGREDIETUR LEX] Unius Dei co- gnitio inde mirum in modum propagabitur. Vers. 3. ET JUDICABIT INTER POPULOS MUL- TOS] Judicia exercebit in populos multos. ET CORRIPIET GENTES FORTES US- QUE IN LONGINQUUM] Per reges Persas reprimet Samaritas, Ammonitas, Azotios, imo & Arabas, qui tem- pli urbisque structuram impedire voluerant, Esdr. IV. 11. Nehem. IV. ET CONCIDENT GLADIOS SUOS IN VO- MERES ET HASTAS SUAS IN LIGONES] Contra- rium ei quod habuimus Joel. III. 10. Sensus est: & Per- sæ & populi qui sub eorum erunt imperio, infestissimi o- lim Judæis, ut Assyrii, Babylonii, Syri, Philistini, Ammo- nitæ, Moabitæ, Arabes, altam pacem cum Judæis colent. Vers. 4. ET SEDEBIT VIR] Id est, unusquisque, lo- cutione Hebraica. SUBTUS VITEM SUAM, ET SUBTUS FI- CUM SUAM] Locutio magnam rerum tranquillitatem exprimens 1. Reg. IV. 25. QUIA OS DOMINI EXERCITUUM LOCU- TUM EST] Id est, quia Deus ita decrevit. Vers. 5. QUIA OMNES POPULI AMBULABUNT UNUSQUISQUE IN NOMINE DEI SUI] Ambu- lant in nomine deorum suorum. Sensus est: non mirum est, Deum tam singularem nostri habere curam, nam cæ- teræ gentes ad res agendas Deos suos invocant. Loqui- tur de gentibus secundum longe majorem earum partem, nam veri numinis cultores inter eas erant paucissimi. IN NOMINE DOMINI] In Hebræo est יהוה, quo nomine Deus verus ab imaginariis distinguitur. NOS AVTEM AMBVLABIMVS] Ambulamus, nam Hebræis modo præterita, modo futura sunt pro præsenti- bus. IN ÆTERNUM ET VLTRA] Nos id facimus, & posteri, ita confidimus, idem facturi sunt. עולם est unius hominis ætas, hoc loco & alibi sæpe.

DEtestanda στρεβλότης illustris vaticinii, in eo Judaizans, quod de corporalibus bonis id in- telligat: templo nempe materiali, ac felicitate ac se- curitate temporali, etsi Judæi ad Messiæ tempora id referant, in eo saniores Grotio, modo non errarent de Messia, verum non suscipiendo, & alium, quem fingunt ipsi, expectando. Vindicavimus id qui- dem a depravatione Grotiana ad Es. II. hic tamen iterum paucis adserendum erit. De uno eodem- que tempore, ac eadem felicitate id loqui, verba prorsus eadem, ac temporis eadem significatio comprobant, ac σύγγονον Esaiæ Michæam fuisse utriusque επιγραφή docet. Quis ergo admittet figmentum Grotianum, quasi de longe aliis tempo- ribus Michæas loquatur, quam Esaias, & hic qui- dem de Ezechiæ regno, ille vero de temporibus post reditum ex Babylone, uterque de temporali felicitate vaticinetur. Manifestum est utrumque Prophe- tam respexisfe tempora Nov. Testam. & spiritualem eorum felicitatem, qua conversionem gentium ad Ecclesiam Judaicam, vel populum Dei & regnum Messiæ. Quod quum de Esaiæ vaticinio proba- tum fuerit, de Michææ præsenti oraculo nullum amplius dubium superesse potest. Repetitur au- tem iisdem verbis vaticinium à Michæa, non per ταυτολογίαν, sed ut crederent Judæi, eodem i- psum agitatum cum Esaia Spiritu, eoque certiores essent de insignis promissionis complemento. Nam repetitio secundum August. firmamenti vim habet. Et confirmant hunc sensum, refellunt verò glossam Grotianam primo scopi consideratio, qui e- rat fideles consolari, ut in publica calamitate ha- beant, quo se erigerent. Etsi autem consolatio e- rat, quod captivitas certo annorum numero finien- da esset, tamen pauci fuerunt, qui usque ad exhibi- tionem promissionis ejus vixerunt. Duravit enim captivitas septuaginta annis. Hæc autem solida conso- latio fuit omnium, certo scire, quod Christi regnum es- set revelandum, per quem remissio peccatorum, & vi- ta æterna credentibus obventura erat, ut recte hic B. Lutherus, de quo etiam Brentius ad Es. II. Pro- phetæ sæpe ac multum disserebant de vastatione urbis Hierosolymæ, quæ facta est à Nebucad Nezare. Zion, inquit Michæas, quasi ager arabitur, & Hierusa- lem quasi acervus lapidum erit, & mons Templi in excelsa sylvarum. Quid ergo, dicet quispiam? Si devastabitur metropolis Judæorum, certe etiam gens ipsa peribit? Quomodo igitur verum erit, quod Prophetæ dixerunt de adventu Messiæ? Dixerunt, eum regnaturum in Zion, in populo Israel, sed quo- modo regnabit in Zion, si Zion arabitur quasi ager? His necesse est prædicari de regno Christi, ut audito- res intelligant, quod etsi Hierusalem delebitur per Babylonios, tamen necesse sit eam restaurari, ut Mes- sias suscipiat in ea regnum suum, & dicat ex eo loco jus omnibus Gentibus. Deinde observanda tem- poris designatio; IN NOVISSIMO DIERUM, quam phrasin temere pervertit Grotius, quasi nihil aliud notet, quam POSTEA. Non enim est ab emphası vocum pro nostro arbitrio disceden- dum, & quum tempus novissimum xτ' ἐξοχὴν infe- ratur, de eo utique Propheta intelligendus. Agno- scit id Calvinus in h. l. Extremitatem dierum Pro- pheta haud dubie nominat Christi adventum, quia tunc oportuit de integro Ecclesiam Dei erigi. Deni- que quum Christus attulerit renovationem urbis, merito ejus adventus vocatur novum seculum, & ideo etiam nunc dicitur extremitas dierum, & hæc locutio satis frequenter occurrit in Scriptura: præser- tim vero scimus vocari tempus prædicati Evangelii dies novissimos & tempus extremum, tam à Iohan- ne, quam ab Autore Epistolæ ad Hebræos & à Paulo etiam, quam loquendi formam mutuati sunt à Prophe- tis. Quæ de re etiam aliquid ad secundum caput Ioelis dictum fuit. Et Paulus ipse assignat rationem c. 10. prioris ad Corinthios. Quia in nos, inquit, fi- nes seculorum inciderunt. Ergo quia Christus com- plementum rerum suo adventu attulit, merito Pro- pheta dicit, hos fore extremos dies, quum Deus restituet Ecclesiam suam per manum Redempto- ris. Raimundus Martini in Pugion. fidei p. XII. notat, He Hajediab dies Judæorum designare, ut il- lorum finis innuatur. Nulla vero ratione cogente fi- nis, vel novissimum dierum vocetur in supra dictis Esa- iæ, & Michææ verbis finis, vel novissimum o- mnium hominum, id est, totius mundi, sed po- tius eorum, quibus isti Prophetæ loquebantur, vide- licet Judæorum, quod aperte monstratur per hanc literam ה He, quæ huic dictioni ימים dierum præpo- nitur, cum dicitur הימים, id est, deis dies, ut vulga- riter loquimur, quod ideo הא הידעה, id est, He notitiæ apud eos vocatur, quia notificat quod dictio cui præponitur non de ignota re, sed de nota dicatur. Hoc autem fatis bene ostenditur, ubi per Mosen hoc modo dictum est, Deut. XXXI. v. 29. Quoniam novi quod post mortem meam corruptione corrumpe- mini, & deviabitis à via, quam mandavi vobis, & ob- viabit nobis malum in fine horum dierum. Nota quod hoc malum Iudæis concedentibus, tunc eis maxi- me obviavit, sive accidit, quando in fine dierum suo- rum, quando scilicet adhuc terram tenebant, & repro- bato Domino Iesu Christo fecerunt duos falsos Mes- sias unum post alium, & hac de causa per Titum & Ve- spasianum, deinde per Adrianum omnes vel captiva- ti, vel penitus sunt destructi. Tertio Templi Domini exaltatio: Non tantum super alia templa mons Domini dicitur exaltandus, sed singularis plane e- minentia phrasi illa indigitatur: ERIT MONS DOMUS DOMINI PRAEPARATUS IN VERTICE vel capite MON- TIUM, atq; additur emphaseos causa: ET EXALTA- BITUR IPSE PRAE COLLIBUS, & exaltatio illa pro- mittitur super omnia regna mundi, quæ per montes designantur. De eminentia ergo regni Christi præ regnis mundi, non de templi Hiero- solymitani prærogativa aut ἐξοχῇ præ templis gentilium agitur. Vocantur & regna gentium mon- tes prædatorii Pf. LXIIX. 16. Sed ea superaturus di- citur sublimitate mons Domini, regnum Messiæ. Conf. Dan. 1. 34. Quamvis vero etiam magna fue- rit gloria montis domus Domini in V. Test. Psal. LXIIX. tamen gloria illa exigua est præ gloria Sio- nis in N. T. (1) ratione Christi, in quo Deus factus est visibilis. (2) quoad prædicationem illustriorem gratiæ Dei. (3) quoad multitudinem miraculorum. (4) quo- ad effusionem S. S. largissimam. (5) quoad libertatem Christianam & immunitatem à ceremoniis Mosaicis; unde Hagg. 2. dicitur, gloriam domus secundæ fore majorem primæ, ut hic B. Höpffnerus. Audia- mus B. Lutherum nostrum: Quod igitur de eleva- tione & stabilitone montis dicit, proprie ad ipsum regnum Christi, non ad corporalem locum refe- rendum est, qui propter peccata populi vastatur, & in excelsa silvarum mutatus est. Regnum autem Christi seu ipsum Evangelium sic firmatum est, ut nullis viribus possit opprimi aut everti, sicut Chri- stus dicit, Portæ inferorum non prævalebunt. Non quod semper clareat miraculis, quibus duplicem ob causam initio opus erat. Quod & in Prophetis promissa essent, & nova doctrina hoc quasi testi- monio divinitus hominibus commendanda esset, ut agnosceretur Christus; sed quod semper vincat & triumphet contra omnes hostes suos. Ideo Pro- pheta verbo (Nachon) usus est, quod non solum præparare, sed etiam confirmare & stabilire signi- ficat. Ut sicut est regnum Christi super omnia re- gna, ita etiam maneat, secundum sententiam, Ver- bum autem Domini manet in æternum. Nec aliter Calvinus: Jam facile est videre, qualis illa altitudo futura fuerit, nempe quia DEUS montem illum vellet habere instar Regiæ sedis: quemadmodum sub Monarchia Regis Persarum scimus totum O- rientem fuisse subjectum uni turri Persidis: sic et- iam quum sedes esset summi Imperii mons Sion, ubi Deus volebat regnare, & unde etiam volebat sibi subjicere totum orbem terrarum. Hæc ra- tio est, cur Propheta dixerit illum fore superio- rem omnibus aliis montibus. Ergo in hoc uno verbo satis liquet ejus consilium.

Quarto Confluxus iste omnium gentium & popu- lorum ad montem Sion nimis jejune explicatur de Persis quibusdam, qui imagines non habuere, & Græcis, qui à Socrate aliquid hauserant, ad atrium gentium perventuris, de quo nec scripturam nec hi- storiam allegare potuit, quasi abunde sufficeret, si sua solum nobis commenta recenseret. At lon- ge amplior frequentia populorum indigitatur à Propheta, & palam respicitur vocatio universa- lis gentium tempore N. T. FLUENT AD EUM POPULI turmatim instar fluvii. Unde Justin. c. Tryphon. legit & flumen ponent in eo populi q. d. ad Ecclesiam concurrent omnes gentes, passibus non corporis, sed mentis & spiritus. Miraculum est, si aquæ è valle ascendant & fluant in montem: ita miraculum est, quod gentes terrenæ ascendent in Ecclesiam, cujus doctrina & vita montosa est, ardua & cœlestis; nimirum id efficit gratia Christi po- tens & alta, utpote è cœlo demissa, ut hic habet Cor- nel. à Lap. B. Lutheri observatio non contemnen- da hæc est: Quod additum est; Et populi confluent ad eum, in eo pulcre ostenditur diversitas hujus regni ab aliis corporalibus regnis. Ibi enim vin- culis legum & coactione est opus, ut homines ma- neant in officio, & nihil turbent: Ideo etiam armis ad Imperia retinenda & defendendam autorita- tem Principum opus est. Sed in Christi regno hac cura non est opus. Non indiget armis, quibus homines cogat, statim cum verbum in auribus & cordibus hominum sonare cœperit, ipsi homines sua sponte, vel potius sua voluntate, ut ille dicit, coacti accurrunt, & in parte hujus Regni hærere volunt, sicut Christus dicit, Regnum Dei nunc vim patitur & violenti rapiunt illud. Quid enim potest lætius audiri, quam quod per Christum Pater reconciliatus, peccata remissa, & vita æterna nobis donata sit? Tantarum opum quis non o- ptaret se quoque participem fieri? Itaque cum primum verbum hoc vulgatur, sicut flumine nemi- ne cogente, sed sua vi per præcipitia decurrunt, ita populi ad hunc montem, hoc est, ad Ecclesiam confluunt, in qua per Evangelium thesauri mise- ricordiæ Dei ostenduntur, & credentibus distri- buuntur. Nam verbum (Naharu) similitudinem fluminis, magna vi per declivia loca decurrentis, complectitur. Sicut etiam ideo (Nahar) fluvium vocant à cursu seu defluxu. Præsertim autem vo- luit Propheta ostendere diversitatem hujus Regni à regno legis seu Mosis. Is enim violentus Doctor est, & vix minis & plagis multis aliquam umbram obedientiæ exsculpere potest. Videmus enim quid Lex faciat, cum maxime cogit & urget, aut despe- ratos, aut præsumtores seu Hypocritas facit. Sed Regnum Christi habet, sicut Psalmus CX. eleganter dicit, spontaneum populum, qui ultra, sicut oves Pastorem suum, sequitur. Trahunt enim eos be- neficia, non cogunt minæ, aut irata verba. No- tatur etiam hac similitudine, quod causa conflu- xus supernaturalis sit. Ut enim aquarum & flu- minum ea est ratio, ut non nisi in declive ruant, in montem autem præter naturam ab externo prin- cipio deriventur, & confluant: ita non possunt ho- mines naturæ viribus confluere ad montem Sion, sed supernaturali gratiæ Dei hoc tribuendum est.

ET PROPERABUNT GENTES MULTÆ, ET DICENT, VENITE ADSCENDAMUS AD MONTEM DOMINI: ET AD DO- MUM DEI JACOB. Verbum IBUNT, ita per- git Megalander, etiam significat summam volunta- tem sine cujusquam coactione, sicut etiam, quod se invicem cohortantur, & dicunt: Venite ascende- mus. Ostendunt autem hæc, quod regnum Christi sit regnum gratiæ, quam optant, & cum summa volu- ptate & voluntate accipiunt omnes, qui sentiunt onus peccatorum suorum. Imprimis autem dignum ob- servatione est, quod dicunt se ituros ad mon- tem Domus Domini, & ad Domum DEI Ja- cob. Et addunt causam cur ituri sint, scilicet ut ipse Dominus eos doceat de viis suis. Hic sicut uno digito Propheta ostendit regnum Christi in novis- simis diebus revelandum; ita etiam retro nos vult re- spicere, & videre, quale regnum Legis fuerit. Q.d. Ho- die ex omnibus Judææ angulis confluunt omnes certis temporibus ad montem Domini, & ad Je- rusalem, ut ibi sacra faciant, ut coram propitia- torio adorent, ut pascha ibi comedant &c. Nam totus cultus erat ad unam Jerusalem & tabernacu- li locum destinatus. Sed in novissimis diebus, cum Christus revelabitur ibi populi & Gentes current ad montem Domini & civitatem Jerusa- lem, Verum longe alias ob causas. Non enim sacrificabunt, non ibi adorabunt, sed ibi au- dient, & doceri se sinent de viis Domini, ab ipso Domino. Ad hunc modum, non solum a- bolitionem cultuum legis, & sacrificiorum Pro- pheta significat, sed etiam docet de novo Verbo, cu- jus, non ut legis, aliquam notitiam homines ha- bent, sed quæ mere cælestis & ab omnium hominum cordibus abscondita est: in cujus enim cor unquam descendit, quod simus salvi merito Christi JE- SU, qui pro nobis mortuus est? Filius qui in si- nu patris est, iste enarravit nobis hæc, de quo Pater cœlo mandat; Hic est filius meus dilectus: Hunc audite. Lex præterquam quod in ipsam na- turam implantata divinitus, sicut Paulus erudite disputat, etiam in Gentium cordibus esse cogitatio- nes, quibus aut accusantur malefacta, aut defen- duntur benefacta, etiam per Mosen antea tradi- ta, & Judæis ostensa est. Itaque Christus in No- vo Testamento novum doctrinæ genus affert, quo de remissione peccatorum docemur, & donamur Spiritu Sancto, ut ambulemus in viis Domini, dum & credimus promissionibus de Christo, & Spiritu sancto adjuti resistimus peccato, & ex- citamur ad obedientiam Deo in omnibus præ- standam. Sequutus hic iterum Lutherum Calvi- nus est: Quum expressa sit mentio multorum Gen- tium, subesse antithefin: quia ad illam usque diem cognitus fuerat Deus in uno populo duntaxat. Quo- niam ergo elegerat Deus solum genus Abrahæ, notatur hic futura mutatio, dum Ecclesiam suam colliget ex variis gentibus, ita ut non sit futurum discrimen in- ter Gentiles & Judæos. Jam sequitur, dicent: Ve- nite & ascendemus ad montem Jehovæ. Propheta his verbis ostendit non tantum singulos Deo morigeros fore, ubi vocati fuerint, sed mutuo etiam se cohorta- turos omnes, & hoc studium merito exigitur a fide- libus, ut scilicet alii alios animent, atq; extimu- lent, neque enim sufficiet, si quisq; nostrum Deo ob- sequatur, sed necesse est etiam hunc Zelum accedere, ut alii alios lucrifacere studeant. Hæc igitur cura nunc Prophetæ verbis exprimitur, quum dicit: Ve- nite ut ascendamus ad montem Domini. Pote- rat dicere venturos populos, & illic finire orationem: sed hic voluit conjungere duo membra, nempe undiq; venturos, qui prius contempserant Deum Israelis; deinde alios etiam aliis fore, hortatores: Venite er- go ut ascendamus.

Quinto cum Doctor hic constituitur Jeho- vah ipse, DOCEBIT NOS de viis suis ET I- BIMUS IN SEMITIS EJUS non per Prophetas, nedum per sacerdotes, αὐτοπροσώπως informa- turus indigitatur, & peculiare privilegium nota- tur novissimorum dierum quod habituri sint ipsummet Dominum DOCTOREM, quod hic non immerito observavit B. Lutherus, Brentius, Calvinus & alii Interpp. Docet Propheta hic de Ecclesia N. T. inquit Lutherus noster, quod se habitura Doctorem ipsum Dominum, qui eam do- ceat de suis viis. Sicut etiam in 2. Psalm. dicitur: Ego constitui regem meum, super Zion montem sanctum meum. Hic rex annuntiabit præceptum, dicens, Dominus dixit ad me, Filius meus es tu &c. Hæc est clara sententia, Regnum Christi positum esse in docendo, sicut Prophetæ ideo ipsum Evangelium vo- cant sceptrum, ut Psal. IX. & Psal. XIV. sceptrum æquitatis est sceptrum regni tui. Nam de verbo loquitur, quod certum ac firmum est & fallere non po- test. B. Brentius notat hic triplicem commendatio- nem Evangelii Christi ad Es. II. p. 166. Una est, quod Messias, qui Evangelion docet, Dominus ipse Deus est. Dicunt enim: Docebit nos, nimirum Dominus Deus. Tractatur autem hic de doctrina Messia, quam Messias primum omnium docuit, & cujus nomine postea Apostoli docuerunt. Quare Propheta hoc loco significat, Messiam seu Christum esse verum Dominum Deum, & qui Evangelion Christi audit, is audit vere divinam Doctrinam. Altera est, quod Evangelion revelat vias Domini Dei, hoc est exponit nobis omnem voluntatem Dei, ut per Evangelium possimus cognoscere, quem affectum Deus erga nos homines gerat, & quibus viis nos velit servare. In Evangelio autem docemur, quod Deus propter Christum faveat omnibus credenti- bus in Christum, & quod hac una via velit ho- mines salvare, si crediderint in Christum. Tertia commendatio est, quod Evangelium afferat nobis Spiritum, ut ambulemus in semitis Dei, ut postquam credidimus in Christum, obediamus vocationi ejus, mortificemus opera carnis, & faciamus opera Spiri- tus, ac postremo ingrediamur, devicta morte in æter- nam & cælestem vitam. Hæ sunt semitæ Dei, in quibus ambulandum est.

Sexto illustris imprimis est promissio; De Sion egredietur lex, & verbum Domini de Jerusalem, quam frustra suo commento obfuscare conatur Grotius, quasi nihil aliud notetur, quam unius Dei cognitionem miris modis propagatam iri post reditum è captivitate Babylonica. Respicit enim Propheta illud tempus, quo emissurus erat Mes- sias sceptrum regni sui è Sion Ps. CX. quemadmo- dum Christus ipse hæc vaticinia suum comple- mentum sortitura indicavit, cum remissionem pec- carorum annunciari jussit per totum orbem, ita, ut initium ejus rei fiat in Sion & Jerusalem Luc. XXIV. Quo de S. Cyrillus: Immensæ & innume- rabiles gentium catervæ petentes montem Domi- ni, hoc est, Hierusalem, cupientesque discere viam Domini & per eam se ituras alacriter pro- mittentes, causam hoc loco exponunt, cur nolint ultra legis pœnæ vectigales fieri, & ad Judaismum accurrere. Ante adventum quippe Salvatoris, stante adhuc gentium legibus & institutis, quidam de errori servientibus accedebant, & idololatriæ nocumentis valere jussis, carnemque circumcisi, Judæorum moribus & legibus se dicabant, Ta- lium apud eos innumera multitudo visebatur. Itaque Salomon Hierosolymis templum illud augustum meditans, centum quinquaginta millia lapicidarum & operarum, proselytarumque dele- git: sic enim in Paralipomenis legimus. Sane quod tum agebatur typus erat, & adumbratio my- sterii: verum enim & undique spectabile tem- plum, puta Ecclesiam, Deo constructuri erant, non Judæi magis, quam qui ex gentibus essent, eum qui in abscondito est Judæum circumferen- tes & circumcisionem habentem, non illam, quæ in carne, sed quæ in spiritu est. Itaque ante hac adventum quidem idololatriæ ad Judæos se con- ferebant, eorumque legibus vivebant. Ast ubi postea mons Domini vere conspicuus exhibitus est, ac demonstratus, majore cupiditate ejus exar- serunt, gaudentes & dicentes: Quia de Sion exi- bit lex & verbum Domini de Hierusalem. Neque temere observat B. Lutherus aliud verbum hic de- signari, quam quod de Sinai exivit, adeoque fi- mul innui legis abrogationem, cum nova doctrina de Sion egressura dicitur in novissimo dierum. Sed quid sibi vult ratio addita, Quoniam de Zion egredietur lex & verbum Domini de Jerusalem? Hoc nimirum, ut & propriam causam cognoscamus, cur tanto nu- mero Gentes ad montem Domini confluant & disca- mus hoc verbum à verbo legis discernere. Hic enim iterum omnes hujus regni thesauros in verbum transfert. Dicit autem aliud verbum fore, quam de Sinai exivit per Mosen, Lex inquit de Zion exibit, & verbum de Jerusalem. Hic nisi percussi amentia & cæcitate Judæi essent, an non clare ostendit Propheta, hoc regnum non fore corporale? Si- quidem post illam magnificam prædicationem de confluentibus Gentibus nihil aliud dicit, quam quod Dominus docebit, & verbum, inquit egredie- tur, de Zion. Cur autem promittit novum Verbum, si illud à Mose datum valere debet? Valet qui- dem lex & debet valere ad nos docendos de obe- dientia erga Deum in hac vita; Sed de possessione futuræ vitæ non solum nihil (fidelibus) promittit ve- rum etiam spem ejus adimit, dum nos convincit, quod voluntati Dei non satisfecerimus. Hinc oritur il- lud animorum horribile periculum, ut cognita voluntate Dei ex lege, nihil quam mortem & damnationem nostram sentiamus. Implentur i- gitur animi desperatione & ira contra judicium Dei. Summa igitur Dei bonitas est, quod per Evangelium aliter nos de sua voluntate docet. In eo annuntiatur remissio peccatorum per Chri- stum. Hanc enim lege perterrefacti, accipiunt summa cum voluptate, Deum prædicant, ejus bonitatem admirantur, Misericordiæ ejus fidunt, in nomine Christi invocant, & læti promissionem futuræ vitæ expectant, Satanæ & carni suæ resi- stunt. Atque hæc omnia faciunt per Doctorem hujus verbi, quod de Zion egredietur. Sic e- nim docetur verbum hoc, ut simul Dominus ad- dat Spiritum. Hæc B. Lutherus. Quæ tamen eo ac- cipienda non sunt, ac si tantum Evangelii doctri- na hic indicaretur, sed quod ea præcipue desi- gnetur: Nam tota doctrina cœlestis voce legis notatur uti Ps. XIX. & CXIX. Ideo per verbum Domini explicatur, quod comprehendit legem & Evangelium: & judicium fieri dicitur per hanc legem, quæ aliis quidem remissionem pec- catorum, aliis vero damnationem denunciat. Nec alium sensum infert locus parallelus, in quo vati- cinii complementum habetur, Luc. XXIV. 42. Annuit his iterum Calvinus: Scimus, inquit ad h. l. Judæos venisse ad templum non modo ut adora- rent, sed etiam ut instituerentur in Lege DEI. Lex ergo tunc residebat in Sion; illic erat sacrarium cœ- lestis sapientiæ. Quid autem Propheta noster? Lex ex Sion prodibit, hoc est, longe lateque personabit: non tantum Dominus in uno angulo ostendet, quo- modo ipse coli velit: sed vocem suam procul emit- tet usque ad extremos terræ fines. Exibit ergo Lex è Sion: sicut dicitur Psalm. 110. Sceptrum potentiæ tuæ emittet DOMINUS è Sion. Il- lic metaphorice vocatur DOCTRINA CHRI- STI sceptrum, vel confertur Regio sce- ptro: quia non aliter dominatur CHRISTUS inter nos, nisi per Evangelii sui doctrinam.

Illic autem pronuntiat David sceptrum illud pro- cul emittendum esse à Deo Patre, ut scilicet Chri- stus sub se contineat omnes populos, qui prius a- lieni erant. Ita hoc loco Lex ex Sion prodibit. Conf. de hoc textu Dn. D. Mulleri Iudaism. c. XX. p. 67.

Septimo judicium Domini inter populos mul- tos & correptio gentium fortium procul dissitarum mere ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει de represione Samaritanorum, Ammonitarum, Azotiorum, Arabum, ne impedi- rent templi & urbis reparationem, explicatur. Nam de judicio Domini quod per verbum sit, non externa vi Principum aut Monarcharum hic ser- monem esse, antecedentia evincunt. Neque so- lum de represione populorum hic agitur, sed de ju- dicio vel gubernatione inter populos, quia verbum Ebræum de gubernatione adhiberi solet Ex. XIIX. 21. Jud. III. 3. atque ita Christus judicare terram dicitur Ps. XCVI. 8. Conf. Es. XLII. 1. Matth. XV. 18. aut si reddere malis, judicem agat inter populos, in- telligendum id erit è Iob. XII. 49. c. XVI. 8. quod de peccatis suis eos convincere, & annunciare de- beat, ut pœnitentiam agant Act. XVII. 3. quod lege fit Rom. II. 12. causa & actiones diriguntur ad vo- luntatem Dei ac gloriam ejusdem: Evangelio au- tem instituimur de gratia DEI in Christo: qua- propter ad judicium ejus & Lex & Evangelium pertinet: nec denique solum de paucis vel vicinis populis res est, sed de populis MULTIS, de gentibus fortibus PROCUL DISSITIS, imo quænam illæ gentes sint, quale judicium ac quomodo arguendæ sint, è superioribus manifestum est, quod nempe illæ gentes, quæ ad montem Domini adducendæ in- telligantur, quodque per verbum judicandæ & ar- guendæ sint. Suadens enim abstinere ab erroribus, ut hic Cyrillus, manifeste ostendens, eos properare ad perniciem, nisi velint recte vivere, veterumq; pecca- torum maculas abstergere, judicat & redarguit quo- dammodo, nec unam gentem duntaxat (sed usque in terram longinquam) hoc est usq; ad terminos or- bis terrarum: ubiq; enim salutis verbum prædica- tur. His addit, verba sunt B. Lutheri, Propheta quasi expositionem superiorum, ut clare doceat, quod hoc regnum, non in externa vi, aut armis, sed in verbo sit positum & quod Gentes ad id pertineant. Non erat vetitum etiam in Lege, ut convenirent Gentes Hierosolymam, sicut Naaman, Regina Saba, & sine dubio aliqui vicini Reges, ut Rex Tyri & alii. Sed Propheta hic dicit futurum, ut Rex, qui in Jerusa- lem suos cives docebit, etiam doceat magnos po- pulos, & arguat gentes fortes, longe ab Hieroso- ymis dissitas. Hoc est, quod Lucæ ultimo dicitur, Pœnitentia & remissio peccatorum prædicabitur εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη in omnes gentes, sic tamen, ut in- cipiat à Jerusalem. Porro cum scriptura etiam Gentes ad Regnum Christi accessuras dicit, non solum ab- jicit Mosen cum Politia sua, tanquam inutilem Doctorem ad æternam vitam, sed simul ostendit, Regnum Christi esse regnum gratiæ & remissio- nis peccatorum. Quid enim est esse Gentilem, quam non pertinere ad populum Dei, esse sine le- ge, vivere in peccatis, in idololatria, in impietate? Quod igitur tales ad regnum Christi vocantur, an non regnum Christi vere tale regnum est, quo non judica- tur secundum opera, sed annunciatur gratuita remis- sio peccatorum per Christum. Sicut Paulus dicit, justitiam DEI revelari in Evangelio sine lege, hoc est, in regno Christi justos haberi eos, qui carent justitia Legis, & qui peccatores sunt, si scilicet credant per CHRISTUM peccata sua sublata esse. Utitur autem Propheta significanti- bus vocabulis, cum vocat populos multos seu magnos, est enim vox (Rabbim) & gentes for- tes. Commendat enim hoc modo potentiam Verbi, quo non alia res in mundo contemptior. Et tamen huic contempto verbo, nisi credant gentes & populi, quantumvis magni & fortes, pessum ibunt, secundum sententiam: Qui non crediderit condemnabitur. Hoc periculo moventur populi & gentes, ac submit- tunt colla Evangelio, patiuntur se judicari, h. e. o- stendi & argui peccata, ea agnoscunt & credunt re- missionem: per Christum. Nam Propheta hoc in loco verbo judicandi & arguendi utitur, sicut CHRISTUS Iohan. XVI. Spiritus Sanctus ar- guet mundum de peccato, de judicio. Hoc est, in Evangelio arguentur homines, ut agnoscant in- credulitatem esse summum peccatum & docebun- tur, ut remissionem peccatorum credant per CHRISTUM donari, & ut statuant tyrannidem Satanæ fractam esse, ne possit iis nocere, qui in CHRISTUM credunt. Hæc B. Lutherus no- ster. Quibus consonant ea, quæ Calvinus habet, quæ quum faciant etiam ad explicandam Prophe- tæ mentem, non pigrabimur hic subjicere: Bifa- riam loquitur scriptura de regno Dei. Deus enim gubernat Diabolum & omnes impios, sed non verbo suo, neq́; Spiritus sanctificatione, ita fit, ut pareant Deo nolentes & inviti: sed peculiare Dei imperium pertinet ad solam Ecclesiam, ubi scilicet DEUS & verbo & spiritu suo corda flectit in obsequium, ut sponte & libenter eum sequantur, qui intus & foris edocti sunt: intus Spiritus instinctu: foris, verbi prædicatione. Ideo dicitur eodem Psalm. 110. Po- pulus tuus spontaneus tunc conveniet. Talis gubernatio DEI hic nobis describitur à Propheta. Deus igitur judicabit non ficuti judicat universum orbem, sed quia peculiari modo subjiciet sibi fide- les, ita ut nihil magis expetant quam se illi totos tradere. Cæterum quia prius subigendi sunt homi- nes, quam præstent Deo tale obsequium, diserte ad- junxit Propheta: Corripiet vel arguet populos multos. Et hæc particula diligenter notanda est, quia hinc colligimus, talem nobis ingenitam esse super- biam, ut nemo nostrum idoneus futurus sit Discipu- lus Dei, nisi qui violenter domitus fuerit. Doctrina igitur frigeret per se in tanta corruptione ingenii no- stri, nisi Dominus nos argueret, hoc est, nisi para- ret nos prius quasi violento modo. Nunc ergo te- nemus Prophetæ consilium, cur conjungat imperio Dei correctionem; nam verbum והוכיח significat interdum expostulare, arguere, significat etiam corripere. Deniq́; hic notatur malitia & perversitas carnis no- stræ, quia nunquam se offerent DEO etiam optimi quiq́; nisi prius subacti: & qualiter? nempe violen- ta correptione Dei. Hæc igitur sunt exordia regni Christi. Jam quod dicit populos robustos, hoc etiam eloquio extollit & illustrat idem regnum, de quo disserit. Et hinc etiam colligitur potentia doctrinæ, quod homines robusti sese absque ulla repugnantia offerent Deo regendos, ubi ita corre- cti fuerint. Necessaria item est correctio, sed Deus non utitur vi aliqua externa, neque armata manu cum vult sibi Ecclesiam subjicere, & tamen colli- git robustas gentes. Hinc ergo perspicitur ef- ficacia doctrinæ, nam ubi est robur, illic etiam est confidentia & fastus, deinde etiam rebellio. Quum ergo verbum absq́; aliis adjumentis ita corrigat in hominibus contumaciam, videmus quam incredibili modo operetur Deus, ubi Ecclesiam suam colligit. Cæ- terum minime dubium est, quin hæc ad CHRISTI personam debeant referri. Et postea: notan- da particula, quæ interjicitur עד רחוק tam diu- turnitatis temporis quam locorum distantia potest no- tari hac voce. Jonathan refert ad longum tempus.

Quod scilicet usq; in seculum Deus arguet populos, sed non dubito, quin Propheta hic voluerit complecti re- giones longe dissitas, ac si diceret, Deum tunc non unius tantum populi Regem fore, neque unius tantum Judææ, sed regnum ejus propagatum iri usque ad ultimos terræ fines, arguet ergo populos usque in longinquum. Hæc Calvinus, qui alias lubenter solet vaticinia de Christo pervertere.

Octavo pax & tranquillitas universalis, quam promittit Michæas, de Temporali pace intelligi ne- quit: Nunquam enim tempus fuit, quo inter o- mnes populos pax & concordia floruerit, quem- admodum hic prædictum est: Et concident gladios suos in vomeres & hastas suas in ligones, non sumet gens adversus gentem gladium, & non discent ultra belligerare. Quod Grotius accepit de populis o- mnibus, altam pacem cum Judæis culturis sub Persa- rum imperio; sed refragatur historia. Nunquam enim tantam pacem habuit gens Judæorum, & recensuit Grotius ipse proxime Samaritas, Am- monitas, Azotios, & Arabas, qui adversati populo Dei valdeg; infesti fuêre: in ipsa etiam imperato- ria aula, & per imperium Persicum insidiæ exi- tiosissimæ structuræ eidem sunt ab Hamane, aliisque hostibus, de quibus historia Esdræ, Nehemiæ & Esther. Non igitur est sentiendum, quod Prophe- ta loquatur hoc loco de publica pace in his terris, quia sicut bellatum est ante Christum natum, ita bellatum etiam est ipso nato, & bellabitur inter gentes usque ad novissimum tempus hujus seculi. Sed loquitur de ipso Christi regno & de modo, quo hoc regnum dilatabitur in orbe terrarum. Non loquitur de mundanis regnis, quæ solent bel- lo occupari, contineri, & proferri: Sed loquitur de regno Christi. Hoc enim regnum non occu- pabitur, nec proferetur bombardis, sicut mundana regna: sed proferetur pacate & tranquille. Con- flabunt (inquit) gladios suos in vomeres &c. hoc est, hi qui nomine Christi accepturi sunt regnum or- bis terræ, & subjecturi sunt Christo gentes & na- tiones, non inferent gentibus arma, ut cogant eos violenta manu Christum agnoscere: nec armabunt subditos, ut regnum Christi gladiis tueantur, sed percurrent orbem terræ inermes: non excitabunt eos, qui agnoscunt nomen Christi per fidem, ut ju- vent se armis ad subjiciendas imperio Christi reli- quas gentes, sed jubebunt unumquemque suæ vo- cationi servire, ac quantum in ipsis est, publicæ paci & tranquillitati studere, non instituent scho- las, in quibus tyrones exerceantur ad militiam mundanam: sicut Principes & Reges hujus terræ facere solent. Sed instituent scholas in quibus au- ditores discant militiam Spiritualem adversus pec- cata, mortem & infernum, ut ad Es. II. habet Dn. Brentius. Neque solum respicitur modus propagan- di regnum Christi, sed etiam status pacificus in Christi regno. Quo de B. Lutherus: De tali pace Propheta hic loquitur, qua corda liberantur metu corporis & judicii Dei, per Evangelium de Filio Dei tradito pro- pter peccata nostra. Quia autem per Evangelium ex- æquantur omnes (Sicut enim Deus sub peccatum o- mnia conclusit, ita etiam omnium vult misereri) sequitur ex hac exæquatione etiam pax externa inter Ecclesiæ membra, nec manet amplius acerrimum illud odium, quod fuit inter Judæos & gentes, stante adhuc maceria legis. Quid enim aut Judæus se præferat gen- tili, aut gentilis Judæo, cum Jesus Christus Filius Dei æqua & communis omnium possessio sit? Cum omnes simus baptizati in mortem Christi, & vivamus in spe æternæ vitæ per Christum conse- quendæ? Fit igitur, ut qui ante cognitum Evange- lium, odio isto tanquam acutis gladiis & venenatis telis usi sunt, hi nunc inter se concordes vivant, & u- tantur illa sancta concordia, tanquam vomeribus & falcibus ad secandos & metendos nobiles illos fru- ctus fidei, erudiendo alios quoque ad justitiam, & in- vitando eos pietate & inculpatis moribus, ad cogno- scenda & consequenda beneficia, quæ Evangelium nobis per filium Dei ostendit exhibita esse. Ideo ad- dit Propheta, non elevabit gens gladium contra gentem, nec erit amplius studium belli, hoc est, erit summa animorum inter se conjunctio, postquam homines hoc modo agnoscunt Christum, & per remissionem peccatorum corda pacata sunt. Non studebunt amplius bello, hoc est, non solum non nocebunt aliis, sed omni genere officiorum inter se utentur, re & opera juvabunt fratres, ac præcipue illa eximia præstabunt, ut doceant rudes, ut admoneant incautos, ut castigent ignavos, ut consolentur pavidos, ut exhortentur periclitantes, ut confirment infirmos &c. Hæc enim officia in Ecclesia debent esse perpetua. Nihil itaque hic præsidii habent Anabaptistæ; si quis ita sacrarum rerum imperitus est, ut hæc eo accommodet, ne Christiano aut arma gerere aut iis legitime uti liceat, in sententiam Prophetæ ineptissime perver- tit. Nam transfert sententiam à Christi regno Spiri- tuali ad regnum corporale. Idque contra mani- festam scripturam, quæ Magistratui necessitatem imponit, defendendi subditos ab injusta vi, & cu- stodiendæ pacis. Sicut Abraham armis defendit Lot, & regum historiæ ostendunt, non solum maxi- ma bella gessisse pios Reges, sed etiam consilia eorum fortunasse Deum. Et manifesta senten- tia est in Concione Johannis de pœnitentia, ubi jubet milites contentos esse stipendiis suis. Probat enim armorum legitimum usum, vel concessum vel mandatum à Magistratu, nec jubet abjicere arma. Vera igitur hujus loci sententia est, quod Propheta figurate loquatur de fructu, qui Evange- lium in Gentes vulgatum sequitur. De quo etiam monuit Brentius: Non est autem sentiendum, quod cum dicitur conflabunt gladios suos in vo- meres, & Apostoli, quorum officium erat, regno Christi subjicere populos, jusserint legitimum ma- gistratum deponere, & non exercere subditos ad prælium: sed quod ipsi ad accipiendum regnum nomine Christi non sint corporalibus armis usi, nec hortati sint subditos suos, hoc est, credentes Evangelio suo, ut sumant nomine Christi arma: interim vero jusserunt unumquemque postquam cre- didisset in Christum, suæ legitimæ vocationi diligenter & ex fide servire. Itaque si quis Princeps aut Cen- turio factus est auditor Evangelii Christi, & dedit nomen suum Christo, justus quidem fuit quantum ad Christianismum attinet, gladium suum in vome- res convertere, hoc est, operam dare publicæ paci & tranquillitati: quantum autem attinet ad offici- um ejus, justus fuit vomeres in gladios mutare, hoc est, tueri subditos suos, & defendere eos ab ho- stibus & latronibus. Nam hæc est vocatio Magistra- tus. Si quis opifex aut agricola agnovit Christum per fidem, justus fuit & hic conflare gladium suum in vomerem, & suam vocationem in tranquillitate, quantum quidem ad Christianismum attinet, se- ctari: sed quantum attinet ad officium civis, qui est in corporalibus rebus subjectus mundano impe- rio, justus fuit gladium, si Magistratus mandaverit, gestare. Doctrina enim Evangelii, qua regnum Christi in terris accipitur & dilatatur, non mutat aut in- vertit, quantum in ipsa est, externum statum mun- danorum imperiorum, & earum rerum, quæ ad il- la legitime conservanda pertinent, sed exponit ma- jestatem Christi spiritualem, qua offertur nobis re- missio peccatorum, justitia coram DEO, & vita æterna, jubens interim unumquemque, ea officia ex fide facere, ad quæ in his mundanis regnis vocatus est.

Nono securitas ea hic promittitur à Prophe- ta in illa alta pace, quæ omnem prorfus terrorem & metum excludit, qualis in nullo terreno regno unquam expectanda est. Quodnam enim re- gnum adeo tranquillum fuit, aut futurum est, ut ne quidem metus aut terror hostis alicujus locum habeat, ut hic promissum est; Et sedebit UNUS- QUISQUE sub vite sua, & sub ficu sua, NEC ERIT QUI EOS TERREAT. Quapropter necessum est, spiritualiter hæc intelligi. Significant hæc quoque, inquit B. Lutherus noster, summam tranquillitatem, quâ animi fruentur, qui in ista Evangelii prædicatione acquiescunt. Et tamen videtur Propheta singulari consilio primum vo- luisse uti non tantum specie arborum, deinde ta- libus arboribus, quæ & fœcundissimæ sunt & propter fructum solum, non propter umbram aut speciem coluntur. Nam & in Ecclesiæ variæ sunt functiones, & officia varia, & nullus Christia- nus est, quin in suo genere sit tanquam fœcunda vitis seu ficus. Diversa officia sunt, docere Eccle- sias, & administrare gladium, sicut diversæ spe- cies sunt, vitis & ficus. Et tamen utraque habent suos pulcherrimos fructus. Additur autem βε- βαιώσεως ergo: QUONIAM OS DOMINI ZEBAOTH LOQUUTUM EST, tanquam confirmatio tam magnificæ promissionis Christi, qua, monente B. Luthero, opus erat propter illud in- gens scandalum vastitatis & captivitatis regni Ju- da: Videbatur enim non solum exitium toti po- pulo & religioni imminere, sed etiam in dubium revocari promissio de regno Christi. Consola- tur igitur Propheta pios, ut in illa publica calami- tate magno sint animo, & se consolentur certa spe regni Christi futuri, in quo & remissionem pec- catorum & vitam æternam, hoc est, summam pa- cem & securitatem, omnes consecuturi sint, qui in Jesum Christum credunt. Nam os Domini Ze- baoth hæc locutum est.

Decimo de Ecclesia perpetuo conservanda ser- monem esse Propheta significat, cum ait, nos autem ambulabimus in nomine Domini IN SECULUM ET IN PERPETUUM. Vulgata perperam & inconvenienter reddidit IN ÆTERNUM ET ULTRA. Nam quid hoc est ultra æternitatem? Sed sensum ipsum pervertit Grotius, dum ad u- nius hominis ætatem hoc refert: nam ubi voci לעולם conjungitur ועד, non longum tempus, non seculum erit ætas hominis, sed æternitas designatur interminabilis. Et quodnam illud Ecclesiæ sola- tium foret, conservatum iri eandem ad unius ho- minis ætatem & ultra? Annon promissa ei est per- petua conservatio usq́; ad consummationem seculi, imo in omnem æternitatem? Nam uti hic ambu- lamus per fidem, ita fidem olim secutura est beata visio 2. Cor. V. Quod autem hic dicitur, o- mnes populi ambulabunt, unusquisque in nomine Dei sui, id non videtur cum superioribus, quod omnes confluxuri sint ad montem Sion, congruere. Grotius hæc in præsenti reddit: Ambulant in no- mine deorum suorum, additque: Sensus est: non mirum est, Deum tam singularem nostri habere cu- ram: nam cæteræ gentes ad res agendas deos suos in- vocant. Loquitur de gentibus secundum longe ma- jorem earum partem, nam veri numinis cultores in- ter eas erant paucissimi. Sed etiamsi in futuro red- datur, ac tempora novissima spectentur, conciliari hæc facile possunt cum præcedentibus, uti B. Lu- therus docuit. Nam utut promittatur vocatio u- niversalis omnium gentium & conversio multorum populorum ad verum Deum, non tamen cessabit in orbe idololatria & falsus cultus: Quomodo au- tem convenit id quod supra dixit, Gentes & popu- los multos venturos, cum eo quod nunc addit, sin- gulos populos ambulaturos in nomine sui Dei? Re- spicit Propheta ad Satanæ & mundi malitiam. Sicut enim cum Christus hujus regni præco esset, impii Judæi, Pharisæi, Sacerdotes, Reges à Satana con- citabantur contra Christum, & Apostolos, ita semper in mundo accidit. Nunquam hoc ver- bum regni Christi prædicatum est, quin alii se op- ponerent, quin alii alios Deos & religionem a- liam sequerentur. Sicut Christus quoque osten- dit, cum dicit: Pauperes Evangelizantur. Item si meum verbum servaverunt, etiam vestrum serva- bunt. Pertinet igitur particula hæc ad docendam Ecclesiam, & præmonendam de scandalo. Quod ubicunque hoc regnum in mundo est, ibi etiam e- runt, qui hunc Deum nolint sequi, & glorientur de aliis Diis, de alia religione & cultibus aliis. Imo quod semper erunt, qui veram Ecclesiam da- mnabunt, tanquam quæ non habeat Deum. Sic enim singulæ gentes ambulant in nomine Dei sui, ut diversa sequentes judicent esse impios.

Undecimo, congregatio illa claudicantis ple- bis Israëliticæ, super quam Dominus in æternum regnaturus, non aliter intelligi potest, quam de congregatione ad Ecclesiam Christi, facta sub Nov. Test. Nunquam enim Israëlitæ ad Judai- cum populum iterum congregati, & cum eodem uniti sunt, sicuti hic Michæas prædixit. Optime hic B. Lutherus: usitatum est in Prophetis, mulie- ris nomine appellare Gentem vel populum. Hæc igitur claudicans & projecta mulier est Domus Israel, quam Propheta supra cap. 2. sic dicit projicien- dam & dissipandam in gentes, ut & amplius non sit pars in sorte Domini, hoc est, ut stante illa Repu- blica & cultu Mosaico, non sit reditura in terram suam. Vocat autem (Hazoleah) claudicantem, sive ob sterilitatem, quod quibus os fœmoris loco motum est, parum sint aptæ ad partum, sive quod domus Israel (sicut Elias quoque loquitur) post- quam se à regno Judæ avulsit, in perpetua idolo- latria vixerit, nec recte incesserit in cultu Dei di- vinitus instituto. Et hæc appellatio ostendit causam calamitatis, quod propter idololatriam regnum Israel vastatum sit. Necessaria itaque hæc consolatio fuit. Quod etsi spes, redeundi ad populum Judæo- rum, præcisa esset, tamen audiunt se non ideo ex- cludendos esse à regno Christi. Vult itaque Prophe- ta, ut non solum respiciant in præsentem vasta- tionem, quam Assyrius erat allaturus, ut colle- cti ad Ecclesiam promisso semine fruerentur & æternis bonis per semen Ecclesiæ fidelium partis. Hæc tanta sunt, ut facile fuerit bonis incom- moda præsentis captivitatis & vastationis fer- re. Quis enim in certa spe æternorum bo- norum non facile patiatur temporalia sibi adi- mi? Sed hæc tantum fidelium consolatio fuit. Major autem pars fuerunt impii, qui & promissiones Spiritualis liberationis neglexe- runt, & cupiditate corporalium commodorum, non inviti se adjunxerunt gentibus, sicque im- pietate perierunt. Porro hic locus clare expli- cat aliorum Prophetarum obscuriores sententias de restitutione decem tribuum Israel. Quia enim diserte dicit restituendas esse, postquam regnum Christi in Jerusalem cœpit, & gentes Evange- lium amplexæ sunt, sine dubio restitutio talis e- rit, quale hoc regnum est, nempe non corpo- ralis, qualem somniant adhuc Judæi, sed spiritua- lis. Quod Evangelio inter gentes prædicato e- tiam ipsi credent, & participes efficientur bene- ficiorum Christi, per fidem in Christum. Ac secundum hanc sententiam etiam intelligenda sunt, quæ sequuntur: Et faciam ut claudicans ha- beat posteritatem, & ut infirma crescat in gentem robustam. Et regnabit Dominus super eos in monte Zion, à modo usq́; in seculum. Non hoc vult, quod potentiam & opes assequentur. Sicut enim Rex hujus Regni pauper, & calamitosus in hac vita fuit: Ita etiam pauperes & calamitosi erunt in hac vita, quotquot in eum credunt. Frustra igitur Judæi expectant corporalem dominationem. Omnis gloria hujus Regis & subditorum in eo erit, quod cum Rege suo in æternum vivent. Est enim hoc in loco primum insigne testimonium, quod caput hujus Regni, Christus, sit verus Deus, tribuit enim ei nomen veri Dei (Jehova.) Deinde etiam est testimonium clarum de resurrectione mortuorum & alia vita post hanc vitam. Si enim Dominus regnavit super eos, non solum in hac vita, sed & in æternum, profecto necesse est, eos in æternum vivere. Deus enim est Deus non mortuorum, sed viventium. Et cur prædicaretur hic tam ma- gnifice regnum in mortuos, qui nihil sunt? Si re- gnum est, est vivorum regnum. Sicut igitur necesse est, omnes homines semel mori: ita hu- jus regni ea vis est, ut in eo mortui vivant iterum, & non moriantur, sicut hæc in Novo Testamento clarius dicuntur: Qui credit in me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet. Item: Ut omnis, qui credit in Filium Dei, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Hanc consolationem desertæ & abjectæ domui Israel proponit, ut spe horum æternorum bonorum se erigant, & vincant corporalia incommoda, quæ peccatis suis meruerunt. Theodoretius hæc ita in- terpretatur: Contritam & ejectam, animas pietati servientes vocat, propter quas unigenitum DEI ver- bum carnis assumtione humana in terra visum, cum hominibus versatum est, ipsumq; horum testis est ad Judæos verba faciens: non est opus Medico valenti- bus, sed male habentibus. Et, non veni vocare justos, sed peccatores ad pœnitentiam. Idcirco Publicanum, & meretricem, & latronem, atque ejusmodi congregans, & eorum mores in melius com- mutans, Ecclesiam Sanctam constituit, eis imperans ex hoc nunc usque in seculum. De cætero vo- ces ipsas non male explicat Grotius, sed quum in superioribus sensum corruperit, totam Prophetæ sententiam pervertit. Ita habet de versu 6. 7.

## 4:6
Vers. 6.

IN THAT DAY] At that same time. I WILL ASSEMBLE HER THAT HALTETH] The LXX [translate it as] 'the broken one,' for which Justin cites 'the oppressed one,' namely, the people. To halt (צָלַע) is said by the Hebrews even of one who, pressed by a burden, cannot walk straight, Psalm 35:15, 38:18; therefore, the Greeks translate the noun derived from it sometimes as 'weakness,' sometimes as 'scourge'.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

IN DIE ILLA] Eodem illo tempore. CONGREGABO CLAUDICANTEM] LXX. τὴν συντεθριμμένην, pro quo Justinus citat τὴν ἐκτεθλιμμένην ple- bem scilicet. Claudicare צָלַע Hebræis dicitur etiam qui onere pressus recta nequit incedere Psalm. XXXV. 15. XXXVIII. 18. itaque nomen inde deductum modo ἀσθέ- νειαν, modo μάσιγα vertunt Græci.

## 4:7
Vers. 7.

AND I WILL MAKE HER THAT HALTETH A REMNANT] I will give to those afflicted ones a progeny. AND THE LORD SHALL REIGN OVER THEM] They shall live freely according to the laws of God, with no one hindering them. See Obadiah 20:1.

Calvin explained these latter parts concerning the kingdom of the Lord more correctly; the Prophet expresses here some distinction between that shadowy kingdom and the later new one, which God was about to make manifest by the arrival of the Messiah. Jehovah, therefore, himself shall reign over them: as if he were saying, hitherto indeed, when the descendants of David held the empire, because God himself had created both David and his sons, and they had been anointed by his name and command, this could be considered his kingdom, although he governed his own people mediately through the ministry and work of men: but now God himself shall ascend the throne in a conspicuous form, so that no one may doubt that he himself is the King of his people. And this was truly and solidly fulfilled in the person of Christ. For although Christ was the true seed of David, yet at the same time he was also Jehovah, namely, God manifested in the flesh.
