Therefore we see how this Prophet extols the glory of the kingdom of Christ with a magnificent eulogy: as if he were saying, it will not be shadowy, as it had been under the law. Jehovah, therefore, shall reign over them. As for the place of the kingdom, in Zion, B. Luther, whom Calvin has followed in most things concerning this Prophet, expresses the same sentiment for the most part in other words: What is it that he says: 'he shall reign over them in mount Zion'? Why does he name a corporal place, if this restoration is spiritual and not also corporal? This is the reason why the Jews still expect a corporal restoration, inasmuch as the Prophets mention corporal places. And the Doctors also sometimes fall into these carnal opinions. But if anyone looks at the words of the Prophet, it agrees beautifully with experience. For the reality shows that Zion has been overturned and utterly devastated; in vain, therefore, is the restoration of a corporal place and people expected. Nor does the Prophet speak of a corporal Zion: for he speaks of such a Zion that might endure forever: He does not, therefore, speak of stones and wood, but of Zion, that is, of that people who believe in the word which began to be spread first in Zion, and is thus saved. This people, this Church of those who believe in Christ, is that eternal Zion over which the Lord shall reign. Just as the Prophets also elsewhere use the name Jerusalem for this very sentiment, for that people who believe in the word which was first preached in Jerusalem. And Theodoret, long ago, refuted the Grotian gloss among the Jews and those who Judaize from these words: 'And the Lord shall reign over them in the mount, from henceforth even for ever.' If, of course, the kingdom of the Jews had remained in Zion, and they were cared for by the constant eternal providence of God, the Jews would rightly seize this prophecy for themselves, and, having interpreted these things similarly as they are accustomed to do, they would agree with them. But if the kingdom of the Jews has long since been extinguished, and they, living very far from Jerusalem, serve in the ends of the earth, and have been stripped of the providence of God: let them not, therefore, offer their trifles to us any longer, and let the Doctors of truth support the truth.

Twelfth, the prophecy of Eder, the tower of the daughter of Zion, which is joined to this, also agrees with this interpretation concerning the kingdom of the Messiah, in which he promises spiritual beauty again even to the Jews in the times of the New Testament. Just as he has hitherto promised the limping Israelite woman a congregation, and offspring, and multiplication, and spiritual happiness, of which more later. Now it seems only to remain that we add some supporting evidence to our interpretation. Justin in his Dialogue with Trypho, p. 262, not only interprets this passage concerning Christ, but also teaches that the Jews themselves interpret it thus: Furthermore, that it was predicted by prophecy; that the nations, having been led astray by error from their depravity in which they lived, would recover their minds through repentance, and would perform penance, after they had heard the word suffered by them from his Apostles even from Jerusalem:

Bear with me, I pray, while I cite a few words from the Prophecy of Micah, one of the twelve; they are of this kind: & it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest &c. These things finished, I proceeded to say: I know, O men, that your masters confess all the words of this passage, that they were spoken concerning CHRIST: and I also know that they affirm that he has not yet come. And in Apology II for the Christians, page 60, he has this to say concerning this oracle: But when the prophetic Spirit speaks as if prophesying what things are to come, he speaks thus: for out of Zion shall go forth the law &c. And that this has been done in this way, you can be persuaded to believe and be taught. For twelve men went forth from Jerusalem into the world, and they indeed unlearned, and by no means eloquent: but by the power of God they announced to every race of men that they were sent by CHRIST to teach all men the word of God. Therefore, we who formerly engaged in mutual slaughter, not only do not attack our enemies, but even (that we may not lie, nor deceive our inquisitors) very willingly confessing CHRIST, we even face death: although we could indeed usurp and do in this matter that which has been said: The tongue has sworn, but the mind is unsworn. Irenaeus, book IV against Heresies, chapter LXVII, says: From the coming of the Lord, the New Testament reconciling to peace, and the life-giving Law went forth into the universal earth, just as the Prophets said, for out of Zion shall proceed the Law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, and he shall judge many people, and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles, and they shall no longer learn to fight. If, therefore, another law and word going forth from Jerusalem made such peace among those nations which received it, and through them reproves a people much given to imprudence, it seems a consequence that the Prophets spoke of another. But if the law of liberty, that is, the word of God, announced by the Apostles who went out from Jerusalem, brought the universal earth into such a transformation that they fashioned their swords and warlike spears into plowshares, and changed those which he gave for reaping grain into peaceful instruments, and now they do not know how to fight, but being struck even offer the other cheek, the Prophets did not speak these things of another, but of him who did them. And this is our Lord. Tertullian, book III against Marcion, chapter XXI, p. 398. Moreover, the calling of the Nations has arisen from the last days. In the same words Isaiah, and it shall be, he says, in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, that is, the sublimity of God, and the house of God above the tops of the mountains, that is, Christ the catholic temple of God, in whom God is worshipped, established above all eminences of virtues and powers. And all Nations come to him, and many shall go, and shall say: Come let us ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and into the house of the God of Jacob, and he shall announce to you his way, and we shall walk in it. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. This shall be his way, the Gospel of the new law, and of the new word in Christ, now no longer in Moses. And he shall judge between the Nations, concerning their error, that is to say. And he shall convict a large people, especially the Jews themselves and the proselytes. And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into sickles, that is, the devices of harmful minds and hostile tongues, and of all malice and blasphemy, they shall convert into studies of modesty and peace. And nation shall not take up sword against nation, that is, of discord, and they shall no longer learn to wage war, that is, to carry out enmities, so that here too you may learn that Christ was promised not as a warrior, but as a peacemaker. But the Prophet denies these things, when they are seen to be present, or are read as fulfilled. Or if you do not deny both, they will be fulfilled in him in whom they were prophesied. For look even now at the very entry and course of the calling into the Nations from the last days approaching the God creator, not into the proselytes, whose calling is rather from the first days. For the Apostles introduced this faith. Origen, book V against Celsus, p. 739. We individually come in the last days, after the advent of our Jesus, into the conspicuous mountain of the Lord, the word more sublime than every word, and into the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and base of truth: let us contemplate how this has been built upon the tops of the mountains, all the prophetic discourses, which are its foundations. But this House is exalted above all the hills, which seem to promise something excellent in wisdom and truth among men. To this mountain we all nations hasten, in a column exhorting one another to embrace the religion of Jesus Christ which has shone forth in these last days, and saying, come let us ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and into the house of the God of Jacob: and he shall announce to us his way, and we shall walk in it. For the law went forth from Zion, and migrated to us spiritually. The word of the Lord also went forth from that Jerusalem, that it might be distributed into all lands, and to judge in the midst of the nations, by choosing as many as would show themselves compliant, and by reproving the refractory crowd. But to those asking whence we come, or what leader we follow: we answer that we come at the command of Jesus, that we may recast our rational warlike and savage swords into plowshares, and from our formerly pugnacious spears make sickles. For now we do not take up the sword against any nation, nor do we learn to wage war, having been made sons of peace through Jesus, whom we prefer to follow rather than the institutions of our fathers, in which while we remained, we were strangers to the covenants: now having received the law, giving thanks to the liberator &c. Athanasius, On the Incarnation of the Word of God, Vol. 1 of works, p. 106. Who joined in peace peoples hostile to one another? unless the beloved Son of God, that common Savior of all, Jesus Christ, who by his own charity endured all things for our salvation. For oracles concerning peace of this kind, which he was about to procure, were also published long ago: he shall beat (says the scripture) their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks, neither shall nation take up sword against nation, nor is it so that they shall learn war hereafter. Nor is that incredible, since even now barbarians of savage customs, and sacrificing to idols at this time, rage against themselves, nor can they endure to live without arms for even one hour: yet the same people, when they hear the doctrine of Christ, immediately turn from war to agriculture, and instead of wielding swords, extend their hands to prayers: and instead of mutual wars among themselves, they are armed against demons with modesty and virtue of soul. Cyril of Alexandria in his Commentary on this passage. In the very words now, the prediction of the Church to be gathered from the nations appears clearly. For with Israel according to the flesh as it were taken from the midst, and the sacrifices prescribed in the law ceasing: likewise with the priesthood of the Levitical family deserted, and that temple itself, famous for its renown, burned down, and Jerusalem destroyed, Christ instituted the Church from the nations, and as it were in the last time, that is, at the end of this Age, for then he became like us. Therefore he calls the Church a mountain, (which is the house of the living God.) Truly sublime, since there is nothing at all humble or depressed in it; but the knowledge of divine dogmas is raised on high. Furthermore, the very life of those justified in Christ, and the sancti fied in the spirit is built high. Theodoret on this passage not only approves our opinion, but also gravely refutes the Jews and those Judaizing, who interpret these things concerning the return from Babylon: The Evangelical and divine proclamation has reached and flowed through to the ends of the earth according to the Lord's prediction, which is held in the sacred Gospels: and this Gospel, he says, shall be preached to all nations as a testimony. Then he also commanded the Apostles, saying: Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: teaching them to observe all things, whatsoever I have commanded you. This Evangelical law and Apostolic word, when it had begun from Jerusalem as if from some fountain, has spread through the whole world, bringing irrigation to those approaching with faith. But nevertheless, the Jews do not think these things are to be understood in this way, but that these very things are a prediction concerning the return from Babylon. And certainly it is no wonder that those filled with stupidity understand it thus: for in their other impieties, aberration from this prophecy also fits. But that certain pious Doctors have inserted the same interpretation into their writings seems to me not to be borne, nor worthy of pardon. What nations, both neighboring and living furthest away, ran to the temple of the Jews after their return to receive their laws? to embrace the word proceeding from there? among which nations or peoples did the word of the Lord thus judge, reproving their evil deeds? And those things which follow thereafter openly refute the falsity of that interpretation: for after the return from Babylon, as it also seems to those who have interpreted it thus, both Gog and Magog, with very many nations, waged war against the Jews: and all the neighbors besides continually waged wars with them. On this side indeed the Idumeans, and Ammonites, and Moabites: on that side truly the foreign nations, and the Samaritans: and not long after that time, disasters were brought upon them by the Macedonians, which the books of the Maccabees encompass. But in this place the prophetic discourse promises the deepest peace. Jerome also subscribes to this interpretation in his Commentary on this passage; other ancient interpreters subscribe; nor is it easily found among the more recent, whether Pontifical, or Reformed, or our own, who has not acknowledged that this prophecy is to be understood concerning the times of the New Testament. What of the fact that among

some of the Jews themselves refer these things to the times of the Messiah: which Justin recalled to the mind of Trypho. R. Eliezer in the Talmud in the book Sabbath, distinct. Bemah Ischoah, interprets these things concerning the days of the Messiah; Aben Ezra on this passage. And they shall flow unto him. From that place until the end of the book he speaks on the subject of the Messiah, and concerning the impious, who will act impiously in the heels of the Messiah or his successors, just as our Masters. And the Messiah himself shall judge between many peoples. Finally, it is known that the Jews, from the fact that these things, which they understand according to the letter, have not yet been completed, contend that the Messiah has not yet come, holding it for certain and indubitable that this concerns the times of the Messiah, on which see Raimund Martini, Pugio Fidei, part II, C. XII. Lord Dr. Tarnovius on this passage and Lord Dr. Müller in his Judaism. C. XVII. p. 512. against R. Isaac Ben Abraham, where the Rule of the Rabbis is to be observed, that the prophecies of the Prophets concerning the kingdom of the Messiah are to be understood אלחי Elahi Spiritually לאגשמי and not Gaschmi corporally, and the Admonition of Rab. Mos. Maimon, page 11, More Nevuchim, C. XXIX, that the oracles of the Prophets and especially of Isaiah are not always to be explained according to the letter, but figuratively and metaphorically. Compare Joel III. 10. Am. IX. 11. 12. 13. Obad. v. last. Zach. III. 13. Joh. IX.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET PONAM CLAUDICANTEM IN RELI- QUIAS] Dabo illis afflictiis progeniem. ET REGNABIT DOMINUS SUPER EOS] Li- bere vivent secundum Dei leges nemine prohibente. Vi- de Abdiam XX. 1.

Rectius hæc posteriora de regno Domini Calvi- nus exposuit; Propheta exprimit hic aliquod di- scrimen inter umbratile illud regnum, & posterius novum, quod adventu Messiæ Deus palam facturus erat. Jehova ergo ipse regnabit super eos: ac si diceret, hactenus quidem, ubi imperium tenuerunt posteri Davidis, quia Deus ipse creaverat & Davi- dem & ejus filios, & uncti fuerant ejus nomine & mandato, potuit censeri hoc ejus regnum, quam- vis mediate gubernaret suos hominum ministerio & opera: sed nunc Deus ipse conspicua forma conscendet solium, ita ut nemo dubitet ipsum es- se Regem populi sui. Et hoc vere ac solide imple- tum fuit in Christi persona. Tametsi enim Christus fuit verum semen Davidis, tamen simul etiam fuit Jehova, nempe Deus manifestatus in carne. Ergo vide- mus ut hic Propheta magnifico elogio extollat gloriam regni Christi: ac si diceret, non fore umbratile, sicuti sub lege fuerat. Jehova ergo regnabit super eos. Quod ad locum regni, in Sion, optime B. Luthe- rus, quem super hunc Prophetam in plerisque se- quutus est Calvinus, aliis verbis eandem maximam partem exprimens sententiam: Quid est, quod di- cit: regnabit super eos in monte Zion? cur nomi- nat corporalem locum, si haec restitutio spiritua- lis, & non etiam corporalis est? haec causa est, cur Judaei adhuc corporalem restitutionem exspe- ctent, siquidem Prophetae corporalium locorum meminerunt. Et Doctores alicubi etiam in has carnales opiniones delabuntur. Sed si quis Pro- phetae verba videat, pulchre cum experientia con- venit. Res enim ostendit Zion eversam & fun- ditus vastatam esse, frustra igitur expectatur cor- poralis loci & populi restitutio. Nec Propheta de corporali Zion loquitur: loquitur enim de ta- li Zion, quae duret in aeternum: Non igitur de la- pidibus & lignis loquitur, sed de Zion, hoc est, de illo populo, qui verbo, quod in Zion primum spargi coepit, credit, & sic salvatur. Hic populus, haec Ecclesia credentium in Christum, est illa ae- terna Zion, super quam regnabit Dominus. Si- cut etiam Prophetae alicubi in hanc ipsam sententiam utuntur nomine Jerusalem, pro eo populo, qui verbo quod in Jerusalem primum praedicatum est, credit. Et refutavit ex his verbis jam olim glos- sam Grotianam in Judaeis & judaizantibus Theodo- retus: Et regnabit Dominus super eos in monte, ex hoc nunc & usque in seculum. Si nimirum Judaeorum regnum in Sion permansisset, & assidua ae- terna Dei procuratione curarentur, jure Judaei hanc si- bi prophetiam arriperent, & merito similiter haec interpretati, ut solent Iudaei, cum illis consentirent. Sin autem Judaeorum regnum dudum extinctum est, longissime habitantes ab Hierusalem, serviunt in ex- tremis terris, atq; Dei procuratione denudati sunt: ne idcirco amplius nugas suas nobis proferant, veri- tatisq; Doctores veritati patrocinentur.

Duodecimo consonat huic interpretationi de regno Messiae etiam subjunctum vaticinium Eder, turri filia Zion caliginosa, quo spiritualem decorem etiam Judaeis denuo promittit sub tem- pora Nov. Test. Uti hactenus claudicanti mulieri Israeliticae congregationem, & sobolem, & mul- tiplicationem ac felicitatem spiritualem pollici- tus est, de quo postea. Jam id tantum super- esse videtur, ut suffragia nostrae interpretationi nonnulla adjiciamus. Justinus in dial. cum Tryph. p. m. 262. non tantum de Christo interpretatur hunc locum, sed Judaeos etiam ipsos ita interpre- tari docet: Ceterum quod vaticinio praedictum sit; gentes a vitiositate sua, in qua errore transversim abductae vixerunt, per resipiscentiam mentem re- cepturas, & poenitentiam acturas esse, post- quam ex Apostolis ejus praedicantibus ab ipsis usque Hierosolymis verbum passum audissent:

pauca verba ex Prophetia Michææ, unius è duodecim, me referentem sustinete; ea sunt bujusmodi: & e- rit in extremis diebus præclarus mons Domini &c. His finitis, dicere perrexi: Magistros vestros, ô viri, verba loci hujus omnia confiteri, quod de CHRISTO dicta sint, scio: & eosdem quod nondum venerit, af- firmare, id quoque scio. Et Apolog. II. pro Chri- stian. pag. 60. ita de hoc oraculo habet: Quan- do verò veluti vaticinans quæ futura sint, verba fa- cit Spiritus propheticus, ita loquitur: ex Zion e- nim egredietur lex &c. Et quod hoc sic factum sit, persuaderi ad credendum docerique pote- stis. Nam Hierosolymis duodecim viri profe- cti sunt in mundum, atque ii quidem indocti, mi- nime eloquentes: Dei autem virtute omni ho- minum generi denunciarunt à CHRISTO missos se esse, qui cunctos verbum Dei docerent. Pro- inde qui olim mutuis inter nos grassati sumus cæ- dibus, non modo ne inimicos quidem oppugna- mus, verum etiam (ut non mentiamur, neque in- quisitores nostros fallamus) perlibenter CHRI- STUM confitentes, mortem quoque adimus: cum quidem illud, quod dictum est. Jurata lingua, animus sed injuratus est. hac in re usurpare & facere possemus. Irenæus lib. IV. advers. Hæres. cap. LXVII. A Domini, in- quit, adventu Novum Testamentum ad pacem recon- cilians, & vivificatrix Lex in universalem exivit ter- ram, quemadmodum dixerunt Prophetæ, ex Sion enim procedet Lex, & verbum Domini de Hie- rusalem, & arguet populum multum, & conci- dent gladios suos in aratra, & lanceas in falces, & jam non discent pugnare. Si igitur alia lex, & verbum exiens ab Hierusalem tantam pacem fe- cit apud eas gentes, quæ eam receperunt, & per eas arguit imprudentiæ multum populum, vide- tur consequens de altero dixisse Prophetas. Si au- tem libertatis lex, id est, verbum Dei, ab Aposto- lis, qui ab Hierusalem exierunt, annunciatum, u- niversalem terram in tantam transmutationem fecit, ut gladios & lanceas bellatorias in aratra fa- bricaverunt ipsi, & in falces, quas donavit ad me- tendum frumentum in organa pacifica demutave- runt, & jam nesciunt pugnare, sed percussi & alte- ram præbent maxillam, non de alio Prophetæ di- xerunt hæc, sed de eo, qui fecit ea. Hic autem est Dominus noster. Tertullian. lib. III. contra Mar- cionit. c. XXI. p. 398. Cæterum allectio Nationum à novissimis diebus exorta est. Iisdem verbis Esaias, & erit, inquit, in novissimis diebus manifestus mons Domini, utique sublimitas Dei, & ædes Dei super summos montes, utique Christus catholicum Dei templum, in quo Deus colitur, constitutum super omnes eminentias virtutum & potestatum. Et ve- niunt ad eum universæ Nationes, & ibunt multi, & dicent: Venite ascendamus in montem Domini, & in ædem Dei Jacob, & annunciabit vobis viam suam, & incedemus in ea. Ex Sion enim ex- ibit lex, & sermo Domini ex Hierusalem. Hæc erit via sua novæ legis Evangelium, & novi sermo- nis in Christo jam non in Moyse. Et judicabit inter Nationes, de errore scilicet earum. Et re- vincent populum amplum, ipsorum inprimis Ju- dæorum & proselytorum. Et concident machæ- ras suas in aratra, & sibynas in falces, id est, animo- rum nocentium & linguarum infestarum, & omnis maltitiæ atque blasphemiæ ingenia, convertent in studia modestiæ & pacis. Et non accipiet gens super gentem machæram, utique discordiæ & non discent amplius bellare, id est, inimicitias persice- re, ut & hic discas, Christum non bellipotentem, sed paciferum repromissum. Hæc autem Pro- pheta negat, quum coram videntur, aut adimple- ta leguntur. Aut si non negas utrumque, in eo erunt adimpleta, in quem sunt prophetata. Inspi- ce enim adhuc etiam ipsum introgressum, atque decursum vocationis in Nationes à novissimis die- bus adeuntes ad Deum creatorem, non in prosely- tos, quorum à primis magis diebus allectio est. Etenim fidem istam Apostoli induxerunt. Ori- genes l. V. contra Celsum p. 739. Nos singuli veni- mus in extremis diebus, post adventum Jesu no- stri, in conspicuum montem Domini, verbum o- mni verbo sublimius, & in domum Dei, quae est Ecclesia Dei viventis, columna & basis veritatis: hanc contemplemur quomodo aedificata sit in summis montibus, omnibus propheticis sermoni- bus, qui ejus fundamenta sunt. Extollitur autem haec Domus, super omnes colles, qui videntur ali- quid eximium in sapientia & veritate polliceri a- pud homines. In hunc montem omnes gentes pro- peramus, in agmine cohortantes se mutuum ad amplectendam Jesu Christi religionem quae efful- sit diebus his novissimis, & dicentes, venite ascen- damus in montem Domini, & in domum Dei Ja- cob : & annunciabit nobis viam suam, & ambula- bimus in ea. Exivit enim ex Sion lex, & migra- vit ad nos spiritualiter. Verbum quoque Domini exivit in illa Hierusalem, ut distribueretur in omnes terras, & judicare in medio gentium, seligendo quotquot se praeberent faciles, & redarguendo tur- bam refractariam. Istis autem percontantibus un- de veniamus, quemve ducem sequamur: responde- mus, venire nos ad mandatum Jesu, ut recudamus rationales nostros gladios bellicos & saevos in ara- tra, & ex pugnacibus olim nostris lanceis falces fa- ciamus. Jam enim non sumimus contra ullam gentem gladium, neque bellare discimus, facti fi- lii pacis per Jesum, quem sequi malumus, quam in- stituta patria, in quibus dum maneremus, alieni à testamentis eramus: nunc accepta lege gratias li- beratori agentes &c. Athanaf. de Incarn. Ver- bi Dei Tom. 1. oper. p. 106. Quis odio inter se in- festos populos pace copulavit? nisi dilectus Dei Filius, communis ille Salvator omnium Jesus Christus, qui praesua charitate omnia ad nostram salutem sustinuit. Nam & olim oracula de pace istiusmodi, quam ille procuraturus erat, edita fuere: concidit (inquit scriptura) gladios suos in vomeres, & lanceas suas in falces, neque arripiet gens contra gen- tem gladium, neque est, ut posthac bellum di- scant. Neque id incredibile, cum etiam nunc bar- bari feris moribus, idolisque hoc tempore sacrifican- tes, in sese furiant, neq; vel ullam horam sustineant sine armis vivere: iidem tamen ubi Christi doctri- nam audiunt, statim à bello ad agriculturam ver- tuntur, & pro gladiis tractandis manus ad preces ex- tendunt: ac pro mutuis inter sese bellis, adversus daemones pudicitia & animi virtute obarmantur. Cyrillus Alexand. in Comment. ad h. l. In verbis ipsis jam nunc Ecclesiae ex gentibus congregandae praedictio perspicue apparet. Israele enim se- cundum carnem velut sublato è medio, sacrificiis- que in lege praescriptis cessantibus: deserto item sacerdotio familiae Leviticae, & ipso demum tem- plo illo fama nobili exusto, & Hierosolyma destru- cta, Christus Ecclesiam ex gentibus instituit, & velut in novissimo tempore, hoc est, in fine hujus Seculi, tunc enim nostri similis factus est. Mon- tem ergo appellat Ecclesiam, (quae est domus Dei viventis.) Sublimen vero, quoniam in ea humile ac depressum prorsum nihil est; sed divi- norum dogmatum notitia, sublime tollitur. Ipsa praeterea vita justificatorum in Christo, & sancti- ficatorum in spiritu alte ædificata est. Theodor. in h. l. non tantum nostram sententiam approbat, sed Judæos etiam atque Judaizantes, qui de reditu de Babylone hæc interpretantur, graviter redarguit: Usque ad extremas terras Evangelica & divina de- nunciatio pervasit, & permanavit juxta Domini prædictionem, quæ in sacris Evangeliis habetur: & prædicabitur, inquit, hoc Evangelium omnibus gentibus in testimonium. Tum etiam Apostolis præcepit, dicens: Euntes docete omnes gentes, ba- ptizantes eos in nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus Sancti: docentes eos servare omnia, quæcunque mandavi vobis. Hæc lex Evangelica atque ver- bum Apostolicum, cum ab Hierusalem veluti à fonte quopiam incepisset, per omnem terrarum orbem pervagatum est, cum fide accedentibus ir- rigationem afferens. Sed tamen Judæi hæc non ita intelligenda existimant, sed hæc ipsa esse de re- versione ex Babylone prædictionem. Et certe nihil mirum est, illos stupiditate refertos sic intel- ligere: nam in alias eorum impietates ab hac et- iam prophetia aberratio convenit. Quod autem quidam pii Doctores eandem interpretationem in sua scripta inferuerint, non ferendum mihi, neque venia dignum videtur. Quænam gentes & vicinæ & longissime habitantes post reditum in Judæo- rum templum accurrerunt ad leges eorum acci- piendas? ad verbum illinc proficiscens amplexan- dum? inter quasnam gentes populosve sic ver- bum Domini judicavit eorum malefacta repre- hendens? & ea, quæ deinceps consequuntur, aper- te illius interpretationis falsitatem refellunt: post enim à Babylone reditum, ut etiam his, qui sic in- terpretati sunt, videtur, & Gog & Magog, cum per- multis gentibus Judæis bellum intulerunt: omnes- que præterea finitimi continenter cum eis bella gesserunt. Hinc quidem Idumæi, & Amanitæ, & Moabitæ: illinc vero exteræ nationes, & Samari- tæ: & non ita multo post tempore à Macedonibus clades in eos invectæ fuerunt, quas Maccabæo- rum libri complectuntur. Hoc autem loco pro- pheticus sermo altissimam pacem promittit. Sub- scribit etiam huic interpretationi Hieronymus in Comment. ad h. l. subscribunt cæteri interpretes antiqui; neque facile inter recentiores sive Pon- tificios, sive Reformatos, sive Nostrates reperitur, qui non agnoverit hoc vaticinium de temporibus N. Test. intelligendum esse. Quid quod inter

Judæos ipsos nonnulli hæc ad Messiæ tempora re- ferant: quod Justinus Triphoni in mentem revo- cavit. R. Eliezer in Thalmude in libro Sabbath, distinct. Bemah Ischoah de diebus Messiæ hæc in terpretatur; Aben Ezra in h. l. Et fluent ad eum. Ab isto loco usque ad finem libri loquitur super mate- ria Messiæ, & de impiis, qui impiè agent in talos Messiæ vel successores, sicut Magistri nostri. Et ju- dicabit ipse Messias inter populos multos. Denique notum est, quod Judæi ex eo, quod hæc, quæ se- cundum literam intelligunt, nondum completa sint, Messiam nondum venisse contendant, id pro certo & indubitato habentes, quod hic de tempo- ribus Messiæ agatur, de quo vid. Raimund. Martini pug. Fid. part. II. C. XII. Dn. D. Tarnovius in h. l. & Dn. D. Müllerus in Judaismo. C. XVII. p. 512. ad- versus R. Isaac Ben Abraham, ubi observetur Re- gula Rabinorum, quod Prophetarum vaticinia de regno Messiæ intelligenda sint אלחי Elahi Spirituali- ter לאגשמי & non Gaschmi corporaliter, & Moni- tio Rab. Mos. Maimon pag. 11. More Nevach. C. XXIX. de Prophetarum & cumprimis Esaiæ oracu- lis non semper secundum literam, sed figurate, ac metaphorice explicandis. Confer. Joel. III. 10. Am. IX. 11. 12. 13. Obad. v. ult. Zach. III. 13. Joh. IX.

## 4:8
Vers. 8. AND YOU TOWER OF THE FLOCK] The tower עדר Ader, that is, of the flock, is near Bethlehem, as appears Gen. XXXV. 21. By that tower is understood here μεταληπτικῶς (metaleptically), Bethlehem, and by Bethlehem the stock of David having its origin from there, and clearly this is the same sense which is repeated in other words below v. 1.

NEBULOSA] The Greeks ἀνυχμώδης, squalid, that is, O family long neglected.

FILIÆ SION USQUE AD TE VENIET] Jerome wrote: Daughter of Sion, it shall come unto you. That is, the whole city of Jerusalem shall seek laws from you. This was fulfilled in Zerubbabel, but in such a way that he bore the image of Christ, who was to arise from the same house.

ET VENIET POTESTAS PRIMA, REGNUM FILIÆ JERUSALEM] The principality shall fall to you, not indeed with Royal splendor, but yet obtaining royal majesty in the minds of the Jerusalemites, because of the promises made to the house of David.

This prophecy too is twisted by violence toward Zerubbabel, and at the same time the way is paved for a similar στρεβλότητα [distortion] of the more illustrious oracle concerning the fatherland of the Messiah, C. V. 1. The discourse is about the eminence and dignity of the tower of Eder, but which it is to attain in the Messiah, not in Zerubbabel. Nor do any traces of a type occur here, nor a double sense, which scripture also nowhere admits: But just as the preceding [passages] dealt with the times of the N.T. according to the letter, so also here the prophecy is continued concerning the same. The word עדר is taken either as a proper noun for the tower near Bethlehem Gen. XXXV. 21, or as an appellative, as the Vulgate rendered it, tower of the FLOCK. Similarly, others take the word עפל as a proper noun, because Ophel was the name of a place in the city 2 Chron. XXXIII. 14, Neh. III. 27, others as an appellative: by the Greek LXX it is rendered ἀυ- χμώδης [squalid], by the Vulgate Nebulosa [cloudy]. Drusius from the Hebrew schools expresses it as the CITADEL of the daughter of Zion. Blessed Luther also rendered it, 'eine Veste der Tochter Sion' [a fortress of the daughter of Zion]: which explanation he does not disapprove of in his commentaries, by which through metalepsis, as he says, עפל is taken for a fortification or bulwark, although he warns that the word properly signifies that which, being hidden among thick clouds, cannot easily be seen, as if you were to say, misty or wrapped in clouds. But by the tower of Eder he understands the kingdom of Judah by synecdoche, because this tower was in the tribe of Judah. But those words תאתה עדיך rendered by B. Luther, 'es wird deine Rose kommen' [thy rose shall come], because עדי denotes an ornament. But because here we have עדיך, Junius, Piscator, the English, Genevan, Italian, and Belgian [versions] render it 'it shall come to thee,' yet they do not refer it to the daughter of Zion; but the Italian translation refers it to the lame [woman], while the others draw it to the following words, 'it shall come to thee,' I say, the first dominion. Yet that translation would not be to be disapproved of, 'Daughter of Zion, it shall come even unto thee' (which is indeed falsely attributed to Jerome: for his commentary shows that he did not write it so), nor the explanation, 'The whole city of Jerusalem shall seek laws from thee, O family of David,' if these things were understood solely of Christ. Similar is the explanation of Haymo, Remigius, and Bede in Luke II, and Baronius in the year of Christ 1, who, according to Cornelius a Lapide, believe there is an allusion to the shepherds of Eder, to whom the angel first announced the birth of Christ: for that reason it is called the tower of Eder, that is, of the flock and of the shepherds, whence clearly explaining this in the following chapter v. 2, he says: 'And thou Bethlehem (near which was the tower of Eder) Ephrata, art little among the thousands of Judah, out of thee shall come forth unto me he that is to be Ruler in Israel, etc.' Therefore they give this sense to this passage, as if to say, Thou, O tower of Eder, rustic, vile, and pastoral, lift up thy head, rejoice and exult: because first to thee shall come the heavenly messenger, namely an ANGEL announcing the birth of CHRIST THE KING, whose first power and kingdom shall begin in JERUSALEM, and from thence shall be propagated through the whole world. Therefore you shall now be a tower not only of the flock, but also of Ophel, that is, of lofty darkness: because upon you, the high summit of Olympus, shall descend a multitude of spirits and heavenly musicians, singing together, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will. That these things are to be drawn to Zerubbabel at the same time, is not to be conceded. For the FIRST power did not come to him, such as that of David or Solomon was, but an inferior one, nor the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem, but only a Principality. An opinion in the minds of men, which makes royal dignity, is not sufficient to fulfill such august promises; indeed, all divine promises demand truth for their fulfillment, not the opinion or persuasion of men. Then, if the same meaning is clearly here, which is in chapter V. 1, it can be understood of no one else than the Messiah. And the Jews themselves acknowledge, and certainly by the authority of the Targum they are bound to acknowledge, that these things are to be understood of the Messiah. For thus the Chaldean rendered this verse: And you, O Christ of Israel, who are hidden because of the sins of Zion, to you the kingdom shall come, and the first power shall come to the kingdom of the congregation of Israel; for the tower of the flock he placed the Christ of Israel, which Cocceius notes as agreeable to the Christian faith, that the Messiah is the fortress and tower of Israel, so that we may flee to him in the confidence of the heart, just as it is also read in Midrash Tillim on Psalm 18:1, I will confess to you among the nations, and I will sing to your name, who magnifies salvations, or who makes a tower of salvations for his king: And what is the tower that was made for them? King Messiah is like a tower, as it is said in Proverbs 18:10, the name of the Lord is a tower of strength. Furthermore, if the words 'tower of Ader (or of the flock) cloudy (or fortress) of the daughter of Zion, even to you shall come, i.e., the limping (or also the first power)' are rendered with others, and by the tower of the flock is understood Jerusalem, or the kingdom of Judah itself by synecdoche, the meaning, as far as the sum of the matter is concerned, will come to the same thing, namely, that the former majesty is promised to the kingdom of Judah, although it never attained it. It is certain that these things must be understood spiritually, and that they had their fulfillment only in Christ, whence Calvin does not speak ill. There is no doubt that by the first kingdom he understands that most flourishing dignity which is celebrated in scripture under David and Solomon. For after the ten tribes were cut off, that kingdom was obscure and thin; here, therefore, the Prophet promises that kingdom which had flourished under David and Solomon. The kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem, therefore, shall come, he says. He expressly mentions the daughter of Jerusalem, because the kingdom of Israel had obscured the glory of the true kingdom. Therefore, the Prophet here testifies that God is not unmindful of his promise, and will thus act so that Jerusalem may recover the dignity which it had lost, and the whole people may coalesce again into one body, so that they may not be two divided members, but one King may contain under himself and by his empire the whole race of Abraham. But it is certain that this was not fulfilled by the coming of Christ in the eyes of men. It is necessary, therefore, to recall to memory what Micah taught a little before, that this kingdom is spiritual, for he did not give Christ a golden scepter, but doctrine: Come, and let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord, he will teach us of his ways: Then from Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. Therefore, that principle must always be held, that God did not render Jerusalem beautiful in the eyes of men, as it had been before, nor did he enrich it with wealth and riches and earthly power: but yet he restored the supreme empire, for he did not only subject to it the ten Tribes, which had previously defected, but the whole world. Blessed Luther had preceded. Here the kingdom of Judah returns. Since that was to be laid waste by the Babylonians, and the people were to be led away captive, he also consoles them, so that they may not despair of such a glorious kingdom of Christ. A horrible devastation was pressing upon the people, and so, lest they should despair entirely, he consoles them, so that they may not estimate the matter by its present appearance. For by that devastation all the beauty that was in the polity, as well as in the priesthood, was taken away. But here, he says, is a temporal beauty, which otherwise must cease. Therefore, do not be very anxious about it. There is another spiritual and eternal beauty; that is owed to this kingdom; look to this, and in the hope of this, forget all temporal inconveniences. That beauty is the first dominion, or the first kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem, as if to say: Hitherto you have had no true kingdom, if you look at wealth, power, and other things; the kingdom flourished under David, Solomon, and certain other kings, but what kind of kingdom was it, when all things were bound by death, polluted by sins, and oppressed by the wrath of GOD? But when Christ comes, there at last the true beauty and the principal Dominion, of which there was nothing like it before, shall come: For death shall no longer rule over you, nor shall sin accuse you, nor shall Satan infest you with his tyranny, but you shall be free, because the Son shall set you free. Tarnovius explains it thus: And you, tower of the flock of the Church, which, because you contain the spiritual sheep of Christ, deservedly have the honor of this name, although you are, as to external appearance, as squalid and despised as that hut was in the tribe of Judah, of which Gen. 35:21 speaks, yet you shall also stand and be fortified so firmly as the tower of the flock, which was later built in the southern part of the city of Jerusalem, and so called because through this gate of the flock they were brought into the cattle market, and into the pool called probatica, of which John 5:2 speaks. See Neh. 3:1, 32, and 12:39, and if you delight in more and longer accounts, go, if you please, to Corn. à Lap. p. 454, 455, and you, hill of the Daughter of Zion, which are situated on a mountain, as the fortress of Zion, Ps. 125:2, 2 Chron. 27:3, and 33:14, Neh. 3:26, and above v. 1, even to you (Hebr. עדיך which others translate as your ornament, but with the form of the word resisting, which would then be עדיך, that primary dominion will arrive, and the former kingdom of the Daughter of Jerusalem, such as it was formerly under David and Solomon corporally and typically, when it was at least one spiritual kingdom, and truly under the antitype of David and Solomon, Christ Jesus, which the consequences prove. Others, however, interpret the former member concerning the judgment about to arrive as far as Zion. Thus Cocceius: But you, tower of the flock, hill of the Daughter of Zion, to you shall come, and shall arrive, the former royal dominion of the Daughter of Jerusalem. This verse joins two things: the destruction of Zion and the kingdom of the Messiah proceeding from it.

Osiander understands both members in a penal sense, and so also do the Greeks Theodoret and Cyril, because the Septuagint interpretation, which here departs not a little from the Hebrew text, implies it. Thus those elders rendered it: Και συ Πυργος ποιμνις αυχμωδους, θυγατηρ Σιων Dπισε ἠξει, και εισελεύσεται αρχη ἡ πρωτη, βασιλεια εκ Βαβυλωνος τη θυγατρι Ιερουσαλημ. And you, tower of the squalid flock, Daughter of Zion, to you shall come and shall enter the first Principality, the kingdom from Babylon to the Daughter of Jerusalem. Whence Cyril paraphrases thus: O Zion, or Jerusalem, miserable Daughter, O miserable and obscure dwelling of my sheep, you shall be exposed entirely, even against your will, to enemies. For there shall come, there shall come, and not long after, upon you, the chief and most robust of earthly kingdoms, namely, that of the Babylonians. But the original text presents a promise, not a threat, which also agrees better with the preceding verses, for the Prophet consoles the tribe of Judah, to which he here turns himself, both from the promise of the kingdom of the Messiah and from the liberation from the Babylonian captivity, as Winckelmann rightly notes here.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET TU TURRIS GREGIS] Turris עדר A- der, id est, gregis, est apud Bethlehemum, ut apparet Gen. XXXV. 21. Per eam turrim hic intelligitur μεταληπ- τικῶς, Bethlehem, & per Bethlehemum stirps Davidis in- de ortum habens, planeque idem est hic sensus, qui repe- titur aliis verbis infra v. 1.

NEBULOSA] Græci ἀνυχμώδης, squallida, id est, ô familia diu neglecta.

FILIÆ SION USQUE AD TE VENIET] Scri- psit Hieronymus: Filia Sion usque ad te veniet. Id est, ci- vitas tota Hierosolymorum à te petet, jura. Impletum hoc in Zorobabele, sed ita ut is Christi, ex eadem domo orituri, gesserit imaginem.

ET VENIET POTESTAS PRIMA, REGNUM FILIÆ JERUSALEM] Tibi continget principatus, non quidem cum Regio splendore, sed tamen in animis Hie- rosolymitarum majestatem regiam obtinens, ob promis- sa Davidis domo facta.

Detorquetur & hoc vaticinium per violen- tiam ad Zorobabelem, ac simul via sternitur ad illu- strioris oraculi de patria Messiæ C. V. 1. similem στρεβλότητα. Sermo est de eminentia & dignitate turris Ader, sed quam in Messia consecutura sit, non in Zorobabele. Neque hic ullæ typi vestigia oc- currunt, nec gemini sensus, quem etiam nuspiam ad- mittit scriptura : Sed quemadmodum præcedentia de temporibus N. T. secundum literam egerunt, ita etiam hic de iisdem continuatur vaticinium. Vox עדר accipitur vel ut nomen proprium de turri pro- pe Bethlehem Gen. XXXV. 21. vel ut appellativum, ut reddidit vulgata, turris GREGIS. Similiter vo- cem עפל alii pro nomine proprio habent, quia O- phel erat nomen loci in urbe 2. Paral. XXXIII. 14. Neb. III. 27. alii pro appellativo : Græcis LXX. ἀυ- χμώδης squallida,vulgatæ Nebulosa redditur. Dru- sius è scholis Ebraicis exprimit ARX filiæ Sion. B. Luth. reddidit etiam, eine Veste der Tochter Si- on : quam explicationem in commentar. non im- probat, qua per metalepsin, ut ait, עפל pro munitio- ne seu propugnaculo accipitur, etsi moneat, proprie vocem significare, quod crassa inter nubila conditum non facile conspici potest, ac si dicas, caliginosum seu involutum nubibus, Per turrim autem Eder intelli- git regnum Judæ per Synecdochen,quia hæc tur- ris in tribu Judæ fuit. Sed illa תאתה עדיך à B. Lu- thero reddita sunt, es wird deine Rose kommen, quia עדי notat ornamentum. At quia hic habetur עדיך, Junius, Piscator, Angli, Genev. Itali, Belg. red- dunt ad te veniet, non tamen referunt ad filiam Si- on; sed ad claudicantem refert Italica translatio, ad sequentia vero trahunt cæteri, ad te veniet, inquam potestas prima. Non improbanda tamen foret ille translatio Filia Sion usque ad te veniet (quæ vero falfo Hieronymo tribuitur : non enim ita scripsisse ipsum commentarius ejus docet) neq; explicatio, civitas tota Hierosolymorum à te jura petet, familia Davidis, si de Christo unice hæc intelligerentur. Affinis est Haymonis, Remigii, Bedæ in Luc. II. Ba- ronii ann. I. Christi explicatio, qui apud Cornel, à Lap. alludi censent ad pastores Eder, quibus ange- lus primo nunciavit Christi ortum : ideo enim no- minari turrim Eder, id est gregis & pastorum, unde id clare explicans cap. sequenti v. 2. ait. Et tu Bethlehem (juxta quam erat turris Eder) Ephrata parvulus es in millibus Judæ, ex te mihi egredietur, qui sit Dominator in Israel &c. Itaque hujus loci hunc dant sensum, q. d. Tu ô turris Eder, rusticana, vi- lis, & pastoritia, caput extolle, gaude & exulta : quia primo ad te veniet nuncius cælestis, puta ANGE- LUS annuncians CHRISTI REGIS ortum, cu- jus potestas prima & regnum incipiet in JERU- SALEM, indeq; propagabitur per totum orbem Quocirca eris jam turris non tantum gregis, sed & Ophel, id est, celsæ caliginis: quia in te excelso O- lympi vertice descendet, Spiritum & Musicorum cœlestium multitudo, concinens, Gloria in excel- sis Deo, & in terra pax, hominibus bonæ volun- tatis. Ut ad Zorobabelem trahantur hæc simul, non concedendum. Non enim ipsi potestas PRIMA venit, qualis Davidis aut Salomonis fuit, sed infe- rior, nec regnum filiæ Jerusalem, sed tantum Prin- cipatus. Opinio in animis hominum, quæ faci dignitatem regiam, nec sufficit ad tam augusta promissiones implendas, imo omnes divinæ pro- missiones veritatem pro complemento poscunt, non opinionem aut persuasionem hominum. Tum si idem sensus plane hic, qui cap. V. 1. de nul- lo alio, quam Messia intelligi potest. Et agno- scant ipsimet Judæi, certe ob autoritatem Targum agnoscere tenentur, hæc de Messia intelligenda esse. Sic enim reddidit hunc versum Chaldæus: Et tu Christe Israelis, qui absconditus es propter pec- cata Zionis, tibi regnum veniet, & veniet potestas prisca regno cœtus Israelis; pro turri gregis posuit Christum Israelis, quod notat Coccejus ceu consen- taneum fidei Christianæ, quod Messias sit arx & turris Israelis, ut confugiamus ad ipsum in fiducia cordis, quemadmodum etiam in Midrasch Tillim legitur ad Psal. 18, 1. Confitebor tibi in gentibus, & nomini tuo psallam magnificanti salvationes, vel fa- cienti turrem salvationum regis sui: Et quæ est tur- ris, quæ facta est iis? Rex Messias est sicut turris, si- cut dictum est Prov. 18, 10. turris fortitudinis nomen Domini. De cætero, si reddantur cum aliis ver- ba turris Ader (vel gregis) nebulosa (vel arx) filiæ Sion, usq; ad te veniet, sc. claudicans (vel etiam po- testas prima) ac per turrem gregis intelligitur Je- rusalem, vel ipsum Judæ regnum per Synecdo- chen, sensus, quantum ad summam rei, eodem re- cidet, nempe regno Judæ pristinam majestatem promitti, quanquam assequutum nunquam sit. Certum est spiritualiter hæc intelligenda esse, & in Christo tantum complementum habuisse, unde non male Calvinus. Dubium non est, quin per re- gnum primum intelligat florentissimam illam dignita- tem, quæ celebratur in scriptura sub Davide & Sa- lomone. Postquam enim abscissæ sunt decem tribus, fuit obscurum illud & tenue regnum, hic ergo promit- tit Propheta regnum illud quod floruerat sub Davide & Salomone. Regnum ergo filiæ Jerusalem veniet, inquit. Diserte exprimit filiam Jerusalem, quia regnum Israel obscuraverat gloriam veri regni. Ergo hic testatur Propheta, Deum non esse immemorem suæ promissionis, atque ita facturum, ut Ierosolyma recuperet dignitatem, quam perdiderat, & totus po- pulus iterum in corpus coalescat, ne sint duo mem- bra divisa, sed unus Rex sub se contineat ac suo im- perio totum genus Abrahæ. Atqui certum est, hoc non fuisse impletum Christi adventu in oculis homi- num. Necesse est igitur repetere memoria, quod paulo ante docuit Michæas, regnum hoc spirituale esse, nam Christo non dabat sceptrum aureum, sed doctrinam: Venite, & ascendamus in montem Domini, docebit nos de viis suis: Deinde ex Sion prodibit lex, & verbum Domini ex Jerusalem. Semper igitur ra- tio illa tenenda est, quod Deus non reddidit Jerosoly- mam in oculis hominum speciosam, ut prius fuerat, neq; opibus & divitiis & terrena potentia eam locu- pletavit: sed tamen restituit summum imperium, neque enim tantum subjecit illi decem Tribus, quæ prius desciverant, sed totum orbem. Præiverat B. Lu- therus. Hic redit regnum Iuda. Id quoniam per Babylonios vastandum, & populus captivus ab- ducendus erat, etiam consolatur, ne desperet de tam præclaro regno Christi. Instabat populo horribilis vastitas, itaque ne omnino desperarent, consolatur eos, ne æstiment rem ex præsenti facie. Nam vastita- te illa tolli decorem omnem, tum qui in politia, tum in sacerdotio erat. Sed hic, inquit, est decor tem- poralis, quem alioqui oportet cessare. Itaque nolite de eo valde esse soliciti. Est alius decor spiritualis & æternus, ille debetur huic regno, in hunc respicite, & spe hujus obliviscimini omnium temporalium incom- modorum. Est autem ille decor primum dominium, seu primum regnum filiæ Ierusalem, q. d. Hactenus nullum verum regnum habuistis, si opes, poten- tiam & alia respiciatis, floruit regnum sub Davide, Salomone, & quibusdam aliis regibus, sed quale Regnum fuit, cum omnia morte constricta, pecca- tis polluta, ira DEI oppressa essent? Sed cum Christus veniet, ibi demum verus decor & prin- cipale Dominium, cujus antea nihil simile fuit, veniet: Non enim dominabitur vobis amplius mors, non peccatum accusabit vos, nec Satan ty- rannide sua infestabit vos, sed liberi eritis, quia Fi- lius vos liberabit. Tarnovius ita exponit: Et tu turris gregis Ecclesiæ, quæ quia oves Christi spiri- tuales contines, habes merito hujus nominis hono- rem, licet sis, quod ad externam speciem tam squa- lida & contemta, quam fuit illud tugurium in tri- bu Juda, de quo Gen. 35, 21. tamen etiam tam firmi- ter consistes & munieris, ut turris gregis, quæ po- stea in meridiana Jerosolymorum urbis parte fuit ædificata, & sic dicta, quod per hanc portam gregis intromitterentur in forum pecuarium, & in pisci- nam προβατικήν, de qua Joh. 5, 2. Vide Neh. 3, 1. 32. & 12, 39. & si pluribus & prolixioribus delecta- ris, adi sis Corn. à Lap. p. 454. 455. & tu clive Filiæ Sionis, quæ in monte sita es, ut arx Sionis Pf. 125, 2. 2. Chron. 27, 3. & 33, 14. Neh. 3, 26. & supra v. 1. ad te usque (Hebr. עדיך quod alii vertunt ornamentum tuum, sed forma vocis repugnante, quæ tum esset עדיך perveniet Dominum illud primarium, & prius regnum Filiæ Jerosolymorum, quale fuit olim sub Davide & Salomone corporaliter & typice, quan- do erat saltem unum regnum Spirituale, ac vere sub Davidis & Salomonis antitypo Christo Jesu, quod consequentia probant. Alii tamen prius mem- brum de judicio perventuro usq́; ad Zionem inter- pretantur. Ita Coccejus: Tu autem turris gregis clive Filiæ Zion ad te usq́; veniet, & adveniet domi- natus pristinus Regius Filiæ Hierosolymorum. Duo conjungit hic versus, Sionis destructionem & regnum Messiæ ex illa prodiens.

Osiander utrumque membrum sensu pœnali intelligit, atque ita etiam Græci Theodoretus & Cy- rillus, quia LXX. Interpretatio, quæ hic non parum abit ab Ebræo textu, id importat. Sic reddidere senes illi, Και συ Πυργος ποιμνις αυχμωδους, θυ- γατηρ Σιων Dπισε ἠξει, και εισελεύσεται αρχη ἡ πρωτη, βασιλεια εκ Βαβυλωνος τη θυγατρι Ιε- ρουσαλημ. Et tu turris gregis squalidi Filia Sion, ad te veniet & ingredietur Principatus primus, regnum ex Babylone Filiæ Hierusalem.. Unde ita παρα- φραζει Cyrillus: O Sion, sive Hierusalem, misera Filia, O mearum ovium miserum & obscurum habita- culum, exponeris omnino etiam invita inimicis. Ve- niet enim, veniet, & non multo post tempore, super te, regnorum terrestrium præcipuum & robustius, nem- pe Babyloniorum. Sed textus originalis promissio- nem, non comminationem exhibet, quæ etiam supe- rioribus magis congruit, nam consolatur tribum Juda Propheta, ad quam se hic convertit, tum è promissione regni Messiæ, tum è liberatione ex captivitate Babylonica, ut recte hic Winckel- mannus.

## 4:9
Vers. 9.

Verse 9.

NOW WHY ARE YOU CONTRACTED WITH SORROW] He addresses the people as if present, living miserably in exile and servitude. In the Hebrew it is: now why do you cry out by crying out? Why do you exclaim so miserably?

IS THERE NOT A KING FOR YOU?] Is it because there is no King for you? Namely, from your own people.

OR HAS YOUR COUNSELOR PERISHED?] Is it because your counselor has perished? Your senators: for it is a hypallage of number. The Greeks well [translate it] ἡ βουλή σου.

BECAUSE PAIN HAS SEIZED YOU LIKE A WOMAN IN LABOR] Is this why pain has found you, as of one giving birth?

B. Luther, Brentius, Winckelmann, Tarnovius, and others judge that by that interrogation: Is there not a King for you? Christ the King is regarded: as if to say, Is not the Son of God himself, the promised Messiah, certainly a King for you, and likewise your counselor in most difficult matters, or, as Osiander says, do you think that Christ your King will not come, who is and will be your counselor, who will show you the way to heaven? B. Luther says here that the name of counselor is attributed to Christ the King, just as also in Isaiah ch. 9. Because even when He allows us to be afflicted, He counsels us, so that we do not perish: But when they were led away captive, the Jews judged that they had lost God as their counselor, and were being led away among the nations without any hope of help. The Prophet therefore warns that minds should fight against this doubt in temptation, because the Church is the care of its King and counselor. He also warns of this, that in dangers we should abstain from trust in human protections, for this is to take away from King Christ His name and His honor.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Vers. 9.

NVNC QVARE MOERORE CONTRAHE- RIS] Alloquitur velut præsens populum in exilio ac servi- tio misere agentem. In Hebræo est: nunc quare vocife- nando vociferaris? Quid ita misere exclamas?

NVMQVID REX NON EST TIBI?] An quia Rex tibi non est? nempe è tua gente.

AVT CONSILIARIVS TVUS PERIIT? ] An quia consiliarius tuus periit? Senatores tui: est enim ὑπαλ- λαγὴ numeri. Græci bene ἡ βουλή σου.

QUIA COMPREHENDIT TE DOLOR SICUT PARTURIENTEM] An hoc est, cur dolor te invenerit, quasi parturientis?

B. Lutherus, Brentius, Winckelmannus, Tarno- vius, alii interrogatione illa: Numquid non est Rex tibi? respici Christum Regem censent: q. d. Est certe Rex tibi ipse Filius DEI promissus Messias, & idem consiliarius tuus in rebus difficillimis, vel, ut Osiander, num propterea putas Christum Re- gem tuum non venturum, qui est & erit consilia- rius tuus, qui monstrabit tibi viam in cœlum. Tribuit, inquit B. Lutherus hic Christo Regi nomen consiliarii, sicut etiam Esaias c. 9. Quod etiam cum affligi nos sinit, consulit nobis, ne pereamus: Sed cum captivi abducerentur, Iudæi judicabant, se Deum consiliarium amisisse, & sine omni spe auxilii in gen- tes abduci. Monet itaque Propheta, ut animi, in tentatione contra hanc dubitationem pugnent, pro- pterea, quod Ecclesiæ curæ est Regi consiliario suo. Etiam hoc monet, ut in periculis abstineamus à fidu- cia præsidiorum humanorum, hoc enim est regi Chri- sto nomen & honorem suum adimere.

## 4:10
Verse 10.

GRIEVE AND STRIVE] Groan, but do not truly grieve, there is just cause, but I bring consolation.

BECAUSE NOW YOU GO FORTH FROM THE CITY] You have gone forth.

AND YOU SHALL DWELL IN THE REGION] You dwell in the field. You cultivate foreign fields.

AND YOU SHALL COME EVEN TO BABYLON] You have arrived even to Babylon. For there also were many of the Jews.

THERE YOU SHALL BE DELIVERED] But from there you shall be delivered.

THERE THE LORD SHALL REDEEM YOU] From there He shall redeem you.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

DOLE ET SATAGE] Ingemisce, non vero te dolere, causa justa est, sed solatium adfero.

QUIA NUNC EGREDERIS DE CIVITATE] Egressa es.

ET HABITABIS IN REGIONE] Habitas in agro. Agros alienos colis.

ET VENIES USQUE AD BABYLONEM] Per- venisti ad Babylonem usque. Nam & illic erant multi Ju- dæorum.

IBI LIBERABERIS] Sed inde liberaberis.

IBI REDIMET TE DOMINUS] Inde redimet te.

## 4:11
Verse 11.

AND NOW MANY NATIONS ARE GATHERED AGAINST YOU] Against you. By nations he understands the Chaldeans and the peoples who were under their empire.

WHO SAY: LET HER BE STONED, AND LET OUR EYE LOOK UPON SION] In the Hebrew: Let her be defiled, let our eye look upon Sion. Let us pollute her, and let us look upon her polluted. They speak as if of a woman. The sense is: let us mock the miseries of the Jewish nation.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET NUNC CONGREGATÆ SUNT SUPER TE GENTES MULTÆ] Contra te. Gentes intelligit Chaldæos & populos, qui sub eorum erant imperio.

QUI DICUNT: LAPIDETUR, ET ADSPI- CIAT IN SION OCULUS NOSTER] In Hebræo: Contaminetur, inspectet Sionem oculus noster. Polluamus eam, ac pollutam inspectemus. Quasi de fœmina lo- quuntur. Sensus est: illudamus miseriis Judaicæ gen- tis.

## 4:12
Verse 12.

BUT THEY HAVE NOT KNOWN THE THOUGHTS OF THE LORD] The counsels of GOD are unknown to them.

FOR HE HAS GATHERED THEM, AS HAY OF THE FLOOR] Because He (God) has gathered them as a sheaf of the floor; namely, to make a threshing of them, which follows: that is, to trample and break them.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

IPSI AUTEM NON COGNOVERUNT CO- GITATIONES DOMINI] Ignota sunt ipsis DEI consi- lia.

QUIA CONGREGAVIT EOS, QUASI FOE- NUM AREÆ] Quod eos congregavit (Deus) quasi mani- pulum areæ; nempe ad trituram de illis faciendam, quod sequitur: id est, ad eos calcandos atque frangendos.

## 4:13
Verse 13.

ARISE AND THRESH, O DAUGHTER OF SION] Trample the Chaldeans, who were in Babylon, when it was being captured.

FOR I WILL MAKE THY HORN IRON, AND THY HOOFS I WILL MAKE BRASS] You will be able to do this safely, armed with the benevolence of the Persians towards you.

AND YOU SHALL CRUSH MANY PEOPLES] In the Hebrew: You shall grind, namely, those slain by the Persians.

AND YOU SHALL DEVOTE TO THE LORD THEIR SPOILS, AND THEIR STRENGTH TO THE LORD OF THE WHOLE EARTH] In the Hebrew it is: And I will devote to the Lord their greed, (what they have greedily seized) and their resources to the Lord of the whole earth. There is here, as often, the third person for the first, or a noun for a pronoun; for GOD is speaking. The simple speech would have been: I will devote to me: that is, I will cause the vessels, which the Chaldeans had greedily carried away from my temple, to return to my uses, Ezra 1:1.

This sense can be admitted. And Cyril, Theodoret, Jerome, Wigandus, Cornel. à Lapide, the Belgian paraphrasts, and others, even the Weimar theologians, explain this as penal threshing, by which the enemies of the Jews are to be trampled, comparing Eph. 21:10, Jer. 51:33. Although they refer these things to the spiritual later on. Coccejus thinks this threshing was accomplished by the Maccabees. Most refer it to the slaughter of Sennacherib, and so also Tarnovius in this place. That God gathers those collected nations (above v. 11) for evil and destruction like a sheaf onto the threshing floor, not that he may store and preserve them, but that he may burn those tares with fire, which was completed not long after, when GOD, with Sennacherib as leader, allows various nations gathered against Jerusalem to ascend, so that they might perish together and be threshed as if in one and the same floor, 2 Kings 18 and 19, 2 Chron. 32, Isa. 36, 37. These are the words of Tarnovius, who also explains the following thus: Arise, you who until now have lain in ashes, mourning, and squalor, Arise, come, strengthen yourself, Isa. 60:1. Daughter of Zion, let there be a change of affairs from GOD almighty, and at some time you will be superior to your enemies, and by the just judgment of GOD and the law of retaliation, afflict them with the harshest punishments, i.e., in the style of scripture, thresh them; see Amos 1:3. But the blessed Luther, Brentius, Osiander, Winckelmannus, Eman. Saa, as well as Calvin, speak of threshing, nor does Tarnovius disapprove of the explanation of Winckelmannus, who briefly encompassed the sum: Threshing is promised to the Daughter of Zion, by which she is to lower and collect the goods of the nations, as if from threshing. Indeed, in the Babylonian captivity itself, Daniel with his companions, and subsequently Ezra, Nehemiah, Mordecai, and Esther, gained Nebuchadnezzar for the Lord, and many Babylonians, likewise CYRUS, DARIUS, and Ahasuerus, who also contributed their resources to the rebuilding of the temple and the city, but yet that spiritual and victorious threshing is promised primarily, by which the Apostles and other Apostolic men gathered the nations like winnowed wheat into the kingdom of Christ, as if into a barn. The blessed Luther prefers these things to be understood of the time of the Old Testament. This prophecy is usually explained of the kingdom of Christ, that through the Apostles the nations were threshed, that is, brought over to the obedience of the Gospel and faith. But because this prophecy has its place below, when it prophesies about the head of this kingdom being born in Bethlehem, these things seem to be more correctly transferred to history, namely that the captive Jews in Babylon will transfer the nations to the true knowledge of God and true worship through the word. Thus Daniel, through a miraculous occasion, becomes known in the court of King Nebuchadnezzar, and through him and other pious men, the knowledge of God is spread throughout the whole Kingdom. Just as there exist Edicts by which that King exhorts all subjects to the worship of the true GOD. The same happened with his son Evil-Merodach. For unless he had held the GOD of the Jews to be the true GOD, he would by no means have freed their King from prison and held him in a royal position. Meanwhile, Daniel, when he is among the Medes, instructs Darius and Cyrus in piety. And there exists a notable Edict of Darius concerning the God of Daniel, but Cyrus has magnificent testimonies of piety, both in Isaiah and Jeremiah. And it is his notable work that he dismisses the captive Jews and adds expenses for the building of the Temple, Ezra 5. Thus the piety of Artaxerxes is famously proclaimed, who wishes for himself and his kingdom to be prayed for in the Temple, and provides magnificent expenses, both for the building and for the sacred rites, Ezra 7. This is that threshing, of which he says the LORD is thinking, to which the Jews would never have come, had they not been scattered among the Nations in this way.

To which the commentary of Brentius also agrees. However, the exposition of the ancients concerning the penal threshing seems simpler, and since they describe the preceding evils which the Chaldeans were about to bring, and the counsels of the Lord are opposed to the thoughts of those enemies of the Lord's people, this does not seem to refer to the slaughter of Sennacherib, inasmuch as it preceded the abduction by the Chaldeans. Furthermore, these things cannot likewise be referred to the slaughter which the Chaldeans received from the Persians, with Grotius: because the daughter of Zion was to trample and thresh her enemies, and God was willing to place an iron horn and bronze hooves upon her, so that she herself might crush many peoples. But those things which were brought upon the Chaldeans by the Persians cannot be vindicated for the Jews and the daughter of Zion. Wherefore, perhaps the Cocceian explanation is not to be rejected. The simple and historical sense of this prophecy is this. After the Babylonian captivity was resolved and Israel was asserted from it, nonetheless the promised Kingdom was not to come immediately. For before this, neighboring nations were to gather themselves against Jerusalem, with the opinion of its contamination and the hope of a pleasant spectacle: This happened under Antiochus. For Jerusalem seemed defiled, and reduced to the census of hypocrites (such as all Gentiles are), with the daily sacrifice taken away. Compare Matt. 24:51, 'he will cut him in pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites.' Which matter provided an occasion for the neighboring nations to triumph, as it were, over the Israelites and the true religion and the hope of the kingdom, which the Israelites had long since conceived. Furthermore, God explains his counsel. That they were gathered so that they might be subdued by the Israelites, and might concede into their dominion and commonwealth. And so it would come to pass that God would animate and strengthen the Israelites, who were oppressed in a wondrous manner, so that they might thresh the surrounding nations. And the subjection of them is well compared with threshing. The wicked are cut down like chaff, so that the remnants, like useful grains, may be brought into the barn. The event is that the wealth and resources of all those peoples serve God, and the Lord of the whole earth, i.e., Christ. That is, so that when the nation and commonwealth of the Israelites had been so propagated and amplified, then Christ would come and begin his kingdom in every part of Palestine. And so it was done. The Maccabees, on the occasion of the tyranny of Antiochus, took up arms, asserted the Commonwealth into a certain liberty, and did not lay down their arms before they had subdued all of Palestine, Moabitis, Idumea, Samaria, Iturea, etc. See Josephus, Antiquities, book 13, chapter 21.

However, it does not seem inconvenient to us that, just as Micah predicted the abduction into captivity and the redemption from the same in verse 10, so he now designates his own times, and this prophecy, which is certain from the collation of chapter 3:12 with Jer. 26:18 to have been issued under Hezekiah, had preceded the slaughter of Sennacherib, whence the Prophet points out these his own times as if with a pointing finger: ועתה AND NOW many nations are gathered against thee or against thee, so that by those many nations, not the Chaldeans but the Assyrians, namely those huge armies of Sennacherib, in which there were many nations, are to be understood. And thus the passage will be for the explanation of Cyril; while Hezekiah was obtaining the Kingdom in Jerusalem, Sennacherib brought devastation upon Samaria, and with it also overturned many cities of Judea. Then he sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish, who blustered immoderately against the glory of God, when in one night by an angelic hand one hundred and eighty-five thousand perished. He mentions this history again. Many nations, he says, are gathered against thee, all but mocking thee, and now about to fall and trample with their feet. Nevertheless, they did not know what GOD had determined. For they have been brought together as if into a threshing floor, and like a sheaf they will be subjected to thy feet (arise therefore and thresh them), for thou shalt have iron horns and bronze hooves, that is, thou shalt be impregnable and invincible to thy enemies, and thou shalt all but trample those who have resisted thee. For since he made mention of the threshing floor and the sheaf, he kept the decorum of the metaphor, and speaks of horns and hooves as if of a calf: if indeed those who lay dead were not consumed by human hand, but finished by divine wrath. Do not ascribe this praise to thyself, he says: but consecrate rather to the Lord of the whole earth, both their multitude and the strength of the uncircumcised. Wherefore there is no need that we should posit here the third person for the first, or even a noun for a pronoun. For although GOD speaks, it is known that the Lord speaking about the Lord is introduced in the scriptures to designate the mystery of the Holy Trinity. Jehovah therefore speaks, promising to the Daughter of Zion the trampling of enemies, and I will devote to the curse, Jehovah, their gain and their strength to the Lord of the whole earth. Which was also noted by Cocceius: God says that he will devote the wealth of the nations to the Lord, and to the Lord of the whole earth. Again, a testimony of the Divinity of Christ. God the Father will devote to God the Son, to whom the dominion of the whole earth has been given. When Christ is called the Lord of the WHOLE earth, you cannot except from his dominion the Patriarchs, one of whom, David, even called him his Lord, Ps. 110:1. Concerning the use of threshing, which they had in Judea, the blessed Luther warned that the Prophet here had regard for the same: For they did not shake out the grains with flails, as with us in Germany, but as is still customary in Italy and other foreign nations, they used beasts of burden for that purpose. Therefore he says, He is my ox, whom I will arm with iron horns, with bronze hooves. Bronze hooves are necessary, so that they are not fatigued, so that they are not worn down by shaking out the grains. Compare Deut. 25:4, 1 Cor. 9:9, 1 Tim. 5:18. Concerning which also see Ludov. de Dieu on this passage. Winckelmann, what do horns have to do with threshing? Because it is a matter of the threshing of men, power is needed, although the feet of threshing oxen are also in one part of them horny.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

SURGE ET TRITURA FILIA SION] Procul- cate Chaldæos, qui Babylone erant, cum ea capere- tur.

QUIA CORNU TUUM PONAM FERREUM, ET UNGULAS TUAS PONAM ÆREAS] Tuto hoc facere poteritis, armati Persarum in vos benevolentia.

ET COMMINUES POPULOS MULTOS] In Hebræo: Conteres, nempe interfectos a Persis.

ET INTERFICIES DOMINO RAPINAS EO- RUM, ET FORTITUDINEM EORUM DOMINO UNIVERSÆ TERRÆ] In Hebræo est: Et devorabo Domino avaritiam eorum, (quod avare arripuerunt) & facultates eorum Domino universæ terræ. Est hic, ut sæ- pe, tertia persona pro prima, sive nomen pro pronomi- ne; DEUS enim loquitur. Simplex sermo fuerat: mihi devorabo: id est, faciam ut ad meos usus redeant vasa, quæ Chaldæi avarè è templo meo abduxerant, Esdr. I. 1.

Admitti potest hic sensus. Ac de trituratione pœnali, qua conculcandi sint hostes Judæorum, exponunt Cyrillus, Theodoretus, Hieronymus, Wigandus, Cornel. à Lapide, paraphrasta Belgici, & alii, etiam Vinarienses, conferentes Ef. XXI. 10. Jer. LI. 33. Etsi postea ad Spiritualem hæc referant. Coccejus à Maccabæis hanc triturationem peractam censet. Plerique ad cladem Sennacheribi referunt, atque ita etiam Tarnovius h. m. Deum congregare illas gentes collectas (supra v. 11.) ad malum & interitum velut manipulum in aream, non ut reponat & conservet, sed ut igne comburat illa Zizania, quod non multo post completum est, quando DEUS duce Sennacherib varias gentes congregatas contra Jerosolymam sinit ascendere, ut simul perirent & velut in una eademque triturarentur area 2. Reg. 18. & 19. 2. Chron. 32. Esa. 36. 37. cap. Hæc Tarnovius, qui etiam sequentia ita exponit: Surge quæ hactenus incinere, luctu, ac squalore jacuisti, Surge, age, teipsam confirma Es. 60, 1. Filia Sion, mutatio rerum sit à DEO omnipotente,& quandoque tuis hostibus eris superior, eosque ex justo DEI judicio, ac jure talionis durissimis affice suppliciis, h. e. scripturæ stylo tritura; vide Am. I. 3. B. Luth. vero, Brentius, Osiander, Winckelmannus, Eman. Saa, ut & Calvinus de trituratione, nec improbat Tarnov. Winck. explicationem qui summam breviter complexus est: Promittitur Filiæ Sion trituratio, qua illa demissura & collectura sit bona gentium, tanquam ex trituratione. Sane in ipsa captivitate Babylonica Daniel cum suis sociis, & deinceps Esdras, Nehemias, Mardochai Esther Domino lucrifecerunt Nabuchodonosorem, & multos Babylonios, item CYRUM, DARIUM, Ahasverum, qui etiam facultates suas contulerunt ad reædificationem templi & urbis, sed tamen inprimis promittitur trituratio illa Spiritualis, & victoriosa, qua Apostoli & alii viri Apostolici gentes tanquam triticum excussum collegerunt in regnum Christi, velut in horreum. B. Lutherus mavult hæc accipi de tempore V. Test. Solet hæc Prophetia plerumque exponi de regno Christi, quod per Apostolos gentes trituratæ, hoc est, ad obedientiam Evangelii & fidei traductæ sint. Sed quia hæc Prophetia infra suum locum habet, cum de capite regni hujus in Bethlehem nascendo vaticinatur, rectius videntur hæc transferri ad historiam, quod scilicet captivi Judæi in Babylone per verbum ad veram Dei notitiam & veros cultus Gentes tranferent. Sic Daniel per mirabilem occasionem innotesicit in aula Regis NebucadNezar, ac per eam, aliosque pios cognitio Dei in totum Regnum spargitur. Sicut extant Edicta, quibus Rex ille omnes subditos hortatur ad cultum veri DEI. Idem accidit cum filio ejus Evil Merodach. Is enim nisi DEUM Judæorum habuisset pro vero DEO neutiquam Regem eorum liberasset ex carcere, regioque loco habuisset. Interim Daniel, cum in Medis est, Darium & Cyrum instituit ad pietatem. Et extat insigne Darii Edictum de Deo Danielis, Cyrus autem magnifica testimonia pietatis, tum in Esaia, tum Jeremia habet. Et est insigne ejus opus, quod captivos Judæos dimittit, & sumptus addit ad ædificationem Templi, Esdr. V. Sic Artaxerxis pietas egregie prædicatur, qui vult pro se & regno orari in Templo, & magnificos sumptus ponit, tum in ædificationem, tum in sacra Esdr., 7. Hæc est illa trituratio, de qua dicit DOMINUM cogitare, ad quam nunquam Judæi venissent, nisi hoc modo in Gentes essent sparsi.

Cui consonat quoque Commentarius Brentianus. Simplicior tamen videtur expositio veterum de pœnali trituratione, & quum antecedentia mala, quæ Chaldæi illaturi erant, describant, illorumque hostium populi Domini cogitatis opponantur Domini consilia, videtur hoc ad cladem Sennacheribi, utpote quæ antegressa est Chaldæorum abductionem, non spectare. Porro ad cladem, quam Chaldæi à Persis accepere, hæc itidem referri non poterunt cum Grotio: quia filia Sion proculcare ac triturare hostes suos debebat, ejusque cornu ferreum, & ungulas æreas Deus ponere volebat, ut ipsa populos multos comminuat. Quæ autem à Persis illata Chaldæis sunt, Judæis & filiæ Sion vindicari non possunt. Quapropter non reprobanda forte Coccejana explicatio. Simplex & historicus sensus hujus prophetiæ hic est. Post solutam captivitatem Babylonicam & assertum Israelem ex ea, nihilo minus non statim venturum Regnum promissum. Ante enim Gentes vicinas se collecturas, contra Hierosolymam, cum opinione contaminationis ejus & spe jucundi spectaculi: Hoc evenit sub Antiocho. Visa enim est Hierosolyma profanata, & in censum hypocritarum (quales Gentiles omnes sunt) redacta, ablato sacrificio jugi. Confer. Matth. XXIV. 51. τὸ μέρος αὐτῦ μετὰ τ̃ ὑποκριτῶν θήσι. Quæ res occasionem præbuit vicinis gentibus quasi triumphandi de Israelitis & religione vera & spe regni, quam dudum conceperant Israelitæ. Porro Deus explicat consilium suum. Collectos esse, ut subigerentur ab Israelitis, & in ipsorum ditionem ac rempublicam concederent. Itaque futurum, ut Deus Israelitas mirum in modum oppressos animet, roboret, ut circumsitas gentes triturent. Et bene subactio illarum cum trituratione confertur. Improbi velut paleæ cæduntur, ut reliquiæ, tanquam grana utilia in horreum inferantur. Eventus est, ut omnium istorum populorum opes & copiæ serviant Deo, & domino totius terræ, h. e. Christo. Id est, ut quum ita propagata & amplificata fuerit Israelitarum gens & respublica, tum veniat Christus & regnum suum ordiatur in omni parte Palæstinæ. Et ita factum est. Maccabæi occasione tyrannidis Antiochi arma corripuerunt, in libertatem quandam asseruerunt Rempublicam, neque antea arma deposuerunt, quam totam Palæstinam, Moabitidem, Idumæam, Samariam, Ituræam &c. subegissent. Vide Joseph. l. XIII. antiq. cap. 21.

Nobis tamen non videtur incommodum, uti vers. 10. abductionem in captivitatem, & redemptionem ex eadem prædixit Michæas, ita sua nunc eundem designare tempora, atque vaticinium hoc, quod sub Hiskia editum esse è cap. III. 12. cum Jer. XXVI. 28. collatione certum est antegressum fuisse cladem Sennacheribi, unde Propheta velut indice digito hæc sua tempora demonstrat: ועתה ET NUNC congregatæ sunt super te gentes multæ vel contra te, ut per illas gentes multas, non Chaldæi sed Assyrii, exercitus nempe illi ingentes Sennacheribi, in quibus multæ gentes fuere, intelligantur. Atque ita locus erit explicationi Cyrilli; Regnum Hierosolymis obtinente Ezechia, Samariæ vastitatem intulit Sennacherib, & cum illa multas quoq́; Judææ urbes evertit. Deinde misit ex Lachis Rabsacen, qui adversus gloriam Dei immodice blateravit, quando manu angelica una nocte centum octoginta quinque millia disperierunt. Hujus historiæ rursum meminit. Congregatæ sunt, inquit, super te gentes multæ, tantum non ludentes super te, & jamjam procubituræ pedibus insulta- turæ. Veruntamen non cognoverunt, quid sta- tuerit DEUS. Comportati enim sunt velut in aream, & instar manipuli pedibus tuis subjicientur (surge igitur & tritura eos) cornua enim ferrea ha- bebis, & ungulas æreas, hoc est inexpugnabilis & invicta eris hostibus tuis, & tantum non con- culcabis, qui restiterint tibi. Quoniam enim a- reæ & manipuli mentionem fecit, decorum me- taphoræ servavit, & tanquam de vitulo cornua & ungulas dicit: siquidem non humana manu consumpti, sed ira divina confecti erant, qui jace- bant mortui. Ne tibi laudem isthanc adscribas, inquit: sed consecra potius Domino universæ ter- ræ, & multitudinem eorum & robur imperfecto- rum. Quapropter non opus est, ut hic statuamus positam esse tertiam Personam pro prima, vel et- iam nomen pro pronomine. Etsi enim DEUS loquatur, notum est, quod Dominus de Domino loquens in scripturis introducatur ad designan- dum S. S. Trinitatis mysterium. Loquitur ergo Jehovah promittens Filiæ Sionis conculcationem hostium, & anathemate devovebo Jehovah quæstum torum & fortitudinem eorum Domino universæ ter- ræ. Quod notatum etiam Coccejo: Deus dicit se devoturum opes gentium Domino, & Domino to- tius terræ. Rursus testimonium Divinitatis Christi. Deus Pater Deo Filio, cui Dominium totius terræ datum est, devovebit. Quum Chri- stus appellatur Dominus TOTIUS terræ, non po- tes excipere ab illius Dominio Patriarchas, quo- rum aliquis, David, eum etiam Dominum suum appellavit Ps. CX. 1. De triturationis usu, quem in Judæa habuere, monuit B. Lutherus, quod hic eundem respexerit Propheta: Non enim flagris ex- cutiebant grana, sicut apud Nos in Germania, sed sicut adhuc in Italia, & aliis exteris nationibus so- let, jumentis ad eam rem utebantur. Ideo dicit, Es meus bos, quem armabo ferreis cornibus, æreis ungulis. Ungulis æreis opus est, ut non defatigentur, ne at- terantur excutiendo grana. Conf. Deut. XXV. 4. 1. Cor. IX. 9. 1. Tim. V. 18. De quo etiam vid. Ludov. de Dieu ad h. l. Winckelmannus, quid cornibus cum trituratione?
