Quia agitur de tritura- tione hominum, opus est potentia, quamvis etiam pe- des boum triturantium una sui parte sint cornei.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V. Again CONSOLATORY.

He promises the temporal birth of the eternal Son of God in Bethlehem, and although the Jews are to be afflicted with various plagues, they are nevertheless to be preserved, until in the meantime the Israelites are gathered to them under their king Christ, who is to be exalted throughout the whole world, where, with the people liberated and the enemies overturned, and idols also renounced, vengeance will be exercised against the refractory nations. Bethlehem brings forth a King, to whom the whole world may obey.

Verse 1.

NOW YOU SHALL BE DEVASTATED, O DAUGHTER OF THE ROBBER] All these things in the Hebrew rightly cohere with the preceding discourse. The Greeks have divided them poorly: You shall be cut off shortly, O daughter of the cutter. He addresses Babylon, and therefore uses a Chaldean word: for גדד is to cut off for the Chaldeans, whence also the Arabs use this word with a like meaning. Daughter of the cutter, that is, built by Nimrod, the greatest robber, and having imitated his ways, Gen. X. 8. 9. 10.

THEY HAVE LAID A SIEGE AGAINST US] They shall perish who have besieged us.

WITH A ROD THEY SHALL STRIKE THE CHEEK OF THE JUDGE OF ISRAEL] They who have beaten with a staff the cheek of the judge of Israel, that is, the judgment, as the Chaldean translates here. To strike the cheek is to treat injuriously. Ps. III. 8, where the word is added to staves, that increases the insult. Often prophets as the chief cause of the evils which befell Babylon: they report, mercilessness toward the Jews.

The coherence of these with the preceding is rightly observed, which the Vulgate version wrongly separated along with the Greeks. But that Babylon is addressed here, and that the judges of Israel treated injuriously are designated by the Babylonians, is not equally manifest. And since the immediately preceding verses do not deal with the Chaldeans, that συνέχεια upon which Grotius relies is non-existent, as if the discourse were continued about the Babylonians being cut off by the Persians. For no mention of the Persians is made in this prophecy, which relates to the immediately preceding chapter IV. 12, 13. Others say Babylon is addressed thus: gather troops of robbers, that is, of your soldiers and plunderers, O Babylon, that you may besiege the Jerusalemites, and strike the cheek of the judge, that is, the King of Israel, say Zedekiah: Others prefer that the Prophet addresses Damascus here, you shall be laid waste, O Damascus, robber and plunderer of Israel. Most, with Jerome and Haymo, think Jerusalem is so called. You, O Jerusalem, who have been made the daughter of a robber, shall be laid waste. But those things do not agree, nor do they cohere with what is immediately connected, nor is it likely that she whom he just raised up under the name of the daughter of Zion should be addressed by such an infamous name. And although some explain it passively, that she was often attacked in wars by troops of soldiers, Osiander even thought it could be rendered thus: O daughter of war, or you city of Jerusalem, restless and desirous of war. You will indeed be a warlike city, enough restlessness and wars will be given to you. B. Höpfner also explains it thus: Now you are distressed, Jerusalem, daughter of a troop (passive, just as one is called a son of death who has been judged guilty of death, so that it deals with the siege of the Chaldeans: It does not seem consistent, however, after verse 10 has already dealt not only with the abduction into Babylon, but also with the liberation from it, that now, after many things that are not a little different, it should deal with the siege of Jerusalem, and that it should be proposed in such abrupt words: but much less does the explanation of Jerome and Lyra, rejected here by B. Luther, fit the text, as if the Prophet were prophesying about Christ, struck with blows by the soldiers of Pilate: whom Cocceius interpolated thus: now lead your legions, daughter of legions, so that this may be an excitation of the Roman empire, as the avenger of the injury to be inflicted on Christ the King: He placed a siege around us (Pompey surrounded and captured Jerusalem with a siege. The Romans from that time held Judea enclosed on all sides, and as if surrounded by a crown) They shall strike the judge of Israel on the cheek with a rod, that is, Christ. The connection with the preceding suggests that we should understand this passage, in which the word 'Now' is repeated so that it is clear that the same time is being dealt with, as referring to Sennacherib and the Assyrian camps, just as chapter V. 16 further deals with the Assyrians, concerning which see Cocceius and Cornel. à Lap. in loc. that is to say: Now you shall be cut off, daughter of robbers or of a troop (Ludov. de Dieu rendered it 'daughter of a troop') the Assyrian multitude shall perish, or those shall be cut off who besieged us, who like a rod struck the cheek of the judge of Israel, i.e., treated King Hezekiah ignominiously. Thus Castrius paraphrases: Now shortly you shall be plundered, O Assyria, daughter of the plunderer Sennacherib, whose army besieged Jerusalem, and whose leaders treated King Hezekiah and his other judges with no less reproach than one who strikes the cheek. The Vinarie Paraphrasts also understood it of the mockery of King Hezekiah.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Iterum CONSOLATORIUM.

Nativitatem temporalem Filii Dei æterni in Bethlehem promittit & quamvis Judæi variis plagis afficien- di, conservandi tamen sunt, donec aggregentur in- terim iis Israelitæ sub rege eorum Christo per totum orbem exaltando, ubi liberato populo & eversis ho- stibus, idolis etiam abdicatis contra gentes refra- ctarias vindicta exercebitur. Bethla parit Regem, cui totus pareat orbis.

Vers. 1.

NVNC VASTABERIS FILIA LATRONIS] Hæc omnia in Ebræo recte cum præcedente sermone cohæ- rent. Græci male discerpserunt: Brevi exscinderis, ô filia exscissoris. Babylonem alloquitur, ideoque voce utitur Chaldaica: nam גדד Chaldæis est exscindere, unde & Arabes pari significatu hanc vocem usurpant. Filia ex- scissoris, id est, ædificata à Nimrodo prædone maximo, e- jusque mores, imitata, Gen. X. 8. 9. 10.

OBSIDIONEM POSUERE SVPER NOS] Peri- bunt illi qui nos obsederunt.

IN VIRGA PERCVTIENT MAXILLAM JV- DICIS ISRAEL] Qui bacillo verberarunt maxillam ju- dicis Israel, id est, judicium, ut hic vertit Chaldæus. Verberare maxillam est injuriose tractare. Ps. III. 8. ubi verbo bacillis adjicitur, id auget contumeliam. Sæpe Pro- phetæ pro præcipua causa malorum, quæ Babyloni evene- runt: referunt, immifericordiam in Judæos.

REcte observatur cohærentia horum cum præ- cedentibus, quæ vulgata versio perperam diftraxit cum Græcis. At Babyloniam hic compel- lari, judicesque Israelis injuriose tractatos, à Baby- loniis designari, haud æque manifestum est. Et quum immediate præcedentia de Chaldæis non a- gant, συνέχεια illa, qua nititur Grotius, nulla est, quasi continuetur sermo de Babyloniis à Persis ex- scindendis. Persarum enim nulla in hoc vaticinio facta est mentio, quod ad immediate antegressa c. IV. 12. 13. Alii ita compellari Babylonem dicunt: congrega turmas latronum, id est, militum & præ- donum tuorum, ô Babylon, ut obsideas Hie- rosolymitas, & percutias maxillam judicis, id est, Regis Israel, puta Zedeciæ: Alii Prophetam Da- mascum hic compellare malunt, vastaberis ô Da- masce, latro & prædo Israelis. Plerique cum Hie- ronymo & Haymone Jerusalem ita vocari censent. Tu ô Jerusalem, quæ facta es filia latronis, vasta- beris. Sed illa non consonant, nec cohærent im- mediate connexis, neque quam modo erexit sub nomine filiæ Sionis, tam infami nomine compel- lari, verisimile est. Et quamvis passive exponant nonnulli, quod fæpe bellis sit impetita à turmis militum, Osiander etiam ita reddi posse putarit, ô filia belli, seu tu urbs Jerusalem, inquietis, & belli cupida. Du wilt doch eine kriegerische Stadt seyn, Satis inquietudinis & Bellorum tibi dabitur. B. Höpfnerus quoque sic exponit: Nunc angeris Hierosolyma filia turmæ (passive uti filius mortis dicitur, qui mortis reus judicatus est, ut de obsi- dione Chaldæorum agatur: Non videtur tamen consentaneum, postquam v. 10. jam non modo de abductione in Babyloniam; sed & de liberatione ex eadem actum, nunc post aliquam multa non parum diversa, de obsessione Hierosolymæ agi, eamque tam abruptis verbis proponi: multo vero minus congruit textui Hieronymi & Lyræ explica- tio à B. Luthero hic reprobata, quasi vaticinetur Propheta de Christo, cæso colaphis à militibus Pila- ti: quem ita interpolavit Coccejus: nunc duc tu legiones, filia legionum, ut hæc sit excitatio imperii Romani, tanquam vindicis injuriæ Christo Rege inferendæ: Obsidium posuit circa nos (Pompejus Hierosolyma obsidione cinxit & cepit. Roma- ni ex eo tempore undiquaque inclusam tenue- runt Judæam, & tanquam corona cinctum) Virga percutient in maxilla judicem Israelis, id est, Chri- stum. Nexus cum superioribus suadet, ut hanc pericopen, in qua vox Nunc repetitur, ut constet de eodem tempore agi, de Sennacheribo, & castris Afsyriis intelligamus, quemadmodum etiam cap. V. 16. de Assyriis porro agitur, de quo vid. Cocce- jus & Cornel. à Lap. in h. l. q. d. Nunc exscin- deris filia latronum vel turmæ (filiam turmæ reddi- dit Ludov. de Dieu) Assyriaca multitudo peribunt, vel exscindentur illi, qui nos obsederunt, qui veluti virga percussere maxillam judicis Israel, h. e. Eze- chiam Regem ignominiose tractarunt. Ita ϖαραφρά- ζει Castrius: Nunc brevi diripieris ô Assyria filia di- reptoris Sennaherib, cujus exercitus obsedit Jerusa- lem, & duces probro affecerunt Ezechiam Regem, cæ- terosque judices ejus non minori, quam qui percutit maxillam. De illusione Regis Hiskiæ acceperunt etiam Vinarienses Paraphrastæ.

## 5:2
Vers. 2.

AND YOU BETHLEHEM EPHRATHA] But you, he returns to what he had said above in IV. 8, as the Prophets often repeat the same things, so that they may the more cling to the mind. Bethlehem Ephratha is the same as Bethlehem of Judah, as we said at Matt. II. 6.

YOU ARE LITTLE AMONG THE THOUSANDS OF JUDAH] It can conveniently be read as a question: are you little, that is, are you considered so by the people of Judah? which form of speaking vehemently denies, as we noted at the cited place of Matthew; it can also be translated: it is a small thing that you are, that is, that you have your place among the chiliarchs of Judah. A far greater honor is destined for you.

OUT OF YOU SHALL COME FORTH TO ME] That is, shall be born. For thus יצא is taken in Gen. XVII. 6, XXV. 25, Is. XI. 1. Zerubbabel is rightly said to be born out of Bethlehem, because he was of the family of David, which originated from Bethlehem.

AND HIS GOINGS FORTH ARE FROM THE BEGINNING, FROM THE DAYS OF ETERNITY] His origin (Zerubbabel's) is from of old, from long times. That is, he draws his origin from an illustrious house, ancient and reigning for five hundred years.

The corruption of the prophecy concerning the Messiah's homeland is most illustrious and detestable, by which Grotius clearly Judaizes. That Micah predicts here the same things which he had prophesied in other words in ch. IV. 8, is less clear. If, however, those are twin to these, it must be said that the homeland of Christ was designated in both places, more obscurely there, but more clearly here. These in no way fit Zerubbabel, although some of the Jews have dared to twist this prophecy to him, whom our author has followed here as a blind guide, just as in many other things. For Chrysostom at Matt. II and Theodoret at this place testify that the Jews in the age of Chrysostom explained these things concerning Zerubbabel. Moreover, these things teach that that Jewish gloss concerning Zerubbabel is to be rejected: First, because there is no trace in the text of Zerubbabel; neither do the preceding things, which Micah predicted from v. 11 of the preceding chapter, look to his times, nor do the following things pertain to him. Then, since the Prophet arrives at this prophecy on the occasion of the liberation from the siege of the Assyrians, Zerubbabel has no place here, but he could conveniently treat of the Messiah, whether you connect these things with Theodoret as if he were saying: The military troop of Sennacherib will be devastated, but not by your strength, O Jerusalem, but by the strength of Christ, who was one day to arise from Bethlehem according to the flesh, just as Isaiah ch. VII joined the liberation of the Jews from the hand of the robber of Syria and Assyria with the prophecy concerning the birth of Christ, by whose power that was done: or whether you say with Castrius that Micah foresaw Jerusalem besieged by the Assyrian and the villages bordering it captured and desolated, and cast the eyes of his mind upon Bethlehem, and saw it, which perhaps was then captured and overturned, as the future homeland and mother of that Ruler who was about to liberate the Jews from their afflictions and redeem them from the hand of their enemies, and said, and you Bethlehem, although you are small and not able to resist the Assyrian, you will bring forth from yourself the Ruler of Israel, the Messiah. B. Höpfner notes that after the announced captivity the restoration of the polity is promised, because they are not only to recover Jerusalem, but also the small villages and towns, such as was Bethlehem, the future homeland of the Messiah; so that at the same time the final cause of the liberation of the Jews is indicated, the birth of Christ according to the flesh. Thirdly, the birth city and homeland of that Ruler, concerning whom the Prophet prophesies, is designated here: for as it is certain that by the going forth from Bethlehem the birth is indicated, and Grotius confesses it: HE SHALL GO FORTH from Bethlehem, to be the same as he shall be born, because thus יצא is taken in Gen. XXV. 25 and ch. XVII. 6. Is. XI. 6. thus that distortion is by no means to be admitted, that one is rightly said to be born from BETHLEHEM who is from the family of David, which originated from BETHLEHEM. For where is such a phrase in Scripture? And are they not as far apart as heaven and earth, to be born from someone's Bethlehemite family, and to go forth or be born from BETHLEHEM?

If those who went out from the family of David are to be said to be born from Bethlehem, then Solomon also, and all the Kings of Judah, will have been born from Bethlehem. But here a certain peculiar axiom is expressed, proper to that little town; and it is commended, and preferred to others because of this ἐξοχὴν (preeminence), that from that city a Ruler in Israel is to arise. Therefore, it is not the family of some Bethlehemite, but the birth from Bethlehem, as a native soil, that is regarded. Now, Zerubbabel was by no means born in Bethlehem. Nor does Scripture teach that anywhere. Nor does the Chronology agree. We have also Grotius confessing this in the matter. He was born rather in Babel, whence most suppose he was called Zerubbabel, as if 'seed of Babel,' because, born in the Babylonian captivity, that name was given for the sake of every good.

Fourth, it is certain that the discourse in this place is about some prerogative of Bethlehem. Grotius renders the words of Micah by way of interrogation. 'Art thou small,' that is, 'art thou to be held by the people of Judah,' so that by this formula of speaking it is vehemently denied that it is to be held small. In which manner Isidore, as also Ludov. Vives in book XXIX of Augustine's De Civitate Dei, ch. XXX, as well as Franc. Riebera, Cornelius Iansenius, and then from the Reformed, Johannes Drusius, Frider. Spanhemius, and others, have reconciled the words of Matthew with the words of the Prophet, just as the most ancient Gothic Codices of Isidore in the Church of Toledo read, 'And thou Bethlehem, Ephrata, art thou not little?' The Hebrews are indeed accustomed to form their interrogations otherwise, but it cannot be denied that sometimes they also lie hidden among them, and yet are to be elicited from the sense. Another explanation: 'it is little, that thou art,' that is, 'that thou hast thy place among the chiliarchs of Judah,' borrowed from Urbano Regio in the Dialog. de Conc. Christi Emaunt. f. 21, Osiander, and Forster, is disapproved by Angelus Caninius, and although Lud. de Dieu defends it, it does not, however, entirely please Frid. Spanhemius (although he defends it against the harassment of Riebera), p. II, Dub. Evangel. XLV, p. 422, primarily because the Hebrews never use על צעיר in this form of speaking, but מן צעיר, because the LXX interpreters, the Chaldean paraphrase, and most interpreters, whether Jews or Christians, oppose it. Concerning which, see Hackspan on this passage. The most illustrious Hottinger in histor. Creation. p. 16, from Eduardo Peckok in Miscell. not. c. 2, notes the name צעיר Jer. XLVIII. 4, Zach. XIII. 9. That 'Leader,' 'Prince,' 'Judge,' and thus not only 'not small,' but also 'great,' signifies 'excellent,' and that thus the ἐναντιοφάνειαν (contradiction) which has hitherto exercised great minds between Micah and Matthew is solidly removed! That is beyond doubt, that a certain extraordinary ἐξοχὴν (preeminence) of this city is expressed, which it was to obtain from the birth of this Ruler in Israel. But if he did not have his departure or his birth from the city of Bethlehem, but in Babel or elsewhere, how could honor be procured for Bethlehem from that? Did a new splendor accrue to that little town from it, above other cities of Judea, because Solomon the wisest King of Israel, because Hezekiah the most pious King, because other great Kings existed in Judea? Could Bethlehem be celebrated in such a way from that, because it is μηδαμῶς ἐλαχίση, by no means the least, if we may speak thus with Lucretius, among the thousands of Judah, and indeed in this way because FROM IT the Ruler in Israel was to go forth? Therefore we conclude thus: Because of the eminent distinction of which Ruler born from Bethlehem Bethlehem is most celebrated, he acknowledges Bethlehem as his birthplace or fatherland. But Zerubbabel does not acknowledge Bethlehem as his native soil. Therefore Zerubbabel is not that Ruler because of whose eminent distinction, as if born from Bethlehem, Bethlehem is most celebrated here.

Bethlehem is celebrated. When the words of the Prophet בְּאַלְפֵי are rendered by Matthew as ἐν ἡγεμόσιν (among the leaders), nothing is detracted from either the sense of the Prophet or the dignity of the commendation. For that city is noted which is not to be estimated as small among the chiliarchs of Judah. Since those cities are leaders which are large and populous, in which there are many thousands of men: just as the Jewish people were distributed into Decuries, Centuries, Chiliads, and their prefects were Decurions, Centurions, Chiliarchs, Exod. XVIII. 21, Jud. VI. 18, 1 Sam. X. 19. And it may be said that the Prophet speaks collectively about the chiliads, and Matthew demonstratively about the leaders of the chiliads or chiliarchs. For such were the prefectures, that a city which could bring forth 3,000 men with its villages also had three Chiliarchs. He teaches, therefore, that it is a small town, and of almost no power.

Fifth, the discourse is about such a מוֹשֵׁל (Ruler), who is to rule not only over the people of the two tribes, but in Israel, i.e., the entire people of the XII tribes, which does not befit Zerubbabel: likewise, who is not to be of inferior dignity, power, and glory than David the Bethlehemite, but rather of more eminent and sublime status. For if that ruler is not to prevail in dignity, power, virtue, and glory, no greater honor could accrue to Bethlehem from his departure from Bethlehem than that which it had already long since obtained from David its citizen. Which honor it certainly could not obtain from Zerubbabel, but has obtained from the Messiah, of whom David bore some image.

Sixth, the matter here is about the ruler of Israel, so called ἐξοχικῶς (by way of preeminence) and κατ’ αἰτωιομασίαν (by antonomasia), whom Israel had long expected, and who had long since been destined for him by GOD, who was to go forth to GOD himself from Bethlehem: therefore, he says, he will go forth TO ME, with emphasis, which Matthew seems to have accepted as meaning that he ought to govern and feed the people of the LORD or Israel, as it was the people of the LORD. Which is proper to the Messiah. For this is the Moschel (Ruler) in the entire Israel, as it is the people of the Lord, Is. XLIV. 5, Rom. IX. 6, seqq., and he had to go forth to GOD the Father, to whose honor and glory alone, as that chosen Lord, in whom alone He had His good pleasure.

Seventhly, the discourse is concerning that ruler, who besides his future going forth from Bethlehem or his temporal birth, had a going forth, מִקֶּדֶם מִימֵי עוֹלָם from the beginning, from the days of eternity, that is, an eternal birth. Which does not suit Zerubbabel, but CHRIST alone, who went forth from eternity by generation from the Father, Prov. VIII. 23. In order to twist this to Zerubbabel, Grotius invented another metaphrase or translation: his origin is from of old, from long times, and he imposed an insolent and unusual paraphrase upon these words in this manner: He draws his origin from a house illustrious from antiquity, and reigning for 500 years. But going forth denotes not origin or lineage, but birth, Gen. X. 14, chap. XXXV. 19, Jud. IX. 30, 1 Chron. II. 35. Job I. 25, nor is a family ever called by the Hebrews מֹצָאוֹת but either בַּיִת or מִשְׁפָּחָה or תּוֹלְדוֹת or finally שְׁבָטִים. That word, however, is used concerning birth: nor is there any doubt about it among interpreters, just as Grotius himself rendered it: out of thee shall he come forth unto me, that is, shall be born. Nor is there any word here concerning the antiquity of the family of the ruler in Israel, but concerning the going forth from the beginning from the days of eternity of the ruler himself, whose not ancient lineage (for this Zerubbabel had in common with the Kings of Judah) but eternal birth is celebrated. For it is concerning something that is proper and peculiar to him alone, not what is common to others, that this is the point at issue, from which, namely, such great splendor ought to have accrued to that city, that it deserved to be preferred to any others whatsoever. Which must also be opposed to the corruption of Volkel. Certainly, if he had wished to commend him from a famous family, and one ancient, he would have traced his origin from Abraham, which in antiquity far surpassed the Davidic one, which the Photinians wish to be looked to, of which, however, no mention is made here. This is therefore a manifest sρεβλότης [perversity], which neither the words nor the πε- ρισάσεις [circumstances] of the text support. For even if those words עולם & קדם, taken separately, may sometimes occur regarding time: yet when joined, as is done in this place, mikedem, mime olam, they cannot be taken otherwise than regarding eternity. Add that the prefix מ is rightly rendered BEFORE, as Tarnovius teaches from Prov. 8:23, Ps. 90:2, 93:2, Is. 43:13, that the goings forth of Christ were before the beginning of all things, before the days of the age, or of the world. Nor does the word מוצאתיו have any other sense than that in which the verb יצא was used before, namely the sense of birth: since that word does not sound of house & family, nor does anything occur in the text. Cocceius is right here against the Jews: it is sufficient if it be proved from this that Christ was before he arose by being born from Bethlehem, and that he was in all the days of the age, and thus in the very beginning of creation: It does not follow, he who is on the first day of the world, he has the beginning of existence: But much more, he who is in the very beginning, he is from eternity, and has no beginning of his life. Certainly, indeed, מן here does not denote after. Nay, the eternity of God is wont to be described by this phrase, as in Ps. 90: וּמֵעוֹלָם עַד־עוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל: Kimchi explains it by בטרם before, and why does he not interpret מִימֵי עוֹלָם in the same way as before the days of the age? The passage cited from Prov. 8 & seq. proves the eternal ὑπόςασιν [hypostasis] & ἐκπόρευσιν [procession] of the Son of God, who is wisdom, to whom belongs the kingdom over all. Some also seek in the plural number the mystery of the twofold going forth of the Messiah, but because it is used only of the eternal generation, it is said to be more rightly used, because that word is destitute of the singular, or also, so that its eminence may be designated. For the Hebrews are wont sometimes to express excellent things in the plural number, to intimate their ἐξοχὴν [preeminence] & excellence. But nothing is more eminent than the eternal generation of the Son of God, whose excellence far exceeds πᾶσαν κατά- ληψιν [every comprehension] of nature. That mystery is truly ἀνεκδιήγητον [inexplicable], truly ἄῤῥητον [ineffable], καὶ ἀνέκφρασον [and inexpressible], Prov. 30:4. Concerning which Cocceius has this: Furthermore, that מוצאת [goings forth] is said here in the plural, that it is placed without emphasis, I cannot be persuaded to believe, namely that the son did not go forth from the Father, as man from man, who begins to be when he is poured forth from man, and when he has gone forth, ceases to be poured forth and to go forth. In all the days of the age the Son goes forth from the Father, and is the eternal ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης αὐτ̄ [brightness of his glory]. There is a certain συγκaτά- βασις [condescension] to the smallness of our intellect, when that which is eternal is compared to our days and moments, and is distinguished from them. Thus you are the same, and your years do not end. Ps. 102:28. Years are attributed to God insofar as they coexist with his eternity to us. But because the moments of eternity do not pass away, he denies that the years of God end, and depart as ours do. Likewise Dan. 7:9, עַתִּיק יוֹמִין [Ancient of Days] remaining in days, i.e.

e. whose days remain and do not slip away. Calvin's gloss on the eternal decree has already been defeated by our blessed Aegidius Hunnius, nor could Pareus defend his teacher, without being forced to admit that he was reluctant to depart from the common opinion, because the Prophet does not say that the decree which consists of all things from eternity went forth, but that the going forth itself is from the days of eternity, and the going forth of the Messiah cannot pertain to anything other than the eternal generation: nor is it to be considered here what can be extorted from the Jews, since even that is never extorted from them, that Christ is preached as the father of eternity, and finally that the Prophet distinctly joins the going forth from Bethlehem and the eternal goings forth. Since therefore Calvin weakens such a notable testimony of the eternity of Christ with this gloss, and betrays it to both Jews and Arians, with what conscience does Pareus still contend that the interpretation of Calvin is neither impious nor Jewish? Therefore, Fridericus Spanheim rashly asserts the innocence of Calvin as having been solidly defended here by Pareus, and in vain desires candor and Christian charity in the blessed Hunnius: since it is a matter of candor to call a spade a spade, nor is that charity sincere which neglects the glory of divine truth. For although Calvin says that the Prophet joins these two things together, that Christ was the eternal Word, through whom the world was created, and from that time was destined by the eternal counsel of God to be the head of the Church, yet that which he gives with one hand he takes away again with the other, as is the custom of those who have a νῦς ἀδόκιμος [reprobate mind], for he explains his goings forth as being eternal in no other way than this: that it had already been decreed long ago that he would come from Bethlehem who would govern the elect: Whence finally Spanheim himself contradicts this sense. I do not deny that I judge the more common interpretation, which explains those goings forth מקדם מימי עולם as the eternal generation of the Son of God, to be more solid and true, and I subscribe to it with all my heart. It is strange, therefore, that Spanheim should patronize those who explain the goings forth by works, as Ribera does, or as Munster does, who refer those words also to the promises concerning the Messiah made from the beginning of the world, or as Junius and Tremellius do, who refer them to the light of the Word and the power of works, by which he revealed himself to all from the beginning (to which Piscator also assents). For even if they did not otherwise doubt the eternal Deity or generation of the Son of God, yet this oracle was not to be derogated from, and those who derogate from it are by no means worthy of patronage (however much they may not otherwise act with the Arians), because they offer violence to such an illustrious testimony of Scripture. We note the very conclusion of Spanheim, and how it has been proved by him, namely that it is to be understood with Athanasius and other orthodox Fathers as the προαιώνιον [pre-eternal] generation of the Messiah from the Father. (1) Because ומוצאתיו can be referred neither to the eternal decree, nor to the works already long since performed by the Messiah, nor can it have any other suitable meaning. (2) Because the word מוצא can be referred quite suitably to the generation of the Son of God, and is used elsewhere concerning the rising of the Sun, the issuing of waters from a spring, the bringing forth of speech, and other things of that kind, by which that most holy mystery can sometimes be aptly adumbrated for us in accordance with the capacity of our weakness. Rightly, therefore, were these things added by the Prophet, lest it should be thought that the Messiah about to come forth from Bethlehem was merely a man and a bare creature, who would arise only in time, just as the Prophets elsewhere are accustomed to indicate and inculcate the twofold nature of the Messiah throughout. (3) Because the doubling of the words מקדם מימי עולם cannot but designate the highest ἀϊδιότης of this antiquity of the Messiah, and consequently his eternity. (4) Because here other predicates arguing for infinite power are set forth concerning this subject. (5) Because other parallel passages teach the same thing, that the Messiah was begotten by God, and at the same time is the father of eternity. (6) Because this going forth is distinguished from a going forth, and generation from generation, namely, the temporal going forth from Bethlehem from the eternal going forth, and the temporal generation from the eternal. Nor is it to be wondered at that the Prophet uses the plural number מוצאות and makes mention of goings forth, not of a going forth, not as Mariana and others wish, to indicate both nativities of Christ, both divine and human, for the following words do not allow it, or either by an enallage of number customary to the Hebrews when they speak of an excellent thing, or because the mystery of the eternal generation is perennial, and can be narrowed to no difference of time, so that it might be shown that that emanation of the Son of God from the Father is not a transient or transitory action, but a certain continuous and perpetual ἀπόῤῥοιὰν [outflow] by which, as the Father has life in himself, so he has given to the Son, and gives him to have life in himself, whence the Messiah is proclaimed as begotten in that today of eternity. So he. Who then still yields the palm to Riebera, Calvin, Münster, Junius, and Tremellius, who here go into all other things? Who excuses their ψευδερμηνείαν [false interpretation]? Coccejus acted candidly while he taxed that distortion on its merits: As regards the person, he has eternal goings forth, and he will be born, that is, the eternal Son of God, and will become man in time. Above ch. II. 13. he is called יהוה and מלך: Compare John I. 1. 1. John I, 1. II. 13. Prov. VIII. the word יצא [to go forth] is often about generation. See Jer. XXX. 21. The Chaldean [Targum] in Jewish and crafty fashion [says] די שמיה אמיר מלכדמין מיומי על מא whose name was spoken of old from the days of eternity. Heretics cannot do better, but this is to do violence to words and to conscience. Also: I would not want anyone to despair of the efficacy of this testimony of Christ's eternity. It is one thing that his goings forth are from before, another that they were decreed before. Neither to the Jews nor to the heretics should that distortion of words be granted; let us believe the same one who called the King of Israel and Teacher of the Gentiles Jehovah, asserting the twofold birth of Christ, one to the Φανέρωσιν ἐν σαρκί [manifestation in the flesh], the other, by which he is the eternal God, and without which he could be neither the sponsor according to the eternal Spirit, nor the Hope, and assertor and intercessor of Israel. Because of the hardness of the Jews, we ought not to omit the express senses of Scripture, and evacuate its power. For to what end would it be inculcated here that the birth of Christ from the Davidic race was decreed from eternity, since it is established by itself that nothing happens without God's eternal decree, and he was promised from the first age of the world? Thus far he. Concerning which the blessed Luther had also warned: The following particle, whose goings forth are from of old, is especially to be noted. For just as the rest that follow show the office of Christ: so this particle depicts the person, so that we may understand of what kind of Lord he speaks. Therefore, as far as the meaning is concerned, it agrees plainly with that of John: In the beginning was the Word. Also John 8. Before Abraham was, I am. Col. I. He is the firstborn of every creature. For the word (Mazaothaf) which we translate as goings forth is not to be depraved in the Jewish manner, as if it meant promised from eternity or of old. It signifies substance and being itself, that he existed from the days of eternity, before time or any other creature existed. Just as Paul therefore significantly said: Born of a woman in time, to show that he existed before time. Also, according to the flesh the son of David, to show that he existed before he put on this flesh. Here, therefore, he first distinguishes this (Moschel) or Lord, not only from all men, but also from all Angels. For there is a time when neither man nor angels existed, but then that Lord had his goings forth, nor did he begin to exist then for the first time.

Add on account of the Jesuit Riebera, another of the same stamp from the same society, Cornel. à Lapide, who says, p. 429, all the Orthodox confess that this treats of true eternity: although some understand the eternity of predestination, not of generation, but wrongly. For to go forth is not to be predestined, but to emanate, to be begotten, to be born, as he said a little before: Out of you shall come forth to me, that is, shall be born, he who is to be Ruler in Israel. Therefore, in his judgment, Riebera would not be orthodox.

Eighthly, the Prophet further explained who that Ruler in Israel is, v. 4. And he shall stand, and shall feed in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God, and they shall be converted, because then he shall be magnified UNTO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH. For that was fulfilled not in Zerubbabel, or any other Prince, but in Christ alone, who stood as Ruler in Israel, by which word his care and providence, as well as his vigilance and constancy, is noted; and he fed, and even now feeds the faithful in the strength of the Lord, as his sheep, John X. So that he may be magnified unto the ends of the earth. Whence Spanheim rightly [says] l.c. p. 430. He is said to be one to be magnified to the ends of the earth; to whom indeed, coming forth from Bethlehem, can that be adapted, except to the Messiah, and to our Messiah? To whom that which Psalm II says corresponds best, where God is said to have given him the nations as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth for a possession. Thus by these characters others are also noted: the conversion of the Gentiles v. 3; that the brothers of the Messiah, who are to be converted to the Israelites, [are] the Kingdom of the Messiah; that it is to be administered not tyrannically, but in a pastoral manner: the weapons of the Messiah, which are not to be spears, a sword, or other corporal weapons, but the proclamation of the Gospel, which is the power of God, Rom. 1, 16; as well as the amplitude of the kingdom v. 4; and peace in the kingdom of the Messiah v. 5; see Dn. D. Muller, Judaism. c. XI. 403. Here the office of Christ, says Spanheim p. 433, is prefigured by excellent characters, that he had to be a ruler, and that indeed ἐξόχως [preeminently] such, but also a shepherd, that ἀρχιποιμὴν [chief shepherd] of 1 Pet. V. 4, who had to lay down his life for his sheep. What kind of weapons ought his to be, what equipment, what basis, what virtue, what auspices? The strength of Jehovah, and the majesty of his name. And indeed the powerful hand of God so exerted itself at his arrival, that his name became famous and was exalted, and is exalted even today to the ends of the earth. But of these things later. Now we only urge primarily the explanation handed down in the N.T. Namely, that the Jews ὁμοθυμαδὸν and in a common council gathered for that purpose by King Herod, without hesitation, accepted this as κυρίαν δόξαν, and in a synodical conclusion handed it down and defined the aforementioned in this place to be ῥητῶς, not of Zorobabel or some other Prince in Judea, but the homeland and birth of the Messiah. For when King Herod consulted them, when they had gathered in council, all the chief priests and scribes of the people, where Christ ought to be born? all with unanimous voice and opinion answered, and said: in Bethlehem of Judea, for thus it is written by the Prophet: (Micah) And you Bethlehem of the land of Judah are by no means least among the princes of Judah: For out of you shall come a Leader who shall rule my people Israel Matt. II. 4. 5. 6. To contradict this explanation handed down from the sense of the Jewish Church, and approved by the Evangelist with tacit consent, is more than to Judaize; and to oppose oneself directly to the Christian faith. Add here the passage John VII. 42. Does not the Scripture say that from the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was, Christ shall come? Where does the Scripture of the O.T. say this, if not in this place? It is manifest therefore from the common sense of the O.T. Church, and the consent of the Christian Church, that the Messiah ought to have arisen from Bethlehem by the force of this prophecy, and according to its literal sense. Tenth, the Grotian ψευδερμηνεία is condemned as Jewish, having long since been condemned in the heretic Theodore of Mopsuestia, who likewise understood by this Ruler of Israel Zorobabel in the 5th Council of Constantinople, Act II, as the Council

Under Vigilius the Roman, as Cornelius à Lapide notes, who observes that all orthodox Greeks and Latins understand this Ruler to be Christ, and that it is certain in matters of faith that no one other than Christ is to be understood: Grotius, who otherwise showed himself not uncompliant with the sayings and counsels of the Jesuits, ought not to have contradicted this, nor to have opposed those things which are certain regarding faith and approved by the common suffrage of the ancient Doctors, for the sake of the Jews. Therefore, the passage where Theodoret rebukes the Jews of his own time strikes also at the Judaizing Grotius: the Jews of our time have attempted to accommodate this to Zerubbabel, openly attacking the truth, nor do they blush when they hear that his goings forth are from of old, from the days of eternity. And indeed, after the captivity, Zerubbabel was born in Babylon, and took his name from the place. The ancient Jews, similarly to those of our age, understood this prophecy: but many years after Zerubbabel, when asked by Herod where Christ would be born, they brought this testimony to him. Hence, therefore, it is clear how perversely the Jews of our memory interpret the meaning of the Prophet. It is evident from the Targum that the ancient Jews were sounder. 'From thee before me shall come forth the Messiah,' and from the Talmud in Cheleck, where it is taught from chapter V of Micah that the Messiah, the Son of David, will not come until the wicked kingdom (so they call the Roman) rules the whole world for nine months. Indeed, there were even some more recent ones, R. Solomon Iarchi, who says thus on this passage: 'Thou hast deserved to be the least of the families because of the profanation of Ruth the Moabitess among you; from thee shall come forth to me the Messiah, the son of David,' just as it is said (Psalm 118:22), 'The stone which they rejected,' and likewise R. David Kimchi. Whereby you cannot be reckoned among the chief cities of Judah, in respect of which you are the least, nevertheless from you shall come forth to me the Messiah. For he shall be of the seed of David, who was born from Bethlehem: and also R. Isaac Ben Abraham, who in his book against the Nazarene Jesus, ch. XXXIII, likewise confesses that this oracle concerns the Messiah; let Jerome on the holy faith, book c. 3, also be compared.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET TU BETHLEHEM EPHRATA] At tu, redit ad id quod dixerat supra IV. 8. ut sæpe eadem repe- tunt Prophetæ, quo magis ea animis hæreant. Beth- lehem Ephrata eadem est, quæ & Bethlehem Judæ, ut di- ximus ad Matth. II. 6.

PARVULUS ES IN MILLIBUS JUDA] Potest commode per interrogationem legi, parvane sis, id est, ha- bearis à populo Judæ? quæ loquendi formula vehementer negat, ut ad dictum Matthæi locum notavimus; potest et- iam verti: parum est ut sis, id est, locum tuum habeas inter Chiliarchas Judæ. Longe major tibi honor desti- natur.

EX TE MIHI EGREDIETUR] Id est, nascetur, Sic enim יצא sumitur Gen. XVII. 6. XXV. 25. Es. XI. 1. natus ex Bethlehemo Zorobabel recte dicitur, quod ex Davidis familia esset, quæ orta Bethlehemo.

ET EGRESSUS EJUS AB INITIO, A DIE- BVS ÆTERNITATIS] Origo ipsi (Zorobabeli) ab olim à temporibus longis. Id est, originem trahit à domo illustri antiquitus, & per quingentos annos regnatrice.

Depravatio vaticinii de Messiæ patria perquam illustris detestanda, qua plane Judaizat Grotius. Eadem hic prædicere Michæam, quæ aliis verbis c. IV. 8. vaticinatus erat, minus luculentum est. Si tamen illa hisce gemina sint, utrobique patriam Christi designatam fuisse, illic obscurius, hic vero luculentius, dicendum fuerit. Zorobabeli hæc nullatenus conveniunt, etsi nonnulli ex Judæis ad eundem hoc vaticinium detorquere ausi sint, quos cæcos Ductores hic, ut in multis aliis sequu- tus est Noster. Judæos enim Chrysostomi æta- te de Zorobabele hæc explicasse Chrysostomus ad Matth. II. ac Theodoretus ad h. l. testatur. Repro- bandam autem etiam illam de Zorobabele Glos- sam Judaicam hæc docent: Primo quod nullum vestigium sit in textu de Zorobabele; Neque an- tecedentia, quæ à v. 11. cap. præcedentis Michæas prædixit, ad ejus tempora spectent, neque conse- quentia ad eundem pertineant. Deinde quum occasione liberationis ab obsidione Assyriorum ad hoc vaticinium deveniat Propheta, nullum hic lo- cum habet Zorobabel, de Messia autem commo- de agere poterat, sive cum Theodoreto hæc ita con- nectas, ac si dicat: Vastabitur militaris turma Sen- nacheribi, at non viribus tuis ô Jerusalem, sed vi- ribus Christi, olim è Bethlehem secundum carnem o- rituri, quemadmodum Esaias c. VII. liberationem Judæorum de manu latronis Syriæ & Assyriæ cum vaticinio de nativitate Christi, cujus virtute illa fa- cta est, conjunxit: sive cum Castrio dicas, Michæam prospexisse obsessam Jerusalem ab Assyrio & viculos ei finitimos captos, & desolatos, oculos mentis conjecisse in Bethlehem, ac vidisse eam, quæ forte tunc capta, & subversa erat, futuram patriam, matremq́; illius Dominatoris, qui Judæos è suis af- flictionibus erat liberaturus, & è manu hostium re- demturus, ac dixisse, & tu Bethlehem utut parvula sis, & non potens Assyrio resistere, produces ex te Dominatorem Israel Messiam. B. Höpfnerus post denunciatam captivitatem restitutionem politiæ promitti notat, quod non tantum Hierosolymam recuperaturi sint, sed & parvos vicos & oppida, quale erat Bethlehem, futura Messiæ patria; ut simul indicetur causa finalis liberationis Judæo- rum, nativitas Christi secundum carnem. Tertio urbs natalis & patria hic designatur istius Domi- natoris, de quo vaticinatur Propheta: uti enim certum est per egressum ex Bethlehem nativitatem indicari, & fatetur id Grotius: EGREDIETUR ex Bethlehem, idem esse quod nascetur, quia sic יצא sumitur Gen. XXV. 25. & c. XVII. 6. Es. XI. 6. ita nulla ratione admittenda illa στρεβλότης, natum ex BETHLEHEMO recte dici, qui ex Davidis fa- milia sit, quæ BETHLEHEMO orta. Ubi e- nim ejusmodi phrasis in scriptura? Et annon to- to cœlo distant, nasci ex alicujus Bethlehemida familia, & egredi vel nasci ex BETHLEHEM?

Si illi è Bethlehem nati dicendi, qui ex Davidis fa- milia egreffi funt, Salomo etiam, atque omnes Re- ges Juda è Bethlehem prognati erunt. Atqui hic peculiare quoddam axioma exprimitur oppidulo illi proprium; & commendatur id, aliisque præ- fertur ob hanc ἐξοχὴν, quod ex illa civitate oritu- rus sit Dominator in Israël. Non ergo familia ali- cujus Bethlehemitæ, sed ortus è Bethlehem, ceu natali solo, respicitur. Jam Zorobabel neutiquam natus est in Bethlehem. Nec uspiam id Scriptura docet. Neque congruit Chronologia. Habemus etiam in eo confitentem Grotium. Natus potius ille in Babel, unde ipsum Zorobabel dictum plerique autumant, quasi semen Babel, quod in ca- ptivitate Babylonica natus, boni omnis causa id nominis datum sit.

Quarto certum est de aliqua prærogativa Beth- lehem hoc loco sermonem esse. Verba Michææ per interrogationem reddit Grotius. Parvane sis, id est, habearis à populo Juda, ut hac loquendi for- mula vehementer negetur, eam parvam habendam esse. Quo pacto verba Matthæi cum verbis Pro- phetæ conciliarunt Isidorus, ut & Ludov. Vives in lib. XXIX. August. de C. D. c. XXX. nec non Franc. Riebera, Cornelius Iansenius, tum è Reformatis Io- hannes Drusius, Frider. Spanhemius, & alii, quem- admodum & Codices Gothici Isidori antiquissimi in Ecclesia Toletana legerunt, & tu Bethlehem, Ephrata, numquid parvula es? Solent quidem E- bræi suas interrogationes etiam aliter formare, verum negari non potest, quin aliquando apud illos eæ quoque lateant, & ex sensu tamen elicien- dæ sint. Explicationem alteram: parum est, ut sis, id est, locum tuum habeas inter Chiliarchas Judæ, ab urbano Regio in Dialog. de Conc. Christi Emaunt. f. 21. Osiandro, Forstero mutuatam, Angelus Ca- ninius improbat, & quamvis eam Lud. de Dieu tuea- tur, non tamen illa omnino placet Frid. Spanhe- mio, (licet adversus insectationem Rieberæ ipsam defendat) p. II. Dub. Evangel. XLV. p. 422. im- primis ideo, quod Ebræi in hac loquendi forma nun- quam utantur על צעיר, sed מן צעיר quod repugnent LXX. Interpp paraphrasis Chaldaica, & pleriq; In- terpp sive Judæi sive Christiani. De quo videatur Hackspan. in h. l. Clariss. Hottinger. in histor. Crea- tion. p. 16. ex Eduardo Peckok in Miscell, not. c. 2. notat, nomen צעיר Ier. XLIIX. 4. Zach. XIII. 9. Ducem, Principem, Judicem, adeog; non parvum tantum, sed & magnum, excellentem significare, at- que ita ἐναντιοφάνειαν, quæ magna hactenus exercuit ingenia inter Michæam & Matthæum solide tolli! Id extra dubium est, eximiam quandam ἐξοχὴν hujus urbis exprimi, quam à natalibus hujus Dominato- ris in Israël consequutura sit. Si autem ille non ex urbe Bethlehem egressum, vel natales suos habuit, sed in Babel, aut alibi, quomodo inde Bethlehemo decus conciliari potuit? Num accessit isti oppidu- lo ex eo novus splendor, præ aliis Judææ civitati- bus quod Salomo Rex Israelis sapientissimus, quod Ezechias Rex pientissimus, quod alii magni Reges in Judæa extiterint, num inde celebrari ita poterat Bethlehem, quod μηδαμῶς ἐλαχίση nequaquam parvissima, ut cum Lucretio ita loquamur, sit in millibus Juda, & quidem hoc pacto quia EX IPSA egressurus erat Dominator in Israël? Quapro- pter ita concludimus: Ob cujus Dominatoris è Bethlehem nati eminentiam insignem maxime celebratur Bethlehem, ille Bethlehemum pro na- tali suo vel patria agnoscit. At Zorobabel non a- gnoscit Bethlehemum pro natali solo. Ergo Zo- robabel non est Dominator ille, ob cujus ceu è Bethlehem nati eminentiam insignem maxime hic

Bethlehem celebratur. Verba Prophetæ בְּאַלְפֵי cum redduntur à Matthæo ἐν ἡγεμόσιν, nihil dero- gatur vel sensui Prophetæ, vel dignitati commen- dationis. Ea enim notatur civitas, quæ non est parva æstimanda inter chiliarchas Juda. Siqui- dem illæ urbes principes, quæ amplæ & populo- sæ, in quibus multæ hominum chiliades: quem- admodum distributus erat populus Judaicus in Decurias, centurias, Chiliadas illisque Præfecti Decuriones, Centuriones, Chiliarchæ, Exod. XVIII. 21. Jud. VI. 18. 1. Sam. X. 19. Et dici possit Prophetam collective loqui de chiliadibus, Mat- thæum δεικτικῶς de Ducibus chiliadum vel chiliar- chis. Tales enim erant præfecturæ, ut quæ urbs posset cum pagis 3000. hominum educere ha- buerit etiam tres Chiliarchas. Docet ergo exi- guum esse oppidum, & nullius fere potentiæ.

Quinto de tali מוֹשֵׁל Dominatore sermo est, qui non in populo tantum duarum tribuum, sed in Israël, h. e. universo XII. tribuum populo domina- turus sit, quod Zorobabeli non competit: item qui non inferioris dignitatis, potestatis & gloriæ sit futurus, quam David Bethlehemita, sed eminen- tioris potius ac sublimioris. Nam si dignitate, potestate, virtute ac gloria non prævaliturus ille dominator sit, major Bethlehemo honor ab ejus egressu ex Bethlehem accedere non potuit, quam ille, quem à Davide cive suo jam pridem consecu- ta fuerat. Qualem certe honorem à Zorobabele consequi non potuit, sed à Messia, cujus aliquam imaginem David gessit, adepta est.

Sexto agitur hic de dominatore Isrælis ἐξοχι- xῶς ita dicti, ac κατ’ αἰτωιομασίαν, quem Israël diu expectarat, quique jam pridem à DEO ipfi destinatus erat, qui DEO ipsi egressurus erat ex Bethlehem: ideo MIHI, inquit, cum emphasi e- gredietur, quod Matthæus eo accepisse videtur, quod populum DOMINI vel Israelem, qua popu- lus DOMINI erat, gubernare ac pascere debeat. Quod proprium est Messiæ. Hic enim Moschel est in universo Israele, qua populus Domini est Es. XLIV. 5. Rom. IX. 6. seqq. & DEO Patri egredi debuit ad cujus unius honorem, & gloriam, ceu electus ille Dominus, in quo uno ipse benepla- citum suum habuit.

Septimo, de illo dominatore sermo est, qui præter egressum è Bethlehem futurum vel nativi- tatem temporalem egressionem, מִקֶּדֶם מִימֵי עוֹלָם ab initio, à diebus æternitatis, h. e. nativitatem ha- buit æternam. Quod non convenit Zorobabeli, sed uni CHRISTO, qui ab æterno egressus est per ge- nerationem à Patre Prov. VIII. 23. Ut detorqueret id Grotius ad Zorobabelem, & metaphrasin vel translationem aliam finxit: origo ipsi ab olim, à tem- poribus longis, & paraphrasin insolentem atque in- usitatam verbis istis induxit h. m. Originem trahit à domo illustri antiquitus, & per 500. annos regna- trice. At egressus non originem vel prosapiam, sed nativitatem notat Gen. X. 14. cap. XXXV. 19. Jud. IX. 30. 1. Par. II. 35. Job. I. 25. neque uspiam Ebræis familia dicitur מֹצָאוֹת sed vel בַּיִת vel מִשְׁפָּחָה vel תּוֹלְדוֹת vel denique שְׁבָטִים, Illud vero de nativitate adhibetur: neque de eo du- bium est penes Interpp. sicut ipse Grotius reddi- dit: ex te mihi egredietur, id est, nascetur. Nec de Antiquitate familiæ dominatoris in Israel ul- lum hic verbum, sed de egressu ab initio à diebus æternitatis ipsius dominatoris, cujus non antiqua prosapia (hanc enim communem habuit Zoro- babel cum Regibus Juda) sed nativitas æterna ce- lebratur. Nam de aliquo, quod ipsi uni pro- prium ac peculiare est, non quod commune aliis, hic agitur, ex quo sc. tantus splendor civitati illi accidere debuit, ut quibusvis aliis præferri merea- tur. Quod etiam corruptelæ Volkelii opponendum. Certe si à familia celebri commendare voluisset, eaque antiqua Dominatorem, ab Abrahamo ejus originem duxisset, quæ antiquitate longe supera- bat Davidicam, quam Photiniani respici volunt, cujus vero hic nulla facta est mentio. Manifesta er- go hæc sρεβλότης est, quam nec verba, neque πε- ρισάσεις textus ferunt. Etiamsi enim voces illæ עולם & קדם seorsim acceptæ de tempore quando- que occurrant: Conjunctæ tamen illæ, uti hoc lo- co factum, mikedem, mime olam, non aliter, quam de æternitate accipi possunt. Adde, quod מ præfixum recte reddatur ANTE, ut è Prov. IIX. 23. Ps. XC. 2. XCIII. 2. Es. XLIII. 13. docet Tarnovius, quod egressiones Christi fuerint ante rerum omnium ini- tium, ante Dies seculi, seu mundi. Neque alium sen- sum vox מוצאתיו habet, quam quo adhibitum verbum יצא antea, sensum nempe nativitatis: quum de domo & familia neque vox illa sonet, nec quicquam in textu occurrat. Recte hic Coccejus contra Judæos: sufficit si probetur hinc Christum fuis- se antequam è Bethlehem nascendo oriretur, & quod fuerit omnibus diebus seculi, & sic in ipso creationis ex- ordio: Non sequitur, qui primo die mundi est, is ini- tium extandi habet: Sed multo magis, qui in ipso ini- tio est, is ab æterno est, & initium suæ vitæ non habet. Certe quidem מן à hic non notat post. Imo hac phrasi æternitas Dei describi solet ut Psal. XC. וּמֵעוֹלָם עַד־עוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל: Kimchius id explicat per בטרם ante, & quare hic non eodem modo מִימֵי עוֹלָם ante dies seculi interpretatur? Locus ex Prov. 8. & seq. ci- tatus probat æternam ὑπόςασιν & ἐκπόρευσιν Filii Dei, qui est sapientia, cui competit regnum in omnia. Quidam etiam in plurali numero quærunt myste- rium egressionis geminæ Mesiæ, sed quia is solum de æterna generatione adhibetur, rectius usurpari dicitur, quia vox illa singulari destituitur, vel etiam, ut ejusdem eminentia designetur. Solent enim E- bræi res excellentes quandoque plurali numero efferre, ad innuendam earum ἐξοχὴν & excellen- tiam. Nihil autem eminentius est æterna Filii Dei generatione, cujus excellentia πᾶσαν κατά- ληψιν τῆς φύσεως longe excedit. Mysterium illud vere ἀνεκδιήγητον, vere ἄῤῥητον, καὶ ἀνέκφρασον est Prov. XXX. 4. De quo Coccejus ita habet: Cæterum, quod hic dicitur pluraliter מוצאת ἐκπο- ρεύσεις, id absque emphasi positum, ut credam, persua- deri non possum, nempe filius non egressus est à Pa- tre, ut homo ex homine, qui incipit esse, quum ex ho- mine funditur, & cum egressus est, fundi egredique de- finit. Omnibus diebus seculi egreditur Filius à Pa- tre, & æternum est ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης αὐτ̄. Est quædam ad exilitatem intellectus nostri συγκaτά- βασις, quando, quod æternum est, & diebus nostris momentisque comparatur, & ab iisdem distinguitur. Sic tu idem es, & anni tui non finiuntur. Ps. CII. 28. Anni Deo attribuuntur quatenus æternitati ipsius no- stri coexsistunt. Sed quia æternitatis momenta non transeunt, annos Dei negat finiri, & abire ut nostros. Item Dan. VII. 9. עַתִּיק יוֹמִין permanens diebus, h.

e. cujus dies manent & non labuntur. Calvini glos- sema de decreto æterno profligavit jam B. Ægid. Hunnius noster, nec tueri præceptorem potuit Pareus, quin fateri cogeretur, sibi religionem esse à communi sententia discedere, quia Propheta non egres- sus decretum quod constat omnium rerum ab æterno esse, sed egressum ipsum à diebus æternitatis esse dicat, & egressus Messiæ æternus non possit alio, quam ad æternam generationem pertinere: nec esse hic respi- ciendum quid Judæis extorqueri possit, siquidem etiam illud illis nunquam extorqueatur, quod Christus pa- ter prædicetur æternitatis, & deniq; Prophetam di- stinctè egressum ex Bethlehem, & æternos egressus conjungere. Cum ergo Calvinus hoc glossemate tam insigne testimonium æternitatis Christi ener- vet, idque cum Judæis tum Arianis prodat im- pie, qua conscientia adhuc Pareus interpretatio- nem Calvini, nec impiam esse, nec Judaicam contendit? Frider. ergo Spanhemius innocentiam Calvini à Pareo hic solide assertam, temerarie af- firmat, ac frustra desiderat candorem & charita- tem Christianam in B. Hunnio: siquidem cando- ris sit, scapham scapham dicere, neque charitas illa sincera sit, quæ gloriam veritatis divinæ negli- git. Quanquam enim Calvinus dicat, Prophetam simul hæc duo conjungere, Christum fuisse æternum ser- monem, per quem creatus est mundus, inde fuisse de- stinatum æterno Dei consilio, ut esset Ecclesiæ caput, Id tamen, quod una manu dat altera rursum ra- pit, uti solent quibus νῦς ἀδόκιμος, nam egressus ejus esse æternos, non aliter explicat, quam ita: jam fuisse olim decretum, venturum ex Bethlehem, qui gubernet electum: Unde tandem huic sensui con- tradicit ipse Spanhemius. Non diffiteor, me commu- niorem interpretationem, qua egressus illos מקדם מימי עולם de æterna filii Dei generatione exponit, solidiorem & veriorem judicare, & illi ex animo sub- scribere. Mirum ergo, quod Rieberæ egressus per o- pera exponenti, quod Munstero, voces illas etiam ad promissiones de Messia inde à mundi initio factas, quod Junio & Tremellio ad lucem Verbi & virtutem operum, quibus omnibus inde se à principio patefecit, referentibus (quibus etiam Piscator annuit) pa- trocinetur Spanhemius. Nam etsi alioquin de æter- na Deitate, aut generatione Filii Dei non dubita- rint illi non tamen erat huic oraculo derogan- dum, & qui ei derogant, haud quaquam patrocinio digni sunt, (utut alias cum Arianis haud faciant) quod tam illustri scripturæ testimonio vim infe- rant. Notamus ipsam Spanhemii conclusionem, & quomodo ab eo probata sit, intelligendam nempe esse cum Athanasio & Patribus aliis orthodoxis προαιώνιον Messiæ γέννησιν ἐκ τ̃ Πατρὸς. (1) Quia ומוצאתיו nec ad decretum æternum, nec ad ope- ra jam olim edita à Messia referri potest, nec aliam significationem commodam habere (2) Quia vox מוצא commode admodum ad generationem filii Dei referri potest, & alibi adhibetur de exortu Solis, de exitu aquarum è scaturigine; de pro- latione sermonis, & aliis id genus, quibus ali- quando apposite pro imbecillitatis nostræ ratione mysterium illud sanctissimum nobis adumbrari potest. Merito ergo hæc à Propheta adjecta, ne pu- taretur Messias è Bethlehem proditurus esse tan- tum homo, & nuda creatura, cum tempore tan- tum exoritura, prout & alibi Prophetæ passim geminam Messiæ naturam indicare, & inculcare consuevêre. (3) Quia geminatio vocum מקדם מימי עולם non potest non summam ἀϊδιότη desι- gnare antiquitatis hujus Messiæ, adeoque æterni- tatem. (4) Quia hic alia prædicata virtutem infini- tam arguentia de hoc subjecto efferuntur. (5) Quia alia locaparalella idem docent, Messiam esse ge- nitum à Deo, & simul patrem æternitatis. (6) Quia contradistinguitur hic exitus exitui, generatio ge- nerationi, exitus nimirum è Bethlehem tempora- lis exitui æterno, generatio temporaria æternæ. Nec mirandum, Prophetam uti numero plurali מוצאות & egressuum meminisse, non egressus fa- ctum id non ut & Mariana, & alii volunt, ad nativi- tatem utramq; Christi tum divinam tum humanam indicandam nec enim verba sequentia id patiun- tur, seu vel per enallagen numeri consuetam He- bræis, quando de re eximia loquuntur, vel quia mysterium æternæ generationis perenne est, & ad nullam temporis differentiam arctari potest, ut o- stenderetur, emanationem illam Filii Dei à Patre non esse actionem transeuntem, vel transitoriam, sed continuam & perpetuam quandam ἀπόῤῥοιὰν qua ut Pater habet vitam in seipso, sic & filio dedit, & dat habere vitam in seipso, unde in hodie illo æ- ternitatis genitus prædicatur Messias. Hæc ille. Qui ergo adhuc Rieberæ, Calvino, Münstero, Junio & Tremellio in alia omnia hic euntibus herbam porrigit? Qui excusat eorum ψευδερμηνείαν? Candidus egit Coccejus, dum contorsionem illam ex merito taxavit: Quoad personam habet egressio- nes æternas, & nascetur, hoc est Filius Dei æternus, & fiet homo in tempore. Supra cap. II. 13. יהוה & מלך appellatur: Confer Johan. I. 1. 1. Joh. I, 1. II. 13. Prov. VIII. verbum יצא de generatione sæ- pe. Vide Jer. XXX. 21. Chaldæus Iudaice & subleste די שמיה אמיר מלכדמין מיומי על מא cujus nomen dictum antiquitus à diebus seculi. Non pos- sunt melius hæretici, sed hoc est facere vim verbis & Conscientiæ. Item: Nolim quemquam de- sperare de testimonio hujus æternitatis Christi effi- cacia. Aliud est, egressiones ejus sunt ab ante, aliud decretæ sunt ante. Neque Judæis neque hæreticis illa contorsio verborum concedenda est; eidem, qui Regem Israelis & Doctorem gentium vocavit Jehovam, credamus asserenti geminam Christi nativitatem, unam ad Φανέρωσιν ἐν σαρ- κί, alteram, qua æternus Deus est, & sine qua nec sponsor secundum Spiritum æternum, nec Spes, & assertor ac intercessor Israelis esse pote- rat. Propter duritiem Judæorum non debemus nos omittere expressos sensus Scripturæ, & eva- cuare potestatem ejus. Nam cui fini hic inculca- retur, decretum esse ab æterno Christi nativitatem ex gente Davidica, quum per se constet, nihil fieri sine Dei æterno decreto, & à prima mundi ætate promissus sit? Hactenus ille. De quo etiam mo- nuerat B. Lutherus: Particula sequens, cujus e- gressiones ab antiquo, præcipue notanda est. Si- cut enim cætera, quæ sequuntur, officium Christi ostendunt: Ita hæc particula personam pingit, ut in- telligamus de quali Domino loquatur. Quod igitur ad sententiam attinet, convenit plane cum illo Iohan- nis: In principio erat verbum. Item Joh. 8. An- tequam Abraham esset, ego sum Col. I. Ipse est primogenitus omnis creaturæ. Neg enim voca- bulum (Mazaothaf) quod nos egressiones vertimus, Iudaico more depravandum est, quod significet ab æterno seu antiquo promissum. Substantiam & i- psum esse significat, quod extiterit à diebus seculi, antequam tempus, aut ulla alia creatura esset. Si- cut Paulus ideo significanter dixit: In tempore na- tus de muliere, ut ostendat eum ante tempus fuisse. Item secundum carnem filius David, ut ostendat eum antequam carnem hanc indueret, extitisse. Hic igitur primum discernit hunc (Moschel) seu Domi- num, non solum ab omnibus hominibus, sed etiam ab Angelis omnibus. Est enim tempus, quo neque ho- mo, neg angeli fuerunt, sed tum habuit ille Do- minus egressiones suas, nec cœpit tum primum esse.

Adde ob Rieberam Jesuitam, alium præcipui commatis ex eadem societate Cornel. à Lapide, qui, omnes, inquit p. 429. Orthodoxi fatentur, hic de vera æternitate agi: licet aliqui æternitatem præ- destinationis, non generationis intelligant, sed perpe- ram. Nam egredi non est prædestinari, sed emanare, gigni, nasci, ut cum paulo ante dixit: Ex te mihi egredietur, id est nascetur, qui sit Dominator in Israël. Non ergo orthodoxus ejus judicio fue- rit Riebera.

Octavo, quisnam ille Dominator sit in Israël, exposuit ulterius Propheta v. 4. Et stabit, & pascet in fortitudine Domini in sublimitate nominis Domini Dei sui, & convertentur, quia tunc magnificabitur USQUE AD TERMINOS TERRÆ. Id enim non in Zorobabele, aut ullo alio Principe, sed in Christo solo impletum est, qui ceù Dominator in Israël stetit, quo verbo cura & providentia, nec non vigilantia & constantia ejus notatur; & pavit, atque etiamnum pascit fideles in fortitudine Do- mini, quasi oves suas Joh. X. Ita ut magnificetur usq; ad fines terræ. Unde recte Spanhemius l.c. p. 430. Magnificandus dicitur ad terminos terræ; Cui vero ex Bethlehem prodeunti id aptari potest, præter- quam Messiæ, & Messiæ nostro? cui respondet opti- me, quod Psalm. II. ubi Deus dicitur dedisse ei gentes hæreditatem, & pro possessione terminos terræ. Ita aliis etiam hi characteres notantur, con- versio gentium v. 3. quod fratres Messiæ, qui ad Is- raelitas convertendi sunt, Regnum Messiæ; quod non tyrannice, sed more pastorali administran- dum id sit: arma Messiæ, quæ non futura lanceæ, gladius, aut alia corporalia arma, sed præconium Evangelii, quod est potentia Dei Rom. 1, 16. nec non amplitudo regni v. 4. & pax in regno; Messiæ v. 5. vid. Dn. D. Muller. Judaism. c. XI. 403. Hic of- ficium Christi, inquit Spanhemius p. 433. eximiis cha- racteribus præfiguratum, quod debuerit esse domina- tor, idq; ἐξόχως talis, sed & pastor, ἀρχιποιμὴν ni- mirum ille 1. Pet. V. 4. qui debuit animam suam po- nere pro ovibus suis. Qualia debebant esse ejus ar- ma, quis apparatus, quæ basis, quæ virtus, quæ auspicia? fortitudo Jehovæ, & sublimitas nominis ejus. Et sane ita potens Dei manus se in illius ad- ventu exeruit, ut nomen ejus inclaruerit & exalta- tum fuerit, & exaltetur hodieque ad terminos ter- ræ. Sed de his postea. Nunc solum urgemus imprimis explicationem in N.T. traditam. Quod nempe Judæi ὁμοθυμαδὸν & in communi concilio à Rege Herode ad id congregato, sine cuncta- tione, hoc ceu κυρίαν δόξαν acceperint, atque in conclusione synodica tradiderint, ac definiverint prædictam hoc in loco esse ῥητῶς, non Zorobabe- lis aut alterius cujusdam Principis in Judæa, sed Messiæ patriam & nativitatem. Consulente enim eosdem Rege Herode, cum in concilio convenis- sent, omnes Principes Sacerdotum & scribas populi, ubi Christus nasci debuit? omnes unanimi voce ac sententia responderunt, ac dixerunt: in Beth- lehem Judææ, sic enim scriptum est per Prophetam: (Michæam) Et tu Bethlehem terræ Judæ nequa- quam minima es in Principibus Juda: Ex te enim exibit Dux qui regat populum meum Israël Matt. II. 4. 5. 6. Cui explicationi ex sensu Ecclesiæ Ju- daicæ traditæ, ac ab Evangelista tacito consensu approbatæ contradicere, est plus quam Judaizare; ac fidei Christianæ se directe opponere. Adde hic locum Johan. VII. 42. Nonne Scriptura dicit, quod ex semine David, & de Betlehem, castello, unde erat David, veniet Christus? ubi hoc dicit scriptura V. T. nisi in hoc loco? Manifestum er- go ex sensu Ecclesiæ V. T. communi, & consen- tu Ecclesiæ Christianæ Messiam è Bethlehem vi hujus vaticinii, ac secundum ejusdem sensum li- teralem oriri debuisse. Decimo damnata Grotia- na ψευδερμηνεία ceu Judaica jam pridem in Theo- doro Mopsvesteno hæretico, qui itidem per Domi- natorem hunc Israelis intellexit Zorobabelem in Concil. Constantinopol. V. Act. II. ut Concilio

Romano sub Vigilio, notante Cornel. à Lap. qui orthodoxos omnes Græcos & Latinos hunc Domina- torem de Christo intelligere, idœ, de fide certum esse, quod non alius, quam Christus intelligendus sit, ad- vertit : hunc audire, neque in his quæ de fide cer- ta sunt, & communi Dd. veterum suffragio com- probata, in Judæorum gratiam contradicere de- bebatGrotius, qui Jesuitarum dictis & consiliis a- lioquin se non inobsequentem præstitit. Quo ergo Theodoretes Judæos sui temporis reprehen- dit h. l. ferit etiam Judaizantem Grotium : Judæi nostri temporis hoc ad Zorobabel accommodare ten- tarunt, apertè veritatem oppugnantes, neque cům audiunt, rubore perfunduntur, quod hujus egressus ab initio à diebus seculi. Et vero post captivitatem Zorobabel Babylone natus fuit, atque à loco nomen duxit. Veteres Judæi similiter, ut hi nostræ ætatis, hanc Prophetiam intellexerunt: sed multis annis post Zorobabel ab Herode interrogati, ubinam nascere- tur Christus, hoc ei testimonium attulerunt. Hinc igitur patet, quam perverse Iudæi nostræ memoriæ sensum Prophetæ interpretentur. Saniores fuisse antiquos Judæos constat è Targum. Ex te coram me prodibit Messias, & è Talmude in Cheleck ubi è cap. V. Mich. docetur, non venturum Messiam Davidis Filium, donec regnum nequam (Romanum ita vocant) toti mundo mensibus novem imperet. Imo etiam fuere nonnulli,recentiores. R. Salomo Iarchi, qui ita in h. l. Meruisti minima esse fami- liarum propter prophanationem Ruth Moabitis apud te, ex te exiet mihi Messias filius David, quomo do dicitur (Psal. 118, 22.) lapis quem reprobarunt & ut & R. David. Kimchi. Quo non possis censer inter urbes principes Juda, quarum respectu mini- ma es, nihilominus tamen ex te exiet mihi Messias. Erit enim de semine David, qui erat ex Bethlehem o riundus : nec non R. Isaac Ben Abraham, qui libr. contra Jes. Nazar. c. XXXIII. itidem fatetur in hoc oraculo de Messia actum esse, conferatur e- tiam Hieronymus de sancta fide l. c. 3.

## 5:3
Verse 3. THEREFORE WILL HE GIVE THEM UP UNTIL THE TIME] Certainly He (God) will deliver them (the Hebrews) up until the time into the dominion of the Chaldeans. IN WHICH SHE THAT TRAVAILETH SHALL BRING FORTH] Until she is freed from her pains. Just as pains are compared to childbirth in IV. 9, 10. So here, the liberation from them is compared to childbirth.

That birth of the one travailing is taken by some as a spiritual birth, just as Theodoret explained, comparing Isaiah LIV, 'Rejoice, O barren one who dost not bear,' etc., as also does Tarnovius among our own. By not a few, it is understood as the birth of the Theotokos. Cornelius à Lapide teaches that this is the sense of the ancients, and declares it in this way: The time in which she that travaileth, or as the Hebrew has it, she that beareth, shall bring forth, is the time in which the Mother of God brought forth Christ in Bethlehem: for she is called 'she that beareth' and 'mother' antonomastically, because her birth was most noble, and therefore most desired by heaven and earth, and this is what that doubling 'she that beareth' signifies, or, as our version has it, 'she that travaileth shall bring forth,' for the word 'travailing' does not signify pain but vehement desire, joy, and the acceleration of the birth. The sense, therefore, is as if he were saying: For this reason, namely because Christ, whom God has decreed and appointed as the savior and Ruler of Israel, will be born in Bethlehem: for this reason He will give them up, that is, He will permit Israel and the Jews to be afflicted by the Assyrians, Chaldeans, and Greeks, until the Mother of God brings forth Christ. For He shall be the redeemer and savior of Israel and of all nations. Thus St. Jerome, Haymo, Remigius, Hugo here, and Eusebius, book 7 of the Demonstratio, chapter 2. The exposition of others pertains to this, which is as follows: the successive affliction of the Synagogue and the Babylonian, Greek, and Roman captivity will endure until she herself brings forth Christ, for He will deliver her from all servitude.

Blessed Luther also approved the same sense with his own calculation. 'This sentence is explained by almost everyone as referring to a spiritual birth, that through the Gospel preached among the nations by the Apostles, a new Church from the nations was brought forth to God; but nothing prevents us from understanding the travailing one most simply as the blessed Virgin, who through the Holy Spirit conceived and brought forth Christ into this world. For the Prophet shows emphasis, and signifies a singular birth, the like of which has not been in the world, nor shall be. Just as Isaiah also in chapter VII uses the same word: A Virgin shall conceive and bring forth a Son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel. The meaning, therefore, is: before that happy birth is brought forth, the people will be variously afflicted by the successors of Alexander, by the Romans, by Herod. But these bodily inconveniences will be compensated for when she who is travailing, that is, she of whose birth the Holy Spirit prophesies, shall have brought forth.' For then it shall come to pass that 'the remnant of his brethren, that is, the remnant of the ten tribes of Israel, shall return to the children of Israel, that is, they shall embrace the Gospel, believe, and be saved.' This seems to be the simplest and genuine meaning, which includes that one concerning the spiritual birth. Thus far Blessed Luther. Osiander and the Vinarie Paraphrases and others of our own agree. Blessed Winkelmann has it thus: THEREFORE WILL HE GIVE. The time of the birth of the Messiah is indicated. For the pious could have asked, when at last will that Moschel, the longed-for Ruler, be born? Micah answers that some delay will still intervene until the time of the Messiah, and that the people will be delivered up to be afflicted, namely by the Assyrians, the Syrians, Antiochus Epiphanes, the Egyptians, and finally also by the Romans. IN WHICH SHE THAT TRAVAILETH SHALL BRING FORTH, namely the Virgin Mary, the Mother of the Messiah. These words, however, contain consolation and a promise: that the kingdom or land of Judah, although it is destined to be miserably afflicted and laid waste, will not nevertheless be utterly destroyed, because it is destined for the birth of the Messiah: just as by this same sign Isaiah confirms the house of Judah against the incursion of Pekah son of Remaliah and Rezin king of Syria, Isaiah VII. B. Hopsnerus in his commentary, still ἀνενδοτω, 'Therefore,' he says, 'He will give prophets, that is, He will allow or permit them to remain after the captivity, until she who is bringing forth shall bring forth, that is, until the Virgin Mary shall bring forth the Messiah into the world.' For the Prophet shows emphasis by the repetition of the same word 'to bring forth,' and teaches that the birth will be singular, the like of which has not been nor will be in the world: just as Isaiah also in chapter VII. 14 uses the same word. And R. Solomon rightly gathers that the discourse here is about a virgin birth, from the fact that no mention is made of a husband. The sense, therefore, of these words is: 'He will give them,' that is, GOD will permit the Jews to possess the region again, and will suffer the Jewish polity to stand for a time, until the virgin brings forth the Messiah. And thus this prophecy will be in agreement with the prophecy of Jacob, Gen. XLIX. Nor does the causal particle THEREFORE, which the Prophet prefixes to this paragraph, stand in the way of our interpretation, for it fits perfectly. For 'therefore,' that is, to this end, God allowed the Mosaic polity to endure, because under it the Messiah was to be born in Bethlehem, and upon this birth taking place, the Jewish Scepter was at the same time to decline and be taken away. Likewise, neither does the following particle, which speaks to us of the conversion of the Gentiles, oppose us: for although at the time of Christ's birth the universal calling of the Gentiles did not immediately take place, yet after the ascension of Christ, while Jerusalem was still standing, it was brought into effect, and before that, the firstfruits of the Gentiles were called to the cradle.

of Christ, Matt. II. Nor do the Belgian Paraphrasts deny it, although they also bring forward other senses. Some deny that it should be understood concerning the delivery into the hands of enemies, and they accept these things rather concerning the preservation of the Jewish people, to which Osiander also accedes: For this reason, says the Prophet, the Lord will give them (the Israelites) back to their homeland for a time, so that for some years they may enjoy the land of Canaan, in which the Messiah was to be born, in which time also the virgin Mary, being with child, will bring forth Christ, God and man. For God restored and preserved the Jewish polity, so that under it Christ, the Savior of the world, might be born according to the promises spoken to the fathers.

Verse of the same. AND THE REMNANT OF HIS BRETHREN] Namely of Zerubbabel, that is, those who will remain from the tribe of Judah.

THEY SHALL BE CONVERTED] They shall return.

TO THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL] With the children of Israel. Thus על is often taken: That is, with the Benjaminites, the Levites, and some also of the other tribes.

There is no place here for Zerubbabel. Nor is the discourse about the return of the Jews with the Benjaminites, but about the conversion of the remnant of the brethren of the ruler in Israel to the children of Israel. The Benjaminites are numbered in the Scriptures to the tribe of Judah, they are not opposed under the name of Israelites after the division of Israel from Judah had taken place. This is therefore a mere distortion of the words of the Prophet, whose sense is, according to the interpreter Tarnovius: And the residue of his brethren shall be converted with the Israelites, that is, the remnant of the nations co-opted by God in Christ shall join themselves to the Church of the N. T. Eph. II. 11. 12. Mal. IV. 5. Luke I. 6. More fully, the blessed Höpfner: The other end of the preserved Jewish polity is the conversion of the remnant of his brethren: that is, both of the rejected ones from the ten tribes, who in their ancestors had once been made not a people of God from being the people of God, and also of the Gentiles, who were likewise strangers, through their departure from God. He predicts that these will return to Christ with the Israelites, that is, with the faithful, and those embracing the doctrine of grace, namely the Israelites of the promise, and Paul testifies that this was fulfilled in Rom. IX. v. 15.

Vers. 3. PROPTER HOC DABIS EOS VSQVE AD TEMPVS] Certe tradet eos (Hebræos Deus) usque ad tem pus in ditionem Chaldæorum. IN QVO PARTVRIENS PARIET] Donec libe retur à doloribus. Sicut dolores comparati sunt parturi gini IV. 9. 10. Ita hic liberatio ab illis partui.

B. Christi Matth. II. Nec abnuunt Paraphrastæ Belgi- ci, etsi alios sensus etiam adducant. Nonnulli ne- gant de traditione in manus hostium ea intelligenda esse, ac de conservatione potius Judaici populi hæc accipiunt, quibus etiam Osiander accedit: Pro- pter hoc, inquit Propheta, dabit eos (Israëlitas) Do- minus reduces in patriam ad tempus, ut per aliquot annos fruantur terra Chanaan, in qua nasci debe- bat Messias, in quo etiam tempore parturiens virgo Maria pariet Christum, Deum & hominem. Deus enim politiam Judaicam restauravit & conserva- vit, ut sub ea Christus mundi Salvator, juxta pro- missiones patribus dictas nasceretur.

Vers. eod. ET RELIQUIÆ FRATRUM EJUS] Nem- pe Zorobabelis, id est, qui de Judæ tribu supererunt.

CONVERTENTUR ] Reverentur.

AD FILIOS ISRAEL] Cum filiis Israel. Ita על sæ- pe sumitur: Id est, cum Benjaminītis, Levitis, & nonnul- lis etiam aliarum tribuum.

Nullus Zorobabeli hic locus. Nec de rever- sione Judæorum cum Benjaminītis, sed de conver- sione reliquiarum fratrum dominatoris in Israel ad fi- lios Israel sermo est. Benjaminītæ annumerantur in Scripturis Judæ tribui, non opponuntur sub Is- raelitarum nomine post factam divisionem Israelis à Juda. Mera ergo hæc verborum Prophetæ de- torsio, quorum sensus est interprete Tarnovio: Et residuum fratrum ejus convertetur cum Israelitis, id est, reliquiæ gentium à Deo cooptatæ in Christo se adjungent Ecclesiæ N. T. Eph. II. 11. 12. Mal. IV. 5. Luc. I. 6. Plenius B. Höpfnerus: Alter finis conservatæ politiæ Iudaicæ est conversio reliquiarum fratrum ejus: h. est, tum rejectitiorum ex decem tri- bubus, qui in suis majoribus olim perditis ex po- pulo Dei facti fuerant non populus Dei, tum etiam Ethnicorum, qui similiter erant extranei, per suam à Deo discessionem. Hos prædicit reversuros ad Christum cum Israelitis, id est, cum fidelibus, & do- ctrinam gratiæ amplectentibus, Israelitis scilicet pro- missionis, idq́; Paulus impletum esse testatur Rom. IX. v. 15.

## 5:4
Verse 4. AND HE SHALL STAND AND FEED] A Hebraism, for he shall continue to feed, that is, to rule the people.

IN THE STRENGTH OF THE LORD IN THE MAJESTY OF THE NAME OF THE LORD HIS GOD] With God strengthening and exalting him, the name of God is frequent among the Hebrews for God himself.

AND THEY SHALL BE CONVERTED] And those who have returned shall dwell securely.

FOR NOW HE SHALL BE MAGNIFIED UNTO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH] Now, that is, immediately after they have returned, the fame of God from that benefit will be propagated far and wide through all lands, see above IV. 1.
