Chapter IV. 1 is rightly compared. For these things pertain to the same times. But that those things are said concerning the most recent time of the Jews, and look to the N. T., has been shown there. Nor did the Jerusalem Synodics in Matt. II accept these things as concerning any other than the Messiah, who took their ποιμανεῖ τὸν λαόν µ8 from there to explain the office of מֹשֵׁל Moschel or ἡγεµόν8, they certainly professed that the same ruler, the Messiah, would be the shepherd of the Lord's people. Add what Spanheim has concerning these on p. 416. Matthew adds by way of explanation, ὅςις ποιμανεῖ, so that he may show of what kind of dominion the Prophet is speaking, which the Messiah was about to exercise, namely of a dominion not political, but pastoral, not violent, but gentle, useful to those over whom he was to rule, namely that the Messiah would institute a pastoral regimen, and would rule by feeding, that is, he would perform all things for his people that belong to a good shepherd, not only by ruling him, but also by feeding, governing, defending, and indeed the people having need of such a regimen like a flock of sheep inept for their own governance or protection. Where at the same time an excellent mixture of the Prophetic and kingly office is hinted at.

Theophylactus: He said he shall shepherd, but he shall not play the tyrant or devour; for the others are kings, not shepherds, but wolves, whereas Christ is the shepherd. The Messiah also truly proposes himself as such in John 10, and in reality has everywhere shown himself to be so. Dare to call the Messiah promiscuously by the Prophets Leader, prince, shepherd, king (Isa. 40:11, Jer. 22:5, Ezek. 33:23, Dan. 9:25), because he ought to unite in himself in the highest degree all the dignities divided among the descendants of David; since he was long ago designated by every one of those orders of men. Thus it is known that kings themselves were called ποιμένας λαῶν (shepherds of the people) by the Gentiles, by which it was shown that peoples do not exist for the sake of kings, but kings for the sake of the people, and that their rule ought to be political and paternal rather than despotic, directive, not coercive, established by love rather than fear. And because τὸ ποιμάινειν (shepherding) includes all-encompassing care, it is transferred everywhere by sacred writers to the ecclesiastical office. Thus also, whether by the Evangelists or by the scribes, it has been shown that the Messiah is that shepherd called such κατ' ἐξοχὴν (by way of eminence), of whom Ezekiel 34:23 says: I will raise up for them one shepherd, who shall feed them (the sheep), my servant David, he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd. Which is also frequent elsewhere among the Prophets, by whom God himself is frequently compared to a shepherd, as in Ps. 23:1 and 77:21. The Vulgate Interpreter here has 'ruler,' which indeed expresses the sense, but not that emphasis of the Messiah's direction, such as that would be in the future, namely, sweet and pastoral. Whence it is vainly excused by Maldonado as more coherent with the word ἡγόμενος (leader). For Matthew was not ignorant of that coherence, nor did he use the word ποιμανεῖ (he shall shepherd) without cause. But by human interpreters, not only the sense is to be expressed, but also the words, where it is a matter of translation.

But above all, there is here a clear proof of the kingdom of Christ, that he who is to be the ruler in Israel is to be magnified even to the ends of the earth, which by no means happened under Zerubbabel, but in the time of the New Testament. Whence Theodoret: And indeed you may see the sacrosanct Church of God gloriously adorned with that name of the Lord, and the name of God celebrated with the highest praises everywhere on land and sea: concerning which the Jews will demonstrate nothing to have been done until the coming of the Lord, and the passion of the savior, and the calling of the Gentiles.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET STABIT ET PASCET ] Hebraismus, pro perget pascere, id est, regere populum.

IN FORTITUDINE DOMINI IN SUBLIMI- TATE NOMINIS DOMINI DEI SUI] Deo ipsum roborante & attollente, nomen Dei pro Deo frequens He- bræis.

ET CONVERTENTUR] Et habitabunt secure illi reversi.

QUIA NUNC MAGNIFICABITUR USQUE AD TERMINOS TERRÆ] Nunc, id est, illico postquam reversi fuerint, Dei fama ex isto beneficio longe lateque propagabitur per terras omnes, vide supra IV. 1.

Recte confertur c. IV. 1. Ad eadem enim tem- pora hæc pertinent. Illa vero de tempore Judæo- rum novissimo dici, & ad N. T. spectare, isthic o- stensum est. Neque de alio, quam Messia accepe- re hæc Synodici Hierosolymitani Matth. II. qui suum ποιμανεῖ τὸν λαόν µ8, inde sumsere ad expli- candum officium מֹשֵׁל Moschel vel ἡγεµόν8, certe eundem illum dominatorem Messiam pastorem fore populi Domini professi sunt. Adde, quæ de his Spanhemius habet p. 416. Addit exposite Matthæus per ἐπεξήγησιν, ὅςις ποιμανεῖ, ut ostendat, de quali dominatione loquatur Propheta, quam sit exerciturus Messias, de dominatione nimirum non politica, sed pa- storalis, non violenta, sed suavi, utili illis, quibus esset imperaturus, Messiam videlicet regimen pastorale instituturum, & pascendo regnaturum, h. e. omnia præstiturum circa populum suum, quæ boni pastoris sunt, illum non tantum regendo, sed & alendo, gu- bernando, defendendo, & populum quidem opus habentem ejusmodi regimine instar gregis ovium ine- pti ad sui gubernationem vel tutelam. Ubi simul innuitur mistura egregia muneris Prophetici & regis.

Theophylactus: ποιμανεῖ εἶπεν ἀλλὰ ὄυ τυραννή- σει ἤ καταφάγεται, ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἄλλοι βασιλεῖς ὄ ποι- μένες, ἀλλὰ λύκοι, ὁ δὲ χρισὸς ποιμὴν. Talem et- iam revera se proponit Messias Joh. X. & reipsa u- bique præstitit. Aude Messiam à Prophetis promi- scue vocari Ducem, principem, pastorem, regem Jes. XL. 11. Jer. XXII. 5. Ezech. XXXIII. 23. Dan. IX. 25. quia omnes dignitates divisas in posteris David in se summe unire debeat; quippe qui omni illo ordine hominum jam olim erat designatus. Sic no- tum, Reges ipsos vocatos ποιμένας λαῶν à genti- libus quo ipso ostensum populos non esse propter reges, sed Reges propter populum & imperium il- lorum debere esse πολιτικὸν potius & πατρικὸν, quam δεσποτικὸν directivum, non coactivum, amo- re potius quam metu stabilitum. Et quia τὸ ποιμάι- νειν omnimodam curam includit, à Scriptoribus sacris ad munus Ecclesiasticum passim transfertur. Sic etiam sive ab Evangelistis, sive à scribis often- sum, Messiam esse illum pastorem κατ' ἐξοχὴν sic dictum, de quo Ezechiel XXXIV. 23. Excitabo eis pastorem unum, qui pascat eas (pecudes) servum meum Davidem, ipse pascat eas, & ipse erit eis pa- stor. Quod frequens etiam alibi apud Prophe- tas, à quibus Deus ipse pastori frequenter con- fertur, ut Ps. XXIII. 1. & LXXVII. 21. Vulgatus In- terpres hic habet reget, quod quidem sensum ex- primit, sed non emphasin illam directionis Mes- siæ, qualis illa futura esset, suavis nimirum & pasto- ralis. Unde frustra à Maldonato excusatur ut ma- gis cohærens cum voce ἡγόμενος. Nec enim cohærentiam illam ignoravit Matthæus, vel sine causa verbo ποιμανεῖ usus fuit. Ab Interpretibus vero humanis non tantum sensus exprimendus, sed & verba, ubi de versione agitur.

Sed imprimis luculentum est hic τεκμήριον regni Christi, quod usq; ad fines terræ magnifican- dus sit dominator in Israel, quod nullatenus sub Zo- robabele, sed tempore N. T. contigit. Unde Theodoret: Et sane sacrosanctam Dei Ecclesiam vi- deas Domini eo nomine gloriose ornatam esse, & u- bique terrarum & maris Dei nomen summis laudi- bus celebrari: de quibus nihil Iudæi demonstrabunt fa- ctum fuisse ad adventum Domini, & conservatoris passionem, & gentium vocationem.

## 5:5
Verse 5. AND THIS SHALL BE PEACE] And things shall then be prosperous. וזה (and this) is accustomed to be taken as a note of time, as in Num. 12:22, 22:32. שׁלום (peace) for prosperous things. Whence that prosperity shall come, he will now say.

WHEN THE ASSYRIAN SHALL COME INTO THE LAND] After he shall have come into our land (that is, Judea), the Assyrian namely with Nimrod, as follows, that is, with the Chaldeans, in whose army there were many Assyrians: nay, even Babylon itself is a part of Assyria, not only to the poets, but also to Strabo.

AND WHEN HE SHALL TREAD IN OUR HOUSES] After he shall have trodden our houses, Jerusalem having been captured.

AND WE SHALL RAISE UP AGAINST HIM] Then we shall raise up against him: namely, by our prayers poured out to God.

SEVEN SHEPHERDS] Cyrus with some other kings (Jer. 51:27, 28).

AND EIGHT PRINCIPAL MEN] That is, great satraps, who are called סגנים (prefects) and פחותים (governors) in the cited place of Jeremiah.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET ERIT ISTE PAX] Et erunt tunc res prospe- ræ. וזה pro temporis nota sumi solet, ut Num. XII. 22. XXII. 32. שׁלום pro rebus prosperis. Unde ventura sit ista prosperitas, jam dicet.

CUM VENERIT ASSTRIUS IN TERRAM] Post- quam venerit in terram nostram, (id est, Judæam) Assyrius nempe cum Nemrodo, ut sequitur, id est, cum Chaldæis, in quorum exercitu multi erant Assyrii: imo & ipsa Baby- lon pars Assyriæ non Poetis tantum, sed & Straboni.

ET QUANDO CALCAVERIT IN DOMIBUS NOSTRIS] Postquam calcaverit domos nostras captis Hie- rosolymis.

ET SUSCITABIMUS SUPER EUM] Tunc suscita- bimus contra eum: nempe precibus nostris ad Deum fusis.

SEPTEM PASTORES] Cyrum cum aliis aliquot regibus Jerem. LI. 27. 28.

ET OCTO PRIMATES HOMINUM] Id est, magnos Satrapas, qui Jer. dicto loco סגנים & פחותים.

## 5:6
Verse 6. AND THEY SHALL FEED THE LAND OF ASSUR WITH THE SWORD, AND THE LAND OF NIMROD IN ITS LANCES] In its lances, that is, they shall subdue Assyria and Babylonia with arms, which is to rule with a rod of iron (Ps. 2). He keeps the order well: for Cyrus came through Assyria into Babylonia.

AND HE SHALL DELIVER FROM ASSUR WHEN HE SHALL COME INTO OUR LAND, AND WHEN HE SHALL TREAD WITHIN OUR BORDERS] Here ו is 'lest,' as the Chaldean rightly noted. He shall deliver (us, Cyrus) from the Assyrian, lest he come into our land, and lest he tread within our borders: namely, as he once did. This is the cause of the prosperity of the Jews, that the Persians shall keep all those nations hostile to the Jews in check.

This explanation is assumed by Lyranus, and others, Cornelius à Lapide, Calvin, and even our own countrymen, especially Osiander, and the Weimar Paraphrasts: but in such a way that the Prophet shows that the kingdom of the Assyrians and Babylonians will fall before the incarnation of Christ, and will not bring any harm to the Jews at that very time, but rather that the Lord will avenge through the Medes and Persians the injuries with which they afflicted the Israelites, so that the liberation of the people of God from captivity may thus be connected. Blessed Winkelman also followed this sense. But he referred those words: And he himself shall be peace, to the Messiah, i.e., the Son of God himself, the promised Messiah, who has always been present with his Church, will also procure peace for us when Asshur comes into our land; however, most explain it concerning the time of Shalmaneser, who led away the ten tribes, and the incursion of Sennacherib into the Kingdom of Judah, and the siege of Jerusalem. Blessed Chytraeus has it thus; I understand the sentence concerning the Assyrians and Babylonians being repressed by 7 shepherds and 8 Princes, as being repressed, I understand simply as the Princes of the Medes and Persians, who 150 years after Micah punished the Assyrians and Babylonians, the destroyers of the Jewish polity, and overturned the Babylonian empire. Blessed Luther himself also retained that explanation in his marginal Scholia. The Persians and Medes shall in this subdue the Assyrians and Babylonians, until Christ comes, who shall save us entirely and completely. We judge that this opinion, as being the simplest and also handed down by Theodoret, is to be embraced. Blessed Luther in his Commentary handed down another interpretation: It is not necessary that we translate the masculine pronoun into the neuter. For if you understand it of Christ, that he himself is peace, it is the same sentiment that is in the Gospel: In me you have peace, but not such as the world gives. For this peace "is, that we know our sins have been forgiven "us, and that we have been liberated from eternal death by this "King Christ. This peace mitigates the troubles, "dangers, disturbances, and all the inconveniences of the flesh. "As for the rest in the text, Assyria is known, but the Land of Nimrod is the Babylonian "Kingdom. For these two kingdoms harmed the Jews the most; Shalmaneser the Assyrian led away the ten "tribes of Israel, Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian led "away the tribe of Judah. And although Lyra and others refer these to history, that the power of both the Assyrians and the Babylonians was transferred to the Medes and Persians, yet since we are also forced to necessarily understand the following concerning the Kingdom of Christ, why should we make a translation here that is not necessary? I therefore feel that by the Assyrians and Babylonians are understood in general the enemies whom the Church has had at all times, for just as the people of Israel suffered these enemies: So also the Church suffers its own enemies. Against these he promises that it will come to pass that seven Shepherds and eight Princes shall be raised up from the people, i.e., a great abundance of Doctors. For this is a Hebrew phrase, by which a great abundance and a great number is signified. For just as Solomon speaks in Ecclesiastes 11, give portions to seven and to eight, i.e., give liberally, not sparingly: So he says here: The Church shall have a great abundance of Evangelists, who will teach among the nations and will humble them, that they may obey the preaching of the Gospel, or will overthrow them, not with arms, (For they are only shepherds and appointed men, not soldiers) but only with the word. For it is necessary that those who resist the word perish by arms. As we also said above. The word Nesiche is from Nasach, which means to constitute, to ordain as a Prince, etc. Therefore we have made it 'constituted', so that the Apostles chosen from the lowest class of men for teaching and governing the world by the word might be signified. David uses the same word in Ps. II; But I have been constituted (nasachti) King. For the word has a peculiar force, to show the delegation of the ministry. This is Blessed Luther. The Belgian Paraphrasts also made this explanation of theirs concerning the enemies of the Church of Christ and its spiritual defense. Concerning the defeat of all the enemies of the Church, Jerome, Haymo, Rupert, Albert, Hugo, Montanus, Clarius, Ribera, as also Cornelius à Lapide, likewise understand it. Tarnovius, however, although he thinks Sennacherib is pointed out, nevertheless interprets it also concerning spiritual rule and victory.

Coccejus is here again singular: The great enemy of the Christian Church, the Assyrian, is named in particular, and he indeed is to enter the land of the Christians, to trample their palaces. But the Christian Church will nevertheless have peace, viz., with the nations among whom it will live, so that it may serve the Church. A proof of this matter is that Kings and Emperors will be stirred up against Assyria, who with huge armies will penetrate into his land, and will consume it with the sword. Nothing is more certain than that by the Assyrian are first understood the Persians: For the Persians did not receive the faith, and they attacked it not only in their own dominions, but had also invaded the Roman Empire for this reason. An example is Chosroes in the time of Heraclius. In the sacred scriptures the Persians are also called Assyrians. The Saracens and Turks are added to these. When he says seven and eight anointed shepherds, he signifies that there will be among Christians many most powerful Kings, who at one time can invade Assyria, and are about to invade it. The Land of Nimrod is Assyria, Babylonia, etc. Its gates, from whence they go out. He will drive back the war even to the gates of the Persians and Saracens. Finally, someone will snatch [it] from the Assyrian, viz. Like Duke Godfrey of Bouillon, who began the Jerusalem kingdom. There is mention of this war into Assyria also in Hosea ch. XIII. 7. but with the signification of the slaughters to be received in that expedition. This is Coccejus. But those things can be proven neither from the continuity of the text, nor from the connection of the words. The glosses of this man are too arbitrary, which, as far as is evident from public monuments, never came into the mind of any Interpreters.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET PASCENT TERRAM ASSUR IN GLA- DIO, ET TERRAM NEMROD IN LANCEIS EJUS] In lanceis suis, id est, armis domabunt Assyriam & Babylo- niam, quod est regere in virga ferrea Ps. II. Ordinem be- ne servat: Nam Cyrus per Assyriam venit in Babyloniam.

ET LIBERABIT AB ASSUR CUM VENERIT IN TERRAM NOSTRAM, ET CUM CALCAVE- RIT IN FINIBUS NOSTRIS] Hic ו est ne, ut recte no- tavit Chaldæus Liberabit (nos Cyrus) ab Assyrio, ne veniat in terram nostram, & ne calcet fines nostros: nempe, ut olim fecit, Hæc est causa prosperitatis Judæorum, quod Persæ o- mnes illas gentes Judæis infestas continebit in officio.

Explicationem hanc Lyranus, & alii, Cornel. à Lap. Calvinus, etiam nostrates assumunt, imprimis Osiander, & Paraphr. Vinarienses: sed ita ut osten- dat Propheta, regnum Assyriorum & Babyloniorum ruiturum ante incarnationem Christi, neque eo ipso tempore quicquam incommodi illaturum Ju- dæis, quin potius Dominum per Medos & Per- sas vindicaturum injurias, quibus illi Israelitas af- fecerunt, ut ita connectatur liberatio populi Dei è captivitate Babylonica, & spirituale Regnum Christi. Quem sensum etiam sequutus est B. Winkelmanus. Sed verba illa: Et ipse erit pax, ad Messiam retulit, h. m. ipse Filius Dei promissus Messias, qui semper affuit Ecclesiæ suæ etiam no- bis pacem procurabit, cum Assur venerit in terram nostram, plerique autem de tempore Salmanasse- ris X. tribus abducentis, & Sennacheribi in Regnum Judæ impressione, & Hierosolymorum obsidione explicant. B. Chytraus ita habet; sententiam de Assyriis & Babyloniis per 7. pastores & 8. Principes reprimendis intelligo simpliciter de Principibus Me- dorum & Persarum, qui annis 150. post Micham As- syrios & Babylonios eversores politiæ Judaicæ pu- nierunt, & imperium Babylonicum everterunt. Re- tinuit etiam illam explicationem B. Lutherus ipse in marginalibus Scholiis. Die Persen und Me- den sollen in des die Assyrier und Babylonier dempfen, bis das Christus komme, der uns gantz und gar errette. Quam sententiam utpote sim- plicissimam à Theodoreto etiam traditam ample- cissimam à Theodoreto etiam traditam amplecten- dam censemus. B. Lutherus in Commentario a- liam interpretationem tradidit: Non necesse est, ut pronomen masculinum vertamus in neutrum. Si enim de Christo intelligas, quod ipse sit pax, est eadem sententia, quæ in Evangelio est: In me habe- tis pacem, sed non quam mundus dat. Hæc enim pax "est, quod scimus nobis peccata nostra condona- "ta, & nos à morte æterna liberatos esse per hunc "Regem Christum. Hæc pax mitigat molestias, "pericula, turbas, & incommoda omnia carnis. "Quod ad reliqua in textu attinet, Assyria nota "est, Terra Nemrod autem est Regnum Babylo- "nium. Hæc enim duo regna plurimum Judæis "nocuerunt, Salmanasser Assyrius abduxit de- "cem tribus Israel Nebucadnezar Babylonius ab- "duxit tribum Juda. Etsi autem Lyra & alii hæc ad "historiam referunt, quod tum Assyriorum, tum "Babyloniorum potentia ad Medos & Persas trans- "lata sit, tamen cum etiam sequentia de Regno Chri- "sti necessario intelligere cogamur, cur faceremus "hic non necessariam translationem? Sentio igitur per Assyrios & Babylonios intelligi in genere hostes, quos Ecclesia omnibus temporibus habuit, sicut enim populus Israel hosce hostes passus est: Ita etiam Ec- clesia suos patitur hostes. Contra hos promittit fu- turum, ut suscitentur septem Pastores, & octo Principes, ex plebe h. e. magna copia Doctorum. Est enim hæc Ebraica phrasis, qua magna copia & magnus numerus significatur. Sicut enim Eccle- siastæ 11. Salomo loquitur, da partes septem & o- cto, h. e. da liberaliter, non parce: Ita hic dicit: Habebit Ecclesia magnam copiam Evangelistarum, qui inter gentes docebunt & humiliabunt eos, obe- diant prædicationi Evangelii, aut evertent eos, non armis, (Nam sunt pastores tantum & constituti homines, non milites) sed tantum verbo. Necesse est enim perire armis, qui verbo resistunt. Sicut supra quoque diximus. Vocabulum Nesiche est à Nasach, quod significat constituere, in Principem ordinare &c. Ideo fecimus constitutos, ut signifi- centur Apostoli ex infimo genere hominum dele- ti, ad docendum & gubernandum mundum ver- bo. Eodem verbo utitur David Ps. II; Ego autem nasachti constitui Regem meum. Habet enim vocabulum peculiarem vim, ut ostendat ministerii demandationem. Hæc B. Lutherus. Quam de hostibus Ecclesiæ Christi & defensione ejusdem spirituali explicationem suam quoque fecere Pa- raphrastæ Belgici. De profligatione omnium Ec- clesiæ hostium cum Hieronymo, Haymone, Ruperto, Alberto, Hugone, Montano, Clario, Riberâ, ut & Cor- nelius à Lap. quoque intelligunt. Tarnovius vero etsi Sennacheribum indigitari putat, de spirituali tamen quoque regimine, ac victoria interpretatur.

Coccejus hic iterum singularis est: Nominatur im- primis magnus hostis Ecclesiæ Christianæ Assyrius, & cejus, ille quidem intraturus terram Christianorum, calca- turus palatia ipsorum. Sed habebit nihilo minus Ec- clesia Christiana pacem, scil. cum gentibus, inter quas vivet, ut serviat Ecclesiæ. Hujus rei documentum, quod in Assyriam Reges & Imperatores excitabuntur, qui cum ingentibus exercitibus penetrabunt in terram ejus, & depascentur eam gladio. Nihil certius quam per Assyrium primo Persas intelligi: Persæ enim non receperunt fidem, & illam oppugnarunt non tantum in suis ditionibus, sed etiam Imperium Romanum hac de causa invaserant. Exemplum est Cosroes tempo- re Heraclii. In sacris literis Persæ etiam Assyrii vo- cantur. Succenturiantur hisce Sarraceni & Turcæ. Septem & octo pastores unctos homines quum dicit, si- gnificat fore inter Christianos plures Reges potentissi- mos, qui uno tempore Assyriam invadere possint, & invasuri sint. Terra Nimrod est Assyria, Babylonia &c. Ostia ejus, unde egrediuntur. Bellum ad ostia usq́; Persarum Sarracenorumq́; retroagent. De- niq́; eripiet ab Assyrio scil. aliquis. Ut Dux Bullio- næus Gothofridus, qui regnum Hierosolymitanum exorsus est. Hujus belli in Assyriam mentio est & Hoseæ cap. XIII. 7. sed cum significatione cladium in ea expeditione accipiendarum. Hæc Coccejus. Sed ea neque è textus συνεχεία, neque è verbo- rum συναφεία probari possunt. Nimis arbitra- riæ sunt viri hujus glossæ, quæ nulli unquam In- terpp. in mentem venere, quantum è publicis monumentis constat.

## 5:7
Ver. 7. AND THE REMNANT OF JACOB SHALL BE] Those who shall have returned from Babylon,

IN THE MIDST OF MANY PEOPLES] With the peoples looking on,

AS THE DEW FROM THE LORD, AND AS SHOWERS UPON THE GRASS] As thin rains upon the grass.

WHICH DOES NOT WAIT FOR MAN, AND DOES NOT TARRY FOR THE SONS OF MEN] Just as dew and rains come from heaven without human help, so the Jews will live securely, without their own labor,

AND THE REMNANT OF JACOB SHALL BE AMONG THE GENTILES IN THE MIDST OF MANY PEOPLES AS A LION AMONG THE BEASTS OF THE FORESTS, AND AS A YOUNG LION AMONG THE FLOCKS OF SHEEP: WHO WHEN HE SHALL PASS THROUGH, AND TREAD DOWN, AND TAKE, THERE IS NONE TO DELIVER.] This looks to the times of the Maccabees and those following, through which the Jews made Idumea, much of the Ammonite and Moabite territories, and also Samaria and the surrounding regions subject to their own law.

These things, however, can in no way be drawn to the times of the Old Testament, so that you might say that all or some of them were fulfilled in those times, either immediately after the release from the Babylonian captivity, or subsequently in the time of the Maccabees. But all interpreters easily agree that they must be referred to the times of the N.T., even those who differ greatly in their opinions regarding the preceding verses 6 and 8, except that Osiander understands the former, 'and the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples as dew from the Lord,' as referring to the remnant from Babylon, while the others refer even those to the times of the N.T. Concerning which Castrius: The remnant of Jacob, namely the Apostles of Christ, and apostolic men sent to propagate the Gospel among peoples and among nations, were to those receiving the Gospel indeed as dew sent by God, and as a drop of rain falling upon the herbs: which there is no one who expects from man, no one who awaits from any of the sons of man, for they are expected from God alone. But as for those who resist, like a lion among the other animals of the forest: and like a lion's whelp among the flocks of sheep, which if it moves from its place will trample and seize, and no one will dare to snatch away: thus do Jerome, Theodoret, Haymo, Remigius, Rupert, Albert, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, Isidore, Vatablus, and Montanus explain this passage concerning the Apostles disseminating the Gospel among the nations. Add blessed Luther, Brentius, Chytræus, Wigand, Winkelmann, Pappus, Tarnovius, and the Weimar Paraphrasts, to whom, among the Reformed, Calvin, the Belgian Paraphrasts, and others do not disagree. Theodoret has it thus: When he calls the saved here the remnant, then elsewhere, if the number of the sons of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, the remnant shall be saved. Just as, he says, dew has fallen from heaven, those who have believed and brought the Evangelical declaration to the nations will irrigate the whole world. The beginnings of the Apostles lay like dew, and like lambs they were grazing on the grass of impiety, living by doctrine and miracles as lambs in the midst of wolves according to the Lord's prediction. Behold, he says, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves. But after the world received the declaration of the Gospel, and kings and Emperors were enrolled in the number of the Church, fear settled upon the enemies of the truth. And indeed, if they are made like beasts of burden, they are filled with fear and horror, destitute of help from all sides. But these, who teach the Evangelical doctrine, bearing lion-like spirits, and strength, with the greatest freedom, defending the truth with the word of truth, conquer lies. These are the words of blessed Luther, whom our people follow: He compares the remnant of Jacob among the nations, that is, the Apostles and their successors in the ministry, to heavenly dew and rain. This, first, ought to be referred to the dignity of the ministry. For the Gospel is a heavenly gift, far excelling all other gifts. As the Baptist says, No one has ever seen God. The Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him to us. Deservedly, therefore, it ought to be preferred to all things. Next, the comparison ought also to be referred to the fruits of this ministry. For just as the earth is refreshed, grows green, and increases by heavenly dew and rain: so a certain fruit follows the word. Just as Isaiah also uses this very comparison for this sentiment. The fruits, however, of this heavenly gift are the Holy Spirit, who through the word of the Gospel descends into the hearts of men and excites faith in them. But through faith, the forgiveness of sins and eternal life are received. Likewise, for those who receive the word of faith, this is truly heavenly dew and rain, as Christ says: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. But those who oppose themselves to the word, not only do they not receive it by faith, but they persecute it and wish it extinguished, just as the impious Synagogue did, just as the Roman kingdom did; to them, the word and the whole ministry is a lion seizing and scattering.

Grotius, having held all the interpreters in contempt, tears this apart, and snatches a part of them for the time of the released captivity, and a part for the times of the Maccabees. Which distraction is by no means to be granted, for the discourse is everywhere concerning the remnant of Jacob in the midst of many peoples, i.e., not with the peoples looking on, as Grotius perverts the first member, but as the words themselves sound, they bring it in with the common sense: among many peoples and among the nations, for the remnant of Jacob in the nations in the midst of peoples are declared to be such that the place and seat is expressed where they are to unfold themselves, not that spectators are designated. Nor indeed do those things concerning the servitude of the Jews after the return from Babylon cohere with the Maccabean [times], just as the Prophet related the same remnant of Jacob to both the comparison of the dew of fruitfulness and the lion trampling; so when he had the ruler in Israel in mind, he looked rather to the times of the New Testament, when he was to feed and rule his own people in a peculiar way, just as at the beginnings of the same, hardly a few remnants survived, through whom as holy seed he propagated his own people, who in the midst of many peoples among the nations were like fruitful and most pleasing dew to the word of the Gospel for those whose hearts they sought to irrigate, Ps. 72, Ps. 110, Is. 55, Hos. 6. To the others, they were like a famished lion attacking drunken cattle, tearing them apart for vengeance against the disobedient. Therefore he adds: YOUR HAND SHALL BE LIFTED UP OVER ALL who trouble you, and ALL YOUR ENEMIES shall be exterminated: Which was not fulfilled by the Maccabees: for were their hands lifted up over ALL, were ALL their enemies utterly exterminated? But this was fulfilled through Christ in the Church, who puts all enemies as a footstool for his feet, Ps. 110. Whence some think the ruler in Israel is addressed here, with Jerome, Haymo, Remigius, Albert, Hugo. Thus, by the ministry of your servants the Apostles, your power, O Christ God, will be superior to your enemies: for all enemies resisting them will be cut down. But to Theodoret, Rupert also, Lyra, Dionysius, Vatablus, and Montanus wish the remnant of Jacob, namely the flock of the Apostles, or the small Church carried throughout the world, to be understood: for since he compared the Apostles to a lion, a lion's whelp against those not receiving the Gospel, he now concludes their victory more clearly, so it will come to pass that their power will turn out superior to the attempts of the enemies: for all enemies of the Gospel will be cut down by God, if they are unwilling to acquiesce, as Christ à Castro has it on this passage. Which latter explanation is more suitable. For thus it is not necessary to change the person.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET ERUNT RELIQUIÆ JACOB] Illi quē è Babylonia redierint,

IN MEDIO POPULORUM MULTORUM] Po- pulis adspectantibus,

QUASI ROS A DOMINO, ET QUASI STILLÆ SUPER HERBAM] Quasi pluviæ tenues super herbam.

QUÆ NON EXSPECTAT VIRUM, ET NON PRÆSTOLATUR FILIOS HOMINUM ] Sicut ros & pluviæ sine humana ope cœlitus veniunt, ita Judæi secure vivent, sine suo labore,

ET ERUNT RELIQUIÆ JACOB IN GENTI- BUS IN MEDIO POPULORUM MULTORUM QUA- SI LEO IN JUMENTIS SILVARUM, ET QUASI CATULUS LEONIS IN GREGIBUS PECORUM: QUI CUM TRANSIERIT ET CONCULCAVERIT ET CEPERIT, NON EST QUI FRUAT.] Hoc spectat ad tempora Maccabæorum ac sequentia, per quæ Judæi I- dumæam, multa Ammonitidos & Moabitidos, Samariam quoque & circum sita sui juris fecere.

Hæc vero nullo modo trahi possunt ad tempora Veteris Testamenti, ita ut in illis fistatur sive imme- diate post solutionem captivitatis Babylonicæ, si- ve deinceps Maccabæorum tempore omnia aut a- liqua eorum impleta dicas. Sed referenda ad tempora N. T. esse, omnes Interpp. facile consen- tiunt, etiam qui circa versus præcedentes 6. & 8. sententiis admodum discrepant, nisi quod priora & erunt reliquiæ Jacob in medio populorum multo- rum quasi ros à Domino, de reliquiis è Babylone in- telligat Osiander, cæteri vero illa etiam ad tempo- ra N. T. referant. Quo de Castrius: Reliquiæ Ja- cob, nempe Apostoli Christi, virique Apostolici missi ad propagandum Evangelium inter populos & inter gentes, erant suscipientibus quidem Evangelium ut ros à Deo immissus, & uti stilla imbris decidentis su- per herbas: quas nemo est qui expectet ab homine, nemo qui ab ullo filiorum hominis præstoletur, à solo enim Deo expectantur. Resistentibus autem, uti leo inter cætera sylvæ animalia: & uti catulus leonis inter greges pecorum, qui si loco se moverit conculcabit & rapiet, & nemo audebit eripere: ita de Apostolis Evangelium disseminantibus inter gentes hunc locum exponunt Hieronymus, Theodoretius, Haymo, Remigius, Rupertus, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, Isidorus, Vatablus, & Montanus. Adde B. Lutherum, Brentium, Chytræum, Wigandum, Winkelmannum, Pappum, Tarnovium, Paraphrastas Vinarienses, quibus è Reformatis Calvinus, Paraphrastæ Belgici, aliisque haud abnuunt. Theodoretus ita habet: Cum hic salvatos reliquias vocat, tum alibi, si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel, ut arena maris, reliquiæ salvabuntur. Perinde inquit, ut ros est de cælo elapsus, qui crediderunt atque Evangelicam declarationem gentibus attulerunt, orbem terrarum irrigabunt. Apostolorum principia roris similia jacebantur, & quemadmodum agni impietatis gramen depascebantur, doctrinâ & miraculis tanquam agni in medio Luporum versantes juxta Domini prædictionem. Ecce, inquit mitto vos sicut oves in medio luporum. Postea vero quam orbis terræ Evangelii declarationem suscepit, & reges & Imperatores ad numerum Ecclesiæ adscripti sunt, in veritatis hostes metus excubuit. Et quidem si jumentorum similes facti, metu & horrore complentur ex omnibus partibus auxilio destituti. Hi vero, qui Evangelicam doctrinam docent, leoninos animos gerentes, & robur, cum summâ libertate mendaciis patrocinantes veritatis verbo expugnant. B. Lutheri, quem nostri sequuntur, hæc sunt; Comparat reliquias Jacob inter gentes, hoc est, Apostolos & eorum in ministerio successores rori cælesti & pluviæ. Hoc, primum ad dignitatem ministerii referri debet. Est enim Evangelium cælesfe donum, omnia alia dona longe antecellens. Sicut Baptista dicit, Deum nemo vidit unquam. Filius, qui in sinu Patris est, enarravit nobis. Merito igitur omnibus rebus debet anteferri. Deinde referri etiam similitudo debet ad fructus hujus ministerii. Sicut enim rore cælefti & pluviâ recreatur terra, virescunt & augentur omnia: Ita certus fructus sequitur verbum. Sicut in hanc sententiam hac ipsâ similitudine quoq; Esaias utitur. Fructus autem hujus cælestis doni sunt Spiritus Sanctus, qui per verbum Evangelii, descendit in corda hominum, & excitat in eis fidem. Per fidem autem accipitur Remissio peccatorum & vita æterna. Item qui verbum fidei accipiunt, his vere est cælestis ros & pluvia, sicut Christus dicit: Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis, Ego reficiam vos. Sed qui verbo se opponunt, id non solum fide non accipiunt, sed persequuntur & extinctum volunt, sicut impia Synagoga, sicut regnum Romanum fecit, his verbum & totum ministerium sit leo rapiens & dissipans.

Grotius fusque deque habitis Interpretibus omnibus hæc discerpit, & partem eorum rapit ad tempus solutæ captivitatis, partem ad Maccabeorum tempora. Quæ distractio minime concedenda, nam de reliquiis Jacob in medio populorum multorum utrobique sermo est, h. e. non populis aspectantibus, ut prius membrum pervertit Grotius sed uti verba ipsa sonant, sensu vulgato id inferunt: inter multos populos & inter gentes, nam reliquiæ Jacob in gentibus in medio populorum tales futuræ perhibentur, ut locus & sedes exprimatur, ubi se explicaturæ sint, non Spectatores designentur. Nec vero illa ratione cohærent ista de servitute Judæorum post reditum è Babylone cum Maccabaicis uti easdem reliquias Jacob utramque similitudinem roris fœcunditatis & leonis concul- cantis retulit Propheta, ita quum dominatorem in Israele in animo haberet, potius ad tempora N. T. respexit, quo is populum suum pascere ac re- gere peculiariter debuit, uti sub initia ejusdem vix paucæ reliquiæ supererant, per quas ceu sanctum semen propagavit populum suum, quæ in medio populorum multorum in gentibus tanquam ros fœ- cundus & gratissimus fuere verbo Evangelii illis, quorum corda rigari petebant Ps. LXXII. Ps. CX. Es. LV. Hos. VI. Cæteris instar famelici leonis erant in pecudes ebrias grassantis easᾶ, laniantis ob vindi- ctam adversus inobedientes. Ideo addit: EXTOL- LETUR MANUS TUA SUPER OMNES, qui tribulant te, & OMNES INIMICI TUI exterminabuntur: Quod per Maccabæos imple- tum non est: num enim super OMNES manus eorum elatæ, num OMNES inimici eorum pe- nitus exterminati? Impletum autem id per Christum in Ecclesia, qui hostes omnes ponit scabellum pedum suorum Ps. CX. Unde nonnulli dominatorem in Israele hic compellari putant cum Hieronymo, Haymone, Remigio, Alberto, Hugone. Sic ministerio servorum tuorum Apostolorum potestas tua, ô Christe Deus, superior erit hosti- bus tuis: nam succidentur omnes inimici illis ob- nitentes. Theodoreto vero, Rupertus quoque, Lyra, Dionys. Vatabl. & Montanus residuum Ja- cob, nempe gregem Apostolorum, seu pusillam Ecclesiam per orbem invectam volunt intelligi: nam cum comparaverit Apostolos leoni, catuloᾶ leonis adversus non recipientes Evangelium, mo- do clarius concludit eorum victoriam, ita fiet, ut potestas eorum superior evadat hostium conati- bus: nam omnes Evangelii inimici succidentur à Deo, si noluerint acquiescere uti habet Christ. à Castro in h. l. Quæ posterior explicatio convenien- tior. Sic enim non neceslum est mutari personam.

## 5:10
Verse 10. AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY] That day, namely, of which [I spoke] above in 1, for here the word of God returns to Babylon. I WILL TAKE AWAY YOUR HORSES FROM THE MIDST OF YOU AND YOUR CHARIOTS] Almost the same words in Jer. 31. 21.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET ERIT IN DIE ILLA] Illa nempe de qua supra 1. nam hic ad Babylonem Dei sermo revertitur. AUFERAM EQUOS TUOS DE MEDIO TUI ET QUADRIGAS TUAS] Eadem ferme verba apud Je- rem. l. 31. Ll. 21.

## 5:11
Verse 11. AND I WILL DESTROY THE CITIES OF YOUR LAND, AND ALL YOUR FORTIFICATIONS] Jer. 51. 30, 43.

AND I WILL TAKE AWAY SORCERIES FROM YOUR HAND, AND THERE SHALL BE NO DIVINATIONS IN YOU] Jer. 50. 36.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET PERDAM CIVITATES TERRÆ TUÆ, ET OMNES MUNITIONES TUAS] Jer. LI. 30.43.

ET AUFERAM MALEFICIA DE MANU TUA, ET DIVINATIONES NON ERUNT IN TE] Jer. L. 36.

## 5:12
Ver. 12. AND I WILL CAUSE THY GRAVEN IMAGES TO PERISH AND THY STATUES FROM THE MIDST OF THEE, AND THOU SHALT NO MORE WORSHIP THE WORKS OF THY HANDS] Isa. XLVI. 1. Jerem. L. 2. LI. 41. 44. The Persians were enemies of images.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET PERIRE FACIAM SCULPTILIA TUA ET STATUAS TUAS DE MEDIO TUI, ET NON ADORABIS ULTRA OPERA MANUUM TUARUM] Esa. XLVI. 1. Jerem. L. 2. LI. 41. 44. Persæ hostes erant imaginum.

## 5:13
Ver. 13. AND I WILL PLUCK UP THY GROVES FROM THE MIDST OF THEE] Which are the temenea in Herodotus, where he describes the customs of the Babylonians.

AND I WILL DESTROY THY CITIES] The cities of thy empire, as above II.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET EVELLAM LUCOS TVOS DE ME- DIO TUI] Qui τεμένεα Herodoto, ubi mores Babylonio- rum describit.

ET CONTERAM CIVITATES TVAS] Vrbes imperii tui, ut supra II.

## 5:14
VENGEANCE IN ALL NATIONS] Of the Chaldean Empire.

WHICH HAVE NOT HEARD] Which will oppose themselves to Cyrus. Compare Isa. XLV. 1.

These things have again been newly devised by Grotius against the mind of all Interpreters, so that he might favor his own distortion of the illustrious prophecy concerning Bethlehem, the fatherland of the Messiah, and draw back to ancient times those things which Micah predicted concerning the times of the N. T., but he falsely assumes that in v. 1 it was a matter of Babylon. Furthermore, even if that were admitted, it would not be proper to draw back these things, which were said concerning that day or that time which the Prophet has hitherto pointed out, to much more ancient centuries, much less is it to be conceded that the subjects should be so changed, and when it is a matter of Judah and Israel, that Babylon should be substituted in its place. Finally, the vengeance which the Lord threatens against all disobedient nations is perversely restricted by Grotius to the nations of the Chaldean empire opposing themselves to Cyrus.

These things, however, are explained in two ways primarily. Most understand them concerning the destruction of Judea effected by the Romans. Since the Prophet had dealt with those times. Thus Winckelmann: AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY I WILL TAKE AWAY. This is a prophecy concerning the extreme deletion of the Jewish polity of the Jews, the devastation of the land, and the destruction of the cities, which was done by the Romans. AND I WILL TAKE AWAY WITCHCRAFTS FROM THY HAND. The extermination of magical, superstitious, and diabolical arts, such as crystallomancy, rhabdomancy, sorceries, astrological predictions that are altogether singular, and auguries, to which Achas, Manasses, Ammon, and other impious Kings were addicted, and without doubt also in the time of Christ, and many among the people studied in the time of the Apostles. AND I WILL CAUSE TO PERISH GRAVEN IMAGES. It is certainly not read that that gross idolatry was in use among the Jews in the time of Christ, such as the nations and the Israelites practiced in the time of our Prophet: But yet there is also a subtle idolatry, when the Pharisees, scribes, and Pseudo-Apostles thought that men were justified and saved before God by legal works, even by their own choice. The Prophet, however, uses words customary in his own time. Generally, however, all disobedience is noted, just as it is said in 1 Sam. 15: to rebel is the sin of divination, and stubbornness is iniquity and idolatry. AND I WILL EXECUTE IN FURY. A prophecy concerning the vengeance of God against all nations that do not obey the Gospel. It was fulfilled in the Jews cast out from their land, in Emperors and prefects opposing the Gospel of Christ and persecuting Christians: all of whom almost met a tragic end, and it will be fulfilled hereafter. In almost the same way B. Luther, Brentius, Wigandus, Osiander, the Vinarie Paraphrasts, and most others.

Some, however, because the Synagogue did not worship idols anymore, wish these things to be said of the Church, and the removal of the impediments to the promulgation of the Gospel to be designated by them: That horses and chariots, cities, and idols are to be destroyed, by which the nations might resist, or even trust is to be placed in God, because for victory over enemies there will be no need for horses, nor chariots, nor fortified cities, but for divine power and the gentleness of ministers, and not for the help of idols, but for the grace of the true God, as Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus [say], or that they will be faithful in these customs, so that whatever overturns peace and draws away from piety is to be despised, as Castrius explains: Your faithful ones, O Church, will enjoy total peace, cultivated by the Gospel; for I will remove from them every use of horses and chariots, I will overturn the walls of cities, and all fortifications which are in use for those who fear: for they will live without walls, under the fig tree and the vine, because there will be no one who might terrify, finally with all superstition removed, they will depend on God alone, and will trust in Him alone. Cornel. a Lapide also interprets it thus: O Jacob, that is, O Church, which has arisen from Jacob, but has been most propagated through the nations, I will take away from you all defenses, all weapons, all fortresses and fortifications, by which you previously opposed Christ and the faith of Christ, or resisted Him, and specifically I will take away witchcrafts, divinations, oracles, idols, and their shrines and cities. For these the infidels opposed to the faith and the Church, and with them they attacked the Church as if with battering rams. Thus also B. Höpfner thinks that the impediments to the true worship of GOD are removed here, first horses, chariots, cities and fortifications, and other instruments of dissension of that kind, which CHRIST wishes to exterminate and destroy in the hearts of the impious, both because they delay trust, and because they are in use for those who fear, then enchanters and diviners, who turn [people] away from GOD. Finally, idolatry and the adoration of the work of hands.

However, in the former [cases] the literal sense can be retained concerning the destroying of the cities of Judea and the fortifications, just as it is established that they were horribly devastated by the Roman army: even if the rest are referred to the freeing of the faithful in the city from all idolatry and ἐθελοθρησκεία [will-worship]: So that in Judea they might be compelled, partly the stubbornly resisting, who are to be overturned with their cities and fortifications, and partly those submitting themselves to the Ruler in Israel, who are to be purged or kept immune from every stain of impiety and idolatry, whether to which they were once subject, or which they could easily contract otherwise. For could not these things be said to Judea, even if at that time it did not devote effort to graven images, worship, and magical divinations? Since they had once been addicted to those greater ones, and could have relapsed into the same impiety, unless they were relieved by the power and grace of the Ruler Christ. Finally, Prophetic Scripture preserves its custom, by which it is accustomed to use the phrases of its own age, and by them to explain the things of the New Testament, and by certain species of impiety once accepted, to comprehend all impiety, so that nothing else is indicated here than that under the N. T. the impiety of ἐθελοθρησκεία [will-worship], which once flourished, will not have a place among the people of the Lord, and that the same will be immune from magical witchcrafts, the worship of statues, graven images, and icons, and the veneration of groves.

Latin:

VLTIONEM IN OMNIBVS GENTIBVS] Chal- daici Imperii.

QVÆ NON AVDIERVNT] Quæ se Cyro op- ponent. Confer. Es XLV. 1.

Hæc iterum contra mentem omnium Inter- pretum noviter excogitata sunt à Grotio, ut suæ detorsioni illustris vaticinii de patria Messiæ Bethlehem velificaretur, & ea, quæ de temporibus N. T. prædixit Michæas, ad antiqua tempora re- traheret, sed falso assumit, quod v. 1. de Babylonia actum fuerit. Adhæc etiamsi id admitteretur, non integrum foret, hæc quæ de illa die, vel de illo tempore, quod hactenus indigitat Propheta, dicta retrahere ad longe antiquiora secula, multo mi- nus concedendum, ut subjecta ita mutentur, & quum de Iuda ac Israele agatur, ejus loco Babylonia substituatur. Denique perverse ultio, quam ad- versus omnes gentes inobedientes minatur Do- minus, restringitur à Grotio ad gentes Chaldaici imperii Cyro sese opponentes.

Explicantur autem hæc bifariam imprimis. Plerique de excidio Iudææ per Romanos facto intel- ligunt. Siquidem de illis temporibus egerat Pro- pheta. Ita Winckelmannus: ET ERIT IN DIE ILLO AUFERAM. Est hoc vaticinium de extrema Iudæorum politiæ Iudaicæ deletione, terræ vastatione, & urbium destructione, quæ facta est per Romanos. ET AUFERAM MALEFICIA DE MANU TUA. Artium magicarum superstitiosarum & Dia- bolicarum, ut sunt κρυςαλλομαντεία, ῥαβδο- μαντεία, sortilegia, astrologicæ predictiones pror- sus singulares, auguria, quibus Achas, Manasses, Ammon, & alii impii Reges addicti fuerunt, & sine du- bio etiam tempore Christi, & Apostolorum multi in po- pulo studuerunt, exterminatio. ET PERIRE FA- CIAM SCULPTILA. Non sane tempore Christi in usu fuisse legitur apud Iudæos crassa ista idololatria, qualem exercuerunt gentes, & Israelitæ tempore Pro- phetæ nostri: Sed tamen est etiam subtilis idololatria, quando Pharisæi, scribæ, Pseudo-Apostoli sentiebant, homines operibus legalibus, etiam suopte arbitrio, co- ram Deo justificari & salvari. Utitur autem Prophe- ta verbis suo tempore usitatis. Generatim tamen omnis inobedientia notatur, quemadmodum 1. Sam. 15. di- citur: peccatum ariolandi est repugnare, scelus & idololatria est, nolle acquiescere. ET FACIAM IN FURORE. Vaticinium de vindicta Dei ad- versus omnes gentes, quæ Evangelio non obediunt. Impletum est in Iudæis è terra sua ejectis, in Impera- toribus & præfectis, Evangelium Christi oppugnanti- bus, & persequentibus Christianos: qui omnes fere tragicum exitum sortiti sunt, & deinceps adimplebi- tur. Eodem fere modo B. Lutherus, Brentius, Wigandus, Osiander, Paraphr. Vinarienses & pleri- que alii.

Nonnulli tamen, quia Synagoga ido- latum non coluit amplius, Ecclesiæ hæc dici, ac amotionem impedimentorum promulgationis Evangelii istis designari volunt: Disperdendos esse equos, & quadrigas, urbes, & idola, quibus gentes obnitentur, vel etiam fiduciam in Deum collocan- dum, quod ad victoriam de hostibus neque equis, neq; curribus, neque munitis urbibus opus futurum sit, sed divina virtute, & ministrorum mansuetudine, nec i- dolorum ope, sed veri Dei gratia, ut Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus, vel quod his moribus futuri sint fideles, ut quicquid pacem evertit, & pietate abstrahit, de- spiciendum, uti Castrius exponit: Summa pace fruen- tur fideles tui ô Ecclesia, Evangelio exculti; nam removebo ab eis omnem usum equorum & qua- drigarum, urbium muros evertam, omnesq; muni- tiones, quæ metuentibus sunt in usu: nam degent absq; muris, sub ficu & vite, quod nemo sit, qui exter- reat, deniq́; omni superstitione remota, è solo Deo pen- debunt, eique soli fident. Cornel. à Lapide etiam ita interpretatur: O Iacob, id est, ô Ecclesia, quæ orta es ex Jacob, sed maxime propagata es per gentes, auferam tibi omnia præsidia, omnia arma, omnes arces & munitiones, quibus antea Christum, fi- demque Christi oppugnabas, vel illi resistebas, ac nominatim auferam maleficia, divinationes, oracula, idola, eorumque fana & urbes. Hæc enim infi- deles opponebant fidei & Ecclesiæ, iisque quasi arietibus Ecclesiam impetebant. Sic etiam B. Höpf- nerus removeri hic putat impedimenta veri DEI cultus, primum equos, quadrigas, urbes & muni- tiones, aliaque id genus dissidentiæ instrumenta, quæ CHRISTUS velit exterminare, & perdere: ac destruere in cordibus impiorum, tum quia remo- rantur fiduciam, tum quia metuentibus in usu sint, deinde incantatores, & divinatores, qui a DEO a- vertunt. Denique idololatriam & adorationem operis manuum.

Potest autem in prioribus retineri sensus lite- ralis de perdendis civitatibus Iudææ & munitionibus, quemadmodum a Romano exercitu illas horribili- ter vastatas esse constat: etiamsi cætera ad libe- randum fideles in civitate ab omni idololatria & ἐθελοθρησκεία referantur: Ut in Judæa compel- lentur partim pervicaciter resistentes, qui evertendi cum suis civitatibus & munitionibus, partim vero sese dominatori in Israel submittentes, qui purgan- di aut immunes præstandi sint ab omni macula im- pietatis & idololatrias, sive cui olim obnoxii fue- rint, sive quam contrahere facile alioquin possent. Annon enim Judææ hæc dici poterant, etsi isto tempore sculptilibus, cultui & divinationibus ma- gicis operam haud dederit? Siquidem olim in majoribus illis addicti fuerint, & in eandem impie- tatem relabi potuerint, nisi Dominatoris Christi virtute ac gratia illa subleventur. Denique ser- vat Scriptura Prophetica morem suum, quo solet phrasibus uti sui seculi, iisque res Novi Testamen- ti explicare, certisque speciebus impietatis olim receptæ, omnem impietatem comprehendere, ut nihil aliud hic indicetur, quam sub N. T. non lo- cum habitaturam in populo Domini, quæ olim vi- guit, impietatem ἐθελοθρησκείαν, adeoque im- munem eandem futuram a maleficiis magicis, cul- tu statuarum, sculptilium, & imaginum, ac venera- tione lucorum.

## 6:1 Argument
SERMON III. Penitential. CHAPTER VI. LEGAL.

The punishments of Israel are set forth for great and small alike, on account of their ingratitude for the benefits of the exodus from Egypt, and of their liberation from Balak, and because of sacrifices offered without faith. The observance of the divine word, Charity, and Humility are demanded: and to the city of Jerusalem, on account of injustice and lies and the imitation of Omri and Ahab—since the examples of idolatry and other sins flowed from Israel to Judah—devastation, famine, and war are announced.

Burnt offerings are worth nothing; let us join Love to faith.

Ver. 1.

HEAR WHAT THE LORD SPEAKS] Hear, I pray, what the Lord says. It is a new discourse, again expressing the causes of the evils impending over the Jews.

ARISE, CONTEND IN JUDGMENT AGAINST THE MOUNTAINS] That is, you, Prophet, plead my case against Judea, which is called a mountain or mountains, because it is very mountainous. Ezek. VI. 2. XXXVIII. 8. Joel II. 1.

Latin:

CONCIO III. Pœnitentialis. CAPUT VI. LEGALE.

Proponuntur magnis pariter & parvis supplicia Is- raelis ob ingratitudinem pro beneficiis eductionis ex Ægypto, & liberationis a Balako & reprobatis sacrificiis sine fide oblatis. Verbi divini observa- tio, Charitas & Humilitas postulatur: Urbique Hierosolym propter injustitiam & mendacia ac imitationem Amri & Achabi, quum ab Israele ad Iudam malum idololatriæ aliorumque peccato- rum exempla manarint, vastatio, fames & bel- lum indicatur.

Nil holocausta valent, fidei jungamus Amorem.

Vers. 1.

AUDITE QUÆ DOMINUS LOQUITUR] Au- dite quæso quod dicit Dominus. Novus est sermo, causas rursus exprimens imminentium Judæis malorum.

SURGE CONTENDE JUDICIO ADVERSUM MONTES] Id est, tu Propheta causam meam age con- tra Judæam, quæ dicitur mons aut montes, quia valde montosa est Ezech. VI. 2. XXXVIII. 8. Joel. II. 1.

## 6:2
Ver. 2.

LET THE MOUNTAINS HEAR THE LORD'S JUDGMENT] The Lord's case. Here the Prophet begins to execute what had been enjoined upon him.

AND THE STRONG FOUNDATIONS OF THE EARTH] That is, the hills, which are like the columns of the earth. By mountains and hills, however, their inhabitants are understood synecdochically.

FOR THE LORD'S JUDGMENT IS WITH HIS PEOPLE] The Lord has a dispute with His people. The Greeks, Κρίσις τῷ Κυρίῳ.

AND HE WILL DISPUTE WITH ISRAEL] He will argue. Great is the goodness of God, who, although He is by supreme right the Lord of all, nevertheless wishes to prove the equity of His actions to men, that is, to worms of the earth, if they are compared to Him. See Isaiah V. 3. XLIII. 26.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

AUDIANT MONTES JUDICIUM DOMINI] Causam Domini. Hic Propheta incipit, quod sibi injun- ctum erat, exequi.

ET FORTIA FUNDAMENTA TERRÆ] Id est, colles, qui velut columnæ sunt terræ. Per montes autem & colles inhabitatores eorum συνεκδοχικῶς intelliguntur.

QUIA JUDICIUM DOMINI CUM POPULO SUO] Lis est Domino cum populo suo. Græci, Κρίσις τῷ Κυρίῳ.

ET CUM ISRAEL DIJUDICABITUR] Dispu- tabit. Magna Dei bonitas, qui cum sit omnium summo jure Dominus, tamen hominibus, id est, vermibus terræ, si ipsi comparentur, probare vult actionum suarum æquita- tem. Vide Esaiæ V. 3. XLIII. 26.

## 6:3
Ver. 3.

MY PEOPLE WHAT HAVE I DONE] A most pathetic oration, such as that one of similar argument in Jeremiah II. v. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

POPVLE MEVS QUID FECI] Oratio μάλα πα- θητικὴ, qualis & illa similis argumenti apud Jeremiam II. v. 8.

## 6:4
Vers. 4.

MOSES] Who might give you the best laws. AND AARON] Who might pray for the people. AND MIRIAM] Who might be an example to the female sex.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

MOSEM] Qui leges tibi daret optimas. ET AARON] Qui pro populo precaretur. ET MARIAM] Quæ exemplum esset fœminino sexui.

## 6:5
Vers. 5.

REMEMBER I PRAY, WHAT BALAK KING OF MOAB THOUGHT, AND WHAT BALAAM THE SON OF BEOR ANSWERED HIM] That is, what Balaam had answered Balak, that you could not be overthrown unless the law of God were despised through idolatry and other flagrant sins, see 2 Pet. II. 16, Jude 11, Rev. II. 14, and see what we have said at Num. XXV. and XXXI. 8.

FROM SHITTIM EVEN UNTO GILGAL] The word 'remember' must be repeated by ellipsis, and there is furthermore an omission, namely of those things which I have done. From Shittim to Gilgal, that is, beyond and on this side of the Jordan. Shittim is that place which is mentioned in Num. XXV. Gilgal is that which is in Joshua V. Many things indeed happened before, but at that time notable benefits of GOD befell the Israelites, especially in the crossing of the Jordan. The LXX here have ἀπὸ σχοίνων: but Jerome rightly conjectures that it was written by them as σείνων, which is a type of wood not unlike the wood שִׁטִּים, from which that place gets its name.

That explanation of 'remember from Shittim even unto Gilgal, how great things God has done for your sake,' has pleased the Chaldean, and also Vatablus, Montanus, Clarius, R. Solomon, Castrius, and others: nor is it to be disapproved. However, the Lord seems especially to be calling back to the people's memory those two notable miracles and benefits: the crossing through the Red Sea at the departure from Egypt, and the crossing of the Jordan in sight of the promised land. For other explanations, please see Christoph à Castro and Cornel. à Lapide. That the miracle of the people crossing the Jordan on dry ground is hinted at here, even B. Luther noted.

THAT YOU MIGHT KNOW THE JUST DEEDS OF THE LORD] That you might know the benefits of God: and say what follows. For often such things are understood among the Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

MEMENTO QUÆSO, QUID COGITAVERIT BALACH REX MOAB, ET QUID RESPONDERIT EI BALAAM FILIUS BEOR] Hoc est, quod Balacho responderat Balaam, non posse te everti, nisi lege Dei contempta per idololatriam, aliaque flagitia, vide 2. Petr. II. 16. Judæ 11. Apoc. II. 14. & vide quæ diximus ad Num. XXV. & XXXI. 8.

DE SETIM USQUE AD GALGALAM] Repetendum ἀπὸ κοινῇ memento, & est præterea ě̀κλειψις nempe eorum quæ fecerim. A Setim ad Gilgalam, id est, ultra cisque Jordanem. Setim est is locus cujus mentio Num. XXV. Gilgala is, cujus Josuæ V. multa quidem & ante, sed illo tempore insignia DEI beneficia Israëlitis contingere, præsertim in Jordanis transitu. LXX. hîc habent ἀπὸ œχοίνων: sed recte conjicit Hieronymus scriptum ab iis œχίνων, quod ligni genus non absimile ligno שִׁטִּים, unde illi loco nomen.

Illa explicatio memento de Setim usœ, ad Galgala, quanta in gratiam tui fecerit Deus, à Chaldæo tradita, Vatablo etiam, Montano, Clario, R. Salomoni, Castrio & aliis placuit: nec improbanda. Revocare autem populo imprimis videtur Dominus in memoriam duo illa insignia miracula & beneficia transitus per mare rubrum in exitu ex Ægypto, & transitus Iordanis in terræ promissæ conspectu. Alias explicationes vide sis apud Christoph. à Castro & Cornel. à Lapid. Innui hîc simul miraculum de populo sicco pede transeunt per Iordanem, etiam B. Lutherus notavit.

UT COGNOSCERES JUSTITIAS DOMINI] Ut cognoscas Dei beneficia: ac dicas, quæ sequuntur. Sæpe enim talia subintelliguntur apud Hebræos.

## 6:6
Vers. 6.

WHAT WORTHY THING SHALL I OFFER TO THE LORD] קדם among the Hebrews and Chaldeans and Arabs, among other things, is to appear before someone. With what thing shall I present myself to the Lord?

I WILL BEND THE KNEE TO THE MOST HIGH GOD] I will submit myself to the most high God. כפף indeed signifies a humble bending of the body, but it is also transferred to the mind, and thus the Chaldean seems to have taken it here.

SHALL I OFFER HIM BURNT OFFERINGS] Which signify the dominion of God over all things, Levit. I.

AND CALVES OF A YEAR OLD] Which were accustomed to be offered for the Priest, Levit. IX. 3.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

QUID DIGNUM OFFERAM DOMINO] קדם Hebræis & Chaldæis & Arabibus inter alia est coram aliquo apparere. Cum qua re me sistam Domino?

CURVABO GENU DEO EXCELSO] Submittam me Deo excelso. כפף corporis quidem humilem flexum significat, sed & ad animum transfertur, & ita videtur hic cepisse Chaldæus.

NUMQUID OFFERAM EI HOLOCAUSTOMATA] Quæ Dominium Dei in res omnes significant Levit. I.

ET VITULOS ANNICULOS] Qui pro Sacerdote offerri solebant Levit. IX. 3.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

WILL THE LORD BE ABLE TO BE APPEASED WITH THOUSANDS OF RAMS?] In the Hebrew: Will God be content with thousands (some) of rams? such as Solomon offered 1 Kings 8:36, and Hezekiah 2 Kings 20:24, and Josiah 2 Chronicles 35:7.

OR WITH MANY THOUSANDS OF FAT GOATS] So also the Greeks: ἐν μυρίασι χιμάρων πιόνων. They read, however, otherwise than it is in the Hebrew, בּרִבְבוֹת נַחֲלֵי־שָׁׁמֶן, in ten thousands of rivers of oil. Which reading if it is true, by rivers are to be understood vessels of the greatest capacity. Oil was customary in the sacrifices of the Hebrews Leviticus 2, 6, 7; besides, there was much need of oil for the lamps.

There is rash doubt concerning the variety of the Hebrew reading. What certainty will be left, if we wish to suspect corruptions of the authentic text in such a way according to our whim? Mariana more correctly conjectures a σφάλμα (error) in the LXX interpreters' edition. He suspects the LXX did not place χιμάρων, that is, of goats, but χειμάρρων, that is, of torrents.

SHALL I GIVE MY FIRSTBORN FOR MY WICKEDNESS] In the Hebrew: my wickedness, that is, the ransom of my wickedness. For punishments and expiations for sins are accustomed to be called by the name of the firstborn among the Hebrews: namely, as the King of Moab did 2 Kings 3:27.

THE FRUIT OF MY WOMB FOR THE SIN

OF MY SOUL] In the Hebrew it is sin. The fruit of my womb, that is, of my wife, as Psalm 132:11, as if they were saying: shall we do what Jephthah did, who vowed his daughter to God?

Latin:

Vers. 7.

NUMQUID PLACARI POTEST DOMINUS IN MILLIBUS ARIETUM?] In Hebræo: An contentus erit Deus millibus (aliquot) arietum? qualia obtulit Salomon 1. Regum VIII. 36. & Ezechias II. 2. Reg. XXX. 24. & Josias II. Paralip. XXXV. 7.

AUT IN MULTIS MILLIBUS HIRCORUM PINGUIUM] Sic & Græci: ἐν μυρίασι χιμάρων πιόνων. Legerunt vero aliter quam in Hebræo est, בּרִבְבוֹת נַחֲלֵי־שָׁׁמֶן, in denis millibus fluentorum olei. Quæ lectione si vera est, per fluenda intelligenda sunt vasa maximæ capacitatis. Oleum usitatum in sacris Hebræorum Levit. II. VI. VII. præterea multa oleo ad lychnos opus.

De varietate lectionis Ebrææ temere ambigitur. Quæ certitudo relinquetur, si ita pro libitu suspicari corruptiones authentici textus velimus? Rectius Mariana σφάλμα in LXX. Interpretes editionem conjicit. Suspicatur LXX. non posuisse χιμάρων, id est, hircorum, sed χειμάρρων, id est, torrentium.

NUMQUID DABO PRIMOGENITUM MEUM PRO SCELERE MEO] In Hebræo: scelus meum id est, λύτρον sceleris mei. Solent enim apud Hebræos pœnæ & piamenta peccatorum nomine appellari: primogenitum nempe, ut fecit Rex Moab 2. Reg. III. 27.

FRUCTUM VENTRIS MEI PRO PECCATO

ANIMÆ MEÆ] Ethic in Hebræo est peccatum. Fructum ventris mei, id est, uxoris meæ, ut Pf. CXXXII. 11. quasi dicant: faciemus, quod fecit Jephthe, qui filiam suam Deo vovit?

## 6:8
Verse 8.

I WILL SHOW THEE O MAN WHAT IS GOOD] In the Hebrew: he will show thee (God, namely, through me the Prophet) what is good: by itself, namely, not only by institution, as other things.

AND WHAT THE LORD REQUIRES OF THEE: CERTAINLY TO DO JUDGMENT, AND TO LOVE MERCY, AND TO WALK HUMBLY WITH THY GOD] In the Hebrew: What does the Lord require of thee, but to do what is just: to love beneficence, and to submit oneself where the matter is with God. There is an excellent preparation here for the Gospel, except that these very things are to be fulfilled after Christ the more perfectly, the more we have received precepts in this triple category that are more excellent, and in the life and death of Christ a most exact example, and the revelation of eternal reward, and greater aids of the Spirit, and freedom from so many rites, so that we might be more unencumbered to apply ourselves entirely to these more important things.

We seem to hear Pelagius and Socinus revived in these, who contended: that the law of Moses was once imperfect, that it was enriched by Christ with such an accession of new and more excellent precepts, that Christ first revealed and openly preached the eternal reward, and promised greater aids of the Spirit, and they thought that not the merit of life or satisfaction for sins was to be sought in the life and death of Christ, but an exact example. Concerning which elsewhere. But those three things which God requires here are not a preparation for the Gospel, which Grotius, in the Pelagian-Socinian manner, confuses with the law, when it is a mere sermon of grace concerning the remission of sins, and is opposed to the law John 1:17, 2 Corinthians 3:1. But they are the sum of those things which were demanded of us both under the Old Testament and are demanded in the New, which we prefer to explain in the words of the Blessed Luther rather than our own: It is known that judgment is often used for the word of God. As Psalm 119 proves, and for this reason, that the word judges men, while it condemns evils, and teaches holy and true things.

Therefore, to perform judgment in this place is to attend to the word: to follow and obey it, not to resist the word, not to hate the word, but to receive it with thanksgiving, to obey it, to undertake nothing without the word, to do diligently what the word commands, etc. Moreover, not only are the duties of the external life, or good works, included in this command, but those spiritual motions about which the first table teaches. For these are the two things of the word of God especially: that it teaches to trust in God and to fear God. Trust in God, however, requires the knowledge of Christ. And so, this is the first thing to be striven for, that we attend to the word of God, that we trust in the mercy exhibited through Christ, and that we fear Him. Such, however, is the worship here that it can be performed by all. For if sacrifices were required, the condition of the rich would be better, that of the poor worse. But God does not require magnificent expenses. He requires a soul trembling at His words and trusting in His mercy.

The second is to love mercy or beneficence. And he expressly uses the word 'to love.' For he sees that a singular desire is implanted in the minds of all men to do good to themselves and to neglect others. He wishes this affection to be removed from our minds, and he wishes there to be in us a singular desire for beneficence toward all. This also is a kind of worship that can be performed by all. For what condition is so base in which you cannot be of use to others? The condition of menservants and maidservants is judged the worst. But these, when they diligently perform what is commanded while they take care of the household affairs or the children, perform a holier work than all monks and nuns;

for they do what God commands. They are exhausted by labors undertaken of their own accord, without a command from GOD, nay, even against the command of GOD. The third is, to walk humbly before God. This pertains not only to this, that we should not be arrogant, proud, presumptuous, but that we should be patient under the cross. As Peter says, Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of GOD, that is, bear the will of GOD with an even mind: Do not be indignant. Do not be turned away from God to human and illicit protections. But humble yourselves, that is, acknowledge the punishment of sins, or at least the necessary mortification of the old man. Then seek and hope for liberation through Christ. These are true acts of worship, and true repentance, and those who perform these, God wishes to love, protect, and defend. And the true Church applies itself to this, that it may offer these acts of worship to God, and that men may be stirred up to such a manner of life and morals. He has summarized those things succinctly in a marginal note in three words: Glauben, lieben, leiden. Cf. here B. Tarnovius.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

INDICABO TIBI O HOMO QUID SIT BONUM] In Hebræo: indicabit tibi (Deus scilicet per me Prophetam) quid bonum sit: per se scilicet, non tantum ex instituto, ut alia.

ET QUID DOMINUS REQVIRAT A TE: VTIQVE FACERE JVDICIVM, ET DILIGERE MISERICORDIAM, ET SOLLICITVM AMBVLARE CVM DEO TVO] In Hebræo: Ecquid Dominus à te exigit, nisi facere quod jus est: amare beneficentiam, & submittere se ubi cum Deo res est. Egregia hic est ad Evangelium præparatio, nisi quod hæc ipsa post Christum tanto implenda perfectius, quanto & præcepta accepimus in triplici hoc genere excellentiora & in Christi vita ac morte exactissimum exemplar, & præmii æterni revelationem, & majora Spiritus auxilia, & libertatem à tot ritibus, quo expeditiores rebus his potioribus toti incumberemus.

Redivivum in his audire videmur Pelagium & Socinum, qui contenderunt: legem Mosis quondam imperfectum fuisse, à Christo istiusmodi accessione novorum præceptorum excellentiorum locupletatam esse, Christum primum revelasse ac palam prædicasse æternum præmium, ac majora Spiritus auxilia promisisse, nec in Christi vita ac morte meritum vitæ, aut satisfactionem pro peccatis, sed exactum exemplar quærendum duxere. De quo alias. Tria autem illa, quæ hic requirit Deus, non præparatio ad Evangelium, quod cum lege, more Pelagio-Socinia no confundit Grotius, quum sit mera gratiæ concio de remissione peccatorum, ac legi opponatur Joh. I. 17. 2. Cor. III. 1. Sed summa eorum sunt, quæ à nobis tum sub V. T. postulata sunt, tum in N. T. postulantur, quæ verbis B. Luth. explicare malumus, quam nostris: Notum est, quod judicium sæpe usurpetur pro verbo DEI. Sicut probat Psalmus 119. idque eam ob causam, quod verbum judicat homines, dum damnat mala, & docet sancta & vera.

Ergo hoc in loco judicium facere, est verbo attendere: id sequi & obedire, non repugnare verbo, non odisse verbum, sed id cum gratiarum actione accipere, ei parere, sine verbo nihil suscipere, quæ verbum mandat sedulo facere, &c. Non solum autem includuntur in hoc mandato externæ vitæ officia, seu bona opera, sed motus illi spirituales, de quibus docet prima tabula. Nam verbi Dei hæc duo præcipue sunt, ut doceat fidere Deo, & timere Deum. Fiducia autem in Deum requirit notitiam Christi. Itaque hoc primum conandum est, ut attendamus verbo Dei, ut fidamus misericordiæ per Christum exhibitæ, & timeamus eum. Ejusmodi autem hic cultus est, ut possit ab omnibus præstari. Nam si sacrificia requirerentur, melior esset divitum conditio, pauperum deterior. Sed non requirit Deus sumptus magnificos. Animum requirit trementem ad sermones suos, & fidentem misericordia ejus.

Secundum est diligere misericordiam seu beneficentiam. Ac diserte utitur verbo diligendi. Videt enim omnium hominum animis inditum esse studium singulare, ut sibi benefaciant, & negligant alios. Hunc affectum vult eximi ex nostris animis, & vult in nobis singulare studium esse beneficentiæ erga omnes. Hic quoque ejusmodi cultus est, qui ab omnibus potest præstari. Quæ enim tam vilis conditio est, in qua non possis prodesse aliis? Deterrima judicatur conditio servorum & ancillarum. Sed hi tum imperata sedulo faciunt, dum curant rem familiarem aut liberos, sanctius opus faciunt, quam omnes Monachi & moniales;

faciunt enim quod Deus mandat. Illi sponte suf- ceptis laboribus defatigantur, sine mandato DEI, imo etiam contra mandatum DEI. Tertium est, humilem ambulare coram Deo. Hoc non solum eo pertinet, ne simus arrogantes, superbi, præsum- ptuosi, sed ut in cruce simus patientes. Sicut Pe- trus dicit, Humiliamini sub potenti manu DEI, hoc est, ferte voluntatem DEI æquo animo: Nolite indignari. Nolite averti à Deo ad humana & illi- cita præsidia. Sed humiliamini, id est agnoscite pœnam peccatorum, aut saltem necessariam morti- ficationem veteris hominis. Deinde petite & spera- te liberationem per Christum. Hi sunt veri cultus, & vera pœnitentia, quam qui præstant, hos amare, tueri, defendere vult Deus. Ac vera Ecclesia in id incumbit, ut hos cultus Deo præstet, & homines ad talem rationem vitæ & morum excitentur. Succin- cte illa Scholio marginali complexus est tribus verbis: Glauben, lieben, leiden. Conf. hic B. Tarno- vius.

## 6:9
Verse 9.

THE VOICE OF THE LORD CRIES TO THE CITY AND SALVATION SHALL BE TO THOSE WHO FEAR THY NAME] Where the voice of the Lord cries to the city, it is wisdom if one fears thy name: trembles at thy majesty.

There is no reason why Grotius should abandon Jerome's version, which is otherwise authentic among the Papists. For although the Hebrew word is variously explained by the Rabbis, yet it is sufficiently agreed that it signifies salvation, success, happiness, and whatever is similar. As the passage in Proverbs 8 shows. Mine is counsel and success. For because right counsels sometimes turn out badly, success (Tuschijah) is required. Likewise ch. 3. He will store up for the righteous (Tuschijah), that is, He will make them prosperous, He will save them in dangers, the wicked will perish, etc., as B. Luther rightly [noted]. Osiander expressed the sense well, as if to say: I now, by the command of the almighty God, exhort you citizens of Jerusalem to repent. Whoever therefore shall have listened to the voice of the Lord, and shall have feared the Lord, and shall have repented, will escape punishments, and will obtain eternal salvation. So also others.

Verse of the same.

HEAR THE TRIBE AND WHO SHALL APPROVE IT] Others, hear the rod, and him who appointed it: so that there is מי for אשר, as elsewhere. But the Chaldean appears to have read מטה and שמען מטה רמי וערה which is, polysemous, taken by him for a scepter, and by the scepter he understands the king: for he translates: Hear O king, and nobles, and assembly, not a bad sense. Thus רמי here will be placed in the construct state in place of the absolute, which we have shown elsewhere is not without examples.

Whatever the Chaldean may have read or not read, whose misinterpretations are frequent enough, his translation ought not to be preferred to the Hebrew truth. Concerning the sense of which, because B. Luther [explained it] clearly enough, it is helpful to hear him here: For others take the word (Mateh) for a rod, so that the meaning is: Hear the rod or the scourge, and him who testifies concerning it. Jerome, however, translates: Hear the tribe, and who shall approve it? but in his Commentaries he follows another opinion. For he says thus, Hear the tribe, which the Lord testifies to you. For the word (Jaad) in common phrase signifies to preach, to proclaim, to teach. But if we look to the text, the simplest meaning is, the Prophet commands first that the tribe should hear, afterwards as if despairing of the fruit, Who, he says, will testify to it? that is, Who may teach this people? Who may preach to it? since no fruit follows, but they themselves persist in their sins, without any repentance as follows in the text: Is there still fire in the house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness, and the meager measure, full of wrath?

Latin:

Vers. 9.

VOX DOMINI AD CIVITATEM CLAMAT ET SALUS ERIT TIMENTIBUS NOMEN TUUM] Ubi vox Domini ad civitatem clamat, sapientia est, si quis ti- meat nomen tuum: majestatem tuam tremat.

Nulla est causa, cur Hieronymi versionem, quæ alias Pontificiis authentica, relinquat Grotius. Etsi enim Ebræa vox varie à Rabinis exponitur, tamen satis constat, significare salutem, successum, felicitatem, & si quid simile est. Sicut ostendit lo- cus Proverb. 8. Meum est consilium & successus. Nam quod recta consilia nonnunquam male ce- dunt, requiritur Tuschijah) successus. Item c. 3. Recondet rectis (Tuschijah,) hoc est, Fortunabit eos, servabit in periculis, impii peribunt, &c. uti re- cte B. Lutherus. Sensum expressit probe Osiander q. d. Ego jam vos cives Jerosolymitanos jussu Dei o mnipotentis ad agendum pœnitentiam hortor. Qui igitur voci Domini auscultaverit, & timuerit Do- minum, atquè resipuerit, pœnas effugiet, & salutem æ- ternam consequetur. Sic & alii.

Vers. eod.

AUDITE TRIBVS ET QUIS APPROBABIT IL- LUD] Alii, audite virgam, & eum qui constituit eam: ut sit מי pro אשר, ut alibi. At Chaldæum apparet legisse מטה & שמען מטה רמי וערה quod est, πολύσημον, ab eo acceptum pro sceptro, & per sceptrum regem intel- ligit: vertit enim: Audite rex, & proceres, & conventus, sen- su non malo. Ita רמי hic erit in regimine positum vi- ce absoluti, quod exemplis non carere alibi ostendimus.

Quicquid legerit, aut non legerit Chaldæus, cujus παρερμηνεῖα satis frequentia, non debebat præferri ejus translatio Ebraicæ veritati. De cu- jus sensu, quia enucleate satis B. Lutherus, eundem hic audire juvat: Nam alii vocabulum (Mateh) accipiunt pro virga, ut sit sententia: Audite virgam seu flagellum, & eum qui testificatur de eo. Hie- ronymus autem vertit: Audite tribus, & quis ap- probabit illud? sed in Commentariis sequitur a- liam sententiam. Sic enim dicit, Audite tribus, quæ vobis contestatur Dominus. Nam verbum (Jaad) usitata phrasi significat concionari, prædicare, do- cere. Sed si ad textum respiciamus, simplicissima sententia est, jubet Propheta primum, ut tribus au- diant, postea tanquam desperans de fructu, Quis inquit, testificabitur ei? hoc est? Quis hunc populum doceat? Quis ei concionetur? cum nullus fructus sequatur, sed ipsi pergant in suis peccatis, sine o- mni pœnitentia sicut sequitur in textu: Nonne adhuc ignis in domo impii, thesauri impietatis, & mo- dius macilentus, ira plenus?

## 6:10
Verse 10.

STILL FIRE IN THE HOUSE OF THE WICKED] He reads יש with tsere, not with hiric, and so do the Greeks. It can rightly be called fire, because it is the cause why all things are consumed. Jas. 5:3.

If we follow the Hebrew, the sense will be: Does there still (remain) to anyone the house of the wicked. A house acquired by wickedness. And are not those things returned after so many warnings which were snatched away?

The Vulgate is to be corrected entirely, which substitutes fire for the LXX's erring [text], as if אש were written. Tarnovius renders the sense from the Hebrew thus: Is there not still, after so many admonitions that you should desist from them, a house of the wicked among you, and treasures of wickedness above c. 2, 2. In which there is desolation rather than consolation. Jac. V. 1. 2. 3. Where the rhetorical question, very often noted, presses them not to deny what conscience testifies to be true. Rightly, therefore, did B. Luther translate: Still unrighteous goods remain in the house of the godless.

TREASURES OF WICKEDNESS] Ill-gotten wealth. AND THE LESSER MEASURE FULL OF INDIGNATION] And the Epha less (than just, which is) abominable. The Epha is a measure for dry goods. He explains what he signified above by the word judgment.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ADHUC IGNIS IN DOMO IMPII] Legit יש cum tsere, non cum hiric, sic & Græci. Ignis recte dici potest, quod causa est, cur omnia consumantur. Jac. V. 3.

Si Hebræum fequamur, fenfus erit: Adhucne alicui (ma- net) Domus impii. Domus impietate quæfita. Nęc tot post monitus redduntur quæ rapta funt?

Corrigenda omnino Vulgata, quæ ignem ex LXX. errantibus fupponit, quasi אש scriptum sit. Senfum ex Ebræo ita reddit Tarnovius: Nonne adhuc post tot admonitiones, ut desisteretis ab illis, est alicui inter vos domus improbi, & thefauri impro- bitatis fupra c. 2, 2. In quibus est potius defola- tio, quam confolatio. Jac. V. 1. 2. 3. Ubi interro- gatio Rhetorica sæpissime notata, premit eos ne negent, quod conscientia verum esse testatur. Recte itaque transtulit B. Lurtherus: Noch bleibet unrecht Gut in der Gottlofen Hauß.

THESAURI INIQUITATIS] Opes male partæ. ET MENSURA MINOR IRÆ PLENA] Et Epha minus (justo, quod est) abominabile. Epha menfura arido- rum. Explicat quid fupra fignificaverit voce judicii.
