The Prophet says not only that no care is to be taken for sins. That all memory of them is to be abolished is fully implied in Ps. CIII. 12. Is. XLIII. 12. Nor is it observed without reason that there is an allusion to the submersion of Pharaoh, with Basil preceding in Sermon I. on Ps. LXXIIX. and Aug. hom. on Ps. 103. Just as the Egyptians in the Red Sea, so our sins are submerged and extinguished in Baptism or when they are forgiven by God. Tarnovius rightly noted the emphasis in the preceding phrase, of which this is the explanation, and our iniquities which, by the rigor of the law 1 Cor. XV. 56, were tyrannically dominating us like slaves Is. LI. Rom. VI. and VII., these chains of the devil being broken, he will subject, trample, and crush (which is the emphasis of the verb כבש) us, asserting us for his glory and our salvation, since its meaning, as the Rabbis write, is תפוסה and רדיה of dominion and comprehension Gen. I. 28. Num. XXXII. 22. 29. 2 Samuel IIX. 11. 2 Chron. XXIX. 10. Esth. VII. 8. Jer. XXXIV. 16. B. Chytreus taught how the entire doctrine of justification is explained here by the Prophet: This Sermon of Micah is among the chief testimonies of the Prophets, which describes the righteousness of the Gospel, or the remission of sins granted on account of Christ, illustrated by an exposition of the efficient, impulsive, and formal causes. The principal efficient cause of righteousness is God, who with immense goodness and mercy forgives sins, as is said here: Who is a God like God, forgiving iniquity? Rom. IIX. It is God who justifies. The impulsive causes, by which God is moved to forgive us our sins, are not our virtues and good deeds, but the truth and mercy of God, or the grace promised to Abraham and Jacob on account of the blessed seed, and confirmed by the oath of God Gen. XXII. Ps. CX. Which the Epistle to the Hebrews ch. VI. unfolds. The formal cause of our righteousness before God is the gratuitous remission, i.e., the pardon of our sins, the alien righteousness of Christ imputed to us through faith,

who by his obedience in passion and death, paid the debt for us, and fully satisfied divine justice. Micah repeats this formal cause in this place six times with almost synonymous words through an explanation. 1. He forgives iniquity, i.e., lifts and takes away iniquity from us. Ps. 32. Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven. 2. He passes over, i.e., passes by, and does not deign to look upon the sins of those who believe in Christ. 3. He does not retain forever, but with immense goodness and mercy forgives his anger against sin, Psalm 103. The Lord will not be angry forever, he is merciful and compassionate; for that whole Psalm is to be used as a notable Commentary on the present sermon of Micah, and is to be learned by heart word for word by everyone. 4. He returns to us, and has mercy on us, whom he had left and deserted, being angry on account of sins. 5. He subjects and suppresses under his feet and tramples, or crushes our iniquities, so that they are completely abolished, and come into eternal oblivion. 6. He casts all our sins into the depth of the sea, where, covered and buried, they will no longer be able to be seen by anyone. Micah inculcates this with so many words for this reason, that minds may hold true and effective consolation to be opposed to the poisonous bites of despair: and that he may teach that our righteousness before God is nothing other than the gratuitous Remission or pardon of our sins, and that there are not two parts of our righteousness or justification: Remission of sins on account of Christ, and renewal of nature through the Holy Spirit, i.e., new obedience, i.e., our qualities and virtues. Therefore, also in this place, Micah, and the whole Scripture preaching the remission of sins through Christ, shows that our entire salvation and righteousness is placed in it. And Paul in Rom. 3 and 4, where he expressly undertakes to explain the article of justification entirely and accurately, clearly places the righteousness and blessedness of man in the remission, or non-imputation of sin. And the same affirms that to impute righteousness is the same as not to impute, or to cover sin. Nor does he make mention of newness of life in that whole explanation, even with a single word. Therefore, our newness or vivification cannot be constituted as a part of righteousness before GOD, since in that place, which contains the most absolute and perfect explanation of the doctrine of justification in all of Scripture, it is not even named by Paul. But he mentions only the remission of sins or the imputation of righteousness, and among other things says that Christ was appointed by God as a propitiator through faith in his blood, to show that he justifies by the remission of sins which were present. Afterwards he often opposes justification to condemnation, and indeed uses the terms justification, remission of sins, reconciliation, and imputation of righteousness indiscriminately. Just as Christ also in Luke 18 affirms that the publican, seeking reconciliation or remission of sin, went down to his house justified. Finally, the whole scripture of the Old Testament also, and especially Isaiah chapters 53, 40, 43, 44, 38, 35, and elsewhere, places our righteousness and salvation solely in the remission or deletion of sins accomplished through the savior Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 19. REVERTETUR, ET MISEREBITUR NOSTRI] Id est, iterum nostri miserebitur: ut sæpe olim. Hebraismus notus.

DEPONET INIQUITATES NOSTRAS] In Hebræo est: Subjiciet, sive, sub pedibus ponet: ut ea quæ adspicere nolumus.

ET PROJICIET IN PROFUNDUM MARIS OMNIA PECCATA NOSTRA] In Hebræo: Eorum,i. e. singulorum de populo. In mare projici dicuntur & Græcis & Latinis ea, quorum nulla cura habetur. Horatius: - - - tristitiam & metus Tradam protervis in mare Creticum Portare ventis.

Non tantum nullam curam peccatorum habendam, dicit Propheta. Omnem eorum memoriam abolendam plene innuitur Ps. CIII. 12. Es. XLIII. 12. Nec temere observatur, alludi ad Pharaonis submersionem, præeunte Basilio Serm. I. in Psal. LXXIIX. & Aug. hom. in Ps. 103. Sicut Ægyptios in mari rubro, ita delicta nostra in Baptismo vel cum remittuntur a Deo demergi, & extingui. Emphafin in phrasi præcedente, cujus hæc est explicatio, notavit probeTarnovius, & iniquitates nostras quæ nobis ex legis rigore 1. Cor.XV.56. tanquam mancipiis dominabantur tyrannice Es. LI. Rom. VI. & VII. disruptis hisce diaboli vinculis, nos gloriæ suæ & saluti nostræ asserens subiget, pessundabit, concullobit (quæ est verbi כבש emphasin) fiquidem significatio ejus, ut scribunt Rabini, est תפוסה & רדיה dominii & comprehensionis Genes. I. 28. Num. XXXII. 22. 29. 2. Samuel. IIX. 11. 2. Chron. XXIX.10. Efth. VII. 8. Jer. XXXIV. 16. Quomodo hic universa doctrina justificationis a Propheta explicata sit, docuit B. Chytreus: Est hæc Michææ Concio inter præcipua Prophetarum testimonia, quæ justitiam Evangelii, seu remissionem peccatorum propter Christum donatam describit, illustratam expositione causarum efficientis, impulsivæ & formalis. Causa efficiens principalis justitiæ est Deus immensa bonitate &misericordia remittens peccata,ut hic dicitur: Quis Deus sicut Deus remittens iniquitatem? Rom. IIX. Deus est qui justificat. Causæ impulsivæ,quibus movetur Deus,ut peccata nobis re- „mittat, non sunt virtutes & benefacta nostra, sed „Dei veritas & misericordia,seu gratia Abrahæ & „Jacob propter semen benedictum promissa, & ju- „rejurando Dei confirmata Gen. XXII. Psal. CX. „Quod Epistola ad Ebræos c. VI. evolvit. Causa „formalis justitiæ nostræ coram Deo est gratuita „remissio f. condonatio peccatorum nostrorum, „imputata nobis per fidem aliena Christi justitia,

„qui sua obedientia in passione & morte, debitum „pro nobis persolvit, & justitiæ divinæ integre fa- ”cisfecit. Hanc causam formalem Michæas hoc „in loco sexies mutatis verbis fere synonymis per ”Explicationem repetit. 1. Remittit iniquitatem s. ”levat & tollit à nobis iniquitatem. Ps. 32. Beati ”quorum remissæ sunt iniquitates. 2. Transit s. ”præterit, nec aspicere dignatur peccata eorum, ”qui in Christum credunt. 3. Non retinet in perpe- ”tuum, sed immensa bonitate & misericordia re- ”mittit iram suam adversus peccatum, Psalm. 103. ”Non in perpetuum irascetur, misericors & mi- ”serator Dominus; nam totus ille Psalmus, velut ”insignis Commentarius ad præsentem Michææ ”concionem adhibendus, & de verbo ad verbum ”à singulis ediscendus est. 4. Revertitur ad nos, & ”miseretur nostri, quos propter peccata iratus de- ”liquerat & deseruerat. 5. Subjicit & supprimit pe- ”dibus ac conculcat, seu pessundat iniquitates no- ”stras, ut plane aboleantur, & in æternam oblivio- ”nem veniant. 6. Projicit in profundum maris o- ”mnia peccata nostra, ubi tecta & sepulta, non am- ”plius à quoquam conspici poterunt. Hæc eam ”ob causam tot verbis inculcat Michæas, ut veram ”& efficacem consolationem venenatis morsibus ”desperationis opponendam animi teneant: ac ut ”doceat, justitiam nostram coram Deo, nihil aliud ”esse, quam gratuitam Remissionem seu condo- ”nationem peccatorum nostrorum, nec duas ”esse partes justitiæ seu justificationis nostræ: ”Remissionem peccatorum propter Christum, & ”renovationem naturæ per Spiritum Sanctum s. ”novam obedientiam s. nostras qualitates & vir- ”tutes. Ideo & hoc in loco Michæas, & univer- ”sa Scriptura remissionem peccatorum per Chri- ”stum prædicans, ostendit totam salutem & justi- ”tiam nostram in ea positam esse. Et Paulus ”Rom. 3. & 4. ubi ex professo articulum justifica- ”tionis integre & accurate explicandum suscipit, ”diserte justitiam & beatitudinem hominis in re- ”missione, aut non imputatione peccati collocat. Et ”imputare justitiam affirmat idem esse, quod ”non imputare, vel tegere peccatum. Nec ullam ”in tota illa explicatione novitatis vitæ mentio- ”nem vel unico verbo facit. Non igitur potest ”pars justitiæ coram DEO constitui nostra no- ”vitas aut vivificatio, cum in eo loco, quæ ”absolutissimam in tota scriptura & perfectam do- ”ctrinæ justificationis explicationem continet, à ”Paulo ne quidem nominatur. Sed solius remis- ”sionis peccatorum s. imputationis justitiæ memi- ”nit, ac inter cætera ait, Christum à Deo propitia- ”torem constitutum esse per fidem in sanguine ”ejus, ad ostendendum quod justificet Remissio- ”ne peccatorum, quæ adfuerunt. Postea sæpe ”Justificationem opponit condemnationi, & qui- ”dem promiscue vocabulis justificationis, remis- ”sionis peccatorum, reconciliationis, Imputatio- ”nis justitiæ utitur. Sicut & Christus Luc. XIIX. ”publicanum petentem reconciliationem s. remis- ”sionem peccati, affirmat justificatum descen- ”disse in domum suam. Denique tota etiam ”scriptura veteris Testamenti, ac imprimis Esaias ”cap. LIII. XL. XLIII. XLIV. XXXIIX. XXXV. & ”alibi justitiam & salutem nostram in sola Remis- ”sione s. deletione peccatorum per salvatorem ”Christum facta collocat.

## 7:20
V. 20. THOU WILT GIVE TRUTH TO JACOB] Truth here and often elsewhere is faithfulness in fulfilling promises. You will fulfill to the descendants of Jacob what you promised to Jacob. Gen. 35:12.

MERCY TO ABRAHAM] That is, you will show your goodness toward the offspring of Abraham. For descendants are accustomed to be called by the name of their ancestors, just as Zerubbabel is also called David.

QUÆ JURASTI] It can be correctly translated as, which you swore. PATRIBUS NOSTRIS A DIEBUS ANTIQUIS] Already long ago, to the Fathers, that is, to Abraham himself Gen. XII, 2. XV. 6. XVII. 7. & following: to Isaac Gen. XXVI. 4. to Jacob Gen. XXVIII. 13. In this promised goodness is also comprehended this, that the progeny of those fathers may never perish & that as often as it turns itself entirely to God, it may be restored to its ancient possession. Deut. XXX. 1. 2. 3. 4. This is the privilege given to this one people on account of the fathers: τὰ δῶρα ἀμεταμέλητα.

To τὰ δῶρα τὰ ἀμεταμέλητα, neither the preservation of the progeny of the Patriarchs, nor its conversion to God, nor its restoration to its ancient possession contributes; indeed, these things seem to smack of Judaism. For if the progeny of the Patriarchs is still preserved by God with that hope of restoration to its ancient possession, if it turns itself, it is no wonder that the Jews await a restoration to the land of Canaan. But that those things concerning the promise of Jacob & the mercy of Abraham, & which were made to the Fathers from days of old, look toward the mission of the Messiah, the scripture itself is a most reliable witness Gen. XII. c. XVI. c. XIX. c. XXII. 16. 17. c. XXVI. 1. Deut. VII. 8. c. XXIV. 13. Ps. LXXXIX. 3. CIV. Ps. CXXXII. 11. Is. LV. Luke I. Rightly, therefore, the Blessed Luther, whom all other interpreters support (for there has not been any doubt about it among any Christian interpreter). The final clause concerning the faith & mercy promised to the fathers, & faithfully kept, pertains to this, that we may learn that the cause of such great benefits is none other than that God by his nature is merciful. And so he did not wish us, submerged in sin & the wrath of God, to perish; he wished to save, and promised salvation to Abraham through the blessed seed. Jacob also had this promise. For he sees Christ about to be born from the descendants of Judah

Latin:

V. 20. DABIS VERITATEM JACOB] Veritas hic & alibi sæpe est fides in præstandis promissis. Præstabis Jacobi posteris, quod Jacobo promisisti. Gen. XXXV. 12.

MISERICORDIAM ABRAHAM] Id est, boni- tatem tuam ostendes erga Abrahami sobolem. Solent e- nim posteri vocari nomine majorum, quomodo & Zoro- babel David dicitur.

QUÆ JURASTI] Recte verti potest, quam jurasti. PATRIBUS NOSTRIS A DIEBUS ANTIQUIS] Jam olim, Patribus, id est, Abrahamo ipsi Gen. XII, 2. XV. 6. XVII. 7. & sequentibus : Isaaco Genes. XXVI. 4. Ja- cobo Gen. XXVIII. 13. In hac bonitate promissa & hoc comprehenditur, ut nunquam intereat illorum patrum progenies & ut quoties se universam ad Deum convertat, restituatur in veterem possessionem. Deut. XXX. 1. 2. 3. 4. Hoc est privilegium uni isti populo propter patres da- tum : τὰ δῶρα ἀμεταμέλητα.

Ad τὰ δῶρα τὰ ἀμεταμέλητα non conservatio progeniei Patriarcharum, non conversio ejusdem ad Deum, non restitutio in veterem possessionem facit, imo hæc Judaismum sapere videntur. Si enim Pa- triarcharum progenies adhuc cum spe illa resti- tutionis in veterem possessionem, si se convertat, à Deo conservetur, non mirum quod Judæi præ- stolentur restitutionem in terram Canaan. Quod autem illa de promissione Jacobi & misericordia Abraham, & quæ facta Patribus à diebus antiquis, respiciant Messiæ missionem, ejus testis locupletif- simus est ipsa scriptura Gen. XII. c. XVI. c. XIX. c. XXII. 16. 17. c. XXVI. 1. Deut. VII. 8. c. XXIV. 13. Pl. XXCIX. 3. CIV. Ps. CXXXII. 11. Es. LV. Luc. I. Recte itaq; B. Luth. cui omnes reliqui Interpp. suffragantur (neque enim de eo penes ullum Chri- stianum interpretem dubium fuit) Postrema par- ticula de fide & misericordia promissa patribus, & fi- deliter servata, pertinet eo, ut causam discamus tanto- rum beneficiorum aliam non esse, quam quod Deus natura sua est misericors. Itaque non voluit nos de- mersos in montem & iram Dei perire, salvare vo- luit, ac salutem promisit Abrahæ per semen bene- dictum. Hanc promissionem etiam Jacob habuit. Videt enim Christum ex posteris Judæ nasciturum

# Nahum

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
YEAR AT THE PRESS FOR NAHUM

The name Nahum from נחם denotes comforted or comforter; but he is called an Elkoshite, not from his Father as some in Jerome, nor from his family, as Vatablus, but from his native land, a small village in Galilee, as Jerome notes. On the occasion of the cruelty & Ἐπιχαιρεκακία (rejoicing in evil) of the Assyrians against the Jews, he denounces destruction to them, and especially to the great city of Nineveh, which after the times of Jonah had fallen away from piety, but to these [the Jews] a happy outcome from their evils.

Rightly Jerome: Nahum is expressed as comforter. And in truth his discourses were written for the consolation of the Israelite people. For the destruction of enemies is the consolation of the Church.

There are two parts. I. The denunciation of the destruction of the Ninevites and of Sennacherib, with the subjoined announcement of Evangelical peace among the Jews, chapter 1.

(II.) A fuller explanation of the destruction, Chapter II and III, where in chapter II indeed a miserable description is had of the horrible Babylonian army and the devastation of Nineveh, which was as it were a habitation of lions. But in the third chapter the causes of such great evils are set forth at the same time, slaughter, lies, and rapacity, along with the tremendous armament of the enemies and the immense multitude of the slain, and on account of fornications with foreigners and sorceries, the uncovering of shame before foreigners, without any pity, is proclaimed in the storming of the same, and

to be, as his prophecy testifies Gen. 49. In this manner Mary remembered the promise in the Canticle: He hath holpen Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy, As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed, for ever. And Zacharias the father of John the Baptist Luke 1. He hath remembered his holy covenant, the oath which he sware to our father Abraham. To this God the Father of the τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν [mercies] be glory in Christ Jesus, that blessed seed, our only Saviour for ever and ever Amen. I too will say, with Jerome at the end of the volume, sealing the labor of my little work with the invocation of the Lord: God, who is like unto thee? Take away the iniquity of thy servant, pass over the sin of the remnants of my soul, do not cast thy fury upon me, nor rebuke me in thy wrath: For thou art merciful, and thy mercies are many: Return and have mercy on me, cast my iniquities and send them into the depth of the sea, that the saltness and bitterness of vices may perish in the salt region. Give the truth, which thou didst promise to thy servant Jacob, and the mercy, which thou didst promise to thy friend Abraham, and deliver my soul from the persecutors of thy prophets, Ahab and Jezebel, as thou didst swear to my fathers in the days of old, saying: As I live, saith the Lord: I desire not the death of the sinner, only that he return, and live: And elsewhere: As soon as you have groaned having turned, you shall be saved. Then my enemy shall see, and shall be covered with shame, who now says to me: Where is the Lord thy God? I shall see thy vengeance upon her, and she shall be as the mire of the streets, and shall be trodden down, that she may no longer build Egyptian cities out of mud and straw, Amen.

QUIUM.

is confirmed by the similar example of the city of No, from which destruction it could be freed neither by fortifications, nor by wealth, nor by the strength of heroes, nor is it to be raised up by the συμπαθείᾳ [sympathy] of anyone.

Latin:

ANNO AD NAH PRÆLO

NOmen Nahum à נחם consolatus est consolatorem notat, Elkeseus autem non à Patre ut quidam apud Hieronymum, nec à familia, ut Vatablus, sed à Pa- tria, parvo in Galilæa viculo, notante Hieronymo dictus Propheta. Occasio- ne crudelitatis & Ἐπιχαιρεκακίας Assyriorum ad- versus Judæos, illis, & cumprimis magnæ civitati Ni- nives, quæ post tempora Jonæ à pietate defecerat, exitium, his vero lætum è malis exitum denunciat.

Recte Hieronymus: Nahum exprimitur consola- tor. Et revera conciones ejus ad consolationem popu- li Israelitici scriptæ sunt. Nam hostium deletio est Ecclesiæ consolatio.

Partes sunt duæ I. Excidii Ninivitarum & Sennacheribi denunciatio, cum subjuncta Pacis in- ter Judæos Evangelicæ annunciatione cap. 1.

(II.) Excidii amplior explicatio Cap. II. & III. ubi cap. II. quidem Exercitus Babylonici horribilis & vastationis Ninives, quæ veluti leonum habitacu- lum fuit miserabilis descriptio habetur. Capite ve- ro tertio causæ simul tantorum malorum exponun- tur, cædes, mendacia & rapacitas, cum hostium ar- matura tremenda & occisorum multitudine immensa, & ob scortationes cum exteris, & veneficia pudendo- rum denudatio penes exteros, sine ullius commise- ratione, in expugantione ejusdem indicitur, atque

esse, sicut testatur ejus vaticinium Gen. 49. Ad hunc modum meminerunt promissionis Maria in Cantico: Suscepit Israel puerum suum, recordatus misericordiae suae, Sicut locutus est ad Patres nostros, Abrahae & femini ejus, in seculum. Et Zacharias pa- ter Johannis Baptistae Luc. 1. Recordatus est Testa- menti sui sancti, juramenti, quod juravit Abrahae Pa- tri nostro. Huic Deo Patri τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν sit gloria in Christo Jesu, semine illo benedicto, Salvatore no- stro unico in secula seculorum Amen. Dicam & e- go, cum Hieronymo in fine voluminis, laborem opusculi mei Domini invocatione consignans: Deus quis similis tibi? aufer iniquitatem servi tui, transi peccatum reliquiarum animae meae, ne immittas in me furorem tuum, neque in ira tua corripias me: Quoniam misericors es, & multae miserationes tuae: Revertere & miserere mei, praecipita iniquitates meas & mitte eas in profundum maris, ut salsugo & amaritudo vitiorum in salsa regione dispereat. Da veritatem, quam promisisti servo tuo Iacob, & mi- sericordiam, quam pollicitus es amico tuo Abraham, & libera animam meam a persequentoribus Propheta- rum tuorum, Achab & Hiezabel, sicut jurasti Patri- bus meis in diebus antiquis, dicens: Vivo ego, dicit Dominus: Nolo mortem peccatoris, tantum ut re- vertatur, & vivat: Et alibi: Statim ut conversus ingemueris, salvus eris. Tunc videbit inimica mea, & operietur confusione, quae nunc dicit ad me: Ubi est Dominus Deus tuus? Videbo in ea ultionem tuam, & erit quasi lutum platearum, atque calcabi- tur, ne amplius de luto & paleis Ae- gyptias extruat civitates, Amen.

QUIUM.

simili exemplo civitatis No confirmatur, à quo ex- itio nec per munitiones, nec per opes, nec per for- titudinem Heroum liberari queat, nec cujusquam συμπαθείᾳ erigenda sit.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. The denunciation of the Ninevitic destruction, with the announcement of Evangelical peace in Judea. CHAPTER I.

By the zeal and wrath of GOD graphically depicted, which no one is able to sustain, and the grace of God towards the faithful proclaimed, the Prophet threatens the Ninevites with total destruction along with the destruction of King Sennacherib among his idols, and the announcement of the Evangelical peace to come through the Apostles, and joyful festivals in Judea: which for that reason is also to be liberated from that enemy (Sennacherib).

Nahum sings dire things of Nineveh, good fates of Judah.

Vers. 1. THE BURDEN OF NINEVEH] That is, dire things against the city of Ninus, under which is simultaneously comprehended the whole empire of the Assyrians: which after the times of Jonah had returned again to its old ways. The Hebrews think that both Nahum and Habakkuk wrote in the times of Manasseh: and this is persuaded to us both by the order in which these Prophets were anciently placed after those who lived in the times of Hezekiah: and by the things themselves which are contained in their writings. For this prophecy of Nahum was fulfilled by Nabopallasar, the father of Nebuchadnezzar. Strabo book XVI. Ἡ Νινευῆ ἠφανίσθη παραχρῆμα μετὰ τὴν τῶν Σύρων κατάλυσιν [Nineveh was made to disappear immediately after the overthrow of the Syrians]. Josephus, about to come to the affairs of Nebuchadnezzar, antiq. X. 6. thus prefaces: τοὺς βαβυλωνίους οἳ τὴν Ἀσσυρίων κατέλυσαν ἀρχὴν [the Babylonians who overthrew the empire of the Assyrians], which Jerome says happened while Josiah was reigning among the Hebrews on Jonah. You will refer this prophecy here even better than to that calamity which happened 105 years after this Prophet: and if you rightly consider all things which are said here, you will not find the destruction of the city, but its surrender, and the loss of its empire and affairs.

They render the Hebrew משׂא as an onerous prophecy: משׂא means he lifted, he carried, which refers to a burden heavy and difficult to carry. By this title are distinguished the prophecies denouncing heavy punishments, Isa. 13. 1, ch. 15. 1, ch. 18. 1, ch. 19. 1, ch. 21. 1, 11, 13, Jer. 23. 33, Hab. 1. 1, Zech. 9. 1, ch. 12. 1, Mal. 1. 1. Concerning the passage in Zech. 12. 1, it could be doubtful. But more on that in that place. There is no small question concerning the time of both the prophecy or prediction of Nahum, and its fulfillment. Regarding the time of the prophecy, Grotius followed the Jews in Seder Olam, Vatablus, and Arias Montanus, who wish for Nahum to have published his prophecy under Manasseh. But others refer the same to the times of Father Manasseh or Hezekiah, and wish for him to have prophesied after his sixth year and before the 14th, which was the year of the siege of Jerusalem made by Sennacherib, with this argument especially, that Nah. ch. 1 foretold the arrival of Sennacherib and the liberation of the city from him. Jerome has it thus: Nahum is placed after Jonah, because they seem to prophesy about the same city. For it is written in Jonah: The word of the Lord came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying: Arise and go to Nineveh the great city and preach in it. But in Nahum this is the beginning: The burden of Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite. Therefore both weave a prophecy about Nineveh, the metropolis of the Assyrians, which is now called Ninus: Furthermore, in the Hebrew, Micah is placed after Jonah, and Nahum follows Micah, which is interpreted as comforter. For already the ten tribes had been led into captivity by the Assyrians under Hezekiah king of Judah, under whom even now, for the consolation of the transplanted people, the vision is seen against Nineveh; nor was it a small consolation, as much for those who were already serving the Assyrians, as for the rest who were being besieged by the same enemies under Hezekiah from the tribe of Judah and Benjamin, to hear that the Assyrians also were to be captured by the Chaldeans. These are his words. Theodoret, Theophylact, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Ribera, Castrius, Corn. à Lapide, and other interpreters also refer it to the times of Hezekiah.

Grotius reduces the time of fulfillment to the reign of Nabopolassar: but not with sufficiently weighty arguments. Not a few others refer it rather to the reign of the son of Nebuchadnezzar. Nor do they have contemptible arguments, of which we will bring forward only one: that it is predicted in Nah. 3. 7, 8: that Nineveh was to be overturned after the overturning of Alexandria, which is proposed as its example. For this is said to have been overturned only after Jerusalem. Josephus certainly is the author that Nebuchadnezzar, in the fifth year after the devastation of Jerusalem, invaded Egypt, whose metropolis is Alexandria. And it seems likely that Nebuchadnezzar, having razed Jerusalem and occupied Egypt, invaded Nineveh, the citadel of the Assyrian Monarchy, and having captured it, transferred the Monarchy from Nineveh to Babylon, even though it had been captured even before that under Esarhaddon, the son of Sennacherib, by Merodach-Baladan, King of Babylon: from which time the Kings of the Assyrians were no longer named, but only those of the Babylonians.

Cocceius has invented a new and unheard-of commentary on this Prophet as in most others: namely, that it treats here of Jerusalem (1) as to be finally cut off in the last time, (2) as to be freed from the yoke of Sennacherib, (3) as to be destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, (4) as to be restored for the restoration of the temple and worship and the celebration of the Feasts. Who also pretends that Habakkuk treats more fully of the Babylonians and

Romans and of the Anti-Christ, so that through these two Prophets the WHOLE ORDER of times is woven together, but those private and merely arbitrary interpretations do not deserve a review, let alone a refutation.

ELKOSHITE] Jerome hands down here that Elkosh is a small village of Galilee. The Chaldean calls it Beth-Keffi? so that 'el' here might be an article as among the Arabs.

Latin:

PARS I. Excidii Ninivitici denunciatio, cum pacis Evangelicae in Iudaea annunciatione. CAPUT I.

Zelo & ira DEI graphice depicta quam nemo sustine- re valet, & gratia Dei erga fideles depraedicata mi- natur Propheta Ninivitis totale excidium cum exi- tio Regis Sennacheribi inter idola, & annunciatione pacis Evangelicae per Apostolos futura, laetisque Fe- stivitatibus in Judaea: quae ideo etiam ab isto hoste (Sennacheribo) liberanda est.

Dira canit Ninive, Iudae bona fata Nachumus.

Vers. 1. ONUS NINIVE] Id est, dirae adversus urbem Ninon, sub qua simul comprehenditur totum imperium Assyriorum: quod post Jonae tempora iterum ad veteres mores redierat. Censent Hebraei tam Nahumum, quam Habacucum scripsisse Manassis temporibus: idque nobis persuadent tum ordo, quo antiquitus positi sunt hi Pro- phetae post eos, qui Ezechiae vixere temporibus: tum res ipsae, quae in eorum scriptis continentur. Nam haec Na- humi Prophetia impleta est per Nabopallasarum patrem Nabuchodonosori. Strabo libro XVI. Ἡ Νινευῆ ἠφα- νίσθη παραχρῆμα μετὰ τὴν τῶν Σύρων κατάλυσιν. Josephus ad res venturus Nabuchodonosori, antiq. X. 6. sic praeloquitur: τοὺς βαβυλωνίους οἳ τὴν Ἀσσυρίων κατέλυσαν ἀρχὴν, quod eve- nisse Josia apud Hebraeos regnante, ait Hieronymus ad Jonam. Huc etiam melius hoc vaticinium referes quam ad eam calamitatem, quæ CV. post hunc Prophe- tam annis evenit: & si recte consideres cuncta quæ hic di- cuntur, non invenies excidium urbis, sed deditionem, at- que imperii rerumque jacturam.

EBræum משׂא prophetiam onerosam reddunt: משׂא sustulit, portavit, quod onus portatu gra- ve ac difficile referat. Quo titulo insigniuntur va- ticinic, gravia supplicia denunciantia Ef. XIII. 1. cap. XV. 1. c. XVIII. 1. c. XIX. 1. c. XXI. 1. 11. 13. Ierem. XXIII. 33. Hab. I. 1. Zach. IX. 1. c. XII. 1. Mal. I. 1. De loco Zach. XII. 1. dubium esse posset. Sed de eodem istic loci. De tempore tum Prophetiæ vel vaticinii Nahumi, tum complementi non levis quæ- stio est. De vaticinii tempore sequutus Iudæos Gro- tius in Seder olam, Vatablum & Ariamontanum, qui Nahumum sub Manasse Prophetiam suam edidisse volunt. At alii ad Patris Manassis vel Ezechia tem- pora eundem referunt, ac post sextum ejusdem annum, & ante 14. qui obsidionis Hierosolymitanæ à Sennacheribo factæ annus erat, prophetasse eum volunt, hoc inprimis argumento, quod Nah. c. I. Sennacheribi adventum & urbis ab eodem libera- tionem prædixerit. Hieronym. ita habet: post Ionam Nahum ponitur, quia videntur de eadem urbe prophe- tare. Scriptum siquidem est in Iona: Factus est sermo Domini ad Jonam Filium Amithai, dicens: Surge & vade in Ninivem civitatem magnam & prædica in ea. In Nahum vero istud exordium est: Assumtio Ninivæ, liber visionis Nahum Helkesei. Igitur uterque de Ninive Assyriorum metropoli, quæ nunc vocatur Ninus, texunt vaticinium: Porro in Hebraico post Ionam Michæas ponitur, & Michæam sequitur Nahum, qui interpretatur consolator. Iam enim decem tribus ab Assyriis deductæ fuerant in ca- ptivitatem sub Ezechia rege Iuda, sub quo etiam nunc in consolationem populi transmigrati, adversus Nini- vem visio cernitur; Nec erat parva consolatio, tam his, qui jam Assyriis serviebant, quam reliquis, qui sub Ezechia de tribu Iuda & Benjamin ab iisdem ho- stibus obsidebantur, ut audirent, Assyrios quoque à Chaldæis esse capiendos. Hæc ille. Ad tempo- ra Ezechiæ referunt etiam Theodoret. Theophylact. Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Ribera, Castrius, Cornd. à Lapid. & alii Interpp.

Complementi tempus Grotius redigit ad re- gnum Nabopallassaris: Sed non satis gravibus ar- gumentis. Alii non pauci potius ad filii Nebucad- nezeris regnum referunt. Neque contemnenda habent argumenta, è quibus unum solum adducemus: quod Nah. III. 7. 8. prædicatur: Ni- nivem evertendam esse post eversionem Alexandriæ, quæ in exemplum ejus proponitur. Nam hæc post Hie- rosolymam demum eversa dicitur. Josephus cer- te Nebucadnezarem anno quinto post vastatio- nem Jerusalem, Ægyptum, cujus metropolis A- lexandria est, invasisse, autor est. Et verisimile videtur, Nebucadnezarem excisa Hierosolyma, occupataque Ægypto arcem Monarchiæ Assyria- cæ Niniven invasisse, eaque capta Monarchiam ex Ninive Babylonem transtulisse, etsi etiam antea sub Asserbaddon filio Sennacheribi è Merodad Baladan Rege Babylonis capta fuerit: ex quo tem- pore non nominati sunt amplus Reges Assyrio- rum, sed solum Babyloniorum.

Novum & inauditum commentarium Coccejus in hoc Propheta ut in plerisque aliis commentus est: quod nempe agatur hic de Hierosolyma (1.) ut exscindenda tempore ultimo finaliter (2) ut libe- randa à jugo Sennacheribi. (3) ut destruenda per Nebucadnezarem. (4) ut restauranda ad restitutio- nem templi & cultus & celebrationem Festorum. Qui fingit etiam Habacuc agere plenius de Babyloniis &

Romanis & de Anti Christo, ita ut per duos hos Prophetas TOTUS ORDO temporum pertexatur, sed illæ privatæ mereque arbitrariæ ἐπιλύσεις non merentur recensionem, nedum confutatio- nem.

ELCESÆI] Elkesei esse Galilææ viculum tradit hîc Hieronymus. Chaldæus eum vocat Beth-Keffi? ita אל hîc sit articulus ut apud Arabas.

## 1:2
Ver. 2. GOD A JEALOUS GOD] Who can neither watch his own friends oppressed, nor his enemies flourishing for long.

AVENGING] This word placed three times affirms vehemently, as elsewhere the names of the holy, the temple, the land, and gestures repeated three times.

A threefold repetition is accustomed rather to imply the mystery of the Trinity. This is evident both from other passages and especially from the trisagion in Isaiah 6: holy, holy, holy is Jehovah of hosts, as we have said at that passage. Nor is there anything to prevent the wrath of all three persons of the Godhead from being designated here.

AND HAVING FURY] In the Hebrew: Lord of wrath. That is, he who, if he wishes, can most easily bring his wrath to effect.

AND HE HIMSELF BEING ANGRY WITH HIS ENEMIES] In the Hebrew: reserving, namely wrath for its own time, against his enemies.

Latin:

Vers. 2. DEUS ÆMVLATOR] Qui neque amicos suos oppressos, neque inimicos florentes diu conspicere possit.

VLCISCENS] Ter posita hæc vox vehementer af- firmat, ut alibi nomina sancti, templi, terræ, & gestus ter repetiti.

Trina repetitio solet potius mysterium Trini- tatis inferre. Quod cum ex aliis locis, tum in- primis è trisagio Es. VI. sanctus, sanctus sanctus Je- hovah exercituum, constat, uti ad illum locum dixi- mus. Nec quicquam obstat, quo minus omnium trium personarum Deitatis ira hîc designetur.

ET HABENS FVROREM] In Hebræo: Dominus iræ. Id est, qui facillime, si velit, possit iram suam effe- ctam dare.

ET IRASCENS IPSE INIMICIS SVIS] In He- bræo reservans, nempe iram in suum tempus, adversus i- nimicos suos.

## 1:3
Ver. 3.

THE LORD IS PATIENT] He long dissimulates wicked acts, watching to see how far men will go: then, (as Valerius Maximus wisely speaks) he compensates for the slowness of the punishment with its severity. See Plutarch, On the Delays of the Divine Vengeance.

AND GREAT IN STRENGTH] Who could avenge himself immediately, if he wished.

AND CLEARING HE WILL NOT CLEAR THE GUILTY] In the Hebrew: In clearing he does not clear: in the Greek ἀθωῶν οὐκ ἀθωώσει, as it appears from the Commentary that Jerome read. It is commonly edited very poorly: ἀθῶον οὐκ ἀθωώσει. The sense is: he will not always allow his enemies to carry off with impunity what they do.

THE LORD IN THE TEMPEST AND WHIRLWIND IS HIS WAY] A sufficiently frequent Hebraism. A simple expression would be: The ways of the Lord are with tempest and whirlwind: that is, he sends storms wherever he pleases.

AND THE CLOUDS ARE THE DUST OF HIS FEET] He stands upon the clouds just as men stand upon dust, that is, he is the lord of the clouds, and uses them as he wills.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

DOMINVS PATIENS] Diu dissimulat iniqua acta, speculans quousque homines sint evasuri: deinde, (ut Valerius Maximus sapienter loquitur) tarditatem supplicii gravitate compensat. Vide Plutarchum περὶ τῶν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θείου βραδέως τιμωρουμένων.

ET MAGNVS FORTITVDINE] Qui illico se ulci- sci possit, si velit.

ET MVNDANS NON FACIET INNOCEN- TEM] In Hebræo: In mundando non mundat: Græcis ἀ- θωῶν ἐκ ἀθωώσει quomodo legisse Hieronymum ex Com- mentario apparet. Vulgo pessime editur: ἀθῶον ἐκ ἀθωώσει. Sensus est: non semper sinet hostes suos impune ferre quæ faciunt.

DOMINVS IN TEMPESTATE ET TVRBINE VIÆ EJVS] Hebraismus satis frequens. Simplex locu- tio esset: Domini viæ cum tempestate & turbine: id est pro- cellas immittit quo ipsi libet.

ET NEBVLÆ PVLVIS PEDVM EJVS] Nubi insistit sicut homines pulveri, id est, dominus est nubium, & eis utitur ut vult.

## 1:4
Ver. 4.

REBUKING THE SEA AND DRYING IT UP] He who, as he rebuked the sea, immediately dries it up: as he did to the Red Sea.

AND ALL THE RIVERS TO THE DESERT [LEADING] He dries up all the rivers: namely, ἀπὸ κοινοῦ. Where he himself rebuked, that is, commanded.

BASAN IS WEAKENED] Basan becomes sterile: that is, places most suitable for grazing cattle: namely, where God rebuked as above. The Chaldeans call Basan מתנן by a double mutation of ב into מ, which is equally labial, and of ס into ת, which is very frequent among the Syrians and Chaldeans. Let an example of this saying be in the times of Elijah.

AND CARMEL] The fields of Judea or Syria.

AND THE FLOWER OF LEBANON LANGUISHED] Even the most flowery parts of Lebanon become sterile. Thus the Greeks. After pastures and fields, it even comes to trees, to indicate that there is nothing that can endure, if God is unwilling.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

INCREPANS MARE ET EXSICCANS ILLVD] Qui ut increpuit mare illico idipsum arefacit: ut fecit mari rubro.

ET OMNIA FLVMINA AD DESERTVM DE- VCENS] Omnia flumina exsiccat: nempe ἀπὸ κοινοῦ. ubi ipse increpuit, id est, imperavit.

INFIRMATVS EST BASAN] sterilefときt Basan: id est, loca maxime apta pascendo pecori: nempe ubi Deus increpuit ut supra. Chaldæi Basan vocant מתנן gemina mutatione ב in מ æque labialem, & ס in ת, quod valde frequens Syris & Chaldæis. Exemplum hujus dicti sit in temporibus Eliæ.

ET CARMELVS] Arva Judææ aut Syriæ.

ET FLOS LIBANI ELANGVIT] Etiam floridissi- ma Libani sterilefcunt. Sic Græci. Post pascua & arva et- iam ad arbores venit, ut indicet nihil esse quod durare pos- sit, Deo nolente.

## 1:5
Verse 5.

THE MOUNTAINS WERE MOVED BY HIM AND THE HILLS WERE DESOLATED] His mountains are moved by force and the hills melt: that is, they give forth water. Ps. 114:4, 6, 8. Exod. 17:6. Num. 22.

AND THE EARTH TREMBLED FROM HIS FACE] In the Hebrew: The earth burns from his sight: like the land of Sodom and the neighboring cities.

AND THE WORLD] תבל is accustomed to be called κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν, the Israelite land, which itself also smoked with fires through Shalmaneser and Sennacherib.

This prophecy preceded the fires of Sennacherib; as we have said. Nor is the Israelite land precisely signified here. But it is said in general that the world trembles at the face of God, when his anger is kindled, nay, the whole habitable world, with all the inhabitants in it. There is no reason, therefore, why that word of most ample signification should be restricted here, since the Prophet is occupied in exaggerating the magnitude of divine power and wrath, and its supreme energy. And the rest are general, concerning mountains, hills, rivers, the sea, and the earth. Why therefore is the word ORBIS to be restricted? Whence B. Luther rightly renders: The circle of the world, and all who dwell therein.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

MONTES COMMOTI SVNT AB EO ET COL- LES DESOLATI SVNT] Montes ejus vi commoventur & colles liquefcunt: id est, aquam edunt. Ps. CXIV. 4.6.8. Exod. XVII. 6. Num. XXII.

ET CONTREMVIT TERRA A FACIE EJVS] In Hebræo: Conflagrat terra ab ejus adspectu: ut terra So- domorum, & vicinarum urbium.

ET ORBIS] תבל solet dici κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν, terra Israe- litica, quæ & ipsa fumavit incendiis per Salmanasarem & Sennacheribum.

Hæc Prophetia antegressa est incendia Sen- nacheribi; uti diximus. Neque præcise terra Is- raelitica hic significatur. Sed in genere dicitur orbis tremere à facie Dei, cum ira ejus accensa est, imo omnis orbis habitabilis, cum omnibus habitanti- bus in eo. Non est ergo, quod vox illa amplissi- mæ significationis hic infringatur, cum Prophe- ta ta occupetur in exaggeranda divinæ potentiæ & iræ magnitudine, summaque ἐνεργείᾳ. Et ge- neralia sunt cætera, de montibus, collibus, flumi- nibus, mari, ac terra. Qui ergo restringenda vox ORBIS? Unde merito reddit B. Lutherus: Der Welt Kreyß, und alle die drinnen wohnen.

## 1:6
Ver. 6. BEFORE THE FACE OF HIS INDIGNATION WHO SHALL STAND?] What people could be safe when He himself is angry, who shows himself so powerful by so many proofs?

HIS INDIGNATION IS POURED OUT LIKE FIRE, AND THE ROCKS ARE DISSOLVED BY HIM] If his indignation pours itself out like fire, the very crags will be broken by it. Hannibal made the Alps passable for himself by burning a pile of wood.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ANTE FACIEM INDIGNATIONIS EJUS QUIS STABIT?] Quis populus salvus esse posset ipso i- rascente, qui tam potentem se tot ostendit documentis?

INDIGNATIO EJUS EFFUSA EST UT IGNIS, ET PETRÆ DISSOLUTÆ SUNT AB EO] Si indigna- tio ejus ut ignis se effundat, ipsæ rupes inde frangentur. Strue lignorum incensa pervias sibi Alpes fecit Annibal.

## 1:7
Ver. 7. THE LORD IS GOOD AND A STRENGTHENER IN THE DAY OF TRIBULATION] And a protection (to his own, of course, as the following shows) in a time of distress.

AND KNOWING THOSE WHO HOPE IN HIM] He knows who they are who trust in him: That is, who worship God from the heart 2 Tim. II, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 7. BONUS DOMINUS ET CONFORTANS IN DIE TRIBULATIONIS] Et præsidium (suis scilicet, ut sequentia ostendunt) tempore ærumnoso.

ET SCIENS SPERANTES IN SE] Novit qui sint qui ipsi confidant: Id est, qui Deum ex animo colant 2. Tim. II, 9.

## 1:8
Ver. 8. AND WITH AN OVERFLOWING FLOOD HE WILL MAKE A CONSUMMATION OF ITS PLACE] מְקוֹמָהּ which is here translated 'its place', the Greeks translate 'those rising up', for which 'those rising up' is wrongly in some Codices. He takes it thus like the Chaldean, so that it is a feminine participle and one must understand עַם, or עֵדָה a multitude. As if by an overflowing flood of destruction he will give the one rising up against him, namely the multitude.

That the word מְקוֹמָהּ is not a feminine participle but the noun מָקוֹם 'place' with a feminine suffix, the mappiq in H sufficiently teaches. Therefore there is no place for the Grotius version. All translate it 'its place', and refer the pronoun to Nineveh. Pagninus: And with an overflowing flood he will make a consummation of its place. The Tigurines: With an overflowing flood he will utterly destroy its place. Junius: Therefore with an overflowing flood he is about to effect a consummation of its place. Vatablus: And with an overflowing flood he is about to make a consummation in its place. Ludov. de Dieu prefers it thus: And with an overflowing flood he will make its place a consummation, that is, he will cause the place of Nineveh to be the very consumption: or in this way, And with an overflowing flood (GOD) passes by and will make its place a consumption: so that a reason is given why Nineveh cannot but be consumed by the wrath of God, because, namely, he passes by with an overflowing flood. So also Tarnovius: With an overflowing flood finally passing through, after Nineveh has often been infested by the waves of wars, God is about to effect a consummation, and will utterly destroy with slaughter, Jerem. 4, 27. & 5, 10. & 30, 11. & 46, 28. Ezech. 11, 13. & 20, 17. its place, I say, of Nineveh, that greatest city Jon. I. 2. & 3, 2. 3. which the suffix of the feminine gender in the Hebrew text sufficiently indicates, which cannot be referred to the preceding masculine; where note, that in Scripture the place of some thing is often said to perish, when the thing itself perishes Psal. 37, 35. 36. Dan. 2, 35. Apoc. 12, 8. & 20, 11. Mr. D. Himmelins says the destruction of Nineveh is illustrated by the comparison of the flood of the first world, and the Red Sea, by whose waters the world and Pharaoh were suffocated, and to point the finger at the manner of the Ninevite overthrow about which Diod. Sicul. l. III. They had a very old oracle that the city would be overthrown if it were to have the river Euphrates as an enemy, and that this happened at the time of the siege, and the river had broken all the embankments and demolished a great part of the fortifications. Grotius sought another metaphrase as it appears, which would sail for his own opinion, that not the destruction of the city, but only its surrender was predicted here.

Coccejus translates it thus: And with an overflowing flood he will make a consummation of its place. He says it signifies that the wrath of God will be poured out into the place of perfection, and with that place he will make a consummation συντέλειαν. For the suffix in the word מְקוֹמָהּ 'its place' cannot be conveniently referred to anything else, and most conveniently is referred to the 'tribulation' of which he speaks in v. 7. and 9. That place of pressure is the temple, the Synagogue, the city, the Republic, the land. But Coccejus is mistaken in his hypothesis, thinking these are directed against the Jews, since the title of the Prophecy and the treatment itself teaches that the punishment of Nineveh is being denounced, not that of Jerusalem.

Ver. same. AND DARKNESS SHALL PURSUE HIS ENEMIES] All evils will follow them. The Chaldean refers it to Gehenna: not badly, if you look not at the primary sense, but at the more abstruse one.

There is no need for a double sense, primary and abstruse, if darkness is taken generally: for thus they can encompass not only the darkness of this life, but also of the future, the outer darkness, which Scripture calls, namely all the punishments which pursue and await the enemies of God.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET IN DILUVIO PRÆTEREUNTE CON- SUMMATIONEM FACIET LOCI EJUS] מְקוֹמָהּ quod hic vertitur loci ejus, Græci vertunt ἐπεγειρομένους, pro quo male est in nonnullis Codicibus ἐξεγειρομένους. Sic su- mit ut Chaldæus, ut sit participium fœmininum & subin- telligatur עַם, vel עֵדָה multitudo. Velut diluvio super- sadente exitio dabit insurgentem contra se, nempe multitudi- nem.

Vocem מְקוֹמָהּ non esse participium fœmini- num sed nomen מָקוֹם locus cum affixo fœminino, H mappikatum satis docet. Non ergo locus est versioni Grotianæ. Omnes locum ejus vertunt, & pronomen ad Niniven referunt. Pagninus: Ve- rum & inundatione transeunte consummationem fa- ciet loci ejus. Tigurini diluvio superante prorsus de- lebit locum ipsius. Junius: Itaque inundatione per- vadente affecturus est consummatione locum ipsius. Vatablus: Et cum inundatione transeunte consum- mationem facturus est in loco ejus. Ludov. de Dieu mavult ita: Et cum inundatione transeunte consummationem faciet locum ejus, id est, faciet, ut locus Ninives sit ipsa consumtio: vel hoc mo- do, Et cum inundatione transit (DEUS) consum- ptionem faciet locum ejus: ut causa reddatur, cur non possit non consumi Ninive ab ira Dei, quia sc. cum inundatione transit. Sic etiam Tarno- vius: Inundatione tandem prorsus pervadente, post- quam sæpe bellorum fluctibus infestata est Ninive, affe- cturus est Deus consummatione, & omnino interne- cione delebit, Jerem. 4, 27. & 5, 10. & 30, 11. & 46, 28. Ezech. 11, 13. & 20, 17. locum illius, Ninives, in- quam, urbis illius maximæ Jon. I. 2. & 3, 2. 3. quod in textu Hebræo affixum fœminini generis satis in- nuit, quod ad præcedens masculinum referri haud potest; ubi nota, quod in Scriptura sæpe rei alicujus locus perire dicatur, cum perit ipsa Psal. 37, 35. 36. Dan. 2, 35. Apoc. 12, 8. & 20, 11. Dn. D. Himmelins ait interitum Ninives illustrari comparatione di- luvii mundi primi, & maris rubri, cujus aquis suffocabatur mundus & Pharao, digitumque inten- dere ad modum eversionis Niniviticæ de quo Diod. Sicul. l. III. Habuerunt pervetus oraculum urbem eversum iri si fluvium Euphratem habitura esset hostem, & tempore obsidionis id evenisse, fluviumq́; omnes aggeres rupisse & magnam partem munitio- num diruisse. Aliam metaphrasin quæsivit Gro- tius ut apparet, quæ suæ velificaretur sententiæ, non excidium urbis, sed deditionem solum hic prædictam esse.

Coccejus ita vertit: Et per inundationem perva- dentem consummationem faciet locum ejus. Significat inquit iram Dei effusum iri in locum perfectionis, & cum eo loco se facturum consummationem συντέλειαν. Nam affixum in voce מְקוֹמָהּ locum ejus non potest alio commode referi, & commo- dissime ad θλίψιν de qua loquitur v. 7. & 9. refer- Is locus pressuræ est templum, Synagoga, urbs, Resp. terra. Sed fallitur in hypothesi Coccejus existi- mans hæc directa esse contra Judæos, cum titulus Prophetiæ & tractatio ipsa doceat, Ninivæ pœ- nam denunciari, non Hierosolymæ.

Vers. eod. ET INIMICOS EJUS PERSEQUENTUR TENEBRÆ] Omnia mala ipsus sequentur. Chaldæus ad gehennam id refert: non male, si sensum non primum, sed abstrusiorem spectes.

Non opus est gemino sensu primo, & abstrusio- re, si tenebræ generaliter accipiantur: ita enim non tantum tenebras hujus vitæ, sed etiam futuræ com- plecti possunt, exteriores, quas Scriptura vocat, tenebras, pœnas nempe universas, quæ Dei inimi- cos persequuntur, & manent.

## 1:9
Vers. 9. WHAT DO YOU THINK AGAINST THE LORD] What are you thinking against the Lord? To escape his wrath, that is.

HE WILL MAKE A CONSUMMATION] He will bring about destruction.

DOUBLE TRIBULATION SHALL NOT ARISE] Calamity. He will not strike you down with repeated blows, but with one.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QUID COGITATIS CONTRA DOMI- NUM] Quid cogitareti scontra Dominum? ad effugiendam scilicet iram ejus.

CONSUMMATIONEM IPSE FACIET] Exitium immitter.

NON CONSURGET DUPLEX TRIBULATIO] Calamitas. Non iteratis ictibus, sed uno vos prosternet.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. AS LIKE THORNS THEY EMBRACE ONE ANOTHER] Like thorns tangled together: which, namely, are cast into the fire together.

SO THE BANQUET OF THEM DRINKING TOGETHER] Or like the banquet of those who are drinking together, that is, who perish together when the house is suddenly set on fire.

THEY SHALL BE CONSUMED LIKE STUBBLE FULL OF DRYNESS] Which suddenly catches flame.

Do not these verses 9 and 10, thus explained, bring about total destruction? Why does Grotius assert that only the surrender of the city was predicted? Furthermore, Dievius rendered them differently: For they are entangled even to the thorns, and they are as if drunk with their own wine, they are consumed (or shall be consumed) as fully dry stubble. He provides the reason why he said in the preceding verse that they were to be consumed, and that the distress would not arise twice: because their perplexity is so great, the vertigo of their drunken mind is so great, that it is easy to consume them utterly, and there will be no need to repeat the war. So he. But it can be admitted that a triple simile occurs here, as Tarnovius explains: The first is taken from thorns, which, tied into a bundle, are burned together, so that nothing of them remains: The second from drunkards who are most easily overcome and slaughtered: The third from stubble, which is ignited without any effort, and is most easily consumed entirely by the flame. For there still remains little time (inasmuch as the particle עד in this place is put for עוד: as Job 1:16, Psalm 58:9) the Assyrians will be perplexed and hindered, surrounded from without by the enemy, and within entangled with their own inextricable difficulties, so stupefied that they do not know at all what counsel to take. Compare Zephaniah 2:13, Isaiah 33:12, Micah 7:4. For just as thorns, when they are so entangled that they cannot easily be loosened, are cast by the farmer into the fire together: so God will cast these, who have entangled themselves in intricate matters, into the flame of war together, so that they may be captured as easily as if they were overcome by wine and plainly drunk, buried in sleep and wine, but truly in the wine of divine wrath. See Obadiah v. 16 and compare the example of Daniel 5. Thus they shall be consumed like dry stubble plainly and fully, concerning which simile, often occurring in scripture, see above Joel 2:5, Obadiah v. 18. Compare Job 41:21. Ps. 83:14. Is. 40:24, and 47:14. Jer. 13:24.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUASI SICUT SPINÆ SE INVICEM COMPLECTUNTUR] Sicut spinæ inter se confertæ: quæ scil. pariter in ignem conjiciuntur.

SIC CONVIVIUM EORUM PARITER PO- TANTIUM] Aut ut convivium eorum qui compotant, nem- pe qui subito incensa domo pariter pereunt.

CONSUMENTUR QUASI STIPULA ARIDI- TATE PLENA] Quæ subito flammam concepit.

Nonne hæc v. 9. & 10. ita explicata totale ex- cidium inferunt? Cur ego solum deditionem urbis prædictam asserit Grotius? Cæterum aliter illa reddidit Dievius: Nam usq; ad spinas perplexi sunt, & tanquam vino suo inebriati sunt, consumpti sunt (vel consumentur) tanquam stipula arida plenè. Causam tradit, cur versu præcedente dixerit, eos consumendos esse, nec angustiam bis surrectu- ram: quia tanta est ipsorum perplexitas, tanta ebriæ mentis vertigo, ut facile sit eos penitus consumere, nec opus futurum sit bellum iterare. Hæc ille. Sed admitti potest, triplicem similitudi- nem hic occurrere, uti explicat Tarnovius: Pri- ma desumpta est à spinis, quæ colligatæ in fascicu- lum, simul comburuntur, ita ut nihil ex illis super- sit: Secunda ab ebriis qui facillime superantur & trucidantur: Tertia à stipula, quæ nullo negotio incenditur, & facillime à flamma prorsus absumi- tur. Nam adhuc parum restat temporis (siquidem particula עד hoc loco pro עוד ponitur: ut Job. I. 16. Psalm. LIIX. 9.) perplexi & impediti erunt As- syrii, foris ab hoste circumclusi, & intus cum ani- mis suis inextricabilibus implexi difficultatibus, ita obstupefacti, ut nesciant omnino quid consilii ca- piant. Confer. Zephan. II. 13. Esa. XXXIII. 12. Mich. VII. 4. Nam velut spinæ, cum sunt ita im- plicatæ, ut dissolvi facile non queant, simul à rusti- co conjiciuntur in ignem: sic Deus hos, qui se- ipsos rebus intricatis implicuerunt, simul in belli flammam projiciet, ut tam facile capiantur, tan- quam si mero obruti essent, & plane inebriati, so- mno vinoque sepulti, mero vero iræ divinæ. vide Obad. v. 16. & confer exemplum Dan. V. sic con- sumentur velut stipula arida plane, & plene, de qua similitudine in scriptura sæpe occurrente vide supra Joel. II. 5. Obad. v. 18. Conf. Job. XLI. 21. Ps. XXCIII. 14. Es. XL. 24. & XLVII. 14. Jer. XIII. 24.

## 1:11
Vers. 11. OUT OF THEE SHALL GO FORTH] In the Hebrew: shall go forth.

THINKING AGAINST THE LORD MALICE MENTALLY REVOLVING PREVARICATION] A wicked counselor: That is, Rabshakeh, of whom 2 Kings 18:19 and following. Isaiah 36:2 and following.

Not only of Rabshakeh, but in general of any wicked counselors, who have thought, given, and taken counsel against the Lord and the people of the Lord. Others understand it of the Assyrian Kings, and of their counselors. If this is to be understood specifically of Sennacherib or Rabshakeh, it will have to be taken not historically and in the past, but prophetically and in the future, as Prophets are accustomed to use past tenses for future ones, for the sake of the certainty of the prophecies. Cocceius is here again singular according to his custom: judging that Jerusalem is indicated, because every machination against the kingdom of Christ and especially the impulse of the Gentiles to persecute Christians proceeded from Jerusalem and the Senate of the Jews, as is the example in Paul after he was converted. But these things are clearly foreign and are forced into the text, not drawn out of the text. It is false that the Lord was not invoked. For he was indeed invoked through the preaching of Jonah, to which they themselves did penance. Nor does it help Cocceius that v. 12, 13. Jerusalem is addressed: because apostrophe to other persons is not infrequent among the Prophets; therefore, even though in v. 11 he addressed Nineveh, the Prophet could nevertheless then turn his speech to Jerusalem or Judea, to whom these things about Nineveh were being preached, in v. 12, 13, just as afterwards in v. 14 he addresses the King of Assyria himself through an apostrophe directed elsewhere again, where Cocceius also acknowledges that Sennacherib is addressed: who besides, in v. 15, immediately invented that the speech is made with the words: he is entirely cut off, about a completely different person, namely Nebuchadnezzar. It is not new, says Cocceius on Nahum 3:14, for a city or some person to be pointed out by a mere demonstrative.

Latin:

Vers. 11. EX TE EXHIBIT] In Hebræo: exibit.

COGITANS CONTRA DOMINUM MALI- TIAM MENTE PERTRACTANS PRÆVARICATIO- NEM] Consiliarius nequam: Id est, Rabsaces, de quo 2. Regum XVIII, 19. & sequentibus. Esa. XXXVI. 2. & se- quentibus.

Non de Rabsace tantum, sed in genere de quibusvis consultoribus nequam, qui contra Do- minum & populum Domini mala cogitârunt, de- derunt & ceperunt consilia. De Regibus Assyriis, eo- rumque consiliariis intelligunt alii. Si de Sennache- ribo, vel Rabsace speciatim id intelligendum, non ἱστορικῶς, & in præterito id accipiendum erit, sed προφητικῶς, & in futuro, uti solent Prophetæ uti præteritis pro futuris, certitudinis vaticiniorum gratia. Singularis hic iterum pro more suo est Coc- cejus: Hierosolymam indigitari censens, quod omnis machinatio contra regnum Christi & imprimis impulsio gentilium ad persequendos Christianos egres- sa sit ex Hierosolyma & Senatu Judæorum, ut exem- plum est in Paulo post converso. Sed hæc plane ἀλ- λότρια sunt ac textu ingeruntur non efferuntur è textu. Falsum est, quod Dominus invocatus non sit. Erat enim utique invocatus per prædicationem Io- næ, ad quam pœnitentiam ipsi egerunt. Nec juvat Coccejum, quod v. 12. 13. Hierosolyma compelletur: quia non infrequens est apostrophe ad alias perso- nas penes Prophetas, utut ergo v. 11. compellarit Niniven, orationem tamen deinde ad Hierosoly- mam, vel Judæam, cui hæc de Ninive prædicaban- tur, convertere poterat Propheta v. 12. 13. quemad- modum postea v. 14. compellat ipsum Regem Assy- rium per apostrophen aliorsum iterum directam, ubi Sennacheribum compellari etiam Coccejus a- gnoscit: qui præterea v. 15. sermonem statim fieri verbis: totus excisus est de longe alia persona nimi- rum de Nebucadnezare commentus est. Non no- vum est, inquit Coccejus ad Nah. III. 14. civitatem vel personam aliquam solo δεικτικῶ demonstrari.

## 1:12
Verse 12. IF THEY SHALL BE PERFECT] Even if they are perfect: namely in wisdom. Thus the Chaldean here. They are praised in a certain oracle by this name: Lydians and the race of Assyrian men.

AND SO MANY] In the Hebrew: And clearly many. SO ALSO THEY SHALL BE SHORN] Nevertheless they shall be shorn. Their glory shall perish. Such is that: By our counsels the praise of the Laconians is shorn.

AND HE SHALL PASS THROUGH] The Chaldean makes a way for himself. Junius explains it thus: If the Assyrians had cultivated peace (and had not treated my people so cruelly) they would have been more ample, not so clearly worn away, or at least lightly affected by disaster, and as if they had been shorn like grass, fleece, or the hairs of the head, so that they might be able to grow again, or as if the evil had passed through. But we easily agree that a more serious shearing and passing through is noted: for the words of shearing and shaving are accustomed to be taken in that way in Isaiah 7:20, as well as passing through in Isaiah 37:86, Psalm 141:10, and the underlying subject matter demands such a sense: whence Jerome also walked on foot into that opinion: As the number of hairs does not resist a sharp pair of shears: so the number of the adversaries of God will be easily taken away by succession. And Blessed Luther: They come as equipped and mighty as they wish, yet they shall be cut down and pass away. The shearing of the Assyrians, however, is understood by most interpreters not as that which the Chaldeans [did], but that which was done by the Angel cutting down the army of Sennacherib in one night. Thus Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Clarius, and others. Therefore, that AND HE SHALL PASS THROUGH, they refer not to the Chaldean, but to the army of the Assyrians that was about to pass through and perish, or even to the Assyrian King, who passed through killed by his sons. Theodoret, Vatablus, and Montanus understand it of the city of Nineveh that was about to pass away. But in that case, a verb of the feminine gender should have been used.

Verse same. I HAVE AFFLICTED THEE, AND I WILL NOT AFFLICT THEE ANY MORE] When I have afflicted thee, I will not afflict thee any more, O Nineveh: that is, I will strike thee down with one blow, as above in v. 9.

This sense could be admitted. But thus the destruction of the Ninevites, and not merely the transfer of the empire, would be predicted here. Which is against the Grotian interpretation: most, however, wish these things to be said to Jerusalem, with Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Albert, Rupert, Hugo, Vatablus. He comforts, says Castrius, Judea and Jerusalem, because it is not to be oppressed further by the Assyrians, since he threatens here that they are to be utterly devastated. Which sense is simpler and more convenient. Whence he adds, and now I will break his rod from off thy back. Namely the power which he exercised through his army, as Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Albert, Hugo, and Dionysius wish, or the yoke of servitude by which the Assyrian held the Jews subject to himself, as if bound, as the Chaldean, Vatablus, and Robert explain. But because he began to treat of Nineveh, and no mention was made of Jerusalem in v. 9, it seems rather that destruction is still being predicted for it; especially by force of the comparison of v. 9, which Blessed Tarnovius himself explained thus: distress shall not rise up twice, because you will be clearly destroyed by the first disaster, comparing 1 Samuel 26:8, so that the total deletion of the Assyrians is adumbrated.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SI PERFECTI FUERINT] Etiamsi perfecti sint: nempe sapientia. Ita hic Chaldæus. Laudantur in oraculo quodam hoc nomine: Λυδοί τε καὶ Ἀσσυρίων γένος ἀνδρῶν.

ET ITA PLURES] In Hebræo: Et plane multi. SIC QUOQUE ATTONDENTUR] Attamen at- tondebuntur. Peribit eorum gloria. Tale illud: Consiliis nostris laus est attonsa Laconum.

ET PERTRANSIBIT] Viam sibi facit Chaldæus. Junius ita explicat: Si pacem coluissent Assyrii (nec populum meum tam crudeliter tractassent) ampli etiam fuissent, non sic plane attriti, aut certe leviter saltem clade affecti, ac si fuissent ita tonsi, ut gramen, vellus, vel pili capitis, ut possint denuo suc- crescere, seu quasi transivisset malum. Sed facile annuimus, tonsionem & transitum graviorem notari: nam ita accipi solent voces tondendi & abradendi Es. VII. 20. nec non transeundi Esa. XXXVII. 86. Ps. CXLI. 10. ac sensum ejusmodi postulat mate- ria substrata: unde in eam sententiam pedibus quoque ivit Hieronymus: Quomodo numerus ca- pillorum acuta forcipi non repugnat: ita numerus adversariorum Dei succesione facile tolletur. Et B. Lutherus: Sie kommen so gerüst und mächtig als sie wollen, sollen sie doch umbgehauen wer- den, und dahin fahren. Detonsio autem Assyrio- rum à plerisque Interpp. ea intelligitur, non quæ à Chaldæis, sed quæ per Angelum Sennacheribi ex- ercitum una nocte excindente, facta. Ita Hie- ronymus, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Clarius, & alii. Illud ergo ET PERTRANSIBIT, non ad Chaldæum, sed ad exercitum Assyriorum transitu- rum & periturum, vel etiam ad Assyrium Regem referunt, qui pertransiit interfectus à filiis suis. De civitate Ninive transitura Theodoretes, Va- tablus & Montanus intelligunt. Sed ita verbum fœminini generis adhibendum fuisset.

Vers. eod. AFFLIXI TE, ET NON AFFLIGAM TE ULTRA] Ubi afflixero te non ultra te affligam ô Nini- ve: id est, uno ictu te prosternam, ut supra v. 9.

Admitti posset hic sensus. Sed ita excidium Ni- nivitarum, non vero translatio solum imperii hic prædiceretur. Quod est contra interpretatio- nem Grotianam: plerique tamen hæc Hierosolymæ dicta volunt, cum Hieronymo, Remigio, Haymone, Alberto, Ruperto, Hugone, Vatablo. Consolatur, inquit Castrius, Iudæam, & Ierusalem, quod non sit ulterius ab Assyriis opprimenda, cum eos hic va- standos omnino comminetur. Qui sensus simplicior & convenientior. Unde subjicit, & nunc conteram virgam ejus de dorso tuo. Nempe potentiam, quam per exercitum suum exercebat, ut volunt Hieron. Theodoret. Remigius, Albertus, Hugo, & Di- on. vel jugum servitutis, quo sibi subditos habebat Assyrius Judæos, quasi vinctos, ut explicant Chal- dæus, Vatabl. & Robertus. Quia vero cœpit de Ni- nive agere, ac Hierosolymæ nulla facta est mentio videtur potius illi excidium adhuc prædici; im- primis vi collationis v. 9. quam B. Tarnovius ipse ita exposuit: non surget bis angustia, quia prima clade plane perdemini, conferens 1. Sam. XXVI. 8. ut omnimoda Assyriorum adumbretur deletio.

## 1:13
V. 13. AND NOW I WILL BREAK HIS ROD FROM OFF THY BACK] In the Hebrew: I will break the yoke of that one (Esarhaddon) from upon thee, so that that hard king may not lie upon thee.

AND I WILL BURST THY BONDS] With which he holds thee bound,

Latin:

V. 13. ET NUNC CONTERAM VIRGAM EJUS DE DORSO TUO] In Hebræo: Confringam jugum istius (A- sarchadonis) à super te, ne tibi incumbat rex ille durus.

ET VINCULA TUA DISRUMPAM] Quibus il- le te adstrictam tenet,

## 1:14
Verse 14. AND THE LORD SHALL GIVE COMMAND CONCERNING THEE] He shall appoint concerning thee that which follows.

THERE SHALL NO MORE BE SOWN OF THY NAME] That seed (namely royal) may no longer exist from thy name. That is, that henceforth those who rule over thee may not be called kings of Nineveh, as in Jonah 2:6, for from that time those who ruled there were called kings of Babylon.

This interpretation is akin to Theodoret's explanation, that no subject was henceforth to be called an Assyrian, since those who were subsequently subject to the Babylonians were to be called Chaldeans or Babylonians. But the Prophet is no longer addressing the city here, nor does he use the feminine gender, as in the preceding verses, but the masculine, and therefore these things cannot be referred to Nineveh. Wherefore most interpreters more correctly say that the speech is now directed to Sennacherib, and that it is predicted that his name will cease. For his elder sons, by whom he was killed, fled, and Esarhaddon died without posterity. Thus Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, [Rupertus], Hugo, Vatablus, and others, also Cocceius in this place.

Verse of the same. AND OUT OF THE HOUSE OF THY GOD] Adad.

I WILL CUT OFF THE GRAVEN IMAGE] I will cut off.

AND I WILL MAKE THY GRAVE A MOLTEN IMAGE] That is, as it were thy grave: that it may be held unclean, as a grave; for victors are accustomed to substitute their own gods in the place of those who were previously worshipped, Euripides in the Troades: For when a city is taken by evil, the things of the gods are sick, and wish not to be honoured.

Most observe that the excision not only of the idols but also of the King himself among the idols is designated, so that this is the sense: I will cut off every graven and molten idol, and in the same place I will arrange thy grave, so that the killing of Sennacherib in the temple is implied. Jerome, and with him Remigius, Haymo, Lyra, and others, as noted by Christoph. à Castro, distinguish these words thus: out of the house of thy God I will cut off, the graven image, and the molten image I will make thy grave, that is, out of the house of thy God, whence thou didst hope for help, death shall come to thee, for thus thou shalt be killed between the altars of the idols, among the graven and molten images, while thou art worshipping them, thou shalt be killed, and thy corpse shall be committed to burial from there. Thus the Hebrew will flow in this way: Out of the house of thy God I will kill thee, O Sennacherib, I will make the graven and molten image thy grave. The discourse is not about a grave simply, but about the GRAVE OF THE KING, whom the Prophet is addressing: it is not said it shall be unclean as a grave, but I will make thy grave.

Verse of the same. BECAUSE THOU HAST BEEN DISHONOURED] The Chaldean reads without a Cametz at the end, and translates: for this is easy for me: word for word: for easy, namely these things are.

The Chaldean text is wrongly preferred to the sources; the sense in the Hebrew is excellent, and is rightly rendered by the Vulgate, because thou hast been honoured, namely in my eyes: others, after thou hast become vile, having received that great slaughter and the destruction of thy soldiers, thou who wast so celebrated throughout the world, Isaiah 10:12.

13. chap. XIV. 25. c. XXXVII. 13. Jer. XLIX. 31. Ludov. de Dieu wishes it to be indicated that his burial is despised: that he himself is to be buried so vilely, that they are not only not going to adorn him with a royal monument, but are going to seize some futile idol, already held as a profane thing, in which to bury him.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET PRÆCIPIET SUPER TE DOMINUS] Constituet de te id quod sequitur.

NON SEMINABITUR EX NOMINE TUO AMPLIUS] Ne semen (nempe regium) exsistat ultra de tuo nomine. Id est, ne posthac qui tibi imperabunt appellen- tur reges Ninives, ut Jon. II. 6. nam ex eo tempore dicti sunt, qui ibi imperabant reges Babylonis.

Affinis hæc interpretatio est Theodoreti ex- plicationi, neminem subditum deinde vocandum esse Assyrium, qui deinceps subjecti Babyloniis Chaldæi, seu Babylonii vocandi erant. Sed non alloquitur hic Propheta amplius civitatem, neque utitur genere fœminino, uti in præcedentibus, sed masculino, ideoque hæc ad Niniven referri nequeunt. Qua- propter rectius pleriq; Interpp. ad Sennacheribum jam orationem dirigi ajunt, ac desiturum nomen ejus prædici. Filii enim natu majores, à quibus in- terfectus est, aufugiunt, & Asarhaddon sine poste- ritate decessit. Ita Hieronymus, Remigius, Haymo, pertus, Hugo, Vatablus, & alii, etiam Coccejus in h. l.

Vers eod. ET DE DOMO DEI TUI] Adad.

INTERFICIAM SCULPTILE] Exscindam.

ET CONFLATILE PONAM SEPULCHRUM TUUM] Id est, quasi sepulchrum tuum: ut immundum ha- beatur, quasi sepulchrum nam victores solent deos suos in locum eorum, qui ante colebantur, substituere, Euripides Troaslibus: Ἐρημία γὰρ πόλιν ὅταν λάβῃ κακὴ Νοσεῖ τὰ τῶν θεῶν, ὐδὲ τιμᾶσθαι θέλει.

Non tantum idolorum, sed etiam ipsius Regis inter idola excisionem designari plerique obser- vant, ut sit hic sensus: Excindam idolum omne scul- ptile & fusile, ibidemque disponam sepulchrum tuum, ut innuatur interfectio Sennacheribi in templo. Hieronymus, & cum eo Remigius, Haymo, Lyra alii que notante Christoph. à Castro ita distinguunt hæc verba: de domo Dei tui interficiam, sculptile, & conflatile ponam sepulcrum tuum, h. e. de domo Dei tui, unde sperabas auxilium, adveniet tibi mors, nam ita interficieris inter aras idolorum, inter scul- ptilia & conflatilia, dum ea adoraveris, occideris, & cadaver tuum inde sepulturæ mandabitur. Ita Ebræa fluent hoc modo: De domo Dei tui inter- ficiam te ô Sennacheribe, sculptile & conflatile po- nam sepulcrum tuum. Non de sepulcro simplici- ter, sed de SEPULCRO REGIS, quem alloquitur Propheta sermo est: non dicitur immundum erit quasi sepulcrum, sed ponam sepulcrum tuum.

Vers. eod. QUIA INHONORATUS ES] Chaldæus legit sine Cametz in fine, & vertit: facile enim id mihi: ad verbum: nam facilia, nempe hæc sunt.

Perperam præfertur Chaldæus textus fontibus, sensus in Ebræo est optimus, & recte à vulgato red- ditur, quia honoratus es, sc. in oculis meis: alii, postquam vilueris, accepta illa magna clade, ac mi- litum strage, adeo celebris eras per orbem Esa. X. 12.

13. cap. XIV. 25. c. XXXVII. 13. Jer. XLIX. 31. Lu- dov. de Dieu indicari vult comtemtam ejus sepultu- ram: ipsum tam viliter inhumandum, ut non modo non regio sint ornaturi monumento, sed fu- tile aliquod, & jam pro re prophana habitum ido- lum sint arrepturi, in quod eum condant.

## 1:15
Ver. 15. BEHOLD UPON THE MOUNTAINS THE FEET OF HIM THAT BRINGETH GOOD TIDINGS] To the mountains, that is, to Judea, runners will suddenly go, bringing joyful news. (To the Jews.

AND THAT PUBLISHETH PEACE] That is, prosperous things. CELEBRATE O JUDA THY FEASTS] Keep your feast days securely.

AND PERFORM THY VOWS]. Which you have made, if you shall be delivered from the fear of the Assyrians.

Although some interpreters refer these specifically to the security to be rendered to Judea from the Assyrian enemy: not a few, however, acknowledge at the same time that they are to be taken generally concerning the peace or prosperity of Judah, and that under it is also comprehended that happiness which was reserved primarily for the New Testament, and for which reason the spiritual happiness and blessedness was to be announced by the Evangelists of peace. We consider this sense most convenient, that it be taken as an Evangelical prophecy (1) Because all the Prophets, as Peter testifies, Acts X. 43, prophesied and testified concerning the free remission of sins through Christ. Therefore our Prophet is not to be excepted from this universality. But unless you explain this passage concerning the Gospel of grace, nothing of the Gospel will be held in it. (2) Because he uses the same words which Isaiah uses in ch. LII. 7. And we have demonstrated at that place that those words treat of the Evangelical message under the New Testament. (3) Because we have an undoubted and authentic interpreter, the holy Apostle, Rom. X. 15, who teaches that these things are to be taken concerning the messengers of Evangelical grace. (4) The context does not contradict, but favors this sense, as if the prophet were saying: That will be the exit of the enemies of Judah. Therefore, it is so far from the case that Judea is to be utterly subverted before the scepter is taken away from Judah and Shiloh comes, whom all the Prophets had in their mouths, that the feet of those bringing good tidings and announcing peace are one day to appear on its mountains, and Judea is to have cause to celebrate its feasts with joy and to perform its vows to God. (5) Thus B. Luther in his German preface: Also he comforts the people of God according to his name (for Nahum means Comforter, in German a Comforter), how their enemies the Assyrians shall in turn be destroyed. At the end of the 1st chapter he also sounds like Is. 52, 7, about the good preachers who proclaim peace and salvation on the mountains, and tells Judah to celebrate joyfully. And although the same may be understood of the time of Hezekiah, after Sennacherib, when Judah was saved and remained before King Sennacherib: yet it is a general prophecy also concerning Christ, that the good news and the joyful divine service should remain in Judah, taught and confirmed by God's Word, whence he is indeed rightly called a true Nahum. Thus B. Wigandus in this place, p. 373. Exhortation and Prophecy, that the Church should prepare itself for great joy. But although the news about Sennacherib being slaughtered by his own children was most welcome, the Prophet looks further, namely that this protection and preservation of Judah happens primarily on account of the exhibition of the Messiah, and that from there the Gospel, which brings peace of hearts, is to emanate into the whole world. Behold (it contains a certain congratulation here, in a joyful and difficult matter. Upon the mountains, Is. 52, the same words exist. Therefore the Prophets agree in a matter of the greatest importance. It is, however, a prophecy about the Gospel being spread throughout the whole world. Peace (Effect for cause. For the effect of the Gospel is the peace of conscience with God. Celebrate) Exhortation. Therefore prepare yourself for joy. B. Winckel also admits in this place that the present passage is not inappropriately referred to the preaching of the Gospel done by the Apostles. Nor do the Belgian interpreters deny that these things agree with the spiritual redemption made through Christ.

HE SHALL NO MORE PASS THROUGH THEE BELIAL] That wicked one, the Assyrian, who despised God, shall no more reach you.

Ver. same. THE WHOLE IS PERISHED] He is cut down. The glory of the Empire is taken away.

Others wish it to be treated not of the glory of the Empire being taken away, but of the excision of the Assyrian himself and of his whole [army], since both his whole army was cut off, and he himself was killed by his sons, and his posterity is also to be cut off, and he himself is no longer to pass through Judea. Thus both the spiritual happiness of Judah and also its liberation from an external enemy are proclaimed. For although one may also understand the name of Belial as Satan, that he no longer has power over the faithful, because the whole is killed through Christ: yet this prediction concerning the destruction and excision of the Assyrian does not contradict the preceding explanation concerning the Gospel of peace, so that, namely, both benefits are promised here to Judea, both of the Evangelical announcement that would follow in its own time, and of the liberation from the hand of the Assyrian, concerning whose excision we had treated before. Tarnovius wishes the Prophet to progress from earthly to heavenly things, from corporal to spiritual things, in the manner of the Prophets: If the news of the destruction of the enemy Sennacherib is joyful, how much more joyful will be the news of the Gospel concerning CHRIST, and concerning the subjection of the Devil and the remaining infernal and spiritual enemies brought about through Christ? Coccejus has again invented something new here; namely, that by Belial is understood Nebuchadnezzar, of whom there is neither a trace nor a footprint in the text.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ECCE SUPER MONTES PEDES EVAN- GELIZANTIS] Ad montes, id est, ad Judæam subito ibunt cursores lætum afferentes nuntium. (Judæis.

ET ANNUNCIANTIS PACEM] Id est, res prosperas CELEBRA JUDA FESTIVITATES VESTRAS] Secure age dies festos.

ET REDDE VOTA TUA]. Quæ fecisti, si ab Assyriorum metu liberaberis.

Etsi Interpp. nonnulli hæc speciatim ad secu- ritatem ab Assyrio hoste Judææ reddendam refe- rant: generatim tamen de pace vel prosperitate Ju- dæ accipi, ac sub ea etiam illam felicitatem, quæ imprimis N. T. reservabatur, eoque spiritualis fe- licitas ac beatitudo per Evangelistas pacis annun- cianda erat, comprehendi, non pauci simul agno- scunt. Sensum hunc convenientissimum existi- mamus, ut accipiatur tanquam vaticinium Evange- licum (1) Quia omnes Prophetæ, teste Petro, Act. X. 43. de gratuita remissione peccatorum per Christum vaticinati, ac testati sunt. Non ergo ab hac uni- versalitate excipiendus noster Propheta. At nisi hunc locum de Evangelio gratiæ explices, nihil in eo habebitur Evangelii. (2) Quia verba eadem usurpat, quæ Esaias c. LII. 7. Quæ vero de nun- cio Evangelico sub N. T. agere, ad istum locum demonstravimus. (3) Quia interpretem habemus indubitatum & authenticum S. Apostolum Rom. X. 15. qui hæc de nunciis Evangelicæ gratiæ ac- cipienda esse docet. (4) Non refragatur, sed fa- vet huic sensui contextus, q. d. propheta: Ille erit exitus hostium Juda. Itaq; tantum abest, ut Iudæa sub- vertenda penitus sit antequam auferatur sceptrum de Juda & Schilo veniat, quem omnes Prophetæ in o- re habuere ut in montibus ejus apparituri sint olim pedes Evangelizantium, pacemq; annunciantium, causamq; habitura Iudæa sit, festivitates suas cum gaudio celebrandi, & vota sua Deo reddendi. (5) Sic B. Lutherus in præfat. Germ.
