In vain, therefore, do the Papist interpreters here sweat over the two animals, to be explained both literally and allegorically, Cornelius à Lapide, Ribera, and others, to whom the two living creatures are now connection, the Medes and Persians [are] Darius and Cyrus, now the Babylonians and Jews, now the two testaments, now the two Cherubim or Seraphim, now God the Father and the Holy Spirit, now Moses and Elijah, now the two thieves among whom Christ was crucified, now the ox and the ass in the Bethlehem stable—which trifles whoever wishes may read among them. Cornelius likes a double sense, so that indeed the Medes and Persians are understood according to the literal sense, but the ox and the ass according to the allegorical, about which he is prolix enough: but since the Vulgate version is authentic for the Papists, which is entirely ignorant of those two animals, how can they leave room for them against the decree of the Council of Trent? And in what way is it permitted to insert here the animals at the manger of Christ, if indeed the discourse is about the liberation from the Babylonian captivity? For we have long since exploded the double sense of the same saying. And therefore we cannot cast our vote for those who perhaps among our own admit a double sense here, and attribute a prophetic spirit to the LXX Interpreters by which they predicted the ox and the ass at the manger of the Lord (concerning which see the preface of B. Walther to Dissert. Theol. de immortalitate animæ), even if they philosophize much more moderately about those animals than the Pontificials do. For it is clearer than the midday sun that those things are ἀλλότρια [alien] to these Prophetic words.

IN THE MIDST OF THE YEARS MAKE KNOWN: WHEN THOU HAST BEEN ANGRY, THOU SHALT REMEMBER MERCY] In that middle time show that you, although angry, remember mercy. Show this, indeed, to your people.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DOMINE AUDIVI AUDITIONEM TUAM, ET TIMUI] Respondet Habacuc acceptæ jam revelatio- ni, & ait: Domine dicta tua audivi, reveritus sum: agnoscens summam tuam justitiam, adversus Judæos primum, dein- de & adversus Chaldæos.

DOMINE OPUS TUUM IN MEDIO ANNO- RUM VIVIFICA ILLUD] Illud Hebræo more תחייהו, cum divina revelatione cognosset propheta intervallum temporis futurum breve inter vastitatem Judææ & pœnas irrogandas Chaldæis, orat Deum ut medio tempore con- servet opus suum, id est, populum Judæum. Homines quidem omnes Dei opus, sed peculiariter Judæi, quos DEUS ex Ægypto deductos populum fecit, legibus instru- xit. Græci, pro שנים legerunt hoc loco חיים vertunt enim ἐν μέσῳ δύο ζώων, quod illi videntur intellexisse de illis cœlestibus potestatibus quæ חיות apud Ezechielem. Quam variis modis Christiani hæc sint interpretati, vide Hieronymum.

Per opus Domini Judæos intelligi, exemplo caret. Etsi peculiariter Judæi approprientur Deo, nun- quam tamen opus Domini, quod sciam, Judæos notat. Osiander reddit: Opus tuum proprium quod est benefacere, erga nos exerce, & in media tribulatione nobis fuccurre. Convenientius per opus Domini intelligitur liberatio Judæorum è ca- ptivitate Babylonica, quod vivificari, & adimpleri petit Propheta. Siquidem Ebræi soleant vitam etiam rebus inanimis, annis, diebus aëri, fertilitati, liberationi dare: cum illa sunt & vigent, dicun- tur Ebræis vivificari & vivere. R. Salomo similiter fere exponit: Vivifica opus tuum pristinum, quo fuisti ulciscens nos ab inimicis nostris, in medio anno- rum angustiæ in quo habitabamus, vivifica, id est, refuscita, & reducito illud postliminio. Verba IN MEDIO annorum calamitatis istius, sic explicat Vatablus, cum ingruent vehementius pericula, cum circumfluentibus undiquaque calamitatum flucti- bus nulla emergendi effulgebit spes: ubi medium umbræ mortis Ps. XXIII. 4. alii in medio annorum, id est, intra annos præfinitos & destinatos. B. Winckel- mannus in medio annorum exponit in summis neces- sitatibus, vel etiam justo & opportuno tempore. Quod aliter LXX. Interpp. legerint non tam Codicum varietati, quam ipsorum ἀβλεψίᾳ, aut nimiæ li- centiæ (si ita transtulere ipsi) imputandum. Con- sentiunt enim cum veritate Ebraica eamque fir- mant hic Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion, Chaldæus & alii. Quod nonnulli de prophetico spiritu se- ptuaginta senum hic tradunt, aut de distinctione Keri & Ketif in hoc loco suspicantur, fidem nul- lam meretur. Interpretes isti fuere variis lapsibus obnoxii, (quod nimis probat translatio ipsorum) non vates: nec ullum istius diversæ lectionis textua- lis & marginalis apparet hoc in textu vestigium. Undecunq; tandem illa duo animalia irrepserint, non certe in dubium vocanda Ebræa veritas. Imo & שנים annos in suis Codicibus habuisse LXX. In- terpp. Codices Vaticani, Complut. Reg. & alii cum Hieronymo, Cyrillo, ac Theodoreto testantur, quia ad- didere,cum appropinquaverint anni,cognosceris,cum advenerit tempus,demonstraberis. Frustra ergo hic Papistici Interp. de duobus animalibus, & literaliter & allegorice explicandis sudant, Cornelius à Lapide, Riebera & alii, quibus duo animantia modo sunt Medi & Persæ Darius & Cyrus, modo Babylonii, & Iudæi, modo duo testamenta, modo duo Cherubim aut Seraphim, modo Deus Pater & Sp. S. modo Moses & Elias, modo duo latrones, inter quos Chri- stus crucifixus est, modo bos & asinus in stabulo Bethlehemitico, quas ineptias, qui volet apud eos- dem leget. Cornelio geminus placet sensus, ut nempe secundum literalem sensum intelligantur Medi & Persæ, quoad allegoricum vero bos & asinus, de quibus prolixus satis est: sed quum Papistis au- thentica sit vulgata versio, quæ illa duo animalia prorsus ignorat, quomodo illis adversus Concilii Tridentini decretum locum relinquere possunt? Et quo pacto hic ingerere licet animantia ad præ- sepe Christi, siquidem de liberatione e captivitate Babylonica sermo sit? Geminum enim sensum e- jusdem dicti jam pridem explosimus. Ideoque et- iam illis qui forte ex nostris geminum sensum hic admittunt, & spiritum vatidicum LXX. Interpp. tribuunt quo bovem & asinum ad præsepe Domini prædixerint (quo de videatur præfatio B. Walthe- ri ad Dissert. Theol. de immortalitate animæ) etsi multo moderatius, quam Pontificii de illis animan- tibus philosophantur, calculum adjicere non pos- sumus. Plane enim ἀλλότρια illa ab hisce verbis Propheticis esse, sole meridiano clarius est.

IN MEDIO ANNORUM NOTUM FACIES: CUM IRATUS FUERIS, MISERICORDIÆ RECORDA- BERIS] Medio illo tempore ostende te, quamvis iratum, mi- sericordiæ meminisse. Ostende hoc nempe populo tuo.

## 3:3
Ver. 3. GOD SHALL COME FROM THE SOUTH, AND THE HOLY ONE FROM MOUNT PHARAN] He comes. He gives the reasons why he called the work of God [the work] of the Jews, and the sense is taken, as is also a part of the words, from Deut. XXXIII. 2. Those mountains, which have various names, Seir, Sinai, Pharan, both cohere with each other and lie to the South of Judea.

HIS GLORY COVERED THE HEAVENS] The air was full of lightnings. Exod. XX. 18.

AND THE EARTH IS FULL OF HIS PRAISE] It was full, because of the excellent precepts which he gave.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEUS AB AUSTRO VENIET, ET SAN- CTUS DE MONTE PHARAN] Venit. Reddit causas cur Judæos opus Dei dixerit, & sumtus est sensus, pars quoque verborum, ex Deuteron. XXXIII. 2. Montes illi, qui varia habent nomina, Seir, Sinai, Pharan, & inter se co- hærent & Judææ ad Austrum objacent.

OPERUIT COELOS GLORIA EJUS] Plenus fuit aër fulgurum. Exod. XX. 18.

ET LAVDIS EJVS PLENA EST TERRA] Ple- na fuit, propter egregia, quæ dedit, præcepta.

## 3:4
Ver. 4. HIS BRIGHTNESS SHALL BE AS THE LIGHT] It shall be. Light. ἀντονοματικῶς [by antonomasia] is the sun: as Job XXXI. 26. and elsewhere. See the history Exod. XIX. 18.

HORNS IN HIS HANDS] That is, sparks, as the Chaldean takes it here. See Ex. XXXIV. 29. 30.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SPLENDOR EJVS VT LVX ERIT] Erit. Lux. ἀντονοματικῶς est sol: ut Job. XXXI. 26. & alibi Hi- storian vid. Exod. XIX. 18.

CORNVA IN MANIBVS EJVS] Id est, scintil- læ, ut hic sumit Chaldæus. Vide Ex. XXXIV. 29. 30.

## 3:5
Ver. 5. THERE IS HIS STRENGTH HID] There his majesty is hidden, supply: he revealed himself, as the Chaldean [does] here.

BEFORE HIS FACE SHALL GO DEATH] It went. Death, that is, the certain destruction of the Canaanites and neighboring nations. He tacitly hints that God would one day act thus with the Chaldeans also. The Greeks read רֶשֶׁף with a different point: for they say λόγος [word], others πτῶσις [fall], which agrees with the Latin; we learn from Jerome that Symmachus and Aquila followed the same sense.

AND THE DEVIL SHALL GO FORTH BEFORE HIS FEET] רֶשֶׁף is not translated in one way; it seems to be a disease akin to the plague, such as ἄνθραξ [anthrax]. And thus the Chaldean took it. See Psalm LXXVIII. 47.

The Vulgate is to be corrected here, if indeed it cannot be shown where רֶשֶׁף denotes the Devil. But the Prophet seems rather to look back to the plagues of the Egyptians, who were struck with plague and anthrax, than to the Canaanites, about whom Grotius understands these things. See Exod. IX. 3. 6. 23. 24. For then also his glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise. Which is more correctly accepted concerning the miracles performed in Egypt than concerning the circumstances of the promulgation of the law. The interpretation concerning lightnings filling the air does not exhaust the force of the phrase about the glory of the Lord covering the heavens, nor does the explanation about the excellent precepts which God gave [exhaust the phrase] about the earth being filled with the praise of the Lord. The brightness of the Lord was as light, and the hiding of his strength, when in Egypt he illustrated the glory of the Lord and the strength hidden to them, especially to be feared by the Egyptians. B. Winckelmannus rightly spoke this παρεφθεγξατο [incidentally]: Although the Lord was not seen in the people with the eyes, and his strength was thus hidden, yet it shone forth from his stupendous works, and these were like rays proceeding from his hand, from his power.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IBI ABSCONDITA EST FORTITUDO EJVS] Ibi abscondita majestas ejus, supple patefecit se, ut hic Chaldæus.

ANTE FACIEM EJVS IBIT MORS] Ibat. Mors, id est, pernicies certa Cananæorum, & vicinarum gentium. Tacite innuit sic & cum Chaldæis acturum Deum aliquan- do. Græci רֶשֶׁף legere cum alio puncto: dicunt enim λόγος, alii πτῶσις quod cum Latino convenit; eundem sensum se- cutos Symmachum & Aquilam ex Hieronymo discimus.

ET EGREDIETVR DIABOLVS ANTE PEDES EJVS] רֶשֶׁף non uno modo vertitur; videtur esse mor- bus pestilentiæ affinis, qualis ἄνθραξ. & sic sumsit Chal- dæus. Vide Psalm. LXXVIII. 47.

Castigandus hic Vulgatus, siquidem ostendi nequeat, ubi רֶשֶׁף Diabolum notet. Videtur au- tem potius Propheta respicere plagas Ægyptio- rum, qui peste & anthrace percussi sunt, quam Ca- nanæorum, de quibus Grotius hæc intelligit. Vid. Exod. IX. 3. 6. 23. 24. Nam & tum cælos operuit glo- ria ejus, & laude ejus plena fuit terra. Quod rectius de miraculis in Ægypto patratis, quam de circum- stantiis promulgationis legis accipitur. Non exhau- rit vim phraseos de gloria Domini cælos operien- te interpretatio de fulgoribus aerem replentibus, aut de terra laude Domini repleta, explicatio de præceptis egregiis, quæ dedit Deus. Splendor Domini ut lux fuit, & absconsio roboris ejus, cum in Ægypto illustrabat gloriam Domini & robur absconditum ipsis, imprimis Ægyptiis metuen- dum. Recte hæc παρεφθεγξατο B. Winckelmannus: Tametsi Dominus in populo oculis non cerneretur, at- que ita abscondita esset fortitudo ejus, ex operibus ta- men stupendis illucescebat, & hæc erant instar radio- rum à manu, à potentia ejus prodeuntium.

## 3:6
Vers. 6.

HE STOOD AND MEASURED THE EARTH] God stood, that is, his ark rested in the promised land. And he measured the earth: that is, he distributed it to his people, as measurers are accustomed to do, see Acts VII. 45. Josh. XIII. and following. HE LOOKED AND DISSOLVED THE NATIONS] He terrified. Josh. V. 1. AND THE MOUNTAINS OF THE AGE WERE BROKEN] That is, the men who had long dwelt in those mountains. THE HILLS OF THE WORLD WERE BOWED DOWN] The ancient hills submitted themselves: that is, the peoples who had lived for a long time in those hills. There is no reason why one should attribute the ark of the covenant to them here. For the discourse is perpetually about the Lord himself. And therefore another subject is rashly introduced. Nor is his ark understood by the Lord anywhere. Blessed Luther interprets these things not of the division of the holy land, but of the overthrow of Pharaoh and the Egyptians: for there the Lord is said to have stood between the Egyptians and his people: and thus to have measured the earth, so that he set a limit for the Egyptians, which they could not cross: But afterwards he utterly overturned Pharaoh and the remaining princes of Egypt, whom the Prophet calls the mountains and hills of the age, in the Red Sea. Those are called mountains of eternity and hills of the age, because they had held the kingdom of Egypt from ancient times for many ages, and trusted that they would possess it forever, as Winckelmann has it here. We easily admit, however, that after those wonders in Egypt, it is explained in this place how the Lord, when he stood in the land of Canaan, distributed the land, and by his mere gaze dissipated the nations, since the eternal mountains and perpetual hills were sufficiently fortified and durable, whose kingdom seemed so established as if it were to be perpetual.

Vers. same. FROM HIS ETERNAL JOURNEYS] In the Hebrew: Journeys of the age to him: that is, all things that are done in the world are subject to him. The Chaldean took it thus. Most interpret it concerning the Canaanites, but the change of number, since the singular is used here, persuades that these things are more correctly taken concerning God, which Blessed Luther also observed, with whom is the government of the whole world, and whose wisdom moderates this whole orb. Some [interpret it] concerning the celestial spheres, which are always moving, i.e., that the Lord takes care not only of inferior things, but also of superior ones. But the interpretation of the Chaldean is more to be approved, which most of our own also embrace.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

STETIT ET MENSVS EST TERRAM] Stetit Deus, id est, arca ejus quievit in terra promissa. Et mensus est terram: id est, distribuit populo suo, ut mensores so- lent, Vide Actor. VII. 45. Jos. XIII. & sequentibus. ADSPEXIT ET DISSOLVIT GENTES] Perter- ruit. Jos. V. 1. ET CONTRITI SVNT MONTES SECVLI] Id est, homines qui pridem in montibus illis habitaverant. INCRVVATI SVNT COLLES MVNDI] Submi- serunt se colles antiqui: id est, populi, qui diu in illis colli- bus vixerant. Non est, quod hic tribuat illis arcam foederis. Nam de Domino ipso perpetuus sermo est. Ideo- que temere ingeritur aliud subjectum. Nec us- piam per Dominum arca ejus intelligitur. B. Lu- therus non de divisione terrae sanctae, sed de eversio- ne Pharaonis & Aegyptiorum haec interpretatur: I- bi enim Dominus dicitur stetisse inter Aegyptios & populum suum: & ita terram mensurasse, ut Aegyptiis terminum constituerit, quem transilire non potuerint: Postea autem Pharaonem & reli- quos proceres Aegypti, quos montes & colles se- culi vocat Propheta, prorsus in mari rubro sub- vertisse. Dicuntur illi montes aeternitates & colles seculi, quod antiquitus a multis seculis regnum Ae- gypti tenuissent, & perpetuum sese possessuros esse confiderent, uti hic habet Winckelmannus. Fa- cile tamen admittimus, post illa mirabilia in Ae- gypto exponi hoc loco, quomodo Dominus, ubi con- stitit in terra Canaan, terram distribuerit, & solo intuitu gentes dissiparit, cum montes aeterni & colles perpetui satis muniti & durabiles erant, quorum re- gnum ita stabilitum videbatur, ac si perpetuum futu- rum esset.

Vers. eod. AB ITINERIBVS AETERNITATIS EJVS] In Hebraeo: Itinera seculi ei: id est, omnia quae in mundo aguntur ipsi subsunt. Ita accepit Chaldaeus. Plerique de Cananaeis interpretantur, sed nume- ri mutatio, quum hic singularis adhibeatur, rectius de Deo haec accipi suadet, quod etiam B. Lutherus observavit, penes quem est totius mundi gubernatio, & cujus sapientia totum hunc orbem moderatur. Non- nulli de sphaeris caelestibus, quae semper moveantur, q. d. Dominum non tantum inferiorum, sed et- iam superiorum curam gerere. Sed magis pro- banda Chaldaei interpretatio, quam nostri etiam plerique amplectuntur.

## 3:7
V. 7. FOR INIQUITY I SAW THE TENTS OF ETHIOPIA, THE SKINS OF THE LAND OF MIDIAN SHALL BE TROUBLED] I saw, that is, I understood, that because of that crime which is mentioned in Num. XXV., the tents of the Ethiopians, that is, the skins of the Midianites, were moved. He explains whom he signified by the word Ethiopians, namely the Midianites, similar in appearance to the Ethiopians, for which reason also the wife of Moses is called a Midianite woman in Num. XII. 1. The tents of these trembled, with not a few of the Midianites killed in Num. XXV. 17. The Chaldean thinks Chusan is the name of a king of the Midianites, and refers these things to the times of Gideon, which the series of what follows hardly allows. There is no reason why we should confuse the Midianites with the Ethiopians here, or restrict these things to the history of Num. XIV. For fear and trembling seized both the Midianites and the Ethiopians, and other neighboring nations, when they saw the rays of divine power, because the curtains of the land of Midian were moved and trembled, or those regions trembled like curtains, or because of tents made from extended curtains.

Latin:

V. 7. PRO INIQVITATE VIDI TENTORIA AE- THIOPIAE, TVRBABVNTVR PELLES TERRAE MA- DIAN] Vidi, id est, intellexi, propter scelus illud, quod me- moratur Num. XXV. commota esse tentoria Aethiopum, id est, pelles Madianitarum. Explicat quos voce Aethiopum si- gnificaverit, nempe Madianitas Aethiopibus facie similes, qua de causa & uxor Mosis Madianitis dicitur Aethiopissa Num. XII. 1. Horum tentoria contremuere, occisis Ma- dianitarum non paucis Num. XV. 17. Chaldaeus Chusan no- men esse putat regis Madianitarum, & refert haec ad tempo- ra Gedeonis, quod sequentium series aegre patitur. Non est cur Midianitas cum Aethiopibus hic confundamus, aut ad historiam Num. XIV. haec restringamus. Nam & Midianitas & Aethiopas, a- liasque vicinas gentes timor & tremor occupavit, cum radios divinae potentiae viderent, quod com- motae sint & trepidaverint cortinae terrae Midian, vel instar aulaeorum, vel ex aulaeis extensis facto- rum tentoriorum regiones illae tremuerint.

## 3:8
Vers. 8. WAS THE LORD ANGRY AT THE RIVERS, OR WAS THY FURY AGAINST THE RIVERS] Was thy fury, forsooth, kindled against the rivers? OR THY INDIGNATION IN THE SEA] Against the sea? He asks very poetically whether GOD is to be thought to have been angry in those times, either at the river waters, or at the sea, because he changed their nature, namely so that, this cause being removed, he might posit another more strongly, namely the singular care of God for his people. THOU WHO RIDEST UPON THY HORSES, AND THY CHARIOTS ARE SALVATION] Nay, thy chariots brought salvation to thee following thy horses. He calls the ark the chariot, the Cherubim the horses of God.

Nothing here about the ark, nothing about the Cherubim. And it is foreign to the Scriptures to call the ark a chariot, and the Cherubim the horses of God. He is said to sit above the Cherubim, Ps. 80:2; nowhere, as far as is known, is He said to be carried by the Cherubim or horses. Nor did the ark or Cherubim exist when the Egyptians were drowned in the Red Sea. Nothing else is implied, therefore, than that God appeared as if carried by horses and chariots against the cavalry and chariots of the Egyptians: whence the Prophet says: you who rode (were carried) upon your horses and chariots (for) salvation. It can also be said that the horses upon which He sat and those chariots were the saving clouds in which He appeared when He prepared salvation for the people. Ex. 13:21, ch. 14:4, v. 9. YOU WILL AWAKEN YOUR BOW, OATHS TO THE TRIBES, WHICH YOU HAVE SPOKEN] In leading out, you led out your bow, from the quiver, of course, as soldiers are accustomed to do when the enemy is near. Oaths spoken to the tribes: that is, no differently than if you had spoken a military oath to them. Not unlike that of Virgil: Apollo, seeing these things from on high, was bending his bow. It refers rather to the oath given to Abraham and the other Patriarchs, Gen. 15:14, 15, ch. 17, just as kindnesses are said passively, which were promised to him. Some apply these specifically to the Amalekites, Ex. 17, and to King Arad, as also to Sihon and Og, Num. 21, because the Lord armed His people against them; for by the bow they understand by synecdoche all armor. YOU WILL CLEAVE THE RIVERS OF THE EARTH] With rivers you cleaved the earth, that is, you split the earth so that waters might burst forth. Exod. 17:6, Num. 20:11, 12, Ps. 105:40. THEY SAW YOU] They felt your power. AND THE MOUNTAINS GRIEVED] The mountains travailed, ὠδήσουσι, here the Greeks. Thus חול is taken in Isaiah 23:4, 26:18, 45:16, 46:8, 54:1, Jer. 4:3, Micah 4:10. Habac. 3:9, in which places the Greeks have placed ὠδίνειν. A FLOOD OF WATERS PASSED] As if by some birth. THE ABYSS GAVE ITS VOICE] Just as newborn infants reveal themselves by crying, so too the waters bursting forth from the deep with a certain roaring. The abyss is elsewhere the sea, here the waters hidden under the earth, as Deut. 8:2, Ps. 78:15. THE HEIGHT LIFTED ITS HANDS] It lifted its hands on high, namely the abyss: this simile is also drawn from infants. Verse 11. THE SUN AND MOON STOOD IN THEIR HABITATION] Joshua 10:12. IN THE LIGHT OF YOUR ARROWS THEY WILL GO] The Israelites went, with lightnings shining before them. IN THE SPLENDOR OF YOUR FLASHING SPEAR] It is the same as what preceded. Verse 12. IN INDIGNATION YOU WILL TRAMPLE THE EARTH] Angry, you were shaking the earth. IN FURY YOU WILL STUPEFY THE NATIONS] You were crushing the Canaanites, Amorites, and others under the leadership of Joshua. Verse 13. YOU WENT FORTH FOR THE SALVATION OF YOUR PEOPLE, FOR SALVATION WITH YOUR CHRIST] You were present with David in his expeditions. YOU STRUCK THE HEAD FROM THE HOUSE OF THE WICKED] Hadadezer, king of Zobah, 2 Sam. 8:3. YOU STRIPPED THE FOUNDATION OF IT EVEN TO THE NECK] Namely of that house, that is, of the kingdom of Zobah, you demolished the highest and the lowest.

We do not disapprove of these things regarding David, but those victories should not be restricted precisely to Hadadezer and his kingdom: since he also overcame other Edomites, Ammonites, Syrians, and Philistines, and stripped them of their bow, and thus of the foundation and strength of their kingdom. Others interpret these less correctly regarding Pharaoh and the slaughter of the firstborn in Egypt. Those who understand by the anointed Christ Jesus wander far from the context, which continues in the historical review and proclamation of the miracles and benefits of God: but no one deviates more than Cocceius, whose commentary here, as in most other Prophetic matters, is very strange. For by ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει he has attempted to carve out from this canticle, v. 3 seq., seven periods of the kingdom of Christ which he had preconceived in his mind: the flashing of the Gospel v. 3, 4; the judgment of the incredulous v. 5, 6.

7. of the destruction of Gentile idolatry in the world v. 8, 9, 10; of the conservation of truth and the Church in darkness v. 11, 12, 13; of the beginning of restoring the Church v. 14; of the vindication of the Church, scarcely liberated and immediately suffering persecution v. 14, 15, 16, 17; of the salvation and erection of the Church v. 18, 19. And he understands this exit of GOD with CHRIST THE SON OF GOD to attack the Anti-Christ and save the Church, and he refers the time to the age of the Hussites, in its fulfillment. But these are not of such importance that we should dwell on them.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NVMQVID IN FLVMINIBUS IRATVS ES DOMINE, AVT IN FLVMINIBVS FVROR TVVS] An contra flumina furor tuus? accensus scilicet fuit. VEL IN MARI INDIGNATIO TVO] Adversus mare Poetice admodum quaerit, an cogitandus sit DEVS illis temporibus iratus fuisse, aut aquis flumineis, aut ma- ri, quod eorum naturam immutaverit, nempe ut hac cau- sa sublata, alteram fortius ponat, singularem scilicet Dei pro populo suo curam. QVI ADSCENDES SVPER EQVOS TVOS, ET QVADRIGAE TVAE SALVATIO] Imo te secundo equis tuis currus tui salutem attulerunt. Arcam vocat currum, Cherubinos equos Dei.

Nihil hic de arca, nihil de Cherubinis. Et ar- cam currum, Cherubinos equos Dei dici à Scriptu- ris alienum est. Sedere super Cherubim dicitur Pf. 80, 2. à Cherubim seu equis vehi nuspiam, quod con- stet, dicitur. Neque tum arca, aut Cherubim extite- runt cum Ægyptii in mari rubro submersi sunt. Ni- hil ergo aliud innuitur, quam quod Deus visus fuerit quasi equis vehi, & quadrigis contra equitatum & quadrigas Ægyptiorum : unde ait Propheta : qui equitasti (vectus es) super equos tuos & quadrigas (ad) salutem. Dici etiam potest, quod equi, qui- bus insedit & currus illi salutares nubes fuerint, in quibus apparuit, cum salutem populo paravit. Ex. XIII. 21. c. XIV. 4. Vers. 9. SUSCITANS SUSCITABIS ARCUM TUUM, JURAMENTA TRIBUBUS, QUÆ LOQUUTUS ES] Educendo eduxisti arcum tuum, E coryto scilicet, ut face- re milites solent, ubi hostis prope est. Iuramenta tribubus dicta : id est, non aliter quam si sacramentum militare ipsis dixisses. Non dissimile illud Virgilii : Altius hæc cernens arcum intendebat Apollo Desuper. Respicitur potius juramentum Abrahamo, a- liisque Patribus datum Gen. 15, 14. 15. c. 17. uti be- nignitates passive dicuntur, quæ ipsi promissa sunt. Specialiter applicant nonnulli hæc ad Amalecitas Ex. 17. & Arad Regem ut & Sihon & Og Num. 21. quod Dominus armaverit populum suum adver- sus eosdem; per arcum enim synechdochice intel- ligunt omnem armaturam. FLUVIOS SCINDES TERRÆ] Fluminibus scidisti terram, id est, terram fidisti, ut erumperent aquæ. Exod. XVII, 6. Num. XX, 11. 12. Pf. CV. 40. VIDERUNT TE] Senserunt vim tuam. ET DOLUERUNT MONTES] Parturierunt mon- tes, ὠδήσουσι, hic Græci. Ita חול sumitur Esaïæ XXIII. 4. XXVI. 18. XLV. 16. XLVI. 8. LIV. 1. Jer. IV. 3. Mich. IV. 10. Habac. III. 9. in quibus locis Græci posuere ὠδίνειν. GURGES AQVARUM TRANSIIT] Quasi par- tu quodam. DEDIT ABYSSUS VOCEM] Sicut recens nati in- fantes vagitu se produnt, ita & ex imo erumpentes aquæ fremitu quodam. Abyssus alibi mare, hic aquæ sub terra occultatæ, ut Deut. VIII, 2. Pf. LXXVIII. 15. ALTITUDO MANUS SUAS LEVAVIT] In al- tum manus suas extulit, nempe abyssus : hæc quoque simili- tudo ab infantibus ducta. Vers. 11. SOL ET LVNA STETERUNT IN HABI- TACULO SUO] Josuæ X, 12. IN LVCE SAGITTARUM TVARUM IBUNT] Iverunt Israëlitæ, prælucentibus fulgoribus. IN SPLENDORE FULGURANTIS HASTÆ TUÆ] Idem est, quod præcessit. Vers. 12. IN FREMITU CONCULCABIS TERRAM] Iratus terram concutiebas. IN FURORE OBSTUPEFACIES GENTES] Con- terebas Cananæos, Amorrhæos, & alios duce Josue. Vers. 13. EGRESSUS ES IN SALUTEM POPULI TVI, IN SALUTEM CUM CHRISTO TUO] Da- vidi in expeditionibus adfuisti. PERCUSSISTI CAPUT DE DOMO IMPII] A- darezerum regem Sobæ II. Sam. IIX, 3. DENUDASTI FUNDAMENTUM EJUS USQUE AD COLLUM] Nempe domus illius, id est, regni Sobæ, summa & ima demolitus es.

Non improbamus ista de Davide, sed victoriæ illæ non restringendæ præcise ad Adarezerum ejus- que regnum: siquidem & alios Edomitas, Ammo- nitas, Syros & Philistinos superarit, eosque arcu, adeoque fundamento & robore regni exuerit. Mi- nus recte alii de Pharaonis, & primogenitorum in Æ- gypto internecione hæc interpretantur. Qui per un- ctum Christum Jesum intelligunt, à contextu val- de aberrant, qui pergit in historica miraculorum, & beneficiorum Dei recensione ac deprædicatio- ne: sed nemo magis deviat, quam Coccejus, cu- jus Commentarius hic, ut in plerisque aliis Pro- pheticis valde mirabilis. Nam ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει septem periodos regni Christi, quas animo præconceperat, ex hoc cantico v. 3. seq. exsculpere conatus est, co- ruscationis Evangelii v. 3. 4. Iudicii incredulos v. 5. 6.

7. destructionis idololatriae gentilis in mundo v. 8. 9. 10. conservationis veritatis & Ecclesiae in tenebris v. 11. 12. 13. Initii restaurandi Ecclesiam v. 14. Ecclesiae vix liberatae, & statim persecutionem patientis vindi- cationis v. 14. 15. 16. 17. Ecclesiae salvationis & erectio- nis v. 18. 19. Et hunc exitum DEI cum CHRI- STO FILIO DEI ad oppugnandum Anti-Chri- stum & salvandum Ecclesiam intelligit, tempus- que ad Hussitarum aetatem, in complemento, re- fert. Sed ea tanti non sunt, ut iis immoremur.

## 3:14
Verse 14. YOU CURSED HIS SCEPTERS, THE HEAD OF HIS WARRIORS] With staves you pierced the head of his warriors, that is, of his allies, namely the king of Damascus, 2 Sam. 8:5.

COMING AS A WHIRLWIND TO SCATTER ME] Who was coming like a whirlwind to scatter me. Here the Prophet assumes the person of the Israelite people.

THEIR EXULTATION] Of the Syrians.

AS OF HIM WHO DEVOURS THE POOR IN SECRET] The poor man hiding for fear. Such things the Syrians had promised themselves concerning the Hebrews, but falsely. They had sung a triumph before the victory.

Others take these as a prophecy concerning the Babylonian tyrant, to whom the Lord, as if he were about to curse the head of many villages, and who is to come like a whirlwind with his army to scatter the people of Judah from their land, no otherwise than if he were about to devour the poor and afflicted in secret, that is, with no one, not even the Lord himself, being about to be the avenger, which is the explanation of the blessed Winckelmann. But even if the Prophet still continues the historical celebration, it would not be necessary to restrict these to the Kings of the Syrians. The blessed Tarnovius renders such a sense: You, O GOD, pierced the head of the villages of his anointed King (David) with his rods, thus you overthrew those who were remaining in the regions and neighboring territories and were infesting your people, through David, as if you had bored through with an auger the mountains and fortifications in which they trusted, and that with no trouble, because they had been the rods of your anointed, sufficient for piercing, and then, when they stirred up a storm to scatter me, your people, when their exultation was as if they were about to eat and completely consume me, the poor Israelite, often hiding in fear of them, in the time of the Judges in secret. Cornelius a Lapide introduces here, as in this whole poem, his triple sense: historical, concerning the scepter of Pharaoh destroyed; Prophetic, concerning the scepter of Belshazzar and the Chaldeans being cast down by Cyrus, whom he wishes to be properly regarded here; and allegorical, concerning Christ being about to prostrate the scepters of Nero, Decius, and other persecutors, and of the Anti-Christ himself, Gog and Magog. But how can such a diverse sense have a place, so that the same word is taken both in the past and in the future, and such diverse subjects are to be placed under the same predicates?

Latin:

Vers. 14. MALEDIXISTI SCEPTRIS EJVS, CA- PITI BELLATORVM EJVS] Baculis pertudisti caput bella- torum ejus, id est, sociorum ejus, regem nempe Damasci 2. Sam. IIX. 5.

VENIENTIBVS VT TVRBO AD DISPERGEN- DVM ME] Qui veniebat ut turbo ad me dissipandum. Assu- mit hic Propheta personam populi Israelitici.

EXSVLTATIO EORUM] Syrorum.

SICUT EJUS QUI DEVORAT PAUPEREM IN ABSCONDITO] Pauperem prae metu latentem. Ta- lia sibi Syri de Hebraeis spoponderant, sed falso. Trium- phum cecinerant ante victoriam.

Alii haec pro vaticinio de Babylonico tyranno habent, cui Dominus, ut capiti multarum villarum maledicturus sit, & qui instar turbinis venturus sit cum exercitu suo, ad dispergendum populum Juda e terra sua, non secus ac si pauperem & afflictum devoraturus sit in abscondito, hoc est, nullo, neque ipso Domino, vindice futuro, quae est B. Winckel- manni explicatio. Sed etsi adhuc pertexat Prophe- ta historicam celebrationem, non tamen ad Reges Syrorum haec restringere necessum esset. Sensum talem reddit B. Tarnovius: Tu DEUS perforasti virgis illius uncti tui Regis (Davidis) caput pagorum ejus, ita eos, qui in plagis & regionibus finitimis erant reliqui, & tuum infestabant populum, per Davidem evertisti, ut si montes & munitiones, quibus confide- bant, terebra pertudisses, idq; nullo negotio, quia virgae uncti tui fuerant, ad perforandum satis, & tum, quum excitarent procellam ad dispergendum me, populum tuum, quum exultatio illorum esset, ac si comesturi planeq; absumturi fuissent me pauperem Israelem sae- pe latentem metu illorum, tempore Iudicum in ab- scondito. Cornel. a Lapide ingerit hic, uti in to- to isto carmine triplicem suum sensum historicum de sceptro Pharaonis destructo, Propheticum de sce- ptro Balsasaris & Chaldaeorum per Cirum deji- ciendo, quem proprie hic spectari vult, & alle- goricum, de Christo sceptra Neronis, Decii & a- liorum persecutorum ipsiusque Anti-Christi, Gog & Magog prostraturo. Sed quomodo tam diversus sensus locum habere possit, ut verbum idem tum in praeterito, tum in futuro accipiatur, & tam diversa subjecta praedicatis iisdem substernenda sint?

## 3:15
Verse 15. YOU MADE A WAY IN THE SEA, FOR YOUR HORSES, IN THE MUD, OF MANY WATERS] You made a way to the sea for your horses, to the heap of many waters. Going before David, as a horseman sent ahead, you made a way to the Red Sea, having conquered the Moabites, Ammonites, Philistines, and Idumeans, 2 Samuel 8:11, and on the other side to the great river Euphrates, 1 Chronicles 18:3.

If these are to be taken prophetically, not historically, which we prefer, it is a complaint about the changed fortune of the people, as the blessed Winckelmann observes: as if to say, formerly our horses were most swift for good fortune, and our chariots for salvation: but now you seem to be trampled with your horses in the sea and the mud of many waters, as if he were saying, our horses proceed slowly, with the Lord withdrawing his help.

Latin:

Vers. 15. VIAM FECISTI IN MARI, EQUIS TUIS, IN LUTO, AQUARUM MULTARUM] Viam fecisti ad mare equis tuis, ad acervum aquarum multa- rum. Praeiens Davidi, velut eques praemissus, viam fe- cisti ad mare rubrum, expugnatis Moabitis, Ammonitis, Philistinis & Idumaeis 2. Reg. VIII. 11. & alia ex parte ad magnum flumen Euphratem 1. Paralip. XIIX. 3.

Si prophetice haec, non historice accipiantur, quod praeferimus, querela est de mutata fortuna populi, uti B. Winckelmannus observat: q. d. o- lim equi nostri de fortunante erant expeditissimi, & quadrigae nostrae ad salutem: jam autem videris cum equis tuis calcari in mari & luto multarum aquarum, quasi dicat, lente procedunt equi nostri Domino sub- trahente auxilium suum.

## 3:16
Verse 16. I HEARD AND MY BELLY WAS TROUBLED] The Prophet, having received God's response concerning the destruction of the Chaldean empire, and at the same time strengthened by the memory of things done in the past, prepares himself to bear patiently the things that were about to happen through the Chaldeans, the Jews having deserved them. My belly indeed, that is, my inward parts, were troubled, that is, the plight of my countrymen indeed stirred me.

AT THE VOICE MY LIPS TREMBLED] I do not dare to speak, because of the magnitude of the evils which I foresee,

LET ROTTENNESS ENTER INTO MY BONES, AND LET IT TEEM BENEATH ME] Rottenness has invaded my bones, and I trembled within myself. That is, I can no more remain composed while thinking of these things than he whose bones are consumed by decay: I tremble all over.

THAT I MAY REST IN THE DAY OF TRIBULATION] Because I shall have to rest in the calamitous time. That is, by no prayers shall I be able to avert such a great evil.

THAT I MAY GO UP TO OUR ARMED PEOPLE] When he (namely the Chaldean) shall go up against the (Jewish) people to cut them off.

Latin:

Vers. 16. AUDIVI ET CONTURBATUS EST VEN- TER MEUS] Propheta accepto, Dei responso de Chal- daici imperii exitio, ac simul rerum olim actarum memo- ria confirmatus, parat se ad patienter ferenda, quae per Chaldaeos, Judaeis id meritis, erant eventura. Venter qui- dem meus, id est, viscera mea, conturbata sunt, id est, misceret me quidem popularium.

A VOCE CONTREMUERUNT LABIA MEA] Loqui non audeo, ob magnitudinem eorum, quae prospi- cio malorum,

INGREDIATUR PUTREDO IN OSSIBUS MEIS, ET SUBTER ME SCATEAT] Invasit ossa mea putredo, & intra me contremui. Id est, non magis ista cogitans consi- stere possum, quam is cui ossa tabe exesa sunt: tremo totus.

UT REQUIESCAM IN DIE TRIBULATIO- NIS] Quia quiescendum mihi erit in tempore calamitoso. Id est, nullis precibus malum tantum potero avertere.

UT ASCENDAM AD POPULUM ACCIN- CTUM NOSTRUM] Cum adscendet (nempe Chaldæus) contra populum (Judaicum) excisurus eum.

## 3:17
Ver. 17. THE FIG TREE SHALL NOT BLOSSOM] Be it so, let not the fig trees blossom. Συγχώρησις (Concession).

AND THERE SHALL BE NO FRUIT IN THE VINES] Let there be no produce in the vines.

THE LABOR OF THE OLIVE SHALL FAIL] Let the olive crop fail. Thus, 'the crop belied the hope,' in Horace.

THE FIELDS SHALL YIELD NO FOOD] Let not the fields bear fruit. THE FLOCK SHALL BE CUT OFF FROM THE FOLD] Let it be taken away.

AND THERE SHALL BE NO HERD IN THE STALLS] Let there be no ox in the stables.

In these words, indeed, the Prophet does not compose himself to endure what the Chaldeans were about to inflict upon the Jews, but rather he pathetically exaggerates those evils and testifies to the sorrow conceived therefrom, as if in the person of the people. Therefore, those words, 'The fig tree shall not blossom,' are not to be understood by way of συγχώρησις (concession): 'Be it so, let not the fig trees blossom,' but as they sound, prophetically. For this is the cause of such great disturbance and trembling of that prophet, that he foresaw the evils that were to come, whence he predicted that the face of things would be most sad at the time of the Babylonian captivity, during which the land would be desolate, and agriculture and cattle-raising would cease. For the rest, the Grotian exposition of the words can easily be admitted, although B. Luther takes 'THAT I MAY REST IN THE DAY OF TRIBULATION' in such a way that the Prophet, in the person of the pious, prefers to rest in the grave and die rather than behold such great tribulation with his own eyes, when the Jews are about to go up to the people by whom they will be attacked.

Latin:

Vers. 17. FICUS NON FLOREBIT] Esto, Ne flo- reant ficus. Συγχώρησις.

ET NON ERIT GERMEN IN VINEIS] Nullus sit proventus in vineis.

MENTIETVR OPVS OLIVÆ] Mentiatur oleitas. Sic spem mentita seges, apud Horatium. (gem.

ARVA NON ADFERENT CIBUM] Ne ferant arva fru- ABSCINDETVR DE OVILI PECUS] Auferatur.

ET NON ERIT ARMENTVM IN PRÆSEPI- BVS] Ne sit bos in stabulis.

Non componit in his quidem verbis sese Pro- pheta ad ferendum, quæ Chaldæi Judæis illaturi erant, sed exaggerat potius mala illa pathetice, ac mœrorem inde conceptum testatur, velut in per- sona populi. Non ergo per συγχώρησιν illa intelli- genda: Ficus non florebit: Esto, ne floreant ficus: sed ut sonant prophetice. Nam hæc causa est tantæ conturbationis & tremoris istius prophetæ, quod mala eventura præviderit, unde prædixit, faciem tristissimam fore tempore captivitatisBabylonicæ, quo terra desolata erit, agricultura & pecuaria ces- sabunt. De cætero expositio verborum Grotiana facile admitti potest, quamvis illa: UT REQUIE- SCAM IN DIE TRIBULATIONIS B. Luth. ita accipiat, q. præoptet Propheta in persona piorum quiescere in sepulcro & mori, quam tantam tribu- lationem oculis suis cernere, quando Judæi ascen- suri sint ad populum, à quo oppugnabuntur.

## 3:18
Ver. 18. BUT I WILL REJOICE IN THE LORD] I, however, will rejoice in the Lord, trusting in the promises of God.

AND I WILL EXULT IN THE GOD OF MY SALVATION] The Greeks say ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτηρί μῦ, for in the Hebrew it is ישעי, a common noun, not a proper one: the following words explain it.

Latin:

Vers. 18. EGO AVTEM IN DOMINO GAVDEBO] Ego tamen gaudebo in Domino, fisus Dei promissis.

ET EXVLTABO IN DEO JESV MEO] Græci ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ σωτηρί μυ, est enim in Hebræo ישעי, nomen commune, non proprium: explicant id sequentia.

## 3:19
Ver. 19. GOD THE LORD IS MY STRENGTH] My protection.

AND HE WILL SET MY FEET LIKE THE HINDS'] He will cause me to escape that slaughter.

AND HE WILL LEAD ME UPON MY HIGH PLACES] He will make me go to my mountains: that is, those which may preserve me. An allusion to the history in Gen. XIX. 17, to which the passage in Matt. XXIV. 16 also refers.

VICTOR IN THE PSALMS SINGING] To the master of my strings: supply, I have delivered this song to be adapted to the strings. Ps. IV. at the beginning.

As for the name ישעי, although it may be common, it can nevertheless be taken as a proper name, since that common name is appropriated to our Jesus in the Holy Scriptures, as in Gen. XLIX. 15, Ps. XIV. last, Isa. XLIX. 6, and elsewhere, and he is even called Jesus by it in Matt. I. 21. Therefore, the Vulgate does not need correction in this place, which Grotius cannot reject since the Pope and the Council of Trent have canonized it. And there is no joy in the Lord, except that which the faithful conceive in their God Jesus: outside of whom there is no salvation, Acts IV. 12; he is also our strength: as the faithful profess concerning him in Isa. XLV. 28, In the Lord is our strength. Whence Jerome rightly says on this passage: I will have no other strength except in Christ, and I will compare all the righteousness of the law to refuse. In the same and through the same, the Prophet and all the faithful, whose person he bears there, could uniquely rejoice, be glad, and exult in the midst of these calamities and perturbations, certain of the salvation to be provided through him, Phil. IV. 4. Cornelius is not wrong here. à Lapide: Habakkuk, therefore, foreseeing in the spirit that Joshua, who led the Hebrews out of Egypt, and Cyrus, who liberated the same from Babylon, were types of Jesus Christ both in fact and in name, and that he had brought this liberation and salvation to the people of God by the power of his divinity and the merits of the humanity of Jesus Christ: finally, that he himself, by being born, would bring a far greater and eternal liberation and salvation to the human race, exulting in the spirit, he jubilates, and he prophesies and names his name Jesus six hundred years before his birth, and is delighted with him: because he foresaw that he and we were to be liberated by him from all enemies, from the devil, sin, concupiscence, the flesh, the world, and hell, and were to be filled with every grace, glory, salvation, and happiness. And again: furthermore, this prophet exults and triumphs not in himself, but in the Lord, saying: God the Lord is my strength. For just as the sun is the light of the air; nor does it matter whether this light is innate to it or borrowed from the sun, provided it is as ready and at hand for it as if it were innate: so we use the powers of God and Jesus as if they were our own, and therefore he himself is our strength. But what does this strength of his effect in us? He will set, he says, my feet like the hinds', so that they may run nimbly, briskly, and without fatigue, not only in the lowlands and on the plain, but upon the high places and all difficult things, and that not while I am grieving or groaning, but while I am singing in the Psalms with jubilation and thanksgiving. Concerning which St. Jerome says in Ps. XVII: Just as hinds tread upon thorns with their feet and leap over woods, so the saints tread upon thorns, that is, sins, leap over woods, that is, infidelity, and approach even unto God. He who perfected my feet like the hinds', and for leaping over the impediments of this age, set me upon high places: he placed my hope in heavenly things. Although we admit that these things also refer to the liberation of the people, whose person the prophet bears in this exultation, they are nevertheless συνάλληλα (mutually related): For God sets our feet like those of hinds or hinds, and leads us upon high places, when he causes us to escape destruction nimbly and joyfully and to be placed in safety, which the faithful among the people of God in the Babylonian captivity were to hope for and expect from their Jesus, both in the corporal liberation and in the spiritual which was promised to them, so that there is no need for a double sense, but the metaphorical words should be explained generally, provided that the metaphorical reason of the expression has a place in both liberations: Meanwhile, we do not deny that these latter words properly sound of the return to the fatherland, where with Wigand, Winckelmann, Tarnovius, B. D. Himmelius: These words are taken from Ps. 18.34. The prophet compares the return from captivity to the alacrity and running of hinds or does, to show with what alacrity and promptness of spirit the Jews were to enter upon the journey from Babylon toward Jerusalem on foot and to complete it with a hurried pace. He calls the Judean fatherland his high places, not only because it was mountainous, Deut. 2. v. 10, but also because, its foundations having been laid on the holy mountains, Ps. 87. v. 1, it was exalted to the heavens on account of the true worship of God. Nothing, however, prevents applying them with Jerome and Remigius to the triumphs and hymns of the blessed, after they have trodden upon all the high places of the world, which was also done by B. Himmelius, p. 358. Then, says Jerome, whoever is found just and worthy of election will speak exulting: But I will exult in the Lord, I will rejoice in God my savior: The Lord is my strength: And as if placed by God upon the consummation of the age, so that he may afterwards ascend to higher things and be led by God to the highest, he will say: And he will set my feet unto the consummation, he will place me upon high places, so that when the prize has been set for those singing to the ἀθλοθέτη (arbiter) Jesus who first overcame in the contest, I may win in his song, and my hands will compose the cithara and the psaltery, and I will write every kind of instrument, a panegyric of the one triumphing. Remigius says: He will lead me upon my high places. He himself, however, will lead me, because this will not be effected by my strength, but by his grace. He will lead me, however, singing to the victor, that is, to Christ the triumpher over death and the Devil. He will therefore lead me upon the high places, that is, to the blessed assembly of the heavenly city which consists of angels and holy men, so that, being mingled and joined with them, I may sing to the victor with the angels: GLORIA IN EXCELSIS DEO. Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 19. DEVS DOMINVS FORTITVDO MEA] Præsidium meum.

ET PONET PEDES MEOS QVASI CERVO- RVM] Efficiet ut ego evadam istam internecionem.

ET SVPER EXCELSA MEA DEDVCET ME] Ire me faciet ad montes meos: id est, qui me servent. Allusio ad HistoriamGen. XIX. 17. quo spectat & locus Matt. XXIV. 16.

VICTOR IN PSALMIS CANENTEM] Magistro fidium mearum: supple tradidi hoc carmen aptandum fi- dibus. Ps. IV. in principio.

Quod ad nomen ישעי, etsi id commune sit, accipi tamen potest ut proprium, quum nomen illud commune Jesu nostro in S. literis, utpote Genes. XLIX. 15. Ps. XIV. ult, Esa. XLIX. 6. & alibi appro- prietur, atq; ab illo etiam Jesus nuncupetur Matth. I. 21. Non ergo indiget hoc loco vulgata emenda- tione, quam quumPapa & Concilium Tridentinum canonizarit, rejicere Grotius nequit. Et nullum est gaudium in Domino, nisi quod fideles concipiunt in Deo Jesu suo: extra quem nulla est salus, Act. IV. 12. idem etiam est fortitudo nostra: uti profitentur de ipso fideles Ef. XLV. 28. In Domino fortitudo no- stra. Unde recte Hieron. ad h.l. Nullam aliam, nisi in Christo habebo virtutem, & cunctas legis justitias quis- quiliis comparabo. In eodem & per eundemPropheta & fideles omnes, quorum personam illic gerit, gaudere, lætari atq; exultare unice poterant in me- diis istis calamitatibus & perturbationibus, certi de salute per ipsum præstanda Phil. IV. 4. Non ma- le hic Cornel. à Lapide: Habacuc ergo in spiritu præ- videns, Josue, qui eduxit Ebræos ex Ægypto, & Cyrum, qui eosdem de Babylone liberavit tam re, quam nomine fuisse typos Jesu Christi, adeog banc liberationem & salutem populo Dei attulisse virtute divinitatis & me- ritis humanitatis Jesu Christi: denig, ipsum longe ma- jorem, æternamg, liberationem & salutem nascen- do, generi humano allaturum, exultans in spiritu ju- bilat, nomeng̃, ejus Jesus, sexcentis annis ante ortum ejus prophetabat, & nominat, cum eog̃ diffuaviatur: quia prævidebat se & nos per eum liberandos ab ho- stibus omnibus à dæmone, peccato, concupiscentia, car- ne, mundo, inferno, ac omni gratia, gloria, salute & fe- licitate cumulandos. Et iterum: porro propheta hic exultat & triumphat non in se, sed in Domino, dicens: Deus Dominus fortitudo mea. sicut enim aërislumen est sol; nec interest ut cum hoc lumen innatum ei sit, an à sole mutuatum, modo ita ei promtum sit & ad ma- num ac si ei esset innatum: Sic nos Dei & Jesu viri- bus utimur, ac si essent nostræ, ideoque ipse est forti- tudo nostra. Quid autem hæc ejus fortitudo in nobis efficit? Ponet, inquit, pedes meos qs. cervorum, ut impigre alacriter & sine fatigatione currant, non solum in infimis & in planitie, sed super excelsa & diffici- lia quæq; idq; me non dolente aut gemente, sed in Psal- mis cum jubilo & gratiarum actione canente. Quo de S. Hieronymus in Psal. XVII. Sicut cervi calcant pe- dibus spinas, & transiliunt sylvas, ita sancti calcant spinas, id est, peccata, transiliunt sylvas, id est, infideli- tatem, & subeunt usq́, ad Deum. Qui perfecit pedes meos tanquam cervorum, ac transilienda seculi hujus impedimenta, super excelsa statuit me: spem meam in cœlestibus collocavit. Quanquam vero admittamus hæc etiam referri ad liberationem po- puli, cujus personam gerit in hac exultatione pro- pheta, ea tamen συνάλληλα sunt: Nam ponit Deus pedes nostros, tanquam cervorum, vel cervarum, & su- per excelsa deducit nos, cum facit, ut alacres & læti interitum effugiamus & in tuto collocemur, quod fideles in populo Dei in captivitate Babylonica sperare & expectare habebant à Jesu suo, tum in cor- porali liberatione tum in spirituali quæ ipsis promissa fuit, ut sic gemino sensu opus non sit, sed verba me- taphorica generaliter explicanda veniant, siquidem in utraque liberatione ratio metaphorica locutio- nis locum habeat: Interim non abnuimus hæc ver- ba posteriora de reductione in patriam proprie sona- re, ubi cum Wigando, Winckelmanno, Tarnovio, B. D. Himmelius: Hæc verba desumta sunt ex Psal. 18.34. Comparat autem propheta reditum ex captivitate a- lacritati & cursui cervorum seu cervarum, ut ostendat, quanta animi alacritate & promtitudine Iudæi è Ba- bylone Hierosolymam versus iter pedibus sint ingres- suri festinog̃ cursu confecturi. Iudæam autem patriam excelsa sua vocat, non solum quia montosa fuit Deut. 2. v. 10. verum etiam quod fundamentis ejus positis in montibus sanctis Psal. 87. v. 1. propter verum Dei cul- tum ad cœlos usq̃ exaltata. Nil tamen prohibet ea cum Hieronymo & Remigio applicare ad triumphos, & hymnos beatorum, postquam calcaverint excelsa mundi quæq; quod à B. Himmelio etiam factum p. 358. Tunc inquit Hieronymus, quicung̃ justus & ele- ctione dignus inventus fuerit, loquetur exultans: Ego autem in Domino exultabo, gaudebo in Deo salu- tari meo: Dominus fortitudo mea: Et quasi posi- tus à Deo super consummationem seculi, ut postea ad superiora conscendat, & à Deo educatur ad sum- mum, dicet: Et ponet pedes meos in consumma- tionem, super excelsa imponet me, ut cum ἀθλοθέ- τη Jesu qui primus agone superavit præmium fuerie cantantibus positum, ego vincam in carmine ejus, & manus meæ component citharam & psalterium, & o- mne organorum genus scribamq́ panegyricum trium- phantis. Remigius deducet, inquit, me super excelsa mea. Ipse autem deducet me, quia hæc non mea vir- tus efficiet, sed ejus gratia. Deducet autem me canen- tem victori, id est, Christo triumphatori mortis & Diaboli. Deducet ergo me super excelsa, hoc est, ad beatam supernæ civitatis frequentiam quæ ex an- gelis & sanctis hominibus constat, ut illis admixtus atq́ conjunctus canam victori cum angelis: GLO- RIA IN EXCELSIS DEO. Amen.

# Zephaniah

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
In the name of God. Annotations on Sophonias. Preface.

Sophonias, from צפן (he hid) and יה (that is, GOD), is said by some to mean 'he whom GOD has hidden and protected' (Psalm 27:5); according to Jerome, 'the secret or hidden thing of GOD,' as if to say 'GOD's Secretary'; likewise 'Speculator of the Lord' from צפה (he watched), though the former etymology is to be preferred on account of the spelling of the name. He is the last of those who, among the minor Prophets, foretold the Babylonian captivity to the Jews; he prophesies both legal threats, primarily concerning the future destruction of Jerusalem and the ruin of the entire kingdom, so that he might recall the impious to repentance and keep the faithful in piety, so that they might escape punishments or experience milder ones; yet he does not neglect judgments against foreigners, whom the Jews looked upon; and he adds a promise that the Church will not be utterly cast away, but rather restored through the Messiah and enriched by the calling of the Gentiles, and that all its true members will be endowed with the remission of sins through this their King, while their enemies will be restrained or destroyed.

There are two parts: The former is legal, partly penitential, where in chapter I there is a threatening of judgment against the Jews, and in chapter II a recall of the Jews to repentance, with examples of foreigners proposed. It is partly ἐπανορθωτικὴ (corrective), where Jerusalem is most severely rebuked for impenitence, because it is willing neither to obey nor to trust in the Lord; the tyranny and injustice of the Princes and Magistrates, the perversity of the Prophets, Levites, and Priests, and the stubborn disobedience of all against GOD are reproved; and extermination is declared from chapter III up to verse 7. The latter is Evangelical, from verse 8 of chapter III to the end, concerning the destruction of the enemies of the Church and the propagation of the kingdom of Christ, on account of which joy is intimated to the daughter of Zion and to Israel in the Messiah, King and Savior.

Latin:

I. N. ANNOT AD SOPH PRÆLOQ

SOPHONIAS à צפן abscondit & יה id est, DEUS, quem abscon- dit & protexit DEUS (Psalm. XXVII. 5.) juxta quosdam di- citur, Hieronymo arcanum vel absconditum DEI, q. d. DEI Secretarium, item Speculator Domini à צפה spe- culatus est, cujus tamen prius etymon ob scriptio- nem nominis præferendum. Ultimus est eorum, qui inter minores Prophetas Judæis captivitatem Babylonicam prædixere, tum minas legales, de futuro imprimis Hierosolymæ exitio regnique totius excidio vaticinatur, ut impios ad pœnitentiam re- vocet, fideles in pietate contineat, quo pœnas ef- fugiant aut mitiores experiantur: non neglectis tamen Judiciis contra exteros, quos Judæi respicie- bant; & addita promissione, de non abjicienda pe- nitus, imo instauranda per Messiam Ecclesia & vo- catione gentium locupletanda, omnibusque veris e- jusdem membris remissione peccatorum per i- stum Regem suum dotandis, hostibus vero eorum compescendis, aut perimendis.

Partes duæ sunt: Prior legalis, partim pœni- tentialis ubi cap. I. Judicii contra Judæos commina- tio, & cap. II. Judæorum ad pœnitentiam, propositis exteris exemplis, revocatio habetur. Partim ἐπανορ- ϑωτικὴ ubi Hierosolyma ob impœnitentiam gra- vissime redarguitur, quod nec parere nec Domino confidere velit; Principum & Magistratus tyrannis & injustitia, Prophetarum, Levitarum, Sacerdotumque perversitas, omnium adversus DEUM inobedien- tia contumax reprehenditur; & exterminium in- dicitur cap. III. usque ad v. 7. Posterior est Evange- lica à v. 8. cap. III. usque ad finem de hostium Ec- clesiæ deletione, regni vero Christi propagatione, ob quam gaudium filiæ Zionis & Israeli intimatur in Mes- sia Rege & Salvatore.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. LEGAL. CHAPTER I. Threatening of Judgment.

The Prophet intimates the abduction of the idolatrous Jews, and indicates that the day of the destruction and slaughter of the city of Jerusalem, on account of luxury, rapine, and carnal security, along with miserable pillaging and devastation, is imminent, like a day of smoke and darkness and extermination. Zephaniah terrifies the Hebrews who cling to the dregs.

Verse 1. THE WORD OF THE LORD WHICH CAME TO SOPHONIAS] A revelation made to Sophonias; צפניה is 'the secret of God,' according to the interpreter Jerome. From the same origin comes the name of the woman Pœna in Livy, Punic for צפן איש בה, that is, 'the secret of the husband remains in her,' supply 'remains'.

That Sophonias received the office of prophesying from his parents by a kind of hereditary right, because his father, grandfather, and other ancestors are listed in the title, some gather from the tradition of the Hebrews, that whatever Prophet has his father or grandfather placed in the title, his father and grandfather were also Prophets. But that tradition lacks reason, nor can it be confirmed by induction. Nor is King Hezekiah, whom R. Joseph Kimchi and R. Abraham make the great-grandfather of Sophonias, a Prophet.

QUIUM.

was. Although that opinion of theirs is uncertain. Since it is not at all certain that he had another son besides Manasseh. See 2 Kings 20:21, 1 Chronicles 3:13, and Josephus, Antiquities, Book 10, Chapter 3. There is no doubt, however, that the Prophet was born of an illustrious lineage, whose ancestors are recounted so extensively.

IN THE DAYS OF JOSIAH, THE SON OF AMON, KING OF JUDAH] A good king, and one who indeed restored sacred things according to the law and removed public impediments as much as he could: but he could not fully heal the domestic superstitions of each person and the depraved morals of the people. See Isaiah 57. God took away every excuse from the Jews: they used to say: the kings forced us to do this and that: the answer is ready: Josiah did not force you: nay, as much as he could, he turned you away from those morals: yet you persisted in doing evil.

Josiah not only purged Judah and Jerusalem from high places, groves, idols, and graven images in the twelfth year (2 Chronicles 34:3), but also bound the people in the eighteenth year with a new covenant, so that they would observe the divine law, having abjured idolatry (2 Chronicles 34). Meanwhile, it is known even from the prophecies of Jeremiah and Huldah (2 Kings 23:17, 2 Chronicles 34:25) that many still worshipped idols in secret. And therefore, the just judgment of God is here predicted to the people. Nor is there any doubt that the Prophet, by his severe threats, greatly aided the pious King's institution, and terrified those who worshipped God not sincerely but hypocritically, and even won some over to the Lord. Theodoret rightly assigns the argument of the Prophet: that he not only predicts those things which are to happen to the city of Jerusalem and the tribe of Judah, but also indicates the final destruction of the Assyrians, as well as the neighboring nations. Then, however, he announces the recall of the people and the future salvation for all nations after the incarnation has taken place. This latter point does not appear in Grotius's Annotations, since he loves to weaken the prophecies of the Old Testament that deal with the state of the New Testament.

Latin:

PARS I. LEGALIS. CAPUT I. Judicii Comminatio.

Propheta abductionem Judæorum idololatrarum inti- mat, diemq́; excidii & interfectionis urbis Hiero- solymæ ob luxum, rapinas & securitatem carnalem cum deprædatione & vastatione miserabili, immi- nere ceu diem fumi & tenebrarum & exterminii indicat. Fecibus hærentes Zephanias terret Hebræos.

Vers. 1. VERBVM DOMINI QVOD FACTVM EST AD SOPHONIAM] Revelatio facta Sophoniæ, צפניה est arcanum Dei, interprete Hieronymo. Ab eadem origine nomen mulieri Pœnæ apud Livium, Punice צפן איש בה id est, arcanum mariti in ipsa, supple manet.

Sophoniam à parentibus hæreditario quasi jure munus prophetandi accepisse, quia Pater avus & alii majores in titulo recensentur, nonnulli è traditione Ebræorum, quod cujus Prophetæ pa- ter aut avus in titulo ponitur, ejus pater & avus etiam Prophetæ fuerint, colligunt. Sed illa traditio & ratione caret, nec ab inductione firmari potest. Neque Rex Ezechias, cujus abnepotem Sophoniam faciunt R. Ioseph Kimchi, & R. Abraham, Prophe-

QUIUM.

ta fuit. Quamvis illa eorum opinio incerta sit. Siquidem Ezechiam alium præter Manassem ha- buisse filium haud constet. Vide 2. Reg. XX. 21. 1. Par. III. 13. & Josephus l. X. Antiq. c. III. Id ta- men dubium non est, Prophetam ex stirpe illustri prognatum fuisse, cujus majores tam prolixe re- censentur.

IN DIEBUS JOSIÆ, FILII AMON, REGIS JUDÆ] Regis boni, & qui sacra quidem ex lege restituit & abstulit publica, quantum poterat, impedimenta: do- mesticas vero cujusque superstitiones, & mores populi pravos persanare non potuit. Vide Esaiam LVII. Abstulit Deus omnem excusationem Judæis: solebant dicere: re- ges nos coegerunt ad hæc & ista: responfio parata est: Jo- sia vos non coegit: imo quantum potuit, vos ab illis mo- ribus avertit: tamen perstitistis male agere.

Josias non tantum Juda & Jerusalem ab ex- celsis lucis, simulacris & sculptilibus purgavit an- no duodecimo 2. Par. XXXIV. 3. Sed etiam po- pulum anno XIIX. novo pacto, ut legem divinam, abjurata idololatria, observaret, adstrinxit 2. Paral. XXXIV. Interim multos clam adhuc coluisse Ido- la, etiam è Jeremiæ & Oldæ prophetiis 2. Reg. XXIII. 17. 2. Par. XXXIV. 25. notum est. Ideoque justum Dei judicium populo hic prædicitur. Neq; dubium est, Prophetam severis suis comminationi- bus multum pii Regis institutum juvisse, & eos, qui non sincere, sed hypocritice Deum coluere, terruis- se plurimum: nonnullos etiam Domino lucratum esse. Argumentum Prophetæ Theodorets recte affi- gnat: quod non solum prædicat ea, quæ urbi Jerusa- lem & tribui Iuda eventura sint, sed etiam Assyriis ultimam cladem indicet, ut & nationibus finitimis. Deinde vero populi revocationem & omnibus genti- bus post factam incarnationem futuram salutem præ- nunciet. Quod postremum apud Grotium, quum amet vaticinia V. Test. enervare, quæ de statu N. T. agunt, in Annotatis ejus non comparet.

## 1:2
Verse 2. I WILL UTTERLY CONSUME ALL THINGS FROM OFF THE LAND, SAITH THE LORD] That is, I will sweep everything away, even with the dust, as the saying goes,

Latin:

Vers. 2. CONGREGANS CONGREGABO OMNIA A FACIE TERRÆ DICIT DOMINUS] Id est, omnia averram cum pulvisculo, ut dici solet,

## 1:3
Verse 3. MAN AND BEAST, I WILL CONSUME THE FOWLS OF THE HEAVEN AND THE FISHES OF THE SEA] For both birds and fish desert places that stink from corpses. Jerome on this passage: That when cities are laid waste and men are killed, there is also a solitude and scarcity of beasts, and of birds and fish, Illyria is a witness, Thrace is a witness, the soil in which I was born (that is, Pannonia) is a witness, where, except for the sky and the earth and growing briars and thickets of woods, everything perishes.

AND THE RUINS OF THE WICKED SHALL BE] In the Hebrew: those stumbling blocks with the wicked: that is, the idols with their worshippers.

AND I WILL CUT OFF MAN FROM OFF THE FACE OF THE LAND] I will cause it so that none are seen, with some killed and others deported.

Thus, with Jerome, most interpreters—Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, and more recent ones—understood this concerning the particular judgment impending upon the land of Judah. Cocceius, however, preferred to take these things as referring to the universal judgment of the world and the consummation of the age: the words of Zephaniah, he says, do not need to be interpreted short of the fullness of their meaning, and they are more conveniently explained as referring to the last judgment and the consummation of the world. And this is because of the particular judgments which he subsequently explains distinctly. But the distribution is to be noted. First, he says 'all things.' Then he specifies men, cattle, birds, fish. Again, men under a double category he proposes: Of the wicked, and understand it universally also of the righteous. This judgment is hinted at also by Balaam in Num. XXIV. 17. A scepter shall rise out of Israel and shall destroy all the children of Seth, that is, Christ shall erect a kingdom, which shall progress even to the abolition of all flesh, so that His kingdom and the new creation may remain.

Latin:

Vers. 3. HOMINEM ET PECUS, CONGREGANS VOLATILIA COELI ET PISCES MARIS] Nam & aves & pisces loca deferunt à cadaveribus fœtentia. Hie- ronymus ad hunc locum: Vastatis urbibus, hominibusque interfectis, solitudinem & raritatem bestiarum quoq; fieri, & volatilium pisciumq; testis Illyrium est, testis Thracia, te- stis, in quo ortus sum, solum (id est, Pannonia) ubi præter cœlum, & terram, & crescentes vepres, & condensa sylvarum cuncta pereunt.

ET RUINÆ IMPIORUM ERUNT] In Hebræo: ea offendicula cum impiis: id est, idola cum suis cultoribus.

ET DISPERDAM HOMINES A FACIE TER- RÆ] Faciam, ut nulli conspiciantur, aliis interfectis, aliis deportatis.

Ita cum Hieronymo pleriq; Interpp. Theodore- tus, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, & recentiores de judicio particulari terræ Iudææ imminente, intel- lexere. Coccejus tamen maluit hæc de judicio mun- di universali & consummatione seculi accipere: verba Zephaniæ, inquit, nihil necesse est citra plenitu- dinem sensus interpretari, & commodius de ultimo judicio, & consummatione mundi exponuntur. Idq; propter particularia judicia, quæ deinceps exponit di- stincte. Est autem notanda distributio. Primo di- cit omnia. Tum specificat homines, pecora, volu- cres, pisces. Rursus homines sub duplici genere proponit : Improborum, & universaliter intellige etiam Justorum. Hoc judicium innuit & Bileam Num. XXIV. 17. Surget sceptrum ex Israele & di- ruet omnes filios Sethi, h,e. Christus regnum eriget, quod proficiet usq, ad abolitionem omnis carnis, ut maneat regnum ejus & nova creatio.

## 1:4
Vers. 4. AND I WILL STRETCH OUT MY HAND UPON JUDAH] I will show my power against the two tribes, just as I showed it against the other ten.

AND I WILL CUT OFF FROM THIS PLACE] From Judea.

THE REMNANT OF BAAL] Those hidden ones, which Josiah, although he had striven much, had not been able to remove.

AND THE NAMES OF THE CHEMARIM] Of the Camilli. Which name was Tyrian, it came from the Tyrians to the Tyrrhenians, with the ת changed into L. It signifies ministers of the gods, according to the interpretation of Servius on the XIth Aeneid. See 2 Kings XXIII. 4.

WITH THE PRIESTS] He calls those priests who were indeed of the Aaronic stock, but were secretly devoting effort to idols, Ezek. VIII. XXII. 26. XLIV. 10.

By the remnant of Baal, Jerome and Hugo understand the Jews surviving after the capture of Jerusalem; but the Prophet is speaking of the removal of idolatrous and superstitious worship by the Chaldeans. The LXX call the הכמרים priests. But since the ministers of idols of a lower order are designated, the Vulgate has not interpreted it badly as 'aedituos' (temple-wardens) here, and in Ps. X. 5. They are named from כמר which is to blacken, to scorch, because they were clothed in black garments, dark or dusky, as Pagninus and Vatablus hold: others, because of the preservation of fire, call them 'ignitos' (fiery), burning, like the Pyrites in Strabo, book XV of his Geography, from burning or offering incense; others from the stigmata which they branded upon their bodies; some, with Elias Levita in his Lexicon, wish them to be called contracted or folded up, because they were confined in cloisters; others from revolving, because they performed sacred rites by revolving themselves in certain dances. Compare 2 Kings XXIII. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET EXTENDAM MANUM MEAM SU- PER JUDAM] Vim meam ostendam adversus duas tri- bus, sicut adversus decem alias ostendi.

ET DISPERDAM DE LOCO HOC] De Judæa.

RELIQUIAS BAAL] Illas latentes, quas Josias, quanquam multum connifus, auferre non potuerat.

ET NOMINA ÆDITUORUM] Camillorum. Quod nomen erat Tyrium, à Tyriis ad Tyrrhenos venit, mutata ת in L. Significat deorum ministros, interprete Setvio ad XI. Æneidos. Vide 2. Reg. XXIII. 4.

CUM SACERDOTIBUS] Sacerdotes vocat eos, qui ex stirpe quidem erant Aaronica : sed clam idolis o- peram dabant Ezech. VIII. XXII. 26. XLIV. 10.

Per reliquias Baal Hieronymus & Hugo intel- ligunt Judæos post captam Hierosolymam super- stites : sed Propheta loquitur de tollendo cultu ido- lolatrico & superstitioso per Chaldæos. הכמרים LXX. ἱερεῖς vocant. Sed quum ministri idolo- rum inferioris ordinis designentur, non male Vul- gatus ædituos interpretatus est hic, & Ps. X. 5. dicti sunt à כמר quod est denigrare,adurere,quod nigris vestibus,atris pullisve induerentur,ut volunt Pa- gninus & Vatablus : alii ob ignis asservationem igni- tos, ardentes, uti Pyrites apud Strabonem l. XV. Geograph. ab adurendo, seu adolendo thure, alii à Stigmatibus,quæ corpori suo inurebant, nonnulli cum Elia Thesbita in Lexic. q. contractos,convolutos dictos volunt,quod claustris conclusi fuerint: alii à revolvendo, quod certis saltationibus se revolven- do sacra fecerint. Confer. 2. Reg. XXIII. 5.

## 1:5
Vers. 5. AND THEM THAT WORSHIP UPON THE HOUSETOPS THE HOST OF HEAVEN] They worshipped the stars on their roofs, 2 Kings XXIII. 12.

Albertus Magnus understands by the host of heaven images of the Sun, Moon, and stars painted on the roofs, but most others rightly wish the stars themselves to be designated, which were forbidden to be worshipped in Deut. IV. 19; which rite some conjecture they received from the Persians, from Strabo, book XV of his Geography.

AND WORSHIP AND SWEAR BY THE LORD, AND SWEAR BY MELCHOM] They bow down toward the ark, and they bow down before idols; they mix the legitimate worship of God with profane worships, like those of whom 1 Kings XVIII. 21 speaks. Melchom is Moloch, that is, their god; for from kings the Ammonites and other nations had made gods, and had transferred them to the stars. See Amos V. 26.

By Malchom their King, Arias understands [it]: just as oaths elsewhere have, the King lives, likewise your soul lives O King: but the context teaches that the discourse here is about idols. And therefore others commonly understand the idol of the Ammonites.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET EOS QUI ADORANT SUPER TE- CTA MILITIAM COELI ] Astra colebant in solariis suis 2. Reg. XXIII. 12.

Albertus M. per militiam cœli imagines So- lis, Lunæ, & stellarum in tectis pictas intelligit, sed rectius astra ipsa, quæ coli prohibita sunt Deut. IV. 19. alii pleriq, omnes designari volunt: quem ritum à Persis eos accepisse nonnulli conjiciunt è Strabone l. XV. Geogr.

ET ADORANT ET JURANT IN DOMINO, ET JURANT IN MELCHOM] Procumbunt versus ar- cam : & procumbunt coram idolis : miscent cultum Dei legitimum cultibus profanis, ut illi de quibus 1. Regum XVIII. 21. Melchom est Moloch, id est, Deum suum : nam ex regibus Ammonitæ, gentesque aliæ deos fece- rant, eosque in astra retulerant. Vide Amos. V. 26.

Per Malchom Regem ipsorum intelligit Arias : uti alias juramenta habent, vivit Rex, item vivit a- nima tua ô Rex: verum de idolis hic sermonem es- se contextus docet. ideoque Ammonitarum idolum alii communiter intelligunt.

## 1:6
Vers. 6. AND WHO TURN AWAY FROM BEHIND THE BACK OF THE LORD] Who pour out prayers turned away from the Sanctuary. Ezek. 8. 26.

AND WHO HAVE NOT SOUGHT THE LORD, NOR INVESTIGATED HIM] Atheist men, who neither wish to be instructed about God, nor to pour out any prayers.

Others more correctly interpret this not only concerning prayers, but concerning universal worship, namely that some indeed left the Lord [after having been] sought and found, and turned their back to him, but others never brought themselves to seek or worship him. For it is a general accusation.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET QUI AVERTUNTUR DE POST TER- GUM DOMINI] Qui preces fundunt aversi à Sančtua- rio. Ezech. IIX. 26.

ET QUI NON QUÆSIERUNT DOMINUM, NEC INVESTIGAVERUNT EUM] Homines ἄθεοι, qui ne- que institui de Deo volunt, neque ullas preces fundere.

Alii rectius non de precibus solum, sed de u- niverso cultu interpretantur, quod nempe nonnul- li quidem Dominum quæsitum & inventum reli- querunt, eique tergum obverterunt, alii vero nunquam eum quærere, vel colere in animum in- duxerint. Generale enim est ἔγκλημα.

## 1:7
Vers. 7. BE SILENT FROM THE FACE OF THE LORD] The Greeks [say] be in awe, as Habakkuk 2. 20.

FOR THE DAY OF THE LORD IS NEAR] The day of vengeance.

THE LORD HAS PREPARED A SACRIFICE] He will delight in the slaughter of the wicked.

MORE THAN OF CATTLE] Isa. 34. 6. Jer. 46. 10. Ezek. 39. 17.

HE HAS SANCTIFIED HIS CALLED ONES] He will call together his guests: just as men are accustomed to be called to a feast. The guests here are birds and wild beasts and dogs.

BE SILENT, i.e., tremble before the face of the Lord, and submit yourselves to him, and show reverence with holy silence: A metaphor taken from those who, having been conquered, do not dare to speak. Job 39. 37. Rom. 3. 19. Silence may also be distinguished in this way, that at one time it is of attention and expectation, Ezek. 29. 15, at another time of reverence and veneration, as in this place and Zech. 2, at another time of confession and humiliation, as Job 39. 37. By the sanctified and called, Jerome, Theodoret, and Haymo and others more correctly understand soldiers, although the Chaldean and Vatablus wish birds and wild beasts to be designated, whom Grotius followed. Cocceius's interpretation concerning the day of the incarnation of the Lord and his propitiatory sacrifice is foreign. This can be understood in emphasis and more lightly. More lightly, so that זבח may be a feast, or a ready occasion for satisfying one's desire: and the called are those whom God has destined to bring to this, that they may satisfy themselves in any way: their sanctification, the preparation and segregation for this feast to be exhibited by God, and the ministry to be performed for the glory of God, even if not by their intention, is thus used in Ezek. 39. 17, 18, 19, 20. Rev. 19. 17. In emphasis, so that we may understand the true Sacrifice, through which sins ought to be expiated: concerning which, by participating in faith, those whom God calls to this, that is, brings by calling, may feast: namely those whom he sanctifies by the sprinkling of the blood of that victim and by his spirit. Such as were even then and have been from every age, who hoped for the salvation of Israel. Concerning whom Psalm 50. 5 says: Gather to me those devoted to me, making my covenant upon sacrifice, namely in the blood of the covenant, Zech. 9. 11, or of the Testament, Matt. 26. 28. Hebr. IX. 16. Certainly that emphatic meaning is most appropriate to the matter: and if we accept it in this way, then in the following verse there will be an antanaclasis in the word זבח. Thus, therefore, the day of Jehovah will be the time of the visitation of the people through grace and the manifestation of God in the flesh. These things, I say, are foreign, because the Prophet himself explained the sacrifice and the day of the Lord otherwise.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SILETE A FACIE DOMINI] ἐυλαβεῖσθε Græci, ut Habacuc. II. 20.

QUIA JUXTA EST DIES DOMINI] Dies vindictæ.

PRÆPARAVIT DOMINUS HOSTIAM] Delecta- bitur occidione impiorum..

MAGIS QUAM PECUDUM] Esa. XXXIV. 6. Jerem. XLVI. 10. Ezech.XXXIX. 17.

SANCTIFICAVIT VOCATOS SUOS] Convoca- bit convivas suos : sicut homines ad diem festum convocari solent. Convivæ hic sunt aves & feræ & canes.

SILETE, q. d. contremiscite ante faciem Do- mini,eique vos subjicite, ac reverentiam exhibe- te sancto silentio: Metaphora ab his sumpta,qui vi- cti non audent loqui Job. XXXIX. 37. Rom. III. 19. Silentium etiam ita distinguere liceat, quod modo sit attentionis,& expectationis Ezech. XXIX.15.mo- do reverentiæ,& venerationis, ut hoc loco & Zach. II.modo confessionis & humiliationis uti Job.xxxix. 37. per sanctificatos & vocatos rectius Hieronymus, Theodoret.& Haymo & alii milites intelligunt, etsi Chaldæus & Vatablus aves & feras designari ve- lint, quos sequutus est Grotius. Aliena est Cocceji interpretatio de die ἐνσαρκώσεως Domini & sacri- ficia ejus propitiatorio. Potest hoc intelligi in empha- si & tenuius. Tenuius, ut זבח sit δεῖπνον,sive prom- pta occasio ad satiandum suam cupiditatem: & voca- ti sunt ii,quos Deus destinavit adducere ad hoc, ut se satient quovis modo: sanctificatio illorum, præpara- tio & segregatio ad hoc convivium à Deo exhiben- dum, & ministerium, ad gloriam Dei quamvis non ex intentione illorum, obeundum, sic usurpatur Ez. XXXIX.17.18.19.20. Apoc.XIX. 17. In emphasi,ut in- telligamus Sacrificium verum, per quod expiari de- beant peccata: de quo,participando in fide, epu len- tur ii,quos Deus ad hoc vocat, hoc est, vocando ad- ducit: nimirum ii, quos sanctificat fpersione san- guinis illius victimæ & spiritu suo. Quales jam tum erant & ab omni ævo fuerunt, qui salutem Israelis spe- rabant. De quibus dicit Psalmus L. 5. Congregate mihi studiosos mei,pangentes fœdus meum super sacrificio,nempe in sanguine fœderis, Zach. IX. 11. sive Testamenti Matth. XXVI. 28. Hebr. IX. 16. Certe quidem emphatica illa significatio est ad rem accommodatissima: & si hoc modo accipiamus, tum versu sequenti in voce זבח erit antanaclasis. Sic i- gitur dies Iehovæ erit tempus visitationis populi per gratiam & φανερώσεως θεῦ ἐν σαρκί.Hæc inquam, ἀλλότρια sunt, quia aliter sacrificium diemque Domini exposuit Propheta ipse.

## 1:8
Vers. 8.

I WILL VISIT UPON THE PRINCES] I will decree punishments upon the princes.

AND UPON THE KING'S SONS] You have the fulfillment of both sayings in 2 Kings XXV. 7, 21.

AND UPON ALL WHO ARE CLOTHED IN FOREIGN GARMENTS] The Greeks: ἐπὶ πάντας τὲς ἐνδεδυμένως ἐνδύματα ἀλλότρια. Things are often called foreign which are forbidden by law, such as masculine garments on women, feminine on males, because in that way they would worship Mars and Venus through idolatry, as we said in Deuteronomy XXII, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

VISITABO SUPER PRINCIPES] Supplicia in principes decernam.

ET SUPER FILIOS REGIS] Utriusque dicti complementum habes 2. Reg. XXV.7.21.

ET SUPER OMNES QUI INDUTI SUNT VE- STE PEREGRINA]Græci: ἐπὶ πάντας τὲς ἐνδεδυμένως ἐν- δύματα ἀλλότρια. aliena sæpe vocantur, quæ lege sunt vetita, qualia sunt vestimenta masculina in feminis, femi- niua in maribus, quod eo modo idololatriæ colerent Martem & Venerem, ut diximus Deuter, XXII, 5.

## 1:9
Vers. 9.

UPON EVERYONE WHO ARROGANTLY STEPS OVER THE THRESHOLD] Those who leap over the threshold of the temple. This was an ancient custom of the Philistines, 1 Sam. V. 5. Thus also among the Romans, new brides used to leap over the thresholds of houses. The Chaldean also interpreted this passage in this way.

WHO FILL THE HOUSE OF THE LORD THEIR GOD WITH INIQUITY AND DECEIT] In the Hebrew: They fill the house of their lords, namely of the kings and princes, with things acquired through violence and injury.

Lyranus, as well as Arias and Vatablus, explained it as referring to the sons of Zedekiah, who were slaughtered before his eyes.
