But Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, and Cocceius understand the sons of Josiah, of whom Jehoahaz was led away into captivity by Pharaoh, Jehoiakim led into Babylon, Jehoiakim killed by the Chaldeans, Zedekiah blinded. However, because the day of destruction is designated as the day of the sacrifice, in which destruction of Jerusalem there was no other King than Zedekiah, whose sons were also slaughtered, we easily prefer the former opinion. Nebuchadnezzar made no sacrifice out of the sons of Josiah. And here the destruction of the princes and the King's sons is joined, whom Nebuchadnezzar killed at the same time, 2 Kings XXV. 7. By those clothed in foreign garments, the Jews are more correctly understood, who out of levity used the clothing of the Gentiles, Egyptian, Tyrian, etc., as Jerome explained, imitating with their clothes also their customs, namely the idolatries of the Gentiles. Conf. Ez. XXIII. 12. 13. Nor is this discourse about the superstition of the Ashdodites, by whom the god Dagon was worshipped, who out of reverence for the temple did not tread upon the threshold, because that idol was cut off at the threshold, 1 Sam. V. 11. For it is certain that the Jews abhorred these as enemies. The Chaldean, Pagninus, Arias, Vatablus & the Tigurines, translate from the Hebrew thus: I will visit every one that leaps over the threshold in that day, who fill the house of their Lords with rapine: as if the ministers of the Princes were being taxed, because they leap over the threshold of their neighbors, that they may steal their goods, and also of their lords, that they may hide their thefts there: or divide those things with them: Coccejus wishes to note the audacity of leaping over the threshold of the temple with violence & fraud. Conf. Eccles. IV. 17. Others, because they offer to God things obtained by rapine & frauds. But the authentic text does not speak of God, but of Lords.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

SUPER OMNEM QUI ARROGANTER IN- GREDIETUR SUPER LIMEN] Qui limen templi transi- liunt. Hic ab antiquo mos Philistinorum 1.Sam.V.5. Sic & apud Romanos domuum limina transiliebant novæ nu- ptæ. Sic sumsit hunc locum & Chaldæus.

QUI COMPLENT DOMUM DOMINI DEI SUI INIQUITATE ET DOLO] In Hebræo: Domum dominorum suorum, regum scilicet & Principum domos implent rebus per vim & injuriam quæsitis.

De filiis Sedeciæ,Lyranus, etiam Arias, & Va- tablus exposuere, qui in oculis ejus jugulati sunt. Verum Hieronymus, Theodoretus, Remigius, Cocce- jus filios Josiæ intelligunt, è quibus Ioachaz abdu- ctus fuit in captivitatem à Pharaone, Ioachim ductus in Babylonem, Jojakim à Chaldæis occisus, Se- dekias excæcatus. Cæterum quia dies excidii, dies Hostiæ designatur, in quo Hierosolymitano excidio non alius Rex fuit quam Sedekias, quo mactati et- jam filii ejus sunt, facile priorem sententiam præfe- rimus. E filiis Josiæ Nabuchodonosor nullam fecit hostiam. Et conjungitur hic excidium Principum & filiorum Regis, quos simul occidit Nabuchodo- nosor 2. Reg. XXV.7. Per indutos veste peregrina rectius Judæi intelliguntur, qui ex levitate vestitu gentilium utebantur,Ægyptio, Tyrio &c. uti expo- fuit Hieronymus, vestibus etiam mores, puta idolo- latrias gentilium imitantes. Conf. Ez. XXIII. 12. 13. Neque de superstitione Azotiorum, quibus Deus Dagon colebatur, qui ex reverentia templi limen non calcabant, quod idolum illud in limine trun- catum fit 1. Sam. V. 11. hic sermo est. Ab his enim ceu hostibus abhorruisse Judæos constat. Chal- dæus, Pagninus, Arias, Vatablus & Tigurini, ex E- bræo sic vertunt: Visitabo omnem transilientem limen in die illa, qui implent domum Dominorum suorum rapina: quasi taxentur ministri Principum, quod tum limen proximorum transiliant, ut eorum bo- na furentur, tum dominorum suorum, ut ibi furta recondant: vel cum illis ea dividant: Coccejus no- tari vult audaciam insiliendi limen templi cum violen- tia & fraude. Conf. Eccles. IV. 17. Alii, quod ra- pinis & fraudibus partas Deo offerant. At tex- tus authenticus non de Deo loquitur, sed de Do- minis.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. FROM THE FISH GATE] There shall be a howling in the whole city, which he describes from three most noble parts. The fish gate was in the city of David 2. Par. XXXIII. 14.

AND A GREAT DESTRUCTION FROM THE HILLS] From the palace & the temple.

The Chaldeans seem to have first burst into the city through the fish gate, which looked toward the sea, so that fish might be imported through it. If you wish to believe Adrichomius, it is also called the gate of David, because it is nearest to the tower of David, and the gate of the merchants, because merchandise from Bethlehem, Hebron, Gaza, Ethiopia & Egypt was brought in through it. Villalpandus, however, locates that gate not to the West with Adrichomius, but to the North: so that the Chaldeans might rush in through it. Cornel. à Lap. thinks they broke in by both ways, namely that having broken through the northern wall of the city they penetrated into the second, and having broken through the western fish gate they burst into the valley of Mello, just as into the lower city, which was called the daughter of Sion: for this gate was near to both, and opened to both approaches; and therefore Sophonias signifies that there would be a howling in both places, to wit, as much in the fish gate as in the second. The voice of a cry from the fish gate, and a howling from the second and a great destruction from the hills, to wit, of Sion and the temple and other similar places, to which, as being more fortified, the Jews fled from the second and outer region when the city was captured by the Chaldeans; but they were caught, crushed, and slaughtered there by the pursuing Chaldeans. Thus St. Jerome & Theodoret. Coccejus noted Grotius, whose passage we transcribe: The fish gate was in the lower city around the northern corner of the eastern side. Junius contends that it pertains to the city of David from 2 Chron. xxxiii. 14. which Grotius follows rashly. It is said there: Manasseh built an outer wall of the city of David, (understand on the southern side above the valley of Hinnom) to the West as far as Gihon, (the mountain Gihon was situated to the west of the city. Therefore it cannot be translated, as Junius translates; to the west of Gihon. The city & walls were to the east of Gihon) in the valley, that is, as far as the valley, in which the mountain Gihon terminates: (This is the corner of the western side to the South) and where one enters into the fish gate, that is, the wall was continued from the valley of the mountain Gihon through the western and northern side to the fish gate in the corner of the North and East: and it goes around to Ophel, to wit, through the eastern side. For Ophel was in the corner of the East and South. Thus Nehem. III. 3. is 1. The sheep gate near the Temple, on the side of the East. There follows the tower of Meah, and Hananeel. Then 2. The fish gate. It is impossible for it to be placed now to the West; since Nehemiah goes around from the side of the East through the North to the West; and returns through the south to the sheep gate. Thus by going backward the fish gate, the tower of Hananeel, and Meah, and the sheep gate are continued Neh. XII. 39. Therefore between the sheep gate and the fish gate no other at least notable gate intervenes; But two towers. There is no need to place the fish gate to the West, for that reason, because the sea is to the West. Nay, the corner of the East and North is far more suitable for a fish market, because the Jordan and the Sea of Tiberias are near there, and goods were conveniently brought there to Tyre. See Nehem. XIII. 16. Therefore Jerome is also mistaken, who wishes to lead the fish gate, which the sons of Asnaa built in Nehem. III., to Diospolis and Joppa, and that it was nearer to the sea than all the ways of Jerusalem. So much for him.

Latin:

Vers. 10. A PORTA PISCIUM] Erit ululatus in tota urbe, quam describit ex tribus partibus nobilissimis. Porta piscium erat in urbe Davidis 2. Par. XXXIII. 14.

ET CONTRITIO MAGNA A COLLIBUS] A palatio & templo.

Per portam piscium primo in urbem irruisse videntur Chaldæi, quæ spectabat mare, ut per eam pisces importarentur. Si Adrichom. credere vis, dicta etiam porta David, quod turri Davidis pro- xima sit, & porta negotiatorum, quod per eam mer- ces à Bethlehem, Hebron, Gaza, Æthiopia & Ægy- pto inveherentur. Vilalpandus tamen eam portam non ad Occidentem cum Adrichonico, sed ad Se- ptentrionem locat: ut per eam ingruerent Chal- dæi. Cornel. à Lap. utraque via eos irrupisse pu- tat, nimirum Aquilonari urbis muro dirupta pene- trasse in secundam, & Occidentali porta piscium effracta irrupisse in vallem Mello, æque ac in civi- tatem inferiorem, quæ filia Sion dicebatur: utrique enim vicina erat hæc porta, & ad utrumq; aditum pandebat; ideoque Sophonias utrobique, scil. tam in porta piscium, quam in secunda ululatum fore significat. Vox clamoris à porta piscium, & ululatus à secunda & contritio magna à collibus scil. Sionis & templi aliisque similibus, ad quos utpote muni- tiores, capta à Chaldæis urbe, ex secunda & ex- tima regione confugerunt Judæi; sed à Chaldæis persequentibus ibidem comprehensi, contriti & trucidati sunt. Ita S. Hieron. & Theodor. Notavit Grotium Coccejus, cujus locum adscribimus: Por- ta piscium fuit in civitate inferiore circa angulum A- quilonem lateris Orientalis. Iunius contendit eam pertinere ad civitatem Davidis ex 2. Chron. xxxiii. 14. quod sequitur Grotius temere. Ibi hoc dici- tur: Manasses struxit murum exteriorem civitatis Davidis,) intellige in latere Australi supra val- lem Hinnom) ad Occidentem usq́; ad Gichon, (mons Gichon situs erat ad occasum urbis. Igitur non potest verti, ut Junius vertit; ad occidentem Gihonis. Urbs & mœnia erant ad ortum Gichonis) in valle, hoc est, usq́; ad vallem, in quam mons Gi- chon terminatur: (Hic angulus lateris occidenta- lis ad Austrum) & qua intratur in portam piscium, hoc est, murus continuatus est à valle montis Gi- chon per latus Occidentale & Septentrionale ad portam piscium in angulo Aquilonis & Orientis: & circumit ad Ophel, scil. per latus Orientale. Nam Ophel erat in angulo Orientis & Austri. Sic Nehem. III. 3. est 1. Porta ovium prope Templum, in latere Orientis. Sequitur turris Meah, & Chananael. Tum. 2. Porta piscium. Impossibile est, eam jam ad Occasum collocari: quum Nehemias à latere Orientis per Aquilonem ad Occasum cir- cumeat; & per meridiem ad portam ovium regre- diatur. Sic retrocedendo porta piscium, turris Cha- naneelis, & Meah, & porta ovium continuantur Neh. XII. 39. Ergo inter portam ovium & piscium nulla alia intercedit saltem notabilis porta; Sed duæ turres. Nihil necesse est, Portam piscium ad Occasum collocare, propter eam rationem, quia ad Occasum est mare. Imo angulus Orientis & Septentrionis longe opportunior est foro pisca- rio, quia illic vicinus Jordanes, Mare Tiberiadis, & illuc Tyro commode afferebantur. Vide Ne- hem. XIII. 16. Fallitur ergo & Hieronymus, qui por- tam piscium eam, quam Nehem. III. ædificarunt filii Asnaa, vult ducere Diospolim & Joppen, & viciniorem mari fuisse inter cunctas vias Hierusa- lem. Hæc ille.

## 1:11
Vers. 11. HOWL YE INHABITANTS OF THE MORTAR] מכתש properly indeed signifies a mortar, that is, a vessel for pounding, but by similarity it is adapted to every cavity, as appears in Judg. XV. 18. The Chaldean speaks of the torrent Cedron: others interpret it of the valley of Siloam.

But the valley of Siloam, & the torrent Cedron were outside the city: But the mortar seems to have been both inside the city: whence the chasm of Mello, which is also called Tyropoeon by some, is rather understood: of which Josephus l. VI. Bell. Jud. which valley, because of its depth called a mortar, reached as far as Siloam.

ALL THE PEOPLE OF CANAAN HAVE HELD THEIR PEACE] The people of the Merchants. Who dwelt in the hollow part of the city.

Thus the word כנעך is taken in Hos. XII. 8. Others however prefer that the Israelitic people be called the people of Canaan, because it imitates the customs of that people, and is no less liable to destruction than the Amorites. Conf. c. II. 5.

THEY HAVE ALL PERISHED WRAPPED IN SILVER] All the money-changers will perish, who were, to be sure, in that same part of the city.

The covetous are more correctly understood; who do not handle or meditate upon anything other than money, and wrap themselves in it with their heart. For silver is the idol which the covetous man adores, which he consults, which he pursues through right and wrong, to which he obeys in all things, and enslaves himself as if a servant Eph. V. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ULULATÆ HABITATORES PILÆ] מכתש proprie quidem pilam, id est, mortarium signifi- cat, sed per similitudinem aptatur omni cavitati, ut appa- ret Judæ XV. 18. De torrente Cedron Chaldæus: alii de valle Siloes interpretantur.

At vallis Siloe, & torrens Cedron fuerunt ex- tra urbem: Pila autem videtur utraque intra ur- bem fuisse: unde vorago Mello, quæ etiam Tyro- pæon dicta à nonnullis potius intelligitur: de qua Joseph l. VI. Bell. Jud. quæ vallis, ob profunditatem pila dicta usq; ad Siloam pertingebat.

CONTICUIT OMNIS POPULUS CANAAN] Po- pulus Mercatorum. Qui in cava urbis parte habitabant.

Ita accipitur vox כנעך Hos. XII. 8. Alii tamen malunt populum Israeliticum populum Canaan vocari, quod illius populi mores imitetur, nec mi- nus excidio obnoxius sit, quam Amorrhæi. Conf. c. II. 5.

DISPERIERUNT OMNES INVOLUTI ARGEN- TO] Peribunt omnes argentarii, qui scilicet in eadem illa urbis erant parte.

Rectius avari intelliguntur; qui non tractant, aut meditantur aliud; quam argumentum, eique corde suo se involvunt. Argentum enim est idolum, quod adorat avarus, quod consulit, quod per fas & nefas sequitur, cui per omnia obedit, & se quasi servum mancipat Eph. V. 6.

## 1:12
Ver. 12. I WILL SEARCH JERUSALEM WITH LAMPS] The victorious Chaldeans will search out all things most diligently, even with torches applied, so that nothing may escape them. A proverbial manner of speaking Luc. XV. 8.

AND I WILL VISIT UPON THE MEN SETTLED IN THEIR LEES] Who had lived tranquilly until now, like wine which is not poured from one vessel to another, but rests upon its own lees. It is the same similitude Jer. XLVIII. 11.

WHO SAY IN THEIR HEARTS, THE LORD WILL NOT DO GOOD, AND WILL NOT DO EVIL] Who have said in their hearts: That is, who have thought heretofore that human affairs are not cared for by God: that human business is turned and driven by chance and rashly, as it is in Curtius.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SCRUTABOR JERUSALEM IN LUCER- NIS] Victores Chaldæi omnia diligentissime pervestiga- bunt, etiam facibus adhibitis, ne quid eos effugiat. Lo- quendi genus proverbiale Luc. XV. 8.

ET VISITABO SUPER VIROS DEFIXOS IN FÆCIBUS SUIS] Qui tranquille egerant hactenus, ut vinum, quod non transfunditur, sed fæcibus suis incum- bit. Est eadem similitudo Jer. XLVIII. 11.

QUI DICUNT IN CORDIBUS SUIS, NON FACIET BENE DOMINUS, ET NON FACIET MA- LE] Qui dixerunt in cordibus suis: Id est, qui cogitarunt antehac, à Deo non curari res humanas: forte ac temere humana negotia volvi, agique, ut est apud Curtium.

## 1:13
Ver. 13. AND THEIR STRENGTH SHALL BE FOR A SPOILING] Their opulence.

THEIR HOUSES INTO A DESERT] Into a solitude.

AND THEY SHALL BUILD HOUSES, AND SHALL NOT INHABIT] That is, the houses which they had built, those they shall not inhabit.

AND THEY SHALL PLANT VINEYARDS AND SHALL NOT DRINK THE WINE OF THEM] That is, they shall not drink the wine of those vineyards which they planted. Both are from Deut. XXVIII. 30. The same sense Amos V. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET ERIT FORTITUDO EORUM IN DI- REPTIONEM] Opulentia eorum.

DOMUS EORUM IN DESERTUM] In solitudi- nem.

ET ÆDIFICABUNT DOMOS, ET NON HA- BITABUNT] Id est, quas ædificaverant domos, eas non habi- tabunt.

ET PLANTABUNT VINEAS ET NON BI- BENT VINUM EARUM] Id est, earum, quas planta- runt, binearum vinum non bibent. Utrumque est ex Deut. XXIIX. 30. Idem sensus Amos V. 11.

## 1:14
Ver. 14. THE MIGHTY MAN SHALL BE TROUBLED THERE] Even the most valiant shall be crushed.

Latin:

Vers. 14. TRIBULABITUR IBI FORTIS] Conte- rentur etiam validissimi.

## 1:15
Ver. 15. A DAY OF DARKNESS AND GLOOMINESS] A black day.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DIES TENEBRARVM ET CALIGINIS] Atra dies.

## 1:16
Ver. 16. A DAY OF THE TRUMPET AND ALARM AGAINST THE FENCED CITIES] For cities are accustomed to be taken at the sound of the trumpet.

AND UPON THE HIGH CORNERS] That is, towers: which are accustomed to be in the corners of walls.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DIES TUBÆ ET CLANGORIS SUPER CIVITATES MUNITAS] Nam ad tubæ sonitum capi urbes solent.

ET SUPER ANGULOS EXCELSOS] Id est tur- res: quæ esse in angulis murorum solent.

## 1:17
Ver. 17. AND I WILL DISTRESS MEN, AND THEY SHALL WALK LIKE THE BLIND] I will afflict them with such great straits that they shall see no better than the blind where they ought to turn themselves.

THEIR BLOOD LIKE THE GROUND] Like dust, which is of no value.

AND THEIR BODIES LIKE DUNG] Here לחם, which is accustomed to signify bread, is translated as body, after the manner of the Arabs. See what we have said at Matt. XXVI. 6.

The word לַחֻם signifies flesh entirely, as in Job XX. 28, but by no means food, which Abarbenel maintained. The sense is, their unburied corpses shall be cast out like dung, i.e., they shall be buried with the burial of an ass, which God also threatened to King Jehoiakim in Jerem. XXII. 19.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET TRIBULABO HOMINES, ET AM- BULABUNT UT CÆCI] Angustiis afficiam tantis, ut non magis quam cæci videant, quo se vetere debeant.

SANGUIS EORUM SICUT HUMUS] Sicut pul- vis, qui nullius est pretii.

ET CORPORA EORUM SICUT STERCORA] Hic לחם, quod panem significare solet, vertitur corpus, more Arabum. Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. XXVI. 6.

Vox לַחֻם omnino carnem significat, uti Job XX. 28. neutiquam vero cibum, quod voluit A- barbenel. Sensus est, cadavera eorum insepulta proji- cientur, uti stercora, h. e. sepultura asini sepelientur quod etiam Deus Jojakimo Regi comminatus est Jerem. XXII. 19.

## 1:18
Verse 18. BUT ALSO THEIR SILVER AND THEIR GOLD SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO DELIVER THEM] Ezech. VII. 19.

IN THE FIRE OF HIS ZEAL] With the burning wrath of God. So also below III. 8.

HE SHALL MAKE A CONSUMMATION WITH HASTE] He calls the destruction of the Jewish Republic a consummation here.

Blessed Gerhard refers this to the consummation of the Age in his Commonplaces on the Consummation of the Age, § 7. Others refer it both to the time of the Babylonian Captivity and to the time of the Roman destruction; but this discourse is about the devastation of the land of Chaldea, as the context teaches and most interpreters acknowledge.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SED ET ARGENTUM EORUM ET AURUM NON POTERIT LIBERARE EOS] Ezech. VII. 19.

IN IGNE ZELI EJUS] Æstuante Dei ira. Sic & infra III. 8.

CONSUMMATIONEM CUM FESTINATIONE FACIET] Consummationem hic vocat Reipublicæ Judai- cæ interitum.

Hoc ad consummationem Seculi refert B. Ger- hardus in LL. CC. de Conf. Sec. §. 7. Alii & ad Ca- ptivitatis Babylonicæ, & ad excidii Romani tempus; sed hic sermo est de Chaldæa terræ vastatione: uti contextus docet, & plerique interpp. agnoscunt.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

An invitation of the Jews to repentance through examples of divine judgment.

The Prophet calls together the people and exhorts them to repentance, presenting an example of judgment against the Philistines, yet inserting a promise concerning the faithful, about the sheepfolds, the remnant of the people to be saved, and the reproaches of the Moabites and Ammonites to be avenged, so that with idols exterminated, the name of the Lord may be invoked everywhere. He also proposes judgments against the Ethiopians and Assyrians, and graphically describes the most horrible devastation of proud Nineveh. He calls them to return to their senses and offers sacred things to the nations.

Verse 1. GATHER YOURSELVES TOGETHER] Namely, for prayers, so that you may at least save your lives.

A NATION NOT DESIRABLE] A nation of no shame. For thus the Chaldeans and Rabbis use כָּסַף.

The Tigurines, Vatablus, and Coccejus translate: Search yourselves, but the Hebrew קוֹשׁ is to gather, not to search. The Chaldean renders לֹא נִכְסָף: not willing to be converted to the law. Pagninus: not desirable.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Judæorum per exempla judicii divini ad pœnitentiam invitatio.

Convocat populum & hortatur ad pœnitentiam Pro- pheta sistens exemplum judicii adversus Philistæos, inferta tamen promissione ob fideles de ovium tu- guriolis, reliquiis populi servandis, & Moabita- rum ac Ammonitarum opprobriis vindicandis, ut exterminatis idolis nomen Domini ubique invoce- tur. Proponit etiam judicia adversus Æthiopes & Assyrios, ac graphice describit devastationem su- perbæ Ninives maxime horribilem. Ad resipiscendum vocat & sacra gen- tibus offert.

Vers. 1. CONVENITE CONGREGAMINI] Nempe ad preces, ut vitam saltem salvam habeatis.

GENS NON AMABILIS] Gens nullius pudoris. Ita enim Chaldæi & Rabbini כָּסַף usurpant.

Tigurini, Vatablus & Coccejus vertunt: Scru- tamini vos ipsos, sed Ebræum קוֹשׁ congregare est, non scrutari. לֹא נִכְסָף Chaldæus reddit: nolens con- verti ad legem. Pagninus non desiderabilis.

## 2:2
Verse 2. BEFORE THE DECREE BRING FORTH AS THE CHAFF THAT PASSETH THE DAY] Before the decree (of God) brings forth the day, like chaff passing by: by which chaff they are separated from the wheat, and with the wheat saved, the chaff perishes.

The Chaldean, for the sake of illustration, added another simile: Before the decree of the house of judgment goes forth against you, and you be like chaff, which the wind blows away, and like a shadow, which passes from the sight of the day.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PRIUSQUAM PARIAT JUSSIO QUASI PULVEREM TRANSEUNTEM DIEM] Priusquam de- cretum (Dei) pariat diem, velut glumæ transeuntis: qua gluma separentur a frumento, & frumento salvo gluma pereat.

Chaldæus illustrationis causa aliam addidit si- militudinem: Antequam prodeat in vos edictum domus judicii, & similes sitis glumæ, quam perflat ven- tus, & umbræ, quæ transit a conspectu diei.

## 2:3
Verse 3. SEEK THE LORD ALL YOU MEEK OF THE EARTH] Here he turns his speech to others, that is, to the few good people among the people.

WHO HAVE WROUGHT HIS JUDGMENT] You who have followed the laws of God.

Verse 3. SEEK THE JUST, SEEK THE MEEK] In the Hebrew: Seek justice, (that is, beneficence) seek meekness: that is, entreat the clemency of God.

So indeed Jerome and Remigius. But it is taken by others as referring to justice and humility, which they ought to study. For they had already been commanded to seek God before.

IF BY ANY MEANS YOU MAY BE HIDDEN] That is, protected, as the Chaldean explains here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. QUÆRITE DOMINUM OMNES MAN- SUETI TERRÆ] Hic orationem ad alios, id est, paucos in populo bonos convertit.

QUI JUDICIUM EJUS ESTIS OPERATI] Qui Dei leges sectati estis.

Vers. 3. QUÆRITE JUSTUM, QUÆRITE MAN- SUETUM] In Hebræo: Quærite justitiam, (id est, bene- ficentiam) quærite mansuetudinem: id est, Dei clementiam exposcite.

Ita quidem Hieronymus & Remigius. Atre- ctius de justitia & humilitate accipitur, cui studere debebant. Nam Deum quærere antea jam jussi erant.

SI QUOMODO ABSCONDAMINI] Id est, pro- tegamini, ut hic explicat Chaldæus.

## 2:4
Verse 4. FOR GAZA SHALL BE DESTROYED] He shows that escapes would be most difficult, with all the surrounding places captured by the enemy. You have many of the Phoenicians and Syrians captured by Nebuchadnezzar in the fragment of Berosus, which we cited in the third book on the truth of the Christian Religion.

AZOTUS THEY SHALL CAST OUT AT NOON] The Chaldeans shall expel the Azotians in the clear day.

There were five Satrapies of the Philistines, whose metropolises were these same ones: Gaza, Ascalon, Azotus, Accaron, and Geth. In the Hebrew there is an elegant Paronomasia: עַזָּה עֲזוּבָה Gaza shall be forsaken. עֶקְרוֹן תֵּעָקֵר Accaron (named from eradicating) shall be eradicated.

Latin:

Vers. 4. QUIA GAZA DESTRUCTA ERIT] O- stendit difficillima fore effugia, omnibus circum locis ab hoste captis. Multos Phœnicum & Syrorum a Nabucho- donosoro captos habes in Berosi fragmento, quod citavi- mus ad tertium librum de veritate Religionis Christianæ.

AZOTUM IN MERIDIE EJICIENT] Azotios clara die expellent Chaldæi.

Quinq; fuerunt Satrapiæ Philistinorum, qua- rum metropoles totidem erant hæ, Gaza, Ascalon, Azotum, Accaron & Geth. In Ebræo est elegans Pa- ranomasia עַזָּה עֲזוּבָה Gaza erit derelicta. עֶקְרוֹן תֵּעָקֵר Accaron (ab eradicando dicta) eradicabitur.

## 2:5
WOE TO YOU WHO INHABIT THE LINE OF THE SEA] The maritime coast.

NATION OF THE PERDITION] The nation of the Cherethites is a part of the Philistines. See 1 Sam. 30:14 and Ezek. 25:16, from which we suppose the Cretans originated.

THE WORD OF THE LORD UPON YOU CANAAN THE LAND OF THE PHILISTINES] The copula is missing: Canaan, and the land of the Philistines. He enumerates the parts of Phoenicia.

Aquila, Theodotion, and the Fifth edition take the word כרתים as an appellative, 'a people of destruction'; the Tigurine version, 'a devastating people'; Luther similarly, 'warriors'. Furthermore, the Cerethite people were not all the Philistines, as Jerome and Ribera hold, but certain men in those regions to the south, as Abulensis in 1 Sam. 30, q. 10, Vatablus, Mariana, Montanus, and others have noted, which is apparent from the passage cited, 1 Sam. 30:14, from which people David's most valiant praetorian legions were collected, the guards of the Royal body, as they are called by Josephus, Antiquities book 7, ch. 11. These are called Cerethites, as if 'slayers' (of enemies), and they were called Pelethites as 'liberators', to which names Pineda suspects that the 'cetrati' (targeteers) and 'peltati' (shield-bearers) in Livy, Dec. 3, Book 1, allude, in his book 2 on the affairs of Solomon, ch. 5. See 2 Sam. 15:18, 1 Chron. 18:17, Ezek. 25:16. Compare Christoph à Castro on this passage. How the Cretans originated from these Cerethites, see, if you please, Pradus and Cornelius à Lapide on this passage.

Latin:

VÆ QUI HABITATIS FUNICULUM MARIS] Oram maritimam.

GENS PERDITARUM] Gens Cerethim, pars est Philistinorum. Vid. 1. Sam. XXX. 14. & Ezech. XXV. 16. unde ortos Cretas opinamur.

VERBUM DOMINI SUPER VOS CANAAN TERRA PHILISTHINORUM] Deest copula : Canaan, & terra Philistinorum. Partes Phœnices enumerat.

Vocem כרתים ut appellativum accipiunt A- quila, Theodotion, & Quinta editio, gens perditionis ; Tigurina, gens vastatrix, similiter fere Lutherus Krieger. Cæterum gens Cerithim non erant omnes Philistini, uti Hieron. & Ribera, sed certæ in illis re- gionibus homines ad meridiem, ut Abulensis in 1. Sam. XXX. q. X. Vatablus, Mariana, Montanus & alii notarunt, quod è loco dicto 1. Sam. XXX. 14. apparet, è qua gente collectæ sunt Davidi legio- nes prætoriæ fortissimæ, corporis Regii custodes, uti vocantur Josepho l. VII. Antiqq. c. XI. Quæ sunt dictæ Cerithi, quasi interfectores (hostium) & Pelethi dicebantur ceu liberatores, ad quæ nomina cetratos & peltatos apud Livium Dec. III. Libr. 1. alludere Pineda suspicatur l. II. de reb. Sal. cap. V. Vid. 2. Sam. XV. 18. 1. Par. XIIX. 17. Ezech. XXV. 16. Conf. Christoph. à Castro in h. l. Quomodo Cre- tenses ab hisce Cerethim provenerint vid. si pla- cet, Pradum & Cornel. à Lapide h. l.

## 2:6
Verse 6.

AND IT SHALL BE THE CORD OF THE SEA] The maritime coast: as we just said.

REST OF SHEPHERDS, AND FOLDS OF FLOCKS] With the merchants driven far away.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET ERIT FUNICVLVS MARIS] Ora maritima: ut modo diximus.

REQUIES PASTORUM, ET CAVLÆ PECO- RVM] Mercatoribus longe abactis.

## 2:7
Verse 7.

AND IT SHALL BE ITS CORD, WHICH SHALL REMAIN OF THE HOUSE OF JUDAH, THEY SHALL FEED THERE] And it shall be the coast (of that place) of the remnant of the house of Judah, (that is, of those who shall have remained with Gedaliah) so that they may feed their flocks there.

IN THE HOUSES OF ASHKELON THEY SHALL REST AT EVENING] The shepherds shall lie down in those desolate houses.

FOR THE LORD THEIR GOD SHALL VISIT THEM] Because the Lord shall have punished them, namely the Ashdodites and their neighbors.

AND HE WILL TURN THEIR CAPTIVITY] He will bring back. For thus שוב is often used. Psammetichus had already captured Azotus before, as Herodotus testifies in Euterpe, and had led away many captives: when in time Azotus was inhabited again and captives were again led away from there by the Chaldeans under Nebuchadnezzar. See Jerem. XXV. 20. Ezech. in the aforementioned place XXV. 15.

Others refer it to other, earlier times, and explain it thus with Cornel. à Lapide: And it will be his cord (the lot of the sea, that is, and the land of the Philistines will be his) which shall remain of the house of Judah, that is to say, the Jews remaining from the Babylonian captivity returning will possess Philistia, devastated by the Chaldeans, and there, as if in a desert, will pasture their flocks. That was done under the Maccabees, Simon and Jonathan, who captured Gaza and Ascalon, and subdued the Philistines. See Theodoret. Coccejus at the same time draws it to the kingdom of Christ. The Israelite people had boasted above all nations of that prerogative, that they acknowledged and worshipped the true God: and that he had become their God by a special covenant, and had assigned to them the land of Canaan, in which he had promised that he would visit them. Therefore they were mocked by the neighboring nations, especially the Palestinians to the west, and the Moabites and Ammonites to the east. God declares that he will truly demonstrate that he is their God, not only by not cutting them off, and by granting them a refuge; but also by cutting off those nations, and visiting his people, and so enlarging and strengthening them, that they may occupy the deserts of the Palestinians and Moabites and Ammonites, and dwell in them, and hold their assemblies. Parallel to this prophecy is the general one in Deut. XXX. 5. and the special ones in Zech. IX. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. XII. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Mic. IV. 11. 12. 13. 14.

This is the history: God brought back the people from the Babylonian captivity into the land of Canaan, there restored to them the temple, the city, and the republic of the twelve tribes, and asserted them into liberty: but Gaza having been taken by Alexander the Macedonian, and the neighboring places were occupied by the Jews: the Jews also possessed the towns of the Moabites snatched from the Greeks. See concerning these Josephus, Antiquities, book XIII, ch. XXIII. Moreover, I do not think that one should stop even at this fulfillment, but that this is especially to be considered, how Christ published his kingdom among those nations, and so despoiled them, which however was not done without judgment, as against the Jews, so against the Moabites and Idumeans associated among the Jews. This is Cocceius. Theodoret and Isidore do not deny this, who wish this prophecy to be perfectly fulfilled through the Apostles by the remnant of all Israel led from the Babylonian captivity and the reception of the Gospel promulgated in Jerusalem, who went forth into the land of the Philistines, just as Philip, Acts 8, was sent to the coast which leads to Gaza, and was found in Azotus.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET ERIT FVNICVLVS EJVS, QVI REMAN- SERIT DE DOMO JVDA IBI PASCENTVR] Et erit ora (ista) reliquiarum domus Iudæ, (id est, eorum qui re- manserint cum Godolia) ut ibi pascant pecora.

IN DOMIBVS ASCALONIS AD VESPERAM REQVIESCENT] Cubabunt in desolatis illis domibus pastores.

QVIA VISITABIT EOS DOMINVS DEVS EORVM] Quia punierit eos Dominus, nempe Azotios & vicinos.

ET AVERTET CAPTIVITATEM EORVM] Re- petet. Ita enim שוב sæpe ponitur. Pfammitichus jam ante Azotum ceperat, teste Herodoto Euterpe, captivos- que abduxerat multos: cum tempore rursus habitata Azo- tus iterumque inde captivi abducti per Chaldæos sub Na- buchodonoforo. Vide Jerem. XXV. 20. Ezech. dicto lo- co XXV. 15.

Ad alia tempora superiora referunt, atq; ita explicant alii cum Cornel. à Lapide: Et erit funicu- lus ejus (maris puta sors & terra Philistinorum erit illius) qui remanserit de domo Iuda, q. d. Judæi reli- qui ex captivitate Babylonica redeuntes posside- bunt Philistæam à Chaldæis vastatam, ibique qua- si in deserto pascent pecora sua. Factum id sub Macchabæis, Simone & Jonatha, qui ceperunt Ga- zam & Ascalonem, ac Philistæos subigerunt. Vid. Theodoret. Coccejus simul ad regnum Christi trahit. Populus Israeliticus præ omnibus gentibus gloria- tus fuerat illa prærogativa, quod agnoscerent & colerent verum Deum: quodque is ipsorum Deus peculiari fœdere factus fuisset, & terram Canaan ipsis addixisset, in qua se illos visitaturum pro- misisset. Igitur ridebantur à gentibus vicinis ma- xime Palæstinis ad Occidentem, & Moabitis & Am- monitis ad Orientem. Declarat Deus se revera de- monstraturum, quod Deus ipsorum sit, non tan- tum ipsos non exscindendo, & suffugium eis lar- giendo; sed etiam exscindendo illas gentes, & visi- tando populum suum, eumque ita amplificando & roborando, ut deserta Palæstinorum & Moabita- rum atque Ammonitarum occupent, & in iis habi- tent, cœtusq; suos agant. Huic prophetiæ paralle- la est generalis Deut. XXX. 5. & specialis Zach. IX. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. XII. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Mich. IV. 11. 12. 13. 14.

Historia hæc est: Deus populum ex captivitate Babylonica in terram Canaan reduxit, ibi tem- plum, urbem, rempublicam duodecim tribuum ipsis reddidit, in libertatem eos asseruit: Gaza au- tem ac Alexandro Macedone expugnata, & finiti- mi loci à Judæis occupati sunt: Moabitarum et- iam oppida Græcis erepta possederunt Judæi. Vid. de his Josephum δεχ. lib. XIII. c. XXIII. Cæterum ne in hoc quidem implemento subsistendum pu- to, sed illud vel maxime considerandum, quomodo Christus apud illas gentes regnum suum publica- verit, & eas sic despoliaverit, quod tamen non fa- ctum est absque judicio, ut in Judæos, ita in Judæis consociatos Moabitas & Idumæos. Hæc Cocce- jus. Non abnuit Theodoretius & Isidorus, qui vatici- nium hoc perfecte impletum volunt per Apostolos ex omni Israele reliquos è captivitate Babylonica ductos & susceptionem Evangelii in Hierusalem promulgati, qui in terram Philistinorum profecti sunt, uti Philippus Act. IIX. in oram, quæ ducit Ga- zam, missus, & in Azot inventus est.

## 2:8
Verse 8. I HAVE HEARD THE REPROACH OF MOAB] For they were most proud, Jer. 48:29. AND THE BLASPHEMIES OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON: WHEREWITH THEY HAVE REPROACHED MY PEOPLE] Ezek. 25:3. AND HAVE MAGNIFIED THEMSELVES AGAINST THEIR BORDER] They invaded the borders of the Israelites. Jer. 49:1.

Latin:

Vers. 8. AUDIVI OPPROBRIUM MOAB] Erant enim superbissimi Jer. XLVIII. 29. ET BLASPHEMIAS FILIORUM AMMON: QUÆ EXPROBRAVERUNT POPULO MEO] Ezech. XXV. 3. ET MAGNIFICATI SUNT SUPER TERMINOS EORUM] Israelitarum terminos invasere. Jer. XLIX. 1.

## 2:9
Verse 9. FOR MOAB SHALL BE AS SODOM, AND THE CHILDREN OF AMMON AS GOMORRAH] That happened in the fifth year after Jerusalem was taken, as we said at Isaiah 48, 44, and Ezekiel 25. THE DRYNESS OF THORNS] A place abandoned to nettles: Jerome notes here that the LXX read Damascus for the Hebrew word mimshaq, which is a mistake. AND HEAPS OF SALT] Salt pits. AND A DESERT FOR EVER] leolam, which Jerome notes here in his Commentaries is to be taken for some time, and one age. THE RESIDUE OF MY PEOPLE SHALL SPOIL THEM, AND THE REMNANT OF MY PEOPLE SHALL POSSESS THEM] Namely the borders, because they had invaded the borders of Israel, as will now follow. The residue here are, as just now, the Jews left under Gedaliah.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QUIA MOAB UT SODOMA ERIT, ET FILII AMMON QUASI GOMORRHA] Factum id quinto anno post capta Hierosolyma, ut diximus ad XLIIX. XLIV. Esaiæ, & XXV. Ezechielis. SICCITAS SPINARUM] Locus derelictus urticis: Pro ממשק LXX. hic mendos è legisse דמשק notat Hieronymus. ET ACERVI SALIS] Fodinæ salis. ET DESERTUM USQUE IN ÆTERNUM] לעולם, quod pro aliquanto tempore, & unâ ætate acci- pi notat hic in Commentariis Hieronymus. RELIQUIÆ POPULI MEI DERIPIENT EOS ET RESIDUI GENTIS MEÆ POSSIDEBUNT IL- LOS] Nempe terminos, pro eo quod illi terminos Israelis invaserant, ut jam sequetur. Reliquiæ hic sunt, ut modo, Judæi relicti sub Godolia.

## 2:10
Verse 10. THIS SHALL THEY HAVE FOR THEIR PRIDE: BECAUSE THEY HAVE BLASPHEMED AND MAGNIFIED THEMSELVES AGAINST THE PEOPLE OF THE LORD OF HOSTS] Repeated from the above 8.

It does not appear how these things can be referred to those remnants. For they were very few, whence Theodoret, Hugo, and others here understand by the remnants those who returned from Babylon under Zerubbabel. More correctly these are reduced to the times of the Maccabees. See 1 Macc. 5:6. Josephus, Antiquities, book XII, ch. XI; book XIII, ch. XXIII; book 1 of the Jewish War, ch. III. Jerome prefers to understand it in the literal sense concerning the Apostles, who subdued Ammon, Moab, and the other nations to Christ. To which we have observed Cocceius also departs.

Latin:

Vers. 10. HOC EIS EVENIET PRO SUPERBIA SUA: QUIA BLASPHEMAVERUNT ET MAGNIFI- CATI SUNT SUPER POPULUM DOMINI EXER- CITUUM] Repetitum ex superiore 8.

Non apparet, quomodo ad illas reliquias hæc referri possint. Erant enim oppido paucæ, unde Theodoretus, Hugo, alii que hic per reliquias intelli- gunt eos, qui redierunt è Babylone sub Zorobabele. Rectius ad tempora Maccabæorum hæc rediguntur. Vid. 1. Macc. V. 6. Josephus l. XII. Antiqu. c. XI. l. XIII. c. XXIII. l. 1. de Bell. Jud. c. III. Hierony- mus sensu literali mavult intelligere de Apostolis, qui Ammon, Moab, cæterasque gentes subegerunt Chri- sto. Quo etiam abire Coccejum observavimus.

## 2:11
Verse 11. HE WILL ATTENUATE ALL THE GODS OF THE EARTH] Dagon, Chemosh, Moloch. Chrysostom, in his 2nd homily against the Jews, cites this passage as it is in the LXX, and adapts it to the Evangelical times in a more excellent sense. AND MEN SHALL WORSHIP HIM, EVERY ONE FROM HIS PLACE] Through the captive Jews, many of the Gentiles will learn that there is one God, and each will worship him in his own home. These are the hasidei ummot, the saints from the Gentiles. EVEN ALL THE ISLES OF THE GENTILES] Even in the places of the Gentiles across the sea.

But these pertain not only in a mystical sense, but in a literal sense to the times of the New Testament. For ALL the gods of the earth were not attenuated except under the New Testament. And the Prophet prophesies not only concerning some few nations taught by the captive Jews and the places of the Gentiles across the sea, but concerning the nations commonly, and ALL the isles of the Gentiles. More correctly, therefore, Jerome, Theodoret, Chrysostom, Eusebius, book II, Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. XVI, Augustine, book XVIII, De Civitate Dei, ch. XXXIII, Remigius, Albert the Great, Lyranus, Vatablus, Arias, and other Christian interpreters interpret these things concerning the New Testament, because at the coming of Christ all idols were to be abandoned, which was a great destruction for the Gentiles, and the only true God was to be worshipped in the whole world. Concerning which Cornelius à Lapide: This began to be fulfilled through the Chaldeans against Ammon and Moab, when they plundered the golden and silver idols from there, as Hugo thinks: it was promoted through the Maccabees, who compelled the Ammonites and Moabites to Judaism and the worship of the true God, as I said at the end of Obadiah. But it was truly and fully effected in the whole world through the Apostles at the time of the Gospel. For then the destruction of idolatry was accomplished, and the true religion of God and Christ was received everywhere among the nations, and dominated the whole world. Thus St. Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, St. Augustine, book 18, De Civitate Dei, 33, Eusebius, book 2, Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. 16, and others passim. The Prophet therefore rises from the type to the antitype, from the Jews to Christ and the Christians who occupied not only Moab and Ammon, but all nations, and imbued them with the worship of God, having removed the idols, as if to say, God will cast down his enemies, and those of his people, namely Ammon and Moab, and their gods, through the Apostles, and will cause that each nation, not only in Jerusalem, where the Jews are, but everywhere in the world, each in its own place and religion, may worship, invoke, and sacrifice to Christ and the true God. This is Cornelius Christoph. à Castro, who says the words seem to be woven together thus: God will be terrible against the Ammonites and Moabites, who have so pursued my people with insults; for he will not only subvert them through the remnants of his people, but God will also destroy all their gods. But this is little, for he is also about to attenuate and consume the gods of the whole earth, and so to change things through the remnants of his people, the Apostles, and Apostolic men converted from the Jews, that in every place, both of the continent and of the islands, the one true God is to be worshipped. This method of amplification, says Castro, the Hebrew particle ki has implicitly, as Jud. 8:5, are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand? ki, why do you ask that we give bread to your weary men? Gen. 45:26, Joseph your son lives vechi and why? He himself shall rule in all the land of Egypt, as if to say, not only does he live, but he shall rule. Therefore he predicts that God is to be worshipped everywhere, not only in Asia and Syria, but also in the islands, namely those surrounded by the sea, as Theodoret, Lyra, and Dionysius understand: and in those provinces to which one crosses by sea from Judea, as Montanus understands, such as Europe, in which is Greece, Italy, Spain. From the Reformed, we especially produce John Cocceius, who notes that the beginning must be distinguished from the consummation. Certainly then it will be most especially known that the Lord is among His people, and He will be feared among them; when He has already emaciated all the gods of the whole world entirely; and He alone has asserted His throne and His kingdom. Nevertheless, the Abolition or Emaciation of the gods has a very long course, and it happens gradually, now in one kind, now in another; but as often as that happens, so often is God recognized to be among His people with fear. The words of Zephaniah therefore have this full meaning: God will not only visit His people in the Babylonian captivity, through the spirit of repentance and of His fear and the power of the spirit in the mind of the kings of Persia, and His grace, so that He may restore them to their land and their former state, but He will also vindicate and amplify them, and that will happen in this way: First, the lands of the neighboring enemy peoples will yield to the Israelite people. Then He will be manifested among them, and thus manifested among them He will send forth His scepter, and His sons from Zion, and He will conflict with all the gods both fictitious and so-called: all of whom He will finally emaciate; so that all the islands may finally serve Him.

The same Cocceius rightly compares here Zech. XIV. 9. The Lord shall be King over all the earth, Hos. XIV. 4. We will no more say, our God, to the work of our hands. And he observes not without reason that worship is referred particularly to all the isles. For the isles are mentioned primarily in the kingdom of Christ. Is. XLII. 4. Psalm LXXII. 10. (And it is fitting that in the isles of the sea, in which the posterity of Japheth took up their seat, the most glorious propagation of the Gospel was first made through the Apostle Paul. See Gen. IX. 29. X. 2. 3. 4. 5. Rom. XV. 19.) and in the last time Is. LX. 9. He notes moreover the liberty of worship. EVERY ONE FROM HIS PLACE. Without the necessity of offering an external victim at Jerusalem. Mal. I. 11. Finally, he refutes Grotius, because while leading us to Chrysostom, he leads us away from his mind by prevaricating, while he suggests that that is the more excellent understanding which exceeds the scope and διάνοιαν of this text and wishes worship to be fulfilled in the pious among the Gentiles, among the Jews, who were both rare, and if they were, they had to become προσέλυτοι, so that they might deserve to be called חסידים, and by their fewness they do not fulfill the magnificence of the Prophet, nor the mode of worship, which could not have been of proselytes except in servitude and figure, which is hinted here to be future only in spirit and not in carnal rite, and in truth not in figure. For that which is said here about worship must be taken purely and solitarily, and that which is predicted here and there about the Gentiles in the isles must be taken in abundance. Which, as they are rightly opposed to Grotius, so they also refute the gloss of Calvin, concerning the fame of the redemption of the people from Babylon penetrating to the ends of the earth. For the Prophet speaks not only of the fame to be divulged, but of the worship and religion of the true God to be propagated through the world: whence not even Abarbenel himself doubts that this passage pertains to that time when the Lord God of the whole earth was to be called. Is. LIV. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ATTENUABIT OMNES DEOS TERRÆ] Da- gonem, Chamosum, Molochum. Hunc locum, ut est in LXX. citat, & ad Evangelica tempora sensu excellentiore aptat Chrysostomus 2. adversus Judæos. ET ADORABUNT EUM VIRI DE LOCO SUO] Per Judæos captivos multi de gentibus discent u- num esse Deum, & quisque domi suæ eum colent. Hi sunt חסידי אומות sancti ex gentibus. OMNES INSULÆ GENTIUM] Etiam in locis gentium transmarinis.

Hæc vero non mystico sensu tantum, sed lite- rali pertinent ad tempora N. T. Nam OMNES DIi terræ non nisi sub N. T. attenuati. Nec solum de paucis quibusdam gentibus per captivos Judæ- os edoctis & transmarinis locis gentium, sed de gentibus communiter, & OMNIBUS insulis gen- tium Propheta vaticinatur. Rectius ergo Hiero- nymus, Theodoretus, Chrysost. Eusebius l. II. De- monstr. Evangel. c. XVI. Augustin. libr. XIIX. de Civ. Dei c. XXXIII. Remigius, Albertus M. Lyra- nus, Vatablus, Arias, & alii Interpp. Christiani hæc de N. T. interpretantur, quod sub adventum Chri- sti deserenda sint omnia idola, quod pro magno exi- tio fuit gentilibus, & solus verus Deus in universo orbe adorandus sit. Quo de Cornel. à Lapide: Ce- pit hoc impleri per Chaldæos in Ammon & Moab, cum inde idola aurea & argentea diripuerunt, ut censet Hugo: promotum est per Machabæos, qui Ammonitas & Moabitas ad Judaismum, & veri Dei cultum compulerunt, uti dixi in fine Abdiæ. Verum plane & plene id in toto orbe effectum est per Apostolos tempore Evangelii. Tunc enim per- actum est excidium idololatriæ, & vera Dei Christi- que religio ubique gentium recepta, toti mundo dominata est. Ita S. Hieron. Theodor. Remig. S. Au- gust. lib. 18. Civit. 33. Euseb. lib. 2. de Demonstr. Evang. c. 16. & alii passim. Assurgit ergo Propheta à typo ad antitypum, à Iudæis & Christum & Christia- nos qui non tantum Moab & Ammon, sed omnes gentes occuparunt, Deique cultu sublatis idolis, imbuerunt, q. d. Deus hostes suos, suiq; populi, pu- ta Ammon & Moab, eorumq; Deos dejiciet per Apo- stolos, facietq;, ut quæq; gens non in sola Ierusalem, ubi Judæi, sed ubiq; terrarum, quælibet in suo loco & religione, Christum, Deumq; verum colat, invocet, & sacrificet. Hæc Cornelius Christoph. à Castro, Verba inquit, sic videntur contexenda: Terribi- lis erit Deus adversus Ammonitas, & Moabitas, qui adeo insectati sunt convitiis populum meum; nam non tantum ipsos subvertet per reliquias populi sui, quin & Deus eorum omnes delebit. Sed hoc parum est, nam & Deos universæ terræ est attenuaturus & consumturus, & ita res per reliquias populi sui Apo- stolos, & viros Apostolicos ex Judæis conversos com- mutaturus, ut in omni loco tam continentis terræ quam Insularum sit verus unus Deus adorandus. Hanc amplificandi rationem inquit Castrius, im- plicitam habet particula Hebræa כי Chi ut Jud. 8, 5. num manus Cebee & Salmana in manu tua? כי quid postulas, ut demus viris tuis lassis panem? Gen. 45, 26. Joseph Filius tuus vivit וכי Vechi & quid? Ipse dominabitur in omni terra Ægypti, quasi dicat non solum vivit, sed dominabitur. Itaque prædicit, Deum adorandum ubique, non tantum in Asia & Syria, sed & in Insulis nempe mari cinctis, ut intel- ligunt Theodoretes, Lyra & Dionysius: & in iis pro- vinciis, ad quas trajecto mari è Judæa transitur, ut intelligit Montanus, qualis est Europa, in qua est Græcia, Italia, Hispania. E Reformatis imprimis Ioh. Coccejum producimus, qui notat, debere distin- gui inchoationem à consummatione. Certe tum ma- xime cognoscetur, quod Dominus sit apud popu- lum suum, & timebitur apud illum; quando jam e- maciaverit omnes omnino deos totius mundi; & ipse solus thronum suum & regnum suum asserue- rit. Attamen Abolitio, sive Emaciatio deorum habet longissimum tractum, & fit paulatim nunc in omni genere, nunc in alio, quoties autem illa fit, toties De- us recognoscitur esse apud populum suum cum timore. Verba igitur Sophoniæ hunc plenum sen- sum habent: Deus non tantum visitabit populum suum in captivitate Babylonica, per spiritum resipi- scentiæ & timoris sui & spiritus potentiam in animo regum Persidis, & gratiam suam, ut eos restituat in ter- ram & statum suum pristinum, sed & vindicabit & amplificabit eum, idq; fiet hoc modo: Primo terræ vi- cinorum populorum inimicorum cedent populo Israelitico. Tum manifestabitur apud illos, & sic manifestatus apud illos emittet sceptrum suum, & filii sui ex Sione, & confliget cum omnibus diis tum fictis tum nuncupatis: quos omnes tandem ema- ciabit; adeo ut omnes insulæ ipsi tandem serviant.

Recte hic confert idem Coccejus Zachar. XIV. 9 Fiet Dominus Rex in tota terra Hof. XIV. 4. Non dicemus amplius, Deus noster, ad opus manuum no- strarum. Et observat non abs re peculiariter ado- rationem referri ad omnes insulas. Insulæ enim imprimis in Christi regno memorantur. Es. XLII. 4. Psalm. LXXII. 10. (Et convenit, quod in insulis maris, in quibus Japheti posteritas sedem cepit clarissima Evangelii propagatio primitus facta est per Apostolum Paulum. Vide Genes. IX. 29. X. 2. 3. 4. 5. Rom. XV. 19.) & in ultimo tempore Esa. LX. 9. Notat insuper adorationis Libertatem. QUIS- QUE E LOCO SUO. Sine necessitate offe- rendi victimam externam Hierosolymis. Mal. I. 11. Refellit denique Grotium, quod ad Chrysostomum nos ducens, ab ejus mente nos prævaricando abducat, dum suggerit, eam esse excellentiorem intelligentiam, quæ excedat scopum & διάνοιαν hujus textus & ad- orationem velit impletam, in gentium piis, inter Ju- dæos, qui & rari fuerunt, & si fuerunt, debue- runt προσέλυτοι fieri, ut mereantur, appellari חסידים, & sua paucitate non explent Prophetæ ma- gnificentiam, neǵ adorationis, quæ proselytorum non potuit esse, nisi in servitute & figura, modum, qui hic innuitur futurus tantum in spiritu & non in carnali ritu, & in veritate non in figura. Mere enim & solitarie accipiendum est, quod hic de ad- oratione dicitur, & in copia, quod de gentibus in insulis passim prædicatur. Quæ uti recte Gro- tio opponuntur, ita Calvini etiam refellunt glos- sam, de fama redemptionis populi è Babylone ad fi- nes terræ penetrante. Non enim de fama solum divulganda, sed de cultu & religione veri Dei pro- paganda per orbem Propheta loquitur: unde nec ipse Abarbenel dubitat, quin hic locus pertineat ad illud tempus, quo Dominus Deus totius terræ vo- candus erat. Es. LIV. 5.

## 2:12
Ver. 12.

BUT YOU ALSO O ETHIOPIANS SHALL BE SLAIN BY MY SWORD] In the Hebrew: slain of my sword: how it is said διδακτοὶ τῶ θεῶ John VI. 45. These cohere with the things said above 8. 9. 10. This was fulfilled when the Ethiopians, who were in the aid of Necho king of Egypt, were slain by Nebuchadnezzar Jer. XLVI. 2. The Prophet follows the order of the nations, not of time.

He returns to pursue the destruction which dominates the nations through Nebuchadnezzar. Moreover, the Ethiopians are included under Egypt: whence most believe that this was fulfilled in the fifth year after the destruction of Jerusalem, when Nebuchadnezzar invaded and took Egypt. See Joseph. b. X. Antiq. c. XI. Jerome, however, thinks it was fulfilled more by Cyrus and the Medes in this place; but the Rabbis wrongly take the Chusim, that is, the Ethiopians, to be the Chaldeans themselves, as if their destruction by Cyrus were here foretold. For the Ethiopians and the Chaldeans differ and are distinguished by the whole climate, and if I may say so, by the whole heaven.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SED ET VOS ÆTHIOPES INTERFECTI GLA- DIO MEO ERITIS] In Hebræo: interfecti ensis mei: quomodo dicitur διδακτοὶ τῶ θεῶ Joh. VI. 45. Hæc co- hærent cum dictis supra 8. 9. 10. Impletum hoc, cum Æthiopes, qui in auxilio erant Neconis regis Ægyptii, cæ- si sunt à Nabuchodonosoro Jeremiæ XLVI. 2. Ordinem gentium sequitur Propheta, non temporis.

Redit ad prosequendum exitium, quod do- minatur gentibus per Nabuchodonosarem. Com- prehenduntur autem Æthiopes sub Ægypto: unde id plerique completum credunt quinto anno post excidium Hierosolymitanum, cùm Ægyptum invasit Nebucadnezar & cepit. Vid. Joseph. l. X. An- tiq. c. XI. Hieronymus tamen id magis impletum putat per Cyrum & Medos in h. l. perperam autem Rabbini per Chusim, id est, Æthiopes accipiunt ipsosmet Chaldæos, quasi eorum hic excidium per Cyrum prænuncietur. Æthiopes enim & Chaldæi toto climate, & ut ita dicam, toto cœlo distant & distinguuntur.

## 2:13
Ver. 13.

AND HE SHALL STRETCH OUT] The same Nebuchadnezzar.

OVER THE NORTH] Against the Medes.

AND WILL DESTROY ASSHUR] We have spoken about this history at Nahum.

AND WILL MAKE THE BEAUTIFUL A DESOLATION] In the Hebrew: Nineveh: he will deprive it of wealth and commerce so that a great part of the city may be empty of inhabitants; for it was not razed, as we showed at Nahum.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET EXTENDET] Idem Nabuchodonosor.

SUPER AQUILONEM] In Medos.

ET PERDET ASSUR] Diximus de hac historia ad Nahumum.

ET PONET SPECIOSAM IN SOLITUDINEM] In Hebræo: Niniven: eam privabit opibus & commerciis ita ut magna pars urbis vacua sit ab habitatoribus; excisa enim non est, ut ad Nahumum ostendimus.

## 2:14
Ver. 14.

AND FLOCKS SHALL LIE DOWN IN THE MIDST OF IT] This is wont to happen in places abandoned by human cultivation, as above 6.

AND THE PELICAN AND THE PORCUPINE] From Isaiah XXXIV. 11. the Hebrews put the Pelican for the onocrotalus, and the Latin himself elsewhere, as we have said at the place in Isaiah. But in the Commentaries on this place, Jerome says there are two kinds of onocrotali, one aquatic, the other of the wilderness.

THEY SHALL DWELL IN ITS THRESHOLDS] In the Hebrew: In its pomegranates: that is, in the figures of pomegranates, which were wont to be placed on the tops of buildings. See Amos IX. such are those which the Greeks call ἀκρωτήρια.

THE VOICE OF THE SINGER IN THE WINDOW] Birds will sing there safely. So the Chaldean here, and Isaiah XIII. 21. 22. XXXIV. 11. 15. confirms it.

Montanus and others explain the North as Babylon, and wish its destruction by Cyrus to be predicted here. Jerome, however, Remigius, and Hugo think Babylon is designated by the name 'the beautiful'. Because Isaiah chapter XIII. threatens these same things to Babylon. But although we admit that Nineveh is understood, to whom Zephaniah predicts similar fates as Isaiah does to Babylon, it is nevertheless clear that the Prophet is prophesying not merely the deprivation of wealth and commerce, from which a large part of the city might be rendered empty of inhabitants, but the destruction of the city of Nineveh. For it is said that it is to be placed into A DESOLATION: and the waste and solitude is described too graphically and at length, certainly not as a partial one, but a total one. Furthermore, the insulting and hissing of passers-by, v. 15, argues for solitude and devastation, not just some deprivation of wealth. Nor are those phrases to be understood otherwise, when similar things are predicted of Babylon. Whence it is to be gathered that the same sense is here also brought to bear on them. Finally, Nahum is not opposed to this sense, but rather confirms it, as we have noted regarding that Prophet. And Chronologists observe that the completion of the prophecy and the destruction of Nineveh by Nebuchadnezzar falls in his first year: or at least preceded the destruction of Jerusalem, and therefore it is to be judged that it is insinuated here to that end, so that in those things there might be a pledge of the truth of the remaining predictions for the destruction.

Verse of the same.

THE RAVEN IN THE LINTEL] It appears that both the LXX and Jerome read ערב; where we have חרב. The similar place in Isaiah XXXIV. 11. proves their reading. The Chaldean reads חרב, and translates, they shall desolate its gate. סף is a threshold, as appears in Judges XIX. 27. Ezekiel XL. 6.

Here Grotius follows his Capellus again: but it must be denied that the LXX and Jerome read otherwise here; the contrary is evident from himself: who observes that in his Hebrew there was placed חרב: although he himself, because of the commutation of the guttural letters ע and ח, held the word חרב and ערב in the same place. He therefore rendered it Raven, not desolation, because he saw that the mention of other ill-omened birds had preceded.

FOR I WILL WEAKEN ITS STRENGTH] For it shall strip its cedar work. That is, the floorings of many houses will be exposed to ravens and other birds; the active is used impersonally for the passive.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET ACCUBABUNT IN MEDIO EJUS GRE- GES] Id in locis derelictis ab humano cultu fieri solet, ut supra 6.

ET ONOCROTALUS ET ERICUS] Ex Esaiæ XXXIV. 11. pro onocrotalo Pelicanum ponunt Hebræi, & ipse Latinus alibi, ut ad Esaiæ locum diximus. Verum in Commentariis ad hunc locum, Hieronymus onocrotalorum duo esse ait genera, aliud aquatile, aliud solitudinis.

IN LIMINIBUS EJUS MORABUNTUR] In Hebræo: In malis punicis ejus: id est, in figuris malorum punicorum, quæ summis ædibus imponi solebant. Vide Am. IX. talia sunt, quæ Græci vocant ἀκρωτήρια.

VOX CANTANTIS IN FENESTRA] Aves ibi canent tuto. Ita hic Chaldæus, & confirmat id Esa. XIII. 21. 22. XXXIV. 11. 15.

Montanus, & alii Aquilone explicant de Babylone, ejusque excidium per Cyrum hic prædici volunt. Hieronymus vero, Remigius, & Hugo, per nomen speciosa Babylonem designari putant. Quod Esaias cap. XIII. hæc eadem comminetur Babyloni. Sed quamvis admittamus Niniven intelligi, cui similia fata prædicit Zephanias, quæ Babyloni Esaias non tamen solam opum, & commerciorum privationem, ex qua magna urbis pars vacua reddita sit habitatoribus, sed excidium urbi Ninive vaticinari Prophetam in aprico est. Nam dicitur ponenda in SOLITUDINEM: & vastitas ac solitudo non partialis certe, sed totalis nimis graphice ac prolixe describitur. Porro insultatio & exfibilatio transeuntium v. 15. solitudinem & devastationem arguit, non tantum aliqualem opum privationem. Neque phrases istæ aliter intelligendæ, cum de Babylone similia prædicuntur. Unde colligere est, eundem sensum hic etiam iisdem inferri. Denique non adversus est huic sensui Nahum, sed confirmat potius illum uti ad Prophetam istum notavimus. Et observant Chronologi complementum vaticinii, ac destructionem Ninive per Nabuchodonosarum cadere in annum ejus primum: vel certe antecessisse Hierosolymæ excidium, ideoque ea fini etiam hic insinuari id censendum est, ut in illis excidio pignus esset veritatis reliquarum prædictionum.

Vers. eod.

CORVUS IN SUPERLIMINARI] Apparet & LXX. & Hieronymum legisse ערב; ubi nos habemus חרב Probat illorum lectionem Locus Esaiæ similis XXXIV. 11. Chaldæus חרב legit, vertitque, desolabunt portam ejus. סף est limen, ut apparet Jud. XIX. 27. Ezech. XL. 6.

Sequitur hic iterum Grotius suum Capellum: verum negandum hic aliter legisse LXX. & Hieronymum; Contrarium ex ipso patet: qui observat, in Ebræo suo positum fuisse חרב: quamvis ipse ob commutationem literarum gutturalium ע & ח vocem חרב & ערב eodem loco habuerit. Reddidit ergo Corvum, non vastitatem, quod viderit aliorum inauspicatarum avium mentionem præcessisse.

QUONIAM ATTENUABO ROBUR EJUS] Quoniam cedrina ejus nudabit. Id est, tabulata domuum multarum patebunt corvis, aliisque avibus; activum impersonaliter positum pro passivo.

## 2:15
Verse 15.

THIS IS THE GLORIOUS CITY] Supply, passersby will say; this is that city which used to exult.

DWELLING IN CONFIDENCE] Which was inhabited confidently.

WHICH SAID IN ITS HEART I AM, AND THERE IS NONE OTHER BESIDE] Isaiah had said this concerning Babylon in 47.8.

HE SHALL HISS] Out of astonishment, as in 1 Kings 9.8.

AND SHALL MOVE HIS HAND] As those who are astonished are accustomed to do.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

HÆC EST CIVITAS GLORIOSA] Supple, dicent transeuntes; hæc est urbs illa quæ exsultabat.

HABITANS IN CONFIDENTIA] Quæ habitabatur confidenter.

QUÆ DICEBAT IN CORDE SUO EGO SUM, ET NON EST ALIA AMPLIUS] Hæc Esaias de Babylone dixerat XLVII. 8.

SIBILABIT] Præ stupore, ut 1. Reg. IX. 8.

ET MOVEBIT MANUM SUAM] Ut solent facere attoniti.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAP. III.

CHAPTER III. Partly corrective, partly evangelical.

In the first part, Jerusalem is rebuked for impenitence, by which she [rebukes] unjust princes and magistrates, prophets who are despisers, priests who profane the sanctuary and pervert the law, and all the contumacious who reject God teaching rightly and calling to repentance: with the added punishment of extermination and desolation up to verse 8. In the other part, evangelical consolation is added up to the end of the chapter. v. 30. Threatening harsh things to the wicked, it speaks soft things about Christ.

Ver. 1. WOE TO THE PROVOKING] Woe to the unexamined. This is usually said of women of prostituted modesty. AND REDEEMED] Polluted. For גאל means to pollute, as Mal. 1:7, Isa. 63:3, Lam. 4:14. DOVE] To the predator. How we explained יונה in Jer. 46:16, 50:16, understand the city of Jerusalem, where the poor had long been oppressed by the rich.

Cocceius also takes the word יונה as a participle because of that הוי עיר Woe to the city oppressing. But he renders the preceding words thus: to whom it was given to see, and who was asserted, because Jerusalem became possessed of the vision of God manifested in the flesh, and had him as her גאל, her brother and redeemer. Therefore, he does not explain it with R. Solomon, and Aben Ezra, and R. David Kimchi, with Junius, Drusius, Diodati, and the Dutch, as concerning the gate of Jerusalem and the temple of Solomon, but with Abarbanel he judges that this concerns the Jerusalem which Nehemiah built and the second temple and its destruction, which opinion he proves with these points: (1) that otherwise a tautology must be posited in ch. 1:18, ch. 3:8. (2) that a prophecy of the final destruction will not be found here. (3) and that a very great leap is made from the destruction of the city by the Babylonians to the conversion of the Gentiles: and about to perish. (4) if the force of the particle אז then v. 9. For neither in the destruction of the Babylonians was a pure language given to the Gentiles. (5) That thus no prophecy concerning Christ is left in this prophecy. (6) That the weight and emphasis of the words is elided. (7) That this pericope of verses 1-2 is a graphic description of the presence of the Son of God in the flesh. Furthermore, others explain the first word as monstrous, foul in appearance: Moreah from the verb Raah, he saw. Because the city was monstrous in the sight of the Lord and the angels on account of its crimes. Cocceius declares that the dignity of the vision of God in the flesh, accepted without fruit, is signified thus: Woe to whom the vision has been granted. For the verb הראה in Hophal signifies to receive a vision, or to be admitted to see, wherever it is used: as Exod. 25:40, 24:30, Deut. 4:35, except for Lev. 13:49, where it can be reciprocal, to show oneself to be seen. Thus, the dignity of the Vision of God in the flesh, accepted ungratefully and without fruit, will be signified. For the same reason of the vision of God, Israel is called Jeshurun even in those places where its disobedience is taxed. Therefore, מוראה will be for מראה, as הועלה for העלה Judg. 6:28, רעלה for רעלה Hab. 1:15. A parallel in phrase and sense is Gen. 16:13, Hagar named Jehovah, who was speaking to her, El Roi, God of vision or the visible God, etc. Compare John 1:18, 14:9. Refer here to Isa. 5:19, Who say, let him hasten, let him speed his work (promised in the prophecies concerning Christ) that we may see, and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, and let us know. To which Isa. 6:9 responds: Hear by hearing and do not understand, and see by seeing and do not know. The Savior appeals to this in Matt. 13:15, 16, 17. Concerning the other word נגאלה, which most explain as you are contaminated, he thinks that נגאל nowhere occurs as meaning iniquity; and that therefore the Targum rendered it מתפרקא, asserted, rescued, and the LXX, redeemed. Old redeemed, and because גאל becomes to take hold of, to assert, to call something one's own and to claim it; and, with a price intervening, to redeem. This is Cocceius.

Latin:

CAP. III.

CAPUT III. Partim Epanorthoticum, partim Evangelicum.

In parte prima redarguitur Hierosolyma impœniten- tia, qua principes & Magistratus injustos, Pro- phetas contemtores, Sacerdotes Sanctuarium pro- phanantes & legem pervertentes, universos con- tumaces, qui Deum recta docentem & ad pœniten- tiam vocantem repudiant: addita pœna exter- minationis & desolationis usq; ad vers. 8. in altera parte subjungitur Evangelica consolatio usq; ad fi- nem cap. v. 30. Dura malis minitans de Christo mollia fatur.

Vers. I. VÆ PROVOCATRIX] Væ inspectata. 'Dici id solet de feminis prostituti pudoris. ET REDEMTA[ Polluta. nam גאל est pollue- re, ut Malach. I. 7. Esa. LXIII. 3. Thren. IV. 14. COLUMBA] Prædatrici. quomodo יונה exposui- mus Jer. XLVI. 16. L. 16. intellige urbem Hierosolyma, ubi diu pauperes à divitibus oppressi fuerant.

Vocem יונה etiam ut participium accepit Coc- cejus ob illud הוי עיר Væ. Væ urbi opprimenti. Sed præ- cedentia ita reddit, cui datum est videre, quæq; asser- ta est, quod compos facta sit Hierosolyma visionis Dei manifestati in carne, eumq; habuerit גאל fratrem & redemptorem suum. Non ergo cum R. Salo- mone, & Aben Esdra, ac R. David Kimchio, cum Junio, Drusio, Deodato, Belgis de Hierosolymæ porta, & templo Salomonis explicat, sed cum Abarbenel censet agi hic de Hierosolyma, quam ædificavit Nehemias & templo secundo ejusque ex- cidio, quam sententiam hisce probat (1) quod alioqui ταυ τολογία statuenda sit c. I. 18. c. III. 8. (2) quod non reperietur hic vaticinium ultimæ de- structionis. (3) maximusque saltus fiat à destructio- ne urbis per Babylonios ad conversionem genti- lium: ac peritura. (4) si vis particulæ אז tunc v. 9. Neque enim in destructione Babyloniorum data est gentibus lingua pura. (5) Quod ita nulla relin- quatur prophetia de Christo in hac prophetia. (6) Quod elidatur pondus & emphasis verborum. (7) quod hæc pericopa vers. 1. 2. sit graphica descriptio παρουσίας Filii Dei in carne. Cæterum primam vocem alii exponunt monstiosam, aspectu fœdam: Morean à Verbo Raah vidit. Quia monstrosa erat urbs in conspectu Domini & Angelorum propter scelera. Significari dignationem visionis Dei in carne sine fructu acceptam, Coccejus ita declarat: Væ cui visio concessa est. Nam verbum הראה in Ho- phal significat visionem accipere, sive Admitti ad videndum, ubicunque usurpatur: ut Exod. XXV. 40. XXIV. 30. Deut. IV. 35. excepto Levit. XIII. 49. ubi potest esse reciprocum, Videndum se præbe- re. Ita significabitur dignatio Visionis Dei in carne in- grate, & sine fructu accepta. Ex eadem causa visio- nis Dei Israel vocatur ישורון etiam in illis locis, ubi taxatur ejus inobedientia. Erit igitur מוראה pro מראה ut הועלה pro העלה Jud. VI. 28. רעלה pro רעלה Abac. I. 15. Parallelum in phrasi & sensu est Gen. XVI. 13. Hagar nominavit Jehovam, qui allo- quebatur eam, אל ראי Deum visionis sive visibilem. &c. Confer. Joh. I. 18. XIV. 9. Huc refer Esa. V. 19. Qui dicunt festinet, acceleret opus suum (in prophetiis promissum de Christo) ut videamus, & approximet & veniat consilium sancti Israelis, & cognoscamus. Cui respondet Esa. VI. 9. Audite audiendo & ne confide- retis, & videte videndo & ne cognoscite. Huc pro- vocat Servator Matth. XIII. 15. 16. 17. De altera voce נגאלה, quam plerique exponunt contami- nata es, putat, quod nuspiam נגאל pro iniquitatus fuit, occurrat: quodque proinde Targum reddi- derit מתפרקא asserta, erepta, LXX. άπολελυτρω- μένη. Vetus redemta, & quod גאל fit ἀντιλαμ- βάνεσθαι asserere, suum aliquid dicere & vindicare; &, intercedente pretio, redimere. Hæc Coccejus.

## 3:2
Ver. 2. SHE DID NOT HEAR THE VOICE] Of the prophets. AND DID NOT RECEIVE DISCIPLINE] That is, she did not follow the law. SHE DID NOT TRUST IN THE LORD] But now in the Assyrian, now in the Egyptian, now in the Chaldeans, and often in their idols. SHE DID NOT DRAW NEAR TO HER GOD] She did not worship God: for that is קרב, whence קרב.

Latin:

Vers. 2. NON AUDIVIT VOCEM] Prophetarum. ET NON SUSCEPIT DISCIPLINAM] Id est, legem non est secuta. IN DOMINO NON EST CONFISA] Sed mo- do in Assyrio, modo in Ægyptio, modo in Chaldæis, sæpe & in illorum idolis. AD DEUM SUUM NON APPROPINQUAVIT] Deum non coluit: id enim קרב unde קרב.

## 3:3
Ver. 3. HER PRINCES IN THE MIDST OF HER ARE LIKE ROARING LIONS] A similar complaint in Ezek. 22:27. HER JUDGES ARE LIKE WOLVES IN THE EVENING, THEY DID NOT LEAVE UNTIL MORNING] Wolves in the evening are most greedy. Jer. 1:6. For they did not leave until morning, the Hebrew has, they do not gnaw the bones until morning: that is, they do not delay to gnaw, but immediately consume everything.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PRINCIPES EJUS IN MEDIO EJUS QUA- SI LEONES RUGIENTES] Similis querela apud Ezech. XXII, 27. JUDICES EJUS QUASI LUPI VESPERE, NON RELINQUEBANT MANE] Lupi vespere avidissimi. Jer. I, 6. Pro non relinquebant mane, Hebræum habet, non ossa rodunt ad mane: id est, non differunt rodere, sed sta- tim omnia absumunt.

## 3:4
Ver. 4. HER PROPHETS ARE LIGHT, FAITHLESS MEN] Ezek. 22:28. Mic. 3:11. HER PRIESTS HAVE POLLUTED THE HOLY] That is, the sanctuary, the temple. THEY HAVE ACTED UNJUSTLY AGAINST THE LAW] In the Hebrew: they have transgressed the law, namely in many ways. Ez. 22:26.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PROPHETÆ EJUS VESANI, VIRI INFI- DELES] Ezech. XXII. 28. Mich. III, 11. SACERDOTES EJUS POLLUERUNT SAN- CTUM] Id est, sanctuarium, templum. INJUSTE EGERUNT CONTRA LEGEM] In Hebræo: legem transgressi sunt, multis scilicet modis. Ez. XXII, 26.

## 3:5
Ver. 5. THE LORD IS JUST, IN THE MIDST OF HER HE WILL NOT DO INIQUITY] Of her, namely the city. God, who sees all these things being present, does nothing contrary to what is right. MORNING BY MORNING HE WILL BRING HIS JUDGMENT TO LIGHT] Daily he publishes some notable judgment against those princes, prophets, and priests. An allusion to the custom of the Jews and neighboring nations, among whom judgments were exercised only in the morning. We spoke to Job 24:17. AND IT WILL NOT BE HIDDEN] It does not fail. That is, he never omits to do such things. BUT THE UNJUST MAN DID NOT KNOW CONFUSION] Yet the unjust man does not know how to be ashamed.

Cocceius interprets all those things concerning Jerusalem rebuilt by Nehemiah, and he urges among other things (1) that the profanation of the holy [thing] v. 4 committed by the priests is to be understood of the true temple of God, in which the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily, the body of the Son of GOD, which they wickedly treated, to which he also draws that [passage] Mal. II. 11. Judah has profaned the holy [thing] of the Lord, which he loves, and Deut. XXXII. 15. He treated the rock of his salvation as a wicked thing. (2) that v. 5. The Lord is righteous in the midst of it, is to be understood of the Son of God manifested in the midst of Jerusalem. (3) that the words, the unjust knows not how to blush, provide the cause of the latest destruction, because they were unwilling to acknowledge him as God, and were not put to shame by his judgment. (4) that the words: I have destroyed the nations, exhibit a sign of the time of the coming of Christ, which was to come. Such characters he observes here in greater number. Let us hear the same man in his own words explaining his own [views]: God manifested, he says, in the midst of Jerusalem attributes his own characters, namely that Jehovah was righteous in the midst of it. He alludes to Deut. XXXII. 4, from which it is to be estimated what this word signifies. Righteous denotes here, as regards the truth of his person, He who has testimony from heaven and earth that he does not lie, declaring himself the Son of God, one with the Father, who descended from heaven, and speaking the words of God, and demanding that he be believed in; again as regards the sanctification of his name. He who reveals to the whole creation that the word of faith, by which it is believed that God forgives sins, is not a wonderful thing, nay, that it is the righteousness of a sinful man; since he brought this word from heaven and from the abyss, that is, from the dead Deut. XXX. 12. 13. 14. The term righteous, as to the servant of God and the one justifying many through the knowledge of himself, is attributed to Christ Isa. LIII. 11 antonomastically with that emphasis with which it is here attributed to Jehovah. For it is nothing but the name of JEHOVAH. Furthermore, he denies that he committed injustice. This savors of an apology against the accusation and blasphemy of the princes, who were rejecting him.

Thus Isaiah 53:9. There is an allusion again to Deut. 31:4, without injustice. See also Is. 50:8-9, where Christ appeals to the judgment and actual help of God against the false accusations and unjust persecutions of his own peoples. The question, however, about which there was a struggle and for which Isaiah indicates Christ was made a martyr, is in verses 2-3. Namely, whether he is the almighty God, clothing the heaven with darkness? The third characteristic is to bring forth his judgment into the light daily, and indeed in the morning, without fail. By judgment, understand the words of the Lord, by which he either refutes the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, who, omitting the weightier matters of the law and being ignorant of the law (Matt. 5:20), tithed mint (Matt. 23:23), and indeed even transgressed the law of God on account of traditions (Matt. 15:20), or their tyranny, because they burdened the people with unbearable precepts (Matt. 23:4), and that to devour the houses of widows (Matt. 23:14), and their pride and ostentation (Matt. 6 and 23:5-10, 12, 14), and their ignorance of the mystery of God and Christ, which is the key of knowledge (Matt. 23:13; Luke 11:52), and their false righteousness, situated in the observance of external works and the use of legal purifications (Matt. 5:10), or he defends his own cause and that of God against their slanders. To bring forth judgment into the light is to give evident assurance to that judgment through the testimony of Moses and the Prophets and divine works as the works of his own Father. In the end, he connects the outcome of this appearance of God with justice and judgment; that the unjust man did not know how to blush. The unjust are those whom God is understood to have judged by his word, and whom he designated in verses 1-4, and for those reasons, they are unjust. All the Prophets testify with one voice that Christ was not going to be received by his own, but was going to be rejected and reprobated, and would be a stumbling block to both houses of Israel and Judah. And this passage, if any other, shows that the cause of the final destruction of Jerusalem is that they would not acknowledge him as their God, who was truly their God, and they were not laid open by his judgment. Thus he.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DOMINUS JUSTUS, IN MEDIO EJUS NON FACIET INIQUITATEM] Ejus, nempe civitatis. Deus qui ista omnia præsens videt, nihil agit præter æquum. MANE MANE JUDICIUM SUUM DABIT IN LUCEM] Quotidie aliquod insigne edit judicium in il- los principes, Prophetas, Sacerdotes. Allusio ad morem Judæorum & vicinarum gentium, apud quos judicia tan- tum mane exercebantur. Diximus ad Jobum XXIV, 17. ET NON ABSCONDETUR] Non deficit. Id est, nunquam omittit talia agere. NESCIVIT AUTEM INIQUUS CONFUSIO- NEM] Attamen homo iniquus nescit pudescere.

Omnia illa Coccejus interpretatur de Hiero- solyma à Nehemia ædificata, & urget inter alia (1) quod profanatio sancti v. 4. à sacerdotibus facta intelligenda sit de vero Dei templo, in quo plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter habitat, corpore filii DEI, quod illi scelerate tractarunt, quo etiam trahit il- la Mal. II. 11. Profanavit Jehuda sanctum Domini, quod diligit, & Deut. XXXII. 15. Pro scelerato tra- ctavit rupem salutis suæ. (2) quod v. 5. Dominus ju- stus in medio ejus, intelligenda de Filio Dei mani- festato in medio Hierosolymæ. (3) quod verba, injustus nescit erubescere, causam novissimi excidii tradant, quod noluerint eum pro Deo agnoscere, & judicio ipsius non fuerint pudefacti. (4) quod verba: disperdidi gentes signum temporis exhibe- ant adventus Christi, quod venire debuit. Quales characteres hic plures observat. Audiamus eun- dem ἀυτοφωνῶς sua exponentem: Deo manifest a- to inquit, in medio Hierosolymæ attribuit suos chara- cteres, nimirum Jehovah justus erat in medio ejus. Al- ludit ad Deut. XXXII. 4. unde, quid hæc vox vale- at, æstimandum est. Justus notat hic, quoad perso- næ veritatem, Qui à cœlo & terra testimonium habet, quod non mentiatur, se dictans Filium Dei, unum cum Patre, qui descenderit de cœlo, & Dei verba loquens, ac postulans in se credi: rursus quoad sanctificationem nominis sui. Qui toti crea- turæ patefacit, non esse mirabile verbum fidei, qua creditur Deum remittere peccata, imo esse justi- tiam hominis peccatoris; quippe cum hoc ver- bum è cœlo & ab abysso, h. e. à mortuis attulerit Deut. XXX. 12. 13. 14. Justi vocabulum ut servo Dei & justificantimultos per agnitionem sui, attribuitur Christo Esa. LIII. 11. antonomastice in ea emphasi, qua hic Jehovæ. Non enim est nisi nomen JE- HOVÆ. Præterea negat ipsum fecisse injusti- tiam. Hoc sapit apologiam contra accusationem & blasphemiam principum, rejicientium ipsum.

Sic Esai. LIII. 9. Alluditur rursus ad Deut. XXXI 4. sine injustitia. Vide etiam Es. L. 8. 9. ubi Christu provocat ad judicium & actuale auxilium Dei, falsis criminationibus & injustis persecutionibu suorum populorum. Quæstio autem, de qua cer tatum fuisse & pro qua martyrem factum Christun indicat Esaias, est vers. 2. 3. An scilicet sit Deus omni potens, induens cælum caligine? Tertius characte est quotidie, & quidem mane proferre judicium suun in lucem sine defectu. Per judicium intellige sermo nes Domini, quibus vel redarguit Pharisæorun hypocrisin, qui omittentes graviora legis, & vin legis ignorantes Matth. V. 20. decimabant cumi num Matth. XXIII. 23. imo etiam propter traditio nes transgrediebantur legem Dei Matt. XV. 20. eo rundemve tyrannidem, quod præceptis importa bilibus onerabant populum Matth. XXIII. 4. idque ad devorandum domus viduarum Matt. XXIII. 14 & superbiam atq; ostentationem Matt. VI. & XXIII. 5. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. 12. 14. & ignorantiam mysterii Dei & Christi, quæ est clavis cognitionis, Matth. XXIII. 13. Luc. XI. 52. & falsam justitiam, sitam in externorum operum observantia & purificationum legalium usu, Matth. V. 10. vel causam suam & Dei defendit contra ipsorum calumnias. Edere judicium in lucem est ei judicio fidem evidenter facere per testimo nium Mosis & Prophetarum & opera divina tan quam opera proprii Patris.
