In fine annectit even- tum hujus apparitionis Dei cum justitia & judicio; quod injustus nesciverit erubescere. Injusti sunt illi, quos Deus verbo suo judicasse intelligitur, & quos designavit v. 1. 2. 3. 4. & ex iis causis injusti. Omnes Prophetæ uno ore testantur, Christum non iri re- ceptum à suis, sed rejectum & reprobatum iri, & utrique domui Israelis & Judæ fore scandalo. Et hic locus, si quis alius, ostendit causam novissimi ex- cidii Hierosolymæ esse, quod noluerint eum agno- scere pro Deo suo, qui revera Deus ipsorum erat, & ipsius judicio non fuerint patefacti. Hæc ille.

## 3:6
Verse 6. I HAVE DESTROYED THE NATIONS] I have cut off the nations. That is, the ten tribes through Tiglath-Pileser and Shalmaneser. God is speaking.

AND THEIR CORNERS ARE DISSIPATED] That is, the towers, as above in 1:16.

I HAVE MADE THEIR WAYS DESERTED] The streets.

WHILE THERE IS NO ONE WHO PASSES BY] So that there is no one who passes by.

WITH NO MAN REMAINING NOR ANY INHABITANT] That is, not even women or children.

It is not credible that Israel is signified by the name of the nations. Others think that verbs of the past tense denote a certain future event. I will destroy the neighboring nations, and their corners, in vengeance for Jerusalem, so that, moved by it, it may learn to fear me. Thus Christoph. à Castro; Cornel. à Lapide understands by the nations the Syrians, Armenians, Parthians, and others lying between or adjacent to Babylon and Jerusalem, which, as being nearer, Nebuchadnezzar subjugated first before he invaded the Jews. The Israelites were not so much cut off as they were led away elsewhere by Shalmaneser. But those things sound in the past tense: I have cut off the nations, their corners are desolate, I have made their streets desolate, so that there was no one who would pass by, their cities are devastated, so that there was no man, no inhabitant. And therefore, an enallage should not be established rashly. For the consequences also sound in the past tense. I said, surely he will fear me, etc. And therefore Cocceius accepts these things in such a way that this prophecy has the character of a commemoration, and a sign of the time of the coming of Christ is expressed here; namely: After God had brought to ruin notable nations as an example to the Jewish people. But what are these nations? In the previous chapter, we understood it concerning the Assyrians, Cushites, Philistines, and Moabites. From these, it is clear that Christ had to come after Nineveh had been destroyed by the Chaldeans, after Egypt had been fully defeated by the Persians, after the Philistines had been subdued by the Greeks, and these themselves had been so enervated in a part of their empire that their colonies founded in Palestine were reduced to servitude by the Jews: and thus with the Roman empire now prevailing; for the power of the Greeks was to be diminished by the Romans. With which matter the Colossus of Daniel in chapter 2 and the prophecy of chapter 11 clearly agree.

Latin:

Vers. 6. DISPERDIDI GENTES] Excidi gentes. Id est, decem tribus per Teglath phalassarum & Salmanasarem. Deus loquitur.

ET DISSIPATI SUNT ANGULI EARUM] Id est, turres, ut supra I. 16.

DESERTAS FECI VIAS EORUM] Plateas.

DUM NON EST QUI TRANSEAT] Ut non sit qui transeat.

NON REMANENTE VIRO NEQUE ULLO HABITATORE] Id est, ne feminis quidem aut pueris.

Non est credibile Israelem gentium nomine si- gnificari. Verba præteriti temporis rem futuram cer- tam denotare alii putant. Disperdam gentes vicinas, & angulos earum in vindictam Hierosolymæ, ut ea permota discat me timere. Ita Christoph. à Castro, Cor- nel. à Lapid. per gentes Syros, Armenos, Parthos aliosq; inter Babylonem & Hierosolymam inter- jacentes vel adjacentes intelligit, quas, utpote vici- niores prius subjugavit Nabuchodonosor, ante- quam Judæos invaderet. Israelitæ non tam excisi erant, quam aliorsum traducti à Salmanasare. Sed in præterito illa sonant: Exscidi gentes, desolati sunt anguli earum, desolavi vicos earum, ne esset, qui trans- iret, devastatæ sunt urbes earum, ne esset vir, ne esset incola. Ideoque non temere enallage statuenda. Nam & consequentia præteritum sonant. Dixi certe timebit me, &c. Ideoque accipit hæc Coccejus ita, ut Prophetia hæc habeat instar commemora- tionis & signum hic exprimatur temporis adven- tus Christi; nimirum: Postquam Deus notabiles gentes pessum dedisset in exemplum populo Judæo. At quæ hæ gentes? Superiore capite intellexi- mus de Assyriis, Cuschæis, Palæstinis, Moabitis. Ex iis liquet debuisse Christum venire, postquam Ninive esset destructa per Chaldæos, postquam Ægyptus plene esset debellata per Persas, postquam Palæ- stini essent edomiti per Græcos, & hi ipsi in parte sui imperii sic essent enervati, ut eorum coloniæ in Palæstina conditæ à Judæis, in servitutem redi- gerentur: atque adeo jam obtinente imperio Roma- no: quippe Græcorum potentia per Romanos mi- nuenda erat. Qua cum re plane concinit Danie- lis Colossus cap. II. & Prophetia capitis XI.

## 3:7
Verse 7.

I SAID: YET YOU WILL FEAR ME] I said: at least you will fear me: the city of Jerusalem.

YOU WILL ACCEPT DISCIPLINE] You will follow the law.

AND HER DWELLING WILL NOT PERISH] Lest her dwelling perish. A change of person is frequent among the Hebrews.

FOR ALL THINGS IN WHICH I HAVE VISITED HER] Every (good) thing which I established (which I promised in the law) upon her, supply: will come. Thus the Chaldean, and פקד is taken no otherwise in 2 Chron. 36:23.

BUT RISING EARLY THEY CORRUPTED ALL THEIR THOUGHTS] They pursued the worst endeavors. Rising early: that is, most diligently. A similar manner of speaking is found in Jer. 11:7, 25:3, 29:19, Isa. 5:11.

THE SECOND EVANGELICAL PART. Vers. 8, following.

Zephaniah promises the outpouring of divine wrath upon the enemies of the Church and the evangelical preaching among the peoples, so that all may commonly call upon the name of the Lord; and he predicts the reduction of the dispersed, and the conversion of the remnants of the people: and thus he provokes even the abject to joy in Christ the King and Savior, and promises the remission of sins and glory.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

DIXI: ATTAMEN TIMEBIS ME] Dixi: sal- tem tu timebis me: civitas Hierosolymorum.

SUSCIPIES DISCIPLINAM] Legem sequeris.

ET NON PERIBIT HABITACULUM EJUS] Ne pereat habitaculum ejus. Mutatio personæ frequens He- bræis.

PROPTER OMNIA IN QUIBUS VISITAVI EAM] Omne (bonum) quod constitui (quod in lege pro- misi) super eam, supple veniet. Ita Chaldæus, nec aliter sumitur פקד 2. Par. XXXVI. 23.

VERUNTAMEN DILVCVLO SVRGENTES CORRVPERVNT OMNES COGITATIONES SVAS] Pessima sectati sunt studia. Diluculo surgentes: id est, di- ligentissime. Simile loquendi genus Jerem. XI, 7. XXV, 3. XXIX. 19. Esa. V. 11.

PARS SECUNDA EVANGELICA. Vers. 8. seqq.

Promittit Zephanias effusionem iræ divinæ in hostes Ecclesiæ & Evangelicam concionem penes populos, ut omnes communiter nomen Domini invocent; ac prædicit reductionem dispersorum, & conversio- nem reliquiarum populi: adeoque ad gaudium in Christo Rege, & Servatore etiam abjectos provo- cat, & remissionem peccatorum ac gloriam polli- cetur.

## 3:8
Vers. 8.

WHEREFORE WAIT FOR ME] Wait for me. He returns to the second person. It is the same as elsewhere: I [will come] to you.

IN THE DAY OF MY RISING FOR THE FUTURE] For that time when I shall rise for the spoil. He is said to rise who goes out from the camp into battle.

FOR MY JUDGMENT] It is decreed for me:

THAT I MAY GATHER THE NATIONS, AND ASSEMBLE THE KINGDOMS] I will drive into one place a huge multitude of Judah and Benjamin from many prefectures (which prefectures the Hebrews often improperly call kingdoms, and the Greeks have translated in some places as metropolises), namely within the city of Jerusalem.

AND I WILL POUR OUT UPON THEM] Thus gathered.

MY INDIGNATION] The effect of my wrath, through the Chaldeans.

FOR IN THE FIRE OF MY ZEAL SHALL ALL THE EARTH BE DEVOURD] Judea, as above I. 18. The Jews refer these things in a more excellent sense to the day of universal judgment, as the preceding things to the war of Gog and Magog.

By the nations and kingdoms the tribes of Judah and Benjamin cannot be understood. This interpretation is unusual. Therefore, others interpret the nations and kingdoms of the Gentiles as all referring to one thing, but not in the same way. Most view the nations as the object of punishment, upon which God wishes to pour out His severity. Cocceius, however, makes the nations the instrument of punishment and judgment, which is to be exercised against the Jews. For by these words, 'therefore wait for me, saith Jehovah, for the day that I rise up לעד FOR PERPETUITY,' he wishes to imply that an intimation and a time for exercising judgment are contained therein, because Christ addresses His own, and bids them patiently await His resurrection from the dead to PERPETUAL and immortal life. But by these words he judges that the allied nations, the gathered kingdoms, and the circumstance of time are noted, namely, the gathering of most kingdoms into one empire, to wit, the Roman: so that by the resurrection of Christ the pouring out of wrath upon Jerusalem is connected, so that it might be consumed by the zeal of God, through the nations gathered into one empire and society: which he thinks is written with a sunbeam.

We do not affect, nor do we easily approve of, singular interpretations. But this explanation, I know not how, commends itself to us. For those characters which Cocceius observed indicate not obscurely the time of the New Testament. And the sum of the accusation fits it perfectly: Woe to him to whom it was given to see (God manifested, which the elders so greatly desired) and to those things brought (peculiarly into the possession of the Lord) to the oppressing city (but it did only this, that it might oppress its asserter and Goel) it did not listen to the voice (of him) the voice, understand, says Cocceius, not so much of the pious prophets, and the forerunner of Christ, Is. XL. 3, as of the Son of God himself, compare verse 5 and Micah VI. 9. The voice of Jehovah, who calls to the city, is heard. Whom it saw and heard, and did not obey. For if it were without this emphasis, it would have sufficed to say לא שמעה it did not hear. JEHOVAH IT HAS NOT TRUSTED IN ITS GOD (whom it had in its midst, Christ, John XX. 20. The Father speaks of the Son:) IT HAS NOT APPROACHED, when it saw and heard its God and was addressed by him as his own people. This was the sum of the mandate, that it should acknowledge the Son of God revealed in the flesh as Jehovah and its God; Jehovah, that is, he who was from the beginning, and came to it, that he might become in fact that which he declared himself to be, namely, just and the justifier of him who believes in himself; its God, that is, he who had set this people apart from all nations, and had offered to it righteousness in himself by faith through the νομοθεσίαν of the covenant of grace, John I. 11. He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. Nor do those things which are proposed for the sake of proof in the following verses fit any less: Her princes in her midst are roaring lions: Her judges are evening wolves, who have not gnawed the bones in the morning (famished wolves, who all day from morning to evening have gnawed no bone) Her prophets are futile, men of deceits: Her priests profane the holy, they do violence to the law. If at any time such were in JERUSALEM, it is notorious that they were so in the latest time: yet that phrase, they profane THE HOLY, I would rather take as referring to the place dedicated to God, which they profaned with their vices, infidelity, and injustice, than to the body of the Son of God, the temple: because the law is connected with the holy: they do violence to the law, and it is finally a matter of the presence of the Lord in their midst, verse 5, and of the contempt and rejection of the same: concerning which Cocceius says thus: THE LORD WAS IN THE MIDST OF IT. This cannot be understood of the presence through symbols, the Ark and the Cherubim (for those were not in the second temple) or the temple, because there was no שכינה σκήνωσις in it after the Babylonian captivity. Nor even through the Prophets; because in the latest time Prophecy ceased. Nor does the treatment of the law suffice, insofar as it was instituted by the elders. For they did violence to the law. The emphasis of the words demands no less a real presence of God among his people than that concerning which Moses adjured God. Exod. XXXIII. 2, 3, 5, 9, 10, 11, 14. Moses and the people saw God in the appropriated tent, in the cloud and pillar of fire, and heard his voice. Here the phrase is the same; and it is an antithesis of the Lord to the temple, the priests, and the prophets treating the law; and it is attributed to the Lord that he brought forth judgment every morning according to the law. How was this word fulfilled, if he was not as present as he was to Moses and the people in the desert? In this way, therefore, all the Prophecies are to be understood which promise that God will dwell among his people while the second house stands, and will visit it, such as are the excellent ones in Zechariah, and which we have collected in our treatise on the last things of Moses. But since it is also evident from this Prophet that the Lord will so conduct himself among his people that he will judge those who contradict, and be accused by them, and even be killed: it is impossible that the words of this prophecy could have been fulfilled without the incarnation of God himself or the assumption of human nature. How the other predicates, which occur here concerning God manifested in the midst of Jerusalem, fit the days of the flesh of Christ, we have observed in relation to verse 5 from the same Cocceius.

Furthermore, the sign of the time of the advent is also explained at verse 8. Thus also this speech of GOD the Father, who had spoken in verse 5, and indeed will be continued from the beginning of the chapter to verse 7. I said surely you will fear me, you will be corrected by example, (or you will receive discipline) and his dwelling (the city of Jerusalem) will not be cut off, all that which I commended to it. That is, the treasure of the wisdom of God hidden from the ages for the Church and the holy ones of God. For these things had been entrusted to it, which the Lord even wished to leave to them, if they had revered him. But they anticipated and corrupted all their pursuits: whence follows the divine sentence: Wherefore (God the Father is still speaking, but in such a way that he now introduces the Son speaking) wait for me, says Jehovah, (the Son of God thus inciting believers to a faithful expectation of himself, and refreshing them with the sweet promise which is subjoined in verse 9 and following) wait for me for the day, when I shall rise into perpetuity. For my judgment is (God the Father continues speaking) to gather the nations and to associate the kingdoms, to pour out upon THEM my severity, all the heat of my wrath. For by the fire of my zeal the whole earth shall be consumed. These words are now of God the Father, as the following verse teaches: Then I will restore to the peoples a pure lip, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord. For God speaks of the Lord. The Father of the calling upon the name of the Son: and verse 12, They shall trust, he says, in the name of the Lord (the Messiah) in whom is all our trust and hope. Compare Ps. II. 12, Joel II. 32, of whom verse 15, The King of Israel the Lord is in your midst. Now, therefore, God, about to console the faithful, threatens judgment through the gathered nations and associated kingdoms, a judgment to be exercised UPON THEM, whose extreme wickedness he had noted. For that the Jews are the object, and not the nations, the whole context urges. For he had complained about the Jews, and had recounted their stubbornness at length. Therefore, the final destruction is now threatened to them: but not to the nations. He had already spoken of the nations in the past in v. 6. I HAVE CUT OFF NATIONS, their corners are desolate, etc., and he had brought them forth as a παράδειγμα to the Jewish people, who, however, could not be brought to repentance either by their example or by the very coming of the Son of God. Whence the nations were to be gathered to pour out the severity of the Lord against the Jews, so that that whole land (totally and finally) may be consumed by the fire of the Lord's zeal.

Therefore, other interpretations do not agree, which make the nations the object of the severity. And we see how the interpreters have twisted themselves here, while they did not notice this opinion of the Prophet. Sanctius, with the Chaldean and Cyril, interprets these things concerning the plundering of Babylon by Cyrus. Osiander thinks that these things were fulfilled in the Egyptians, Idumeans, Moabites, Ammonites, Philistines, and other enemies of the people of God, partly afflicted by Nebuchadnezzar after the capture of Jerusalem, and partly overthrown by the Medes and Persians who destroyed the Babylonians. But in this way, they are referred to very different times, which are predicted to be in the future at the same time, with the kingdoms gathered and collected: and the nations are constituted as the object of the judgment, not the people, with whom the Prophet has business, and to whom the judgment of God is threatened, because rising early they corrupted all their thoughts, that is, they applied themselves with great zeal to sins, and devoted effort to evil things on purpose. Nor did God then bring it about that He was worshipped by all nations with one shoulder, which with that judgment of God, in this order of time is connected. And Castrius rightly notes that the promises are more excellent than those which were fulfilled in that people returned from captivity.…

Finally, the Hebrews themselves acknowledge that these things were by no means fulfilled at that time, and therefore they refer their fulfillment to the coming of their Messiah. But also almost all Christians agree on this, that these things are to be understood concerning the coming of Christ: although some refer them to the first, others to the second coming. Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus, Lyra, Vatablus, and Clarius explain this concerning the second coming and the punishment of the nations therein, so that the elect may celebrate God with a pure lip; whose opinion, however, as Castrius likewise observed, cannot hold ground, because the ingratitude of the Jews is brought forward here as the cause of the Lord's severe judgment, by the illative particle: Therefore wait for me: whence not the nations, but the Jews will be subjected to the same. Nor can these things be accepted concerning the final coming of Christ, because the discourse is about the concordant and unanimous worship of the Christian people, to be propagated even beyond the rivers of Ethiopia. Furthermore, those who acknowledge that it concerns the first coming, and say that Christ was about to rise to the Evangelical battle, or to the prey, and was about to emerge a victor to those acting, are unable to explain how such a spiritual victory is consistent with the indignation which the Lord here threatens to the nations, and with the wrath of his fury and the fire of zeal about to devour the whole earth. Whence Cornelius, since he cannot otherwise explain such divine vengeance, feigns that that severity and indignation of God consists in this, that he makes enemies friends, and converts infidels, and makes them faithful: Which, however, is not of severity, not of wrath, but of grace and mercy, both according to the style of the Holy Spirit and according to the truth of the matter. In what, therefore, the treasure of divine mercy explains itself, that is ascribed to divine wrath, indignation, and severity only in an alien and distorted way. No less ignorantly does the same Cornelius interpret these things concerning the first and second coming of Christ at the same time, and says that Christ rose to the prey, both because he preyed upon the nations through the Gospel, and because he preyed upon the Fathers from Limbo: and that at the second coming he will prey upon all infidels, and will deliver them to hell. Which, as they are inept, so to recall such disparate things to the same letter is of nothing but Jesuitical or stony subtlety.

Moreover, almost all interpreters agree on this, that these things pertain to the times of Christ, and Eusebius (Book I, Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. XVII), Augustine (Book XVIII, De Civitate Dei, ch. XXXIII), Jerome, Theodoret, Hugo, Dionysius, Arias, Castrius, Winckelm, Tarnovius, and others refer these to the coming of Christ, although some understand the words קומי לער concerning the Lord rising, or girding himself for the prey, while others interpret them concerning his resurrection from the dead, by which he was about to rise to eternity or eternal life. Most interpret the particle לער as 'for the prey' with David Kimchi from Gen. 49:27, Isa. 33:23. But R. Aben-Ezra explains it as perpetuity, whom Coccejus follows. The Hebrews themselves, especially the ancients, as Jerome reports, confess that the Prophet is prophesying about the time of the coming of the Messiah, in which kingdoms are to be destroyed, and the people of the Lord are to worship one God, and speak the Hebrew language, as in the beginning, although they wish this to be understood concerning their Messiah, whom they still expect, and not only in a more excellent sense, as Grotius perverts their mind, but according to the letter. Because they do not provide another literal sense there. They, however, err not only in this, that they still await the Messiah, but that they connect his coming with the universal judgment. Meanwhile, they rightly explain it concerning the Messiah. And these things are explained concerning the calling of the nations to the kingdom of the Messiah in Bereshith Rabba, section 88. Saying of Amos 9:11.

on that day I will rebuild the tabernacle of David, etc. So that the whole world may become one collection, according to that of Zephaniah ch. 3, v. 9. Because then I will give to the nations a chosen lip, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, and serve him with one shoulder. And upon Gen. 41:44. And because of this, David says in Ps. 67:4, All peoples will confess to you, etc. And why did he mention, 'they will confess to you,' four times? As if to say, they will confess to you with their heart, with their mouth, with their good works, and they will confess to you with all these together, just as it is said in Soph. 3:9. Because then I will turn to the peoples a chosen lip, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, and that they may serve him with one shoulder. Moreover, there is no name of the Lord except the Messiah, of whom it is said in Es. 30:27, Behold the name of the Lord comes from afar. He teaches that it is to be said concerning God, just as it is said in Jer. 31:3, From afar God appeared to me. And because of this God said in Jer. 23:23. Am I a God from near, and not a God from afar? And why will they serve him with one shoulder? Therefore, because the principality was made upon his shoulders, just as it is said in Es. 9:6. And the principality was upon his shoulder. So also R. Solomon in Es. 54, He shall be called the God of the whole earth, because the nations will be converted to the law of God, and thus it is written in Sophon. 3:9, That they may all call upon the name of the Lord, and serve him with one shoulder.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

QVAPROPTER EXPECTA ME] Exspectate me. Redit ad secundum personam. idem est quod alibi: ego ad vos.

IN DIE RESVRRECTIONIS MEÆ IN FVTV- RVM] In id tempus cum surgam ad spolium. Surgere di- citur, qui è castris in prælium egreditur.

QVIA JVDICIVM MEVM] Decretum mihi est:

VT CONGREGEM GENTES, ET COLLI- GAM REGNA] In unum compellam ingentem multitudi- nem Judæ & Benjaminis ex præfecturis plurimis (quas præ- fecturas sæpe regna improprie vocant Hebræi, & Græci ver- tcrunt alicubi μητροπόλεις) nempe intra urbem Hierosoly- ma.

ET EFFVNDAM SVPER EOS] Ita collectos.

INDIGNATIONEM MEAM] Effectus iræ meæ, per Chaldæos.

IN IGNE ENIM ZELI MEI DEVORABITVR OMNIS TERRA] Judæa, ut supra I. 18. Judæi hæc sen- su excellentiore, ad diem judicii universalis referunt, ut præcedentia ad bellum Gog & Magog.

Per gentes & Regna intelligi non possunt tri- bus Judæ & Benjamin. Insolens est hæc acceptio. De gentibus igitur & regnis gentium, interpretantur alii ad unum omnes, sed non eodem modo. Pleri- que gentes ut objectum pœnæ spectant, in quod seve- ritatem suam Deus velit effundere. Coccejus vero gentes instrumentum pœnæ & judicii facit, quod ex- ercendum sit adversus Judæos. Verbis enim istis, quapropter præstolamini me, ait Jehovah, ad Diem, quo surgam לעד IN PERPETUITATEM, inti- mationem & tempus judici exercendi contineri vult, quod Christus alloquatur suos, eosque pa- tienter jubeat expectare resurrectionem suam à mortuis ad vitam PERPETUAM, & immortalem. His vero verbis gentes sociatæ, regna collecta & instrumentum judicii, & circumstantiam temporis notari censet, collectionem sc. plerorumque re- gnorum in uno imperio, nimirum Romano: ut ita resurrectione Christi connectatur effusio iræ in Hiero- solymam, ut zelo Dei tota conflagret, per gentes in imperium unum, & societatem congregatos: Quæ radio solis scripta putat.

Non affectamus, nec facile etiam probamus singularia. Sed explicatio hæc nescio quomodo se- se nobis probet. Nam characteres illi, quos obser- vavit Coccejus, haud obscure indicant tempus N. T. Et summa accusationis apprime illi congruit: Væ cui datum est videre (Deum manifestatum, quod tantopere optarunt majores) quæque afferta, (pe- culiariter in peculium Domini) urbi opprimenti (sed id solum egit, ut opprimeret assertorem & Goelem suum) non auscultavit voci (ejus) voci, in- tellige, inquit Coccejus, non tam prophetarum piorum, & Anteambulonis Christi, Es. XL. 3. quam ipsius Filii Dei, confer. vers. 5. & Mich. VI. 9. Vox Jehovæ, qui civitatem vocat, auditur. Quem vidit & audivit, & non obedivit. Nam si absque hac emphasi esset, suffecerat dicere לא שמעה non au- divit. JEHOVÆ NON EST CONFISA AD DEUM suum (quem in medio habebat Christum Joh. XX. 20. Loquitur Pater de Filio:) NON ACCESSIT, quum videret & audiret Deum suum & ab eo tanquam populus suus compellaretur. Hæc summa mandati erat, ut agnosceret Filium Dei revelatum in carne Jehovam & Deum suum; Jehovam, h. e. illum, qui ab initio fuit, & venit ad illum, ut fieret ipso facto hoc, quod se esse de- claravit, nimirum justus & justificans eum, qui credit in se; Deum suum, h. e. illum, qui hunc populum ex omnibus gentibus secreverat, eique justitiam in se ex fide per νομοθεσίαν fœderis gratiæ obtulerat Joh. I. 11. Ad propria venit, & proprii eum non recepe- runt. Nec minus conveniunt, quæ probationis cau- sa vers. seqq. proponuntur: Principes ejus in medio ejus leones rugientes: Judices ejus lupi vespertini, qui non roserant ossa matutino (lupi famelici, qui toto die à mane ad vesperam nullum os roserunt) Prophetæ ejus futiles, viri fallaciarum: Sacerdotes ejus profanant sanctum, vim faciunt legi. Si ullo tempore tales HIEROSOLYMIS fuere, novis- simo certe fuisse, notorium est: illud tamen profanant SANCTUM, malim de loco Deo dica- to, quem vitiis suis, infidelitate, injustitia profana- runt, quam de corpore Filii Dei templo accipere: quia cum sancto connectitur lex: vim faciunt le- gi, & de præsentia Domini in medio earum vers. 5. ejusdemque comtemtu & rejectione demum agitur: ad quem ita Coccejus: DOMINUS ERAT IN MEDIO ILLIUS. Hoc non potest intelligi de præ- sentia per symbola, Arcam & Cherubinos (Nam ea non fuerunt in templo secundo) vel templum, quia in eo non fuit שכינה σκήνωσις post captivitatem Babylonicam. Neque etiam per Prophetas; quia novissimo tempore cessavit Prophetia. Neque sufficit tractatio legis, quatenus ea fuit instituta à senioribus. Nam ii vim fecerunt legi. Verbo- rum emphasis postulat non minus propriam præ- sentiam Dei apud populum suum, quam de qua ob- testabatur Moses Deum. Exod. XXXIII. 2. 3. 5. 9. 10. 11. 14. Moses & populus viderunt Deum in tu- gurio appropriato, nube & columna ignis, & ipsius vocem audiverunt. Hic phrasis eadem est; & est antithesis Domini ad templum, Sacerdotes & Pro- phetas tractantes legem; & Domino attribuitur, quod singulis matutinis judicium, secundum legem protulerit. Quomodo impletum fuit hoc verbum, si non fuit æque præsens, ac Mosi & populo in deserto? Hoc igitur modo intelligenda sunt omnes Pro- phetiæ, quæ promittunt, fore ut Deus habitet inter populum suum stante domo secunda, & visitet eum, quales sunt egregiæ apud Zachariam & nos conve- ximus in tractatu de ultimis Mosis. Quoniam ve- ro etiam ex hac Propheta constat, sic Dominum ver- saturum in populo suo ut judicet contradicentes, & accusetur ab ipsis, imo & occidatur: impossibile est ut verba hujus prophetiæ potuerunt impleri citra incarnationem ipsius Dei sive assumtionem hu- manæ naturæ. Quomodo cætera prædicata, quæ de Deo manifestato in medio Hierosolymæ hic occurrunt, diebus carnis Christi conveniant ad v. 5. ex eodem Coccejo observavimus.

Porro signum etiam temporis adventus ad v. 8. expositum. Ita etiam oratio hæc DEI Patris qui v. 5. loquutus erat, imo inde à capitis initio continua- bitur v. 7. Dixi certe timebis me, emendaberis exem- plo, (vel suscipies disciplinam) & non exscindetur mansio illius (Civitas Hierosolyma) omne id quod commendavi illi. Id est thesaurus sapientiæ Dei à se- culis reconditus Ecclesiæ & sancti Dei. Hæc enim credita ipsi erant, quæ ipsis etiam relinquere vole- bat Dominus, si ipsum reveriti fuissent. Atqui præverterunt & corruperunt omnia studia sua: unde sequitur divina sententia : Quapropter (lo- quitur adhuc Deus Pater, sed ita, ut introducat nunc loquentem Filium) præstolamini me, ait Jeho- vah, (Filius Dei excitans ita ad fidelem sui expe- ctationem credentes, eosdemque suavi promis- sione, quæ v. 9. seqq. subjungitur, recreans) præ- stolamini me ad diem, quo surgam in perpetuitatem. Nam judicium meum est (pergit loquendo Deus Pa- ter) ad congregandum gentes & ad sociandum regna, ad effundendum in ILLOS severitatem meam, omnem æstum iræ meæ. Nam igne zeli mei comedetur tota terra. Verba hæc jam Dei Patris, uti versus sequens docet : Tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut in- vocent omnes in nomine Domini. Loquitur enim Deus de Domino. Pater de Filii invocando no- mine: & v. 12. Sperabunt, inquit, in nomine Domini (Messiæ) in quo omnis nostra fiducia & spes est. Confer. Ps. II. 12. Joel. II. 32. de quo v. 15. Rex Is- rael Dominus in medio tui. Jam ergo fideles con- solaturus Deus judicium per gentes collectas & regna sociata, judicium minatur IN ILLOS, quo- rum improbitatem extremam notarat, exercen- dum. Nam quod objectum sint Iudæi, non vero gentes, totus contextus urget. De Judæis enim questus erat, eorumque pervicaciam prolixe re- censuerat. Ideoq; illis novissimum exitium jam com- minatur: non vero gentibus. De gentibus jam in præterito loquutus erat v.6. EXSCIDI GENTES, desolati sunt anguli earum, &c. easque in παράδειγ- μα. Judaico populo produxerat, qui vero nec exemplo earum, nec ipso adventu Filii Dei ad fru- gem reduci potuit. Unde gentes congregandæ erant ad effundendam adversus Judæos severita- tem Domini, ut terra illa tota (totaliter & finaliter) igne zeli Domini comedatur.

Non ergo conveniunt aliæ interpretationes, quæ gentes objectum severitatis faciunt. Et videmus, quomodo se hic torserint Interpp. dum hanc sen- tentiam Prophetæ non adverterunt. Sanctius, cum Chaldæo, ac Cyrillo, de direptione Babylonis per Cy- rum hæc interpretatur. Osiander ea in Ægyptiis, Idumæis, Moabitis, Ammonitis, Philistæis, aliisq́; ho- stibus populi Dei, partim per Nabuchodonosarem, post captam Hierosolymam afflictis, partim per Medos & Persas eversis Babyloniis, impleta esse putat. Sed ita ad diversissima tempora referuntur, quæ eodem tempore futura, congregatis & colle- ctis regnis prædicuntur: & objectum judicii con- stituuntur gentes, non populus, cum quo res est Prophetæ, & cui judicium Dei comminatur, quod diluculo surgentes corruperint omnes cogitationes suas, h. e. magno studio in peccata incubuerint, & rebus malis de industria operam dederint. Neque tum effecit Deus, ut ab omnibus gentibus humero u- no coleretur, quod cum isto judicio Dei, hac tem- poris ratione connectitur. Et excellentiora promissa esse, recte notat Castrius, quam quæ in illo popu- lo è captivitate reddito completa.

Denique ipsi Ebræi agnoscunt hæc illo tem- pore minime adimpleta fuisse, ideoque ad adven- tum Messiæ sui referunt eorum complementum. Sed & Christiani pleriq́; omnes in eo consentiunt, hæc de Christi intelligenda esse adventu : tametsi alii ad primum, ad secundum alii referant adven- tum. De secundo adventu, & gentium punitione in eodem, ut electi puro Deum celebrent labio, explicant Hieronymus, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus, Lyra, Vatablus, Clarius, quorum vero sententia, ut Castrius itidem observavit, ideo locum habere ne- quit, quod causa judicii severi Domini hic addu- catur ingratitudo Judæorum, vocula illativa : Qua- propter expectate me : unde non gentes, sed Judæi eidem subjicientur. Neque de adventu Christi novissimo hæc accipi possunt, quia sermo est de con- cordi, & unanimi Christiani populi cultu, etiam ul- tra flumina Æthiopiæ propagando. Porro qui de primo adventu agi agnoscunt, & Christum surre- cturum ad pugnam Evangelicam, vel ad prædam, vi- ctorem evasurum agentibus dicunt, explicare ne- queunt, quomodo talis victoria spiritualis indigna- tioni, quam hic minatur Dominus gentibus, i- ræque furoris ejus & igni zeli devoraturi omnem terram conveniat. Unde Cornelius, cum aliter nequeat vindictam ejusmodi divinam expedire, fingit eam severitatem & indignationem Dei in eo consistere, quod inimicos faciat amicos, & infideles convertat, faciatque fideles : Quod vero non est severitatis, non iræ, sed gratiæ & misericordiæ, & se- cundum stylum Spiritus S. & secundum rei veri- tatem. In quo ergo divinæ misericordiæ thesau- rus se explicat, id non nisi aliene ac contorte divi- næ iræ, indignationi, ac severitati adscribitur. Nec minus imperite idem Cornelius hæcce de primo & secundo adventu Christi simul interpretatur, Chri- stumque dicit surrexisse ad prædam, tum quod prædatus sit gentes per Evangelium, tum quod præda- tus Patres è Limbo : & quod adventu secundo præ- daturus sit omnes infideles, eosque inferno traditurus. Quæ uti inepta sunt, ita tam disparata ad eandem literam revocare subtilitatis non nisi Jesuiticæ, aut lapideæ est.

Cæterum in eo conveniunt pleriq; omnes In- terpp. ad tempora Christi hæc pertinere, atque ad adventum Christi referunt hæc Eusebius l. I. demonst. Evangelic. c. XVII. Augustinus l. XIIX. de Civ. Dei c. XXXIII. Hieronym. Theodoretus, Hugo, Dionysius, Arias, Castrius, Winckelm. Tarnovius, aliiqve, etsi nonnulli verba : קומי לער de Domino furgente, vel accingente se ad prædam intelligant, alii vero de resurrectione ejus à mortuis interpretentur, qua לער ad æternitatem vel æternam vitam surrecturus erat. Voculam לער de præda pleriq; interpretantur cum David Kimchio è Gen. XLIX. 27. Esa. XXXIII. 23. Sed R. Aben-Ezra perpetuitatem exponit, quem se- quitur Coccejus. Ebræi ipsi, imprimis veteres, re- ferente Hieronymo, fatentur de tempore adven- tus Messiæ Prophetam vaticinari, quo regna de- struenda, populusque Domini unum Deum vene- raturus sit, lingua Ebraica loquuturus, ut in princi- pio, tametsi hoc de Messia suo, quem adhuc expe- ctant, intellectum velint, nec id tantum sensu ex- cellentiori, ut Grotius mentem eorum pervertit, sed secundum literam. Quia alium literalem sensum ibi non tradunt. Qui vero non in eo solum errant, quod Messiam adhuc præstolentur, sed quod ad- ventum ejus cum judicio universali connectant. In- terim recte de Messia explicant. Et de vocatione gentium, ad regnum Messiæ hæc exponuntur in Beroschith Rabba sect. 88. Dictum Amos. 9. v. 11.

illo die reædificabo tabernaculum David &c. Ita ut universus mundus fiat una collectio, juxta illud Tsephaniæ cap. 3. v. 9. Quia tunc dabo gentibus la- bium electum, ut invocent omnes nomen Domi- ni, & serviant ei humero uno. Et super Gen. XLI. 44. Et propter hoc, dicit David Ps. 67. v. 4. Confite- buntur tibi populi omnes &c. Et cur memoravit, confitebuntur tibi, quatuor vicibus? Quasi dicat, confitebuntur tibi corde suo, ore suo, operibus suis bonis, & confitebuntur tibi his omnibus simul, sicut dictum est Soph. 3. v. 9. Quia tunc convertam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes in no- mine Domini, & ut serviant ei humero uno. Non est autem nomen Domini nisi Messias de quo dictum est Es. 30. v. 27. Ecce nomen Domini venit de lon- ge. Docet dicendum de Deo, sicut dictum est Jer. 31. v. 3. De longe Deus apparuit mihi. Et propter hoc dixit Deus Jer. 23. v. 23. Numquid ego Deus de prope, & non Deus de longe? Et quare servient ei humero uno? propterea, quia factus est principatus super humeros ejus, sicut dictum est Es. 9. v. 6. Et fuit principatus super humerum ejus. Sic & R. Salomo in Es. LIV. Deus totius terræ vocabitur, quo- niam gentes convertentur ad legem Dei, & sic est scri- ptum Sophon. 3. v. 9. Ut invocent omnes ipsi no- men Domini, & serviant illi humero uno.

## 3:9
V. 9. BECAUSE THEN I WILL RENDER TO THE PEOPLES A CHOSEN LIP, THAT THEY MAY ALL CALL UPON THE NAME OF THE LORD] But then (that is, afterwards; for often אז is taken in the meaning of a much distant time, as we said at Matth. 24:14 and 30) I will render to the peoples a pure lip, that they may all call upon the name of God. I will bring it about through the most grievous calamities which they will feel, and through the added promises, that led by repentance they may become such as they were once in the times of David, when the true God was worshipped with pious words and deeds. For ברורה, which is pure, the Greeks read בררה Εἰς γενεὰν ἀυτῆς, as Jerome also noted.

AND THAT THEY MAY SERVE WITH ONE SHOULDER] That is, jointly: shoulder or arm is to be taken here, μεταληπτικῶς, for that which is placed upon the arms, that is, a yoke. The LXX here not badly, ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἵνα.

Latin:

V. 9. QVIA TVNC REDDAM POPVLIS LABIVM ELECTVM, VT INVOCENT OMNES IN NOMINE DOMINI] At tunc (id est, postea; sæpe enim אז sumitur in significatione multum distantis temporis, ut diximus ad Matth. XXIV. 14. & 30.) reddam populis labium purum, ut omnes invocent Dei nomen. Efficiam per gravissimas quas sentient calamitates, & per promissiones additas, ut pœ- nitentia ducti tales fiant, quales olim Davidis temporibus fuere, cum piis verbis ac factis verus Deus coleretur. Pro ברורה, quod est purum, Græci legerunt בררה Εἰς γε- νεὰν ἀυτῆς, ut & Hieronymus notavit.

ET SERVIANT HVMERO VNO] Id est, jun- ctim: humerus sive armus hic sumendus, μεταληπτικῶς, pro eo quod armis imponitur, id est, jugo. LXX. hic non male, ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἵνα.

## 3:10
V. 10. FROM BEYOND THE RIVERS OF ETHIOPIA, THENCE MY SUPPLIANTS THE DAUGHTERS OF MY DISPERSED SHALL BRING MY OFFERING] We said at Isa. XVIII, where the same rivers of Ethiopia are treated, that מעבר often signifies not 'beyond,' but 'beside.' You may therefore translate not badly: From (places) beside the rivers of Ethiopia (situated) my suppliants, the offspring of my dispersed, bring me μαννὰ: that is, a cake of fine flour. In the war of Necho, many Jews were captured and carried off into Egypt, and from there sold as far as Ethiopia. Cyrus also, having made a treaty with the Ethiopians, took care that these be liberated, so that they too, with the others, returned to their fatherland and offered gifts there. See something similar in Isa. XI. 11, where there is likewise mention of those returning from Ethiopia. Thus Ptolemy Philadelphus liberated more than a hundred thousand Jews serving in distant lands by paying a price, and sent them back to their fatherland, as Josephus testifies, XII, 2.

These are not to be snatched away to the times of Cyrus, nor is the little word אז to be vexed: which in its customary meaning is the same as THEN. It therefore refers itself to the preceding, and teaches that these things will be in the same time. Nor is it permitted to attach another meaning to it at will. Add that the Prophet appends an explanation in v. 11, IN THAT DAY. It does not therefore designate a time far distant, but the same time which he had indicated. And the thing itself convinces that these pertain to the times of the N.T., which the subject then testifies: For the discourse is not about the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, but about PEOPLES AND NATIONS, which words Grotius, according to his custom, twists so that they refer to the Jews, when they denote nations rejected from the polity of Israel. Gen. XLIX. 10. Ps. CXVII. 1. Then the predicates themselves confirm it. For the propagation of divine worship beyond the rivers of Ethiopia is promised, in which all Interpreters agree, explaining the word מעבר according to the famous and most customary acceptance of BEYOND. [5] Christian Doctors acknowledge with great consensus that the prophecy is to be understood not of the Jews dispersed to the rivers of Ethiopia, but of the Gentiles to be converted to the kingdom of Christ. Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus M.

Hugo and other interpreters agree that it concerns the nations, and they understand 'a pure lip' either as the language of the nations or as the language and lip of God; and the former explain it thus: that the nations, having abandoned their diverse languages, will speak with one mouth, and will invoke the one name of God with one mind and heart, just as the Chaldean also explained: 'I will turn to all the nations a chosen language, so that they may all pray in the name of the Lord.' Others interpret it as one language, either Greek, from Galatinus, book XII, On the Arcana, chapter 3, or Latin. The Jews understand it as the Hebrew language to be used in the next life, but the unity refers not to the idiom, which cannot be one among all nations in this life (of which these things sound), but to the confession. But in truth, this is more correctly understood concerning the lip of God, and concerning the voice of the Gospel by Blessed Luther: 'Alsdann wil ich den Völckern anders predigen lassen mit freundlichen Lippen daß sie alle sollen des HErrn Namen anruffen' [Then I will let the nations be preached to differently with friendly lips, so that they all shall call upon the name of the Lord]: which he explains in the margin: 'das ist das Evangelium von der Gnade GOttes, welches uns erlöset von unsern Sünden' [that is the Gospel of the grace of God, which redeems us from our sins]: which exposition Cocceius also followed after Osiander, and confirmed more laboriously: It seems to me that the Prophet is not speaking about the purity of the lip of the nations yet! (For he might perhaps have stated it thus: אהפך לעמים שפה טהורה compare Isaiah 6:5. and that purity of the lip of the nations is understood in the second clause, 'they will call upon the name of the Lord') but about speech, whether pure, or rather clear or select, with which He Himself is to address the peoples, in place of the fact that He had not previously deigned to address them, or had spoken about them and to them, insofar as the word of God had been published through the Israelites, with a lip as if veiled and in speech not only sad and terrible, but also obscure. Parallel is Isaiah 2:2: 'Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem'; and He will argue, or will make a demonstration to many peoples. Isaiah 49:2: 'He has made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of His hand He has hidden me; and has made me a polished, or chosen, arrow,' etc. verse 6: 'I will give you as a light to the nations.' Isaiah 50:4: 'The Lord Jehovah has given me the tongue of the learned, that I may know how to speak a word in season to him who is weary.' Isaiah 61:1: 'Jehovah has anointed me to preach good tidings to the meek; He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,' etc. Psalm 45:3: 'Grace is poured upon your lips.' Conversely, to Israel, Psalm 2:5: 'Then He will speak to them in His wrath, and will trouble them in His fury.' Isaiah 28:11: 'For with stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people.' Isaiah 6:9, 10. He embraces that contrariety in these sayings: Isaiah 29:10, 19; Isaiah 65:1, 2, which St. Paul also cites in Romans 10:20, 21. Therefore, a polished, clear, chosen lip is the speech of the Gospel, unfolding every mystery of the kingdom of heaven, and placing it in the light without ambiguities, without wrappings, without a mixture of terror and accusation. That most sweet speech of invitation to the faith of grace was prepared for the nations, Isaiah 42:4: 'And the isles shall hope for His doctrine,' or they will listen with the hope and perseverance of learning, which is called προσκαρτέρησις [steadfastness]. This passage teaches that the nations will be called by another kind of speech, yet one built upon those things which the ancients had heard, namely, by the announcement of the promise made, the curse removed, peace procured, and servitude taken away, with the stipulation of faith. The Apostle treats of this calling in Romans 10:14. Thus Cocceius. To which also pertains the passage in Isaiah 52:7. Whatever the Greek LXX may have read in place of the word בררה, the Chaldeans, the translations of Aquila, Theodotion, and the Vulgate, and also of Symmachus, confirm that the Hebrew text certainly had it thus: for they rendered it ELECT, but the latter rendered it PURE.

But the words: 'THAT THEY MAY INVOKE THE NAME OF THE LORD,' are not interpreted as referring to invocation alone, much less to the pronunciation of the name of the Tetragrammaton, as the Jews foolishly imagine, but to the reception of the word of God, in which God is named, who and what He is, and the confession of the same (to which invocation also pertains), and the reception of the name of God, as Savior and Lord, so that they may wish to be called by Him, from a comparison of the passages Joel 3:5, Isaiah 40:15, Genesis 4:26, 2 Timothy 2:19. Cocceius, rendering it thus in this place, 'THAT THEY MAY CALL UPON THE NAME OF JEHOVAH,' says that the discourse is about the calling of the nations to the faith of the Messiah, 'AND THEY SHALL SERVE HIM WITH ONE SHOULDER.' It is signified, he says, by one spirit, consensus, one love, one faith, one word of God, and one Gospel, and one form of exercising the worship of God. Here liberty is rooted in peace. For because they ought to become one people, therefore they also ought to serve with one shoulder, and bear one yoke, and have one precept concerning the worship of God, namely, that the Jews should not worship God otherwise than the nations, and the nations should no longer be an abomination to the Jews: but the nations should so serve God, as Abraham in uncircumcision, and sanctified, and justified. We see this argumentation also used in Acts 15:14, 17, 19. Thus again Cocceius.

And the interpreters agree on this. But no one has easily been found, except Grotius, who believed that these should be restricted to the Jewish people. Calvin certainly refers the words to the dispersed Jews, 'beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, my suppliants, the daughters of my dispersed, shall bring my offering,' because those who offer sacrifices to God are to return to Judea from the furthest region of the Ethiopians. But he acknowledges that the former parts speak about the calling of the nations, and so he thinks it is added now that the Jews also will come with the nations, so that they may coalesce together in one consensus of faith into the true and pure worship of one God, and he extends this prophecy to the time of the Gospel. Others, however, judge that these also pertain to the nations to be called. Some take those words 'Atharai' and 'Phozai' as proper names, and understand them as concerning the nations living beyond the rivers of Ethiopia in this sense: 'beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the Atharai, the daughters of the Phozai, shall bring my offering.' But those names are more correctly established as appellative: and our blessed Osiander properly expressed the sense of these words: rendering the Hebrew thus: Beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants the daughters of my dispersion shall offer to me in sacrifice, that is, I shall have even among the nations scattered here and there in the world elect ones, whom I shall call to eternal life through the Gospel, they shall be offered to me through the preaching of the Apostles, as a most acceptable sacrifice. For as many persons as the Apostles, and their legitimate successors, converted either from the Gentiles or from the Jews, so many sacrifices they offered to God. Similarly Coccejus: Thence beyond the streams of Cush, my forces the daughter of my dispersed ones shall offer my gift: an oblation of this kind is that which is indicated in those places Is. XVIII. 7. LXVI. 20. Ps. XX. 3. עמך נדבות thy people are voluntary offerings, by the will of kings, and of peoples it is offered to thee as a gift. The passage in Is. XIX seems also to pertain to this.

21. and they shall serve, or shall perform worship with sacrifice and gift, namely by dismissing the free people of God to exercise spiritual worship, and by applying their resources to that matter. This oblation, therefore, by which the nations offer the sons of GOD as a gift, is resolved into the multiplication of the glorification of the name of GOD, and thus into a spiritual sacrifice. Such is that of which Malachi treats in chapter I. 11. Whoever cooperates so that the oblation of the Gentiles may be holy, Rom. XV. 16. they act, each in his own way, so that a true gift may be offered to God. This is opposed to the irrational, mute, and brute sacrifices of the Israelites: see the aforementioned place of Malachi, Ps. L.

Hof. XIV. 3. Dan. IX. 27. he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease. Therefore, those who offer are MY FORCES, as he explains the word אותי in Ez. VIII. 11, ch. XXXV. 13, Jerem. XXXIII. 26, from parallel passages (as to the sense) Gen. XVII. 14, Ps. XXII. 26, Isa. LIII. 11, 12, and he judges that the Church is designated by that reasoning, which consists of many: comparing Cant. VII. 4, ch. VIII. 11. Those to be offered are the assemblies of the dispersed, to be gathered to the Church, and to be offered to God, John XI. 52, Jer. III. 18, and speaking of the example (of those who are beyond the rivers of Cush), the Prophet understands the whole race of the Gentiles. In almost the same way, blessed Luther: Man wird mir meine Anbeter, nemlich die Zerstreueten von jenseit dem Wasser in Morenland, herbeybringen zum Geschenck: And blessed Winckelm. from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia they shall bring my suppliants, the sons of my dispersed (my dispersed ones), as my gift, or to me as an oblation. The matter of the Church. For it is gathered from the nations living throughout the whole world even beyond the rivers of Ethiopia. These nations, converted by the ministry of the Apostles and their successors, are offered to the Lord as a gift.

Latin:

V. 10. VLTRA FLVMINA ÆTHIOPIÆ, INDE SVP- PLICES MEI FILII DISPERSORVM MEORVM DE- FERENT MVNVS MIHI] Diximus ad Esa. XVIII. ubi de iisdem fluminibus Æthiopiæ agitur, מעבר sæpe non trans, sed juxta significare. Vertas igitur non male: A (locis) ad flumina Æthiopiæ (sitis) supplices mei, proles dispersorum meo- rum adferunt mihi μαννὰ: id est, libum è simila. Neconis bello multi Judæi capti, & in Ægyptum avecti, inde in Æ- thiopiam usque venditi sunt. Hos quoq; Cyrus, fœdere cum Æthiopibus facto, liberari curavit, ita ut & hi cum cæteris in patriam redierint, ibique dona obtulerint. Simile quid vide Esa. XI. 11. ubi itidem ab Æthiopia redeuntium men- tio est. Sic Ptolomæus Philadelphus Judæos plures centum millibus in oris longinquis servientes pretio dato liberavit, & in patriam remisit, testis Josephus XII, 2.

Non ad tempora Cyri hæc abripienda, neq; vo- cula אז vexanda: quæ usitata significatione idem est, quod TVNC. Refert ergo se ad præcedentia, atq; hæc eodem tempore futura docet. Neque enim pro lubitu aliam ipsi affingere licet significationem Adde, quod subjungat Propheta explicationem v. 11. IN DIE ILLA. Non ergo multum distans, sed idem tempus designat, quod indicarat. Et res ipsa convincit, hæc ad tempora N. T. pertinere, quod tum subjectum testatur: Non enim de Judæ & Ben- jaminis tribubus, sed de POPVLIS ET GENTI- BUS sermo est, quas voces, pro more suo, torquet Grotius, ut Judæos referant, quum gentes à poli- tia Israelis rejectas notent. Gen. XLIX. 10. Ps. CXVII. 1. tum prædicata ipsa confirmant. Nam promittitur cultus divini propagatio ultra flumina Æthiopiæ, in quo consentiunt omnes Interpp. vocem מעבר jux- ta famosam & usitatissimam acceptionem ULTRA exponentes. Nec de Judæis ad flumina Æthiopiæ dispersis, sed de gentilibus ad regnum Christi con- vertendis, vaticinium intelligendum esse magno consensu Doctores Christiani agnoscunt. Hiero- nymus, Theodoretius, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus M.

Hugo, aliique Interpp. conveniunt de gentibus agi, & vel de gentium lingua labium purum accipiunt, vel de lingua & labio Dei; & priores ita explicant, quod gentes relictis diversis loquutionibus uno ore loquuturæ, unum Dei nomen animo & corde uno sint invocaturæ, uti etiam Chaldæus exposuit: convertam in omnes gentes locutionem unam electam, ut precentur omnes in nomine Domini. Alii de lingua una vel Græca è Galatino l. XII. de Arcanis cap. 3. vel Latina interpretantur. Iudæi de lingua Ebræa in altera vita usurpanda accipiunt, verum unitas respicitur non idiomatis, quod inter omnes gentes in hac vita (de qua hæc sonant) unum esse nequit, sed confessionis. Verumenimvero rectius de labio Dei hoc intelligitur, & de Evangelii voce à B. Luthero: Alsdann wil ich den Völckern anders predigen lassen mit freundlichen Lippen daß sie alle sollen des HErrn Namen anruffen: quod in margine explicat: das ist das Evangelium von der Gnade GOttes, welches uns erlöset von unsern Sünden: quam ἔκθεσιν post Osiandrum Coccejus etiam sequutus est, & operosius confirmavit: Mihi videtur Prophetam non loqui de puritate labii gentium adhuc! (Hoc enim forte sic enunciasset: אהפך לעמים שפה טהורה confer. Es. VI. 5. & ea puritas labii gentium intelligitur in secundo colo, nuncupabunt nomen Domini) sed de loquela sive pura, sive potius clara aut selecta, qua ipse allocuturus sit populos, pro eo quod eos vel non dignatus fuerat alloquio antehac vel de illis & ad illas, quatenus verbum Dei per Israëlitas publicatum erat, locutus fuerat labio quasi velato & sermone non tantum tristi ac terribili, sed etiam obscuro. Parallelum est Es. II. 2. Ex Sione exibit lex, & verbum Domini ex Hierusalem; & arguet, sive demonstrationem faciet multis populis. Es. XLIX. 2. posuit os meum, ut gladium acutum, in umbra manus suæ occultavit me; & posuit me in telum nitidum, vel electum &c. vers. 6. Dabo te in lucem gentium Es. L. 4. Dominus Iehovah dedit mihi linguam eruditorum, ut norim opportune loqui cum fesso. Es. LXI. 1. unxit Jehova me ad evangelizandum mansuetis, misit me ad obligandum fractos corde &c. Psal. XLV. 3. effusa est gratia in labiis tuis. Contra ad Israelem Ps. II. 5. Tunc loquetur ad eos in ira sua, & æstu suo conturbabit ipsos. Es. XXVIII. 11. Nam fannis labii & in lingua alia loquetur ad populum hunc Es. VI. 9. 10. Contrarietatem illam complectitur his dictis Es. XXIX. 10. 19. Efa. LXV. 1. 2. quod & S. Paulus citat Rom. X. 20. 21. Labium igitur nitidum, clarum, electum est sermo Evangelii pandens omne mysterium regnum cœlorum, idque in luce ponens fine ambagibus, fine involucris, fine mistura terroris & accusationis. Suavissimum illud eloquium invitationis ad fidem gratiæ gentibus paratum erat Es. XLII. 4. Et doctrinam ejus insulæ sperabunt, sive cum spe, & perseverantia discendi, quæ προσκαρτέρησις dicitur, audient. Docet hic locus, Gentes alio genere sermonis, sed tamen exstructo in iis, quæ veteres audiverant, vocatum iri, nimirum annunciatione promissionis factæ, maledictionis sublatæ, pacis procuratæ, servitutis ablatæ cum stipulatione fidei. De hac vocatione agit Apostolus Rom. X. 14. Hæc Coccejus. Quo etiam pertinet locus Es. LII. 7. Quicquid vero Græci LXX. legerint loco vocis בררה Ebræum certe textum ita habuisse, Chaldai, Aquila, Theodotionis & Vulgati, nec non Symmachi quoque translationes confirmant: fiquidem illi ELECTUM, hic vero PURUM reddiderint.

Verba autem: UT INVOCENT NOMEN DOMINI, non de sola invocatione, multo minus de pronunciatione nominis Tetragrammati, ut ineptiant Ebræi, sed de receptione verbi Dei, in quo Deus nominatur, quis, & qualis sit, ejusdemq́, con- fessione (ad quam etiam invocatio pertinet) & sus- ceptione nominis Dei, tanquam Salvatoris & Domi- ni, ut ab ipso appellari velint, interpretatur è colla- tione locorum Joel. III. 5. Es. XL. 15. Gen. IV. 26. 2. Tim. II. 19. Coccejus, ita hoc loco reddens, UT NUNCUPENT NOMEN JEHOVÆ, de vo- catione gentium ad Messiæ fidem sermonem esse, ET SERVIANT IPSI HUMERO UNO. Signifi- catur, inquit, spiritus unus, consensus, amor unus, fides una, verbum Dei, & Evangelium unum, & for- ma exercendi cultum Dei unum. Hic radicatur liber- tas in pace. Quia enim unus populus fieri de- bent, ideo etiam debent servire humero uno, & unum jugum ferre, atque unum præceptum de co- lendo Deo habere, sc. ut non aliter colant Deum Judæi, atque gentes, & gentes Judæis non sint am- plius abominationi: Gentes autem sic serviant Deo, ut Abraham in præputio & sanctificatus, & justificatus. Hanc argumentationem etiam vide- mus usurpatam Act. XV. 14. 17. 19. Hæc iterum Coccejus.

Et conveniunt in eo Interpp. Ne- mo vero facile inventus est, præter Grotium, qui ad populum Judaicum hæc restringenda esse, cre- diderit. Calvinus sane ad Judæos dispersos refert verba, trans Æthiopiæ fluvios, supplices meæ filiæ di- sponsorum meorum offerent munus meum, quod ab ultima regione Æthiopum redituri sint in Judæam, qui sacrificia Deo offerant. Sed priora de vo- catione gentium loqui agnoscit, adeoque adjun- gi nunc putat, etiam cum gentibus venturos Ju- dæos, ut simul coalescant uno fidei consensu in ve- rum, & purum unius Dei cultum, & extendit hoc vaticinium ad tempus Evangelii. Alii tamen hæc etiam ad gentes vocandas pertinere censent. Qui- dam illas quoque voces Atharai & Phozai pro no- minibus propriis habent, & de gentibus intelligunt trans flumina Æthiopiæ habitantibus hoc sensu: trans flumina Æthiopiæ Atharai, filiæ Phozai defe- rent munus meum. Sed rectius ea nomina sta- tuuntur appellativa: sensumque horum verborum probe expressit B. Osiander noster: Ebraica ita reddens: Ultra flumina Æthiopiæ supplices mei fi- liæ dispersionis meæ offerent mihi in sacrificium, id est habebo etiam inter gentes passim in orbe disper- sas electos, quos per Evangelium vocabo ad vitam æternam, illi mihi per prædicationem Apostolo- rum offerentur, tanquam gratissimum sacrificium. Quot enim personas vel ex gentibus, vel ex Judæis Apostoli, eorumque legitimi successores conver- terunt, tot sacrificia Deo obtulerunt. Similiter Coccejus: Inde ultra fluenta Cuschitidos, copiæ meæ filiam dispersorum meorum offerent munus meum: hujus generis oblatio est, quæ indicatur istis locis Es. XVIII. 7. LXVI. 20. Psal. XX. 3. עמך נדבות populus tuus sunt voluntariæ oblationes, voluntate regum, & populorum tibi offertur tanquam mu- nus. Eo pertinere videtur etiam locus Es. XIX.

21. & servient, sive cultum præstabunt sacrificio & munere, sc. dimittendo liberum populum Dei ad cultum spiritualem exercendum, eique rei appli- cando suas opes. Hæc igitur oblatio, qua gentes filios DEI munus offerunt, resolvitur in multipli- cationem glorificationis nominis DEI, atque ita in spirituale sacrificium. Quale est de quo agit Malachias cap. I. 11. Quicunq; cooperantur ad hoc ut oblatio gentium sit sancta, Rom. XV. 16. faciunt suo quisq; modo, ut munus verum offeratur Deo. Hoc opponitur sacrificiis Israelitarum irrationa- libus, mutis, & brutis: vide d. l. Malachiæ, Psal. L.

Hof. XIV. 3. Dan. IX. 27. ceffare faciet facrificium & munus. Offerentes ergo sunt COPIÆ MEÆ, uti vocem אותי explicat Ez. IIX. 11. c. XXXV. 13. Jerem. XXXIII. 26. ex locis (qua fenfum) paral- lelis Gen. XVII. 14. Pf. XXII. 26. Efa. LIII. 11. 12. atque Ecclefiam ea ratione defignari arbitratur, quæ ex multis constat: conferens Cant. VII. 4. c. IIX. 11. Offerendi sunt cœtus difperforum, ad Ec- clefiam congregandi, Deoque offerendi Joh. XI. 52. Jer. III. 18. & de exemplo loquens Propheta (eorum, qui ultra flumina Cufchitidos sunt) to- tum gentilium intelligit genus. Eodem fere mo- do B. Lutherus: Man wird mir meine Anbeter, nemlich die Zerstreueten von jenseit dem Wasser in Morenland, herbeybringen zum Geschenck: Et B. Winckelm. à trans flumina Æthiopiæ fupplices meos filios difperforum meorum (difperfos meos) deferent munus meum, vel mihi in oblationem. Ma- teria Ecclefiæ. Colligitur enim ex gentibus per to- tum mundum habitantibus etiam ultra flumina Æ- thiopiæ. Hæ gentes ministerio Apoftolorum, & fuccefforum eorum conversæ offeruntur Domino in munus.

## 3:11
Ver. 11. IN THAT DAY] After that time.

THOU SHALT NOT BE ASHAMED FOR ALL THY DOINGS] You will no longer be affected with shame because of all your old pursuits: namely, because they will abstain from idolatry and other depravities.

WHEREIN THOU HAST TRANSGRESSED AGAINST ME] Before the time of the captivity.

FOR THEN I WILL TAKE AWAY OUT OF THE MIDST OF THEE THEM THAT REJOICE IN THY PRIDE] Those who were once the authors for you of exalting yourselves against the law of GOD, having died by an evil fate, will not be present with you.

AND THOU SHALT NO MORE BE HAUGHTY IN MY HOLY MOUNTAIN] Do not be haughty any longer in my temple: namely, by their example. It is pride to despise the law, which the priests themselves had done in the temple, above III. 4. this is what is called to sin ביד רמה that is, through pride. Num. XV. 29.

These things were not fulfilled after the return of Cyrus. For the doings of the Jews did not cease then. Not a few returned to their old pursuits. Nor were the authors of transgressing against the law, and those who sinned with a high hand, taken away entirely from the midst. He is speaking with Jerusalem, or with Judea converted to Christ, according to the opinion of all, as Castrius observed here: In that time, in which the nations shall be converted to me, you also, Jerusalem, with your sons who shall have adhered to Christ, will not have cause to be affected with shame for all your evil works which you have committed against me, now already forgiven to you. Thus Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, Montanus, and others understand it. But David Kimchi, whom Vatablus and Robertus follow, explains it not ineptly: in that day you will not be forced to blush for any of your works which you are about to do, because you will do them in equity and justice, not as now, when you are forced to blush for the evils in which you are accustomed to transgress against me. He adds two causes, however, why she will not then have cause to be ashamed: because I will take away the occasions of pride, which is the origin of all vices. The second, because I will take away from the midst of you those who rejoice in your pride. In Hebrew, those who exult in your pride, that is, in your excellence and dignity: who, namely, please themselves because of the benefits with which I have deigned to favor you above the nations. Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Lyra, and Montanus think these to be the Scribes and Pharisees, or he understands those Jews who bore with difficulty that the nations were being admitted to the Evangelical law, and boasted that they alone were worthy of that grace: whom the book of Acts ch. 10 and the Epistle to the Romans refute. The other occasion of pride was: and thou shalt no more be haughty in my holy mountain. Namely, concerning the temple built on Mount Zion, of which they boasted most, saying in Jer. 7. The temple

of the Lord. As if it were not permitted to adore and worship God in any other place. Thus Theodoret, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Vatablus, and Robertus understand it. But Remigius, Haymo, and others explain it as the Church, in which, since it is a school of humility under Christ the master of humility, it was to come to pass that, with the masters of pride and the priests rejected, the converted Jews would follow humility and would not boast of the temple and religion. These are the words of Castrius. Our own agree in this sense: Osiander: in that day thou shalt not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: that is, thy sins which thou hast committed shall be blotted out: nor shall they be imputed to thee any longer: therefore (in the judgment of God) thou shalt not be ashamed. (For the sins of those who believe in Christ are forgiven and covered: according to that of David and Paul: Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered, Ps. 32. Rom. 4.) For (it is an expletive particle) then I will take away from the midst of thee the boasters of thy pride: i. e. The proud, hypocrites, Pharisees, scribes, and the like, who will be puffed up in the Jewish people by the opinion of their own righteousness and holiness, shall be separated from the Church of Christ. And thou shalt no more be exalted in my holy mountain: i. e. thou shalt not be proud on account of the Levitical ceremonies, and on account of the Jerusalem Temple. For when the Messiah shall have performed the sacrifice of his death (for the sins of the whole human race), there will be no need henceforth for Levitical sacrifices: by which the passion of Christ is shadowed forth, and consequently there will also be no need any longer for that temple, which was built on account of the sacrifices and the Levitical worship. Let Wigandus, Winckelmannus, and Tarnovius also be compared on this passage.

Latin:

Verf. 11. IN DIE ILLA] Poft id tempus.

NON CONFUNDERIS SUPER CUNCTIS AD- INVENTIONIBUS TUIS] Non ultra pudore afficieris, pro- pter omnia tua ftudia vetera: nempe quia abftinebunt fibi ab idololatria, aliisque pravitatibus.

QUIBUS PRÆVARICATA ES IN ME] Ante captivitatis tempus.

QUIA TUNC AUFERAM DE MEDIO TUI MAGNILOQUOS SUPERBIÆ TUÆ] Illi qui olim au ctores vobis fuerant, extollendi vos contra legem DEI, malo fato mortui, non aderunt vobis.

ET NON ADJICIES EXALTARI AMPLIUS IN MONTE SANCTO MEO] Ne ultra fuperbias in tem- plo meo: nempe illorum exemplo. Superbiæ eft legem contemnere, quod fecerant ipfi facerdotes in templo, fu- pra III. 4. hoc eft, quod dicitur peccare ביד רמה id eft, per fuperbiam. Num. XV. 29.

Hæc non impleta poft reductionem Cyri. Non enim tunc ceffarunt adinventiones Judæorum. Re- dierunt non pauci ad ftudia vetera. Neque abla- ti prorfus de medio auctores prævaricandi contra legem, & qui elata manu peccarunt. Loquitur cum Ierufalem, seu cum Iudæa ad Chriftum conver- sa, ex omnium fententia, uti hic Caftrius obferva- vit: In illo tempore, quo gentes ad me convertentur, tu quoq́, Jerufalem cum filiis tuis, qui Chrifto adhæfe- rint, non habebis, quo pudore afficiaris de omnibus tuis malis operibus, quæ contra me commifisti, jam ti- bi condonatis. Sic intelligunt Hieronymus, Theodore- tus, Remigius, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Dionyfius, Mon- tanus, & alii. Sęd David Kimchi, quem fequun- tur Vatablus, & Robertus, ita explicat non inepte, in die illa non cogeris erubefcere ob ullum operum tuo- rum, quæ factura es, quia ea facies in æquitate, & ju- ftitia, non ut modo, cum cogeris erubefcere ob mala, quibus foles in me prævaricari. Duas autem cau- fas addit, cur tunc non fit habitura, quo pudeat: quia auferam occafiones fuperbiæ, quæ origo eft o- mnium vitiorum. Altera, quia auferam de medio tui magniloquos fuperbiæ tuæ. Hebraice, qui exultant in fuperbia tua, id eft, de excellentia tua & dignita- te: qui nimirum fibi placent ob beneficia, quibus dignatus fum te fuper gentes. Hos putant effe Scri bas & Pharifæos Hieronymus, Remigius, Haymo, Lyra, & Montanus, aut illos Iudæos intelligit, qui gentes ad legem Evangelicam admitti ægre fere- bant, & fe folos dignos ea gratia gloriabantur: quos retundit liber Actuum cap. 10. & Epiftola ad Romanos. Altera fuperbiæ occafio erat: & non adjicies exaltari amplius in monte fancto meo. Nem- pe de templo in monte Sion conftructo, de quo maxime gloriabantur, dicentes Jerem. 7. Templum

Domini. Quasi non in alio loco liceret Deum ad- orare & colere. Sic intelligunt Theodoretus, Alber- tus, Hugo, Lyra, Vatablus & Robertus. Sed Remi- gius, Haymo, & alii Ecclesiam exponunt, in qua cum sit schola humilitatis, sub magistro humilitatis Christo, futurum erat, ut rejectis magistris super- biæ, & sacerdotibus, Judæi conversi humilitatem sequerentur, & non gloriarentur de templo, & re- ligione. Hæc Castrius. Conveniunt in hoc sen- su nostri: Osiander: in die illa non confunderis su- per cunctis adinventionibus tuis, quibus prævarica- ta es in me: id est, peccata tua, quæ commisisti, de- leta erunt: nec tibi amplius imputabuntur: itaq; propterea (in judicio Dei) non confunderis. (Cre- dentium etenim in Christum peccata remissa & te- cta sunt: juxta illud Davidis, & Pauli: Beati, quo- rum remissæ sunt iniquitates, & quorum tecta sunt peccata, Psal. 32. Rom. 4.) Quia (expletiva vocu- la est) tunc auferam de medio tui magniloquos super- biæ tuæ: i. e. Segregabuntur ab Ecclesia Christi superbi, hypocritæ, Pharisæi, scribæ, & similes, qui opinione propriæ justitiæ & sanctimoniæ in popu- lo Judaico turgebunt. Et non adjicies exaltari amplius in monte sancto meo: i. e. non superbies propter ceremonias Leviticas, & propter Tem- plum Jerosolymitanum. Quando enim Messias sa- crificium mortis suæ (pro totius humani generis peccatis) peregerit, non opus erit posthac sacrifi- ciis Leviticis: quibus Christi passio adumbretur, & per consequens etiam non opus erit amplius illo templo, quod propter sacrificia & cultum Levi- ticum fuit ædificatum. Conferatur etiam Wigan- dus, Winckelmannus, & Tarnovius in h. l.

## 3:12
Vers. 12.

AND I WILL LEAVE IN THE MIDST OF THEE A POOR AND NEEDY PEOPLE] Gentle and modest, the Chaldean aptly to the sense: for we have noted elsewhere also that the meanings of the nouns ענו and עני are accustomed to be intermingled with one another.

AND THEY SHALL TRUST IN THE NAME OF THE LORD] Who will confide in God, not in themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET DERELINQUAM IN MEDIO TUI POPU- LUM PAUPEREM ET EGENUM] Lenem & modestum, Chaldæus apte ad sensum: nam nominum ענו & עני si- gnificationes permisceri inter se solere, alibi quoque no- tavimus.

ET SPERABUNT IN NOMINE DOMINI] Qui in Deo, non in semetipsis confident.

## 3:13
Vers. 13. THE REMNANT OF ISRAEL SHALL NOT DO INIQUITY] Those who have returned will not return to idolatry, which is עולה, by way of eminence.

NOR SHALL THEY SPEAK A LIE] They will not deceive one another, as formerly. They will have been purged by many evils.

FOR THEY SHALL FEED] Therefore they shall feed: that is, they shall abound in necessary things.

AND THEY SHALL LIE DOWN] That is, they shall live securely, as he says: -----Reclining under the cover of a spreading beech.

AND THERE SHALL BE NONE TO MAKE THEM AFRAID] There shall be deep peace all around under the protection of the kings of the Persians.

These things concerning the faith and holiness, as well as the happiness and peace, of the remnant of Israel, cannot be restricted to the state under the protection of the Kings of the Persians, but as is already evident from the preceding, they extend themselves to the times of the New Testament. For neither did idolatry against the first table, nor iniquity or lying against the second table, cease there entirely, nor was there such deep peace for them under the Persian regime, as History bears witness. And that these things are to be understood spiritually concerning the spiritual seed of Israel, and concerning spiritual happiness and peace, not only the preceding and following context teach: but the very words themselves, according to the phraseology of the Holy Spirit received in the prophetic oracles, confirm it. And therefore Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Isidorus, Vatablus, and Montanus understand by the remnant of Israel, the Apostles and all the disciples, who were chosen instead of the scribes and Pharisees for the Evangelical grace and to follow humility, whose holiness is also celebrated, and the spiritual pasture under the good shepherd CHRIST, as well as the peace and tranquility which we enjoy in him, and under his sole protection. The Osiandrian Paraphrase is very appropriate here: And I will leave in the midst of thee a poor and needy people, i.e., in the primitive Church most believers will be men of slender fortune, and despised in the world: not conspicuous for riches or power. And they shall trust in the name from all evils: (but hope does not disappoint, Rom. 5.) The remnant of Israel (true Christians) shall not do iniquity (they shall not study injustice and crimes:) nor shall they speak a lie, (but they shall cherish truth in all things: but especially in Religion,) and a deceitful tongue shall not be found in their mouth: but they shall speak and act candidly with their neighbor. For they shall feed and lie down (as sheep satiated in the best pastures) and there shall be none to terrify: they shall rest in spiritual security, in tranquility of conscience, and divine protection: for Christians have the most wholesome food, and they know that no creature can separate them from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. Rom. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 13. RELIQUIÆ ISRAEL NON FACIENT INIQUITATEM] Illi reversi non redibunt ad idolola- triam, quæ עולה, κατ' ἐξοχήν.

NEC LOQUENTUR MENDACIUM] Non deci- pient alter alterum, ut olim. Per multa mala purgati e- runt.

QUONIAM IPSI PASCENTUR] Ideo ipsi pascen- tur: id est, abundabunt rebus necessariis.

ET ACCUBABUNT] Id est, secure vivent, ut ille: -----Patulæ recubans sub tegmine fagi.

ET NON ERIT QUI EXTERREAT] Alta cir- cum pax erit sub præsidio regum Persarum.

Hæc de reliquiarum Israelis tum fide ac san- ctitate, tum felicitate ac pace, non possunt restringi ad statum sub præsidio Regum Persarum, sed uti è præcedentibus jam constat, porrigunt sese ad tem- pora Novi Testamenti. Nam neque idololatria adversus tabulam primam, neq; iniquitas aut men- dacium adversus secundam tabulam ibi omnino cessarunt, nec tam alta pax fuit ipsis sub Persico re- gimine, teste Historia. Et spiritualiter illa intelligen- da esse de semine Israelis spirituali, ac de felicitate, ac pace spirituali, non antecedentia solum & conse- quentia docent: sed ipsa etiam verba juxta Phra- seologiam Sp. S. receptam in oraculis propheticis confirmant. Ideoque per residuum Israel, Apostolos & omnes discipulos, qui pro scribis & Pharisæis ele- cti sint ad gratiam Evangelicam, & humilitatem se- ctandam intelligunt Hieronymus, Theodoretus, Re- migius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Isidorus, Vatablus & Montanus, quorum etiam sanctitas celebratur, & pastura spiritualis sub pastore bono CHRI- STO, nec non pax, & tranquillitas, qua fruimur in illo, & sub illius unius tutela. Optime se hic ha- bet Paraphrasis Osiandrina : Et derelinquam in me- dio tui populum pauperem & egenum, i. e. in primi- tiva Ecclesia plerique credentes erunt homines tenuis fortunæ, & in mundo despecti: non divitiis aut potentia conspicui. Et sperabunt in nomine Do- mini : i. e. in spe expectabunt Christiani a Domino liberationem ab omnibus malis: (spes autem non confundit, Rom. 5.) Reliquiæ Israel (veri Christia- ni) non facient iniquitatem (non studebunt injusti- tiæ, & sceleribus:) nec loquentur mendacium, (sed veritatem in omnibus rebus: præcipue vero in Religione diligent,) & non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa: sed candide loquentur & agent cum proximo suo. Quoniam ipsi pascentur & ac- cubabunt (ut oves in optimis pascuis saturatæ) & non erit, qui exterreat: spirituali securitate, in tran- quillitate conscientiæ, & protectione divina ac- quiescent: Christiani enim habent saluberrimum Depabulum, & sciunt, quod nulla creatura pos- sit eos separare a dilectione Dei, quæ est in Chri- sto Jesu Domino nostro. Rom. 8.

## 3:14
Vers. 14. SING O DAUGHTER OF ZION] Give thanks to God then.

Latin:

Vers. 14. LAUDA FILIA SION] Deo tunc gratias agito.

## 3:15
Vers. 15. THE LORD HATH TAKEN AWAY THY JUDGMENT] That is, thy punishments.

HE HATH TURNED AWAY THINE ENEMIES] He hath emptied thine enemies, that is, he will take away from the Samaritans, Ammonites, Arabians, and Philistines the power of harming thee. See Nehem. IV. VI.

THE KING OF ISRAEL THE LORD IN THE MIDST OF THEE] God shall be King for thee, that is, he shall defend thee.

THOU SHALT NOT FEAR EVIL ANY MORE] For long after the return the state of Judea was most happy.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ABSTULIT DOMINUS JUDICIUM TUUM] Id est, pœnas tuas.

AVERTIT INIMICOS TUOS] Vacuefecit inimi- cos tuos, id est, vim tibi nocendi adimet Samaritis, Ammo- nitis, Arabibus, Philistinis. Vide Nehem. IV. VI.

REX ISRAEL DOMINUS IN MEDIO TUI] Deus tibi pro Rege erit, id est, te defendet.

NON TIMEBIS MALUM ULTRA] Diu enim fuit post reditum felicissimus Judææ status.

## 3:16
Vers. 16. LET NOT THY HANDS BE SLACK] Proceed in the building of the temple and the city.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NON DISSOLVANTUR MANUS TUÆ] Perge in ædificatione templi & urbis.

## 3:17
Vers. 17. HE WILL BE SILENT IN THY LOVE] That is, he will rest in his love for thee.

HE WILL REJOICE OVER THEE WITH PRAISE] He will rejoice because of thee with a song. When men are joyful they sing paeans, hence the translation is taken.

The discourse is not of lasting temporal, but of perpetual spiritual happiness. Thou shalt not fear evil ANY MORE, says the Prophet. Nor does this promise sound only of certain external or bodily enemies, but universally of all enemies, the chief of whom, and the more fierce and to be feared, are spiritual. For what is this solid joy of the daughter of Zion, if, being delivered from an external bodily enemy, she is not immune and secure from an internal and spiritual enemy? Under the name of Zion, therefore, in the Prophetic manner, he addresses the Church and the faithful of Christ, and especially the Church of the N.T., as Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus, Lyranus, Dionysius, Vatablus, Montanus, Castrius, à Lapide, and all of our own people without exception explain. And those goods which are promised here are so great that some believe the present prophecy will finally be fulfilled in the other life, with Jerome, Haymo, Albertus M., and Hugo. He teaches that the Prophetic κέλευσμα itself, by which they are profusely invited to the highest joy, indicates not only the final liberation: Praise daughter of Zion, shout Israel, rejoice and exult with all your heart daughter of Jerusalem. For the solid joy of the faithful is not in external peace or security, but solely in the Lord Phil. IV. 4. Rom. XIV. 12. (2) The removal of judgment as the first argument for joy. For it is not only the aversion of bodily punishments that is designated; the judgment which hangs over the unfaithful is far more serious, from which the pious and faithful have been liberated, which provides the very cause for rejoicing so greatly. And the enemies from whom we are liberated are more serious than the Ammonites, Samaritans, and the like, who cannot harm the soul. Therefore Osiander is right here: The Lord has taken away my judgment, i.e., He will avert from believers all His wrath, with which He is accustomed to punish and condemn the impious.
