(For God did not send His Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through Him. He who believes in Him shall not be judged John 3. And elsewhere Christ says: Amen, Amen, I say to you, he who hears my word, and believes in Him who sent me, has eternal life, and does not come into judgment: but will pass from death into life, John 5. For although even those who believe in Christ will appear before His tribunal: yet they will not be judged, i.e., they will not be condemned) He has averted: more correctly: He has removed (the Lord) your enemies: so that they may not be able to harm you in any way; and our enemies are Satan, sin, eternal death, hell: Christ has conquered these, and has so repressed them that as long as we persist in the Faith of Christ, they have absolutely no right over us). (3) The security which we have under our King the Lord Christ. For this is the security and peace of conscience Rom. V. 1. c. IIX. 1. The King of Israel the Lord is in your midst, you shall not fear evil. In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem do not fear Zion, let not your hands be slack, your Lord in your midst is mighty: He will save: This is an exhortation to confidence, and it pertains to this: that we do not fall in arms because of the insults of the Devil and the world Heb. XII. 12. It is a discourse about the gracious presence, proper to the faithful, which expels all fear and dread. Jehovah is so present that He supplies strength, so that in Him we may be able to overcome every evil, and He fills our soul with solid peace and joy. That Jehovah is Christ the King. For the Prophet speaks of this King, who, namely, has been established as King on Mount Zion Ps. II. 6. who is in our midst Matt. XVIII. 20. & c. XXVIII. 20. of whom also above v. 5. he had said the just Lord is in her midst. Who is here called mighty as Is. IX. 6. Savior, because it is the proper office of Christ to save us 1. Tim. I. 15. And He rejoices over our salvation in joy Is. XII. 5. HE WILL BE SILENT IN HIS LOVE. Heb. He will impose silence (on your accusers) because of His love Rom. IX. 34. And He will exult over you in praise (Heb. with jubilation) He will rejoice greatly and seriously over you, so that He may save you with His salvation, He will be vehemently joyful. How WILL HE BE SILENT? That rendered in the Vulgate is explained thus by Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Albert, Hugo, Lyranus, and others: He will no longer remember, nor will He reproach your past faults, because He loves you, The Chaldean: He will hide your faults in His mercy. Coccejus, this can certainly, he says, be referred to the forgiveness of sins: so that God does not reproach His own for their sins, because of love: it can also be referred to the time that God is silent, and does not show His power in such a way, so that it may be signified that this is from the love by which God wishes all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Conf. Is. XXX. 15. 16. 17. 18. 19. For the rest, Coccejus is clearly singular here: and unfolds his new apocalyptic: For he wishes that what is handed down in v. 11. 12. 13. had its fulfillment in the Waldensians, the Bohemian Brethren, and those who in great number underwent martyrdom in the previous century. He also wishes the first pacification, which he calls that promised to the Church, and v. 14. 15. the enemy, from whose fear the Church is to be liberated, he constitutes as the Anti-Christ v. 9. and makes it the colophon of all prophecies from Dan. VII. and Apoc. XI. and thus thinks the promises have not yet happened: But this is his own private interpretation. (4) The sum of the Evangelical preaching, which is expressed here: in that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: do not fear Zion: Let not your hands be desolate: Your Lord in your midst is mighty, He will save, He will rejoice over you in joy &c. This is therefore the epitome, this is the argument and summary of all Evangelical proclamation. Whence the first heavenly herald of the N.T. used almost the same words: Do not fear: Behold I announce to you great joy. For today a Savior is born to you, who is Christ the Lord (King the Lord) Luke II. 10. 11. Cyril although regarding peace after the return from Babylon he reports these things, yet he adds: But as regards the inner sense of the words, he commands one to rejoice vehemently, and to exult wonderfully, and to be delighted with the whole heart entirely, as being, for instance, forgiven of sins through Christ. For she has been justified in Christ, that is, and in him alone, which understanding is perceived also by holy Sion, that is to say, the Church, or the holy multitude of the faithful. And we have been saved through him, and in him we escape the damages and disasters from invisible enemies, and having him, and the King of all things seen in our form, and God, the Word from God the Father, on account of whom we have seen evils no more. That is, we have been exempted from every violent evil. Theodoret, he says, I am not ignorant that some have applied these very things to the return from Babylon and the renovation of Jerusalem, to which I do not object: because the prophecy does not dissent from those things which were then done. But a more suitable outcome can be found after the incarnation of our Savior. For indeed, then he made those contrite in heart whole by the washing of regeneration, and then he restored the human condition, when he loved us to such a degree that he gave his own soul for us.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SILEBIT IN DILECTIONE TUA] Id est, acquiescet in amore tui.

EXSULTABIT SUPER TE IN LAUDE] Exsul- tabit propter te cum cantico. Homines cum læti sunt παια- νίζουσι, hinc sumta translatio.

Non de diuturna temporali, sed de perpetua spi- rituali felicitate sermo est. Non timebis malum ULTRA, inquit Propheta. Neque de inimicis so- lum quibusdam externis, aut corporalibus hæc promissio sonat, sed in universum de omnibus ini- micis, quorum præcipui, magisque feroces & ti- mendi sunt spirituales. Quænam enim solida hæc lætitia filiæ Sion, si liberata ab externo hoste cor- porali, non sit immunis & secura ab interno & spi- rituali hoste? Sub Sionis ergo nomine, more Pro- phetico, Ecclesiam & fideles Christi alloquitur, & imprimis Ecclesiam N. T. ut exponunt Hierony- mus, Theodoretus, Remigius, Haymo, Albertus, Lyra- nus, Dionysius, Vatablus, Montanus, Castrius, à La- pide, ac nostrates ad unum omnes. Et tanta illa sunt bona, quæ hic promittuntur, ut nonnulli demum vaticinium præsens in altera vita impletum iri cre- dant cum Hieronymo, Haymone, Alberto M. & Hu- gone. Non solum extremam liberationem indicari primo docet ipsum κέλευσμα Propheticum, quo ad summam lætitiam prolixe invitantur: Lauda fi- lia Sion, jubila Israel, lætare & exulta in omni corde filia Ierusalem. Solidum enim fidelium gaudium non est in externa pace aut securitate, sed unice in Domino Phil. IV. 4. Rom. XIV. 12. (2) Ablatio judi- cii ceu primum argumentum lætitiæ. Non enim pœnarum tantum corporalium aversio designatur, longe gravius est judicium, quod infidelibus in- cumbit, à quo pii & fideles liberati sunt, quod cau- sam ipsam tantopere lætandi præbet. Et graviores sunt hostes, à quibus liberamur, quam Ammonitæ, Samaritæ & similes, qui animæ nocere non possunt. Ideo recte hic Osiander: Abstulit Dominus judi- cium meum, i. e. avertet à credentibus omnem iram suam, qua punire & damnare impios solet. (Non enim misit Deus Filium suum in mundum, ut judi- cet mundum, sed ut servetur mundus per ipsum. Qui credit in eum, non judicabitur Ioh. 3. Et alibi inquit Christus: Amen, Amen, dico vobis, qui ver- bum meum audit, & credit ei, qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, & in judicium non venit: sed tran- siet à morte in vitam, Joh. 5. Etsi enim etiam cre- dentes in Christum, coram ipsius tribunali compa- rebunt: tamen non judicabuntur, h. e. non con- demnabuntur) Avertit: rectius: Removit (Do- minus) inimicos tuos: ne quid tibi nocere queant; inimici auetm nostri sunt Satanas, peccatum, mors æterna, infernus: hos Christus devicit, & ita re- pressit, ut quamdiu in Fide Christi perstiterimus, nihil illi prorsus juris in nos habeant). (3) Securi- tas, quam sub Rege Domino nostro Christo ha- bemus. Hæc enim est securitas & pax conscientiæ Rom. V. 1. c. IIX. 1. Rex Israel Dominus in medio tui, non timebis malum. In die illa dicetur Ierusalem noli timere Sion, non dissolvantur manus tuæ, Domi- nus tuus in medio tui fortis: ipse salvabit: Exhor- tatio hæc est ad fiduciam, atque eo pertinet: ne propter insultus Diaboli, & mundi, armis cada- mus Ebr. XII. 12. De gratiosa præsentia sermo est, fidelium propria, quæ omnem metum & timorem expellit. Jehovah ita præsens est, ut vires sufficiat, ut in ipso omne malum superare queamus, solida- que pace & lætitia animum nostrum repleat. Je- hovah ille Rex Christus est. Nam de hoc Rege lo- quitur Propheta, qui sc. in monte Zion constitutus est Rex Pf. II. 6. qui in medio nostri est Matt. XIIX. 20. & c. XXIIIX. 20. de quo etiam supra v. 5. dixerat Dominus justus in medio ejus. Qui hic dicitur fortis ut Es. IX. 6. Salvator, quod hoc proprium Christi sit officium nos salvare 1. Tim. I. 15. Et super nostra salute gaudet in lætitia Esa. XII. 5. SILEBIT IN DILECTIONE SUA. Ebr. Silentium imponet (accusatoribus tuis) propter dilectionem suam Rom. IX. 34. Et exultabit super te in laude (Ebr. cum jubi- latione) valde & serio gaudebit super te, ut te sal- vet sua salute, vehementer lætabitur. Quomodo SILEBIT? Id redditum in vulgata ita exponitur ab Hieronymo, Remigio, Haymone, Alberto, Hugone, Lyrano, & aliis: non recordabitur amplius, neq; ob- jurgabit præteritas tuas culpas, eo quod te diligat, Chaldæus: abscondet delicta tua in misericordia sua. Coccejus, hoc potest sane, inquit, referri ad condona- tionem peccatorum: ut Deus non exprobret suis peccata ipsorum, propter amorem: potest etiam re- ferri ad tempus, quod Deus sileat, & virtutem suam non ita ostendat, ut significetur, hoc esse ab amore quo Deus vult salvari omnes homines & ad cogni- tionem veritatis venire. Conf. Es. XXX. 15. 16. 17. 18. 19. De cætero Coccejus hic plane singularis est: & nova sua apocalyptica pandit: Nam quæ v. 11. 12. 13. traduntur complementum habuisse vult in Wal- densibus, Fratribus Bohemis, & illis, qui magno numero martyrium subierunt superiori seculo. Vult etiam pa- cificationem primam, quam vocat, Ecclesiæ promis- sam, & v. 14. 15. hostem, à cujus timore liberanda Ecclesia, constituit Anti-Christum v. 9. & eo omnium prophetiarum colophonem facit è Dan. VII. & A- poc. XI. atq; ita promissa nondum evenisse putat: Sed hæc idia ἐπίλυσις ipsius est. (4) Evangelicæ præ- dicationis summa, quæ hic exprimitur: in die illa di- cetur Ierusalem: noli timere Sion: Non desolabuntur manus tuæ: Dominus tuus in medio tui fortis, ipse sal- vabit, gaudebit super te in lætitia &c. Hæc proin e- pitome, hoc argumentum & breviarium est omnis præconii Evangelici. Unde primus cœlestis præco N.T. iisdem pene verbis usus est: Nolite timere: Ec- ce annuncio vobis gaudium magnum. Hodie enim natus est vobis Salvator, qui est Christus Dominus (Rex Dominus) Luc. II. 10. 11. Cyrillus etsi ad pacem post reditum è Babylone hæc referat, addit ta- men: Quod autem ad intimum verborum sensum „spectat, gaudere vehementer, & exultare mirifi- „ce, & toto pectore delectari omnino jubet, utpo- „te peccatis condonatis, per Christum, puta. Justi- „ficata est enim in Christo sc., eoque solo, quæ in- „telligentia percipitur & sancta Sion, Ecclesia ni- „mirum, sive fidelium sancta multitudo. Et salvati „sumus per ipsum, & apud ipsum ab hostibus non „aspectabilibus damna, & clades effugientes, & „ipsum habentes, & medium in forma nostra vi- „sum univerforum Regem, ac Deum, ex Deo Pa- „tre verbum, propter quem non vidimus amplius „mala. Hoc est, ab omni violento malo exempti sumus. Theodoretus, inquit, non ignoro quosdam hæc ipsa ad reditum ex Babylone, & renovationem Hierusalem accepisse, quibus non repugno: quod non ab his, quæ tum gesta fuere, dissentiat prophetia. Sed accommodatior exitus reperiri potest, post serva- toris nostri incarnationem. Siquidem tum lavacri regeneratione contritos corde sanos fecit, tum huma- nam conditionem instauravit, cum eo usq; nos dilexit, ut animam suam dederit pro nobis.

## 3:18
Verse 18. NUGAS, QUI A LEGE RECESSERANT, CONGREGABO, QUIA EX TE ERANT, UT NON ULTRA HABEAS SUPER EIS OPPROBRIUM] Jerome thought the Hebrew נוגי, as in sound, so in meaning, was the same as the Latin, nugæ (trifles). But the Chaldean pleases me greatly in this place: Those who hindered your feast days, them I will segregate far from you. Woe to those who have carried the reproach (i. e., weapons) against that: that is, against the liberty of keeping feast days and sacrificing, which could not be done without the Temple. הגה is to remove. After ממך a distinction must be placed, they explain היו for הו, by themselves, besides the Chaldean, also the LXX. Understand those peoples, of whom we spoke above in 15, who wished to hinder the building of the temple in every way.

Grotius deservedly discards the 'nugas' of the Vulgate. But from that he could have learned that the Vulgate is undeservedly pronounced authentic by the Tridentines. He undeservedly praises the Chaldean, which diverges from the authentic text in more than one way. In which, first, it does not have 'who hindered your feast days,' but 'grieving on account of the solemnity.' Which are clearly contrary: for the pious are designated, who grieve that the solemnities of the feasts are hindered, not indeed the impious, who hinder them. נוגי 'affected with grief' is from יגה 'to have sadness,' which occurs in Lam. 1:4, 'her virgins נוגות are affected with grief.' Which Grotius wrongly confuses with הגה 'he removed.' Then, אספתי is not 'I will segregate,' but rather 'I will gather,' which is again contrary to that. Thirdly, the little word ממך does not cohere with that verb, but with the following היו, and therefore it cannot be rendered 'I will segregate' or 'I will gather from you': but THEY ARE FROM YOU. Fourthly, the accent is rashly moved from its place. For the distinction is not found after ממך, but after the word היו in all the Codices, in the authentic text. Fifthly, the little word היו 'ARE' is transmuted into הו 'Woe.' All of which Grotius snatched at so that he might carve out a hindrance of the temple, about which, however, neither in verse 15 nor here in 18 is there any word. Osiander rendered the sense of the Hebrew text thus: 'I will gather the afflicted by constitutions, those, namely, who are from you, upon whom the burden of reproach lies.' Similarly, B. Luther almost: 'Die so durch Saßungen geängstiget waren, will ich wegschaffen, daß sie von dir kommen, welche Satzungen ihre Last waren, davon sie Schmach hatten.' To take the word מועד as 'constitution' or 'decree': which, even if it usually denotes a specially appointed or proclaimed solemnity, yet in general, by the force of the etymology and formal meaning, it can be rendered by 'proclamation' and 'constitution,' as it is taken in Genesis 21:2. And since that word is also of the feminine gender, the Hebrew text is rendered word for word thus: 'those grieving on account of the constitution or proclamation I will gather: they are from you. The burden upon that'

(constitution) is reproach. Or the burden (is the constitution) upon which (burden) is reproach: as Luther: 'welche Satzungen ihre Last waren, davon sie Schmach hatten.' Thus this will be the mind of the Lord: I will gather through the Gospel those who grieve and are afflicted on account of the manifold constitution and proclamation, because they are from you, O Church: they are yours, they pertain to you (that is, the Jews afflicted on account of various decrees); that constitution and proclamation is a burden, upon which is reproach. For that burden of the law (which neither they nor their fathers could bear) presses them, and it results only in confusion and reproach for them, because those who wish to be justified by the law eventually bring back confusion. For they are always accused by the law and convicted of disobedience. Ludov. Dievius interpreted these things a little differently: 'Those grieving on account of the solemnity are from you, a burden, upon which is reproach.' משאת wishes never to signify 'burden,' but 'gift': so that the sense may be: 'I will gather all the pious who grieve that the solemnities of the feasts have been hindered: because they are from you, O Church: and I will gather them for you as a gift, upon which indeed there is now reproach.' This is the interpretation of Cocceius: 'I have gathered those saddened by the congregation, they have become from you, whose burden is a reproach, or to whom a reproach is as a gift.' Others, with Vatablus, think it is indicated that those affected with grief on account of the long time in which they awaited the coming of Christ are to be gathered into the Church, and are no longer to be affected with reproach. See Castrius in this place.

Latin:

Vers 18. NUGAS, QUI A LEGE RECESSERANT, CONGREGABO, QUIA EX TE ERANT, UT NON ULTRA HABEAS SUPER EIS OPPROBRIUM] Hie- ronymus נוגי Hebræum, ut sono, ita significatu, idem putavit esse quod Latinum, nugæ. Sed valde mihi se hoc lo- co pro bat Chaldæus: Qui impedierunt festos dies tuos, eos procul à te segregabo. Væ illis qui portaverunt opprobrium (i. e. arma,) contra illud: id est, contra libertatem festos dies agendi, & sacrificandi, quod sine Templo fieri non poterat. הגה est removere. Post ממך ponenda distinctio, היו pro הו, per se exponunt, præter Chaldæum, etiam LXX. illos populos intellige, de quibus diximus supra 15. qui templi ædificationem impedire omni modo voluere.

Nugas vulgatæ merito mittit Grotius. Sed in- de vulgatam immerito authenticam à Tridentinis pronunciatam discere poterat. Immerito laudat Chaldæum, qui non uno modo divaricatur ab au- thentico textu. In quo primo non habetur, qui im- pedierunt festos dies tuos, sed dolentes ob solemnita- tem. Quæ plane contraria sunt: designati enim pii sunt, qui festorum solemnitates impediri dolent, non vero impii, qui eosdem impediunt. נוגי mœro- re affecti est à יגה) mœstitiam habuit quod Thr. I. 4. occurrit, virgines ejus נוגות mœrore sunt affectæ. Quod perperam confundit Grotius cum הגה re- movit. Deinde אספתי non est segregabo, sed potius colligam, quod iterum illi contrarium est. Tertio cum illo verbo non cohæret vocula ממך, sed cum sequenti היו ideoque reddi nequit segregabo, aut colligam ex te: sed EX TE SUNT. Quarto ac- centus temere loco movetur. Non enim post ממך, sed post vocem היו distinctio in Codicibus omni- bus reperitur, in textu authentico. Quinto vocula היו SUNT transmutatur in הו Væ. Quæ omnia id- eo arripuit Grotius, ut exsculperet impeditionem templi, de qua vero nec v. 15. neque hic 18. ullum verbum habetur. Sensum textus Ebræi sic reddidit Osiander: Afflictos constitutionibus colligam, eos vid. qui ex te sunt, quibus onus opprobrii incumbit, Similiter fere B. Lutherus: Die so durch Sa- ßungen geaͤngstiget waren, will ich wegschaffen, daß sie von dir kommen, welche Satzungen ih- re Last waren, davon sie Schmach hatten. Vocem מועד de constitutione, vel decreto acce- pere: quæ etsi specialiter solemnitatem constitu- tam, vel indictam notare soleat, in genere ta- men per indictionem, & constitutionem, vi e- tymi & formalis significati reddi potest, uti Ge- nef. XXI. 2. accipitur. Et quum ea vox etiam fœminini generis sit, κατὰ πόδα textus Ebræus ita redditur: mœrentes ob constitutionem, vel indictionem colligam: ex te sunt. Onus super ea

(constitutione) opprobrium. Vel onus (est consti- tutio) super quo (onere) opprobrium: ut Lutherus: welche Satzungen ihre Last waren, davon sie Schmach hatten. Ita hæc mens Domini erit: Ego per Evangelium colligam eos, qui dolent, & afflicti sunt, ob constitutionem & indictionem multivariam, quia ex te sunt, ô Ecclesia: tui sunt, ad te pertinent (hoc est, Judæos afflictos ob va- ria decreta) onus est illa constitutio & indictio, su- per quod opprobrium. Onus enim illud legis,(quod neque ipsi, neque Patres eorum portare potue- runt) premit illos, & confusioni saltim, atque op- probrio ipsis cedit,quod qui justificari ex lege vo- lunt, confusionem tandem reportent. Semper enim à lege accusantur, & inobedientiæ convin- cuntur. Paulo aliter hæc interpretatus est Ludov. Dievius: Dolentes ob solemnitatem ex te sunt, mu- nus, super quod opprobrium. משאת vult nun- quam onus, sed munus significare: ut sensus sit: pios omnes, qui dolent, impeditas esse festorum sole- mnitates, colligam: quia ex te sunt, ô Ecclesia: & ego eos tanquam donum tibi colligam, super quod quidem jam opprobrium est. Cocceji hæc est inter- pretatio: Contristatos à congregatione collegi, ex te facti sunt, cujus onus est probrum, vel cui pro dono est probrum. Alii cum Vatablo indigitari putant, mœrore affectos,ob tempus prolixum, quo expecta- runt adventum Christi, congregandos in Ecclesiam, nec jam probro afficiendos. vid. Castrius in h. l.

## 3:19
Verse 19. ECCE EGO INTERFICIAM OMNES, QUI AFFLIXERUNT TE IN TEMPORE ILLO] I will destroy all. For thus עשׂה is often taken, and in this place it has the same value as כלה above.

ET SALVABO CLAUDICANTEM] To limp here signifies to suffer inconveniences, as in Ps. 35:15. Therefore the LXX here translated it ἐκπεπιεσμένην, as συντετριμμένην in Micah 4:6, 7.

ET EAM, QUÆ ELECTA FUERAT, CONGREGABO] Daily others and still others will approach those who have returned.

AND I WILL SET THEM FOR A PRAISE, AND FOR A NAME, IN EVERY LAND OF THEIR CONFUSION] That is, I will cause them to have a celebrated name, even in those places where they were for contempt and mockery.

By the limping one he understands the Synagogue of the Jews: by the cast out one, however, the multitude of the Gentiles, according to Tarnovius from Micah IV. 6. in this sense: those who will be limping will be gifted by me with that strength so that they may be able to approach, and those who have been driven away, and are aliens to the Covenants, will be called, and I will arrange for them praise and a name in the whole, nay, every land of their shame, where hitherto they have been confused with shame in exile. Osiander and Winckelmann, however, understand by the cast out one the Israelite nation, scattered among the Assyrians and Babylonians, to be gathered into the Church of Christ. Osiander calls the limping one the weaker part of the Church, which does not have great strength of faith. Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Lyra, and Vatablus and others believe it to have been fulfilled in the time of the primitive Church: similarly Cornelius a Lapide [believes it refers to] the Church, that is, the assembly of the faithful, cast out by persecutors, I will gather, and I will restore to its city, place, and country, so that they may be there in honor, praise, and glory, where they were previously affected by confusion, reproaches, and beatings. This was done through Constantine. These are the words of Cornelius.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ECCE EGO INTERFICIAM OMNES, QUI AFFLIXERUNT TE IN TEMPORE ILLO] Re- primam omnes. Sic enim עשׂה sæpe sumitur, & hoc lo- co idem valet quod supra כלה.

Per claudicantem intelligit Synagogam Judæo- rum: per ejectam vero gentium multitudinem, jux- ta Tarnovium è Mich. IV. 6. hoc sensu: qui clau- di erunt, donabuntur à me illâ vi, ut possint acce- dere, & qui depulsi sunt, & à Testamentis alieni, ad- vocabuntur,disponamque eis laudem & nomen in tota,imo omni terra pudoris eorum, ubi hactenus in exilio pudore confusi sunt. Osiander vero & Win- ckelrn.per abjectam intelligunt gentem Israeliticam, sparsam inter Assyrios & Babylonios in Ecclesiam Christi congregandam. Hæc Cornelius.

## 3:20
Ver. 20. WHEN I SHALL TURN YOUR CAPTIVITY] I shall have caused those to return who had lived as captives.

BEFORE YOUR EYES] So that you may behold one another, with the greatest joy.

Jerome, Cyril of Alexandria, Theodoret, Hugo, and others explain it concerning spiritual captivity from the servitude of the Devil and sin. Lyranus, Vatablus, and Cornelius a Lapide explain it concerning the captivity under Gentile Emperors and Tyrants, from which they were liberated by Constantine the Great. Meanwhile, nothing prevents the promise of a return from the Babylonian captivity in these words, even if the preceding things pertain to the times of the New Testament. For the conversion of that captivity was made primarily on account of the promised Messiah, who was to appear in Judea. Nor were those benefits of the New Testament destined to be obtained, except after the conversion of the captivity of the Jews. And the interpreters note here that CAPTIVITIES are spoken of in the plural, inasmuch as several Jewish captivities are counted: (1) the abduction of King Manasseh 2 Chron. XXXIII. 11. Jehoiakim chap. XXXV. 6. (3) of Jehoiachin and Jeconiah 2 Kings XXIV. 12. 2 Chron. XXXVI. 10. (4) of Zedekiah 2 Chron. XXXVI. 17. 2 Kings XXV. That the promise of these being resolved was therefore made here. Thus B. Tarnovius: To which B. Wigandus also seems to incline: when he observes in this place that the end of the restoration and preservation of the Jewish polity is the advent of the Messiah, because indeed God promised that the Messiah would be born among them. But it pleased B. Osiander, whom B. Winckelmann and B. Himmelius follow, to adopt the former explanation concerning spiritual liberation, with whose paraphrase I am pleased to conclude this Prophet: Although, he says, the benefit of God was great, by which the Israelites were led out of the Babylonian captivity into their fatherland, Judea: yet the prophet denotes a far greater benefit by these words: (for many Israelites were not participants in that bodily benefit: inasmuch as they had died in exile) he signifies therefore that by the Gospel of Christ the Jews were to be gathered into the Church of the living God. This benefit could reach those who had remained in Assyria or Babylonia, just as well as those who had returned to Judea. But those also were saved through Christ who, dying in exile, placed their trust in the Messiah, whom they believed would come. But all Christians (whether they have been gathered into the Church from the Jews or from the Gentiles) are then truly liberated from exile and captivity, when in true faith they depart from this world into the heavenly fatherland; into which may our most kind heavenly Father deign to receive us for the sake of Christ the Mediator: to whom with the co-eternal only-begotten Son, and the Holy Spirit, be praise, honor, and glory for all eternity, Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 20. CUM CONVERTERO CAPTIVITATEM VESTRAM] Redire fecero eos, qui velut captivi ege- rant.

CORAM OCULIS VESTRIS] Ita ut alter con- spiciatis alterum, summo cum gaudio.

De captivitate spirituali à servitute Diaboli,& peccati explicant Hier.Cyrillus Alex. Theodoretus, Hugo & alii.De captivitate sub gentilibus Imperato- ribus & Tyrannis,à qua per Constantinum M. libera- ti,Lyranus, Vatablus,Cornel. à Lapide. Interim ni- hil vetat his verbis reductionem è captivitate Ba- bylonica promitti,etsi superiora ad temporaN.T. pertineant.Nam conversio istius captivitatis facta imprimis est ob Messiam promissum, in Judæa appariturum. Neque obtingere illa beneficia N. T. debebant, nisi post conversionem captivitatis Judæorum. Et notant hîc Interpp. in plurali CAPTIVITATES dici, siquidem plures numerentur Judaicæ captivitates (1) abductio Manassis Regis 2. Chron. XXXIII. 11. (2) Regis Jojackim cap. XXXV. 6. (3) Jejachin & Jochonia 2. Reg. XXIV. 12. 2. Chron. XXXVI. 10. (4) Sedecia 2. Chron. XXXVI. 17. 2. Reg. XXV. Harum ergo solvendarum promissionem hîc factam esse. Ita B. Tarnovius: Quo etiam inclinare videtur B. Wigandus: cum observat h. l. finem restitutionis & conservationis politiæ Judaicæ, Messiæ esse adventum, quia nempe promiserit Deus, Messiam inter ipsos nasciturum. B. Osiandro autem, quem B. Winckelmannus, & B. Himmelius sequuntur, placuit prior de liberatione spirituali explicatio, cujus paraphrasi hunc Prophetam concludere lubet: Etsi, inquit, ingens fuit beneficium Dei, quo Israelitæ è captivitate Babylonica in patriam, Judæam, sunt educti: tamen longe majus beneficium his verbis propheta denotat: (multi enim Israëlitæ, illius corporalis beneficii non fuere participes: quippe qui in exilio mortui erant) significat igitur per Evangelium Christi collectum iri Judæos in Ecclesiam Dei viventis. Hoc beneficium tam illis contingere potuit, qui manserant in Assyria, aut Babylonia, quam qui in Judæam redierant. Sed & illi per Christum salvati sunt, qui in exilio morientes suam fiduciam in Messiam, quem venturum credebant, collocarunt. Omnes autem Christiani (sive ex Judæis, sive ex Gentibus in Ecclesiam sint collecti) tum vere ab exilio & captivitate liberantur, cum in vera fide ex hoc mundo in patriam cælestem abeunt; in quam nos propter Christum Mediatorem, recipere dignetur benignissimus Pater noster cælestis: cui cum Filio unigenito coæterno, & Spiritu Sancto sit laus, honor & gloria in omnem æternitatem, Amen.

# Haggai

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 2). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
I. N. I. ANNOTATIONS ON HAGGAI.

Latin:

I. N. I. ANNOTATA AD AGGÆUM.

## 1:1 Introduction: Preface of Grotius
PREFACE OF GROTIUS.

There are three Prophets who saw the people returned, Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, to whom Daniel must be added: for he too, surviving many kings, is believed to have been in Judea, and at some time to have been a part of τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς μεγάλης, by which the people were governed at that time. In these four, prophecy ceased until the times of Christ. For God wished by that famine of the word (as the Prophets speak) to make the Jews more desirous of the Messiah, who was to surpass all the Prophets in miracles. And because these were the last of the Prophets of the old covenant, they therefore point their finger more openly to the new covenant and its leader Christ, and do not only figure him through other intermediate histories, but show him directly.

vities are celebrated in it: he is called the Angel of the Lord in the embassy of the Lord to the people c. I. 13. and his writing is praised as Canonical Heb. XII. 20. He lived after the Babylonian captivity, to which Zechariah was joined while still prophesying Heb. V. 1. Zach. I. 1. These sermons were delivered to the returned Jews: who had laid only the foundations of the temple, but had built splendid houses for themselves. On which occasion Haggai reproves their negligence, as those who, previously hindered by enemies, feared similar things, even though the edict of Cyrus was confirmed by Darius Ezra VI. 3. The Prophet therefore exhorts the Jews, that, warned by the evils by which they have hitherto been afflicted, they should seriously undertake the work; and he makes them certain of the gracious assistance of GOD, of the future glory of the temple, in which the Messiah himself was to perform the office of teaching, and of various benefits of God, both bodily and spiritual, if they should turn themselves to God and his worship.

ἐπίκρισις with our Prolegomena.

Although the later Prophets, regarding some ὑποτάσεις, announce Christ more openly, as far as his advent, time, forerunner, and some other things are concerned, yet the benefits of Christ, which extend themselves to all times, forward and backward, on account of which Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today ὁ αὐτὸς, and forever Heb. XIII. 8. and is the lamb slain from the beginning of the world Rev. XIII. 8. were announced no less clearly by other Prophets, especially by David and Isaiah, whom, on account of his illustrious testimonies concerning Christ, some have called the Evangelist of the Old Testament, θεοδίδακτοι. They did not, however, only represent Christ through the middle of their histories, but directly pointed Him out, as regards the grace of redemption, nay even as regards His birth from a virgin, the place and country of the same, and other circumstances, which Grotius has hitherto attempted in no way to invalidate or weaken: although he has not spared these later Prophets either, as we observed in Daniel, and as will be observed hereafter in these most recent prophetic books: in which he is certainly discovered to have been little mindful of this confession, which truth itself and the evidence of the matter wrung from him, concerning Christ not being represented by these Prophets, but directly pointed out: since Grotius leaves them very few (if any) direct prophecies concerning Christ.

It is distributed into four sermons: the first of which is described in chapter one, held in the second year of Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day: on the occasion of the saying of the people, that it is not yet time to build the house of the Lord, the summary of which is presented, namely a rebuke, because they build their own houses, having left the house of the Lord, whence punishment and a curse upon their houses, sterility of agriculture, famine, nakedness, and poverty, and a command is added concerning the building of the house of the Lord, and a promise of the demonstration of the glory of the Lord. Since, on account of the neglected house of the Lord, a meager yield and its dissipation and drought have hitherto occurred. Finally, the effect of this sermon is subjoined, namely the obedience of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people, and the promise of divine assistance. The remaining three sermons are contained in chapter two: namely the second sermon held on the twenty-first day of the seventh month concerning the external vile appearance of the second temple, on account of which diffidence arose, which is tacitly reproached in them, with the promise of divine presence and the future glory of the temple: and furthermore the third sermon on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. A correction of hypocrisy, and an excitation to the building of the temple, with the abundance of divine blessing promised in place of the drought that had been sent: the fourth, finally, held on the same day, is consolatory: promising the overthrow of enemies and the preservation of Zerubbabel.

Furthermore, Haggai חַגַּי from חָגַג he celebrated a feast, is truly festive, urging the restoration of the temple as a fe-

SERMON I. Containing both a rebuke and a promise concerning the building of the house of the Lord, and its effects.

Latin:

PRÆLOQUIUM GROTII.

Tres sunt Prophetæ, qui populum videre reducem, Aggæus, Zacharias, & Malachias, quibus addendus Daniel: nam & is, multis regibus superstes, fuisse in Judæa creditur, & tempore aliquo partem fecisse τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς μεγάλης, à qua tunc tune populus gubernabatur. In his quatuor desiit Prophetia usque ad Christi tempora. Voluit enim Deus ista fame verbi (ut Prophetæ loquuntur) appetentiores Messiæ facere Judæos, qui Prophetas omnes miraculis esset superaturus. Et quia hi postremi fuere Prophetarum veteris fœderis, ideo ad novum fœdus, & ducem ejus Christum, digitum apertius intendunt, nec tantum per medias historias alias eum figurant, sed directè monstrant.

vitates in eo celebrentur: dicitur Angelus Domini in legatione Domini ad populum c. I. 13. ejusque scriptum laudatur ceu Canonicum Ebr. XII. 20. Vixit post captivitatem Babylonicam, cui adhuc vaticinante junctus Zacharias Ebr. V. 1. Zach. I. 1. Judæis reducibus hæ conciones habitæ: qui fundamenta tantum templi jecerant, sibi ipsis autem domos præclaras exstruxerant. Qua occasione negligentiam eorum reprehendit Haggæus, utpote qui prius impediti ab hostibus similia metuebant, etsi à Dario confirmaretur Cyri edictum Esdr. VI. 3. Hortatur itaque Propheta Judæos, ut malis, quibus hactenus afflicti sint, commoniti, serio opus aggrediantur; certosque reddit de gratiosa DEI assistentia, futura templi, in quo Messias ipse officio docendi functurus sit eminentiori gloria, variisque Dei beneficiis cum corporalibus tum spiritualibus, si ad Deum ejusque cultum se converterint.

ἐπίκρισις cum nostris Prolegomenis.

Etsi Prophetæ posteriores, quoad nonnullas ὑπο τάσεις apertius Christum prænuncient, quantum ad adventum ejusdem, tempus, prodromum, & alia nonnulla, beneficia tamen Christi, quæ ad omnia tempora sese extendunt, antrorsum & retrorsum, ob quæ Jesus Christus heri & hodie ὁ αὐτὸς idem est, & in secula Ebr. XIII. 8. & agnus mactatus est inde ab initio mundi Ap. XIII. 8. non minus clarè ab aliis Prophetis annunciata sunt, maximè à Davide atq; Esaia, quem ob illustria de Christo testimonia, Veteris Testamenti Evangelistam nonnulli θεοδίδακτοι dixere. Non vero tantum per medias historias illi figurarunt Christum, sed directè eundem monstrarunt, quoad redemptionis gratiam, imo etiam quoad nativitatem è virgine, ejusdem locum & patriam, & alias circumstantias, quæ exauthorare aut enervare nequicquam hactenus molitus est Grotius: quamvis neque his Prophetis posterioribus pepercerit, uti in Daniele à nobis observatum, atq; in novissimis hisce libellis propheticis deinceps observabitur: in quibus certe parum memor fuisse deprehenditur hujus confessionis, quam eidem ipsa veritas & evidentia rei expressit, de Christo ab hisce Prophetis non figurato, sed directè monstrato: siquidem admodum pauca (si ulla) Grotius illis relinquat directà de Christo vaticinia.

Distribuitur in quatuor conciones: quarum prima cap. primo describitur anno II. Darii M. VI. d. 1. habita: occasione dicti populi, quod nondum tempus sit extruendi domum Domini, cujus summa exhibetur, reprehensio nempe, quod suas extruant domos, relicta domo Domini, unde pœna & maledictio in domibus ipsorum, agriculturæ sterilitas, fames, nuditas, & egestas, additurque mandatum de extruenda domo Domini, & promissio demonstrationis gloriæ Domini. Siquidem ob neglectam domum Domini proventus exiguus ejusque dissipatio & siccitas hactenus evenerit. Subjungitur deniq; effectus hujus concionis partitio nempe Serobabelis, Josuæ & populi, ac promissio assistentiæ divinæ. Reliquæ tres conciones cap. II. continentur: utpote concio secunda Mense septimo d. 21. habita de externa vili specie templi secundi, ob quam diffidentia oriebatur, quæ his tacite exprobratur, cum promissione divina præsentia, & futuræ templi gloriæ: ac porro tertia concio d. 24. Mensis Noni. Epanorthosis ab hypocrisin, & excitatio ad templi ædificationem, promissa loco immissæ ficcitatis ubertate divinæ benedictionis: Quarta denique die eadem habita consolatoria est: promittens hostium eversionem, & Zorubabelis conservationem.

Porro Haggæus חַגַּי à חָגַג festum celebravit, vere festivus est, templi instaurationem urgens ut fe-

CONCIO I. Cum objurgatoria, tum promissionem continens circa ædificationem domus Domini, ejusque effectus.

## 1:1 Argument
CHAPTER I.

Designation of the time of the Prophecy. Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people are rebuked for neglecting the house of God, on account of which a curse befell them, and they are commanded to build it, so that the Lord may be glorified by a blessing. Their obedience is subjoined, with a divine promise of παραστάσεως (presence/support).

Ver. 1.

IN THE SECOND YEAR OF DARIUS THE KING, IN THE SIXTH MONTH, IN THE FIRST DAY OF THE MONTH] That is, the first, according to the Hebrew custom, as in Gen. 1:5 and elsewhere. He began, therefore, to be enlightened by God with these visions seven months before him who follows, Zechariah. Both this prophecy is that very one which Ezra 5 deals with. This was the occasion. Cyrus, moved by God, who had predicted this through Isaiah, had granted the Jews a return to their homeland, with the right to restore the temple and the city. For thus Josephus reports the edict of Cyrus in Book 11. Many had returned from the tribe of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, and some also from other tribes, to whom the worship of God was dear, and they had laid the foundations of the temple. But with Cyrus occupied by wars, and Cambyses circumvented, the neighboring Satraps, envying the Jews, had hindered the building of the temple for a sufficiently long time. This Cambyses is called by a common name, Artaxerxes, in the sacred histories: concerning which name we have dealt at the beginning of Esther. Darius Hystaspis having attained the Persian kingdom, God revealed to the Prophets who were then in Judea, Haggai and Zechariah, that He willed that the work begun should be continued, because He had determined to instill into the mind of King Darius thoughts favoring the Jews and promoting this work. There were those who believed Haggai, among whom stood out Zerubbabel the Ethnarch of the lineage of David, and JESUS the son of Josedech, the High Priest. Many of the common people, fleeing from labor and expense, preferred to believe anything rather than that which was troublesome to them: for they had enough in the houses which they had suddenly made for themselves, to dwell well-roofed against every injury of the sky, and to enjoy the produce of the fields: which hope, however, God so willing, had deceived them. The authority of these two Prophets and of the two men whom I mentioned, the princes who joined themselves to them, prevailed so much that the work, long interrupted, was resumed: which pious zeal, God so directing the matter, was approved and aided by the edict of King Darius.

Cambyses was that Ahasuerus of whom Ezra 4:6 speaks. But Darius was the son of Hystaspes (not, as many wish, Darius Nothus, nor Artaxerxes Longimanus), in whose second year the structure of the temple was resumed, Ezra 4:24, 5:1, etc. We have confirmed that opinion in the book of Ezra and at Daniel 9, and have refuted the modern opinion of Scaliger concerning Darius Nothus. Josephus, Book 11, Antiq. ch. 3, Clement of Alexandria, Book 1, Strom., Eusebius in his Chronicle and Book 10 of the Preparation for the Gospel, ch. 3, Theodoret, Jerome, Albert the Great, along with almost all others, explain it as Darius the son of Hystaspes. Christopher à Castro agrees in this place. We have Grotius here not dissenting. This opinion concerning Darius Hystaspis is not approved by Cocceius, even though he confesses it is asserted by Josephus, Jerome, Peter Cruger, the most learned mathematician of Danzig, and other not ignoble authors. He whom it pleases to hear: But if it is so, he says, where shall we place the many years of Zechariah 1 and almost 70 of Zechariah 7, during which they had fasted in the land? For if these are the years of the Babylonian captivity, why are they not counted as 110 instead? For there are that many up to the year of Darius Hystaspis, unless we also subtract as much as we like from the years of Cyrus. There will be at least 89. But according to their own calculations, for fifteen years or so, the opportunity for fasting was provided to those returned to the land because the building of the temple was prohibited. Why is Artaxerxes called Cambyses? Who will be the Ahasuerus between Cyrus and Cambyses? Or perhaps Cambyses himself, and thus Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes and Cambyses will be the same? For that Artaxerxes is a common name of the Persian Kings is far from all probability. For they are called by different names, some Cyrus, others Darius, others Ahasuerus, others Artaxerxes. But if he is Cambyses, why is he placed after Darius? Ezra 4:5, 6, 7. Or if Ahasuerus is Smerdis, why is he placed before Artaxerxes, who is Cambyses? Who will be the Artaxerxes following Darius the restorer of the temple, when Xerxes, the fourth King of the Persians, succeeded Hystaspis, Daniel 11:2? These are his points, to which, that we may respond briefly: (1) The years of the captivity and Babylonian servitude are confused with the years of the desolation and devastation of Jerusalem. The latter begin from the destruction of the city, the former from the fifth year of Jehoiakim. There were, therefore, 70 years elapsed from the destruction of Jerusalem, as Zechariah ch. 1:12 indicates, up to the second year of Darius Hystaspis: namely, 27 years of Nebuchadnezzar, 2 of Evil-Merodach, 4 of Neriglissar, 9 months of Labashi-Marduk, 17 of Nabonidus, 9 of the Monarchy of Cyrus (not 19, as Cocceius counts, confusing the years of the reign of Cyrus the Persian with the years of the Monarchy and Empire of Cyrus), 8 of Cambyses and the Magi, and 2 of Darius Hystaspis. (2) Cambyses is named Ahasuerus in Ezra 4:6. (3) Between Cyrus and Cambyses there is no Ahasuerus, but Cambyses was followed by Smerdis, called by the common name Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, Ezra 4:7. Which name, although it was common, was nevertheless appropriated to certain ones. Whence he was called Artaxerxes the Long-handed and the Mindful, just as also the name of Darius, according to some, is a common name appropriated to some, Darius Hystaspis, Darius Nothus, Darius Codomannus. (4) Ahasuerus is not placed after Darius in Ezra 5:5, 6, 7, but Darius is introduced as later, which is manifest from verse 24 of the same chapter. (5) Artaxerxes did not immediately follow Darius the restorer of the temple, but Xerxes, which is also evident from Daniel 11:2. But him Artaxerxes the Long-handed (Longimanus) succeeded, Ezra 7:1, 8, ch. 6:44, Neh. 1:1, ch. 13:6.

Verse of the same. THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME BY THE HAND OF HAGGAI THE PROPHET] That is, through Haggai, the Prophet: a sufficiently well-known Hebraism.

TO ZERUBBABEL THE SON OF SHEALTIEL] Concerning his lineage, see what we have said at Luke 3:23 and the following.

Most maintain that Zerubbabel was not the son, but the grandson of Shealtiel, whom Junius wishes to be called a son not by nature, but by right of succession. Concerning the opinion of Grotius, we have spoken at Luke 3:23.

GOVERNOR OF JUDAH] Ethnarch, leader, ruler of the Jews, as Josephus speaks. The Jews indeed revered him in their hearts as if he were a King, because he drew his origin from the family of David which had long reigned, but they did not surround him with the royal name and splendor, lest they offend the minds of the Persian kings, under whose protection, and partly under whose empire, they were.

Grotius assumes that Zerubbabel was greeted and honored as King by the Jews, so that he may apply the passages of Scripture which treat of the King Messiah under the name of David to Zerubbabel, whom, however, the Holy Scriptures never named King, but Governor, and it is established by certain proof that he was not held as King by the Jews, even though he drew his origin from the reigning family, to whom it had been predicted rather in Ezekiel ch. 21:26, Take away the crown, because it shall be no more so, etc.

AND TO JOSHUA THE SON OF JOZADAK THE HIGH PRIEST] This man was indeed born of the blood of Aaron, but was elected to the high priesthood by the Sanhedrin, just as it was accustomed to be done formerly by the Jewish kings. These things were said to those two, but in the presence of the people, as appears below in verse 12.

Latin:

CAPUT I.

Designatio tempore Prophetiæ increpantur Zorobabel, Josua, & populus ob neglectam domum Dei, cujus causa maledictio obtigit, ac jubentur eam extrue- re, ut benedictione glorificetur Dominus. Subjun- gitur eorum obedientia, cum promissione divina παραστάσεως.

Vers. 1.

IN ANNO SECUNDO DARII REGIS, IN MENSE SEXTO, IN DIE UNA MENSIS] Id est, pri- ma, more Hebræo, ut Gen. I. 5. & alibi. Cœpit ergo hic à Deo his visis illustrari septem mensibus ante, quam is, qui sequitur Zacharias. Utraque hæc prophetia ea ipsa est, de qua agit Esdras V. Occasio hæc fuit. Concesserat Cyrus à Deo, qui id per Esaiam prædixerat, motus, Judæis reditum in patriam, cum jure restituendi templi & urbis. Ita enim Cyri edictum refert Josephus XI. Redierant è tribu Ju- dæ, Benjaminis & Levi plurimi, nonnulli etiam ex tribu- bus aliis, quibus Dei cultus erat cordi, & fundamenta fe- cerant templi. Cyro autem per bella occupato, & Cam- byse circumyento, vicini Satrapæ invidentes Judæis, im- pedierant ædificationem templi longo satis tempore. Is Cambyses nomine communi Artaxerxes dicitur in sacris historiis: quo de nomine egimus ad initium Estheris. Da- rio Hystaspis regnum adepto Persicum, aperuit Deus Pro- phetis, qui tum in Judæa erant, Aggæo & Zachariæ, velle se ut pergeretur in cœpto opere, quia scilicet constituisset regis Darii animo indere cogitata Judæis faventia, & hoc opus promotura. Erant qui Aggæo crederent, inter quos eminebant Zorobabel Ethnarcha è Davidis stirpe, & JE- SUS Jesedecides Sacerdos maximus. Multi ex plebe labo- ris & impensarum fugientes, quidvis malebant credere, quam id, quod ipsis molestum esset: satis enim habebant in domibus, quas sibi subito fecerant, bene adversus o- mnem cœli injuriam tectis habitare, & agri proventibus frui: quæ tamen spes eos, Deo ita volente, fefellerat. Ho- rum duorum Prophetarum & ad eos se adjungentium duo- rum virorum, quos dixi, principum auctoritas tantum va- luit, ut interruptum diu opus repeteretur: quod pium studium Deo sic res dirigente, Darii regis edicto compro- batum adjutumque est.

Cambyses Ahasverus ille fuit, de quo Esdr. IV. 6. Darius vero Hystaspis fuit filius (non ut multi vo- lunt, Darius Nothus, neque Artaxerxes Longima- nus) cujus anno secundo templi structura denuo re- assumta est Esdr. IV. 24. C. V. 1. seqq. sententiam illam in libro Esdræ, & ad Dan. IX. firmavimus, & neotericam Scaligeri opinionem de Dario Notho con- futavimus. De Dario filio Hystaspis explicat e- tiam Josephus L. XI. Antiq. c. III. Clem. Alexandr. L. I. Strom. Eusebius in Chron. & L. X. de Præparat. Evang. c. III. Theodorect. Hieron. Albertus M. cum cæteris fere omnibus. Confert Christoph. à Castro in h. l. Habemus hic Grotium non dissentientem. Coccejo non probatur hæc sententia de Dario Hy- staspide, etsi eandem à Josepho, Hieronymo, Petro Crugero, Dantiscano Mathematico doctissimo, a- liisque autoribus non ignobilibus assertam fatea- tur. Quem audire juvat: Sed si ita est, inquit, ubi ponemus multos annos Zach. I. & fere 70. Zach. VII. quibus jejunaverant in terra? Si enim hi sunt anni captivitatis Babylonicæ, quare non 110. potius nume- rantur? Tot enim sunt ad annum usg, secundum Hy- staspide, nisi & de annis Cyri demimus quantum libet. Erunt minimum 89. at qui secundum ipsorum rationes quindecim præter propter annis fuit in terram redu- ctis ob prohibitam templi ædificationem occasio jeju- nandi præbita. Quare Artaxerxes nominatur Cambyses? Quis erit Assueros inter Cyrum & Cam- bysem? An forte & ipse Cambyses, & sic Assueros & Artaxerxes & Cambyses idem erit? Nam esse commune nomen Persicorum Regum Artaxerxes, ab omni verisimilitudine abludit. Diversis enim no- minibus appellantur, alii Cyrii, Darii alii, Assue- ri alii, Artaxerxæ alii. Si vero is Cambyses, cur ponitur post Darium? Esdr. IV. 5. 6. 7. Aut si Assueros Smerdes, cur ponitur ante Artachsastam, qui sit Cambyses? Quis erit Artaxerxes sequens Da- rium restitutorem templi, quum Hystaspidi successerit Xerxes, quartus Rex Persarum, Daniel. XI. v. 2. Hæc ille, ad quæ ut strictim respondeamus (1) con- funduntur anni captivitatis, & servitutis Babylo- nicæ, cum annis desolationis & vastitatis Hierosoly- mitanæ. Hi ineunt ab excidio urbis, illi à quin- to Jojakimi. Erant itaque LXX. anni inde ab ex- cidio Hierofolymæ elapsi, uti Zach. c. I. 12. indi- cat, usque ad annum II. Darii Hystaspis : nimirum XXVII. anni Nebucadnezaris. II. Evilmerodachi, IV. Niricassolassaris, 9. menses Labosodoarchi, XVII. Nabonidi, IX. Monarchiæ Cyri (non XIX. uti Coccejus numerat, confundenis annos regni Cyri Persici, cum annis Monarchiæ & Imperii Cy- ri) IIX. Cambysis, & Magorum, & II. Darii Hy- staspis. (2) Cambyses nominatur Esdr. IV. 6. A- hasverus. (3) Inter Cyrum & Cambysen nullus est Ahasverus, sed Cambysem sequutus est Smerdis communi nomine vocatus Ahasverus vel Artachsa- sta Esdr. IV. 7. Quod nomen etsi commune fue- rit, certis tamen appropriatum est. Unde nun- cupatus Artaxerxes ὁ μακρόχειρ & ὁ μνήμων, si- cuti etiam nomen Darii, juxta quosdam, commune nonnullis appropriatur Dario Hystaspis, Dario Notho, Dario Codomanno. (4) Non ponitur Ahasverus post Darium Esdr. V. 5. 6. 7. sed Da- rius ut posterior introducitur, quod ex ejusdem ca- pitis v. 24. manifestum (5) Darium restauratorem templi non immediate sequutus est Artaxerxes, sed Xerxes, quod è Dan. XI. 2. etiam constat. Hunc autem excepit Artaxerxes ὁ μακρόχειρ Lon- gimanus Esdr. VII. 1. 8. c. VI. 44. Neh. l. 1. c. XIII. 6.

Vers. eod. FACTUM EST VERBUM DOMINI IN MANU AGGÆI PROPHETÆ] Id est, per Aggæum, Prophetam: Hebraismus satis notus.

AD ZOROBABEL FILIUM SALATHIEL] De hujus genere vide quæ diximus ad Luc. III. 23. & sequen- tibus.

Non Filium Zorobabelem, sed nepotem Sala- thielis fuisse statuunt plerique, quem filium non naturale, sed jure successionis dici vult Junius. De Grotii sententia diximus ad Luc. III. 23.

DUCEM JUDA] Εθνάρχην, ἡγεμόνα, ἄρχοντα τῇ Ιυ- δαίων, ut Josephus loquitur. Reverebrantur quidem eum Judæi in animo suo quasi Regem, quod ex Davidis fami- lia diu regnatrice ortum duceret, sed regium nomen ei splendoremque non circumdabant, ne Persarum regum, sub quorum erant tutela, partim & imperio, animos offen- derent.

Zorobabelem pro Rege salutatum & cultum à Judæis fuisse, assumit Grotius, ut loca scriptu- ræ, quæ de Rege Messia sub nomine David agunt, Zorobabeli applicet, quem vero S. S. nunquam Regem, sed Ducem nominavit, neque à Judæis pro Rege habitum fuisse, etsi ex familia regnatri- ce ortum traxerit, certo documento constat, qui- bus prædixerat potius Ezech. c. XXI. 26. Tolle co- ronam, quia non ultra sic erit &c.

ET AD JESUM FILIUM JOSEDEC SACER- DOTEM MAGNUM] Natus quidem hic erat ex Aaro- nis sanguine, sed ad summum Sacerdotium electus à Syne- drio, sicut olim à regibus Judæis fieri solebat. Dicta hæc illis duobus, sed coram populo, ut apparet infra 12.

## 1:2
Verse 2.

THIS PEOPLE SAYS] That slothful and greedy commonalty, THE TIME IS NOT YET COME FOR THE HOUSE OF THE LORD TO BE BUILT] They had no just causes for not believing Haggai, who exhorted them daily, except for private affections standing in the way of public benefits. The Prophet will now touch this sore.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

POPULUS ISTE DICIT] Plebs illa pigra & avara, NONDUM VENIT TEMPUS DOMUS DOMI- NI ÆDIFICANDÆ] Nullas justas habebant causas Ag- gæo qui eos quotidie hortabatur,non credendi, nisi priva- tos affectus obstantes publicis commodis, Hoc ulcus jam tanget Propheta,

## 1:3
Verse 3. AND THE WORD WAS MADE] Nevertheless it is true that God has commanded me what I say.

IN THE HAND OF HAGGAI THE PROPHET] That is, mine. Thus the Hebrews often place a noun for a pronoun.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET FACTUM EST VERBUM] Attamen verum est Deum mihi quæ dico præcepisse.

IN MANU AGGÆI PROPHETÆ] Id est, mea. ita sæpe Hebræi nomen ponunt pro pronomine.

## 1:4
Verse 4. IS IT TIME FOR YOU TO DWELL IN CEILED HOUSES] In your own affairs no time is too late: in the affairs of God you believe every time is premature; David was not so minded, to whose words there is an allusion here not obscurely. They are 2 Sam. 7:2, Psalm 132. בתים ספנים, are ceiled houses. Thus ספינה among the Chaldeans and Arabs is a covered or decked ship.

AND THIS HOUSE DESERTED] While that house remains prostrate: that is, the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 4. NUMQUID TEMPUS VOBIS EST UT HABITETIS IN DOMIBUS LAQUEATIS] In vestris rebus nullum tempus serum est: in Dei rebus omne tem- pus præmaturum creditis, non ita animatus fuit David, ad cujus verba non obscure hic respicitur. Sunt ea 2. Sam. VII. 2. Psal. CXXXII. בתים ספנים, sunt domus tectæ. Sic ספינה Chaldæis & Arabibus navis tecta, sive constra- ta.

ET ISTA DOMUS DESERTA] Ista domo manen- te prostrata: id est, templo.

## 1:5
Verse 5. SET YOUR HEARTS UPON YOUR WAYS] Again and again attend to what you are doing.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PONITE CORDA VESTRA SUPER VIAS VESTRAS] Etiam atque etiam attendite quid agatis.

## 1:6
Verse 6. YOU HAVE SOWN MUCH AND BROUGHT IN LITTLE] Into the barns, God not prospering your labors, and thus avenging the neglect of Himself.

YOU HAVE EATEN AND ARE NOT SATISFIED] Hosea 4:10.

YOU HAVE DRUNK AND ARE NOT FILLED] There was not enough wine from which you might drink for cheerfulness.

YOU HAVE CLOTHED YOURSELVES, AND ARE NOT WARMED] περιεβάλετε. You have clothed yourselves, as also the Chaldean, you were so thinly clothed that it was not enough for well warming the body. See what we have said at James 2:16.

AND HE WHO HAS GATHERED WAGES, HAS PUT THEM INTO A BAG WITH HOLES] Like the jar of the Danaids, which always leaks. Whatever your labors have produced, that immediately goes into expenses. Thus one rarely lives.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SEMINASTIS MULTUM ET INTULISTIS PARUM] In horrea, Deo labores vestros non prosperan- te, & sic ulciscente neglectum sui.

COMEDISTIS ET NON ESTIS SATIATI] O- see IV. 10.

BIBISTIS ET NON ESTIS INEBRIATI] Non satis fuit vini unde ad hilaritatem biberetis.

OPERUISTIS VOS, ET NON ESTIS CALE- FACTI] περιεβάλετε. Vestivistis vos, quomodo & Chal- dæus, tam tenuiter fuistis vestiti, ut non satis id fuerit bene fovendo corpori. Vide quæ diximus ad Jacobum II. 16.

ET QUI MERCEDES CONGREGAVIT, MI- SIT EAS IN SACCULUM PERTUSUM] Quasi dolium Danaidum, quod semper perfluit. Quicquid opera vestra peperistis, id statim abit in impendia. Ita raro vivitur.

## 1:8
Verse 8. GO UP INTO THE MOUNTAIN] Moriah.

AND I WILL BE ACCEPTABLE TO ME, AND I WILL BE GLORIFIED] It will please me to show my majesty in that house, thus the Chaldean here very well.

Ludov. de Dieu understands הבית as common houses, as in v. 9, which each of the Jews was building for himself, and he renders those words 'go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house, and I will take pleasure in it and I will be glorified,' that is, I will not take pleasure, nor will I be glorified, since in v. 9 a penalty is added: yet the Jews and other interpreters commonly explain it as the House of the Lord. At the end of the word ואכבד the letter He is missing, from which the Rabbis and Talmudists gather that five things were missing in the second temple: the Ark of the Covenant, the Urim and Thummim, the sacred fire, the presence of God in the holy of holies above the mercy seat and the Cherubim, and the Prophets and prophecies. R. Bechai indeed adds to these also the sacred oil, but Buxtorff refutes him in his Exercitations, and thus not five but six sacred things would have been missing, which is against the Talmudic opinion.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ASCENDITE IN MONTEM] Moria.

ET ACCEPTABILIS MIHI ERIT, ET GLO- RIFICABOR] Placebit mihi in ea domo ostendere maje- statem meam, ita optime hic Chaldæus.

Ludov. de Dieu הבית de domibus communi- bus intelligit, ut v. 9. quas sibi Judæorum quisque struebat, & reddit verba ista ascendite ad montem, & adferte lignum, & ædificate domum, an delecta- bor & glorificabor, id est, non delectabor, neque glorificabor, siquidem v. 9. pœna subjiciatur: Judæi tamen & alii Interpp. communiter de Domo Domini explicant. In fine vocis ואכבד defide- ratur He ex quo Rabbini & Talmudici colligunt quinque in templo secundo defuisse, arcam Testa- menti, Urim & Thumim, ignem sacrum, præsentiam Dei in sancto sanctorum super propitiatorium & Cherubim, Prophetas & prophetias. Addit qui- dem R. Bechai his etiam oleum sacrum, sed eum refellit Buxtorff. in Exercitat. & defuissent ita non quinque sed sex res sacræ quod est contra senten- tiam Talmudicam.

Vers. 9. YOU LOOKED FOR MUCH] To increase your wealth, while you neglect the temple.

AND LO IT BECAME LITTLE] Your property has been diminished.

AND I BLEW IT AWAY] I caused it to perish in this way, just as an exhaled breath perishes. Job XI. 20.

AND YOU RUN EVERY MAN TO HIS OWN HOUSE] To enrich it. You only attend to your own affairs. You do not care for God, nor does He care for you.

ET ECCE FACTUM EST MINUS] Res vestra deminuta est.

INTULISTIS IN DOMUM] Res partas,

ET EXSUFFLAVI ILLUD] Ita perire feci, sicut perit emissus halitus. Job. XI. 20.

ET VOS FESTINATIS UNUSQUISQUE IN DOMUM SUAM] Locupletandam. Vestras res tantum agitis. Deum non curatis, nec ille vos curat.

Vers. 10. THE HEAVENS ARE RESTRAINED FROM GIVING DEW, AND THE EARTH IS RESTRAINED FROM GIVING ITS FRUIT] Deut. XXVIII. 23.

Vers. 11.

AND I CALLED FOR A DROUGHT UPON THE LAND] I summoned sterility.

AND UPON THE MOUNTAINS] That is, the pasture land.

AND UPON ALL THE LABOR OF THE HANDS] Cultivated trees. Deut. XXVIII. v. 33. Psal. LXXVII. 47.

Vers. 11.

Vers. 12.

## 1:13
Ver. 13.

AND HAGGAI THE MESSENGER OF THE LORD IN THE MESSAGES OF THE LORD] The legate of the Lord in the embassy of the Lord, the Prophet said this which follows, not in his own name, but in the name of God himself. This fits the Hebrew very well: and so the Chaldean also understands it.

I AM WITH YOU] I will be with you for help, as the Chaldean translates here. See what we have said at Matt. XXVIII. v. 20.

Vers. 13.

EGO VOBISCUM SUM] Auxilio vobis ero, ut hic vertit Chaldæus. Vid. quæ diximus ad Matth. XXVIII. v. 20.

## 1:14
Ver. 14. AND THE LORD STIRRED UP THE SPIRIT OF ZERUBBABEL THE SON OF SHEALTIEL, GOVERNOR OF JUDAH, AND THE SPIRIT OF JOSHUA THE SON OF JEHOZADAK, THE HIGH PRIEST, AND THE SPIRIT OF THE REST OF ALL THE PEOPLE] He added courage to them,

AND THEY WERE DOING THE WORK] That is, they were gathering the materials. The things which are below in II. 19 require this sense.

That reasoning from ch. II. 19 does not conclude in favor of the opinion of R. Solomon and Kimchi, that these things deal only with hewn wood and stones. But if only material was prepared, and the structure itself not begun until the ninth month, how are they already commanded to see the new house in the seventh month, ch. II. 3? Add that in v. 14 the prophet institutes an exhortation to those already working. Compare Cocceius on this passage and on ch. II. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET SUSCITAVIT DOMINUS SPIRITUM ZOROBABEL FILII SALATHIEL DUCIS JUDA, ET SPIRITUM JESU FILII JOSEDEC SACERDO- TIS MAGNI, ET SPIRITUM RELIQUORUM DE OMNI POPULO] Animos illis addidit,

ET FACIEBANT OPUS] Id est, materiam conge- rebant. Hunc sensum exigunt quæ sunt infra II. 19.

Ratio illa è c. II. 19. non concludit pro R. Sa- lomonis & Kimchi sententia, quod tantum de cæsis lignis & lapidibus hæc agant. At si tantum mate- ria præparata, non cœpta ipsa structura, nisi mense nono, quomodo jam videre domum novam ju- bentur mense septimo cap. II. 3. Adde quod v. 14. cohortationem propheta instituat ad jam ope- rantes. Cons. Coccejus ad h. l. & ad c. II. 18.

## 2:1 Argument
THE REMAINING SERMONS OF THE PROPHET. CHAPTER II.

In the second sermon, lest they be deterred by the meaner appearance of the resumed rebuilding of the house of the Lord, Haggai predicts that the glory of the second temple will be greater on account of the παρουσία of the Messiah: In the third, he convicts them of hypocrisy and uncleanness, with the sterility that was sent being designated as the cause of the neglect of the temple of the Lord, and the divine blessing promised on account of the care undertaken for it. The fourth intimates the confusion of the enemies of the Church, and the assumption of Zerubbabel or his seed.

He urges, and teaches that the coming of CHRIST is near.

SERMON II.

Ver. 1.

ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY OF THE MONTH IN THE SIXTH MONTH, IN THE SECOND YEAR OF DARIUS THE KING] These are to be connected with the first chapter: for the time is described in which hands were first applied to the gathering of materials, as we have said. The time in which Haggai delivered his second sermon to the princes and the people now follows: whence the beginning of the second chapter ought to be made.

Latin:

CONCIONES RELIQUÆ PROPHETÆ. CAPUT II.

Altera concione, ne assumta reædificatione domus Do- mini specie viliori absterreantur, prædicit Ag- gæus majorem templi secundi gloriam fore ob παρ- ουsίαν Messiæ: Tertia hypocrisin, & immundi- tiem convincit, sterilitatis immissæ causa designa- ta neglectu templi Domini, & promissa ob susce- ptam ejus curam benedictione divina. Quarta hostium Ecclesiæ confusionem, & Zorobabelis vel seminis ejus assumtionem intimat.

Instat, & adventum CHRISTI docet esse propinquum.

CONCIO II.

Vers. 1.

IN DIE VIGESIMA ET QVARTA MENSIS IN SEXTO MENSE, IN ANNO SECUNDO DARII REGIS] Hæc connectenda sunt cum capite primo: de- scribitur enim tempus, quo primum manus admotæ sunt materiæ, ut diximus, congerendæ. Tempus quo Aggæus alterum sermonem ad principes populumque habuit, jam sequitur: unde initium fieri debet capitis alterius.

## 2:1
Ver. 2.

IN THE SEVENTH MONTH] This sermon was delivered a little before that of Zechariah.

So indeed most think, but there is no reason why we should depart here from the distinction of the Hebrew text, and admit a completely unusual connection: nay, since it seems hardly likely that they delayed for twenty-three whole days from the first sermon, until they came and did the work of the house of the Lord, B. Winckelmann prefers their opinion, who join these with the following in this sense, that the same word was made twice to the Prophet, and the same sermon was delivered twice by him to urge the work of the Lord and to remove the scruples conceived, first on the 24th day of the sixth month Elul, and afterwards again on the 21st day of the seventh month Tishri. B. Balduinus understands these things in such a way that on the 24th day of the sixth month the Prophet received the sentiment of that sermon from GOD, but only proposed it to the people on the 21st day of the seventh month. There had therefore elapsed at the very least 2 weeks from the first sermon which the prophet had delivered to the people, exhortatory to the restoration of the temple, and in this space of time the structure of the temple, by the industry of Zerubbabel and Joshua and the whole people, received such remarkable increments that it now caught the eyes of men, and in some way represented the figure of the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

IN SEPTIMO MENSE] Hic sermo habitus est paulo ante illum Zachariæ.

Ita sane censent plerique, sed non est, quod ab Ebræi textus distinctione hic discedamus, & connexionem prorfus insolitam admittamus: imo quum vix verisimile videatur, illos per integros viginti tres dies à prima concione cunctatos esse, donec venerint & fecerint opus domus Domini, eorum opinionem præfert B. Winckelmannus, qui hæc cum sequentibus conjungunt in hanc sententiam, quod idem verbum bis ad Prophetam factum, eademque concio bis ab eo ad urgendum opus Domini, scrupulosque conceptos eximendos habita sit, primum 24. die mensis sexti Elul, & postea iterum 21. die mensis septimi Thisri. B. Balduinus ita hæc intelligit, quod die 24. mensis sexti Propheta sententiam istius sermonis à DEO acceperit, sed die 21. Mensis septimi demum populo proposuerit. Defluxerant igitur ad minimum 2. septimanæ à prima concione, quam propheta ad populum habuerat, hortatoria ad instaurationem templi, & hoc temporis spatio structura templi industria Zorobabelis & Josuæ totiusque populi, tam eximia incrementa cepit, ut jam in oculos hominum incurreret, & qualitercunque templi figuram repræsentaret.

## 2:3
Vers. 4. WHO AMONG YOU IS LEFT WHO SAW THIS HOUSE IN ITS FORMER GLORY? AND HOW DO YOU SEE IT NOW, IS IT NOT AS IF IT WERE NOTHING IN YOUR EYES] No one could have been a survivor after nearly 180 years. Therefore, you should translate it best this way: If any of you were left who had seen this temple in this place in its former magnificence (such as Solomon and the following kings had given it and Ezekiel described) certainly that which we see (that is, whose foundations we behold laid under Cyrus, much smaller than the old ones 1 Esdras 3, 4) would seem in our judgment to be a thing of nothing. For the temple was ἐνδεέστερος ὁ ναὸς τῶ πάλαι [the temple was more lacking than the former one], because of the meager resources of the people, and because of the haste, as we noted from Josephus on Ezekiel 40.

Setting aside the temple of Ezekiel, which Grotius wrongly makes the same as Solomon's, his calculation is not correct. For if these prophecies were delivered in the 2nd year of Darius Hystaspis, how could 180 or 170 years have passed since the time of the destruction of the former temple? The temple was devastated in the 18th year of Nebuchadnezzar, from which to Evil-merodach 27 years are counted. For he presided over the kingdom for 45 years from the time he was brought into the partnership of the Empire by his parent. Evil-merodach reigned for two years. Niricaffallassarus (Balthasar) for 4 years. Labosodarchus for 9 months. Nabonadus for 17 years, from which emerge 51 years up to the Monarchy of Cyrus. To these add 9 years of the Monarchy of Cyrus, and 8 years of Cambyses (Ahasuerus, Ezra 4:6), including the reign of Smerdis the Magus (Artaxerxes, Ezra 4:7), and two of Darius, and 70 years emerge, which Zechariah designated in chapters 1 and 7. Those, therefore, who were twelve years old at the time of the destruction of the former temple, they could have instituted a comparison of this new structure with the old temple, provided they had reached their eighty-second year of life: so that Grotius committed a parachronism of an entire century here when he required an age of 180 years. There is no need, therefore, for us to understand conditionally those things which sound absolutely: and the Prophet addresses the surviving elders, and commands them to institute a comparison, those who had previously seen the temple, whom Josephus (Antiquities of the Jews, Book 10, Chapter 4) is the authority that they could not restrain themselves from tears. Whence it is manifest that this Darius cannot be established as Nothus, for to his 2nd year from the second year of Darius Hystaspis, 98 years had still flowed, to which, added to the 70 years elapsed from the extermination of the temple to the 2nd year of Darius Hystaspis, 168 years emerge, in which way it would have been necessary for those who had to institute such a comparison of the first and second temple to have been 180 years old.

Cocceius tries to escape with this discovery; that Haggai is doing nothing here other than commemorating the tears of the elders shed long ago, as if to say: long ago when the temple was being founded, many elders were weeping, looking at its smallness. Meanwhile, so many years have flowed. If, therefore, there is now anyone among you of such an age that he can still remember the former building, does this temple not seem like nothing to you? Certainly, if those who saw that one were living, they would consider this as nothing. But this is a vain refuge; for the Prophet does not commemorate in any word the tears of the elders shed LONG AGO: nor does he speak hypothetically, if those who saw the former temple were living, they would consider this as nothing, but he asks absolutely, just as Cocceius himself translated: who among YOU is there, who is a SURVIVOR, who SAW this house in its former glory? And how do YOU see it now? Is it not as nothing in YOUR eyes?

Latin:

Vers. 4. QVIS IN VOBIS EST DERELICTUS QUI VIDIT DOMUM ISTAM IN GLORIA SUA PRI- MA? ET QUID VOS VIDETIS HANC NUNC, NUMQUID NON EST ITA QUASI NON SIT IN OCULIS VESTRIS] Nemo superstites esse poterat post annos ferme CLXXX. Itaque sic vertas optime; Si quis ex vobis superesset qui vidisset templum hoc loco in priori magni- ficentia (qualem Salomon & reges sequentes ei dederant & descripsit Ezechiel) certe ea quam nos videmus (id est, cujus fundamenta adspicimus sub Cyro jacta, multo mi- nora veteribus 1. Esdr. III. IV.) videretur judicio nostro, res esse nihili. Fuit enim ἐνδεέστερος ὁ ναὸς τῶ πάλαι, ob tenues populi opes, & ob festinationem, ut ex Josepho notavimus ad Ezech. XL.

Misso templo Ezechielis, quod perperam idem facit cum Salomoneo Grotius, Calculus ejus non recte habet. Nam si anno II. Darii Hystaspis ha̛ prophetiæ habitæ, quomodo à tempore destru- ctionis prioris templi, 180. vel 170. anni elapsi esse poterunt? Templum devastatum est anno Nebu- cadnezaris XIIX. à quo ad Evilmerodachum nume- rantur XXVII. anni Regno enim præfuit ex quo à parente ad Imperii consortium adsertus fuit per XLV. annos. Evilmerodach duobus annis regnavit. Niricaffallassarus (Balthasar) annis IV. Labosodo- archus 9. mensibus. Nabonadus XVII. unde emer- gunt usque ad Monarchiam Cyri LI. anni. His adde IX. annos Monarchiæ Cyri, & IIX. annos Cam- byfis (Ahasveri Esdr. IV. 6.) incluso Smerdis Magi Artachsasthæ Esdr. IV. 7.) regno, & duos Darii, e- mergunt anni LXX. quos designavit Zacharias I. & VII. Capp. Qui ergo tempore destructionis tem- pli prioris duodecim annorum fuere, illi potuere comparationem novæ hujus structuræ cum veteri templo instituere, quotquot nempe annum octua- gesimum secundum vivendo attigerint: ut para- chronismum integri seculi hic commiserit Grotius, cum ætatem requisivit annorum 180. Non ergo o- pus est, ut conditionaliter ea intelligamus, quæ ab- solute sonant: & compellat Propheta superstites seniores, eosque collationem instituere jubet, qui prius templum adhuc viderant, quos etiam sibi à lacrymis temperare non potuisse autor est Jose- phus l. II. Antiq. Jud. c. IV. Unde manifestum est, non posse hunc Darium statui τὸν Νόθον, nam ad e- jusdem annum II. à Darii Hystasp. secundo fluxe- re adhuc XCIIX. anni, quibus ad LXX. annos ela- psos ab exterminio templi ad II. Darii Hystaspi- dis adjectis emergunt CLXIIX. quo pacto utique 180. annorum fuisse oportuisset, qui talem primi & secundi templi σύγκρισιν instituere debuissent.

Effugere conatur Coccejus hoc ἑὑρήματι; Haggæum hic nihil aliud agere, quam lacrymas se- niorum olim effusas commemorare, q. d. olim cum fundaretur templum flebant multi seniores, inspi- cientes ejus exiguitatem. Fluxerunt interim tot anni. Si igitur jam est aliquis inter vos ejus æta- tis, ut possit adhuc meminisse prioris ædificii, non- na vobis templum hoc pro nihilo videtur? Certe si viverent, qui viderent illud, hoc pro nihilo du- cerent. Sed vanum hoc κρησφύγετον est; Nul- lo enim verbo commemorat Propheta lacrymas Seniorum OLIM effusas: neque hypothetice loqui- tur, si viverent, qui viderunt prius templum, hoc pro nihilo ducerent, sed absolute interrogat, uti Cocce- jus ipse transtulit: quis in VOBIS est, qui SUPER- STES est, qui VIDIT domum hanc in gloria sua priore? Et quid VOS videtis illam nunc? Nonne ut nihilum est in oculis VESTRIS?

## 2:4
Vers. 5. AND NOW BE STRONG, O ZOROBABEL] Be of good courage, you and others. SAYS THE LORD OF HOSTS, AND DO IT] That is, build the temple,

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET NUNC CONFORTARE ZOROBABEL] Bo- no sis animo tu, aliique. DICIT DOMINUS EXERCITUUM, ET FA- CITE] Id est, ædificate templum,

## 2:5
Vers. 6. THE WORD WHICH I COVENANTED WITH YOU WHEN YOU CAME OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT] I will perform for you the same things which I promised to your ancestors coming out of Egypt, Exodus 15:26, Jeremiah 7:23.

AND MY SPIRIT SHALL BE IN THE MIDST OF YOU] That is, you will have the prophets Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. Thus the Chaldean rightly.

Concerning the hypostatic WORD and the HOLY SPIRIT, not ignoble interpreters accept the second and third persons of the divinity, so that the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is held here: for God the Father speaks here and promises his presence to the people, and also that of his Word and Holy Spirit. Cocceius thinks this is clear, that a great testimony is held here concerning the three Witnesses. And unless the words are rendered: I am with you with the Word, and my Spirit stands in the midst of you, everything would be twisted and dislocated. He renders, however, WITH THE WORD WHICH I PROMISED YOU, when you went out of Egypt, so that the angel of the covenant is indicated, i.e., the sponsor, interpreter, and applier of the covenant, and that אֲשֶׁר [asher] may be 'that' or 'concerning which', as in Exodus 33, 'concerning which I swore' Psalm 95:11, 'concerning whom I swore' etc., and the word כָּרַתּי [karathi] may be 'I promised', as in 1 Samuel 22:8, 2 Chronicles 7:18, and the finger may be pointed at the promise in Exodus 22:20, 21. I send an angel before you, which promise may be deduced from the most ancient promise concerning the giving of the Son as Redeemer. These things are not unlearned, but another closer and more suitable promise concerning the matter can be shown to have been made from a comparison of Ex. 20:19 and Deut. 18:16, 17, 18, 19, as we observed in the explanation of Deut. 18. Wherefore, for establishing the testimony of the Holy Trinity, these things serve: (1) because all the persons are expressly stated, the Father speaking, his Word, and his Spirit. (2) That the Son of God is called the Word in the Old Testament, as is gathered from a comparison of 2 Sam. 7:20, 'for thy word's sake,' and 1 Chr. 17:19, 'for thy servant's sake': and it is manifest especially from Ps. 33:6. (3) That the presence and assistance of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit could and should have been especially raised up by the builders of the temple. For what more joyful promise, what greater magnificence can there be in the world than that promise and magnificence of the Church, that God the Father, in the Son the Redeemer, through his Spirit, should wish to be present with it, and is present? I the Father, as Cocceius paraphrases, am with you, who once cast you off as not my people, and I will be a wall of fire around you. With me is the Son, your Sponsor and Advocate. The Angel of the covenant is with you, nor will he depart from his house before he has offered himself as a victim: my Spirit is in the midst of you, nor will he depart from you, but will preserve the lawgivers and teachers sitting in the seat of Moses until, according to my promise, he is poured out upon your children. (4) Here the federal or testamentary promise of the WORD or MESSIAH is recalled to their memory; with the word which I promised to you. For this is the most simple translation of that phrase. Which promise is the foundation of all grace and blessing. Those who translate, with the word IN WHICH I COVENANTED, posit an ellipsis of the preposition ב without cause, not to mention with Cocceius that it is unusual for it to be read בַּאֲשֶׁר; others supply the ellipsis thus: the word which I covenanted with you, to wit, I will make valid, but there is no need to invent an ellipsis if our explanation is applied. (5) Thus Haggai will harmonize with his contemporary and colleague Zechariah, who openly promises the dwelling of God several times in the second temple, and most clearly describes the Angel of the Lord, who is here called the Word. And with Malachi, who promises the Angel of the covenant and the Lord of the temple in a clear voice, chapter 3:1. (6) Our prophet here pledges the coming of the promised Word in the following verse 6, 'the desire of all nations shall come.' (7) Thus Jerome explained it:

I am with you & My Spirit, & the word, in which I have placed the Testament, acknowledging that the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is exhibited here. B. Tarnovius places here a sufficiently clear testimony concerning this mystery in this passage. The blessed Himmelius, although he refers it to the covenant which Jehovah had struck with the people in Exodus XX, and posits an elliptical expression along with others, nevertheless adds from his own opinion: That it seems to him especially that there is a reference to the promise made to the people concerning the Great Prophet in Deuteronomy XVIII, concerning Christ, who is called the WORD here. Cornelius à Lapide also praises Athanasius for this opinion, Epist. ad Serap., Gregory of Nyssa, book of testimonies against the Jews, Cyril of Jerusalem, Cat. XIX, Theodoret, Remigius, Albert, M. Haymo, and indeed even the Targum. The Chaldean favors this while he translates, my word will be a help to you.
