For these things pertain no more to the Pope than he pertains to the priests of the Old Testament, and this collection is faulty in many ways, as B. Tarnovius rightly [notes] here p. 60.

Latin:

Verf. 12. INTERROGA SACERDOTES LEGEM] Nam illorum erat de ceremoniis respondere, qui eas opti- me noverant. Levit. X. 10. Ezech. XLIV. 23. Mal. II. 7.

Collegit ex hoc loco Bellarm. lib. III. de ver- bo Dei c. IV. plane non esse privatorum hominum ju- dicare de legis sententia, sed observare debuisset Je- suita, quod Sacerdotes consulendi à Propheta re- prehendantur, negligentiæ in officio accusentur, nec fuerint concilium, neque ex suo ingenio in- terpretationes fingere debuerint, sed simpliciter ad legem seu scripturam alligati fuerint, ut de lege consulentibus secundum hanc in rebus dubiis re- sponderent. Quæ vero hæc est consequentia? in re- bus dubiis in Vet. T. præsertim ceremonialibus consulendi erant sacerdotes, qui ex verbo Dei re- velato cogebantur responsa dare. Ergo in dictis scripturæ clarissimis omnibus semper, etiam in N. T. ille tantum sensus eorum genuinus erit, quem solus Papa cum Concilio præter & contra Scriptu- ram plerumque fingit? Item, hi sacerdotes negli- gentiæ in officio rei peraguntur, cum ipsis quæstio hæc præsens à Propheta proponitur. E. Papæ Romano cum Concilio hic stabilitur autoritas? ni- hilo enim magis hæc pertinent ad Papam, quam iste ad sacerdotes V. T. & multis modis vitiosa est hæc collectio, uti recte hic B. Tarnovius p. 60.

## 2:12
Verse 13. IF A MAN SHALL CARRY HOLY FLESH] That is, sacrificial [flesh], which is sanctified by the altar.

IN THE SKIRT OF HIS GARMENT] In the hem.

THEY ANSWERED NO] Well, for that legal holiness is not communicated as easily as legal impurity. Thus also there are many ways of vices: one of virtue, and it is difficult:

Ἐσθλὸν μὲν γὰρ ἁπλῶς, παντοδαπῶς δὲ κακὸν.

Latin:

Verf. 13. SI TULERIT HOMO CARNEM SAN- CTIFICATIONEM] Id est, victimalem, quæ, sanctifi- catur per altare.

IN ORA TESTIMENTI SUI] In lacinia.

DIXERUNT NON] Bene, neque enim tam facile legalis illa sanctitas communicatur, quam impuritas le- galis. Sic etiam vitiorum multæ sunt viæ: virtutis una ac difficilis:

Ἐσθλὸν μὲν γὰρ ἁπλῶς, παντοδαπῶς δὲ κακὸν.

## 2:13
Verse 14. AND THE PRIESTS ANSWERED, AND SAID, IT SHALL BE UNCLEAN] From the law Num. XIX. 22.

Latin:

Verf. 14. ET RESPONDERUNT SACERDOTES, ET DIXERUNT, CONTAMINABITUR] Ex lege Num. XIX. 22.

## 2:14
Verse 15. SO IS THIS PEOPLE]. With a mind not well cleansed, nor composed to full obedience, the gifts which they have hitherto offered to God upon that altar built in the open air in the time of Cyrus (Ezra III. 3.) did not make them holy, that is, acceptable to God, but on the contrary, an impure mind contaminated the gifts themselves, that is, rendered them unacceptable.

The Prophet looks primarily at the disobedience and neglect of the structure of the temple, because they cared only for private matters, but neglected the house of the Lord, and he teaches that sacrifices and all works are polluted thereby, and that most certain punishments are drawn down, by the example of sanctified things, which by legal rite and custom did not sanctify common and profane things, but rather were themselves contaminated by unclean things if they were touched, and he contends so that the people, having performed repentance, may strenuously do the work of the Lord. Therefore, the old error of the Jews is refuted here, that sacrifices appease man to God ex opere operato, even if a man offers them without repentance and faith. Coccejus rightly says here, p. 463: This is a document by which every καθαρότητι τῆς σαρκὸς was prejudiced, because there was no τελείωσις in it, and because all sacrifices were useless for expiating sins and pacifying the conscience. Likewise, to every work of ours, however good it may be in appearance, if either the faith of the heart or the righteousness of Christ is lacking, without which sin, which defiles all things, is not removed, so that finally in the communion of Christ, which we obtain through faith, our works please GOD as one who forgives and shows mercy, not despising them as fruits of righteousness and the glorification of justification.

Latin:

Verf. 15. SIC POPULUS ISTE]. Animo non bene emundato, neque ad omnem obedientiam composito, quæ Deo hactenus obtulere dona super altare illud sub dio ædificatum Cyri tempore (Esdræ III. 3.) ea illos non fecere sanctos, id est, Deo gratos, sed contra impurus animus dona ipsa contaminavit, id est, ingrata reddidit.

Respicit imprimis Propheta inobedientiam, & neglectum structuræ templi, quod res tantum privatas curarent, domum vero Domini negligerent, eo- que sacrificia & omnia opera pollui, ac certissimas pœnas attrahi, docet exemplo sanctificatorum, quæ ritu & more legali non sanctificabant res com- munes & prophanas, sed potius ipsa ab immundis, si tangerentur, contaminabantur, adeoque conten- dit, ut populus, acta pœnitentia, strenue faciat o- pus Domini. Refutatur ergo hic vetus Judæorum error, sacrificia ex opere operato hominem Deo placa- re, ut maxime homo sine pœnitentia & fide ea of- ferat. Recte hic Coccejus p. 463. Hoc est docu- mentum, quo præjudicabatur omni καθαρότητι τῆς σαρκὸς, quod in ea non esset τελείωσις, quodq; omnia sacrificia essent inutilia ad expianda peccata & pacifi- candam conscientiam. Item omni operi nostro, quan- tumvis in speciem bonum sit, si desit vel fidei cordis vel justitia Christi, sine qua peccatum omnia fœdans non tollitur, ita ut demum in Christi communione, quam per fidem obtinemus, opera nostra DEO placeant ut condonanti, miseranti, ut fructus justitiæ & glorifi- cationem justificationis non spernenti.

## 2:15
Ver. 16. AND NOW SET YOUR HEARTS] Observe what has happened to you until now, before you set your hand to this work.

BEFORE A STONE WAS LAID UPON A STONE] A stone laid by you upon a stone in the times of Cyrus. Ezra III, 10.

Latin:

Verf. 16. ET NUNC PONITE CORDA VESTRA] Animadvertite, quid hactenus vobis evenerit, antequam huic operi admoveretis manum.

ANTEQUAM PONERETUR LAPIS SUPER LAPIDEM] Lapis à vobis supra Lapidem positum Cyri temporibus. Esdr. III, 10.

## 2:16
Ver. 17. WHEN YOU CAME TO A HEAP OF TWENTY MEASURES] In the Hebrew: From the time they existed, namely those times of your negligence: when someone came to a heap of twenty: namely of measures: that is, from the time he hoped that he would thresh out twenty measures.

AND THERE WERE TEN] There were only ten. To such an extent was a large part of the crops corrupted in a short time. The same follows regarding the grapes.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CUM ACCEDERETIS AD ACERVUM VIGINTI MODIORUM] In Hebræo: Ex quo exstitere, nempe tempora illa negligentiæ vestræ: veniente aliquo ad acervum viginti: nempe modiorum: id est, ex quo sperabat, se excussurum viginti modios.

ET FIERENT DECEM] Ibi fiebant tantum decem. Adeo brevi corrumpebatur pars magna frugum. Idem de uvis sequitur.

## 2:17
Ver. 18. I SMOTE YOU WITH A SCORCHING WIND] With blight. For that is שׁדפון Deut. XXVIII. 22. 1 Kings VIII. 37. Amos IV. 9. You, that is, your fortunes, as he will now explain.

AND WITH MILDEW] With rust. For it is a question here of the diseases of crops, not of men. The Latin interpreter translates ירקון as rust in Deuteronomy XXVIII. 22, where, however, mildew could have been understood no less correctly.

ALL THE WORKS OF YOUR HANDS] All the sowings. It is an explanation of that 'you'.

AND THERE WAS NO ONE AMONG YOU WHO TURNED TO ME] With your whole heart, that is.

Latin:

Vers. 18. PERCUSSI VOS VENTO URENTE] Uredine. Id enim שׁדפון Deut. XXVII. 22. 1. Reg. IIX. 37. Am. IV. 9. Vos, id est, fata vestra, ut jam explicabit.

ET AURUGINE] Rubigine. De frugum enim non de hominum morbis hic agitur. ירקון rubiginem vertit & Latinus interpres Deuter. XXIX. 22. ubi tamen aurugo non minus recte poterat intelligi.

OMNIA OPERA MANUUM VESTRARUM] Sata omnia. Est explicatio illius vos.

ET NON FUIT IN VOBIS, QUI REVERTERETUR AD ME] Toto scilicet animo.

## 2:18
Ver. 19. FROM THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY OF THE NINTH MONTH] That is, keep in memory this day, which we are now observing, from which all things will henceforth be prosperous for you.

FROM THE DAY THE FOUNDATIONS WERE LAID OF THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD] From this day, on which the temple is begun, that is to say, built upon foundations laid long ago. יסד is often to begin, and is translated ἄρχεσθαι in 2 Chronicles 3:3, κτίζειν in Exodus 9:18, and elsewhere συνάγειν, ἐπισυνάγειν, καταρτίζειν.

This is the opinion of Arias, that on the 24th day of August, as is held in chapter 1 at the end, the necessary materials only began to be prepared. But after three months, on the 24th of November, the foundations were laid in every part: but because the foundations had already begun to be placed in the 2nd year of the Monarchy of Cyrus in the month of April, Lyranus, Dionysius, and Vatablus believe that on the 24th of November of this 2nd year of Darius, stones were arranged in a certain order upon the foundations previously laid. Nor can it be proven that the word יסד ought to be translated ἄρχεσθαι. For what the LXX Interpreters rendered thus in 2 Chronicles 3:3, as Bælius notes in his Historical and Chronological works, p. 193, is against all other ancient and modern interpreters, and against the sense and scope of the passage. For there it is not the beginning of the work, but its arrangement by the Spirit or by Father David and Solomon, the instruction and foundation, that is handed down, as to how the whole work was to be carried out. Castrius interprets it thus on p. 452. Cast the eyes of your mind to all the previous years up to that year in which a stone had not yet begun to be placed upon a stone, namely up to the second year of Cyrus, in which the house of the Lord began to be founded. Cast also the eyes of your mind to the future years after this 24th day of November. Cast, I say, the eyes of your mind to this whole series of years, which begins from the 1st day of April of the second year of Cyrus, in which the foundations of the temple were laid, and ends in the future: and you will recognize that the certain cause of your past unhappiness and calamity was the neglected worship of God, and the temple not being built: on the contrary, that the cause of future happiness, which you will enjoy in the following years, will be the care of divine worship and the diligence applied to building the temple, so that from this the true counsel of Christ in Matthew 6:33 may be proven: Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you. Ludovicus de Dieu, although he acknowledges that וִמַעְלָה is correctly rendered by Junius in verse 16 as 'to the days which had preceded,' nevertheless prefers in this place the Vulgate version 'AND IN THE FUTURE.' Since God, who had punished their negligence in the further days before they devoted effort to building the temple, commands that they now observe from this day and henceforth, whether he is not on the contrary going to bless them most abundantly: moreover, that מַעְלָה refers not only to past time, but also to the future, he teaches from 1 Samuel 16:13. Furthermore, there is no need for us to say that the foundations were finally laid on the 24th day of November, for this description of the day on which the foundations were laid can be referred to earlier times, from which, because the work of the LORD was interrupted, the less fertile years flowed. And it is certain from the book of Ezra, chapter 2:8, 9.

That the foundations were laid in the time of Cyrus. Therefore, from that time until the present second year of Darius Hystaspis, that is, for about 17 years, the Prophet signifies that they did not experience as great a blessing as they are to receive in the years to come from this time, when they have again set their hands to the work of the Lord, if they continue it. Wherefore there is no need for us, with Lyranus, Arias Montanus, Ribera, Sanctius, and Cornelius, whose opinion Bailius interpolated, to believe that upon the foundations laid in the days of Cyrus, as if they were first and imperfect, others were built up in the days of Darius, completed and perfect. For shall we judge foundations placed upon foundations and the previous labor to be thus as it were void, and deny that work its reward?

Latin:

Vers. 19. A DIE VIGESIMA ET QUARTA NONI MENSIS] Id est, memoria retinete hunc diem, quem nunc agimus, à quo omnia deinceps vobis erunt prospera.

A DIE QUA FUNDAMENTA JACTA SUNT TEMPLI DOMINI] Ab hoc die, quo incipitur templum, strui scilicet super jactis pridem fundamentis. יסד sæpe est incipere, & vertitur ἄρχεσθαι 2. Paralip. III. 3. κτίζειν, Exod. IX. 18. alibi, συνάγειν, ἐπισυνάγειν, καταρτίζειν.

Est hæc Ariæ sententia, die 24. Augusti, ut habetur in c. 1. fine, parari tantum cœpisse necessaria. Post tres autem menses die 24. Nov. jacta esse omni ex parte fundamenta: sed quia fundamenta jam cœperunt poni Anno 2. Monarchiæ Cyri Mense Aprili, Lyranus, Dionysius & Vatablus die 24. Nov. hujus anni II. Darii lapides supra fundamenta prius jacta, serie quadam digestos censent. Neque probari potest verbum יסד verti debere ἄρχεσθαι. Quod enim ita reddiderunt LXX. Interpp. 2. Par. III. 3. id, notante Bælio in oper. Histor. Chronol. p. 193. contra omnes alios interpp. veteres & novos est, & contra loci sensum & scopum. Ibi enim non initium operis, sed ejus dispositio à Spiritu vel Patre Davide & Salomone, instructio & fundatio traditur, quomodo totum opus peragendum. Castrius sic interpretatur p. 452. Conjicite oculos mentis vestræ ad omnes superiores annos usq́, ad annum illum, quo nondum cœperat poni lapis super lapidem, nempe usq́ ad annum Cyri secundum, quo cœpit fundari domus Domini. Conjicite quoq́, oculos mentis vestræ in annos futuros post diem hunc 24. Novembris. Conjicite, inquam, oculos mentis in hanc omnem seriem annorum, quæ incipit à die 1. Aprilis anni secundi Cyri, quo jacta sunt fundamenta templi, & desinit in futurum: & cognoscetis præterita vestra infelicitatis, & calamitatis causam certam fuisse cultum Dei neglectum, & templum non ædificatum: contra vero futuræ felicitatis, qua persequentes annos perfruemini, curam divini cultus futuram, & templi ædificandi adhibitam diligentiam, ut hinc verum comprobetur consilium Christi Matth. 6, 33. Quærite primum regnum Dei & justitiam ejus, & hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Ludovicus de Dieu, etsi agnoscat וִמַעְלָה recte à Junio v. 16. reddi ad dies quæ præcesserant, præfert tamen hoc loco vulgatam versionem ET IN FUTURUM. Siquidem jubeat Deus, qui ulterioribus diebus antequam templo struendo operam navarent, negligentiam eorum puniverat, jam ab hoc die & deinceps animadvertant, annon contra sit cumulatissime benedicturus: מַעְלָה autem non tantum ad præteritum tempus, sed & ad futurum referri, docet è 1. Sam. XVI. 13. Cæterum non opus est, ut 24. die mensis Nov. demum jacta fuisse fundamenta dicamus, hæc enim diei descriptio, quo jacta sunt fundamenta, ad superiora tempora referri potest, ex quibus ob intermissum opus DOMINI fluxere anni minus fertiles. Et certum est è libr. Esdr. cap. II. 8. 9.

Cyri tempore fundamenta jacta fuisse. Ex illo er- go tempore usque ad præsentem annum secun- dum Darii Hystaspis, h. e. per 17. circiter annos tantam non sensisse ipsos benedictionem, quan- tam ab hoc tempore, quo iterum manus admove- runt operi Domini, deinceps futuris annis, si id continuaverint, percepturi sint, Propheta signifi- cat. Quapropter non opus est, ut cum Lyrano A- riamontano, Ribera, Sanctio & Cornelio quorum sententiam interpolavit Bailius, credamus funda- mentis in diebus Cyri jactis ceu primis & imperfe- ctis diebus Darii alia superstructa completa & perfe- cta. Fundamenta enim super fundamenta posita & laborem priorem ita veluti irritum esse curdica- mus, operæque isti pretium suum denegemus?

## 2:19
Vers. 20. IS THE SEED YET IN THE BARN?] Is the germ not yet in the barn? That is, no seed has yet been committed to the earth. For it was the month of November.

AND THE VINE, AND THE FIG TREE, AND THE POMEGRANATE, AND THE OLIVE TREE HATH NOT BROUGHT FORTH] You see that the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive have not yet blossomed.

FROM THIS DAY I WILL BLESS] That is, even now I promise the greatest abundance of all these things, of which no beginnings yet appear, so that it may be evident that this is owed to me, not to nature.

SERMON IV. AND THE LAST.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NUMQUID JAM SEMEN IN GERMINE EST?] Nonne adhuc germen in horreo est? Id est, nullum adhuc semen terræ madatum est. Erat enim mensis No- vember.

ET ADHUC VINEA, ET FICUS, ET MALO- GRANATUM ET LIGNUM OLIVÆ NONDUM FLORUIT] Videtis nondum florere vitem, ficum, malum punicam, & oleam.

EX DIE ISTA BENEDICAM] Id est, jam nunc promitto ubertatem maximam omnium istarum rerum, quarum nulla adhuc initia comparent, ut appareat mihi hoc, non naturæ deberi.

CONCIO IV. ET ULTIMA.

## 2:20
Vers. 21. AND THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME THE SECOND TIME] The second time, namely on the same day: for otherwise this is the third discourse.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET FACTUM EST VERBUM DOMINI SE- CUNDO] Secundo, nempe eadem die: nam alioqui tertius; hic est sermo.

## 2:21
Vers. 22. I WILL SHAKE THE HEAVENS AND THE EARTH] I will bring about great things, with great storms stirred up in the heavens, and wars on the earth. One storm at Mount Athos destroyed twenty thousand men of King Darius.

Latin:

Vers. 22. EGO MOVEBO COELUM PARITER ET TERRAM] Res magnas efficiam, magnis in cœlo excita- tis tempestatibus, in terra bellis. Una tempestas ad mon- tem Athon Dario regi viginti hominum millia absumsit.

## 2:22
Vers. 23. AND I WILL OVERTHROW THE THRONE OF KINGDOMS] The empire of the Persians in Egypt, which is near to the Jews: see Herodotus at the beginning of book VII.

AND I WILL DESTROY THE STRENGTH OF THE KINGDOM OF THE GENTILES] Darius, king of many nations, will receive the greatest defeats from the Greeks by land and sea. See Herodotus book VI, Pausanias in the Attica, Justin book II, and Plutarch in the Life of Cimon.

AND I WILL OVERTHROW THE CHARIOT, AND HIM THAT RIDETH IN IT, AND THE HORSES AND THEIR RIDERS SHALL COME DOWN] That is, they shall fall.

BY THE SWORD OF HIS BROTHER] He calls the Persians, Egyptians, Ionians of Asia, and Greeks brothers among themselves, who were all polytheists.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET SUBVERTAM SOLIUM REGNO- RUM] Imperium Persarum in Ægypto Judæis vicina: vi- de Herodotum initio libr. VII.

ET CONTERAM FORTITUDINEM REGNI GENTIUM] Maximas clades Darius, rex plurimarum gentium, à Græcis accipiet terra marique. Vide Hero- dotum libr. VI. Pausaniam Atticis, Justinum libro II, & Plutarchum Cimone.

ET SUBVERTAM QUADRIGAM, ET ASCEN- SOREM EJUS, ET DESCENDENT EQUI, ET ASCENSORES EORUM] Id est, cadent.

IN GLADIO FRATRIS SUI] Fratres vocat in- ter se Persas, Ægyptios, Jonas Asiæ, Græcos, qui o- mnes erant πολύθεοι.

## 2:23
Vers. 24. I WILL TAKE THEE, O ZOROBABEL, THE SON OF SALATHIEL, MY SERVANT, SAITH THE LORD, AND WILL MAKE THEE AS A SIGNET] By such movements, with almost the whole world shaken, I will bring it about that Judea, with you as leader, shall be safe and molested by no one. We are accustomed to guard a signet ring well. See Cant. VIII, 6, and what was said on Jer. XXII, 24.

BECAUSE I HAVE CHOSEN THEE] That is, because I love thee: σὲ ἠρίτησα, LXX. which is the same as if you were to say, ἐν σοὶ ἐυδόκησα: which locution the Chaldean uses here. See what is said at Matt. III, 17.

Theodoret also explained it of Zerubbabel alone (although he himself wishes the subversion of Gog and Magog to be indicated), as also primarily the Hebrews according to Lyra and Vatablus, who judge that the destruction of the Persians is promised here. Others, however, receive this prophecy concerning Christ, who is noted by the name of Zerubbabel by that formula of speaking by which the names of fathers are wont to be taken in the Holy Scriptures as patronymics for their descendants, as Solomon for a descendant of Solomon in Ps. LXXII, 1, David for a descendant of David in Ezek. XXXIV, 23, Hos. III, 5, so that Zerubbabel is said for a descendant of Zerubbabel: and indeed Ambrose in lib. III, Epist. XII, Jerome, Haymo, and Hugo explain it of the later advent of Christ, when, with all kingdoms subverted and nations crushed, after the shaking of heaven and earth, all things will be subjected to the feet of Christ, whom the Father established as a seal, to whose image all the elect are to be conformed.

Dionysius and Vatablus, however, understand it of the former advent, when heaven and earth were shaken, and other kingdoms subverted and subjected to the Roman, and God assumed flesh from Zerubbabel: as Cyril of Alexandria in this place, p. 650. Who wishes the destruction of the malignant and contrary powers and mighty works to be designated, which the Savior triumphed over on his cross. And thus Cocceius in this place. interprets it of Christ, and just as Christ is otherwise called David, both because he is of the seed of David and because David was a type of Christ, so he thinks Zerubbabel himself is called here, both because Christ is the seed of Zerubbabel and because Zerubbabel in the reduction from captivity and in the building of the temple is a type of Christ, who is called the servant of God with emphasis, because he fulfilled the law to provide righteousness even for sinners: explaining it in this way: Meanwhile, while I overturn thrones, I will take thee, and I will demonstrate thee to be him in whom I am pleased, and I will mark thee with all his signs, after the servitude is finished, and finally, when I shall abolish heaven and earth, I will place thee as a seal, or signet ring, i.e., I will be glorified in thee and the Church. Kingdoms will be moved, but so that a new kingdom may arise. Heaven and earth will pass away, but so that the kingdom of glory may be manifested and remain forever. We cannot simply approve this interpretation: both because it is too manifest that these things are to be understood of that Zerubbabel to whom the Prophet had been sent: Speak to Zerubbabel the Governor of Judah, saying: I will move, etc. In that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will take THEE, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant. Assuredly the Lord promises that he will take that Zerubbabel as his servant, to whom the Prophet was then to speak: Whence Castrius rightly asks, why in so few words must the meaning of the name Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, be changed? so that when the Prophet is sent to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, he immediately finds himself speaking with Zerubbabel about Christ: and because this promise was made to Zerubbabel, so that he might be stirred up and confirmed in the instituted work of the construction of the house of the Lord, since he himself as a servant of the Lord faithfully procured divine worship. Wherefore there is no doubt that Zerubbabel himself is addressed here: both because this text is explained of that Zerubbabel by Sirach, who with Joshua the priest built the house of the Lord, c. XLIX, 3. How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? For he also is as a sign (σφραγὶς) a seal in my right hand. Whence most of our people unanimously understand these words of that Zerubbabel according to the letter. Almost only D. Pappus explained it of Christ and his fruits. B. Tarnovius indeed also adds, and the Weimar Paraphrasts add a sense concerning Christ, but they say that it is mystical, and they do not exclude the literal sense concerning Zerubbabel, which may also be observed in the notes of the Belgian Paraphrase in this place. But how the same name, placed once in the same verse, can signify both Zerubbabel and the son of Zerubbabel, and all the predicates and words, each and every one, can sustain a double sense at the same time, does not appear at all. And B. Tarnovius himself urges this axiom elsewhere in his Commentary on this Prophet, that a double sense of one word or saying cannot be established. But this Paraeus is absurd in his Commentary on this place, who acknowledges that the speech is direct to Zerubbabel and ought to be understood of him, yet afterwards explains the same at the same time of his descendants, the leaders of the Jewish people, and of the people themselves, and finally explains it also of the Church and of Christ, so that by Zerubbabel Christ is understood, because he signified Christ. Thus not only two, but three or more senses, and those the same literal ones, will have to be established for the same oracle. Balth. Willius is wiser here in his Commentary, page 75.

The object of the promise is Zerubbabel, whom God shows to be most dear to Himself both by reason of his ancestors and by reason of his office. This, while He calls him His servant with a friendly address, shows how He attributes to Zerubbabel faith and industry and zeal in the committed government of the people, and proclaims concerning him the acknowledgment of faith and love. That, while He makes mention of Shealtiel, who was the grandfather of Zerubbabel as shown in chapter 1, verse 1, but the son of Neri, springing from the family of Nathan, the successor of the right and royal dignity which Jeconiah, the grandson of Josiah, had left deserted and orphaned. For by this pact He shows that He had remembered the promises made to David, and that on that account He would also hold him dear and establish him, according to Psalm 132:11-12: The Lord swore to David in truth, from which He will not turn Himself: Of the fruit of thy body I will set upon thy throne. And these two addresses even alone could have sufficiently animated Zerubbabel. Although the same Willius adds: Furthermore, under Zerubbabel all his descendants together are understood, and Christ Himself also, who lay in his loins, as will be seen immediately. Which we have already warned are ἀσύςατα (inconsistent), unless they are explained in such a way that a double sense is avoided.

Moreover, what is to be carefully observed, there are distinct things in this oracle. First, the prophecy concerning the shaking of heaven and earth is repeated, which the Prophet had proposed to Zerubbabel and the people in the seventh month, and this promise is made to Zerubbabel as Prince not only for the sake of greater βεβαιώσεως (confirmation), so that he might consider that that shaking, by which the desire of the nations will be exhibited and He will unfold His glory, and by it will illuminate the temple which had begun to be built, will most certainly follow: but also for that peculiar reason which pertained specifically to the person of Zerubbabel, and not to the rest of the people, that by that shaking the glory of Zerubbabel himself was to be rendered more illustrious: since he himself was a leader from the royal Davidic stock, from which the Messiah, the desire of the nations, was to come forth. God had therefore chosen the same man, so that the Messiah might be born from his seed, which is hinted at by that repetition. Wherefore there is no other shaking of heaven and earth designated here by the Prophet than that which was previously explained at greater length in verse 6: nor is this shaking to be restricted to the subversion of kingdoms, which the Prophet subjoins, nor is this subversion of kingdoms to be confused with that shaking: for the subversion of kingdoms indeed produces a shaking, but on earth: God, however, says that He will shake heaven and earth alike. Cocceius wishes this shaking to be understood in two ways, namely properly concerning the abolition of the visible form of this world, and improperly concerning the abolition of the external form of the Church, and says that both ought to be understood under these words. But I confess that I do not grasp what he means. And how will it be necessary to understand these same words both properly and improperly at the same time? Calvin is more correct: The Prophet affirms here that a wonderful work of God is at hand, which will shake heaven and earth. That therefore must necessarily be referred to Christ, because it was as it were a new creation of the world, when Christ gathered what had been dissipated in heaven and earth, just as the Apostle says in Colossians 1, when He reconciled men to God and the Angels, when, having defeated the devil, He restored life to the dead, when He shone forth with His righteousness, then truly God shook heaven and earth, and still shakes them today, while the Gospel is preached: because He reforms the sons of Adam to His own image. This spiritual regeneration, therefore, is such a document of the power of the grace of God that it may deservedly make heaven and earth tremble. This is Calvin. We therefore think it sufficiently manifest that this shaking of heaven and earth is the same as that which the Prophet had commemorated above. For he had already protested before that there would not be one shaking and then another: YET ONCE MORE I will shake heaven and earth, which word ἔτι ἅπαξ (yet once more) must be strictly retained and observed, and therefore we hold it as undoubted from the prophetic phrase and the interpretation of the Holy Spirit Himself made in the New Testament that another shaking of heaven and earth has no place before the final συντέλειαν (consummation) of the world. Wherefore, as far as this shaking is concerned, Cyril's commentary is correct: And the most wise Paul indeed, agreeing with the meaning of the proposed words, says that (the being shaken) signifies the future translation of the things that are moved, so that those things which are immovable may remain. But those things which were made through Him were new, namely stable, firm, and remaining. Observe, therefore, the economy of the discourse. For when He had promised them a wonderful abundance of fruits, and had said that He would provide with a full hand all things that pertained to cheering the mind and to delights, He soon subjoined the fruitful time of truth, namely the copious largesse of spiritual and heavenly blessing. For I have shaken the earth, He says, when I led Israel out of the land of Egypt: yet I will shake it again, that is, I will again make it notable and famous to all mortals, shaking almost everything. Rudolph Gualther agrees in Homily VII on Haggai, page 265. He repeats what he had said in the third sermon: I shake the heavens and the earth: and thus he recalls to mind the promise concerning the coming of the Messiah, in whom all other promises are ratified. It is also just as if He were saying: Let not those things which you will see happen hereafter terrify you, O Zerubbabel. For what I once promised to the fathers, and have also recently repeated, will be firm and ratified. And when that predetermined time has arrived, nothing will be able to stand in the way of the Messiah coming and illuminating my house, namely the Church, with the promised glory. For I will shake the heavens and the earth at the same time, and the most solid parts of the world will be moved from their place rather than that I should allow anything to be detracted from this decree of mine. But we have recently said that the whole world was shaken at the coming of the Messiah. Therefore, the too meager gloss of Grotius is not to be approved: I will move heaven and earth: I will accomplish great things by having stirred up storms in heaven and wars on earth. We have previously warned that the Apostle accepted these things in a far different way.

But furthermore, as to the subversion of kingdoms, concerning which the Prophet prophesies, not only Grotius, but others also restrict it to the kingdoms of the Persians, under whose Monarchy Zorobabel flourished, especially the Hebrew ones, whose sense Castrius reports from Lyranus and Vatablus: I will subvert the kingdom of the Persians, whom you fear, along with the rest of the kingdoms of the nations subject to the Persian, and amidst so many wars and dangers I will preserve you, O Zorobabel, and I will have you before my eyes as a signet ring. Others think that the subversion of other kingdoms is also predicted here, and they explain those things distinctly which are contained in verse 22. Thus Castrius: I will subvert the throne of the kingdoms of the Persian Empire, which you fear, and I will crush the strength of the kingdoms of the nations subject to the Persians, and I will subvert the kingdom of the Greeks distributed into four heads, along with their Kings, and finally the Roman Empire will perish: their horses and riders will fall, pierced by mutual swords and civil wars: and amidst these so many downfalls, and so many crises of affairs, and such diverse mutations of kingdoms, I will take you under my care to be guarded, O Zorobabel son of Salathiel, because you have taken care of my worship by building a house for me, as my servant. These are his words. Coccejus thinks the fourth clause concerning horses and riders is APOCALYPTIC. Whose opinion, which is clearly singular, we shall transcribe:

Let us try, he says, whether we might be able to understand this verse according to the cola, so that we may have in it a distinct representation of the empires of the world, which are to yield to the kingdom of Christ, as they are exhibited in other prophecies. We rightly understand the empire that was then, the Persian, in the first colon, which is correctly proposed under the title of the Throne of kingdoms. For the King of the Persians was the king of kings, ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας: who had under his empire one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, whom even the Greeks at that time courteously revered: to whom he acted as the balancer of war and peace. Under the title of the power of the kingdoms of the nations, the empire of the Greeks divided into many kingdoms, of which Scripture designates four in Daniel 8, and describes two in Daniel 9, namely of the Seleucids and the Lagids, administering all things with great violence, can be conveniently understood. Under the name of the Chariot and the riders, the Roman Empire is best understood. By which the power of the kingdoms of the nations was overthrown. For it is a system of one Empire governed by many, namely the Roman Senate, the consuls as charioteers, or even a prince, drawn and advanced like a triumphal chariot by many legions and peoples as if by horses in part of Asia and Africa, in Greece and more Western parts, Europe, Italy, and annexed regions. Daniel points to this empire under the name of the King after the Seleucids and Lagids in chapter 11:36. There is more about the chariots in Zechariah chapter 6. The Horses and Riders falling by fraternal swords follow. Here are understood those kingdoms which, as if horses detached from that triumphal chariot, arose from the division of the Roman Empire, which are mentioned as ten, to have power with the beast for a certain time, according to the Apocalypse, together with other particular kingdoms scattered throughout the whole world, whose end is to wear down and humble one another. But the hypothesis of Cocceius concerning the most recent commotion of heaven and earth, which he assumes, is merely precarious. Indeed, it must be believed that the commotion which was to happen at the coming of Christ is to be understood. Therefore, the explanation of Castrius is to be preferred.

However, the Grotian gloss does not exhaust the sense of the Prophet. For the Prophet does not speak only of the Persian Empire being overturned in Egypt: But simply: I will overturn, he says, THE THRONE OF KINGDOMS, and thus he designates the overturning of the whole Persian Monarchy. Nor only of the disasters of Darius Hystaspis, which he was to receive from the Greeks. But he prophesies about the crushing of the power of the entire kingdom of the nations. And greater were the disasters which Xerxes suffered in Greece with an army of ten hundred thousand in land battles, both at Thermopylae, under the Spartan leader Leonidas, and at Plataea, as well as just as many naval ones at Artemisium and Salamis. Nor is it likely that the Persians, Egyptians, Ionians, and Greeks are called brothers here because they were all polytheists. For thus all nations would have been brothers. Everything is therefore twisted when Grotius attempts to drag these to the times of Darius. But if they extend themselves as far as the Roman empire, how, I ask, were they fulfilled in Zerubbabel, who presided long before the times of Alexander? Resp. (1) The words, in that day, do not precisely designate a certain day, but a tract of time, within which Zerubbabel is to remain secure and safe under divine care and custody amidst the movements and tumults. Furthermore, even if that assumption of Zerubbabel is said to concern Zerubbabel himself: yet it is not to be believed that it pertains only to him, or as his unique person is viewed. The Lord addresses him alone, and promises the grace of assumption to him, but for himself and his posterity. In which manner the expositions of other interpreters are to be conveniently explained, so that a duality of the sense of the words, or of the same clause, is not introduced. Namely, it is not to be thought that Zerubbabel is understood both properly as that ancient Zerubbabel, the leader of the people, and improperly and figuratively as Christ as the antitype. For thus a double sense of the same word is established: much less is it to be said that by Zerubbabel, both the person of the leader, and his people, and Christ his seed are signified, so that a triple sense of the same word emerges. What then? The ancient Zerubbabel himself is understood, but with his posterity included, or rather that assumption is to be explained in such a way that it extends to his preservation, not only regarding his life and rule, but also regarding the propagation and blessing of his posterity. I will take you, Zerubbabel, in such a way that I may preserve you, and protect you, and propagate your lineage amidst these turmoils and overturnings of kingdoms. Thus Castrius: Amidst these so many falls, and so many crises of affairs, and such diverse mutations of kingdoms, I will take you to be guarded under my care, O Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, because you have cared for my worship by building a house for me as my servant: and I will guard you, namely your posterity, as a signet ring in my right hand so that you may be the singular ornament of all Israel. For I, the Lord of hosts, have chosen you, so that Christ may draw his origin from you, who will erect his kingdom, and amidst so many mutations and ruins of kingdoms, will raise his head. Similar to this is that prophecy of Daniel chapter 2, 44.

(2) It can also be said that that assumption is attributed to the Son of God, who is introduced speaking here, as is gathered from the collation of verse 7 with Heb. 12:26, because he himself is to shake heaven and earth alike, and is to overturn the throne of the Kingdom. And thus the Son of God will be said to be assuming Zerubbabel, in such a way that it looks to the special mode of ἐπιλήψεως, by which he is said to take hold of (ἐπιλαμβάνεται) not angels, but the seed of Abraham, as in Heb. 2:16, and this promise is to be compared with that which was made to Abraham in Gen. 12:5: In you shall all nations be blessed. For just as there God promised this to Abraham himself, and so ennobled his lineage, and raised it to this sublime axiom, that the source and cause of all blessing had to come forth from his loins, yet the blessing is promised to come not in Abraham, but in the seed of Abraham, with the Son of God himself as interpreter in Gen. 22:18. Thus here this grace and dignity is promised to Zorobabel himself, in that he is to be assumed by the Son of God, insofar as the seed about to proceed from him is to be assumed by the Son of God. To this may be referred the exposition of Cyril, of Dorotheus in the life of Haggai in the Synopsis of Remigius, of Lyranus, and of Vatablus, when they judge that these things are promised not to Zorobabel, but to Christ according to his humanity, by which he is the seed of Zorobabel. Coccejus on this passage understands 'I will take thee' in the full sense and palpability of the thing. Who not badly compares Ps. 49:26. And the matter comes to the same thing, whether it be said that the promise was made to Zorobabel, not in himself, but in his seed Christ according to the flesh, or you say, to Christ himself, as man: yet it is more congruously said the former, because the Lord addresses Zorobabel, and treats of Zorobabel, and promises this grace to him, for the reason that he built a house for Him, as interpreted by Ecclesiasticus 49:13. (3) Worthy of note is the observation of Castrius, which he delivered here: It was once famous for God, when He wished to reward the obsequies of His servants, to promise Christ from their progeny, which they placed in the highest honor and favor for themselves: and by this hope alone they deemed themselves most happy. Hence Gen. 12:3, in order to reward Abraham because he had gone out from his land and his kindred, He promised him that Christ would be in his descendants, when He said, 'In thee shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.' And ch. 22:18, on account of the obedience of the sacrificed son, it is said to him: 'In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because thou hast obeyed my voice' of mine.' And the same promise was made to Jacob Gen. 28, 14. Also to David, that he might repay the turn, because he had sworn Psal. 131, 5. If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house, if I shall ascend into the bed of my couch, etc. The Lord swore to David the truth: of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy seat. For this very reason the ancient Fathers so greedily expected sons, lest they be deprived of so great a son, Christ. And therefore Hezekiah so anxiously lamented being deprived of life Isa. 38, 12. when he said: My life is cut off as by a weaver: whilst I was yet beginning, he cut me off. He fears, says Jerome, lest like a web he be cut off at the very beginning of light, and lest Christ in no way arise from his seed. By what reason, therefore, God promised David, because he had taken care to build a house for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob, that He would build him a house in which Christ would be King, of whose kingdom there shall be no end, Luke 1, so to Zerubbabel, because he took care to build another house for God, God promises that He will glorify him with Christ the Lord to be born from him, and with his kingdom to endure forever. And this is the cause why such a prophecy was made to Zerubbabel alone, that Christ was to be born of his posterity.

(4) In the name, therefore, of THEE, the figure must be placed, so that the name Zerubbabel may retain its proper sense; I will take thee, that is, thy seed, according to the analogy of similar Evangelical promises, such as Gen. 12, 3. in THEE, that is, in thy seed shall they be blessed; chap. 18, 18. in him (Abraham), that is, in the seed of Abraham. Thus also that 'I will set thee as a seal' Cornelius à Lapide explains with Castrius: These things befit Zerubbabel rather in person, not his own, but Christ's. For Haggai speaks of him literally, saying: In that day, namely in the time of Christ, i.e., he says from Castro: I will take thy flesh, O Zerubbabel, which I will insert like a golden signet ring into my right hand, namely my son, who is my arm, my right hand, my power and strength Isaiah 53, 1. so that by such a son born of thee thou mayest be adorned by all and glorified, nay, be exalted above all kings, and as it were deified in the human nature, which my son will assume from thy posterity, and will unite to himself and deify, and that forever, so that it may always adhere to him for all ages, like a ring to a finger. Thus, therefore, Christ shall be called here the sign, or seal of God, as man, not as God, as he assumed humanity, not Deity, from the flesh and stock of Zerubbabel, both through the communication of idioms, through which those things which are of God are attributed to man, for because the Son of God is both the seal and image of the Father Heb. 1, χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως ἀυτοῦ, therefore the man Christ is also called the seal and image of the Father; and because the incarnate Son of God is as it were an express seal; in whom we read, nay, we see expressed the love and will of God towards us John 6, 27. The Son of God, who in himself is invisible, clothed and veiled himself with flesh assumed from Zerubbabel, so that through it he himself might shine through and be translucent, just as the divine glory and majesty shine through the stars, which are as it were the signets of divine power and glory Job 9, 7. For the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only-begotten from the Father John 1, 14. Just as a seal or signet ring bears an express image, is guarded above all things and held dear, so that it is always as if in the eyes, and is like an ornament: So Christ is a seal, and a signet ring, he bears the image of God, and is guarded, and held dear above all, as the one man in grace, in whom is the εὐδοκία of God. Concerning the ornament of this seal, Castrius has it thus: Just as the hand of one having a precious ring is adorned by it, so by the flesh assumed from thy posterity, as by a ring, I shall be adorned and glorified. For if the Son of God is crowned by a crowd of believers, and the martyrs by their victories, as if by a variety of gems, distinguish for him the diadem of empire, according to that of Isaiah 62, 3. and thou shalt be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of thy God, as Jerome notes there. Whence also Paul Phil. 4, 1. called the faithful my joy and crown, why would not Christ's humanity with the best right be the crown of the Son of God, the diadem of the kingdom and the highest glory, and the precious ring by which he is adorned, although it received all its preciousness from him? Furthermore, just as a seal is applied for sealing and for impressing a figure or character: so through Christ, who is placed as a signet, the faithful are sealed, and thus the divine figure and character is impressed, so that they may have the sign of the living God Apoc. 7, 2. 1 Cor. 9, 2. just as wax bears no other figure than that of its seal, so let us bear no other likeness than that of Christ 1 Cor. 11, 1. and be transformed into the same image 2 Cor. 3, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 49. As a signet is applied for guarding pleasant and precious things: So Christ is called a signet for guarding the faithful, so that no one may snatch them away: just as formerly the Israelites were signed by circumcision, which is called the signet of faith Rom. 4, 11. and were guarded in that assembly of the people of God: so now by the character of Baptism, as by a signet of faith, and of Christ, the faithful are sealed, and guarded within the Church: and just as formerly Exod. 12, 13. with the blood of the lamb smeared on the doorposts and lintels of the children of Israel the striking Angel passed over them, and Ezech. 9, 4. no one in whom was the Tau, the sign of the living God, Apoc. 7, 3. was struck, which, as Origen says in his Homily on the Epiphany, Jerome, and Isidore, was a figure of the Lord's cross, with which those groaning and grieving were sealed on the forehead: so, sealed with the most divine sign of the cross, and smeared with the blood of the true Lamb of God, they are guarded, lest anyone dare to touch them. Whence concerning that Hebrew, whom Gregory surnamed the Great reports in book 3 of his Dialogues, chapter 7, that he had signed himself with the cross, the enemy of the cross said: woe, woe, a vessel empty, but signed. By which reasoning also the words of the bridegroom can be understood: Set me as a seal upon thy heart. That is, take care that you guard your heart, thus closed as if by a seal, and keep your arm thus safe, so that you permit no one any access to you; but keep yourself for me unharmed and untouched. Because love is so hard, and the zeal that proceeds from it, that it is like death, and it is something sinister in love to perceive anything of hell; and to permit your arm to be twisted by another rather than me, or to unlock and deliver your heart to another, while I am despised, as Castrius has it here again. Finally (that we may also add this from the same Castrius), Christ is rightly called a seal for enrolling his soldiers, and for distinguishing his servants from the triumphant enemies, from the servants of the demon, who fight under his banner. Emperors were once accustomed to bestow upon their leaders the character of their military service, inscribed with their own name, so that they might imprint it upon the soldiers whom they gathered into their camps, fixing the name of the emperor upon the hand of each: which they called the royal or imperial character. As St. Augustine reports in book 1 against Cresconius the Grammarian, chapter 30, and in his sermon on the acts with Emericus the Donatist Bishop, and Tractate 6 on John. Thus are the soldiers of Christ signed and enrolled with his character, and are known to be different from the soldiers and servants of others. There were also certain insignia hanging from the neck, such as the bulla was for the Romans, the ornament of those celebrating a triumph, which they carried before them in the triumph, with remedies enclosed within it, which they believed were most powerful against envy, according to Macrobius, lib. 1. Saturnal. cap. 6. and they were granted on shields and bucklers attached to the arms, so that one clan or family might be distinguished from another: which they had either acquired by their own prowess, or had chosen out of love for someone. Not unlike this, it is granted to Christians from the neck, may cling to the breast and adorn the seat of the heart: and the shield of faith attached to the arm, on which Christ himself is depicted as if he were a most excellent image, so that, divided from others by such a badge, and preserved like some heavenly amulet from all the snares and fascinations of enemies, we may think only of him and serve as his soldiers. And this is, set me as a seal upon your heart, like a necklace hanging from the neck upon the breast, the seat of the heart: and like a seal upon the shield of your arm. For you are the sign of those shooting, as one exclaims, the banner of those fighting, the prize of those running, the distinction of the sheep, the guard of hearts, the pattern of those working, the form and rule of servants, and the seal and character of those warring. So that upon seeing it, enemies may flee, and to the rest all may say: Behold the nation whose Lord is its God, the people whom the Lord has chosen for an inheritance for himself. Cyril handed down this meaning: Not to Zerubbabel in reality; but rather to our Lord Jesus Christ, so that in Zerubbabel, through whom these words are quite conveniently expressed, they come to pass: since he was also of the tribe of Judah, and a prince of those liberated from captivity, and as a governor of those building the house of the Lord. I will take you, therefore, he says, my servant (that is, you who appeared in the form of a servant, although by nature you are free), at that time when I shall wish to cast down dynasts or the powerful from their throne, and remove them from Principalities, I will set you as a seal. For the Son of God is the seal of the Father, containing his whole and perfect likeness, and shining in the proper beauty of the nature of the begetter. Furthermore, in him God also seals us to his own likeness: since, transformed into Christ, we acquire the image of God as it were. The Son, therefore, is the perfect seal of God and the Father, and he chose him, that is, he rendered him eligible, and chosen.

(5) And thus also the third pronoun, because I have chosen YOU, is understood by Cyril concerning the son and seed of Zerubbabel, Christ: because to choose YOU, that is, your son and seed. Concerning whom also Isa. XLII. 1. 4. My chosen one, etc. So also Cocceius: The reason is divine election and good pleasure, which includes the eternal πρόγνωσιν of Christ, as the immaculate lamb 1 Pet. I. 20. and that it pleased God that all fullness should dwell in him Col. I. 19. and our eternal predestination into sons in him Eph. I. 5. 6. The Chaldean rendered it: because in you I have been well pleased: which was the voice of God concerning Christ Matt. III. 17. (6) If that singular meaning of ASSUMPTION concerning the hypostatic assumption does not please, and the general sense of protection and custody is preferred, this promise is to be understood concerning Zerubbabel, including his posterity, concerning whom those words also, I will set you as a signet ring, can be explained, because the Lord wishes to hold him dear like one, and to guard him, and to always carry him in his eyes: but so that in the final words added as a reason, BECAUSE I HAVE CHOSEN YOU, regard may be had for that special election with which the Lord wished to honor Zerubbabel, namely, that he might assume his own flesh from his family, and the desire of all nations might come forth from his loins, for whose sake he testifies to Zerubbabel that he will shake heaven and earth again. To which the paraphrase of Castrius p. 436 tends. I will subvert the Persian monarchy, and I will crush the strength of the kingdoms of the nations subject to it.

I will also subvert the kingdom of the Greeks divided into four heads, along with their kings; and the horses of the Romans with the riders of the horses will fall pierced by the mutual swords of civil wars. And at that time, amidst so many falls of kingdoms, I will take you and your posterity to be protected under my patronage, O Zerubbabel: because as my faithful servant you have procured my worship, by building a house for me; and I will constitute you most closely joined to me, as a signet ring is accustomed to cling to someone's right hand: because I have chosen you and your posterity, that I might assume human flesh from it, and erect a spiritual kingdom that will endure forever, says the Lord of hosts, who cannot lie. Thus this epithet will be left according to Sirach chap. XLIX. 3. To Zerubbabel, that he is as it were a sign on the right hand, and just as GOD, about to testify to his supreme disgust against Jeconiah, Jerem. XXII. 24. says: Even if Jeconiah were a seal on my right hand, yet I would pluck you from there: so on the contrary here he promises concerning Zerubbabel: I will set you as a signet ring, he indicated that he himself will not only be dear to the Lord, but that he also wishes to carry him around on his fingers as if he were a most precious thing and to glorify him, and to preserve him in confusion: And nevertheless that dignity will be designated, by which Zerubbabel was chosen, so that he might be inserted into the genealogy of the Messiah, and be counted among his ancestors.

(7) To express this dignity of Zerubbabel, Gualtherus also not inappropriately employs the simile of the seal, hom. VII. in Hagg. p. 266. In that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will take you, O Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, my servant, says the Lord, and I will set you, as a ring, etc. The individual words have emphasis. For he diligently remembers Zerubbabel himself, and also touches upon the name of his father Shealtiel, so that he may show that he has known all things about him. Then he calls him his servant, and not without a great sign of love he says, my servant. Furthermore, he says, I will take you, namely into my faith and protection. He adds moreover: And I will set you as a ring, that is, you will be in the place of a signet ring to me. Others explain this concerning supreme favor and most diligent custody. (For signet rings are wont to be held in the highest esteem, and therefore to be kept more diligently, lest they either be lost or fall into the hands of impostors and fraudulent men.) While I do not altogether reject their opinion, I think that God had regard for something greater and more sublime: namely, the promise of the Messiah, to which it is certain that all the pious in former times looked. For because He was expected from the lineage of David, the descendants of David were like a seal with which God, as it were, visibly sealed His promise, since among so many upheavals and dangers and the horrible ruins of most illustrious families, He kept them safe from whom that promised Savior was to be born. In the same sense, the descendants of David are also called lamps, and God had predicted that such would be the case in Psalm 132: There I will make a horn to sprout for David, and I have prepared a lamp for My anointed. For just as a lamp is lit from a lamp, and no place is given to darkness where any lamp remains: so in the posterity of David there was a perpetual succession of heirs of the promise, which assiduously fostered the faith of the pious, until that true and eternal light JESUS CHRIST, by His coming into the world, shook off all darkness and brought salvation to desperate human affairs. Therefore GOD promises that He acknowledges Zerubbabel as a genuine son of David, and that there will never be lacking from his posterity those who give assurance to His promises. The genealogies of CHRIST JESUS, which Matthew and Luke wove together, confirm this meaning, in which that perpetual The succession of David's descendants up to CHRIST is pointed out as if by a finger. Balt. Willius made this explanation his own, and illustrated it from Zechariah on page 77. I have no doubt that something greater is signified by this phrase, and I compare it with a similar one which Zechariah uses in chapter III. 8 concerning Joshua and his companions, intending to teach that they are living testimonies of future things, especially of the Messiah, the high priest: Hear now, he says, Joshua, O high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for you are a sign. Just as Joshua is called a sign there because he acted as a living type of the Messiah, as we explained at greater length in that place, so also here in this place Zerubbabel is called a signet ring with his descendants, because these, taken all together, were seals confirming the divine promise concerning the Messiah who was to come from the seed of David, and the Israelites were made more certain daily through the sight of them concerning the truth of the divine covenant. Whence Willius observes that, besides Zerubbabel, his descendants and Christ himself are understood here, who was to arise from his loins, and thus this promise is made to Zerubbabel himself, inchoatively for his own person, but continuatively with respect to his descendants, and finally finitively for Christ himself, so that the sense is: in future times, when I shall overturn neighboring kingdoms, I will hold you, Zerubbabel, with your descendants, but especially Christ, as grateful and acceptable, and I will most carefully preserve you as a testimony of the future Messiah. Which is also in that reason which the Lord added: Because I have chosen YOU, he observes. Furthermore, the reason and impulsive cause is added to the promise, which GOD calls his election and good pleasure, by which it pleased him to choose Zerubbabel as leader and prince for the people from the family of David. Thus Psalm LXXVII. 10: He chose David his servant. This reason extends as widely as the promise itself. For the descendants of Zerubbabel will also be and will be preserved as seals for this reason, because GOD chose the posterity of David above others, so that the Messiah might arise from it. Also, it pleased GOD in Christ for this reason, because he is his chosen servant, who ought to bring the light of life and salvation to the Gentiles and nations, Isaiah XLII. 1. This is Willius. Which, however, cannot be approved in every respect. For how is this signet referred to Christ himself, if that explanation of Walther is accepted, that Zerubbabel with his descendants was like a seal by which God as it were visibly designated his promise concerning the Messiah; is the Messiah the seal of the promise concerning the Messiah, is Christ a testimony of the future Messiah? What has that election to do with Christ, by which Zerubbabel was held worthy to be placed in that genealogy of Christ and among his ancestors; was Christ himself chosen for that with Zerubbabel and his grandsons? And therefore Christ is indeed included in this prophecy as the primary scope, but he is not comprehended in the subject to which the predicates of taking, of the seal, and of election belong, according to Gualther's exposition.

(8) And thus also our blessed Winckelmann

expounds concerning Zerubbabel with his successors, yet without neglecting Christ. I WILL TAKE YOU) A very consolatory promise for Zerubbabel and his successors, by which he promises that he will undertake the singular care and custody of him as his faithful servant, no differently than if someone does not neglect a signet ring, but guards it most diligently. This promise shows that Zerubbabel was dear to GOD, even because of Christ who was to descend from him, who lies hidden in this ring like a most precious gem, just as Matthew places Zerubbabel in the genealogy of Christ. Which things are also repeated and approved by blessed Himmel. Nor do the Jews deny that Christ is insinuated in this prophecy: indeed R. Abarbanel, as Cocceius notes, makes this the sense of this passage: that God would indeed not give the kingdom to Zerubbabel under the second house, and that it would not stand either, but nevertheless that the Messiah would one day be raised up as King in the congregation of the people from his seed, and he proves from the ancients that the Messiah is designated here. Wherefore, since both the ancient Doctors of the Church, Dorotheus, Cyril, and others, and among the more recent interpreters, the Papists, the Reformed, most of our own, and also some of the Jewish Rabbis acknowledge that this promise made to Zerubbabel looks to the head of all promises, concerning the coming Messiah (even if they do not all show Christ in the same way), there is no reason why we should rise up with Grotius to the glosses of other Jews who eliminate Christ from this oracle and stop at the person of Zerubbabel. For not only was Judea to be kept safe by this Prince, but the scepter and the lawgiver had to be preserved in it until the advent of the Messiah: nor did he himself have it as his sole or primary wish that Judea should be harassed by no one in his time, but Zerubbabel, like other pious Kings, Leaders, and Prophets, panted for and desired the Messiah, to whom nothing could be announced and promised more pleasing, nothing more honorable, than that the Lord wishes to count him among the ancestors of the Messiah, and to raise up the Messiah from his lineage. And that phrase, BECAUSE I HAVE CHOSEN YOU, is to be understood in an eminent sense, concerning the primary peak and summit of dignity and honor to which Zerubbabel was chosen by the Lord. But without doubt, the primary thing is that he was chosen to be placed in the catalog of the ancestors of the Messiah: than which axiom the holy Patriarchs, Kings, and Leaders under the Old Testament had nothing earlier, nothing more ancient. And these things also concerning that oracle. Let us now sigh with the mystical Bride (Cant. VIII. 6) to Christ, the Bridegroom of our soul: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm. Let the desire of all nations answer the faithful soul: I will set you as a seal: because I have chosen you.

Amen, Lord JESUS, Amen. To you be praise, honor, and glory forever, Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ASSUMAM TE ZOROBABEL FILI SA- LATHIEL SERVE MEUS, DICIT DOMINUS, ET PONAM TE QUASI SIGNACULUM] A tantis moti- bus totius prope orbis concussis efficiam, ut Judæa te principe tuta sit, & à nemine infestetur. Annulum signa- torium solemus bene custodire. Vide Cant. IIX, 6. & quæ dicta ad Jerem. XXII, 24.

QUIA TE ELEGI] Id est, quia te amo: σὲ ἠρίτησα, LXX. quod idem valet ac si diceres, ἐν σοὶ ἐυδόκησα: qua locutione hic utitur Chaldæus. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. III, 17.

De Zorobabele solo etiam exposuit Theodoretius (etsi subversionem Gog & Magog ipse indicari ve- lit,) ut & imprimis Ebræi apud Lyranum & Vata- blum, qui destructionem Persarum hic promitti censent. Alii vero de Christo hanc prophetiam ac- cipiunt, qui notetur nomine Zorobabelis ea lo- quendi formula, qua solent nomina Patrum in S. literis instar Patronymicorum pro posteris accipi, ut Salomon pro Salomonide Psal. LXXII, 1. David pro Davidide Ezech. XXXIV. 23. Hos. III. 5. ut ita Zo- robabel dicatur pro Zorobabelide: ac de Christi qui- dem adventu posteriori explicant Ambrosius lib. III. Epist. XII. Hieronymus, Haymo, & Hugo, cum sub- versis omnibus regnis, attritisque gentibus, post cœ- li & terræ commotionem omnia pedibus Christi sub- jecta erunt, quem Pater constituit ceu signaculum, ad cujus imaginem omnes electi conformentur.

De priori vero adventu intelligunt Dionysius, & Va- tablus, quando cœlum & terra commota sunt, & subversa alia regna, ac Romano subjecta, & Deus assumsit carnem ex Zorobabele: ut Cyrillus Alex. in h. l. p. 650. Qui destructionem potestatum & virtutum malignarum & contrariarum designari vult, quas Salvator in cruce sua triumphavit. Atque ita Coccejus in h.l. de Christo interpretatur, & quem- admodum alias Christus David dicitur, tum quia ex semine Davidis est, tum quia David typus Chri- sti fuit, sic etiam Zorobabelem ipsum hic vocari putat, tum quia Christus est semen Sorobabelis, tum quia Sorobabel in reductione ex captivitate, & in ædificatione templi est typus Christi, qui ser- vus Dei dicitur in emphasι, quia legem implevit ad præstandum δικαίωμα etiam peccatoribus: hoc modo exponens: Interim dum evertam thronos, assumam te, & demonstrabo te eum esse, in quo dele- ctor, omnibusq́; suis notis, post servitutem obitam, in- signiam, & tandem, quum abolebo cœlum & terram, Te ponam ut sigillum, sive annulum signatorium, h. e. glorificabor in te & Ecclesia. Regna movebuntur, sed ut novum regnum oriatur. Cœlum & terra præ- teribit, sed ut regnum gloriæ manifestetur, & maneat in perpetuum. Quam interpretationem simpliciter approbare non possumus: tum quia nimis mani- festum, hæc de illo Zorobabele intelligenda esse, ad quem missus erat Propheta: Loquere ad Zorobabe- lem Ducem Iudæ, dicens: Ego movebo &c. In illa die, dicit Dominus exercituum, assumam TE Zoro- babel fili Salathiel, serve meus. Nimirum illum Zo- robabelem ceu servum suum se assumturum pro- mittit Dominus, ad quem tum loqui debebat Pro- pheta: Unde recte Castrius, cur in tam paucis ver- bis nominis Zorobabelis, filii Salathielis significatio mutanda est? ut cum mittatur Propheta ad Zorobabe- lem filium Salathielis, statim se inveniat loquentem cum Zorobabeli de Christo: tum quia promissio hæc facta est Zorobabeli, ut excitaretur & confirmare- tur in instituto opere exstructionis domus Domini, siquidem ipse ut servus Domini procuravit fideli- ter cultum divinum. Quapropter nullum dubium est, ipsummet Zorobabelem hic compellari: tum quia de illo Zorobabele explicatur hic textus à Si- racide, qui cum Josua sacerdote domum Domini ædificavit c. XLIX. 3. Quomodo amplificemus Zoroba- bel? Nam & ipse quasi signum (σφραγὶς) signaculum in dextra mea. Unde nostrates pleriq; ὁμοθυμαδὸν hæc verba de illo Zorobabele κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν intelli- gunt. Solus propemodum D. Pappus de Christo ejusque fructibus exposuit. Addit quidem etiam B. Tarnovius, addunt Paraphrastæ Vinarienses sensum de Christo, sed eum mysticum esse ajunt, literalem vero de Zorobabele non excludunt, quod etiam observare licet in Paraph. Belg. annotatis in h. l. Quomodo autem idem nomen, in eodem comma- te semel positum, & Zorobabelem & filium Zoro- babelis significare, ac prædicata, verbaque omnia & singula duplicem sensum simul sustinere possint, nullatenus apparet. Et urget B. Tarnovius ipse hoc axioma alias in Commentario ad hunc Prophe- tam, non posse unius vocis aut dicti geminum statui sensum. Absurdus vero hic Paræus est in Com- ment. ad h. l. qui agnoscit sermonem directum esse ad Zorobabelem & de illo intelligi debere, postea ta- men eundem explicat simul de posteris ejus Duci- bus populi Iudaici, ac populo ipso, denique exponit etiam de Ecclesia, & de Christo, ut per Zorobabelem Christus intelligatur, quia significabat Christum. Ita non duo solum sed tres vel plures sensus, iidem- que literales statuendi erunt ejusdem oraculi. Re- ctius hic sapit Balth. Willius in Comment. pag. 75.

Objectum promissionis Zerubbabel est, quem DEUS cum ratione majorum, tum ratione officii sibi charissi- mum esse ostendit. Hoc, dum illum servum suum a- mica compellatione nominat, quomodo Zerubbabeli fi- dem & industriam ac zelum in commisso regimine po- puli tribuit, de se vero agnitionem fidei & amorem predicat. Illud, dum Sealthielis meminit, qui fuit avus Zerubbabelis ut cap. 1. vers. 1. ostensum, filius vero Neri ex Nathanis familia oriundi successor juris & dignitatis regiæ, quam Jechonias nepos Josiæ de- sertam & orphanam reliquerat. Hoc enim pacto o- stendit, se promissionum Davidi factarum meminif- se, atq; propterea ipsum etiam gratum habiturum & stabiliturum, juxta Pf. CXXXII. 11. 12. Juravit Do- minus Davidi veritatem, à qua non avertit se: De fructu ventris ponam in folio tuo. Et hæ duæ compel- lationes etiam solitariæ Zerubbabelem satis animare potuissent. Quamvis idem Willius adjiciat: Por- ro sub Zerubbabele omnes simul ejus posteri, & ipse etiam Christus, qui in lumbis ejus latebat, intelligitur, ut statim videbitur. Quæ ἀσύςατα esse jam mo- nuimus, nisi ita explicentur, ut geminus sensus e- vitetur.

Cæterum, quod probe observandum, distincta in hoc oraculo habentur. Primum repetitur vatici- nium de commotione cæli & terræ, quod mense se- ptimo Propheta Zorobabeli & populo proposue- rat, ac non tantum majoris βεβαιώσεως causa ite- rum Zorobabeli ceu Principi hæc promissio fit, ut nempe illam commotionem, qua desiderium gen- tium exhibebitur, & gloriam suam explicabit, eaq; templum, quod extrui cœperat, illustrabit, certo certius sequuturam consideret: sed etiam ob illam peculiarem rationem, quæ personam Zorobabe- lis sigillatim attinebat, non vero reliquum popu- lum, quod illa commotione gloria ipsius Zoroba- belis illustrior reddenda sit: Siquidem ipse Dux fuerit è stirpe Regia Davidica, è qua proditurus e- rat Messias, gentium desiderium. Eundem ergo Deus elegerat, ut ex semine ejus nasceretur Messias, quod ea repetitione innuitur. Quapropter non alia commotio est cœli & terræ à Propheta hic designa- ta, quam ea, quæ antea v. 6. prolixius exposita fuit: nec restringenda hæc commotio ad subversionem regnorum, quam subjungit Propheta, neq; confun- denda hæc subversio regnorum cum illa commo- tione: nam subversio regnorum commotionem quidem parit, sed in terra: Deus autem cælum pari- ter & terram se commoturum dicit. Coccejus duo- bus modis intelligi posse hanc commotionem vult, proprie nempe de abolitione aspectabilis formæ hujus mundi, & improprie de abolitione formæ ex- ternæ Ecclesiæ, & utramque debere sub his verbis intelligi ait. Sed fateor, me non capere, quid velit. Et quomodo hæc eadem verba tum proprie tum improprie intelligere simul necessum erit? Rectius Calvinus: Propheta affirmat hic instare admirabi- le opus Dei, quod cœlum & terram concutiet. Id ergo necessario ad Christum debet referri, quia fuit quasi nova mundi creatio, ubi collegit Christus quæ dissipata erant in cœlo & terra, quemadmo- dum Apostolus dicit 1. Coloss. c. dum homines Deo & Angelis reconciliavit, dum victo diabolo resti- tuit mortuis vitam, dum illuxit cum sua justitia, tunc vere Deus concussit cœlum & terram, & ad- huc hodie concutit, dum prædicatur Evangelium: quia filios Adæ ad imaginem suam reformat. Hæc igitur regeneratio spiritualis tale est documentum potentiæ gratiæ Dei, quod merito tremefaciat cœ- lum & terram. Hæc Calvinus. Id ergo manifestum satis existimamus, hanc commotionem cœli & ter- ræ eandem esse, quam supra commemorarat Pro- pheta. Non enim aliam atque aliam commotio- nem futuram, jam antea protestatus erat: ADHUC SEMEL movebo cœlum & terram, quam vocem ἔτι ἅπαξ stricte retinendam & observandam esse, id- eoque aliam commotionem cœli & terræ, ante no- vissimam mundi συντέλειαν locum non habe- re, è phrasi prophetica, & interpretatione ipsius Spir. S. in N. T. facta indubitato habemus. Qua- propter recte, quantum ad hanc commotionem se habet Cyrilli Commentarius: Et sapientissimus quidem Paulus propositorum verborum sententiæ ad- stipulans illud (Commotum iri) significare ait fu- turam mobilium translationem, ut maneant ea, quæ sunt immobilia.) Facta autem sunt nova, quæ per ipsum facta sunt, nempe stabilia, firma & manentia. Animadverte igitur sermonis œconomiam. Cum enim admirabilem frugum abundantiam ipsis spopondisset, omniaque plena manu præbiturum dixisset, quæ ad animum hilarandum & delicias pertinerent, verita- tis tempus fructuosum, spiritualis nimirum & super- næ benedictionis copiosam largitionem mox subjecit. Commovi enim terram, inquit, quando Israe- lem eduxi de terra Ægypti: tamen commovebo iterum, hoc est, iterum insignem & celebrem u- niversis mortalibus faciam, tantum non omnia commovens. Consonat Rudolph. Gualtherus hom. VII. in Hagg. pag. 265. Repetit, quod tertio sermone dixerat: Ego concutio cœlos & terram: & ita in mentem revocat promissionem de adventu Messiæ, in quo omnes aliæ promissiones ratæ sunt. Perinde etiam est, ac si diceret: Non terreant te ô Zorobabel, quæcunque posthac fieri videbis. Quod enim olim patribus promisi, & nuper quo- que repetii, firmum ratumque erit. Et ubi tem- pus illud præfinitum advenerit, nihil obstare po- terit, quo minus veniat Messias, & meam domum, Ecclesiam nimirum, promissa gloria illustret. Nam cœlos simul & terram concutiam, & potius solidis- simæ mundi partes loco movebuntur, quam ut huic decreto meo aliquid patiar derogari. Ut vero sub Messiæ adventum orbis totus concussus sit, nuper diximus. Non ergo probanda glossa Grotii jejuna nimis: Ego movebo cœlum & terram: res magnas efficiam excitatis in cœlo tempestatibus & terra bellis. Longe aliter hæc accepisse Aposto- lum, antea monuimus.

Quod autem porro ad regnorum subversionem, de qua vaticinatur Propheta, eam non solum Grotius, sed etiam alii restringunt ad Persarum regna, sub quorum Monarchia floruit Zorobabel, Ebrai potis- simum, quorum sensum hunc è Lyrano & Vatablo tradit Castrius: Subvertam regnum Persarum, quos tu formidas, cum cæteris gentium regnis Persico subjectis, & inter tot bella & pericula ego te servabo ô Zorobabel, & præ oculis tanquam annulum habebo. Alii regnorum etiam aliorum subversionem hic præ- dictam censent, & distinctim ista explicant: quæ in vers. 22. habentur: Ita Castrius: Subvertam solium regnorum Persici Imperii, quod tu formidas, & conteram fortitudinem regnorum gentium Persis sub- jectorum, & subvertam regnum Græcorum in qua- tuor capita distributum, cum eorum Regibus, & tan- dem Romanum Imperium interibit: equi & equites eorum mutuis gladiis, & bellis civilibus confossi cadent: & inter hos tot casus, & tot discrimina re- rum, & tam diversas regnorum mutationes, Ego sub mea cura te assumam custodiendum, ô Zoro- babel fili Salathielis, quod curaveris cultum meum domum mihi ædificando, uti servus meus. Hæc ille. Coccejus quartum colon de equis & sessoribus APOCALYPTICUM esse putat. Cu- jus sententiam plane singularem adscribemus:

Tentemus, inquit, annon hunc versum secundum co- la sic intelligere possimus, ut in eo habeamus distin- ctam repræsentationem imperiorum mundi, quæ Christi regno cessura sint, uti in aliis Prophetiis exhi- bentur. Imperium, quod tunc erat, Persicum merito in primo colo intelligimus, quod sub titulo Throni re- gnorum recte proponitur. Erat enim Rex Persarum rex regum ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας : qui sub imperio suo habebat centum viginti septem provincias, quem et- iam Græci comiter eo tempore reverebantur : ad quos belli pacisq́ libratorem agebat. Sub titulo vis regnorum gentium, Græcorum imperium in plura re- gna divisum, è quibus quatuor designat Scriptura Da- niel. IIX. & duo describit Daniel. IX. nimirum Se- leucidarum & Lagidarum, magna violentia omnia administrans, commode intelligi potest. Sub nomine Quadrigæ & vectorum, Romanum Imperium opti- me intelligitur. Per quod profligata est vis regnorum gentium. Est enim systema unius Imperii gubernati a multis, videlicet Senatu Romano, aurigis consuli- bus, vel etiam principe, triumphalis currus instar tracti & provecti multis legionibus & populis tanquam equis in parte Asiæ, & Africæ, in Græcia & Occiden- talioribus, Europa, Italia, annexisq́ partibus. Hoc imperium sub nomine Regis post Seleucidas & Lagidas indigitat Daniel c. XI. 36. De quadrigis plura apud Zachariam sunt cap. VI. Sequuntur Equi & Sesso- res cadentes gladiis fraternis. Hic intelliguntur regna illa, quæ ex divisione Imperii Romani, quasi à curru illo triumphali abjuncti equi, extiterunt, quæ decem memorantur, certo tempore cum bestia habi- tura potestatem, ab Apocalypsi, una cum aliis regnis particularibus per totum mundum sparsis, quorum exitus est mutuo se atterere & humiliare. Sed hy- pothesis Cocceji de commotione cœli & terræ novis- sima, quam supponit, mere precaria est. Imo commotionem eam, quæ sub adventum Christi primum futura erat, intelligi, credendum est. Id- eo præferenda Castrii explicatio.

Non exhaurit autem sensum Prophetæ glos- sa Grotiana. Nam non tantum de Imperio Persa- rum in Ægypto evertendo dicit Propheta: Sed sim- pliciter: Subvertam, inquit, SOLIUM REGNO- RUM, adeoque totius Monarchiæ Persicæ eversio- nem designat. Neque tantum de cladibus Darii Hy- staspis, quas à Græcis accepturus erat. Sed de conte- renda potentia universi regni gentium vaticinatur. Et majores fuere clades, quas in Græcia Xerxes cum exercitu decies centenorum millium præliis terrestribus, tum ad Thermopylas, duce Leonida Spartano, tum ad Platæos, nec non totidem navali- bus ad Artemifium & Salamonium victus perpes- sus est. Neque hic fratres vocari Persas, Ægyptios, Jonas, Græcos, ideo, quod omnes πολύθεοι, verisi- mile est. Sic enim omnes gentes fratres fuissent. Contorta ergo omnia sunt, cum hæc ad Darii tem- pora trahere conatur Grotius. At si ea porrigunt sese ad Romanum usque imperium, quomodo, ob- secro, in Zorobabele adimpleta, qui longe ab Alex- andri temporibus præfuit? Resp. (1) Verba, in die illa, non præcise diem certum designant, sed tra- ctum temporis, intra quem Zorobabel in cura & custodia divina securus & tutus mansurus sit in- ter medios motus & tumultus. Porro etiamsi as- sumtio illa Zorobabelis, ipsum Zorobabelem con- cernere dicatur: solum tamen ipsum, aut qua spe- ctatur unica ejus persona, attinere credenda non est. Solum alloquitur Dominus, eidem etiam pro- mittit assumtionis gratiam, sed pro se & posteritate ejus. Quo pacto commode explicandæ sunt alio- rum Interpp. expositiones, ne διττότης sensus vo- cum, aut commatis ejusdem inferatur. Nimirum non existimandum, Zorobabelem intelligi & proprie Zorobabelem illum antiquum Ducem populi, & improprie & figurate Christum ceu antitypum. Sic enim ejusdem vocis geminus constituitur sensus: multo minus dicendum, per Zorobabelem, & per- sonam Ducis, & populum ejus, & Christum semen ejus significari, ut trinus ejusdem vocis sensus emergat. Quid ergo?
