Lauda & lætare, Filia Sion! Voce jubili & lætitiæ omnis comprehenditur fructus nativitatis Dominicæ. Quia ipsa æterna beatitudo quid erit aliud, quam æternum gaudium, æterna celebratio? Ademta erat omnis jubilatio, omnis lætitia uni- verso humano generi: squalebant omnia luctu & æterna tristitia. Peccatum, quod commissum erat, nullam admittebat lætitiam, æternam secum trahe- bat tristitiam. Prævaluerat hostis infernalis, & eo abripuerat nos, ubi erat fletus & stridor dentium. Sed nunc mutantur vices rerum: Facessat tristitia, laudet & lætetur filia Sion, perenni lætitia. In ad- ventu Dominico solutus est omnis paternæ præva- ricationis metus, quem Diaboli dudum fraudibus incurrit circumventa mortalitas. Adest enim no- bis hodie cœli terræque judex, qui rescisso Chiro- grapho delictorum reatum nostrum miseratus ab- solvit. Adest ille Dominus, qui jugum captivitatis antiquæ à nostris cervicibus solvens, mœrorem mundi æterna libertate lætificet. Adest rex ille mansuetus, qui per spacia totius orbis cœlestis ju- stitiæ gressibus incedens, superbientem furentis inimici conterat tyrannidem. Atque hoc est gau- dium, quod Filiæ Sion obtingit, quo omnes fide- les fruuntur læti per Nativitatem Domini, imo, quod universo populo in hac solemnitate Geneth- liaca cœlestis prædicavit nuncius: Ecce Evangeli- zo vobis gaudium magnum, quod erit omni popu- lo; quia natus est vobis hodie Salvator. In hoc na- tali lumen additum mundo est, & immortalitas, quæ per peccatum perierat, mortalibus reddita est. Exultemus ergo, præeunte Leone M. in Domino, & spirituali jucunditate lætemur: quia illuxit no- bis dies redemtionis novæ, reparationis antiquæ, felicitatis æternæ. Exulta filia Sion: jubila filia Je- rusalam: Ecce Rex tuus venit tibi justus & Salva- tor, monuit Zacharias, Propheta suavissimus. Gau- dete in Domino semper, & iterum dico, gaudete; Dominus prope est, exclamavit Apostolorum co- ryphæus. In dulci jubilo, nun singet und seid froh, accinit nunc Ecclesia, & totus sanctorum chorus. Resonet in laudibus, cum jucundis plau- sibus, Sion cum fidelibus: Apparuit, quem genuit Maria. Hodie super terram canunt Angeli, lætan- tur Archangeli, Deus ipse exultat: Solus Diabolus & omnia cum eo Dæmonia contremiscunt, quia restauratur genus humanum per interitum Diabo- li. Causam lætitiæ adducit ipse Dominus: quia Ec- ce, Ego venio. Adventus filii Dei fons & scaturi- go est omnis nostræ lætitiæ. Qui hic loquitur, alius non est, quam ipse Dei Filius; Jehovah, qui se mis- sum dicit à Jehovah, ut cognoscas, inquiens, quod me ad te miserit Jehovah Zebaoth: idemque voca- tur à Propheta Angelus Domini. Quis vero est mis- sus à Domino, & Angelus Domini, nisi angelus il- le fœderis, Angelus magni Consilii, Angelus fa- ciei Domini, Filius Dei? Hic se venturum promis sit, & sub VENTURI nomine promissus, & cele- bratus passim est. Neque alteri magis propria est o- ratio, qua hæc persona, quæ hic loquitur, utitur, quam ipsimet Filio Dei: Ecce venio & habitabo in medio tui, & applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Do- minum in die illo, & erunt mihi in populum. Ea si- bi vendicat, quæ non nisi uni Deo conveniunt: quod gentes convertat & colligat sibi in populum, Judam habeat partem hæreditariam, hostes repri- mat, & præsentia sua omnibus lætitiam afferata Habemus ergo luculentum testimonium, quod nos visitavit JEHOVAH ipse, unus ille & verus Deus, extra quem non est alius. Natus est vobis hodie Salvator, qui est Christus Dominus, inquit Angelus. Christus ex Patribus est secundum car- nem, idemque Deus est benedictus in secula super omnia, testatur Apostolus. Atque hoc est stupen- dum illud, & citra controversiam magnum pietatis mysterium, quod Deus manifestatus est in carne: de quo merito exclamavit S. Augustinus: O mira & inexquisita compago, ô nova & inaudita commi- xtio! Deus, qui est, & qui erat, creator sit creatura.

Qui immensus capitur, divites constituens pauper efficitur, incorporeus carne vestitur: Sermo crasse- scit, videtur invisibilis, palpatur impalpabilis, comprehenditur incomprehensibilis. Quem cœ- lum & terra benedicit, in præsepio angusto col- locatur. Numeratur in sæculo, qui est ante secula. Hic fundus est, & fons æternæ nostræ beatitudi- nis, quam nemo reparare nobis poterat, nisi æter- nus Deus. Neque enim alterius officium erat, ut Athanasius monet de incarn. Verbi Dei, corrupti- bile in incorruptibilitatem transmutare, nisi ipsius Salvatoris, qui in principio omnia è nihilo condi- derat, neque alterius opus fuit, exemplar imaginis divinæ hominibus restituere, nisi ejus, qui imago erat Patris: neque alterius, ex morte immortale suscitare, nisi ejus, qui ipsissima vita est. Decebat eum, per quem omnia, ex quo omnia, multos filios in gloriam adducentem, cum princeps auctorque salutis eorum esset, passionibus consummari, ait Apostolus Ebr. II. 10. Quæ verba, interprete eo- dem Magno Athanasio, hoc sibi volunt: Non alte- rius fuisse, à corruptione, quæ jam incubuerat, ho- mines recipere, nisi Dei Verbi, quod eos ab initio condiderat. Quod denique ad formam & modum incarnationis Filii Dei, insinuatur ea adventus & inhabitationis nomine. Non enim adventus & in- habitatio sanctificationis, aut glorificationis, sed adventus apparitionis vel manifestationis, in as- sumta carne, & inhabitatio in templo personali corporis Dominici indicatur, quam ἐπιφάνειαν ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ ἔνσαρκον ἐπιδημίαν Veteres appellant. Ecce venio, inquit Dominus; qua voce adventus incarnationis exprimi consuevit. Ecce venio, in volumine libri scriptum est de me, Ps. XL. 8. Ecce, Deus vester veniet Es. XXXV. 4. Ecce Dominus ve- nit & merces ejus cum eo. Es. XL. 10. Dicite Filiæ Sion, Ecce Salus tua venit, Ecce merces ejus cum eo Es. LXII. 11. Ecce Rex tuus venit tibi, Zach. IX. 9. Et mox veniet ad templum suum Dominus, quem quæritis Mal. III. 1. Ideo quærebat Johannes per Legatos suos. Tunc ille es, qui VENTURUS est? Matth. XI. 3. Qualis hic adventus sit, exponat nobis S. Athanasius: Incorporalis ille & incorru- ptibilis λόγος Dei ad regionem nostram accessit, non quidem antea inde longinquus, (nihil quippe ab eo vacuum relinquitur in rebus creatis, cum omnia omnino impleverit præsens cum suo Patre in omnibus) sed eatenus accessit, quatenus scil. sua Φιλανθρωπίᾳ & ἐπιφανείᾳ ad nos se demisit, & corpus sibi sumsit, idque non alienum à nostro corpore. Neque enim simpliciter voluit in corpo- re consistere, aut nudam sui præsentiam exhibere, quippe penes quem erat, si ita placuisset, tantum sese oculis exponere, & per aliud quippiam, quod præstantius esset, divinum suum adventum osten- dere: Sed nostrum assumsit corpus, quod mori posset: ut illud Verbi, quod super omnia est, par- ticeps factum, pro omnibus morti ad plenam sa- tisfactionem sufficeret, & tamen ob Verbum in- habitans incorruptibile perseveraret. Quod idem Sanctus Pater alibi, oratione nempe contra Sabel- lii gregales, ita declarat: Cum igitur Majestas & magnificentia in Deo super-cœleste quoddam no- minetur, id quod huic contrarium est, humile ter- rene dicatur, & in terris versari, facillime compe- ris, descensum Verbi inclinationem esse ex incor- porali majestate ad vilitatem corporis, cum se- ipsum dederit incorporalem speciem, humani ge- neris amore, & salutari universorum providentia, ideoque missus comperietur, quoniam ineffabili Patris incorporei voluntate corpori seipsum tra- diderit. Descensus item humanæ speciei ἐπαμφία- c

σις superinductio, atque investitio est, secundum Patris voluntatem instituta. Nec minus congruit inhabitationis nomen exprimendæ incarnationi. Chaldæus hic reddidit: Ponam divinitatem meam, vel habitationem meam in medio tui: LXX. In- terpp. κατασκηνώσω ἐν μέσῳ σꝫ. Qua voce S. Jo- hannes adventum incarnationis descripsit c. I. 14. ὁ λόγος σάρξ ἐγένετο, καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν. Et ver- bum Caro factum est, & habitavit in nobis, quem- admodum interpretatur Epiphanius lib. II. T. I. hæres. LI. ἄνθρωπος γέγονε, homo factus est: quia scenam eandem, per incarnationem, nobiscum inhabitare cœpit. Hæc enim κατασκήνωσις & inha- bitatio monstrat humanam naturam, in qua æter- nus Dei Filius & personaliter inhabitavit ipse, tan- quam in proprio templo cum omni sua plenitudi- ne, teste Apostolo Col. II. 9. & per quam conver- satus est, & quasi tabernaculum suum fixit in me- dio populi sui. Quæ explicatio etiam Cyrillo sese probavit lib. I. in Joh. Cum dixerit, carnem factum esse Dei verbum, ne quis propria ipsum natura ex- cidisse stultissime suspicaretur, & in carnem vere transmutatum esse, recte utique Theologus statim infert, & habitavit in nobis, ut cum duo necessario intelligas, & eum, qui habitat, & id, in quo habita- tur, in carnem ipsum non esse transmutatum, exi- stimes, sed habitare potius in carne, ut proprio utentem corpore, templo, quod est ex sancta vir- gine. Consonat Chrysostomus: Semper habitat hoc tabernaculum. Carnem enim nostram tan- quam non depositurus, sed ut semper secum habi- turus, induit. Atque ita etiam explicat Ephræm Patriarcha Theopolitanus apud Photium Biblioth. Cod. CCXXIIX. p. 806. τὴν εἰς μίαν ὑπόςασιν σύνο- δον καὶ τὸ ἀμετάβλητον τῆς ἑκατέρας φύσεως de- signari docens: Ita quoq; explicare cum Cyrillo & Chrysostomo, Athanasium & Gregorium Theo- logum, observat. Neque dubium videtur, hinc pe- titum esse illud, quod cum Theodor. ἀτρέπτῳ inculcat Euthymius & Theophylactus: aliud esse tabernaculum, aliud, qui habitat in eo. Nec à Scri- pturæ phrasi aut Græcis scriptoribus aliena est hæc ἐξήγησις: Corpus enim σκῆνος dicitur Apostolo 2. Cor. V. & Hesychius notat, σκῆνος σῶμα esse, ut τὸ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν nihil aliud sit, quam σκῆνος ἀνέλαβεν ἐν ἡμῖν corpus assumsit in nobis, sive inter nos, vel in nobis, in homine & ex homine, uti ha- bet Heinsius ad h. l. Quæ illustriora erunt, si con- feratur typus corporis Christi, tabernaculum Mo- saicum, de quo Apostolus Ebr. IX. Neque con- temnenda tamen observatio Cyrilli, exprimi hac phrasi loquendi simul insignem incarnationis fru- ctum, inhabitationem nostri gratiosam. Quin & in nobis habitasse verbum utiliter asserit, altissi- mum quoque nobis istud revelans mysterium. Su- mus enim omnes in Christo, & communis huma- nitatis persona in ipsum reviviscit. In omnibus ita- que Verbum habitavit per unum, ut uno constitu- to Dei Filio in virtute secundum spiritum sancti- tatis in universam humanitatem dignitas illa re- dundaret, adeoque per unum ex nobis in nos quo- que perveniret. Atque iterum: Habitat autem Ver- bum in omnibus, in uno templo, scilicet, quod propter nos & ex nobis assumsit, ut omnes in se- ipso habens, omnes in uno corpore, sicuti Paulus ait, reconciliaret Patri. Sed hæc persequi, uti par erat, non licet. Fideles primos tempore Christi ex- citari à Propheta, ut jubilent, Deoque gratias a- gant, eo quod videant Messiam Deum corpora- tum visibiliter in medio sui versantem, ibique fun- dantem Ecclesiam, ad quam mox per Apostolos congregaturus sit omnes gentes, agnoscit Corne- sius à Lapide, eumque sensum Hieronymi, Theo- doreti, Remigii, Lyrani, Vatabli, Ariæ & aliorum esse fatetur, quamvis mysticum solum, præter isto- rum Autorum mentem, dicat. Addatur Eusebius II. Dem. Evang. 18. Albertus M. Haymo, Hugo, Dionysius, quamvis nonnulli ex his cœtum Ju- dæorum, è captivitate redeuntium,compellari ve- lint, ut lætentur, in Patria sua, quod habituri sint tandem Dei Filium ex se, carnem indutum, & in medio eorum habitaturum. Quæ saniora sunt iis, quæ Cornelius, Joh. de Rayroles, Christoph. à Ca- stro, aliique Papistæ habent.Superest, ut κέλευσμα Propheticum etiam inter nos resonet: Sileat omnis caro à facie Domini, quia consurrexit de habita- culo sancto suo. Sileant, & conticescant omnes tu- multus reproborum : Adest princeps pacis,defen- surus Ecclesiam. Sileat universa caro: quia judex omnis carnis, in carne apparet. Silentium ergo re- quiritur attentionis,ut mysteria incarnationis de- vote percipiamus, silentium fidei & submissionis, ut cognita reverenter suscipiamus, non rationis decempeda discutiamus, silentium pietatis, & ti- moris,ut τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ Domini digne,hoc est, pie, juste, & sobrie vivamus:silentium patientiæ,& per- severantis expectationis, ut in spe & silentio forti- ter agamus. Cesset omnis solicitudo, Christus no- bis vera securitas advenit. Cessent bella, desinant lites, hodie pax vera de cœlo descendit. Cesset omnis amaritudo, hodie per totum mundum mel- liflui facti sunt cœli; esset omnis impuritas, omnis injustitia, omnis invidia; hodie Sanctus Sancto- rum,qui est justitia nostra, & charitas ipsa in lu- cem editus est. Canat mens nostra, lingua nostra, vita nostra, quotquot ἰσάγγελοι esse cupimus, cum exercitu angelico : Gloria in excelsis Deo,in terris pax, hominibus bona voluntas. Ne ergo desera- mus cœtus sacros:sed ædificemus non invicem mu- tuis cohortationibus, sanctisque exemplis : illis denique,qui vice Dei legatione ad nos funguntur, ad aram Domini gratitudinem frequentes teste- mur. P. P. Witebergæ profesto Nativitatis Do- mini. Anno cIɔ Iɔc LIIX.

INCREPET DOMINVS IN TE SATAN) ἐπιτιμή- σαι κύριος ἐν σοι, LXX. hic, pro quo ἐπιτιμήσει σοι, Judas. Sensus est, coërceat te, ne huic viro satis dura passo ampliùs noceas.

NVMQVID NON ISTE TORRIS EST ERVTVS DE IGNE?) Nonnè ex gravibus periculis eum servavit Deus? Fabulantur Judæi Jesum hunc à Chaldæis in ignem fuisse conjectum, postulantibus id Pseudo-Prophetis Acha- bo, & Sedecia, quorum mentio Jer. XXIX. 21. ipsum au- tem ex igne servatum, vestibus tantum adultis.

## 3:1
Ver. 1.

STANDING BEFORE THE ANGEL OF THE LORD) Michael, who opposes himself to Satan, as we see Jud. 9. where he has the same words which follow here, ἐπιτιμήσαι σε κύριος.

AND SATAN STOOD AT HIS RIGHT HAND, TO RESIST HIM) In the tribunals the right side was that of the accuser.

Latin:

Vers. 1.

STANTEM CORAM ANGELO DOMINI) Michae- le, qui Satanæ se opponit, ut videmus Jud. 9. ubi eadem verba habet,quæ hic sequuntur, ἐπιτιμήσαι σε κύριος.

ET SATAN STABAT A DEXTRIS EJVS, UT ADVERSARETUR EI) In tribunalibus latus dextrum erat actoris.

## 3:2
Verse 2.

AND THE LORD SAID TO SATAN) There is indeed here the word יהוה but it is to be understood here as referring to Michael by metalepsis, or emphasis, because he acts in the place of God.

enemy (for it is called the right, which outweighs another, and stands on the right in opposition, who fosters a favorable cause in judgment, Ps. 109:6-7). Whence easily, had not this Angel stood in the way, Satan could have escaped superior in the judgment of God. But he who undertook the patronage of the priests, as of servants standing by him, and before whom Satan pleads the cause of the sinful man and accuses him, he is not a created Angel, but the eternal God. Furthermore, this Angel had other Angels who stood before him and served and ministered to him, v. 4, 7, to whom he commanded by his authority, take away the filthy garments from him, v. 4. But whom do the Angels serve, if not God, in such a way that they obey at his nod, and who can command and give orders to the Angels, except Jehovah? It is therefore clearer than light that it is not a created Angel Michael, but the Lord himself, before whom Joshua stood, who rebuked Satan. It is added that no created Angel could usurp these words, which this Angel usurped in v. 5: Behold, I have taken away your sin from you; it is the property of the one God to take away iniquities from us. And therefore it is not a created Angel, but the uncreated Son of God, who is indicated, who bore our sins and clothed us with change of garments, Is. 61:10. Indeed, this Angel claims for himself works that are truly divine: (1) the remission of sins. Joshua stood before him in filthy garments, which were not only, as Grotius wishes with the Jews, an indication of that guilt, that he allowed his sons to live with foreign wives: but they designated him as polluted with sins before God, and that which is carnal and stained is a tunic, Jude v. 23. Therefore, by divine authority, the Angel commands to take away the filthy garments, which Grotius ineptly explains with the Chaldean (for he easily licks the spittle of the Jews): cast out those foreign wives from the house: since the words subjoined bring a far different meaning: BEHOLD I HAVE TAKEN AWAY YOUR INIQUITY FROM YOU, which Grotius does not explain as, I have taken away the foreign wives from you. For it is too manifest that they import the remission of sin. AND I HAVE CLOTHED YOU WITH CHANGE OF GARMENTS, which does not denote cleaner wives, but, by Grotius's own interpretation, signifies that Joshua was freed from guilt. But the authentic taking away and remission of sins is of God alone, Ps. 103:3, Is. 45:23, Mic. 7:18, Luke 5:15. (2) The donation of righteousness. But what are those change of garments? Garments that are most precious and festive are so called, derived from extracting, or because they are kept for festive days, having been extracted from common use, or because they are taken off again when the feasts are finished. See Gen. 45:22, Judg. 14:12, 13, 19, 2 Kings 5:5, 22, 23, which are called garments of desires, Gen. 27:27; but as filthy garments were a symbol of iniquities, so change of garments, or cleaner ones, are a symbol of righteousness. But what Angel takes away iniquity from us and clothes us with righteousness? Certainly not Michael the created Angel, but the Angel Goel, our avenger and Redeemer, who clothes us with the garment of salvation and righteousness, Is. 61:10, gives us a white garment, lest the shame of our nakedness appear, Rev. 3:18, and adorns us with the best robe, Luke 15:22, and the wedding garment, Matt. 22:11. Since we put on Christ, as he has been made righteousness for us, 1 Cor. 1:30, Gal. 3:20. We have here, therefore, a notable figure of our justification, which takes place in the judgment of God, when we are accused by Satan, even if he stands at the right hand and has a cause against us; (For rightly Ambrose, Book 11, de interpel. c. 2, Adam gave his right hand to the Devil, which he caused to be extended to the forbidden fruits: thus it was prejudiced in him for all, and the Devil began to stand at the right hand of all: for we are all born condemned and children of wrath) for Christ undertakes our patronage and says to Satan, the Lord rebuke you, Satan, and lest those filthy garments, our iniquities, be an abomination in the eyes of God and bring condemnation upon us, behold Christ takes the filthy garments from us, removes our iniquities, and clothes us with change of garments, the garment of his most pure righteousness, that we may obtain favor in the eyes of the Lord, for the squalid toga, as Dr. Klozius on the Angels, Point 4, with which we are all clothed from head to toe in the judgment of God, is taken off us, and the splendid toga of righteousness, which Christ acquired for us by the ransom of his most precious blood, is given to us. Sin that is present is not imputed, as if it were absent, but the righteousness of Christ, which is not present inherently, is imputed, as if it were present, so that in the judgment of God we are purged from our sins and held to be truly righteous, and for our injustice we acquire the righteousness of Christ, for death life, for wrath thanks, for the underworld the heavens in Christ. Joshua, having been stripped of his filthy garments and clothed with change of garments, is finally commanded to walk in the ways of the Lord. Thus, having been cleansed from sins and justified, we finally do good works that please God. For the blood of Christ cleanses our conscience from dead works to serve God, Heb. 9, as Winckelmann has it. Coccejus thinks Christ the JUDGE is expressed here, because he SAT: which he gathers from a comparison of v. 3 and 5. Concerning whom Acts 17:3, John 5:27, Rom. 14:10. But this proof is more obscure than it is solid. For the fifth verse can be understood as the Angel of the Lord still standing: it is not necessary to accept it as meaning that he had sat before. Osiander: And the Angel of the Lord was standing, and was looking with pleasure upon this Priest, to whom sins had already been forgiven (for the Lord Jesus Christ and the Angels in heaven rejoice if any sinner is reconciled to God, Luke 15). (3) The restoration of the priesthood. For this Angel commands authoritatively: Set a clean turban upon his head, and by that symbol he vindicates to him the restoration of the priesthood for the administration of sacred things, which the high priest took care to be adorned with a turban, which constitution of ministry is the work of God alone, not of any created Angel, Ps. 68:12, 1 Cor. 12:28, as also Jer. 13:15, ch. 23:4, Joel 1:23. In the Hebrew it is AND I SAID. Not as the Vulgate renders: And he said. Because the prayer of the uncreated Angel is continued: Behold I have taken away thy iniquity from thee: And I have clothed thee with change of garments, and I said: put a clean mitre upon his head. Because all these things proceed from that Angel, and are done by his will and command. There is no need, therefore, that we should attribute these words to the Prophet, as expressing his vow and desire, as is held in the Belgic annotations; for all things flow most excellently in the prayer of the same person. These arguments, therefore, like others which the following texts will provide, confirm that the uncreated Angel, the Son of God, is to be understood here, whom accordingly Cyril, Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Dionysius, Isidore, and Clarius understand; and some Papists, compelled by the evidence of the matter, here desert their own, namely Hugo, Vatablus, Albertus Magnus, and Arias, who with the Jews R. David Kimchi and others understand Michael. Thus de Reyroles argues against the same, q. 1 on Zech. III. v. 2, that no other than God is to be understood here, and that the sentence could not have been passed by any other than God, although ineptly and καθ’ ἑαυτομαχίαν he subsequently attributes to the Angel Michael those words, I have clothed thee with change of garments, and inquires concerning him how an Angel can change the human intellect, quest. VI.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET DIXIT DOMINVS AD SATAN) Est quidem hic vox יהוה sed de Michaele hic intelligenda per μετά- ληψιν, aut ἔμφασιν, quia Dei partes agit.

inimico (dextrum enim dicitur, quod præponderat alteri, & à dextra stat adversando, qui causam favorabilem in judicio fovet Psal. CIX. 6. 7.) Unde facile, nisi hic Angelus obstitisset, Satan in judicio Dei superior evadere potuisset. Qui autem Sacerdotum, tanquam servorum sibi astantium, patrocinium suscepit, & coram quo Satan hominis peccatoris causam agit, eumque accusat, ille non est Angelus creatus, sed vetus Deus. Porro habuit hic Angelus alios Angelos, qui coram ipso stabant, ipsique inserviebant, & ministrabant v. 4. 7. quibus ipse pro autoritate præcipiebat, auferte vestimenta sordida ab eo v. 4. Cui autem serviunt Angeli, nisi Deo, ita, ut ad nutum ejus pareant, & quis præcipere ac mandata dare Angelis potest, præter Jehovam? Luce ergo hoc clarius est, non Michaelem creatum Angelum, sed Dominum ipsum esse, coram quo Josua stetit, qui Satanam increpavit. Accedit, quod nullus creatus Angelus hæc verba usurpare possit, quæ hic Angelus usurpavit verf. 5. Ecce abstuli peccatum tuu abs te; unius Dei hoc proprium est, auferre à nobis iniquitates nostras. Ideoque non creatus Angelus, sed increatus Filius Dei, indigitatur, qui peccata nostra tulit, & nos vestibus mutatoriis induit Ef. LXI. 10. Nimirum vindicat hic Angelus sibi opera vere divina (1) peccatorum remissionem. Stabat coram eo Josua vestibus sordidis, quæ non erant solum, uti Grotius vult cum Judæis, indicium illius culpæ, quod filios suos sineret vivere cum uxoribus externis: sed designabant, ipsum peccatis pollutum coram Deo, & ea, quæ carnalis, & maculata est tunica Jud. v. 23. sordidatum. Huic ergo pro autoritate divina auferre vestimenta sordida jubet Angelus, quod inepte exponit cum Chaldæo Grotius (facile enim sputum Judæorum lingit) è domo ejicite uxores illas externas: Siquidem longe alium sensum verba subjuncta inferant: ECCE ABSTULI A TE INIQUITATEM TUAM, quæ non exponit Grotius, abstuli uxores exteras à te. Nimis enim manifestum est, quod peccati remissionem importent. ET INDUI TE MUTATORIIS, quod non notat uxores mundiores, sed ipso Grotio interprete significat, Josuam à culpa esse liberatum. At authentica peccatorum ablatio & remissio non est nisi solius Dei Pf. CIII, 3. Ef. XLV. 23. Mich. VII. 18. Luc. V. 15. (2) Justitiæ donationem. Quæ autem sunt vestes illæ mutatoriæ? Dicuntur ita vestes maxime pretiosæ & festivæ, מהלצות ab extrahendo dictæ seu quod à communi usu extractæ festivis diebus serventur, seu, quod exactis festis iterum exuantur. Vid. Genes. XLV. 22. Jud. XIV. 12. 13. 19. II. Reg. V. 5. 22. 23. quæ vestes desideriorum dicuntur Gen. XXVII. 27. ut autem vestes sordidæ symbolum iniquitatum erant, ita vestes mutatoriæ, vel mundiores symbolum sunt justitiæ. Quis autem Angelus aufert à nobis iniquitatem, & vestit nos justitia? Non certe Michael creatus Angelus, sed Angelus Goël, vindex & Redemptor noster, qui nos veste salutis & justitiæ induit Ef. LXI. 10. vestimentum candidum nobis donat, ne compareat turpitudo nuditatis nostræ Apoc. III. 18. ornatque nos stola præcipua Luc. XV. 22. & veste nuptiali Matth. XXII. 11. Quandoquidem Christum, ut factus nobis est justitia I. Cor. I. 30. induamus Gal. III. 20. Habemus itaque hic insignem figuram nostræ justificationis, quæ sit in judicio Dei, cum à Satana accusamur, etsi ipse à dextris stet, causamque adversus nos habeat; (Recte enim Ambrosius Libr. XI. de interpel. c. II. Adam dextram suam Diabolo dedit, quam extendi fecit ad interdicta poma: ita præjudicatum est in illo omnibus, & cæpit universis Diabolus à dextris stare: omnes quippe na- scimur damnati & filii iræ) nostri enim patrociniu suscipit Christus, & Satanæ dicit, increpet te Domi- nus Satan, atque ne vestes illæ sordidæ, iniquitates nostræ, abominatio in oculis Dei sint, nobisque condemnationem adferant, ecce aufert Christus à nobis vestes sordidas, tollit iniquitates nostras, nosque induit vestibus mutatoriis, veste justitiæ suæ purissimæ, ut gratiam in oculis Domini consequa- mur, squalida enim toga, uti Dn. D. Klozius de An- gel. Punct. IV. qua omnes induti sumus à capite ad calcem in judicio Dei nobis exuitur, & splendida ju- stitiæ toga, quam Christus nobis acquisivit sanguinis pretiosissimi λύτρῳ, nobis donatur. Peccatum quod adeft, non imputatur, ac si abesset, Christi vero ju- stitia, quæ inhæsive non adest, imputatur, ac si ad- essset, ita, ut in Dei judicio à peccatis nostris pur- gati, & vere justi habeamur, & pro injustitia no- stra justitiam Christi, pro morte vitam, pro ira gra- tiam, pro inferis cælos in Christo acquiramus. Jo- sua exutus vestibus sordidis, & indutus mutatoriis demum ambulare jubetur in viis Domini. Ita scilicet mundati à peccatis, & justificati demum facimus bo- na opera Deo placentia. Sanguis enim Christi emun- dat conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuis ad ser- viendum Deo, Heb. IX. uti habet Winckelmannus. Coccejus JUDICEM Christum hic expressum putat, quod SEDERIT: quod colligit è collatio- ne v. 3. & 5. De quo Act. XVII. 3. Joh. V. 27. Rom. XIV. 10. Sed obscurior hæc est probatio, quam so- lidior. Nam versus quintus intelligi potest, quod adhuc steterit Angelus Domini: non necessum est ita accipi, quod antea sederit. Osiander: Et Angelus Domini stabat, & cum voluptate in hunc Sacerdo- tem, cui peccata jam remissa erant, intuebatur (Dominus enim Jesus Christus, & Angeli in cœ- lis gaudent, si quis peccator Deo reconciliatur Luc. XV.) (3) Sacerdotii restaurationem. Præcipit enim hic Angelus autoritative: Ponite cidarim mundam super caput ejus, eoque symbolo Sacerdo- tii restaurationem, ad rerum sacrarum administra- tionem, quam cidari ornatus summus Sacerdos curabat, illi vindicat, quæ ministerii constitutio est opus solius Dei, non Angeli alicujus creati Pf. LXIIX. 12. I. Cor. XII. 28. ut & Jer. XIII. 15. cap. XXIII. 4. Joel. I. 23. In Ebræo habetur ויאמר ET DIXI. Non ut vulgatus reddit: Et dixit. Quia con- tinuatur Angeli increati oratio: Ecce abstuli à te iniquitatem tuam: Et indui te mutatoriis, & dixi po- nite cidarim mundam super caput ejus. Quia hæc o- mnia ab Angelo illo proficiscuntur, ejusque vo- luntate, ac jussu fiunt. Non ergo opus est, ut verba hæc Prophetæ, ceu votum & desiderium ejus ex- primentia, tribuamus, uti habetur in annot. Bel- gic. omnia enim fluunt optime in oratione ejus- dem personæ. Hæc ergo argumenta, ut alia, quæ subsequentes textus dabunt, confirmant angelum increatum filium Dei hic intelligendum esse, quem proinde intelligunt Cyrillus, Hieronymus, Theodo- retus, Remigius, Dionys. Isidor. Clarius, & deserunt hic evidentia rei coacti suos Pontificii nonnulli, Hugonem nempe, Vatablum, Albertum M. & A- riam, qui cum Judæis R. David Kimchio, & aliis Michaelem intelligunt. Ita de Reyroles disputat con- tra eosdem q. 1. ad Zach. III. v. 2. non alium nisi Deum hic intelligendum esse, nec ab alio, nisi Deo ferendam fuisse sententiam, etsi inepte & καθ’ ἑαυτομαχίαν deinde Angelo Michaeli tribuat illa, indui te muta- toriis, ac de eo disquirat, quomodo Angelus possit hu- manum intellectum immutare quæst. VI.

## 3:3
Vers. 3.

AND JESUS WAS CLOTHED WITH FILTHY GARMENTS) That is, there was some fault in him; namely, that he allowed his sons to live with foreign wives, against the law of Deut. XIV. 15, Ezech. XLIV. 22. Satan seized upon this, as having a right over those who are outside the law.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET JESVS ERAT INDVTUS VESTIBVS SORDI- DIS) Id est, erat aliquid in eo culpæ; nempè quod filios suos sineret vivere cum uxoribus externis, contra legem Deut. XIV. 15. Ezech. XLIV. 22. hoc arripiebat Satan, ut jus habens in exleges.

## 3:4
Vers. 4.

TAKE AWAY THE FILTHY GARMENTS FROM HIM) That is, cast out those foreign wives from the house. Thus the Chaldean here.

BEHOLD I HAVE TAKEN AWAY THY INIQUITY FROM THEE) I have cleansed you from that which alone could be objected against you,

AND I HAVE CLOTHED THEE WITH CHANGE OF RAIMENT) That is, with cleaner garments. This signified that he was freed from guilt.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

AUFERTE VESTIMENTA SORDIDA AB EO) Id est, è domo ejicite uxores illas externas. Ita hiè Chaldæus.

ECCE ABSTULI A TE INIQVITATEM TVAM) Repurgavi te ab eo, quod unum tibi objici poterat,

ET INDUI TE MUTATORIIS) Id est, vestibus mundioribus.Id significabat, eum à culpa esse liberatum.

## 3:5
Vers. 5.

SET A CLEAN MITRE UPON HIS HEAD) Because that which he had had before was as it were defiled by this guilt. The mitre is an ornament of the head proper to the High Priest Exod. XXVIII. 4. 34. Levit. VIII. 9. XVI. 4.

AND THEY CLOTHED HIM WITH GARMENTS) New ones.

The Vulgate has added of its own the word Lord. And the Lord showed me, which is contained neither in the Hebrew nor the Chaldean. It can be understood that the Angel showed these things, who had spoken before. Cocceius also implies an Angel as interlocutor: but he wishes him to be the Holy Spirit, which is clearly foreign to the Scriptures. For nowhere is it read that the Holy Spirit is called an Angel. But the argument which is brought forward concerning Michael the created Angel is too thin. For even if this Angel were to use certain similar words Jud. v. 9. is the same Angel therefore to be understood in the case of Zechariah? Although not even that is placed beyond controversy, that Michael in Jude is a created Angel. Others, and also Cocceius here, understand it of the Son of God: Michael ὁ τολμᾷ, does not sustain the opinion of uttering a railing accusation against Satan, because the Son can say and do nothing, except what he has heard and seen the Father say and do Ioh. V. 19. 30. The reason is not of minority, but of unity p. 488. But just as it has been established by clear and invincible testimonies that it was not a created Angel Michael who was indicated thus far, but the Son of God himself, by the mention of the man among the myrtle trees, and the Angel speaking in Zechariah, and giving commands to another Angel meeting him, so here likewise no other Angel can be understood than the Angel Lord, or the uncreated Angel, as we speak for the sake of distinction, the Son of God. For Zechariah explicitly calls the same one in the nominative case Jehovah the Lord. And the Lord said to Satan; where Grotius invents in vain I know not what metalepsis, (certainly unknown to Scripture and lacking example) or even an ellipsis, by which method it is necessary to introduce confusion of the person sent and the sender, of the legate and the one sending, nay of the servant and the Lord, so that in such relations nothing certain is left, if indeed, the Lord said by metalepsis by ellipsis, it is permitted to take it thus: The Angel of the Lord said. Therefore the Jehovah Son of God speaks here entirely, threatening Satan with the rebuke of God the Father, The Lord rebuke thee. Before this Angel Joshua the High Priest is said to have stood v. 1. & 3. by which the ministry of Joshua is indicated. Who was not the minister of Michael, but of God. v. 4. Satan is said to stand at his right hand, not only because he held the part of the accuser, but because, as Jerome has it, his accusation was true, and he promised himself certain victory over

CHAPTER III. The fourth vision; the investiture of the High Priest with the promise of the Branch and the stone to be cut out for the sins of the world.

Satan resisting Joshua standing before the uncreated Angel is rebuked, Joshua, having put off his impure garments as a sign of the washing away of sins, is adorned with solemn garments and a priestly cap, receiving a promise concerning the government of the house of the Lord, and angelic company, and also concerning God's servant the Branch and the excision of the eyed stone to take away the sins of the land and to procure true peace.

The sordid Priest is clothed in a beautiful garment.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PONITE CIDARIM MVNDAM SVPER CA- PVT EJVS) Quia ea, quam anteà habuerat, erat pe- iftam culpam quasi contaminata. Cidaris ornamentum capitis proprium summo Sacerdoti Exod. XXVIII. 4. 34. Levit. VIII. 9. XVI. 4.

ET INDVERVNT EVM VESTIBVS) Novis.

Vulgata de suo addidit vocem Dominus. Et o- stendit mihi Dominus, quæ nec in Ebræo, nec Chaldæo habetur. Intelligi potest Angelus hæc o- stendisse, qui antea locutus. Angelum collocuto- rem etiam subintelligit Coccejus: sed eum vult es- se Sp. S. quod à Scripturis plane alienum. Nusquam enim Sp. S. Angelus dictus legitur. Nimis exile au- tem argumentum est, quod de Michaele Angelo creato adfertur. Nam etiamsi similia verba quæ- dam adhiberet hic Angelus Iud. v. 9. num ideo et- iam penesZachariam idem Angelus intelligendus? Quamvis nec id extra controversiam positum sit, Michaelem apud Judam esse Angelum creatum. De Filio Dei tum alii, tum etiam hic Coccejus in- telligunt: Michael ὁ τολμᾷ, non sustinet sententiam convitii contra Satanam proferre, quia Filius nihil potest dicere & facere, nisi quod audiverit & vide- rit Patrem dicere & facere Ioh. V. 19.30. Ratio est non minoritatis, sed unitas p. 488. Ut autem non Mi- chaelem creatum Angelum indigitatum fuisse ha- ctenus, sed ipsummet Filium Dei, mentione viri inter myrtos, & Angeli in Zacharia loquentis, al- terique Angelo sibi occurrenti mandata dantis, luculentis & invictis testimoniis constitit, ita hiè similiter Angelus alius intelligi nequit, quam An- gelus Dominus, vel Angelus increatus, uti nos di- stinctionis causa loquimur, Filius Dei. Vocat enim Zacharias eundem diserte in casu recto Iehovam Dominum. Et dixit Dominus ad Satan; ubi frustrà comminiscitur Grotius, nescio quam μετάληψιν, (ignotam certe Scripturæ & exemplo carentem) aut etiam ἔλλειψιν, quo pacto confusionem inve- here oportet personæ missæ & mittentis,legati & le- gantis, imo servi & Domini, ut in ejusmodi relatio- nibus nihil certi relinquatur, si nempe, dixit Do- minus per μετάληψιν per ἔλλειψιν,liceat ita accipe- re: Dixit Domini Angelus. Loquitur ergo omnino hic Iehovah Filius Dei,interminans Satanæ incre- pationem Dei Patris, Dominus increpet te. Coram hoc Angelo Josua summus Sacerdos stetisse dici- tur v.1. & 3. quo indicatur ministerium Josuæ. Qui non Michaelis minister erat, sed Dei. v. 4. Stare à dextris dicitur Satan, non solum, quod actoris par- tes haberet, sed quia, ut Hieron. habet, vera erat ejus accusatio, ac certam victoriam pollicebatur de

CAPUT III. Quarta visio; summi Pontificis investitu- ra cum promissione Zemach & lapi- dis pro peccatis mundi exscin- dendi.

Josuæ coram Angelo increato stanti resistens Satanas increpatur, Josua exutis impuris vestibus in signum ablutionis peccato- rum, vestibus solennibus & pileo Sacer- dotali ornatur, accipiens promissionem de gubernatione domus Domini, & comita- tu angelico, nec non de Dei servo Ze- mach & excisione lapidis oculati ad tol- lendum peccata terræ & conciliandam veram pacem.

Sordidus induitur speciosa veste Sacerdos.

## 3:7
Ver. 7.

IF THOU WILT WALK IN MY WAYS) If thou wilt carefully keep the law.

AND YOU SHALL KEEP MY CHARGE) That is: you shall well perform the parts entrusted to you. For that is properly שמרה. See at Luke 1.5.

YOU ALSO SHALL JUDGE MY HOUSE) That is, you shall rule the ceremonies of the temple, for a long time, of course. For that is the duty of the Priests. Lev. 10.10. Ezek. 44.23. Mal. 2.7.

AND YOU SHALL KEEP MY COURTS) You shall preside over the temple for a long time.

AND I WILL GIVE YOU THOSE WHO WALK) Who may walk with you, that is, who may defend and protect you. Ps. 91.11. Mal. 4.6.

OF THESE, WHO NOW STAND HERE) As it were the attendants of Michael. See above 4, and what was said at Matt. 18.10. Many of the Hebrews refer these things to eternal life, so that, because it is difficult for them, they may prove it is expressly promised in the Old Covenant. But the sense which we have brought forward is plainer.

That, if you will walk in my ways, is more correctly understood generally of the ways of the Lord's precepts: just as the Lord's charge denotes in particular the Levitical ceremonies to be kept in the Priestly office. Osiander correctly explains the threefold promise subjoined: You also shall judge my house: i.e., as High Priest among my people (which is as it were my family) you shall pronounce judgment in grave matters, the decision of which belongs to the High Priest of the Levitical priesthood: And you shall keep my courts: i.e., you shall perform with authority and dignity the office of High Priest in my Temple. For the Lord confirms in his sanction those who devote faithful effort to him, but casts down from their rank the negligent and unfaithful workers) And I will give you those who walk with you from among those who now stand here, that is, I will join to you a company of Angels who may protect you. For the Lord joins guardian Angels to pious men, Ps. 34, but especially to faithful Ministers of the Church, as this passage of the Prophet testifies. Similarly B. Balduinus p. 258. He signifies by charge the function in the temple, which was administered by the Levites either by sacrificing, or by singing, or finally by teaching, just as it is read in 2 Chron. 7. v. 6: The Priests stood in their charges (בשמרותם) whence Priests and ministers of the Church are called guards, or watchmen. Ezek. 3.17, 33.7. Therefore, by this precept, diligent inspection of the Church and of the worship among the people of God, now about to be renewed, is entrusted to Joshua. The benefits which he promises he sets forth in order: 1. dexterity in political judgment, 2. ἱκανότη[?]a and suitable strength in ecclesiastical inspection: 3. The aid of Angels in both. For there were two kinds of offices entrusted to the Levitical High Priest, as is evident from Deut. 17. v. 8 seqq. The first, To judge between blood and blood, leprosy and leprosy, cause and cause, that is, to decide even political controversies according to the law, as is explained in 2 Chron. 19. v. 10, and in this office he promises dexterity and happy success: you shall judge, he says, my house, that is, you will most easily and happily settle the controversial causes among my Israelite people. The other, to minister in the Sanctuary Exod. 28.43, to pray for Israel 1 Chron. 7. v. 49, to offer sacrifices, Heb. 10. v. 11, and to have general inspection of the whole Levitical worship, just as it is written concerning Aaron and his sons, that they were appointed over the service of the Priesthood. Num. ch. 3. v. 10. In this office he promises sufficient strength to Joshua. You shall keep, he says, my courts, that is, you will diligently and with success administer whatever pertains to the offices of the temple, and the works of the Priests, and to the ecclesiastical government of the people. For in the court the remaining Priests stood and sacrificed Ps. 135.2. Some explain the third benefit as walking among the Angelic assemblies after this life Matt. 22.30, Heb. 12.22. See the Belgic annotations. Willius adds yet a third sense:

I will give you those who may walk among these standing ones, that is, from your descendants I will preserve those who may minister together with my Angels, and be their companions in this part. So that the amplification and continuation of the Priestly dignity may be promised: which is Cocceius's explanation: but the former interpretation concerning the Angelic guards, which pleased Jerome, B. Luther, and others almost commonly, is to be preferred.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

SI IN VIIS MEIS AMBULAVERIS) Si legem sollicite servaveris.

ET CVSTODIAM MEAM CVSTODIERIS) Id eft: partes tibi mandatas bene obieris. Id enim pro- prie שמרה. Vide ad Lucam I. 5.

TV QVOQVE JVDICABIS DOMVM MEAM) Id est, templi ceremonias reges, diu scilicet. Id enim mu- nus Sacerdotum. Levit. X, 10. Ezech. XLIV. 23. Mal. II. 7.

ET CVSTODIES ATRIA MEA) Diu præeris templo.

ET DABO TIBI AMBVLANTES) Qui ambu- lent tecum, id est, qui te defendant ac protegant. Ps. XCI. 11. Mal. IV. 6.

DE HIS, QVI NVNC HIC ASSISTVNT) Vel- ut apparitores Michaelis. Vide supra 4. & quæ dicta ad Matth. XVIII. 10. Hæc Hebræorum multi referunt ad vitam æternam, ut, quod ipsis difficile est, eam probent in veteri fœdere diserte promitti. Sed sensus, quem attuli- mus, est planior.

Illa, si in viis tuis ambulaveris, rectius de viis præceptorum Domini generaliter intelliguntur: uti custodia Domini ceremonias Leviticas in officio Sa- cerdotali custodiendas in specie notat. Promissio- nem subjunctam triplicem recte exponit Osian- der: Tu quoque judicabis domum meam: i. e. ut sum- mus Sacerdos in populo meo (quæ est quasi fami- lia mea) pronunciabis sententiam in rebus gravi- bus, quarum decisio ad summum Pontificem Sa- cerdotii Levitici pertinet: Et custodies atria mea: i. e. fungeris cum autoritate & dignitate officio Sacer- dotis summi, in Templo meo. Dominus enim eos in sanctione sua confirmat, qui fidelem ipsi ope- ram navant, negligentes vero & infideles opera- rios de gradu suo dejicit) Et dabo tibi tecum ambu- lantes de his, qui nunc hic assistunt, id est, adjungam tibi comitatum Angelorum, qui te protegant. Do- minus enim custodes Angelos adjungit piis homi- nibus, Psal. 34. præsertim vero fidelibus Ecclesiæ Ministris, ut hic locus Prophetæ testatur. Simili- ter B. Balduinus p. 258. Significat custodia functio- nem in templo, quæ vel sit sacrificando, vel psallen- do, vel denique docendo à Levitis administrabatur, quemadmodum II. Paral. VII. v. 6. legitur: Sacer- dotes stabant in custodiis suis (בשמרותם) unde Sa- cerdotes & ministri Ecclesiæ, custodes, seu speculato- res dicuntur. Ezech. 3, 17. 33, 7. Demandatur igitur Josuæ hoc præcepto diligens inspectio Ecclesiæ, cultusque in populo Dei jamjam renovandi, Bene- ficia quæ promittit, tria ponit ordine, 1. dexteri- tatem in judicio politico, 2. ἱκανότη[?]a & vires ido- neas inspectione Ecclesiastica: 3 Subsidium An- gelorum in utroque. Duo enim erant officiorum genera commissa summo Sacerdoti Levitico, uti constat ex Deut. 17. v. 8. seqq. Primum Judicare inter sanguinem & sanguinem, lepram & lepram, causam & causam, hoc est, controversias etiam politicas juxta legem decidere, ut explicatur II. Paral. XIX. v. 10. & in hoc officio dexteritatem ac felicem suc- cessum promittit: judicabis, inquit, domum meam, id est, causas in populo meo Israëlitico controver- sas facillime & feliciter compones. Alterum mini- strare in Sanctuario Exod. 28, 43. precari pro Israel I. Paral. VII. v. 49. offerre hostias, Heb. X. v. 11. & ge- neralem inspectionem totius cultus Levitici habere, quemadmodum de Aarone, & filiis ejus scriptum est, quod constituta fuerint super cultum Sacerdo- tii. Num. c. III. v. 10. In hoc officio vires sufficientes Josuæ pollicetur. Custodies, inquit, atria mea, id est, quicquid ad officia templi, & opera Sacerdotum, ad gubernationem populi Ecclesiasticam perti- nent, diligenter & cum successu administrabis. In atrio enim Sacerdotes reliqui stabant, & sacrifica- bant Ps. CXXXV. 2. Tertium beneficium nonnulli explicant de ambulatione inter cœtus Angelicos post hanc vitam Matth. XXII. 30. Ebr. XII. 22. Vid. an- not. Belgicæ. Willius tertium adhuc sensum addit:

Dabo tibi, qui ambulent inter astantes istos, id est, ex posteris tuis servabo, qui una cum Angelis meis ministrent, eorumque hac in parte consortes sint. Ut dignitatis Sacerdotalis amplificatio & continuatio promittatur: quæ est Cocceji explicatio: sed præferenda est prior de excubiis Angelicis interpretatio, quæ Hieronymo, B. Luthero, aliisque placuit fere communiter.

## 3:8
Ver. 8. YOU AND YOUR FRIENDS WHO WERE SITTING BEFORE YOU) They sit with you. Understand this as Zechariah, Haggai, Malachi, and perhaps also Daniel.

FOR THEY ARE MEN OF PORTENT) Men of a portent: That is, worthy that signs of future things should be displayed through them, for that is what מופת means.

FOR BEHOLD I WILL BRING) Hither to you.

MY SERVANT THE BRANCH) My servant the sprout: that is, Zerubbabel, the shoot of the Davidic stock who is called צמח and in Isaiah 11:2, Jeremiah 23:5, 33:15, and likewise below in ch. 6:12. The Chaldean and other Jews interpret this passage concerning the Messiah. Others add that צמח is ἰσόψηφον (equal in numerical value) to the name מנחם, which signifies a comforter, and is among the titles of the Messiah. They call that kind of interpretation by numbers Gematria, that is, συμμετρίαν (symmetry). Nor is there any doubt that this passage pertains in a certain mystical way to Christ, the author of eternal peace, but if we seek the primary and obvious sense, the passage 4:10 with those that follow, and the said passage 6:12, will prove that it treats here of Zerubbabel.

By צמח not Zerubbabel, but Christ is indicated. Which (1) the name indicates. For this is applied to Christ, not to Zerubbabel. Christ is called the branch of the Lord in Isaiah 4:2, the branch of righteousness and the righteous one in Jeremiah 23:5, ch. 33:15. The root of which name, צמח, sprouted, is used to explain the Messiah and his benefits in Zechariah 6:12, Psalm 85:12, Psalm 132:17, Isaiah 43:19, ch. 61:12. The Septuagint interpreters express it as ἀνατολήν (the rising/branch), and thus John calls Christ in Luke 1:78. (2) The name of the servant of the Lord, which is attributed ἀντονομαστικῶς (by antonomasia) to the Messiah in Isaiah 53:1, 11, ch. 42:1. For no servant can show such obedience to a master as Christ showed to the Father in Philippians 2:8. (3) The addition of the branch of the servant of the Lord. Zerubbabel was not to be brought at last, but had already been brought. But as this promise was altogether the most important in the Prophetic Writings, that the Lord would bring the Messiah, that righteous branch, so the Holy Spirit inculcates it frequently. S. so that, indeed, they may in no way doubt the truth of that promise which is necessary for all to believe. Now God the Father speaks this, whom the Angel, the Son of God, introduces as speaking in v. 6, 7. But not, as others who do not rightly weigh the text say, that the Son of God is speaking about himself. AND THE ANGEL OF THE LORD (the Son of God) TESTIFIED TO Joshua (the Priest) saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts (God the Father) Hear, Joshua, great Priest. For behold I will bring my servant (Christ) the Branch or sprout. Everything is plain in this way, nor does it appear why it should be said that the Son of God is speaking about himself, but in the third person. Nor is there any similar example of that thing.

By the FRIENDS of Joshua are understood not Prophets, but other Priests: For they dwell before Joshua, and were committed to his oversight and inspection. But they are called MEN OF PORTENT, or OF A PORTENT, because they handled mystical sacred things, by which that future Messiah of the world with all his benefits was signified. For as the blessed Balduinus rightly says, He uses the word מופת for this reason, because when it is attributed to persons, it signifies a portent, or the signification of future things, as Pagninus notes; just as אות is a sign of present things: Others, especially the blessed Luther, understand it thus, as if the confessors of Christ are portentous to all in this world, hated and despised, held as fools and insane before the wise of this world, as those who have faith in a doctrine so ridiculous (as it seems to foolish reason) concerning Christ crucified: just as this description of the faithful is not unusual in Scripture elsewhere. See examples in Eph. VIII. v. 18. Ezek. XII. 11. Ps. LXXI. v. 7. I Cor. IV. v. 9. etc. Others call them men of a portent because of their miraculous observance in Babylon: Others, because they were held as such by the impious, on account of their observance of the divine word. Thus Winckelmann: The faithful, who were building the temple of Christ in the hope of a future Priesthood, were to the rest of the Jews like a sign, a prodigy, and a spectacle, since they, whether out of pusillanimity or out of stubborn contempt for the promise, thought that they were laboring in vain. The first explanation is also approved by Cocceius: I have given them to the Israelite people as a sign, a manifestation of my counsel. They sustain the figure of my Son. They foreshadow his Priesthood. Therefore it is necessary for them to go before and shine before the people, so that they may lead them to Christ, as to the goal of their calling. He adds: These words can therefore (and perhaps ought to) be joined with the following in this way. For they are men of a sign, because I am bringing my servant the Branch v. 8. In these words is the second part of the speech of God, narrated through the Angel, namely the promise of the coming of Christ in the near future. He calls him צמח, the Branch. He takes this name from the earlier Prophets. Is. IV. 2. Jer. XXIII. 5. XXXIII. 15. He gives the reason for the appellation in Zech. VI. 12. Refer here to Luke I. 78, where emphatically the Branch from on high. John III. 31. I Cor. XV. 47. He is called servant, because he was born of a woman, born under the law Gal. IV. 4. Psalm VIII. 6. Is. LIII. v. 11. Now if you join the words in that manner, it will be understood that Joshua and his disciples are more men of a sign than Aaron himself and his sons before the Babylonian captivity. For in them was a certain argument that God was now about to bring the Messiah. Indeed, according to the Prophecies, this session of Joshua and his disciples before him was destined to last until the revelation of Christ. Gen. XLIX. 10. And this so miraculous restoration of ceremonial worship and of the congregation and ecclesiastical institution could strike the minds of all men, so that they might think that it portended something greater, which, namely, the Prophecies were promising. Let the undoubted principle of the demonstration of the kingdom of God be held. The Priesthood of the Aaronites and their assembly for learning the law and exercising it after the Babylonian captivity is the firmest proof of the coming of Christ connected with it. Whence Willius accepts it thus, that they themselves are signs of the restoration of the temple and the Priesthood: and he wishes the particle כי in the following words, For behold I am about to bring my servant the branch, to indicate the reason why he called Joshua the priest a sign, because, namely, he himself represents the Messiah and the true Priest whom God is about to bring. Therefore, Joshua can infer from his own person that the Priesthood will remain, because he himself is a type of the eternal Priest. And there seems to be an emphasis on the word 'to bring,' by which he wishes to hint that one can be certain of the continuation, because his antitype is not yet present, but must first be brought.

The fourth reason, therefore, will be taken from the continuity of the text, explained in this way. Cornelius à Lapide alleges for this continuity Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, and Hugo, that they are called men of a portent because they portended Christ, who was to be the greatest portent of portents, the branch is the seven-eyed stone, etc. And Cyril: Because they desire to see and hear portentous things, let them hear the portent of the ages, namely, I am bringing my servant the rising one, etc. Add (5) that from ch. VI. 12 it is manifest that no one other than the Messiah is understood by the name צמח. And (6) that the subjoined promise concerning the stone is to be accepted concerning Christ. Whence (7)

most interpreters agree that the discourse is about Christ. Calvin himself, who otherwise willingly drags prophecies about Christ into another sense, also interprets this concerning Christ, and brings forward reasons for his explanation that are not to be despised; There is no doubt, he says in this place, p. 623, that God signifies the priest of hosts, who will excel above the common sense of men. But he is called the Branch because he will come forth like a shoot, just as it is said in the second chapter of Isaiah and in other places. It is therefore the same as if he were saying: This Priesthood is still despised, yet my servant will come forth, i.e., the Priest, just as a branch is accustomed to arise from the earth, then to grow: and צמח also signifies a shoot. He therefore compares Christ to a shoot, because he seemed to arise from nothing, so to speak, because his beginning was contemptible. For what excellence did Christ obtain in the world when he was born? Then, how did he inaugurate his kingdom? And how was he initiated into his Priesthood? Certainly, we know that whatever honor or excellence the Father had given him was held in mockery: it is not surprising, therefore, if he is called the branch for this reason. Now the reason for the comparison appears sufficiently. Although the Angel speaks indefinitely about the priests, there is no doubt, however, that he meanwhile designates the person of Christ. Why? One may judge from the event itself. What priest succeeded Joshua who equaled his honor, or even who approached him by a tenth part? We know that almost all of them were profane and impious men, we know that the Priesthood among them was venal: we know that they contended with the most cruel hatreds, indeed we know that a priest was slaughtered in the very temple, so had ambition flared up that they could not break through except by innocent blood. Nothing, therefore, after the death of Joshua was more foul or more shameful for the Jewish Priesthood. Where, then, will that servant of God, the branch, be found? Then that principle must always be held, that the renovation of the temple was in the person of Christ: it is necessary, therefore, to come to his person, so that we may have this servant who is mentioned. Nor indeed are these things to be understood only in a mystical sense concerning the Messiah; but in a proper and literal one: For no reason persuades us to understand it of Zerubbabel: nor is a double sense to be admitted in the Scriptures. Indeed, the Jews themselves interpret it according to the letter, not only mystically, concerning Christ, as is clear from the Targum of Jonathan, which in place of the word צמח uses the name משיח.

Latin:

Vers. 8. TU ET AMICI TUI QVI HABITABANT CORAM TE) Assident tibi. Intellge hunc Zachariam, Aggæum, Malachiam, forte & Danielem.

QVIA VIRI PORTENDENTES SVNT) Viri portenti: Id est, digni quibus signa rerum futurarum edantur, id enim מופת.

ECCE ENIM EGO ADDUCAM) Huc ad vos.

SERVUM MEUM ORIENTEM) Servum meum germen: id est; Zorobabelem furculum Davidicæ stirpis qui צמח vocatur & E saia II. 2. Jerem. XXIII, 5. XXXIII, 15. sic & infra c. VI, 12. Chaldæus & Judæi alii de Messia hunc locum interpretantur. Addunt alii צמח esse ἰσόψηφον nomini מנחם, quod consolatorem significat, & inter indigetamenta est Messiæ. Id interpretandi genus per numeros partes גמטריא, id est, συμμετρίαν vocant. Neque dubium, quin mystico quodam modo hic locus ad Christum, pacis æternæ auctorem, pertineat, sed primum obviumque sensum si quærimus, agi hic de Zorobabele evincet locus IV. 10. cum sequentibus, & dictus locus VI. 12.

Per צמח non Zorobabel, sed Christus indigitatur. Quod (1) nomen indicat. Hoc enim de Christo adhibetur, non de Zorobabele. Christus dicitur germen Domini Es. IV. 2. germen justitiæ & justus Jerem. XXIII. 5. c. XXXIII. 15. Cujus nominis radix צמח germinavit, ad Messiam ejusque beneficia explicanda adhibetur Zach. VI. 12. Psal. LXXXV. 12. Psal. CXXXII. 17. Es. XLIII. 19. c. LXI. 12. LXX. Interpp. ἀνατολήν exprimunt atque ita Christum vocat Johannes Luc. I. 78. (2) Nomen servi Domini, quod ἀντονομαστικῶς tribuitur Messiæ Es. LIII. 1. 11. c. XLII. 1. Nullus enim servus hero tantam præstare potest obedientiam, quantam Christus Patri præstitit Philip. II. 8. (3) Additio germinis servi Domini. Zorobabel non adducendus demum, sed jam adductus erat. Ut vero promissio in Scriptis Propheticis omnino præcipua fuit hæc, adducturum Dominum Messiam, germen illud justum, ita frequenter eam inculcat Sp. S. ut nempe de veritate promissionis istius omnibus creditu necessariæ nullatenus dubitent. Loquitur autem hæc Deus Pater, quem loquentem introducit Angelus, Filius Dei v. 6. 7. Non vero, ut alii, haud recte perpendentes textum, ajunt, Filius Dei de se ipso loquitur. ET CONTESTABATUR ANGELUS DOMINI (Filius Dei) Josuam (Sacerdotem) dicens: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum (Deus Pater) Audi Josua, Sacerdos magne. Ecce enim ego adducam servum meum (Christum) Germen seu virgultum. Omnia plana ita sunt, nec apparet, cur dicendum sit, Filium Dei de seipso, sed in tertia persona loqui. Neque ejus rei simile exemplum habetur.

AMICI Josuæ non Prophetæ, sed Sacerdotes alii intelliguntur: Illi enim habitant coram Josua, Ephoriæ & inspectioni ejus erant commissi. VIRI autem PORTENDENTES, vel PORTENTI dicuntur, quia mystica sacra tractabant, quibus futurus ille mundi Messias cum omnibus suis beneficiis significabatur. Nam ut recte B. Balduinus, Ideo utitur vocabulo מופת quod cum personis tribuitur, portentum, seu significationem rerum futurarum significat, annotante Pagnino; quemadmodum אות signum rerum præsentium est: Alii, imprimis B. Lutherus, ita intelligunt, quasi confessores Christi omnibus in hoc mundo sint portentosi, exosi & contemti, ut stulti & insanientes habiti præ sapientibus hujus mundi, ut qui doctrinæ tam ridiculæ (ut vi- detur stolidæ rationi) de Christo crucifixo fidem habeant: quemadmodum alias hæc fidelium de- scriptio Scripturæ non est insolens. Exempla vide Ef. VIII. v.18. Ezech. XII. 11. Pf. LXXI. v.7. I.Cor. IV. v. 9. &c. Alii viros portenti dicunt ob miracu- losam observationem in Babylonia: Alii, quod tales ab impiis habiti sint, ob verbi divini observatio- nem. Ita Winckelmannus: Fideles, qui spe futuri Sacerdotii Christi templum ædificabant, reliquis Judæis erant instar figni, prodigii & spectaculi, quan- doquidem illi vel ex pusillanimitate vel ex præ- fracto contemptu promissionis, ipsos inanem ope- ram sumere putabant. Prima explicatio Coccejo e- tiam probata: Ego illos dedi populo Israelitico in si- gnum Φανέρωσιν consilii mei. Sustinent figuram Filii mei. Adumbrant ipsius Sacerdotium. Præire igitur ipsos oportet, & prælucere populo, ut eum adducant ad Christum, tanquam ad scopum vocationis suæ. Addit: Possunt adeo (& fortasse debent) hæc verba cum se- quentibus sic conjungi. Nam viri figni sunt illi, quod Ego adduco servum meum Tsemach v.8. In iis ver- bis est secunda pars orationis Dei, narratæ per An- gelum, nempe promissio adventus Christi in proxi- mum tempus. Eum vocat צמח Germen. Nomen hoc sumit ex Prophetis anterioribus. Ef. IV. 2. Je- rem. XXIII. 5. XXXIII. 15. Rationem appellationis reddit Zachar. VI. 12. Huc refer Luc. I. 78. ubi em- phatice Germen ex alto. Joh. III. 31. I. Corinth. XV. 47. Vocatur servus, quia γενόμεν- ἐκ γυναικὸς ἐγένετο ὑπὸ τὸν νόμον Galat. IV. 4. Plalm. VIII. 6. Ef. LIII. v. 11. Jam si verba in illum modum jungas, in- telligetur, Josuam & discipulos ejus magis esse vi- ros figni, quam ipsum Aaronem, & filios ejus, an- te captivitatem Babylonicam. Nam in ipsis erat certum argumentum, quod jam adducturus esset Deus Messiam. Quippe secundum Prophetias, hæc sessio Jehoshuæ, & discipulorum ejus ante ipsum du- rare debebat usque ad Christi revelationem. Gen. XLIX. 10. Et hæc tam miraculosa cultus ceremonia- lis & congregationis ac institutionis Ecclesiasticæ in- stauratio omnium hominum animos percellere poterat, ut cogitarent, eam aliquid majus, quod scil. Prophetiæ promittebant, portendere. Teneatur indubitatum principium demonstrationis regni Dei. Sacerdotium Aharonidarum & confessus ipso- rum ad discendam legem, & eam exercendam, post captivitatem Babylonicam est firmissima ἀπόδειξις adventus Christi cum eo connexi. Unde Willius ita accipit, quod ipsi sint signa instaurationis templi & Sacerdotii: & particulam כי in verbis seqq. Nam ecce ego adducturus sum servum meum germen, causam indicare vult, cur Josuam Sacerdotem often- tum vocarit, quia nempe ipse repræsentat Messiam, & verum Sacerdotem, quem Deus adducturus est. Ideo igitur Josua à sua persona colligere potest, Sacerdotium mansurum, quia ipse typus est æterni Sacerdotis. Ac videtur emphasis in adducendi vo- cabulo, quo innuere vult posse esse certum de con- tinuatione, quia nondum adsit antitypus ejus, sed primum adducendus sit.

Quarta ergo ratio erit συνέχεια textus, hoc modo expositi, desumta. Cornelius à Lapide allegat prò alli συνέχεια Hieronym. Remig. Haym. & Hugo- nem, viros portenti dictos, quia portendebant Chri- stum, qui futurus erat portentorum maximū por- tentum, germen sit lapis septioculus &c. & Cyril- lum: Quia cupiunt videre & audire res portentosas audiant portentum seculorum, nempe adduco ego servum meum orientem &c. Adde (5) quod è c. VI. 12. manifestum sit, non alium, quam Messiam per nomen צמח intelligi. Et (6) quod subjuncta pro- missio de lapide de Christo accipienda sit. Unde (7)

plerique Interpp. conveniunt, fermonem esse de Christo. Calvinus ipse, qui libenter alias vaticinia de Christo in alium sensum rapit, & de Christo hoc interpretatur, & rationes affert suae explicatio- nis non contemnendas; Non dubium est, inquit h. l. p. 623. quin significet Deus exercituum Sacerdo- tem, qui excellet supra communem sensum homi- num. Germen autem ideo vocatur, quia prodibit quasi surculus, ficuti dicitur II. cap. Jesaiae & aliis locis. Perinde est igitur, ac si diceret; Adhuc de- spicitur Sacerdotium hoc, tamen prodibit servus meus, h. e. Sacerdos, quemadmodum solet germen oriri è terra, deinde crescere: & צמח significat et- iam surculum. Comparat ergo Christum surculo, quia de nihilo, ut ita loquar, oriri visus est, propter- ea quod principium ejus contemptibile fuit. Quid enim obtinuit excellentiae Christus in mundo qui natus est? deinde quomodo auspicatus est regnum suum? & quomodo initiatus est suo Sacerdotio? Certe ludibrio scimus fuisse habitum, quicquid Pa- ter dederat honoris vel excellentiae: non mirum est igitur, si vocatur germen hac de causa. Nunc satis apparet ratio similitudinis. Etsi autem indefi- nite loquitur Angelus de Sacerdotibus, non du- bium tamen est, quin personam Christi interea de- signet. Quare? ab ipso eventu licet facere judici- um. Quisnam Sacerdos successit Jehosuae, qui ae- quaverit honorem ipsius, vel etiam, qui decima ex parte ad eum accesserit? Scimus plerosque fere o- mnes fuisse homines profanos & impios, scimus Sa- cerdotium inter ipsos fuisse vænale: scimus certas- se crudelissimis odiis, imo scimus in ipso templo jugulatum fuisse Sacerdotem, ita exarserat ambitio, ut non possent, nisi per sanguinem innoxium per- rumpere. Nihil ergo post mortem Jehosuae foe- dius, vel magis pudendum fuit Judaico Sacerdotio. Ubi ergo reperietur servus ille Dei germen? De- inde principium illud semper tenendum est, reno- vationem templi fuisse in Christi persona: necesse igitur est, ad ejus personam venire, ut habeamus servum hunc, cujus fit mentio. Nec vero haec tan- tum sensu mystico de Messia intelligenda; sed pro- prio & literali: Nam ut de Zorobabele intelligamus nulla suadet ratio: neque geminus in Scripturis ad- mittendus est sensus. Imo Judaei ipsi secundum li- teram, non solum mystice, de Christo interpretan- tur, uti è Jonathanis Targum liquet, qui loco vocis צמח adhibet nomen משיח.

## 3:9
Verse 9.

FOR BEHOLD THE STONE) By the stone he understands a small tin ball, hanging from a plumb line, which Zerubbabel, using it, was about to lay as the first stone upon those foundations cast under Cyrus, as Prince of the people. IV. 7. 8. 9. 10. To the Hebrews אבן is more general than lapis among the Latins, and signifies everything heavy: as Deut. VIII, 9.

WHOM I HAVE GIVEN) Whom I willed to be given into the hand of Zerubbabel. IV. 10.

UPON ONE STONE ARE SEVEN EYES) Signifying the ever-watchful providence of God that would be present for this work. IV, 10.

Coherence with the preceding compels one to understand by the STONE no other than the promised BRANCH, the Messiah. For he is pointed out by the name of stone not rarely in Is. XXVIII. 16. Dan. II. 34. Ps. CXVIII. 22. And he is said to be placed by God before Joshua, so that Joshua, as priest and teacher of the people, might have him before his eyes as the stone of foundation and corner I. Cor. III, 11. Eph. II. 20. I. Pet. II. 4. It designates, therefore, the foundation of the heavenly Jerusalem, the Church of God, which now after a notable dissipation was to be restored upon the foundational stone Christ, and that from the occasion of the foundation and structure of the temple: I. Cor. III. 11. inasmuch as all the rites of the Levitical Priests leaned upon it, and upon which the faithful of all times were bound to build Ephes. II. 20. Who is also given before Joshua, or exposed to his eyes, because Joshua acknowledged him, and believed in him; as Osiander explains, as also Danaeus. This Stone is said to be placed before Joshua and that whole Levitical order, and the entire Church itself, so that all may lean upon him, and look upon him as their only foundation. For the reason for Joshua is the same as for the Church, and Joshua is viewed as Priest and Doctor of the Church. Blessed Winckelmann is somewhat different. Before Jesus: That is, while the Levitical Priesthood still stood, which is now being restored in Joshua. Others understand this stone to have been placed before Joshua in a type, because God, who himself was the Architect, by placing the foundation stone of the temple in a type, thus testifies that he has placed the foundation of the Church: which that building of the temple shadowed forth the Church to be built upon the only foundation, besides which no one can lay another. Thus the Weimar Paraphrasts, as also the Belgian, who render the Hebrew words with Ludov. de Dieu: For behold, as regards the stone, which I have placed before Joshua, upon one stone are seven eyes. Some say this stone was placed before Joshua, because God showed Joshua through a vision the foundation stone of the temple, and revealed to him that Christ was represented by it. Thus Cornelius à Lapide with Lyranus, Hugo, Vatablus, Clarius, and others: The sense will be rendered not unsuitably enough: For see that stone, which I have placed before the face of Joshua (who himself is also a sign and a portent) upon one stone (namely that singular and only stone, which I shadowed forth in the building of the former temple Ps. CXIIX. 22. and again shadow forth in the foundation stone of this temple) there SHALL BE seven eyes. That stone will not be common, but clearly unique and admirable. For there will be upon it seven eyes etc. The first explanation, however, is simpler. For although these things were said on the occasion of the foundation of the second temple, they treat only of the mystical stone. Christ having now been placed in the place of the foundation, upon whom the Church is to be built up now anew after the Babylonian calamity and dispersion. To which also Blessed Luther goes T. IV. Jen. Germ. f. 259. Here the Prophet himself gives the allegory, or interpretation of the physical temple, and speaks of a spiritual building of the living temple. In which a very different stone is to be laid for a foundation, than in that one. It is to be a single stone. But in the physical temple many stones are laid. This stone is what Eph. 28 and Peter I. Epist. II. speak of: And God laid that same stone himself, not Joshua, nor Zerubbabel, for God builds this temple himself, as He speaks here, the stone, which I lay before the face of Joshua. For GOD already began to build the spiritual temple, because He let the physical temple be built for the sake of the spiritual: And besides that, such a spiritual building is before the face of Joshua, that is, before the face of the priesthood of Joshua. For Christ's temple and kingdom began when Joshua's lineage and priesthood still stood, by which it is indicated that Christ was to come before Joshua, and his lineage and priesthood perished. So that thus among Joshua's descendants, before their eyes this stone is laid, although they neither saw nor understood it, nay, even rejected Him for it.

Lyranus, Vatablus, Fernandes, Sanctius say that the seven eyes are separated from the stone, looking back at that stone, that they are Angels intent upon Christ, so that they may execute his will: Clarius and Arias, however, think it is God's providence toward Christ; others, the eyes of all Angels and men, especially the faithful, directed toward Christ, Blessed Balduinus, the eyes of the minds of Christians illuminated, who with true and perfect faith look upon and acknowledge Christ the mediator and savior of the world Eph. I. 18. Thus also Gualtherus, Coccejus, who willingly mixes apocalyptic things, understands the eyes of the faithful in the seven periods (which he feigned the Apocalypse to distinguish from the Prophets of the O.T.). But more correctly the seven eyes are attributed to the STONE Christ himself, (1) to denote his omniscience, and all-seeingness, because the number seven is of perfection, for nothing is hidden before his eyes. (2) To designate his providence, by which he looks out for all things in the Church, of which Lamb. Danaeus: Those seven eyes are attributed to him, by which he looks out for all the calamities and affairs of his Church, lest we think that stone to be blind and inert. (3) to indicate the sevenfold, i.e., manifold grace of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, as if to say, upon this stone I will pour out my Spirit without measure, so that adorned with the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit he may preside over his Church most excellently, most wisely, and most happily (being indeed most sharp-sighted). Thus Osiander, and the Belgian Paraphrasts, who hand down this explanation: In Christ are seven eyes, understand first the whole fullness of the Deity, then the abundance of spiritual gifts, and furthermore his full care and providence for the Church. The Weimar Paraphrasts and Tirinus combine the eyes, with which the foundation stone is adorned, and the eyes of the faithful looking back at Christ. But if the eyes of Christ, or in Christ are understood, the eyes of Christians looking back upon the stone, or directed into Christ, cannot be understood at the same time. But that the eyes of Christ are indicated is clear from a similar place Ap. V. 6, where St. John saw the lamb slain having seven horns, and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent into all the earth: Where as the horns, so also the eyes of Christ himself are understood, namely his divine power, and force by the horns, divine omniscience, and universal providence designated by the eyes, are those manifold gifts of the Spirit, with which he is instructed, and uses in the government of the whole earth, as one to whom all power has been given in heaven and on earth, therefore they are said to be sent into all the earth; Others add a similar place of this Prophet c. IV. 10. Those seven eyes are the Lord's, which run through the whole earth. Which is not badly, in our judgment, as far as the seven eyes are concerned, compared with this passage. Because as here the spiritual temple, the Church, is insinuated to be preserved and sustained by the power of the most watchful providence of Christ, so in chapter IV the preservation of the material temple is also committed to the seven eyes of Christ, that is, to his παντεποψίᾳ and providence, by whose office the structure of the temple had to be brought to its end and preserved against all insults up to the end of the Jewish Polity. Some also compare here the Cherubim of Ezekiel ch. I. 18 and of John in the Apocalypse IV. 8, full of eyes, and the wheels of the Cherubic chariot Ez. I. 18, by which the action of divine providence is represented, and its most watchful and attentive exertion. The ancients, Jerome, Haymo, Remigius, Dionysius and others, also interpret this vision concerning the eyes of Christ himself, understanding the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which render the soul of Christ watchful. Gregory the Great, book XXIX. Moral. ch. XVI. upon one stone are seven eyes. For for this stone (Christ) to have seven eyes is at the same time to retain every power of the Spirit of sevenfold grace in operation. For one receives prophecy, another knowledge, another miracles, another kinds of tongues, another interpretations of speeches according to the distribution of the Holy Spirit: but no one attains to having all the gifts of the same Spirit. But truly our creator, looking upon our infirmities, because he taught that he himself possesses all the powers of the Holy Spirit at the same time by the power of his divinity, has joined the shining Pleiades without a doubt. From our own, B. Winckelmann explains the seven eyes as the sevenfold gift of the Holy Spirit, because Christ as man receives the Spirit without measure (the seven gifts of the Spirit, or the perfection of all gifts,) and from him the charisms of the Spirit overflow into the Church. B. Tarnovius comments thus on p. 93. Lest anyone think, if the Messiah is the branch, his kingdom will be fragile, behold, (which are God's words about Christ) the promised Messiah is that stone, upon which the Church is built, a stone of refuge for the pious, and a stone of stumbling by their own fault for the impious Is. 8, 14. and 28, 16. Ps. 118, 22. I. Pet. 2, 7. which I firmly place before Joshua, that is, in the Church, where he bears the type of Christ, and I place it so that there are seven eyes upon that one stone, applying to it most perfectly the most absolute providence, as below in chapter IV. 10. since in the style of the Scriptures (the analogy of which it is easy to prove) eyes denote providence, and the number seven denotes perfection, and therefore I shall not easily concede to the opinion of those who understand by the eyes in this place either the Doctors of the Church or Angels, or the faith of the pious and believers, since the Prophet speaks of the eyes of the stone itself, not of any creature, nor can the analogy of Scripture be easily shown. Corn. à Lapide acknowledges here that the eyes of Christ, through which he himself looks around, surveys, protects, cares for, and promotes the whole fabric of the Church, are understood, and yet he wishes the seven primary angels to be indicated by the seven eyes, adding moreover, as is his custom, many other senses, tropological, allegorical, and symbolic. Christoph à Castro thinks that those explain them more pleasantly and elegantly who say that the stone is ocellated, or distinguished by multiple eyes, taking the metaphor from garments most beautifully elaborated with Phrygian work, as if with certain eyes woven in, and he thinks that Christ the stone was so elaborated and distinguished by various carvings that it was full of eyes, and that by this is signified the variety of graces, virtues, and gifts bestowed upon him, according to that which follows, I will engrave its sculpture, or certainly that it is said of the welts and wounds, by which as if by certain eyes the body of Christ was distinguished and adorned with most beautiful variety: which sense he prefers in his paraphrase. But the one we have given from the Fathers, which Menochius also brought forward, is simpler and more convenient to the phrase of Scripture: In one stone seven eyes engraved signify the full and perfect providence and vigilance of Christ, concerning the erecting, increasing, promoting, and preserving of the fabric of his temple, that is, his Church: although others may prefer to understand it of the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, which illuminate the soul and render it in a certain way eyed. Castrius likewise praised this double explanation: Those who accept the eyes as implanted in the stone itself, as if in a head, Jerome, Haymo, Remigius, Lyra, Dionysius, and Vatablus explain them as the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which render the soul eyed and illustrious: thus the soul of Christ is illuminated and rendered eyed. Others think it is the supreme providence and protection of Christ, by which he looks out for his spouse the Church, as it is said in 2 Chron. 16, 9: The eyes of the Lord contemplate the whole earth. But they can be conveniently joined, as we warned before: because Christ is so adorned with the gifts of the Holy Spirit that he looks upon all things most keenly, and looks out for his Church above all. For he received the gifts of the Spirit for that purpose οὐκ ἐκ μέτρου not by measure John III. 34. If anyone, however, prefers with B. Balduinus to understand by the eyes the faithful built into Christ, especially the Doctors, because Scripture calls Doctors eyes I. Cor. XII. 16. 17. he will have Luther as a predecessor in Vol. IV. Jen. Germ. on this passage. Grotius's gloss, that a tin globule hanging from a plumb line, which Joshua held in his hand, is understood, distinguished by eyes designating the providence of God, taken from Lyranus, deserves no consideration. For how will it be proven that there is talk of a tin plumb stone? The passage Zech. IV. 10 is clearly alien. THERE A STONE OF TIN is expressly expressed, and is designated by such a periphrasis, which is IN THE HAND OF ZERUBBABEL. But here there is nothing about a stone OF TIN. Nor is there talk of Zerubbabel, but of Joshua, nor is that stone said to be in his hand, but given or placed before Joshua. Furthermore, it is a question here of a singular stone, which is called ONE placed before Joshua, in which are seven eyes. Therefore these things cannot be snatched away to that common stone of a plumb line. And how was the stone of tin, or of the plumb line, eyed, or how do the eyes on it designate the providence of God over it, or over the fabric of the temple? For if eyes were impressed on the stone, they noted something on the stone, but not the eyes of the Lord intent upon the stone.
