Singularis in hac promissione κατά πάντα est Balt. Willius: quod etiam passim in commentis ejus observare licet. Non enim placent ipsi communia, ideoque subinde nova excogitavit gloffemata, me- ro singularitatis studio. Agnoscit hos versus ab o- mnibus sere Interpp. de Christo lapide angulari Ec- clesiæ explicari : Hunc tamen sensum communem ex- agitatur : neque parcit Magistri sui Calvini interpre- tationi: Oculos hos septem vel per delirium Scholasti- corum de septiformi gratia, vel de abundantia Spiri- tus in persona Messiæ explicari ait. Sed ejusmodi lo- quendi ratio, ipso sc. judice, in Scriptura plane inu- sitata est, atque æque inconcinna interpretatio eorum, qui oculos hos de fidelium multitudine ad Christum re- spiciente accipiunt : & ejusdem farinæ esse ait, quod Calvinus de lapidis oculis oculos exponit, q. d. lapidem non conversurum tantum ad se aliorum oculos, sed a- lios illuminaturum & splendorem emissurum, qui pos- sit suo reflexu dirigere homines ad conspectum ejus. Abhorrere enim à more loquendi in Scriptura, nec probabilitatem ullam ex loco parallelo aliquo habere.

Porro sculpturam lapidis plerosque veterum & Hie- ronymum de vulneribus Christi futili argutia inter- pretari, cum Calvino, facile judicat. Ipse vero to- tius loci hunc reddit sensum: Ostento sunt socii tui penes te cum cura sua & labore, quem enim ipsi posue- runt lapidem angularem, hunc ego ipse posui, quam ipsi curam in templi structura & ornatu adhibent, hæc mea cura est, qua ædificii illius accuratissimam ra- tionem habeo, illudque exornare cogito, ita, ut simul omnes hostium cogitationes & machinationes contra- rias pessundem, vosque quiete & pace altissima exhi- barem. Sed vere futilis & insulsa est hæc glossa no- viter à Willio excogitata. Nam (1.) nihil de sociis Josuæ in his verbis: nec ob precariam ἀναλυσιν Willii, quam animo suo præconcepit, illi huic in- serendi textui (2) Ostento esse socios Josuæ cum ipso, cum cura, & labore suo, vel in eo, quod lapidem, quem ipsi posuerint, Deus ipse posuerit, è textu exsculpi haud potest. Licet enim Josuam cum so- ciis viros portenti hoc etiam sensu esse concedatur, quantum ad restaurationem templi & Sacerdotii, hoc tamen de iisdem habendum, non tam ideo, quod in iis significata continuatio ædificationis tem- pli, & reparationis Sacerdotii, quam quod hoc opere significaverint restaurationem Ecclesiæ & sacerdotium verum Novi Testamenti, uti Castrius observat, cum Synchronis & amicis, Haggao, Zacharia, Mala- chia, Anania, Azaria, Misaele & Daniele, viros portenti secundum sensum communem Hierony- mi, Haimonis, Remigii &c. dictos, quod futura sub N. Test. suis personis, gestisque portenderint. Quam- vis alii alias tradant appellationis istius causas. Ob id certe solum, quod Deus per Josuam & socios tem- plum ædificet, viri portenti hic non dicuntur. (3) Neque oculi septem super lapide unico intelligendi oculi providentiæ Domini super materiali lapide in templi structura. Nam oculi IN lapide, & quidem in UNICO illo singulari lapide indigitantur, non oculi directi in lapidem, oculi, inquam, lapidis, non oculi providentiæ divinæ. (4) Neque sculpturus sculpturam lapidis Dominus dicitur, hoc sensu, quod ornatus ipse sit templum materiale. Sensus ille mere precarius est, & communi fere consensu Interpp. reprobatur. Etiamsi similis phrasis de ornatu lapi- dum adhiberi videatur, Exod. XXXIIX. vers. 11. 36. XXXIX. v. 6. Chron. II. 6. 13. hic tamen de lapide materiali sermonem esse gratis assumitur. Et num unicus tantum lapis in structura templi ornatus fuit? Quid ergo illa hic sibi volunt de unico lapide? (5) Non de hostium cogitationibus & molitioni- bus in impedienda templi structura pessundandis, nec de quiete & pace temporali, sed de anferenda iniquitate terræ, & de tranquillitate ac pace spiri- tuali, quæ ablationis peccati consequens est, sermo est. (6) Quomodo UNA DIE ablata est terræ iniquitas, nisi dies passionis & mortis Dominicæ intelligatur, cum plerisque Interpp. (7) Quid quod Willius ipse agnoscat verba die illo vocabit quisque amicum suum sub vitem & sub ficum, altam Evan- gelii pacem, quam pax Salomonis figuravit, notare, idque ex Mich. IV. 4. patescere, imo mystica hic ha- beri expresse textum arguere, ac mysterii revelan- di causa phrasin illam de die N. T. adhibitam vi- deri fateatur, cur ergo sensum illum exagitat? (8) Non est, quod in sensu aut nexu verborum, juxta communem interpretationem, quicquam deside- ret Willius: Quis sensus ille, inquit, si Christum la- pidem dicas: Ecce Christus, quem pono coram providētia mea, ornatur & curatur? Quis nexus, aut quæ declaratio: adduco servum meum germen, quia lapis, id est, Christus ille coram Josua à me curatur? Resp. Sensus recte se habet, sive lapidē dicas Josuæ peculiariter significatum, aut figuratum, aut co- ram Josua in typo positum intelligas, sive post Jo- suam fequuturum, ut alii phrasin exponunt, sive etiam lapidem materialem, ceu signum illius lapidis UNICI, super quo septem futuri sunt oculi, Chri- sti nempe accipias, & primo loco lapis materialis (Signum) altero lapis spiritualis, qui lapis unicus & singularis dicitur vere μονότροπος (signatum) in- telligatur. Non autem providentiam Dei per o- culos septem, sed dona multiformia Christi, nec ornatus lapidis per cælaturam designari, sed pas- sionem Christi, antea monitum. Quam explicatio- nem apprime cohærere cum promissione de ad- ducendo germine, servo Dei justo, nemo non intelli- git. Hoc enim lapide fundamentali signatus in- struendus Spiritus S. donis, Ecclesiæ curam gerere, & in fundamentum Ecclesiæ poni debuit, cælatus probe à Domino in passione, qua expianda peccata totius mundi, ut solida pace ac tranquillitate frue- remur. Neque juvat Willium locus Zach. IV. 10. Nam ibi septem oculos de providentia Dei intelligi, sine fundamento assumsit Willius.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. The fifth vision of the golden lampstand and the two olive trees.

The prophet, awakened by the angel, sees a golden lampstand with seven lamps and two olive trees, and is informed about that vision, that by the power of the Spirit Zerubbabel is to build the temple, and that two sons, a double lineage anointed with oil, shall not be lacking for the temple and the worship of the Lord of the whole earth, such as were Zerubbabel the prince and Joshua the High Priest.

Zerubbabel, though destitute, founds huge walls.

Ver. 1.

WHO WAS SPEAKING IN ME) To me, as above several times, so also below 5.

THERE is no need to believe that the preposition was placed in vain; rather, an interior inspiration of the angel is noted, and that angel is not Michael or any other of the created beings: But the Son of God, as shown above, who in verse 8 is called LORD, sent by the Lord. Compare ch. II. 11. The angel's address follows: AND HE SAID TO ME, WHAT DO YOU SEE? and according to the Qere the response of the Prophet: AND I SAID, I SEE, AND BEHOLD A LAMPSTAND &c. just as the LXX, the Chaldean, the Vulgate, B. Luther, and other interpreters have rendered it. According to the Kethiv, however, it is held thus: AND HE SAID, which Ludov. de Dieu thinks should be retained: so that the angel himself answers and explains that vision, just as below in chapter V. 5, 6, when the Prophet had been ordered to see what was coming forth, and did not recognize it, the angel himself answered what it was that was coming forth.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. Quinta visio aurei candelabri & dua- rum olearum.

Propheta ab angelo excitatus videt aureum candelabrum, cum septem lucernis & duabus olivis, & informatur de ea visio- ne, quod virtute Spiritus Zorobabel tem- plum exstructurus, atque duo filii, du- plex oleo unctum genus templo & cultui Dominatoris universæ terræ non sint de- futuri, quales erant Zorobabel princeps, & Josua Pontifex.

Zorobabelus inops ingentia mœnia fundat.

Vers. 1.

QVI LOQVEBATUR IN ME) Mihi, ut supra aliquoties, sic & infra 5.

NON est opus, ut frustra positam præpositio- nem credamus, immo notatur interior angeli inspiratio, estque angelus ille non Michael aut a- lius aliquis è creatis: Sed Filius Dei, ut supra osten- sum, qui vers. 8. DOMINUS dicitur à Domino missus. Conf. c. II. 11. Sequitur angeli alloquium: ET DIXIT AD ME, QUÆ VIDES? & juxta τὸ כרי responsum Prophetæ: ET DIXI, VIDEO, ET ECCE CANDELABRUM &c. quemadmodum LXX. Chaldæus, Vulgatus, B. Lu- therus & alii Interpp. reddidere. Juxta τὸ כתיב autem ita habetur: ET DIXIT, quod retinen- dum censet Ludov. de Dieu: ut angelus ipse respondeat, atque visionem illam enarret, quem- admodum infra cap. V. 5. 6. quum jussus esset Pro- pheta videre quid exiret, neque id agnosceret, angelus ipse respondit, quid esset, quod exiret.

## 4:2
Ver. 2.

A GOLDEN LAMPSTAND ENTIRELY) The magnificent work of the temple.

AND ITS LAMP UPON ITS HEAD) גלה is a λήκυθος, an oil flask, which this interpreter called a small lens elsewhere, from the similarity of form, which meaning of this word is noted also by Pliny XXXVII. 12. It is, however, an enallage of number, for he said flask for two flasks. Below 12.

AND ITS SEVEN LAMPS UPON IT) In it.

AND SEVEN FUNNELS) Funnels, through which oil flowed from the flasks into the seven lamps.

WHICH WERE UPON ITS HEAD) Which were at the top of the lampstand.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CANDELABRVM AUREUM TOTUM) Magnifi- cum opus templi.

ET LAMPAS EJUS SUPER CAPVT IPSIVS) גלה est λήκυθος, ampulla olearia, quam lenticulam ali- bi dixit hic interpres, à formæ similitudine, quæ vocis hu- jus significatio notata & Plinio XXXVII. 12. est autem enallage numeri, ampullam enim dixit pro ampullis dua- bus. Infra 12.

ET SEPTEM LUCERNÆ EJVS SVPER ILLUD) In eo.

ET SEPTEM INFUSORIA) Infundibula, per quæ de ampullis oleum in septem lucernas fluebat.

QUÆ ERANT SUPER CAPVT EJUS) Quæ erant in summo candelabro.

## 4:3
AND TWO OLIVE TREES UPON IT) Trees dripping oil into the flasks. These signified that both princes and priests would always exist for the protection of the Temple, which is to be understood as lasting until the coming of the Messiah according to the prophecy of Jacob, with divine grace administering things in this way, below VI, 14.

ONE AT THE RIGHT OF THE LAMP) At the right flask.

AND ONE AT ITS LEFT) At that left one, namely the flask: he speaks as if he were pointing out the thing with his finger.

We do not disapprove of this explanation of the vision. And not only do the Hebrews understand Zerubbabel the Prince and Joshua the priest by the two sons of the olive tree: but almost all Christian interpreters agree, except perhaps Calvin and Junius, whom Willius has followed here, and Tarnovius among our own. Calvin understands it generally, as if God wished to explain to the Jews why He had commanded the lampstand to be placed in the middle of the temple, namely to make it testified that the grace of His Spirit always shines in the Church, and not of one kind only, but in such a way that nothing was lacking for perfection; and he does not even approve of that which others say, that Doctors are represented by the lamps, whom he says he argues are philosophizing, although he cannot deny that God pours out His graces to illuminate the Church through ministers. But this vision is without doubt special, pertaining to Zechariah and the times that were to follow, not merely a typical illustration of the lampstand once placed in the middle of the temple. It is certain that the lampstand in the temple had its own special significance, and there is no doubt that God wished to adumbrate the illumination of the Holy Spirit and the influx of divine grace into the Church in that way, just as all the shadows and figures of the Old Testament had their own significance. But that God here wished only to explain what those things signified in the past is in no way made probable. Wherefore others more correctly teach that the restoration of the temple and the sacred ministry to be carried out by Zerubbabel and Joshua is adumbrated in this vision, and indeed not of the material temple, but primarily of the Church, for whose sake the temple was to be repaired, and we acknowledge that its conversation and perfection under the Princes and Priests of the Lord's people were figured until the coming of Christ. Which are not opposed, but subordinated. For the temple was being restored for the sake of the Church, of whose restoration and success of the work, however, this people of the Lord, and Zerubbabel himself, had to be confirmed. Willius therefore wrongly opposes them to each other: that the temple is denoted by the lampstand is the opinion of some: but I prefer to take the lampstand as a type of the whole Church then, because not only the restoration of the temple, but also the protection of the whole visible Church is promised to the political prince. The reason for the type is taken from the office of the Church, which, just as it has the oracles of God entrusted to it, so it presents the same to its members, and proposes them to be seen and considered for the illumination of souls, just as the lampstand supports the light and exhibits its use and light to others. These are his words, from which it appears that he himself acknowledged that the restoration of the temple was adumbrated here. Therefore it is not only a figure that is exhibited concerning the continuous influx of God's graces into the Church. The Belgian interpreters teach that this is the meaning of that vision, that this beautiful golden lampstand (formed without the hand of men) adumbrates that the temple is to be fully built, so that the golden lampstand may be inserted into it, just as the golden lampstand was once placed in the middle of the temple. Similarly Castrius p. 450. It will be better to explain the whole chapter concerning the present matter to the Prophet himself; since the words properly taken can be rightly accommodated to him. Therefore, just as in the previous chapter JESUS was encouraged when he was clothed in priestly garments, so that he would not fear Satan in any way, so now Zerubbabel is encouraged

Willius here invents a significative phrase, as in the Sacraments: This is the word of the Lord: that is, this lampstand signifies the word of the Lord, or the promise made to Zerubbabel: but absurdly: For who is ignorant of what those words mean: This is the word of the Lord: Thus says the Lord: It is strange that in such obvious and common words a clearly unusual meaning is invented, which does not easily come to anyone's mind. But what do the Sacramentarians not invent, so that they may encrust their sacramental or significative IS? What meaning, pray, will finally be carved out of these words of the Lord? Not by an army nor by strength, but by my spirit, says the Lord. The plain sense is that which almost all interpreters have handed down; that this is said to Zerubbabel: You shall build the temple, and you shall duly establish the ministry of the word, nor will you have need of external power for that matter, to repress with an army the attempts of those who wish to hinder my temple and worship: I will advance the work by my spirit. Thus the blessed Wigandus: The angel says: there is no need of an army, no need of external force against enemies to complete the building in tranquility: that God will assist these attempts with His Spirit, and will give them rest. And so also the Belgian interpreters. But other Sacramentarians seek a mystical meaning in this way: Junius: Just as no human art and no forces are applied to the lampstand and those instruments, whether in making and establishing them or in maintaining them, but God made them by His Spirit, and maintains them from above through the same Spirit: so also my people and my Church have been restored by no human counsel or strength, and will be maintained and preserved henceforth, not even by their own efforts or those of their leaders, but by the sole power of my spirit. Willius likes that, but he thinks he has devised a more convenient meaning. Beautiful, he says. Perhaps, however, it will be even more suitable to the purpose if the application is made in this way: Just as you see that lampstand receiving the nourishment of its lamps from above through the olive trees and their berries, and being nourished from there: so that Church of mine is nourished, strengthened, and takes strength and increase through my grace and spirit, as its oil. But who would either seek or find the Junian or Willian Sacrament in these very words, Not by an army nor by strength, but by my Spirit, says the Lord? It is too manifest that there is nothing in these words about the manufacture of the lampstand, nothing about the heavenly influx into the lampstand: that only the scope of the vision is presented, which was directed to this end, that Zerubbabel might be made more certain that the structure of the temple would be finished with its adornment, with the Lord advancing that work by His Spirit even against external force, in which, if anyone places a type of the divine preservation and protection of the Church, we are so far from denying it, that we concede that for its sake the temple was to be restored with its adornment, so that indeed the Church might be preserved, since the Lord rules and covers it with His Spirit. We only deny that these words of the angel explain the figure and likeness of the manufacture and influx of the lampstand, which only indicate the scope of the vision in a general way. But what the golden lampstand specifically shadowed forth, they do not explain with their fathers. Which must be learned from elsewhere, whether you look at the lampstand represented here, or that which was used in the tabernacle and the former temple.

Latin:

ET DUÆ OLIVÆ SVPER ILLVD) Arbores stil- lantes oleum in ampullas. Significabant hæ, semper & principes & sacerdotes futuros ad Templi tutelam, quod intelligendum ad Messiæ usque adventum ex vaticinio Ja- cobi, divina gratia ita res administrante infra VI, 14.

UNA A DEXTRIS LAMPADIS) Ad dextram am- pullam.

ET UNA A SINISTRIS EJVS) Ad sinistram illam, scilicet ampullam: loquitur quasi rem digito monstraret.

Non improbamus hanc visionis explicationem. Nec Ebræi solum per duos filios oleæ Zerubabelem Principem, & Josuam sacerdotem intelligunt: Sed consentiunt fere omnes Interpp. Christiani, exce- pto forte Calvino, & Junio, quos hic sequutus est Willius, & e nostris Tarnovius. Calvinus intelligit generaliter, quasi explicare voluerit Deus Judæis, cur in medio templi præceperit, candelabrum po- ni, ut nempe testatum faceret semper in Ecclesia lucere Spiritus sui gratiam, nec unius tantum ge- neris, sed ita, ut nihil ad perfectionem deesset, ac ne illud quidem probat, quod alii dicunt, per lu- cernas Doctores repræsentari, quos arguere philosopha- ri ait, quamvis negare non possit, Deum infundere suas gratias, ut Ecclesiam illuminet per ministros. Sed speciale sine dubio hoc visum est, ad Zachariæ, & sequutura tempora pertinens, non solum illustra- tio typica candelabri olim in templi medio collo- cati. Certum id est, candelabrum in templo ha- buisse suam specialem significationem, neque du- bium, illuminationem Sp. S. & gratiæ divinæ in- fluxum in Ecclesiam ita adumbrare olim voluisse Deum; uti omnes umbræ & figuræ V. T. suam ha- buere significationem. At Deum hic solum explica- re voluisse, quid olim ista significabant, nullo modo fit verisimile. Quapropter rectius alii instauratio- nem templi & ministerii sacri per Zorobabelem & Josuam peragendam in hac visione adumbrari do- cent, & quidem non templi materialis, sed impri- mis Ecclesiæ, cujus gratia templum reparandum e- rat, ejusdem conversationem & perfectionem sub Principibus & Sacerdotibus populi Domini figu- ratam esse, usque ad Christi adventum, agnosci- mus. Quæ non opposita sunt, sed subordinata. Nam propter Ecclesiam restaurabatur templum, de cujus tamen restauratione ac successu operis confirmandus erat hic populus Domini, & Zoro- babel ipse. Perperam ergo illa sibi opponit Wil- lius: per candelabrum templum denotari, quorundam sententia est: Malo autem pro typo totius Ecclesiæ tunc lychnuchum accipere, quia non modo templi in- stauratio, sed totius quoque Ecclesiæ visibilis protectio, principi politico promittitur. Ratio typi ab officio Ec- clesiæ desumta est, quæ, uti concredita habet eloquia Dei, ita eadem membris suis præfert, & conspicienda ac consideranda ad animorum illuminationem propo- nit, non secus candelabrum lumen sustinet, ejus- que usum & lucem aliis exhibet. Hæc ille, un- de apparet, quod agnoverit ipse templi restaura- tionem hic adumbratam esse. Non ergo figura tan- tum exhibetur, de continuo gratiarum Dei in Eccle- siam influxu. Belgici Interpp. hanc visionis istius si- gnificationem esse docent, quod pulchrum istud candelabrum aureum (sine manu hominum forma- tum) adumbret, templum plene extruendum esse, ut aureum candelabrum eidem inseratur, quemadmo- dum olim in medio templi aureum candelabrum positum fuit. Similiter Castrius p. 450. Satius erit universum caput de re præsenti ipsi Prophetæ ex- planare; cum verba proprie accepta possint re- cte illi accommodari. Sicut ergo in superio- ri capite animatus est JESUS, cum induere- tur vestes sacerdotales, ne Satanam ullo mo- do timeret, ita modo animatur Zorobabel

Phrasin significativam hic singit, ut in Sacramen- tis, Willius: Hoc est verbum Domini: id est, hoc can- delabrum significat verbum Domini, vel promissio- nem Zorobabeli factam: sed inepte: Nam quis i- gnorat, quid illa sibi velint: Hoc est verbum Domi- ni: Sic inquit Dominus: Mirum in tam obviis & u- sitatis singi sensum plane inusitatum, qui non faci- le ulli in mentem venit. Sed quid non singunt Sa- cramentarii, ut suum EST sacramentale vel signi- ficativum incrustent? Quænam vero tandem ex his verbis Domini exsculpetur significatio? Non in exercitu neque robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Do- minus. Sensus planus est, quem Interpp. fere omnes tradidere; quod hoc dicatur Zorobabeli: Tu ædifi- cabis templum, & ministerium verbi rite constitues, nec ad eam rem opus tibi erit externa potentia, ut eo- rum conatus exercitu reprimas, qui templum meũ & cultum impeditum volunt: ego spiritu meo opus provebam. Sic B. Wigandus: Angelus inquit: non opus esse exercitu, non vi externa contra hostes ad ædificium in tranquillitate perficiendum: Deum Spiritu suo hos conatus adjuturum esse, & ipsis quietem daturum. Atque ita etiam Interpp. Belgici. At alii sacramentarii significationem mysticam ita quærunt: Junius: Quemadmodum lychnucho & in- strumentis illis sive faciendis & constituendis, sive curandis, nulla ars humana, nullaque vires adhiben- tur, sed Deus Spiritu fecit, & superne curat per eun- dem Spiritum: ita etiam populus meus & Ecclesia mea nullo humano consilio, aut viribus restitutus est, cu- rabiturque & conservabitur porro, ne sua quidem aut ducum suorum opera, sed unica virtute spiritus mei. Placet id Willio, sed commodiorem tamen se excogitasse putat significationem. Pulchre, inquit. Forte tamen adhuc convenientius erit instituto, si hoc modo fiat applicatio: Quemadmodum vides, cande- labrum illud superne per oleas & baccas earum ali- mentum suarum lucernarum concipere, ac inde nu- triri: ita Ecclesia illa mea per gratiam & spiritum meum, ut oleum suum, nutritur, confirmatur, & vi- res ac incrementa sumit. At quis vel Junianum, vel Willianum Sacramentum in istis quidem verbis aut quæreret, aut inveniret, non in exercitu neque in robore, sed in Spiritu meo dicit Dominus? Nimis manifestum est, nihil in istis verbis haberi de lych- nuchi fabrica, nihil de influxu superno in lychnu- chum: scopum tantum exhiberi visionis, quæ eo di- recta, ut certior redderetur Zorobabel, finitum iri structuram templi cum ornatu, Domino Spiritu suo opus illud etiam contra externam vim prove- hente, in quo, si typum quis collocet divinæ conser- vationis & protectionis Ecclesiæ, tantum abest, ut abnuamus, ut ejus causa templum cum ornatu suo restaurandum fuisse, concedamus, ut nempe con- servaretur Ecclesia, quumSpiritu suo regit ac tegit Dominus. Id solum negamus, hæc verba angeli, explicare figuram & similitudinem fabricæ & in- fluxus lychnuchi, quæ scopum visionis generatim solum indicant. Quid autem speciatim adumbraret candelabrum aureum, cum suis patribus, non ex- plicant. Quod aliunde discendum, sive respicias hic repræsentatum candelabrum, sive quod in ta- bernaculo & templo priori adhibitum fuit.

## 4:6
Vers. 6. THIS IS THE WORD OF THE LORD TO ZERUBBABEL; NOT BY AN ARMY, NOR BY STRENGTH, BUT BY MY SPIRIT) Your resources will indeed be meager, but God will breathe His power into you, and will protect the Temple. No obscure image of Christ is in this.

Others interpret it concerning the humiliation of the Persians, because the Jews had them favorable in the building of the temple. But the Blessed Luther wishes this very conciliation of the mind of the Persian Monarch and his favor to be insinuated here f. 262. My Spirit shall do it, He shall strengthen you with yours, and shall give the King of Persia a gracious mind for this, that He may let you build in peace, and help you furthermore with all his captains. Osiander explains it generally: You, Zerubbabel, seem to yourself now to have before your eyes a mountain high and great, (while you build the temple, and establish the ministry of divine worship) and that mountain appears to you higher than that you can cross it, especially when you think how great impediments occurred before under Cambyses, but I will bring that mountain into a plain, and I will make the thing, which seems most difficult to you, easy and expedited: You think, you have a great mountain before you, but be comforted, I will make it all fine and right. Interpreters. The Belgian [interpreters] think that Sanballat and other enemies of the people of the Lord are denoted, Ezra III, IV, V. But it pleased Grotius to understand these things concerning past events. But truly it is more likely that the Prophet wished to meet the temptations by which Zerubbabel was then solicited, therefore it is better with B. Luther to understand it of the Persian Court, in which without doubt many not so favorable were still found, and of any other enemies whom Zerubbabel could fear.

Verse of the same.

Latin:

Vers. 6. HOC EST VERBVM DOMINI AD ZERU- BABELEM; NON IN EXERCITU, NEC IN ROBO- RE, SED IN SPIRITU MEO) Opes quidem vestræ te- nues erunt, sed Deus vim suam vobis adspirabit, Templum- que proteget, Haud obscura Christi in hoc imago.

Alii de Persarum humliatione interpretantur, quod Judæi in templo extruendo faventes eos ha- buerint. At B. Lutherus hanc ipsam animi Monar- chæ Persici conciliationem & gratiam ejusdem hic insinuari vult f. 262. Mein Geist soll es thun, der soll dich stärcken mit den Deinen, und soll dem König zu Persen einen gnädigen Sinn darzu geben, daß Er euch mit frieden bauen lasse, und euch noch dar- zu helffe mit allen seinen Hauptleuthen. Osiander generatim explicat: Tu Zorobabel videris tibi nunc ante oculos habere montem excelsum & grandem, (dum templum ædificas, & ministerium cultus di- vini constituis) & altior ille mons tibi apparet, quã ut eum transcendere possis, præsertim cum cogitas quanta impedimenta antea sub Cambyse incide- rint, at ego illum montem in planum deducam, & rem, quæ tibi difficillima videtur, facilem atque expeditam dabo: Du meinest, du hast einen gros- sen Berg vor dir, aber sey getrost, ich will es alles fein richtig machen. Interpp. Belgici denotari pu- tant Saneballat & alios hostes populi Domini Esdr. III. IV. V. Grotio autem placuit de præteritis rebus hæc acccipere. At vero est similius Prophetam vo- luisse occurrere tentationibus, quibus Zorobabel tunc solicitabatur, ideo præstat cum B. Luthero de Aula Persica, in qua sine dubio adhuc multi non ad- eo faventes reperti, & de aliis quibusvis hostibus intelligere, quos metuere poterat Zorobabel.

Vers. eod.

## 4:7
Verse 7. WHO ARE YOU, O GREAT MOUNTAIN BEFORE ZERUBBABEL?) Who are you? (O Babylon) you were a great mountain before Zerubbabel: your empire was huge, compared to that of Zerubbabel.

supplying oil and help to God through His prophets, so that he might fear no one would hinder the work of the temple, but would happily complete it himself. Thus Theodoret, Remigius, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, and Montanus explain it. The explanation of our own people also tends to this, although, as we have previously professed, that form of the lampstand, both as it was described in the first temple and as it was figured here to Zechariah, has a spiritual meaning regarding its parts, and designates the influx of grace into the Church, which the Lord at the same time shadows forth and promises here. Which meaning our people have not neglected: For by the golden lampstand the Church is figured, just as the Son of God was seen walking in the midst of the seven golden lampstands, or seven churches, as in Rev. 20, the added explanation is, the seven lampstands are the seven churches. Gold denotes the purity and constancy of the Saints, who constitute the Church: because gold is the purest metal, and such that it does not yield even to fire, Ps. 45:10, 15. The vial or oil-vessel at its top designates Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom, Col. 2:3, the fountain of all grace, from whose fullness we all receive grace for grace, John 1:16. The seven lamps denote the ministers and Doctors of the Church, who, like a lamp, ought to shine before others with the light of doctrine and life, John 5:35. The individual lamps have individual little vessels, or funnels, by which oil is communicated and poured into them: because by the nourishing oil of the Holy Spirit or His gifts those spiritual lamps are, so that their light may not be extinguished. But Ribera is absurd, who invents that the seven sacraments are designated by the seven funnels. The blessed Luther thus exhibits the figure of the lampstand in his German Commentary, Vol. IV, Jena, f. 262. But this vision of this golden lampstand is shaped a little differently than Moses's lampstand in Exod. 25. Moses's lampstand has pipes on the side out from the shaft or stock etc. But this one stands straight up with its shaft, and has on top a round, large, wide plate or bowl, which I have translated as a rim, and on that same plate around about seven lamps in a ring, which have all burned and shone, and so that the light would not go out for lack of oil, there are seven vessels, or pipes, which are full of oil, always to follow. For we cannot know what kind of shape those same vessels had, whether they were like little pots or little cans, or pipes. One poured oil with them into the lamps, that is enough for us, whether they were like cans or pitchers or not, and all of pure gold. It also reads in the Hebrew that there were more than seven of those same funnels, for the text stands thus: Septem & septem infusoria pro lucernis, that is, seven and seven funnels for the lamps. That sounds almost as if seven funnels belonged to every single lamp, to indicate that the lamps are most abundantly supplied with oil, and there is no concern that they might go out. Duæ olivæ, vel filii oleæ, qui assistunt dominatori terræ sunt illi, qui Spiritu S. uncti sunt ad tutelam & gubernationem Ecclesiæ, quales Zorobabel, & Josua erant: quorum uterque in sua vocatione ministerium sacrum summo studio promovebat, ita ut essent instar olearum, quæ oleum proferunt ad alendum lumen in lucernis.

IN PLANVM) Supply, you have been cast down by Cyrus. He alludes to the name of Zerubbabel, which had been given to him as a good omen, signifying that Babylon would be dispersed: at the same time he hints that the same thing would happen to others who would oppose themselves to the people of God.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVIS TV MONS MAGNE CORAM ZORO- BABELÉ?) Quid tu? (O Babylon) mons erat magnus præ Zorobabele: ingens tuum erat imperium, præ isto Zoro- babelis.

subministrante oleum & opem Deo per suos Pro- phetas, ne quemquam opus templi metueret impe- diturum, sed feliciter ipsum confecturum. Sic ex- plicant Theodoretus, Remigius, Albertus, Hugo, Ly- ra, Dionysius & Montanus. Eo etiam explicatio abit nostratium, etsi, quod antea professi sumus, illa candelabri forma, cum prout in primo templo de- scripta, tum quatenus Zachariæ hic figurata, spiri- tualem significationem, quoad partes suas habeat, & gratiæ influxum in Ecclesiam, quem simul hic adumbrat, ac pollicetur Dominus, designet. Quam significationem non neglexere nostri: Per cande- labrum autem aureum Ecclesia figuratur, quemad- modum Filius Dei visus in medio septem candela- brorum aureorum, vel septemEcclesiarum ambu- lare, uti Apoc. 20. explicatio addita, septem candela- bra sunt septem Ecclesiæ. Aurum notat puritatem & constantiam Sanctorum, qui constituunt Eccle- siam: quia aurum est purissimum metallum, & tale, quod etiam igni nequaquam cedat Ps. XLV. 10, 15. Phiala vel lecytbus in summitate ejus Christum de- signat, in qua omnes thesauri sapientiæ absconditi Col. II. 3. fontem omnis gratiæ, ex cujus plenitudi- ne accipimus omnes gratiam pro gratia Joh. I. 16. Lucernæ septem ministros & Doctores Ecclesiæ notant, qui instar lucernæ, doctrina & vitæ luce aliis debent prælucere Joh. V. 35. singulæ lucernæ habent singula vascula, vel infusoria, quibus oleum illis communicatur & infunditur: quia fovendo o- leo Spiritus S. seu donis ejusdem sunt lucernæ illæ spirituales, ne lumen earum extinguatur. Ineptus autem est Ribera, qui per septem infundibula septem sacramenta designata esse singit. Figuram candela- bri sic exhibet B. Lutherus in Commentar. Germ. Tom. IV. Jen. f. 262. Diß Gesichte aber dieses güls denen Leuchters ist ein wenig anders gestalt, denn Moses Leuchter Exod. 25. Moses Leuchter hat Rös ren zum Seiten auß an dem Schafft oderStock 2c. Aber dieser stehet stracks auff mit seinemSchafft, und hat oben drauff einen runden grossen breiten Teller oder Schüssel, welchen ich einen Reiff ver- deutscht habe, und auffdenselbigen Teller umbher sieben Lampen im Ringe, die haben alle gebrand und geleucht, und auff daß ja das Liecht nicht auß- lesche, auß Mangel des Oels, so sind da siebenKel- len, oder Rören, die voll Oels sind, immer nachzu- folgen. Denn wir nicht wissen können, was für eine Gestalt dieselbigen Kellen haben gehabt, ob sie wie Töpfflein oder Kännlein, oder Rören gewest sind. Man hat Oele damit in die Lampen gegof- sen, das ist uns gnug, sie seyn Kannen oder Krügen gleich gewesen, oder nicht, und alle auß reine Golde. Auch lautet es im Ebräischen, daß derselbigen Kel- len mehr denn einmahl sieben gewesen sind, denn so stehet der Text; Septem & septem infusoria pro lucernis, das ist, je sieben und sieben Kellen zu den Lampen. Das laut fast, als haben zu einer jegli- chen Lampen sieben Kellen gehöret, anzuzeigen, daß gar reichlich die Lampen mit Dele versorget seyn, und keine Sorge sey, daß sie verleschen möchten. Duæ olivæ, vel filii oleæ, qui assistunt dominatori terræ sunt illi, qui Spiritu S. uncti sunt ad tutelam & gu- bernationem Ecclesiæ, quales Zorobabel, & Josua erant: quorum uterque in sua vocatione ministe- rium sacrum summo studio promovebat, ita ut ef- fent instar olearum, quæ oleum proferunt ad alen- dum lumen in lucernis.

IN PLANVM) Supple, dejecta es per Cyrum. Allu- dit ad nomen Zorobabelis, quod ei bono omine datum fuerat, significans Babylona dispersum iri: simul innuit idem eventurum aliis, qui se opposituri essent populo Dei.

## 4:7
AND HE SHALL BRING FORTH THE HEADSTONE) And he brings forth the first stone, which he is to place upon the foundation, as the initiator of the work. Ezra III, 8. AND HE SHALL BRING FORTH THE GRACE OF HIS GRACE) With acclamation, grace, grace be to it: that is, the people will acclaim to Zerubbabel who is laying the stone, may God always favor him. The same sense as in hosanna, Matthew XXI, 8.

Latin:

ET EDUCET LAPIDEM PRIMARIVM) Et is pro- fert primum lapidem, quem scilicet fundamento imponat, operis auspicator. Esdr. III, 8. ET EXÆQVABIT GRATIAM GRATIÆ EJVS) Cum acclamatione, gratia gratia sit illi: id est, populus ja- cienti lapidem Zorobabeli, acclamabit, Deus illi semper faveat. Idem sensus qui in ὡσαννὰ, Matth. XXI, 8.

## 4:9
Verse 9.

THE HANDS OF ZERUBBABEL HAVE FOUNDED THIS HOUSE) They shall found: as appears by comparing the passage of Haggai II, 19, and the beginning of this Prophet. AND HIS HANDS SHALL FINISH IT) He shall see the work consummated. AND YE SHALL KNOW THAT THE LORD GOD OF HOSTS HATH SENT ME UNTO YOU) That I might be a help to you: I, Michael, as above II, 11.

The BELGIAN interpreters understand these things, he shall bring forth the stone, not only concerning the consummation of the temple, but also concerning the procreation of Christ, who descended from Zerubbabel according to the flesh, Matthew I, 12. But both senses cannot have place at the same time. If therefore you take it of Christ, so that the Lord is understood: And God the Father shall bring forth the stone Christ, and shall manifest him to the world, and shall make him grow into a great mountain, which was shown to Daniel, into which sense Castrius brings Cyril, Jerome, Haymo, Remigius, Rupert, Albert, Hugh, Dionysius, Vatablus, Robert, and Montanus, even the Chaldean himself rendering it thus: And the Messiah shall emerge, whose name is from eternity, and he shall possess the empire of all kingdoms, the sense concerning Zerubbabel cannot indeed be admitted in these words. Yet that interpretation concerning Zerubbabel in this place, which Osiander hands down after B. Luther (with the rest of our Doctors concurring), is simpler, and the adjoined words, and the explanation of the Lord himself seem to demand it. And Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone, that is, he himself also shall apply his hand, when (upon the foundation, placed by the command of Cyrus) the first stone shall be placed in the building of the temple: and he shall bring forth the grace of his grace. Hebrew: with (joyful) acclamations, saying grace, grace (may divine grace be present) to it (to the new work: the Israelites will say, giving thanks, may the Lord give grace, so that this undertaking may be happily finished) (the prayers of the pious, however, are effective petitions.) And the word of the Lord came unto me, saying: The hands of the Prince Zerubbabel have founded this house: (for he himself, and Joshua the priest together with the people laid the foundations of the Temple, in the second year from the return from Babylon, Ezra ch. 3.) and his hands shall finish it, that is, he shall take care that it be completed while he is still alive and ruling, and indeed shortly: He has begun this building, He will also finish it. Wherefore also Castrius prefers this sense with Dav. Kimchi, Lyranus, and others, provided that it be sufficiently clear from the preceding and following, and no word occurs which does not properly suit Zerubbabel. But if the words can be explained properly, one should not have recourse to allegories. In which sense Willius also acquiesced, insisting here on the footsteps of Calvin: He shall bring forth the stone of his head. The relative is of the feminine gender, and thus it ought to be understood of the building itself. Zerubbabel therefore shall bring down the stone, which may stand out at the head of the Temple. By the stone of the head, I understand the highest, or that which was to be placed at the very summit. Now the foundations of the temple had been laid: it was a mediocre building and almost contemptible: yet it could not progress, since many enemies were gathering to disturb the work, or at least to delay it. Nevertheless the Angel promises, which he will explain more clearly later, that the temple will come to its perfection, because Zerubbabel will bring forth, that is, will bring into the light or on high the headstone, that is, which hangs over the very summit of the temple, and afterwards he adds the shouts: Grace, grace to it: that is, may God grant prosperous success to this stone or temple, for the relative 'to it' is again of the feminine gender. It cannot therefore square with the person of Zerubbabel, but it is suitable either to the temple or to the stone. So he. But because that temple was being built on account of the Church, which was to be preserved among this people until the coming of the Messiah, and Zerubbabel can be established as a type of Christ, we do not object (provided that a double sense of the same words is not introduced) that by that very thing the Lord wished to confirm the faithful concerning his coming and the propagation of his Church, who were not ignorant that God does not dwell in a material temple, but wished to cherish those shadows and figures until the skēnōsis, which they prefigured in the midst of his people in a personal temple. Conf. John I. 14. chap. II. 9. seqq. Col. II. 9.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

MANVS ZOROBABEL FUNDAVERUNT DO- MUM ISTAM) Fundabunt: ut apparet collato loco Ag- gæi II, 19. & initio hujus Prophetæ. ET MANVS EJVS PERFICIENT EAM) Videbit opus consummatum. ET SCIETIS QVIA DOMINVS DEVS EXERCI- TVVM MISIT ME AD VOS) Ut vobis auxilio essem: me Michaelem, ut supra II. 11.

Interpp. BELGICI hæc, educet lapidem, non so- lum de templi consummatione, sed etiam de Christi procreatione, qui à Zorobabele secundum carnem descendit Matth. I. 12. intelligunt. At sensus uter- que locum simul habere nequit. Si ergo de Christo accipias, ut subintelligatur Dominus: Et educet la- pidem Christum Deus Pater, & mundo manifesta- bit, & crescere faciet in magnum montem, qui o- stensus est Danieli, in quem sensum adducit Ca- strius Cyrillum, Hieronymum, Haymonem, Remi- gium, Rupertum, Albertum, Hugonem, Dionysium, Vatablum, Robertum, & Montanum, etiam Chal- dæum ipsum ita reddentem: Et emerget Messias, cu- jus nomen ab æterno est, & potiatur imperio omnium regnorum, non poterit sensus de Zorobabele in his quidem verbis admitti. Simplicior tamen illa de Zorobabele hoc loco interpretatio, quam post B. Lutherum tradit Osiander (suffragantibus cæteris Dd. nostris) & exposcere subjuncta verba, atque ipsa Domini explicatio videntur. Et Zorobabel edu- cet lapidem primarium, id est, admovebit ipse etiam manum, cum (super fundamentum, imperante Cy- ro positum) primus lapis in ædificio templi ponetur: & exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus. Hebr. cum (læ- tis) acclamationibus, dicentibus gratia, gratia (di- vina adsit) illi (novo operi: Dominus det gratiam, inquient Israëlitæ, gratulantes, ut hoc inceptum feliciter perficiatur) (piorum autem vota sunt effi- caces precationes.) Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens: Manus Ducis Zorobabel fundave- runt domum istam: (ipse enim, & Jesus sacerdos una cum populo jecerunt Templi fundamenta, an- no secundo à reditu ex Babylone Esdr. cap. 3.) & ma- nus ejus perficient eam, id est, curabit, ut ipso adhuc vivo & imperante, & quidem brevi absolvatur: Er hat diesen Bau angefangen, Er wird ihn auch vol- lenden. Quapropter etiam Castrius hunc sensum præfert cum Dav. Kimchio, Lyrano, & aliis, siqui- dem ex antecedentibus & consequentibus satis per- spicuus sit, neque verbum occurrat, quod non proprie conveniat Zorobabeli. Si autem verba proprie possint explicari, ad allegorias recurren- dum non sit. In quo sensu acquievit etiam Wil- lius, Calvini hic insistens vestigiis : Educet lapidem capitis ejus. Relativum est fœminei generis, & ita intelligi debet de ipso ædificio. Zerubabel ergo lapi- dem deducet, qui emineat in capite Templi. Per lapidem capitis, intelligo summum, vel qui locandus erat in ipso culmine. Jam fundamenta templi jacta fuerant : erat mediocre ædificium & fere con- temptibile: tamen non poterat progredi, quum multi hostes ad turbandum opus, vel saltem tar- dandum confluerent. Tamen promittit Angelus, quod postea clarius exponet, templum ad perfe- ctionem suam venturum, quia Zerubabel educet, hoc est, proferet in lucem vel in sublime lapidem capitis, id est, qui immineat in ipso fastigio templi, & postea subjungit clamores: Gratia,gratia ei: hoc est, prosperum successum huic lapidi vel templo Deus concedat, nam relativum Ei, iterum est fœ- minei generis. Non potest igitur quadrare personæ Zerubabeli, sed vel templo convenit vel lapidi. Hæc ille. Cæterum quia ob Ecclesiam templum il- lud extruebatur, quæ in isto populo, usque ad Mes- siæ adventum conservanda erat, & Zorobabel ty- pus Christi constitui potest, non repugnamus(dum modo geminus non invehatur eorundem verbo- rum Sensus) quin eo ipso confirmatos voluerit Dominus fideles de suo adventu & Ecclesiæ suæ propagatione, qui non ignorabant, Deum non ha- bitare in templo materiali, sed illas umbras & figu- ras fovere velle, usque ad σκήνωσιν, quam figura- bant in medio populi sui in templo personali. Conf. Joh. I. 14. cap. II. 9. seqq. Col. II. 9.

## 4:10
Vers. 10.

FOR WHO HAS DESPISED THE SMALL DAYS, AND THEY SHALL REJOICE, AND SHALL SEE THE TIN STONE IN THE HANDS OF ZERUBBABEL) If anyone has despised this time of small things, supply beginnings, they shall now rejoice, when they have seen that globe of the plumb line in the hands of Zerubbabel: namely, divinely engraved with seven eyes: by this portent they will understand that a great and prosperous thing is being begun.

THOSE SEVEN EYES ARE OF THE LORD, WHICH RUN THROUGH THE WHOLE EARTH) that is, they signify the multiform providence of God,

The Hebrews, Pagninus, Vatablus, Isidorus, and Robertus also understand the stone of tin as a plumb line, as promised in chap. I. 17, and the plumb line shall be stretched over Jerusalem, because joy is to arise when they are to see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel for the foundations and walls to be erected. So also Osiander: They will see with pleasure the tin stone (that is, the lead plumb line, die Bleywag) in the hand of Zerubbabel the leader: for he himself will sometimes apply his hands to the work, and will take care that all things are done skillfully and rightly: He will himself at times take the plumb line in his hand, and see whether the building is level and upright. Lyranus and Dionysius interpret it as a lead or tin stone, with which the temple was to be covered. Drusius posits an asyndeton between stone and tin. Jerome, however, deriving it from בּדַל, translates it as the stone of separation, and understands Christ: some wish it to be called the stone of separation, because as an excellent stone at the head of the building, as if at the head by Zerubbabel with the applause of the whole people it was placed, having been set apart. However, the first explanation, as it is simple, so it is more common. Those things which are added concerning the eyes seem to have greater difficulty. Interpreters vary regarding the distinction, which Albert the Great, Rupert, Hugh, Lyra, Dionysius, Pagninus make thus: And they shall see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven eyes which are the Lord's, going about through the whole earth: B. Luther: With the seven, which are the Lord's eyes: The seven, which shall be with Zerubbabel, He says, are the eyes of the Lord, that is, His Spirit with manifold gifts, which shall be present to strengthen and help with grace. So also the Weimar Paraphrasts. Grotius inserts a point, which was also done by the LXX, the Vulgate interpreters, Vatablus, the Tigurine, Clarius, Arias. And they shall see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. But Grotius understands by those seven the eyes engraved on the stone: Others thus: Those seven (suppose the little channels, through which oil was ministered to the lamps,) are the eyes of the Lord running through the whole earth, which Castrius explains, those seven signify the manifold providence and care by which God looks out for all. Osiander explains it thus: Those seven (those lamps) signify that many faithful teachers will be divinely raised up in the Church, whose work the Lord will use everywhere in enlightening men. He wishes the Prophet to look, however, not only to the sincere teachers among the Israelite people, but primarily to the Apostles of Christ (the most perfect teachers of the Church) who were to carry the light of the Gospel around the whole world. But what Grotius brings forward concerning the seven eyes divinely engraved on the knob of the plumb line, signifying the providence of God, rests on no foundation: and it is directed by him to this end, that from the confusion of this vision and the preceding one, which was made to Joshua, the promise concerning the singular stone to be engraved by the Lord, the illustrious prophecy concerning the Messiah might be weakened. It is a very ridiculous display that seven eyes should have appeared on a knob: nor is it taught here how they were to be confirmed concerning success by any display, but the joy is described which they were to perceive from the very completion of the work, who had previously despised the small days, and had all but despaired of success.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

QUIS ENIM DESPEXIT DIES PARVOS, ET LÆ- TABUNTUR, ET VIDEBUNT LAPIDEM STAN- NEUM IN MANVS ZOROBABEL) Si quis despexerit tempus hoc tenuium, supple principiorum, ii jam lætabun- tur, ubi viderint globum illum perpendiculi id manibus Zoro- babelis: nempe divinitus cælatum septem oculis: hoc o- stento intelligent rem magnam ac prosperam cœptari.

SEPTEM ILLI OCULI SUNT DOMINI, QUI DISCURRVNT IN UNIVERSAM TERRAM) id est, significant multiformem Dei providentiam,

Lapidem stanni de perpendiculo etiam Ebræi, Pa- gninus, Vatablus, Isidorus, Robertus intelligunt, ut cap. I. 17. promissum, & perpendiculum extendetur super Jerusalem, quod lætitia oritura sit, cum visuri sunt perpendiculum in manu Zorobabelis ad fun- damenta, & parietes erigendos. Sic etiam Osiander: Cum voluptate videbunt lapidem stanneum, (id est, perpendiculum plumbeum die Bleywag,) in manu Zorobabel Ducis : ipse enim quandoque manus operi admovebit, & curabit, ut omnia dex- tre & recte fiant: Er wird selbs zun zeiten die Bley- wag in die Hand nehmen, und sehen, ob das Gebäu eben und auffrecht sey. Lyranus & Dionysius inter- pretantur de plumbeo vel stanneo lapide, quo tem- plum contegendum fuerit. Drusius asyndeton ponit lapidem & stannum. Hieronymus vero à בּדַל sepa- rare, vertit lapidem separationis, & Christum intel- ligit: nonnulli lapidem separationis dictum volunt, quia ut eximius lapis ad caput ædificii, velut in ca- pite à Zorobabelo cum totius populi applausu col- locaretur, segregatus fuit. Cæterum prima expli- catio, ut simpliciter, ita communior est. Difficulta- tem majorem habere videntur illa, quæ adduntur de oculis. Variant interpp. quoad distinctionem, quam Albertus M. Rupertus, Hugo, Lyranus, Dio- nysius, Pagninus hanc faciunt: Et videbunt lapidem stanni in manu Zorobabel cum septem illis oculis qui Domini sunt circumeuntes per universam terram: B. Lutherus: Mit den sieben, welche sind des Her- ren Augen: Die Sieben, die mit Serubabel sollen seyn, spricht Er, sind die Augen des HErren, das ist, sein Geist mit mancherley Gaben, der soll gegen- wärtig seyn mit Gnaden stärcken und helffen. Sic etiam Paraphrasta Vinarienses. Grotius, interjicit punctum quod etiam factum à LXX. Interpp. Vul- gat. Vatabl. Tigurin. Clario, Aria. Et videbunt lapi- dem stanneum in manu Zorobabel. Sed Grotius per septem illa intelligit oculos cælatos in lapide: Alii ita: Septem isti (canaliculos puta, per quod oleum lucer- nis ministrabatur,) oculi Domini discurrentes in u- niversam terram, quod explicat Castrius, septem illa significant multiplicem providentiam ac curam, qua Deus prospicit omnibus. Osiander sic exponit: Se- ptem ista (istæ lucernæ) significant multos fideles in Ecclesia Doctores divinitus excitatum iri, quorum opera Dominus passim utetur in illuminandis ho- minibus. Respicere autem Prophetam vult, non modo ad sinceros Doctores in populo Israelitico, sed imprimis Apostolos Christi, (perfectissimos Ec- clesiæ Doctores) qui per universum orbem lumen Evangelii circumlaturi erant. Quod vero Grotius de septem oculis divinitus in globulo perpendiculi cæ- latis providentiam Dei significantibus adfert, nullo nititur fundamento: eoque directum ab ipso est, ut è confusione hujus visionis & præcedentis, quæ Josuæ facta est, promissionis de lapide singulari à Domino cælando, illustre vaticinium de Messia ener- vetur. Ostentum ludicrum valde est, quod oculi septem apparuerint in globulo: neque hic doce- tur, quomodo aliquo ostento de successu confir- mandi fuerint, sed describitur lætitia, quam per- cepturi erant ex ipso operis complemento, qui an- tea despexerant dies parvos, & tantum non de suc- cessu desperaverant.

## 4:11
Ver. 11.

AND I ANSWERED AND SAID TO HIM) And I spoke and said to him. So also in the following, ענה is often used even where no speech of another has preceded.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET RESPONDI ET DIXI AD EUM) Et locutus dixi ad eum. Sic & in sequentibus ענה sæpe dicitur etiam, ubi nullas alterius sermo præcessit.

## 4:12
Ver. 12.

WHAT ARE THE TWO OLIVE BRANCHES?) That is, the tubes.

WHICH ARE BESIDE THE TWO GOLDEN BEAKS) Beside the two golden flasks. For צנתרת is the same as גלה above. The Chaldeans for the same say עשירת, but also צנתר.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QUID SVNT DUÆ SPICÆ OLIVARVM?) Id est, tubuli.

QUÆ SUNT JUXTA DUO ROSTRA AVREA) Juxta duas ampullas auri. Idem enim צנתרת, quod supra גלה. Chaldæi pro eodem dicunt עשירת, sed & צנתר.

## 4:14
Ver. 14.

THESE ARE THE TWO SONS OF OIL) These olives signify the double kind of those anointed with oil, who will not be lacking to this Temple, the princes and the high priests: whose care for the temple is signified through these tubes.

WHO STAND BY THE LORD OF THE WHOLE EARTH) They serve God in caring for the temple according to the parts assigned to each.

We admit the interpretation concerning the two sons of the olive tree, Princes and high priests who would not be lacking to the temple, which almost all of our people have also embraced. Thus, after the blessed Luther, Winckelmann: These are the two sons of oil, namely Zerubbabel the Prince, and Joshua the Priest: so called not only because of the external anointing, but also because of the gifts of the Holy Spirit by which the former was made fit for the government of the Republic, and the latter for the ministry of the Church. Or one may interpret the two olive trees as the priesthood and the principate, and the two olive branches as the priest and the prince. Thus also Osiander: These are the two sons of oil: that is, anointed by the Holy Spirit, one for the government of the Republic, the other for the ministry of the Church: who stand in the sight of God almighty, and faithfully perform their office before Him; and they are a care to our Lord. Through these olive trees, therefore, the Lord was designating Zerubbabel, the Leader of the people, and Joshua the High Priest: both of whom in their own vocation were promoting the sacred Ministry with the greatest zeal, so that they were like olive trees, which produce oil to feed the light in the lamps. (For when the Magistrate applies himself to this, that the ministers of the Church may rightly perform their office, and also have sustenance, and prevents the Ministry of the word of God from being despised or even trampled upon, and especially when the Ministers of the Church labor in this, that the studies of sacred letters may flourish, so that the Churches of God may have a sincere and copious doctrine of truth, then in very truth (Politicians and Ecclesiastics) are as it were two fruitful olive trees in the sight of the Lord, by whose work the ministry is preserved and propagated to posterity. For example, a pious Prince, and a faithful and learned Superintendent, are two olive trees beside the golden lampstand. And such olive trees are a care to the Lord our God: He holds their faithful work in thanks, and guards and protects them. But the interpretation of Bede, Tyconius, and Brightman concerning the two Testaments, Old and New, is foreign, unless perhaps by the two golden spouts they wish to understand the Old and New Testament, or the Scripture of the O. and N. T.: the Papists' inept and ludicrous idea about Enoch and Elijah returning before the end of the world is also foreign, nor does the explanation of Junius and Willius fit, who, following his Calvin with Junius, interprets it thus: These two trees figure the manifold gifts of the Holy Spirit, to come to the Church eternally from God through Christ, but the two berries and tubes signify the abundant measure of the Holy Spirit, and in the Church from the fullness of Christ flowing down endlessly in their own ways as if through pipes. For thus the occasion and scope are neglected, the antecedents and consequences of this figure are neglected: the reason for the binary number is also neglected, for why should two branches be shown, and not more? But one must marvel at Willius's confidence, to put it most mildly, who although he confesses that Hebrews and Christians alike, all whom he has seen, with the exception of Calvin and Junius, understand Zerubbabel and Joshua, yet dares to argue against that interpretation as in no way convenient to the text, nay, contrary to it, as if Calvin alone had hit the nail on the head. For to Willius he alone is wise, the rest flutter about like shadows. He pretends that it is indicated by God that the Church is to be cared for and sustained by the immediate efficacy of His Spirit, not by the virtue and power of Joshua, nor of Zerubbabel, nor of any man. Which is an ignorant, and almost Schwenkfeldian, opposition of the principal and ministerial cause. For God does not exclude the latter, while He claims success and blessing for His own virtue. Nor because the sons of the olive tree stand by the ruler of the earth is an immediate influx of grace into the Church therefore designated: But since it redounds into the Church through the sons of the olive tree, it is not obscure that ministerial causes are indicated by them. But as for Willius here attacking the blessed Luther for taking the tubes as snuffers, that is to be imputed to the character and genius of the Calvinist Spirit. How much zeal Megalander was occupied with in these words, his German Commentary could have taught the man. But what is the wonder, if someone sticks on a more obscure text? Which we know happens even to the best Interpreters. Osiander rendered the words κατὰ πόδα: What are the two branches of the olive trees (Grotius calls them tubes) which are beside the two golden spouts (Grotius, golden flasks) which offer themselves as golden, that is, pure and splendid liquid of oil) But he calls those extremities of the lamps, in which the wicks lie and burn, drawing oil from the bottom of the lamps: those beaks are shaped almost like pipes, but he calls the ears of olives branches full of fruits: and he likens the fruit to grains, but the branch to a stalk.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ISTI SVNT DUO FILII OLEI) Istæ olivæ signi- ficant duplex oleo unctorum genus, qui Templo isti non deerunt, principes & summi sacerdotes: quorum curæ pro templo per tubulos istos significantur.

QVI ASSISTUNT DOMINATORI UNIVER- SÆ TERRÆ) Deo inserviunt in curando templo pro mandatis sibi quisque partibus.

Admittimus interpretationem de duobus filiis o- livæ Principibus & summis sacerdotibus templo non defuturis, quam etiam amplexi sunt nostrates pleri- que omnes. Sic post B. Lutherum Winckelmannus: Isti sunt duo filii olei, nimirum Zorobabel Princeps, & Jehosua Sacerdos: sic dicti non tantum propter unctionem externam, sed etiam ob dona Spiritus S. quibus ille ad gubernationem Reipubl. & hic ad Ecclesiæ ministerium idoneus efficiebatur. Vel li- cet duas olivas sacerdotium & principatum, & duas spicas olivæ sacerdotem & principem interpretari. Sic etiam Osiander: Isti sunt duo filii olei: id est, fun- Sp. S. uncti, alter ad gubernationem Reipublicæ alter ad Ecclesiae ministerium: qui stant in conspectu Dei omnipotentis, & coram ipso fideliter nunc suum officium faciunt: ac sunt Domino nostro curae. Per has igitur olivas, designabat Dominus Zorobabe- lem, Ducem populi, & Jesum Sacerdotem Ma- gnum: quorum uterque in sua vocatione Ministe- rium sacrum summo studio promovebat, ita ut es- sent instar olearum, quae oleum proferunt ad alen- dum lumen in lucernis. (Quando enim Magistra- tus in hoc incumbit, ut ministri Ecclesiae recte of- ficium faciant, & alimenta etiam habeant, & pro- hibet, ne Ministerium verbi Dei contemnatur, aut etiam conculcetur, praecipue vero Ministri Eccle- siae in eo elaborant, ut studia sacrarum literarum floreant, quo Ecclesiae Dei sinceram & copiosam veritatis doctrinam habeant, tum revera utique (Politici & Ecclesiastici) sunt quasi duae olivae foe- cundae in conspectu Domini, quarum opera mini- sterium conservatur, & ad posteritatem propaga- tur. Exempli gratia, pius Princeps, & fidelis atque doctus Superattendens, sunt duae olivae juxta can- delabrum aureum. Et tales olivae sunt Domino Deo nostro curae: earum fidelem operam gratam habet, easque tuetur & protegit. Aliena autem est imterpretatio Bedae, Tyconij, Brigtmanni de duobus Testamentis, Veteri & Novo, nisi per duo aurea ro- stra forte Testamentum Vetus & Novum, seu Scri- pturam V. & N. T. intelligere velint: inepta & ludi- cra Papicolarum de Enocho & Elia ante mundi fi- nem redituris, neque congruit explanatio Junij ac Willii, qui cum Junio Calvinum suum sequutus ita interpretatur: Duae istae arbores figurant omnimo- da Sp. S. dona, a Deo in aeternum ad Ecclesiam obven- tura per Christum, duae autem baccae & tubi signifi- cant demensum Spiritus S. abundans, & in Ecclesia a plenitudine Christi suis modis tanquam tabulis inde- finenter defluens. Sic enim negligitur occasio & sco- pus, negliguntur antecedentia & consequentia hujus figurae: negligitur etiam ratio numeri bina- rii, cur enim duae exhiberentur spicae, non plures? Mirari autem oportet Willianam confidentiam, ut mollissime dicam, qui etsi fateatur, Ebraeos pa- riter & Christianos, quos viderit omnes, Calvino & Junio excepto, Zorobabelem & Josuan intelligere, arguere tamen audet eam interpretationem, ceu textui nullo modo convenientem, imo contrariam, ac si Calvinus unus rem acu tetigerit. Nam Willio ille sapit solus, reliqui volitant velut umbrae. Scilicet fin- git indicatum a Deo immediata Spiritus sui effica- cia Ecclesiam curandam & sustentandam, non Josuae, non Zorobabelis, nec ullius hominis virtute ac poten- tia. Quae est imperita, & propemodum Schvenc- feldiana causae principalis & ministerialis oppositio. Non enim hanc excludit Deus, dum suae virtuti successum & benedictionem vindicat. Nec quia filii oleae assistunt dominatori terrae, ideo influxus gra- tiae in Ecclesiam immediatus designatur: Sed quum is per filios oleae redundet in Ecclesiam, per eos- dem causas ministeriales indicari, haud obscurum est. Quod vero Willius hic exagitat B. Lutherum tubos pro emunctoriis sumentem, id indoli atque genio Spiritus Calviniani imputandum. Quanto studio occupatus in hisce verbis fuerit Megalan- der, edocere hominem potuisset Commentarius ejus Germanicus. Quid vero mirum, si quis in ob- scuriori textu haereat? Quod optimis etiam Interpp. accidere novimus. Verba κατὰ πόδα reddidit O- siander: Quid sunt duae spicae olivarum (tubulos vocat Grotius) quae sunt juxta duo rostra aurea (Grotius, ampullas auri) quae se praebent aureum, id est, pu- rum & splendidum liquorem olei) Rostra autem vocat illas lucernarum extremitates, in quibus lychni jacent & ardent, attrahentes oleum ex fun- do lucernarum: illa rostra sunt fere instar fistula- rum formata, spicas autem olivarum vocat ramos plenos fructibus: & fructus quidem granis, ramum autem culmo assimilat.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

The sixth and seventh vision of the flying scroll and the ephah with the mass of lead.

A scroll is seen, long and wide, and it is explained as the curse which goes forth over the face of all the earth because of injustice, thefts, and perjuries. An amphora is also seen going forth with a talent of lead, which is explained as the impiety (of heresy) to be transferred by two women (false teachers having nothing manly) into the land of Shinar, that is, of heresy to be cast down into hell, so that the people may thus be deterred from iniquity and false doctrine.

The paper flies, the judge of lead is carried far from the amphora.

Ver. 1.

AND I TURNED) I turned myself to a new vision coming upon the other.

Drusius is right here: I turned and lifted, is said for I lifted again, as in Hosea 5:6. I will add yet I will have mercy, for I will have mercy again.

Ver. the same.

A FLYING SCROLL) מגלה is a book so written that it can be rolled up. But that it is flying signifies that it was open, ἀναπτυσσόμενον. מגל signifies a sickle, and so the LXX took it here, as if the מ had been παραγωγικὸν. For they put δρέπανον πετόμενον, to which perhaps Revelation 14:14 and following referred: But the Chaldean also began with a scroll here, and the following things demand it. Compare Ezekiel 2:9, Revelation 10:10.

Grotius wishes it to be shown as a thing not future, but already done. Most, however, explain it as something represented or future. Blessed Luther and others of our people understand it as false doctrine, human traditions, and impiety. And indeed, false doctrine is well proposed in the form of a book, because it carries the appearance of wisdom. That book flies, because false doctrine or the speech of perverse men, as Paul says, creeps like a cankerous disease (2 Tim. 2:17). And it is disseminated far and wide. Then it is also said to fly because it makes men fluctuate in their consciences, and to be driven hither and thither (Eph. 4), so that they seem to hang between heaven and earth, as Winckelmann has it in this place. Tarnovius prefers that it be shown by this vision that the Jews sinned nefariously against both tables of the divine law.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Sexta & septima visio Epistolæ volantis & Ephæ cum massa plumbi.

Videtur Epistola longa, & lata, & explica- tur de maledictione, quæ egreditur super faciem omnis terræ ob injustitiam, furta & perjuria. Videtur & amphora egre- diens cum talento plumbi, quæ exponitur de impietate (hæreseos) per duas mulieres (falsos doctores nihil virile habentes) transferenda in terram Sennaar, id est, de hæresi in infernum præcipitanda, ut ita populus ab iniquitate & falsa doctri- na deterreatur.

Charta volat judex plumbi procul amphora fertur.

Vers. 1.

ET CONVERSUS SVM) Verti me ad visum no- vum alteri superveniens.

REcte hic Drusius: Conversus sum & levavi, di- ctum pro iterum levavi ut Hos. V. 6. Addam adhuc miserebor, pro denuo miserebor.

Vers. eod.

VOLUMEN VOLANS) מגלה est liber ita scri- ptus, ut convolvi possit. Sed illud volans significat fuisse apertum, ἀναπτυσσόμενον. מגל falcem significat, & ita hic sumpsere LXX. quasi מ fuisset παραγωγικὸν. ponunt enim δρέ- πανον πετόμενον, quo forte respexit Apoc. XIV. 14. & de- inceps: Sed volumen cœpit hic etiam Chaldæus, & id exi- gunt sequentia. Confer. Ezech. II. 9. Apoc. X. 10.

Ostendi rem non futuram, sed gestam vult Gro- tius. Plerique autem de repræsenti vel futura ex- ponunt. B. Lutherus & alii Nostrates intelligunt falsam doctrinam, traditiones humanas, & impieta- tem. Et bene quidem falsa doctrina in forma libri proponitur, quia præ se fert sapientiam. Liber iste volat, quia falsa doctrina vel perversorum homi- num sermo, ut Paulus ait, serpit sicut cancer mor- bus II. Tim. II. v. 17. Et longe lateque disseminatur. Deinde ideo etiam volare dicit, quia facit homi- nes in conscientiis fluctuare, & hinc inde agitari Eph. 4. ut inter cœlum & terram hærere videan- tur, uti habet Winckelmannus in h. l. Tarnovius mavult ostendi hac visione, quod Judæi nefarie contra legis divinæ utramque tabulam peccarint.

## 5:2
Verse 2.

THE LENGTH OF IT TWENTY CUBITS, AND THE BREADTH OF IT TEN CUBITS) The scrolls in those places were oblong. At the same time, the size of the book is shown.

The porch of Solomon was of the same measure, 1 Kings 6:3. Such length and breadth of the book indicates, according to B. Luther, the multitude of human traditions. For they brought heavy and unbearable burdens, and imposed them upon the shoulders of men. Tarnovius: he says that innumerable sins and infinite cursing were contained in so large a volume. Willius: Perhaps, however, God wished to teach by this scope that this volume is the same as the volume of the law handed down by God through Moses, which the priests were accustomed to read and explain to the people in the atrium. But this gloss is foreign: What was the point of exhibiting the volume of the law in that manner!

Latin:

Vers. 2.

LONGITUDO EJVS VIGINTI CVBITORVM, ET LATITUDO EJVS DECEM CVBITORVM) Erant volumina illis in locis oblonga. Simul magnitudo libri ostenditur.

Eadem mensura fuit porticus Salomonis I. Reg. VI. 3. Tanta libri longitudo & latitudo indicat juxta B. Lutherum, multitudinem traditionum humana- rum. Allegabant enim onera gravia & importabi- lia, eaque imponebant in humeros hominum. Tar- novius: innumera peccata, & infinitam maledictio- nem in tam grandi volumine contentam fuisse ait. Willius: Forte tamen docere voluit hoc ambitu Deus, idem hoc esse volumen cum volumine legis à Deo per Mosen tradito, quod in atrio populo prælegere & explicare sacerdotes consueverant. Sed hæc glossa aliena est: Quid attinebat ea ratione volumen legis exhibere!

## 5:3
THIS IS THE CURSE) This book contains punishments. WHICH GOETH FORTH OVER THE FACE OF THE WHOLE EARTH) Of the promised land, both that which the ten tribes had held, and that which the two tribes had. EVERY THIEF, AS IT IS WRITTEN THERE, SHALL BE JUDGED) He shall be cut off. The punishments corresponding to all crimes were in that book: for נקה, Theodotion reads נכה, he shall be beaten. AND EVERY ONE THAT SWEARETH) That is, forswearing, as the following things explain.

Latin:

HÆC EST MALEDICTIO) Hic liber pœnas continet. QUÆ EGREDITUR SUPER FACIEM OMNIS TERRÆ) Terræ promissæ, tum illi quam habuerant de- cem, tum illi quam duæ tribus. OMNIS FVR, SICUT IBI SCRIPTUM EST, JUDICABITUR) Exscindetur. Respondentes omnibus criminibus pœnæ erant in illo libro: pro נקה, Theodo- tion legit נכה, verberabitur. ET OMNIS JVRANS) Id est, pejerans, ut expo- nunt sequentia.

## 5:4
Verse 4.

I WILL BRING IT FORTH) I will extract decrees from it against individuals. AND IT SHALL REMAIN IN THE MIDST OF HIS HOUSE, AND SHALL CONSUME IT AND THE TIMBER THEREOF, AND THE STONES THEREOF) It will leave nothing of the house. Thus also concerning the punishment of perjury, the oracle in Herodotus, Erato: -- Εἰσόκε πᾶσαν Συμμάρψας ὀλέσῃ γενεὴν καὶ οἶκον ἅπαντα.

The interpreters explain these things concerning the effects of false doctrine, which brings a curse upon those who receive it. Since, therefore, it pervaded all Judea, and the whole people, having spurned Christ and His Gospel, embraced that, finally the wrath and curse of the Lord overwhelmed the land and the people. Luther translates it thus: Because every thief thence as innocent, and every perjurer thence as innocent. The fruit of this false doctrine and human traditions is that avarice, thefts, lies, and every impiety are painted with the color of truth, and are not considered sins. Thus Christ accuses the Pharisees, Matthew 23: Woe unto you, etc., because you devour widows' houses, while making long prayers. Again, Matthew 15, He accuses them because for the sake of their traditions they transgress the commandments of God, saying that a gift or sacrifice is more acceptable than obedience toward the 4th commandment. Again, they estimated that the gold of the altar or the temple was more acceptable than the altar and temple itself, Matthew 23. Finally, in sacrifices they sought their own gain, and for that purpose granted a place to money-changers, buyers, and sellers in the temple itself, Luke 19, John 12. And yet they covered these things, which were truly thefts, with a veil of piety, holiness, and worship. Thus also the perjurer is pronounced innocent according to that book. For false doctrine also has this peculiar trait, that it is sold under the title of the very word of God and the Divine name. The name of God is used as a pretext for lies, which is truly to lie, to forswear, just as the Lord accuses false prophets everywhere by this name, as Winckelmann does here again: whence the judgment of God follows: I WILL BRING FORTH THAT VOLUME: The Lord will manifest the avarice, thefts, lies, and impiety of the book: AND IT SHALL COME TO THE HOUSE OF THE THIEF, i.e., the volume metonymically, the very Judgment of God, which follows false doctrine. AND IT SHALL CONSUME IT, that happened to the Jews, just as the Lord had threatened them, Matthew 23. Osiander, who provides the same interpretation concerning false doctrine, explains it thus: And my just judgment shall come to the house of the thief. E. Tarnovius thinks it is shown here that the sentence of God is not borne unjustly: Because whoever steals from this, i.e., the people, like that dregs of the wicked living in the land and region of the nations, asserts himself to be innocent, and whoever swears falsely from this people, like that profane crowd of the impious, asserts himself to be innocent, and excuses his own most wicked deed. Pagninus and Vatablus with R. Dav. Kimchi render: As it is written on the other side of it: that the volume was inscribed with letters on both sides, or faces. Thus also Ludov. de Dieu.

The interpretation of Cocceius seems simpler, who renders that מזה AS FROM THIS, i.e., time, or hereafter

ἀπαγ]. For everyone who steals is emptied out from this according to that: & of the Belgians and Willius. For whoever steals from this (land, because ארץ precedes, which is no less masculine than feminine) according to it (מגלה is of the feminine gender, according to that volume) is emptied out. Willius teaches that the noun נקה is to empty out, from Isa. III. 26, Jer. XLVI. 28. The sense therefore according to him is that thieves and perjurers are to be removed from the land according to the book of the curse and are to perish: and that by thefts and perjuries, synecdochically, any sins against the second and first table are designated, so that those who violate the duties of charity are called thieves, and those who neglect or adulterate divine worship are called perjurers. The interpretation of Grotius, that it seemed to be a volume which contained punishments, departs not only from that of most others, but also from the common opinion of the interpreters, yet in this Grotius departs from the common opinion of the interpreters with

Calvin and a few others, in that he wishes to show that the matter is not present or future, but already long since accomplished, which cannot be proven. For those visions concern the present state: and the issue here is about the crimes of that time, and the punishment to be inflicted, not already inflicted, and thus it is shown rather why the promises have not hitherto attained their fulfillment, or what things still provoke divine judgment in that people, or, as others say, are in need of reformation. But whether these be called false doctrine and superstitions, or sins against the first and second table, nothing is lost from the scope of the Prophet, whence the accusation of Willius is vain, that our countrymen here wander entirely from the scope of the vision. Indeed, false doctrine, by which even thieves and perjurers themselves are judged innocent, as the blessed Luther explained, can be posited as the cause of the curse over the whole earth no less than the crime of theft, perjury, or any other whatsoever. But the blessed Luther preferred to understand that VOLUME as a writing filled with false doctrines and traditions, rather than as a book of divine judgments, or the book of the Law itself, as Willius interprets it with Rupert, because according to that book thieves and perjurers are pronounced innocent, just as the word נקה in its more common meaning is 'was innocent,' which Junius himself followed here, since one should not easily depart from the more famous meaning. Nor does the explanation of the blessed Luther, which can be read in T. IV. Jen. Germ. on this passage and in Winckelmann, seem inconsistent. It certainly did not deserve the censure with which Willius marked it in this passage, who ought rather to have chastised his own Calvin here, because he contends that those things which were already long since accomplished were exhibited in this vision. We do not see the wallet that is on our back. There is no doubt, says Calvin, that God wished to show Zechariah that the Jews had deservedly paid the penalties, because the whole land was filled either with thefts or with perjuries: Since therefore religion had been despised, and then all equity and justice, he therefore shows that it is no wonder if the curse had spread through the whole land: because, namely, the Jews by their impiety and their crimes had provoked the wrath of God to the very extreme. The blessed Balduin thus hands down the continuity and explanation of Luther's opinion.

p. 313. We, with the blessed Luther, understand this concerning the corruptions of orthodox doctrine and human traditions, which the Prophet had foreseen would spread among the Jewish people and in the Jerusalem temple in place of the divine word. For the Lord wished to signify both things to His people: both the goodness of God in renewing the worship of the word of God through the orthodox teachers of the Church, whom he had named sons of oil in the preceding vision: and the malice of the Devil in corrupting sound doctrine and depraving true worship through the will-worship of men: and therefore that there is a need, being henceforth concerned for their own affairs, to live cautiously and not believe every spirit. And the history of the following times testifies that all these things happened in this way. For this volume first began to fly when the temple of the Lord was built on Mount Gerizim, in the likeness of the Jerusalem one, by the authority of a certain royal prefect, Sanballat—and that was done one hundred and ninety years after the second temple was built: nearly three hundred and sixty-three years before the beginning of the ministry of Christ. —Then this volume of iniquity flew further when Jason the pseudo-high priest erected a gymnasium of gentility near the temple in the holy city itself, as this impiety is described in II Maccabees IV. and I Macc. I, in which the youth of the Hebrews were to be instructed in the laws and rites of the heathens, to the fraud of the divine law, Lev. XVIII. v. 3, c. 20. v. 23, and that was done in the year 300 from the publication of this vision of our Prophet, nearly 150 years before Christ was born: Thirdly, when in the following years Onias the Priest, son of the holy High Priest Onias, fleeing with many of the Jews into Egypt, began to build a temple near Leontopolis in the Heliopolitan prefecture, after the form of that which was in Jerusalem, where, having appointed Levites and priests, he instituted divine worship, pretending by this pact that he was fulfilling the scripture which had said: In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, Isa. 19. verse 19, concerning which abomination see Josephus, book 12 of the Antiquities, chapter 15, and book 13, chapter 6. --- Fourthly, when a little later the Jewish people were split into as it were three sects, of the Pharisees, Sadducees, and Essenes, who all proposed things alien to the law of God, and corrupted the true worship of God with human traditions. --- Fifthly, when the Babylonian Talmud of the Jews began to be written, by which the whole Synagogue of the Jews is governed, and that was done in the year 436 from the burning of the second temple, as Galatinus testifies in book 1, chapter 5.
