By these ways, therefore, that volume of impiety flew through the region of Judea especially, as long as the Jerusalem temple stood and worship flourished in it publicly: whence it is also said to have been of the same magnitude as the court of the temple. These things are from Balduin, the blessed. Meanwhile, if anyone prefers to explain that volume as the book of the judgments and punishments of God, and interprets the word נקה as 'was emptied out,' we will not object. Since that word נקה seems to be explained when it is added, that a curse will come into the house of the thief and the perjurer, and thus most ancient Hebrew, Greek, and Latin interpreters explain it in a penal sense. Jerome, Theodoret, Haymo, Rupert, Remigius, Albert the Great, Hugh, Lyra, etc., as noted by Castrius. Nor do the translators differ: the Targum [renders] נקי as struck, the LXX as ἐκδικηθήσεται [he shall be punished], the Vulgate as judicabitur [he shall be judged]. The Antiochene Arabic [renders it] to death (he shall be condemned), the Alexandrian [renders it] he shall pay the penalty even to death. Whence B. Tarnovius of our own (as we observed before) warns that it is shown by this vision how it happened that the fulfillment of the promises has not yet appeared, namely because they themselves had wickedly sinned against both tables of the divine law. The Dutch interpreters, Junius, and others also explain it concerning future punishments. Rupert, Dionysius, Vatablus, and Montanus refer these judgments to the times of the Maccabees, when Antiochus raged against the Jews: but since the Prophet is rather concerned with comforting the fearful people, Castrius prefers, with Theodoret, that it be signified that the curse contained in this scroll has already been cast out, or at least is to be cast far from the people of God into the house of any thief or perjurer, just as afterwards impiety is driven far away and cast into Babylon. But in truth, even if the Prophet comforts the faithful who returned from Babylon, because there were not a few reprobates mixed in with them, who through the captivity Ba- lonian captivity, as is wont to happen, not that they became better, but worse, Zechariah threatens that their houses will be consumed by their own crimes. For these threats do not strike the nations, but the Jews, swearing falsely IN THE NAME OF THE LORD. Cocceius refers this to the final times of the second temple. The prophecy of the summit, he says, is that the time is at hand when, because of the theft and perjury of the people and its princes, the curse of the law is to rage against the whole people, and against the temple itself, so that it is no longer the house of God, but a house of a thief and a perjurer, since the Son of God is building another temple, ch. VI. 13. Which opinion of his, as far as the time and the sum of the matter are concerned, regarding the theft and perjury of the princes of the people being punished by divine curse, is not alien to the explanation of Blessed Luther, even if he understands the flying volume not as a volume of false doctrine, but of the curse and judgment of God. Although both explanations can perhaps be joined in a certain way, namely by this reasoning: that by this volume false doctrine is designated, by which [the people] are liable to the judgment and curse of God, or together with the divine anathema.

decreed and predetermined by God for the definition and destruction of the same, by which, as it was gradually fulfilled, the Jews were punished and destroyed: But this measure was fulfilled in the time of Zedekiah, and punished by God with the Babylonian captivity. Zechariah therefore saw an amphora or measure, in which wickedness was sitting, being transferred from Judea into Babylon, by which he signifies that the wickedness of Judea and the impious Jews were transferred into Babylon, and consequently that Judea was now purged and pure from wickedness, but that Babylon was the seat and sewer of wickedness, wherefore wickedness would remain in Babylon, and would no longer return to Judea. Henceforth idolatry was not seen in Judea, because the Jews left it, with its amphora, that is, its punishment, in Babylon, when its measure was paid out over seventy years, and they, expiated and free, returned to Jerusalem. This is Cornelius in this place, p. 206. To whose interpretation the glosses of Castrius, Menochius, and others agree. These, therefore, refer to past histories with Grotius: but they differ in this, that Grotius wishes these things to pertain both to the ten tribes and to the Jewish people, and understands by the two women both of those peoples: But most others refer it to the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and the times of the Babylonian captivity. He consoles, says Castrius, the two tribes which had returned from Babylon, into which they had been led captive, not the ten, which were led to the Assyrians, and never returned. The two women, namely the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, carried the bushel, that is, the punishment of their sins, especially idolatry, into Babylon, where they remained for so long bearing the punishment of captivity, as long as the house was being built, in which wickedness might sit, and be placed there upon its base to remain perpetually; that is, until the Babylonians filled the bushel with their crimes, and deserved the punishment of devastation to be effected by Cyrus and Darius, for then, with the measure paid out and the bushel completed, the two tribes returned, now never again to be punished by that bushel, having left Babylon, liberated from their wickedness and from the punishment following it. This is Castrius. But in truth, consolation could not be sought from the captivity, which he says is figured here, but rather liberation from captivity should be proposed. Nor did the tribes of Judah and Benjamin carry wickedness into Babylonia; but rather they were carried there because of wickedness, whence Castrius prefers to understand two evil spirits by the two women. But what is the sense, that the Angel caused wickedness to be carried by two evil spirits to Babylon, where it might sit, never to return to Judea? Cornelius à Lapide with some others understand Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuzaradan. But these women are joined as equals: but Nebuzaradan was a minister of Nebuchadnezzar. Franciscus Junius handed down this explanation: that to be relegated to Babylonia is the same as to be adjudged and implicated in the same judgment that awaited the other Jews who had preferred Babylonian life to a pious and holy life, and that by the two women is designated the Church of two times, when namely Ezra, sent from Babylon into Judea, constituted the Church, and purged the Church from those impious ones with whom it was defiled, Ezra IX; likewise when Nehemiah, with the counsel of the priests employed, did similarly, Nehemiah VII. Which interpretation Willius also embraced from the Reformed, fol. 151. That the Angel of God cast down thieves and perjurers and the wicked in general, all of them and the handles of wickedness together, from their state and the constant exercise of crimes, and by the weight of his providence

Latin:

Vers. 4.

EDUCAM ILLUD) Excerpam inde decreta in sin- gulos. ET COMMORABITUR IN MEDIO DOMUS EJUS, ET CONSUMET EAM ET LIGNA EJUS, ET LAPIDES EJUS) Nihil de domo reliquum fa- ciet. Sic & de pœna perjurii oraculum apud Herodotum Erato: -- Εἰσόκε πᾶσαν Συμμάρψας ὀλέσῃ γενεὴν καὶ οἶκον ἅπαντα.

Explicant hæc Interpp. de effectis falsæ doctrinæ, quæ maledictionem iis affert, qui eam recipiunt. Quoniam ergo pervasit totam Judæam, totusque populus spreto Christo, & ejus Evangelio istam exosculatus est, tandem ira & maledictio Domini terram & populum obruerunt. Lutherus ita vertit: Quia omnis fur inde ut innocens, & omnis perjurus inde sicut innocens. Fructus is falsæ doctrinæ & hu- manarum traditionum, quod avaritia, furta, men- dacia, omnisque impietas colore veritatis pinguntur, & pro peccatis non habentur. Ita Christus Phari- sæos accusat Matth. 23. Væ vobis &c. quia comedi- tis domos viduarum, orantes orationes longas. Rur- sus Matth. XV. ipsos accusat quod propter suas tra- ditiones transgrediantur Dei mandata, dicentes: munus vel sacrificium præstabilius esse obedientia erga 4. præceptum. Rursus æstimabant, aurum al- taris vel templi præstabilius ipso altari & templo esse Matth. 23. Denique in sacrificiis quærebant lucrum suum, eoque fine nummulariis, ementibus & vendentibus in ipso templo locum concedebant Luc. XIX. Joh. 12. Et tamen hæc, quæ revera erant furta, velamento pietatis, sanctitatis & cultus tege- bant. Ita etiam perjurus juxta librum illum inno- cens pronunciatur. Nam falsa doctrina etiam pe- culiare hoc habet, ut sub ipsius verbi Dei & Divini nominis titulo venditetur. Mendaciis Dei nomen prætexitur, quod revera est mentiri, pejerare, quemadmodum hoc nomine Dominus falsos Pro- phetas passim accusat, ut iterum hic Winckel- mannus: unde judicium Dei sequitur: EDUCAM ILLUD VOLUMEN: Dominus manifestabit a- varitiam, furta, mendacia & impietatem libri: ET VENIET AD DOMUM FURIS sc. volumen μετωνυμικῶς ipsum Judicium Dei, quod falsam do- ctrinam consequitur. ET CONSUMET EUM, id accidit Judæis, quemadmodum Dominus illis comminatus fuerat Matth. XXIII. Osiander, qui eandem interpretationem tradit de falsa doctrina, ita explicat: Et veniet justum meum judicium, ad domum furis. E. Tarnovius sententiam Dei non in- juria ferri oftendi hic putat: Quia quisquis furatur ex hoc sc. populo, ut illa, reliqua improborum in terra ac regione gentium degens colluvies, se in- nocentem asserit, & quisquis jurat falso ex hoc po- pulo, ut illa impiorum turba, profana, se innocen- tem asserit, factumque suum pessimum excusat. Pa- gninus & Vatablus cum R. Dav. Kimchio reddunt: Sicut scriptum est ex altera parte ipsius: quod volu- men in utraque parte, vel facie literis consigna- tum fuerit. Sic etiam Ludov. de Dieu.

Simplicior videtur interpretatio Cocceji, qui il- lud מזה reddit EX HOC sc. tempore, vel posthac

ἀπαγ]. Nam omnis furans ex hoc secundum illam evacuatur : & Belgarum atque Willii. Nam quisquis furatur ex hac (terra, quia præcedit ארץ, quod non minus masculinum est, quam fœmininum) secundum eam (מגלה fœminini generis est, secundum illud volumen) evacuatus est. Nomen נקה esse evacuare ex Esa. III. 26. Jerem. XLVI. 28. Willius docet. Sensus ergo juxta ipsum est, fures & perjuros, secundum maledictionis librum de terra removendos & perituros esse : ac per furta & perjuria Synecdochice quævis peccata contra tabulam secundam & primam designari, ut fures vocentur, qui officia caritatis violant, perjuri, qui cultum divinum negligunt, vel adulterant. Quo non modo aliorum plerorumque, sed etiam Grotii abit interpretatio, visum fuisse volumen, quod pœnas continuerit : Sed in eo abit à communi Interpp. sententia Grotius cum

Calvino & paucis aliis, quod ostendi velit rem non præsentem, aut futuram, sed jam olim gestam, quod probari nequit. Nam visiones illæ statum præsentem concernunt : agiturque hic de sceleribus istius temporis, & pœna irroganda, non irrogata, adeoque ostenditur potius, cur promissiones hactenus complementum suum consequutæ non sint, aut quænam adhuc in populo illo judicium divinum provocent, vel, ut alii, reformatione indigeant. Hæc autem seu dicantur falsa doctrina & superstitiones, seu peccata contra primam & secundam tabulam, scopo Prophetæ nihil decedit, unde vanum est ἔγκλημα Willii, quod nostrates hic plane à visionis scopo aberrent. Enimvero maledictionis super universam terram causa non minus statui potest falsa doctrina, qua etiam ipsimet fures & perjuri innocentes judicantur, ut exposuit B. Lutherus, quam scelus furti, perjurii, aut quodcunque aliud. Maluit autem B. Lutherus VOLUMEN illud de scripto falsis doctrinis & traditionibus referto, quam de libro judiciorum divinorum, vel ipso Legis libro, uti Willius cum Ruperto interpretatur, accipere, quia juxta librum illum fures & perjuri innocentes pronunciantur, uti verbum נקה usitatiori significatione est innocens fuit, quam Junius ipse hic sequutus est, siquidem non facile recedendum sit à famosiori significatione. Neque inconcinna videtur B. Lutheri explicatio, quæ T. IV. Jen. Germ. in h. l. & apud Winckelmann. legi poterit. Illam certe censuram non meruit, qua notavit eam Willius h. l. qui Calvinum potius suum hic castigare debuisset, quod ista visione ea, quæ jam olim gesta, exhibita esse contendat. Non videmus manticæ, quod in tergo est. Non dubium est, inquit Calvinus, quin Deus Zachariæ ostendere voluerit, Judæos merito pœnas dedisse, quia tota terra vel furtis vel perjuriis referta erat : Quoniam ergo contempta fuerat religio, deinde omnis æquitas & justitia, ideo ostendit, non esse mirum, si maledictio grassata fuerit per totam terram : quia scilicet Judæi sua impietate & suis sceleribus iram Dei ad extremum usque provocaverant. Συνέχειαν & explicationem sententiæ Lutheri ita tradit B. Balduin.

p. 313. Nos cum B. Luthero intelligimus de corruptelis orthodoxæ doctrinæ, & traditionibus humanis, quas loco verbi divini in populo Judaico & templo Hierosolymitano grassaturas præviderat Propheta. Utrumque enim populo suo significari voluit Dominus : & bonitatem Dei in renovando cultu verbi Dei per orthodoxos Ecclesiæ doctores, quos filios olei nominaverat in præcedente visione: & malitiam Diaboli in corrumpenda sana doctrina, & depravando cultu vero per ἐθελοθρησκείας hominum : ideoque opus esse, ut deinceps rerum suarum satagentes, caute vivant, nec omni spiritui cr- dant. Hæc autem omnia ita evenisse testatur sequentium temporum historia. Primum enim volare cœpit hoc volumen, quando templum Domini fuit conditum in monte Garizim, ad instar Hierosolymitani, autore Sanaballath quodam præfecto regio --- idque factum annis, post conditum templum secundum, centum nonaginta: ante inchoationem ministerii Christi, annis ferme trecentis sexaginta tribus. --- Deinde volavit hoc volumen iniquitatis ulterius quando Jason Pseudo-pontifex gymnasium gentilitatis è regione templi in ipsa urbe sancta erexit, ut describitur hæc impietas II. Maccab. IV. & I. Macc. I. in quo juventus Hebræorum in legibus & ritibus ethnicorum informaretur, in fraudem legis divinæ, Lev. XVIII. v. 3. c. 20. v. 23. idque factum est anno 300. ab edita hac Prophetæ nostri visione, annis fere 150. ante Christum natum: Tertio quando sequentibus annis Onias Sacerdos, sancti Oniæ Pontificis filius, cum multis Judæorum in Ægyptum profugus, templum ædificare cœpit apud Leontopolim in præfectura Heliopolitana, ad formam illius, quod erat in Hierusalem, ubi constitutis Levitis, & sacerdotibus cultum instituit divinum, fingens hoc pacto, se implere scripturam, quæ dixerat: In die illa erit altare Domini in medio terræ Ægpti Esa. 19. vers. 19. de qua abominatione videatur Josephus lib. 12. antiq. cap. 15. & lib. 13. cap. 6. --- Quarto, quando paulo post populus Judaicus in tres quasi sectas scindebatur, Pharisæorum, Sadducæorum & Essenorum, qui omnes aliena à lege Dei proponebant, & traditionibus humanis verum Dei cultum corrumpebant. --- Quinto quando Judæorum Thalmud Babylonicum conscribi cœpit, quo tota Judæorum regitur Synagoga, idque factum anno à secundi templi incendio 436. teste Galatino lib. 1. cap. 5. His igitur modis volumen illud impietatis Judæam imprimis regionem pervolavit, quamdiu templum stetit Hierosolymitanum, & cultus in eo publice viguit: unde & ejusdem magnitudinis cum atrio templi fuisse dicitur. Hæc Balduinus, ὁ μακαρίτης. Interea, si quis volumen illud de libro judiciorum & pœnarum Dei explicare malit, ac verbum נקה interpretetur, evacuatus est, non repugnabimus. Siquidem explicari videatur illud verbum נקה cum additur, maledictionem venturam in domum furis & perjuri, atque ita plerique Interpp. veteres Ebræi, Græci & Latini exponunt, sensu pœnali. Hieron. Theodor. Haymo, Rupertus, Remigius, Albertus M. Hugo, Lyra, &c. notante Castrio. Nec aliter metaphtastæ: Targum נקי percussus LXX. ἐκδικηθήσεται punietur. Vulgat. judicabitur. Arabicus Antiochenus ad mortem (damnabitur) Alexandrinus, pœnas dabit usque ad mortem. Unde è nostris B. Tarnovius (quod antea observavimus) monet, ostendi hac visione, qui factum, ut hactenus promissionum complementum nondum apparuerit, nempe quod ipsi nefarie contra legis divinæ utramque tabulam peccassent. De futuris etiam pœnis explicant Belgici Interpp. Junius, & alii. Rupertus, Dionysius, Vatablus & Montanus ad tempora Maccabæorum hæc judicia referunt, cum Antiochus in Judæos sæviit: sed quum Propheta potius in eo sit, ut populum meticulosum consoletur, mavult cum Theodoreto Castrius, significari, projectam jam esse maledictionem hoc volumine contentam, aut certe procul à Dei populo in domum furis, aut pejerantis cujuscunque projiciendam, quemadmodum postea impietas procul pellitur, & ejicitur in Babylonem. Verum enim vero, etsi Propheta fideles consoletur Babylone reversos, quia tamen illis admixti fuere non pauci reprobi, qui per captivitatem Ba- bylonicam, ut fieri amat, non meliores, sed-dete- riores facti, minatur Zacharias, illorum domos con- sumtum iri propriis sceleribus. Nam hæ minæ non feriunt gentes, sed Judæos, IN NOMINE DO- MINI falso jurantes. Coccejus refert hoc ad tem- pora postrema secundi templi. Summi Prophetia est, inquit, instare tempus, ubi propterFurtum &Per- jurium populi & principum ejus legis exsecratio sit grassatura in totum populum, & in ipsum tem- plum, ut jam non amplius Dei domum, sed do- mum furis & perjuri,quippe Dei Filio aliud tem- plum ædificante cap. VI. 13. Quæ ejus sententia, quantum ad tempus & summam rei, de furto & perjurio Principum populi, divina maledictione puniendo, à B.Lutheri explicatione aliena non est, etiamsi volumen volans non de volumine falsæ do- ctrinæ, sed exsecrationis & judicii Dei intelligat. Quanquam utraque explicatio certo modo forsan conjungi possit, hac ratione sc. quod volumine hoc falsa doctrina designata sit, qua judicio & exe- crationi Dei obnoxia, vel una cum anathemate divino.

nitioni & excidio eorundem à Deo decretam & bræfinitam,qua sensim impleta Judæi puniti & ex- cisi sunt: Impleta autem hæc mensura fuit tempo- re Sedeciæ, & castigata à Deo captivitate Babylo- nica. Vidit ergo Zacharias amphoram sive mensu- ram, in qua sedebat impietas, è Judæa transferri in Babylonem, quo significat impietatem Judææ, im- pioíque Judæos translatos esse in Babylonem, ac proinde Judæam jam esse ab impietate expurga- tam & puram, Babylonem vero esse sedem & clo- acam impietatis, quocirca impietatem in Babylo- ne mansuram, nec amplius in Judæam reditu- ram. Hinc deinceps idololatria non est visa in Ju- dæa, quia illam, cum sua amphora, id est, pœ- na, Judæi reliquerunt in Babylone, quando ejus mensura per septuaginta annos persoluta, expiati, & liberi redierunt in Jerusalem. Hæc Cornelius in h. l. p.206. Cujus interpretationi consonant Ca- strii, Menochii & aliorum glossæ. Hi ergo ad hi- stotias præteritas referunt cum Grotio: sed in eo discrepant, quod Grotius tum ad tribus decem, tum ad populum Judaicum hæc pertinere velit, ac per duas mulieres intelligat utrumque illum popu- lum: Cæteri autem plerique referant ad duas tri- bus Juda & Benjamin, & captivitatis Babyloni- cæ tempora. Consolatur, inquit Castrius, duas tribus, quæ Babylone redierant, in quam ductæ fuerant captivæ, non decem, quæ ad Assyrios du- ctæ sunt, nec unquam reversæ. Duæ mulieres, nempe duæ tribus Juda, & Benjaminis portaverunt modium, id est, punitionem suorum peccatorum, præsertim idololatriæ in Babylonem, ubi tamdiu permanserunt ferentes pœnam captivitatis,quam- diu domus ædificata est, in qua consideret im- pietas, & collocaretur ibi super basim suam per- petuo mansura; hoc est, donec Babylonii suis sceleribus impleverunt modium, & meruerunt punitionem vastitatis per Cyrum, & Darium ef- ficiendæ, tunc enim exoluto dimenso, & modio absoluto, duæ tribus redieruut, jam nunquam ultra modio illo puniendæ, relicta Babylone, li- beratæ ab impietate sua, & à pœna illam conse- quente. Hæc Castrius. Verum enim vero conso- latio non è captivitate peti poterat, quam hic fi- guratam dicit, sed proponenda ita potius libera- tio è captivitate. Neque tribus Iuda & Benjamin portarunt impietatem in Babyloniam; sed potius eo portatæ sunt ob impietatem, unde per mulieres duas mavult Castrius duos malos Spiritus intellige- re. At quis sensus, Angelus per duos malos Spi- ritus impietatem portari fecit Babylonem, ubi consideret nunquam in Judæam reditura? Corne- lius à Lapide cum aliis nonnullis Nabuchodonosso- rem & Nebuzaradan intelligunt. Sed hæ mulie- res ceu æquales junguntur: Nabuzaradan autem Minister Nebucadnezaris. Franciscus Iunius hanc tradidit explicationem, in Babyloniam relegari i- dem esse, quod adjudicari atque implicari eodem ju- dicio, quod manebat Iudæos cæteros, qui Babyloni- cam vitam pia & sanctæ vitæ prætulerant, & per duas mulieres designari Ecclesiam duorum tempo- rum, cum nempe Esdras ex Babylone in Judæam missus, Ecclesiam constituit, & ab impiis illis, quibus commaculata fuit, Ecclesiam repurgavit, Esdr. IX. item cum Nehemia adhibito sacerdo- tum consilio similiter fecit Nehem. VII. Quam in- terpretationem amplexus etiam est è Reformatis Willius fol. 151. Angelum Dei fures & perjuros ac improbos in universum omnes & ansas impieta- tis conjunctim de statu suo & jugi exercitio sce- lerum dejecisse, & providentiæ suæ pondere

## 5:5
Verse 5.

THE ANGEL WENT FORTH) He returned who had gone away, to explain the new vision. WHO WAS SPEAKING IN ME) To me, as above several times. WHICH GOES FORTH) From the Temple, that is, God ordaining.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

EGRESSVS EST ANGELUS) Rediit qui abierat, ad novum visum explicandum. QUI LOQUEBATUR IN ME) Mihi, ut supra a- liquoties. QUOD EGREDITUR) E Templo, id est, Deo or- dinante.

## 5:6
Verse 6.

THIS IS THE EPHAH THAT GOETH FORTH) The ephah going forth, that is, the measure of sins has reached its height. Ephah is the name of a measure for dry goods, corresponding almost to a modius. It is shown as a thing not future, but done, so that the Jews may beware in the future of bringing similar punishments upon themselves. THIS IS THEIR EYE IN ALL THE EARTH) This eye signifies a form, Levit. XIII. 55, Num. XI. 6, Ezech. I. 16. The sense is, that which you see bears the figure of those things which the Hebrews have done, and which they have suffered.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

HÆC EST AMPHORA EGREDIENS) Epha egre- diens,id est,mensura peccatorum ad summum venit. Epha nomen mensuræ aridorum, modio ferme respondens. Ostenditur res non futura, sed gesta, ut Judæi in posterum caveant similes pœnas in se accersere. HOC EST OCULUS EORUM IN UNIVERSA TERRA) Oculus hic formam significat Levit. XIII. 55. Num, XL. 6. Ezech. I. 16. Sensus est, id quod vides, figu- ram gerit eorum, quæ fecere Hebræi, quæque passi sunt.

## 5:7
Verse 7.

AND BEHOLD A TALENT OF LEAD WAS CARRIED) A mass. For ככר signifies every large part of any thing whatsoever. AND BEHOLD ONE WOMAN SITTING IN THE MIDST OF THE EPHAH) That is, upon the Ephah: proud, and fearing no evil. THIS IS WICKEDNESS) Namely, the mother of both thefts and perjuries, and of all crimes. AND HE CAST IT INTO THE MIDST OF THE EPHAH) Inside the Ephah.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET ECCE TALENTUM PLUMBI PORTA- BATUR) Massa. Nam ככר omnem partem magnam cujuscunque rei significat. ET ECCE MULIER UNA SEDENS IN ME- DIO AMPHORÆ) Id est, super Epha: superba, & nihil mali metuens. HÆC EST IMPIETAS) Mater scilicet & furto- rum & perjuriorum, & omnium scelerum. ET PROJECIT EAM IN MEDIO AMPHORÆ) Intra Epha.

## 5:8
Verse 8.

AND HE CAST THE LEADEN MASS INTO THE MOUTH THEREOF) Namely, of the Ephah, so that there might be no exit.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET MISIT MASSAM PLUMBEAM IN OS E- JUS) Nempe Ephæ, nequis esset exitus.

## 5:9
Verse 9.

TWO WOMEN GOING FORTH) From the temple. These are the two nations, one of the ten, the other of the two tribes, as the Chaldean takes it here. AND THE SPIRIT IN THEIR WINGS) That is, they were propelled by a carrying wind: by this is signified the swiftness of the deportations: those wings are the Assyrians and Babylonians. AND THEY HAD WINGS, AS THE WINGS OF A KITE (חסידה others translate stork, others ἐρώδιον, others hoopoe, the Chaldean eagle. See what we have said on Job XXXIX, 13. The wings of the stork, that is, wings causing migration. AND THEY LIFTED UP THE EPHAH BETWEEN HEAVEN AND EARTH) Namely, those wings.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

DUÆ MULIERES EGREDIENTES) ETemplo. Hæ sunt gentes duæ,altera decem, altera duarum tribuum, ut hic sumit Chaldæus. ET SPIRITUS IN ALIS EARUM) Id est, ex vento ferente propellebantur: significatur per hoc celeri- tas deportationum: alæ istæ sunt Assyrii & Babylonii. ET HABEBANT ALAS, QUASI ALAS MIL- VI( חסידה alii transferunt ciconiam, alii ἐρώδιον, a- lii upupam, Chaldæus aquilam. Vide quæ diximus Job. XXXIX, 13. alæ ciconiæ, id est, alæ transmigrare facientes. ET LEVAVERUNT AMPHORAM INTER COELUM ET TERRAM) Nempe alæ istæ.

## 5:11
Verse 11.

THAT A HOUSE MAY BE BUILT FOR IT IN THE LAND OF SHINAR) In Babylonia. See Gen. XI. 2, and what we have said in the Annotations to the first book on the Truth of the Christian Religion. Babylonia, however, was first under the Assyrians, then the royal seat of the Chaldeans. AND IT SHALL BE ESTABLISHED, AND SET THERE UPON ITS OWN BASE) As idols are accustomed to be, which thereafter cannot depart. This is, those two nations were detained for a very long time in the places beyond the Euphrates. Let the Jews therefore beware, lest the same happen again. Compare what we had above III. 7.

…Cornelius à Lapide almost similarly, the ephah or Ephah signifies the measure of the sins of the Jews

to contain the compressed things until they are read through in their entirety. And page 153. The sense is that all the ungodly will be cast out of the Church forever and will eventually be involved in a similar judgment with the ungodly despisers of God in Babylon, which he thinks was done by the work of Ezra and Nehemiah. Our Tarnovius also embraced this on page 138. Why two women are joined in this place is not the opinion of all interpreters: to me, that which is Junius's commends itself most; namely, because the Church is often compared to a woman, it designates the Church of two times quickly purged of evils, one, which the Church that Ezra, sent from Babylon into Judea, established and purged as quickly as could be done from the ungodly with whom it had been defiled, Ezra 9. and 10, especially verse 8; the other, when Nehemiah, by the counsel of the priests, did the same, Nehemiah 13, which two reformers were in themselves weak, and yet they courageously executed this judgment of God. These are the words of the blessed Tarnovius, who paraphrases verse 11 thus: He said and answered to me: he shall banish that wickedness, and as many as obstinately adhere to it, out of the Church by perpetual banishment, that she may build for herself a house in the land of Shinar, that is, Babylon itself, Genesis 10:10. and chapter 11, verse 5, where it may be established and placed, that she may reside there for a long time, nay, dwell and stay there perpetually, which is wont to be figured by the building of a house, Jeremiah 29:5, 28, as we also say proverbially: Wir wollen da kein Hauß bauen, that is, we shall not stay there for long: but let her be placed on her base or that seat where they had already previously been founded and rooted and had drunk in their most corrupt customs, and where their brothers, neglecting the benefits of God, fixed their seats, 1 Chronicles 4:22, 23.

Most others of our countrymen, with the blessed Luther, understand by the woman sitting in the basket or ephah an ungodly doctrine, which is said to sit because false teachers affect authority, Matthew 23:2. And let her sit in the middle, that is, let her occupy the minds of hypocrites, who seek only their own advantages by teaching, therefore at length by the just judgment of God, like some heavy lead (because it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Lord, Hebrews 10:31), let her be cast down to the bottom, so that although she may seem to have the applause of the crowd for a time, she can never truly emerge. Those flying women, therefore, are false teachers, who are compared to women because of their weakness, because they have nothing manly, nothing of strength due to the defect from God, 1 Timothy 2:14. and they are likened to fornication, which is attributed to a woman rather than to men, because of her beautiful external appearance: also because of paint and blandishments, and because of useless garrulity: and they are two because of their mutual conspiracy, and they carry around the basket of impiety between heaven and earth: because heretical doctrine is doubtful and pendulous, which will find no place of rest and certainty anywhere. She has wings: for she flies through all places with wonderful speed. Others interpret the Hebrew חסידה as a stork, others as an ostrich. The blessed Luther, with Jerome, translates it as a kite. But the wings of a kite are attributed to false teachers, because the kite is an ill-omened and unclean bird, Leviticus 11, most rapacious and famished.

But in the land of Shinar this impiety finally finds a stable seat, by which they understand the dispersion of the Jews into all lands, just as in the land of Shinar their languages were confused and as it were dispersed, in which dispersion they are established who stubbornly defend their opinion, even if they hang between heaven and earth by their contumacy, while they await an earthly Messiah, but they cannot have this Messiah, and they can have his spiritual kingdom preached in this world, but they do not want such a Messiah, and thus they are destitute of political and ecclesiastical government. Some fix that seat in the underworld, where there is no order, but mere confusion more than Babylonian, just as Babylon is also called the habitation of demons. Cocceius, according to his custom, proceeds here more specifically to the later times of the New Testament, but his singular and perplexed interpretation will not easily deserve applause.

These things seem to militate for the opinion of the blessed Luther. (1) That all things do not harmonize badly if these are explained concerning false doctrine. (2) That one vision explains and illustrates another. (3) That the word נקה, retained in its received and customary sense, confirms the same: for according to false doctrine, thieves and those swearing falsely are pronounced innocent, but not according to the volume of the judgments and decrees of God, and these are the marks of false teachers: first, to seek private advantages and to steal the goods of the hearers, 2 Peter 2:3, Philippians 3:19; then to tell lies, Ezekiel 13:19, Romans 16:18, and to paint, confirm, and propagate the same by their perjuries. (4) A curse is designated here, which goes forth over the WHOLE EARTH. Therefore, it is not to be understood concerning certain wicked persons among the people of God. But false doctrine has inundated the whole earth and filled it with a curse. (5) That it is hinted at similarly when this is called the face of the WHOLE EARTH. For it is not fitting here to understand providence by the word עין, but the face or external appearance, as in Ezekiel 10:5, where we have Grotius agreeing; the eye here signifies form, Leviticus 13:55, Numbers 11:6, Ezekiel 7:16. Nor is there any need to inquire how the appearance of false teachers is similar to a measure or basket, because it indeed seems to be a basket, but that alone does not complete the vision; for in it is seen a woman sitting, and a mass of lead, which was placed upon the measure like a lid, so that the woman might be thrust down to the bottom of the measure. For all these things are rightly referred to one vision, which Willius also observed, namely that the first member of the response, this ephah which goes forth, can be understood concerning the ephah itself, so that the remaining words, exhibiting the second member of the response: This is their appearance in all the land, do not explain what the ephah signifies, but are understood concerning the woman sitting in the ephah. For there was already then without doubt a woman in the ephah, as can be gathered from the following verse 7, where זאת seems to denote such a woman who had already been seen before, and concerning whom speech had already been held before, so that the sense is that the woman sitting in the ephah is the appearance and living image of the impious Jews. (6) What was the point of exhibiting the crimes and punishments committed and endured eighty years before by new visions of the flying scroll and the woman sitting in the ephah? Prophetic visions are accustomed to figure not past things, but future ones. (7) It does not seem to agree sufficiently with the argument and scope of our Prophet if it is said that those things which had already been done long ago were adumbrated by those visions, since he intends to excite the people to promote the structure of the temple and to restore divine worship, and at the same time to excite them to the work of the Lord by promises and threats. Therefore, this was not the time to exhibit by visions things already done, which were otherwise not unknown to them, and had been sufficiently adumbrated in advance by the Prophets of earlier times, the very event confirmed by the vision predetermined, says Wil- lius on chap. VI. verse 6. (8) Cornelius à Lapide, and Menochius indicate not obscurely that the sense concerning the transportation of the Jews into the Babylonian captivity does not satisfy them, inasmuch as they understand it of the jar and the measure of sins having begun to be filled after the return from Babylon, and gradually filled over 360 years, and evacuated by Antiochus Epiphanes in the time of the Maccabees, but especially and fully filled by the parricide, nay, Deicide, Matt. XXIII. verse 32, where they were punished with extreme and eternal destruction, so that in the land of Shinar, that is, in the whole world, as Sanctius also explained, they wander as vagabonds and fugitives. They add from Emanuel Saa, Ribera, [and] Fernandez, that the Anti-Christ will truly be worshipped by the Jews even in the land of Shinar, that is, in Babylon, as if it were a stable and firm place of the Kingdom: but this is a fabrication about a Utopian Jewish Anti-Christ, whom the Papists have devised, so that they might not have need to acknowledge their own Pope as the Anti-Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

UT ÆDIFICETVR EI DOMVS IN TERRA SENAAR) In Babylonia. Vid. Gen. XI. 2. & quæ diximus in Annotatis ad librum primum de Veritate Religionis Christianæ. Babylonia autem primo sub Assyriis fuit, Inde Chaldæorum Regia. ET STABILIATUR, ET PONATUR IBI SV- PER BASEN SVAM) Sicut idola solent, quæ deinde abire non possunt. Hoc est, duæ istæ gentes longissimo tempore detentæ fuere in locis trans Euphratem. Ca- veant ergo sibi Judæi, ne idem rursus eveniat. Confer quæ habuimus supra III. 7.

Similiter fere Cornelius à Lapide, amphora sive Epha significat mensuram peccatorum Judæorum pu-

compressa continere, donec in totum rele- gentur. Et pag. 153. Sensus est, omnes im- pios in perpetuum ex Ecclesia ejectum iri & simi- li judicio involvendos aliquando cum impiis De in Babylone contemtoribus, quod opera Esdræ & Nehemiæ factum putat. Amplexus eam etiam est Tarnovius noster pag. 138. Cur hoc loco duæ conjungantur mulieres, non una omnium inter- pretum est sententia: mihi se maxime probat illa, quæ est Junij; nempe quia fere cum muliere com- paratur Ecclesia, designari Ecclesiam duorum temporum cito a malis repurgatam, unam, quam Esdras ex Babylonia in Judæam missus Ecclesiam Judaicam constituit, & ab impiis, quibus com- maculata erat, quam celerrime fieri potuit, re- purgavit Esd. 9. & 10. imprimis vers. 8. alteram, quando Nehemia adhibitio sacerdotum consilio idem fecit Nehem. 13. qui duo reformatores in se fatis erant imbecilles, & tamen Dei hanc senten- tiam fortiter exequebantur. Hæc B. Tarnovius, qui vers. 11. ita παραφράζει: Dixit ac respondit ille mihi: releget eam improbitatem, & quotquot illi obstinate adhærent, extra Ecclesiam relega- tione perpetua, ut ædificet sibi domum in terra Sin- haris, hoc est, ipsa Babylonia Genes. X. 10. & c. 11. v. 5. ubi stabiliatur & collocetur, ut sibi diu resideat, imo perpetuo habitet, ac commoretur, id quod domus ædificatione solet figurari Jer. XXIX. 5. 28. ut & nos proverbialiter dicimus: Wir wollen da kein Hauß bauen/ hoc est, non diu ibi commo- rabimur: collocetur vero in basi sua seu sede illa, ubi jam antea fundati & radicati corruptissimos suos mores hauserunt, & ubi fratres ipsorum ne- glectis Dei beneficiis sedes suas fixerunt I. Chron. IV. 22. 23.

Plerique alii nostrates cum B. Luthero per mu- lierem in amphora vel Epha sedentem impiam do- ctrinam intelligunt, quæ sedere dicitur, quia falsi Doctores authoritatem affectant Matth. XXIII. 2. Et in medio sedeat, hoc est, occupet animos hypo- critarum, qui sua tantum docendo quærunt com moda, ideo tandem justo Dei judicio, veluti ponderoso quodam plumbo (quia grave est in- cidere in manus Domini Ebr. X. vers. 35.) ad imum præcipitetur, ut licet ad tempus applausum vulgi habere videatur, nunquam tamen vere emergere possit. Mulieres ergo illæ volantes sunt falsi do- ctores, qui mulieribus ob imbecillitatem, quia nihil habent virile, nihil roboris ob defectum a Deo I. Timoth. II. vers. 14. & fornicationem, quæ mulieri tribuitur præ viris, ob speciem externam formosam: ob fucum item & blanditias, & ob inutilem garrulitatem assimilantur: & duæ sunt ob mutuam conspirationem, ac circumferunt am- phoram impietatis intra cœlum & terram: quia do- ctrina hæretica dubia est, & pendula, quæ nu- spiam quietis & certitudinis locum inveniet. Alas habet: Mira enim celeritate omnia loca pervolat. Ebræum חסידה alij ciconiam, alij Struthionem interpretantur. B. Lutherus cum Hieronymo mil- vum vertit. Milvi autem alæ falsis Doctoribus tri- buuntur, quia milvus est avis infausta & immunda Lev. XI. rapacissima & famelica.

In terra autem Sinear demum stabilem invenit hæc impietas sedem, per quam dispersionem Ju- dæorum in omnes agros intelligunt, quemad- modum in agro Sennear linguæ ipsorum fuerunt confusæ, & quasi dispersæ, in qua dispersione sta- biliuntur, qui præfracte sententiam suam tuen- tur, etsi inter cœlum & terram sua contumacia pendeant, dum Messiam terrenum expectant, sed hunc habere non possunt Messiam, & ejus regnum spirituale in hoc mundo prædicatum habere possunt, sed talem Messiam nolunt, atque sic politico & Ecclesiastico regimine destituuntur. Nonnulli sedem illam apud inferos figunt, ubi nullus est ordo, sed mera confusio plusquam Babylonica, quemadmodum & Babylon habitatio dæmonum dicitur. Coccejus pro more specialius hic progreditur ad tempora ulterioraNovi Testamenti, sed singularis ejus & perplexa interpretatio, non facile applausum merebitur.

Pro B. Lutheri sententia hæc militare videntur. (1) Quod ita omnia non male consonent, si de doctrinâ falsâ hæc explicentur. (2) quod una visio alteram explicet atque illustret. (3) quod verbum נקה sensu recepto & usitato retentum eandem confirmet: nam juxta falsam doctrinam fures & mendaciter jurantes innocentes pronunciantur, non vero juxta volumen judiciorum & decretorum Dei, & notæ hæ sunt falsorum doctorum, primo privata quærere commoda, & auditorum bona furari II. Petr. II. vers. 3. Philipp. III. vers. 19. tum mendacia dicere Ezech. XIII. vers. 19. Roman. XVI. vers. 8. eademque perjuriis suis pingere, confirmare ac propagare. (4) Maledictio hic designatur, quæ egreditur super UNIVERSAM TERRAM. Non ergo de quibusdam sceleratis in populo Dei ea intelligenda. Doctrina autem falsa inundavit terram universam, eamque maledictione replevit. (5) Quod innuitur similiter, cum hæc dicitur facies UNIVERSÆ TERRÆ. Non enim convenit hic providentiam per vocem עין intelligere, sed faciem seu speciem externam, ut Ezech. X. vers. 5. ubi annuentem habemus Grotium; oculus hic formam significat Levit. XIII. vers. 55. Num. XI. vers. 6. Ezech. VII. vers. 16. Neque vero opus est, ut disquiratur, quomodo falsorum doctorum species similis sit modio vel amphoræ, quia videtur quidem amphora, sed ea sola non absolvit visionem; nam in ea conspicitur mulier sedens, & massa plumbi, quæ operculi instar modio imponebatur, ut mulier in imum modij detruderetur. Hæc enim omnia ad unam visionem recte referuntur, quod etiam Willius observavit, primum nempe responsi membrum hæc epha, quæ progreditur, de ipsa epha accipi posse, ut verba reliqua, alterum responsi membrum exhibentia: Hæc est facies ipsorum in universa terra, non explicent, quid epha significet, sed de muliere in epha sedente intelligantur. Fuit enim jam tum mulier absque dubio in epha, quemadmodum ex vers. 7. sequente colligere licet, ubi זאת notare ejusmodi mulierem videtur, quæ jam ante visa, & de qua jam ante sermo habitus, ut sensus sit, mulierem ephæ insidentem esse faciem ac imaginem vivam impiorum Judæorum. (6) Quid attinebat flagitia & supplicia ante octoaginta annos patrata & exantlata novis visionibus voluminis volantis & mulieris amphoræ insidentis exhibere? Visiones Propheticæ figurare solent non res præteritas, sed futuras. (7) Non satis argumento & scopo Prophetæ nostri convenire videtur, si dicatur, visionibus istis adumbrata fuisse, quæ jam gesta olim erant, siquidem intendat excitare populum, ad promovendum structuram templi, & restaurandum cultum divinum, & simul promissionibus, & comminationibus ad opus Domini excitet. Non ergo hic tempus erat, res gestas visionibus exhibere, quæ ipsis alioquin non ignotæ, ac per Prophetas superiorum temporum in antecessum satis adumbratæ fuere, ipso eventu comprobatas in visione præfinita, ait Wil- lius ad cap. VI. vers. 6. (8) Cornelius à Lapide, & Menochius haud obscure indicant, sibi non sa- tisfacere sensum de transportatione Judæorum in captivitatem Babylonicam, siquidem de amphora & mensura peccatorum post reditum è Babylone impleri cœpta, & sensim per 360. annos impleta, ac per Antiochum Epiphanem tempore Macca- bæorum evacuata, sed imprimis plane & plene per parricidium, imo Deicidium impleta Matth. XXIII. vers. 32. intelligant, ubi extremo & æter- no excidio puniti sunt, ut in terra Sinear, id est, toto orbe, uti Sanctius etiam exposuit, vagi & pro- fugi exulent. Addunt isti ex Emanuele Saa, Ribe- ra, Fernandez, vere etiam in terra Sennaar, id est, in Babylone, quasi stabili & firmo loco Re- gni Anti-Christum à Judæis cultum iri: sed hoc è commento est de Utopico Anti-Christo Judaico, quem Papistæ excogitarunt, ne Papam suum pro Anti-Christo agnoscere opus habeant.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

The eighth vision of four chariots with a command concerning the crowns to be placed on Joshua.

The Prophet saw four chariots coming out from the midst of two mountains of bronze with horses red, black, white, and dappled, which are explained as the four winds (however, angelic hosts are noted, sent forth for the sake of defense throughout Judea, for the comfort of the faithful.) Finally, a symbolic precept is added concerning two crowns for Joshua, and his prophetic explanation concerning Christ the Branch, under whom all things will sprout, our King and Priest.

The winds are in the horses: the temple stands by King Branch.

Ver. 1.

AND I TURNED) As above V. 1. BEHOLD FOUR CHARIOTS) Four chariots, they are four empires, as the Chaldean explains here.

Not only the Chaldean, but also Jerome, Cyril, Remigius, Haymo, and among the Pontificals Lyranus, Arias, Ribera, Sanchez, Fernandez, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, Reyrola, etc., interpret them as four Kingdoms, but they understand the IV. Monarchies, in which Grotius diverges from them; but Scripture, as observed by Tarnovius, does not denote by chariots the kingdoms, which are indicated in Daniel by parts of the body and four animals. Nor is it declared here what has happened, or is to come, in political kingdoms, but rather in the spiritual Kingdom of Christ. Nor does that explanation sufficiently agree with the angelic interpretation, which must be entirely attended to. Calvin, although he refers the horses to empires, nevertheless judges that those diverse colors pertain to the state of the Church of God. Blessed Luther explains the four chariots as the preaching of the Gospel in all parts of the world, in the time of the New Testament, which he made his exposition, and which Blessed Balduinus illustrated. Coccejus understands them as warlike hosts, to which, however, he says that angels can be joined, moving rather evil ones than good. He judges that between two Kingdoms, one of the house of David, the other of Christ, indicated by the two mountains, four intermediate Kingdoms with their armies or hosts are signified as about to brood over the promised land, and that under the fourth the Kingdom of Christ is about to arise. Not a few interpreters today, with Theodoret, take them as four hosts of good angels, such as among the Pontificals Palatius [and] Castrius, among the Reformed Fr. Junius and others, and indeed most of our own. This opinion is supported by the fact that angels are figured by chariots in 2 Kings II. verse 11, chapter VI. verse 16, Psalm LXVIII. verse 18. & in this Prophet various horses were seen, white & red, when the angels, companions of the Son of God, appeared among the myrtle trees, and because in verse 5 the same explanation seems to be delivered by the Angel speaking in Zechariah; These are the four Spirits of heaven (or celestial ones, or angels stationing themselves before God from the four parts of heaven, and running forth from Him to execute His commands Job 1. verse 6. 1 Kings 22. verse 19.) which go forth, that they may stand before the Lord of all the earth. Concerning whom Christ. à Castro thus: The chariot of Angels, which was carried by black horses, was sent into the Northern land, about to bring extreme destruction to the Chaldeans, the enemies of the Jews, through the Medes and Persians. The chariot of Angels of white horses was sent after the former, that they might lead the Jews, gifted with liberty, back into their fatherland through those same joyful ones. The chariot of Angels of various horses was sent toward the South, that they might restrain the enemies of the Jews, who envied their happiness, according to the variety of the nations, so that they might not harm them in any matter. Junius verse 6 thus renders it: Those who are in that chariot (those red horses named in verse 2, which Christ was pointing out with his finger) go forth into the Northern land (that is, Babylonia, which is called Northern with respect to Judea) & those white ones go forth after them: but those spotted with hail go forth into the Southern land (of the Jews, which with respect to Babylon, to which the other angels had set out, is Southern.) The sense is, the greater part of those angels, the ministers of God, set out into Babylonia, that they might care for the Jews, who still remained among their enemies; but a part was occupied in Judea, that it might minister to the people of God dwelling therein. Red ones, says Willius, denote the executors of divine judgments, through flames & the sword, black ones the bringers-in of dark calamities, white ones the consolers, and preservers of peace and tranquility, those spotted with hail such as partly punish, and partly raise up and defend. But the common condition of these horses, as it were, is that they all are אֲמֻצִּים robust, confirmed, as Junius translates, namely for the work to which they were girded, instructed by the power of God. He says that these four רוּחוֹת Spirits collectively are the four armies of celestial spirits, who execute the commands of God through all the regions of heaven. He says that those who translate: THESE GO FORTH TO THE FOUR WINDS of the heavens, offer violence to both the construction and the distinction of the text. But he renders the words subjoined thus: They go forth from there, where they stood before the Lord of the whole earth, so that it may be explained what is signified by those brazen mountains, namely that they are sent into the world by the providence of GOD, who presses the whole face of the earth with His command. But Willius at the beginning indeed delivered the same sense as Junius, concerning angels of three colors, white, black & red, to be sent into Babylon, that they might there exercise the judgments of the Lord upon the disobedient, while among others darkness dispel with their light, and assist them with comfort, and concerning the hail-colored angels destined for Judea, because as the color of the hail-colored horses is mixed, so in Judea itself also the situation was still very confused, so that they had need of a warning and an uplifting. But after those things, the opinion concerning these later angels having been suddenly changed, the same Willius determined that they were sent into Egypt, since he saw that Drusius takes the land of the South for Egypt, which is called the King of Egypt in Judea of the South, as in Dan. XI. verse 4. The King of the South is called the King of Egypt, and that he cites the canon of Jerome, that in these descriptions of regions it is to be observed that κλίματα, that is, the regions of a city according to the position of Jerusalem and the temple, are called so in the Scriptures. But they were sent into Egypt for the reason that even there many Jews still lingered, who had fled there, and whose care God was undertaking, because they too were one day to be united into one body of the Church through Christ. Wherefore he affirms that the next ones following, the CONFIRMED, constitute a distinct troop, and he thinks that they ought to have traversed Judea itself, which he wishes to be denoted by הגדיה Ha-jediah, whose observers are said to be peculiarly strong and confirmed, because these ought to have peculiarly comforted, uplifted, and defended Judea, and resisted their enemies, and established their Republic until the coming of Christ, and preserved it in the greatest disturbances, so that it might be indicated that, while elsewhere the visible Church is to migrate from place to place, in Judea itself, however, it is to be confirmed. Finally, the angels sent there are said to have quieted the Spirit of the Lord in the Northern land, because they did His will, as the Targum renders it, by exercising the judgments of the Lord against the impious, so that His fury might be stayed, but in the case of the remnants of the pious, by keeping them in the course of integrity, so that the Jews to whom these things are explained might be able to gather from this that it would not go very badly with everyone in Babylon, but that in a most deplorable and desperate state God would preserve His remnants, and that the passive crowd of the impious having been removed by just judgments, He would embrace the little flock of the faithful with His benevolence and grace. Thus far, therefore, is the opinion of Junius (especially as it has been illustrated by Willius), to which, although the blessed Tarnovius agrees in most things, he nevertheless institutes the application a little differently: It is signified, he says, by the type of the four chariots, through the ministry of the holy angels, that many who were still lingering in Judea, and also in Babylonia itself, but who would shortly come to Jerusalem, would be received into favor and saved, having consecrated themselves and their own to God. And afterwards he warns that the angels would quiet Babylonia, and concerning those to the kingdom

of Christ to be called, it is treated here, and it is taught that not all living outside of Judea are entirely excluded from the grace of God, since even in the midst of Babylon many pious ones are kept whole, and those from afar, or the nations, are one day to come to the kingdom of Christ. The Belgian paraphrasts, however, with Daneus, as also the blessed Wigandus among our own, interpret it indeed concerning the fourfold army of the angels, but in such a way that it is hinted that God, by their ministry, would repress the attempts of the enemies and establish peace, so that they might be able to restore the temple according to the command of God. Similarly, the blessed Winckelmannus explains it concerning the good angels and their singular ministry in procuring and promoting the peace of the people among the Persians and neighboring kingdoms; he says that various horses went out against the Egyptians and Idumeans, to prohibit likewise all hostile motions there. So also the blessed Pappus: It is signified by this vision that the Lord will grant halcyon days to this Republic, nor will He permit it to be dissipated again before the exhibition of the Messiah. But in order that the pious, whom present weakness and, on the contrary, the fury of the enemies terrified, might the more place their faith in this promise, the Lord again brings onto the stage that most firm army of holy Angels fighting for the Church and executing the divine will against the furies of the Devil and the world. To these are added the blessed Himmelius, the Weimar Paraphrase, and the Osiandrian: The various colors of the horses signify the various power and various effects of the angels, by which they break the attempts undertaken against the Church, so that in the meantime the Church may enjoy tranquility.

Verse of the same.

COMING OUT FROM THE MIDST OF TWO MOUNTAINS, AND THE MOUNTAINS, THE BRAZEN MOUNTAINS) He understands the gates of Cilicia, among the mountain passes, through which the Babylonians and Persians, and also Alexander and his leaders, were accustomed to pass into Syria, Judea, and Egypt.

That the gates among the mountain passes are designated by the brazen mountains, whence shall it be taught? And how did all four empires come out through the gates of Cilicia? To others, the two brazen mountains signify Mount Moriah, on which the temple was being built, and Mount Zion, on which the palace of David had been: because on Mount Moriah God had promised that He would be present, and would dwell as it were in His own domicile in the temple: Which are called brazen, so that it may be signified that the Lord would confirm the Priesthood and the Polity of the Jews, so that they might be able to stand most strongly against the insults of enemies. Thus Osiander, Wigandus, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and others. Nor does anything stand in the way of this explanation, that this revelation was made from heaven, and that the angels ought in no way to have gone out of Jerusalem, but rather to have entered it, so that they might guard it. For even in assemblies, when a revelation was made, the mountains could overshadow Jerusalem, nor because some angelic hosts seem to go forth from there is Jerusalem entirely deprived of angelic protection. There was on Mount Moriah, as it were, the Palace of the Lord, because it pleased Him to fix His seat there, 1 Kings 8; therefore, angelic hosts are seen to come forth from there. Wherefore, there is no reason why we should explain the bronze mountains, concerning inevitable divine providence, as most Calvinists do: For why should two bronze mountains be set forth? Is not divine providence unique, just as God Himself is but one? The Calvinist interpreters could certainly find nothing regarding this duality of providence; to say nothing of the fact that the spirits do not go forth from divine providence locally, even if they are directed by divine providence. It is one thing to go forth from something, another to be directed by the same. However, the term from which, or what is like it, is presented here with respect to the going forth of the angelic hosts. Cocceius's interpretation of the two bronze mountains would be more suitable. The meaning, he says, is that two mountains, i.e., two strong and unshaken kingdoms, have been established by God, or rather that the Kingdom of God, subjecting the world, has two manifestations as if in a double kingdom. One is the kingdom of the house of David; the other is the Kingdom of Christ, which is indeed spiritual, but also has a terrestrial effect in the subjection of all nations. Daniel 7:22, 27. The kingdom of the Davidic house, as far as its external form is concerned, is abolished, but it remains nevertheless in the root, until it appears in the other mountain. In the meantime, four kingdoms with their armies are to lie upon the Promised Land. So that the fourth is that under which the Kingdom of Christ will arise. Nor is this prophecy or its emblem new. For in Daniel 2 also there is mention of two mountains, verses 46, 35. And these chariots correspond in part with the parts of the statue.

This chapter is only passed over here, because it had already gone by. And the third part is divided here into two, on account of the different places of the expedition. But in the statue they are one, on account of the nature of the ruling people: who were Greeks. But that unity and distinction is hinted at in Dan. ch. VII, verse 8. And let the success of the little horn into the South be noted there. So verse 21, 22.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Octava visio quatuor quadrigarum cum mandato de coronis Josuæ imponendis.

Vidit Propheta quatuor quadrigas egredien- tes de medio duorum montium æreorum cum equis rufis, nigris, albis, & variis, quæ exponuntur de quatuor ventis (no- tantur autem angelicæ turmæ defensionis causa per Judæam emissæ, in solatium fi- delium.) Additur denique præceptum Symbolicum de duabus coronis Josuæ, e- jusque Prophetica explicatio, de Christo Zemach, sub quo omnia germinabunt, Rege & Sacerdote nostro.

Sunt in equis venti: templum stat Rege Zemacho.

Vers. 1.

ET CONVERSUS SUM) Ut supra V. 1. ECCE QUATUOR QUADRIGÆ) Currus quatuor, sunt quatuor imperia, ut hic explicat Chal- dæus.

Non solum Chaldæus, sed etiam Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Remigius, Haymo, & è Pontifi- ciis Lyranus, Arias, Ribera, Sanchez, Fernan- dez, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, Menochius, Reyrola &c. de quatuor Regnis interpretantur, sed IV. Monarchias intelligunt, in quo ab ipsis diva- ricatur Grotius; sed Scriptura, ut observatum Tarnovio, per currus non denotat regna, quæ a- pud Danielem per partes corporis ac animalia qua- tuor indicantur. Neque hic declaratur, quid e- venerit, aut venturum sit in regnis politicis, sed potius in Regno Christi spirituali. Neque satis convenit illa explicatio angelicæ interpretationi, quæ omnino attendenda. Calvinus etsi ad impe- ria referat equos, colores tamen istos diversos ad statum Ecclesiæ Dei pertinere censet. B. Luthe- rus explicat quatuor currus de prædicatione Evan- gelii in omnibus mundi partibus, tempore No- vi Testamenti, quam ἔκθεσιν suam fecit, & il- lustravit B. Balduinus. Coccejus turmas bellicas intelligit, quibus tamen adjungi posse ait Angelos motares potius malos, quam bonos. Inter duo Regna unum domus Davidis, alterum Christi, per duos montes indicata, quatuor Regna intermedia cum suis exercitibus seu turmis incubitura terræ promissæ, & sub quarto Regnum Christi oriturum significari censet. Non pauci Interpp. hodie cum Theodoreto de quatuor turmis angelorum bonorum accipiunt, utpote è Pontificiis Palatius Castrius, è Reformatis Fr. Junius & alii, nec non è nostris plerique. Pro qua sententia facit, quod angeli curribus figurentur II. Regum II. vers. 11. cap. VI. vers. 16. Psal. LXIIX. vers. 18. & in hoc Propheta visi sint equi varii, albij & rufi, cum angeli comites Filii Dei inter myrtos apparuere, & quod vers. 5. videatur ab Angelo in Zacharia loquente eadem explicatio tradita; Hi sunt quatuor Spiritus cæli (vel cœlestes, vel angeli ex quatuor cæli partibus se sistentes Deo, & ab illo excurrentes ad exequenda mandata illius Job. I. vers. 6. I. Reg. XXII. vers. 19.) qui egrediuntur, ut sint coram Dominatore omnis terræ. De quibus ita Christ. à Castro: Quadriga Angelorum, quæ nigris equis vehebatur, missa fuit in terram Aquilonarem, extremum Chaldæis exitium illatura hostibus Judæorum, per Medos & Persas. Quadriga Angelorum equorum alborum missa est post priorem, ut Judæos libertate donatos per eosdem hilares in patriam reducerent. Quadriga Angelorum equorum variorum missa est versus Austrum, ut hostes Judæorum, eis felicitatem invidentes, pro varietate gentium, continerent, ne ulla in re eis nocerent. Junius vers. 6. ita reddit: Qui sunt in illo curru (equi illi rufi nominati vers. 2. quos digito monstrabat Christus) egrediuntur in terram Aquilonarem (id est, Babyloniam, quæ respectu Judææ Aquilonaris dicitur) & albi illi egrediuntur post eos: grandine vero guttati egrediuntur in terram meridianam (Judæorum, quæ respectu Babylonis, ad quam angeli alii profecti erant, Meridiana est.) Sensus est, istorum angelorum administrorum Dei pars major in Babyloniam profecta est, ut curarent Judæos, qui adhuc inter hostes hærebant; pars vero in Judæa fuit occupata, ut populo Dei in illa versanti ministraret. Rufi, inquit Willius, notant executores divinorum judiciorum, per flammas & gladium, nigri calamitatum tenebrosarum immissores, albi consolatores, & pacis ac tranquillitatis conservatores, grandine guttati tales, qui partim puniunt, partim erigunt, & defendunt. Communis autem horum equorum quasi conditio, quod omnes sint אֲמֻצִּים robusti, confirmati, ut Junius vertit, ad opus scilicet, cui accingebantur Dei virtute instructi. Hos quatuor רוּחוֹת Spiritus collective, ait esse quatuor exercitus spirituum cœlestium, qui mandata Dei per omnes cæli plagas exequantur. Qui vertunt: HI AD QUATUOR VENTOS cœlorum egrediuntur, eos & constructioni & distinctioni textus vim inferre, dicit. Verba autem subjuncta ita reddit: Egrediuntur inde, ubi constiterunt apud Dominum totius terræ, ut explicetur, quid per montes illos chalybeos significetur, quod nempe mittantur in orbem à DEI providentia, qui universam terræ faciem imperio suo premit. Sensum autem initio quidem eundem cum Junio tradidit Willius, de angelis trium colorum, albis, nigris & rufis, in Babylonem mittendis, ut ibi judicia Domini in immorigeros exerceant, penes alios tenebras luce sua discutiant, ac solatio illis subveniant, & de angelis grandineis in Judæam destinatis, quia ut mixtus grandineorum equorum color est, sic in ipsa Judæa quoque res adhuc valde confusa e- rat, ita ut comminatione & erectione opus ha- berent. Post illa vero subito mutata sententia de his posterioribus angelis eos in Ægyptum missos statuit idem Willius, siquidem viderit Drusium terram Austri pro Ægypto accipere, quæ Judææ Australis, uti Dan. XI. vers. 4. Rex Austri dici- tur Rex Ægypti, & Hieronymi canonem citare, in his descriptionibus regionum observandum, quod κλίματα, id est, plagæ urbis juxta situm Je- rusalem & templi in Scripturis appellentur. Missos autem ideo in Ægyptum, quia etiam illic multi adhuc hærebant Judæi, qui eo aufugerant, & quorum curam Deus suscipiebat, quia & ipsi ali- quando in unum Ecclesiæ corpus per Christum adunandi. Quapropter proxime sequentes CON- FIRMATOS jam distinctam turmam constitue- re affirmat, easque ipsam Judæam, quam per הגדיה Ha- jediah notari vult, percurrere debuisse censet, quorum observatores peculiariter fortes & confir- mati dicantur, quia hi peculiariter debuerint Ju- dæam consolari, erigere, defendere, & hosti- bus ipsorum resistere, ac Rempubl. ipsorum, us- que ad Christi adventum stabilire, & in maximis turbis conservare, ut indicetur, quum alibi visi- bilis Ecclesia de loco in locum migratura sit, in Judæa tamen ipsa confirmatum iri. Denique tran- quillasse Spiritum Domini in terra Aquilonari ita dicuntur angeli eo missi, quod fecerint voluntatem ejus, ut Targum reddit, in impios quidem ju- dicia Domini exercendo, ut furor ejus sistatur, in piorum reliquias vero eas in probitatis curricu- lo retinendo, ut inde colligere potuerint Judæi, quibus hæc exponuntur, non cum omnibus in Babylone pessime actum iri, sed in deploratissimo ac perditissimo statu Deum reliquias suas conser- vaturum, ac impiorum passiva turba justis judi- ciis sublata parvulum fidelium gregem benevo- lentia ac gratia sua complexurum. Hactenus ergo Junii sententia, (maxime prout eadem à Willio il- lustrata est) cui, etsi in plerisque accipere B. Tar- novius, paulo aliter tamen applicationem insti- tuit: Significatur, inquit, typo quatuor curruum ministerio sanctorum angelorum a Deo cum in Ju- dæa, tum etiam in ipsa Babylonia multos adhuc qui- dem hærentes, sed paulo post Hierosolymam ventu- ros, seque suaque Deo consecraturos in gratiam rece- ptum ac salvatum iri. Et postea monet, angelos tranquillaturos Babyloniam, & de iis ad regnum

Christi vocandis hic agi, ac doceri, non omnes extra Judæam degentes prorsus exclusos esse à gratia Dei, quandoquidem etiam in media Ba- bylonia multi pii serventur integri, & olim ad re- gnum Christi venturi sint longinqui, seu gentes. Paraphrastæ tamen Belgici, cum Daneo, ut & è nostris B. Wigandus interpretatur quidem de an- gelorum exercitu quadruplici, sed ita, ut innua- tur, Deum ministerio eorum hostium conatus re- pressurum, & pacem sanciturum, ut possint juxta mandatum Dei templum restaurare. Similiter B. Winckelmannus exponit de angelis bonis, eo- rumque singulari ministerio in procuranda & pro- movenda pace populi apud Persas & vicina regna, varios equos egressos dicit adversus Ægyptios & Idumæos, ad prohibendum itidem ibi omnes ho- stiles motiones. Sic etiam B. Pappus: Significa- tur hac visione, Dominum concessurum esse huic Reipublicæ Halcyonia, nec permissurum, ut dissi- petur iterum ante exhibitionem Messiæ. Ut autem pii, quos præsens imbecillitas, & e contrario fu- ror hostium terrebat, tanto magis huic promif- sioni fidem adhiberent, rursus producit Domi- nus in theatrum firmissimum illum exercitum san- ctorum Angelorum pugnantem pro Ecclesia, & exequentem voluntatem divinam contra Diaboli & mundi furores. Quibus accedunt B. Himme- lius, Paraphrasis Vinariensis, & Osiandrina: Va- rii equorum colores significant variam potentiam, & varios effectus angelorum, quibus conatus ad- versus Ecclesiam susceptos infringunt, ut interim Ecclesia tranquillitate fruatur.

Vers. eod.

EGREDIENTES DE MEDIO DUORUM MON- TIUM, ET MONTES, MONTES ÆREI) Portas Ciliciæ intelligit, inter montium ardua, per quas Babylo- nii & Persæ, Alexander quoque & duces ejus in Syriam, Judæam, Ægyptum transire soliti.

Portas inter montium ardua per montes æreos designari, unde docebitur? Et quomodo omnia quatuor imperia per Ciliciæ portas egressa? Aliis montes duo ærei significant montem Moria, in quo ædificabatur templum, & montem Sion, in quo fuerat Regia Davidis : quia in monte Mo- ria promiserat Deus se adfuturum, & quasi domi- cilium suum in templo habiturum : Qui ærei di- cantur, ut significetur Dominum & Sacerdotium & Politiam Judæorum confirmaturum, ut contra insultus hostium fortissime constare possint. Ita Osiander, Wigandus, Paraphrastæ Vinarienses, a- lii. Neque vero quicquam, huic explicationi ob- stat, quod cœlitus facta sit hæc revelatio, quod- que nullo modo debuerint angeli Hierosolyma egredi, sed potius eam ingredi, ut eam custo- diant. Nam etiam in cœtibus facta revelatione montes adumbrare poterant Hierosolymam, nec quia inde egredi videntur turmæ nonnullæ angeli- cæ, Hierosolyma prorsus destituitur angelico præsidio. Erat in monte Moria quasi Regia Do- mini, quod illic sedem suam figere ipsi placuerit I. Reg. IIX. ideo inde videntur prodire turmæ an- gelicæ. Quapropter non est, quod cum plerisque Calvinianis montes æreos, de inevitabili divina pro- videntia, explicemus : Cur enim duo montes æ- rei sisterentur? Annon providentia divina unica est, uti Deus ipse non nisi unus? Nihil sane inve- nire potuere de hac διττότητι providentiæ Calvi- niani Interpretes; ut taceam, quod Spiritus non egrediantur à providentia divina τοπικῶς, etsi dirigantur divina providentia. Aliud est egredi ab aliquo, aliud ab eodem dirigi. Exhibetur autem hic terminus à quo, aut quod instar ejus est, re- spectu egressus turmarum angelicarum. Conve- nientior foret Cocceji interpretatio de duobus mon- tibus areis. Sensus est, inquit, Duos montes, h. e. duo regna valida & inconcussa esse constituta à Deo, sive potius Regnum Dei subjiciens mundum duas ha- bere manifestationes tanquam in duplici regno. U- num est regnum domus Davidis: alterum Regnum Christi, quod quidem est spirituale, sed etiam ad ef- fectum terrestrem in subjectione omnium gentium. Daniel. VII. 22. 27. Regnum domus Davidicæ, quo- ad externam formam est abolitum, sed manet ta- men in radice, donec in altero monte appareat. Me- dio tempore quatuor Regna cum suis exercitibus in- cubitura Terræ promissæ. Ita ut quartum sit illud, sub quo Regnum Christi orietur. Neque est hæc pro- phetia aut ejus Emblema novum. Nam & Danielis II. duorum montium mentio est vers. 46. 35. Et hæ quadrigæ cum partibus statuæ ex parte conveniunt.

Tantum præteritur hic caput, quia illud jam abive- rat. Et pars tertia hic secatur in duas, propter diver- sos expeditionis locos. At in statua unum sunt, propter naturam populi imperantis : qui Græci erant. Ea ve- ro unitas & distinctio innuitur cap. VII. Dan. vers. 8. Et ibi animadvertatur successus cornu parvi in Au- strum. Ita vers. 21. 22.

## 6:2
Verse 2.

IN THE FIRST CHARIOT RED HORSES) Or mares, of which gender the word is below 7. Red horses signify the Chaldeans, who were very bloodthirsty. See the Lamentations of Jeremiah. He mentions these in passing, for the sake of keeping order, and so that he may compare past things with future ones, but afterwards he will say nothing about them, naturally, because that empire had already passed away when this vision came to the Prophet. Compare what is above I, 20.

AND IN THE SECOND CHARIOT BLACK HORSES) A black horse signifies famine, Apoc. VI, 5, 6, and by metonymy the devastation which the Persians brought upon very many lands. See what we have said on Dan. VIII, 5; it is apparent from the history of Darius and Xerxes.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

IN QUADRIGA PRIMA EQUI RUFI) Vel e- quæ, cujus generis est verbum infra 7. Equi rufi Chaldæos significant valde sanguinarios. Vide lamenta Jeremiæ. Horum obiter meminit, ordinis servandi causa, & ut præ- terita futuris conferat, postea vero nihil de illis dicet, ni- mirum, quia imperium id jam transierat, cum hoc visum Prophetæ obtingeret. Confer quæ supra I, 20.

ET IN QUADRIGA SECUNDA EQVI NI- GRI) Equus niger famem significat Apoc. VI, 5. 6. & per μετωνυμίαν vastitatem quamplurimis terris intulere Persæ. Vide quæ diximus ad Dan. VIII, 5. apparet id ex Darii & Xerxis historia.

## 6:3
Verse 3.

AND IN THE THIRD CHARIOT WHITE HORSES) That sign of triumph signifies the perpetual victories of Alexander.

AND IN THE FOURTH CHARIOT VARIEGATED AND STRONG HORSES) The fourth chariot is likewise of the kings of Syria and Egypt, whom the Prophets join together, because the Jews were sometimes under these, sometimes under those, and the very families were often mixed by marriages, and possessions transferred by force or by pacts. For strong, the Chaldean translated ash-colored, the Greeks ψαρούς. The variegated are the Egyptian Kings, to whom the fortune of war was sometimes favorable, sometimes adverse, as we have learned from Daniel. The ash-colored, however, are the Syrian Kings, concealing their counsels, as is to be learned from the affairs of Antiochus.

In this explanation we find lacking, first, that he assumes without proof that four empires are designated: Second, that he judges those empires to be described by different colors, as political kingdoms, and such as they were in themselves: whereas this vision looks rather to the state of the Church, and what has happened or is about to happen to the people of the Lord, for whose sake these revelations were made. (3) That he assumes as certain that the red horses are then neglected or passed over in the angelic explanation. For others deny that, and posit an asyndeton, explaining it in this way: v. 6. Who (are) in it (the chariot) as the angel of the Lord, as if he were pointing a finger at the red ones. And those black horses go out into the North country, and those white ones go out after them. They therefore wish for horses of triple color, red, black, and white, to have gone out there. So Junius, Willius. (4) That in place of the fourth Empire, he does not hint at the Roman Monarchy, but the Kingdom in Egypt and Syria. In this part Grotius's opinion departs from the common Interpreters, as many as explain these as the four empires. For here they agree that the Roman Monarchy is designated by the fourth chariot, and by the variegated horses, because the Romans were variegated in policy and government, first under Kings, then under Consuls, third under tribunes of the people, fourth under Emperors, and these from various nations, Italian, Spanish, Gallic, Grecian, etc., and with various attitudes toward the Jews. (5) That he takes it for indubitable that in the fourth chariot different horses were seen: namely, some variegated, others ash-colored, for some render that doubtful, and say it pertains only to horses of one kind, which are also called בְרֻדִּים variegated by the Vulgate, scheckichte by Luther and Piscator, schimlige by others, grandinati or spotted with hail by Junius and Willius: and אֲמֻצִּים, which word, added by apposition to the former, does not denote other horses of a different color, but describes those variegated ones, because they appeared strong above others, as the Vulgate rendered it, and Aquila, who interpreted it, as Jerome notes, κρατερούς. For they wish the proper meaning of the word to be observed here, and that one should not look at how the Jews perhaps understood it, or the Chaldean, but what the authentic text implies. Others, even if they also understand color, wish the word אֲמֻצִּים to be placed by changing the gutturals

for חמצים which is had in Is. LXIII. 1. Stained. Coccejus, from a comparison, he says, of verse 2 and 7, it appears that אמצים is the same as אדמים red. Whence ברדים אמצים is to be explained as grandinati, rubri [hail-spotted, red] in verse 3. חמוץ בגדים agrees as if fermented in garments, Isaiah LXIII. 1, which is soon אדם ללבושך red in your garments in verse 2. For אמצים for strong, which is אמיץ, is neither read, nor is it suitable. These are Coccejus's, and it seems too arbitrary that he interprets the variegated as the Kingdom of Egypt, the strong as the Kingdom of Syria. (6) If the chariots are to be understood entirely as the four empires, and Alexander and the Macedonians are designated by the white horses, who succeeded the Persians and extorted the Monarchy from them next to Babylon, of which Curtius book V and Plutarch in the Life of Alexander, then by the VARIEGATED ones that went out to the South, the Romans who went out into Egypt are to be understood. What Arias and Vatablus think was done by Julius Caesar, who first conquered Egypt, is better judged by others, according to Cornel. à Lapide p. 216, to have been done by Augustus, the successor of Julius. For Augustus, through the victory at Actium, defeated Antony and Cleopatra, and thus extinguished the kingdom of the Greeks, that is, the Ptolemies in Egypt, and transferred it to himself and the Romans. Whence he himself first made Egypt a province, as Suetonius testifies in his life, chapters 17 and 18, which Julius had not dared to do. Then, therefore, the third monarchy of the Greeks having been overturned, the fourth of Augustus and the Romans began. Whence, shortly after, by Augustus as if already monarch, an edict went out that the whole world should be registered, so St. Jerome, Ribera, Sanchez, Fernandez, and others. But the most robust of them traveled through the land of Judea, concerning which

Coccejus thus: the order of the operations of the armies of God here is: 1. The black horses went forth into the land of the North. Namely, from the face of the Lord, that is, they are sent into the land of the North. In comparison to the land of Israel, Babylon and Assyria are northern, verging toward the East. Into that land were sent the Medes and Persians, who were not indeed bloodthirsty toward the people of God, but nevertheless burdensome and troublesome. 2. The white went out after them, that is, they were sent into the same region, namely, to subjugate those holding the same seat as the former. And according to the order of the prophecy of Daniel, these were the Greeks under Alexander. These were favorable to Israel. 3. The grisled went out into the land of the South. The sense of the prophecy is simple and plain. After the Persian kingdom is destroyed, a new commotion will be stirred up tending toward Egypt. But that this expedition is to be undertaken by the Northerners, Daniel says more explicitly in chapter XI, 5 and following. Where it must be noted that among the leaders of Alexander, Ptolemy, son of Lagus, emerged most prominently, concerning whom Dan. XI. 5. Against his greatness, therefore, the counsels and efforts of the Seleucids were compared. Then also Euergetes came into Asia and obtained the strongholds of the kingdom: but a sedition having been stirred up, he is compelled to return to his own kingdom, Dan. XI. verses 8 and 9. Also the successes of Philopator against Antiochus the Great are noted in verse 11. But, because of his deed, the course of his affairs is turned. ibid. verses 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. Again, Antiochus Epiphanes moved successfully against Philometor, verses 25, 26. But his second expedition is inhibited by the Romans, verses 29, 30. 4. The red and bloodthirsty went out, verse 7. (They are called forth, Mic. IV. 14.) and sought to go and walk through the land. And the Angel who spoke said, go, walk through the land. The Romans deliberately wanted to have Judea in their power; and it was given to them to have it in their power. These were red to them. A known matter. Pompey captured Jerusalem, the kingdom

He took it away from Hyrcanus. Gabinius, Crassus, Bibulus, etc., held it. The census was proclaimed. The Jews were registered as subjects of the Roman Empire. There were perpetual governors. Archelaus was banished. Judea was reduced to the form of a province. Under Nero, the city and the polity were destroyed. Cocceius says this again.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET IN QUADRIGA TERTIA EQVI ALBI) Id signum triumphi perpetuas Alexandri victorias significat.

ET IN QVADRIGA QUARTA EQVI VARII ET FORTES) Currus quartus est pariter Syriæ & Ægy- pti regum, quos conjungunt Prophetæ, quod Judæi mo- do sub his, modo sub illis fuerint, & ipsa genera sæpe ma- trimoniis permixta, possessionesque translatæ vi aut pa- ctionibus. Pro fortes Chaldæos transtulit cinereos, Græci ψαρούς. Varii sunt Reges Ægyptii, quibus fortuna belli modo favens, modo adversa, ut ex Daniele didicimus. Ci- nerei vero Reges Syriaci occultantes sua consilia, ut ex Antiochi rebus discere est.

In hac explicatione desideramus, primo, quod citra probationem assumat, quatuor imperia desi- gnari : Secundo, quod imperia illa describi per colo- res diversos censeat, ut politica regna, & qualia ipsa fuerint per se : quum visio hæc respiciat potius sta- tum Ecclesiæ, & quæ populo Domini evenerint, aut eventura sint, cuius gratia factæ hæ revelationes. (3) Quod tanquam certum assumat, negligi deinde aut præteriri in explicatione angelica equos rufos. Id enim alii negant, & asyndeton statuunt, hoc modo explicantes : v. 6. Qui (sunt) in illo (curru) ut an- gelus Domini, quasi digitum intendat ad rufos. Et equi illi nigri egrediuntur, in terram Aquilonarem, & albi illi egrediuntur post eos. Triplicis ergo co- loris equos, rufos, nigros & albos eo egressos vo- lunt. Ita Junius, Willius. (4) Quod quarti Imperii loco, non Monarchiam Romanam innuit, sed Re- gnum in Ægypto & Syria.
