Qua parte à communi Interpp. quotquot hæc de quatuor imperiis expli- cant, sententia discedit Grotius. Hic enim Mo- narchiam Romanam per quartam quadrigam, & per equos varios designari consentiunt, quia varii fuere Romani politia ac regimine, primo sub Regibus, de- inde sub Consulibus, tertio sub tribunis plebis, quar- to sub Imperatoribus, & his ex varia gente, Italica, Hispanica, Gallica, Græcanica &c. & vario in Ju- dæos affectu. (5) Quod pro indubitato habeat, in quadriga quarta diversos equos conspectos fuisse : nimirum alios varios, alios cinereos, id enim non- nulli dubium reddunt, & unius generis equis so- lū convenire ajunt, qui & בְרֻדִּים varii vulgato, Lu- thero & Piscatori scheckichte, aliis schimlige, Junio & Willio grandinati, vel grandine guttati dicun- tur : & אֲמֻצִּים quæ vox per appositionem priori addita non alios equos alterius coloris notat, sed il- los varios describit, quod præ aliis fortes visi sint, uti vulgatus reddidit, & Aquila, qui interpretatus est, notante Hieronymo κρατερούς. Hic enim signi- ficationem propriam vocis observandam, nec vi- dendum esse volunt, quomodo Judæi forte acce- perint, aut Chaldæus, sed quid textus authenticus inferat. Alii etsi colorem quoque intelligant, vo- cem אֲמֻצִּים permutatis gutturalibus volunt positā

pro חמצים quod habetur Es. LXIII. 1. Commaculati. Coccejus ex collatione, inquit, versus 2. & 7. apparet, quod אמצים sit idem cū אדמים rubris. Unde ברדים אמצים & grandinati, rubri explicandi est vers. 3. Convenit חמוץ בגדים quasi fermentatus vestes Esa. LXIII. 1. quod mox אדם ללבושך rubrum in vestibus tuis vers. 2. Nam אמצים pro fortes, quod est אמיץ, nec legitur, nec aptum est. Hæc Coccejus, & nimis arbitrarium videtur, quod varios de Regno Ægypti, fortes de Regno Syriæ interpretatur. (6) Si omnino quadrigæ de quatuor imperiis intelligantur, & per albos equos Alexander & Macedones designentur, qui Persis succefferunt, ac Monarchiam illis juxta Babylonem extorserunt, de quo Curtius l. V. & Plutarchus in Vit. Alexandr. per VARIOS egressos ad Austrum Romani in Ægyptum egressi intelligendi erunt. Quod Arias & Vatablus factum putant per Julium Cæsarem, qui primus devicit Ægyptum, verum melius juxta Cornel. à Lapide p. 216. alii censent id factum per Augustum successorem Julii. Augustus enim per Actiacam victoriam profligavit Antonium & Cleopatram, itaque Græcorum, puta Ptolomæorum in Ægypto regnum extinxit, illudque ad se & Romanos transtulit. Unde ipse primus Ægyptum fecit provinciam, teste Suetonio in ejus vita cap. 17. & 18. quod Julius facere ausus non fuerat. Tunc ergo eversa tertia Monarchia Græcorum, cœpit quarta Augusti, & Romanorum. Unde paulo post ab Augusto quasi jam Monarcha, exiit edictum, ut describeretur universus orbis, ita S. Hieronym. Ribera, Sanchez, Fernandez, & alii. Robustissimi vero ex illis terram Judaicam perambularunt, de quo

Coccejus ita: ordo operationem exercituum Dei hic est: 1. Atri equi prodierunt in terram Aquilonis. Scilicet à facie Domini, hoc est mittuntur in terram Aquilonis. In comparatione terræ Israel Babylon & Assyria est Aquilonaris vergens ad Orientem. In eam terram immissi Medi & Persæ, qui populo Dei non quidem sanguinarii extiterunt, sed tamen graves & molesti. 2. Albi exierunt ad post illos, hoc est, missi sunt in eandem partem, scilicet ut priores eandem sedem tenentes subjugarent. Et secundum ordinem Prophetiæ Danielis hi fuerunt Græci sub Alexandro. Hi commodi fuerunt Israeli. 3. Grandinati exiverunt in terram Austri. Sensus prophetiæ simplex & planus. Post destructum Regnum Persicum excitabitur nova commotio tendens in Ægyptum. Quod autem hæc expeditio sit suscipienda à Septentrionalibus, explicatius dicit Daniel cap. XI. 5. & sequentibus. Ubi animadvertendum, inter duces Alexandri maxime emersisse Ptolomæum Lagi filium, de quo Dan. XI. 5. Contra illius igitur magnitudinem comparata sunt Seleucidarum consilia & conatus. Tum etiam Evergetes in Asiam venit, & arces regni obtinuit: sed concitata seditione in regnum suum reverti cogitur, Dan. XI. vers. 89. etiam Philopatoris successus contra Antiochum magnum notantur in vers. 11. Sed, ob factum ejus, convertitur cursus rerum ejus. ibid. vers. 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. 17. Rursus Antiochus Epiphanes contra Philometora movit feliciter vers. 25. 26. Secunda autem ipsius expeditio inhibetur à Romanis vers. 29. 30. 4. Rufi & sanguinolenti exiverunt vers. 7. (Evocantur Mich. IV. 14.) & quæsiverunt ire & perambulare terram. Et dixit Angelus Collocutor, ite ambulate in terra. Romani Judæam de industria voluerunt habere in potestate; & datum est illis, ut eam in potestate haberent. Hi illis rufi fuerunt. Res nota. Pompejus Hierosolymam cœpit, Regnum

Hyrcano abstulit. Gabinius, Crassus, Bibulus, &c. tenuerunt. Edictus census. Judæi ut subditi Ro- mani Imperii censi. Perpetui præsides fuerunt. Archelaus relegatus. Judæa in formulam provin- ciæ redacta. Sub Nerone urbs & politia deleta. Hæc iterum Coccejus.

## 6:5
Verse 5.

THESE ARE THE FOUR WINDS OF HEAVEN) Empires in different climates. The impetus of these is usually compared to winds. WHO GO FORTH TO STAND BEFORE THE LORD OF ALL THE EARTH) From standing before the Lord of all the earth. They stood before God, that is, they will receive commands: having received them, they will go where it seemed good to God. The gloss is not sufficiently consistent. That empires are denoted by the winds of heaven, and that the winds stand before God. Perhaps a simpler explanation is concerning the angels: Who are CELESTIAL SPIRITS, and stand before the Lord of all the earth, and obey at his nod, and go forth Dan. VII. 14. Heb. I. 14. Unless Cocceius's observation pleases, that peoples making an attack are accustomed to be compared to winds. See Isa. XXVII. 8. Hos. XXI. 15. Apoc. VII. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ISTI SVNT QVATUOR VENTI COELI) Im- peria in diversis climatibus. Ventis eorum impetus com- parari solent. QVI EGREDIVNTUR UT STENT CORAM DOMINATORE OMNIS TERRÆ) A stando coram Domino omnis terræ. Steterunt coram Deo, id est, mandata accipient: iis acceptis ibunt quo Deo visum. Glossa non satis concinna. Per ventos cœli impe- ria notari, ventosque stare coram Deo. Simplicior fortassis explicatio est de angelis: Qui sunt COE- LESTES SPIRITUS, & consistunt coram do- mino omnis terræ, atque ad nutum ejus parent, & egrediuntur Dan. VII. 14. Ebr. I. 14. Nisi placeat Cocceji observatio, quod populi impetum facientes ventis comparari soleant. Vid. Esa. XXVII. 8. Hos. XXI. 15. Apoc. VII. 2.

## 6:6
Verse 6.

IN WHICH WERE BLACK HORSES, THEY WENT FORTH INTO THE NORTH COUNTRY) The Persians went forth into Chaldea, which is northern to the Jews. AND THE WHITE WENT FORTH AFTER THEM) Alexander also came to Babylon. AND THE VARIOUS WENT FORTH TO THE SOUTH COUNTRY) Those Lagidae held Egypt, which is to the South for the Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

IN QVA ERANT EQVI NIGRI, EGREDIE- BANTUR IN TERRAM AQVILONIS) Egressi sunt Persæ in Chaldæam, quæ Aquilonaris Judæis. ET ALBI EGRESSI SVNT POST EOS) Venit Babylona etiam Alexander. ET VARII EGRESSI SVNT AD TERRAM AVSTRI) Illi Lagidæ Ægyptum tenuere, quæ ad Au- strum Judæis.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

BUT THEY THAT WERE MOST ROBUST) The ash-colored ones, as above. WENT FORTH, AND SOUGHT TO GO, AND TO WALK TO AND FRO THROUGH ALL THE EARTH, AND HE SAID: GO, WALK TO AND FRO THROUGH THE EARTH, AND THEY WALKED TO AND FRO THROUGH THE EARTH] The Seleucids now waged war against the Egyptians, now against the Jews and Arabs and their neighbors, now against Armenia, the Medes, and the Parthians, so that they left nothing untouched, by the wise permission of God. Some, as observed before, interpret the former words of verse 6 as if the red horses with the first chariot were not omitted, but were pointed out here demonstratively. They who in that (sc. the first chariot), i.e., the red horses, and the black horses went forth into the North country. Thus there will be no place for the gloss about the Persians going forth into Babylon: which also does not seem appropriate for the reason that that going forth had already passed: but here the vision is exhibited concerning future things. Nor are those most robust ones, whom the Vulgate calls so, said to have walked to and fro through different lands, as Grotius, or through the whole earth, as others wish, but through THIS LAND, in which Zechariah was acting, i.e., through Judea. For it is not in vain that the demonstrative He was added. Others interpret more correctly concerning the angels sent through Judea, so that they might protect the faithful in the work of the Lord against enemies, and be a guard to them.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

QVI AVTEM ERANT ROBUSTISSIMI) Cine- rei. ut supra. EXIERUNT, ET QVÆREBANT IRE, ET DI- SCVRRERE PER OMNEM TERRAM, ET DIXIT: ITE ET PERAMBULATE TERRAM, ET PERAM- BULAVERUNT TERRAM] Seleucidæ modo Ægyptiis bellum intulere, modo Judæis, & Arabibus, eorumque vi- cinis, modo Armeniæ, Medisque & Parthis, ita ut nihil in- tactum sinerent, sapiente Dei permissu. Verba priora vers. 6. nonnulli, ut observatum antea, interpretantur, ac si equi rufi cum quadriga prima non prætermissi, sed hac δεικτικῶς monstrata indigitari sint. Qui in illa (sc. prima quadriga) h.e. equi rufi, & equi nigri egrediebantur in terram A- quilonis. Ita glossæ locus non erit de Persis in Baby- loniam egressis: quæ etiam ideo non videtur con- veniens, quod ille egressus jam transierit: hic vero de rebus futuris visio exhibeatur. Neque robustis- simi illi, quos vocat Vulgatus vel per terras diver- sas, uti Grotius, vel per universam terram, ut alii volunt, sed per HANC TERRAM, in qua agebat Za- charias, h.e. per Judæam discurrisse dicuntur. Non enim frustra adjectum est He demonstrativum. Rectius interpretantur alii de angelis per Judæam emissis, ut fideles in opere Domini adversus hostes tuerentur, ipsisque præsidio essent.

## 6:8
Verse 8.

BEHOLD THEY THAT GO FORTH INTO THE NORTH COUNTRY] They who went forth, for that had already passed. HAVE CAUSED MY SPIRIT TO REST IN THE NORTH COUNTRY] That is, there they have abundantly satisfied my wrath conceived against the Chaldeans. Spirit signifies now wrath, now benevolence. The interpretation must be varied from the diversity of the subject matter. This rest of the Spirit of the Lord in the North country is explained by Osiander thus: they will prevent my wrath (through the Babylonians) from raging against them any longer from the North: I have several times stirred up against you, the Northern peoples, the Assyrians, the Babylonians, and have stimulated them to afflict you: but that will not happen hereafter: the Spirit of my zeal will rest. Others understand the judgments of God, which He had intended to exercise upon the impious Jews in Babylon, as about to cease, and the remnants of the pious as about to be brought back by the work of the angels: but the former paraphrase is simpler. And so also the blessed Tarnovius in this place. Those who say that empires are figured here explain it thus: The Persians satisfied my wrath, and when I was angry at the Chaldean tyrants, while they devastated them, they fulfilled my vengeance; and so they calmed my mind, which was desirous of just vengeance, as Cornelius à Lapide has it on page 217, where he notes that these things are said for the consolation of the Jews, who had been devastated by the Babylonians and led away into Babylon: and to stir up hatred of impiety and idolatry (of which Babylon was the metropolis) so that the Jews might abhor it, as they subsequently abhorred it. And therefore only the mention of the things done by the chariots in Babylon, to wit, the vengeance accomplished therein, is made here.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ECCE QVI EGREDIUNTUR IN TERRAM AQVILONIS] Qui egressi sunt, nam id jam transierat. REQ VIESCERE FECERVNT SPIRITVM MEVM IN TERRA AQVILONIS] Id est, ibi iram meam contra Chaldæos susceptam abunde satiarunt. Spi- ritus modo iram, modo benevolentiam significat. Ex ma- teriæ diversitate varianda interpretatio. Hæc Spiritus Domini requies in terra Aquilo- nis ab Osiandro ita explicatur: prohibebunt, ne ab Aquilone amplius ira mea (per Babylonios) in eos sæviat: Ego aliquoties adversus vos, populos Se- ptentrionales Assyrios, Babylonios excitavi, eas- que stimulavi, ut vos affligerent: id vero posthac non fiet: Spiritus Zeli mei quiescet. Alii intelligunt judicia Dei, quæ in impios Judæos in Babylonia exercere cogitaverat, cessatura, & piorum reli- quias adductu iri opera angelorum: sed prior pa- raphrasis simplicior est. Atque ita etiam B. Tarno- vius in h. l. Qui imperia hic figurata ajunt, sic explicant: Persæ satisfecerunt meæ iræ, mihique in Chaldæos tyrannos irato, dum eos vastarunt, expleverunt meam vindictam; itaque sedarunt meum animum justæ vindictæ cupidum, ut habet Cornel. à Lapide p. 217. ubi notat, hæc dici ad consolationem Judæorum, qui à Babyloniis vastati, & in Babylonem abducti fuerant: & ad concitandum odium impietatis & idololatriæ (cujus metropolis erat Babylon) ut Judæi eam abominentur, uti deinceps abominati sunt. Ideoque tantum rerum à quadrigis in Babylone gestarum, puta vindictæ in ea peractæ hic fieri mentionem.

## 6:10
Verse 10.

TAKE FROM THE TRANSMIGRATION] That is, from those who now recently come from exile.

FROM HOLDAI] Who is Helem below, unless there is a scribal error in this or that place.

AND FROM TOBIAH, AND FROM JEDAIAH] Whose names are the same below.

AND YOU SHALL COME ON THAT DAY, AND ENTER THE HOUSE OF JOSIAH THE SON OF ZEPHANIAH] Having entered on this very day the house of Josiah, in which they are staying. It is uncertain whether this Josiah is the same as Helem the son of Zephaniah below, or whether Helem is his brother, and a companion of those who had come from Babylon.

WHO CAME FROM BABYLON] An interpretation of that which preceded, from the transmigration.

No one here dreamed of a mistake, since by both names, Holdai and Helem, the same person could be denoted: just as interpreters also easily agree that the same person was called both Josiah and Helem. There is no reason, therefore, why we should add Helem as a brother of Josiah; since no more than four persons are designated, to whom Zechariah was sent. As for those words: Take from the transmigration, which Grotius renders: from those who now recently come from exile, some understand them thus: take from the captive Jews, who either in themselves, or in their parents, were led away to Babylon by the Chaldeans, and migrated, and they maintain that these four men were of chief authority among those who returned from captivity. Others, however, maintain that they were sent from the transmigration, or the captives in Babylon, and were legates of the Jews, who brought gifts to Jerusalem to be offered in the temple (which Grotius also acknowledges), the intention of which legates Willius not incorrectly states to have been that they might assist the structure of the temple with religious offerings, and might be made certain, if the same were accepted, that they belonged to the communion of the temple and the Jewish people, which is gathered from the conclusion of the chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

SUME A TRANSMIGRATIONE] Id est, ab iis qui nunc recens ab exilio veniunt.

AB HOLDAI] Qui infra Helem, nisi erratum est scribæ hoc vel illo loco.

ET A TOBIA, ET AB IDAIA] Quorum infra nomina eadem.

ET VENIES TU IN DIE ILLA, ET INTRABIS DOMUM JOSIÆ FILII SOPHONIÆ] Ingressus hoc ipso die domum Josiæ, in qua illi divertunt. Incertum est an hic Josias idem sit, qui infra Hem filius Sophoniæ, an vero Hem frater illius sit, & comes illorum, qui à Babylone venerant.

QVI VENERVNT DE BABYLONE] Interpretatio ejus quod præcessit, à transmigratione.

Nemo hic somniavit Sphalma, quum utroque nomine Holdai & Helem eadem persona notari potuerit: quemadmodum etiam facile consentiunt interpretes, eundem & Josiam & Hem dictum fuisse. Non ergo est, quod Hem fratrem Josiæ aliis adjungamus: quum non nisi quatuor personæ designentur, ad quas missus Zacharias. Quod ad verba illa: Sume à transmigratione, quod reddit Grotius: ab iis, qui nunc recens ab exilio veniunt, nonnulli ea ita intelligunt: sume a Judæis captivis, qui vel in se, vel in suis parentibus in Babylonem à Chaldæis abducti, transmigrarunt, atque hos quatuor viros præcipuæ autoritatis fuisse volunt inter eos, qui redierunt è captivitate. Alii vero missos volunt à transmigratione, vel captivis in Babylonia, & legatos Judæorum, qui attulerint munera Jerusalem, in templo offerenda, (quod agnoscit etiam Grotius) quorum legatorum intentionem hanc fuisse, non male statuit Willius, ut religiosis oblationibus structuram templi juvarent, certique fierent, si eædem acceptarentur, se ad communionem templi & populi Judaici pertinere, quod è conclusione capitis colligitur.

## 6:11
Verse 11.

AND YOU SHALL TAKE] Take, I say.

GOLD AND SILVER] Which they bring from the collection of the exiles for the adornment of the Temple, which is now to be built.

AND YOU SHALL MAKE CROWNS] Several, which are then to be suspended in the Temple.

AND YOU SHALL PLACE UPON THE HEAD OF JESUS SON OF JOSEDEC THE HIGH PRIEST] One of them, of course, for the high priests also wore a crown on joyful days.

This is openly contradicted by both the words and the scope of the vision. For the Prophet, or rather the angel of the Lord, Christ himself, who is here called the Lord, whose word came to the Prophet, does not speak of several crowns, but of two, one golden, the other silver. For that angel had dealt with the Prophet, having spoken in the preceding verses, and deals with him throughout this whole chapter, which is evident from the συνεχεία of the text, and he gave a clear command concerning the crowns which he ordered to be made, not that they were only to be suspended in the temple εἰς μνημόσυνον, but that they were first to be placed upon the head of Joshua the Priest. Nor was the Prophet to place only one or the other of them upon Joshua, but both.

Wherefore Cyril, Theodoret, Rupert, Lyra, Vatablus, and Isidorus Clarius observed that first one crown, then another, had been placed upon Joshua.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET SUMES] Sume, inquam.

AVRVM ET ARGENTVM] Quod illi ex collatione exsulum ferunt in Templi, quod jam struetur, ornatum.

ET FACIES CORONAS] Complures, quæ deinde suspendentur in Templo.

ET PONES IN CAPITE JESU FILII JOSEDEC SACERDOTIS MAGNI] Unam scilicet earum, nam & summi Sacerdotes coronam ferebant in diebus lætis.

Refragatur id palam & verbis & scopo visionis. Nam non de compluribus, sed duabus coronis, altera aurea, altera argentea, loquitur Propheta, vel potius angelus Domini, Christus ipse, qui hic dicitur Dominus, cujus verbum factum ad Prophetam. Nam egerat cum Propheta angelus ille, locutus in superioribus, atque hoc toto capite cum illo agit, quod è συνεχεία textus evidens est, & de coronis, quas fieri jussit, mandatum luculentum dedit, non quod solum suspendendæ sint in templo εἰς μνημόσυνον, sed quod prius imponendæ eædem sint capite Josuæ Sacerdotis. Neque solum alterutram earu Josuæ imponere Propheta debuit, sed utramque.

Quapropter Cyrillus, Theodoretes, Rupertus, Lyranus, Vatablus & Isidorus Clarius, primo unam, deinde alteram Josuæ impositam fuisse coronam observarunt.

## 6:12
Verse 12.

BEHOLD THE MAN) Pilate, with God directing, applied these words to Christ, saying: ἴδε ὁ ἄνθρωπος.

THE BRANCH IS HIS NAME) The Branch is his name: that is, a shoot as if reborn from the stock of David. See above III. 8. and the things cited there.

AND UNDER HIM IT SHALL SPRING UP) Through him it shall sprout. There is an allusion to the name צֶמַח: the Temple shall be reborn, just as in him the house of David was reborn.

AND HE SHALL BUILD THE TEMPLE TO THE LORD) The Temple of the Lord, which he himself is about to build, of which he is about to lay the first stone.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ECCE VIR) Hæc Deo dirigente Pilatus ad Christum aptavit dicens: ἴδε ὁ ἄνθρωπος.

ORIENS NOMEN EJVS) Germen nomen ejus: id est, surculus velut renatus ex stirpe Davidis. Vide supra III. 8. & ibi allata.

ET SUBTER EUM ORIETUR) Per eum germinabit. Est allusio ad nomen צֶמַח: renascetur Templum, sicut in illo domus Davidis renata est.

ET ÆDIFICABIT TEMPLUM DOMINO) Templum Domini, quod ipse ædificaturus est, cujus primum positurus est lapidem.

## 6:13
Verse 13.

AND HE SHALL BEAR THE GLORY) He himself also shall bear the glory: That is, the crown, namely, of a prince. See I Sam. XII. 30.

Grotius, as it appears, took this notable promise to be about Zerubbabel, Lyra about Joshua, which, however, is to be understood of no one else but the Messiah. For (1) the name of Christ is צֶמַח THE BRANCH, that this Zemach is the Messiah here, is evident both from other prophecies and from the previous oracle of this Prophet, ch. III. 8. This name is nowhere attributed to Zerubbabel, nor to Joshua the High Priest. (2) The matter here concerns a thing and a person altogether singular, which the words themselves indicate: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: BEHOLD THE MAN THE BRANCH (THE ORIENT) IS HIS NAME. Which Grotius also acknowledged, when he compared here the voice of Pilate concerning Christ: BEHOLD THE MAN. Concerning this name, Cocceius has it thus: The name of him who is designated here is the Man the Branch, i.e., the Man who can and ought rightly and deservedly to be called the Branch: indeed, a new stock of a new kind, or of the sons of God according to the promise of God and regeneration. The second Adam. For just as Adam was the germ and root of the ancient race, so is this one the primary origin of a new and restored race. (3) The discourse is about a future thing, not one that was already happening. But the construction of the temple had already been undertaken at that time. (4) Those words UNDER HIM SHALL HE SPRING UP, or HE SHALL GERMINATE, explaining the name of this Zemach, denote not a transitory germination, but a perennial act. Because this is proper to that Zemach, and so perpetual that he even obtains his name from it, and is deservedly called THE GERM, because under him all things germinate. Thus with the blessed Luther, blessed Balduin, p. 398. It is the simplest and plainest of all to take the particle Vav with the blessed Luther causally, in this sense: he is the germ, who under him, or his kingdom, all things will germinate and flourish, so that it can be gathered from the name itself that all the citizens of this kingdom will be in perpetual bloom. And it is conveniently done that he makes mention of no place from which he is to spring forth, but simply says, under him he shall germinate, to show that the flower of the Christian kingdom will be not only at Jerusalem, as hitherto in the old covenant, or in any other certain place, but everywhere, wherever there may be those who are to aggregate themselves to him. Tarnovius thinks otherwise of this in this place. He deservedly obtains this name, because in his own time he will germinate from his own place, from his own people, the tribe of Judah, and the destined seat, and having now been brought to light, he will grow up and flourish, like an irrigated shoot from the root of Jesse, Isa. 11:1, and in the city of Nazareth that נֵצֶר shall appear, Matt. 2:23. So also Wilkius, from the Reformed, explains it with Junius: The Hebrew letter speaks properly of the origin of the Messiah, or the germ, which is to germinate from its own place, and these things can be explained either in such a way that by his own proper virtue without human aids he is to arise, as regards both his person and his kingdom, and that this was done concerning his person is testified by Luke 1:35, as also his kingdom by Dan. 2:34, 45, or as that he is to germinate from his own proper seat and people, which the ancient prophets designated, namely from Nazareth, from which he was called a Nazarene, Matt. 2:52, as in my judgment the most ingenious Junius most conveniently explains, cf. Belg. Interpp. (5) The building of the temple of the Lord looks to the primary promise made to David concerning the Messiah, therefore it is repeated for the sake of confirmation and emphasis: AND he shall build the temple to the Lord, i.e., and he himself shall be the one of whom the word of the Lord was made to David (II. Sam. 7:13.) HE shall build a house for my name: It has emphasis, says Willius, because he repeats what he had said about the building, he himself shall build the temple of the Lord, i.e., just as my servant the germ shall build the Temple, so the same one, and not you Joshua, is the true architect, and therefore, because he himself will truly perform the spiritual building.

Blessed Balduin on this matter says thus: He repeats twice who is to be the architect of the true temple, for the people desired this most, and heard it most willingly of all. But because he introduces the Messiah as the architect of the temple, he indicates that there remains a temple far other than that which had been erected, however, by Joshua and Zerubbabel: namely, the Church of the New Testament built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief cornerstone: in whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord, etc., Eph. 2:20. This building the Messiah himself truly built up excellently by teaching and by performing miracles, by which parts of his office he powerfully destroyed the kingdom of the devil in this world, and healthfully erected the temple of the Lord, which is the Church of the living God, I Tim. 3:15, among Jews and Gentiles alike. (6)

To this also it most especially agrees, what is added: AND HE SHALL BEAR THE GLORY. Which does not fit Zerubbabel or Joshua at all; for the glory of Zerubbabel was far below the glory of David, Solomon, and other predecessors of the kings of the Lord's people. But it is said of Christ by way of excellence and in the most eminent manner, he himself shall bear the glory. He is the Lord of glory, I Cor. 2:8, and a King full of glory, who fills the whole earth with his glory, Isa. 6:3, John 12:39. He had to shine with the majesty and splendor of both crowns, and to bear the dignity which each of them represents. (7) To him also the Kingdom had been promised long ago in words similar to those which the Lord uses here, and he shall sit and shall rule upon his throne. II Sam. 7:13, Isa. 9:7. Zerubbabel did not sit on the royal throne, much less Joshua. For this expression is used of royal majesty, I Kings 2:19, and of the glory of the King of Kings, Ps. 2:4, Ps. 103:19. (8) In the Messiah, royal and pontifical dignity concur, not in Zerubbabel, nor in Joshua. But the discourse here is about him who ought both to sit on the royal throne and to be a priest upon his throne. For a priest also sat upon his throne, I Kings 4:18. Balduin thinks the same throne is designated: Sitting and ruling upon the throne is ascribed to him, because he was King and that eternal successor promised to David, II Sam. 7:13 and Ps. 132:11, and because he was to be King and Priest at the same time, therefore the Priesthood is also attributed to him on the same throne: namely, the Priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek, who was himself both King and Priest, as the Apostle interprets, Heb. 7:1. (9) It was similarly predicted concerning the Messiah, when the prophets prophesied about his royal throne, that peace would germinate under his rule, Ps. 72:3, that he would be called the prince of peace, and of his peace there would be no end, Isa. 9:6, that under this GERM and KING the Israelites would have peace and security, Jer. 23:6. Concerning which King Zechariah himself also predicted, ch. 9:9 seqq.

that under his rule chariots and horses are to be abandoned, bows broken, and peace promoted among the nations. (10) Concerning that Zemach, the builder of the temple, the Prophet prophesies, to whom nations or peoples were to flow from distant lands, that they might build the temple for the Lord. Which was fulfilled in the calling and gathering of the nations to the Messiah, who as the supreme architect built the Church of the Lord, Matt. XVI. 16. Cf. Eph. II. 21. (11) When a crown is placed upon Joshua the Priest, and it is a prediction about a man who was to bear glory and sit upon a Royal throne, it is manifest that this does not apply to Joshua, which is predicted on the occasion of the crown placed upon him, concerning the glory and Royal throne of the man Zemach, and therefore that the crown was placed upon Joshua only to figure this Zemach, who was to be both Priest and to bear a royal crown. Therefore this prophecy is to be understood of him, whose type was in the wearing of the crown and in the Priesthood of Joshua. But that he was a type of Zerubbabel, no one would say, but that he was a type of the Messiah, all acknowledge. Indeed, the Papists themselves, however much they may compare this crown of Joshua with the triple crown of the Roman Pontiff, and wish for the double dignity, Ecclesiastical and civil, to be signified to Joshua by the same, which they also claim for their own Pontiff, as Cornel. à Lapide rhetorizes at length about these things, yet they confess that it is not about Joshua, nor about Zerubbabel, but about Christ that it is treated here, and that Joshua was a type of him in the wearing of the crown. But it was placed upon him, not to signify that the principate would be joined in his person with the pontificate: for Zerubbabel held the principate, but not Joshua; but that it might be indicated that the antitype of Joshua, Christ Jesus, would have royal dignity with the Pontificate, and would sit upon the Royal throne of David, just as had been promised. Whence (12) the Chaldean interpreter explained these things concerning the Messiah, rendering it thus: Behold the man, whose name is Messiah, and he shall be magnified and shall build the temple of the Lord. Concerning whom see Galatinus, Book III, on the secrets of the Catholic truth, ch. XVI. Raimundus in Pug. Fid. part III, dist. III, c. XVI, p. 604. R. Nachman on Num. I. 4. There is no man called in this place, except the Messiah, the Son of David, as it is said (Zech. VI. 12) Behold the MAN whose name is the branch. And in Echa Rabathi on Lamentations I. 16, it is read thus: R. Joshua Ben Levi said: The Branch is his name (of the Messiah) as it is said Zech. VI. 12. R. Moses Hadarschan in R. Solomon Jarchi on Genesis XXXV. 8. The Redeemer, whom I shall raise up from among you, shall not have a Father according to that (Zech. VI. 12) Behold the man whose name is the branch, and he shall sprout UNDER HIMSELF. Similarly Is. LIII. And he shall grow up as a tender plant before him. The same Solomon Jarchi on this passage: The Branch is his name: It designates the Messiah. What of the fact that more recent Jews also acknowledge that these things treat of the Messiah, even though they snatch them away to a third temple, the building of which they expect, concerning which they also understand the temple of Ezekiel. But that the temple is spiritual, R. Alschech admits in Hagg. II. v. 10, that it will have spiritual walls and partitions. Christian Interpreters with great consensus interpret the present prophecy concerning the Messiah, Cyril, Jerome, Haymo, Albert the Great, Rupert, Vatablus, and almost all more recent ones, even Calvin himself, who is otherwise wont to be prone to snatching away prophecies about Christ to other things, but here he has pursued both the scope of the prophecy and the force of the words more closely: This vision was given to Zechariah, that he might raise up weak spirits to a better hope, since, namely, the Jews saw that they were being harshly pressed on all sides by their neighbors: because enemies were rising up from the front and from the rear, so that there was no end to their troubles. They thought, therefore, that they were miserable, who had returned from exile, if such a condition had to be undergone. For they could live tranquilly among the Babylonians, and they had already become accustomed to it, so that the exile was not so bitter to them. Thus, therefore, the grace of God had come into such disdain that it was almost hateful: because they thought it better to lack their homeland than to be attacked by new struggles daily. Furthermore, the very habitation of the land was not in itself so desirable, except in respect of the hope given: namely, because God had promised through his Prophets that the kingdom of David would be glorious anew, and then that the dignity and glory of the temple would be greater than it had been before. The Jews, when they saw themselves being assiduously afflicted by their enemies, thought this whole thing was frivolous. Thus there is no doubt that many complaints flew about here and there, and much clamor. Therefore, that they might cease to murmur thus against God, this vision was offered to the Prophet, in which he is commanded to take gold and silver from four men, and from it to make two crowns, which he should place upon the head of Joshua the high priest, namely, that the Jews might be certainly persuaded that the state of the people would be safe, such as it had been of old, when, namely, the kingdom and the priesthood flourished. For these were the highest honors, and as it were the two eyes of the body, when, namely, the priest was the mediator of God and men: the King also would sustain the person of God in governing the people. We see, therefore, that the restoration of the Church is denoted by the two crowns. But at the same time it is to be noted that both crowns are placed upon the head of Joshua, which was new and unusual. We know that a tiara had been given to the priests: we know also that Kings had been adorned with a diadem, but no one was to bear both a royal diadem and a priestly tiara. Here, therefore, is shown in the person of one man the conjunction of kingdom and priesthood, which before had not been in use. For God had openly distinguished those two orders in his law. We see, therefore, that something previously unknown is portended by this prophecy; namely, that the same person would be King and Priest. For what Jerome says among other things, that it is possible that there were several crowns, this is vain and frivolous, and furthermore it openly fights with the words of the Prophet. For a little later he will add that there will be a counsel of peace between these two, namely, between the Kingdom and the Priesthood. That the same person also thinks that only one crown was given to the Priest, this also is false; finally, it overturns the whole doctrine of the Prophet, as much as in it lies. This is Calvin.

Verse of the same.

AND HE SHALL SIT AND SHALL RULE UPON HIS THRONE) That is, sitting on the throne, he will pronounce judgments together with the senators.

AND HE SHALL BE A PRIEST UPON HIS THRONE) Also the Priest will have his throne in that same senate.

AND THE COUNSEL OF PEACE SHALL BE BETWEEN THEM BOTH) That is, they will agree very well, as once Moses and Aaron did. A happy Republic where both the Prince and the Priest agree and perform their duty well.

Grotius either invented these glosses, or certainly interpolated them as received from the Jews, to overturn the prophecy concerning Christ. But they collapse by their own vanity. For it is one thing to sit and rule upon one's throne, and another to administer justice together with Senators. The former implies royal majesty and dominion: the latter, however, is an ἀξίωμα common to all Senators. Nor is the Priesthood attributed to one subject, and Dominion to another. It is the same person who is both King sitting upon a throne, and priest, to whom a proper throne is attributed. For the discourse is about only one subject, about the Branch, whose glory and office is described: there is nothing here about a Senate or Sanhedrin, much less that Zerubbabel and Joshua are to have their seat in the Senate. These things are from private interpretation. Those predicates are of one and the same person to sound everything, whom he points out δεικτικῶς: BEHOLD THE MAN, the context itself teaches, and all Christian interpreters easily agree. To Grotius, however, it pleased here, as in any other oracles, to Judaize. Nor is the emphasis observed rashly, that he says he will sit on his throne, thus expressing the stability and propriety of the priestly and kingly office, that he is about to perform his own peculiar and singular priesthood and kingly office, and is about to hold this throne as his own and perpetual. Others also observe that the Prophet here signifies the four chariots, that is, the Monarchies, which will end in the Kingdom of Christ, of whom he now says, he shall rule upon his throne. Nor indeed do those words THE COUNSEL OF PEACE SHALL BE between those two refer to Zerubbabel and Joshua. For no mention had been made of either Zerubbabel or Joshua in those august things being proclaimed and explained, and although Joshua had been commemorated before, when the crowns were to be imposed, here however the prophecy is now had concerning the Branch who is to arise, and who is to build the temple of the Lord, who is to be King and Priest alike. Wherefore these things are to be accepted thus, that in these between THOSE TWO thrones, viz. the Priesthood and the kingdom, those two states, figured by the golden and silver crown, the counsel of peace is to be. Concerning the two thrones, because כסא is of the Masculine gender, Jerome, Rupert, Vatablus, Isidorus Clarius, Montanus, and others, accept it. Cornelius à Lapide judges it to be more appropriate if a reflection is made to the Prince and the Priest, because the mention of the Prince sitting on the throne, and the Priest sitting on his throne preceded, so that the sense may be: In Christ there will be the highest consensus and concord between the prince sitting on the royal throne, and the Pontiff sitting on the pontifical throne, because Christ will be both, and will join in himself both the dignity of the pontificate and of the Kingdom. Thus B. Balduin. Since God otherwise would not permit that others should be Kings and Priests at the same time, just as He severely punished this when attempted by King Uzziah 2 Chron. XXVI: verse 19, in Christ indeed both had to concur, because through him we have been made a Kingdom and Priests to God Apocal. I. 6. Although therefore formerly there was sometimes the greatest dissonance between the Kingdom and the Priesthood in the people of God, when kings very often hostilely persecuted the Priests: yet it is indicated that this dissension is to be removed in Christ, and that in him the Kingly and Sacerdotal dignity can very well agree, since it is by him that the Church is sanctified and defended for the very same end. B. Tarnovius with some others understands by both, Jews and Gentiles. At the same time, however, he will also be a Priest on his throne, offering himself as a victim most acceptable to the Father in his passion and on the altar of the cross, so that thus through his blood the enmity might be removed, the counsel of peace between both, those who are near in Judea, and those who are among the Gentiles, and are still far from the Church, Is. LIII. 8. Eph. II. 13, 14, 15, 16. Col. II. 13, 14. R. Salomon Jarchi understands the Jews and Israelites by those two; Willius prefers to understand by both those, the Jerusalemite and Babylonian Jews, and indeed even the Egyptians with the proselytes, and in general all who call upon the name of God outside Judea, because Christ, King and Priest, is about to erect a counsel of peace among them, and to join those far apart into one and reconcile them to God Is. LVII. 19. Eph. II. 13. Lud. de Dieu renders: And he shall build the temple of Jehovah, and he himself shall bear the majesty, and shall sit, and shall rule upon his (JEHOVAH'S) throne and shall be a priest upon his throne, and the counsel of peace shall go forth BETWEEN THOSE TWO, namely the BRANCH and Jehovah; so also Joh. Coccejus, comparing Ps. CX. 1, 4. Ps. LXVIII. 19. Ps. II. 7.

and noting here the fruit of the priesthood of Christ. The fruit of priestly intercession is the obtaining of peace. The words cohere thus: And he shall be a Priest (approaching) on his throne, and thus the counsel of peace shall be between those two, i.e. his intercession shall be the cause of the counsel of peace, i.e. as it were the will to remove the enmity, which was between the Gentiles through the middle wall of partition. Thus the Priesthood of Christ is opposed to the Aaronic priesthood. This was the middle wall of partition, that is the cause of reconciliation, Eph. 12, 13, 14, 15. Col. I. 21, 22. concerning which peace ch. III. verse 10. When he attributes the counsel of peace to the Father and the Branch (for what is the branch but the Son?), he signifies the one will of both founded on the most wise reason. The will of the Father and the Son, as the essence is one: but insofar as they are distinct persons, it is the counsel of two. Zechariah imitates the Master of the Prophets, Moses, Gen. I. 26. Let us make, and the like. For it is for those who have the counsel of peace to say Let us make Peace, to which the Osiandrian paraphrase also goes: Christ will direct his counsels to this, that he may establish peace between God and men. But the former explanation is to be preferred, as being simpler.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET IPSE PORTABIT GLORIAM) Ipse quoque portabit gloriam: Id est, coronam, nempe principis. Vide I. Sam. XII. 30.

De Zorobabele, ut apparet, hanc insignem promissionem accepit Grotius, de Josua Lyranus, quæ vero de nullo alio, quam de Messia intelligenda. Nam Christi (1) nomen est צֶמַח GERMINIS, quod Zemach hic Messias sit, ut tum ex vaticiniis aliis constat, tum ex superiori oraculo hujus Prophetæ c. III. 8. Zorobabeli hoc nomen nuspiam tributum, neque Josuæ Pontifici. (2) agitur hic de re & persona prorsus singulari, quod verba ipsa indicant: Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens: ECCE VIR GERMEN (ORIENS) NOMEN EJUS. Quod agnovit etiam Grotius, cum Pilati vocem de Christo: ECCE HOMO hic contulit. De hoc nomine Coccejus ita habet: Nomen ejus, qui hic designatur, est Vir Germen, h. e. Homo, qui recte & merito Germen nominari possit & debeat: quippe stirps nova novi generis sive filiorum Dei secundum promissionem Dei & regenerationem. Adamus secundus. Ut enim Adamus fuit Germen & stirps generis vetusti, ita hic prima origo generis novi & instaurati. (3) De re futura sermo est, non quæ jam agebatur. At extructio templi isto tempore jam suscepta erat. (4) Illa verba SUBTER EUM ORIETUR, vel GERMINABIT, nomen hujus Zemachi explicantia, non transitoriam pro germinationem, sed actum perennem notant. Quia hoc illi Zemacho proprium est, & perpetuum adeo, ut inde etiam nomen obtineat, meritoque GERMEN dicatur, quod sub eo omnia germinent. Ita cum B. Luthero, B. Balduin. p. 398. Simplicissimum omnium & planissimum est, particulam Vav cum B. Luthero caussaliter accipere, hoc sensu, germen est, qui sub eo, vel ejus regno omnia germinabunt & florebunt, ita ut ex ipso nomine colligi possit, omnes regni hujus cives in perpetuo flore futuros. Et commode factum est, quod nullius loci mentionem facit, unde sit progerminaturus, sed simpliciter dicit, sub eo germinabit, ut ostendat, non Hierosolymis tantum, ut hactenus in veteri fœdere, aut alio certo in loco, sed ubique locorum florem fore regni Christiani, ubicunque modo fuerint, qui se ad ipsum sint aggregaturi. Aliter hæc Tarno. vius in h. l. Merito hoc nomen obtinet, quia suo tempore ex suo loco germinabit, ex propria gente, tribu Juda, ac sede destinata, & jam in lucem editus succrescet ac virescet, velut surculus irriguus de radice Jesse Ef. XI. 1. & in urbe Nazareth ille נֵצֶר apparebit Matth. II. 23. Sic etiam è Reformatis cum Junio explicat Wilkius: Litera Ebræa proprie de origine Messiæ, sive germinis loquitur, quod ex loco suo sit germinaturus, possuntque hæc vel ita explicari, quod virtute sua propria absque humanis auxiliis sit exoriturus, cum quod personam, tum quod regnum ejus spectat, idque de ejus persona factum testatur Luc. I. 35. ut & regno Dan. II. 34. 45. vel ut quod ex propria sua sede ac gente sit germinatu- rus, quam veteres Prophetæ designarint, nempe è Nazaretha, à qua Nazarenus fuit appellatus Matth. II. 52. uti meo judicio convenientissime exponit ingeniosissimus Junius, conf. Belg. Interpp. (5) Æ- dificatio templi Domini respicit primariam promif- sionem, Davidi factam de Messia, ideo repetitur βεβαιώσεως & δεινότητος caussa: ET ipse extruet templum Domino, q. d. & ipse erit is, de quo ver- bum Domini ad Davidem factum (II. Sam. VII. 13.) IPSE nomini meo ædificabit domum: Emphasin ha- bet, inquit Willius, quod repetit, quæ de ædificatio- ne dixerat, ille ipse ædificabit templum Domini, q. d. Uti servus meus germen ædificabit Tem- plum, ita idem, non vero tu Josua, verus archite- ctus est, ac propterea, quia ipse reverà ædifica- tionem spiritualem præstabit.

B. Balduinus de hac re ita: Bis repetit, quis sit fu- turus veri templi architectus, hoc enim maxime desiderabat populus, & omnium libentissime au- diebat. Quia autem Messiam, ut architectum tem- pli introducit, indicat, superesse templum longe a- liud, quam hactenus à Josua & Zorobabele utcun- que erectum fuerat:nimirum Ecclesiam Novi Te- stamenti ædificatam super fundamentum Aposto- lorum & Prophetarum, ipso summo angulari la- pide Jesu Christo: in quo omnis ædificatio con- structa crescit in Templum sanctum in Domino &c. Eph. II. v. 20. Hoc sane ædificium Messias ipse præclare exædificavit docendo & miracula eden- do, quibus officii sui partibus regnum diaboli, in hoc mundo potenter destruxit, & templum Domi- ni, quod est Ecclesia Dei vivi I. Tim. III. v. 15. salu- tariter inter Judæos pariter & gentes erexit. (6)

Huic etiam maxime convenit, quod additur: ET IPSE PORTABIT GLORIAM. * Quod Zoro- babeli, aut Josuæ adeo non congruit; gloria enim Zorobabelis longe erat infra gloriam Davidis, Sa- lomonis, & aliorũ antecessorum Regum populi Do- mini. At de Christo ἐξοχικῶς & eminentissima ra- tione dicitur, ipse portabit gloriam. Ipse est Domi- nus gloriæ I. Cor. II. 8. & Rex plenus gloria, qui u- niversam terram replet gloria sua Ef. VI. 3. Job. XII. 39. Ipse fulgere debuit utriusque coronæ majestate ac splendore, & dignitatem, quam unaquæque ea- rum repræsentet, gerere. (7) Huic etiam Regnum promissum erat pridem verbis similibus, quibus hic utitur Dominus, & sedebit & dominabitur super solio suo. II. Sam. VII. 13. Ef. IX. 7. Zorobabel in thro- no regio non sedit:nedum Josua. Adhibetur enim hæc locutio de regia majestate. I. Reg. II. 19. & de gloria Regis Regum Psal. II. 4. Psal. CIII. 19. (8) In Messia concurrit Regia & Pontificalis dignitas, non in Zorobabele, nec in Josua. At sermo hic est de eo, qui & in throno Regio sedere debeat, & sa- cerdos esse super solio suo. Nam & sacerdos inside- bat solio suo I. Reg. IV. 18. Balduinus idem solium designari censet: Sessio & dominatio super solio duo ei adscribitur, quia Rex erat & successor ille æ- ternus Davidi promissus II. Sam. VII. 13. & Psalm. CXXXII. 11. & quia simul Rex & Sacerdos futurus erat, idcirco ei quoque Sacerdotium tribuitur in eodẽ solio: Sacerdotium nimirum secundum ordine Melchisedec, qui & ipse Rex & Sacerdos fuit, in- terprete Apostolo Hebr. VII. 1. (9) De Messia præ- dictum similiter fuit, cum de regio throno ejus va- ticinati sunt Prophetæ, quod pax germinatura sit sub regimine ejus Pf. LXXII. 3. quod princeps pacis dicendus sit, & pacis ejus non sit futurus finis Esi IX. 6. quod sub hoc GERMINE ac REGE Israelitæ pacem & securitatem habituri sint Jer. XXIII. 6. De quo Rege etiã Zacharias ipse prædixit c. IX. 9. seqq.

quod sub regimine ejus currus & equi abdicandi, arcus frangendi, pax inter gentes proferenda sit. (10) De illo Zemacho, templi extructore vaticinatur Propheta, ad quem è longinquis terris nationes vel gentes confluere debuere, ut extruentur templum Domino. Quod impletum est in vocatione & confluxu gentium ad Messiam, qui ceu summus architectus Ecclesiam Domini extruxit, Matth. XVI. 16. Conf. Eph. II. 21. (11) Cum corona imponitur Josuæ Sacerdoti, ac prædictio sit de viro, qui gloriam portaturus erat, & in throno Regio sessurus, manifestum est, non convenire hoc Josuæ, quod occasione coronæ eidem impositæ prædicitur, de gloria & throno Regio viri Zemachi, ideoque Josuæ solum coronam impositam fuisse ad figurandum hunc Zemachum, qui & Sacerdos futurus, & coronam regiam portaturus erat. De eo ergo hoc vaticinium intelligendum, cujus typus fuit in gestatione coronæ & in Sacerdotio Josua. At eum Zorobabelis typum fuisse, nemo dixerit, Messiæ autem typum fuisse, omnes agnoscunt. Sane Papistæ ipsi, utut hanc coronam Josuæ cum Romani Pontificis triplicata corona componant, ac duplicem dignitatem, Ecclesiasticam & civilem Josuæ fignificatam eadem velint, quam suo etiam Pontifici vindicant, uti Cornel. à Lapid. de his prolixe rhetoricatur, fatentur tamen non de Josua, neque de Zorobabele, sed de Christo hic agi, ejusdemque typum extitisse Josuam in coronæ gestatione. Quæ vero eidem imposita est, non ut principatum in ejus persona cum pontificatu conjunctum fore significaret: nam principatu fungebatur Zorobabel, non vero Josua; sed ut indicaretur, antitypum Josuæ Christum Jesum cum Pontificatu regiam dignitatem habiturum, & in throno Regio Davidis, quemadmodū promissum erat, sessurum. Unde (12) Chaldæus interpres exposuit hæc de Messia, ita reddens: Ecce vir, cujus nomen est Messias, & magnificandus & ædificaturus templum Domini. De quo apud Galat. Libr. III. de arcan. Cathol. verit. cap. XVI. Raimund. in Pug. Fid. part. III. dist. III. c. XVI. p. 604. R. Nachman in Num. I. 4. Non est vir dictus in hoc loco, nisi Messias, Filius David, sicut dicitur (Zach. VI 12.) Ecce VIR germen nomen ejus. Et in Echa Rabathi super Thren. I. 16. ita legitur: R. Josua Ben Levi dixit: Germen est nomen ejus (Messiæ) sicut dictum est Zach. VI. 12. R. Moses Hadarschan apud R. Salomon. Jarchium in Genes. XXXV. 8. Redemtor, quem suscitabo è vobis, non habebit Patrem juxta illud (Zach. VI. 12.) Ecce vir germen nomen ejus, & SUBTER SE germinabit. Similiter Es. LIII. Et ascendit sicut virgultum coram eo. Idem Salomo Jarchi in h. l. Germen nomen ejus: Designat Messiam. Quid quod recentiores quoque Judæi agnoscant hæc de Messia agere, tametsi ea abripiant ad tertium templum, cujus ædificationem expectant, de quo etiam Ezechielis templum intelligunt. Quod vero templum רוחני spirituale esse fatetur R. Alschech in Hagg. II. v. 10. quod muros & parietes spirituales habiturum sit. Christiani Interpp. magno consensu de Messia vaticinium præsens interpretantur, Cyrillus, Hieronymus, Haymo, Albertus M. Rupertus, Vatablus, & recentiores plerique omnes, etiam Calvinus ipse, qui pronus alioquin esse solet in vaticiniis de Christo aliorsum abripiendis, hic vero & scopum vaticinii, & vim verborum pressius persequutus est: Hæc visio data fuit Zachariæ, ut erigeret debiles animos in spem meliorem, quoniam scilicet videbant Judæi se duriter undique premi à vicinis: quia surgebant à fronte, & à tergo hostes, ita ut nullus esset molestiarum finis. Putabant ergo se esse mise- ros, qui reversi essent ab exilio, si talis conditio subeunda erat. Poterant enim tranquille agere a- pud Babylonios, & jam assueverant, ita ut illis non tam acerbum esset exilium. Sic ergo venerat in fa- stidium Dei gratia, ut prope odiosa esset: quia sa- tius putabant carere patria, quam novis quotidie certaminibus impeti. Deinde ipsa terræ habitatio non adeo per se erat optabilis, nisi respectu spei datæ: nempe quia pollicitus fuerat Deus per suos Prophetas regnum Davidis de integro fore glo- riosum, deinde majorem fore templi dignitatem & gloriam, quam ante fuisset. Judæi, cum viderent se assidue affligi à suis hostibus, putabant hoc to- tum esse frivolum. Ita non dubium est, quin multæ querimoniæ passim volitarint, & multi strepitus. Ergo ut desinerent ita obmurmurare Deo, Pro- phetæ hæc visio oblata fuit, in qua jubetur accipe- re aurum & argentum à quatuor viris, & inde con- ficere duas coronas, quas imponat capiti Jehosuæ sacerdotis magni, nempe ut certo persuasi sint Ju- dæi, fore statum populi incolumem, qualis olim fuerat, cem scilicet florerent regnum & sacerdo- tium. Erant enim hæc summa decora, & quasi duo oculi corporis, quum scilicet sacerdos esset media- tor Dei & hominum: Rex etiam Dei personam sustineret in populo gubernando. Videmus ergo per duas coronas notari Ecclesiæ restitutionem. Sed simul notandum est, imponi utramque coro- nam capiti Jehosuæ, quod novum fuit, & insoli- tum. Scimus tiaram fuisse datam sacerdotibus: sci- mus etiam Reges diademate fuisse ornatos, sed ne- mo unus debuit & regium diadema, & tiaram sa- cerdotalem ferre. Hic ergo ostenditur in unius ho- minis persona conjunctio regni & sacerdotii, quod ante non fuerat in usu. Deus enim aperte in lege sua distinxerat illos duos ordines. Videmus ergo portendi hoc vaticinio aliquid prius incognitum; nempe quod idem futurus sit Rex & Sacerdos. Nam quod Hieronymus inter alia dicit, fieri posse, ut plures coronæ fuerint, hoc vanum est, ac frivo- lum, deinde aperte pugnat cum verbis Prophetæ. Nam paulo post subjiciet, fore consilium pacis inter hæc duo, nempe inter Regnum & Sacerdotium. Quod etiam idem putat unam duntaxat coronam fuisse datam Sacerdoti, hoc quoque falsum est de- nique evertit totam doctrinam Prophetæ, quan- tum in se est. Hæc Calvinus.

Vers. eod.

ET SEDEBIT ET DOMINABITVR SVPER SOLIO SVO) Id est, in solio sedens, simul cum senato- ribus jura dicet.

ET ERIT SACERDOS SVPER SOLIO SVO) Etiam Sacerdos in eodem illo senatu solium suum ha- bebit.

ET CONSILIVM PACIS ERIT INTER ILLOS DVOS) Id est, optime inter illos conveniet, ut olim inter Mosen & Aaronem. Felix Respubl. ubi concordant, offi- ciumque bene faciunt & Princeps & Sacerdos.

Commentus has glossas est, vel certe à Judæis acceptas interpolavit Grotius, ad evertendum va- ticinium de Christo. Sed illæ vanitate sua conci- dunt. Nam aliud est sedere, & dominari super solio suo, aliud simul cum Senatoribus jura dicere. Illud regiam majestatem & dominationem infert: hoc vero ἀξίωμα commune omnibus Senatoribus. Nec alteri subjecto tribuitur Sacerdotium, alteri Do- minium. Idem est & Rex sedens super throno, & sacerdos, cui tribuitur solium proprium. Nam non nisi de uno subjecto sermo est, de Zemacho, cujus gloria & officium describitur: Nihil hic de Senatu aut Synedrio, nedum quod Zorobabel & Josua in Senatu sedem suam habituri sint. Hæc ab ἰδίᾳ sunt ἐπιλύσει. De una eademque persona prædicata illa omnia sonare, quem δεικτικῶς indicat: ECCE VIR, συνέχεια ipsa docet, omnesq; interpp. Christiani facile consentiunt. Grotio autem hic, ut in aliis quibusvis oraculis, Judaizare placuit. Neque temere observatur emphasis, quod in solio suo sessurum dicit, sacerdotii & regii muneris stabilitatem & proprietatem ita exprimens, quod peculiare & singulare suum & sacerdotium & regium munus obiturus sit, soliumque hoc habiturus sit proprium & perpetuum. Alii etiam observant, Prophetam hic significare quatuor quadrigas, id est, Monarchias, desituras in Regnum Christi, de quo nunc ait, dominabitur super solio suo. Neque vero verba illa CONSILIUM PACIS ERIT inter duos istos ad Zorobabelem & Josuam sese referunt. Nulla enim vel Zorobabelis vel Josuæ mentio facta erat, in augustis illis prædicandis explicandisque, ac licet Josua antea commemoratus fuerit, cum coronæ imponendæ, hic tamen de Zemacho orituro, & templum Domini extructuro, qui Rex pariter & Sacerdos futurus sit, vaticinium jam habetur. Quapropter hæc ita accipienda, quod in his inter DUO ILLA solia, Sacerdotium sc. & regnum, duos illos status, aurea & argentea corona figuratos, consilium pacis futurum sit. De duobus thronis, quia כסא generis Masculini est, Hieronymus, Rupertus, Vatablus, Isidorus Clarius, Montanus, & alii, accipiunt. Cornelius à Lapide magis appositum esse judicat, si reflexio fiat ad Principem & Sacerdotem, quia sedentis in throno Principis, & Sacerdotis in solio suo sedentis mentio præcessit, ut sensus sit: In Christo summus erit consensus & concordia inter principem sedentem in solio regali, & Pontificem sedentem in solio pontificali, quia Christus utrumque erit, & utramque dignitatem pontificatus & Regni in se conjunget. Ita B. Balduin. Cum Deus alioquin non permitteret, ut alii simul & Reges & Sacerdotes essent, quemadmodum hoc ab Ozia Rege attentatum graviter punivit 2. Paral. XXVI: vers. 19. in Christo sane utrumque concurrere debuit, quia per ipsum facti sumus nos Regnum & Sacerdotes Deo Apocal. I. 6. Etsi igitur olim interdum maxima fuit dissonantia inter Regnum & Sacerdotium in populo Dei, quando reges sæpenumero hostiliter persequebantur Sacerdotes: hoc tamen dissidium in Christo sublatum iri indicatur, in eoque perquam optime & Regiam, & Sacerdotalem dignitatem convenire posse, quippe à quo eodem plane fine & sanctificatur & defenditur Ecclesia. B. Tarnovius cum aliis nonnullis per utrosque Judæos & gentes intelligit. Simul vero etiam erit Sacerdos in solio suo seipsum victimam Patri gratissimam in passione ac ara crucis offerens, ut sic per ejus sanguinem sit sublata inimicitia, consilium pacis inter utrosque, eos qui in Judæa sunt propinqui, & eos, qui inter gentes sunt, atque adhuc ab Ecclesia longinqui, Es. LIII. 8. Eph. II. 13, 14. 15. 15. 16. Col. II. 13. 14. R. Salomon Jarchi Judæos & Israelitas per duos illos intelligit; Willius mavult per ambos illos Judæos Hierosolymitanos, & Babylonios, intelligere, imo etiam Ægyptios cum proselytis, & in universum omnibus Dei nomen invocantibus extra Judæam, quod inter ipsos consilium pacis erecturus sit Christus, Rex ac Sacerdos, ac longe dissidentes in unum conjuncturus & Deo reconciliaturus Esa. LVII. 19. Eph. II. 13. Lud. de Dieu reddit: Et ille ædificabit templum Jehovæ, atque ipse portabit majestatem, & sedebit, ac dominabitur super thronum ejus (JEHOVÆ) & erit sacerdos super thronum ejus, & consilium pacis exibit INTER DUOS ILLOS, nempe GERMEN & Jehovam; sic etiam Joh. Coccejus, conferens Psal. CX. 1. 4. Psal. LXIIX. 19. Ps. II. 7.

& notans hic fructum sacerdotii Christi. Fructus sacerdotalis intercessionis est impetratio pacis. Verba sic cohærent: Et erit Sacerdos (appropinquans) in folio ejus, & sic consilium pacis erit inter illos duos, h. e. ipsius intercessio erit causa consilii pacis, h. e. quasi voluntatis tollendi inimicitiam, quæ erat inter gentes per parietem intergerinum. Sic opponitur Sacerdotium Christi, sacerdotio Aharonico. Hoc erat paries intergerinus, illud est causa ἀποκαταλλαγῆς, Ephes. 12, 13. 14. 15. Coloss. I. 21. 22. de qua pace cap. III. vers. 10. Quum Patri & Germini (quid enim germen nisi Filius?) attribuit consilium pacis, significat unam utriusque voluntatem sapientissima ratione fundatam. Voluntas Patris & Filii, ut essentia una est: sed quatenus distinctæ personæ sunt, consilium duorum est. Imitatur Zacharias Magistrum Prophetarum Mosen Genes. I. 26. Faciamus, & similia. Nam qui consilium pacis habent, eorum est dicere Faciamus Pacem, quo abit quoque Osiandrina paraphrasis: Christus, consilia sua eo intendet, ut pacem inter Deum & homines constituat. Sed præferenda prior explicatio, ceu simplicior.

## 6:14
Vers. 14.

AND THE CROWNS SHALL BE FOR HELEM, AND TOBIAH, AND JEDAIAH, AND HEN THE SON OF ZEPHANIAH AS A MEMORIAL IN THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) They shall be hung in the Temple, with the name of those who duly dedicated them noted. Neither the priest nor the prince kept the crowns for themselves: for in that age it was held a sacrilege, outside of supreme and inevitable necessity, to turn things devoted to God to private uses: nor had that contempt of the divine power and of sacred things yet prevailed in their minds.

An overly jejune interpretation, concerning a mere mnemonic anathema. Those crowns ought rather to have been (1) didactic, from which they may understand that even those from afar have the right of approaching God, as the subjoined explanation holds, for which purpose it is also believed the building of the altar in Jos. XXII. v. 23 was done. See Junius, Tarnovius, & Willius. (2) Prophetic, concerning the certain coming Messiah, who will bear the crown of the Kingdom & Priesthood. (3) Exhortatory, so that by the sight of them other citizens of the Church may be stirred to liberality & munificence.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET CORONÆ ERUNT HELEM, ET TOBIÆ, ET IDAIÆ, ET HEM FILIO SOPHONIÆ MEMORIALE IN TEMPLO DOMINI) Suspendentur in Templo, annotato nomine eorum, qui ea rite dicarunt. Non retinuerē sibi coronas, aut sacerdos aut princeps: nam ea ætate nefas habebatur, extra summam & inevitabilem necessitatem, Deo devota in privatos usus vertere: neque is qui nunc contemtus numinis, rerumque sacrarum invalerat animos.

Nimis jejuna interpretatio, de nudo anathemate μνημονευτικῳ. Signa potius esse debebant illæ coronæ (1) didactica, è quibus intelligant, etiam longinquis jus esse accedendi ad Deum, uti habet subjuncta explicatio, quo consilio etiam creditur facta ædificatio altaris Jos. XXII. v. 23. Vid. Junius, Tarnovius, & Willius. (2) Prophetica de certo venturo Messia, qui coronam Regni & Sacerdotii portabit. (3) Paranctica, ut eorum intuitu alii Ecclesiæ cives ad liberalitatem & munificentiam excitentur.

## 6:15
Verse 15.

AND THEY WHO ARE FAR OFF SHALL COME, AND SHALL BUILD IN THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) Even strangers, either they will supply material, or they will be helpers to you in the work. Isaiah LX. 10. add what is above II. 11.

These things are not to be understood as concerning the material structure of the temple. For to complete this, neither were such supplies from those afar so much desired any longer, nor did the prophecy above treat of that material temple, but of the building of the temple to arise from the BRANCH. Add that the external temple was not to be finished by the nations, but by the hands of Zerubbabel, which had begun it, Zech. IV. 9. Therefore, Christian interpreters have observed with great consensus that the calling of the nations is predicted in this place, which Zechariah also predicted above in c. II. 11. & Isaiah in c. LX. 10. Therefore, those from afar are signified not so much by place, as by right & affection, who are to come & build the mystical & spiritual temple of the Lord. Conf. Joel III. 5. Am. IX. 26. 27. Hagg. II. 7. Zech. VIII. 22. Acts II. 39. I. Pet. II. 3.

Verse the same.

AND YOU SHALL KNOW THAT THE LORD OF HOSTS HATH SENT ME UNTO YOU) Namely, when the outcome shall correspond to the things predicted.

These words are not the Prophet's, but of the angel speaking in the Prophet, the Son of God, who introduced the words of God the Father in v. 12. 13. treating of the branch to arise: Thus saith the Lord of hosts. But He Himself began to speak in turn from His own person in v. 14. and here He professes that, through the calling of the nations, it will be acknowledged that He

(the Messiah) was sent to the Jews. Which Eusebius rightly observed concerning Christ in book V of the Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. XXV, though he is rashly criticized here for this by Cornelius. For it is manifest that these are the words of that Lord, whose word is said to have come to Zechariah v. 9, and not that Zechariah himself spoke them: And the Lord used similar words above in ch. II. 9, 11.

BUT THIS SHALL BE, IF YOU HEARKEN TO THE VOICE OF THE LORD YOUR GOD) Not even this promise of His was without a condition.

Since it is clear that that promise concerns the Messiah, His spiritual temple, and the calling of the Gentiles, it can by no means be established as conditional: and therefore these words are explained in two ways, (1) that the condition concerns the participation of the Jews, and an aposiopesis is established in this manner: And it shall be, or it shall come to pass, that you may participate in this grace, if you hearken to the commandments of God. Thus the blessed Balduinus on page 417. He understands not so much the obedience of works as of faith, in this sense: If you believe the Gospel concerning Christ, which is now preached to you under the wrappings of figures, and which He Himself will manifest to you a few years from now, you will certainly experience all these promises of mine having their fulfillment; but if you are unwilling to believe, truly whatever I have said to you concerning the Messiah, His kingdom, and priesthood, will be covered, and will remain wrapped in the darkness of your ignorance: This therefore was a tacit prediction of the blinding of the Jews in the Kingdom of Christ. For although the promises and gifts of God are without repentance Rom. XI. v. 29, and our unbelief cannot make void the faithfulness of God Rom. III. 3, yet faith is that saving medium by which the fruit of the divine promises is apprehended. Because, therefore, the Jews were unwilling to have faith in the words of the omnipotent God, for that reason, to this very day, the veil of the Old Testament remains not yet revealed to them, as the Apostle speaks II. Corinthians III, v. 14, and the Gospel preached concerning Christ is to them a savor of death unto death II. Cor. II. 16, because the god of this world has blinded their minds, that the illumination of the Gospel might not shine upon them II. Cor. IV. v. 4. Thus Balduinus. (2) that by the little word אִם a condition is not posited, but time is designated, as Tarnovius and Willius explain with Junius, as if they were saying, after that time in which you have built the temple of God and have performed the singular prophecies enunciated above: after that time, I say, this kingdom of Christ is to come to the Church. The former explanation is more approved by us, which Cocceius also embraced: It shall be for a memorial to them, that their descendants may enjoy this peace procured through the priest, and through him be preserved as living stones in the temple of the Lord: If only they hearken to the voice of the Lord, i.e., to the Son of God speaking the words.

THE SECOND PART OF THE PROPHET ZECHARIAH.

THE THIRD SERMON.

An Epanorthotic-Pedagogical [discourse] disapproving of {arbitrary forms of worship, and instructing concerning true piety.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET QUI PROCVL SVNT VENIENT, ET ÆDIFICABVNT IN TEMPLO DOMINI) Etiam extranei, aut materiam suppeditabunt, aut in opere vobis erunt adjutores. Esaiæ LX. 10. adde quæ supra II. 11.

Hæc non de materiali structura templi accipienda. Nam ad hanc perficiendam neque tales longinquorum suppetiæ adeo desiderabantur amplius, neque superius vaticinium de templo illo materiali egit, sed de templo à GERMINE orituro extruendo. Adde, quod templum externum non gentes, sed manus Zorobabelis, quæ ceperant, consummaturæ erant Zach. IV. 9. Proinde observarunt Christiani Interpp. magno consensu, prædictam hoc loco esse evocationem gentium, quam etiam Zacharias supra c. II. 11. & Esaias c. LX. 10. prædixere. Significantur ergo longinqui non tam loco, quam jure & affectu venturi & ædificaturi templum Domini mysticum & spirituale. Conf. Joel. III. 5. Am. IX. 26. 27. Hagg. II. 7. Zach. VIII. 22. Act. II. 39. I. Petr. II. 3.

Vers. eod.

ET SCIETIS, QVIA DOMINVS DEVS EXERCITVVM MISIT ME AD VOS) Nempe ubi eventus prædictis congruet.

Verba hæc non Prophetæ sunt, sed angeli loquentis in Propheta, Filii Dei, qui verba Dei Patris introduxit v. 12. 13. de germine orituro agentia: Sic ait Dominus exercituum. Ipse vero ex persona propria loqui vicissim cepit v. 14. atque hic profitetur, per vocationem gentium agnitum iri, se

(Messiam) missum esse ad Judæos. Quod recte ob- servavit de Christo Eusebius l. V. Demonstr. Euan- gel. c. XXV. temere hic ideo notatus à Cornelio. Manifestum enim est, hæc Dominum illum, cujus verbum factum dicitur ad Zachariam v. 9. non ve- ro Zachariam ipsum loquutum esse: Et usus est Dominus similibus verbis supra c. II. 9. 11.

ERIT AUTEM HOC, SI AUDITU AUDIE- RITIS VOCEM DOMINI DEI VESTRI) Ne hæc quidem promissio sua carebat conditione.

Quum in aprico sit, promissionem illam de Mes- sia, ejus templo spirituali, & vocatione gentium a- gere, neutiquam conditionalis ea statui potest: I- deoque verba hæc bifariam explicantur, (1) ut conditio respiciat participationem Judæorum, & apo- siopesis statuatur h. m. Et erit, sive fiet, ut de gratia hac participetis, si auscultetis Dei mandatis. Ita B. Bal- duinus pag. 417. Intelligit non tam obedientiam ope- rum, quam fidei, hoc sensu: Si credideritis Evange- lio, de Christo, quod vobis jam sub involucris figura- rum prædicatur, quodque ipse vobis paucis abhinc an- nis manifestabit, utique experiemini omnes has pro- missiones meas suum habituras eventum, sin vero credere nolueritis, sane quicquid vobis de Messia, ejus regno & sacerdotio dixi, opertum erit, & i- gnorantiæ vestræ tenebris involutum manebit: Hæc ergo tacita fuit prædictio excæcationis Ju- dæorum in Regno Christi. Etsi enim promissiones & dona Dei sunt ἀμεταμέλητα Rom. XI. v. 29. ne- que incredulitas nostra fidem Dei evacuare potest Rom. III. 3. tamen fides est salutare illud medium, quo fructus promissionum divinarum apprehen- ditur. Quia igitur Judæi verbis Dei omnipotentis fidem habere noluerunt, ideo in hodiernum usque diem velamen Veteris Testamenti manet eis non- dum revelatum, ut Apostolus loquitur II. Corinth. III, v. 14. & Evangelium de Christo prædicatum sit eis odor mortis ad mortem II. Cor. II. 16. quia Deus hujus seculi excæcavit mentes eorum, ut non ful- geat eis illuminatio Evangelii II. Cor. IV. v. 4. Ita Balduinus. (2) ut per voculam אִם non conditio po- natur, sed tempus designetur, ut cum Junio Tarno- vius & Willius explicant, quasi dicant, post illud tempus, quo ædificaveritis templum Dei & Pro- phetias singulares supra enunciatas, feceritis: post illud, inquam, tempus regnum hoc Christi ad Ec- clesiam venturum est. Prior explicatio magis nobis probatur, quam etiam amplexus est Coccejus: Erit illis in memoriale, ut ipsorum posteri pace hac per sa- cerdotem parta fruantur, & per eum in templo Do- mini, ut vivi lapides conserventur: Si modo auscul- tent voci Domini, h. e. Filio Dei verba loquenti.

PARS SECUNDA PROPHETÆ ZACHARIÆ.

CONCIO TERTIA.

Epanorthotico-Pædeutica improbans {cultus electitios, & informans de vera pietate.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII.

The time of the sermon is expressed as the fourth year of Darius, the ninth month, the fourth day, and the occasion, an embassy to the Priests and Prophets: who are rebuked concerning the fasts of the fifth and

seventh month, because they were not at all pleasing to the Lord, having been instituted and celebrated without the Lord, and they are stirred up to perform justice and mercy to their neighbor sincerely and in the fear of the Lord: with the example proposed of the punishment of disobedience against God foretold by the Prophets, the scattering of the people, and the devastation of the land. Fasting helps nothing, if you do not abandon impious deeds.

Verse 1.

IN THE FOURTH YEAR OF KING DARIUS) In the year following the one after the construction of the Temple was begun by Zerubbabel.

IN THE FOURTH OF THE NINTH MONTH, WHICH IS CASLEU) After the Temple was restored, the Hebrew names of the months also began to be used again.

Latin:

CAPUT VII.

Tempus concionis exprimitur anni IV. Da- rii mensis noni dies quarta, & occasio, le- gatio ad Sacerdotes & Prophetas: qui redarguuntur de jejuniis quinti & septi-

mi mensis, quod Domino minime placue- rint sine Domino & instituta & celebra- ta, & excitantur ad Justitiam & miseri- cordiam proximo sincere & in timore Do- mini præstandam: exemplo proposito pœ- næ inobedientiæ adversus Deum à Prophe- tis prænunciatæ, dissipationis populi, & devastationis terræ. Jejunare nihil juvat, impia facta relinquas.

Vers. 1.

IN ANNO QUARTO DARII REGIS) Anno eun- te altero post cœptam à Zorobabele Templi structuram.

IN QVARTA MENSIS NONI, QVI EST CASLEU) Post restitutum Templum, etiam nomina mensium Hebraica repeti cœperunt.

## 7:2
Verse 2.

AND THEY SENT) Those Jews who lived outside Jerusalem in the villages and country houses. See above II. 4.

TO THE HOUSE OF GOD) That is, to the Priests, who ought to be consulted in controversial matters, according to the law in Deut. XVII. 9. But the Priests themselves, if there were a question of law not yet defined, either referred it to the Sanhedrin, or consulted the Prophets, if any were present at that time.

SARASAR AND ROGOMMELECH) Sarasar and Rogommelech, men of primary importance among them.

AND THE MEN WHO WERE WITH HIM) The men who were with him, some lesser ones, their companions.

TO ENTREAT THE FACE OF THE LORD) To offer prayers in the Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET MISERUNT) Judæi illi, qui extra Hierosoly- ma in vicis, villisque habitabant. Vide supra II. 4.

AD DOMUM DEI) Id est, ad Sacerdotes, qui in rebus controversis consuli debebant, ex lege Deut. XVII. 9. Ipsi autem Sacerdotes, si quæstio esset juris non dum de- finiti, aut ad Synedrium referebant, aut Prophetas, si qui eo essent tempore consulebant.

SARASAR ET ROGOMMELECH) Sarasarum & Rogommelechum viros de se primarios.

ET VIRI QUI ERANT CUM EO) Viros qui erant cum eo, minores aliquos, illorum comites.

AD DEPRECANDUM FACIEM DOMINI) Ad preces faciendas in Templo.

## 7:3
Verse 3.

TO SAY TO THE PRIESTS) And at the same time to be said to the priests, the conjunction is missing.

The embassy to the house of the Lord and the priests was made not from the neighboring villages (concerning which the passage above c. II. 4. was wrongly explained) but from the whole people, among whom the leaders appear to have been, or the principal ones of the company, Sar Ezer and Regemelech, or as others think, from the exiles. By the house of God, the Priests are wrongly understood. They were SENT to the Temple, partly to offer prayers there, and partly to consult the Priests and Prophets concerning the fasts which they had hitherto celebrated in exile. Therefore, it is not the city of Bethel, which had been made Bethaven on account of the idolatry instituted there by Jeroboam (II Kings XII. 29) and had already been destroyed according to the prophecy of Amos III. 14, but the house of God is indicated here, which the Prophet calls Beth-Jehovah Zebaoth in verse 3.

Verse of the same.

SHOULD I WEEP IN THE FIFTH MONTH, OR SHOULD I SANCTIFY MYSELF, AS I HAVE DONE FOR MANY YEARS? Should I mourn in the fifth month, or should I separate myself (from all delightful things) in the fifth month, as I have already done for many years? God had not only instituted anniversary days of fasting, but the people had added some, in memory of sad events; I would wonder that it is disputed in this age whether this is permitted to the people, were it not that the desire for contradiction makes everything uncertain out of certain things. On the days of fasting, however, all signs of mourning were shown: with bowed head, bare feet, most vile clothing, sprinkled with ashes, and whatever other things are of that kind. Isaiah 58:5. Indeed, there was abstinence from more delicate foods, from wine, and from the use of spouses. Now the exiled Jews had instituted four such days: in the fourth month, in memory of the wall being broken through, Jeremiah 52:6; in the fifth month, in memory of the Temple being burned, Jeremiah 52:12; in the seventh month, in memory of Gedaliah being killed, Jeremiah 41:2; in the tenth month, in memory of the siege having begun, 2 Kings 25:1. They had observed these days not only in exile but also in Judea, between the times of Cyrus and Darius the son of Hystaspes. Now, with the Temple restored, those Jews living in the fields institute a question, not an absurd one: especially concerning that day which had been mournful on account of the Temple being burned. A knot worthy of a deliverer: for this question could probably be treated on either side. Let the cause cease, and the effect should also cease. On the contrary, it could be said that the memory of evils endured is useful. The prophet defines the matter with a wonderful temperament: the days are to be retained, but for giving thanks to God, and therefore with joy, not with mourning, below 7:19. But before he puts forth this opinion, he prefaces most useful things] concerning the right use of fasting, concerning the causes of evils, and how they ought to conduct themselves in prosperous circumstances.

We pass over the discussion concerning fasting, whether it is permitted for the people to institute a fast in memory of sad events? For it does not appear whom Grotius touches; that the fasts of the Papists, falsely so called, which consist in the choice of foods, and καποκαπηλίαν, because the Pope claims for himself the power of sanctioning such institutions, which is appropriate for the secular Magistrate, are disapproved by our people, is well known: otherwise, if fasts are duly instituted, they are by no means disapproved. But what Grotius says, that the question proposed here, whether the temple having now been restored, the Jews ought still to mourn? was defined by the Prophet with wonderful moderation, in this way, that the days were to be retained, but truly for giving thanks to God, and therefore with joy, not with mourning c. VIII. 19. in this he is entirely mistaken. For in the following chapter v. 19. this question is not decided, but festive and joyful days are promised to the people to be celebrated in the time of the New Testament. They were inquiring especially about the fifth month, because that fast had been celebrated until now in memory of the temple being cut down, along with the house of the King, by Nebuzaradan, the commander of the Chaldean army, II Kings XXV. 9. The decision of the Prophet, however, tends to this, that God is not pleased with such external fasts, much less with elective acts of worship; but with justice, kindness, beneficence, and charity ἀνυποκρίτῳ, and that the people had been incited to this especially by the earlier Prophets, but since they turned their back to them, and stopped their ears, it was dissipated by the just judgment of God, and the land itself was laid waste. Therefore the Prophet exhorts to the pursuit of truth and sincere charity, with a promise made of grace, and divine blessing, and a happier change of the days of fasting into festive days, toward the imminent time of the New Testament, when for the sake of increasing public joy many other peoples were to be gathered to the people of the Lord, from various nations and languages c. IIX. 20. seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

UT DICERENT SACERDOTIBUS) Et simul di- cendum sacerdotibus, Deest copula.

Legatio ad domum Domini, & sacerdotes fa- cta non ex vicis vicinis (de quibus perperam locus supra c. II. 4. explicatus) sed à populo univer- so, in quo capita videntur fuisse, aut præcipui com- matis Sar Ezer, & Regemelech, vel ut alii putant, ab exulibus. Ad domum Dei, perperam Sacerdotes intelliguntur. MISSI sunt ad Templum, partim ad preces ibi faciendas, partim ut consulerent Sacer- dotes & Prophetas de jejuniis, quæ hactenus in exilio celebraverant. Non ergo civitas Bethel, quæ Bethaven facta erat ob idololatriam à Jeroboamo ibi institutam II. Reg. XII. 29. & juxta vaticinium Am. III. 14. jam eversa suit, sed domus Dei hic in- digitatur, quam vers. 3. Beth-Jehovah Zebaoth Propheta vocat.

Vers. eod.

NVMQVID FLENDUM EST MIHI IN QUIN- TO MENSE, VEL SANCTIFICARE ME DEBEO, SICUT JAM FECI MULTIS ANNIS) Numquid lu- gendum est mihi in quinto mense, vel separare me debeo (ab omnibus rebus delectantibus) mense quinto, ut jam feci mul- tis annis. Dies jejunii anniversarios non Deus tantum insti- tuerat, sed addiderat aliquos populus, in rerum tristium memoriam, quod an populo liceat, disputari hoc seculo mirarer, nisi contradicendi libido omnia de certis incerta faceret.
