In jejunii autem diebus omnia luctus signa osten- debantur, demisso capite, nudis pedibus, vestitu vilissi- mo, asperso & cinere, & quæ alia sunt ejus generis. Esaiæ LVIII. 5. abstinebatur vero à cibis delicatioribus, à vino, ab usu conjugum. Tales autem dies quatuor instituerant Judæi exsules, mense quarto, in memoriam perrupti mu- ri Jerem. LII, 6. mense quinto, in memoriam combusti Templi Jerem. LII, 12. mense septimo, in memoriam interfecti Godoliæ Jerem. XLI, 2. mense decimo, in me- moriam cœptæ obsidionis II. Reg. XXV. 1. Hos dies observaverant non tantum in exsilio sed etiam in Judæa, inter Cyri tempora & Darii Hystaspis filii. Nunc restituto Templo quæstionem instituunt Judæi illi in agris habi- tantes, non absurdam: de illo præcipue die, qui luctuo- sus fuerat, ob Templum incensum. Dignus vindice no- dus: poterat enim hæc quæstio probabiliter in utramque partem tractari, Cessat causa cesset & effectus. Contra di- ci poterat, malorum toleratorum utilem esse memoriam. Propheta miro temperamento rem definit: retinendos dies, verum ad gratias Deo agendas, eoque cum gaudio, non cum luctu, infra VII. 19. sed antequam eam sen- tentiam promat, utilissima] præfatur de recto jejunii usu de causis malorum, & quomodo in rebus prosperis gerere se debeant.

Mittimus disputationem de jejunio, anne liceat populo in rerum tristium memoriam instituere jejunium? Non enim apparet, quos tangat Grotius Pontificiorum jejunia falso nuncupata, quæ in delectu ciborum consistant, & καποκαπηλίαν, quod Pontifex sibi vindicet potestatem sanciendi talia instituta, quæ Magistratui seculari convenit, improbari à nostris, notum est: jejunia alioquin si rite instituantur, minime improbantur. Quod autem ait Grotius, quæstionem hic propositam, an restituto jam templo adhuc lugendum Judæis sit? miro temperamento à Propheta definitam esse, hoc pacto, retinendos dies, verum ad gratias Deo agendas, eoque cum gaudio, non cum luctu c. VIII. 19. in eo omnino fallitur. Nam sequenti capite v. 19. non deciditur hæc quæstio, sed promittuntur populo festivi ac læti dies tempore Nov. T. celebrandi. De mense quinto imprimis quærebant, quia illud jejunium celebratum hactenus fuit in memoriam templi excisi, cum domo Regis, à Nebuzardan præfecto exercitus Chaldaici II. Reg. XXV. 9. Decisio autem Prophetæ eo tendit, non delectari Deum ejusmodi externis jejuniis nedum electitiis cultibus; sed justitia, benignitate, beneficentia, ac charitate ἀνυποκρίτῳ, atque ad eam populum excitatum imprimis fuisse per superiores Prophetas, sed quum tergum illis obverterit, auresque obturarit, justo Dei judicio dissipatum, terramque ipsam vastatam esse. Quapropter hortatur Propheta ad studium veritatis & sinceræ charitatis, promissione facta gratiæ, ac benedictionis divinæ, lætiorisque commutationis dierum jejunii in festivos dies, ad imminens tempus Novi Testamenti, quo ampliandi gaudii publici causa multi populi alii aggregandi erant ad populum Domini, ex variis nationibus & linguis c. IIX. 20. seqq.

## 7:5
Ver. 5.

SPEAK TO ALL THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND) Both to those sent here from the fields, and to the city dwellers. DURING THESE SEVENTY YEARS) During those seventy years, namely, while the exile lasted. DID YOU FAST A FAST TO ME) Did any good come back to me from that fast? He says this against the foolish persuasion that fasts please God by themselves, and without other things.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

LOQVERE AD OMNEM POPVLVM TERRÆ) Tum ad hos missos ex agris, tum ad urbanos. PER HOS SEPTUAGINTA ANNOS) Per illos septuaginta annos, nempe durante exilio. NUMQVID JEJVNIVM JEJVASTIS MIHI) An ex illo jejunio aliquid ad me boni rediit? hoc dicit contra stultam persuasionem, jejunia Deo per se, ac sine aliis rebus placere.

## 7:6
Ver. 6.

AND WHEN YOU ATE AND DRANK) As much as you pleased, and what you pleased, as outside the days of fasting. DID YOU NOT EAT FOR YOURSELVES, AND DRINK FOR YOURSELVES) Just as nothing comes to me from your feasts, so neither from the fast. Those, if they are viewed by themselves and nakedly, are equal to me.

Others think that fasts were simply disapproved here, because they were instituted without the command of God, and they did not seek the honor of God by them, but the ostentation of their own holiness. But the words of the Prophet seem to refute primarily that persuasion of the Jews, as if fasts by themselves please God, or constitute a part of divine worship, or even merit something before God, which opinion of necessity, worship, and merit also clings to the fasts of the Papists. Therefore Cornelius rightly renders the sense: Did I not speak these same words to you long ago through the Prophets, namely that fasts not founded on good works but on evil ones, displease me? In which way also Theodoret and Lyra explain it. Whose proclamation, however, Jerome, Hugo, and others rightly refer also to the following things concerning spiritual fasting, judge true judgment, and show mercy and compassions etc.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET CVM COMEDISTIS AC BIBISTIS) Quan tum libebat, & quæ libebat, ut extra jejunii dies. NUMQVID NON VOBIS COMEDISTIS, ET VOBISMET IPSIS BIBISTIS) Sicut ex epulis vestris nihil ad me accedit, ita nec ex jejunio. Illa, si per se ac nude spectentur, mihi ex æquo sunt.

Alii putant, simpliciter jejunia hic improbata fuisse, quod sine jussu Dei instituta, nec honorem Dei iis quæfiverint, sed ostentationem propriæ sanctimoniæ. Sed verba Prophetæ videntur persuasionem illam Judæorum imprimis redarguere, quasi jejunia per se Deo placeant, aut partem cultus divini constituant, vel etiam aliquid penes Deum mereantur, quæ necessitatis, cultus, & meriti opinio etiam Papistarum jejuniis hæret. Recte ergo sensum reddit Cornelius: Numquid non hæc eadem verba, nimirum quod jejunia non condita operibus bonis sed malis, mihi displiceant, olim vobis per Prophetas loquutus sum? quo pacto etiam Theodoretes & Lyranus exponunt. Quorum tamen præconium etiam ad sequentia de jejunio spirituali, judicium verum judicate, & misericordiam, & miserationes facite &c. merito referunt Hieronymus, Hugo, & alii.

## 7:7
Ver. 7.

ARE THESE NOT THE WORDS WHICH THE LORD SPOKE BY THE HAND OF THE FORMER PROPHETS) Did not Jeremiah say the same things to you long ago?

The Lord refers them not only to Jeremiah, but especially also to the Prophet Isaiah, through whom in chapter 48, verses 5 and following, such superstitious and hypocritical fasts are taxed at length in similar words, and the true nature of fasts is shown, and especially the spiritual fast is taught, concerning which in Augustine, Tractate 17 on John, the great and general fast is to abstain from iniquities and illicit pleasures of the world, etc.

AND TO THE SOUTH) Which region is more mountainous, as Jerome notes here.

AND MIGHT BE INHABITED IN THE PLAINS) That is, since no part of the land was uncultivated.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

NVMQVID NON SUNT VERBA, QVÆ LOCVTVS EST DOMINUS IN MANU PROPHE- TARUM PRIORVM) Nonne eadem pridem vobis dixit Jeremias?

Non ad Jeremiam solum, sed imprimis etiam ad Prophetam Esaiam remittit ipsos Dominus, per quem c. XLIIX. 5. seqq. prolixe superstitiosa & hy- pocritica ejusmodi jejunia similibus verbis taxan- tur, ac vera jejuniorum ratio ostenditur, atque im- primis spirituale jejunium docetur, quo de Au- gust. tr. XVII. in Joh. jejunium magnum & gene- rale est abstinere ab iniquitatibus, & illicitis volu- ptatibus seculi &c.

ET AD AUSTRUM) Quæ regio montosior, ut hic notat Hieronymus.

ET IN CAMPESTRIBUS HABITARETUR) Id est, cum nulla pars terræ esset inculta.

## 7:9
Verse 9.

JUDGE TRUE JUDGMENT) Without corruption, or favor, or hatred.

AND SHOW MERCY AND COMPASSIONS EVERY MAN TO HIS BROTHER) To his fellow countryman. But in the Gospel every man is a brother.

Grotius is mistaken when he makes a distinction in the showing of mercy and kindness between the times of the Old and New Testaments, as if under the former it was to be shown only to fellow countrymen, but under the latter to all men. Which error we have elsewhere refuted in the Socinians. Scripture knows no such difference of times in that regard. The law concerning the love of one's neighbor, just as it is inscribed by nature upon all, so it holds equally at all times. Nor did Christ interpret the sense of the old law otherwise in Matthew 5 and 22, and Luke 10, than that according to the intention of the divine law, every man is a neighbor. And when the Jews are commanded in this place to exercise justice and beneficence, they certainly ought not to have exercised the same only toward their own people. For indeed, were they able, while keeping the divine law and this prophetic admonition, to treat others unjustly, or to deny beneficence and mercy to others?

Latin:

Vers. 9.

JUDICIUM VERUM JUDICATE) Sine sordi- bus, aut gratia, aut odio.

ET MISERICORDIAM, ET MISERATIONES FACITE UNUSQUISQUE CUM FRATRE SUO) Populari. At in Evangelio omnis homo frater.

Fallitur Grotius, cum discrimen facit exhiben- dæ misericordiæ & benignitatis inter tempora Ve- teris & Novi Testamenti, quasi sub illis populari- bus solum ea exhibenda fuerit; sub his vero omni- bus hominibus. Quem errorem in Socinianis alias profligavimus. Scriptura nullam novit ea in parte temporum differentiam. Lex de dilectione pro- ximi uti natura insculpta omnibus, ita omni tem- pore æqualiter se habet. Neque aliter sensum le- gis veteris interpretatus est Christus Matth. V. c. XXII. Luc. X. quam quod juxta divinæ legis inten- tionem proximus sit omnis homo. Et cum justi- tiam & beneficentiam exercere jubentur hoc loco Judæi, non certe solum erga suum populum ean- dem exercere debuere. Quod enim, num licebat injuste tractare alios, num beneficentiam & mise- ricordiam aliis denegare, salva lege divina, & mo- nitione hac prophetica, poterant?

## 7:10
Verse 10.

AND THE WIDOW, AND THE FATHERLESS, AND THE STRANGER, AND THE POOR, DO NOT OPPRESS) Do not oppress. For that is what עשׁק means. See what was said at Luke 3:14.

AND LET NOT A MAN IMAGINE EVIL AGAINST HIS BROTHER IN HIS HEART) Let him not even allow a plan to harm anyone to come into his mind. But the Septuagint take it more strictly concerning the prohibition of private desire for vengeance: And let not each one harbor a grudge against his brother in your hearts. Which agrees with that which we have in Leviticus 19:18, and in this sense Tertullian cites this passage in Against Marcion, Book 4: Let not each one recall the malice of his neighbor. But the former sense is simpler, which the Chaldean also follows here.

ET MALUM VIR FRATRI SUO NON COGI- TET IN CORDE SUO) Ne in animum quidem sibi venire patiatur consilium cuiquam nocendi. XIX. 18. & hoc sensu hunc locum adducit Tertul- lianus adversus Marcionem IV. Malitiam proximi sui unus- quisque ne recogitet. Sed prior sensus simplicior est, quem & Chaldæus hic sequitur.

## 7:14
Ver. 14.

THROUGH ALL THE KINGDOMS WHICH THEY KNEW NOT) Even into Assyria.

This discourse is not about the Israelites dispersed into Assyria, but about the two tribes, which were partly carried over into Chaldea, and partly also, when they fled from the Chaldean enemies through Syria, Egypt, Mesopotamia, Persia, Media, and other kingdoms, were dispersed. The word אסערם is like a storm, I snatched away, as a whirlwind I dispersed them. AND THE LAND IS DESOLATE FROM THEM BECAUSE THERE WAS NO ONE PASSING THROUGH AND RETURNING) So that there was no one passing through or returning. AND THEY HAVE SET THE DESIRABLE LAND) Whence that land is called צבי. II Sam. I. 17. Dan. XI. 15. It is called desirable, not only for its elegance and fertility, and the yield of its fruits, because it flowed with milk and honey, but also because of the Messiah, who was to be born in it, and was to execute the redemption of the human race, who was the desire of all nations Hagg. II. 8. INTO A DESERT) Truly said. See II Paralip. XXXVI. 21. Arias Montanus wrongly renders the word לשמה, which the Vulgate translates as into a desert, others as into astonishment, in which what? of which travelers astonished might say, what of good remains in that land? But they are said to have set that desirable land into a desert, because they caused by their sins that it should be so laid waste by God.

THE THIRD PART is completed in four sermons on notable prophecies, in seven chapters. THE FOURTH SERMON, Paracletic-Paraenetic, AND THE FIFTH, purely consolatory, concerning matters pertaining especially to the Old Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

PER OMNIA REGNA QUÆ NESCIVNT) In Assyriam usque.

Non hic sermo est de Israelitis in Assyriam di- spergis, sed de duabus tribubus, quæ partim in Chaldæam traductæ, partim etiam cum hostes Chaldæos fugerent per Syriam, Ægyptum, Meso- potamiam, Persiam, Mediam, aliaque regna disper- sæ fuere. Vox אסערם est instar procellæ abripui ut turbo dispersi eos. ET TERRA DESOLATA EST AB EIS EO QVOD NON ESSET TRANSIENS ET REVERTENS) Ita ut nemo esset transiens aut rediens. ET POSUERUNT TERRAM DESIDERABILEM) Unde ea terra dicta צבי. II. Sam. I. 17. Dan. XI. 15. Desiderabilis dicta est, non modo ob elegantiam & fertilitatem, ac proventum frugum, quia lacte & melle fluebat, sed etiam ob Messiam, qui in ea nasciturus, & generis humani redemtionem exequuturus erat, qui erat desiderium omnium gentium Hagg. II. 8. IN DESERTUM) Vere dictum. Vide II. Paralip. XXXVI. 21. Perperam Arias Montanus vocem לשמה, quam Vulgatus vertit, in desertum, alii in stuporem reddunt, in qua quid? de qua viatores stupentes dicerent, quid in illa terra superat boni? Posuisse autem terram illam desiderabilem dicuntur in desertum, quod peccatis suis effecerint, ut à Deo ita vastaretur.

PARS TERTIA QUATUOR CONCIONIBUS Insignibus vaticiniis, septem capitibus absolvitur. CONCIO QUARTA Paracletico - Parænetica ET QUINTA Mere consolatoria de rebus potissimum ad V. T. pertinentibus.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

Just as the Lord was very jealous against Zion because of sins, so now He promises that He will return to Zion, and will dwell there, so that it may be a holy mountain, and the desolate city may be filled with a great multitude, however difficult this may seem in the eyes of His people: and so He promises that He will bring back the dispersed and will be their God. He exhorts, however, to the restoration of the temple, which is now to succeed happily, to be crowned with halcyon days and blessing, and to the pursuit of truth, justice, and concord without hypocrisy. Furthermore, the Lord promises that the days of fasting will be changed into feasts of joy, and that the nations will be gathered to the people of the Lord to seek and worship God. The city of Jerusalem again abounds with men and people.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Sicut Dominus adversus Zionem propter peccata valde zelatus fuit, ita jam se reversurum ad Zion, ibique habitaturum, ut mons sanctus sit, & urbs desolata multitudine magna repleatur, utcunque hoc difficile in oculis suorum videatur: adeoque se dispersos reducturum eorumque Deum futurum promittit. Hortatur autem ad restaurationem templi jam feliciter successuram, halcyoniis & benedictione coronandam, & ad studium veritatis, justitiæ, & concordiæ sine hypocrisi. Pollicetur præterea Dominus, jejuniorum dies in festa lætitiæ commutatum, & gentes populo Domini ad Deum quærendum & colendum, aggregatum iri. Urbs Solymæa viris iterum, populoque redundat.

## 8:3

IN DIEBVS ILLIS) In his diebus. NUMQVID IN OCVLIS MEIS DIFFICILE ERIT) Cui scilicet nihil difficile: nam ut Linus cecinit: Ρᾴδια πάντα θεῷ τελέσαι καὶ ἀνήνυτον οὐδὲν.

Ver. 7. BEHOLD I WILL SAVE MY PEOPLE FROM THE LAND OF THE EAST, AND FROM THE LAND OF THE SETTING OF THE SUN) That is, I will lead them out.

## 8:8
Ver. 8. AND THEY SHALL BE TO ME FOR A PEOPLE, AND I WILL BE TO THEM FOR A GOD IN TRUTH AND IN JUSTICE) They to me, I to them, we will perform the promises.

Under those two regions of the East and West, the other two are included. Which is also observed in Matthew VIII. 11. They shall come from the east and west. If you compare the passage in Luke XIII. 29. From the East and West, and North, and South. For there is no doubt, as Cornel. à Lapide observes here, that although the Jews were taken directly into Chaldea, which is to the north of Judea, yet many migrated from there to other eastern and western kingdoms. Again, it is clear from Isaiah ch. XVI. 4 that others, when the Chaldeans were arriving in Judea, fled to the Ammonites, Moabites, Idumeans, Syrians, etc. These, therefore, having heard of the return of their people from Babylon to Jerusalem, and the rebuilding of it and the temple, as well as the prosperity and happiness of the inhabitants, returned there quickly. Thus St. Jerome, Theodoret, Rupert, and others. For most understand it concerning the bodily restoration of the Jews, and the times near at hand: although some mystically refer it at the same time to the times of the New Testament and the conversion of the Israelites according to the Spirit (which double sense cannot stand at the same time, since the meaning of each prophecy is certain), but Cocceius explains it concerning the spiritual bringing back in the time of the New Testament, with this argument especially, that the earthly Jerusalem is not capable of that habitation. But if it was capable before the division of the Israelite Kingdom, so that on feast days assemblies could be celebrated there from the whole kingdom, why could it not have contained after the return from the Babylonian captivity those returnees who had been dispersed to the various regions of the world, during solemn feasts and assemblies?

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET ERVNT MIHI IN POPVLVM, ET EGO ERO EIS IN DEVM IN VERITATE ET IN JVSTITIA) Illi mihi, ego illis, promissa præstabimus.

Sub illis duabus plagis Orientis, & Occasus reliquæ duæ comprehenduntur. Quod etiam observatur Matth. IIX. 11. Ab oriente, & occidente venient. Si conferas locum Luc. XIII. 29. Ab Oriente & Occidente, & Aquilone, & Austro. Non enim dubium est, ut hic Cornel. à Lapide observat, quin licet Judæi directe in Chaldæam, quæ Judææ est ad Aquilonem, sint abducti, inde tamen multi ad alia regna orientalia & occidentalia migrarint. Rursum alios, adventantibus in Judæam Chaldæis, profugisse ad Ammonitas, Moabitas, Idumæos, Syros &c. patet ex Isaia c. XVI. 4. Hi ergo audito reditu suorum è Babylone in Jerusalem, ejusque & templi reædificatione, æque ac incolarum prosperitate & felicitate, eo propere redierunt. Ita S. Hieron. Theod. Rupert. & alii. Plerique enim de corporali reductione Judæorum, & temporibus proximis intelligunt: etsi nonnulli mystice simul referant ad tempora N. T. & conversionem Israëlitarum secundum Spiritum (qui geminus sensus simul constare non potest, quum certa sit cujusque vaticinii sententia) at Coccejus explicat de spirituali adductione tempore N. Test. hoc imprimis argumento, quod Hierosolyma terrestris non sit capax illius inhabitationis. Verum si capax fuit ante divisionem Regni Israëlitici, ut diebus festivis ex toto regno conventus ibi celebrari potuerit, quidni post reditum è captivitate Babylonica reduces illos, qui ad varias plagas mundi dispersi fuere capere potuisset, in solemnibus festis & conventibus?

Talia enim opera Diaboli sunt, non Dei, nec

Ver. 16.

SPEAK THE TRUTH) Abstain from evil deceit.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

LOQVIMINI VERITATEM) Abstinete à dolo malo.

VERITATEM ET JUDICIUM PACIS JUDI- CATE IN PORTIS VESTRIS) Vos judices quærite ve- ritatem ex testibus, ac judicate secundum legem, quæ est causa pacis in populo.

## 8:17
Ver. 17.

AND LET NONE OF YOU THINK EVIL IN YOUR HEARTS AGAINST HIS NEIGHBOR) Against a fellow countryman, for here in the Hebrew רעה is the same as אח.

We have observed what error Grotius hides here at chapter VII, v. 9. They are not only forbidden to think evil in their hearts against a fellow countryman, but against every neighbor. Nor were the Jews commanded to speak the truth only to their fellow countrymen, i.e., as Grotius interprets, to abstain from evil deceit only when the matter was with fellow countrymen. For thus it would have been entirely permissible for them to deceive others, provided they were not of the number of their fellow countrymen. It is therefore manifest that by the word רעה any neighbor whatsoever is indicated.

Ver. 19.

AND ON THE SPLENDID SOLEMNITIES) In the Hebrew: good. Now the Hebrews are accustomed to call those days good, which are dedicated to joy.

Not just any days of joy are designated, but the Prophet refers primarily to the solemnities and joyful times of the N.T., in which we are commanded to rejoice in the Lord Phil. IV. 4. What kind of joy the daughter of Zion has in the following chapter he intimates in verse 9.

LOVE TRUTH AND PEACE ONLY) A preparation for the Gospel.

The Socinian error of Grotius recurs that other new precepts were delivered in the N.T. But the pursuit of truth and peace was commanded at all times, and was to be cultivated by all, nor was it inculcated upon the Israelites only by the latest Prophets, but it pertains to all who were bound to devote effort to piety, and it was sacred to all who truly feared God from the beginning of the world: It is absurd to feign a zeal for true piety without a zeal for truth and peace. And it is no less absurd to feign that there are saints under the New Testament without a zeal for unfeigned piety or truth, and without a zeal for peace.

Verse 20.

UNTIL THE PEOPLES COME) It shall yet come to pass that peoples shall come: namely, Jews from the furthest shores, as above VIII, 7.

Verse 21.

LET US ENTREAT THE FACE OF THE LORD) Let us pour out prayers to God in the temple, where the Ark is. AND LET US SEEK THE LORD OF HOSTS) Let us learn those things which are of the law from the Prophets and Priests.

Verse 22.

AND MANY PEOPLES AND STRONG NATIONS SHALL COME) That is, foreigners. See what was said above II. 11.

THEY SHALL TAKE HOLD OF THE HEM OF A JEWISH MAN) That hem commanded in the law, Num. XV. 30, Deut. XXII. 12. By this mark, Jews were distinguished from other nations, as we said at Matt. IX. 20.

FOR WE HAVE HEARD THAT GOD IS WITH YOU) We have understood by what wondrous ways, and indeed as foretold, He has restored you to your homeland, returned the Temple to you, and either made your enemies your friends or repressed them: whence we believe that God, who both foretold and did these things, is the true God. The same sense, pertaining to these same times, is in Psalm CXXVI. 2.

Although these promises began to be fulfilled after the return from Babylon, when not a few from the nations flocked to Jerusalem for the sake of worship—which was the fruit of the dispersion of the Jews among the nations, because the fame of the true God was spread everywhere through them—nevertheless, they attained their full complement finally in the time of the New Testament, when the nations were generally converted to the Church. For the discourse is about the inhabitants of MANY cities (for thus the words must be rendered, 'and the peoples and the inhabitants of many cities shall come,' so that it may be designated who are to come, not where they are to come, as the Vulgate rendered it) and about many peoples: AND MANY PEOPLES SHALL COME, and about strong nations: furthermore, about men from ALL the languages of the nations who shall take hold of the hem of a true Jew; and therefore the Prophet prophesies about the illustrious calling of the nations. Compare Isaiah LX. 3, 4. Those mutual exhortations also: 'Let us go and entreat the face of the Lord, and let us seek the Lord of hosts,' are clearly similar to those incitements which are read in Isaiah II. verse 2 and Micah IV. verse 2, which speak openly about the time of the New Testament. And thus these things depend rightly upon the preceding: all fasts shall be for joy and gladness and for excellent solemnities, SO MUCH SO, that peoples shall even flock together. Wherefore, most interpreters explain these as referring to the times of the New Testament: Jerome, Theodoret, Rupert, Hugo, Lyra, Vatablus, Corn. à Lapide, as well as most of our own. Nor does Calvin dissent, whose explanation we subjoin: It must also be seen why he says that the nations will come to seek God at Jerusalem and call upon Him there. The foolish Jews imagine that God cannot be worshipped otherwise than if sacrifices are still offered in the temple, for the Prophet meant something far different, namely that the light of doctrine would arise from that city, which would spread itself far and wide, and this prophecy ought to be joined with that of Isaiah, The law shall go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. Since therefore the doctrine of salvation flowed forth from that city, which filled the whole world, for that reason the Prophet says that the nations would come to Jerusalem: not that it was necessary to run there, but because it was necessary for all to seek from there what could not be found elsewhere. Since therefore no one could be reckoned among the sons of God, unless he made progress in that school, and acknowledged that there was only one true religion, which had previously had its domicile at Jerusalem: we see why the Prophet here expresses the name of Jerusalem. Meanwhile it must also be held that the temple was built at that time with the end and purpose that the doctrine of salvation might remain there and have its seat until the coming of Christ; for then was fulfilled that of the hundred and tenth Psalm, God will send forth the sceptre of your power from Zion: there the Prophet teaches that Christ would not be the King of only one people, whose power might be enclosed within narrow borders, but that he would rule over the whole world, because God would extend his sceptre here and there. Since therefore it was necessary for this end to be looked to by the Jews, for that reason, in order to encourage them so that they might not fail in the middle of the course of the work, the Prophet says that that place is so sacred to God that salvation is to be sought from there by the whole world, because, namely, all will be disciples of that Church, whoever desire to be reckoned among the sons of God. The remaining Reformed also add their calculation, from whom Willius thus exhibits the connection. Those whose Church will be enlarged by the accession of the nations, and will be rendered more illustrious by the devotion of many peoples, they can be certain that they will have cause not for sadness, but for hilarity and joy: and that all proofs of former calamity are therefore to be little regarded.

SIXTH SERMON

Which pertains especially to the times of the New Testament and is mixed.

SECTION I.

CONSOLATORY.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ET UNVSQVISQVE MALVM CONTRA A- MICVM SVVM NE COGITETIS IN CORDIBVS VESTRIS) Contra popularem, nam hic in Hebræo רעה est idem quod אח.

Quem hic errorem occultet Grotius, observa- vimus ad cap. VII. v. 9. Non tantum contra popula- rem prohibentur malum cogitare in cordibus suis, sed contra proximum quemque. Neque veritatem tantum dicere jubebantur Judæi popularibus suis, h. e. ut interpretatur Grotius, abstinere à dolo malo solum, ubi res erat cum popularibus. Sic enim in- tegrum ipsis fuisset fallere alios, si modo non essent è popularium numero. Manifestum itaque voce רעה quemlibet proximum indigitari.

Vers. 19.

ET IN SOLEMNITATES PRÆCLARAS) In Hebræo: bonas. Solent autem Hebræi dies bonas appella- re eas, quæ lætitiæ dicantur.

Non dies lætitiæ qualescunque designantur, sed imprimis solemnitates & tempora læta N. T. respi- cit Propheta, quibus jubemur in Domino lætari Phil. IV. 4. Quale gaudium filiæ Sion sequenti ca- pite intimat vers. 9.

VERITATEM TANTVM ET PACEM DILI- GITE) Præparatio ad Evangelium.

Recurrit error Grotii Socinianus in N. T. alia nova præcepta tradita esse. Ast veritatis, & pacis stu- dium omni tempore præceptum fuit, & omnibus colendum fuit, nec Israëlitis solum à Prophetis no- vissimis inculcatum est, sed ad omnes pertinet, qui pietati operam navare debuere, & omnibus san- ctum fuit vere Deum timentibus inde à mundi primordio: Ineptum est fingere veræ pietatis stu- dium, sine studio veritatis & pacis. Nec minus in- eptum est, sanctos fingere sub N. T. sine infucatæ pietatis aut veritatis, & absque pacis studio.

Vers. 20.

USQVE QVO VENIANT POPULI) Adhuc erit ut veniant populi: nempe Judæi ex ultimis oris, ut supra VIII, 7.

Vers. 21.

DEPRECEMVR FACIEM DOMINI) Deo preces fundamus in templo, ubi Arca. ET QVÆRAMVS DOMINVM EXERCI- TVVM) Discamus ea, quæ sunt legis, ex Prophetis & Sacerdotibus.

Vers. 22.

ET VENIENT POPVLI MVLTI ET GEN- TES ROBVSTÆ) Id est, externi. Vide quæ dicta su- pra II. 11.

APPREHENDENT FIMBRIAM VIRI JVDÆI) Fimbriam illam præceptam in lege Num. XV. 30. Deut. XXII. 12. Hac nota Judæi à gentibus aliis dignosceban- tur, ut diximus ad Matth. IX. 20.

AUDIVIMVS ENIM QVONIAM DEVS VO- BISCUM EST) Intelleximus, quam miris modis, & qui- dem ex prædicto, vos in patriam restituerit, Templum vobis reddiderit, hostes vestros aut vobis amicos fecerit, aut represserit: unde credimus Deum, qui hæc & prædixit & fecit, verum esse Deum. Idem sensus est ad eadem hæc tempora pertinens Psal. CXXVI. 2.

Etsi hæ promissiones impleri cœperint post re- ditum è Babylone, cum non pauci è gentibus Hie- rosolymam cultus gratia confluxerint, qui fructus fuit dispersionis Judæorum inter gentes, quod fa- ma passim per illos dispersa fuerit de vero Deo: plenum tamen complementum sortitæ sunt demum Nov. Test. tempore, cum gentes ad Ecclesiam ge- neraliter conversæ sunt. Nam sermo est de habita- toribus civitatum MULTARUM (sic enim red- denda verba, & venient populi & habitatores civi- tatum multarum, ut designetur, quinam venturi sint, non quo sint venturi, ut vulgata reddidit) de populis multis: ET VENIENT POPULI MUL- TI, & de gentibus robustis: adhæc de hominibus ex OMNIBUS gentium linguis fimbriam veri Judæi apprehensuris, ideoque de illustri gentium vocatione vaticinatur Propheta. Conf. Es. LX. 3. 4. Illæ etiam cohortationes mutuæ: Eamus, & depre- cemur faciem Domini, & quæramus Dominum exer- cituum, similes plane sunt excitationibus istis, quæ Esa. II. vers. 2. Mich. IV. vers. 2. leguntur, quæ aper- te de tempore Nov. Test. loquuntur. Atque ita pendent recte hæc à superioribus: jejunia omnia erunt in gaudium & lætitiam & in solemnitates præ- claras, ADEO, ut populi etiam confluxuri sint. Quapropter de temporibus Nov. Test. hæc ex- plicant Interpp. plerique Hieronymus, Theodore- tus, Rupertus, Hugo, Lyranus, Vatablus, Corn. à Lapide, ut & nostrates plerique. Nec abnuit Cal- vinus: cujus explicationem subjicimus: Viden- dum etiam est, cur dicat gentes venturas, ut Deum quærant Jerosolymæ, & illic invocent. Stulti Judæi imaginantur, non posse aliter coli Deum quam si adhuc offerantur in templo sacrificia, nam longe aliud Propheta voluit, exorituram scilicet doctri- næ lucem ex illa urbe, quæ longe lateque sese dif- funderet, & hoc vaticinium conjungi debet cum illo Jesaiæ, Lex exibit è Sion, & verbum Domini è Jerusalem. Quoniam ergo ex urbe illa profluxit salutis doctrina, quæ replevit totum orbem, ideo Propheta dicit venturas gentes Jerosolymam: non quod necesse fuerit illuc accurrere, sed quoniam oportuit omnes petere illinc, quod non poterat alibi reperiri. Quando igitur nemo potuit cense- ri inter Dei filios, nisi qui in schola illa proficeret, & agnosceret unicam esse veram religionem, quæ Jerosolymæ prius domicilium habuerat: videmus, cur Propheta hic exprimat nomen Jerosolymæ. Interea simul etiam tenendum est, templum fuisse eo fine & consilio tunc extructum, ut illic mane- ret salutis doctrina & sedem suam haberet usque ad Christi adventum; tunc enim impletum fuit il- lud Psalmi centesimi decimi, Sceptrum potentiæ tuæ emittet Deus è Sion: illic docet Propheta, Chri- stum non fore tantum unius populi Regem, cu- jus potentia inclusa sit angustis finibus, sed domi- naturum in toto orbe, quia scilicet sceptrum ejus extendet Deus huc & illuc. Quoniam ergo opor- tuit finem hunc à Judæis spectari, ideo ut animet eos Propheta, ne deficiant in medio cursu operis, dicit, locum illum ita esse Deo sacrum, ut inde petenda sit salus è toto orbe, quoniam scilicet o- mnes erunt Ecclesiæ illius discipuli, quicunque censeri cupient inter Dei filios. Calculum etiam addunt reliqui Reformati, è quibus Willius ita συνέχειαν exhibet. Quorum Ecclesia gentium acces- sione dilatabitur, & populorum multorum devotione illustrior reddetur, ii certi esse possunt, se non tristitiæ, sed hilaritatis & lætitiæ causam habituros: ac omnia propterea prioris calamitatis documenta esse parum curanda.

CONCIO SEXTA

Quæ ad N. T. tempora potissimum spectat & mixta est.

SECTIO I.

CONSOLATORIA.

## 9:1 Argument
Ver. 1. I HAVE BEEN JEALOUS FOR ZION WITH GREAT JEALOUSY) For Zion's sake I have burned with anger against her oppressors. Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, and others interpret it as jealousy against Zion, not for Zion against her enemies. But the syntax seems to favor Grotius: I have burned with anger on account of Zion, or for Zion, and the following discourse explains the present one.

Latin:

Vers. 1. ZELATUS SUM ZION ZELO MAGNO) Pro Sione excandui adversus ejus oppressores. THEodoretus, Remigius, Haymo, & alii de Zelo adversus Sionem, non pro Sione adversus hostes interpretantur. Sed favere videtur Grotio Syntaxis, Excandui propter Sionem, vel pro Sione, & explicat sequens concio præsentem.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX.

A prediction concerning the overthrow of enemies and the coming, passion, and kingdom of the King of Zion.

Having premised for the comfort of the faithful a prophecy concerning the either overthrow or conversion of Syria, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre, Sidon, Ashkelon, Gaza, and other Philistines, and their gathering to the people of the Lord, and the protection of the house of the Lord, he invites Jerusalem to joy, on account of the coming of the King who is just, saving, afflicted, riding on a donkey, about to teach peace, and about to extend his dominion through the world, by whose blood those bound are sent forth from the infernal pit, and who, by the bow and the ministry of the Apostles, to be taken from the Jews and Israelites, will report victories against the nations, so that the faithful everywhere, as Holy stones, are to be erected, and many children are to be procreated by the power of the Word of the Lord.

With the enemies overthrown, Jesus will reign peacefully.

Verse 1.

THE BURDEN OF THE WORD OF THE LORD) A sad prophecy. IN THE LAND OF HADRACH) The opinion of those who take חדרך as a common noun, not as a proper noun, does not displease, so that the sense may be: upon the land which surrounds you (O Judea): that is, Syria.

AND OF DAMASCUS HIS RESTING PLACE) And Damascus is his resting place: that is, the land which has its confidence in Damascus, a strong and well-fortified city. All these things were fulfilled in the times of Alexander, who took possession of both Damascus and all of Syria. See Curtius, books III and IV.

Some here think that not a punishment, but a benefit is proposed, to be shown to the nations in the gathering to the Church. For the Prophet rises to this from the building of the temple. Thus Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Haymo, Clarius, Vatablus, Arias, Ribera, and Castrius, as also Cornelius à Lapide. So also Coccejus, who does not render ONUS of the word, but PROCLAMATION OF THE WORD; but there is no reason why one should depart from the customary meaning of the word, and the thing itself teaches that sad and burdensome things are predicted here for the Syrians, Phoenicians, and Palestinians. Which were fulfilled in the times of Alexander. For he, having defeated Darius Codomannus, came into Syria, and subjugated Damascus, Sidon, Tyre, and other neighboring places. Some take the land חדרך as a proper name: yet they think Syria is signified by it: or some leader or King in Syria; others interpret it from the Syriac language as the land surrounding you (O Judea), by which they understand Syria in that place. For such words occur frequently in the Prophets in neighboring places: but they think Damascus is called his resting place with the pronoun referring to the word משא, because the rest of the entire Prophecy is to be especially in it, such formulas as are observed in Ezek. V. ver. 13, chap. XVI. ver. 42, chap. XXII. 20. Which interpretation Ludovicus de Dieu judges is by no means to be despised. The more common explanation is that Syria rests and trusts in the fortified city of Damascus, which B. Luther also embraced.

Same verse.

BECAUSE THE EYE OF THE LORD IS ON MAN) The observer of men. It is an ellipsis. AND OF ALL THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL) That is, no less than of all the tribes of Israel: he is the judge of all nations, not of one people.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Prædictio de hostium eversione Regis- que Zionis adventu, passione, & regno.

Præmisso in solatium fidelium vaticinio, de Syriæ, Damasci, Hamath, Tyri, Sidonis, Asklon, Gazæ, & aliorum Philistinorum aut eversione, aut conversione, & ad po- pulum Domini aggregatione, domusque Domini protectione, invitat Hierosoly- mam ad gaudium, ob adventum Regis ju- sti, salvandi, afflicti, asinæ vehendi, pa- cem docturi, & dominium per orbem ex- tensuri, cujus sanguine vincti è lacu in- fernali emittuntur, quique arcu, & mi- nisterio Apostolorum, è Judæis & Israe- litis assumendorum, victorias adversus gentes reportabit, ut passim fideles, ceu lapides Sancti, erigendi, multique liberi virtute Verbi Domini procreandi sint.

Hostibus eversis placide regnabit Jesus.

Vers. 1.

ONVS VERBI DOMINI) Prophetia tristis." IN TERRA HADRACH) Non displicet eorum sen- tentia, qui חדרך sumunt pro nomine communi, non pro- prio, ut sensus sit: super terram quæ te (ô Judæa) circuit: id est Syriam.

ET DAMASCI REQVIEI EJVS) Et Damascus requies ejus: id est, quæ terra in Damasco, urbe valida ac bene munita fiduciam suam habet. Omnia hæc impleta temporibus Alexandri, qui & Damasco & Syria omni po- titus est. Vide Curtium libro III. & IV.

NOnnulli hic putant, non supplicium, sed bene- ficium proponi, gentibus in collectione ad Ecclesiam exhibendum. Ad hanc enim assurgere Prophetam à templi fabrica. Sic Hieronymus, Theo- doretus, Remigius, Haymo, Clarius, Vatablus, A- rias, Ribera, & Castrius, ut & Cornelius à Lapide. Ita etiam Coccejus, qui non reddit ONUS verbi, sed PROLATIO VERBI; sed causa nulla est, cur recedatur ab usitata vocis significatione, & res ipsa docet, Syriæ, Phœnicibus & Palæstinis hic tri- stia & onerosa prædici. Quæ Alexandri tempori- bus impleta. Hic enim devicto Dario Codoman- no in Syriam venit, Damascum, Sidonem, Ty- rum & alia loca vicina subjugavit. Terram חדרך nonnulli ut nomen proprium accipiunt: Syriam ta- men eo significatam putant: vel ducem aliquem aut Regem in Syria; alii ex Syriaca lingua inter- pretantur terram circumstantem te (O Judæa) per quam ibidem Syriam intelligunt. Talia enim in vicinis locis plura vocabula occurrunt in Prophe- tis: Damascum autem requiem ejus dici arbitran- tur pronomine relato ad vocem משא, quod in ea imprimis requies futura sit universæ Prophetiæ, quales formulas observant Ezech. V. vers. 13. cap. XVI. vers. 42. cap. XXII. 20. Quam interpretatio- nem nequaquam spernendam judicat Ludovic. de Dieu. Communior est illa explicatio, quod Syria in urbe Damasco munita requiescat & confidat, quod B. Lutherus etiam amplexus est.

Vers. eod.

QUIA DOMINI EST OCULUS HOMINIS) Spectator hominum. Est ἕλλειψις. ET OMNIUM TRIBUUM ISRAEL) Id est, non minus quam omnium tribuum Israël: judex est universa- rum gentium, non unius populi.

## 9:2
Verse 2.

HAMATH ALSO IN ITS BORDERS) that is, within its borders, namely of the sad prophecy. We spoke about Hamath, a city of Syria, at 2 Kings XVII. ver. 24. Jerome, on this passage, wishes it to be that which was later called Epiphania in Coele-Syria. Curtius, book IV. Now all Syria, now Phoenicia also, except for Tyre, belonged to the Macedonians.

So also B. Luther: Darzu auch über Hemath/ which translation is more convenient than those of others who merely invent a chorographic periphrasis here, that Hamath is situated in those borders. But since the feminine pronoun does not allow it to be referred to this BURDEN, Ludov. de Dieu and Willius refer it to the word עין EYE or inspection, because he will also terminate (Hamath) through that (inspection), as also Tyre and Sidon, so that they may not proceed further, or he will set boundaries by his inspection (the eye of providence) of the iniquity in Hamath. If you refer the feminine pronoun to the resting place, the sense will be plain, namely, because Hamath also is within its borders, namely of the resting place of the sad prophecy. Hamath is Antioch, the metropolis of Syria after the devastation of Damascus, called Hamath the Great in Amos VI. 2.

AND TYRE) Taken with much labor. See Curtius, book IV. AND SIDON) To whom Alexander imposed a king, Abdolonymus: that is עבד עליונים, which word in the Syriac language signifies a worshiper of the gods. FOR THEY HAVE TAKEN WISDOM UNTO THEMSELVES GREATLY) In the Hebrew: although she was wise: the Phoenicians were always crafty.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

EMATH QVOQVE IN TERMINIS EJVS) est, intra terminos ejus, nempe tristis Prophetiæ. De E- math Syriæ urbe diximus ad II. Regum XVII. vers. 24. Hieronymus ad hunc locum eam esse vult, quæ dicta est postea Epiphania in Syria Cœle. Curtius libro IV. Iam tota Syria, jam Phœnicia quoque, excepta Tyro, Macedonum erat.

Sic etiam B. Lutherus: Darzu auch über He- math/ quæ translatio convenientior est, quam illo- rum, qui nudam solum chorographicam περίφρα- σιν hic fingunt, quod Emath in terminis illis sita. Sed quum pronomen fœmininum non patiatur ad O- NUS hoc referri, ad vocem עין OCULI vel in- spectionis referunt Ludov. de Dieu, & Willius h.m. quia etiam (hamath) terminabit (Deus) per illam (inspectionem) ut & Tyro & Sidon, ne ulterius gra- diantur, vel terminos ponet inspectione sua (oculo providentiæ) iniquitatis in Camath. Si ad re- quiem pronomen fœmininum referas, planus sen- sus erit, m. quia etiam Chamath intra terminos e- jus, requiei nempe tristis Prophetiæ. Chèmath est Antiochia metropolis Syriæ post devastatam Da- mascum Am. VI. 2. dicta Emath magna.

ET TYRVS) Multo labore capta. Vide Curtium libr. IV. ET SIDON) Cui Regem Alexander imposuit Ab- dolonimum: id est עבד עליונים, quæ vox Syriaca lin- gua deorum cultorem significat. ASSUMSERUNT QUIPPE SIBI SAPIENTIAM VALDE) In Hebræo: quanquam fuit sapiens: Phœnices vafri semper.

## 9:3
AND TYRE BUILT HER FORTIFICATION) For herself, and repeat 'although' from the above. Neither did her craftiness save Sidon, nor walls and wealth save Tyre. Concerning them, see Curtius in the said book, and Ezek. XXVI. ver. 4.

AND HEAPED UP SILVER AS DUST, AND GOLD AS THE MIRE OF THE STREETS) See a similar passage in 2 Kings X. ver. 21. Concerning the wealth of Tyre, see Ezekiel XXVI. ver. 12, XXVII. ver. 27, XXVIII. ver. 4.

Latin:

IN ÆDIFICAVIT TYRVS MVNITIONEM SVAM) Sibi, & repete quanquam ex superiori. Neque Si- donem sua vafrities servavit, neque muri & opes Ty- rum. De illis vide Curtium dicto libro, & Ezech. XXVI. vers. 4.

ET COACERVAVIT ARGENTUM QVASI HVMVM, ET AURUM UT LUTUM PLA- TEARUM) Simile vide II. Regum X. vers. 21. De opi- bus Tyri vide Ezechielis XXVI. vers. 12. XXVII. vers. 27. XXVIII. vers. 4.

## 9:4
Ver. 4. STILL) Both at this time and after. OLD MEN AND OLD WOMEN SHALL DWELL) That the men of those times had reached a great age, the very things themselves show, nor can such works be done by God himself without any fault. For to drive someone into savagery and madness, and to be the author of cruelty to him, savors of nothing but sin. Nor is there any need for a law to be dictated to God in this matter, since he himself, and his most holy nature, and his law is most holy, which does not suffer that the author of the law should act against the law, even though he be greater than it. And how, I ask, can men bear the whole blame for crimes, if God drags them hither and thither against their will, and they fall into sins? Certainly, for an act done against one's will there is no blame, no punishment, which even the Gentiles understood from the light of nature. And, if they are dragged into sins by a secret motion through the hidden counsel of God, why are they not excusable? Certainly they will be excusable, because they have an external principle of their actions, to which they contribute nothing, and which is too vehement and powerful for them to be able to resist, which three conditions render an act involuntary in every respect, and excuse it. But will this really attach blame to them, that nothing is less proposed to them than to obey the word of God? Certainly, if you take the word of God for a command or instinct of God ordering or persuading them to evil, that disobedience of theirs will wash away all blame. For it is good to resist evil and the persuaders of evil. But if you take the word of God for divine precepts, this reasoning is more inept than that it could add any probability to this opinion. For what is sound in such an argumentation? Whoever has the purpose of not obeying divine laws, God can drive them into sin by a secret counsel and motion without any fault. The wicked have the purpose of not obeying divine laws. Therefore, God can drive the wicked into any sin whatsoever by secret counsel and motion. The consequent of the major premise is most absurd. For can the purpose of sinning justify an instigation and dragging into sins? If someone were to solicit a thief intent on theft to homicide or adultery and drag him into it, would he therefore be free from blame because that thief had another sin proposed to himself? I do not think so. And would God not act against his own holiness if he were to drag those who are certain to resist God's precepts into sins that please them by a secret motion? Certainly, certainly, such things cannot even be thought of God without sin, much less said. For thus sins would be multiplied by God rather than punished. And finally, this motion into sins cannot be justified by the goodness of the cause and the end. For it is not fitting to use evil means to achieve a good end, but just as the malice of the end ruins the goodness of the means, so on the contrary, evil means infect a good end. Although, therefore, God may be said to act in such a dragging into evil for the sake of just punishments and for the sake of his own glory, the goodness of the end can in no way amend the mode of acting, or render it immune from blame. Evil, wherever it may be, and for whatever end it may be admitted, is evil, and something contrary to the law, and to the divine will and holiness. It will therefore be more prudent to amend such harsh expressions and opinions about God's providence than to imitate or defend them: indeed, it is most Christian to speak of God and his providence as the Holy Scripture leads us, and as the most holy nature of God and reason, which is conformed to him, dictates. All these things Willius, which we have wished to bring forward so prolixly, so that other followers of Calvin may learn to imitate the candor of this man, and not excuse the impiety of their teacher in those things which can in no way be excused, which are diametrically opposed to the holiness of God, and attribute to God works which are the Devil's, and cannot be done by God without fault. Willius explains the phrase itself thus on p. 233: Those evils which have happened to you, you ought not to regard as fortuitous; I not only denied success to your works, but even by my direction and ordination, the infestations of enemies and domestic contentions found a place among you, and I inflicted them upon you as a due punishment, so that you owe all these things to my provocation on account of your sins. Therefore, these formulas of speaking do not denote any instigation to sin, or a secret and necessary motion toward malice, but the holy ordination and direction of sin, freely permitted and committed by the creature of its own accord, for the chastisement of the wicked. So that, to make the matter clearer by one more example, when God says of Pharaoh in Exodus VII. 9, 'But I will harden the heart of Pharaoh,' he does not say that he will cast and detain the heart of Pharaoh in disobedience by secret motion and counsel, but that he will so direct and order the sins permitted to him that, detained in them by just judgment, he may at last pay the deserved penalties, as the following words sufficiently declare. These things again are his, which he also illustrates with the words of Augustine, Book V, Chapter III, against Julian: 'God does not make evil wills, but uses them as he wills, since he cannot will anything unjustly.' Which is to be observed against other Calvinists.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ADHUC) Et hoc tempore, & post. HABITABUNT SENES ET ANUS) Ad magnam ætatem pervenisse illorum temporum homines, ipsæ res nec talia opera ab ipso Deo absque omni culpa fieri pos- sunt. In sævitiam enim & rabiem aliquem agere, ei- que crudelitatis auctorem esse, nihil nisi peccatum re- sipiunt. Nec opus est, ut hac in parte Deo lex dicatur, siquidem ipse, & sanctissima ejus natura, & lex san- ctissima est, quæ non patitur, ut legis auctor contra le- gem, licet ea major sit, agat. Et quomodo, quæso, pos- sunt homines totam culpam sustinere facinorum, si Deus eos invitos huc illuc trahat, & in peccata ruant. Inviti sane facti nulla culpa, nulla pœna est, quod vel gentiles ex lumine naturæ intellexerunt. Et, si occulto motu per arcanum Dei consilium in peccata trahun- tur, cur non sunt excusabiles? Sane excusabiles erunt, quia externum principium actionum suarum habent, ad quod ipsi nihil conferunt, & quod vehementius ac potentius est, quam ut illi resistere possint, quæ tres conditiones factum omni ex parte invitum reddunt, & excusant. Hoccine vero culpam ipsis affricabit, quod nihil minus propositum est eis, quam verbo Dei obedire? Sane si verbum Dei sumas pro jussu aut in- stinctu Dei malum ipsis imperantis aut suadentis, cul- pam omnem eluet eorum ista inobedientia. Malo enim & suasoribus malorum resistere bonum est. Si vero verbum Dei pro præceptis divinis sumas, ineptior est hæc ratio, quam quæ possit ullam probabilitatem ac- cessere huic sententiæ. Quid enim sani, in ejusmodi argumentatione? Quicunque propositum habent non obediendi legibus divinis, eos Deus arcano consilio & motu absque ulla culpa in peccatum a- gere potest. Improbis propositum est legibus di- vinis non obedire. Ergo improbos Deus arcano consilio & motu in peccatū quodvis agere potest. Majoris consequens absurdissimum est. An enim pro- positum peccandi instigationem & tractum in peccata justificare potest? An si quis furem furto intentum ad homicidium vel adulterium sollicitet & in illud pertrahat, culpa propterea careret, quia fur ille aliud sibi habuit peccatum propositum? Non puto. Et an Deus non ageret contra sanctitatem suam, si eos, qui Dei præceptis resistere certi sunt, in peccata, quæ sibi placent, occulto motu pertraheret? Sane, sane, ejus- modi absque peccato de Deo ne quidem cogitari, multo minus dici poterunt. Sic enim potius pec cata à Deo multiplicarentur, quam punirentur. Nec potest denique justificari iste in peccata motus causæ & finis bonitate. Neque enim decet ad bonum finem consequendum malis uti mediis, sed uti finis malitia bonitatem mediorum pessundat, ita contra media ma- la bonum finem inficiunt. Licet igitur Deus pœnarum justarum causa, & suæ gloriæ gratia agere dicatur in ejusmodi tractu ad malum, nihil modum agendi finis bonitas emendare, aut immunem à culpa reddere po- test. Malum ubicunque sit, & quocunque admitta- tur fine, malum est, & aliquid legi, ac divinæ volun- tati & sanctitati contrarium. Duras igitur ejusmo- di de Dei providentia locutiones & sententias con- sultius erit emendare, quam imitari aut defende- re: imo maxime Christianum, ita de Deo & ejus providentia loqui, ut sacra Scriptura nobis præit, & sanctissima Dei natura & naturæ, quæ ei con- formata, ratio fert. Hæc omnia Willius, quæ tam prolixe adducere voluimus, ut alii Calvinisequæ discant candorem hujus viri imitari, nec excusent impietatem præceptoris in his, quæ nullo pacto excusari possunt, quæ sanctitati Dei καδδιάμετρον contrariantur, Deoque tribuunt opera, quæ Dia- boli sunt, nec absque culpa à Deo fieri possunt. Phrasin autem ipsam ita explicat Willius p. 233. Ma- la illa, quæ vobis evenerunt, non ceu fortuita reputa- re debetis, ego vestris successum non modo denegavi o- peribus, verum etiam mea directione & ordinatione hostium infestationes & domestica contentiones apud vos locum invenerunt, easque vobis, ceu pœnam de- bitam inflixi, adeo, ut omnia hæc meæ exacerbationi propter delicta vestra debeatis. Non igitur hæ lo- quendi formulæ aliquam ad peccandum instiga- tionem, aut arcanum & necessarium ad malitiam motum, sed peccati libere permissi & à creatura sua sponte facti, sanctam ordinationem & directio- nem ad castigationem impiorum denotant, Ita, ut uno adhuc exemplo res fiat manifestior, cum Deus ait de Pharaone Exod. VII. 9. Ego vero obdurabo cor Pharaonis, non dicit, se arcano motu & consilio cor Pharaonis, in inobedientiam conjecturum & de- tenturum, sed se peccata ei permissa ita directurum & ordinaturum, ut justo judicio in iis detentus, tan- dem promeritas pœnas luat, quomodo hæc verba se- quentia satis declarant. Hæc iterum ille, quæ illu- strat etiam verbis Augustini l. V. cap. III. contra Julian. Deus non facit voluntates malas, sed utitur eis ut voluerit, cum aliquid inique velle non possit. Quod adversus alios Calvinianos observandum.

## 9:4
Verse 4.

BEHOLD THE LORD WILL POSSESS HER) He will cast her out: that is, her inhabitants. Thus the Chaldean aptly.

AND HE WILL STRIKE HER STRENGTH IN THE SEA) And he will cast her forces into the sea: that is, the fleet and the marines. See Curtius.

AND SHE SHALL BE DEVOURED BY FIRE) And she herself shall be devoured by fire. Curtius on Alexander: he orders fire to be thrown upon the roofs.

This persuasion of Wisdom was also reproached to the King of Tyre, Ezek. XXIX. Behold you are wiser than Daniel, etc. Trust, therefore, in Wisdom, fortifications, and riches will destroy Tyre and Sidon, along with the avarice and injustice which is tacitly objected to it in the hoarding of silver. Compare Ezekiel XXIX. Alexander the Great besieged Tyre, and although it was previously 200 paces distant from the shore, he made it contiguous to the mainland by a mole, and made a peninsula out of an island. See Diodorus Siculus, book XVII.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ECCE DOMINVS POSSIDEBIT EAM) Eji- ciet eam: id est, habitatores ejus. Ita Chaldæus ap- posite.

ET PERCUTIET IN MARI FORTITVDINEM EJUS) Et projiciet in mare vires ejus: id est, classem, & classiarios. Vide Curtium.

ET HÆC IGNI DEVORABITUR) Et ipsa igne devorabitur. Curtius de Alexandro: ignem tectis injici jubet.

Hæc persuasio Sapientiæ exprobrata etiam Re- gi Tyri Ezech. XXIX. Ecce sapientior es tu Da- niele &c. Fiducia ergo in Sapientia, munitionibus & opibus, Tyrum & Sydonem perdet, cum avaritia & injustitia, quæ tacite in coacervatione argenti eidem objicitur. Conf. Ezechielis XXIX. Ex- pugnavit Alexander Magnus Tyrum & cum antea 200. passibus à littore abesset aggere continenti contiguam reddidit, & ex insula peninsulam fecit. Vid. Diodor. Siculus l. XVII.

## 9:5
Verse 5.

ASCALON SHALL SEE, AND SHALL FEAR, AND SHALL GRIEVE EXCEEDINGLY) These cities had hoped that if Tyre could resist Alexander, they too could escape his hands. They fell from this hope when Tyre was captured.

AND GAZA) Which was captured immediately after Tyre. Josephus, XI, verse 8.

By the King of Gaza, he understands a petty king, just as the princes of cities were also once called kings. The prefect of the city of Gaza under Darius Codomannus was Betis, whom Alexander the Great, having besieged Gaza, caused to be captured around the city, as Curtius testifies in book IV. Others explain it as the taking away of the scepter and empire from the Philistines, of whom Gaza was the head. Zephaniah also prophesied about the desolation of Ascalon, chapter II, verses 4, 6. לא תשב SHALL NOT DWELL, an active form for a passive, as in Isaiah chapter XIII, verse 20.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

VIDEBIT ASCALON, ET TIMEBIT, ET DO- LEBIT NIMIS) Speraverant istæ urbes, si Tyrus resistere posset Alexandro, se quoque posse ejus manus evadere. Ab hac spe decidere capta Tyro.

ET GAZA) Quæ statim post Tyrum capta. Jo- seph. XI. vers. 8.

Per Regem Gazæ, regulum intelligit, sicuti Principes urbium etiam vocati olim sunt reges. Præfectus urbi Gaza à Dario Codomanno fuit Betis, quem Alexander Magnus expugnata Ga- za circa urbem captivari curavit, teste Curtio lib. IV. Alii de sceptro & imperio à Philistæis, quo- rum caput fuerit Gaza, tollendo explicant. De desolatione Ascalon vaticinatus etiam est Sopho- niæ cap. II. vers. 4. 6. לא תשב NON HABI- TABIT, forma activa pro passiva ut Esaiæ c. XIII. vers. 20.

## 9:6
Verse 6.

AND THE SEPARATOR SHALL SIT IN AZOTUS) In Hebrew: Mamzer: how those born from a union for which the penalty is death, or כרת, are called, as we said regarding Deuteronomy. Improperly, all who are not rightful heirs are called this. ἀλλογενεῖς, here the LXX, nor does the Chaldean say otherwise.

Some explain the word ממזר, separator, stranger, as referring to a bastard, who is born to a strange father outside of marriage, and they understand Alexander the Great, who subjugated Azotus and the remaining Philistines, since his mother bore him not from Philip, but from the magician Nectanebo. Others think that foreigners, Greeks, under Alexander, or even later Jews under the Maccabees, who were scattered through Azotus and Philistia, Acts VIII, verse 40, are noted. The Greeks are called newcomers from the region of the Chittim, Isaiah chapter XXIII, verse 1. Therefore, the Prophet threatens four evils. The loss of empire for Gaza, extermination and destruction for Ascalon, the substitution of other inhabitants for Ashdod. A total destruction for the other Philistines. Compare a similar threat in Zephaniah chapter II, verse 2. Willius has encompassed the completion of the prophecy from history: Syria was often, indeed almost continuously, moved by domestic and external wars by the Egyptians and finally by the Romans afflicted. When Sidon had revolted from Artaxerxes Ochus, and was betrayed by the treachery of Mentor, and could not escape the hand of the victor by any other way, it burned itself by applying flames to the individual houses. Diod. Sic. lib. XVI. p. 534. Tyre, after Alexander had joined it to the mainland with a mole, was captured, and the inhabitants were destroyed to the point of extermination. More than 7,000 men were slaughtered, 1,600 youths were hanged, and over 13,000 of the female sex and non-combatant age were led away into captivity, as Diodorus Siculus testifies, l. 17. Biblioth. histor. page 566. 30,000 were sold as slaves, if we follow Arrian, lib. II. on the Deeds of Alexander. Gaza was captured by the same Alexander not long after he had conquered all of Palestine; he slaughtered the greater part of the citizens who resisted to the end, consigned their wives and children to slavery, and having imposed new colonists upon the city, he used it as a fortress of war because of its convenient location for expeditions into neighboring regions. Arrian, lib. II. near the end: Thus the truth of this threat was proven.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET SEDEBIT SEPARATOR IN AZOTO) In Hebræo: Mamzer: quomodo vocantur nati ex congressu, cui pœna mors, aut כרת, ut ad Deuteronomium diximus. Improprie sic vocantur omnes, qui non ju- re hæredes sunt. ἀλλογενεῖς, hic LXX. nec Chaldæus aliter.

Vocem ממזר separator, alienus, de spurio, qui alieno patri extra matrimonium natus, ex- plicant nonnulli, & Alexandrum Magnum qui Azotum & reliquos Philistæos subjugavit, quum non ex Philippo, sed Mestobano mago, mater eum genuerit, intelligunt. Alienigenas, Græ- cos, sub Alexandro, vel etiam deinde Judæos sub Maccabæis notari, qui per Azotum & Philistæam sparsi fuere Actorum IIX. vers. 40. alii existimant. Græci vocantur advenæ è regione Chittarum Esaiæ cap. XXIII. vers. 1. Quatuor er- go mala minatur Propheta. Gazæ amissionem imperii, Ascaloni exterminationem & exitium, Asdodo incolarum aliorum substitutionem. Phi- listæis aliis totale excidium. Confer. similis com- minatio Sophoniæ cap. II. vers. 2. Complemen- tum vaticinii ex historia complexus est Willius: Syriam sæpius, imo fere continuo domestica & ex- terna bella ab Ægyptiis & Romanis denique mota afflixere. Sidon cum ab Artaxerxe Ocho defecisset, & Mentoris perfidia prodita, alia via victoris ma- num evadere nequiret flammis singulis ædibus ad- motis seipsam combussit. Diod. Sic. lib. XVI. p. 534. Tyrus ab Alexandro, postquam eam aggere continen- ti junxisset, capta, incolæ ad internecionem deleti. Vi- rorum ultra 7000. trucidati, juvenes 1600. suspensi, su- pra 13000. è sexu fæmineo, & ætate imbelli in capti- vitatem abducti, teste Diodoro Siculo l. 17. Bi- blioth. histor. pag. 566. 30000. millia pro servis ve- nundati, si Arrianum lib. II. de Reb. Alexandri se- quimur. Gaza ab eodem Alexandro non longe post eum universa Palæstina expugnata, qui cives ad ex- tremum resistentes maximam partem trucidavit, uxo- res & liberos servituti mancipavit, novisque colonis urbi impositis, ea, ut arce belli, propter commodam in vicinas oras expeditionem usus est. Arrianus lib. II. sub finem: Ita veritas hujus comminationis com- probata est.

## 9:7
Verse 7.

AND I WILL TAKE AWAY HIS BLOOD FROM HIS MOUTH) That is, I will cause that the Philistine no longer threatens slaughter, as he was accustomed to do.

AND HIS ABOMINATIONS FROM BETWEEN HIS TEETH) So that, pressed by poverty, he may no longer prepare feasts for the τοῖς εἰδωλοθύτοις (things sacrificed to idols).

AND HE HIMSELF SHALL BE LEFT TO OUR GOD) This was fulfilled at the time when the Maccabees captured many of the τῶν ἀλλοφύλων (thus the Philistines are excellently called, and the LXX are accustomed to translate the Philistines with this word) cities. Joseph. XII. 12. I. Macc. V. 6. The same Josephus on the times of Alexander, King of the Jews: At this time the Jews already held the cities of the Syrians, and Idumeans, and Phoenicians; by the sea, Straton's Tower, Apollonia, Joppa, Jamnia, Azotus, Gaza, Anthedon, Raphia, Rhinocolura. And in the interior, in Idumea, Adora and Marissa, and Samaria, Mount Carmel, and Mount Itabyrion, Scythopolis, Gadara, Gaulanitis, Seleucia, the Moabite cities of Heshbon, Medaba, Lemba, Oronaim, Gelithon, Zara, the valley of the Cilicians, Pella. And they razed this one, because the inhabitants would not change to the ancestral customs of the Jews, and other leading cities of Syria, which had been destroyed. Among the cities overcome by the Jews, you have here by name both Azotus and Gaza.

AND HE SHALL BE AS A LEADER IN JUDAH) For proselytes were capable of holding property among the Jews: as the exception to that rule in Deuteronomy XXIII teaches.

AND ACCARON) A city of Palestine also named above.

AS A JEBUSITE) By which right were the Jebusite proselytes, as Araunah in II Kings XXIV. 16 and following.

Arias Montanus and others understand this as the blood of the victims which they offered to the idol Dagon at Azotus being taken away, and the sacred rites of the Lord being introduced in the place of sacrilegious sacrifices, both Jewish through the Maccabees, and Christian through Philip and the Apostles: Jerome, Theodoret, and Hugo interpret it as the taking away and restraining of their threats, by which they threatened that they would shed, or boasted that they had shed, the blood of the Jews, provided that they are to be subjected and aggregated to them. It is predicted, therefore, that the hatred and discord which existed between the Jews and the Philistines would be removed, and that the ferocity and cruelty with which the Philistines thirsted for the blood and flesh of the Jews would cease, as Winckelmann and others of our own here [state]. Which Lyranus wrongly refers to the threats of Alexander, as to what one devoted to God and His High Priest Jaddua ought to have done. For it concerns the remnants of the Philistines being consecrated to God. For since the preceding [verses] threaten destruction to the enemies of the Jews, now the threat is mitigated by the promise that even from the most wicked enemies a place is to be left in the Church for God. Willius also acknowledges this sense in this verse 7, departing from his teacher Calvin and refuting him. The fulfillment of this promise, he says, pertains to the Kingdom of Christ. For although even before, with the Jews spreading themselves most widely through the regions, many from these neighboring nations became proselytes, yet only in the time of the Apostles was a great multitude from these subjugated through the Gospel of Christ, as the book of the Acts of the Apostles testifies. Nor indeed should it be thought that this place is corrupted by that true interpretation, and that readers are turned away from the true and genuine sense, as a certain great man thinks. For this Prophet passes on to promises, and with them tempers the severity of the threat, not only with respect to the Philistines, but also of the remaining kingdoms, of which he made mention. The Prophet distinctly names the benefit itself and the effect joined with the benefit. As regards the benefit, he promises that he will remove his slaughters from his mouth, and his detestations from his teeth. A metaphorical form of speech taken from wild and carnivorous beasts, by which he signifies that he will purge their cruelty and tyranny. They will therefore abstain from their slaughters and abominable ferocity, and will obtain the remission of their iniquities in the blood of Christ, through whom the nations, when they were enemies, were reconciled to God, Rom. V. verse 10. Furthermore, the Prophet proceeds to describe the effect of the benefit, and he shall be a remnant, he says, even he for our God, and shall be as a leader in Judah. Behold a notable consequence of the benefit! First, the enemies will become a remnant for God, and their survivors will be saved, which is indeed a great benefit and an evident proof of mercy, while total ruin is spared to those who deserve it. But the second thing, which follows, is by far the greatest, that they will furthermore be numbered among the people of God, and will obtain an honorable place in the Church, and will be of the number of אלופים, of teachers, leaders, and guides, who will devote their effort to God for leading and instructing his people in the way of salvation. And this prophecy was fulfilled when many from the nations not only gave their names to Christ, but furthermore instructed others also unto salvation by living voice and writings, as is known from history and the series of the fathers. These are the words of Willius, who, while he agrees with these, having left Calvin to our own and ancient interpreters, it is necessary to wonder why in the following verse he attacks them, and suddenly pretends that the Prophet passes from promise to threat, even though the subsequent words concerning the encamping at the House of the Lord sufficiently testify that he is pursuing and continuing the same promises. Naturally, so that he might not entirely fail his Calvin, he preferred to take the words 'Ekron shall be as a Jebusite' as threatening, that the citizens of Ekron are to suffer a similar slaughter. But it is too manifest that the Vau here is to be rendered not in an adversative sense, but in the more customary copulative one, because these things are coupled as similar, not disjoined as disparate. And he who is a remnant from the Philistines (not from the Jews, as Calvin wishes, for the mention of the former, not the latter, preceded) even he shall be for our God, and shall be as a leader in Judah, so also Ekron (shall be) as a Jebusite, as the Philistines shall be as leaders in Judah, so the Ekronites as the Jebusites. Whether you render it thus, that Ekron will be faithful, as Jebus became Jerusalem, Josh. XVIII, Judg. XIX, or rather thus, that the Ekronites will dwell with the people of God as the Jebusites, or whether with Junius you wish to look to the Jebusite Arnon, 2 Sam. XXI. 16, or whether with Hugo and others you explain: As David subjected the Jebusites, so the Ekronites will be subjected to the Church, the matter thus far comes to the same thing, that a promise is held here, not a threat concerning the overthrow of the Ekronites persisting in malice. For not only the Ekronites, but also other nations persisting in malice had to be overthrown. Cocceius acknowledges this in this place, p. 519. The mind of the prophecy is, just as there are in the tribe of Judah families having their own

Princes and Elders, so also the remnants of the Palestinian people will act as a tribe or family belonging to the people of God, being subject to their elders in the fear of God. And indeed this will happen before the coming of Christ according to the letter and the formula of that time. After the coming of Christ, it will happen by the gathering of the Church through the word of the Gospel. Parity of law is signified by this: that the prince כגר כאזרח, just as the stranger and the native, is frequent in the law: but also because they will dwell in a part of the inheritance of the holy land. As the Jebusite, just as the Jebusites remained mixed with the Israelite people, and in that very place where the temple was established; so Accaron and other Palestinians will not be exterminated, as the other Canaanites, but will be gathered. Conf. Joseph. XIII. Antiq. cap. 22. These are Coccejus'.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET AUFERAM SANGUINEM EJUS DE ORE EJUS) Id est, efficiam ne amplius Philistinus cædes mi- netur, ut facere solebat.

ET ABOMINATIONES EJUS DE MEDIO DENTIUM EJUS) Ut paupertate pressus, non amplius epulas instruat τοῖς εἰδωλοθύτοις.

ET RELINQVETUR IPSE DEO NOSTRO) Impletum hoc quo tempore multas τῶν ἀλλοφύλων (ita eximie vocantur Philistini, solentque LXX. Philistinos hoc vocabulo vertere) urbes cepere Maccabæi Joseph. XII. 12. I. Macc. V. 6. Idem Joseph. de tempor. Alex. Judæoru Regis: Κατὰ τὸν τοῦτον καιρὸν ἤδη τῶν Σύρων, καὶ Ἰδουμαίων, καὶ Φοι- νίκων πόλεις εἶχον Ἰουδαῖοι, πρὸς θαλάσσῃ μὲν Στράτωνος πύργον, Ἀπολλωνίαν, Ἰόππην, Ἰάμνειαν, Ἄζωτον, Γάζαν, Ἀνθηδόνα, Ῥαφίαν, Ῥινοκόλουραν. ἐν δὲ τῇ μεσογείᾳ, κατὰ τὴν Ἰδουμαίαν, Ἀδῶρα καὶ Μαρίσσαν, καὶ Σαμάρειαν, Καρμήλιον ὄρος, καὶ τὸ Ἰταβύριον ὄρος, Σκυθόπολιν, Γάδαρα, Γαυλα- νίτιδα, Σελεύκειαν, Μωαβίτιδας Ἐσσεβῶν, Μήδαβα, Λεμβᾶ, Θρώνιας, Γελίθωνα, Ζαρὰ, Κιλίκων αὐλῶνα, Πέλλαν. ταύτην δὲ κατέσκαψαν, οὐχ ὑποχομένων τῶν ἰν κέντων εἰς τὰ πάτρια Ἰου- δαίων ἔθη μεταβαλέσθαι, ἄλλας τε πόλεις πρωτευούσας τῆς Συ- ρίας, αἳ ἦσαν κατεστραμμέναι. Inter urbes à Judæis superatas, habes hic nominatim & Azotum & Gazam.

ET ERIT QVASI DUX IN JVDA) Nam pro- selyti bonorum apud Judæos erant capaces: ut docet ex- ceptio ejus regulæ Deuter. XXIII.

ET ACCARON) Urbs Palæstinæ supra etiam no- minata.

QUASI JEBUSÆUS) Quo jure fuerunt Proselytæ Jebusæi, ut Arevna II. Regum XXIV. 16. & sequentibus.

De sanguine victimarum, quas Dagon idolo of- ferebant Azoti auferendo, & in locum sacrificio- rum sacrilegorum inducendis sacris Domini, tum Judaicis per Maccabæos, tum Christianis per Phi- lippum & Apostolos Arias Montanus & alii in- telligunt: de auferendis & compecendis minis eo- rum, quibus minabantur se effusurum, aut gloria- bantur, se effudisse sanguinem Judæorum, Hiero- nymus, Theodoretius, Hugo interpretantur, siquidem illis subjiciendi & aggregandi sint. Prædicitur ergo sublatum iri odium & dissidium, quod inter Judæos & Philistinos erat, & cessaturam truculentiam & crudelitatem, qua Philistini Judæorum sanguini & carnibus inhiabant, uti hic Winckelmannus & alii è nostris. Quæ perperam Lyranus ad minas Alexan- dri refert, quid fieri debuerit devotus Deo, ejusq; Pontifici Jaddo. Nam de reliquiis Philistinorum Deo consecrandis agitur. Quum enim superiora hostibus Judæorum minentur interitum, jam com- minatio mitigatur promissione, quod etiam ex per- ditissimis hostibus quibusdam locus in Ecclesia Deo relinquendus sit. Quem sensum in hoc vers. 7. agnoscit etiam Willius discedens à præceptore suo Calvino, eumque refellens. Complementum hujus promissionis, inquit, ad Regnum Christi spectat. Li- cet enim etiam ante, latissime per regiones se dif- fus fundentibus Judæis, multi ex vicinis hisce genti- bus proselyti facti sint, tamen Apostolorum de- mum tempore maxima multitudo ex his per Evan- gelium Christi subjugata est, ut liber Actorum A- postolicorum testatur. Nec sane putandum vera ista interpretatione depravari hunc locum, lecto- resque à vero & genuino sensu averti, ut vir qui- dam magnus censet. Transit enim hic Propheta ad promissiones, iisque comminationis severitatem temperat non modo respectu Philistæorum, sed reliquorum etiam regnorum, quorum mentio- nem injecit. Distincte autem Propheta ipsum be- neficium nominat & effectum cum beneficio con- junctum. Beneficium, quod attinet, promittit, se re- moturum cædes ejus ab ore ejus, & detestationes ejus è dentibus ejus. Formula loquendi metaphorica à be- stiis feris & carnivoris desumta, qua crudelitatem & tyrannidem eorum se expiaturum significat. Ab- stinebunt igitur à cædibus & feritate sua abomi- nanda, & iniquitatum suarum remissionem conse- quentur in sanguine Christi, per quem gentes, cum inimici essent, Deo reconciliati sunt, Rom. V. vers. 10. Porro pergit effectum beneficii Propheta describere, & residuus fiet, inquit, etiam ipse Deo nostro, & erit tanquam Dux in Juda. En insigne beneficii consequens! Primum residui fient hostes Deo, & reliquiæ ipsorum servabuntur, quod sane magnum beneficium est, & evidens misericordiæ documentum, dum totalem ruinam meritis par- citur. Alterum vero, quod sequitur longe maxi- mum est, quod insuper populo Dei annumera- buntur, & honorificum in Ecclesia locum conse- quentur, eruntq; è numero אלופים doctorum, du- cum, ductorum, qui operam suam Deo commoda- bunt ad ducendum & erudiendum populum suum in via salutis. Et hoc vaticinium impletum est, quando multi ex gentibus non modo nomina sua Christo dederunt, verum insuper alios etiam ad salutem viva voce & scriptis erudierunt, ut ex hi- storia & serie patrum notum est. Hæc Willius, qui cum his, relicto Calvino nostris & antiquis Interpp. adstipuletur, mirari oportet, cur in com- mate sequenti eosdem exagitet, & subito Prophe- tam à promissione ad comminationem transire fingat, tametsi subsequentia de castri metatione ad Domum Domini satis testentur, eundem promis- siones persequi ac continuare. Nimirum, ut Cal- vino suo non plane deesset, verba Ekron erit q. Ie- busæus pro comminatoriis habere maluit, quod si- milem cladem perlaturi sint cives Ekron. Ast nimis manifestum, Vau hic reddendum non sensu adver- sativo, sed usitatiori copulativo, quia copulantur hæc tanquam similia, non disjunguntur ut dispa- rata. Et residuus erit è Philistinis (non è Judæis, uti vult Calvinus, non enim horum, sed illorum præcessit mentio) etiam ipse erit Deo nostro, & e- rit quasi dux in Jehuda, sic & Ekron (erit) quasi Ie- busæus, ut Philistæi erunt quasi duces in Juda, ita Ekronitæ, quasi Jebusitæ. Quod sive ita reddas, Ekronem fidelem fore, ut Iebus facta est Hiero- solyma Jos. XIIX. Jud. XIX. seu ita potius, Ekro- nitas habitaturos cum populo Dei ut Iebusitas, sive cum Junio respicere velis Arnonam Iebusæum II. Sam. XXI. 16. Sive cum Hugone & aliis exponas: Sicut David subjecit Jebusæos, sic Ekronitas subje- ctum iri Ecclesiæ, res eodem hactenus recidit, pro- missionem hic haberi, non comminationem de E- kronitarum in malitia perseverantium eversione. Neque enim soli Ekronitæ, sed etiam aliæ gentes in malitia perseverantes everti debuere. Agnoscit id Coccejus in h. l. p. 519. Mens prophetiæ est, quem- admodum sunt in Iudæ tribu familiæ habentes suos

Principes & Seniores, ita quoque Palæstinæ gentis re- liquiæ facient quasi tribum aut familiam pertinentem ad populum Dei, rectam suis senioribus in timore Dei. Et quidem hoc ante Christi adventum fiet secun- dum literam, & formulam illius temporis. Post Christi adventum fiet collectione Ecclesiæ per verbum Evangelii. Paritas juris significatur per hoc: ut princeps כגר כאזרח perinde advena & indigena, frequens est in lege: sed & quia in parte hæreditatis terræ sanctæ habitabunt. Ut Jebusæus, quemadmodum Jebusæi manserunt permixti po- pulo Israelitico, & in illo quidem loco, ubi tem- plum fuit constitutum; ita Accaron & alii Palæstini non exterminabuntur, ut cæteri Cananæi, sed ag- gregabuntur. Conf. Joseph. XIII. Antiq. cap. 22. Hæc Coccejus.

## 9:8
Verse 8.

AND I WILL ENCAMP AROUND MY HOUSE FROM THOSE WHO FIGHT FOR ME GOING AND RETURNING) I will pitch camp around my house against an army, against those going and returning. That is, I will give angels who may guard the Temple, so that it may neither be besieged by an enemy, nor even infested by incursions. I will avert great and lesser dangers from the Temple, namely until the times of Antiochus.

AND NO EXACTOR SHALL PASS OVER THEM ANY MORE) That is, a tyrant, as here the Chaldean: for it is the custom of tyrants to oppress the people with tributes.

Because the preceding [verses] speak of the conversion of the nations, which was to happen in the time of the New Testament, this promise is not to be restricted precisely to the temple of Zerubbabel, but is to be referred to the Church of the Lord, which is called the house of the living God, I Tim. III. 15, to which God promises from that time defense against the force of enemies and the protection of holy angels, Ps. XXXIV. 8. But he seems to allude to the temple in which the Levites and Priests kept watch. See Ps. CXXXIV, and thus he promises that he himself, immediately and through his angels, will protect his Church then and in future times. Therefore, we do not exclude here those times in which the neighboring nations were to suffer disasters, the Syrians, Phoenicians, Palestinians, but we include that the Lord will then pitch camp around his Church, so that his people may not also be involved in those disasters, and thus he will continue to protect his Church perpetually, so that it may not be oppressed by an exactor. The Chaldean paraphrast illustrates these things thus: And I will cause the majesty of my glory to dwell in the house of my sanctuary, and the strength of the arm of my power will be, like a wall of fire, in its circuit, because of those passing and returning. The Lord pitches camp because of an army, because of those passing, and because of those returning, i.e., because of hostile armies and their excursions, AND NO EXACTOR SHALL PASS OVER THEM ANY MORE, which some understand concerning the liberation from the curse of the law and the tyranny of the Devil; but just as the rest speak of defense against the force of enemies, so here by נגש, an EXACTOR or OPPRESSOR is understood by anyone. Conf. Is. XIV. 2. 7. Zech. X. 4. The Church is no longer to be exposed to the violence and plunderings of enemies.

Verse of the same.

FOR NOW I HAVE SEEN WITH MY EYES) For now (that is, heretofore) I have seen with my eyes. That is, it appears to me that there are many neighboring nations that would invade the Temple in a hostile manner, or plunder it in the manner of robbers, if I did not oppose them in wondrous ways.

It is a Hebraism for 'I have seen with my eyes.' Some explain it as being of the Prophet. But the words are of the Son of God, who is clearly speaking here from a comparison of verses 6, 7, and 8. For he who in verse 6 says 'I will cut off the pride of the Philistines,' and in verse 8 'I will pitch camp at my house,' is without doubt Jehovah, the true God.
