At Interpp. Christiani plerique interpretantur de prælio & victoria spirituali: Theodoreteus, Cyrillus, Re- migius, Rupertus, Lyranus, Dionysius, & recentiores propemodum omnes, si Calvinianos excipias, & qui hic eosdem sequutus est, D. Tarnovium. Nam va- ticinatur Propheta non solum de Judæis, sed etiam de Ephraim, vel decem tribubus. Quod restrin- gi non potest ad pauculos illos, qui forte Judæis se adjunxerunt, post reditum è Babylone. Adhæc cohærent hæc cum superioribus, quæ de pace spiri- tuali & diffusione regni Messiæ agebant: ideoque prosequitur hoc argumentum Propheta, vi συ- νεχείας contextus. Nec regibus Syriæ & Ægypti, cum quibus Maccabæis negotium fuit, Græcorum nomen congruit, etsi Alexandri M. successores fuerint. Gentes autem cùm opponuntur Judæis, Græcorum nomine venire è N. T. constat. Vid. Rom. 1, 17. c. 2, 9. c. 3, 2. Ait ergo: Extendam mihi Iudam, implevi Ephraim sagittis, quia arte jaculan- di præcellebant Ephraimitæ Pf. 77, 9. Assumam ex Iuda & Ephraim Duces Apostolos, & excitabo filios tuos ô Sion, super filios tuos ô Græcia, & ponam te (po- pulum meum Israëlïticum) quasi gladium fortium. Ego per Apostolos meos, qui omnes erunt Judæi & Israëlitæ, tanquam armis validissimis debellabo gentes (nam gentes scriptura sæpe Græcos vocat) ut sese in obsequium meum tradant, Et Dominus (Deus) super eos videbitur, apparebit manifestus, & præsens, uti habet paraphrasis Osiandrina: ET SALVABIT EOS DOMINUS DEUS EO- RUM IN DIE ILLA, UT GREGEM PO- PULI SUI: id est, Dominus & Apostolorum (alio- rumque ipsorum ministrorum fidelium) & audito- rum, qui sese in obsequium Christo tradiderunt, pa- ternam curam geret, non aliter, quam Pastor fidelis gregem suum curat Joh. 10. Consentit paraphra- sis Vinariensis, nec non Wigandus, VVinckelmann. Pappus, Himmelius in Commentar. ad h. l. ut & Balduinus noster p. 621. Per Iudam intelligit more scripturæ regnum Judæ, quod duab9 constabat tri- bubus, Juda & Benjamin, in quibus vera olim erat sedes Ecclesiæ: per Ephraim cæteras decem tribus, quæ à legitimo rege & religione defecerant ad cul- tum vitulorum sub Jeroboamo 1. Reg. 12. Ex utro- que regno Ecclesiæ se Doctores daturum pollice- tur, qui doctrina sua velut infallibili quodam ar- cu scopum salutis nostræ tangent, qui est Christus cum universo suo merito. Idque factum est, quan- do Apostolos ex regno Judaico & Israëlitico ori- undos emisit ad prædicandum Evangelium inter gentes. Comparat autem regnum Iuda arcui, quia plures Apostoli ex eo oriundi erant, quam ex isto: & ex Juda egressa est prædicatio de Christo, ideo dicitur arcus Evangelicæ doctrinæ in Juda ex- tendi: & mox additur, suscitabo filios tuos Sion, super filios tuos Græcia, quia Apostoli Hierosolymæ cœ- perunt prædicare remissionem peccatorum, Luc. 24, 47. & inde ad gentes egressi aliis quidem natio- nibus etiam præ cæteris doctrina Apostolica scripto propagata fuit, quemadmodum Epistolæ Pauli te- stantur. Quibus omnibus præivit B. Lutherus noster in Commentar. ad h. l. cum veneranda anti- quitate, è qua imprimis hic Cyrillus Alex. è Græca Ecclesia conferri meretur: Quonam modo vocan- da sit, & per fidem ingressura gentium multitudo, mi- ser contra futurus, qui olim triumphabat, hoc est, Sa- tanas spoliatus, adoraturus, quos cupidissime acquisie- rat, adhuc declarat. Alloquitur autem quasi sanctos Apostolos sive magistros ex Israel, qui & gentium re- giones percursantes, ad agnitionem veritatis indigenas vocarunt, & reti suo concluserunt. Ait ergo (O Ju- da, intendi te mihi arcum, hoc est, per te jaculis tan- gam adversarios: & (te ô Epraim implevi) Quod quid sit, dicam quoq; : Cum enim sagittarii arcum ferratum curvantes, nervum ad pectus addunt, tunc arcum implere dicuntur, & sagittam volantem, sive telum jaciunt. Est igitur idem diverse dictum. Ar- cu te feci, inquit, ô Juda, implevi te etiam Ephraim. Judas porro & Ephraim universum genus Israeliti- cum complectuntur. Itaq; ante alios ex Judeis cre- dentes velut arcum fecit, eo animi provectos, ut gentes instituerent, & à seductis dæmonum greges abigerent, ferirentq; Satanam, & universæ divinis decretis ad- versantes, & doctrinæ sacræ inde proficiscenti repu- gnantes. Sic & alicubi divinus David ad univer- sorum Deum & Salvatorem (sagittæ tuæ salutis a- cutæ, ô potens, populi sub te cadent, in corde ini- micorum regis) Feriunt enim inimicos Dei & Patris, in cor, & renes intus sagittæ potentis, hoc est, Christi. Et postea: Quinam enim filii Sion insurgentes con- tra filios Græcorum, nisi divini discipuli, & Ecclesia- rum, suis quiq; temporibus, Præsides! (Et recte tra- ctantes verbum Dei) Nam Sion quæ animo videtur, quomodo alia præter Ecclesiam intelligatur? Oppu- gnant autem filios Græcorum, & bello lacessunt errore seductos, Deo illis utente ut gladio bellatoris. Hæc Cyrillus. E Latinis Hieronymus: Hunc locum (Ju- dæi) ad Maccabæorum referunt tempora, quod illis contra Antiochum dimicantibus atque vincentibus, Domini fuerit pugna atq; victoria: qui egressus sit for- tis ad prælium: & instar fulguris illius potentia appa- ruerit, victisq; adversariis & turbinis amore disper- sis protexerit populum Judæorum. Nos autem refe- remus cuncta ad intelligentiam salvatoris, de quo su- pra dictum est: Extendi mihi Judam, quasi arcum. Quo extento & hæreticis atq; gentilibus à Sion filiis in- terfectis, apparebit gloria Domini: & egredietur ut fulgur jaculum ejus: de quo fulgure & in Habacuc legimus: in luce sagittarum tuarum ibunt in splen- dore fulgurantis hastæ tuæ, salvabit quoque Domi- nus eos, sicut oves, & gregem populi sui: Non enim ut armatus exercitus & instructus arte bellandi ad- versum Macedones dimicabit: sed veniet quasi grex paratus ad mortem, & Domino auxiliante supera- bit. Consentiunt etiam Pontificii Interpp. plerique omnes. Videatur paraphrasis, & Commentarius Christoph. à Castro, Cornelius à Lapide, Menochius, &c. Tirinus etsi de victoriis Maccabæorum inter- pretetur, frumentum tamen & vinum, sub finem ca- pitis, ad Sacramentum N. T. refert, adeoque agno- scere tenetur, etiam hæc (quia cohærent omnia) ad N. T. tempora pertinere. Calviniani Magistrum suum sectati hic itidem carnalia solum sapiunt, ut cum apud Calvinum, tum in paraphrasi Belgica, apud Piscatorem, Iunium, Willium, & alios videre est. Ab illis tamen recedit, nostræq; interpretationi suffra- gatur Coccejus: Ratio valida est, ut convertantur ad arcem, & in παῥῥησίᾳ ad Deum accedant, quia Deus decrevit utramq; domum Israelis adhibere, ut σκεῦ- ος ἐκλογῆς ad dilatationem regni sui. Quia arcus est in- strumentum subigendi hostes, proferendi imperii, igitur qui fiunt organa Dei ad amplificationem re- gni & demolitionem arcium, comparantur cum ar- cu sagittis instructo. Indicantur hic Apostoli im- primis, omnes tribus repræsentantes: tum etiam credentes ex omnibus tribubus: Filii Sionis exci- tabuntur contra filios Javan, h. e. mittentur præcones Evangelii ex Sione in Græciam maxime, ut illorum sa- pientiam & eloquentiam & potentiam confundant. Convenit hoc reliquis Prophetiis, quæ innuunt primam dilatationem regni Christi fore versus oc- cidentem, Genes. 9, 28. Esa. 42, 4. Ps. 72, 10. Idem docent eæ Prophetiæ, quæ monstrant Regnum Christo cum quarto imperio colluctaturum. Dan. 2. & 7. Nec immerito observat Coccejus p. 580. Chri- stum à Deo Patre, (qui hic loquens introducitur) designari voce Dominus Deus eorum. Salvator à Deo nominatur Dominus Deus illorum. Vide Esa. 40, 9. Non enim est alius Deus Ecclesiæ, nisi יהוה. Intelligitur Filius Dei, innuitur, ereptum & salva- tum iri Ecclesiam eam, quæ Filium recognoscit re- vera pro יהוה Deo suo. Sic refutantur hæreses Deitatem Christi etiam illo tempore abnegantes.

Vers. eod. QUIA LAPIDES SANCTI ELEVABUNTUR SUPER TERRAM EJUS]

In Hebræo: Lapides coro- næ, id est, corona ex lapidibus. Solent pastores lapides in orbem disponere, quo gregem includant, ne evage- tur.

## 9:17
Verse 17. FOR WHAT IS HIS GOOD, AND WHAT IS HIS BEAUTY, UNLESS THE CORN OF THE ELECT, AND THE WINE MAKING VIRGINS TO FLOURISH?]

In Hebrew there is no 'unless'. For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty [of the land? namely] corn shall come forth, and wine shall make virgins sing; so that ינובב יבב Young men shall sing a joyful song, because of the harvest, and the maidens of the countryside because of the happy vintage.

This is a new interpretation concerning a crown of stones enclosing a flock, so that it may not wander; others interpret it as a monument of victory, or as crown-stones, just as Willius, with Junius, understands trophies adorned with ribbons and made with crown-work: or whatever other monuments there may be, erected for the sake of victory. But those who are called נזר stones (the LXX and Vulgate render them 'holy') to be chosen upon the earth, Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Lyranus, and Dionysius, Castrius concerning

They explain as the Apostles, who have an eminent place in the spiritual building of the Church. To Winckelmann, the Apostles are stones erected and exalted, upon whose doctrine the Church is built: These stones, says B. Balduinus p. 63, are called אבני נזר in the Hebrew sources, which some interpret as stones of the crown, others as separated stones; in sum, they are select stones, by which the Apostles are understood, who were separated in this from the rest of the dregs of the populace, so that they might convert the nations to the Church. He says these were lifted up upon the land of the nations, that is, among them, as if established on high like a banner, to which those who are to return may look, and never follow any other doctrine than that which is engraved upon these as if they were select stones, that is, comprised in the Apostolic writings. The Vinarienses: For in his land (in his church) holy (chosen) stones shall be erected; the holy apostles shall be, with their preached and written word, the stones that are erected at crossroads, by which travelers guide themselves, so that they do not go astray, Eph. 2:20, 1 John 2:14. Osiander and others take it of any believers whatsoever, i.e., holy stones shall be erected upon his land, that is, a spiritual building shall be raised in the kingdom of Christ from holy stones, 1 Pet. 2. Similarly Cocceius p. 530. Crown-stones, or Gems, denote faithful men, whose light shines before men. Ezek. 28:14, in the midst of the stones of fire, i.e., you walked as carbuncles. These are in part those gems with which the great harlot adorns herself, Apoc. 17:4, compared with Ezek. 28:13.

Concerning the rest, Cocceius says thus: For what is his goodness, and what is his beauty? Corn (makes) young men (to flourish), and must makes virgins to flourish. He commends the excellence and beauty of the people, by a formula of one admiring, 'What' instead of 'How great'? They are young men and virgins, flourishing, blooming. The former by reason of the strength of faith, the latter by reason of chastity in judgment, by which they abstain from evil, Apoc. 14:4. The cause of this excellence is ascribed to the blessing of their corn and must, i.e., of doctrine and consolation, so that it may vivify and invigorate them. Antithesis Isa. 23:4. Corn and must are the goods of the Church, Ps. 4:8. Which are sounder than those things which have been handed down by other Calvinists, and here by Grotius, who, with the Jews, merely dreams of carnal things here. Of our own, who easily agree here, Osiander has properly expressed the sense: What good and excellent thing does the Church of God have before all other peoples? I will tell you: in the Church there is such food and drink, which does not beget infants who wail for a long time in cradles, and who can scarcely be raised with great trouble and over many years, so that they may become mature for marriage and for managing other affairs, (but the word of the Gospel, which is like the best grain and wine, when received by faith, begets such children who are immediately young men, and it begets virgin daughters, mature for marriage, that is, it makes men capable, who can give an account of their faith, and spiritually beget other children for Christ as well. Thus in the primitive Church many, who received the faith of Christ, were soon made pastors of the Church, so that they might spiritually beget more children for Christ. But even today (by the benefit of God) such examples can be shown, so that those who have recently emerged from Papistic darkness, having recognized the Gospel of Christ, soon happily preside over the Church of God by teaching) B. Luther in a marginal gloss: The Gospel is such a word that it does not beget children who lie in the cradle, but when they are begotten, they are young men and virgins, fit for marriage, that is, for honor, and to beget other spiritual children. Villius accuses him, along with St. Jerome, without cause, because they translated it awkwardly as 'wine germinating': that is, producing virgins. For he himself acknowledges this to be the primary meaning of the Hebrew word. Why, therefore, having abandoned that, should one turn to the metaphor with Junius, 'it will make them fruitful'? But who will deny that the sense is pious, and consonant with the analogy of Scripture, for explaining the efficacy of the Gospel? Jerome explains the grain and wine as Christ, who, namely, is proposed to us in the Gospel; others apply it specifically to the Eucharist, in which the body and blood of Christ are exhibited under bread and wine. I will add Titinus's interpretation, who in the preceding had gone in all other directions: FOR WHAT in all the heavenly treasures has God more good or beautiful, than that which He daily bestows upon them, GRAIN, or the bread OF THE ELECT? The Hebrew bachurim, the LXX, the Syriac, the Arabic, Vatablus, and Pagninus translate as 'of young men': namely, this bread makes select young men, strong, lively, flourishing, vivid, and ready for even all arduous tasks. AND WINE; in Hebrew, tiros, that is, must, which is at once sweet, potent, fervent, bubbling, and GERMINATING VIRGINS, namely, it makes them chaste, shining, beautiful, succulent, and distinguished by a vivid and rosy color, in one word, incorrupt and immortal: for virginal youth is a type of incorruption and immortality, says Jerome Pradus. By this grain and wine, the Hebrews, Theodoret, Sanchez, and Mariana understand the abundant temporal nourishment granted to the Jews. Albert and Hugo understand the spiritual nourishment of the Mosaic law sent down to them from heaven: Clarius, Vatablus, and Arias understand the law and the Evangelical doctrine. But most aptly of all, St. Jerome, Remigius, Paschasius, Haymo, Lyranus, Ribera, à Castro, à Lapide, and others everywhere, take it as the body and blood of Christ in the Eucharist, veiled by the species of bread and wine. For God has nothing more beautiful, nothing more noble, nothing better than this food, nor anything more effective for curbing the depraved motions and passions of the soul, for inducing chastity, liveliness, vigor, strength, the beauty of both the inner and outer man, vivacity and incorruption, and therefore also immortality. For he who eats this bread shall live forever, and shall be raised up on the last day. This is Tirinus. To which B. Pappus also adds his vote: In these words the sum of the former promises is repeated, and without doubt a glorious Mystery lies hidden here. For although only customary benefits seem to be described, namely that there will be many courageous Confessors in the Church, retaining an incorrupt faith: yet there is no doubt in my mind but that the Holy Spirit through the Prophet alludes to the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, in which there is truly exhibited to us grain making the young men flourish: and wine making the virgins flourish, that is, with the Bread and Wine, which are sacramental signs, there is exhibited to us the true body and blood of the Lord: by which our Faith is confirmed, and nourished unto the hope of resurrection and eternal life: so that the flesh and blood of the Lord, which are exhibited to us with the bread and wine, supply perpetual youth and virginity, that is, perpetual vigor.

SECTION II. EXHORTATORY.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QUID ENIM BONUM EJUS EST, ET QUID PULCHRUM EJUS, NISI FRUMENTUM ELECTORUM, ET VINUM GERMINANS VIRGI- NES?]

In Hebræo non est nisi. Quanta enim bonitas ejus, & quanta pulchritudo ejus [terræ? scilicet] frumentum pro- veniet, & vinum cantare faciet virgines; ut fic ינובב יבב Juvenes lætum carmen canent, ob messem, & puellæ ruris ob felicem vindemiam.

Nova hæc est interpretatio de corona lapidum gregem includente, ne evagetur; alii de monumento vi- ctoriæ interpretantur, sive ex lapidibus coronariis, uti cum Junio Willius trophea lemniscata, & opere coronario facta intelligit: seu quæcunque alia sint monumenta, victoriæ causa erecta. Qui vero la- pides נזר separati vocantur (LXX. & Vulgatus red- dunt sancti) eligendi super terram, Hieronymus, Theo- doretus, Remigius, Lyranus & Dionysius, Castrius de

Apostolis explicant, qui in ædificio spirituali Eccle- siæ locum habent eminentem. Winckelmanno Apo- stoli sunt lapides erecti & exaltati, super quorum doctrinam Ecclesiæ ædificatur: Lapides isti, inquit, B. Balduinus p. 63. in fontibus Hebræis vocantur אבני נזר, quod alii lapides coronæ, alii lapides se- paratos interpretantur, summa sunt apides selecti, per quos Apostoli intelliguntur, qui in hoc sepa- rati erant ex reliqua fece plebis, ut converterent gentes ad Ecclesiam. Hos elevatos esse dicit super terram gentium, id est, inter eos, quasi in sublimi constitutos instar vexilli, ad quod respiciant redi- turi, nec aliam unquam doctrinam sequantur, quam his veluti lapidibus selectis incisam, id est, scriptis Apostolicis comprehensam. Vinarienses: Denn es werden in seinem Lande (in seiner Kirche) heili- ge (ausserwehlete) Steine auffgerichtet werden, die heiligen Apostel sollen mit ihrem gepredigten und geschriebnen Wort seyn die Steine, so an Wegscheiden auffgerichtet sind, nach welchen sich die Wandersleute richten, damit sie nicht irre ge- hen, Eph. 2, 20. 1. Joh. 2, 14. Osiander, & alii de quibusvis fidelibus accipiunt h. m. lapides sancti e- rigentur super terram ejus, id est, excitabitur in regno Christi ædificium spirituale ex lapidibus sanctis 1. Petr. 2. Similiter Coccejus p. 530. Lapides coronarii, sive Gemmæ notant homines fideles, quo- rum lux lucet coram hominibus. Ezech. 28, 14. in medio lapidum ignis, q. d. carbunculorum ambulasti. Hæ sunt ex parte gemmæ istæ, quibus se ornat me- retrix magna Apoc. 17, 4. collato Ezech. 28, 13.

De cæteris Coccejus ita: Nam quæ est bonitas ejus, & quæ est pulchritudo ejus? Frumentum (facit vigere) juvenes, & mustum facit vigere virgines. Commendat præstantiam & pulchritudinem po- puli, formula admirantis Quæ pro Quanta? sunt juvenes & virgines, vigentes, florentes. Illud ratione roboris fidei, hoc ratione castitatis in judicio, quo se abstinent à malo Apoc. 14, 4. Causa hujus præ- stantiæ adscribitur benedictione frumenti & musti illorum, h. e. doctrinæ & consolationis, ut eos vivificet & vegetet. Antithesis Esa. 23, 4. Frumentum & mustum bona Ecclesiæ Pf. 4, 8. Quæ saniora sunt iis, quæ à Calvinianis aliis, & hic à Grotio, qui cum Judæis mere carnalia tantum hic somniat, tradita sunt. E nostris, qui hic facile consentiunt, sensum probe expressit Osiander: Quid habet Dei Ecclesia boni & præclari præ omnibus aliis populis? dicam tibi: in Ecclesia est talis cibus & potus, qui non generat infantes, qui diu in cunis vagiant, & magnis molestiis atq́; multis annis vix educari possint, ut maturi fiant conjugio, aliisq́; rebus gerendis, (sed verbum Evangelii, quod est instar optimi frumenti & vini fide susceptum tales filios gignit, qui statim sint juvenes, & gignit filias virgines, matrimonio maturas, hoc est, efficit homines idoneos, qui possint fidei suæ rationem reddere, & alios etiam filios spiritualiter Christo gignere. Sic in primitiva Ecclesia multi, qui Christi fidem susceperunt, mox dati sunt Ecclesiæ pastores, ut plures filios spirituales Christo generarent. Sed & hodie (Dei beneficio) talia exempla monstrari possunt, ut qui è Papisticis tenebris nuper emerserunt, agnito Christi Evangelio, mox Ecclesiæ Dei docendo feliciter præsint) B. Luther. in glossa marginali: Das Evangelium ist ein solch Wort, das nicht Kinder zeuget, die in der Wiegen ligen, sondern wenn sie gezeuget sind, sind sie Junggesellen und Jungfrauen, zur Ehe tüchtig, das ist, zu Ehren, und andere geistliche Kinder zu zeugen. Quem cum S. Hieronymo præter causam arguit Villius, quod inconcinne verterint vinum germinans: id est, producens virgines. Agnoscit enim ipse hanc esse primam verbi Ebræi significationem. Cur ergo ea relicta, ad metaphoram cum Junio divertendum, fœcundas faciet? Pium autem esse sensum, & analogiæ scripturæ consonum, ad efficaciam Evangelii explicandam, quis negabit? Hieronymus frumentum & vinum de Christo explicat, qui sc. in Evangelio nobis proponitur, alii specialiter ad Eucharistiam applicant, in qua sub pane & vino corpus & sanguis Christi exhibentur. Adscribam Titini interpretationem: qui in præcedentibus in alia omnia iverat: QUID ENIM in omnibus cœlestibus thesauris bonum aut pulchrum magis habet De⁹, quam quod illis quotidie largitur FRUMENTUM, seu panem ELECTORUM? Hebræum bachurim LXX. Syrus, Arabicus, Vatablus & Pagninus vertunt, juvenum: nempe panis hic facit selectos juvenes, validos, alacres, florentes, vividos, ad omnia etiam ardua expeditos. ET VINUM; Hebraice, tiros, id est, mustum, quod simul est suave, potens, fervens, ebulliens, & GERMINANS VIRGINES, nempe facit castos, nitentes, speciosos, succulentos vivido roseoq́; colore insignes, verbo uno, incorruptos & immortales: virginalis enim juventa typus est incorruptionis & immortalitatis, inquit Hieronymus Pradus. Per hoc frumentum & vinum, Hebræi, Theodorectus, Sanchez & Mariana intelligunt uberem alimoniam temporalem Judæis concessam. Albertus & Hugo alimoniam spiritualem legis Mosaicæ iisdem cœlitus submissam: Clarius, Vatablus, & Arias legem & doctrinam Evangelicam. Sed omnium aptissime S. Hieronymus, Remigius, Paschasius, Haymo, Lyranus, Ribera, à Castro, à Lapide, & alii passim, corpus & sanguinem Christi in Eucharistia accipiunt velatum speciebus panis & vini. Hoc enim alimento nihil pulchrius, nihil nobilius, nihil melius habet Deus, nihil etiam efficacius, ad pravos animi motus passionesque compescendas, ad castitatem, alacritatem, vigorem, robur, pulchritudinem utriusque hominis, vivacitatem & incorruptionem, adeoq; & immortalitatem inducendam. Qui enim manducat hunc panem, vivet in æter- num, & refuscitabitur in novissimo die. Hæc Ti- rinus. Quibus calculum etiam adjicit B. Pappus: His verbis repetitur summa priorum promissionum, & latet hic sine dubio præclarum Mysterium. Etsi e- nim usitata tantum beneficia describi videntur, quod in Ecclesia multi futuri sint animosi Confessores, & fidem incorruptam retinentes: tamen non dubium mihi quidem, quin Spiritus S. per Prophetam allu- dat ad Sacramentum Cœnæ Dominicæ, in quo revera nobis exhibetur frumentum germinans adolescentes: & vinum germinans virgines, hoc est, cum Pane & Vino, quæ sunt signa sacramentalia, exhibetur no- bis verum corpus & sanguis Domini: quibus Fides nostra confirmatur, & alitur ad spem resurrectionis & vitæ æternæ: ita ut perpetuam adolescentiam & virginitatem, hoc est, perpetuum vigorem caro & san- guis Domini, quæ nobis cum pane & vino exhiben- tur, suppeditent.

SECTIO II. PARÆNETICA.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

Exhortation to the worship of the one GOD.

They are commanded to entreat from the Lord the rain of spiritual blessing, since idols are vain and false prophets are useless comforters, and Pastors are to be visited by the Lord in anger: with the addition of a promise of giant-like strength, protection, gathering, and increase, as well as the humiliation of the Assyrian and Egyptian enemies, and strengthening in the Lord.

Seek rains with prayers: the Lord will punish the he-goats evilly, He will strengthen those who return, the wicked scepter shall cease.

Ver. 1.

ASK OF THE LORD RAIN IN THE LATTER SEASON] Lest those magnificent promises which preceded should be believed to be about to happen to those living in any manner whatsoever, the Prophet adds that they are to be expected in their own time only if the Jews, and those from other tribes who had joined themselves to them, worshipped God and prayed: but when they should again relapse into their old faults, evils such as before would be at hand. The latter rain to the Hebrews is that which promotes the crop already grown. By the word of one species, however, the whole genus is understood, that is, prosperous things of any kind.

HE WILL MAKE SNOWS] The prayers of trees and crops are common, that snows may remain for a long time, Pliny XVII. 2, where he also gives the reasons.

AND HE WILL GIVE THEM THE RAIN OF THE SHOWER] That is, a plentiful one.

TO EVERY ONE HERB IN THE FIELD] עשב is so general to the Hebrews that it includes those things which are in human diet. The sense is, that God will give crops, both those which are suitable for man, and those which are suitable for animals that provide their use to man.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Adhortatio ad unius DEI cultum.

Iubentur exorare à Domino pluviam spiritua- lis benedictionis, quum idola vana sint & falsi Prophetæ inutiles consolatores, ac Pastores, à Domino in ira visitandi: ad- dita promissione gigantei roboris, prote- ctionis, collectionis & auctionis, nec non humiliationis hostium Assyriorum & Æ- gyptiorum, & confortationis in Domino.

Quære imbres precibus: Dominus male puniet hædos, Firmabit reduces, Sceptrum cessabit iniquum.

Vers. 1.

PETITE A DOMINO PLUVIAM IN TEM- PORE SEROTINO] Ne magnifica illa, quæ præcesse- runt promissa crederentur eventura quovis modo viventi- bus, addit Propheta, ita demum ea suo tempore exspe- ctanda, si Judæi, & qui ex aliis tribubus eis se adjunxe- rant, Deum colerent, ac precarentur: ubi vero iterum relaberentur ad veteres culpas, præsto fore mala, qualia an- tea. Pluvia serotina Hebræis est, quæ segetem jam adul- tam promovet. Unius autem speciei vocabulo genus to- tum intelligitur, id est, res prosperæ qualescunque.

FACIET NIVES] Vota arborum communia sunt, frugumque, nives diutinas sedere, Plin. XVII. 2. ubi & causas reddit.

ET PLUVIAM IMBRIS DABIT EIS] Id est, largam.

SINGULIS HERBA IN AGRO] עשב Hebræis tam generale est, ut ea, quæ in humano sunt victu compre- hendat. Sensus est, Deum daturum fruges, tum quæ homini, tum quæ animantibus usum suum homini præ- bentibus conveniunt.

## 10:2
Verse 2.

BECAUSE THE IMAGES HAVE SPOKEN WHAT IS USELESS] Vain are the things which the Priests answer in the name of idols. All these things are repeated for this reason, that the Jews may beware for themselves in the future.

AND THE DREAMERS HAVE SPOKEN VANITY] The diviners have spoken falsely. קוסמים is usually rendered in Greek as μάντεις, but in Isaiah III. 2 as ςοχαταί.

THEY WERE COMFORTING IN VAIN]

THEREFORE THEY HAVE BEEN LED AWAY]

AS A FLOCK] As easily as cattle are driven.

THEY SHALL BE AFFLICTED, BECAUSE THERE IS NO SHEPHERD FOR THEM] They have been ill-treated, there being no prince for them. By the name of shepherds, both Kings and Princes are understood here, as the Chaldean explains.

He has followed here again, and in the whole chapter, the Jews, who explain these things concerning fertility and temporal prosperity, and refer them to the times of the Maccabees, to which most Calvinists also add their own calculation. Our Doctors, if we perhaps except Tarnovius, interpret them concerning spiritual rain and the leading to the faith, and judge that the times of the New Testament are being looked at, whose opinion, as is evident from the explanation of the previous chapter, since the same discourse and preaching is continued here, can be confirmed not only from similar forms of speaking occurring in Scripture, but also from certain promises in this prophecy, which must necessarily be explained concerning the time of the New Testament. Whence Jerome, Cyril, Remigius, Rupert, Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus, Clarius, and others have interpreted this prophecy concerning the time of the New Testament. There are those among the Papists who join both senses, and make one literal concerning temporal happiness and the victories of the Maccabees, and the other spiritual concerning conversion to the Gospel, which kind of double interpretation Castrius the Jesuit attributes even to Jerome, but wrongly: But although Jerome, asserting the sense concerning spiritual fertility and the time of the New Testament according to tropology, teaches that it should be explained in that way, yet that sense itself is not different from the literal sense, expressly intended by the Holy Spirit, but is called tropological, because the words are to be understood tropically in that way, but he does not approve of another sense, which the literal meaning properly accepted introduces, but rejects it in the Jews; nay, he even observes that among some Jews an interpretation concerning Christ is received. And in this place, he says, there is a twofold exposition of the Jews, for some think that all things are to be fulfilled at the coming of Christ, others that they have already been fulfilled under the Maccabees. Our people (Christians) refer these things to the times of persecution: And afterwards he rejects the carnal sense at verse 8. We do not accept the multiplication and blessing of children carnally, otherwise Elijah and Elisha, and Jeremiah, and John the Baptist, than whom there was no greater among those born of women, lacked this blessing, but [we accept] that by which the multitudes of the nations are called to the faith. He also urges this against such a carnal sense: that we seek in vain when Judah and Israel fought equally against the Greeks, or at what time Ephraim returned from the Assyrian captivity. And at verse 11. He called the sense of the Jews concerning a bodily return a killing letter to be abandoned by Christians. But we, who are counted by the name of Christ, abandon the killing letter, and follow the life-giving spirit, nay, we compare spiritual things with spiritual. And Castrius himself is forced to acknowledge that this was the mind of Jerome in his Commentary, even though he pronounced otherwise about him in the argument of the chapter: where he explains what rain they are commanded to ask for: Hebr. ask of the Lord rain in the time, the latter rain, the Septuagint thought that both rains were being requested, the early and the latter: the former [they called] opportune or morning [rain]. This they called the latter. The Vulgate and other interpreters think that only the late rain is sought, which falls opportunely if it satisfies the desire: for this puts the crown on the wine, and applies the finishing touch, and although many think that the discourse is about temporal happiness, and on the occasion of grain and wine, now rain is requested to ripen the crops, lest the Jews recur to idols, about to request it, as Theodoret, Haymo, Albert, and Hugh assert, yet Jerome, Remigius, Rupert, Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus, Isidore, and Robert explain the rain as the Evangelical doctrine, which is called late, perfecting and leading to the end and to maturity the crops of virtues, since the old law was the morning or temporary doctrine, which makes the sown seeds germinate: as Cyril notes here. For Moses shows that doctrine is signified by the name of rain through a metaphor, Deut. 32, 1.

While he says: Let my doctrine drop as the rain, let my speech flow as the dew. Whence also the Prophets are said to distill. This is Castrius. Although, however, the latter and former rain are otherwise opposed in Deut. 11:14, Jer. 5:24, Hos. 7:3, Joel 2:23, yet the former is called then יורה, while here is held בעת rain IN THE TIME of the latter, or as Pagninus, at the opportune time of the latter. That this is to be understood here of spiritual rain, even some of the Calvinists acknowledge, especially Coccejus: Here is to be understood the doctrine, to be sought from the mouth of God, that is, from the scriptures in which He speaks. Cf. Deut. 32:2, Job 29:22, 23. By a similar metaphor the Prophets are called מטיפים distilling, bedewing, Mic. 2:6, 10, and Apollos ποτίζων. This is he. But especially to be compared here is Ps. 68:10. Thou shalt set apart a voluntary rain, O God, for thine inheritance: as also Is. 65:10. As the rain and the snow descend from heaven and do not return thither, but inebriate the earth and water it, and make it to germinate, and give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater, so shall the word be that shall go forth from my mouth, it shall not return to me void, but shall do whatsoever I have willed and shall prosper in those things to which I sent it. Nor could Willius deny this sense here, judging that under the type of corporal promises, spiritual ones are understood at the same time. But thus a double sense would have to be admitted. However, it is necessary that there be only a single sense of the same saying. And such grain and wine as is promised to germinate for young men and virgins in the preceding words, such also is the rain to be sought from God. But that was only spiritual.

What the Vulgate rendered SNOWS, in Hebrew is חזיזים, which Coccejus in Job 38:25 explains as lightnings. Willius from the same place and Job 28:26 [calls them] coruscations of the clouds, Junius [calls them] storms, the Targum [calls them] winds, the LXX [calls them] Φαντασίας, concerning which version Jerome does not know who ought to judge; Cyril and Theodoret explain them by lightnings, because they terrify those who see them, or because they appear suddenly; B. Luther rendered the Hebrew as Gewolcke. The Talmudists, as Pagninus notes, say this is one of the names of a cloud, whence some render: The Lord will make bright clouds, and thus they think Jerome translated it here, as do Pagninus and the Complutensian Dictionary. That the Vulgate translation is inconvenient appears from this, that although long-lasting snows are useful for seeds cast into the earth, they are of no use at the time of harvest and summer. See Jer. 26:1. Whether therefore the Apostles (and other Doctors) are called clouds with Castrius, which with the thunder of the word and divine irradiations disperse the water of the Gospel, or whether the irradiation and coruscation of scripture is compared to lightning, it is certain that the discourse is about the fruit of the word, to which is opposed false doctrine, by which those who were seduced were led into the Babylonian captivity: Thus Jerome: Ask of the Lord, that he may give you the latter rain: that Christ, who was promised, may come and grant you dews and snows: for which it is written in Hebrew: חזיזים. And I know not what the seventy intended by interpreting them as phantasies, unless perhaps they wished to describe the magnitude of grace and the admiration of the gifts by the name of phantasy. The Lord therefore, who is about to make snows, and is about to irrigate the dryness of all the earth with the rain of evangelical preaching: He himself will give showers to the believers, and all things will be filled with abundance: so that after the nations have believed in Christ, they may understand that those things which they worshipped before are vain. Or Israel himself may understand, who was once deceived and held by the errors of idolatry, that he had worshipped idols in vain: and had heard the lies of diviners, and had acquiesced in dreams, which scripture commands not to be believed. And for this cause they were led like a flock into captivity: and were afflicted without a shepherd from God, because they did not have the knowledge of the law. And St. Cyril: One must therefore attend not to liars and flatterers and dreamers speaking vain things, but rather to God, who flashes the light of true divine cognition into the soul, and sends down intelligible rains, I say, the consolations of the Holy Spirit, and produces grass for the rustics, which is as if feeding in the greenest grass, in the knowledge of scripture which is subject to no reproach and is divinely inspired. We add from our own B. Winckelmann: Ask of the Lord rain) He addresses the daughter of Zion and the daughter of Jerusalem, that is, the Church, and because in the previous chapter he prophesied about the preaching of the Gospel in the whole world, he wants the Church to pray that it may be preached with fruit. Evangelical doctrine is compared with the latter rain, because just as this refreshes crops born in the spring time when there is great heat, and makes them grow briskly, so also the doctrine of the Gospel consoles, raises up, and exhilarates consciences terrified by the power of the Holy Spirit. And the Lord shall make clouds) The Hebrew word chofizim signifies lightnings, which follow rains: He speaks, however, about a desired and fruitful storm. Rain of the shower) That is, abundant rain. To every herb) Metaphorically he understands the increase and much fruit of the preached Gospel. Because the idols have spoken) He opposes false doctrine to Evangelical doctrine, by which false teachers try to hinder the course of the Gospel. He posits three kinds of false Doctors. The first is that of the idolaters, not so much those who exercise and defend gross idolatry, as those who teach men to place their trust in external ceremonies, sacrifices, and works, but in vain. 2. Of diviners and dreamers, of which kind there were in the people before the Babylonian captivity, and perhaps afterwards are also understood all those who deceive men even with feigned and vain promises and threats. 3. Vain consolers, who speak to the pleasure of men, or involve the truth in lies, and detain men so that they do not receive the truth.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

QUIA SIMULACRA LOCUTA SUNT INUTI- LE] Vana sunt, quæ idolorum nomine respondent Sacer- dotes. Hæc omnia ideo repetuntur, ut imposterum ca- veant sibi Judæi.

ET SOMNIATORES LOCUTI SUNT FRU- STRA] Divini falsa locuti sunt. קוסמים Græce reddi solet μάντεις, at Esa. III. 2. ςοχαταί.

VANE CONSOLABANTUR] In mediis pecca- tis prospera spondebant populo Ezech. 13, 9. 10.

ICCIRCO ABDUCTI SUNT] Judæi.

QUASI GREX] Tam facile quam pecudes agun- tur.

AFFLIGENTUR, QUIA NON EST EIS PA- STOR] Male tractati sunt, nullo ipsis existente principe. Pa- storum nomine hic tum Reges tum Principes intelli- guntur, ut Chaldæus explicat.

SEquutus hic iterum, & in toto capite Judæos est, qui de fertilitate ac prosperitate temporali hæc exponunt, & ad tempora Maccabæorum refe- runt, quibus calculum suum etiam adjiciunt Calvi- niani plerique. Nostri Doctores, si Tarnovium forte excipiamus, de pluvia spirituali, & deductione ad fi- dem interpretantur, & tempora N. T. spectari censent, quorum sententia, uti è superioris ca- pitis, quum hîc eadem concio & prædicatio conti- nuetur, explicatione constat, ita non solum è simili- bus loquendi formulis, in Scriptura occurrentibus confirmari potest, sed etiam è promissionibus qui- busdam in hoc vaticinio, quæ necessario de tempo- re N. T. explicandæ sunt. Unde hoc vaticinium de tempore N. Test. interpretati sunt Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Remigius, Rupertus, Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus, Clarius, & alii. Sunt qui è Ponti- ficiis utrumque sensum conjungunt, & alterum de temporali felicitate, ac victoriis Maccabæorum li- teralem faciunt, alterum de conversione ad Evan- gelium spiritualem, cujusmodi geminam interpre- tationem etiam Hieronymo, at perperam tribuit Ca- strius Jesuita: Sed quamquam Hieronymus sensum de spirituali fertilitate ac tempore N. T. adserens juxta tropologiam ita explicari doceat, non tamen is sensus ipse est diversus à literali sensu, diserte à Sp. S.intento, sed tropologicus dicitur, quia verba tro- pice ita intelligenda sunt, sensum autem alium, quem τό ῥητὸν proprie acceptum infert, non pro- bat, sed in Judæis reprobat, imo observat etiam a- pud Judæos nonnullos receptam esse interpreta- tionem de Christo. Et in hoc loco, duplex est, inquit, Iu- dæorum expositio, alii enim arbitrantur in adventu Christi universa complenda, alii sub Maccabæis jam esse completa. Nostri (Christiani) hæc ad persecutionis tempora referunt: Et postea carnalem sensum rejicit ad v. 8. Multiplicationem & benedictionem libero- rum non accipimus carnaliter, alioquin Helia & He- lisæus, & Jeremias, & Johannes Baptista, quo major inter natos mulierum non fuit, hac benedictione carue- runt, sed illam, qua vocantur ad fidem multitudines nationum. Urget etiam hoc adversus carnalem e- jusmodi sensum: quod frustra quæramus, quando Judas & Israel adversus Græcos pariter dimicarint, vel quo tempore Ephraim de captivitate Assyriaca sit reversus. Et ad v. 11. Sensum Judæorum de corporali reditu occidentem literam vocavit à Christianis relin- quendam. Cæterum nos, qui Christi censemur nomine, occidentem relinquimus literam, & sequimur spiritum vivificantem, imo spiritualia spiritualibus compara- mus. Et hanc mentem fuisse Hieronymi agnoscere in Commentario cogitur ipse Castrius, etsi aliter de ipso in argumento capitis pronunciavit: ubi expli- cat, quamnam pluviam jubeantur petere: Hebr. petite à Domino pluviam in tempore, pluviam seroti- nam, Septuaginta putarunt utramque pluviam po- stulari temporaneam & serotinam: illam opportu- nam seu matutinam. Hanc serotinam vocaverunt. Vulgatus & cæteri interpretes solam serotinam peti putant, quæ opportune cadit, si desiderio satisfa- ciat: nam hæc coronam imponit vino, & ultimam manum adhibet, & quamvis multi putent de felici- tate temporali sermonem esse, & occasione fru- menti & vini, nunc postuletur pluvia maturans sege- tes, ne Judæi ad idola recurrant, postulaturi, ut Theo- doretus, Haymo, Albertus & Hugo asserunt, at Hieronǯ- mus, Remigius, Rupertus, Lyra, Vatablus, Montanus, Isodorus & Robertus pluviam exponunt doctrinam Evangelicam, quæ serotina dicitur perficiens, & ad fi- nem deducens, & ad maturitatem segetes virtutum, cum vetus lex fuerit doctrina matutina seu tempo- raria, quæ jacta semina germinare facit: ut notat hic Cyrillus. Nam doctrinam pluviæ nomine per metaphoram significari ostendit Moyses Deut. 32, 1.

Dum ait: Concrescat in pluviam doctrina mea, fluat ut ros eloquium meum. Unde & Prophetæ dicun- tur stillare. Hæc Castrius. Quanquam autem a- liàs pluvia serotina & tempestiva opponantur Deu- ter. 11,14. Jer. 5, 24. Hos. 7,3. Joel. 2, 23. illa tamen vocatur tum יורה hic vero habetur בעת pluvia IN TEMPORE serotina, vel ut Pagninus, oportu- no tempore serotina. Quam de spirituali pluvia hic intelligendam esse, etiam è Calvinianis nonnulli agnoscunt,imprimis Coccejus: Hic intelligenda do- ctrina, petenda ex ore Dei, hoc est, ex scripturis in quibus loquitur.Conf. Deut. 32, 2. Job. 29, 22. 23. simili metaphora Prophetæ appellantur מטיפים stillantes, rorantes Mich. 2, 6. 10. & Apollos ποτί- ζων. Hæc ille. Sed imprimis etiam conferen- dus hic Psal, 68,10. Pluviam voluntariam segregabis Deus hæreditati tuæ: ut & Es. 65,10. Quomodo descen- dit imber & nix de cælo & illuc non revertitur, sed inebriat terram & infundit eam, & germinare facit eam, & dat semen serenti, & panem comedenti, sic e- rit verbum, quod egredietur de ore meo, non reverie- tur ad me vacuum, sed faciet quæcunq; volui & pro- sperabitur in his, ad quæ misi illud. Neque hunc sensum dissiteri hic potuit Willius, sub typo promis- sionum corporalium simul spirituales intelligi censens. Sed ita geminus sensus admittendus esset. Oportet autem ejusdem dicti unicum tantum esse sensum. Et quale frumentum ac vinum juvenes & virgines germinans promissum est verbis præcedentibus,ta- lis etiam pluvia à Deo petenda est. Illud autem spirituale tantum erat.

Quod vulgatus reddidit NIVES,in Ebr. est חזיזים, quod Job. 38,25. expo- nitCoccejusfulgetra.Willius ex eodem loco &Job. 28, 26. Coruscationes nubium, Junius nimbos, Tar. gum ventos, LXX. Φαντασίας, de qua versione ne- scit Hieronymus,qui judicare debeat, Cyrillus & The- odoretus explicant per fulgura, quod videntes ter- reant, aut quod subito appareant: B. Lutherus E- bræum reddidit Gewolcke. Talmudici,notante Pa- gnino,hoc unum esse dicunt è nominibus nubis,unde nonnulli reddunt: Dominus faciet nubes candidas, atque ita hic vertisse Hieronymum putant Pagni- nus,& Complutense Dictionarium. Incommodam autem esse translationem vulgatam hinc apparet, quod etsi nives diutinæ commodæ seminibus sint in terram projectis, tempore messis tamen & æsta- tis minime prosunt. Vide Jer. 26, 1. Sive ergo Apostoli (& alii Doctores) cum Castrio nubes dican- tur, quæ cum tonitru verbi, & divinis irradiationibus aquam Evangelii dispergunt, sive fulguri compare- tur irradiatio & coruscatio scripturæ, certum est de verbi fructu sermonem esse,cui opponitur falsa do- ctrina, qua seducti in captivitatem Babylonicam re- dacti sunt: Ita Hieronymus: Petite à Domino, ut det vobis pluviam serotinam: ut Christus,qui promis- sus est, veniat & tribuat vobis rores & nives : pro qui- bus scriptum est in Hebræo: חזיזים. Et nescio quid vo- lentes septuaginta phantasias interpretati sunt, nisi forte magnitudinem gratiæ admirationemq́; donorum, nomine phantasiæ voluere describere. Dominus ergo, qui facturus est nives, & siccitatem omnis terræ evan- gelicæ prædicationis irrigaturus est pluviis: ipse dabit imbres credentibus,& ubertate omnia complebuntur: ut postquam in Christo crediderint nationes,intelli- gant vana esse, quæ antea coluerunt. Sive ipse Israel intelligat, qui quondam deceptus idololatriæ erroribus tenebatur, frustra se coluisse simulachra: & divino- rum audisse mendacia, & acquievisse somniis, quibus scriptura præcipit non credendum. Et ob hanc cau- sam ducti sunt quasi grex in captivitatem: & afflicti absq́; pastore Deo, quia legis notitiam non habebant. Et S. Cyrillus: Attendendum igitur non loquentibus vana mendacibusq́;, & assentatoribus, & somniato- ribus, sed Deo potius, lumine veræ cognitionis divinæ in animum coruscati, & pluvias intellectiles, Spiri- tus Sancti consolationes, inquam, demittenti, & her- bam agrestibus producenti, quod est velut in viridissi- ma herba,in cognitione nulli reprehensioni obnoxiæ, ac divinitus inspiratæ scripturæ pascenti. Addimus è nostris B.Winckelmannum: Petite à Domino plu- viam) Alloquitur filiam Sion & filiam Hierusalem, hoc est, Ecclesiam,& quia superiori capite vaticinatus est de prædicatione Evangelii in mundo universo, vult Ecclesiam orare, ut cum fructu prædicetur. Confer- tur doctrina Evangelica cum pluvia serotina, quia quemadmodum hæc fruges verno tempore enatas, cum magnus æstus est, reficit, & facit ut alacriter cre- scant, ita etiam doctrina Evangelii virtute Spiritus Sancti perterrefactas conscientias consolatur, erigit & exhilarat. Et Dominus faciet nubes) Hebræa vox chofizim fulgura significat, quæ sequuntur plu- viæ: Loquitur autem de tempestate optata & frugi- fera. Pluviam imbris) Id est, abundantem plu- viam. Singulis herbis) μεταφορικῶς intelligit incrementum & fructum multum prædicati Evange- lii. Quia simulacra locuta) Doctrinæ Evangelicæ opponit falsam doctrinam, qua cursum Evangelii impedire conantur falsi doctores. Tria autem ponit falsorum Doctorum genera. Primum est idolola- trarum, non tam eorum, qui crassam idololatriam exercent & propugnant, quam illorum, qui docent ho- mines in externis ceremoniis, sacrificiis & operibus fi- duciam ponere, sed frustra. 2. Divinatorum & somniatorum, cujusmodi fuerunt in populo ante ca- ptivitatem Babylonicam, & fortasse postea etiam in- telliguntur omnes isti, qui etiam fictis & vanis promis- sis atq́; comminationibus homines decipiunt. 3. Va- ni consolatores, qui loquuntur ad placitum homi- num, vel veritatem mendaciis involvunt, hominesq́; detinent, ne veritatem recipiant.

## 10:3
Verse 3.

MY FURY IS KINDLED AGAINST THE SHEPHERDS] That is, I am implacably angry with the Kings and Princes, because they had been leaders to the people in idolatry: therefore I also willed that the sons of the king and other princes be killed by the Chaldeans: but King Zedekiah, blinded of his eyes, finally to die without offspring 2 Kings 25:7, 19, 20.

AND UPON THE GOATS I WILL VISIT ] The Greeks [say] ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀμνοὺς ἐπισκέψομαι, not badly: for by עתודים, that is, goats, synecdochically here is understood the whole flock, and by the flock the people. Moreover, 'I will visit' in this place signifies 'I will have mercy.' I sent destruction upon the Kings and Princes: but I willed the people indeed to be oppressed, but not to be rooted out entirely, so that at some time, seeing themselves deceived by the kings and princes, they might return to their fatherland by divine aid, and be more cautious in the future.

These things were said concerning the future, not the past. And therefore they are wrongly explained by Grotius as if spoken against Zedekiah, his sons, and his princes. The Jews, as Jerome notes, refer them to the times of the Maccabees. Some, however, as we observed from the same [author] before, acknowledge that these were to be fulfilled at the coming of Christ. The former sense of the Jews having been recounted, Jerome adds: 'Our people refer these to the times of persecution, because for the vice of the priests the people are also frequently handed over to adversaries: and yet the Lord Almighty will afterwards visit his flock, the house of Judah: who confesses God both in speech and in spirit, and will place them as the horse of his glory in war, of which the saints say: Ascend upon your horses, and your riding is salvation. He himself will be also the bow of the fury of the Lord, of which he says: He inebriates my arrows with blood. And again: my arrows shall consume them.' Concerning this bow and these arrows we read in the seventh [psalm]: He has bent his bow and prepared it: And in it he has prepared the vessels of death: he has made his arrows burning. Deut. 32. Psal. 7. AND THEY SHALL TREAD DOWN, he says, their adversaries in martyrdom and they will say: The Lord is my light, and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life, of whom shall I be afraid? Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh. My enemies that trouble me have themselves been weakened, and have fallen: if camps in consist against me, my heart shall not fear: if battle should rise up against me, in this will I hope. When that saying shall be fulfilled: one of you shall chase a thousand, and two shall put many thousands to flight Ps. 26. Furthermore, by shepherds it is not necessary that we understand kings and princes of the people, but as the Lord spoke concerning the idolatrous and divining false prophets, by whom the Jews were seduced before the Babylonian captivity, so now concerning the evil shepherds in the time of the New Testament, at which time they ought to have expected the timely rain of evangelical doctrine and a joyful harvest of corn and wine, He threatens that He will visit the same in anger, which Cyril interprets concerning the false prophets and masters of error, and blessed Luther and others of ours interpret concerning the Pharisees, who observe that the same are also called he-goats on account of the tyranny which they exercised over the consciences of men with their impure doctrines. And whoever may be understood by the he-goats, they are certainly not exempted here from punishment, but are said to be visited with the shepherds by a visitation of anger, which appears even from the very tenor of the words: my fury is kindled against the shepherds, and I will visit upon the he-goats. But there is another visitation, which is subsequently subjoined: for that one was about to visit the enemies of the Church in anger, the evil shepherds and impure he-goats, who were ruining it: but this one is about to visit graciously the house of Judah, His flock: about to fight against His enemies. Thus we have a visitation in a bad sense or of anger Exod. 20, 15. Isa. 27, 1. Jer. 51, 47. and in a good sense or of grace Exod. 3, 16. c. 4, 3. Willius, whose private opinion this is, wishes the divine judgments against the impious shepherds of the people, the Pharisees and kings, and their cause, the seduction of the shepherds v. 2, to be described, thinking that these were fulfilled in the time of Alexander, brother of King Aristobulus and Queen Alexandra, and their successors.

BECAUSE THE LORD OF HOSTS HATH VISITED HIS FLOCK] Now the Prophet is introduced, now God speaking. Here the Prophet proves that these things were most truly said by God. He hath visited, that is, He hath had mercy, as we have said.

THE HOUSE OF JUDAH] Which, of course, was to be understood by those he-goats, or, which is the same thing, the flock, in the preceding words of God.

AND HATH SET THEM AS THE HORSE OF HIS GLORY IN BATTLE] That He might at some time, namely in the times of Antiochus and thereafter, use those Jews, just as kings are accustomed to have horses reserved for battles.

The Lord speaks of the Lord, the Lord speaking is God the Father, as is concluded in v. 12 of the chapter: THE LORD SAITH. The Lord of whom He Himself speaks, whom He commands to be invoked: ASK YE OF THE LORD rain and THE LORD shall make snows, and whose visitation He promises, THE LORD OF HOSTS hath visited, is the Son of God, that Shepherd promised in Isa. 40. Ezech.

34. who was about to visit His flock. Grotius, along with the Jews, refers these and the following to the times of Antiochus, but most things are so constituted that they cannot be drawn to that. Willius, when he has referred the preceding to the times of the Jewish Kings Aristobulus, Alexander, and Alexandra, which followed after the fates of the Maccabees, is forced to acknowledge here that such excellent complements of the benefits of God are not found after the Maccabees, and therefore he turns back in turn, and interprets these concerning benefits past and already conferred upon the Church before. Whence it sufficiently appears that his analysis does not cohere, and does not at all agree with the course of times and the series of history which he himself had preconceived in his mind. But rightly Franc. Junius notes in this, that he himself refers these words to the enemies, that they were disposed as the horses of his glory in battle, and proceeded with their instruments from God, that they trampled upon the Jews, and fought with divine aid and put to shame the riders of the horses. For it is too manifest that they embrace a more illustrious assistance and exaltation of God than could pertain to enemies, whence Willius prefers, with all others, both Greek and Hebrew interpreters, both ancient and recent, to take it concerning the benefits of God to the Church, which benefits, however, he himself wrongly refers, likewise with the Jews, to the times of the O.T. under the Maccabees, since, as is evident from the preceding and the immediately antecedent, and as the following will more fully teach, they are to be understood concerning the times of the N.T. But the Prophet promises, as Osiander rightly says, that better Teachers are to be substituted in the place of those he-goats. Who hath visited (the past for the future) the Lord of hosts His flock, the house of Judah: He will kindly undertake the care of His Church, and will give to it faithful and excellent shepherds, and hath set: more correctly: He will set them as Teachers, as the horse of His glory in battle: i.e., He will instruct His Apostles with the admirable gifts of the Holy Spirit, and through them, as through noble horses fit for battle, He will conquer the minds of the peoples, so that they may submit themselves to the Gospel of Christ. (For excellent Ministers of the Church are like noble horses, by which Christ is carried when He subjects the world to His spiritual empire, but that they are ministers fit for that purpose, that they have from Christ, not from themselves. B. Balduinus: Those whom they considered as the simplest asses, and led around by the nose, as it were, with their illusions and dreams, the Lord will use as most glorious horses, with whom He will also display Himself in His Church, and endowed with the same spirit of wisdom and discernment, He will fight against those impostors. Similarly, Cyril, having rejected the gloss of the Jews: 'He will make him like a comely and most warlike horse, by whom, as if carried spiritually, he will attack the language of the Greeks, as I have said, and will lay open the deformity of their wisdom and the emptiness of all their fruit.' For who would doubt that through the dispersions of the Greeks the divine disciples were like certain horses, all but neighing against their loquacity and their fallacy, which is hateful to God? Since Christ says concerning blessed Paul to Ananias: 'Go, for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles and kings, and the children of Israel.' And Habakkuk, as if addressing our Lord Jesus Christ: 'For you will ascend upon your horses and your riding is salvation,' etc.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

SUPER PASTORES IRATUS EST FUROR MEUS] Id est, Regibus & Principibus implacabiliter ira- tus sum, quia illi ad idololatriam duces populo fuerant: itaque & filios regis & principes alios interimi à Chaldæis volui: Regem vero Sedeciam orbatum oculis, tandem mo- ri sine prole 2. Reg. 25,7. 19. 20.

ET SUPER HIRCOS VISITABO ] Græci ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀμνοὺς ἐπισκέψομαι, non male: nam per עתודים, id est, hircos, συνεκδοχικῶς hic intelligitur grex omnis, & per gregem populus. Visitabo autem hoc loco valet miserebor. Regibus & Principibus excidium immisi: at populum premi quidem volui, sed non radicitus exstiripari, ut ali- quando videns se à regibus & principibus deceptum, divi- na ope in patriam rediret, & cautior esset in posterum.

Hæc de futuris dicta sunt, non de præteritis. Ideoque perperam à Grotio ceu adversus Sede- kiam,ejus filios & principes dicta explicantur. Ju- dæi,notante Hieronymo,ad tempora Maccabæorum referunt. Nonnulli tamen, quod ex eodem antea observavimus, in adventu Christi hæc complenda fuisse agnoscunt. Priori Judæorum sensu recen- sito, addit Hieronymus: Nostri hæc ad persecutionis tempora referunt,quod pro vitio sacerdotum frequen- ter etiam populus tradatur adversariis: & tamen Do- minus omnipotens visitet postea gregem suum domum Juda: qui Deum & sermone & animo confitetur, & ponat eos quasi equum gloriæ suæ in bello, de quo san- cti dicunt: Ascende super equos tuos, & equitatio tua salus. Ipse erit & arcus furoris Domini, de quo ait: Inebriat sagittas meas sanguine. Et rursum: sa- gittæ meæ consument eos. De hoc arcu & de his sa- gittis in septimo legimus: Arcum suum tetendit & paravit illum: Et in ipso paravit vasa mortis: sa- gittas suas ardentibus effecit. Deut. 32. Psal. 7. ET CONCULCABUNT, ait, adversarios suos in martyrio coronati & dicent: Dominus illumina- tio mea, & salus mea, quem timebo? Dominus pro- tector vitæ meæ, à quo trepidabo? Dum appro- pinquarent super me nocentes, ut ederent carnes meas. Qui tribulant me inimici mei, ipsi infirma- ti sunt & ceciderunt: si consistant adversum me castra, non timebit cor meum: si exurgat adver- sum me prælium, in hoc ego sperabo. Quando implebitur illud eloquium: unus ex vobis perseque- tur mille, & duo convertent in fugam multa millia Ps. 26. Porro per pastores non est necessum, ut intelligamus Reges & principes populi, sed uti de Pseudo-Prophetis idololatris & divinis, per quos ante captivitatem Babylonicam seducti sunt Judæi, loquutus est Dominus, ita nunc de pastoribus ma- lis tempore Novi Testamenti, quo pluviam opor- tunam doctrinæ Evangelicæ & lætum proventum frumenti & vini expectare debebant, minatur se eosdem visitaturum in ira, quod de Pseudo-Prophe- tis & Magistris errorum Cyrillus, de Pharisæis B. Lu- therus & alii nostri interpretantur, qui eosdem et- iam hircos appellari propter tyrannidem, quam in conscientias hominum impuris suis doctrinis exer- cebant, observant. Et quicunque per hœdos intelligantur, non certe hic eximuntur à pœna, sed cum pastoribus visitandi dicuntur visitatione iræ, quod vel ex ipso verborum tenore apparet: super Pastores iratus est furor meus, & super hircos visi- tabo. Alia vero est visitatio, quæ deinde subjungi- tur: illa enim visitaturus erat hostes Ecclesiæ in i- ra, malos pastores & impuros hircos, qui eam pessum- dabant: hæc vero visitaturus est gratiose domum Juda gregem suum: pugnaturus adversus hostes suos. Sic habemus visitationem in malam partem vel iræ Exod. 20, 15. Esa. 27, 1. Jer. 51, 47. & in bo- nam partem vel gratiæ Exod. 3, 16. c. 4, 3. Willius quæ privata ipsi est sententia, judicia divina in impios populi Pastores, Pharisæos & Reges, eorumque cau- sam seductionem pastorum v. 2. describi vult, im- pleta ea esse putans tempore Alexandri fratris Ari- stobuli Regis & Alexandræ Reginæ, ac successorum.

QUIA VISITAVIT DOMINUS EXERCITUUM GREGEM SUUM] Modo Propheta, modo Deus loquens inducitur. Hic Propheta probat, hæc verissime à Deo esse dicta. Visitavit, id est, misertus est, ut diximus.

DOMUM JUDÆ] Quæ scilicet per hircos illos, si- ve quod idem est, gregem, in antecedentibus Dei verbis erat intelligenda.

ET POSUIT EOS QUASI EQUUM GLORIÆ SUÆ IN BELLO] Ut aliquando temporibus scilicet Antiochi, & deinceps, Judæis illis uteretur, sicut reges ha- bere solent equos ad prælia reservatos.

Dominus loquitur de Domino, Dominus loquens est Deus Pater, uti v. 12. concluditur caput: DICIT DOMINUS. Dominus de quo ipse loquitur, quem invocare jubet: PETITE A DOMINO pluviam & DOMINUS faciet nives, & cujus visitationem promittit, visitavit DOMINUS EXERCITUUM, est Filius Dei Pastor ille promissus Esa. 40. Ezech.

34. qui gregem suum visitaturus erat. Refert hæc & sequentia ad Antiochi tempora Grotius cum Judæis, sed pleraque ita comparata sunt, ut eo tra- hi nequeant. Willius quum superiora ad tempo- ra Regum Judæorum Aristobuli, Alexandri & Ale- xandræ retulerit, quæ sequuta sunt post fata Mac- cabæorum, agnoscere hic cogitur tam excellen- tia complementa beneficiorum Dei post Macca- bæorum non inveniri, ideoque vicissim retrogre- ditur, ac de præteritis & jam ante Ecclesiæ collatis beneficiis hæc interpretatur. Unde satis apparet, non cohærere ejus ἀνάλυσιν, temporumq; cursui, & historiæ seriei, quam ipse animo suo præconce- perat, haud congruere. Recte autem Franc. Junium in eo notat, quod ipse verba hæc ad hostes referat, quod dispositi sint, velut equi decoris ejus in bello, & processerint cum suis instrumentis à Deo, quod concul- caverint Judæos, & pugnaverint cum auxilio divino ac pudefecerint ascensores equorum. Nam nimis manifestum est, quod ea magis illustrem Dei assi- stentiam & exaltationem, quam quæ hostibus com- petere queat, complectantur, unde mavult Wil- lius cum aliis omnibus cum Græcis, tum Ebræis In- terpp. cum veteribus, tum recentioribus de bene- ficiis Dei in Ecclesiam accipere, quæ vero beneficia ipse male cum Judæis itidem ad tempora V. T. sub Maccabæis refert, siquidem uti è superiori- bus & proxime antecedentibus constat, & sequen- tia uberius docebunt, de temporibus N. T. intelli- genda sint. Promittit autem Propheta, ut recte Osiander, meliores Doctores in locum illorum hirco- rum substituendos. Qui visitavit (præteritum pro futuro) Dominus exercituum gregem suum, domum Juda: benigne curam Ecclesiæ suæ suscipiet, dabit- que ei fideles & excellentes pastores, & posuit: re- ctius: ponet eos Doctores, quasi equum gloriæ suæ in bello: i. e. instruet Apostolos suos admirandis do- nis Spiritus Sancti, atque per eos, tanquam per e- quos generosos ad bellum aptos expugnabit ani- mos populorum, ut Evangelio Christi sese sub- jiciant. (Sunt enim excellentes Ecclesiæ Ministri instar equorum generosorum, quibus Christus vehitur, cum mundum spirituali suo imperio sub- jicit, ut autem ministri sint ad eam rem idonei, id à Christo habent, non ex seipsis. B. Balduinus: Quos illi pro simplicissimis asinis habuerunt, & præsti- giis somniisque suis veluti naso circumduxerunt, iis utetur Dominus tanquam gloriosissimis equis, quibus & ipse in Ecclesia sua se ostentabit, iisdem- que spiritu sapientiæ & discretionis præditis ad- versus impostores illos præliabitur. Similiter Cy- rillus reprobata Judæorum glossa: Faciet autem eum velut equum decorum, & bellicosissimum, quo quasi spiritualiter vectus, Græcorum linguam, ut dixi, op- pugnabit, eorumq́; sapientiæ deformitatem, & omnis fructus vacuitatem patefaciet. Quin enim per Græ- corum dispersiones divini discipuli tanquam equi qui- dam fuerint, adversus eorum loquacitatem, & Deo exosam fallaciam tantum non binnientes, quis du- bitet? Cum Christus de Beato Paulo dicat ad Ana- niam: Vade, quoniam vas electionis est iste mi- hi, ut portet nomen meum coram gentibus & re- gibus, & filiis Israel) Et Abacuc quasi Dominum no- strum Jesum Christum alloquens (Quoniam ascendes super equos tuos & equitatio tua salus) &c.

## 10:4
Ver. 4.

FROM HIM THE CORNER] The corner, that is, the joining together of the tribes, which was done through Judah. For whoever wished to return, they attached themselves to the tribe of Judah and submitted themselves to its rule. Thus the city of Jerusalem is called the cornerstone in the times of Ezekiel, Isa. 28:16.

FROM HIM THE NAIL] The firmness of the state. For everything that is used for strengthening other things is denoted by the name of a nail, with the similitude taken from tents, as can be seen in Exod. 27:19, ch. 35:17, ch. 38:7, Jud. 4:21, Isa. 33:20, ch. 54:2, and therefore it is also translated by στήριγμα in Ezra 9:8. Thus Eliakim is called the nail of the royal house, Isaiah 22:23.

FROM HIM THE BATTLE BOW] From the same tribe the chief strength of the military.

FROM HIM SHALL GO FORTH EVERY OPPRESSOR TOGETHER] Every tyrant shall depart from him. The same as above 9:8.

Grotius understands these things of Judah. But the continuity of the text teaches that these things pertain to the New Testament. Moreover, it is a violent twisting of the passage in Isa. 28 to the city of Jerusalem, since it is certain from the interpretation of the New Testament that Christ is called the cornerstone there, nor do the sounder Jews themselves deny it.

Nor is the interpretation of Grotius sufficiently consistent with itself, in that he understands what is to go forth from the flock of the Lord itself as that which is to arise from it—the corner, the nail, the battle-bow from it—but finally that the last is not to go forth from it, but to recede from it. From it shall go forth every exactor together, every tyrant shall recede from it. These things, however, are explained by some privatively, but by others positively. Blessed Luther understands it privatively, namely, that all those military instruments will no longer have a place in those who fight against false teachers: So also the paraphrase of the Vinerians: The corners (which hold back the thrust against the house), the nails (which hold the building firmly together), the battle-bow (and other war equipment, by which three pieces all human power and force is indicated), and the drivers (tyrants and unmerciful regents) shall all come away from them (from the true members of the Church); on the other hand, however, they shall have in the Lord a firm castle (Prov. Sol. 18:10), a strong stay, and a proven armor: He himself will strengthen them and give them power, so that they will in turn rule over their soul-enemies and be able to drive them away. See above, chapter 9, verse 14. For the weapons of their warfare are not carnal, but spiritual and mighty before God, 2 Cor. 10:4. Willius interprets that the Church will be liberated from all hostile force, tyranny, and oppression. By the corner, he understands corner-towers from Zeph. 1:16; by the nail, tents, military [gear], and other equipment; by the bow, hostile invasions, which are to cease along with the exactors: and he explains this positively in this way, that from the Jews shall arise corners, nails, bows, and exactors—that is, such as administer and sustain the Republic, who drive away enemies, and since those have hitherto been exactors, they in turn exact tribute from them. This our people, along with the ancient Doctors, understand spiritually. The Prophet, says Osiander, calls the Apostles and other excellent Ministers of the Church Corners, that is, captains who sustain the chief burden of the war. As for the nails, because great things are divinely committed to them to be procured, just as a nail sustains what is hung upon it, and it is handed over to it as if to be kept: the battle-bow, because through them the Lord subdues the Gentiles: the exactors, because by spiritual violence, and as it were by a certain tyranny, they compel men (in conscience) by the word of God to come to that great supper which the Lord has prepared. Some, with the Chaldean leading the way, refer the corner and the nail to Christ, but Christ was mentioned in verse 3: The Lord will visit his flock.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

EX IPSO ANGULUS] Angulus, id est coagmen- tatio tribuum, quæ per Judam facta est. Nam quicunque redire voluerunt, ii Judæ tribui se applicuerunt, ejusque imperio se subdidere. Sic urbs Hierosolyma dicitur lapis angularis Ezechiel temporibus, Esa. 28, 16.

EX IPSO PAXILLUS] Firmitas status. Nam o- mne quod firmandis aliis rebus adhibetur, paxilli nomine denotatur, similitudine à tentoriis desumta, ut videre licet Exod. 27, 19. c. 35, 17. c. 38, 7. Jud. 4, 21. Esa. 33, 20. c. 54, 2. ideoque & per στήριγμα vertitur Esdr. 9, 8. Sic E- liacim dicitur paxillus domus regiæ, Esaiæ 22, 23.

EX IPSO ARCUS PRÆLII] Ex eadem tribu præcipuum militiæ robur.

EX IPSO EGREDIETUR OMNIS EXACTOR SIMUL] Recedet ab ipso omnis tyrannus. Idem quod supra 9, 8.

De Juda hæc intelligit Grotius. Sed συνέ- χεια textus docet ad Nov. Testam. hæc pertinere. Violenta autem detorsio est loci Ef. 28. ad urbem Hierosolymam: quum ibi lapidem angularem Christum dici ex interpretatione Novi Testam. certum sit, nec ipsi saniores Judæi diffiteantur.

Neque satis sibi constat interpretatio Grotiana in eo, quod quæ ex ipso grege Domini egressura sint, ita intelligat, quod inde oritura sint, ex illo angulus, ex ipso paxillus, ex ipso robur prælii, postremum vero non ex ipso egressurum, sed ab ipso recessurum. Ex ipso egredietur omnis exactor simul, recedet ab ipso omnis tyrannus. Explicantur autem illa ab aliis quidem privative, ab aliis autem positive. Privative B. Lu- therus intelligit, omnia nimirum ista instrumenta militaria non amplius habitura locum in iis, qui contra falsos Doctores pugnant: Sic etiam para- phrasis Vinariensium: Die Ecken (welche den Anstoß wider das Hauß auffhalten) Nägel (wel- che den Bau vest zusammen halten) Streitbogen (und andere Kriegsrüstung, durch welche drey Stücke alle menschliche Macht und Gewalt an- gedeutet wird) und Treiber (Tyrannen und un- barmhertzige Regenten) sollen alle von ihnen (von den wahren Gliedern der Kirchen) wegkommen, dagegen aber sollen sie an dem HErrn ein vestes Schloß, Sprichw. Salom. 18. v. 10. einen star- cken Auffenthalt, und eine bewährte Rüstung ha- ben: Derselbe wird sie stärcken und Krafft ge- ben, daß sie wiederumb werden über ihre See- len-Feinde herrschen, und sie abtreiben können. Besiehe droben cap. 9. v. 14. Denn die Waffen ihrer Ritterschafft seynd nicht fleischlich, sondern geistlich und mächtig für Gott, 2. Corinth. 10. v. 4. Willius interpretatur Ecclesiam ab omni hostili vi, tyrannide & oppressione liberatum iri. Per angu- lum turres angulares è Soph. 1, 6. per clavum ten- toria, militaria, aliumque apparatum, per arcum invasiones hostiles intelligens, quæ cum exactoribus cessatura sint: atque positive h. m. explicat, quod ex Judæis orituri sint anguli, clavi, arcus & exacto- res, id est, tales qui Rempubl. administrent & su- stentent, qui hostes abigant, & cum illi hactenus fuerint exactores, vice versa ab illis tributum exi- gant. Quod spiritualiter intelligunt nostri cum antiquis Doctoribus. Apostolos, inquit Osiander, & alios excellentes Ecclesiæ Ministros vocat Prophe- ta Angulos, hoc est, capitaneos, qui præcipuum onus belli sustinent. Paxillos quod illis divinitus res ma- gnæ procurandæ committantur, ut paxillus susti- net, quod in eo appenditur, & illi quasi asservan- dum traditur: arcus prælii, quod per ipsos Do- minus subigat Gentes: Exactores, quod spirituali violentia, & quasi quadam tyrannide homines (in conscientia) verbo Dei compellant, ut veniant ad illam cœnam magnam, quam Dominus præpara- vit. Nonnulli, Chaldæo præeunte, angulum & paxillum ad Christum referunt, sed Christi facta mentio v. 3. Dominus visitabit gregem suum.

## 10:5
Verse 5.

AND THEY SHALL BE AS MIGHTY MEN TREADING DOWN THE MIRE OF THE STREETS IN BATTLE] This is a transposition to be explained thus: And they (those of the tribe of Judah) shall be mighty men treading down in battle (the enemy) as if it were the mire of the streets.

AND THEY SHALL FIGHT, BECAUSE THE LORD IS WITH THEM] With God as their helper.

AND THE RIDERS OF HORSES SHALL BE CONFOUNDED] Antiochus's cavalry, Ezek. 38:4, Dan. 11:40. A description of this cavalry from Polybius is in Athenaeus.

The paraphrase of Osiander is more correct: And they shall be as mighty men: more correctly, like heroes. Treading down false teachers as the mire of the streets in battle. (For although false teachers struggle greatly against the truth, and for a time seem insuperable, yet, being convicted at last, they become vile, and are trodden down like mire. What is Arius now, if not the mire of the streets? It is, however, the duty of the Ministers of the Church not only to teach what is true, but also to refute what is false—that is, to tread down false doctrine, along with its defenders, like mire.) And they shall fight successfully, but spiritually, because the Lord God himself is with them: He, being present, gives them strength and happy successes, and the riders of horses shall be confounded, i.e., the horsemen, their enemies. So also Blessed Balduin in his Commentary. They will resist those vain-talking impostors and most perfidious seducers of the simple so powerfully that they will prostitute them to public contempt and mockery everywhere; and they will do this not by their own virtue, but because the Lord is with them, who has strengthened them with the word of his power. Cyril has already refuted the Jews who understand these things carnally, like Grotius: They assert again, patronizing Jewish narratives, that a battle was begun with the Greeks, that their horsemen perished, that the Israelites conquered, so that they inhabited their own region, namely Judea, free from all terror, with no one at all being abducted or made captive. But we, striving to bring an explanation and sense consistent with the former, contend that the confounded riders of horses are none other than the leaders of the Greek dogmas and the champions of a seduction hateful to God, by whose overthrow Judah conquered, and the house of Joseph was also saved.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET ERUNT QUASI FORTES CONCULCAN- TES LUTUM VIARUM IN PRÆLIO] Est transpo- sitio sic explicanda: Et erunt (illi de tribu Judæ) fortes conculcantes in prælio (hostem) quasi lutum viarum esset.

ET BELLABUNT, QUIA DOMINUS CUM EIS] Deo adjutore.

ET CONFUNDANTUR ADSCENSORES E- QUORUM] Antiochi equitatus, Ezech. 38, 4. Dan. 11, 40. descriptio hujus equitatus ex Polybio est apud Athenæum.

Rectius sese habet paraphrasis Osiandri: Et erunt quasi fortes: rectius instar heroum. Concul- cantes falsos Doctores, ut lutum viarum in prælio. (Etsi enim falsi Doctores valde reluctantur verita- ti, atque ad tempus videntur insuperabiles: tamen convicti tandem bonis sordent, & tanquam lutum conculcantur. Quid jam Arius est, nisi lutum platearum? est autem officium Ministrorum Ec- clesiæ, non modo, quæ vera sunt docere, sed et- iam, quæ falsa sunt, refutare, hoc est, falsam doctri- nam, cum ipsius defensoribus, ut lutum conculca- re) Et bellabunt feliciter, sed spiritualiter, quia Dominus Deus ipse est cum eis: præsens illi vires & felices successus donat, & confundentur ascenso- res equorum, i. e. equites ipsorum hostes. Ita et- iam B. Balduin. in Comment. Tam potenter re- sistent vaniloquis illis impostoribus & perfidissi- mis simpliciorum seductoribus, ut eos publico comtemtui & irrisioni passim ubique prostitu- ant: idque facient non propria virtute, sed quia Dominus cum ipsis est, qui verbo potentiæ suæ eos roboravit: Judæos, qui carnaliter hæc, ut Grotius, intelligunt, refutavit jam Cyrillus: Asseve- rant rursum Judaicis narrationibus patrocinantes: pugna cum Græcis inita, illorum equites periis- se, vicisse Israelitas, ut regionem suam, Judæam nempe habitarent, omni terrore vacui, nemine o- mnino abducto aut captivo facto. At nos priori- bus convenientem & germanam explicationem sen- sum afferre studentes ascensores equorum confusos non alios esse contendimus, quam Græcorum dogma- tum præsides, & seductionis Deo exosæ propugna- tores, quibus prostratis vicit Judas, & salvata quoq; est domus Joseph.

## 10:6
Verse 6.

AND I WILL STRENGTHEN THE HOUSE OF JUDAH] As that which was chief in the war, as has already been said. AND I WILL SAVE THE HOUSE OF JOSEPH] The Israelites, who added themselves to the tribe of Judah. AND I WILL BRING THEM AGAIN] I will cause them to return, safe, that is, from the battles. AND THEY SHALL BE AS THEY WERE, WHEN I HAD NOT CAST THEM OFF] That is, in a flourishing state, such as they were in the first times of David, below 11:7.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET CONFORTABO DOMUM JUDA] Ut quæ præcipua erat in bello, sicut jam dictum est. ET DOMUM JOSEPH SALVABO] Israelitas, qui se Judæ tribui addiderunt. ET CONVERTAM EOS] Redire faciam, salvas scilicet è præliis. ET ERUNT SICUT FUERUNT, QUANDO NON PROJECERAM EOS] Id est, in statu florente, quales erant primis Davidis temporibus, Infra XI. 7.

## 10:7
Ver. 7.

AND THEY SHALL BE AS THE MIGHTY MEN OF EPHRAIM] The Ephraimites [the same who were just called Joseph's] shall be like those heroes in the times of David: concerning whom see 2 Sam. 23:8 and following. AND THEIR HEART SHALL REJOICE] Concerning the victory. AS WITH WINE] Which is said to make men rejoice. AND THEIR CHILDREN SHALL SEE AND REJOICE] The boys themselves and the youths not yet fit for war shall be partakers of their parents' joy.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET ERUNT QUASI FORTES EPHRAIM] E- phraimita [iidem qui modo Josephi dicti] erunt quasi heroes illi Davidis temporibus: de quibus vide 2. Sam. 23, 8. & deinceps. ET LÆTABITUR COR EORUM] De victoria. QUASI DE VINO] Quod homines lætificare dicitur. ET FILII EORUM VIDEBUNT ET LÆTA- BUNTUR] Pueri ipsi & adolescentes nondum bello ha- biles, participes erunt gaudii parentum.

## 10:8
Ver. 8.

I WILL HISS FOR THEM, AND GATHER THEM] He returns to the simile taken from a flock. I will hiss, that is, I will play on a shepherd's pipe, for to the Greeks συρίζειν signifies both, and Cicero called the hissing of the common people a shepherd's pipe. He treats of those who had not yet returned, but returned afterwards; such as those hundred thousand redeemed by Ptolemy Philadelphus, as we have said.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SIBILABO EIS, ET CONGREGABO ILLOS] Revertitur ad similitudinem de grege sumtam. Sibilabo, id est, fistula pastorali canam, nam & συρίζειν Græcis u- trumque significat, & sibilum plebis pastoralem fistulam dixit Cicero. Agit de iis, qui nondum redierant, sed po- stea rediere; qualia illa centena millia redemta à Ptole- mæo Philadelpho, ut diximus.

## 10:9
Ver. 9.
