Posterior autem hæc lectio plane sensui congruit, & significat curam Dei ad retinendum in concor- dia populum, ut patet infra 14. Sicut Masoreticorum di- ligentiam spernere non debemus, ita nec superstitiose ni- mis ac Judaice non debemus, ita nec superstitiose nimis ac Judaice nos alligare ipsorum conjecturæ, ubi aliæ suppe- tunt meliores.

De duabus virgis tot sensus invenies, quot se- re capita. Alludi ad pedum pastorum nemo facile ambigit. Hieronymus virgam נעם de vocatione cunctarum gentium, חבלים funiculos, ut reddit, de Judæis Dei hæreditate interpretatur. Ebræi vocem hanc posteriorem pro corruptoribus accipi volunt. Quibus non abnuit Flacius in Clavi voce Virga, bonos & malos Pastores notari censens, sed Mes- siam, cum pavit Judæos, corruptoribus usum fuisse quis admittet? Quidam per priorem vocem legem naturæ, per posteriorem legem Mosis notari volunt. Sed hoc ineptum. Junius ita habet; Prior baculus, qui amœnitatis dicitur, figuravit gratiam & beneplacitum Dei conquiescens in populo ipsius per Christum prædicatione verbi: posterior vero, qui devincentium baculus appellatur, significat Eccle- siam ex Jehuda & Israelis reliquiis adunatam; quod præcessurum erat ante vocationem gentium, ut prædi- ctum fuerat per Prophetas, & ipse Christus ostendit Matth. 10, 5. & 6. Quam sententiam veritati pro- ximam censet Willius, baculus jucunditatis concio Evangelica, baculus autem devincientium dicatur conatus & studium Christi in combinandis & ad- unandis Judæis. Sed studium & conatus Christi non est instrumentum, vel medium in officio pasto- rali, quale pedum esse constat. Et excogitavit Willius ipse aliam sententiam, חבלים naucleros esse è Jon. 1, 6. vel ductores & gubernatores navis Ezech. 27, 28. 29. & per baculum jucunditatis signi- ficari Christum ipsum, ejusque officium: per ba- culum vero devictorum Apostolos Christi, & eorum ministerium. Sed Christus distinguitur hîc à ba- culo, ceu pastor à pedo. Et ut pedum non est pastor, vel officium ejus, sed instrumentum Pasto- ris: ita Christus & officium ejus per baculum in- convenienter intelligitur. Neque etiam ministri Pastoris pedum ejus dici possunt: ideoque nec A- postoli Christi ministri hic per baculum ejus desi- gnati. Coccejus per virgam clementiæ Cæsares, & eo- rum præsides, per nautas presbyterium intelligit. Sed hæc contorta sunt. Calvinus textum Ebræum corrigit, quem cum Capello, ut apparet, sequutus Grotius, suspectum etiam reddere conatur, quasi aliter olim vox חבלים quantum ad vocales, lecta fuerit, nec ad puncta Ebræis Codicibus addita nos astringi vult, ut aliæ conjecturæ meliores suppe- tant, gravissimum in eo, cum Calvino, errans erro- rem, quasi à Masoretis puncta addita, non vero coæva sint textui: quodque illi ea adjecerint pri- vatis conjecturis. Qua hypothesi admissa, nihil facile certi habebitur in Scriptura Vet. Test. sed u- nicuique libera erit sua conjectura, siquidem id virtutis sit, uti judicat Grotius, non pati se alligari superstitiose nimis ac Judaice ad puncta codicibus Bi- blicis adscripta. Interpretatur autem Calvinus baculum priorem de elegantia ordinis in regimine divino: posteriorem de unitate vel concordia, quod Deus dispersos Israelitas iterum collegerit, ut es- sent unum corpus, post reditum è Babylonia. Si- militer fere Grotius vertens dulcedinem & funicu- lum: ac per dulcedinem perfectionem à malis exter- nis, per funiculum internam concordiam intelligens. Quæ vero explicationes nec metaphoricæ locutioni congruunt: elegantia enim ordinis, & unitas vel perfectio & concordia, quomodo cum pede pasto- rali comparari possint, non apparet, & à textu alienæ sunt: siquidem hic non de Dei regimine, sed pastoratu Messiæ θεανθρώπε, non de tempo- ribus Veteris Testam. sed Novi sermo fit. Nul- lam autem corruptelam hic suspicandi causam ha- bemus. Nam vocem חבלים funiculi commo dio- rem esse, doceri nequit. Optime congruit vox חבלים sive reddas eandemperdendi significatione, quam respexit B. Lutherus, sive cum Junio, Tar- novio, aliis devinciendi vel colligandi. Ludov. de Dieu ex Arabismo reddit fœderatos? Sed non videmus ra- tionem, cur à B. Lutheri versione discedendum sit; imo exposcere eam videtur oppositio: nam non tam opponuntur sibi amœnitas & colligatio, (nisi de vinculis legis dulcedini & amœnitati adversis eam accipias) quam virga amœnitatis & virga perden- tium, vel dolo afficientium, quam rationem è Re- formatis Buxtorfius hic adduxit pro B. Lutheri in- terpretatione : Einen hieß ich sanfft, den andern hieß ich wehe. Videtur, inquit in Vindic. Ebraic. Verit. p. 557. in illis duobus nominibus duarum virgarum oppositio subesse; ut una sc. fuerit נועם id est, מקל נועם Baculus vel virga jucunditatis, id est clementiæ & mansuetudinis, altera מקל חובלים Baculus vel virga perdentium, vel, dolore afficientium, h. e. iræ & fæveritatis, qua usus est, ad irritam reddendam fraternitatem inter Juda & Israël v. 14. h. e. ad rejectionem populi Israëlïtici universi. Duabus certe his virgis utitur Deus, ad pascendum h. e. regendum populum suum. Missis autem aliis expositionibus harum virgarum, ex omnibus maxime probabilem agnoscit etiam B. Tarnovius B. Lutheri, quod per baculum jucunditatis doctrina Evangelii, per baculum devincientium (ut ipse reddit) lex moralis designetur : quam & plerosque orthodoxos Interpp. sequi non dissimulat, quibus ex antiquitate addimus Cyrill. Alexandr. Ast postquam nostrum similis factus est homo, duas virgas assumsit. Pascit enim ut adoratores suos per fidem nimirum justificatos, & sanctificatos in Spiritu, legalibus simul & Evangelicis præceptis non ad boves immolandos impellens, neq; ut oblationibus secundum legem studeamus nos docens : sed jubens potius, uti cultum in Spiritu tanquam incruentum sacrificium celebremus. Quæ vero Tarnovius adversus hanc receptam explicationem adfert, ejus momenti haud sunt, ut ab ea nos dimovere queant. Dicit loqui Prophetam de illis baculis, quos solus Christus ἀρχηποιμὴν ante se reperit, & post se nulli concessu, cum utrumq; sciderit v. 10. & 14. Resp. Christus baculos illos in pascendo grege populi Judaici adhibuit : scidisse autem dicitur non absolute, sed respectu illius populi, qui sese illis indignum reddiderat. Dicit (2) utrumq; baculum succisum fuisse irritum aliquid. Resp. penes populum Judaicum. Dicit (3) per baculum amœnitatis succisum fœdus Dei factum esse irritum. Resp. Factum est non à parte Dei, cujus dona sunt ἀμεταμέλητα; Sed ex parte ipsiusmet populi Judaici. Dicit (4) si baculo jucunditatis succiso demum agnoverunt verbum Dei, pauperes, seu fideles pauci sine Evangelio salvati sunt. Resp. Respectu illorum baculus amœnitatis succisus non est, qui crediderunt, sed respectu eorum, qui regnum Christi abs se repudiarunt. Dicit (5) Id sequuturum ex illa sententia, quod Christus cum unoquoq; prius ex Evangelio, deinde ex lege agat, quodq́; Evangelium in V. T. magis & prius, quam lex viguerit, quod baculus amœnitatis prius & magis viguerit in V. T. aut prius adhibeatur penes oves, quam baculus legis. Intelligit autem ipse per baculum amœnitatis prærogativam Judæorum, per baculum devincientium ut vocat, certam tribuum distinctionem. At illa non sunt media, vel instrumenta Pastoris Christi Judæorum prærogativa & distinctio Israëlïticarum tribuum, quemadmodum pedum est medium vel instrumentum aliquod Pastoris gregarii. Præferenda itaque adhuc omnino B. Lutheri sententia. Nam lex & Evangelium sunt media, quibus pascit gregem ὁ Ἀρχηποιμὴν Christus. Lex est baculus perdentium, Evangelium vero baculus est amœnitatis. Prius autem nominatur Evangelium, non quod in usu prior sit hic baculus, sed quod dignior & præstantior sit, ac Christo magis propria sit hæc virga amœnitatis, quando virga perditionis, quam non adhibet, nisi ut virgæ amœnitatis & dulcedinis locus sit, & ab ea nos solari possit, uti Psal. 23, 4. de hoc Pastore cecinit David : Virga tua & baculus tuus ipsa me consolata sunt. Osiander : Duo baculi sunt duæ partes doctrinæ cælestis. Doctrina Evangelii in amabilis est conscientiis perturbatis admodum grata. Doctrina legis dolores in conscientia exci­ tat & tamen ipsa quoq; salutaris est, si quis ea recte utatur. Christus autem etsi principaliter Evange­ lion docuit, tamen etiam legem Dei explicuit: eamque à corruptelis Pharisæorum repurgavit.

V. eod. ET PAVI GREGEM] Feliciter per Davidem. Vers. 8. ET SUCCIDI TRES PASTORES IN MEN­ SE UNO] Sed succidi. Cum populus ingratissimum se in Deum & Davidem ostendisset, in scelerata factione Ab­ solomi, uno in mense abstulit illi tres principes egregios, Davidem ipsum, Adoniam regis filium, & Joabum for­ tissimum Ducem.

## 11:8
AND MY SOUL WAS CONTRACTED IN THEM] My love for them was much diminished.

FOR THEIR SOUL ALSO VARIED AGAINST ME] It did not show faith to me. That is what the word בחל signifies, from the Arabic دخل, it is not found elsewhere in Hebrew letters.

Latin:

ET CONTRACTA EST ANIMA MEA IN EIS] Amor in eos meus multum imminutus est.

SIQUIDEM ET ANIMA EORUM VARIAVIT IN ME] Fidem mihi non exhibuit. Id significat verbum בחל ex Arabico دخل alibi in Hebræis literis non repe­ ritur.

## 11:9
Verse 9. AND I SAID: I WILL NOT FEED YOU] I said: I do not wish to bear fatherly care for you any longer.

LET THAT WHICH DIES DIE] Let that which is diseased perish by disease; for the likeness is taken from the flock. Reference is made to the huge pestilence toward the end of David's reign.

AND THAT WHICH IS CUT OFF LET IT BE CUT OFF] That which is snatched away by the wolf, let it be snatched away. Those wolves are Hadad and Rezon. 1 Kings 11, 14. 23.

AND LET THE REST EAT EVERY ONE THE FLESH OF HIS NEIGHBOR] And let the rest (the sheep neither dead of disease, nor snatched by the wolf) devour one another's flesh. They will be driven by a certain madness into mutual destruction.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET DIXI: NON PASCAM VOS] Dixi: nolo vestri ultra curam paternam gerere.

QUOD MORITUR MORIATUR] Quod mor­ bidum est, morbo intereat; de grege enim sumitur simili­ tudo. Respicitur pestilentia ingens sub finem Davidis.

ET QUOD SUCCIDITUR SUCCIDATUR] Quod à lupo abripitur, abripiatur. Lupi isti sunt Adad & Razon. 1. Reg. 11, 14. 23.

ET RELIQUI VORENT UNUSQUISQUE CAR­ NEM PROXIMI SUI] Et reliquæ (pecudes nec morbo intermortuæ, nec à lupo raptæ) devorent alteræ alterius carnem. Rabie quadam agentur in mutuam perniciem.

## 11:10
Ver. 10. AND I TOOK MY STAFF, WHICH WAS CALLED BEAUTY] Sweetness. I took away that special protection.

AND I CUT IT ASUNDER] I cut it into fragments, I destroyed it.

THAT I MIGHT BREAK MY COVENANT] WHICH I HAD MADE WITH ALL THE PEOPLES] By peoples here understand the tribes, as in Judges 5:14. God is said to break His covenant when, the conditions of the covenant having been broken by the people, He also does not fulfill the promises on His part.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET TULI VIRGAM MEAM, QUÆ VO­ CABATUR DECUS] Dulcedo. Abstuli protectionem illam specialem.

ET ABSCIDI EAM] Scidi in fragmenta, corrupi.

UT IRRITUM FACEREM FOEDUS MEUM] QUOD PERCUSSI CUM OMNIBUS POPULIS] Po­ pulos hic intellige tribus, ut Jud. V. 14. Irritum facere fœ­ dus suum Deus dicitur, cum ruptis à populo fœderis con­ ditionibus, ipse quoque à sua parte promissa non implet.

## 11:11
Ver. 11. AND IT WAS BROKEN IN THAT DAY] When Solomon openly broke out into idolatry.

AND THE POOR OF THE FLOCK KNEW, THAT IT IS THE WORD OF THE LORD] And the meek of the flock, who attended to me, knew rightly that this matter was of the Lord. That is, done by me. They saw that those evils did not happen in vain, but deservedly. The Chaldee also has 'meek' here; for they are interchanged, as we have often said, עני and ענו. The LXX here for כן עני read as one word, less correctly, ככעני. Which Jerome also noted.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET IN IRRITUM DEDUCTUM EST IN DIE ILLA] Cum Salomon aperte in idololatriam pro­ rupit.

ET COGNOVERUNT SIC PAUPERES GRE­ GIS, QUIA VERBUM DOMINI EST] Et cognove­ runt recte mites gregis, qui attendebant mihi, quod res hæc esset Domini. Id est, à me facta. Viderunt mala illa non fru­ stra, sed merito evenire. Mites habet hic & Chaldæus; nam permifcentur, ut sæpe diximus עני & ענו. LXX. hic pro כן עני legerunt una voce minus recte ככעני. Quod & Hieronymus notavit.

## 11:12
Ver. 12. AND I SAID TO THEM] About to render further the reason for the people being abandoned by Him, He shows through an excellent figure how greatly He Himself had been despised by the people, which indeed was true in ancient times: but much more clearly in the times of Christ; of whom all ancient things bear an image.

IF IT IS GOOD IN YOUR EYES]. Unless you declare that it is unjust.

GIVE ME MY WAGES.] For the work which I expended in protecting you. He speaks as a shepherd would speak to the Lord of the flock.

AND IF NOT, FORBEAR] If you think I have deserved nothing, give nothing.

AND THEY WEIGHED FOR MY WAGES THIRTY PIECES OF SILVER] Maimonides thinks this was shown to Zechariah in a vision, and that the following things were also fulfilled in a vision through Zechariah. This he says: they valued the pastoral work exhibited over five hundred years (for there are almost that many from the exodus out of Egypt to the end of Solomon) at thirty shekels, that is, at a most unjust price. The valuation of a day's work was a denarius, as we also learn from the Gospel. It does not much exceed an Attic drachma: four Attic drachmas make a shekel: therefore, in a hundred and twenty, or a little more days, someone could earn thirty shekels from his work. You see the injustice of the valuation. He dwells on the comparison of the shepherd. This vile wage signifies sacrifices and rites without solid piety.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET DIXI AD EOS] Causam derelictià se populi amplius redditurus, ostendit per egregiam figuram, quantopere ipse à populo comtemtus fuerit, quod olim quidem verum exstitit: sed multo clarius Christi tempori­ bus; cujus vetera omnia imaginem gerunt.

SI BONUM EST IN OCULIS VESTRIS]. Nisi id iniquum prædicatis.

AFFERTE MERCEDEM MEAM.] Pro opera quam impendi vobis protegendis. Loquitur, ut pastor loqueretur Domino gregis.

ET SI NON QUIESCITE] Si nihil me meritum putatis, nihil date.

ET APPENDERUNT MERCEDEM MEAM XXX. ARGENTEOS] Hoc Zachariæ in viso ostensum putat Maimonides, & sequentia quoque in viso expleta per Zachariam. Hoc dicit: operam pastoralem exhibitam per annos quingentos (tot enim ferme sunt ab exitu ex Ægypto ad finem Salomonis) æstimarunt XXX. siclis, id est, pretio iniquissimo. Operæ diurnæ æstimatio erat denarius, ut ex Evangelio etiam discimus. Is non multum excedit drach­ mam Atticam: quatuor drachmæ Atticæ siclum faciunt: ergo centum & viginti, aut paulo amplius diebus poterat a­ liquis ex operis suis lucrari XXX. siclos. Vides iniquum æstimationis. Moratur in comparatione pastoris. Vilis hæc merces significat victimas & ritus sine pietate solida.

## 11:13
Ver. 13. AND THE LORD SAID TO ME] So that by some action commanded to him, Zechariah might impress the matter even more upon his mind.

CAST IT TO THE POTTER] To the potter, that is, at the pottery. For there was an area there into which the broken earthenware of the Temple was cast. See what we have said at Jeremiah 19, 2. Cast it, he says, as a thing of no value, to be held by God as worth no more than a broken piece of pottery.

The Chaldean reads האוצר in this place. But the LXX and the interpreter of Matthew stand by the received reading. A GOODLY PRICE THAT I WAS PRICED AT BY THEM] It is a mockery: such as that in Tacitus: I have received a goodly price for my labor. Hist. 5. AND I TOOK THE THIRTY PIECES OF SILVER, AND CAST THEM INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD TO THE POTTER] In the Hebrew it is house, without a preposition: it is more correct to understand it as near. See what was said just now on the place in Jeremiah. Then to the potter, as just now. Zechariah obeyed the command of God, whether it was done in reality, or, as we said some think, in a vision. Both could have happened: for there is no mention here of spectators, in whose presence the thing was done. This was only a document for Zechariah himself.

He calls every punishment from God a sword; the right arm of Manasseh was his father-in-law Sanballat: a withered arm, as a withered hand is called in Matt. 12:10, which is destitute of all vigor, like a branch drawing no sap from the tree. The arm of Manasseh was withered when all the soldiers of Sanballat were led away by Alexander the Great into Egypt, and his favor with Alexander was so slight that he could not obtain for his Shechemites the immunity from tribute in the sabbatical year, which Alexander had granted to the Jews, Jos. 11:8. But the right eye, which grew dim for Manasseh, is the knowledge of divine things, just as the left eye is of human things. This cost him: he lost the use of the other, as almost all ambitious and greedy men do. See Matt. 6:22.

We wished to exhibit the entire gloss, not interrupted. Which is truly wonderful, and can please no one, unless someone to whom such monstrous novelties, such as never entered the mind of others, besides Grotius, even in a dream or in a fever.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD ME] Ut fa­ cto aliquo sibi imperato Zacharias rem magis etiam animo imprimeret.

PROJICE ILLUD AD STATUARIUM] Ad fi­ gulum, id est, apud figulinam. Erat enim ibi area in quam projiciebantur fracta Templi fictilia. Vide quæ diximus ad Jeremiam 19, 2. Projice, inquit, tanquam rem nihili, non pluris Deo faciendam quam fractum fictile.

היוצר hoc loco Chaldæus legit האוצר. Sed à recepta lectione stant LXX. & Matthæi interpres. DECORUM PRETIUM QUO APPRETIATUS SUM AB EIS] Est irrisio: qualis illa apud Tacitum: egregium pretium laboris cepi. Hist. 5. ET TULI TRIGINTA ARGENTEOS, ET PROJECI ILLOS IN DOMUM DOMINI AD STATUARIUM] In Hebræo est domum, sine præpositione: rectius est subaudiri prope. Vide quæ ad dictum modo locum Jeremiæ. Deinde ad figulum, ut modo. Paruit Zacharias Dei præcepto, sive id reipsa factum sit, sive, ut quosdam existimare diximus, ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ. Utrumque fieri potuit: nulla enim hic mentio spectatorum, coram quibus res facta sit. Fuit tantum hoc documentum Zachariæ ipsi.

TUR] Gladium vocat omnem à Deo pœnam; brachium dextrum Manaffis fuit socer ejus Samballetes: brachium aridum, ut manus arida, Matth. 12, 10. dicitur, quæ vigore omni destituta est, ut ramus nullum de arbore succum trahens. Brachium Manaffis ficcatum est, cum omnes Samballetæ milites ab Alexandro Magno abducti sunt in Ægyptum, & tam tenuis ei apud Alexandrum fuit gratia, ut suis Sicimitis obtinere non potuerit immunitatem tributi anno sabbatico, quam Judæis Alexander concesserat Jos. 11, 8. Oculus autem dexter, qui Manaffi caligavit, est cognitio rerum divinarum, sicut oculus lævus humanarum. Hic ei constitit: alterius usum perdidit, ut ferme ambitiosi, & avari omnes. Vide Matth. 6, 22.

Glossam integram, haud interruptam exhibere voluimus. Quæ vere mirabilis est, nec placere poterit ulli, nisi cui novitates ejusmodi portentofæ, quales aliis, præter Grotium, ne per somnium aut per febrim quidem unquam in mentem venere.

## 11:14
Verse 14. AND I CUT ASUNDER MY SECOND STAFF] Here the speech of God, interrupted by a parenthesis, is continued. For I cut asunder you will rightly put I broke, as above 10. I broke, namely when I saw that I was held in such little esteem by them, as has already been said.

The text convinces that those things which the Messiah speaks, appointed by God the Father as shepherd, refer to God the Father. Those things which deal with the times of the New Testament, after the Messiah was sent to the sheep of Israel, he drags to the times of David, Solomon, and Manasseh the builder of the temple on Gerizim. Three shepherds cut off in one month, whom some Jews ineptly make Judas Maccabeus, Jonathan, and Simeon, the three sons of Mattathias, Kimchi makes the three sons of Josiah, Grotius understands it far more ineptly of David, Adonijah, and Joab. The rejection of the Jews v. 9. And I said I will not feed you, he distorts to the latest times of the Davidic reign, and what followed thereafter, during which times it is most falsely asserted that the fatherly care of God was withdrawn from the people: to the words of the Lord, that which dieth, let it die, he attaches this inept meaning, as if the pestilence toward the end of David's reign were being looked at, (that which is diseased, let it die of disease;) those words, that which is cut off, let it be cut off, with the word wolf inserted, he drags to Adad and Rezon rising up. The rest, And let the rest eat every one the flesh of another, they will be driven by a certain madness into mutual destruction, he drags to the times of Solomon against all historical truth, since those were clearly tranquil and peaceful. He takes the removal of the staff of beauty as the removal of special protection. But how was the special protection of God removed under the reign of Solomon? By ALL peoples he wants to be understood ALL TRIBES, and he says that God made his covenant void against the faith of Scripture, when Solomon broke out into idolatry. By the thirty pieces of silver he understands victims and rites without solid piety cast away by God, which everyone sees how frivolous and insipid that is. Nor is the gloss better when he interprets the cutting asunder of the second staff as the dissolution of the concord between Judah and Israel made by Jeroboam. Finally, those things about Manasseh the vain man, how vain they are in this place! The Jews themselves could not have devised more inept glosses, the most famous masters of ineptitudes. Whence Cocceius rightly says of these interpretations p. 545. For anyone to be insane, and to interpret the beginning of this chapter with Grotius concerning the Maccabees and Antiochus; Three shepherds, David, Adonijah, and Joab; the broken covenant of the peoples as the defection of the tribes with Solomon to idolatry, the thirty pieces of silver as victims and rites without solid piety; the casting to the potter, into the area into which the broken pottery of the temple was cast; the breaking of the staff not as חובלים Chobelim, but חבלים Chabalim, i.e., a cord, and the dissolution of the brotherhood between Judah and Israel, the schism of Jeroboam, finally the foolish shepherd as Manasseh designated in Nehemiah 13:28, named in Josephus 11:7 and 8, who built the temple on Mount Gerizim. But this is indeed to mock the scriptures, not to interpret them. This is Cocceius. But not

WHICH WAS CALLED BANDS] The concord of the tribes among themselves, as we have said.

THAT I MIGHT BREAK THE BROTHERHOOD BETWEEN JUDAH AND ISRAEL] Between the two and the ten tribes, through the deed of Jeroboam instructed by me for that purpose.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET PRÆCIDI VIRGAM MEAM SECUNDAM] Hic continuatur intermissus κατὰ παρένθεσιν Dei sermo. Pro præcidi recte pones scidi, ut supra 10. scidi, nempe cum viderem tam parvi me ab ipsis fieri, ut dictum jam est.

Quæ Messiam loqui, constitutum à Deo Patre pastorem, textus convincit, ad Deum Patrem refert. Quæ de temporibus agunt Novi Testamenti, postquam Messias ad oves Israelis missus fuit, ad tempora Davidis, Salomonis & Manaffis structoris templi in Garizin rapit. Tres Pastores mense uno succisos, quos Judæi nonnulli inepte Judam Maccabæum, Jonathanem, & Simeonen, tres filios Matthatiæ, Kimchius tres Josiæ filios faciunt, longe ineptius de Davide, Adonia, & Joabo Grotius intelligit. Abjectionem Judæorum v. 9. Et dixi non pascam vos, ad novissima regiminis Davidici tempora, & quæ porro sequuta sint, detorquet, quibus vero temporibus populo paternam Dei curam subtractam fuisse falsissime adseritur: verbis Domini, quod moritur, moriatur, hunc sensum ineptum affingit, ac-si respiciatur pestilentia sub finem Davidis, (quod morbidum est, morbo intereat;) verba illa, quod succiditur succidatur, inserta voce lupi, ad Adad & Razon oborto collo abripit. Cætera, Et reliqui vorent unusquisq; carnem proximi sui, rabie quadam agentur in mutuam pernitiem, ad tempora Salomonis contra omnem veritatem historicam trahit, siquidem ea plane tranquilla & pacifica fuerint. Ablationem virgæ amœnitatis de ablatione protectionis specialis accipit. Sed quomodo sub Salomonis imperio specialis protectio Dei ablata? Per OMNES populos intelligi vult OMNES TRIBUS, & fœdus suum irritum fecisse Deum dicit contra Scripturæ fidem, cum Salomo in idololatriam prorupit. Per argenteos triginta victimas & ritus sine solida pietate à Deo projectos intelligit, quod quam frivolum & insulsum sit, nemo non videt. Nec melior est glossa, cum præcisionem secundæ virgæ de dissolutione concordiæ inter Judam & Israelem per Jeroboamum facta interpretatur. Denique illa de Manaffe homine vano quam vana sunt hoc in loco! Ineptiores utique glossas ne Judæi ipsi excogitare potuiffent, ineptiarum Magistri famosissimi. Unde merito de his interpretamentis Coccejus p. 545. Cuilibet insanire, & hujus capitis initium cùm Grotio interpretetur de Maccabæis & Antiocho; Tres pastores, Davidem, Adoniam & Joabum; ruptum fœdus populorum tribuum defectionem cùm Salomone ad idololatriam, triginta argenteos victimas & ritus sine pietate solida; projectionem ad figulum, in aream, in quam projiciebantur fracta templi fictilia; fractionem virgæ non חובלים Chobelim, sed חבלים Chabalim, h.e. funiculi, & dissolutionem germanitatis inter Judam & Israel, schisma Jeroboami, denique pastorem stultum Manaffen designatum Nehemiæ 13, 28. nominatum Josepho 11, 7. & 8. qui struxit templum in monte Garizim. Sed hoc quidem est scripturas irridere, non interpretari. Hæc Coccejus. Sed non

QUÆ APPELLABATUR FUNICULUS ] Concordiam tribuum inter se, ut diximus.

UT DISSOLVEREM GERMANITATEM INTER JUDAM ET ISRAEL] Inter duas & decem tribus, per factum Jeroboami per me in id instrui.

## 11:15
Vers. 15. AND THE LORD SAID TO ME] He shows the use of the aforementioned things: Namely, that even now after the return, if anything similar should happen, the pious ought to refer it to similar causes; see above 7, 11.

ADHUC] Even at this time.

SUME TIBI VASA PASTORIS STULTI] Such as a staff shod with iron, by the striking of which the sheep are killed: a wallet, in which there is nothing useful for the sheep, and similar things.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD ME] Usum oftendit antedictorum: Nempe etiam nunc post reditum, si quid simile eveniat, pios id referre debere ad causas similes; vide supra 7, 11.

ADHUC] Etiam hoc tempore.

SUME TIBI VASA PASTORIS STULTI] Ut pedum ferratum, cujus incussu pecudes occiduntur: peram, in qua nihil sit ovibus utile, & similia.

## 11:16
Vers. 16. FOR BEHOLD I WILL RAISE UP A SHEPHERD IN THE LAND, WHO WILL NOT VISIT THAT WHICH IS LEFT] Who will not search out that which is hidden (the sheep, for the comparison continues).

DISPERSUM NON QUERET] He will not seek the lamb, namely, one that cannot yet follow the flock because of its age.

ET CONTRITUM NON SANABIT] That which has been bitten by wild beasts.

ET ID QUOD STAT NON ENUTRIET] That which is whole (in the flock) he will not count, which diligent shepherds do.

Thus וכלכלו is taken in 1 Kings 20, 27.

ET CANES PINGUIUM COMEDET] But he will eat the flesh of the fat ones. He will do everything in the republic for his own sake.

ET UNGULAS EORUM DISSOLVET] He will so fatigue the rest with journeys that their hoofs will be broken. The one who is ἀνωγογείται here is Manasseh, designated in Nehemiah 13, 28, and named in Josephus 11, 7 and 8. Jeroboam had split the people, God permitting. God had healed the long-standing schism by granting a return to the Jews and to those from other tribes who would join themselves to them: concord remained for some time: but as the worship of God again became cheap, God stirred up Manasseh, a vain man, who, having found in Sanballat a father-in-law similar to himself, so that he might make himself also a high priest, and indeed against his own brother, built a new Temple on Mount Gerizim: and he drew to himself those of the Jewish people whom he could; thus the bond was broken again. I have rightly said that the cause of this evil also was the neglect of the worship of God: for whoever feared punishment among the Jews on account of forbidden foods, violated sabbaths, or other faults, for him a refuge was open at Shechem near that new Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 16. QUIA ECCE EGO SUSCITABO PASTOREMIN TERRA, QUI DERELICTA NON VISITABIT] Qui latentem (pecudem, durat enim comparatio) non investigabit.

DISPERSUM NON QUERET] Agnum non quæret, nempe qui gregem præ ætate sequi nondum potest.

ET CONTRITUM NON SANABIT] Admor-sum à feris.

ET ID QUOD STAT NON ENUTRIET] Quod integrum est (in grege) non enumerabit, quod faciunt diligentes.

Sic וכלכלו sumitur 1. Reg. 20, 27.

ET CANES PINGUIUM COMEDET] Sed carnes pinguium comedet. Sui causa faciet omnia in republica.

ET UNGULAS EORUM DISSOLVET ] Reliquos ita fatigabit itineribus, ut ungulæ dirumpantur. Qui hic ἀνωγογείται est Manasses designatus Nehemiæ 13, 28. nominatus autem Josepho 11, 7. & 8. Jeroboamus populum sciderat, Deo sinente. Sanaverat diuturnum dissidium Deus dato reditu Judæis & ex aliis tribubus qui se iis adjungerent: mansit concordia per tempus aliquod: sed iterum vilescente Dei cultu excitavit Deus Manaffem, hominem vanum, qui Samballetem, hominem sibi similem nactus socerum, ut se quoque sacerdotem summum, & quidem contra fratrem suum faceret, novum struxit Templum in monte Garizitano: & quos potuit de populo Judaico attraxit ad se; ita rursus ruptus est funiculus. Merito autem dixi causam etiam hujus mali fuisse neglectum Dei cultum: nam quicumque ob cibos vetitos, sabbatum violatum, aliasve culpas inter Judæos pœnas metuebat, ei confugium patebat Sicimis apud novum illud Templum.

## 11:17
Vers. 17. O PASTOR AND IDOL] Woe to the vain shepherd. Who wishes to be called a shepherd, or prince of the people, but in reality is nothing of the sort. Thus רפאי אליל by the name of physician, not in reality. Job 13, 4.

DERELINQUENS GREGEM] That legitimate assembly, which was in the Jerusalem Temple, made by the oracle of God, by the authority of the king, which the consensus of the whole nation had followed.

A SWORD UPON HIS ARM, AND UPON HIS RIGHT EYE, HIS ARM SHALL BE DRIED UP WITH DROUGHT, AND HIS RIGHT EYE SHALL BE DARKENED AND OBSCUR-

I do not believe Cocceius will more easily convince the reader of his interpretation, who makes the rod of clemency a government under the Roman Caesars and Presidents, Caligula, Claudius, Cumanus, because that clement government of the Romans had been removed, their disposition having then changed to ferocity. He understands the other staff, however, as the authority of the presbytery. Once this was cut, and Bishops were raised above Presbyters, the brotherhood was broken, and two kingdoms arose, of Judah and Israel, in the Christian people, with the West divided from the East. All of which things taste of nothing but an ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν (private interpretation), and are thrust upon the text, with which they have nothing in common, whence such Cocceian ideas no more than those Grotian ones ever came into anyone's mind before.

But having dismissed those τερατολογίαις (monstrous tales), we insist upon the opinion of the better interpreters which is more generally received, and just as the συνέχεια (continuity) of the text compels and convinces us that the shepherd who fed the flock is none other than Christ, so we understand the three shepherds cut off in one month to be the three orders of government among the Jewish people, with blessed Luther: the Prophets, who ruled the people by revelations and divine oracles; the priests, who ruled by the explanation and inculcation of the law; and the wise, who ruled by counsel. Jer. 18:18, Ezek. 22:25, 27, 28, Mal. 2:12, Matt. 11:13, ch. 23:13, 34, 38. Others, with Tremellius and Junius, think the Pharisees, Sadducees, and Essenes are meant. Willius, with no semblance of probability, understands Christ, the Apostles, and false teachers by the three shepherds. But it is Christ who was about to cut off the three shepherds. How, therefore, is Christ himself placed among those to be cut off? Some, with Junius, explain 'one month' as a short time. Abarbenel, Osiander, Willius, and Cocceius understand thirty years from a similar sacred calculation in Daniel 9, Ap. 9:5, 10, ch. 11:1. Not badly. For after the proclamation of Christ, not many more than thirty years elapsed until the destruction of those shepherds. Those false teachers did not remain for a month and a half, let alone for two months, after Christ began to teach in Judea. AND MY SOUL WAS CONTRACTED IN THEM, SINCE MY SOUL ALSO VARIED AGAINST ME. The verb קצר (qatsar), to be contracted, diminished, abbreviated, signifies the grief and loathing of the soul, because those affections contract the powers of the soul. See Job 21:4, Num. 21:4, Judg. 10:16. The disobedience of the Jews often produced loathing and grief for Christ, as the Evangelical history testifies. The verb בחל (bachal), which Grotius investigates from the Arabic, the Targum renders as קצה (qatsah), to loathe; so also others, and blessed Luther: 'So wollen sie mein auch nicht' (So they do not want me either). Cocceius explains it: 'it swelled against me'. Osiander: their soul detested me. Avenarius: he is livid against me, he envies me. The LXX: ἐπορεύοντο ἐπ' ἐμὲ (they walked against me), because they rejected Christ himself, they were also rejected by Christ. He who said: I WILL NO LONGER FEED YOU, which is the rejection of the people, whose pastoral care he is unwilling to undertake from then on, and to have compassion on them any longer, therefore he adds: LET THAT WHICH DIES, DIE, AND THAT WHICH IS CUT OFF, BE CUT OFF.

Christ [did] these things by a just judgment on account of their contempt and rejection, by the decree of his consequent will. Such a renunciation of his office was made by Christ before the Pharisees (Matt. 21:43) and the city of Jerusalem (ch. 23:37 ff.). AND LET THE REST DEVOUR EACH ONE THE FLESH OF HIS NEIGHBOR. By which it is indicated that Christ would permit them to destroy themselves by mutual seditions and perish by mutual slaughter. AND I TOOK MY ROD WHICH WAS CALLED BEAUTY (or lovely) AND I CUT OFF, or rather broke, IT, THAT I MIGHT MAKE VOID (toward the Jews) MY COVENANT WHICH I STRUCK WITH ALL THE PEOPLES. Which Osiander has rightly interpreted: I took away from them my lovely Gospel, so that the Jews might neither hear it any longer, nor be included in that covenant of grace, which covenant I offered TO ALL NATIONS, AND IT WAS MADE VOID ON THAT DAY. That is, the covenant of grace between me and the Jews was removed at that time, so that they would not become partakers of the heavenly benefits which are offered in the Gospel (Matt. 21:41, Acts 13:15). AND THE POOR OF THE FLOCK WHO WATCH FOR ME KNEW THAT IT IS THE WORD OF THE LORD. And the miserable sheep who observed me (as their shepherd) recognized this, that it (my word) was the word of the Lord. That is, when all these things were happening, and the obstinate Jews were perishing most miserably, the pious Israelites who had been converted to me were more confirmed in their faith that my Gospel was the very word of God, which, because the other Jews had rejected it, they were paying such heavy penalties for that reason. To which some also refer the fact that those pious ones concluded from it that the destruction of Jerusalem was imminent, and from there, as Eusebius testifies (bk. 3, ch. 5), they migrated to Pella. The things which Willius has here are foreign: I feel that the excision of the flock is fulfilled in that bloody and violent death of Christ, which he sustained for the sins of the world, having been driven to the cross by the Jews. By the old covenant struck with the old people, however, I understand that which was finished and abrogated by the death of Christ, the total and extreme rejection of which the Jews completed in the denial of Christ. AND I SAID TO THEM, IF IT IS GOOD IN YOUR EYES, BRING MY WAGES, more correctly my price, AND IF NOT (if it does not please you), CEASE; he prophesies concerning his own sale made through Judas. But lest anyone, with Calvin (Inst. bk. 3, ch. 25, § 6) or Beza in his notes on Matt. 26:9, think that God so bent the human will that Judas betrayed and the Jews bought Christ: it is to be noted that nothing else is implied than the voluntary passion of Christ, and that he himself permitted his own sale. Cocceius also observes this: Christ willingly permitted that betrayal to be done by Judas. When, therefore, Judas said to the priests: 'What will you give me, and I will deliver him to you?' if you look at Christ governing these things and laying down his soul of his own accord, it has this force, as if he were saying to them: 'Behold me ready to be killed by your hands: if you wish, you can expend my wages, i.e., make an expenditure for my death; if you do not wish, you can omit it.' They are words of temptation. B. Balduinus explains it thus, saying: I see that I have labored among you in vain: I therefore depart from my duty: but if you are good, give me my wages, of which every laborer is worthy: but if, on account of the obstinate malice of your mind, you refuse to give me the wages due to me, know that I do not care about this: but with what conscience that may be done by you, you yourselves shall see: and thus he renounces all friendship to be cultivated with them in the future, as being unworthy of receiving further benefits from him. AND THEY WEIGHED OUT MY WAGES, more correctly my price (at which I was valued by the Jews, and they count that price to the traitor Judas) namely, THIRTY PIECES OF SILVER. Drusius, following the opinion of Elias, wishes thirty pounds to be understood, not shekels: since it is not credible that a field near the city of Jerusalem, so populous, could have been sold for 30 shekels, nor does Willius disapprove of that. But the Evangelists contradict this, and the extreme cheapness of the price is noted here, and therefore those things which Grotius annotated on Matt. 26:15, regarding τριάκοντα αργύρια, are more correct: When Judas had left it to the discretion of the priests how much they valued Jesus, they valued him at as much as the least of any man could be valued. For τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, or silver shekels, are just as many tetradrachms, which the LXX call didrachms because they use double drachmas. Therefore, Exod. 21:32, the head of a slave is valued at thirty shekels, where in the Greek it is τριάκοντα δίδραχμα, and in Josephus just as many tetradrachms. But in the prophecy of Zechariah, which will be examined below, the same LXX translate [τρ]ιάκοντα ἀργυρᾶς, where one must understand shekels: as here, coins: for to the Jews the shekel is the coin κατ' ἐξοχήν. This very passage of Zechariah shows that this sum has the meaning of a vile price: and the Hebrews note that a male human was usually valued at fifty shekels, a female slave at thirty. Also in the second book of Samuel 18:11, כסף is translated in Greek as σίκλ& ἀργυρῖs. Wherefore one must not think here of pounds or of talents. This serves to note that Judas's mind was so enslaved to avarice that he could be driven to crime for any price.

But what the Holy Spirit predicted here concerning this purchase, Grotius wrongly explained in this our Prophet as a vile reward given to God for labor, even though he insinuates that it bears some image of the contempt of Christ. He has it, as far as it appears, from Calvin, whose similar ςρεβλώτης it is: Just as once the Jewish people paid the Lord a sordid reward for his pastoral care, and one unworthy of his majesty, namely thirty pieces of silver, i.e., the trifles of ceremonies, which they performed without any piety; so God wished to exhibit a visible symbol of that matter in his Son, against whom they hired a traitor for the reward of 30 pieces of silver for the office of Shepherd faithfully administered among them, by whose agency they might drag him to death: but the silver pieces will have a double meaning in such a way that, with respect to the old people, they metaphorically denote the trifles of ceremonies in a sense devoid of piety, but with respect to Judas the traitor, they are properly understood as the money of 30 pieces of silver, as Matthew has interpreted. Then indeed the potter will signify first the potter appearing on the scene in the prophet's times to buy bricks to restore the temple, and then indeed the potter who after some centuries would sell his field to the Priests, as Calvin dreamed. How absurd these things are, the blessed Aegidius Hunnius shows clearly in his Anti-Pareus, in the second place, XI, p. 480, while defending his Calvin against Pareus. But lest we doubt that Grotius is following in the footsteps of Calvin here, one must compare what he himself has in his annotations on Matthew 17:9, p. 476.

This saying of Jeremiah, repeated by Zechariah, is of the kind that would primarily signify the affairs of their times, yet in such a way that they would also fit the times of Christ even more, which God made manifest by a singular direction of events. For with Zechariah, this sense is primarily intended, which it is credible was also the case with Jeremiah: God, in order to teach that his benefits conferred upon the Hebrew people were received with too much ingratitude, says that a reward was demanded of him for the labor spent on them. A vile price was assigned to him by the people, at which the least of slaves are usually valued, thirty shekels. But he says that he ordered that price to be thrown into some field, into which fragments of pottery were accustomed to be thrown: by which act he wished to demonstrate that all the pomp of ceremonies, by which the Hebrews thought they were returning excellent thanks for divine benefits, was unworthy to be accepted by him when a pious mind was absent. But all this, just as it pertained to the times of Jeremiah and Zechariah, so it fit the times of Christ much more. And therefore it happened by the governance of divine providence that what was then said allegorically, with that sense remaining κατ᾽ ἀλληγορίαν in the age of Christ, was also fulfilled according to the literal meaning of the words, which kind of fulfillment of prophecies will often occur in this history of the death of Christ. For God in Christ was valued by the High Priests at thirty shekels, when he was bought for that much in the person of the traitor: and that money was truly not so much spent on a potter's field as thrown away contemptuously, by the act of the Priests, but by divine counsel: whence what they did is rightly ascribed to God's direction. This is Grotius. But those things are frivolous, that 30 shekels were assigned to God by the people in place of a reward, which Zechariah was ordered to throw into some field into which fragments of pottery were accustomed to be thrown, and that the same thing also happened in the times of Jeremiah. For whence is it established that the same thing also happened in the times of either Zechariah or Jeremiah? God is certainly not addressing Zechariah here, but Christ, as we have shown before. Now if that was said by Zechariah only κατ' ἀλληγορίαν, and the rites devoid of piety were denoted by the 30 pieces of silver, as Grotius wants, how was Zechariah ordered to throw those 30 pieces of silver into a field? Did the Lord order him to throw away 30 metaphorical pieces of silver, i.e., rites devoid of piety, or the frivolous worship of hypocrites? Furthermore, if it is asserted that, how will the event that took place in the times of Jeremiah and Zechariah, by the throwing of 30 pieces of silver, and besides that the event to take place in the time of the N.T., be indicated by the same words, and will those coins nevertheless also have to be understood allegorically? These things are inconsistent and absurd. For thus it will necessarily follow (which the blessed Hunnius opposed to Pareus) that the thirty pieces of silver no longer hold one meaning (as we indeed, following Matthew, have established), nor even just two, but that by the name of 30 pieces of silver in Zechariah a triple usage and meaning is insinuated, with an equivocation hitherto unheard of, and unknown and undiscovered by all learned men. For first they will denote those trifles of hypocrites situated in sacrifices performed without faith, and other ceremonies, and thus they will be taken metaphorically. Secondly, they will signify those material coins, or silver pieces, which it is imagined the people in the time of Zechariah weighed out as a symbol, either to the Prophet or to the Lord. Thirdly, they will signify other silver pieces, clearly different, likewise taken literally, which Judas received from the Priests. Now, let him who wishes to defend this also explain the type, and teach us, which silver pieces are types of what? Are they, understood metaphorically, types of true ones? Or are these true ones (taken twice, once in the time of Zechariah, afterwards in the time of the passion of Christ) jointly types of hypocritical worship? Or indeed one or the other? Or were those by which the Lord was valued in the age of Zechariah types of those by which Christ was valued in the time of His passion? It is absurd to call the later ones a type of the former, since in such cases types are accustomed to precede the things delineated by the types. But if he should say that those former ones are a type of the later ones, which Judas received, he will be begging the question: since he has not yet proven that the people weighed out such silver pieces, properly so called, to the Lord externally outside of a vision thus performed, nor is it likely that the Jews in the time of Zechariah did such a thing: Add that with the triple usage of the word 'silver pieces' accepted, that whole context will now of necessity require a triple exposition, in this way: They weighed my reward, 30 silver pieces, i.e., the trifles of hypocritical worship: and then 30 true silver pieces: but also in the time of Christ they weighed other true silver pieces to Judas the traitor, the price of the valuation of the Messiah. And the Lord said to me: Cast it to the potter, that is, You, Zechariah, condemn the silver pieces taken metaphorically: then cast the silver pieces understood literally into the house of the Lord to the potter: but also you, Judas, cast the other 30 silver pieces, which you acquired for yourself by crime, into the temple, that they may be given to the potter. There is no need for these monstrous inventions of glosses for those who in interpreting follow solely the clear truth demonstrated by the Evangelist Matthew. Nothing here is treated by the Prophet concerning a hypocritical reward, which is noted by the name of 30 pieces of silver, nothing concerning ceremonies performed without a sense of piety, nothing concerning sacrifices, nothing at all concerning a potter buying bricks or tiles, nothing concerning restoring the ruins of the temple. These are pure and simple inventions of Calvin, nay, mockeries of Satan, by which he strives to blacken with the dark soot of Jewish opinions this most illustrious prophecy delivered concerning the passion of the Lord. The Prophet prophesies concerning the passion of Christ, and concerning the 30 pieces of silver, not metaphorically but properly understood, to be counted out to Judas the traitor, and to be thrown back by him into the house of the Lord, so that they might be given to the potter, not so that he might buy tiles or bricks (let these trifles, more empty than Sicilian nonsense, depart) but for the burial of strangers. Of which matter the undoubted interpreter is Matthew, from whom Calvin, out of a mere desire for novelty, most shamefully dissents in fact and deed, however much he may not wish to appear contrary to him in words. These things our blessed predecessor opposed to Calvin, these he opposed to Pareus, his champion; these we wished to oppose to Grotius, who follows Calvin here, in the same words. For they deserve no further refutation, since they only beg the question: that this kind of fulfillment of prophecies often occurs, so that things said allegorically are also fulfilled according to the literal meaning of the words. Certainly, he could produce no example of such a thing. Nor does it suit the clarity or simplicity of Scripture; nay, as has been shown, it is utterly absurd. Willius admits that Christ looks to the sale of himself made by Judas the traitor, and brings it forward as a testimony of his own greatest contempt: and it is imputed to the whole people, what was transacted between Judas alone and the Priests, because the people approved with their own vote that contract between Judas selling and the Pharisees buying, and wished it to be ratified, when they demanded for the punishment of the cross him to whom they had shown royal honor with their acclamation a few days before.

But let us proceed in the explanation of the Prophet. AND THE LORD SAID TO ME: THROW IT TO THE STATUARY. Those things were said to him who had previously said: bring my price, and for which they weighed out 30 pieces of silver, verse 12. Said to him who, in verse 9, had said: I will not feed you, and had cut the rod of pleasantness, and had made void his covenant with the Jewish people, v. 10. Said to him who had previously fed the flock, and had cut off three Shepherds, v. 8, to whom God the Father had commended it, v. 1, feed the flock of slaughter. But he is none other than the Messiah God-man: this is an invincible argument, because all things cohere adamantly. But what is said in the Vulgate: to the STATUARY, Grotius correctly rendered as to the potter, and Jerome acknowledged that it should be so rendered, concealing his former error. For πλάστη and molder I once interpreted as statuary, compelled by the ambiguity of the word, which signifies both statuary and molder in one term. But that Grotius wishes 'to the potter' to be the same as 'to the potter's field,' to which the broken pottery of the temple had been thrown, in that he is seduced by Calvin, just as in the metaphorical sense which he applied to these things: throw it as a thing of no value, no more to be valued by God than a broken piece of pottery. One must not depart from the propriety of the letter without a weighty cause. Nor does Matthew admit that metaphorical interpretation, who understood the potter properly. The price is said to be thrown to the potter because it was to be carried to him immediately. For it is said to have been carried afterwards to the house of the Lord, but finally, so that it might be indicated that those 30 pieces of silver would fall to the potter, just as Matthew provides a torch for this passage, while he teaches that a field was bought with these pieces of silver from the potter. The Prophet, or rather the Lord in the Prophet, subjoins: A DECOROUS, f. truly an excellent and great PRICE! Which express the indignation of Christ, because they were about to sell him like a most vile person. There is no need here for a change of person, as Osiander thinks. For what does it have to do with the throwing of the price into the temple? Even if Matthew, ch. 27, 5, says it was done by Judas, the Prophet does not therefore sustain the person of Judas, when the Lord says: throw it to the potter: But just as the Son of God spoke before, so also here, without a change of person, he testifies that those things were said to him. But he himself is said to have thrown the price of himself, because he so directed the mind of Judas that what he had impiously taken from the Jews, he threw into the temple, and it fell into the use of the potter, so that it might be given for a field for the burial of strangers, just as the history of the passion teaches. Therefore, it is only indicated that the providence of Christ directed evil things to a good end. Although Judas desired to convert the silver to his own use, and the Priests preferred to receive it for themselves, yet Christ, although standing before Pilate in the highest state of emptying himself, compelled Judas by his omnipotence to return the reward of iniquity, and moved the minds of the priests so that they would not add it to the treasury of the temple, but truly buy the potter's field, as Tarnovius has it here, p. 308. But Grotius here again perverts the mind of the Prophet, because that price was thrown not into the house of the Lord, as Matthew testifies, but near the house of the Lord, into a field, which he imagines was granted to potters very near the temple, into which fragments of pottery, nay, other filth, were accustomed to be thrown, so that he may carve out his metaphorical sense, that the rite of victims offered without piety, which he understands by the 30 shekels, is held as a thing of no value. By which name he also invents that these things were said to Zechariah, and were done by Zechariah, either in reality or in a vision, which, however, were said to the Messiah, and were finally fulfilled in the New Testament, as is clearly evident both from the continuity of the text and from the interpretation of Matthew.

It follows in the text: AND I CUT OFF MY SECOND STAFF. Grotius imagines that the preceding words were inserted by way of parenthesis, and that now the discourse of God is continued. But there is no need for a parenthesis; everything coheres and follows in good order. The second staff, which was called BANDS, is wrongly explained by him as the concord of the tribes. We have said that the divine law is denoted by it. Which, having been contracted with respect to the Jews, when after Christ was bought for 30 pieces of silver and handed over to death, they were deprived of the staff of the laws as well. THAT I MIGHT BREAK THE BROTHERHOOD BETWEEN JUDAH AND ISRAEL, so that with that bond of ecclesiastical and political society removed, mere confusion might be left, and whatever still remained of communion in Judah and Israel might utterly expire, no commerce of the tribes would remain, no bonds of communion, all would be dispersed into the world, and be involved in eternal confusion. Osiander correctly expressed the sense: I finally took away from them also the Mosaic law, I abrogated it, I removed the sacrifices and the whole Levitical worship: that, along with the Jerusalem Temple, collapsed entirely, which was previously the sinew of brotherhood among the Israelites. The Jews lacked the law after the passion and death of Christ, because they had no true sense of the law, not even one verse in the law which is not entangled in a variety of opinions, just as they themselves admit in the Epitome of the Talmudic volumes; they have no sacrifices, no other rites prescribed in the Levitical law, but whatever today in divine worship they do not act according to the norm of the law itself, but according to the prescription of Talmudic fables, which they prefer to all Scripture: they call it the foundation of the Mosaic law, the recreation of the heart and bones, the treasure of God, which is surely nothing other than being utterly destitute of the Law of the Lord, as B. Balduin notes here.

But the things which follow in verse 15 constitute a new vision: they do not, however, show the use of the things said before, as Grotius babbles: nor are the words here directed any longer from God the Father to the Son, but these things were said to the Prophet. For the reason for these and the former things is far different. For in the former things those things were predicted which in no way befitted the Prophet, nor could be attributed to anyone except the Messiah, the God-man. But what now follows concerning the assuming of the person of a foolish shepherd in no way befits the Messiah: YET TAKE TO THYSELF THE INSTRUMENTS OF A FOOLISH SHEPHERD. The little word 'yet' does not indicate that these things are said to the same person to whom the preceding things were said: for it has already been noted that this does not fit. But that this also will happen YET. Therefore, it is not the continuity of the speech or address that is indicated, but of the events, as the Weimar scholars seem to have rightly observed. These words can also not inappropriately be referred to the prediction made in chapter 10, 3. and 11, 8, that it ought to prophesy YET concerning false Doctors, and indicate their perverse administration and punishments, which had already been intimated before: my fury is kindled against the shepherds, and I will visit upon the goats. Likewise, I cut off three shepherds in one month; the instruments of a foolish shepherd are such instruments as would not befit anyone except a foolish shepherd, for example, a broken staff, a wallet without food, a vessel without oil, a hoarse pipe, to signify the stupidity of false Doctors, or the instruments of a cruel shepherd, weapons, a heavy staff, a sword for slaughtering, shears for shearing the little sheep. FOR BEHOLD I WILL RAISE UP A SHEPHERD IN THE LAND, WHO WILL NOT VISIT THAT WHICH IS LEFT, etc. By this shepherd, Cyril and Jerome understand the Anti-Christ. But since these things still strike the Jews, to whom the Lord threatened total destruction, it does not appear how this Anti-Christ, whom Paul and John foretold, can be inserted here. Most think that 'Shepherd' is said in the singular, but is understood in the plural: so that it may be indicated that to the punishments which He had predicted for the ungrateful people, this also would be added, that the Lord wishes to send Doctors who do not take care of the flock, but are only given to avarice, since they themselves rejected Christ and his disciples. Therefore, these things pertain to the last times of the state of the Jews. Tremellius and Junius interpret this as the wicked Kings, administrators, and procurators of Judea, who exhausted and consumed Judea, but false Doctors are looked at here, not Kings or political administrators: which both the exposition of Christ and the Apostles, and the administration of the office teaches. Which is described as truly the worst, partly negatively, because such a shepherd WILL NOT VISIT THAT WHICH IS LEFT or CUT OFF, he will not succor the sheep that have a wounded conscience. 2. HE WILL NOT SEEK THAT WHICH IS DISPERSED, he will not lead back into the way of truth and justice those which are dispersed in the pathless woods and precipices of errors, or according to the Hebrew, those which are of an imprudent mind, and because of infirmity do not know how to take counsel for themselves, he will not undertake their instruction. (3) HE WILL NOT HEAL THAT WHICH IS BROKEN, he will not have care for those whose minds are wounded. (4) HE WILL NOT FEED THAT WHICH STANDETH, he will not confirm those persisting in the faith, nor does he exhort them to perseverance, whence it can easily happen that, overcome by the suggestions of the flesh and the wiles of the Devil, they make shipwreck of their souls: partly affirmatively (1) HE WILL EAT THE FLESH OF THE FAT, he will not only not perform the duty of a good shepherd, but will even rage like wolves against the miserable little sheep, and will feed himself on the goods of the hearers. 2. HE WILL TEAR OFF THEIR HOOFS, he will lord it over his sheep, not even sparing the Magistrate, whose authority he will detract from, and will strive, as much as in him lies, to subjugate him to himself. These things were fulfilled not only in the priests and Pharisees, but also in the Pseudo-Christs and other impostors before the Jewish total destruction, who were leading the miserable populace away from the doctrine of the Apostles, and involving them in seditions and other dangers, concerning whom Josephus writes in his books on the Jewish War. But Christ. à Castro wrongly understands the Roman soldiers or Commanders by the foolish Shepherd. Since the Lord speaks openly about Ecclesiastical Shepherds.

But the Lord threatens these false Doctors with the most severe punishments in verse 17. O SHEPHERD AND IDOL THAT LEAVETH THE FLOCK, THE SWORD UPON HIS ARM: AND UPON HIS RIGHT EYE. HIS ARM SHALL BE DRIED UP WITH WITHERING, AND HIS RIGHT EYE DARKENING SHALL BE OBSCURED. In the Hebrew it is, woe to the shepherd of NOTHING. By the arm, power is noted; by the right eye, counsel and prudence; that such a shepherd will be deprived of both fortitude and counsel and prudence, so that both his strengths and his frauds may be turned into mockery, or being deprived of all strength and spiritual light, he will be plainly blinded and given over to a reprobate mind. By the sword, B. Balduin understands the word of the Lord, Eph. 6, 17, Heb. 4, 12, by which alone all the defenses of evil shepherds are shattered and reduced to nothing. Thus also the Weimar paraphrasts: All their power, which is indicated by the arm, and all their wit and understanding, which is indicated by the eye, shall be brought to nothing by the sword of the Spirit through the word of God, Eph. 6, 7, Heb. 4, 12. Others take the word 'sword' for punishment, and for the sword of divine judgment, by which the Lord is about to strike the arm and right eye of such men. With the sword of his vengeance he will break the strength of thy arm. The arm shall wither, i.e., its vigor shall flow away, so that it is as if it were rotten wood, then his right eye, i.e., the health of the mind, that is, right understanding, shall be contracted by contracting, as Calvin rendered it.

THE SEVENTH AND LAST SERMON, PURELY EVANGELICAL.

SECTION I. CONCERNING THE TRUE ISRAEL.

Latin:

Vers. 17. O PASTOR ET IDOLUM] Væ pastori vano. Qui pastor, sive princeps populi dici vult, sed reipsa nihil minus est. Sic רפאי אליל medici nomine, non re. Job. 13, 4.

DERELINQUENS GREGEM] Cœtum illum le-legitimum, qui erat in Templo Hierosolymitano, facto ex Dei oraculo, regis auctoritate, quem secutus fuerat gentis totius consensus.

GLADIUS SUPER BRACHIUM EJUS, ET SUPER OCULUM DEXTRUM EJUS, BRACHIUM EJUS ARIDITATE SICCABITUR, ET OCULUS DEXTER EJUS TENEBRESCENS OBSCURABI-

non facilius Coccejus, credo, suam interpretatio- nem lectori probabit, qui virgam clementiæ regi- men facit sub Cæsaribus & Præsidibus Romanis, Ca- ligula, Claudio, Cumano, quod regimen clemens Romanorum sublatum fuerit, mutato deinde ani- mo eorum ad feritatem. Baculum autem alterum de presbyterii autoritate intelligit. Qua incisa, & Episcopis supra Presbyteros evectis rupta sit fra- ternitas, & duo regna orta sint Judæ & Israelis in populo Christiano, diviso occidente ab Oriente. Quæ omnia nil nisi ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sapiunt, & inge- runtur textui, cum quo nihil commune habent, unde non magis talia Coccejana, quam ista Grotia- na ulli antea unquam in mentem venerunt.

Missis autem illis τερατολογίαις receptiori In- terpp.meliorum sententiæ insistimus, atque uti pa- storem, qui gregem pavit, nullum alium, quam Christum esse, textus συνέχεια cogit & convincit, ita tres pastores in mense uno succisos tres ordines gu- bernatorem in populo Judaico cum B. Luthero, intelligimus Prophetas, qui revelationibus & ora- culis divinis, sacerdotes, qui legis explicatione & inculcatione, ac sapientes, qui consilio populum regebant. Jer. 18, 18. Ezech. 22, 25. 27. 28. Mal. 2, 12. Matth. 11, 13. c. 23, 13. 34. 38. Alii cum Tre- mellio & Junio Pharisæos, Sadducæos & Essenos notari putant. Willius nulla probabilitatis specie, per tres pastores, Christum, Apostolos & falsos doctores intelligit. Sed Christus est, qui excisu- rus erat tres pastores. Quomodo ergo Christus inter excindendos ipse collocatur? Mensem unum de brevi tempore nonnulli explicant cum Junio. Triginta annos è simili sacro computo apud Danie- lem 9. Ap. 9, 5. 10. c. 11, 1. Abarbenel, Osiander, Willius & Coccejus intelligunt. Non male. Nam post præconium Christi non multo plures anni, quam XXX. elapsi sunt, ad excidium istorum Pa- storum. Non permanserunt illi falsi Doctores sesquimensem, nedum per duos menses, postquam Christus docere in Judæa cœpit. ET CON- TRACTA EST ANIMA MEA IN EIS, SI- QUIDEM ET ANIMA MEA EORUM VA- RIAVIT IN ME. Verbum קצר contractus, imminutus, abbreviatus fuit, significat animi do- lorem & fastidium, quia illi affectus vires animi contrahunt. Vid. Job. 21, 4. Num. 21, 4. Jud. 10, 16. Inobedientia Judæorum Christo sæpe fasti- dium & dolorem peperit, teste historia Evangelica. Verbum בחל quod ex Arabismo investigat Gro- tius, Targum reddit קצה fastidit sic etiam alii, B. Lutherus: So wollen sie mein auch nicht. Coccejus exponit: intumuit contra me. Osiander, animus eorum me detestatus est. Avenarius: lividus est in me, invidet mihi. LXX. ἐπορεύοντο ἐπ' ἐμὲ, quia Christum ipsum repudiarunt, etiam à Christo re- probati sunt. Qui dixit: NON PASCAM vos amplius, quæ est rejectio populi, cujus curam pa- storalem suscipere deinceps non vult, ac ne com- miserationem habere amplius cum eodem, ideo addit: QUOD MORITUR MORIATUR, ET QUOD SUCCIDITUR, SUCCIDATUR.

Hæc Christus justo judicio ob sui contemtum & reprobationem ex decreto voluntatis conse- quentis. Talis renunciatio officii sui facta est à Christo penes Pharisæos Matth. 21, 43. & urbem Hierosolymam c. 23, 37. seqq. ET RELIQUI DEVORENT UNUSQUISQUE CARNEM PROXIMI SUI. Quibus id indicatur, permis- surum Christum, ut seditionibus mutuis se per- dant, mutuaque laniena intereant. ET TULI VIR- GAM MEAM QUÆ VOCABATUR DE- CORUM (vel amabilis) ET ABSCIDI, vel po- tius confregi EAM, UT IRRITUM FACE- REM (erga Judæos) FOEDUS MEUM, QUOD PERCUSSI CUM OMNIBUS POPULIS. Quæ recte interpretatus est Osiander: Abstuli ab eis a- mabile Evangelion meum, ut Judæi illud nec am- plius audirent, nec illo fœdere gratiæ comprehen- derentur, quod fœdus obtuli OMNIBUS GEN- TIBUS, ET IN IRRITUM DEDUCTUM EST IN DIE ILLA. Id est, sublatum est eo tem- pore fœdus gratiæ inter me & Judæos, ut non fie- rent participes beneficiorum cœlestium, quæ in Evangelio offeruntur Matth. 21, 41. Actor. 13, 15. ET COGNOVERUNT SIC PAUPERES GREGES QUI CUSTODIUNT MIHI QUIA VERBUM DOMINI EST. Et hoc agnosce- bant miseræ oves; quæ me (ut pastorem suum) observabant, quod (verbum meum) verbum Domi- ni esset. Id est, cum hæc omnia gererentur, & obstinati Judæi miserrime perirent, pii Israëlitæ, qui ad me conversi fuerant, magis in fide sua con- firmati sunt, meum Evangelium esse ipsissimum verbum Dei, quod cum cæteri Judæi reprobassent, tam graves eam ob causam pœnas darent. Quod eo etiam nonnulli referunt, quod pii illi ex eo con- cluserint exitium Hierosolymæ imminere, inde concedentes Pellam migrarint teste Eusebio l. 3. c. 5. Aliena sunt, quæ hic habet Willius: Excisionem pedi impletam sentio in cruenta & violenta illa morte Christi, quam pro peccatis mundi, in crucem à Ju- dæis actus sustinuit. Per fœdus vero vetus illud cum veteri populo percussum intelligo, quod morte Christi finitum & abrogatum, cujus itidem totalem & ex- tremam rejectionem in Christi abnegatione Judæi compleverunt. ET DIXI AD EOS, SI BO- NUM EST IN OCULIS VESTRIS, AFFER- TE MERCEDEM MEAM, rectius pretium meum, ET SI NON (libuerit) QUIESCITE, de sui venditione per Judam facta vaticinatur. Ne autem quis cum Calvino l. 3. Inst. c. 25. §. 6. aut Beza in notis ad Matth. 26, 9. censeat: Deum vo- luntatem humanam ita flexisse, ut Iudas proderet, Iudæi emerent Christum: notandum nihil aliud innui, quam voluntariam Christi passionem, & quod permiserit ipse sui venditionem. Id observat quoq; Coccejus: Christus volens permisit à Iuda eam proditionem fieri. Quum igitur Judas Sacerdoti- bus dixit: Quid mihi dabitis, & ego eum tradam vobis? id, si Christum hæc gubernantem, & ani- mam à seipso ponentem respicias, habet istam vim, quasi ipsis diceret: Ecce me paratum per manus vestras occidi: si vultis potestis expendere merce- dem meam, h. e. sumtum facere in necem meam; si non vultis, potestis illud omittere. Verba ten- tationis sunt. B. Balduinus ita explicat, q. dicat: frustra me apud vos laborasse video: officio igitur meo discedo: quod si boni estis, date mihi merce- dem meam, qua dignus est quilibet operarius: sin vero pro obstinata animi vestri malitia debitam mihi mercedem dare recusatis, sciatis, me hoc non curare: qua vero conscientia id à vobis fiat, ipsi videbitis: atque sic omni amicitiæ cum ipsis in po- sterum colendæ renunciat, tanquam indignis, qui- bus amplius benefaciat. ET APPREHENDE- RUNT MERCEDEM MEAM, rectius pretium meum (quo æstimatus sum à Judæis, numerantque proditori Judæ illud pretium) videl. TRIGINTA ARGENTEOS. Triginta libras non siclos intelli- gi vult ex Eliæ sententia Drusius: siquidem cre- dibile non sit 30. siclis venire potuisse agrum pro- pe Hierosolymam urbem tam populosam, nec id improbat Willius. Sed contrariantur Evangeli- stæ, & notantur hic summa vilitas pretii, ideoq; re- ctius sese habent, quæ annotavit Grotius ad Matth. 26, 15. ad τριάκοντα αργύρια: Cum Iudas sacerdotum arbitrio permisisset, quanti Jesum æstimarent, illi æstimarunt, quanti minimi homo ullus æstimari poterat. Nam τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, sive sicli argentei, sunt totidem τετράδραχμα, quæ LXX. quia duplaribus utuntur drachmis δίδραχμα vocant. Itaq́; Exod. 21, 32. caput servi æstimatur triginta siclis, ubi in Græco est τριάκοντα δίδραχμα, apud Josephum totidem τετράδραχμα. At in Zachariæ vaticinio, quod infra examinabitur, iidem LXX. [τρ]ιάκοντα ἀργυρᾶς vertunt, ubi subintelligendum est σίκλες: ut hic νομίσματα: Nam Judæis σίκλ& νομισμα est κατ' ἐξοχήν. Qui ipse Zachariæ locus ostendit eam summam vilis pretii habere significationem: & notant Hebræi, hominem marem plerumq́; æstimatum quinquaginta siclis, ancillam triginta. Samuelis quoq́; secundo libro XVIII. 11. כסף Græce vertitur σίκλ& ἀργυρῖs. Quare neq́; de libris, neq́; de talentis hic cogitandum est. Facit hoc ad notandum Judæ animum ita avaritiæ mancipatum, ut quovis pretio impelli ad scelus potuerit.

Quæ vero de hac emtione prædixit hic Sp. S. perperam Grotius in hoc nostro Propheta de vili mercede pro labore Deo data exposuit, etiamsi ea imaginem aliquam contemtus Christi gerere subinnuat. Habet ea, quantum apparet, à Calvino, cujus similis est ςρεβλώτης: Sicut olim populus Iudaicus Domino pro pastorali cura solvit mercedem sordidam, & ipsius majestate indignam, nempe triginta argenteos, h. e. nugas ceremoniarum, quas absq́; omni pietate præstabant; sic ejus rei exhibere voluisse Deum visibile symbolum in Filio suo, contra quem pro officio Pastoris fideliter inter eos administrato proditorem conduxerunt mercede 30. argenteorum, cujus operâ illum ad necem traherent: sed ita argentei geminum habebunt sensum, ut respectu quidem veteris populi metaphorice notent nugas ceremoniarum pietatis sensu varias, respectu Iudæ proditoris vero proprie intelligantur pro pecunia 30. argenteorum, uti interpretatus est Matthæus. Tum vero figulus significabit primo figulum, prophetæ temporibus in scenam prodeuntem, ad emendum lateres, ad instaurandum templum, deinde vero figulum post aliquot secula venditurum agrum suum Sacerdotibus, uti somniavit Calvinus. Quæ quam absona sint, ostendit luculenter Pareo, Calvinum suum defendenti B. Ægid. Hunnius in Anti-Pareo, altero loco XI. p. 480. Ne autem ambigamus, Calvini hic vestigiis insistere Grotium, conferenda sunt, quæ habet ipse in annot. ad Matth. 17, 9. p. 476.

Dictum hoc Jeremiæ, repetitum à Zacharia, in eorum est genere, quæ primitus res illorum temporum significarent, ita tamen, ut in Christi tempora etiam magis congruerent, quod Deus manifestum fecit singulari eventuum directione. Nam apud Zachariam sensus hic est primo intentus, qualem & apud Jeremiam fuisse, credibile est: Deus ut sua beneficia in populum Hebræum collata ingrata nimis accepta doceat, ait operæ in illos impensæ mercedem à se postulatam. Assignatum sibi à populo vile pretium, quo minima æstimari solent mancipia, triginta siclos. Se vero illud pretium jussisse projici in agrum aliquem, in quem fragmenta fictilium projici solebant: quo facto demonstratum voluit, omnem pompam ceremoniarum, qua impleta egregiam se beneficiis divinis gratiam referre, Hebræi existimabant, cum abesset pius animus, indignam esse, quæ à se acceptaretur. Hoc vero omne sicut ad Jeremiæ & Zachariæ tempora pertinebat, ita multo magis congruebat Christi temporibus. Atq́; ideo factum est divina providentiæ gubernatione, ut quod ἀλληγορικῶς tunc erat dictum, Christi ætate manente sensu illo κατ᾽ ἀλληγορίαν, etiam secundum proprietatem verborum impleretur, quod genus impletionis vatici- ci- niorum in hac mortis Christi historia sæpe occurret. Deus enim in Christo æstimatus est à Pontificibus si- clis triginta, cum tanti emtus est in Christum prodi- tor: atq; ea pecunia vere in agrum figulinum non tam impensa, quam contemtim projecta est, facto quidem Pontificum, consilio autem divino: unde quod illi fe- cerunt, recte Deo dirigente adscribitur. Hæc Gro- tius. At frivola illa sunt, assignatos fuisse Deo à po- pulo loco mercedis 30. siclos, quos projicere jussus fuerit Zacharias in agrum aliquem, in quem fra- gmenta fictilium projici solebant, idemque etiam Jeremiæ temporibus contigisse. Unde enim con- stat vel Zachariæ, vel Jeremiæ temporibus idem quoque contigisse? Non certe alloquitur Deus hic Zachariam, sed Christum, quod antea ostendi- mus. Jam si κατ' ἀλληγορίαν solum id dictum fuit a Zacharia, & notati per 30. argenteos ritus pietate vacui, quod vult Grotius, quomodo projici jussus est 30. istos argenteos Zacharias in agrum? Num jussit Dominus projicere argenteos 30. metaphori- cos, h. e. ritus pietate vacuos, seu frivolos hypo- critarum cultus? Porro, si id asseratur, quomo- do simul res gesta Ieremiæ, & Zachariæ temporibus, projectione 30. argenteorum, ac præterea res ge- renda tempore N. T. iisdem verbis indicabitur, & nummi illi ἀλληγορικῶς tamen etiam intelligen- di erunt? Ἀσύςατα, & inepta hæc sunt. Sic enim necessario sequetur (quod Pareo opposuit B. Hun- nius) triginta argenteos non jam unam sustinere si- gnificationem (sicut quidem nos Matthæum secuti, statuimus) quin neque duas duntaxat, sed omnino jam 30. argenteorum appellatione apud Zachariam triplicem usurpationem & significationem insinuari, æquivocatione hactenus inaudita, cunctisque doctis incognita & incomperta. Primo enim denota- bunt illas hypocritarum nugas in sacrificiis sine fi- de præstitis, aliisque ceremoniis sitas, atque sic metaphorice capientur. Secundo significabunt eos materiales nummos, seu argenteos, quos tempore Zachariæ fingitur populus symboli vice appendis- se seu Prophetæ, seu Domino. Tertio significabunt alios plane diversos argenteos, itidem sumptos pro- prie, quos Judas accepit à Sacerdotibus. Jam vero explicet etiam cui id tueri libet, typum, & nos e- doceat, qui argentei, quorum sint typi? num meta- phorice intellecti verorum? vel hi veri (bis sum- pti, semel Zachariæ tempore, postea tempore pas- sionis Christi) junctim sint typi cultuum hypocri- ticorum? an vero alterutri? vel ii quibus Zacha- riæ seculo æstimatus est Dominus, fuerint typi eo- rum, quibus appretiatus est tempore passionis suæ Christus? Absurdum est, posteriores dicere ty- pum priorum, siquidem in talibus typi præcedere solent res typis delineatas. Sin dicat, priores illos esse typum posteriorum, quos Judas accepit, prin- cipium petet: quandoquidem haud dum evicit, ta- les argenteos proprie dictos extra visionem forin- secus sic gestam populum appendisse Domino, nec est verisimile, quod Judæi tempore Zachariæ tale quid fecerint: Adde quod recepta triplici usurpa- tione vocabuli argenteorum jam totus ille contex- tus triplicem expositionem ex necessitate requiret, hoc modo: Appenderunt mercedem meam 30. argen- teos, i. e. nugas cultuum hypocriticorum: & deinde 30. veros argenteos: sed & tempore Christi appende- runt alios veros argenteos Judæ proditori pretium æ- stimationis Messiæ. Et dixit Dominus ad me: Pro- jice ad figulum, id est, Tu Zacharia, argenteos meta- phorice sumtos damna: deinde argenteos proprie in- tellectos projice in domum Domini ad figulum: sed & tu Iuda alteros 30. argenteos, quos tibi scelere compa- rasti, projice in templum, ut dentur figulo. His mon- strosis glossematum commentis opus non est iis, qui limpidam veritatem à Matthæo Evangelista commonstratam in interpretando unice sequun- tur. Nihil hic Propheta de mercede hypocritica, quæ 30. argenteorum notetur nomine, nihil de ceremo- niis absque pietatis sensu peractis, nihil de sacrificiis, nihil prorsus de figulo emente lateres aut tegulas, ni- hil de ruinis templi restaurandis agitur. Sunt hæc pura puta commenta Calvini, imo Satanæ ludibria, quibus hoc tam illustre vaticinium de passione Do- mini proditum, atra fuligine Judaicarum opinio- num denigrare satagit. De passione Christi vati- cinatur Propheta, deque argenteis 30. non meta- phorice, sed proprie intellectis, numerandis Judæ proditori, & ab eo projiciendis rursum in domum Do- mini, ut figulo darentur, non ut ille tegulas emeret aut lateres (facessant hæ nugæ gerris Siculis inanio- res) sed in sepulturam peregrinorum. Cujus rei in- dubius interpres est Matthæus, à quo Calvinus, so- lo novitatis studio turpissime dissentit re & facto, quantumvis verbis nolit ei videri contrarius. Hæc B. Prædecessor noster Calvino, hæc Pareo ejusdem hyperaspistæ opposuit; hæc Grotio Calvinum hic sequenti opponere iisdem verbis voluimus. Ulte- riorem enim non merentur refutationem, cum principium tantum petant: id genus impletionis va- ticiniorum sæpe occurrere, ut quæ allegorice dicta, e- tiam secundum proprietatem verborum impleta sint. Nullum certe exemplum ejusmodi proferre po- tuit. Nec id perspicuitati aut simplicitati Scriptu- ræ convenit, imo, ut ostensum, perquam absur- dum est. Respicere Christum advenditionem sui à Juda proditore factam, eamque ceu testimonium maximi contemtus sui adducere, fatetur Willius: & toti populo imputatur, quod inter Judam solum & Sacerdotes gestum, quia contractum illum inter Judam vendentem, & Pharisæos ementes populus suo suffragio comprobavit, & ratum esse voluit, quando illum, cui pauculos ante dies acclamatio- ne sua regium honorem exhibuerat, ad crucis sup- plicium poposcit.

Sed pergamus in Prophetæ explicatione. ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD ME : PROJICE ILLUD AD STATUARIUM. Dicta illa sunt ad eum, qui antea dixerat: afferte pretium meum, & pro quo appenderunt XXX. argenteos vers. 12. Dicta ad eum, qui vers. 9. dixerat; non pascam vos, & virgam amœnitatis sciderat, & irritum fecerat fœdus suum cum populo Judaico v. 10. dicta ad eum, qui antea paverat gregem, & succiderat tres Pastores v. 8. cui id commendarat Deus Pater v. 1. pasce pascua occisionis. Is vero alius nullus est, quam Messias θεάνθρωπος: Argumentum invictum hoc est, quia ἀδαμαντίνως omnia cohærent. Quod au- tem in Vulgata dicitur. ad STATUARIUM, re- cte reddidit Grotius ad figulum, atque ita redden- dum esse agnovit Hieronymus, errorem suum prio- rem dissimulans. Pro πλάστη atq; fictore statuarium olim interpretatus sum, verbi ambiguitate compulsus, quod statuarium fictoremque uno sermone significat. Quod autem Grotius ad figulum idem esse vult, quod ad figulinam aream, ad quam projecta fuerint fracta templi fictilia, in eo à Calvino seductus est, æque ut in sensu metaphorico, quem hisce affuit: projice tanquam rem nihili, non plus Deo faciendum quam fractum fictile. A proprietate literæ non discedendum sine fontica causa. Nec metaphori- cam illam interpretationem admittit Matthæus, qui proprie figulum intellexit. Ad figulum projicien- dum dicitur pretium, quod immediate eo deferen- dum sit. Nam postea delatum dicitur ad domum Domini, sed τελικῶς, ut nempe figulo cessuros illos 30. argenteos indicetur, quemadmodum huic loco facem præfert Matthæus, dum à figulo agrum hisce argenteis emtum esse docet. Subjungit Propheta, vel potius Dominus apud Prophetam: DECO- RUM f. egregium sane & magnum PRETIUM! Quæ indignationem Christi exprimunt, quod in- star vilissimæ personæ vendituri ipsum sint. Non opus hic mutatione personæ, uti Osiander putat.
