Quid enim ad projectionem pretii in templum at- tinet? etsi Matth. c. 27, 5. à Juda factam dicat, non ideo Propheta Judæ personam sustinet, cum Do- minus ait: projice illud ad figulum: Sed uti antea Filius Dei locutus est, ita etiam hic sine mutatione personæ ilia ad se dicta testatur. Projecisse autem ipse dicitur pretium sui, quod ita dixerit animum Judæ, ut quod impie à Judæis sumserat, in templum projiceret, atque illud in usum figuli cederet, ut pro agro in sepulturam peregrinorum daretur, quem- admodum historia passionis docet. Indicatur ergo tantum Christi providentia mala ad finem bonum directa fuisse. Cum Judas cuperet argentum in suum usum convertere, & Sacerdotes mallent ad se recipere, tamen Christum, quanquam in summa exinanitione coram Pilato consistentem, adegisse Judam sua omnipotentia, ut mercedem iniquitatis redderet, & sacerdotum animos permovisse, ne thesauro templi adponerent, verum agrum figuli emerent, uti hic habet Tarnovius p. 308. Perver- tit autem hic iterum mentem Prophetæ Grotius, quod pretium illud projectum fuerit non in domum Domini, uti Matthæus testatur, sed propè domum Domini, in aream, quam fingit proxime templum figulis concessam, in quam fragmenta fictilium, imo aliæ sordes abjici consueverint, ut suum sensu metaphoricum exsculpat, quod tanquam res nihili habeatur ritus victimarum sine pietate oblatarum, quem per 30. siclos intelligit. Quo nomine etiam comminiscitur, hæc ad Zachariam dicta, & à Zacha- ria, seu reipsa, seu ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ facta esse, quæ vero ad Messiam dicta, & in Novo demum Testamento completa esse, cum è textus συνεχεία tum ex inter- pretatione Matthæi luculenter constat.

Sequitur in textu: ET PRÆSCIDI VIR- GAM MEAM SECUNDAM. Fingit Gro- tius, priora per parenthesin esse inserta, jam autem continuari Dei sermonem. At nulla opus παρεν- θέσει, cohærent & consequuntur omnia bono or- dine. Virga secunda, quæ appellabatur FUNICU- LUS, ab ipso perperam explicatur concordia tri- buum. Legem divinam ea notari diximus. Quæ respectu Judæorum contracta, cum post Christum ad necem 30. argenteis emtum, & ad mortem tra- ditum ipsi legum quoque privati virga sunt. UT DISSOLVEREM GERMANITATEM IN- TER JUDAM ET ISRAEL, ut isto vinculo societatis Ecclesiasticæ & politicæ sublato, mera re- linqueretur confusio, atque expiraret penitus quic- quid supererat adhuc communionis in Juda & Israe- le, nulla tribuum reliqua essent commercia, nulla communionis vincula, omnes in orbem disperge- rentur, & æternæ confusioni involverentur. Recte sensum expressit Osiander: Abstuli tandem etiam ab eis legem Mosaicam abrogavi eam, sustuli sacri- ficia & totum cultum Leviticum: ille cum Tem- plo Jerosolymitano totus concidit, qui prius ner- vus fraternitatis erat inter Israëlitas. Caruerunt Judæi lege, post Christi passionem atque mortem, quia nullum habebant verum sensum legis, ne qui- dem unum versum in lege, qui non opinionum va- rietate implicitus sit, quemadmodum ipsi faten- tur in Epitom. Thalmudicorum volum, nulla habent sacrificia, nullos ritus alios, in lege Levitica præscriptos, sed quidquid hodie in cultu divino suscipiunt, non ad normam ipsius legis, sed ad præscriptū Thalmudicarum fabularum faciunt, quas omni scripturæ præferunt: vocant funda- mentum legis Mosaice, recreationem cordis & ossi- um, thesaurum Dei, quod sane nihil aliud est, quam Lege Domini penitus destitui, ut hic B. Balduin.

Quæ vero v. 15. sequuntur, novam visionem constituunt: non vero usum ante dictorum, ut nu- gatur Grotius, ostendunt: neque verba hic am- plius à Deo Patre ad Filium diriguntur, sed Prophe- tæ hæc dicta sunt. Longe enim dispar est horum & superiorum ratio. Nam in superioribus ea e- rant prædicata, quæ Prophetæ nullatenus conve- niebant, nec ulli nisi Messiæ θεανθρώπῳ tribui possint. At quod nunc sequitur de assumenda per- sona stulti pastoris, nullatenus convenit Messiæ: ADHUC SUME TIBI VASA PASTORIS STULTI. Vocula עוד Adhuc non indicat, eidem personæ hæc dici, ad quam præcedentia dicta: Id enim haud congruere, jam monitum. Sed AD- HUC id quoque eventurum. Non ergo orationis vel allocutionis, sed eventuum συνέχεια eadem innuitur, ut recte videntur observasse Vinarienses. Referri etiam non incommode possunt hæc verba ad prædictionem c. 10, 3. & 11, 8. factam, quod AD- HUC de falsis Doctoribus vaticinari, atque eorum perversam administrationem ac supplicia indicare debeat, quæ jam antea intimarar: super pastores i- ratus est furor meus, & super hircos visitabo. Item Exscidi tres pastores mense uno, vasa pastoris stulti sunt ejusmodi vasa, quæ non conveniant, nisi stoli- do pastori, verbi gratia, baculus fractus, pera absq; cibo, vas sine oleo, fistula rauca, ad significandam falsorum Doctorum stoliditatem, vel instrumenta sævi pastoris, arma baculus gravis, gladius ad jugu- landum, forcipes ad tondendum oviculas. QUIA ECCE EGO SUSCITABO PASTOREM IN TERRA, QUI DERELICTA NON VI- SITABIT &c. Per hunc pastorem intelligit Cyrillus & Hieronymus Anti-Christum. Sed quum hæc adhuc feriant Judæos, quibus πανολε- θρίαν minatus est Dominus, non apparet quomodo hic Anti-Christus ille, quem Paulus & Johannes prædixere, ingeri possit. Plerique Pastorem μο- ναδικῶς dici, sed intelligi πληθυντικῶς censent: ut pœnis, quas populo ingrato prædixerat, hæc etiam accessura indicetur, quod Dominus immittere ve- lit Doctores, qui curam gregis non gerant, sed a- varitiæ dediti tantum sint, siquidem ipsi Christum ejusque discipulos repulerint. Pertinent ergo hæc ad tempora novissima status Judæorum. Tremel- lius & Junius de Regibus administratoribus & pro- curatoribus Judææ sceleratis, qui exhausere & con- sumpsere Judæam, interpretatur, sed respiciuntur hic falsi Doctores, non Reges vel administratores Poli- tici: quod tum expositio Christi & Apostolorum, tum officii administratio docet. Quæ vere pessi- ma describitur partim negative, quod talis pastor DERELICTA vel SUCCISA NON VISI- TABIT, ovibus, quæ conscientiam succisam ha- bent, non succurret. 2. DISPERSUM NON QUÆRET, quæ in errorum avia & præcipitia dispersæ sunt, non reducet in viam veritatis & ju- stitiæ, vel juxta Ebræum הנער, quæ animo impru- denti sunt, & ob infirmitatem sibi consulere nesci- unt, earum informationem non suscipiat. (3) CON- TRITUM NON SANABIT, quarum animi vulnerati sunt, earum curam non habeat. (4) ID QUOD STAT, NON ENUTRIET, persi- stentes in fide non confirmet, nec hortatur ad per- severantiam, unde facile fieri potest, ut à suggestio- nibus carnis, & Diaboli technis superati, animæ jacturam faciant: partim affirmative (1) CAR- NES PINGVIUM COMEDET, non modo non faciet officium boni pastoris, sed insuper lupo- rum instar sæviet in miseras oviculas, & bonis audi- torum sese pascet. 2. UNGVLAS EARUM DISSOL- VET, dominabitur ovibus suis, ne quidem Magi- stratui parcens, cujus autoritati detrahet, eumque, quantum in ipso est, sibi subjugare studebit. Hæc impleta sunt non tantum in sacerdotibus & Phari- sæis, sed etiam in Pseudo-Christis, aliisque impo- storibus, ante πανωλεθρίαν Judaicam, qui miseram plebem à doctrina Apostolorum abducebant, eamque seditionibus & aliis periculis involvebant, de quibus Josephus libris de bello Judaic. Perpe- ram autem Romanos milites aut Duces per Pasto- rem stultum intelligit Christ. à Castro. Cum de Pastoribus Ecclesiasticis aperte loquatur Dominus.

His autem falsis Doctoribus minatur Dominus gravissimas pœnas v. 17. O PASTOR ET IDOLUM DERELINQUENS GREGEM, GLADIUS SUPER BRACHIUM EJUS: ET SUPER OCULUM DEXTRUM EJUS. BRA- CHIUM EJUS ARIDITATE SICCABITUR, ET OCULUS DEXTER EJUS TENEBRESCENS OBSCURABITUR. In Ebræo est, væ pastori NIHILI. Per brachium po- tentia, per oculum dextrum consilium & pruden- tia notatur; talem pastorem & fortitudine, & con- silio, & prudentia orbatum iri, ut & vires & frau- des ejus vertantur in ludibrium, vel omni robore & lumine spirituali privatus plane excæcetur, & in mentem reprobam detur. Per gladium intel- ligit B. Balduinus verbum Domini Eph. 6, 17. Ebr. 4, 12. quo solo omnia malorum pastorum præsi- dia discutiuntur, & in nihilum rediguntur. Sic etiam paraphrastæ Vinarienses: Alle ihre Macht, so durch den Arm wird angedeutet, und alle ihr Wiz und Verstand, so durch das Auge wird ange- deutet, sol durch das Schwerdt des Geistes durchs Wort Gottes Eph. 6, 7. Hebr. 4, 12. zu nicht gemacht werden. Alii vocem gladii pro pœna accipiunt, & gladio divini judicii, quo talium brachium, ocu- lumque dextrum percussurus sit Dominus. Gladio suæ vindictæ robur brachii tui confringet. Arescet brachium, h. e. vigor ejus defluet, ita ut sit quasi li- gnum putridum, deinde oculus dexter ejus, h. e. sa- nitas mentis, id est, recta intelligentia contrahendo contrahetur, ut reddidit Calvinus.

CONCIO SEPTIMA ET ULTIMA MERE EVANGELICA.

SECTIO I. DE VERO ISRAELE.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

Consolation against the cruelty of tyrants.

The pitiable madness of the enemies of the Church is foretold, and the wondrous defense of the Church, the power and efficacy of the Leaders (the Apostles and their successors), who like a fire will lay waste to the enemies, and the strengthening of the fearful: and the outpouring of the Spirit of grace and of prayers is promised, and penitential lamentation on account of the passion and death of Christ, and consequently the conversion of many to the Lord.

Punishment awaits the reprobate: the Spirit strengthens the sick.

V. 1. THE BURDEN OF THE WORD OF THE LORD UPON ISRAEL.) After that dissension brought about by Manasseh, for the same cause, that is, the neglect of the divine law, he proceeds to foretell other evils about to come: which itself also will draw with it a new breaking of the cord, that is, a new dissension, namely in the times of Antiochus. Understand here by Israel the greater part of those who had sprung from Israel, which just as formerly was in the power of Samaria, so then it will be in the power of Jerusalem, with the Shechemites about to obtain the lesser part. The Hebrews refer these things to the times of Gog: rightly if they understood Antiochus himself by Gog, as we do in relation to Ezekiel: but they themselves expect Gog and Magog a little before the end of the world, which, as believed by them, the Apocalypse seizes upon, and shows to be true in an anagogical sense.

How rashly and falsely Grotius may have snatched the preceding things to Manasseh, the son-in-law of Sanballat, of whom neither a trace nor a vestige is seen here, we judge to be by no means obscure. Therefore, the present gloss rests on no foundation, that the Prophet is now prophesying about a new schism that will arise in the times of Antiochus. For there is nothing that convinces that the times of Antiochus are looked to here. With whatever facility, therefore, it is asserted, with the same it can also be rejected. We do not delay over the absurdities of the Hebrews who refer these things to the times of Gog: than whom, however, the Grotian trifles are no sounder, that by the Gog of Ezekiel is understood Antiochus. But to them is now added even blasphemy, because, forsooth, the Apocalypse SEIZES UPON those absurdities of the Hebrews, or an ingrained error, and shows it to be true in an allegorical sense. Does piety permit one to speak thus of the Holy Spirit, the author of the Apocalypse? Will the Spirit of truth SEIZE UPON errors and make them His own? or will the God-breathed book, or the most holy Spirit Himself, be occupied with turning common errors into allegories? Away with impious trifles and blasphemies! There is nothing here about a new breaking of the CORD, such as that which was under Jeroboam, which Grotius dreamed was designated in the preceding chapter, v. 14.

Nor is it necessary that we understand THE BURDEN OF THE WORD OF THE LORD concerning Israel, as if sad and burdensome things were being preached to Israel. Since the Hebrew particle can be rendered FOR Israel, or on account of Israel, the burden being denounced against the enemies, but for the good or thanks of Israel. Which sense most interpreters follow, and the context itself demands. For burdensome and sad things are not preached to Israel, but to the enemies of Israel, to whom defense and divine grace are promised: not to mention that those who refer the BURDEN to Israel understand it of the cross and affliction of the Church, which turns out for its own good. Thus, with the blessed Luther and the blessed Winckelmann leading the way: This chapter contains a prophecy concerning the afflictions and persecutions of the Christian Church, and at the same time also concerning its defense, the confusion of its persecutors, and living consolations through the Spirit of grace and supplication. Where, secondly, the foundation of this promise of the Holy Spirit is indicated, namely, Christ crucified. Furthermore, although some, for instance Theodoret, Remigius, Hugo, wish it to be noted by Israel that they are the descendants of Jacob, to whom also one of ours, the blessed Wigandus, has added in this way: that it is signified here that they would indeed have certain afflictions, but that God would preserve some state of the polity, until the promises concerning the Messiah are fulfilled. That not only neighboring Gentiles, but also the Romans would invade the Jews, just as happened when Pompey subjugated the Jews and reduced them to the form of a province, in the Year of the World 3903, in which dangers, however, God has hitherto preserved the Jewish nation; others, however, prefer to accept these things concerning the Church, which is the Israel of God, such as Lyranus, Vatablus, Arias, Isidorus, Clarius, and from our own, the blessed Balduinus, Tarnovius, Winckelmann. It does not speak here of Israel according to the flesh, from whom in the preceding chapter He made a divorce on account of the contempt of the Gospel with these words: I will not feed you; that which dies, let it die. Likewise: and I took my staff, which was called lovely, and I broke it. From the Reformed, Junius and Willius, who here also refutes his own Calvin and Gualther, because they have invented another reason for the inscription, namely, that the Prophet is inveighing against the Israelites who had neglected the return and were still daily despising the grace of God, intent on their own delights and earthly things, by which it is shown that that thin people, for whose salvation they despair, will continue even in the land and will repress the insults of their enemies. In this, however, Willius is mistaken, that he imagines that the word massa in his fabricated synthesis of decades denotes not a burden, but a carrying, and wishes the collection or Symbol of the Prophets concerning the state of the true Church to be judged in this title, if indeed he dreams that prophecies are contained here, according to the series of times up to the end of the world concerning the seven periods of the Church of the New Testament, which were devised by Thomas Brightman the Englishman, together with his colleague D. Ludov. Crocio interpolated, and attempted to extract from the seven epistles written to as many Asian churches in the second chapter of the Apocalypse, which he also determines that Zechariah follows here in order, when he sets them forth succinctly in this chapter up to v. 9, and then a little more distinctly from v. 10 of this chapter to the end of the prophecy. Thus, with a wondrous invention, these new interpreters strive to extract from the seven aforementioned epistles of the Son of God the seven periods of the Church of the New Testament, and then to introduce the same into the prophecy of Zechariah, and to interpret this from the Apocalypse in an unheard-of way, so that they may promise not only the cessation of collisions among Protestants (by which name they designate Lutherans and Calvinists, and perhaps even the Papists themselves) but also a signal conversion of the Jews, and the addition of Oriental peoples after the hour of temptation in the Sardian period, in which they have persuaded themselves they are now acting, and under the Philadelphian period, they promise the same I know not what happiness. Which have no greater firmness than the golden tranquility of a thousand years, which Alstedius, along with certain others in the same school, dreamed was to be expected in this dregs of the world. Everything in those glosses is surely so arranged that the bare recitation of them is a solid refutation. Thus they collapse by their own vanity and futility. A greater semblance of truth might appear in the Grotian commentaries, which in most places appear sufficiently specious, which, however, when they are weighed more accurately, can by no means stand. Undoubtedly, just as Willius extends these things more than is just to later centuries, and the fates of the Church in the same, nay, even to the consummation of the age, and strives to force into them the periods of all times which he had conceived in his own mind: So it pleased Grotius to draw these back too much to earlier times, to such an extent that he admits no other prophecies in these final chapters of our Prophet than those which concern only ancient things under the Maccabees, even neglecting the interpretation of the New Testament, by which we are taught that most things concerning the passion of Christ, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the propagation of the Church throughout the world are to be accepted, and are therefore convinced that they refer to the times of the N.T. Whence both those explanations, namely the Willian and the Grotian, occurred to no one before them, as far as is known. For the sake of which to wish to reject the commonly received interpretations, approved in great part even by the authority of the Holy Spirit in the books of the N. Testament, would be to be blind in broad daylight.

8. Jerome observes yet two other explanations, which the Jews have embraced, one of which he does not so much reject as commit to the prudence of the reader. Which indeed also commends itself with a probable appearance; meanwhile, however, he teaches that Christian Doctors of the Church have handed down another sense, and have accepted these things concerning the perennial preservation of the Church; and he prefers their opinion to the Jewish explanation. There is a triple interpretation from that place in which we read: Behold I will make Jerusalem a lintel of surfeiting unto all the people round about, up to that place where it is written: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that cleaveth to me, says the Lord of hosts: Strike the shepherd and the sheep shall be scattered. For some of the Jews think these things are already in part fulfilled from Zorobabel down to Cn. Pompeius, who first took Judea and the temple, which history Josephus writes. But others, when Jerusalem shall have been restored at the end of the world, are to be fulfilled: which the miserable Jewish nation promises to itself with its ἠλευσιμώρῳ, whom we read of above as the foolish shepherd; but others, that is, we, who are reckoned by the name of Christ, record that they are daily fulfilled and to be fulfilled in the church down to the end of the world. And lest we extend the measure of the volume by individual points, proposing: These things say they, thus others suspect, we feel thus: We have placed three opinions, so that from the variety of interpretation, the prudent reader may understand what is to be chosen by whom. It will be helpful to compare those glosses of Jewish interpretation with the Grotian commentaries, so that the sensible reader may see how prone it is, if one wishes to indulge in one's own speculations, to snatch certain things from history, and to infer the same into the sacred text with some appearance of truth, and how easily, led away from the true sense, we stumble nevertheless, and remain in doubt among these plausible glosses, which one finally is to be approved, and held as genuine. But this must be warned of first here, if by chance anyone thinks that a place should be left for the Grotian or Jewish interpretation, by which the fulfillment of the prophecies is drawn back to the times of the Old Testament before the incarnation of the Word; one must take care entirely, lest one be carried away with the Jews or Grotius even to the distortion of those oracles which are clearly expounded in the New Testament concerning the passion of Christ, and his benefits, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the propagation of the kingdom of Christ, as if the same, as far as the literal sense is concerned, also exhibit a far different meaning. By which method the authority of the sacred books of the New Testament will be not a little shaken, and a door will be opened to Jewish impiety to elude the remaining prophecies of the Old Testament in a similar manner. Which indeed was attempted by Grotius in almost all the Prophetic oracles that treat of Christ and his kingdom, with sacrilegious impiety, even while the man's own conscience resisted. Concerning the last prophets indeed, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi, he himself confessed at the beginning of Haggai, that they, because they were the last of the prophets of the Old Covenant, therefore pointed the finger more openly to the new covenant and its leader Christ, and did not only figure him through other intermediate histories, but showed him directly. Which confession the truth itself extorted from him. But in this whole rather long prophet, Grotius did not leave us even a single prophecy safe, which treats of Christ, as far as the literal sense is concerned. That servant of the Lord, the branch in ch. 3, 8 and 6, 12, is to him Zorobabel. Nor does he understand the letter concerning the entry of the just King upon a donkey into the city of Jerusalem as being about anyone other than Zorobabel, however much the Evangelists proclaim with a sonorous voice that that King carried on a donkey was the Messiah, and even the Jews themselves for the most part acknowledge it. Nor does he acquiesce in the interpretation of the Evangelist concerning the price of the sold Messiah, which was predicted by our Prophet, ch. 11, 12, but he attaches to the Prophetic oracle a meaning that is clearly different; nor does he accept in the same sense what St. John interpreted from this chapter 12, 10 concerning the piercing of the Messiah, but he carries away the prophecy of the Prophet to those who in the time of the Maccabees fought against God with reproaches: nor finally does he interpret any other prophecy in this so clear a prophet concerning the Messiah according to the literal sense. Which is a certain proof that that man was not moved by the Spirit of truth, who cannot contradict himself, but by a spirit of giddiness.

Verse of the same.

THE LORD EXTENDING THE HEAVEN] He who extends the heaven, as if a tent. See Gen. 1, v. 6.

AND FOUNDING THE EARTH] He who gave the earth a fixed place in the air itself.

AND FORMING THE SPIRIT OF MAN IN HIM] He who implanted the spirit of life in the first man.

They abuse these words, who invent that God even today creates souls and infuses them into our bodies, against the open letter of the divine blessing made to man concerning the propagation of his species, which certainly is not the propagation of an inanimate body, but an animated one, Gen. 1, 27: But Grotius rightly notes that the first creation of the soul is looked to, just as the creation of heaven and earth made in the beginning is also indicated.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Consolatio adversus sævitiam tyran- norum.

Prædicitur hostium Ecclesiæ miseranda de- mentatio & miranda Ecclesiæ defensio, Du- cum (Apostolorum & successorum ipsorum) vis & efficacia, qui instar incendii hostes depopulabuntur, ac meticuloforum etiam corroboratio: & promittitur effusio Spiri- tus gratiæ, & precum, ac planctus pœniten- tialis ob passionem & mortem Christi, a- deoq; conversio plurimorum ad Dominum.

Pœna manet reprobos: confirmat Spiritus ægros.

V. 1. ONUS VERBI DOMINI SUPER ISRAEL.) Post illud factum per Manassem dissidium, ex eadem causa, id est, neglectu legis divinæ, alia superventura mala per- git prædicere: ipsa quoque novam funiculi rupturam, id est, novum dissidium, tractura secum, Antiochi nempe temporibus. Israelem hic intellige majorem eorum, qui ex Israele orti erant, partem, quæ sicut olim erat penes Samariam, ita tunc futura erit penes Hierosoly- ma, Sicimitis partem obtenturis minorem. Hæc ad tem- pora Gog referunt Hebræi: recte si per Gog ipsum Antio- chum intelligerent, ut nos ad Ezechielem: sed ipsi Gogum & Magogum paulo ante mundi finem exspectant, quod, ut ab ipsis creditum, arripit Apocalypsis, & sensu ἀναγω- γικῷ verum esse ostendit.

QUam temere ac falso præcedentia ad Manas- sen Sanballati generum abripuerit Grotius, de quo nec vola, nec vestigium hic conspicitur, mini- me obscurum esse arbitramur. Nullo itaque funda- mento præsens glossa nititur, de novo dissidio nunc vaticinari Prophetam Antiochi temporibus ori- turo. Nihil enim est, quod convincat, Antiochi tempora hic respici. Qua facilitate itaque id as- feritur, eadem etiam id rejici potest. Ebræorum ineptias ad tempora Gog hæc referentium nihil mo- ramur: quibus vero nihil saniores sunt nugæ Gro- tianæ, per Gogum Ezechielis intelligi Antiochum. Illis autem jam accedit etiam blasphemia, quod nempe ineptias illas Ebræorum, vel errorem inolitumn ARRIPIAT Apocalypsis, & sensu allegorico verum esse ostendat. Itane de Spiritu S. Apocalypseos autore loqui permittit pietas? An Spiritus verita- tis errores ARRIPIET, suosque faciet? an er- roribus vulgatis in allegorias vertendis occupabi- tur liber θεόπνευστος, vel ipse sanctissimus Spiri- tus? Facessant impiæ nugæ & blasphemiæ! Nihil hic de nova FUNICULI ruptura, qualis illa fue- rit sub Jeroboamo, quam Cap. præcedente v. 14. designatam esse somniavit Grotius.

Nec ONUS VERBI DOMINI עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל necessum est in- telligamus, ac si tristia ac onerosa Israeli prædican- tur. Siquidem particula Ebræa reddi possit PRO Israele, vel propter Israelem, onus hostibus denun- ciari, sed Israelis bono vel gratia. Quem sensum plerique Interpp. sequuntur, & contextus ipse po- stulat. Non enim onerosa & tristia prædicuntur Israeli, sed hostibus Israelis, cui promittitur defen- sio & gratia divina: ut taceamus, quod, qui O- NUS referant ad Israelem, de cruce & afflictione Ecclesiæ, quæ ipsius bono cedit, id intelligant. Ita præeunte B. Luthero, B. Winckelm. Continet hoc caput vaticinium de afflictionibus & persecutioni- bus Ecclesiæ Christianæ, & simul etiam de ejus defen- sione, persecutorum confusione & vivis consolationibus per Spiritum gratiæ & precum. Ubi secundo hu- jus promissionis Spiritus S. fundamentum indica- tur nimirum Christus crucifixus. Porro etsi non- nulli, Theodoretes puta, Remigius, Hugo, per Israe- lem Jacobi posteros notari velint, quibus etiam ac- cessit è nostris B. Wigandus hoc modo: quod hic si- gnificetur, eos quidem habituros esse afflictiones quas- dam, verum Deum conservaturum esse politiæ statum aliquem, donec compleantur promissiones de Messia. Quod non tantum finitimi gentiles, sed etiam Romani Judæos invasuri sint, sicuti factum, cum Pompejus Judæos subjugavit, atq; in Provinciæ formam redegit, Anno Mundi 3903. in quibus vero periculis Deus gen- tem Judæam adhuc conservavit; Alii tamen malunt de Ecclesia, quæ est Israel Dei, hæc accipere, ut- pote Lyranus, Vatablus, Arias, Isidorus, Clarius, è nostris B. Balduinus, Tarnovius, Winckelmannus. Non loquitur hic de Israele secundum carnem, à quo præcedenti capite divortium fecit ob con- temtum Evangelii his verbis: Non pascam vos, quod moritur moriatur. Item: & tuli virgam meam, quæ vocabatur amabilis, & confregi eam. E Reformatis Junius, Willius, qui Calvinum etiam suum hic redarguit, & Gualtherum, quod aliam inscriptionis rationem commenti sint, invehi nempe Prophetam contra Israelitas, qui reditum neglexerant, & gratiam Dei quotidie adhuc con- temnebant, deliciis ac terrenis suis intenti, quibus oftendatur tenuem illum populum, de cujus salute desperant, perennaturum etiam in terra, & hoftium infultus repreffurum. In eo tamen fallitur Willius, quod confictæ suæ συνθέσεως δεκαδίων vocem משׂא non onus, sed comportationem notare comminisca- tur, ac collectionem seu Symbolum Prophetarum de Statu veræ Ecclesiæ in hoc titulo judicari velit, siq; ui- dem Prophetias hic contineri, juxta seriem tempo- rum usque ad finem mundi de periodis septem Ecclesiæ N.T. somniet, quas à Thoma Brigthmanno Anglo ex- cogitatas cum suo Collega D. Ludov. Crocio inter- polavit, & è septem Epistolis ad totidem Ecclesias A- siaticas exaratis Ap. II. cap. exsculpere conatus est, quas etiam Zachariam hic ordine persequi, cum succinctim in hoc capite usque ad v. 9. tum pau- lo distinctius à v. 10. hujus capitis ad finem Prophe- tiæ statuit. Ita miro commento novelli isti inter- pretes è septem epistolis prædictis filii Dei, septem periodos Ecclesiæ N. T. eruere, atque easdem de- inde prophetiæ Zachariæ inducere, & hanc ex A- pocalypsi inaudito modo interpretari satagunt, ut Ecclesiæ non modo cessationem collisionum inter Protestantes (quo nomine Lutheranos & Calvinia- nos indigitant, forte etiam Pontificios ipsos) sed Judæorum quoq; conversionem insignem, & Orien- talium populorum appositionem post horam tentatio- nis in Sardenfi periodo, in qua jam sese agere persua- si sunt, exantlatam polliceantur, & sub Philadel- phensi periodo, nescio quam felicitatem, eidem promittant. Quæ non majorem firmitatem ha- bent, quam mille annorum aurea tranquillitas, quam Alstedius cum aliis quibusdam in eadem Schola somniavit, in hac fæce mundi expectandam. Omnia profecto in illis gloffematis ita comparata sunt, ut nuda eorundem recitatio solida sit confuta- tio. Ita vanitate ac futilitate sua concidunt. Ma- jor videri possit similitudo veri in Grotianis com- mentis, quæ in plerisque satis speciosa apparent, quæ tamen, ubi accuratius expenduntur, subsiste- re minime possunt. Nimirum, uti Willius justo am- plius hæc extendit ad secula posteriora, & fata Ec- clesiæ in iisdem, imo usq; ad consummationem seculi, atque periodos, quas animo suo conceperat, o- mnium temporum iisdem inferre molitur: Ita Grotio placuit hæc nimium retrahere ad anteriora tempora, adeo, ut nec alia admittat in Prophetæ nostri postremis hisce capitibus vaticinia, quam quæ tantum vetera sub Maccabæis concernant, posthabita etiam interpretatione Novi Testamen- ti, qua de passione Christi, de effusione Spiritus S. de propagatione Ecclesiæ per orbem pleraque accipienda esse edocemur, ac proinde tempora N. T. respici convincimur. Unde utræque illæ explicationes, Williana nempe & Grotiana, ante ipsos nemini, quod constet, in mentem venerunt. Quarum causa communiter receptas interpreta- tiones auctoritate etiam Spir. S. in libris N. Test. magnam partem comprobatas, reprobare velle, esset in media luce caligare.

8. Hieronymus observat adhuc alias duas expli- cationes, quas Judæi amplexi fuerint, quarum al- teram non tam reprobat ipse, quam prudentiæ lectoris committit. Quæ utique etiam probabili specie se commendat; interea tamen Christianos Ecclesiæ Doctores alium sensum tradidisse, ac de Ecclesiæ conservatione perenni hæc accepisse, docet; eorumque sententiam Judaicæ explicationi præfert. Triplex interpretatio est ab eo loco, in quo legimus: Ecce ego ponam Hierusalem superlimi- nare crapulæ omnibus populis in circuitu, usq; ad eum locum, ubi scriptum est: Framea suscita- re super Pastorem meum, & super virum cohæ- rentem mihi,dicit Dominus exercituum: Percute pastorem & dispergentur oves. Alii enim Judæo- rum putant jam hæc ex parte completa à Zorobabele usƣ ad Cn. Pompejum, qui primus Judæam cepit & templum, quam historiam scribit Josephus. Alii vero, quando Hierusalem fuerit instaurata in fine mundi esse complenda: quod sibi cum ἠλευσιμώρῳ suo, quem supra stultum pastorem legimus miserabilis gens Judæa promittit; alii autem, hoc est, nos, qui Christi censemur nomine, in ecclesia usƣ ad finem mundi quotidie expleri & explenda memoramus. Et ne per singula extendamus modum voluminis, proponentes: Hæc dicunt illi, sic alii suspicantur, nos ita sentimus: Tres posuimus sententias, ut ex interpretationis varietate, quid cui cooprandum sit prudens lector intelligat. Juvabit conferre cum Grotianis commentis illas Judaicæ interpretatio- nis glossas, ut videat lector cordatus, quam pro- num sit,si propriis quis indulgere velit speculatio- nibus, ex historia quædam arripere, eademque textui sacro aliqua veri specie inferre, quodƣ ita facile à vero sensu abducti cespitemus tamen, & dubii hæreamus in istis verisimilibus glossis, quæ- nam tandem approbanda sit, & pro germana ha- benda.Id autem imprimis hic monendum,si forte quis locum Grotianæ, aut Judaicæ interpretationi relinquendum censeat,qua vaticiniorum comple- mentum retrahitur ad tempora Vet. Test. ante ἐνσάρκωσιν τů λόγư; cavendum omnino esse, ne cum Judæis, aut Grotio abripiatur etiam ad illo- rum oraculorum, quæ in Novo Testam. de passione Christi, ejusƣ beneficiis, de effusione Spiritus S. de propagatione regni Christi, luculenter exposita sunt, detorsionem, ac si eadem, quoad sensum literalem, etiam longe aliam sententiam exhibeant. Quo pacto autoritas librorum sacrorum Nov. Testam. non parum convelletur, & Judaicæ impietati por- ta aperietur,reliqua vaticinia Veteris Testamenti simili modo eludendi. Quod utique à Grotio in o- mnibus fere oraculis Propheticis, quæ de Christo, ejusque regno agunt, sacrilega impietate tenta- tum, renitente etiam propria hominis conscien tia. De Prophetis sane postremis Aggæo, Zacha- ria, Malachia, fassus ipse est sub initium Aggæi, eosdem, quia postremi fuêre Prophetarum Veteris fœderis, ideo ad novum fœdus & ducem ejus Chri- stum, digitum apertius intendere, nec tantum per medias historias alias eum figurare, sed directe mon- strare. Quam confessionem ipsa veritas eidem extorsit. Sed in toto hoc Propheta bene longo, ne unicum quidem vaticinium nobis salvum reli- quit Grotius, quod de Christo agat, quantum ad literalem sensum. Servus ille Domini germen c. 3, 8. & 6,12. ipsi est Zorobabel. Nec de alio,quam Zorobabele intelligit literam de ingressu Regis justi super asina in urbem Hierusalem, utut Evangelistæ sonora voce proclament, Regem illum asina ve- ctum esse Messiam, ipsique etiam Judæi magnam partem id agnoscant. Neque in pretio venditi Messiæ, quod à Propheta nostra prædictum, c. 11, 12. interpretationi Evangelistæ acquiescit, sed a- lium affingit oraculo Prophetico sensum plane di- versum; nec quæ de consixione Messiæ ex hoc cap. 12,10. interpretatus est S. Johannes, eodem susci- pit sensu, sed abripit vaticinium Prophetæ ad eos, qui tempore Maccabæorum probris conflixerunt Deum: nec denique ullum aliud vaticinium in hoc tam luculento Propheta de Messia secundum li- teralem sensum interpretatur. Quod certum est documentum, virum illum non à Spiritu verita- tis, qui sibi adversari nequit, sed à Spiritu vertigi- nis actum fuisse.

Vers. eod.

DOMINUS EXTENDENS COELUM] Qui cœlum extendit, quasi tentorium. Vide Gen. 1. v. 6.

ET FUNDANS TERRAM] Qui terræ fixum dedit locum in ipso aërę.

ET FINGENS SPIRITUM HOMINIS IN EO] Qui Spiritum vitæ primo homini indidit.

Abutuntur his verbis, qui Deum adhuc hodie animas creare, illasque corporibus nostris infundere, contra apertam literam benedictionis divinæ, homini de propagatione speciei suæ, quæ certe non est propagatio corporis exanimis, sed animati Gen. 1, 27. factæ, comminiscuntur: Sed recte notat Grotius respici primam animæ creationem, quemadmodum etiam creatio cœli & terræ in principio facta indigitatur.

## 12:2
Verse 2.

BEHOLD I WILL MAKE JERUSALEM A THRESHOLD OF DRUNKENNESS TO ALL PEOPLES ROUND ABOUT] A cup of drunkenness, the Chaldean not badly. The neighboring peoples will join themselves to Antiochus, and will behave themselves unseemly against the city of Jerusalem, as drunkards are wont to do.

AND JUDAH SHALL BE IN THE SIEGE AGAINST JERUSALEM] צור sometimes indeed means to besiege, but most often to afflict with evils: and therefore in very many places it is translated by θλίβειν. He speaks of a wonderful thing, that there would even be some from among the Jews who would behave themselves hostilely against Jerusalem, which had never happened before. These are Menelaus and the sons of Tobias, who, prepared to indulge their own ambition, to cast off the worship of God and the most holy laws, voluntarily summoned Antiochus to the destruction of their country and their laws. Jos. 12, 6. 2. Macc. 4, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ECCE EGO PONAM JERUSALEM SUPERLIMINARE CRAPULÆ OMNIBUS POPULIS IN CIRCUITU] Craterem ebrietatis, Chaldæus non male. Populi vicini adjungent se Antiocho, & adversus urbem Hierosolyma indecore se gerent, ut ebrii solent.

ET JUDA ERIT IN OBSIDIONE CONTRA JERUSALEM] צור interdum quidem obsidere significat, sed sæpissime malis afficere: ideoque plurimis locis per θλίβειν vertitur. Rem miram dicit, fore ut etiam ex Judæis sint, qui se in Hierosolyma hostiliter gerant, quod factum nunquam ante fuerat. Hi sunt Menelaus & Tobiæ Filii, qui parati, dum ambitioni suæ morem gererent, Dei cultum, sanctissimasque leges exuere, in exitium patriæ suæ ac legum, ultro Antiochum acciverunt. Jos. 12, 6. 2. Macc. 4, 5.

## 12:3
Ver. 3.

AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY, I WILL MAKE JERUSALEM A BURDENSOME STONE FOR ALL PEOPLES, ALL THAT BURDEN THEMSELVES WITH IT SHALL BE CUT IN PIECES] They shall be wounded by wounding. They will indeed test their strength against it, but not with impunity. Jerome explains this expression very well: It is the custom in the cities of Palestine, and even to this day the old custom is kept throughout all Judea, that in the villages, towns, and castles, round stones of very heavy weight are placed, to which the young men are accustomed to exercise themselves: and to lift them according to the variety of their strength, some to the knees, others to the navel, others to the shoulders and head, some even above the crown of the head, with straight and joined hands, demonstrating the magnitude of their strength, they lift the weight. In such an exertion it happens that in some, some part of the body is injured, in others, veins are ruptured. Claudian concerning Rome: No one who has attacked this city with insane war has returned having rejoiced to have violated it.

AND ALL THE KINGDOMS OF THE EARTH SHALL BE GATHERED AGAINST IT] Although all the kingdoms of the earth are gathered against it.

Jerome reports this opinion of the Jews concerning Judah in the siege of Jerusalem, that Judah, having been besieged in Jerusalem, was captured by the Gentiles, and passing into their society, was compelled to besiege his own metropolis. And to v. 3. The sense is this: I will make Jerusalem for all nations as a most heavy stone to be lifted: They will indeed lift it, and according to the variety of their strength they will devastate it: but it is necessary that, while it is being lifted, in the very exertion and elevation of the weight, the most heavy stone should leave some cut or abrasion on the bodies of those who lift it. But having left that, he proposes the sense of the Christian Doctors concerning the Church thus: that all persecutors, who fight against the house of the Lord, shall be made drunk with that cup which Jeremiah offers to all nations in chapter 25. That in the time of persecution even many of our own are compelled to fight against the Church: But whoever shall wish to lift this weight, he will indeed lift it, and according to the wrath of the Lord, with which He chastises sinners, he will sustain it with his own hands. But he himself shall not be unpunished, with the sword of God fighting against him. That which is held in the Vulgate:

BEHOLD I will make Jerusalem a threshold of drunkenness; others render it more correctly a cup of drunkenness, or of trembling. Osiander interprets it as a cup of poison. By this is understood the spiritual Jerusalem, which is above, the mother of us all, Gal. 4:26. The Christian Church, which the nations that surround it on all sides indeed attempt to swallow up, as if in a single draught, but they themselves will tremble like drunkards, will fall, will be confounded, or will drink the most present poison. The Vulgate poorly renders it threshold of drunkenness. It is true that סף denotes a threshold and a doorpost in many places, and the LXX everywhere attended only to that meaning; yet there is another use of the word, in which it is taken for a cup, and other wine vessels and household items, as David Kimchi notes, and as is manifest from the passages Exod. 12:22, 2 Sam. 17:18, Jerem. 52:19, 2 Kings 12:9. Since, however, the discussion here is about an instrument from which one drinks, it is best translated by 'cup,' with the Roman word and the Greek word not obscurely corresponding to the Hebrew. רעל properly signifies horror and trembling, and is the same as תרעלה. Without a doubt, however, such horror and trembling is noted as is accustomed to accompany drunkenness, as is evident from the fact that it is joined either with כוס or יין, Ps. 60:5, Isa. 51:17, 22. It will therefore be translated as horror or trembling, and סף־רעל will be a cup of horror, a drink of such a kind that it induces trembling in the limbs and disturbs and strikes those who drink it, so that they cannot rightly use their own strength: such as we see happen to drunkards, who usually report a trembling of the hands and body as the fruit of their gorging, as Willius rightly [notes] p. 436. This formula is frequent in Scripture, by which the evils of punishment and the judgments of God upon sinners are compared to a cup, as can be seen in Isa. 21, Ps. 75, Ezech. 23, and elsewhere. The reason is that God, through His providence, determines the punishment for the sins of enemies, and measures out and offers the same to them as if by a certain measure and cup, and that often with such severity that He forces the dregs into their mouths, even against their will, and compels them to drain them. Furthermore, because men very often involve themselves in divine judgments through the greed of sinning, and as it were gorge themselves with the very evils, just as drunkards rush into intoxication through a Cyclopean ingestion of wine. But when it is added: BUT ALSO JUDA WILL BE IN THE SIEGE; most understand that the Jews will persecute the spiritual Jerusalem; others wish to designate by Juda those who are in the Church, even if they are not of the Church, and who likewise cause trouble for the Church when it is attacked by enemies. But because the Lord promises that He will open His eyes over Juda, the interpretation of Osiander is more suitable, with which the blessed Balduinus agrees, but also 'there will be great tribulation over Juda,' or a cup of error in the siege against Jerusalem, so that a universal persecution is designated. Therefore, the gloss of Willius p. 438 is not suitable. The sum of the whole sentence is: the Church of the new covenant will strike and disturb the nations and the hostile Jews through the preaching of the Gospel. There is held here, as I said, the character of the Ephesian Church. For by the promulgation of the Gospel, such a commotion of the nations and Jews occurred in all places, which was for the salvation of many, but also for the confusion and destruction of many, as is clear from the Acts, concerning which Haggai ch. II, 6, 7, 21, 22. Nor [is the interpretation] of Grotius [correct]: For the earthly Jerusalem was not set as a stone of stumbling for all peoples in the time of Antiochus: nor were ALL the kingdoms of the earth gathered against it, and therefore this must be understood of the Church. Thus among the Latins Jerome, among the Greeks Cyril: In the preceding predictions, the war to be brought upon Judea by the Roman army is clearly mentioned. But in the words just introduced, he clearly prophesies the persecutions instituted against the Church. Willius is right here: He affirms in general concerning the Church of the new covenant these three things: First, that it would be immovable by any human strength due to its own weight: second, that the nations and kingdoms would nevertheless attempt its overthrow: third, that those most vehement attempts would lack success. But he wrongly restricts these to the Smyrnean Church.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET ERIT IN DIE ILLA, PONAM JERUSALEM LAPIDEM ONERIS CUNCTIS POPULIS, OMNES QUI LEVABUNT EAM CONCISIONE LACERABUNTUR] Sauciando sauciabuntur. Experientur quidem in ea vires suas, at non impune. Optime hanc locutionem explicat Hieronymus: Mos est in urbibus Palæstinæ, & usque hodie per omnem Iudæam vetus consuetudo servatur, ut in viculis, oppidis & castellis rotundi ponantur lapides gravissimi ponderis, ad quos juvenes exercere se solent: & eos pro varietate virium sublevare, alii ad genua, alii ad umbilicum, alii ad humeros & caput, nonnulli super verticem, rectis junctisque manibus, magnitudinem virium demonstrantes, pondus attollunt. In tali nisu evenit, ut aliis lædatur pars aliqua corporis, aliis rumpantur venæ. De Roma Claudianus: Hanc urbem insano nullus qui Marte petivit Lætatus violæsse redit.

ET COLLIGENTUR ADVERSUS EAM OMNIA REGNA TERRÆ] Quamvis colligantur adversus eam omnia regna terræ.

Judæorum sententiam de Juda in obsidione Hierosolymæ Hieronymus hanc tradit, quod Judas obsessa Hierusalem captus à gentibus, & in illarum transiens societatem coactus fuerit obsidere metropolin suam. Et ad v. 3. Sensus iste est: Ponam Hierusalem cunctis gentibus quasi gravissimum lapidem sublevandum: Levabunt quidem eam, & pro virium varietate vastabunt: sed necesse est, ut dum levatur, in ipso nixu & elevatione ponderis gravissimus lapis scissuram aliquam vel rasuram in levantium corporibus derelinquat. Sed relicto illo sensum Christianorum Doctorum de Ecclesia ita proponit: quod cuncti persecutores, qui contra domum Domini dimicant, inebrientur eo calice, quo universis gentibus propinat Jeremias c. 25. quodœ persequutionis tempore etiam è nostris multi contra Ecclesiam pugnare compellantur: Sed quicunq́ hoc pondus voluerit sublevare, levabit quidem, & pro ira Domini, qua corripit peccatores, suis manibus sustentabit. Verum ipse non erit impunitus, Dei contra se gladio dimicante. Quod in Vulgata habetur:

ECCE EGO ponam Jerusalem superliminare crapu- le, rectius reddunt alii calicem ebrietatis, vel tre- moris. Osiander interpretatur calicem veneni. Spiritualis intelligitur Hierosolyma, quæ sursum est, mater omnium nostrum Gal. 4,26. Ecclesia Chri- stiana, quam gentes, quæ eandem undique cingunt, absorbere quidem conantur, unico quasi haustu, sed ipsæ instar ebriosorum trement, corruent, con- fundentur, vel præsentissimum haurient venenum. Vulgata male reddit superliminare crapulæ. Notat quidem סף limen & postem pluribus in locis, & LXX. eam solam significationem ubique attende- runt, alius tamen etiam vocis usus est, in quo pro Scypho, aliisque vasis vinariis, & domesticis sumitur, ut David Kimchi annotat, & ex locis Exod. 12, 22. 2. Sam. 17, 18. Jerem. 52, 19. 2. Reg. 12, 9. manife- stum est. Cum autem hic de instrumento, ex quo bibi- tur, sermo sit, per scyphum optime transfertur, vo- cabulo Romano, & Græco non obscure Ebræo re- spondente. רעל proprie horrorem ac tremorem si- gnificat, ac idem est cum תרעלה. Dubio procul autem ejusmodi horror notatur ac tremor, qui e- brietatem solet comitari, uti ex eo elucet, quod vel cum כוס, vel יין, conjungitur Ps. 60, 5. Esa. 51, 17. 22. Vertetur igitur per horrorem vel tremorem, & e- rit סף־רעל scyphus horroris, ejusmodi potus, qui membris tremorem inducit, bibentesque pertur- bat, ac percellit, ut viribus suis recte uti non pos- sint: qualia videmus ebriosis usu venire, qui manus & corpus tremulum plerumque, ut fructum ingur- gitationis reportant, ut recte Willius p. 436. Fre- quens in Scriptura formula hæc est, qua mala pœ- næ & judicia Dei in peccatores calici comparantur, ut Esa. 21. Ps. 75. Ezech. 23. & alibi videre est. Ra- tio est, quia Deus per providentiam suam hostium delictis pœnam determinat, eandemque ceu cer- ta quadam mensura & poculo iis admetitur ac pro- pinat, idque sæpe tanta cum severitate, ut vel invi- tis fæces in os ingerat, easque exhaurire cogat. Deinde, quia homines sæpissime aviditate pec- candi se judiciis divinis involvunt, atque ipsis ma- lis se quasi ingurgitant, quemadmodum ebriosi per cyclopicam vini ingestionem in temulentiam ruunt. Cum vero additur; SED ET JUDA ERIT IN OBSIDIONE; plerique intelligunt Judæos spiritualem Hierosolymam persequuturos, alii per Judam designari volunt, qui in Ecclesia sunt, etsi nec de Ecclesia sint, & Ecclesiæ ab hostibus impu- gnatæ itidem quoque negotium facessant. Sed quia Dominus promittit, se oculos aperturum super Juda, convenientior est interpretatio Osiandri, cui consonat B. Balduinus, sed & supra Juda erit tribu- latio magna, vel scyphus erroris in obsidione contra Je- rusalem, ut designetur universalis persecutio. Non ergo convenit Willii glossa p. 438. Summa totius sententiæ est: Ecclesiam novi fœderis concione Evan- gelii gentes & Judæos inimicos perculsuram ac turba- turam. Habetur autem hic, ut dixi, character Ephe- sinæ Ecclesiæ. Promulgatione enim Evangelii ejus- modi commotio gentium & Judæorum ubiq; locorum facta est, quæ multis saluti, multis etiam confusioni & exitio fuit, ut ex Actis claret, de qua Haggæus cap. II, 6. 7. 21. 22. Nec Grotii: Non enim Hierosolyma terrena omnibus populis in lapidem oneris posita, Antiochi tempore: nec adversus eam collectæ fuere OMNIA regna terræ, ideoque de Ecclesia hæc in- telligenda. Ita inter Latinos Hieronymus, inter Græcos Cyrillus: In prædictionibus antegressis bellum Judææ à Romano exercitu inferendum dilucide memo- ratur. In verbis autem modo illatis institutas con- tra Ecclesiam persecutiones liquido vaticinatur. Re- st cte hic Willius: Affirmat in universum de Ecclesia novi fœderis tria hæc: Primum eam suo pondere fore omnibus humanis viribus immobilem: alte- rum gentes nihilo minus & regna ejus eversionem molitura: tertium conatus illos vehementissimos successu carituros. Sed male hæc restringit ad Smyrnensem Ecclesiam.

## 12:4
Verse 4. IN THAT DAY] That is, afterwards, as often, I WILL STRIKE EVERY HORSE WITH STUPOR] This is because Antiochus was very strong in cavalry. See above IX. 10. AND OVER THE HOUSE OF JUDA I WILL OPEN MY EYES] I will have mercy on the pious, who will remain unpolluted. AND EVERY HORSE OF THE PEOPLES I WILL STRIKE WITH BLINDNESS] With fear, which may be the cause that they do nothing rightly. Examples 1 Macc. III. 27, IV. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 4. IN DIE ILLA] Id est, postea, ut sæpe, PERCUTIAM OMNEM EQUUM IN STUPO- RE] Hoc ideo, quia Antiochus equitatu maxime valebat. Vide supra IX. 10. ET SUPER DOMUM JUDÆ APERIAM O- CULOS MEOS] Miserebor piorum, qui restabunt impolluti. ET OMNEM EQUUM POPULORUM PER- CUTIAM CÆCITATE] Metu, qui causa sit, ne quid re- cte faciant. Exempla 1. Macc. III. 27. IV. 20.

## 12:5
Verse 5. AND THE LEADERS OF JUDA WILL SAY IN THEIR HEART] Namely the Maccabees. LET THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM BE STRENGTHENED FOR ME IN THE LORD OF HOSTS THEIR GOD] They will be strengthened through me.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET DICENT DUCES JUDA IN CORDE SUO] Nempe Maccabæi. CONFORTENTUR MIHI HABITATORES JERUSALEM IN DOMINO EXERCITUUM DEO EORUM] Confortabuntur per me.

## 12:6
Verse 6. LIKE A FIREPAN] A censer, which although small, is nevertheless sufficient to set entire cities on fire. Thus a beginning was made from very small undertakings.

AND THEY WILL DEVOUR TO THE RIGHT AND LEFT ALL THE PEOPLES IN THE CIRCUIT] The Ammonites, Idumeans, Tyrians, Ptolemaidenses.

These words: IN THAT DAY: refer to that time; of which the Prophet had been treating: For 'day' is used by the Hebrews for 'time'. Therefore, they are not correctly rendered by Grotius as 'AFTERWARDS': nor are his examples of that signification proven, or adduced. From where is it evident that by horses all the cavalry of Antiochus is meant? From a comparison of the passage Zech. 9:10, it will rather be gathered that ALL hostile power is to be destroyed, just as it is also added here: I will strike EVERY horse OF THE PEOPLES (not of Antiochus alone). The gloss of Grotius is too arbitrary. The exposition of the Jews in Jerome is as follows: When the Lord shall have opened His eyes upon Judah, and shall have struck all the horses of the nations with blindness: The leaders of Judah, of whom it was spoken above: But also Judah shall be in the siege against Jerusalem: they shall make vows in their hearts, because they will not dare to speak freely, that Jerusalem may win, and Judah, having been conquered with the enemies, may win with its own citizens. When the leaders of Judah shall have said in their hearts: Strengthen for me, O Lord, those besieged in Jerusalem: that they, who are conquered by their own weakness, may overcome by Thy help: Then I, the Lord Almighty, their God, will make the princes of Judah like a furnace of fire among wood and like a torch in stubble: that they may devour the adversaries to whom they were joined by feigned friendship. Let them devour on the right and on the left, and let them kill all the peoples in the circuit, so that Jerusalem may again be inhabited in its place, and may in no way fear hostile attacks. They shall also restore the cities and towns and villages and hamlets of the tribe of Judah, which had been plundered and laid waste, just as they had been before they were laid waste: and the Royal House and the renowned and magnificent ones of the tribe of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall by no means glory against the tribe of Judah, that it is ruled by their command, and governed by their counsel. But they shall know that the victory in both belongs to the Lord. But those carnal victories have nothing to do with the scope of the Prophet. Nor does he treat of Judah and its leaders according to the flesh. For He had already taken away His staff from Israel, and had already broken the covenant with the Jews in chapter XI.

This, therefore, is what the Lord promises, that He will strike the enemies of the Church with stupor and madness, so that they cannot harm His people, but that He will look upon the house of Judah, or the Church, with eyes of grace, so that it may not be utterly oppressed, but may be preserved against the force of any enemies whatsoever. It is also hinted by that reasoning as the manner of averting enemies, as if to say: I will not use horses or arms to subvert the enemies, but I will blind them, I will render them stupid and mad, so that even they themselves may at last be compelled to desist, not without ignominy: but I will enlighten my own, and to them I will give the Spirit of wisdom and counsel, that they may easily be able to avoid snares and deceitful traps. Cyril in this place observes that to open the eyes is to note, because he wishes to look upon them most amply, and as it were with a full gaze, and he calls that a certain sign of indulgence and charity. Willius's paraphrase is not bad: As my grace overflows upon my people, all grace will be withdrawn from the nations, as my light shines in the Church, the nations will be struck with blindness: But the restriction of these to the Pergamene Church (or period) is bad. Now by the leaders of Judah are understood the Apostles and other faithful ministers of the Church, who both stir up themselves with confidence in the divine presence and power, and promise spiritual strength to their hearers, all the faithful inhabitants of the heavenly Jerusalem, and obtain it by their prayers, and furthermore are like a furnace of fire among wood, and like a fiery torch in smoke, they burn with the ardor of the Holy Spirit, and like a conflagration they consume all the rocks of heresies and all the power of the enemies.

Thus Jerome explains the mind of the Christian interpreters. The leaders and tribunes are the Apostles, apostolic men, and Doctors, who have been in charge of Christ's army. And afterwards: Let us say that in the time of the persecution of the Church, the leaders and tribunes of the Christian name, of whom we spoke above, when the Lord has restored peace to Jerusalem and has slain the adversary with the spirit of his mouth, shall be as a furnace of fire among wood, to devour the unfruitful trees, and as torches in stubble: so that whatever has no foundation, and is carried about by every wind of doctrine, may be delivered to the fire. And they shall devour (he says) the leaders of Judah and the tribunes on the right and on the left those who did not wish to burn in the middle of the journey, they did not know ὥς ἐκβολὰς εἶναι κακίας: whence the people of God promise; we shall turn aside neither to the right nor to the left: we shall walk the royal road. Similarly Cyril of Alexandria. He names the tribunes of Judah the Holy Apostles or even simply all the leaders of the Holy Churches. And he affirms that their speech, or sacred doctrine, will so command their minds that it seems to have fallen like a firebrand into wood, or a torch into stubble, which catches fire most easily. For they will devour, he says, all the peoples on the right and on the left in the circuit, that is, wherever they wish to go, there they will be able in every way, calling to acknowledgment, and as if with divine and intellectual fire warming the cold. Wherefore the divine disciples were as firebrands in stubble, and they indeed devoured the nations in the circuit, yet they did not utterly destroy them: but rather they burned the detestable and impure dogmas of false knowledge in them, and consumed the filth of the old fallacy, and did not allow the minds of those who had once believed to be chilled any further into folly and rashness, so that exulting in themselves, they might say to Christ the Savior of all: Thy word is very fiery, and thy servant hath loved it Ps. 119. Willius acknowledges here that these things can be referred in general to the Doctors, or the chief of the believers, we do not place our strength in the multitude of the people and the magnitude of carnal power, but we glory in the members of the Church gathered by the grace of God, this is our glory, this is our strength, to see a people living in the fear of God by the grace of God. But what he places here as the character of the Thyatiran Church is merely arbitrary: Those things which he adds on p. 445 to v. 6 are also correct. The confidence and confession of the Church having been set forth, it proceeds to the preservation of the same by the procuring of the consumption of obstacles. But God says that he will procure this preservation through the leaders of Judah, that is, the Doctors and Pastors. He attributes to these very ones the power of consuming obstacles, and a most efficacious one, while he compares them to a furnace of fire and a firebrand, and a most easy one, while he likens the adversaries to stubble and wood. For fire subjected to wood and flame added to stubble easily consume both. You have a similar phrase in Obadiah v. 18. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall be kindled against these and consume them, and there shall be no survivor of the house of Esau, because the Lord speaks; which words furthermore testify that such consumption will be total, which is also expressly added here. And they shall consume on the right and left all the peoples round about. Finally, the effect of this consumption is added: And Jerusalem shall remain still in its place in Jerusalem. These things are said according to the nature of a type, as are the preceding and following. But the preservation and safety of the Church is thus hinted at, in this sense, that with the nations and idolatry subverted, the Church shall remain safe and immovable in its place, and as once Jerusalem in the Old Testament held up the torch of the divine word to the nations, so in the New Covenant the spiritual Jerusalem is to kindle the light of the Gospel for all. These are Willius's: which we do not disapprove. But he rashly seeks here the character of the Sardian Church, rejecting things said generally to a certain time and state of the Church under the New Testament from a mere private interpretation, and tearing apart those things which cohere in the text, and distributing them into certain periods of time, against the mind of the Holy Spirit and against the evident continuity of the text, in which there is no trace of different periods.

Verse of the same. AND JERUSALEM SHALL BE INHABITED AGAIN IN ITS PLACE IN JERUSALEM] In the place retaining the old name, not in a new colony. 1 Maccab. 4. It was said before that the earthly Jerusalem is not looked to, which had not been destroyed then, nor was it to be destroyed, and therefore there was no need for such a promise, that it would be inhabited in the place retaining the old name, not in a new colony. Others more correctly observe in that repetition, that Jerusalem may be inhabited in its place, in Jerusalem, a singular emphasis, as if to say, however much Jerusalem or the Church may be attacked from all sides, it shall nevertheless be Jerusalem or the Church in its place, where the Lord also willed their being to be. Cocceius in this and the preceding verses posits three signs of the time of redemption or signs of the coming of Christ. And first in v. 2. Behold I make Jerusalem a cup of trembling &c. he wishes to include the restoration of the walls and of the habitation of Jerusalem, which was procured through Ezra and Nehemiah, and the peace under the Persian Empire up to Darius the Last, the struggles of the Seleucids and Lagids over Jerusalem, and even the persecution of Antiochus himself, who also drank from this basin, as well as the aid of the Priests and Princes of Judah in attacking Jerusalem, whom he wishes to be pointed out in v. 2, rendered thus: and also he who is over Judah shall be in the siege against Jerusalem. Thus he agrees in part with Grotius, when he thinks that Antiochus is included at the same time. But who besides Cocceius would have either sought or been able to find all those things in these words? There is nothing here about the building of Jerusalem, nothing about its peace up to Darius the Last, nothing about the contention of the Seleucids and Lagids over Jerusalem, or about the varied fortune of this city; nor can these things be dragged back to those times. He seeks another thing in v. 3, 4, 5, in the efforts of the Kings against Jerusalem, and the state of the city and the people unmoved, protected by the power of God, in the time of the Maccabees, noting the stupor and blindness in the expeditions of Antiochus, Epiphanes, Eupator, Demetrius, Alexander, Demetrius II, Antiochus Sidetes. But how was this prediction fulfilled in all the Kings who opposed themselves to Jerusalem, all who burden themselves with it shall be torn by tearing it? Indeed, Ptolemy son of Lagus had subjected Jerusalem to himself, Philopator had subjected myriads, and subsequently Judah was under various vexation, and furthermore came into the power of Antiochus in the year 113 from the death of Alexander. Joseph. Antiq. XII. 3. and when Antiochus Epiphanes had been moved to the scepter, it had been exposed to most grievous persecutions. Nor is it to be believed that verse 2 is to be torn away from the following ones. For the designation of the same time in verse 3, AND IT SHALL BE IN THAT DAY, opposes it. For those for whom Jerusalem is set as a basin of dizziness, or a cup of drunkenness and stupor, they are said here to be struck with stupor and madness, verse 4; nor can there be any doubt that what is handed down more concisely in verse 2 is explained by the subsequent ones. Cocceius seeks a third sign in verse 6, the expansion of the empire and peace, understanding by the Leaders of Judah the Priests and Senators constituting the Sanhedrin, and he wishes the history, as it appears, to be looked at under Alexander Jannaeus according to Josephus XIII. Antiq. c. 23. concerning the expansion of the Jews through Syria, Idumea, and Phoenicia. But here again the circumstance of the times stands in the way. For the Prophet refers these to the same time, and does not admit such distinct periods of time: furthermore, he deals with the Church in the time of the New Testament, after the covenant with the Jews has already been abolished. Therefore these are not to be drawn back to ancient times. Nor is it the devouring of wars, but what is done by the power of the Word and the Spirit that is indicated. These things concerning the Cocceian interpretation. Which, however, we do not doubt is much more suitable here than either the Grotian or the Willian, if it were permitted to draw these back to the times preceding the advent of Christ, and to distribute them into different periods of time.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SICUT FACEM IGNIS] Batillum, qui exi- guus licet, sufficit tamen ad totas urbes incendendas. Sic a cœptis perexiguis initium factum.

ET DEVORABUNT AD DEXTRAM ET SI- NISTRAM OMNES POPULOS IN CIRCUITU] Am- monitas, Idumæos, Tyrios, Ptolemaidenses.

Verba ista: IN DIE ILLA: respiciunt tem- pus istud; de quo egerat Propheta: Nam dies E- bræis dicitur pro tempore. Non ergo recte reddun- tur à Grotio, POSTEA: nec exempla ejus signi- ficationis probata, adducla sunt. Per equos omnem Antiochi equitatum respici, unde constet? E colla- tione loci Zach. 9, 10. potius colligetur, OMNEM hostilem potentiam destructum iri, quemadmodum etiam hic additur: OMNEM equum POPULO- RUM (non Antiochi solum) percutiam. Nimis arbitraria est glossa Grotii. Expositio Iudæorum a- pud Hieronym. ita habet: Quum aperuerit Domi- nus oculos suos super Iudam, & percusserit omnes e- quos gentium cæcitate: Duces Iuda, de quo supra di- ctum est: Sed & Judas erit in obsidione contra Hie- rusalem: vota facient in cordibus suis, quia loqui libe- re non audebunt, ut vincat Hierusalem, & victus Iu- das cum hostibus vincat cum civibus suis. Quando Duces Iudæ dixerint in cordibus suis: Conforta mihi Domine obsessos Hierusalem: ut, qui sua imbecil- litate victi sunt, tuo superent auxilio: Tunc ego Do- minus omnipotens Deus eorum ponam Principes Ju- da, sicut fornacem ignis in lignis & sicut facem in stipula: ut devorent adversarios, quibus simulata amicitia jungebantur. Devorent autem à dextris & sinistris, & omnes populos occidant in circuitu, ut rursum Hierusalem habitetur in loco suo, & ne- quaquam hostiles impetus timeat. Urbes quoq; & oppida ac villas ac viculos tribus Iudæ, qui direpti fue- rant, atque vastati, instaurent, sicut fuerant, an- tequam vastarentur: & nequaquam Domus Regia & inclyti ac magnifici tribus Iude & habitatores Hierusalem glorientur adversum tribum Iuda, quod suo regatur imperio, suo consilio gubernetur. Sed scient, quod Domini sit in utrisq; victoria. Sed illæ carnales victoriæ nihil ad scopum Prophetæ faciunt. Neque is de Juda ejusque Ducibus secundum car- nem agit. Nam virgam suam ab Israele jam abstule- rat, & fœdus cum Judæis jam confregerat cap. XI.

Hoc ergo est, quod pollicetur Dominus, se percus- surum hostes Ecclesiæ stupore & amentia, ut populo suo nocere non possint, gratiæ autem oculis respecturum domum Iuda, vel Ecclesiam, ne penitus opprimatur, sed adversus vim hostium quorumvis conservetur. Innuitur etiam ea ratione modus avertendi hostes, q. d. non utar equis aut armis ad subvertendos ho- stes, sed excæcabo eos, stupidos & amentes reddam, ut vel ipsi tandem non sine ignominia desistere co- gantur: meos autem illuminabo, iisque Spiritum sapientiæ & consilii dabo, ut decipulas, laqueosque dolosos facile evitare possint. Cyrillus in h. l. a- perire oculos observat notare, quod amplissime, & toto velut aspectu respicere eos velit, idque dicit indulgen- tiæ & charitatis certum indicium. Non mala est Willii paraphrasis: Gratia mea in populum meum redundante gentibus omnis gratia subtrahetur, luce mea in Ecclesia fulgente gentes cæcitate perstringentur: Sed mala est horum ad Ecclesiam (vel periodum) Pergamensem restrictio. Duces autem Judæ in- telliguntur Apostoli, aliique fideles Ecclesiæ ministri, qui & seipsos excitant fiducia præsentiæ & virtu- tis divinæ, & auditoribus suis, omnibus fidelibus habitatoribus Hierusalem cœlestis, robur spiritua- le promittunt, precibusque suis impetrant, ac præ- terea sunt instar camini ignis in lignis, & instar facis igneæ in fumo, ardore Sp. S. flagrant, & instar incen- dii omnes hæresium scopulos, omnemque hostium potentiam consumunt.

Ita Hieronymus exponit mentem Christiano- rum interpp. Duces ac tribuni Apostoli sunt, Aposto- lici viri atque Doctores, qui Christi exercitui præfue- runt. Et postea: Nos dicamus, quod in tempore perse- cutionis Ecclesiæ, Duces & tribuni nominis Christia- ni, de quibus supra diximus, cum Dominus pacem red- diderit Hierusalem, & interfecerit adversarium spiri- tu oris sui, futuri sint quasi caminus ignis in lignis, ut devorent infructuosas arbores, & sicut faces in sti- pula: ut, quodcunque fundamentum non habet, & cir- cumfertur omni vento doctrinæ, tradatur incendio. Et devorabunt (inquit) Duces Juda & tribuni ad dex- tram & ad sinistram eos, qui in medio itinere incen- dere noluerunt, nesciverunt ὥς ἐκβολὰς εἶναι κα- κίας: unde Dei populus pollicetur; nec ad dextram nec ad sinistram declinabimus: via regia gradiemur. Similiter Cyrillus Alex. Tribunos Juda S. Apostolos aut etiam omnes simpliciter Sanctarum Eccle- siarum præpositos nominat. Adeo autem sermonem, si- ve sacram doctrinam ipsorum mentibus imperaturam affirmat, ut torris in ligna, aut fax in stipulam, quæ facillime ignem concepit, incidisse videatur. Devo- rabunt enim, inquit, omnes populos à dextris & à sini- stris in circuitu, hoc est, quocunque ire voluerint, il- lic omnimodo valebunt, vocantes ad agnitionem, & tanquam igni divino & intellectuali frigidos ca- lefacientes. Quamobrem divini discipuli, ut torres i- gnis in stipula fuerunt, & gentes quidem in circuitu devorarunt, veruntamen non penitus perdiderunt: sed potius falsa in ipsis scientiæ detestanda & impura dogmata incenderunt, veterisque fallaciæ sordes absum- pserunt, & animos eorum, qui semel crediderant, ad insipientiam & temeritatem frigefieri amplius passi non sunt, ut in seipsis exultantes, universorum Salvato- ri Christo dicerent: ignitum eloquium tuum vehe- menter, & servus tuus dilexit illud Ps. 119. Agno- scit hic Willius hæc in genere ad Doctores, aut cre- dentium præcipuos referri posse, nos robur nostrum non ponimus in multitudine populi & magnitudine po- tentiæ carnalis, sed gloriamur de membris Ecclesiæ ex Dei gratia collectis, hæc nostra gloria, hoc nostrum ro- bur est, cernere populum in Dei timore per Dei gratiam versantem. Sed quod hic ponit characterem Eccle- siæ Thyatyrensis, mere arbitrarium est: Recte etiam habent, quæ addit p. 445. ad v. 6. Exposita fiducia & confessione Ecclesiæ ad conservationem ejusdem ac- cedit per consumptionem obstaculorum procurandam. Conservationem autem hanc Deus dicit se procuratu- ram per Duces Judæ, id est, Doctores & Pastores. Tri- buit his ipsis vim consumendi obstacula & effica- cissimam, dum eos camino ignis ac tadæ ignis com- parat, & facillimam, dum adversarios stipulis & lignis assimulat. Ignis enim lignis subjectus & flamma stipu- la addita facile utrumq; consumunt. Similem phrasin habes Abdiæ v. 18. Erit domus Jacobi ignis, & do- mus Joseph flamma, domus autem Esavi in stipu- lam, & accensi in hos consument ipsos, neque erit superstes domus Esavi, quia Dominus loquitur; quæ insuper verba testantur consumtionem ejus- modi totalem fore, id quod etiam diserte hic ad- jicitur. Et consument ad dextram & sinistram o- mnes populos circumquaque. Effectus deniq; addi- tur hujus consumtionis: Et permanebunt Hieroso- lyma adhuc loco suo Hierosolymis. Sunt hæc pro ratione typi dicta, ut & præcedentia ac sequentia. In- nuitur autem ita Ecclesiæ conservatio & incolumitas, hoc sensu, quod gentibus & idololatria subversis Ec- clesia suo loco salva sit mansura ac immobilis, & ut olim Hierosolyma in V. Test. facem verbi divini gentibus præferebat, ita in Novo fœdere spiritua- lis Hierosolyma omnibus Evangelii lucem sit ac- censura. Hæc Willius: quæ non improbamus. Sed temere hic quærit characterem Ecclesiæ Sardensis, generaliter dicta rejiciens ad certum tempus, sta- tumque Ecclesiæ sub N. T. ex mera privata ἐπιλύ- σει, & discerpens ea, quæ in textu cohærent, ac di- stribuens in certas temporum periodos, præter mentem Spir. S. & contra evidentem συνέχιεαν textus, in quo nullum vestigium diversarum pe- riodorum.

Vers. eod. ET HABITABITUR JERUSALEM RUR- SUS IN LOCO SUO IN JERUSALEM] In loco ve- tus nomen retinente, non in nova colonia. 1. Mac- cab. 4. Dictum antea non respici Hierosolymam terre- nam, quæ tum destructa non fuerat, nec destruen- da, ideoque opus non erat tali promissione, habita- tum iri eam in loco vetus nomen retinente, non in nova colonia. Rectius alii observant in repetitione illa, ut habitetur Jerusalem in loco suo, in Jerusalem sin- gularem emphasin, q.d. utut Jerusalem seu Ecclesia oppugnetur undiquaque, erit tamen nihilominus Jerusalem seu Ecclesia in loco suo, ubi etiam Do- minus eorum esse voluerit. Coccejus in hoc & præ- cedentibus versibus tria ponit σημεῖα καιρõ ἀπολυ- τρώσεως vel signa adventus Christi. Et primo in v. 2. Ecce ego pono Hierosolymam pelvim vertiginis &c. comprehendi vult restitutionem murorum, & habi- tationis Hierosolymæ, quæ per Esdram & Nehemiam procurata, & pacem sub Imperio Persarum usque ad Darium Ultimum, certamina Seleucidarum & Lagidarum de Hierosolyma, ipsamque etiam An- tiochi persecutionem, qui etiam ex hac pelvi bibe- rit, nec non Sacerdotum & Principum Judæ in op- pugnanda Hierosolyma auxilia, quos indigitari vult v. 2. ita reddito: atque etiam qui est super Iehudam, erit in obsidione contra Hierusalem. Sic accedit ex parte Grotio, cum Antiochum simul comprehendi putat. Sed quis illa omnia in his verbis vel quære- ret, vel invenire potuisset præter Coccejum? Nihil hic de exstructione Hierosolymæ, nihil de pace ejus- dem usq; ad Darium Ultimum, nihil de contentione Seleucidarum & Lagidarum super Hierosolymam, aut de varia urbis hujus fortuna; nec retro ad ista tempora hæc trahi possunt. Alterum quærit in v. 3. 4. 5. in studiis Regum contra Hierosolymam, & statu civitatis & populi immoti ob potentiam Dei protecto- ris, tempore Maccabæorum, notans stuporem & cæ- citatem in expeditionibus Antiochi, Epiphanis, Eu- patoris, Demetrii, Alexandri, Demetrii II. Antiochi Sedetis. Sed quomodo in Regibus omnibus, qui se opposuere Hierosolymæ, impleta hæc prædictio omnes onerantes se ea lacerando lacerabuntur. Si- quidem Ptolemæus Lagi Hierosolymam sibi subje- cerat, Philopator myriades subjecerit, & sub vexa- tione varia deinde Juda fuerit, ac porro in potesta- tem Antiochi venerit Anno à morte Alexandri CXIII. Joseph. Antiq. XII. 3. & cum Antiochus Epi- phanes sceptris admotus esset, gravissimis perse- quutionibus exposita fuerit. Neque concreden- dum, ut discerpatur vers. 2. à sequentibus. Repu- gnat enim designatio ejusdem temporis v. 3. ET ERIT IN DIE ILLO. Nam quibus est posita Hierosolyma pelvis vertiginis, vel calix ebrietatis ac stuporis, illi hic stupore & furore percutiendi di- cuntur v. 4. neque dubium esse potest, quæ v. 2. concisius tradita sunt, subsequentibus exposita esse. Tertium signum quærit Coccejus in v. 6. dilatatio- nem imperii & pacem, per Duces Judæ intelligens Sacerdotes & Senatores constituentes Synedrium, at- que historiam, ut apparet, respici vult sub Alex- andro Jannæo penes Josephum XIII. Antiq. c. 23. de dilatatione Judæorum per Syriam, Idumæam & Phœniciam. Sed obstat hic iterum temporum πε- ρίστασις. Nam ad idem tempus refert hæc Pro- pheta, neque admittit tales temporum distinctas periodos: adhæc de Ecclesia tempore N. T. agit, postquam jam fœdus cum Judæis abolitum est. Non ergo hæc retrahenda sunt ad vetera tempora. Nec devoratio bellorum, sed quæ sit virtute verbi & Spiritus indigitatur. Hæc de Coccejana inter- pretatione. Quam vero hic multo convenientio- rem esse, quàm vel Grotianam vel VVillianam non dubitamus, si liceret hæc retrahere ad tem- pora adventum Christi antegressa, atque in diver- sas temporum periodos ea distribuere.

## 12:7
Verse 7. AND THE LORD SHALL SAVE THE TENTS OF JUDAH, AS IN THE BEGINNING.) He will restore the city and the towns; not through the Jerusalemites, but through the Maccabees from Modin.

THAT THE HOUSE OF DAVID MAY NOT GLORY MAGNIFICENTLY.) Whose descendants had no part in this glory; see below 12.

AND THE GLORY OF THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM AGAINST JUDAH.) Formerly the inhabitants of the city despised the other Jews in all the towns and villages in comparison with themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET SALVABIT DOMINUS TABERNA- CULA JUDA, SICUT IN PRINCIPIO.) Restituet urbem & oppida; non per Hierosolymitas, sed per Mac- cabæos ex Modin.

UT NON MAGNIFICE GLORIETUR DOMUS DAVID.) Cujus posteri nullam in hac gloria partem ha- buere; vide infra 12.

ET GLORIA HABITANTIUM JERUSALEM CONTRA JUDAM.) Olim urbis habitatores cæteros in omnibus oppidis & vicis Judæos præ se spernebant.

## 12:8
Verse 8. IN THAT DAY THE LORD SHALL PROTECT THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM.) After the return to the city.

AND HE WHO SHALL HAVE STUMBLED AMONG THEM SHALL BE.) He who shall have fallen against the law by the imitation of others.

AS DAVID.) He shall be touched by as grievous repentance as David was on account of his sins against Uriah.

AND THE HOUSE OF DAVID AS GOD.) The house of the descendants of David shall be so full of piety, as if it were a Temple.

AS THE ANGEL OF THE LORD IN THEIR SIGHT.) As if they always had some Angel of God visible among them.

That these deal with the restoration of the city and towns made by the Maccabees, whence shall it be taught? And how did the Jews then aspire to it or to the tents of Judah with the happiness which they had formerly in the beginning? What? Since Grotius has already explained the preceding things concerning the victories of the Maccabees and the preservation of Jerusalem against Antiochus and the neighboring peoples in verse 2 and 3, and wishes the subsequent times to be designated in verse 4. Who therefore now returns to the earlier times? Whence Cocceius not undeservedly noted Grotius here (who indeed was seduced here by Lamb. Danaeus, explaining these in the same way): Grotius here again follows his anomalies: who in chapter 9, 9, had understood the King of Zion in the first and obvious sense as Zerubbabel, as if Zechariah, with Zerubbabel now old, and indeed after the victories of the Jews had been prophesied, could prophesy next about the coming of Zerubbabel as King: he, in this place, where there is again an oracle about Christ the Savior, when he himself in verse 5 & 6. let him note that the act concerns the victories of the Jews, yet he returns to the liberation of the people by the Maccabees from the hand of Antiochus. It appears that this man expressly concealed most of the prophecies concerning Christ and true salvation.

Some take that IN THE BEGINNING in a comparative sense, others in an absolute one. The former explanation is more common. And the Lord will save the tabernacles of Judah, AS IN THE BEGINNING, that is, He will preserve the Churches scattered throughout the world, just as God, being faithful, never abandoned the care of His Church, as Osiander says, or just as He once preserved the tabernacles of the Israelites in the desert, as the Vinarians hold. Calvin acknowledges that a particle of similitude is to be understood, and he refers it to the dwelling of the Jews in tabernacles when, having been redeemed from Egypt, they had entered the land and for the most part lived in villages.
