The impious also lament the crucifixion of Christ when they feel the wounds of conscience, because by their sins they caused such great pains to Christ, and because they drove him to the cross with hands and feet, nay, with all the members of the body and all the affections of the mind, and yet they do not dare to believe in this crucified Christ: which lamentation the Holy Spirit effects in them no less than that former one, but by the voice of the law, by which, terrified, they daily feel the unspeakable torments of conscience, until at length, rejected from the face of the Lord and ordered to depart on the day of horrible judgment, they will lament a lamentation tolerable by no human strength and to be finished by no ages. The blessed Winckelmann has succinctly encompassed everything: The disciples and friends of Christ certainly fulfilled this lamentation when they saw him hanging on the cross and dead. But it is still fulfilled by believers in serious contrition and penitence over the sins in which they made the Son of God serve, and by their iniquities provided him labor, Is. 43. It is fulfilled when the faithful, as members, are conformed to the head in the cross, filling up those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ, Col. 1. It will be fulfilled on the last day, when the Jews and all the enemies of Christ, who pierced him either in his person or in his members, will look upon him as a terrible Judge, whom they did not want to receive here as Savior, just as it is said in Apoc. 1.

But all will lament separately, because that lamentation will be neither particular, or of some, nor feigned or of hypocrites, but all will lament from the sentiment of their mind, as if they were mourning alone; for each one has need of true contrition and penitence, because the just shall live by his faith, Habac. 2, 4. Women also will lament separately, because there is an allusion to the sacred rites of the Jews, in which women were accustomed to gather separately, and in public mourning, spouses were otherwise accustomed to sleep apart, so that they might be more fit for prayers and fasts. Villius here seeks the character of the Ephesian Church in the conversion of Jews and Gentiles in the primitive Church. But that lamentation does not pertain only to the primitive Church, but to all times, just as we have already warned. Nay, even as regards the impenitent, it extends to all eternity, because they will lament when they see Christ the judge, whom they pierced, with a lamentation that will never cease. From this passage some Fathers and other Theologians gather that Christ will appear at the judgment with wounds, and will eternally retain the scars of the wounds. The blessed Gerhard notes in Harm. Resurrect. c. 9. p. 315, that the blessed Luther did not disapprove of these meditations of the ancients concerning the traces of the wounds in the hands and feet and in the side of the pierced Christ, nor did Chemnitius. For thus he says in John 20: Whether Christ retained the traces of the wound in his side and of the nails even after the resurrection, I will not dispute, but yet in such a way that there is no deformity in the appearance, as otherwise, but beautiful to behold and full of consolation. Here, however, he expressly determines that Christ, even after his entry into heavenly glory, retained the traces of the wounds in memory of the price exhibited for us, so that we may daily remember at what a great price we were bought, where the blessed Gerhard adds that it is probably at least determined that the wounds do not adhere to the body by some necessity, but are retained by a free economy and dispensation, the various causes of which he elegantly adduces there. Corn. à Lapide on Zach. 12, 6. p. 287, brings forward twenty causes for that thing, so that, namely, those wounds may be 1. the most certain indicators of the true flesh assumed, not fantastic, as the Manichaeans wanted. 2. witnesses of the most atrocious passion. 3. the stings of conquered death and undoubted arguments of the resurrection, namely, that the same body of Christ in number that was crucified rose again, not another. 4. characters of most ardent love, by which, as Isaiah says, he described us on his hands, not with a reed, but with nails. 5. most illustrious trophies of victory over sin, the demon, death, and hell. 6. shining ornaments and triumphs of the glorious body. 7. the token of our redemption. 8. stigmata of obedience even unto death. 9. sacred relics of the labors and pains of Christ. 10. the ransom of all sins, which Christ represents by continually supplicating the Father for them. 11. the consolation of the troubled. 12. the example of the suffering. 13. the refuge of the afflicted. 14. the incitement of the penitent. 15. the asylum of the tempted, according to that of Cant. 2, 13. Arise my beloved, and come: my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the cavern of the wall. 16. the stimulus of the laboring. 17. the model of martyrs. 18. joy to the elect. 19. disgrace to the reprobate on the day of judgment. 20. admiration and stupor to the Angels.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

FAMILIÆ DOMUS NATHAN SEORSUM, ET MULIERES SEORSUM] Nimirum etiam Zorobabelis, viri tam pii, posteritas peccavit, & sic indignam se fecit re- gno, quod non recepit, nisi in Domino Jesu modo subli- miore.

FAMILIÆ DOMUS LEVI SEORSUM, ET MU- LIERES EORUM SEORSUM] Etiam Sacerdotes multi peccaverant. Docet id oppositio 1.Macc. 4, 42. vide & 2. Macc. 4, 13. & nota, cum Mathathias causam sacrorum armis (ut illa tempora tum ferebant) tuendam suscepit, ne- minem ex collegis ei adfuisse.

FAMILIÆ SEMEI SEORSUM, ET MULIERES EORUM SEORSUM] Ex hac familia plurimos fuisse do- ctores testatur hoc loco Hieronymus: & forte ex illis fuit Sameas posterioribus temporibus memoratus Josepho, & Hieronymo ad 8. Esaiæ, sed & Thalmudicis & Rabbinis sæpe.

FAMILIÆ ET FAMILIÆ SEORSUM ET MU- LIERES EORUM SEORSUM] Postquam illustriores familias nominavit, designat cætera κατ’ ὁμάδα: ut intel- ligatur ingens fuisse illorum, qui peccaverant, numerus. Alii sacrificaverant Diis Græcis: alii ἐπεσπάσθησαν, alii suillas in Templo obtulerant; alii libros legis tradiderant iis, qui eos incensuri erant.

Videndum hic partim de lectione v. 10. genui- na, partim de interpretatione ejusdem & sequentium vera & germana. Primum nonnullos aliter legisse putat, quam nunc habet codex authenticus. At si per- inde est, quod ad sensum, sive legatur pronomen primæ personæ אלי, seu tertiæ אליו, siquidem pri- ma persona sequente maxime relativo sæpissime tertia exprimatur, observante Grotio, causam non habemus lectionem codicum nostrorum in du- bium vocandi, quamvis nondum productus sit co- dex, qui posteriorem lectionem habeat, sed exem- plaria constanter priorem retineant, quibus frustra omnino hic se opponit, corruptionem textus Ebræi in hac voce fingens contra consensum non solum codicum omnium, sed & contra Græcam, Vulgatam, aliasque interpretationes. Porro quod ad vocem דקרו, aliter eam legisse LXX. Interpp. in suo codice minus firmum documentum est, quod aliter reddi- derint. Obstat enim iterum consensus Codicum Ebræ- orum summus, codicum item Græcorum Interpp. quo- rundam, quos laudat Grotius, & imprimis autoritas S. Johannis, de quo Hieronymus in h. l. Johannes Evangelista, qui de pectore Domini hausit sapientiam, Hebræus ex Hebræis, quem salvator amabat plurimum, non magnopere curavit, quid Græcæ literæ continerent, sed verbum interpretatus è verbo est, ut in Hebræo le- gerat: & tempore Dominicæ passionis dixit esse com- pletum. Quod si quis non recipit, det testimonium, è quo Sanctarum Scripturarum loco Joannes ista pro- tulerit, & cum non repererit, cogetur ingratis susci- pere veritatem. De Interpp. autem LXX. ita Cocce- jus p. 556. Hallucinatio ea videtur interpretum esse, qui, quum nescirent, quid ibi faceret confossio, putare po- tuerunt, in scriptione sphalma esse, & ex conjectura substituerunt רקדו. Hoc multo probabilius est, quam in quoquam codice reperisse has literas רקדו. Quæ hic de lectione adversus Grotium suffi- ciant.

De interpretatione magis laborandum. Secun- dum literam hæc de Deo probris confixo explicat Grotius, sequutus forte Calvinum, qui inquit, meta- phorice hic accipitur confixio pro continua irrisione, ac si diceret, Judæos sua pervicacia fuisse quasi accin- ctos ad bellum, ut Deum pungerent, ac configerent sua malitia, vel telis rebellionis suæ, cui Lamb. Da- næus hic consonat. Sed de Filio Dei hæc acci- pienda esse, non metaphorice confixo calumniarum, vel rebellionis telo, sed proprie in assumta humana natura in passione magna confixo primum litera ipsa confirmat. Non enim est à proprio sensu ad metaphoricum descendendum, nisi ipsa necessitas cogat. Quum ergo hæc verba proprie accepta confixionem inferant, & transfossionem, cur relicta il- la significatione metaphoricam sectemur? Recte hic Willius p. 456. דקר cor transfigere, transfodere, confodere gladio, lancea, vel alio instrumento mor- tifero. Usurpatur de Pineha virum Israeliticum cum scorto Midianitico transfodiente Num. 25, 8. & de armigero Abimelechum confodiente Jud. 9, 54. Aliis itidem in locis proprie de confossione violenta accipitur. Rectissime igitur etiam heic loci de trans- fossione proprie sic dicta explicatur, & primario ad eam referendum est. Quod dicit PRIMARIO, videtur alium adhuc sensum admittere, licet secun- darium, quod probari nequit, siquidem ejusdem dicti non potest geminus sensus constitui, alius pri- marius, alius secundarius.

Deinde, verba hæc non sunt Dei Patris, sed Filii Dei, qui cap. præcedenti æstimatur venditurq́; pretio XXX. Siclorum v. 12. 15. & c. 9, 11. sanguine suo emit- tere dicitur vinctos è lacu, in quo non est aqua. Coccejus arbitratur quidem hic loqui Deum Patrem, non negat tamen crucifixionem Christi designari, sed verba ita interpretatur, & intuebuntur me cum (eo) quem transfoderunt, ut Deo ita conjungatur Chri- stus, ut Psal. 2, 2. Joh. 17, 3. Verum sic receditur à communi significatione particulæ את, quæ nota est Accusativi casus, & ingeritur textui pronomen tertiæ personæ, quod in eo non habetur, & ex una per- sona duæ fiunt. Tertio Filium Dei esse eum, quem confixuri sint, & ob quem plangent, innuitur mentio- ne unigeniti & primogeniti. Nam is unigenitus est ratione divinæ naturæ, & primogenitus ratione hu- manæ. Atque ita particula כ accipi potest, ceu כ veritatis, ut vocant, quemadmodum ὡς Joh. 1, 14. accipitur. Vidimus gloriam ejus ut unigeniti à Patre, h. e. quæ vere est unigeniti gloria. Unde Coccejus : exaggeratur planctus ab æstimatione perso- næ. Qui unigenitus Dei Filius Joh. 1, 14. (Nam ra- tione humanitatis non esset unigenitus) & primoge- nitus multorum fratrum Rom. 8, 29. h. e. qui est ante omnes filios Dei, & sine quo nemo fit filius Dei (qui in ipsius oppositione, qui est μονογενὴς & πρωτότο- κος, sunt κτίσις & θετοὶ) ac proinde in quo san- ctificantur omnes filii Dei. Si retineatur sensus similitudinis, convenit tamen comparatio luctus super morte unigeniti & primogeniti magis luctui super morte Filii Dei, quam super probris & con- tumeliis Deo Patri illatis.

Quarto de aspectu hic agitur ejus, qui configen- dus erat. Videbunt eum, in quem pupugerunt. Is ergo, qui configendus, oculis etiam corporalibus aspiciendus erat. At hoc non convenit Deo Pa- tri, sed Filio Dei in carne manifestato, quem vide- runt oculis corporis in diebus carnis discipuli Luc. 10. 1. Joh. 1. viderunt etiam pii complures, ac visuri olim sunt in reditu visibili omnes cum fideles, tum infideles. Si verbum ADSPICIENT ita hic ac- cipiendum, sensu abstracto, ut de quovis aspectu, si- ve oculis fiat animi sive corporis, intelligi queat, ex- cludendus certe non est aspectus & intuitus, qui fit oculis corporis. Quia peculiare quid hic indigita- tur de hoc Domino & transfodiendo vel configen- do, & in transfixione sua conspiciendo.

Quinto aspectus hic tribuitur illis, qui Dominum confixerunt, indefinite omnibus, adeoque cum fide- libus, tum infidelibus, qui non eadem ratione futu- rus. Alii eum adspiciunt cum vera pœnitentia ac fiducia in eum, qui confixus est, alii sine fide, sine vera pœnitentia; de pœnitentiali intuitu accipit Grotius. Esto de eodem hic agatur. At quodnam est objectum, quod intueri pœnitentes & fideles de- bent, ut remissionem peccatorum consequantur, nisi Messias, suspensus in ligno crucis & confixus pro nobis, quem adspicientes per fidem salvamur, perinde uti serpentem æneum in ligno suspensum aspicientes salvabantur Joh. 3, 15. Neque tamen pœnitentes solum adspiciunt confixum. Aspi- ciunt etiam, qui non pœnitentiam veram agunt, imo aspiciunt omnes, qui confixerunt. Unde sexto ita colligimus: De eo hic conspiciendo agitur, qui ab omnibus, à quibus confixus est, conspicietur. At hic non est Deus Pater, sed Messias, qui ab omnibus hominibus conspicietur in die novissima, confixus ab omnibus, quia peccatis nostris ipsum vulnera- vimus,& confiximus omnes Esa. 53, 6. Rom. 4, 24. & ab omnibus respici debet per fidem,utpote pro omnibus confixus. Septimo ideo donatur Spiri- tus gratiæ & precum, ut aspicere possimus eum, quem confiximus, salutariter; & passione ac cru- cifixione sua meritus erat nobis Messias hoc do- num Spiritus, ut ab eo gratiose illuminati fidei o- culis hunc Salvatorem nostrum pro nobis confi- xum & crucifixum intueremur.

Octavo planctus causa designatur non solum crucifixio Domini,sed etiam ipsa mors, & quidem mors unigeniti & primogeniti. Nam, etiamsi ad- mitteretur proverbialis locutio, uti Jerem. 6, 26. Amos 8, 10. comparationes tamen & locutiones proverbiales tales adhiberi solent, quæ materiæ aptissime conveniant, & in istis locis non excludi- tur, sed vel imprimis etiam comprehenditur inter luctus causas occisio primogenitorum, & unigeni- torum, quæ in ejusmodi publicis calamitatibus plurimis ad gravissimam luctus causam sufficit. Ideoque cum confossio Domini hic causa luctus sit, atque luctus ille dicatur, velut luctus super morte unigeniti & primogeniti, non obscure hac phrasi in- dicat Sp. S. luctus causam fore mortem unigeniti & primogeniti filii, & confessionem illam cum mor- te confossi & transfixi conjunctam fore, quemadmo- dum transfixio Josiæ cum morte ejus conjuncta fuit 2. Par. 35, 24. cujus deploratio ideo aptissime con- venit huic planctui super confixione & morte Do- mini, cujus typum insignem in plusculis etiam Josiam fuisse, historiæ collatio docet.

Nono planctus hic vel de planctu conversionis & pœnitentiæ, vel de planctu confusionis & ignominiæ accipi potest. Ille est vere pœnitentium, & fide- lium, quem intelligit Grotius hic & ad Matth. 26, 30. Qui vero hic proponitur, ut universalis luctus o- mnium tribuum, qualis planctus universalis causam etiam oportet universalem assignare,fidelibus omni- bus convenientem; hæc vero non est illa injuria in Deum. Non enim certe omnes Deum lacessive- rant probris,non omnes ipsum irritaverant,& telis rebellionis confixerant. At omnes, cujuscunque fortis,conditionis,tribus,vere fideles causam plan- gendi habent,ob confixionem & mortem Christi, siquidem peccatis nostris ipse confixus sit, & ob peccata nostra in mortem traditus. Quis ergo fi- deliũ non lugeret,non plangeret vera cordis con- tritione, quod peccatis suis ipsummet Filium Dei confixerit, eundemque in crucem & mortem ege- rit? Sed non tantum planctus conversorum indica- tur:in genere planctus eorum,qui confixerunt, nota- tur,etsi non diffiteamur,conversos vere fideles im- primis respici. Nam explicatur ille planctus etiam de illis,qui pœnitentiam non egerunt, qui non sa- lutari contritione dolent ob peccata, sed tristi de- speratione strident ob supplicia peccatorum.Lam- bertus Danæus causam planctus hujus constituit mortem tum Matathiæ, tum Judæ Maccabæorum, 1. Macc. 2,70. c. 9,23. Joseph. l.XII. Ant.c.ult.& vo- cem relativam EUM in hac sententia, & lugebunt super eum,neque ad Deum,neque ad Christum re- fert,sed ἀντονομασικῶς ad eum eosḡ, per quos Deus illo tempore miraculosam populi liberationem opera- tus est,nempe ad primos Maccabæos. Sed, quomodo pronomen relativum ad EOS referri potest, quo- rum nulla in textu facta est mentio? Quomodo lu- ctus hic de morte referri potest adluctum de diver- sis tum de Matathiæ,tum de Judæ, qui tam diverfo tempore occubuere, quum de unico subjecto hic sermo sit,&causa planctˣ assignetur confossio,quam μεταφορικῶς intelligit Danæus de irritatione Dei.

Quod cum viderit Grotius, non sequutus est in eo Danæum, sed verba Ebræa: plangent de EO, retulit ad factum illud, confixionem nempe, plangent ob con- tumelias Deo illatas. Nimirum affixum illud prono- men tertiæ personæ, vel referri potest ad personam, ad EUM, quem confixerant, vel ad ipsum confixio- nis actum: Uterque sensus commodus est, atque eo- dem recidit. Nec priori obstat, quod adhibitum fu- erit pronomen primæ personæ: ADSPICIENT AD ME; Nam additum est: QUEM confixerunt, q. d. adspicient me tanquam ad EUM, quem confixerunt, & super hunc, quem confixerunt, plangent. Quo facit observatio ipsius Grotii, quod prima persona sequen- te maxime relativo sæpissime per tertiam in his libris exprimatur. Coccejus planctum in textu propheti- co distinguit, & aliam atque aliam ejus causam assi- gnat. Primum plangentes facit, qui respiciunt De- um & Christum, fideles, quod respicere fidei sit se convertentis à vana spe ad veram salutis arcem Zach. 9, 12. & in ea acquiescentis. Conf. Psal. 34, 6. Joh. 6, 11. Esa. 45, 22. siquidem hic Christi passio ex- hibeatur in transfixione. Conf. cap. 9, 11. cap. 11, 12. 13. Implementum hujus planctus constituit Actor. 2, 36. 37. id tamen non esse unius articuli recte agno- scit, ut nec donum Spiritus. Externus effectus, in- quit, est plangere super confosso ab ipsis. Qui planctus exaggeratur ab æstimatione Personæ. Planctus no- tat desperationem peccati confodientis Christum; o- mnes rei sumus confossi Christi, quia propter pec- cata nostra confossus est Esa. 53. Porro in sequenti- bus vers. 11. 12. 13. alium planctum, aliasque planctus causas introduci putat, nimirum ob vastationem Hie- rosolymæ. Judicium est, inquit, in non plangentes su- per confosso, ut plangant super alia causa; vide plan- ctus locum in Hierosolyma, magnitudinem & æstima- tionem per comparationem planctus, qui fuit occisio Josiæ in bello circa Hadadrimmon. Singuli privatam plangendi causam habebunt, ut privatam cupiditatem habuerant. Domus David planget erepta sibi spe regni: quum videbunt interire Rempublicam. Do- mus Nathan Prophetæ illiusq; successores degeneres plorabunt interitum suæ magnitudinis, & irascentur Scripturis, quod veritas non respondeat ipsorum præsa- giis. Ita Sacerdotes ob interitum Sacerdotii, Simei- tæ, Levitarum familia, referentes illum Simein Ben- jamitam, qui Davidi maledicebat, plangent ob sui mi- nisterii abolitionem. Sic cæteræ familiæ, quæ super- erunt. (Nam consumentur multæ, multæ eripien- tur ex illa necessitate per fidem.) Quævis ob suum commodum per destructionem Reipublicæ lamentabi- tur. Fœminæ vero deplorabunt filios suos & fructum ventris sui. Confer Hos. 8, 11. 12. 13. 14. Hæc Coc cejus. Verum hic unica solum causa planctus al- legatur: culpa scilicet illa gravissima, qua confixus Messias ipse fuit: non vero ulla mentio habetur de planctu ob pœnam, & judicium Dei in πανωλεθρίᾳ, & cohærent illa, nec discerpi possunt, qua v. 10. & 11. habentur ac sequentibus, imo ad eundem planctum illustrandum faciunt, cujus gratia non solum plan- ctus in morte unigeniti & primogeniti mentio fit, sed confertur etiam planctus Adadrimmon in morte Io- siæ. Interim non diffitemur applicationem fieri posse ad infideles illos, qui judicium Dei experti luxere in excidio Hierosolymitano, ac convicti in conscientia de culpa transfixi, & occisi justi illius, eo majorem lugendi causam habuere, quod pro- pria culpa, & vindictæ divinæ provocatione tantum sibi accersiverint malum Matth. 27, 25. quem plan- ctum gravissimum ipsis prænunciavit Christus Luc. 23, 28. sed si de proprio objecto planctus, de pro- pria causa, ob quam planctus ille futurus sit, quæra- tur, qui à Propheta hoc loco innuitur, plangent de se

EO, non apparet, excidium Hierosolymitanum hic indigitari, de quo cap. 14. demum agitur, sed potius confixionem Messiæ, quam fideles omnes lugent, ut- ut Hierosolymam ac familias, quæ hic recensentur, non intelligamus præcise urbem terrenam, aut tri- bus Israeliticas, sed Hierosolymam cœlestem, & cre- dentes omnium ordinum, qui verbis Veteris Testa- menti receptis describuntur, more Scripturæ con- sueto: nam alias nulla distinctio tribuum locum ha- bet inter Israelitas in extrema confusione, qua op- pressi ipsi fuere novissimo tempore. Et, de ea agi- tur Hierosolyma, ac Davidica Domo, cui promitti- tur effusio Spiritus gratiæ & precum, nec non fons a- pertus adversus peccata & impuritatem. Quæ non solum Hierosolymitanis & familiæ Davidicæ, sed omnibus in Ecclesia promissa sunt tempore Nov. Test. Hæc enim apud nos (Christianos) post adven- tum Christi quotidie impleri intelligimus & proba- mus, ait Hieronymus. Ordines autem, qui hic si- gnificantur, ita explicat idem Hieronymus: In plangen- David, regia tribus accipitur, hoc est, Juda: In Na- than,prophetalis ordo describitur: Levi refertur ad Sacerdotes, ex quo ortum est sacerdotium: In Simei doctores accipiuntur: ex hac enim tribu magistrorum agmina pullularunt. Reliquas tribus tacuit, quæ non habent aliquod privilegium dignitatis. In eo autem quod ait, Omnes tribus reliquæ, tribus & tri- bus seorsum, & uxores eorum seorsum,universas absq; nomine comprehendit. Similitudo luctus ob Josiam etiam favet nostræ sententiæ: Non enim lu- ctus ibi ob cladem publicam, sed ob Regem interfe- ctum, cum quo componitur luctus ob Messiam Re- gem crucifixum & occisum, cujus ille typus ex- titit. Ideoque non ob excidium Hierosolymita- num planctus indicitur,etsi in eo excidio conscien- tia ipsis causam suggerere potuit, confixionem nempe Regis sui Messiæ. Quod etiam continget in πανωλεθρίᾳ universi, ubi lugebunt in fideles, quod Messiam confixerint peccatis, & imprimis impœnitentia & incredulitate finali, quia hæc cau- sa erit æterni ipsorum exitii.

De comparatione illa Grotius dubius alios du- bios redderet,nisi præferendum scirent expressum locum authentici textus 2. Reg. 23, 30. 2. Paral. 35, 24. dubiæ Chaldæi de nomine Regis Syri Hadarrum- mon,quod nihil ad rem præsentem facit,conjecturæ. De planctu vero ex præcepto Synedrii indictis pœnis huic familiæ gravioribus, illi levioribus san- cito, ob graviora & leviora peccata, Antiochi, & Maccabæorum tempore, mera somnia proferri Gro- tius, nullamque fidem meretur. Indulget præ- conceptæ opinioni. Quod etiam in Lamb. Da- næo hoc loco animadvertimus.

Accedit Decimo συνέχεια cum sequenti capite, quo non solum de fonte aperto adversus impurita- tem in S. Baptismate, destructione idololatriæ, & falsorum Prophetarum, sed etiam de unici veri Pa- storis θεανθρώπꙋ percussione, ac discipulorum ejus fuga, & conversione agitur. Quæ omnia ad tem- pora N. T. pertinent. Quomodo ergo hæc tra- henda ad tempora Maccabaica?

Undecimo habemus hic consentientes ipsosmet Rabbinos,qui de Messia explicant vaticinium, non sensu mystico,sed literali,ut è R. Hadarsan in Gen. 28. aperte liquet: Ipse(Messias) erit donans gratiam & devotionem Israeli, sicut dictum est Zachar. 12, 10. Et effundam super domum David,& super habita- tores Jerusalem Spiritum gratiæ, &c. Et in Mas- sechec Succa distinctione Hachalil Camischa:Et plan- get terra, & familia familiæ seorsim (Zach. 12, 12.)

Iste planctus cur fiet? Dixit Rabbi, discordes sunt cir- ca hoc R. Rosa & Rabbanim, sive Magistri, unus di- xit propter Messiam, vel super Messiam filium Joseph, qui occisus erit, & unus dixit super fomite malo, vel sensualitate, vel concupiscentia, quæ occisa erit; pax illi sit, qui dixit super Messia Filio Joseph, qui occisus erit; hoc est enim, quod jam scriptum est (Zach. 12, 10.) Et respicient ad me, quem transfixerunt. Quem locum è libro Succa laudat R. Salomo Iarchi ad h. l.

Duodecimo interpretatur ipse Sp. S. hunc locum de Messia, non sensu mystico, sed literali, idque in duobus locis, primo circa transfixionem Christi in cruce factam. Ea enim impletum esse testatur, quod prædixit hoc loco Propheta, Joh. 19, 34. seqq. Non fregerunt ejus crura, sed unus militum lancea latus e- jus aperuit, & continuo exivit sanguis, & aqua. Et, qui vidit, testimonium perhibuit, & verum est testi- monium ejus. Et ille scit, quia vera dicit, ut & vos cre- datis: facta autem sunt hæc, ut Scriptura impleretur, os non comminuetis ex eo. Et iterum alia Scriptura dicit, videbunt, in quem transfixerunt. Grotius an- notat. ad N. T. ad h. l. verba ὄψονται εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέν- τησαν ex aliqua Græcarum versionum adducta putat, quia in multis libris ea lectio reperitur, à Symmacho, Aquila aut Theodotione: sed Hieronymus observavit supra, non curasse Johannem, quod Græcæ literæ conti- nerent, sed verbum è verbo esse interpretatum, ut in He- bræo legunt, docet tamen, quomodo etiam verbum Græcum LXX. Interpp. conveniat. Verbum κατωρ- χήσαντο apud Græcos non ab illusione, sed à saltatu compositum est: quod scilicet contra Dominum quasi ludendo saltaverint, quando dicebant illudentes atque ridentes: Vah, qui destruis templum, & in tribus diebus ædificas illud, salvum fac temetipsum de- scendens de cruce. Hæc & alia illudentes, & quodam amentiæ tripudio saltantes loquebantur. Nullatenus consistit illa glossa, quam à Calvino habet Grotius: quod à Deo de se comtemto tralatitie dictum, in Jesu κατὰ πόδας evenisse. Nam si de Deo extra œcono- miam τῆς ἐν σαρκώσεως tempore V. T. hæc dicta atque olim impleta jam sunt, quomodo vaticinium continere possunt de Deo manifestato in carne, tem- pore passionis ejus demum implendo? Si verba tra- latitie dicta, & metaphorice intelligenda sunt, qui ea- dem verba sensu proprio & nativo accipienda? Num ejusdem dicti simul in eodem loco & proprius & figuratus est sensus? Si nihil aliud volunt, quam quod Israëlitæ sacrificaverint Diis Græcis, aut suillas in templo obtulerint, aut libros legis incendendos tra- diderint, & ob alias contumelias Deo tum illatas, quo pacto S. Johannes dicere potuit, Scripturam illam impletam, cum Messias in cruce transfixus fuit? Un- de à Calvino suo hic non discessit tantum Franc. Ju- nius cum Tremellio in annotat. ad h. l. & in parallel. LXXXV. l. 1. ut & Joh. Coccejus in h. l. sed refutavit etiam eundem Balth. Willius: Minus recte vir do- ctissimus censet, non citari Prophetæ verba ab Evan- gelista pœnitentiæ respectu, sed consilium ejus esse bre- viter ostendere, Christum esse Deum illum, qui ab ini- tio locutus fuerat per Prophetas. Licet enim Evan- geliographus non de pœnitentia Judæorum tractet, monstrat tamen veræ resipiscentiæ objectum. Argu- mentum autem divinitatis Christi hinc peti potest, quod illa transfixio, quam hic verus Deus sibi tribuit, de Christo dicitur, ac Deus & Christus unius ejusdem- que transfixionis subjectum statuuntur. Cæterum tribuitur merito hæc transfixio Judæis, licet lancea Ro- mani militis facta, quia eam jusserunt & approbarunt. Habes autem hoc pacto descriptum, ut dixi, resipiscen- tiæ objectum ac fidei scopum, simulq; causam conver- sionis, quæ erit conscientia peccati in Christi crucifi- xione admissi, & dolor super malo eodem. Hæc Willius.

Planctus autem ille complementum suum ha-""" buit passionis Christi tempore in discipulis ejus, &""" piis mulierculis, aliisque fidelibus, tum maxime """ post effusionem Spiritus S. quemadmodum Act. """ 2. & seqq. aliquot millia Judæorum conversi, sine """ dubio vera pœnitudine peccatum confixi Messiæ""" deplorarunt: atque omnibus temporibus vere fi-""" deles id maximè dolent, quod peccatis suis causa """ extiterint confossi & in mortem traditi Filii Dei """ unigeniti. Qui vero id non agnoscunt, nec do- """ lent vera mentis pœnitentia, æternum perituri """ sunt, exemplo Judæorum, qui etsi manibus suis """ Christum cruci affixerant, & autorem vitæ inter- """ fecerant, atque à discipulis ejus ad pœnitentiam """ jugiter invitati erant, in incredulitate & impœni-""" tentia persistere, quam peccatum gravissimum a-""" gnoscere, Messiamque confixum & crucifixum """ respicere volebant, ob id totaliter excisi & repro- """ bati. Unde ad illos etiam hoc vaticinium applicat S. Cyrillus: Ubi animam suam pro nobis posuit, """ & spiritibus apud inferos prædicavit & revixit, """ terræ motu concusso monumento, qui assidebant """ mirabundi dixerunt, (Vere filius Dei erat iste) nec """ mediocri pœnitudine multi capiebantur. Post- """ quam autem & Romani eos bello presserunt, re- """ gione devastata, & urbibus incensis, & domibus """ vacuefactis, jamque ipsa Hierosolyma obsessa, & """ fame oppidanos conficiente, vix quidam suos in """ Christum ausus nefarios agnoverunt, tandemque """ animadverterunt, quamobrem dira paterentur, """ & propter impie in eum commissa sese illa perpe- """ ti. Profusissimis namque lacrymis parentes pri- """ mogeniti & dilecti mortem semper prosequun- """ tur, nec plangendi, & lamentandi invenire mo- """ dum sustinent, estque dolor loginquus plane, & """ quasi perennis acriter, & intolerabiliter velli- """ cando animos macerans. Judæis autem calami- """ tates istiusmodi experturis Christus prædixit, """ mulieres super ipso flentes ita castigans (Filiæ """ Hierusalem, nolite flere super me, sed vos ipsas, & fi- """ lios vestros flete.)

De visione ergo corporali Christi judicis in ad- ventu novissimo & planctu infidelium cum æterna desperatione conjunctio idem S. Johannes oraculũ allegavit Apoc. I. 7. Ecce venit cum nubibus, & vi- debunt eum, qui pupugerunt, & plangent super eum o- mnes tribus terræ: uti iterum manifestum est, non μυσικῶς tantum id adduci, sed doceri Christum il- lum esse, quem quoad literam designavit Zacha- rias, eundemque conspectum iri ipsis etiam oculis corporis ab omnib9, cum nempe adveniet in nubi- bus, atque ab illis quoque, qui eum pupugerunt. Quapropter visionem istam non solum restringi posse in nostro oraculo ad intuitum fidei: sed, uti di- ximus, complecti etiam visionem corporalem. Deni- que planctum tribui infidelibus, omnibus tribubus terræ, quæ peccatis ipsũ pupugerunt suis, & in cru- cem egerunt, fideq; eum non aspexerunt, sed in in- credulitate perseverarunt: ac proinde non posse solum de pœnitentiali planctu Zachariam intelligi, sed generatim planctum comprehendere cum fi- delium, qui est veræ pœnitentiæ & tristitiæ secundum Deum, tum infidelium, qui æternum horrorem, con- scientiæ morsum, & vermem non pereuntem infert. Plangunt ergo utriq;, illi, cum ob peccatum dolent, & convertuntur, hi cum peccati pœnam luunt, & æternum pereunt. Quem sensum recte expressit O- siander: Et adspicient ad me, quem confixerunt: intue- buntur (inquit Christus) olim me impii in novissi- mo die, maximo cum horrore, & videbunt, in quan- ta sum majestate, quem illi crucifixerunt; & cuj9 la- tus lancea transfixerunt, ut sanguis & aqua efflueret.

Sed & resipiscentes Judæi intelligent, se Dominum gloriæ crucifixisse. Discipuli Christi propter mor- tem ipsius vehementissime fuere perturbati. Sed & Judæi conversi procul dubio multis lacrymis de- plorarunt, quod Ducem salutis suæ crucifixe- rint. (Mortuus est autem in cruce unigenitus Dei Filius, & primogenitus omnis creaturæ, sed id fa- ctum est in humanitate assumta.) Cætera de tribu- bus diversis explicat de cruce fidelium omnium or- dinum, quod omnes vere Christianos Christo com- pati oporteat: Verum, quia luctus causa redditur à Propheta non nostra crux, sed Christi confixio nostræ culpæ causa facta, in eadem acquiescere præstat, ad quam tamen hactenus luctus in cruce nostra reduci potest, quod eadem ejusdem, quæ crucifixionis Christi causa, nostra sc. peccata. Quo pacto B. Balduinus de hoc planctu, Pii, inquit, plan- gunt mortem Christi, partim, quia innocentiam ejus agnoscentes, deplorant hominum cæcitatem, qui cruen- tas manus in Sanctum illum Sanctorum conjicere non fuerunt veriti: partim quia considerant atrocitatem lapsus, qui tantos corporis animiq́; cruciatus Agno Dei peccata mundi portanti promeruit, partim etiam, quia sciunt se στίγματα Christi in suo portare corpo- re, adeoque si non pari, simili tamen persecutioni ho- stium, cruci & adflictionibus obnoxios esse: quæ me- ditationes omnes à Spiritu Sancto proficiscuntur, qui hoc pacto passionem dominicam considerare jubet. Impii etiam plangunt Christi crucifixionem, quando conscientiæ vulnera sentiunt, quod suis peccatis tantos Christo pepererunt dolores, quod- que ipsum manibus pedibusque, imo omnibus corporis membris, omnibusque animi adfectibus, in crucem adegerunt, neque tamen audent in hunc crucifixum Christum credere: quem planctum non minus quam priorem illum etiam Spiritus Sanctus efficit in ipsis, sed voce legis, qua territi ineffabiles conscientiæ cruciatus quotidie persen- tiscunt, donec tandem rejecti à facie Domini, & in die horribilis judicii discedere jussi, planctum plangent nullis hominum viribus tolerabilem, & nullis seculis finiendum. B. Winckelmannus omnia succincte complexus est: Hunc planctum sane im- pleverunt discipuli & amici Christi, cum viderunt i- psum pendentem in cruce & mortuum. Sed adimple- tur adhuc à credentibus in seria contritione & pæni- tentia super peccatis, in quibus servire fecerunt filium Dei, & suis iniquitatibus ei laborem præbuerunt Es. 43. Impletur, cum fideles ut membra capiti confor- mantur in cruce adimplentes, quæ desunt passionum Christi Col. 1. Implebitur in novissimo die, cum Judæi & omnes hostes Christi, qui ipsum vel in persona sua, vel in membris suis compunxerunt, aspicient ut ter- ribilem Judicem, quem ut Salvatorem hic recipere no- luerunt, quemadmodum Apoc. 1. dicitur.

Plangent autem omnes seorsim, quia planctus ille neque particularis, aut aliquorum, neque simulatus aut hypocritarum erit, sed plangent omnes ex animi sententia, ac si soli lugeant; nam cuique seorsim o- pus est vera contritione ac pœnitentia, quia justus fide sua vivet, Habac. 2, 4. Mulieres etiam seorsim lugebunt, quia ad sacra Judæorum alluditur, in qui- bus seorsim mulieres convenire, inque luctu publi- co conjuges alioquin secubare consueverant, ut ad preces & jejunia magis essent idonei. VVillius hic quærit Ecclesiæ Ephesinæ characterem, in Judæo- rum & gentium in primæva Ecclesia conversione. At planctus ille non pertinet tantum ad primævam Ecclesiam, sed ad omnia tempora, quemadmodum jam monuimus. Imo etiam, quod ad impœniten- tes, ad omnem æternitatem sese porrigit, quia plan- gunt gent, cum videbunt Christum judicem, quem con- fixerunt, planctu nunquam defituro. Ex hoc loco colligunt Patres nonnulli aliique Theologi, Christum cum vulneribus compariturum ad judicium, ac cicatrices vulnerum æternum reten- turum. Quas veterum meditationes de vestigiis vulnerum in manibus ac pedibus, & in latere Chri- sti transfossi, nec B. Lutherum improbare, nec Che- mnitium, notat B. Gerhardus Harm. Resurrect. c. 9. p. 315. Sic enim ille in Joh. 20. Num Christus etiam post resurrectionem vulneris in latere & clavorum vestigia retinuerit, ego non impugnabo, sed ita tamen, ne quid deformitatis sit in aspectu, sicut alias, sed for- mosum ad videndum, & consolationis plenum. Hic vero diserte statuit, Christum etiam post suum in glo- riam cœlestem ingressum vestigia vulnerum retinuisse in memoriam pretii pro nobis exhibiti, ut quotidie re- cordetur quam caro pretio emti simus, ubi addit B. Gerhardus, probabiliter saltem statui, non hærere ne- cessitate quadam vulnera in corpore, sed ex libera œco- nomia, & dispensatione retineri, cujus causas varias eleganter ibi adducit. Corn. à Lapide in Zach. 12, 6. p. 287. viginti causas ejus rei adfert, ut nempe pla- gæ illæ sint 1. certissimi assumptæ carnis veræ, non phantasticæ, ut volebant Manichæi, indices. 2. atro- cissimæ passionis testes. 3. devictæ mortis aculei, & indubitata resurrectionis argumenta, quod scilicet idem numero corpus Christi crucifixum resurre- xerit, non aliud. 4. ardentissimi amoris characteres, quibus, ut ait Esaias, in manibus suis descripsit nos, non calamts, sed clavis. 5. illustrissima victoriæ de peccato, dæmone, morte, & inferno trophæa. 6. ful- gida gloriosi corporis decora & triumphi. 7. re- demptionis nostræ tessera. 8. obedientiæ usque ad mortem stigmata. 9. Sacræ laborum & dolorum Christi reliquiæ. 10. peccatorum omnium lytrum, quod jugiter Patri pro iis supplicando, Christus re- præsentat. 11. tribulatorum consolatio. 12. patien- tium exemplum. 13. afflictorum refugium. 14. pœ- nitentium incitamentum. 15. tentatorum asylum, juxta illud Cant. 2, 13. Surge amica mea, & veni: co- lumba mea in foraminibus petræ, in caverna maceriæ. 16. laborantium stimulus. 17. martyrum exemplar. 18. electis gaudium. 19. reprobis in die judicii pro- brum. 20. Angelis admiratio & stupor.

## 13:1 Argument
SECTION II. OF THE SEVENTH SERMON. Concerning the Messiah as Shepherd and King of Israel. CHAPTER XIII. The promise of the purification and gathering of the Church. The time of Christ's passion is designated by the character of the institution of Baptism against the impurity of sin, and the elimination of idols, and it is predicted that when Christ the Shepherd is struck, and the sheep scattered, the hand of the Lord shall be turned toward those little ones, and through them some shall nevertheless be gathered for the Lord in the world, and a third, that is, the smallest part, shall be saved for Him, which shall be like purified gold and shall glorify God.

A fountain washes away sins, the flock flees when the Shepherd is struck. V. 1. IN THAT DAY THERE SHALL BE A FOUNTAIN OPENED TO THE HOUSE OF DAVID.) Continuing the discourse begun, he shows that that mourning and the signs of repentance undertaken shall not be without fruit. This open fountain signifies the forgiveness of sins. A similar expression is in Ps. 51:8, Isa. 1:8. He names the house of David specifically, because it too had sinned gravely. AND TO THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM.) Of whom few were untouched by the crime.

FOR THE ABLUTION OF THE SINNER AND THE MENSTRUOUS WOMAN.) In the Hebrew: For sin and for a menstruous woman, that is, those grave sins of idolatry (for which no ablution is promised in the Law) will be washed away as easily as the contamination from a corpse (for that too is called נדה Num. 19, 17) or from the flux of the female sex is washed away. And yet, nothing of the sort is set forth in the Law. I confess, for individuals. But as often as the people had sinned (and the greater part of the people, who were in fault at this time, is considered as the people) and would perform repentance, God had promised that pardon was ready, on account of the fathers, Deut. 30. These are τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ ἀμεταμέλητα. Rom. 11, 29.

Regarding the error of Grotius, that no ablution or pardon for idolatry is promised in the Law, there is no reason for us to deal with it at length here, by which certainly the general statements occurring in the Old Testament concerning the remission of all sins are overturned, the force of the universal annual sacrifice instituted for sins and any iniquities whatsoever, Lev. 16, is enervated, and it is asserted at the same time that there was no hope of grace for idolaters, against so many clear and excellent promises by which idolatrous Israelites were invited by the Prophets to repentance, with the hope of grace and the ablution of sins having been made. Grotius, however, drew this and similar errors from the pools of the Socinians, which we have elsewhere refuted in the same.

One must look into the mind of the Prophet. This is not about the fruit of repentance after the return to the city, brought about by the Maccabean victories. For there has been no discussion of the time of the Maccabees before, but of the day of the New Testament. IN THAT day of the N.T., therefore, a fountain is promised, open to the house of DAVID AND TO THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM: For the Prophet continues to prophesy about the benefits of Christ to be provided to the Church concerning his passion, among which that fountain open for the Holy Sacrament of Baptism stood out. By which the pardon of sins is not understood; for this never comes under the name of a fountain: but the medium of obtaining the pardon of sins, divinely sanctioned and proper to the New Testament, which is nothing other than the Sacrament of Baptism.

For (1) the circumstance of time agrees with this fountain. That that fountain had to be opened around the time of Christ's passion; for around that time, when Christ willed to be inaugurated into his office, by virtue of which he had to give his soul as an ἀντίλυτρον for us, the first baptizer opened that fountain openly by the command of God, as witnessed by Matthew and Luke ch. 3, Mark and John ch. 1. But when Christ was pierced on the cross, and water and blood came out from his side, the pious ancients with great consensus establish that the holy Baptism was prefigured by the water that came out from the pierced side; concerning which piercing Zechariah had dealt in ch. 12, 10; finally, having been raised from the dead, he instituted the Sacrament of Baptism and commended it to his Apostles, that they might open this fountain of grace and salvation to the whole world. (2) The circumstance of place agrees: Jerusalem is named: by which word, even if the mystical Jerusalem which is above, the Church, and the communion of saints is understood, it is nevertheless not to be doubted that the Holy Spirit wished to use this appellation in describing the Church because the beginning of the distribution of the benefits of Christ in the New Testament had to take place in this holy city, which from there were to diffuse themselves through the whole world, Luke 24, 47. And yet it is certain from Acts 2 that that fountain was first opened after the passion of Christ by the disciples of Christ in Jerusalem at the Feast of Pentecost, where three thousand of Peter's hearers were washed and purged in this sacred fountain in one day. It is also said that all Jerusalem went out to John the Baptist, who was the boundary, as Tertullian says, in whom Judaism ceased and Christianity began, for the sake of Baptism, as witnessed by Matthew ch. 3, 5. (3) The benefit connected with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit agrees. For on that day, or time, in which the Spirit of grace and supplications was to be poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that fountain also had to be opened to the same. Which was so fulfilled in the fullness of time, that even on that very day on which the illustrious and most solemn outpouring of the Spirit took place, after the ascension of Christ into heaven in the city of Jerusalem, the Sacrament of Baptism was first dispensed in the same city, and afterwards, with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon the firstfruits of the Gentiles, Acts 9, they were immediately admitted to the same laver of regeneration. Can anyone forbid water, that those who have received the Holy Spirit, just as we have, should not be baptized, says Peter, and he ordered them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, v. 47, 48. So connected are these benefits, which the Prophet joins and recalls to the same time, the more generous outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the opening of the fountain against spiritual impiety. (4.) The description of the fountain agrees. For it is called a FOUNTAIN, which name is most apt for Baptism, because in it the ablution of sins takes place, just as we are washed in a fountain or river, whence also the first baptizer performed this sacred ablution at the Jordan, Matt. 3, 5, John 1, 28, and in Aenon near Salim, where there were many waters, ch. 3, 23. It is called an OPEN FOUNTAIN, because it was to be patent, manifest, and exposed to all in the house of David and to the citizens of the Church. For the fountain of Baptism is open to all in the Church, to which access is open to all; and all are invited divinely; It is a fountain, says Cocceius, not simply, but open. Open is opposed to closed and veiled: Access to that fountain will be free to all without any impediments and obstacles, without a veil. The LXX Interpreters have τόπος διανοιγόμενος, an open place, as if it were מקום. Which is an open παρόραμα, also noted by the Alexandrian. To Cyril: although he tries to recall that to the same sense: You should know that in the Hebrew edition this sentence stands otherwise. For instead of (every place shall be open, he says, it will be that every fountain shall gush forth) it is quite probable, and the LXX interpretation tends the same way, although the words are otherwise, so that something of that kind is signified. To the inhabitants of Jerusalem what intelligence is perceived, or the house of Judah, that is, of Christ, every place shall be open, or in every place a fountain, flowing with the water of purification, certainly of holy Baptism for the benefit of believers. It is called a FOUNTAIN open to the HOUSE OF DAVID, AND TO THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM, which some take synonymously, so that the house of David is the house of Christ, who is accustomed to be called David, i.e., of the inhabitants of Jerusalem or citizens of the Church. The Church can also be called the house of David, as it is called the house of Jacob Luke 1, 33. Others distinguish the house of David from the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Tarnovius understands that to be the Jewish Church first called to the communion of the spiritual goods of the New Testament Luke 24, 47. Acts 1, 8. chap. 13, 46. but through all the inhabitants of Jerusalem the citizens of the entire Church of the New Testament. Others wish the Apostles and other ministers of the Church to be indicated by the house of David, as Osiander. Not badly, by force of the comparison in chap. 12, 8. Some say the house of David is named because this grace pertains even to the Princes themselves. The simplest interpretation seems to be that the house of David is so named because the promise was made to David that God would build him a house: but the citizens of Jerusalem, because salvation is from Jerusalem. The sum is that the Church is designated. Baptism is the fountain of the Davidic house and of the citizens of Jerusalem, that is, a good of the Christian Church, which fountain the Lord opened to those who are born in the Church; for those who are outside are strangers to the covenants of the promises Eph. 2, and therefore are called unclean 1 Cor. 7, because they must remain outside the camp of the Church until, instructed by the word, they declare their assent in the faith, or come into the power of Christians in a legitimate way: and then through Baptism they too can be grafted into the Church; but the children of the faithful are called holy, because they are born in the Church, to whom that fountain of Baptism is open, although they cannot yet declare their assent in the faith. Whence it appears that those who are outside are not simply excluded from this saving fountain, but by the power of the divine will and institution, Baptism pertains to all who are born of the flesh and have need of regeneration: and therefore, if the Lord has called those who are also from afar, as Peter speaks in Acts 2:29, we affirm that this fountain is open to them also, as the blessed Balduinus has in this place. Jerome here compares the fountain of Ezekiel: Concerning this fountain, which shall go forth from the house of David, it is also written in the prophet Ezekiel: that a fountain shall burst forth in the house of the Lord, and grow into a river, which is called the water of remission and indulgence: And it shall go to the wilderness and to the sea, which is now called the Dead Sea, and shall give life to all the fish, and on both banks of the river shall arise trees of various kinds, always abounding in new fruits every month. And that we may know the house, that is, the temple of God, to be the very house of David, which in Ezekiel is called the house of God, and in Zechariah the house of David: this fountain going forth from the house of God is referred to the Church and to the knowledge of the Scriptures: so that we may all be reborn in Christ, and our sins be forgiven us in the water of baptism. The fountain is said to be open TO THE INHABITANTS of Jerusalem indefinitely to all, as if to say: Formerly there was a certain laver in the atrium of the Temple, where the priests washed before they ministered to the Lord, 2 Chron. 4, but it was not permitted for any but the priests to wash in it, and indeed it was necessary that clean water be brought into those vessels from time to time. But the time shall come that a gushing fountain shall be opened in the Church, to which access shall be open to all, of whatever condition they may be. And this fountain shall wash away sins and all uncleanness before God, as Osiander has here.

It is said to be open FOR THE WASHING OF THE SINNER AND THE MENSTRUOUS WOMAN, as the Vulgate has rendered it. The Hebrew has לְחַטַּאת, i.e., sin, and לְנִדָּה, which word denotes separation, as also the thing which is removed because of uncleanness, and it also denotes the menses and a menstruous woman; see Lev. 11:24, 25. Whence by the former word actual sin is designated, but by the latter original sin, which separates a man naturally, just as the menses separated a woman from her husband, and which is born with man, as that menstrual uncleanness is to a woman. The fountain therefore opened here is for original and actual sin, so that, namely, the former may be washed away in this fountain: just as the former word not only denotes sin, but is also accustomed to indicate a sin-offering and the expiation of sin. See Exod. 30:10, Lev. 4:3, ch. 6:24, Isa. 40:7. But what other fountain can be commemorated in the New Testament as openly revealed for washing away every original and actual sin, besides Baptism, concerning which Cassiodorus says in Cant. ch. 7: It is a divine fountain, by which the faithful are regenerated into a new creature. And Tertullian, book on Baptism, ch. 1: Happy is the sacrament of our water, because, our sins of former blindness being washed away, we are set free into eternal life. Bede, book 1, ch. III, on John: The sinner, he says, descends into the fountain, he ascends purified; he descends a son of death, he ascends a son of the resurrection; he descends a son of prevarication, he ascends a son of reconciliation; he descends a son of wrath, he ascends a son of mercy; he descends a son of the Devil, but he ascends a son of God. St. Chrysostom, Oration on Baptism. of Christ compares the Jewish and Christian Baptism in this way: The Jewish expiation indeed did not at all set one free from sins, but only from bodily filth, but ours is not such, but much greater, and full of much grace; for it both sets one free from sins, and cleanses the soul, and bestows the grace of the Spirit. The LXX Interpreters rendered it here far otherwise. For they interpreted it εἰς τὴν μετακίνησιν and εἰς τὸν ῥαντισμὸν, into transmutation and sprinkling. Yet Cyril explains these things concerning Baptism thus: What is this transmutation

of the Jews from the legal institution to life in Christ, from shadow to truth, from type and letter to spiritual worship. But what will be the transmutation of the Greeks? They come from unbelief to believing in Christ, and from the greatest ignorance to the pure knowledge of the true God, from darkness to illumination. But the common transmutation, suitable to everyone called through faith, for Jew and Greek, is the resolve to cease from savoring the things of the flesh, to live holily and purely, and to walk in the spirit, as the blessed Paul exhorts: from the admiration of those things which are in the world, to loving those things which are above the world. Furthermore, as we receive the divine and sacred Baptism, who would doubt that we are sprinkled with the blood of Christ for the purging of sin? Therefore, the way to transmutation and sprinkling for those inhabiting the house of Judah is the saving Baptism, or every place opened, or every fountain widened, and the water of purification or expiation gushing forth. St. Jerome similarly explains and reconciles the sense of the translation of the LXX Interpreters with the authentic text: Nothing is more unclean than a menstruous woman, who makes unclean whatever she touches, and yet the filth of this woman shall be washed away by the Baptism of Christ. For the washing of sins and the menstruous woman, the LXX translated transmutation and sprinkling, because we pass from the law to the Gospel, from the letter to the spirit, from shadow to truth: so that future and eternal things may succeed the brief and present ones. Moreover, sprinkling signifies the blood of the Lord, of which the Apostle Peter also speaks: May grace and peace be multiplied unto you in obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ. And again: Knowing that you were redeemed not with corruptible silver and gold, but with the precious blood, as of an unspotted and most pure lamb, by which he who shall have been sprinkled and redeemed will be able to say with the Prophet: Thou shalt sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

(5) A second benefit connected with this is the extirpation of idolatry, because the opening of the fountain of Baptism gushing forth throughout the whole world was joined with the overthrow of the idolatry which flourished throughout the world before the coming of the Lord; and in the Sacrament of Baptism we are freed from the power of Satan, where the ἐπερώτημα of a good conscience and a covenant with the Holy Trinity is entered into, and by this Sacrament we are bound to the worship and profession of that same one God, renouncing the Devil and all his works. Whence Dionysius, Hierarch. Eccl. c. III, called Baptism the seal of the divine pact, and Cyprian, l. IV, Epist. VII, to Magnus, says: In Baptism, all the powers of the Devil lose their wickedness. Just as scorpions and serpents, adds St. Cyprian, which prevail on dry land, when cast into water cannot prevail or retain their poisons: so also the wicked spirits, which are called scorpions and serpents, and yet are trampled upon by us through the power given by God, can no longer remain in the body of a man in whom the Holy Spirit begins to dwell, having been baptized and sanctified.

(6.) The oracle of the following chapter, verse 8, agrees: In that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem, and half of them shall flow to the eastern sea and half of them to the hinder sea, Zech. 14, 8. This water is rightly compared here, even if it is explained by most as the Word of God or the Holy Spirit. For the Holy Spirit diffuses His gifts in the Church not without the Sacrament of Baptism, which is the fountain of His graces and gifts; and the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, who is poured out abundantly in the same, Tit. 3, 5, as well as the washing of water by the word, Eph. 5, 26. Therefore, Baptism cannot be excluded from the flow of living waters promised there, which Theodoret, quest. 26 in Genesis, also calls living water. Baptism is called living water, not because the water of Baptism has a different nature, but because through that water divine grace grants eternal life.

The analogy agrees, which is discovered in the latest Prophets of the Old Testament. For these, being closer to the New Testament, designate those signs of the coming of Christ, from which it ought to have been recognized that Christ was near, or already present, such as that notable shaking of heaven and earth, and sea and dry land of Haggai, and John the forerunner of the Messiah in Malachi, for the sake of which thing Zechariah also had to set forth this fountain opened about the time of the Messiah's coming, which was to be openly manifested, which the Proto-baptist was first to open.

To these we add that (8) other interpretations, if we compare them with this one of ours, deservedly yield to it. (1) Some explain it concerning the fountain of the temple, by which the unclean and menstruous women were washed, restored in the time of the Maccabees. Similarly, Danaeus interprets it concerning the sacrifices then restored: But this is cold and Jewish. Nor is Danaeus consistent with himself in this; indeed, he confesses that this prophecy was truly fulfilled when John the Baptist baptized in the rivers all the penitents who came to him, and was the first to use in the Church, by God's command and by this prophecy, the Baptism of the Church (which is the testimony of all our sins washed away by God through the blood of Christ), and thus that the prophecy and promise of instituting that Baptism which we have today in the Church are contained therein, and which is said to have been commanded from heaven by God to John the Baptist, Matt. 21, 25. Finally, approved and sanctioned by Christ himself in his own person, Matt. 3. (2) Haymo and Hugo interpret it concerning the fountain of divine mercy. But the fountain of divine mercy is always open to the faithful, whereas here something peculiar and proper to the time of the New Testament is promised. (3) Remigius understands doctrine by the fountain, as in Prov. 20, the mouth of the righteous is called a vein of life, with which Winckelsm. agrees. That open fountain is the doctrine of the Gospel, concerning the grace of God and the remission of sins, through which the Holy Spirit announces the remission of sins, the washing away of sin through faith in the blood of Christ, and consoles and vivifies terrified consciences; to which also the Chaldean version goes, in that time the doctrine of the law will be revealed, and a spring of waters to the house of David. But the house of David, or Jerusalem, was not destitute of a spring of doctrine in Zechariah's time; and was there not then doctrine, which flowed from the mouth of Zechariah, like an open fountain, if this fountain is to be indicated as doctrine? (4) Theodoret, Gregor. M. Homil. IX. in Zach., Montanus, Castrius, Cornelius say this fountain is God incarnate, the true spring perpetually flowing into men in every age with the water of all grace and doctrine, which fountain and origin is also the Holy Spirit, whom he pours into us, that he may purge sins and quench the thirst of the soul. (5) Others interpret it concerning the Holy Spirit, who is called living water by Christ, John 7, 34. (6) Some concerning the side of Christ opened on the cross, from which flowed water and blood. (7) Coccejus says the fountain denotes the blood of the covenant itself, Zech. 9, 11, which was poured out through the piercing. To which also the explanation of Junius goes, as well as Piscator. Indeed, and Calvin in loc. Which opinion is more suitable than the others. For although the Holy Spirit is compared to a fountain and living water, yet this character, that this fountain is opened for the washing away of sin and menstruation, is proper to the blood of Christ. Moreover, just as Christ the God-man is the efficient cause of our washing, so the opening of Christ's side and the blood of Christ contribute to our cleansing in the category of the meritorious cause, but here the medium of communication and application is rather designated, and the fountain is opened to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that by the same act they may be washed from the filth of sin and menstruation, which is indeed done by the blood

of Christ, but as it is dispensed in Baptism, inasmuch as it is the washing of our regeneration, Tit. 3, 5, in which we are washed from sins, as it was said to Paul, Acts 22, 15: Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of Jesus.

Therefore, that we may bring forward (9) authorities, Jerome, Cyril, Rupert, Hugo, Lyranus, Raim. Martini, Dionysius the Carthusian, Galatinus, Isidorus Clarius, and others establish that this fountain is Baptism. Thus, of our own, the blessed Balduinus: Such a washing is promised, by which both original evil and actual sins are washed away. The blessed Gerhard, in his Commonplaces on Baptism, §. 10: That fountain, open and accessible to all, is Baptism, washing away actual sins and original uncleanness, Eph. 5, 26. Add the blessed Wigand, the blessed Pappus, the blessed Tarnovius, Dr. Müller in Judaismus, p. 785, Dr. Klotz, Disp. on Baptism, with whom most others agree. The blessed Luther, although against the Sacramentarians he explains the present passage not concerning Baptism but concerning the Holy Spirit, yet he rightly teaches that the same is to be understood concerning Baptism in his German Commentary, Vol. IV, Jena, on this passage, which Commentary was prepared in the year 1528. But eight years later, Megalander, in his explanation of Joel in the year 1536, placed beyond all doubt that the Prophet prophesied in this place concerning Baptism, and he compares with the present oracle the passage in Isa. 12, 3, as also Joel 3, 18, and waters shall go through all the rivers of Judah, and a fountain shall go forth from the house of the Lord, and shall water the valley of thorns. See Vol. VIII, Wittenberg, German, f. 406, Vol. 6, Altenburg, p. 491, and Vol. IV, Latin, Jena, f. 481. Nor do more recent Papists deny that Baptism is predicted here. "Tirinus: On that day, on which Christ (as preceded in ch. 12) shall be looked upon suspended from the cross, there shall be opened from him and his wounds a most abundant FOUNTAIN, not only of doctrine, as Remigius wishes, but also of the Sacraments and every kind of grace, and that for the WASHING OF ANY SINNER WHOSOEVER, AND also OF A MENSTRUOUS WOMAN, that is, for the taking away of all uncleanness and filth contracted from transgression, whether of the law of nature or of the Mosaic law." He alludes first to the waters of purification, Num. 19, 11. then to the waters of Siloam, Isaiah 8, 6. and John 9, 7. finally to the waters bursting forth from under the threshold of the temple, Ezek. 47, 1. All of which were types and figures of our living fountain Christ, as even the Hebrews cited by Galatinus acknowledge. Moreover, it is evident that this fountain is perpetual, not only for the LORD, that is, for the family and descendants of David, that is, for the primates and more noble persons, but indiscriminately for all the INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM, even the commoners, even those converted from paganism. Nor is the reasoning of Castrius and Cornelius of any weight, that this fountain is said to be opened for the washing away of all sins; for sins to be washed away are those committed not only before, but also after Baptism, because the efficacy of Baptism extends itself into the future, since the gifts of God are ἀμεταμέλητα.

From the Reformed, Danaeus acknowledges the same, who interpreted it typically indeed concerning the Levitical washings to be restored by the Maccabees, but professed that this prophecy was truly fulfilled in Baptism. Although we admit that Baptism was also prefigured by such typical washings, we deny that the literal sense of this prophecy looks to the times of the Maccabees and treats of Levitical washing, nor do we concede that a double sense of the same prophecy is given here or anywhere else.

Finally, Grotius also acknowledged here that the Prophet prophesied concerning Baptism, Annot. John 1, 25. on John 1, 25.

Willius is again singular in this place, and, as he carves out from this prophecy his Smyrnean period, strong in testimonies, he invents that the 'fountain' is to be understood as a vein and spring of blood, and that it will be opened with respect to the Church indeed, so that the martyrs may offer themselves to God like sacrifices, and by the shedding of blood separate themselves from the Gentiles; but with respect to the tyrants, so that they may remove the pious like expiatory offerings from the human race, and in place of sacrifices offer them to their idols for their sins, and cast them out from themselves as unclean and beset with vices. But who indeed would have seen this sense concerning a vein of blood, and concerning that cause of the flow, to be taken in one way with respect to the Church and in another way with respect to the tyrants in the same words in this oracle, except this Delian of Bremen? The word מקור placed absolutely nowhere denotes a vein of blood; for in Lev. 20:18 it does not occur absolutely, but the FOUNTAIN OF A WOMAN is indicated, and an ἐξήγησις is added besides, the fountain of her blood. Nor is the fountain said to be opened so that sacrifices may be offered, but so that the impure may be washed from their sins; then if the pious are said to be offered by them to idols for the sins of the Gentiles, how is it indicated by the same words that the pious will offer themselves to the one true God like voluntary sacrifices? And where is the separation from the Gentiles, whether active or passive, established in this place as the cause of martyrdom? Finally, is it not thus impiously attributed to God, that He will open a fountain of blood, so that martyrs may be offered in place of sacrifices to the idols of the Gentiles?

Latin:

SECTIO II. CONCIONIS SEPTIMÆ. De Messia Pastore & Rege Israelis. CAPUT XIII. Promissio purificationis & congrega- tionis Ecclesiæ. Tempus passionis Christi charactere institu- tionis Baptismi adversus impuritatem pec- cati, & eliminationis idolorum designatur, & percusso Christo Pastore, ovibusque di- sparsis manum Domini ad parvulos illos convertendam, & per eosdem in orbe ali- quos tamen Domini colligendos, & ter- tiam, h. e. minimam partem ei servan- dam, quæ instar auri depurati futura Deumque glorificatura sit, prædicitur.

Fons peccata lavat, cæso Pastore fugit grex. V. 1. IN DIE ILLA ERIT FONS PATENS DO- MUI DAVID.) Continuans cœptum sermonem osten- dit luctum illum, & susceptæ pœnitentiæ signa non futura sine fructu. Fons patens hic veniam peccatorum significat. Similis locutio Ps. 51, 8. Esa. 1, 8. domum Davidis spe- cialiter nominat, quia & ipsa graviter dliquerat. ET HABITANTIBUS JERUSALEM.) Quorum pauci intacti à crimine.

IN ABLUTIONEM PECCATORIS ET MENSTRUATÆ.) In Hebræo: In peccatum & menstruum, id est, tam facile abluentur gravia illa peccata idololatriæ (cujus nulla in lege ablutio promittitur) quam facile abluitur contaminatio ex cadavere (nam & id dicitur נדה Num. 19, 17.) aut ex profluvio sexus muliebris. Atqui in lege nihil tale proditum. Fateor, pro singulis. At quoties populus peccasset (pro populo autem habetur pars major populi, quæ in culpa erat hoc tempore) & pœnitentiam ageret, veniam Deus paratam promiserat, propter patres Deuteron. 30. Hæc sunt τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ ἀμεταμέλητα. Rom. 11, 29.

De errore Grotii, quod in lege nulla ablutio, aut venia promittatur idololatriæ, non est, quod hic multis agamus, quo certe convelluntur dicta generalia de remissione peccatorum omnium in V. T. occurrentia, vis sacrificii universalis anniversarii pro peccatis, & iniquitatibus quibusvis instituti Lev. XVI. enervatur, atque asseritur simul, nullam idolatris spem fuisse gratiæ, adversus tot luculentas & præclaras promissiones, quibus invitati sunt Israëlitæ idololatræ à Prophetis ad pœnitentiam, facta spe gratiæ, & ablutionis peccatorum. Hausit autem hunc & similes errores Grotius è lacunis Socinianorum, quos alibi in ijsdem profligavimus.

De mente Prophetæ dispiciendum. Non hic agitur de fructu pœnitentiæ post reditum in urbem, Maccabæorum victoriis conciliatum. Neque enim de Maccabæorum tempore antea actum, sed de die Novi Testamenti. IN ILLA ergo N. T. DIE fons patens domui DAVID ET HABITANTIBUS JERUSALEM promittitur: Pergit enim Propheta vaticinari de beneficiis Christi circa ejus passionem Ecclesiæ præstandis, inter quæ eminebat fons ille patens S. S. Baptismatos. Per quem non intelligitur venia peccatorum; hæc enim nuspiam fontis nomine venit: sed medium consequendi peccatorum veniam, divinitus sancitum Nov. Test. proprium, quod nullum aliud est, quam Sacramentum Baptismi.

Nam huic fonti convenit (1) circumstantia temporis. Quod circa passionem Christi fons ille aperiri debuerit; Nam sub illud tempus, quo Christus inaugurari ad officium suum voluit, vi cujus animam suam ἀντίλυτρον pro nobis dare debuit, πρωτοβαπτιστὴς fontem illum palam mandato Dei aperuit, testibus Matth. & Luc. c. III. Marco & Johanne cap. I. Quum vero Christus transfigeretur in cruce, atq; exiret aqua & sanguis è latere ejus, figuratum per aquam è latere transfixo egressam sanctum Baptismum pii veteres magno consensu statuunt; de qua transfixione c. 12, 10. Zacharias egerat, deniq; resuscitatus à morte Sacramentum Baptismi instituit, atq; Apostolis suis commendavit, ut hunc fontem gratiæ & salutis universo orbi adaperirent. (2) convenit circumstantia loci: Nominatur Hierosolyma: qua voce, etsi mystica Hierosolyma, quæ sursum est, intelligatur, Ecclesia, & communio sanctorum, minime tamen dubitandum est, hac appellatione in describenda Ecclesia ideo uti voluisse Sp. S. quod initium distribuendorum beneficiorum Christi in Nov. T. fieri debuerit in hac sancta urbe, quæ exinde se diffusura erant per totum orbem Luc. 24, 47. Atqui constat ex Actor. 2. quod fons ille post passionem Christi primum apertus sit à discipulis Christi Hierosolymis in Festo Pentecostes, ubi sacro hoc fonte abluti ac purgati sunt uno die ter mille de auditoribus Petri. Ad Johannem Baptistam etiam, qui limes fuit, dicente Tertulliano, in quo cessavit Judaismus, & cœpit Christianismus, tota Hierosolyma exiisse dicitur Baptismi causa, teste Matthæo cap. 3, 5. (3) Convenit beneficium connexum effusioms Spiritus Sancti. Nam in die illo, vel tempore, quo effundendus erat Spiritus gratiæ & precum super habitatores Jerusalem, aperiri & fons ille iisdem debuit. Quod ita adimpletum in temporis pleni- tudine, ut etiam eo ipso die, quo illustris & maxime solennis effusio Spiritus facta est, post ascensionem Christi in cœlum in urbe Jerusalem, Baptismos Sacramentum primitus dispensatum in eadem ur- be fuerit, ac postmodum cum effusione Spiritus S. super gentium primitias Act. 9. ad idem lavacrum regenerationis actutum illæ admissæ sint. Nunquid aquam quis prohibere potest, ut non baptizentur ii, qui Sp. S. acceperunt, sicut & nos, ait Petrus, & jussit eos baptizari in nomine Domini Jesu Christi, v. 47. 48. Adeo connexa hæc beneficia sunt, quæ conjungit & ad idem tempus revocat Propheta, Sp.S. largior effusio, & fontis adversus impietatem spiritualem apertio. (4.) Convenit fontis descriptio. Nam dicitur FONS, quod nomen aptissimum est Baptis- mo, quia in illo peccatorum fit ablutio, uti in fonte aut flumine abluimur, unde etiam πρωτοβαπτι- στης ablutionem istam sacram peragebat ad Jor- danem Matth. 3, 5. Joh. 1, 28. & in Enon prope Sa- lim, ubi multæ aquæ erant cap. 3, 23. Dicitur FONS APERTUS, quod sit futurus patens, manifestus, & omnibus expositus in domo Davidis, & civibus Eccle- siæ. Nam Baptismi fons omnibus apertus est in Ecclesia, ad quem omnibus patet aditus; omnesque invitantur divinitus; Est fons, inquit Coccejus, non simpliciter, sed apertus. Apertus opponitur clauso & velato: Aditus ad illum fontem erit omnibus li- ber absque ullis impedimentis & obstaculis, absque velo. LXX. Interpp. habent τόπος διανοιγόμενος, locus apertus, quasi esset מקום. Quod apertum est παρο- ραμα, notatum etiam Alexandr. Cyrillo: etsi id ad sensum eundem revocare conetur: Scias velim in Hæbræa editione sententiam hanc aliter extare. Nam pro (erit omnis locus apertus, ait, fore, ut omnis fons scaturiatur) & probabile est admodum, & LXX. interpretationem eodem tendere, quamvis verba secus habeant, ut quiddam ejusmodi significetur. Habitan- tibus Hierusalem quæ intelligentia conspicitur, sive domum Juda, id est, Christi, erit omnis locus apertus, sive in omni loco fons, purgationis aqua manans, utique sacri Baptismatis ad utilitatem credentium. Dici- tur FONS patens DOMUI DAVID, ET HA- BITANTIBUS JERUSALEM, quæ nonnulli συνωνύμως accipiunt, ut domus David sit domus Christi, qui David dici solet, h. e. habitatorum Jeru- salem seu civium Ecclesiæ. Dici etiam potest Eccle- sia domus David, ut dicitur domus Jacob Luc. 1, 37. Alii domum Davidis ab habitantibus Hierusalem distinguunt. Illam Tarnovius intelligit Ecclesiam Judaicam primum vocatam ad communionem bo- norum spiritualium Nov. Test. Luc. 24, 4. Actor. 1, 8. cap. 13, 46. per omnes vero habitatores Jerusa- lem cives universos Ecclesiæ Nov. Test. Alii per do- mum Davidis Apostolos, & Ecclesiæ ministros alios in- digitari volunt, uti Osiander. Non male, vi collatio- nis c. 12, 8. Nonnulli nominari ajunt domum Davidis, quod etiam ad ipsos Principes pertineat hæc gratia. Simplicissima interpretatio videtur, domum David ideo nominari, quia Davidi promissio facta, Deum ei ædificaturum domum: cives autem Hierusalem, quia salus ex Hierosolyma est. Summa est, designari Ecclesiam. Baptismus est fons domus Davidicæ, & civium Hierusalem, id est, bonum Ecclesiæ Christianæ, quem fontem aperuit Dominus iis, qui in Ecclesia nati sunt; nam qui foris sunt, alieni sunt à testamen- tis promissionum Eph. 2. ideoque immundi dicuntur 1. Cor. 7. quia extra castra Ecclesiæ ipsis manendum est, donec verbo instituti suum in fide assensum de- clarent, aut modo legitimo in potestatem Christia- norum veniant:& tunc per Baptismum & ipsi inseri possunt Ecclesiæ; liberi vero fideliũ sancti dicuntur, quia in Ecclesia nati, quibus patet ille fons Baptismi, licet nondum suum in fide assensum declarare pos- fint. Unde apparet, eos, qui foris sunt, non simpli- citer ab hoc fonte salutari exclusos esse, sed vi vo- luntatis & institutionis divinæ pertinet Baptismus ad omnes, qui ex carne nati sunt, & regeneratione opus habent: ac proinde si advocaverit eos Dominus, qui etiam à longe sunt, ut Petrus loquitur Actor. 2. v. 29. his quoq; hunc fontem patere adfirmamus, ut habet B. Balduinus in h. l. Hieronymus hic con- fert fontem Ezechielis: De hoc fonte, qui egredie- tur de domo David, & in Ezechiele Propheta scribitur: quod erumpat fons in domo Domini, & crescat in fluvium, qui appellatur aqua remissionis & indulgen- tiæ: Et pergat ad solitudinem & ad mare, quod nunc vocatur, mortuum, piscesque omnes vivifi- cet, & ex utraque ripa fluminis varii generis con- surgant arbores per singulos menses semper novis fructibus abundantes. Et ut sciamus domum, hoc est, templum Dei ipsam esse domum David, quæ in E- zechiel domus Dei, in Zacharia, domus David appel- latur: hic fons de domo Dei egrediens refertur ad Ec- clesiam & ad scientiam Scripturarum: ut omnes rena- scamur in Christo, & in aqua baptismatis nostra nobis peccata donentur. Dicitur fons apertus HABI- TANTIBUS Ierusalem indefinite omnibus, q. d. Olim fuit lavacrum quoddam in atrio Templi, ubi Sacerdotes lavabant, antequam ministrarent Domi- no 2. Par. 4. sed non licebat nisi Sacerdotibus in il- lo lavare, & quidem opus erat, ut subinde munda a- qua in illa vasa comportaretur. Sed tempus veniet, ut scaturiens fons in Ecclesia aperiatur, ad quem omnibus pateat accessus, cujuscunque sint condi- tionis. Et iste fons peccata & omnem coram Deo im- munditiem abluet, ut hic habet Osiander.

Dicitur patere in ABLUTIONEM PECCA- TORIS ET MENSTRUATÆ, ut Vulgatus reddidit. Hebræum habet לְחַטַּאת, h. e. peccatum & לְנִדָּה, quæ vox separationem, ut & rem, quæ pro- pter immunditiem removetur, nec non menstruum ac mulierem menstruatam notat; vid. Lev. 11, 24. 25. Unde priori voce peccatum actuale, posteriori vero peccatum originale designatur, quod hominem se- parat naturaliter, quemadmodum menstruum sepa- rabat mulierem à viro, quodq́; homini connascitur, ut menstrua illa immundities mulieri. Fons ergo a- pertus hic est peccato originali & actuali, ut sc. illud abluatur in hoc fonte: quemadmodum etiam vox prior non solum peccatum notat, sed piaculum & expiationem peccati quoque indigitare solet. Vid. Exod. 30, 10. Lev. 4, 3. c. 6, 24. Esa. 40, 7. Quis ve- ro alius fons in N. T. commemorari potest palam apertus ad abluendum omne originale peccatum & actuale, præter Baptismum, de quo Cassiodorus in Cant. c. 7. Est fons divinus, quo fideles in novam cre- aturam regenerantur. Et Tertullian. libr. de Baptism. c. I. Felix Sacramentum aquæ nostræ, quia ablutis de- lictis pristinæ cæcitatis in vitam æternam liberamur. Beda l. I. c. III. in Joh. Peccator, inquit, in fontem de- scendit, purificatus ascendit, descendit filius mortis, ascendit filius resurrectionis, descendit filius prævari- cationis, ascendit filius reconciliationis, descendit filius iræ, ascendit filius misericordiæ, descendit filius Diabo- li, sed ascendit filius Dei. S. Chrysostom. Orat. de Baptism. Christi confert Iudaicum & Christianum Baptismum hoc modo: Judaica quidem expiatio nequaquam à peccatis liberabat, sed a corporeis sordi- bus tantum, nostra vero talis non est, sed multo major, ac multæ plena gratiæ; nam & a peccatis liberat, & animam abstergit & Spiritus gratiam largitur. LXX. Interpp. hic longe aliter reddidere. Interpretati e- nim sunt εἰς τὴν μετακίνησιν & εἰς τὸν ῥαντισμὸν in transmutationem & aspersionem. Hæc tamen de Bapti- smo ita explicat Cyrillus: Quanam ista transmutatio

Iudæorum ex institutione legali ad vitam in Christo, ab umbra ad veritatem, à typo & litera ad cultum spiritualem. Quænam autem Græcorum erit trans- mutatio? ex incredulitate ad Christo credendum ve- niunt, & ex ignorantia maxima ad agnitionem puram veri Dei, à tenebris ad illuminationem. Transmuta- tio autem communis, cuilibet per fidem vocato conve- niens, Iudæo & Græco à sapiendo ea, quæ carnis sunt, sancte ac pure vivendi, & in spiritu ambulandi consi- lium, uti B. Paulus hortatur: ex admiratione eorum, quæ in mundo sunt, ad diligenda, quæ supra mundum sunt. Divinum porro & sacrum Baptisma suspicien- tes nos aspergi sanguine Christi ad expurgationem pec- cati, quis dubitet? Ergo via ad transmutationem, & aspertionem domum Iuda habitantibus salutare Ba- ptisma est, sive omnis locus apertus, sive omnis fons di- latatus, & purgationis seu expiationis aqua scaturiens. Similiter explicat & conciliat sensum translationis LXX. Interpp. cum authentico textu S. Hierony- mus: Nihil immundius menstruata, quæ, quicquid at- tigerit, immundum facit, & hujus tamen sordes Chri- sti abluentur Baptismate. Pro ablutione peccatorum & menstruata LXX. transtulerunt transmutationem & aspersionem, quod de lege transeamus ad Evange- lium, de litera ad spiritum, de umbra ad veritatem: pro brevibus & præsentibus futura & æterna succe- dant. Aspersio autem sanguinem Domini significat, de quo & Petrus Apostolus loquitur: Gratia vobis & pax multiplicetur in obedientiam & aspersionem sanguinis Jesu Christi. Et rursum: Scientes, quod non corruptibilibus argento & auro redemti estis, sed sanguine pretioso, ut agni immaculati & puris- simi, quo qui aspersus fuerit & redemptus, dicere pote- rit cum Propheta: Asperges me Domine hyssopo & mundabor, lavabis me, & super nivem dealbabor.

(5) Convenit connexum alterum beneficium extirpandæ idololatriæ, quia apertio fontis Baptismi per universum orbem scaturientis conjuncta fuit cum eversione idololatriæ, quæ ante adventum Do- mini per orbem viguit; & in Sacramento Baptismi liberamur à potestate Satanæ, ubi ἐπερώτημα bonæ conscientiæ, ac fœdus cum S. S. Trinitate initur, & ad ejusdem unius cultum & professionem hoc Sa- cramento adstringimur, renunciantes Diabolo, & omnibus ejus operibus. Unde Baptismum Dio- nysius Hierarch. Eccl. c. III. vocavit sigillum pactio- nis divinæ, & Cyprian. l. IV. Epist. VII. ad Magnan. In Baptismo, ait, omnes nequitiæ vires Diabolum amit- tere. Sicut scorpii & serpentes, addit S. Cyprianus, qui in sicco prævalent, in aquas præcipitati prævalere non possunt, aut sua venena retinere: Sic & Spiritus nequam, qui scorpii & serpentes appellantur, & tamen per nos data à Deo potestate calcantur, permanere ul- tra non possunt in hominis corpore, in quo baptizato & sanctificato incipit habitare Spiritus Sanctus.
