Which Grotius himself, openly fighting with himself, interpreted, whom I love most: with this observation added: As often as GOOD men perished by a violent death, so often among the pious did the faith of the resurrection grow, (Shall we attribute a glorious resurrection to an evil shepherd, whom he himself called Manasseh, a vain and profane man, whose right eye was to be darkened by divine judgment, i.e., according to his own interpretation, who was to be deprived of the knowledge of divine things?) and this economy, differing from the legal one (these things smack of Socinianism, and the delirium of the Pelagians, nay of the Sadducees, that the faith of the resurrection was not handed down in the law or the O.T.: which he accumulates with a new error, as if the promises of the law regarding temporal happiness are to be taken simply, and do not admit the exception of the cross) was a preparation for the Gospel. But Grotius finally admits the passage of Zechariah pointed out here, even if he denies that Christ is directly looked to by the words of Zechariah. He still wants it to be a proverbial maxim, which is found in Matthew, and to that end he alleges Virgil, and Livy and Homer, so that we may learn the mind of Scripture from these excellent Interpreters of Scripture. Certainly, he says, those thoughts which are placed in Histories, when placed outside of Histories become maxims, and it is not so much looked to, for what occasion they were originally said, but how widely the force of the maxim extends. Similar is that of Virgil concerning the Bees:

When the king is safe, all have one mind. When he is lost, they break their faith.

and of Livy: Just as an army is routed when the leader is killed, so they slipped away here and there. Homer had said concerning the death of Sarpedon: but they were all routed, since they saw their king with wounded heart lying in the assembly of the dead. But, what do these historical thoughts have to do with a Prophetic prophecy, which Christ taught how it was fulfilled. These differ as much as heaven from earth, to show the fulfillment of a Prophetic prophecy, and to apply it to oneself, and to use a historical thought, as some maxim. But we finally dismiss these ravings, nay, these impious cuckoo-cries against Christ, more worthy of some Julian than a Christian interpreter. All Christian interpreters everywhere understand the prophecy of Christ, which even if Calvin drags to others also, he nevertheless confessed that it treats chiefly of Christ: in which, however, the reason escapes him, since the same saying cannot treat both of Christ the ONLY SHEPHERD, and of shepherds in general, nor can others be understood secondarily, where the Prophet prophesies of nothing but one Shepherd, as far as the literal sense of the same is concerned, which must be unique, and consistent with itself: whence we have also observed that Calvin was refuted here by his own disciples; to whom the Belgian Paraphrasts are to be added, as those who understand this striking uniquely of Christ, the Son of God of the same essence with the Father, and of the dispersion of the Apostles at the time of the passion of Christ. What? That the Jews themselves acknowledged that these things treat of the Messiah? For thus R. Aben Ezra: He still prophesies of many wars, which will be in the whole earth in the time of the Messiah, the Son of Joseph. Which St. Jerome also observed concerning the Jews in this place. The Jews refer these things to Christ, and contend that they will happen in the last time. But this is between us and them, that we say they are already fulfilled, they commemorate that they are to be fulfilled.

Latin:

V. 9. ET DUCAM TERTIAM PARTEM PER IGNEM ET URAM EOS SICUT URITUR ARGENTUM, ET PROBABO EOS SICUT PROBATUR AVRVM.) I. e. per multa mala eorum explorabo constantiam. Pf. 68, 9. Scilicet, ut fulvum spectatur in ignibus aurum Tempore sic duro est inspicienda fides.

IPSE VOCABIT NOMEN MEUM.) ille popu- lus reliquus de cladibus.

Detestanda depravatio vaticinii luculenti. Quæ enim de passione Christi diserte agunt, ad per- cussionem Judæ Maccabæi detorquet Grotius, ne ullum vaticinium nobis de Christo relinquat, nihi- li faciens authenticam interpretationem ipsiusmet Christi, cujus Spiritus hæc dictavit Prophetæ 1. Petr. I, 11. Præiverat L. Danæus, & imprimis Cal- vinus Judaizans: Summa est, antequam Dominus Ecclesiam suam repurget atq; revocet in perfectum ordinem, gravissimas clades fore intermedias: quo- niam accidet horrenda dissipatio, ubi Deus pastores ipsos percusserit. Qui impie etiam ipsi Christo ob- loqui non dubitavit: Nostri fere omnes restringunt hunc locum ad personam Christi, quia Matth. 26. citatur sententia illa, Percutiam Pastorem & di- spergentur oves. Sed non videtur solida esse ratio, quia, quod de Pastore dicitur, potius extendi proba- bile est ad ipsum ordinem totum, quemadmodum ubi dicit Deus, Prophetam vobis excitabo è medio ve- strum, certe illic non sit mentio unius Prophetæ solum, sed complectitur Deus omnes Prophetas. Sic impie- tatem impietate tegit, ne perpluat. Non minus e- nim impia est depravatio loci Mosaici Deut. 18. quam oraculi Prophetici, quod sub manu habemus. Sed Calvinum, prout merebatur, castigavit B. Hunnius, quem tueri in perversa hac causa nequivit Patronus Paræus, quin victas daret manus: Me quod attinet, libenter accipio priorem sententiam, ea cumprimis ratione, quod Deus in singulari Pastorem suum, & virum socium suum percutiendum dicit; haud dubie Pastorem certum, eumq; non gregarium, sed κατ’ ἐξοχὴν magnum designans, qui est Christus. Qui nihilominus γοητεύει, Calvini quoque senten- tiam simul retinendam esse, quod non de solo Chri- sto, sed de toto ordine Pastorum Propheta disserat. Quod annon sit certissimum indicium projecti pu- doris & conscientiæ, malle contradictoria statuere simul esse vera, quam Deo dare gloriam, & confi- teri errasse, cunctis Deum timentibus judicandum non immerito relinquit B. Hunnius. Nam qui pro- bat hanc propositionem: Vaticinium Zacharia- num intelligendum est de SOLO Christo, & non de aliis, imo, qui argumentis etiam adstruit ad solum Christum pertinere, quo ore deinde propositionem huic tam approbatæ è diametro repugnantem di- cet non esse abjiciendam? Hoc certe est ex uno ore efflare calidum & frigidum.

Aliam excogitavit glossam VV illius, Calvinia- nus Doctor, sed æque perversam, quia, quod de uno Christo dictum, & juxta ipsius Christi explica- tionem, omni exceptione superiorem, de passione Christi intelligendum, trahit Willius in reddendo sensu literali, ad Ecclesiæ Christi persecutionem sub Papatu, per gladium intelligens Pontificiam poten- tiam, tyrannidem, bella, mactationes, exustiones, omniaq; Pontificiæ persecutionis instrumentis. Sic abripit homines cæcus impetus, Scripturam sa- cram, insuper habita textus evidentia, & dilucida Sp. S. interpretatione, pro arbitrio tractandi, & ad quævis alia trahendi. Agit Propheta de uno Pasto- re, ejusq; percussione, quod Sole clarius constat. Et trahitur à Willio ad innumerorum Ecclesiæ mem- brorum percussionem & afflictionem. Propheta de Pastore vere magno, κατ’ ἐξοχὴν Pastore Domini di- cto, agit, & detorquetur ad mille alios, non dicam Pastores, sed cujuscunque fortis homines: v. c. ad Imperatoris Leonis Isaurici excommunicationem à Papa Gregorio II. factam, & Imperatorum, alio- rumque Sanctorum, qui Pontifici Romano resti- tere, persecutionem. Propheta de passione Christi magna vaticinatur, quam Pastor ille bonus pro nobis subiit. Willius id abripit ad passiones fidelium sub Pontificibus Romanis Gregorio II. & imprimis VII. ac sequentibus. Percussio autem hæc hujus Pastoris & viri proximi Deo per Anti-Chri- stum Romanum in effectum deducta, quando ipse thronum ejus occupavit, & Deo se æquans, potesta- tem sibi supra Ecclesiam & Principes Politicos arro- gavit universali jure, in Gregorio VII. ante Hilde- brando dicto ejusque successoribus, quoque tempore Sol Justitiæ Christus tenebris tertiam partem percus- sus est, unaque cum ipso Luna & stellæ Ecclesiarum Doctores.

Propheta dispersionem Apostolorum Christi tem- pore passionis ejus prædicit: Willius ad dispersio- nem & dissociationem Occident. & Orientalis Ecclesiæ, ut & particularium membrorum oppressionem & ex- ilium obtorto collo illa pertrahit, eumque sensum literalem esse vaticinii contendit. Propheta par- vulos dispersos vicissim collectum iri, interprete ipso Christo, cum Apostoli dispersi denuo congrega- buntur, pollicetur. Willius ex adverfo hanc esse propriam & germanam sententiam vaticinii asse- rit, quod Deus fideles in persequutione mulieris Jesabel defensurus, & gratia sua consolaturus sit, ac de ejus im- plemento ita tradit: Hæc autem conversio ad par- vulos facta, quando Deus reliquiis quibusdam ser- vatis, eas à tyrannide animarum eripuit, & pontifi- ciæ iniquitati, ceu testes veritatis, opposuit, quod Imperatorum & multorum piorum exempla testan- tur, inter quos Leo Isaurius, Constantinus Coprony- mus, Leo Armenius, Otho Magnus, Henricus III. & IV. Fridericus Barbarossa: inter Principes, Ber- tramus, Hincmarus, Berengarius; Sigebertus, Mo- nachus Gemblacensis, Otto Frisingensis, Waldenses, Thomas Bradwardinus, Johannes Wicklevius, Hussus, Hieronymus de Praga, Laurentius Valla inter Doctores eminent. Annon hoc est egregie Scripturam interpretari?

Non dissimulat VVillius, citari hoc testimo- nium Matth. 26, 31. ab ipso Christo, ceu vaticini- um de sua passione & Apostolorum dispersione subse- quuta, ac loco illius, quod reducturus vel conver- surus sit manum ad parvulos, promitti Apostolis à Christo, postquam autem suscitatus fuero, præibo vobis in Galilæam. Qua ergo fronte hæc de perse- quutione fidelium sub Anti- Christo Romano agere contendit, Christo palam & in os contradicens? Obvertit quidem Willius, locum Zachariæ ibi sal- tim κατ' ἀναλογίαν passioni Christi accommodari hoc sensu, quod primitiæ veritatis ibi prædictæ in mor- te & passione Christi ac dispersione Apostolorum se ma- nifestarint. Sed hoc est lusum aleatorium in dictis non tantum Propheticis, sed & Evangelicis illa in- terpretantibus exercere. Quid enim certius, quam quod Christus hæc de sui percussione in passione magna & Apostolorum dispersione agere in se & in Apostolis impleta, ac porro in Apostolorum con- gregatione implenda esse, testetur? Et quodnam obsecro, vel apud Prophetam, vel in tota Scriptu- ra reliqua vestigium, hæc implenda esse quoad li- teralem & proprium sensum in persequutione sub Anti- Christo? Unde docebitur, quod primitiæ veritatis istius solum in Christo & Apostolis imple- tæ sint, vere autem illa impleta fuerint in passione membrorum Christi & dissociatione Orientalis & Occidentalis Ecclesiæ ac testificatione testium ve- ritatis contra Anti-Christum Romanum? Calvi- nus cum Paræo in eo prudentius adhuc versatur, quod agnoscat in Christi Pastorum Principis passio- ne, de fuga & conversione discipulorum eo non quo- ad veritatis primitias, sed vere impleta: etsi con- tendant, ea de Pastorum ordine generaliter loqui: Hoc igitur, inquit Danæus, generale est, sed κατ'

ἐξοχὴν in Christo trucidato à Iudæis hoc MAXIME impletum est Matth. 26, 30. Nam in ista glossa a- liquis respectus adhuc observatur inter Christum Principem Pastorum, & Pastores alios gregarios sub Christo, itemque inter Pastorem percutien- dum, & gregem dispergendum, & vicissim congre- gandum: Sed in Williana detorsione respectus ille locum non habet. Nam percussum iri non Pasto- rum ordinem cum Calvino dicit, sed quosvis fideles: nec dispersum iri gregem sub Pastorum percussorum ordine, sed dissociandas Ecclesias Occidentales ab O- rientalibus: nec denique illos dispersos colligendos iterum esse; nunquam enim Orientalis Ecclesia Occidentali vicissim copulatur, sed repertum iri, qui se opponant Romano Pontifici. Quæ plane sunt ἀσύςατα.

Sed ad Grotium, qui in eo solum sanus est, quod agnoscat, pergere hic Prophetam narrare fu- tura: In reliquus ὐδὲν ὑγιὲς in ejus glossa. Pastor ipsi hoc in loco est Iudas Maccabæus, qui in præ- lio cum Bacchide interiit. Pastorem percutere jussus est Bacchides, oves dispersæ sunt Judæ exerci- tus fugitrivus, parvuli, ad quos conversa est manus Domini, sunt pauci, quos fecit Dominus sospites: & quæ porro ejus sunt affaniæ, gerris Siculis vanio- res. Cæterum Prophetam hic non de Juda Mac- cabæo agere, sed de Christo Servatore, multis do- ceri potest. Primo à temporis circumstantia. Non enim de tempore Maccabæorum, sed N. T. agi, quo Spiritus gratiæ & precum largissime effunden- dus, Christus in cruce transfigendus, Baptismi fons palam aperiendus, idolatria & dæmonum oracula passim destruenda, multi ex idololatris & falsis Pro- phetis ad Deum convertendi erant. Ad idem enim tempus refertur hæc Pastoris percussio, non diffi- tente Grotio. Deinde è συνεχεία superiorum Theodoretus: Postquam dixit: Adspicient ad me, quem compunxerunt, ne arbitrentur eum invitum salutarem passionem perpessum fuisse, docet, ut vo- luntate sua venerit & seipsum abjecerit, factus obe- diens usq́; ad mortem, mortem autem crucis; quare propheticus sermo divinam concessionem format & delineat, & frameam ostendit à Patre concessam. Quod ad immediate præcedentia, postquam falfo- rum Prophetarum & Pastorum, aut eversionem, aut conversionem prædixisset Zacharias, jam magnum illum Prophetam & Pastorem ovium divino percu- tiendum gladio sistit, sed longe alio eventu. Neque enim oves cum ipso perituræ, sed utut dispergen- tur in passione, congregandæ vicissim sunt ad eum in ipsius resurrectione. Postquam convertendos nonnullos è falsis Doctoribus docuisset, jam ipsos Apostolos Christum deserturos, ad Christum vi- cissim congregatum iri prænunciat, & conversis falsis Doctoribus ipsorum Apostolorum exemplum à desertione Christi revocandorum conjungit. De ratione cohærentiæ cum præcedentibus ita habet B. Dn. D. Winckelmannus: Ex abrupto Prophe- ta videtur vaticinari de Christi Passione & morte, cui fideles confirmantur, & cruce, sicuti aurum igne, probantur. Nec tamen prorsus ex abrupto in hanc de Christi passione prophetiam delabitur, sed conversis fidelibus ab errore Christum exemplum proponit, ut ne animo sint dejecto, propteram, quod pro suo merito corripiantur, quandoquidem ipse Christus Filius Dei nullo suo merito, sed innocens, propter nos percussus sit. Junius hic nobis ὁμόψηφος (quod in gratiam Calvini adjicimus) sic connectit: Ad hunc locum Propheta transit occupatione hoc mo- do: videbitur fortasse inanis esse tota superiorum bonorum promissio, quum Pastor meus Christus op- primendus vi, & percutiendus sit tam graviter, atque albi si Pseudopropheta esset: quo ex scandalo tam gravi- ter ipsæ oves, hoc est, discipulorum grex afficierur, ut momento uno diffugiant Matth. 26. Sed, inquit Deus, hoc saltem pii recordari debent, à me ante tot secula illud ipsum scandalum prædici atque imperari, ne, quum eveniet, ipsorum animi conturbentur, ut ipse Christus admonuit Matt. 26, 31. & Ioh. 14. & 16. & 18. Deinde vero hoc cogitandum est, me nullis vinculis distineri posse, quo minus in electis meis effi- ciam promissiones meas.

Tertio à Pastoris Domini simplici denomina- tione. Indigitatur ἁπλῶς Pastor Domini. Framea suscitare super PASTOREM MEUM. Quis hic cogitare posset Iudam Maccabæum, qui nunquam hoc nomine appellatus atque simpliciter Pastor vo- catus est. Messias autem ἀντονομαστικῶς Pastor di- citur, eoque nomine celebris est in Scripturis Psal. 23, 1. Ez. 34, 23. c. 37, 24. Ioh. 10, 11. Ebr. 13, 20. 1. Petr. 2, 25. c. 5, 4. Dicit PASTOREM MEUM, de- signans illum, quem ipse peculiariter elegit, ordi- navit, & constituit, non ad tempus aliquod vel ra- tione populi certi, sed qui semper est PASTOR JEHOVÆ & perpetuus gregis Domini Pastor, nullum habens ante se, nullum post se, cui munus hoc proprium est, & perpetuum. Ideo simplici- ter vocatur Pastor Domini. Uti Dominus nun- quam non habet oves suas, ita nunquam non ille præest pascendis ovibus, ideo etiam UNICUS PASTOR dicitur Pastor Domini Ez. 34, 23. cap. 37, 24. qui omnibus ubivis ovibus perpetuo pro- spicit, easdem pascit, ducit, defendit, fovet, ac æ- ternum salvat, nec eas ex manibus suis eripi per- mittit, imo pro iisdem animam suam ponit Joh. 10, 15. 28. de quo S. Bernhard. Christus redimit oves pre- tiosè, pascit lautè, ducit solicitè, collocat securè. Est enim, inquit Cyrillus, Princeps Pastor noster " Christus, & sub ipso sumus omnes, qui credimus: " veruntamen non extra manum Dei & Patris. Im- " perat enim nobis in Christo, perque ipsum & in " ipso salvati sumus, & per ipsum accessum obtinui- " mus. Proprius igitur Dei & Patris Pastor & Fi- " lius, non alienum gregem pascens, sed suum po- " tius & Patris, cum mercenarii pastores non esse " ejus proprii intelligantur, qui contra omnem mi- " sericordiam oves mactabant.

Quarto à Pastoris hujus cum superiori colla- tione. Hunc vocat Dominus Pastorem suum, priores ceu falsos Prophetas reprobrans v. 2. Quum ergo Pseudoprophetis opponatur Pastor Domini, manifestum est, per Pastorem hunc non intelligi Principem Politicum, Iudam Maccabæum, sed Epi- scopum animarum nostrarum, Principem Pastorum Christum Iesum 1. Petr. 2, 25. c. 5, 4. Deus & Pa- " ter, inquit Cyrillus, proprium Filium suum pro " nobis tradidit, dispensatoriè sinens quamvis De- " um & ex se naturaliter inexplicabili modo gene- " ratum, & in forma servi venire, & hominem nobis " similem fieri, & crucem sustinere, ut mundo sa- " lutem restitueret, & Satanæ in omnes dominatum " erueret, & impuram idololatriam everteret & " vaticinationem, Pseudoprophetias & imposturas " ex suo cujusque corde profectas aboleret, aufer- " ret item Spiritum immundum de terra, & mun- " dum præterea constitueret, formaretque, sedu- " ctos ad divinitatis agnitionem transferens, eosq; " ad pias & honestas vitæ rationes, & ad opinionem " omnigenæ virtutis de se præbendam impellens.

Quinto è superiori hujus Pastoris commemo- ratione. Egerat enim Zacharias jam c. 11, 6. de Pastore, quem infidis pastoribus opposuerat & qui vendendus erat pretio XXX. argenteorum. De quo proinde hic porro : Framea suscitare super

Pastorem meum. Non enim est, quod alium intel- ligamus, quam quem Propheta ipse designavit, aut aliunde accersamus Pastorem Domini, quum ab ipso Propheta introductus ibi sit Pastor ille bonus, qui pauperes gregis pascere, & duas virgas eo fine assu- mere debebat, etsi pro mercede reportaturus vendi- tionem & traditionem scelestam. Quæ uti in Chri- sti passione complementum suum habuere, ita hic de eodem Pastore Christo, gladio percutiendo, sermonem itidem esse, dubitandum non est.

Sexto a Pastoris hujus descriptione. Vocat enim Deus VIRUM COHÆRENTEM SIBI, ut Vulgata habet: In Ebræo est: ועל־גבר עמיתי: super virum proximum meum, qua phrasi, notan- te B. Glassio, alter idem, imago Dei invisibilis, character hypostaseos Patris, & splendor gloriæ ejus exprimitur Ebr. 1, 3. Et quis, inquit idem in Ono- matolog. Mess. p. 282. Patri in cælis propinquior & conjunctior est, quam Filius, qui est in sinu Patris? Huc pertinet locus Es. 44, 24. Ego Dominus fa- ciens omnia, extendens cælos solus, formans ter- ram מאתי ab (illo, qui est) mecum, quod Jonathan Chaldæus ita transtulit: Ego Deus faciens omnia, extendi cælos VERBO MEO. Coccejus de eo ita habet: Quasi dicat, virum, qui est par mihi. „ Nam τὸ עמת & לעמת significat contrapositio- „ nem in æquali situ, dispositione, forma, magnitu- „ dine, jure; ut in ducendis fortibus, ut 1. Chron. 25, „ 8. Hinc quando homini jungitur עמיתו proximus „ ejus, notatur אנוש כערכו )ut imitemur phrasin „ Psalmi 55, 14.) Vir ejusdem naturæ particeps. „ Quicquid sit, nihil exilius significare potest hæc „ vox, Vir proximus meus, Dei verbis prolata, „ quam qui apud me est, & à me divelli non potest. „ Sed τὸ עמית inter homines non est significativum „ amoris aut conjunctionis quoad locum, sed com- „ munionis naturæ. Sit igitur vir proximus Dei, „ qui est unum cum Patre, apud Deum, quem dili- „ git Pater, ut quærat gloriam ejus, & propterea „ ut ipsius gloriam manifestet, dedit omnia „ in manum ejus, ut quemadmodum ab æ- „ terno voluit, & postulavit, ita & populum sibi „ datum sanctificet sanguine & spiritu suo, omnia „ subjiciat Deo & sibi, & eo fine tandem in gloria „ Patris ἶσα Θεῷ comparens suos vivificet, mun- „ dum damnet. Vir proximus meus, quum prius „ sit denominatio à natura humana, secundum „ quam & gladius eum percutit, posterius à divina „ majestate est communicatio idiomatum, ut Filius „ hominis, qui est in cælo Joh. 3, 13. Quam empha- sin notat quoque B. Tarnovius vocem גבר ad hu- manam referens naturam Jer. 31, 22. vocem עמתי ad Divinam, quæ notet stricte & proprie non quemvis proximũ, qui dicitur קרוב vel חבר רע, sed intimum, qui è regione in conspectu alicujus aut circa eum semper est, cum qua voce similem phrasin de intima familiaritate, quæ potest esse in- ter homines, usurpatam Gen. 2, 18. כנגדו confert. Fateri hoc etiam debuit Willius, atque in eo sese Calvino suo opponere, Christum hac περιφράσει denotari. Qua ergo temeritate ad fideles Christi eo- rumque afflictiones abripuit, quod de passione Christi agere dissiteri non potuit? Rationem, in- quit, nominis quidam reddunt, quod Deus Christum sibi associaverit ad pascendas oves, atq; eodem modo de aliis Doctoribus hæc explicant, quos Deum hoc nomine insignire volunt, qui idem cum ipso munus subeant & curam ejus repræsentent. Sed rectius hæc ad Christum ipsum applicari mihi dubium non est propter Evangelistæ Matthæi disertum testimonium cap. 26, 31. Nominatur autem ita Christus, quia in divina essentia Patri honore & dignitate par est, & ceu ἀντίπατρος ex adverso ejus in conspectu rerum ge- creatarum. Pulcherrime Junius : Hoc nomine Deus Pater honorifice compellat Christum, quia Christus est alter idem, imago Dei invisibilis, cha- racter hypostaseos Patris, & splendor gloriae illius, ex adverso micans in conspectu rerum creatarum o- mnium. Hebraea vox proximum ac amicum sonat, qui stat è regione alterius &c. Haec persona illa est, & Pastor, contra quem gladius excitatur. Recte e- tiam notat B. Gerhardus noster in Harm. Pass. c. 1. p. 7. exprimi hic simul causam, propter quam per- cussio Christi facta à Patre coelesti in redemtionem nostram & plenariam pro peccatis satisfactionem cedat, nimirum, quia est vir Deo proximus & a- qualis, h. e. verus cum Patre Deus, quia in societa- tem illam majestatis coelestis neminem admittit, nisi sit ejusdem cum ipso essentiae Es. 42, 8. sed hic Pastor, quem Pater coelestis gladio percutit, est non solum vir, hoc est verus homo, sed etiam Pa- tris coelestis socius, ipsiq́; proximus, est in sinu Patris Joh. 1, 18. est in Patre Joh. 14, 10. imo unum cum Patre Joh. 10, 30. inde atque ideo propter pecca- ta nostra à Patre coelesti percussus ab aeternis pla- gis nos liberavit. Eodem etiam respicit vox Pasto- rus, quod sc. Christus sit verus ille, ac summus ani- marum Pastor, qui posuit animam suam pro ovibus suis, ac pro grege mori dignatus est Joh. 10, 5.

Septimo à gladii excitatione. Non excitat Deus Bacchidis gladium, ut percutiat Judam. Ine- ptum hoc. Non excitat gladium Anti-Christi ad percutiendum fideles, uti Willius nugatur. Sed do- cetur hac excitatione consilium Dei in redemtione generis humani, cujus gratia gladium excitare, at- que eodem sibi proximum percutere voluit Jeho- vah, uti Act. 2, 23. dicitur Christus τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βϰ- λῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ Θεοῦ traditus, & Es. 53. à Deo plagis percussus & humiliatus, ac vulneratus propter praevaricationes nostras. Hieronymus in lib. de opt. Interpret. genere ad Pammach. haec verba Prophe- tae esse putat ad Patrem coelestem directa, qui po- stulat Christi passionem, dicens percute Pastorem; sed è contextu liquet, Patrem ipsum coelestem allo- qui gladium, ut sese suscitet, & Pastorem percutiat. Quo gladii nomine metaphorice intelliguntur o- mnes afflictiones, quas Christus & corpore & ani- ma sustinuit, vel judicii divini instrumenta omnia, uti gladii vindicis Dei fit mentio Es. 27, 1. c. 34, 5. Jer. 12, 52. Ez. 21, 8. & Luc. 2, 35. habetur : Tuam ipsius animam pertransibit gladius : Cyrillus, con- surge super Pastorem meum, & super virum civem ejus (πολίτην αὐτοῦ, sic reddidere LXX.) Rhamphae- am hoc loco, ὡς ἐν εἴδει, ut in specie, gladii tentatio- nem significare dicimus, aut ipsos quoque cruciatus ex Judaeorum vecordia Emanueli adhibitos. Ait er- go, ô Romphaea surge, h. e. procedat deinceps salu- taris passio, & veniat tempus, quo se boni ostendant. Neque temere observatum à Gerhardo l. c. remit- tere nos vocabulum gladii ad historiam Gen. 22, 6. 10. ut enim Abraham ibidem extendit gladium suum in Isaacum, sic Pater coelestis evaginato quasi gladio adoritur in passione dilectum suum Filium propter peccata mundi, quae in se susceperat, in ara crucis immolandum.

Octavo à gregis dispersione : Percute Pasto- rem, & dispergentur oves. Ut Pastor, ita oves e- tiam intelliguntur, non de Duce belli & exercitu, sed de Pastore animarum & ovibus ejus, nec de fi- nali dispersione ovium sermo est, in qua pereunt, vel separatae manent à Pastore suo, sed de tali sepa- ratione, è qua iterum ipsae congregandae sunt, & ad Pastorem suum revocandae. Pastor solus percutitur, non oves. Nam hae solum dispergendae, non vero gladio percutiendae in hac quidem poena sunt. Quae dispersioni discipulorum Christi conveniant, ubi solus Pastor percutiebatur gladio, ipsi vero disci- puli intacti servabantur salvo conductoChristi mu- niti Joh. 18, 8. Inepte autem hæc ad dispersionem exercitus Judæ trahuntur. Nam nec solus Judas percussus est, sed multi etiam de exercitu ejus, nec qui dispersi sunt, iterum ad Judam congregati sunt, utpote qui in bello periit.

Nono à manus Domini ad parvulos conversione. Per hoc enim non denotantur alii, quam qui per- cusso Pastore dispersi erant: quorum solatio hoc dicitur, quod Dominus iterum ad eos manum gratiæ convertere velit, ne in dispersione illa pere- ant. Non ergo per parvulos intelligi possunt illi, qui aliis casis superabant post cladem Judæ, LXX. In- terp. intelligunt Principes Judæorum; unde Cyril- lus explicat de conversione manus vindicis ad eos- dem, non manus gratiæ congregatricis. Sed indigi- tantur disperse oves, quæ iterum congregandæ: Ideo rectius Hieronymus: Postquam Pastor bonus, qui animam suam posuit pro ovibus suis, qui locutus ad Patrem est: Quem tu percuslisti, ipsi persecuti sunt, & super dolorem vulnerum meorum adjicie- bant: Patris voluntate percussus est: & vir cohæ- rens Deo, qui ait: Ego in Patre & Pater in me: pe- pendit in patibulo, & dixit: Pater in manus tuas commendo spiritum meum: statim dispersæ sunt oves, omnis in Christo multitudo credentium. Con- vertitque Dominus manum suam, ut in LXX. legi- mus, ad Pastores, quos multi male JudæorumPrin- cipes intelligunt: Vt autem in Hebræo scriptum est, ad parvulos, quibus Dominus dixerat in Evangelio: Ne timeas grex parvule. Et in Esaia: Ecce ego & pueri sive parvuli, quos mihi dedit Deus. Quapro- pter sensum probe expressit B. Tarnovius ita red- „ dens: Verum enim vero, cum Christus Pastor ita „ percutitur, & oves disperguntur, anne jam de Ec „ clesia actum erit, & omnes promissiones hacte „ nus factæ irritæ? non ita, quin statim paulo post „ resurrectionem reducam manum meam, quam „ paulisper sibi ipsos relinquens subduxeram ad „ parvulos, videlicet Apostolos eorumque simi- „ les, quos congregabo & congregatos conserva- „ bo, sicut etiam evenisse legitur Matth. 28. Marc. 16. Luc. 24. Joh. 20. & 21. Act. 2. cap. Quam e- tiam sententiam Prophetæ è Reformatis agnovit Franc. Iunius l. 1. Parall. XLVII. Finis hujus loci a pud Prophetam fuit plane idem, quem etiam Iere- miæ fuisse propositum (c. XXXI.) in Parall. VII. do- cuimus, nempe ut certo aliquo insigni & luculento signo publice demonstraretur Iesum Christum eum Pastorem esse, qui in ipso perpessionum suarum cer- tamine oves suas dispersas curavit, quas postea in u- num ovile manu sua erat reducturus. Itaque sum- ma est, quum prope fuit, ut Christus pateretur, ipsum à Deo Patre percussum esse, & traditum in manus inimicorum: discipulos vero & comites i- psius singulos gravitate ferulæ istius offensos, huc illuc abivisse tanquam errantes oviculas: sed ipsos à Christo Servatore nostro, cum perpessionis illius tempore conservatos esse, tum vero, postquam re- surrexerit, curatos & reductos ipsius manu, quem- admodum Propheta prædixerat. Alii de Apostolo- rum afflictionibus hæc interpretantur, q. d. ipsos e- tiam afflictionibus exercebo. Sed prior sensus con- venientior est. Plane autem pervertit hæc Grotius: Et convertam manum meam ad parvulos: id est, paucos faciam sospites. Aliud enim est hospitare aliquos in cæde publica reliquis intereuntibus, aliud vero ad eos, qui sotspites sunt post Pastoris unius percussionem, manum convertere.

Decimo ex addita de Ecclesia N. T. promissione. ET ERUNT, dicit Dominus, IN TERRA

PARTES DUÆ, IN EA DISPERGENTUR ET DEFICIENT, ET TERTIA PARS RE- LINQVETUR IN EA. In Ebræo est, Et erit in omni terra. Quod prædicitur, non concernit jam paucos, nec solum terram Judaicam, sed OMNEM TERRAM. Grotius perquam inepte ac perverse hoc trahit ad clades, quas Bacchides non isto tantum prælio, quo Judas interiit, sed & aliis antecedentibus intulerat Judæis. At non loquitur Propheta de ante- cedentibus, sed consequentibus percussionem Pasto- ris, & quidem per universam terram. De populo sc. universo hujus Pastoris per orbem post ejusdem passionem & reductionem Apostolorum, quod etsi universa terra ipsius morte redemta, in univer- sam terram emittendi Apostoli sint, ut redemtione Pastoris hujus fruantur, & cibo animæ sub eo pa- scantur, duæ terræ partes sint dispergendæ & defectu- ræ, & vix tertia pars reliqua futura sit. Duas illas par- tes de Judæis & gentibus quæ persistunt in suo erro- re, tertiam de Christianis intelligit Hieronymus con- versis ad animarum Pastorem; Et duæ partes factæ sunt in omni terra Judæorum atque gentium, qui pari- ter perierunt & defecerunt, pereuntibus Judæis & gentilibus, tertia in orbe pars, h. e. tertius Christiano- rum populus repente succrevit. De tertia parte Ju- dæorum servata pereuntibus reliquis Cyrillus exponit, ut & Fr. Junius: Sed prior explicatio convenientior est: quia de tota terra, non de Judæorum solum terra, & de interitu non temporali, sed æterno agi- tur. Quo facit supputatio illa Edwardi Brerewodi in Linguar. ac Religionum investigat. c. XIV. quod orbe universo, qua cognitus est, in 30. æquales distributo partes, vix quinque portiones Christia- ni possideant, Mahumedanis sex portiones, Ido- lolatris paganis 19. obtinentibus, Judæis vero mul- tis myriadibus per orbem universum dispersis; qui status modernus si comparetur cum veteri Aposto- lorum ætate, utpote feliciori, quid mirum, si vix tertia orbis pars Christianorum cœtus fuerit, ut- ut Apostoli omni creaturæ sub cœlo Christum an- nunciarint, ubi hodie ne quidem sexta orbis co- gniti portio Christiani nominis decore splendeat? B. Lutherus non inconcinne duas partes intelligit de iis, qui deficiunt vel cruce & persequtionibus, vel ab hæreticis & impostoribus seducti: tertiam de cœtu fidelium, qui in ipsa cruce fidem Christi reti- nent constanter, atque, velut aurum, igne, proban- tur. Quem sensum etiam amplectitur Winckelman- nus. Balt. Willius, per somnium puto febrile, vidit hic in duabus partibus exscindendis copiosissimam martyrum mactationem tempore Waldensium & Hussitarum, & cum reliquis instaurationem fœde- ris in initio Sardensis Ecclesiæ. Sed mittimus somnia ista. Opponitur enim tertia pars, ceu cœtus fidelium duabus ceu infidelibus. De illa itaque tertia parte vel cœtu fidelium pargit Dominus: ET DUCAM TERTIAM PARTEM PER IGNEM, ET U- RAM EOS, SICUT URITUR ARGENTUM, ET PROBABO EOS, SICUT PROBATUR AURUM. Quæ recte quidem exponit Grotius, per multa mala eorum explorabo constantiam, sed perperam ad populum reliquum de Bacchidis cladibus trahit. Agunt enim de fidelibus N. T. i- gne crucis probandis 1. Petr. 1, 7. quorum hæc est descriptio: Ipse (populus ille) vocabit (invocabit) nomen meum; hoc enim proprium est populi Do- mini, servari per nomen Domini, illudque in vera fide invocare, Joel. 2. Rom. 9. & ego exaudiam eum Psalm. 50, 15. Psalm. 91, 15. Joh. 16. Dicam, populus meus es tu, & ipse dicet, Dominus Deus meus, quo summa fidelium cum Deo per fidem com- munio, ac fœderis & despontationis spiritualis te- nor exprimitur Joh. 2, 19. conf. Joh. 20, 28. Recte- Hieronymus: Ipsa quoque tertia pars ne delicata effet, & secura confessione, quasi argentum & au- rum per ignem probatur. Cum sic probati fue- rint parvuli, super quos Dominus convertit ma- num suam, & per vocationem eorum omnis nationum turba crediderit, tunc credentium populus vocabit Christum, nomine suo: & illo dicente: Tu es po- pulus meus; Populus respondebit: Dominus Deus meus tu es.

His undecimo accedit interpretatio in N. T. tradita, siquidem ipse Christus hoc vaticinium ex plicet (1) non de alio Pastore, quam semetipso, non de Juda Maccabæo, Duce bellico, sed de se redemptore nostro. (2) non de clade in prælio, sed de percussione in passione, quæ tum ipsi immine- bat. (3) non de exercitu cadendo, sed de Pastoris unius cæde. (4) non de clade ac dissipatione mi- litum bellicosorum, vel exercitus militaris, sed de dispersione ovium, discipulorum meticulosorum, & scandalo è passione Christi accepto. (5) Non de finali interitu, aut dissipatione, sed de tali dispersio- ne, è qua iterum oves dispersæ congregandæ sint post Christi resurrectionem. Tunc dixit illis (discipulis) Jesus, inquit Matth. c. 26, 31. Omnes vos scandalum patiemini in me ista nocte. SCRIPTUM est enim: Percutiam Pastorem & dispergentur oves gregis. Postquam autem resurrexero, præcedam vos in Ga- lilæam, ut sc. vos iterum congregem. Sic etiam Mar- cus habet cap. 14, 27. Et ait eis Jesus, omnes scan- dalizabimini in me in nocte ista, quia scriptum est: Percutiam Pastorem & dispergentur oves, sed post- quam resurrexero, præcedam vos in Galilæam. Con- feratur v. 50. 51. 52. Quum itaque tam luculentam habeamus vaticinii integri explicationem, à Chri- sto ipsomet traditam, ecquis non mirabitur, Gro- tium & Calvinum in sensum plane alium illud acci- pere ausos fuisse? Miratur certe Hieronymus de nonnullis, qui suo tempore idem conati fuere. Mi- ,, ror quosdam hanc Prophetiam, quam Evange- ,, lista Matthæus retulit ad Dominum Salvatorem, ,, postquam in passione ejus fugere discipuli, & ,, tunc eam dicit esse completam, allegoricis inter- ,, pretationibus velle tenuare: & dum plus cupi- ,, unt videri nosse, quam cæteri, veritatis regulam ,, non tenere. Refert enim Evangelista Matthæus: Tunc dicit illis Jesus, omnes vos scandalum patie- mini in me in ista nocte. Scriptum est enim: Per- cutiam Pastorem & dispergentur oves gregis. Et iterum: Hoc autem totum factum est, ut imple- rentur Scripturæ Prophetarum. Tunc discipuli omnes relicto eo fugerunt. Hæc Hieronymus. At Grotius ne nullum quidem mentionem explica- tionis Christi hoc loco fecit non quod ea in men- tem ipsi venire non potuerit, sed quod eandem sus- que deque fecerit, quod in plerisque aliis vaticiniis hactenus pariter observavimus. Ad Judam Mac- cabæum detorsit omnia, de quo ne Jota quidem ullum in toto vaticinio.

Cæterum, cum in Annotatis ad Matthæum hanc Christi explicationem præterire non potue- rit, eo progressus est temeritatis, atque impuden- tiæ, ut negarit, quod hactenus, quantum constat, a nemine negatum fuit, Christum ibi respexisse vel al- legasse vaticinum Zachariæ, ac commentus sit, pro- verbium tantum quoddam adhibuisse Christum, non adduxisse vaticinium Propheticum. Quod ta- men non ausus est pro certo affirmare. VIDE- TUR, inquit, hoc dicto proverbii in modum uti Chri- stus, ut sensus sit: fiet, quod dici solet quodque ali- cubi scriptum meministis: Pastore percusso oves disperguntur. Sed ubi scriptum tale prover- bium sit, Polyhistor dicere non habuit. Et an- non ex verbis Christi satis liquet, SCRIPTU- RAM indigitari Propheticam, quam IMPLERI oportebat, quia omnia, quæ de ipsius passione scripta erant, impleri in ipso debuere, quod to- ties professus erat Christus, cujus gratia etiam sem- per ipse, aut amanuenses ejus Evangelistæ ad Scri- pturam, nempe non aliam quamcunque, sed Pro- pheticam, ac Divinam provocarunt, ut omnia de- finito Dei consilio & secundum scripturam eve- nisse docerent. Neque, credo, admittet facile quis, aut æquo animo feret hanc impiam temerita- tem, Christum hic non divinam, sed prophanam aliquam Scripturam, in qua forte tale proverbium habeatur (licet nec eam invenire potuerit librorum Helluo Grotius) respexisse. Si non dixisset Chri- stus, SCRIPTUM EST, sed DICTUM EST, fortassis commento illi aliquis locus esset; nam id ad dicteria & proverbia forsam rapi potuisset. At, quum ad Scripturam provocet Christus, & adji- ciet insuper, hoc totum factum esse, ut impleren- tur Scripturæ PROPHETARUM, ecquis dubi- tandi locus superesse potest, Scripturam Divi- nam & Propheticam ab ipso indigitatam esse? Sed quasnam, obsecro, adversus hanc rei evidentiam conjecturas habuit hujus proverbialis dictionis Grotius? Dicit, Christum imperativum modum in indicativum mutasse, quia proverbiali locutioni magis id congruebat. Atqui IMPERATIVUS habetur apud Zachariam: PERCUTE Pasto- rem; si ergo hunc Zachariæ imperativum in in- dicativum PERCUTIAM mutavit Christus, uti- que Zachariæ locum Christus in animo habuit, non aliam (nescio quam, nescivit & Grotius) Scripturam. Addit: neque illud πατάξω certam personam designat, sed prima persona pro quavis po- nitur, nec aliud est πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, quam πα- τάσσεται ὁ ποιμὴν. Id vero falsum est, non defi- gnari certam personam; nam respicitur Deus Pa- ter, qui excitavit gladium, eoque percussit Pasto- rem. Quod ab Hieronymo discere poterat Gro- tius, ni collatio cum Propheta id eundem docuis- set, quæ satis luculenta est: Nec putandum est de altero loco assumptum testimonium: quia in Evan- gelio Deus à se dicit Pastorem esse percussum, & in præsenti loco gladio & mucroni legimus, impera- tum: Percute Pastorem, & dispergentur oves. Hic gladius & hæc romphæa est, & framea: de qua in vicesimo primo Psalmo Dominus loquitur ad Patrem: Erue à framea animam meam, & de manu canis unicam meam. Illud vero, inquit B. Tarnovius, neminem turbare debet, quod quando apud Prophetam est in imperativo הַךְ percute, si- cut etiam Græce versum olim πάταξον, oratione di- recta ad gladium, apud Evangelistam sit futurum πατάξω percutiam, in prima etiam persona, quasi Deus ipse percuteret. Cum enim gladius iste non nisi Dei jussu Christum percutiat, merito hoc ad ipsum, ut causam principalem, refertur, & alias sæpe imperativus apud Hebræos pro futuro ponitur. Genef. 20, 7. Deut. 32, 50. Proverb. 3, 4. & 4, 4. & 20, 13. Psalm. 37, 28. quemadmodum etiam constat ex collatione loci Esa. 6, 9. ubi Impera- tivus שִׁמְעוּ, & allegatione ejusdem Matth. 13, 14. Act. 28, 26. ubi futurum ἀκούσετε: quibus adjunge, quæ dicta sunt ad Amos 5, 25. 26. 27. de generali conciliatione dictorum Scripturæ, quæ aliter, quam extant allegari in N. T. viden- tur. Agnovit id quoque Franc. Junius, at- que idcirco palam Præceptori suo Calvino hic contradixit in Parallel. XLVII. Mutatio in verbis aliqua videtur esse, res tamen unica est.

Nam pro eo, quod Zacharias verbis Dei compellat gladium, dicens, evigila gladie, percute &c. Chri- stus omissa locutione illa figurata, rem propriis ver- bis & simplicibus enunciat, percutiat Pastorem &c. nimirum gladio, qui officium hoc in mandatis à Deo habuit, ut à Zacharia figuratur. Quæ cum ita sint, omnino illum locum de Christo accipi necesse est, quemadmodum sanctissime Christus de seipso inter- pretatus est non analogica accommodatione, sed hi- storica & necessaria interpretatione. Etiam Willius, utut suis de cætero hic indulserit speculationibus, quam maxime alienis, DISERTUM esse testimo- nium Matthæi, ac propterea illud sibi DUBIUM NON ESSE, hoc vaticinium ad Christum applicari fassus est.

Sed ut appareat, quomodo Spiritu vertiginis agitatus fuerit hic, non interpres, sed corruptor Scripturæ (Grotium indigitamus) quem locum de Juda Maccabæo, Pastore ac Duce non malo, sed multis meritis insigni exposuit in nostro Propheta, eundem in Annotatis ad Matthæum inficiatus est de bono Pastore agere, ac detorsit ad malum Pasto- rem, de quo cap. 11. egerat Propheta, qui locus à nostro toto cœlo distat, uti inspicienti luculentissi- mum est. Tantum autem abest, inquit, ut Za- chariæ directè verbis Christum putem respici, ut multo magis credam agi inibi de aliquo non bono Pastore, & quidam ni fallor, (in quo quidem vehe- menter fallebaris Groti, consentibus omnibus In- terpp.) de eodem, de quo actum erat in fine cap. 11. ubi itidem ille, quisquis est, vocatur Pastor meus (id vero falsum, Pastorem idolum vel nihili Deum vocare Pastorem SVVM) & gladius illi imminere dicitur. Quis vero tandem directè respicitur à Propheta, si Christus non respicitur directè? Nemo nominari potest. Non Judas Maccabæus; hunc enim Pastorem non bonum, Pastorem idolum & nihili haud dixisset Grotius. Quis ergo ille non bonus Pastor? Et, quomodo Pastorem non bonum diceret Deus Pastorem suum, quomodo vocaret virum sibi proximum? Quod ipse Grotius, aper- te secum pugnans, interpretatus est, quem maxime amo: addita hac observatione: Quoties viri BO- NI morte violenta perierunt, toties apud pios crevit fides resurrectionis, (Num Pastori malo, quem Manassem hominem vanum & prophanum ipse di- xit, cujus oculus dexter obscurandus divino judi- cio erat, h. e. juxta ipsius interpretationem, qui co- gnitione rerum divinarum privandus erat, glorio- sam resurrectionem tribuemus?) fuitque hæc œco- nomia à legali differens (hæc Socinismum sapiunt, & Pelagianorum, imo Sadducæorum delirium, quod in lege vel V. T. non fuerit tradita fides resur- rectionis: quod novo errore cumulat, ac si legis promissa quoad felicitatem temporalem, simpliciter accipienda sint, nec exceptionem crucis admittant) præparatio ad Evangelium. Sed admittit tandem Grotius Zachariæ locum hic indigitatum, etsi neget verbis Zachariæ Christum directè respici. Ad- huc vult proverbialem gnomam esse, quæ apud Matthæum habetur, eumque in finem & Virgilium allegat, & Livium atque Homerum, ut ab his e- gregiis Scripturæ Interpretibus mentem Scripturæ addiscamus. Certe, inquit, quæ in Historiis posita νοήματα sunt, extra Historias posita γνῶμαι fiunt, neque tam respicitur, quæ occasione primitus sint di- cta, sed quam late se vis γνώμης porrigat. Simile est illud Virgilii de Apibus:

Rege incolumi, mens omnibus una. Amisso rupere fidem.

& Livii: Sicut acies funditur duce occiso, ita di- lapsi passim alii alio. Homerus circa Sarpedonis mortem dixerat: ἀλλ’ ἐφύθηθεν Πάντες, ἐπεὶ βασιλεῖα ἴδον βεβλαμμένον ἦτορ Κείμενον ἐν νεκρῶν ἀγόρει. At, quid hæc νοήματα Historica ad vaticinium Pro- pheticum, quod quomodo impletum sit, Christus docuit. Toto hæc differunt cœlo, vaticinii Pro- phetici complementum ostendere, & ad se applica- re, & νόημα historicum, tanquam gnomam ali- quam, usurpare. Mittimus autem tandem assanias istas, imo impios adversus Christum coccysmos, Juliano aliquo empecta magis, quam interprete Christiano dignos. Omnes ubique interpretes Christiani de Christo vaticinium intelligunt, quod etsi Calvinus ad alios etiam rapiat, de Christo tamen præcipue agere, itidem fassus est: in quo tamen i- psam fugit ratio, cum non possit idem dictum & de Christo UNICO PASTORE agere, & de Pastoribus generatim, neque secundario alii intel- ligi queant, ubi non nisi de uno Pastore vaticina- tur Propheta, quantum ad literalem ejusdem sen- sum, quem oportet unicum esse, ac certo sibi con- stare: unde etiam ab ipsis discipulis suis hic refuta- tum esse Calvinum, observavimus; quibus Para- phrastæ Belgici adjiciendi, utpote qui unice de Christo, Filio Dei ejusdem essentiæ cum Patre, hanc percussionem intelligunt, & de Apostolorum dispersioné tempore passionis Christi. Quid? quod Judæi ipsi agnoverint, hæc de Messia agere? Sic enim R. Aben Ezra: Prophetat adhuc de bellis multis, quæ erunt in universa terra tempore Messiæ, Filii Joseph. Quod etiam de Judæis observavit S. Hie- ronymus in h. l. Judæi hæc ad Christum referunt, & in ultimo tempore futura contendant. Sed hoc in- ter nos & illos est, quod nos expleta jam dicimus, illi explenda commemorant.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. A prophecy concerning the ascension of Christ into heaven and his kingdom, and especially the confluence of the nations to his worship.

The final plundering of Jerusalem and the captivity of the people are foretold, and the Lord's victory for the Church: His ascension into heaven, and the preaching of the Apostles throughout the whole world, and the universal kingdom of the Lord, who will rule throughout the entire spiritual Jerusalem, with all who oppose him being afflicted by a most grievous plague and the remnants of the enemies being saved, and about to celebrate the solemn feasts of the Lord; the others being entirely deprived of divine blessing, so that in this way all vessels may be consecrated to the Lord, and no Canaanite be found in the house of the Lord.

The city will be taken, there will be one King in all the world

Vers. 1. AND YOUR SPOILS WILL BE DIVIDED IN YOUR MIDST.) In Judea itself, spoils taken from the Jews will be divided here and there by the Greeks.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Vaticinium de ascensu Christi in cœlum & regno ejus, ac confluxu imprimis gentium ad cultum ejus.

Prædicatur novissima direptio Hierosolymæ & captivitas populi, Dominique pro Ecclesia victoria: Ejus ascensus in cœlum, & prædi- catio Apostolorum per totum orbem, re- gnumque Domini universale, qui per totam Hierosolymam spiritualem dominabitur, o- mnibus ei se opponentibus plaga gravissima afficiendis & reliquiis ex hostibus servan- dis, & Domini festa solennia celebratu- ris; cæteris benedictione divina prorsus carituris, ut ita omnia vasa Domino con- secrentur, nec ullus Cananæus in domo Domini reperiatur.

Urbs capietur, erit toto Rex unus in orbe

Vers. 1. ET DIVIDENTUR SPOLIA TUA IN MEDIO TUI.) In ipsa Judæa passim à Græcis spolia dividentur capta de Judæis.

## 14:2
Vers. 2. AND I WILL GATHER ALL NATIONS TO JERUSALEM FOR BATTLE.) One hundred thousand foot soldiers, twenty thousand horsemen, thirty-two elephants under Antiochus Eupator. Written in 1 Maccab. 6, 28. concerning this time: καὶ ἀπὸ βασιλέων ἑτέρων, καὶ ἀπὸ νήσων θαλασσῶν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν δυνάμεις μισθωταί.

AND THE CITY SHALL BE TAKEN,) The Jews were forced to retreat into the temple Jos. 12, 14. it is not a great retreat, so that the diminution made in the people may be the better understood,

AND THE HOUSES SHALL BE PLUNDERED, AND THE WOMEN SHALL BE RAVISHED,) As had also been done before at the arrival of Antiochus Epiphanes.

AND HALF OF THE CITY SHALL GO FORTH INTO CAPTIVITY.) Because of famine they will surrender. Josephus, πολλοὶ τοιγαρῦν τῶν πολιορκωμένων ἐπεδίδρασκον διὰ τὴν τῶν ἀναγκαίων ἀπορίαν.

AND THE RESIDUE OF THE PEOPLE SHALL NOT BE CUT OFF FROM THE CITY.) They will defend the Temple.

A threefold explanation of this chapter occurs primarily. The first is that all these things are yet to be fulfilled, which is asserted again by a fivefold reason. First, the Jews say these things are to be fulfilled at the time of the coming of the Messiah, whom they expect, and indeed according to the literal meaning; but since the Messiah ought to have come while the temple was still standing, and before the scepter was taken away from Judah and the lawgiver from between his feet, which things, along with other characteristics, have already had their fulfillment 16 centuries ago, the perfidious race of the Jews expects the Messiah in vain. Nor does the literal sense have any place; for how will the city of Jerusalem take all the nations of the earth? How would all the pots in Jerusalem and Judah be consecrated to the Lord? For thus they would have none at their own homes for their own uses. These and other things teach that the literal sense cannot be retained, but that these things must be understood figuratively.

Furthermore, secondly, the Chiliasts, although they acknowledge that Christ has come, likewise dream of the fulfillment of these things according to the letter, whence Jerome joins them with the Jews in this passage: The Jews dream according to the letter, and our Chiliasts, who desire to hear again, 'increase and multiply, replenish the earth,' and for the continence of this life, and a short fast, they promise themselves bulbs and wombs and birds of Phasis and the attagen, by no means Ionic but Judaic.

From whom, thirdly, the more recent Chiliasts differ in this indeed, that they do not promise themselves such worldly things, yet they hope for the kingdom of Christ for a thousand years on these lands, and seek it also in this place, concerning which see Alstedius, treatise on the thousand years of the Apocalypse.

Fourthly, others, according to Calvin in this place, refer these to the times of the Anti-Christ, signifying here a future devastation of the Church by the Anti-Christ, whom some Papists say the Jews are to receive as their own Messiah. Who is to place the throne of his tyranny at Jerusalem towards the end of the world. That this sense is by no means literal, according to Lyranus and Dionysius, Cornelius à Lapide proves from the fact that if these things were to happen at the end of the world, those things which are said concerning the restoration and celebrity of Jerusalem—that all nations shall come to it every year to celebrate the feast of tabernacles—could not be understood literally. Thus, therefore, he understands it anagogically concerning the celebration of that feast in heaven. But the things that Papists trifle about concerning an Anti-Christ still to come at the end of the world are mere fables.

Others (5) refer these differently to the most recent times, especially among the more recent Reformed, Cocceius and Willius. The former says that this chapter contains the final time before the last day. He says the beginning is the assault on the Church by nations gathered from everywhere, the catastrophe is the peace and amendment of the Church and the amplification of the same throughout the whole world, and that those beginnings fall into our own time, in this sense: Behold, the day of Jehovah comes, and your spoils shall be divided (because the goods of the Anti-Christian assembly are being despoiled) in your midst. Those goods, along with your goods, shall be divided as spoils, and men shall return to those from whom they had departed (which Cocceius wishes to apply especially to that time when the Church prepares itself for a military expedition against the command of God, Is. 30:15, 16, 17). By Jerusalem, he understands the Reformed Church, which also has Judah among the attackers, v. 14. By the congregation of the nations, he explains their coming together both in the observance of Gog and his law, Ez. 38:7, and in a league and common expedition against the Church, Ap. 9:14, 15, 16, c. 16:14, c. 19:9, c. 20:8, 9, Is. 66:18. And he explains the city captured as the occupation of Bohemia, Germany, especially the Palatinate, a great part of Denmark, the entry into more than one part of Belgium, and the coercion of Britain through deceit and terror. And the mind of Willius seems to be the same, except that he clings to his own periods and refers these to the Sardian period. But what kind of leap is that from the time of the passion of Christ, and the fountain opened against sins, to these most recent times? And what traces occur here either of spoils carried off by the Anti-Christ, or of the Calvinian Church—deformed rather than Reformed—or that by Judah attacking Jerusalem, the Lutherans are understood, as he himself thinks, to whom the injury of a fight against the true Church is attributed, when they are contending for heavenly truth against impious Cinglio-Calvinian dogmas. Furthermore, if the Reformed Church, as it is distinguished from the Lutheran, is the city of Jerusalem, which is said here to be captured, why is a great part of Denmark included under this city, in which kingdom there is no place for Calvinian assemblies? Besides, I confess I do not understand how the passages which Cocceius accumulates fit here, at least, as it appears, because it pleases him so. What does the prophecy concerning Gog in Ezekiel 37 have to do with this oracle? What does Is. 66:18? What do the Apocalyptic passages? (Which comparison of Cocceius is merely precarious.) What are those nations that have come together into the observance of Gog and his law, and into a league and common expedition against the Church, when Bohemia was occupied? What the cause of the Bohemian war was, is known to the world. Certainly, the Reformed did not fulfill the duty of the spiritual Jerusalem in it when they occupied the kingdom of Bohemia, whence the most serious disturbances arose in the Roman Empire. There is no reason for us to touch upon the rest.

Let there follow, therefore, secondly, the exposition of those who maintain that these things were fulfilled long ago, and indeed in the time of the Maccabees, in which fulfillment a divorce of opinions is again detected. For Palacius, Mariana, à Castro, Cornelius à Lapide, Menochius, and Tirinus judge it predicted here that Jerusalem was to be captured by Antiochus Epiphanes and restored by the Maccabees. Grotius, however, refers these partly to Antiochus Eupator as regards the congregation of the nations against Jerusalem, and partly to Antiochus Epiphanes as regards the occupation of Jerusalem. Gvalterus accepts it both concerning Antiochus Epiphanes and the subsequent times, in which the city was captured by Pompey, the temple plundered by Crassus, and Herod was designated King of Judea by the Romans, who, after a six-month siege, made a great slaughter of citizens in the captured city. So also Calvin: I do not doubt that the Prophet wished to include here all the disasters that were impending: because the city had not yet been built when the Jews were harshly vexed by their neighbors. Then we know what an atrocious tyranny Antiochus exercised. Finally, there was a continuous series of evils from the time the temple began to be built with the city until the coming of Christ. Thirdly, most others refer this occupation of the city to the storming done by the Romans, to which opinion, as being the truest, we add our vote. But that this prophecy is not to be accepted concerning Antiochus Epiphanes, not concerning his successor, not concerning others before the coming of Christ, but concerning Vespasian and the final destruction of the city, is clear first from the continuity of the context: because he had previously dealt with the coming and the passion of Christ the Prophet c. 9. 11. 12. 13. Since therefore these things which he predicts, those former things are to follow, Behold the day of the Lord will come, and the spoils will be divided, it is manifest that these things refer to the slaughter before the coming of the Lord, and cannot be drawn backward. Furthermore, this punishment must without doubt be explained concerning that Jerusalem, whose guilt had been designated before, in the selling and piercing of Christ, and the evils with which they had afflicted him, when the sword was raised against this shepherd of ours, cf. Matth. 23, 38. Besides, because the dispersion was predicted to them in particular c. 13, 8. now the judgment of God is described against this city and the whole people.

Nor indeed does the Grotian solution harmonize with itself, for it mixes the expedition under Antiochus Eupator with the occupation which took place under Antiochus Epiphanes. But the text speaks openly of that expedition which was joined with the occupation of the city. The expedition under Eupator, however, was not joined with the occupation of the city. Therefore it does not speak of that at all. Nor did Antiochus have so many nations and peoples in his army that it could be said of them that God had gathered all nations to Jerusalem for battle.

By far, therefore, the explanation of our people is more correct: Behold the day of the Lord will come, the day of the vengeance and judgment of the Lord, by which he will punish the horrible impiety of the Jews, especially indeed, because they killed the only-begotten Son, a man near to God. And your spoils (O Jerusalem) will be divided in the midst of you: the Roman soldier, the city having been occupied, within the very walls, will divide the spoils. For I will gather all (various) nations to Jerusalem for battle, that they may attack and take the city. For the Roman army consisted of various nations and peoples when Vespasian besieged the city. And the city will be taken: by the Romans. And the houses will be devastated, or rather plundered, and the women will be violated. And half of the city will go out into captivity. They will be sold by the Romans, like beasts of burden, and will be scattered among all peoples. And the rest of the people will not be taken away from the city, half of the people will remain in the city, and will perish there at the time of the siege, by sedition, plague, famine, and sword. For so many thousands of Jews perished in the seditions in the city at the beginning, so many were afterwards taken away by famine, so many perished by plague, so many were slaughtered and butchered by the enemy, the city having now been captured, that it is deservedly said that half the part was not driven out of the city. Which explanation is confirmed by a comparison with chapter 11, 4. Open, O Lebanon, thy doors, and Jerome, Cyril, Theodoret, Eusebius l. 6. demonstr. c. 18. Rupert, Vatabl, Ribera, Sanchez, and our people after B. Luther, all to a man, easily agree to it. Also among the Reformed, Junius, Piscator; the Belgian Paraphrasts, etc. especially to be noted here is the suffrage of L. Danaeus, who although he explained the former things just as Grotius did, concerning the time of the Maccabees and the restoration following them made by them, yet he did not refer this to Antiochus, but to the Romans, and the slaughter brought about by them: an army gathered from every nation will come against Jerusalem, God willing, with Roman leaders. Some, however, understand the latter words concerning the remnants saved, as Theodoret: the rest will not perish from the city. There is a report that when Vespasian and Titus were undertaking the war at the time, the faithful left the city by revelation. Thus also B. Tarnovius interprets it.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET CONGREGABO OMNES GENTES AD JERUSALEM IN PRÆLIUM.) Centum millia peditum, XX. millia equitum, elephantos XXXII. sub Antiocho Eupatore. Scriptof 1. Maccab. 6, 28. de hoc tempore: καὶ ἀπὸ βασιλέων ἑτέρων, καὶ ἀπὸ νήσων θαλασσῶν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν δυνάμεις μισθωταί.

ET CAPIETUR CIVITAS,) Judæi in tem- plum se recipere sunt coacti Jos. 12, 14. est retrogres- sio non magna, quo magis intelligatur imminutio in po- pulo facta,

ET VASTABUNTUR DOMUS, ET MULIE- RES VIOLABUNTUR,) Ut & ante factum fuerat in Antiochi Epiphanis adventu.

ET EGREDIETUR MEDIA PARS CIVITATIS IN CAPTIVITATEM.) Propter famem se dedent. Jo- sephus, πολλοὶ τοιγαρῦν τῶν πολιορκωμένων ἐπεδίδρασκον διὰ τὴν τῶν ἀναγκαίων ἀπορίαν.

ET RELIQVUM POPULI NON AUFERETUR EX URBE.) Defendent Templum.

TRiplex imprimis occurrit capitis hujus expli- catio. Prima est, hæc omnia adhuc implenda esse, quod quintuplici ratione rursus asseritur. Pri- mo Judæi hæc implenda dicunt tempore adventus Messiæ, quem expectant, & quidem secundum li- teræ proprietatem; Sed quum Messias venire de- buerit stante adhuc templo, & antequam auferre- tur sceptrum de Juda & legislator de pedibus ejus, quæ cum aliis characteribus ante 16. secula suum complementum jam habuere, frustra expectat perfida Judæorum gens Messiam. Neque locum ha- bet sensus proprius literæ, quomodo enim urbs Jeru- salem capiet omnes gentes terræ? quomodo lebetes in Jerusalem & Juda consecrandi essent omnes Domi- no? Sic enim nullos domi suæ haberent ad usus suos. Quæ & alia docent, retineri non posse sensum proprium, sed figurate hæc intelligenda esse.

Porro secundo Chiliastæ etsi Christum advenisse agnoscant, somniant itidem complementum ho- rum secundum literam, unde eos conjungit Hiero- nymus cum Judæis in h. l. Judæi juxta literam somni- ant & nostri Chiliastæ, qui rursum audire desiderant, crescite & multiplicamini, replete terram, & pro hujus vitæ continentia, brevique jejunio, bulbos sibi & vulvas & aves phasidis & attaginem, nequaquam Jo- nicum sed Judaicum repromittunt.

A quibus tertio recentiores Chiliastæ in eo quidem differunt, quod non mundana talia sibi promittant, regnum tamen Christi per mille annos sperent in his terris, idque in hoc etiam loco quærant, de quo vid. Alstedius tr. de mille annis Apocalyptic.

Quarto ad tempora Anti-Christi hæc referunt alii apud Calvin. in h. l. significari hic vastationem Ecclesiæ futuram per An- ti-Christum, quem Judæi recepturi sint quasi suum Messiam Papistæ nonnulli ajunt. Qui Hierosolymis positurus sit thronum tyrannidis suæ sub finem mundi. Quem sensum Lyrani & Dionysii minime literalem esse, inde probat Corn. à Lapide, quia si in fine mundi hæc fiant, ad literam ista intelligi nequeant, quæ de restitutione & celebritate Jerusalem dicuntur, quod quotannis ad eam venturæ sint omnes gentes, festum tabernaculorum celebraturæ. Sic ergo ana- gogice de celebratione festi istius in cælis intelligit. Sed meræ fabellæ sunt quæ de Anti-Christo adhuc venturo sub finem mundi nugantur Papistæ.

Alii (5) aliter referunt hæc ad novissima tempora, præ- sertim è recentioribus Reformatis Coccejus & Wil- lius. Ille contineri ait hoc capite ultimum tempus ante novissimum diem. Initium esse oppugnationem Ecclesiæ per gentes undiquaque collectas, catastrophen pacem & emendationem Ecclesiæ & amplificationem ejusdem per totum mundum, & initia illa in no- strum incidere tempus, hoc sensu: Ecce dies venit Jehovæ, & dividentur spolia tua(quia spoliatis An- ti-Christi cœtum bonis suis (in medio tui. Bona ista cum vestris bonis tanquam spolia dividentur, & homines redibunt ad eos, à quibus discesserant (quæ convenire maxime vult Coccejus illi tempo- ri, quo se parat Ecclesia ad expeditionem bellicam contra mandatum Dei Es. 30, 15. 16. 17.) Per Hiero folymam intelligens Ecclesiam Reformatam, quæ & Judam habeat inter oppugnantes v. 14. Per con- gregationem gentium coitionem illarum tum in ob- servantia Gogi & legis ejus Ez. 38, 7. tum in fœdus & communem expeditionem contra Ecclesiam Ap. 9, 14. 15. 16. c. 16, 14. c. 19, 9. c. 20, 8. 9. Es. 66, 18. At- que urbem captam explicat de occupatione Bohemiæ, Germaniæ, imprimis Palatinatus, magnæ partis Daniæ, ingressu in partem Belgii non unam, & coer- citione Britanniæ per dolum & terrorem. Et eadem videtur Willio mens, nisi quod inhæreat suis periodis, & hæc ad periodum Sardenfem referat. Sed qualis ille saltus à tempore passionis Christi, & aperti fontis adversus peccata, ad novissima hæc tempora? Et quæ hic vestigia occurrunt vel de spo- liis ab Anti-Christo reportatis, vel de Ecclesia Cal- viniana, deformata potius quam Reformata, aut quod per Judam oppugnantem Hierosolymam, Lu- therani, ut ipse putat, intelligantur, quibus injuria pugna adversus veram Ecclesiam tribuitur, cum adversus impia dogmata Cinglio-Calviniana pro veritate cœlesti decertant. Porro si Ecclesia Refor- mata qua distinguitur à Lutherana, est urbs Hiero- solyma, quæ hic capta dicitur, cur comprehenditur magna pars Daniæ sub hac urbe, in quo regno nul- lus est Calvinianis cœtibus locus. Adhæc non capio, fateor, qui huc quadrent loca, quæ cumulat Coccejus, saltim, ut apparet, quia ita placet. Quid ad hoc oraculum faciat prophetia de Gogo Ezech. 37, quid Es. 66, 18. Quid loca Apocalyptica? (Quæ collatio Cocceji mere precaria est.) Quæ gentes illæ sint, quæ coivere in observantiam Gogi & legis ejus, & in fœdus & communem expeditio- nem contra Ecclesiam, cum occupata Bohemia? Quæ causa fuerit belli Bohemici, orbi notum est. Non certe in eo Hierosolymæ spiritualis officium explevere Reformati, cum Bohemiæ regnum oc- cuparunt, unde gravissimi in Romano Imperio motus orti. Cætera non est quod tangamus.

Succedat itaque secundo eorum expositio, qui hæc jam pridem impleta esse statuunt, & quidem tempore Maccabæorum, in quo complemento ite- rum deprehenditur sententiarum divortium. Nam Palacius, Mariana, à Castro, Cornelius à Lapide, Menochius, Tirinus prædictum hic censent, quod Jerusalem capienda fuerit ab Antiocho Epiphane, & restituenda à Maccabæis. Grotius vero partim ad Antiochum Eupatora hæc refert quoad congre- gationem gentium adversus Jerusalem, partim ad Antiochum Epiphanem, quoad occupationem Hierosolymæ. Gvalterus tum de Antiocho Epi- phane, tum de subsequentibus temporibus accipit, quibus à Pompejo urbs capta, à Crasso templum direptum, & Herodes à Romanis Judææ Rex de- signatus, in urbe post obsidionem semestrem ca- pta stragem civium fecit maximam. Sic etiam Calvinus : Ego non dubito, quin Propheta comple- cti hic voluerit clades omnes, quæ instabant : quia nondum urbs ædificata fuerat, quum Judæi duriter vexati fuerunt à suis vicinis. Deinde scimus quam atrocem tyrannidem exercuerit Antiochus. Denique continua fuit series malorum, ex quo cœpit templum cum urbe extrui usque ad Christi adventum : Tertio hanc occupationem urbis ad expugnationem à Ro- manis factam alii plerique referunt, cui sententiæ, utpote verissimæ adjicimus calculum. Quod au- tem non de Antiocho Epiphane, non de succes- sore ejus, non de aliis ante Christi adventum accipiendum sit hoc vaticinium, sed de Vespasia- no, & novissimo urbis excidio, primum è συνεχεία contextus patet : quia antea egerat de adventu & passione Christi Propheta c. 9. 11. 12. 13. Quum ergo hæc quæ prædicit, illa superiora consequutura sint, Ecce veniet dies Domini, & dividentur spolia, mani- festum est, hæc ad cladem ante adventum Domi- ni referri, ac retro trahi non posse. Adhæc de illa Hierosolyma hæc pœna sine dubio explicanda, cujus culpa antéa designata erat, in venditione & transfixione Christi, & malis, quibus ipsum affece- rant, cum framea suscitabatur super hunc pasto- rem nostrum, conf. Matth. 23, 38. Præterea, quia ipsi imprimis prædicta erat dispersio c. 13, 8. jam describitur judicium Dei adversus hanc urbem & universum populum.

Nec vero consonat sibi Grotiana ἐπίλυσις, nam commiscet expeditionem sub Antiocho Eu- patore cum occupatione, quæ facta est sub Antio- cho Epiphane. At de illa expeditione textus a- perte loquitur, quæ conjuncta fuit cum urbis oc- cupatione. Expeditio autem sub Eupatore non conjuncta fuit cum occupatione urbis. De illa ergo minime loquitur. Neque Antiochus tot gentes & populos in exercitu suo habuit, ut de illis dici potuerit. Deum congregasse omnes gentes ad Jerusalem in prælium.

Longe ergo rectius se habet Nostratium ex- plicatio: Ecce dies Domini veniet, dies ultionis & judicii Domini, quo puniet horribilem impieta- tem Judæorum, imprimis vero, quod Filium uni- genitum virum Deo proximum, occiderint. Et di- videntur spolia tua (ô Jerusalem) in medio tui: mi- les Romanus occupata urbe, intra ipsa mœnia, spolia dividet. Etenim congregabo omnes (varias) gentes ad Jerusalem in prælium, ut urbem oppugnent, & expugnent. Romanus enim exercitus è variis constabat genibus & populis, cum Vespasianus urbem obsideret. Et capietur civitas : à Romanis. Et vastabuntur, vel potius diripientur domus, & mulieres violabuntur. Et egredietur media pars civitatis in captivitatem. Vendentur à Romanis, quasi jumenta, & distrahentur inter omnes popu- los. Et reliquum populi non auferetur ex urbe, dimidia pars populi manebit, in urbe, & obsidio- nis tempore ibi interitura est, seditione, peste, fa- me, gladio. Tot enim millia Judæorum in seditio- nibus in urbe sub initium occubuerunt, tot postea fame adsumti sunt, tot peste periere, tot ab hoste, capta jam urbe, trucidati, ac jugulati, ut merito di- catur, dimidiam partem non fuisse ex urbe expul- fam. Quam explicationem collatio cum cap. 11, 4. aperi Libane portas tuas confirmat, inque eam fa- cile consentiunt Hieronymus, Cyrillus, Theodoreţus, Eusebius. l. 6. demonstr. c. 18. Rupert. Vatabl. Ribera, Sanchez, & nostrates post B. Lutherum ad unum omnes. Etiam è Reformatis, Junius, Pisca- tor; Paraphr. Belgici &c. imprimis notandum hic L. Danæi suffragium, qui etsi perinde, ut Grotius, superiora de tempore Maccabæorum & consequen- tium restaurationem ab ipsis factam exposuit, hoc tamen non retulit ad Antiochum, sed ad Ro- manos, & cladem ab ipsis illatam : ex quavis gente exercitus adversus Hierosolymam allectus conveniet, Deo volente, Ducibus Romanis. Posteriora tamen verba nonnulli de reliquiis servatis intelligunt, uti Theodoret. reliqui non peribunt de civitate, Fama est Vespasiano & Tito bellum, suscipientibus in tempo- re, fideles ex revelatione urbem reliquisse. Sic etiam interpretatur B. Tarnovius.

## 14:3
Vers. 3. AND THE LORD WILL GO FORTH, AND WILL FIGHT AGAINST THOSE NATIONS.) Has. For the besieged often broke out successfully, as the already mentioned writers report: and that contributed not a little to peace.

AS HE FOUGHT IN THE DAY OF BATTLE.) That is, at the Red Sea, when he overthrew Pharaoh and his forces.

These do not treat of the sorties of the besieged against the enemies by whom they were besieged. Others, therefore, who with the Chaldean and Vulgate translate AGAINST the nations, interpret it concerning the miraculous battles of the Maccabees against Antiochus; 1 Macc. 4, 9. 2 Macc. 10, 19. C. 11, 8. C. 15, 12. but it was warned before that it does not concern Antiochus, or the nations joined to him. Most, therefore, of our people understand it concerning the spiritual war: And the Lord will go forth into the world through the preaching of the Gospel, just as he is accustomed to fight in the day of battle, that is, according to his custom, when he subjects peoples to himself in spiritual battle. And that the Lord fought in this way against the Romans, when he sent out the Apostle Paul, so that he might preach the Gospel of Christ in Rome not only to the Jews, but also to the nations, and win his hearers for Christ, Acts 28. see. Tarnovius: but the preposition ב can be rendered IN, or WITH the nations, as the LXX rendered it: so that it may be indicated that the Lord will go forth like a warrior and will fight himself in those nations against his enemies. For the enemies had opposed themselves to the Lord and had most gravely irritated and provoked his wrath. Thus Theodoret explains it: he will fight, not defending for the Jews, but adorning and instructing an army against them; similarly also Cyril. Of the more recent ones, Danaeus p. 998. The cause and reason why such a calamity can be brought upon such a fortified and populous city (such as Jerusalem once was) is that God himself is about to fight against it, and will be in the midst of the forces of the hostile army. For thus I interpret these words, he will fight Bajogim, i.e., among or in the midst of those very nations gathered against Jerusalem, and he will fight among them, not as an enemy and adversary to those nations, but as a helper. Thus I do not interpret the letter ב as 'against', but as 'for' or 'between'. Moreover, two things are contained here. First, that it will come to pass that God, who until that day had been the guardian of that people and city, will go out from the city, and will desert his inner sanctuary, his temple, and the city, and will hold them as abandoned. Finally, that he will migrate elsewhere, namely to the enemies besieging the city; see Josephus, Jewish War, book 7, chapter 12. The second is that it will also come to pass that God will fight against the Jews and Jerusalem, being present in the army of the enemies as a fellow soldier and their ally, and indeed God himself will fight against the Jews not lightly, but most ardently and vigorously, as he is accustomed to do when he clashes most fiercely in the gravest battles, where it appears most manifestly that he is present and fighting as if for Gideon, for David, for Hezekiah, and often for others, as Danaeus says here again.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET EGREDIETUR DOMINUS, ET PRÆ- LIABITUR CONTRA GENTES ILLAS.) Has. Sæpe enim feliciter erupere obsessi, ut tradunt dicti jam scripto- res : idque non parum profecit ad pacem.

SICUT PRÆLIATUS EST IN DIE CERTA- MINIS.) Id est, ad mare rubrum, cum Pharaonem ejusque copias prostravit.

Non agunt hæc de eruptionibus obsessorum contra hostes, a quibus obsessi. Alii itaque, qui cum Chald. & Vulg. vertunt CONTRA gentes, de præliis Mac- cabæorum contra Antiochum miraculosis interpre- tantur; 1. Macc. 4, 9. 2. Macc. 10, 19. C. 11, 8. C. 15, 12. sed monitum antea non agi de Antiocho, aut ei junctis gentibus. Plerique ergo è nostris intelligunt de spirituali bello: Et egredietur Dominus in orbem terrarum per prædicationem Evangelii, sicut præ- liari solet in die certaminis, id est, pro more suo, quando populos spirituali prælio sibi subjicit. At- que ita præliatum esse Dominum contra Romanos, cum emitteret Paulum Apostolum, ut is Romæ Evangelium Christi non modo Judæis, sed etiam gentibus prædicaret, & auditores suos Christo lu- crifaceret Act. 28. vid. Tarnovius: sed præpositio ב reddi potest IN, vel CUM gentibus, ut LXX. red- diderunt: ut indicetur, Dominum bellatoris instar egreffurum & præliaturum ipsummet in gentibus illis adversus hostes suos. Opposuerant enim sese hostes Domino ejusdemque iram gravissime irritarant, ac provocarant. Sic exponit Theodoretus: prælia- bitur non pro Judæis propugnans sed contra illos exer- citum adornans, & instruens; Similiter etiam Cy- rillus. E recentioribus Danæus p. 998. Causa & ratio cur tanta calamitas, tam munitæ populosæque urbi (qualis olim erat Hierosolyma) afferri possit, est, quod Deus ipse contra eam sit pugnaturus, & in mediis hostilis exercitus copiis futurus. Sic enim interpretor verba hæc pugnabit Bajogim, i. e. inter aut in medio ipsarum gentium adversus Hierosolymam collecta- rum, & pugnabit inter eos, non ut hostis & adversa- rius illis gentibus, sed ut auxiliator. Ita literam ב non interpretor contra, sed pro aut inter. Cæterum hic duo continentur. Primum, fore, ut tunc Deus, qui ad illum usque diem fuerat custodia istius gen- tis & urbis, egrediatur ex urbe, & adyta, templum suum, ac urbem deserat, & pro relictis habeat. Denique alio migret, nempe ad hostes urbem ob- sidentes; vid. Joseph. lib. 7. Jud. Bell. cap. 12. Se- cundum est, fore quoque ut Deus adversus Judæos & Hierosolymam pugnet versans in hostium ex- ercitu, tanquam commilito, & eorum socius, & quidem dimicabit Deus ipse contra Judæos non leviter, sed ardentissime & strenuissime, quomo- do solet, quum acerrime confligit in gravissimis præliis, ubi manifestissime apparet, ipsum adesse & præliari veluti pro Gedeone, pro Davide, pro Ezechia, & aliis sæpe, ut iterum hic Danæus.

## 14:4
Verse 4.

AND HIS FEET SHALL STAND.) Of Bacchides, who will be in command of those nations. Thus, a person is often understood from the sense. IN THAT DAY UPON THE MOUNT OF OLIVES,) Which is convenient for pitching camp.

Bacchides is introduced too rashly. If it is permitted to insert into the text at will those persons of whom no traces are found in the text, nothing certain will be left in the Holy Scriptures. The sense, from which he understands that leader, likewise rests on no foundation. However, all interpreters agree that the Lord is pointed out by the relative pronoun, as he was mentioned before. Cyril interprets it as concerning Christ the Lord, and others do so as well.

AND THE MOUNT OF OLIVES SHALL BE SPLIT IN THE MIDST THEREOF TOWARD THE EAST, AND TOWARD THE WEST, A VERY GREAT VALLEY.) In the Hebrew: a very great valley. That is, much earth will be carried away, so that the mountain will gape open in a great part of itself,

AND HALF OF THE MOUNTAIN SHALL BE REMOVED TOWARD THE NORTH, AND HALF OF IT TOWARD THE SOUTH.) That is, the earth thus removed from the mountain will be carried partly to attack the northern parts, partly to attack the southern parts of the temple. Ver. 5. AND YOU SHALL FLEE TO THE VALLEY OF THEIR MOUNTAINS, FOR THE VALLEY OF THE MOUNTAINS SHALL BE JOINED UNTO THE NEAREST.) The Chaldean אצל, which is here translated as nearest, took it for a proper name: and no less so the Greeks. The same Greeks, and the Chaldean in this place, and the Greeks also in the following words, נסתם, do not take it in the second plural from נס, but in the third singular from סתם, for they translate: and the valley of the mountains shall be stopped up and the ravine of the mountains shall be joined unto Azel. Both Symmachus and Theodotion have placed the proper name Azel. Some think the Latin interpreter wrote of my mountains, because in the Hebrew there is הרי: but it can be a regimen for the absolute, which permutation we have noted elsewhere. Especially in these writers, who not rarely speak in the Syrian manner. The sense seems to me to be this: and (after the departure of the enemies) the valley of the mountains shall be obstructed (because the earth removed from one mountain of Olivet had made it as it were two) so that that valley of the mountains may be leveled to the height: namely, of the mountain. אציל height also in Ezekiel 41, 8. AND YOU SHALL FLEE AS YOU FLED.) It shall be obstructed, I say, just as it was obstructed, namely, the valley once made in the same place. FROM THE FACE OF THE EARTHQUAKE.) That is, because of the earthquake, which had made a gap in the same mountain. IN THE DAYS OF UZZIAH KING OF JUDAH.) Of which earthquake Amos 1, 1 makes mention, where see what is said. Add Isaiah 1, 6. These things are said parenthetically, because mention had been made of a valley made by the enemy, lest anyone should think it would remain forever.

That this was fulfilled on the day of Christ's ascension into heaven, Luke the last chapter, where his feet stood on the Mount of Olives, and thence he was taken up into heaven, B. Luther, Osiander, Winckelmann, the Weimar Paraphrasts, Tarnovius, and others of ours think: (which sense neither the Papists, nor Gwalther among the Reformed disapprove; although they wish other senses to be hinted at at the same time) because Christ stood there, and at the same time gave commands to the disciples about preaching the Gospel in the whole world. This interpretation does not suit the palate of Willius, to whom nothing seems to taste of anything but his own ideas, however much the Belgian Paraphrasts may have chosen and followed the same. In such an interpretation, he says, there is nothing accurate. What, therefore, does he offer that is more accurate? He invents a Philadelphian period from verse 3, for which he has persuaded his own mind not only of the assertion of the Reformed Church from the hand of the enemies of the Anti-Christ, and the kings addicted to him, drawing the words hither: after the Lord shall go forth, and shall fight against those nations etc., the truth of which he thinks began to be fulfilled, and will be fulfilled hereafter, so that (the Philadelphian Calvinists (followers of syncretism and peace not based on the word of God) may reach full happiness. But he also dares to promise the most ample expansion of the Calvinian kingdom (which to him is the kingdom of Christ) from verses 4 and 5, and furthermore, he promises I know not what golden age of his Orthodox, i.e., Reformed Church, of which there is nothing in this prophecy, nor anywhere in the scriptures, and which does not at all fit the extreme malice of the last times, devoid of all faith, of all charity, and most full of seducers and wickedness.
