Nor can that be gathered from Lev. IV. 3. Heb. V. 3. It is absurd that sins could not be expiated except through a holy priest. The efficacy of the ministry does not depend on the holiness of the minister.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET NVNC DEPRECAMINI VVLTUM DEI) Coram Deo orate.

VT MISEREATVR VESTRI) Vt condonet contra legem admissa.

DE MANV ENIM VESTRA FACTVM EST HOC) Fecistis enim quæ dixi: vosmet ipsi negare non potestis.

SI QVOMODO SVSCIPIAT FACIES VESTRAS) Non desperare jubet: sed ostendit veniam esse difficilem tam aperti ac diuturni contemtus legum divinarum. Similis locutio Actorum cap. VIII. vers. 22. & alibi.

Nonnulli Ironice vel ἐπανορθωτικῶς hæc accipiunt, cum Isidoro Clario, & Aria Montano, Willio; sed est exhortatio ad pænitentiam, ut Hieronymus, Theodoretus & plerique alij docent, q. d. vos ergo Sacerdotes suppliciter deprecamini vultum Domini, quia vos cum offendistis, vestrum hoc est peccatum si quomodo auferat à vobis faciem iratam, ut nonnulli Ebræa reddunt. Quæ vero alij sic potius explicanda du- cunt; numquid suscipiet vobis vultum? id est, num habiturus ipsum rationem officij vestri putatis, ut suscipere faciem accipitur Lev. XIX. 15. Ps. XV. 5. Atque ita cum Cyrillo B. Lutherus: Meinet ihr/ Er werde euer Person ansehen. Quem sensum phraseos versus præcedens confirmat, offer illud duci tuo, & vide si placuerit ei, aut si susceperit faciem tuam? Magnum autem pondus habet oratio ἀσύνδετος & crebris interrogationibus, quæ conscientiæ pun- cturis, ac crebris stimulis aculeata ad socordes ex- citandos. Aliena autem hic est interpretatio Coc- ceji nec textui analoga, quam cum Abarbenele tra- didit: Considerate ergo, an Deo possit esse gratum, quod vobis ministris & intercessoribus offertur, & an ullius ex vobis faciem accepturus sit? Falsum est, quod hactenus subjectus fuerit sacerdotibus pius offe- rens, ut quoad consolationem de fructu terreno non prodessent Sacrificia offerentibus, quæ per impios adolebantur & consecrabantur: sed potius metuendum essent, ut ira esservesceret in totum cœtum. Nec colligi id potest è Lev. IV. 3. Ebr. V. 3. Absurdum, peccata non potuisse expiari nisi per sacerdotem sanctum. Non dependet è sanctitate ministri efficacia ministerij.

## 1:10
Ver. 10. WHO IS AMONG YOU THAT WOULD SHUT THE DOORS AND KINDLE MY ALTAR FOR NOTHING?

Who among you that would shut the doors, (for nothing) nay, you do not even kindle my altar for nothing. The sense is: all those things which you pretend for your avarice are empty. Thus the law well provided not for the priests, but also for the people and the doorkeepers that they might have an abundant reward for their labor, the Greek here is more obscure, which as we have it in our codices, Chrysostom cites, in his sermon that Christ is God.

Concerning the base greed of the priests, and of all the ministers of the temple, referring even all the most minute ministries to shameful gain, Jerome, Hugo, B. Luther, Osiander, Winckelmann, Danæus, and others also explain, i.e., You burn with such zeal for the true worship of God, that unless you hoped for profit from it, surely none of you would shut the doors of the temple, and foster the fire on my altar. Others with the LXX and the Chaldean translate it thus; who is among you, who would shut the doors, that you might not kindle my altar for nothing? i.e., would that one of you would shut the doors of the temple, that you might not burn these polluted victims upon my altar in vain, or to no purpose. Thus Theodoret, Vatablus, Clarius, Corn. à Lapide, Willius & Lud. de Dieu: the sense is, so far am I from wishing to accept your face, that on the contrary I command every one of you priests, who ought to open the doors of my temple to offer sacrifices, to shut them, lest you continue to kindle my altar, for you do it in vain, why in vain? because I do not accept either you or your gifts. Thus also B. Luther T. VII. Altenb. 203. in Comment. ad h. l. That is to say as much as: Would to God there were one among you who would shut the temple, so that you would not offer so in vain. Conf. Is. I. 12. Cyril wishes it to be a prophecy according to the version of the LXX. For also among you doors will be shut, and you will not kindle my altar for nothing. He says that the doors will be shut upon them, either because the priests of the law will not burn the kindled offering, or certainly when the true tabernacle has been exhibited, i.e., the Church, some still performing the legal priesthood will not enter. But because of unbelief, as if excluded, they will remain outside, and will not touch the holy things. But these do not agree with the Hebrew text, the sense of which the former explanation expressed most correctly.

I HAVE NO WILL IN YOU) I do not love men intent only on their own gain, such as you are, and from whence the greatest evils will be born for you.

AND I WILL NOT ACCEPT A GIFT FROM YOUR HAND) I will not have it as pleasing, as the Chaldean here.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVIS EST IN VOBIS QVI CLAUDAT OSTIA ET INCENDAT ALTARE MEUM GRATUITO?

Quis vestrum qui claudat ostia, (gratis) imo ne altare quidem meum accenditis gratis. Sensus est: omnia illa quæ avaritiæ vestræ prætenditis inania sunt. Ita bene lex prospexit non sacerdotibus, sed & popi s & janitoribus ut abunde merce- dem habeant operæ, Græca hic obscuriora sunt, quæ ut in nostris codicibus habemus, citat Chrysostomus, ser- mone Christum esse Deum.

De αἰσχροκερδία sacerdotum, & omnium templi ministrorum, omnia etiam minutissima quæque ministeria ad turpem quæstum referentia explicant etiam Hieronymus, Hugo, B. Lutherus, Osiander, Winckelmann. Danæus, alij, q. d. Tanto scil. zelo ve- ri cultus Dei ardetis, ut nisi emolumentum inde speraretis, nemo profecto vestrum ostia templi clauderet, atque ignem in altari meo foveret. Alij cum LXX. & Chaldeo ita vertunt; quis est in vobis, qui claudat fores, ut non accendatis altare meum gra- tis? q. d. utinam aliquis vestrum clauderet fores templi, ut non uratis super altare meum victimas hasce pollutas frustra, sive in vanum. Ita Theodore- tus, Vatablus, Clarius, Corn. à Lapide, Willius & Lud. de Dieu: sensus est, tantum abest, ut vultum vestrum suscipere velim, ut contra unumquemque etiam vestrum sacerdotum, qui fores templi mei ad offe- renda sacrificia aperire debetis, jubeam eas clau- dere, ne pergatis altare meum accendere, frustra enim id facitis, cur frustra? quia nec vos nec mu- nera vestra accepta habeo. Sic quoque B. Lutherus T. VII. Altenb. 203. in Comment. ad h. l. Das ist so viel gesaget: Wolte Gott es wäre doch einer unter euch/ der den Tempel zuschlüsse/ daß Jhr nicht so vergeblich opffertet. Conf. Es. I. 12. Cyrillus vaticini- um esse vult juxta versionem LXX. Διότι καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν συγκλειθήσοντα θύραι, ὼς ὐκ ἀνάψατε τὸ θυσια- σήριόν με δωρεὰν. Quia & in vobis claudentur ostia, & non accendetis altare meum gratis. Clausum iri super ipsis ostia dicit, aut quia sacerdotes legis non ado- lebunt accensum, aut certe cum verius tabernaculum exhibitum fuerit, h. e. Ecclesia, quidam legale sacer- dotium adhuc obeuntes, non intrabunt. Propter incre- dulitatem vero quasi exclusi, foris manebunt, & san- cta non attingent. Sed hæc Ebræo textui non con- veniunt, cujus sensum prior explicatio rectissime expressit.

NON EST MIHI VOLUNTAS IN VOBIS) Non amo homines quæstui tantum suo intentos, quales vos estis, & unde maxima vobis mala nascentur.

ET MUNUS NON SUSCIPIAM DE MANU VESTRA) Gratum non habebo, ut hic Chaldæus.

## 1:11
Ver. 11.

FOR FROM THE RISING OF THE SUN EVEN UNTO THE SETTING MY NAME IS GREAT AMONG THE GENTILES) In the Hebrew 'is' is not read. The ellipsis will be more correctly supplied by 'shall be'. It could have been objected: If our offerings are not pleasing to you, you will have none. God answers that he is thinking of something else, namely that he may be worshipped by all nations, not laboriously, but with a pure mind. This is the plan which God fully executed through Christ and his messengers, but the whole dispersion of the Jews among the nations, the illustrious return to the fatherland, the knowledge of the Chaldean, Persian, Greek, and Roman languages among the Jews, the discordant sects of the masters, the cares of the rites turned into old-womanish superstition, foul gains, and the neglect of true amendment, paved the way for this thing.

IN EVERY PLACE A CLEAN OBLATION IS SACRIFICED AND OFFERED TO MY NAME) Here also, as if to be understood as in Zech. 14:21, the Chaldean has also supplied this defect in this place: you may also translate the rest very well: in every place there shall be offered to my name as it were incense and a pure [offering]: as it were incense are pious prayers, Rev. 5:8, but the מנחה are the oblations of the faithful, from which the Eucharist was made, and the poor were fed.

FOR MY NAME IS GREAT AMONG THE GENTILES) It will be again: among all the gentiles, not in Judea, or among the Jews only.

It is strange that Grotius in this prophecy here and in his annotations on Luke 24:47 did not follow the Jews, which we have observed in him in most other places. Three of their expositions occur in Abarbanel.

I. The first of Jonathan and Rabbi Solomon, that God imputes to the Israelites prayers in every place instead of a pure sacrifice, which Abarbanel rejects, because the subject 'prayers of Israel' is not found in the Prophet.

II. The second of Aben Ezra and Kimchi, concerning the gentiles in a conditional sense, they shall be offered by the gentiles if it were commanded to them as to you: but here no condition appears, nay, it is held as a categorical prophecy as is clear from verses 11 and 14. Therefore Abarbanel does not approve of that exposition either.

“He himself, however, hands down a third, that the gentiles, recognizing God through the cause of the rising of the sun and its setting, offer a sacrifice which is most pure, as they think, not indeed to me, but to my name, insofar as they conceived an opinion of the first cause from the motion of the celestial bodies, and they worship it under that name by which it is named by their wise men. But this is the most inept of all. For the מ here is not causal, but local, which the opposite particle ועד AND EVEN TO clearly teaches, nor is it a matter of the cause or means of knowing God, but of the place of the celebration of God and of the oblations, from the rising of the sun even to the setting, which the declaration subjoined further confirms: AND IN EVERY PLACE a host shall be offered. Compare Ps. 113:3. Nor is it a matter of a sacrifice pure only according to the opinion of the gentiles, but of one pure in truth, and approved by God himself, since it is opposed to the rejected sacrifices offered by the Jewish priests in verse 10. But this is inept, that to offer to the name of God is less than to offer to God, and it is impious that the name of God should be held to be what the wise men of the gentiles said; in what way will pagan worship be able to be excused, just as Abarbanel also excuses the worship of the sun and the stars? See Cocceius on this place. But Abarbanel himself was forced to admit with Aben Ezra that the nations and peoples of the world, or the gentiles, are established here as offering: of whom also in verse 14: My name shall be reverenced among the gentiles.

Since therefore the Prophet prophesies that the name of God will be great and reverenced among the gentiles, from the rising of the sun even to the setting, and in every place an ob- “That a pure sacrifice is to be offered to the name of God, how can the Jews deny it, unless they wish to openly contradict the prophets, that the conversion of the nations is predicted, and that the ceremonial worship is to be abolished? For this could not be celebrated in every place, but in the place which God had chosen, Deut. XII. 5. 6. Nor does the prophet obscurely indicate that this would happen at that time when the priests were still profaning the name of the Lord, namely in the second temple, verse 13, and that it was near. Cf. Mal. III. 4. 5. Is. XIX. 19. 21. John IV. 23. 24. And here the prophet simultaneously threatens the desertion of the Jews. For it is not a simple prophecy about the calling of the nations, but God testifies that, the Jews having been cast off, He wishes to substitute other worshippers for Himself, which the causal particle teaches: I will not accept “a gift from your hand, for from the rising of the sun even “to its setting my name shall be great. Cf. “Hos. I. 9. Matt. XXI. 13. Next, the offering, “says Cyril, “he clearly rejects according to the legal worship, and almost departs from charity towards the Jews, and abhors the priesthood, and does not admit the shadow, the immolations of oxen, and the odors, I say: since that is not his scope here from the beginning.

Therefore, the gloss of Hugo concerning the offerings which proselyte nations offered from every place in the Jerusalem temple is to be rejected. For the prophet does not speak of nations about to offer from every place in Jerusalem, but of nations about to offer IN EVERY place, from the rising of the sun even to its setting. However, the spiritual sacrifices of the New Testament are understood, such as (1) the preaching of the Gospel concerning Christ crucified, by which the sacrifice performed on the cross is commemorated, Rom. XV. 16. (2) The sacrifice of faith, when the Gospel concerning Christ is received, or Christ offered for us, and is presented to God by true faith. For faith in Christ is a sacrifice and worship pleasing to God, Phil. II. 12. I am poured out upon the sacrifice and service of your faith. (3) The sacrifice of a contrite heart, Ps. LI. 19. (4) The consecration of ourselves to the service of Christ, by which we present our bodies as a living, holy, and pleasing sacrifice to God, Rom. XII. 1. (5) The sacrifice of patience and readiness to spend one's life for the glory of Christ, 2 Tim. IV. 6. (6) The sacrifice of gratitude towards the ministry, Phil. IV. 18, and of the love of mercy towards one's neighbor, Hos. VI, and especially of beneficence towards the poor, Heb. XIII. 16. (7) The sacrifice of prayers and supplications, Ps. CXLI. 2, Rev. VIII, and of praises and confession, Heb. XIII. 7. Which are truly pure and God-pleasing sacrifices, because both we and our works are pleasing to God on account of Christ. See the Osiandrian paraphrase on this passage, concerning which Cyril says: “He openly said to the priests of the law that he did not want them: or rather, that he had no will in them, namely in those sacrificing in shadow and figures, and that he would not accept their sacred rites.” Moreover, he announces beforehand that his name will be great and illustrious among all mortals throughout the whole world, and that in every place and nation a pure and unbloody sacrifice will be offered to his name, not now by those priests obscuring his dignity, nor by those carelessly offering spiritual worship to him, but by those striving with diligence and goodness and holiness to offer the sweet fragrance of spiritual incense, namely faith, hope, charity, and the adornments of good works, with the heavenly and life-giving sacrifice of Christ thus established, through which death is destroyed, and this earthly flesh subject to corruption puts on incorruption. And Jerome: “Let the word of the Lord be to the priests of the Jews. Who offer the blind and the lame and the languid for immolation: that they may know that spiritual victims are to succeed carnal victims.” And by no means the blood of bulls and goats: but incense, that is, the prayers of the saints, are to be offered to the Lord, and not in one province of the world, Judea, nor in one city of Judea, Jerusalem: but in every place an offering is to be offered, by no means unclean, as from the people of Israel: but pure, as in the ceremonies of the Christians. Theodoret likewise: “I will utterly reject you, for I greatly detest your deeds and the victims which you offer, I execrate them, in whose place I have the whole world worshipping me with the highest religion. For the inhabitants of all the lands which the rising and setting sun illuminates with its rays, when they offer incense everywhere, will also perform a sacred, pure, and pleasing sacrifice to me. For they will know my name and will and will render the due honor, and will apply the appropriate worship.” Add also Eusebius, book I, Demonstratio Evangelica, ch. VI, p. 9. Malachi, however, at the same time directs his discourse to those who are of the circumcision, and predicts such things about the nations: It is not my will, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands, since from the rising to the setting my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure sacrifice. For what does he mean when he says that incense and sacrifice are offered to God in every place, except that it will not be at Jerusalem, nor definitely in this or that place? But in every region and among all nations, which indeed would offer to the most high God not through blood, but through pious actions, both the incense of prayer and the sacrifice which is called pure. And chapter X. These things, therefore, which were divinely predicted from the beginning, are celebrated at the present time by all nations through the evangelical doctrine of our Savior, with truth bringing testimony to the prophetic voice, through which voice God, having rejected the Mosaic sacrifices, divinely announces what our own institution was to be, saying: Since from the rising of the sun to the setting, my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name and a pure host. We sacrifice, therefore, to the most high God a sacrifice of praise: we sacrifice to God a full, and awe-inspiring, and most holy sacrifice: we sacrifice in a new manner, according to the New Testament, a pure host. But a sacrifice to God is said to be a contrite spirit: therefore, a contrite and humbled heart God will not despise. And now we also kindle that prophetic fragrance in every place, and offer to him the sweet-smelling fruit of a theology abounding in every virtue, doing this very thing by prayers directed to him. Which indeed another prophet also teaches, who says: Let my prayer be as incense in thy sight. Therefore we both sacrifice and kindle, at one time celebrating the memory of that great sacrifice, according to those mysteries which have been handed down by him, and giving thanks to God for our salvation, and offering to him religious hymns and holy prayers, at another time consecrating our whole selves, and dedicating ourselves to his High Priest, the Word himself, in body and soul. Therefore we strive to keep the body untouched and immaculate from all obscenity for him, and we render to him a mind purged of every passion and every foulness that proceeds from malice, and we worship him with sincere thoughts, unfeigned affection, and decrees of truth. For we have been taught that these things are more pleasing to him than a great number of sacrificial victims, by whose blood, smoke, and stench we might be occupied. B. Luther, T. VII. Altenb. p. 204, understands by the word Mincha the proclamation of the Gospel, and by incense, prayers. What kind of sacrifice this is, he shows

Paul in Rom. XV, where he says: that I should be a servant of Christ among the Gentiles, to offer the Gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering etc. Thereby he indicates that he, through the Gospel, as through a priestly instrument, has offered the Gentiles: That is, he has surrendered them to God, and offered them, cleansed from sins, and killed in body and flesh. For through the Gospel the old errors are destroyed, and truth is awakened in the heart, which confesses God, believes in Him, entices Him, and finally kills the flesh.

Incense and grain offerings were the most prominent offerings among the Jews, which they held as the best, for divine service in all valleys, and by all green trees. By incense we understand prayer. Thus, the Word and prayer are two offerings of Christians. The prayer of Christians should be done with thanksgiving and praise. The offerings of Christians are pure, for they are without guilt, washed away with the blood of Christ etc. Unbelievers cannot offer, and Christians do not offer lame, weak, blind offerings, but with faith and gratitude. When the heart is believing, sin is not imputed.

Therefore, this prophecy is rashly seized upon by the Papists for the sacrifice of the mass, which they have invented, a propitiatory one, which nevertheless Grotius did not dare to drag into this place, even if, lest he seem to them to be entirely lacking, he restricts the word Mincha to offerings in the Eucharist, which, however, embraces every spiritual offering pleasing to God to be dedicated to God by the Gentiles, nor can it be restricted to the agape in the Eucharist. For these are neither the only, nor especially the spiritual victims in the N.T. Bellarmine, book I, on the mass, ch. X, argues that the Prophet is not speaking of spiritual sacrifices, but of a true external sacrifice, which succeeded the old ones in the N.T., which he says is none other than the Massatic sacrifice. Which, however, is impious and sacrilegious. For we have a unique propitiatory sacrifice, Christ Jesus, Heb. IX. 14, ch. X. 11. Hos. II. 2. To add another propitiatory sacrifice in the N.T. is of the highest impiety, but to substitute the Massatic one in its place, and to hawk it as the unique sacrifice of the N.T., is of extreme sacrilege. Cornelius à Lapide also contends, indeed he wishes it to be a matter of faith that this pure offering is a sacrifice of the body and blood of Christ in the Eucharist, but with the lightest of arguments. He says (1) that the word Mincha is appropriated to one grain sacrifice, Lev. II, which was a type of the Eucharistic sacrifice: I reply, that word denotes sacrifice generally, and is used absolutely for the lifting up of hands, Ps. CXLI. see Sanctius on this passage & Ps. XCVI. 8. (see Bellarmine & Ioh. Bapt. Folengius on this passage) and also of the spiritual sacrifices of the N.T., Is. LXVI. 20. nor does it fit the sacrifice of the Mass, unless it must be said that in the sacrifice of the Mass nothing but bread is offered to God; indeed, for a Mincha properly so-called, oil, incense, salt, burning, and cremation are required, Lev. II, which have no place here, and it is against the nature of the Mincha to be destitute of earthly substance, and to be joined to the species of wine. Nor was the grain sacrifice a type of the sacrifice of Christ, but of Christians, much less of the unbloody sacrifice in the Eucharist, which Scripture clearly does not recognize. He says (2) that only the Eucharist is pure, but the question is not about the Eucharist, but about the Eucharistic sacrifice, and although our spiritual sacrifices are very imperfect and unclean if they are looked at in themselves, they are nevertheless pure and pleasing to God, because they are performed by those whose hearts have been justified by faith, Acts XV. 9. & are offered through Christ, in whom all things are pure, 1 Pet. II. 3, Heb. XIII. 16. They say (3) that Malachi is speaking only to the Aaronite priests, and opposes to their tables and victims the priests, altars, and victims, which, because they were properly in the old law, and under the new law they ought to be proper. I reply: He opposes the priests of the New Testament to the priests of the Old Testament and makes them all Gentiles offering spiritual sacrifices. Furthermore: if all things under the N.T. ought to be proper, which were properly under the old, the entire Levitical cult will have to be recalled. In the O.T. slaughtering was done properly, burning was done properly, consumption was done properly; are victims therefore to be slaughtered, are they to be burned, are they to be consumed in the New Testament? It is false what Cornelius à Lapide assumes, that nature dictates that God must be worshipped with an external sacrifice. Sacrifices are of positive divine law, not of nature, nor did they have a place instituted in nature, but were destitute of it, and were divinely instituted to figure the unique propitiatory sacrifice to be offered on the altar of the cross, nor were they transferred to the Gentiles except through zeal without knowledge and diabolical illusions. He says (4) that מקטר is to be burned, to be fumigated, to be cremated, but not that prayer is burned or cremated; but a victim properly so-called. I reply: thus it would not fit the Massatic sacrifice either, because that too is not burned or cremated: But that it is transubstantiated, as the Papists trifle, and is eaten, that does not serve to prove either the burning, or the cremation, or the consumption properly so-called: Whence not even the Papists themselves have been able to agree on it thus far, in what the formal reason of this fictitious sacrifice consists. But prayer is rightly called מקטר or incense from the formula of the Holy Spirit, Ps. CXLI. 2, let my prayer be set forth as incense before thee. Thus also Apoc. V. 8. ch. VIII. 34. the incense of prayers is named. He says (5) that there is no sacrifice which is offered anywhere among the nations, like the Eucharistic sacrifice. I reply: spiritual sacrifices are offered everywhere, John IV. 22. 1 Tim. II. 8. not so the Mass sacrifice, which they wish to be offered itself on a consecrated altar: indeed, an ἱλασικὸν sacrifice could not be offered except in that place in which peace was also to be given through it, Hagg. II. 10. but not in every place. The Eucharist, however, although it is celebrated everywhere, cannot be held for a sacrifice properly so called and therefore propitiatory, because there is none without the shedding of blood, even though in the Eucharist a commemoration of the propitiatory sacrifice of Christ is instituted, as also prayer and the collection of love-feasts; they are spiritual sacrifices, for the sake of which the prophetic prediction is applied to the Eucharist by Irenaeus b. IV. ch. XXXII. and Eusebius b. I. Demonstr. ch. VI. Tertull. b. III. ch. Mark ch. XXII. b. IV. ch. I. in the book against the Jews. Nor does Jerome or even Theodoret favor the papists, as is manifest from their words previously adduced. To them, therefore, Cornelius appealed in vain, Justin also in his Dialogue with Trypho, and likewise Augustine Ep. CXX. and b. X. of the City of God ch. VI. as also Chrysostom hom. XVII. on the Ep. to the Hebrews stands on our side; the Constitutions of Clement of Rome are supposititious; we do not delay over the authority of more recent writers. But concerning the other testimonies which the Papists have patched together for that matter, it is not the place here to examine them. Both our people and the Reformed deal with them, where they expressly destroy the Mass Idol. In matters of faith, the authority of Holy Scripture alone is the αὐτὸς ἔφη.

Bellarmin urges this, that here it is a question of a new sacrifice. But spiritual sacrifices were also used in the O.T., to which the blessed Balduinus has already replied: Spiritual sacrifices were prayers, praises, faith, etc., even in the O.T. but their objects were obscured by nothing but the various types of sacrifices: in the N.T. a clearer light of them has shone forth, with the mists of the Levitical shadows dispersed: and thus they are not indeed new sacrifices by reason of the thing, but by reason of a clearer manifestation. For we believe in and invoke the Messiah no longer as about to come,

Jerome explains his translation: Behold, from the labor and you have puffed it away, in this way: You have said, 'We have returned from captivity: we have been prey to enemies: we have labored much on a long journey, we are poor: whatever we could have, has been consumed by the labor of the journey, whatever we have, we offer,' and by saying these things you have puffed away your sacrifices, that is, you have made them worthy of my puffing away: Calvin and Gualtherus in almost the same way, because they complained about labors, and miseries endured, and the difficulty pressing upon them, and expressed their weariness with panting, which is the kind of gesture usually made by those who are exhausted or affected by weariness. Ludov. de Dieu thinks that מהלאתה is put for מה תלאה, for often מה with a maccaph of the first letter of the following word imprints a Dagesch, perhaps as in Jud. XI. 12, ch. XV. 11, and sometimes with the ה cast off, it coalesces with the following word as in Exod. IV. 2, Isa. III. 15, Ezek. XXIX. 6. He wishes the sense of the passage to be this: You complain that you are fatigued by the burden of my precepts, and indeed pressed, because you are bound to offer me nothing but the best and most perfect of cattle; and so you puff away that, and you offer me what is by far the easiest and most corrupt. Regarding the former word, Junius, translating, has the same mind: Behold how much fatigue, when you can puff away that; who explains his sense thus: The words of hypocrites: who, when they were offering to the Lord things that were most trivial, and which could have been dispelled by almost a mere breath, on account of their leanness, nevertheless proclaimed that they were exhausted beyond measure, and had consumed all their effort in the worship of God. The Belgian Paraphrasts followed this explanation. Oecolampadius handed down almost the same sense. But since the Hebrew verb in Hiphil is to breathe, or to expire, or you have made to blow away, Job XI. 20, ch. XXXI. 39. Willius rendered it, behold the fatigued and you have made it to breathe, in this sense: If anyone brings an unblemished animal, you say it is fatigued, and as if it were less suitable on that account, you spare its life for your own profit, and having converted it to your own use, you substituted another defective one in its place. Coccejus rendered it in the contrary sense, and twisted it to Christ, i.e., And you have made him to expire, so that this is to be referred either to the grief and anguish of Christ, or to his death itself, and the words: What is the fatigue? have the sense of contradiction against Christ's invitation in Matt. XI. 28, 29, as if to say: The Israelites ought not to be called from legal worship as if it were tiring, to another rest. But these things are forced. Blessed Luther translated it thus: And you say, Behold it is only weary, and you blow it to the wind. But in the Commentary T. VII. Alt. p. 704. It is read thus: It is only trouble, with this explanation subjoined: That is, We have hardly obtained this bread with great labor, if we had better, we would certainly offer it. And to the words: And blow it to the wind: You have sought a profit: You have sacrificed to yourselves and not to me, and you only put forward your poverty as a pretext. B. Winckelmannus: It is fatigued: Thus the priests excused their sin, saying: That animal is not defective, but only fatigued. You have puffed away. In the Hebrew it is: vehippachthem. Those contemptuous priests seem to have extenuated their sin with a certain gesture of the mouth and by the very breath, just as if they had emitted breath with raised lips: The animal is fatigued, is this matter of such importance? So also the Weimar Paraphrasts, and B. Wigandus: You have puffed away: A Hebraism, You make light of it. And it is a comparison taken from gestures, when something is despised, then a breath is usually emitted. The Belgians note another sense: You have puffed away, that is, you have despised it itself, namely God.

Blessed Balduinus explained it thus: You pretend great labor, as if you were serving God even to the point of exhaustion, when nevertheless your sacred rites are so vile that they could be dissipated like spider webs, even by a breath, without any trouble. We retain the explanation of the former member: Behold how much fatigue! but in the latter, because the Hebrew verb is in Hiphil, you have made to puff away, we render this sense: you boast of labor and fatigue, meanwhile you cause the table of the Lord, or all that worship or that labor of yours, to be puffed away, hissed at, and despised, by your own fault, negligence, and hypocrisy. Not only did they themselves hold the table of the Lord as vile, but they also caused it to be despised and held in contempt by the people. If you prefer to refer it to God, the sense will be: You make it worthy of my puffing away. Thus the sense of the LXX Interpreters. and of the Greeks will agree with the explanation, and Jerome also thought that the Hebrew could be explained in this way: And by saying these things, you have puffed away your sacrifices, that is, you have made them worthy of my puffing away: Or as it can be read in the Hebrew: And you have puffed away me by saying these things, you have done injury not to the sacrifice, but to me to whom you were sacrificing. Furthermore, some refer this rebuke to the people, because the Prophet had previously taxed similar things in the Priests, as Jerome, Remigius, Haymo, Hugo: But since at the beginning of the following chapter he still continues to speak to the Priests, these things are more correctly referred to them as well.

Verse of the same.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

AB ORTU ENIM SOLIS USQVE AD OCCA-SUM MAGNUM EST NOMEN MEUM IN GENTI-BUS) In Hebræo non legitur est. Supplebitur ἐλλειψις re-ctius per erit. Objici poterat : Si nostræ oblationes gratæ tibi non sunt, nullas habebis. Respondet Deus aliud se co-gitare, ut scilicet ab omnibus gentibus colatur, non ope-rose, sed mundo animo. Hoc est consilium quod per Chri-stum ejusque legatos plene exsecutus ex Deus, omnis au-tem dispersio Judæorum inter gentes, illustris in patriam reditus, linguæ Chaldaicæ, Persicæ, Græcæ, Romanæ apud Judæos cognitio, discordes magistrorum sectæ, ri-tuum curæ in anilem superstitionem, fœdos quæstus, & veræ emendationis neglectum versæ, viam huic rei stravere.

IN OMNI LOCO SACRIFICATUR ET OFFER-TUR NOMINI MEO OBLATIO MUNDA) Hic etiam quasi intelligendum ut Zach. XIV. 21. supplevit hunc defectum hoc loco etiam Chaldæus: cætera quoque sic vertas optime: in omni loco offeretur nomini meo quasi suffitus & pura pura: quasi suffitus sunt piæ preces, Apoc. V. 8 μαναὰ vero sunt oblationes fidelium, ex quibus & Eucharistia fiebat, & alebantur pauperes.

QVIA MAGNUM EST NOMEN MEUM IN GENTIBUS) Iterum erit: in gentibus omnibus, non in Judæa, aut inter Judæos tantum.

Mirum, quod Grotius in hoc vaticinio hic & in annot. ad Luc. XXIV. 47. non sequutus fit Iu-dæos, quod in plerisque aliis in ipso observavimus. Illorum tres expositiones occurrunt penes Abar-benelem.

I. Prima Ionathanis, & R. Salomonis, Deum imputare Israelitis orationes in omni loco pro sa-crificio puro, quam rejicit Abarbenel, quia Subje-ctum orationes Israelis non habetur apud Prophe-tam.

II. Altera Aben Ezræ & Kimchij, de gentibus sensu conditionali, offerentur gentibus si illis præceptum esset, ut vobis: sed hic nulla apparet conditio, imo cathegorica habetur prophetia ut è v. 11. & 14. liquet. Ideo nec illam expositionem probat Abarbenel.

„ Tradit autem ipse tertiam, gentes recognoscen- „ tes Deum per causam ortus solis & occasus ejus, „ sacrificium quam purissimum, ut ipsi putant, of- „ ferunt, non quidem mihi, sed nomini meo, qua- „ tenus primæ causæ, opinionem è motu cœle- „ stium corporum conceperunt, eamque colunt „ sub eo nomine, quo à Sapientibus ipsorum no- minatur. Sed hæc ineptissima omnium est. Nam מ hic non causale, sed locale est, quod particula op- posita ועד ET USQVE luculenter docet, nec de causa vel medio cognoscendi Deum, sed de loco ce- lebrationis Dei & oblationum agitur, ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, quod declaratio subjuncta ulte- rius confirmat: ET IN OMNI LOCO hostia offeretur. Conf. Ps. CXIII. 3. Neqne de sacrificio κατὰ δόξαν secundem opinionem gentium tantum pu- ro agitur, sed de puro κατ' ἀλήθειαν, Deoque ipsi probato, cum opponatur reprobatis Sacrificiis à Judaicis Sacerdotibus oblatis v. 10. At hoc ineptum est, quod offerre nomini Dei minus sit, quam offerre Deo, impium vero, nomen Dei haberi quod sapien- tes gentium dixere, quo pacto excusari poterit cul- tus paganus, quemadmodum etiam Abarbenel ex- cusat cultum solis & siderum. Videatur Coccejus in h. l. Fateri autem coactus fuit ipse Abarbenel cum Aben Ezra nationes & populos mundi, seu gentes hic constitui offerentes: de quibus etiam v. 14. Nomen meum erit reverendum in gentibus.

Quum ergo vaticinetur Propheta, nomen Dei „ magnum fore, & reverendum in gentibus, ab or- „ tu solis usque ad Occasum, & in omni loco ob- „latum iri nomini Dei mundum Sacrificium, quo- modo negare possunt Judæi, nisi palam refragari velint Prophetæ, gentium conversionem prædici, ac ceremonialem cultum tolli. Hic enim non celebrari poterat in omni loco, sed in loco quem Deus ele- gerat Deut. XII. 5.6. Nec obscure indicat Prophe- ta, id futurum eo tempore, qua adhuc Sacerdotes profanabant nomen Domini, scil. in templo secundo vers. 13. idque prope esse. Conf. Mal. III. 4. 5. Es. XIX. 19. 21. Joh. IV. 23. 24. Et minatur hic simul Prophe- ta desertionem Iudæorum. Non enim simplex est va- ticinium de vocatione gentium, sed Deus Judæis abjectis, alios cultores se substituere velle, testa- tur, quod particula causalis docet: non suscipiam „munus de manu vestra, nam ab ortu solis usque „ad occasum magnum erit nomen meum. Conf. „Hos. I. 9. Matth. XXI. 13. Deinceps oblationem, „inquit Cyrillus, juxta cultum legalem manifeste „repudiat, & propemodum à charitate erga Ju- „dæos discedit, & à sacerdotio abhorret, & um- „bram non admittit, boum immolationes, & ni- „dores, inquam: quoniam neque à principio hic „illi scopus.

Reprobanda itaque Hugonis glossa de oblatio- nibus, quas gentes proselytæ ex omni loco in templo Hie- rosolymitano obtulere. Non enim Propheta de gen- tibus ex omni loco Hierosolymis oblaturis, sed de gentibus loquitur IN OMNI oblaturis loco, ab ortu solis usq́; ad occasum. Intelliguntur autem Sacrificia Spiritualia Nov. T. qualia sunt (1) prædi- catio Evangelii de Christo crucifixo, qua comme- moratur Sacrificium in cruce peractum Rom. XV. 16. (2) Sacrificium fidei, cum suscipitur Evange- lium de Christo, vel Christus pro nobis oblatus, Deo- que sistitur vera fide. Fides enim in Christum est sacrificium & cultus Deo gratus Phil. II. 12. immo- lor super Sacrificio & obsequio fidei vestræ (3) Sacrifi- cium contriti cordis Ps. LI. 19. (4) Consecratio nostri in obsequium Christi, qua corpora nostra hostiam vi- ventem, sanctam, Deo placentem sistimus Rom. XII. 1. (5) Sacrificium patientiæ & promtitudinis vitam pro gloria Christi impendendi 2. Tim. IV. 6. (6) Sacrificium gratitudinis erga ministerium Phil. IV. 18. & amoris misericordiæ erga proximum Hos. VI. atque beneficentiæ imprimis erga pauperes Ebr. XIII. 16. (7) Sacrificium precum & orationum Psal. CXLI. 2. Ap. IIX. & laudum, ac confessionis Ebr. XIII. 7. Quæ vere sunt munda, ac Deo placentia sa- crificia, quia & nos, & opera nostra Deo sunt pro- pter Christum grata. vid. paraphrasis Osiandrina in h. l. de quo Cyrillus: Aperte igitur Sacerdotibus „legis dixit, se ipsos nolle: vel potius, se in ipsis vo- „luntatem non habere, in umbra nempe & figuris „sacrificantibus, eorumque Sacra non susceptu- „rum. Prænunciat autem fore magnum & illustre „nomen suum apud omnes toto orbe mortales, & „in omni loco, ac gente sacrificium mundum & „incruentum nomini suo oblatum iri, non jam sa- „cerdotibus illis ejus dignitatem obscurantibus, „neque incuriose spiritualem cultum ei offerenti- „bus, sed cum diligentia & bonitate & sanctimo- „nia incensorum Spiritualium suaveolentiam of- „ferre satagentibus, fidem scilicet, spem, charita- „tem, & honestamenta bonorum operum, ita con- „stituto scilicet Christi sacrificio cœlesti ac vivifi- „co, per quod destructa est mors, & caro ista ter- „rena & corruptioni obnoxia incorruptionem in- „duitur. Et Hieronym. Ad sacerdotes Judæorum „sermo sit domini. Qui offerunt cæcum & clau- „dum & languidum ad immolandum: ut sciant „carnalibus victimis spirituales victimas successu- „ras. Et nequaquam taurorum hircorumque san- „guinem: sed Thymiama, hoc est, sanctorum ora- „tiones Domino offerendas, & non in una orbis „provincia Judæa, nec in una Judææ urbe Hieru- „falem: sed in omni loco offerri oblationem ne- „quaquam immundam, ut à populo Israel: sed „mundam, ut in ceremoniis Christianorum. Theo- „doretus item: Funditus vos rejiciam, nam permul- „tum detestor vestra facta & victimas quas offer- „tis, execror, quarum loco universum orbem ter- „rarum me summa religione colentem habeo. „Nam omnium habitatores terrarum, quas Sol „exoriens & occidens suis radiis illustrat, cum u- „bique incensum offerent, tum etiam sacrum „purum & mihi gratum conficient. Cognoscent „enim nomen meum & voluntatem & debitum „honorem præstabunt, &, accommodatum cul- „turn adhibebunt. Adde & Eusebium l. I. demon- „str. Evangel. c. VI. p. 9. Malachias autem simul, & ad eos qui ex circumcisione sunt, sermonem diri- git, & de gentibus talia prædicit: Non est voluntas mea, dicit Dominus omnipotens, & sacrificium non suscipiam de manibus vestris, quoniam ab or- tu usq; ad occasum nomen meum glorificatum est in gentibus, & in omni loco incensum offertur no- mini meo, & sacrificium mundum. Quod enim in o- mni loco dicit, incensum & sacrificium offerri Deo, quid aliud significat, nisi non Hierosolymis, neq; defini- te in hoc aut in illo loco futurum? sed in omni regione & in omnibus gentibus, quæ quidem & orationis in- censum & sacrificium, quod mundum dictum est, non per cruores sed per pias actiones summo Deo essent ob- laturæ. Et cap. X. Hæc igitur omnia, quæ ab initio di- vinitus prædicta sunt, in præsenti tempore per Evan- gelicam salvatoris nostri doctrinam ab omnibus genti- bus celebrantur, Propheticæ voci test. afferente verita- te, per quam vocem Deus Mosaicis rejectis sacrifi- ciis, quod futurum erat nostrum ipsorum institutum, divinitus nuntiat, dicens: Quoniam ab ortu solis usq; ad Occasum, nomen meum glorificatum est in gentibus, & in omni loco incensum offertur nomini meo & ho- stia munda. Sacrificamus igitur Deo altissimo sacri- ficium laudis: sacrificamus Deo plenum, & hor- rorem afferens, & sacrosanctum sacrificium: sacrifi- „camus novo more, secundum N. Test. hostiam „mundam. At sacrificium Deo, spiritus contritus „dictusesst: cor igitur contritum & humiliatum „Deus non despiciet. Jamque etiam incendimus „Propheticum illum odorem in omni loco, & of- „ferimus ei bene olentem fructum omni virtute „abundantis Theologiæ, hoc ipsum orationibus ad „eum directis facientes. Quod sane ipsum, alius „quoque docet Propheta, qui ait: Fiat oratio mea „sicut incensum in conspectu tuo. Igitur & sacrifi- „camus & incendimus, alias quidem memoriam „magni illius sacrificii, secundum ea, quæ ab ipso „tradita sunt, mysteria celebrantes, & gratias Deo „pro salute nostra agentes, religiososque hymnos „& orationes sanctas illi offerentes, alias nos ipsos „totos consecrantes, ejusque Pontifici ipsi utique „verbo corpore animoque dicantes. Proinde ab „omni obscoenitate corpus intactum, atque imma- „culatum eidem conservare studemus, omnique „affectu, atque omni foeditate, quæ à malitia pro- „ficiscatur, purgatam mentem illi reddimus, co- „gitationibusque sinceris & affectione non ficta „veritatisque decretis illum colimus. Grata e- „nim illi hæc esse magis, quam hostiarum magnum „numerum, quarum sanguine & fumo, & nidore „operemur, edocti sumus. B. Lutherus T. VII. Altenb. p. 204. per Mincha verbum vel præconium Evangelii, per suffimentum preces intelligit. Was diß für ein Opfer sey, zeiget

Paulus an Rom. XV. da er spricht: daß Jch soll seyn ein Diener Christi unter die Heyden, zu opfern das Evangelium Gottes, auff daß die Heyden ein Opfer werden 2c. Damit er anzeiget, daß er durch das Evangelium, als durch ein Priesterlich Instrument, die Heyden geopfert habe: Das ist, er hat sie GOtt übergeben, und geopfert, gereini- get von Sünden, und an Leib und Fleisch getöd- tet. Denn durch das Evangelium werden die alten Jrrthümer vertilget, und wird im Hertzen die Warheit erwecket, welche GOtt bekennet, an jhn gläubet, jhn locket, und das Fleisch lezlich tödtet.

Das Räuchwerck und die Speiß-Opfer waren die fürnemsten Opfer bey den Jüden, wel- che sie als die besten gehalten haben, zum Gottes- dienst in allen Thälern, und bey allen grünen Bäumen. Für das Rauchwerck verstehen wir das Gebett. So sind nun das Wort und Gebett zwey Opfer der Christen. Das Gebett der Chri- sten soll mit Dancksagung und Lobe geschehen. Der Christen Opfer sind rein, denn sie sind ohne Schuld, abgewaschen mit dem Blut Christi 2c. Ungläubige können nicht opfern, und Christen opf- fern nicht lame, schwache, blinde Opfer, sondern mit Glauben und Danckbarkeit. Wenn das Hertz gläubig ist, so wird die Sünde nicht zugerechnet.

Temere itaque hoc vaticinium arripitur à Pa- pistis ad sacrificium missæ, quod commenti sunt, pro- pitiatorium, quod tamen eo pertrahere ausus non fuit Grotius hoc loco, etsi, ne deesse ipsis plane vi- deretur, ad oblationes in Eucharistia restringat vo- cem Mincha, quæ vero omnem oblationem spiritua- lem Deo gratam à gentibus Deo dedicandam com- plectitur, nec ad agapas in Eucharistia restringi potest. Hæ enim nec solæ, nec præcipue sunt spi- rituales victimæ in N. T. Bellarm. l. I. de miss. c. X. disputat Prophetam non loqui de sacrificiis spirituali- bus, sed de vero externo sacrificio, quod veteribus in N. T. successit, quale nullum esse aliud, quam sacrifi- cium Missaticum dicit. Quod vero impium & sacri- legum est. Habemus enim sacrificium propitiato- rium unicum, Christum Iesum Ebr. IX. 14. cap. X. 11. Hos. II. 2. cui aliud addere in N. T. propitiatorium summæ impietatis, Missaticum autem illius loco supponere, & pro unico sacrificio N.T. venditare, extremi sacrilegii est. Contendit & Cornel. à La- pide, imo de fide esse vult hanc oblationem mundam esse sacrificium corporis & sanguinis Christi in Eucha- ristia, sed argumentis levissimis. Dicit (1) vocem Mincha appropriatam esse uni sacrificio farreo Lev. II. quod typus erat sacrificii Eucharistici: Resp. vo- cem illam generatim notare sacrificium, & de ele- vatione manuum absolute adhiberi Ps. CXLI. vid. Sanctius in h. l. & Psal. XCVI. 8. (vid. Bellarm. & Ioh. Bapt. Folengius in h. l.) nec non de sacrificiis spi- ritualibus N. T. Es. LXVI. 20. neque sacrificio Mis- sæ convenire, nisi dicendum sit, in sacrificio Missæ non nisi panam offerri Deo, imo ad Mincham proprie dictam requiritur oleum, thus, sal, adolitio, concrema- tio Lev. II. quæ hic locum non habent, estque con- tra naturam Minchæ, destitui substantia terrena, conjungi vini specieei. Nec farreum sacrificium typus fuit sacrificii Christi, sed Christianorum, multo mi- nus sacrificii incruenti in Eucharistia, quod scri- ptura plane non agnoscit. Dicit (2) solam Eucha- ristiam esse mundam, sed non de Eucharistia quæri- tur, verum de sacrificio Eucharistico, & quamvis spiritualia nostra sacrificia valde imperfecta & im- munda sint, si ex se spectentur, munda tamen & Deo grata sunt, quia fiunt ab iis, quorum corda fide justi- ficata sunt Act. XV. 9. & offeruntur per Christum, in quo omnia sunt munda 1. Pet. II. 3. Ebr. XIII. 16. Di- cunt cit (3) Malachiam loqui solis sacerdotibus Aaronitis, eorumque mensæ & victimis opponere sacerdotes, altaria, & victimas, quæ quia proprie in veteri lege fuere, & sub nova lege propria esse debeant. Resp. Opponit sacerdotes Novi Test. Prophetasacerdotibus V. T. & eos facit omnes gentes sacrificia spiritualia offerentes. Porro : si omnia sub N. T. propria esse debeant, quæ proprie fuere sub veteri, totus cultus Leviticus revocandus erit. In V. T. proprie fiebat mactatio, proprie fiebat incensio, proprie consumtio, num ergo mactandæ, num incendendæ, num consumendæ victimæ in N. Test.? Falsum est, quod supponit Corn. Lapideus naturam dictare Deum colendum esse sacrificio externo. Sacrificia sunt juris non naturæ, sed divini positivi, nec in natura instituta locum habebant, sed destituta, & ad figurandum Sacrificium unicum propitiatorium in ara crucis offerendum, divinitus instituta sunt, nec nisi per κακοζηλίαν & Diabolicas illusiones ad gentes traducta. Dicit (4) מקטר esse adoleri, suffumigare, cremari, non autem orationem incendi, aut cremari; sed victimam proprie dictam. Resp. ita nec missatico sacrificio conveniret, quia nec illud incenditur aut crematur : Quod autem transsubstantietur, ut papistæ nugantur, & manducetur, id neque ad incensionem, neq; ad cremationem, neque ad consumptionem proprie dictam probandam facit: Unde nec ipsi Papistæ convenire de eo potuere hactenus, in quonam formalis ratio hujus fictitii sacrificii consistat. Oratio autem recte dicitur מקטר vel suffimentum ex formula Spirit. S. Ps. CXLI. 2. statuatur oratio mea ut suffitus coram te. Ita & Ap. V. 8. c. VIII. 34. suffitus precum nominantur. Dicit (5) nullum sacrificium esse quod ubivis gentium offeratur, ut sacrificium Eucharisticum. Resp. sacrificia spiritualia ubivis offeruntur, Ioh. IV. 22. 1. Tim. II. 8. non item sacrificium Missaticum, quod ipsum offerri volunt in altari consecrato : imo sacrificium ἱλασικὸν non nisi eo loco offerri poterat, in quo & danda pax per illud Hagg. II. 10. non vero omni in loco. Eucharistia vero, quamvis celebretur ubivis, non potest haberi pro sacrificio proprie dicto eoque propitiatorio, quia id nullum est sine effusione sanguinis, tametsi in Eucharistia instituatur commemoratio sacrificii Christi propitiatorii, ut & oratio & agaparum collatio; sunt spiritualia sacrificia, quorum causa ad Eucharistiam applicatur vaticinium propheticum ab Irenæo l. IV. c. XXXII. & Eusebio l. I. Demonstr. c. VI. Tertull. l. III. c. Marc. c. XXII. l. IV. c. I. in libr. adv. Jud. Neque Hieron. vel etiam Theodore-tus favet papistis, ut e verbis ipsorum antea adductis manifestum. Ad illos ergo frustra provocavit Cornelius, Justinus etiam Dial. cum Tryph. nec non August. Ep. CXX. & l. X. de Civ. Dei c. VI. ut & Chrysost. hom. XVII. in Ep. ad Ebr. a nostris stat partibus, Clementis Roman. Constitutiones supposititiæ sunt; Recentiorum autoritatem non moramur. De cæteris vero testimoniis, quæ in eam rem consarcinant Papistæ, hujus loci non est dispicere. Agunt de illis & nostri, & Reformati, ubi ex professo Idolum Missaticum configunt. In rebus fidei solius Scripturæ S. autoritas est αὐτὸς ἔφη.

Bellarminus id urget, quod hic agatur de sacrificio novo. Sacrificia vero spiritualia etiam in V. T. usitata fuerint, cui respondit jam B. Balduinus : Fuerunt Sacrificia spiritualia preces, laudes, fides &c. etiam in V. T. sed objecta eorum, non nisi variis Sacrificiorum typis obscurata : in N. T. clarior illorum lux effulsit, discussis umbrarum Leviticarum nebulis : atque sic non quidem ratione rei nova sint sacrificia, sed ratione clarioris manifestationis. Credimus enim & invocamus Messiam non amplius futurum,

Hieronymus translationem suam: Ecce de labo- „ re & exsufflastis illud, ita explicat: Dixistis de „ captivitate reversi sumus: hostibus prædæ fui- „ mus: multum in longo itinere laboravimus, pau- „ peres sumus: quicquid habere potuimus, viæ la- „ bore consumtum est, qualiacunque habemus, „ offerimus, & hæc dicendo exsufflastis vestra sa- „ crificia id est exsufflatione mea digna fecistis: Eo- dem fere modo Calvinus & Gualtherus, quod de laboribus conquesti fuerint, & miseriis exantlatis, & difficultate illis incumbente, ac anhelatione tœ- dium suum expresserint, qualis gestus defatigato- rum, aut tædio affectorum esse solet. Ludov. de Dieu, מהלאתה pro מה תלאה positum censet, sæpe enim מה cum maccaph primæ sequentis dictionis literæ imprimere Dagesch forte ut Jud XI. 12. cap. XV. 11. & interdum abjecto ה coalescere cum se- quenti dictione ut Exod. IV. 2. Esa. III. 15. Ezech. HX. 6. Sensum autem loci hunc esse vult: Vos con- „ querimini fatigari vos onere meorum præcepto- „ rum, & nimirum premi, quod non nisi optimas pecudum atque integerrimas, mihi offerre tenea- mini; itaque exsufflatis illud, & quod longe est fa- cillimum corruptissimum quodque mihi offertis. De priori voce eadem mens Junio vertenti: Ecce quantum defatigationis, quum exsufflare possitis illud: qui sensum suum sic exponit: Hypocritarum verba: qui cum res levissimas, & quæ solo prope- modum flatu dispelli potuissent, præ macie, offe- rebant Domino, prædicabant tamen se supra mo- dum defessos esse, & omnem suam operam in cultu Dei consumsisse. Quam explicationem sequuti sunt Paraph. Belgici. Eundem propemodum sensum tradidit Oecolampadius. Sed quum verbum Ebræum in Hiphil sit spirare, vel exspirare, aut difflare feci- stis Job. XI. 20. cap. XXXI. 39. Willius reddidit, ec- ce defatigatum & spirare fecistis illud, hoc sensu: „ Si quis affert pecus integrum, dicitis illud esse „ defatigatum, ac quasi minus propterea aptum „ esset, vitæ ejus vestro emolumento parcitis, illo- „ que in usum vestrum converso, ejus loco aliud „ vitiosum substituistis. Coccejus sensu contrario reddidit, & ad Christum detorsit, h. m. Et exspira- re eum fecistis, ut referendum hoc sit vel ad λύπην & ἀδημονίαν Chrsti, vel ad ipsam mortem, & ver- ba: Quid est defatigatio? sensum habeant contra- dictionis adversus Christi invitationem Matth. XI. „ 28 29. q. d. Non debent Israelitæ à cultu legali „ tanquam lassante, ad aliam requiem vocari. Sed hæc coacta sunt. Beat. Lutherus ita transtulit: Und Ihr sprecht, Siehe es ist nur müde, und schlagets in den Wind. In Commentario vero T. VII. Alt. p. 704. Sic legitur: Es ist nur Mühe, subjuncta hac ex- plicatione: Das ist, Wir haben mit grosser Arbeit diese Brodt kaum bekommen, hätten wir bessere, wolten wir sie ja auch opffern. Et ad verba: Und schlagets in den Wind: Ihr habet einen Nutz ge- sucht: Euch und nicht mir geopffert, und wendet nur zum Schein euer Armuth für. B. Winckelmannus: Defatigatum est: Ita Sacerdotes excusabant pecca- tum suum, dicentes: Pecus ista non est vitiosa, sed „ tantum defatigata. Exsufflastis. In Hebræo est: vehippachthem. Videntur Sacerdotes isti contem- ptores, gestu quodam oris & ipso Spiritu extenuas- se peccatum suum, perinde ac si elatis labiis spiri- tum emiserint: Defatigata est pecus, anne hæc res tanti momenti est? Sic etiam Vinarienses Para- phrastæ, & B. Wigandus: Exsufflastis: Hebrais- mus, Vos flocci facitis. Estque comparatio à gesti- bus sumta, quando aliquid contemnitur, tum solet emitti spiritus. Sensum alium notant Belgici: E- efflastis, id est contemptistis ipsum, nempe Deum

B. Balduinus ita exposuit: Vos prætenditis magnum laborem, quasi ad defatigationem usque Deo ser- viatis, cum tamen sacra vestra tam vilia sint, ut in- star telarum araneæ vel flatu dissipari possint, abs- que ullo negotio. Prioris membri explicationem retinemus: Ecce quanta defatigatio! in posteriori vero, quia verbum Ebræum in Hiphil est, exsufflare fecistis hunc sensum reddimus: laborem & defatiga- tionem jactitatis, interim facitis ut exsuffletur, exsi- biletur, ac despiciatur mensa Domini, vel omnis ille cultus aut labor iste vester, vestra culpa, negligentia, & hypocrisi. Non tantum ipsi vilem habebant men- sam Domini, sed efficiebant etiam, ut à populo contemneretur & despicatui haberetur. Si ad Deum referre malis, sensus erit: Exsufflatione mea dignum id facitis. Sic sensus LXX. Interpp. & Græcorum conveniet explicationi, atque ita etiam censuit Hieronymus explicari posse Ebræa: Et hæc dicendo, exsufflastis vestra sacrificia, id est, exsufflatione mea digna fecistis: Sive ut in Hebræo legi potest: Et exsuf- flastis me hæc dicendo, non sacrificio, sed mihi cui sacrificabatis, fecistis injuriam. Cæterum referunt nonnulli hanc reprehensionem ad populum, quia prius similia in Sacerdotibus taxaverat Propheta, ut Hieron. Remig. Haymo, Hugo: Sed quum initio capitis sequentis adhuc pergat loqui Sacerdotibus, rectius hæc etiam ad eosdem referuntur.

Vers. eod.

## 1:13
AND YOU HAVE BROUGHT OF RAPINE) You bring what is snatched into the Temple: That is, prey, which it was not lawful even to eat, much less to offer. Exod. XXIII. 31.

Others understand offerings of rapine, because they offered what had been snatched from their neighbor by force and against justice, as if to say: You say that you have obtained these sacrifices, such as they are, from your own labor: you lie, for you have prepared them from rapine, as Cornel. à Lap. has it, or you say, you expend great labor on my worship, but in reality you make yourselves and your labors worthy of being puffed away, because you offer sacrifices without discrimination or just discussion, even if they are of rapine, lame or languid.

Latin:

ET INTULISTIS DE RAPINIS) Raptum infertis in Templum: Id est θηριάλωτον, quod nec edere licebat, multo minus offerre. Exod. XXIII. 31.

Alii Oblationes de rapinis intelligunt, quod ob- tulerint, quod vi & contra justitiam proximo ere- ptum fuerit, q. d. Dicitis vos ex labore vestro has ho- stias quales quales comparasse: mentimini, nam ex ra- pinis parastis, ut Cornel. à Lap. habet, vel dicitis, ma- gnum laborem vos impendere cultui meo, sed facitis revera vos & labores vestros exsufflatione dignos, quia sine discrimine aut justa discussione offertis sacrificia, etiamsi de rapinis, clauda vel languida sint.

## 1:14
Verse 14.

CURSED IS THE DECEITFUL ONE) Just as he had rebuked the Priests, who were not offering approved things in the constant Sacrifice, so now he also rebukes those guilty of a vow, who were discharging their duty with diseased or defective victims. The Law on the contrary commanded that the victim should be both male, and without defect or disease, Levit. 19, 20.

AND MAKING A VOW) And a vow having been made.

SACRIFICES THE WEAK) Corrupt, that is, diseased, or defective, or female.

AND MY NAME TERRIBLE AMONG THE GENTILES) Even among the gentiles.

Some refer this to the gentiles, to whom God had shown himself to be feared through various miracles and punishments, and had rendered his name illustrious: but Cyprian, book II, Testimonies against the Jews, chapter XXIX, Theodoret, Vatablus, and Cocceius indicate that this is to be fulfilled in the time of the New Testament, when all nations would fear God: My name (shall be) נורא to be revered, to be dreaded, venerable among the gentiles; thus the LXX version agrees, επιφανὲς illustrious. For this is not referred to hatred and detestation, but pertains to the fear, worship, and religion of God. He looks back to verse 6, Where is my fear, and at the same time illustrates verse 11. This was true, says Cornelius à Lapide, in the time of Malachi and the Maccabees, whose heavenly victories made God illustrious and formidable to all nations throughout the whole world; it is more truly so in Christ and Christians: for all nations celebrate Christ, and his God the Father.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

MALEDICTUS DOLOSUS) Sicut Sacerdotes re- prehenderat, qui in jugi Sacro non proba offerebant, ita nunc & voti reos reprehendit, qui victimis morbidis aut vitiosis defungebantur. Lex contra jubebat ut & victima esset mascula, & sine vitio morboque, Levit. 19, 20.

ET VOTUM FACIENS) Et voto facto.

IMMOLAT DEBILE) Corruptum, id est morbi- dum, aut vitiosum, aut femininum.

ET NOMEN MEUM HORRIBILE IN GEN- TIBUS) Etiam inter gentes.

Ad gentes referunt nonnulli, quibus per varia prodigia & supplicia timendum se præbuerat Deus, nomenque suum illustre reddiderat: Cyprianus ve- rol. II. Testimon. advers. Jud. cap. XXIX. Theodo- retus, Vatablus & Coccejus tempore N. T. hoc in- plendum indicant, quo omnes gentes Deum time- bant: Nomen meum (erit) נורא reverendum, tremen- dum, venerabile inter gentes, ita congruit LXX. ver- sio επιφανὲς illustre. Hoc enim non ad odium & detestationem refertur, sed ad Dei timorem, cul- tum & religionem pertinet. Respicit v. 6. Ubi est timor meus, ac simul illustrat vers. 11. Hoc verum fuit, ait Cornel. à Lap. tempore Malachiæ & Mac- cabæorum, quorum victoriæ cœlestes Deum toto orbe cunctis gentibus illustrem & formidabilem fecerunt, verius est in Christo & Christianis: omnes enim gentes celebrant Chri- stum, ejusque Deum Patrem.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. Repeated rebuke of the priests and the people.

A curse is denounced against the contumacious priests and the rejection of their festivals, with the covenant entered into with Levi and the office of the priests violated by them, and their disgrace being set forth. To the people, however, are reproached marriages with Gentiles, polygamy, and unlawful divorces from their spouses, and the divine vengeance quickly brought about, the example of Abraham being neglected.

The punishment of the ministry and of the violated marriage bed.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Reprehensio Sacerdotum & populi iterata.

Sacerdotibus contumacibus maledictio & fe- stilitatum ipsorum reprobatio denunciatur, proposito fœdere cum Levi inito & Sacer- dotum officio ab ipsis violato, eorumque opprobrio. Populo vero exprobrantur con- jugia cum gentilibus, polygamia & divor- tia à conjugibus illicita, neglecto exemplo Abrahami propere habita divina vin- dicta.

Pœna ministerii comes & thalami violati.

## 2:2
Ver. 2.

AND IF YOU WILL NOT LAY IT TO HEART.) To turn the mind to warnings.

THAT YOU MAY GIVE GLORY TO MY NAME.) That you may treat me with due honor.

I WILL SEND UPON YOU WANT) He explained the metonymy well: for in the Hebrew it is a curse.

AND I WILL CURSE YOUR BLESSINGS.) It was the duty of the priests to pray well for the people: But God says that He will bring it about that these auspicious prayers have the outcome of curses. Thus the Chaldean.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET SI NOLVERITIS PONERE PVPER COR.) Animum advertere monitis.

VT DETIS GLORIAM NOMINI MEO.) Ut debito honore me afficiatis.

MITTAM IN VVS EGESTATEM) Bene expli- cavit μετωνυμίαν: in Hebræo enim est exfecrationem.

ET MALEDICAM BENEDICTIONIBVS VE- STRIS.) Sacerdotum erat bene precari populo: At Deus dicit se effecturum ut hæ faustæ preces dirarum eventum habeant. Ita Chaldæus.

## 2:3
Ver. 3.

BEHOLD I WILL CAST THE ARM TO YOU.) He reads as the Greeks זרע with a Holem before the Ajin: our books have it with a patach before the Ajin. זרע, that is seed: but the Greek sense is best. The shoulder of the victim fell to the priests by the law, Leviticus 7:32, Deuteronomy 18:3. I will cast it, namely, into your faces, as follows. This is what those are accustomed to do who indignantly grant something to an importunate beggar, as if saying: lo, have what you want.

The Greek and Latin text is wrongly preferred to the Hebrew. The best sense is in the source: Behold I will corrupt the seed for you. The word גער is properly to rebuke, and it is used of verbal and real rebuke. see Psalm 9:6. Some refer it to the corruption of the seed. Others not inappropriately wish God to portend a curse not only to them, but also to their posterity. To which the version of B. Luther, the paraphrase of Osiander and the Vinarienses, Winckelm. in his commentary, etc., tend. The Tigurine version in this manner: "I will rebuke and by rebuking I will destroy the seed for you, I will destroy you with your seed, that is, your children."

Verse of the same.

AND I WILL SPREAD UPON YOUR FACES DUNG.) He could have said belly, but he preferred to say dung more ignominiously, which is accustomed to adhere to the belly.

OF YOUR SOLEMNITIES.) Of your victims: for חגים are called not only feast days, but also the victims themselves, Psalm 118:27, Isaiah 29:1.

AND HE WILL TAKE YOU WITH HIM.) That is, so that you may be cast out of the Temple as foul-smelling by the soldiers of Antiochus.

These things are forced concerning the belly instead of dung, even though the belly occurs in the LXX. The sense is plain, which Osiander rendered: And I will spread; more correctly, I will sprinkle dung upon your faces of your solemnities, and he will take you with him: more correctly, and it will adhere to you: I will confound you, so that you may be a mockery to others, just as if someone is defiled by dung sprinkled on his face. You seek the multitude rather than the excellence of sacrifices: I will therefore cause that the dung which is purged from the intestines of the victims on feast days (when sacrifices are offered more frequently) be thrown into your faces: that is, I will render you despised, on account of your avarice and your remaining impiety.

Coccejus wishes these to have been fulfilled when the Temple and the polity of the Jews were destroyed, or he thinks that the great famine in the days of Claudius predicted by Agabus, Acts 11:28, is pointed out in their most recent total destruction, but these are too remote, nor do they fit this prophecy.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ECCE EGO PROJICIAM VOBIS BRACHIVM.) Legit ut Græci זרע cum Holem ante Ajin: nostri libri ha- bent cum patach ante Ajin. זרע, id est semen: sed sensus Græcus est optimus. Sacerdotibus ex lege cedebat armus victimæ & ventriculus Levit. 7, 32. Deuteron. 18, 3. Projiciam nempe in facies vestras, ut sequitur. Hoc so- lent facere, qui importuno flagitatori aliquid indigna- bundi concedunt, quasi dicentes: en habe, quod vis.

Male præfertur Græcus & Latinus textus E- bræo. Sensus optimus est in fonte: Ecce ego corrumpam vobis semen. Verbum גער proprie est increpare, ac de verbali & reali increpatione adhibetur. vid. Psal. 9, 6. Referunt id nonnulli ad Sementis corruptionem. Alii non incommode Deum volunt ominari maledictionem non tantum ipsis, sed etiam posteritati ipsorum. Quo abit B. Lutheri versio, Osiandri & Vinariens. paraphrasis, Winckelm. in comment. &c. Tigurina h. m. in- „ crepabo & increpando disperdam vobis semen, „ disperdam vos cum semine, id est, filiis vestris.

Vers. eod.

ET DISPERGAM SVPER VVLTVM VE- STRVM STERCVS.) Potuit dicere ventriculum, sed maluit ignominiosius dicere stercus, quod adhærescere ventriculo solet.

SOLENNITATVM VESTRARVM.) Victimarum vestrarum: nam חגים vocantur non tantum festi dies, sed & victimæ ipsæ Psalm. 118, 27. Es. 29, 1.

ET ASSVMET VOS SECUM.) Id est, ut tan- quam fœtidi ejiciamini è Templo per Antiochi milites.

Hæc de ventriculo pro stercore coacta sunt, etsi apud LXX. ventriculus occurrat. Sensus planus est, quem reddidit Osiander: Et dispergam; re- ctius, aspergam super vultum vestrum stercus so- lennitatum vestrarum, & affumet vos secum: re- ctius & adhærebit vobis: ego vos confundam, ut aliis ludibrio sitis, perinde ac si quis stercore in fa- ciem consperso fœdatur. Vos multitudinem po- tius, quam præstantiam sacrificiorum quæritis: ef- ficiam igitur, ut fimus qui diebus festis (quando sacrificia frequentiora offeruntur) ex intestinis ho- stiarum expurgatur, vobis in faciem conjiciatur: h.e. contemptos vos reddam, propter avaritiam & reliquam vestram impietatem.

Coccejus hæc impleta esse vult, cum Tem- plum & politia Judæorum exscinderetur, vel in no- vissima ipsorum πανωλεθρίᾳ & famem magnam in diebus Claudii ab Agabo Act. XI. 28. prædictam indigitari putat, sed hæc nimis remota sunt, nec huic vaticinio quadrant.

## 2:4
Verse 4.

AND YOU SHALL KNOW THAT I HAVE SENT THIS COMMANDMENT UNTO YOU.) Know that I have sent this commandment unto you, through my Prophet.

THAT MY COVENANT MIGHT BE WITH LEVI.) Because my covenant is with Levi. I summon you by the covenant, not only that common one which I made with the people, but a proper and peculiar one, which I made with the priests and Levites. Numbers 8:14, 18:19.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET SCIETIS QVIA MISI AD VOS MANDA- TVM ISTVD.) Scitote misisse me hoc mandatum ad vos, per Prophetam meum.

UT ESSET PACTVM MEVM CVM LEVI.) Quia pactum meum est cum Levi. Ex pacto vos convenio, non illo tantum communi, quod cum populo feci, sed pro- prio ac peculiari, quod cum sacerdotibus ac Levitis. Num. 8, 14. 18, 19.

## 2:5
Verse 5.

MY COVENANT WAS WITH HIM OF LIFE AND PEACE.) With Phinehas, and those succeeding him in the priesthood, Numbers 25:13, for this discourse is directed peculiarly to the priests. I promised all things happy to them if they did what was commanded.

AND I GAVE HIM FEAR.) That is, the priestly law: by whose prescription he might fear me, that is, revere me.

AND HE FEARED ME) He performed the duty of Phinehas and many after him.

AND AT THE FACE OF MY NAME HE WAS AFRAID.) They approached sacred things with great reverence.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PACTUM MEVM FVIT CVM EO VITÆ ET PACIS.) Cum Phinea, & ei successuris in sacerdo- tium, Num. 25, 13. nam sermo hic peculiariter ad sacerdo- tes dirigitur. Omnia ipsis felicia promisi si imperata fa- cerent.

ET DEDI EI TIMOREM.) Id est, legem sa- cerdotalem: ex cujus præscripto me timeret, id est, co- leret.

ET TIMVIT ME) Præstitit officium Phinees & multi post eum.

ET A FACIE NOMINIS MEI PAVEBAT.) Magna cum religione accedebant ad sacra.

## 2:6
Ver. 6.

THE LAW OF TRUTH WAS IN HIS MOUTH.) They taught the people things consistent with the law.

AND INIQUITY WAS NOT FOUND IN HIS LIPS.) They did not invent anything for their own gain.

IN PEACE AND EQUITY HE WALKED WITH ME.) In the Hebrew: In peace and uprightness: that is, he retained my friendship by doing what is right.

AND HE TURNED MANY AWAY FROM INIQUITY.) By pious admonitions.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

LEX VERITATIS FVIT IN ORE EJVS.) Do- cebant populum legi congruentia.

ET INIQVITAS NON EST INVENTA IN LABIIS EJVS.) Nihil ad suum quæstum comminisce- bantur.

IN PACE ET ÆQVITATE AMBVLAVIT ME- CVM.) In Hebræo: In pace & rectitudine: id est, ami- citiam meam retinuit, recta agendo.

ET MVLTOS AVERTIT AB INIQVITATE.) Piis monitis.

## 2:7
Ver. 7.

FOR THE LIPS OF THE PRIEST SHALL KEEP HIS KNOWLEDGE;) They used to keep. Of the priest, that is, the high priest, who had succeeded Phinehas.

AND THEY SHALL SEEK THE LAW FROM HIS MOUTH.) The Hebrews used to seek from him the meaning of the law. Levit. 10, 10. Ezech. 44, 23.

BECAUSE HE IS THE ANGEL OF THE LORD OF HOSTS.) He was. Angels carry the prayers of men to God, and the commands of God to men. The high priest did the same under the law, who once a year made atonement for the people Lev. 16, 1. and who was consulted regarding controversies that arose concerning the meaning of the law Deut. 17, 9. The Bishop fills his place in the Christian Church, called an Angel for that very reason in the Apocalypse. Diodorus Siculus concerning the Jews in Photius: ἀρχιερέα δὲ τὸν προσαγορεύουσι, καὶ νομίζουσιν αὐτοῖς ἄγγελον γενέσθαι τῶν τοῦ θεῶ προσαγμάτων.

Most others more correctly take these as a general statement concerning the office and decorum of priests. For it is their duty to know the law and to teach it to others. Moreover, he says that the lips will guard his knowledge, because the mouth of the priest is a certain ark, in which the heavenly deposit is guarded. Papists make a divine promise out of this rule, as if priests could not err in the business of religion: But what the Prophet adds teaches clearly; that it is indicated not what kind of priests they are, but what kind they ought to be. Furthermore, what Grotius hands down concerning angels carrying our prayers to God is asserted ἄτερ γραφῆς. Nowhere in the canonical scriptures is that office attributed to angels. Jerome believes these things suffice for this comparison: says: An angel, that is, a messenger, is most truly called a priest of God: because he is a mediator between God and men, and announces His will to the people, and for that reason there is a breastplate on the priest's breast, and in the breastplate doctrine and truth are placed, so that we may learn that a priest ought to be learned and a herald of the Lord's truth.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

LABIA ENIM SACERDOTIS CVSTODIENT SCIENTIAM EJVS;) Custodiebant. Sacerdotis, id est summi sacerdotis, qui Phineæ successerat.

ET LEGEM REQVIRENT EX ORE EJVS.) Requirebant Hebræi ab ipso sensum legis. Levit. 10, 10. Ezech. 44, 23.

QVIA ANGELVS DOMINI EXERCITVVM EST.) Erat. Angeli preces hominum ad Deum, Dei man- data ad homines deferunt. Idem faciebat in lege summus sacerdos, qui semel anno expiationem faciebat populi Lev. 16, 1. & qui controversias de legis sensu ortis consu- lebatur Deut. 17, 9. Ejus locum implet in Ecclesia Christia- na Episcopus, Angelus ob id ipsum dictus in Apocalypsi. Diodorus Siculus de Judæis apud Photium: ἀρχιερέα δὲ τὸν προσαγορεύουσι, καὶ νομίζουσιν αὐτοῖς ἄγγελον γενέσθαι τῶν τοῦ θεῶ προσαγμάτων.

Rectius hæc alii plerique accipiunt ceu gene- ralem sententiam de officio ac decore sacerdotum. Nam horum est legem novisse, eamque alios do- cere. Dicit autem labia custodient scientiam ejus, quod os sacerdotis sit arca quædam, in qua cu- stoditur depositum cæleste. Papistæ ex hac regula divina promissionem faciunt quasi sacerdotes in reli- gionis negotio errare non possint: Sed quæ subjicit Propheta, luculenter docent; indicari, non quales sint sacerdotes, sed quales esse debeant. Cæterum quod de angelis preces nostras ad Deum deferentibus tradit Grotius ἄτερ γραφῆς asseritur. Nuspiam in canonicis scripturis id officium angelis tribuitur. Hieronym. hæc sufficere huic comparationi credi- dit: dit: Angelus, id est, nuncius, facerdos Dei verissime di- citur: quia Dei & hominum sequester est, ejusque ad populum nunciat voluntatem, & idcirco in facerdo- tis pectore rationale est, & in rationali doctrina & veritas ponitur, ut discamus facerdotem doctum esse debere & præconem dominicæ veritatis.

## 2:8
Verse 8.

BUT YOU HAVE DEPARTED FROM THE WAY.) You turn aside from the institutions of your ancestors. YOU HAVE CAUSED MANY TO STUMBLE IN THE LAW.) You were the cause why many stumbled, by receiving foreigners into the interior of the Temple, by profaning the Sabbath, Nehemiah 13:4, 5, 6, 7, 15, and following. YOU HAVE MADE VOID THE COVENANT OF LEVI.) By not fulfilling the promises, you have also freed me from those things which I had promised to the Levites and specifically to Phinehas and his successors. See Zechariah 11:10.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

VOS AVTEM RECESSISTIS DE VIA.) Ab in- stitutis majorum deflectitis. SCANDALIZASTIS PLVRIMOS IN LEGE.) Causa fuistis, cur multi impingerent, recipiendo homines alienigenas in interiora Templi, profanando sabbatum, Nehem. XIII. 4. 5. 6. 7. 15. & sequentibus. IRRITVM FECISTIS PACTVM LEVI.) Non implendo promissa, me quoque liberastis ab iis quæ Levi- tis ac nominatim Phineæ ejusque successoribus promise- ram, Vide Zach. XI. 10.

## 2:9
Verse 9.

THEREFORE I ALSO HAVE MADE YOU CONTEMPTIBLE AND LOW BEFORE ALL THE PEOPLE.) I will make you vile and subject to all peoples: to those foreigners who, with Antiochus, will be your prey and object of contempt. AND YOU HAVE ACCEPTED PERSONS IN THE LAW.) In the judgments which you ought to have exercised according to the law, you gave place to favor, and you adapted your sentences to the wishes of the powerful, you favored the usurers.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

PROPTER QVOD ET EGO DEDI VOS CONTEMTIBILES ET HVMIIES OMNIBVS POPV- LIS.) Faciam vos viles & obnoxios omnibus populis: externis illis, qui cum Antiocho, eritis prædæ ac despicatui. ET ACCEPISTIS FACIEM IN LEGE.) In judi- ciis, quæ secundum legem exercere debebatis, locum de- distis, gratiæ, & ad potentium vota aptastis sententias favi- stis foeneratoribus.

## 2:10
Verse 10.

HAVE WE NOT ALL ONE FATHER?) Have we not all sprung from Jacob, and are we not therefore equal in liberty? HAS NOT ONE GOD CREATED US?) Did He not form us into a people by leading our fathers out of Egypt? Thus the word ברא is used in Isaiah 43:1, 45:8, 9, Psalm 102:19.

That one father is to be understood not as Jacob, as Grotius wishes, nor as Abraham, as others think, but as God Himself, the appended epexegesis teaches: Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? As Osiander, Winkelmann, and the Weimar theologians rightly hold, with Jerome not denying it. Compare Deuteronomy 32:6, Isaiah 43:2, Ephesians 1:3, chapter 3:15.

Verse the same.

WHY THEN DOES EACH ONE OF US DESPISE HIS BROTHER.) Do you oppress the poor with usury? The history is touched upon which is in Nehemiah chapter 5, verse 3, 4, and following. VIOLATING THE COVENANT OF OUR FATHERS.) The law which forbids usury to be taken from fellow countrymen. Exodus 22:25, Leviticus 25:35, 36, Deuteronomy 23:19, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

NVMQVID NON PATER VNVS OMNIVM NOSTRVM?) Nonne omnes à Jacobo orti sumus, ac proinde in libertate pares sumus? NVMQVID NON DEVS VNVS CREAVIT NOS?) Formavit nos in populum, educendo patres no- stros ex Ægypto? sic vox ברא sumitur Esaiæ XLIII. 1. XLV. 8. 9. Pf. CII. 19.

Patrem unum, nec Jacobum, ut Grotius vult, nec Abrahamum, ut putant alii, intelligi, sed Deum ipsum, ἐπεξήγησις subjuncta docta docet: Num- quid non pater unus est omnium nostrum? Numquid non unus Deus creavit nos? Uti recte Osiander, Winkelm. Vinarienses, non abnuente Hieronymo. Conf. Deut. XXXII. 6. Ef. XLIII. 2. Eph. I. 3. c. III. 15.

Vers. eod.

QVARE ERGO DESPICIT VNVSQVISQVE NOSTRVM FRATEM SVVM.) Opprimitis pauperes fœnore? tangitur historia, quæ est apud Nehemiam c. 5. v. 3. 4. & sequentibus. VIOLANS PACTVM PATRVM NOSTRO- RVM.) Legem quæ usuras à popularibus vetat accipi. E- xodi 22, 15. Levit. 25, 35. 36. Deuteronom. 23, 19. 20.

## 2:11
Verse 11.

JUDAH HAS DEALT TREACHEROUSLY.) The tribe of Judah returned home. AND AN ABOMINATION IS COMMITTED IN ISRAEL.) In Benjamin and those who had joined Judah from other tribes. AND IN JERUSALEM.) Even in the primary city, in the sight of the Temple. BECAUSE JUDAH HAS PROFANED THE HOLINESS OF THE LORD.) A not insignificant part of which consisted in this, that the Jews should not contract marriages with the worshippers of idols: for what the law had established against women from the seven nations devoted by God, Deut. 7:3, a just interpretation had extended to other women adhering to idols. AND HAS MARRIED THE DAUGHTER OF A STRANGE GOD.) That is, a worshipper. For just as gods are called fathers by their own, Jerem. 2:27, so those who worship them are called children: he has married, בעל, that is, he has had in marriage. The history which is in Ezra 9, 10, Neh. 13:23 is touched upon.

Cocceius has here provided a new ἔκθεσιν [exposition], understanding the holy of the Lord, which He loves, which was profaned by Judah, as the Son of God: "He who establishes that Christ is a mere man and nevertheless a king in the kingdom of God and a lord, he profanes the holy of the Lord, and commits fornication with idolaters, because he makes Christ a new God and Lord, unknown to the fathers, or at least, in whom the fathers did not hope for the sake of salvation and justice." But although these things may be true, it does not appear how they agree with the present text. The holiness of the Lord, says Willet, calls the excellence of the Jewish people communicated to them before all other nations, and he says this is polluted, because Judah loved and took to wife the daughter of a strange god, that is, a gentile daughter, who worships strange gods. For just as the worshippers of the true God are called His children, so the worshippers of false ones are also called their children. The sense is: Therefore the Jews act treacherously, and commit an abomination, because by taking strange wives they prostitute their own dignity and holiness.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

TRANSGRESSVS EST JVDA.) Tribus Judæ do- mum reversa. ET ABOMINATIO FACTA EST IN ISRAEL.) In Benjamine & iis, qui ex aliis tribubus ad Judam acceffe- rant. ET IN JERVSALEM.) Etiam in urbe primaria, in conspectu Templi. QVIA CONTAMINAVIT JVDAS SANCTIFI- CATIONEM DOMINI.) Cujus pars non exigua in hoc posita erat, ne Judæi cum idolorum cultoribus matrimo- nia copularent: nam quod lex constituerat adversus fœ- minas ex septem populis à Deo devotis, Deut. 7, 3. id ju- sta interpretatio ad alias fœminas idolis adhærentes pro- tulerat.
