Hebr. 3, 1. ex parte respondet ἀπόςολο͂ τ̃ ὁμολο- γίας legatus adstipulationis, hoc est, qui mittitur à Deo, ut nobis proponat Testamentum Dei, de hæ- reditate ipsi tradenda, & Ecclesia in ipso justifican- da per fidem, & per verbum & spiritum suum à no- bis Fidem stipuletur, ut ei recte adstipulari per fi- dem possimus, & in ea cum bona conscientia indul- gentiam & vitam repetere, ut hic Coccejus.

Nono ab angeli fœderis expectatione. Quia de Evangelio fœderis hic sermo est, quem fideles maximopere desiderabant, & in quo unice volupta- tem habebant, utpote, qui non tantum in fœdere promissus fuerat Deut. 18, 15. sed etiam ruptum id solus instaurare, novumque sancire poterat Ebr. 7, 22. cap. 8, 6. cap. 9, 15. quo proinde omnes pii dele- ctabantur. Nam illud חפצים in bonam, ut prius מבקשים juxta nonnullos in malam accipiendum partem, ut ex constanti illius usurpatione constat, neque dubium est, de fidelibus ex animo adventum angeli fœderis desiderantibus, non modo de malis eundem ludificantibus, sermonem esse. Prono- men iterum אתם partitive accipiendum, ut prius quidem compellat improbos: VENIET Dominus, de quo vos improbi in blasphema vestra interroga- tione quæritis, ubi sit, & angelus fœderis, à quo vos fi- deles in vestra miseria, ut Sospitatore & salvatore venturo oblectamini. Cyrillus ita habet: Veniet igitur Dominus, inquit, quem vos quæritis, expusil- lanimitate dicentes (ubi est Deus justitiæ?) Veniet au- tem ac docebit, quæ supra legem & supra umbras ac typos sunt. Erit quippe angelus testamenti, quod olim voce Dei & patris prænunciatum est. Ita Hie- ronymus: supra legimus motam Domino quæstionem ab his, qui dicunt: Omnis qui facit malum, bonus est in conspectu Domini, & tales ei placent, aut cer- te si displicet, ubi est Deus judicii, hoc est, ubi est ju- stitiæ veritas? Ad quam dissolvendam Domini ser- mo respondit: Mittam angelum meum, qui præpara- bit viam meam, & veniet ad templum suum domi- nator, quem vos quæritis, qui judex est veritatis, de quo dicitur Psalmo: Deus judicium tuum regi da, & justitiam tuam filio regis: Non enim Pater judicat quenquam, sed omne judicium dedit Filio, & ille est angelus testamenti, quem vos quæritis.

Decimo à Messiæ munere, quod sit quasi ignis con- flans, & herbæ fullonum, & undecimo à sacrificio- rum oblatione tempore Nov. Testam. de quibus vers. 4. Hæc enim luculenter itidem Messiam de- monstrant. Duodecimo ab urbis & templi exci- sione: quæ sequitur adventum Domini vers. 5. De- cimo tertio ab Eliæ excitatione. Per quem iterum πρωτοβαπτιςής designatur cap. 4, 5. 6. Quæ omnia deinde expendemus. Decimo quarto è loci pa- ralleli comparatione: Johannem prodromum Mes- siæ prædixit etiam Esaias cap. 40, 3. de quo illic vi- dimus. B. Tarnovius hic etiam confert Psal. 132, 12. de Lucerna uncto Domini (Messiæ) præpara- ta. Quam de Johanne etiam veteres nonnulli in- tellexere, de quo ad illum locum. Conf. Joh. 1, 7. cap. 7, 35. Decimo quinto è Nov. Testam. explica- tione Matth. 11. Marc. 1. Luc. 7.

Quibus postremo accedat Judæorum ipsorum confessio. Recte observat Grotius: Judæos ante natum Christum omnes firma fide tenuisse Messiam in templum secundum venire debuisse: & R. David Kimchium agnovisse præsentem locum de Messia in- telligendum esse. Quod agnovit etiam R. Abar- benel, Eliam ante diem novissimum resuscitandum, ac tum venturum angelum fœderis Messiam. Verum id est de Elia excitando ante novissimum diem po- liticæ Jud. h. e. de Joh. qui in spiritu Eliæ venit Luc. 1, 17. Matth. 11, 14 cap. 17, 11. 12. ceu Messiæ prodro- mus. Quo etiam facit illud R. Mosis Maimonidis, in Jud. Chazakah tract. de Regib. c. XII. Quidam sapientes dicunt ante adventum Regis Messiæ Eliam venturum. Item : in diebus Messiæ per Spir. S. qui requiescet super eum, genealogizabuntur filii Israel per os ejus, sicut dictum est (Malach. 3.) Ecce ego mitto &c. Item illud R. Saadiæ Gaon in libro Haemu- noth. tract. 8. de Redemtione ultima; Præcursor Messiæ filii David erit, quasi legatus ejus, quasi disponens populum & expurgans viam juxta illud: Ecce ego mitto Angelum, meum, &c.

Dicitur vero Johannes Angelus Christi, non quod natura Angelus humano corpore vestitus fue- rit, ut Origenes teste Beda in Marc. 1. credidit, erat enim verus & merus homo Joh. 1, 7. non ob vitam angelicam, qua superare visus sit angelicam purita- tem, uti Jesuitæ Costeropart. II. Concion. p.69. pla- cuit, qui ideo Angelum à S. Johanne Baptista non su- stinuisse adorari, utpote suspiciente in eo culmen Apo- stolicam & Angelicam puritatem, turpiter & impe- rite S. Johannem Apostolum cum S. Johanne Ba- ptista confundens, asserit. Sed ob officium, quod legatus Filii Dei fuerit. Cornelius a Lapide varias hic reddit appellationis rationes, quæ vero pleræ- que frivolæ, confictæ ac ineptæ sunt, utpote quod angeli infantiam non habeant, & Johannes sex tantum menses habuerit infantiæ, quod Baptista pene sine cibo & potu instar angeli vixerit, quod purissimus & semper virgo fuerit instar angeli, quod à puero in eremo con- templationi vacans cum Deo, & angelis conversatus, quod gratiam acceptam nunquam perdiderit, nun- quam peccaverit, saltem deliberato & graviter, & quæ hujus generis alia. Sola illa vera est, & conveniens, quod ab officio dictus angelus sit. Quo de Cyrill. An- gelum nominatum sacrosanctum Baptistam dicimus, non propter naturam quidem (ex muliere enim natus homo proinde ut nos fuit) sed quoniam illi talia nobis prædicandi, nunciandique munus est impositum. Ab officio igitur vocabulum inditur nec naturam angelo- rum significat.

Verba ANTE FACIEM MEAM recte Messiæ tribuit Grotius, sed explicatio illa, quod in Mes- sia vivat Deus multo plenus ac perfectius, quam in ullo Prophetarum eo sensu accipi posset; quasi gra- du tantum differret κατοίκησις Filii Dei in humana natura assumpta, ab illa inhabitatione, qua Prophe- tis adfuit: quod Nestorianum. Orthodoxi Patres eadem verba & Patri & Filio tribui observant; addo eandem faciem, quia Pater & Filius unum sunt τῇ ὀσίᾳ vel essentiæ unitate, etsi personis distinguan- tur Johan. 10, 30. Quod autem Christus verba hæc aliter citat Matt. 11, 10. causa esse videtur, quod docere voluit, Deum Patrem, quem Judæi suum Deum profitebantur, ista non de se aut sua manife- statione, sed de Filii incarnatione ejusque revelatio- ne pronunciasse, imo se eundem esse Deum, de quo illic loci sermo, quique ibidem loquatur, ut recte hic Willius.

Porro quod Grotius ingerit: de Messia Judæis maxima bona etiam IN STATU PUBLICO, si ei paruissent, allaturo, unde illud habeat, & quæ bona publici Status intelligat, non satis liquet, nisi quod fortassis illud etiam hauserit ipse è traditionibus Judæorum, quos in multis sequutus est. Nos è divinis oraculis Messiam promissum scimus non ob bona status publici vel temporalia, sed ob bona spiritualia, & regni cœlestis. Regnum enim ejus non erat de hoc mundo, nec esse debebat. Venit ad templum suum, non ad Rempubl. ut angelus fœderis gratiæ, non ut legatus ob statum publicum, venit ut dominator in monte Sion vel Ecclesia, non ut Dominator terrenus vel politicus.

ECCE VENIT, DICIT DOMINUS EXERCITUUM.) Veniet haud dubie stante hoc templo: Expectate eum.

Hæc de adventu posteriori Euseb. l. V. demonstr. Evang. cap. 28. Chrysostom. Augustin. l. cit. intelligunt (etsi præcedentia de adventu priori explicent) Hieronymus, Haymo, & Hugo de utroque adventu interpretantur. Sed recte Grotius adhuc de eodem adventu angeli fœderis, de quo priora loquuntur, sermonem esse, agnoscit, nec dubitandum est, certitudinis gratia promissionem repeti, simulque indigitari adventus propinquitatem, uti solet participium præsens eo modo accipi. Quem sensum probavit etiam Theodoreius, & imprimis Cyrillus: Nam ut plane ipsis affuturum, imo jam præsentem ostendens, clarissimis verbis pronunciat, tempus adventus ejus in mundum hunc non diu dilatum iri. Nam venturus dicitur, ut emundet filios Levi, ut offerant Domino sacrificia in justitia, quæ non possunt de adventu secundo, & novissimo die intelligi.

## 3:2
Verse 2.

AND WHO SHALL BE ABLE TO THINK OF THE DAY OF HIS COMING.) Who shall be able to endure the time of His coming? So the Chaldean, and the LXX, τίς ὑπομένει. Why this? Because He Himself will endure the cross, so that He may come to the kingdom, and He will show the same way to His own. The advent of Christ, when it concerns the Jews, is from His preaching to the destruction of the city.

AND WHO SHALL STAND TO SEE HIM.) Who shall stand, when He shall appear: So the Chaldean. The same as what preceded.

Grotius therefore considers the day of the Lord's coming intolerable, partly because of the cross which He imposes on His own who are about to enter the heavenly kingdom, and partly because of the destruction of the city, if indeed the day of the coming extends as far as the destruction of the city. But there is nothing here about the cross or the tribulation of the faithful, even though Vatablus and also Lyranus draw these to the affliction of the righteous at the time of Christ's coming and in the primitive Church. Some explain it thus: who will be able to measure, or even conceive of, the good things that that day will bring, and who will be able to bear such light and majesty? The interlinear Gloss: No human sense will be able to conceive when He will come, or what kind of person He will be when He comes. Lossius on this passage: He complains, he says, of the negligence and sloth of men at the time of the Messiah's coming, because very few will observe it: first, because of the false interpretation of the Prophets concerning the Messiah's corporal kingdom. Secondly, because of the righteousness of works, trusting in which the Pharisees and Chief Priests will reject the Messiah. Thirdly, because of the lowliness and contempt of Christ's person. Fourthly, because of the absurdity of the doctrine, that salvation is given to the Church only on account of this Lord who died and was crucified, and not on account of the righteousness of works. But the word מכלכל is more correctly rendered by the LXX, the Chaldean, and others as 'who will endure,' than by the Vulgate as 'who will be able to conceive,' because although that word in Kal and Hiphil signifies to contain, yet in Piel it is never taken in the Bible for capacity, and the words subjoined explain this sense: 'and who shall stand to see Him?' which the wicked regard, and men of similar bran, with whom he here disputed, and whose crimes the Prophet censured. Who shall sustain the day of his coming of the wicked and ungodly? The coming of the Lord indicates that the virtue of the economy will be intolerable to the incredulous, as Cyril here. Who of the wicked shall stand before this teacher of justice, who of those loving darkness before this sun? Who shall be able to stand WHEN HE SHALL APPEAR? For thus the Hebrew word is more correctly rendered than TO SEE HIM, as the Vulgate has it. The LXX render it: ἐν τῇ ὀπτασίᾳ αὐτὸ, which Cyril correctly explains by ἐπιφάνειαν, For being invisible by nature as God, he became manifest, having taken upon himself the likeness towards us. How the word ἐπιφανείας, φανερῦσθαι, and ἐπιφαίνεσθαι is attributed to Christ visibly present both in the advent of humiliation and of glorification in the New Testament, 1 Tim. 6:14, 2 Tim. 4:8, Tit. 2:11 and ch. 3:4, 1 Pet. 5:8, Col. 3:4, 1. Petr. 5:4. The metaphor is taken from those whose eyes cannot look directly at or bear the splendor of the rising sun, as Tarnovius here correctly. Compare Matt. 2:3, ch. 3:12, ch. 21:46, etc.

The same verse.

FOR HE HIMSELF IS LIKE A REFINING FIRE.) This is what Christ himself says in Luke 12:49, that he came to cast fire upon the earth, namely, an exploratory fire, as the following in Luke indicate. See what is above on Zechariah 13:9.

LIKE FULLERS' HERB.) In Hebrew ברית. It grows in the green and moist places of Palestine, and has the same power for cleansing filth as nitre. So we are taught by Jerome, who lived in those places, on Jeremiah 2:22.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET QUIS POTERIT COGITARE DIEM ADVENTUS EJUS.) Quis ferre poterit tempus adventus ipsius? Ita Chaldæus, & LXX. τίς ὑπομένει. Quare hoc? quia crucem perferet ipse, ut ad regnum veniat, eandemque viam suis monstrabit. Adventus Christi, cum de Judæis agitur, est à prædicatione ejus, ad excidium urbis.

ET QUIS STABIT AD VIDENDUM EUM.) Quis consistet, ubi ille apparebit: Ita Chaldæus. Idem quod præcessit.

Intolerabilem ergo diem adventus Domini censet Grotius, partim ob crucem, quam imponit suis, regnum cœleste ingressuris, partim ob excidium urbis, siquidem adventus dies usque ad excidium urbis porrigatur. Sed nihil hic de cruce aut tribulatione fidelium, etsi hæc ad afflictionem justorum tempore adventus Christi & in primitiva Ecclesia Vatablus etiam atque Lyranus trahunt. Nonnulli sic explicant: quis poterit metiri vel cogitatione bona, quæ adferet dies ille, & quis ferre poterit tantam lucem & majestatem? Gloss. interlinearis: Nullus humanus sensus poterit cogitare, quando venturus, vel qualis venturus erit. Lossius in h. l. Querela, inquit de negligentia ac socordia hominum, tempore adventus Messiæ, quod pauci admodum observabunt: primum propter Prophetarum falsam interpretationem de Messiæ regno corporali. Secundo propter operum justitiam, qua fidentes Pharisæi & Pontifices Messiam rejicient. Tertio propter personæ Christi vilitatem & contemtum. Quarto propter doctrinæ absurditatem, quod propter hunc solum Dominum mortuum & crucifixum, tantum datur salus Ecclesiæ, non propter justitiam operum. Sed verbum מכלכל rectius à LXX. Chald. & aliis redditur, quis sustinebit, quam à Vulgato, quis cogitare poterit, quia cum verbum istud in Kal & Hiphil significet capere, in Piel tamen nunquam in Bibliis pro capacitate accipitur, & explicant verba subjuncta hunc sensum: & quis stabit ad videndum eum? quæ malos respiciunt, ac similis furfuris homines, cum quibus hic disceptavit, & quorum scelera taxavit Prophe- ta. Quis malorum & improborum sustineat diem adventus ejus? Virtutem œconomiæ adventus Domi- ni incredulis intolerabilem fore indicat, ut hic Cyril- lus. Quis malorum coram hoc justitiæ præcepto- re, quis tenebras amantium coram hoc sole consi- stet? Quis stare poterit QUUM APPARUE- RIT? Sic enim verbum Ebræum rectius redditur, quam AD VIDENDUM EUM, ut Vulg. habet. LXX. reddunt: ἐν τῇ ὀπτασίᾳ αὐτὸ, quod recte ex- ponit Cyrillus per ἐπιφάνειαν, Ἀόρατός γαρ κτ φύσιν ὑπάρχων ὡς Θεός γέγονεν ἐμφανής, τὴν πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁμοίωσιν ἀναλαβὼν. Quomodo ἐπιφανείας φανερῦσθαι, & ἐπιφαίνεσθαι vocabulum Christo visibiliter præsenti tam in adventu humiliationis, quam glorificationis in Nov. Testam. attribuitur 1. Timoth. 6. v. 14. 2. Timoth. 4, 8. Tit. 2, 11. & c. 3, 4. 1. Petr. 5, 8. Coloss. 3, 4. 1. Petr. 5, 4. Metaphora sumpta est ab illis, quorum oculi exorientis solis splendorem recta intueri, aut ferre nequeunt, ut hic recte Tarnovius. Confer Matth. 2, 3. cap. 3, 12. cap. 21, 46. seqq.

Vers. eod.

IPSE ENIM QVASI IGNIS CONFLANS.) Hoc est, quod ipse Christus Luc. 12, 49. dicit, venisse se ignem mittère in terram, ignem nempe exploratorium, ut se- quentia apud Lucam indicant. Vide quæ supra Zachar. 13, 9.

QVASI HERBA FVLLONVM) In Hebræo ברית. Ea in Palestinæ locis virentibus, & humectis nascitur, & ad sanandas sordes eandem vim habet, quam & nitrum. Ita nos docent, qui in illis locis vixit Hieronymus ad Jerem. 2, 22.

## 3:3
Verse 3.

AND HE SHALL SIT REFINING AND PURIFYING SILVER, AND HE SHALL PURIFY THE SONS OF LEVI.) There is here, as often, ל for ut (as), which the Chaldean also saw: as a refiner sits to purify silver, (See the representation of this matter in Ezekiel 22:18,) so shall he purify the sons of Levi. For many of the family of the priests devoted themselves to Christ after the resurrection, Acts 6:7.

AND HE SHALL STRAIN THEM LIKE GOLD, AND LIKE SILVER.) He shall purify them, having cast away the dross, of which he complains in Matt. 15:9, ch. 23:23, 28, and Luke 10:31, where the priests are specifically touched upon.

AND THEY SHALL BE OFFERING SACRIFICES TO THE LORD IN JUSTICE.) That they may offer just sacrifices to the Lord: that is, with a pious mind, as Zacharias did,

As no dross can stand before the fire of a goldsmith, nor any spots or stains before the soap of a fuller or washerwoman, so neither can the words and deeds of the incredulous and ungodly stand before that accurate judge of things, who searches hearts and words. For he himself is like the fire of a refiner, which melts metals so that every impure thing may be separated, and like the soap of fullers, which can wash away stains and make garments white, Mark 9:3. Compare Ps. 51:4. The Chaldean, R. David Kimchi, and Vatablus explain soap as what Jerome rendered as fullers' herb, concerning which there is no need to dispute, when it is agreed that it signifies that by whose benefit garments are washed and purged of stains. Some think that light sins are indicated, which are to be washed away by fullers' herb, and heavier ones, which are to be consumed by the spirit of burning or the fire of the goldsmith. Compare Isaiah 4:3. For AS THE GOLDSMITH SITS REFINING AND PURIFYING SILVER (which comparison Grotius here correctly observes with the Chaldean), so with great zeal and accurate effort, the Messiah coming SHALL PURIFY THE SONS OF LEVI, he shall repurify all those established in the ministry of the word from the dross of doctrine and wicked life. Where Willius correctly says: To note accurate care and diligence, he attributes to him the sitting, which is required in this kind of work, at the same time also thus hinting at constancy in the work of reformation, because he is not to treat it lightly and cursorily. To indicate the most exact act of purification, he mentions refining. It is an act of refining proper to goldsmiths, who, when they take metals to be melted or refined, sharpen the vehemence of the fire with continuous blasts. Hence to refine is properly to melt metal. Finally, to note the most limpid mode of purification, he adds: he shall purify and refine them like gold and silver. Now, it is not some most exact reformation of the Church of this kind that is noted, which is free from every stain and dross (for those things, because of the weakness of the flesh, still remain in it), but one that is more exact than its corrupt state, and as great as can possibly fall to it.

The Prophet now speaks specifically of the sons of Levi, as those whose vices he had previously censured, as observed by Cyril: he indicates, therefore, that they would not be better, but worse, and unworthy of the greatest reformation at the time of the advent of Christ. See the fulfillment in Matt. 5, 6, 7, 21, 23; Luke 19, 46; John 2, 3, 8, etc. PURIFYING THEM LIKE GOLD AND SILVER, THAT THEY MAY BE TO JEHOVAH, THOSE WHO OFFER AN OFFERING IN RIGHTEOUSNESS, namely, the λογικὴν λατρείαν (reasonable service) Rom. 12, verse 1, the πνευματικὰς θυσίας (spiritual sacrifices) 1 Pet. 2, 5. So that, as is customary for the Prophets, the things of the New Testament are described by the phrases of the Old Testament, and the name of the figure is attributed to the thing figured. For the sons of Levi in the Old Testament were a figure of the ministers of the word in the New Testament, and those sacrifices were a figure of Christ and the worship of Christians, who are spiritual Jews and the heavenly Jerusalem, a certain Church: whence in the following verse mention is made of the offering of Judah and Jerusalem, as rightly noted here by the blessed Tarnovius. Therefore, the sons of Levi are not to be restricted to Barnabas and others, of whom mention is made in the Acts of the Apostles, as seems to have been done by Theodoret, nor are they to be extended with Arius to all Christians, who are a royal priesthood, 1 Pet. 2, 9, but are to be understood with Jerome, Rupert, Remigius, Haymo, Albert, Hugh, Lyranus, and others as all ministers of the word, not excluding the Levitical ministry of the Jews, which he especially desired to be purged, even if he purged most of them in vain.

The end of this purging is that they may offer sacrifices in righteousness, where by מנחה (offering) the Papists understand the Mass-sacrifice, but rashly: Albert the Great, Vatablus, and Montanus more rightly acknowledge that spiritual sacrifices are indicated, such as faith in God, sincere obedience toward the word of God, patience under the cross, prayers, thanksgivings, alms, and the mortification of the flesh. There is truly nothing here that favors the Mass-sacrifice, which is furthermore destitute of any foundation in Scripture, nay, it is diametrically opposed to the sacred writings and to the unique propitiatory sacrifice of the New Testament, performed on the altar of the cross. Nor are priests properly so called in the New Testament opposed here to the priests of the Old Testament, Testament, which acknowledges no priest except the unique priest Christ, whose priesthood is ἀπαράβατον (unchangeable) Heb. 7, verse 24, nor is this offering restricted to the sons of Levi, or the ministry of the word, as a function proper to it, but it is the effect of the purging of the sons of Levi, or of the ministry. For they are purged for this reason, that by their ministry they may reconcile to God such as offer sacrifices in righteousness. This is the end and fruit

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET SEDEBIT CONFLANS ET EMVNDANS ARGENTVM, ET PVRGABIT FILIOS LEVI.) Est hic ut sæpe ל pro ut, quod & Chaldæus vidit: sicut confla- tor sedet ad mundandum argentum, (Vide hujus rei ὑποτύ- πωσιν Ezech. 22, 18.) ita purgabit filios Levi. Nam multi de familia sacerdotum post resurrectionem Christo se ad- dixere Actor. 6, 7.

ET COLABIT EOS QVASI AVRVM, ET QVASI ARGENTVM) Purgabit eos, abjectis scoriis, de quibus conqueritur Matth. 15, 9. c. 23, 23. 28. & Luc. 10, 31. ubi nominatim tanguntur sacerdotes.

ET ERVNT DOMINO OFFERENTES SA- CRIFICIA IN JVSTITIA.) Ut Domino offerant sacri- ficia justa: id est, pio animo sicut fecit Zacharias,

Ut coram aurifabri igne nullæ scoriæ, nec co- ram fullonis aut lotricis smegmate ullæ maculæ, aut labes possunt consistere, ita nec incredulorum & improborum dicta & facta coram illo accurato re- rum judice, corda & verba scrutante. Nam ipse est quasi ignis conflatoris, qui liquefacit metalla, ut o- mne impurum excernatur, & ut smegma fullonum, qui possunt maculas eluere, & vestes candifacere Marc. 9, 3. Conf. Ps. 51, 4. Smegma exponunt Chal- dæus, R. David Kimchi, Vatablus, quod Hieronymus reddidit herbam fullonum, qua de re non est, quod disputetur, ubi constat id significari, cujus benefi- cio vestes eluuntur ac purgantur à maculis. Levia autem peccata indicari, nonnulli putant, quæ herba fullonum eluenda, graviora, quæ spiritu combustionis, vel igni aurifabri consumenda. Conf. Esa. 4. v. 3. Nam UT SEDET AURIFABER CON- FLANS ET PURGANS ARGENTUM (quam comparationem recte cum Chald. hic ob- servat Grotius) ita magno studio, & accurata ope- ra Messias adveniens PURGABIT FILIOS LE- VI, omnes in ministerio verbi constitutos à scoriis doctrinæ, pravæque vitæ repurgabit. Ubi recte Willius: Ut curam accuratam ac diligentiam notet, sessionem ipsi tribuit, quæ in isthoc operarum gene- re requiritur, simul quoque ita constantiam in ope- re reformationis innuit, quod non leviter & cursim eam sit tractaturus. Ut exactissimum actum pur- gationis indicet conflationis meminit. Est actus conflandi aurifabris proprius, qui ubi metalla sibi liquefacienda aut defecanda sumunt, flatibus con- tinuis ignis vehementiam acuunt. Hinc conflare proprie est metallum liquefacere. Ut denique modum limpidissimum purgationis notet, subjicit: purgabit & defæcabit eos veluti aurum & argentum. Ita autem non exactissima aliqua ejusmodi Eccle- siæ reformatio notatur, quæ omni labe & scoriis va- cet (ea enim ex carnis imbecillitate in ea adhuc re- sidua manent) sed quæ corrupto ejus statu exactior, & tanta, quanta in ipsam cadere potest.

Defiliis Levi specialiter jam loquitur Propheta, utpote quorum vitia ipse antea taxarat, ut obser- vatum Cyrillo: non meliores ergo, sed deteriores, maximaque reformatione indignos illos fore ad- ventus Christi tempore, indigitat, Vide comple- mentum Matth. 5. 6. 7. 21. 23. Luc. 19, 46. Johan. 2. 3. 8. &c. DEFECANS EOS VELUT AURUM ET ARGENTUM, UT SINT JEHOVÆH, QUI OFFERANT MUNUS JUSTE, nempe λογικὴν λατρείαν Rom. 12. vers. 1. πνευματικὰς θυσίας 1. Petr. 2, 5. Ut ita, quod solenne est Pro- phetis, phrasibus Vet. Testam. res Nov. Testam. describantur, & nomen figuræ tribuatur rei figura- tæ. Filii enim Levi in Vet. Test. erant figura ministrorum verbi in Nov. Testam. & sacrificia illa Christi ac Christianorum cultus, qui sunt Judæi spirituales, & Ecclesia superna quædam Jeru- salyma: unde sequente versu muneris Jehudæ & Jerosolymorum fit mentio, ut recte hic B. Tarno- vius. Non ergo restringendi filii Levi ad Barna- bam & alios, quorum fit mentio in Actis Apost. ut à Theodoreto factum videtur, nec ad omnes Christia- nos, qui regale sunt Sacerdotium 1. Petr. 2, 9. cum Aria extendendi, sed cum Hieronymo, Ruperto, Remigio, Haymone, Alberto, Hugone, Lyrano aliis- que intelligendi omnes ministri verbi, non exclu- so ministerio Judæorum Levitico, quod imprimis repurgatum cupiebat, etsi plerosque frustra pur- garet.

Finis purgationis istius est, ut offerant sacrificia juste, ubi per מנחה Sacrificium Missaticum intel- ligunt Papistæ, sed temere: Spiritualia sacrificia, qualia sunt Fides in Deum, sincera obedientia erga verbum Dei, patientia in cruce, preces gratiarum a- ctiones, eleemosynæ, mortificatio carnis indigitari, re- ctius agnoscit Albertus M. Vatablus, Montanus. Ni- hil profecto hic est, quod faveat Sacrificio Missati- co, quod præterea omni Scripturæ fundamento destituitur, imo è diametro sacris literis, & unico Sacrificio propitiatorio Nov. Testam. in ara crucis peracto, adversatur. Neque hic opponuntur Sa- cerdotibus Vet. Testam. Sacerdotes proprie dicti in Nov. Testam. quod non agnoscit nisi unicum Sa- cerdotem Christum, cujus Sacerdotium est ἀπα- ράβατον Ebr. 7. vers. 24. neque hæc oblatio restrin- gitur ad filios Levi, vel ministerium verbi, ceu pro- pria eidem functio, sed purgationis filiorum Levi, vel ministerii effectus est. Ideo enim ipsi purgantur, ut ministerio suo conciliare possint Deo tales qui offerant sacrificia in justitia. Hic est finis & fructus-

## 3:4
Verse 4.

AND THE SACRIFICE OF JUDAH AND JERUSALEM WILL PLEASE THE LORD.) In the Hebrew minchah, that is, a gift; for that word is taken sometimes for the genus, sometimes for the species. He will approve what is given with such a spirit, even if they are of small value, as Luke 2, 24. Matt. 8, 4. ch. 12, 41. Acts 21, 26.

AS THE DAYS OF THE AGE, AND AS THE ANCIENT YEARS) As in days long past, that is, in olden years: as in the times of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, David, Elijah.

Cyril refers it to eternity, explaining it regarding the sacrifices which befit the days of the age or of the heavenly and holy spirits, but he adds also another explanation regarding the worship once exhibited to God: He returns, namely, to the times that were before those rites and the religion once exhibited to God by the saints. For the glory and celebrity of the ancients was in obedience. Thus Abraham offered his son to GOD (and it was reckoned to him as righteousness) and he was called the friend of God. Thus also Noah built an ark for the salvation of his house, as it has been handed down in the scriptures: (Therefore, he says, the sacrifice of Judah will be pleasing,) that is, of the people carrying about circumcision in heart and spirit. Indeed, even Jerusalem, which the mind contemplates, that is, the Church: just as also the sacrifice of those possessing the days of the age and of the saints, who were in life in previous ages, who pleased God through obedience and faith. Which, being approved by other interpreters, is altogether to be preferred.

then you will no longer mock me, and you will seek the God of judgment, but you will feel and experience me as judge. Where Rupert, Arias, Robert, and Castrius also go.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET PLACEBIT DOMINO SACRIFICIUM JU- DA ET JERUSALEM.) In Hebræo מנחה manad id est, donum; sumitur enim ea vox modo pro genere, modo pro specie. Tali animo data probabit, etiamsi pretii sint exigui, ut Luc. 2, 24. Matth. 8, 4. c. 12, 41. Actor. 21, 26.

SICUT DIES SECULI, ET SICUT ANNI AN- TIQVI) Sicut diebus olim exactis, id est, annis veteribus: sicut temporibus Abrahami, Isaaci, Jacobi, Samuelis, Davidis, Eliæ.

Ad æternitatem refert Cyrillus, explicans de sa- crificiis, quæ decent dies seculi vel cœlestium sancto- rumque spirituum, sed addit etiam aliam explica- tionem de cultu Deo olim exhibito: Reditur a nempe tempora, quæ fuerint ante illos cultus, ac religionem a sanctis olim Deo exhibitam. Priscorum enim glo- ria & celebritas fuit in obedientia. Sic Abraham obtulit filium DEO (& reputata ei est fides ad justi- tiam) & amicus Dei appellatus est. Sic & Noe ar- cam fabricavit ad salutem domus suæ, ut literis pro- ditum est: (Itaque placebit, inquit, sacrificium Judæ,) hoc est, populi, in corde & spiritu circumcisionem cir- cumferentis. Quin & Hierusalem, quam mens in- tuetur, id est, Ecclesiæ: sicut & sacrificium possiden- tium dies seculi & sanctorum, qui fuperioribus æta- tibus in vita fuerunt, qui per obedientiam & fidem Deo placuerunt. Quæ cæteris Interpp. probata, omnino præferenda.

tunc non amplius ludificabitis me, & Deum judicii quæretis, sed me judicem sentietis & experiemini. Quo abit quoque Rupertus, Arias, Robertus & Castrius.

## 3:5
Verse 5.

of the ministry, that there may be those who offer in righteousness. It is to be noted, says Cocceius, that it is not said, they will offer a gift to the Lord, or they will be offering a gift to the Lord; but, They will be to the Lord, (and indeed with the addition of the Zakeph distinction) offering a gift in righteousness. We shall be consecrated to God, says Cyril in the explanation of this passage, if we no longer live for ourselves, and in all ways cultivate charity towards Him, and with all our strength desire to perform well what He wills. Something of this kind also the divine Paul says concerning Christ, the Saviour of us all. (For one died for all, that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.) Describing to us in a way the goodness of his own conduct, and the power and virtue of the mystery of Christ, he says again: (I have been crucified with Christ. And I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And that I now live in the flesh, I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me. I do not reject the grace of GOD.) He says, therefore, (they will be offering to God) that is, they will be consecrated to His will: Not minding earthly things: not loving pollutions from iniquity: not affecting to excel others: but rather offering sacrifices of righteousness. Whence Willius rightly: The fruit of a true and purified priesthood will therefore be a pure and grateful people, pleasing to God for their piety and the gratitude of their soul.

THAT I MAY DRAW NEAR TO YOU IN JUDGMENT, AND I WILL BE A SWIFT WITNESS AGAINST SORCERERS AND ADULTERERS AND PERJURERS, AND THOSE WHO DEFRAUD THE HIRELING OF HIS WAGES, THE WIDOWS AND THE ORPHANS: AND OPPRESS THE STRANGER, AND HAVE NOT FEARED ME.) God responds seriously to that statement above 1, 17. Where is the God of judgment? I will come, He says, to you, and I will be a witness (for God alone is both witness and judge) speedily against sorcerers (φαρμακοὺς or Φαρμακίας, Rev. 21, 8. ch. 22, 15. the crime Φαρμακεία. Gal. 5, 20. Rev. 9, 21. ch. 18, 23.) and adulterers, (concerning whom see Luke 18, 11. 1 Cor. 6, 9. Heb. 13, 4. Matt. 15, 19. Mark 7, 21. Gal. 5, 19. Rom. 11, 22.) and perjurers, (concerning whom it is treated in Rom. 1, 31.) and those who withhold the wages from the hireling (these are comprehended under the name of ἀργάγων Luke 8, 11. 1. Cor. 5, 10. 11. ch. 6, 10.) and those who oppress the widow, the orphan, and the stranger, (these are ἀνελεήμονες Rom. 1. v. 31.) and those who do not fear me: (who are ἀσεβεῖς throughout the New Testament.) That swift judgment, however, was the destruction of wicked men: together with the city, in which destruction both the destruction of the world and that eternal judgment were prefigured: namely, all those not corrected by Christ and the Apostles, were storing up for themselves wrath against the day of wrath Rom. 2, 5.

The Papists also attempt to blow up purgatory fire from this passage, Bellarmine, lib. 1. de Purgat. cap. 3. concerning which see in Dr. Gerhard, tom. 8. of Theological places, tract on death §. 239. It is truly strange that Bellarmine understands by the sons of Levi the whole Church and just men in general, to be purged from the rest of their sins: although (contradicting himself) lib. 1. de Missa cap. 10. he asserts and proves that by the sons of Levi not all Christians can be understood, but only a certain part of the Christian people, namely the Priests of the New Testament (who perform the Mass).

That explanation concerning the destruction of Jerusalem is not inappropriate, provided that eternal punishment is joined with that penalty. I will draw near to you in judgment not only temporal, but as regards the impenitent, everlasting, and I will be a most swift witness, in a short time, and you will experience me as a witness convincing you in your conscience, and as a judge; for as at the hour of death all the impious and unbelieving feel this eternal judgment, so in the destruction of Jerusalem countless numbers of them experienced this witness and judge, as many, namely, as perished then in impenitence: but because the prophet exhorted the men of his own time to repentance v. 7. and institutes a disputation with them here, he seems to be dealing with the judgment against the sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers, etc., of that time, which nevertheless, from parity of reason, can be applied to all times, like other legal and penitential sermons. To which sense those words seem to favor: I WILL DRAW NEAR as a SWIFT witness: unless one chooses to distinguish this prediction from the following exhortation, so that the prediction concerns future times, but the exhortation is to be referred to the times of the Prophet. Which we do not disapprove. Thus, therefore, the prediction being completed, he proceeds to the exhortation and a new disputation with his men. Others understand it of the coming to judgment. But these things are more rightly explained of a particular judgment, which indeed brings not only temporal punishments, but also eternal ones, as we have just said. To the question, therefore, Where is the God of judgment? The Prophet teaches not only that the Son of God will be present, whose day the wicked will hardly be able to endure, but also introduces the Father, who threatens that He will be a swift judge and witness against the wicked. But God, whose eye beholds all things, whose ear hears all things, and who alone is the eyewitness and ear-witness of all things that are done and said, furthermore searches most deeply the hearts and reins of all, and is the most suitable and certain witness of all, and is at the same time the most just judge of all, as being the author of all justice and justice itself. I will draw near to you in judgment, that is, I will draw near as judge (And I will be a swift witness) of my own accord, and summoned by no one. For I will condemn the wicked to punishments by my own sentence. And I will pronounce judgment upon them, with no one else uncovering their vices: but knowing them as God, manifest and hidden, and hence a witness to everyone of their crimes, as Cyril says. By which method it is indicated that shortly after the advent of the Messiah the Jews would experience the God of judgment when they would suffer total extermination. Which sense Willius also provides p. 220. As I shall have sent my forerunner ahead and shall have shown myself a reformer,

Latin:

Verf. 5.

ministeri, ut sint, qui offerant in justitia. Notan- dum est, inquit Coccejus, non dici, offerent munus Domino, vel erunt offerentes munus Domino; sed, Erunt Domino, (& quidem adjecta distinctione Zakeph) offerentes munus injustitia. Conse- crabimur Deo, inquit Cyrillus in explicatione hujus loci, si amplius nobis non vivamus, & modis omnibus charitatem erga illum excolamus, totisque viribus pro- be prestare cupiamus, quæ ille vult. Tale quid etiam divinus Paulus de omnium nostrum Salvatore Christo. (Unus enim pro omnibus mortuus est, ut & qui vi- vunt, jam non sibi vivant, sed ei, qui pro ipsis mortuus est, & resurrexit.) Suæ autem conversatio- nis bonitatem, & vim ac virtutem mysterii Christi quodammodo nobis describens, rursum inquit: (Chri- sto confixus sum cruci. Vivo autem jam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus. Quod autem nunc vivo in carne, in fide vivo filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me. Non abjicio gratiam DEI.) Ait igitur, (erunt Deo offerentes) hoc est, ejus voluntati consecrabuntur: Non terrena sa- pientes: non ex iniquitate inquinamenta diligentes: non quibusdam præcellere affectantes: sed sacrificia potius justitiæ offerentes. Unde recte Willius: Ve- ri igitur & repurgati sacerdotii fructus erit populus purus & gratus, Deo ob pietatem & animi gratitudi- nem placens.

UT ACCEDAM AD VOS IN JUDICIO, ET ERO TESTIS VELOX MALEFICIS ET ADULTE- RIS ET PERJURIS, ET QUI CALUMNIANTUR MERCEDEM MERCENARII, VIDUAS ET PU- PILLOS: ET OPPRIMUNT PEREGRINUM, NEC TIMUERUNT ME.) Respondet serio Deus isti dicto su- pra 1, 17. Vbi est Deus judicii? veniam, inquit, ad vos, & ero testis (Deus n. solus est & testis & judex) propere contra ma- leficos (φαρμακοὺς five Φαρμακίας, Apoc. 21, 8. c. 22, 5 1. cri- men Φαρμακεία. Galat. 5, 20. Apoc. 9, 21. cap. 18, 23.) & adulteros, (de quibus vide Lucam 18, 11. 1. Corinth. 6, 9. Hebr. 13,4. Matth. 15, 19. Marc. 7, 21. Gal. 5, 19. Rom. 11, 22. & perjuros, (de quibus agitur Rom. 1, 31.) & qui sub- trahunt, mercedem mercenario (hi comprehenduntur nomi- ne ἀργάγων Luc. 8, 11. 1. Cor. 5, 10. 11. cap. 6, 10.) & qui viduam pupillum & peregrinum opprimunt, (hi sunt ἀνελεήμονες Rom. 1. v. 31.) & qui me non timent: (qui ἀσεβεῖς passim in Novo Testamento.) Velox autem illud judicium, fuit inte- ritus sceleratorum hominum: simul cum urbe, in quo inte- ritu & mundi interitus, & judicium illud æternum figura- bantur: nimirum omnes isti per Christum & Apostolos non correcti, ἐθησαύριζον ἑαυτοῖς ὀργὴν εἰς ἡμέραν ὀργῆς Rom. 2, 5.

Conantur & purgatorium ignem ex hoc loco sufflare Papistæ Bellarmin. lib. 1. de Purgat. cap. 3. de quo vide apud Dn. D. Gerhardum tom. 8. loco- rum Theologicorum tract. de morte §. 239. Mi- rum vero quod Bellarminus per filios Levi Eccle- siam totam & homines justos in universum intelligit, a reliquis peccatorum purgandos: cum tamen (sibi contradicens) lib. 1. de Missa cap. 10. per filios Levi non posse omnes Christianos, sed tantum partem quandam populi Christiani, nimirum Sacerdotes Novi Testamenti (missificantes) intelligi, asserat probetque.

Non inconveniens illa de excidio Hierosolymitano explicatio, modo cum pœna illa conjungatur æter- num supplicium. Accedam ad vos in judicium non solum temporarium, sed quantum ad impœniten- tes sempiternum, ac ero testis festinantissimus, brevi, & testem in conscientia vos convincentem, & ju- dicem me experiemini; nam ut in hora mortis o- mnes impii & increduli hoc æternum judicium sentiunt, ita in excidio Hierosolymitano innumeri ex ipsis hunc testem & judicem experti sunt, quot- quot scil. tum in impœnitentia periere: sed quia propheta hortatus sui temporis homines ad pœni- tentiam v. 7. & cum illis disceptationem hic insti- tuit, videtur de judicio contra maleficos, adulteros, perjuros, & c. istius temporis agere, quæ tamen ex pa- ritate rationis ad omnia tempora applicari possunt, ut aliæ conciones legales & pœnitentiales. Cui sen- tui favere videntur illa: ACCEDAM testis VE- LOX: nisi hanc prædictionem a sequenti adhortatio- ne distinguere libeat, ita ut prædictio concernat fu- tura tempora, adhortatio autem ad tempora Pro- phetæ referenda sit. Quod non reprobamus. Ita ergo prædictione absoluta, ad parænetin & disce- ptationem novam cum suis hominibus progredie- tur. Alii de adventu ad judicium intelligunt. At re- ctius de judicio particulari hæc explicantur, quod vero non solum temporales pœnas infert, sed etiam æternas, uti modo diximus. Ad quæstionem ergo, Vbi est Deus judicii? Non modo Filium Dei adfutu- rum, cujus diei mala haud toleraturi sint, Propheta docet, sed & Patrem introducit, qui judicem & te- stem velocem se futurum improbis minatur. At Deus cujus oculus omnia intuetur, auris omnia audit, quique solus αὐτόπτης & αὐτοήκους est, eorum omnium quæ fiunt, & dicuntur, adhæc scrutatur penitissime corda & renes omnium, & testis est o- mnium maxime idoneus certissimusque, & judex simul omnium est justissimus, utpote justitiæ omnis autor & ipsa justitia. Accedam ad vos in judicio, hoc est, judex accedam (Et ero testis velox) sponte mea, & a nemine advocatus. Improbus enim ad supplicia sententia mea condemnabo. Et judicium super ipsis proferam, non alio quopiam eorum vitia de- tegente: sed sciens illa ut Deus, manifesta & occulta, & hinc cuilibet scelerum suorum testis, dicente Cyril- lo. Quo pacto indicatur, brevi post adventum Messiæ Judæos Deum judicii experturos cum to- tale exterminium patientur. Quem sensum etiam tradit Willius p. 220. Vti anteambulonem meum præmisero & ipse me reformatorem præstitavero,

## 3:6
Ver. 6.

FOR I AM THE LORD, AND I CHANGE NOT.) I am inexorable to the persistently wicked.

Most explain it thus: I have not changed, or I do not change my sentence. For in the law the Lord threatened punishment to its transgressors; this sentence, he says, I do not change. Thus Cyril: "When you see sorceresses called to judgment, then by the things themselves you will know that I am the Lord your God, both formerly and now, good at once and a lover of good things and of virtue. For I know no change or vicissitude. For I am always, and without mutability, what I am." And afterwards: "Therefore God is indeed always immutable, and as it were fixed and strengthened in good, and unshaken in justice: they on the contrary have kept almost mutability itself in their heart, and have most strenuously followed the crimes of their fathers." He gives the reason for the constancy of his sentence against the impious, lest they should think he is changed like a man, so as not to punish the wicked, since he is by nature immutable. For thus Jerome, Theodoret, Remigius, Rupert, Haymo, Albert, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, Vatablus, and Isidore. That my vengeance, he says, does not immediately rage against the wicked, do not think that there will therefore be no judgment: For as my promise cannot be made void, so neither will I forget my threats, since I cannot be changed like a man, but what I have once spoken, it is necessary that it come to pass. For I always persevere in the same sentence against the wicked, although I sometimes delay. As here Christ. à Castro. Others explain it concerning the immutable promises of God, as will be said now. Conf. Num. 23, 23.

Ver. same.

AND YOU O SONS OF JACOB.) You pious ones among the Jews.

YOU ARE NOT CONSUMED) You shall not be consumed. I will give you a way out of the city. See what was said at Matt. 24, 16. 22. 23. Just as in the time of Nebuchadnezzar those were exempted from the common destruction who were marked (as Ezekiel allegorizes) with the letter Thau, so in the time of Vespasian those who bore the cross in their soul. See a similar way of speaking in Lam. 3, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

EGO ENIM DOMINUS, ET NON MUTOR.) Inexorabilis sum pertinaciter pravis.

Plerique sic exponunt: non mutavi, seu muto sententiam meam. In lege enim comminatus est Dominus pœnam transgressoribus ejus, hanc sententiam, inquit, non muto. Ita Cyrillus: Quando " ad judicium vocari videritis veneficas, tum re- " bus ipsis cognoscetis, quia ego sum Dominus " Deus vester, & olim & nunc, bonus simul & bo- " norum ac virtutis amans. Nescio enim muta- " tionem aut vicissitudinem. Ego enim semper, " & citra mutabilitatem sum quod sum. Et postea: " itaque Deus quidem est immutabilis semper, & " velut in bono fixus ac firmatus, & inconcussus in " justitia: illi contra tantum non ipsam mutabili- " tatem in corde servarunt, & patrum scelera stre- " nuissime sunt secuti. Rationem reddit constantiæ sententiæ suæ contra impios, ne existimarent instar hominis se mutatum, ne puniat improbos, cum naturâ sit immutabilis. Sic enim Hieronymus, Theodoretius, Remigius, Rupertus, Haymo, Albertus, Hugo, Lyra, Dionysius, Vatablus, & Isidorus. Quod ultio mea, inquit, non illico in malos desæviat, non putetis nullum propterea futurum judicium: Nam ut promissio mea evacuari non potest, sic nec minarum obliviscar, cum ego mutari non possim ut homo, sed quod semel locutus sum, necesse quod eveniat. Semper enim in eadem persevero sententia contra malos, licet aliquando differam. Ut hic Christ. à Castro. Alii de immutabilibus Dei promissis explicant, uti jam dicetur. Conf. Num. 23,23.

Vers. eod.

ET VOS FILII JACOB.) Vos pii inter Judæos.

NON ESTIS CONSUMTI) Non consumemini. Dabo vobis exitum ex urbe. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 24,16. 22. 23. Sicut Nabuchodonosori tempore exemti sunt communi exitio, qui notati erant (ut Ezech. ἀλληγορεῖ) littera Thau, ita Vespasiani tempore qui crucem gerebant in animo. Loquendi genus simile vide Lam. 3, 22.

## 3:7
Ver. 7.

FOR FROM THE DAYS OF YOUR FATHERS YOU HAVE DEPARTED FROM MY ORDINANCES, AND HAVE NOT KEPT THEM) For is not in the Hebrew. The discourse, having omitted the pious, returns to the impious, as if he were to say: you live just as you lived when you deserved deportation: and you wish to deserve the same things again.

RETURN TO ME) Through repentance, and amendment of life.

AND I WILL RETURN TO YOU.) By your care.

LXX. They rendered it thus: And you, sons of Jacob, have not departed from the sins of your fathers. For the Hebrew word can be explained in this way, namely, you have not ceased to do evil. In which manner Osiander also interprets it: And you, sons of Jacob, do not consume, that is, you do not put an end to your crimes, you do not cease: Es wil kein Ende oder Auffhören bey euch seyn. Cyril also has this sense: You, however, although generated from Jacob, a pious and good man, and one who always hates contumacy and served God, have not earnestly striven to express his character: but you prefer to imitate the disobedience and pertinacity of your fathers. Others likewise refer it to the impious, but in this way: I the Lord and I do not change, and you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed, i.e., although because of these crimes of yours you are not yet consumed, nevertheless nothing has been taken away from the right of my justice, but the punishment which I once threatened in my law for such offenses, I will not retract, but will execute it at its own time. Willius explains it somewhat differently regarding the truth in promises, namely in this way: That I have hitherto deferred the day of judgment and your consumption, you owe to me and to my mercy, and to my immutable promises, not to your obedience, which you have denied me from the days of your ancestors, and by the perpetual omission of which you accumulate my wrath. And afterwards: To my mercy, and to my covenant and promises you owe it that you are still a people: since I have pledged eternal benevolence to Jacob and his posterity, therefore I have hitherto spared you. This is the true and only cause why I do not take notice of your wicked ways according to their deserts, because I am mindful of my promises. I am just, I remain just, and I am delighted with the just, and I will also at some time bring my justice into the light, but I tolerate your iniquity with long-suffering, lest my faith promised to the fathers should fail.

However, some explain it concerning the pious, rendering it with the Vulgate: And you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed, B. Luther: Es sol mit euch Kindern Jacob nicht gar auß seyn / and in Comment. Therefore it is pure mercy that they do not perish entirely, because the Lord spares them and preserves them in public calamities. B. Tarnovius: You, sons of Jacob, with whom I entered into a peculiar covenant in your ancestors, are not entirely consumed by the punishments and calamities sent upon you, because there have always been some good ones left among you, for whose sake I have spared all, but especially on account of the intercession of my Son, who is descended from one of your tribes, and I have given you a longer space for repentance. Coccejus refers these things with the preceding clause to the truth of the promise of the coming of the Lord, and the preservation of the house of Jacob until that time. The reason, he says, is given for sending the Angel with that effect of purification from the immutability of God. Did he say he would not do it? And yet he would change. But God does not lie, is not affected by repentance, does not suffer change, or the shadow of variation. He adds an argument of the truth and constancy of God, which could also sustain faith, lest men should be precipitate. And you, house of Jacob, have not failed. Thus Jacob had promised in Genesis 49:10. The name of many nations has even perished; Israel, although guilty of the greatest sins and already deported out of his land into Babylon, did not fail, but even retained his polity. That is an argument that the God of judgment does not sleep, but will surely come at his own time. But the former sense indicated by us seems simpler. For the accusation of the wickedness and defection of the people is continued in the following ninth verse: FROM THE DAYS OF YOUR ANCESTORS you have almost always DEPARTED FROM MY STATUTES: NOR HAVE YOU EVER duly OBSERVED THEM: And therefore RETURN to me: if you still wish to escape judgment, perform serious repentance: AND I WILL RETURN TO YOU. Thus I will show myself placated and gracious to you in turn, and by my grace and kindness I will turn myself to you again, SAYS THE LORD OF HOSTS. YOURS, who will also keep that promise for you which is in Jerem. 18, 8, no less constant and immutable in promises than in threats, cf. Zachar. 1, 3. Jerem. 4, 1. chap. 38, 3. 7. Ezech. 18, 32. The exhortation to repentance pertains to those present, or those who were living in the age of Malachi; therefore he announced the judgment of the Lord to them, but he did not prophesy concerning a judgment to be in the future after several centuries.

Verse of the same.

AND YOU SAID, IN WHAT SHALL WE RETURN?) If you ask what needs to be corrected in you, I will tell you.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

A DIEBUS ENIM PATRUM VESTRORUM RECESSISTIS A LEGITIMIS MEIS, ET NON CUSTODISTIS) Non est enim in Hebræo. Sermo omissis piis ad impios revertitur, quasi dicat: ita vivitis sicut vixistis cum deportationem estis commeriti: & paria rursum commereri vultis.

REVERTIMINI AD ME) Per pœnitentiam, & emendationem vitæ.

ET REVERTAR AD VOS.) Per vestri curam.

LXX. Ita reddidere: Et vos filii Jacob non recessistis à peccatis patrum vestrorum. Nam sic Ebræum verbum exponi potest, non cessastis scil. malefacere. Quo pacto etiam interpretatur Osiander: Et vos filii Jacob non consummatis, id est, non finem imponitis vestris sceleribus, non cessatis: Es wil kein Ende oder Auffhören bey euch seyn. Hunc sensum habet quoque Cyrillus: Vos autem quamvis ex Jacob progenerati homine pio & bono, & qui semper contumaciam odit, ac Deo servivit, illius mo- res exprimere non enixe studuistis: sed Patrum ve- strorum inobedientiam & pertinaciam imitari ma- vultis. Alii pariter ad impios referunt, sed hac ra- tione, Ego Dominus & non mutor, & vos filii Jacob non estis consumti, q. d. licet ob hæc vestra scelera nondum sitis consumti, nihil tamen decessit de ju- re justitiæ meæ, sed quam semel talibus delictis in lege mea minatus sum pœnam, eam non retracta- bo, sed suo tandem tempore exequar. Paulo ali- ter de veritate in promissis explicat Willius, hoc scil. modo: Quod diem judicii vestramque consum- " tionem hactenus distuli, mihi meæque miseri- " cordiæ, & promissis immutabilibus debetis, non " vestræ obedientiæ, quam à diebus majorum ve- " strorum mihi negatis, ac cujus perpetua inter- " missione iram meam accumulatis. Et postea: Meæ " misericordiæ, meoque fœderi & promissioni- " bus debetis, quod adhuc populus estis: quoni- " am æternam benevolentiam Jacobo & ejus po- " steris pactus, ideo vobis hactenus peperci. Hæc " vera & unica causa est, cur in improbos mores " vestros non animadvertam pro meritis, quod " promissionum mearum sim memor. Sum justus, " maneo justus, & justis delector justitiamque me- " am etiam aliquando in apricum producam, ini- " quitatem autem vestram longanimitate tolero, " ne fides mea patribus promissa deficiat.

De piis tamen explicant nonnulli reddentes cum vulgata: Et vos filii Jacob non estis consumti, B. Lutherus: Es sol mit euch Kindern Jacob nicht gar auß seyn / & in Comment. Darumb ists eitel Barmherzigkeit, daß sie nicht gantz umbkommen, quod illis Dominus parcat, eosque in publicis cala- mitatibus conservet. B. Tarnovius: Vos filii Jacobi, quibuscum in majoribus fœdus peculiari inii, non omnino consumti estis pœnis ac calamitatibus vo- bis immissis, quia & semper inter vos quidam boni fuere reliqui, propter quos omnibus peperci, præ- cipue autem ob intercessionem Filii mei, qui ex vestra tribuum aliqua est oriundus & pœnitentiæ longius vobis dedi spatium. Coccejus hæc cum præcedenti colo refert ad veritatem promissi ad- " ventus Domini, & conservationem eo usque " domus Jacobi. Ratio, inquit, redditur mittendi " Angeli cum isto effectu repurgationis à Dei im- " mutabilitate. Dixit non facerem? Atqui sic " mutaret. At Deus non mentitur, non afficitur " pœnitudine, non patitur mutationem, aut varie- " tatis obumbrationem. Addit argumentum ve- " ritatis & constantiæ Dei, quod etiam fidem susti- " nere poterat, ne homines præcipitarent. Et vos, " domus Jacobi, non defecistis. Sic promiserat Ja- " cobus Genes. 49, 10. Multarum gentium no- " men etiam periit, Israel, licet maximorum pecca- " torum reus & jam extra terram suam in Babylo- " nem deportatus, non defecit, sed & politiam suam " retinuit. Argumentum id, Deum judicii non " dormire, sed suo tempore certo venturum. Sed " prior à nobis indicatus sensus simplicior videtur. Nam continuatur accusatio improbitatis & defe- ctionis populi versu subsequenti nono: A DIE- BUS MAJORUM VESTRORUM fere sem- per RECESSISTIS A STATUTIS MEIS: NEQVE EA UNQVAM rite OBSERVA- STIS: Ideoque REVERTIMINI ad me: si ad- huc judicium effugere velitis, pœnitentiam agi- te seriam: ET REVERTAR AD VOS. Ita placatum vicissim & gratiosum me vobis exhibe- bo, gratiaque ac benignitate mea ad vos iterum me convertam, AIT DOMINUS EXERCI- TUUM, TUUM, qui etiam illud promissum, quod Jerem. 18, 8. sancte vobis servabit, non minus in promissis, quam comminationibus constans, & immutabilis, conf. Zachar. 1, 3. Jerem. 4, 1. cap. 38, 3. 7. Ezech. 18, 32. Adhortatio ad pœnitentiam ad præsentes pertinet, vel illos, qui ætate Malachiæ vivebant, illis ergo etiam judicium Domini denuntiavit, non vero de judicio, post aliquot secula futuro vati- cinatus est.

Vers. eod.

ET DIXISTIS, IN QVO REVERTEMVR.) Si quæritis, quid opus sit corrigi in vobis, dicam.

## 3:8
Verse 8.

WILL A MAN ROB GOD: YET YOU ROB ME.) Does anyone despoil (that is, dare to despoil) his judges as you have despoiled me? קבע means to despoil, Prov. 22, 23. קבען is a despoiler in the Chaldean. The Chaldean also took אלהים here to mean judges.

AND YOU SAID: IN WHAT DO WE ROB YOU?) If you say: in what do we despoil you? I will tell you.

IN TITHES AND IN FIRST FRUITS.) What is translated here as first fruits is תרומה in Hebrew: in Greek ἀφαίρεμα. It was a part no less than a sixtieth of the grain, must, and oil, which part was given to the priests, Deuteron. 18, 4. These offerings were indeed for the priests, as were the tithes of the Levitical tithes: but since the priests ought to have performed the daily sacrifices from those offerings, they did not do it, or they did it perfunctorily, as can be seen in chapter 1, verse 4. Furthermore, they drew all the tithes to themselves, nor did they allow the nine parts of them to be brought to the Levites, Nehem. 13, 10. Josephus teaches us that the priests also did this before the Vespasian destruction. Therefore, God was despoiled of his right in two ways: first, because the offerings were not provided for the things for which they were instituted; second, because the Levites fled due to hunger, and thus God was deprived of their ministry, as can be seen in the cited passage of Nehemiah.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SI AFFIGET HOMO DEVM: QVIA VOS CON- FIGITIS ME.) An quisquam spoliet (id est spoliare ausit) Iudices suos ut vos me spoliastis? קבע est spoliare Prov. 22, 23. קבען spoliator Chaldæis. אלהים pro judicibus etiam Chaldæus hic accepit.

ET DIXISTIS : IN QVO CONFIGIMVS TE.) Si dixeritis: in quo spoliamus te? dicam.

IN DECIMIS ET IN PRIMITIIS.) Quod hic ver- titur primitiæ, תרומה est in Hebræo: Græcis ἀφαίρεμα. Erat pars non minor sexagesima de frumento, musto, oleo, quæ pars dabatur sacerdotibus, Deuteron. 18, 4. hæ quidem obventiones erant sacerdotum, ut & decimæ de- cimarum Leviticarum: at sacerdotes cum deberent ex illis obventionibus jugia sacrificia facere, id non facie- bant, aut faciebant perfunctorie, ut videri us cap. 1. vers. 4. Præterea decimas omnes ad se trahebant, neque patie- bantur earum partes novem ad Levitas deferri, Nehem. 13, 10. quod sacerdotes etiam fecisse ante excidium Vespasiæ- neum docet nos Josephus. Duobus ergo modis Deus spoliabatur suo jure, tum quod non præstabantur ipsi, qua- rum rerum causa institutæ erant obventiones; tum quod Levitæ fame diffugerent, & sic eorum ministerio Deus destitueretur, ut dicto Nehemiæ loco videre est.

## 3:9
Verse 9.

AND IN PENURY YOU ARE CURSED.) In Hebrew: With a curse you will be cursed: great evils will follow you from this.

AND YOU ROB ME, THE WHOLE NATION.) You despoil, as just now. The whole nation, because when the common people saw the Levites were not there, they refrained from bringing the tithes.

There is no need for us to understand the word אלהים improperly as judges, with the Chaldean: for this, when placed absolutely, denotes God: nor is it rendered otherwise by the other interpreters, who with the highest consensus interpret it as God, even if some with the LXX explain it as to supplant, others with Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion as to defraud, as also B. Luth. Is it right that a man should deceive God, as you deceive me? Jerome with the Rabbis renders it to pierce. Which, however, come to the same thing. For these things are not to be understood as the piercing of the Son of God with Jerome and Rupert, which does not fit this passage, but the piercing is to be understood metaphorically, concerning the affliction of God and the provocation of the same to anger, and thus Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Dionysius, Carthusius and others, does man dare to afflict God with his frauds and robberies, and bring trouble upon him? but you have been vehemently troublesome to me. However, the translation of those who render it to despoil through deception, teuschen, with the LXX εἰ πτερνιεῑ, and the remaining Greeks μὴ ἀποστερήσει, is better, see Num. 18, 9. 19. Neh. 10, 27. ch. 13, 7. 9. Some understand the word אלהים with Calvin and Gualther as the gods of the nations, i.e., does any one of the nations do this to their fictitious gods, which you do to me? Compare Jer. 2, 10. 11. Willius thinks the interpretation is perhaps plainer and less forced if the words are rendered: Shall a man despoil God, since you despoil me, and you say, in what do we despoil you? Is it therefore, because you despoil me perversely of my goods, that it would be just for a man to act thus with God? By no means, unless perhaps your deeds carry right, or form a new rule. Should it therefore be right, because you do it? Should a man be allowed to rob God, because you rob me? but B. Luther's version is sufficiently plain and not forced. Tarnovius: Shall a man, or anyone created by God, despoil his creator God, from whom he received all that he has? It ought not to be done so, therefore I rightly complain, because you despoil me, and yet acknowledging no fault you stubbornly say, in what do we despoil you? The passage Neh. 13, 10 sufficiently teaches that Malachi looked to those times, and therefore this exhortation and threatening is not to be restricted to the times of the coming of the Lord and the most recent destruction of the city of Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET IN PEnVRIA VOS MALEDICTI ESTIS.) In Hebræo: Maledictione maledicti vos eritis: magna vos mala hinc sequentur.

ET ME VOS CONFIGITIS GENS TOTA.) Spoliatis, ut modo. Gens tota, quia cum plebs videret Levitas non alii, abstinebat adferre decimas.

Non opus est, ut vocem אלהים improprie in- telligamus de judicibus cum Chaldæo: Hæc enim absolute posita Deum notat: nec aliter redditur ab Interpp. cæteris, qui summo consensu de Deo in- terpretantur, etsi nonnulli cum LXX. exponant supplantare, alii cum Aquila, Symmacho, Theodo- tione defraudare, uti etiam B. Luth. Ists recht/daß ein Mensch GOtt teuschet/ wie ihr mich teuschet? Hieronymus cum Rabbinis reddit configere. Quæ vero eodem recidant. Neque enim de confixione Filii Dei hæc intelligenda cum Hieronymo & Ru- perto, quæ huic loco non quadrat, sed confixio me- taphorice intelligenda, de afflictione Dei ejusdem- que ad iram provocatione, atque ita Remigius, Haymo, Hugo, Lyranus, Dionysius, Carthusius & alii, num audet homo suis fraudibus & rapinis De- um affligere, eique molestiam inferre? vos autem vehementer molesti fuistis mihi. Melior tamen est eorum translatio, qui reddunt spoliare per deceptio- nem teuschen cum LXX. εἰ πτερνιεῑ, & reliquis Græ- cis μὴ ἀποστερήσει, vid. Numer. 18, 9. 19. Nehem. 10, 27. cap. 13. 7. 9. Nonnulli vocem אלהים cum Calvino & Gualthero de diis gentium intelligunt h.m. an quisquam gentium hoc suis fictitiis faciat Diis, quod vos mihi? Confer Jerem. 2, 10. 11. Willius putat planiorem, & minus contortam forte inter- pretationem, si verba reddantur: An spolia- " bit homo Deum, quoniam vos spoliatis me, & di- " citis, qua in re spoliamus te? An propterea, quia " vos me spoliatis pervicaciter meis bonis, ju- " stum foret hominem ita cum Deo agere? Ne- " quaquam, nisi forte facta vestra jus important, aut regulam novam formant. Solts darumb wol recht seyn/ weil du es thust? Solt ein Mensch GOtt wol berauben dürffen/ weil ihr mich be- raubet? sed satis plana, nec contorta est B. Lutheri versio. Tarnovius: An spoliet homo seu quisquam à Deo creatus creatorem suum Deum, à quo, quæ habet, accepit omnia? non ita fieri debebat, merito igi- tur conqueror, quia vos spoliatis me, & tamen nul- lam culpam agnoscentes præfracte dicitis, qua in re spoliames te? Locus Nehem. 13, 10. satis docet ista tempora spectasse Malachiam, ideoque hanc paræ- nesin & comminationem non esse restringendam ad tempora adventus Domini, & excidii urbis Hierosalem novissimi.

## 3:10
Vers. 10.

BRING ALL THE TITHES INTO THE STOREHOUSE.) Into the storehouses: namely, under faithful guards, who may distribute their portions to the priests and Levites. Nehemiah followed this admonition of the Prophet, ch. 13, 12. 13.

AND LET THERE BE FOOD IN MY HOUSE.) טרף properly signifies prey. Thus here it is called that which the altar snatches away from the victims. Let those prefects of the storehouse take care that from those offerings there is what may be given to the altar according to the law. See above 1, 12. 13. 14.

PROVE ME CONCERNING THIS.) Make a trial of me.

IF I WILL NOT OPEN TO YOU THE WINDOWS OF HEAVEN.) Shall I not be about to give abundant rain, 2 Kings 7, verse 19.

AND POUR OUT TO YOU A BLESSING EVEN TO ABUNDANCE.) He says this because there had already begun to be hunger, Neh. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

INFERTE OMNEM DECIMAM IN HOR- REVM.) In horrea: nempe sub fidis custodibus, qui sa- cerdotibus & Levitis suas partes erogent. Hoc Prophetæ monitum secutus est Nehemias c. 13, 12. 13.

ET SIT CIBVS IN DOMO MEA.) טרף rapi- nam proprie significat. Ita hic vocatur id, quod altare abripit de victimis. Illi præfecti apothecæ curent ut de obventionibus illis sit, quod detur in altare secundum le- gem. Vide supra 1, 12. 13. 14.

PROBATE ME SVPER HOC.) Periculum de me facite.

SI NON APERVERO VOBIS CATARACTAS COELI.) An non largum daturus sim imbrem, 2. Reg. 7. vers. 19.

ET EFFVDERO VOBIS BENEDICTIONEM VSQVE AD ABVNDANTIAM.) Hoc ideo dicit, quia jam esuriri cœperat Nehem 5.

## 3:11
Vers. 11.

AND I WILL REBUKE FOR YOUR SAKE THE DEVOURER) The locust and other animals harmful to the crops. For your sake, that is, for your good.

He promises a most abundant blessing: I will pour out to you a blessing so that you will not have enough. The word of pouring out, borrowed from waters, for the most part denotes a most abundant communication, see what we said on Zech. 12, 9. You have examples in Joel 2, 28. Isa. 44, 5. But what follows עד—בלי־די declares the metaphorical form, Jun. so that you will not have enough, i.e., to consume it, he refers it to men. Rabbi Joseph Kimchi adapts it to the instruments, vessels, and storehouses. Thus Vatabl. and Pagnin. so that there may not be sufficient vessels for you. Jonathan: so that you will say it is enough. Hieron. even to abundance. Montanus, even to not sufficient, who explain it in general concerning abundance. All these can be joined together, provided that such an abundance is denoted, for which neither vessels to contain it nor men to consume it are sufficient. He promises, therefore, a most abundant affluence, and to make them more certain of it, he adds the removal of all obstacles which could hinder it. For locusts and similar insects not rarely hinder fertility.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ET INCREPABO PRO VOBIS DEVORAN- TEM) Locustam & animalia alia nocentia frugibus. Pro vobis, id est, vestro bono.

Benedictionem promittit largissimam: Effun- dam vobis benedictionem adeo, ut non sufficiatis. Vox effusionis ab aquis mutuata, plerumque largissimam communicationem notat, vide quæ diximus Zach. 12, 9. Exempla habes Joel. 2, 28. Esa. 44, 5. meta- phoricam autem formam declarat quod sequitur עד—בלי־די Jun. adeo ut non sufficiatis, scil. consu- mere illam, refert ad homines. Rabbi Joseph. Kimchi accommodat ad instrumenta, vasa atque horrea. Ita Vatabl. & Pagnin. adeo ut non sint sufficientia vobis vasa. Jonathan: ut dicturi sitis sufficit. Hie- ron. usquead abundantiam. Montanus, usque ad non sufficiens, qui in genere de abundantia explicant. Possunt omnia hæc conjungi, siquidem ejusmodi abundantia notatur, cui nec capiendæ vasa, nec consumendæ homines sufficiant. Affluentiam ita- que copiosissimam promittit, cujus ut adhuc cer- tiores reddat, amotionem obstaculorum omnium, quæ illam impedire possunt, subjicit. Fertilita- tem enim non raro impediunt locustæ, similiaque insecta.

## 3:12
Vers. 12.

FOR YOU SHALL BE A DESIRABLE LAND.) The names of the land and the people are interchanged συνεκδοχικῶς.

Coccejus refers that promise: AND ALL NATIONS SHALL CALL YOU BLESSED, because YOU SHALL BE A LAND OF DELIGHT, to the calling of the Gentiles, and the ἐυδοκίαν (good pleasure), which the Angels celebrated at the time of the birth of Christ: but the common explanation, which Willius also retained, is simpler and more agreeable to the text; the sum is: if they were to render to God what is His, and pay their tithes, they themselves would be happy even to the point of envy on account of God's benefits toward them: A land of complacency and desire, which can be referred both to God and to fertility. To GOD, because He would rest in them and bless them. To fertility, because on account of its abundance their land would be most desirable. In this sense, Judea is also called elsewhere ארץ הצבי, the land of beauty, Dan. 11, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ERITIS ENIM VOS TERRA DESIDERABI- LIS.) Terræ & gentis nomina inter se permiscentur συνεκδοχικῶς.

Promissionem illam : ET BEATOS VOS PRÆDICABUNT OMNES GENTES, quia VOS ERITIS TERRA OBLECTATIONIS, refert Coccejus ad vocationem gentium, & ἐυδοκίαν, quam celebrarunt Angeli tempore nativitatis Christi: sed simpliciter, & textui magis consenta- nea est communis explicatio, quam etiam retinuit Willius, summa est: si Deo sua sint reddituri, & de- cimas exsoluturi, ipsos futuros ad invidiam usque felicissimos propter Dei in ipsos beneficia : Terra complacentiæ & desiderii, quod cum adDeum tum fertilitatem referri potest. Ad DEUM, quod ille in ipsis sit acquieturus, eosque benedictu- rus. Ad fertilitatem, quod ejus ob abundantiam terra ipsorum futura desideratissima. Hoc sensu etiam alibi Judæa vocatur ארץ הצבי terra decoris, Dan. 11, 16.

## 3:13
Ver. 13.

YOUR WORDS HAVE PREVAILED AGAINST ME.) You weary me.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

INVALVERVNT SUPER ME VERBA VESTRA.) Obtunditis me.

## 3:14
Ver. 14.

AND YOU HAVE SAID.) And if you say: as several times above.

YOU HAVE SAID.) In your minds, like that fool in Ps. 14. 1. see also Ps. 73. The state of the Jewish Republic in the times of Zerubbabel was indeed illustrious, but to God, who inspects hearts, certain seeds of that impiety appeared which in a later age erupted with great force. See above 1, 14.

AND BECAUSE WE HAVE WALKED MOURNFULLY BEFORE THE LORD.) קְדֹרַנִית signifies with a sad countenance. Thus the word from which this term is derived is taken in Ps. 38, Ps. 42, 10, Ps. 43, 2, where the Greeks use σκυθρωπάζων (looking gloomy); here, ἐπορεύθημεν ἱκέται (we walked as suppliants). The Chaldean [uses] in depression of spirit; it is a description of the demeanor of those fasting, see Matt. 6, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET DIXISTIS.) Et si dicatis: ut supra aliquoties.

DIXISTIS.) In animis vestris, ut insipiens ille in Ps. 14. 1. vide & Psal. 73. Fuit præclarus sane status Judaicæ Reipublicæ Zorobabelis temporibus, sed Deo corda inspi- cienti apparebant semina quædam ejus impietatis, quæ posteriore ætate vi magna erupit. Vide supra 1, 14.

ET QVIA AMBVLAVIMVS TRISTES CO- RAM DOMINO.) קְדֹרַנִית significat vultu mœsto. Ita su- mitur verbum unde vox hæc derivata est Psal. 38. Psal. 42, 10. Ps. 43, 2. ubi Græci σκυθρωπάζων h. 1. ἐπορεύθημεν ἱκέται. Chaldæus in depressione spiritus; est descriptio habitus jeju- nantium, vide Matth. 6, 16.

## 3:15
THEREFORE NOW WE CALL THE PROUD BLESSED.) That is, those who contumaciously despise the laws of God. The Chaldean here [calls them] the impious.

THEY ARE BUILT UP.) They flourish with offspring. Thus בנה is taken in Gen. 16, 2 and chap. 30, 3, where the Greeks use τεκνοποιῶ (I beget children).

AND THEY HAVE TEMPTED GOD.) They have provoked. It is the same word in Ps. 95, 9. The LXX here [use] ἀντέστησαν τῷ θεῷ (they withstood God).

AND THEY HAVE BEEN SAVED.) They have escaped dangers.

Latin:

ERGO NVNC BEATOS DICIMVS ARRO- GANTES.) Id est eos, qui contumaciter leges Dei con- temnunt. Impios hic Chaldæus.

ÆDIFICATI SVNT.) Florent sobole. Ita בנה sumitur Gen. 16, 2. & cap. 30, 3. ubi Græci τεκνοποιῶ.

ET TENTAVERUNT DEVM.) Irritarunt. Est idem verbum Psal. 95, 9. LXX. hic ἀντέστησαν τῷ θεῷ.

ET SALVI FACTI SVNT.) Evaferunt pericula.

## 3:16
Ver. 16.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

## 3:16
Verse 16.

THEN THEY THAT FEARED THE LORD SPAKE EVERY ONE WITH HIS NEIGHBOUR) But in the evening the pious will address one another thus. The impious secretly: the pious openly.

AND A BOOK OF REMEMBRANCE WAS WRITTEN BEFORE HIM.) A book of memory, in Hebrew. Kings are accustomed to make a list of those who are commended to them, so that they may have special care for them, and so that, if any honors are vacant, they may promote them. The similitude is taken from there. A not dissimilar translation in Dan. 7, 10. The Greeks say ἐγράφη ἐν Διὸς δέλτοις.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

TVNC LOCVTI SVNT TIMENTES DOMI- NVM UNVSQVISQVE CVM PROXIMO SVO) At sero pii alter alterum sic alloquentur. Impii clam: pii palam.

ET SCRIPTVS EST LIBER MONVMENTI CORAM EO.) Liber memoriæ, in Hebræo. Solent re- ges eorum qui ipsis commendantur indiculum facere, ut eorum curam habeant singularem, & ut, si qui honores vacent, illos provehant. Inde sumpta similitudo. Non dispar translatio Dan. 7, 10. Græci dicunt ἐγράφη ἐν Διὸς δέλτοις.

## 3:17
Verse 17.

AND THEY SHALL BE MINE, SAITH THE LORD OF HOSTS, IN THE DAY THAT I MAKE, AS A PECULIAR TREASURE.) When I shall make, namely, those things to come forth, of which [I spoke] above, they shall be mine as a set-apart thing, like precious stones, which are accustomed to be diligently preserved. For thus the Hebrews take סגל, which the LXX here translate as εἰς περιποίησιν. Aquila, as also the LXX elsewhere, [translate it as] περιούσιον.

AND I WILL SPARE THEM AS A MAN SPARETH HIS SON THAT SERVETH HIM.) Whom he loves both as a son and as one who is obedient.

Others [say] in the day, which I make. Which most interpreters understand as the day of the final judgment, along with Jerome and Theodoret, and that explanation seems not inappropriate, because the distinction between the just and the unjust who are mixed together in this age must be most explained on the day of universal judgment, and the book of divine memorial will then be publicly opened, Apoc. 19, 12. We do not deny, however, because of those things which follow in chapter 4, where mention is made again of THAT DAY, which the Lord makes, and indeed also because of the preceding things, in which God threatened that after the coming of the Messiah, from whom very few will allow themselves to be purified, a swift witness will be present, and will approach for judgment against sorcerers and other incredulous and impenitent people, that these things are to be accepted as concerning the day of the Jerusalem destruction. For then the Jewish people, to whom the Lord spoke these things, experienced thoroughly what the difference is between the just and the impious, the one serving God, and the one not serving him. Therefore the book of memorial is attributed to God in the human manner, just as it is customary for kings and princes to have things recorded in special books for the sake of memory, which they wish to remember, Esth. 2, 23. chap. 6, 1. Deut. 31, 34. Are not these things laid up with me, sealed in my treasures, namely, in books of memorial, that is, in the archives of the divine mind.

Willius subscribes to Malach. 4. p. 248. The question is, of which day of judgment there is speech here. Most interpreters interpret these things as the last judgment, "in which wickedness will be perfectly abolished. Although "however there is nothing absurd in this opinion, I prefer nevertheless "to refer these things to the coming of Christ and the day of judgment, in which he destroyed the rebellious Jews, because here it is a matter of the same day as above. The word סגלה for the Hebrews "properly signifies a precious treasure, which one has acquired for himself, and preserves peculiarly for his own uses 1. Chron. 19, 3. Gal. 4, 8. and in a metaphorical sense it denotes a thing, however dear and proper, which one has separated and acquired for himself; in the same sense it is used of the Church and the people whom God chose for himself Exod. 19, 5. 6. Deut. 7. This people Paul calls λαὸν περιέσιον Tit. 2, 14. and St. Peter 1. Epist. 2, 9. λαὸν εἰς περιποίησιν. The sense therefore is: then when I shall come to avenge the profanity, I will claim for myself the pious separated from the impious, and I will preserve them as a most dear and most precious thing.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ET ERVNT MIHI AIT DOMINVS EXERCI- TVVM, IN DIE QVA EGO FACIO, IN PECV- LIVM.) Cum ego faciam, nempe prodire ista, de quibus su- pra 5. erunt mihi ut res seposita, tanquam lapides pretiosi, qui diligenter asservari solent. Ita enim סגל sumunt Hebræi quod LXX. hic vertunt εἰς περιποίησιν. Aquila ut & LXX. alibi περιούσιον.

ET PARCAM EIS SICVT VIR PARCIT FI- LIO SERVIENTI TIBI.) Quam amat & ut filium & ut obsequentem.

Alii in die, quam facio. Quam plerique interpre- tes de die judicii extremi intelligunt cum Herony- mo & Theodoreto, & videtur illa explicatio non in- conveniens, quia discrimen inter justos & injustos qui hoc seculo permisti sunt, in die παντοκριτικῳ maxime explicandum, & liber memorialis divini tum publice aperietur, Apoc. 19, 12. Non abnui- mus tamen ob ea, quæ cap. 4. sequuntur, ubi iterum DIEI ILLIUS, quam facit Dominus, mentio fit, imo etiam ob superiora, quibus Deus minatus est se post adventum Messiæ, à quo se paucissimi puri- ficare patientur, celerem testem adfuturum, & in judicium accessurum contra præstiagitores, alios- que incredulos & impœnitentes, hæc accipi de die excidii Hierosolymitani. Tum enim Judaicus popu- lus, cui hæc loquutus Dominus, expertus oppido est, quid intersit inter justum & impium, servien- tem Deo, & non servientem ei. Liber itaq; memoria- lis humano more Deo tribuitur, quemadmodum penes Reges & principes memoriæ causa consigna- ri peculiaribus libris solent, quorum meminisse vo- lunt Esth. 2, 23. cap. 6, 1. Deut. 31, 34. Nonne hæc condita sunt apud me signata in thesauris meis scil. in libris memorialibus, puta in archivis mentis divinæ.

Subscribit Willius ad Malach. 4. p. 248. Quæsti- est, de quo die judicii heic loci sermo. Plerique in- terpretes de ultimo hæc judicio interpretantur, " quo improbitas perfecte abolebitur. Quamvis " autem hac in sententia nihil absurdi, malo tamen " hæc ad adventum Christi & diem judicii, quo Ju- " dæos rebelles exscidit, referre, quia hic de eodem " die, de quo supra, agitur. Vox סגלה Ebræis pro- " prie significat pretiosum thesaurum, quem quis " tibi comparfit, & ad suos usus peculiariter asser- " vat 1. Chron. 19, 3. Gal. 4, 8. & sensu tralatitio no- " tat rem quamvis charam & propriam, quam quis " sibi separavit & acquisivit; eodem sensu de Ec- " clesia & populo quem sibi Deus selegit adhibetur " Exod. 19, 5. 6. Deut. 7. Hunc populum Paulus vo- cat λαὸν περιέσιον Tit. 2, 14. & S. Petrus 1. Epist. 2, 9. λαὸν εἰ περιποίησιν. Sensus ergo est: tunc quando ulturus veniam profanitatem, pios ab impiis sepa- ratos mihi asseram, & ceu rem charissimam & pre- tiosissimam asservabo.

## 3:18
Verse 18.

AND RETURN.) But return. Supply, you others: for the discourse is turned toward the impious. AND YOU SHALL SEE, WHAT IS BETWEEN THE JUST AND THE IMPIOUS.) Namely, in the time of judgment, how different is the lot of the pious and the impious. The Hebrew text has it thus: And you shall return, and you shall see between the just and the impious. Therefore, it is not a conversion to a better mind, or even to subscribing to the opinion of the pious, but it is hinted at the pious themselves. For it is a conversion of intuition: such as that in Zech. 5, 1. which makes for a greater exaggeration of the happiness of the pious, inasmuch as it will be so great that the eye of the impious will not only fix upon the pious, but will also convince their very mind, so that it may rightly pronounce concerning them: therefore B. Luther most excellently: And you shall on the other hand see again.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

ET CONVERTIMINI.) Sed convertimini. Supple, vos alii: nam ad impios sermo convertitur. ET VIDEBITIS, QVID SIT INTER JUSTUM ET IMPIUM.) Videlicet in tempore judicii, quantum di- versa sit sors pii & impii. Ebræus textus sic habet: Et convertemini, & vi- debitis inter justum ac impium. Non ergo conver- sio ad meliorem mentem, vel etiam ad piorum sen- tentiam subsignandam, sed ad ipsos pios innuitur.
