Est enim conversio intuitionis: qualis illa Zach. 5, 1. quod facit ad majorem felicitatis piorum exagge- rationem, utpote quæ tanta futura, ut impiorum oculus non modo in pios desigat, sed etiam men- tem ipsorum convincat, quo de iis recte pronun- ciet: optime itaque B. Lutherus: Und ihr solt da- gegen wiederumb sehen.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV.

Again the advent of Christ and his fore-

The day of judgment is foretold against the despisers, and the rising of the Sun of justice and salvation and the increase of the faithful with a reminder of the memory of the law of the Lord, and the promise of another Elias about to come before the day of the Lord, to turn the hearts of the fathers and the children, lest the earth be struck with an anathema. The impious shall be burned, the converted shall enjoy the Sun.

Verse 1.

FOR BEHOLD THE DAY SHALL COME.) The day of the final judgment upon the Jews, and an image of the final judgment upon the human race.

BURNING AS A FURNACE.) Burning like an oven. Thus the Chaldean, the LXX, ὡς κλίβανον: there is little difference between a clibanus and a furnace. See what is said at Matt. 6:30. The conflagration of the Temple and the city is referred to.

AND ALL THE PROUD SHALL BE.) Concerning whom see above [verse] 15.

STUBBLE, AND THE COMING DAY SHALL SET THEM ON FIRE.) They shall perish in those calamities.

WHICH SHALL NOT LEAVE THEM ROOT AND BRANCH.) They shall not even have children surviving, for whose sake they committed so many unjust crimes.

The Papists think that the discourse is about the day of the universal judgment according to the literal sense, whose precursor they contend will be the Prophet Elijah, but Grotius rightly departed from them here. Danaeus, whom Grotius likewise wished to follow in other matters, understands it of those disasters which the Jews suffered after the times of Malachi up to the advent of Christ, such as under the Greek Kings of Syria and Egypt, but this does not fit the context, and therefore Blessed Luther [understands it] of the power of the light of the Gospel, by which the whole Synagogue was to be consumed; most of our people, Osiander, Wigandus, Winckelmann, Tarnovius, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and others, judge that the true fire of the final judgment upon the Jews is treated here. Also among the Reformed, Villius, and indeed Gualtherus, although there might perhaps be doubt about this. Arias Montanus, among the Papists, also explains it of the first advent of Christ. And indeed that the destruction of Jerusalem is referred to, besides the above, the phrase concerning the judgment that would quickly follow the first advent in chapter 3, verse 5, 'you shall not leave root or branch,' confirms it. Likewise: 'You shall go forth and leap like fatted calves.' Likewise, 'the wicked shall be dust under the soles of your feet,' which do not seem to fit the final judgment so well, and the repeated promise of the first advent of the Messiah and his forerunner confirm this.

Concerning the threat 'it shall not leave them root or branch,' Gualtherus [says] thus: 'The root of the Jewish nation perished then, and with it the branches also were consumed: for the promises, the temple, the priesthood, along with all sacred things, and whatever symbols of divine grace they had hitherto possessed, were taken away from them. There followed a horrible dispersion of the whole nation, which stripped them of every form and name of both Church and State. And these indeed perished like stubble in the fire, while the Roman leaders themselves tried in vain to save the city.' Those who try to explain it as the hope of eternal life being cut off for the damned in the other world are undoubtedly twisting the text. Coccejus provides another meaning: 'It shall not leave them root and branch. They shall be separated like unfruitful and dead branches from the vine or olive tree, so that it may be made manifest that they have no communion, neither with the root nor with the branches, Rom. 11, v. 16, 17, 18.' The root is either Christ, the root of Jesse, Isa. 11:10, and of David, Rev. 5:5, supporting and vivifying all the children of God, or Abraham, to whom the promises were made, who is the father of all believers: from whose blessed seed they are separated through infidelity, and the judgment following it, and the calling of the Church to liberty. But who does not see that these things are more subtle than solid? The former sense is simpler, which he presented thus: 'Root and branch.' Both parts

“he shows that the polity will perish, namely the people, because “they will be in dispersion, and the government, because “they will have no magistrates, Hos. 3:4, Malach. 2:12. For the fathers of the flesh or the rulers are like the root, the remaining people like the branches. The comparison of the republic of Israel with a vine or vineyard is frequent.

He compares that day, however, to a burning furnace, the wicked to stubble, noting at once both the vehemence and the swiftness of the punishment. For suddenly and at that very time, when they would have feared nothing less, the Romans were present, besieging the city and storming it, so that the Emperor himself had to confess that this victory was not of human power but of divine might. For Josephus testifies, lib. 6 of the Jewish War, cap. 14, that Titus, when he had seen the valleys of the walls full of corpses and deep gore flowing down from the putrefied bodies, groaned and with outstretched hands called God to witness that that deed was not his own, as here the blessed Balduinus.

Latin:

CAPUT IV.

Iterum adventus Christi ejusque pro- dromi.

Prædicitur dies judicii adversus contemtores, ortusque Solis justitiæ & salutis & incre- menta fidelium cum commonitione memo- riæ legis Domini, ac promissione Eliæ alte- rius ante diem Domini venturi, ad conver- tendum Patres atque filios, ne terra percu- tiatur anathemate. Impius uretur conversus Sole fruetur.

Vers. 1.

ECCE ENIM DIES VENIET.) Dies judicii ultimi in Judæos, & imago judicii ultimi in humanum genus.

SUCCENSA QVASI CAMINUS.) Ardens velut furnus. Ita Chaldæus, LXX, ὡς κλίβανον: parum interest inter clibanum & furnum. Vide quæ ad Matth. 6, 30. re- spicitur incendium Templi & urbis.

ET ERUNT OMNES SUPERBI.) De quibus supra 15.

STIPULA, ET INFLAMMABIT EOS DIES VE- NIENS.) Peribunt in istis calamitatibus.

QVÆ NON DERELINQVET EIS RADICEM ET GERMEN.) Ne liberos quidem habebunt superstites, quorum causa tot injusta facinora fecerunt.

Pontificii de die judicii universalis secundum li- teralem sensum, sermonem esse putant, cujus præ- cursorem Eliam Prophetam fore contendunt, sed merito hic ab iis discessit Grotius. Danæus quem itidem in aliis sequi voluit Grotius, de iis cladibus accipit, quas post Malachiæ tempora usque ad Christi adventum passi sunt Judæi, velut sub Syriæ & Ægy- pti Regibus Græcis, sed hoc contextui non con- gruit, ideoque de vi lucis Evangelii, quo consumen- da tota Synagoga, B. Lutherus, de igne vero judicii novissimi in Judæos hic agi plerique nostri judicant Osiander, Wigandus, Winckelmann. Tarnovius, Pa- raphraste Vinarienses & alii. Etiam è Reformatis Villius, nec non Gualtherus, quamvis de hoc du- bium forte esse possit. De adventu Christi primo explicat quoque è Papistis Arias Montanus. Et sane exitium Hierosolymitanum respici, præter su- periora, de judicio adventum primum velociter subsequuturo cap. 3. v. 5. phrasis, non relinques ra- dicem aut ramum. Item: Exibitis & salietis sicut vi- tuli saginati. Item, impii erunt pulvis sub plantis pe- dum vestrorum, quæ non ita convenire videntur ex- tremo judicio, nec non iterata promissio adventus primi Messiæ, & prodromi ejus, confirmant.

De comminatione non relinquet eis radicem aut ramum, ita Gualtherus: Periit tunc Judaicæ gentis radix & cum illa rami quoque consumti sunt: Ablatæ enim sunt ab illis promissiones, templum, sacerdotium, una cum sacris omnibus, & quæcunque antehac divinæ gratiæ symbola habuerant. Secuta est gentis totius horribilis dispersio, quæ omnem Ecclesiæ simul & Republ. formam atque nomen ipsis eripuit. Et hæc qui- dem ut stipula in igne perierunt, ipsis Romanis ducibus urbem nequicquam servare conanti- bus. Qui explicare conantur de spe damnatis præ- cisa in altero seculo, ad vitam adspirandi æternam, textum sine dubio torquent, Coccejus alium tradit sensum: Non relinquet ipsis radicem & ramum. Se- parabuntur tanquam rami infrugiferi, & emortui à vite sive olea, ut manifestum fiat, eos non habere communionem, neque cum radice, neque cum ramis Rom. 11, v. 16. 17. 18. Radix est vel Christus, radix Jessæ Esa. 11. v. 10. & Davidis Apocal. 5. v. 5. portans & vivificans omnes filios Dei, vel Abra- ham, cui promissiones factæ sunt, qui est pater omnium credentium : à cujus semine benedi- cto separantur per infidelitatem, & eam conse- quens judicium, ac vocationem Ecclesiæ ad liber- tatem. Sed quis non videt hæc arguta magis esse quam solida: simplicior est prior sensus, quem ita exhibuit: Radix & ramus. Utramque partem

„politiæ oftendit perituram,populum scilicet,quia „in dissipatione erunt, & imperium, quia nullos „habebunt magistratus Hos.3,4. Malach.2,12. Nam patres carnis sive præsides radicis instar habent, populus reliquus ramorum. Frequens est reipu- blicæ Israelis comparatio cum vite vel vinea.

Comparat autem diem illum camino ardenti, impios stipulæ, notans simul & vehementiam & cele- ritatem pœnæ. Subito enim & eo imprimis tem- pore,quo nihil minus metuissent,aderant Romani, urbem obsidebant, & expugnabant, ut fateretur Imperator ipse,non esse istam felicitatem opis hu- manæ sed divinæ virtutis. Testatur enim Joseph. lib. 6. belli Jud. cap. 14. Titum, ubi plenis cada- veribus vidisset valles murorum, altamque saniem tabefactis corporibus defluentem, ingemuisse, & extentis manibus Deum testatum esse, factum illud non suum esse, ut hic B. Balduinus.

## 4:2
Vers. 2.

AND UNTO YOU THAT FEAR MY NAME SHALL THE SUN OF RIGHTEOUSNESS ARISE.) The Holy Spirit, that one whom Christ will obtain for those believing in him, will shine in your heart. See Eph. 5, 14.

By the Sun of righteousness Drusius understands the Sun kindly bestowing its light. Which Willius approves, if indeed righteousness denotes kindness, and Joel 2, 23, a large, copious, fruitful rain of righteousness is spoken of: so that thus the Sun of righteousness is a day shining kindly, serene, fruitful, which by its serenity brings health, abundance, and the affluence of all things. Afterwards, however, Willius acknowledges that by the Sun of righteousness Christ is denoted, because, just as the sun rises to us from on high and shines upon us: so Christ, having gone forth from heaven, his bridal chamber, and the bosom of the Father to finish his course, shone forth as the bridegroom of the Church. And just as the kindly sun illuminates and makes serene the whole face of the world and makes it joyful and quickens it: so Christ illuminates the blind hearts of men with his rays, exhilarates them, and impregnates them with every kind of blessing. Conf. John 1, 5. 9. cap. 8, 12. Willius also acknowledges that Christ is called the Sun of righteousness, because he makes men sparkle and shine by his righteousness, both imputed and inherent, which explanation will not have a place if righteousness denotes only kindness. And thus other interpreters explain it concerning Christ. For Christ is named the Sun, Psalm 18, and concerning him Zacharias, Luke 1, 78, says: the dayspring from on high has visited us, to illuminate all of us who sit in darkness and the shadow of death. He is called the light of the world, John 8, 12, illuminating all men, chapter 1, 9. Furthermore, he is the sun of righteousness, because as the sun is the fountain of all light, so from Christ is all righteousness, Jerem. 22, 6, 1 Cor. 1, 30. And regarding that illumination of Christ, of which Ephes. 5, 14 speaks, it is because he himself rises in our hearts as the Morning Star, 2 Peter 1, 19, and as the Sun of righteousness, so that he may fill the same with the light of grace, salvation, and joy, conf. Apoc. 22, 16. This rising of the Sun of righteousness, which Malachi promises, is opposed partly to the shadows of the Old Testament, where our righteousness before God was only obscurely prefigured; but through CHRIST in the New Testament it was brought forth in actual fact, and through the doctrine of the Gospel was propagated quite clearly into the whole world: and partly to our natural darkness. For Christ was to come into the world for this reason, that he might illuminate all who are born into the world, John 1, v. 9, as the blessed Balduinus holds here; he is called the sun of righteousness, not only because he himself is righteous in all things, in whose mouth no iniquity was found, but also because he has been made our righteousness, whence he also received the name of the righteous servant, Isa. 53, nay even Jehovah, who is our righteousness Jerem. 23. & 33. They are therefore parhelia or rather will-o'-the-wisps, whatever is joined to this sun, whether concerning the merits of the saints or our own little works, from which there is no illumination, but rather greater obscurity from time to time. Just as therefore the Moon borrows its light from the Sun; so the Church has its splendor and its life witness, that in his name they have remission of sins, who believe in him Acts 10. v. 43. Concerning which B. Luther Tom. VII. Altenburg. p. 713. A new sun will shine / he says / not such a one / as even the irrational animals see / but the sun of righteousness / which makes righteous / which gives such brightness / whereby people become righteous / and delivered from sins / whereby is boiled out all harmful moisture of fleshly lusts. The same brightness is the word of the Gospel / which penetrates the hearts / and the sun is seen only with the eyes of the heart / that is / through faith / and is much more to the God-fearing / than this visible and bodily sun. For through the Holy Spirit it shines day and night / and the clouds cannot hinder it / but it is always in the rising. To you / who fear my name / shall arise. That is / to those / who are humbled / who are not wanton and proud / do not trust in their works / but acknowledge / that they are sinners. Regarding the Holy Spirit, who might understand, besides Grotius, not easily will any be found. Coccejus explains it concerning Christ, but interprets the rising as the nativity, doctrine, works, passions, resurrection, ascension into heaven, effusion of the Holy Spirit, removal of the veil in the destruction of the temple, city, and princes, which others, however, more correctly interpret as the rising through the preaching of the Gospel.

Same verse.

AND HEALTH IN HIS WINGS.) That is, rays: his rays will bring supreme health to the soul.

By the feathers or wings of the Messiah some understand the wings of grace and mercy, under which he wished to gather even the Jerusalemites Matt. 23. v. 37. others the doctrine of the Gospel, by which he himself with all his merit is carried around in the world no differently than the sun is as it were brought to us by its rays. Hence health and exhilaration arise for contrite souls, and for those dismayed by a serious recollection of their natural depravity, just as true recreation of the soul follows from the sight of solar rays among those who were once deprived of the use of light. And just as when the sun approaches us more closely in the spring season the air becomes healthier, and all things revive which previously seemed dead in the winter season: so together with the arrival of Christ in the flesh life returned to those who were dead in sins, and from his salutary doctrine they received flower and vigor, who under the winter of temptations were deprived of all juice of true consolation, whence his word is called the word of life John 6. v. 68. For spiritual healing, medicine is required, cleansing from sins, healing through the stripes of CHRIST, purification of the conscience from dead works, vivification, renovation, &c. all of which we have under the wings of the Sun of righteousness, from whose rising and light is life itself and the preservation of spiritual life. Conf. Apoc. 22. vers. 2. B. Luther in h. l. And health under the same's wings. From this you see clearly / that one cannot understand this passage as the Last Day / when the judgment will be / but now there is health and protection under the shadow of Christ. Such a kingdom is Christ's kingdom / wherein he himself is Mediator and protecting Lord / as a hen defends her chicks from the vulture / whoever now wishes to be safe from God's wrath and judgment / upon which the law presses / let him flee under the wings of Christ / under the law is weakness and damnation / but under the wings of Christ and under the Gospel health / strength and salvation. The sun rises / when one preaches the Gospel / one flies under the wings / when one believes. Although you are indeed a sinner / yet you will be healthy / when you fly under his wings / you will not fear death / the lust of the flesh will not overcome you.

AND YOU SHALL GO FORTH.) God will lead you out as if by the hand from the city about to fall. See what is above III, 6.

AND YOU SHALL LEAP AS CALVES FROM THE STALL.) Joyful with the peace of conscience and presuming in their mind a similar liberation once in the general judgment, Acts 8, 8. c. 13, 32. c. 15, 3. c. 20, 24. Rom. 5, 13. c. 14, 17. Gal. 5, 22. Phil. 1, 4. Coloss. 1, 11. 1. Thess. 1, 6. 1. Petr. 1, 8.

That 'going forth' is wrongly understood as a going forth from the city. For as health is to be referred to the soul, and what is added further: 'you shall leap like a calf,' as Grotius admits, so also the 'going forth' is not to be understood otherwise than according to the opinion of Christ in John 10:9: 'I am the door; if anyone enters by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and find pasture.' Compare Psalm 23:29 [sic]. Psalm 26. For in these places there is discourse concerning the leading of the LORD and the 'going forth' under a double similitude. Blessed Luther rightly says: 'You shall go out and in and increase like fatted calves. This is the fruit of faith and the kingdom of Christ, namely a joyful conscience and public confession, thanksgiving, joy in tribulation, preaching and converting others. It is the nature of joy to increase, for sadness causes decrease. A Christian thinks the whole world is his, walks openly, and does not seek corners.' 'Like the fatted calves, so,' he says, 'will you also be, fatted in the righteousness of faith and joyful: your pasture is Christ.' Similarly also the Weimar Paraphrase and others of our own. Nothing is being discussed concerning a leading out from the city, but concerning spiritual leading and increase in faith and the knowledge of Christ, by which the souls of the pious are as it were fattened. Compare Isaiah 55. Blessed Tarnovius [discusses] the benefits which from this

We have the Sun of righteousness, thus he gathered from these words of the Prophet, that indeed these are: I. The imputation of righteousness, since he is the sun of righteousness Rom. 3. v. 25. II. The remission of sins, because he is the sun coming with healing in his wings as a Physician Matth. 9. v. 12. Who would take away the diseases of the soul, that is, sins, and would protect those already cured of that disease Matth. 11. v. 21. Psal. 5. v. 12. & 91. v. 1. 4. Matth. 23. v. 37. CHRIST however is the sun of righteousness full of grace, so that we may receive grace for grace from him John 1. v. 14. 16. 17. III. Renewal, which is similar to a procession. For you will no longer be languishing or lying down in one place with spiritual diseases, but you will proceed walking continually in the way of the Lord Psal. 1. v. 1. IV. Increases of gifts, and you will grow like stall-fed calves, abounding in all things you will leap for joy, like those calves. Therefore, a going forth into the pastures of the Gospel and spiritual fattening and luxury is indicated, nor is it said without emphasis you shall go forth and grow like stall-fed calves. For they are accustomed to enclose calves to be fattened, so that they may grow fat more easily. And therefore an unusual, free, and pleasant fattening is noted. Otherwise, that simile of calves is accustomed to be used in a bad sense to denote the insults of the impious, petulance, ferocity, intractability, contumacy, luxury, such as we see dominating in this species of cattle. Thus Jerem. 46. v. 20. 21. Egypt is a very beautiful heifer. Also her mercenaries are like stall-fed calves. Hos. 4. Israel is a refractory heifer, refractory. And chap. 10. v. 11. Ephraim is a trained heifer, loving to thresh. Therefore, the opposites of all these are here foretold in a good sense concerning the pious, exultation, joy, gladness in Christ. Willius in h. l. Jerome, Remigius, Albert the Great understand a going forth from this world and from this life, Cornelius à Lapide a going forth from the sepulchers with Tertullian in his book on the resurrection of the flesh chap. XXXI. and Theodoret. Whence Cornelius further gathers full vigor, joy, and the gift of agility, a leap from mire into heaven, from death into life, celestial choirs and applause: all ἀπροσδιονύσως (irrelevant).

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET ORIETUR VOBIS TIMENTIBUS NOMEN MEUM SOL JUSTITIÆ.) Spiritus Sanctus, ille quem Christus in se credentibus impetrabit, lucebit in corde ve- stro. Vide Eph. 5, 14.

Per Solem justitiæ intelligit Drusius Solem be- nigne largientem lucem suam. Quod approbat Willius, siquidem justitia benignitatem denotet, ac Joel. 2, 23. pluvia justitiæ larga, copiosa, frugifera dicatur: ut ita Sol justitiæ sit dies benigne lucens, sere- na,fructuosa,qui serenitate sua sanitatem, copiam- que & affluentiam omnium importet. Postea ta- men agnoscit Willius, per Solem justitiæ Christum denotari, quia, quemadmodum sol ex alto nobis o- ritur, & affulget: ita Christus ex cœlo thalamo suo, sinuque patris egressus ad conficiendum cursum suum ceu sponsus Ecclesiæ illuxit. Et quemad- modum sol benignus illuminat & serenat univer- sam mundi faciem eandemque lætificat & vivificat: ita Christus corda hominum cæca radiis suis illu- strat, exhilarat, & benedictione omnimoda impræ- gnat. Conf. Johan. 1, 5. 9. cap. 8, 12. Agnoscit e- tiam Willius Christum Solem justitiæ dici, quia justitia sua tum imputata tum inhærente homines co- ruscare & splendescere facit, quæ explicatio locum non habebit, si justitia solum benignitatem notet. Atq; ita de Christo explicant cæteri interpp. Nam Christus nominatur Sol, Pfal. 18. & de eo Zacharias Luc. 1, 78. visitavit nos oriens ex alto, illuminandi nos omnes, qui in tenebris & umbra mortis sedent. Dicitur lux mundi Joh. 8, 12. illuminans omnes ho- mines cap. 1, 9. Adhæc sol justitiæ est, quia ut sol scaturigo est omnis lucis, ita à Christo omnis est ju- stitia, Jerem.22, 6. I. Cor. 1, 30. & ad illuminationem illam Christi, de qua Ephes. 5,14. facit, quod in cor- dibus nostris ipse oriatur ceu Phofphorus 2. Petr.1, 19. & tanquam Sol justitiæ, ut luce gratiæ, salutis & gaudii eadem repleat, conf. Apoc. 22, 16. Ortus hic Solis justitiæ, quem promittit Malachias, oppo- nitur partim umbris Veteris Testamenti, ubi nostra coram Deo justitia obscure tantum præfiguraba- tur; per CHRISTUM autem in Novo Testamen- to ipso actu parta, & per doctrinam Evangelii in omnem orbem terrarum satis clare propagata fuit: partim naturalibus nostris tenebris. Ideo enim Christus venturus erat in mundum, ut illumina- ret omnes, qui nati sunt in mundo, Johan. 1. v. 9. ut hic habet B. Balduinus; justitiæ sol nomina- tur, non tantum quia ipse justus per omnia est, in cujus ore non est inventa iniquitas, verum etiam quia nostra factus est justitia, unde & nomen servi justi accepit Esa. 53. quin & Jehovah, qui nostra sit justitia Jerem. 23. & 33. sunt igitur parelii aut potius ignes fatui, quæcunque vel de sanctorum meritis vel nostris opellis huic soli adjunguntur, à quibus nulla sit illuminatio, sed major subinde obscuritas. Quemadmodum igitur Luna à Sole suum mutua- tur lumen; ita Ecclesia splendorem & vitam suam habet à Christo, cui omnes testimonium perhi- bent, quod in nomine suo remissionem peccato- rum habeant, qui credunt in eum Actor. 10. v. 43. Quo de B. Lutherus Tom. VII. Altenburg. p. 713. Es wird / spricht er / eine neue Sonne schei- nen / nicht eine solche / die auch die unver- nünfftigen Thiere sehen / sondern die Sonne der Gerechtigkeit / welche gerecht macht / die solchen Glantz gibt / dadurch Die Leute gerecht werden / und erlediget von Sünden / dadurch außgekocht wird alle schädliche Feuchtigkeit der fleischli- chen Lüsten. Derselbe Glantz ist das Wort deß Evangelii / welches die Hertzen durchdringet / und die Sonne wird allein gesehen mit den Augen deß Hertzens / das ist / durch den Glauben / und ist den Gott- fürchtigen vielmehr / denn diese sichtbare und leibliche Sonne. Denn durch den Heiligen Geist scheinet sie Tag und Nacht / und können sie die Wolcken nicht verhindern / sondern ist allezeit im Auff- gange. Euch / die ihr meinen Namen fürchtet / sol auffgehen. Das ist / denen / Die gedemüthiget sind / die nicht muth- willig und hoffärtig sind / nicht auff ihre Wercke vertrauen / sondern erkennen / Daß sie Sünder sind. De Spiritu Sancto qui intelligant, præter Grotium, non facile invenietur ullus. Coccejus de Christo explicet, sed ortum in- terpretatur de nativitate, doctrina, operibus, pas- sionibus, resurrectione, ascensione in cœlos, effu- sione Spiritus Sancti, ablatione veli in destructione templi, urbis & principum, quem vero rectius de ortu per prædicationem Evangelii alii interpre- tantur.

Vers. eod.

ET SANITAS IN PENNIS EJUS.) Id est, radiis: radii ejus sanitatem summam animo adferent.

Per pennas seu alas Messiæ nonnulli intelligunt alas gratiæ & misericordiæ, sub quibus congregatos etiam Hierosolymitanos volebat Matth. 23. v. 37. alii doctrinam Evangelii, qua ipse cum omni suo me- rito circumfertur in mundo non secus atque sol ra- diis suis quasi ad nos advehitur. Hinc sanitas & ex- hilaratio contritis animis, & ex seria depravationis suæ naturalis recordatione consternatis oritur, quemadmodum ex conspectu radiorum solarium vera sequitur recreatio animi apud eos, qui lumi- nis usura aliquando fuere destituti. Et sicuti sole ad nos propius accedente tempore verno aër fit salu- brior, omniaque reviviscunt, quæ antea tempore hyberno emortua videbantur: ita una cum adven- tu Christi in carnem vita rediit iis, qui in peccatis erant mortui, & ex salutari ejus doctrina florem & vigorem acceperunt, qui sub hyeme tentatio- num omni succo veræ consolationis erant destitu- ti, unde verbum ejus vocatur verbum vitæ Johan. 6. v. 68. Ad sanationem spiritualem requiritur me- dicina, mundatio à peccatis, sanatio per vibices CHRISTI, conscientiæ purgatio ab operibus mortuis, vivificatio, renovatio, &c. quæ o- mnia sub alis Solis justitiæ habemus, à cujus or- tu & luce vita ipsa & conservatio vitæ spiritualis est. Conf. Apoc. 22. vers. 2. B. Lutherus in h. l. Und Heyl unter desselben Flügeln. Hier- auß siehstu klärlich/ daß man dieses Stück nicht kan vom Jüngsten Tage verstehen/ da das Gerichte seyn wird/ jetzt aber ist Heyl und Schutz unter dem Schatten Christi. Ein solches Reich ist Christi Reich/ darinnen er selbst Mitt- ler und Schutz-HErr ist/ wie eine Hen- ne ihre Küchlein vor dem Geyer verthei- diget/wer nun wil vor Gottes Zorn und Gerichte sicher seyn/ auff welche das Ge- setz dringet/ der fliehe unter die Flügel Christi/ unter dem Gesetz ist Schwach- heit und Verdammnüß/ unter den Flü- geln Christi aber und unter dem Evan- gelio Gesundheit/ Stärcke und Heyl. Die Sonne gehet auff/wenn man das Evangelium prediget/ unter die Flügel fleugt man/ wenn man gläubet. Ob du nun wol ein Sünder bist/ so wirst du doch gesund seyn/ wenn du unter seine Flügel fleugst/ du wirst den Tod nicht fürchten/ deß Fleisches Lust wird dich nicht überwinden.

ET EGREDIEMINI.) Deus vos velut manu edu- cet ex urbe ruitura. Vide quæ supra III, 6.

ET SALIETIS SICUT VITULI DE ARMENTO.) Læti pace conscientiæ & similem olim liberationem in communi judicio præsumentes animo, Actor. 8, 8. c. 13, 32. c. 15, 3. c. 20, 24. Rom. 5, 13. c. 14, 17. Gal. 5, 22. Phil. 1, 4. Coloss. 1, 11. 1. Thess. 1, 6. 1. Petr. 1, 8.

Egressus ille perperam de egressu ex urbe intelli- gitur. Nam ut sanitas ad animum referenda, & quæ porro adduntur: salietis sicut vitulus, fatente Gro- tio, ita etiam egressus aliter intelligendus non est, quam juxta sententiam Christi Johan. 10, 9. Ego sum ostium, per me si quis introierit, salvabitur, & ingredietur & egredietur, & pascua inveniet. Confer. Psal. 23. vers. 29. Psal. 26. His enim locis de deductione DOMINI & egressu, sub simili- tudine gemina sermo est: Recte B. Lutherus: Ihr solt auß- und eingehen/ und zuneh- men wie die Mast-Kälber. Dieses ist die Frucht deß Glaubens und Reichs Chri- sti/ nemlich ein fröliches Gewissen und öffentliche Bekäntnüß/ Dancksagung/ Freude in Trübsal/ predigen und ande- re bekehren. Zunehmen ist der Freude Art/ denn Traurigkeit machet Abneh- men. Ein Christ meynet/die gantze Welt seyn sein/gehet offenbar daher/suchet nicht Winckel. Wie die Mast-Kälber/ also/ spricht er/ werdet ihr auch seyn/ gemä- stet in der Gerechtigkeit deß Glaubens und frölich: Eure Weide ist Christus. Similiter etiam Paraphrast. Vinariens. & alii è no- stris. Nihil de eductione ex urbe, de spirituali de- ductione & incremento in fide & agnitione Christi agitur, qua animi piorum quasi saginantur. Con- fer Esa. 55. B. Tarnovius beneficia, quæ ab hoc

Sole justitiæ habemus, ita ex hisce Prophetæ verbis collegit, quod nempe ista sint : I. Justitiæ imputatio, siquidem est sol justitiæ Roman. 3. vers. 25. II. pec- catorum remissio, quia est sol cum curatione in alis ipsius veniens ut Medicus Matth. 9. vers. 12. Qui animi morbos, hoc est, peccata tolleret, & jam ab illo morbo curatos protegeret Matth. 11. vers. 21. Psal. 5. v. 12. & 91. v. 1. 4. Matth. 23. v. 37. CHRI- STUS autem sol justitiæ gratia plenus est, ut gra- tiam pro gratia inde capiamus Johan. 1. v. 14. 16. 17. III. Renovatio, quæ similis est processioni. Non enim amplius morbis spiritualibus languidi aut decumbentes in uno loco hærebitis, sed procedetis in via Domini ambulantes jugiter Psal. 1. vers. 1. IV. Donorum incrementa, & augefcetis vituli sagi- narii, omnium rerum abundantes præ lætitia ge- stietis, ut illi vituli. Egressus ergo in pascua Evan- gelii & saginatio ac luxuries spiritualis indigitatur, nec sine emphasi dicitur egrediemini & augefcetis ut vituli saginarii. Nam solent vitulos saginandos includere, ut facilius pinguefiant. Ideoque nota- tur pinguefactio insolita, libera, ac jucunda. Solet alioquin similitudo illa de vitulis in malam partem adhiberi ad insultus impiorum, proterviam, fero- ciam, intractabilitatem, contumaciam, luxuriam notandam, qualia in hac pecorum specie videmus dominari. Ita Jerem. 46. v. 20. 21. Ut vitula speciosissima est Ægyptus. Etiam mercenarii ejus ut vituli saginati. Hos. 4. Ut vitula refractaria refractarius est Israël. Et cap. 10. vers. 11. Ephraim vitula est edocta, amans triturare. Istorum igitur omnium contraria hic in bonam partem de piis prænunciantur, exultatio, gaudium, lætitia in Chri- sto. Willius in h. l. Hieronymus, Remigius, Alber- tus M. egressum de hoc seculo & ex hac vita, Cor- nelius à Lapide egressum de sepulchris intelligunt cum Tertulliano lib. de resurrectione carnis cap. XXXI. & Theodoreto. Unde Cornelius porro colligit plenum vigorem, lætitiam & dotem agili- tatis, saltum è cœno in cœlum, è morte in vitam, cœlestes choros & plausus : omnia ἀπροσδιο- νύσως.

## 4:3
Vers. 3.

AND YOU SHALL TREAD DOWN THE IMPIOUS WHEN THEY SHALL BE ASHES UNDER THE SOLE OF YOUR FEET.) If ever you return to Jerusalem, there you shall tread upon the ashes of many impious men in the burned city. After the destruction, in the city moderately restored, and called Aelia, there was a Church of Christians under the Bishops, Simeon, Justus, Zacchaeus, Tobias, Benjamin, John, Matthias, Philip, Seneca, Justus, Levi, Ephres, Joseph, Judas; who all were of the circumcision, as Eusebius testifies in his Chronicle.

Not about treading the land of Jerusalem, or about a return to a city restored in any way, to which the Jews are said to have returned rashly from the perishing city, even if Christian Bishops from the circumcision sat there; as the former things treat of health and fattening and spiritual pleasure, so these are to be taken primarily concerning the spiritual treading down of the impious or concerning victory against the same: for those are said to be trodden by the feet who, having been brought under power, are as it were subjected to the feet of the victor, see John 10. v. 24. Ps. 110, 1. Rom. 16. v. 20. therefore a total subjection and treading down is noted, when the impious are said to become ashes under the sole of the feet of the faithful, so that solid tranquility and liberation from enemies may be implied.

But although some understand these things concerning the victory which Christian Emperors sometimes obtained over tyrants, to whom they were previously forced to be subject, others explain them only concerning a spiritual victory: yet it can be joined with a spiritual victory in this way, that by this metaphorical formula of speaking the defeat of any enemies is proclaimed, but primarily that victory which is obtained by the sword of the spirit. For then they tread the impious like ashes or mud, when by the preaching of the Gospel they curb the mouths of idolaters, or when by the ministry of the spirit they so confound and defeat the enemies of the truth, that they become a contempt even to those to whom they were previously of the highest value 1. Corinth. 10. v. 14. Blessed Luther also handed down this sense concerning victory against the tyrants who are enemies of the Church, no less than heretics: You will tread down the godless: The Christian Church has enemies at all times, either tyrants, or heretics, or false brothers. The God-fearing always have to do with heresy, and yet they perish at last, and become nothing, ashes and powder, etc. But the truth of GOD remains eternally. The fire of CHRIST will make them into ashes, therefore they can easily be trodden down. They indeed tread us with their feet at first, but at last the little wheel will turn around, nothing grows from ashes.

But the Jews in vain promise themselves earthly victories to be obtained over the nations, so that they may live securely thereafter in the holy land. For it is a matter concerning Christ, whose kingdom is not of this world, Matth. 20, 25. 26. Luc. 22, 25. 28. John 18, 36. And the promise here is made to those who are fearing the name of the Lord, and betake themselves to the sun of righteousness by true faith; but to the Jews, extreme destruction is denounced.

Vers. same.

IN THE DAY THAT I MAKE.) Explain as above III, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET CALCABITIS IMPIOS CUM FUERINT CINIS SVB PLANTA PEDVM VESTRORVM.) Si quando redibitis Hierosolyma, ibi calcabitis in urbe incen- sa multorum impiorum cineres. Post excidium in urbe modice instaurata, dictaque Ælia, fuit Ecclesia Christiano- rum sub Episcopis, Simeone, Justo, Zachæo, Tobia, Benja- mine, Johanne, Matthia, Philippo, Seneca, Justo, Levi, Ephre, Jose, Juda; qui omnes ex circumcisione fuere, ut testatur in Chronico Eusebius.

Non de calcanda terra Jerusalem, aut de redi- tu in urbem aliquo modo restauratam, adquam Judæi è peritura urbe egressi temere rediisse dicuntur, etfi Episcopi Christiani ex circumcisione egressi ibi- dem sederint; ut de sanitate & saginatione, ac volu- ptate spirituali priora agunt, ita hæc imprimis de spirituali conculcatione impiorum accipienda vel de victoria adversus eosdem : nam pedibus calcari dicuntur, qui sub potestatem redacti, victoris pe- dibus quasi subjiciuntur, vid. Joh. 10. v. 24. Ps. 110, 1. Rom. 16. vers. 20. omnimoda ergo subjectio & con- culcatio notatur, cum impii dicuntur fieri cinis sub planta pedum fidelium, ut solida tranquillitas & li- beratio ab hostibus innuatur.

Etsi autem nonnulli hæc de victoria, quam Chri- stiani Imperatores interdum à tyrannis reporta- runt, quibus antea servire coacti fuere, intelligant alii de spirituali solum victoria explicent : con- jungi tamen cum spirituali victoria hac ratione il- la potest, ut hac metaphorica loquendi formula ho- stium quorumvis devictio, imprimis autem ea vi- ctoria prædicatur, quæ gladio spiritus obtinetur. Tunc enim calcant impios tanquam cineres sive lu- tum, quando prædicatione Evangelii ora idolola- trarum compescunt, aut quando ministerio spiri- tus hostes veritatis ita confundunt & debellant, ut iis quoque fiant despectui, quibus antea in summo erant pretio 1. Corinth. 10. v. 14. Quem sensum de victoria adversus hostes Ecclesiæ tyrannos, non mi- nus quam hæreticos tradidit quoque B. Lutherus: Ihr werdet die Gottlosen zertreten: Die Christliche Kirche hat allezeit Feinde/ent- weder die Tyrannen/oder Ketzer/oder fal- sche Brüder. Mit Ketzerey haben die Gottfürchtigen allezeit zu thun/ und sie kommen doch zuletzt umb / und werden zu nicht/ zu Aschen und Pulver/ 2c. Die Warheit GOTTES aber bleibet ewig- lich. Das Feuer CHRISTI wird sie zu Aschen machen / darumb können sie leichtlich zutreten werden. Sie treten uns wol erstlich mit Füssen / aber letztlich wird sich das Rädlein umkehren / auß Aschen wächset nichts.

Frustra autem Judæi victorias terrenas de genti- bus reportandas sibi pollicentur, ut secure dein- ceps in terra sancta agere possint. Agitur enim de Christo, cujus regnum non est de hoc mundo, Matth. 20, 25. 26. Luc. 22, 25. 28. Johan. 18, 36. Et illis hic facta est promissio, qui sunt timentes nomen Domini, & ad solem justitiæ se vera fide recipiunt; Judæis autem denunciatur extremus interitus.

Vers. eod.

IN DIE QVA EGO FACIO.) Explica ut supra III, 17.

## 4:4
Ver. 4.

REMEMBER THE LAW OF MOSES MY SERVANT, WHICH I COMMANDED HIM IN HOREB FOR ALL ISRAEL PRECEPTS AND JUDGMENTS) Namely until a better law should shine forth, 2 Pet. 1:19, Gal. 3:23, 24, the new covenant, to wit, of which mention has already been made in ch. 3:1.

Since many good years still remained until all those things should be fulfilled, and the Gospel concerning Christ already having suffered and died should be spread throughout the world, in the meantime he commends to them the doctrine of Moses, which they had received from his mouth on Mount Horeb. For he had foreseen what was to happen among the people of God, when no more prophecies would be granted to them, how the doctrine delivered of old by God through the ministry of Moses, and diligently guarded by the Prophets, would gradually fail, and would lose much of its genuine dignity on account of the corruptions of men. Therefore he exhorts them to keep in the meantime the precepts and judgments which they had received through the ministry of Moses, that is, the moral and ceremonial law. The former, lest they should make themselves unworthy of the benefits of the Messiah; the latter, indeed, so that they might daily progress in the faith of the Messiah, whose types the Mosaic ceremonies were, and not despair altogether on account of the delay of the Lord's coming. Concerning the distinction between the moral law, the ceremonial, which is noted by the name of statutes, and the forensic, which is noted by judgments, see B. Chemnitz, part II, Loci Communes, on the law, ch. I and IV.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

MEMENTOTE LEGIS MOSIS SERVI MEI, QVAM MANDAVI EI IN HOREB AD OMNEM ISRAEL PRÆCEPTA ET JUDICIA) Nempe donec lex melior affulserit, 2. Petr. 1, 19. Gal. 3, 23. 24. fœdus scilicet novum, cujus mentio jam facta c. 3, 1.

Quum adhuc anni bene multi restarent, donec ista omnia implerentur, & Evangelium de Chri- sto jam passo atque mortuo in orbem terrarum diffunderetur, interim doctrinam Mosis eis com- mendat, quam ex ore ejus in monte Horeb acce- perant. Viderat enim quid futurum sit in populo Dei, cum nulli amplius ipsis concederentur Pro- phetiæ, quomodo doctrina antiquitus à Deo per ministerium Mosis tradita, & à Prophetis sedulo custodita, paulatim defectura sit, & de genuina sua dignitate propter corruptelas hominum quam- plurimum amissura. Ideo hortatur, ut custodiant interim præcepta & judicia, quæ per ministerium Mosis acceperant, id est, legem moralem & cere- monialem. Illam, ne semetipsos beneficiis Meffiæ faciant indignos: hanc vero, ut in fide Meffiæ, cu- jus typi erant ceremoniæ Mosaïcæ, indies profici- ant, neque propter moram adventus Dominici o- mnino desperent. De discrimine legis moralis, ceremonialis, quæ statutorum nomine, & forensis, quæ per judicia notatur, vide B. Chemnit. part. II. LL. CC. de lege c. I. & IV.

## 4:5
Verse 5.

BEHOLD I WILL SEND YOU ELIJAH THE PROPHET.) You will be destitute of prophets for a time. The first prophet after me will be that pointer to the Messiah, of whom above 3, 1. In this sense it is true what the Jews say, that the Messiah must be anointed by Elijah, that is, as it were, introduced into the possession of his office, which was formerly done by anointing. Elijah is here called John the Baptist, who came in the spirit of Elijah, sparing neither the people nor the Kings, Luke 1, 17. Matt. 11, 14. 17, 11. 12. John is thus called Elijah, just as Phinehas is Elijah himself to the Hebrews because of a similar zeal in the things of God. Well, however, a prophet, as Matt. 11, 9. he will tell you what things must be done beyond the law and will point out Christ who is to say the rest. Thus here is the connection of the old and new covenant through John, Matt. 11, 13.

Regarding the opinion of the Jews and Judaizers, Jerome says thus on this passage: "The Jews and Judaizing heretics, before their τὸ λειμμένον, think that Elijah is to come and will restore all things. Whence also the question is proposed to Christ in the Gospel: Why do the Pharisees say that Elijah is to come? To whom he answers: Elijah indeed will come, and if you are willing to receive it, he has already come, understanding John in Elijah. They expected the Tishbite by metempsychosis, as also R. David Kimchi: I send you Elijah. The meaning is: that his soul which had ascended into heaven will return into a created body, similar to the first body. For his first body had returned to the earth, namely, as every element to its element. But after God restores him to life in a body, he will send him to the God of judgment. Why then do the Scribes say that it is necessary that Elijah come first. Christ handled this question in such a way that he taught that a third Elijah was not yet to be expected, which had seemed so to some, but that the Elijah promised by Malachi had already come, and Christ Matt. 11, 7. If you are willing to receive this, he is the Elijah who was to come and the Angel Luke 1, 17. He himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah. B. Asselm. The words of Christ Matt. 17, 11. concerning a third Elijah are interpreted by B. Luther with this argument: "He who will come and has already come is not one. But in verse 11 he speaks of him who will come, but in verse 12 of him who has already come, therefore the discourse is not about the same, but a double Elijah. Compare also the Oration of B. Tarnovius on the three Elijahs. But the minor premise is less firm, for Christ does not speak in v. 11 of him who is to come after his advent, but who was to come after the times of Malachi. For this must be referred here to the time of the prophecy. i.e. Malachi did not say this falsely, for Elijah has already come. The prophecy was fulfilled by John the Baptist coming in the spirit and power of Elijah, as is rightly held in the Junio-Tremellian notes on this passage. Elijah indeed ἔρχεται comes, here ἐλεύσεται. For this is not said with respect to the deed itself; for thus he had already come; but with respect to the prophecies of the O.T. just as Matt. 11, 41. where it is also to be observed that the word πρῶτον is to be rendered 'first' i.e. "Why then do the Scribes say that Elijah must come first, i.e. before the Messiah comes. Erasmus in his paraphrase on this passage: A certain scruple had taken hold of the minds of the disciples from the fact that they had seen Elijah standing by Jesus, they propose this to him while on the way. What is it, therefore, they say, that the scribes, teaching the advent of the Messiah, are accustomed to say on the authority of Malachi, that before the Messiah comes, Elijah the Tishbite is to come. But he did not precede your advent, but has only today been seen on the mountain.

Vain also is the fiction of the Papists, who imagine that Elijah the Tishbite will return to these lands with Enoch, who are to oppose the Anti-Christ and be killed by him. Which fable, even if similar things have been produced by Papias and certain others seduced by him of old, needs no refutation, but collapses by its own vanity. Jerome explains it not as Elijah being sent, but as the whole choir of prophets being sent in Elijah, which he seems to understand figuratively, because he interprets Elijah as 'my God', and Tishbi as 'conversion', that is, he says Moses is the whole choir of prophets. And the Fathers disagree here: on which see B. Gerhard, Loci Communes, on the Last Judgment, §. 108. Nor do the Papists agree on that fable. For the Jesuit Maldonatus contends with Victorinus that not Enoch but Moses will come with Elijah, whom this Cornelius à Lapide therefore taxed; finally, Burgensis, Arias, and Clarius acknowledge on this passage that Elijah is the Baptist, to whom the Jesuit Lapideus opposes primarily the passage Eccl. XLIX. 10. because this Elijah is the precursor of the second advent of Christ: but that book is Apocryphal: and the present passage is falsely taken concerning the precursor of the second advent of Christ, when it is clearly explained by the Angel Luke I. 19. and by Christ Matt. XI. and XVII. as the precursor of the first advent. Augustinus Eugubinus in Recogn. Vet. Testam. in chapter II of Genesis, as also Catharinus in his work on the consummation of Christ's glory, teach that Enoch and Elijah enjoy the beatific vision and reign in heaven in glorious bodies. How then can they descend to the earth from heaven, how can they be killed by the Anti-Christ?

There are those who think that Malachi also looked to the advent of Elijah the Tishbite himself, and think that it was fulfilled when Elijah appeared to Christ on the mountain Matt. XVII. see B. Wigandus on this passage, but since the Prophet prophesies of an Elijah who is to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, which was not done when Elijah appeared on the mountain, and the angel clearly teaches that it was fulfilled in John, who in the spirit and power of Elijah preceded Christ and prepared the way for him, it cannot be understood of the person of Elijah at the same time.

BEFORE THE DAY OF THE LORD COMES, GREAT AND TERRIBLE,) i.e. of the last judgment upon the Jews Acts II. 20.

Some of the Fathers and Papists, with the Jews, understand the great day of the last judgment, in which the whole world will be judged; from whom Grotius deservedly departs here, since we have Christ as the interpreter of this oracle, which is to be understood of John the Baptist, the forerunner of the first advent. But although the Grotian explanation concerning the great day of the last judgment upon the Jews is somewhat more correct, it nevertheless does not deserve approval, because it is clear from Matt. 17:10 that the scribes had gathered from this passage that Elijah must come before the Messiah, which Christ confirms: but He says that it was fulfilled in John, verses 11 and 12. Since, therefore, the scribes understood not a forerunner of the final judgment upon the Jews, but a forerunner of the advent of Christ, and Christ ratified that explanation, those who understand it of the day of the destruction of Jerusalem contradict Christ. Nor do they any less contradict the Angel Gabriel, inasmuch as he in Luke 1:17 openly explains this passage concerning the forerunner who was to precede Christ in His prophetic office for the conversion of the unfaithful to the wisdom of the just, and not indeed concerning the precursor of the final judgment of Christ upon the Jews. Nor does the comparison of the passage in Acts 2:20 contribute to this, where the prophecy of Joel, chapter 2:18, is treated, concerning which it has been dealt with in the vindications of that Prophet.

Wherefore the great day is called the day of the advent of Christ, which is rightly designated by the expression יום הגדול.

Others render this not as horrible but as reverend and honorable, just as that word is used in Gen. 29:17, according to the interpretation of Pererius, Marius, Cornelius à Lapide, and Bonfrerius, such as is entirely the day of the first advent, most worthy of all veneration and honor (Conf. Joel 2:31) which to all who fear God was truly salutary and pleasant, but was horrible and dreadful not only to the Jews, Pharisees, priests, and scribes, to whom it was like the refining fire of a goldsmith, and to the unbelieving Jews, to whom, because of their blindness and incredible hardness of heart, when they rejected, nay, even nailed to the cross the Lord of glory, and killed the author of life, who was bringing life and salvation to them, extreme destruction was imminent, or even with respect to the devils, whom he despoiled and led away, Col. 2:15, and who complain in Matt. 8:29 that Christ had come to torment them before the time, and also with respect to the infidels and the damned, to whom he preached in prison, not without the greatest confusion and horrible pain 1. Petr. 3:19, and also of others in this age, because that day of grace will testify against them before the tribunal of God, because they would not accept the accepted time, and spurned that counsel of God concerning their own salvation against themselves. Blessed Luther: Terrible, that is, which blinds the proud and enlightens the humble. Great, which makes glorious, living, righteous, and blessed. Wigandus, A GREAT DAY because of the advent of Christ, who is greatest in both person and office. TERRIBLE because of the Jews, and those not embracing the Messiah, but nailing him to the cross.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ECCE EGO MITTAM VOBIS ELIAM PRO-PHETAM.) Prophetis destituemini ad tempus. Primus Propheta post me erit ille Messiae monstrator, de quo supra 3, 1. Hoc sensu verum est quod dicunt Judaei, Messiam un-gi debere ab Elia, id est quasi in possessionem muneris sui introduci, quod olim per unctionem fiebat. Elias hic di-citur Johannes Baptista, qui in spiritu venit Eliae, nec po-pulo nec Regibus parcens, Luc. 1, 17. Matth. 11, 14. 17, 11. 12. Johannes sic Elias dictus, sicut Ebraeis Elias ipse Phinees ob parem in Dei rebus ardorem. Bene autem, Prophetam, ut Matth. 11, 9. is vobis dicet, quae praeter legem facienda sunt & Christum monstrabit caetera dicturum. Ita hic con-nexio est veteris novique foederis per Johannem, Matth. 11, 13.

De Judaeorum & Judaizantium sententia ita Hie-ronymus ad h. l. "Jud. & Judaizantes haeretici ante τὸ λειμμένον suum, putant Heliam esse venturum, & restituturum omnia. Unde & Christo in Evange-lio proponitur quaestio: Quid quod Pharisaei di-cunt, quod Helias venturus est? Quibus ille re-spondit: Helias quidem veniet, & si creditis, jam venit in Helia Johannem intelligens. Expecta-runt Thesbiten per μετεμψύχωσιν, ut etiam R. Da-vid Kimchi: Mitto vobis Eliam. Sensus est: quod redibit anima ipsius quae in coelum ascenderat, in corpus creatum, simile corpori primo. Nam corpus ipsius primum reversum erat in terram, nempe quodq; elementum ad elementum suum. Sed postquam vitae restituerit eum Deus in cor-pore, mittet eum ad Deum judicii. Quid igitur dicunt Scribae, oportere, ut Elias primum veniat. Quam quaestionem ita exequutus est Christus, ut docuerit non tertium adhuc expectandum esse Eliam, quod quibusdam visum, sed quod jam ve-nerit promissus à Malachia Elias, & Christus Matth. 11, 7. Si vultis hoc recipere, ipse est Elias, qui ven-turus erat & Angelus Luc. 1, 17. Ipse praecedet ante illum in Spiritu & virtute Eliae. B. Asselm. Verba Christi Matt. 17, 11. de Elia tertio B. Luthe-ro interpretatur, hoc argumento: "Is qui veniet & jam venit, non est unus. At vers. 11. loqui-tur de eo, qui veniet, versu vero 12. de eo qui jam venit, ergo non de eodem, sed gemino Elia sermo est. Conf. & Oratio B. Tarnovii de tribus Eliis. Sed minor minus firma est, nam non loquitur Christus v. 11. de eo qui post adventum suum venturus est, sed qui venturus erat post Mala-chiae tempora. Referri enim hic debet ad tempus Prophetiae. q. d. Malachias non falso hoc dixit, nam jam venit Elias. Completum fuit vaticinium Johanne Baptista veniente in spiritu & virtute Eliae, ut recte habetur in notis Junio-Tremellianis ad h. l. Elias quidem ἔρχεται venit, hic ἐλεύσαται. Non enim respectu ipsius rei gestae hoc dicitur; sic enim jam venerat; sed respectu prophetias V. T. perinde ut Matth. 11, 41. ubi observandum etiam vocem πρῶτον reddendam esse prius h. m. "Quid ergo Scribae dicunt quod Eliam oportet venire primum, h. e. prius videlicet quam Messias ve-niat. Erasmus in paraphrasi h. l. Scrupulus qui-dam ceperat animos discipulorum ex eo, quod Eliam conspexerant assistentem Jesu, hunc inter eundum proponunt illi. Quid est, igitur, inqui-unt, quod scribae docentes adventum Messiae dicere soleant ex autoritate Malachiae, quod priusquam veniat Messias, venturus est Elias Thesbitis. At is non praecessit adventum tuum, sed hodie demum visus est in monte.

Vanum etiam est Papistarum commentum, qui Eliam Thesbitem in has terras rediturum cum Enocho fingunt, qui se opposituri Anti-Christo, ab ipso occidendi sint. Quæ fabula, etsi à Papia & aliis quibusdam ab ipso seductis veteribus similia prodita sint, nulla eget refutatione, sed vanitate sua corruit. Hieronymus non de Elia mittendo, sed de mittendo in Elia omni Prophetarum choro, explicat, quod figurate videtur intelligere, quia E- liam interpretatur Deus meus, & Thesbi conversio- nem, id est, Mosen inquit omnem Prophetarum chorum. Et discrepant hic Patres: de quo vid. B. Gerhard. LL. CC. de Extr. Jud. §. 108. Nec de illa fabula consentiunt Papistæ. Maldonatus enim Jesuita cum Victorino contendit cum Elia, venturum non Enoch sed Mosen, quem hic Cor- nelius à Lapide ideo taxavit, denique Burgensis, Arias, Clarius agnoscunt h. l. Eliam esse Baptistam, quibus opponit Lapideus Jesuita imprimis locum Eccl. XLIX. 10. quod Elias hic præcursor sit se- cundi adventus Christi: sed liber ille Apocryphus est: & falso præsens locus de adventus Christi se- cundi prodromo accipitur, quum luculenter ab Angelo Luc. I. 19. & à Christo Matth. XI. & XVII. de adventus primi prodromo explicetur. Augusti- nus Eugubinus in Recogn. Vet. Testam. in cap. II. Genes. ut & Catharinus in opusc. de consummat. Chr. glor. Enochum & Eliam beatifica visione frui, & in cælis in corporibus gloriosis regnare docent. Quomodo ergo in terras descendere de cœlo, quomodo interfici ad Anti- Christo possunt?

Sunt qui Malachiam etiam respexisse censent adventum Eliæ ipsius Thesbites, atque id impletum putent cum Elias apparuit Christo in monte Matth. XVII. vid. B. Wigandus in h. l. sed quum Prophe- ta vaticinetur de Elia, qui conversurus sit corda patrum ad filios, quod non factum, cum Elias in monte apparuit, & angelus diserte id impletum doceat in Johanne in spiritu & virtute Eliæ præce- dente Christum, eique viam præparante, non po- test id simul de Eliæ persona intelligi.

ANTEQVAM VENIAT DIES DOMINI MA- GNUS ET HORRIBILIS,) Judicii sc. ultimi in Judæos Act. II. 20.

Diem magnum ultimi judicii, quo totus mun- dus judicabitur intelligunt cum Judæis patres nonnulli & Papistæ, à quibus hic merito discedit Grotius, quum habemus interpretem hujus ora- culi Christum, quod de primo adventus prodromo Johanne Baptista intelligendum sit. Etsi autem paulo rectius sese habeat Grotiana explicatio de die magno judicii ultimi in Judæos, calculum tamen non meretur, quia è Matth. XVII. 10. liquet scri- bas ex hoc loco collegisse, quod ante Messiam Elias venire debuerit, quod Christus confirmat: sed in Johanne impletum esse dicit vers. 11. 12. Quum ergo scribæ intellexerint non prodromum judicii novissimi in Judæos, sed prodromum adventus Christi, eamque explicationem Christus ratam ha- buerit, Christo repugnant, qui de die excidii Hie- rosolymitani intelligunt. Nec minus etiam repu- gnant Angelo Gabrieli, utpote qui Luc. I. 17. aper- te hunc locum de prodromo Christum in munere suo prophetico antecessuro ad conversionem infi- delium ad prudentiam justorum, explicat, non ve- ro de anteambulone judicii Christi novissimi in Ju- dæos. Neque loci Act. II. 20. collatio huc facit, ubi vaticinium Joel. c. II. 18. tractatur, de quo in vindiciis istius Prophetæ actum.

Quapropter dies magna dicitur dies adven- tus Christi, quæ voce יום הגדול recte designatur.

Hanc reddunt alii non horribilem sed reverendam & honorabilem, uti vox illa usurpatur Gen. XXIX. 17. interprete Pererio, Mario, Cornel. à Lapide & Bonfrerio, qualis omnino est dies adventus primi omni veneratione & honore dignissimus (Conf. Joel. 2, 31.) qui omnibus Deum timentibus vere salu- taris & jucundus, horribilis autem & tremendus fuit non modo Judæis, Pharisæis, sacerdotibus & scribis, quibus fuit quasi ignis conflans aurifabri, & Judæis incredulis, quibus ob cæcitatem & duriti- em cordis incredibilem, quum rejicerent, imo cru- ci affigerent Dominum gloriæ, & interficerent au- torem vitæ, qui vitam & salutem ipsis afferebat, imminebat extremus interitus, seu etiam respe- ctu Diabolorum, quos expoliavit & traduxit Col. 2, 15. quique Matth. 8, 29. queruntur, Christum venisse ante tempus eos torquere, nec non respectu infidelium ac damnatorum, quibus ἐν φυλακῇ ἐκήρυξεν non sine summa confusione & horribili dolore 1. Petr. III. 19. tum aliorum in hoc seculo, quia contra hos testabitur dies ille gratiæ coram tribunali Dei, quod tempus acceptum acceptare noluerint, consilium illud Dei de salute sua con- tra semetipsos aspernati fuerint. Beatus Lutherus: Schröcklicher/ das ist / welcher die Hof= färtigen blendet/ und die Demütigen er= leuchtet. Grosse/ der herrlich/ lebendig/ gerecht und selig machet. Wigandus, DIES MAGNUS ob adventum Christi, qui & persona & officio maximus est. TERRIBILIS propter Judæos, & non amplectentes Messiam, sed eum cruci affigentes.

## 4:6
Verse 6.

AND HE SHALL TURN THE HEART OF THE FATHERS TO THE CHILDREN AND THE HEART OF THE CHILDREN TO THEIR FATHERS.) After the times of the Maccabees to the times of Christ, Judea had been agitated not only by discords but also by civil wars, a brief memory of which is in Tacitus, Histories 5, and a more exact one in Josephus: furthermore, sects, the Sadducees from the Pharisees, and among these the new sects of Hillel and Shammai, had distracted the people. John will begin to bring remedies to these evils, instilling precepts of charity, Luke 3:11, and sending everyone back to one master, Matt. 3:11, Mark 1:7, Luke 3:16, John 1:15. Thus, where the Prophets end, the four Gospels begin, as is most evident in Mark. But what is set forth in Matthew, Luke, and John are prolegomena, to designate the persons of John and the Messiah himself. The beginning of the Gospel is the same among all, from where Mark begins. See what has been said about this passage in Luke 1:7.

There is no reason why we should explain these things as the settling of the dissensions agitated after the times of the Maccabees to the times of Christ, and the removing of the sects of the Sadducees and Pharisees, for dissensions and sects never cease. Nor were they removed under the advent of John; rather, they prevailed more gravely among the people. They are rather to be understood concerning the spiritual unity and concord of the children of God, which is preserved intact even in the midst of wars and various sects disturbing the Church, which some interpret concerning the fathers and children of that time, along with R. Solomon, Kimchi, and Aben Ezra: Who will be, he says, all one heart, or of one heart to return to God, as much the fathers as the children; so that the sense is: that Elijah will bring it about that the dissenting hearts of fathers and children may come together into one, that they may conspire in faith, piety, and holiness of life, which, even if it was not brought about everywhere, nay, the contrary happened, Matt. 10:21, yet this was the end proposed for Elijah, and this discourse is not about adversaries, but about the members of the Church itself, who cohere by mutual charity, and seriously abhor the profane dissensions of external men.

Others think the ancient fathers are being referred to, to whose faith their children and descendants are to be brought back by this preparer and proclaimer of the Messiah. How Cocceius is said to have brought back the heart of the fathers to the children, so that, namely, Abraham and the rest might not be ashamed of their children, Isa. 29:22, 23. and the heart of the children to the fathers, that is, the children to the sense of the righteous, or to their faith, Luke 1:17, because by his doctrine he called the Israelites to repentance and faith by demonstration from the law and the Prophets without miracles, by the indication of the promised Messiah, and by testimony concerning both his person and office, and his exhibition: Blessed Balduinus followed the former sense concerning the reconciliation of minds among those who were dissenting: For just as Elijah once refuted the Baalitic idolatry, and from it turned the Israelitic people to the one true God: So John most gravely touched upon Pharisaism with his sermons, and turned the people away from the corruptions of their teachers to the one Messiah. Similarly Osiander: Just as the prophet Elijah once, when there was a great dissension of religion (as some worshipped Baal, others the God of Israel), refuted impiety with great and divine zeal, and brought back the Israelitic people to the acknowledgment of the true God, so that after the signal and stupendous miracle of Elijah (by which he called down fire from heaven) all with one mouth, as much fathers as children, confessed the true God of Israel, 1 Kings 18, so John the Baptist will rebuke the dissensions of the sects in the people of God with great zeal, and (to his obedient hearers) will remove them: and will lead his disciples to the acknowledgment of the true God (Jesus Christ the Redeemer of the World). So also Blessed Tarnovius, as well as B. Wigandus, that the office of John would be to hand down the true religion, to lead everyone to Christ. This is the concord, for it is necessary that the faith of all be fixed in Christ, as many as desire to be saved, Acts 4:12. Augustine delivered the latter sense in book XX of The City of God, chapter 29. The sense is that the children, that is, the Jews, may also understand the law in the same way that the Fathers, that is, the Prophets, in whom Moses himself also was, understood it: For thus the heart of the fathers shall be turned to the children, when the understanding of the fathers shall be led to the understanding of the children, and the heart of the children to the fathers of the same, while the latter agree in that which the former perceived. Which Toletus on Luke 1:17 and Cornelius à Lapide on this passage have also embraced. Both are sufficiently elegant, whence the blessed Winkelmann rejects neither, though he proposed the latter a little differently. There were in the people the sects of the Pharisees, Sadducees, Epicureans, and Essenes. Whence the fathers differed from the children, and these from those, but John, having pointed out the errors and corruptions, brought back the fathers and children to the unity of the faith. Or he turned the descendants to the faith of the holy Patriarchs and the Jewish Fathers to receive the doctrine of Christ and the Apostles. The blessed Luther also joined both: Now the prophecy ceases / and the messenger Elijah is expected / who is John the Baptist / who will perform the office of Elijah / which is / that He may turn the heart of the fathers to the children / that is / that they may recognize the wisdom and the faith of the fathers / that they may unanimously recognize Christ / who are now torn and divided into sects, as John found when he preached baptism for repentance and saw many Pharisees and Sadducees, etc. In sum, that this one people might have one heart, one faith, etc. We consider the former explanation simpler, which also most of the Reformed, as well as Vatablus and Castrius among the Catholics, have approved, who believe that by this phrase nothing else is meant than that all, both fathers and sons, are to be converted to one faith and religion, as if he were to say: Elijah will convert the heart of the fathers to the sons, and the heart of the sons to the fathers, that is, he will cause the fathers and sons to have one heart; that is, they may be unanimous in faith and the love of God, so that with one common heart and mind the fathers with the sons and the sons with the fathers, that is, both the older and the younger, may receive and worship Christ.

But the sense which Cornelius peddles as mystical is forced: Elijah will convert the heart of the fathers; that is, of the Jews, to the sons, that is, to Christ and the Apostles: for these, born of the Jews, were their sons: and the heart of the sons to the fathers, namely, of the Christians to the Jews (for the first Christians arose from the Jews), as if to say, Elijah will cause the Jews to believe in Christ and the Christians, so that the faith and religion of the Christians may be infused into the Jews, and consequently that both may have one heart, that is, mind, faith, and religion, namely the worship of Christ. From which he tries to carve out that almost all Jews at the end of the world are to be converted to Christ through Elijah, although he was not ignorant that a firm argument is sought only from the literal sense: nor did the Angel in Luke 1:17 explain this oracle concerning Elijah the Tishbite, but concerning John who was to come in the spirit and power of Elijah. He himself shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, where he omitted the second member: because it has the same sense as the former and both express the concord of fathers and sons: But lest we be ignorant of what kind this concord is, he added, the disobedient to the wisdom of the just, or into wisdom. IN for AD, as in Mark 1:15, 1 Thess. 4:7, John 4:9, so that he might show the foundation of true concord, which is pleasing to God, which is finally that which is fostered in the unity of faith: The incredulous, therefore, were to be converted to the faith, which is the wisdom of the just, and to be bound together in mutual concord in that faith.

Gualtherus has thus embraced the more important members of the comparison of John with Elijah: For first, as in the times of Elijah under King Ahab there was the greatest corruption of divine worship and doctrine and even of morals: So under the coming of John among the Jewish people it sufficiently appears from the history of that age and the writings of the Evangelists that all things were most corrupt. Then, as Elijah with incomparable zeal opposed himself to the false priests and prophets, and even dared to resist the king himself to his face, so John struggled with the priests and scribes of the Jews, and furthermore with King Herod himself, with the unconquered power of the spirit. And as Jezebel most infested Elijah: so it is evident that John was most especially attacked by the snares of Herodias. Finally, as Elijah restored the worship of God, while the impious adversaries resisted in vain; so John brought many back to the obedience of faith, even though the enemies of purer doctrine opposed themselves to him. Deservedly, therefore, the name of Elijah is attributed to John: Nor should it cause any scruple to anyone that he himself, when questioned by the legates of the priests, denies that he is Elijah and the Prophet, for he was not Elijah in that sense, nor anyone from the number of the Prophets, which they had conceived from common error. Furthermore, John was intent on this, that he might send back to Christ those whom he saw were too much addicted to him. The Talmudists (as Abarbenel reports) dream that Elijah the Tishbite, having been awakened, will tell the sons of others and the fathers of others, upon whose report men will believe in the truth of the judgment.

LEST PERCHANCE I COME AND STRIKE THE LAND WITH A CURSE.) That is, lest when I come, I destroy utterly all who are in Judea: for that is חרם. For already the axe was being laid to the root, Matt. 3:10, Luke 3:9. Through this mission of John, and of Christ shown by John, many did penance, and thus were snatched from the common destruction of the nation. This is what Paul says in Rom. 9:29.

However, these things are not to be understood as concerning those who were to be snatched from common destruction at the time of the final judgment against the Jews, nor does it concern only temporal destruction, from which it is evident that some were liberated, but just as there was speech concerning the coming of Christ as a Prophet announcing and offering salvation, not concerning the coming of Christ the judge, bringing the final judgment upon the Jews: so it was John's task, by the proclamation of repentance and the announcement of the coming kingdom of God, to convert the sons of Israel to the Lord their God, lest they all perish, whether those who were living at the time of the first coming of Christ, or those whom that final destruction of the Jews found alive. For Christ could have struck the whole land with a curse when he came in this manner, but he indulged the Jews with a time of repentance, a full 40 years, and those who did not neglect this time of the visitation of grace escaped the divine curse. In the Hebrew there is no particle of doubting 'perchance', nor is the sentence doubtful, but certain and ratified (whence Cornelius cannot help the Vulgate by referring that particle not to the coming, but to the striking) lest I come and strike the land with a curse, that is, one filled with incredulity and crimes.

Regarding the land of Judea, some understand it with Grotius, others understand it generally as the whole land, and Arias among the Papists explains the anathema as the destruction of the Jews by Titus and the Romans. But the other Papists interpret it as the final judgment of the world, yet nothing prevents it from being understood generally, because if the people had not been prepared for the Lord for repentance and faith, what would have hung over the whole land, if not the anathema of eternal curse? In the same sense Jerome, Augustine, Remigius, Rupert, and Haymo understand by the name of land generally earthly men, and those sticking in sins. In which way also the Chaldean: Lest perhaps when I shall have been revealed, and shall have found the land with its sins, I shall strike it then with extermination: The Hebrew חרם denotes a curse and extermination, as does the Greek ἀνάθημα Gal. I. 8. 9. 1 Cor. XVI. 22. thus B. Luther: That is/ to bring to nothing entirely/ for so Scripture uses the word Cher, Anathema, Ban/ which one ought not to use/ or purchase/ but had to bring to nothing. That this may not happen to this people, but that some who remain may be saved, I will send John. &c. Whenever they are unwilling to receive the mercy of God, which is called חרם in Hebrew, they are conversely compelled to experience the חרם, the anathema of God, since they refuse to obey Christ who says, COME, they must hear the same [saying] DEPART, Matt. XXV, 41. May the Lord Jesus grant a faithful and obedient heart in the kingdom of grace, by which we may joyfully hear the voice that will send us into the kingdom of glory, so that we may enjoy spiritual and heavenly health under the wings or rays of the Sun of righteousness eternally, and there, where there shall be no more anathema, but the throne of God and of the Lamb and His servants, there we may serve Him, and see His face, and bear His name on our foreheads: And there shall be no night there, and we shall need no light of lamp, nor light of Sun, because the Lord God shall enlighten us, and we shall reign for ever and ever, Amen. Let it be so, Lord Jesus, Amen. To Thee with the Father and the Holy Spirit be eternal glory, Amen.

Lastly, I would wish those who are about to read our labor to be admonished by the words of Theodoret: concerning those things which we have said well and rightly, let them pursue the TRINITY with praises. For knowledge is His gift: thus likewise blessed David says: teaching man knowledge. But if anything from the prophetic oracles has escaped our understanding, let them forgive the infirmity of nature, praise our purpose, and compensate for our labors with prayers. May the Provider of good things, the fountain of Wisdom, instruct the Author and the Readers with prudence in all things, so that serving Him with the keenest zeal, we may glorify Him in our body and in our spirit, since glory befits Him for ever and ever, Amen.

TO THE TRIUNE GOD AGAIN AND AGAIN BE GLORY.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

ET CONVERTET COR PATRUM AD FI- LIOS ET COR FILIORUM AD PATRES EORUM.) Post tempora Maccabæorum ad Christi tempora agita- ta fuerat Judæa non discordiis tantum, sed & bellis civi- libus, quorum brevis memoria apud Tacitum est Histo- riarum V. exactior apud Josephum: sectæ præterea Sad- ducæos à Pharisæis & inter hos novæ sectæ Hillelis & Sameæ populum distraxerant. Johannes incipiet his malis adferre remedia, caritatis instillans præcepta, Lucæ 3, 11. & ad unum magistrum omnes remittens Matth. 3, 11. Marc. 1, 7. Lucæ 3, 16. Johann. 1, 15. Ita ubi desinunt Prophetæ, incipiunt quatuor Evangelia, ut in Marco aper- tissimum est. Quæ autem præmittuntur in Matthæo, Luca & Johanne, sunt προλεγόμενα, ad designandas per- sonas Johannis & Messiæ ipsius. Evangelii initium apud omnes idem est, unde Marcus incipit. Vide quæ de hoc loco dicta ad Lucam 1, 7.

Non est quod hæc de dissidiis post tempora „ Maccabæorum ad Christi tempora agitatis, „ componendis, & sectis Sadducæorum & Phari- sæorum tollendis exponamus, nam dissidia & sectæ nunquam cessant. Neque sub adventum Johan- nis sublatæ sunt, imo gravius in populo invalue- runt. De spirituali potius unitate atque concor- dia filiorum Dei, qui etiam inter media bella & se- ctas multivarias Ecclesiam perturbantes, integra conservatur, intelligenda sunt, quod nonnulli de Patribus & filiis istius temporis pariter interpretan- tur, cum R. Salomone, Kimchio & Aben Ezra: Qui erunt, ait, omnes cor unum, sive unius cordis ad revertendum ad Deum, tam patres, quam filii; ut sensus sit: Eliam præstiturum, ut patrum & filiorum corda dissidentia in unum coeant, ut in fide, pietate, vitæ sanctimonia conspirent, quod, etsi ubivis præstitum non sit, imo contrarium e- venerit Matth. 10, 21. hic tamen finis Eliæ proposi- tus fuit, & sermo hic non de adversariis est, sed de membris ipsius Ecclesiæ, quæ mutua charitate co- hærent, & à profanis hominum exteriorum diffidiis serio abhorrent.

Alii Ptres antiquos respici censent, ad quorum fidem reducendi sint per hunc Messiæ προετοιμα- σὴν καὶ προκαταγγέλτωρα filii & posteri ipsorum. Quomodo reduxisse dicitur Coccejo cor Patrum ad filios, ne scil. Abrahamum & cæteros puderet filio- rum suorum Es. 29, 22. 23. & cor filiorum ad pa- tres, hoc est filios ad sensum justorum, sive ad fidem ipsorum Luc. 1, 17. quia doctrina sua vocavit Israe- "litas ad pœnitentiam & fidem demonstratione "è lege & Prophetis sine miraculis, indigitatio- "ne Messiæ promissi, & testificatione cum de i- "psius persona & officio, tum de exhibitione ipsius : Priorem sensum sequutus est B. Balduinus de conciliatione animorum inter eos, qui dissentie- bant: Nam quemadmodum Elias olim idolola- triam Baaliticam refutavit, & ab ea populum Israe- liticum ad unum verum Deum amandavit: Ita Jo- hannes concionibus suis Pharisæismum gravissime tetigit, & à corruptelis doctorum suorum populum ad unicum Messiam ablegavit. Similitet Osiander: Sicut olim Propheta Elias, cum magna esset dissen- sio religionis (ut alii Baal, alii Deum Israelis cole- rent) magno & divino zelo impietatem redarguit, & populum Israeliticum ad agnitionem veri Dei reduxit, ut post insigne & stupendum Eliæ mira- culum (quo ignem de cælo devocavit) omnes uno ore tam patres quam filii, verum Deum Israe- lis confiterentur 3. Regum 19. ita Johannes Bapti- sta dissidia sectarum in populo Dei magna zelo reprehendet, atque (ad obsequentes suos au- ditores) tollet : & discipulos suos ad veri Dei (Jesu Christi Redemptoris Mundi) agnitionem adducet. Sic etiam Beatus Tarnovius, ut & B. Wigandus, officium Johannis fore veram reli- gionem tradere, omnes adducere ad Christum. Hæc est concordia, nam omnium fidem necesse est in Christo esse fixam, quotquot salvi fieri cu- piant Actor. IV. 12. Posteriorem sensum tradi- dit Augustinus l. XX. de civitate Dei c. 29. Sen- "sus est, ut etiam filii sic intelligant legem, id "est, Judæi, quemadmodum Patres eam intellexe- "runt, id est Prophetæ, in quibus erat & ipse Moy- "ses: Sic enim cor patrum convertetur ad filios, "cum intelligentia patrum perducetur ad intel- "ligentiam filiorum, & cor filiorum ad patres "eorundem dum in id quod senserunt illi, con- sentiant & isti. Quem etiam Toletus in Luc. I. 17. Cornelius à Lapide in hunc locum amplexus est. Uterque satis concinnus est, unde neutrum respuit Beatus Winkelmannus, posteriori tamen paulo aliter proposito. Erant in populo sectæ Pharisæorum, Sadducæorum - Epicuræorum, & Essæorum. Unde patres à filiis, & hi ab illis dissidebant, Johannes autem monstratis errori- bus & corruptelis, patres & filios ad fidei uni- tatem reduxit. Vel posteros ad fidem sancto- rum Patriarcharum & Patres Judæos ad doctri- nam Christi & Apostolorum recipiendam flexit. Utrumque etiam conjunxit Beatus Lutherus : Nun höret die Prophezey auff / und wird erwartet der Bote Elias / welcher ist Johannes der Tåuffer/der das Ampt Elia führen wird / welches ist/daß Er be- kehre das Hertz der Våter zu den Kin- dern / das ist/ daß sie erkennen die Weis- heit und den Glauben der Våter/daß sie eintråchtiglich Christum erkennen / wel- che iet in Secten zerrissen und zertheilet sind/wie es denn Johannes funden hat/ als er die Tausse zur Busse predigte/ und sahe viel Phariseer und Saduceer &c. In Summa/ daß dieses einige Volck hätte ein Herz/einen Glauben &c. Simpliciorem tamen censemus priorem explicatio- nem, quam etiam è Reformatis plerique, nec non è Pontificiis Vatablus & Castrius probarunt, qui censent hæc phrasi non aliud significari, quam omnes tam patres, quam filios ad unam fidem ac religionem convertendos, q. dicat: Elias con- vertet cor patrum ad filios, & cor filiorum ad pa- tres, id est, faciet ut patres & filii habeant unum cor; id est, sint unanimes in fide & amore Dei, ut uno communi corde & animo patres cum filiis & filii cum patribus, id est, tam majores quam minores Christum recipiant & colant.

Coactus autem est sensus, quem pro mysti- co venditat Cornelius: Elias convertet cor patrum; id est, Judæorum ad filios, id est, ad Christum & Apostolos: hi enim ex Judæis prognati, eorum fuerunt filii: & cor filiorum ad patres, nimirum, Christianorum ad Judæos (primi enim Christia- ni ex Judæis sunt orti) q. d. Elias faciet ut Ju- dæi credant Christo & Christianis, ut Christia- norum fides & religio infundatur Judæis, ac pro- inde utrique habeant unum cor, id est, animum, fidem & religionem, nimirum cultum Christi.
